reviews_attraction.text: Park at the Sunset Beach Pier.  Pack your pen, camera water and a towel.   Walk to the Pier and Turn right and then just walk.  I kept seeing dunes which I thought were the right one and it wouldn't be there... so, I kept walking.  As get closer to the Jetty you'll find it.  Now the is the hike worth it?  Sun, Sand, Water, Sky and friends both seen and unseen and a chance to share your thoughts, wishes and desires away from the madding crowds.  Is it worth it, Yes, 100%

What a great day trip from Greenville or Charlotte or Ashville.   So many interesting stops to make and then the view from Caesars head is amazing.   This was a trip well worth taking.  Especially in the fall as the leaves change and then early morning is also worthwhile with fog on the distant vistas. So pack up your car with family and food and set off and find adventure.

The NPS does a good job detailing the story behind the battle and what led up to the engagement.  But where the strongest marks come is actually walking the battlefield and the many trails around Kings Mountain; one can almost feel the wild frontier.  I think here more than most battles we understand the influence of the frontier Militias in winning our independence.

What a great shop and museum.  My grandparents were Pepsi Cola Bottlers so for me this was almost like going home.  I certainly felt a connection to family while visiting.  The prices were reasonable.  With the influence Soft Drinks have had on America and the World this is a great stop.  And its not over the top like the rival brand.

We had an interesting tour and many stories from Hollywood.  He added interesting flavor to the the history of Jackson and early Rock & Roll, Rock-a-Billy. there was always a story behind an object or photo.    The museum has tons of photos and a whole section just on Elvis.  I just wish there was more music playing.

It's a bit out of the way but I think that is kind of the charm.  The afternoon I went there was really no one there and I had it all to myself.  The Spring was roaring and beautiful the colors were almost magical.  There is a lot of parking and scenic views at various spots.  I want to visit again and again.

Beautiful inside and out.  Such a peaceful and inviting spirit about the building.  This is one of the most beautiful Temples I’ve visited and I recommend that should you have the time and inclination that you too visit ponder and pray nearby and if able inside, you will find insight and inspiration.

I remember hearing of the Death of Elvis when I was 10 years old and being really sad.  Visiting and walking through his home was an amazing experience,  there is just so much to see and hear and being their with so many fans is awesome.    I'm so happy I was able to visit with family.

What a beautiful setting for a Temple, the house of God.  It's so peaceful and serine; even if you're not able to attend the Temple go and walk the grounds and feel of the spirit and take in the happiness of those who worship.

For too long I didn't go to the broad river greenway then when I finally did I loved it but it was a month before I moved away from NC.   Perhaps one day I can be close by and again enjoy the wonder and beauty that is there.

This National Battlefield is well maintained and presents the narrative of the Battle well.  The Trails around the National Park offer great opportunity for exercise and perspective of the Revolutionary War Battle.

Want a downtown walk outside the hustle and bustle of Atlanta?  Try Oakland Cemetery.  Beautiful, historic, and pleasant.  You’ll find something different with each visit and yet you will not tire of going back.
Beautiful, moving and a well kept National Monument.  The displays and educational tools were well done, informative.   The Rangers were helpful and knowledgeable.
A beautiful and well kept battlefield the visitors center is a must see and I recommend you get out and walk the battlefield so you have the complete experience
With so much to see and do in Littleton and lake Gaston this is a must stop just for the those inclined to wonder about mysterious phenomena
Beautiful, spiritual and powerful.  Visit learn about the gospel of Jesus Christ and walk in the peaceful grounds away from maddening crowds
The Park was well kept and offers so much amazing information on the Campaign and Battle.  Its worth the drive and the history lesson.
I'd been to Portland many times but did not know about about this park.   Now I only want to visit here and sit and think and dream.
Wonderful history and displays and great staff who answer all your questions.   Really a must stop if you’re in Franklin

"I hear a tender rhapsody; but in reality she doesn't even know me.
Just my imagination once again runnin' way with me."
This is a great park to visit and if you stand in the right place your photos can get quite the laugh.  Worth the visit
One of the better renditions of the King and worthy of his greatness and voice and ability to awe as a performer.
Its seems small but as you tour you realize that it has so much to offer with History and the sacrifices offered
The history of this place is a must stop to learn and understand the battle and the birth of our Nation.
Such a special place and a sweet spirit of love and promise of a hopeful tomorrow in Christ our Savior.

Awsome Park! This is so much nicer then Six flags or any other! There was so much to do! And you cant beat the price!!! Tickets were only $50 per person for two days including water park and concert!?! That is an insane deal that you cant beat!  The park is so clean and shaded and the staff are so friendly and willing to help! This is our second visit to Wild Adventures and it just keeps getting better! And to mention all the cute animals!!! Love it! Basically a zoo Themed park!!

Wonderful Boardwalk and swimming area! If you are in Niceville this is a must visit! Have been coming here since I was a little girl! Walk all the way down the board walk with a tube or float and then float all the way back down! This is always a blast with friends and family! Make sure you watch out for snakes though! If you dont mess with them they won't mess with you! Have fun!

You must visit Disney Springs!!! Its FREE! Even if you aren't going to Disney you should still come and enjoy some time at Disney Springs! Lots of shopping and great food! Also the views were very nice and they had lots of fun activities for kids! Also plenty of parking in the parking garage!

Great experience but I wouldn't pay $15 per person for 3 rotations on a Faris wheel. Also the wait was about an hour and half and growing! And unfortunately it did seem to be in a sketchy part of town! And the some staff were friendly but others not so much!

Beautiful pier! Much Much longer then we thought it would be it took us almost 20 minutes to walk down while looking around! Their were even bathrooms at the end with water fountains! I think the facilitates are very clean and the price was great!

Wonderful visit! You could spend a couple of hours here exploring this beautiful park! You could bring the whole family! Unfortunately did not get to go inside because everything was closed for the season! Still worth looking around!

Great experience! One of the coolest aquariums I have visited! Although it was not as big as some but you can still spend 4 hours here easily! Easy access and fun for the family! I would highly recommend this Chatanooga Adventure!
A must visit! I have visited bald river falls 5 times and everything I come I am in awe! You can even go swimming! I would recommend water shoes!! Just be careful not to get pulled under!
Amazing state park with so much to offer! This is most definitely a worth the visit! Nature all around and right on the bay with a private beach! It is a perfect weekend camping trip!
Amazing trail! This trail was gorgeous but could be kind of difficult as it was very steep in some areas! We took a taxi from downtown because the free shuttle doesn't go up that far!
I would highly recommend! The drive up alone is worth every second of your time! There is also no addmision charge which is awesome! Stunning views & beautiful light house & grounds!
So much fun! I would highly recommend! It is a must do when in Michigan! We had a blast & our tour guide was so knowledgeable! We learned so much about the area as well! Thank you!
MUST SEE!!! If you are in Northern Michigan you have to see this view! We actually stumbled on this stunning point at random & i can't imagine not seeing it! It was so beautiful!
Had a great time at here! It seems that the staff really care about what they do and it shows! Everything was clean and there was lots to see and do! I will be back!
Wonderful dog park! We love taking our dogs here! It is great! All fenced very nice and lots of doggies for our babies to play with! They love this dog park!
Such a wonderful park! This is in such a great area as well with gorgeous views! There is shopping near by and the city is always hosting events here!
Such a great visit! A must see! There is so much to see at the USS Alabama you could easily spend a whole day! And make to your wear walking shoes!
I have been visiting this park since I was a little girl and have always enjoyed it! We live close and always enjoy walking down to the water!
Nice hike! However I wouldn't say this is a easy hike in any way! It was up hill most of the way if not all! And the view wasn't that great.
This place was so cool it was completely hidden! It took us by surprise! I would definitely put this on your to do while visiting disney!
I wasn't very impressed with the pier it seemed very run down & there wasn't much to do. The area also seemed to be a little sketchy.
We stumbled upon this park while driving through town! I think it is a must see if your in the area! Gardens and incredible views!
Very nice museum! The museum was on the smaller side bur had so much to offer! The staff were very friendly and helpful as well!
Nice beach with plenty of space. Keep a close eye on your belongings though! My friends shoes were stole here!!
We love cades cove! A must visit when in the Smokies! So much wildlife & such a fun family activity!!

To see a 4.5 acre lake underground like that is an amazing thing. The picture on their brochure shows the area at the lake to be much more lit up than it really is. It is actually quite dark. Only a few lights underwater that allow you to see the fish at a certain spot only where they throw out some of fish food. My only thought is that they should place some more lights around the lake a bit so that you can see where you are and what is around you a bit better. Admission to Ruby Falls is the same price, but they have made it so that you can see so much more of what is down there. I hope they will consider doing a bit more to make it more viewable at the Lost Sea, it is definitely a hidden treasure.
A quick tip so that you can see what's down there for yourself with the limited lighting, bring your own flashlight.
dislikes: Less viewable compared to Ruby Falls

reviews_attraction.text:
A truly wonderful gem out in the middle of the desert. About 3 miles off 95 on the right, very large, not too be missed! Just beautiful!
And while you're out here, continue on about three more miles to the parking area to Palm Canyon. It's about a 3/4 mile hike to view the palms. The path is rocky and should be taken slowly, but with the effort.
And if you have the opportunity, abundant camping with some most amazing sunsets!

What fun!!  It's free to check the whole thing out and it's bigger than you think. There is a donation can if you decide you want to make one, but it's not mandatory and there's no 1 going to even be out there anyway. It is so cool! The things this man did with stuff he found everywhere. Amazing! Definitely worth a visit!

I could literally spend days in the Duesenberg Museum! What's a good place to visit!  $12.50 admission. This is right by the national Auburn corn truck and Automotive Museum. And you can boondock in the parking lot across the street free, they've even got electric hookup, no charge either. Highly recommend this place!

Very pretty and well-maintained park with gorgeous views! It's only about 5 miles or so from Main Street in Hendersonville to the park, but it's a nice curvy road, perfect on my motorcycle! This park would be a beautiful stop no matter what kind of day. But a sunny day would give you the most gorgeous views.

Wow, even the smell just like the old garage is coming the great old days. They had so many different vehicles oh, so now I have never seen before. I thought it would take about an hour maybe two, to get through it...
Took me almost 4. LOL.
Recommended to any classic car and truck enthusiasts. What fun!

Absolutely fantastic! Be aware that there are a lot of steps to go down to the falls and every one of those steps has to be taken in order to get back up again. LOL. The suspension bridge makes that hike all the way down there and back up worth it as well! Highly recommend this place!

What a wonderful place to visit! Do yourself a favor, Google it real quick like and read the story behind the Mystery Castle before you go. It adds a whole new perspective when you visit. What a great time! $10 apiece for adults. Hi, Ramon, thank you both for a wonderful tour! Lol!

What a fun place! It would be fun for anyone, but especially if you are an RVer. I got here too late this afternoon to see everything so I'll be back again in the morning. This is so fun! I would highly recommend this place if you've ever even thought about RVing!

Wow, what a view! The stairs getting up there take a little time, especially when you have a bad knee, but well worth it!
And the owner, a very nice man, full of all kinds of interesting information! This is definitely a stop for the whole family!

What a great little spot! A very nice place to stop, especially if you are into local railroad history. Free admission, donations accepted if you're so inclined. Just a really nice place for a short visit, even a picnic!

Another wonderful place to visit. So much more than just the Lighthouse  which would be a fabulous visit all unto itself. But then there's the Shipwreck Museum and the beach. Just an all around great way to spend a day!

Absolutely beautiful! And I was fortunate enough to come visit on a day when the church band was practicing outside in the pavilion. They were singing all the old Christmas carols, made my day! Merry Christmas to all!
What amazing place, a step back into time. Definitely worth the visit. Best times to visit though would be when school is in session during the week. It gets really crowded in the summer.
Nice little part to stop for a break and rest for a while after a long day on the road. Only downside is that the tree branches hang so low. Thank you though for the respite. :)
If you are at all interested in military lifestyle, particularly Naval, this is a must-see! Between the USS Alabama and the USS drum, you'll need a whole day to see everything!
Just a fabulous place! It's not real big, but they sure do have a lot of neat stuff packed in there! Wait until you see the car! Loved the whole thing, highly recommended! :-)
Oh my goodness, how much more fun can you have that's got so much to see and is actually free! Great place to bring the kids, lots of fun stuff to check out.
Oh my goodness, loved this place! It's a very short hike, but there are rocks and roots to be careful of. Wear good shoes and enjoy!! I know I did! :-)
Absolutely wonderful place to visit and it's free! I love the way it's all set up with history and pictures and even a boardwalk. Perfect!
The highest point east of the Mississippi, I am told. The views are outstanding! And the ride on a motorcycle? It's a dance... :-)
So much more there than I expected! I highly recommend a visit to this museum. It's not very big, but it sure packs a punch. Free.
What a beautiful spot to just sit on one of the benches and rock some time away. Just smells wonderful! Highly recommended stop.
Oh wow, this place is amazing! Who would expect to see this on a college campus! Definitely worth the detour!
What a nice place to stop and check out the black sand beach with the lighthouse across the way. Love it!

This place is well worth it if your in the area. It's well kept especially being that it's been almost 250 years ago. I would stop off at the visitor center and ask to watch the 20 minute video narrated by Trace Adkins. It shows basically a reenactment of what your about to walk through so you can use your imagination as you walk through there knowing what you then know after watching it. This place is very well maintained especially the restrooms. The staff was wonderful and there is information everywhere you look the whole way through. If your a hiker there is the Gouedy Trail, the Historical Cherokee Path, the Historical Charleston Road and different trails about half way through the 1 mile interpretive trail that begins at the visitor center and takes visitors to the remains of Star Fort as well as the original site of Ninety Six. May I warn you hiking through the tall grass, there is a high population of ticks in the area.

This is my favorite place to hike in this area. It's a long hike to the lake and back. You can hike a good 2 miles before it gets overgrown. It's still likable the whole way but I would be careful with the pygmy rattlesnakes in the brush along the narrow parts of trail. I found a couple on one hike in the middle parts of trail. Also near the creeks you can definitely spot large cottonmouth snakes. Watch the kids near the water for the cottonmouth and be careful near the narrow part of trail farther in the trail. Also check for ticks if you go in the farther parts too.

This place was very cool and even if you were in a hurry and in this area its a short walk from the parking area. There is a small entry charge I believe, but well worth it.
The Natural Bridge formation is 60 ft high, 148 feet long, and composed of sandstone and iron ore. This bridge is the longest natural bridge east of the Rocky Mountains in North America. Also here there is a outcropping of rock, presenting the image of a large American Indian head. The stone image is just over 15 feet high and a short walk from the natural bridge here.

This place was awesome! You park on the side or the road which is a paved shoulder. There will be a guy there selling boiled peanuts and snacks. The entrance of the trail you'll see a small waterfall. As you continue you'll see the remains of a home in the woods, all that's left is the stone foundation and chimney. The last Falls is gigantic next to the first one and slides down the rock and lands amongst some pretty big boulders. I found a snake and a salamander there. So keep your eyes peeled, not just at the waterfalls.

This review is not for the tour or inside of this place, just the outside. I was driving down I-26 and seen this on the map. Its very cool and out of the ordinary. Great place to fuel up next door and stretch your legs. I'm not sure what all there is to do if you go during the day and pay to get in. You can spend like 5-10 minutes and maybe tailgate with a snack at least. If your in the area, this is worth the stop even if it's for 5 minutes.

I drove all the way out there and it took me to one pissed off farmer's property. I kept driving around that area driving miles down the road and getting lost. He got suspicious of the same truck driving slow down the road. He came up to my truck and was saying there isn't anything special out here and acted like he didn't know what I was talking about. What did I miss, where is this place!?

This is a nice scenic spot for a short visit. This place is easy to get to after the parking area. Your allowed to actually cross over the natural bridge and go down under it. The parking is tight and off a short one lane paved driveway. Don't attempt to bring any type of trailer back there. You can park it at the dead end before turning down that tight one lane little road.

I went to this state park on a tuesday morning. I went to the visitor center where I found out they had rain recently and got directions to the trailhead. I'm not from Arkansas and I really liked how it was a free state park. It's about a 10-15 minute hike the the waterfall. You hike alongside the lake most the way and it looks nice this time of year.

I went to this state park on a tuesday morning. I went to the visitor center where I found out they had rain recently and got directions to the trailhead. I'm not from Arkansas and I really liked how it was a free state park. It's about a 10-15 minute hike the the waterfall. You hike alongside the lake most the way and it looks nice this time of year.

I went there and wasn't sure of the path, the trail was really short and seemed to dead-end randomly. I left feeling like a didn't even hike. There we're no signs and no trail markers. There was signs about liter, yet garbage was everywhere. It's just smaller than I expected and there is some what of access to the river.

Cool spot to stop real quick and check out. The cave itself is closed to the public but you can park outside the gate and walk up to the mouth of it. If your driving on 72 and want to stretch your legs for a minute this is a cool spot for that. Other than that there's really not much to do here.

This was a must see and the people running this place made it worth the trip. They are so passionate about her and teaching everyone about her story. Go in June and get tickets for the play! Its the highlight of the year for this place and the gardens and vegetation is truly Ivy "Green".

My review is really for the waterfall you see when zip-lining. Very scenic area to hike through with the railroad tracks and bridges. The waterfall itself is wild looking, especially for this part of North Carolina. I would come back just for the view alone.

This place is awesome when I went. There wasn't a whole lot of people and I was able to enjoy all Falls without distractions. There is a nice trail and a very informative museum/main office with maps of the trails/falls. I really enjoyed this State Park.

It was very cool for kids to see all the trains but it was a little crowded. Probably really nice in the cooler months for all the outside stuff and maybe on a weekday where it's less crowded or when the open on the weekend before the crowd.

Very well maintained State Park, with a great staff. Great place to camp and get on the river. They have miles of trail and a variety of different ones to choice from. It's well mapped out with all the information for all your questions.

It was way too muddy for a walk with the dog. I barely was able to avoid it but she just sank into it half way up her legs. It was mess, if it was a board walk through this swamp it would be 4-5 stars.
This is the hiking trail parking. I've updated the location from the middle of the woods to the parking lot. Biking trails and parking are near the golf course on the other side of 985 on Elachee Dr.
I went here a year ago, cool spot! I showed up in the middle of the the and threw a tent out near running water and woke up to a nice hike. Saw a bunch of waterfalls in this area.
LOL well here it is... The smallest city block in the world. I just ran around it like a maniac for a minute. Now I can brag about how fast I can run around the block.
This is a well kept state park and captures the feel of South GA. There is tons to do between the lake and the trails. I have to come back and do more hiking here.
This place caught my eye I drove in on my way back to GA. I really didn't have time do explore. From what I saw, I'll definitely be back.
Only come if it's been raining, it's been dry as a bone lately. Cool little spot right off the road past the bridge though.
Its a great spot for a long hike. I've been here twice nothing too special but a cool spot if your in the area.
Plenty of trail for hikers, lake was pretty and overall the park was in great shape. No litter which was nice.

Arguably the best views in the valley. Sitting on top of the hill, we have 360 degree views of vineyards all around as well as Mt. Hood in the backdrop of the weather is clear. The tasting room itself is somewhat small, as it all takes place within a small “hut”, but the interior is decorated in a very cool manner. The low lite tasting room serves as a great atmosphere to enjoy their wines. The tasting consisted of 3 Pinot noirs as that’s the only varietal they produce. The prices were a little steep for such a small winery but the flavors certainly lived up to the price, they were delicious. This should be on everyone’s list of wineries to visit!

One of our favorites wineries in the northern Michigan area. The Italian inspired building is a site on its own and sits on top a hill that produces some of the best views. Italian style wines that are all pretty good. Our favorite was the Bel Tramonto which is a red blend of merlot, sangiovese, cab franc, and refosco. Their tasting room was really cool and had a long bar so a bunch of people could all gather and taste at the same time. Their outside patio was the perfect spot to order a glass and relax while taking in great views of the vineyards and the lake in the background.

Some of the best views in the valley! Their tasting room opens at 10am so this was our first winery visit of the day. The staff was very friendly and made us feel very welcome. We started our tasting and enjoyed our pours both inside the tasting room and outside on the patio overlooking their vineyards. If it was a little warmer outside, we would have sat down at one of the many tables outside on the patio for hours! Their bubbles were ok but their Pinots were super tasty!

One of my favorite wines! Came here for the first time with my family and had an incredible experience. We arrived around 11:15am and had the while tasting room to ourselves. Jordan was an excellent host and provided an in-depth tasting experience for us all. Their wines were unique and full of flavor...plus they were all very nicely priced! Needless to say we left as club members and consider this winery to be among our favorites in the valley!

If you've ever been curious about what's overhead, this is a place you must visit!  The exhibits are educational and fun plus the views are stunning.  You can overlook LA and catch a great glimpse of the Hollywood sign.  Parking can be a little bit of a nightmare so be prepared to drive around a while looking for a spot or walk a good distance.  All worth the visit!

Some of the best views in Northern Michigan! The parking lot has plenty of spaces and there are public restrooms here as well. If you want to get crazy and take the steep sand down to the water, plan on a 2 hour ascent as it will take you a while! The overlook can get crowded so plan on hanging out for a little while so you can grab a good spot to site see.

Great trail that’s around 4 miles (2 miles in and 2 miles back out). I believe the trail was rated moderate which was fairly accurate as the path was good and had some incline/steps throughout. Parking could be tricky so I certainly recommend getting there early so you can find a space. And bring plenty of water!

Incredible whiskey with an amazing story! If you’re in the KC area you have to visit their distillery. The layout is amazing and you’re able to see all the magic happen while you enjoy a tasting from their tasting table. Everyone there was super nice and friendly which made my last visit even more enjoyable!
Wine tasting at its best! Their tasting area with right in the middle of all the action and since it was small, it made for a very intimate tasting experience.  Their wines are out of this world!!
Definitely worth seeing, even if from afar. We went on Sunday so the main drive up to the lighthouse was closed, but we still got to experience the great view of the lighthouse in the background.
A great place to walk around and enjoy the canals. Best time to go seems to be in the morning. The homes along the canals are also really cool to look at as they are of all different styles.
Great historical site where Thomas Jefferson drafted the Declaration of Independence. The original house was demolished in 1883 but the National Park reconstructed the house you see today.
Fun place for family dining! Their food is awesome and has some great drinks to try throughout dinner. It's always crowded so be sure to plan accordingly.
Fairly neat place to take a picture of these houses that are all different colors. It’s a quick stop so no need to spend a whole bunch of time here.
Amazing to be surrounded by such historical figures. Never thought I'd be excited to visit a burial ground but it was amazing to walk through.
Great display of water features and displays that honor those who fought in WWII. It’s really cool to see at night when everything is lit up!
This is by far one of my favorite places in KC! Their exhibits are well put together and always offer a great variety to fit all interests.
I never realized how tall the monument actually was until I stood next to it. The best views were at night when all the lights were on it!
Pretty cool to drive through but the experience can be ruined depending on how many homeless people are sleeping underneath the bridge.
Very friendly service up at the tasting bar. They had a huge selection of wines to try and the ones we had were pretty good.
Their tasting room was incredible and overlooked their vineyards! Great wine also, their red lineup was one of my favorites.
Beautiful drive along the coast! You can even see some of the giant houses in the backdrop of you're driving to the East.
Very cool winery with a great patio to enjoy views of their vineyard. Their wines are awesome, especially their pinots!
A must see if your in town, the tour was great and got a chance to hit the batting cages before we left!
Didn’t get a chance to go inside as we were short on time but the exterior of the museum was beautiful!

Wow!  What an unexpected delight.  I drove through town to see the courthouse, and this museum caught my eye.  Gorgeous building, and the displays are amazing.  There aren't too many actual artifacts, but there are murals/paintings covering the walls in three downstairs rooms.  You pick up a handheld audio player from the front desk, and type in the number under the piece of mural you want to learn about.  A brilliant way of telling the story without having you read panel after panel after panel.  The narrator had an engaging voice, and the information he was presenting was very interesting.  I couldn't stay as long as I wanted, but for the low entry price, I'll be back to learn the rest of the Kenedy tale!

I'm so glad this little lighthouse was salvaged and brought ashore for us to enjoy!  I timed my visit well - the friendly groundskeeper at the Bauer Community Center next door let me inside the lighthouse and gave me a little tour (it's not a big structure).  If you are feeling adventurous, he'll take you up the ladder to the lantern room (no lens in there anymore).  If you arrive during regular hours and find the place locked, pop in to the Chamber office in the big building and they'll have it opened for you.  They also have the stamp for the USLHS Passport, if you collect those.

Excellent spot to get a look at a dig site.  You need to be on a tour, for which there is a nominal fee (Parks pass doesn't work).  Worth the small charge, for sure!  There's a bit of a walk down a paved path to reach the climate controlled building that houses the site.  No food or beverages allowed inside.  Entire tour lasts about 45 minutes, with the last leaving around 4, so don't leave it too late!  Small gift shop and restrooms are located adjacent to the parking area.

Rangers and staff are friendly, welcoming, and extremely knowledgable.  The Visitor Center has tons of historical information laid out in an interesting display, and there are many more informative signs along the various trails throughout the park.  Seems to be very popular with locals for hikes/walks/jogs, especially on the weekend and after work.  If you have kids (or are interested yourself), there are numerous junior ranger activities available.

An absolute gem of a place.  I went during the day, which was pretty, despite it being "off season" for flowers.  The boat ride was both entertaining and informative, but beware of low winter tides - the planned 11am excursion was cancelled so as not to ground the boats.  I was in town longer than expected, so I dropped by again that night to see the Christmas Lights.  I'd highly recommend a visit, especially since there is no entrance fee.
dislikes: Facilities & Services: Low winter tides (boat cancellations)

reviews_attraction.text: Much bigger than it appears from the outside, the collections span a wide variety of local history.  Ample information about Indianola, which is handy since the town is no longer.  If you have any questions, don't hesitate to ask the volunteers - the good lady operating the museum while I visited was incredibly knowledgeable about all things Port Lavaca and Calhoun County.  I left with a much deeper appreciation for the area.

This isn't a big attraction, by any means, but there is an awful lot of history crammed into its small footprint!  The main draw is the "Jesse James" carving in the upstairs wall, but don't miss out on a scramble through the rest of the rooms.  The caretakers on hand during my visit were both friendly and knowledgable.  Definitely worth a few minutes of your time and the $1 suggested entry "fee" donation.

Stayed one night at the campground on a busy summer Friday.  Although it was packed, it didn't feel crowded.  Site was spacious, although the sites on the inside of the loop road have the hookups located on the wrong side.  Managed to position the RV in a way to reach, though, so it wasn't a major issue.  Friendly & helpful staff, lovely setting.  Hope to be back for a longer stay in the future.

Amazing views across the water, and plenty of paved walking trails to get some exercise (and/or walk the dog).  Lots of parking, and there are a number of interpretive signs telling you about the history of the Fort.  (The panels facing the water are a little hard to read.)  Bird blinds near the pond for those that enjoy that sort of thing.

Lovely step back in time!  There are no other houses like this, and the history is fascinating.  Informative tour by the charming volunteers, all very knowledgeable about the structure.  There is a small entrance fee, but it is well worth the cost.  And don't miss the wide selection of local products in the gift shop area on your way out.

Wow!  What an amazing place.  So informative and carefully maintained.  Took the self-guided stroll through the entire village - I'd budget at least an hour to explore all the buildings and read all the signs.  Lovely little shop with friendly staff at the entrance.  Absolutely worth a stop if you are in the area.

One of the friendliest museums I visited along Route 66.  Well done displays, interesting information, and all housed in a fascinating facility, too.  Don't drive the Route without stopping in, and, if you are hungry, there are plenty of historic choices along this stretch to enjoy before or after your visit.

Not much of a turnout here, just a dirt lot (plenty of room to maneuver oversize vehicles) with some informational signs.  The view, however, is spectacular.  I was lucky to have relatively clear (non-foggy) skies, and Mount Rainier was breathtaking.  Don't skip this pull-out, you'll regret it if you do!

Exactly what you would expect.  Although they do look a little smaller from the road - be prepared to walk a ways through the field.  There is a lingering odor from all the spray cans, most of which have been discarded haphazardly around the site.  Take care if you venture out with dogs or little ones.

A lovely place that is surprisingly peaceful for being in such close proximity to a fairly busy roadway.  Loved following the paths through the gardens, past the historic cabins, and over the namesake stone bridge.  There was even a friendly flock of ducks to greet me by the water's edge.

Always fun to explore.  The structures are becoming quite worn down, as one would expect with such an old movie set (that was only built to last a few months).  Glad it has been saved to some extent, and even happier that the public is allowed onto the island to enjoy it!

I was lucky enough to time my visit while Henry was about - he's a wonderful asset to Route 66.  So much history crammed into one place!  Love all the VW Rabbits, and loved getting a peek at Waldmire's old car.  Absolutely worth a stop!

What a little gem!  Noticed the "campground" signs as I was driving into town, and pulled off to have a look.  Ended up staying the night.  Great location, peaceful setting, friendly manager, and crazy cheap price.
Shady walk through the woods to a picturesque waterfall.  Lovely spot to do some exploring - lots of trails leading in different directions, but contained enough that you won't get lost.
Great spot for watching the airplanes coming in for landing at Tampa International.  Lots of walking paths, and a beach area if water recreation is more your style.  Can get crowded.
So much space!  My pup appreciated being able to stretch his legs, and I loved the friendly, welcoming people.  One of the very best dog parks that I have ever found.
Stayed one night in the campground.  Stunning views across the lake.  Great facilities and well maintained grounds.  Easy to find, and the staff are friendly.
Very well maintained part of Route 66 history.  Lovely staffer who was more than happy to answer my questions.  Not a long stop, but well worth the time.
Historic marker, in a lovely park setting.  One of three monuments along the Old Spanish Trail (the others being in San Antonio and San Diego).
Lovely park for a stroll with the dog.  Surrounded by city noise - roads and planes - but an amazing little gem that isn't too remote.

#LetsGuide family friendly The visitors center across the street has bathrooms and quite a lot of information in each room.  If your children are young it may be difficult going through the home and staying on the path.  The tour doesn’t extend upstairs.  5 and over would probably be fine.  Under 1 would be ok, because the tour is short enough to carry your child.  If you’re unsure.  I’d split and have some go to the visitors center and the rest to the home.  The Piano in the home is one of my favorites and check out the paint color in the kitchen.  Tickets should be available on the Independence square.

I love this park.  It is interesting for young and older kids alike.  There are trails to walk your dog.  A zip line, rope climbing, hammock swing, teeter totters, merry go round.  The bathrooms are even clean! There is enough parking.  I love the large stone walls that provide unique places to sit.  And one of the bathrooms is labeled unisex.  How weird?  If one is occupied wouldn't you just use the other?  I was happy that one bathroom was freshly painted.  It is hard to find a park with decent bathrooms and changing tables.

This has potential to become a pretty cool park.  It just doesn't feel like a very safe place.  The bathrooms next to the park looked like something exploded inside there.  There are lots of dumpsters, but trash is all around.  I didn't head for the trail.  The park wasn't empty, but it was mostly guys hanging out in their cars.  It really gave me the creeps.  I didn't stray to far from my car.  Sugar Creek police should have their hands full patrolling this area to keep it safe.

I have toured this home no less than thrice.  The tour guide let our girls try on a hoop skirt once.  Many tours can be difficult with kids, but this is kid friendly.  The slanted porch and curved staircase are very interesting.  Even when the house is closed, the visitors center museum is informative.  I love historic homes.  This was a hospital during the civil war.  It's worth a visit.

There was hang gliding school, sandbar rental, and kite flying.  The sand can sometimes be hot, but when it's nice you can walk barefoot on huge sand dunes.  I've never really been to a place quite like this.  The restrooms are open, but gift shop closed.  Hang gliding school was open.  Once you visit you may want to come back.  There was not a fee for entry.  It's a beautiful sandy park.

Bring money to pay for parking.  #LetsGuide Family Friendly Science City is two floors of just cool fun exhibits.  Plan your visit ahead, because closing time comes so soon.  The Water area you might want to bring something for that.  It’s ok to bring a stroller, but it’s your call. It’s easier to get around without one.  There is something here to entertain babies up to older kids.

This museum and home attraction is a wonderful place to take small kids on their first tour.  I've been at least three times.  Here, I didn't have to worry about the kids losing attention because the home isn't that big.  The bathroom facilities located in the museum were clean.  I think they even built another bathroom by the farm house.  It's the perfect place for tiny tourists.

You need to go on the website to reserve a day to enter.  Plan ahead pay ahead.  We saw elk, deer, and moose in the park.  Sprague Lake was a nice trail.  Lava Rocks was also pretty.  The road to the top has a stop to a waterfall that was very beautiful.  There is so much to see.  The Alpine visitors center was closed because of corona I guess.

This fairly new park has a timeline of milestones in flight etched on giant rudders.  If you have visited the Wright Brothers National Memorial this is a good addition to your trip.  I didnt notice any trails or children's park, but I believe I saw a porta potty.  It's a beautiful Monument and worth the visit if you are in the area.

This place has come a long way in 30 years. Splash park, wheel chair access to the playground equipment!!!!!!  Nice baseball field.  Now if Independence could only fix those bathroooms.....  walking path around playground and park.  It's busy and usually there is a birthday celebration going on.  Very popular place.

This family friendly place is one of a kind!!! It is new the rides are well maintained.  They are safe.  I recommend the water log ride.  It is 7$ to enter, but more for an arm band to ride.  You can easily spend a day on the pier.  Wednesdays are discounted and it is a fee to park.  Plan ahead and spend the day.

I have toured here about 5 times.  The civil war mansion is three floors high.  Third floor is closed.  Second floor isn’t wheelchair accessible.  Children are welcome on tours.  #LetsGuide #familyfriendly The walls are so thick and riddled with history and bullets from the past.  Tour guides are amazing.

It's not good for bigger groups.  There is not very much room to park.  We were expecting longer trails.  The big trees are beautiful.  On a really hot day it's probably better to go someplace else.  This will only take about 10 minutes to see.  The Audobon Bird trails are a little longer.

It's a beautiful place to stop and take pictures.  There are some antique stores nearby and a perfectly clean little gas station.  Wilson has a history of Czech and Bohemian beginnings.  The Czech egg is honoring the town's heritage.

This has a boardwalk and there are lots of turtles.  It seems like a popular fishing area.  The park was still closed, but there is a porta potty.  It was a wonderful place to stop and walk the boardwalk very well maintained.

This fun indoor park is always changing.  Sometimes the best deal is to get a season pass.  The kids enjoyed their gift shop and surprisingly some things are affordable.  It doesn't seem like toys are marked up either.

I liked this place.  Wear shoes because the pavement is hot.  There are lots of lifeguards to keep things safe.  The lazy river has a waterfall that is pretty nice.  Bathrooms aren’t too bad and lockers are available.
This is a cold natural spring to swim in.  If you dont jump in on a hot day, you might wish you did.  There are two short trails for non swimmers.  There is also a wading area to stick your feet in.
This bridge is remote and an excellent place for professional photography.  It is a small distance from the parking lot.  The trail was muddy when we were there.  Good for families with small kids.
The visitors center is a good place to get information and come in out of the heat while you wait for your tour.  The tickets are not available here.  However, there is a restroom.
I wasn't here for a long time.  It was busy.  There were people walking dogs.  I saw a morning yoga class by this reflecting pool.  It's a busy place, but the parking was free.
This is a historic park that is worth a visit if you live in the area.  There is usually some sort of update to keep the park  going.  Great place for taking photos.
Smaller beach with a good crowd of people, but not too busy.  Steer clear of the rocks!! They are sharp.  Sand showers provided.  An easy day or afternoon trip
Audio self guided tour for first and second floor 12$ Adults.  Basement gift shop.  I wish I could add some pictures of this mansion belonging to the Grisham's
This is an interesting place with replicas and history about Walt Disney.  #LetsGuide Family friendly.  We learned about some history.  I would love to return.

We went with out three kids (3, 6, and 7). They have a nice series of children's exhibits, and there is a great interactive section for kids as well. We all liked the glasswork and silver work. There was a large section of art from local children artists (K-12) that our kids enjoyed and seemed to appreciate more than the other galleries. The museum building itself is located next to a park with a large fish pond and walking paths that we also enjoyed.

Centennial Park is much more than a dog park. There are playgrounds and walking trails with a large duck pond, and an outdoor theater (for plays and concerts). Of course, there is also the Parthenon, which is  a museum and art gallery (there is an entry fee). There are often music/crafts/food events in the park too. There are at least two pavilions with picnic tables. One is located near an old (full size) steam locomotive that my kids love to see.

Neat place to spend an afternoon or all day with kids. Although it's "last" on the recommended tour route, I recommend that you tour the Saturn V hall first. It has the best exhibits and by the time we got there everyone was a little tired. We also saw and paid a little extra for the "Extreme Weather" movie in 3D, but we got bored with it; I don't recommend it. Coupons for admission cam be obtained from the Huntsville visitor center.

The Hands-On museum has combined with the Gray Fossil Site Museum. It's a neat place for kids to explore and play. However, the old Hands-On in downtown Johnson City had many more exhibits for children than the new one. I hope that the new location will grow. Nevertheless, this is a great deal, especially is you are an ASTC member (we are through our membership with the Adventure Science Center in Nashville).

Great place for a weekend with the kids. The campground is great, and the trail around the "fort" is short and fairly flat, but rewarding with multiple waterfalls. The Manchester recreation center is nearby, and it has amazing outdoor pool area with two big slides, a lazy river, splash play area, and more.

Great place for young kids. They have a new tinker garage where you can make things  with provided materials and tools. We made a sailboat. The tinker garage has a test area for sailboats, racecars, and other things. The play area at the middle and top of the center is amazing, and with a visit in itself.

Nice place for a short (or longer) hike. Looks like most of the trails are also used by mountain bikers. In fact, the most complete map I've seen was on the Knox MTB Racing Facebook page (see attached photo for map). The quarry itself is also pretty neat. There is ongoing construction in the park.

Great place to bring kids to play. The park can be reached from downtown across the pedestrian bridge, but I recommend parking on the stadium side; it's free where downtown parking can be very expensive. The park has some unique play areas and an area to view the river.

We did the stone cuts trail (2.4mi loop) with three kids (3-8) and they did great. The stone cuts area is really neat and worth the easy hike. The cabins in this area look neat as well, and have great views. I'd like to go back to stay there for a night or two.

Really neat natural area with lots of kid-friendly hiking. We walked to the stone bridge from the quarry parking area with kids as young as 3. Great experience. Will definitely come back to walk the river boardwalk.

Pricey, but one of the best activities to do with small children in Gatlinburg. Buy tickets early online and look for coupons/discounts. I also recommend the trolly is you're staying at a local hotel.
Beautiful park about an hour drive from Knoxville. I hiked to the east tower from the east side of the park. The trail is an access road, so it was easy (uphill) hiking. Great views at the top.
Bayes Mountain is a great place for kids and adults to explore and play outdoors inexpensively. They have many animal exhibits, hiking, and walking along the lake, and many other activities.
Must see in Nashville! The Parthenon with statue of Athena (entrance fee required). Full size locomotive, old growth oaks and other tree species, are some of the best Nashville has to offer.
Great place for a stroll and a break from walking the Seattle Center area. There are restrooms and wifi at the visitor center. Great views of the water. Great place for kids to run around.
This is a hidden gem. Short and longer hiking trails are great for kids. There are strategically placed benches on the trails to take in some of the Brentwood landscape.
Stayed in campground. The park is well designed and maintained. This area is really beautiful. If you visit the park, take time to also visit the Carver's Gap area.
Great place for short or long hike. Also great for mountain biking. The quarry is neat. However, it's in a seedier part of town. I'll bring a buddy next time.
Great little park (connected to a big park) with a playground, restrooms, and picnic areas. We walked up to the small lake and had fun there.
This is a neat place with several walking paths and playgrounds. Great for kids and adults (I think we saw more adults walking than kids).
Neat place. Several of the trails around the ampitheater are closed, but visitors can still see inside by driving to the top parking lot.
I enjoyed several of the exhibits, but there are too many exhibits to consume in an hour or so. I think it could be more focused.
Beautiful park along the Nachez Trace in Williamson County. They have several trails for hiking and they are well marked.
Nice park for a walk. There is a good size playground for kids and a dog park. Great views of the nearby mountains.
This place is a treat for the senses. All of the colors, shapes and smells, and variety of plant are amazing.

Great place to take the kids and enjoy nature. There's a children's garden that is a blast. But there's things for them to do all over the garden.
There's a miniature train with a little town built around the tracks.
A "cave" that was built next to a campfire ring.
The hammocks are a big hit the the kids. There's also a Koi pond that you can pet and feed the fish in.
The Azalea garden is romantic when it is in bloom.
There's a fort that has sand for the floor and many sand toys. The fort is next to a play structure that looks like Noah's ark. There's a slide and 2 swings too.
Next to that is the sluce box that has running water.
Many ponds and many different types of birds, trees, plants and herbs. It's beautiful to just Stoll through and enjoy a peaceful breath of fresh air.

Great place to bring children of all ages. My 1 year old enjoyed it and so did my 4 year old. There was much to learn in the STEM area. Dissecting a human torso, kinects, weights to learn balancing, a microscope, and fish in a bathtub!
The staff here are all kind and want to help children develop and do their best.
6 month membership is $40, 1 year is $70. Under 2 is free, kids are $4, and adults are $6. We purchased a membership and plan on going frequently. It's a warm play to play when it's snowing.

Great adventure! I would go again.  We were traveling and I have a zoo membership that got me 1/2 price tickets. 2 adults 1-4 year old and 1 infant was $45.
My son loved the shark and starfish petting tanks. And the crawl through aquariums with various fish. The ocean exhibit had recently opened and was a lot of fun watching the fish from below and above.
The sharks aquarium was impressive. The kids sat under and watched for quite some time.

Great exhibits! There's a rainforest exhibit (with a sloth and birds), a movie theater, an outside splash pad, and all the Marine life. There were plenty of opportunities to pet the animals. Sharks, jellyfish, rays and some fish.
We have a zoo membership so we got in for 1/2 price, however it was still expensive (as all aquariums are).
Amazing day! We will visit again, if we lived closer, we would buy the membership.

Beautiful exhibits! Variety of animals. Clean space. Food court is reasonable with pizza, ice cream, hamburgers, and local Cajun food.
You can get and feed the sting rays.
We bought a membership because it covers the zoo as well.
The only downfall of the aquarium is the parking situation and location. It takes quite a while to get there because of traffic. The parking for 2ish hours was $18!

Clean park. 2 sides, one for toddlers and one for"big kids". Sand pits are covered. Swings are on both sides. Castle and town structures. Small parking lot. I parked on the street, busy street with wide sidewalks.
Picnic tables and restrooms are on site as well. Located next to a school and some fields. Easy to get to from the freeway.

Fun park for the kids. 6 swings and a few slides. There's a walking path that's 1/2 mi next to the playground. Very easy for my 5 & 2 year old children to walk. However, people are not picking up after their dogs defecate. The mountain bike trails are fun and challenging too.

Clean park, play equipment was mostly in working order. One slide had snow fencing to block it off at the top and the bottom.
Bathroom was clean.
There was a loose dog running around, but animal control had been phoned by other concerned park goers.

Clean park. Good location.
Nine swings, one of which there's a tire swing, four toddler swings, and four regular swings. Two play structures, one for older kids and one for toddlers. The ground is covered in bark and sand.
Clean restrooms.

We went on a day with intermittent showers. They cancelled our trip, and refunded us 100%. We will come back another day to see the animals. While waiting the kids saw zebras, catfish, kangaroos, and turtles.
Kind and knowledgeable staff.

Fun place to explore. Beaches have clearer water than the rest of the Mississippi gulf coast. We saw dolphins and mantarays. Lovely weather that day. Also the snack shop is reasonably priced.
Not a place for young kids, long day trip.

Amazing displays. A multitude of historical artifacts were on display. Including a portion of the Berlin Wall 10/12ft tall and 5 feet wide, graffiti and rust! Amazing!
Egyptian, Oriental, cowboys, wars, and celebrities.

Max stay is 2 weeks. $35 a night. Kind staff. Not willing to bend the rules. Larger trailers must stay without septic hook up.
If you stay with all the other trailers, you're piled in like sardines. 2 trailers per spot.

Great place to take a walk and see some local statues/memorials. I took the kids and they had a blast!
There are homeless that live under the bridges along the river. Be aware of your surroundings.

Many tigers here. A few lions and bears. The wolves are up close too!
The only downfalls are the gravel (not good for strollers) and porta potties.
It was a fun experience, the animals were active.
Fun place to explore. A bit pricey for the experience. Bathrooms are in the parking lot, the hike is about a mile and a half loop away from the parking lot. Plan accordingly with small children.
Overpriced, over regulated. None of the other parents hopped with their kids. The kids all wanted my attention. One little boy followed me around making it unsafe for me to hop.

$72 for 5 people, 3 of which are under 6.
Good variety of animals for the size of the zoo.
They now have timeshare salesmen trying to sell  while you are enjoying the zoo.

Very crowded. Maybe expected on a hot summer day.
A multitude of exhibits. All age groups can enjoy.
Clean, many staff members, and hand sanitizer conviently located!

The zoo is well maintained. Zookeepers are well informed about the animals.
We have a membership and go frequently. We recommend it our friends with small children.
This park is huge and amazing. Very beautiful and well maintained. We went to the botanical gardens inside the city park, it was wonderful too.
I've been going to this park for years. Always clean and maintained. There are bathroom stall without doors over by the playground.
Great program, buy a membership if you plan on coming more than once. Lions, tigers, and bears! Great elephant exhibit too!
We walked along the river and stopped in the ice cream and chocolate store. I highly recommend this as a bucket list item.
Fun place for the kids to play. Beach and pier are clean. Playground it updated. Wood chips are under the play equipment.

Meticulously maintained and extremely well architected. Amazing gardens with lots of great views, events, gift store, and Cafe. Other reviews mentioned a boat ride, but I did not get that option. House and garden it just garden tour options. Just garden with plenty of contemplative stops took me 2.5 hours, 3 hours with lunch from the cafe. One hot entree option or sandwiches from cafe.

Parents: In mid March there were a bunch of families there taking spring photos in fancy clothes. Be warned, there is an exit through the gift shop with lots of stuff for kids to want.

Such an interesting place. The sands with captive most people, it's just such a contrast to the surrounding dessert. Nature lovers with enjoy the information and movie at the visitors center.

Definitely buy a sled at the gift shop and sled down the dunes. You can return the sled to the gift shop after to recover some of the cost and not have to take it home. As of July 2018, it was $18.99 to buy a new sled, $10 to buy a used one, and you could return a sled and get $5 back. The was might help, we skipped that and didn't go quite as fast.

Such an awesome place! Tons of up sells, but I like the classic exhibit hall pass with the electricity/lightning show. If you have older kids or adults the Omni theater, 4D theater, simulator or planetarium are good add ons.

Parents: Be warned that the gift store is huge and awesome. You will spend more money than you want if you go in.

EV Drivers: Charging stations on the forth floor are free until your car is charged. After that, it's $5/hour if you don't move your car.

Beautiful State Park with well maintained trails. Blazes are well marked and the trail map online is accurate. 3.7 Mile Walk around the lake is beautiful, with mild gains in elevation and really nice scenery. Very few people were out while we were on the trail, passes two joggers and a dog walker.

Parents: Nice place for a walk with kiddos. There are also 2 playgrounds that we saw and a disc golf course.

EV drivers: No charging available.

Tiny museum but super well done. Worth more than the $6 admission fee. Staff was also super friendly. Store was well organized with plenty of different things to choose from.

Parents: There is enough to keep kids, even the small fry entertained. Our 3 year old liked all the taxidermy animals, the kids room, the bees, the"lift the flap", the beavers, and the florescent minerals cave.

EV drivers: No charger anywhere nearby.

Beach side amusement park. Staff was friendly and helpful, but it's kind of dirty and a little less nice looking (chain link fence and roll down shutters). Kids will go through more tickets than you expect. They'll also want to play more rip off games than possible and not win something. That's normal for arcades and amusement parks, but at least they have unlimited passes if you want them.

Beautiful park with a little bit of everything. Playground, pool, ball field, carousel and tree lined walking area.

EV drivers: Two level 2 chargers are in the parking area near the ball field. Clipper Creek style, free, and both in good repair at the time of this post. Both chargers occupied in an evening in June while baseball games were going on.

Beautiful place! Shops and restaurants along the boardwalk with dock and marinas to walk along. We were there at night and you could see all the little fish swimming up to the lights for the dock. It was interesting to see. It looked like during the day there were pontoon boat, stand up and paddle board, and kayak rentals available.

Such a beautiful place! Great view, nice short holes, historical references, art gallery, great programs, nice restaurant, and nice gift store. In the summer, great patio for dinner overlooking the great view.

Parents: Nice short hikes for kids, couple of gift store options, I might skip the art areas unless your kids are patient.

I've driven by this a million times and never stopped. So glad we did today! It's a beautiful bog with well maintained walkways. Quick trip too, perfect with non-toddler kids because it's quick and they're past the tripping/taking off the board walk age.

Surprisingly good sanctuary for big cats. I was expecting a bad roadside zoo when we drove in, but the animals were well cared for, the staff really cared, and there was good educational information at every single animal enclosure.

Awesome place to visit with kiddos. Our 2 year old enjoyed the whole thing. I was a little disappointed that you're not supposed to go on the sculptures in the lawn area; they are too enticing to little ones.
Beautiful covered bridge! Nice beach area when the water is low enough, parking area right next to the bridge for park 'n ride. Drive over bridge, one car at a time so proceed with caution!
Great museum that emphasized for me not to forget the attrocities of the past lest we repeat them. I was moved to tears throughout the exhibits, so come prepared for strong emotions.
Tiny trail with over 2000 petroglyphs. Really short hike in and out to see them, maybe a half mile each direction. Tiny bit of elevation gain, maybe 100' up a short rocky outcrop.
Nice park with lots of events in the summer. If there is no event, there's a homeless problem in Manchester and they are often here, which makes some people uncomfortable.
Nice park near the river. Ralph Baer (father of videogames) bench. Close to Cotton restaurant and Waterworks cafe. Tons of students often here because it's near SNHU.
Beautiful beach. Must be a town resident or guest of town resident at times it is staffed. Playground and bathrooms it port a potty available in summer.
Great beach for the kids with outside showers, playground, and bathrooms. At the end of the pier is a great restaurant with burgers, fries and shakes.
Beautiful location! My daughter loved the exhibit on wildlife and the bronze bear was a huge hit! Perfect place to take off for a nice hike from too!
So cool! So many neat planes and helicopters to look at! We arrived there after closing, but before sunset and got to walk around and see everything.
Beautiful little park with a nice bandstand for music performances. They also setup a movie screen and show movies in the summer.
Beautiful park with water features. Daffodil fest in spring and holiday lights in December are especially great times to visit.
Beautiful art, but not great for a 1 year old. Some of the staff was really good with a little kid, some not so much.
So cool to see all the animals up close! Even saw a bald eagle that wasn't part of the exhibits!

One of my absolute favorites that I've discovered so far. It's almost a hidden gem. I came up to visit a friend from Mobile, Alabama and while she was working she had made a list of state parks around the area, she knew I loved to be outside and explore. This was one of the parks she suggested, so I took a chance and went and I have to say I'm glad to have discovered this breathtaking park. The parking can be a little tricky if you don't get there early but it almost seems like this is a hidden park in the middle of town. The Falls is an easy hike to get to and the trails are pretty good to take on the other side. Let me say the falls are breathtaking, and the fact that you can actually get into and under the waterfall is even better. There is an old Mill that you can see the parts still resting on the ground. I ended up staying all day while my friend was at work. It's that peaceful, the best part is it was also my birthday that weekend which made it even more special. I ended up going back a second time before leaving to head back to Alabama and getting in the Waterfall. I would be back in a heartbeat! Can't say enough about this beautiful hidden gem.

This place, what can I say? Stunning doesn't even begin to describe it. Went for my first time over Memorial Day weekend and it was absolutely astounding with breathtaking views. You really feel like you step back in time. The waterfalls and everything are superb. Make sure you book a glow worm or dismalites tour. You'll thank yourself. If you love nature and truly outdoors you definitely will get a calming sense when roaming around. Not quite sure why I see  a lot of negative feedback, What did you expect a 5 star hotel? It's nature it's supposed to wild and untamed. So yeah bridges will be out and some things not kept up. I get it but then again I like to enjoy the beauty that surrounds me and not​ be tethered into technology. The staff was super helpful and knowledgeable. I was happy to pay a fee to get in, just keeps the riff raffs  away and not trash the place, the grounds were really clean. Really impressed says people stay around 2.5 hrs. Well we stayed all day it's just that great. Will definitely be back.

Love, Love, Love this place. I can't say enough. Good for a short or you can even make this an all day hike. It interconnects with the beaches as well. The Sanctuary always boasts a swamp, a lake and a wetlands. It's a self sustaining ecosystem in it's own. Various types of birds inhabit this system hence the name. It's a good getaway if you're just wanting to be alone or with some friends. It's also tucked in on the beautiful Dauphin Island. Millions of birds call this place home. Also the hiking trails aren't too bad as they can lead you out on to the beaches of Dauphin Island. The fact that it is so close to where I live makes it even better as it is just a short drive. The trails aren't too difficult as they all interweave and run together.  There is so much to see that a lot of people take their time with the beautiful views.  The lake has a pier you can go out on and view Gators, and turtles as well. Just overall a great place to go and forget your troubles and view a little paradise.

Absolutely love this place. I hadn't been in awhile and decided to go for a Sunday Funday as I love, love, love Dauphin Island. The Estuarium is small but packs a fair amount for the size of it. Has three main tanks offering all kinds of insight to the fish varieties surrounding our area. Also has a bunch of mini tanks with all different kinds of other sea creatures from an Octopus to Lionfish to the bizarre like a frogfish. They even have hands on exhibits  where you can physically touch horseshoe crabs and other little creatures. They even have a tank outside that has a couple different varieties of Stingrays! Another note is that if you plan if right you can watch live feedings of all the big tanks and stingrays. This place is very insightful to our waters that surround our area and offers a glimpse of what we might otherwise not see. Everyone should see this place at least once. One of the many things to do on the Island.

Finally got to check this place out. We stopped on our way back from Huntsville,Al because we heard about a waterfall that you could actually get in. We had been on our own waterfall tour and decided to stop. The hike to the falls is pretty interesting being that if you want to get to it quick you scale down almost vertically and it's almost not well marked if you aren't looking. A little challenging to some newbies but the reward in the end is worth it. Definitely would come back to check out everything else. The waterfall is beautiful and cold which is good because you'll work up a sweat getting to it. Lovely little place but can get a little crowded over the holidays. Definitely would recommend coming during the week. But Peavine Falls is definitely beautiful and will be back to explore more of this State park

Loved it, an absolutely stellar trip if I may say so myself, we were in town from a fossil hunt and came across things to do in Tupelo and this was #1 so we decided to see, and let me tell you, glad we did such a great place, make sure you do the ViP tour it's $10 and you can get super close rather than stuck in  a bus viewing from a distance it makes the experience that much better, I never thought I'd be face to face with  1,000 + lb bison but here I am, what an amazing experience to be in the presence of these majestic creatures. Anthony our tour guide was top notch when telling us about the animals. The whole place was great and I would definitely recommend trying this place at least once. I'm forever grateful to get to have an experience like this instead of just seeing them on programs and in pictures.

I wouldn't necessarily call it a water park. It's an old Gris Mill that is still standing and flows into the river.  Since having the mill it created one of the prettiest waterfalls I've seen. Especially for Mississippi, actually it's pretty awesome to see a waterfall in Mississippi. There's really no where to swim I guess if you wanna swim in the river you can, but that being said it's really awesome that you can climb up the Waterfall giving you a very unique experience. Also I if I can get into a Waterfall you best bet that I'm gonna get in one. We drove from Mobile, Alabama to see this and it was definitely worth it. Also has some hiking trails which will be fun next time we come. Truly a unique experience.

Absolutely loved this falls. You can drive up to it which makes it unique as many you encounter don't really offer that. That aside when first driving up the falls literally took my breath away, starts out at the dam which is a really nice size with water flowing aplenty. Then flows down to what is a 100ft+ drop into the canyon. It is a beautiful sight to behold. I took someone who had never really seen a waterfall before and she absolutely loved it. The Canyon wall was amazing as we actually got to see someone repelling down the side which was nice. All in all would definitely go back. You can also kayak and swim at the top which is kinda nice. Really clean trail and park. Definitely would recommend.

I love this place, ever since I "discovered"  it last year in the blistering heat. It was beautiful big Lilly ponds, flowers all around a mini "waterfall" to wildflowers and turtles, and koi galore there is so much to see. I recently went again and took my camera now the snakes are out saw a 4ft long ratsnake and a couple black racers, It really is a great place to get away for a bit and just keep to yourself and think. I just wish it was more kept up. It desperately needs a cut and weeding and it has so much potential, and to think it's right here in Mobile. Wish I could actually help out with it. Later in Spring more wild flowers will be blooming and I will keep coming back.

I came to this place with my brother and friends. We came out for the day. This place is beautiful but can get crowded. We hiked and found a cold water hole that was undisturbed. The only downside​ is we came up there to hike and explore when the drought hit and there was an extreme burn ban going on. Other than that it was still a memorable hike and experience. Would definitely come back when we could.

*Edit Came back this past weekend to check out Waterfalls and since we've been having a lot of rain lately I finally got to see the Canyon flowing and flowing quite well. It's is just as beautiful filled as is just Rock bed to go around and hike on.

We've had this one on our Radar for some time now. We finally decided to see it as we were up that way and it was in our path the way back.  It's a little hike and if you know where you're going it's a breeze. It's not a long hike just kinda hidden and you could get turned around. Once to the falls which it takes you to the top it's breathtaking. To get down is a little tricky, don't go to the left over the stream go to the right and shimmy down the mountain. Trust me it's worth it. It just happen to be frozen when we went. It's beautiful

Absolutely beautiful place, there is a .5 mile boardwalk hike that takes you over a Pitcher Plant bog that holds some endangered white tops, infact this place has several species of carnivorous plants that call it home. Ending with a spectacular view of the bay.There is also a 7.2 mile hike called the Perdido Bay Trail that goes to the bay or beach crossing over bogs and such. Most of it was underwater from all the rains from the week but it was a beautiful hike nonetheless. Highly recommend getting out and exploring this place.

Nice well kept in Mississippi. This refuge is actually quite lovely. Small in comparison to others but what it lacks, makes up for in scenery. Nice little loop takes you through wild flowers and a pitcher plant bog, various birds and a creek down on the other side of it. Get out and experience it through the various seasons. It's well worth it. Not only does it have pitcher plants but several other kinds of carnivorous plants reside here!

Beautiful rock formation that was carved out by the sea thousands of years ago. It's the longest natural bridge East of the Rockies. Nature is amazing be sure to see this when you can when in this area, also take the 1 mile nature hike after visiting the bridge. We got there around low light but it still was amazing to see. Ohh and at the end of the hike flows an amazingly beautiful cascade.

This is a great place. Cheaha included it's a great day or couple of days spent exploring there are a couple of Waterfalls here that we went to see. If you're a waterfall Hunter Salt Creek Falls is definitely one to see it is amazing. If you're looking for hiking there is plenty but some of the trails aren't marked well at all so you need to watch out.aside from that it's fun to go explore

I have to say. I haven't been to this park since I was a little kid. I was too young to appreciate the beauty it really has if you stop and look at it, of course it's changed since I was little but it was nice to go an explore and walk Thoroughly enjoyed our visit here and you can really see the beauty in the pics. Definitely a different perspective when older, will be back

Loved it. Such a beautiful spring. And cold all year round. Beautiful to spend the day at. Little hikes and it only costs a little to get in, very clean, looks like something out of a movie. Found this after going to Falling Waters State Park. Florida has some great natural areas. Just wanted to make a day out of it and I'm glad we stopped here.

Amazing place. It's actually two places managed by 1.  Over 12 different species of carnivorous plants dwell in this Preserve. This place is absolutely beautiful, so much fun to find the different types of plants there's so much to see. You can plan on staying for a good chunk of the day. There is a 4 mile loop that you can take.

Beautiful overlook with stunning views. Excellent stop after seeing Graces High Falls. Peaceful yet unrefined. If you truly want to see the presence of nature stop here and bask in the glory of the Canyon, each direction overs massively stunning views. They don't call it Alabama the Beautiful for nothing.

Beautiful covered bridge in the area of Blountsville, Al. Didn't get to make it to the other 2 but if your in the area, make sure you do this tour then stop by the falls of Mardis Mills. This town is awesome and the history of these bridges is astounding to see the craftsmanship of how it was constructed.

Very beautiful spot. Senic spots all the way through. Went on a hike with a local club. Enjoyed every minute of the hike and senery. Highly suggest you do a hike here if not to just go see the wonders Alabama has.

I'm from Mobile Alabama an it was my first time visiting the park. Must say so beautiful and we'll placed and the crowd Interaction was amazing. Company was not too bad either. Not a bad seat in the house at all.
Very clean park. Really beautiful nature. We came through to find Waterfalls for the weekend and it did not disappoint. Found 4 this past weekend. Definitely beautiful parks up in North Alabama.
Man this place is awesome and I happened to find Pitcher plants along the the road where I didn't think there would be, definitely give this place a go and explore where you can.
Really awesome to see. Nature provides so much. All you need to do is respect it. A beautiful spot indeed.

The grounds are well preserved and the general history of Andrew Jackson is well-known presented but a lot of the finer details are swept under the rug. Issues like slavery are not represented nor the atrocities of the Jackson presidency. The Trail of Tears for example. It's no wonder the Hermitage hires a visible security force to protect the grounds. While gloating of Andrews successes such as the War of 1812 and securing himself as the 7th president of the United States none of his faults (if which there were many) are discussed. Still, for anyone interested in history, this is a worthy trip. Just know there's more to Andrew's story than the white washing presentation on display at the Hermitage.

Expect to spend at least six hours here if you want to see everything Patriot's Point has to offer.  There's such verity in the exhibits and walk through tours.  We experienced our first tour of a Naval submarine (USS Clamagore).  While the air inside was toxic it was an experience worth taking.  The USS Laffey and the USS Yorktown were simply fascinating and Patriot's Point allows unprecedented access to the ships.  We were able to freely explore nearly all decks expect the very bottom deck which was likely contaminated with diesel and corrosion.  Don't forget your camera!

I have toured several museum Battleships throughout the United States and must say the USS North Carolina provides the most accessible tour among them all. While not the largest museum battleship of the rooms accessible to the public there are few that feature barriers to keep you from touching and photographing the various rooms aboard.  Besides the radio room and a few decorated office quarters every room on the tour is open to explore.  Only problem is poor crowd control and parents allowing their children to run free below deck. It's an accident waiting to happen.
