I've been to quite a few aquariums across the country but the South Carolina Aquarium remains my favorite.  This facility has excellent theming throughout.  The staff is helpful and knowledgeable.  No question goes unanswered.  The deep sea ocean tank area gets pretty crowded and tourist might not always behave themselves, but I don't fault the aquarium.  This is an excellent way to a morning and early afternoon in Charleston.

Gift shop was outrageously overpriced.

Full scale replica buildings, a decent museum and historical film and the Polk family cemetery await your arrival at this North Carolina gem of a state park.  There's no visitor fee although there's a donation kiosk which I gladly contributed to.  On site park rangers guide you into the replica buildings spending a good amount of time explaining Polk's earlier 'simple' way of life.  This is an excellent way to kill a hour or two while in the area.

Not a much to see or do at here.  The recreation of the old school house was nice, there as were the grounds – they have a nice statue of Andrew Jackson as an adolescent riding a horse and some walking trails and a small museum.  Not quite worth the $2 per person admission.  The nearby James K Polk birthsite state park in North Carolina does a better job entertaining and educating visitors and there's no fee.

The outdoor gardens were in pretty bad shape, overgrown with weeds and showing obvious signs of neglect.  However the indoor facilities are the complete opposite, however small, features air conditioning, a small cafe, free WiFi and a wide number of species on display well tagged with identification.  The state should consider changing an admission to fund a refurbishment of the outdoor gardens.

The boardwalk was closed for repairs during our visit so we weren't able to experience the main attraction of visitors center but the approach was open and the grounds were stunningly beautiful and covered with hundreds of yellow and orange crickets. The bathrooms here are clean and provide you with an ability to change clothes after a hot sweaty day of adventuring in the Everglades.

Not a whole lot to see here. The mounds themselves are the main attraction and are worth the trip. The park rangers were super friendly and knowledgeable. The museum left a bit to be desired but they offer a historical educational video in the back room. Surprisingly there's nice Indian inspired artwork and jewelry for sale in the gift shop. Admission is $5 per adult.

North Carolina does an excellent job presenting their historical history and the museum at Fort Fisher is no exception. However, there is little history left on the site other than some earthworks built by the Confederacy. We were a bit disappointed after visiting Brunswick State Park to see how little history remained.

Don't let the pictures fool you.  Morningside Natural Preserve is overgrown, full of mosquitoes and the boardwalk amd and bridge is in grave disrepair. It's only a matter of time before someone is injured walking across the bridge.  ⅓ of the boardwalk is submerged in swamp water and another ⅓ is broken apart.

An excellent on site museum details the various events that have taken place on the grounds of Brunswick. We spent about an hour walking through the ghost town and the remnants of the Civil War fort. The continuing archaeological work is present and happening out in the open for the public to see.

I was disappointed to learn the brick foundations visitors see aren't real and the NPS buried what was left of Jamestown in the 1950s to preserve the structures. Besides the muesem with a handful of 1600s artifacts there's nothing genuine about this park. Disappointing!

It's not advertised but you can walk in streets and tour Colonial Williamsburg for free without paying admission to enter the buildings. You'll still be immersed by the surrounding and character actors without paying the extravagant $35 per person admission.

The automated show wasn't working on the night we visited, but the colored lights were on. This fountain display is something Jacksonville should be proud of. Quite stunning and wroth visiting if anyone is staying in the area for the first time.

Unable to enjoy the trail due to the number of swarming insects. Biting mosquitoes and deer flies were relentless while trying to access the trail. Our party turned and ran back to our vehicles. You'll need industrial strength inspect repellent!

Nice place to spend a hour walking along the broadwalk and taking in nature.  During my winter visit I encountered various species of duck and tortoises.  During the summer season when there's more vegetation I'm sure it's even more beautiful.

The bridge is exactly as it was on that faithful day scores of people were attacked on Bloody Sunday. Walk in their foot steps across the bridge, but be careful as the walk way is narrow and people do not drive the posted speed limit.

Permanent library is very bleak. However, the building and its grounds are beautiful. I recommend visiting when a traveling exhibit is on display rather than coming solely for the permanent collection.
Walk among the ruins of the old south, you could easily perform this as a driving tour, in fact I recommend it considering how overgrown most of the landscape has become. Beware of poison Ivy.
Looks fun from the road. Came here to kill some time but found nothing worthwhile. Unless you came here looking for cheap souvenirs or mutilated corpses of marine life drive on by Johns Pass.
The grounds are beautiful, but the price is astronomical.  Everything employee we encountered was friendly and helpful though.  It made for a nice afternoon outting with my mother.
Trails here are overrated, perhaps it's the off season but all the vegetation is all dead however the water features and nearby hydro dam are stunning.
Worth seeing for the historical factor.  However, I can't bring myself to respect this place for the evil it represents.
Nice walking trail around the lake. A bit rugged at times, but you'll totally forgot your inside a metropolitan city.

One of the lesser-known highlights of New York City. Governor's Island is an 8-minute ferry ride (free on the weekends before 12 pm, otherwise $3 for adults) away from the financial district, but a world away in terms of crowds and nature. There are plenty of paths, gardens, a farm, a lavender field, bikes, playgrounds, food stands, lawn chairs, and old-style houses to provide something for the entire family. I highly recommend visiting Governor's Island if you are stopping by the city or a native. It's quite amazing that this natural resource is so close to downtown and the view from the ferry alone is worth the trip! Check out the Earth Matters farm and lavender field on the island if you can. Overall, a great place to spend a weekend and one of the best natural secrets in New York!

An outstanding public destination park in Brooklyn. I'd highly recommend visiting Prospect Park and the surrounding area if you are a tourist or a native. There are plenty of things to see and do in the park - from the botanical gardens to a zoo to a museum, to the main branch of the Brooklyn public library, to just taking a stroll through the park or riding a bike (Citi Bikes are available for rental). Prospect Park is one of the natural highlights of Brooklyn and it's a great asset for the community. I'd recommend taking full advantage of it even if you are just visiting. Also make sure to take a look at the surrounding attractions as you'll be able to find something for everyone in the family to enjoy.

A nice public square, closed to traffic with an incredible selection of stores nearby. There are also a number of subway lines (Q, N, B, D, M, R, W) that go right to the square. It's often busy (except early in the morning) so if you don't like crowds, avoid here, especially in the evenings. There are a few chairs and tables and a little green space where you can temporarily get a nature fix while in the heart of the city. Herald Square is one of the more touristy parts of Manhattan, but it's not as crowded as Times Square.

Incredibly extensive art museum with works that will appeal to everyone. I was expecting to not be that enthralled with only American Art, but was pleasantly surprised by the diversity of works. I would definitely recommend spending a few hours (I spent around 8) at this art museum (which is connected to the National Portrait Gallery). DC is fortunate to have so many great public museums showcasing American culture, and this is one of the best art museums I've visited in DC or around the country.

A stellar art museum in Brooklyn with a wide range of exhibitions for all tastes. This is one of the top attractions in Brooklyn and it's easy to spend an entire day here looking at all the works of art. There is a diverse range of artwork that should appeal to everyone in the family! I highly recommend visiting the Brooklyn museum for both visitors and natives (who can pay whatever they like). Brooklyn is fortunate to have so many wonderful, high-quality cultural institutions.

A great institution showcasing both native Ohio plants and biomedical from around the world. The indoor exhibits show two different climates and the outdoor areas have plenty of diverse trees, shrubs, herbs, flowers, and gardens. During the winter, the Glow holiday exhibit is a wonderful place to bring the family. I would highly recommend for anyone who appreciates gardening or wants to spend a few enjoyable hours strolling through the gardens.

A sort-of-pointless public art installation in the heart of Hudson Yards. It's free to climb up the artwork (a set of stairs) but you do need to reserve a ticket and there can be a long line on the weekend. The surrounding mall is very high-end but the highline (the elevated park) is incredible. The vessel itself serves no purpose and is not a must-see in Manhattan.

A great quiet park in northern Manhattan. The park is generally not overly crowded and is a nice escape from midtown. This is a great place to come for a walk or to enjoy the views. There are also some commercial shops in a fairly quiet neighborhood. In my opinion, definitely worth the subway trip up from lower Manhattan although it's not as grand as Central Park.

A small art exhibition center featuring mostly contemporary work. There is a permanent collection owned by the Art Center as well as changing exhibits. The exhibition spaces are well-designed with a modern aesthetic and plenty of natural lighting. The art might not appeal to everyone, but admission is free and it's worth at least taking a walk around.

A great location to get outdoors in the heart of Manhattan. The arch is impressive and there are spectacular views of the surrounding skyscrapers. This place can get crowded with tourists, but I'd recommend checking out the large, lighted Christmas tree in the winter. Definitely a good location for a quick rest as you make your way through the city.

You either like Modern Art or you don't and if you aren't a fan, it's probably not worth the trip. I found the building itself mildly interesting, but the exhibits were sparse and generally unattractive. I'd recommend going to the other Met locations first and only here is you have the extra time or a deep attachment to Modern Art.

The art museum is an incredible cultural experience. There are hours of free exhibits to explore, and one paid exhibit that changes every few months. I highly recommend the Cleveland Museum of Art even to those not typically into art because there is plenty of variety and pieces that will interest everyone.

A wonderful park to play tennis, walk, run, bike ride, or just enjoy the outdoors. It's located close to Citi Field and the USTA Tennis Center (site of the US Open). New York City is fortunate to have so many quality public spaces! I highly recommend visiting if you are a native or a tourist to New York.

An incredible art museum with great views of Boston harbor. Contemporary art may not appeal to everyone, but if it does appeal to you, then this museum is a can't miss in Boston. The building is also spectacular and the view of the harbor from the fourth floor is well worth the price of admission.

A great park on the Boston harbor. You can visit the museums, take a look around two different ships, or just enjoy the breeze off the sea. This is a wonderful place to walk around or sit and enjoy a book. I recommend the national historic park both for Boston natives and newcomers to the city!

A wonderful outdoor natural parkway on the harbor near downtown Boston. This is a great place to go for a walk and get outside into nature. It's about a mile-and-a-half of continuous parks with occasional art installations. All in all, a nice place to get outside and go for a walk.

Monte Sano State Park is a stellar hiking/running /biking area only a few miles from downtown Huntsville. I thoroughly enjoy getting away to the park on the weekends and there are plenty of trails to keep me coming back. The park is well worth the drive up the mountain.

A nice place to go for a walk, run, or bike ride with paved trails. They're aren't many trails, but the location is beautiful with the lake and forest. If recommend coming here if you like to get outdoors for your exercise.

A nice place to go for a walk along the river in Hartford. I often come to this park when I need a little fresh air and enjoying strolling along the Connecticut. The only downside is the park is not kept very clean.

All of the Cleveland cultural gardens are wonderful places to walk or spend a few minutes thinking or reminiscing. I highly recommend visiting any of the cultural gardens or even taking them all in with a nice walk.

A very impressive performing arts center in Midtown Manhattan. I would definitely recommend visiting here for both natives and tourists. New York is fortunate to have such excellent cultural institutions.

A nice family park in Park Slope. This is a good place to take the kids to play, go for a walk, relax in the outdoors, read a book, or visit the small museum on the grounds. A great community resource!
An impressive gothic style church in the heart of Boston. This place is nice to visit if you are in the area and even if you don't want to attend a service.
An impressive gothic-style church in downtown Boston. This is a nice place to admire even if you are not going for a service.
A good green space in the city. I enjoy being able to walk here and just take a break from the city.

Great tour to directly learn about the Wright family (prior to his departure), his architectural style, preferences and influences for his home and studio. Our docent stayed within the history of his time living in this Oak Park landmark with little bits and pieces about the children and Catherine. We purchased our tickets in the lovely gift shop instead of online. It was a busy Sunday and a gorgeous autumn day, but we had no problems fitting into one of the groups with a wait of about 25 minutes, which allowed us plenty of time to browse. It is also worthwhile to walk around this area taking in all the amazing homes and places of worship. The architecture around the neighborhood is astounding!

Warren was an excellent docent and he gave a wonderful tour. The house is gorgeous inside and out and, of course, so nature inspired by FLW. Loved browsing through the gift shop also - very large with unique items. There is also a cafe and art gallery by the beautiful information center. Lots of walking to the house and back to the parking area. Dress for comfort according to the weather and definitely wear walking shoes. FYI: There are many, many stairs involved in this tour, so take that into consideration. Photography is not allowed inside the house.

A step back in history learning about the Koreshan religious community, which this ground originally was. Follow the signs and read about the people and their lives. It was pretty much a cult following that died out naturally. If you're lucky you'll see the gopher turtles roaming around. The state park also has a campground (appears to be electric and water hookups). Each site, although close together, is separated by trees and shrubbery. There is also a playground, picnic area and kayaking and I believe there's also a boat launch.

Gorgeous Victorian home and gardens. Wear good walking shoes because the gardens go on forever! The house tour is not too long, but very interesting. The Bellingraths had many collectibles (china, silver, Coca Cola bottles) and huge open rooms with lots of windows that were great for viewing the grounds. Mrs. Bellingrath was philanthropic but in a different sort of way when you listen to their story. There is also a nice guft shop and a cafe.

A must see (must hear) when near the Lake Wales area. The grounds and tower are stunning and overlook citrus groves below. Sit and listen to Geert D'Hollander play the carillon bells for 30 minutes. The guy is amazing, and you can meet him and ask questions when he comes out of the tower. There is a nice gift shop and cafe; it's a great place to spend an afternoon. Oh, and the kiddies will love feeding the huge koi fish too.

So much fun meeting Byrd and having her share her life and stories growing up in the Usonian house built for her family. It is definitely worth touring this very uniquely designed Frank Lloyd Wright pod home, which is only one of two built. The home is in the process of restoration but elegant nonetheless. Byrd told us it will be restored to  its originally designed plans.  Visitors may photograph the exterior only.

A part of American history I had been wanting to know more about. Very somber experience but well worth learning about it, which was never taught in history class in the midwest. The survivors were resilient after everything they had been through and rebult their town. Very few of the wealthy owned up to their negligence and simply left, never ro return. The film, flood display and artifacts tell it all.

This is Kankakee County's local children's museum, and if staying in the area with children around ages 2 - 10, they will love all the hands on activities including a castle, grocery store, diner, craft station, and more. While there, also stop at Perry Farm to pet and feed the animals, play in the playground and walk the trails that go down by the river. If you walk near dusk, deer are sometimes out.

This is a great place to bring the kids. They will love watching and touching manta rays and watching how fast they swim at feeding time. Learn all about the habitats of the sea life in the coastal area. Watch the video first and then enjoy the exhibits. It was pretty fascinating, and it only takes maybe one hour to see everything. It has a very nice gift shop too.

Learned a lot about Thomas Edison that I never knew. I enjoyed listening to his recordings on the phonographs. We had very good guides through his birthplace and the museum. The whole complex is definitely worth a visit, and Milan is such a beautiful well preserved town. Did not get to see Percy the peacock though who supposedly roams freely around the area.

Such a beautiful place to wander. Very serene with many paths to choose from. There is even a children's garden and each person may pick and pull up a vegetable of their chosing. Before exploring the outside, read the history of the Dow family inside the building first. The influence of the Dow family resulted in the beautiful city of Midland, Michigan.

If you visit Lakeland, definitely visit Lake Mirror right in the heart of the town. This was our second time walking around Lake Mirror and it is one of the most beautiful areas of downtown Lakeland. There are great photo opportunities, restaurants, a beautiful garden area, exotic bird wildlife (at least to those of us from cold climates) and more.

This beautiful museum was once a private residence and now is part of the University of Chicago campus. It is well worth a visit to tour and learn its history. The Hyde Park area that grew up around it in the early 1900's is such a lovely neighborhood to explore as well from 59th to 53rd Streets.

Second time there in past few years we are camping at Lake Shelbyville). Fun place for our group to gather and enjoy wine.  We ordered food at Tailwinds across the street, which they delivered to the winery for us to enjoy at Niemerg's with our wine. The owner is nice and a character too!

Beautiful well kept state park. We had a pull through site with full hook ups. There are many walking trails and domesticated deer roaming around. It's an easy walk to the water also. There is a store for groceries and many clean rest rooms around the park. Recommend!

I think I loved this house the most of the five we visited in this area of PA. Photography is allowed outside but not inside the house. Our guide was excellent. Visit the very large gift shop and then relax in the ice cream parlor and enjoy the beautiful surroundings.

Nice museum. We were mostly interested in the Annie Oakley exhibit, which was very interesting. Staff very nice. Younger kids may not find enough to hold their attention, but older ones may enjoy the historic items displayed.

Somber experience especially reliving that day through the displays in the Visitors' Center. It's quite a tribute and memorial. Be prepared for tears listening to the sensitive phone calls by the passengers.

Learned so much about Amish life on the tour. Took a guided tour of an Amish house dating back to 1800s and then a bus tour. Both guides were excellent. Made two stops at Amish/Mennonite houses/shops.

Great tour of the historic Victorian Oakleigh House. Our guide was very sweet and seemed to love telling us the history of the different familes that owned the house before it became an historic site.
Great place to camp! It's a beautiful location on the lake and the and the other RVers staying there were very friendly too. I would love to stay again next time we are in the area.
A beautiful day to see the historic lighthouse and beautiful grounds. We couldn't go inside as it closed for the season after Labor Day except for specific upcoming days.
Up the peninsula, not far from Traverse City, MI, is this historic town with specialty shops and the famed Bluebird Restaurant. It is worth the drive to visit the town.
This place is amazing and incredible whether or not you like visiting museums. It is a must see!! So impressive; so much history!
Fun walking the paths, but we didn't see any birds. We did, however, see a small alligator and several turtles in the water.

Great park close to San Diego.   Learn about the arrival of the first Spanish explorers in California.   Visit the lighthouse.  A short drive down to the tide pools and the coastal hiking path.  Great views of San Diego from the visitors center.   Watch navy and commercial ships as they go in and out of port. The conquistador gave a great presentation about the weapons and gear of the Spanish soldiers.

Excellent place for a walk in a primitive canyon.  The rock formations were surprising .  The waterfalls were very nice.  Plenty of birds and moss to look at.  There are stairs to climb but not excessive.   The end of trail needs better markings and the crossing point of the stream should be better  marked.  Overall,  highly recommended for a fun afternoon.

A very good museum well worth a visit.  The Ballantine house is a nicely restored Victorian era home attached to the museum.  A nice assortment of Asian, African, European and American art.  There is a parking lot right next to the museum.  A cafe is being installed.  There is a planetarium also within the building. Great place to spend a day.

Another small museum with a focus on the Revolutionary war.  Lots of info on the battles fought in the Mohawk valley.  Nice exhibits of native American artifacts.  Drive up to the site of the original fort.  Nice view of the river.  Well worth spending a few hours.

The small museum at the visitor center was good.  Take the time to walk up to the house and visit the family cemetery.   The grounds have many interesting exhibits.  The cellars under the house are very good.  Make sure you visit the gardens.

Very nice museum with amazing artwork by Thomas Cole.  Did the self guided tour.  Docents were very helpful answering questions.  Get up close to several paintings.  Photography is allowed.   Tour the grounds and garden.  Close to Olana.

Great park with a variety of trails with varying degrees of difficulty.  Picnic shelters and rv parking available.  You can climb down to the falls if you are up to the challenge or view it from the paved walkway at street level.

A really impressive collection.  Plan on spending the entire day exploring the galleries.  Nicely annotated and displayed.   The cafe was a nice place for a light meal.  We will definitely need to visit again.

Great museum with authentic period farm houses from the US, Germany,  Ireland and England.   Knowledgeable staff to talk about farm life in the 18th and 19th century.  Sheep shearing was interesting to watch.

Great historic home of the Rockefeller family.  The lower level art gallery is great.  The gardens are very nice in the spring and summer.  A great collection of carriages and autos in the coach barn.
Excellent small museum with a variety of exhibits related to life on the Hudson river.   Many ship models, photos and boats to view.  Good info on the Erie canal and industry along the river.
Historic lighthouse with a grest view from the top.  Plenty of free parking.  There is a small museum of local history/wildlife on site.  Clean restrooms and a good size beach for walking.
Interesting museum of modern art.  There are artist cards to provide additional background on the installations.  Photography is allowed in most areas.  Nice garden,  bookstore and cafe.
The outside of the building is more interesting than the contents of the museum.  Reproduction pre-Columbian art and Egyptian mummies without real mummies.  A 30 minute museum.
Great historic mission ruins.  Wonderful gardens.  Make sure you visit the new basilica outside grounds of the old mission.  Nice little town to explore and catch a good meal.
A good tour of the old state house.  Interesting history facts.   The room of curiosities was a surprise.  The basement had exhibits about Connecticut industry and history.
Great museum.  Good display of the Fremont Indian village life.  Make sure you visit the outdoor petroglyphs near the visitor's center.  Good shop with books, pottery etc.
Great historic house.  The Halloween themed night time tour was fun.  Make sure you go back for the regular tour.  Great views of the river and Tappen Zee bridge.
Great museum with a range of displays related to the early settling of Utah.  Outdoor exhibits of houses, farming and industry.  Good place to spend a few hours.
A bit of early colonial history.  The Mayflower was away undergoing maintenance during our visit.   Good assortment of shops and restaurants.
Great small park to walk around.  The waterfall was nice and the paths were easy to follow.  The train ride is a kid and adult favorite.
Another revolutionary war site with an interesting history.  Self guided tour of the grounds.  House tours available on the weekend.
Went to the Great Jack O' Lantern Blaze.  Really great displays.  Good assortment of snacks.  Great place to bring kids at night.
Nice 1.5 hour cruise on the Hudson.  Bring a jacket because it does get chilly.  There were a few eagles roosting in the trees.
A wonderful piece of Americana.   If you are a fan of Twain, then you really should visit the house and museum.

Normally, I'm quite sure I would have given this place five stars.  They have a great selection of buildings, and I love historical buildings and culture.  However...

In an entire morning wandering here among the (some) original, (some) restored, and some replicated old historical buildings,  all the buildings were closed.  Understandable amid a pandemic. We could see in windows on a few buildings.  At least they had the park open.  Thank You!  But, on the 40 acre site, which normally (non-covid) has volunteer re-enactor interpretors, there was one map sign and a total of 6 info signs.  All these were at the Ft Howard site, we're one of the original buildings, dating from the 1830s, is the oldest standing military hospital in the country.  A few other buildings had plaques identifying them, but no background information.  In the downstairs of the guardhouse was a one room display room about the fort too.
I believe that it would probably take one employee or volunteer only a week to create,  print, laminate, and post some information signs around the park.  It would add so much to the education, experience, and quite possibly donations!  Oh yes, there was also a sign not to disturb the chickens and one small map posted on the bathroom door to the women's restroom.  However, no one saw it because the other sign on the door was easy to read from a distance and said "closed".

Wonderful tour of the Victorian living village by Mr Ed, our very enthusiastic and animated guide.  He was having fun sharing and we were too.  Lasted 1 1/2 hours!  Great info!  I can't imagine trying to do the tour in just an hour.  He gave us info outside, socially distancing, then we all put on masks to go inside to look around.  Still plenty of distancing because there were only 10.  The museum of Rockford history was also a 5 star, very spacious, thorough, and well laid out.  However, only 1 star for the museum staff!  I was disappointed at the hypocrisy of the mask policy.  Perhaps it was just the blatant disregard of the maintenance man who spent 20 minutes when we entered with no mask.  When I said something to him, he ignored it.  So I said something to the desk clerk.  She pulled down her mask in order to reply (!!) that he didn't have to keep it on because he was drinking coffee!  Wow!  He should have gone to the break room.  15 minutes later, I returned to use the restroom.  He was still standing in the lobby with no mask, talking to visitors, (who did have masks.)  Then later we saw him inside again twice with no mask doing other tasks.  The same guy drove his smelly noisy cart right through Mr Ed's tour group not once but twice.

Lovely little lakeside public park with some nice amenities!  Clean rest rooms with baby changing areas, soap!!, hand dryers, drinking fountains. Outdoor showers, small sandy beach with wading area, swimming area, clear water, swimming dock, fishing dock, boardwalks, lily pad area for bird watching, bike racks, picnic tables, covered pavilion, shade trees, grassy areas, kids playgrounds (one near the decent size parking lot, one near the beach), and free use of life jackets for the kids. Posted hours are conflicting: one sign says closes at dusk, one says 9:30.

Closed Monday - Wednesday.  Only the gift shop and craft shops are openThur -Sun 10-4.   House tours will not resume this year!  Sad!  And interestingly hypocritical that this, as well as several of the other Blue Ridge Parkway visitor centers open the gift shops, but not the exhibits.  Is the covid null and void in gift shops?  Sadly, $$$ talks.  This building has been in bad need of repair for a long time.  Wood is rotting.  Paint is peeling.  Never seen anything like this.  I would not waste time stopping here.

What a gem hidden not far off the road along the MS River in SE MN. The mill is 160+ years old and houses a fabulous museum as well as a working interior. 22' water wheel was rebuilt, along with much of the wooden interior, but they have all the working parts...working and many more period items on display. Well worth the short side trip and $5 donation. The volunteer when we visited, Vic, was full of info and very helpful. 15 minute video too.

If I could give 10 stars, I would. This is an amazing place with such incredible energy. Thousands of people, doing everything from walking and jogging to partners yoga, drum circles, and swimming. People are picnicing, sitting in hammocks, biking, rollerblading, playing frisbee and soccer. Two swimming areas offer both high and low diving boards. Ample parking up the hill in the main park away from the lake

Wonderful wood dance floor!  We attended for a dance weekend. The facility is dated, but well maintained and a great place to dance. They have really taken food care of the floor. Surrounding area is interesting. Neighbor doesn’t like the place, as he seems to think that those of is who come with RVs are adding to his homeless problem in the adjacent park.

Wonderful forested park with plentiful trails, both a paved one that circumnavigates the entire park and several gravel trails that criss cross the area. Don’t miss the totem pole just up the trail from the visitor center. Plenty of parking around, as well as ebikes waiting to be used.

A really well done museum marks the site of the 1969 Woodstock concert. The original outside area, plus a small monument/marker are still here. A huge new outdoor performance theater where current concerts are held is part of the not-for-profit venue, as is an indoor events hall.

You can see these through the window of the shop, which is only open Thursday-Sat (Oct).  Great story about how the lady used the needles to actually knit, and also sat on the edge of the giant rocking chair once to knit... incredible, since they weigh 25 pounds each!

Beautiful pedestrian bridge across the Deerfield River. Multiple flower, shrubs, trees, and vines adorn the sides of this narrow bridge. Very picturesque. Visit the pot holes nearby. Worth a visit if you are in the area, but I wouldn't drive out of the way for either.

Beautiful park in the center of Denver bordered by the CO State Capitol and the US Mint, filled with gorgeous big fountains, Amphitheaters, gardens, statues and walkways. The homeless are a big problem though. They can be intimidating when there are so many.
likes: Facilities & Services: Fountains, amphitheaters, gardens, statues, walkways

reviews_attraction.text: Adorable big fountain lined with 12 statue “heads” depicting the 12 years of the Chinese zodiac. Same heads as line the pond at the Palace in Vienna Austria. Never seen them like that anywhere else, but they are identical.

Good place to stop for a couple hours.  For the hikers, the TVA has made it very comfortable with lovely bathrooms and tent sites nearby. The Visitors Center has some nice displays and videos. Good views from the dam.

Amazingly beautiful, with adorable garden decorations literally everywhere.  Lovely lights at night.  Cared for by a group of volunteers, but they have a donation box near the shed...help them out.  Definitely visit!

One of the best science centers that we have visited, and we have a membership that gives us access all over the country. This center is well supplied with cool stuff, and extremely well laid out. A must!
Nicely restored, with good signage to explain the history. It appeared to be open to the public, just not when we were there in the middle of a Friday, is there was a rope across the gangplank.
Great spot for a nice walk or photos. Free!  If it were a garden where a fee was charged, I would give it only 3 stars... bit just ok, nothing special except the incredible stairway waterfall.
Was closed in September...too bad because the weather was warm and kids could have enjoyed wading in it. Don't know if you are ever allowed to wade though. Cute frog statues.
This is a nice little Park, with a marina that offers Lake tours, a visitor center, sports fields, and a small Garden Walk. They do not allow overnight parking.
Currently reconstruction on the quarry parking lot. Fort is an earthen place with a couple cannons, but ample parking and a lovely picnic pavilion.
Nice place to stop for a quick visit. Lovely 300year old mission, located a couple minutes drive off the highway 10 miles south of Tucson.
Quit interesting. An elevator takes you down 20 stories to view the largest ocean cave in the US and one of the largest in the world.
Nice gardens but small. The pond and brook water was nasty. Can hardly see the koi. Good senior and student discounts, $4.
dislikes: Poor water quality in pond and brook

reviews_attraction.text: Scenic overlook is OK, falls are good. Ample parking. Clean restrooms. Hike down to view falls is steep coming back out.

This ice bar is actually pretty cool.  They charge cover, but that's really just a rental fee for the coat/gloves.  The inside of the place isn't huge, but they have three different sections of the bar, along with plenty of seating.  There are neat sculptures and decorations to enjoy, so you won't get bored.  Because it's super cold in there, you probably won't want to stay more than an hour.  Drinks are also pretty expensive, but they're strong.  Go there at least once. It wasn't crowded at all when we went (Feb 2019), but I can see the wait being very long in the summer.  ALSO check the website or call to make sure you won't get bumped due to an 'private event'.  Would go again.

This is a nice little hiking trail.  An average American will have no issues with these trails.  The trail head is right by the parking lot, and has a small park for kids to play at before/after the hike.

There are a few different trial options.  The trails also intersect, so there are several combinations for different hikes.  The trails range from about 1.54 mi, up to more than 5mi depending on how you connect them.  See the map on the website.  The terrain is easy, but does have some large rocks to step over.

There are plenty of up/down steep grades, but nothing the average human and/or dog can't do.  These trails are dog friendly, but not stroller friendly.  Would go again.

Importance of this bell aside, the building complex is well organized.  The staff inside the bell building (mostly security at the metal detectors) is nice and quick.  There's plenty of information about the bell inside as you make your way towards it.

If you don't want to wait in line (or prefer to not go through security), you can get a great look at the bell through the outside window near the exit of the building.

Note that going inside is free, but you can't ring the bell.  Would go again.

A great place to take your basic stereotype Instagram pictures.  Show how dedicated you are by standing in line for 45 min to pose in front of paint on a wall.

This place is perfectly situated near a few hipster brunch places, so you'll get the maximum impact when posting about your Sunday Funday.  Make sure and hashtag your #AvocadoToast in order to maximize your reactions.

People like you and are impressed by your lifestyle.  May go again.

This is a pretty neat museum.  All of the exhibits are well maintained, well guarded, and well organized.  You'll find lots of the typical 'modern art' pieces, as well as some that are more accessible to non-art people.  There area  few pieces that are interactive, but most things are 'do not touch'.

Although most of the items are paintings, there are also tons of sculptures, and entire rooms on display.  Would go again.

This is a typical beach house museum, but with cats.  The grounds are very well maintained, and the staff is knowledgeable and friendly.  They charge for entry, but the tours are included.  The cats are friendly, and you can pet/hold them if they want.

The house seems to be left as is, and has lots of cool decorations from when it was lived in.  It's worth visiting if you're familiar with the author.
Would go again.

This is probably the most famous place in town. It's crowded,  and it will annoy you. It's very well laid out with signs and lines. If you're lucky,  you might see "lanyard man" taking pictures (for a price) and helping to organize the chaos.

Don't be a jerk and cut in line. Wait your turn or come back at 2am when it's empty.

Pro tip: The back of the sign makes for a cool and unique picture as well. Would go again.

yep, it's about what all the pictures make it out to be.  This place has a nice sized parking lot (tons of room for bikes/scooters), but does require a 5 min walk down stairs to access.  These stairs are in great shape, and easy to navigate.  It's really not bad at all.  This place is great for hanging out on the beach and people watching.  It also has a great view of the windmills offshore.  Would go again.

I'm not sure what makes this park "International", but it is a neat area.  It's the location of several yearly events in Huntsville.  They redid the pond in 2018.

There are several good restaurants within a 5-10min walk.  The Von Braun center is alway within a short walk.

They recently started putting car ads in the park, which is pretty lame.
Hopefully they will keep the park ad-free.  Would go again.

Yes, this is the pineapple fountain park.  Come here and Instagram your trip, or dip your feet in for good luck or whatever.  The park is well maintained, the fountain is large and neat.  I'm not really sure about the origin or purpose of the fountain, but it's kind of cool.

On busy days you may find a lemonade and water vendor.  It's right by the beach, but it's not a nice sandy beach.  Would go again.

This is a nickname of Broadway street.  There are dozens of bars, most of which have live music.  The drinks aren't cheap (around $8-$12).  Some of the bars have food.  Some of them are full restaurants.

There's also a very nice candy and ice cream shop in the middle of the strip.  The river is all the way at the end, and the stadium is walking distance across the bridge.  Would go again.

This is a short section of town with 5-6 houses that are painted different colors.  It's a photo opportunity that is popular with some tourists.  The houses are indeed different colors, and this is noteworthy.

If you're wondering where the best place to stand while photographing these houses, simply look for the largest group of millennials in the immediate area.  May go again.

The waterfall is about a 20 min hike (easy, but fun) from the trail head. The trails are nicely maintained. There's plenty of tree cover so it's not hot at all in the summer.

The water fall itself is surprisingly tall. It's actually pretty cool. There's a stairway to the bottom, but it was out of order in the summer of 2018 (and looks permanently closed). Would go again.

visited summer 2019

Yes this is the park with all the cannons.  Yes they're real cannons and cannon balls.  Yes you can climb on them.  There are plenty of information signs to give you more info.  The park is full of trees that provide nice shade in the summer.

The park is surrounded by the beach on one side, and old southern houses on the other.  Would go again.

This is a very well organized shopping and eating outdoor mall.  Most of the stuff is focused around kid activities.  You'll find most of the Disney store, and simple food stands, but there's also a few nice restaurants and tons of bars.  Everything was clean and staff was friendly.  This place is huge so be prepared to walk outside for a few hours.  Would go again.

This is a neat little beach park.  It's right on the water, but also a short walk to the town's main street.  There are lots of shops and food places (even a couple of coffee shops) close by.

The park itself seems well maintained and in good order.  Everything was clean.  We didn't interact with any staff, but I'm sure they're just charming.  Would go again.

visited Spring 2021
This is a great little falls that you probably won't be able to find.  It's located behind an old, seemingly abandoned baseball field.  You walk down the gravel road, past a few buildings, and there's the falls.  The better falls is off to a trail to your right, and down the hill at the  bridge.  Good luck finding it.  Would visit again.

The park is pretty nice.  It has a fort (which we didn't visit), but it also has a large beach area.  The sand isn't the best, and probably requires shoes for most people, but the water is fine.  The beach area has tables, grills, and is great for hammocking or picnicking.  There is a cover charge though, since it's in a state park.  Would go again.

This isn't really a park in a traditional sense, but it is a neat area to visit.  There are plenty of sculptures, and great views of downtown from all angles.  This place is located in the middle of downtown and is famous for the "LOVE" sculpture.

Come by and get a picture so you can prove to Instagram that you visited Philly.  Would go again.

This is a pretty typical lake.  The marina we visited was pretty nice with a good restaurant/bar.  All the facilities we visited seemed to be in good working order.  Everyone we met was friendly.  They weren't trashy or snooty.

The lake itself seemed clean and the shores weren't nasty.  No weird smells either.  Would float again.

This is a pretty standard state park.  It's well maintained, a little difficult to navigate, and terrible cell reception.  It has the usual Alabama wild animals, and vegetation.

The main cabin is very nice, and has a great cabin/motel reception area.  They also do an inexpensive breakfast in the same building.  Would go again.

Great and well maintained trails.  Even though the entire mountain is filled with natural springs, the trail was only muddy in a few places.  They had workers out fixing those places as well.  Several neat waterfalls can be seen along with trail.  The trail was easy and had very slight elevation changes.  Would go again.

This complex is huge, and includes Space Camp, the planetarium, as well as the indoor and outdoor exhibits.  Everything is clean, well maintained, and there's always knowledgeable staff around to tell fun stories or explain things.

This place is awesome.  Stop by and check it out.  Will certainly go again.

They definitely make use of the $15 entry fee. The trails are in very good shape. The stairs (of which there are tons) are all well maintained and sturdy. The elevator guy is nice and informative. The gift shop is well stocked. The rock and water falls are cool too. Would go again.

Segway tour review:

The guide was great. The tour included almost all of the grounds and out buildings. The Segways are a pleasure to ride and easy to master (several baby boomers were in the group and had no issues at all). Would go again.

If you're a tourist, pick a different museum (recommend the Nuclear Science Museum). This is a good museum but it's not great compared to other cities. I felt like the exhibits were old (but not in a nostalgic way), some of the displays felt "dumbed down," and I felt like they could have done a lot more with the fossils on display. The "infamous" Bisti Beast is sitting by a wall, barely labeled - I almost missed seeing it. I was told the gems/minerals display was good - it hardly takes up a small room. The redeeming qualities are that the museum does have some unique fossils I have not seen before, and the display on phytosaur fossils was really cool. If I lived here then I'd enjoy going, but I would not recommend it for someone just passing through or visiting - there's way more unique things to do elsewhere.

This museum is a must-see. I haven't thought much about the civil rights era since high school history class. This museum helped me understand much of what I didn't back then. The exhibits are very informative and well-done, with excellent explanations of historical events. I hadn't realized the depths of human cruelty demonstrated during the civil rights era, some of it made me sick to think about. The most important and moving exhibit is that of MLK's motel room with the balcony where he was shot. Words cannot describe the emotions you'll feel when you walk into that room. Going to this museum gave me a lot to think about, this should be your first stop if visiting Memphis.

Need a real museum after looking at UFOs? Come here for some excellent art AND science. The center is free, and has both art and exhibits on Robert Goddard, father of rocketry. Check out a display of his workshop, and go outside to see a sculpture of Goddard getting ready to launch a rocket. I'm not usually an art person, but I really enjoyed the variety of art on display, both by local artists and artists that have done a residency in Roswell in the past. There's art to please everyone's tastes. This was a much more enjoyable and satisfying experience than the UFO museum, and was the highlight of my visit to Roswell.

Ever seen a giant radio dish up close? It's a bit of a drive, but totally worth it to see a... very large array of radio telescopes. The visitor center is small but informative, and there's a short walking tour that will take anywhere from 30-60 minutes. Plenty of information about what the radio telescopes do, how they work, and what they look for. The best part is getting to walk right up to one of the working dishes. If you're lucky, you'll see it move! The staff are really friendly. I'm glad I made the drive out, it's a cool experience!

I wanted so badly to like the Alamo...but I can't. It's the location of THE famous battle that helped to unite Texas and is (supposed to be) the epitome of Texan heritage. But this message of Texas pride gets buried by the absolute touristy atmosphere of the surrounding streets. A few feet away from this famous battle, you can find Ripley's and Madame Tussaud's tourist traps. It minimizes the importance of the events. Compared to many historic locations run by the National Park Service, this doesn't do the Alamo justice.

Amazing views and great hikes. It's not a horribly long detour from 101 or I-5. We went via the western entrance, which offers two ~2hr hikes that can be combined into a loop (~4hr hike). It was the perfect amount of hiking for me. The rock formations are really interesting, not sure how to describe them so you'll have to go and see for yourself. Hiking to the top gives a great view for miles around. Make sure to talk to the park rangers for great hiking tips!

Such a fun place! There are hundreds of mini-experiments demonstrating a countless number of scientific concepts throughout the museum, mostly focused on mathematics and physics, but some chemistry and biology thrown in too. I loved how hands-on the museum was and how it brought back many concepts I haven't thought about since my college physics class. Definitely check out the adults-only evening hours, because it's even more fun (sorry kids)!

So much more than just a "science museum"! The aquarium exhibits were so cool, with all sorts of interesting fishes (including a lungfish). We saw a planetarium show - it's not your average planetarium experience, so check it out. Go up to the roof, enjoy the sun, and see all the ways the building is made more sustainable. The Cal Academy has a great balance of information and fun, not being too flashy or too boring. Highly recommend a visit!

One of the most unique museums I've ever been to. So many cool exhibits, including the life sized prehistoric animal dioramas, the exhibits of fossils with their living relatives for comparison, and so much more! The fossil displays were fascinating and informative, learned a lot about the fishes and other sea creatures found in Kansas, and about Sternberg and other paleontologists. Definitely recommend to anyone passing through the area!

Get in touch with nature, less than an hour from Cleveland. There's a main road that goes from one end of the park to the other but it's not super scenic like some other parks. I'd recommend going to the visitor center for recommendations on scenery or trails. The coolest spots were Brandywine Falls and an overlook near Bridal Veil Falls. My biggest regret is not riding my bike on some of the paths while living nearby.

Come in via the Utah side, it's the only way to drive to the building which contains a 30ft high wall of exposed dinosaur fossils, which I don't think you can see many other places. The rangers are happy to explain the history of the monument and the different fossils present. The surrounding scenery is beautiful and makes for a great drive or hike. 100% worth the visit.

Love this bridge! Sweet view of Margaret Hunt Hill bridge and downtown Dallas, perfect for practicing your photography skills. Bring the kids to play on the playgrounds along the pedestrian bridge. Go wander underneath and get up close with the Trinity River. Super close to Trinity Groves with loads of food options to make any picky eater happy.

It takes a little detour to get here, but it's completely worth it. Start at the visitors center to get some info about the area, then head to the waterfall for some great views. Take a drive along the canyon rim to do some hiking or take in some scenic views. My favorite spot was Eberhart Point. Glad I made the trip!

Amazing park! It's a great stop on your way to Scenic Route 12, with loads of hiking and rock formations both on and off the beaten path. Drive down the scenic drive, take in some amazing views from the top of cliffs, and see some petroglyphs. Hope to go back some day and check out the less accessible areas for sure!

Oak Ridge was built to assist in the Manhattan Project and the WWII effort. It's important to have this positive symbol of freedom and peace nearby, representing the efforts of both Japan and the US to move past their previous actions. It's a cool monument and symbol, make sure to ring the bell while you're here.

Utah has plenty of huge, weird, and unique rock formations, but Kodachrome Basin is in its own category of weirdness. Enjoy a short drive and hike around, looking at the different chimneys and spires. Big fan of the pyramid-looking one. A little bit off the main drive, but worth a detour if you have time.

A pandemic is the perfect time to drive to see a bright-orange abandoned futuristic house on the outskirts of the DFW area. Walk around it, go inside, take your picture, appreciate the possibilities of a future that could be. Then go home (and wash your hands!)

Awesome little hike with amazing views of the town and surrounding area. All the petrified wood is in the middle of the hike but loads of cool specimens to check out. Take one of the trail guides and learn about the plants and fossils along the way.

What's better than a tiny castle built in the 1930s with unparalleled views of the surrounding area in the middle of Kansas? This place is so cool, wander around, enjoy the views, even have a picnic! So glad I stopped by for a visit.

Make the short drive from DFW to see flocks of birds rest/relax on their migratory routes. We saw hundreds of pelicans, turkey vultures, heron, water birds, and even an ibis! Lots of places to hike. Highly recommend a visit.

Awesome bridge with a nearby parking lot to park and walk across the bridge and enjoy the views. There's some paths that allow you to walk along the edge of the gorge and even some benches to sit and enjoy the views.
It's an interesting pop-up experience, but it's pricy ($25/person) and we exhausted all the exhibits within 20 minutes. It made for some good instagram posts to show off, but that's about it.
I've visited twice, each time it's an impressive monument. I'd recommend going to the top, the view is incredible and it's a great place to watch a sunset.
Amazing tide pools full of anemones and sea stars, highly recommend making the walk from Rialto Beach. Just make sure you time it with low tide!
Went here on a gray and windy day but it still made for an amazing walk with great views. A fun and relatively quick stop if you're in the area.

This is definitely worth 3-4 hours of your time to visit bears, deer, wolf, more bears, bison, a cougar, and other critters roaming around in very well maintained, very clean, and nicely landscaped viewing areas. You can drive through much of the area and view the animals from your own vehicle. Be forewarned! You aren't allowed to stop your vehicle in the bear enclosures. Some of the bears are quite friendly and like to play with the rearview mirrors that you have so generously offered as gifts. But overall, it is such a great opportunity to see many of these animals up close and personal. Apart from the drive through exhibit, there are many enclosures with badgers, bobcats, foxes, racoons, otters, raptors, etc. that you can walk to and even see handlers interact with in shows for visitors. Lots of great souvenirs and gifts to take home.  Don't pass this place up!

This is a fun 4D show for all ages. Prepare to laugh, as you are going to see, hear, feel and even smell the bugs. A couple of young children were startled by the surprises but overall it's a good show for kids and adults alike. The audience is seated in semi-divided benches to allow for the 4D special effects to literally be felt. The show itself is within the Tree of Life, which makes the waiting line a fun place for kids to search for animals carved within the walls and the tree itself. Once inside, guests will stand in a crowded, waiting room filled with punny show titles and a ceiling resembling an ant mound. Overall, it's a great show and a nice, relaxing and air conditioned place to rest your feet.

Gorgeous waterfall! The park is perfect for a short stop and it's parking area is adjacent to the main road. The park is fairly small. You can spend some time and follow a trail along the river or even have lunch at one of the picnic tables but if you just want to take in some beautiful scenery, take a few pictures and go, the park is ideal.

Plenty of parking, restrooms, handicapped ramp to observation deck, picnic tables and handicapped accessible tables, open 24 hours, a field to walk the dog, safe for kids, convenient, and no fees. Enjoy!

The trail to the top of Indian Falls is maybe 400 feet from the parking area with no rough terrain. You can follow the trail across the bridge and to the bottom of the falls. Here it is a little steep and rocky ground but it is only another 400 feet from the bridge to the bottom. The trail continues along the river for those looking for a little more to their hike. Behind the waterfall and next to its pool are 2 fairly large caves. Looked like a mountain lion's den to me but I guess they don't inhabit the area.

An ideal place for a quick stop on a long road trip. We were fortunate enough to stop here AT SUNSET! If you are traveling north from the desert, the view is beautiful. If you are traveling south, the view is less spectacular, after seeing Sedona, Flagstaff, the Grand Canyon, etc. It's a matter of perspective. The facilities here are basic. A good place to stretch your legs, take some photos, use fairly clean restrooms and grab a snack from vending machines behind heavy security bars. Lol

If you like (messy, dripping, use a fork) hot dogs, this is the place to eat. The menu is quite diverse for all things hot dog. Expect to wait. We stood in line for about 45 minutes and it wasn't really peak hours. The place is a Hollywood landmark. Its iconic and that's the big draw. Lots of signed photos of celebrities and some memorabilia. Overall, the price was good. It was tough deciding which dog to destroy and well... the food was okay.

Arguably the most disappointing ride at Animal Kingdom. It's a short, relaxing boat ride through Pandora. Basically a dark, cave-like feel with imaginary, bioluminescent plants and animals, along with projections of the Na'vi singing and doing whatever the Na'vi do.

Long story short.. don't wait in line for more than 30 minutes for this, Aside from all the cool things to look at in line, you'll probably be underwhelmed by this ride.

Probably the best ride I've ever been on from any theme park in the world. A 4D experience that will overwhelm your senses and make you feel like you are flying through Pandora on the back of a banshee. Currently, visitors stand in line upwards of 3 hours to experience this ride and I have to say it's worth it. Good luck scoring a Fast Pass but if you don't, get in line and get ready to be amazed.

This is the best place to see Cathedral Rock before sunset. There is a fee, unlike most places to hike and explore in Sedona. The trail is beautiful and there are a lot of places to sit by the creek or go swimming. The park can fill up quickly. Some days you wait in line outside the park until a parking spot is available. Other days its nearly empty.

Good size park with baseball and soccer fields, a pool that is hardly utilized, and disc golf course. Aside from 2 or 3 picnic pavilions, the above mentioned sports fields, a lake that you can't fish or swim in, and a couple of small trails, it just feels like it's missing something. It is underutilized and is lacking in things to do and see.

Who doesn't like an amusement park, on a pier, along the Pacific Coast, with perfect weather nearly everyday of the year? Lots of things to see and do here. The park has the usual rides, games and food. There are a few restaurants and bars, along with a really nice public park and beach. Definitely worth a day tip, if you've never been.

Sadly the waterfall is so far across the canyon that even when the water is flowing from heavy rains, it is not that impressive to the naked eye. This waterfall is actually huge at 130 feet but you'll need good quality camera equipment to take it all in. Parking is not very good. Overall, it was worth a 5-minute stop.

Charming little island campground surrounding the movie set Town of Spectre from the film Big Fish. I found a little goat that was separated from his mama. Little guy tried to leave with me. I was only passing through so I didn't get to do any fishing or camping but it looked amazing.

The starting point for the Grand Canyon Railway. There is a beautifully maintained steam locomotive on display for photos. Take the time to stop here and grab a good meal at one of the local restaurants, visit the train display, and take pictures. This is the heart of Williams, AZ!

Not bad but not amazing. I feel like there were too few animals in this zoo-like area. It's Animal Kingdom! If any place should be displaying an extensive amount of animals it should be this place. Asia has so much more wildlife not being represented here.

I'm rating 5 stars, simply because we got the entire car to ourselves, and because it was Veteran's Day, it was free. We went after midnight and the view was amazing. The ride was 30 minutes long with one rotation. You can see everything from this ride.

If you come to Tombstone, you have to see the reenactment of the shootout at the O.K Corral. The actors did a great job and got the crowd involved. Grab a sarsaparilla or a huckleberry soda and popcorn and enjoy the 20 minute show.

Small park with boat launches, kayak and canoe launch area, boardwalk, observation tower, picnic pavilion, and a playground. No camping, open fires or alcohol allowed. Has bathroom facilities and a good sized, clean parking area.

Enjoyed the ghost tour. An hour was dedicated to telling the history of the theatre/brothel. The other 45 minutes was spent sitting in the dark with our guide trying to speak to spirits that wander the old building.
A nice, relaxing ride that I'm not sure has been updated significantly since it's introduction in the '80s. The line and the ride are indoors and offer a relief on hot days.
Beautiful representation of a truly beautiful place. It made me miss my years in Japan. The food is very good and there are a lot of great souvenirs here.
Gorgeous! The coastal redwoods are indescribable. Many places to stop and explore. Beaches, forests, etc. This is a must see, if passing through the area.
Clean, well maintained park and beach area. The beach area is large and there are a lot of good spots for picnics, parties, and barbecues.
Great show to watch from the street side. Each show is different. It costs nothing to stand along the shore/walkway and watch. A must see!
This was the spot where my girlfriend first saw the Grand Canyon. She cried, because it was too beautiful to put into words.

This was a great park and trail system.  With both climbs, water accessibility, falls, and ponds, it's a rewarding hike.

This not really wheelchair accessible from the main entrance, though you can drive to some of the overlooks.

Many of the trails when we came were waterlogged so waterproof boots if it's been raining will help. So too will hiking sticks. None of the inclines are too long, but they are steep in some places.

The swinging bridge over the stream was a highlight and it is possible to walk out onto the dam.

Allow at least 2 hours.

Coolidge park is a great public park. There is paid parking and a free electric shuttle to get there. You can also arrive by kayak or small water craft.

The park features a carousel, access to shops a board walk, fields to play, and a stage. There's also a climbing wall.

Food trucks, especially for dessert, frequent the place. There are wheelchair accessible restrooms across from the carousel in the pavilion.

The park could use better upkeep. When all the fountains are on, and everything's running smoothly it's more fun.

What a great little museum! There are 7 main galleries and a retail gallery.

The price is very reasonable, $4, and you can learn a lot. There are three main foci: Scottish history, the history of tartans, the interaction of Scots with Native American tribes. All of this is explored through clothing.

The galleries are narrow,  so wheelchair folks will have a tougher time.

They'll also not be able to view the lower galleries.

Still, what a neat place to visit! The store has tartans ties, kilts, books, and whiskey fudge!
likes: Cultural Value (Scottish history, tartans, Scots-Native American interaction)

reviews_attraction.text: This is a first rate museum. The exhibits are well done and the material itself is one of a kind. The ability to climb aboard several of the air planes and to even get rides in the air is really great.  Now, it's worth noting that this is propaganda. There's nothing here that would make the air force look bad. No 'We missed and bombed civilians' or 'This plane was ordered because of extensive bribery' so take some things with a grain of salt. The equipment, however is fascinating.

What a lovely little arboretum! Though less than 5 acres, this is a peaceful series of walks centered around a dammed pond for turtles.

The labeling could be better, but the trails and bridges make the whole experience a pleasure.

One could rush through in twenty minutes, but at a leisurely pace, allow 45 minutes.

There is a plenty of parking and partial  wheelchair accessibility.

Harvard square has been a central American meeting point fir almost 400 years. These days, it's a bit touristy and while clever, the pan handlers are more aggressive.

Don't miss Out Of Town news, which has among the better collections of foreign newspapers and magazines you'll find. The Curious George store and Dewey, Cheetem, abd Howe building are not to be missed.

The Jepson center is a great standard art museum for a city Savannah's size. The highlight of the collection is the American impressionism collection.

Modern Sculpture is also a plus as is a locals section.

The space is taking covid precautions with madks required and timed tickets when busy. There are shields as well.

The space is wheelchair accessible.

This great little park is hilly and great to walk off a delicious lunch from the.    restaurants near by.

Though no more than acres, the park has trails, hills, bridges over streams, and a small playground for kids.

There's a small amount of paved area that's wheelchair accessible. Parking is easy too.

Allow 20 to 30 minutes!

This is a great history center. It is well organized with large section dedicated to native peoples, piracy, cigar history, and Tampa sports.

Allow a good two hours for this location. The staff is friendly and the facility is wheelchair friendly.

You can either pay to park or there's a street car stop close by.

ABG is a lovely garden, and their greenhouse complex is amazing. However, in recent years they've decided that the wonder of Nature is not enough and so they've added other elements which detract from nature.

Still, it's worth visiting and one should allow a couple of hours. Wheelchair accessibility is easy.

Great collections over 3 buildings. See them all. The Telfar building itself us an experience.

The new building has the easiest parking and is most wheelchair accessible. It also has the modern collections and children's sections.

There is a lovely Cafe for lunch.

This is an important visit in Savanah.

Red Top Mountain State Park is a great park with adventure for hikers and boaters alike. There is a boat ramp, but also good opportunities to put a small craft in the water.

Trails come in easy to moderate. There is even a wheelchair accessible trail.

Camping is available with hookups and without.

The Georgia Museum of Art is a free art museum with a really good collection. The museum is divided in to wings. One is the temporary exhibits and the other is the permanent collection.

It's worth giving yourself 90 minutes to two hours and to give yourself time with the permanent collection.

What a fun day trip! Very friendly staff. The train has both indoor and outdoor seating. Go during the day. The train can run a little warm.

Make sure to visit the gift shop early to get your tickets. Also allow extra time for parking.

There are handicapped ramps.

It's a solid regional art museum that varies between local exhibits and Georgia works of national interest.

Great building, free parking, and friendly staff make it a worthwhile trip.

Wheelchair accessibility is not too difficult, but do call ahead.

The chateau is rustic fun time! The wine tastings are affordable and the cafe has fun and music options.

Try the Georgia Cuvee as it's primary grape is Norton. Plan an hour or more for your visit.

Give them a heads up for wheel chair options.

What a cordial experience! The wine maker is highly knowledgeable and the pours led to knowledge about the winery's philosophy and purpose.

Go for native grape wines. Wheelchair accessibility is possible but call ahead.

This park has a great selection of trails and features. The trails are long enough to have both hills and water access. The amenities are also good. Whether it's exercise rails or a playground there's good stuff!
Though a little expensive, this was a realky neat visit. If you like the band, this is hallowed ground. For everyone else, its neat to see the history of a band. It helps if you're a gear head too.
The gardens were lovely and there were good trails. There is a bit of up and down, so wheel chair bound folks can go but should be careful. It's smaller than expected, but very pleasant.
The smith is a solid university museum, though it's total gallery space is smaller than one might expect. Their permanent collection of impressionism is the highlight.
Really, this is one of the great small parks in North America. The swan boats are fun. The actual swans are great and the flowers are gorgeous.
This one of America's great Art Museum. Great collection of pre 20th century art! Don't the special exhibits which ate always well curated!
Tha gardens have great variety and paths. Labeling is great and the wildlife thrives. It's fun for everyone and has accessible paths!
Great city park with lake, pier, and fishing access. Tennis courts too. Great for picnics and has limited wheelchair accessibility.

EDIT: I am updating my review to say that this year Walton County has been testing the spring area for enterococci bacteria and found unsafe concentrations at Morrison Springs.  This is unsurprising, as the spring run is so close to the Choctawhatchee River that in floods you inevitably get a backflow of pollution.  For most accurate testing quality, you should check the county website for health status.
-----
What kind of genius sticks a boat ramp right next to a spring?!  This place had a huge sheen of oil/gas on the surface of the water, that noticeably got all over your skin.  Why do people want noisy, polluting boats right next to such a beautiful wonder of nature?  This park is managed by Walton County; it is not a State Park, and despite my numerous attempts to have Google try and correctly rename it, they keep denying my request.  As for the spring itself, it's massive!  And gorgeous...when it's clear.  But you have to essentially wait for at least a one week drought before it gets crystal clear.  Also this recently modernized facility is massive.  Lots and lots of parking - and lots and lots of people too.  This place has unfortunately gone from pristine natural wonder to exploited tourist attraction.

To avoid confusion: There is a general parking fee, which gets you into Battleship Memorial Park, and then there is a separate general admission fee, which gets you into the separate USS Alabama exhibit area.  Inside just Battleship Memorial Park, you have access to limited number of static displays, several picnic pavilions, a pier out over the water, as well as the gift shop.  Inside the USS Alabama exhibit, you have access to the USS Alabama battleship, the USS Drum sub, and the Aircraft Pavilion.  I strongly recommend doing the whole exhibit if you have never experienced it.  Plan on spending at least a few hours if you want to see most of it, anywhere to half a day, depending how much you stop.  The self-guided tour aboard the USS Alabama is divided into three sections and is very well marked.  The Aircraft Pavilion and USS Drum are also straight forward enough.  Both the USS Alabama and USS Drum require going up and down small stairways and through narrow hatches, so it may not be full accessible to elderly and those with disabilities, and be sure to bring comfortable shoes and clothing.  It can get hot inside the ship, so cooler months are a good time to visit.  Overall we really liked coming here.
