The Fort itself was so interesting. I also really loved the camping. Having the water on all sides was so amazing and peaceful.

It was probably the most boring mini golf course I have ever done. Usually when you think of mini golf you think of obstacles and things moving. This was just way too easy. However, the water volcano is very awesome. There is another mini golf place right across the street that is way better.

Awesome.  It is the ultimate display of everything Alabama football including a realistic recreation of the office of Bear Bryant.  It is an A+ museum.  The staff is also super friendly and you can tell they love what they do.  I was visiting from Oregon. Roll Tide!!

Amazing and sad at the same time. Such a horrific loss of life took place here in one of the bloodiest battles in the Civil War. I absolutely love what they have done with the park. Very educational and yet very beautiful and poignant at the same time.

Great park for running to walking. The lake is filthy though. I would not want to be boating or fishing in this lake like people do. It was pretty gross when I was there. The park is fantastic though. Great for biking and running.

Beautiful and Scenic Park. They have restrooms and a pretty big parking lot. There is a boat launch with access to the water and it's only about a five or six minute walk to the beginning of the Cascade Head trail.

Not very fun. They only have card games so if you're expecting an actual casino this is not the place for you. I had dinner in the sports bar and it was very good though. Table games just are not my thing though.

It is a smaller Zoo that many, but we had a good time. The $10 admission price is very fair for the size of the zoo. They have six meerkats now which are very cool. The black jaguar and bears are awesome also.

Amazing! I stumbled upon this on accident while on my 370 mile Charity Run across California. We had to stop. An awesome piece of History. One of my favorite stops on my journey and totally unexpected.
Amazing to see you in person. The city has done a great job preserving history. I was visiting from Oregon head only seen it on TV and it was so much more amazing in person.
Beale Street is awesome and fun. It is a tourist trap though so eating and can be very expensive and some of the restaurants even at lunch. The experience is awesome though.
Great scenic hike up and back  With great views of the coast and Lincoln City. It can be a little treacherous when it's muddy though so it's good to take your time.
Very awesome!  The volunteers were great. It was surreal to finally visit Dealey Plaza and the museum and see it first hand. It adds new perspective.
Great park with an amazing playground, especially for a small town.  It's the 1st place my friend's kids want to go when they come to town to visit.
Very scenic. I would strongly suggest doing it on a bike when you can really take in the scenery. It's hard in a car when you have to watch the road
I love the pier. Pier Burger is good too. I love The Eclectic feel with all the performers people selling things.

Great views from the top. There is a nice hike to Hidden Lake, about three miles  round trip to the viewing area add another two if you go to the lake.  It is rated medium difficulty because there are 600+ steps on the trail.  The view is worth it.  we also saw some Bighorn sheep and mountain goats. Some said they saw a bear by the lake so bear spray is recommended.  Even though its cool take some water.  The trip to the viewing area and back took us about 3 hours.  we made many stops for pictures.  If you plan to drive plan on arriving before 8 AM otherwise it will be difficult to find parking.  The visitor's center opens at 9, they have restrooms, but no running water.

Really interesting Texas State Park.  There are nearly 3,-000 rock arts dating from about 2,000 years to the early 20th century.  we stayed in the campground.  There are 20 sites many with electric and water.  Price for extrications site is $22 plus $7 per day per person.  If you have the Texas State Park pass the per person fee is waived.  They strictly limit the number of people and where they can go.  If you are camping you will need to get the day pass to hike any of the trails.  Many of the trails you will need a guide.  Suggest to book a guided tour to get the full experience.

Quality artifacts, well presented all in a historic beautifully restored building.    Most of the items deal with the history of Galveston and east Texas.  We were these on a Thursday morning, small crowd.  Friendly staff and docents throughout that will add extra information about the exhibits.  Only issue is its $14 for adults, which seems a bit pricy compared to other similar quality private museums.  We did have a coupon for one free entry with purchase of another.  This can be found at most Texas visitor's centers.

Fantastic place to camp, hike, ride and experience the southwest Texas.  Its a little confussing as the address listed for the park is the ranger station/visitors center.  If you camping, hiking or riding trail you need to register here.  Friendly knowledgeable staff all housed in an old ranch compound.  Its 27 miles down a gravel road from Texas Farm road 170.  Recommend a high clearance vehicle.

Hidden gem, not well publicized.  Rachael from the Benson Historical Museum told us about this place.  We arrived about 2:30, they close at 4:00 so not enough time to see all the archaeological and art exhibits.  plan at least 2 hours.  Cost is $10 per person, with discounts for seniors and children.  They do not allow pictures inside.  There are nice picnic areas outside.

A must go to place when visiting Birmingham.  Well maintained park, good views of the city and friendly staff.  Wife had been there many years ago and enjoyed seeing it again.  The climb up the tower is not too bad, the view is fantastic.  The museum is not large but covers a lot of history and is well laid out.  Spent about 90 minutes, cost is $6 per adult.

This is a well maintained county campground with good sized sites.  Electric only, electric/water and full hook-up sites are available.  some pull throughs.  Most are gravel, some concrete.  Reasonably clean shower facilities, friendly hosts, late checkout 3PM.  Only issue I had is the water pressure is high so bring your regulator,

Very nicely kept recreation area.  Lots of picnic shelters, large grassy areas and several places to fish.  The reason its not a five is they have the locks viewing area and visitors center.  Its about 12 miles to get to it from the campground even though you can see it about 200 yards across the dam.

Wonderful museum.  They tell the history from the perspective of the men and women who were involved.  Much more personal and emotional experience.  It takes more than a day to see it all.  You can come back then next day and reenter for $7 with your receipt.

Very nice center with helpful and knowledgable people.  They have a nice boardwalk that winds through the mangroves.  Cost is $8 per person with senior and student discounts.  Check their schedules as they have programs daily.  we spent about two hours there.

Looking for something a little different this museum offers it.  I like the technical details so thought it was interesting, my wife less so.  Exhibits very nicely done, all on a retired drilling platform.  $8 for seniors (+55), spent about two hours.

Have stayed at Toop sail several times.  Very nice campground with full hook-ups, good privacy and friendly staff.  bring bicycles as the beach is about half a mile from the campground.  hey do have shuttles with run every hour from 8 - 5.

Nice pier which is in the middle of a refresh.  The pier is about 60% complete with a refresh of the deck and railings, when complete it will be very nice.  For now if the tide is out you can't get to the far enough out to fish.

Clean park and good place to sit a relax a while.  Outside around the park are lots of artists, musicians and street performers.  I ran into a fellow that tells jokes fo a quarter (5 for a dollar).  Something for everyone.

Nice stop on the Goldcamp road.  Overlooks the Newmark open pit mine.  They have an old dump bed from one of the large Caterpillar trucks that you can climb up to see into the mine.  You can also wee Pikes Peak from here.

Parked here to walk the beach.  We ere there on a Saturday and there were several spaces available, $2 per hour.  Nice beach access and and restroom facilities.  Only draw back is could not find a place to rinse off.

Stopped by while traveling through the area.  Parked the RV in the visitors lot ate lunch and toured the exhibits.  Took a short hike near the center.  Would like to come back and spend a few f=more days.

Spent a week camping in the disbursed area north of Burgess Junction.  every day we saw Elk and Mule deer grazing in the meadow blow our campsite.  Caught some trout in the streams, great place to visit.
Nice museum with natural history and history of the area.  The movie is worth the time, it's well done.  Liked the old photo of the inside of the saloon with someones donkey in the background.
Nice park in the middle of town.  Good access to the lake with several small beach areas and docks for launching kayaks.  Grounds are well kept, the restrooms could use more attention.
Statue of the first governor of the Montana Territory.  Interesting history/: Sounds that like most Irishmen Tommy not only had good leadership skills he had the gift of gab.
Stopped by a while back, very moving.  Great way to bring history into the current generations.  Must see if traveling through the area.
Cool place to stop at the corner of Rt 66 and Main.  Iconic building which has been well preserved.  Tesla charging station in the back.
Great place to visit, you have access to nearly all the fort.  There is good signage explaining the rich history of the fort and area.
Friendly helpful staff and well stocked with NP items.  Nice walk through a desert garden.  Not much room for RVs

This place is actually beautiful and has great facilities. The bummer is that it is always super crowded, and almost impossible to make any kind of actual reservation. The third party online platform makes it way too difficult and then I can’t actually make a reservation for the days I want as “their policy is that a user cannot reserve any less than two days” although Vogel says they have no such policy. What’s further is that I final made a reservation for this Friday (06.13.20 at campsite e) and then they gave me a completely random campsite next to the bathrooms and dumpsters (site p lol) with these ridiculous lights that were on all night. I want to love this place but I’m always SO frustrated by the time I leave, if I can make it there at all. They need more support,  better reservation abilities, and for the love of all that is good turn the bathroom lights down a bit it’s like the intensity of a thousand glowing suns.

Beautiful. We will be back! Stopped in here on our way through town and loved it. The bonsai garden was amazing and the general layout was just so cool. They had a plant sale too and we got to leave with a couple great lil plant babies! The staff was very helpful. Parking is a lil steep but the actual arboretum is free. We made the mistake of parking at the back of the parking lot as well. You enter from the back so make sure to drive all the way up.

Wow. What a place. So weird. Somehow me and my family had a great time here and spent almost two hours just exploring and looking around and trying to find new hidden niches. The staff is very friendly and helpful and the overall experience is incredibly easy. We waited an hour in line but it was well worth the wait. The merch is reasonably priced which was appreciated.

Pretty remarkably fun. Super private, not very loud, great restaurants. Tons of space to lay out and play in the grass, eat food, and hang out with your friends. Not super easy to get to but that’s not a bad thing. Reasonably close to the piedmont park in garage, which is also the botanical garden parking garage, make sure to get out on the second level.

Incredible place to camp. Would come back! Super close to Fort Davis National Monument. We got to hike over and hike back while we were there. Staff was very friendly. 10/10 word to the wise. The bike trail is trash. Don't waste your time. Tons of large loose rock and large stairs. It was a joke! Still a ton of cool things and great views.

Great lil zoo! Entry price isn’t too much but it’s a bummer if you just want to go to the garden and conservatory, it’s not super clear on Google that those are separate. We got to see most of the zoo though before it started raining. And got to go to the conservatory once the rain picked up. The plants and butterflies are awesome.

Always love to visit this spot! They are one of the best gardens in the country and the holiday show is second to none. I love the canopy walk and the indoor area is fascinating! A wonderful and super affordable spot to bring someone visiting. Great for covid times as well.

Love this place so much. The Central Park of Atlanta. Quiet with stuff to do. A gorgeous lake and an incredible splash pad and a pool. Very good time. I would recommend biking in from somewhere else and hanging out in the meadow. The parking garage is hella inconvenient.

This place is a gem. Used to be totally under the radar but the word is out. Worth the visit but you’ll wanna go early. The hike is fairly strenuous with some pretty good climbs if you’re not used to it. So kids and casual hikers be ready.

Very incredible museum. Ive seen different works after multiple visits and am always refreshed by o’keefs perspective on the world and life in it. Worth every penny and it’s easy to get through and fully immerse yourself in her work.

Very cool place. We came in late May for the farmers market and artists market on a Saturday. 10/10 great experience. Tons of local folks selling and shopping. I made off with some freakin great Chile powder and some great fruit.

Amazing state park. Maybe one of the best in Georgia. I can see how this spot would get super busy. The hikes are mild but the views are awesome. The staff is so helpful and kind and the campsites are incredible. Will be back!

Amazing collection with a wonderful landscape. The exhibits are free and the docents are incredibly kind and knowledgeable. This will be a frequented spot for me as I go through Houston! Everybody should take a look.

I've done Utah, Big Bend, Colorado etc. and Palo is always one of my favorite places to be. Absolutely incredible mountain biking for Texas and gorgeous views and things to see no matter the time of year.
Great spot in Charlotte. The caretakers were very friendly and the greenhouse has some really incredible specimens. Parking was very weird so some signage around that would have been helpful.
Very beautiful fall. Only downside is you have to walk past a million tubers and listen to screaming on the river. Looks like a fun place to tube tho. Not much of a peaceful hike.
Amazing state park. The hike is awesome and pretty strenuous but the view is unreal. The staff is very friendly and the overall place is very clean. Will be back!
Really incredible spot. Hard to get to but a good retreat from the city! We used the getaways package by the mta and it ended up making it pretty easy.
This place is gorgeous. A good spot to feel some of the heart of bar harbor. Every dish is amazing and the piano player was top notch.
Absolutely wonderful place. Have been to gorges sp and stayed in panthertown valley. Really great vistas for this part of the world.
This is a great spot! Putting in here is hard as the river after is pretty rocky. There is a trail and parking is $5 credit.
Wow such an incredible place. History literally laying on the ground. Everybody on the caprock needs to visit this spot.
Wow what a place. Good for walking or bikes. So beautiful and even romantic. A better city feature than Central Park.
Fun lil spot.  Very packed, definitely have to wait for a hammock and people are pretty loud but the idea is nice.
Great spot, although the walk out there is pretty dicey if it is windy or cold. So keep an eye on the weather!

Do you love nature, geology and history?   This is the place.   I can't believe I almost didn't see because it is not on any tourist brochure.  The formations are beautiful.  The bonus is the wind farm that can be seen in distance.  I've read some negative reviews here and my thoughts.   Go early or in the evening.  It's open from Dawn to dusk.  Two reasons are it is very hot during the day here and at dawn and dusk, the formation colors are more beautiful. The mile plus road to the site is bumpy.  Either slow down or donate money to fix the road.  It is a long walk on a trail to the site from the parking lot. Just up the road is another parking lot that appears to be closer.  I didn't walk that trail but it is much closer to formations.  Go online to read the brochure put out by park.  Great brochure with lots info.   I can't believe the formations are not more protected.  It's free to go and please stay off formations so future generations can enjoy.

Newly reopened due to covid with limited dates and times to visit. The museum is free along with parking but you must call the number on the web site to reserve a visit. There are no guided tours due to covid but Sarah who met me at the door answered my few questions I had and the museum is very organized with detailed information throughout. It's a small museum but full of Penrose's carriages used throughout the era and the full history of The Race to the Clouds.  That is the race to Pikes Peak which started in 1916.  So if you love history

Very easy to get lost with 546 acres and 10 miles of trails in this urban park and that's just what I did. Trails were all graveled, wide with some elevations where I could see downtown, Garden of Gods and mountains.  Trails are used for hiking, biking and horseback riding.  I walked all the way to the Nature Center and back.  Mostly in full sun with some shaded areas.  Beautiful fall colors with all the trees turning reds and yellows this time of year.   The park is well manicured with pavilions, playground and large open grass area.

Tunnel 1 and Tunnel 2 are part of an old railway called Short Line that went from Colorado Springs to Cripple Creek. You can drive from the parking lot Just above Helen Hunt Falls or from 26th Street. It is a gravel. road with no guard rails and at times turns into one lane road. The tunnels are also single lane. The views are amazing of Colorado Springs. The tunnels are fun.  I read online where the tunnels are haunted but I parked my car and walked through them.  I went early and not many cars but few bike riders.     I enjoyed!

Tunnel 1 and Tunnel 2 are part of an old railway called Short Line that went from Colorado Springs to Cripple Creek. You can drive from the parking lot Just above Helen Hunt Falls or from 26th Street. It is a gravel. road with no guard rails and at times turns into one lane road. The tunnels are also single lane. The views are amazing of Colorado Springs. The tunnels are fun.  I read online where the tunnels are haunted but I parked my car and walked through them.  I went early and not many cars but few bike riders.     I enjoyed!

The trail head is in a residential area with no parking nearby.  Have to hike a very steep hill 0.6 miles to get to the  trail head.  I crossed the first bridge, saw a beautiful waterfall and appeared the trail went directly down but another hiker said it starts here.  That's where I saw lots of rocks and not a clear path at all.  The trail goes directly up with lots of climbing rocks.  I made my way up to see the top of the falls and realized this hike was not for me. This is not an easy hike plus it is not very well marked.j

Overpriced! You pay one price that just gets you in.   Everything else is extra.   Also they charge $10 to park.  Yikes! Then I checked the program and they have something every 15 minutes which I thought was great until we attended one and couldn't hear a thing as their speakers were all distorted.  I understand all the money goes to rehabilitating the animals and I also understand they have some big corporate sponsors so why are they charging so much?   The Aquarium in Tampa is worth the drive .

Came for the day and enjoyed some of the many hiking trails and there are many.  Lots of trees down from the hurricane and the boardwalk by the water is damaged also and blocked off for safety.  Liked learning the history of each area by calling the number and hearing pre-recorded information. After the entry, the roads are not paved and at times very narrow.  At the entrance, the woman who approached our car to take our money for the entrance fee, was not wearing a mask nor social distancing.

I love history so only natural to visit here.   It is free to get in but during covid they ask that you go online and schedule your date and time.  When I got there I was greeted by many very friendly people who offered their assistance if I had any questions.  It's an old court house with multiple floors of history.  There's stairs to get each floor but there is a 1917 Otis elevator too. That was fun.  Lots to see and learn about Colorado history.  I would definitely return.
likes: Facilities & Services: Friendly staff, historical elevator

reviews_attraction.text: Trails, trails everywhere.  Most are wide and graveled trails that are covered with snow today.  Many views of downtown, Broadmoor, and the  mountains.  The South Surburban reservoir is a short hike up and hiking is allowed around the reservoir.   In the summer, dogs are allowed to swim in the reservoir.  It's closed for the winter.   Lots of bikes and dogs.  Since most trails are wide there is plenty of room for everyone.

The drive up is beautiful.  There are so many trails to explore or just pull along side the road on the creekside and relax and enjoy!   The weekends are busy.  There's not a lot of parking and it is frustrating circling the parking area awaiting for a spot to open up.  If you do go on weekends, go early.  Also on the weekends, there will be many people walking on the winding streets and lots of cyclists, so go slow.

This is the only beach left in Pinellas County where you only pay $8 to get in and park close to the beach. Therefore this park can get very crowded.   I've been many times over many years and notice there are many more small rocks this last time I went.   Still a great beach.  If you want to compare, take the ride to Clearwater Beach, pay $20 to park in a parking garage and then walk the mile to the beach.

My love of history brought me here.  It cost $12 to get in with no tour guide. They gave me a piece of paper with info on it.  So it is self guided.  The woman who took my money was strict and not friendly.  The woman in the gift shop was very friendly and had a wealth of info to share.   I enjoy history and if I'm paying this much money, I prefer a tour guide.  Glen Eyrie was a much better experience.

The ride in to Cripple Creek and Victor is beautiful.  Cripple Creek is an old mining town that is full of casinos now. Lots of history here.  The train ride was slow and at times, I thought it may not make it but it is old 1894.  What I loved about the ride the most was the young man telling stories about history of Cripple Creek.

These falls are only open a few days of the week.  They are free but they do ask for $1 donation.  There is limited parking but just down the hill is a gravel parking lot.  The day I was there, I was greeted by a volunteer who had so many stories about history of the falls and the area. It's an easy walk to the falls.

Old Colorado City History Center and Museum is located in the 1890 First Baptist Church.  The Museum is small but full of history and I was lucky enough to be there when historian Leo was there.  There are so many stories to tell about history that happened in Old Colorado City and Leo makes it all come to life.

At my age, I learned and saw so much!  This museum is well documented with all kinds of money and the history of the money.  They have an amazing coin collection of Harry Bass.  As I was looking at this massive collection and wondered where he found all these amazing coins. A must see!

Beautiful morning hike with just a touch of snow on the ground. I've not camped here but the sites looked nice and clean with beautiful views. In addition to hiking, there are biking trails too. A great place to bring your family as there are many trails from super easy to difficult.

A great place to stop to get all your questions answered and a map detailing all the trails and formations in The Garden of God's.  The bonus is the view from the upper deck of the visitor center of the rock formations just across the street.

Some very dedicated volunteers here restoring the history of Colorado Springs.  There are many streetcars to see and walk on.  If your interest is the early transportation of Colorado Springs then old and young will enjoy.

I can understand why this trail is so popular. Well maintained trail with some beautiful views.  Definitely stay away on the weekends as it is so busy.  I hiked mid week with very little hiking traffic.

Beautiful hike along the river. So many beautiful sounds of the river moving, kids playing, birds singing.  Very peaceful.  There are benches along the way for comfort and to enjoy nature at its best.
A massive urban park with beautiful views of mountains, Garden of God's and surrounding views of Colorado Springs.  There's something for everyone!   Trails. Picnic areas, dog park, etc.
Beautiful park and springs!   Lots of wildlife to see.  The downfall is I had no cell service and only got internet at the concession area.
Great playground for young and older children.   2 playgrounds and a splash pad.  Lots of places to sit and watch the kiddos.

Fun experience jumping into a "bottomless" pool. Water us clean and refreshing (and very cold) but you get used to it. Laid back. Fun yo your remains of old amusement park and zoo adjacent. Can also do a tubing experience nearby. No shallows do be careful with kids and nonswimmers. Nothing to stand on once you're in.

The ride up the mountainside is a blast. The tram rotates do everyone gets a chance at every 360 degree view. Be prepared for temperature to be 30 or 40 degrees cooler at top. 39 degrees today. There is a restaurant, gift shop and hiking trails up there. Fun time. Great views though today it was fogged in.

Very cool. Parking for 1 hour for free at Bellagio gives you time to see the fountains in action and walk through the hotel lobby. Amazing decor.  Shows are on the hour and half hour. Go after dark for the best experience. Eiffel tower is right across the street.

Fun place to see vistas from highest point in Alabama. Nice boardwalk trail to bald rock. Tower at highpoint is a little disappointing. Windows obscure view and are dirty. Otherwise it's worth the drive up, beautiful roads going up and down mountain.

Parking is sometimes hard but it is fun to walk through the eclectic shops for nicknacks and antiques. The park on the river is beautiful, photo op in front of the little lighthouse there. Restaurants here are very good.

Park at Impark lot on Stanton, only $14 for all day.  Boats to Alcatraz leave from this port. There are restrooms and a store there with food and souvenirs... And seating for while you're waiting for your embarkation.
Unfortunately it was drizzly and overcast the day we drove the 17 Mile drive. Still a pleasant drive with lots of amazing sights. Gas up first and be prepared to pay $10.50 to access the road.
Just walked in on an off day to walk around. Very interesting. Lots of seating, all wooden. Cool stage. Other amenities on the ground too. Museum was closed. Staff was very nice. Free parking.
Nice facility and easy walk to overlook, but view of lake is mostly obscured by trees and brush. Interesting stairway down to forest below overlook deck. Nice drive getting there too.
Love the beach. The long March from the parking lot is bad if you don't get lucky enough to snag a spot in the north lot. The parking by phone is horrible unless you download the app.
Interesting park that includes Round Beach. Nature trail through mangrove area is ok. Has safe beach area for kids to play and convenient restrooms. Must pay to park using phone app.
Restrooms, playground, pavilions, benches and free access to beach. You can see anclote key from here. Very nice spot to relax when smokers aren't around spoiling the fresh breeze.
Beautiful beach location right next to boardwalk attraction. Big waves and occasional seals. Lots of homeless people unfortunately. Must pay to park almost everywhere in town.
Nice facility. I liked walking out on long wooden dock to see lake up close. Too bad the water is so gross. I hope the lake can recover from decades of pollution abuse.
Very nice facility. Beach access, watch out for caes that can drive on the beach, life guard on duty, nice playground, restrooms and showers. Great for kids.
Beautiful sandy beach but of course water is terribly cold. Sand is so thick in some areas it is hard to walk. Lots of people playing in the sand.
Nice accessible trail from main road. All these trees are an amazing site. The trail was wet and muddy because of snow melt runoff.
Great hiking trails and facilities. Didn't finish the full trail but enjoyed the walk. Easy trails with lots of views of the river.
Beautiful grounds and very nice staff who gave us an interesting your. Impressive building for the time period it was constructed.
Beautiful scenery and affordable rentals of paddle boats or canoes. Staff is very kind and helpful. Cottages are well maintained.
Beautiful walk along the Savannah River. Lots of interesting sights. Of course very hot right now. Good local restaurants nearby.
Beautiful lakeside park. Setting up highlands festival the day we were there. Pleasant visit very close to downtown Mt. Dora.
Interesting overlook on way to Hoover dam. Worth stopping to take in the water. It's really low right now. Worrisome?
$13 per person to go inside. Plenty to see outside for free. Very hot today though. Lots of real history here.
Interesting little park in the middle of downtown Park City. Gives you a hint of the history of the area.

The Adventure Science Center is the perfect family activity, especially in the summer when it gets so hot outside.  Lots of exhibits to discovery, and it was great finding things around every corner.  Don't be afraid to explore!  Also be sure and climb up to the 3rd floor to see a great view of the Nashville skyline (you can cheat and take the elevator).  My daughter (6) was in summer camp here all week and had a great time.  In camp, they get to do a different activity each day that's centered around a science theme.  There's a Subway inside if you want to stay for lunch.

My family really enjoyed our weekend at CMSP. We rented a rustic cabin which had more perks than I was expecting: fridge, stove, dishes and utensils, towels, blankets, heaters in each room, and a cozy fireplace. We came in late fall when it's not busy and the kids enjoyed s'mores and hot cocoa by the fire and lots of hiking. There are several kid play areas nearby and the Homestead Harvest restaurant with a buffet is just a short walk away. Overall a great last-minute weekend getaway for the family!

We visited family in Tyler and they took us here for a day outing with the kids. We didn't know what to expect and was pleasantly surprised. The exhibits chronicle the great East Texas oil boom during the prohibition (1930s). An "elevator" ride, interactive diorama, and a full scale model of downtown Kilgore complete with animatronics are some of the highlights. The kids loved running around and exploring the different areas of the museum. A fun day was had by all!

A state treasure. I have been going to Petit Jean since I was a kid and didn't fully realize how special this park is until I moved out of state. Excellent trails that are still rustic enough to experience nature. There are some steep drop offs with no railing so smaller kids should be watched. Cedar Falls is a great place to cool down and relax and the hike is short and not too strenuous. Some longer trails and several that can be done in a day trip.

Great and underused park. I spent a couple of hours here with two little kids (ages 4 and 7) and they had a blast. Very few people around and we saw the sheriff drive by several times while we were there. The park has two big play areas for kids, a swing set, picnic tables, restrooms, and a covered pavilion. Heavy rain flooded a lot of the grassy area, but the paved paths and play equipment were dry. Good trails here for walking.

Great place for kids to explore nature and get some energy out. We did the Tower Trail and circled back on the River Trail which took us and our two kids (8 and 4) about an hour to finish. There was light rain when we visited but we barely felt it beneath the trees. Restrooms and drinks/snacks are at the visitors center, plus everything was free, though they do accept donations. Masks are required indoors.

This is a fascinating place to visit, however the fort itself is in ruins and what little stonework is visible is walled off with wooden barriers. If you're visiting for the (excellent) view of the Nashville skyline, take the left part of the loop and the trail up to the top of the hill. There are several wooden outlooks built at the top of the fort and with a few shade trees there as well.

Good stop along the Cades Cove loop to see several man-made structures including several barns and the Cable Mill itself. The Center has souvenirs and some basic amenities. Good bathrooms here. The mill wasn't moving but they have a shop selling molasses and sorghum meal. Water was running down the mill race when we visited but the sluice gates redirected much of it off to the side.

Beautiful brick lighthouse situated precariously on the remnants of Sand Island.  Can only be accessed by boat, but worth visiting as it doesn't have much time left before it collapses into the Gulf.  When we visited it in 2014, the Keeper house was long gone and the light sat atop a pile of rocks with stabilizing cables that were starting to give way.

Quiet place for fishing and having a picnic. No frills. There are covered picnic tables and a small boat ramp here. I took the family here for some fishing on labor day weekend and it was not busy at all. We caught a few small fish which was great for my 6 year old. Plenty of parking here and theres a paved path to the Big Dam Bridge.

A nice park with a shaded trail that goes over and beside a creek. It's located right in the middle of the busier part of the Cool Springs/Franklin area, but still manages to feel a little secluded. There's a few picnic tables, bathrooms, a covered pavilion, and a play area for younger kids that's in good shape.

Nice park with several trails for jogging or biking. There are places you can park along the trailheads to access the trails and the river. Clean restrooms, posted trail maps, benches and a bike repair station. This park felt very safe and is well-maintained. Nice neighborhoods nearby.

Great day areas for shore fishing, picnics, grilling, and mild hiking. Long, paved trail along the shore. Our kids loved going out to the lakeshore for fishing and exploring. Clear, shallow water with a rocky bottom--water shoes are recommended. The trail is paved with no inclines.

Incredible aquarium that is split into two separate exhibits you can choose from: a freshwater and saltwater. Admission gets you into both. We did fresh water in the morning, grabbed lunch, then did the saltwater in the evening and still had time for afternoon dessert.

We visited the Hermitage twice with family and enjoyed both times. The grounds are well kept and touring the estate gives you an incomparable glimpse at life in the past. There is a lot to see but i recommend taking your time if you have it to spare.

This is our favorite music venue in Nashville. Great acoustics (not overrated) and we love the smaller shows that come here. The pew seating isn't comfortable but but worth enduring for a few hours for great performances.

Not a big park but the best park in Newport! This one has a big play area for kids, swings, a climbing rock, and splash pad. There is also a basketball court and bike loop towards the back. Clean and new.

This is a great zoo.  Lots of shade and things to discover.  The Farm at Grassmere near the carousel was a pleasant surprise and ended up being the perfect place to get away from the crowds and explore.
Visiting The Alamo is a must if you haven't seen it before. Yes, it's very small but the tour is fast and the facilities are well maintained with knowledgeable volunteers. Worth the visit.
Awesome fun!  Exploring the endless rooms of interactive "art" and climbing through the mazes of free-standing tunnels and corridors makes you feel like a kid again.
A good 3 hours to the Falls and back. Bring comfortable shoes and water, maybe even a snack. This was the highlight of our trip to Cades Cove.
Small but well-maintained park with some play equipment for kids. It always seems to be busy but my kids like finding people to play with.
This turned out to be a great place to take our 3 year old at the end of a road trip. She enjoyed "fishing" and sorting microbes.
The kids enjoyed feeding the animals and seeing the alligators. We spent a little over an hour here. Parking is free.
We did the lunch cruise and it was a fun way to spend a few hours out on the lake.

It was my first time at this place I always want to go so it was magnificent, you have to see the whole process of closing and opening and changing level of water and boats can come out and come in, it's really interesting and I had a chance to ask employee information about whole process, so he was so informative, he explained everything, it was amazing experience, and also it was perfect time, when you can see salmon, it was breathtaking. Definitely worth to go and they have three parking so it's really convenient.
likes: Facilities & Services: Informative staff, Convenient parking

reviews_attraction.text:
We went to SAM for special exhibit of Kehinde Wiley "A New Republic". It was well organized, really interesting, his works were amazing. Easy access to parking and from parking, it's a same building, and even after when museum close, you can use parking(open door with your card. I bought membership (dual membership, you can add another person), so for whole year you can visit 3 locations :
SAM,  Asian Art Museum and Olympic Sculpture Park for free.

I love it, very interesting, well organized. My daughter took me when it got just opened, so you had to have reservations time. Amazing customer service, workers were guiding, helping with any questions. Half way through my knee hurting, because I was after surgery, so my daughter asked for a wheelchair, they brought it really quick, so I was be able to continue enjoying my tour. Amazing building, amazing exhibition.

It's a nice, small garden with lots of small waterfalls, beautiful trees and flowers, and they have more trails for hiking, and the best part it's a dog friendly, and also it has the little box, is like a library you can get the book, you can put the book, you can exchange the book, it's really nice, but place needs to be maintain better, and news  more signage, it's really hard to navigate.

I went to Sunset Beach, it was Tuesday and wasn't crowded, lots of parking, it's definitely different on weekends. Very clean and well-maintained, amazing playground for children, so kids can enjoy and be busy for long time. You need Discover Pass to get there, it's $10 daily pass and $30 annual pass. Definitely enjoyable place, must go.

Beautiful building, you will not miss that uniquely designed masterpiece even from far, it has underground parking. Be aware that you can go in with little backpack, or big purse, you have to put in the locker(25¢)
Nice collections and exhibits.

Beautiful museum, I spent 3 hours, enjoyed every minute of it. Well organized and maintained, also very friendly and informative employees. Free general admission, a fully accessible for  people with disabilities. Highly recommend to visit.

Beautiful place, one of the best and biggest I've seen, very well organized and maintained, beautifully designed, each Dome has different theme, Desert Dome, Tropical and Show Dome(which changes every time, beautifully done for Christmas)

Small but beautiful garden, well organized, designed and well-maintained, little crowded on weekends, waiting for the parking and another waiting to buy a ticket and get in, but it was beautiful experience. Must see, specially in fall..

I love this beach 🏖 beautiful, well organized, lovely restaurants nearby, little tough with parking on weekends, but during the week days no problem, also special place you can play volleyball, badminton or just enjoy laying on a sand.

It's nice park with beautiful surroundings, we went for 4th of July firework, it was well organized, nice music, beautiful fireworks.
Amazing view of lake, boat, also you can see Space Needle which was beautiful at night.
Beautiful green house, with huge selection of plants, very tastefully and amazingly done all compositions, and because of Christmas, one whole room had a Christmas theme, I really enjoyed my visit.
Great gallery, really enjoyed my time there, beautiful collection of Monet, Picasso and more. Good customer service, knowledgeable employees who can help with any questions, big parking.
One of my favorite places to go, amazing attractions, rides, performances.... You can go since afternoon and be there up to evening, make sure you stay and enjoy beautiful fireworks 🎆
Beautifully designed and well-maintained, each display has different theme and style, very fun for children to find hiding animals on displays. Make sure you have $5 cash for parking.
Beautiful small city, windmill is amazing, they have vine tasting, and other small shops and restaurants nearby. One day tour is perfect to explore this unique Danish City.
Very nice place, I was there in July and it was beautiful, lots of people, life concert, it was really fun, free parking, lots of different restaurants and stores around.
Gorgeous view, specially in the evening time, when all lights on. The place was clean, well organized and had enough information to learn about the city and surroundings.
It is really beautiful garden, even though it was November, but still have amazing colors. It was relaxing and enjoyable visit, we will definitely come back.
Beautiful Japanese Garden 🏯 with lake, Tea House. We went on Spring time, so most of the cherry trees were blooming. We are really enjoy this park.
It's a very nice garden, you can visit for free. You can have little tour around historic building and have peaceful and relaxing time in garden.
Beautiful place, the house was closed when I was there, but I still browse around for 30 min.(it was really cold), it was amazing experience.
Beautiful view of the lake, relaxing, you can spend little time next to the water, and after walk around, enjoy small shops and restaurants.
It was beautiful weather, so sat and walked around for a hour, watching boats were passing by, always lots of people.
Always working, even in the winter, but much better in the summer, with music and children playing in the water.

A visit to Riverbottom Park in Montrose, CO is enjoyable. Locals of many age groups are there to take advantage of the structures built up such as the skateboard ramps, swings and climbing apparatus. The river offers a cool escape to develop your white water skills upon. The river walk provides a nice family friendly paved path for walking, jogging or biking. Bathroom and picnic facilities are provided. If you are lucky to be there at the right time, then those new to driving will demonstrate the acceleration capabilities of their cars. Quite a show as they come across the parking lot.

The National Park Service presents the story of this location historically became the playground of the rich to find relaxation and restoration. The exercise room with its many fore runners to todays enhanced mechanical apparatus that challenge the healthy individual was enlightening.
The staff was very helpful and greatly enhanced the visitor’s experience.

I recommend that you drive slowly through this National Park and stop frequently at the pull offs.  The views are spectacular!  Multiple trips are needed in both directions to observe the changing landscape, morning, noon and later in the day or night. The natural lighting is slowly changing as the earth rotates.

As with many natural wonders, this place isn’t easy to get to but it is well worth the trip. The Bridges View Road around the park brings you to view points to the natural bridges with short walks to the overlooks. Plan you walks along the longer trails during the cooler parts of the year and day.

The visitor’s center is the must starting place for anyone hoping to fully experience this National Park. The staff is friendly and well informed about the opportunities that await you.
Don’t miss the videos that are offered for a unique view of park offerings that you may never experience.

The visitor’s center is the must starting place for anyone hoping to fully experience this National Park. The staff is friendly and well informed about the opportunities that await you.
Don’t miss the videos that are offered for a unique view of park offerings that you may never experience.

This museum offers a unique opportunity to observe the nuances of the subject. Specific detailed presentations provide a glimpse into the American way and history of thought that will inspire you to think about how you might have contributed to the events and happenings that are shown.

The National Forest is always a great place to visit for a weekend, a week or longer. Typically quiet and peaceful with too much scenery to mention individually. Great variety of trees, rocks, cliffs, mountains, and views. Not to mention wildlife; mammals, reptiles , insects and birds.

The National Forest is always a great place to visit for a weekend, a week or longer. Typically quiet and peaceful with too much scenery to mention individually. Great variety of trees, rocks, cliffs, mountains, and views. Not to mention wildlife both mammals and birds.

Local town Parks are gems that many residents and non-residents regularly visit to enjoy their unique and varied features. A hike along this paved pathway always seems to relax and recuperate from the nearby city. There is multiple opportunities to do a little birding.

Discover the state of Texas from it origins through multiple changes to the present day.
Plan to spend a full day here to absorb the content by viewing the displays and reading the detailed descriptions of the development of the current great state of Texas.

Alaska is not all ice and frozen people which this botanical garden demonstrates with a variety of plants. While visiting the area it seemed that the local people extend the botanical garden to parks and landscaping presentations everywhere you look.

Walk in the steps of early American explorers as they followed the local natives across the mountains through the gap. An excellent museum and thought provoking video to educate you about the history of crossing the previously blocking mountains.

A midweek visit to the Black Rock State Park is quiet and enjoyable. The weekend crowds have gone. The birds are singing and the fish are jumping. A hike to the overlook brings a fabulous view of the local countryside and hills.

Discover the historical artillery machines the Army has used through multiple conflicts to assist and support our troops. The interior dioramas and exterior larger weapons show the variety of equipment that has been available.

Connecticut State Parks are gems that many residents and non-residents regularly visit to enjoy their unique and varied features. Lovers Leap State Park offers shaded hiking and views that have inspired people for centuries.

View the life and times of a celebrated Texas son at this LBJ state park how he first educated the children and then represented the entire public for a long career in politics from locals to state and finally the country.

The Black Canyon of the Gunnison National Park is an excellent place to view the deep canyon encompassed by the park. Drive along the road and get out of your vehicle to walk along the trails that exist in the park.

Learn the story of the 1964 earthquake from the signage and remember the loss of the homes that slide off the shelf into the bay. Nice walking trails along the edge and if you are adventurous step off the edge.

Cedar Breaks is popular on weekends by become less crowded during the week. The staff is friendly and helpful always willing to respond in a helpful manner to your questions, many times with positive results.

The friendly staff that is well informed about local business to serve your needs and opportunities for entertainment of whatever your persuasion is; outdoors, museums, historic sites and many other venues.

Friendly staff that is well informed about local business to serve your needs and opportunities for entertainment of whatever your persuasion is; outdoors, museums, historic sites and many other venues.
A nice large park convenient to the central park of Anchorage when you don't have time to get to the vast expanse of wilderness that surrounds the area. Great for a quick lunch walk.
If you have only a short time to hike in Denali, this is a good choice to experience the wilderness. Be sure and follow the guidelines for the area where wild animals are wild!
Don't be a dummy and visit this place on a cloudy overcast day like I did. The view extended to the end of the parking lot.

This review is for the entrances to the preserve in Seminole County. The Lower Wekiva River Preserve is located just east of the Wekiva River and north of rte 46 in Sanford FL. There are two parking areas, one on rte 46 (free) and the other on Wekiva Park Dr at Katie's Landing. Katie's Landing is nicer, has restrooms, and gets to to my favorite parts of the park faster, but you're supposed to pay $3 in an envelope slot there.

There are over 18 miles of trails through some wonderful pine forests. I discovered this park in May, but it's becoming one of my favorite places to visit. From Katie's Landing you cross the street, and you'll see a sign for the trail head. There are paper maps there. I always get one because the trail blazes are often absent. Intersections of the trails are lettered on the map and on posts along the trail.

So far I've seen about 50 species of birds in this park, but it's also the only place in Seminole County where I've been able to find Bachman's Sparrows,  and for that reason alone, this is one of my favorite places to visit. It's also one of the better places to find Red-headed Woodpeckers in the county. I've found breeding Great Crested Flycatchers, Common Yellowthroat, and even a possible breeding Yellow-billed Cuckoo. The other wildlife I've seen here are Oak Toads, White-tailed Deer (many of them), and Florida Black Bear. Well, I haven't actually seen a Black Bear in the park (I've seen one in a nearby park), but I have seen bear tracks along the trails, so I know they're there.

Other than the restrooms at Katie's Landing, there's nothing here by way of accommodations.  Major parts of the trail receive direct sunlight all day, so it can be pretty hot, and in the hardwood canopy, mosquitoes can be a problem. So bring water, sun protection and bug spray.

I visit this area frequently to look for wildlife, especially shorebirds, wading birds and other wildlife that can be found in marshy areas. There are three tracts to the conservation area--the East Tract (south of Lake Jesup on Elm St), the North Tract (north of Lake Jesup on Cameron Ave) and Marl Bed Flats (north of Lake Jesup near rte 417 on Oak Way). Marl Bed Flats is the most popular of the three destinations for birders and other nature lovers.

When you arrive at Marl Bed Flats, you can walk through an oak hammock until you get out to the Marl Bed Slough. It can be very wet at times, so I always bring wading boots with me.  You also share this area with cattle, so watch your step!

I've logged over 160 species of birds in this area, along with Bobcats, White-tailed Deer, Coyotes, lots of butterflies and dragonflies, and unfortunately, feral pigs.

This park has a beautiful playground, many ball fields, a beach volleyball court, and a short nature trail that follows the south side of Lake Jesup.  It's also one of my favorite places to look for birds and other wildlife in Seminole County.  During September and October, lots of warblers, tanagers, vireos and other birds migrate through, and often they can be seen in this park in pretty large numbers. In fact, I've logged over 150 species of birds in this park alone.

The nature trail can be pretty buggy, so I'd bring some bug spray.  There is a restroom and a drinking fountain, but the water doesn't taste very good.  All in all, this is one of my favorite parks to visit in Seminole County.

This is one of my favorite places to visit in Seminole County for viewing nature and wildlife. The wilderness area contains about 180 acres with about 2 miles of trails through flatwoods, pine scrub and bay swamp environments. The trail takes you by three ponds, and there's a rustic chapel that overlooks a grassy clearing with two of the ponds. I find this area truly beautiful, and I highly recommend it to anyone who loves hiking, beautiful scenery, and wildlife.

It's a very pretty place to take a walk, especially around Christmas time when the park is decorated with Christmas lights. I come here with my family once or twice around Christmas time. However, it's a wonderful relaxing park for a nice walk around the lake any time of the year. And as a bonus, during the summer months there are concerts you can attend, and the fourth of July celebrations here are wonderful too, but you have to get here early.

This is one of the tallest falls in peninsular Florida, which is to say it may be a full 2 feet high. It's a beautiful hike to get here from Lockwood Blvd, and it's not far, perhaps only about a half mile from the trailhead. If you live nearby, it's definitely worth visiting this to enjoy the falls, affectionately referred to as one of the natural wonders of Seminole County.

This is a very nice park with a new playground. They've even added a zip line, which is very popular with my daughter.  There's a nice picnic area and exercise area as well.  There's not much by way of a nature walk, but there is a short boardwalk that will take you to the eastern portion of the lake. It's a little hard to find, but if you look for it, you can find it.

Absolutely beautiful beach, and I love that it's a national park. Even though they raised admission prices to $10, it's still worth it. There are beautiful places to pull over and look at the lagoon, and the lots that go to the beach have restrooms. Unfortunately, there are no showers to clean off when returning to your car.

I love coming here to walk around the lake. It's very fun to see the exotic geese that are here as well. Give yourself some time when you're in Orlando to visit this place. Take your time and enjoy the stroll. There are public restrooms and even a concert area, and you can see the skyline of the city.

This is a great place to visit to see shorebirds.  Parking is tricky. You can't park by the entrance to Snook Islands, but there is limited parking at a crossroad not far away. You can walk down the boardwalk and check out the area for wildlife.  It's a beautiful place!
There's a lot of construction in the park, and it's somewhat of a small park, but it's pretty, with lots of nice pine trees and open areas. This is also a wonderful place for frisbee golf.
It's pretty small, but there's a beautiful boardwalk and a lovely views of wildlife.  Birds, iguanas, exotic lizards and other wildlife can be seen here. It's well worth a visit.
This is a beautiful park tucked away in a corner of Seminole County. There are  beautiful trails to walk with lovely scenery, especially if you like walking among the pines.
Pretty trails and friendly atmosphere. A great place for families to come.  It's very near the library, so after a visit here, you can pop by the library for a bit.
Nice boat ramp, but I normally go here to look for wildlife. There are a lot of birds that pass through this area--gulls on the way to or from the landfill, etc.
Free parking, restrooms, and a "shower" to clean sand off yourself. The beach itself was not as pretty as I'd hoped, but it was still a very nice place to visit.
I just found this park recently, but I will have to visit far more frequently. There are 7 miles of trails to walk here, and it's beautiful, natural Florida.
In my opinion, this is the best ball park in the country. It's gorgeous, there are no real bad seats, the food is great, and the Orioles are playing.
likes: Facilities & Services: Great food, Good seating

reviews_attraction.text: There's a boat ramp, picnic area and trails entering the conservation area. The trails are not always well marked, but it's a great area to explore.
Of all the areas of the Patapsco State Park, this is probably my favorite. I especially love the cascades and waterfalls.
Wonderful and beautiful park.  You have to pay a fee to get in, but the plus side is it's not as crowded and it's nicer.
Gorgeous park with lots of trails and beautiful scenery. From the beach area you can also see a great view of Miami.
It's a very pretty trail that follows a tributary of the Econ River. Mile markers tell you how far you've walked.
Beautiful park with lots of places to walk and hike.  Beautiful scenery and a nice, lovely dog park as well.
What a wonderful place to visit!  If you do, make sure you check out the beach here too; it's gorgeous.

My family and I arrived on a Monday. It was around 930 when we got there and there was no wait and no line. We scored a covered table area in the kiddie pool section. It was perfect because it shaded from the sun all day and provided cover from the impending rain.

The springs are absolutely gorgeous but keep in mind that the water is frigid. It took a while to get acclimated and even then it’s still cold, you’re just used to the cold. There were only 2 slides open. My kids went down the double slide. Be aware...it is FAST. 😊

The kiddie area is small but great for toddlers and very small kids. I saw a review where someone was upset that their 16 month old fell and the lifeguard didn’t run over. They had to save their own kid. Our 2 year old had a blast and unfortunately she tripped over something and fell face down. We immediately grabbed her because we were with our kid.

There is one lifeguard and like 50 little kids. It’s no way they can see everything the entire time. They aren’t babysitters.  Watch your babies.

The park stopped twice for weather related issues but it seemed like as soon as they could open, they did. We brought in snacks and water. We also bought our own lawn chairs but didn’t end up needing them.

We ordered French fries from the snack bar. They were tasty and reasonably priced. There is also a bar. I had the strawberry margarita. It was whack but I had low expectations and it helped pass the time while the park was shut down.

The river boat tour was educational but a bit underwhelming. It was cool to see the fish and a bird but it was hard to keep the little one engaged. Older kids and adults probably like it better. The staff were super nice and knowledgeable.

Since the mermaid show is temporarily closed, they added a wildlife show but we didn’t get to experience it due to the weather. Not blaming the park though. It’s Mother Nature.

For the cost we paid, it was a great experience. We made some cool memories and although we didn’t get to see the Mermaid show, I’m so happy we went on a weekday. It never felt packed or overly crowded. We would definitely come again.
dislikes: Underwhelming wildlife show (not experienced due to weather)

reviews_attraction.text: This was a good value since it's a lot cheaper than most corn maze places but you get what you pay for. Everyone was nice but the attractions aren't ran by employees so you have a bunch of kids running around doing whatever on the rides. All kids get a free baby pumpkin. The snacks are appropriately priced. We lucked up and found a Groupon so Che k before you go. The corn maze is cool. The slides are fun for little kids. The jump pillow was hot because of the sun so make sure your little one wears socks. The hayride is included with admission. It was a good deal since we had a Groupon but I'm not sure I would have felt the same way if I paid full price. It's cool for really little kids. There was also a place to have a birthday party.

I have only been to the dog park part of this park but our rescue dog loves it. There is a dog run for all sizes of dogs. There is also a fenced in area for small dogs and one for large dogs. There's a water fountain there so your dog can drink as much water as he or she wants while running and playing.

The park is open year round but they cut off the water in the winter. Also when daylight savings time goes into effect, it gets darker earlier. The parking lot is lighted but the dog areas aren't.

Every time I've been here people have been really good with watching their dogs and picking up if the dog uses the bathroom.

If you want to give your dog a chance to burn off some energy, I strongly recommend this park.

We spent $50 on tickets for 2 adults and 3 kids. Not a bad price in my opinion. I felt like we got our money’s worth. Spent about an hour to walk through.

Everything was interesting and informative. The kids enjoyed it. It’s a tight space so if it’s a crowded day, it will take longer to move from exhibit to exhibit.

We saved $2 per ticket by purchasing online. Super cool veterans parking in the front so we didn’t have to hunt for a space.

Lots of opportunities to spend more money so bring a few singles and/or quarters. All in all, for the price, I’d recommend it.

No strollers allowed so you’ll need to carry your baby/babies. (We had a 3 year old and a 1 year old but my husband was with me to help.)

We went here for a relative’s birthday party. The reserved space is at the front by the entrance. After cake and ice cream, the kids got to run and play. Downstairs there are a few stations that the kids can play with and they are interactive.  It was cool. Our 2 year old enjoyed it. My 10 year old was bored to death.

There is an upstairs however it’s supposed to have 5 rooms and only 2 were open. It was okay but I think I would have been substantially disappointed if we had paid an actual admission fee for entrance however this was a great setting for a birthday girl turning 3 and her smaller friends and family members.

Honestly a bit underwhelming. We went on a Saturday night and the line was a ridiculous 2 hour wait. I would have most certainly sprung for the fast pass had I had any idea that it would be that long. The website said it’s usually about an hour.

The Awakened main attraction was okay. It was a lot less employees and a lot more animatronics then I expected. The second attraction, Subject Unknown was much better. It was set up so much more professional and it had more employees.

I loved having the option to take pictures with various “creatures” in between visits. I wouldn’t go back.

This was an excellent family trip. We took 5 kids aged 15 to 1 and they all had fun. There was a plethora of cool science experiment tables available that were staffed with friendly people who explained everything to the kids.

There are so many opportunities for kids to use their imagination and learn. The staff was very friendly. The museum is non-profit and the $13.95 price tag was well worth it. We ended up being there for almost 4 hours. A lot longer than we expected but the kids kept finding cool stuff to do.

Super cute collection of restaurants and stores. There is something for everyone here including a bar, sushi, Mexican food, ice cream, a corner store and more.

Normally you will need to pay for parking and keep in mind there is a homeless population in the area so you may see quite a bit of homeless people. If that doesn’t bother you, then rock on.

There are also a few nice places to take pics over here.

An awesomely me place to visit with Kids. It was so hot outside that we were happy to be inside. The cost wasn’t super high either. I was pleasantly surprised with all of the cool facts and the numerous interactive activities. There were many activities for the entire family to participate.

As a family we learned a lot, had fun, and created some great memories. I would definitely recommend this place.

An experience for everyone. Like seriously. If you are close and have the time, you should go. My husband and kids and I went and everyone enjoyed it. So much information and knowledge in one place. History and cirrwnr times. It was remarkable. A lot of interactive exhibits. No photos allowed inside but you can take a free picture at the end.

An experience we will never forget.

We saw a billboard for this spot while driving to Charleston and I’m glad we did. It was only about 5 minutes off of the highway. It looks like it’s in someone’s front yard.

It’s literally a silver enclosure that you can go inside. There is electricity inside and a bunch of random items. It was a cool photo op.

Free to go inside but there is a tip box.

Super awesome views. My husband and I visited and was very impressed. There are picnic tables, a museum, and a walking trail. At the end of the walking trail, you can hike a 3 mile or 7 mile trail.

Terrain is rough so be sure to wear comfortable and safe shoes. We want to comeback when we are better dressed and so the 7 mile trail.

This is a really nice park where quite a few events are held. There is a nice open field and a fountain that has dreams if water that kids can play in.

Across the street are multiple cute places including restaurants, a spa, and a dog grooming spot.

This is a great place to enjoy a quiet walk or being the kids to run and play.

We visited for the Christmas Lights and the kids had a blast. Tons of lights and exhibits. More than we could cover with two little ones.

The line to park is super crazy so come early, come during the week, or be prepared to wait at least 30 mins to get to the garage.

Snacks and drinks are sold inside. It was awesome.

Under heavy construction. Not a lot to do or space to walk. The playground was taped off too. It will probably be nice in a few months when all of the construction is finished.

We walked around in a big circle. One cool thing is the book box. You can borrow a book or donate books.  My kids enjoyed that piece.

So awesome that we came and I’d love to come back when I have more time. We were awestruck with all of the information available and my mother in law was so happy that we got to visit Dr. King’s birthplace and home.

If I had to lodge one complaint it would be the inability to take pictures inside the house.

My husband and daughter were very disappointed. They say it was geared towards much younger kids. It didn’t cost a lot of money but make sure if your over 13, you know that it won’t really be too scary. I wish we wouldn’t have gotten the tickets.

The Guinness World Record museum was super cool though.

This is a beautiful park. We came for a food truck festival but there were people there doing yoga, jogging, and hanging out.

There’s a nice little lake and some steps and benches. There’s ample parking in the local residential neighborhood.

The park is walking distance to the Ponce City Market.
likes: Diverse activities (food truck festival, yoga, jogging)

reviews_attraction.text:
A cute park with two main entrances. We went for the playground and my kids had a blast. Some of the playground toys were different than what you normally see. For instance I was able to ride the seesaw with my kids.

This is a beautiful park to take pictures and ample parking.

Very scenic and peaceful. My family did a scavenger hunt along the river walk and it was a blast. There is a playground and lots of places to sit and rest. I’d love to go back again and walk through to see everything that we missed the first time.

Beautiful. Lots of people, a large beach, tons of cool vendors. You can get food, drinks, and souvenirs. There are a ton of homeless people down there but no one bothered us. We got some amazing pictures. I can’t wait to go back.
My kids love it here.  The staff is really nice and it's not overly expensive. This includes the food. There is the regular trampoline and then a few other things like a foam pit and basketball goal.
A cool little park with a playground for the kids. A lot of Grayson activities take place here. The bathrooms are nasty and parking is horrible on days that the park is busy.
Cool spot for Lawrenceville events. Spacious and there is a ton of parking close by. We came here for my daughter's production with Aurora Theater.
Nice park for festivals and stuff. We went for a congo festival and it was nice and clean. It’s also located on the bus line.

Rivers Edge Golf Club: Look forward to plenty of variety, adventure and challenge on this exciting and, at times, immensely scenic Arnold Palmer designed golf course. Several holes are laid out alongside the wide, stunning expanse of the Shallotte River - as spectacular as you'll find anywhere in the Carolinas. However, visually impressive can also imply dauntingly tough, and Palmer serves up this element in no small measure.
Maintenance and presentation should be better than it was when we visited, but some allowance is made for the course's newness. Real estate is also making its presence felt, detracting slightly from the naturalness of the "high drama on the river's edge".

Turtle Point is located in a wonderfully quiet and mainly natural setting, the closest of the five Kiawah Island Resort courses to the flagship Sanctuary Hotel. This early Jack Nicklaus design was the second of the Kiawah Island golf courses to be built. It remains a thoroughly enjoyable test of golf, offering three oceanside holes into the bargain.
With real estate generally kept well behind the tree-line, there's always a pleasantly natural feel to this relatively flat but thoroughly absorbing layout. An elegant and challenging course, with its three oceanside holes adding an exciting extra dimension.

Located just north of Farmingdale, you'll find a world-class layout, the Black course, rated 5-1/2 stars, and four other 18-hole courses, all radiating out from the same large clubhouse. This out-and-back roaming layout now ranks with the best in the United States. Before teeing off on the Black (alongside the opening tee of the Green course), you are minded to read the sign at the starter's hut: "The Black Course is an extremely difficult course, which we recommend only for highly skilled golfers." Never a truer word!

If you had to choose one Robert Trent Jones Golf Trail course to represent and define all the others, then Cambrian Ridge might well be your choice. Within this 27-hole layout the outstanding Sherling and Canyon nines contain many of the characteristics frequently found on the Trail: a splendidly natural woodland and lakeside domain, lots of undulating ridges and valleys, all of which is utilised to superb effect to provide a raft of memorable, challenging and scenic golf holes.

Very much part of Californian golfing legend, Del Monte is a member of the impressive stable of courses owned and operated by Pebble Beach Resorts. Compared to its peers, which lie to the west on the ocean-facing shoreline of the Monterey Peninsula, Del Monte poses a less demanding and less scenic golfing challenge.
The final holes of this pleasant parkland course are played in front of the Hyatt Regency hotel, the 17th green located just a few feet away from the hotel terrace.

Oak Point sits on the opposite bank of the Kiawah River from the other Kiawah Island courses. Although accessed before you arrive on Kiawah Island itself, the course is very much part of the Kiawah Island family, benefitting from the same high standards of maintenance and presentation.
The wonderful closing hole is played alongside the expansive marshland of the Kiawah River, with the marsh cutting in twice, once across the fairway and again in front of the green.

Few courses in the Coachella Valley can boast a closing stretch of holes as stunning as those found on La Quinta's Mountain course, rated 4-1/2 stars. There are few courses in the world that possess a par-3 as fabulous as the Mountain's 16th. Pete Dye's probing and challenging design will require good-quality driving and accurate approach work to avoid the combination of expansive bunkering and small mischievous pot bunkers around the greens.

Coronado Golf Course: In the San Diego area, golfing on a municipal coastal gem is not limited to the mighty, US Open-hosting Torrey Pines. Every local golfer will happily tell you about the special attractions of a very busy and scenic golf course, located on Coronado island just a mile west of downtown San Diego. Coronado will not disappoint - a lovely parkland course, occupying a very special bayside setting.

Like the other four Bear Trace courses designed by Jack Nicklaus for Tennessee State Parks, the layout at Harrison Bay benefits from a wonderfully natural setting. It's not difficult to see why this course in particular is often rated the best of them all. Although just 20 minutes north of downtown Chattanooga, it's well worth going out of your way to have this course on your Tennessee itinerary.

This links-style layout nestles in a natural environment in the El Chorro Valley, just east of Highway 1 between San Luis Obispo and Morro Bay. There is no housing on or around the course, which boasts some dramatic elevation changes, with forced carries over water and rocky arroyos.The par-71 course rises and falls by 300 feet twice, offering wonderful views of the surrounding El Chorro Valley.

The Beach and Kings' courses at Mauna Lani Resort are two well-rated and pleasantly testing layouts. The Kings' course is an open parkland course that should not disappoint, with many attractive features and several excellent holes to enjoy. One to include on your play list if you are in the area. At this Stay&Play venue, the on-site accommodations are located close to the golf facilities.

The Wailea Golf Club is home to three 18-hole championship golf courses, which include the highly-ranked Gold course and the also well-rated and popular Emerald and Blue courses. The Blue course is a tree-lined parkland course that should not disappoint, with many attractive features and several excellent holes to enjoy. One to include on your play list if you are in the area.

Oyster Bay Golf Links, stunningly located beside the Calabash River and its expansive marshlands, is a layout that exudes maturity and style at every turn.
Generally good-width fairways, large, well-paced and seriously undulating greens, and quite deep, high-lipped bunkering all reinforce the quality and enjoyment that Oyster Bay holds in abundance for the visiting golfer.

Eagle Creek Golf Club, rated 4-1/2 stars: Although laid out as part of a residential development, this is undoubtedly one of Orlando's most enjoyable and well-rated courses. Always well maintained and presented, comprising two nine-hole loops, the course is distinctly linksy and Scottish in character, open and exposed to the wind when it blows through here.

Although shorter than the signature Links course at Wild Dunes, the Tom Fazio designed Harbor course is also going to test every facet of your game, and most especially your ability to hit straight rather than long.
Some amazing real estate seemingly sits in the middle of the vast marshlands. A memorable course ... absolutely; tough and testing ... you bet!

Torrey Pines (South course): In common with many of the legendary seaside courses of Britain and Ireland, Torrey Pines is both a municipal golf facility as well as home to a wonderfully testing and immensely scenic layout. The South course, as distinct from the also enjoyable and well-rated North, is a test of golf that stands alongside the world's finest.

The Rookery at Marco Golf Club is home to a well-rated championship golf course. You'll need to stay at the Marriott Marco Island if you want to play this course, which is generally reserved for members and resort-guests only.
Plenty of golfing challenge, a well-crafted design and usually good upkeep all contribute to the appeal of this course.

The layout might only weigh-in at 6000-yards with a par of 70, but Mt Woodson, rated 4-1/2 stars, is also one of the most dramatic and naturally beautiful golf courses around San Diego. Located amidst the hills and slopes of boulder-clad Mount Woodson, this challenging course is a tribute to the design skills of Lee Schmidt and Brian Curley.

Located just south of Las Vegas, the tightly folding foothills of Black Mountain are home to a desert-style course that stands with the best. Beyond Cascata’s private gates lies a stunningly natural landscape, onto which Rees Jones has crafted a fabulous par-72 layout. This is unquestionably a desert version of golfing nirvana.

River Bend Links at Casino Strip Resorts is a good quality layout, popular with local golfers. This links-style course contains a variety of attractive holes and pleasant features, which should provide an enjoyable test of golf at a generally affordable rate. Worth a visit if you are in the area and have some time to spare.

The Beach and Kings' courses at Mauna Lani Resort are two well-rated and pleasantly testing layouts. The Beach course, which winds its way along historic lava flows near Anaehoomalu Bay, is a tree-lined and open parkland course that should not disappoint, with many attractive features and several excellent holes to enjoy.

World Tour Golf Links, rated 3-1/2 stars, is a championship layout that ranks with some of the best in South Carolina. This tree-lined and open parkland course provides a wonderful test for your all-round game, with many attractive, skilfully crafted and challenging holes to enjoy. A must play if you are in the area.

Mauna Lani Resort (South course): The Francis H. I'i Brown North and South courses at Mauna Lani Resort are two well-rated, pleasantly testing and immensely scenic layouts. Both courses include many attractive features and several excellent holes to enjoy ... with lava flow and ocean views a plenty.

Mauna Kea Golf Course, located on the northwest coast of Big Island, lies at the very end of the lava field of the volcano Mauna Kea. Here you'll find a championship layout that ranks with some of the best in the Hawaiian Islands. A must to include on your Hawaii Island play list.

Wailua Municipal Golf Course is a well-rated and pleasantly testing layout. Plenty of golfing challenge, a well-crafted design and usually good upkeep all contribute to the appeal of this course. One to include on your play list if you are in the area.
