Love that it's part of the town I call home. Woo, it'll feel cold if you're hot-blooded, though. Great to visit for a relaxing day or for special events - my favorite being the annual Polar Bear Plunge on New Year's. I was ignorant of other reviewer's concern until looking it up - cheap for local residents, not quite so cheap for visitors. So, Austinites: go see where your city started; visitors: it's unique and much easier to access than Hamilton Pool.

One of the best distillery tours in the States, cool to see the oldest bourbon outside of Kentucky. It can get hot and will involve a lot of moving around, but they helped with wheelchair access for our group. Beautiful property, interesting stories. Dip your own bottle. You'll get your money's worth of free tastings, but they also have local drinks in a fridge based on the donation honor system.

Went for the last X Games, and had an easy time wandering around the site. Really enjoyed that the track was stocked with Austin's local food trucks, including Torchy's and Amy's. Got pretty hot, so be prepared if going to a summer activity. Motorcycle parking was free when I went, so may be worth checking if you ride. Find a reason to check it out at least once!

Great experience for all ages. Better price than the aquarium, although also quieter. We were completely self-guided, and it was noticeably quieter when we arrived in the morning than when we left in the afternoon. Our favorites: the view from the top, and the jets on the deck. Just watch your head if you're over 6' (1.85m) tall!

Remote and smaller than their 'big brother', so take advantage of the peace and quiet. Extra friendly rangers. Small gift shop area. Hiking as good as at the other location, with fewer distractions, and much closer to Kailua-Kona. Now that the volcano has stopped erupting, expect this outpost to become more evenly popular.

Magical location - no wonder it's important to Hawaii culture. You'll want it to be as sunny as possible, but also needs to be morning. Rainbow is viewable from below (super easy and accessible) or above the falls (little bit of an uneven hike, but with a railing). Can make for a short visit on the way to/through Hilo.

Exceptionally quiet and easy to access from the Courtyard King Kamehameha. Better than any hotel pool, plus historically significant landmarks are right there. Plenty of fish to see if snorkeling, but also just fine for pulling up a chair and umbrella (included if at Courtyard).

Went for a private function, and had a pleasant evening experience. Decent beer selection, good fajitas, and nice atmosphere. Stayed cool enough even on a midsummer evening. Bring a beach volleyball for the sand court. Good place for a big family or company event.

Great spot to see ospreys, hike on rocky trails, and stop for a beach side picnic. Cooler and breezier than inland, with plenty of shade. Neat activities that vary with the seasons. Not a bad drive from Portland, and much closer than bigger parks. Worth the trip.

Pros: exactly the kind of thing your 2-7 year old will enjoy and wear themselves out on. Con: expensive for non-members - $11 per person, including kids > 2, plus paid parking. Better value for locals with annual pass or those willing to spend several hours here.

The best time to go kayaking is in the morning, since the Tom Miller Dam usually releases water in the afternoon to meet peak Austin energy demands. Parking is dismal on afternoons and weekends. Be warned that there are no restroom facilities on the island.

The retail shop has been closed for years, but you're still welcome to visit during business hours to see the Guinness Record-holding geodesic rotating globe (the coolest part the the place, anyway). It can be a really quick stop right off of the highway.

Bring a can of spray paint! Crowds are diverse and friendly, but can be avoided for better pictures at off hours or times of the year. No signs on I-40, but the frontage road is two-way, so you can easily pass it and come back to it on the frontage.
dislikes: No signs on I-40 (Excluded as it is related to transportation)

reviews_attraction.text: More rugged terrain to reach, including two massive steel truss bridges (very cool key feature). Sharp, new visitor center. As well informed on the tour as other major distilleries. Underwhelming 'specials' at the gift shop, but fine place overall.

Great space for both professional muralists and amateurs. Don't make the mistake we did - take spray paint and get creative! Just try not to cover the big, high quality works. Getting to the upper tiers is a hike, but worth exploring all facets.

If you're visiting Maine, it's the thing to do. Free, beautiful, and iconic. Frequent fog, but can wait it out. Consistently cooler than inland. Grab a lobster roll from nearby food truck while visiting.

Great free zoo! Plenty of active animals. Scenic views of Chicago. Plenty of shade to help keep cool. Parking can be difficult (a nearby deck goes for $19), but it's hard to beat overall price and value.

The fastest and easiest way to see evidence of volcanic activity, plus the massive central crater. Starting point for several hikes, but also pleasant for those with limited time or accessibility. Hot!
Easy enough hike with a great view of the cascading pools. No swimming was allowed during a recent visit due to high rain-related flows, but it was still exciting to see. Be sure to bring bug spray!
Well curated, and surprisingly balanced (not too Texas-is-the-best). Can easily spend a few hours here; many informative exhibits. Bigger than it looks. Every Texan should visit!
Better than most along the Urban Bourbon Trail. Quality products; clean, bright decor; pleasant staff. Their mornings are even better priced than at many places around LouKen.
For those inclined, the Fort Worth Ale Trail that is organized through the visitor's center is one of the neatest ways to experience a city's local beer scene. Look it up!
Excellent free museum, recently modernized filling a philanthropic influx. Cleverly curated and arranged pieces. Quiet and peaceful. Really impressive part of campus.
Nice place to visit on a bike, once you're here. Little bit treacherous biking on 620, but worth it. Great views.
Hidden gem of a monument in the Ham. Largest cast iron statue in the world, and with a bare butt to boot!

Good place to spend 3 hours or so with the kids.  Get there when they open!  By noon the line is out the door.  If you get there at 9am by the time you finish it is lunch time and you won't feel so rushed or crowded.  A bit expensive, 2 adults & 2 kids will cost you $74 for just the aquarium & science exhibits.  Right now there is a kids play area based on Mr Potato Head that is just incredible and is great for small children to blow off some energy. I believe this goes away sometime in May 2015 though.  They have added a wilderness adventure area as well where you can zip line between trees and do some climbing and repelling. We did not do that but it looked like fun.  All in all a good time.

Wonderful experience all the way. This is not your typical zoo. It is a drive through safari where your vehicle is basically bumrushed by a lot of mammals of various types. Very fun time to meet everything from llamas to bison up close and personal. You can buy feed at the gate to feed the animals but not really required.     There is also a walk through zoo with various animals as well that was equally entertaining.  A bit pricey compared to other traditional zoos but you get a very unique experience and you can tell these animals are very well taken care of.

Only thing I can say bad about the place is it is TOO big! We got most of the way through and it wore us out! Absolutely gorgeous Japanese garden and the kids will love all the rocks and steps and places to explore. The treehouse area is phenomenal. We did the entire nature preserve loop and it did us in! Make sure you have good walking shoes and a bottle of water if you intend to explore. It will take you the better part of a day to see it all.

They have made amazing strides in creating a unique experience.  The period attired characters are a fountain of information.  They are not just actors but historians as well and are pleasant to talk to.  Some of the buildings were actually built by them by hand using 17th century techniques.  This an almost unknown park for being the site of the 2nd colony in Virginia and home to John Rolfe and Thomas Dale.  A must see if you are in the area!

Have spent many an afternoon here with the kids.  The trails are extensive and well marked.  They wind down to the marshes as well. The playground is just enough to keep them occupied and are clean and well maintained. Have been to B-day party at one of the pavilions and they are a great place for large gatherings. Bathrooms are good. Catch a ball game here as well!

This is great place to bring the kids! They have really gone out of their way to make it a family experience.  The prices are reasonable and only complaint is it can be busy and hard to get someone's attention.  Bring cash or check they do not take plastic.  The website directions are easy and it is 10 mins off route 25.

One of the better historical parks.  Extensive grounds and several old buildings that made up the old Courthouse and village proper.  Interesting film and exhibits as well as a guided tour of the house where the surrender was confirmed. Volunteer ranger that did tour had fascinating stories you will not hear elsewhere.

I must say that they have some really nice pieces here and the admission is quite reasonable. However, if you don’t like to have kids in your museum then just don’t let them in.  A 10 & 12 year old know better than to touch anything. When a boy is 3 feet from a painting he is not “too close”.  A little over the top.

Definitely worth seeing when in Memphis. I caught a show at the Soundstage here and went through the Elvis Memphis museums. A good collection of not only Elvis but the Sam Phillips / Sun Records exhibit was especially interesting. $10 to just park kind of sucks though and seems like a needless charge.

Very interesting and informative self guided tour. Was just fun exploring the ship and seeing how the crew would live. Give yourself a couple hours to fully experience everything. Admission includes the aviation building and the USS Drum, a dry docked WWII submarine. Good souvenirs in gift shop also.

Can spend an entire morning taking in the sights and history here. Kids will love all the batteries to climb up on. Pristine views, crazy tunnels and arches are just a small part of it. Go see the discovery center first to get a good idea of how to do the tour. The film there is very informative.

This is a nice small zoo that you can roll through in less than an hour if you want. It is also adjacent to a large park that has a playground and such. Better to get the family membership if you plan on visiting more than twice with a family of four.

Good place to spend a couple hours checking out some awe inspiring scenery.  There is also a snack bar that has some decent food for a decent price. Shuttle service back to parking lot so you do not have to walk back up all those     uneven stairs.
Very pretty views, friendly and attentive staff and some good wine.  Great wrap-around porch to chill out in an Adirondack chair.  BBQ vendor there on the weekend which was a welcome surprise.
Very interesting and informative museum about the early manned and unmanned space flights. Lots to see and read. Plan on spending 2-3 hours here. Some really amazing exhibits and history here.
Interesting museum filled with the history of both the county area and the meat industry that grew up around it.  My two small kids had fun as they have some hands on stuff for them to do.
Wide open expanses of nature mixed with a wonderful children’s area. Especially liked the off the road trails and rustic structures. Vibrant colors and foliage. Well worth being a member!
The rangers here are fantastic!  They know their stuff and freely give it.  The exhibits and displays are also good and really fill you in on one of the final battles of the civil war.
Nice gallery and gardens with a reasonable price. Good for a stroll and mostly impressionist and post-impressionist artwork with a smattering of sculpture and pewter works.
Really interesting park that you can explore at your own pace while also checking out the downtown area.  A true historical gem that is good for the entire family.
You can spend the better part of a day exploring everything to see.  It is amazing that this is free also.  Free parking in the area on the weekends as well!
Very well crafted historical museum with a LOT to look at and explore. You will easily spend 2+ hours to do the tour. Staff very friendly.
Anyone who is interested in the railroads should go see this place.  The model train set up has to be the most detailed I have ever seen.
Crack a geode!  Great place to take the kids and learn about rocks, fossils and minerals.  Friendly staff and great items for sale.
Yes we had to stop to get a picture in front of the tower. Looked like a decent park as well!

I guess for the right people, this place would be great, but it definitely wasn't for us. We went in not knowing what to expect.  Make sure you're prepared if you go.  They feed live rats to the gators and large snapping turtle.  Yes, this is the circle of life, but we weren't prepared to see this.  It's also very, very small.  Looking at the animals was fun, but I can't say we will ever be back or that we recommend this place.  The animals didn't seen happy and most of the cages were small.

This place is so much fun!  We did the treasure hunt first.  The guide in character explained the hunt and gave us our first clue.  There's a series of clues and puzzles to solve and you get to use a metal detector to find the burried treasure at the end.  Then we panned for gold.  The employees took time to teach us the proper technique and we panned for gold, finding a few pieces.  We're looking forward to coming back and trying the disc golf course next time, as it looked really fun!

We loved this place!  I wish there was something comparable near home.  If we lived here, we would definitely become members.  Everything is kid friendly.  The ride attendants were also great with kids. The animal areas were also very nice, the goats were our favorite today. My son even loved reading the books from the little library.  Excellent value for your money.

This was an amazing adventure for our toddler.  The staff was very friendly.  The ride was entertaining.  The food prices on the train were very reasonable.  The best part for my toddler was that he got to go in the engine, meet the conductor, and sit in the driver's seat.  It's a great trip and is the least expensive of the mountain trains available.

This musuem is perfect for young kids.  My toddler loved it.  It's the little things like stools everywhere and little ladders by the exhibits.  It was really nice that he could explore on his own without having to be picked up constantly.  He was also fascinated by the compost microscope.

This place is a one of a kind experience.  It is small and perfect for small children.  We didn't end up going in the cave, but everything else was amazing.  We absolutely loved petting and feeding alp of the animals.  I never thought we'd ever pet and feed kangaroos!

This place was amazing.  The boat and tram rides are included in the price.  I highly recommend taking the boat.  We saw lots of animals and the captain was very informative.  The park itself was excellent, it is very kid friendly and there are tons of animals to see.

This is a really nice small water park.  If you are bringing a toddler, make sure to bring a cloth (reusable) swim diaper.  They make you purchase one for $6 if you don't have one.  All of the staff were friendly and there were tons of activities for my toddler.

This place is great!  I didn't know what to expect, but it has a bit of everything.  The garden is huge and is has a lot of birds and some turtles too.  All three generations in our group loved this place.  Definitely a good value for the price.

This is a great place!  It's well away from the crazy busy main tourist area.  We were the only ones here. The boardwalk makes for a nice short walk.  The little beach area was a perfect first beach experience for my toddler.

Amazing place to visit.  Make sure to book your tours 2ish weeks in advance.  You will only get the self guided tour if you try to purchase at the visitor center!  The tour guides were great.  We'll definitely be back.

We tried to go to Clearwater Beach, but all the lots were full so we decided to keep driving south, and found this really nice beach.  Parking was only $5, and the beach wasn't crowded at all.  It was also very clean.

This is such a neat place and it's free!  This is a great place to bring kids, tons of planes to explore and touch outside and a couple that they can sit in inside.  I highly recommend stopping if you are in the area.

This is an excellent zoo!  My son had a blast.  They have a safari train that takes you through part of the park.  You can also feed a lot of the animals here.  It was just the right size for a 1/2 day trip.

This garden has a little bit of everything.  It's a really nice walk.  My toddler enjoyed the pond which has turtles and huge catfish.  We enjoyed the variety of plants, especially the prehistoric boardwalk.
This is a small museum, but it has a lot of interesting exhibits.  They also have a kids room that is very hands ok; cabinets full of things for kids (or adults) to play with and/or create.
Crowded and overrated, taking pictures was fun, but there should somehow be a people limit or something so that one can move around and look rather than dodge hoards of people with cameras!
This playground is still as amazing as I remember it from visiting as a kid.  My toddler loved it.  The huge concrete slide is one of a kind.  The carousel is also fun.
This place is amazing!  Inside kids can view animals and interact with exibits.  Outside, they have more animals and lots of nice walking paths.
Great mini golf place.  They have a course specifically for little kids and my toddler loved it.  I also loved that under 5 is free!
Great views of the bridge and there's an old fort to explore.  Also, you can park here in the free lot and visit the bridge too. 😊
My toddler loves this place! They have excellent age appropriate activities. Getting the climb membership is also a great value.
This place is terrible, there's nothing here.  We were going to walk around before our zoo time, and it was worthless.
This is an amazing park!  The splash pad is great for the little ones.  It also has two different play areas
This is an excellent park!  It has a playground that my son loved, lots of open space, and a skate park.

Very crowded and some campsites are nearly useless with no grass, not even paved pad for an RV. Plenty of muddy deep dangerous ruts, plenty of mud to park in and track in your RV or camper or tent.
Many teens, tweens walking the width of the roadway at dusk, nightfall so be extremely careful and drive slow since they won't get off the road due to the mud.
It would be extremely helpful to place site #s on a posted sign at the end of each loop. Very confusing layout plus since it's one way traffic becomes time consuming searching each loop for site #. And those are painted on the end of the paved pad, hard to see in the dark.
The restrooms and shower rooms, laundry are kept clean. The staff are wonderful. Some of the volunteers, camp hosts for this weekend were not at all wonderful.
Playground great for the kids as well as miniature golf. Movie was Tim Burton's Dumbo, crafts were in the morning for the kids. Marina area very nice too.
Overall it's a nice place except the blonde camp host and the muddy ruts.

2nd time here although the 1st time was many decades ago. I enjoyed touring the home and artifacts of Hemingway but I have read his novels and watched movies based on his books. Very interesting life of an American man and his adventures.
You don't have to have done this but it gives perspective of his home, life and  adds to it. The guides help with those who know nothing about him or his work. We self toured.
The cats are everywhere and their ancestor was already inbred with the 6 toes from being on a ship. They don't care about the humans being there anymore than your own cat, only if they want to interact do they.
I will say it was packed with visitors and noticed quite a line to get in later in the day.
More than my 1st visit long ago.

Parking was terrible. In a field with mud ruts, not appropriate for any vehicle that wasn't high profile. No allowances for handicapped. No consistency on exiting either.
It was readily apparent to anyone familiar with hot air ballooning that the event wasn't going to occur. No participant was had out their fabric laid out for inflation. The announcement of the cancellation was not made until most of them had loaded up and left the event.
It should have been labeled basket event not balloon fest.
Plenty of paid activities for children and food. 6 Port-A-Potties were not enough for the amount of people, none were a handicapped version.

I have wanted to go here for years. I love Carousels, Carousel horses. The carving is a beautiful craft.
I will ride a Merry-Go-Round anywhere I find one. Love to see historic carousels and how some are saved, restored. They are beautiful.
This is in such a unique building for it with the rounded front. I live old architecture and history.
I noticed on historical marker the name of Longaberger. Such a great man he was to help sponsor these markets of our great state historic places. Shame his unique basket building for company headquarters is abandoned after he died.

This place is a treasure and it's free! Great place to go when weather is bad to break that "cabin fever".  IMAX movie cost nominal. Cafe if you need a bite to eat and nice gift shop.
We went to see new Memphis Belle exhibit Saturday, 19th, although crowded was worth it.
Valkyrie Cafe needs to tone down the sugar in all food except macaroni n cheese, I had. Made my eyes twitch after 1st bite, was not expecting candy bbq, slaw(veggies in slaw crisp as I love), lettuce, tomatoes were fresh, crisp on condiment table.
Volunteers are doing an outstanding job here.
likes: Facilities & Services: Free admission, nominal IMAX cost, gift shop, fresh cafe ingredients
dislikes: Facilities & Services: Overly sweet food (except macaroni and cheese)

reviews_attraction.text: Beautiful landscaping which is why the added "Botanical Gardens". Seems like less animals each visit. So many changes since I was brought here as a child! Saddened at each loss of life for them, especially the babies. Festival of Lights is always beautiful. Animals don't look as miserable when it's cooler outside. Elephant rocking is sad, seems stressed. Loved watching the flamingo walk around the park. Favorite visit was with son on an overnight field trip, very informative but may not be done anymore. Would love to see them borrow Giant Pandas again.

Walking towards Cinderella castle is magical
So many changes in 45 years though.
Unique shops are gone as are the trees, benches that used to be. Opening up the hub has accommodated more crowds and increased heat. Wish that guests would look at the details(story in the imagineering) instead of their phones and be more courteous to everyone. Last visit was too crowded to the point couldn't hear music. Rudeness was off the charts to the point of danger before Wishes starting.

The Malabar Farm Restaraunt just a mile down the road is a great stop before or after visit to this park. So many great events throughout the year(one of 2 parks that taps the Suger Maple trees for syrup), Christmas drcorations, haunts coming up. Great trails on this working farm.
Definitely recommend getting a reservation at the restaraunt. Also this is not a quick meal so enjoy the view, conversation as it's prepared. Savor the flavors of the meal. Very attentive staff.

Loved it! We have had their wine before in St. Petersburg. Each of us picked 5 bottles for tasting, all 10  were great. We bought 3 bottles plus the bags packaged like a Capri Sun and we got 2 glasses. They threw in a free pocket corkscrew which was a surprise. The sparkling wines are very good. Many are made from tropical fruits which give each a unique flavor.

The Frozen Ever After ridecould be improved(I miss Maelstrom). Princess dinner is great food and fun.
Detail and history here is great, new exhibit in Stave Church is Norse mythology well done. Troll in gift shop is nice photo opportunity.
Love Skool bread in cafe(under renovations).
And of course Topiary of troll, Anna and Elsa.
Meet and Greet with Anna, Elsa.
likes: Facilities & Services: Princess dinner, Food quality
Activities: Meet and Greet, Topiary displays
dislikes: Attraction Type: Ride quality (Frozen Ever After)

reviews_attraction.text:
Sacred place that deserves respect. Peaceful, beautiful. Deserves world Heritage designation to protect from idiots. Thanks to all taking care of it.
Quite upset that Ohio History Center cancelled our light the Serpent on Winter Solstice, 2017.  Everyone and everytime I attended no damage, and much respect was given to this sacred site.

It is beautiful, secluded landmark. Was confused seeing a sign posted about crime at trailhead, have never encountered(heard about) anything bad ever here. It was not there our last visit in April. Nor at John Bryan State Park, Clifton Mill, Glen Helen, or the Village of Yellow Springs have I saw any crimes. Sad if true for the area.

The imagineers did great in the building of this. Beirgarten is a must do. I love the shops, especially the plush Mickey Mouse holding a teddy bear.
The train layouts are entertaining and enjoyable(I love how they put miniature Flower and Garden Festival sign). Heard a rumor it's to be taken out but I hope that's false.

So close to the city but still peaceful. Benches at the overlook is soothing watching the river roll on by. Picnic area at the twin ponds with the ducks is shaded.
Whole park is beautifully landscaped. Of course the Krohn Conservatory and the Art Museum can easily take up a whole day.

SpaceX launch was awesome!
So much stuff to see that I wish to return. We only had a short time after driving all night to see the launch. It  has completely changed since our last visit which was free admission. Cost about $200 for family of 4.
Cafe has healthy food choices.

Longish pier with benches. Great views of the lighthouse, island. Plenty of fishing whilst I was there. There is a fee. Restrooms are available. Clean, well maintained
The beach is clean, water refreshing
1 plank on pier amused me "I'm not dead yet" carved into new lumber.

Visited campground. Sites are close. Not enough toilets, showers for the amount of people in each loop.
Playground nice for kids.
Camp store ladies very nice, store is small but lot is large.
No place for hammock camping on campsites but there is shade.

Meet Mary Poppins here sometimes. The Alice was best! No more photopass CM anymore🙁 so we don't stop to do selfies. The Tea Shop is great(Mini tours sometimes in the morning). Landscaping is gorgeous. Miss the old performers.

Hard for me to believe what once was here! So nice with plenty to do. Music in warm months is great. The festival's fun. Love the Celtic Festival, we go every year. Just to sit under tree watching river activities is alright

Outside sculptures, area nice. Would have loved to enter to see exhibits but unfortunately didn't have the time in this weekend. (So much to do, never enough time)
I hope to return to give a mote detailed review

Great park of history that seems to add more. Love the cafe and the Brewery/restaraunt. Convenient location.
The Christmas lights on the Carrillon tower are beautiful

Usually a very quiet peaceful place. Especially for a picnic.
Please everyone pick up your trash before you leave! And clean up after your dog!
Loved the gift shop. Unfortunately missed the last train of the day. I have always have loved trains, soothing sound as it rolls on the rails.
Love bears! Loved this since the beginning. Hoping it never is replaced (or shortened). Sit in air conditioning and laugh.
So fast, so tall! So worth it! Lost sunglasses, hoping no one was hurt by them being pulled by the rides force.

Great park just outside the city, full of flowering trees. Every month has a few different trees/plants in bloom, so it’s great in any season. The primary tree is camellias. Mr. Maclay was fond of them and planted numerous ones. At the back of the garden is the Maclay house which is now a museum and has some nice pieces from the family as well as a lot of nice info about gardens and camellias.

Great little Park. Quiet with some basics. Set on the confluence of two rivers, which offer boating of all sorts. There are serval picnic areas some basic facilities, and a little jungle gym. There is also a nice little drive and hike in the nicely manicured flat land. There are camping facilities as well.

What a gorgeous park. Easy to get to, easy to get around. There are a lot of little pull offs from the road to just sit by the lake and enjoy. I rented a bicycle from Nicolet beach and went for a wonderful bike ride through the forest and along the lake. The trail markings were good most of the time.

Just stopping for a quick visit, so we didn’t get to go inside the castle. But it was fun to walk around the outside. You don’t get many castles in America. Located right next to uptown to was nice to go walk around the shops and have a coffee and some gelato afterward.

It’s Hemingway’s former house! Where he did the majority of his writing. It’s really a beautiful house and very well preserved. And of course....full of 6 (and 5) toed cats, who live like kings. Not far from all the things in Key West it was a great stop.

Nice and simple park right on the water amongst the tall hotels and nightlife on sand key. It’s just a beach some grass (and native sea oats! Don’t walk in them!!) and a dog park. Walking distance from several hotels great place to visit.

Great modern art museum. Some nice pierces that make you think or are just nice to view. Some of the pieces really drew me in and it was tough to walk away. Didn’t cost too much to visit either. Quite a surprise for its downtown location.

It’s like a zoo and outdoor museum of local history and fun place. I dunno I thought it was pretty cool getting to see some local history stuff and get to know local(ish) ecology. Weather was just right, lovely for a stroll.
Simple trailhead for St. Marks trail leaving Tallahassee. Has bathrooms, shelter and parking lot. Trail is great, canopy and dedicated road. Trail end just comes out the river. Great scenery.
Wild 100ish year old house styled like 18th and 19th Century Europe. Lovely view of the water and beautiful gardens. Worth your time and a nice break from the city, like a trip back in time.
Yes, go, now! Repeatedly. I love this place, beautiful art from a wide variety of places, times and styles. Huge, free, everything I love and an awesome Chihuly to greet you at the entrance
Basic open green space. Lots of space for a country walk and is a nice drive out to it. Only shame is the freeway next door. Otherwise quite pleasant for a break from the city
Great urban respite right near down town with stuff for kids, some ponds, a Korean War memorial, amphitheater and restaurant. Great place to come and relax inside the city
Nice park with a lot of shade, some baseball diamonds, nice little Frolf course, even has a little skate park and stuff for kids to climb on. RV places are available.
It’s a neat thing to see. Probably have to wait in line to take a picture next to it. Judge carefully if that’s worth your time, or just take one in the background.
Great trip into the mangroves to check out nature, would love to do it again! Don’t let the brown water fool you, it’s very clean water, just full on nature!
Nice little park, some baseball diamonds, a couple little rose gardens and a basketball hoop hidden in the trees. A little oasis right off Thomasville rd.
Nice park on the edge of the city. Lots of things to do from play equipment, places to walk/bike, a pond to check out, frolf course and more.
Great place to get some exercise and have some fun, jumping around, dodgeball, basketball, and foam pit. Great for a group.
I didn’t get a chance to take advantage of the facilities, but it’s a great little hidden away beach with gorgeous scenery.
What a nice little park on the edge of the city. Has a little pond and a dog park along with some simple hiking trails.
Great park for hiking, swimming and taking tours of the springs. Lots of wildlife, although it does get a little busy.
Great little park with a lot of green space. A playground, a pond, swimming pool and a pavilion. Nice location too.
A hidden away little park with nice hiking and an old house. An excellent deal for the small entrance fee.
Long pier with a large area at the end. Great view of the sea, just watch out it likes to creep over!

Travelers, this is a delightful museum that tells a fantastic story of local maritime history, which is very rich in Beaufort. Basically, in a hurricane, when boats were stranded on sandbars off cape Lookout, the local men would row out to the outer islands to rescue the shipwrecked sailors. The locals shot a rope to the boat to make a pulley. Someone from the boat had to swim to the island back with the rope to make the pulley work. Lots of times sailors couldn't swim so they sent the horse to land with the rope around it's beck. When it got to shore the local took the rope off and the horse ran away and turned feral. Some of the islands have horses that have been living there for hundreds of years. Anyway, that is just one fascinating this g I learned going through that museum. There is so much more. We recommend. Enjoy.

Travellers, this is a fantastic national park with so much to do and see that is out of the ordinary and gets you close to nature. You can go to the visitors center and learn all about the park and you can get a boat tour at the visitor center as well. There is a boardwalk that takes you to the Chesser homestead which is worth the visit. It is in pristine condition and really gives you a sense of what it was like to live on this island I the swamp in the mid-1800's. It is a trip back in time . Continue on the boardwalk to the fire tower where the views of the swamp are magnificent. We saw several alligators in their natural habitat which was a wonderful experience. The scenery is worth the walk. Check this beautiful park. We recommend.

Travellers, this museum, located in the original Deerfield academy building, is one of the oldest museums in the country. It was founded in 1880. The museum is filled with early American artifacts of all kinds. There is a room full of cookware, a room of quilts, clothing and shoes, pottery, dolls, and so much more. The dollhouse is amazing as is the shoe collection. The feet were tiny in those days. Most interesting is the front door that bears a tomahawk chop mark from a home that was attacked in the Indian raid on old Deerfield. Wonderful local museum. The staff is very knowledgeable and was able to answer all the questions. A wonderful way to spend the afternoon. Open weekends. Check it out. We recommend.

Travelers, this is a must stop on you journey. It is an amazing place that tells so many American stories. I always go with a small toy and candy for the girl buried in a barrel. She is easy to find once you are there. She is just one of so many fascinating people who rest there. And they are packed in there too. Sometimes the dearly departed are in repose under the paths through the cemetery. The live oak trees are covered in Spanish moss and they shade the cemetery. It is very beautiful and reverent and engaging. The history of Beaufort told through the lives of the folks who lived there. We recommend. Enjoy.

Travellers, this is one of the most gorgeous houses in the entire United States. And infamous too. This house embodies Savannah in every way. Including the crazy past and ghost stories. The entire city is worth exploring. Read the book, midnight in the garden of good and evil and then tour savannah starting in this locale. It is across the road from beautiful Monterey square. This is a city that is easy to walk around in and is beautiful to look at. Walk up Bull st from mercer house through the lovely squares which are like jewel boxes of scenery. Check it out. We recommend.

Travellers, this state park, is small, quiet, and lovely. Nestled along the st mary's river it is quite scenic with the palmetto trails and Spanish moss covered trees. There are bike and walking trails, a playground for the kids, a fishing pier on the river, an outdoor gym for working out, a put put golf course and a lot more. The campground is lovely and private and the biking read are very pretty. Great place to spend the day with a picnic and wonderful for family reunions. Check it out. We recommend. So

Travellers, Forsythe park is a lovely place to walk or ride your bike or throw a frisbee. It is a very pretty park that serves a lot of purposes in downtown savannah. You can play tennis or basketball in the courts at the south end of the park, or you can attend the farmers market on Saturday morning and get wonderful fresh foods and handmade arts and craft items. Food in the market is farm to table with excellent meats and seafoods. There is something for everyone in this park. Check it out. We recommend.

Travellers, the Savannah riverwalk is a lovely stroll on the savannah river. There are all sorts of shops and restaurants to peruse and the walk along the river is very pretty and there is a lot to see. There are several points of entry because the riverwalk is below street level. There is one particular set of historic steps that you climb at your own risk because the ancient steps are narrow and steep. They give authenticity to the age of the riverwalk. Check it out. We recommend.

Travelers, this is a special piece of American history. The scenery is beautiful and that makes it eerie considering everything that happened there. It is almost Frozen in time. The houses that are standing on the battlefield really give you a sense of what it felt like in 1865. The bonus is Eisenhower's farm on the edge of the battlefield. It really makes you think. A moving and somber visit. We recommend you go and spend the day.

Travelers, Beaufort is a gem of a town. The beaches are gorgeous. You can find any kind of beach you want. Bustling tourists out on Emerald Isle, or the utter wilderness of the national seashore beaches, where you can drive your car on the beach and won't see anyone. Maybe pelicans. Downtown Beaufort is filled with beautiful old buildings and pirate stories. The old burying ground is worth the visit too. Check it out. We recommend.

Travelers, we really enjoyed visiting this museum. It is loaded with information about Lincoln and the civil war. This is where Lincoln finished writing the Gettysburg address. The entire town of Gettysburg is serene and peaceful and it seems strange to walk through town and places like the Wills house and know what happened in those walls. I wish they could talk. We recommend getting your American history lesson. Enjoy.

Travelers, this is a special place in new salem. Legend has it this is where metacomet, son of Massasoit, planned King Philip's war. Massasoit was the native American who met the pilgrims and helped them through the first winter. After one generation things had changed. I won't be a spoiler but find out what happened to metacomet. But, Bears den is beautiful. It is worth the hike to to this gem of a place enjoy.

Travellers, another beautiful square in downtown savannah ga. Take a stroll and enjoy the beautiful landscape and the sounds of horse and carriages church bells, and people walking around enjoying the sights of savannah. You will not be disappointed. The camilla's in bloom in March as well as the azaleas. Soon the gardenia's will perfume the entire downtown. So lovely. Check it out. we recommend.

Travellers, this is one of the jewel box squares located in downtown savannah ga. This square, like all the others, is beautifully landscaped and dripping with old southern charm. The buildings around the square are also charming. Take a stroll and sit on a bench in the square and enjoy the scenery, people watching, the breeze, the wildlife. It's all here. Check it out. We recommend.

Travellers, this is a lovely park directly on the St Mary's riverfront. The park is perfect for walking and picnicking. You can even have a gathering thee. It is close to everything downtown, all shops and restaurants. The park fountain is pretty and adds to the charm of the trees covered in spanish moss. A great place to spend a sunny afternoon. Check it out. We recommend.

Travelers, do not miss this precious local museum. Harker's island is a unique place with a unique culture going back many generations. Spending an afternoon in this museum will make you feel like you know these people. There are stores and businesses today with the names of the people who you will learn about in the museum.it is worth the stop. We recommend. Enjoy.

We went here for the model train show and it was fantastic. There were so many different train displays to see. The were huge and intricate and fascinating to watch. The details are unbelievable. There are souvenirs, shirts, hats, and all sorts of stuff including very collectible train art available for sale. It is a lot of fun. We recommend. Enjoy.

Travelers, the new England aquarium is a wonderful experience for the whole family. The penguins are charming and can be seen from every level of the aquarium. The Giants turtles are beautiful. The divers add to the fun of the visit. The manta letting tank is a hit with young folks. Check it out. We recommend.

Travelers, this is a great place to walk around and enjoy the art work. The collections are wonderful. I enjoy the Currier and Ives exhibit but there are many. The Dr Seuss garden is a great place for kids. This is a jewel in Springfield. We recommend.

Travelers, this is a wonderful place filled with an amazing variety of beautiful plants and flowers. The gardens are lovely. The plants are well done, well maintained, and definitely worth the visit. Check it out. We recommend.

Travelers, this is a fantastic small local museum with so much to offer about the area. Museum staff was nice and friendly and knowledgeable. They answered all our questions. Check it out. We recommend.
Great place to enjoy the boat rentals. My husband and I learned how to paddle board there. Beach is okay but nothing to write home about.
Great place to walk around and learn about transportation history. Always nice to do something outside and outdoors when we travel.
Great place for kids. My son loves to come here and see the exhibits. We enjoy walking through and around these giant locomotives.
Beautiful place with big view of Quabbin. New Salem, where overlook is located, is lovely too. Check it all out.

This state park is located within the Okefenokee Wildlife Refuge. It's a beautiful state park and the sites are large. The roads in the campground are narrow and full of bumps and holes. For a tall unit, you have to be very careful of overhanging branches. The sites require some leveling and are difficult for a big rig to get into. The shower house is wonderful - toilet, sink and shower all in one unit. But the soap dispensers in the sink didn't work. There is one washer and one dryer in each campground loop - $1 each. A great kids playground. Wood is $11 a bundle, so you might want to find another source. All in all, we loved camping here and will come again. Oh - there is very little cell reception - wifi at the office - and no OTA TV. We watched lots of dvds. We camped at Stephen C. Foster State Park in a Motorhome.

We stayed in the Cactus loop where there is electricity and water. These are beautiful campsites. They are all pull through, and have beautiful shelters around the picnic tables. Fire rings are also provided. The bathrooms were mostly clean. The showers are the kind where you press a button and get water for maybe a minute - then it goes off. You can soap up, wash hair, whatever - then hit the button again. The showers were roomy with plenty of hooks. There is a very nice playground for kids and some trails by the Rio Grande river.

A wonderful tour of a particularly well-kept mansion. So fun to learn about the William Randolph Hearst and the building of the castle. The tour was well organized from on-line ticket purchase to check in to greeting the guide and finding our way back. Tours are small so you can ask lots of questions. We took the Upstairs Suite tour and we're blown away.

My husband and I were amazed at the beauty and diversity in this beautiful botanical garden. It's small, but has so much! Lots of rhododendrons and Japanese maples, large trees, small trees, shrubs. A small meadow and lots of paths meandering around the garden. It's dog friendly. There are picnic tables and a short walk to the Sacramento River.

We camped here for a week. The campsites are small, but adequate and free! RV spots are level and concrete. The park has walking trails, two playgrounds, a disc golf course and so much more. Lots of open green space, lots of picnic tables and trash cans. A 40 minute drive into Houston, or 15: minutes to the Woodlands.

The most beautiful desert we have visited. Dante's View allows you to look over the entire Death Valley basin. Be sure to take the Twenty Mule Team Canyon drive, as well as the Artists Drive. Both are very colorful. Harmony Borax Works are also very interesting.

Beautiful park, even in winter.  Nice paths, all interconnected. Beech trees and sweet gum still had beautiful leaves. Some camellias still flowering. There is a model train exhibit set up for Christmas. Will be coming here again.

RV campground sites are level and fairly spacious. But the area us covered with dirt and a few tall trees. The total lack of shorter vegetation allows for little privacy. The tent campground has lots more privacy.

A really easy trail with lots of petroglyphs to view. Bring water though. You're out in the open. Lots of parking at trailhead, but no restrooms. Has trash and recycle bins. Dogs allowed but must be on leash.

Beautiful buildings in a nice forest setting. Very nice Native American exhibit. Exhibits could use better signage. Example: great sawmill, but no explanation of how it works. Indoor and outdoor exhibits.

Food is great. The talent of the players is so good I wondered why they weren't performing in a bigger City. But then, I guess that's the point of the whole night. Denali is a wonderful place to live.
Not a lot to see here - good descriptions of the Civil War in the area, specifically the Battle of Sabine Pass. Great place to watch tankers go up and down the Sabine River.
We camped in a motorhome. I don't think I'd come here again. It was okay, but with none of the privacy or spaciousness of most state parks. A bit pricey for electric only.
Very interesting tour. Be prepared for Lots of walking with steep up and down slopes. Caverns are lighted so it's easy to see the different formations and colors.
A very interesting tour of the battlefield. We downloaded the tour guide on our phones and walked then drove the path. There is a good museum and gift shop.
Very level, spacious RV sites. Beautiful grassy area next to lake. Yurts are available for rent. Dump station clean and easily accessed. And they recycle!
Very spacious sites with a sheltered picnic table and fire ring. Lots of birds and wildlife. Some shade. Electric and water. A few short walking trails.
Wonderful collection of CM Russell and other western artists. The Trigg exhibit and the lodge screens allow a view into the artist's personal life.
A smaller national park, great stops along the drive, nice picnic areas. For Covid, the visitor center store allows only one shopper at a time.
Big, wide beach with clean public restrooms. Beach is also very clean. No dogs allowed. Wheelchair accessible with a special seating area.
Cypress drive gives a lot of great info about the park and the swamp. There's a preserved farm to visit and a mile and a half walk
Not much here. Just a patch of ground with a trail around it. There is some good signage that explains this part of the battle.
Visiting in the daytime. Nice to walk around, but not hugely special. Would love to come back on a Friday night.
Beautiful place to visit to see the Springs but also to hike and to see some of the Missouri River waterfalls.
Too crowded. Bring the kids to dip their feet in the water, then get our of here and hike somewhere else.

Bling Blinky of TEXAS Shout Out: Thank you to those pioneers who came before us here at Fort Bend. Rest in peace.

What an adventure! In our 2013 Dodge Challenger - a stick-shift! OMG! The fall colors - breathtakingly beautiful at every turn and picture after picture. The Old Red Courthouse was always magical to me visiting Downtown Dallas! The gargoyles atop are looking down and I wondered who was in there! Be sure and visit Old Red now and look at the great exhibits to learn about the making of our big city here in Dallas! Bling Blinky of Texas Shout Out: Native Dallasite! Proud Texan!
