I won’t spoil it for you! Bling Blinky of Texas Shout Out: BOO! That’s no joke!! Really a great experience!! Highly recommend you be there when the clock strikes midnight!

We had a truly enjoyable experience at the Cameron Park Zoo! The beautiful old growth and trees here made the walking and interacting so pleasant! All of the animals were active and the size of the zoo was just right. A well kept secret Deep in the Heart of a Texas! Bling Blinky of Texas Shout Out:  Zookeepers and staff - the love and well care of these animals is so apparent - thank you so much!!!

Spacious and full of interesting exhibits. Some only for specific time periods so visit often! Walk outside and enjoy the outdoor garden of art and sculpture to broaden your experience amidst the treescapes and skyscrapers here in downtown Dallas. Be sure to allow yourself plenty of time to browse and enjoy everything! Bling Blinky of Texas Shout Out: Art is life! Experience it!

Cannot say enough another fabulous garden and place of serenity in Dallas. The annual color bursts and blooms along with old growth are fabulous all year long. Birds, squirrels  and rabbits are in abundance in this blessed haven. Bling Blinky of Texas Shout Out: No better place to escape the buzz of life ... come into the garden! I love it!

Chandelier Redwood Tree experience was terrific! Not a tight squeeze at all! Looking up to the canopy of the beautiful redwood you just know you can see Heaven! Bling Blinky of Texas Shout Out: It has been many years ago and I know this amazing tree is no longer there. It gave all it had to give. Rest In Peace - sweet memories.

So much to see crossing over the "Mighty Mississippi River" heading east or west! Traffic on the river - traffic on the bridge and a train just might buzz by on the trestle next to this magnificent iron bridge! State line is in the middle of the bridge! Bling Blinky of TEXAS Shout Out:  How Cool a design is this! ROAD TRIP USA!

My Great-Great Grandfather was with Stone's Brigade, Company F, Dallas/Lancaster, Texas that cold night in March 1862. I cannot imagine what he saw and felt here. Thank you to our National Park Service for preserving America's history. Thank you to All of our Veterans. Bling Blinky of Texas Shout Out: God Bless America

Had an amazing time in Historic Downtown Eureka Springs! Walking up the hill and down and all around town! Wonderful Shoppes here! Revitalized with friendly merchants and delightful dives to eat or have coffee! Bling Blinky of Texas Shout Out: A perfect weekend getaway destination!

Wonderful panoramic view from above the  landing of the great Mendenhall Glacier. Folks ready to answer questions, lots of merchandise and souvenirs to take back home! Bling Blinky of TEXAS Shout Out: Be sure and buy postcards to mail to your family and friends!

Get ready for a tour inside Downtown San Antonio on the River seeing beautiful old growth trees and historic architecture along the way. Watch out for bats hanging under the bridges! Have fun! Bling Blinky of Texas Shout Out: Rolling on the River!

Saw celebrities from way back when to Presidents and First Ladies. Loved the attention to details on expressions and clothes. Almost like seeing famous people in person. Bling Blinky of Texas Shout Out: Favorite exhibit was “The Last Supper” .

Amazing collection by Trammell Crow and family from his world travels. How generous to build such a showcase for the public to share this phenomenal collection of art! Bling Blinky of Texas Shout Out:  A must see for anyone visiting Dallas!!

A family fun destination! Kids will love the hands on busywork and curiosity invoking things to see here!  Plan a few hours of hanging out here when in Seattle! Bling Blinky of TEXAS Shout Out: I love Science - that's what it's all about!

Great bit of green space in Downtown Dallas! Flowers blooming and people scurrying about. Sit and relax and take in the great sky scraper views! Just looks up! Bling Blinky of Texas Shout Out: steel and Glass Empire amongst the garden!!

Wonderful time way up on top of the Rockies! Chilly outside! Windy! We went inside and enjoyed hot chocolate and shopped! Thank he view back down Old Fall Road was astonishing! Bling Blinky of Texas Shout Out: We will be back soon!

Even on a cold and foggy December day the Cadillacs and cattle make you smile!!  12/27/19 and on into the next Decade they will go on and on! Bling Blinky of Texas Shout Out: Y’all Come Back! Ya hear! Even our chihuahuas had fun!!!

A wonderfully preserved part of American History here literally beneath the Golden Gate Bridge. Bling Blinky of Texas Shout Out: Thanks to al who ever and thank you me to those who keep the memories alive. With respect.
The boat guide will tell you about everything your seeing along the River in beautiful Downtown San Antonio. Don’t miss it! Bling Blinky of Texas Shout Out: Enjoy the glide!!
Family here since 1846! Love the majestic State Capitol Building! Bling Blinky of Texas Shout Out: Proud to be 4th generation Texan!
Dragons and honor! Beautiful entrance here at Chinatown Dan Francisco! Bling Blinky of Texas Shout Out: Very happy to be a visitor.

We got to visit the museum today for the first opening week. My little loved it, spent 1.5 hours and could have spent double that. Dentist, vet, constructon, exercise, garden, reading, bank, cave, toddler, train, space ship, trader Joe's, plane, pizza, and a pirate ship areas. Some exhibits were more engaging than others for my two year old. The cave and space ship had very little to interact with but the other areas were awesome. He loved shopping and making pizza and digging in the "dirt". I hope in the future they have an area with climbing like a tree house or more crawling like in the cave but longer. Stool in the bathroom for littles to use the sink. We will definitely be back

Nice short hike, less than a quarter is a mile to the falls. You can go up the hill and do a much longer one. Parking at the top to hike up the hill or parking at the bottom for the falls. My toddler had a hard time walking as lots of rocks in the trail so have to pick your feet up. Follows along the creek so some steep drop offs with one creek crossing that has stepping stone. Nice pond under the falls, cliffs all around so cooler. You can go swimming or just enjoy sitting on the rocks.

Great hike. Parking lot by the road with a .5 miles walk on a dirt road to the first overlook. Currently in May 2019 looks like they are building a new parking lot right by the first overlook. Another .5 miles on a large rock strewn trail along the rim to the top of the trail headed down. 3-4 switchbacks with a cable handrail lead into the canyon. Stairs and another viewpoint at the bottom with the trail looping around to the end. Currently May 2019 stairs are broken apart and falling.

Great hike. First 1/4 mile goes up a hill above private property. Then fairly flat for 1.5 miles. Last 1/4 mile is hard, climbing up rock stair cases, walking over rocks but once you get to the hot spring it was worth it. A few good camp sites along the trail. Hot springs was a perfect temperature for my 11 month old. Too cold for most people. We went early and saw only one person on the way in but at least 6 groups on the way out. Only saw/picked up 1 piece of trash.

Beautiful tasting room, it used to be an old fruit shed. They do 6 tastings for free. They had 4 whites, 4 reds and 2 desert wines to choose from. We visited on Black Friday. It was very busy and they were doing a barrel tasting for $5 and they also had free soup and rolls for everyone. This was the only one of the 4 we visited that day that had crackers for between the different wines.

Very nice park. There is a line of food trucks at lunch time with lots of verity. Several splash pads. A couple smaller ones in the middle. A large one at the east end and another in the children's area that was pool like on one end with a stream of jets to the other end. Lots of tables and chairs in the shade to eat or relax at.

We love the playground for our one year old. It is mostly for younger kids ages 2-5 so he is able to walk around most of it without to much help. It is fully fenced except the one entrance so I can let my little one have a little more freedom then usual. Four baby swings and four slides with a couple of tunnels. Very nice park.

Nice large playground for the kids and a large open field for them to run around in. Restrooms right by the playground. To keep the kids in view you do have to move around some, especially if they are younger. Four baby swings that my child loved. There is a fence between the road and the playground but the rest of it is open.

Very nice park in the winter. They plow the path so it was nice and snow free. Lot of kids were having a great time sledding down the small hill. Several stations to get poop bags for the dog. You can walk out onto the frozen lake from here, several people were out ice fishing.

Nice drive back to the state park, you go past a hot spring. Road is pretty skinny at times so need to pay close attention. Three boat ramps. Lots of people out enjoying the water on a hour day. A small little store at the second camping area. Lots of parking.

A great large wooden playground and park. Small parking area. A littler kids area with only a couple of swings. Old west theme to it. Bathrooms were fairly clean especially for being in a public park. Large open grassy area and several picnic tables.

Beautiful park. Came here on a Saturday sunny fall afternoon. Parking lot was full and every group had a photographer with them including us. Lots of benches with beautiful backgrounds. A pond, grassy area, and ducks.

Stopped in the parking lot at 5:00am to rest since was part of the rest stop parking lot. Two RVs were parked for the night as well. Was pretty quiet until about 6 when people started to head to work.
Great park right next to the library. A fully fenced in playground great for the smaller kids age 2-5. This will definitely be our favorite place on sunny days with all of the shade trees.
A small playground. Two baby swings. Three slides. Candy cane stripes on the legs of the swings. Large grassy area, plenty of street parking. Right down the street from the University.
Parking for the hike, about 8 cars can nose in and more along the road. No turn around for trailers. A pit toilet at the beginning of the trail. It is all private property around it.
This was a very nice park. Had a large splash pad to play on. Although the water has lots of chlorine in it. Nice grassy hill for the kids to climb and so on.
Great little park. Definitely more for older kids. My 3 year old did not like the slides. Big grassy field for them to play in. Port-a-potty for a restroom.
dislikes: Slides not suitable for young children

reviews_attraction.text: Great park, a pond and view of the river. Small playground and bathrooms. Kids liked the little play fort and there was a changing table in the bathroom.
Totem pole. Very cool to see. Small beach by the gravel parking lot. $5 entry per person for the totem park now. Self pay station
Great playground to stop at. Also has the swimming pool beside it. Creek runs through the park and lots of large shade trees.
Love the free days at the zoo. The new male lion was espicially best to see. Can't wait until the construction is done.
Nice large parking lot. Was annoying that cars were parking in RV spaces even though plenty of room for them.
Great place to spend the day. On low tide you can go out on the sand bar. Pretty popular with the locals.
Nice view is the lake and island from here right from your car. No need to walk unless you want to

THE BIGGEST RIP OFF EVER. do not go, do not waste your time and a lot of your money. the people are rude and poorly staffed. people go all the way out there, and then you cant drive to the site, you are forced to pay for the shuttle, and the whole package tour that no one wants anyway. and to make it worse NO CAMERAS ALLOWED, NOT EVEN PHONES. they literally take you through a metal detector before you go on the bridge. they only do this so you have to take a photo with their company and pay like 75$ more for the pictures.

THIS IS THE BEST TOUR GUIDE LOCATON the greatest natural wonder I have ever seen. way better than upper antelope canyon, great personal guides on small cheep tours. go for the two morning "photographer" tours, you get a whole hour instead of just 30 min, and the lighting is at its best. not nearly as hard a climb as I thought, im a big guy and found this space accommodating.

Don't wear flip flops. Some rough gravel along the way. You will feel every bump. Bring a water bottle and wear sun block. Totally worth it. With the buss from downtown this can easily become a half day thing. Spend time at the top. Go early or late to beat the crowds. Last walk in is at 430pm

I love architecture so this was my main reason to visit Sedona. There was a lot of people there. Sont bother driving to the top. There wont be parking. Park on the street and enjoy the views and different angles. Thwre is a golf cart that will drive you up and down for free  or donation.

Great grounds and views. But sadly the house itself is so small, they only let you see like 3 rooms mostly topped off. Not as good as his other public houses. Very friend people though. And cheap only 7$ good if you're a die hard FLW fan. Also drive by ennis house.

Amazing site. Much easier to get to with a car. But bus from honolulu is about an hour each way, so may not be worth it. There really isn't much there. Just one room you can get into with the giant budah. Pretty lake with koi and birds you can feed

I didn't love this place. Kind of small. Lots of toys and miniatures in the grand hall. It does have an electric mix of international pieces. I was there less than an hour.  Not worth 12$ but it is a good deal as part of the 30$ culture pass.

Best thing I saw downtown. Loved the russia exhibit. A lot of the space was closed for renovations summer 2017. I wish the ticket had been discounted. Don't get tricked paying for their parking. Cheaper is only 2 blocks away

Half of the museum is closed right now for renovations. But they still charge full price. There were only really 2 small exhibits. It's worth it if you buy the 30$ culture pass for all the local museums. Nice roof top view

Really the only reason to go is the waterfall which you can swim in. 16$ to get in. The plans are all pretty wild looking and just blend into nature. Nothing spectacular or overly maintained. Easy walk.
Really geared toward the under 10 crowd or those with kids. Huge building but a whole floor for administration? And then one gallery closed for remodel sucked paying 20$. Love the planetarium
Expensive, but worth the 18$. Go on a cool day or early. Most of its outside obviously. Inside is ok, but it's all pretty much the same upstairs. No photography inside at all, that blows.
It's worth it if you go to the main building and get this one for free. The current African art exhibit is lovely but small. I can't imagine paying for it by itself
Awsome place. Don't forget to walk around rhe surrounding blocks and the ally ways. There is much more of his work in the neighborhood. Very funky non tourist place
It's nice, but so over priced. I don't know what all the money goes to. 15$ per person and I was barely there 15 minutes. .. nice people but, I'd skip it
Not as Architecturally amazing as the London eye. But very tall. And a great thing for orlando. Best to go at dusk or night when the lights come on
Very small gallery not a full museum. Some nice pieces non of her most famous ones though.over priced. 13$ all I could stay was 15 min max
Need 6 stars. Best thing in the city. Free lobby. Cheap, only 4 dollars to go I to the rooms. One of my favorite sites in the usa
One of the best ones in town. Cheaper if you do the 30$ culture pass which includes lots of other museums too. Great architecture
Not worth the walk or uber ride. Maybe if you already have a car and are trying to fill time. Best thing is the view of Alcatraz
Only one floor. Kind of simple place. I went on a donation night. Wouldn't think it was worth the full cost of admission
It's a shame they don't do tours. But if you're a die hard FLW fan it's worth checking this one out after hollyhock.
Fun little short trails. No real map, it's easy to get sort of lost but some fun sites to check out along the way
It's worth the cost one of only 3 rotating teams in the world. Great views at the top. You can hike up there too
Not much to see in the winter. But I went for their night time glow show for the holidays. Very pretty lights.

Used to love this place for a quick hike. Some great views of the LA Basin, on a clear day you can see all the way to Palos Verdes. Parking, if you proceed straight in, past the first parking area (ignore the suckers who turn left immediately), usually is ample, even if it costs a few bucks.'

However it's definitely gotten more crowded over the years, and maybe it's all the rain this year, but we didn't remember the trails being so overgrown in previous years. Maybe it's old brains and bad memories from the college days?

Total tourist trap... but to their credit the parts of the mansion itself that you are allowed to see are very, very well done and well taken care of.

Not sure it's worth the money to visit, especially if you go when it's crowded-- best to go at off-peak times to really see the inside and appreciate the history. And if you're a fan, you could probably spend many, many hours here.

But it's part of American history, and as such, is worth a stop if you're in the area.

Alaska is so full of scenic views, it's hard to give this one 5*.

But it's literally the second scenic view outside of Anchorage when you head south, and the first scenic view with a real parking area, a little prominence you can spend three minutes hiking out to, and the views on both sides of the prominence are worth a few minutes of your time.

Considering you're maybe five minutes from Anchorage, I'm not complaining!

Total tourist trap and not cheap. Or if you're an Elvis fan, a well-preserved and surprisingly detailed museum to Elvis' life.

It can be seen both ways. The cost is not cheap, but the experience has much to offer if this is your thing. If it's not your thing, then it's really up to you if it's worth the time and money-- if so, at the very least, go off-season so you don't have to deal with the crowds.

Great park but usually seems to be full of huge groups who have (reserved? Just showed up super early?) taken sections of the park for all day picnics, so a bit harder to drop by casually unless it's literally for just a quick drink of water.

That isn't a knock against the park, which is reasonably well kept and a nice size considering how busy it is. Ample parking too.

Some exhibits here are always worth a visit-- especially Space Shuttle Endeavour!

The rest, tho, I would check to see before you go, at least as adults. Kids and families, OTOH, should always have a good time here. The IMAX always has interesting science/nature showings for kids.

And yes, there's an A-12 Blackbird outside for airplane geeks.

A refreshing change from the Mojave desert just south, although facilities here are a bit limited and access is via dirt roads that, while good for 90% of the road, are a bit more real-off-road than most guests are going to expect. (aka this might be the one time the mall-running SUV actually touches more than smooth, well-graded dirt!)

A beautiful national park. Definitely do a day cruise if you can, it's such an inaccessible place for cars and on foot for most people.

If you can take a few days or weeks off to backpack in, you can see a lot more, but since the park is a large part water and marine wildlife, I'd still recommend a cruise to complete your experience.
dislikes: Inaccessibility by car and on foot

reviews_attraction.text: Canyonlands National Park has at least one famous arch, and this is it. There's more, but it's a short, easy hike to Mesa Arch, and it's unique in that it's basically right at ground level. Come early if you can to beat the heat, or come late to soak in the night sky.

Excellent collection of American and Western European art. Not a whole lot from other areas, but it’s so well done it’s hard to fault the limited geographic scope. Plus they have one of the only (perhaps the only?) Leonardo da Vinci in the USA?

Last and newest of the Space Shuttles. The temporary pavilion is clearly less than what the full stack is going to be, yet it's still worth a visit, even if you've seen the other Space Shuttles at the Smithsonian or Kennedy Space Center.

Miniature hoodoos = goblins? And for some scale, there's a massive butte at the edge of the park. For an out of the way state park it's still very impressive. Remember to bring lots of water, it's hot as hell in the summer.

There are apparently lots of beautiful arches outside of Arches National Park. This one is practically right across the highway, and is well worth a visit. Fewer tourists and at least in the morning glow, a beautiful view.

Perfectly decent casual hike. Not quite flat, but about as flat as one could reasonably expect.

The pools in late fall are not all that impressive--- perhaps another time of year with more water, they would be?
Great outdoor venue, long lines at concessions, and parking is ample but usually has an excruciating wait to get out after a show- it's usually packed plus a lot of the lots are stack parking.
Nice enough park for some very short hikes, with decent elevation gain. Just remember to coordinate parking with your friends beforehand, less you end up on opposite sides of the park!

Great museum with fantastic cars. But they've gotten very corporate lately, and the manufacturer influence is very, very strong.

If you can get over than bit, it's quite enjoyable.
Comfortable park and dog park. A few years ago I would've said it was way out of town, but these days it abuts a bunch of townhouses and stuff, it's basically a nice suburban park.
Nice viewpoint right off the road. The gap between the trees, the road crossing or the proper trail just a few feet below... no matter what time of day it's worth the (quick) stop.
Great place for a baseball game. Has the historic feel and the well-lived-in atmosphere of a good established ballpark, even if leaving the parking lot is a bit of a nightmare...
Pretty damned cool, and a very accessible ice cave all things considered-- not many of those you can just park at and then walk ~1.2 miles to via flat ground!
Great little park for medium sized group outings. Maybe even medium-large groups. Convenient parking, basketball court, shaded tables and adjacent restrooms.
Smallish, basically a gift shop, but some great knowledge by the park rangers inside. And free wifi, which is more useful than anything else.
Old school but a classic. Parking can be a nightmare- ample but lots of traffic not only to get there, but to park.
Kind of a fun place for families and kids, plus a nice enough little hill to get a decent view across Puget Sound.

Quite the transformation to the geography to the area.  A boat ramp to nowhere, new black beach, and roads and sidewalk to dead ends.  I must include the corroded showers that served swimmers at a different time.  Now, they are sentinels of copper corrosion standing nowhere near water.  It is amazing to see new lava all around and the red house untouched by it, by chance? It certainly is a reminder of how vulnerable people are to the elements.  For people who are here for the first time, imagine what this place looked like at one time, for those who were here prior to lava flows, remember the lushness of the place, the hot springs, all that once was.  It is exciting to think about what this place will be like 20 years from now, like a marker in time waiting for change.  About the boat ramp area, it makes for a great swimming hole, I wonder if there a possibility of extending a breakwater and a channel to the ocean once more? There are so few opportunities to launch a boat on this side of the island.  I hope to make an annual trip here to mark the changes that will occur.

Our rented condo was close to Kepuhi Beach, so we could run down when the sun was setting, or the waves looked high.  This is not by any means a swimming beach, there were waves here in the winter that could kill.  The southern point of the beach is a rock hill which from the top gives a great view of the beach.  The rock point on the southern end of the beach takes the brutal waves in splendor, I've seen the waves crash 20-30’ in the air.  We saw green flashes at two sunsets, heard about but never saw them before.

Finger Mountain was our favorite place along the Haul Road.  The rest stop has a grand view of the countryside, good parking, and bathrooms.  There is a hike to Finger Rock, which is about a half-mile in length.  Also, you can scramble on the rock pile just north of the parking lot for a better view of the road ahead and surrounding country.  The geology is fascinating, and most of the stones here have rock fragments embedded into them.

The guided tour is the way to go, they take groups by bus to the gardens by Lawai Stream a few miles away.  The guide describes all the different garden landscaping areas and went in great detail introducing the kinds of plants here.  I'm typically not the plant kind of guy but this place was fascinating.  The roots of one particular tree were huge.  The Lawai stream to the beach is as lovely as they come.

There is hiking available around the visitor center and the fish pond area.  Our family enjoyed the beach area.  The park service has presented a great visual representation of what the ancient village was like, fascinating.  If you have young children have them go through the junior ranger program and they will discover the place well.

The geology of Kiholo Bay is interesting, fairly new beaches in the making as rock is ground into sand. The turtles seem attracted to the bay as many can be seen feeding along the shoreline.  A newer lava flow butts up along the northern shore covering some if not most at a large ancient fispond.  Some interesting homes along the bay.

Before there was a bridge crossing the Tanana River, there was a vital ferry service and roadhouse to assist people heading or coming from the Fairbanks area.  Paddlewheelers also made this far up the Tanana River as well.  The history of the Big Delta area is preserved mainly in this area; it was in its time, a bustling place.

Slow flowing Pristine spring waters, ideal for a one day (about nine miles) float trip.    The float trip can start here at the campground and end up at the Clearwater  Lake for the takeout.  It you miss the turn to Clearwater Lake the next take out is another 15 miles downstream to the Tanana River bridge in Big Delta.

There is a sweeping view of the mountain (Mauna Kea) as the backdrop for this park.  Our family finished a nice picnic lunch, it doesn't get much better.  There is a great playground near the picnic tables where parents can watch their kids play.  The restroom is not far away, it is a well thought out facility.

It was a great day for a hike, fog drifted in close by, but did not detain the sunshine.  I was pleasantly surprised by how forested the area was with so much lava rock.  The trail is marked with rock piles.  I met up with people birding, they were saying this was an as good place to see indigenous birds.

The lighthouse is a wonderful structure on a magnificent point of land.  The elevation gives you a great perspective along the coast.  The point is also an attraction to marine birds that nest here.  You can spend a lot of time here observing these birds if that is your thing.

In not a distant past people traveling into Interior Alaska (Fairbanks) had to take a ferry barge across the river to continue their journey.  The people here at this station had much to do with shaping the area to what it is today.  The history here is well preserved.

Not only were we treated with the best view of the canyon here but there was a young man dressed in polynesian warrior clothing and armor who gave us a very unique perspective of native history.  The waterfall across from the lookout is something worth seeing.
likes: On-site Activities: Unique perspective, Warrior demonstration

reviews_attraction.text: Our family came fairly early and we seem to be the only people around.  We hiked the loop trail which was a good representation of the higher altitude forest.  Took about 40 minutes, at a casual pace.  There were a few mosquitoes about.

I very much enjoyed the trails here especially the lookout, it is quite an impressive drop in elevation from here.  There is ample room for camping if you are so inclined.  The trees here make a lot of noise in the wind, very pleasant.

Such a beautiful garden valley location.  The wind was driving the waves into the beach today so we made it a walking day.  My wife and I were able to cross the river easily and check out the entire shoreline.

After our tour of the national botanical garden we decided to take in the sunset here at the blowhole.  It was a great time to see the low angle sunlight into the spray.  A great way to end a beautiful day.

A pleasant surprise to visit this zoo, the grounds make for beautiful gardens with flowering trees and plants. As for the animals the tigers are a big thing to see, for the kids the lizards were a hit.
This park is big, many options for outdoor activities, I took a kayak trip with family down a portion of Eagle River.  It was a great 10 mile, 4 hour float through a very scenic area.
The trail to the beach is an adventure, a sign along the way indicates dangerous at times, meaning if it is wet.  Parking is a mystery, one of those places you hope you got it right.
Part of the history and culture of 19th century Hawaii is well preserved in this church.  The surrounding grounds are well kept and signs will help you identify plants.
The ash deposited here is as red as anywhere I've seen.  It is worth hiking along the small stream here to see the color and erosion features caused by water.
This is an annual event for my family.  The grandkids take the slides, glides, and the art work for all it's worth and have the greatest time.
A rich history of the gold rush era.  It was a treat to see the steam locomotive build in 1899 that is still in good running shape.
A quick duck out of traffic and your along the peaceful shore.  Watch the boats, take in the lighthouse, watch the sea birds.

Definitely #1 attraction in Chicago. A huge collection of paintings and sculptures. Must visit if you are in Chicago. The information centre and the staffs are very friendly. Opens around 10 am in morning, and I recommend you to reach early. It’s good to get your ticket online, otherwise you might need to wait in a queue. We got it through the city pass, and through Groupon, which might get you some deal. It’s almost half a day visit, if you are art enthusiast. Be prepared for long walk. I have not tried any restaurant / food inside, so can’t comment on that. Get the map with you from the reception, that would help a lot to spot te restroom and staff. Also, this is a big place if you are from India. If you know about swami vivekananda and his works, then this place has something more to offer. This is the place where he delivered his lecture during the parliament of religion. The Columbus hall is no more, however the new Fullerton hall is there in the exact same place, where they kept the dais and the chair. In front of the hall there is a picture of him and his entire speech written. So indeed it’s a proud moment for every Indian to see these. If you can not locate, simply ask in the lobby, they will direct. #Letsguide

This is a nice and small park to see some Lava piles, formed using trees as mould. There is a small walking trail to follow to see some structures. You need hardly 20-30 minutes to spend, however you can spend some with your family for picnic or outing, as there are benches available. There are enough parking spots and restrooms kept nicely. But I have not given ‘5 stars’ just for this small place. The real attraction is located 2 minutes away, outside of the park. We came to know from people that we can see some ‘Live’ Lava there. After reaching we saw, that is the very recent lava piles formed during the very recent eruption ( May 2018). Though the area is kinda ‘closed’ by the authority for public, people are there to see. We also went there to walk on that Lava for some exotic experience. This is the most fresh Lava, hence quite dangerous. There is no expert available to guide. The lava surface seems brittle, and if you are not careful enough, you might break the surface and hurt your legs. I have seen people called down, cut their legs. So don’t try to walk much of your own. However, that’s the most exotic experience I have ever done with Lava.

Though this is the most popular and very cool attraction in Chicago, I am giving the poor rating because of their poor management. No doubt the view is incredible from here. We visited in the day time, so we could see an absolutely fantastic view of Chicago. However, the wait time was extremely long. We booked through Chicago city pass, and it turned out later that it’s not the ‘fast pass’ ! We had to wait for an about two hours in a queue, before getting into the elevator. That’s still okay. But things became even more worse when we reached at the top. There was no serious queue, but extremely haphazard mess. We had to wait there more than 40 minutes to get a chance to reach to the window!! We were really tired and frustrated ! However, the view was incredible and we really enjoyed our time in the glass window. Without this view, your Chicago trip is incomplete, but my suggestion is to reach early in the morning as soon as they open (9 am) to avoid the crowd. Also check some deals on Groupon. #Letsguide

5 stars are not enough to rate this beautiful scenic drive. It’s a ‘must do’ while in Maui. This is a wonderful, picturesque drive towards a small village named Hana. Try to start early in the morning to make the most out of it. This is very winding and narrow, hilly drive along the ocean shore, through the rain forest. So if you have motion sickness ( Like me, 😰😫), take medicine before, or you would suffer. Else, drive yourself. For me, the driving acts like the medicine. However, because of the narrow, winding roads through the forest, take precaution while driving. There is no light in the night! there are a lot of view points, waterfalls, shacks selling fresh fruits during the drive. Make sure to stop by at least some of them. The fresh fruits are really nice.

This is another hidden gem in Hana, Maui. Must do while in Maui. You have to take a short hike through the tropical forest to reach a point, where you can see the picturesque view of waterfalls falling into the ocean. The ocean is pretty rough, big waves are breaking on the rocks, and the violent waterfalls are adding to it. It’s wonderful. The nature at its best. There is another hike, from this place to see the waterfalls, which is 2 hours! We had no time to take that one. I have seen people coming back with muddy legs. Before taking any hike, it would be good to know your own limits, because the nature could be violent.

One of the famous and popular destination in Smokey mountain national park. It’s in the cades cove region. In the trail head region you can park your car, go to the restroom. There is a small stream. The stream is really nice. Abram trail is written as medium- to difficult hike. It’s a 4-5 miles hike ( round trip). Considering their description and my ability, I decided not to walk. My friends went for the hike and I was waiting in the trailhead area, mostly spending time in the stream. The stream is narrow and shallow. You can walk, however the rocks and bed is slippery. So take precaution.

This is really the ‘must do’ thing, while in Boston. This is a huge historical park inside the ‘downtown’ area, where there is a walking trail called ‘Freedom Trail’. You can walk by yourself with the road sign and self explanatory landmarks. They offer guided tour as well, where the guides ( in an old, colonial costumes) show up and take you through the history. I myself did not take this ‘guided’ tour, however spent my time through the trail in my own pace. It’s a pretty good walking and enjoyable. You would really enjoy if you love history.

The most iconic spot. Must must visit if you are in NYC. There is ferry service from the Battery park to reach here. There is different options of tickets available, some of them include the entree to the crown ( there is no elevator, you have to climb 160 stairs !), some of them even does not allow you to get down in the island. So make sure which one you are buying. The ferry service is there at a frequency of 20 minutes. Most of the time it’s so crowded. I’m sure you don’t wanna miss the view of the NYC skyline from here, that’s amazing.

Definitely a must visit, if you love art and visit NYC. This is not that big one, still you can spend at least 4 hours here. They have the original ‘Starry starry night’ by Van Gogh. They have some collections by Picaso, Frida Kahlo. They have one floor dedicated to photography. We have not seen any long waiting to enter, however it’s always a good idea to reach early. You can get an option to pay less for your entree if you are a student ( make sure to show the id).

Noxubee refuge is an wonderful wetland and an amazing place for a hide out, if you love nature. Very good place for picnic, BBQ or a day out, especially in summer. BBQ grills are provided free. Parking is free. You can go for kayaking/ fishing. But there are alligators in the water, so don’t forget to keep an eye ! There are some bird watching tails, but make sure to wear nice hiking shoes to walk in the trail, as there are some snakes and bugs.

This is scenic lookout point. Absolutely stunning and breathtaking view of ocean shore, black sand, green rain forest, mountain cliff and the waterfalls. You will feel the true essence of a tropical Pacific island. The lookout point has restrooms. None of us had our mobile networks there. You can definitely hike down towards the beach, however, the ascend hike is not very easy one. So if you want to really hike, be prepared.

Aloha! This is a serene beach park, very near to the airport. You can literally walk down here from the airport. We had a long lay over here in this airport, on our way to Honolulu. So we decided to go out and spend the time here. The Blue water, nice waves, natural sand beach and the laid back atmosphere is very refreshing. Enough parking places, bathrooms and shower area are available.

A wonderful piece of greenery, right inside the hustles and bustles of the city. Must visit if you are in Boston. Wonderful fall colour if you are visiting in fall time. The T station is called ‘ Park street’ . There are so many cafe, fast food restaurants, malls nearby. You can see some vendors selling food and little stuffs in front of the Boston common as well.

Absolutely nice, mostly if you have a kid with you. This ducklings making their way state is in Boston public garden. You can simply lie
Down on the green grass, after a tiring day ( in good weather off course) and state at them. Kids definitely love playing around. Nice place to practice your photographic skill as well. Don’t miss it if you are around.

This is a historic urban park. A nice piece of greenery right inside the hustles and bustles of the city. You can simply take a break and go there, lie down on the grass / run or simply do nothing ( for good weather time). The fall colours are awesome. Don’t miss the duckling sculptures, or the real ducks. Must must visit if you are in Boston area.

It was good, but mostly for kids. Honestly, I expected more. The museum is good, but nothing new if you have already visited NASA/smithsonian museum. We attended two shows, 9th planet and the cosmic wonder. ( if I’m not mistaken ). The first one was little unimpressive but the second was was good. However, must visit for kids and young adults.

Another must visit if you are in DC area. This is a nice monument in central DC, in between the Lincoln memorial and the state capital. The spectacular wide greeneries and the iconic buildings make the place very pretty. There are a lot of food trucks seeking good food. Given the weather is nice, you would always find the place very busy.

Nice beach, with picnic benches and restrooms. People go for surfing here. We stopped during our drive towards Hana. We saw a bunch of sea turtles chilling on the beach. So stop by this place if you want to see a turtle. There are fresh fruit shacks around. Keep your cash ready if you want to grab some local juicy tropical fruits.

It's a must go place in DC if you are a history lover, specially if you are interested in WWII. It would take at least half a day, or more  if you decide to give a serious attention. Lot of photographs and rare video and audio clips. The interior is very cold, might need a light jacket.

I am not even a Christian, still feel peace and religious after entering into this historic place. This is a cathedral basilica of saint Louis, the oldest cathedral in US. I love the architecture and design and the ambience. A must visit if you are around.

This is an Oceanside Park, an amazing  place for hanging out, walk or run. There are a lot of places around for food or drinks, but most of the places are expensive. But most of the good things you get here are free, sunshine, ocean and breeze !

Nice point to see sunset in key west.one of the best sunset point. However very crowded, make sure to reach early and grab a good position. Lot of street side food and drink, performance. Truly amazing way to celebrate the setting of sun.

This is fun filled living history museum, good to enjoy with your family. It's living show case of 18th century colonial life. There are plenty of options to buy as souvenir/gifts. Most of them are expensive !

This is an overrated and hyped place in the historic Boston. Anyways, good for an one time
Visit. The ship looks good, and off course the people in costume. Kids will enjoy.The souvenir shop seems good.
This is a nice and picturesque view point in the SFO area. It’s very windy out there. There are hiking trails around, which we could not take though. I am sure the hike and the view would be amazing.

The fee to get in is very reasonable for all of the activities in the beauty of this one marveled natural resource. Once you're in you can see as many mermaid shows as you like and you can take a boat ride and witness a ranger presented educational seminar in the open-air theater. The whole family will love the water slide if it's in operation it closes in the winter time. Bring some peanuts to feed the peacocks that wander around the park. Still eat right out if your hands.

We walked out here from the cruise ship waterfront. Bit of a hike and some up hill but very manageable. In short order you are out of town on a nice trail into real Alaska! I walked about total of 4 miles out and back. I actually took the Perseverance Trail. There were lots of others hiking too. Not a solitary experience but very rewarding. I did a bunch of geocaching. Internet fades fast out here so if you geocache be sure to download before you go.

We saw the Cirque Dreams Holidaze show at Thanksgiving time. We were uncertain about whether we would want to go or not because we were looking for a music venue. But the show was absolutely fantastic and Ia knocked out performance. Even though we bought the cheap tickets we were very happy because we could see everything very well, so it was a very wonderful evening indeed for aThanksgiving treat!

May not be a bad place to go and have your lunch if you work nearby parking area is shaded and parking is free. If you're biking the bike trail is paved but it's dry versus around the sanitation department and the police academy and it is smelly and foul. There are far better places still spiked recreationally this has to be one of the worst.

You don't want to miss this if you're traveling through the area. Free of charge. Doesn't take long to get there and the site is awesome. Can be windy up there sand blowing around from time to time so you might take something to cover your mouth. Hold on to your children and pets It's a Long Way to the bottom of the bottom.

Visitors Center is a must first stop to get oriented there's so much to do here you can't quite get your arms around its in the first day study the maps before you get there have a plan. It's free bus system is fabulous definitely do that right off the bat so you can get a third side view of what's around.

Fantastically remote  quiet and peaceful. We rode bikes. Un monitored pay station for parking but pay $5 per car. We saw deer and armadillos. Roads can be very bumpy, especially the road to the Distillery. Take three bridge road to the path to the deep spring where people scuba in the underwater caves.

OMGosh, yes do visit. Chocked full of info you must have before visiting the park. The rangers are the tops. They have a video/movie room that provides a complete essential rundown of must know stuff before hiking or camping in the park. Denali is so big! It's wild! Majestic and untamed! Enjoy.

Was on a tour bus coming back from Denali, made a potty stop here. Toilets were far better than most of this type. Quite clean and not too smelly. Didn't actually see the Veterans Memorial though. Time constraint due to being part of the tourist herd on the bus.LOL

I wasn't sure that I was going to enjoy this but after we got on board and set sail it was magnificent! You can't believe in the Majestic Beauty of this paddle boat its size its amenities and the show was a stopper! Fantastic would love to do it again someday!

If you're looking to pick up some free shells on the beach this is the place. Check the tide charts and get out there when the tide has gone down and hopefully that will be early in the morning because parking here is very limited and it fills up super fast.

Nice water getaway if you live in Phoenix. The beach is kind of muckey and it's very dry, after all it is a desert but worth the visit. There are barbecue receptacles available the bathrooms have no water. There are picnic tables and shelters available.

Free! Educational! Nice quiet walk in the woods out to the lake and Boardwalk. This is truly a little gem hidden in the woods. Just do it you won't regret it! You can even do a little bit of Geocaching while you're out there.

Nice park. Watch out for the poorly marked speed tables (bumps) the first time you drive in towards the park. The first one is near the Church. If your going any faster than 5 mph you're going to chip a tooth going over them.

Nothing special about the pier we wanted to do some fishing but the guy was very honest and said the fish were not biting and haven't been fighting for a long time so we gave that idea up and found something else to do.

We just drove through checking it out. Looks like a good place to launch either a kayak or a boat to get into the Weeki Wachee River or out onto the Gulf. Like many of the boat launches there is a small fee for parking.

Good trails if you want an a
Activity to do within walking distance from the dock. Fair amount of up hill. Limited network access. Take comfortable shoes, water and some snacks.
I love that especially going Thursday evening when you can get in for $10. Learned a lot about Salvador Dali and his paintings and philosophy is awesome!
Must visit place for the wildlife, manatee in winter wear everywhere. Armadillos abound. Well worth the $5 to get in. Very tourist heavy with visitors.
The beach was great. There's a fire there that you can fish from. And there's a gift shop. And we toured the fort and it was very interesting to see.
Very hot tourist spot. You can catch a free bus ride up to the place from the bus stop right near the visitor info office on the waterfront.
Free public boat access to the Dora Canal. Dock and cement launch area. Good spot to launch kayaks too. About 1.3 miles too Lake Eustis.
Nice little side Trail along the beach in the woods but we enjoyed it and found a geocache out there too!
This McD is close to the bus stop. We sat near the windows and could watch for our busses arrival.
You can sun and swim but it's not the kind of sugar sand beach you will find out on the keys.

If you only have be time for one excursion in Skagway, i recommend the White Pass Train ride. The scenery is amazing... Beautiful forests, multiple water falls, you can't possibly miss the ingenuity and determined Spirit of the creatores of the White Pass Railroad... It is simply remarkable what they accomplished. The staff is wonderful the narration is insightful. The walk to the train from the ship is only a couple hundred yards, so it's quick and easy. When you return after the train ride, they drop you at the train station in the middle of Skagway too, so it's kind of like a two for one deal. I hope you enjoy....

This is a relatively small park, from one end to the other is only eight miles or so but this is really worth the stop. There are several hikes and photo opportunities. The red rock formations and cliffs are spectacular. There is a fun lava tube that you can climb into. There are don sand dunes to play in on the lower end of the canyon. Last time in the park we had a leisurely walk up the dry riverbed where we saw evidence of the desert life with lizard and bug tracks, quail and other bird tracks, we even saw the wing prints on the sand where an owl or hawk had swept in for a meal of lizard. Fun day in the park.

This was the annual arts fair. I love this event, with hundreds of booths with artisans from all over the nation. I usually find some treasure that u think I have to have. We found photographers, jewelry makers, wood Carvers, artists, pottery, ceramics, hat makers metal Crafters and a hundred other things. It also includes much for children of all ages to engaged in with craft and painting booths, events and much more for The kids. There's entertainment going all the time and dozens of fabulous food booths. This is certainly worth the time...... Warm wonderful day.

Lake Powell has so much to offer in terms of recreation, but the scenery steals the show! You'll find wonderful warm, deep blue water, towering red rock cliffs, canyons to explore, streams, waterfalls, beautiful secluded sandy beaches, sunny blue skies in the day and a billion star sky at night, natural arches, and so much more. You can certainly use your own equipment (boat), but rental locations abound and a day or a week rental is so much less than owning your own... Lake Powell needs to be on everyone's bucket list.

There is so much church history that occurred here.... there is so much to experience and to see here.... the old Smith log home, the Smith framed home and the Sacred Grove. The missionaries are fabulous and the information they share is wonderful. The absolute high light is the walk through the Sacred Grove. You'll find several paths to wander. There is so much space, and so many paths,  that finding a private little walk is really easy. What an amazing spirit here.

This is a theater that you simply must experience, this place is wonderful and unique. The theater is nestled into a desert red rock box canyon. The scenery and acoustics are unparalleled. Parking is easy and convenient, the food is fun. Ive used Tuacahn for business entertainment as well as fun family events. Ive recommended Tuacahn many times in the past and will continue to recommend the theater... this is truly a one and only theater experience.

This was an amazing find. We've visited Hawaii many times but we'd never been to this place until now. I would highly recommend this location... well worth the time and expense. It was fun to see so many familiar scenes from movies. What a great time we had. We took the movie set tour. They offer several other outings, including horse back and four wheeler tours too. You can spend an hour or two or spend the whole day.... you'll find many options.

What a beautiful place.....what a beautiful spirit. The drive to the top was quick and easy, but I personally liked the walk to the top... it gave me time to consider the sacred things that have occurred here and all of the Book of Mormon history that occurred on or near here. The Visitors Center is beautiful and beautifully maintained and the missionaries are wonderful and informative. This is well worth the time...

This was a fun find... be prepared for rain as this is one of the wettest locations on the island. You also might be prepared with bug spray. The hike was easy and fun, and we found many great photo opportunities. You'll also find a convenient shop right at the parking lot for those items you may have forgotten. You'll need to pay to park, but the scenery and adventure is well worth the time and minor expense.

Great place to take photos in down town Philadelphia. Stand in front of the Love sculpture or play in the Watter feature, or sit and watch people go by. You have a great view of the Town Hall building from the park, which is a spectacular building. You also have a nice view of the "Rocky" building (art museum). It's also surrounded by lots of restaurants, food trucks, and much more.

Wow! I love this place! I've taken the cruise into the area and Glacier Bay is far and above the Tracy arm. The views are magnificent. We saw bear, sea otter, puffin, eagles, what and sea lion. We saw several glaciers. We actually witnessed a Glacier calving, motion times. We could hear the glaciers popping and grinding. If you come to Alaska, you've got to experience Glacier Bay.

So much to see... so much to do. Sightseeing, photography, mountain biking, hiking, fishing, streams and lakes. I love this Forrest. We see deer nearly every time we visit. We've seen antelope and elk. Beautiful vistas! This is a beautiful drive or a wonderful adventure area depending on your ability, mood and time availability. This is definitely worth the time.

This was a really fun road trip. The park was amazing. We stopped at the the visitors center and we took several hikes. We took way more photos than expected... it was just that beautiful. The park is quite close to Tucson, so we stayed in Tucson and traveled through the park during the days. I would not hesitate to go back for another week.

Nice, open, comfortable location with a fabulous view of down town Philadelphia. Great place for photos. This place is also known as the"Rocky Steps" as this is where the famous Rocky movie scene was filmed. We visited the location in the dark. We walked from down town and back again... safe, clean and well lit the entire way.

This is definitely worth the time. The scenery is stunning. You can enjoy the view from your vehicle or you can explore deeper into nature and enjoy any one of hundreds of hikes, mountain bike trails, four wheeler or jeep rides, and, of course you can enjoy the beauties and recreation of Lake Powell.

The Town Hall building is spectacular! You'll also find a beautiful water feature. There are a group of comfortable tables and chairs set up for relaxing or enjoying you favorite food truck fare. You will also find beautiful gardens, sculptures, information plackards and much much more.

This is a wonderful place, filled with interactive learning, including a kids corner.... movies and informative stories. The home has been carefully and beautifully recreated. The missionaries are welcoming, friendly and informative. This was well worth the time.... don't miss this one.

Beautiful and very nicely maintained. There are lots of interesting videos and nicely designed informational placards and displays. The Christus room is the absolute high light. The missionaries will happily give you the tour or you can be self guided. Great info and great spirit.

The tabernacle recently completed its renovation. The finished product is fabulous. The planers, contractors and workers have all done a beautiful job. It's nice to know that another, historical building has been beautifully preserved. When you get a chance this is worth a look.

What a great view of the city! 360 view around Philadelphia..... from the 57th floor. Tickets are affordable and you can spend all the time you want getting photos and exploring the horizon. At the top you'll also find tables and chairs for relaxing and taking in the view.

This was a fun train ride tour of the plantation. We also tried the restaurant. Loved the pineapple freeze! The plantation store is fabulous too. We bought several types of dried fruits and candies. I'd recommend the stop... well worth the time and money.

Just a few minutes from Colorado city Arizona or from highway 18, Kanab Utah. Beautiful, photo worthy scenery. This is really worth the drive.  You'll find mountains of sand topped with a ponderosa forest.
Beautiful place, beautiful fountain. Fabulous view of down town Philadelphia, and s fabulous view of the Rocky Steps. Great place for photos. Safe and well lit. Easy walk from down town.
Great place to visit near down town Philadelphia. Great place for photos. We'r walked from down town, at night. It's a comfortable walk and it's well lit the whole way. Safe and clean.
Beautiful, sunny, warm and peaceful. Fall colors are getting a pretty good start. Saw deer today and many many wild turkeys. Great place for a hike or family pic nick.

This place is conflicting...personally. I've hiked a lot over the years, and seen some truly amazing sites, and had some emotional experiences greater than this (alone on a mountain peak at sunrise for example), however the views are so spectacular they require some time absorb. Chances are high, you will never experience something more breathtaking. Are you personally prepared for the ramifications of this?  If you knew you would never see anything more amazing in your life, could you deal with that knowledge? This is a tough question to answer, and you'll understand what I'm talking about afterwards.
Now, on to the logistics. Be prepared for crowds. It doesn't mean you can't get a great shot, but you will not be alone. If it's mid morning or later, you will be diverted to park at the ski lodge to take a shuttle. It will take about 25 minutes to get to the top, going by 2 other stops first. Shuttles run about every 15 minutes or so to bring you back down, but only till 5. So if you want a sunset view somewhat more alone, wait till later so you can drive up and not be separated from your car. This would be an easy 5 star experience, but crowds and shuttles are the only detractors.
There is so much to absorb here, a quick 15 minutes may get you the shots, but will not be enough time for you to process the sheer beauty that this vista provides. Allow time for contemplation, or you will be planning you're next trip back! I already am, and was just there yesterday.

I really enjoy this place, and have been there 3 times now. If you want to spend a day getting an authentic feel for the desert, I’d say you can have more fun here then in Death Valley or Joshua Tree NP; also, more Joshua Trees here!  There are some unadvertised hidden gems throughout this park; petroglyphs and underground lava tubes. Do your homework online first so you can fully enjoy everything this park has to offer. There can actually be some serious crowds here doing the weekends, but anytime during the week will provide serious solitude.

DO NOT pull over on the side of the road for a picture opportunity if the signs say “soft shoulder”....they’re serious. It is soft dirt, and you will sink into it when trying to pull out. Keep at least two wheels on the pavement, or you’ll be waiting for a truck to drive by and yank you out....because there is little to no cell service in this park, and you aren’t within walking distance to anything.

What an amazing spot! I’m not sure I’ve ever had so many photos wind up being keepers from a single outing; the whole place is so photogenic. I got there with a little less than 2hrs to closing, and it was enough time to see about 80% of the place if you’re a quick mover, but I’d easily want twice that amount of time. I’d say plan for at least half a day in the park, allowing time to wonder and maybe do some of the guided tours.

FYI the parking lot and gates at the entry pay station are both locked up at night, and they were pretty diligent about kicking everyone out at closing time (so no wondering around afterwards).

Also, it’s about 3 miles on a dirt/gravel road 1-way for the final push to the park, it’s a bit winding and can be narrow at points, and has no guard rails as it curves around steep mountain sides. So the drive to from takes some time in itself, but is very pretty all around.

It’s no Pike’s Peak or anything, but worth a swing by to see it and maybe give it a drive. Mid afternoon on a weekday it only took a few minutes to go up Lombard to the top (much scarier than the drive down the switchbacks), reach the top, and drive down to the bottom. There was even parking off the top left and right at the bottom allowing you to get out and give it a walk up for pictures. Just be sure to lock your car and leave valuables out of sight. Also not terribly crowded with tourist at this time, maybe a hundred or so total spread out.

Very surreal place in the shadow of mt. Williamson. I didn't realize you could do a car tour, and I hiked it out the back door and up to the grave sites. Easy walk, and you get to take in more sites and little things then if you had driven. They're are artifacts laying all of the place. It's a sobering reminder of our past, and fair warning, can taint your vacation to or from the Owens valley...so choose wisely which order you want to tackle this in.

This is another national park that you have to question why it’s a national park...like capital reef. No pay station is the giveaway, that it’s not worth money. Is it a pretty space, sure. But it’s just a wildly remote mountain with pretty scenery at the top, and more or less a bottom of the list park to check a box. You want a park in Nevada that beats this hands down and should be a national park? Go to valley of Fire!

I’d save the large amount of unpaved road required to get here. Seriously. It was only OK for birding (perhaps a bad time of year, but I got lots elsewhere during the same time). It’s pretty and out of the way, but just coots there. May be fine for fishing, but I don’t do that. DO NOT attempt to do this and then drive to Great Basin. It’s about 70 miles of unpaved desert road!!!!!! Stay away!

I thought some of the gifts in the shop on the left (the hole in the rock shop) were very reasonably priced. Overall a really cool stop
Edit- I thought some of the stones I was buying were local to the area...only to peel off the price tag at home to discover a ‘made in Pakistan’ tag. Maybe some are local, but not what I bought.

Wildly out of the way and down a 10ish mile unpaved road. But so remote and pretty. The sun doesn’t always actually line up with the tunnels, but cool nonetheless. Just be aware that this 30 mile as the crow flies from Wendover trip is more like 150 miles round trip as the car drives, and will take you hours to visit!

This is a relatively long unpaved road to see a bunch of rocks...it’s neat, but a tuff call if it’s worth it. When I was there, there was a group of about 30 weirdos chanting and swaying around in the middle; this may make it worth your trip, or make you want to avoid it. Typical spiral jetty nonsense I imagine.

Really cool spot. A couple ways in, all on unpaved roads, but not bad and nothing a 2wd or even rwd car can't handle (my Jaguar XF was fine). Not more than a 30 minute stop while visiting the eastern sierra, so make some time if in the area. And don't be a dummy and try and swim in it!

A little more rock hopping a strenuous than I expected, but quite fun and still by no means extremely difficult. Worth the 2.6ish miles round trip. Should take about 2 hours. Kind of peters out at the end, at the “tanks”, but continue on and up just a bit for a great view.

Favorite place to be. Schulman grove is easy to access and a scenic drive up the mountain. Patriarch grove is about 11 miles further down White mountain road and unpaved. The methuselah grove hike at Schulman is about 4 miles and takes a couple hours.

Cool spot to stop, and only about 7-10 miles one way of unpaved road to do so...but it’s mild and easily accessible in any type of vehicle. It is a state park, and requires a $5 fee for a normal private vehicle to enter, albeit no one mans the area.
What a cool spot! Nice, quiet, and fantastic for astrophotography, especially since town is close enough to still have cell service to waste some time while you’re waiting on the stars to come out.
Very pretty park that just glows at sunset. Not too large, but still plenty of small hikes or items to see. A half day will get you most of it in, a full day leaves room for about everything.
Views may not be quite as perfect as the main park a few blocks down, but they’re still very good, and it’s a little less crowded feeling even though it’s smaller. Great spot for photos.
Be careful not to leave valuables in your car if you park around the park. You may still wind up with broken windows though like I saw happen to two different cars today.
This place is so cool. Absolutely worth the visit. But seriously, drive around the beach and be prepared to get stuck. Stick to the roads/parking areas, and walk ya lazy.
Better tufa views at the other entrance, but during winter that can be difficult to access. Here you can pull over and take a quick hike down even with snow around.
Great town, nice folks, and all around good atmosphere. The river front park is really nothing fantastic, unless of course Denali is out!
The museum was nice, but the best experience was talking with the artists attached to the side of the building. Delbert was so kind!
This place is so great it makes me want to move to the Salt Lake City area. Only downside is the 15 dollar entry and closing times!
Out of the way spot, and facilities not really kept up at all, but you’ll most likely get to enjoy the place by yourself.
Great spot to stop for a quick look. But don’t stop here, keep going into Slab City and explore more!

We had no idea such a nice park was tucked away in the Chihuahuan desert ranchlands south of Marathon!  It has a manmade lake, lots of big shade trees and picnic tables, a huge smoker, bathrooms, a large flat concrete area for dancing and for kids to play, and parking area for I would guess at least a  couple of hundred cars, maybe more.  Birding was really good; we got over a dozen species there in just the hour or so we were there.  Fort PC is well worth the short drive south of Marathon!

Ramsey Canyon was very nice.  Reasonable prices, good trails, lots of benches up the lower part of the trail, each with hummingbird feeders.  Visitor Center was clean, roomy, very clean restrooms, pleasant staff.  Odd paucity of sales merchandise that could otherwise make them extra money.  LIMITED PARKING!  Room for only 23 vehicles.  Gate opens at 0800, get in line by 0730 or you may not have a place to park.  There is no legal parking outside the gate.

Overall bad experience for us.  We arrived after hours, registered with their form, drove in, found an open space and settled in for the night.  We learned: Don't EVER arrive late at this park!  Better yet, don't stay there at all!  The roads are horribly potholed and bumpy, trees aren't trimmed enough for RV's to pass without damage, and the staff is VERY rude and short with you because you arrived late.  We couldn't help it!  DO NOT RECOMMEND!!

This is a superbly conceived and built structure with amazing views of the Hill Country and Lake Travis below.  Good access by car, nice public restrooms a few minutes drive away.  It has several well-placed camera support shelves that help greatly with picture taking, yet do not obscure visual enjoyment.  It could use a couple more seats, but its still a solid 5-star public facility.  HIGHLY RECOMMEND!

What an amazing facility and venue!  Well worth going to.  If you are planning a trip to or through Ruidoso, be sure to check their website beforehand for shows and tickets while you're there.  Spencer only seats about 550 total, and can sell out quickly.  All are good seats and views, and the stage lighting and sound system will take your breath away.  HIGHLY RECOMMEND!

Wonderful little oasis of natural beauty in the middle of a well-heeled neighborhood.  Great trails, some paths are concrete, lots of benches and picnic tables, well groomed and mowed.  Loads of owls, other birds, butterflies and moths to view and photograph.   We're very lucky that ruthless, money-grubbing developers spared this little strip of heaven.

Lake Mineral Wells has always been a clean, well-groomed, eco-friendly, kid-friendly state park.  Bathrooms are clean and well maintained.  Canoe and kayak rentals are great.  If rock climbing is your gig, this place has some great scales.  If hiking is, there are wonderful trails awaiting you.  Wildlife is a little scarce, and I don't know why.

We have mixed feelings about this wildlife "preserve" that hosts hunting events.  It has some good viewing stations, and is an excellent place to see the rare and endangered Golden-Cheeked Warblers and Black-capped Vireos.  But promoting hunting at a wildlife "refuge" is the Webster definition of contradiction and hypocrisy.

It's a well-kept park, with lots of accessible  shoreline around Lake Arrowhead and great fishing piers.  The bathrooms are clean and adequately stocked, and the staff was very friendly.   We imagine it would be unbearably hot in the summer, but it's very comfortable in winter.  RECOMMEND!

Wonderful nature center!  Well kept grounds, good walking trails for the most part, pleasant staff, nice main building, great public outreach programs.  Some of the trails are rough and may just be works in progress, so be careful not to stumble or twist an ankle.  RECOMMEND!

Beautiful park!  We've driven through New Braunfels dozens of times over the years and had no idea such a pretty park was there!  The Comal river might as well been poured from Ozarka bottles, it's so clear.  Treat yourself to one of the nicest parks in all of Texas sometime!

We only had time to walk a short way into it, but our jaws dropped at the mega-surprising beauty and bird variety of this place!  Truly an oasis out in the arid scrub desert for dozens of miles around Marathon.  We WILL be back, for at least an all day visit, and maybe two!

Wonderful views!!  And the road to the top is very well maintained.  It's just a short climb to the summit and tower from the parking lot.  The views are spectacular!  But keep a watch on the weather, you do NOT want to be up there in a thunderstorm.  RECOMMEND!

A little-known but amazing museum with extensive history and displays of the Buffalo Soldiers and life in general in the harsh desolation of southeastern Arizona in the 1800's and early 1900's.  Those people were tougher than beef jerky!  We'll worth visiting.

This is the showpiece of the Fort Worth Nature Center!  I always see at least 10 bird species every time I visit.  My only criticism is that they should have built benches into the covered viewing area so we can rest and enjoy it without standing all the time.

It's ENORMOUS, but largely inaccessible.  Lots of unique bird species but often too far away to ID.  Tour trains available, but the conductors seem a little too concerned with time and often hurry or ignore customer requests to stop and allow photography.

A superbly diverse state park!  You can camp right by the seashore, or way back in the woods, or anywhere in between.  Birding is excellent throughout the park.  Bathrooms are clean, park employees very friendly and helpful.  Highly recommend.

Spectacular place to visit IF the weather's clear and IF the seas are calm.  Otherwise it would be absolutely miserable.  Check your local weather sources, and keep checking them up to just hours before you buy a boating trip and board.

Wonderful park for Lake Bridgepoint beachfront and camping spaces. Birding is superb; we've seen several "lifer" (never before personally seen) species there.  Clean, well maintained and stocked bathroom, well-kept grounds.  RECOMMEND!

We REALLY like Estero, better than any Rio Grande Valley birding center except Sabal Palms.  Great facility, big covered viewing area to keep from getting sunstroke, clean bathrooms, good parking, and marvelous variety of birds.

It's an amazing and very LARGE nature preserve, but it's terribly understaffed and underfunded.  Still, its worth visiting, especially during bird migration.  Prepare well for lots of hiking in ticks and chiggers.
Superb birding!  Saw the Golden Crowned sparrow Feb 2 (rare for Texas).  A beautiful nature preserve in the middle of town.  Well worth the visit.  HIGHLY RECOMMEND!
Spectacular wildlife preserve!  Bring drinking water and food, several cameras, long telephotos, full gas tank, full batteries, and empty memory cards!
Fairly good nature center, not as impressive or updated as it used to be.  Kids will enjoy it for a while.  Great hiking trails, birding.
Fairly good birding place.  WAY off I-35, nearly impossible to find without GPS.  Worth a stop only if it's on your way.

The path to the Matanuska Glacier is through Matanuska Glacier Adventures of Alaska.

Before you can walk on the Matanuska Glacier you need to drive the maintained roads, walk along the orange cones, and step on the metal planks over the puddles and crevasses.  Without all these daily improvements accessing the Matanuska Glacier would be much more difficult.  Paying a fee prior to driving to the Matanuska Glacier parking lot is done inside the Matanuska Glacier Adventures of Alaska house/building.

The employees or family is very kind and helpful.  Opening the gate is done manually, so you'll need to wait at the gate until someone inside looks out to see you.  This process works both ways, entering and exiting the road.  There is a gift shop, so you may find a nice looking picture of the Matanuska Glacier should you have poor weather.

A short drive for a long view of Boise.

Caution: If you're here at sunset then park in front (outside) of the gate.  The gate will close at 9:00 PM.  The security guard will drive up to the top and notify as many people as possible, but if you don't move your vehicle from inside the gate then you'll be locked inside until morning.

If you're looking for a spot to take a picture of Boise then Table Rock Cross is the location.  I visited this location in June; the sunrise was at 6:30 AM and sunset was at 9:00 PM.

If you're here at sunrise the sun will be behind you (over left shoulder) and you'll have a great picture of Boise.  If you're here at sunset then Boise will be covered in shadows, but you'll see beautiful orange and red colors on the clouds.

The cross light was activated about 9:50 PM (June 27, 2017).

If you're looking for a view of the Turnagain Arm and to stretch your legs then Beluga Point is a great stop.

No restrooms or water here.  There are telescopes for viewing Beluga's, however the Beluga's are not here most of the year.  If you see Beluga Whales then you're lucky.  Most of the time I see visitors searching for sheep in the Chugach mountains.

Be careful crossing the railroad tracks.  The Alaska Railroad trains come through here regularly.  Don't forget to wave when the train goes by.

Beluga Point is surrounded by silt, so be careful walking along the rocks.  The silt is like quicksand, so the more you move the more you'll sink.

Parking is Free!
