When you want to see many Alaskan animals in one place.

The Alaska Wildlife Conservation Center (AWCC) is an amazing location with improvements to the area every year.  You can see how the management wants to make this location large enough for the animals, but also enjoyable for the public.

If you want to see the bears then arrive around feeding time.  Bring a camera with a long lens, because not all animals are right next to the fence.

Drive slowly for not only safety reasons, but to minimize the amount of dust you'll lift into the air.  People and cars share much of the same area here.

The gift shop has a huge selection of gifts, so take a look.

If this review was helpful please click the Like button.

If you're downtown then stop by the Elderberry Park for a picnic.

Parking is very limited and can be dangerous.  Reverse slowly and look for traffic multiple times because the vehicles fly down the hill and come around the corner before you know it.

There are portable toilets here and one is wheelchair accessible.  There is also a small amount of playground equipment for the kids.  Not enough benches, so bring a blanket to sit on the grass as a backup.

This park is very popular, so prepare yourself to see just about anything here.  Elderberry Park connects to the Coastal Trail, so you can avoid the roads when traveling to and from here.

If you're looking for easy access to the Cook Inlet for fishing or incredible pictures of bald eagles then you need to visit the Deep Creek State Recreation Area.

The Deep Creek State Recreation Area has a good amount of parking, but not much else.  I spoke with a guy who just finished flaying a halibut.  He said that it took him a little over an hour to catch the halibut and return back to the beach with his Zodiac boat.

Around the corner you'll find numerous bald eagles picking at fish carcasses.  The entertainment is watching the bald eagles defend the fish carcasses from the seagulls.  Bring earplugs because those seagulls are loud.

Finally some toilets!

The Denali Road Lottery drive is stressful on the bladder; especially after a cup of coffee or two.  Finding toilets along the drive is a relief to many who have traveled here.  Thankfully you'll also have a walking path to stretch those legs.  The stairs are steep to access the walking path, so please be careful and step slowly.  The alternative is walking around the vehicles and that could be dangerous too.

The view from here is incredible when the weather is clear.  Not all the time is there snow here, but when there is snow I like to make another cup of coffee.

Rest, read, and thank a veteran at the Alaska Veterans Memorial.

My father and I stopped here on our way back to Anchorage from Denali National Park and Preserve.  My father retired from the Air Force after 20 years of service at Eielson AFB.  My father didn't know this memorial was here, so it was nice surprise for him.

The Alaska Veterans Memorial contains Alaska history that relates to different branches of the military such as the Alaska National Guard, Merchant Marine, Air Force, Coast Guard, Navy, Marine Corps, and Army.

Restrooms are here and plenty of parking for cars and RVs.

If you're looking for an aquarium then the Alaska SeaLife Center is your next stop in Alaska.

You'll find plenty of parking and food in the area including areas to sit in the sun and relax.

If you look at everything here then you'll need an hour, but if you interact with the exhibits then you'll need up to two hours.  The people here are very friendly to not only visitors, but also residents of Alaska.  If you're a teacher then you can get a discount on your ticket.

The birds are may favorite exhibit because you can nearly touch them and they sound interesting too.

Surround yourself with lights, shopping, and food at Union Square.

You'll have a great time here.  So much activity here that you need to stay focused.  Crowds cross the streets and the UBER drivers zip through faster than light.  You will also have some interesting people sharing free information about religion and how you look or smell.

Food is everywhere, but you may go a block or two to get what you want.  When the sky is dark the lights on the buildings are very beautiful, so stay here as long as you can for the night show.

If you're in the woods then you might be in the Chugach State Park.  The Chugach State Park is home to many trails, fishing, camping, and sightseeing; however the Chugach State Park doesn't include free parking.  Make sure you have a parking decal or you'll need to bring cash for the parking fee.  You can buy the Chugach State Park parking decal at REI in Anchorage.

Flying drones is prohibited in the Chugach State Park.  Read "AAC 20.020 Aircraft" for more information.

Since I was a baby I've been visiting the Old Fisherman's Wharf.  My father would buy a small cup of shrimp with the cocktail sauce and lemon wedge every time we visited.  That shrimp cup was the best!  Today I see many families visit the Old Fisherman's Wharf and the shrimp cups/bowls still fly off the tables.  Of course you can't leave the Old Fisherman's Wharf without a box of caramel popcorn.  Enjoy the view and I hope you see some sea lions while you're here.

If this review was helpful please click the Like button.
likes: Facilities & Services: Shrimp with Sauce, Caramel Popcorn

reviews_attraction.text:
If you're looking for hours of fun and learning then you'll find it here at the Museum of Pop Culture.

When I visited I saw the Star Trek exhibit and it was totally worth the ticket price.  I was very impressed with the history collected and effort put into presenting all the wardrobes.  The transporter room was also really cool to do.

Beyond the special exhibits you'll find Rock concerts, music videos, and of course food.  This place is hot, so bring a light jacket and bottle water.

If you have a kayak, canoe, or a good pair of hiking boots you can reach Portage Glacier in an hour or two.  If you want to see Portage Glacier in less than an hour then you should take the Portage Glacier Cruise.  Portage Lake will freeze during the winter, so it's possible to ski to Portage Glacier too.  No matter how to get to Portage Glacier it will be worth the journey.

If this review was helpful please click the Like button.

If you're looking for color in life then you'll find it here.

Take an allergy pill because you'll be surrounded by flowers.  The vibrant colors of the flowers will amaze you.  The walking path is very flat, so no tripping while staring off into the distance.  Bring water because you'll be dehydrated by the end of the walk.

If you're lucky you'll see the wild porcupine eating some flowers.

The Soldotna Creek Park is home to many annual events.

During the summer months Soldotna Creek Park is very active.  Locals will relax and eat lunch here, but visitors most likely will see fairs and live bands play here.  Finding a parking spot is a real pain, so you'll want to find a parking lot nearby.  Look for towing signs before leaving your vehicle in any neighboring parking lot.

Words to live by.  The Idaho Anne Frank Human Rights Memorial is worth visiting for inspiration.  The messages give hope and warning to us, so that we can make the best decisions in the future.  We must learn from the past.

There is much to see and read here.  Spend some time by the waterfalls and relax.  There is a road nearby, so you may not have the peace you're looking for here.

You'll never look at glass the same again after you see what Dale Chihuly has created.

The Chihuly Garden and Class should absolutely be on your list of places to visit in Seattle.  You can spend an hour here easily looking around.  If you watch the glass blowing demonstration and film then count on two hours here.

The location is easy to find, just look for the Space Needle.

Delaney Park or "The Park Strip" as locals call it is a great place to take a walk and more.

Delaney Park is easy to find. Look for the large green grass that separates Downtown businesses from the residential neighborhoods.

During the summer you'll see kites flying high; hundreds of people doing yoga; and events like the mayors picnic.

If you're looking for a different view and quick access to water then you need to stay at Anchor River State Recreation Area.

There are so many camping and RV sites here you should find something quickly.  The access to water is a stones throw away at some sites.  If you're towing a boat you may need to look closer to the ocean end.

If you're looking for a place to have a large group picnic then consider the McHugh Creek Recreation Area.  There are plenty of picnic tables and parking here.  The only caution is the chance of having a large moose visit.

The McHugh Creek is beautiful and worth the trip, so enjoy a BBQ next the creek.

A great day trip with friends a family!

The Point Lobos State Natural Reserve has areas to sit and relax and trails to walk or run.  You'll find plenty to see here and easily use an hour or two to see the ocean from different angles.

Drive slowly because people are walking the roads often.

Beautiful at every elevation.

The Road Lottery was my opportunity to see the beauty and wildness of the Denali National Park and Preserve.  The variety of animals I've seen here and the close proximity to them has amazed me.  If you get a chance you must see this place.
The Julia Davis Park is a huge park with many attractions in the area including the Boise Art Museum, Idaho Black History Museum, Zoo Boise, Gene Harris Bandshell, and Discovery Center of Idaho.
A small quiet park with a view. There is no coastal trail access here. Bring a blanket and have a picnic.

There are 5 museums altogether.  Two contain serious art collections.  One contains interesting science and natural history exhibits.  Another is about the rich history of the Springfield area.  The last is about Dr. Seuss, the author of which comes from Springfield. There is also the Dr. Seusss sculpture garden in the middle.  There is something for everyone here!!

There is a trail along the Schuylkill River for several miles which passes this area, and has a boardwalk built out it the river.  When you walk on the boardwalk you see an angle of history and the city you will not find in the streets.  Park close to the corner of South 25th and Locust Streets and cross the train lines at the official crossing to begin exploring.

A very well presented museum with a wide range of exhibits relevant to the State of NY.  It covers the history of the state, including Native American times, and the natural features of the state, such as the Adirondack State Park.  There are extensive exhibits about the development of New York City, and also a special section covering the events of 9/11.

A gem of a museum whenever in the Dover, Delaware, area.  There is an amazing collection of gramophone record players going back to the beginning of its invention.  There are also numerous items related to Nipper the dog, which was made famous by HMV (His Masters Voice).  A must see for anyone who grew up in the age of record players.

A spectacularly beautiful place.  This is a very special pristine location on the Florida coast showing both the unspoilt nature of the coastal island and the history of the artist Frederick Bartlett and the house he built.  Plan to spend a half day here to see everything, and enjoy it.  There is good parking and it is easy to get to.

There is a lot to see here so allow a few hours.  The main museum takes a couple of hours to see and there are several other very worthwhile houses to see.  Walk along the waterfront, see what he rock, walk up the steps above the rock to see several monuments and memorials, and eat lunch in a local restaurant while you are there.

Just like it's cousin, the Legion of Honor, this is a spectacular museum with many wonderful things to see.  Allow a hall day to see it fully.  Also, it has a restaurant which is outstanding and is perfect for a break during a visit to the museum.  The ticket also allows entrance to the Legion of Honor museum on the same day.

This is a small and very focused museum.  It only contains sculptures by Rodin.  However, the range and diversity of the exhibits is impressive and shows just how varied was the work of Rodin.  Allow an hour to fully explore the museum.  You can get a ticket in combination with the Philadelphia Museum of Art which is nearby.

There is much more here than you would expect given the location of the museum.  The building is impressive and many of the rare exhibits even more impressive.  The mosaic floor from Antioch is very special and rare.  Allow 3 hours to see the whole museum.  Parking is available for free on-site, or in surrounding streets.

This site provides an amazing insight into the history of early European settlement of this continent.  Allow about 4 hours to see everything.  There is a cafeteria on-site which helps and several other worthwhile attractions nearby.  You could spend a whole day in this area or drive the colonial parkway to Yorktown.

A wonderful museum that focuses exclusively on American Art of the 19th and 20th centuries.  There are works by both famous and less well known artists in a spacious and modern building.  It is adjacent to the Walnut Hill Park with views of the park from the museum.  You leave with a great insight into American Art.

A spectacular piece of geography, courtesy of nature.  Be sure to climb the lighthouse to see the full perspective of the ocean and the land.  The ocean is constantly rearranging the land, particularly during the hurricane season.  So if you go back to revisit after a few years, the changes can be very surprising.

On this site can be seen the main John Dickinson house as well as other buildings where slaves lived.  You leave here with a wealth of knowledge about early Delaware history and the wider history during the formative years of the country.  The tour guides are very knowledgeable.  Plan to spend 2 hours here.

This historical park is a collection of 7 sites around the state of Delaware.  Taken collectively, they give a tremendous insight into the history of the founding of the state and its part in the early history of the country.  You need a couple of days to see everything but it is well worth it.

This hall is a very interesting place to visit because so much thought went into the design.  It is contemporary and yet warm and inviting.  You get to go on a very high walkway and see great views of the city also.  The tours are free and so is the audio guide.  Allow an hour to do this tour.

A wonderful museum with a wide collection of artifacts and treasures.  There are an immense number of paintings by famous artists as well as so many other art works of many types from many parts of the world including a significant number of Asian art items.  Parking is convenient.

A gem of a museum.  It sounds like a small local museum but the have the world's biggest collection of beautifully restored nineteenth century carriages.  There are many other things to see also related to local history and art from some local artists.  Well worth a visit.

A real gem of a museum.  It's bigger than you would expect and contains some diverse collections of amazing and treasures.  It is probably less well-known than some of the other big city art museums,  and consequently is less busy which makes it very pleasant to visit.

A spectacular museum with many wonderful things to see.  Allow a hall day to see it fully.  Also, the restaurant was outstanding and is perfect for a break during a visit to the museum.  The ticket also allows entrance to the de Young museum on the same day.

A very unique place on the eastern seaboard of the USA.  Nature,  through ocean currents moving the sand around, has created the barrier islands that comprise this seashore, and nature continues to rearrange this vulnerable landscape from time to time.
A unique museum and must see in NYC.  A variety of very special things to see.  Try to avoid the crowded times as a lot of people want to go here!!
Very interesting history in an unexpected location, but this park needs to be developed to make it more attractive to visitors.
A smaller museum than some of the others in NYC, but well worth visiting.  Also, a nice restaurant on the ground floor.
A great history lesson in early life in the history of Connecticut.  A historic house showing how a family lived.
A huge range of arts on offer from world famous orchestras to opera and drama, all set in spectacular  venues.

This is a hidden gem! It's not one of the parks that everyone talks about that they have to see. We happen to be in the area and we couldn't believe we hadn't heard about this national park. The sites and scenic views are just amazing here and it's stunning that it is here as it doesn't look like it should be when just driving around the area. We are so glad we took a day to dedicate to see this park.

An amazing place to visit. I've now been here three times over the last 10 years and each time is a joy. There is so much to learn and see. I love seeing how the floats are made and seeing the artists working live on the sculptures. These artists are so very talented. After seeing the process in action, you get to walk around so many floats. One day I'll have to see these floats in a parade!

This is quite a stunning statue. We had driven past it quite a number of times when we were in town and don't know why we never noticed it just off the road. I'm very glad we stopped when we found out it was there. I found it very awe inspiring and a joy to walk through the garden/path to the statue.

4 Stars - Really good and wouldn't mind returning

An absolute hidden treasure!!!! We had no idea that this was here when we went through Hatcher Pass and found it at the end of it. It is time well spent going through the visitor center, talking to the ranger and then going through the historic buildings!! This was such a huge learning experience and highly recommend this for anyone!

This park was a lot more interesting than we expected it to be. The landscape was varied and beautiful. There was enough roads to see most of everything by car. There was also back roads to drive by jeep. They had plenty of hikes as well. There was plenty to do and see by almost everyone. It's good for at least 3 to 4 days

What a cool thing to do with a park... putting a monopoly board in it :-) If I lived in the area, I'd be forced to have pieces to play on it. It was quite fun to walk around the board. I also liked the tables which also had checkers/chess on them around the board game. This could be such a fun place to hang out.

Just a fantastic experience! We took the 100 foot mine tour and just loved it! We really enjoyed the talk and learned so much about mining, the history of mining and of Butte. We now have such respect for the men who worked those mines and put their life on the line. Highly recommend this tour

This is a GREAT stop while driving along the highway. They have a wonderful information marker that helped you understand where you were and what was around you. We really enjoyed the view and the information provided. We can't wait for the opportunity to drive and stop on this road again.

Has to be the coolest fort/museum. They have done a fantastic job with showing how the fort was used in each era of history. I grew up in Charleston and I had no idea the impact this Fort had in our history. It's a wonderful stop and there are beautiful views from here. Highly recommend.

Very interesting but was expecting a bit more. I was surprised at the number of folks there which was about thirty. There were also a number of photographers taking pictures of models while we were there. Loved walking among the remaining standing building parts.. Well worth the trip.

We have driven our Jeep on the back roads here quite a number of times now. It's a wonderful place to drive through. We once in a while came across others on the road but the traffic is very light. We really enjoy exploring this area and plan to visit again many more times.

This was a GREAT place to boondock overnight. The parking lot was fine to get around and easy to get in and out of. We went inside for dinner which wasn't the best food, but we were happy to support them for the ability to boondock in their parking lot.

We didn't get a chance to spend any time in the area (we will be back). We did have the opportunity to drive by and through on our way South. Highly recommend at least driving through even if you can't spend time here.
Just stunning! You need to take a side road to see the firehole falls and it's really worth the time to see this! There are some good places to stop along the way to see and take pictures.
Very nice farmer's market. There was a nice variety of fruits and vegetables, stores and artisans. I also loved the background live music as we walked around. Very enjoyable!!!
What an interesting place! Who knew there are HUGE HUGE HUGE sand dunes in Indiana? I was stunned! It's just fascinating to see and be able to walk among them.
The Talkeetna lakes are just beautiful! The hikes are wonderful and one can see wildlife along the trails. It is a great stop and activity when in the area.
Interesting history and geology, this location is not worth making a specific trip to see... But if you are in the area it is absolutely worth the stop
Fantastic place to see wildlife! One has to be very patient to see specific animals like bear and wolf, but there is abundant bison.
Love this area within Yellowstone! So many geothermal features to see and be amazed. It is worth the stop here when in the area.
Fascinating roads to drive and ride on! The sites are fantastic and it's a wonderful drive that you should make if in the area!
This location was on my bucket list and I'm glad I went there. I also enjoyed the shopping environment with the local folks.
Very nice place to have a picnic and you see wildlife. Loved our visit here and spent quite a bit of time here watching elk.
Fascinating to see what happened after the 1964 earthquake. They have a great collection to view and the movie was good
It's a nice place to stop and go on the beach and check out the waterfall. It's not amazing but a good place to stop.

Best whale watching trip I have ever been on and I have been on a lot. I have seen whales in Australia, Alaska, Hawaii, and New Zealand, but CAWW in Massachusetts was the best of them. Here's why:

1. The booking was really easy. I even made a mistake, but I called and they were able to change the day for me. They did it very politely and quickly even though I clearly made a mistake.
2. We started boarding exactly a half hour before departure so we had time to get settled. They were very punctual in the boarding and departure.
3. When I did first get onboard on went to the galley for coffee and Steven walked me through the menu and sold me on the coffee with Baileys. They had a lot of packaged things like donuts, chips, honey buns, and such, but they also had hot dogs and pretzels. They had a full bar on the boat; not a fancy bar or anything, but certainly a bar. The bar was open even on the morning cruise and people were enjoying mimosas and bloody marys, but no one got carried away because I imagine Steven wouldn't stand for that kind of thing in his galley.
4. Captain Johnny got us way out to the plateau (where the whales hang out) in a little over an hour, but the boat is big enough that the boat doesn't rock around that much so no one seemed to be seasick at all.
5. There is a marine biologist onboard who talked to us from there and told us all about whales in general, but also about the specific whales that we saw. CAWW is out there twice a day so they are very familiar with each whale and she knew them by name: Salt, Nile, Echo's 2014 Calf, etc. They can be identified by markings on the underside of their tail and other markings. She told us how whale watching in the area had been going on for about 50 years and some of the most important steps to understanding whales were taken on those very seas. Salt (the whale, not the mineral) was one of the first whales to be tracked and it is because of her that we are starting to understand how old whales can be.
6. In total we saw 6 whales and were able to get close to each of them. Captain Johnny found a good balance between respecting the whales, but getting us close enough for good views and pictures. I know they are wild animals and can be hard to predict, but CAWW made it seem easy to find them. No wonder they guarantee sightings on every trip.
7. The whole time, Matt was going around the ship helping people and wiping down surfaces that were being touched like railings and handles. We could take our masks off at our seats, but when we were by the whales we all had to put our masks on again because people tended to bunch a little when the whales were by the sides of the boat.
8. We got back on time and happy and the gift store actually had really legit merchandise that was actually way more stylish/comfortable than I expected.

All-in-all if you're on the fence, do it! To the CAWW team, thank you for an amazing time. I know you must hear that all the time, but it really was awesome!
likes: Variety of food and drink options

reviews_attraction.text:
A large track with a great balance of facilities for the fancy man and the everyman. The main building is large and has good beer and food options for various budgets. The facilities don't have a particularly classic feel, but almost feel like you are at a ball game. There are some nice restaurants as well and good viewing areas. I was there for an event in the picnic area which was a nice place to be with plenty of tables and each table had an umbrella for shade. The betting was easy enough although the employees all seemed grumpy and quickly gave attitude if someone did not know exactly what they wanted or if they didn't understand the betting fully.

Parking was easy to get in and out of and cost $5.

I had a great time and I would go back again.

There's a lot more to this park than I thought. From the east side of the park there is the visitor center and the lake, But on the west side you can park and hike along the ridge which is also awesome and part of the Highland Trail. There is a nice trail around the lake that is flat and accessible for people of all fitness levels. I don't know if it's that nice all the way around the lake but at least part of it is really nice. The visitor center is not some shack with a porta potty, it's a beautiful building with maps and a porch with Adirondack chairs on it, and real bathrooms that they actually keep clean. They even have a lot of historical information about the mining that happened in the area.

One of the biggest and best places to hike for 100 miles in any direction. There is something here for everyone from swimming and grilling to cliffs and mountains. The parking lots fill up early on nice days, but some people park along the roads. I'd you are trying to escape all the people you will find yourself mostly alone when you get a few miles into most hikes. If you want a hike for strollers or wheelchairs there are limited options, but there are options. Stop at the visitor center and the rangers can point you in the right direction. If you really want to have the whole place to yourself, go on a fall weekday in the afternoon.

It is a really amazing memorial park. The whole park is an island with a beautiful bridge out to the island. There is a large, inspirational American flag in the center of the island, welcoming you from the second you step on that bridge. There are benches facing the water and provide a nice view of the sunset. There are many memorials around the island for various branches of the military and there is an area with benches set up for gatherings and there is also a large open field. The island has paths all around and it is accessible with wheelchairs and strollers.

It’s a great activity for friends. There are many lanes to throw in, but you reserve one for your group. You are supervised the whole time which was disappointing at first. After a bit I realized that the employee actually made it way better because they could offer pointers to make sure we all learned to throw well, they facilitated games and competitions, and they showed us new challenging ways to throw like underhand throws. I never felt restricted by the employee supervising. It’s BYOB and you can bring food so it keeps it relaxed and fun and not too expensive.

I have been hiking here for years. There are easy trails for all ages, but they also have more challenging trails for experienced hikers. You can explore the woods from 202 to Skyline drive, from 287 to 17. It is a very big area to accommodate any day hike, but it is somewhat comforting that even if you got terribly lost you could walk straight in any direction and you would be back in civilization within a few miles.

You can fish as well in the river and lake and there are events for kids sometimes. It is a dog-friendly park.

An easy 5 stars. Close-up views of all the animals we wanted to see. The best bear interactions I have seen. 3 grizzleys that we all playing with each other and so close to the fence that I felt like I was right in the mis with them. The views make it feel like you are still in the wild because the enclosures are so large. The staff is also very knowledgeable and there are animal feedings at scheduled times where you can learn even more about the animals from the experts.

The longest elevated pedestrian bridge in the world. It was beautiful. There are facts about the area and the bridge that you can read as you walk. The parking area on the west side is really easy to get to and the path is wide and flat which makes it great for all ages. They also have great suggestions for routes on the Poughkeepsie side so you can make your walk as long or as short as you would like. There is also a beautiful elevator on the Poughkeepsie side.

A regal display of a classic symbol of independence. The bell itself is impressive for it's size and age, but what it stands for is more powerful. The bell can be seen from outside the building at all times of day, through glass and it sits just a few hundred feet from Independence hall where it was once housed. Nicolas Cage told me that the current bell in Independence hall is the Centennial Bell which can also be seen when looking at the Liberty Bell.

There is a small parking lot by all the historic buildings but the park is really big. The trails wind all back and around that part of the reservoir and there are some historical markers giving explanations for the forge and water wheels and remnants of the old iron processing areas. It is a place with some really cool history and that should not be overlooked but even if you did ignore that part the trails are pretty great on their own.

Great place for lunch. They have Ice Skating and a winter market around Christmas. In the summer they have dancing and movies and there are always great events. Look up some events and go check them out. They have a carrousel and people playing the piano and ping pong tables(sorry I meant "table tennis" cause calling it ping pong trivializes the sport). I love walking down for lunch even if it is really crowded in the good weather.
likes: On-site Activities (Ice Skating, Winter Market, Dancing, Movies, Events, Carousel, Table Tennis)

reviews_attraction.text: This is where you want to hang out in central park. The fountain feels like the center of the park in some ways and this is a great spot right by the fountain. It's cover from rain, snow, or sun and it's beautiful. The acoustics are really cool too so there are often very talented singers and musicians playing there. It is very picture-perfect. Lots of movies have been filmed all around the area as well.

It is bigger than it looks and it's free. During COVID you have to book tickets for certain time slots, but we booked ours on the spot and only had to wait an hour and a half. There murals are incredible. My favorite part was the gallery inside at the one end because they had some Shepard Fairey and Kobra pieces and a giant metal shark. In all, it was very impressive.

A nice monument up on the hill. It is a few dollars per person to get in to the museum and monument, but you also have to pay for parking (at least in some seasons). The town is right down the hill so you can do the monument and town all in the same day easily. The monument is well kept and very regal. There are great views as well.

It is a very nice visitor center. They have a lot of information and plenty of signs and facts about the canyon and the area. There is a cafe and a bus area and there are bathrooms and spots to fill up water bottles. It does get very crowded in the busy season so you may want to stay clear, if busloads of tourists frighten you.

It is great for fishing and there is a boat launch nearby. There are covered areas and grills on the east side of the bridge where people fish and there is parking on the north and south of the road. You can fish off the north or south, but the north side is much more narrow compared to the sidewalk on the south side.

It was beautiful and relaxing to walk around, but the park is not very big. There were only a few different trails. There is a beautiful picnic table on a platform where they have community notebooks to write haikus and draw pictures.

Very nice and the Inn is beautiful, but this place gets crowded. There are nice hikes around and the bear mountain zoo is only $1 per person. A perfect place for a BBQ or picnic with a large group. You can tent paddle boats too.

It was kind of the off season when we were there, but the facilities are really nice. There are great views of the water and maps on the walls and sometimes they keep a fire going in the great fire pit at the center of the room.
Such a unique structure. It makes quite an impression. Can be seen from across the river and it instantly catches the eye. It has so many staircases and every step is picturesque. It's mesmerizing!
A wonderful park full of greenery and fountains, statues and monuments, trees and pathways. It is a good place for an afternoon nap. It’s big enough to handle the crowds even on the busiest days.
This place is a beautiful park down on the water with views of the bridge, a skatepark, and a pier that goes out over the water with some benches.
It is a great park with fountains and benches. It has lights so you can sit at night. The tortoise shell subway stairs are there as well.
It is a great overlook on a great road. The drive is beautiful and this overlook is too. They have bathrooms and plenty of parking spots.

Wow. I was not expecting this place at all. I figured it would be a few trains, old photos, and some dusty exhibits falling apart. First room I walked into was a GLEAMING steam train coming through a rock tunnel. The sheer scale of these things are out of this world, and they look brand new. I could not believe it, the budget they must have had for this had to be a lot. How did they get the steam train up on the second floor?

Highly recommend, even my four year old loved climbing in the few trains they let you get on. The Pullman car even rocks like it's on the tracks which was unsettling at first but you get used to it. Wish they still made trains this nice today.

A fully restored Nike missile site (minus the nukes of course. Or at least I hope!). Crazy to hear the stats on these things. Breaking the sound barrier within seconds of takeoff? Wow. And the guys that volunteer there are former military folk that worked on Nike sites. They are very serious and any sort of joke will be met with an annoyed look by them.

I can't fault them. They spent who knows how many hours working there hiding from the enemy and being a line of defence for a nuclear attack in the US. And now a bunch of civvies show up, snapping pictures, and cracking jokes like it's no big deal. I don't fault them.

Very conflicted about this Zoo. On the one hand, they way the animals are kept rub me the wrong way, on the other hand how else do I expose my kids to animals other than raccoon and deer? While there with my kid the chimps were very agitated and didn't like the huge crowd watching them. The glass we were standing in front of broke when one chimp threw itself against the glass. We made the determination not to spend money here. And yet, I go back with my kid, because I have a kid, and they like zoos. Ignorance is bliss I suppose and you're never too old to be a hypocrite. Sigh.

A fascinating place, but I guess I built it up to be more than it was. For all the money he spent on it, I just kept getting the feeling that it was a guy with more money than he knew what to do with who spent it on tons of different stuff that he shoehorned into a building. Seemed more sad than amazing to me. Glad I went once.

Great spot for hanging with friends and listen to the ocean beat on the beach. When the weather is nice you better get here super early and keep your fire in the pits (and hide your alcohol) because it's pretty heavily patrolled. Don't be surprised when refugees from a busted up bonfire ask to join in your heat either.

Great place to see amazing views, strange art, and encampments. Or at least it used to be. I believe they've since booted all folks living there off the land which is a serious loss for the Bulb. It spooked some people, but I loved it. Great views shouldn't just be for the rich.

Great place for an easy hike. I took some friends here and the views are amazing. We decided to walk along the top and not dive down to the bottom of the hill. Just take Crest Road to the end and there's parking. It can be steep at times, but for the most part it's pretty flat.

I took my three year old here and thought it might be a bit too much over her head, but the place was set up for all ages. They have a great playroom, awesome interactive exhibits, and easy parking. We will be coming here a lot I think, enough to spring for a membership.

Great dog park! And you can get your dog groomed while sipping a latte. Plenty of space for the critters to run around. Watch out for poop from negligent dog owners! Sometimes they just aren't looking at their dog when it happens, and sometimes they are just douches.

Went here as a kid, now here as an adult with my kids. They love it! Of course for me a lot of the exhibits are old, paint is peeling, now seem a little creepy, but my kids love it. Plus they do adult nights where no kids are allowed and they have free drinks. Woot!

Great park! Easy parking, awesome kids area, and lots of trees. Watch out for flying frisbee discs, it has an 18 hole frisbee golf course and there are some real amateurs on it. There's also a rowing club nearby if you want to find a flat place to scull.

Wow! I saw a ton of Elephant seals here. Didn't see any of the ugly male bulls, I think they were off having guys night. So many seals on the beach laying in the Sun, looked like the aftermath of a seal Beach war. What a stink too!

Great place for kids! Holy moly this place was a kids dream. Crazy intricate puppets, awesome interactive displays, and seemed like a show was happening every 15 minutes somewhere on the grounds. Wish I lived closer.

Pretty decent dog park section. Only downside is not a lot of people come here so if you're looking for dog friends to tire out your pup it's not the best. Probably a great place to train your dog though.
I dig this place, but because it's easy to reach it can be a bit crowded. Also if you're female the regulars there are always eager to give you pointers. Guys, sorry, you're on your own!
What a great place to walk around at low tide! The weird cement "house" adds a sort of Middle Earth vibe to it. Lots of seashells, easy parking, and beautiful views. Great for the kids.
A tiny but nice little park. Great for kids. Parking is a nightmare though and the neighbors are militant about the spots, be careful. Best to park a block or two away and walk there.
A beautiful and historic place to visit. Took my kid here and she had a great time running around while we soaked up the history. Great views and Chrissy Field nearby doesn't hurt.
Dollar Sundays! Weiner dog races! So much fun. Lots of easy parking, great location, and as long as you ignore the folks ruining their lives with gambling it can be a lot of fun.
What a great building. Loaded with all worts of maritime history, the building itself is a wonder to see, and the location can't be beat. Great place to take kids.
Parking can be expensive, but it's a nice walk around the reservoir and renting boats is cheap. Great play structures for kids and birds galore.
What a great place to stay! The cabins here are cheap, clean, and comfortable. Bring kerosene to power the stoves! Highly recommend.
This place is amazing! Hiking is great, not too hard, and a free archery range to boot. Easy to feel like you're isolated.
A great place for a walk. Parking can be difficult, but well worth it. Lots of different plant types and free to all.
I love hiking here! Very easy hiking, great for kids, the occasional cow, and good picnic areas. I go here a lot.

Excellent history lesson.

This was our first stop on a day trip to Oahu.  We got there around 9am; found parking in the second lot.  Security did advise that no backpacks/handbags were allowed.  Valuables in hand; we walked into the Center - go to the leftmost booth, that is where you get your free tickets/appointments to the USS Arizona Memorial (the long white structure in the middle of the bay).  It is free, first-come-first-served.  Again, we got there at 9am and got tickets for the 1:30 tour.  Some of the other attractions are cost attractions.

We did not want to wait around so, we toured the North Shore for a while and made it back to Pearl Harbor for our 1:30 tour.  It did start to rain prior to our tour, I thought that they might cancel, but they did not.  It was not that windy.  You will spend about 20 minutes watching a movie on the events leading to the bombing of Pearl Harbor and later board a Navy boat to the Memorial.  At the memorial, you will spend about 15 minutes looking around.  The memorial is not that big and 15 minutes is really all that you will need.

A hands-on museum and learning center for children of all ages.  The museum is divided into different sections highlighting different themes and developmental skills.

I like the room dedicated to children 0-3 years; very appropriate for their development and easily accessible by them.  This room is quiet and features story time.

Great garden and outdoor exploration area for older children.  Best of all is the water feature: a small running creek where children are allowed to splash in.

Cost: $11 per person (for all above 1 year of age).  Quite pricy for a small museum and interestingly, quite busy despite the admission fee.

Suggestion for current and future visitors:  This is a public space, all things in the museum are meant to be shared; keep an eye on your kids, for the safety of them and others.  Bring a change of clothes, if you plan on having your child play with the water features; shoes must be worn at all times.

The Bellagio Conservatory & Gardens is a well-tended area adjacent to the Bellagio lobby displaying seasonal plants and flowers labeled with their botanical names.  The area is free and open to the public 24/7.

On this visit, I experienced a Winter Wonderland in the middle of the desert.  An approximately 50 foot tree (maybe a fir) is adorned with large ornaments and LED lights.  Topiary polar bears made with thousands of carnations flank a gingerbread village.  I believe the roofs were made with frosted wheaties.  Whirling around the gingerbread village are two motorized trains each with a CCTV which you can view.  On the opposite end of the gingerbread village are a family of skating penguins.

This exhibit is not be be missed during this holiday season.  This area is transformed seasonally, so it's a must on your trip to LV.

Great hands on learning for ages 2 - 15.  Exhibits are pretty up to date.  However, the $10 admission is a bit much considering the size of the museum and the fact that it's quite packed when school journeys are present.  Also, there is a lack of supervision especially in the Preschool area that clearly states it is for children under 5.  At the time of my visit the museum did nothing about a whole class of 5th grade students in this area that were making it quite unsafe for the under 5 children that were there.  I was not the only one with this complaint.  Another mom left because it was just to unsafe, she finally was able to tell an employee who she tracked to the parking lot.

While the displayed collection at NSM is small there is a great variety.  On the day of my visit I went right after work, which was great change of environment.  Using my student ID, I was able to get free admission.  But, I had to rush a bit through the galleries and take a quick stroll through the botanical garden as they close at 6pm.  The basement floor has changing exhibit and on this occasion, they had an exhibit on printmaking in America - quite informative.  Their gift shop is small, but they have a good collection of prints.  I got a couple of 8x11 for only $3.50 each, which is not bad because other museums have the same for $6.

Schabarum Regional Park is one of those hidden gems in the larger LA area.  Despite being right next to one of the busiest freeways in the city, this is one of the cleanest and quietest parks I have ever been to.  It has great hiking trails and plenty of picnic areas.

I happen to go on a Sunday for a light picnic.  The weather was great for a picnic as the trees would alleviate from the heat, yet there were no picnic-ers.  Perhaps it had something to do with the $6 parking fee.  I thought this to be a small fee to pay for having a quiet picnic.  Sometimes you do want a large space just to yourself.

Beautiful little retreat only minutes from the city.  Plenty of free parking.  Free admission on Tuesdays.  Discount rates for students.

Whenever, I am in the La Cañada area, I like to make a quick stop at Descanso.  This place offers the most tranquil walk where you can be alone with your thoughts.  I like going just an hour before closing, I find that not many people are around at this time.

A great space, with distinct foliage, oaken archways, and gurgling fountains.

"Look deep into nature, and then you will understand everything better."
-Albert Einstein

I had the pleasure of attending the grand re-opening of LASHP which was a fun-filled day of activities and dignitaries.  Two months later though, the part is still not completed.  You can see where sod is still being placed and already cables on the bridge have been broken.  I just hope the city does not allow it to get run down by over permitting concert-like events.  Additionally, kids should not be riding their bikes on the grass; there are paved and marked paths for this.  Great open space in the middle of the city for kite flying.

A great place to start before heading out on a tour of the National Park.  Because the park is mostly if not only accessible by boat, the National Park Service has partnered with many of the tour companies in order to offer visitors a comprehensive visit of the park.

The ranger at the Visitor Center was really pleasant and answered all of the questions I had.  If there is one good reason to get taxed, it is this - the creation and preservation of our national treasure - Our National Parks.

A must when in Fairbanks.  This museum pays respect to native Alaskans including its wildlife.

Cost: $10/adult

Navigation: Go counter clockwise.  Begin with the art gallery.  Although very small it features a very interesting art collection all about Alaska and by Alaskans.  Then, enter the main gallery where you will be greeted by an awesome grizzly.  Pose for pictures.  Continue through the rest of the displays.  Finish with a visit to the Gift Shop - of course.

Duration: 1.5 hours

Great museum dedicated to the automobile and its history.

The entrance could be a bit tricky.  While the official address is Wilshire, the entrance is to be accessed by either Fairfax or the other little side street that flanks the museum.

The Petersen has a diverse collection of automobiles, but recently the museum has come to be known more as an event location than an automotive museum.

But, I suppose this is how this museum chooses to make revenue and sustain its existence.

USC v. UCLA tailgate organization review.
Expect a wait to get in to park - better off parking off site and taking the shuttle.
Because the football venue is no where near the campus, the feel that you get of going to a college game is simply not there - unlike USC tailgates (no bias in this statement).
Though there is convenience of tailgating where you park (hence tailgating) when it comes to college football, there is just something lacking.

Amazing!  Amazing! Museum.  This positively is the best museum of its kind there is.  A great display of our once formidable form of transportation.  Truly a glimpse into history.  We have Travel Town down in LA and I thought this museum was great; but this one kicks its butt.  I really do wish this museum was in LA because I would go to it every chance I would get.  Great for kids too.

Wow!  Talk about the exploitation and commercialization of a fruit.  Aside from that, the Dole Plantation is fun for all ages and a must while in Oahu.  You'll probably spend about an hour here at most.  I did not enter the maze, because I was on a time crunch and the other attractions did not appeal to me.  Be cautious of making unnecessary purchases.

Beautiful space featuring Latin American Arts.  The occasion of my visit was the 3rd Annual The Taste of Mexico - a showcase of some of LAs best Mexican Restaurants.  The event was well organized, allowing for easy access to all food and drink booths.  Live mariachi music throughout the event made this festival quite festive.
likes: Easy access to food and drink

reviews_attraction.text:
Small greens in the middle of the city that affords some of the most spectacular cityscape views.

This is a great place for an afternoon lunch.  So, grab your favorite take-out from your nearby favorite eatery.

Tip: This park would serve as a great date meeting place.  It's not too public and it's not too private.

Great for strolling alone or with the family.  The array of homes that line the canals are so different, each exhibiting the personality of its owner (if owner lived in).  The only thing I wish, is that the canals were cleaners and had more recreation use.  The canals are also a good place for photo opportunities.

A must visit.  Glimpse into 1840s 1850s living prior to California admission to the Union.  This is a do it yourself museum.  Make sure to pick up a map and scavenger hunt at the entrance.  Great for kids to explore.  Demonstrations are year-round and vary by craft.

A definite stop whilst in Homer.  If you do not have your activities already planned this is a great place to start.  The AI&O Visitors Center boasts knowledgeable rangers and staff.  Make sure to check out the trail that is right behind the center.

Make sure you pop in right before your boat tour.  The ranger will give you a quick description of what to expect in the particular season you are visiting.  Make sure to pick up a quick souvenir and get your National Park's Passport stamped.

Clean.  Plenty of shady areas.  the one draw back is that the concrete "picnic" tables are really bunched up together, so you are really close to other groups.  Good children's playground and open space to set up a volleyball game.

Griffith Observatory Hiking Trail:
Exceptional hiking path.  Busier than most in Griffith Park because of the destination.  However, it offers some of the most spectacular scenery of LA.

The most etherial experience ever!  Scene: You are at 10,000 ft., above the clouds and anxiously waiting the rising of the sun.

Suggestion: Bring warm clothes - it's cold and windy!
Great example of Novelty architecture, which LA was once upon a time known for.  Currently, it is the headquarters of YouTube and Google Venice.  Public art but private building.
A local favorite, Diamond Head Beach is perfect for surfers and water sports enthusiasts.  A good lookout point from the road.

Great addition  to Washington d. C. There's a security  check when you first enter so you might want to only carry your essentials I got to see what actual  dead sea scrolls look like and what the actual writing looks like.  The elevators keep you in the museum atmosphere of the Bible by showing you videos of Israel. The ceiling when you first walk in changes.  Drive thru Bible gives you a 20 info on some of the Bible stories and where the artifacts were found. The theater isn't done yet. I will be back to experience  that.  Manna restaraunt has a scrumptious  pita chicken pizza so so and savory.  The fries were well seasoned. They have different types of cold ice teas. I heard that they are going to change the menu from plastic to scrolls.  The line was long only took about 10 minutes to get through the line.  My food tasted as though it just came out of the oven. The wait for the food only took about 10 minutes I want to know they're secret.  Plenty of docents, police and security walking around. There's a more artistic expression of the Bible when it talks about flies on fruit.  But my aunt especially liked it when they talked about the Jewish culture history  she thinks Jesus was a rockstar
likes: Cultural Value: Dead Sea Scrolls, Jewish culture history
Facilities & Services: Security, Docents, Well-seasoned food, Freshly cooked meals
Activities: Educational videos, Interactive exhibits, Artistic displays
dislikes: Facilities & Services: Long lines, Incomplete theater

Now I definitely  felt like a princess going in. one of the exhibits that really caught my attention was the reflexion water fall very nice place to go to relax. The have an exhibit of a train and you can go inside and it shows the difference between the white section and the black section of the train.The genealogy part of the museum is very nice although when I went there was a public speaker coming so they just gave me a pamphlet on how I can look up my family history on my own. There were high school aged kids when I went and theres a loud speaker that comes on that says no running or jumping on any of the exhibit items or you will be escorted off the premises The food court was nice the creole food looked really  good. its a bit pricey though.

One of the drinking fountains didnt work outside. The ambulance showed up. A lot of k9 units. Looks like the gaurds stare at people all day. Some of the reporters seemed disgruntled.

Great museum. Has a nice classic collection of artifacts. Nice modern paintings. On the outside they actually have a garden of things the Pueblos would use for clothing and they have art on a garden entrance close to the museum. Tje restaurants food smelled delicious

We took a tour of the house it was authentic just learning about how different cultures live in avante garde times. The tour guide said a car rolled up and said are you the real amish. He said no the real amish live 5 miles back or something like that

Amazing experience. Your ticket last for seven days. How cool is that?! The staff are friendly, professional and knowledgeable about the whole park. I met Tina N while hitchhiking who is a geologist for the park. Thanks for your hospitality

nice bridge to walk across probably took me  40 minutes. there's trash cans at the end of the walk wish they could be throughout the walk. there's certain parts where you can catch a cab. the bridge has graffiti on it

nice park to go to have some time by yourself meditate and focus on the warmth of the sun.  the dogs they have this like soldiers march with the front two legs
really nice at night time you see buses going over there cars biles and people going on the big glide reminds me of spider man. takes about 15 minutes to walk

used to go there for the techno but now it cost $15 so does the jazz and  the country festival is free the water is nice to get into on a hot day
one of the best quietest parks to have lunch theres different  tennis balls everywhere. theres a romantic feel to it when you go under the gabezo
Nice garden full of different type of species of horticulture. Theres a water fountain in the ground feels nice. Nice place to have a snack
nice monument. where i can look at the fountain i beleive that the apple store is across the street. saw a rat
Really tall to look at. Remonds me of the xmen movie. they had a lightship the other day and made a triangle
Park is pretty clean. A little debris. When I went there no one else was there and it was a pretty nice day.

OMG!!!
What a fabulous museum. Never has there been so much folk art under one roof. Mr.Girard was a man ahead of his time in collecting all 100,000+ items. The displays are amazing and the variety is not to be believed. Best museum in Santa Fe, by far.
Go today. You will not be disappointed.
If in the area put it number one on your list. Then plan to spend many enjoyable hours.
In fact make it a destination stop right now.

Nice hometown zoo. Perfect for kids and their parents. For adults without kids, not so much. Several animals were unavailable. Several exhibits still in development stage. Several buildings closed.
In other words, don't expect world class.

Truth be told not worth the price of admission, without a membership. I would not make this a top tier stop unless in the area for a week.

Worth more than a three but not a full four.

Very interesting historic site. The visitors center gives you enough ways to look at what happened here to feel a part of it . Well delineated when out on the driving part between British and revolutionary troops.
Only thing to make this a 5-stsr attraction is to run a guided shuttle around the loop and explain in detail what took place.
Worth a visit since they turned the tide of the Revolutionary war.

OMG!! This has to be one of the best city museums in the USA. From special exhibits to the phenomenal new Mexico art, this place has it all. On too of that we had a husband and wife docent team. They were thorough, knowledgeable and fun to boot. The museum is kayed out very well and logically. Plan on spending 2-3 delightful hours absorbing the cultural and artistic history of new Mexico.

Very disappointing. Nothing on website prepared us for the poor amount of items to see. Yes they are rehabbing the facility, but it should be clearly stated on website that it is not extensive. Took 3o minutes with a guide to see everything. Do not waste your time going for at least a year. Even then who knows how limited it will be.
Not very good. Stay away.

If you want to be taken for a ride this is the place to do it. While a bit pricey you will not be disappointed. We saw many varieties of birds as well a turtles and alligators. The tour guides are well verse in the geology, ecology and filmocology the springs and resultant river. Our second ride and it was as good as the first just one year ago.

Fun trip. Just the right length to give a good overview of area. Attendants were helpful and very knowledgeable. The valley is amazing and this is one of the best ways to see it.
A bit more expensive than comfortable for a family, but still should be in the mix as a way to better understand this part of Arizona.

This isone of the nicest parks in punta Gorda. It's about a Mike long and offers nice views of the Peace River. It also is a nice way to safely cross rt 41.
Well maintained and safe. Who could ask for more.
Needs a bit better policing for people not cleaning up after their dogs.

I never knew so many variety of different plants grew in a desert environment.
Well laid out with plenty is signage. Paths were mostly paved and easy for walkers or wheel chairs.
Being from the Northeast this place was a serious eye opener.
Worth many visits.

This a a superb museum highlighting a very important American artist. The works chosen for display are far ranging and beautiful. The movie is a must to get the best flavor of her works.
This is a destination museum and merits returning to many times.

Cute little pocket Bea ch. Facilities are well kept and enough for everyone without crowding. Pay by the hours at a kiosk. Rent kayaks, or swim in heated pool. Great picnic facilities.  But don't tell anyone about it. We don't want it to get crowded.

Great launch site whether ina power boat or...better yet...a kayak. You can paddle up stream or down for about three miles either direction. Lots of animals life as well as beautiful scenery. Paddled there twice in a month. Can't wait to go back.

Nice place. Clean, updated, looks good with lots of great information.
Definitely should be your first stop when heading to South rim. They will get you oriented and help with suggestions if what to see based upon the time you have available.

What a fun and educational place. Something for every one in family. The displays and set up are very well done. Staff is very friendly and helpful.
Worth every penny and by the way, plan on at least 4 hours.

OMG! What an adventure story. From the rise of Capt Bellamy to his demise. Then three hundred years later the discovery and recovery of the pirate ship.
A must visit for anyone heading to cape cod.

Interesting venue and park. Live the dancing fountain and waterfall.
Too bad they are building a 20 story monstrosity across the river. Will surely ruin it. Go soon before it loses it's charm.
I enjoyed this former dwelling area. It was easy to walk, though there were a number of stairs. It's not so big that you are overwhelmed. Nice place for an afternoon outing.
Interesting art within the chapel. The renovation in the mid 1970's restored it back to original.a great improvement. If you like old churches you will enjoy this place.
This tells  the story of the state of Florida. It does the job way better than almost.every other state. Fascinating. Well done. Keep up the good work.

What a fun place. Even moreso if you like moving sculptures and cats. No fee, but donations gladly accepted.
Great way to spend 90 minutes.
Nice exhibits. Found the student picks for their rooms especially interesting. Not a big museum, but always something new to learn and see.
Ok. Not anything I would go out of the way to see. Views are nice. But if you like crowds and steep walks then this us your kind of place.

Cute Little pocket park.
Maintained trail, viewing platform.
Couple of picnic tables.
Nice place to spend a couple of hours.
Interesting and somewhat little know but of history. Worth the visit if in the area. Remarkable views in a nice setting.

Nice Putin spot for paddling. Ok parking.
Bit muddy and steep to get in, but acceptable.
Could use a bit of sprucing up.

My intent was to capture another session of night photos from one of our mid-western lakes, this time that being the Salt Plains National Wildlife Refuge. This review is similar to the one I left of the lake itself.   While I'm not professional by any means I do love to use the clouds, stars and moon to make at least some "interesting" images. I was only able to see a small portion of the refuge due to road and access restrictions but it seems well accessible and protected from careless visitors. (I think that’s why a road was closed that crossed the area to the east.)  I encountered some wind so clouds were moving – something to highlight the night sky. I was able to find enough access via a short hike or drive right up to the edge of the eastern side to get a few pictures. I snapped a few pictures from some nearby roads, although it’s not of the refuge itself it still reminds me of the interesting land around it. I’m looking forward to another visit in the “winter” months although I’m not sure of the weather in that part of the country. Does it snow?  I’ll just have to find out.

This was our last full day in Alaska and the Anchorage area. We decided to take a break from the roads and visit the conservation center, which was also recommended by several local friends. This is hibernation season and we didn't know what to expect but were extremely satisfied with what the enter had to offer. There are unique views this time of year in and around the center. The snow added natural authenticity one would expect from Alaska this time of year.  We were lucky enough to be present for the show at the wolf display. Howling like I've never seen or heard before. It's a must visit any time of year to first time visitors and veterans alike.

I made the trip to Blanchard Sprint Caverns based on previous reviews by other visitors. The drive was enjoyable through the winding roads of Arkansas. Directions to the visitors center were easy to follow. The staff at the front counter were receptive. Only the short tour was available when I went this time so I misunderstood the tour schedule. I'll go later in the season next time. We were able to take photos without being rushed as has been the case in other places I've visited which seems to indicate they have allowed appropriate time per tour. Another note: There are several displays to see while waiting for your tour including a film.

There's a lot of room for improvement and it appears that it's on its way. Some of the road near the park is closed but looks like it may open once more progress is made. Parking is limited for now but is near the park when available. The views are hampered by power lines and poles but that appears to be unavoidable at this stage. For now, I wouldn't suggest bringing young kids there in the evening but I think once construction completes or is nearer completion the visitors will have a better family type environment.

I found quite a few places to park while driving around the park last week. Each is it's open entrance to enjoy the natural features of that area. There were a few nice shelters and one in particular near the overlook appeared very new. It would give whoever is using it a unique view of the Des Moines skyline. I'm from Missouri but grew up in Iowa. This was my first drive through the park since it was recommended for a great photo of a sunrise. There rain took away that chance but I'm glad I found the park.

I believe I was in the upper west side of the park. I traveled around Alaska in February so many of the noticeable spots were snow covered and this day wan't planned so I just got in the vehicle and drove. Google maps tracked me and I'm using that as a photo guide. I'll post some pictures and they should be close according to the time and day. Anyway - the views were amazing as were most of what I saw during this trip. The last two days were dedicated to Anchorage and the surrounding area.

The park returned exactly what I had expected relative to my focus of nature photography in Alaska, in February.  Miles and miles of scenery, endless opportunities to use the sunlight, snow, terrain and general weather to produce every kind of winter photos I could have imagined, and more. I'm posting many photos from the trip and I think that all were from the Denali park area. I have to admit.....it's kinda large :) and I couldn't quite tell where I was all the time.

I was fortunate enough to be selected to participate in laying there wreath at the Tomb Of The Unknown Solider, which is what brought me to the DC area. I took this opportunity to travel in our rental to some places in the limited time I had after the event. Pohick Bay Regional Park caught my eye. I was looking for a quick stop to get some non-tourist scenes before leaving. I'd like to spend some more time there, possibly next time. It's open and has great lake views.

I visited the park and nature area for night photos purposes this time around. It was extremely easy to access and find using Google maps. The trip plan is precise. Roads are well taken care of on the way to the park and, as far as I know, have three options to drive into it. I observed several picnic areas close to the lake and were built into the landscape in most cases. I'm looking forward to going back during daylight hours to enjoy the park.

I have taken a photo trip to the place but it's been a couple of years ago. I've learned much more about the art of the camera that I need to make another drive to Ha Ha Tonka Springs. I remember this image to have plenty of parking during the off season and the roads were well kept. It was an easy walk to the springs from the parking lot. There are places to see along the way that will make a camera happy. 😉

For my purpose, photography, this is an excellent playground. There are county road leading to hills, sharp turns, open sky and trees all over. There are great lake access points, unlike some places where commercialism has every inch of shoreline occupied. There are enough business scattered around to keep the gas tank full and the same with the stomach. Can't wait until the fall colors hit.

My visit was for a passion of photographing night scenes around the Midwest and I had been here before I believe, but during the day. The preserve is easy to find and fully accessable. Some areas tend to close gates and assume nobody has interests after hours but this one seems open. Parking was apparent and I saw other facilities that would make this a great place to bring a family

I drove around the park while sightseeing in the Dallas area. There are few easy places to get great night horizon type photos for visitors not familiar with the area but this park has some potentially great vantage points. Free parking seems to be plentiful around the park. There is a playground area and room to walk/exercise while there.

I visited the lake to explorer, and hopefully take night low light photos. I found it very accessible and easy to navigate around. It's out of the lights far enough to have a great background for star gazing.  The roads allowed me easy access to the shore areas and I was able to walk, with flashlight, to the areas I needed for exclusion.

This is one of my personal favorite places to visit and revisit in Kansas City, even as a long time resident. This is also one of the places I always take first time visitors to our area. There's enough history to keep one busy reading for quite a while. It's a place to learn, visit, take photos from our just sit and watch a sunset.

I thought I'd take a few pictures at night from Peabody conversation area since there sky was fairly clear, and get it before the moon came up. It's a quiet place at night in a Sunday. I'm not sure if it gets regular campers in the weekends or not, Friday and Saturday. It's not far from highway 71 so I like the location.

We traveled through this area on a drive from Anchorage driving south. he February views were breathtaking in spike of the pending snow fall.  But that expected weather change simply added to exactly what we were there to photograph. We observed hikers, children on sleds and snow machines along with us photo enthusiast.

The location was easily accessible and easy to find from the highway. There was plenty of free parking with accommodations for dropping off guests in front of the hotel. There are restaurants with at least one open 24 x 7.  As for the casino - normal accommodations. There's a stage for a live band on the weekends.

This visit was actually to starlight theater for a concert but I was in the parking lot used for zoo visits as well. Parking is convenient anyway even though the zoo was closed during my trip there. I could see the facilities and was reminded of how much fun it is to walk around the zoo, or by train and boat. 😉

I often swing by there for the excellent view of Kansas City, but also for the historic value of the park. There is a little hiking available, fishing ramp, great night views, easy access to the river banks of the Kansas and Missouri Rivers and a great area dedicated to the Lewis and Clark story.

I use this place primarily for night photos of Kansas City but there are walking paths there and space for exercise. There's an ampitheater and some historical information related to Lewis and Clark. There's a boat ramp nearby with Kansas River access and close to the Missouri River.

The park is easily accessible from the main road and well marked around the surrounding area. There are quite a few picnic areas and plenty of parking. There are good places to settle in a take photos from, which was my purpose to visit the area.

Very accessible. The lake, at this point, surrounds the end of TT so you have travel options once here. There are great views to the east, west and north. Google directions are accurate so arriving is easy using maps.

Park access was great and well marked but everything does close early. That may be a state requirement but it would be a great place to take some night photography if it was able to remain open, even partially
A very knowledge staff at the gate. Beautiful scenery on the way up and photo opportunities all along the way.

Wow! Just WOW!
If you’re a history buff, this place is going to get your juices flowing! With over 20,000 historic pieces, your mind is going to be in overdrive. The guides are fantastic and their vivid accounts and descriptions turn the exhibition to life! I stayed for half the day but could have easily spent a solid 3 months observing every intricate details. If you have kids, don’t bring them, they won’t enjoy it as well as annoying everyone else who is trying to absorb the surrounds.

Goodness - $40 for an adult ticket so prepare yourself for the bill shock if you’re paying for more than one person! The museum; however, is beautifully designed giving guests a diverse and rich learning experience. The aquarium sections were absolutely stunning and the location was great - it meant you could visit the modern art gallery across the way as well as exploring golden gate park to see the Bison

I felt a little nostalgic entering the museum knowing that it’s going to be replaced with a brand new building next door in 2019. It’s a compact collection but a nice cross section between evolutionary and geological history as well as exhibitions on humans - who are we?! It’s also a great place to remind you of the intrigue, fascination and excitement of children as they run around with their parents

If you want the best experience of the dunes, make sure you arrive in the morning or towards sunset otherwise you’ll get fried on the sand. We made the mistake of going mid-afternoon and if you want good photos with no other tourists or footsteps in the sand, you have to be prepared to work. Basic bathrooms at the site and make sure you bring sanitiser as they don’t have a place to wash your hands.

This was easily one of my favourite museums in DC as well as destinations in the entire US. You can’t help but feel a sense of magic as you are taken on your tour through the various galleries, halls and rooms and think of the marvellous minds and horrific decisions that have been made. The symbolism is so rich and blatant that it’s hard to deny a link between state and Masonry or NWO

The mysticism, social structure and simple style of the Nordic countries, their people, architecture, history and food is simply endearing - it makes you wonder where the rest of the world went wrong. A great collection of all elements of everything that has contributed to their current state. Highly recommend especially grabbing a plunge coffee at the cafe downstairs

Every time I visit Seattle, I make sure I visit this museum! It’s like travelling to Willy Wonka’s Chocolate Factory with its amazing candy like works of glass; but trust me, they don’t taste sweet 😂 brilliant colours and impossible structures challenge your belief that glass is fragile! The huge structure in the atrium toward the end of the exhibit it’s pure magic!

Why a dynamic group of visitors at this library? Half of the attendees are legitimately here to conduct their study and the other half are the homeless of Seattle, charging their phones and enjoying the free newspapers and magazines. Apart from the amazing architecture, a browse around the floors will give you a very good cross section of Washington State.

A moose! It was right there, below us as we strolled along the boardwalk! An amazing experience to be so close and watch such a majestic animal, go about its daily life below us. It was the perfect place to catch the sunset and a couple of the friendly locals were more than happy to point out birds or landmarks as we enjoyed our walk around the marsh

Rockefeller not only funded the museum but had the foresight to purchase the land across the river which is not to be developed. This means that you get a spectacular museum and pristine views across the way. It’s such a fascinated museum that appears to be constructed of artefacts from all over Christendom. Unique and worth a small trek out of town

In the middle of autumn, the rolling hills are transformed into a plush carpet of soft yellows, browns and orange. It’s an enlightening experience to take a stroll through the park and watch deer and hare scatter in front of you or eagle soar above. Short drive from downtown Denver which made it the easiest to access if you’re limited for time.

Even without having abs, this is still a nice hike through the hills surround LA. If you have my level of fitness, prepare to overtaken by fit locals and tourists but it’s an additional benefit to watch the toned and tanned wildlife pass by. Sweeping views of downtown below with a brown smog cloud which highlights the blue of the water beyond.

An absolutely divine museum that pays a wonderful homage to the history of America as well as the collections of prominent (rich) American people. A modern layout does not detract from the incredible pieces on display. I really loved the staff and volunteers here - super friendly and always asking if there is any other way to help.

If you’re into sci-fi and horror like me; you’ll have a geek-gasm exploring this museum! Original props and costumes beautifully presented with interactive information pads as well as experiential components! 4 years ago, the special exhibit was original Star Wars costumes - today, it was Marvel - wow! I was in absolute heaven!

The Indian exhibition was simply exquisite with jewel encrusted weapons and jewellery! It was the cherry on top of a superb gallery housing a range of masterpieces from all parts of the globe. There is a nice flow to the collection and my personal favourite was the ancient artefacts with some daring to as far back as 2,500 BC

What a perfect contemporary art museum! Start at the top level and work your way through amazing pieces and exhibitions. The flow is lovely and incorporates outdoor sculpture galleries as well as a couple of cafes and restaurants. Lovely store on the ground level so you can take a piece of SF home with you

Whatever time you think you need to spend at this gallery, treble it in your mind! It is huge and phenomenal labyrinth of art, culture and sculpture. The building itself is ludicrously lavish and thank god the Americans had money when Europe was fire selling everything off. It is an amazing collection!

An interactive and free exhibition - what else could you ask for?
