If you want to test out contemporary art, this is the place! The staff were so helpful and if you find as if you’re not into the modern works, there’s a great hall at the back with more typical pieces hung in a spectacular way!

Sunrise, daylight, sunset - there is no doubt that you’ll get the best views of the city from this park at any time during the day! It’s one of those places that you’ll keep returning to in Seattle - if you’re downtown it’s maybe a 35 minute walk or a $9-$11 Uber ride and so worth it!

Just absolutely spectacular to have this beautiful garden in the heart of downtown Seattle! The golds and reds of autumn reflect perfectly off of the mirror lake surface. For a buck extra, purchase the Khoi food and make them go nuts as your feed them off of the wooden wharf

One of the great parks in Seattle to capture amazing photos of downtown! A little too far to be captured with a smart phone camera but definitely worth it if you have a lens with a good zoom. Beautiful green grass and plenty of dogs out for their daily walks - bliss

Kudos to the American people for providing this museum for everyone to enjoy for no charge! It’s absolutely amazing and such a surreal experience to see everything that you’ve learned about at school, in textbooks or seen on television right in front of your eyes!

Autumn (Fall) is just the most perfect time to stroll through Seattle’s beautiful arboretum! You’re spoiled with golden yellow and blood red leaves! The walking paths are easy and there are plenty of nice break off areas to enjoy having a rest in the shade.

An extraordinary piece of sculpture in the middle of Seattle - more poignant now in American history than probably ever before. As Lenin once said ‘fascism is capitalism in decay’ - hopefully either side of this dichotomy doesn’t come into fruition

The best time to catch the Memorial Pool is at sunrise when there are no crowds, only joggers and you’re also rewarded with the most spectacular reflection of cloud and colours of the sunrise on the lake. It’s absolutely phenomenal

June 27, 2018 A must see if you are in the OBX area. We canoed one morning, great guides, wasn't much wildlife. We drove through Sawyer Lake Road and saw 6 Black bears in the mid morning and 9 in the evening right before sunset. Sawyer Rd runs between Buffalo City Rd and Miltail rd. Canon 150-600mm Lens.

June 12, 2016. Hiked and snowshoed to andrews glacier, made it to 2nd level past weather equipment. Weather was perfect but snowfields with water running under wasn't our cup of tea. About 3 hours to get there including pictures along the way. Lot fills early,

July 17 2020, short 15 minute walk to falls. You can go longer and the canyon is very interesting. Lots of people and dogs on the trail since this is a roadside rest area as well. Watch your step on the trail for the tree roots and the trail is mostly flat.

from 2013, A must see if you are in the area. I only gave it a 4-star because I think the Great Sand Dunes in Colorado are cooler! The colors at Pink are unique and I'm sure with the correct lighting would make some awesome views for photos.

July 15, 2020, nice view from the top. Short, even graded pebble path. Almost ADA compliment to the top. Loop trail takes maybe 20 minutes or more of you read all of the "I" information signs along the way.

August 14, 2017, A late post but a great area to visit if you are in the area. Fairly easy walk out to the toadstools. The weather was perfect, we visited here the same day we won the lottery for the Wave.

June of 2018, a very vast memorial honoring the Wright Brothers. Plan to do some walking, paths are paved or clear. The new visitor center will open in 2018. $10 per person entry fee. Worth every penny.
9-2-16, We mostly drove through the park but hiked the Tors and Angel Rock area. Lots of water and alpine zones. The rocks on the Tors are mystical looking and well worth the 15 mile round trip.
9-25-16, drove through the park but didn't hike. spent a few minutes laying in the sand along the shore but the flies came out and we left. Very beautiful area along the shore and lagoon area.
June 26, 2018. Very busy today. Didn't have time to wait in line. Hope to make it back. Bodie Lighthouse is a must see. The grounds are very nice. Plenty of parking nearby.
6-4-15. Awesome cruise, worth every dollar.  Great staff and views. We saw spinner dolphins and a sea turtle. All the drinks you want, appetizers were good. Pork was great.
2-24-2018, a perfect day, perfect weather and road conditions. We checked out the lower falls and upper falls. Over a 30" base of snow on the ground in the Paradise area.
6-1-15, very demanding trail both physically and mentally. Pack lite with plenty of water if you goto Kalalau beach. Check out facebook Kalalau Trail for more info

1_2_18, snowshoed along the river and out to the eagle viewing. Blue skies, packed snow, and 1°.

Eagles next in park, eagle in the tree today.  5-22-16
June 2018, worth the stop as you travel on NC12. Didn't see many birds but im glad we visited. Walk out to the viewing deck takes about 20 minutes.
July 14 2020, a must see if in the area. Road was closed then we came back after 1pm. Check for times of you plan to drive the 1 way route.
May 2015, a must see for aviation buffs. The tomcat was tied down outside the hanger. The  hanger had bullet holes still in it from WWII
5-29-15, it was sunny until we reached here. The clouds changed every 5 minutes so take your time. Awesome views and worth the drive.
12-19-16, cold, 12 degrees, beautiful park and Lighthouse view of Lake Michigan. 12_29_17, very cold, 19° not as much ice as 2016.
8-28-16, must stop if you are driving by.  $12 donation to see wolves, bears, caribou, wood bison, muskoxen, lynx and orhers.
Great state park,  240ft elevation gain over 8 miles on the trails. No bike trails, white River runs through park.
8-29-16, nice falls,  ready hike.  Take a trash bag with you and pick up some trash on the trail on your way out.
May of 2015, awesome seeing this.  Get the guided tour. Amazing that a ship like this was taken out of service.
February of 2014, a must see if you are in the area. The smell isn't too bad. Great views from the peak!
About 10 miles of bike trails and about the same in hiking trails if you do all the loops little hills.

Wonderful, remote park with abundant sea life, glaciers and more. I spent 2 days here, one on a cruise and the other hiking near exit glacier. It was a great mix of activities (one very cold and the other quite warm).

I think I lucked out on the weather as it was clear and calm the day I went out on the boat with Major Native tours. I did the 8.5 hour tour but that was a little long. Maybe the 6 hour cruise with the Park ranger I originally chose would have been better. Saw 5 whales, innumerable seabirds, otters, sea lions and several glaciers.

Hiking was very nice on a bright, sunny day. Still some snow on the mountain that made it tricky so take shoes with some grip (no Converse all Stars). Be sure to take plenty of water if you want to go all the way to the top. I went through at least 2 liters (to be fair I don't rest much and am naturally sweaty). Really good views along much of the trail and especially at the top. It's windy and cold at 3800' so you might want to bring a light jacket (you should have one anyway if you're hiking in the mountains). If you bring something durable and water resistant you can slide down the mountain a bit (I saw evidence of people doing this. I just slid on my shoes)

Park personnel were very friendly as were there people on the trail. It's a positive attitude kind of place.

Note that no fee is required to visit but I suggest you make a donation when you go (I gave $10/day) so that we can continue to have nice places like this to visit.

It's funny, I have been here many times before but for some reason completely forgot how AWESOME it is! Beautiful sunsets, amazing night skies, impressive sunrises and those Hoodoos.

Hikes generally involve some elevation changes but you can get very nice views from the rim as well. In the past I've hiked trails outside of the ampitheater and enjoyed them but this time just did the Queen's garden, peek a boo & Navajo (Wall Street side) loop. Not only are the names fun but the scenery is breathtaking and unique. You can't see this anywhere else.

Park is VERY busy so recommend taking the shuttles, either from town or the visitors center.. Added bonus, no worrying about traffic and plenty of opportunity to gape out the windows. Plus you're helping reduce impact on the environment (you do like the environment don't you?)

Be sure to check out the awesome rotating solar array by the visitors center. Looks like something out of a sci fi movie.

General store has showers for $3(!) Which is great for those of us camping our way through southern Utah.

After 3 visits I still am awed and inspired. First visit was in 2005, then again on 2008 and now 2018. I came into this visit with low expectations figuring I'd already done everything. Boy was I wrong!

So many different scenic drives, hikes and learning opportunities here that I still have much to discover. Just a sampling of the things you can do: walk under groves of enormous trees (you just have to go to understand), pick wild berries, play in the ocean and check tide pools for marine life, walk through golden praries, investigate old structures from a bygone era, look for gold, explore the enchanting fern canyon, see wildlife including eagles, turkeys, bears, elk and deer.  You can even meditate inside the hollowed out hulk of a redwood tree (as I did).

Highly recommend viewing the sunset from Lyons Ranch. It may have been the most beautiful I've ever seen (photo included)

A park that can only be truly appreciated over a multi day experience. I was there almost 5 days, experiencing rain and sunshine. One day of just me hiking and exploring. One day on the bus going the full length of the road. One day on a ranger led discovery hike. Bits of 2 other dates spent hiking and sitting in a cafe just outside of the park working.

I saw all the animals except a wolf or a lynx. That was great and experiencing some of that with other people on the hike and bus was great (people get REALLY excited).

I also beat the odds and saw Denali 3 days in a row. Each time I saw it I was struck by how enormous and majestic it is. Difficult to describe in words so I hope you see it, too!

Be sure to go see the sled dogs and hear the informative ranger talk. The dogs were very friendly (you can pet them) and they seem to love their work.

What fun! Living in South Bend, I had heard of the toboggan run but had never thought to go until I ended up at Pokagon for a work retreat. The weather was perfect for some sledding, sunny but cold and crisp.

It's a little nerve wracking to ride down because it seemed like we might jump the track but I never saw anyone do it and the hint of danger ramped up the fun level.

The ride is short but sweet and you get a great workout/warmup hauling the sled back up to the tower. I think we went down 5 times in the hour we had allotted. For $10 or so dollars that seemed like a great deal for two people to have a lot of fun.

It's a very family friendly activity with lots of kids riding down on the day we were there.

Highly recommended as a day trip or overnight stay at the lodge in the winter

Expansive and excellent national park best visited during a rain storm, preferably in a capable 4 wheel drive vehicle. Much of the park requires a 4wd and a lot of driving to access but the solitude and views would make it worth it. I only visited one district and got to experience this unique setting during rainy/cloudy weather that helped cut the heat and provided some outstanding atmospheric photos.

Really enjoyed the crater area where they are still working out what caused it and the hike to the Indian ruins and nearby plateau which offered great views.

Looks like this would be a really cool place to visit in the winter when it might be covered in snow. Really wish they had solar panels here. Can't figure out why these southern Utah parks aren't all on solar!

Very accessible national park that offers the ability to do a mostly driving tour with quick stops it a lengthy, physical hike into the canyon (which I didn't do but talked to others who did). The South rim is much more "developed" than the North but both sides were nice. Got to see the canyon in various lighting conditions thanks to a summer rain storm. Favorite thing was the hike at the end of the road on the south rim which I trail ran. I was also able to get good cell signal at the trailhead. Ymmv.

Highly recommend visiting the cities of Montrose and Delta which are nearby the park. I really enjoyed them and even saw a movie (by myself as the only person there) at the restored Egyptian theatre in Delta.

Beautiful hike though what looked like Boreal forest with a river crossing in a hand tram and a couple of wood bridges you can cross.

Hike is suitable for almost any age. It's only 1 mile to the hand tram and if you just want to experience that you can do a 2 mile loop and head back. Longer hikes are available to the Aleyska resort and further up canyon.

Mosquitoes were minimal and I didn't see much wildlife. Lots of interesting mushrooms if you keep your eyes peeled. The trail is very popular so if you want to do the hand tram under your own power you'll need to get there really early.

There's a bus that will take you from the nearby town to the trailhead. This is a nice option as the road is unpaved

According to the park literature this is the most photographed arch in the world and it's easy to see why. Very photogenic at almost anytime during the day. Really kind of set apart from anything which allows it to be the focal point. Hike is moderately strenuous with some wayfinding required but the view is so rewarding you won't even notice.

There is a bonus baby Arch on this hike, up and to the right of the trail, just before you get to the delicate Arch. You can get great photos of the arch though this viewport as well as climb through and take a less well traveled path to delicate Arch

Like many other reviewers I stumbled upon this place. I had seen billboards in South Bend for what looked like a checkered can museum and I was looking for a little adventure on a Saturday so I figured why not. 3+ hours after I got there I hadn't seen everything and they were closing. So many really cool cars from a variety of different eras. I think the only thing that was missing were exotic cars like Porsches and Ferraris. Plenty to see, seemed to be family friendly and kind of a cool environment (farm with barns) to wander through

Helpful park rangers, lots of parking, informative displays, comfortable shaded seating, bottle filling station, bathrooms and many trails that lead to glaciers and an icefield. Not too shabby!

There's no entry fee for this park but I made a $10 donation because you can't create great things like this out of thin air and I'm happy to pay the price of 2 beers or coffees to get 6+ hours of amazing natural experiences.

Thank you to the national parks staff and administrators for doing an amazing job despite budget cuts!

Excellent for a winter visit with really interesting ice piles on the shores of the lake and tons of deer. Not recommended for camping but definitely awesome for sightseeing.

When the lake freezes over then starts to thaw out the ice breaks up into thin sheets that look like glass pieces. Wave and wind action then pile these pieces up on the shore line into really interesting piles. Super cool.

Also fun is to throw rocks out on to the ice because it makes this really cool sound and it can end up sliding way far.

Free, easy to get to attraction that you can spend as much time as you want there whether it's 2 minutes to snag the touristy photo or a couple of hours to just sit and enjoy the panoramic views.

These aren't the only houses worth looking at around the park. There is a great set on the opposite side as well that doesn't attract as many tourists.

If you really to get more views the nearby Buena Vista park is a good choice. More natural stair master workout for those glutes, calves and core :)

Great observation point for Denali with several hikes leading from it, helpful rangers, artwork created by the artists in residence program, a bus dispatch office for upgrading tickets and getting a spot on a bus, interesting exhibits and an amazing quilt made by a local woman.

I really appreciated the bottle filling station and the intelligent design that makes the center almost disappear into the hillside, encouraging you to focus on the surrounding natural wonders

Very cool park interspersed among normal life and beautiful scenery in the upper peninsula of Michigan. I really like mining stuff for some reason so getting to walk through and learn the history was a lot of fun (and very scenic). You can dive in as deep (literally by going into mines) as you like to learn about an industry that helped power the electrification of America and the world through the miles and miles of copper wire produced using the copper mined here

Awesomeness! Hard to separate from the park but the forest continues the excellence. Spur trips allow you to view some huge examples of the core tree species in the area (cedar, hemlock, spruce, fir). I only went to the cedar one (ran out of time).

Great place to camp. Like all national forests in the US you can camp for free in unimproved areas.

Bonus: berries! Not sure they are blackberries/raspberries/marionberries but they are free and delicious

I stayed here overnight on my drive East from Moab. There was lots of fire crew activity but I didn't see any. Many thanks and much gratitude to the firefighters for helping to manage all the forest fires!

From what I saw (mostly at night), it was gorgeous and offered a wide variety of recreational activities. The transition from forest to red rock desert was pretty dramatic and kind of cool

Easy hike to a refreshing Little falls. The drive up is beautiful with different styles of cabins to ogle. Hike might be 1/4 mile with lots of roots. Be sure to respect the private property sign.

There was a natural log bridge across the creek that I didn't try to cross. Might lead somewhere interesting and it not at least the crossing is a good (if dangerous) photo op.

Great cruise when the weather is cooperating. I've been on the sunset Cruise before and that is a great way to see the rocks. Be sure to bring warmer clothing than you think you might need as it gets pretty chilly. You're basically on the open seas because the lake is so big!

Also bring a camera or your cell phone to take lots of photos.

Drove through this preserve as part of my Capitol Reef adventure. This area of the country is just beautiful everywhere you go with the rock formations and mountains. Recommend that you have a high clearance vehicle to enjoy all of the different access that is available.

It's a great museum you can visit many times. I can't handle more than a couple of hours because of the hard, concrete floors and dehumidified air but there's plenty of reasons to come back and enough variety to have something for everyone's tastes

Great falls, beautiful riverside trail with smaller falls and swirling currents along the way plus a super cool looking wood stave water pipe that supplies water for a hydro project.

Umpqua hot springs are nearby and worth the drive to check it
Quick, interesting stop with good information about the pipeline, a nice place to look at and touch it if you want and some interesting artifacts. Nice 5 minute pit stop.
Hidden gem in South Bend. Well cared for park with all the amenities plus a giant hill overlooking this small lake. Highly recommended!
Lovely place to go on a snowy winter day. Very quiet and secluded yet only a few minutes from town.

My first review was five stars, but I have to leave 3 stars for my second visit. Why? I showed up with a friend with about 90 minutes left for open hours. But even with the discount for the later attendance, I felt like the ticket price wasn't worth it. 2-3 of the sections of the garden were completely closed. In addition, there is no way to learn about any of the cacti when the signs aren't visible. This is an accessibility issue that the garden could easily fix with some kind of pamphlet, AR app, or even just better evening lighting. I'll probably go back, but not at night again.

Visited during the Rodin Exhibit. The entry staff was incredibly rude/curt with me, which gave me some ominous feelings about the place. I found the standard cost for entry to be incredibly high for the handful of rooms and applied spaces that are available. That said, the art that was there, particularly the computer-based art, was enjoyable to see. I did not find the Rodin Exhibit to be on par with others I've seen around the US.

Oh my god, this place. What a legendary institution. Beware going on weekends, as you won't be able to breathe very well and the live shows will be booked. If you don't mind crowds (or if you happen to go on a night when there aren't any), there is so much amazing information to be learned and I'd recommend at least a couple of hours exploring.

This is probably one of the best touristy things to do in Philly. Be warned: the audio tours alone can take upwards of 3 hours to listen to completely, especially with the art exhibits. There are guided tours as well which can make this an entire day's worth of activities (though you might get bored by that point).

It's kind of hard to visit Savannah and not see the historic district, since the majority of downtown is the historic district. It's a fantastic place that I probably will never forget--the layout and design of the city, its architecture, and the square/parks contained within are truly inspiring.

Really nice tasting room. Interesting approach--you can get a tasting that goes into all the types of beverages they have for one solid price. I enjoyed two ciders, one mead, and one dessert wine. All was fantastic. Would gladly return if I were in the area again.

It's a bit underwhelming, but it's nice that such a controversial company is offering the opportunity to see some of their wealth. It would be great if they added some wayfinding or signage to describe exactly what is so special about the Comcast Center.

This place should be a necessary visit for all those living in/visiting Charleston. It truly is terrifying and cathartic all-the-same. Though the space is small, the information contained within could take several hours to explore word-for-word.

My initial visit had some challenges, but I have had the opportunity to work through my challenges with my first visit to the garden and will look forward to visiting again down the road. I'll update my review then with more information!

Considered by many to be a staple of Savannah, I found the park to be both pleasant and accessible. It's not terribly huge, and there's plenty of space to hang out, people-watch, and relax. I loved the fountain.

A fantastic place to encounter the views of the areas around the park, including the Salton Sea and Palm Springs areas. There can be haze, which is a good opportunity to learn about pollution in California.

Pretty awesome that Sundays get college students in for free. There's quite a bit to see, but I'm surprised it isn't a bit more organized. It feels a bit more spontaneous/organic in terms of exploration.
This might be the most incredible tree a person will ever see in their life. It truly is massive. Even a brief stop is worth it. Even stopping by when there are lots of people is worth it.
Cool little spot--seems like it's mostly used for staging for watercraft. There are a couple picnic tables and a bench though, and an interesting sign about the local heron population.
World class art museum. Highly underrated (Which is kind of a good thing!) so less crowds and more open galleries. I appreciate that the majority of Duchamp's work is contained here!
The best park in Seattle. Even with the summer hubbub, you can't beat a park that is this accessible, sees this many types of people, and offers this many types of activities.
I kind of stumbled upon this (it hadn't come up in my tourist research) and was glad to spend a handful of minutes exploring this section of the historic district.

Really nice park. Much bigger than it looks on the map. Watch out for the steep incline and gravel road--very slippery on the feet!

Very picturesque coastline.
Where's the view? Pretty awful and more like a pillbox turret with a canopy for a cover. Still, nice that there is a park rather than just another house.
Would appreciate more labels, but for its size this cut conservatory packs a lot of punch! Loved the coy fish in the corner. Loved the hanging fern!
A straightforward park, with lots of secrets. Would love to go back and stay for a week, to explore more. I'm glad it is as accessible as it is.
Please do not go here. It is terrible, brutal, and antagonistic to humans. It will eat you alive and swallow you in its darkness. Stay away!
Part of the charm of Boise is in its small, unassuming features like this one. Great access to the city's history. And some delicious food.
Totally beautiful and worth the visit, especially during an event. Stopped by during the Hanukkah celebration and was quite impressed.
Not the best views of the mountains, but a really nice place to chill out, and get away from the nearby society.

My kids love coming here to tube. They talked about how much fun it was, so we all went around Christmas time in 2020 and had a blast. It was easy to buy tickets online and we had a starting and end time. They had a nice outdoor area with a firepit going.

Getting in and out was easy, they had a motorized walkway that led you up to the runs. I think they had four or five tubing runs open that day and there was barely ever a wait. Staff was also courteous and funny at the same time.

Had a great time!

It has been awhile since I was here, but nothing seems to have changed much. Maybe a couple more smaller rides. Had my first experience on Renegade and that's an amazing coaster!

Had a really good bucket of fries at the sports bar too. $25 for a huge bucket that fed my family of five went over really well. The Park itself is pretty clean and well maintained.

Some of the staff seemed lackadaisical but that's what you get when you hire young adults I guess. Also parking costs extra at $17 so beware!

Stopped here with my family over the weekend. As another reviewer stated, it is more expensive for out of state tourists to come see the falls - it was about $11 for us to park.

Plenty of parking and the trails were well maintained. Just as a warning, the steps are very slippery. There is a 1.7 mile trail and parts of it are breath taking. Plenty of falls to see and there is a area where you can splash around in the Bad River if you want to.

Pretty cool place and we would visit again.

Have been coming here since I was a child. The artesian well fills me with nostalgia every time that I see it. I have never camped here personally, but have spent plenty of time at the beach.

Speaking of, this park has seen better days. I saw online that there are plans to revamp it, but that was in 2015 and I didn't see anything being changed. The parking lot flooded last time I was here.

It's still a beautiful area and on the right day its almost magical. It just needs some TLC.

Had an amazing lunch here recently along with a couple flights of wine. Hunter was fantastic about setting us up with wine choices and he was always there if we needed something.

We also ordered split pea soup and a grilled cheese to share and it was delicious. Definitely a recommended spot to stop in.

Beautiful home and grounds. They have an ice skating rink as well, we didnt use it though.

Brought our kids here over the summer time and had a great time exploring the caves and seeing bats.

We spent some time and money in the gift shop as well, they cracked open geodes and we all thought that was pretty cool.

The caves were dimly lit but easy enough to navigate. Saw some bats flying around and some areas of the caves are quite pretty. A pretty quick drive from the Twin Cities.

Words cannot accurately describe this place. Well, that's incorrect, but it would take a large book to do so. Came here last summer without doing any research on what we were getting into and I am glad we didn't.

I don't want to ruin anyone elses fun, but this place is definitely worth a stop. Give the tour a good four hours, I don't think you could see it in less.

Stopped here as part of a tour. Had a great time seeing all of the wildlife. Our tour guide also had stories about some of the individual animals as well which made it a lot more special than going to a zoo.

We got to see some of the bears playing and also got to watch a porcupine get fed (shout out to Snickers and Kit Kat) would definitely recommend stopping here.

Fell in love with this area this summer. Found this on a list of things to do in Vegas and did not regret coming out here to check it out. Where else can you see Turtles and birds and rabbits in Las Vegas? 10 miles off of the strip no less.

I walked here from the New York New York hotel and it wasn't through the best neighborhoods.

I have been coming here as a small child and this place is wonderful. There are extravagant gardens and animals you won't see anywhere else.

They ask for donations to get into certain areas and it is well worth it. Many areas for small children to play at. They also have some tasty food. Well worth a trip!

Had a great time here sampling wines. Was a big fan of the cider and some of the whites. Extremely helpful staff and I bet the place is gorgeous in the summer when it isnt covered in snow.

Cannot wait to check out their outdoor patio sometime in the summer as well.

Have loved coming here since I was a child. Great zoo with plenty to see. The standouts are the tropical area and the aquarium part.

They kind of lack in the large animal department like lions and elephants.

Still very clean and well laid out.

Was here last night on a tour and during a networking event. Wish the event lasted longer because this is a pretty amazing place. They have a hanger and a museum full of cool planes and historical artifacts. Would definitely come again.

Had a really good time playing arcade games here. Pricing seemed decent and there were a lot of options. Will come back with my kids sometime soon. Lots of parking and it wasn't that busy on a Saturday morning during the summer.

We really enjoy this Park and Zoo. There are miles of trails to walk and it is landscaped beautifully. I think the Zoo requires a separate review. There is ample parking but the park is usually very busy on nice days.

What a gorgeous place to spend some time with your family enjoying the scenery and work that it would take to put together a garden such as this.

The grounds are immaculate and breath taking to wander through.

Had a great time walking around the park with my family recently. Didn't pay too much attention to the sculptures but did see two owls which was pretty cool.

Very nice park, easy parking and nice footpaths.
Attended a golf event here over the summer and Theo Wirth treated us so well. The chalet was beautiful even though we spent most of our time outside. Everyone had really good things to say about it.
Gorgeous local park in New Hope. Has some great walking paths that wind through Pond/Streams and Forest areas. Also a nice playground and softball fields. Glad this is in my neighborhood.
Huge tourist trap but kind of cool at the same time. Lots of shopping and restaurants. Be prepared that just like everything Disney - its going to be packed, even on colder nights.
Great place to bring the kids and watch the ponies run. Great selection of food and there are small bars everywhere to grab a drink. Plenty of seating inside and outside.
Came here to go on a hike over the weekend and had an excellent walk. Very nice trails that are well kept and marked. Would definitely come again to explore more trails.
Beautiful zoo! Had a great trip here and had a really good time. Got to feed a giraffe and saw a lot of animals. Very nice place and friendly staff.
Great walking trails and a fantastic beach await you here. They even have a shuttle to bring you to and from the parking lot.
Was here in the morning and it was filled with derelicts. Not much going on. Heard it is a pretty fun place at night.

A must see place in Lansing, a short drive from downtown and you will be blessed with a great view. Upstream you can see the Mississippi as it winds its way along the banks of Wisconsin, also you can see the infamous Blackhawk bridge. The bridge itself is a relic, expansive steel  girders go from column to column. the bridge deck is a steel grid that you can actually see through  when driving over. partake in both if your in the area, the beautiful park overlook or diving over the bridge
likes: On-site Activities (park overlook, driving over bridge)

reviews_attraction.text: It's another great stop on the north shore. We had seen pictures but it's something that I think you need to see in person. The rock itself is enormous and with trees growing in and on it plus a small tunnel that is at and below the waters level. The day we were there the snow and wind was brutal but the waves created a masterpiece with the ice. Some parking for pictures but it is a resort where it is located. Make it a quick  stop but it will be well worth it.

A great little State park on a wonderful piece of land. Know what you are getting into with this park, there is a great elevation change. By climbing the stairs you will rise over five hundred feet up above the Mississippi River. The over look is spectacular and you can see up and down the river for Mile's. In the fall this is great for looking at the fall colors. It's a tricky stop along the highway but you will not be disappointed

A great big city park. You can walk around the ruins and stone Arch bridge. Always something going on around the park, either the farmers market during the summer or it's right next the Guthrie theater. Parking is the only downfall, not much if there is something going on in downtown Minneapolis on the side of the city. A nice starting spot for a walk, run or bike. A must stop in the summer

Was fun but they need to do something about the mice problem in the tropical adventures. We saw at least a dozen mice in and around the whole exhibit, many underneath the bird feeders for the tropical birds. Other parts of the park are great any time of the year. We will be back but if you have one mouse you have bunch. What do you have if you have twelve?

A nice park on the banks of the Missouri River right downtown Kansas City. The only drawback is that and I can understand for safety reasons that you cannot get too close to the water but it's very open Air Park and we will go back. By the looks of the new Condominiums coming around there this should be a fairly busy Park in a couple of years.

It's worth the trip to find this gem. It borders the United States coast guard lighthouse. There is a walk way along the property that leads to the Pier. The pier itself extends out parallel to the shipping canal and has a larger bulk building at the very end. Many fish from the pier or just go out to admire lake Michigan. It's a must see

What a great old park. We came from Wisconsin to do some exploring in the area. With the park situated high above and on the Mississippi River, you overlook a lock and dam plus a veiw up and down the river. The park also has wonderful walking trails and very beautiful buildings. If your in the area it's a must see

It's a destination place to go. The history of the building of the Arch is very interesting. The must-do at the Arch is the pod ride to the top. The veiw is spectacular from all sides. You can see Busch stadium and all of downtown. It's a little tight but we'll worth it. The whole experience will be worth it.

Nice state park if your in the area. Plenty to do and see and the history of the park is neat. When we went it was a rainy day but it did not deter us from some of the overlooks. Not far from Potsis with has a wonderful brewery and restaurant. Again if your in the area it is worth the stop

Nice park, with two waterfalls. It's been years since we last been there but the new lookout on the south side by the picnic area is a great look at the whole waterfall. You can really see how tall the waterfall is.
Nice park in door county. Not to busy compared to peninsula state park. The tower trail was a lot of fun and brought you right along Sturgeon Bay . We will be back
Quite the story about Abbie Gardner, it's worth looking into this episode in our history. Along with the cabin there is a  cemetery and a monument. It's a must see
Kind of tucked away in the other side of a train overpass but an interesting story behind it. Great part of history that used the resources in the area.
A great ride on the train, up the mountain and back. The new turn-around at the top in Canada is nice. Great views and history along the way
A must stop, even a day trip to see these acres of flowers. To describe it, would not do it justice. Just go and you will find out
A must stop if your in the area, it's a good walk up the bluff. Breathtaking veiws over the Wisconsin river valley
It's the best place to get up close to all your racing needs. What a venue. If you have a chance do not miss out.
A highlight of a trip to Juneau, also a must see. Great walking trails and no better place to photograph.
Great place to stop and remember the fallen hero's. If your lucky you may be able to see the mountain
a bit off the beaten path but worth the visit, crystal clear water and large trout make it a must see
Nice area, a cove nested on the shores. The black flys hatched a day earlier so it was pretty buggy
On a very windy day, we had a great time. Would love to be back and walk it again in the summer
An icon that says Duluth when you look at it. It is a very busy bridge, never a dull moment
So big and words can not describe the place. Any time of the year bis a good time to visit

WINTER REVIEW:  I am a National Parks Nerd! I have rated every national park a 5 star, just look. We came down to Denali from Fairbanks to just see what it had to offer in the winter and wow were we disappointed . 3 miles of less interesting views than the drive down. The drive was beautiful and thats were we actually saw Denali the best! The 3 miles of the park were great with small trails to do, but this is a colossal waste of time if you are coming here to experience a park. I have been to many National Parks in the winter, such as Yellowstone and Glacier and I feel that Denali could have offered more than the minuscule 3 mile corridor that you could experience anywhere in Alaska in the winter.  The park rangers were phenomenally awesome as usual though!  We will be back another season.

Way overrated! This might be a fun trail for someone who has never been on a trail. For anyone looking to enjoy nature and not a busy airport terminal then they should avoid this trail. The parking is set up for over 70+ vehicles for a 1.25 mile trail and is usually full (Tuesday at 10am it was 50%).  Half the crowd is obnoxious LA Instagrammers just getting a shot here because of the name. The other half of the crowd is dog owners that take up the trail not allowing up hill walkers the right-away and only half of the dogs are leashed. Graffiti covers any 3' smooth rock surface available.  The water fall itself is also a disappointing pitter-patter. The switchbacks are disregarded and people have clearly slide down between them to cut thru.

Don't go here now in Jan 2020!!! ALL the trails are closed as well as the amazing boardwalk down below, which was not explained well by the extremely rude AZ Parks representative. She took my $7 without making it clear the better 50% of the park was off limits. She also made it clear with her tone and body language that she didnt like me showing up at 3:30, ruining her early exit from work. I spent 15 minutes seeing what was available. It's a shame one person can ruin such a beautiful  place and experience.

I came in here at night time to camp in the winter and the sites were an easy park and set up. I woke up to the perfect sunrise that really brought out so many color in the stones that the ruins were buit with. It was such a great accident of timing, but I suggest the same for anyone else.  This is an easy 1-2 hour exploration if you are on a traveling schedule, but do not pass this one up!

Awesome lava tubes. The climb down the south cave is easy, the north cave was difficult to climb and nothing much different but a fun challenge none the less. There is a 3rd tube that isnt a cave north of those on the white rock trail as well.

This was great! A smaller museum geared towards family but everything was done very well and worth the low cost! The german fighter jet in the parking lot, HAM the chimp memorial, and design of the tour were the highlights.

Great simple little trail to do if passing by to see very unique rock formations. Anywhere from about an hour or 2 of exploring can be done. Who the F$@$ though putting power lines through here was a good idea though!?!?!

Worth the drive to see a unique site. The trail itself would be amazing if it wasn't littered in horse dung from the business nearby that does rides and the often complaining sandal clad blonde stepping on sharp rocks

A hidden gem of a campground. The balancing rocks are stunning and we spotted California Condors in the area. There are good pay showers and laundry at the gas station by Navajo Bridge if you plan to stay long.
More like Pumpkin Spice Sand Dunes. Bring a circular or wooden flat sled for sand sledding.  Worth the side trip for an hour or uniqueness. The rare California Condors  tend to hang out in this area!
So many amazing birds and thanks for all the hard work these people do to help the wildlife. You must take 20 minutes to stop here on a Keys trip and please donate even a few dollars to this cause.
A cool pier that you can drive and park on. There's some lazy seals under the pier hanging out. Some lady washed up dead on the beach in the morning while we were there.
The highest concentration of Joshua trees is on Morning Star Mine Rd.  The Kelso Sand Dunes are an amazing hike to the top. The best is walking thru the Lava Tubes.
A great park with lots of playground space, open area, well lit basketball/volleyball/baseball fields,  covered areas to eat and grills. Safe and free of vagrants.
A very unique alpine lake with brackish green water and a beautiful still water reflection for photos. The boardwalk makes it very easy for anyone to access.
Camping area is good for getting away but it's at the bottom of the canyon so it's out in the open. The park up above is very quaint and well taken care of
If you are moderate to good hiking shape, this is an amazing day-hike goal for packed lunch viewing spot on the Bright Angel Trail.  4.5 miles Each way!
Well laid out camp site. The upper site was great,  but lacked trees for hammock sleepers and there was a school field trip at the group site.
Cool spot if you like nerding out over engineering or just like to see something different.  Easy drive, parking, and a quick visit.
Perfect small yet exciting ruin where you can get close up. The drive was equally as fun. No body needs a Jeep tour to get here.
3 times visiting this year! One of my favorite National Parks/Monuments! Do the 7 mile hike at the top of the mountain.
Worth the hike down the cliff.  Don't be a lame tourist and annoy the true adventurers that actually get in the water.
Pup fish are awesome.  Devils Hole is caged off but you can easily see the fish up close on the other trails.
Bicycling northeast is about the hardest ride I've done in a while with the wind and big trucks passing by!
One of the best sand beaches on the big island. Not a person on a weekday but full on weekends.

The Museum: Museum is 1st & 3rd floor. 2nd floor is restroom, conference room and the administration offices.

From outside the building looks huge but limited artworks compared to other museums in LA. It won't take too long to finish the whole museum. Didn't like the layout of the museum, very confusing, like a maze?

Now they are offering FREE admission tickets. Reserve the tickets on their website.

Once arrive , there are two lines for general admission and also on-site tickets (limited  tickets offered per day and wait line is long). For the online reserved general admission tickets, they are timed entrance, every half an hour. They will start let you wait in line 30 minutes before your appointment time.

The Parking:

1. The Broad parking structure - $12

2. California Plaza parking structure (set GPS to 351 Olive St) $8. The parking entrance is right next to Omni Hotel. Take the elevator to LP level, there will be sign directing to The Broad.

Go to customer service counter on ground floor at The Broad, next to the gift shop in the lobby. They will give you a validation ticket. After validation, $8.

3. Private parking lots on 2nd Street. Might be a little bit cheaper.

Only one word to describe..... "WOW!"

I have never seen anything like this in my life!! There are thousands of glacier in Alaska, only a few that you can see it by car... others you have to take the planes.

Once we got off from our cruise on Juneau cruise port. Tons of local vendors selling excursion. YES, way cheaper than the excursion package on the cruise. We did whale watching and Mendanhall Glacier for $110 compared to the cruise charging $210. That is a big saving!! If you just want to see the Mendanhall Glacier, round trip bus $20.

When we go off the bus, we could see the glacier from far.... THE COLOR IS JUST GORGEOUS!! The sky blue color makes it so dreamy and unreal. The bloating ice look like cotton candy~

There is stairs to go all the way down to the water. YES, you can really touch the icy cold water!!

Then there is a path way to guide you to as close as possible in front of the glacier. OMG!!! Now I truly appreciate what nature have created this amazing view!

There is a waterfall right next to the glacier, about 1 mile walk.

If you are in Juneau, DEFINITELY have to check out Mendenhall Glacier! You won't regret!

Weekdays are way less crowded. It only took about few minutes waiting in line to get on the elevator.

3 floors on this location. Started with 3rd floor then follow the route to first floor... ended with 4D show then exit to the gift shop. Great layout! You won't miss anything.

Only 3rd floor has some seating area. Restroom on 3rd floor as well. On 2nd floor, there is a water fountain. On 1st floor, there is hand wax station for purchase.

There are a few photo spots (e.g. Obama, ET, etc), their staffs will take pictures for you. However, those are for purchase only. Pretty pricey too.

Lots of picture opportunity. Bring your selfie stick with you!!

GM's headquater. Love the skyline buildings. Can't miss it~ The building is right by the water. Gorgeous view!

On the ground floor, there are all kinds of GM models displayed. No admission fee. Open to public. It is like going to car dealership without car salesmen. There are description for each car with the features and price. Unfortunately, no test drive. However, give you an overview of what's their latest models.

Panera Bread is opening soon at the ground floor. There is restaurant on 2nd floor as well.

There is a parking structure next to the building. First 30 minutes $2. First hour $5.

Love to see all these wildlife animals up close!!!

Instead of joining the cruise excursion and HOPING we can spot any wildlife in the jungle, we chose to come to the wildlife conservation center!!

Maybe because they have seen human everyday, they are very friendly and actually like to show off in front of our camera! The brown bear saw more & more people standing near the wired fence, they came even closer to us! So cute~

Not a huge area, a few hours is more than enough to check out the place.

There is a gift shop and snacks bar on the site too.

The city hall is located in the heart of the Center City. If you are on the hop-on hop-off tour bus, you will definitely pass by this historic landmark several times. The architecture is beautiful. The visitor center inside the building is very helpful. I really enjoy the observation deck tour. $8 for 15 minutes. 360 degree view. From here, I can view all the high-rise buildings. And is more than enjoy taking lots of nice photos. They also have interior tour as well.

The Admission: FREE!! Very small museum, displaying the home/furniture in the past.You get to see the life style as well.

The Museum: It is a historic site built in 1818. It is right on Olvera Street. If you are in the neighborhood, check it out. It is free and informative.  Besides the museum, there are small shops and restaurants nearby. You can definitely spend an hour or so on Olvera Street. It is one of LA Landmark.

Admission: FREE

The visitor center is very small, very limited merchandise.

The Roosevelt' s home is under construction. Check their website for new update.

The museum is open to the public. There is very strong odor... either from the old carpet or the furniture?? Very small museum.

They have video showing the history of their home. It is very informative.

Parking: Private lot (Free)

Got off from the cruise ship.... walking distance about 15 minutes to the train station.

Love the cute little train station. The staffs at the ticket office are super friendly. There is a gift shop and snacks shop. You can do some shopping or grab a coffee while you are waiting for the train!

The view is gorgeous and love to witness part of the history.
likes: Facilities & Services: Friendly staff, gift shop, snacks shop, coffee availability

reviews_attraction.text:
The view: Absolutely MILLION DOLLARS views!!! Fantastic place for photos~ Lots of tourists stop by and local people jogging alone the coast.

Sitting on the rocks and appreciate the beauty of the nature. The ocean breeze, the sound of the waves, gorgeous California sunshine..... PRICELESS!!!

The Parking: Few small private lots (FREE)

Beautiful bridge~ if you are up for a nice walk, a mile and half distance (less than an hour walk). This bridge is connecting between Philadelphia & New Jersey.

If you are taking hop-on hop-off bus tour, you definitely will pass by this bridge. If you are on any of the observation deck, definitely look for this bridge.

I have been to many aquariums. This one has something very unique....

The divers feeding the sharks/fish in front of our eyes!!! It is so much fun & exciting to see divers around the sharks and introduce different kind of fish. Very informative as well~

The aquarium is kept very cleaned. The staffs are very helpful.

The Admission: FREE!!!

If you want to see cable cars... come to this block, there will be cable cars pass by every few minutes!

This museum is very informative. Many display, video, photos and historic cable car inside the museum.

The museum is not too big but definitely worth it to check it out.

The exterior of the cathedral is just gorgeous!! I take lots of photos of it. Beautiful architecture.

Everyone entering the cathedral is very respectful and keep the voice down. I really enjoy all the glass works.

It is maintained very well. Very clean. Staffs are very friendly.

Small museum in the Center City in Philadelphia. Informative for sure. I like the Storytime corner outside the museum. Always hear new & interesting fun fact.

There are many other tourist attractions nearby the museum. Definitely can spend all day in that neighborhood.

Very nice theater, have seating area for cup of coffee or snack. People really dress nicely to come here for a show. I like it~

Staffs are very friendly. Not a big theater, every seat is a good seat.

It is great to spend a evening here and watching a great show!!
likes: Facilities & Services: Seating area, Friendly staff

reviews_attraction.text:
What a beautiful holiday decorations!!

Absolutely a place to check it out if you are in Bellagio. Always crowded because definitely a tourist attraction.

It might be hard to get a good picture without the crowded. Either you come really early in the morning.

What an elegant theater!! The moment I walk in.... very impressive!

John Kennedy's status is the main focus in the lobby. Consider big theater, lots of seating. The sound system is great. The theater is clean. The staffs are friendly and helpful.

Definitely one of the landmarks in NY city.

However, nothing much to see inside the building. It is just a office building.

The best way is to go few blocks away and take picture with the full building. The architecture is beautiful~

This city is full of history. So many museums here. You can spend hours and hours visiting different museums. This museum is well maintained and very informative. If you like learning about history, definitely can't miss this museum.

If you are going to the Art Museum, you definitely can't miss the Rocky Statue (next to the stairs) and Rocky food print (on top of the stairs).

Many tourist coming here for a photos because of the famous movie scene.

Lots of parking space, might need to walk for a while to the gate.

Love the energy there!! People are crazy about this sport.. or maybe because there is $$ involved! :)

It is always fun to see any sports LIVE!
This is a former prison in Philadelphia. Awesome place for Halloween event!! They do offer daily tours. If you are on hop-on hop-off tour bus, there is a stop at this location.
Historic site/landmark in Philadelphia. Not a super huge church but definitely full of history. The staffs there are friendly to answer any questions.
Fun sculptures~ it is still fun walk around the park and check out the art sculpture. The eraser is my favorite one!

Amazing national park. No vehicles are allowed beyond a set point, so plan to hike or to take one of the park buses. We took the narrated tour with a naturalist one day--he was very knowledgeable and had a camera that could zoom in on the wildlife and display the pic on tv monitors (like on a plane). That made it possible to see the "little white dots" (Dahl's sheep) and other animals that we might have missed.
The second day we took the shuttle bus and had narration that was about equal with the naturalist, but no telephoto video camera. It was a lot less expensive and almost as good a quality tour.

Amazing, huge redwoods in old growth forest that has been preserved from logging. Lots of turn outs to stop and admire, short hiking trails, pamphlet and signs to explain what you are seeing. 8 main stops, plus a campground, gift shops, etc. At stop 3 you can download an app for your phone to take along and use off line.

Too much fun! Ice sculptures to explore and even touch after a short film that explains the art. Even a toboggan run (indoors!) to go down as many times as you want, all included in the price. The owner/operator will take your photos with your camera/phone while you pose. Well worth the visit.

Incredible private museum featuring taxidermy animals from all continents. Our private guide kept leading us up stairways and into other areas. This museum is very large for a small town. Well worth phoning for an appointment. Free admission! Knowledgeable guide.

Gorgeous views of San Diego and surrounding area clear to Mexico, the Pacific and mountains. Big cross commemorates military personnel who served, low granite walls have names and photos of many. Very moving. Appeals on many levels.

Beautiful views of west end of Grand canyon. Main access road is paved. Park and ride the comfortable shuttle around 3 stops: old west town, visitor center and outdoor restaurant, sky bridge. Generous portions of roast beef.

Interesting national monument which is visible from space. Largest gypsum deposit in the world. Many unique species. Powdery crystalline sand which is shining white-- great for sliding, sand angels, playing.
Beautiful canyon in Balboa Park with entrance  framed by Friendship Gate from Yokohama. Nice landscaping makes a quiet corner in this park which gets crowded on weekends. Relaxing place to stroll.
Naturally split redwood that even SUV will fit through by folding mirrors in. Photo op. Different price for car, motorcycle or walking through. Also a kid's step through stump and a drive on log.
Nicely presented educational site. Clean restrooms. Good displays with photos, videos, audios to explain them. Guided tours available.  Short movie on the half hour. Gift shop. Subway restaurant.
Large outcropping of boulders in the midst of a sandy plain. Very impressive from the vista point at the top of the hill. Picnic tables are scattered among the rocks and there are hiking trails.
Well worth the time to explore this old growth forest. Lots of turn outs, explanatory signs, discover nature app to get closer. Huge trees that, thankfully, have been saved and never logged.
Nice park with playground equipment for kids, tennis courts, restrooms. Drinking fountains didn't work. Picnic shelters with tables and benches, trash cans. Generally well kept park.
Nice, grassy park with large shelters for shady picnics at the tables. Children's play equipment,  trash cans, barbecue grills. Memorial to Vietnam and Korean Vets. Well kept.
Beautiful views of San Diego and the harbor, old light house, historical displays, statue of Juan Rodriguez Cabrillo. Gift shop, snack bar and restrooms. Movie every hour.
Home of the Sequoia redwoods, huge evergreen trees, among the largest in the world. Well marked roads, restrooms, turnouts and parking areas. Not as crowded as Yosemite.
Coolest place in death valley national park. We took our picnic lunch here and ate on the tailgate. It was 20 degrees cooler than the valley floor--only 84 in September.
Smaller ruins of Pueblo people. Nice size for smaller kids who have  shorter attention spans. Good intro to native people's of the area. We like to take visitors here.
Nicely maintained park with playground equipment, tennis courts, public restrooms, picnic tables, shade pavilions, free parking. Regularly patrolled by local police.
Drive for 2+ hour's on graded dirt roads and when you get here, you are still nowhere. But the tribe has developed a nice attraction to reel in some tourist dollars.
Nearly 2 hour's of narrated tour with hop on hop off stops at 10 major tourist areas in San Diego and Coronado. Helpful staff onboard and at most stops.
Beautiful trail and parking area. A bridge was out, so the hike was just 1/2 mile down and 1/2 mile back instead of 1.5 miles. But amazing trees.
Great view of San Diego and the harbor, the Pacific, even Mexico. Interesting exhibits, restored old lighthouse. Good place to visit.
Gorgeous mountain views as you drive through this national forest. Some areas are beginning to recover from fire damage a year ago.
Nice open air park showing natural plants and animals. Beautiful with autumn color just beginning to show among the evergreens.

This was a great river boat trip. It was beautifully arranged. Started with a float plane taking off bc and landing. There was a stop by the husky dog training place. This was interesting and informative. The highlight of the trip was the stopping by the recreated Indian village. There were reindeer.   At various other places they had demonstrations about Indian dress, trappers cabins, and a chance to meet the sled dogs. A great trip.

Just did a primrose hike at Sunnybrook Preserve. The candlelabra primrose where  in full bloom. It was glorious. I would highly recommend this park at this time of year.(last week in May). Park is small, about 3 miles of trails. But is a very nice park. One of Geaugs Park Districts better kept secrets.

Great place to tour a bourbon distillery. The tour was quite interesting. At the end they gave you a credit card so you could sample 3  of their bourbons. You inserted the credit card into one of their dispensing machines and selected which bourbon you would like to try.

Great place to visit. Spent 4 hours wondering around in the hangars. If you read all the placks you could spend 2 days there. Greatest collection of planes I have ever seen. The hole history of aviation is on display. It is worth making the trip to see.

A good place to hike. Saw lots of wild life on the hike, about 15 turkeys, 6 deer and an owl.i like to hike on the valley at the north end of this area. The center section that was the old gravel pit can be very brushy and hard to get thru.

North Chagrin is a nice metro park. It has miles of trails to hike with lots of good hills to climb. Don't forget to visit the nature center and duck ponds. Squire Castle is quite photogenic and lots of wedding pictures are taken there.

This is a great place to see trillium in bloom. Whole areas are covered in white trillium. There are also bluebells and marsh merrigolds in great profession. Some of the trails down by the creek can be muddy. I like this place.

This is the northern most parking lot in South Chagrin Park. From here you can hike the whole park. The horse show is located here staring July 5 this year and going for almost 2 weeks. A good spot for hiking, I recommend it.

This is a good place to hike. The rock formations are   interesting and you can climb over, around, and through them. Rock walls can be up to 45 feet tall in places. This place is good for a couple hours of entertainment.

Edgewood Park is a good place to hike , run the trails or just be outside. Great views of San Francisco bay from the top of the hill. Deer are abundant in the park. And there are lots of good hiking trails.
Salt  Fork Lodge is guite nice. Stayed in the cabins by the lake. The drive back to the lodge is 3.8 miles, seemed very long drive after a long day. I would recommend this place, so check it out.
This is a beautiful city park. Well kept up and clean. Saw 2 groups of deer one had 7 deer in it the other had 8. Besure to hike down and see  the falls. Good rock formations along the way.
Good place to go for cross country skiing. They have an outdoor gas fire ring to warm up by. And 5 or 6 miles of groomed skiing and snow shoe trails. Gear rental is available.
A very nice little park. One can do a 5 mile hike here along Euclid Creek. The South end ends near the old Blue Stone Quarry. The North  ends near Highlands parking lot.
Good place to park for hiking the Buckeye trail and the Valley trail. Five or ten mile hikes can be done easily out of here. This is a nice place to hike.
This is a stop along the bridal trail.  Restroom facilities are available. There is a shelterhouse here. Access to the trails along the river from here.
Wounderful place to hike. The waterfalls are amazing, the rock formations and caves are grate. You just have to explore this place too appreciate it.
This is a good place to hike. The trails are gravel and no mud. Saw a bald eagle and crane on today's hike. Had the park all to our selves today.
Good place to take a hike. Good variety of spring wildflowers in bloom. Interesting rock formations. Very senic down along the creek.
Castle was built around 1864. Lot of interesting history here. Castle is in need of repair. A good place to spend a couple of hours.
Good place for hiking. You can hike the Buckeye Trail from here. Good place for taking longer hikes, I often do 10 hikes from here.
Good place to visit. Many old Packard's and Corvettes. This is good for about a 2 hour visit. Lots of Packard history here.
Good place to visit. This is where Lincoln was born and the memorial is here. Lincoln only lived here until he was three.
Very nice park to hike in. Saw 10 deer on my hike. Lost of trails to hike and lots of giant trees.
A place to watch the six bison in the field. At feed time the all go into the feeding pen.

Located on the Camden water front is this massive 888 foot battleship that was launched on 12/7/1942.  During WWII, the New Jersey began its career as the flagship for the Fifth Fleet, seeing action at Truk in the Carolines and was involved in many major & minor campaigns during the WWII.  "Big J or Black Dragon" (nicknames used for the New Jersey) again seen major action during the Korean conflict, using its incredibly accurate 16" Guns to support ground forces up and down the Korean peninsula.  Also seeing service in Vietnam, Beirut and the Persian Gulf (prior to Desert Storm) before being finally decommissioned 2/8/1991.   During its active duty the ship earned a total of Nineteen Battle and Campaign Stars, the Big J is America’s most decorated surviving battleship.  It is a super cool to walk the decks, check out many of the room, climb into the gun turrets its a trip you'll remember for a long time.  Enjoy.

We've enjoyed our trips to Penn's Landing every time.  There are so many activities different activities during the summer there is something for everyone.  You can do many, many things from carnival-style games, a beer garden, restaurants and food stands and hammock lounge, rent swan boats, kayaks for a light paddle around the marina. You can enjoy firework displays, full length movies, concerts of all sorts.  At the RiverRink you can roller skate in the summer and ice skate in the winter, there is a ferris wheel as well as amusement rides, mini golf.  Located near Penn's Landing Marina on south end is the Cruiser Olympia and submarine Becuna are anchored to be visited. This whole area makes a fascinating picture backdrop from the water at sunset.  Enjoy we have many times.
likes: Recreational facilities (roller/ice skating, ferris wheel, mini golf)

reviews_attraction.text: On the road to Seward you'll be enjoying the scenery and then after 60-70 miles the Center will be on the right.  Basically, they take in injured, sick and orphaned wildlife and nurse them back to health.  If they have been orphaned then they will continue to live at the center since they would not have the necessary skills to survive in the wild.  There are a fair number of animals at the center, this allows visitors to see these animals up close. This is something that the visitors would probably never get the chance to do or see.  To list a few there were: Black Bear (& orphaned Cub in tree), Grizzly (Mom & Cub) Bears, Bison, Elk, Reindeer, Deer, Moose, Eagle, Wolves and porcupine.  The scenery at the center is pretty awesome as well.  So take a few hours and enjoy.

There are many views in daylight, twilight, night, light-show, above and below, that make this beautiful suspension bridge magical in its own right.  As major span over the Delaware River connecting Philadelphia PA and Camden NJ, carrying traffic for US Routes 676 & 30 and it was opened in July 1926.  A bit of trivia, also in 1926 US Route 30 became the east–west main route of the system of United States Numbered Highways.  Today US 30 is still the 3rd longest numbered US highway at 3,070 miles, anchored in the East by Atlantic City NJ and in the West by Astoria OR.  The Ben Franklin Bridge and the Golden Gate Bridge other than both being suspension bridges also, both were originally painted by the same Philadelphia painting contractor.  Enjoy

This a great park for lots of fun, hiking, camping (you'll have to reserve in advance), swimming, just enjoying life or communing with nature.  It's the Falls Trails (7+ and 3+ miles) that journey through 21 different and magnificent waterfalls that is certainly one of the major highlights.  The trail can be difficult at times and slippery when wet but boy you'll be treated to some great sights.  Be sure to bring your camera and extra batteries, because you will certainly use it a lot.  The Park staff is excellent, helpful and fun to talk with and knowledgeable  of their charge.  It is best to go when there has been a lot of rain as the flow of Kitchen Creek varies a lot.  We have visited multiple times and have never been disappointed.

The trip from Marble Canyon on RT 89A & 89 to Glen Canyon Dam was beautiful and a delightful drive.  The Visitor Center was interesting and provides a great starting point for the tour.  The Dam itself is incredible in its size and the massive amount of water it controls, which is the start of Lake Powell and it is picturesque.  We took the tour down into the dam, eventually we went through the visitor chamber for the electrical power generator room, which was really huge, clean, well maintained.  A fun fact is they have to regularly mow the grass that covers the roof of the electrical power generation room :) .  This is really a neat place which we will have very good memories of our visit here and you will too.  Enjoy.

Visiting old Forts and discovering the history of them has been a fun thing to do for us.  Fort Zachary Taylor Fortress is another interesting find, parts of it date back to 1845 when construction was started as a southern fortification because of the War of 1812.  In addition it was used during the US Civil War, 1898 Spanish–American War, World Wars I and II, and the Cuban Missile Crisis.  It was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1971 and designated to a National Historic Landmark status in 1973.  Originally it was to be the anchor fort, to a string of forts to act as a deterrent, but that didn't come to fruition.  Enjoy.

We have visited lighthouses across the country and couldn't resist this one.  Nicely maintained, courteous staff, helpful and friendly.  This was the oldest lighthouse (1840's) we've visited, it has a very interesting history.  It was designed by Lt. Meade who would go onto to lead the Union Army in the battle of Gettysburg, after the war he returned to designing and building Lighthouse's as well as other things.  The Lighthouse keepers home was full of all sorts of information and facts and history.  If you're looking for something interesting to do at a slower pace then this is the place for you.  We enjoyed.

This the typical takeout point for whitewater rafting trips down the Lehigh River.  It is very exhilarating experience, depending on when you decide to go.  This park features, rafting, fishing, picnicking, hiking and biking and many other outdoor experiences for families, friends or even on your own.  It has a old railroad bed that has been improved for walking, jogging and lots of other activities.  It is beautiful anytime of the year you go and there are super opportunities for amateur and professional photo taking for whatever suits your style.  Have a blast we have had many here.

Number 3 in our lighthouse tour was beautiful Hereford Lighthouse, the exterior and interior were in pristine condition, staff was helpful in explaining the history of the lighthouse and grounds.  This lighthouse is well taken care of and maintained. There is a great little flower garden out back that was full of butterfly's when we were there.  Presenting us with many photo opportunities to capture both flowers and butterfly's.  This was an enjoyable place to visit, explore and have some fun too, we did.  Enjoy.

You never know what you'll encounter on at Boardwalk and one visit put us in the middle of the St Patrick's Day Parade.  It was fun and there were marching bands, Mummers, Fire Fighters, trailers, vehicles and everyone was Irish (lol) candy was tossed to the kids along the boardwalk route.  You'll see the Absecon Lighthouse and it's a short walk to a cool piece of history.  Then there is always the beach to enjoy.  There are so many great things to do and eat on the boardwalk, you'll certainly enjoy.

This little gem is just a short drive from Bryce Canyon.  While the cave is a little bit of a let down by itself.  It is the trails and surrounding views that range from a clear cold small stream, a waterfall feature, there are hoodoo's, there is a fascinating one with windows that is easily climbable that offers spectacular views of the surrounding areas.  This is truly a beautiful enjoyable side trip that many pass by, they don't know what they are missing it's something special.

If you are into petroglyphs this is an amazing place with lots to work with and enjoy.  If you're not this is still an interesting place to learn a little more about the people who called this area home for a long time.  It is a fairly long drive from Phoenix but we thought it was worth it, bring plenty to drink, there is no shade and it is plenty hot (what a surprise for a desert). I provided you with some picture to give you a taste for the sight. Enjoy either way.

Great places to see, lots of paved & unpaved walking trails all over the park, there is canoeing, picnicking, Frisbee golf and lots more, just relaxing under a tree or sunning in a field, taking photos of nature in her many states.  It is a great place to lose yourself for a while while you soak up the pleasure of being out in nature.  It is an all season adventure and the park changes magnificently for each one.  It really is an enjoyable place to visit often.

Another adventure and a big reward from Zion, we hiked the trail to Emerald Pools and under the waterfall from the pool above.  While it was not a heavy flowing waterfall it was pretty cool and got some good photo's.  It 's not a hard hike and we visited only one of the pools and now we have the remorse of not continuing on to the others.  So take the time and enjoy the sights that are all around you as you travel though thin amazing National Park.

Another stop on our Grand Circle tour of National & State Parks in Utah and Arizona.  You must take the ride on Scenic Byway Highway 12 and the famous Hogs Back on the other side of Boulder, you'll see some of the most spectacular and gorgeous scenery along the way.  Be sure to stop by the Visitor Center in Escalante, they are nice and helpful, you'll be able to get a great overview of the area.

Flagler Station was a small interesting museum with a collection of memorabilia from a model of Fort Jefferson on the Dry Tortugas (Garden Key) the people and times of the railroad.  It is also part of the Conch Train Tour where you can get off and on at the museum. The surrounding area was full of novel stores and attractions worth the stop in our opinion.  Enjoy.

When coming through the desert we were just ahead of a huge thunderstorm  and stopped for the Little Colorado River Overlook it was pretty bland, but still it is a significant feature and worth a few photo's.  But it is an introduction to the Grand Canyon which will take your breath away, so enjoy both, we did.

Great place to relax and enjoy a bit of everything the shore can offer.  Plenty of photo opportunities, enjoy a picnic, do some painting, a little fishing, have fun walking the trails and learning a bit of nature along the way.  This is a good place to have fun and enjoy with others.  Have a great time, we did.

An interesting State Park with many beautiful features that will delight anyone with a camera.  Hiking around exploring the arch and up to the many monoliths is a lot of fun, allowing you a 365 degree view.   This was a fun place to visit and we would recommend you to take the time to do so.  You'll enjoy.

Have enjoyed this recreation area multiple times.  There are a few jewels that we have visited more than once, Dingmans Creek walkway, Dingmans  Falls and Silver Thread Falls are our favorites.  We have also rafted the Delaware River and have thoroughly enjoyed ourselves here.

Canyonlands is like thee parks in one.  Spectacular views, exciting roads and magnificent formations abound and you'll leave in awe.  Mesa Arch  provides some dizzying views 1500 feet below and is a must should you come, you'll certainly enjoy it as much as we did.

Great little park, we stopped there to take a break and rest while walking around and through the downtown area.  It was eclectic area full of various shops, boutiques, various types of art shops and restaurants.  We enjoyed our visit and expect you will too.
Have crossed this bridge thousands of times.  It has never failed to be a challenge, particularly when an 18 wheeler is coming in the opposite direction.  But the views are worth the crossing.
Philly Marathon Finished near the steps, what a great place to be at, we'll certainly be back to enjoy the museum as well.

One of our favorite spots is the hummingbird garden as it is very quiet and there are several benches to sit on and observe the hummingbirds. This is one of the most beautiful places to go to while in Maui. It should definitely be on your list. Both sunrise and sunset are very unique. The drive from the entrance to the summit is about 30 minutes long and, along the road, there are different trails for hiking. If you decide to hike, it's best to go before sunset time or after you have enjoyed the sunrise. For the sunrise, make sure you drive there early. It's pretty chilly up there so I would suggest to bring warm clothes and a blanket. You can also bring your breakfast. Recently, the rules have changed for tickets. If you drive there on your own for the sunrise, you will have to make a reservation on their website. Make sure you bring your pass with you.

(Translated by Google) Highly recommended. Inside there is a collection of more than one and a half million objects from different historical periods. In addition, you can buy the combo ticket and also visit the botanical gardens. The visit lasts at least four hours.

Spectacular 3 miles long white sand beach located about 45 minutes drive from Waikiki. The beach is pretty windy, especially during the winter months, and it actually gets a little cold. This beach is great for the whole family as the waves are not too high. The park has everything you need for a day at the beach (showers, restrooms, picnic tables), and lots of shade from the ironwood trees.
We were also able to schedule a ride with Uber from the beach to go back to our hotel in Waikiki.

My husband and I had a really good time zip lining and climbing here. The staff was super friendly and they didn't rush the group so we were actually able to enjoy the views. The staff was very knowledgeable and we learned a lot about zip lining and the area. We also loved to meet a wild hog that lives there named Pua. It was too cute! I would definitely recommend to come here if you like or want to try zip lining.

My husband and I first visited the arboretum when we used to live in the area and it became one of our favorite places to go to every time we visit. The bonsai museum is very interesting. The fern trail is one of our favorite trails in the arboretum. The place is actually pretty big so I would suggest to pack some snacks and water. Definitely looking forward to move back here and visit this place.

(Translated by Google) A beautiful park where you can do many things including horse riding, canoeing, fishing etc. I recommend going early in the morning to find a parking spot for free.
