My husband and I are in Flagstaff with a group of neighbors. This park was recommended by the hotel staff where we are staying and I am so glad they did. We all thought the park was beautiful and we actually walked around it quite a bit. Further inside the park it smells great. The kids had lots of fun, too. Would definitely recommend, especially during sunset.

We found a baby jackrabbit on the road yesterday evening. It was really hot outside. We took it with us for the night and called Tucson Wildlife Center this morning. They were very kind and fully explained how we can help this little jackrabbit. They said we couldn't bring it unless it was injured, but they provided useful information.

Esperienza molto interessante in cui ci si rende conto di quello che le persone hanno passato e di come siano riusciti a vivere per mesi in queste strutture.

Un piccolo parco un po' rumoroso essendo circondato da due strade molto rumorose ma è comodo per sedersi e riposarsi dopo aver camminato per tanto tempo.

The Tucson Botanical Gardens are beautiful. Definitely the right place if you want to see different kinds of desert plants. The butterfly area was closed, so I am planning to go back to see that. I was able to see some of the butterflies from the glass window and they were spectacular.

A very quiet beach located right under the Diamond Head in fact here there is a trail that will take you up to the summit. Here you can also check out the Diamond Head Lighthouse and the tide pools. If you like surfing, this is a great place.
I was here for a baseball game with my husband and his coworkers. Personally, I don't like baseball, but the stadium is very well made. I thought there was a really good food and drinks option.
This is a great park for dogs but I wouldn't say it's the right place if you want to swim. The ocean is rough and there isn't too much space on the beach. There is no parking so plan ahead.
The ride was very scenic and fun. It's a great place to drive to during the summer months to get a break from the valley heat or during the winter to see the snow.
I used to love hiking here when I used to live in Maryland. My husband used to love fishing here. Very tranquil and relaxing. You can hike to many trails.
I love this place and I totally recommend going even though it'll be closed for a while. The park is very big and it's full of people during the day.
We loved it here. Make sure you wear good hiking shoes and bring water if you plan to stay longer than an hour. The trail can be missed easily.
I liked the show. My husband and I were watching the show from across the street and we could still feel the heat from the flames.
Definitely something to check out at this national park. It felt nice standing close to the vents since it was cold outside.

(Translated by Google) A nice walk and nice area for a picnic.

We drove by with a tour. The statue is impressive. I would definitely recommend to stop by and even visit the museum.
Definitely a must-do in Balboa Park. You can access the tower from the second floor at the Museum of Man.

Which words describes this place the best? Amazing? Fascinating? Awesome? Incredible? Magnificent? Mindblowing? Unique? Great? Cool? Well take all of these words and you have only 1% of what you will see!!! This museum rocks! It has so many cars, engines, models, part, toys ... you can spend here days (!!) not hours. There is so much to read, admire and discover that time flies by. There are three floors with tons of models in extraordinary shape. If you have fuel running through your veins you will cry when you see this place. I guess that it is one of the biggest car collections in the US. So many beautiful cars - simple incredible. The staff is very nice and friendly too, but be aware: They have much to tell. So if you ask a simple question you get the history of the car - which is simply fantastic! Great job by all the people working there. Thank you for the incredible day. Highly recommended!!!

If you are a railroad fan you have to come to this place. It is simply amazing how huge this place is. Over 10.000 railcars are moved and 300 train engines repaired - every day. The workers have been trained by Nascar pit crews to operate as fast and precise as possible. There are many small informations spot on the tower itself. There is one viewing floor on the 8th floor (with windows and protected by winds/rain) and one viewing floor on the 7th floor (completly open; it can get windy/cold up there!). Highly recommended.

Awesome. This is the word which best describe this little, but fascinating railroad museum. They have some stuff to look at but the main attraction is the giant (!!) railroadcity with many trains and cars. If you like railroad or have little children they will love this. There are so many buttons to push - wow! The details are great - many many hours have ben invested in this attraction. Definitly worth a visit. Highly recommended. The managing ladies are doing a wonderful job.

Mixed feeling on this attraction: On one hand its a must if you like Nascar and all the history around it. On the other side tickets are quiet expensive for what you get, you have some attractions, some cars and so on, but it could be a little bit less. I liked it, but you must really be a Nascar fan to enjoy all the stuff. I give it 4 stars - a real fan would give 5 stars, people who have no connection with Nascar may give only 1 star ...

Really awesome. From the outside you don't expect so much to see, but inside you have a museum, some planes plus the ones on the deck, 5 tours aorund the ship and you get so much entertainment and informations. Fantastic. A must see for history fans. We spent around two hours on the carrier. There are snack points and toilets. Highly recommended. Take sunprotection with you because on the flight deck you start burning (if the sun shines).

Amazing. You can see so many reptiles and so many flowers. Wow. Pay attention to the Lizards as they just cross the street. Or the birds which scream very loud. And the flowers which emit nice intense scent. The snakes which can sometimes impress with their size. The crocodiles with their massive tooths. Not to forget the giant turtles which are so patient and nice. There is something for everybody here. Highly recommended!!

Very interesting and good remains of the mill. Unfortunately much of its equipment were destroyed with the fire. So there is not so much to see, but you can get a good impression, learn much about the work life and receive an unique view. I personally loved the historic elevator ride! That was my personal highlight. The museum is more for kids (also grownup kids) as it has different water experiments.

Awesome! Seen so many different animals! The first twenty minutes I was disppointed: Road works and it started raining. But then we received what we wanted. Nature, Bisons, Birds, Mustangs, Deers, ... Simply amazing. Hintes: Drive slowly. Go where nobody is, wait calmly, BE PATIENT - animals are often only 150 feet from the road but well hidden.

A great and very informative museum! It has many informations and photos about trains and railroad. Furthermore you can enter the Truman wagon which he used for his campaign. Then you can see some model trains. Nice. Also some informations on colonists and natives is presented. For kids highly recommended, for adults too!

Here animals are kept in wide open spaces. No small cages. The humans have to sit in their tiny cars, while the animals can move freely around. Altough many people, me included, open their windows to shot photos, you always have to be aware that these animals can react FAST. So watch out. Highly recommended.

Incredible how much stuff is on display in this museum. Airplanes, photos, parts, moodels, ... you can easily spend 3 to 5 hours in this museum, there are three hangars and some have up to three floors. So much to walk and much to see. But the best thing is: It is totally free!! Highly recommended!!!

A nice small museum which offers very good informations on the work of the misselers and what was going on in the 60s, 70s and 80s. Absolutely wonderful. Reminds me the intro of the movie Wargames (1983). Highly recommended. By the way make sure to visit the two nearby missile stations D1 and D9.

Really enjoyed ansd loved it. FItrst I thought thios eould be a super crowded area, but you don't realize how many people are around you - especially at the port you can easily shot photos and walk around without the crowd. Took some great photos and enjoyed the views. Highly recommended.

This is really done good! Lots of love is put into the display and all the effetcs. From the wrecked jeep smoking to all the sound effects. Altough there aren't that many exhibits, I liked it. The ac is extremly strong when you get inside the little museum. Highy recommended.

Lovely recreational park. Seems not populated, we were the only ones there. Nice goose and ducks. Peaceful, simply heaven on earth. The train bridge offers a nice contrast to all the green surrounding you. Recommended for nice views and for it's tranquillity.

I did not do the tour but saw only the visible installation. Having some background information I can partly imagine what was going on during he cold war. Highly recommended and to book a tour (in advance) to be reminded how close we were at World War 3!
Awesome free site! Loads of photo opportunities: colorful dragonflies, alligators, many different birds, bugs, flowers, airplanes and nature. This is really high recommended and a must. Loved it!!
It is a nice place to spend some hours. Yes they have shops, restaurants and you can dive into american history. Expected a bit more ... but it is nicely done. Prices are high for what you get.
Very interesting museum - not only for tobacco. The daily life in the 1800s is pretty well described with some good displays. Staff was very nice. THere are some old houses to walk around.
Spectacular caverns - we had the luck to be only 5 on the guided tour and got extra informations. You will really like this - but please don't touch anything. Highly recommended!!
Nice store with many things to see and discover. If you're looking for some souvenirs here you have a wide choice. Staff is friendly and nice.
Nature can be so beautiful and unique. This place is extraordinary, something so colorful that you can't believe it. But it's true!
Beautiful spot. We were alone. Only birds, raccoons and a deer. Awesome. Only problem: there were also 1000 mosquitoes with us...
Very nice lighthouse - be sure to buy the combo icket for the WWII museum which is located 1.4 miles away. Both are worth a visit
A must see to remind us of what was going during the cold war. There is not much to see but it is highly recommended.

tomorrow morning, so we booked The Fallingwater House at 2.30pm. Unfortunately, however, the museum opens at 10:00 and we don't think we have the time to visit it, also because we have seen that the traffic is very slow.

If you're into fishing this is a great place to call home for a day or two, or even a few hours. The campsites are well marked and large enough for a good size RV or trailer. We visited in the offseason as it was the last week of March and temps were still on the chilly side.

I'm giving it three stars because I'm not into fishing and given that we visited in the off season (camp is opened all year), there didn't seem to be much information on things to do in the shoulder season. We'll be back when the temps are warmer and we can ride or hike more

I wish I could give this 5 stars. I can give it 5 on the overall cleanliness of the grounds and the hot water and duration of the showers (free). Plus the campsite has limited wifi (based on where you're site is). The only reason I give it 4 is the cost. For an out of state guest it cost 38$. This is crazy. You can camp at a private campsite for 30$ and get most of the same perks. No matter, it was a great stay and Mt. Battie is a great hike or ride up via your bike. It's close town and the rangers are helpful and friendly.

This park has so much to offer, in the high season. We came in the off season and we had the place pretty much to our self. The hiking is moderate and enjoyable. The views are spectacular of the canyon.

The campsites are level all around and the restrooms are clean and have heaters for the winter months.

During our trip the crazy cold snap hit the area and 3" of snow moved it and we moved out.

A wonderful state park just outside of Austin, TX. it's 4 miles as the crow flies, but if you want to bike to down it's easy and the one way journey will be 11 miles.

The campsite are flat and well shaded (great for the Texas summer heat). The falls are cool and the hiking in the are is OK, but short.

The onsite restrooms are well kept and there is wifi at the ranger station if needed.

How can you NOT give Fenway Park 5 stars. I've loved this park since I was a kid going to games. Whenever I'm back in New England and Boston for that matter I try and find a way to attend a game. Each year seeing the changes to the park and how they seamlessly fit in are great. The views at sunset are unmatched and the overall vibe is something that any baseball fan needs to experience.

This place is outstanding. There really isn't a bad campsite in the entire park. The view of the stars at night will blow your mind. There is some great dirt road riding in and around the park.

The volunteers seemed to be a bit lazy, but informative. They are hit or miss and don't judge the park based on them.

There are showers and restrooms. Both are nice and well pressurized.

This place...A diamond in the rough. Wow..The views of the lake, the nature trail and camp host make this place a MUST VISIT. If you want to get away from the noise and hustle and bustle of life, visit here in the late fall. The camp host are outstanding and keep things as clean as you would at your house. The bathrooms are spotless and the showers have great hot water.

A great gem of a campground right on the water and in the heart of all the bustle that is the Daytona area. The staff is friendly, camp host on top of it and the restrooms clean.

Part of the beach is closed due to the hurricane still, but if you walk down a bit you can access all of the water and dogs are welcome!

If you love hiking this is a place that must be on your list. You can hike to the highest point in TX. The views on a clear day will blow your mind away. The RV/Camping is nothing special but you're at the start of the hikes and that is worth its weight in gold. The bathrooms are clean and the views breathtaking.

Love this park. It's one special place. If you're looking for a view of the park most people don't take...that's going up Fall River Road. Do it. The visitor center is always busy and a bit overwhelming. Traffic can be overwhelming at times, but it's part of the package with such a cool park to visit.

I'm not sure how to rate a State Capitol. It's pretty cool to see the history of the building and of the state inside. There is a TON of marble and the fact that the dome can be viewed from all over is outstanding.

Around the building there are some homeless but they are harmless and quite.

A great state park and campground in southern, wy. This place can be windy, so be warned.

If you're looking to camp you'll need to make a reservation well in advance. If you're looking to camp in the off season you'll be OK.

enjoy.

A great place to stop and get more info on the park and the area of the park that you're looking to visit. The Rangers are friendly and know all about the dirt roads in the park and if they are passable or not.

This place is outstanding. A diamond in Tucson. The Golden Gate drive is outstanding. The best way to see the park is to hike a bit and to also ride your bike in and around the park and up Gates Pass!
A great place to take a stroll with friends, kids or one's 4 legged friend. I highly recommend this for a mellow walk, run, ride. Great views of Boulder's Flatirons and surrounding landscapes.
A great park at the edge of the everglades. Lots of sites with hookups and the restrooms are clean. There is also a great little central area that is screened in to keep you clear of the bugs!
Great spot for a run or walk with your dog. Sadly dogs are not allowed on the beach but lots of folks seems to have their dogs out there which was ok with us and those around. Very clean!!!'
A pretty cool tourist trap of a landmark. The walk out to the point is sweet and clean. The only downside is the pay to park areas. It seems like the whole area is pay to park.
Absolutely breathtaking. Worth the hike in from the campground. Amazing hike along the river and the ferns are outstanding. I can see why they would film Jurassic World here.
This place is amazing. The running path is awesome and you can follow up a nice 3m run with a dip in the lake. Or use the free showers to clean up.
We stayed here in a sprinter camper van in a overflow campsite...best spot in the place right  in front of a majestic tree. Would come back again!!
Of the cooler lighthouses on the west coast. Great views of and from the light house. The walk is peaceful and breathtaking.
A great place if you're a college kid. A bit crowded if you're just checking it out. But still cool to visit just once.
A cool waterfront park area in old town Beaufort. Lots of history in the area and a great place to people watch .
A nice beach to hangout at during low tide. Tons of room for dogs to run and play. Amazing views.

Near the end of Cape Cod by Providencetown the National Seashore Visitors Center is a must. The protected landscape in this area is fantastic.  Besides the exhibits and great Rangers the view is super. Short drive to beach access.  View of another lighthouse.  Can get off road pass to drive on beach to lighthouse.  Also saw RV's on the beach too. Bicycle trails are a huge thing throughout the park to all the sites to be seen and in between riding through pristine landscape. Handicap access to the beach over dunes by a huge blue mat which is secured to the ground and extends from parking lot past the dune line onto the beach. At the end of the mat you are about half way to the water and sand does get a bit soft. Bathrooms and showers at beach area.

First off, if your not prepared or willing to drive down a dirt/gravel road at 10-15 mph for 10 miles, don't go here. I went in a 22' RV and it took an hour. Just keep driving East on Castle Dome Mine Road from off 95, till you hit the dead end.
Great old mining town with lots of artifacts. Leisurely walk through the town, every building has something different inside. Lots of written explanations of who, what, and when on buildings and items (self guided tour).
The gal working the admission and gift shop was very helpful. Looking in the gift shop I asked her if they had any florescent rock up here. Yes, they do, ask to see! Call to check times of mine tour.

Very interesting for a man to have a vision to put the Worlds history engraved into granite, to last for over 5000 years.  He is preserving what others are trying to hide. We learn from past history, it should never be forgotten. Quaint little gift shop, which also the Felicity Post Office. Out on the highway the population of Felicity says 2, they have a population of 10 now. The Maze of Honor is unique and interesting even though it is a recent addition to the grounds. Little Church on the hill is breathtaking in views and in architecture, especially the ceiling.

Love staying in the campground but sad that you have to wait 11 months form reservation placing till time to stay. Just about the best of everything in the Keys they have to offer. Camping, cabins, kayaks, snorkeling tours. Boat ramp, marina, fishing, snack bar, gift shop, nature center, nature trail. Swimming beaches on Atlantic Ocean or Bayside. New bathrooms by the beach with showers and new bath house in campground (could use better venalation).
likes: Amenities (snack bar, gift shop, nature center, nature trail)

reviews_attraction.text: Beautiful boardwalk but lacking birds this time of year... too hot. Gopher turtles and lizzards seen regularly here.  Nice educational room with some live reptiles, taxadermy, also some animal skulls.  Has bathrooms and picnic tables under cover to eat lunch. Free to park and wander the boardwalk. They have moonlight strolls on certain dates throughout the year. Handicap parking and access to boardwalk.

Sensory overload of how much this man has collected over the last 31 years. He has so many interesting stories and can answer any question you may have. The Model A's and Model T cars and trucks were great. Some restored and some all origional, others build out of just parts put together. I would recommend visiting the museum and see how many things you can identify!

Beautiful campground right on the lake. Has bath house with showers, picnic table and fire pit at every site. Nice swimming beach and boat launch. 5 here is also another launch close to the campsites for kayaks. I-75 is right next to campground so you do here some traffic noise but get use to it quickly.  Spending 4 nights here.

A birders paradise.  Great exhibits and a nice gift shop.  What really makes this place is the boardwalks over the tidal marshy area of the Bayside of South Padre Island.  Would go here every day if I lived here. During the winter months there are so many migratory birds. I added a few to my lifetime list.

Fantastic birding site. Saw a Harrier Hawk after I turned onto the road back to visitor center.  Ponds behind visitor center teaming with water birds... couple alligators too.  Picnic area here behind visitor center overlooking the ponds. Nice hiking trail but I enjoyed the auto tour of the wetlands best.

Very few parking spots around the traffic rotary. You can easily ride bikes here from town. Can see two lighthouses from this point. Can walk out the rock jetty (but wear good tennis or boat shoes) to one and walk the tidal zone when tide is out. Lots of wading birds in area.

It was interesting to see this place.  I remember when the scientists got locked in this environmental test to see if we could sustain life on another planet. Now the University of Arizona has the facility and climate control is being studied here.

Very unique story behind this house from its beginning to now. Worth the $10 admission for the tour. Tour guide was excellent! Take your time looking at everything because there is so much to see, just mind boggling.

Amazing on how many Petroglyph's are here in one area.
I am disabled and was able to get up to the second switchback.  I was also able to do the trail from the trailhead to restrooms and picnic tables.
Loved this Mission!  Grounds very well kept. Disappointed that the Visitor Center was closed and rangers not on duty Monday and Tuesday.  Couldn't get my stamp for my Passport Book.
Totally amazing as to the perfect spiral this labyrinth is. One guy visiting was even measuring it to find out what the distanced walking it would be. Kronos to whomever made it.
Best wetlands I have been to in a long time. Nice walking trails either concrete or hard Arizona dirt. Seats alongside ponds for viewing.  Big lake that you can fish in too.
Think that $45 a night is a bit much for a county park campground.  It is just a parking lot area with electric and you can't see the ocean unless you cross over the dunes.
Was totally handicap accessible.  Ranger directed to walk trail starting to the left, was an easy grade up.  Loved looking at the ruins from the past.  Much history here.
Very clean kept snakes.  Didn't realize there were so many different kinds of rattlesnakes. They did have a couple of non venomous snakes for sale.
The State Park for LBJ is across the street from the ranch.  More memorbilia in their building and they also have a living town to visit.
Would have liked it better if you were still able to drive your own vehicle on the park roads. They do have an open air tram.
What an inspiring place.  The statues were awesome.  Bring markers to write on a rock to leave in the prayer rock area.

Nice piece of history to visit. Birding is suppose to be excellent, but not for me today.
Still recommend going here.
Nice stop to see something no one else has... add to the quarky list when passing by.  Nice place to stretch legs.
Strange place in the middle of nowhere.  Many people stopping as they drive by. Bring a lock to put on the fence.

Nice park. Has plenty of trails and the river is pretty nice. They must have been doing some tree clearing or something because the tractor tracks tore up ground and there was trees and branches in some of the trails. 1of the wooden walkways have been tore up for awile. Plenty of parking.

Great place to stop. Waterfalls isn't too far away. The lake is beautiful, a little bit warmer than some other places but still cold..
Some of the best Trails so far. Whoever is making them good job. The best part is it looks like you're using natural Timbers from around the area.

Beautifully taken care of Park the service people are really great, the trails are excellent for running& biking.  Trail markers and signs are excellent. The soccer fields and Lacrosse fields look in very good shape with good drainage

Has some very good history. Lots of books and information on the trail. Has some interactive stuff for the kids in the basement area. The only thing I would have liked to see is a t-shirt under $28, $18 -$20 more likely to buy 1or 2.

We had a great trip. Everybody was wearing masks - canoes and kayaks were in good shape. The only thing that would have been better is if they'd have someone come by to have people sign slip in line to clear people from line.

Looks like they're getting ready to destroy some of the old Trails, no gravel on the trails people are using and the lakes filled with silt makes it hard to kayak in. Other than that it's a great place to hike, bike or climb

I like the park. The trails are pretty long and loop aroun lookd the parking lot and the river nicely. They need to do some more maintenance it was trees in the way and one of the wooden walkways was missing the floor.

Great park. Glad I made it. The tours seem to go from bathroom to bathroom but the scenery in between was beautiful -we saw Moose, wolverine, deer, rabbits & more. . The clouds cleared and witnessed the mountain.

We stopped to stretch our legs. The beach was somewhat clean but the water was very cold. I don't know about having a picnic there but it was a good place to stop and stretch our legs for the rest of our trip.

Great time and a lot of great volunteers. Expanding their collection and Museum. Really glad I got to stop and can't wait to see some of the stuff that they're refurbishing right now make it out on the floor
Great hike & Rock formations. We had a great time more technical if you want to actually climb & play around. You may want to leash your younger kids also there are a lot of cliffs and overlooks...
Great place to climb ,Mountain Run. Usually pretty quiet in some areas although people do litter a lot. Too real nice caves to hide in if it's raining and always seems to be something new to find.
Well maintained trails, glad somebody was smart enough to put wire over the wooden walk ways somebody should tell that to the national Park system instead of them cutting out wooden walkways.
Great place to stop for a short hike. It's wheelchair-accessible all the way and I bathroom at the beginning. Road closed afterwards though no hot springs access unless you bicycle then hike
The surrounding scenery is beautiful most of the buildings are closed off, Staff only, but the garden was nice & the yards are well kept. Good place to stop and stretch your legs.
Great place to hang out with your family and friends. Plenty of stuff to do and see. Whether you want to Bicycle ,run ,walk, hike or climb rocks. There is something for everyone..
Nice park. I thought there would be more trails through the woods, but maybe I'm just missing them. The soccer fields were in good shape, parking lots a little small though.
Great place to stop, $30+ a person for all 4 attractions.. We all had a great time. Think we should have done the shooting game first.. The ride was better than expected.
I wish I could have a garage like that. Motorcycles, bicycles, antique cars and more. Today's auto executives should go there for a clue on how a good car is built.
Nice park. Had a clean beach in front of it and the walking trail was nice. I like watching the boats go through the canal on the west side.
Great place to have a picnic or relax and chill out. Had a maintained grill and trash can. Very little road noise and traffic going by.
Good food, Great atmosphere, wine & outdoor space.. They even let you bring your dogs in for the outside patio.
Great place to take the family. There are camping areas in the area. Some nice hiking trails and things to do.
Great park. Most of the trails are well-kept. Only part I don't like is most trails are no dogs allowed.
Great place to visit. Very somber place. I never even knew it was here before today I'm glad I found it.

Denali National Park and Preserve is a beautiful place with lands untouched by man. It is important to note that Denali is more of a preserve than a "park." Cars are not allowed beyond the bus station. You must buy a bus ticket to go very deep into the park. There are no real "trails" past the bus depot either. My husband and I hiked the tundra by compass just to make sure we didn't get turned around in all the wide open land. If you buy a bus ticket, you can get off the bus at any stop and catch another bus later. The only problem with this is, the buses are really full, and it's very hard to find a bus that has room for you to hitch a ride back. I feel like Denali needs to get a better system for making sure hikers don't get stranded. Some hikers were waiting and told by 5-6 buses that there was no room. When my husband and I were trying to catch a bus back after a hike, we were over 50 miles from our car, so walking back wasn't an option. When we finally caught a bus, it was almost completely full and we had to sit away from one another. The bus driver would stop if someone spotted wildlife, but you had to remain on the bus and it was so crowded that getting a good view of anything was difficult. The bus system is really set up like more of a sight-seeing adventure. It's very crowded and touristy. If you enjoy that type of thing and want to sit on a crowded bus for 4+ hours, you would probably enjoy this. I prefer exploring alone.
I should also add, there is no where to buy food or drinks past the bus station, so make sure you bring all you will need for a full days' adventure!

Denali National Park and Preserve is a beautiful place with lands untouched by man. It is important to note that Denali is more of a preserve than a "park." Cars are not allowed beyond the bus station. You must buy a bus ticket to go to Eielson Visitor Center. If you buy a bus ticket, you can get off the bus at any stop and catch another bus later. The only problem with this is, the buses are really full, and it's very hard to find a bus that has room for you. At Eielson there is a ranger that will put you on a waiting list, and they control how many people get back on the buses from there so it is easier to get back on a bus there than at other stops.
I should also add, there is no where to buy food or drinks past the bus station, so make sure you bring all you will need for a full days' adventure! Eielson has picnic tables where you can eat lunch if you brought it. It also has a couple of small trails to beautiful views.

My family and I loved the Downtown Aquarium in Denver. The price was a little high, but exactly what you would expect from an aquarium this size. I'm sure it costs a lot to upkeep this place and it was kept up very well.  There are many species on display. Kids can stop and feed the spitting fish and touch starfish. My boys loved petting and feeding the sting rays. There is a small snack bar at the end of the exhibit, and an Aquarium restaurant if you want to have a full meal. As with most  aquariums, you exit through the gift shop so you can stop and buy a souvenir if interested!

I visited the Guinness World Records Museum and although it was interesting enough, it wasn't anything to write home about. Many of the exhibits were outdated or simply didn't work. I have read they are currently renovating, so that will probably take care of this issue. I thought the museum was very similar to Ripley's, which may have also lessened my enjoyment of the place. (I visited this one second.) I thought my kids would really enjoy this because they love the World Record books, however they were less than impressed with this experience.

I was extremely skeptical about going to this show at first. I truly don't enjoy horse shows or rodeos, and thought those things didn't mix with dinner. However, I will be the first to admit, I was wrong. This show was great. It held not only my attention, but the attention of my children as well. The food was absolutely amazing. I loved the creamy vegetable soup. My children loved getting to walk by the horse stalls and see the "stars" before and after the show. I would definitely recommend this show/dinner to anyone!

My husband and I recently attended the Robert Earl Keen Count Down to Christmas tour at the Ryman Auditorium. The show was great and the venue was a wonderful piece of history. On one hand, it's obviously not as comfortable as a new venue but on the other, you are experiencing a piece of history. I sat in Row D of section 10 in the balcony and it felt very close. Our views were not obscured. I will likely be back for another show if given the chance.
likes: Facilities & Services: Good seating, unobstructed views

reviews_attraction.text: The gateway arch is a great place to visit. There is a great history museum on the complex. The only negative about this place is the journey to the top. If you are claustrophobic at all, this is a very tough ride. You will be seated in a very small egg shaped elevator, and they pack it full. You must ride to the top this way, and when you get to the top, it is very small and there are normally a lot of people there.

Pirate's Cove has been a long-time favorite of my family since I was a child myself. It has two levels of mini golf, and one is wheel-chair and stroller accessible. The other level has a lot of stairs to navigate, but it is my favorite. My children love playing mini golf here as well. Each day there are 2 holes chosen as "free game" holes if you score a hole-in-one, so make sure you keep score on your score card!

My husband and I visited Mount Nebo during a trip to nearby Mount Magazine. We decided to take the 2nd day and visit Mount Nebo, and I'm so glad we did. We both felt the hikes and the views were actually better from Mount Nebo. Even though it was overcast, foggy/misty day we were still able to see a lot. I would definitely recommend this place for hiking or even just to take in the beautiful scenery!

If you've never been to a Ripley's Believe It or Not museum, you will probably enjoy this quite a bit. Every Ripley's Museum I've been to are basically the same, so if you expect it to be a lot different than others you will be disappointed. There are obviously a few different exhibits in each museum, but they are still extremely similar. Overall, I enjoyed the museum and my kids loved it.

My kids loved Grant's Farm. It was a very nice place to visit. We were able to watch animal shows. My kids loved seeing elephants, and my daughter got to ride a camel. The baby goats were also a favorite. You can feed them bottles, but you should be careful because they get pretty aggressive when they are trying to get to a bottle. A smaller child could get knocked down pretty easily.

Silver Dollar City is my absolute favorite amusement park. I'm not a huge amusement park enthusiast, but this park has a much more laid back feel to it than most. I have been here dozens of times. The Christmas light display they have in November and December is a must-see. The park is always clean and very family-oriented.

First of all, I almost always rate things at 4 or 5 so I am not hard to please. HOWEVER, this was the biggest waste of money I've ever experienced in my life. There was nothing exciting about...not even close. You could get the same effect by sitting in a box and letting someone shake the sides. Seriously....it's BAD.

Independence Mine State Historical Park is a fascinating place if you love history. The site still has most of the original buildings and has signs explaining each one. It was very fun to walk around and read each sign and go into the buildings. (You can't go into all of them, but you can go into several.)

We call this place Heaven on Earth. This riverway offers so much. There are trails to walk,  crystal clear water (deep and shallow), gravel bars to spend the day, and the views are beautiful. If you love floating, kayaking, canoing, camping, or just hanging out riverside you won't be disappointed here

On a recent trip to RMNP in June, I was so disappointed to hear Trail Ridge Road was still closed from winter snows. Luck had it that it opened up a day before we left, so we were able to take our kids up the road and show them the scenery that we loved so much during our previous visit.

I love to hike the trails and Johnson's Shut-Ins. I have not visited in the summer, as I enjoy the peace and tranquility of the winter months when there are not many other visitors. The hiking trails have many beautiful views.

This Haunted House was well put together. I don't particularly care for this type of entertainment, but my family wanted to try it out. It was an interesting experience. . .about par for the course in terms of Haunted Houses.

Busch Stadium is a great place for a baseball fan. I've seen a lot of complaints about prices, but that is just part of the experience when it comes to Major League Baseball. Food prices are always high in stadiums.
I absolutely love history, so historical sites are always of interest to me. This cabin has easy access and is interesting to visit. It will be worth your time if you like history at all!
My husband and I stopped by the Eiffel Tower Park in Paris for that obligatory Paris selfie. LOL. It was a cute little park. I really enjoyed the small town of Paris.
I  took my children to Ripley's Aquarium of the Smokies during a visit to Gatlinburg. They loved seeing all the fish and different species of sea animals.
This place is very cool. I loved looking around and imagining this place as it was built in history. It is built on a massive cliff, and is very majestic.
This stop-off is well worth the time and energy it takes to see the view. It gives view of the entire valley area.
This is a great historical place. It is a great place to snap a few pictures and admire a piece of history.

Incredible rotating collection in a central and histoic spot downtown . Come on in and see the nations top artists on display and FOR FREE. The museum has paired up with Yampatika, a local naturalist guiding non-profit, to have an interactive and educational corner for kids of all ages. Take a walk with one of the passionate volunteers to find joy and wonder in every work of art on the wall. Step in at any chance you have to warm your hands and your spirit.

Beautiful lush pnw trails with great incline. The trail system covers a lot of area and pop out on to urban streets making this park a great way to weave physical activity into you on foot commute to town.
The lodge is a great venue for classes and feature a commercial kitchen and even a number of bunk beds. I was pleased with this well maintained and frequented park reflecting some of the Northwest's natural beauty.

What a great surprise. A members based gallery also featuring other local artists. I was greatly impressed with the wide range of themes, mediums and styles of this eclectic group of artists. I had a pleasure speaking with the staff and look forward to returning for their 2nd Friday monthly gallery openings. Stop in for a look and spark up a conversation to learn more about this great D.C artists hub.

I joined Yampatika on their emerald mountain Snowshoe hike. Our guide Karen was knowledable, fun, and so kind. It was incredible exploring the trails and roads on Howelson hill and learning more about the emerald mountain history. We were pleased with the incredible view of Steamboat and storm peak. So much fun and can't wait to go back and ski.

I love this park! There are multiple play structures for kids, play fields, an incredible earth art to run around,  tennis courts, dog parks, the historic boys school and cow barn, the out door theater and as of lately they have done a great job developing the northern beach. There is parking on the south end of the park and the middle point.

Peel off the road on your way to or from AS capital for this little piece of heaven. A beautifully maintained park and walk way allong the water. Make sure to being binoculars to glass the many birds and wildlife that call this area home. Perfect for kids, family outtings, or walls alone.

We spent almost 5 hours here at the different interactive stations. The staff were great and the kids had a blast. I encourage parents to look over the many games and bin options that you can ask the front desk for. There is so much to offer from the FIG, take advantage of it all!

Great recreation park. Includes easy put in and pull out for water sports. A nice field and trees for slack lining and lawn games. This park connects to the inter urban trail that takes you past our famous water treatment park, the blue heroin reserve and a dog park.

A huge collection of plants. Not only is this an incredible place to learn about and see amazing botanicals but they also host events. Live music, parties, events of all kinds. Stop by this free museum, visit the indoor and out door, tropical and desert gardens.

Great interactive museum covering air and space. You can wander around space shuttles or investigate the history of celestial navigation. Family friendly and usually packed. They also have flight simulators and an Imax 3D movie theater.

Just $15 for hours of fun and over stimulation. They have a huge range of tables from the 60's, 70's and present. All working and free! We made a day of it going to dim sum before and tea tasting after all in the international district.

Usually a busy trail head. Plan a day hike or bring a picinic. Artist Point has incredible views, so being your camera or water color set. Getting to the top can be trickey, have a good driver or take a shuttle if you must.

Check in with reservations before if you are hoping to camp. Silver lake is a great day trip with the lake and little hikes, you can rent a boat or just enjoy the area. Alao awesome for camping with kids or adults.

A great display of Chihuly's work. Very exspensive for the size of the exhibit. The garden is nice and I'm sure the space is great for events. I liked the museum of glass much more if you are going to chose.
Beautiful and free! This museum covered a lot of bases showing ancient and contemporary art. Themes exhibits and interactive stations. I love the gift shop too. They host wonderful events as well.
Interactive and educational. This free museum has and incredible collection of art. Be ready to dedicate 3 hours to experince all of the video art and interactive stations. I can't wait to return
Wall, run or stroll through this great park. Watch the boats come through, fish climb the fish ladder, or explore the incredible collection of trees, shrubs and flowers in this park.
Incredible collection of information and artifacts including the Berlin wall. Scheduled to close December 31st due to lack of funding which is such a shame, GO SEE IT WHILE YOU CAN!
I was impressed with this interactive  and welcoming homestead. The gardens were fantastic, especially the fragrance garden. Nice  for a picnic or a not too far get away with kids.
This place is HUGE! Totally worth the stop if you're in the area. It's FREE and there is so much information. Well curated, i would love to see more events held in that space.
A beautiful welcoming space open for worship or other events. Recently remodeled it is both modern and classic. Easy to find and great parking for being in North capital hill.
For only $2 this place can entertain you for a goos hour, great for kids too. Make sure to check out this spot for the monthly art walk!
Parking can be tough and sketchy, and the hike in is pretty steep. A fun little hike and a great get away not too far out the Chuckanuts
A beautiful collection of plants plus a beautiful space with a colorful history. Friendly and knowledgeable staff and cool events!
A Seattle icon! He gets dressed  up for holidays like bunny ears on Easter, and a great reflection of PNW art and creativity.

This ia a trailhead for some good hikes, and also a small and quiet campground.  Check out online for the largely off trail hike to Gibon Mtn. if you are up for and capable of off trail navigation.  There is an interesting story to the name.  Hirabayashi was a Japanese citizen who challenged the internment of the Japanese during WW2.  He lost the case in the Supreme court, but the decision was repudiated in 2011.  He was also a Quaker and was convicted of draft resistance, serving a sentence of hard labor (building the highway) at a low security Federal prison camp at the trailhead location - a number of old foundations are there.   Read about it on the wiki, interesting story.  It is a very scenic location at least to spend a prison sentence, and reasonable temp in the summer.

Unless the road is wet  or snowy, you can get there in a sedan; I've done so at least four times.  You don't need a permit to day hike into Wire Pass / Buckskin Gulch (but you do need one, which is hard to get, for The Wave).  Wire Pass is a slot canyon of a minor drainage into Buckskin Gulch.  In places it is only a few feet wide.  There is one drop that varies from year to year; some years it is easy, in others people put logs or rocks into place. Be careful going down - you must climb back up to get out!  There are petroglyphs on the rock wall just as you join Buckskin.  Going downstream in Buckskin gets towering canyon walls though there is often stagnant water just as things close up after the confluence.  You can also hike upstream in Buckskin.

Death Valley is an amazing though austere place.  The park itself is huge - the biggest US national park in the 48 states.  The first time visitor can see large portions of the park from paved roads - Badwater, Dante's View, the Mesquite Dunes.  Hikes are numerous although there are not a large number of trails.  In fact one can get out into huge empty places with either four wheel drive or by hiking on old miner roads and trails.  But take plenty of water and you must have maps and decent navigation skills.  If you like solitude and vast views, you won't be disappointed.

This is a short little trail on the north side of the paved highway.   It is not very well marked - I had driven by it a few times before I pulled over to check it out.  A relatively short (a mile or two) trail leads north into a bay beneath the mesa above,  where all manner of "toadstool" rocks can be found. These are cool columns of softer rock with a harder boulder balanced on top.  You can walk around and see quite a few interesting rock formations.  It can be hot and there is little shade, so bring lots of water if it is sunny.

I took the trail North from the interstate rest area. The trail goes about 5 miles until it hits in Indian reservation which you are not supposed to enter. There are several side trails that are well marked with a nice sign by the trailhead so you can easily hike 12 miles or so. Conditions range from level and straight to track old road to smaller foot paths in the forest. Lots of alligators. Mostly a very quiet except right by the beginning at the highway. Many many birds very nice

This is a nice but rather small beach between the road and the ocean on the narrow key.   It is about 3/4 mile long.  The beach continues past houses in both north and south directions, and seems fine to walk on.  There is a very large and free parking area, and nice toilet building.  There is a ramp for wheelchair access as well.  There is also a short nature trail on boardwalk on the inland side of road, where you can walk through mangrove forest.

Whipple Hill is a small conservation area on the Winchester / Lexington border.   There is sometimes limited parking but you can park on nearby side streets.  There is a central ridge - Whipple Hill is the highest point on the NW side of Boston of the hills surrounding Boston Basin - with a few views, and a number of marked forest paths.  There is also a nice pond with a small loop around that.   Boardwalks protect some of the muddiest areas.

The trail is rough in places, volcanic rocks and stuff, definitely would recommend sturdy shoes for this.  There is no shade, and it gets hot - bring plenty of water.  The wind turbines are huge and further off than they appear, but that ridge gets a marvelous cool breeze.  The adventuresome can make a loop from the eastern trailhead on some dirt roads, but there's a bunch of miles and climbing involved.

This is a beautiful hiking area reached from Madera Canyon, but "waterfall" is a bit of an exaggeration.  It is really a spring, Sprung Spring, which flows over a rocky ledge and over the trail.   The spring is less likely to be your destination than some of the nearby peaks in the Mt. Wrightson area, or Baldy Saddle which is up on the ridge going NW from the main summit block.

Keys view is the end of the paved road with a parking area and stunning views to the south, over Palm Springs to San Jacinto mountain and over to the east to the Salton Sea.  But it's even nicer to leave your car and walk on use trails to the west, along a ridge line, and over several small summits.  The intrepid will reach Inspiration Peak and... be inspired!

Trailhead for many places.  Head through the cactus forest on side trails to the south.  Or continue up and make a loop via the Cabrillo or Three Tanks trails - map on the park web site.  Bridalveil falls is pretty when flowing.  Or continue in solitude on and up over rolling grasslands and open forest to Douglas Spring camp area, which often has flowing water

The "M" as a destination in itself is pretty meh.  Steep trail gets you some views, which are nice, but the M is really just a bunch of white rocks.  The trail continues on (and up!) for many miles along the ridge, and that is quite nice.  Parking lot gets crowded.  A busy place.

Interesting place with cool plants.  A lot of the time it is in the clouds for much of the day.  There is a paved road that goes up the mountain.  Once it levels out it turns to dirt and is pretty rough.  Decent hiking trails here though hard to find much info on them.

Wonderful hiking opportunities from low saguaro desert to higher grasslands.  A cool oasis with seasonal stream lined with cottonwood and sycamore trees.  You can pay ten bucks and ride a tram up canyon and get on and off or walk miles and miles.  Wonderful.

A very popular trail.  Steep and only partially shaded, but a breeze tends to blow up there.  No chance for solitude but you go through some interesting forest and get up to a nice overlook   1500 ft climb, a bit over 2 miles.  Lots of people.

Wonderful hiking from Saguaro lowlands to higher grasslands to forested peaks.  Just bring plenty of water if it is hot.  Good visitor center exhibits and gift shop.  At its best early and late in the day.

It was summer and I went to hike not to ski. The route to the top is not well marked so it's good to have a map but you get up to the ridge rather quickly. In the early summer the flowers are beautiful

The Art Smith trail is very scenic and rolli g after the initial climb.  Nice rocks and varied vegetation.  Quite a few birds about.  Great views out over the valley to Joshua Tree and the Salton Sea.
Ah the best hiking in Maui.  Wonderful volcanic landscapes, reds and blacks, cinder cones and cliffs.  Silversword plants found nowhere else.  Some great trails.  A bit short on oxygen :)
These forests broadly describe the area south of Rocky Mountain National Park, and include the very scenic Indian Peaks wilderness.  Many many many trails in the area!
Drops down 1k feet on the way to the crater.  Look for nene at Holua cabin.  Continue up to see red cinders and silverswords.  A bit further 5.5 mi in for black sand!
This TH itself is just a wide spot in the road, but it has a number of trails leading to very beautiful places up near and on the Continental Divide.
A very small beach at the east of the entrance to the Lagoon.  People fish off the pier.  Good for a short stroll  Not very remote.
Scenic, a bit rough for hiking across the lava.  I enjoyed the Cape.  Not a swimming place but peaceful.  Tons of feral goats.
The parking lot is tiny.   After circling for 5 times looking for a space when someone left, we gave up and left.

New York State Parks are wrll-maintained and beautiful in general.  This park is special because of the geological rock formations exihibited on the walls of the gorge and the three beautiful waterfalls labeled as Upper Middle and Lower on the Genesee River.  This park is about twenty miles long had has several hiking trails through it.  There are restaurants, stores, a museum and a Civil War parade training field on the premises.  We hiked and climbed the steep stairs to see these natural wonders.  We enjoyed the scenic views as we walked and got out exercise at the same time.  It was truly a beautiful way to spend the day.

The Capitol Building is a beautiful building and the Ariel view is in the shape of an H.  This is a replica of the original building which unfortunately burned down.  The only original artifact is a chair in the front of the court room.   Originally, the first court house was in Jamestown, then it moved to Willamsburg and finally to the current location in Richmond, VA.  The tour guide provided some good examples of previous court cases and how and why they were litigated.  We also saw the various Chambers in the building and saw what it means to "approach the bench" and "pass the bar".  Very interesting indeed.

Live viewing animals in their natural habitat.  Every time you go, you see something new and different.  The Lions are my favorite but I like seeing all of the animals.  Don't drop your phone because you will be unable to venture out to get it.  Keep your camera steady and stay seated for the guided tour.  If you don't have a fast pass, arrive by 9:00 am and wait usually is not too long relative to other times of the day.  Think I will try same strategy for Avatar ride.  That can be a few hours wait if you don't hit it right.

This was not like the Opry I went to years ago when you could hear real music played and good songs sung.  We will be more careful next time what show we pick out when looking for a true Christmas show.  This was not child appropriate.  It was more like a acrobat circus show.  It was a Holidaze show and we were truly dazed by it.  Do not go to this show if you believe in a traditional Christmas message and do not want to watch so-called Christmas decorations which are sexual in nature and contain virtual nudity.

Very interesting museum about the Titanic and the terrible tragedy of 2012.  The ship was supposed to be unsinkable but obviously was not when it hits the iceberg.  Many lives we're lost and the Captain went down with the ship.  The ship had beautiful China and furnishings but not enough life boats.  I volunteered to play Nearer My God to Thee on the piano, a replica of the original over 100 years old and did the Irish Jig.  Good to commemorate the lives that we're lost on this tragic occasion.

Never grow tired of coming here to see the terrific selection of animals from the wild kingdom of Africa.  Everyday is a new experience as the animals are captured doing different and unusual things.  It is really a site to behold.  The Lions, giraffes and cheetahs are my favorites and all of the animals are part of God's beautiful creation.  Come share in the beauty and wonder of this Safari experience.  You won't regret it!

This is a nice place to walk and view growth and care of various types of fish at different stages of development.  Yesterday additional exhibits were set up under tents disseminating information about fishing and other types of wildlife and conservation.  Families with children were able to fish, shoot and use bow and arrows free of charge.  There was good food  and refreshments available and a good time was had by all.

Very interesting, well-built, historic place.  Very scenic fort with good view of lighthouse on lake.  Five buildings exist to your and underground artillery stations for protection of fort.  Enjoyed walking around top perimeter of fort as well where men used to guard incoming forces with canons and other artillery.  Museum is interesting and guide book received after admittenance is very informative.

Visiting historic Fredericksburg Virginia was very interesting.  We went to the main visitor center just west of downtown.  We did the walking tour and saw the famous stone wall at Mayre's Heights.  We also visited the store.  The National Cemetery is located just above the center on the hill with a monument.  A driving tour takes you through the Prospect Hill area of the battlefield.

Enjoyed walking through the zoo next to Hershey Park.  Interesting animals and exhibits.  It was a rainy day and it is hilly so you need to watch your step here.  We viewed everything without mishap.  The prairie dogs and other animals were very cute.  When we were done at the zoo we continued riding some rides and then on to the chocolate factory.  Very fun and diversified place.

Montpelier was the home of President James Madison, Father of the Constitution and Architect of the Bill of Rights.  Enjoyed hearing history Of Dolly Madison, America's first "First Lady," and the history of the Founding Era.  Montpelier teaches us how our Constitution affects our everyday lives.  We also learn more about daily life in the 18th and early 19th centuries.

Historic Walnford was a working farm until the 20th Century.  The was also a saw mill operating through the 1870s. The Waln house was built in 1773 and is the largest existing pre-revolutionary home in Monmouth County,. The home and outbuildings are stately situated in the picturesque grounds.  A beautift place to see and visit.  Have a picnic and/or go on a hike,

Enjoyed Bubba's restaurant and walking around before entering park.  Parking and entering property was arduous for us.  Once you gain access it is fine.  We we're mainly walking for exercise in beautiful and warm Orlando location.  I'm not really interested in the night life and was not there in late evening when place is in full swing.

Enjoyed seeing visitors center including ship, movie and tour guide briefing.  We completed the full auto/CD tour of the property as well.  Learning about the strategies and responsibilities of the troops to win the war was fascinating.  What was only a promise of Independence in 1777 became a reality in 1781.

Don't miss this the panoramic view and battle enactment was very informative and good visual aid on the enactment of the Gettysburg battle.  See tie artifacts, have lunch and go on the tous inside and out.  New building is much improved and there is so much here to see and do.  Store has great souvenirs.

Today was a good afternoon to tour the Safari.  It was cool out with a few raindrops.  We had some very good close ups of some animals that are usually more distant.  Every ride on the Safari is a new experience.  Animals are always doing new and interesting things and the African terrain is beautiful.

We launched our new boat from the dock next door.  People gave us information on the area and boating there and were extremely friendly, helpful and supportive.  Very nice park, establishment and atmosphere.  Had a fun and relaxing time.  Plenty of good parking too.

Enjoyed visiting this museum and seeing the history of boxing.  There were movie clips and pictures of the great fights and memoribilia belonging to the boxers, managers and sportscasters.  Some of these items we're for sale in the store.  Very interesting place.
likes: Facilities & Services: Memorabilia, movie clips, pictures

reviews_attraction.text: We enjoyed the virtual reality ride on Avatar and looking at the science exhibits while waiting in line.  It is a great adventure experience.  The scenery is beautiful and the ride is fun.  There is also a store and restaurant nearby that we enjoyed going to.

Outstanding place.  Fresh air, beautiful scenery and a boat ride fishing with my husband down a gently flowing stream was the recipe for a beautiful day.  We were previously here last year and had fond memories so we returned again this year.

This is a beautiful facility and well maintained place with interesting exhibits about wolfs and grizzlies.  Exciting to see these species because they are harder to find in the forest than other wildlife like elk and buffalo.
This is a beautiful and clean park with camp ground, lakes, trails, beach, playground and serene lakes and beautiful trees.  There are two lakes you can walk around and surrounding trees.
Always enjoy the beauty of this park and the great lakes.  Good place to launch a boat.  Does not look flooded this year like it did last year.
Great place with excellent customer service and care and concern for the customer.  This is a beautiful and well maintained facility.
Excellent place to visit to see the animals and scenery.  There were herds if Bison and many bears and other animals.

This is a great Roadside Attraction on the way between Tucson and Phoenix. The kids loved it and the addition of all the different types of animals including the stingray feeding and particularly kissing the goats was quite fun. Low admission price in my opinion given the amount of food and types of animals you get to feed. The only feeding that we really felt like we needed more food for was the lorikeets. They landed on your head and ate their nectar very quickly so bring some extra cash if you want to buy additional feed while in the lorikeet area. All in all certainly worth a visit and is much more than just an ostrich Farm.

One of the smallest Zoos I have been too but this is one of the features in my mind. Each exhibit meets the needs of display / privacy to give a sense your seeing something you should not. The kids love it and one of the best features is feeding the giraffes. When I was a kid they did not have that but since it is so small the trees near the edge of the enclosure were in reach so you could get real close to them. Now you can have one eat out of your hand for a small fee. I recommend that you buy the feeding ticket at the start so you don't have to worry about it later.  Again this a great zoo and the kids had a great time.

Had a great time. the exhibits were well-thought-out and the museum overall is very large so you can spend a good amount of time without the children getting bored of any one section. The Alice in Wonderland section was a particularly well-designed location. There were Gardens and a mirror maze wall for the kids to enjoy. I highly recommend to visit if you have not been in a while as while I went as a child we have not come back in several years with our kids. Even though it's at a new location it is certainly also a newer Children's Museum to enjoy.

Start early in the day and visit this spot on your scouting trip. This is a hidden gem. It is a small house that acts as a guide for the trails and experiences possible in the Carr area. It is a non profit and provides a good amount of value without huge funding. You can get trail maps here and there are mini lectures on topics relevant to the mountains. They also have a small hike and nature walk on the property but of course you goal should be to make it to Carr peak!

Great hidden gem. Tight paths lead you to the river where we saw tons of frogs and birds. Bought cold drinks and ate snacks at the covered tables after our walk. The kids loved it and we will be back.
UPDATE 9-24-2016: Came back again for Humming Bird Banding but you have to come over an hour before to get a number for catch and release. The just widened the trail to the river and made other trail improvements. Still a great place.

Enjoyed this museum quite a bit. Have been to Bisbee many times but never went in. While it is not a free museum it is worth the price. I learned thinks about the town I would not have know otherwise. Lost of reading so the younger kids might get bored but the second floor is much more interactive with gems, trucks, and other points of interest to kids and adults alike.

Went here as an add on to a trip to Nogales. This is a deceptively large museum. The most interesting element to me was the underground excavation site of the original building. Fun notes for the chalkboards in the school and the population charts overtime. This site is now ran by a non profit and is certainly worth a visit.

Have been here several times and I have always loved the look of delight on my daughter's face. Went at night most recently and also did the slingshot. Got the ticket pack and it comes with some included coupons for food and other items in the area like ice cream or a kids tattoo. Great fun for sure.
likes: Value for money (ticket pack with coupons)

reviews_attraction.text: Great site and worth the hike. It has an easy trail that even families with kids can go. The parking is ridiculously small so go before 9am if you want to have a chance to park or better yet rent an ATV or Jeep from one of the local tour companies and get up even faster.

Went on family day so as a local we got in for free. Great event and different t hands on activities for the kids. We got to make a metal picture frame and artist paper. They also we're giving out copper roses for all the mothers as it was mother's day.

History in the very heart of the city. Not a huge site but a powerful one. Great grounds with indoor museum quality displays of artifacts from the period. Well worth the visit and at a cost of free you have no excuse not to go.

A good representation of stack stone building. What I really love is that this building is over 100 years old and was always designed as a gift shop. Has to be the oldest giftshop I have ever been to.
Took my family visiting from out of town and they loved it. Also got to see the Annex that has UAVs and more modern items in it now. Worth a visit if your family can get a base access pass.
Largest poker room in Arizona that I have been at. Full tables well after midnight on Saturday. I played 3-6 spread for the first time. Table had a good mix of new and old players.
Easy hike for the family with many rest areas and signs to read. Shame this is not better known. Recommend you come for a vist. Site has parking and bathrooms.
Very cool and worth the visit. You can't really access anything if your not a student but it a very fun building to be in and look around.
Been here several times. As a kid, when in college, and now brought my own kid here for her first time. Always a fun visit when in Yuma.
Fun time. The overall museum does not take that long even with how fun / frustrating the puzzles are. Planetarium is where it is at.
Great small park in a housing area. Given the proximity to PDS it mostly has the elimentary crowd. My duaghter loved playing here.
Great family fun. Went here as a child and now bringing my children back for the first time. Loved the heart and brain exhibits

Great central park. My daughter loves the playground.
Lots of great events here as well like art in the park and movie night.
Defiantly a great tourist attraction and worth the visit. My kid loved it and the history of Lucy is very interesting.
Great senic spot. A must hit when you are at Bisbee.  The pit is actually 3 different mines combined over the years.
A thought provoking site but just a sign to see. Nothing here but the plaque. Relaxing drive to the site however
Very cool one of a kind location. Well worth the visit! Has a 17 minute film and about an hour tour.

Free parking.
