Crowders Mountain State Park separates itself from other state parks in a few ways (I've seen them all).

1)It is so sprawled that it has three parking lots/entrances: Linwood, Sparrow Springs, Boulders. These aren't connected within the park so you have to exit to get to each.

2)It isn't as rural in my opinion, particularly the Linwoood entrance, as it is close to Charlotte and I85. You also have excellent cell service throughout.

3)It gets more crowded on the weekends and a hell of a lot quicker. I got to the Linwood gate 15 minutes before open and there were already about 10 cars ahead of me waiting to enter. I did my hike and left around 10:15 and it was completely full. The trails were hopping by that point too.

This review is for the Linwood access section of the park. Has a small bathroom station right before the trails. The trails here are the Backside (strenuous), Rocktop (strenuous), Tower (strenuous). You start where the Backside and Tower split.

Backside Trail: This seems to be the most popular trail because it leads to the overlook and radio towers. It then continues to where the Tower/Rocktop split. This trail is .8 miles of you-better-be-ready-from-the-get-go. In other words, from the parking lot, it is immediately difficult. No buildup. It is extremely strenuous even though it is mostly stairs and a wide, well formed trail. It reaches a cliff overlook complete with dangerous rock formations. Yes, this part is potentially fatal but the views are amazing. The trail continues to the radio towers and then to the Tower/Rocktop split.

Tower Trail: This is a wide trail, wide enough for vehicles, mostly gravel and a gradual ascent/descent depending which direction you are going.

Rocktop Trail: Longer trail at 1.5 miles, strenuous, but doesn't seem as strenuous as Backside. It will meet up at Sparrow Springs Road and switchback to Crowders Trail. Crowders Trail will return you to the Backside Trail and toward the Linwood parking lot.

I have always done Backside-Rocktop-Crowders in that order as this loops you back to the Linwood access lot. It is killer and not for everyone. But the overlook with rock formations are pretty darn neat.

Preface: If you are coming from 40 east of the park going west, the drive through Burke county is  nothing less than spectacular. NC 18 and George Hildebrand Road are rural mountain drives of pure awesomeness. Make sure you have gas and your car is running well. Hallelujah for GPS because holy freaking nothing around for miles. I  can't stress this enough. You will lose cell service when you enter the entrance to the park.

Came on a Monday at about 8:30 am and there may have been ten cars at the Jacob parking. Perfect.

The kiddo and I did the High Shoals Falls loop which is about 2.7 miles. It is labeled as strenuous with blue markers. It is definitely difficult. Most people just take the LEFT trail from the parking lot to the Falls and back. It is one mile each there and back. This side has a lot of stairs and runs parallel to the river. Clearly more scenic and if you are looking for that, stick to this side.

The 2.7 mile loop takes you above the falls and back down. The aforementioned left side is where I would go up (easier to ascend and scenery) and you will come down the right. The right isn't as rocky and I thought this was why it was the easier side coming down. Bathrooms are right near the parking at this part of the loop.

My 7 year old could do this and we took it slow. It took us about 1.5 hours and we stopped for photos etc.  This is a difficult trail but it isn't the worse I've done. It is manageable IMO if you are in decent shape and go slow. It isn't a beginner's hike however.

Fun fact: This crossed off every NC state park for me and have finally seen em all!

Plenty of trails and views of the Neuse.

Spanish Moss Trail: My favorite trail for views. Connects to Sand Path and Longleaf Trail as a loop. This section is the most difficult (it isn't) and has both views of the Neuse at eye level and from a "cliff" type area. There are some makeshift steps at spots and that helps with muddy conditions. Have seen people fishing  on this trail. The campground area is beside this trail so there are cabins, tents, etc. Amphitheater is also here.  Parking of course is adjacent to both the trail and campground area.

Paddle Trail: This is a long paddle trip (7+ miles) and NOT like whitewater rafting. You will work and this isn't for everyone as the Neuse isn't exactly a swift flowing river. I would say you could spend anywhere from 2-5 hours on the river depending. This isn't my thing but people who like kayaking etc would be happy with it. I am acquainted with a family who owns some and let us borrow. You can also rent boats near the visitor center and I imagine most would do this.

The visitor center is near the entrance off of 111. Parking here. There is a lake where people swim and boat. You can rent the boats here, there is a small concession type thing selling drinks and nicknacks, and there are facilities to bathe and relieve yourself. The facilities are well kept.

It works for a quick hike or for someone looking for serenity for a few hours.

11-22-20

Not as crowded as other state parks and not as scenic either. But still awesome.

Have done both the Morrow Mountain and Sugarloaf (Backpack Trail leads to both) starting at the museum and office.

Morrow Mountain trail is probably the better one for scenery as it takes you to the viewing summit. It is labeled as moderate but it is 2.5 miles one way. So if you did a return, do the math. That's a ton of walking. Some bridges and streams but not many.

Sugarloaf Trail is definitely strenuous. Steep. Uneven. Narrow. Slippery at spots. You name it. Tough. Would not recommend after rain. This trail also loops by the main road that leads to the Morrow Mountain parking area. Either side you take on it is killer. Not for everyone.

The Morrow Mountain Parking lot is huge, has the summit, and an awesome shelter in Shelter A.  Picnic area with bathrooms are here.

Park office has some keepsakes for sale, maps, etc.

I think this is a 4-star hike but the 5th star is for how well labeled the trails are. Best I've seen in a state park in NC.

There was some burning smell and trees down from burning. Not smokey but did smell. If this bothers you, then come at a different time.

Love love love this park. I used to hike all the trails when I was a tad younger. Some are tough and you need to be in great shape. Steep, switchbacks, uneven, streams, fallen trees with muddy turf after storms, the works. Have seen some groups do rock climbing.

Most people just come for the viewing at the top of the knob. The entrance has a small ranger station with bathrooms. Limited parking. Access to the difficult (ascending) trails are here. The road to the top winds but is a gradual ascent. Coming down is the fun part!

The top has a ton of parking, another ranger station with bathrooms, viewing areas, picnic areas, and access to some trails (downhill and easy or flat throughout). The views are beautiful and nothing I type here will do it justice.

Coming here as the leaves are changing in fall makes this park stunning. Just the drive on 52 is a great view. Have encountered wildlife here such as deer and one small bear.

Do it.

NC does a fantastic job with their aquariums. This location isn't the largest one in our state (I think Fort Fisher is),  but it does things well and is actually my favorite location. Of course the exhibits are specific to NC.

Price is reasonable and you can spend several hours here. The layout flows, is easy to walk, and the exhibits are well maintained.

Like most aquariums, you have several exhibits, touch tanks, a theater, a gift shop, etc. This location separates itself as a sea turtle rehab center. Sea turtles that have been injured from human interaction are brought here to get them back up to speed to be released. Others are kept here if this isn't possible.

The back has a nature trail that takes you through wetlands typical of NC. There is a boardwalk where you will see crabs among other wildlife in their natural habitat. Wear mosquito repellent!

Plenty of parking and never seems too busy.

This is different than most national parks and this makes it unique. It commemorates the dead of the American Revolution.

The park has a visitors center that shows recovered artifacts from soldiers. This includes weapons, clothing, etc. Parking here on New Garden.

The park itself has a main paved loop. There is a parking lot here for this on Old Battleground Road. There are several monuments on this loop. There are other hiking trails that take you through wooded areas with streams, bridges, etc. Some monuments are hidden off of these trails. People walk and run these frequently.

The Atlantic and Yadkin Greenway intersects the parking lot off Old Battleground Road. It is long and takes you to Bur-Mil Park. There are alway people exercising here and this gets busy on weekends or weekday mornings.

Adjacent to Country Park and you can walk back and forth between them.

A lot like Country Park in offerings. Hester Park is open for cars on the weekend however. There are two entrances, off Vandalia and Groometown. The entrances meet up so you can enter one and exit the other passing through the entire park.

Shaded shelters, plenty of parking, pond with several docks, tennis courts and soccer field, volleyball nets, several bathrooms scattered, tables, gazebo, etc. One small playground.

The knock on Hester is the area isn't the best in Greensboro. True. The fields and tennis courts seem a tad run down and under utilized unlike Country Park which is booming. The rest of the park seems well maintained however.

Hester doesn't seem to have the traffic as other parks in the city so it is never as busy as other parks.

A great NC state park. This is directly off of the Blue Ridge Parkway. The summit is perfect and I like the guide thing to show you what you are looking at in all directions. I always giggle at the "Big Butte." The views are excellent.

This is the highest point east of the Mississippi. Cool.

The drive to the summit is easy. There is a ranger station with bathrooms, picninc areas, and access to several trails. I've only done a few of the trails and they were relatively easy. Plenty of parking. I have come here in summer and winter and neither times seemed busy.

This is probably an overlooked park due to its location but worth the effort

I am Catholic by birth and rearing so cathedrals and chapels are supposed to be something I am interested in. I am not in general but this one separates itself by architecture.

It isn't like the large ones you see in Europe as it seems like once you've seen a couple of those, things run together. This is specific to Sedona with its rock formation and location. It really is pretty cool in shape and style.

I came on a Sunday and a mass was just finishing. So candles etc were lit, decorations were abound on everything including the crucifix. Not sure if this is something done perpetually but I noticed.

Neat.

One of 27 NC State Historic Sites.

What Dr. Brown accomplished for African American youth in the early 1900s is nothing short of ridiculous. I won't detail much about it as that would ruin it for others who may like to view her campus.

I don't know who showed me the Canary Building and visitor center today but she was knowledgeable and liked her job.

One of the halls is still used for receptions and weddings. Well preserved and good upkeep.

Great for field trips, if you have a couple of hours free, and for those interested in history of the segregated US South.

Other worldly and no words can describe this park. Pele is alive and well and has been for years. Walking the park is liking walking on another planet. There are several things you can see. There are fissures, lava tubes, etc. Take in all of this. Get out and walk around. Come at night to see the glowing lava.

Just freaking amazing and a bucket list item everyone should have. Try to take a helicopter ride to see the rest of the park that isn't accessible or safe to walk on.

Essentially part of Greensboro Arboretum but this is where the baseball field, two playgrounds, greenway, and basketball courts are. Has bathrooms and water fountains.

What I don't like is the grass area between the playgrounds. It rains and becomes a swampy mess for days. The back playground is hard to get to when it is like this.

One of the entrances to the Arboretum is here and the walking trails etc are excellent. Greensboro Arboretum is a different review.

This is a great area for beginner level/new to hiking. Can be tough at spots but relatively easy (in ideal temperatures of course).

Piestewa Peak can be tough for some but nothing like Camelback or Superstition Mountains.

Should still bring water, wear shoes with support, and stay on the trails (critters!). Can do some biking here and have seen folks bring their dogs.

Dig it and I sum this up as an easy to moderate hiking area for most hikers.

Love this park.

Easily walked loop around water with lots of ducks. Has some workout stations on the loop, benches, bathrooms/ranger station, and even some botanical type stuff. It is adjacent to several sports fields.

There are benches and picnic tables throughout but not a lot of shade.

For a park directly off of Hayden, it never seems busy aside from the random person doing exercise and this makes this park awesome for me.

I like visiting national parks and monuments so here we are. I don't like the cost to visit this one.

Dwellings in the side of a mountain and a well is further north. All these are in the Camp Verde area. These are cool to look at and peruse. I believe these were created by the original indigenous folks living here (Hohokam?) like in the 1200s. Could have my dates wrong.

Tougher of the two trailheads in my opinion.

Park on Invergordon and walk up Cholla. There will be some awesome houses (see my pics) to walk past. The entrance will be on your left. It is fairly easy until you get to the saddle and then things get more difficult.

Take water, do each climb in bearable temperatures, and for added effect do it at sunrise or sunset.

Has Kathleen Clay Branch in the park. Walking trails, shelters, parking. This is a secluded area and away from hubbub even though you are well within city limits. This isn't my favorite park in the city but if you are in NW Greensboro and are looking to do some walking in a relaxed, scenic setting then give it a shot.

Cruise ships take you into this and just booking a cruise for this is worth it. You get close enough to the glaciers to hear them break off and fall into the sea. It is a thunder that will bring a smile to your face

The walking paths here are great and my favorite aspect of this park.

There are several greenhouses, floral areas, a bridge, and a field with beehives.

Pretty in spring when flowers are in bloom.

Have dived here three times over a 20 year period. It isn't the best dive spot I have been to but it is solid.

The water can be rough and is cold. You will see lots of fish etc.

Too pricey to park ($10). We have lighthouses here in NC so this isn't something that really sticks out to me. Has ocean views and some wildlife.

It's OK.
Has bathrooms and is an "easier" hike than the other trails within Superstition Mountain. Still bring water and wear good shoes.
Near City Center Park. A giant playground with different game tables, an amphitheater, and food options. A lot of seating.
Awesome drive and one of my favorite things to do in Phoenix. Great views of the city, some wildlife, and neat scenery.

Crystal Cove park includes beach part, about 6 miles of pristine coastal wilderness,  and dozens of miles of in-land hiking trails.  Local animal life includes coyotes, bob cats, rattlesnakes, quails, hawks. There are two campgrounds in-land, and one next to the ocean. It is quite steep to hike to the up-land.
If you take the most popular 11 mile loop, you will see it all. Visitor center locared next to the beach  has a few original bungalows preserved as a part of museum.

Pristine nature, a valley surrounded by rolling hills. In order to get to visitor center and to see signature flat plain fields filled with flowers you need to drive a 7-mile dirt road segment. My Prius could not handle it, and I had to turn back after a mile 3. Hiking the rolling hills, off the paved road,  still gives you  a wonderful experience. Flowers bloom for a very short period March through April. Endless hiking trails , don't hesitate to venture :-)

You will find yourself somewhere in Europe...  Numerous masterpieces of European artists in the gallery, science museum, fine intricate architecture of the manor building turned into a public Library, and... endless gardens which include species from all over the world, divided into sections depicting Japan, China, South Americas. You want to come back here again and again! Located near Pasadena with Old Town area worth visiting too.. Free parking.

Amazingly renovated Nixon Library, with interactive displays, numerous screens projecting documentaries, comprehensive  timeline of Watergate, touching display of Love Letters between Pat and Richard throughout their 53-years of marriage... I saw visitors watching the historical videos with tears in their eyes...There are exact  replicas of White House Oval Cabinet and Ballroom.

Very remote but very attractive 4.5 miles hiking trail and waterfall. We went during 2019 superbloom: lots of pink and blue lupins, poppies, wild peonies, blooming yuccas too. There was a lot of water in the falls. You have to drive at least 5 miles on unpaved road in order to reach the trailhead. Adventure pass is required to park.

Peaceful little park with picturesque overlook at Crescent Bay. Sometimes you can see and hear sea lions  who love to stay on the rock near by. Lots of hummingbirds  in January-February when coastal aloe in bloom. There is no dedicated parking, you have to find a spot on the street in residential area.

Beautiful green forest just about 20 minute-drive from San Juan Capistrano, off 5 freeway. There are a dozen of pretty established hiking trails and many campgrounds which start around famous Candy Store. You need to have an Adventure Pass in order to park at the trailhead.

This corner of my city will give your imagination some food: you could see how California looked like before humans urbanization...Headlands have a hiking trail on top of peninsula, filled with wild sunflowers, and a seashore trail leading to a sea cave on the bottom.

This is an open terrace with a large panoramic views of the southern Orange County with Saddleback mountain and Aliso Wilderness Park below. The park has a number of benches for sitting and enjoying the view. This park is good for sunrises especially.

Beautiful park with endless view of Pacific  ocean shore. Visitors flock to see the Lighthouse which is within a half mile steep walk from a parking lot. Parking is free but very limited.Strenious walk down Lighthouse, have good shoes when you go!

Christian Orthodox  Architecture Opulence at it's grandest.  This church is worth carrying the same name as Constantinople's original  Hagia Sophia. Very impressive, friendly stuff, plenty of parking available.
likes: Facilities & Services: Friendly Staff, Ample Parking

reviews_attraction.text: Each island has unique plants and animals which could not be found anywhere else. An adventure to visit by taking a boat ride from Oxnard or Ventura by Island Packers. You can rent kayaks on Santa Cruz Island.

Beautiful views of the coast: Laguna Niguel and Laguna Beach, the trail is pretty short: a half mile, but it is enough for walking a dog, so you meet local dog walkers here all the time :-) Dirt road trail .
Orange Circle is a charming location in the heart of Orange County with a vintage vibe, surrounded by a dozen of antique stores, old-fashioned restaurants. This location was cast in several movies.
One of the most lively beaches in Orange County. Children's playground,  several basketball fields, lots of benches, Starbucks and Gelato Paradise next to it. Beautiful, beautiful sunsets.

Sophisticated Modern Architecture outside and minimalistic simplicity inside.
The acoustics are great, but the sound of wooden chairs on a wooden floor is not pleasant during concert.
Beautiful cliffy coastline, like a tiny replica of Algarve. A lot of caves could be explored along the coast, including an open ceiling cave, but only during negative tide.
Romantique beach park with lots of comfy benches to watch the sunset. There is not much shade, so it gets hot at summer time. Parking along the PCH is limited to 3 hours.
The first fall on the short trail with 4 watwrfalls, within 5 minute walk from parking lot. There is a restroom next to parking lot and a few picnic tables near by
Polished manicured park with oceanviews. Only one short narrow walking path between rails and parking lot.Many visitors never coming out if their cars.
Spacious Green Park at the entrance to Aliso Woods Wilderness . THere are two children's playgrounds on the grounds, but surprisingly no restrooms :-(
While here - enjoy fishing, looking at waves, surfers and passing by trains, two great seafood restaurants, and a hiking trail for your pleasure :-)
A wilderness area full of oak and sycamore trees  very popular with mountain bikers and hikers. Paid $3.00 parking area available at entrance.
Always a delight to visit at springtime. This farm is over a hundred years old. Located right next to a 5 freeway , and Carlsbad outlets.
Very special and beautiful arch formation at the floor of Monument Valley. A 4WD required to get to this point.

Overall a nice trail to hike.
The parking lot does get full pretty quick so if you want to snag a spot, I'd say go there early morning. Also, the trails can get very busy too. A bit too busy for my liking if I had to be honest- especially if you go during the peak hour time of late morning on a weekend when everyone is awake and ready to workout. Some people go a bit fast too and some are a bit slow,  causing occasional "clogs" on the trail.
Crowds aside, the views are very nice. Within 5 minutes of starting on the trail, you immediately start getting a nice bird's eye view of the Scottsdale area. The trail is one way in and the same way back, so you don't have to worry about getting lost either. It's like a camel hump pattern- you go up, then down, then up , then down again and then if you choose- you can continue the sandy path that will lead you to a metal gate that you can cross and then walk for about 2-3 minutes and then you hit the street.

A word of caution: there is a sign at the very last downhill that says strenuous past this point. Take heed, because although downhill might not be too bad, once you turn around and climb up, that's where you will feel that exertion. :D

I really enjoyed this museum. Keep in mind you can get a free pass if you visit your public library.

Anyhow, the museum has 2 parts- the paid part is their indoor exhibit, and then they have some historical artifacts on the outside. The indoor exhibit took me a little over an hour to see. It was small, but if you take your time reading each sign, it can take a bit longer. I saw exhibits on animals in the deserts, Indian artifacts, geology of the area, and then also displays on the history of the area as well as stories of people that tried to look for the lost treasures. It was interesting to read, albeit it was a bit text heavy and sometimes the font was a bit small and tiring on the eyes. The older man walking around the exhibits was very kind and knowledgeable and really strived to add that personal touch!- kudos to him.

The outdoors part was very fun as well. It took about an hour and half to walk around and carefully look at each exhibit. There was a chapel dedicated to Elvis, old mining and stamp mill displays, historic houses, and even a mini railroad. So much to see! It was still a bit hot though, so make sure to bring you water.

Amazing museum. I got a free pass for 2 from the Tempe Public Library and I didn't think this museum would be that interesting. Boy was I wrong. There was a lot to see and I was there for a little just under 2 hours and unfortunately it was nearing 5 pm so I had to head out. I rushed through one of the sections to make it through everything. I would say if you are like me and like reading all exhibit signs and doing a meticulous walkthrough, then give yourself 3 hours to see this place.
One thing to keep in mind. The museum has 2 buildings: the first one is a smaller one called the Cultural center. You can buy your tickets there and they have some Native American artifacts and modern day art there. Then if you go out and turn right, you reach the main museum. The first floor has an art gallery (that changes every so often), a room with old Western artifacts, and then another room with historic Western paintings. Then, downstairs, you have historical displays of a store, bedroom, kitchen, etc. You really feel immersed in the experience.
Lastly, I must say the ladies working there are amazing. They were friendly and helpful.

There's plenty of parking spots for this park. The park consists of a concrete loop that loops around a large grassy area, and this loop is connected by a sidewalk that leads up to the parking lot and the dog park.
Walking from there, you see the ramadas. For some reason though, they were locked. After that, you see the playground. The playground was reasonably large but it did not have as much of the updated equipment that you see in other playgrounds. From there, you stroll past a sand volleyball court.
On the far end of the loop, there is a sandy area with world flags flying in front of a bridge. Under that bridge, I spotted a lot of homeless folks. As you continue the loop, you pass by the fenced off Japanese Garden on your left. It took about 15 minutes to complete the circular loop.
The only other thing that kind of a downside is some of the owners were letting their large dogs run around without a leash. They were well-mannered but it was a bit scary.

Love the aesthetics! The outside of the museum is glass walls and then indoors, there is a wooden flooring. Very nice.

The lady at the front was friendly and welcoming to those who came.
It took me a little over an hour to see everything! There were 5 rooms- National Geographic animal photographs, pinata exhibit, flora and animals exhibit, and then there were 2 more rooms each dedicated to one artist. One of them was all about birds (and the artist used wire and fabric to make those 3D models); the final room had 2 blocks on the wall -each carved with random objects in nature by an artist.
It appears most if not all the exhibits are on sales. The prices range from the thousands to upwards of $40,000. Wowzers!

Overall, the museum was small but I can't complain - it's free and well-kept, and the exhibits show truly talented artists.

This park is smaller compared to Wet N' Wild (Hurricane Harbor) in Phoenix. There's not many slides and a lot of the slides are similar. I climbed up one of their stair structures from which there were about 4 different slides. 3 of them were essentially the same, just different colors and the 4th one was one of the super steep ones that goes straight down (I didn't go on that one).

The wave pool was ok, and I think the waves come about every 15 (?) minutes, but I noticed some brown specks floating about when I came back at dusk to cool off. That was not a welcome sight....

Specks aside, the water park was a satisfactory experience and nice way to cool off on a summer day.

This place is a a bit far out, however it's a nice oasis-like spot. Once you get there, you don't feel like you're in the desert. There's a lot greenery and trees, and you feel as though you're walking through a forest.
I personally would reccomend going on their guided tour- check per the Maricopa Regional County Park website. I did the Bird Watch hike (although I'm no birdwatcher, I went for the hike and exercise). The ranger who led it was great and knowledgeable of the area and the birds.
I just wished I didn't look down. The sandy trail leading to the water area was full of huge ants crawling everywhere. Yucky!
Other than that, it was a nice cozy easy one hour hike.

The park has a lot of play areas which is a plus, Walking through it, I spotted 2 playgrounds- one colored one and another one with light brown hued slides. They also have a water splash area.
Clean level sidewalk going along both sides of the park, and the sidewalk on the right is the start of the Indian Greenbelt trail.
My only 2 gripes was the lake water looked a bit murky and if  you go early in the morning on the weekday- it might be busier than expected. There was the workman's truck constantly driving about and I had to stand aside a few times to let his truck pass. Def know he was doing his job but not the peaceful sunrise walk I was expecting. ;)

I am very happy with this park. One thing that really stands out to me is their playground area. They have not just one but 3 playground areas! All of the playground look very new and well-maintained. Two of them have slides/climbing equipment and the one in the middle has actual musical instruments you can tap with their provided drumsticks to play; instruments were variations of the xylophone.
Walking around the lake took about an hour as I was taking my time to look at everything, but I think normal speed- it would take about 30 minutes to complete the lap, if not faster... The map quoted it to be a little over a mile.
Very relaxing start to my day.

It's an okay park. I have no complaints, but it's a bit small. The park consists of a small sidewalk loop (which takes about 10 minutes give or take to walk), a colorful playground (which I would say is the highlight), and a flag memorial area at the very forefront.
I spotted one or two picnic tables which were unfortunately not shaded, and they also have a pavilion up front with more tables- however, said pavilion did still have some construction tape around part of it... so I'm led to think it's not ready for use.
The park is very clean though. Lawn is well maintained and sidewalk is smooth and neat.
Good for a one-time visit! :)

This is still an urban hike, but it is a a thousand steps up from the Camelback and Squaw Peak that are smack dab in the middle of Phoenix. At least this preserve is a bit farther away from the city hub. This means that while on certain portions of the trail you might see some housing, for the most part, you can't really see any urban views and it's mostly just mountains.
My favorite trail here is the one that starts at the Desert Vista trailhead. Trail views for the most part are a bit drab, but the hot air balloons rising around early morning are beautiful and you can get a good view of that from this trail.

This park is beautiful. I however, made the mistake of arriving at 11 am in July last year, so it felt quite toasty for a long hike. However, I was able to see the highlights of the park. From the parking lot, walking straight ahead for about 5 minutes (?) you get on a metal bridge. Luckily the ranger told me to look down, or else I would have missed that scenery. Right beneath my feet was the Tonto Bridge arch. I was blown away.
After seeing that, I walked to another side of the parking garage which led to another mini trail. You walked down steps which takes you to a tiny waterfall. Nice and cooling!

This is an ok park overall. I do sometimes early morning it can get a bit busy in the parking lot. One time, I tried to drive over and saw a group of people in the lot (maybe an exercise group)... In those cases, you can always park in the G.R. Herberger Park lot for overflow, and then it takes about 10 minutes or less to walk over to this park.
Playground was small but packed with fun things to play on! :)
Only other downside is in the mornings, they have the sprinklers going so the sidewalk and grass are wet, and then if you try to walk on the sidewalk, you might get sprayed by the sprinklers.

The Beach park is a grassy area that is next to the Tempe Town Lake. They have a few tiny hills, and there's a Veterans statue by the front gate. They also have about 5 or 6 picnic tables scattered throughout. It's okay, but once you are near the lake, there's not many shaded areas... In addition to that, it lacks a playground and oftentimes you will find homeless folks here.
My biggest gripe about this park are its restrooms. Metal toilets and they just don't look clean at all.
I'll give it an extra star though because it does provide an easy pathway down to the Lake and the Boat Rental area.

This trail is about a one mile loop across the base of a relatively small rocky hill. You can increase the length by taking the uphill path to the top of the rocky hill. It was a bit short for my liking- especially if you have to drive out here- you don't want to just walk a mile and then just head back out and drive home.

I imagine, it could be a nice sunset or sunrise hike. You could hike to the top of the hill pretty quickly and get a nice birds eye view. Also, the loop around the base of the hill is pretty flat with little to no jutting rocks so you could even use it to jog laps. :)

This lake is simply gorgeous! The waters are calm too, as they don't allow water boats on here that create wake.
It's a nice area for kayaking too, as there are just so many coves to explore.
Speaking of kayaking, the rates are very affordable and they only charge you once you get back to shore- based on how many hours you actually kayaked vs you having to guesstimate upfront how many hours you will be out on the water. The two people that manned the kayaking rentals were definitely very friendly and helpful. I hope to be back soon. :)

One of my favorite trails in the McDowell area! It's great for beginners- just some gentle ups and downs, and you really get your cardio in. I would recommend doing this trail counterclockwise . This way, it's more of steep uphill and then coming downhill is smooth sailing. Also, this way the views are better- once you reach the highest point - which is labeled as the Saddle, you turn the corner and are greeted with a nice scenic overview of the park.
Great trail. Will be back soon.

You can easily access this mill from the Mission Palms North Lot - Public Parking. Park and walk to the place with the metal gate and rocky path. From there, you can either take the sidewalk there OR you can continue up the rocky path and then merge onto A Mountain's trail which will take you to the mill.
It's a nice historical landmark, however unfortunately no one is allowed in. I wish they gave tours of the place at least so we could explore the inside. :)

I love this area! It's a perfect refreshing spot to go to especially in the summertime when it's 100 degrees plus in the Maricopa County area. Up there, last July when I went, it was a cool 67 degrees. I got there before sunrise and I actually felt chilly!
The park is very neat...but just keep in mind due to the higher elevation, you might feel a bit lightheaded..
I also like their store- lots of nice snacks to give you some energy before or after a hike.

Very beautiful hike. It takes me about 2-3 hours to complete. I would rate it an intermediate beginner hike due to the distance and because of some bit of uphill there. Nothing too scary though or technical- just gentle ups and downs.
If you go early enough- closer to 7-8 am, you can see the hot air balloons taking off into the skies. (I think they only do this though when it's cooler weather and don't think they do it during the summer. (?))

It's ok.
Pros
-There were some trees scattered about to provide some shade.
-Spotted some picnic tables scattered about the grassy area and they were spaced out for privacy.
-There is off-street parking at the lot by the school.

Cons
-It's super small.
-The playground is bare bones with no shade and only 2 outdated slides.
-There are no sidewalks to connect the picnic tables. The only sidewalk leads to the playground.

This is probably the only bridge there is that allows you to cross from one side of the lake to another. My only suggestion is they should make another one of these at the other end of the lake so people can do a loop-trail around the lake.
Other than that, this bridge is beautiful. It offers a nice view of the lake. It stays well-lit at night, and around Christmastime, it's decorated with colorful lighting.

The park has a few nice trains that you can observe from afar, or you can choose to pay a fee to go inside the tiny museum and into about 3(?) trains. It seemed a bit small for my liking so I stayed outside.
The restroom facilities are clean, and the playground is very expansive. There are lots of variations of monkey bar galore and slides. Looked super fun, however it was a bit crowed.

I passed through this park while walking on the Indian Bend Green Belt trail. It felt a bit small for my liking. It took me no more than 10 minutes to walk through it at a moderate pace.
The positive was that I did like that Indian sculpture they had standing in the middle of the water. It looked nice and artsy.

Fat Man's Pass was fun. This was part of the group night hike. It was interesting to see the formation of two slabs pressed together and you had to squeeze in between for about what felt to be 45 seconds. Some people had to even take their backpacks off just to get through. It was a great experience.

Manchester Meadows!  I was told that when this place was constructed it marked the turning point of the city of Rock Hill.  It marked the change that kept the ball rolling to where things are now: booming and hard to find cheap real estate.

Manchester Meadows offers a really cool soccer filed.  Ton's of them actually.  I mean when are you gonna need all those soccer fields? But they have a really cool walking path their that goes around a lake.  It also goes through a tunnel of foliage.  What a beautiful place to walk.  If you take one of the paths it even end up at an Olive Garden.  So you can get bread sticks to reward yourself for being such a good walker.

Go onto your Facebook right now.  Scroll through your friends pictures.  You will see them on top of the peak of this place with a content grin or maybe making a cheering gesture.  This is a rather hard place to hike up.  By hard I mean you have to grab a hold of a railing and climb up a slippery rock face.  It is not for a beginner hiker or someone who is out of shape.  Some times of year you will also run into chuckwallas.  Don't know what one is.  It is a LARGE black lizard.  The only complaint about this place is that it has very limited parking.

COPIED FROM MY REVIEW OF THE ENTIRE ECHO CANYON PARK AREA.

Hands down the best lake front park on Lake Wylie.  This place is such a fun time.

So they have these water ski show.   I am wondering how they figure it out.  The caped crusader will dive into the water while the green witch glides by on water skis.  Then they meet on the shore.  The witch is pulled into the water.  She melts.  Then some other person comes by on a jet ski.  Rescues the witch from her fate of melting into the water.... the saga goes on.....

The petrified Forest Park is one of many parks that I am discovering throughout Arizona in terms of how they are reviewed. I have been all these parks firsthand over the years. It really warms my heart to see that so many people I’ve rated these areas so highly. This national park is very awesome but I will warn you do not ever attempt to take any of the petrified world it is just simply not right to do this and you can get into big trouble as well.

Got big plans to go to the Bahama's?  Got that big trip to California planned out?  Packing up to do a road trip down to Miami?  Go ahead and save some money and just head on oer to Woodlawn Beach State Park.  Just lay down in the sand here and listen to the ocean waves crash and fizz when they hit the shore.... oh wait that doesn't happen it's a lake.  But hey!  It feels like the ocean because of the sand.  So enjoy yourself.

Everyone has fallen in love with this place.  You will see pictures all over your friends social media accounts and be able to recognize this place in the background.  This was basically just a rock formation that got eroded over the years with massive holes in it.  You will feel like you are an ant crawling around an ant hill.  If you climb to the top areas of this rock you will get some great views of the city.

VERY FEW PEOPLE KNOW THIS ABOUT UNION SQUARE PARK!!!!

So I guess I can let you in on a secret about this park.  Many people know bits and pieces of the history but few know the real truth.  Many have come to adore this place with its convenient subway interchanges, lively crowds and iconic speed chess matches.  Few know the truth.  This park is actually not a square, it is a rectangle.

THE TRUTH BEHIND THIS PLACE!!!
Yes we get it.  We all know about it!  The real reason why most people come here is not for the art.  It is not for the stuffy art events that they have from time to time.  It is not for the exhibits.  People come here for one reason and one reason only... THE ROOM WITH THE REALLY COOL LIGHTS!!!!!! WOOOOOOOOOOOOOOO HOOOOOOOOOOOOOO

Wow just wow.  You can take photos here.  You can go fishing on this thing.  It has a food court that reminds me a little of Coney Island.  It is a beautify designed wooden pier that is rather long but overlooks some nice views.   It is also a rather crowded place where you may meet people from all over the world.  Don't miss out on this free entertainment.

Yes parking can be limited but just bear with it until you find a spot.  This hiking trail is one that you do not want to pass up.  You will ascend nearly the entire time you are on the trail.  It starts with a switch back or two then you are climbing up the side of a valley.  By the time you reach the top you have a nice view to reward yourself with.

This wave pool is absolutely amazing and it feels like you were at a beach. This way for it’s so crazy how the police actually works and it leaves you wondering geez this technology is rather old but it feels like something that is so futuristic and new. You are bound to have just an amazing time hanging out at the waves at this wave pool.

This is an absolutely phenomenal zoo!  Yes it is a bit of a drive to get all the way out here but it is a nice drive so long as there is no traffic.   You will also drive by some flower fields assuming they have not been sold and developed by the time you read this.  This zoo is massive!  The biggest highlight to it is the petting zoo.

It is kind of funny to think that you can live in your cookie cutter suburb in a desert that gets so hot you can fry and egg on the sidewalk and then drive up to a lake like this with a motor boat.  This lake is rather large considering that it is in a desert.  You are bound to have a fun time if you go here just to walk around.

Watch out for the talking horses that hang out here.  They roam around in the desert and talk.  They are massive and they will just go up to you and talk your ear off.  You can't out run them, you can't out power them, they will follow you everywhere and talk to you.  They are very irritating.  hope you found this funny.

At the Musical Instrument Museum you will find musical instruments from all four corners of the earth.  This place is absolutely amazing!  The reviews online for this place are in the four point eight star range.  This entire place was recently constructed also.  The people that work here are also as kind as can be.

You gotta check out the Mesa Arts Center.  You can do all sorts of things.  There is a lot going on.  You can watch live performances and there are a lot of events that go on.  The architecture of the place is really cool and you can feel it lighting muse's.  The art on display here is great as well.

I really think that the Little Sugar Creek Greenway could easily top a list for one of the best urban parks in the entire country.  You can get your cardio cone here in style.  As you are walking around you will sometimes forget that you are even in a large city yet look up and see the buildings.

Do you like seeing yellow stone geysers?  How about one in Rock Hill?  There is something magical about this fountain park.  Sitting down next to it when the weather in nice, at night.  Watching the light hit the water.  Hearing the spraying noise.

When I die sprinkle my ashes in this fountain.

The large dragon lies underground asleep unearthed beneath this lake.  His, well you know what, is still outside the ground but under the waters of this lake.  When the enormous dragon has to go make a number one that is where the mighty stream of this fountain comes from.  It is dragon urine.

The Margaret T. Hance Park is absolutely magnificent!  This is the park that covers the I-10.  When you are driving down the I-10 and go through that really cool tunnel with the amber lights this is what is above your head.  This is a very cool park to check out and walk around at.

I am going to make the assumption that a lot of people who first see the Cancer Survivors Park see it when they are driving down the road to get to the library.  This amazing park uses the space very well and is decorated with wonderful sculptures and zeroscape.

Stressed?  Want to get away from it all.  This is your getaway.  There is a ton of stuff to do here but it can be a great way to just walk around and be at peace.  This is a wonderful park.  Charlotte does not mess around when it comes to making amazing parks.

It is a bridge.  Bridges are cool. Have you ever seen a bridge like this before?  Well you haven't. Because this bridge is one of a kind.  Technically all bridges are different.   It is impossible to make two bridged that are identical at the atomic level.

So I was here and I saw this big rock and I was sure that it was the Turtle Rock... then it started to move... false alarm it was a turtle.... daaaaduuunchiiinggggg... I did one time see a massive tortoise around this area that was crossing the road.

So this is a really cool park.  You can play frisbee golf here if I am not mistaken.  This is a large and long green space that covers quite an impressive amount of earth.  You can definitely get your cardio in if you go for a jog here.

Well it's still about the same as last time I went it's a little more warmer down in the caves it's pretty wet damp with all of this rain the beginning is always the toughest it's pretty Rocky and steep but as you get more towards the back I'd say after you enter the cave go back about 800 feet it's kinds of those flattens out and gets a little bit smoother it's still rocky and tough to rain but it's smoother than the entryway it gets warmer as you go back also I wouldn't really recommend it for elderly or pets or a bunch of kids under the age of 6 years old it takes about 45 minutes to walk to the end and about 45 minutes to walk back out take Flashlight batteries for sure and plenty of water
dislikes: Not suitable for elderly, pets, or young children

I think it looks really good considering it was built in 1871 to 1891 operations for the fort but it's made of adobe so it's kind of hard to tear down and reuse or to burn down great place to visit $7 to go through the museum and then across the street there are three buildings open you can walk through I would recommend it

After the great last flood the ground is like new Earth to explore different places to see there are no abnormal growths of vegetation really cool places to go explore I mean as like places to build as it regrows you can build your own little fort within the trees on ground  level in the pile of debris the flood left behind

Outdoors not busy this time of year great place for meditation, pictures, BBQ and covered picnic tables areas , taking pictures.
Relaxing, hiking, swimming areas, $10.00 to get in cash only, exit gate doesn't close, as I was leaving there a wedding reception was about to start , pet friendly

Great place to take photos or go under the bridge and hike down the trail to Oak Creek take some better photos there in the summertime there's also a very good swimming holes underneath it's a bit of a hike but it's worth it nice cool water get your Red Rock pass to park here

Well depending on the time of year you go there's a various amount of whether that can happen approach fast be prepared plan ahead, this time of year in the fall it's good, Aspen trees are in change mode the Shadows are different little bit darker longer more intense

Great place to go for a hike it's a pretty easy hike until you get to the end and it's pretty steep watch out for deer why did encounter one deer on the way back but overall it was very good great time of year to be doing this hike in September

When it's not Smokey it's a really great view you can also purchase some Native American Jewelry at this location, and I believe there's also a Trailhead around there somewhere, I have yet to hike but one of these days

So cool here. It's very different and difficult to imagine the past there but the decomposing and the colors even some petrified wood is a great story teller if you can put your mind there at that time
Never been there I will probably return, there are tress, rocks, birds, and things the air was crisp when I was there  but the ground was burnt and dry, patches of snow here and there
Great place to go, got there at 9:00 am got out at 2:30pm went about 12 miles roundtrip a few icy covered areas of the trail made it tricky to hike. A nice quiet time
It was outside later in the day during the week nobody around about two week for color to arrive on the trees , the water looked nice and fresh
Lots of trash in the bushes, monofiliment along shore but other than that it was just fine its also the center of Arizona or close to it

I thought it was a bigger hiking area it's not very big it's not really a place to go hiking just a lot of stairs and that's about it
Place to park and cross the street go along oak Creek to get some great photos and fish there is also picnic table and BBQs there
Great place to go middle of week hike the color was great the temperature was just fine not too crowded worth going
It's outside and free place to hike and take photos or swim plus there are restrooms .. Not sure about the fishing
It was outside and I found places I've never been been to before what's in the canyon who will ever know
They were out of soda and I read the gas here was bad and  would not be good for any engine's

Excellent information well described including info on women, slaves, econony etc. Don't miss the duel. It explained so many interesting details about culture and values in the early 1800s. Docents have basic knowledge. Be sure to walk the grounds to see where the cotton was grown, slave quarters etc There is a cart for those unable to walk. Don't have to go to the second floor of the mansion. Be sure to visit the dining room and kitchens accessible from outside and push the button to start the electronic explanation. This is such a great place. We had guests from age 12-75 and didn't more than 3hrs. Everyone loved it.

Great shows. Check the schedule on line and organize your visit accordingly. Different shows for different ages on the hour. Saw a kid show and all the kids about age 7-10 loved it. Also saw an excellent asteroid show for adults for only $3 more per person. Great glow in dark t-shirts for kids in gift shop. Mineral display in basement. Check out science section for elementary age kids. This is a small place but worth a visit. Park in Cherry Street lot about a block walk on other side of University Street. Free parking on weekends when there is no ball game.

Small home and museum with small grounds. This is the only home preserved where Polk lived other than the White House itself. Pleasant tour. Nice local staff. Nothing at all like The Hermitage home of Andrew Jackson in Nashville. James Polk was the 11th president and deserves more than this modest effort considering he added Oregon, Washington, part of Idaho, California, Arizona, New Mexico, Texas, Nevada to the United States. Underrated and rarely discussed very important President. This house and museum definitely worth visiting.

Don't miss the cafe after visiting the fine exhibits. Hidden in the back of the building overlooking a pleasant courtyard with outdoor tables as well as indoor space, the food is excellent and fairly priced. The half chicken salad sandwich on croissant roll is delicious. Homemade chips or a yummy salad come with. The fruit tea is a local treat and the desserts are amazing. The exhibits change regularly. The building itself is delightful art deco and the museum shop provides special gifts some made by local artisans.

Check out the little museum inside the Parthenon. Great photo exhibit of the history of the building. Revolving art exhibit always with a quick look. But the upstairs Athena is amazing. Walk all around it, all four sides of you will miss important views. Step behind the wall to replicas of the Elgin marbles. If you have young children all of they have free admission for the family if the child does the kiddies program which starts around 11am. Very fun and worth it if you have several adults.

Wonderful tram ride with knowledgeable Park Ranger Eric every  1.5 hrs beginning 10am. Visitor center has uptodate short film and nice modern exhibits of artifacts. Good timelines and historic context. The site is well maintained, easy to drive around or walk. Great place for families with picnic area and lots of space to run. Adults $4 62+ free and free 12 or under. Close to I-20. We spent 3+ hours and saw everything. Could do in 1+ hour if in hurry

Small house mansion from the civil war era. Good decent give lots history and local color. There are some interesting paintings and decorative arts. Allow maybe 45 minutes not because it's so large but because the docents are chatty and enjoy sharing information and answering questions. Don't miss the gift shop. It has some hard to find books on local history and unique gift items. They also give talks so ask for the schedule for their free talks

Wonderful tours! We signed up for a ranger led tour of Guevabi and Calabasas. Was a five hour tour including the van rides between sites
Ranger Rick was a fantastic guide with interesting historic and cultural commentary. They also have special tours to the church and fresh tortillas Thurs-Sun from January thru first of April and the weekend in October - November. Small museum can do in 5 minutes and small shop with good books.

Incredible experience. Buy tickets online and go to will call. Saves time. Definitely buy movie narrated by Tom Hanks and see first if you can. We did submarine as well. Hidden gem is second floor above submarine with interactive  battle descriptions. Food is great at all restaurants. We saved Bob Hope movie for last. We needed a laugh just like the troops did.

Intimate setting, good acoustics. Seats are church pews and uncomfortable. Bring stadium seats. Columns holding up balcony will block views on main floor under balcony. The gift shop has great merchandise but it's pricey. Often has free music outside on the plaza before performance. Wonderful historic venue.

This museum is a must see. Excellent displays explaining all the Indian Removals not just the Cherokee. Excellent archives. Large bookshop with other souvenirs. There is also an outdoor village with tour. You could easily spend several hours if you are interested in this period of history.

Very friendly helpful staff. Takes 15 minutes to read displays but worth every minute. Just drop in and have the kids understand something of the people who fought for this country. The book on the code talkers is available on audio and would be great to listen during the drive

Great group airboat ride saw iguanas, egrets, tri- colored heron, alligators in the wild. You will get very wet so if you don't want to get wet buy the $1 poncho in the gift shop. Saw alligator feeding which was gruesome. Totally worth the price. The airboat ride is super fun.

It's closed until January 2. Regardless of what the info says on the internet, they are closed between Christmas and New Year's. The informational plaques desperately need replacing. The plexiglass is so cracked you can't read the information on several of the plaques.

Absolutely amazing visitor center. The gun collection has been received ajd the displays are much easier to follow. Great film. Fantastic explanation of the difference between Spencer rifle and earlier single shot rifles. Can easily spend 2 hours here.

They have games on the sidewalk in Tuesday and Thursday nights in the summer! Ping pong, foosball, jenga, pitching bean bags. Really fun. Park and rec employees are around supervising. Movies at night in Thursday. Fountains for kids great place
Wonderful place very organized. Great staff. The library staff is so helpful, really really helpful. Good bookstore. This is just a must stop for native American researchers
Small site crammed with petroglyphs. Easily seen from path. Don't walk among them. The dust and foot traffic is damaging!  Toilet facilities. 3800 ancient glyphs! Amazing
dislikes: Facilities & Services (damaging dust and foot traffic)

reviews_attraction.text: Needs updating but the visitor center is excellent if small. Good film. Rangers have lots of detailed information about this and other sites in Nashville.
Read up on history of this discovery from1960s before you go. Largest mammoth site in North America but without the history it's just another wash
Wonderful display of African American  geneology of slaves on second floor of smokehouse. Ask about Native American research and coming displays
Love this place! Once a month reinactments and tours with living history folks. It's so interesting we've been twice and going again this month.
Easy walking trails, good signs describing battle, great views. Be sure to visit the museum and the fabulous Walker painting of the Battle.
This is the second year we did the 5k/10k walk/race. Well organized, gorgeous views, very fun for kids and adults even seniors.
Live music, artists with local art, mule drawn carriage rides, lots of fabulous food. This is the place to be

The most important single thing you can do before you hike Bright Angel Trial is to pre-hydrate 48 hours before you start your hike. If you are thirsty, you're already dehydrated. Arizona sucks water out of you like a vampire. You're dead before you know it. For me the best views on Bright Angel Trail are along the river and up through Pipe Creek Canyon to Indian Garden. If you're coming from the bottom, Three Mile Resthouse means you are almost to the top. It is a nice spot to spend 10 or 15 minutes catching your breath for the final climb out of The Grand Canyon and to the nearest spot that sells a cold beer. Hiking in The Grand Canyon is a mental and physical challenge for the average hiker. I see people running up! Not me though. I average about 1 mph, when I factor in stopping to take pictures with my Canon SX720, which is, I think the perfect camera for this hike: light-weight, incredible zoom and lots of battery life. Always check the weather and water situation with the rangers before you begin this hike. Lightning storms during the monsoon are incredible events that will scare you to death. Sometimes the water lines break, so check. On a moderately hot day here in Arizona, I average 32 ounces of water for every two miles I hike in this kind of terrain. There is a 4,700 foot elevation change in just 9 miles. I take extra water with me to splash on my face, feet, pour on my cooling towel and have some extra to offer fellow hikers in need. Water is life out here in the desert. Always bring extra just in case you need it or a fellow hiker needs it. I never take my heavy cameras. A 5 pound Canon 5D Mark IV with a 200mm L lens becomes a 25 pound canon ball around your neck on the way back up. In Arizona, rule number 1 is: when you're hiking in a challenging environment like The Grand Canyon, if you're halfway done with your water, you are halfway done with your hike. Period. I've seen people wandering around like zombies. It is frightening how fast you deteriorate without water. Juice up your water with supplements. Always listen to our rangers. They always know the best course of action to take. Never be so committed to your hike that you ignore the weather. I've seen big rocks coming down during a downpour. The water, the rocks and the lightning ain't not joke folks. Bring an extra pair of socks. When you reach the halfway point of your hike, let your feet air out and put on fresh socks for the hike back up. When you walk up, think like a mule. Never step up onto something when you have to step down. Look 10 feet ahead and find the flattest parts of the trail to step in. Step over the log breaks and stone walls, not on them. They are often the highest points on the trail. Don't be in a hurry. Be sure and stop to take this stunning scenery in. Cheers! Be safe and leave it better than when you found it.

Hiking inside The Grand Canyon is an epic experience. Bright Angel Trail is the gateway into one of the 7 natural wonders of our world. The Park Service is right when they say this hike can be a revelation or an ordeal.  I find it to be somewhere in-between. It is a physical and mental challenge that you have to prepare for. As I write this review, I am a 55 year old man who lives in Arizona. I walk my dog twice a day everyday for up to and over 10 miles a day. I last did the hike on March 12 and 13th of 2018. I made it down the SA in 7 hours and up the BA in just over 10 hours. The way I do this hike is snag bed at Phantom Ranch. They serve a great steak dinner, cook up a big breakfast and give you a sack lunch for the walk back up. If you can swing it, stay two nights. You can hang out on the beach and watch the rafts go by or take any number of day hikes. The River Trail between SA and BA is really nice. If you camp, let the mules haul your equipment in and out. It is the best 150 bucks you will ever spend. Campers can reserve breakfast, lunch and dinner at Phantom. You can spend less time cooking and more hiking. BA is a series of switchbacks. To hike it you have to think like a mule. Never step up onto something when you have to step down. The log and rock supports on the trail are the highest points. Step over them, not on them. Look 10 feet ahead and step in the most level spots, which are often exactly where the mules step. I live in Arizona. On a moderately hot day (105 degrees), I will consume about 32 ounces of water for every two miles I hike. The number one hiking rule in Arizona is when you are halfway done with your water, you are halfway done with your hike. Wear a hat and sunscreen. Walking sticks really help on the BA going up and down. I always bring an extra pair of socks. Remember, lite is right. I bring a small Canon 720, not my 5D Mark IV. That 5 pound 5D morphs into a 25 pound cannonball  that is wrapped around your neck on the way back up. Leave No Trace!

If you pass the Painted Rock Petroglyph Site up without stopping to see this little jewel, then you have some serious personal issues! Most petroglyph sites are hard to reach and might have a dozen or so markings. Painted Rock has hundreds! "The Painted Rock Petroglyph Site is a collection of hundreds of ancient petroglyphs near the town of Theba, Arizona, listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1977." The site is operated and maintained by the Bureau of Land Management (BLM), and includes an improved campground as well as an informative walking trail showcasing the petroglyphs. Pack a lunch. Great place to have a picnic and contemplate time. There are bathrooms, and they are clean. Everything is well kept. If you're a photographer, the best time to go is mid day or, if you're good at working shadows, then early morning. Many of the petroglyphs face the Sunrise. When the Sun is setting your camera is pointed straight at it. The best conditions would be mid day with plenty of puffy white clouds. The light at Sunrise and Sunset is a surreal blue. Maybe that is why the Native Americans chose this place. Keep it nice and report those who don't! Over forty petroglyph sites have been recorded in the area, however; most of these sites are small with only a few dozen petroglyphs. The Painted Rock Site is the largest known site with about 800 images. The petroglyphs are pecked onto weathered basalt boulders overlaying a granite outcrop. The outcrop is in the form of an east to west orientated oval about 400' long, and about 20' tall with two small knob tops. Most of the petroglyphs are concentrated on the boulders along the eastern edge, but the petroglyphs face in all directions from that edge.

Bring plenty of water. There are shelters; but, nothing can protect you from the summer heat. I went early in the morning and late in the evening during mid August. I was hoping for some monsoon clouds. There were none. Maybe next time!

My favorite time to visit Delicate Arch is the new moon in September. The Milky Way becomes visible early. The galactic center emerges around 10:00 PM. Venus, Jupiter, Saturn, and Mars are the brightest objects in the sky. You can sense the movement of the earth through space as you watch those planets dash across the night sky. The brightest of them all, Venus, goes down below the horizon first, and it starts to get really dark. The Milky Way soon reveals itself in the southern skies right beside Delicate Arch. The hike up isn't easy; but, it isn't hard either. I believe there is a 500 foot elevation change. My Garmin tells me I walked 1.65 miles from the parking lot to the arch. Go to the bathroom before you leave. Bring a headlight, and make sure you have extra batteries. The most challenging part of the hike back is the canyon you walk through just before you see the arch. The path narrows, and there is a considerable drop should you slip. The second most challenging part is hiking up and down the slick rock hill that leads to the arch. You get all your elevation change in just over 1/4 of a mile. There is a well worn path up the hill that you can see during the day and at night, just try not to veer off of it. Some sections have stairs chiseled into the rock to make it a bit easier. Bring plenty of water, especially in the summer. You get the heat from the Sun above and the rock from below. I use walking sticks here. Makes it easier going down. Always check the weather and do what the rangers say do. Getting caught in a monsoon storm during the summer is not a pleasant experience. Keep it nice. Cheers!

You can access Vermilion Cliffs National Monument by 89 or 89A and turning on House Rock Valley Road. I prefer 89A. 89A is flatter and the condition of the road is always better. This section of HRVR follows Coyote Wash and sometimes veers into it. If you get caught in a monsoon, stop and wait it out. The road dries quickly. If you are going to Wire Pass to hike North Coyote Buttes or Buckskin Gulch or camp at Stateline, the trip from 89A is 22 miles. If you come in from 89, it is only 8.5 miles; but, HRVR is much steeper here, the rocks are bigger and the washes are deeper. Don't forget to stop at the Condor viewing area if you are coming in from 89A. You might get lucky and see a Condor. It is a truly magnificent sight. Always call the BLM office in Kanab before using House Rock Valley Road, so you can get road and weather conditions.

My favorite section of the South Kaibab Trail is between The Tipoff and the Kaibab Suspension Bridge. Working the cancellations, I usually get a couple of nights in a dorm at Phantom Ranch twice a year. I always spend my free day strolling along the River Trail between the South Kaibab Suspension Bridge and Silver Bridge. Hike west along the River Trail. The River Trail turns into Bright Angel. Hike west a little farther, until you can see the Kaibab Bridge and Silver Bridge. Great spot to catch the Sunrise. I spend most of my day right there soaking up the sound of the Colorado River, watching the rafts go by, talking to fellow hikers, eating lunch and enjoying life. Leave No Trace!

Hiking down to Ooh Aah Point gets you off the rim and into the canyon. I've read only 5% of the people who visit the Grand Canyon get off the rim and into the canyon. I don't know why that is. Fear, I guess. As long as you stick to the trail, there isn't much to worry about. In my opinion, Ooh Aah Point offers the easiest and best view and feel of what it is like inside the canyon. Watch the selfies though. Several people have died falling from that very spot, usually by tripping over themselves to take a selfie. Some have been blown off by a sudden gust of wind. As long as you stay away from the edge, you're fine. Keep it nice. Cheers!

I do my best to get down to Chiricahua National Monument two or three times a  year timed generally with birding opportunities and night sky conditions. I love Bonita Campground. They keep it up so well. The Visitor Center is first-rate. The people that staff this little treasure are so helpful and so nice. Always check in at the Visitor's Center to see what is going on. There is a great gift shop. The landscape here is surreal. The wildlife you see flying and running around the park is extraordinary. You are smack in Arizona's wine country, and it is good and getting better by the year.

I go in and out of Yellowstone through Jackson, Wyoming, so I can catch a sunrise at Oxbow Bend, a sunset at Snake River Overlook, the view of the Tetons at Antelope Flats and a hike at Schwabacher's Landing, then dinner at Jackson at the Wort Hotel Bar.  I've seen grizzly bears, moose, elk, black bears, beaver, otter and the occasional buffalo here. They've made some real improvements over the years to, especially the bike path, which is fabulous, so keep it nice and let others find what you've discovered. Cheer's!

I always camp at Mammoth Hot Springs. It provides easy access to Lamar Valley and the Tower Fall area, has a nice restaurant and a great campground. Mammoth Hot Springs Hotel has been completely redone; but, as always, hard to get a reservation. Take a stroll around town. Lots to see. One of my favorite places to take a morning walk is the Upper Terrace Loop Drive. One of my favorite features is the Orange Spring Mound. Wonderful spot for wildflowers up there. Enjoy and leave no trace!

Fray Marcos De Niza is the first European to explore West of The Rocky Mountains. We were all raised to believe it was Lewis & Clark. Harshaw Road is a great road to explore. I wouldn't take a car though. Always watch the weather. Lots of gulches along the road. I imagine in hard rains you could get stuck. There are some camping spots scattered up and down the road. I saw some trailers and tents. Lots of Border Patrol; but, they all leave when the Sun goes down!

I had heard there was a sun dial at the V-Bar-V Heritage Site, so I went as close to the September equinox as I could to see if it were true, and it is! I had a wonderful visit. The volunteer staff were extremely knowledgeable. I walked out knowing a lot more than when I walked in. The hike in is only about 1/3 of a mile and is mostly flat. There is a well kept bathroom at the visitor's center. I'll be going back.
likes: Facilities & Services: Knowledgeable staff, well-kept bathroom

reviews_attraction.text: Arizona Fish & Game works miracles. They keep the place spotless. I've seen lots of different birds here; but, it really comes alive when the Sandhill Cranes arrive. I try and go every year. I always have a great time. You can camp there too. It is so nice to hear the cranes talk to each other all night long. The Sunrises and Sunsets are great here, so bring your camera.

This is a wonderful spot. Sometimes you see a Condor. Sometimes you don't; but, the views and the sense of serenity you get by being here makes it a place you have to stop and take it all in. The people that take care of the Condors are all first rate. They do amazing work and need our support, especially in today's world. Keep it nice. Cheers!

I spend 4 or 5 days a year in this area. There is just so much too see. I usually camp at Hovenweep and Mesa Verde, so I drive by Battle Rock and the Sand Canyon Trailhead often and always make it a point to stop for a morning hike or late at night to catch the stars. Bring plenty of water and your camera. Keep it nice!

Super spot to see the end of The Colorado River. I've rafted through The Grand Canyon on The Colorado.  The river is 300 yards wide and raging. Here, I can swim across the mighty Colorado River in 5 strokes. Bike, hike, bird watch. The trail that goes along river is really nice. Bathrooms too. Enjoy.

There are lots of dino tracks here: big ones, little one and medium size ones. My guide was Alvin. Great guy. Knows where every track is. He poured his water into the tracks so I could see them better. Most dino tracks are hard to get to folks. These are and are a must see.

In order to really see Spider Rock, you have to hire a Navajo Guide to drive you back. Once you get past the wash and into Canyon de Chelly, the going gets easier. I always hire a private guide. It is well worth the $150 bucks.

The Upper Falls may be smaller than the Lower Falls; but, the Upper Falls is still one of the largest waterfalls in the Rocky Mountains. Tom Thumb is a wonderful area to get out and stretch your legs too. Keep it nice!

Decision time! You've descended about 3,100 feet and have just over 2 miles to go and another 1,800 or so feet in elevation change. There is an emergency phone and a pit toilet here; but, no water and no shade.

If you get a chance, visit Mesa Verde during Monsoon. Go up to Park Point and watch each sunrise and sunset.  While you do this, the Monsoon storms will swept through,  and you will have a first class seat.
The people are so nice and helpful here. I always make the visitor center my first stop to get conditions on the trails, info on the Buffalos and info on any activities the staff has planned.
Fantastic campground.  Hire a Navajo guide and go visit the canyon floor. For sure walk down and see White House Ruins. Get off you ass, gas up your car and go for a great 3 day weekend.
The Snake River and The Tetons are simply beautiful. I can sit at the Snake River Overlook all day and just watch the mountains interact with the clouds.
I love Butterfly Beach; but the action is at Leadbetter Beach. There is a wonderful little beach front restaurant there too. Lots of special events.

Definately for the anthropologists out there. You will find out about man in general but also about some of the local indigenous tribes in the area. There are, in some days ladies there making fry bread or tortillas. There are mid friendly areas and even the early man exhibits are partially clothed to keep the giggling to a minimum. Across the street but part of the museum is The Miracle of life which is for older kids ans adults, unless they already kniw where babies come from. Very nice museum all the way around to included in Museum Day!!

I recommend everyone see this. If for no other reason than to pay tribute to the men, women and children that were forced to uproot from their homes( most that were owned), vacate their businesses, and move into quansett huts or wooded shacks ALL because they had a familial heritage to Japan. There is alot to me learned about that part of history that that generation of Americans were not very proud of. Young children especially should see this because remember that people who forget history are doomed to repeat it!

I love this zoo!! And being frim San Diego originally, THAT us really flattering! I qas impressed at hiw many curators there were tk ask questions of and how clean alk the enclosures were. I loved how the zoo is laid out and how easy the site map is to follow. The gals that wkrk in the gift shops are very knowledgeable about tbe animals that live there. AND The zoo is free!! So keeo in mind they run on donations, anything you give goes to support these beautiful animals. My favorites are Molly and Pavel tbe tigers!

If you dont want to have to go all tbe way to Cairo to see a mummy, come here!! When they were asked to leavd Egypt, they took their mummies!! Now, they dont have Imhotep, Ramses, or King Tut but heck you cant have everything! They have alot of other stuff from other civilizations but I went basically to see real honest to gosh Egyptian mummies!! I forget what they charge, its not alot though or I would remember. I emcourage you to go if you are the least bit o tetested in Archeology.

This is sort of a landmark for this little town. It has been featured in/on Arizona Highways magazine and the tv show. That fellow who used to do the old highways and byways show on Sunday mornings featured here too. Anyway, the food is typical cafe food( patty melts, club sandwiches, chili, milkshakes, KILLER french fries) but served with small town charm. The servers look like a bygone era, but they really know Arizona, so dont hesitate to quiz them!

You really must not miss these. Very historical. They didnt do a great job at preservation at first( as exhibited by the old graffiti still visable) but they have made strides in tje last few years. There isnt a school child in a 200 miles radius that didnt get taken there or a college anthropology student that wasnt assigned going to see it. It is very educational. No guides but there are signs that fill you in on highlights.

Wouldn't call this a fun place to go but it is certainly diverting and educational. It is very interesting. They have students and faculty from the University there to answer questions. They have a lovely gift shop too. I wouldn't go there in the summer fir two reasons: the trail to see the petroglyphs is VERY hot, no shade at all, and their hours are very abbreviated. Go in the winter or spring.

A little sonething for everyone! Picnic areas, camping, hiking, communing with nature, whatever you want. The one thing I always have enjoyed about it is they have such super rangers; knowledgable, caring, helpful and brave. During a huge fire one year they stayed until they could get as many animals to safety as they could. Two brought 2 baby cougars to safety. This is just a great park!!

Great place to visit if you are interested in California History or Hollywood history. Hearst built it for an actress and spent a pretty penny doing it. It is situated on top of a small mountain and sorta scarey getting to it. There is a visitor center at the bottom where you catch a tour shuttle up to it. It is designated an historical site so it NEVER changes. You will enjoy the tour!

They still film here for movies, documentaries and tv. I would advise nit taking children under 8, as they wont understand what is going on. Further more, when the tiur guides take about John Wayne, Rory Calhoun, or Audie Murphy, you habe be a little older to not say "WHO?" They have fun rides, live animals, street shows and fun places to shop. Tbe candy store qas my favorite!!

A working church but there is a museum with an actual Anthroplogist behind it. It is all very interesting. This wholevarea is more than just the casino.
