A little further west is where Rambo III was filmed. So many  westerns were filmed near there before Winterhaven was incorporated. There id a railroad presence there as well. Try not to go to the church a s tourist on Sundays.

THE BEST aerospace museum on thr west coast!! Considering that San Diego is a truly Aeronautic city the museum is right up to date from Montgomery's glider to stealth technology and beyond! Be ready to learn alot of stuff. They do have an area better suited to the young kids but the rest of the museum would better appreciated by those over 12.

If you are into history in general or the history of Yuma/ Arizona, then this place needs to be on your list of places to see when here! You will lrarn so much. I lived there fir 23 years, saw when I first got there and then about 20 years later with a 6th grade field trip; nothing had changed. They really maintain it well.

California's first Catholic church( mission) built by Father Serra. It is very well preserved and still active. You can get married there! They have lovely tours to tell you all about it, its historical significance and the like. Try not to go on a Sunday unless you are going for services. They also have a lovely gift shop.

Very VERY historical. They have preserved it well. The tour guides are very knowledgeable and they have a nice gift shop. There is a cemetary below it that is interesting too. That whole area is historic in nature. The second place built in Yuma by the Government, the first was the Fort.

This art museum has a little of everything except priceless art. You can see Monet, Manet, and Pollack here. Very well laid out and lots of places to sit and just look at a painting. If you want to see priceless art ie Rembrandt or Titian then you need to go to the Timkin next door.

One of the best places in the area to go for fast food picnic. Sits directly behind the Chicken Pie Shop, so if they are busy there are tons of fast food places around there to get chickem or fish or tacos and then go to this park and eat. Great atmosohere, quiet, abd lots of shade.

Sorry, have never been a fan. Dont enjoy the smell of fish unless Im at a restaurant. I dont like getting wet unless Im bathing. And I think they are overpriced, it is very expensive to spend the day here. I do enjoy the otter show but that is sorta it.

For the amateur geologist among us. You will be able to see the difference between gneiss, granite, dolimite and gold. You learn alot here" no mistaking it will make you look at the mountains, cliffs, valleys and the desert differently.

One of Father Serras originals. This place is not only historical but it is also still a working church. They have mass and confession, weddings and funerals, the whole shebang. They offer tours and there is a gift shop.

Beautidul fountain. May remember it from the beginning of Married With Children. It is situated smack in the middle if a very popular park. You will dind a void cross section of people there if you like to people watch.

If you are into off roading this is a nice place to do it. Not as crowded as some places but it does get crowded in the winter whrn its cool. A little trivia here: They filmed part of Return of the Jedi here.
One of the best picnic/party spotsvin the county!! Has everything to offer: plenty of parking, lots of things to see and do, a super playground for the kiddos, and great places to just sit and relax.
Nice little area honoring Veterans. It is in front of "the train station". Not a comfy place because there is no shade but is nice and clean and quiet.
THE best place to take pictures of the valley below!! Also the safest. A good place to stop and rest your car, that mountain is murder going up!

A mile up the conflux of Salt & Gila rivers on the Salt river side was the site of two massacres involving Akimel O’odham & Pee Posh warriors against  French-Canadian fur trappers. On January 25th of 1827, the 13 trappers had been invited to stay in the village of the normally friendly tribes. While there the trappers had demanded native women to be their bed side companions, which infuriated the welcoming hosts. around midnight the warriors attacked the trappers killing 10 leaving 3 trappers named Robidoux, Pattie & one unnamed trapper fleeing south to the Estrella mtns to escape with their lives. The trappers were able to meet up with another trapping party of 30 trappers led by Ewing Young that had approached up the Gila river. They had found where the French trappers had been slain and buried 8 of the trappers they were able to find. On the morning of January 31st, the trappers retaliated on the tribes village killing 110 in less than 10 minutes with their far superior weapons, none of the trappers had been injured in the attack. the hill here is Baseline hill, its the point where all the city streets of Phoenix are mapped out from. thats where Baseline rd got its name,Its lined up with Baseline hill.

historic, scenic & peaceful, a great place to see where the Spaniards built the fort in defense of the raiding apaches to protect the locals & missionaries . Yet over time over 160 apaches lived just south of the mission and was a first line defense against raiding apaches, their own people. Altho some were known to jump in with rogue bands on the warpath as well. lot of history in this area worth checking out. The Arizona Highways artist & the paintings of Arizona historic events was very impressive!!

SE AZ is AZ’s hidden gem!!  The hiking trails thru the CNM are awesome! Id recommend hiking from Massai point, thru Heart of Rocks and then back down to Bonito Campground. You will have to reserve a spot in advance if you plan on camping out. Which is a must do! Plan it around a full moon, you will love it! It does get a little busy during peak season but nothing like the Grand Canyon. More of a reason why i prefer to explore the wonders of SE AZ

Had to see where General Nelson Miles hung his hat during the Apache wars.  General Crook met his match with the Apaches all over Arizona.  After Geronimo surrendered to Gen. Crook, & went on a drinking binge & fled again with 35 other Apaches.  Crook requested a transfer, wanted out.  that was admirable for a General to do that, but iam sure it hurt like hell for him. To pass the torch when you know you cant catch a ghost.

didnt know what to expect to on the drive from MT back to phx area thru here, boy was i in for a pleasant drive! def a remote area and the grandness of the gorge was def in display! glad i did this drive, basically had the road all to myself thru here. You cant help but be humbled in mother nature’s vast grand open areas, its a treasure we still have yet, we all should take more advantage of that

if you want to get away from it all, this place will not disappoint. Phenomenal archeological history in the area, views and chances of solitude. Can get busy on weekends with side by sides and ATV’s tho.  Id recommend going during the week or after a recent storm. Roads are primitive in most places, but thats the whole point, get off the beaten path.

the drive to get to this place is worth it in itself! to see the cliff dwellings and to see where elisha reavis is buried amongst ancient ruins is something to behold! the trail up to Reavis ranch, the apple orchard and to see sacred circlestone, well do some research and come discover this place! take pictures and leave footprints behind only

3 out of the last 4 times driving thru this area the Museum was always closed. Happen to roll thru on a Sunday after leaving Bonita campground in the Chiricahua’s & we found & it was open, sweet!! $10 bucks per adult and $8 for children. Great little museum, the native runner’s and their stories was phenomenal!!!

the remains of Jeremiah Johnson, aka liver eating johnson, one of the toughest mtn men to wander the west lies here. This place is as authentic western history as it gets!! 👍🏼👍🏼 Def see the Buffalo Bill Center of the West Museum down the road too, a must see in Cody! Gun collection is phenomenal!!

the history of two guns and canyon diablo are def entrenched in Az history. this place has really become popular the past years. without anyone to watch over these historic places i see them disintegrating back to nature very soon tho unfortunately. please take pictures and leave footprints only

The visitors center is closed due to Covid but the park, bathrooms & trails are open.  The main trail down and around the old dwellings are closed too unfortunately. I was able to experience that a few years ago and was fascinated with how the ancients lived in the canyon
likes: Facilities & Services: Open park, bathrooms, trails

reviews_attraction.text: Ancient sacred Geoglyphs made in the past that were meant to be seen from the sky.  I couldnt help but imagine the people making them as i walked amongst them in the very remote terrain.  Def something special about this place and why the people that built them.

hiked to half dome when there was 200% snow runoff roaring over Vernal falls, was by far one of the most intimidating terrifying beautiful experiences ive ever had!! the water sounded like a freight train as we were hiking up.

The hike up to inspiration point isnt that bad but def a must do while in Bryce Canyon. Id highly recommend the hike down below the point and do Navajo loop as well for a very different perspective from up above.

def gets crowded during the summer by Phoenicians trying to escape the heat. parking can be a nightmare as well. its still a nice lil get away if u wana bring the canoe or kayaks and cool off for a bit
great day trip to do from the valley esp coming up the old apache trail. Not too many places where you can actually hike in amongst ancient ruins. i would recommend the 3 mile hike to the upper ruins
another great day trip from the valley of the sun to check out. wear decent hiking shoes to get down to underneath the bridge. also your brakes will get a workout on the drive in so drive accordingly
Wyatt Earp’s sanctuary cottage to avoid all the people seeking him out from his Tombstone days. He mined in the mtns north of the area and spent time in the Parker area along the Colorado river.
older memorial park that could use some upgrades and general maintenance. i thought it wasn’t appropriate for young adults to be hanging out and partying in the historic kit carson cemetery tho
one of the best museums of western art! place is awesome! One of the first great western artists who actually lived the life of a working cowboy before there were fence lines in Montana.
great trailhead to some great trails in sedona! haven’t hiked a bad trail in Sedona yet! The trek up brins mesa trail to soldier pass and down to devil’s kitchen is worth doing!
hiking trails can get packed in Sedona, id recommend coming during the off season or during the week to avoid the crowds. Its Sedona though, its awesome here regardless
this is a great area to do some backcountry exploring in a 4 wheel drive to check out the sonoran desert. The drive to the base of 4 peaks is one to remember!
if your into Hollywood nostalgia, this is a great spot for it. busy place. def some characters walking hollywood blvd, keep your purses and wallets close
A Japanese Oasis in the Sonoran desert.  Gets very busy on the weekends, make time to see it during the week, it’ll be worth it

Note that there are two gardens here.  There is one at the west end which is public and is open 24 hours a day and I would call it a park garden.  The other is at the east end and you walk through a gate to get  to it.  It's hours are limited.  This is the botanic garden and it is truly exceptional.  It was exciting to see the variety of plant themes and I have to admit surprising considering the size of Woodlake.  That is, the botanic garden is on par with larger metropolitan gardens I have been to around the world.

If you are visiting the national parks in the Sierras it is definitely worth your time to visit this hidden gem in the valley.

A nice park among the casinos on the strip.  It is a little hard to find since everything nearby has 'park' in its name.  The sculptures are at the west end and the fountain is at the east end (you can't see one from the other because of the trees).  The fountain draws people to itself to touch the water, a testament to the desert climate of Las Vegas.

There are also planter gardens with an assortment of desert plants and informational signs.

The Bliss Dance sculpture is a tribute to women who have had augmentation.

I had been to a lot of the park by the time I got here and was still impressed by these magnificent trees.  The photos don't really do them justice.

btw - This area is the site of two clashing worlds.  In the 1890's logging was underway to the west and Muir came in from the east.  Fortunately this area was saved from the ax so it can be enjoyed today.

Inside the church and associated shops were closed in Jan. 2021 for COVID so not a lot could be seen.  Also, if you wanted to finally squeeze in a confession that is closed*.  The site itself is just a few miles off the interstate and you drive by farmers markets which are an added attraction.

* - Grotto Hill is also closed.

Well, they don't want this called "City Center" anymore since the Harmon Tower debacle (google it).  The branding is now 'Aria' and you will see that on the local signage.  This project is also one of Vega's leading investment failures.  Aside from that there are shiny buildings to see and some interesting architecture.

Utah doesn't have many botanic gardens so I think this one is the best.  There are numerous identification tags so it is easy to determine the plant names.  In mid-April A LOT of the plants were in bloom.

High marks to the designers for the plant selection in relation to blending colors and textures.

The collection is very nice but probably the most pretentious museum staff I have come across.  Don't dare have lunch on their property or the guards will shoo you off.  Once inside you have to check your back pack quickly or they will be on you about that.

The photos show a variety of brushwork.

A popular attraction and well worth it.  I was there in late October and parking was limited.  It must be a real mess when it is busier.

NPS rangers are in the parking lot to help with the situation.  They also can answer general questions about hike times to the assorted arches.

A very interesting museum  in the 'salon' style (galleries are like rooms in a house in with paintings, furniture, sculpture all in one room).  I especially liked the inclusion of Vance's studio so I could see how a professional artist works.

A good place to get in a kike while in Hollywood.  In addition to views of LA you can also see some house that hang out over 100' of nothing.

Bonus - There is an Honor Bar at the entrance for water, snacks, and what-not (July 2019).

High marks to the Park Service for changing the way this area is managed.  Formerly clogged with autos, a gas station, stores, and lodging, it was a real tourist trap.  It is now managed as a forest and not a disneyland knockoff.

Another gimmick from days gone by where you can drive through a dead tree.  If you are into that kind of thing you won't be disappointed here.

There is a bypass around the tree for those that don't want to drive through it.

Visit to this little known natural area is a must.  Site of one of the most significant archaeological site in North America this is the location of a 10,000 year old indigenous peoples meeting place.

Well staffed visitor center with folks lined up asking about park amenities.  There is a theater which has a good film about the area.

Historically, about 500' north, there is an old gas station.
Volcanic activity have given a little accent to the typical red Utah landscape at the park.  Lava flows (basalt) and tuff have painted the red sandstone with a highlight of black and white.
One of the few surviving structures of native peoples from before the Anglo invasion.  The education placards are well maintained and excellent along with the helpful staff.
I learned something here.  Native peoples settled the mesas before the cliff dwellings.  The Park Service has also done a good job of protecting the sites with structures.
The visitor center itself is quite small and of course closed for COVID.  The map that is handed out is actually the Zion map which includes a small insert for Kolob.
A unique park where the lawn is made of clover.  This is a nice shady spot to get out of the sun and stretch your legs and maybe meet some dogs and their owners
Well run and maintained beautiful spot just on the west side of Palm Beach.  The price for entry is the same as other similar parks in the region.
A surprising oasis in the desert.  I took the 1 mile trail (moderate) and was overwhelmed by all the song birds and the sound of rushing water.
A great place to get information on all the local sites which can be hard to find due to the 'disperse' nature of this type of recreation.

Pluses -
1. Free
2. Dogs are allowed on trails
3. Pretty rocks
4. Academic geology interpretive signs
5. Close to civilization

A nice panoramic view and a restroom.

The staged photo of Powell is worth the stop itself (hiding his missing arm).
This would be a 5 star overlook anywhere else but at Bryce it pales in comparison to the other scenic overlooks.

My favorite state park in Virginia (so far). My husband and I are currently working our way through the state parks in Virginia, and this one is my favorite. The views are beautiful! They have a cool farm at the welcome center with chickens and a large garden. The trails are dynamic and fun. Lots of wildlife. We saw rabbits, cows, and even a snake. The trails are steep so factor that in when choosing a trail.

My husband and I really enjoyed this museum. There were so many exhibits and they varied from room to room. The centeral courtyard was amazing to behold, it was lovely to be able to see it from multiple stores and admire it. The museum also has an interesting history of stolen of Rembrandt paints. They left the frames on the wall as a reminder.

Really cute museum lots of stuff for children to do. They have a nice greenhouse and a few live animals. There is also a lot of water play and even sand so expect some mess. Very interactive. The staff was friendly. I would definitely recommend this as an activity to do with the kids; especially, if the weather is unpleasant.

Really scenic. This is very convenient to get to from anywhere in the DMV area and it's so pretty. There are a lot of people that are out on the trails, so be careful. Also parking can be tricky to find are certain trailheads. Overall it is definitely worth it and I cannot wait to come back and conquer more trails!

Very interesting state park. A lot of the history is dedicated to the Lee family which owned the land for several generations. It was also the site of a blockade during the civil war and you can still see some of the cannons. There is also great access to the Potomac, hiking trails, and bald eagles.

A beautiful part of Central Park. It's a very lovely memorial to John Lennon. It's right across the street from where he used to live. There is  convenient access to the subway. Do note, it is always busy plenty of people coming to pay their respects. Definitely recommended if you are Beatles fan.

Good sized park. Most of it is actually located under the Woodrow Wilson Bridge which serves as a cover. There is an outdoor playground, cover basketball courts, docks for fishing, and a paved multi-use track. There is plenty of parking. Definitely recommended for the whole family.

A scenic part of New Orleans, and a great place to stop if you need a rest from wandering around the French Quarter. Many local artists are in this area so it’s full of music and painting for sale. It is also next to a lot of great restaurants including the famous Café Du Monde.

A memorial to the victims of the Salem Witch Trials. It has actual testimony of their innocence etched into the stone works that really drives the injustice home. Also, since it was close to the anniversary of many of the victims hanging, there were flowers left in remembrance.

Probably my favorite ride. It was fast and it tilted all sorts of ways. You got to fly through Hogwarts and see a lot of your favorite characters. Definitely a must do while in Hogsmeade. Note the line can get long. I recommend investing in a fastpass so you can skip the line.

The price for entry was very reasonable. It was a small museum as it is mainly just the house. It  was interesting and gives insight of the life of Paul Revere and colonial life in general. The gift shop is neat because it shows the silver ovens used in the silver business.

Did you ever want to ride along with Transformers? Well you are in luck, with this ride you can. The line can be a bit long, but it's full of TV screens and the premise of the ride is played on them, it is fairly entertaining. The ride spins a lot, but it was a lot of fun.

The aquarium is very nice, and the range of exhibits was good. The staff handling the ticketing could have been less grumpy. Aside from that, the trip was a pleasant experience and recommended as a good indoor tourism spot especially during winter or rainy weather.

One of the better presidential libraries I have been too. Very emersive and it flows well. Definitely recommended if you're in the area. It's convenient to get to from the T as well. They have a shuttle bus that will run from the T to the library.

If you do nothing else in Tombstone watch the shoot out at the O.K. Corral. That is really why you are there, right? It is lots of fun to watch. They provide a lot of background context. They reenact this a few times each day.

This is one of the more quirky places I have ever visited in my life, but the story is really cool. They took the bridge down piece by piece and rebuilt it here. Such dedication. It's definitely well loved in it's new home.

Beautiful area to walk through. You can see people painting along the sides of the water. Very peaceful and a great place for morning walk. if you're walking through the summer I recommend going early it does get very warm.

Pretty cool. Bigger than the actual statue of liberty; otherwise, it looks identical. Can be seen from and good distance. The raised walk way goes along side it making it a good spot to stope and take a photo.

This is a very popular statue in the Boston Commons. I think I saw every child in the area sitting on the ducks and a few adults, which is a shame. However the ducks are all cutely dressed. Very unique.
A great spot of getting a quick bite on the go or checking out yhe local preforming artist. Local art galleries are just down the street. Good way to take your time and take in the scenery.
I loved the tour of the facility; however, a major of the location has been turned into a Chuck E. Cheese style restaurant. I feel this takes away from the history of the place.
A really nice little park along the water's edge. It has some art and lots of benches to sit. It is also pet friendly. It can be really popular during the summer.
Beautiful park. Lots a variable scenery. The trails are well maintained, but this park offers some challenging trails. The fossil beach is very cool to see.
Great outdoor space. It is a bit a walk from the metro; however, there are so many monuments and memorials around this area.
We showed up for the hiking and we ended up kayaking most of the day. There is a lot to do, but can be busy during holidays

This place gets packed quickly.  The earlier the better. There is a porta bathroom behind the parking lot as of 3-2018. The hike is not that challenging. There were three creek crossings. The water volume was low only 1 day after it rained. The waterfall smelled like sulfur and methane. Almost sewer like. There is an upper falls. The trail up to the upper falls is very steep up an eroded trail. Lots of people were trying to climb it causing more erosion. I probably would hike out there again unless I knew the water volume was extremely high. Then again the three creek crossings would be difficult.

I love this place. It has lost a lot of it's amazing luster over the years. It still stands as a monument to the history of the Chinese community who once lived here 100+ years ago. The alley is famed for it's restaurants as well. The Imperial Dynasty used to host famous actors and politicians. Now it is a quiet little area that doesn't have much going on except a Tea shop, and grocery, but you can still appreciate the ambiance of what was once there.

You have to do this. I have been four times and still have fun. There is an active dig, though it is not always in operations. They also have some dig material from the nearby parking structure that was recently moved to their site. The inside of the museum is fun and there are things to see and do. They could probably use an update from the 70's type decor but it still a lot of fun.

The tar and water pools outside make for great pictures.

This is a great open space area. It is separated from Saratoga Gap Open Space preserve by Summit Road. There are some gravel roads here, and it is much sunnier here than Saratoga Gap. Hiking is better than biking on this side. Though, if you need some beginner trails, you could potentially use some of the roads and trails as beginner mountain bike trails.

I have been to all of the missions over the years. San Jose could be so much more. The original buildings were damaged by earthquake and fire and while it is a nice place to visit, you just don't get the same feeling you get when you visit Carmel, San Juan Bautista or San Juan Capistrano. Still, it's one of the 21 original missions and should be visited.

The most amazing park for geology, geography, history, and scenery on the West Coast. You won't believe it until you see it. Park on highway 1 to save on parking. There are many trails that people of all ages and fitness can enjoy. If you want a work out, try running all of the trails. It won't take more than about an hour or two.
likes: Trails for all ages and fitness

reviews_attraction.text: I have been to most of the missions, and in particular to this mission many times. I love going here. I love taking friends and family to see a piece of California History. Every time I go, I see something different that I didn't see before. I get an idea of what the monks might have lived like, as well as the native populations.

Great views of the San Fernando Valley. You cannot see the LA Basin from here. There is a ridge to the south that blocks it. There is a small cave at the top and sometimes a book that you can sign. Lots of people take food to eat here. Sometimes, they leave the food there, which is not good. Overall, it is worth the hike.

This mission is still a working mission. They have services here weekly. I have seen festivals, weddings, BBQ's, soccer, etc.. The mission is part of the 21 Mission chain that once extended into North California. The mission is falling apart in places. It is very interesting to see see a bit of California history.

It's the lowest point in the Western Hemisphere -282 ft below sea level. It is also one of the hottest places on the planet. What's not to like about that. It is amazing in the winter. Summer can be very difficult to deal with. You literally feel like you are walking into an oven when it is 120 degrees outside.

They have done a great job here with a small space. There are some great activities, amazing aircraft, and a very cool simulator. They also have a very nice store. The history of the Douglas corporation is also preserved here as well as other aerospace, and aeronautical companies.

Fun park with great views. In the winter people sled down the hillside. It is a nice place to take your pets for a walk, but do not take them down to the beach, there is are no pets allowed on the beach. The bathrooms are really great and a nice touch (very comfortable).
dislikes: No pets allowed on the beach

reviews_attraction.text: A great place to ride mountain bikes or hike. Take a map with you, you can get turned around in the basin, and sometimes not be able to find your way out. It can be chilly as the sun hardly reaches the forest floor. Mountain biking - These are not beginner trails.

It's definitely a magical place. The homeless and the panhandlers tend to make it a bit uncomfortable but in general, Union Square can be an amazing place to see people, the business of the city, tourists, trolley cars, and much more.

Definitely worth the drive and the walk. There is a lot of history here, and the Tufa area tells a great story. If you want great pictures, come in the very early morning for sunrise or in the evening for sun sunset.

A great place for views, pictures, picnics, activities, scuba, and handing out. Be careful of the rocks when the surf is up. People have been washed from the rocks. Don't let the height of the rocks fool you.
Really nice hiking trails. I am a mountain biker and I felt bad for them because there were so many jokers. You can do bouldering on the sisters. Dogs on lease, horses and mountain bikes allowed.
You just know there is gold under the next stone. You feel it, you know it. It's a place that really needs to be visited. It can be warm during the summer, but still a lot of fun.
Nice park with lots of shade and grass. They have several things for kids to do and even a few shopping options for adults. The small museums are with the time to view.
It's a nice park. Soccer, picnic, playground, dog park are all very well maintained. There are several things to do, i.e. Museum of Flying, Spitfire Cafe, etc.
One of the hidden gems of National Parks in the US. This used to be a National Monument and is now a National Park. I love it.
One of the 21 Alto California Missions and one of the most important in Southern California. You can't miss this mission.
Great venue! They did run out of hot food for ordering in the boxes but it was a lot of fun. I would do it again.
This is a fun pier. Not as comprehensive and full of things to do as Santa Monica Pier, but still a lot of fun.
As a human on this planet, you can't miss seeing this tree. One of the largest living organisms on the planet.

If you have a mediocum of interest in you then you should not miss Houston Space Centre. Absolutely marvellous place. Different to Kennedy SC in Florida but just as good. Fantastic tour. Hint;when you get in (as early as possible) head straight to the trolley ride to Mission Control). Food as expected - standard fare. Brilliant to be able to step aboard the 747 that piggybacked the space shuttle then go on top to actually enter a genuine shuttle. WOW! Blown away.

Only reason I gave it five stars is because I couldn't find a 6th or more. Get a 2 day pass, you'll need it. Has aircraft of all descriptions and you can touch most of them. So much history is revealed in the displays. Not just war planes but civil, Presidential, experimental, historic. From the Wright Brothers to space travel it is all here but be rested before you arrive there's lots to see.

Loved it but watch out for snakes. We nearly stepped on a 5' Diamond Back near the battlefield overlook but that just increased the fun of our visit (we're Aussies & used to snakes). Before taking the walk go into the HQ & ask to see the video. Makes all what you'll see there much clearer. Nice display of artefacts & history in the HQ.

The RV resort was terrific. One of the best we have been to. Great facilities (though the lady who runs the aquarobics needs to know EVERYONE at the park is entitled to use it not just her & her 5 clients). Would like to have had a boat & more time here as this area is very interesting.

Incredible ride to dizzying heights. Well worth the $ but unless you have a hike on the trails there isn't much else on top. 2 hints:don't push & shove into the tramway gondola, it rotates. Also go in pm & stay until sunset & watch Palm Springs light up.

What a shock. As mansions go Graceland is tiny. I am not a big Elvis fan but I found the tour of his home good (if not a bit crowded/rushed). Sad to see that opposite they have commercialised every single aspect of his life to turn a buck.

HQ building has nice little history museum but do a tour to the ancient Indian art in the canyon. Not too hard to walk down to the canyon to see the rock art but worth every cent if you value history and heritage.
likes: On-site Activities (canyon tour, rock art viewing)

reviews_attraction.text: Loved the feeling about the area. Some trails are a bit more difficult than the ranger let on but doable with some effort. Can't believe the stupidity of morons who have graffitied & damaged some valuable relics.

Would have loved to be here during better season (mid-year too hot & only 1 public area open). Fantastic place for a camping holiday. Sadly the water wasn't safe for swimming due to cyanobacteria outbreak.
As 3rd generation military (kids 4th) this is a highly emotional and thought provoking tour. Time just a little too short on the tomb. Everyone in the free world should visit.
Wow, what a dramatic location that pops up out of nowhere. Park (free) at end of bridge and walk across it. (hint-watch for Bighorn Sheep. We spotted one below the bridge.)
This is a "must see" venue. Would like to have seen more artifacts & explanations though. Growing up in the 50's & 60's this brings to life much of my childhood.
Daytime is a bit dead. (I shouldn't have used that word as someone was shot & killed here 3 days ago) some good variety gift stores but nights would be best.
No words needed. Just go. Hints: get tix from the Opry Office prior. Park at Opry Mills Mall. Arrive at Opry Mill Mall several hrs before the show to eat.
Great drive through one of America's most lovely areas. Good roads and lots to see (wildlife, petroglyphs, hikes, geological formations of many colours.)
A most awesome place. Not just rocks. Beautiful scenery and the colours are amazing. Dinosaurs, culture & history in a good location on old Route 66.
Wow. This scenic road (from Ojai to Ventucopa) is not for the feint hearted. When you get to the top look back and admire the truly amazing views.
Our first stay in an RV park in the USA. Pleasantly surprised. Great staff. Liked the way tbe sites were in clusters not regimented lines.
Very different to other mound sites. Worth the climb to the top. A fine example of a little known part of the culture of American Indians.
A different way of telling the tale of the wild west. Tickets come with OK Corral Shootout show tickets. I wouldn't miss either.
Good place to kill an afternoon or meet up with a loved one for drinks. Plenty of food and drinks, gifts & clothing stores.
If in Alamagordo, NM, don't miss the chance to catch this. Really loved the German Tornado jet fighter in the car park.
Really wasn't there long enough to make any opinion. However on the surface could be good for your average tourist.
Tiny but with a great gift shop. One of those places you have to visit. Parking behind chapel next door.
Fun location for a photo where the Eagles did a video for Take it Easy. Just gotta get a picture there.

Fantastic historic site of great significance to members of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. Many interpretive exhibits, a visitor's center, and a number of restored buildings from historic Kirtland, the headquarters for the early Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. The highlight is the Whitney Store, where Joseph Smith resided for a time and where a number of revelations significant to Latter-day Saints were received--also the location of the "School of the Prophets." Tours are conducted by missionaries for the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. They range from young and enthusiastic to older and more knowledgeable, but they are all amicable. They will be pretty open about how they feel about their faith; the tours definitely have a religious theme they don't shy away from, but I haven't seen them be overbearing.

The most beautiful building in all of Utah, reflecting the very best in workmanship of the 19th century and the high ideals of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. This building is a religious masterpiece. The interior is as beautiful as the exterior and the grounds. Although only practicing Mormons are permitted inside, there is a nice miniature showing the interior of the temple in a vistor center just south of the temple. I am partial to the Salt Lake Temple because I was married there; the staff of the temple was so gracious and accommodating to us.  Stunning views of the temple from all angles and all times of year--one of the most photogenic buildings in the western United States.

This is not a very well known spot, but you will be glad you take the drive from Natural Bridges National Monument down to Mexican Hat. Not only will you get to drive the gravel switchbacks of Moki Dugway, you will have a chance to take this short drive off the road to Goosenecks State Park, where you will get an impressive view of bends in the San Juan River. The area is desolate and remote, but the view is incredible. You will likely have the viewpoint to yourself. Great views.

One of the most beautifully underrated NPS sites in the southwest, Canyon de Chelly (de "Shay") offers beautiful red rock canyon overlooks, impressive ruins, and an immersion in Navajo culture and spiritual significance. Tours to the valley floor can be arranged through the Navajo, but the overlooks are publicly accessible and are stunning. Well worth the visit to this remote place.

A walking tour of Georgetown is a nice change of pace from touring monuments and museums all day, and the Old Stone House is in the heart of Georgetown. To my understanding, this is the oldest building in Washington still in its original state and on its original foundation. So it is old for the area. Administered by the National Park Service.

This monument is well worth visiting. The sandstone and landscape is quite different from Arches NP. The hike to the bridges is a strenuous, but worthwhile. The neatest bridge, Owachomo Bridge, is an easy walk. The other two can be seen from a distance from the drive-up viewpoints. Beautiful area, and usually very quiet and peaceful.

5-stars not so much for the lighthouse, but for the views and sounds which are the payoff for a one-mile walk along the breakwater, which make the journey worth it. Earn your lobster roll; take the hike along the breakwater.

Don't miss visiting this building on your Chicago architecture tour. Not only is the building a neo-gothic masterpiece, but the collection of fragments from famous buildings around the world is really fun to survey.

Such a great ruin to visit. Montezuma Castle is easy to access and is a very impressive and colorful cliff dwelling. Don't forget to also make the quick trip to Montezuma Well, which is equally impressive.

You can see it from the viewpoint, but much better in person. The hike us a little strenuous 1.2 round trip trail.  A little strenuous, especially if hot. But worth it, because the bridge is incredible.
A very pleasant small-sized Latter-day Saint temple is an attractive city. The temple workers were very gracious. Admission for temple-recommend carrying Mormons only, but the grounds are pleasant.
One of the neatest points of interest along any of the pioneer trails where the ruts worn away in the rock by the endless wagon wheels provides visible evidence of pioneer emigration to the west.
Incredible view of the Painted Desert in Petrified Forest National Park. The Painted Desert views are one of the most unexpected surprises of Petrified Forest National Park, especially at sunset.
This looked amazing just from the sculpture I could see on Interstate 94. I didn't have time to drive it, but from what I saw, it looked like a drive I would very much like to make.
Beautiful forest reservation near Kirtland, Ohio. There is a historic quarry here that is very interesting and the entire reserve is very pleasant with some nice walking trails.
A must-stop location on an architectural tour of New York's financial district and civic center.  A beautiful fusion of French Renaissance and American-Georgian architecture.
As awesome as I expected to be. Visited in spring time when the temperatures were still manageable. Stunning views of the pure white sand as far as you can see in some parts.
So cool! Lots of interesting interpretive exhibits and the crater itself is stunning. Great for kids. It is a pretty desolate drive getting out there though.
A striking, freshly renovated museum. An impressive building modeled after the Louvre's Tuileries addition. Close to the White House and well worth a visit.
Great family-friendly state park in northwest Las Vegas. Great petting zoo. Pleasant pond. Lots of walking trails. Lots of shade. Good parking.
Great public square in the heart of Santa Fe. Pleasant benches. Great people watching. Close to great art galleries and historic buildings.
Pleasant hike from Sand Dune Arch or the campground over level ground. Not the most impressive arch in the park, but still amazing.
Lovely lighthouse, but we could only see if from a nearby park and a restaurant parking lot. Privately owned and not accessible.
One of the finest and most carefully preserved historic sites in the United States, and also maybe its most beautiful.
The only round capitol in the United States that I can think of. Distinct architecture. It was fun to visit.

Great!!! I have tried several cave tours before. I like this one most. The formations in the cave are incredible.  You are allowed to take photos with flash light. Of course, can not to touch them as the cave is still alive. There is no fee for Park Entrance and the charge for the cave tour is only 10 dollars for adult. Also, Discounts for youth,senior and others. What a beautiful formations inside the cave! Really worth to take a long drive to see it. I pay highly respects to those rangers and volunteers. They made a lot of efforts to maintain this treasure.

An isolated place on the lower Colorado River in AZ and CA. Very quite and peaceful. Good for boating and Bird watching. It preserves habitat for bighorn sheep to the endangered birds and other animals. The refuge protects 30 river miles - 300 miles (480 km) of shoreline.

Interesting historical landmark! It is a "must see " if you like to watch trains. I wish there are some park bench on top of the hill.  (35.196972, -118.532469 Google map GPS coordinates)That is the best spot to watch loop and trains. It can be a very good vista point.

Have some nice trials. You can see Riverside city on the west side with a nice view. Also, a nice view on the south side for Moreno Valley too. Watch out for snake and mountain lion.  I met two hikers who had experience with mountain lion encounter over there.

Beautiful and unique landscape. Check the weather and drink some water before you go. Also, make sure your car is running good. :) I prefer to use the east side entrance and stay overnight in Pharump, NV.

This is the closest Grand Canyon location from Las Vegas. The view is magnificent.  Remember, you cannot take your camera on the Skywalk when you visit Eagle Point. Once is enough! I rather go South Rim.
One of those nice beaches in Laguna Beach City. The park  path is connected to Main Beach in Laguna Coast. The only concern is the parking during the weekend. Get there really early in the morning!
Nice museum!! It worth a day trip. Also,  there are a lot of things to see around this area. I wish they can extend their hours in the summer time.  Check their hours and map before you go.
It is not long distance. But, the trial is up and down. Great view!!! There is another small Arch on the right hand side of the trail. Don't miss it. It is fun. Great for photos!!
This is a must see in Tonopah. It is right behind the historical Mizpah Hotel in the centre of town. Staffs have a good knowledge of the mines history and very friendly manner.
Great views of East Lake Tahoe! Nice beaches. I was there on a gusty windy day so there was no activity on the lake. Ranger allowed me to park and take some pictures. Thanks!
Very interesting place. I suggest that you stop by the nearby Shoshone museum before you go there. You might want to get more history background about this Dublin Gulch.
A wonderful place for kids and family. They have museum and large garden.  Also, it is a great place to learn about rocks. The museum has a many collection fossils.
A hidden place for birds watching in L.A. area.  The view is beautiful during sunset. Take Davis road to get there and you will see the sign.
A must see vista point!!! I just stopped by this place. March is best time. The sign is not clear and it is so easy to miss this entrance.
It is not a big park. But, it is clean and well maintained in a nice community.  It has nice grass, tennis courts and baseball fields.
An great educational place to know more about western history. People are very friendly over there. I pay a lot of respect to them.
Met with one of the founders. Very polite person. He told us about a lot of history about this place. Many interesting collections.
Nice view with the lake and mountains. But, there is no park facilities at all. Spring is the best time when the grass are green.
Friendly rangers. Easy drive from the south entrance. The view is different as the north side of the Joshua Tree NP.
It is a good place for biking and easy hiking. No public facility! But, it is next to the city limit. easy access!
It is an okay regional park. Nice trails. Good for walking.  It will be nice to have some sun shades or canopies.
The largest state park in California. Huge area! Do a good study before you go there. Nice to use GPS and 4x4.
Not bad! It is next to the street. The lot is not big as the other train museums.  But, it is very clean.
I have been this place several times. The white domes loop is a must see.  only 1.2 miles. Worth it.

Great trail! You start off with Bathrooms and info about the rock formations and plant life. The trail is well groomed so easily doable in normal tennis shoes. No water anywhere on the trail or even at the start so bring water. The trail has a lot of traffic on it but the trail is wider then a normal single track so it is easy to pass or be passed. And there is a lot of signage on the trail so I don't get lost. Also there are maps at the start! Oh, if ur a rock climber in will enjoy this trail. There are a lot of places to climb here.

Wow what an historic place. It cost $12 to get it in per person and it is rather small inside but there's so much to see you can spend the afternoon in there looking at every little knick knack. It's crazy to think how much happened in one building. I definitely recommend it. Even though you could spend a lot of time in there I ended up spending only about 40 minutes. Enjoy tombstone.

It was cool but pair this visit with something else on your trip. Here, There are two hikes and I was planning on doing both but the other one is only with reservations at 10am. Bummed. I would also go to Roosevelt lake or drive the apache trail to make a day out of your trip from Phoenix. That is what I did. If you do make it you won't be disappointed though. Have fun!

I came here after Ramsey Canyon parking lot was full and I'm really glad I did. The ranch house was great to walk through with lots of History and I like the nature walk trail around the property. When I was there the park ranger was giving tickets to people that did not pay parking. Fyi!

When you're passing by I definitely recommend stopping here. Beautiful views after a short three-quarters of a mile hike. It was very busy and hard to find a place to take a picture so be patient. Even if you're scared of heights I still recommend checking it out. You won't regret it!

Cool spot for a quick pic. There is decent amount of parking since few people stick around for very long. Also down the hill a little bit further there's another cool spot on the same side of the street. I think I'm going to come back here and do a time-lapse!

Great hiking and mountain biking! Trails like Desert Classic for Cross-country riding and if your up for a real challenge do the Mormon National loop. For a hike do the Marcos de Niza Trail. Great place to enjoy the desert in the middle of the city!

If you live next to this monument or you're passing by, I definitely recommend stopping! You won't be disappointed. Amazing views.  I didn't have time to stick around as 3i was passing through so I will be back to do some hiking.

Wow this place is amazing and humbling at the  same time. What history is here. I'm surprised this place isn't an official historical landmark. Google the history before walking around. It will mean more when you walk around.

Very cool. Great stop and close to the 40. Lots of great info talking about the history of the crater. I am so happy we went here. They did great job making this place nice. They have a place to eat and a bug gift shop.

If u want a great place to have a good time and ur not on a budget then this is the place. So fun. The hotels here... you just have to see for ur self. Wow. Anything u can think of to eat while on the strip!
Beautiful! Definally a place to stop. The bridge is amazing and getting to see the wild life afterwords was a fun cherry on top. The rock underneath the bridge is really slippery but doable. So fun!
Great National Park! Lots of info on the park. Great knowledgeable people. Cool scenic drive!  I will say if you do know Arizona there's many other places to go to see really Saguaro.
Very cool place. It's like being on another planet. Lots of great information to read on the history of the lake. Would definitely recommend going here for an hour or two.
I will be back. It was definitely too hot in July to explore. Wasn't thrilled that you need to have a separate pass for this Natural Area but the scenery was great.
I highly recommend checking this out if you're in town. It's a quick site to see you but it's definitely worth it. It's also cool to just relax by the river.
Cool to see but a fast visit. If you live in az it is not as much of a wow as other national parks. It is still a great place to check out at least once.
dislikes: Less impressive compared to other national parks

reviews_attraction.text: A lot  to learn here and see. Worth the trip off the highway. Fun to see the old way of life and how the awesome local Indians used to help in battles.
Great hike! The first half is easy and the second half gets harder the closer you get to the top of the rim. We will be hiking this trail again!
Wow this park has alot of shoreline. Good restrooms. Fun little garden to check out. The a a hiking trail. Several beaches. Nice park.
Nice little park with a playground, basketball court and a couple fields and the bathroom. Looks like there is a splashpad too.
They have a bathroom here and all sorts of souvenirs and they can answer a lot of questions if you have any. Very helpful
likes: Facilities & Services: Helpful staff, Souvenirs, Bathroom

reviews_attraction.text: Short hike that is paved. Lots of signs to read about the history. Great place to streach your legs on a road trip!
Great place to eat. Cheaper option then in the parks. Great place to relax till you get a second wind.
Just check this place out. I learned a lot and they had way more than I expected. Great job NPS!

Very beautiful here. Sad that the water levels are really low. On the beach, you have to walk about a mile to get to the water. There is a great ranch to see a lot of old tools and the old accommodations of the ranchers. The buffalo roam really close with their babies so be careful.

We had so much fun! The only thing we didn't like was standing in line for an hour and a half to get food. If you buy the arm band, know that you can not get something every hour. We got our money's worth but I won't do that again. Lines for rides were not that bad.

This areavis beautiful. We had a lot of fun in the visitor's center as well as driving around the area. There are a few farms around with cattle and horses. Peaceful drive. Some area of the roads are rough because the state does not keep up with the roads.

Very interesting! I learned a lot about the saguaro. Make sure you see the movie that plays every half an hour. Also the cactus on the inside of the guest center has doors with information and small animals that can live in it.

It was interesting. I love conjoined people and animals. They have many conjoined animals. It is a great little place tucked away between all the bars. The staff was very nice. There was even a small freak show afterwards!

Great place to spend a day or two. We didn't even get to go to the other half of the park. There is a lot to see. Even though it was hot, we were able to drive overlooks. If you have time, there are ranger guilded tours.

The spot looks like nothing. There are signs that say no trespassing. However you can drive in the yard. There is a little old man that is really nice. Not a lot to see, just a wall, plants, and a few animals.

You can learn a lot of information center before visiting Death Valley. There is a small museum. The ranger are very knowledgeable and friendly. Great place to stop for water before heading into the heat.

This was really fun. It was $6 for a guided tour. (Or you can walk the ridge by yourself for free.) The tour guide was very nice and knowledgeable! I learned a lot! The gift shop has so much fun stuff!!
Great National park! I just happened to see a sign for it. The half a mile walk down the trail in to the canyon was worth it. Coming back up was a bit hard. However if I can make it, you can too.
I loved looking at all the animals. They seemed well cared for. We saw wildlife workers feeding and making sure the animals had water. The loops around the animal areas let you get a closer look.
This park has 3 different ecosystems. It is beautiful here. Stop at the visitor's center and talk to the rangers. They have loads of information. It was flooded so be careful after it rains.
We were too late to see the ruins but we loved seeing the movie, talking to the rangers, and walking through the museum. The visitor's  center closes at 5 but the trail closes a 4.
I love taking my little daycare kids to this place. It is free and there are lots of dinosaurs and other animals!!! The owner is very nice and each person takes home a small gift.
There is a bit of walking: 3 minutes to the visitor's center and 10 to 15 minutes to the site. Rudy was our ranger. She was knowledgeable about the ranch and the petroglyphs.
Enjoyed this National park. We got there right before closing but they didn't rush us out. They answered questions for us and even told us of another park that we would love.
Love the sign. There is a guy that is there at night that will take your pictures with his light and your camera for tips. Use him if you go at night!! Much better picture.
The rangers were so helpful. They gave us a lot of information about the settlement and surrounding area. They took the time to even discuss the small museum.
Today we got in free but it is usually just $5. There is lots of information. It is very interesting information. The staff is friendly and knowledgeable.
I love National Parks! I learn so much! Make sure you see the movie. It was interesting with lots to see. There was even a lady making fresh tortilla.
Such an interesting place. The rangers are so knowledgeable. They were able to tell us what was the best thing to see. The store has a lot of stuff.
Learned a lot about Clark county. It is very interesting. I would go early to see the outside building. It is $2 for adults and $1 for kids.
Such a beautiful location. The trees and green grass are so relaxing. The visitors center is closed due to covid but the park is open.
Odd sight on the side of the road. It looks like an office was there last. We drove in the yard and it is for rent.
Very interesting place. I didn't know what to expect. It is a see if you are in the area type of place.

I have been to the cave before, it is truly amazing to explore. I brought my son for his first trip, it was a blast you can walk through at your own pace, their are elevators is your handicap, not athletic or just don't really like walking that much. The cave system is huge there is a restaurant, restrooms, and all kinds of other things down there...yes down in the cave. As a bonus you can stay and watch millions of bats leave the cave every night to feed. Pretty dam cool.

Not really sure why I stopped here, I think it was on my way home from a road trip...  Totally worth it though lots of small lakes to swim and play in, camping, 4x4ing, there is even a nature preserve. There is lots of parking clean restrooms and a larger lake with paddle boats and boards plus great swim area for kids.

Lots of stuff to do here other than hike, I did the cave tour it was great Ranger Ben was super fun and informative in a cool not boring way. There is a great resturant with homemade everything good price very laid back, lots of parking, biking, and hiking. Bonus you get to pass through some cool little towns.

Another of Arizona's hidden but not so hidden gems, these ruins easy to walk to and stunning. Plus you have Roosevelt Lake right there as well as the upper Salt River so there is a lot to do nearby after seeing the ruins. Plenty of parking cool museum and lots of chances to see local wild life.

Stopped on our way home to Phoenix from New Mexico, this place is amazing. Very cheap to park or camp. Tins of nice restrooms, garbages, picnic and camp spots. My son loved climbing the rocks and is begging to go back and camp. This place does not disappoint I can't wait to go back.

Awsome trail really cool waterfalls at the end if your there at the right time of year. Trail is well marked heavily trafficked but still have your own space, plenty of parking, no restrooms but food and bathrooms are nearby. Bring lots of water!!!! Lots of mean cactus along trail

Mesa center for the Arts is Awsome. It's hip lots of thing to do and see in a very close proximity, there is plenty of parking. ⚠ though don't waist your time or money to see Shen Yun... almost my wosrt theater experience ever...

Beautiful and super fun.... lots of parking trough out  the  park ,clean restrooms , lots of wildlife  and a botanical  garden. Kids will love this place climbing  everywhere with lots of trails, hiking and mountain  biking

Great place to stop if you don't know Oak Creek and Sedona very well you can get all the info you need maps of all trails and parking passes if needed plus nice clean restrooms and a small shop if your not prepared.

Great trails hiking, biking, horse back riding Peralta Trail has it. It does get busy it is very popular and permit needed but CHEAP and worth it. Can't wait to go back....please bring lots of WATER if you go

Very cool museum, HAVE TO MAKE ONLINE RESERVATIONS FOR MUSEUM  its a dollar  and well worth  it lots of hiking,  the green river, more than just the museum . Camping , kayaking  and other outdoor  activities

Took my kiddo for his first time to see this amazing Arizona history. Great parking really nice friendly staff, and if your in Arizona you really should see these ruins in the center of a modern city.
Awsome for all ages, Saturday is food truck night, music, food , fun. Free.. Some Saturday's they play movie's...horseshoe pitts...water features to play in this park has it all. LOTS OF PARKING
Very busy. Had to wait for parking, Sedona is not what it once was quaint little town gone tourist everywhere. Worth the aggregation though and plenty of spots that are not so well known.
Great park for sports! Soccer, baseball, football ext. Tons of space small playground, however has a great fishing canal and nice basketball court's.... Perfect place to fly a kite
No place on earth quite like it.... Tons of parking for all type's of vehicles, picnic area's 🚻 the works and REALLY cheap too. This is worth the drive a great family day trip.
Went for a morning hike, first time on this trail love it, technically its on a dirt road so most can hike this water during rainy season old ranch and beautiful scenery
Beautiful Indian petroglyphs to see, really cool old ranch, lots of hiking plus Beaver Creek runs right through tons of great spots to hang out, explore or picnic.
Love this hike. Always good parking, cheap, so much to see on the many trails. The staff there is Awsome I go many times a year. Can't wait to go back.
Pretty cool place, owner is a character you'll really like him, probably run into free roaming cows, donkey rescue and located in a beautiful area
Wow... this place is amazing. Offers hiking, camping, biking, wildlife,  lava tubes and so much more. If you in St. George  Utah  its a must go.
Its was great lots to see and learn about got to see some critters and the kids loved the light show, tons of parking good food good prices
Love this spot great stop before or after the lake, lots of little shops, cool railroad ride, zipline, resturant and so much more.
Sand is suprisingly cool, but bring lots of water....Something to sled down the dunes with is recommended for a bit of extra fun
Really cool Museum with lots of old west Arizona history and of course the most amazing rose tree you have ever seen

I’ve awarded 5 stars for the preservation efforts and historical significance which is well worth the short detour (about 15 minutes off I-25).  Fort Union has gone through three iterations.  The last was the largest and most impressive. The National Park Service is going an excellent job in preserving and restoring this important landmark.  Fort Union played an important role in the Civil War and trade and commerce. Fort Union supplied military installations for hundreds of miles and was the home to the first U.S.  Calvary.  The path is an easy walk and the staff are friendly and knowledgeable.  There is a short movie that is worth watching.

The cavern has an interesting history from ancient times to being used in the Civil War for saltpeter production.  There is an old still for used to make moonshine.  The caverns are among the largest I’ve seen although the formations are not as impressive as other caverns. the caverns do have “cave flowers” which we haven’t seen before and are fairly rare. The main attraction is the large underwater body of water.  The lake is stocked with rainbow trout occasionally.  You take a short trip on flat bottom boat on the water.  Our tour guide, Tyler, did a nice job of telling the history pointing out interesting items.

Very crowded on a holiday weekend.  Waited over a half an hour to get into the park.  We had to wait several hours to take the tram.    There were plenty of wildlife sightings (birds, gators, fish. turtles) and flora.  While not as spectacular as other National Parks, the biodiversity and eco system are very interesting.  The tram ride was very crowded however our driver, Richard and guide, Kristine were excellent.  Kristine provided excellent commentary and information and both were good at spotting wildlife.

Let’s start with what you won’t see: The original Golden Spike (at Stanford), original rails (removed for WWII), original engines (they do have very nice reproductions).  In fact, almost everything at the site is a reproduction.  All that said-it is the location of the Golden Spike where the Transcontinental railroad came together and for that alone, is worth a stop.  If you have an engineer in the group, they will probably enjoy the Auto Tour (about 14 miles).

Unfortunately the road to the top of the volcano to see crater washed out about a month ago.  It is not expect to reopen until Spring of 2020 at the earliest.

You can still walk the trails around the Visitor's Center and the scenery is beautiful.  We took the Lava Flow path. While the walk is not difficult, it is uneven with loose rocks and is easy to slip.

My rating reflects the closure of the road and should be reconsider after the Crater Road is re-opened.

We hadn’t been here for about 20 years (or more).  We opted for the self-guided Big Room tour.  While the formations aren’t as good as other caves, the room, which is the largest in the Western Hemisphere is impressive.  The Big Room is more than 4 football fields in size.  Path is paved and fairly easy to navigate although some areas are steep.  I've posted a few pictures even   don't do the cavern justice.

We’d never heard of this designation before our visit to this park.  This park is a partially restored mission.  The small museum is nicely done.  There has been some renovation on the church and other buildings.  The original orchard has been re-planted by Master Gardner volunteers.  If you’re in the area, it’s worth the trip. Or if you’re trying to see all the National Parks in the Sonora Desert.

We recently went with family to Hearst Castle after visiting many, many years ago.  It was  just as beautiful and impressive as we remembered.  The Park tour guides did an wonderful job of conducting the tour and answering questions.  After the tour you are free to roam around the grounds and enjoy the view, gardens and statues.

We have been to Multnomah Falls several times over the years.  The Falls will be a bit different each time due to the volume of water but always beautiful and a worthwhile trip.  The Falls are popular so parking can be a challenge.  Short walk on a paved area for a great view.  Restaurant and gift shop on site.

An interesting museum of Route 66 memorabilia and displays. Includes displays of the depression and an electric car display. We may think the electric car is new but it goes back to the early days of the automobile.  Includes a golf cart owned by Willie Nelson. Worth a stop if you’re passing through.

Our server, Jay was excellent even taking us on a brief tour to see the production facilities including tanks.  We even able to do a barrel tasting.  The wines were all excellent.  We appreciated the unusual wines including Carignane, bBarbera, Malbec.

Friendly, knowledgeable staff, excellent, reasonable priced wines.   Tastings are still free-you can choose up to 6.  On weekends, you can select the Cuvee's as part of your tasting choices.  They also have events on many Wednesday's and Fridays.

Interesting, restored lighthouse built inland and not on the water.  Senior discount.  Lighthouse keeper house also available to view.  Probably overpriced for what it is but the fee does support the lighthouse restoration and upkeep

Small tasting room in Jacksonville.  Our server, Darius, was interesting and knowledgeable.  The wines include Grenache Blanc, Cab Franc and white and red blends.  Tasting fee waived with purchase.  The wines were nice.
We enjoy wine tasting and look for wineries wherever we go.  John, our server and assistant wine maker was friendly and obviously knowledgeable about the wines.  Decent wines.  Charge for tasting.
Woodstock!  50th Anniversary! Was expecting so much more than it turned out to be.  Interesting but not so compelling.  Some original documents.  Good stories.  Quality café. Nice staff.
Short paved walk to the Falls.  The Falls were lovely.   We went in the morning-the parking lots seem to fill up fast.  Spaces when we arrived-none when we left.  Restrooms available.
While not a must see attraction it is a fun stop.  We didn't tour the actual home but walked around the grounds and visited the Trading Post.  They have a small zoo but we didn't go.
The Navajo National Monument has a short walking trail to a view of the ancient ruins in the distant cliff.  There is a mounted viewer but suggest bringing a good pair of binoculars.
The Mohave Museum of Industry is included in the price for the Arizona Route 66 Museum.  An eclectic display of Native American, Cowboy/Ranching/Americana and Andy Devine artifacts.
We stopped in with family group of 5. The staff made us 5 custom flights so we could try all of the wines/sparkling wines.  The service was great and we enjoyed wines.
We enjoyed a relaxing wine tasting outside on the patio.  Although the winery was busy we were not rushed.  Tasting fee waived with an appropriate purchase.
We visited the Park in June  so there was still snow at higher elevations.  We especially enjoyed the sulfur pots.  The drive through the park is beautiful.
My husband, the civil engineer, loves all bridges so this was a must see.  The walk is fairly easy but may be more challenging for some.
The Lavender Pit is an old Copper Mine.  The size of the pit is impressive  and the colors nice.  Worth a stop if you are in the area.

I did two hikes here, one was Elephant Mountain and the other was Skull Mesa.

Elephant Mountain: I came here on a Tuesday weekday morning around 7AM, and after paying the $3 entrance fee, we got a map and started on the hike! The hike was quite scenic and not difficult. It also doesn't really go up to a peak of any sort which is disappointing, but the views all along the hike especially when going downward was great as the sun was shining and the mountains were in our vicinity! Took about 2.5 hours in total, and there were more cars when we got back.

Skull Mesa: I came here on Black Friday, arrived around 10:15AM and the parking lot had quite a few cars but still had spaces to park. It's $3 to enter, cash only, and the people there provide a map which is nice! The trail is pretty rocky but the view is different than a lot of Arizona hikes for a change. Good hike, would recommend!

It was super cold as it's winter now. I got to the parking lot at 6:50AM on a Sunday, but nobody was there (and it was still dark). Waited for hiking buddy until around 7:25AM, still empty parking lot. Started the hike, it was really cold, everything in the shade. Views were alright, lots of dead trees. I can see how this would be very pretty when the trees are alive though and in the sunlight. Lots of creek crossings, many of which were icy so bring a hiking pole or walking stick to help balance. Some creek crossings required going off-trail a bit to find a better place to cross that wasn't freezing cold water and ice. Cool hike, wish I were here to do this again in warmer weather! The sun came out on the way back and it was much more enjoyable then. Parking lot had maybe 10-15 cars when we got back at around 11AM, but still had lots of spots.

I came here to see cherry blossoms, and I really liked that the visitor center was handing out maps for where the cherry blossom trees were. I walked to all of them, and most of them were still in bloom which was great. I didn't like that people could drive on the roads in the arboretum and there wasn't a separate walkway for people. I've been to many arboretums and this is the first one where cars and people share the same path (it's actually the first one I've been to where cars are even allowed inside). There weren't too many people which was great, and it's free! The arboretum is decently sized and pleasant to walk around. There wasn't much else in bloom at the time I came, but I'm sure it's more interesting when there are more plants that are alive!

I came here on a Friday morning close to 9AM, and the parking lot was mostly full. I snagged a spot, took a look at the map, and started hiking - I did Soldier Pass -> Brins Mesa -> Cibola -> Jordan. Soldier Pass and part of Brins Mesa were quite pretty, but Cibola and Jordan were very mediocre. I wish I did this counterclockwise because the views would have been better that way (the downside though is that there's part of the hike that would've been pretty steep). I saw a decent number of people, which wasn't great during covid times. I got back in 2 hours, and the parking lot was completely full by then (with a line outside the parking lot). Get here early!
likes: Pretty hiking trails (Soldier Pass, Brins Mesa)

reviews_attraction.text: I was visiting the Finger Lakes region and came to stop by here. I paid for entry which was $8, and there was a friendly person helping out with that. She also gave me a map, which wasn't super useful as the park is quite small but I still appreciated it. I got quite lucky with parking, and then I went to go walk on the gorge trail. The sign to the gorge trail was misleading though, as the sign said another trail. But, I went back to the entrance to ask and she told me it was the way I already went. In any case, I walked along the trail until the bridge, and then I crossed over it and came back. I wasn't super impressed, but it was a pleasant walk.

I came here on a Saturday and arrived at around 8AM to the parking lot, in which there were two other cars. We started the hike at 8:15AM, and we made it to the top at 10:45AM. The incline wasn't too bad, and it was shaded most of the way. There's some switchbacks in the beginning and it curves around and starts going upward a bit more steadily. Almost near the top, the trees disappear and the space opens up. The top was quite windy and the view was alright. Signage was fine as there was only one fork. We got up in 2.5 hours and got down in about 2 hours. Not too many people on the trail.

I came here on Labor Day, arriving around 7:30AM. The parking lot was about half full, and I passed some people on the way up and a lot more on the way down. The weather was a bit chilly especially at the top where it was quite windy. The hike wasn’t too difficult nor steep, perfect for a low-key hike. The views included walking through meadows and next to a stream, as well as being surrounded by mountains. It took me about an hour and a half to get to the lake and then a little more than a an hour after that to go back down, during which the parking lot was full.

This is one of the visitor centers for Grand Teton, and it's great! The building architecture is amazing, and the informational boards inside are great as well. The park rangers are friendly, and they gave us some suggestions for hikes. There's a gift shop as usual with posters, shirts, magnets, books, and other souvenirs. There's an awesome view of the Tetons as well at the back of the visitor center, and it's great! Definitely recommend stopping by to get some information or just to check out the space.

I came here for snowboarding, and it was quite great! The snow quality was quite good, and I enjoyed the wide runs. There was one part that was super flat, so I couldn't go on a lot of runs otherwise I would end up on the flat area. I liked the tree runs which were quite short and good for starter tree runs, and there were nice mogul runs too. The lines were quite short and I understand why people say this is more of a local's ski resort. I also appreciated it being on the Ikon pass this year!

This park is great! Not many people but sprinkled with cherry blossoms. The paths were a bit muddy though, and it wasn't the cleanest as there was a lot of trash at the south tip. There are benches and tables for barbecuing along the waterfront, and there were a lot of people fishing as well. It was a great walk, very calm and peaceful except for the occasional airplane overhead which was really noisy. Definitely would recommend if you need a break from the crowd at the Tidal Basin!

I came here around 12:45PM on a Thursday and the parking lot was about 2/3 full. There's a map in the beginning and the signage is decent, saw quite a few people on the trail. The trail I did (Thunder Mountain -> Andante -> Chimney Rock Pass) is pretty much in the city, so the views include power lines which isn't really ideal. The hike is pretty flat and not super interesting but is still pretty because it's still Sedona after all. Took me about 1.5 hours to complete the loop.

$5 parking fee, I got here a quarter to 3PM on Saturday, parking lot was pretty much full. The hike goes by a bunch of resorts in the beginning which isn't that great but the views there in my opinion were the best. Afterward, it goes into the trees, gets a bit cold due to the shade, and then just goes on for a bit without any views. I went about 2 miles in before turning back around. Lots of people on the trail although many are wearing masks which is good.
dislikes: Lack of views in some parts

reviews_attraction.text: The information on here is incorrect regarding mileage - it's 1 mile, not 2. I came here on a weekday evening around 7PM and when we arrived, we were the only car, but when we left, there were a few more cars around. The walk up was pleasant and there were some mountain views, and the walk down was fine. There were some picnic tables too which are good to hang out at, and it's not a bad spot to watch the sunset! Short and sweet trail.

I came here on a Sunday morning around 8AM, and there were no cars when we arrived. The hike was okay; the first mile or so was burnt land and not that interesting, but once the trail went into the rocks, it was more interesting although the trail turned into sand. The trail went past the AllTrails to High Point and the trail faded out. We saw more people on the way out coming in, and there were more cars when we got back to the car.

I came here as I was around the Finger Lakes area, and it was a great stop! I came after the gates had already closed, so I didn't need to pay the $8 (although you can use the same ticket for all state parks for the day). I stopped at all three waterfalls, and they were all great. I really enjoyed my time here! Parking was plentiful and the park was quiet and peaceful. I would recommend coming here if you're around the area!

I came here on a Friday afternoon around 3:30PM, and there's a dirt road leading up to the parking lot. There were quite a few cars although I didn't see any people during the hike. I went further in than this trail (about 8 miles roundtrip), but it was mostly walking in the wash which was pretty boring and the canyon itself wasn't too interesting.

Short walk to the rock, lots of people around 2PM on a Sunday afternoon. Parking lot was full, waited for a spot. Hike after the rock didn't have many people, although some people were climbing on there rock despite the sign saying not to. How unfortunate. The rest of the hike was quiet and pretty, especially the north side between the rocks.

A truly hidden gem! It's great. The trail is party paved, shaded, and in general a delight. It goes by some trees and grass, and the trail is obvious and quiet. It's also not too long and slightly sloped, which makes it a good trail to run on as well. The sign at the beginning says it's 2.2 miles roundtrip, so it's a nice walk!

I came here on a Sunday around 10AM and snagged a parking spot in the full parking lot. I hiked clockwise, which was definitely the way to go since there was a steep downhill in the beginning. Views on the west were prettier, and the narrows at the bottom was really awesome! Sandy hiking but not too bad, very pretty!

Ran around on the trail here as part of the Santa Clara River Trail, and the trails here were really pleasant. Lots of people walking their dogs, running, and walking, and it's a bit quieter as it's a bit further away from the street. The trail is flat and paved, and it's just in general a very nice park to be in!

I did this trail a bit after noon and the trail was quite full of people when I went, as was the parking lot. The bridges were cool and the trail is mostly shaded, but there were really just too many people. The bridges are numbered which was informative, and the trail overall was enjoyable and not too difficult.
