When I arrived around 9AM, the parking lot was full but there was plenty of close street parking. I did the loop and while the views were about the same, they were still pleasant. Trail goes down first and then back up, but it wasn't too bad. Signage was pretty clear. Took me about 1.5 hours to complete the loop.

Came here after getting some ice cream nearby during a weekday evening. It's a bit dark but there are lights. One street is lined with homeless people so be careful there, and parking is blocked off after 10PM on some other streets. Nice lake in the middle, paths are paved. Cool park!

I came here on a weekday around 3:15PM, and there were pretty much no people on the trail. It was quite steep and the trail is a dirt path for most of it, also a bit slippery coming down. No shade, not clearly signed although I suppose the path is mostly clear. Decent views.

Came here on a weekday afternoon, had quite a few cars parked. Saw people with dogs off-leash, it was great! Trails are unmarked, didn't really know where I was going. Didn't see the river, trail quite boring.

I am so glad that they kept that part of the old Great Northern Railroad Depot when they prepared for Expo 74. If you are old enough, remember the jumble of railroads, trestles, bridges, depots, warehouses, mills, and other structures obscuring the otherwise beautiful Spokane Galls? That's all gone except the Clock tower. It reminds us of what made Spokane what it is. Thankfully, we have found more aesthetic and more environmentally friendly ways to accomplish the same things.

It's a busy place nowadays. People of all types flock to the trailhead. Some just look into the canyon and gawk at the rim. Others saunter down the crowded upper stretch of the trail. Some go further yet into the great abyss. But far less actually hike the trail from top to bottom and then back up. It's a killer day hike! And still fewer yet go all the way to the north rim.

My wife and I spent the night in Longview. The next morning on the way out we stopped at this extraordinarily beautiful inner city park. We ended up walking almost its full length. Every bend presented yet another landscape masterpiece. The lake water mirrored the trees. Sculptured gardens graced its banks. Huge mossy oaks shaded the sky. Wonderful!

Who doesn't like the centerpiece of Leavenworth? We have been there so many times I never thought to review it. In summer we like to get our ice cream cones from Das Sweet Shop or a pastry from the Danish Bakery and stroll through Art-In-The-Park. Great people watching! In winter, the colorful lights are a menagerie. Every year they do it up better.

The long trek up Stafford Creek culminates in view spectacular. Mountain meadows, snow capped peaks, canyonous valleys, and vibrant wildflowers fill the mind with wonder. The saddle-like pass divides Earl and Navaho Peaks. Both can be easily scrambled up with even better views of everything, especially the neighboring Enchantments.

I am glad to see the tired old park renovated this last year. As a kid we used to play here and families had picnics and games. Seeing it used that way again today warmed my heart. Parks rarely are a waste of money. They get people outside for wholesome social activity and a break from electronic media.

Shasta is one of the nations great dams, not just in scope, but in aesthetic appeal. I cannot think of another that spans a valley with such grace, like it belongs there. And it is huge! It takes a while to walk across. Only until you look over the Spillway to you realize how high you are.

Who doesn't like the lava rock observatory at the summit of McKenzie Pass? One would hardly know they were in the Pacific Northwest being totally surrounded by the massive destruction of tsunami-like lava flows. Craters everywhere. Islands of forest. Snow-capped peaks. Another world.

This church and its surrounding made us wonder if we were transported to Cape Cod. The church and the residences impressed us for their immaculate care and upkeep. The old town was a flower garden of wonder. Right by the church is a historical marker showing the key places.

The new exhibits on the oval viewing platforms on the east and west end of the Dismal Nitch Rest Area are well done. They also made them wheelchair friendly. The place has a nice view of the wide Columbia River. Washington State maintains a rest area at the same location.

Leavenworth is a living fantasyland. Waterfront Park is no exception. Stroll wide trails in peaceful sublimity away from the hoards on Front Street. The Wenatchee River turns placid down there. Knife-edged peaks reflect on the water as seen through gaps in the trees.

In back of the Kamehameha Statue is a building similar to the Iolani Palace. It was to be a palace but became a government headquarters instead. Then it became the site of the coup that overthrew the monarchy and the rest is history. Today it houses the judiciary.

While driving by Connell, a park caught my eye. I decided to look at it. Pioneer park really impressed me. Spacious, well kept grounds, a water park for summer, some really cool slides, and a skateboard park. I have in minds to take my grandkids down here.

Otter Crest Viewpoint is one of our ritual stops when touring the Oregon Coast. I particularly like the view of Cape Foulweather. Since childhood, I've noticed the slow, steady encroachment of the ocean surf. The fence line keeps being moved inland.

We looked at the park out of curiosity. Although there were park facilities like picnic tables, the few that were there used it for fishing. We walked around on the limited paths which helped us unwind from heavy traffic up the Kamehamwha Hwy.

I am amazed that an architectural marvel like this stands in Eastern Oregon. The interior is beautiful! The warmth of the place reflects the warmth of the church. They seem to have a special interest in the sanctity of the unborn as well.

My grandkids consider it the best part of Columbia Park. The complex fort keeps their attention for more time than I have patience to supervise. And what kid (or adult) doesn't want to dodge water sprays in the aquatic playground?

I was surprised by the size of this park. It had all the stuff you would look for in a beach park: nice surf, sandy beach, wide open grassy area, and mountains next door. Curious little Mokolii Island draws a lot of attention too.

I found the Garden rather unique. It showcased indigenous plants and flowers in a semi-formal fashion. While examining the Garden I realized that in was the only visitor. It's definitely off the main tourist course.

The Omak Stampede Rodeo grounds were bigger than I expected. It is surrounded by a large park with the Visitor Center front and center. I liked seeing where they race the horses down the side of the Okanogan River.

The park area around the old depot is nice. I've driven by for years on the highway and did not realize how pretty this part of town is. Now, you can ride your bike all the way to Yakima on the rail made trail.
The large platform right on the lake edge affords a nice view of the fountain and island gazebo. I noticed solid timber inserts in the exposed aggregate concrete.
I would like to rate it higher since we stopped during a winter storm and everything was closed. The historic aspect looked interesting.
I loved this small beach near Kaaawa. It's just right on the ocean highway. Hardly anyone there. Nice sand and surf. Peacefulness.
Too bad for me, the fountain was dry when I looked at it. However, I can imagine it, especially at night.

This is a very beautiful clean campground Mamosa trees near the coast. Camped there in February the beautiful lower campground was closed. Upper campground is very nice and well-maintained.  The sites on the inside of the loop or have power the sites on the outside do not. Showers and bathrooms are A+ clean and modern. We stayed in site 23 and did not have AT&T cell phone reception but a short walk to the other side of the campground gave us full LTE. The upper loop is located right next to Highway 101 but the road wasn’t all that busy in February. In the winter this campground does not get much sun so our solar panels did not charge your batteries during the day. It’s a short 10 minute walk to the beach. The upper campground site to have some privacy between each spot and many of the lower campground spots also have privacy. This campground excepts reservations all your long so plan your trip accordingly. The best sites are in the lower loop far away from US 101. Many of the sites on the lower loop accommodate very large trailers or class a motorhome‘s. Several of the campsites on the lower loop are pull throughs that look to be about 80 feet long. Beach access is down a path from the lower campground and under the US 101 highway bridge
dislikes: Poor cell phone reception at some sites

reviews_attraction.text:
Amazing and unique way to see the countryside from the seat of a peddle powered Velocipede.  It takes about two hours for a round trip and the track is mostly flat.  It does burn some calories so be prepared for a little bit of a workout.  On our trip there was an 70+ year old couple that did just fine because the crew placed two younger people in their cart.
TIP: tell the crew member that you want to ride in the front car with the crew member.  You will get more info and he had really strong leg muscles.

Great place to camp.  Lots of space between sites and the price is right: $8 regular and $4 with senior discount card.  The petroglyphs are a really interesting but a bit disappointing.  There are not many petroglyphs ( maybe 100 or so that you can get close to) but there’s a lot of ‘petroglyph graffiti that ruins the experience for me.  Camping stop for one night = A, historic sight = B-

Amazing place to stop if you're in the Mojave National Preserve.  I would STRONGLY suggest you stop here BEFORE spending much time in the preserve because there are so many great resources about what to see while visiting.  They also have an excellent collection of railroad items with detailed explanations of how the railroad came to Kelso.  Lots of quality souvenirs too.

If you’re into military history, this is one super interesting stop.  Loved seeing the simulated middle launch and the tour of the underground facility. Our tour guide was stationed there durning to Cold War and he had some unique perspectives about operating a missile with a 9 megaton warhead and how it felt to have his workplace targeted by the Soviets. Amazing.

An interesting state park that seems to have been forgotten.  While other beach state parks nearby were full, Ocean Beach SP was mostly deserted. You can tell this is normal because most of the site appear to not have been occupied in the past summer season.  Most of the electric sites were occupied tho.  LOTS of privacy in the non-electric sites.

Best hike on the island
Park at Ebey’s Landing or on the street (free)
Hike up the bluff and along the ridge for2 miles. The views are AWESOME. Then take the he switchbacks down to the beach (0.3 miles). Then hike the 2 miles on the beach back to the car.
Make sure to bring some snacks so you can sit, eat, relax, and enjoy the gorgeous views.

The campground here is not that great. Most of the sites are on even small unlevel and very close to the site next-door. There’s very little privacy here. Also the train runs through the state park very close to the campground so you will hear train horn’s and squeaking training wheels all hours of the day and night.

Great quiet park on the Spokane River.  It will fill up on summer weekend but it’s much quieter during the week.  At Nine Mile Recreation Area, there’s a boat launch that’s pretty busy in the mornings and late afternoon.  We were able to catch Rainbow Trout from a float tube just off the shore of the park.

What a beautiful, well maintained park!  Lots of space between sites. Kayak, jet ski, and boat rentals available. Lots of green grass with sprinklers running morning and night.  Tennis and baseball courts too. Major boat launch.  What more to ask for?

Trash, trash everywhere.   Our first campsite had so much trash that we had to move.  Our second site was still trashed.  The pic I area near the lake was full of trash.  The bathrooms were old and filthy.
We left after on day.  A real nasty place.

Super great park next to a lake.  Was easy to get an RV spot during the middle of the week with no reservations.  Easy access to the boat ramp.   Lots and lots of tent only camping spots that are nearest the lake.  Great place for summer fun!

A must stop place on your drive down the Oregon coast.  Easy half mile walk up to the lighthouse.  The camp hosts give short tours of the lower floor of the main lighthouse building. The view from the lighthouse hill are breathtaking.

Must see when on Orcas Island.
RV Note: The campgrounds were mostly closed during the winter months and most sites would not accommodate a small RV because they are too small or unlevel
Nice 10 minute walk from the dirt parking lot at the end of the road up to the lighthouse.  When you get close, you can see the old lens turning and send out it’s beacon of light.

Great place to have a picnic on the beach.  Lots of parking and access to the trails in Deception  Pass State Park
Tip: Super great place to watch the sunset over the Puget Sound
Nice little state park along Highway 101. Nothing special about the place but it seems easier to get a campsite late in the day if you can't get in anywhere else
Nice WW1 gun battery.  There are some posters inside which help explain the operations of the battery.  Most of the doors are open to explore the rooms inside.
A great place to watch the military fighter jets blast up the canyon.  When we were there, there were about 20 people waiting for the jets with their cameras.
Nice shopping area with galleries, restaurants, bars.  The place didn’t have much of a buzz the April weekday evening we visited but it was still cute.
Easy .6 mile walk from the parking lot to the lighthouse.  You will be rewarded with a great view of where the Columbia River meets the Pacific Ocean.
Most sites are in the trees away from the beach. Good separation between sites.  Very little light in the winter.  Super beautiful place tho
There are three nice shelters all the way at the end that work great as a place to stay dry to during the rainy days in the winter.
AMAZING.  AMAZING. AMAZING.  We spent 3 hours in Meow Wolf and had such a great time exploring.  Get there early.
This is a great place to rent a doing buggy and spend the day driving around in the great sand dunes

Well-done reenactment and displays of what we believe the settlement was like. It is a large property so you can spend as much time as you like interacting with period-costumed employees, asking questions and watching demos.
The ships and buildings were excellent, there are several focal points to help round out your understanding of the era, and the different important cultures.
Follow this up with a visit to the actual settlement location and it is hard not to have a well-rounded feel of this important time in US history.

Rustic but peaceful. Great sunset and plenty of camping spots open.
The rock pile of petroglyphs are a notable piece of history. So many glyphs that they overlap and jumble. This was a common stop for numerous historical trails through the area. Fun to imagine that point in time.
Some nice signage ro help explain the significance of the area.

Interesting displays and very unique presentations compared to many other museums. I needed a bit more time to fully explore and will stop back to complete my tour. It has been completely remodeled since my last visit and I was impressed.
This time it was mid-week so I did not get enjoy the dancers but I remember how fun that was last visit.

Wonderful quick hike on a blue-sky day.  Yaktrax, skis or snowshoes all perfect for the gradual uphill climb to the old mining town of Boston, and beyond if you must. Use skis if you want the downhill speed going back to the parking lot. Popular spot. Expect dogs, kids and regular encounters with others enjoying the day with you.

So fun to wander! Went back twice to continue to explore. You can walk up to the ridge and see all of Albuquerque and beyond. So convenient to the city and chock full of petroglyphs. Wildlife was everywhere- coyote, jack rabbit, birds of all kinds. Gorgeous flowers too.

Great sculpture outdoors and a varied and interesting array inside as well. The jewelry display was well-done with good detail on the history and evolution of design.
Also a good mix of old and new, classic and modern, art and culture. Very enjoyable afternoon.

Enjoyed hiking and exploring here so much I had to come back again in the evening. Hundreds of petroglyphs and many trails that are easy to maneuver.  Hike up on the ridge for s grand view of Albuquerque and Sandia.

Nice winter entertainment for kids and adults. Facilities were good... though they could use additional heaters for the parents and non-skaters.  The rink is good sized and they have buckets to help the newbies.

Worth a stop. The buildings and artifacts were unique and kept us engaged for almost an hour. Not recalling all of Poe's life story before our visit made it an education as well. Be sure and pet the kitties!
A bit remote but that is actually what I liked. It added a dimaension that is missing from some museum displays as you could more easily guess what life may have been like in the area.
Very fun- whether you are a balloonist or not. Lots of great displays and history. A good variety of artifacts, good explanations and storytelling. Worth a stop for kids and adults..
Large caves appear to have had some significant structures over time. On the cliff in a beautiful valley with sandstone carved by wind and water. Very peaceful setting.
likes: Attraction Type: Natural caves, scenic valley

reviews_attraction.text: My second visit but still a beautiful spot. The tour was fun, and wandering the grounds even more so.  Exhibits are well-done and you get a real feel for the period.
A little too cold at the time for me, but this is a well-appointed spot that I would return to. Nice employees and just about everything I needed was there for me.
They have done a fabulous job of rebuilding the large kiva so it is more easily seen as it once may have been. Lovely walk around the grounds and displays indoors.
I loved this little spot! Lots of very interesting items I had never seen before and such friendly staff! The eaterwise garden outside is worth a visit as well.
Very interesting geologic stop on the way to Santa Fe. It was a cold day that day with snow and wind but it would be fun to take a dip in the summertime.
A bit crowded but a satisfying workout.  Views of Phoenix were vast. Plenty of parking-even for an RV and a nice visitors' center with map signage.
Small but interesting-as much for the small displays as for the history of the building and surrounding land. Super nice and knowledgeable docent.
Worth a visit. Includes an outdoor site a shirt walk away. Nicely done displays and good information including a replica of a typical dwelling.
Interesting little museum with a focus on medical civil war history. The building and grounds themselves are a museum with lots of history.
Very fun day and enjoyable ride. Food was good, drinks were good, the staff was so warm and pleasant. We had a very enjoyable afternoon.
Peaceful and interesting. Lighthouse repairs look to be almost finished. Tons of birds and wildlife. Go to relax and soak up the air.
Really cool spot! Take the time to walk all the trails and see the structures from all angles. Easy hike and extremely interesting.
Excavations and discoveries are still alive here.  It's sobering to think of the hardships and obstacles these folks had to face.

We enjoyed the Rim Trail first because we could take the dog. It gave us a great view of the canyon and the ruins and stairs from a distance.
We returned, dogless, to take the Island Trail. It was clear but windy and the views were amazing. There were lots of steps but it wasn't an issue returning to the top (I'm 63), just take your time, read the signs and enjoy the views and the ruins.
The cliff dwelling ruins were so very Interesting-just trying to imagine what life was like on these cliffs and canyon. Part of the loop was closed for trail maintenance so we had to backtrack but they said we accessed all the ruins.
I highly recommend this hike.

We went to Garden Nights Holiday Lights. I loved it. There were lights everywhere you looked. They had music in three different areas. I loved the orchestral orbs. The highlight was in the loop we walked in Nature's Wonders. We were able to walk amo g the hanging lights that changed colors with the music. It was awesome! We bought preferred tickets so we got a drink ticket and they had a nice variety to choose from. We also got 3D glasses. When you wear them, many of the lights look like snowflakes. Overall, a really nice evening.

This is a great place to bring kids. Pet-friendly. The model train club has a fun display in one of the buildings. A cool play area that looks like a pueblo and more jungle gyms. A triple slide! I've never seen that before. The gyms are for kids younger than 12. Part of the park was blocked off for the Holiday Lights train for Christmas. We will return after Christmas to ride the train and enjoy the lights.

What an interesting museum.we spent three hours here which surprised me. We did not read everything but definitely the areas that interested us the most which was the first 3/4 of the museum. The Ted Bundy exhibit was good-our interest being that we are from Washington state. A great stop for a rainy day like today or a day when you know all the other attractions will be super crowded.

My husband and I both thought this was a fun stop. They offer a sort film with the history of Mardi Gras in NOLA. Then we got to wander around the warehouse and see people working on current float props and see the steps of creation. We got to admire many props around the warehouse. Amazing artwork! We even got a piece of King Cake to try. Fun.
likes: Facilities & Services: Float prop viewing, Artwork display
Activities: Creation process observation, King Cake tasting

reviews_attraction.text: Had a good time visiting here. Take the tour, lots of info is provided and makes your visit more meaningful. Dog-friendly outside the buildings which is great for us. A little bit of everything-shops, food, displays. I found a beautiful hand-embroidered blouse and belt.

Worth a walk in the sunshine. Lots of restaurants if you like. We enjoyed the view. There's a viewing deck at the very end. From there we could see the seals in the marina and at the end of the other wharf. We also saw a sea otter eating his lunch.

A great way to get to Dry Tortugas. They provided us with a sack breakfast and lunch, and snorkle gear. Lots of info on the fort, key and snorkeling. Alcohol was available on the return trip. A fort tour was provided for those interested.

Went to the Christmas Stampede. I found it to be enjoyable but my husband enjoyed it more than me. The food was ok, the chicken came out hot. They had us seated socially distanced. The backdrop was beautiful.

Had a great wine-tasting experience here. Sat outside and enjoyed a little firepit heat as well as the wines. I hear they will have food trucks and live music on Friday nights starting very soon. What fun!

A clean, small casino. Smoke level was low although I could smell it on me when I left. A variety of machines not too many that we liked. Found a fun one before I left and it even let me win a little.
A very interesting place to stop and tour the fort and learn a little history. There are trails too but we just went to the beach. It's small but what a deal for only an $8 entrance fee.
Avery nice little park, part of it along the water. There were lookout spots that were for viewing the water. Apparently manatee come here but nothing today. Still,  ery pretty.
Loved this park. There were three separate areas for the dogs, one included the water feature. There were picnic areas outside the park and a kids play area too.
A great place for an afternoon walk. We took our dog and thoroughly enjoyed it. Saw a number of birds and a couple rabbits enjoying the sunshine.
An excellent museum. I enjoyed the space museum the most. Entrance included an IMAX movie. You've got to go at least once! See the Spruce Goose.
A great view of Emerald Bay. An interesting drive too. At one point there is a drop-off to the lake on each side of the road. A bit unnerving.
We didn't have time for the tour and I really wish we would have. A nice visit to learn more about this talented author. Love all the cats!
A good way to spend a couple hours. Loved all the dinosaur exhibits along with the history of New Mexico (we are from Washington State)
We only hiked part of the way on the dog-friendly path, but we really enjoyed it. We even spotted a tarantula walking across our path.
The building has a short film and displays. I was surprised at the involvement that Henry Ford had on Richmond Hill. An amazing man.
A very nice drive to tour with audio and pics on a website. You don't even have to get out of the car if you don't want to.

Naches Sportsman Days if fun, fun, fun!
A parade and a variety of booths and a carnival.
Good fun for all ages.
We only stopped for a quick look. There is a museum to stop in but we declined. A very nice area for a picnic.
You get a great view here. We could see all the way south to Salton Sea where we just came from.

If you want to see what money meant in the gilded age this is the place to go. Extremely ornate, huge and fun to visit. A self guided tour allows you to move at your own pace and take in as much or a little as you want. Most castles in Europe don't have the detail and high level of ornate trappings that you can find here. My favorite of all of the mansions found in Newport.

This was pretty inspiring, to think back about the people that lived here and made it work in the middle of what appears to be nothing.  But the most amazing part of the visit was when my son recognized that there was an absolute silence, no sound of any type.  No insects, no wind, no people, no engines, absolute silence.

It's a bit hilly if you struggle with walking, but they have a good assortment of animals and exhibits. All of my grandchildren really enjoy coming here.
ADDITION
Just did the drive through here and it was outstanding. It was really well done and my granddaughters were so excited.

We went here for the annual luminary remembrance. It was an overpowering experience, one luminary for each of the more than 23,000 dead, injured, or missing. It was an hour wait to get in but well worth it. You drive along the designated road through rows upon rows of candles.

I found it to be very educational and helpful to understand what happened here by visiting. Most of us have heard snippets of this event, but this whole visit put a spin on it and helped me to truly understand what happened here. Well worth the visit if you enjoy history.

I really liked the layout of this zoo.  They made it easy to see everything and the people were very helpful and friendly.  I had some nice conversations with a fee different workers.  My wife rented a power wheelchair for herself and it all made for a great day.

A really nice museum, only $6. If you are into colonial history this is a great place to visit on Boston's Fees Trail. The old South meeting house is where the planning stage for the Boston tea party took place.
Every National Park I visit gets 5 stars. There is always a reason they were designated as National Parks. This one had great views of the painted desert and petrified wood to boot.
It's been a few years but I remember this as a nice, quiet, catch your breath spot after leaving the Grand Canyon. Just very peaceful and a nice change of scenery for an easterner.
A really nice state park with lots of options. There is swimming, kayaking, canoeing, fishing, picnicking, hiking, and large fields for playing. A nice beach but no lifeguards.
It feels like history comes alive here. There is so much to see, absorb, and process. The workers are extremely knowledgeable and we learn something new every time we visit.
Summer 2018. We always enjoy the ride through the Bighorn Mountains on the way to Cody and Yellowstone. Spectacular views off the east side, great scenery, and wildlife.
A nice park with some good hiking. The trail to the top of the cliffs is a good one. And the view from the top is very cool. Especially in the fall at foliage time.
This is a stunning gem that I was unfamiliar with. Great spot on a peninsula, surrounded by water on threee sides. And a cool Lighthouse right in the middle.
I brought my grandchildren here for the playground and they had a great time. There is a large variety of things to do for all ages. Nice job Killingly.
Summer 2018. My favorite area of the park. I have seen grizzlies, wolves, elk, and bison here. The bison traffic jams make for great entertainment.
Met a wonderful woman and she was extremely helpful.  I found the snowy owl I was looking for. Return trip in September and just a beautiful area.
My granddaughter and I toured the mansions and this was her favorite. She really liked everything about this one. Well worth visiting.
I have always enjoyed the history of the Oregon Trail. Visiting here really helped to put a new perspective on the whole thing for me.
Really nice spot along the Ocean Drive. Great for kite flying, ocean viewing, and walking on the rocky shore. Plenty of free parking.
I'd be hard pressed to think of a place in Utah, outside of cities, that didn't deserve a five. Just a spectacular outdoor state.
This like almost all National Parks was amazing.  The nice views but the amazing trees just made this a great experience.
First off,a really rough road to get here. But some nice hiking trails and a scenic pond but no swimming allowed.
I've never been here during beach season but off season is great. Lots of birds, great views, nice walking areas.
I didn't go in to visit. I couldn't resist using the space shuttle or front for a math lesson into.

This is a pretty remarkable experience. The park is very accessible, and can be enjoyed almost entirely from a car and veery short walks. It would be nicer if there were more hiking options and "off the beaten trail" sightseeing options. The landscape is remarkable, but if you've been to the Badlands before, this is a very unnoteworthy setting (except for the plethora of petrified wood).

During our trip, we found multiple tourists who were raiding artifacts. We called police, and were shocked to find out no park Rangers were working and the county police wasn't going to confront the individuals. The old adage "Thai is why we can't have nice things" is spot on when it comes to some unthoughtful tourists who go off paths and steal artifacts.

If it's your first time visiting, I suggest you start in the north and work your way south. The north has more history and the south has more things to see. (you can certainly start in the south, but by the time you get further north, it will be anticlimactic).

Be sure to bring a set of binoculars. There are petroglyphs and wildlife that is much easier to see with a pair of binoculars aiding you.

Note: if you want a souvenirs, there is petrified wood sold at multiple nearby stores for a very reasonable price. In fact, one such store at the southern entrance gives you a free piece of petrified wood just by visiting the store.

Don't let my 3 star review fool you, this is a neat museum and worth the trip. I just believe the museum is overrated. The bird show was neat, but does not live up to its hype. The grounds are nicely landscaped, but you honestly can get a similar experience for free at a nearby national park hiking on a trial. The highlight of the museum is the hummingbird exhibit. You get to see them up close. Absolutely an amazing experience. Overall, it's worth a trip here, but have measured expectations. The cost of admission is somewhat pricey. Check out what live presentations/shows they have before you go. The presentations generally appear more geared to adult audiences, however, kids will still enjoy aspects of them.

For a small town, this is a fabulous gem, particularly on a rainy day. Their hours are a little bizarre (open only 10am-4pm, Tuesday through Saturday; closed on Sunday and Monday). The building is relatively new and there's lot of animals to see. Their exhibit on pollinaters/bees was well done. There's a nice garden in the back along with a few live birds. Parking is sparse (street parking only), but the museum is not very crowded.

Staff was friendly and welcoming. Cost was very reasonable. Kids are free, adults are $5. Everyone is free on Tuesdays.

The reason for only 4 stars is that the stuffed animals could have better information about them (eg their range, habitat, facts about them, etc).
likes: Facilities & Services: Friendly staff, reasonable cost
dislikes: Facilities & Services: Limited parking, limited hours
Cultural Value: Inadequate information on exhibits

reviews_attraction.text: There are some hiking trails here along with an educational center. Restrooms are available (and open). There is a boardwalk available for some of the walk. Areas of the trails can be flooded, so bring good footwear. You can get lost, so bring your phone with GPS or a map. There was not much wildlife to see other than some birds, but that could have been a function of noisy groups around me.

This museum is free to the public and has many ancient art and artifacts. Of particular interest is some of the old combat armor, mummies, hieroglyphics, and two Fabrege eggs. The museum is not very large. You need about 30 minutes to briskly walk through the exhibits, or 60 minutes if you're on a more leisurely pace. Some of the informational signage could be improved with more detail.

This is a neat trip that will take you about 20-30 minutes. There are some informational signs. There is a small gift shop. You do have to pay an entrance fee of $10 per adult. There is "free" parking. The fee is too high for the experience in my opinion. We had national park pass, but forgot the card and showed our email, which the staff refused to accept. Pretty frustrating...

This is a small reserve and relatively overlooked by others (very few people are ever there). There are some burial mounds, historical signs, and observation deck. There is a small parking lot (for about 10 cars), and pavilion. Free admission. Note there are no bathrooms available. We saw wildlife, including great blue Herron, spoon bills, and egrets.

$10 admission gets you into this absolutely stunning state park. There are lots of hiking trails. The park is well upkept and clean. Park is open dawn to dusk. There is sufficient parking available and plenty of diverse rocks and formations to see. This is a perfect day trip. Consider bringing a cooler with food and drink for a picnic.

This is a very unique spot in Phoenix. It's not as large as you may expect. It's a peaceful experience and we'll upkept. The admission price is steep for what you get, but it's definitely worth seeing at least once. The koi in the pond are the highlight. The tranquil setting can be interrupted by screaming kids at the nearby park.

The Pueblo is pretty delapidated, but there is enough evidence if the walls to give you an idea of some of the borders of the Pueblo. The real highlight of this stop, however, are the petroglyphs. There are multiple helpful informational signs to help orient you. There is a restroom available at the parking lot.

Amazing overlook of one of the largest deposits of petrified wood in the world. This used to be one of the first stops of travelers 140 years ago when the railroad came through. Lots of history here. See if you can spot the tree protruding from the bank. How much of the petrified tree is under the bluff?

The arch is more impressive than I anticipated. This is a quick 5 minute stop for photo opportunities. There is on street parking available at no cost. I wish there was more informational signage about the area and arch. The arch towers over you. You also have a nice view of the river.

Mill has undergone a fresh $3 million renovation. 4 floors of history. Museum guide gave a helpful (and free) talk about how the mill worked. Take a step back in history to explore this gem. A visit takes as little as 10 minutes. You can also learn more about Rock creek there as well.

There are two highlights here at this park. The first is the nature hike near the northwest end of the park. The second is the fort itself and seeing the big guns. Lots of history here. You can also find plenty of pick nick areas, parking and fishing spots. It's a $5 entrance fee.

Friendly and helpful staff. The staff proactively provided great suggestions of things to see and do nearby. The facility is well upkept. There are bathrooms onsite. There is no fee for entrance (aka entrance is free). There is a small gift shop in the visitor center.

A gem. Free zoo. Takes about an hour to walk around and see all the animals. Animals are close to you for easy viewing. Zoo is undergoing a major renovation right now that is set to be completed in 2020. Polar Bear and giraffe exhibits are the highlights.

A nice small beach and swimming area. The lake leaves something to be desired (very green), but the kids swimming don't seem to mind. There are several Porta potties available and a small parking lot. There is a covered picnic area and small playground.

Beautiful area with lots of hiking options. Volunteer guides are friendly and knowledgeable. Entrance fee is $5/day or $10/week. You can also get an annual membership for. $20. There are a variety of hiking trails. Most are easily navigable.

A nice park, that is surprisingly large. It's free to get in. There are public restrooms. The kids have a playground and love the trains. During the holidays, they have a large number of lights on the trees.
A park with a few benches and some statues/artwork. The park is not as well upkept as it could be. Benches could use some new paint. There are oak trees throughout the park that offer shade.
These are pretty impressive ruins. The cost of entry is currently free. The ruins are called Casa Grande, named after the first Spanish explorer who discovered the abandoned site.
A neat short walk. I wish there were more placards with descriptions of the history. There is a handicapped accessible walkway on top of the battery on the south side.
A nice short hike. It honestly isn't anything overwhelming or interesting, although there are some good informational signs and you can see the river.
A nice large park with plenty of parking. There are some mature trees that provide shade. A beach volleyball court, playground and picnic benches.
This is a neat and short hike. There could be a few more informational signs along the more rusty hike area.

This is a great way to spend a few hours north of Flagstaff learning about the Native Americans who called this part of the Southwest home. Take the time to drive the full 34 mile loop from Sunset Crater to the main Wupatki Visitor Center and ruins. I recently stopped by after it had snowed and the road had been plowed. The ruins are even more beautiful with a light snow covering.  There are several ruins to visit along the drive and many that we can only look at. The Visitors Center is full of great information and also gives us the Hopi history. Look to the east and see the Painted Desert in the distance and to the west, the San Francisco Peaks. The path around the main ruins is dirt and has several inclines, I'm not sure a wheelchair could make it unless there were people to help?  Stop for a moment and listen to the desert sounds and look at how they wrapped the pueblo around the rock formation. If this was a main trade center then think of how busy it must of been. Definitely stop at the wind tunnel next to the ball court. The bathrooms are on the outside on the front of the building  and are always clean. This is high desert so take water, a hat, sunscreen and good shoes and most of all, enjoy!
likes: Facilities & Services: Informative Visitor Center, clean bathrooms
Activities: Exploring ruins, scenic drive, listening to desert sounds
dislikes: Facilities & Services: Inaccessible path for wheelchairs

reviews_attraction.text: I came late in the day on a Saturday (3:15pm). I found no one working in the visitors center. I walked the mile trail down to the viewing point for Betatakin and again saw no one working for the park to get answers for my questions. I got back to the visitors center at 4:07 and the door was locked and the closed sign was up. Even though this National Park is located in Arizona, they go by day-light savings time. My advice is to make sure you get to the park early in the day if you want to see the exhibit inside the visitors center. The restroom are on the outside of the building and were still open after they closed the visitors center.  The trails are not open year round, they open on April 15th. Make sure you have the information as to which trails you need to have a guide. This is an amazing park and to see where they built their pueblos and learn about their beliefs is a must for anyone who loves the Southwest. The paved path to the observation area has some inclines so I would have to say that if there were additional people to help someone in a wheelchair, the path would be user friendly.
dislikes: Facilities & Services: Staff Availability, Visitors Center Hours

reviews_attraction.text: I haven't been to this site in a very long time so we packed our lunch and headed out from Phoenix. We went to Globe on US 60 then turned on 188.   We stopped at the lookout approximately one mile south of the park entrance and were able to photograph the Cliff Dwelling from that spot. We then headed to the park.  To get to the Upper Cliff Dwelling, you will need to reserve a spot on a guided tour. Its 3 miles and takes 3 to 4 hours. The Lower Cliff Dwelling is situated behind the Visitors Center and is 1 mile round trip. The walkway is steep so take your time and there are places to stop. Make sure you are prepared to hike up by wearing good shoes, a hat, suntan lotion and plenty of water. Even in the cooler temperatures, the sun's rays bouncing of the rocks is hot! I did visit the park again and was able to hike to the Upper Cliff Dwelling. There are some steep steps over rocks so I do suggest using hiking poles if you have them. Take your time and you will make it to the top!

Currently the trail is the only thing open but there is no fee. There are no restrooms open on site at this time. It is a great time of the year to stop and walk the trail and its quiet do to very few visitors. This museum is close to the heart of Phoenix and it reminds us that this same area was home to Native Americans as well.  When it reopens, take the tour of the canals and imagine what it must have been like to have built them with the tools they had. There is a map on the inside of the building which shows where many of the pueblos have been found and think about how closely modern culture has built in the same areas. The large pueblo and surrounding structures offer us an insight to how they lived. The staff and volunteers are friendly and knowledgeable. The activities and lectures are interesting and well worth the trip!

This was my first visit to the Yuma Territorial Prison and WOW, I can't believe what the prisoners endured there. It couldn't have been easy to be a guard as well. All I can say is that you need to make sure you take the time to walk the grounds and listen/read the stories about life in the prison. I did go into the Dark Cell and didn't get goosebumps but it would be a great place to spend Halloween night! I did end up with one odd photo. not sure how it happened but it will be a great story. Don't miss the cemetery which is a short walk to the east of the parking lot. You can also walk down to the Wetlands to look for birds and animals. Plan on at least 2 hours to get through everything. Carry water and wear a hat, this is Arizona!

No where in the state do you see this high of a concentration of saguaros. This park is set up in the mountains and foothills so you can see over the valley and mountains to the north. There are hiking paths as well as roads to drive on. The visitors center is limiting the amount of people inside so plan on waiting a bit to get in. The information pamphlets are outside to pick up and there were 2 Park Rangers outside answering questions. The restrooms were open and clean. Take time to look at the wildlife that lives on or in the saguaros. It helps to have a pair of binoculars handy! Bring a hat, good walking shoes, camera, and suntan lotion. This is the desert so have plenty of water.

This was our first visit to Goldfield. We were there early to get photos before the crowds arrived, then sat down to cinnamon rolls from the bakery as we watched a red-tailed hawk circle the sky above us.  Plan on spending at least 4 hours here if you are going to go through the exhibits. We spent $40 a person for the exhibits and had a great time. The employees are friendly and knowledgeable. The Sun Valley has a rich history in mining and Superstition Mountains are very much a big part of it. Due to the paths being dirt inclines, I'm not sure how wheelchairs would do here. Wear a hat, carry water, wear good walking shoes, and if your lucky, maybe you'll see a ghost or two!

This is a nice stop. Make sure you go through the museum in the main building which is south of the white picket fence. Unlike Fort Bowie, this fort has 3 of the original buildings. AZ State Parks has done a wonderful job of placing antiques in the building and the uniforms displayed in the main museum are wonderful. This is your chance to see a nice display about the Buffalo Soldiers and the Apache Scouts who contributed so much to the AZ way of life. The Camp Verde jail is just to the west of this so take the time to walk over to it. There is also an Archeology building to the west of the jail on the corner. Another great place to stop and see historical items

This was my first visit to Tumacacori and I was not disappointed. The Park staff was so wonderful to me! I got there early in the morning and was informed I needed to start inside the sanctuary because the morning sunlight was perfect for photos. I am very thankful for that information! I couldn't believe how many species of birds I saw in the garden area but also around the grounds. Go slow. be quiet and it will be amazing what you can see.   We should be thankful for all of the restoration work that has gone into this site so it lasts for future  generations. This is Arizona history! This is the desert so wear a hat, take suntan lotion, water, and a camera.

The San Pedro House is a part of the San Pedro Riparian Conservatory. Stop at the house and get a map of the trails.  Make sure you have a camera, water, good shoes, and a hat for hiking the trails. It's very peaceful and lots to see. I visited when the caterpillars had just hatched and the "Birders" said the migrating birds were due in a week.   There were several bird watchers on the trail that were willing to point out interesting birds in the trees. The trail is not wheelchair friendly but I would suggest you stop, visit the original home and see the area around the home. Bring a pair of binoculars to watch the birds.

Google sent us to the south side of the canal the first night so the next night we parked at 40th St and Camelback to walk on the trail on the north side of the canal. The area is fenced off and marked so you can't miss it. A wheelchair can make it in, just remember the trail is sand. There are no available restrooms. Mexican Free Tail Bats can fly up to 60 mph so photos are tough to take, try making a video of them. We got there about 30 minutes prior to sunset which was perfect. You will walk back in the dark so take a flashlight. This is a child friendly event each night in the summer and is amazing to watch.

Its hard to describe how beautiful this mountainous area is. it is well worth the drive. I suggest you stay in Wilcox and drive early in the morning to this area. Remember you are hiking around rocks so the temp will be warm as the sun rays bounce off the rocks. Carry lots of water and a camera. There are several great hikes so stop at the ranger station to have them help you decide which trail is best for your needs. Don't miss driving to the top (Sugarloaf)  to get an amazing view of the terrain. Plan a whole day here, more if you are camping!

This was my first visit to this site. the signs were easy to follow when you leave state route 8 and head north. Take time to read the signs at the site to see the history of the site and the area around it. Please do not destroy or remove anything from the site, none of it can be replaced! I suggest you get to the site early in the morning or around sunset since the petroglyphs are hard to photograph when the sun is overhead. The restrooms are clean and the path is accessible for wheelchairs.. This site will take about an hour to see.

Beautifully set next to Saguaro National Park, Sonora Desert Museum offers a variety of exhibits to explain the delicate balance of life in the Sonora Desert. Most of the paths are gravel but level enough for a wheelchair with help. The restrooms are clean and there are plenty of them.  I ordered a breakfast burro at the Café which was large and filling. Take time to watch the wildlife throughout the site, while enjoying the exhibits. I enjoyed every minute I spent here! Wear good walking shoes, take a hat, water, and suntan lotion.

The correct address for the museum is 17 South 2nd Ave, Phoenix, AZ 85003. Its on the south side of the Maricopa County Courthouse. If you are downtown, take the time to stop by and see the museum. The staff is friendly and loves chatting with the guests. The museum is set up well, including the first helicopter that PPD owned. I was fortunate enough to have gone on a day one of the first pilots who flew that helicopter was working. So many great stories about the amazing people who wore the Phoenix Police uniform.

If you stop by the Arizona Falls to see some history of the Arizona Canals, make sure you pack a lunch and enjoy GR Herberger Park which is connected to the Falls. The parking is to the west of the park and I always find a place to park. There are ramadas, tennis courts, volley ball, and lots of green grass to play on. There are restrooms. Arizona Falls is just to the east and you can walk the banks of the canal to enjoy the view or read about the history of the canals. This is a wheelchair friendly site!
likes: Facilities & Services: Wheelchair accessibility, Restrooms, Ramadas

reviews_attraction.text: I used to own a home across the street from this Park. I watched the City of Glendale work hard to get it to the Historical Site it is today. Not only are the original ranch buildings here, there is a play area, huge area for families and groups to cook and athletic fields. There is access to the library to the north and Glendale collage is to the South.  They continue to have a large group of peacocks as well which is a delight for all ages.

I've been going to Lake Pleasant for 40 years and still find the lake and the mountains beautiful. I don't go on busy days and I have found the restrooms pretty disgusting but that's from people who visit the park and dont care. I watch the website to review the events scheduled in cause I see something I want to try. This is the desert so bring lots of water, suntan lotion and a hat. And I bring a roll of toilet paper and hand sanitizer.

For those of us who were involved with people in New York that day, this memorial was a surprise! Just seeing a small part of the building brings back a flood of memories of that event.  I thought Gila Bend did a beautiful job in the design of the memorial and when you pass through this wonderful town, take a few minutes to stop at the 911 Memorial. Thank you to all who made this possible!

Its a little out of the way but well worth the trip. I've been here many times over the years but still am amazed on the size of pueblo and what it might have looked like at the height of its glory. The land around it is also beautiful. You can see Jerome from this site. The Park Rangers are friendly and knowledgably of the history of the area.

There is so much of Arizona's history based in Tombstone. Spend the money and get a tour of the town and spend the $7 to go through the Courthouse. Look at all of the artifacts and definitely take time to see the side yard and gallows! Imagine what it was like to live there during the 1880's! Make sure you carry a bottle of water with you!

Each time I visit this park, I am amazed with its beauty. The area is rich with historic sites and Ranger Kevin does an amazing job with passing information out during his hikes. Everyone who I've come into contact with while at the park have been friendly. Its definitely worth the time to visit.

It was nice to be able to walk next to the Colorado River. I was hoping to see a variety of birds but it was warm the day I visited so I'm sure they were hiding. I was surprised with the amount of trash and dog feces on the ground but that's visitors faults for not taking pride in the park.

I've used this rest stop for photos as much as the restrooms. It has a beautiful view of the mountains and sometimes we've stopped because it will have snow in the winter. The rest rooms are usually clean and the grounds/picnic areas are picked up.
Definitely worth the trip to see the amazing sculpture pumpkins. There is lots of food and some crafts this year!

First it was an awesome building..Any organization that repurposes historical buildings is commendable...broad variety of exhibits...the Aboriginal display was unique as was the Oceanic display of wood carvings. Large collection of Buddahs was very interesting and the Ming dynasty collection of figurines, sculptures and vases was also top notch.. Hats off to the schools that brought classes in to view and learn about the exhibits...👏👏👏

Nice park right on the ocean...it was cold (freezing winds with rain) while we were there and was disappointed in the condition of the bath house in section 3. No heat at all. Doors to showers were sprung and difficult to close. Thankfully the new bath house in section 1, made the stay much more enjoyable...campground was clean,,, beaches were fantastic..we walked on them daily...

Amazing place..the drive out on the causeway was beautiful as the mountain had a nice reflection. Quickly greeted by buffalo on the drive out to the ranch. The Frary homestead was quite a remote location to raise a family. The ranch was nicely preserved and had many artifacts from it's heydays.

Amazing experience..The docents were very knowledgeable about the history of the missile site. Special thanks to Bob and Ken. We took the  Blast door tour and accessed the bottom of the Missile Silo. Plenty to see and photograph...wish there was a little more time on the tour to allow for that.

Awesome park on the Arroyo Colorado...Staff was friendly, courteous and helpful. VERY attentive to keeping facility tidy and  in order...we experienced fishing from our campsite...the howl of coyotes at night,,,turkey and owl calls in the early morning and viewed some amazing sunrises.

Visitor center was very informative and helpful to us as we were looking for a trail suitable for dogs...we saw our first green Jay  and the staff was very friendly and courteous. Hope the next time we visit we can drive the trail around the lake in hopes of seeing an ocelot...

Unbelievable!!! We were so taken in by the art museum and the grounds that we never made it to the circus exhibits...staff was courteous on arrival..and the security personnel throughout the displays were friendly and informative...Truly a treasure and worth a return visit...

Absolutely the best NM State Park around. Where else can you camp and fish at your campsite. Park rangers were friendly and helpful. Be sure to spend some time near the Palisades, no shortage of picnic areas, day use spots and places to park to fish the stream...

Remarkable efforts by the Edmund family, Don, Dona and Linda made this a memorable visit...so much knowledge shared about the history of this silver mining town was very interesting and enlightening...could easily spend more time there to absorb it's aura..
A marvelous mission that is nestled in Carmel by the Sea..buildings and grounds are well maintained and cared for. Bountiful opportunities for photographing a piece of California history..
A Colorado iconic landmark. Colorful and picturesque...the trails and loop drive are a perfect way to see the highlights of the park. Well maintained and clean..Hats off to management..
Wierd, magical and very strange place to visit..with the slab city next door, it reminded me of a Mad Max movie set...a creative, spiritual man made this all possible..
Beautiful trails, plenty of waterfowl, the Comal Spring is an interesting phenomenon...awesome place for walking dogs. AND incredibly clean and very well maintained...
Awesome museum!! Photography exhibits were unbelievable... Building itself was even an art form...too much to see in one day..a definite return trip..
Cool place..the power of the river is amazing...lots of fisherman nearby...be cool to see how much water goes through here in the springtime thaw...
Amazing place that we have already revisited. Loop drive is well worth the time to see the cacti sentinels up close. Plenty of photo opportunities
Awesome place for a dog walk... interesting view along the river convergence. Alarming number of homeless people meandering through the park
A pitstop along the beautiful Logan Canyon Scenic drive...interesting story about how they discovered where the water actually comes from...
Nice place to walk our dogs, a bit disappointed in the cost to enter the park..$12 is not a value for what services are provided...
Day trip to this area and a perfect spot to walk the dogs..Amidst the COVID chaos, people were mindful of social Distancing...
Been there a couple times for early morning dog walks...peaceful.. well maintained services and a nice place for the dogs...
Loved it...Friendly staff, nice museum and well stocked gift store. Lots of merchandise on sale so we loaded up on goodies..
Cool but not what we expected...overcast skies didn't help...guess I should have done a little more exploring in the park
Nice park, shameful that people have to trash it out. Never understood why people don't clean up after their dogs... 😞😞
Cool experience...elevator ride was cozy and the view from the top was amazing. interesting story how it came to be..

Bryce Canyon should be on your short list of places to visit when you plan tour the National Parks and Monuments of Southern Utah and Northern Arizona. There is so much natural beauty and so much variety. The colors and shadows shading the nature sculpted Hoodoos are breathtaking. In the earlier part of regular visitor season, the weather can be changeable and quite unpredictable making the possibility of seeing even more variety most likely. I've visited when it was hot, dry and sunny, when it was cool and damp, and when there were snow squalls blowing through. It was beautiful each time!

It's fun to see the Great Wheel grace the waterfront now. But this is a relatively new attraction and it's one aimed directly at tourists, whether local or from afar it doesn't matter. Not that it's a bad thing, just that it and the other newer attractions should not distract you from seeing all Seattle has for you to enjoy. So, yes, take a ride on the great wheel, enjoy the view and the experience, but check the Pioneer Square area too and perhaps the Seattle  Underground.

I hiked in the Palm Canyon area and throughly enjoyed it. The rugged starkness of the desert is beautiful in it's own right. The canyon is home to Arizona's only naturally occurring palm tree species...the California Fan Palm. The hike up the canyon to see the few palms is easy enough at the start, but be prepared to do quite a bit of scrambling as you near where the palms grow.

I enjoy taking in places with historical significance. When I was in the Yuma area, that meant a visit to the old Territorial Prison. The time there was informative and entertaining both. The site barely resembles the original prison, but with some imagination and the displays available, you are able to piece it together. All Arizonans should visit.

Blue Heron Park is the former Moses Lake State Park. The city now has it and it is improved since the transition. Several improvements have made the park more usable and fun for visitors of all ages and interests. Fishing, disk golf, boating, new playground equipment for youngsters and a swimming beach are among the things to enjoy at the park.

A beautiful off the beaten path National Monument. I highly recommend a visit if you plan to be near the area. There are a number of interesting sites to visit in the Four Corners region. From ancient native american and historic settler sites to natural wonders, come check them out! You'll be glad you did.

Educational and informative. I have been by here a few times with family and it has been fun each time. This last time I had my eldest daughter an my parents with me. Dad was in a wheelchair and was able to enjoy the visit as well, though the accessable view points from the rim were limited.

Good views of the area but especially the distant landscape. The downtown Seattle area is too close to really enjoy from this vantage. Still, viewing the city from here gives a new perspective on Seattle. I prefer the view from the Space Needle....but that is just my personal preference.

I was on AMTRAK's Coast Starlight as I passed through the area of the Los Padres National Forest. The National Forest lands deserve to be explored. I have enjoyed hiking the hills here in the past, enjoying the scenery changes as I made my way to the coast. Beautiful!!!

The view from the SkyView Observatory was great but I prefer the view from the Space Needle. I would think on a clear day the view would be better or at least further. Still I don't regret the cost to take in the view from the highest observation area in Seattle.

A nice public park with a better than average playground. My grandkids and I enjoyed an hour at Bonneville Park this evening. There were plenty of active toys to keep them going and entertained for the time we were at the park and beyond.

Beautiful spot and interesting sculpture honoring all the Forefathers of all Americans. They all came here looking for a better life for themselves and their descendants. We should all be helping make that dream a reality.

Not disliked, but was disappointed. Could not take in the visitor center... it's closed Tuesdays and Wednesdays. No mention of this in the online material I researched prior to this trip. Just a sign placed on the door.

Beautiful asian garden. Now, the maples, in particular, are beautifully colored. The garden is smaller and will often fill up when weather is more conducive to a visit, but it is worth making plans to drop in..

I did enjoy visiting the dunes and camping here as well. Three stars indicates my expectations were met as I visited. Disappointment results in loss of stars and pleasantly surprising visits earn added stars.
I always enjoy a visit here when I am up through Baker City. I especially liked the displays commemerating the 50th anniversary of the filming of Paint Your Wagon in the mountains outside of town.
I love to learn the history about places, and that makes all the ruins in the Verde River area fascinating. There is still so much mystery surrounding this people. Always an interesting visit.
The landscape is so different here. These are ancient, now petrified, dunes. A rough area to traverse before the road was completed through it. Until 1948, mail was delivered by mule.
The entire Seattle Waterfront is a destination for me when I visit Seattle. This visit I got this pic of the ferry Puyallup as it approached the Coleman Dock nearby.
Not crowded...that was great. But it is Monday so you would not expect it to be very busy. The lake is picturesque enough, but services are lacking.
I enjoyed the whole experience while at the Pima Air and Space Museum including the 390th. It delivered as I expected it to and was informative.
We had a family get together here. The park is a decent place...large enough and with enough facilities to be a good gathering place.
Always a walking destination when I'm visiting my daughter here in Kenmore. The views from out on the pier can be quite spectacular.
Another of the natural wonders located in the Southwest United States. Monument Valley is a stunning display of nature's artistry.
I love Olympic National Park! From the mountains to the tide pools, there is so much to enjoy and explore.

Tucked away just southwest of Golden Gate Bridge is a gem called Lands End Labrynth. In all the time I've lived in northern Cali I never stumbled across this place until now. I stumbled across it while looking for beaches to go to and found one of the most beautiful spots I've seen in the San Fransisco area.

There is a short hike down to the lookout/beach of which it has both. The beach is a epic little sand beach with very little traffic and some of the most beautiful landscapes you get to see from Cali. Right next to that is Lands End and a constructed stone labyrinth. The view from this low cliff looking back at the Golden Gate is surreal. Pictures looked like the backgrounds were paintings.

Worth every second of the visit and short hike. If you are near Golden Gate, take some time and intentionally make this stop. You will not regret it.

Absolutely perfect for all you hiking needs. Love this place and all the hiking options it offers. It's a good idea to research just a bit before you go so that you know what trail options they have. Whether you're a novice or hardcore, they have options for you. The river is dope if you just want to chill as well. It gets super hot and dry here in the summer and poison oak is abundant (just like all northern California hiking spots), so make sure to plan ahead, stay hydrated and watch your step. Enjoy!

Absolutely breathtaking. Whether you are day hiking, back packing, camping or whatever, you need to get out here. It can get pretty hot in the summer so remember sunscreen and water. Winters are snow filled with very restricted access and most areas are closed. If you haven't been and you are the outdoors type, then do yourselves a favor and go. The longer you spend and deeper you go, the more beautiful it gets so definitely plan ahead and invest some time. It's well worth it.

Super cool for what it is. It's not too much of a beach. It's in a harbor in the bay, so basically a pool, or lake. But maybe less clean water. Don't expect waves here. However, it really shouldn't be there at all, so either they brought in sand for a beach or it's just a cool spot that has it. They have beach volleyball poles and stuff, so it ends up being pretty cool. Especially good for families with small children or simply a lazy day in the sun.

Really nice park. They have a dog park area with multiple fenced areas. Lots of grace and a man made lake. Located right next to the American river. Really fun 4th of July festivities, with an amazing fireworks show.  They have a tiny petting zoo and a miniature train that's pretty cool. Good for summer days and summer nights.  There are lots of picnic tables and bbq's. Take the family, take the pets.

Cool little beach in a place where a beach doesn't seem like it should be. Really like how the strip has a beach town feel to it despite it being the edge of a bay/harbor rather then a beach per say. I really liked it. Good for a sunny afternoon with the fam, or with the girl. They have beach volley ball courts as well. I recommend it. Afternoons on a beach cruiser would be perfect.

Beautiful place for an afternoon bike ride. The bike paths are well maintained and run for miles and miles. Amazing views, shady trees, creekside and riverside stops. Bathrooms and drinking fountains all along the way. Whether you are walking running, biking, swimming, boating, fishing, kayaking, etc, etc... this is a perfect area for it.

This place is really amazing. The views of Golden Gate cannot be beaten. You are underneath the bridge so it is pretty spectacular. Tons of history here from different eras. If you are sight seeing in SF, make it a point to stop here and take it in. I promise it will take your breath away a bit and will not disappoint.

Great day hike. Very easy, so bring the dogs and kids. It's a absolutely beautiful on this trail with the forest hill bridge 700 feet above and an epic dam and waterfall at the end of the journey. I highly recommend this for all levels of hikers. There is a $10 parking cost but it is well worth it. Enjoy!

Very cool place to hike. The valley runs deep back into the mountain with gorgeous trails. Really cool old giant kilns and an epic water fall at the end of the hike. Just below the parking area is also a breathtaking beach. Definitely worth a visit and an amazing way to spend the afternoon.

Unreal place to visit. You have to make it a point to stop by here. There are literally elephant seals everywhere. They litter the beach. Seeing these massive creatures come in from and out to the sea is something else. Make it a point to visit this spot, it doesn't disappoint.

Heart Castle is so overwhelming over the top in every way. It is an absolute must see at least once as you have never seen anything like it and will never again. Don't want to say too much more, as you just need to see it. Make it a point to visit. You will not be disappointed.

Beautiful SD beach. Long sandy beaches, train tracks behind you and waves in from. Full of ambient noises from both sides. Super peaceful and gorgeous. Lots of places to post up as it is so big it never gets too crowded. Add it to your list of beach goals and enjoy!

Absolutely beautiful strip of beach here. The train runs along right behind the beach which adds a unique but very cool element to it all. Tons of beach real estate to post up in. Breathtaking on a sunny afternoon. Definitely give it a try for you beach needs in SD.

The north rim has this awesome narrow paved path that runs out maybe half a mile to a point. Cliffs on both sides and the canyon in front. An unbelievable view and much more rustic and personal than the south rim. Worth every second of the journey to get there.

Truly beautiful stretch of the river. I've ridden here, launched rafts from here, and swam here.  Great in the summer, beautiful in the winter. If you want a lazy afternoon or an epic bike ride, this isn't the worst place to end up. Enjoy!

Stopped here because the fee for Montezuma Castle also gets you in here. Really cool site. I didn't know we even had ruins like this in North America. Seems to have been a very big complex of a thriving civilization. Step back in time.
Love this park. I know it's probably messed up by today's standards. But me, and my 4 year old daughter, and a bag of bread, and all the geese and ducks in the world was epic!
Very cool and super iconic stretch of road where you can stop and literally take a walk in Forest Gump's shoes. Just a few min north of monument valley, it is worth the drive.
An absolutely beautiful stretch of mountainous land. Composed primarily of granite it is full of lakes and unmatched scenery. Perfect for hiking, backpacking and camping.
Epic national park. The rock formations here are something out of Journey to the Center of the Earth. Very cool and a must see if you are anywhere near Denver.
Beautiful piece of architecture. A highlight of Sacramento without a doubt. As a backdrop to Old Sacramento and the waterfront district it is a must see.
Breathtaking. Definitely take the time if you are around the Denver or Boulder area. There is a $25 entry fee to the park. It's worth it though.
Good place to watch the Hagan fireworks show from the other side of the river. Nice park. Has a gold course too.
Not much to it, but it is a dope little historic gold town. Cool place to walk around while visiting the river.

My review of Scottsdale Ranch park.  It is a totally amazing park with large mature shady trees to shade the many walk ways around the serenity of Desert Oak and Pine trees with plenty of picnic benches and extra large grills to accomodate lage gatherings.  You will love how clean this park is.  I think it has the best sand volleyball courts in the entire phoenix Valley.  There is parking very close to the playground but the parking lot there is very well used and is very worn with pot holes.  I loved that there was a pedestrian bridge that goes over the street for easy access to the outdoor mall across the street.  There is a Planet Fitness there, so if you are a member, you can grab a massage on their massage chairs after your park day.  There is also a preschool if you want to check you child in and also a dance studio that has a beautiful view out thier widows of the mountains there.  A the park, there is an exercise stretching station that I really enjoyed.  There were a lot of flowering desert friendly plants that gave beauty to the enjoyment of this park.

The children's playground has wood chips.  The play equipment is new and amazing.  You can rock climb, spin, slide, swing and tunnel.  The water fountain works.  The your one for your water bottle, peope and one for your 4 legged child too.  I'd say this was a Dog friendly Park.  Plenty of dogdy clean up station and trash cans.  Thle bathrooms were clean and modern.  This park is perfect for large groups.

There is a tennis center on the west most end of this park, that I believe is the largest in the Phoenix valley as well.

You will fall in love with this park.  I love all the bridges that go over the water ways.  Its designed in 3 tiers. The bottom most is sports fields, the middle is volleyball and a sensory Discover park, padded with a rubber floor, and filled with bouncy equipment.  The Daisy Mountain train goes past it and there are train crossing signs that flash lights and makes singing sounds as the train passes. Your little train enthusiast will go gaga for this park.  Next to it is a hockey courts for your rollerblade enthusiasts. And a skate park.  The top most tier has it's own separate parking lot.  Water cascades down multiple waterfalls  into 2 smaller ponds and one larger lake.  There are many picnic ramadas. Many large parties can go on at the same time.  A grand gazebo stands at the entrance to a most enchanting playground.  Your kid would never want to go home again.  Spinning, climbing, splash pad, sand pit, rubber floor. There is so much to say about this park. Tucked away in the back of the park, by the big lake is a grassy  amphitheater a quiet private picnic pavilion.  Very enchanting.
likes: Spinning, climbing, splash pad, sand pit

reviews_attraction.text:
My review of: Arizona Science Center

My children would live here if they could.  There is discount parking in the garage as long as you remember to get your parking pass validated inside.  Getting a membership here is well worth the price.  Entry is quicker. I've seen the insane line of people waiting to get in.  So come as early as you can.  It will take all day to discover all the fun in these 4 stories.  Yes, there are elevator but sometimes that is a long wait as well.

There is a cafe & gift shop.  In the corner between them is the entrance to the lunch room for those who want to pack in their lunch.

A new exhibit that has a paper airplane launcher is a big hit for my older children.  A Water works exhibit lets children see water's effects on gears, ball, water pressure and music.  Prepare for your children to get very wet as they put pipes together to guide water along paths of their own devising.

Find out what goes into making a house, how your body works, how electricity works, how rocks are formed, experience "Forces of Nature", and alternate clean energy.
likes: On-site facilities (cafe, gift shop, lunch room)
New attractions (paper airplane launcher, water works exhibit)

reviews_attraction.text:
This is a fantastic park.  Green grass, lots of barbecue grills and covered picnic ramadas and stone benches scattered everywhere.

There are two separate playground areas filled with wood chips.  One is near the beach edge where white buoys mark out the safe swimming area and the bathrooms can be found and the other over by a performer's raised stage.  The water fountains work .

I loved the mini light houses lining the beach.  Each light house was a different color.  I thought that was clever.

There were boat renal stations too.

Some of the neat things I experienced on this visit was when swimming in the lake, we saw carp and scratchy sea weed tickled our feet occasionally.  Over by the parking lot at night was saw a lot of bats busy eating mosquitoes and bugs.  I wasn't bit once by a mosquito during my visit there.  There is a really great statue of a frog to play on over by the outdoor stage.  The walk way along the beach goes all the way under the bridge.

This a a great place walk around and explore.

The Park with a Heart: My review of Granada Park.  The park has a huge grassy area around 2 large ponds that form the shape of a heart inside a desert landscape border. Parking is found on the south end of the park.  A large stature of a boy pulling the bow of a boat up the hill greets you at the park's entrance.

There are bathrooms and a sand filled playground. Many picnic benches are scattered around under the trees but none have covered pavilions. Sometimes there is a waterfall between the 2 ponds with a charming little bridge crossing over it.  There is a beautiful view of Signal butte to the north.

The area is abundant with desert wildlife, cactus wren, jack rabbits and quail.  I saw more dogs than kids at this park.  The large expanses of green fields make for great running.  The walking trails often go under the trees then out through the desert half of the park.

My review of Sereno Park: I love seeing a public park that caters to Horse lovers.  The west side of the park has hills that cut out the noise of traffic from the road The is a corralled sand field with jumping equipment there and another large open sand field near by for Equestrians. The ground squirrel holes made me nervous.  The east side borders a school.  There is a large parking lot in the center of this park where you can find decent bathrooms and a sand filled playground.  I loved the train themed play equipment.  There is a baseball field that is recessed down in the ground to give some shade there.  A cement walkway cuts straight through the park from the parking lot to the road on the North border.  There are picnic tables  under some of the trees and a few barbecue grills near by. All in all a very nice park.

My review of Tonto National Forest: There are many faces to this forest.
