There is also gift shops where many of his works can be purchased. They will ship to you if you cannot take the piece with you. We've done that twice and are very pleased with our purchases. Everything arrived in pristine condition. Ordering can also be done from his website.
Elevators are available for wheelchairs.

If you are from the area, you might recognize several local scenes. But even if you are not, come and enjoy this wonderful place and the slice of Americana that Terry Redlin's art is.

There is plenty of parking and the restrooms are lovely.

I have been to Yellowstone before, although it has been many years, and Morning Glory Pool had been one of my favorite places on the Upper Geyser Basin. I eagerly anticipated seeing it again on this trip.
It was a much longer walk than I remembered... It's 1.5 miles on the boardwalk from Old Faithful Inn.
While it was still clear and lovely, it had lost some of its beautiful blue color that gave it it's name and that set it apart for me.

When I asked about it the Ranger said that the water has cooled some because of the debris that has been thrown into it by visitors and this has partially clogged the water vent. Geysers get their color from the water temperature and the minerals in it, plus the organisms that can tolerate the heat and thrive. Greens and oranges reflect cooler water.

This caused me to respect these water features more for they are what bring people to this place. It is sad that this is happening; caused by people who think its funny. I want to see this place be around for others to enjoy, so I ask that others think about what they are doing to help keep the water features and the park pristine.

The distance between Sunset Point and Sunrise Point is just one mile, with a 34-foot gain in elevation. It is a paved trail and it is the easiest in the park. It’s part of the 11-mile Rim Trail which walks the length of the Bryce Amphitheater. We had limited time so we drove between the other  viewpoints, finding that the view remained much the same.  It was sunny and just 67° but it felt much warmer than this and the sun was bright enough to burn. The rocks hold in the heat and, as we found out, if you take a short walk down into the Amphitheater, it gets warmer fast. The pinnacles were
pretty fantastic and the colors were amazing.
The formations are called ‘hoo-doos’, but to us they look like vast armies standing at attention and ready to march at the signal. There are many trails that go down into the Canyon and they all look inviting. They go downhill, many of them quite a bit, so that means climbing uphill coming out.
Wear good shoes and provide sunshade; hats, sunglasses, sunscreen, umbrella's, etc. Bring water.

The Bridge of the Gods is a steel truss cantilever bridge that spans the Columbia River between Cascade Locks, Oregon, and Washington state near North Bonneville. It is approximately 40 miles east of Portland, and 4 miles upriver from the Bonneville Dam. It is a toll bridge operated by the Port of Cascade Locks.
We had a 'bridge lover' with us, who knows all about those terms, so this amazing bridge was something we had to stop for.
The bridge was completed and opened in 1926 at a length of 1,127 feet. The higher river levels resulting from the construction of the Bonneville Dam in the 1930's required the bridge to be further elevated in 1940 and extended to its current length of 1,856 feet.
The bridge is a toll bridge that spans the Columbia River., and is the only bridge across the Columbia between Portland and Hood River.
We did not want to cross it because we weren’t going that direction.
But we stopped and wandered around some trying to get some photos.
It was hard to get it all inside the camera.

We thought about this hard. We are older and not as spry as the younger people. And this trail is more technical than it would seem. It is 3.2 miles in length, leading from the parking pull out along Lee's Ferry Road down to the Colorado River. Lee's Ferry is a Fee Area. The trail is lightly trafficked, which means there may or not be help coming if you get stranded. The research I did states that this trail is rated as Difficult.
The trail is sand over slick rock, which makes it very slippery and the trail runs in a wash, so if a sudden rainstorm happens while people are down there, it can and will have fast-moving water, which can flood. I posted this review to point out the things that people may overlook in their desire to see this beautiful area.
There is no potable water available, and no restrooms. The rocks will hold in and reflect the heat so it could be quite warm on the trail.
The rainstorm helped us make our decision

Enter this overlook area from the Scenic Drive right across from several hotels. Parking is free at the end of the cul-de-sac and then one walks down on slick rock, aided by some rock steps and embedded hand railings. Use those, as 'slick' rock is appropriately named. If you have balance issues or if walking unaided is difficult, don't attempt the path. Wear good walking shoes.
It is possible to walk down much further than we did but however far one goes down, they must also come back up. We stopped where we could see the river after it had passed through the dam.
The rocks will reflect heat, so it will feel warmer than it actually is. This hike is best done on cooler days or in the morning. There are no facilities at this viewpoint, so take care of that first and bring a water bottle. The light is bright also. There is a shaded picnic ramada near the bottom, if you wish to haul in (and out) some picnic lunch and gear.
dislikes: Challenging for those with balance issues

reviews_attraction.text:
1919 Cafe
Our tour visited the Huntington Library and some of us gathered for lunch at the 1919 Café. I found the ordering system to be confusing and the prices too high for lunch. There are areas set up for the type of food one wants whether ethnic; Asian, Mexican, or something else. Prices are on overhead boards and if you chose the Hamburger Plate, there are slips of paper for you to indicate how you want it prepared. Fries and cheese are extra. These are cooked to order and then you decide on dessert in a different area, drinks from a third place, and pay in another. The order is called when finished. All this to avoid a wait staff, but the prices could have paid for wait persons. Then, one buses their own dishes.
The food was OK, but not worth the hassle or the cost. Nothing was special or remarkable. A disappointment.

Turret Arch is the smallest of the three arches you'll see on the Windows Loop Trail. Its part of a  castle-like rock formation that includes a spire (hence the name). There are two holes in this formation, one you can walk through and one high up on the rock face. The views of the North and South Window Arches from inside the Turret Arch are neat. The trail to Turret Arch is an ncline with only a few stairs.
Its 65 feet high and 35 feet wide, and still growing.
The trail up there is just .02 of a mile, but it climbs at a 5% grade for 61 feet. its kid friendly, but heavily enough traveled so, if like me, you don't want others in your photo, go earlier, or take turns as we did. I was not aware until afterward that one was able to walk through the arch. I now wish I had done so.

Mitchell Corn Palace is an event arena hosting concerts, conventions, and sporting events. The building is a tourist attraction in it's own right. Decorated every two years now with themed murals. Each mural is hand set with various grains, seeds, stalks, and other parts of the local farm crops. There is no fee to see the murals, inside or out. And the parking is free also. There is a nice gift shop and some snack type places in the small courtyard.
More than 500,000 people visit the Corn Palace annually, and this is the third edition in the years since 1892, as the others got outgrown.
2016's theme is 'Rock of Ages', featuring Elvis on the large side panel.
Tours are available if one is truly interested in how many and what types of materials are used.

Skyline Arch Trail is short enough to be overlooked when you are planning your trip to Arches, but the impressive rock span at the end of the short trail is worth checking out. Located near the Devils Garden Trailhead this 0.4-mile round trip hike ascends 50 feet to the base of a sandstone fin that opens in a large elevated natural arch.
A panel at the trailhead tells how a large block of sandstone fell from Skyline Arch in 1940, doubling the size of the arch overnight. Currently, the arch measures 71 feet across and 33.5 feet tall. Boulders from the collapse remain, and can be seen below the arch today.
We had limited time, so we observed this from the pull out on the road and continued toward Devils Garden.

It was a treat to see water here. The area is parched and showcases the power of water in a landscape primarily defined by its absence. There is a sand parking area on the north end of the bridge. UT St. Hwy. 95  is the route that crosses here and it is usually uncrowded. So it was nice to park and walk out onto the bridge (there is a narrow walking area) and listen to the stillness as the brown Colorado flows quietly under the bridge. It is moving quickly but it is spent from the Cataract Canyon further up stream. It's bright, hot, and dry here and the area shows this, except for the green around at the edges of the water. The bridge is almost a surprise and has a dramatic span.

It’s an easy 0.3 mile walk into the area and around the base of the rock, but because of the intense heat, we were content to view it from the trail head, where we could see it all.
The nearby plaque tells about the rock and I posted the text since its hard to see.
"Balanced Rock is a clear example of the various rock layers and their different levels of erosion. The white band of rock forming the pedestal under Balanced Rock is the softer of these and it will wear away the fastest. Currently, just the boulder at the top of Balanced Rock stands at 55 feet and weighs 3,500 tons. The smaller pinnacle to the right in the photo, broke away in the winter of 1975-76”.

As we moved along the Columbia Gorge on our Waterfall Quest, we came to Bridal Veil Falls at Mile Post 28.
The Highway passes over Bridal Veil Falls on a bridge. From a parking lot next to the highway, a winding footpath and another bridge lead to a vantage point for the falls. This was a shorter and more doable walk for us. The falls consists of two cascades in quick succession along angling rock-faces, so when there is a good amount of water the falls looks very much like its namesake. The total drop of both falls is 118-feet.
I loved the moss covered tree trunks and the cool rain forest feel here.

“Everyone should visit a Veteran's Memorial”
This is a lovely tribute to the local Veterans from all wars. It is located on the shores of Lake Kampeska, just outside of Watertown. Picnic and restroom facilities are there. There is no admission fee and it is open year round.
The Wall of Service has local Veteran's names carved into it to remember each veteran's service. It is possible to locate a family member from the area who served.The POW/MIA flag is on the far side of the memorial.
19 donated inscribed benches are located around the park to provide space to contemplate those who served

A fun and historical place to visit. This is the actual London Bridge from London, which was dismantled from it's location over the Thames River when it could not longer handle the traffic load there, and shipped to Lake Havasu City. Each block and piece was numbered and marked for location so the entire bridge could be reassembled in it's new location much like a 3-D puzzle. If you look closely some of the markings might still be visible.
It's in a great location right next to an English Hotel and in the shopping area.  Walking across it gives a great view of the harbor to the Lake.

Pleasant shaded dog park in Kingman. Easy to find on Andy Devine.
Picnic tables, and clean rest rooms with flush toilets for people, and separate fenced areas for dogs. Under 30 pounds are small and there is another area for the big boys. In the fenced atea, dogs can be off leash. They are required to be leashed elsewhere in the park.
This park is popular with people who do not have dogs as well.
There is no overnight camping allowed, otherwise the park is open all days except Thursday from 6am to midnight. Thursday it is closed from 12 noon to 1:30 for yard maintenance.

Owachomo Bridge is an example of an old age bridge. There is no water flowing underneath it and it may have a fatal crack caused by frost damage and seeping moisture, which will be its downfall. Without water, it could be called an arch. It stands 160’ high x 108’ wide. At its narrowest point, the span is just nine feet.
If you are able to stay overnight in the area, Natural Bridges has spectacular night sky views. It was named the first International Dark Sky Park by the association of the same name.

The California Science Museum is the final home for the Endeavor Space Shuttle. We came here as part of a tour group to see it. There's a lot more to the museum than just this, but this is the star attraction. We also rode the Space Mission Simulator, which was an extra charge, but rather fun. It's tame enough for most people.
This is a great activity for children as it makes learning fun, but we were all adults in our group and everyone enjoyed it.

Everyone stops here for the photos with the musicians and the flat bed Ford. We took turns posing and helping others, so they could be photographed together. it's free, outdoors and fun, and then the song that put Winslow on the map runs through your head for the rest of the day! There is enough free parallel street parking, but no restrooms.

Larb Hollow is a 9,200-foot summit. It’s quite pretty and cool and breezy up there and we were glad to find a relatively clean and working restroom of the out-house kind.
Several others were enjoying the view and many had picnic lunches.  There are no services here, it is mainly a viewpoint stop to enjoy the overlook.

The raven wasn’t afraid and didn’t want to leave.  He must be the local mascot. I’m sure he was waiting for a handout. But his beak was pretty intimidating.  Ponderosa Canyon is between Milepost 14 & 15.
It was quite windy there.
Sipapu is the Hopi Indian term for 'place of emergence'. The bridge opening measures: 220’ tall x 268’ wide. Sipapu is an example of a mature, but still healthy bridge. No water runs underneath it.

Outstanding resort for an Arizona mountain! They can compete in part with the big mountain resorts. Their snow blowing capabilities are leaps and bounds above Sunrise. Severe new lift additions ensure people get moved across the mountain. For being a small resort work a huge cliental of Phoenix, they mountain moves people around like Purgatory and has lift lines that are incredibly short for the amount of people in attendance. About the only thing that could use some work is the lack of parking. This resort had set themselves up to keep up with the growth that occurred with snow sports, well done Snowbowl! Highly recommended over Sunrise. It's unfortunate that Sunrise is no longer on part work being any completion.

This has to be one of the coolest, most undiscovered national parks I have been too. Visited during the great year of 2020, and despite the park being closed, all the lookouts and pullouts were still open. The only things closed were the hands on exhibits, the cliff dweling that you can climb through. The drive to the Mesa is absolutely gorgeous, and the history is equally fascinating and beautiful! Highly recommend a visit, even if you are just driving through. Plan on at least 3 to 4 hours for your visit, would be a really beautiful place to camp if the park is open. You will not regret the stop.

My favorite ski resort and town of them all. Lots of people movers, you can get across the mountain quick and skiable terian for all levels spread out. They're is a spot for everyone here. I will say, lift and resort prices are getting out of hand, it costs a fortune to bring your family and but the direction season passes are going is really positive. No longer is skiing just a once a year thing! You can truly bundle and make it a season long enjoyment for the whole family. Check out the Epic mountain pass, they are more partnering with resorts in several states!

An absolute Gem North East of Carefree! The water is flowing with a fairly strong current, water is clear and clean, you will regret not taking the time to explore this area! This had to be one of my favorite spots I have found in Arizona! A short 2 to 3 hour drive down 37 miles of dirt road, would not recommend a car, most definitely an SUV, but do take the time. A gorgeous bridge connect the 2 sides of the Verde River that hello facilitate getting livestock across the torrent of a river, work not much offering for river crossing any other way.

The cutest little park in this neighborhood. A small pond with a walkway the wraps around the whole park. And dozens of juvenile trees have recently been planted. This is truly a little gem in this neighborhood. Or only complaint was the excessive amount of pigeons. That may be due to the fact that it's summer, and the pandemic, so the park has probably remained pretty empty, but these pigeons had taken over the prime seating benches at the waters front, and as such, the benches were covered in gallons of bird $#!+. We will be returning!

Something special! When you stand between the group of trees, you with feel incredible energy, they're is something mythical, and spiritual to stand by these Giants that have experienced and lived an unreliable amount of years. Highly recommend you either go early, or later in the day, and make sure it's a week day. You want to experience The magic of this place by yourself. When you are buried in a incredible large group of people, all trying to take pictures, it makes and ruins the magic that exists with these gentle giants.

Great party with as perfect how of the sunset and beach! Trees are perfect for slack lining, the banyon trees provide incredible shade, and the park backs up right to the ocean. Perfect for a late afternoon stroll. Whole parking is only available along the street, there is a lot and you rarely have to wait. If you want to see the green flash, this park will not let you down. There is also public restroom and a delicious grill with lots of fresh drinks

Really cool little stop, and beautiful area for camping. I would highly recommend camping here between May and September as during the summer months, you can explore the Mammoth Cave. During the winter months, October through April, it is closed off as bats are hibernating to protect them through the winter months. These labs y tubes are fascinating and it's hard to believe that labs flowed through this stress at some point in Earth's history.

Nice late afternoon or evening getaway. Ample parking, dogs allowed miles of trails, and a popular sunset watching spot. On a typical evening you can get a beautiful view of the city with a gorgeous glowing sunset sky backdrop! We love visiting this area after long days. Of course, we typically avoid it during the hot summer months. You will not regret visiting this Phoenix jem that's in the heart of the city!

Love this beach, it's narrow long and shallow work reef, but the beach sand is perfect. This beach is typically only filled with locals and is empty on the week days. Weekends parking can be a bit of a pain. If you want to go snorkeling, this beach is for you, if you want to swim in the deep, about it. It is shallow and doesn't get deeper than waist deep for a ways and is mostly reef.

Love this beach, the same is perfect for barefoot, and there is nothing but sand as you water in deep into the ocean water. This side is however very susceptible to cloudy days, you need to plan on going when the winds are blowing from the north to get afternoon sunshine! One of my favorite beaches for extended hours. Worth more than a quick stop to this beach!

The thing is as huge as it appears. Well worth a nice stroll down to the end. Be aware, however, for such a dog friendly town, dogs are not allowed on the beach or the pier. But fear not for there is plenty of room to walk down the beach walk with your beloved animal. I personally though the route from the pier up to the San Clemente Casino was the best views.
dislikes: No dogs on beach or pier

reviews_attraction.text: Had a great time, big park, eat the street is very spread out, lots of room to grow. Definitely miss the beer garden. Nice park for hosting the venue, great shade trees and ample parking. The head is quality great with no burs and lots of room to run, play games, anything. A bit of a homeless camp across the street but no body bothered is while we were there.

It's the tourist thing to do... Not that exciting to see, especially if you don't like crowds... One of those things you must see when in San Francisco, but way over rated. Beautiful houses and drive, but it's a bit too much with the sight seears. I'd hate to be one of the home owners.

If you go early, your visit will be way more enjoyable.

Great little park. I am a real big fan because there is no real parking, so it tends to remain fairly private to those that walk to it. Easy stair entry into in ocean, a short Sandy Beach front that drops fairly quick. Makes for a perfect miss run stop to soak in the ocean. Open from 5am to 10pm. And a beautiful tree pergola to rest under!

Truly something special in Tucson. Kids rodeo includes Mutton Busting, kids racing on the back of sheep, barrel racing and calls roping. Followed by the Bronco bucking, both bare back and saddled, cattle roping and topped off with bull riding! Truly s lot of fun and the weather this time of year is perfect! The rodeo will not disappoint!

Words cannot describe the view, and emotions felt. The hike is fun, and will get your heart beating. Narrow trail, be careful if it busy, recommend you go on a week day, and either early in the day, or late towards sunset. Otherwise you will be fighting everyone for space to walk up the trail, space to take pictures and space to park.

It is definitely a must see, however, your experience may be ruined by the insane amount of tourists. Especially those from out of the country. The Asian culture seems to have little regard for others attempting to take their perfect picture of the bend. This would be a top notch place if it were not so crowded.

When in Sequoia, you have to get your photo under this tree! While really a pain, because there is no time of day you won't find a line. And the wait can be rather long. Highly recommend a week day and either early in the morning, or late in the afternoon. To have a wait less than 30 minuets.

Truly a neat geological area! The national parks truly make you realize how special, and amazing nature is, and how fragile and small the areas truly are. There is no other place on Earth like it, and the area is so small, a very humbling experience and treat to be able to enjoy it!

Very beautiful mission with rich history. Incredible artwork. All around a great stop, and it's an easy one right off the road, and you can take as long it as short. It doesn't take long to walk through. The bells are rung for service at 6:45pm and it is beautiful.
One of my favorite beaches in Hawaii! Beautiful side of the island, almost always garanteed to be sunny. Must visit beach, ask any local.
Beautiful view of Tucson's City light at night. Seems to be the highest point over looking the city, with sights that will never get old!
Utah had one of the best state line signs I've seen, and you can leave your mark and not worry about the state removing your stickers!
This is one of the most amazing zoos I have been too. It is misleadingly large too! A whole days worth of activities!

I give this two stars not because of the park itself. The park is very clean and well kept. Overall the park is a five-star. The two-star is because of the way the park is run.

We arrived on our reservation day apparently 1 hour early. The front desk office said we would have to wait the hour outside of the park before we could come into the park. since I had to dump my tanks I asked if I could just go to their dump station and do that while we waited for the 30 minutes. They said no we would have to pay the $15 park entrance fee. Ialso noticed by their front entrance is a very large parking lot that handles the boat trailers and trucks which bring boats onto the Lake Havasu State Park. it was very large and only about half full. I asked if we could just pull our RV into that parking lot and wait the hour until we could officially come in. Again they said we would have to pay the $15 if we wanted to wait. We ended up having to drive down the street and sit in a business parking lot for an hour and then return. it should be noted that there was nobody in our space that we were going to occupy during that time.

We booked the park and extended our stay. Midway through our state we were supposed to move to another site. I went up to the front office and spoke to a female employee who said to come back early Saturday morning and they would see what they could do by speaking to the manager. Little after 7:00 a.m. the next morning I was at the front office and the manager was out front. He was courteous. When I asked him if he could let us stay in the spot we were in because we have a large rig with a lot of items, he made no attempt to see if we could even stay in our particular spot. All he said was is we do not modify the schedule. All it would have taken is 30 seconds for him to look at the computer. Even if he just said someone else is coming in our spot I'd have been more satisfied instead of his one line of again, we don't change reservations.

Later that night as we were in our RV we noticed another smaller RV pull onto our site and park behind our rig by the water. The front office personnel had told us previously that there is always someone at the front gate. I tried to call the front office but it went to an answering machine. I drove to the front gate to contact the ranger but nobody was there. I had to call the Lake Havasu City Police department. Their officer responded at the same time a park ranger showed up. They moved the people out of the hour lot. I was surprised since there was no security stopping anyone coming on the property that late at night.

My wife, son (8) and I went to the museum as we enjoy transportation related activities.  As we walked in, an older woman with an accent told us to sign the book.  (This was our greeting as we were the only people in the lobby) she gave us a brief history on the lobby area.
We went into the main area which was a very interactive . Several buttons and switches for kids to press. An older gentleman came out as we looked around.  His interpersonal skills were lacking. While I tried to explain things in a manner our 8 year old son could understand, he pipes up explaining how the system works on a level far higher than my son could understand.  My son moved to a panel with several push buttons. He began to do what most kids do, press the buttons. He yelled over for our son to stop pushing the buttons since the tv monitor was not turned on. (The museum had been open for 25 minutes now.) We told the man our son didn't know.  After the tv came on he said he could press botton #2.  We had no interest in this activity now.  There was a nice miniture rail road with 2 trains. He had the female turn the only working train on complaining there was a Boy Scout Troop there earlier.

We decided we wanted to go outside and look at the train car.  He stated he needed more people for the tour. While he rounded up other guests, our son was playing on an interactive station where you plug in Jack's to different outlets.  We started to go to the outside train as he yells to our son to unplug the jack.  (As if he was supposed to know this.)

By this time we had no desire to be around this man made us feel more of a burden than guest.  We went to the playground next door where our son had a great experience.

I guess I can't complain, the place was free.

We took her nine-year-old son to this park. It seems to be in a very nice neighborhood. The entire park is very nice to include the skatepark. A lot of bowls ramps and jumps and very good for skateboards, scooters and BMX bikes. Here is the only problem! This park is frequented by undesirable characters. We saw a drug transaction in the park, two different people smoking marijuana and a bunch more smoking in the park. There are signs which prohibit such activities but no one is there to regulate it. Also there were some young adults, late teens or early twenties, who are loud and cussing. This park would be great if it was not for this clientele. Also, the bathrooms are nasty and look like prison bathrooms. Their walls are dirty and and have shoeprints all over them. I attached a photo of the exhaust fan in the men's bathroom. You can barely tell it's there with all the dust covering it. This would be a great Park's if they had either an attendant or law enforcement there making sure that it was a safe environment for the kids.

If you're in the Las Vegas area this is such a great attraction.  You ride on specially built bicycles on 4 miles of rail road.   At the end you get a train ride back.  The majority of the track is down hill. We reached speeds of 14 MPH without peddling.  The scenery is great. All of the employees were friendly and informative.  We will ride the rails with this company in the other states.

This museum is a great history on the formation of the underwater demolition teams (UDT) from World War II which turned into the seal program during the sixties. It shows how the Navy frogmen trained and lived their life and sometimes gave their life for God and country.  This is a great homage to all those who have served in the seals and an inspiration to those to become a Navy SEAL

We went during the weekend. Too many adults using foul language around the young kids.  Teen Bullies trying to dictate which way everyone should skate/scooter.  Adult scateboarders drinking beer and smoking marijuana.  The restrooms don't have doors allowing anyone from the outside to see you inside.

This is a neat touristy area where you can paint several Cadillac Switzer sticking out of the ground. It was so disappointing everyone litters there empty paint cans around this statue. There was hundreds of paint cans just littering this field. Quite disappointing

This is a great park period not only can you park your RV here for free for 3 days, this includes electric and water, their memorials to 911 and our military veterans. It's a great place to walk around and there's a playground. They also have a bird sanctuary here

This is a great museum. The outside has numerous static displays of Air Force weapons and Fighters / bombers from all eras. The inside is packed full of airplanes Air Force memorabilia stories and tributes to our heroes. It is free and a must-see

this is a great little campground. Some of the area is for tent camping while they have some spots with full hookups for RV. You're literally on the Rio grande river and concede Mexico on the other side.
This is a great state park. Fairly new to park standards. Clean nice water and great rocks to jump into the water. Get there early because they close the park at about 11:00 because of capacity.
This place is a must see if you're in West Texas. It's 30 minutes from Amarillo. It's like a mini Grand Canyon. They also have RV sites in the valley with full hookups. It was only $10 to get in
This is a great little Park it's got a large open grass area A Bike and Skate Park some play areas like swing sets and slides for younger kids but a beautiful view of the ocean
It's like nothing you've ever seen. I definitely recommend that you go explore this area. You are not close to any grocery stores or Walmart. Lot of great boondocking for RVs.
This was a great county-owned Waterpark. They have several different water slides for kids of all ages. They have two lazy rivers and wave pool. The prices are not that bad.
if you go to Waco this is one of the places you need to go to. They have a mammoth excavation site that has been placed indoors and protected. It's very informative
This is a great Train Museum. They ask for no cover charge just donations. They also have a railroad train that drives around the property you can write on.
Great place for kids 10 and under. But do not go after the high school lets out in the middle school lets out. A lot of kids cuss yell and scream
This place is great for the young and old. There's a huge model train Center which was great. You could actually ride a small diesel train there.
this was a great part not only because of the baseball and other Park activities but we were there for the Scottish highland Games as well
Such a great place where young and old. So many different types of Earth surfaces from petrified wood to Lush desert to Barren areas.
The family had a great time.  Our 8 year old really enjoyed this venue.  Looking forward to the Las Vegas location to open.
Nice little County park. You can take your RVs there also. We utilize the RV black tank dump service. It was $15
Hidden off the beaten path but very cool. It's a shame the tribute sign which speaks about the man has faded
This is a nice little park. Though we saw some Riff Raff hanging out at the train station next door.

Its a nice trail with the Giant and Tallest trees. Beware that there is a stream that needs to be crossed.  They used to have a bridge but today it was gone and you either had to ford the river or climb onto a downed tree and walk across.  I wouldn't recommend either options for those with mobility issues.  Check with the park headquarters before coming.

Wow. I was surprised.  I had a totally wrong idea about this site.  It's worth the ride out. The trail is a bit steep on the east side so if you have mobility issues, go west and you'll skip a tricky up and down part but still see everything up close.  Take the trail map for the descriptions of each.  They also have hiking sticks you can borrow.

5 star park.  Small so you can get around and see the park in a day.  The sights are well marked and the trailhead signs are quite informative.  The trails to the bridges are all down steep canyon walls so you should be in decent shape to go but they are worth the effort.  Especially the 2nd one since you can't really see it from the view site.

Conveniently right off the interstate and you get what you came for with huge fields of petrified wood. Not just a few but thousands that you can walk up to and touch. The road is a bit waving so watch your speed or you might bottom out (maybe on purpose to manage speed).  Bring your own food and water as there is little to get out there.

Great living museum with many desert vegetation and animal examples.  They've added new things like an aquarium and juried art displays in recent years. The entry cost is a bit steep at $24 without discounts but there is free parking.  Parking is somewhat limited so get there early to avoid that issue and before the heat sets in.

I think its the best trail for redwoods. The trail is shorter and easy to follow.  The entrance is tough to find and there is no easy way to turn around, so if you miss it, go on to the giant tree and tallest tree trail and come back.  There are two one lane entrances and limited parking but well worth finding it.

Excellent trail. Long with steep climbs and down hill sections but worth it as the views are great.  You can stop a ways in to soak your feet in the stream or sit at the picnic tables along the way.  Big parking lot with port-a-johns.  You hike through a cow pasture so beware where you step.

We went to hike the trail but it doesn't look like a big park but Its on the Colorado River with a campground.  The trail is good probably a Easy/Moderate level since its a lot of up and down hill climbs but the trail is well marked. $3 day fee to hike.  Not sure what the rest costs.

Nice park once you get there.  The road up is designed for 2 way traffic but its really tight for most of the way so consider using a small car if you can.   You're pretty high up and a few folks were watching whales go by when we got there..  Great views of the coast

Very nice park.  Easy to get to and navigate with many pullouts for viewing, although some are small and could get full on busy days. The views are fantasic.  The trails seem to be well marked but I did hike any all the way.

Meh.  $10 per person to get in and it's a small visitor center and a 100 foot walk to view the castle.  You can't even get very close to it or the other small pueblos.  Other than a short walk to see the river, that's it....

Beautiful active church. You must go inside to see the carved and painted walls.  Its been partially restored.  Parking was $3 but no entry fee.  You can buy candles to light and the gift shop had some interesting items.
likes: Cultural Value: Carved and painted walls
Facilities & Services: Gift shop, candle lighting

reviews_attraction.text: While small they give you an excellent history of the town.  It has a model train depicting the mining town of the 1800's, gems and minerals, stuffed animals and many pictures of the mining days and up to the reservoir.

Not much to see and the windows are all covered with branches and leaves, but its free to see.  The light is very dim.  The cafe had good cobbler though.  A bit expensive but good and she threw in a bit of ice cream.
Huge park with great views.  You need to plan ahead to get on a tour.  The downside is you have to buy tix in person and only 2 days in advance????    Plan on a full day to see it all.
Good trail.  Easy to follow.  Its uphill over rocks for the first mile but at the top its flat.  The west side has great views of the valley.  The east side looks up to the Great Mesa.
Nice park with plenty of paths and shade. The carousel looked very nice and the gondola ride looked interesting. I rode my bike on the Centenial trail east and west of the park.
Great park with good trails.  Limited parking in the peak times so come early or late.  Don't forget to hike down to the waterfall and crawl underneath it..
Good place for info on the south side. Friendly and helpful rangers.  No food or vendng machines though....strange since it's so far out there....
Well worn trail.  Moderate difficulty. Good views with a waterfall.  Watch for horse manure. The entrance road is well marked but very rough.
Parking was easy and the buffet food was very good but we were at a prepaid party. The cost of the buffet seemed expensive for a casino.
Great view of the eastern valley and Salton Sea, and then to the north.  Could use a picnic table or two.  Maybe a bench to sit???
Great views of the canyon. $5 to get in but there is nothing but the overlook to do.  The pit toilets are typical and stocked.
The main trailhead was closed due to fire management but the western trails were open.  Lots of bikers but nice trails.
Nice place to start a bike ride north.  Lots of parking and easy to get to off Golf Links Rd.

In 1-2 hours you can leisurely drive through one of the southwest's hidden geological gems. The Valley of the Gods, near Bluff, Utah and not far from Mexican Hat, is often compared to Monument Valley. It shares similar buttes, mesas, and towers, all geological erosion remnants, however the greatest difference is that Valley of the Gods is on public land and the road to view it takes you up-close and personal with these massive rock formations. In Monument Valley, a tribal park on the Navajo Reservation, you cannot go anywhere you'd like to and the formations are seen at a much greater distance. Overnight camping is extremely limited, too.

The Valley of the Gods allows overnight camping wherever you find an already-used pullout or campsite. Making new trails or new pullouts/camp sites is against BLM laws, however I counted well over 25 spots as we drove the 20+ mile loop road that were available for camping. Some camp sites were literally right at the base of 800 foot tall monuments. In our 2 hour drive we included a short 20 minute hike and numerous photo stops. We only saw 2 vehicles the entire route and only one trailer camp, mostly because of the 95F temps.

If you come from the east, from Bluff's direction, in a short 15-20 minutes you will see the sign on your right-hand side indicating the Valley of the Gods road, #235 I believe. The initial 3-5 miles are passable with a regular car or a vehicle pulling a trailer. After this lead-in, only high-clearance vehicles should continue and because of the sometimes tight turns and short-but-steep hills near the buttes, motorhomes and trailers longer than 10-15 feet should be parked and left behind at one of the earlier camp spots.

Bonus: there is a B&B located just a mile or two from where you will pop out if you enter from this direction....check them online if you'd like a place to stay in order to do some advanced exploring and hiking. Also, the wild Moki Dugway beckons a mile or two north on Utah Highway 261. This series of hairpin curves on a ridiculously exposed dirt road climbs over 2,000 feet in a mere 3 miles, topping out at 6,400 feet on Cedar Mesa. It was built in the 1950's as an access road to haul ore from the Happy Jack Mine on Cedar Mesa to the mill in Halchita, near Mexican Hat.
dislikes: Limited overnight camping (clarification: while the review mentions "extremely limited" in comparison to other places, it actually lists many available spots, so this might not be a strong dislike)

reviews_attraction.text:
The Chiricahua Mountains represent one of Arizona's premiere hiking and wilderness camping areas. The National Monument is just one small piece of the entire range and was set aside because of its unique rock formations and geology. If your travels take you to Bisbee or from Arizona on into New Mexico or points east on I-10, consider a 24-hour detour so that you can get at least a small taste of what this incredible region has to offer.

Be careful going from east to west over the Chiricahuas in the fall, winter, or spring on the only dirt road that connects both sides. It might look passable, however like I discovered this year when I was 10 miles in on that path that hidden on the shady west side of the pass was 3"-6" of fresh snow on the single lane road. In 4-wheel drive Low gear, 1st gear to boot, it took me 70 nervous minutes sliding down iced sections and around drop-off corners until we reached dry dirt, basically at the very bottom of the west slope.

Other than that, it's fantastic....

One of my favorite backcountry drives....if you have the time, drive from Gila Bend to Wickenburg this direction. The dam is a special spot to stop and watch wildlife like Great Blue Herons in the swampy grasslands surrounding the old dam. The bridge, barely wide enough for two vehicles at a time, is also fun to watch. While we were there a large truck hauling heavy equipment went across, scraping the entry sign that indicated maximum height. He made it, however left a nice scrape on his Catepillar Tractor and the swing-mounted sign. Hahaha, great laughs.

The construction of the dam is indicative of the post-WWI construction that took place across America and the southwest in particular, built for holding back the Gila River flow in order to use it for agricultural irrigation. It was built to last and still exhibits the detailed rivet work that characterizes these heavy bridges. The dam is no longer whole and looks to have been broken open to allow free water flow.

An outstanding museum, exhibit, and art experience. My wife ran a 5k at Amerind as a part of their 5th Annual fundraising event. While there I toured the fabulous artifact museum and also met the Native American artist in residence, Duane Maktima, a Hopi-Laguna master jeweler. It turns out that Duane and I share several common friends and probably have crossed paths 30 years ago in Hopi land.

The setting for the Amerind Foundation is not far from Texas Canyon, and has a similar phantasy landscape of giant balanced rocks and granite boulder outcroppings mixed into a mesquite desert grassland. The original buildings date back to the 1930's and reflect decades of loving care. The caretakers, museum employees, and directorship have made the Amerind Foundation a "must-see" for anyone who loves Western and Native American art as well as archaeology.

Son Silver West has been a local landmark for years and years. It has improved its collections over the years and continues to offer collector signs, unique pottery, outstanding jewelry, historic memorabilia, and weird local collectibles, art, and much more.

I make sure to take my family and friends to Son Silver because it symbolizes the best of Sedona. Its location on SR179 is nice, too, because it avoids the Uptown Sedona crowds and has the Old-Time feel that few businesses in Sedona can offer. Like a museum, you'll want to spend plenty of time here because everywhere you turn at Son Silver West you will discover something interesting and new. The store carries only fine quality items so don't expect to find a cheap toy or souvenir. Son Silver West has the creme of the crop in collectibles.

One of the most interesting art museums on Planet Earth for sure. I spent a good 4 hours here with a friend and we needed probably 3 more hours to have ingested it even more slowly and intensively. The Medieval art pieces in this museum's collection will blow your mind. The architecture, imported from Europe piece by piece and reassembled by master stonemasons, is just plain astounding. Enjoy being surrounded by history in its purest form, as art and architecture.

The Tibetan Buddhist Stupa is located conveniently right off of the Chimney Rock trail. For 12 years I lived just two blocks away and watched the construction take place that eventually manifested as this new sacred place.

Hike the Chimney Rock trail and include this place of serenity along the way. Find a local New Age expert to share with you the entire history of the Stupa's creation and the group that brought it to fruition. Quite a story.

A must explore for any Oracle visitor and/or area resident. The history of this area is interesting, peculiar, and unique. The building itself will take you back a century and provide the framework for 100's of historical photos, maps, artwork, and furniture. Sit on the front deck awhile and enjoy watching the local traffic on American Avenue for a bonus experience of what a small town feels like. Have you forgotten?

I never would have thought that this one-time home would become a museum and attraction. My old-friend Phil Tovrea from Jerome had a nice party here in the 1970's (1980's?) and we got to go through all the rooms and exit through the long, underground tunnel passageway that lead way out from the castle. The night lights are great when viewed from here. Can you still saty til sunset at least?

As a roadside attraction that often gets passed up, the bridge is a geological wonder that is both interesting and easy to visit. My favorite part is the north section of the gulch that is like a mini-arboretum. You have to walk north from the main building and trail and head down a separate trail to reach it, however once you do you'll find a verdant world of lush plants and trees. Oasis.

Salt Creek runs through several "woods". One is Bemis and another Brezina. As a kid I spent every spare moment in these woods, riding my Stingray along the hidden trails in 7 foot tall Ragweed forests. We had a tree platform and a wonderful rope swing across Salt Creek, too. So glad that they have actually improved the woods with dedicated trails and well-marked access points.

The wupatki / Sunset Crater loop is a fine way to begin your Grand Canyon visit or end it, depending upon which way you are driving from Flagstaff. Wupatki is one of the finest examples of remote ruins that are relatively intact. The ball court itself is worth the price of admission. The quick visit to Sunset Crater after or before Wuptaki is well worth  the time, too.

Love the Plains of San Augustin and the VLA. Make sure to drive some of the back woods dirt roads leading toward the Gila Wilderness. Joyous nature with few people.

The VLA, Very Large Array: if you saw Jodie Foster's sci-fi movie, "Contact", you'll recognize these miles of large radio telescope dishes that are pointed at the heavens.

An amazing damsite with outstanding views. Until a few years back when the dam was expanded and coated with a concrete coating, Roosevelt Dam was the largest masonry dam in the world. It looked like the Egyptian pyramid construction - large, hand-hewn blocks stacked and melded together. It's still quite the sight.

This is my favorite of the Chaco Canyon complex archeaological sites. You need to spend a few hours exploring the area just to jump start your imagination enough to fathom how advanced and massive this ancient culture was and the subsequent mystery concerning their disappearance and fate.

Wait, wait.....isn't this the Sear's Tower? What happened? When it was first open I took the Express Elevator to the top deck. It pulled down some G's for sure. At that time it was the tallest in the world...but alas, no more. Still, what a view!

I lived in the western suburbs when the Hancock building was finished and visited it during its first year. The v iew from the Center, especially being right on Lake Michigan, is astounding. I will definitely be back.

My brave wife hopped out of our truck midway across the bridge and snapped a few pics. Don't worry: there was no impending traffic. Take a cool hike and picnic along the river below for a memorable outing.
Sugarite is simply one of the nicest places we have ever camped in an organized campground setting. It is remote in a sense, offers great hiking, and has perfect, bare-bones facilities.
95F today and it looks like snow! As others have mentioned, if you do a hike, bring more water than you think you'll need. Watch for cars....it gets a bit busy near the main road.
Better than Apache Gold near Globe; not as good as Cliff Castle Casino in Camp Verde. The cool weather in the summer, though, makes a weekend here just what the doctor ordered.
I've been stopping by this venerable museum since 1973 and always find interesting displays and new contacts when I visit. A gift for those that love this area like I do.
This scenic drive is one of Arizona's finest. Very little traffic overall, great views into old Mexico, and the eventual passage through the berautiful Canelo Hills.
The oldest Arizona single room schoolhouse building still standing in its original location. Nice to visit and ponder why college costs so darn much.
An excellent exploration place. Even the kids will enjoy hiking around in the ruins. The museum, though, is the best part.

This place is awesome and incredible and very difficult to take children to. the reviews about being prepared are 100% accurate. we only had brought light jackets you really need a full-on jacket as you get deeper and deeper into the cave it lowers down well into the 30s. Bring really good shoes especially for the kids as the rocks make it difficult to navigate from time to time. most importantly do not forget the flashlights or headlamp your phone's light will be insufficient and you're going to want to use your hands for scaling down into the cave. from where this is located in proximity to Flagstaff and for how easy to hike to the cave is this is a must for everybody.

Fun little disc golf course here cris crosses back and forth throughout the canal. You'll get annoyed walking up and down over and over again, plus its about 5 miles total so bring plenty of water. At first glance it might be hard to find this place among everything else as it is far from the parking lot. Follow the main path along the street and you'll see the first tee pad looking down into the canal. Last time I checked the teepad were still grass and very uneven and very serious risk to ankles and the like.

This was our first time visiting here and was pleasantly surprised, the drive thru part goes kind of quickly but you can repeat as many times as you want. The village is awesome and if you dont get a chance to see the bird show you are missing out. The birds fly just over your heads...one even brushed up against my child. It was amazing. Every time we're in Flag we'll make the drive over here to visit.

we were just visiting from Phoenix for a couple of days and we knew we had to stop at one of the last known pleasure piers in California. The Santa Monica Pier was a great visit for the afternoon we got to spend a lot of time going through some of the different vendors enjoying the ocean breeze and overall enjoying people watching.

What a great experience at the Phoenix Art museum. We took the kids on free sunday and had a blast. We really were unsure if the kids would last walking around looking at art, however they had so many things that were interactive and fun for the kids to do they had a really great time. We will definitely be coming back soon.

Every time we visit Flagstaff from the valley we make an effort to visit this park. The kids have so much fun climbing on the Seesaw playing in the grass climbing the trees. There's plenty of parking is very close to downtown. I think but I'm not sure the only bathrooms here are Porta-Johns so be aware of that.

I get it, but the bats didn't come out for us in a giant wave of activity so it was a little disappointing. The only thing worse than that was parking. Either you have the park mobile app and have to enter a god forsaken amount of information or you have to wait in line for the 1 pay station. Plan ahead.

Awesome hike, especially in the fall. Took my young kids and they didnt make it far but had fun exploring the ruins, and the cave as well as checking out the changing leaves. The parking lot gets really full fast, but there is parking further north along the road, then you can just pay the walk-in price.

This is an absolutely great tour and really interesting to understand more about Thomas Jefferson and his early life. You really got to see some of the hypocrisy and justification of his personal life and his political life. while little far and out in the woods it's well worth the drive and the visit.

This is quite a very interesting place to visit and learn a little bit more about the nation's history. I really got an inside look at what this town and the area of the United States was like back in the day. Certainly was worth a visit considering Fredericksburg contribution to the nation.

Parked here to wait while I was getting ready to play the disc golf course nearby. This place was super cool and the perfect place for a bbq. There are large kitchens with lots of prep are and eating space. They do need to be reserved, but if you have any kind of group it will be worth it.

Small, quite park, perfect for just a relaxing day. There is 2 tennis balls courts, a basketball court, bathroom that I see workers clenaing all the time. Lots of parking and 2 jungle gyms. While they are a little older my kids haven't noticed yet. Very clean park no issues.

Great park to stroll around, riding bikes, or scooters. We ended up taking the kids here with their scooter and they loved rolling them down hills and around the small fishing lake. The kids enjoyed skipping rocks, chasing the ducks, and watching people fish.

Great local hiking spot. Gets a little crowded on the weekends when the weather is nice, but always able to find a parking spot. The trails are networked well that you can come and go somewhere new every time. A great retreat in the heart of the city.

very interesting place to visit to learn more about Civil War history and to really feel and get a sense of the magnitude of the destruction. This house has been through many generations and seen many people come and go and if these walls could talk.

this is a really fun park for the kids to visit the jungle gym and swing sets are so unusual compared to a classic Park they had a great time exploring and playing. It does get kind of busy in the parking lot is a little small so get there early.

Drove out here for the disc golf. North course is interesting. Open desert holes followed by a short back 6 in and around the lake. The park fairly empty with just a few fisherman and couples out walking, but the park is very well maintained.

This was a really cool Park where the kids had a really good time some really unique and different things for them to play on and Run and Jump with this is definitely a park that would like to come back as soon as the weather cools off again.

this place was sooo much fun, so much for the kids to do and explore. They loved the arts and craft rooms, reading rooms, outside climbing area etc. This is a great spot to take the kids for a couple hours of fun and parking is free!
some of the best birding in yuma is done right here. Also this is one of the only places in Az to hear...good luck seeing...the Black Rail. Nice trail system, lots of areas to explore and enjoy.
This place was awesome. The kids love the trains and the other activities. Everything is reasonable priced and the lines are not very long. The kids beg me to take them back all the time.
Awesome fun place to visit. Beautiful traditional Chinese architecture leading you into the tourist part of Chinatown. This is where your China visit should always begin.
small, causal park perfect for a quick stroll, or perhaps the kids playing on the gym equipment. Large lake, immature trees. Close to Cubs staitdum and the Sheraton.
Great disc golf course. Hands down a staple in the dg community. Course plays nice and away from some of the other activities so works well for others.
awesome fun walk through the canyon in the city here. We were looking for birds, but enjoyed the quite easy hike.

Arlington National Cemetery is both awe inspiring and surreal at the same.  If going through the cemetery does not give you a renewed sense of patriotism, then there is something wrong with you!  Be sure to check out the tomb of the unknown soldier - be sure to see the changing of the guard!

God bless our troops and all that have lost their lives ensuring our freedoms!

Bottom line: beautiful little park with great beach access!  This would be a great place to take a family for the day.  Besides the view and water, there is also convenient access to ice cream shops and convenience stores when you feel it is time spoil your kids or yourself.

Simply a nice place to spend a day of good weather.

Another one of the stops where one can enjoy gorgeous views of the Grand Canyon. I would say that you should stop at them all.

Be sure to pack snacks and fluids - you will want both!  Please, please take your litter with you and help preserve the the view for others.

Another one of the stops where one can enjoy gorgeous views of the Grand Canyon. I would say that you should stop at them all.

Be sure to pack snacks and fluids - you will want both!  Please, please take your litter with you and help preserve the the view for others.

A must see! Just so much history regarding one of our country's founding fathers.  The mansion is stunning - my only disappointment was that the mansion's exterior was being refurbished during my visit.  Guess I will have to come again! :)

Great park! Love the auditorium, trails, park facilities, etc.  There is a lot to do and even more in a non-COVID era.... hopefully soon!  Please CLEAN UP AFTER YOURSELF unless you plan to bring your mother to do so for you!

Beautiful Basilica!  Very traditional - kind of an oddity in Phoenix as it feels everything is knocked down and rebuilt every 10 years! Be sure to check out the stained glass window which is simply stunning!

Yellowstone offers numerous sites that should not be missed; Gibbon Falls must be included on that long list of things to see.  If you like Waterfalls, don't miss these! The scenery belongs on a postcard.
Beautiful park that offers plenty of trails for walking or cycling.  There are also plenty of trails for those that want to mountain bike.   The trails connect to Dodge Park and Riverbends Park.
Beautiful park with playground and a small amphitheater located next to the Pinellas Trail.   Great place to start your walk or bike ride as you can head north or south almost equal distance.
Gorgeous place to walk around and enjoy nature! Next to the Whiting Forest is Dow Gardens - I suggest visiting both.   If you take kids, good luck getting them to leave the playground.
A picture is worth a thousand words - take a look at this shot.  The view is stunning! So if you are at the Grand Canyon, don't miss the opportunity and be sure to take a few pictures.
One of Michigan's amazing Metroparks; offers a variety of aquatic and non-aquatic activities.  I mostly go there to enjoy cycling and it offers a great road and mountain bike options.
Great public beach that also offers disc golf and a dog park.   It was great letting my 4 legged friend run around and check out all those smells that intrigue her.
Great display along a gorgeous water feature.   I would say pond or pool but it is too big to be either.   Would be a relaxing place to read a book.
Great attraction! It was really interesting how the springs would boil and bring mud to the surface; kind of eerie the noises that would accompany.
Such a view... whether you choose to use the overlook or head down the path for a more intimate view / better workout you will not be disappointed!
Great place to stop; be sure to bring good supportive shoes and a good camera.  I would suggest afternoon over morning visits due to lighting.
One of the more unique  springs at Yellowstone's Mud Volcano  attraction. With the right wind, one can really see how it got it's name!
Honestly, this was the site that I was looking forward to seeing the most and it didn't disappoint! The colors are vibrant and amazing!
One of the few places to get something to eat on the south trail and once it make to this which is the farthest point, you deserve it.
Charming little park that is an ideal place to catch a sunrise or spend a sunset.  Pictures are stunning but don't do it justice!
Great preserve to do a little hiking but be sure to wear appropriate footwear as the trail can be a little rough in spots.
I was walking by and had to see if the inside was as beautiful as the outside - it was! Just a simple, gorgeous church!
Great neighborhood park - quiet and quaint. Play structure for the kids and a nice walking path for adults and dogs.

My wife and I came to snowbowl for our first time last week.  We decided to make a trip up because we saw that snowbowl offers free skiing to military on Tuesdays.  Due to this awesome incentive, we decided to see what snowbowl was all about.

This place was awesome!  I am from the northeast and use to ski in northern NY.  The snowbase was sufficient and the conditions were pretty good.  It was obvious that snowbowl takes pride in their runs and had groomed them all the night before.  Since they had not received snow in nearly a week, I was impressed that not one slope was icy.

The food was only alright, but what do you expect for a ski resort?  Stop eating and get outside and keep skiing/snowboarding.

Overall, we loved our experience and will be going back quite a lot more now that we have become familiar with the mountain.  Thank you for the great deal, we look forward to many more days on the slopes.

This place is nothing short of Amazing.  Coming from Arizona for work, I stopped by at this distillery to try their famous bourbon and pick up their limited release bottles of Laguna Madre.  Since I am possibly a morning person, I was there early to avoid any lines.  I was amazed at how friendly the staff were as many of them came by to say good morning while I waited outside the gate.

This distillery was incredibly welcoming and down to earth.  I loved the relaxed atmosphere and was impressed at how much pride each person had in their job.  It was obvious that this was not only a job, but a passion.   Angeleah, the bourbon Jedi, helped me get the Laguna Madre.  She was super helpful and certainly knew what she was talking about.

Garrisons makes some incredibly delicious bourbon that you must try!  This stuff is incredibly unique and has incredibly taste.

In summary, go visit ... Drink.. and enjoy!

Ka'ena point is a stunningly beautiful place.  On multiple occasions,  my wife and I would home out to Ka'ena and watch the sunset.  We were always blessed with seeing wildlife and got to share the beaches with monk seals on multiple occasions.  Please make sure to not disturb them as they are digesting food.  Here is my favorite photo that I took during my time on the beaches.  No, I was not this close... I simply zoomed in and cropped.

If you hike out, make sure to leave valuables at home and not in your car.  Sadly, there are a few that ruin it for all when it comes to the security of your vehicle.  Although I have multiple friends who had their cars vandalized, mine never was.  I simply left the car empty and the doors unlocked.

Happy trails and enjoy the Aina.

I visited the north rim a few years ago after hours.  We were able to enjoy the sunset and night view at the North Rim.  There was no moon out, so the stars were bright and shooting stars everywhere.

However, this place became particularly awesome because of the random drunk guy who found my friends and I.  His name was Rex and he was the friendliest random drunk guy.  Looking around though, our car was the only one there.... who knows where he came from!  He followed us around for a bit and insisted on taking selfies and group photos with his newfound friends.  After this hilarious event had gone on for 30 minutes... he suddenly just walked away.  No clue where he was headed..... but that made it all the more strange and funny.

Walnut canyon is a fascinating park as history is all over the place.  It was incredible to see all of the historic cliff dwellings in various forms.

The trail was paved and was easy to follow.  The island trail is definitely worth the walk, but beware there are a solid amount of stairs.  If it is got out, bring water.  Going early is best as there is plenty of shade and less crowds.

I found this park to be one of the best for cliff dwellings compared to other parks in Arizona.

White sands national monument is an unique place that is awesome to see.  The white sand dunes go forever and are so stunning to see.  If you go for a hike, make sure to carry lots of water and GPS your location of where you started.  It is extremely easy to get lost in the sand dunes.  Also, make sure to give yourself plenty of time to get out since the park closes at night unless you have a permit and are in a specific location.

The Wa'ahila ridge trail is one of my favorite hikes on the island.  Make sure to go when the clouds are high and the weather is good.  The views from the ridge are astounding.  The trail is not extremely difficult but please bring water, proper footwear, and some snacks.

Don't end up like the dummy who gets stuck on the ridge in a storm and is wearing slippers and doesn't have any water or food.

Whenever I come visit Hawai'i, I stop by the Volcano Market to visit with old friends and shop the local booths.  I love the fresh fruit and food that I find at the market.  This community is extremely friendly and kind to visitors.  When at the market, we always feel extremely welcomed and appreciated.  Keep up the great work and variety of vendors.

This hike was fun and easy.  The scenery gets better and better as you keep hiking along the sandy trail.  I love how near the end you begin to get into a narrower portion of the canyon.  It was nice to see a bit of history at the beginning as well.  This trail is awesome for people of all ages and isn't steep or technical.

What a great place to stop in and see what they have to offer inside.  I picked up a few trail maps while at the visitor center.  I like the maps because they are weather resistant and thorough.  They seem to be well marked and accurate.

I have used these maps on hikes throughout the world and never been let down.

Great family-friendly park that is easy to get to and not crowded.  I have never gone to this park and seen more than 2 or 3 people.  The playground is in great condition and the town keeps the grass in fantastic shape.

Keep up the great work.  Also, a great place to take your dogs to run.

My wife and I stayed the night in the forest.  We were able to find a remote campsite with a fire ring.  This place is absolutely beautiful.  The best part is the climate, it was cool with a great breeze.  We welcomed the change from down in Pheonix where it was over 100.

Beautiful place to visit and explore.  I have been going here for a handful of hikes and really like it.  Typically, the trails are pretty quiet and people are considerate.  Respect the wildlife and enjoy it from a safe distance.

Rainbow falls is a beautiful place to stop and see a great sight.  If you are lucky, you will see a beautiful rainbow.  Also, seeing rainbow falls during a storm is impressive as the water gets really violent.

Beautiful park with amazing scenic views.  If you have the time, pay a guide to take you back to the waterfall.  You will learn amazing things about the Hawaiian culture and get to see some incredible sights.

Awesome place to see petroglyphs.  Please respect the 'aina and do not go off the designated trail.  Also, do not be THAT person to destroy petroglyphs or try to make your own... you are not that cool.
This hike is steep but short.  Do yourself a favor and don't go up during a storm when the hill is wet and muddy.  I will laugh at you along with others when you return a muddy mess.
This is a cool spot to walk through and see what a lava tube looks like.  It is a short and easy walk with easy access.  The tube is not long and is good for people of all ages.
This place has all sorts of fun items.  We stop here every time we pass by and find something new for the house.  On our last stop, we got placemats and wall art for outside.
Hawaii Volcanoes national park is a beautiful place.  In the picture, you can see what Halemaumau crater used to look like before the most recent eruption.
Beautiful lake with stunning views.  The walk around the lake is extremely peaceful and quiet.  This is the perfect getaway from the hot valley.
The pier was a great place to visit and full of fun things to see and do.  On a Friday morning, it was relatively quiet with small crowds.
We loved visiting horseshoe bend, it was a great place.  I'd love to go back early morning or night and do some photography.
This unique place is fun to explore and see what is around.   Jerome is definitely worth stopping into and exploring.
Great spot to hike and explore.  Go when it is not so hot out, it will be much more enjoyable.

Like many National Forest, this one is just as unique, big and beautiful! With much to see and do while getting away from life in the city! Always something to photograph while gathering your solitude and peace with nature! The drive is nice and scenic with plenty of stops to relax while using one of the many picnic tables that are offered under cover shaded areas. Remember to have you Tonto Pass when you stop.

What a great place to explore and learn about something you wouldn't want to witness first hand. This place looks good in pictures but looks even better in person! Worth taking in and learning what is being shared and to be able to stand right in front and see with your own eyes the crater itself! Very nice gift shop inside, along with a Subway restaurant, plenty of parking and much to learn!

Nice place to visit and take walks while learning about the local plants you see around here. Volunteers help with information when needed, and there many places to relax and sit down while walking through the garden. There is also plenty of information available, a snack bar, vending machines and the best thing about this place is their special exhibits they often have at night/evenings

Awesome place! no doubt the parade has passed this town years ago when the new freeway made Route 66 a thing of the past. The great thing is that people flock here to stand on the corner while the Eagle's music is being played in what is basically the middle of no where. Much history to see around the old Route 66 and it's nice that places like this are keeping it alive!

Love this place! Of course I’m partial to light houses and find them special in the first place! For anyone who loves lighthouses this one doesn’t disappoint and is a real beauty where you’ll find yourself wishing you could live there! Nicely maintained by people who care with information available about the grounds and lighthouse making for a fun visit!

Great place to see actual items that are from some amazing periods of history! Presidential limousines, the chair Abraham Lincoln sat in at Ford Theater, beautiful aircraft, autos and a giant locomotive. So much to see, plan on walking around, gift shop, penny press available and cafe. Plenty of parking safe and staff that is helpful!

A truly special place that needs protecting from development and greedy political figures looking to make a buck! Having the natural beauty within reach of where you live and able to see not only nature but learn about local history while either taking it easy, having a picnic, playing with your kids or exercising is truly special!

Good place for family's to let the kids have fun, but also good for everyone that enjoys being outdoors with so much to see and do, located not far from several places to eat and shop. Nice to relax and just people watch while getting some exercise walking around and watching others enjoy whatever activities they are doing.

My dog loved it and always enjoys a visit to this place! Overall people are pretty good with their dogs and keeping up after them. Nice to watch all the dogs enjoy themselves and have their own space where they can run and play with each other. Even the grumpy dogs can’t help but crack a smile and enjoy themselves as well.

This place is awesome and nice that it's a museum to show what a service station was like back in the day of travel when overheating, blown tires and being stranded waiting for a part was a part of travel. Worth taking a picture, so please leave a donation so this place can survive and perhaps even grow!

Beautiful zoo that is not too large but just the right size with a lot to see and do. Plenty of parking, easy to follow from start to finish . Well maintained grounds with places to sit,relax and enjoy you lunch or just take in the sights while taking a break from walking around.

A wonderful place to get away and see the natural wonders of this country and perhaps get closer to both nature and relax from the rush of city life. Beautiful sights to see while driving through with many places to stop and enjoy the peace and beauty of this place!

Like most of California this place is crowded and busy, but that's what gives it the magic and brings everyone in! Can't deny the tourist trappings of what it is along with it's storied history there is so much to see that is interesting!

This place gets 5 stars just for being The Grand Canyon! but also for being one of the few national parks that allows dogs to be brought in and walked on the upper trails! Great visitor center, plenty of parking and a lot to see and do!

A great place to visit if you want to learn some history about the area and also check out an old railroad depot. Nice and clean, however the homeless enjoy camping out here when they can. Also a good place to watch the trains go by.

The beauty of the desert is something many will never understand. It's worth the stop to get out and explore what it has to offer. It's so much more and even a place that will rejuvenate you and heal you!
Truly a wonderful gem within the urban sprawl that surrounds it. A nice get a way close to home to either just relax or excercise while taking in the natural beauty of what a park can offer.
Wonderful place to get away from everything else! Scenic drive and great views with something for everyone, from easy hikes, mountain biking, to camping or just a simple ride in the car!
Landmark and Hollywood classic! However they have other locations. Expect long lines especially at peak times however things move fast. Good food and service. Parking can be challenging.
Nice place to take a break from the daily grind without having to travel far away! Awesome to bring your kids, pets and taking a walk for your health and to release some stress.
Wonderful place to shop! Definitely southwest & Mexican style to decorate your home. Plenty of items for all, while looking at an extensive porcelain sign collection.
Great place with charm that they just don't build anymore. Nice to just hang out and people watch, have a drink and enjoy that small town atmosphere.
Great family adventure without traveling far away. Excellent for younger children with so much to keep them busy you will spend an entire day here!
Pretty neat place with a lot to offer just off the freeway. Very nice grounds, great staff, and a nice break from a long drive.
Always nice to take a trip up to Dobbins lookout and take in the view of the valley while the sunsets!

Perfect spot for beginning snowshoers. Just (barely) off I-90 near Snoqualmie pass there's plenty of parking as long as you don't mind parking along the road and walking for a while.

After a short hike up to Gold Creek Pond there's a pleasant loop trail with essentially no elevation change. Another nice option is to hike up the Gold Creek trail for a bit to visit Heli's Pond. Total round trip for both is just over 4 miles.

Great spot to have a look at the North side of Mt St Helens. A couple of excellent films and other educational material. All for only $8 or free if you have an interagency pass. The best part though is that the parking lot also allows access to a trail system with even better views of St Helens and also Spirit Lake and Mt Adams without too much hiking. Highly recommended on a sunny day!

Great place for a hike! Lots of trail options. Water, trees, wildlife, and, if you're lucky, sunshine. Many places to park at different access points. Just enough elevation change to make this a good workout.

On our last hike we walked a couple of miles through the woods and then walked back to the car on a sidewalk through a couple of neighborhoods.

Great spot for a hike! Just over 10 miles - with 1400' of elevation gain - to circumnavigate the lake. The uphill portion is much easier traveling in a counterclockwise direction. A few pieces of logging equipment that was caught in the eruption can be found on the ridge nearest Mt St Helens. Very nice sandy beach about 6 miles in.

It was chilly. It was wet. It was cloudy. It was foggy. And my first trip to the North Cascades National Park was also amazing! Snow-covered peaks hiding behind clouds and fog and periodically showing themselves, hidden waterfalls, beautiful calm lakes. I'm sure it's even better in good weather but Fall is a great time to visit.
