Nice, compact zoo just west of Issaquah. Not surprisingly, there are cougars. Also wolves. A little surprisingly, there are also tigers. Reindeer, mule deer, llamas, emus and a couple of other animals can be fed with food purchased at the zoo. Not a bad way to spend an hour or two on a sunny afternoon in early March 😁.

Excellent hike up to Navaho Pass with an option to add Navaho Peak for an extra couple of miles and a few hundred feet more elevation. Stafford Creek is a constant companion for most of the hike. The only drawback is that the last four miles or so of road is rough and filled with pot holes.

Amazing view of Mount Si and the surrounding area. Lots of benches for resting after a long hike (or just because). Restrooms and a small covered area - with a BBQ - in case of rain. Large open fields for picnicking. Never enough parking but at least it's close to town (North Bend).

It takes a bit to camp here (permit for camping in Olympic National Park, permit for visiting the Makah Reservation, limited and non-free parking) but it is well worth the trouble.

Make sure to visit Point of the Arches at low tide. So many tide pools, just full of life.

Very cool semi-maze of a museum with quite an eclectic array of art. I saw older cars that I'd never heard of before. I saw paintings and sculptures and even a recorded cello performance in a darkened room. Well worth a visit.

The Poo Poo Point trailhead parking lot is usually full but you can park at the high school just up the road. Adds some distance to the hike up to Poo Poo Point but it's a great hike and the view is worth it.
Nice enough suburban park with some old growth Douglas fir and a small stream. Not at all crowded at 8:00 on s Saturday morning but the traffic noise from Hwy 16 is ever present.
Overcast and intermittently very foggy the day I was there so the view was generally not impressive. A nice, short snowshoe from the Mt Baker ski area up to Artist Point though!
Amazing hike! Very different from the forested trails on the west side of the Cascades. Mesas, lakes, basalt columns, waterfalls, and even a rattlesnake or two.
A great hike for beginners! Quite a pleasant walk through the woods with just a bit of elevation gain. Nice territorial view at the top. Great spot for lunch!
Nothing special about this hike. It is good exercise though and there's a decent territorial view from much of the trail since there are no trees whatsoever.
Relatively straightforward, short course with a couple of interesting holes. A bit expensive in my opinion but the greens were in good shape.
Pleasant and very easy stroll along the shore of Lake Washington. The parking lot can fill quickly but The Landing is just a short walk away.
An amazing walk in the woods just outside the city. Entering the grounds past Husky Stadium via Marsh Island is definitely the way to go.
Plenty of paved parking, vault toilets and a bulletin board with a map of the trail system - what more could one ask of a trailhead?
Nice enough park considering its proximity to Pike Place market. Great view of Elliot Bay and - on a clear day - the Olympics.
Pretty good spot for a break along the Olallie trail. Especially if you're on your way up to the Mount Washington summit!
Great way to ease into the hike to Mount Ellinor. Sure it adds a couple of miles but it's a great way to start the day.
Not a bad place to sit and enjoy some sunshine and relatively fresh air. Lots of construction noise lately though.
I had a great - and very easy because no elevation change - hike through the pines and along the Deschutes River.

Small and cute garden. You can check out free tickets for two people in local libraries. Fish are pretty healthy and biiiiger! Even bigger than those ducks. Tens of parking lot and a small souvenir shop with fair pricing. Nice place to bring your kids or enjoy some time by sitting on the bench.

If the park is shut down, you can just keep driving until see a huge sand hill crash the fence and forming a ramp. It’s impossible to see all of it. Dusk would be a preferable visiting time. Please do not left you shoes so far away, the sands could be very cold after sunset.

Perfect place for bird lovers. You can see hundreds of birds during the spring and summer. The best time would be in the early morning or one hour before sunset. One-way loop around the whole place. The visitor center is 10 miles away from the actual site.

A de facto peninsula on the salt lake. 10 dollar admission fee per vehicle. Good place for hiking during morning and dawn. You can also swim in the water but not recommended. Pronghorn antelopes and bison can be seen if you are lucky.

Tens of metal dishes on the most dry and flat plain in the US. A good place to learn some astronomy knowledge. If you just want to take a photo with the array, it wiser to stay far from it, which could also save 6 bucks visiting fee

Most trails are closed. Only could reach the waterfall and the natural bridge. But still worth it. The visitor center’s location should be the best in US. Good place to spend an afternoon for casual walking and doing nothing

A lot of people visiting here. You must not part near the place but use a shuttle provided by the parking lots nearby. It also takes ten minutes from the shuttle stop to where you can see the Bend. But it totally worth it.

Colored desert and petrified wood all over the place. Quite different from other places. It need near an hour just drive through the park. Wind hollowing all the time, so please wear something with a hood
One of the best places to see the full view of Phoenix metropolis, even better at night. Adequate parking space and a lot of trails near it. Great place for hiking and observing cactus
Fabuluous group of buildings. Right in the downtown of the Salt Lake City. Plenty of underground parking space. Free in the first two hours. Some facilities are closed on Sundays.
Good place to do some casual trips. Not far from downtown and perfect vista for the sun valley. Trails overspread the mountains, nearly impossible to set your feet on all of them
Been here three times. Always crowded with cars. If you arrive here later than 12, you’d better parking on other lots down along the road. Or east trail would be a better option.
Ancient residence built in a stone cave. Helpful rangers. Best viewing platform to watch the lake. Adequate parking space. Need ten to fifteen minutes walking to the top.
likes: Facilities & Services: Helpful rangers, Adequate parking

reviews_attraction.text: Lovely visitor center with a mini museum in it themed on western history of this place. The staff here is very helpful and a lot of flyers and maps could be find here.
likes: Facilities & Services: Helpful staff, informative materials

reviews_attraction.text: You can catch great views of sunset and the ISM Raceway here. Need several minutes to climb onto the top. A lot trash like shell case and bottles could be found.
Cute place with a lighthouse standing by the sea and several hostel facilities. A RV campground on the north side. Public restroom and limited parking available.
Not the perfect spot to enjoy the sunset because of those mountains on the west, but good enough. Stop here every time when I return from north.
Nice recreational area. Bring you family and enjoy a cozy afternoon. You can also feed birds or swimming  if you are not afraid of cold water.
Tranquil beach with adequate parking space, picnic area and restroom. There is a toll stand but no staff in it. Beautiful when it is sunny.
Too shining during the summer. Maybe better when  the weather is cooler. Three dollars admission fee. Adequate parking space for visitors.
Great sunset viewing place. You can park the car besides the street except midnights. Public restroom and fountain are also provided.
You definitely cannot miss it when you on the way to Sedona. Several trails under it, could be more beautiful when snowing
Fantastic park with a 5 dollar entry fee per car. Nice place for novice climbing exercise. You can also camp here.
Pretty quite place with little traffic. You can enjoy the view better by climbing up the hill besides the river.
If you want to visit here and you are an adult, you must bring a child with you. Only suitable for little kids.

A little known spot.  A little gem.  The water area makes me feel like I’m not in Phoenix.  There’s a little mountain next to the small parking lot that you can climb.  At the peak you can see straight down baseline road and Avondale blvd.  There are ancient petroglyphs near the top of the mountain.

Due to being lesser known it seems to get trashed a little more.  There was no public trash can the last time I went down there.  People go fishing and leave ALL of their trash down there.  Yet one of my favorite spots.

I love coming here.  It’s free the second Tuesday of every month.  The variety of cacti, succulents and other plants is absolutely mind blowing.  You will see plenty of plants you never knew existed.  It’s fairly sized so you can see everything all in one day if you want, or you can take your time and enjoy each section.  There’s also always art being showcased around the area by different at different times.  One of the must see locations in Phoenix.

Fascinating to see animals from around the world.  Also obviously depressing to see the animals in small enclosures, looking mangey and depressed.  My daughter being only 3, with no prompting wants the animals from the zoo to be set free.

Much respect to the team keeping that place together and I understand the dynamic of taking care of the animals and doing your job.  It’s a price we all pay to see the things we normally wouldn’t.  Hence 3/5 stars.

The most unique geological landform in Phoenix in my opinion.  The rock is like a bunch of different small rocks cemented together, it’s quite fascinating.  The hole has steps leading up to it which makes it accessible for all.  I brought my toddler daughter up here.  I’ve seen people bringing up infants.  It’s free so go check it out.  Only downside is the parking lot is small.  So go when you think you can find a spot.

I helped clean out this building in 2008 when it flooded.  People from all backgrounds and faiths came together to help.  This is a place of peaceful gathering.  A little celebrated gem in Cedar Rapids, a piece of history.  The first official mosque in America.

It’s been a while since I’ve been inside.  I have faint memories of the inside on a rare occasion I was there as a child.  I’d like to see it open more often.

This is a peaceful park with a nice lake that had bridges, and nice spaces to chill by the water.  The whole space of the park is very big, there’s a nice playground for the children.

Park services does a good job cleaning up, but there’s still garbage and junkies in the bathrooms during the day.

The issue of homelessness, drug addiction, and litter are the only things keeping me from giving 5 stars.

This park is absolutely beautiful.  Wooded trails, wood bridges, cliff like structures.  Fabulous place to go and recharge.

Went on the scenic backbone trail which was like a tall skinny cliff that you walk across and there’s a 40ft cliff on either side towards the creek.  Spectacular.

There was also a couple goats free roaming on the trail.  They were very friendly even with my 3 year old daughter.

I love the location of this mountain.  It’s a moderately difficult hike, about 45 minutes to the top at an easy pace.  I really like the little valley between north mountain and shaw butte (the mountain just west of north mountain) walking on it makes you forget your right in the middle of the city.  I used to work and the humane society and come here or Shaw butte once a week to hike and meditate.

PLEASE PICK UP YOUR GARBAGE HERE.  BRING BAGS TO CLEAR OUT OTHERS GARBAGE.

I love this area.  I feel like I’m not in Arizona because of the flowing river and the greenery. An abundance of wildlife.  Unfortunately the litter is out of control.  I don’t think there is any regular garbage service out here and I stress them importance of KEEPING ARIZONA BEAUTIFUL.

Amazingly peaceful place.  You can spend an entire day here and not be bored.  They have a great selection of plants for purchase.
The selection of plants along the trail is much more impressive than the desert botanical garden in Phoenix.  The selection was larger and the area to explore much larger.

Definitely a spot worth driving to.

Such an awesome place.  Wonderful wooded trails, wooden bridges and walkways.  A unique and creative kids area with interactive music stuff, a big slide, a butterfly garden, and little stream set inside a beautiful prairie area.  Had a lovely time and my 3 yr old daughter and wife.  There’s also a high tower with an amazing view.

This is a beautiful trail.  You can hike to the top of the mountain, you want to give yourself at least 5 hours if you want to make it up and back.  If your less experienced give yourself more time.

If you just want to have a little peaceful picnic this is also a great place to park and lay down blanket or a sheet and relax.

Love hiking here in this park.  It’s amazing in the middle of the city it feels like your transported onto a wild mountain.  The preserve is nice.  The trail is typically busy, and it’s nice that the trail is distinct and easy most the way up.  The top is deemed the stair master for the sharp high steps carved to the top.

Obviously gotta love the proximity to north phoenix and getting to enjoy the water.  It’s completely bogus the way they’ve closed off all shore access because or coronavirus.  But it’s lovely.  I jumped the cliff by the sign “1702” my tailbone hurt still a week later.

Very lovely to enjoy the lake on a boat though.

This is really more of a park for locals.  Meaning lots of vagabonds convene here.  If you don’t live in the neighborhood there’s no reason for you to travel to this park to play.

The playground is decent.  I like the musical instruments for the children to play.  There’s a decent size field too.

Beautiful place.  The dam is damn impressive.  The bridge is a spectacle.

The picnic area is great for a picnic and family photo.  DONT BE TRASHY AND LEAVE YOUR TRASH BEHIND.  Unfortunately there is a lot of litter, just like everywhere humans frequent.

I came here for the skatepark.  It’s tiny but fun and better than nothing.  My daughter enjoyed playing in the sand volleyball pit while I skateboarded.  There’s a really nice looking playground we avoided in case it was off limits from covid.

Love this park.  My mom brought me here when I was a child and the monkeys were still there.  Recently brought my own daughter down and it’s really special to me.  The animals and the educational, hands-on stuff is really awesome for the kids!

Great park just north of downtown.  Huge place, nice walking trails, park, lake, historic buildings, veterans memorial, native inspired art installations.  Great place to have a picnic, go on a date, or spend time with your friends or family.

Awesome trail.  It’s typically very busy, your lucky if you get a spot in the parking lot most days.  There are lots of trails that connect from Mormon trail after you go 1.1 miles on the main stretch.  Great views of phoenix from the south.

I love fat mans pass.  It’s tight enough that if you have too big of a belly you might get stuck.  It’s short enough not to make you claustrophobic.  The walls are smooth from so many people touching as they go through.  Awesome spot.

Love this little preserve.  Tranquil nature trails with little groves you can walk through, large trees and flowing water for some parts of the year.  The parking lot is kind of small but there is overflow parking not far.

This place was amazing.  So much to see.  I really like that it all has a flow to it and you won’t feel like you missed out on it.  There’s multiple animal and botanical exhibits.  A great place to spend the day.
I mostly come here for the skatepark.  My daughter also loves to play on the park which is nice.  A lovely neighborhood park in a nice neighborhood.
This is a great park all around.  I love the skatepark and the pump track especially.  There’s a nice lake here and a nice playground.

I only hiked the main trail. I think I lost my excitement for petroglyphs along the way and decided to skip the 3 kings trail. The trails here are pretty rough, they should get the boy scouts or some local group to work on them as a fundraiser. I left with a pretty good scrape on my arm that got stuck by a branch. There are tons of petroglyphs and pictographs here, and some very interesting ones. Would be nice if they offered a virtual tour as well. There is lots of information in check-in building, just hard to process most of it. Some of the petroglyphs are difficult to see, where a drone might be needed to capture them well. Neat view of the valley from the cliffs. $5 cash box, makes this a pretty good value, plan to spend at least an hour on the main trail.
likes: Facilities & Services: Information availability, Affordable entry
dislikes: Facilities & Services: Trail maintenance, Complex information

reviews_attraction.text: This was a pretty awesome tour and demonstration. You take a train about a third of a mile into the mountain, there are 7 levels of tunnels above you. My tour guide was an actual miner, demonstrates several of the tools used in the mining process, they are loud! The tour takes about an hour, very informative and answers any question. The panning was a little underwhelming as there wasn't any gold in the dirt. Overall though, well worth the $24 admission plus a tip for the guide.

Hiking, redwoods, camping, trails, river, bobcats... so much in this state park and only $10 a day. I appreciate they take credit cards at this location. I pulled in and drove through, all the way back to the day use area 4 and was like, oh someone's cat is here... it took a minute for me to realize it was a bobcat. There was a lot of construction equipment back there, so I had a little picnic in day use area 3 among some deer and then parked in 2 and hiked around a bit.

Free, Awesome, Must visit. It's easy to get overwhelmed with ruins in this part of the country but the rebuilt Kiva here is Amazing along with the other ruins that you can walk through and see them being actively restored. You can buy a trail guide or follow along on your phone. I used my phone but lost reception in the Pueblo. It's not huge, you'll probably spend 30-45 minutes here. After visiting Mesa Verde and everything being closed, this was a highlight.

Stunning April hike. Borders some private property, they request you stay on trails here, also borders a state scientific nature area that doesn't have trails. I spent about an hour here, lots of native plants, scenic gorges, a nice stream. Crossing the stream tested my waterproof shoes. Trails are fairly obvious and there are posts but some of the signs have been removed or graffiti on. Seems like they may have removed a trail.

The lighthouse is a private residence but the grounds are part of the state park and open to walk around. The best view is either as you walk up from the parking lot or from the backside. Entrance fee was $3, and there aren't any envelopes, so you just slide the money in a steel pipe. It was pretty foggy the morning I visited and I couldn't see the water or shoreline, I could imagine the fog bell ringing though.

It was raining when I visited so I just popped in to see the lighthouse and didn't make it to the beach. The fall colors in the grasses added a nice contrast. It's a very tall and beautiful light, would love to come back and climb to the top of it. There didn't seem to be a fee to enter the parking lot and enjoy views of the lighthouse.

Warm springs, not hot. The signage at the parking lot seems to be gone. You hike from the parking lot, down to the river and back up to the warm springs. I felt like you would need shoes for the hike given the terrain and distance. The view is amazing! There was quite a bit of trash around the pools when I visited, including a diaper...

Free! I hiked the Barrett's Rim Trail loop as the main trails were closed for repair. I was underwhelmed... if you live in the area and are looking for a trail that gets you out in nature and is scenic, this is a great spot! If you are traveling across the country looking for amazing sites, I'd skip this spot and head to Hocking Hills.

COVID has won the war here in 2020. The visitor center is closed and seems to be undergoing some remodeling. What's disappointing is that the roads through the battlefields are barricaded.  Pretty much all you can do is walk around the visitor center. If you had a bike, it would be easy enough to hop the gate and enjoy a nice ride

Free! Unfortunately the museum and building are closed. I was met by a ranger standing in a doorway answering questions and distributing literature. Most of the mounds here have been rebuilt as they were worn down by farmers and a WWII Camp Sherman. The mounds are not huge but the site is interesting to walk around.

Stopped fairly early in the morning, seemed like it was free to walk around. Nice old mill and convenience store across the street. Several short walking trails around the dam and mill. Nice stop, good spot for a picnic. Would have been neat to see the waterwheel in motion but it was stationary while I was there.

I pulled in here, not really sure what to expect. I walked to the overlook i image the hoodoos are better if you hike the full trail. You get a nice view of the Rio Grande from the overlook. The road had washed out a bit at the entrance to this turn off, causing my car to bottom out... wasn't ready for that.

Nice small Pueblo on the top of the hillside above the Canyons of the Ancients Visitors Center. There is a nice modestly sloped trail up to hear that discusses the native vegetation. It appears that the kiva and many of the walls have been rebuilt giving you a better idea of what was here.

Not quite as scenic as I hoped. I'm guessing the road getting cut through it didn't help. You can see water flowing and terraces forming on the opposite side of the road. There is a small waterfall visible at the end of the dam. There is a small pull off before and after it.

The hike here from Grand Portal Point was a challenge with lots of trees down across the trail. The only unobstructed views of lovers leap are from the east on the trail. There is a spur trail that goes out onto lovers leap but I didn't see much of a view from there.

A nice surprise as I was driving from Zion to Bryce. The Red Canyon had several trails that I didn't stop for but it did offer up some great roadside scenery. Scenic Byway 12 through Red Canyon is apparently known as the All-American Road.

Like pretty much everything else at this park...closed. but the bookstore is open???

They do have some boards up with suggestions of what to do but just don't come until covid restrictions are lifted.
Interesting stop for fans of wireless communication, also found a stunning view of the coastline through a break in the fence. There isn't anything here to see besides some information plaques.
Visitors center was closed but staff was out front helping with suggestions and answering questions. Would be nice to have gone inside the building and see the historic structures.
Doesn't open until 9am and then rangers set up outside. Nice native landscaping outside. Bathrooms were open before 9... nice quick stop for me, enjoyed the lupine in bloom.
Even though the museum is currently closed, there are some examples of the fossilized trees out front. Hopefully I get to make it back sometime to check out the Museum.
Who doesn't want to see the world's largest pistachio? A sampling area, ice cream, pistachio tree farm and more! Great stop while passing through.
Great park with covered picnic tables and a nice view of the river and Troy. Stopped here to enjoy some lunch and a little walk.
It's  a nice view but if you can make it up to the Canyon Overlook or Harpers Corner, you'll be rewarded with far better views.

Garmin took us on the back roads today and decided the Irvin S. Cobb Bridge was the safest place to cross into Illinois. This narrow, entirely metal bridge built in 1929 was the safest option! We first had to just skim under the dangling metal sign that said 9'8". I was worried we were going to scrape. Than we have a half a mile across this clankety thing with oncoming cars and barely enough room for both of us. Scary. Thankfully we were wine tasting later! Do not recommend for RVs.

This place is amazing. A secret BLM monument and Campground. They have pit toilets and zero water so be prepared. The nearest place for water is Gila Bend. The shell station in Gila Bend offers free water and a free dump, but is 30 miles away. With our Weboost 4G, we actually had great internet way out here. The petroglyphs are beautiful, fun to walk to from your campsite. The hosts here are the best, having been there for nearly 10 years.

This place was spectacular. The animal exhibits are very well done and the cactus garden alone is worth the admission. The landscape is a beautiful clustering of cactus found in other regions and brought together in adoringly different ways. This is not the landscape outside of this museum. The animals were all visible and active, which made for some great photography. We loved this place and can see why it's so adored.

Remember The Alamo? I do! It was amazing. Tons of people there, which is a bit suffocating, so go during the week. The long house has a movie and museum that are some of the best aspects. Giving such incredible detail of the people, area, event, etc. This is always open and a government shutdown means nothing when it comes to this monument in Texas.

Camping here is like having your own private forest. The sites at flying A are so well spaced and the amount of palms around you makes for a picturesque scene. The campsite was well prepped and the sites are large. Loved staying here and will definitely be back.

The park was tons of fun. You can drive around the entire park in an RV, seeing everything with ease. The petrified wood is all over the place. One of the visitor centers has an entire forest behind it. There are a lot of petroglyphs and ancient structures.

This monument is fantastic. It's high elevation and in the middle of nowhere. You need to purposefully decide to go here. The weather can be bad but it's worth it. They have a campground there and tons of caves to explore.

The park was fantastic. It's worth going to even though it's a drive. Island in the sky gives you some of the best views you'll ever see. Views from the green river overlook are more stunning then the grand canyon.

A must see stop when in Newport. The lighthouse is surrounded by birds and blooming plants in the spring. The tide pools are some of the best around. It's free to get in with the America the Beautiful pass.

This part of the Redwood State and National Park is the best. You're close to great campgrounds, one being at the Jedediah state park. The area is loaded with old growth redwoods that are amazing to see.
Fun or the family or history buff. The tour is a must see as you get to see the immense work put into creating each hand carved animal. The people there love what they do and are a happy bunch.
The view is Grand! It was massive allowing you to see the the mountains 35 miles away. The canyon is massive and the Colorado River is down there, just not visible.
Had such an amazing time here. I think we enjoyed the cats the most. Those 6 fingered felines were the best. The gardens were a joy and the house beautiful.
We had to go here to see the tomb of our American heroes. The place is gorgeous inside. I'm not even religious, but enjoyed the architecture and artistry.
The grounds here are some of the best. The nautical themed wine tasting room was fun. We loved the insect garden. Their were lots of butterflies and bees.
Beautiful mission. One my favorites with a large grassy area. This is the best place to park and ride the bus to other missions and mainly The Alamo.
It's twice as great as the other Arches. Double the pleasure without the hassle of walking to another arch. It looks even better at sunset.
This park is a gem. We camped for a few nights and loved the scenery and open spaces. Sites are level and the park is so well maintained.
Tons of people. Just take a picture of the point and move on. You'll be happier. Either way, we did it, we conquered the south...Again!
By far my favorite spot in the park. The views of a canyon in a canyon with the green river making a horseshoe turn...Epic!
What a gem. The architecture and restoration are remarkable. A must see. We would have loved to see the inside, but Covid.
Great easy up and down loop of about half a mile. The arch is gorgeous. You can see mesas and the canyon through it.
We got to see Alligators! That made the park visit a highlight. The place is busy, pretty, and a joy to visit.
One of the best places in the Everglades. It's a short 0.8 mile loop that shows the diversity of the area.
This is a great hidden gem in the park. A massive canyon that you easily hike up to. It's a must see.

If you're hiking in Utah, this is one you shouldn't miss. There are two main trailheads: the Aspen Grove trail starts just north of Sundance up Provo Canyon; the Timpooneke trail starts a few miles further north on the Alpine Loop. There is limited parking at both locations so get there early. Watch for parking restrictions; they're heavily enforced. Access to the park and trails is $6 for three days (as of Summer 2017).

What makes Mount Timpanogos (also called "TImp") so special is the variety of things to see during the hike. The Aspen Grove trail comes up along a series of steep switchbacks which eventually lead to waterfalls along the trail and to Emerald Lake, a pool fed by water in the mountain, and a permanent (but disappearing) snow field which hikers sometimes try to slide down while descending south from the peak (although this is very dangerous and not even possible most of the year). The Aspen Grove trail is slightly shorter than the Timpooneke trail but it is steeper. To get to the peak after Emerald Lake, hikers cross a large field of boulders that have fallen off the massive face on the east side of the mountain. The Timpooneke trail ascends through four phases: the first part of the trail runs through trees and crosses small waterfalls; the second part of the trail climbs from a massive rock plateau through pine trees and across rocky paths; the third phase is the climb to the Saddle on a trail that runs across a huge basin (stay to the right at the trail signs to climb to the Saddle and peak or stay to the left to cross the basin and climb up to the Emerald Lake plateau; (from the Saddle you can see the mountain range to the east and the Utah Valley floor and Utah Lake to the west)); the last phase is the climb to the peak along a very rocky and sometimes challenging trail. At the peak, there is room to sit and take in spectacular views and there is a small metal shack that typically contains a booklet you can sign.

Along the trails, it is quite common to see mountain goat herds, rodents, small snakes and lizards, and a variety of birds and insects. The wildflowers are diverse and spectacular. There's no technical climbing, so the difficulty in this hike is primarily its length. Hikers climb over 4,000' across approximately seven miles from the trailhead to the peak. The top is almost 12,000 feet above sea level. It's often a heavily trafficked trail, so if you want to avoid a lot of people hike early or late in the season and avoid weekends. The peak is a popular destination for people that want to watch the sunrise or sunset, so you can find people hiking the trail any time of the day or night.

Cascade Springs is an interesting site. Water seeps from inside Mount Timpanogos where a vast quantity is stored. Water runs out all year long, although it gets pretty low in the summer. The area around the springs includes a paved path with stairs and small bridges. Walking the path does include some elevation change, but it's not too difficult. At the bottom of the springs, the water pools into small ponds. Supposedly, there are fish there but I haven't seen them. Still, it's a pleasant walk. There are two parking lots and both have restrooms. There are benches along the walkway but picnicking is not allowed. It's just a nice place to go for a walk. Plan on 30-60 minutes. Note: the road from Midway to the springs is not paved, so driving it is rough. The route through the Alpine Loop is fully paved.

This museum is more like a campus. There are five different buildings, each with their own theme. One building alone is allocated to the involvement Louisiana had in World War 2, which was substantial, from industry to soldiers to POW camps. The rest of the buildings cover the war more comprehensively. The displays are interactive and there's quite a bit of video and commentary. Obviously, the history covered is huge so the experience is going to take several hours. To do everything including the optional Beyond all Boundaries and Final Mission experiences, plan on at least five hours. The exhibits alone will take over four hours at a moderate pace. Admission is $27 plus $5 more per optional experience. Parking in the museum garage is $10 for 3-7 hours. Street level lots are about $8-9.

This destination is a perfect stopover outside of the Goblin Valley Park. It's popular so parking is crowded. There is no entrance fee and there are restrooms at the trailhead. There is an 8-mile loop but if you only want to hike for an hour or so, the trail will take you through a slot canyon. Right at the beginning of the canyon is a dried out pool that can't be climbed, so stay to the left and go up and over following the canyon and it will shortly descend down to the where Bell and Little Wild Horse join. Go up Little Wild Horse for a ways to go through the fascinating narrow path carved out by water and wind. If you don't plan to hike the whole path, just turn around at the space where the canyon opens up.

The falls were even more impressive than I thought they'd be. Shoshone Falls have been described as the Niagara Falls of the West. That may be a little generous, but the experience is powerful and the falls are quite large. They are also a reminder of how powerful and omni-present the Snake River is in southern Idaho. The falls aren't that far from either Twin Falls or I-84. If you have an hour to spare, take either the Twin Falls exit 173 or 182. You can only access the park from the south side. It takes about 15-20 minutes from either exit. The park itself has a fantastic overlook, and a ridge trail high along the Snake River.

Celebration Park's primary attraction is its petroglyphs. They were carved by the northern Paiute tribe that stopped in the area to fish. The park has several features that support field trips by local students. There's an old iron and wood bridge close by. The Guffey Bridge was built across the Snake River;  originally it was intended to transport ore from silver mines but they were trapped out by the time the bridge was operational. Overall the park is a quick visit for the general tourist. There are restrooms available, although they are only open seasonally. The same may be true for the new visitors center.

The Point Loma Tide Pools are located in Cabrillo National Monument. There is a small parking area with walking access along the short cliffs to the areas. Some of the pool areas are closed off to the public due to rehabilitation but there's plenty to see along the coastline. Be careful, the rocks can be slippery. The easy things to see are anemones and hermit crabs. Some of the pools also contain small fish. It's fun for the whole family to explore. Access to the whole park is $15 for a passenger vehicles, more for vans, less for cyclists, walk-ins, and motorcyclists.

The Cathedral of St. John the Evangelist is a beautiful church located in downtown Lafayette, LA. The cathedral itself is an incredible structure of light colored brick with white accents. On the property is a massive 500-year-old oak tree with a canopy that stretches over 200 feet! The trunk is 28 feet around and has an interesting shape due to the winds that have slowly twisted it over the centuries. If you're in Lafayette, this is a wonderful destination for a quick stop or for a service.

Just visiting from out of town and looking for a quick trail hike. This park looked interesting so I gave it a go. The Mountain loop is just under six miles and had a good mix of terrain. Starting at the Visitor Center, there's about a mile climb to the Kennesaw Mountain top with an elevation gain of around 600 feet. Nice view of Atlanta and the surrounding area. The trail has lots of deer and squirrels to keep you company. There are several other loops if you want a shorter trail.

The museum provides a fascinating walk through Intel's history with artifacts and interactive displays. It's small but there's a lot to read. A casual walkthrough takes about 30-45 minutes. We weren't offered a tour so I'm not sure if it's usually just self-guided. The museum probably is not going to be too interesting to young children inside but there's a play area outside. The parking and museum are free. There's a store inside with shirts and other branded items.

The MIA contains large collections spanning a wide range of time periods and cultures. It's well laid out. Plan on at least two hours to take the whole museum in. Donations are appreciated but the main exhibits are free of charge to members and non-members. There are several interactive experiences for children and special exhibits the special exhibits do have a cost). I

This is a quick stop for a unique experience if you're in Pismo Beach during the wintering season (October through February). The eucalyptus trees are covered with the  butterflies. There are helpful guides and various signs available to answer questions. Access is free. Parking is roadside on Route 1, so be careful. There are portable restrooms available.

This small park located in the Snake River and is accessible from the east and west banks by pedestrian bridges. The park includes the Idaho Falls Friendship Garden (also called Japanese Friendship Garden) which is worth a visit if you are walking down the Greenbelt just south of The Falls. There isn't much to do here, but it's a pleasant stopping point.

Fantastic vista. Good for sunsets and just generally getting a good view of Utah County. No hiking is necessary. It takes about 10 minutes to drive up from its base in Provo Canyon. There is a trail if you want to walk a ways back along the front. I didn't hike more than 30 minutes and it wasn't too strenuous. Kids can hike it.

This park is family-friendly with hundreds of campsites along dozens of lakes. There are trails for short, easy hikes and some longer hikes with climbing. The route from Kamas Utah to Evanston Wyoming has spectacular views including places to pull over and walk around like the incredible Provo River Falls.

This is an attraction that's worth visiting if you want to at least get an iconic experience in the L.A. area. The pier is the end of the line for the famous Route 66. It has an amusement park, restaurants, people watching, a beach, and more. It's not very clean and kind of has an old boardwalk feel to it

This popular destination is about 40 minutes from downtown, including the 15 minutes drive from the park entrance up a winding paved road. The lookout is crowded around sundown, but there is space to walk around and look at cacti or sit on rocks to look at the sunset and the greater Phoenix area.

This is a small park with a Pavilion, a playground, and a few picnic tables with grills. There if a boat ramp which drops into the Rum River. There are a couple of portable toilets and a drinking fountain. It might be a fun place for a quick get together or a canoe trip.

This is a eccentric small urban park. It's interesting to read the vision the founder had of conveying his religious views. The art is eclectic and folksy. A slow walk through it takes about 20-30 minutes if you read the signs and take in all the pieces.

Beautiful, well-maintained Civil War period historical site. The grounds include a large garden, restored, a view of the Rappahannock  River and Fredericksburg. There's a lot to see and do here, so plan on at least 30-45 minutes.

Rhodes Skate Park has a large number of advanced bowls and jumps as well as a variety of rails and hip jumps. The only downside was how busy it is. There is a small parking lot but no restroom building, only portable toilets.
This large, beautiful cathedral sits on a hill overlooking the city of St. Paul. It is clean and very well maintained. Services are held here, so tourists are encouraged to be quiet and respectful.
Clean, attractive little park with parking right next to the beach. The short paths to the beach are through thick trees which help provide seclusion from the traffic on the land.
The sculpture garden was recently reopened and contains several new pieces. It's not a large collection but significant enough to merit a half hour or so through the park.
Huge family friendly park with a large playground, creative musical instrument features, pavillions, tennis courts with shaded bleachers, and a large horseshoe play area.

The first of three buildings houses Howard Hughes' humongous plane, H-4, also known as the "Spruce Goose." It flew exactly once, for one minute, by Mr. Hughes. It is the highlight of this museum and well worth taking the internal plane tour.

The other noteworthy plane is an original late 1930's Douglas aircraft, which can be toured, as well.

The second building houses the remarkable recreation of Apollo's first landing on the moon, buggy and all.
Also, a sweet children's amusement plane ride.

The third structure, is the theater, with incredible 3-D space films. We enjoyed all immensely, and highly recommend bringing every age group.

A wonderful nature experience. See rare and beautiful desert plants and surrounding mountain vistas throughout the park. The awesome shuttle/tram service, up the mountain, is currently closed. It is one of the highlights of the park and would recommend calling, prior to arriving, to check, if they are running again. A beautiful lake and gushing waters on their historic bridges, is quite breathtaking. It is vital that one takes water and a hat, since it can get quite hot here.

From the moment you arrive the fabulous staff guides you from one enjoyable event to another. Loved the Elixer Comedy Show and the hilarious Stunt Show at the Mission; where hundreds of movies were shot. Particularly, the film 'The Three Amigos,' comes to mind.

The drive your own vintage cars, added to the fun. The carousal, run by Delaney, the sweetest operator, enhanced our day. Add, the train ride, all the variety shows, and you have a most enjoyable day!

Incredibly enjoyable. They have animals which I never have seen from such close proximity. Such as, a beautiful black jaguar, unique black bear and the remarkable Red Pandas. There are numerous animals every few steps and they are housed in comfortable natural habitation. We had a fun walk throughout the Zoo and had a delicious salad at their Cafe, which is highly recommended.

Animals who are abandoned, hurt, and abused are provided sanctuary here. They are beautiful taken care of. Staff exhibit caring and love to these special animals, which they absolutely deserve. It is extremely clean and it is quite obvious that all are well taken care of. We enjoyed our walk, throughout this park. Max, the beautiful parrot, delighted us with a warm "hello!"

Small, intimate museum depicting the life and time of the workers, who the built the remarkable Hoover Dam. The quotes and descriptions of their tiny houses, built specifically for them, was my favorite, i.e., "If you sneezed, you're house would fall down." A quality, quick place to bring the family. An adorable gift shop, as well, rounds out this Museum.

An extremely knowledgeable intern ranger provided us with a most interesting tour of the desert plants. After which, we went to the Smoke Signal Petroglyphs trail. A beautiful area with Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC) structures. The walk, with large steps, take you to the petroglyphs and beautiful surrounding views. A most enjoyable time was had here.

This stunning historical interior can easily be called 'The Marble Washington Capitol.' Imported from France, Belgium and Alaska, in a variety of colors, marbel adorns almost every inch of the interior. An impressive, original Tiffany chandelier welcomes you as you enter. This building is a must to see when visiting Olympia.

Historically preserved and a must when visiting Tombstone. This Victorian architecture built in 1882, is also the site of hangings of criminals in the wild, wild West. Original document vaults are in display. There is a charming gift shop. The docents are extremely knowledgeable and are eager to respond to questions.

This 125 foot monument was modeled after the Roman Trajan Column. It is 600 feet above sea level and surrounded by stunning views. One can climb the column which has no windows, however, a nice balcony is your reward on top. There is a small gift shop with souvenirs and information, as well.

Overlooking the water, snow capped mountains looming, this is a truly beautiful park. Concerts are played here. Recommend checking the historic, unique small stone building that houses a large fireplace. Locals enjoy walking on the beach, particularly with their children.  Much to enjoy.

This is our second journey on this cruise and we loved every minute of it. Relaxing and enjoyable. Stunning wayer views and rock formations. Reaching quite  close to the Hoover Dam was quite a highlight. The cafe offers salads, sandwiches, beer and snacks.

At the end of the road, in a beautiful, quiet neighbourhood, this park serves as a great nature preserve. Wonderful and popular for sunset, scenic walks on the bay. They have washroom facilities, a neat parking lot and a picnic area with shelter.

This museum will surprise you. In addition to the mining history, painstakingly detailed, it has great displays of beautiful, colorful minerals. Also, their gift shop is a great place to pick up interesting and affordable stone jewelry.

The flying live wild raptors' demonstration, is the closest thing to having a hawk land on your arm. This natural desert museum, with real animals, is a beautiful, educational park to visit. We thoroughly enjoyed ourselves here.

Educational with a twist of fun. Free aquarium, so kids can come again and again. Volunteers are amazingly knowledgeable, attentive and friendly. They conduct field trips for children. Also, as adults, we enjoyed it immensely.
The best place to experience adorable sea otters up close. One can watch them playing on their backs and grasping onto their rocks. It literally feels like they are smiling at you. A joy to watch.
We enjoyed visiting. Although the building is open 24 hours, staff at the visitor's center are there 9-5 (Sunday's 11-5). Great that they provide information and having restrooms is a big plus.
An amazing 1882 building in the process of painstakingly being reconditioned. The Tombstone Chamber of Commerce is in the midst of raising funds to restore it to its original glory.
A true historic, covered railway bridge to visit. The last one in Oregon. There are only eight left in the U.S. It has been beautifully restored and a great educational monument.
Beautifully restored gallery showcasing impressive works of art in a splendid historic building. Also, the gathering/information center during the Port Townsend Film Festival.
A rare occasion to observe loving camels. The owners have a special relationship with these wondrous exotic animals. They offer a variety of soaps that make great gifts.
A neat idea. They could benefit from a different pricing system in allowing visitors to view only the outside areas, for those who are claustrophobic.
Beautifully kept park. Tables and grilles are provided for awesome picnics. Bring plenty of water, one can get dehydrated in the Nevada heat.
A historic location surrounded by a park. Great place for a stroll and afterwards enjoy a meal at their restaurant on the water.

Gorgeous sunset, but it gets very crowded every day of the week. Worth the $3 parking fee, but there's quite a line of cars getting out after the sunset. If you get there very early (at least an hour before sunset) you can get a free spot at the Airport Mesa Overlook, about half a mile before the parking lot.

We camped here for a week in January and loved it. It was too cold to go swimming in the river, but there is lots of hiking and plenty of other things to do. Make sure to try their ice cream and homemade fudge down by the park store. Just make sure to make your reservations in advance, as they fill up fast.

Well worth the hefty entrance price. My 3 and 6 year olds loved it. Best of all was the dolphin show. If you want a seat, plan on getting to dolphin bay at least 30 minute before the show starts, otherwise you'll be standing on the back. Also, the 4D movie (included with admission) was great.

Not cheap, but worth it. We had a great time with our 3 and 6 year olds, but there's something to do for all ages. You can also find discounts on Groupon. Keep in mind that in addition to the jump time you purchase, you'll also need to buy their special socks if you don't already own a pair.

A must see in Sedona. There are multiple trails surrounding Bell Rock and once you get there, just start climbing. There are plenty of flat areas to stop and enjoy the view. Parking can be a hassle, as the lots fill up early, but if you come mid day, just wait for someone to leave.

A must stop on the drive up to Mount Lemmon! Plenty of parking and space to grab your own spot to enjoy the view. You can explore and climb on rocks, but keep little ones close as there are no guard rails or anything. I can only imagine what the sunset would look like from there...

Plenty of parking and there are covered tables next to the marked off, sandy area for swimming in the lake. The waterbed is rocky, so water shoes or sandals are recommended. Also, the water isn't the cleanest (there a bit of a smell), so if that bothers you keep that in mind.

Hidden gem, just off the highway. It's small, but great for a short walk with kids. Your sure to see turtles, rabbits, butterflies, and plenty of flowers. There's a water fountain at the beginning of the boardwalk and parking at the entrance.
Beautiful bike paths and pristine white sand beaches. They have an hourly tram (every half hour in the summer) that takes you and your gear to the beach from the parking lot or you can walk or bike.
Very cool. Great photo spot along the soldiers pass trail. Don't plan on swimming or anything, but they're nice to look at. And there's plenty of room to spread out and have a picnic here as well.
Simply gorgeous! Day or night, it's just so much fun to walk along the riverwalk. The river cruise is well worth it and there are so many nice bars and restaurants. Definitely a must visit!
Fantastic playground for kids. So much to do and lots of learning opportunities. The water mist was great as well to cool off. There is ample parking and best of all, it's free!
The hiking here is incredible. Try the Echo Canyon Loop for a moderate trail (3.3 miles) with incredible views. And make sure to climb up into the grottos. We had so much fun!
Very nice photo spot. I wouldn't come out just for this, as the hike is very short and always crowded, but definitely worth a stop on your way to or from another destination.
Beautiful place to go for a walk or a bike ride. There is a self guided tour through all the historic buildings. Start at the visitors center next to the museum.
There is a small admission free, but the grounds are gorgeous and there are plenty of walking paths. Also, there's a glad bottom boat ride which was great.
The park and campground were nice, but there is not much to do there besides the lake. They do have canoes/kayaks for rent and a pavilion/playground area.
A cant miss attraction in Vegas! Check their website for updates about times. Keep in mind that job very windy days, the fountain shows may be cancelled.
Very interesting to see the slave exhibit and hear about the history of the house. Bring your camera because there are some great photo spots.
Beautiful park. Great place for a picnic or to go for a stroll with plenty of good spots for a photo, especially around sunset.
Nice spot for a picnic. There is plenty of parking with pavilions, tables, grills, and even a small playground (in the sun 🙃).
Just off the side of the road. Definitely worth a stop to take in the beauty and to test out the acoustics
Definitely worth a stop on the scenic drive. It would probably be a great place to watch the sunset also.
Great hike, but no shade outside of the oasis. I would suggest doing it in the earlier hours of the day.
A hidden gem in Dade City. Our 3 and 6 year olds loved it and we all learned a lot.

It's only cost me $5 to get in. It is a very large Park. There is a section for the children that has a play area. There's a hiking area. I went toward the hiking area ate lunch under a tree and they went for my hike. It was just your normal Rocky hike path some vegetation on each side very little amount of flowers. On top of the hill they did have the nature center that was also very nice has a large collection of flowers and a great view. Inside they did have a ranger that could explain certain animals to you a little shop that sold some stuff and they had a movie about the park. All in all I really enjoyed the place I'll probably go see it again sometime soon.
dislikes: Very little amount of flowers on path

reviews_attraction.text: My granddaughter has to do a report on this mission, and her mother thought it would be good to film her report there. Entrance into the museum was very reasonable. We all enjoyed the mission plus we learned about the life and culture of the time. I am not posting all pictures as you would not have any surprises to see and learn about.

Really really enjoyed the park today. The weather was so nice. This is a park that I really really want to bring my grandkids to when they come in the summer time they can run, jump, scream, investigate and just check everything out touch everything.

I just decided to stop there all of a sudden it was already getting to be sunset soon. That's why I did not get to investigate the whole park the little bit I did see was very nice and clean I will probably going there before the summer's out again

I love sightseeing and traveling. I stopped on the way from Solvang to Sacremento. Looked interesting, spent some time walking around and feeling the wind. It was a very nice day and not too overcrowded. Wish I would have brought a picknick lunch.

Very nice and clean place they have a little outhouse you can use. It's dirt road I was only able to do 2 miles roundtrip.I saw people riding horses families people walking dog everybody was very friendly and nice.
likes: Diverse activities (horse riding, walking, dog walking)

reviews_attraction.text: I just happened to pull over. I decided to walk over to the edge and then I happen to see the little waterfall and the running creek and it look like there was some snow but it didn't come out good on the pictures.

Very small we almost missed it. But very worth seeing. The cave rock is very strange looking to me, I have no clue about rocks. The art also is unusual.the drive up is a bit scary as it has hairpin turns.
dislikes: Scary drive up (Note: While the drive is not part of the attraction, it's mentioned as a negative aspect related to accessing the site. However, based on your criteria, this should be excluded. Therefore, under the strict criteria, the valid dislike is:)

reviews_attraction.text: Loved it, I unfortunately started late in the day, and couldn't get to the falls. The walking and scrambling was fun. It was nice being outdoors, it was busy but still not a feeling of being overcrowded.
It looks like maybe in the last few years they maybe had a fire I noticed some of the petroglyphs you couldn't see. Otherwise very nice and clean. Has a picnic area BBQ pit campground and restrooms.
I have been to Tucson so many many times for the many years and I never knew about this place we just discovered it. It is so much fun as soon as I my grandkids come back I want to take them there.
We have the senior yearly pass so we were able to get in for free. It's a beautiful place it probably would have taken at least two days to see the whole thing. Amazing trees and rock.
I really enjoyed it. The hiking was easy unfortunately the little Creeks were too full 2 crossover for me so I could not reach the falls. But I'm determined to come back soon!
It's nice park with a small lake in the middle. Very clean and quiet. I saw some ducks and turtles there. There is free fishing there but you have to have a state license.
Pretty nice park, clean. Good play area for the kids. There is a paved walk around the park. It's very popular on the weekends for parties and get togethers.
The grandkids all loved it they kept going from the water to the rides and Back again. Only thing I saw was that the food was a bit too expensive.
Very nice and clean. Good view of lake. Good bathrooms, very clean. Allot of information about water, etc. Very nice and helpful curators.
Loved seeing all the old time buildings, mining processes and the actual mine. They even had an app for a self tour of the mine.
Lots of open space it was only $5 to park for the whole day. Lots of the trails branch off so you can have your own adventure.
Love this nature center. The trails make you feel like you really are very far from all the hustle and bustle of the city.
It's a beautiful Park but it was extremely extremely full today but it was nice to see all the people out enjoying the day
Very nice Beach. We enjoyed it. It was a bit long climb down a little bit harder climb up for me. But we had tons of fun
I only did the nature center I didn't go into the different hike paths. It's pretty nice. I didn't have much time.
Very nice and clean Park. Almost empty when I got there. Could use some kind of gazebos or other items for shade.
It was nice not a lot of people. Just some dog Pooh on the sand. Wish people would clean up after their animals.

There are over 500 petroglyphs at the Little Black Rock Mountain site. It can be reached by traveling south on River Road and continuing about 1/4 of a mile after the road turns to dirt. Look for a brown sign on your left directing you to the site. Turn left onto this dirt road and  you will find it at the base of a mesa around mile five. The site has rock art from the Anasazi, Great Basin and other cultures. There are easy walking trails to view the petroglyphs, a picnic table and a pit toilet. There is no water so make sure you have plenty with you.
likes: Facilities & Services: Picnic Table, Pit Toilet

reviews_attraction.text: A wonderful museum that has over 400 specimens of mammals, insects and birds from around the world. I found the displays and exhibits on taxidermy and how the animals displayed were made fascinating. The dioramas featuring the animals in their natural settings were so well done, you had to look twice to make sure they were not alive. The McElroy Hall was amazing with the collection of animals he hunted and collected for over 50 years. This museum is a must see!

The tracks in this area can be reached by a dirt road from the Warner Valley exit off the Southern Parkway. The hike is less than a half mile and there is an interpretive sign explaining the tracks and the area. There are three different types of dinosaur tracks in this once wetland area. The scenery around the tracks is stunning with the red cliffs and colorful hills. Please be careful when visiting and help to preserve this site for future generations.

Ridgeway sits at the base of the San Juan Mountains. This spectacular park covers five miles of beautiful scenery used by boaters, swimmers, fisherman, hikers, bicyclists and campers. It has three campgrounds with tables, fire pits, grills, bathrooms and shower houses. The beach is well maintained. There is a playground and a fish cleaning station. A small marina is on the lake and the visitor center is staffed with knowledgeable people.

A historic camp that was built in the 1930s. The Raber family ran the camp during the summers until 1966. The family moved cattle to the grasslands of Grand Mesa. It was a hard life with no electricity, running water or gas. They kept food from spoiling in the cold creeks. The women worked along side the men and the camp was listed on the National Register of Historic places. There is a short interpretive trail around the camp.

Sand Hollow State Park covers 20,000 acres of blue water, red rock outcroppings and sand dunes. Boating, swimming, fishing and hiking around the park are all great. There is even a dive park for those who enjoy scuba diving. The dunes attract OHV riders. There are picnic areas and a campground with terrific views. A small restaurant near the dunes serve the basics along with kayak and paddle board rentals.

Interesting place as waste water is treated in these wetlands by being recharged in basins. Water percolates through sediment below the basin to the water table. The recharged water is recovered by wells and delivered for use in Tucson's reclaimed water system. The area draws bird watchers and photographers to view different species of birds, ducks, turtles and other animals that inhabit the area.

The bridge has a long history. In1967, London started looking for buyers of the bridge. Robert McCulloch bought it for 2.4 million in 1968 and started the dismantling and reconstruction of the bridge in Arizona. The lampposts on the bridge were made from melted cannons from the 1815 Battle of Waterloo. The bridge consisted of over 10,000 blocks. The bridge was finished in 1971.

An easy trail to follow past historic buildings with access to the river. Rich in geologic formations, this trail is also a riparian habitat and one of my favorites. Great place to walk with your dog off leash..just remember to pick up after your pet and to bring water for yourself. There are restrooms at the trailhead.

The trail to the Ice Cave is only a few hundred feet from the parking area. These "natural refrigerators" we're important to the Native Americans. This one can be found off hwy. 14 just past the Duck Creek visitor center. It is very small and only has one chamber which can be accessed by a fixed rope.

Small but nice park with a fishing pond, grassy area, covered picnic tables, benches and clean public restrooms. There is a paved bike and walking trail that goes around the pond and continues to other areas. Fun place to watch the geese, birds and ducks. Parking is good.

Interesting visitor center with a wonderful gift shop and museum. Rangers are available to answer questions about the park, hiking trails and supply maps of the area. The museum has many interesting displays on the geology,  inhabitants, animals and plants of the area.

Located 11 miles southeast of Kodachrome Basin, this spectacular arch is well worth traveling the dirt road to view. The trail to the arch is short and the views looking up from its base is spectacular. There is an on site bathroom and a picnic table.

A wonderful theater and school located in the red rocks of Utah. Productions in the outdoor amptheater are classified as a delight for young and old alike and their Christmas Living Nativity is beautiful and emotional no matter what your beliefs are.

The War Memorial Center is dedicated in honoring the men and women who have given their lives since WWII. It is a beautiful building along Milwaukee's Lakefront which also includes an outside memorial to Vietnam and an Eternal Flame to honor all.

Quail Creek is a beautiful State Park that is open year round. You can enjoy camping, swimming, boating and other water activities. There are hiking trails and bike trails and the views of the lake among the red rocks of Utah is spectacular.

This small park off Riverside Drive has a covered picnic area with grills, a public restroom, a rock climbing wall for children and adults and riparian area for watching birds. There is a short paved trail around the park.
There are many museums within Balboa Park in San Diego and if you are short on time for visiting them all, this should be at the top of your list! It is a hands on display of the history of aviation.
Interesting and informative on the route Lewis & Clark took through this area. Explained the hardships they endured and how they survived on their journey.
Great store to find that special gift or unique item for your home. Lovely jewelry pieces. They have specials worthy of  taking your time to look around.
Nice park with picnic areas, grass and restrooms. This park also has access to a dog walking area across a bridge and along the Virgin River.

Cliff jumping:
This is a popular cliff jumping spot, but because of the swell and slippery rocks, getting back out of the water can and has been dangerous for a few unlucky individuals. I won’t explain how to safely get out because it will be more confusing than it’s worth. I suggest looking up YouTube videos and/or watching locals at the actual spot. But overall, just remember to stay calm and let the swells go past before attempting to get out. Also, it can be tempting to swim further away from the main jumping spot because it *looks* easier to get out. Don’t do this - the rock is extremely slippery with little to nothing to grab onto.

If you are tired of the crowds of some the touristy beaches, check out this place. Even though there are a lot of people, you still have big parts of the beach to yourself, a beautiful mountain backdrop, and oceanic sounds as opposed to traffic and construction. A couple of things to be aware of:

Bring some cash, a local might be cutting fresh coconuts for a couple of bucks

The Seven Mile Bridge was a part of the Flagler Train line that opened the way for people to travel to Key West Florida by train instead of boats. In the 1930's the rail way was converted into a auto highway to Key West,and Florida keys. The old 7mile bridge was apart of that highway until the 1980's when new modifications were made to the highway. The old section was not a part of the new updates. Now it's a walking path over open water so far out. Not open the car traffic anymore. You sure can take some beautiful pictures out there thou.

Did most of the tails in one afternoon, mostly easy to do. There was a really nice wind coming from the bay to keep me cool.

A nice little in downtown San Antonio to get away from all the busy streets and relax by a waterfall at the Japanese tea garden. This is a beautiful place to do a a little walking around. They have a lot of colorful flowers, walk ways along the coy ponds and even some overlooks.

A great little place to stop in and get a really fresh beer 🍻 the service was amazing also even if it wasn’t busy on a Friday evening. The place would be even better with more food menu options to choose from, games and more music when they have the food trucks too.

This is a really Nice place 👍 to come and relax or go for a little walk. It has a lot to offer with free easy parking, walking trials and clean public bathrooms. There was also people playing music for your enjoyment and a really nice museum and hotel close by.

This is a really nice park on the lake with lots of shoreline and great campsites right on the water too. The boat ramp set up for good sized boats too. There is a few hiking trails for hiking and some cliffs for jumping in the water.

Such an amazing place with so many spectacular views!!  You can drive up or do the 4 mile hike which is more like 4.5 miles or steep hard hiking !! There is no shuttle or bus back down to the bottom so make sure to plan.

This is on of the most iconic hotels and Casios in The new part of Las Vegas 👍👍 great rooms, slots, tables, shopping, entertainment and even the many pools where great too. I will definitely be going back again.👍

Probably the best go karting place in SA but that’s not saying much.  We did 3 races and every one was several slow cation laps because of bad drivers. We also had to wait in the cars for over 20 mins each time 🤔
If you like the outdoors, hiking, camping ⛺️ and great views then this is the place to come. The drive up the mountain ⛰ is very twisty and can be busy when they are doing the peddle bike 🚲 ridding
A nice little park on the lake with some picnic tables and a boat ramp. The beaches are alright just a little rocky. You can drive right up to the water set up your tent and grill out
I drove over to the USF riverfront park to get some fresh air and check it out. Super private and small-- has old boat ramp that is no longer in use, but still a really nice park 👍👍
A really nice park with some flat easy trials to up hill challenging trails. There is a lot of trials out in the cow pastures so watch out for the cow poo 💩
A nice park on the lake with a rocky trail down to the lake. The shore line is nice for most of it. There was a lot of trash along the rocky cliffs though.
We came, we saw, but it didn’t blow 😂 you have to come when there is big enough waves and the right tide to see it. This is still a nice spot for the view

This is a great little hike (with nice stairs and hand rails) at the top is an amazing view especially at sunset 🌅
The parking lot can fill up quick.
A very nice little park on the riverfront, in the downtown area of Tamp. The park can be a little busy and crowed depending on the day and the event.

A nice park on the lake. You can come and do some relaxing or rent a paddle board and paddle around the lake.
It will get very busy on the weekends.
A neat little pull off that over looks both sides of the dam. If the water is not high enough there isn’t much action to see
dislikes: Limited activity when water level is low

reviews_attraction.text: A really nice park 👍. This place is a pretty good size park with lots of stuff to do, it can be kinda busy at times though.
A really nice park with some good hiking trails, newer public restrooms, nice camping sites and the river to swim in.
A really nice museum on the top of the hill. They have a lot of great information and pics too. Very friendly staff
A really nice place to go for a hike, they have easy to hard trails, or take your horse 🐎 or peddle bike.
One of the best TX state parks in this part of TX. Lots of camping ⛺️, hiking trails and a nice big lake.
A very nice little park on the river 👍 a nice Boat Ramp with some parking, but not a lot.

This review is on the mine site within the park. The museum in the visitor center is very small. There is the old mine site and the owners home site here. The only way to see anything beyond exteriors and gardens is on tours that were too long (approx. one hour each). There was too much talking by volunteers before entering the buildings instead of viewing and talking as you go through the buildings.

This is not the tallest lighthouse that I have been in but it may be the busiest. Saturday two weeks ago, there was a waiting list to climb the tower. The parking lot was almost full and people every where in this park even though it was very windy. Considering the lovely park, the beautiful views, an enjoyable lighthouse tour, the light keeper's house and the great staff I definitely give 5 stars.

We saw the falls sign on I-70 and got off. The state park was very busy on this nice Sunday. The staff helped us and others with overflow parking. Then we took the short walk to the falls and were blown away by the 3 side by side falls. This was unique in many ways. Water flows here all year. If you like waterfalls this is a must see in Colorado. So glad that decided to visit.

This is the largest air museum that I have ever visited. Bring your walking shoes to explore the four huge buildings full of planes, exhibits and history.
Even though this is a museum about the air force it is also a museum about the history of planes and the evolution of flight. The displays are as interesting as the planes. This is a must see, so add it to your bucket list.

We took the scenic drive from Grand Lake to Estes Park with the detour to Bear Lake. Amazing views. Another National Park that is too loved as you have to take a shuttle to Bear Lake and Alberta Falls due to very limited parking. Alberta Falls is lovely. This was a moderate hike. We spent 5 hours doing the drive and the Bear Lake, Alberta Falls area.

This is one of the best zoos that I have visited in our country. They have provided great habitats for the animals while still providing adequate visitor viewing in beautiful settings. The themed areas of the park add to the overall experience. Helpful staff could be found throughout the park. A very nice place for "All".

This is a very large well done museum containing a recreated historical town and numerous other displays on Detroit's history. This may be the best city history museum that I have ever visited. The museum covers both the good and bad times in Detroit's history. I recommend seeing this when in Detroit.

I want to give more than 5 stars! Amazing! There are many unique features and formations. This is a more colorful cavern than others that I have visited. This place is professional run with very informative staff. A must see. Thanks and again WOW.

Lived in Washington all my life and this was my first visit here. There much to see and history that spans 2 centuries. This site played important roles in both WW I & WW II. This is a well maintained park. Definitely worth the visit.

Loved the falls but hard to find and the parking is limited to 8-10 cars. The sign on the road says Griggs Nature Preserve and nothing about Hayden Falls. Wooden stairs and boardwalk lead to a viewing platform. A great city gem.

The volunteer tour guides were great and very informative. I wished that I had more time to see everything here and not just the inside of the home. The furnishings are Victorian era but not the original owners. Worth a visit.

Most of the historical displays here are about the lumber history of this town. Overall this is a small museum. I did like that they used the old prison cells for period home displays. Even though small it is worth a visit.

Lovely horsetail falls. Still a good flow. Very short walk. Some large rocks to work around for best views. Thanks to the homeowner made the parking lot. Bring directions as you may lose cell coverage in the area.

Small but unique. Interesting animal collection. Great care went into design of each of the habitat areas for the needs of the animals. There is also a nice collection of animal sculptures throughout the zoo.

I enjoyed my visit here. The docents were very informative. I was here late in the day when it was slow and wrapping up. I may have given this 5 stars on a more lively day. I do recommend a visit here.
Small museum with large rock collection. Some other displays of toys and  miniature car collections. Another building has a few historic vehicles. The staff was very friendly and helpful.
This is one of the worst zoos that I visited around the country. Not well maintained. Mainly small enclosures. Not many animals. I hope the animals get better care than the property.
The lighthouse really needs a cleaning or paint job. The North Head Lighthouse is currently being worked on so maybe this will be next. A good use for our Discovery Pass Fees.
The Sacajawea Interpretive Center is small but tells more about Sacajawea's role in the Lewis and Clark expedition than most other expedition sites that I have visited.
This is a small museum. The history of DuPont is interesting and told in a chronological progression. Many artifacts are displayed as part of the history timeline.
This is more like and as big as an arboretum. The gardens are long walks between. The Japanese garden is small. The positive is that there are some nice gardens.
There were some nice displays here but it is a very small museum, therefore my 3 stars. For a state museum I would expect a larger history museum.
Visited in early June. There is a short trail and a few stairs to get to the viewing platform. The attached photo explains my 5 stars.
Visited here on the last open tour day for 2018.  Enjoyed the tour. Thanks to the Coast Guard Auxiliary for providing the opportunity.
Mainly display cases filled with historical items. I felt that this museum was too cluttered. The out buildings were not open.

The famous main road of the Las Vegas City. Popular tourist destination, lively and crowdy place, all hours of the day. Famous casino and hotels, commercial shops, bars and restaurants events and live shows endless entertainment options for all kind of tastes. We have pretty nice time there although we are not gamblers.

One of the beautiful places for someone to visit at the State of Missouri. We have visited it as a part of Historic Route 66 points of interest. The nature of the area is beautiful and there are many colorful signs, monuments and buildings related with the history of the road. Nice spot for rest and memorial photos.

Pretty impressive last floor of the Stratosphere hotel and casino. The city view from this spot is amazing, especially during the evening hours, as the city has pretty impressive lighting. Perfect location for memorial photos. There is also a nice restaurant bar with indoor seating and the same beautiful view.

Beautiful, peaceful and quiet park with many trees, shaded areas and benches next to the Cathedral of Santa Fe city. Nice place to walk or a stop for relaxing after visiting the more crowdy central places of the city. There are also a couple of historical statues, nice spots for memorial photos.

Pretty nice museum at the centre of Santa Fe city of New Mexico State. Both modern and classic beautiful and interesting paintings are presenting at the many different areas of the museum, from different artists. It has also a small yard with elegant garden, nice for rest.

Breathtaking views from the 103rd floor of the Willis tower at the heart of Chicago city. Touristic attraction and crowdy place place most of the time, with long waiting time, but a worth visiting place as it has amazing city views and good spots for memorial photos.

Beautiful small lake at the city of Santa Rosa of New Mexico State. The swimming is allowed, a pretty nice experience if someone can handle the water's cold  temperature (16 degrees aproximately). Scuba diving lessons are also offered, a place which worth a visit.

The central square of the Santa Fe city, with many cafe, bar, restaurants and commercial shops at the area. Lively place and popular tourist destination at the city, a temporary open air market was existing at the square during our visit. Nice place for all ages.

Beautiful picturesque central square at the old town of Amburquerque city. There are memorial canons, trees and trimmed gardens, as well as a place for musical events at the centre of the square (we were lucky enough to watch one with country traditional music).
