Beautiful small park with two old but very well preserved trains at the city of Kingman. We have visited as a part of the Historic Route 66 points of interest, a very nice place  for rest at the benches under the trees, walk around and take some memorial photos.

Beautiful and breathtaking views of the Grand Canyon, many nice spots for memorial photos at the area around. Crowdy place as it is a very popular tourist attraction, but absolutely a worth visiting one. There is also a souvenir shop at the Skywalk building.

One of the best locations at the city of Chicago. Many good entertainment options at the river side (e.g. bars, restaurants, playgrounds for kids e.t.c), shaded areas nice for relaxing and picnic, beautiful views of the river and activities (e.g. kayaking).

Popular destination and tourist attraction marina at the beach of Los Angeles. Crowdy place with many shops, nice for all ages, good for families and kids. Beautiful view of both Venice and Santa Monica beach, as well as panoramic view of the Pacific Ocean.

Pretty impressive modern art construction at the Millennium Park of the Chicago city. Popular tourist attraction, crowdy enough during our visit, with many people taking photos around the mirrors of the construction. Funny and entertaining experience.

One of the points of interest museums of the Historic Route 66 at Joplin city of Oklahoma State. We have not visited the indoor space of the museum, we have seen only the outdoor exhibition with traditional country tools, which is an interesting one.

One of the beautiful locations at the famous and lively Las Vegas Strip. The outdoor space with the lake and the rocks is a beautiful one, popular tourist attraction with nice lighting and show at the evening hours. Nice spot for memorial photos.

Useful information are provided and a small exhibition is existing, regarding the history and the construction of the Glen Dam. The parking area is a comfotrable one and the staff is helpful. There is also a shop with souvenirs and accessories.
likes: Facilities & Services: Comfortable parking, Helpful staff, Souvenir shop

reviews_attraction.text: One of the most picturesque neighborhood of the Los Angeles city. Beautiful canals and bridges, houses with elegant, trimmed gardens and beautiful colors. Walking through the canals is a nice experierience, many nice spots for memorial photos.

Beautiful national park at the state of Arizona. Breathtaking views of the Colorado river and the amazing rock formations which have the shape of a horseshoe. Many nice spots for memorial photos, attention is needed at the edge of the rocks.

Popular fountain at the Millennium park of the Chicago city. Families and kids were having good time around the fountain which is a pretty interesting construction. Nice place for walking around, relaxing and take some memorial photos.
Beautiful park next to the Navy Pier with a lot of trees, green areas, fountain and gardens. Nice for all ages, kids are having a good time at the most sunny days, nice for walking or just relaxing.
It seems to be a pretty nice and interesting museum, at least from the outside, as constructions were made during our visit. Pretty nice lighting during the evening hours.
A modern construction theatre at the Millenium Park, we did not watch a performance during our visit but it seems to be a pretty nice place to watch one.
Pretty nice bridge but the access was not allowed for the public during our visit (We were able to take photos and videos only from the area around).
One of the points of interest of the Historic Route 66, at the beautiful and traditional city of Grants. Pretty nice spot for memorial photos.

Many old Carnegie Libraries such as this are wonderful historical treasures in and of themselves. For some communities, the limited space became too restrictive as the towns grew and they were replaced with bigger libraries. Fortunately, some have been preserved and are being utilized as history museums. This one is fantastic! The collection has been curated well in telling a story of people of area and providing representations of how they lived. Some items are not as localized, but are representative of people identified with the expansionism of the 19th century. One such item is a saddle that had belonged to Kit Carson. Check this place out. It's good for young and old. It's free. It won't take you but maybe an hour to peruse. Then, reward yourself with a burger at the nearby Burger Bar.

My sons and I were on a short trip across west Texas, up through eastern New Mexico where my older son was going to work for the summer. Monahans Sandhills SP was our first stop. We camped there. It was mid/late May and already getting hot. Driving through that part of Texas would make you wonder why anything or anyone would live out there. It was very windy, hot, . . . When we pulled off the interstate into the SP, I thought to myself, "the boys are never going to forgive me for this." We setup camp and drove into town to find something to eat. When we came back, the sun was starting to set and we walked out onto the dunes and it was like the world had changed. It took on a whole new beauty. We had a blast sledding the dunes and watching the wildlife. Don't expect fancy camp sites.

If you are interested in WW II history, military history, or just north central Texas history, you want to check this place out. In WW II when the Germans were invading European countries, Britain did not have a place to train pilots. So, Roosevelt quietly let Churchill send their pilots to the US to train as the US originally wanted to appear "neutral." The Terrell Airport was one of the few places they trained and its the only location that has preserved its heritage. Very nice little museum. A former mayor of Terrell was one of those British pilots who returned to Terrell after the war and married a local girl.

I almost didn't stop at this museum. I'd seen it on Google Maps. But, I had an itinerary and wanted to make sure I got every stop I wanted. But, having driven up there to see where Red River Station (Chisholm Trail crossing) was and Spanish Fort (site of old native American community and town for the cowboys on the Chisholm Trail, I figured I should at least check it out. Wow! Wonderful people who know their history. This is a very well designed little museum that has an excellent collection of artifacts and is educational and engaging. I would definitely go back.

I give National Parks five stars because I love our NPs. This isn't Yellowstone, Yosemite, or one the the greater ones. But, it's still pretty cool. The one thing that bothers me is that they hype the Indian ruins which are cool, but treat the battle site of the Battle of Glorietta Pass (One of the western most Civil War battles) as though they are storing it in a broom closet. If you're a Civil War history fan, go to the visitor center, spend the $2 for the  interpretive trail guide. Otherwise, you're just out for a nice walk in the woods.

If you're interested in 19th century American history, cowboys and trail drives or frontier history, you need to read about this man Charles Goodnight. He and his wife are credited with saving the American Bison from extinction. He is also credited with inventing the chuck wagon. His cattle drives with Oliver Loving provided at least some of the inspiration for the story Lonesome Dove. This museum was his last house.

The only thing not to like about this place is that compared to Fort Davis down the road, it's not very big or extensive. Yet, they do a very good job telling the story of this fort. There's more historic stuff nearby that I was not aware of when I first came here. I will return and spend a little more time the next time.

This museum is a wonderful old Carnegie library. So, if you like history, it's worth coming here just for that. The collection inside is a hodgepodge of items that make you wonder if you've come to a rummage sale. However, in talking to the docent and strolling around, you'll discover a few historical jewels.

Highly educational. Probably not the best for small kids as there are no "hands on" game-like activities that one find at the Space Center. But, it is like nothing else. My college age and high school sons enjoyed it with my wife and I. Get a discount on admission by buying the Island Pass.

Carlsbad Caverns cannot be rated highly enough. Everyone should come here and see this American treasure. If you come from late Spring through late Summer or early Fall, you can watch the bats come out of the caverns at dusk. They fly to Mexico during the Winter months.

This place has been on my bucket list for at least a few years. I live 3-4 hour drive north of it. So, it wasn't real convenient. But some friends and I scheduled a camping/hiking weekend there. It was everything I'd hoped for. We even saw a bald eagle fly overhead.

In comparison to some of the other (many) frontier forts one can visit in Texas, this is not spectacular at all. However, it was one of the first line of forts in Texas. The docent at the visitor center was very friendly and knowledgeable.

The Rangers there (two ladies) were awesome. They knew their stuff about the history of this important fort and seemed excited to share it with anyone wanting to take it in. Very educational. I hope to jave the chance to return someday.

This is a one-of-a-kind museum. This was the only place during WWII where women were trained to fly certain planes for various missions. Museum is somewhat small at this time, but hoping to expand.  It is very educational and free.

This was surprisingly awesome. It doesnt look like much from the highway. But the views up at the top are great. It is interesting and a nice little bit of exercise hiking around the rim or into the crater of the volcano.
My only problem with this place is that one has to be there at the "limited" right times to visit the inside of the historic structure. Otherwise, they do a good job of preserving what's left.
Out of this world gorgeous outside and in. Historic home of the Gresham family and later the Archbishop of the area. Used to shelter people who lost their homes in the hurricane of 1900.
What a beautiful area with camping as well as lodge options. Great way to get away from heat in the late summer. Nearby Fort Davis is a wonderful place for nature and history.
Definitely worth a visit if you're in the area. The Palo Pinto Old Jail Museum I preferred a little more due to its history. But, the docents here were friendly and helpful.
likes: Facilities & Services: Friendly docents, Helpful staff

reviews_attraction.text: You just need to go to this park. It's beautiful around the springs. Very relaxing. If you're a tourist in the area, plan a little time in nearby Gruene while you're at it.
Beautiful municipal park that we sometimes stop at for a quick break from our road trips through the Hill Country of Texas. I'd love to spend some more time here sometime.
Very interesting building that, unfortunately, cannot remain a constant theme with which to sustain itself throughout the year. Very photogenic building.
We got a personal tour from the docent there who was friendly and knowledgeable. This place was educational and engaging  for young and old alike.
Friendly people with some interesting finds in this museum that you probably won't find in many other war aircraft museums.
Tyler is a very interesting town and this is one of the reasons. You need to check out this place if you come here.

We stayed here for two weeks in the end of March, beginning of April 2019 in spot #18.  It is $14 per night unless you have a senior or Access (disability) National Park pass, then it is $7 per night.  There is an entry fee to the park as well, but we have the annual park pass.  Absolutely worth either price.  You are right by the beach!  No hookups, but they have fresh water and a dump before entering the campground.  It is nice because there are two dumps and two fresh water stations.  We planned to stay a night or two and then camp on the beach for free, but after seeing the crowds at the beach and the tide, we decided to stay here the whole time instead.  I’m glad we did.  The weather didn’t cooperate most days, but we had several days of gorgeous sun.  It was constantly breezy which kept the bugs away but made it a bit too chilly for hanging out on the beach all day.  The campground filled up most days but was quiet and relaxing.  Everyone adhered to the quiet hours and was considerate.  We have a solar setup and any site would be perfect for it.  No trees to block the sun.  Despite the cloudy days, we had no trouble with no generator backup.  There is no cell reception at all with AT&T.  None.  However, we have a WeBoost cell booster and we were able to get enough for me to work remotely.  There were a few times it crapped out, but for the most part it worked well, especially considering there was none without it.  We arrived around 1pm and didn’t have any trouble finding a spot on the beach side.  IMO, the beach side on the right (as you come in) is better.  The spots are angled and when you open your door, you can see the beach and ocean easily.  Here is the process for getting a spot. If you have arrived after check-out at noon, find an empty spot and claim it.  There are occupied signs at campground host site (to the left of the registration area) or put out chairs or something to show it is occupied. You have one hour after claiming the site to pay.  Since you have a spot claimed, you can go fill your tanks if necessary or just park your rig.  Within an hour, go back and pay at the self-registration area.  You will see the self-registration area immediately to the left when you arrive at the campground.  It is cash or check, and they have an area you can write your credit card information if you want to do that.  If you arrive before noon, you can pick an empty spot with no occupied sign or evidence it is occupied and follow the same process.  You can also review the board to see if anyone in a spot is set to leave that day.  The board is to the right of the self-registration area.  It has slots for each camping site.  The papers in the slots are filled out by campers as part of the registration process and it shows when they are leaving.  I believe the camp host removes the papers in the morning for people who are leaving that day.  If there is no paper in the slot, the site (in theory) is available once the person currently occupying it leaves.  If you see a spot like that, I would recommend talking to the current occupants and confirming they are leaving that day.  If they are leaving, I would recommend registering and paying for the site immediately.  That will prevent other people from claiming it since your paper will show evidence the spot is taken.  Then you can setup as soon as the other person leaves.  The stay limit is 14 days.  There are several access points to the beach, and you can be there in about 100 feet depending on site location.  There are picnic tables at the campground and at the beach.  There are showers, restrooms, and spigots for sand removal.  Dogs are allowed at the campground and on the beach.  As always, they must be leased and picked up after.  Corpus Christi is about 45 minutes away so I would recommend bringing anything you may need with you, but in a pinch, you can go there for shopping.  There are gas stations and a few stores on the island, but nothing close to the campground.  Overall, we loved our stay and will definitely be back.

This is a county park in Travis County, Texas.  We stayed one week in the middle of March 2019.  We decided to stay outside the campground in the dispersed area.  Technically, you can camp anywhere in the park; however, we believe there are only a few decent spots for RVs.  Camping is limited to 7 days in a 30-day period.  We stayed at Mudd Cove Mesquite Point and found a great spot right by the lake.  We were able to get level without leveling blocks after some trial and error.  There were several spots in that area that would be great for a RV of any size.  As of April 1, 2019, they are closing the Tournament Point area to camping, so Mudd Cove Mesquite Point will have some of the only RV spots (IMO).  Those spots are off Grisham Trail.  The areas down Pace Bend Road were not RV friendly.  Most were a tight squeeze, and many did not have turnaround spots.  Great areas in there for tent camping, but not RVs.  On Grisham Trail, you will find potable water.  It is easy to miss and in a horrible spot on a curve and hill.  It will be on left if you are coming from the park entrance.  The dump station is outside of the park, right before the entrance on the right.  Easy in and out when leaving.  Since we were in the dispersed area, we relied on our solar for electricity.  The area we found was perfect for that.  We were able to find a nice open spot with no trees and the weather cooperated, so we had no trouble with electricity.  The park was quiet and empty for most of the week.  Things did pick up Thursday and over the weekend, but most people were respectful and quieted down after 11pm.  We walked the trails a few times, but overall there is not a ton to do here unless you are swimming.  The cost for us was $20/night.  $15 for the truck and $5 for the travel trailer.  Day use fees are $7 a person which is included in the camping costs.  The employee working when we arrived was not friendly or helpful at all, but the other employees we encountered were very helpful and nice.  Overall, we will likely not be back.  The price seemed steep for no hookups and the park just didn’t offer enough for us to want to stay again.
likes: Easy in and out dump station
dislikes: Tight squeeze and lack of turnaround spots

reviews_attraction.text: We stayed at this campground overnight in late October 2018.  It was a weekday and there were plenty of spots to choose from despite being first-come, first-serve.  With the cost and location, I can imagine it would fill up during peak season.  I believe you can stay up to 5 months at the park at a time which is surprising.  There were a few people who seemed to take advantage of that and their areas were a bit overrun and trashy.  Overall though the park was clean and well-maintained.  We stayed on spot #25 on the west campground.  We did not have to level and we did not unhook since we were only staying one night.  That spot was away from everyone (all others around it were empty) and was nice and shaded.  All spots seem to be right by the bay, but you do not have a good visual because of all the overgrowth.  That was a bit disappointing, but it is a conservation park, so I’m sure they keep it that way for habitat.  We walked the entire campground and park when we arrived.  The west and east campgrounds seemed very similar.  I would not say there was a better side.  They have a nice boat dock area and we were able to see St. Petersburg and Tampa from there.  There are several fishing piers and a beach as well.  The beach was a little run down when we were there, but several hurricanes had come through the area recently, so it was understandable.  Tons of osprey and shorebirds throughout the park.  We enjoyed watching osprey eat their fish dinner.  We didn’t use the Verizon hotspot so cannot speak to it, but we had good signal for AT&T.  We also had a good number of TV channels over the air.  Each spot has water and electric and there is a dump station on each side of the campground.  Any size RV should be fine to stay there as well.  Overall, it was an excellent place for an overnight.  Easy access to Tampa if you want to explore it while you are there.  We would stay again if ever in the area.
dislikes: Some long-term sites are overrun and trashy

reviews_attraction.text: We stayed here for 2 nights in early May 2019.  We stayed in the Hackberry campground.  The park was completely full, and we grabbed the last spot 30 ft spot available.  This park is beautiful, and I can see where it gets it name “The Grand Canyon of Texas”.  They had some rain recently when we there so everything was green and beautiful against the canyon walls.  We didn’t have much time since we were only able to stay two nights, but I feel we were able to explore enough in those two days.  I would recommend doing to the hike to Lighthouse Rock.  2.7 miles one-way and then when you get there, it’s about another .4 hike up to the area where you can see it.  I would also recommend you go to the Big Cave.  Very short walk for that and neat.  The park has a 10% grade and all campgrounds are at the bottom of the canyon.  We had no trouble in our 30 ft travel trailer with our Ram 2500.  The visitor center had a disappointing selection of souvenirs but go there for the view.  We stayed on site #2 in Hackberry which was 30 ft long.  We had no trouble getting in and had enough room to park the truck in front of the trailer (at an angle).  Site was level as well.  We had no cell service at all without a booster.  With a booster, we had no Verizon, but enough AT&T to use internet.  We were even able to stream Game of Thrones one evening.  The park was quiet at night.  I would have liked to have stayed maybe one more night to explore more, but two days worked for us.  Nothing around the park as far as services, so bring what you need.  There is a store at the park that has a few essentials at a high cost.  Overall, I was a great stay and we would stay again.  $24 price reflects camping only.  There is also a $8/person day use fee if you do not have a Texas State Park pass.

We stayed here for 4 nights in early May 2019.  We stayed in the Red Arroyo Campground at the South entrance of the park.  The best thing about this park is the amount of space between spots.  Plenty of space between you and your neighbors.  The park is beautiful and very quiet.  When we were there the wildflowers were in full bloom.  Spots are water and electric only, but there is a dump onsite.  We had spot #13 and it was steep, but we were able to tuck our 30ft trailer at the bottom where it leveled out.  No levelers required.  The park has many trails for hiking and biking.  Some of the trails were a bit muddy, but they had recently had rain.  Cell phone service was good.  We were able to get internet through the hotspot.  Overall, it was a nice stay and we would stay here again.

Not as good as Kennedy Space Center, but if you don't compare this one was excellent in its own right. You can get through it in a day, but if you do nothing else you have to do the bus tour. It takes you to historic mission control were all the famous launches were tracked and controlled. It also takes you to the still used astronaut training facility and vehicle area where ideas are being tested for the next missions. Very neat to see inside buildings that are still being used for training and research. You end the tour with a Saturn V rocket which is always neat to see. The inside exhibits are nice and lots of great info. If you have time take in a show. Thought it was worth the trip and the admission price. Go to Randall's for some good coupons.

Beautiful park to stay. We were slated to stay 4 nights but the day we were leaving was going to be 50mph winds so we stayed 2 more nights. Easy access to town and the caverns (about an hour drive). Ranger frequently drives by and everything was quiet. We have a covered patio and picnic bench which was nice. We were in site #22 on the reserved side and the view was great. Price was very reasonable. Site was pretty level and easy to get in and out. Would recommend and we would stay there again.

Beautiful park and easy to get to everything. Pretty busy considering it is out in the middle of nowhere. Visitor center is nice and a has a nice video to watch. The scenic drive was just ok, but we have the national park pass so it was free. I wouldn't pay more than $5 for it. You can visit everything else for free. The Fruita section was nice. Would recommend the cinnamon roll at the house there.

Good historical value here. Small hiking trails. Museum had a good video on the history. Would recommend watching before you start hiking. Gives you a good perspective. Ranger staff were very nice and answered all our questions. Very knowledgeable about the area and the history. Would recommend a day trip at least.

My husband and I loved it. Very nice exhibits and staff was friendly and helpful. Especially enjoyed the dolphin viewing area, sea turtles and the river otters. Do not miss the 4D show, it was fun! We spent about 5 hours here and enjoyed it all. If you are a member of the AZA it is half off so a great deal!

So much too see, it is crazy. Didn't get to do the tour because we had the dogs. Very dog friendly. Everyone is very nice and had water bowls and treats at every hangar. Lots of planes. Very cool place to spend the day. I thought the price was worth it. Would recommend.

It was cool, but there really isn't much else there. Glad we had the National Park pass so it was free. Not sure how much it is otherwise. Nice to go once to see it. Don't miss the well that is a bit further down the road. It is nice and free to everyone.

Very cool experience. The town was laid out well and had a lot of history to tell. Lots of shops for souvenirs, food, candy, etc. Definitely recommend the shows, those were very good, especially the stunt show. It was worth it!

Not a whole lot to do here. A few hiking trails and the goblins and that's about it. I thought the price was a little steep because there is so little. I guess they can do that since it is so unique. Won't go back.

Well worth a visit. It is a pretty small area of prints but there are several you can see really well. Great opportunity to go back in time and imagine the dinosaur life. Would recommend for people of all ages.
Lots of nice gifts at the visitor center. The staff was very helpful in providing maps and telling is what we can do given the amount of time we were in the area. Would recommend a day trip at least.
Nice overlook. Very pretty. The road is gravel but nicely done so no trouble getting back there. Worth the drive. Not quite as nice as the Needles Overlook but would recommend going here as well.
Good little park/zoo. The animals were beautiful. I thought it was more "park" but it wasn't really. Just a small walk around with occasional animals. It was nice and very inexpensive.
Very nice, helpful staff. The movie was good too. It told you about the significance of the area. They told us all about the places to go to see what we wanted. Very nice!
Very cool to see. Pretty easy to get to with Google maps. Can't really seem them to well from the ground but they are small enough to get the idea. Worth a quick trip.
dislikes: Attraction Type: Limited visibility from ground

reviews_attraction.text: Worth it. Beautiful scenery. We didn't get to hike at the top like we wanted due to weather. We had to catch the return tram pretty quickly. It was still worth it.
Beautiful arch. You can see it right from the road. You can hike up closer and it is not a bad hike at all. Would recommend taking a look if you are in the area.
Beautiful drive. Took the dogs because we spent hours there!! Pull-offs all over for sightseeing and picture taking. Beautiful sunset opportunities too.
We took an awesome train ride to Cascade Canyon. Beautiful scenery and all train staff were very friendly and helpful. Would recommend.
Beautiful area! You can see Lake Powell and part of the dam. Very easy to find. Would recommend seeing if in the area.

Beautiful views of the river and town of Hannibal.  The lighthouse sits on top of Cardiff Hill which was supposed to be a favorite spot for Tom Sawyer, Huckleberry Finn and friends.  The walk up the steps from the very bottom street which is the north end of Main Street,  is strenuous at 244 steps, but there is parking  near the top.  There is also a rear entrance from Cardiff Hill Drive, which offers handicapped accessible parking. The lighthouse area offers a very panoramic view with photo ops of Hannibal and the Mississippi River.  The lighthouse was built in 1935 as a memorial to Mark Twain on his 100th birthday and it is the second to be built on this site.  In 1963 a windstorm leveled the old lighthouse and it was rebuilt in 1963.

Amazing, iconic home of the great emancipator and 16th President.  Lincoln lived here from 1844-1861.  This is the only home Lincoln owned.  All of his children were born here.  The house has 12 rooms on 2 floors and you are allowed to take photos.   The President's son, Robert, donated the home to the State of Illinois in 1887, under the condition it would be open to the public for free.  It was designated a National Historic Landmark on Dec 19, 1960 and a National Historic Site on Aug 18, 1971.

This amazing monument is a U.S. National Monument at Lackland Air Force Base in San Antonio, Texas.   The monument was unveiled on Oct 28, 2013.  The monument was designed by the John Burnam Foundation, which represents the handlers, dogs and veterinary support for all military branches.  In all my travels this is one of my personal favorite monuments, a true treasure!  Our military service dogs should always be greatly appreciated!

Boerner Botanical Gardens China Lights Festival features 40 large Chinese lantern displays which illuminate the nine acre gardens in Whitnall Park.  Running times are Tues-Sunday 5:30-10pm.  Each night staff lead a parade that ends at the main state where performances begin.  There are various food vendors with fall favorites like cider, caramel apples, etc...  We went last year and we're amazed, headed back up this weekend.

Love this museum, a baseball fans top of the list to see.  Incredible history of baseball on display.  Personal favorites are the Hall of Fame area, going all the way back to the first class to some of the early great and mementos from Babe Ruth, Cy Young, Ty Cobb and Walter Johnson.  A cornerstone from Ebetts Field and  Negros League section.  So much you won't be able to stop taking pictures.

Great museum with world's largest baseball bat out front of the building, a great photo op.  You can even have your very own Louisville Slugger bat made there and tour to see how the bats are made.  Cool statues of Babe Ruth, Cal Ripken and many other hall of Farmers, plus great displays of baseball history.  For the baseball fan this and Cooperstown are the jewels of baseball history!

Beautiful cemetery, nice grave setting for the Olympic light-heavyqeight and 3 time Heavyweight Boxing Champion.  Easy to find and on a corner allowing you to come to it from two different directions.  Comes with marble benches to sit and reflect.  When we were there there was small butterfly and bee flags planted out front of his grave.

Building is amazing, right on the lake, a cool art museum.  The building was used in the Transformers movie!  When we were there they were having a wedding by the large glass wall overlooking Lake Michigan and it was so cool!  Convenient parking is directly under the building and there are walkways leading to the scenic lake front.

Outside appearance is a great looking haunted house look!  The floors creek, the rooms are dimly lit just right, a balcony gives ways making you think you will fall to your death, the smells are right on.  This is a classic from 1980 and been upgraded with new features recently.  One of our favorite things we did in Gatlinburg.

Beautiful, quaint Woodstock town square is like stepping back in time!  The shops and people are small town friendly.  The old bricks around the square, the Opera House, etc... make this picturesque town a must see and visit.  The historic buildings have been nicely restored and add to this one of a kind small town.

One of the coolest Route 66 landmarks and one of the coolest vintage gas stations in the country with a cool deco look!  Even has history of Elvis having stopped at the diner half.  Just down the road is a piece of Blarney Stone landmark also.  Very cool when the neon is lit up on this historic site.  Don't miss!

Cool museum to a sports legend, Olympic light-heavyweight and 3-time professional heavyweight boxing champion.  Many personal items, awards, and cool displays from the life of "the greatest."  Not far down the street from the Louisville Slugger Museum.  Another must see is his boyhood home here in Louisville.

Nice family park, has a pavilion, Lake with fishing and paddle boats (seasonal), a zoo, softball fields, war memorials, a steam locomotive and more.  During the summer months there is an outdoor theater with productions.  In addition, the pavilion runs classes throughout the year.

A super cool stop on this great Route 66 town of Cuba, Missouri.  If you are into antique and classic advertising signs, figures, and great Americana advertising, then this is a must stop and see!  Just down the road from Fannings and the giant Route 66 rocking chair.

One of the most beautiful falls I've ever seen, with caves surrounding it!  There are 3 falls coming off the top and its a short walk from the parking lot.  It is a fair drive from the town and you may lose GPS, so remember the turns, but it is so worth it!

Great memorial and bust of Colonel Harlan Sanders, founder of Kentucky Fried Chicken in Cave Hill Cemetery.  The bust was sculpted by his daughter Margaret.  Colonel Sanders passed away in 1980.  A yellow line on the cemetery road leads to his gravesite.

Beautiful, historic and iconic grounds, well maintained and good parking.  The Statue of Barbaro, the 2006 Kentucky Derby winner is out front and it was announced in 2008 that his remains would be intered at Churchill Downs beneath the statue.

Very impressive art murals on the sides of buildings for this Route 66 town of Cuba, Missouri. They tell the story of the town's history and civil war era.  Truely a great work of Americana in this historic Route 66 town.

Incredibly beautiful landmark!  They now have paid parking, but so worth it.  The hike is sandy and a little tiring, but you won't regret it.  Make sure to bring a camera!  Best time is sunrise or sunset for photo ops!

Cool 70s memory of "the Fonz"  played by Henry Winkler in the television series Happy  Days!  Stands on the Milwaukee downtown riverwalk with nice restaurants with a view of tour boats going by and under draw bridges.

Loved this cool site, right out of a King Arthur's tale.  Incredible photo ops, nice grounds.  Try pulling the sword out, sit at King Arthur's seat at the Round Table and on.  Cool roadside attraction!
Nice photo op area, clean and informative staff.  Impressive Osage native American Indian statues stand on a walk up hillside next to the visitors center.
Picturesque, quaint Park not far from Bloomington/Normal, IL.  Boating, trails, picnicking areas, nice family atmosphere and easy to get around.
Great historical site from 1897, the site is being worked on right now, but still open.  A must see replica of Greek lore!
Great visitor's center with a great information area, displays and one of the best shops in all of the parks!

My MIL bought my hubby and I tickets back in January. We should have gone in February when it was cooler outside, but we were dawdling about and didn’t get here. Then COVID happened and they closed down for a bit. As soon as they opened, we popped in the car and came for a visit! We came first thing in the morning, shortly after they opened, so that the weather would be a bit cooler. That was a smart decision! There are some shady areas, but not a ton.
There are water fountains, bottle refill stations, and bathrooms throughout the garden.
There are large plastic animals all over the gardens, which are lovely in helping you remember where you’ve been. They are a cute touch! Meerkats, an elephant, wolves, bunnies, penguins, etc.
The trails are easy to follow and impossible to get off course as they are clearly marked.
Most of the plants are labeled, but not all of them. We saw a wide variety of cacti and plants. We came in the beginning of July and there wasn’t much that was flowering, but still very pretty.
We saw a lot of little lizards and bunnies. There were a few roadrunners, butterflies, hummingbirds, and pocket mice.
The Plant Shop was in the Garden Shop when we were there. There was a very nice variety of things you could buy with a small variety of plants.
Such a good experience and an enjoyable date! We definitely recommend to new Arizonans and those looking to experience the wilderness, wildlife, and plant life.
likes: Water fountains, bottle refill stations, bathrooms
Wildlife (lizards, bunnies, roadrunners, butterflies, hummingbirds, pocket mice)
Plant Shop with a variety of items
dislikes: Few flowering plants in early July

reviews_attraction.text: You’ve got to take this drive if you are vacationing here or if you live here. It’s beautiful and scenic. Calming and enjoyable. I highly highly recommend taking Dramamine or Bonine, if you tend to get carsick. The switchbacks on the east side are killer. I recommend starting on the east side and going clockwise around. Such a nice variety of plants, trees, scenery, and areas. There are a lot of turn offs so you can stop to take pictures. There is a gas station on the way up from the east side and it was insanely well priced! The Pit Stop, I believe it was called. Lots of areas where you could go on a little hike. Hemet Lake is up there as well. There are campgrounds you could stay at.

The west side is much more of the foliage and Joshua Trees than the east side is!! If you come in the Joshua Tree Visitor Center side, you will see most everything worth seeing by the time you have the option to take a road to the east side. On the east side you do have the Cholla Cactus Garden which is very cool!! There are bathrooms all over the place, which is fantastic!! Tons of places to pull off and check out different signs. Lots of places to take a walk or hike or even climb rocks.

It was just okay. Honestly, not worth the $10 admission. There’s a beautiful little koi fish pond that is really lovely, but that’s the highlight. The plants aren’t anything special. They just look like plants you could see anywhere in Arizona. It was just a let down for the way everything was described. I expected lovely plants and flowers and just had green trees and bushes.
The good note, the koi fish and the little ducklings that happened to be there when I was there!

I was so excited to come here and check this place out. There were some type of flying bug everywhere!!! The one spot underneath the one waterfall had thousands of them!! So that was a little weird. The ground area where you were supposed to walk had some sort of sludge mud that smelled funky and it was tough to walk around. All in all, check it out, but just note the bugs. I had heard it would be cooler here due to the water, and it was a little bit.

A great hike!!! It has ups and downs, but nothing too steep. It is a pretty narrow path, so it's a single file hike. There are a lot of spots to stop and view the lake, and overall, the view of the lake is gorgeous!! There's a nice cool breeze because of the lake! There is a decent bit of parking with bathrooms and picnic benches. There's also a charcoal grill or two. You can get onto the trail immediately and are able to just go!

A very neat place to stop in a walk around! There’s a large dog park, two restroom locations, soccer fields, and decent parking. They have so many plants, trees, bushes, and cacti. Many of them are labeled with little signs giving the name. There’s multiple locations with a map to share where you are. The Mesquite Bosque was very calm and tranquil. I really liked that. The Water Harvest Basin was super cool and visually appealing.

This park has a HUGE area of field where you could let your kids run around. It’s too bad it’s not fenced in because it would be perfect to let your dogs run around too! It’s got a playground and a basketball court or two as well. It’s right in the middle of the block, so it seems to be easily accessible.

I had saved this place to check out at some point in time, but on our trip home, we drove passed it by surprise! We were able to get right in and park. We were able to walk the whole way around the pond on a nice cleared trail. It was a lovely little place. Very picturesque!

I’ve been to numerous games over the years and every experience was a great one! The seating is great, but there are some sections that can get really hot due to the sun’s place in the sky. The food is good, but expensive. Honestly though, that’s every stadium.

A nice little playground!! There’s a basketball court, a huge field, and then a little dirt field. A couple of benches and a couple covered tables. There’s a water fountain and a good amount of shade. There are recycling and trash cans too. Nice little place!

This park is actually really great!! There is a decent amount of parking. There are restrooms, basketball courts, what looked to be a huge field, a great playground, and a disc golf course. All of this is right by a neighborhood and Buffalo Ridge Mountain.

A nice dog park where you can let your dogs loose in a fenced space. It’s always very populated and busy with many friendly dogs. There’s plenty of parking and also quite a lot of space that isn’t fenced in, if you had kids who wanted to play and run.

They were just putting on the finishing decorations when I was there, in mid-November. They didn’t have any of the big nutcrackers or presents out yet, so I didn’t get to see it fully complete, but it was nice for what we did see!!

The visitor center is delightful!! It was cute and quaint. There were quite a lot of souvenirs in the shop, but they weren’t app “touristy” and gaudy! It was a nice place and both of the gals at the desk were nice and friendly.

A park that covers the whole block!! There’s a parking lot, tons of open field space, pool nearby, basketball courts, huge playground, and the community center too. Also looked like there was a fenced in space for dogs!

It was a neat little place to go to! Plenty of free parking, which is great!! It’s a short climb up to the hole and you get a nice view from looking out either side of the hole. The rocks are HOT though, so beware!!
A nice easy little poke out in the middle of the Joshua Tree forest. A lot of Joshua Trees, Mojave Yuccas, kangaroo rats, and teddy bear cholla. There is a parking lot, bathroom, and trash can.
Honestly, I didn’t get it. We walked over here to see it and it was a bridge with big silver posts. I tried to understand the draw, but I think I missed something.
Gave a different view of the Grand Canyon and allowed you to see two bits of the Colorado River. There’s a lot of information there about the Grand Canyon too.
We had such an awesome time doing this hike with our parents!! Beautiful views and easy trail to follow. Tons of signs labeling the plants and various animals!
Stop here to grab your day pass for the lake!! It was $12! There isn't much to do here unless you are here for the restaurant or for your boat at the marina.
Absolutely gorgeous. Incredible to be here in real life. A bit of a hike to get back into here, but if you’ve got stamina and determination, so worth it.
Lovely people. Fun cave tour and an even better wildlife tour. Just neat to see animals you don’t usually. Would definitely recommend taking your kids!
Just a neat little spot to pop to and take some pictures. There were gorgeous purple flowers growing around it. A pretty nice statue!!

Let's be honest. The miracle mile is a wholly American dream. You HAVE to walk the strip. It's a bucket list items for any red blooded human. The lights, the sounds, and the money on display boggles the mind.

What you won't like are the smell of weed, obnoxious drunks, the nude cards being passed out, the many drug sick and mental ill on display, and the fact many of these things aren't an easy fix.

You can tell the city is trying hard to stop the riffraff from keeping away honest people. They are doing better in my opinion. Harrah's was the center stage for the sh%t show on display. That area is an avoid, with the other side of the street (Caesar's) being much better condition.
dislikes: Visible drug and mental health issues

reviews_attraction.text:
The videos don't do this justice. I watched the video and nearly didn't come see the show. Epic. Just epic. The stage is its own actor. The amount of times things change, and change in ways you wouldn't expect is beyond belief.

The actors are all ninja warriors. The amount of effort they exert to produce this show is mind boggling. I want to see the engineering behind this place. The actors fall, jump, and dive off the set so many times to wonder how many work comp forms have been completed.

This is a top rated show for a reason. You'll burn about two hours here, and won't regret it. Go see KA!

You will never be so mad if you hike to get here. Four and a half miles up and down. When you get done with the miserable hike you find an amazing view. The view however is spoiled by all the fat tourists eating ice cream. After suffering through a hard hike you'd assume some reward of exclusivity or peace but no! There is a road that goes here. Anywhere there is a road the lazy people will come. Save the energy for a real hike like Half Dome or Yosemite Falls. Drive up here and eat ice cream with the fat people.

Epic. Unfortunately very little parking. Locals have their own cones out preventing some street parking. We parked two blocks away and I’m not upset. Basically a look out with a bathroom and small pavilion. Kids enjoyed rolling down a grass hill. Did I mention the road to the valley is 4wd only? You’ll enjoy it if you rented the Frontier Pro-4x but not otherwise.

Who doesn't want a picture of their family under a massive arch of antler?! Oh and if there are a lot of people, no worries, there are four arches. Once you're done, walk around town, do some shopping, and come back in a couple years. Very touristy town. Lots of people and foreigners. I wouldn't want to stay close to downtown as I'm not a fan of crowds.

It doesn't take much time to go through the whole facility. It is a little small, but due to its location I don't think it would support itself being any larger. There is plenty to see, and the animals look well fed, and taken care of. The gift shop is a little pricey and small too. Definitely something more for the kids than the adults.

This is the only place that smells like a dumpster fire you'll ever want to hang around. Long hike through many spewing geysers. Most emit hot sulphur gas not water. Makes you wonder if your not on another planet. Very weird landscape. Make sure you go here. You'll get over the smell fast once you start hiking.

Small state park with one epic waterfall. Nice walk. High BMI friendly. Not many stairs, just enough unfortunately to keep people in wheelchairs out. Half of the trail doesn't really need stairs either! You basically pay $5 here to walk for half an hour, take a picture, and leave. The drive down is pretty!

Absolutely beautiful country. It was very green in late June, no elk, but a great drive. It does turn to gravel and there can be locals that drive fast on the road. I had to pull over several times to let others go by or was passed before I could pull over. Great spot for pictures and a drive.

Much better than I'd have thought. On par with most major city Zoos. The size is a little bigger than others! Lots of walking though, bring some comfortable shoes, you can spend the whole day here. The food court is indoors so you can enjoy the shade and A/C for a bit.

Get here early or fight for parking. I watched two tourists knife each other to death over a premium stall. By knife each other, I mean they threw cold daggers of discontent at each other until one relented, pulled away, and used his middle finger to say goodbye.

Probably one of the nicest city parks I've ever visited. Lots of stone walls, tall shade trees, and places to sit. Very kid friendly with several places to play. Great place for a walk or more. If you're in town its a great place to take a break or eat lunch.

This and Spencer are the best beaches I’ve found in my 2-1/2 weeks on the island. Hapuna is big. Plenty of parking. Restrooms are clean. There are chair and umbrella rentals etc. The only thing I didn’t like is that it is an hour from K Town...

This is the best park we found on the west side. It is more of a neighborhood park but the kids love playgrounds. I love flying 1/4 around the world to visit every playground within driving distance. Have kids they said... :D

It could be 5 stars if it didn't have the worlds most complicated turn around. I'm amazed I didn't see any slow speed collisions. You know the part in Austin Powers where he makes a 30 point turn? That happens here.

Perfect for families. It has two protected swimming areas and a large play structure. I've driven by several times and I never wanted to stop. Sad that I never did as it was a lot better than I thought it would be.

Not much of a beach as it is mostly rock. Beautiful views of Maui. There is a shaded pavilion and maybe I missed the bathrooms but there was a port-a-John. It was gross. Somebody needs to clean it more.
Who doesn't want to walk through a lava tube. Wasn't crowded while we were here. Even if it was its so big who cares. Had lunch just outside the entrance. A must see walk with few stairs.
Playground here is very new and clean. Early in the morning there was no one here. Not a lot of shade but enough that I wouldn’t worry later on when it is warmer out.
You don't need to stop unless you want some great pictures. Nothing here but a turn out. Nice place to stretch the legs, you've probably driven a lot today!
Lots of learning to do for those that did not read in advance and still you'll learn something if you did. Kids love the exhibits.
Did anyone else imagine themselves in Ocean's Eleven when they saw this for the first time? I did. Iconic Vegas right here.
Great place for a picnic and for the kids to run around. Or just a walk on a black sand beach. Saw some people camping too.
There are a lot of places along the road to get similar views but parking is limited and traffic is dangerous...
For a stadium it feels small so there aren't a lot of bad seats. We have typically left early to avoid traffic.

This hike was amazing! The entire way up you are treated to stunning views, amazing landscapes, and spectacular plants! You are hiking through a jungle that feels very Jurassic Park-ish, while climbing switchbacks and looking out over Kauai.

If you follow Google Maps it is actually pretty easy to find. The parking lot holds quite a few cars, but it does tend to get busy, so get here early, or later. The trail can get muddy and when it does it is as slick as ice! Wear good shoes and be prepared. It was perfect when we went other than a small section on top. There is a couple of park benches before you reach the covered picnic area with tables. If you aren't hikers or are scared of heights I would stop here especially if you have kids, but if you are comfortable scrambling and your kids are good with it than I would continue up. It's probably another 5 or so minutes to the very top.

My group went later in the afternoon and we were the only ones on the trail, it was so nice. Just know what time sunset is because it got dark on us on the way down, like pitch black dark. If you hear things rustling in the bushes on the sides it's probably frogs, or at least that is what kept jumping at my legs. They were everywhere! Hundreds of them. All after dark though.

Don't take the offshoot routes, stick to the well traveled trail or you may get lost, and don't do the shortcuts through the switchbacks, it causes erosion and ruins the trails, just walk around the switchback, it's not that hard! Have fun!

For what it is, this is a fun little area with lots to do. You can do the aquarium, dolphin exhibit, butterfly area, and lots of shopping. Everything is really expensive though, and it gets very busy. Parking can be terrible and you may have to walk a ways, but they do offer valet parking.

I have only gone to the aquarium, but hope to return to see the butterflies, the aquarium was ok, again, just extremely expensive, but it can be fun if you haven't been and need something to do.

This is a really nice 3 acre neighborhood park with surpringly lots of shade. It has a covered pavilion and even a covered playground. There are lots of trees and cool grass. It has a restroom, a basketball court, and even a sand volleyball court! There are some nice areas to picnic if you want too. It was very clean and everything was in really good shape. The playground was interesting enough to keep the kids busy.

Gorgeous lookout! This was definitely worth the stop, it is a very short hike up a paved hill to the point. There is a trail here that you can do a smaller loop, or you can hike all the way down to the Golden Canyon. The sunsets and sunrises are amazing here, and even the star gazing is spectacular.

It can get a bit windy and you are still higher up in elevation so watch the weather and bring a jacket.

This is a a really nice park with a weird layout. It borders a little runoff wash on one side, and the road on the other making it a long narrow park. It has a pavilion on each end with a playground on one side and basketball on the other. It does tend to get really trashy, so please pick up after yourself and maybe take a moment to pick up a piece of trash or two that you find.

This is a really nice park, it has a nice covered playground, a large covered pavilion, and a nice grass field. It's currently being worked on so the restrooms are just outhouses at the moment. There is also a baseball diamond here as well as some courts. The city bike path connects to this park as well so you can go to sun river or the other way towards Washington from here.

This is a really nice smaller park. More of a basic location, but it does have a restroom and even a climbing wall. It's never really busy which is nice. There is a great path that wraps around the park and makes for a really nice stroll. There is also some nice grass sections. It sits just far enough off the main road that you don't have to really worry about traffic.

You pass this arch on the way to Corona arch, and yet it can stand on its own. It is very rich with color and even the little pebbles that run through it are very cool. Don't over look it, and maybe stop and take a couple of photos. I wish I could see it when it was raining. There are a couple of spots where you can get this Arch and the Corona arch in the same photo.

Easily the best state park in Utah. If it wasn't in Utah it would be a national park. There are lots of hiking opportunities of all levels, great for the whole family. They have several picnic areas, places to walk dogs, bike paths to bike ride, just an awesome park. If you want a nice morning run or bike ride try West Canyon road right next to the Sand Dunes.

This is a pretty decent visitor center, I would say average. It's gift shop is smaller and it does have a restroom. The rangers are also very helpful here. Just make sure to get here REALLY early. The parking lot fills up and cars drive around and round for hours. Literally. Some great hikes start here and there are lots of chances to see wildlife.

This is a great turning around spot, and it has phenomenal views. You can keep going to the lake if you have it in you though. Look for marmots, bear, big Horn sheep, deer, and even mountain goats. This trail is very family friendly, just take your time and be patient. it gets busy, and there will be a lot of people at this spot.

The Broken Arch trail is a very simple but nice hike right off of the campground. It's not very busy, and the Broken Arch itself is superb. Make sure you go through it to see both sides and take lots of pictures. We seen lots of wild life along this route, even some deer. I think this is one of the underrated trails in the park.

This is an amazing hike. It isn't hard, but there are some scrambling sections. It is a smaller hike in distance, but the payoff through the whole thing is definitely worth it. If you are staying or just visiting Capitol Reef, this is a must do. It doesn't seem to get overly busy either, so you can have a lot of it to yourself.

This is a great neighborhood park. It has a 1,000 square foot splash pad for those extremely hot days, and the water is even re-used and filtered. It has a smaller playground, a half court basketball court, and a large covered pavilion. There are also several shorter walking paths. It's not overly busy either which is great.

When combined with Chirch Rocks, this is easily one of my favorite mountain bike loops. I usually start at the Grapevine trailhead, ride Church Rocks in either direction, and then finish off with Dino Cliffs and loop all the way back around to the car. There are several technical sections and a few really deep Sandy hills.

I had heard so much about the Spouting Horn, that I was excited to come see it. The parking lot was packed, and the viewing area had a million people all crammed in this little space. Then the sprouting horn goes off and... Huh. I was disappointed. Maybe it was over-hyped, but unless you were bored I would skip it.

This is a pretty neat overlook of the canyon. It is easy enough and mostly paved so you can bring a wheelchair and it's great for the kids. There is lots of areas to explore, but it's mostly an overlook. It can get really busy and the parking can get full during busy seasons, but it is a great stop along the way.

Fun little detour, It does add quite a bit of distance to the overall hike though, but why not. There is a lot of elevation change, and quite a bit of sand to walk through. You can see it from further away if you don't want to walk all the way up to it, but I did enjoy the hike more than I thought I would.

This is a classic, yet a terrible roller coaster. I feel like the only reason it is still here, or anyone rides it anymore is nostalgia. It is so bumpy, and I just closey eyes because I know the whole thing is going to collapse, yet, somehow it doesn't. It is constantly being rebuilt which is good I guess.

This is the first official, and arguably the best view of the canyon with a parking lot. I would get here early though if you want to enjoy the view by yourself, it does get busy later on and even the parking gets tricky. You also have a better chance of staying ahead of the fog if you get here pre 10am.

Fort Pearce is pretty cool, it was built by the Mormons to act as an alert and defence of their livestock during the Black Hawk "war" from 1865 to 1870. It seems pretty stable but try not to lean on it or climb over it. You can also see some petroglyphs down below for you want to hike for a little ways.

If you haven't been here before this place can be really cool. If it's a return trip there is not much new and it can be quite boring. It's a good place to bring visiting family and friends, and the kids certainly enjoy themselves.easy access, and not usually too busy.
dislikes: Lack of novelty on return visits

reviews_attraction.text: For the area, it's not a bad a hike. Very exposed through the desert, but you will probably see some wildlife. I went in the middle of June and it was hot, but being from southern Utah it wasn't too bad, just remember to bring water.
We drove up and down the road looking for this, and then once we saw it, it was like duh! it's right there! You can see it right from the road, or it is a short hike up to it. Must see.
Very nice loop hike. There are some sandy sections, but just take it slow and you should be fine. If you're lucky, you may even see some sheep!

Great place for a hike. They have trails for all skill levels and a nice short waterfall trail with petroglyphs where the water will flow just after a nice rain. Deeper in the trails it gets more untouched and beautiful but be careful in the warm summer months as you can never really bring enough water. There are also snakes in the park and lots of coyotes so be cautious especially if you go on a night hike.

Excellent little spot to take in the views of Cathedral rock and go for a little hike. Has restrooms and picnic spots as well as large open are for the kids or family to play. Hike a bit and find all sorts of fun stuff and excellent areas to dip your feet in the water and relax. Bring lots of water in the summer. Even though its cooler than Phoenix its still hot and you dehydrate quickly.

Excellent little spot to take in the views of Cathedral rock and go for a little hike. Has restrooms and picnic spots as well as large open are for the kids or family to play. Hike a bit and find all sorts of fun stuff and excellent areas to dip your feet in the water and relax. Bring lots of water in the summer. Even though its cooler than Phoenix its still hot and you dehydrate quickly.

Amazing place for the family or a date night. The staff is so friendly and great at explaining what you are looking at. The views are literally out of this world and its perched on top of a hill overlooking Flagstaff so while you wait for the telescopes on busy nights you can enjoy the city view. Wear comfy shoes as there is a little bit of walking but mostly waiting in line.

Amazing views! Really cool place to see and check out the views. A little high in price for my taste but the grounds are well kept. There was an event going on there when I visited so it was pretty packed but still really enjoyable to see and learn a bit of tales about the site. With the right camera angle too it looks like you're thousands of feet above the trees

Very cool place to see if you live in Texas it's a must, if you are visiting its worth the trip. So much history and the story is incredible. Its a bit washed out to a touristy spot but if you're a history buff its a must see regardless. A couple indoor buildings with grounds to walka round on outdoors so be weather ready when you visit.

Very cool place to visit and learn some history of the town and the region. Plenty of buildings to visit and lots to see. I love the period dress of the staff and the fun things they do like bake using the original style stoves or craft wood with original tools. Place is real fun to walk through late on a foggy night.

Very interesting and well kept museum. Lots of history and lots to see and even the gallows. Though rebuilt still very cool for the kids to see how the end was met back then. There is a room you can ring some old bells too. Worth a visit every time I am in Tombstone. Relaxed atmosphere and friendly employees.

Very cool place located in downtown with tons of shopping and food options. A relaxed atmosphere with beautiful scenery. You can go to relax and watch the ducks or boats float by or walk around and see all the sights and stores. Or take a boat ride yourself and see it all. A very cool place to hang out.

Nice little community park with softball fields and a dog park. There is also a basketball court and a skate park for the younger crowd. Would love to see them bring in a few more things for the kids to do but its still a nice place to get out when the weather is nice.

Great hiking trails and family friendly. Can be a bit crowded since its not a huge area but still great. Trails are well defined and well kept. I enjoyed night hiking here for some relief from the summer sun and great city views. It does get dark so bring a headlamp.

So cool! The history in this place is amazing. Very real cold war relic that is well preserved and offers great family education on how it works. Take the detailed tours they are worth it over the standard tour. Really cool gift shop too with real relics for sale.

Interesting bit of arizona history worth the stop to see if you're in wickenburg. The tree has been around before Arizona was a state and they used to chain prisoners up to it. Kind of a cool little piece to listen to if you push the button and get an audio tour.

Very fun place to take the family. Its intimate where you get much closer to the animals and the little rides are great for the kids. The aquarium is really cool too. Make sure to eat at Dillon's too and dine with the sharks, crocodile or the flamingos.

Really cool cave especially when the water is flowing a bit. The hike is steep so make sure you have good shoes. The rocks are slick too when they get wet so make sure you are careful in the cave. Make sure to check out the dripping springs too.

Fun for all ages. Various buildings with fully restored or original aircraft. So much history in one location. Many planes outside too so bring some sunscreen if you go in the summer and it gets hot but worth walking around.

Really fun place with the small ski lodge feel. The food is nothing special but the runs are excellent when Arizona actually gets snow. I like coming here in summer too and take in the views at the top for the family.

So cool. I love the artsy side of Austin. Very cool place to take the family and write on the wall what you want to accomplish before you die. Some folks are downright funny while others have some interesting wishes.

A great spot to come enjoy the lake with a boat ramp, picnic table areas, playground and restrooms. Parking is plentiful unless its a holiday weekend but this is my favorite little spot next to the lake.
A great little lake with excellent fishing and good swimming spots. The dam is great for sunset walks along the lake. There are a couple parking areas and a playground for the whole family to enjoy.
Really cool place. I went there as a kid on a field trip and have brought my kids back a few times. I love how it is decorated and all the history. They also update the displays. Cool vibe
Really nice place to go for a walk and feel like you're far out of the city without actually leaving anywhere. Awesome pictures and lots of wildlife watching.
Hiked up there once in the 90's and the gang activity was pretty crazy. It's gotten much better since then and is an amazing place to hike and see the sights
So cool! The vibe is laid back and many people come here to picnic or hang out. The views are amazing and the history is even cooler.
Go Dodgers! Love this ballpark. The food is expensive but you have to get the experience with a Dodger dog

Kasha-katuwe National Monument is, in my opinion, one of the most worthwhile sightseeing destinations in the area.  The monument is largely comprised of three main points; The overlook, the Coyote Loop Trail, and the Slot Canyon Trail.

The overlook gives a nice birdseye view of the tent rocks that give the monument its name.

The Coyote loop trail allows those who travel it to see some interesting rock formations.  That particular trail also contains views of cave where some ancient Native Americans lived.

The Slot Canyon Trail is the main point of interest at Kasha-katuwe.  This trail gets you right in the heart of the tent rocks, and leads up to some beautiful views of the canyon itself.  Owing to its spectacular views, Slot Canyon is probably the most visited part of the monument.  It can get very crowded as the day wears on, so going early is a must.

Kasha-katuwe offers several diverse options of viewing the tent rocks and the monument's other contents.  It is well worth a visit.

Being that I had never been to Alamagordo before I had no idea what the Alameda Park Zoo would be like.  The view from the road gave me the impression that there wouldn't be much to see at the zoo, but that was not the case.

While the Alameda Park Zoo is not the largest zoo I have ever seen, it does have several well-kept exhibits, and is much larger than it appears from the street.  I particularly enjoyed the waterfowl, and having the ability to feed them.  The aviaries were laid out well, too.  Taken all-in-all the zoo was well worth the small price I paid for entrance (4.00, I think).

If you are in the area, and want to see a moderately sized, but eminently enjoyable zoo with a low entrance fee, Alameda Park Zoo would be a great addition to your itinerary.

While not without its own charm, Riconada canyon is, in my opinion, the least enjoyable of the main petroglyph viewing sites.  Much of the petroglyphs are both quite far away, and barely visible from the path.  Still, what is visible is well worth viewing if you aren't pressed for time.

If you do happen to have time to only see one section of the monument you should focus on Boca Negra canyon.  It includes some light climbing and walking, but has a lot of petroglyphs you can see very clearly.  If you have time for a bit more hiking and sightseeing, try Piedras Marcadas Canyon.  It, like Rinconada, is more of a traditional trail.  If you still have time, then maybe give Rinconada a try.

I've never been to the plaza for a festival, but I have stopped by a few times on my way through  town.  The church is worth seeing at least once for the murals contained inside.  I've never been able to get inside the Bond house due to a lack of volunteer availability, so I can't speak to its quality.  The fountains are nice, and the Veteran's Memorial is decent.  The visitor center and small museum are okay, but nothing spectacular.  Taken as a whole, I don't consider the plaza a destination, but it does make a nice diversion if you need to kill time, or are in the area already.

I did some research before traveling to the Amarillo Botanical Garden, so I knew to expect a rather small location.  I wasn't expecting the entry price, (14.00 for the two of us) which didn't match the fee listed on the signing.  Once getting in, I was underwhelmed by the grounds.  The one saving grace was the large greenhouse, which was very nicely laid out.  Unfortunately, that one section alone was not, in my opinion, worth the price I paid.  I doubt I will be back.

The Poeh Cultural Center was much more elaborate in its presentation than I had expected.  The displays were both informative, and well presented.  The art collection was a nice addition to the historical and cultural aspects of the center.  Taken all-in-all, the Poeh Center is one of the better small or mid-sized museums I have seen in NM.  I plan to visit once the returned pieces from Washington are fully presented.

The cultural center is a beautiful building, but the galleries are tiny.  Still, the scant displays and the introductory video give you some level of preparation before you depart for the pueblo.  The gift shop is well stocked with local pottery and jewelry, and the cafe is priced similarly to other museum resturaunts.    All-in-all a pleasant, albeit brief, addition to the tour of the pueblo.

Based on the museum's name I figured the place would be some tiny hole-in-the-wall, with little to offer for the price of admission.  I was very pleasantly surprised.  Though The Kid does factor into several displays in the museum, there are a multitude of artifacts, weapons, and vehicles from well before and after Pat Garrett took his quarry.  This museum is well worth a visit.

I went to the Ballooning Museum expecting a quaint museum, with an abundance of Balloon Fiesta merchandise.  I was pleasantly surprised.  This museum has a wide array of information and artifacts covering not only the history of ballooining and the fiesta, but also displays that give insight into the space program as well.

I was pleasantly surprised at the size and scope of the displays in this museum.  They have some excellent examples of ancient native pottery dating back to antiquity.  Definitely worth the stop if you're in town, and have even a passing interest in the cultures and driving forces behind the history of the Tularosa Basin.

Mesa Verde contains a multitude of historically and culturally significant puebloan sites dating back as far as 1400 years.  Between the mesa loop and the various trails (some paved, some not), there is something for people of virtually any physical activity level to see and experience.  Mesa Verde is well worth a visit.

Lowry isn't the largest Chaco outlier, but it is, in my view, one of the most interesting and exciting.  Lowry has a section which has been stabilized, and largely protected from the elements via a cover.  It gives you an opportunity to see an ancestral site from a much different perspective than usual.

The trail was closed due to fire danger, but I was able to view the garden path and the house.  It was well worth visiting for those aspects alone.  The grounds are well-kept, and the volunteers were very helpful and friendly.  I will definitely make a repeat visit once the fire issue is resolved.

The ruins are interesting, but completely inaccessible.  The whole of the monument can be seen in a few minutes time, and would have not been worth the 10.00 entry fee if not for the reciprocal entry my receipt granted me at Tuzigoot National Monument.

There's not much to see at the museum building (both the art, and nature and science museums are located in the same building), but the free admission and dedication to display quality make it worth a visit if you're in the area.

There's not much to see beyond a tiny museum and an interpretive trail.  The ruins have been buried, and, in some areas, built over by homes and residential landscaping.  There are much better ruin sites throughout the state.

This is an expansive park, with a good variety of things to see.  Petroglyphs; a pueblo ruin site; the painted desert; several museums, and of course, petrified wood.  Definitely worth the time, effort, and fee.

The Farmington Museum is not very large, but they do have a couple of very decent galleries to view.  The small riverside viewing behind the building is a nice touch.  Worth a visit if you are in the area.

This attraction consists of a small museum, filled with examples of pottery found at the site, and an impressive interpretive trail that winds through the Besh Ba Gowan.  Well worth the 5.00 entry fee.
The replica uranium mine was extremely cool and educational.  The media room contains video clips about attractions throughout the area, so you're in luck if you don't know the attractions well.
I found the Pueblo Heritage Museum to be well worth the price of admission.  I particularly enjoyed the museum's collection of pottery and pottery sherds.  This place is well worth a visit.
The Petroglyph National Monument is a collection of several sites throughout the westside of Albuquerque that collectively contain an impressive collection of pictographs.
The Albuquerque Museum has a great mix of historical, cultural, and artistic pieces on display.  Taking it in really does give a sense of the social milieu of this city.
There's not much to see at Valle de Oro.  Honestly, I would recommend the open space trails, and the Rio Grande State park instead for animal viewing and atmosphere.
The garden is always in flux, which makes repeat visits more enjoyable.  The grounds are laid out well, and well-kept.  Definitely worth the price of admission.

Check out the 360 degree view from the Mt. Livermore. manage your timings and hikes to experience the nature's best. If you miss the first ferry from angel island, you can always go to tiburon and then take a ferry from there.

Nice organized tour. Good day trip with Round trip time less than 4 hours. The caves are pretty small for you if you have visited Carlsbad Caverns in Texas. Never the less the outside view is worth the visit.
Very nice museum . Lots of exhibits. Amazing experience and worth paying for. The van de Graff generator and the lightning show was really different and unique.must visit if you are an engineer.
