When in the Loop you should make time to stop at the Chicago Fed Money Museum off the lobby of the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago! This museum is great for all ages with lots of activities and learning opportunities and so much history its worth the visit. Be sure to have a valid government issued ID for gaining access to the museum. There's airport type security to get into the museum as well. You have a chance to see different types of current and old currency. You can have your photo take with $1,000,000.00 in a briefcase as well while in the museum. It's always a fun trip to take to check this museum out.

The Morton Arboretum is always hosting special events that interest many to come and explore. I know that it's always a fun adventure going on any normal day to check out the trails, paths and open areas. I especially like going when it's not as crowded this is usually at off times early or later in the day. Also going when it's cold or inclement weather seems to work! When you've decided to go please be sure to be prepared especially during warmer weather to keep ticks and other bugs off yourself wear longer pants instead of shorts.

While in Philadelphia you must stop at the United States Mint, 151 N Independence Mall E, Philadelphia, PA 19106 and go on a self guided tour. No photography is allowed inside but you can certainly learn a lot about how our US coins are designed, fabricated and the minted from beginning to end. There are amazing displays to help guide you from beginning to end for all that you see along the tour.

A trip to the Chicago Cultural Center is like going back in time with the architecture both inside and outside of the building. The Chicago Cultural Center is what was once the original Chicago Public Library. The ornate mosaics and art glass are well worth your time into this free admission public icon. There is also free wifi and incredible staff to help out with your visit while there.

Experiencing the First Division Museum at Cantigny, 1s151 Winfield Road, 1s151, Wheaton, IL 60189 personally is quite amazing to see what our troops experiences would've been like. I'd like to encourage everyone to take the time to go through all the exhibits and also tour the tanks displayed outside of the main museum building as well.

While at the JPMorganChase tower in the Chicago Loop you have to take a couple of minutes to stop by and see "The Four Seasons", 10 S Dearborn St, Chicago, IL 60603 which was created back in 1972 by Marc Chagall. With all of the great free public art on display on Chicago you'll want to stop by and enjoy this from all four sides.

I attended a Chicago Blackhawks game tonight that they unfortunately lost to the Minnesota Wild. The United Center environment is great to go and take in a great hockey game. Great food, beverages and overall everything. I always have fun attending games here. It's worth it to attend a hockey or 🏀 game here.

When in New York City take the time to stop and attend Mass at St. Patrick's Cathedral, 5th Ave, New York, NY 10022. It's historic, big, beautiful and you'll be right near it as it's in the center of Manhattan. Well worth the time to stop and if nothing else say a quick prayer or reflect silently in a pew.

Taking the time to stop at the Lincoln Home National Historic Site, 413 S 8th St, Springfield, IL 62701 is a great time for all in a group. The historical aspect let alone the home where our US President resided many years ago. It's all very fascinating and well worth your time to take a guided tour.

Be sure to stop at Dragonfly Landing, Garfield Ave, Lisle, IL 60532 to allow the young ones in any group to run around and have a fun time. Very nice playground equipment and splash area for the warmer weather as well. This is connected to Prairie Walk Pond between Main Street and Route 53 in Lisle.

Going through the Betsy Ross House, 239 Arch St, Philadelphia, PA 19106 and realizing the history of our nation and how this place held such a significant portion of that history. Truly amazing place and a must see when you're in Philadelphia. I look forward to my next trip back to see this again.

Philadelphia City Hall, 1401 John F Kennedy Blvd, Philadelphia, PA 19107 is an amazing seat for government in center city. Great architecture of this building and it looks great in the daylight and even better all lit up at nighttime. Stop by and enjoy this amazing building when in Philly.

Merchandise Mart Properties, Inc., 222 W Merchandise Mart Plaza, Chicago, IL 60654 is absolutely massive. Each time I've attended any conference here its' been fun. There's at least one radio station HQ'd here and many restaurants and obviously home design and lighting studios.

There's a well hidden gem in the Village of Lisle it's called Sea Lion Aquatic Park, 1825 Short St, Lisle, IL 60532. This water-park has so many areas for all types of groups from babies to teens to adults. Great spot to enjoy the warm weather when it arrives here in Lisle!

When in Philly you have to stop at the Rocky Steps, Spring Garden St, Philadelphia, PA 19130 and run up the steps yourself. Great experience like the Rocky film. Worth your time and you'll end up going into the Philadelphia Museum of Art at the top anyways.

Going with a group to Big Surf Waterpark Tempe, 1500 N McClintock Dr, Tempe, AZ 85281 is always a great time. If you go you'll not be bored and it also makes for interesting people watching as this is a college town lots of tourists here.

Walking across the DuSable Bridge "Michigan Avenue Bridge" is always a lot of fun. Tourist's from all over are always on this bridge adjoining "The Loop" with the "The Mag Mile". Great views of the city and Lake Michigan from this bridge.

Going to the Dana Thomas House, 301 E Lawrence Ave, Springfield, IL 62703 designed by Frank Lloyd Wright is always nice. It's located a little away from the capitol but still worth going by and checking it out when in Springfield, IL.

Going to the The Franklin Institute, 222 N 20th St, Philadelphia, PA 19103 was amazing. Great exhibits here and of course a wonderful Benjamin Franklin statue in the center hall just past the main entrance to the institute.

Going to Love Park, Arch St, Philadelphia, PA 19102 was nice on a walk around center city Philly. Quite a few locals trying to ask you to pay them to take your photo with your camera. Not ideal if you ask me I declined.
Great architecture at the Chicago Board of Trade Building, 141 W Jackson Blvd, Chicago, IL 60604. It's worth just checking the building out so stop over and take the time.
The best ballpark in Chicago is Wrigley Field, 1060 W Addison St, Chicago, IL 60613. You must make time to get tickets to see the Cubs play here it's simply amazing!
The Phoenix Zoo, 455 N Galvin Pkwy, Phoenix, AZ 85008 is a big wide open space with many different animal habitats. It's worth going to while in Phoenix.
Great stop while touring upper Wacker drive. You'll appreciate the art of the Heald Square Monument, E Upper Wacker Dr, Chicago, IL 60601.
Going to Greene Valley Forest Preserve, Naperville, IL 60565 is always alot of fun. Lots of trails and things to do and see here.

I have a lot of love and appreciation for Joshua Tree National Park. I recently took my family on a quick trip to Joshua Tree National Park and they absolutely loved it. We took this trip in August. I'm trying to get them out of the house to enjoy the natural beauty around us. They liked it more than I was expecting, so I'm appreciative of the opportunity for them to enjoy nature and the natural beauty. It's characterized by rugged rock formations and stark desert landscapes. Named for the region’s twisted, bristled Joshua trees, the park straddles the cactus-dotted Colorado Desert and the Mojave Desert, which is higher and cooler. Keys View looks out over the Coachella Valley. Hiking trails weave through the boulders of Hidden Valley.

The Fountains of Bellagio should be on everyone's Las Vegas bucket list. I've wrote about the Fountains of Bellagio before, but now I'm doing it again. It's so easy to take a great photo here. Seriously, you can't mess it up. I can't tell you how many times I've watched this water show, yet I still enjoy it every time. It's absolutely beautiful. If you can get a good view of the fountain and you're not standing behind someone to watch the water display, you're doing Las Vegas correctly. If you miss the show, just wait around if you have time. There will be another show. Don't leave Las Vegas without watching it though. You'll regret that decision.‍

Fox Hill Park is easily one of the most impressive public parks in Las Vegas. I don't have kids, but the amount of playground equipment for children here is impressive. I have no clue who got the contract on this park, but whoever is responsible for building parks (I have no clue who handles this) keep working with the company that built Fox Hill Park.

With almost 10,000 reviews on Google, The Mob Museum is one of those attractions in Las Vegas that you need to experience for yourself to see why so many people visit this museum every year. The Mob Museum didn't disappoint.

If you're a local and you haven't visited the mob museum, you're missing out on something special. If you're a tourist, this is a must see experience while enjoying time in Las Vegas. The Narcos exhibit they have on display rate now is very cool!

Fun fact for those visiting for the first time: over two million visitors come to experience the otherworldly magic of Bryce Canyon National Park each year, most between March and early October. Another fun fact for you is that Bryce Canyon is not a single canyon, but a series of natural amphitheaters or bowls, carved into the edge of a high plateau. My family loved our recent trip and adventure to Bryce Canyon. We stopped by the Bryce Canyon National Park Visitor Center upon arrival and the staff were very friendly and helped us plan our adventure. We will be back again.

The Carroll Shelby Museum is cool in more ways than one. Everything about this attraction and museum is cool. The cars inside of museum are flawless and spotless. There is so much to see for such a small area. I wish I could drive every single car on display here. After the Ford vs Ferrari movie, there seems to be more and more people visiting the Carroll Shelby Museum. The LV Plug team included this museum in our list of the Best Museums in Las Vegas - LV Plug 🔌.

The Carmel Mission was the second mission built by Franciscan missionaries in Upper California. It was first established in 1770. Today, the Carmel Mission serves as a museum, preserving its own history and the history of the area. There are four specific museum galleries: the Harry Downie Museum, the Munras Family Heritage Museum, the Jo Mora Chapel Gallery, and the Convento Museum. Very interesting building. There's a lot to take in. I'll be back again.

If you're visiting Los Angeles or Hollywood, Griffith Observatory must must must must be on your agenda. If you've never been here, you're seriously missing out. This should 10000% be on your California adventure bucket list. Fun fact for all the GTA fans out there: you can find a replica of Griffith Observatory in GTA V. The observatory is located in Galileo Park, Vinewood Hills, north of Los Santos, and is accessed from East Galileo Avenue.

With everything going on in the world, I hope I am able to visit the US Marine Corps War Memorial again. I enjoyed my last trip here and to the national capital. There are so many iconic locations here. It's hard to plan just one day in the nationals capital. If you're visiting, be sure to stop by this memorial. I'm a big supporter of our marines. They do great work. I also don't think they eat crayons, but I guess that's a touchy subject.

My skateboarding days are long gone. I'd probably pull a muscle or something like that if I hopped on a skateboard today, but I wanted to state that I wish I had a skatepark like this near me growing up. This is a top notch facility. There's a little bit of everything in the Craig Ranch Skatepark for skateboarders, roller bladers, scooters, and BMX riders. This is a great facility built for the kids of Las Vegas.

If you're looking for an amazing view of the Las Vegas strip, you're going to want to check out the Eiffel Tower Experience. Due to the current social distancing requirements, the wait for the Eiffel Tower Experience at the Paris Hotel and Casino is longer than usual. However, it is still a great experience. This is one of those Las Vegas attractions that you can't skip. I highly recommend checking this out.

Wow! I'm impressed. I can't believe that Fort Churchill State Historic Park and the remaining structure are still standing. Fort Churchill was named after Sylvester Churchill. Sylvester was a distant relative of Winston Churchill. Fort Churchill was built in 1861 and abandoned in 1869. I'm seriously surprised there is a remaining structure at Fort Churchill. Mother nature has not been nice to this landmark.

As you're driving to Hoover Dam, the Lake Mead - Lakeview Overlook is a nice spot that you can pull off the the road to take a picture. You can take a nice photo of Lake Mead from a decent vantage point. It's a little windy up here and there isn't a ton of parking, but I can't imagine people will stay here too long. This will be a quick little stop for a picture and then you're done.

The Coronado Bridge is very cool. One way to describe this bridge is breath taking. The view is amazing. It's a beautiful bridge. I enjoyed the experience. I will be back again. I had a blast touring this area. It's so cool. I love the ocean. I love traveling. I loved the breeze when I opened my window. I know for a fact that I will be back again.

I didn't know what to expect before visiting Manzanar. I didn't do much research in preparation to my trip to this National Historic Site. This site is one of ten American concentration camps. This site was used from March 1942 to 1945 following the Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor in 1941. This site is an interesting piece of American history.

Beautiful park with a lot to do. Exploration peak Park has a fantastic playground.They also have a splash pad. This old frontier style playground which is very cool if I was a child. There's also a great place to hike. There's a mountain right next to the park so if you're feeling adventurous you can climb this mountain like a pure Savage.

Wow this place was cool. I visited the Utah Olympic Park while I was in Salt Lake City the last time. We had a rental car in a few hours to kill so we drove up to the Utah Olympic Park. It was early June or so. There's so much to look at so much to take in. I felt like I was taking a walkthrough American history and excellence.

The campgrounds are good. The bathrooms are clean. The people and park rangers are friendly. Andrew Molera State Park is  a great place to bring your family to explore for the day or longer. We enjoyed our recent trip here and I look forward to coming back and doing more exploring. I had a blast. Can't wait to come back again.

A nice little park in our community. Aventura Park is a great place to bring the crib midgets for a little fun time at the park. Thankfully this park doesn't have a homeless infestation like a lot of the other parks in the area. There's a splash pad here for the kids to cool off during the hot summer days.

If you have the opportunity to come here around sunset, you should absolutely take advantage of this opportunity. El Matador Beach is one of the most beautiful places in California around sunset. My family loved our trip here. I will be back again. It's been great.

Word to the wise: bring water. You're going to get dehydrated. Stay thirsty my friends and have a great time exploring the Sand Flats Recreation Area. Have fun! I know you will, but seriously bring enough water.
One of the largest parks in Las Vegas. This is a great place to bring your dog, family, even your grandmother. Everyone loves Sunset Park. If you go near the water, watch out for the goose poop.
Larger park with a long walking path. Depending on the time of day that you visit, there may be more people than the walking path can handle. Please plan accordingly.
Another hiking trail in Las Vegas. If you're looking for a good place to hike, Buckskin Cliff Shadows, is a solid choice for hiking.
I loved my recent trip to Ashley National Forest with the family. We had a great time. My kids loved it.

Beautiful wild area that fulfills it's mission perfectly. Drove the entire park from South to North with numerous stops for hikes up to 11 miles. The mountains are stunningly beautiful. The trails relaxing and quiet. The mosquitoes are super friendly, following you everywhere and buzzing with excitement. I'd rate this as one of the best state park experiences ever. Staff are amazingly friendly and helpful.

It's a walk down memory lane. The exhibits are thoughtfully arranged and the descriptions informative. One can't help but get the warm and fuzzies going through. Of all the small towns we've visited in our travels this museum and the entire town exemplify the quaint, pleasant atmosphere of what we all wish life was truly like. An absolute must visit if you're ever in the area.

Very nice but small museum housed in an old convent. Focuses on the religious history of the region and is very well presented. Self paced and photography is permitted. Entrance fee at the time of our visit was $8. There is very affordable parking just a few blocks away at 420 N. Rampart St., and it's just a few minutes walk from there. Highly recommended.

The display is currently split into two segments. Downstairs is an excellent overview of Hurricane Katrina, with numerous artifacts to illustrate the horrendous impact and suffering . Upstairs you'll get a fun look at Mardi Gras and come to understand the meaning and significance of the costumes and events. We'll curated and a must visit site.

We love this park. Only a short half mile walk from home. Facilities for almost any outdoor activity and all top notch .

The newer trail system behind the golf course can be entered at several spots, and is a very pleasant shaded place to walk. Trails are paved and bridges cross the waterways.

Great place for the whole family. Very clean, affordable, and plenty to do. Unlike other amusement parks there are lots of rides suitable for smaller children. The shows are well done, and the water park roomy enough to not feel crowded. Food is reasonable. All in all a wonderful experience.

Just a small house on a side street in a small town, but boy does it bring back memories. The whole atmosphere of the town is welcoming. Couldn't ask for nicer people. Just one of the many places in Mayberry that makes you feel right at home.

A classic historical landmark with knowledgeable staff. The importance of Jefferson's contribution to the sciences and our history reveal themselves throughout. The ugly reality of the lives of his slaves is finally being emphasized as well.

A spectacular national treasure. The campsite areas are easily accessible and the entire facility immaculately maintained. Wild horses can be seen throughout and the bird species to be seen are diverse. We highly recommend this to anyone.

Spent a wonderful day here. The tour is very informative (no photos inside the house). Staff is knowledgeable and friendly. The history is interesting, the house and grounds maintained to good period detail. Very much worth a visit.
This is a Delaware treasure. It is a beautiful park with picnicking, a nature center, hawk watch, and miles of trails of varying levels of difficulty. Convenient and easily accessed.
One of the premier stops to see migratory waterfowl and shorebirds. Beautiful at any time of year, with something to see in every season. One of my favorite birding spots.
A lovely little museum with just the right mix of things for little minds. Exhibits are very kid friendly, and the Nature Nook playroom is a delight. Highly recommended
Small but informative museum covering railroad history in the region. We'll designed exhibits. Model trains upstairs are scale models of the more famous area depots.
Beautiful Lighthouse with fabulous views. Easy access. Don't miss the hiking trail to the high overlook just left of the gate going in. It's worth the short walk.
Beautiful high desert hike, but fairly easy. Spectacular views and the place is littered with huge chunks of petrified wood. The reconstructed house is lovely.
It was such a delight visiting the Roman, and brought back so many memories from my childhood watching the performances on TV as a child. Well worth seeing.
Well worth the trip. A treasure trove of exhibits and information. Staff is friendly and knowledgeable. They also have reasonably priced fossils for sale.
One of my favorite places. Love the hawk migration watch in the fall. Outstanding views of the Susquehanna Flats and head of the Chesapeake Bay
Really lively spot in New Orleans. Street performers all around and convenient to all the French Quarter shops and eateries.
Stunning. Just a short walk to a Hill Crest and down to the bend. There are a few Condors hanging out just north of the bend
A superb public park and performance venue. We attended a country music event here and were pleased with the entire facility
Awesome stop on our tour of Tennessee. Beautiful formations, and the falls at the end are cool. Tour guide was lots of fun.
This is a beautiful park along the river and we were lucky to arrive on a day when the reenactors were here
Stunning views and vistas of the volcano and lava field . In sight of Humphreys Peak. A place worth seeing.

Such an absolutely wonderful place to spend the day, and there is a campground you can stay at during the night. There is free, limited day parking, and you can pay for parking closer to the beach. We did the James Irvine Trail, which is about 4.5 miles to the beach, so if you plan on doing the 9 mile round trip, be prepared and bring plenty of water. It is seriously one of the most amazing places to hike, you feel like you are in a different world. Everything is so beautiful and green, the trees are huge, the silence is wonderful, and the smells are surreal. Such a magical place. Please respect this park, and do not litter or create sound pollution<3

It is a very unsettling place, that is for sure, but I am a history buff, so the history of everything was fascinating. There are all sorts of things here, such as actual letters from serial killers, art, paintings, their belongings. There are multiple rooms surrounding death, such a death devices, a mortician room, a funeral set up, car accidents, and a room of animal bones. They even have a room of suicide, and they have actual artifacts from a group suicide. It's pretty dark but informative. There is a room dedicated to Charles Manson. You will feel weird after, but will learn a lot.

I've been hiking here for years, and there really is no better place to go in the area! There is a really wonderful 5 mile hike here, and it will really work you out! I used to do this twice a week, and it would keep my body and mind in great shape. There is also a 1.5 mile hike, which takes about 30 mins to an hour to complete, and it's very nice. I love coming here. After it rains, everything is green, the flowers are in bloom, and there is a nice stream. Bring plenty of water and comfortable shoes. Watch out for rattle snakes when the weather heats up.

This was a nice, quick hike to the falls, but the trail does not actually lead you down to the falls, just an overlook. I thought it was a trail down to the actual waterfall, but if you go off the beaten path, you can get down there. The side paths are very steep, however, and you have to be very careful. We didn't go all the way down. It was too steep. I'm sure there is a better way, but we couldn't find it. Still a really pretty walk, there is parking at the trailhead, and you get a nice view of the waterfall from above.

This museum is seriously so amazing. The exhibits are all so detailed and wonderous. They have exhibits that look like the actual habitats of the animals that are presented. They have a plethora of dinosaur bones, and so many other amazing artifacts. They have probabaly the biggest gem and crystal exhibit in the country--we spent 3 hours in the gem and crystal exhibit!! We were here from open until close, and still didn't have enough time to take it all in. We will definitely be back!! I'm in love!!

Definitely a must see spot if you are at the Petrified Forest. So stunning!! You will get such beautiful pictures, and I took all of mine on my camera, and not my phone, otherwise I would upload some here. The hike is only 1 mile long, and there is even a handicap spot halfway up the trail for anyone who needs it. The Giant Logs trail is also connected to this trail, so you can do both, and then it ends up being a little bit less than two miles. This was definitely my favorite hike!

The venue is beautiful,  the location is beautiful, staff is very friendly and informed. The whole thing is organizing very well, but definitely arrive about 2 hours early, or at Lee leeeast 1.5 hours. Parking is insane. Do not park at the Hollywood Bowl. Park somewhere a mile a way, and then walk there. Parking will be cheaper, and quicker. It can take hours to get out of the venue. Other than that, this was great, and I had an awesome time!!

This was a beautiful, long hike, and it's not too rigorous at any point. It's worth it to hike up to the waterfall, which is beautiful. We stopped and had lunch there, and it was so nice. They even have a weekly program, where they bring robotic, mountain  wheelchairs, for people who are handicapped, which I thought was so wonderful. We camped over at Indian Paint Brush, and went to Red Rocks Amphitheater, which are all really close by.

It really depends on when you are here. In the summer, this place is packed with tourists, and you DON'T want to be here. At night/after hours, or during the off-season, it can actually be kind of nice, and feels just like any other pier. There are rides, restaurants, vendors, musicians, and much else. Its right next to santa monica beach, and right up the way from venice. You can rent bikes, and ride the whole bike path.

Definitely go to the scenic overlook towards the middle of this hike. It is a seriously beautiful view of all the petrified logs, and also the hills in the distance. The whole hike is only about .6 miles, and it is very beautiful. The museum right at the entrance of this hike is definitely worth checking out. It provides a lot of info about the trees, and when they formed and were petrified, and they even have fossils.

Super beautiful place to stop by for the day! The clouds and mountains are beautiful, and the petrified wood is spectacular! We did the .8 mile Crystal Forest Trail, the .6 mile Giant Logs Trail, and the 1 mile Agate House trail--they were all very beautiful, and there is plenty of parking for each trail head. We also saw the Agate Bridge, and it was very pretty. Please stay on the trail if you come here!!

My best friend just got married here, and it was beautiful. I can't believe something so nice and nature-friendly could be so close to the city! The house is beautiful, and the gardens are so beautiful. There are deer and turkeys walking around, and I loved being here. The house is so cool, and it is like being sent back in time. I loved this spot. Such a beautiful place for a wedding<3

This was such a lovely place to visit, and with the most beautiful sunset. The rock formations are amazing, and the beach is clean, and it has soft sand. The water is clear, and it is just overall a really nice beach to visit. There are really cute rental cottages, and a nice restaurant right on the sand. It was so nice hearing the waves while we ate dinner. Love it.

I came here for the Joe Russo's Almost Dead tour, and the venue is pretty cool. It feels a lot like the Hollywood Bowl, with stadium seating, which I'm definitely not a fan of. The location is nice though, and has plenty of parking. You can even get cheaper parking at a lot, and then you just take a shuttle to the venue. There is minimal cell reception.

Such a cute little spot, and it wasn't packed. Everyone that came to this little beach was super friendly, and cleaned up after themselves. The beach is connected to a really beautiful housing community that is on an actual marina. There are boats and yachts parked in the water, and you can even canoe/kayak/paddle board through the marina/community.

I've been coming here since I was a kid, and it's still awesome. So beautiful, the sand and water is really nice, the shopping and food is great on the boardwalk, and the lifeguards are wonderful. This is a seriously great beach. It does get packed on weekends, so get there early, or be prepared to park far away from the beach itself.

I love this temple:) everyone here is so very kind and respectful. It is definitely a place of peace and tranquility. There is so much information, culture, and it is a beautiful location in general. The monks make vegan lunch every day, between certain hours, and it is very tasty. Definitely stop by, but please be respectful<3

This is probably one of the nicest piers I've been on. The beach is clean and so is the water. There was a decent amount of parking spots, and not a ton of people. There was a neat little aquarium on the end of the pier, and it's free to check out. There are bathrooms also, and they are clean. Very nice.

I've been going to Hart Park since I was very young. The hike is great, you can see all types of wild life, including Buffalo. You can see William S. Hart's houses as a museum, and it is all very beautiful. The old train station is also pretty cool, and haunted. Check this place out :)

We had a great time here--tons of art. Be prepared to spend the whole day looking at beautiful art. Some is recognizable, and some is more modern. The museum has mummies from Egypt to Picasso paintings. Wonderful. It has some very original pieces of art as well. Very entertaining.

I love this little venue. It's basically a big strip of grass, and it's pretty intimate for an outdoor venue. I just saw Odesza here, and it was amazing, of course, and then I've also been to FYF here years ago. Always a cool venue. Love whenever there are shows here:)
This place is AMAZING!! You are literally swimming in a dune of crystals. So literally wonderful, so unique, so special. This is a really cool spot, and we will absolutely be back. Wow!!
Not worth it, its dirty, packed  and overpriced. Do not waste your time here. Go to the beach, or on a hike. Do something better with your time!
There is so much to do and see here. Prices are definitely worth it, and they always have new exhibits. I love coming here and learning!
I love this park! There is a ton of grassy space, and it's also fun to hike the mountain up behind the actual park.

Five storied structure with 20 rooms was built and maintained over a period of three centuries. The structure is more than 800 years old.

No one really know why the Sinagua people chose these types of structure. They were not related to Montezuma - the Aztec emperor. The dwellings were abandoned some 40 years before he was born. The top most dwelling is 90 feet above ground with a location that is protected from rains and floods. It is believed that the top most structure was occupied by the people at the top of the hierarchy.

Unfortunately, due to delicate nature of this limestone structure, we can watch it from far and let the drawings and imagination give us a tour of the inside.

Really beautiful structure which took 21 years to finish. The place is massive with 21 altars, 2800 stained glass panels, and a brand new organ with 7855 pipes. The structure occupies a whole city block and holds 15-18 masses each day! The place is busy with visitors soaking in the whole grand structure. Yet, if you take a sit and close your eyes, you can find calmness and solace.

Decommissioned Navy boat to be used as a ferry boat terminal, but it got away during the storm and ran aground. Time has taken its toll and and only small section of the concrete boat is left as a perching place for the shorebirds.

Concrete boats were never really practical due to their weight, but several were built in the US and Europe. Interesting historical period.

Two level bridge over the East River connecting Manhattan and Queens passing over the Roosevelt Island. Worth taking pedestrian walkway across at night for beautiful views of Manhattan and Queens side. It's also enjoyed in detail by taking the F line which runs parallel. The cantilever construction can be seen through the large viewing areas on the F line.

Mary Colter's design blends so well in the surroundings. Such attention to the details. The house has touches such as fireplace made with recycled broken pottery. Tiny windows to keep the heat out. It is not apparent from the outside that the structure is actually three storied.

Large space with petting zoo where kids and grown up can feed animals. Lots of Black Crown Herons. Ant Eater exhibition is also great. Flamingos in a small lake also attract a lot of attention from the kids. Owls are always a great attraction for kids reading Harry Potter.

Cool family adventure place during winter. You can touch and feed stingrays. Hippo feeding time is also fun. You can easily spend 2-3 hours.

Cafeteria is awful. Parking is outdoors and is about 5-10 min walk from the aquarium doors. It is windy by the water.
Moderate difficulty trail. Some areas can be water logged or muddy during monsoon seasons. Adequate parking with restrooms. There are some low lying areas which could be prone to flash flooding.
Oldest functioning lighthouse in the US. Survived the revolutionary war and nature due to its 10 ft thick walls and loving care it is receiving now from very able and professional Park Service.
You need a lot of patience here. Bears are mostly resting. But sometimes when they are out and about or swimming it is awesome. The way these large creatures carry themselves is unbelievable.
Great place for young kids. Bears, tropical birds, and sea lions shows are a lot of fun. Most can be viewed at an intimate distance - which is great for the young kids.
We enjoy our off season visits to this area. The beach is so wide, it takes forever to reach the water. Great views of the NY skyline and approaching commercial jets.
Tranquil and shallow waters makes this small beach great for all ages. Part of the park is still recovering from hurricane Irma as of Dec 2018 and is off limits.
Constant canopy of trees makes you forget that you are in NYC. A lot of native flora. Many bird nests. Good vantage points to enjoy unique central park views.
Truly stunning church. The place has the largest pipe organ set up in NYC area. The altar is also beautifully lit through stained glass windows.
Ample parking. Access to canal, lake and the river from one area. Abundant birds. Well maintained and safe trails on both sides of the canal.
Nice recreational space with ample parking and picnic area. Lake is accessible for boating and Stony brook right by is stocked with fish.
Similar to the most exhibits at this zoo, the birds have big space to be themselves, yet one can observe them in an intimate manner.
Kids live this place - endlessly climbing the rocks and looking for turtles nearby in the lake. We love the views from this place.
Nice but small botanical garden. Not as wooded and many areas are off limits to public. Bamboo garden is a nice place to visit.
Lewis Carroll tale frozen in time in this intricately detailed bronze statue. Large enough for many kids to climb up and play!
More like a an open space than a park with trees. Good place to watch stunning sunsets and safe area for kids to run around.
A small park with couple of tennis courts, baseball field, and a kids' play area. Among tall old trees which is really nice.
Ridge trail is rocky in some places and descent can be over boulders. Great overall. The place is busy during the weekends.
Lots of information, but watch tower was disappointing. There is a platform for an Osprey nest, but it was not occupied.

Just like almost all national parks, this park is incredible and very different from the other ones. These are the top things that I think are the most unique:
1. Oasises (Fortynine Palms trail, Lost Palms trail) 🌴
They look magical. It’s a hot dry desert everywhere and suddenly you see big juicy palm trees, green bushes and bird and water! The contrast is unbelievable. Highly recommend Fortynine Palms trail, you can actually get inside the oasis, whereas at Lost Palms trail you will only see it from distance.
2. Cacti (Cacti Garden) 🌵
This is just a very interesting place, the cacti are amazing. A short stop but a great experience.
3. Deep desert (Lost Palms trail) 🏜
Unlike the most of the other trails, this trail goes far from the road, it’s not crowded, and it gives you the feeling that you’re actually deep in the desert. Great experience.
4. Bighorn sheep (Ryan Mountain trail) 🐐
If you’re lucky (and luck largely depends on how early you go), you’ll see these courageous inhabitants of the unfriendly desert - the bighorn sheep. They’re amazing.
5. Panoramic views (Keys View, Ryan Mountain, Fortynine Palms, Mastodon Peak).
6. Rock formations (Arch Rock, Hidden Village trail).
Climb a bit and take nice pictures.
7. Body of water in the middle of desert (Barker Dam).
Short hike with a unusual feature: artificial lake with a dam. Great views.

We went in November (on Thanksgiving), and it was amazing. Not too hot during the day and not too cold at nights.
The best tip for all national parks: get up early. The best hikes (and their parking lots) get crowded in the afternoon.

So you come to Joshua Tree National Park, you see Joshua trees (cool!), you see the rock formations, you see water at Barker Dam, and you think “ok, that’s it, now the rest is going to be variations of the same thing”. Wrong. National parks are huge and have so much more to offer.
The Cacti Garden is a great example. It’s so different from the rest of the park, and so amazing - that it can’t be missed. You see cacti miles and miles away, it’s a huge field of them (not a “garden”).
The hike is very short, it’s just a walk near the parking lot among the cacti.
Be very careful when stepping off the trail to take pictures. The big cacti are obvious danger, but there is also a subtle one. There are small ball-like cacti on the ground. If you touch them with your shoe, it will bite you through it.
One girl in our group accidentally did that. I think everybody on the trail became extra careful after that - she was screaming very loud when I was pulling the spikes off her toe. She was fine after. So be careful, these cacti are dangerous. But it’s a must see.

Home to Saguaros, the largest cacti 🌵 in North America. A great choice to visit in winter, when most parks are too cold. Here you can still hike in shorts and a couple of thin layers, even on Christmas.
The park is open all year round. On Christmas Day the visitor centers are closed, but the park itself is open, you can drive in and hike.
I recommend the following hikes: Wasson Peak (a day hike) and Valley Overlook Trail (short introductory hike with great views). For sunset, a must see place is Gates Pass Trail. The views are incredible. All of these are located in the West side. The East side is interesting too.
There are also very beautiful hikes just outside the park, notably Seven Falls. The scenery is quite different, and I highly recommend that one too.
A nice thing about the park is that it’s located just outside Tucson, so you can find good accommodation there and it will take about 30-40 min to get to the park (west or east side).
Overall, the park is great. All national parks are unique and amazing, and this one is no exception.

The trip to Dry Tortugas is great. The ferry is nice, they serve decent breakfast and lunch. There are hot showers on the ferry (outside on the lower deck). A day trip to Dry Tortugas is a great experience. You can go snorkeling (they provide very good quality gear), explore an amazing fort, or just relax on a beach. This is a National Park, and it’s well worth the visit. I wish I could camp there, to get up early, escape the crowds and spend some quality time on the island.
The only problem is that the trip is overpriced. $180/pp for a ferry ride, simple breakfast and lunch, and gear rental is too much. Something like $100-$120 would be more appropriate in my opinion. Note that you can get a discount on the website ($25 off 2 tickets) and get a refund for the park entrance if you have an annual National Park Pass ($15), so it bring down the cost to $152.5 pp, which is still expensive.

The hike is my favorite in Joshua Tree. It starts with great views. It’s 1.5 miles in one direction. Took us about 2 hours round trip. It’s a bit steep, but not much. There is almost no shade on the trail, so it’s better to come earlier.
The parking is decent, there is a bathroom with no running water.
The destination is amazing. It’s a real desert oasis. The contrast is unbelievable. First you go along a hot desert 🌵 with no shade and not much vegetation. And then you get to a place with tall green thick palm trees 🌴, lots of bushes with birds (!) and even small water pond!
Note that you don’t need to buy a pass to the park for this hike. And it’s very close to Twentynine Palms town.
Overall, highly recommended. Another oasis hike in Joshua Tree National Park, Lost Palms Oasis Trail, is also interesting, but not as impressive as Fortynine Palms.

Beautiful area. There are not many views, but the forest is very diverse and looks great.
I went on the Big Trees hike on a rainy Sunday, started at 8am. I haven’t met anybody until 10.30am. The full loop took me about 3 hours.
The parking is on the street, there is plenty.
The hike is steep at times, but overall I’d rate it as moderate.
I haven’t seen any wildlife except for birds and lizards. I saw many lizards were right on the trail. They move slowly (not your mountain lizards), so need to watch out not to step on them.
The hike is very green overall. There is a lot of shade. Very pretty and relaxing.
I think it’s a great hike in the woods, just 1 hour from San Francisco. Highly recommended.

Amazing hiking area. The hike to Seven Falls is awesome.
We started at 7.50am and finished at 1:50pm. On the way there there were only a few people, but on the way back we faced crowds. So start early if you can.
The canyon is amazing. It’s such an unusual scenery, which includes mountains, creek, Saguaro cacti and continental climate vegetation. The mix is incredible. Scrambling on the creek rocks was fun too.
The waterfalls at the end were okay. It’s December and there is not much water. I’d say the views on the way are much more impressive. But still after 4 mi hike it was nice to have some snacks while looking at running water.
Overall, amazing hike.

Nice place. The tickets are $22 per person. It’s worth the price. You drive through the park and see animals near the road. There are no cages or fences, so they can walk on the road too, if they want.
You can see reindeer 🦌 , two kinds of wolves 🐺 (we saw two of only one kind), junior bears 🐻, bisons and big bears (they were not very close).
There are many cars, but the park is well organized, and you have enough time to see each kind of animals and take pictures.
The drive through is 3 miles and it takes about 40 minutes. You can do extra loops for free if you want.
There is also a walk through zone, but that’s really just a regular zoo.

Wow, what a hike! First you have a lot of fun scrambling up. Wear good hiking shoes! And I recommend bringing hiking poles, they make the later descend much easier.
The final spot has great views at the valleys and mountains. We missed the sunset by just a few minutes, but the upside was that there were zero people at the top. We had it all for ourselves. It’s just awesome.
Our descend was a bit sketchy, because it was getting dark. But with hiking poles and some confidence we ended up just fine.
Overall, amazing and interesting hike with unbelievable views. Enjoy after the mandatory Devils Bridge.

This hike is something. The views at the neighboring mountains are breathtaking. And the final spot, the bridge, is just out of this world.

We hiked just before the New Years, and when we started, there was a blizzard! We were prepared and wore warm winter clothes. Then, after short time it ended and we enjoyed clear skies.

The ascend gets steep and a bit slippery at times, so I recommend bringing hiking poles, they are always helpful.

Sedona landscape is unbelievable. I wonder why it’s not a national park yet (well, technically it’s Coconino National Forest).
Highly recommend. Awesome hike.

Nice gardens with access to the coast, that has amazing views. It is smaller than you probably expect by looking at the map. It took us 2 hours to walk every little trail, and we stopped for pictures and to try to see the whales. We haven’t seen the whales though.
UPD:
I removed 1 star after I went to Mendocino Headlands State Park. That park is free, and has amazing coastal views, much better than here. So it makes sense to pay $15 here only for the garden, which I’m sure is great in summer, but in November it was not that impressive.

Amazing coastal hike. We started from the northern side (near the bathrooms) and went all way down to the long beach near the bridge. The views are different along the way and they’re always terrific. It’s free, not windy. Plan 3-4 hours if you want to do it slow.
At some point you can come very close to the ocean, and see the waves crushing right on front of you. It’s an awesome feeling.

Interesting and unique place. You can get tickets online for $10 (with limited availability) or for $15 on the spot. The ice structures look great. There are sleds for kids and even adults. They also sell hot beverages. Overall, a nice place to bring kids or date, or just enjoy yourself. We don’t regret going. And $10/$15 is not expensive for this.

This is the spot where everybody is going to see the sunset at. It gets very very crowded and crazy. So to find parking, come early. Or go at sunrise time - that would be perfect I think.
The views are amazing. The big downside is that there are many people around. But if you get up early and come for the sunrise - you’re golden.

Extremely beautiful place. I was showing 17 mile drive to a friend and we didn’t want to stop at any locations to save time. We were just looking from the car. But at Pescadero point we just couldn’t drive through. The awe stopped us and we spent 15 min walking around and enjoying terrific views.

Would be great for climbing. But hiking was too short - it’s just 0.3 miles, 15 min walk. And I didn’t see anything special (like Hidden Valley or Barker Dam). But still it’s very nice just to be here. And when we were about to leave, we saw a moon rising! That was very impressive.

Nice stop to climb a bit and take some pictures. The hike is very short. The Arch rock is an interesting formation. But generally there are more interesting places in the park (Cholla Cactus Garden, Fortynine Palms Oasis, Ryan Mountain).

Great wakeboarding for reasonable price. Can be quite crowded on the weekends, so it’s better to come earlier. They close in late October. We came on the last weekend and the water was still not cold and it was sunny and nice.

Great and short detour on the way back from Lost Palms Oasis. Climb up to the peak, enjoy the views, and get back to the campground on the Mastodon loop, avoiding going back the same way you went to Lost Palms.

Great place. The park was closed because of the government shutdown. But it was great that we could still do a hike there. And we even could go to wilderness from there, and we saw a lot of petrified wood.
Short trail with a great view at the end. Totally worth it if you don’t have time for a full day hike (I recommend Wasson Peak). There is a bench at the end so you can relax and enjoy the view.
Nice little park with big redwoods in the heart of financial district. Lots of benches (most are without back support though), tiny pond. Great place to rest or bring lunch to.
Great short hike (1.3 mi). You’ll actually see body of water - something you don’t expect in a desert. Water adds special flavor to the views. It’s pretty crowded.
It’s a very small 🐕-friendly park overlooking the bay. Lots of dog owners in evenings. There are some homeless people around, but it generally feels safe.
Beautiful lookout. Great views of the Painted desert. We also took nice portrait pictures with the road in the background, they came out very nice.

Beautiful trail through a desert canyon, with dozens of miles of trails to explore. My daughter and I took the early shuttle to the end of the paved road, then explored part of the Phone Line trail before descending to the main path again. The shuttle drive provided interesting facts about the canyon and nature on our way to our stop.

During our walk on the main path, we stopped several times to wade through the water that cascades down from the mountains. Cold, clear water, and spotted a few small fish and frogs. A very enjoyable time. Glad we did it early, as spring around Tucson is still pretty warm.

One criticism is that, during our trip, there were three shuttles running. One of them was right behind the other, meaning you could easily miss them both (we did) if you weren't at a designated stop. A little more spacing would be nice.

Loved this short trail. It is 1.5 miles long, and is shaped like a balloon, with a trail that runs from the parking lot to a loop. Along the way are numbers posted with details about the forest. It is mostly pine - red and white - with some deciduous as well, and is reached by going down a 1/2 mile dirt road. The trail is easy to follow and pretty flat. I would recommend a mosquito net for your head, as it was very buggy on the hot, dry day I went visited.

Beautiful spot, one of those must-sees for first time visitors. But I'm a 30-or-so-time visitor, and I still go and see it on my yearly trips to the island. You can get great pictures of it from lake level or from the carriage drop off point. If not taking the carriage tour (it's not that far to Arch Rock, so you don't need to), there is a nice path that runs through the woods from the intersection just east of the fort to it.

Nice trails tucked behind the shopping area. There are multiple entrances, but I used the one behind Home Depot. It's not quiet - South Airport and US 31 are nearby - but the trail itself is beautiful. It winds up and down through pine trees and follows a creek as it heads towards the Boardman. Saw a couple of guys smoking pot (one was sitting in the middle of the trail), but they were doing their thing.

We were here on "living history" day, and it was fascinating. The volunteers were very knowledgeable about the crafts they were displaying, like weapons and textiles. My favorite part was the food - fresh bread, tortillas, and butter. Wow - simple, but great. The canon demonstration is not to be missed, and I took some pleasure in the fact that it set off car alarms because its power.

This was exactly what I was looking for - a kitschy reenactment of the gunfight. The actors were funny and entertaining, and we felt like we were part of the show. There are some interesting historical items near the corral you can look to get an idea of the times. The man who sold us our tickets was very helpful in telling us things to do around town before the show.

I visited for some hiking, and it's an OK place for that. The trail was covered with mulch, and was in pretty good shape. The river was a bit high that week, and much of the trail was underwater, so more bridges would be nice. It's not terribly quiet, being close to the road and barking dogs from the houses nearby, but it was an OK break from work.

Quite a small trail system, and not very interesting. There are several trails, and none of them really go anywhere, suddenly ending. Lots of trees down when I went. The most interesting trail leads to a kayak launch, though how you get your kayak down to it (it's quite a distance, but horizontal and vertical from the parking areas) is a mystery.

Amazing place to take small children. Lots of interesting exhibits that keep them interested and entertained. I enjoyed having a break and letting my daughter enjoy running around, but there were things that were interesting for adults to join in on the fun. Can get crowded, as you can imagine, but I found getting there early was the way to go.

The tennis court has recently been repaved and in excellent condition. The second court was removed for a pair of pickleball courts, so that was disappointing. The basketball court is also in nice condition. In addition to a softball diamond and playground, there is a short trail that runs between Lake Lansing Road and Haslett Road.

Excellent place to take your kids. The playground is quite large, with a variety of different equipment for them to entertainment themselves on. Benches and tables for the adults to sit back and take a break. Parking can be a problem on busy days, but parking across the street at St. Thomas Aquinas doesn't seem to be a problem.

My favorite coaster in the park. The ride is very fast, but very smooth, with plenty of air time on the smaller hills near the latter part of the ride. The lines can be long, especially in the afternoon, but if you're a coaster buff, it's a must-ride. And I enjoy the music that plays in the boarding area. I can hear it now...

Interesting little series of trails. They are fairly narrow and though I have not been there after heavy rain, it looks like it would be a pretty wet walk. But the environment is interesting, with lots of pine trees, including some pretty big ones, as well as a wooden walkway along a pond. Worth a visit.

Great little trails, around half of which follows a little creek that empties into the Betsie River, and you're never too far from the sound of running water. The trail is easy to follow over some gentle rises, so no major climbs to tackle. On the rainy morning I walked this trail, there was indeed mist.

Neat trail that climbs the top of small rise to a view of the surrounding area. There are several easily viewed petroglyphs at the end of the trail. Takes less than ten minutes to get there. My favorite part was the "Beware of Rattlesnakes" sign - doesn't see those where I live.

Wonderful park for beach time or for hiking. I went for the latter, and it has a good mix of sandy dune trails and trails running through the forest. Great views of Lake Michigan from atop the dunes, and going on the shoulder seasons, you will not feel crowded on your hike.

This is my favorite "I need a break from riding" spots in the park. You get to see classic paraphernalia from the park's past, and there is a constant video about Cedar Point running in a quiet corner of the room. It's is so peaceful compared to what waits just outside!

Not a long trail overall, but a very nice, smooth path. Great for a walk along the river. As you travel south, it turns into a street before merging into another trail. I enjoy the view of the bridge and Canada, and the boats of all sizes that pass down the river.

Beautiful park at the base of Fort Mackinac. It's a nice place to relax and watch the people. There is a small playground behind the museum, and stairs that lead up to the East Bluff behind that. Watch out for the goose poop, though - there is quite a bit of it.

Had a wonderful time a the museum. The submarine was fascinating, and being 6'2", I only bumped my head a few times. The staff has done a great job of upkeep with the sub, and the interpretive signs were very helpful, as were the videos inside the museum.

Had to stop riding this ride years ago because of the small concussions I got from my head slamming against the restraints. But before that, it was a nice ride that didn't have too long a wait, and it's an iconic piece of the Dragster Midway.

Paved path by the lake with several places to sit and watch the Boardman. You can see some great sunsets here. Hold onto your hats if it's windy. Lots of parking if you are looking to walk on the Boardman Lake Trail or connect to the TART.

Nice, easy trail that leads through a wash to an overlook of the valley (thus the name) to the west. It's a simple trail for families, but provides a good look at the local flora. The trail is easy to follow, so no chance of getting lost.

Fantastic coaster. If the line moved faster, I would ride it more often than I do. But the speed and twists that the coaster has are great, and it's a very smooth ride. It makes losing White Water Landing a little easier to take.
Great play structure with wonderful views of Frankfort across the water. We were there on a Sunday afternoon, and we practically had the place to ourselves.

Quintessential American! Many, many years ago I flew above the area at 30,000 ft having previously seen it in the movies (thanks a million, John Ford). Even at that height I felt an unmistakable twinge. To see it up close was definitely a dream come true.

Need AWD vehicle to do the tour at your own pace. Of course there places where your vehicle cannot go - hike or ride a horse if you can. The visitor center will enumerate your options.

My only peeve is that night lights at the lodge may be architectural sound but interfere with night photography. Magnificent sunrise views from the balconies. From the same balconies you can get nice sunlight shots of the buttes as the sun sets. Use a dedicated camera for time lapse photography if you can or simply soak the viewing for indelible memories.
likes: On-site Activities: Sunrise views, sunset photography, time lapse photography

reviews_attraction.text:
Incredible that the enthusiastic descriptions of this National Park does not do justice to one's initial reaction upon viewing the fossils behind the Visitor Center. Credit to park management for the layout which eliminates photo-bomb nuisance for the majority.

There are several easy trails in the park which highlight variety even with the little live creatures that will inevitably cross your tracks.

You will definitely need sun screen lotion, head cover and sunglasses plus adequate replenishment for fluids. Most of us have seen fossils in museum. Some have even been fortunate to visit archeological digs (my plug for the Waco National Monument) but Petrified Forest surpassed all expectations. The adjacent site across the freeway merits its own review. :)

Parking is FREE after 6 PM and there is never a charge to watch people traffic around CityWalk. The egress tidal surge lasts until 10:45 PM so one can soak the international flavors for hours.

If one is picking up family members this experience is highly recommended for those not adventurous enough to spend the entire day with paid admission.

Came here after twenty-five years since the last visit. Very impressed with the strategic changes by management to keep customers AND stockholders happy. I hope the employees achieve their objectives too.

Very, very helpful staff - wanted to turn on the auditorium show (15 mins) just for me with an obligatory public service announcement in case others were interested. Of course received several suggestions once we explained our constraints. Took advantage of the suggestions and enjoyed these activities, primary short hikes and beach walks, thoroughly.

The Junior Ranger Program booklet had more information than the average equivalent from the other more popular parks - quality usurps quantity for proportional budgets, I guess.

Good for toddlers and infants to immerse themselves in playful activities. Good for food cart enthusiasts too but these are generally done for the day before the designated closing time, 3 PM. Good security  patrols ensuring even smoking laws are observed. Even Dallas Police keep an eye unobtrusively on the proceedings.

You can stroll, sit or even while away using loaner board games. A little bit of road noise interferes with the enjoyment but mercifully no plans for acoustic walls.

Fishing did not get as exciting as some of the other State Parks in the region. The historic structures may soon need renovation work. Good camping sites along a creek (or is it truly a brooklet). Good place to unwind because it is not very crowded (except for the limited fishing spots) and satisfactory tree cover (not dense) even for warmer days. The walking tour of the historic sites serves as a modest equivalent of a hike for urban folks like myself. Good for group picnics.

Take Shuttle #4 from Giant Forest Museum to the footsteps of this hike. There some 350+ steps to the top. Some of the narrow pathways may be unnerving for some but little kids seem to take it in their stride.

Keep some buffer time for the round trip back to the museum. While you can complete the climb and descent in 45+ minutes you will have to wait much longer for the return shuttle bus.

While you are up here, don't forget the Tunnel Log stop on the return leg of the trip.

Excellent dedication by the super friendly staff to wear period costumes in searing heat. Very informative Visitor Center with just the right level of detail for the average "taxpayer" or guest. There is a Junior Ranger program that ensures budding Rangers explore most of maintained buildings.

Best kept secret: the Site has two awesome trails one of which connects to the adjacent State Park.

Don't forget to take advantage of the shaded picnic sites.

One certainty in YNP - you will always see wildlife in Lamar Valley. The usual rules regarding sighting (sunrise/sunset) apply. If you are interested in photography be warned that unless the animals are crossing the road you will need telephoto lens for the Kodak moment.

We saw deer too and there were plenty of fishing along key stretches of the creek.

Was passing through and did the detour on a whim. Well maintained facilities that merit a walkthrough. I hope that the next generation or two will sustain the maintenance of the facilities connected to the leader of very, very special persons, many of whom gave their lives so that we could enjoy the longest peacetime in centuries.

A trail for all ages. Incomparable views almost at each section of the trail. Do go to the top of the trail - the panoramic view of the neighboring peaks is unrivaled. The principal peak is gorgeous too with all that silky snow. The store has snap-on crampons that provide superior traction on the key trails if they are snowbound.

Poor lighting and insufficient parking betray the age of this park. Perhaps adequate for community rec activities (and T-ball) but lack of enforcement on pet litter makes the place a little below expectations. Difficult to fault the City since there so many other important needs that are under funded too.

Fitting memorial for a City of Houston Councilor who, in the absence of term limits, steered many projects to fruitful completion. Family and pet friendly place to stroll or unwind. For skyline pictures go in the afternoons and spend a little time touring the adjacent buildings within walking distance.

Bucket list entry that surpassed high expectations. Obviously considerable planning and superior management makes a full day's exposure to the exhibits seem insufficient. Even the aviary was a delight.

Didn't get too excited by theatrical presentations but hands-on experience was immeasurable.

Worth a visit simply to visualize the immense impact of meteors. The scale is immense. The effects of density altitude on a general aviation aircraft is sadly visible. The full size astronaut cutout also is an eye opener.

What a misguided mining exploration by some pioneers.

Shutter-bugs with a tripod will have endless opportunities to experiment with light and motion. Take your time to soak in (not literally) the different pool arrangements. You will need patience to avoid photobombs in your shots (or you in the way of others).

History was made here - Pluto! Also, liked the way the staff setup two solar telescopes for the visitors. There is a guided tour of the facilities and several exhibits provide educational value for the younger members of the family.

A little more greenery would have been nice. It is more of a parking lot than a park. Of course, the misnomer notwithstanding it is the place to park when visiting the lighthouse or adjacent food and drink joints if driving.
Accessibility issues abound here. Good for lake faring folks but basic picnic goers could find better sheltered places with short driving distance at another sibling lake.
One of my first stops when I embarked on taking pictures of County Courthouses in Texas. Even the young ones are able to learn something new at this building.
Very interesting exhibit - good to see in person but obviously requires a bit more maintenance expense to avoid the fate of similar structures in rural areas.
Nice easy trail with the chance to get one's feet wet in the river towards the sandy end of the trail. Of course, kids will want to swim!
A good change of pace for those visiting nearby shops with or without kids in tow. Shady with a hint of breeze even on hot afternoons.
Please pray that your visit occurs on a day of sparse visitors. Good panoramic viewpoint and a nice history lesson.
Good place to stop and take a walk or two - to the river front or the base of the falls.

Best Valley view. Easy to access by car. If your time is limited  in the park  dont skip this point. You can see Yosemite, Vernal, Nevada falls Half Dome, Yosemite Valley and more. Be there when the ranger is telling about the valley. At night skyview is great. Especially late July and early June you can see one of the best mily way views in the USA in that point. There are restrooms, parking lot is big but maybe full chech before going.  Visit Washburn point before this point. If you have more time you can have a short hike and climb to Sentinel Dome. Dont forget that falls are more stronger in early summer and may dry up in august-september.

Inspirational view made me feel great!!, be there before sunrise, if you want a good point for a good shot the earlier the better, there may be 100 photographers at 6 am. There is a parking lot and restroom close to the arch. It takes 6-7 min to walk. It is on a 500 m high cliff, be carefull not to fall down. If you stay there at night it is the best point in USA for skyview bec there is no light around. Especially in late july and early august you can see best milky way view in USA.

This is the landmark of Chicago city with the famous 3 skyscapers (Willis, Trump and Hancock). Located in millenium Park on Michigan Avenue. You can see Crown Fountains and Harris Theatre in Grant Park. They are all so close to each other. Looks excellent with the skyline of Chicago behind.

Best view in the park, symbol of Utah State, after strenous hike the view makes you feel it is a dream. Dont attempt in the afternoon time. 4-5 pm is best time. There is no shade on the trail, have plenty of water. It is bigger and more fascinating than i expected.

Second highest falling waterfall in the park, hiking closer to the falls maybe dangerous, rocks are slippery but worth to do. Water amount depends on the snow amount in winter. Best time to visit is May and early June. It maybe totally dried in August.

You can see famous Trump and Tribune Towers on the Bridge. Steps takes you down to a riverwalk or a river boat tour. The bridge between two famous avenues of downtown "Michigan Ave" and "Magnificient Mile". One of the must see points for tourists.

One of the landmarks of Chicago. 3rd highest building with 100floors and 344m high. Was built in 1965 and designed by Fazlur Khan. You can get good views of this building from Willis Tower skydeck, watertower on magnificient mile or at navy pier.

One of my top place in Yellowstone. It is a huge boiling colorful pool in midway geyser basin. But you cant see the real beauty from ground level. You should climb to the hill to have a better view of the colours of pool.

Great place, helpful and informative. Not too crowded like the south rim visitor center. You can stamp your passport, fill the ranger booklet, have a junior ranger badge, get information about grand canyon

A museum and visitor center next to the Sentinel Tree and the big parking lot. You can park your car here and use the shuttles. Very informative and helpful museum. Takes 10 min too see everything inside.

The North Rim of the Grand Canyon is someplace you need to plan to visit.  We drove 80 miles one way from Kanab to see it, the closest place with full services.  It was our first visit to this rim.  When we got to the visitors center and lodge area there were some thunderstorms, making it hard to view the canyon.  We learned these should clear up and with limited cell phone service we were able to see that Cape Royal was not getting the thunderstorms.  Now we had a plan, drive to Cape Royal and work our way back to the North Rim lodge area for dinner.
The drive to Cape Royal was good, a decent road for a car, and we made no stops until we got there.  At Cape Royal things were just starting to clear up, but the views were quite good. We enjoyed the views from the trail, including Angels Window.   We could see the Colorado River below,  which many think you cannot see from the North Rim.  We also saw interesting plant and animal life, including wildflowers.
Driving back we were able to stop at all but one stop, with only one minor spot unavailable due to a full parking area.  The sun came out and we had some spectacular views as we made our way back to the main visitors area.
Back at the main area the views were also great and we hiked out to Bright Angel Point and also along the rim near the lodge.  Then we had dinner and drove back to Kanab as the sun went down and we had to be careful because of all the deer near the highway.
The North Rim was very worthwhile.  It was less crowded and more remote than the South Rim.  The views were different and even though the elevation was higher, the tress were taller and it was more of a forest area.  We are glad we made the journey.  We hope to come back and stay overnight.

This is a top notch attraction in the Fort Myers area.  We have stopped here most every time we are here and since we planned to be here for 3 months we got a one year membership, $80 for two.  Our first stop was for the Christmas lights, which are great.  Everything is decorated and they even have a water fountain with music, kind of a small version of Bellagio on Las Vegas.  The second and third time we came for daytime organized tours and stayed afterwards to go through exhibits and go through the gift shops.  Both men were fascinating along with their families and stories of others that worked or came here.  The gift shops have a great book collection, especially on science.  We especially liked the books on scientific mistakes that ended up not being failures, but accidental discoveries.

We try to get to Shark Valley every time we are in South Florida.  This time we got there about 11:30AM and had to wait for about 8 cars to come out before we were let in.  It is busy on a Monday in February. Once parked we were happy to know there was space on the 1PM tram, so we booked two seats for $25 each.  We took some photos by the visitors center, where there is lots of wildlife, and had our picnic lunch. The tram tour was good, the guide said he had been doing this longer than any other and we believe him.  Anyway it was well worth the cost.  After the tram ride we walked about 1-1/2 miles down the road and back taking lots of photos, including baby anhingas.  Lots of alligators, turtles and birds.  Shark Valley delivered again.

One of our favorite places to walk and see wildlife in the winter.  Most days you will see more than a dozen species of birds, ducks, egrets, herons, ibis, sandhill cranes, limppkins, snail kites, etc.  We have also seen interesting snakes and raccoons, including raccoons swimming.  The loop is about 4 miles and there are no restrooms.  The best viewing is closer to the south end, so if you do not have time, go counter clockwise.  We only saw Snail Kites twice, both flying, but others had better luck.  By March the number of sightings of all birds was down, but was great in December, January and much of February.

The Horseshoe Bend of the Colorado River is one of the most photographed places in US.  It is just a few miles south of Page Arizona with a large dirt parking lot and a 3/4 mile (1km) walk over a hill and down to the viewing area.  Right now it is free, but the parks service is setting up to use a shuttle and charge to see it.  Even being hot we enjoyed the hike and really enjoyed getting our photos.  It is worth the hike.

Tuzigoot shows the pre-European history of the area along with Montezuma Castle and Montezuma Well.  It costs money if you don't have a national parks pass, but you can the receipt at Montezuma Castle and vice versa. (Montezuma Well is free).   Tuzigoot is a large dwelling and you can climb the stars to the top and see the area, including Jerome.   The exhibits in the visitors center are also quite interesting,

Even with crowds we find this place somehow peaceful.   We have stopped here multiple times over the years and always found it interesting.  The cliff dwellings, the sycamore trees, the creek going by.  This day the creek was very high from the recent rains, but it still felt like somewhere people lived.  Come for the history lessons and to think about the past, but stay a while and appreciate the setting.

A great place to roam around.  Lots of trails, lots to see.  You have woods, you have historic stuff, bluffs, you have tidelands with birds to see.  There are elevation changes and roots to trip over.  There are two parking lots, a large one across the street from Fort Caroline National Monument and a smaller one in the Theodore Roosevelt area.

You drive about 4 miles off OR-230 on a paved 1-1/2 lane road to the parking area.  The parking area is dirt.  The hike is about half a mile downhill on switchbacks.  The falls are quite beautiful and worth the hike down and back.  There is no cell phone service, so you will have to save the photos to send out later.

A short hike from the large parking area, which has rest rooms, gets you to the Rogue River and eventually to the Natural Bridge.  You first come to where the river comes out of the rock and then you go on to see where it goes into the rock.  Between you don't see the river.  It is very scenic and an easy walk.

Bryce Point is the furthest SE spot to view the Amphitheater area.  It is a walk from the parking lot or a long trail from Inspiration Point.  Well worth getting to for the views and about the best place to see hikers and horse riders on the trails below.  The town of Tropic is also visible here.

Another great place to view the Amphitheater in Bryce Canyon.   We hiked here from Bryce Point, 1.3 miles one way, and it was a good hike with some sections that were a bit narrow with drop offs in both directions.  But we were glad to get here and back for the views.

Sunset and Sunrise Points are somewhat easy hikes from the biggest parking area in the National Park.  We hit them last and were a bit tired, so did not take many photos that were worthwhile.  Luckily many before us have taken and uploaded lots of good photos.

A nice boardwalk, where you normally see something.  Over the years of taking the boardwalk we have seen alligators, various herons, egrets, turtles, hawks, eagles, snakes and plants,, including flowers.  It is educational and fun to take this boardwalk.

This park is a gem and I have been coming here since I was a youngster.  the falls and cascades are always fun and so are all the plantings.  At the right time of year you can witness salmon runs, which is always special.

One of the best spots for a panorama view of the South Rim of the Grand Canyon.  The Geology Museum here is also quite interesting, as are the signs about the Trail of Time along the Rim Trail going West.

A very interesting national monument with history to learn, a recreated fort to explore, walking paths through the woods and it is right no the Saint Johns River, where you can watch dolphins and ships.
Fort Flagler is a wonderful place.  It is a big out of the way, but worth the journey.  The views, trails, campground and about everything else about the place is wonderful and fun.
If you like to hike up ravines, this is your trail.  It is well marked and not that difficult, but it goes up and up and after a while we decided to go try a more level trail.

Great course. Overall, the course is moderate with some tricky holes. The rough isn't too bad usually but some spots are risky for disc loss. However, it appears pranksters switched the hole signs, so now hole 2 isn't actually 15, just as four isn't 18. Not sure how they did it but they did a pretty solid job of a prank. *Edit* the holes rotated so number one is four holes up. Apparently parks and rec felt it was better that way. Very stupid in my opinion, but it is what it is. Still a 5 star course.

Great forest and mountains. You go from mesquite trees to oak to pine with some manzanita and wild flowers on the way. The geology has some epic moments. There are lots of roads and trails to explore from all sides. There is one camp ground I know of called Ramsey Vista around 7400 ft perhaps. There are picnic spots and view points but no amenities or water sources. Now is a good time for fall colors. Most roads are drivable with a sedan but will likely close with the snow pack.

A historical, natural, and exercise park. It has a two mile loop with various exercise stations along the way. There are interested and off-shoot trails as well, some leading to McPherson and others to Mt. Elden. You will see meadow and forest scenery, wildflowers, tiny cactus, and of course Ponderosa pine. There is also a pan panoramic view of Elden and Mt. Humphrey. Fun for kids and hardcore outdoor exercisers, including mountain biking.

Spectacular alternative perspective of Mt. St. Helens and an eerie landscape. You get a vista of Spirit Lake and can see obliterated logs floating. Just down the road is the Miner's Car. The 99 is a great route too as you travel from regular forest, through the ghost forest, to the blown down forest, then finally to the blown bare area. The vista is well worth the extra journey out.

A great and informative visitor center. The exhibits are concise and cover a complete range of topics from geology to the native perspective. If you're planning to do Wupatki as well the visitor center sells dual passes to Sunset Crater and Wupatki by default. Each one merits a couple hours to get the full experience but there is two camping sites if you need to spend the night.
