Note: Bring shoe spikes.  The trail will have snow/ice throughout the winter and while it's not a difficult terrain, there are a lot of narrow, steep sections made much more difficult by the ice.

The park exists on both sides of the highway. On the north side, you have Chavez and Beaver Brook Trail Loop.  This Trail is 5.1 MI round trip. It is a decline for the first half and an incline for the second half (1,100 feet of elevation gain).  I would rate this as 'easy to medium difficulty.'  It's for hiking use only.

On the other side of the park, you will find Genesee Mountain Trail. The trailhead, as well as a portion of the trail, contain a bison enclosure designed to protect the bison population in the area.  This provides you with great photo opportunities as you are very close to the bison, especially when they are being fed. Mountain biked this Trail which is a 5.6 mile out and back, climbing 600 feet in elevation to the Genesee Mountain summit.  There are beautiful views once you arrive at the top.  This Trail can be hiked or biked and would rate it as 'easy.'

This is a very nice park that is not overly crowded on weekdays. While it does not offer an abundance of the typical mountain range views, there are a lot of other great views available and plenty of wildlife. A great place for a peaceful adventure. I highly recommend.

Hessie Trailhead is only accessible by high clearance 4x4 vehicles but there is street parking available a 1/2 mile before the trailhead for us lowriders. This only adds an extra half mile to your hike, no matter which trail you are exploring.

I hiked to Lost lake on this trip.  The lake was a solid sheet of ice in early December.  There were many footprints leading to the center of the lake.  The views from the lake and throughout the hike are awesome!

It is a 2.5 mile hike to the lake from where most people will park (1/2 before Hessie Trailhead) making it a 5 mile round trip hike with an elevation gain of around 900 ft. The trail is very easy to follow as there are signs throughout. The terrain is Rocky but should be manageable for most skill levels. I would rate the trail somewhere between 'easy' and 'medium' difficulty. There is also a trail that will take you around the lake but from what I can tell, it is not a connecting loop trail.

There are longer, much more strenuous lake and summit trails that can be explored from Hessie Trailhead.  90% of the trail is either ice or snow.  Make sure to bring your shoe spikes and bear spray. There were very few people on the trail, making it a very peaceful hike. I would highly recommend this one.
dislikes: Need for special equipment (shoe spikes, bear spray)

reviews_attraction.text:
A beautiful, sunny 62° December day in Lakewood.  No trees in the trail which is great for getting sun on a cold day but could get today in the summer. There are nice views throughout the park and you can summit Green Mountain which is a very easy hike.  You will get nice views of downtown denver, cacti, mountains, and maybe a rattlesnake if you are lucky.

You can also mountain bike throughout the park. For mountain biking, it is easy terrain but a steep, strenuous ride that will definitely give you a workout.  There were sections of mud and ice on each trail I explored in early December (20% of the trails). I would assume that there is mud and ice throughout most of the winter.  It was still very rideable on a Mountain Bike and hikers didn't seem to mind it.  I would recommend bringing some spikes just in case.

There are multiple parking options around the park boundaries and if full, there is also Street parking available in certain spots.

I will definitely be going back to mountain bike and would highly recommend it to anybody who doesn't mind a little mud and ice.

Lost Lake is a 2.5 mile hike from where most people will park (1/2 before Hessie Trailhead) making it a 5 mile round trip hike with an elevation gain of around 900 ft. The trail is very easy to follow.  The terrain is Rocky but should be manageable for most skill levels. I would rate the trail somewhere between 'easy' and 'medium' difficulty. There is also a trail that will take you around the lake but from what I can tell, it is not a connecting loop trail. 90% of the trail is either ice or snow.  Make sure to bring your shoe spikes and bear spray. There were very few people on the trail, making it a very peaceful hike.

The lake was a solid sheet of ice in early December.  There were many footprints leading to the center of the lake.  The views from the lake and throughout the hike are awesome!

Hessie Trailhead is only accessible by high clearance 4x4 vehicles but there is street parking available a 1/2 mile before the trailhead.

Overall, this is a great trail that leads to a beautiful lake. I would highly recommend to all humans.

An amazing geological adventure for all ages!

One of the very cool things about this park, similar to The Badlands, is that they encourage you to explore off trail (unless otherwise marked).    There are plenty of marked trails but this let's you have fun discovering some less traveled parts of the park.  One of the best ways to explore off trail is to start at the Painted Dessert Inn and take the trail that leads you to the ground floor.  It is a steep ascent/descent but there is plenty of exploring to do once down there.

If you are just stopping at the top 8 or so most popular destinations and not spending much time at each stop, you can see the park in a half day.  If you are looking to go on a few hikes and really take in each site, I would recommend spending a full day.

I would highly recommend that you add this National Park to your list!

A must see while you are in the Flagstaff area!  There are 2 main trails to explore. One trail will take you down into the canyon where you can explore and even go inside some of the old Pueblo Cliff Homes.  This Trail is a steep ascent/descent but is only 1 mile long and has steps.  The other trail is relatively flat and takes you along the rim of the canyon.  Both trails are paved.

The Park Staff was very knowledgeable and friendly. They were providing guests with a very informative overview of the park when first arriving.  There is a per person charge but those with a National Park pass can get themselves and 2 guests in at no charge.

A lot of great views and history to this place. I highly recommend!
likes: Facilities & Services: Knowledgeable Staff, Informative Overview
Attraction Type: Scenic Views, Historical Site

reviews_attraction.text:
Beautiful park with great views of the San Juan islands and surrounding mountains.  there is a loop trail that you can either drive, bike, or walk around with many places to stop and enjoy the views.  There are multiple beaches to hang out at and none of them were overly crowded.

There are both reservation-only and first come campsites available for both their utility and non-utility sites.  There are multiple showers and bathrooms available for campers.  The campsites are constantly monitored by Park staff who are very friendly.  The park staff will drop off firewood to your campsite for $5 a bundle.

This is a great Park to visit if you find yourself in Anacortes Washington!

Very panoramic! You can start your journey at either the Bear O the Lair Trailhead or the Panorama Point Trailhead. It is a shorter hike from Bear O the Lair.  If starting from Panorama Point Trailhead, it's a 3 MI hike with an elevation gain of around 700 feet.  Either way you go, it's an easy hike that provides a decent workout.

The trail had a medium level of traffic on a Saturday.  Parking at Panorama Point Trailhead was a little congested and street parking is limited as there are No Parking signs for much of the road.  Bear O the Lair Trailhead appeared to have plenty of parking on a Saturday.

I'd recommend this one. Another great view of Colorado!

A must visit while in the Outer Banks!  The visitor center recently reopened after an extensive remodel.  They kept the exterior of the building in it's original style and did a great job on the inside, displaying a replica of the Brother's first successfully flown plane.

The monument is amazing and provides excellent views from the top.  There is also a path with markers that show the flight milestones.  Make sure to visit the outdoor replica plane that you can climb onto.

There is a public airport on the grounds where you can watch small aircraft arrive and depart (they can park here for free short term).
likes: Facilities & Services: Remodeled interior, informative displays
On-site Activities: Climbable replica plane, flight milestone markers

reviews_attraction.text:
Often overlooked, Saguaro is a perfect example of how each National Park is unique and awesome!  The park contains an enormous collection of huge, saguaro cacti.  There are many trails throughout the park that provide you with several different views and photo opportunities of the landscape.  Signal Hill is a great place to get close-up views of petroglyphs.

Perfect Park to visit in the winter as the temperatures are near perfect (72° on a December day) 😎.  No matter when you are visiting, take plenty of water and plan your hikes out in advance.  I highly recommend adding this National Park to your list!

A beautiful National Park! Best visited during the on-season before the majority of the roads close. If you are into cross-country skiing, this would be a great park to visit during the off-season as the park does not clear the snow from the closed roads. There are great views from the visitor center. From The visitor center, you can hike just a few miles up the closed Road to some beautiful scenic spots. Bikes are not allowed on the closed roads.

This is a great park to visit anytime of the year but I would check their current restrictions before you go to ensure you have the best experience.

Very popular park in Denver and for good reason.  There is something for everybody here! The paved path that goes around the park is very well organized so that cyclists, pedestrians, and runners each have their own lane and move in the same direction. It is a busy Park but with plenty of space!

There are two separate lakes and views of the mountains. There are also tennis courts and basketball courts. I recommend it!

A beautiful place where the convergence of South Platte River and Cherry Creek create a place where the masses gather to enjoy the union of Fresh Mountain water and street level stormwater.

It is also the junction where the Cherry Creek Trail and South Platte River Trail meet, making it a great starting point for your next bike ride, walk, run, or enthusiastic skipping!

A nice, quick, scenic roadside attraction. The walk to the falls and back is a little over a 1/4 mile and suitable for all skill levels.

Note: Whenever exploring Colorado (especially Oct - May) keep a pair of shoe snow/ice spikes on you at all times.  The ice on the steps kept a lot of people from being able to enjoy the falls.

The name is very accurate, I've verified.

Large Park with two lakes to relax by and plenty of wide trails to cycle, run, walk, or any combination of the three. There are also two statues of people, who I'm assuming are of some historical importance unless they just made statues of random park patrons.

Nice park. I'd recommend.

A feeling of being forgotten amongst it's higher end, faster living, better looking peers. Don't write this one off due to its lackluster size and beauty. It has spunk. Not the kind of spunk you find in the country club neighborhood, the kind of spunk you enjoy having deep, raw conversations with.

Wow!  Great views!  Free to visit thanks to a family that donated the land to the city!  While parking lots do fill up, each lot is central to the entire park.  Very busy on a winter weekday so plan on encountering a lot of people.

Completed the Morrison Slide and Red Rocks trails in the middle of February. Some snow on the ground but no need for spikes.  Trails was not too busy, making it a quiet peaceful hike.  Great views throughout the hike.
West Virginia..... mountain mama.. oops wrong state.  Very nice Park near downtown Aspen.  Great for a quick stroll.  Also a nice place to relax on the rocks with water streaming in the background.
The less traveled Estes entrance that is much less crowded than the Beaver Meadows entrance, both located in Estes.  Rocky Mountain currently requires an online reservation so plan ahead!
Very nice trail system with great views.  Easy difficulty level but there are a lot of small rocks to navigate in some sections.  Protect your ankles!
It's a park with grass and all the fixings.  A few tennis courts, a basketball court, a playground, and a small field where you can walk on grass.
Great trail system with excellent views throughout.  There are many fun ways to walk this space.  There are easy and medium difficulty trails.
A few different trail options.  You can stay flat by walking the trail around the lake or you can head up the mountain.
Great trail to the top of Mount Sanitas.  Good for most ages but still requires some endurance and plenty of water.

Had a great experience with the family...nice facilities at the foot for visitor center...tram to the top is a more noisy but I liked the narrated story on the way. The walk down was beautiful with nice rest stops along the way with clean (though primitive) restrooms, water and shaded shelter. Beautiful scenery.

Very cool building, beautiful construction. Ironic to be right across the street from a Freemason Grand Lodge given the contentious historical relation between the church and freemasonry, but, both were very cool buildings to see after the long hike up Nob Hill.

Mad props to the good folks that set aside a little land and mow the little path out to the site to allow people to see this. It's a beautiful little tribute...a couple hundred yard walk off the road and the memorial lies there. Worth a stop to pay respects.

Fun visit. Just stopped by for the center of the nation monument but it is more. Also found it cool many service orgs worked together to male it happen. Chamber, Freemasons, Daughter of the American Revolution...very cool. Fun stop...and free!

Very cool little park...wish I could have gotten closer, but it was neat. Short walk to it though which is nice. Glad we had the parks card for admittance...without it it would be kinda pricey for what is a smaller standard visit.
dislikes: Facilities & Services: Pricey without parks card

reviews_attraction.text: It's a bummer our governor shut down museums during COVID so we couldn't see that...but the gift shop was fun, clerk was nice and friendly, and they brand EVERYTHING! LOL Seriously...worth a stop to see this niche' shop.

What a great venue for live music. Amazing sounding room, the Opry is a fun show as well, even if country music isn't your jam. Parking is goofy, access is somewhat confusing for a first timer, but its worth it.

Very nice stop and leg stretcher on a long road trip. Cute little church, and happy, very nice bathroom available too for us road trippers. Lots of history here, nice grounds and nice courtyard/garden in back.
Small site, but very interesting. The visitor center has an impressive collection of artifacts, restored pottery and information about the site and excavation. Surprisingly interesting visit!
Now this was one very interesting stop on our visit to the Tucson area. A very interesting look back in history with tours given by men that were serving at the time (at least in our case).
Nice stop to stretch legs on a road trip, great view of the falls, and ruins of an old mill that kind of built the town. Nice walking areas, picnic areas, historical markers and the like.
Massive display, and very little "fluff"...he just lived that big of a life. Very interesting...and I'm not even that big of a fan, but very glad I went and spent 2 1/2 hours...
What a fun random road trip...interesting viewing...some outside time in the sun, some laughs with the family....everyone needs to see this at least once just cuz...why not?!
Stunning old church that still holds mass services. Sadly we got there 30 minutes before close but that was enough time to see its beauty. Highly recommended if in the area.
Nicely kept up, it pretty darn good shape, fun to see, only bummer is that of all of the bridges this one is furthest out of town, it's a decent little drive on dusty roads.
Very cool area, nice little shelter with map and information, great scenery and trails, makes me really bummed I couldn't bring my mountain bike out to Arizona with me...
A fun little visit, advancement of the area around it takes a little bit away, and I was there on a somewhat rainy day, but it was cool to see and I got to run the bases!
Nice parking, nice sign indicating that is the first bridge of the tours, can't drive over it, it's a walking path to it, but, a very short walk...like yards...not long.
Nice park, well taken care of, very nice views of red wing from the top, a couple interesting structures, nice picnic areas. It was a nice little stop for a leg stretch.
Nice lunch hour walk, working a few minute walk away. Scenery, exercise, people out and about, everyone smiling at each other as they pass...hard to find these days.
An amazing walk thru history. As I Freemason, I very much appreciated the Masonic area, naming of the sections. The Celestial Lodge display was quite impressive.
Epic little adventure for a child of the 70's and 80's that I am. Had to stop by while driving through, cuz...well...cuz. Fun corner that the city makes fun.
Quick and easy to get to, decent parking, bridge is nothing I'd drive over, fortunately it was blocked off when I was there so it wasn't even a temptation.
Ok...now I am not a garden strolling sort of guy, but this was quite impressive...full bloom, well maintained...a nice little day trip to see.
Not much to see, but kind of a funny story to read, so that has some merit in and of itself.

This museum has some very original artwork. My favorite was the geologic, Strada art on the second floor. The artist depicted every stratigraphic layer from the sky to bedrock using paper discs. You have to see it to believe it.

Customer service is a little bit lacking at this museum, but the admission is free so I'm not counting off for that.

There's also a fantastic room of pop-up art, like pop-up books you're familiar with from when you were a kid.

Don't make a special trip to Bainbridge Island to visit this museum, but if you are here you absolutely must stop in.

This is one of the weirdest and most amazing tourist attractions in the USA. I've traveled the world, and I've never climbed into a cloths dryer and slid into a different dimension. This place is a combination of a si-fi TV set and a modern art gallery. There were kids and there were old women meditating.

WARNING: This place is not suitable for the disabled. Attractions require climbing, crawling, and navigating narrow and confined spaces. It's also not a place to set a young child free to roam.

If you're in Santa Fe you MUST visit Meow Wolf.

My favorite thing about this state park is the geology. Yes there's a lake for boating and swimming. And yes there are some sort of fake sandy beaches. But the geology is the most amazing thing. Come see this place to stand in the guts of an anticline. If you don't know what an anticline is, look it up on the internet, then come here to see one in all its Glory.

There are even some great geologic interpretive signs at the overlook.

Absolutely amazing place with a fantastic staff. Less than a month after the hurricane the park was back to normal. The gardens were amazing, and one of the staff members gave me an impromptu tour. This Botanical Garden is especially great because it sits right in the middle of a noisy intersection. It actually adds to the beauty of the garden to realize the flowers and the plants and the serenity in such a hectic part of town.

Miles of hiking deep into the earth. The natural entrance walkway is FANTASTIC, and if you're in reasonably good shape you'll love the walk. My 16-year-old and I walked in and walked out. The temperature in the caverns are perfect for an invigorating hike up and down a steep incline. Descending into the caverns on foot reveals a shockingly deep view into what looks like an endless abyss.

Absolutely amazing State Park. All around beautiful. Hiking steamboat rock is a challenge but it is what are the most geologically interesting hikes on the planet. The state park charges$10 per day or you must have a pass. I visited in October 2020, and there was no one on duty at the gate. Thankfully I had a $10 bill. I wish there was some alternative for paying.

this is a simple trail with some of the most amazing views in the San Francisco Bay area. At the end you'll find the point Bonita lighthouse over a rope bridge. This is a must-see for locals and tourists alike. But you please surprised how many people live in the Bay Area their whole lives and never come see the point Bonita Trail.

Kind of a mess Right now due to the heavy rain this season. The park has great potential. Unfortunately I drove to the last to parking lot paid $6 to park. Only to realize that most of the trail was closed. This park is plenty of picnic and other nice shady areas. My favorite thing to do here is to hike the road up to Eagle rock.

This park is getting 5 stars, but it's certainly not because of the beautiful River. April 2021, zero water in the River.

but this is a beautiful green space with some nice picnic tables and public bathrooms. There are some swings for the kids, and for adults. Great place to have a family get-together.

Fantastic museum and amazing service. One of the proprietors greeted me at the door and took me on a personal guided tour of the museum. This museum is filled with facts. I never knew there was such a connection between Bainbridge Island and the internment of Japanese citizens during WWII.

Fantastic Urban Urban Park. Beautiful grassy area for laying out on a blanket. And like most of San Francisco, everyone is carefully observing the covid-19 safety procedures. If you got a little energy, hike up to the top of vernal Hill in Bernal Heights Park, right down the street.

Nice eucalyptus Grove. I always like finding a random Grove of trees in an otherwise urban sprawl area. And if you're going to have eucalyptus,dangerously flammable trees, the best place to have them is in a protected Grove adjacent to a large parking lot.

Like Pioneer Square, this place can be a bit seedy at night. If there's a big event at CenturyLink Field, the square full of sports fans. But if it's a regular cold, March evening, you'll find a lot of vagrants and drunks wandering about.

Amazing geology, beautiful scenery, but badly worn trails. If you come here to hike, be ready to improvise. Some of the map hiking trails, especially on the west side of the Butte, are badly overgrown. Others don't seem to exist at all.

Beautiful Urban Park on Pacific heights. Across the street from spreckels Mansion, and the best view of the mansion. Great place to bring the kids to play. Found a curbside parking spot on a Sunday afternoon.

Not impressed. Paid $10 for parking. Didn't have seven so I just put in a $10 bill. examined the policy sign with a fine-tooth comb. I go all the way to the beach, only to learn who they do not allow drones.
Fantastic riverfront area. On a chilly, windy day, dozens of windsurfers and sale borders. Without quite the view, easily comprable to San Francisco's Marina green. There's even a clean Porta-Potty.
These are some amazing steps. They are both beautiful and highly functional. At the top is Lincoln Park. Take a long hike across San Francisco, and include these steps in your journey.
Absolutely amazing. Definitely lived up to the name. there are no shortage of grandview's, but this is definitely one of the best. I only wish you could fly a drone off of it.
this is a great pier to see some amazing surf. But if the surf is too high they close the pier. Waves will actually break over the pier. Very popular with fisherman.
dislikes: Closes when surf is too high

reviews_attraction.text: Nice little quiet park where you can hear the sea lions. Great stop along the waterfront trail. All in all, fantastic views of shoreline real estate.
Monroe Street Bridge. Pretty amazing downtown Bridge. For pedestrians in cars. Great view of the river and some waterfalls. Good interpretive signs.
Mount tamalpais state park is a world-class recreation area. Hiking trails galore.And the view from the mountain, and from the trails, is amazing.
One of the best 6 Mile walks you'll find in the San Francisco Bay Area. Outbound is up a slight grade and great cardio.
Nice Town Center, but I wish more people were wearing face masks. This city is definitely the city to catch covid-19.

(Translated by Google) In my opinion the best Vista Point of the Colorado River, after having traveled a "dirt road", even for a 4x4 high clearance, with the risk of tearing a tire on the rocks that make up the road surface in the last kilometers, after the Ranger Station ... nothing, no connection except GPS.
In this isolated place there is however a clean toilet and you can meet wild animals a little intimidated by our presence, including roadrunners.
The view to the east is certainly the most scenic, while the one to the west is the most geologically interesting: you can see the remains of an ancient volcanic eruption even on the opposite (south) side of the Canyon, compared to the (north) side of the Throne Volcano, at demonstration of the fact that the same had created a "dam" that had temporarily blocked the course of the river.
The river is placed almost 900 m. below our. observation point and getting here is not recommended for those who suffer from vertigo, however it remains a unique point to enjoy a fantastic view.
Visited in August 2016.

(Original)
A mio parere il migliore Vista Point del fiume Colorado, dopo aver percorso una "strada bianca" impervia anche per un 4x4 high clearance, con il rischio di squarciare una gomma sulle rocce che compongono il manto stradale negli ultimi chilometri, dopo la Stazione del Ranger ... il nulla, nessuna connessione se non il GPS.
In questo posto isolato si trova comunque una toilette pulita e si possono incontrare animali selvatici un po' intimoriti dalla nostra presenza, fra cui i roadrunners.
La vista verso Est è certamente la più scenografica, mentre quella verso Ovest la più interessante geologicamente : si possono vedere i resti di una antica eruzione vulcanica persino sul lato (sud) opposto del Canyon, rispetto a quello (nord) del Vulcano Throne, a dimostrazione del fatto che lo stesso aveva creato una "diga" che aveva temporaneamente sbarrato il corso del fiume.
Il fiume è posto quasi 900 m. al di sotto del ns. punto di osservazione ed arrivare fin qui non è consigliabile a chi soffre di vertigini, resta comunque un punto unico per godere di una vista fantastica.
Visitato in Agosto 2016.

(Translated by Google) Most visitors to this skyscraper underestimate the architectural aspect that characterizes it: the supporting columns on the perimeter are not in the corners of the building, as usually happens, but in the center line of the four sides.
This strange conformation, although aesthetically innovative and interesting, was derived from the need not to "touch" a small pre-existing church, but could lead to a possible instability and consequent collapse of the structure, in the case of hurricanes with strong winds coming from one of the corners of the building.
Luckily, a student from Princeton University noticed an underestimation in the calculation hypotheses and informed the Designer, who after a verification of the calculations, had structural modifications carried out to put the building in safety.
It is interesting to know that these reinforcement operations, which lasted three months and were carried out at night, were not made public for about 18 years.
Visited in August 2013.

(Original)
La maggior parte dei visitatori di questo grattacielo sottovaluta l'aspetto architettonico che lo caratterizza : le colonne portanti sul perimetro non sono negli angoli del fabbricato, come di solito avviene, ma  nella mezzeria dei quattro lati.
Questa strana conformazione, pur se esteticamente innovativa ed interessante, era derivata dall'esigenza di "non toccare" una piccola chiesa preesistente, ma poteva comportare una possibile instabilità e  conseguente crollo della struttura, nel caso di uragani con forti venti provenienti  da uno degli angoli del fabbricato.
Per fortuna, una studentessa dell' Università di Princeton, si accorse di una sottovalutazione nelle ipotesi di calcolo e ne informò il Progettista, che dopo una verifica dei calcoli, fece eseguire modifiche strutturali tali da mettere l'edificio in sicurezza.
E' interessante sapere che queste operazioni di rinforzo, durate tre mesi ed effettuate di notte, non furono rese pubbliche per circa 18 anni.
Visitato in Agosto 2013.

(Translated by Google) I visited the Wave on August 16th 2010, after winning the online lottery.
It was the first time in 70 years that I won a lottery and I can say that I was VERY LUCKY.
In fact, in addition to winning the lottery, you must also have luck in the weather conditions on the day of the visit: in fact in case of bad weather the permit can no longer be used on another day.
On the day of the visit we left early to arrive on site at least at 10:00 a.m. (UTAH local time), after two hours of walking under a sun already at that relentless hour and at 11:30 a.m. we walked on the way back, with a reassuring thunder concert finding ourselves in an environment of only rocks, without any shelter.
The place is worth all the fame it deserved: the light conditions greatly influence the colors of the rocks and we have been able to notice the evolution from the initial serene to the subsequent formation of clouds.

(Original)
Ho visitato la Wave il 16 Agosto 2010, dopo aver vinto la lotteria online.
E' stata la prima volta in 70 anni che ho vinto una lotteria e posso dire di essere stato MOLTO FORTUNATO.
Infatti oltre  a vincere la lotteria, bisogna avere anche fortuna nelle condizioni meteo del giorno della visita : infatti in caso di maltempo il permesso non può più essere utilizzato in un altro giorno.
Il giorno della visita siamo partiti presto per arrivare sul posto almeno alle 10:00 a.m.(ora locale UTAH), dopo due ore di cammino sotto un sole  già a quell'ora implacabile ed alle 11:30 a.m. ci siamo incamminati sulla strada del ritorno, con un concerto di tuoni poco rassicuranti trovandoci in un ambiente di sole rocce, senza alcun riparo.
Il posto vale la tutta la fama che si è meritato : le condizioni di luce influiscono moltissimo sui colori delle rocce ed abbiamo potuto notare l'evoluzione dall'iniziale sereno al successivo formarsi delle nuvole.

(Translated by Google) A "sculpture" with a series of stairs that, like those of Escher, lead nowhere !!!
It is however already a Must and it will become even more so, because the structure is 46 m high. designed by Thomas Heaterwick and allows you to see the surroundings from different levels, but above all the view of the interior is enhanced as you go up.
It was made of bronze steel (mostly in Italy by Cimolai di Monfalcone) with 16 floors and 154 flights of stairs: the soffit also reflects the figures of the people on the outside floor.
Tickets per hour are free and are made on the spot: you must scan an image with the QR code and reserve seats at one of the possible times during the day.
Disabled access is allowed by an elevator that can take you to the top.

(Original)
Una "scultura" con una serie di scale che, come quelle di Escher, non portano da nessuna parte !!!
E' comunque già un Must ed ancor più lo diventerà, perchè la struttura è alta 46 m. su progetto di Thomas Heaterwick e consente di vedere i dintorni da diversi livelli, ma soprattutto la vista dell'interno si esalta man mano si sale.
E' stato realizzato in acciaio al bronzo (in gran parte in Italia dalla Cimolai di Monfalcone) con 16 piani e 154 rampe di scale : l'intradosso riflette anche le figure delle persone che si trovano sul pavimento esterno.
I biglietti per ora sono gratuiti e si fanno sul luogo : si deve scannerizzare un'immagine con il Qr code e prenotare i posti in uno degli orari possibili, durante la giornata.
L'accesso ai disabili è consentito da un ascensore che può portare in sommità.

(Translated by Google) It is an interesting place with two "attractions": seeing the passage of boats through two waterways with a 2.40 m difference in height. and watch the salmon rise to the top in the fish ladder.
While the boats pass continuously between the mobile bulkheads that allow them to overcome the difference in height, the salmon obviously only pass in the seasonal periods in which they rise from the ocean to the fresh waters.
Suitable for children and visit also possible for the disabled.
Visited in August 2008.

(Original)
E' un posto interessante con due "attrazioni" : vedere il transito delle imbarcazioni  attraverso due vie d'acqua con dislivello di 2,70 m. e vedere i salmoni risalire verso l'alto nella "fish ladder".
Mentre le imbarcazioni passano in continuo fra le paratie mobili che consentono loro di superare il dislivello, i salmoni ovviamente passano solo nei periodi stagionali in cui risalgono dall'oceano verso le acque dolci.
Adatto ai bambini e visita possibile anche ai disabili.
Visitato in Agosto 2008.

(Translated by Google) In the "largest small city in the world" a car museum with a part of the rich collection of Mr. Harrah, to which other cars have been added, for a total of over 230 ... from the 1900s to the 1930s, up to the 1950s and beyond.
Some object of desire of famous owners such as Elvis Presley, Sinatra and J.F.Kennedy.
This has been awarded as one of the 5 "greatest" auto museums in America and being in the area well worth the visit.
Visited in August 2011.

(Original)
Nella "più grande piccola città del mondo" un museo delle auto con una parte della ricca collezione di Mr. Harrah, cui si sono aggiunte altre autovetture, per un totale di oltre 230 ... dal '900 agli anni '30,  fino agli anni '50 ed oltre.
Alcune oggetto del desiderio di proprietari famosi come Elvis Presley, Sinatra e J.F.Kennedy.
Questo è stato premiato come uno dei 5 "greatest" musei dell'auto in America ed essendo in zona, merita la visita.
Visitato in Agosto 2011.

(Translated by Google) From the Skydeck you have the best view of the city and you can touch the difference between the nearby Smith Tower and this which is the tallest skyscraper in Seattle.
The evolution in buildings built over 70 years is evident in their comparison: the Smith Tower has an unmistakable pyramid-shaped top.
From here the 360 ​​° view sweeps without limits on the city and surroundings.
Suitable for children and possible for the disabled.
Visited in August 2008.

(Original)
Dallo Skydeck si ha la vista migliore della città e si può toccare con mano la differenza fra la vicina Smith Tower e questo che è il più alto grattacielo di Seattle.
L''evoluzione  nelle costruzioni realizzatasi in 70 anni risulta evidente nel loro confronto : la Smith Tower ha una inconfondibile sommità a tronco di piramide.
Da qui la vista a 360° spazia senza limiti sulla città e dintorni.
Adatto ai bambini e possibile per i disabili.
Visitato in Agosto 2008.

(Translated by Google) It is the starting point and docking point for Norwegian cruise ships to Alaska.
Walking through Seattle, we were struck by the movement of people arriving and departing from one of the ships that, not long after being docked, was already under full load of new cruise passengers.
Everything took place in the highest organization, without the usual troubles experienced for boarding in smaller ships.

(Original)
E' il punto di partenza e di attracco delle navi da crociera della  Norwegian per l'Alaska.
Passeggiando per Seattle, siamo rimasti colpiti dal movimento della gente in arrivo ed in partenza da una delle navi che, dopo non molto dall'essere attraccata, era già in piena fase di carico dei nuovi crocieristi.
Il tutto si svolgeva nella massima organizzazione, senza gli usuali affanni vissuti per l'imbarco in navi minori.

(Translated by Google) The chasm created by the fall of the crater is worth seeing: you can get a vague idea of ​​the weight and size of the meteorite by following the illustrative panels and observing the weight and size of a recovered fragment.
The museum, although of limited size, provides interesting indications for this place, while very brief as regards astronauts.
Visited in August 2008.

(Original)
La voragine creata dalla caduta del cratere è da vedere : ci si può fare una vaga idea del peso e delle dimensioni del meteorite seguendo i pannelli illustrativi e osservando peso e dimensioni di un frammento recuperato.
Il museo pur di dimensioni limitate, fornisce indicazioni interessanti per questo luogo, mentre molto sommarie per quanto riguarda gli astronauti.

(Translated by Google) A beautiful outdoor auditorium, built in a natural amphitheater, with a capacity of over 17,000 seats.
A problem is given by the influx of people at any event, which is concentrated in the dedicated parking lots creating a huge traffic jam, as everyone arrives (even families) by car.

(Translated by Google) A small museum on the gold rush in Klondike, which also explains how the revival of the city started from the great fire that destroyed Seattle.

Le ferrovie che raggiunsero la città come base per collegare l'Alaska, diedero un grande impulso.
Adatto anche a bambini.
Visitato nell' Agosto 2008.

(Translated by Google) The tower enjoys a unique view of the bay, you can visit inside and climb to the top.

(Translated by Google) A huge and truly equipped park (many tables with benches even equipped with barbeques) around a large, really large house (mansion).

At the center of the square in front of the Metropolitan Opera is a very beautiful dancing fountain.

Il Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts è un complesso di edifici dedicati nella maggior parte allo spettacolo, con uno stile architettonico vario ma con linee classiche.

(Translated by Google) A very beautiful waterfall, at the end of a trail of moderate difficulty: challenging in the final part due to the presence of boulders and scales on a landslide descended from a ridge.
Mount Hood is a unique opportunity for the many trails it offers.

L'arco naturale più celebrato degli USA, come icona dello stato dell' Utah. Si trova all'interno del Parco Nazionale di Arches e si raggiunge con una camminata di media difficoltà di oltre un'ora di salita.

Un trail facile non molto conosciuto, con una strada bianca per raggiungerlo : si cammina sul greto del torrente ma occorre prestare attenzione al tempo, per il pericolo di possibili Flash Floods.

Pur non essendo tra i più grandi, questo Campidoglio è certamente fra i più belli : si può visitare liberamente, fino ad assistere persino ad Assemblee del Senato della California.

A beautiful biography of Mark Twain.

Un museo interessante in una scuola che ha operato fino a circa 80 anni fa, con una bella serie di macchine da scrivere del tempo.
Una bella biografia di Mark Twain .
Visitato in Agosto 2010.

(Translated by Google) The park is in the northern part of Downtown, at the height of the International Fontain and the Space Needle and includes a series of modern sculptures inserted in a public garden.

(Original)
Il parco è nella parte a nord della Downtown, all'altezza della International Fontain e dello Space Needle e comprende una serie di sculture moderne inserite in un giardino pubblico.

(Translated by Google) Bryce Canyon is undoubtedly one of the most fascinating natural wonders of the United States, and this is one of the most visited Vista Points overlooking the Canyon.

(Original)
Bryce Canyon è senza dubbio una delle meraviglie naturali più affascinanti degli Stati Uniti, e questo è quello tra i Vista Point che si affacciano sul Canyon, fra i più visitati.

(Translated by Google) A really small museum, built inside a tiny ex-prison!
Visited in August 2011.

Un museo veramente piccolo, realizzato all'interno di una minuscola ex-prigione !
Visitato in Agosto 2011.

Wow!! This place is unbelievable, maybe I'm just not used to this area but you can tell somebody put a lot of work into clearing out space for people to run and have a good time. There are picnic tables spaced evenly all along the park and a trash can and a fire pit by each one, what more could you ask for. Bathrooms? Oh yeah!! they've got bathrooms too and they have porta potties kind of hidden in the woods so nobody has to see them but they're there if you need them. And then I wondered why it was only rated 4.1 Stars so I read some reviews. And they just confirmed my suspicions that people will find anything to complain about, if their lives are just that miserable. Yes you have to pay $5 to come in and use this beautiful park for the day, whether there is one person or 20 people in your vehicle, it is $5 for the day. And there is a sign before you get in the park that actually tells you that? Wonder how that sign was missed. And as far as the ranger hounding people? I drove in without paying because I wasn't sure I could get to the beach or not. The ranger, who cleared all this land and set up a beautiful Park!! if you take the time to actually talk to him, you learn that he did all this work and he takes great pride in this park and if you come in here and you don't pay the five bucks, well, he will do just like he did with me and come over and tell you don't forget to pay. For someone like me with some movement difficulties it makes me feel really safe and secure knowing that he is watching the property and that I don't have to worry about people coming in and doing things they shouldn't be doing. That doesn't really bother me I kind of like it but some people, maybe aren't thinking like I'm thinking, and so they find it annoying? I guess again it's all how you look at it. But from grass growing out of old wood deers, to the water watching in and out, if you bring your kids are not only can they play and have fun but they can actually learn about how nature actually work. I would say five bucks is a great deal, the Rangers checking on you is a beautiful thing, and the only thing better than both of them is the park

Well one thing I can say for sure after reading the first reviews on this dog park is that most people have serious " I" infections? You know, I want I feel I need I think etc etc! I wonder if the reason it was muddy is because this is Oregon and it had been raining? But this has very nice and princes it has asphalt walkways all the way up to the park. The park is well fenced-in my only problem is it you can actually see the metal fencing so the dogs probably feel a little enclosed. They do have the wood chips and part of the area and then they have grass in the other parts. The bathrooms are closed, they even have a little work out area kind of park pass workout thing, parking is closed and overall with the exception of there being no trees? You know they had to remove a hundred of them to make the spot? If they move the fence out 20 feet they would have an incredible dog park. But again it all depends on what you choose to focus on. This park is big and open and has plenty of room for your dog to run. The only problem is it only has one picnic table, one trash can, one doggy poop bag, and I would say one plastic chair but I saw a second red one as I was leaving, one Watering Hole, and at least it is consistent in the number of things it offers to you?
dislikes: Limited amenities (picnic tables, trash cans, doggy poop bags, chairs, watering holes)

reviews_attraction.text: This may have at one time been an actual open space. If you noticed the back of the neighborhood expenses are all fenced-in or completed with chain link so I am sure at one time dogs were allowed to run this whole Canyon free. But as you can see from the pictures they have put up fencing along the the walk path and they crossed a fence with a back gate so it is now a totally fenced-in dog park. But with that being said, it is a Incredible Dog Park. It's very big and open Andrew me for them to run, there is more than enough grass, there are Big Trees, some of them very old and actually look like Disney made them himself hahaha. We live in Reno NV and were looking to go to warmer places. We are staying in campground B and find it pretty nice. You are parking on dirt but we have full hookups including 50 amp service .
The park is clean and in pretty good shape  They have restrooms,  showers and a camp store.
You make your reservations online and can only stay for 14 days in a 28 day period.
The park is on Skinner Lake which is owned by the water department and they do stock the lake with fish .
They also allow campfires in fire rings and you can buy firewood at the camp store. They sell gas and propane at the camp store.
They do not provide wifi and we have limited cell service with att here.
Another thing to know if you are coming and going is they lock the gates at sunset from Sunday thru Thursday. They give you the lock combination but a little different. The main ranger check in is open until 10:00 PM on Friday and Saturday nights though.
Overall a nice place to camp and relax but if you are looking for a high end RV resort this not the place for you.

We are on Vegas to have some work done on our motor home. Had some spare time on the weekend so looked for a place to walk our dog Nugget and get some exercise.
Craig Ranch Park was close by so we gave it a shot.
Glad we did as this is a very nice park with a lot to do. They have a baseball field, Volleyball courts, a kids play area, several lakes, an amphitheater, dog runs and more. This is a very large park that is well maintained for a regional park. Since they have the lakes you have ducks and geese and have to watch out for the bird poo.
They have three off lease dog parks and we took our dog to the small dog area. They go under 35 pounds for small dogs and over that for large dogs.
Lots of trees, grass, and shaded pavilions which you need here in the summer.
I would highly recommend.

We were visiting our friend Leslie in Mesa AZ and decided to go to the Goldfield Ghost Town and Mine Tour. This place  is pretty neat. The parking is free and so is the entrance to the place.
The original mine and buildings burned down years ago but they have recreated it.

They also have a steakhouse as well as a place to get burgers so your day is covered.
I think it is worth a visit. Will probably go there again too.

We were visiting Cheyenne WY and wanted to take our dog Nugget for a walk. We found Holiday Park which has the Big Boy steam engine there

I know they advertise that this has a plot, but it doesn't.  It has a beginning and and end, but no middle.  The middle section is all acrobats which is great but has nothing to do with the show itself.
My review is based on the incredible stagecraft that takes place for this show and the fact that they used a lot of the auditorium for the show.  This is a very hi-tech show and I would love to go back stage so see how they do it.  I don't want to give any spoilers, so I just want to tell you the stagecraft is worth the price of admission.

Must see.  My suggestion is that you take the tram to the end of the line and Uber to the Mob Museum.  Price is reasonable.  They have retro-fitted and old post office and you start on the 3rd floor and work your way down.  Put aside at least 3 hours for this tour.  They have part of the original wall from the St. Valentine's Day Massacre, lots of short films and plenty to read as you learn how the Mob climbed into American life and then into Vegas.  And then how they got them out.

We were here for the Belgian Congo musical instruments which was a special exhibit. This is a brilliant exhibit and well worth the money. The costumes and instruments are nicely displayed. TVs are on the wall that play films showing the costumes and instruments used.
My only complaint is that the TV screens could be bigger.
Because we had three museums on our list for the day, we did not do the rest of the museum. However, we will be back.

This is a very good museum for a university.  Includes two Tintorettos.  Particularly liked the Kress collection, which I think is an acquired taste.  The first floor was blocked off because they were building a new exhibit, so we didn't get to see that, so my judgment is based on just the second floor.  It seemed to be run by students because I did not see an adult supervisor the whole time I was there.

The exhibits were very well done, if missing some explanation.  Right now they are featuring Pancho Villa, but they do not give the full story.  It is a PC version.  They also have a display of black millionaires, but there are only two and only one of those is a millionaire.
The mining display is one of the best I have ever seen.  Not to be missed.  Do go through the mine tunnel, it will be educational.

I have been surrounded by Saguaros since I moved to the Valley of the Sun in 1964, however I have never been to the NP.  When we arrived, the saguaros were beginning to bloom (only those 40 years old and older).  The park has an 8 mile dirt trail loop that displays some of the best saguaro and chaparral I have every seen.  There are places for picnicking, however it was too hot that day for man or beast.

Sadly we picked a very hot day to visit and were not able to visit all the exhibits.  We did see the aviary and some of the plants, which was our primary purpose for being there.  Staff were nice and helpful.  Sadly the trails are in the sun.  There was practically no one there because of the heat, so we almost had the place to ourselves.  We will return in the winter to see the other exhibits.

I missed  this when it was in Phoenix and was very sorry.  We got a ticket deal at Luxor for Bodies, Titanic and Shark Experience.  It is extremely educational.  Sadly, at my age I learned how fast I am falling apart. :)  The the bodies are donated humans who have been skinned or chopped so you can see exactly how the body works.

The is the fort that replaces the Tubac Presido as the Spanish move north.  Only a small part has been restored, but they have done an excellent job.  The docent who gave us a tour was a descendant of a soldier stationed at the fort.  The hours are limited and the parking is sparse.  Worth the visit though.

I was fascinated to see the many styles of art the DeGrazia did over the years.  It is sad that the pieces I found alluring, were not the pieces the public found alluring.
I didn't like everything I saw, but I saw a new side of DeGrazia that I could appreciate.  I am very glad my wife talked me into it.

When they first started this exhibit is was mainly sharks and it was free.  Now it is an expanded exhibit with sharks, swordfish, rays, all kinds of fish.  Not a big exhibit, but worth it.  It keeps the kids entertained. :)
Interest place but the rangers tell the same stories about guilty people bringing back pieces of petrified wood that that do in Yellowstone about obsidian.  They have got to get new material.
I visit this museum every time I come to San Diego and every time it gets better.  They have trains running in all gauges.  The background work is exceptional.
A trip into history.  This is a well-repurposed building, now a museum of the milling history of Minneapolis.  There is a lot to see for adults and children.
This is a step back in history to one of the great placemarkers in Western history.  Next to the courthouse is a gallows, which is a little chilling.
Besides the crater there is a great gift shop and museum.  They have added tours.  The astronauts trained in the crater which makes it interesting.
Like most science museums, this one is mostly directed towards children, however adults can pick up a thing or two. :)  Has a great IMAX screen
What a gem!!!  Great exhibit of pre-Soviet, Soviet and post-Soviet art.  Expect to spend a couple of hours.  Staff is wonderful.

Lovely two block sculpture garden.  There are lots of sculptures here and it is easy to miss some.  Take your time and enjoy.

When I first started going here it was very reasonable, but now it is pricey.  Not sure you are getting your moneys worth.
One of the better zoos I have been to.  Well designed, plenty of shade.  Expect to spend the day.  Parking is convenient.
This museum has a lot of different areas so it is hard to decide what to like. Me, I like them all.
A ton of great art.  Too much to see in one day.  Plan to see it in sections or split it into days.

This hike was the most sedate 6 mile round-trip hike I've ever been on. Maybe 800' elevation gained along the was very gradual. The pace is slow because the views are everywhere. Early morning light bounces off the canyon walls making the opposing walls not illuminated by the sun really glow. Spring Creek only flows a short distance once within the tight canyon walls and then it stays dry to the turn around point. We happened upon a Great Basin rattlesnake at the end on the trail but it moved out of the way without a rattle or a hiss. For the most part we kept to the dry creek bottom avoiding any side trails. We also encountered some scrambles where logs and rocks need to be scaled for a few feet at around 2.5 miles in.

This review is for the hiking loop CCW Cottonwood Hills trail, to the Spanish Wash connector, and back on the Prospector trail. In all a 6.75 mile loop. The trailhead is accessed via a dirt road between two businesses making it feel like you might be trespassing on their drives as you ease onto the dirt road.

Encountered a Great Basin rattlesnake, lizards, wild flowers and views. Prospector is too close to the Interstate, but hey it's a trail. Spanish Wash is very sandy, if you take this loop in a CW direction not only do you get to walk in sand, but also uphill. A 4th star if the wash wasn't part of this, and the 5th if further away from the Interstate.

Prospector looks like an excellent mtb trail.

The impact of how good views are from up here are truly dependant on the weather. Hazy air doesn't lend itself to the crisp photos possible up here.

The drive in is a long uphill slog that when reversed puts your brakes and gears to the test, especially the last 1/2 mile with 15% grade. No bathroom at the top so use the one just before you make the last right turn to go up the steep grade. Plenty of parking at the top.

The trail to Dante's Peak is steep and exposed to the valley floor below. Great views of the salt flats.

Don't forget to get views of Ryan, CA on the way up (looks like an old mining community) about 4 miles in off 190.

About a 6.75 mile round-trip, 675' gain. Great views as usual. Various wildflowers are out. Maybe 20 or so people on the trail. You can see the trail from the bottom directly under cable mountain devastated by the rock slide from last summer that has that access route closed.

Had I known how much better it is in the canyon I would have never wasted time at Zabriskie. 6.4 mile r/t which included some side canyons, saw red cathedral, and we didn't take the loop to Zabriskie.

Beautiful trail, beautiful views. Wildflowers such as the Paintbrush and Globemallow are out. The cacti are just starting to pop with some Claret Cups first out of the chute.

One of the more stunning gotta do hikes. The mosaic rocks, and alabaster smooth rocks are fun to look at. Go all the way until the trail ends. There is more scenery in the upper section which after the initial tight canyon opens up (stay in the middle of the wash avoiding and side trails out of the wash).

The last section is some scrambling that takes some nerve. Going up its a challenge due to the smooth rock. Sliding back down is exhilarating.

水量豊かな噴水。周辺には椅子やテーブルがあり、小さな子供がたくさん遊んでいる姿を見かけます。水が衛星処理されているのか少し塩素のような匂いがしました。目の前にはスターバックスと公衆トイレがあります。

(Translated by Google) It is a wonderful museum. There are many exhibitions, and both Picasso and Raphael have no fence so you can take pictures. Students are free to enter if they have a student ID and ID. There are many chairs in the hall, so you can enjoy your work slowly.

(Original)
素晴らしい美術館です。展示数が多くピカソもラファエロも柵がなく写真撮影可能。学生は学生証とIDがあれば入館無料です。館内にはたくさん椅子があるのでゆっくり作品を楽しめます。

(Translated by Google) It is a very beautiful facility and tourists come from all over the world. There is a restaurant on the first floor and an exhibition room on the second floor where you can spend a relaxing time. Live piano music can be heard in the guest building.

(Original)
とても綺麗な施設で世界中から観光客が来ています。一階にはレストラン、二階には展示室がありゆっくり過ごせます。宿泊者用の建物ではピアノの生演奏が聞けます。

(Translated by Google) Great! When the weather is nice, you can overlook Los Angeles. I think it's a place that kids and adults can enjoy. Free parking is available within a 10-minute walk, and the DASH bus to the observatory costs 50 cents each way.

(Original)
素晴らしい！天気が良いとロサンゼルスを一望出来ます。子供から大人まで楽しめる場所だと思います。歩いて10分ほどの場所には無料の駐車場があり、天文台行きのDASHバスは片道50セントとお得です。

(Translated by Google) A building that doubles as a display and stand for materials. Right in front of you, you will have great views of downtown San Diego and Coronado Beach. This is a recommended place. Note that there are no shops or vending machines.

(Original)
資料の展示と売店を兼ねた建物。すぐ目の前からはサンディエゴのダウンタウンやコロナドビーチなどの素晴らしい景色を眺めることが出来ます。オススメの場所です。売店や自販機がないので注意。

(Translated by Google) It is a very beautiful park. There are several museums, and all of the exhibits are wonderful. Rose garden has a sweet scent in the early spring when flowers bloom. The grass is beautifully green and is in good condition.

(Original)
とても綺麗な公園です。博物館がいくつかあり、どれも展示内容が素晴らしいです。ローズガーデンは花が咲く春先には甘い香りが漂います。芝は緑が綺麗で、綺麗に整備されています。

(Translated by Google) When the weather is nice, you can see a beautiful view. Since the sidewalks are not maintained on the way and there are windy days, it is good to have comfortable shoes and clothes.

(Original)
天気が良いと綺麗な景色を見ることが出来ます。途中歩道が整備されていないのと、風が強い日があるので歩きやすい靴と羽織るものがあるとよいです。

(Translated by Google) Great exhibits such as fossils, stuffed animals, gems, and California history. Free admission on the first Tuesday of every month and every Tuesday in September except July and August.

(Original)
化石、剥製、宝石、カリフォルニアの歴史など素晴らしい展示内容です。7月と8月を除き、毎月第1火曜日と9月の毎週火曜日は入館無料。

(Translated by Google) Big stone. The aisles were moderately sloped and there were many people taking pictures as if they were changing positions and lifting stones. This is also art, isn't it? .

(Original)
大きな石。通路が程よく坂になっていて、位置を変えて石を持ち上げているように写真を撮る人がたくさんいました。これもアートなんでしょうね。。

(Translated by Google) It was a very big tree and couldn't fit in the photo of my smartphone. The surrounding lawn is well managed and there is a promenade, so it is a good place to take a walk.

(Original)
とても大きな木でスマホの写真に収まりませんでした。周囲の芝生は綺麗に管理されていて、遊歩道もあるので散歩するのに良い場所です。

(Translated by Google) It's a nice place, but it's a shame that the doodles and garbage of casual tourists were scattered. There are many kitchen cars parked across the road at daytime.

(Original)
素敵な場所ですが、心無い観光客のいたずら書きやゴミが散乱していたのが残念。昼時道路向かい側にはキッチンカーがたくさん止まっています。

(Translated by Google) It is a very beautiful rose garden. You can see various roses. There is a fountain in the center and there are also chairs, so you can spend time slowly.

(Original)
とても綺麗なバラ園です。様々なバラを見ることができます。中央には噴水があり、椅子もあるのでゆっくり過ごせます。

(Translated by Google) Overlooking Long Beach Downtown and Seaport. It is a beautiful green park. It is convenient because there is an unreasonable patrol bus running.

(Original)
ロングビーチダウンタウンとシーポートを眺めるかとが出来ます。緑が綺麗な公園です。無理巡回バスが走っているので便利です。

(Translated by Google) There are two bridges on the left and right, which can be passed by car or bus. It is lit up at night and is beautiful.

(Original)
橋は左右2つあり、車やバスで通過できます。夜になるとライトアップされて綺麗です。

(Translated by Google) It's a wonderful view. Even in summer, there are times when the wind and fog are thick, so it is convenient to wear it.

(Original)
素晴らしい眺めです。夏でも風や霧が濃い時があるので羽織るもがあると便利です。

(Translated by Google) It was a small aquarium, but it was well maintained and I enjoyed being exposed to fish and seaweed outside.

(Original)
小さな水族館でしたが、綺麗に管理されていて、外では実際に魚や海藻にも触れられて楽しかったです。

(Translated by Google) When the weather is good, you can enjoy a very beautiful scenery. It is convenient because the MTS bus is running.

(Original)
天気が良いととても綺麗な景色を楽しめます。MTSのバスが走っているので便利です。

(Translated by Google) When the weather is fine, you can watch the beautiful sunset. The lawn is beautiful.

(Original)
天気が良いと綺麗な夕日を眺めることができます。芝生が綺麗です。

Worth the drive out here to walk among some of the oldest living things on earth. The loop trail through the groves is 4.5 miles long, but took forever as around every bend, every dozen of yards is another magestic bristlecone that demands to be admired. Some elevation gain on the trail, but if you make it out here to see the bristlecones, you should be stopping  almost too frequently to admire these ancients. Towards the end of the trail I had to force myself not to stop in order to finish at a reasonable time. A humbling experience that brings perspective.

Heartbreaking relic of the dark history of our country. This place is a must go to appreciate what happened to the Japanese Americans who were forced to live here under behind barbed wire and watch towers. Very large vistiors center with a huge central exhibit. There is also an auto tour which takes your around to restored buildings to see how they lived, adapted, and ultimately thrived given the hand they were dealt.

Great place to see petrified wood. Great paved trails but also ask the rangers about some backcountry hikes and they'll have some handouts about where to park and suggested routes. Many of them have no defined trails so its fun to make your way through the painted desert landscape. The hike through Jasper Forest to Eagle Nest Rock is one of the best in the park but requires trail finding abilities.

Great hike through a canyon filled with petroglyphs. There is no real trail, so you have to explore to find the petroglyphs, and pottery shards. Eventually the canyon levels out to a stream and you reach a bridge. Keep going past the bridge and follow the stream on the left hand side a ways to find rocky areas with more petroglyphs. Please be respectful of petroglyphs and other cultural resources.

Highly underrated NPS site. Tons of developed lava tubes to explore with easy access. Make sure to bring two sources of lights and a map for the more complex caves, or you will get lost. Some caves have bacterial mats which shine in the light and others have some crazy colors, others have ice, while others have petroglyphs. Some lovely cinder cone hiking trails as well.
likes: Diverse cave features (bacterial mats, colors, ice, petroglyphs)

reviews_attraction.text: The must do gun show in town. Actors are pretty enthusiastic, and admission comes with a mini preshow documentary about the conditions behind the shootout and the town, which is actually really good and informative if all you know is the movies. They let you take pictures with them for free after the show.

Great park with the largest natural bridge of its type. Great for picnics or to hike down into and through the natural bridge. Bring grippy shoes as it gets wet and slippery under the bridge. However, the park is pretty small with not a lot of trails (most of them are centered around the natural bridge)

An easy day trip or place to stop on the drive between Flagstaff and Phoenix. No visitor center (managed by BLM) and mainly dirt roads. Take the Badger Springs exit and follow the dirt road (okay for typical passenger vehicles) to the trailhead. Leads to some nice rock art and a creek.

Great site with lots of trails, great views, and a great visitor site. Entrance fee gets you into Wupatki as well. Cannot hike the name sake sunset crater, but you can hike another cindercone nearby. Easy day trip

Pricey for what they offer. Cool trail and short guided tour around part of the rim. Large visitors center with great exhibits and two overlook decks. Decent sized giftshop with a subway for food. AAA discount.

Fascinating place. Visit at night when they have the telescopes set up for observations. Got a good look at the orion nebula and saturn when I visited. Can be extremely windy and cold though, so come prepared.

Great visitor center and cliff ruins views. Cannot access cliff ruins. Some short trails in the area but not a whole lot to see or do. worth a stop on a longer trip or combined with tuzigoot/montezumas well

Highly underrated NPS site. Worth the drive out to walk among the rock formations. Hike the Heart of the Rocks Loop if you can, it will take you between, and around many of the rock spires and formations.

Many animals were out and about despite the snow. Great raptor show and petting area. Great way to spend the day if you're in the area, but hardly a destination in itself. A bit expensive for what it is.

Great vista, but also ask the rangers for info on hiking into the Jasper forest to the eagle nest rock. One of the best hikes in Petrified Forest, but no defined trail, so it requires some trailfinding

lovely mansion near NAU. They offer tours inside and a self guided walk around the grounds. Doesn't take too long to do everything here, but worth it if you're on NAU campus waiting for something else.
Several ruins, some remarkably well preserved within walking distance of multiple pull outs. They also have some ranger led backcountry hikes offered occasionally but they fill up fast.
Few places like it in the US. Large geoglyphs created by ancient man. Two sites are easy to get to and clearly marked. The third has no obvious trail to get to.
Literally a 5-10 minute hike to get to the hole in the rock. Lovely views of the park and city from the top. Often really crowded with lots of noisy families
Great place for kids and adults alike. Some things inside require additional payment but there is plenty to keep you busy with just the price of admission.
Great NPS site with nice visitors center and you can walk among the ruins of ancient cultures. Massive complex with many interpretive signs.
Great cannon demonstrations where you can practice loading and cleaning a cannon. Interesting exhibits and great view of the bridge. Free.
Great museum. Took a few hours to get through everything. Worth the price of admission just for Yayoi Kusama's infinity mirror room.
A bit underwhelming. A lot of stuffed, dead animals in some interesting poses and dioramas. Worth a visit, but wouldn't visit again.
Cannot access site due to being locked out by a chain linked fence. How ironic. Only a few structures are left standing/restored.

Toured this in 2013 and also had the chance then to eat in the restaurant. By the time we made our way through the exhibit to the restaurant this time the restaurant was closing for the day which is very unfortunate because there are such exciting things to look at in the restaurant. Chihuly is a collector of all sorts of things and they're well displayed within the restaurant.

Maybe this place isn't for everybody but it is for my family and me. We love art we love colors we love Gardens and flowers. We always take plenty of pictures and yes you can wait for an opportunity when you don't get strangers in the background or the foreground of your photos. There are benches to sit down and just admire the amazing works.

The roving photographers will take your pictures and you can access these and have a great Memento of your visit.

I found the gift shop this time to be a little crowded. Last time I bought all kinds of interesting things. Since this is the beginning of our trip I kind of held back on the souvenir shopping here. Yep there are things I would have liked.

Dusk was coming on and I could see that some of the sculptures were starting to light up in the outside garden. I've never seen the exhibit at night yet I have seen pictures of the Chihuly glass lit up at night in this Garden. I was hoping to stay until dark but we had a time to ticket to go up into the Space Needle so we had to get going.

In 2013 we stayed at the Maxwell Hotel and walked back and forth from the hotel to this park. This time I was amazed how easy it was to find close parking although it was expensive and we had to guess how long we would be staying when we parked our vehicle and paid for our space.

I know you can see Chihuly start work and so many different places but if you're in Seattle do not miss this stop. It is worth every penny you pay to get in.

We went just out of curiosity to Point Defiance Park. We drove through the park as we headed to the Olympic Peninsula. We were amazed by the raccoons we saw. It was obvious that people were feeding them. Feeding wild animals is supposed to be discouraged. Some raccoons are passive and other seem like they were ready to jump in our car when I put the window down to take a picture. It was a bit scary.

I don't know about the state of Washington but around here raccoons are night time animals. Author I knew who wrote a book about a skunk said that when nighttime animals are out during the day that's a bad sign. Like maybe they have rabies although these raccoons look pretty darn healthy to me.

The picture of the Raccoon by the tree we took from our car and a lot of little picnic areas. There were two people creeping up on it trying to get as close to it as they could. We don't know what happened because we drove away it was looking like it was going to be fight or flight time.

Frank Lloyd Wright designed this house. In it's day it was probably surrounded by a better neighborhood. But the home is so well preserved one forgets what is outside once the tour starts. There's just so much about this house I think it would be best if you went to see it. It is handicap accessible. I stayed in the kitchen with my sister who was in a wheelchair while my other sisters went with the tour upstairs to the bedrooms. I've been to Springfield many times but this is the first time we ever stopped at this house. I would definitely chore it again when I go back to Springfield.

This place has reinvented itself many times and always spins into something better. I remember when it was Teacher Place with spinning tops and puzzles. What a creative place. Probably couldn't see and do it all in 2 days. Maybe even two weeks. Judith hosts many different types of events. If you've never been here do visit. Even locals don't know it is a gem in their midst. If you've been there once or a few times return. Here's the place to buy low tech toys that don't have screens or buttons to push. Get social at the Logic Puzzle and Spinning Top Museum in Burlington Wisconsin.

Always a fun place to visit. My sisters went up in the ferris wheel and enjoyed that. We enjoyed shopping for souvenirs at one of the local shops. And we had a delicious lunch at The Crab Pot. It's interesting watch how they serve all those pots by just dumping everything on the table in front of people. Even more interesting is watching how people eat the crabs mussels clams shrimp corn and potatoes or whatever else comes in the pot they ordered. Our cousin from Wales met us here in 2013 and we were excited to go here again. We had a table along the windows on the south side.

Whoever thought that we would see salmon swimming up-stream, actually I guess it was a river, so they could lay their eggs and spawn.

It was so interesting we had to stop again on the way down just two take another look, and sure enough the scene had already changed and it was a new photo opportunity.

I was wanting to get to the temperate rainforest. Although it's a little like the Redwood forest in California it is a slightly different ecosystem.

Do you make sure you make this part of your travels if you go to Washington State.

This is a great drive-thru tour. Buy a bag of food before you start to feed the animals as you go. Be conservative it can be a long drive. The variety of animals is amazing. There's a speed limit but you can really enjoy it if you go slower and stop to take lots of pictures. I wouldn't want to drive through there with a vehicle that doesn't have windows or a top. We've driven through twice now and each time has been a completely different experience.

Here's another place we stumbled upon on a hot day. We debated and debated whether or not to go in but we spent a very enjoyable afternoon there. We've been to other aquariums but there was just something quirky and different about this one that we still talk about and laugh about the good time we had. You don't need children to go here we were all adults and enjoyed ourselves immensely

Oh my gosh we love this place. I never thought I'd get to Olympic Peninsula. But the opportunity presented itself on a recent trip to Seattle and Portland. We spent probably two and a half days staying I'm traveling around the Olympic Peninsula. We enjoyed every minute of our trip.

We drove by. We did not stop because we were trying to make it to Bainbridge to spend the night. From the outside it looks like an interesting place. Point Defiance is full of activities and interesting stops if you did it all it would take more than one day.

Can't miss this even if your family didn't come into this Harbor when they immigrated to America. So nice if you can go on a tour of the statue. Don't skip the gift shop they have so many interesting things. Even the cafeteria is fun to eat at.

World class art. I've been visiting here my awhile life...I still remember my first visit where's my baby sister my mom and dad great aunt and uncle ... I must have just been at the end of three years old or the beginning of 4 years old
Blazing hot when we were there. Changed so much since late 60s....it really is a monument now. Don't miss the photo opportunity. We enjoyed it and the vendors. I suggest going in the morning.
Nice watercolor show. I understand the shows change regularly. It looks like they have a wonderful classroom area to take classes. Wish I lived closer. And don't miss the outside sculptures.
This is a must-see. It is eye candy. I don't know if it's possible to take it all in and just one trip. I need to get here again and spend a longer amount of time viewing the collection.
Always interesting to go here. It is a great home with a sad story. Get there at the right time and the gardens are absolutely gorgeous. In the spring they have a fantastic plants sale.
Love this place. Always changing exhibits. Gift shop is fantastic source of art books more gifts then one can probably carry. We love the cafeteria with Wolfgang Puck food.
There early in the morning very quite. Few people. Music must be motion activated as it startled us when it stated. Got our pics and moved on up the road towards Chinle.
It's always fun to go to museums and other places and see their collections. This one is no exception. It is a must stop and see place. I hope you enjoy it.
Do not miss it. Incredible sight. Had to come form Wisconsin to AZ to see Basket Meteor that had been stolen and sold at estate sale in Wisconsin.
So interesting. I wonder what driving over this bridge would be like but it was fun and scenic. I'm glad we went this way.
Do stop here because of each twist and turn of the road the views are always amazing. Make sure you have your camera long.
There with sun making it a glorious experience. Wondering why all the people disappeared and where they went? Do stop!
Gorgeous stop great place for pics. Get out of the car and stretch your legs. Take in some of that Arizona Sun
Came upon it by chance last July while on vacation. Returned again this August because we enjoy it so much.

$3 cash only per vehicle. Plan on 30 minutes.  Keep your expectations in check: there are two signs measuring 2' X 3' explaining the battle, and one "earthwork": (dirt berm measuring 4 feet tall, 15 feet wide, 60 feet long).  That's it for the period stuff.   You can see the river / marsh. The road crosses over it in what I assume to be the natural bridge (40 feet wide, looks like a man-made dike ).  There are also 3 picnic tables under cover, bathrooms with flushing toilets, electricity and running sink water.  There are no electricity outlets in the bathroom,  but one on the wall of the wellhouse - unsure if it is active.  There are two water faucets on the grounds, but no handle.

$13 to go up. $3 off with "America the Beautiful" pass (which costs $60 - nat'l parks thing). Note that it is in a "diverse" neighborhood with a mass transit drop off right there so you ought to be prepared for "local flavor". Don't leave valuable items in view in your car (phone charger or any other cords indicating valuables inside, coins, hat, lighters,  tin foil...).  I tripped over an individual who had injected or smoked enough of something to pass out in the middle of the path. I went at 9PM, it's open 'til 10 this time of year (memorial day to labor day I'd assume).

$10+tax electric only (2 normal 110 house sockets and a 30 amp. No 50 amp).  $15 electric + water - no site has dump.   There is a dump on-site - but awkward to access: must back up a slight incline.   Very clean, nice staff, boat ramp at the campground (noisy jet boats - but only 3 in 12 hours and only at sunrise and sunset).  Walk to shell mound - wear boots: the trail around the mound is muddy.  There is a swing set, deer cleaning and fish cleaning station.  Verizon signal is constant but weak. Can always text, but 3G & 4G comes and goes, always very weak.

Open 24/7. Bring a flashlight if after dusk.  90% of art is on a 1/3+- mile loop (hard packed dirt through the forest) which can be driven.  If you have a high vehicle -  say 8 feet - just walk it.  I would say a high top Roadtrek / Pleasure-Way / Sprinter would be fine.  I would not take my 10' tall RV because low branches would remove my AC & antennas, and branches side-swiping the gel coat.  The road and grounds are very well maintained and art is outstanding.

It is inside an enclosure.  So the good news is it is viewable 24 hours a day.  The bad news is glass = glare.  Regardless of creative angles, trying to physically block the reflection of the world outside it's bubble, and holding a black coat up between the camera and the earth, glare.  It would be nice if they had a scale... like a 10 foot yard stick next to it.  The gift shop / museum / info center was closed and has no posted days or hours.

$20 per vehicle.  Plan on 3 hours minimum. There is no tour, but a 20 minute cannon exhibition four times per day.  Wear boots as there are uneven surfaces and plenty of beach to walk. No food: bring your own.  Bring a scarf, mittens, ear muffs, hat, windbreaker, sweatshirt... well, your whole closet. It's very windy and on the December day I visited barely reached mid 40 degrees.
dislikes: Limited Activities (No tour, only short cannon exhibition)

reviews_attraction.text: $25 adults if you go in the mine.  Plan on 3-4 hours to see it all,  read the signs, and go in the mine.  Arrive 15-20 minutes before tour (check-in is slow. then you walk 3 minutes to tour start point, fill out a form, then await with your group.  The mine is 10 feet tall+- and 15+- wide.  I'm mildly claustrophobic (can't do elevators) and had no issues.
