Self-guided: show up and go through a museum then her house.  Quite a few items, but not a lot.  Plenty of information on her film career.  Museum is high-budget, well maintained,  great condition. I spent 2 hours which was on the upper end. One hour is probably normal.  There's also a huge children's activity area with lots of things for them to do.
likes: Facilities & Services: High-budget, well-maintained, great condition

reviews_attraction.text: Park in the memorial lighthouse parking lot.  Trail head is at the end of the parking lot.  It is unmarked.  Just wander up the stairs and you'll end up on the driveway which leads to the top.  3/4 of the way up the trail branches off to the right.   I'd recommend following the paved driveway to the top, then walking down the gravel trail.

Note that there are Mosquitoes at dawn and dusk.  The walk is about 1000 feet from the road (from the glasses). Whoever owns the property has cleared a 8' wide path so I take that as an indication of it being OK to visit (the farmer is literally losing money by makingit accessible,  so be considerate and respectful of their property).

Not worth the $10 admission.  Takes 35 minutes to see it all. If you go around twice and take lots of pictures: 1 hour.   A stroll in any other park is free and nearly as enjoyable (generally lasts longer, too).  That said, if you don't mind blowing $10, it's definitely pretty and maintained in an excellent manner.

Free admission & parking (thus 5 stars). Plan on one hour. Highlight is a large room filled with "tree people": folk art by a good ol' boy turning trees and limbs he found down by the river into quirky, fun people. 3 more former classrooms and halls upstairs & down filled with art.

Free admission and free parking across the street (1 hour). Closed Mondays.  It takes about an hour to see the gallery.  Presently 4 artists on display (large section for each). Recommend visiting the beautiful Catholic church 2 blocks away while there - it's beautiful inside.

Free admission, donations appreciated. Plan on 1 hour. Free parking in public lot across the side street/ kitty cornerish (RV spots - but they were filled with local's cars, while the car spaces were empty).  Focused on local pioneer history, fishing & lumber, development.

$8 admission.  History of Texas on the bottom floor, (artifacts, displays, huge painting on the wall), local sports & music display upstairs. Plan on 3 hours if you read everything. Free parking.  Note that there is nothing else for tourists to see or do in Port Arthur....

$2 or $3 cash only honor-system pay station. Level, well maintained dit & sand "trail" / road.  No bathrooms or water.  Note that if you have a vehicle over 10 feet tall or 25 feet long, you should park on the cement at the gated exit only park entrance across the highway.

$3 Wyoming resident, $5 non-resident. Definitely worth it. Plan on 30 minutes minimum, 1 1/2 hours maximum. 4 stories, all accessible - less the rooms which are now offices, exterior of carriage house, and the grounds as well (nothing too exciting outside).

It's raining, windy and cold.   But ya know what?  Oregon is so danged awesome that they place their pretty stuff in such inconvenient locations that i don't even havta get my lazy butt out of the vehicles!  As if that's not enough: it's free!

Great about one hour visit.  Nice and welcoming staff.  Cool artifacts.   33% fraternal organizations (e.g. Elks, Masons), 33% Native American (baskets), 33% turn of the century life stuff. It's housed in a gorgeous old bank building.

Free to see.  Accessible 24 /7. Parking right there - note that if you have a high clearance vehicle you need to park in the office/ brewery complex (or somewhere else) as there is a railroad overpass which is low.  I believe 9 feet.
Hard to criticize something which is free to visit.  But... I sure wouldn't want to be a taxpayer shelling out my money to support it (unless there is an incoming revenue stream I'm not aware of).
Absolutely gorgeous!  1, 2, and 3 o'clock tour.  Must register in advance as it's limited to 15 folks.  In mid February with sleet and 35 degrees they all filled up and hour before.
The town has seen better days, but the statue is sitting strong, clean, and maintained. There's a neat old home / hotel / bed & breakfast a block away
I only walked the trail: it is free, very well maintained, and takes about half an hour if you go very slow and read all the signs.  Saw no wildlife.
The park itself is basically open 24/7.  The lighthouse is sunrise-sunset.  There is NO Rv dump station.   (Septic has failed.)

This is a fun family park. I especially like the fact that they have multiple tracks of varying difficulties. They have tracks for little ones and tracks for adults. They have some cars that allow a parent and child to ride together (and one type of kart gives kids a fake steering wheel so they can pretend to drive when the parent really is driving).
They do need to update their mini-golf area. It is not well-maintained at all and most people don't realize you have to go all the way back to the main entrance to pick up clubs and balls. They also need a good sound system in each pit stop so the employees don't have to yell out instructions over the din of the engines (I couldn't hear any of the instructions)

Very unique family-friendly place with a combination of rescued animals, several historic buildings and zip lines throughout the campus. Something for everyone. I spent about 2 hours here but didn't do any zip line activities.
The only reason I didn't give 5 stars is that nearly all of the indoor displays were closed. Not sure why. If it were due to COVID, then all indoor facilities would be closed. The only ones open during my visit were the caboose and the Phipp's Gallery. And yet I still paid full price for entry with everything else closed.

A must-see for anyone interested in Paso wines. Easy access from the highway. Lovely indoor/outdoor tasting area with a cowboy saloon motif. The wines are not only good, but fairly priced. They have an assortment of affordable table wines, which I thought were delicious. Then they have a selection of fine wines to please gourmands, and while the prices are a bit higher, they are not extreme. Tasting is FREE--something you don't see much in Paso--but they are sure you'll want to purchase a bottle or two (or twelve). Don't pass this one by.

Tours are expensive, but I have to admit, the tours are very much worth the cost. My particular tour guide was so versed in all things Hearst, it felt like I was attending a college seminar class. The grounds are absolutely stunning. Very well-kept. Rooms are so decorated, it's almost too much for the eyes to take in. I ended up buying another tour while I was there because the first one was so good.
They also have a number of free EV chargers, which was very convenient to have. One of the closest things America has to a real castle.

Nice museum in a good location. Price is reasonable...but you also have to pay an extra $5 to park. They also charge an extra $2.50 to use a credit card. There are some marvelous displays, but there are also some that are too cluttered, dark, or difficult to read because they are in corners. At the time I visited, 6 different buildings were closed. If they could address some of these issues and possibly create a combo ticket with the parking booth (which takes credit card with no additional charge), this would be a 5-star museum.

I travel to a lot of wineries. Of course, after tasting the wines, some are okay and others I don't care much for. Not Black Mesa (BMW for short!). They have exquisit wines. Their prices are a bit high, but the wine is really worth it. It's worth the trouble to drop down from Taos or up from Santa Fe to taste these wines. Nice outdoor area to enjoy as well as a fine tasting room. BTW I only tried their dry reds and they were out of this world.

Local home-town museum. Lots to look at. Probably too much! Some displays are really well-done (especially the fresnel lens). Others are somewhat hodgepodge, but that's typical of a home-town museum. They even use the space in jail cells for display. A few of the displays are not easy to see because you are blocked off, or the display is behind reflective glass or behind jail cell bars. But for the price, this is a pretty nice museum.

The main museum is FREE. I really enjoyed the displays. Spent probably 2 hours there. I understand the butterfly pavilion costs some extra, but they happened to be closed when I got there because of a rare freeze that made them scramble to protect the butterflies. Oh, and there are 2 electric vehicle charge stations in the parking garage and I was told you don't need a university parking pass to use them.

Goosebumps. Just being at the place where powered flight actually happened. So cool. Very nice memorial area and informative plaques to describe the details of this remarkable time. Small but nice museum. Roads in good shape. Entrance might be a bit high for what it is. Another odd thing: They have reserved parking for "low emission vehicles" but no charging stations. It kinda defeats the purpose.

It's not Smithsonian quality. Many mannequins and display cases look like hand-me-downs. But what they lack in pizazz, they make up for in volume and history. The admission fee is low--and I rarely say that. If you are really interested in reading everything, you could easily spend the whole day here. I ended up spending an hour and a half. Enjoyed the curator as well.

Um . . . this didn't do much for me. Basically you climb into a small "train" that takes you about 20 feet forward and backward. The train tilts one way and the seats tilt another. There's a lot of noise and shaking around you, but otherwise it comes off really cheesy. If you have to pay for an entire family, you'll spend a lot of money for 5 minutes of nonsense.

Better than I thought. Definitely a step up from some of the lame attractions in Gatlinburg. Features a number of iconic TV and movie cars from the Batmobile to the Back to the Future Delorean. Also had some specialty cars that were used by stars such as Michael Jackson, Dolly Parton, Bob Hope and others. A decent collection and nice displays.

Small museum. They have several rail cars to see (not all were open to see). There is a really interesting display of the "Jim Crow" Combine Car. There is a swanky presidential car called the Ferdinand Magellan but you have to book a tour and pay extra to see it. I went fairly slowly and saw everything in under an hour.
dislikes: Limited access (some rail cars not open)
Extra cost for special exhibits (Ferdinand Magellan)

reviews_attraction.text: I happened to arrive during a chili dinner fund-raiser. Didn't know about it, but they ended up waving me into the museum for free! Lots of interesting displays housed in a former school building. Well worth the visit (they also have their own parking lot which is nice with the crowded downtown parking situation.)

I spent about an hour here. $8 might be at the top end of what this smallish "museum" might be worth. However, the layout is really clever and the murals were absolutely top-notch. Looking at the beautiful murals almost makes this museum cross over into art gallery. Kudos to the artist!

This place has two major assets: It's free and it's peaceful. I've seen better botanical gardens. This one is okay. Shelby gardens in Sarasota are much better . . . but also cost something like $20. Free is nice, but I didn't spend more than 20 minutes here. Might be nice for an event.

Fabulous jail building housing this museum! The displays themselves are okay ... but the reason to come here is to talk to the docents about the history and the personal stories that are behind the various collections. I spent over an hour talking to these folks and loved every minute.

Get your kicks here (Route 66 reference, of course). Very well laid-out museum. Good overview of what makes Albuquerque so unique. Price is actually low for what you get to see, and I rarely say that. I particularly liked the Navajo Talkers exhibit. Get down here and get your kicks.

It's a pretty good museum. Not all figures are spot on, but the poses are mostly nice and the best part is that you can get right up close and get your picture taken. Many of the figures allow guests to don costumes or props. Makes it pretty good.

Free museum with decent exhibits. Located in a former school building. In my opinion you can learn just as much about Casa Malpais here as you can going out to see the actual ruins. Well worth a visit. Plan on about 45 minutes to an hour.

Unfortunately the day I visited there were no costumed rangers. I enjoyed the buildings, but without reenactors, there wasn't a lot of information. Lovely setting. Lovely walk. And hey, the price is right!

Really cute show. Good variety of music, dance, contests, comedy. There is a whole slew of food--too much, really. And they don't allow for doggie bags, so the food gets wasted. That's my only criticism.
Very lovely setting. Free wine tours offered. Very decent wines. Knowledgable folks running the tasting. Only reason there is not a 5 star rating: They charge $10 for a tasting.
Nice place to bring the kids, get back to nature, see some unique sculptures and just relax. This is well worth a visit...at least once.
Not much to see here and the displays are not really marked, but the cabin is picturesque and the volunteers are really nice.

This is a really neat falls and park. Black Eagle Dam is a hydroelectric gravity weir dam located on the Missouri River in the city of Great Falls, Montana. The first dam on the site, built and opened in 1890, was a timber-and-rock crib dam. This structure was the first hydroelectric dam built in Montana and the first built on the Missouri River. The dam helped give the city of Great Falls the nickname "The Electric City." A second dam, built of concrete in 1926 and opened in 1927, replaced the first dam, which was not removed and lies submerged in the reservoir. Almost unchanged since 1926, the dam is 782 feet (238 m) long and 34.5 feet (10.5 m) high, and its powerhouse contains three turbines capable of generating seven megawatts (MW) of power each. The maximum power output of the dam is 18 MW. Montana Power Company built the second dam, PPL Corporation purchased it in 1997 and sold it to NorthWestern Corporation in 2014. The reservoir behind the dam has no official name, but was called the Long Pool for many years. The reservoir is about 2 miles (3.2 km) long, and has a storage capacity of 1,710 acre feet (2,110,000 m3) to 1,820 acre feet (2,240,000 m3) of water.

The Cathedral of Saint Helena is the cathedral of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Helena, Montana. Modeled by architect A.O. Von Herbulis after the Votivkirche in Vienna, Austria, the construction began on the Cathedral in 1908, and held its first mass in November 1914. The Cathedral sustained significant damage during the 1935 Helena earthquake, which required extensive renovations. The Cathedral was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1980.

Really cool historical area. Reeder's Alley is situated in the southwest corner of downtown Helena, the capitol of Montana.  It is the oldest intact piece of early Helena. The property is a strong link to the beginnings of a settlement here, offering insights into the lives of miners, the Chinese influence, building techniques of the time, and life of the common men and women who came here seeking their fortune.

Inside the canyon, you are surrounded by walls that soar up to 80 feet into the sky with specs of blue remaining visible. Unlike other slot canyons in the area, you won’t feel claustrophobic because there’s plenty of room, which could possibly add to the acoustics of the place. The walls are red, purple, and pink, and there’s even foliage, which makes a nice contrast to what’s otherwise barren desert beauty.

Great little hike with a pretty cool view. I really enjoy going to this Park. There is a lot of see but not so much in the way of hiking unless you venture down to the river. Still, some many great views. I would try to plan your trip on a day where the air is clear, right after a storm. It will add to the enjoying. All the Rangers are very nice and friendly too.

Great little hike with a pretty cool view. I really enjoy going to this Park. There is a lot of see but not so much in the way of hiking unless you venture down to the river. Still, some many great views. I would try to plan your trip on a day where the air is clear, right after a storm. It will add to the enjoying. All the Rangers are very nice and friendly too.

This is a really nice and easy hike but it is a little long at slightly over 3 miles one-way. Very beautiful the entire time. You need to bring a lot of water (trailhead says 4 liters) during the summer because it is hot with very little cover. Great for kids and dogs but very crowded. Highly recommend it, it is a Utah institution!

This is a very nice trail. It is a little steep in the beginning but after about ¾ of a mile is flattens out and the meadow is very nice. Keep going until the lake, about .5 miles or so. Great day hike for kids and a short getaway from the valley. Keep going around the lake for a little more fun. Trial might be ¾ of a mile or so.

I really enjoy going to this Park. There is a lot of see but not so much in the way of hiking unless you venture down to the river. Still, some many great views. I would try to plan your trip on a day where the air is clear, right after a storm. It will add to the enjoying. All the Rangers are very nice and friendly too.

I really enjoy going to this Park. There is a lot of see but not so much in the way of hiking unless you venture down to the river. Still, some many great views. I would try to plan your trip on a day where the air is clear, right after a storm. It will add to the enjoying. All the Rangers are very nice and friendly too.

This is a beautiful Basilica. Even better if you attend mass too. There is a number of statues and art everywhere. The grand alter area is quite stunning and well worth the visit for just that. Take the short tour after 11 a.m. mass on Sundays, it is fun and gives you so much information about the building and art.

This site is an outstanding example of Barrier Canyon style rock art. It is estimated to be over 2,000 years old. During 1995, the people of Emery County, with the help of the State Centennial Commission, the BLM and the numerous volunteers, restored and dedicated this site a Utah State Centennial Legacy Project.

What a great place! I had no idea this was out here and didn’t really know what to expect. It was a great couple hours. We saw so many different birds and wildlife I could not believe it! It is difficult to get to but if you have time make a trip out of it and enjoy! Great for kids too.

Great national forest with tons of hiking, fishing, climbing, camping, etc. to do. Stop at the visitors center for lots of information on everything you can do in the area plus they have great maps that are very helpful. Take time to enjoy all the forest has to offer and soak it all in.

Such a fun time on the train and there is always a new theme to keep it a little different. Love how the staff is usually high school kids, they are funny and silly. Their story has some fun items to choose from and you will not be disappointed taking an afternoon out on the rails.

Always a great view point to spot in at. The color of the rock and massive size of it make it special. Not too much more to do at this one as there are not any hiking trails around and you cannot get any closer to it then the view point. Still, well worth the stop.

This is a very nice park. Not very large but the playground was quite good. They also have a pool, skate park and a large open field. Seemed to be a nice stop for children to run around and burn off some energy. Could be good for a picnic too. Stop by and take 10.

This is a great city park with so much to do. There are basketball courts, a great playground for small and older children, open green spaces, climbing walls, a river to play in and a great picnic area. Highly recommend this place for locals and travelers alike.

This is a great city park with so much to do. There are basketball courts, a great playground for small and older children, open green spaces, climbing walls, a river to play in and a great picnic area. Highly recommend this place for locals and travelers alike.

There are limited things to do at this park but seeing Dead Horse Point is really awesome. I looks like it would be fun to take Potash Road down to the river and explore there too. I recommend getting to the point for sunrise as the view is beautiful.

There are limited things to do at this park but seeing Dead Horse Point is really awesome. I looks like it would be fun to take Potash Road down to the river and explore there too. I recommend getting to the point for sunrise as the view is beautiful.

Cedar Mountain is a fun little place to see far distances from great elevation. There is a lot of camping in the area and a lot of places to explore. It takes a little bit to get out there and the road can be rough at times but nothing impossible..
Nice enough place with a lot of different creatures to view. Fun time but a little pricey. They have a small cafe too. Penguins are fun to watch!
Great forest and National Park. Great for a short weekend, long weekend or an extended trip. Come on out and enjoy this National Forest.
A spectacular park in a small town. So much for kids to do. Great playground and the pool is nice too.

This is a tough trail (if you go all the way to the bridge), but well worth it. Our two kids were able to do it. I would recommend going super early to avoid the crowds. The parking lots fill and some people have to park out on the main road - which will only add to your hike.

Towards the end, it gets more technical and climbing large rock steps, with lots of people waiting in line. Once to the bridge, there was a very long line to take pics on the bridge.

Also keep in mind sunset, as the sun leaves the east side of the trail and where the bridge is well before sunset. The trail took us two hours round trip and there were people heading up, without headlamps, near sunset. 🧐

Technically, you could drive your properly equipped vehicle past the parking lot and closer to the trailhead. We have a high clearance 4x4 and there is no way I’d take my truck up that rocky trail.

A beautiful less-traveled gem of a National Park. It’s a must see! The views from the visitor center (and the overlook just prior) are amazing. In these Covid times, the visitor center was not open but they had a table set up outside with maps, the passport stamp, and to answer questions. They had a line outside the gift shop, and were getting items people requested to purchase. They were closed from 11:30-1pm for lunch.

We (including two kids) hiked the Oak Flat Loop trail that starts from the visitor center. It is rated as “difficult” but wasn’t too bad! There is a bunch of elevation change but there is also plenty of shade for breaks.

We also traveled down into the canyon (via car) to get to the river. The road is pretty hairy but worth it! We had lunch by the river but beware of bears. There was a sign advising the fisherman to be mindful.

A must see! We visited while the shuttle was not running and the parking lots can fill up quickly. The drive down is a bit scary but doable! Thankful to the park for using the campgrounds as extra parking.

The Devils Postpile loop is a little taxing but short, and well worth it. We also hiked to the Rainbow Falls viewpoint. Take water and use sunscreen! The walk is roughly 2.5 miles and I couldn’t believe the amount of parents with kids with no supplies! Lots of sun and it’s warm!

I found it fascinating that the John Muir Trail and Pacific Crest Trail passed through this area. We decided to hike this trail north to get back to the ranger station. I cannot recommend this enough! Beautiful views and NO people. There were throngs of people on the Devils Postpile Loop and Rainbow Falls Trail.
likes: Cultural Value (John Muir Trail, Pacific Crest Trail)
dislikes: Crowded (Devils Postpile Loop, Rainbow Falls Trail)

reviews_attraction.text:
This art museum is absolutely worth it for the price - and you might even learn something! It’s a small museum, I spent maybe 45 minutes there. I loved their exhibit covering the Great Basin, especially the photographs. They have a large collection of Native American arts - all donated from a couple that collected it.

They do not allow backpacks, but they do have free lockers (maybe 12?) for you to use. If it’s busy, you may need to plan ahead. You have to reserve your tickets (online) at least two hours in advance due to covid. When I checked in, they had a sign that kept track of how many people were in the building. There were only a handful of other people while I was there.

They do have a hands-on kids art area, but it is currently empty due to covid.

An amazing place to visit if you have a budding herpetologist. There are a few alligators, and many types of turtles (feed them for 25¢). They have probably the most impressive display of venomous snakes I’ve ever seen. Think mambas, cobras, and fer-de-lances.

We love animals. We also LOVE conservation and education. I absolute love and appreciated (the owner’s?) talk before the snake milking presentation. You’ve really got to think about what goes into making snake anti-venom and the service this establishment provides to help save lives. He also talked with us and tried to help us ID a snake we found while out west.

What a fabulous hike! 99% of the people here simply hiked down to the water. It’s a pretty gnarly hike down (and back up again) - and is overgrown in areas. I CANNOT believe that some people hiked down with their young children and all their stuff.
We saw (from above the rim) a young family get lost with their baby.

It was more than worth it to hike the entire Box Canyon Trail. With this trail you got great views and the pretty water. Take lots of water and good shoes. No flip flops like some we saw.

We also read about ticks, poison ivy, and stinging nettles so watch out!
dislikes: Safety concerns (ticks, poison ivy, stinging nettles)

reviews_attraction.text:
Just gorgeous!

The visitor center is closed due to Covid but the trails and restrooms are still open. The trails are short, and easy, and parts (most all?) paved - perfect for families. We saw fish, lizards, and birds.

We also drove past the visitor center with our truck. The road is VERY rough and slow going. We didn’t even make it to the campground (20-something miles in). Instead we parked in a pull off and had a picnic. Absolutely gorgeous up there. Didn’t see many other humans other than some Jeeps and OHVs.

A Disney fan’s shopping Mecca. Disney is doing Covid precautions right. Temperature checks and masks are enforced. We went on a Sunday but it parking was not at capacity.

Best stores: World of Disney (all thing Disney souvenirs), the Christmas store (any ornament you could think of), and the Lego store. There are some waits to get in stores but everything moves quickly.

I would not eat at any of the restaurants $$$, but instead head to 192 for familiar favorite chains if you’re just looking to grab a meal.

We were only looking for the view from Forrest Gump. This entire area is just gorgeous and worth the drive.

Monument Valley is owned/controlled by the Navajo Nation. If you are heading east on 163, the signage will direct you to turn right on 42. This led us to a (closed) toll booth for entry to Monument Valley. All of the Navajo Nation is currently closed down due to Covid.

We then turned around and continued East on 163 and soon you’ll see this beautiful view. No entry fee required.

Fabulous, and easy trail. Great views of the lake. It is hard packed so there were many bikes on it as well. We parked at the visitor center, hiked to the Hoover dam, wandered a bit there, and hiked back. That totaled right at 9 miles.

The five tunnels were really fun for the kids to see. According to the signs, the hike is closed June through September, which seems reasonable because there is no shade.

What a beautiful day in February. Although it was a bit deserted, they still charge $10 for entry. And be sure to pay and display your receipt because they were writing tickets that day.

The beach was beautiful and clean. Loved seeing the ice floating in the water on this cold day. I’ve seen this same beach in the height of summer where there were TOO many people. Visit on a. winter day!

A must-visit place for little rockhounders. There is a dirt road that leads to the top, and we did fine in a minivan.

How we found ours... I wandered down the mountain on the side towards the mine. Sat next to a tree and starting inspecting the surface rocks. Found plenty and no need to dig. They are little dark spots in the rocks - look for the mini geodes!

A lovely state park with a beach that is very much worth the admission. When you purchase the entrance fee, it allows you in and out privileges for the day.

There were not many visitors. We saw a lot of people beach combing and a few people fishing. There is also a shop before you get to the beach that rents kayaks, etc.

This is an absolute must do national park unit. At the visitor center, we were lucky enough to see a group of coatimundi - the most fun animals I’ve ever seen. Suzanne Moody at the visitor center was so nice and helpful.

You must take the drive to Massai Point. We did it at sunset and the views were gorgeous.

This was an okay NPS site. There was a ~1 mile loop trail from the visitor center that we walked. I wish there were more interpretive signs explaining what we were looking at. The map/trail was not in the main park brochure. I think we were missing the interpretive trail guide but did not see any anywhere.

A must see! The drive alone is worth it! It is a very high road with severe drop off (and little to no guardrails) but the views are stunning.

We came on a very hot 4th of July (and were able to see the American flag on one of the monoliths) so we only did a short hike to a lookout point.

A wonderful and beautiful place to visit with the kids. Take the (free) shuttle to the quarry exhibit hall and see real dinosaurs bones as they lie in the ground.

We also hiked the Box and Hog canyons. These were very short and easy hikes but so beautiful. We saw deer and a wild turkey!

More of a quick “nature walk” than a hike but still beautiful. We saw fish, birds, and chatty squirrels.

I think it would be perfect for families with littles. Also has vault toilets which is a plus. Not too much parking but still found a spot on a holiday weekend.

What a fabulous hidden gem. Very inconspicuous little turn off of Barnes Blvd. No pets and no feeding allowed.

Trails are clearly visible with small signage. We wandered for two miles.

The scrub jays may come to you if you’re standing still.

A quick roadside attraction south of Las Vegas. I would only stop if I were heading north, not south because it is quite the detour.

There are A LOT of visitors and a lot of litter. The parking lots are gravel and kind of rough.

This was a nice, quiet beach at dawn. Small parking lot. And the bathrooms were unlocked about 7 am.

Keep in mind this is a dog beach. There were a few dogs there. I also found dog toys buried in the sand. Don’t litter, people!

The privately held Four Corners Monument is currently closed due to Covid. The sign indicated that admission is normally $10/person.

Although it was closed, the area and the drive are beautiful and worth it.
This NPS site is small and on the Main Street of a tiny town, but it is great nonetheless. Jay was full of information to share! He recommended a local hike to us and it was fabulous.
It’s right off the main road. It’s a perfectly quirky roadside attraction on a road trip. Be forewarned, the dirt road around the cars is pretty rough.

A must visit if you’re near Tucson. We were there at opening and it was not very busy.

We took a couple of short hikes and the scenery was gorgeous!

Red Ledges is a great adventure!  It is probably not one for little ones unless you had someone with you that knew all the super safe paths, but a great adventure for teens and up. I would have given it 5 stars except for the fact that this trail is not well defined with Cairns or on Google maps, or All Trails.  There is no support once you get up there to help you out, and you can end up in spot that are there for repelling and not hiking that might not be super easy to back out of.  Even considering that though I gave it 4 stars for the beauty and coolness of the hike.

I started up the left side trail and just tried to stay on major trails.  It didn't get stressful until the top and then it was a little tricky to get up that last section. At the top there are trails in so many directions.  Not sure where many of them go, just the trail I ended up on :).  It was so safe and mellow with gorgeous view that I was real happy with this trail..until I got to the east side of Red Ledges.  Now this trail is not on Google maps, or All Trails so there is no help knowing what trail is right and what trail is wrong. That is stressful for me hiking when I am on high cliffs.  I felt like I was on a safe good trail that was leading me to a safe passageway down.  That is what my gut told me, but then I ended up on a ledge and the major trails went off to spots where rock climbers do a lot of climbing and repelling.  I got nervous that this safe happy trail was leading me into a scary situation that I might not be able to get back out of.  Of course, best thing to do is head back the way you came, so that is what I did and sighed a big sigh of relief when I was safely down.  Now Google maps has Red Ledges on the map, but there was also a spot called Diamond Fork Arch that popped up and I knew it was close.  I opened up my Google maps (which I had already downloaded the area) and typed in Diamond Fork Arch.  It said you are 1 minute away.  I had no idea I was so close to I had it walk me to the arch.  It was serious just on the east side of Red Ledges.  I headed up this trail, and at the top I was shocked to find that my safe path I was enjoying early did indeed merge up to a safe way down...right where I was.  There was a little ledge, but I was surprised I missed it.  I was happy to have figured that out for next time, but I could not see any signs of the arch.  I pulled up google maps, and somehow I had walked right by it.  I headed back down again paying more attention to my google map and realizing I am not looking for a huge landmark.  It did not take me long to find it.  It was tucked into the West side on the cliffs and was beautiful.  I was like....now I get why this canyon is called Diamond Fork.  It is after this little beauty.

This falls is a great family hike, and the kids love to stand under the 50 foot falls and get wet.  It is also a favorite for those learning how to rappel.  There is often people at the top repelling  down the side of the waterfall.  To get to the falls, you take the Pleasant Grove Utah exit 275. Turn east, and follow the road up to 100 E in Pleasant Grove.  Turn right to 200 S, then turn left (east).  Follow the road all the way to the top where there is a parking lot, and the trail head.  The hike starts kinda dry and hot, but it as soon as you get up to where the water is not piped in, it gets greener and cooler.  It is only about 1 mile up to the falls, and there is is cool and a delightful area to explore.  If you have more time, you can hike past the falls, and right off the bat you will see 2 more pretty waterfalls.   The hike above is steeper but if you go up about another mile there is a spot where the river gets wide, Rocky and very shallow.  There is a sign here and there is a trail that heads over to Dry Creek Canyon.  If you go from here up about another half mile it gets a little steeper and narrow, but you end up coming to a T in the trail.  The right side heads to Baldy or connects also with Dry Canyon.  The left side gets up to a dirt road that you can drive all the way out to American Fork Canyon.  I usually walk the road for just a little while and then head off on a small trail through the meadow that heads down Grove Creek Canyon, and right by Indian Springs.   This canyon was named because a tribe of Indians used to live up in this meadow.  Some skirmish happened with the Indians and the Pioneer settlers and there really was a battle between the two that happened at the base of Battle Creek Canyons.   A beautiful canyon with spectacular cliffs, beautiful waterfalls (at least 10), and a bonus that you are very close to the river almost the whole hike.

Escalante is still a work in progress in developing roads and making trails really clear, so you expect a little bumps.  To get to this hike you have to travel down Hole in the Rock Road (which is 26 miles south of Escalante of Highway 12)  You travel down Hole in the Rock for 26 miles down a washboard dirt road to the Dry Fork Road that heads Northeast into the dessert.  This Dry Fork Road branches again very soon and you need to stay left.  The road here gets much worse.  On the last part of this road there is a lip that makes it tricky to not bottom out and ruin your car even in a 4x4 vehicle. I wish they would fix it. The parking lot is just a cleared spot in the middle of the dessert with a sign that let's you know you have reached the correct spot.  You start the trail.and you are following Carins down a hill.  Keep track of the Carins, and if you loose track of them, turn around and head to the edge of the cliff drop off and walk back until you find a place to get down safely then search for those Carins and footprints.  The last part you walk along a steep Rock wall and then Dry Canyon will be on your left.  There are actually 3 amazing slot canyons here.  Dry Canyon is not as dare devilish and you can hike it if you are wider than 18 inches.  It has steep walls and is narrow, but not narrow like the others.  PeekaBoo has an entrance that is really steep climb 12-15 feet but has good hand hold, and then once you get past that there is a other spot that is not as steep, but needs a buddy to boost each other to get up.  Most people hike PeekaBoo then turn right and walk about 10 minutes to the entrance to Spooky Gulch, then drop down into Spooky Gulch.  Those who go the other way cause problems for you are trying to get through a narrow 18 inch canyon and passing is not easy.  PeekaBoo is narrower than Dry Canyon but not as narrow as Spooky Gulch.

Last time we went to Stewart Falls we went from someone's cabin, and for some reason I heard or read less than favorable reviews on hiking from other trailheads.  Still I knew this falls is incredible, so I headed out and decided to see for myself what issues this trail might have
Surprisingly, I thought it was a great trail.  U started just past the pay station just barely past Aspen Grove.  It is the same parking lot to the top of Timp from the South Trail.  It is a well marked, well maintained trail here. It is not that long of a hike.  I think it was  less than 3.5 miles round trip.  It was a beautiful hike with lots of pines and views of the Ski Resort.  It comes down from higher up on the right side of the falls and allows lots of beautiful views from up high.  I used Google Maps to get me to the trailhead and All trails.  I downloaded both All Trails map and my Google maps of the area and both worked great, but I am not sure this trail ever gets out of cell range to even need to download anything.  Also the trail is so well defined that it doesn't need anything special to stay on the trail.  The falls were beautiful, but I have seen them when they were spectacular, so I am hoping we get more moisture and that I get back here at those gorgeous moments that I can see it when it is really gushing again. I think I went just a little too early in the seeing this time.  (Early April). I think if I give it a few weeks it will be as amazing as I remember it.

There are 2 things I enjoy the most on a trail, really tall cliffs, and pretty rivers.  This has both in abundance. The cliff are such a beautiful red color, and they are so huge...they are Godlike Grand in scope, and you walk along these cliffs the entire 2.5 miles in.  The river is really a small stream, but you follow it almost the entire time crossing over the stream often.  I would suggest 2 things.  1. Wear spikes or crampons over your shoes.  I had them in my backpack and just started the trail not yet evaluating if I even needed to put them  on, and only a few steps from the parking lot into the trail I hit a big patch of ice and before I knew it I was smack on my bum.  (Broke my tailbone again…huge bruise back there). I wish I would have put my spikes on right from the parking lot.  There is a few more parches of ice, but there are trails now that go up higher above the ice and into safer areas. Watch for them. Second I would suggest either a really good pair if waterproof hiking boots, or waterproof socks. You cross the river so many times that you are bound to get a little wet.  With as cold as it is, it is smart to do on of those 2 to keep you feet happy. Of course the arch at the end is very worth it.  Get all the way to the end of the trail so you can see it.  Amazing trail.  Absolutely LOVED it!

I heard this was a very large aquarium, so I think I was expecting more.  If you visit lots of aquariums this is small in comparison.  It has a lovely variety of the local fish. I thought with how large the sea turtles are that are located around the island that they should have had some larger sea turtles.  The dome film was nice and well done but very short.  There was not any sea lions, or otters, or shows with larger sea life.  The tunnel with the larger fish has some beautiful large rays and they are delightful to walk in the tunnel and see them glide over you.  The have some very large box fish that were beautiful.  There is not a petting area, or touch area.  This area has some beautiful trumpet fish and Corelian fish in the Maui area that I never saw in the aquarium.  They also have grass eels in the Maui area but not in the aquarium.    I enjoyed this aquarium, but it is not as large as is advertised, and I thought it was a shame that they have much wildlife in the surrounding area that are not displayed in the aquarium.
dislikes: No shows with larger sea life
Missing local wildlife (e.g., trumpet fish, Corelian fish, grass eels)

reviews_attraction.text:
This trail exceeded my expectations.  I loved enjoying sunset while walking along the trail.  I enjoyed watching the ducks swim, and caught a glimpse of 2 beautiful cranes.  I enjoyed the sound of a wonderful variety of birds in the grasses.  I loved walking down close to the lake and finding a stream and a swing.  The beauty of the lake, and the fresh lake smell was refreshing, and the views of the mountains was stunning especially when they lite up all pink from the sunset.  The book the Nature Fix  states lots of studies that are proving how being out in nature especially a place that inspires awe dramatically increases your immune system, your creativity, and your emotional wellness.  This walk was a perfect awe hike for me that I felt entirely replenished afterwards.

#LetsGuide #TakeAHikeDay #GoogleTrailGirl

Great aquarium especially for not being on the ocean.  The otters are awesome to watch and there are 2 sets of different types.  The penguins are super fun and the baby chick is adorable.  Thier is a great variety of different types of fish.  My favorites are the octapus, the cuttlefush and scorpion fish, the rays, the turtle of all sizes from small to sea turtles, oh so many beautiful creatures.  They have a butterfly exhibit that was beautiful, but felt low on butterflies, but they have just been hatching some so I am sure it is increasing. They have some beautiful birds, ducks, 2 sloths, poison tree frogs of all colors, and a nice shark tank.  Lots to see, lots to enjoy.

This Banyan Tree is the largest in the world.  Some might look and say it is just a tree, but it is so much more.  You need to follow that branches on the main  Banyan tree and you see that it sends down a root and each branch has a sub tree that became like a sons/daughters of the main tree.  Then you have this son/daughter trees that sent out shoots that have grandkid trees that are still linked and part of the main tree.  It is a genealogical masterpiece to see all the generations or the tree that are still part of the main tree but its life and purpose still moves continuously down all those generations.  Amazing.

#Letsguide #ShaunasAdventures dot com #GoogleTrailGirl

This week we chased the sun down to Sand Hallow Reservoir.  It was perfect temperatures down there in the 70's in early April.  Two of my favorite things to do at Sand Hallow are to Walk along the rocks on North side on the lake, and to Kayak around the Island exploring the little inlets, and then hike to the top of the island for a scenic view. Teenagers love the cliff jumping off the cliffs.  The ATVing on the South side is super fun.  The fishing is good if you like Bass, but the lake gets too hot for trout to survive in the summer. The beauty of the the bright turquoise water and the red cliffs is stunning.

This was a fabulous hike.  I heard that it was a hard trail to follow the Cairns, but they have added nice green rectangles on the slick rock to Mark the trail.  It was easier than watching for Cairns ( some which were knocked over.)  I went in January and the footprints also helped make the trail easy to follow.  An awesome winter hike.  The ice in spots was a little scary, so be careful around the ice.  Both Bowtie and Corona Arches were amazing.

This was a fabulous hike.  I heard that it was a hard trail to follow the Cairns, but they have added nice green rectangles on the slick rock to Mark the trail.  It was easier than watching for Cairns ( some which were knocked over.)  I went in January and the footprints also helped make the trail easy to follow.  An awesome winter hike.  The ice in spots was a little scary, so be careful around the ice.  Both Bowtie and Corona Arches were amazing.

When I first walked up to the Arch, my first thought was I thought it would be larger, but as I walked in front and got a glimpse of the view behind, I was amazed.  We were smart and got here in the morning, so the Arch was spectacular being lite up underneath.  The trail was not long, and was not difficult.  The Cairns that lead the way are box like and unique.  It was beautiful.  #Mesa_arch #Island_in_the_sky  #canyonlands #Utah_Rocks

We hiked the short Upper Falls hike, and then up the Provo River Parkway along the river up to Vivian Park.  It was a perfect start to a morning.  The falls were gorgeous, the walk along the Provo River was shady and beautiful to watch the wildlife in the river.  Many people were biking to Vivian Park, or skateboarding (since this section is not very steep), walking, or running.  It was being used to Vivian Park, but not over used.

I really enjoyed this hike.  It was fun to pretend different HooDoos were characters from our favorite fairytail book.  There was areas that looked like they were towers and gates into the world of fairies. Fun place to use your imagination and enjoy feeling a part of a different world. I would suggest starting early if it is in the summer, or bringing spikes if it is early spring.

While down at Sand Hallow we decided to check out Quail Creek State Park.  I think I like it as much as Sand Hallow.   The lake has better fishing, it has a fun little inlet on the North side that has some rope swings that you can swing out and splash in the water.   The campgrounds are not as boring as the ones at Sand Hallow, but the showers are outside the bathroom pay showers.

Hikes like this are my favorite.  There are enormous cliff walls on both sides, but it is not so narrow you feel clastorphobic. There is amazement at awe around every bend.  It has me amazed from start to finish about the creation of this amazing place, and encourages me to be a better person by living up to my potential.   Beautiful...one if my favorite hikes in Utah!

Beautiful historical wonder that took years to build.  Inside sacred ordinances happen just like in the ancient temple to help groups of people who love God, learn how to return to him.  It needs a special temple recommend authorizing worthiness.  If you don't have a recommended you can still walk the grounds and feel the special spirit that is here.

One of my most favorite places in Northern Utah.  I love walking through the gardens and seeing the statues of Christ.  It fills me with gratitude and encourages me to be the best version on myself. Sculptures are so exquisitely done.  Flowers are beautiful.  Absolutely love my time here.

One of the busiest visitors centers in have seen.  Video is good.  Displays are very nice.  Employees are very helpful.  The air-conditioning is wonderful after.bejng out hiking so it is a great place to cool off.  It is about the only place in Bryce that has decent WiFi also.

Most people that think of Glen Canyon as Lake Powell, the dam, and the Bridges, but the scenic roads are also spectacular.  We took a road call Crosby Canyon Road, and it was amazing.  Also the Lone Rock Beach was extremely beautiful also.
More unique than most blow holes, for this one makes almost a horn noise.  I think it is because it is connected to another cavern and the wind rushing between the two makes cool noises.
Beautiful display of boats.  There are places set up to help you learn how to tie many different kinds of knots.  Nice place to take a stroll on the ocean front.
Such a fun unique spot in San Francisco.  A nice little exercise getting there. If here you really should enjoy walking up the sidewalks on the sides.
Not really a park with a kids playing area.  It is a pavillion at the trailhead of some amazing hikes of Battle Creek canyon and the G hike.

There is a lot of activity on this city block.  There are musical concerts throughout the week, you can even attend the broadcast performance of the famous Tabernacle Choir on Sunday mornings.  There are two visitor centers, and tours that are available for free.  Christmas lime brings thousands of beautiful lights, which is a tradition for many to view.  In the warmer minths, the gardens are always beautiful and well kept.  It is a deationation for visitors from around the world,, at no cost or donation asked for.

My husband and i just wanted to go some place different to read in the afternoon.  Since Davis County does not have a mask requirement, we decided to drive up north.  There are paths for walking, tables under boweries, and a playground for the kids.  We brought our own chairs, and we bowers, it a little difficult to find a flat space in the shade.  However we enjoyed our time, even though my drink tipped over twice in the grass because of the steep hill..

New this year!  I have been looking forward to this visit for quite a while.  There is a jungle gym play area, an oversized back yard where you feel bug sized, an activity where you move ants through a picnic, and a lecture area where you can touch giant cockroaches in addition to the biosphere where you can actually play with the butterflies.   The nursery, with hatching chrysalis, is very interesting.  Over all, the visit surpassed my expectations!

This is probably our grandkids favorite part of Thanksgiving Point.  There is so much to do.  We have literally stayed from opening to closing time before.  They have a special salt dough ornament activity for the holiday.  All the grandkids made several with their allotment of dough...additional charge, but it kept them happy and entertained for an hour or so.

Always fun to see a part of the past and be a part of the future.  It seemed that all interior remodeling has been finoshed, but there is construction outside on the west side.  Parking was not fun, I guess there was a lot going on.  I did see a couple of tourist busses, but there is a lot of space inside and out that I didn't notice crowds.

We brought a quick little picnic here.  The trail must have been quite busy, because the parking was full, but we were alone in the bowery.  Some families were on the play equipment, but not so many to make social distancing difficult.  It is a beautiful view of Rocky Mouth from here.  Restrooms were still open.

What a fun place to visit.  It is not always open, no set hours, but if you are lucky enough to be there when it is open make sure you stop.  The curator so so friendly and enthusiastic!  He has a passion for this little project, and Montpellier is lucky to have him help their struggling Main Street.

I went to see the Eshert exhibit.  I learned a lot, and really appreciated the piano pieces that added to the experience.  I have enjoyed numerous exhibits this museum has brought to Utah over the years and will continue to travel in order to make the 30+ mile journey to do so.

We are not new to the Moab area, however a geo cache brought us to this new attraction.  Our weather was cooler due to a morning rainstorm, but I feel it could get hot here.  We had a very pleasant walk around on well maintained paths.  What a treasure.

Took the grandkids to the water park.  We have often times walked in a trail behind Wal-Mart and Lowe's to get here.  We have used the pavilion for family gatherings.  I hope to visit on a Monday night with the food trucks before the season ends.

My husband and I were on a short trip for our anniversary.  While out geocaching, we met a man who directed us here.  What a lovely little spot that we would have otherwise missed.  We walked around the Cascades, but did not explore the cave.

It is a beautiful place in the spring.  How the curtains open up at the end of the movie is nice.  I wouldn't want to "hike" to the petroglyphs when the weather is warmer.   Unlike any other National Park I have been to, much smaller.

The lady at the desk make our grandson excited to become a Jr. Ranger.  How the ranger who swore him in was just as fun.  Our little 3 year old can say and remember the name better than me, and I'm the one who helped him learn it.

We took our grandkids for the first time.  They loved all the activities.  The buildings showed the history.  They found the gift store interesting.  We did not get to do everything, so we will be sure to return again.

What a fabulous playground! There were different sections for children with different types of disabilities or perhaps I should say abilities. It was nice to see that the entire community can play together.

This was my first visit at this sight.  What an impressive aquarium.  I have been to shoreline aquariums that are equal,in quality.  The grandkids loved the electric eel, butterfly and Utah spaces area.
Went for the free, but tickets needed, concert as a part of Days of 47.  It was sad to see all the empty chairs, walk ups could have gotten in.  I have never tried to walk in myself though.
This was my first visit.  I knew the history, but to see it myself, and speak with a very knowledgeable volunteer was quite fun.  This is a hidden gem in the middle of nowhere.
What a fun outdoor playground!  I'm glad we went when it wasn't so hot outside.  It would have been fun to be the first to discover these interesting landforms!
We finally got to Calf Creek!  Then it started to rain.  What great sights and a fun "hike."  it is so popular.  I am so glad to live in its backyard.
We went geocaching here, and we were not prepared for a hike, so we really did not explore too much.  It appeared to be a lovely and busy campground.
While the kids enjoyed playing here, there were only 3 tables for us to eat lunch at.  Plenty of benches, but not many tables and no garbage cans.
We brought friends who had never visited this area.  It is amazing how far you can see, and there are so many landforms so close together.
What a hidden treasure in Logan.  We good the grandkids to see the animals and enjoyed a picnic and hide n seek in the adjoining park.
This is one of our favorite, year round, spots in Millcreek.  We had a cool out with the grandkids and a quick hike with them too.

Very nice people at the visitor centre. We went to the boardwalk.  Nice views but at the time of being there we just saw 1 gator, 3 egrets and a few lizards. That was about it.  We hoped for more wildlife. Because the park was so empty of wildlife,  we skipped the canoeing.

A very nice birding place. September may not be the best period the park but  we we're still able to see over 250 pelicans, avocet, stilt, cormorant, mallard, ibis, egret, heron and so on . To bad it was soo dry.

Might be good but at the time we were here there was just 2 egrets and a few turtles. The visitor center was open but couldn't find anyone. To bad as I collect the stamps of all parks including the refuge once.

A nice surprise.  For 15 usd you get to see 5 museums. The car museum is the best one. The prison is also worth it but needs repairs. We spend 2 hours and a half to visit everything. Three stop was worth it.
This park feels like it is just added for people visiting hot springs as there is little to do. The trails are not really worth it. Was pretty disappointing. Even the views were not that great.
3th time i come to Badlands, and this park has a weird effect on me as the more I come the more I like it and discover new things, it's actually in my top five of favorite parks in the US
Weird that this one is in the national parks book but that you need to pay 5 usd to see the very small museum even with the annual card pass I have seen much bigger museums for free.
A small park with very friendly staff but the was nothing to see. No cranes... but we couldn't even see a single bird not even a warbler. I will have to come back another time.
A little park with 2 hikes one easy along the rim. And one that goes down the canyon 600 feet with a lot of stairs. There are way better canyons but still worth a little visit.
Excellent museum it took us 3 hours to see everything. There are some unique pieces here. Sometimes it can happen that it looks like abandoned pieces. But it has it charm.
Very nice little park. Loved the boardwalk on the swamps, we saw a deer,  several woodpeckers and so on.  Wish we had more time to do the whole trail.
Very nice park ranger at the visitor center. We also enjoyed the 45 minute movie and the park itself. One of the better battlefields I have seen.
Small and not really worth it. Maybe great for children. For adults it's a bit disappointing especially if you have been to NASA's cavaneral.
Very nice lady received us. There was not much to see when we were there as most things left last week. We will be back some other time.
Would love to go up there at least once, each time I am here it is closed for some reason. Other than that  I love this monument.
Very unsafe place. Inside is ok, but be careful outside and we're you park. ML KING must be proud of what this done has become.
It's pretty unique to see the way things we're constructed inside the rocks. But other then that there is not much to see.
The house was empty when we did our visit just a few pictures we're exposed in the room. But the visit was the same price.
The per and boardwalk aren't bad but the view of the brick wall that the buildings show you  destroys it a little.
A nice little state park with a few tails a waterfall and some rock formation. But overall not that much to see.
Nice gardens and house too bad you can't use your annual park pass to visit the house as they ask 10 usd pp.
A nice little surprise. You can find info at bison range. It is small but there was a lot of birds around.
A nice little state park for 5 $ that toy can use in other state parks the same day. Its worth a stop!
Other part of the Wild life refuge where the visitor center is. If you like birds is the place to be.
We arrived at 4.45 PM and unfortunately it was already closed. Sad as it said it closed a 5 PM.

4/5 Stars (-1 for Covid Precautions of fellow visitors)

I love this park. It is huge. There are a variety of playground equipment, including a spider web and another climbing area. It has a giant splash pad that my kid loved using during summer (last year). There are large ponds to look at and long walking areas to explore. There is even a winding hill with benches at the top to relax and plenty of benches throughout the park.

I want to give this park 4 stars, but I have to knock down my rating one star due to Covid-19 related issues. I know everything is outside, but you need to have your mask on and still try to social distance. Kids and adults alike consistent walk and play near other people. At this moment, AZ has one of the highest infection rates, and a lot of people in the park must think that because we're outside, we can ignore restrictions. Maybe it would have been better to keep the park closed for a few more months, but Arizonans are stubborn I guess (I mean, I'm here too, right?). There are other parks that have the same sized playgrounds or larger with far fewer children.

This park is very large and there are ton of activities to do. There is a large pond that you can walk/skate/bike around or fish in. There is a giant playground with multiple areas (unfortunately, the pirate ship is gone though), and the play areas are more varied than you find at a lot of other parks. There are diamonds to play baseball/softball/kickball and basketball courts.  It's a fairly new park, so you don't have to worry about the equipment breaking, splintering, etc.

However, I'm taking 2 stars away due to Covid. All the areas were PACKED TO THE BRIM with very, very, very few parents or children wearing masks,. Even within the families who had masks, there was usually a parent or child without one. The place was a pandemic nightmare. If you're reading this far, hear me out: wear your mask if you're going to be in close proximity to people, EVEN OUTSIDE!! Please don't get complacent!!!

I really like how many rooms this place has to offer. The clues are generally fair and match the room theme. So far, I've tried the "Hansel and Gretel" and the "Doll House", which were both great. I feel like Hansel and Gretel could have definitely used more clues/unlocks, since the Doll House had twice as many clues and things to unlock.

Overall, its lots of fun. I definitely recommend private rooms with like 1-3 people less than the max. It's pricey, but I'll probably be back for more soon.

This park could be better. The park attendants are rude and kind of aggressive when it gets within 30 mins of close time, riding around in a cart yelling and closing the gates promptly at close. The volleyball courts are almost always taken. The lake/walkways are nice to walk around, but there are people who camp the park at all hours of the day asking for change. I guess it's somewhat nice for a picnic/barbeque, but honestly there are others with fewer people to bother you.

This is a huge dog park with lots of extra subsections/gated off areas within. There is a ton of room for my pet to run around. However, the park closes way earlier than other parks at 8PM!! The lighting was also pretty terrible after the sun went down. Actually the while park has pretty bad lighting except the two softball diamonds. Unfortunately, the nearest dog park is like 10-15 mins away, so you'll have to just deal with it or go for a long drive.

You can technically experience 90% of this place free. The train and the carousel are relatively cheap, and the gift shop is reasonable. It would be great to do a picnic or barbeque here. The mini-train display, like most mini-train displays, had donation slots everywhere which guilted a few dollars out of me. One of these actually triggered a mini event in the mini train display. My kid loves trains which makes it a must-visit place.

This park is in serious need of a makeover. 3 old slides and 2 swing sets (1 for younger children/infants) in a sand box. If you want to use the field, it's big enough for soccer, frisbee, football, etc, but  if you came here for the playground, there are nicer ones everywhere.

On a positive note, there is plenty of parking; so, you won't have to miss the raid if you're playing Pokemon GO.

I came here for Bulbasaur during the Pokemon GO craze. It is definitely a park for those with Asian heritage. It can be daunting for people like my fiance who don't share that heritage. Also, it's huge. If you don't want to pay for parking, get there EARLY and park along the street. Get ready for a long but casual hike, if you plan to go all the up the mountain.

There is a playground and basketball courts, which were pretty well occupied during the afternoon, but as soon as the sun started going down, there was a much rougher crowd, sitting on the parking lot curbs drinking from cans. There was also really poor lighting. Overall, it was okay during the day but not at night. Much better places for exercise/dog walking.

I love this park. It's quiet, small, and relaxing. There is a bar at one end and the science museum on the other. There are tons of benches but walking around is very nice too. There is a covered part with trees in the courtyard that I like to walk through. It's also available at all hours of the day, since it's not enclosed like other city parks.

For me, it was too expensive.  $25/person with a TON of reading. Sparse history on animation, a few references to his characters, and waaay too much about his life. For artists and absolute ultimate Walt Disney fans, this is your place. For fans of just the Disney characters or park (or anyone bringing kids), this place is not for you.

One of the saddest parks I have been to. The soccer fields were closed and the playground is way in the back. The parking lot had no places to park. The park itself is rather large, but it's weird that it's completely surrounded by an 8 foot open bar fence. I guess you can jog and walk your dog, which plenty of people were doing.

The lake was overflowing (several of the bronze turtles were underwater) and it felt crowded. Plus, there was duck feces everywhere. I guess if you live here, it does have a doggy park and a playground, but the smell and the fact that it was smeared all over the sidewalks make it hard for me to justify coming back again.

This is a small park with a pond in the middle. The playground is on the opposite side of the park from street parking, but if you go around, you can park at the school. It's a nice park to casually stroll around, but you won't be playing football/soccer here.

Oddly shaped park, behind all of the businesses on Ray Rd. You can also get here by going around all of the businesses on 48th St. I wouldn't come here for anything but the baseball diamonds. There are also tons of people walking their dogs.

This park is huge. On a bike, it is wonderful. On foot, it can be awful. There is a lot of standing water, leading to a lot of bugs, including mosquitos. It also doesn't smell great. For exercise, it's great. Just don't forget the OFF spray.

Medium to small sized park, but a really small parking lot. There are usually soccer games in the afternoon. The baseball diamond is sometimes used. If you live in the area, it's not bad, but I wouldn't travel to use this park.

Pretty big park with a lake in the middle. During the fall, they start running the train, which is fun for my kid. They have plenty of picnic tables, and there are usually quite a few other people walking around.

This is a cool little park down the street from PV Mall. Lots of baseball diamonds and fields. Plenty of room to walk, run, ride, or picnic. It always has plenty of people walking around which keeps it safer.

This place is surrounded by one-way streets. It's a very small memorial plaza, but there were quite a few people walking around. There are a few bronze statues, plenty of benches, and at least one table.
Plenty of area to walk or ride a bicycle, which is what many are doing. I've also seen a lot of Jr. Soccer and there seems to always be a game going on in one of the diamonds. It's an okay park.
It's very unfinished and there is flooding everywhere. It could be nice, but with the flooding, there are tons of mosquitos. The parking lot is awful. The skate park is pretty awesome though.
This is a very small park, but there are always a bunch of people around. Could be nice for walking your pets or a quick jog. However, both the park and the parking lot felt cramped to me.
Nice long walk around the lake/pond, but there were tons of mosquitos. Visited quite a few times during the Pokemon GO craze last summer/fall. Park on the south end.
Small park. Very creepy toward sundown. I would head to another park, unless you live in the area and need to walk your dog.

Excellent National Park, A must see place for people who like caves. The visit to these caverns was quite impressionable for me. The walk through all these under ground formations is quite an experience. Have not have the chance to see the bats in flight in the evening, will have to go back. Also want to hike some of the trails there. The visitor  center is very well maintained and has a lot of good information.

Great National Park. The Saguaros are breathtaking. Nice visitor center. I only had the chance to visit the East Park. The drive through the park is very nice and there are plenty of places where you can pull of and admire the Saguaros. I hope to get to visit the west park someday and also be able to visit when the saguaros are actually in bloom, which is in the spring.

Nantahala National forest covers a good part of the far Western section on NC. There are many beautiful trails, waterfalls and historic sites. It is also a very good place to do some whitewater rafting. Most of the waterfalls in that area are easily accessible . From the higher mountain tops some very good views can be had. There are also several nice lakes.

Nice small visitor center with great views and  many nice trails. I have stopped at this visitor center several times. My favorite times have always been in June when the Catawba rhododendrons are in full bloom. It is a real treat to hike the trail near the center and admire these beautiful flowers. The mountain tops are just purple with all the blooms.

Excellent park. The 3 missions are  very interesting to visit. The 3 different missions are not too far from each other and the drive to them is very pretty. Each mission is different and merits each own visit. The trails to the missions are easy to walk . Each mission has nice has also a nice visitor center. Lots of history here.

This is great to visit with  your car. The colors are incredible. The drive through the park is very pleasant . The rock formations and colors change all the time . You can see many petrified logs and  also petroglyphs. The Inn at the end of the drive is must stop. nice architecture, history and of course good gift shop.

Very beautiful  park. Many unusual rock formations  great trails and great views. There are many good trails to hike on. Some are long and difficult but some are shorter and not too difficult. There are a lot of beautiful vistas along the way. The trail leading to the ranch is easy and the ranch is well worth a visit.

Great place to soak up on New Mexico's history. The visitor center has a lot of good information about the monument. Trails are fairly easy to walk and the ruins are easy to get to. Some ladder climbing is required to really see everything . The drive down to the monument is very pleasant.

Very good museum. Lot's to do for children. , Outside there are also many places for children to explore and have fun. The grounds are well maintained . There a good little restaurant with outdoor dining. The butterfly house is wonderful, Have been  there a few times with the grand kids.

Nice park with plenty of room for kids to play. Boats can be rented to paddle on the lake.This park has been around for a long time. Good place to have a pic-nick , take your canoe on the lake or have the kids play on the playground. You just can't swim because of the under currants.

Very nice park with an easy trail . Great views of the Dona Ana mountains. The trails are well marked and easy to hike . Many of the plants have identification tags  for people to able to identify them, The walk to the top is not difficult and the views are nice.

Perfect place to visit on the Parkway and purchase some locally made quality crafts. They have very good quality crafts and souvenirs. I really enjoyed  the different quilts . The mountain to Sea trail is also near by and you can take a nice walk in the woods.

Very nice downtown park. Has a gazebo, nice grass  and an area for children to play. The park is surrounded by a historic district which has some very nice historic homes. Walk around the area to appreciate all the nice homes and sights.

Beautiful Historic place. The house is very nice and so are the grounds. The gardens are especially beautiful in early spring when all the azaleas are in full bloom. The gardens have a very nice layout.
Excellent place to have a very good  view of the mountains surrounding the area. The drive up to the rock is rather winding and goes through some nice neighborhoods.
Great state park  with a great visitor center with lots of interesting and informative displays. Enjoyed visiting the fort and going through the different rooms.
Carrizozo is a nice little town to stop in on your way to the Valley of fire. It is small but still charming. Had a good lunch there before my way back home.
Very beautiful building and grounds. The building is quite big and the grounds are very nicely landscaped. Also nice view of the city of Frankfort.
Great National forest. Many nice trails for hiking. Also the higher altitude in the summer is a great way to get away from the heat.
Edisto Island has very nice and educational sites. The sites are a pleasure to visit especially in the off season. Nice museum.
Perfect place to go with children. My grand kids love this place. Lot's for them to do. They also have a very nice gift shop.
Did not get to go on the tour, it was loo late in the day but I did enjoyed seeing this magnificent ruins from the rim.
Great visitor center and a nice place to experience local history. Love the old buildings and the walk along the river.
Very interesting place. The drive to the crater is quite long  on a dirt road, but the place is really worth a visit.
Nice little relaxing place to take a break. The geyser is nice to look at and drive to it is nice also.

The festival is always enjoyable. After having attended this for many years, I was pleasantly surprised that little had changed and the artwork and artist are still amazing. My complaint is with their choice of wearable souvenirs. Typically, I purchase a T shirt or tank that features the selected artwork for that season. Not this year, they did not offer a shirt, hoodie or tank with the full representation of the artwork as seen in the poster.  I did, however purchase a poster to add to my rather large collection. This has not been the only time I was disappointed in the souvenir attire, I suggested several years in a row that they offer tank tops and out of the 20 some odd years I have attended, I have acquired 1. This years tank looked like a throwback to the 60's and the work resembled Erte. This was not appealing to me and did not warrant a purchase. Better luck next time. I will suggest once more that a better selection of tank tops be offered and that you include a full depiction of the exact same poster which represents the festival in any given season.

The performance and pre-show artwork was once again fabulous. Unfortunately, I had to endure a group of inebriates, of which two were talking and providing commentary incessantly throughout the entire performance. Mostly, one person who talked all but about 30 seconds during the Last Supper..which is very near the end. I did not make a direct request and wish I had. I did say..STFU loud enough for her to hear, but it did not stop the attention seeking drunk patron. I was 3 seats to the right of the person with diarrhea of the mouth and it was annoying. I wanted to ask the 2 ladies sitting in front of the rude patron how they enjoyed the show, but they quickly left as soon as it was possible.
People! Please if you cannot shut your mouth and keep your conversations at a minimum during a live performance, don't come to the show!

In town for a brief visit. So, I stopped by my old stomping grounds. Nixa schools was dropping kids off for a cave tour and I thought I might get my opportunity to see in the cave again. Spoke with the Park rep who informed me that public cave tours are available on Sat's. Unfortunately, I am unable to be here on a Sat. and,I am only in town for a few days. I was disappointed that he would not make a concession and let me have a viewing either with or after the school tour. Perhaps I will have another opportunity in the near future. Just sucks that it couldn't have happened today!😢

Another fantastic park in my hometown. This wasn't here when I was a kid. Glad to be able to enjoy it now. Took my Aunt there and we strolled through the flower gardens and took in the Butterfly House! A few plants were in bloom, mostly Peony and a few iris and a scattering of others. Wish I could see it when all the Lillies are in full bloom! Perhaps on another visit. But, for you who are local..Do this! And, do it often. Look at my pics..there is an event coming up in June!!

What a beautiful park. I only had time to hike a couple of trails and drive through to check out camping sites. Camping sites are wide open and on concrete pads. I also saw several RV sites that are full hook up. While the vistas are gorgeous and sites are situated to take in the view..there is limited trees and seclusion between sites. Hiking trails are well marked and the two I took provided wonderful views of Cheyenne Mountain!

Needed a meeting near our hotel, so I came here. The geese and ducks are very fond of this place and will hold up traffic often. The building in the park is secured by chain link fencing and that happens to be were the restrooms are located. I saw only one porta john and it was disgusting. I was curious if I would be able to launch a canoe from here, but probably not since the comments suggest there is no swimming here.

This is one of my favorite zoos!! I worked here as a young adult when the grounds were much more barren. So, happy to see how the foliage and exhibits have changed over time. Today's visit included zoo staff stationed at various exhibits providing samples and information about the animals. I really enjoyed revisiting here!!

This was fun. Known as an echo chamber that only you can hear, it was a neat experience. I tried to video record the echo, but it did not produce the echo sound on the recording. My Uncle said he could hear me echoing while he stood next to me, but was unable to hear himself. All and all, it's a novel thing to do in OKC!
