I absolutely love this place!! I have visited twice and each time explored different areas. I will be back next year to explore more. Too much to get it all in in just a few visits. Seemed to be busiest during the weekdays from 10-4. So, if you want to avoid crowds I recommend early morning or late afternoon.

The museum is just that! A museum! I found the artifacts within to be quite extensive and somewhat unique. I have toured many museums and I find is quite interesting to see the differences in the items collected from an era gone by. Thank you for keeping the ghosts of the wild west alive.

What a fun little find! This was a quiet spot on a Monday afternoon. I enjoyed the Butterfly House and  the themed gardens also! The lady in the gift shop was very friendly and the admission is so reasonable you'll have to spend money in the gift shop. Support this exhibit!!

This is a fabulous experience! Took my troop of Girl Scouts to warn their Musician badge. We also received an activity fun patch! I recommend 4 to 6 hours for the full experience! Headsets provide a sampling of the instruments and music of the world. Don't miss this museum!

First visit occurred  too late in the day,  but got some great shots and found a geocache,  went back a couple days later and got there just before the field trip left and a storm hit. We enjoyed the tour of the mansion and other buildings in spite of the inclement weather!

A very powerful place. Caught part of a tour on an overcast day. If you are sensitive to such things, you can feel the sadness while in this area. The memorial itself is beautifully done with a powerful conceptualization of the day in history..truly..profound!

Beautiful campground!! Just stopping by as I was heading to Downstream to meet with friends. Just the brief visit I had tells me I want to come camping here. Putting it on the schedule for next year!! Electric,water and cement pad!!!

Omg!! Beyond words, this one is...This should be on everyone's bucket list. I could not stop taking pictures and exclaiming how absolutely gorgeous all 4 directions. The creator was magnificent the day this was created!!

Excellent little museum and don't miss the Rose Hill School. I was there in May and they were celebrating a local artist.  Extra bonus..the school marm was still there and we talked with her too!! So...very cool!!

Good place for an overnight. Small campground with pull through not by the water, but water is nearby. Showers will cost you quarters. They are well maintained. Hiking trails will take you to the waters edge.
This was a great little escape in the city. Trails that make you feel like you are walking in the wilderness miles from civilization! Marsh areas were full of various ducks and birds.
Interesting site. There was a livestock feeding demo/discussion on the day I was there. I did not join in. Instead, I enjoyed the interpretive center and photographing the teepees.
Nice place. Geocache in several areas, so I rode around and stopped at many places. My favorite was the Bird viewing area. Nice and quite. I will visit here again to dip my canoe!
Don't miss this beautiful attraction in OKC!!!The Crystal Bridge was in bloom while I was there in early May!! Gorgeous! Outside Momma ducks and Turtles with babies!!!
All the shows were excellent! It was a hot day and not many people out, so we practically had the place to ourselves! Plenty of water provided and fun was had my all.
Great little Route 66 gem!! It has recently been repainted. The gift shop/museum is fabulous!! Don't miss this attraction when in the area!!
Very beautiful place to spend the afternoon! I was lucky enough to be there on a day when two artisans were making pipes!

They have a great annual festival with over 200 vendors.....as well as festivals throughout the year.  The town is a terrific place to visit as the restaurant scene is one of the best on the east coast for small towns.  The stores and the streets are easy to walk and browse.  The nightlife is also very good with some good bars.  I highly recommend visiting to see for yourself.

Terrific example of an old lighthouse that is still working.  George Washington commissioned this lighthouse!  It is kept in great shape and has a small, but well curated, museum.  the gift shop is a nice touch.  Great photo opportunity - well worth the visit when in Portland.

Great park to enjoy the views, picnic, hike, and visit the lighthouse. It is well kept with few services.  The food trucks offer amazing lobster rolls and gelato.  They have a trolley that will take you around the park.  Plenty of parking - free admission.

Great trailhead with a terrific main entrance with clean restrooms.  The trails are well marked and range from novice to advanced hikers.  The trails can be used by cyclists as well.  Sunscreen and water are a must on sunny days.  Nice views from the top.

Great show!  Terrific choreography mixed with great music!  The show is a terrific tribute to the music of the Beatles and the time period.  The multi-media effects are well done and the performers engage the audience. A must see when in Las Vegas!

Beautiful park kept in excellent condition.  Nice plantings and paths to walk on throughout the park. The historical main house is a treasure.  The Veterans Memorial walk is well curated.  The dinosaur section is fun for kids and adults alike.

Great architectural home in the desert!  It's great to experience the history of this timeless masterpiece in Scottsdale.  The stories of FLW's exploits are wonderful.  It is a definite  must see if you are in Scottsdale.

A great historic church in lower Manhattan.  This church plays a  great historical significance in New York history.   The cemetery  is an interesting visit as well.  A must see if in the area. Open to the public.

Covid 19 has affected the zoo and it is not worth goingt o during these times. That is unfortunate, but it is a shell of what it once was.  Nothing is open, and the animals are non-existent if available.
Cool well-curated museum showcasing the history of Motown!  Docent led tours add to the experience.  I was fortunate to visit for the Aretha Franklin memorial.  Well worth the visit when in Detroit.
I would recommend this for very young kids as the offerings are not that great for older children or adults.  Sparse museum with interactive activities, but too expensive for the value received.
Nice looking piece of architecture in which you can climb to the top and get good pictures of the views.  Not sure if it is worth the wait for tickets, elevator etc... but it is fun!
A gem!  They have a great collection, one that rivals any other in the states!  The digital gallery is a fantastic place to learn.  A must stop while in Cleveland!
Fun, worth the visit - especially Lockwood Mansion.  The architecture of the mansion is special!  The interior hallway is similar to Iolani Palace In Honolulu.
Great lighthouse in the Atlantic.  The half mile walk out the house is on granite slabs that is very well done and makes for and easy, most of the time, walk.
Fantastic outdoor sculpture museum!  Great space for families, plenty of food opportunities and areas to picnic.  Staff is very friendly and accommodating.
Excellent art museum!  Well curated showcasing various artists and their work.  The staff is very friendly and hospitable. A hidden gem in Rockland!
I was with a sommelier who said the Shiraz Reserve was an excellent wine!  She said it is worth a visit and she was impressed with their wines.
A cool museum experience showing the destruction of hurricanes Katrina and Ria on the first floor and Mardi Gras on the second floor.
Nice place to walk to the waterfront.  Good place for sports and for meeting friends.  Very clean spot.  Free for Norwalk residents.
Well kept up preserve with terrific hiking and biking paths.  Great place to take leisurely walks with friends and family.
I did this trail when I was in college - they have made many improvements to the trail since then.  Highly recommend it!
What a fantastic find!  Easy walking paths, nice place to rest, enjoy some tea or grab a light lunch.  And it's free!
A nice easy walking trail with river views.  Watch the markers carefully to stay on the trails.  Can be wet in spots.
Nice to finally see it reopened.  They have a few bugs to works out, but worth the visit while in SF.

Okay so full disclosure, the park itself is like 4 stars. Playground, field, good for walking, but the location isn't great for anything non-park or non-residential related. HOWEVER, I bump it up to the 5 star because of its location to so many hiking trails, which are all connected to the Los Penasquitos Canyon Trail, which is right along Penasquitos Creek. I've never dived too deep into the hiking (never more than a couple hours) so I'm not sure how extensive it is, but it's really fun to go exploring around here and see the greenery. The view is sort of nice, in that you can see far away, but you just see other hills and homes.

Lots of parking too. If you're looking to have a picnic with a bunch of people, I would be pretty shocked if you ran out of parking space. I've never seen it even half full, and I've been here a half dozen times.

Lovely park, right along the beach, a walk away from tons of restaurants and shops. The location is great for people who are able to walk around, and it is even better for people willing to get their feet wet. Bring a towel or sandals or related beachwear if you want the full experience, or simply walk around the grassy areas, sit on a bench, read a book, pull out your tablet, relax, and enjoy the warm Pacific wind. For anyone living nearby, you don't have to travel far to feel like you're on vacation.

Meanwhile, in Laguna (and nearby Newport), parking isn't really the easiest thing, and parking to get to Heisler Park is no exception. If you're not getting here obscenely early, then expect the hunt for parking to be extensive and intense. You may get lucky, but you may not.

Altogether a very nice park.

Went kayaking here. Big fan of the Opaeka waterfall. The water is pretty cool, but definitely not freezing. The air right next to the waterfall feels thick. It's a very different experience being under it. Kayaking was quite a bit of a workout for me, but I'm basically a nerd who studies at school for my life, so if you go to the gym constantly it's probably easy.

Looks gorgeous by the way. Highly recommend this.

Really muddy trail, so if you're bringing kids or grandparents who can't really take care of themselves, or other fragile humans, maybe consider going somewhere else or doing something else, other than the kayaking thing. I didn't look into other ways to enjoy the state park since kayaking worked so well for my group.

Small park with a little playground. One of the better locations for a Park in Mira Mesa. Just south of most of the shops, but if you want a quick bite or drink there's a 7/11 just around the corner. Near an elementary school and not too far away from a Middle school as well, but if you're around Wagenheim I'd suggest visiting the superior (larger) Hourglass park. There's a basketball court here though, which is nice, and the playground is quite diverse, considering how small the park overall is. The majority of the park is a field, which is nice if you want to kick a soccer ball, throw a football, or do midnight frisbee (but it's dark).

I tend to be pretty generous, so 4 stars might seem low, but the essence of it is that Maddox Park is small. There's a playground for kids, and a dog park for dogs. There's an overhang with benches/tables to eat at, or relax and talk. If you go to the dog park side, there's a view of UTC.

It's really a lovely little park, but that's most of everything there, beyond just a grassy lawn. I like it, but there's really not much to it. It's a walk away from most things in Mira Mesa, but that walk is long enough that you're probably just going to drive there or call up an Uber or something like that instead.

There is do much to do at waimea canyon state park. My favorite thing was the red dirt that permanently stained my clothes. It's so rich and pretty. The views and outlooks are phenomenal, and i even got to see a few three horned sheep grazing at one of the outlooks. The weather is crazy. It was hot and sunny on one side, and then we went to the other and it was raining hard and it was literally impossible to see anything except for fog... and rain.

This is a must see, even for people who don't like nature much. You can literally stay in your car and get some nice views.

I love parks and this is one of my favorite parks. They're doing some construction as of me writing this review, so it's possible things will change. For now, my biggest gripe is parking. More spots would be great.

So this park is located in the heart of mira mesa, close to a library, and includes fields and basketball courts and ping pong tables inside a recreation center. The rec center is nice and there's tons of activities. There's even a playground for the kiddos.

It's probably my favorite park in mira mesa. Easy walk to tons of shops and restaurants.

Pretty much the classic archetypal park. Playground, basketball courts, grass for picnics, big enough to walk or run around, and bathrooms. It's a bit dirtier than some other parks I've been to in Mira Mesa (or it seems that way), but it has everything you really need in a park. Bring your kids since the playground is surely ample for them. Perfect for anybody who lives in the neighborhood. Not too far from Downtown Mira Mesa if you want to go on a longer walk to there, but Mira Mesa has so many nice parks that this one pales in comparison.

Fairly nice park if you're into a little hike. Very green, but it is close to the freeway so you will be hearing cars go by every so often. If you're looking for animals, this might not be the best place. It's equally possible that I was just unlucky and unable to see any critters. At any rate, it's a nice place for a warm afternoon, or a warm morning. Wouldn't recommend hiking anywhere when it gets too hot though. I didn't feel an ocean breeze here, but ocean breezes in the UTC area vary from day to day anyway.

So I wouldn't come here to eat, but it's really a lovely place to visit. The observatory area itself is cool, and the views are pretty nice. Unfortunately, the city is pretty hazy most of the time (or at least both times I've been here), but you still get a pretty decent view otherwise. Personally, I'm a fan, and I'd take people here who have never been, but it's not somewhere I really plan to go ever again.

Everything for sale here seemed pricey.

If you're somebody who likes sitting in line, in traffic, waiting to drive down a street, full of traffic, this place is PERFECT for you. The homes look nice, the location isn't far out of the way, and it's something to do in San Francisco, especially as a tourist, but out of everything I've ever done in San Francisco, this was probably the most boring to me.

Not really a huge time sink though, so if you're looking to try it out, go for it.

This place is so lovely to walk (or run). There are so many trails and paths to take. Every staff member I've seen around here has been amazing and helpful. There's tons of wildlife inside and outside of the lake. There's a lagoon to swim in. In the summers, it can get very hot here, so be sure to bring sunscreen and water.

The lagoon is a fine place to swim, but as a clean freak it's always seemed a little dirty to me.

This is a smaller park, in a city full of parks, but it's plenty nice with a good open space to walk around, and a place for the kids to play as well. It's everything you need in a park, really, if you're not looking for anything in particular. The location isn't too far off central Mira Mesa either, but I think this works best as just a neighborhood park. No dedicated parking lot that I saw.

One of the best parks for dogs in Santa Rosa that I know of is here. They have a water feature which looks nicer when it's raining. Great place for a picnic. Located by a library which is nice too. Good for a walk, good to take the kids, play baseball, throw a football or baseball, play tag, etc. Great place to relax. Some nice looking trees too.

Kind of a modern seeming park. Has a basketball court, a picnic area, a playground, and tons of grass. Seems great for hanging out with kids, with the big play area (with lots to do, but I don't think I saw any swings). Not bad for a walk, and definitely great if you live in the area. Right off the freeway, too.

I mean you can give this a 1 star if you don't like history or parks. But I thought it was kinda neat standing here after all those lessons and lectures in primary school. Good place to start the red brick road in Boston.

Beautiful park. You can walk up and down this island all day. Tends to be a bit colder than inland SD since it's coastal, so bring a jacket for the wind if you are someone who gets cold easily. Lots of parking all over.
Great place to walk around and get lost. Pretty chilly until you get above the initial tree layers, and even then it can still be cold if it's the season. Nice views...fog permitting.
Location and the park itself are great, but the vibes I've gotten at the park a number of times is like I shouldn't have been there? Maybe it would be better to go with a group.

Honestly a pretty oddly shaped park, and after the fire the location isn't as good as it used to be...but it's not a bad park. It's just...a park.

Lots of parking though.
Okay so I'm admittedly not the biggest auto fan in the world, but I thought this museum was pretty cool anyway. Pretty small and tight, so there isn't a ton to do anyway.
It's a cute little playground. Maybe a bit small for certain needs, but certainly big enough to take the kids or for a little stop if you're walking along Fountaingrove.
Nice views of the ocean, nice views of cliffs, and nice looking vegetation. If I'm in the area, I'd rather look at the canyon honestly. Maybe it's personal preference.
Nice hiking place, but I would definitely keep an eye on the time and weather. It can get pretty hot.
Usually very busy, but a great place to walk to and around, if you get a chance. Lots to do here

One of the coolest trails in Southern Utah that's not in a national park! I loved my visit, and you will too.

Some tips for your visit:

• You can either pay $10 to park by the falls, or you can drive a few blocks away and park on the side of the road for free. It's up to you.

• Your shoes will get soaked. Wear a pair that you're okay with getting drenched.

• There is a ladder and some slippery surfaces, but it's not as treacherous as it looks. Still, I wouldn't recommend this trail to older folks.

This is a must-visit for anyone in the Four Corners area during the summer. There is so much to see in terms of outdoors AND artifacts. The tours are awesome and informative if you want to learn about cliff-dwelling pre-Columbian cultures. If you bring small children, be sure to keep an eye on them as there's plenty of places to fall down. You can spend 2-3 whole days in this park to see the whole thing, so be sure to do some research into camping opportunities beforehand.

I love this place! It's a hidden gem. It's way off the beaten path from civilization, but it's well-worth a visit. Lots of neat hiking trails. Of course, it's not on the same level as, for example, Grand Canyon or Zion, but it's still a beautiful place. If you find yourself in the I-10 corridor and have some time to do something outdoorsy, this is a must-see. Bring water and snacks and you'll be set.

A sweet national monument! The main trails aren't too long, with much of the cliff dwellings and petroglyphs within a mile of the visitors center. The views are stunning from the Tyuonyi Overlook trail. The entrance fee is $25 which why I suggest buying an annual pass. I visited in the winter when the crowds were sparse. It's in a remote location, so I suggest packing a lunch.

This place is great for hiking and taking pics. I would recommend visiting in the winter, as that's when weather is most pleasant. No matter the season, remember to bring water. It's a bit of a drive to get there from the city, but definitely worth it. If you like the South Mountains, you'll love this place.

A little off the beaten path, but Black Canyon of the Gunnison is a true gem! They do have open-air campgrounds (I prefer primitive camping) and a few developed campsites.

The trails offer some breathtaking views! If you're down for hiking, be sure to pack water and snacks. You're far away from any vendor.

We had a great time visiting this old mission in San Antonio. If you're in town, it's a must-visit along with the other missions in the city. It's a beautiful building with lots of history. It's a shame we don't make churches like this one anymore. The grounds were a nice place to walk around and enjoy.

NM-434 is one of the most underrated scenic routes in this state. It runs along the creek in a lush green area with rolling hills and forests. This park is located in a remote area, and it's a pleasant, tranquil place and well-maintained. Definitely a great spot to stop, relax and enjoy the ambiance.

It's a pain to find parking close by, but this river walk is a fascinating place. It's great for jogging or even just walking around and absorbing the atmosphere of this city. Lots of neat historical sites nearby, as well as shops and restaurants. It's a must-visit if you're ever in San Antonio.

200+ year old Catholic Church that reflects New Mexico's Spanish heritage. The Taos River Valley is the epicenter of colonial Spanish culture, which is why it has such fascinating architecture and history. Definitely worth checking out if you like historical stuff. Or you're going to mass.

Totally worth the drive to see this place! The Petrified National Forest can be enjoyed in one day! Lots of logs to perch upon for photo-taking. Also, the painted desert is a site to behold. If you're headed towards the Grand Canyon from the east on I-40, definitely stop here on your way.

Always worth the trip: Lake Powell, the Glen Canyon Dam, and Horseshoe Bend are here. Plus there's numerous trails, scenic points to visit in and around the area, such as Antelope Canyon and the Vermilion Cliffs. I wish I could give this place a sixth star: it's amazing!

What a beautiful park! Great place to enjoy the stillness of nature and these lovely sand dunes. It's fun to climb, slide down, and take pics. It's far enough off the beaten path that it doesn't attract too many tourists.

Utah's least-visited national park is nonetheless one of the finest in the country. Stunning red rock formations and trails to explore. It's worth a whole day to visit, at least. The drive to there is impressive as well.

As far as catwalks go, this one is by far the best! It's a fun outing for the whole family complete with great views, running water, and waterfalls. You will have to get wet to see some of the cool stuff.
It's a beautiful little hike through the woods and around a lake. It ends at the beach with some great views of the cliffs and seashells. One word of warning though: it gets muddy after the rain!
Great place to walk around and soak up the ambiance on a summer evening. I would give in five stars, but while walking along the greenery, I narrowly avoided getting bit by a snake. Be safe!
Nice little oasis of green amidst the urban sprawl. This is where my wife and I took our engagement pics. It's beautiful in the summer and in the fall. Nice place to walk around and relax.
This is a nice little hike! It offers a great view of the Los Lunas community and has some impressive volcanic rocks. My one gripe is that the trail isn't as clearly marked as it could be.
So many classic Western films have been filmed here! It's a must-see if you're visiting the Four Corners area. It's owned by the Navajo Nation, not NPS, so your park pass is no good here.
Great trail! It offers terrific views. I wish it had more parking spaces and a more clearly marked trail. Still, climbing up the trail was a great workout.
This place is unique. It's unlike any other monument: it's a canyon with a little farm at the bottom. Lots of lookouts and places to take pics.
A nice little space museum. One of Alamogordo's greatest attractions. Lots of interesting displays. I had a great time visiting it.
Such a fun trail! So many paths to walk around and it offers a fantastic view of the city from the top of the mountain.
Definitely worth visiting, even if you're not a Roman Catholic. I just like old churches and this one is awesome.

Oh my, can't begin to describe the landscape and the loop trail was incredible (unless you are not light of foot or if you're scared of heights). Get there early as the crowds form quickly and the temperature rises even faster)! Must be experienced to do the primative trail and know how to follow Cairns, bring lots of water. Suggestion for other hikers, be aware of others, not everyone wants you in their photographs, take yours and move along.

A nice relief from the sun in the late afternoon.  Mostly a paved road with a lot of bikers i wish they would maintain the creek path as an alternative for walkers. There are trails around on both sides but no postings of what they are, how long they are or where they go (pet peeve) & didn't coordinate with their map (or on Google maps). Oh well it wasn't that crowded, bugs got bad at dusk.

Best camping tradition ever - however the new rangers need to learn to be ambassadors instead of police.

2020 brought more restrictions and Shane on those using the park that weren't wearing masks (as posted) in the restrooms - you are the ones that will get the park closed down for all of us. Be respectful and follow the rules or go somewhere else.

A beautiful refuge from the city, nice walking trails (too bad one loop was closed due to flooding) and not allot of traffic nose once you're away from the road loop. Highly recommended for those selling to escape the rest traveling for a few hours.
My only critique would be that they had these numbered sign post throughout but no reference guide.
dislikes: Lack of reference guide for sign posts

reviews_attraction.text: Not sure how to rate it, great when we got there and had the place mostly to ourselves but later more and more people showed up and not everyone understood the their dogs had to be on leash as it's a state park. The trails are nice but need a little better signing but they did their job and we wore the kids out!

Wow, definitely worth a visit, a nice still through a huge and varied garden. I missed the Camellia bloom by about a week or two (a few still hung on). Nice signage and variety from jungle to desert but my favorite by far was the vegetable and butterfly gardens. One of my favorite stops in Orlando!

Always a great spot to walk, especially in winter when it's practically vacant. Not sure I should even mention it but on the far side of the park there's a Levy path that takes you to a nice forest path for about two miles (either end can connect you back to the road).

Short walk through a natural area and connects to other parks with Urban street walks. Some interesting art and historic house on an old Apple orchard site. Too bad some dog owners can't read and walk through the nature area meant for birds and other wildlife.

Haven't been here in a few years and they've really done an excellent job expanding the gardens and trail system thru the park. I took my cousin for her first trip and she's hooked. Beauty, diversity, art and (at least today) not a lot of people.

Good place to meander and contemplate, great for kids. Almost everyone wearing masks and being respectful. Short hike, we did it the times, looks like most of the offshoots are closed so it was hard to see the swans but not too muddy. 3-21-21

Kind of wide open and exposed. Plenty of up and down with benched areas to rest at internals. No facilities and the day I was there a school group of kids came thru on bicycles. Surrounding views of the neighborhood and some territorial.

Quiet, tranquil, great scenery and people out enjoying it. They've done a good job improving the trails and specialized gardens, just dad you can't wander inside the redwood tree circle anymore but at least they're being protected.
dislikes: Restricted access to redwood tree circle

reviews_attraction.text: Absolutely worth it, nice views but you have to work for them. Be in shape, wear the right shoes, bring lots of water and a protein snack. Not recommended for those afraid of heights or not part mountain goat

Hidden gem close to the city but a great place to escape from civilization. The raging creek eliminates the highway noise and stunning bridal veil falls is a walk away. People are nice but no showers.
Just a loose gravely road straight up hill but the views are amazing. Bring water but please leave your music private. Love the cows along the way, quite a few birds too and ground squirrels galore.
A bit hidden in a neighborhood but found by quite a few tourists (like me). Not for those with aversions to heights as it stands a ravine week below (wish there was a hike they it).
Amazing! Wide open views of incredible landscapes, take some of the hikes, there are short ones but well worth the time. Not to many people here, at least not early on the morning.
Lots of trails but the main ones are gravel roads. View of fields, interesting trees and water with a Pier that extends out at the tip giving extraordinary views.
My favorite stop today on the coast, small but sparsely occupied,a great vantage point and area to read a book or write poetry -saw some dolphins too!
A great place to give around outdoors while learning of the unique volcanic history of the place. Wild and scenic views so close to the city!
Shh, don't tell anyone about this hidden gem in the Bellevue parks department, lots of trails around the fields and a great kids area.
Sunshine, miss and beauty galore at the Hoh rainforest - everyone should visit at least once in their lives, it's breathtaking
Nice new addition to the waterfront, can't wait for them all to connect. Could use some mileage markers on their signage.
Wonderful walk on the beach (& plenty of beaches to choose from). Can't imagine the chairs in summer, this was perfect!
Not sure what to say, came all this way and it was cool, rainy and apparently too windy for the wheel.

The Science Center is just as wonderful and I remember it from years ago. My 2 & 3 year-olds enjoyed the large dinosaurs and absolutely loved the Discovery Room. My only complaint would be that it cost $5/person (which is fine), but the Discovery Room sessions only last 45 min. Wish it were a bit longer. My kids really enjoyed a movie about elephants they saw last year with their grandparents. Can't wait to see a movie at the Omnimax soon. I would suggest parking on the street or at the Planetarium to avoid parking fees.

Beautiful church with an exceptional choir!! We felt very safe going to Mass here during the pandemic. They have a wonderful process--check in when you arrive, hand sanitizer upon entry, different sections of the pews blocked off to ensure social distancing and communion is served to you in the pew. The windows were open and fans were on to help with air circulation. I recommend visiting this church!!
likes: Facilities & Services: Safety measures, social distancing, air circulation

reviews_attraction.text: I could've spent an entire day here, but I only had two hours. The staff were very helpful and knowledgeable. The survivor stories at the end were very interesting, but I didn't have enough time to read many of them. This museum holds your interest with the many true-to-size exhibits. The entrance fee was very reasonable with the Groupon I purchased. I loved every minute!

Great trail with good views. Can only imagine what the view up at the top would look like on a clear day. It was rainy so it was a difficult descent. Lots of sliding on wet, slippery rocks and hoping we didn't fall. Wear shoes that you don't care about because the weather at the bottom doesn't reflect the weather closer to the top.

This place was amazing! Great course with plenty of obstructions and great scenery. My 3yo daughter and 4yo son loved it! Lots of dinosaurs, a volcano and caves. So many photo ops. What more could you want?! We even had a coupon for $1 off per person. Prices are very reasonable otherwise. Awesome mini golf experience!!

This is one of the best parks! Not only does it still have buildings and areas of the park that were present at the time of the 1904 World's Fair, but it has become one of the most beautiful places in STL area to take pictures, picnic, or exercise. The Boat House, Art Museum, Zoo, Muny--and so much more!

Awesome spot to see some Honu (Hawaiian green sea turtles) and huge waves! Only complaint is the homeless congregation taking over the picnic areas (that are supposed to be blocked off due to Covid) and burning trash and tons of large pieces of wood in the BBQ grills (produced so much smoke!).

Wonderful short side-hike to waterfalls on Road to Hana. Can be muddy so bring shoes you don't care about. Be sure to buy a coconut from the small food truck at the entrance and leave a tip. It was delicious and the money goes toward the portapotties and general upkeep of the property.

Loved this state park. Only complaint is the state should really take care of these beautiful spaces and keep up with the bathrooms so we don't need to use porta-potties. Other than that, beautiful scenery. Short walk up to see the needle. I would love to return when it's a clear day.

Awesome national park!! We entered on Road to Hana to access the Pipiwai Trail (best hike to see amazing waterfalls and bamboo forests). Another day we entered as we drove up to see the summit of the dormant volcano (get there early before the clouds roll in and obstruct the views).

Challenging 3.5-hr hike with great views!! Try to go on a cloudy day as there is absolutely NO shade. Bring lots of water. Expect to maneuver over navigate through rocks during ascent and descent. So surprised we didn't roll our ankles on the way down. Thankfully the trail was dry.

I hadn't been to Grant's Farm since I was a child. My parents and I took my 1-yr-old and 2-yr-old this year and they loved it. We will definitely be back next year. Wish the park was open more weekdays than only Friday in the fall, but I understand as most kids are back in school.

This is a wonderful park, though it is very busy. It's sort of difficult to capture family photos here as there always seems to be people in the background. This park has a pond, a waterfall, walking trail and a gazebo. Overall, this is a beautiful park for photos around sunset.

Great beach for a small child to play in the sand. Alcohol is not allowed on the beach so that's no fun. Too many people chain-smoking cigarettes on the beach and in the water. Found cigarette butts all over the sand. Maybe cigarettes should be banned on the beach as well.

Not only did my parents meet while working working here, but my husband and I had our wedding pictures taken on the Arch grounds. It is a beautiful park. I can't wait until the entire renovation is complete so we can bring our two young kids to experience the Arch.

I found this park hidden within a neighborhood. It's close to my house and the playground is perfect for my running/climbing 1-year-old and 2-year-old. Our new favorite place to go--can't wait to go more often again in the spring.

Very beautiful chapel! It was busy on a sunny Sunday so we had to park down the street and walk up hill to get to it, but totally worth it! Great views from outside and a very short line to make a donation and light a candle.
Beautiful area with trails on the waterfront. Highly recommend taking a stroll around this area before enjoying a delicious lunch at Barrio Queen followed by some shopping in Old Town Scottsdale.
This park is wonderful! Large enough playground area with an older child area and a smaller child area. Plenty of room to run and lots of climbing structures. The splash pad is an added bonus!
I've really enjoyed this park. It has a large walking trail around a pond, a big playground, nice shade, picnic tables and a bridge. It's a beautiful spot to take photographs!!
Beautiful place! Need reservations before you arrive due to Covid. Spent an hour in the butterfly greenhouse. Could've bought everything in the gift shop. We will be back!
Very beautiful spot. Can't wait to return next year when we descend all the way to the bottom of the Grand Canyon to begin our 4-day lower canyon adventure.
One of my favorite places in Maui!! Such a beautiful beachwalk with lava rock, gorgeous beaches, different plants and crashing waves. Highly recommend!!!
This is definitely one of the best zoos in the country. And it's free!! My parents and I take my kids at least three or four times a year.
Beautiful park on the riverfront. There is a train, an old train station and a pavillion. Great place to take pictures.

This place was too crowded in the morning when we first tried to go, so we returned in the late afternoon, approximately 4pm.  Didn't have much time though and when they say they close at 5pm, they close at 5pm - GET OUT.  Just Kidding, they were not that rude, but they did tell us the gate was closing and they wanted to go home.  The Chapel is worth a stop and say a prayer while you are there, try a Hail Mary, as it is a Catholic Chapel and open to all.  The gift shop is nice, small and downstairs and is not Handicap Accessible.  Parking is mainly at the bottom of the hill with some on the hill.  They only have about 5 HC parking spots at the top.  They do have Golf Cart Shuttles to take people up and down the hill.  I was very surprised to see it so crowded when we went around 1100 am.
likes: Facilities & Services: Gift shop, Golf Cart Shuttles
dislikes: Facilities & Services: Limited handicap accessibility, Few HC parking spots

reviews_attraction.text: This museum is huge, with plenty of exhibits and history, I do however question the statement made at the very beginning of the history exhibit.  Slavery has been around far longer than the 1400's and was always been a commodity.  Cheap labor was needed to make wealth, Egyptians, Persians, Chinese, Greeks, etc... had forced slavery.  And it also fails to mention that many of the African slaves were sold by their own people kust to remove them and male wealth for their own rulers.  But even with that missing, the museum is,still worth visiting.

We really enjoyed this place.  The whole MOSH is worth a visit but our favorite exhibits were the Planetarium, History of Jax, and Jax Fire Dept exhibt.
We really enjoyed the Night Sky Over Jacksonville show at the Planetarium, well worth the extra $5 pp.  We must have spent 2.5 hours looking through the History of Jax exhibit, everything from the Timucua Indians to the 14th & 15th British Colonies, the NAS Jax.  Well worth a trip for history buffs.  The JFD exhibit was a must for me, but then again I'm bias.

This is a beautiful museum, it is a private museum so there is a charge but we found it very well worth the $20 pp to enter.  The electronic guide, which is complimentary, we didn't enjoy so much, the verbal explanations of the museum items were very short and not very descriptive.  We spent 3 hours in this museum and did not get to see the entire museum, only 3 floors.  They also have a restaurant on the 6th floor with inside and outside seating.  We will definitely return in the future.

This is a good place to start.  The museum was good and the staff was extremely polite and helpful.

The 2 videos are not that interesting.  They give very little information about the Anasazi or Pueblo Indians or their culture.  It's really more of a Politically Correct BS video about not taking any artifacts,  which you shouldn't do anyhow.

The museum is worth spending some time in.   The exhibits show the different eras of the people who inhabited the area.
dislikes: Lack of cultural information in videos

reviews_attraction.text: Well worth a stop, the museum is Handicap Accessible, they have a video to watch, interviews with people who recorded and worked here.  The memorabilia is worth a look at.  We found it worth the time and money, and we didn't know some of those oldies we like so much were recorded in Clovis, NM.  We wish we could attend their next Clovis Music Fest in June 2109 but we won't be in the area.

We have enjoyed coming  to the Castillo for years. The history is so vivid.  The Park Rangers there are very helpful.  We met the Ranger who helped start the Bark Ranger program in Fort Caroline, up in Jacksonville.  The fort is not handicap accessible.  For those in a chair, they do not have a ramp or elevator to take you to the top, but you can go in the rooms on the ground floor.

This place IS NOT HC Accessible.  The view is beautiful and they do have a video feed of the Sea Lion Cave in the gift shop but they have 37 steps to get down to the ramp to go down to the cave.  It is a nice spot, RV parking is available, but disabled people who cannot do that many steps/stairs cannot go see the Sea Lions.

The visitors center is ok but not worth the hassle of going through the airport like security, including removing your belt.  Going through with a disabled person and all the things we have to carry was too much of a pain to make the museum worth the hassle, been there, done that, it's time to move on.

Loved this place, filled with history and the Ranger was helpful and seemed really excited to be there taking care of history.  The trail is handicap accessible.  We could not go in the Kiva but it was still worth walking around and reading the information.

Good place to visit.  They have a campground and you can go tubing down the rivers.  Most of the area is HC accessible.  We glad we went but it is. Nothing like the Headwaters of the Mississippi River in Itasca State Park Minnesota.

Neat place to visit. there is a sign, and a camera pedestal.  There is a line painted on the road to shoe you where the midway point of RTE 66 is.  The Cafe is a great place to eat, HUGE burgers, friendly, also has a gift shop.

We were in the area for 3 days, rained 2 of the 3 days.  We didn't enjoy it mich but that doesn't mean you won't.  Not much for the HC to do.  Few HC Accessible trails.  Been there, done that, won't both coming back.

Beautiful place.  Love the view.  It is NOT HCA but the do have a portable ramp the staff will bring out and set up so wheelchairs can go inside.  The staff was excellent and took very good care of my wife.
Visiting Washington DC is one destination every American should strive to visit.  Leave your politics at home, visit this city no matter who is President, there is so much to see and learn.
Nice place, we didn't stay very long, just there to check it out, but we will be back with our RV.  They have restricted requirements to stay, it not open to the public.
Neat place to visit, spend some time in the museum, its not vert large and you can go through it in about 20 min then go outside and take all the Dam Pictures you want.
The people who work here are very nice.  They seem to go out of their way to make my wife happy.  Thx y'all do a great job and the park is definitely worth a visit.

The entire plantion is a very interesting place.  History for you to view.  We enjoyed the Presidential Tour Package.

Well worth the trip and the money.
This is a neat place to visit, we went during the day, did some shopping, ate, took a few pictures.  Plenty of panhandlers.  Very interesting history.
We had a nice visit.  The Tower is well worth the minimal cost to go into.  The exhibits are good.  The observation deck has a very good view.

The drive through the park has some spectacular views of the Moncos Valley below.

The Sprucetree Cliff Dwelling is a very intersting site.
The Redwoods are huge.  In much of the NP & SP you feel like you're on the planet Endor waiting for an Ewok to walk by.
Interesting piece of American history, too bad the grass is too high and the signs could use a bit of help.
A good place to visit.  Full of history and a nice short handicap accessible trail to get to the fort.

For some reason, they "require" masks while outside but no one really enforces it if you aren't wearing one.  Other than that, this was a great place to visit.  While I have never been impressed with any botanical gardens, this one was a place I would probably go back to if it weren't so expensive.  For two adults and a 10 yr old, it cost us $75.  The cactuses were amazing to see but they really need to work on getting signs for more of them, very few were labeled, so you don't know what you are looking at other than a cactus.  Never knew there were so many different kinds of cacti!

Fairly easy hike, but busy.  The views at the top are amazing.

Manners are not used by many people here.

There are idiots running the trail that will plow right through groups of people.

Turn off your speakers, I don't want to hear your music while hiking in the woods.

Don't walk two wide and force others off the trail.

So as with most popular trails, humans ruin it.

Great place!  The staff was cheerful and eager to answer any and all questions.  Their wines are some of the best we have tried in the entire Yakima Valley!

The views are very nice from their location, you get a great view of Adams and pretty sure we would have been able to see Rainier if it wasn't clouded in the day we were there.

This is a place we will go back to!

Good hike, a bit tough if you aren't used to hiking.  There are two spots at the top where the wind surfers take off from.  Pretty cool to get up there and look out to see 10-12 parachutes gliding around the area.

Parking is a premium and with most trail heads, there isn't enough.  Locals have turned it into a business and open their land to people for a small fee.

Small park, but rather nice!  We were there on a Sunday, so we didn't have to pay the $10 day use fee which is the only draw back to this park.

Tucked back in a cove, so it is a little protected from the wind.  There is a nice little stream flowing through the park, nice sand and many picnic tables.

Decent place with an easy hike to the waterfalls.

BEWARE!  I noticed on our way home that someone had tried to break into my vehicle.  They had used something to slide in through the drivers side window in an attempt to pop the lock.  I only noticed because they had scratched up the window tinting.

The actual parking lot hold about 12 vehicles.   After that, you are parking along the road which means people are squeezing past when other vehicles are coming up.

The hike itself was pretty easy, but this trail is very close to Seattle so don't expect everyone to be nice or respectful.

Easy hike, but you can't get close to the actual cliff dwellings.  Luckily, there was a great park employee there that pointed us to Walnut Canyon which was about 45 minutes away where you actually get to walk through the dwellings.  Much better experience, just a much harder hike :D

The cable car rides were some of our favorite things we experienced in SF!

As with all the public transit we used there, the drivers were great about letting us know of other near by sites to check out.

Great park for the kids, pretty large play ground area.  There are clean restrooms on the location.  Great views of the lake as well as a good amount of open grassy areas to play with friends and family!

Great place to go for a short hike with a little one.  There are some stairs to get down to the cave on one end, but my 5 year old lived it enough, we had to go through the cave a second time that day!
Nice little beach you can access easily.  You can't walk very far north as we found out, they keep a military guard on the beach about a half mile north of the parking lot to turn people around.
If you are in Seattle, this is a must see.  However, the directions google map gives you will have you circling around it on the roads above it and driving back and forth across the bridge.

Small park with nothing to see or do but a few hundred meters of paved path.

The homeless issues need to be dealt with, sleeping on the benches in the middle of the day.

The flame was not burning, not sure if it normally does or if it has been out for a long time??

Some nice open grass areas to play with kids/pets.
Great trail, not difficult at all, and beautiful views everywhere you look.  And we went on a cloudy day, can't wait to go back on a clear day.

Nice place to toss out some crab pots!

First time crabbing for us.  Ended up with a great meal out of it from the fresh caught crab!
Pretty cool place from the 90's show.  They don't really look like the ones in the TV show though.  Guessing they have been painted.
Nice big park, but restrooms were not very good and a LONG way away.  If you have kids, you understand the need for close restrooms!
Nice park, lots to see and do in the area, but parking is a premium in the area which is the only reason I lowered the rating.
Beautiful place to hike, dog and kid friendly place.  Hikes can be a bit of a challenge if you are not in decent shape.
What kind of park does not allow dogs? Seriously, there is goose and duck feces everywhere, so it can't be about that!
Great site to see, the smell may be too much for some, but pretty cool seeing these animals up close and in the wild!
Nice beach where you can sit and enjoy watching the ferry traffic.  Not much parking, but that is pretty normal.
We camped here with our travel trailer.  Good hookups, but placed oddly close to the front of the camping sites.

Just camped here for the first time in 20+ years.  What a great spot.  More expensive than the federal campgrounds that are closer to the observatory, but worth it.  The group sites are a good size with a a reasonable amount of flat space.  I don't know why there are quite so many fire pits in GS#1, but it's a little fine.  The restrooms are very nice for a campground, the oak trees are amazing and there is hiking available all around you.

This is one of my favorite state parks.  As the largest state park in the country there are LOTS of things to see, from the popular campgrounds like Palm Canyon to the less visited outposts like wind caves, coyote canyon, pumpkin patch, fits point and many other locations.  Furthermore, this park still has established 4wd trails which makes for a fun time.

I have been here three or four times now.  Each time I've had a great experience.  They allow you to bring in food and drink to eat before the show; there are even picnic tables available on a first come-first served basis.  The show is always amazing, but remember to bring your binoculars!  You don't want to miss out on all the details!

Large granite cliffs, roaring river rapids, and tall majestic trees.  The vast majority of this place is unaccessible by car -- a way I wish more national parks were.  While the road side attractions and foot paths are utterly beautiful, to see the larger beauty it's necessary to commit yourself to a few days in the backcountry.

I enjoyed walking around the 260 million year old petrified wood forest but my kids didn't find it quite as amazing.  Although they really did enjoy checking out some of the logs and the beautiful colors throughout.  When we reached the painted desert at sunset, the reds of the cliffs popped against the purple sky.

What a great botanical garden!  They have a little bit of everything, tropical, desert, temperate, indoor, outdoor.... Some of their plants include a Cocoa tree, coffee tree, banana trees, papaya, orchids of all types, vanilla plant, cactus, herbs, palms, cycads, and sooooooo much more.

This is not a huge park but it is beautiful and diverse cactus garden with something for anyone who enjoy desert landscape.  The 8 mile, one-way loop road is great from the car but even more magnificent if you are willing to take some of the hikes easily accessible from the road.

My wife visited the museum with our three kids... They enjoyed it but even the kids said it wasn't worth the cost.  With so many free or low cost things to do, $22/ adult and $15/per kid is too much money.  Sure it was good for about 1-2 hours of fun... Too expensive.

One of the best parks in all of the desert.  Take your time to explore this wonderland.  There is much to see.  From Butler Dam to Skull Rock and 1,000 of climbing opportunities.  Who knows, keep your eyes open you might even see a desert tortoise perusing around.

Beautiful area and probably amazing when there is water flowing.  Quite the drive for such a short hike, but it is kid friendly.  Bring a grocery bag with you and help clean the place up, there is a LOT of litter along the trail and falls.

Cool spiderweb play structure for the kids along with other stuff.  Lots of picnic tables.  The ball field and basketball courts are under  rehabilitation/upgrade during our visit (4/6/19).  Lots of open space to play catch and run around.

We had a great three days at GBNP.  There is lots of hiking and some small fishing to do.  The caves were closed because of COVID, so I cannot comment on that.  Otherwise everything was great and the campgrounds were all beautiful.

Another little gem in the Joshua Tree area.  Stopped here with the family as we were cruising through the area, didn't even know this visitor center was here.  Has all the usual visitor center stuff plus a small garden outside.

Next to Mesa Verde, these are my favorite cliff dwellings.  Take the short hike down 1,000 steps and end up in the past imagining what life was like for the Native Americans that once lived on these steep bluffs.

San Jacinto is an amazing place as is Santa Rosa mountain, but the visitors center was okay.  The staff was very friendly and showed us their snake and we got to see wildlife in the center include a field mouse.
A large spacious park hidden in Escondido.  Facilities are kept in reasonably good condition.  There are lots of beautiful oak trees and plenty of space for group events. And beer/wine is allowed.
The docents are very knowledge and are happy to share information about the seals.  Be sure to ask questions.  I love that CA take the steps necessary to provide these safe habitats!
Everything in the Grand Canyon is amazing, even the visitors center.  Good luck finding parking!  Be sure to watch the video AND take the free shuttle to your next stop.
likes: Facilities & Services: Visitors center, Free shuttle

reviews_attraction.text: Great bit of Native American history.  We didn't get into the park until about 4:15 so we had a short visit but we were able to learn about the history from a decent.
We stopped here on our way through just for the views.  You're high above the valley with picturesque views all the way to the distant mountains.  Worth the stop.
Nice park with beautiful large trees, many of which the kids loved to climb.  There were, however, lots of homeless people sleeping in the shade...
Neat little park to walk around.  Kids liked exploring the old military artifacts and the peer.  The peer was bustling with people fishing.
A large amount of homeless, but otherwise a beautiful park.  Enjoyed a take out dinner before watching the summer pops series.
What a beautiful waterfront park with great views of downtown and wonderful trails to wonder on a sunny California afternoon.
I always love this place.  It's been a long time since I've car camped here, but backpacking is always a good time.

Go deep into the earth like you have never done before. If you a claustrophobic probably do not go. It is 1000 feet underground!
Billions of dollars of gold came out of these mines. Imagine working in almost total darkness to retrieve these riches. You can experience this on this tour, well maybe not the gold.

Spectacular scenery with no crowds. The rock formations are outstanding. Vertical spires and dramatic cliffs. Bring water as it can be very dry and hot. Hike into the cave. It is really just the overlapping of huge rock slabs with a small entry. Your cell phone will do for a flashlight.

This is it. High atop the Rockies you almost need oxygen. Stunning location. Nice gift shop with food. The road to get here is an alpine experience. Views of the Rockies in all directions. Stop here and stretch your legs or maybe take the Alpine ridge trail. Outstanding.

This park is big. Hard to cover in a review when a book is more appropriate. The mountains are Spectacular. The wildlife is unparalleled.
Trees everywhere. It is hard to convey the grand scale of this park. But I am sure that on your first visit you will be in awe.

Great visitors center. Dramatic views of the Pacfic Ocean and the cliffs. Excellent exhibits. Note there is so current access to the ocean. As I stopped along the coast all access was blocked. I am sure it is for our own safety but makes it kind of like Disneyland.

This is the pinnacle of the California Missions. Located walking distance to the Pacific Ocean in beautiful Carmel. Founded by Fr. Junipero Serra in 1770. The Mission has been restored and Mass is celebrated on Sundays. A must see on your Highway One journey.

A very local museum. Cripple creek is such a unique gold rush town. Mining was its life blood. The exhibits highlight that heritage with some local dinosaurs thrown in for good measure. A worth while stop on your travels visiting Cripple Creek.

These falls tower over the valley below. I was there when the snow melt was driving the falls full on. There was still snow on the sheer rock faces and ice from the spray. Very dramatic scene. I took photographs from across the valley floor.

Take the time to get off Highway One (yes it is beautiful). Drive under the bridge and park. Take a hike and see all of this beautiful area. The bridge and ocean are outstanding in this area. Catch the sunset here and it is very dramatic.

This is the place to stop and see Bixby bridge. Certainly one of the most photographed bridges on Highway One. Worth the effort to come here at sunset or late afternoon as the sky can light up giving dramatic senic views. A must do stop.

This is a treasure. Beautiful gardens. Trees flowers. Cactus. I joined the Botanic gardens and became a member. The gardens are extensive and I cannot imagine seeing them all in one day. Take your time and give your sense s a thrill.

Cool small park. Much to be done here. There is a Basketball court. A great children's play ground. A Little League field. The Lagoon with all its birds flying in and out. Picnic tables. Swings. Fun for all with a beautiful setting.

Take a trip to the top. History comes alive on every Trip. The cars are historic original s. The views are dramatic of Los Angeles new skyline. It is one dollar up and one dollar fown. City cents with your tap card. Enjoy your trip

After seeing all the news about the great bloom I went to this reserve. We had to park about 1 mile from the entrance. Then the hike to the poppies. The show was OK but I would attempt to go mid week.
If you love gardens this is the place. The rose gardens are spectacular. This is a very large tract of gardens with small lakes and different growing areas. Take your time there is much to see.
Outstanding botanical gardens. Start early, then have lunch. Continue to tour this outstanding natural reserve. Highly recommend. Many benches to stop and enjoy the beauty of nature.
Great place for a walk. Lots of places to eat. Great views of boats at the docks. Walk over to the Pier and see the Beautiful Pacific Ocean. Always fresh air and something to see.
This is one of the best Newport Beach locations. The Wedge is one of the primer surfing spots on the right day. We saw Geriboldies on the South side of the jetty. What day.
Beautifully designed and beautifully kept. This garden is an outstandingly styled section in the spectacular overall gardens. Make sure that you have time to visit.
California history comes to life. A beautiful must see. The grounds are outstanding. Many historical displays to see how the original Mission was run.
A Pasadena treasure. Outstanding art. Beautiful grounds. Take the time to watch the movie on Norton Simon. History of the man and museum.
This is a beautiful bridge and rock beach.  Take the time to visit this area as it offers many different views of the bridge.
This is a local place to come visit. Come stop for a look. Not a big deal but it is a local spot to come and enjoy.
Fabulous views of the Santa Monica mountains and the valley. The Nike base brings back thoughts of the cold war.
Fantastic views of the canyon. Walk along the rim trail and enjoy the beauty. Come early for the best light.

The contemporary art removes 3 stars.  I'm sorry to admit that a white canvas held to the wall by 4 metal bolts just kind of leaves me cold.  The all blue canvas held to the wall by dog knows what in the next room is not much of a step up. Worse...can it get worse....large canvases titled House Paint with Pencil scribble is hardly good art.  And the Rothko reminds me of Judd and Flavin nonsense of Marfa. Is lack of  talent now a prerequisite for official art collectors.  I don't know.  I don't get it.  And no photography?  Really?  All museums now allow it.  But maybe in this case, I can see why! The end of art as we know it?  I hope so.

What a place to visit, especially in the morning or just before sunset.  Surrounded by and largely built of Triassic age red stone of the  Moenkopi formation, Wukoki was apparently housing for 3 or 4 families of puebloen peoples.  Quite a place to live!  Look at the stone it sits on and see the fossil ripples of sand dunes laid down millions of years ago.  Open sunset to sunrise.

Well, come on folks.  A world class location deserves a world-class review.  So take this for one.  Used to be Americans and a few foreign visitors.  But now the world has come.  Can it get anymore crowded?  Heck yeah.  So you better go while you can.  But drink it in.  It's world-class.  Oh, and be sure to see Moran's watercolor version of the grandest canyon in the world.

The black mailbox just stood there and did nothing.  Wouldn't answer any of our questions.  Just acted as if it was a mailbox.  Which, of course, we all know is nonsense.  But that night while camping nearby strange orange lights lit up the sky over Area 51.  Awesome light show.  Black mailbox had no comment next morning.  He's somewhat of a snob, I fear.

A visitor center with friendly staff and some very expensive trade goods.  Learn about the local history.  They say this is the best place to get pottery and woven goods.  Get them from the source....honestly, I wouldn't know.  Plenty of people do.  If you are one, then have at it.

Some history from bygone Puebloan days.  This is the largest of several National Monuments in this same area of New Mexico. A trail to the top of the hill leads to partially restored outline of how the people lived.  Visitor center has good displays.

This is indeed a great view of an shrinking lake.  Down to 50% capacity.  We may yet get our beloved Colorado river back.  Meanwhile, it is an amazing view.  Bless the presidents who set aside most of this land as National Monuments.

A primo Anazazi partially restored great house.  Walk thru 700 yr old history.  Great visitor center museum and very helpful knowledgeable staff.  Nice gift shop. Spend some time here.  See what was here before Columbus arrived.

It's dinosaurs and tracks.  We all love that.   Down an all summer road.  Tracks beside the parking area.  Short walk.  If the sun is right overhead it can be hard to pick out the tracks. But once you do it become more obvious.
dislikes: Visibility of tracks in direct sunlight

reviews_attraction.text: If you are fit, take one of the morning hikes to Betatakin House.  Almost original never restored cliff house.  But its a 3 mile hike with a 1000 ft drop and then hike back out.  But the trail alone is stunning.
Camping is limited.  First come first serve.  But great hiking for the fit.  Cool geology in that it is almost entirely a permian coral reef. Go to visitor center first.  Carlsbad caverns nearby too.
Birds great.  But no drinking water at HQ.  Really?  It is a Western tradition to have drinking water at refuges, and parks in the West. It always has been and always should be. Shame on Bosque!
Nice tiny county park with good access to the water of Lake Travis.  Long and winding road to get to.  No boat dock.  Small parking lot for 20 cars or so? Swimming area.  Closed at dusk.
Always an excellent museum.  Small with a main room for revolving show.  But the three times we've been there, it has been grade A art.  Free admission.  Small gift shop. Friendly desk.
Really nice stop.  Waterlilies just begin to bloom in mid April and continue all summer when it becomes a riot of leaves and flowers. Free to visit.  Close parking on street. Enjoy.
Great park as envisioned by native tribes and  created by Obama, thanks!   Just so many places to explore and discover.  Go, prepare and be safe.
Great wildlife refuge.  Can be see from it's entrance road and also from one of the whooping crane sightseeing tours.  Highly recommended too.
Nice museum.  Lot of local history and usually some good art too.  Not a huge museum but lots of parking and easy access.  Worth it.
Great park, of course.  Be sure to  pay a visit to the Larry Monroe bridge while you are there and contemplate and well led life.
One of three such ruins in the area.  All are free.  And all somewhat restored to get and idea of a little that was once here.
Wow. Great art and big beautiful museum building in interesting downtown Tucson. Will come back here whenever I'm in Tucson.
This place is in all the textbooks.  Sometimes its even the front cover of textbooks.  Go see it.  The view is worth it.
Ok, but the original river was better. Come to think about it....with the lake so low, it almost is the original river!
Excellent museum of Anaszi history!  The mugs alone that they made 700 yrs ago are more beautiful than anything today.
We often camp here when passing through. 5 bucks to camp.  5 or 6 shelters.  Plus a toilette.  Lot of sand!

Nice trail, definitely take it as far as the Geyser overlook as it gives you a great view and different perspective looking down on it.  Going the rest of the way to the Falls is a fairly flat hike, with a decent Falls, but water flow was somewhat limited when I visited in June 2018.

Nice park with a few good trails.  I started my hike at the visitor center,  then up the 900 feet of Firetower trail (just a gravel road), cut over on the Mudlick trail near the Firetower, then returned on the Shut-ins trail (about 5.25 miles).

Nice little park, but the facilities were still closed when I arrived.  It lost a star since the road in and out was rough gravel.  Hiked several of the teails which were in good condition, but wish I have better views of the current river

A great waterfall, love how it disappeared into a sinkhole.  Both times I have hiked here, it was worth as the water was flowing and I had ut to mysrlf or just a few other people (get an early start)   Campsites are right by the falls.

Great park with nice trails for running.  Bathrooms are open year round which is nice as well.  Also, in the upper portion of the park is a nice unpaved hiking trail which is fairly new and worth checking out.

Nice place to meet friends when visiting the park.  Have an option toget something to eat.  Most importantly,  the restrooms are clean so it makes a great starting and ending point when running the park.
I have hiked the trails several times,  a nice combination of distances with nice overlooks.  Also, a senic drive with some overlooks.  Restaurant is just OK, but worth checking out.
Two short trails for a total of 1.5 miles (easy to follow and not too rugged)  The one water fall would be nice with a little more water flow than when I visited.
Note, the overlook is not of the Falls, but the river and its a little ways away from the parking area.  The Falls are really cool, but the overlook is just so-so
Dirt road getting there, but the last 1/2 mile of the hike is spectacular.   So worth the journey and plenty of places to site and enjoy the sites
Great views of the valley and Yosemite Falls.  Be sure to have enough water as it's a decent elevation gain with plenty of sun in the afternoon.
Very nice area to take a short hike along the Shut-ins.  I was the only person there so good to avoid the crowds.  Paved path to the river.
Less busy than the Gatlinburg side, nice little historic village behind it.  If passing nearby, keep a lookout for the Elk in the area
Very impressed with the park, related facili6and trail around the falls.  Definitely happy I stopped during my ride up to Canada.
Great trails, decent lookouts, and clean bathrooms.  Very few people there.  Only negative,  lots of bugs so bring your bug juice
A great park for a hike.  Just enough elevation change to make it scenic.  Nice trails for hiking and a cool little Canyon area.
A really nice park, it had a nice 2.3 mile paved loop trail with numerous exercise stops.  Plus an overlook of the Mississippi.
Short, but steep trail of you are able to park at the rock (I arrived before 7 AM and had no issues).  Great views at the top.
A few nice trails and a cave that was closed.  Worth a visit if you are in Clarksville,  but no reason to make a special trip.
A really nice park with nice facilities.   I hiked the Jacks Loop trail and Cattle Ridge for a toral of 5 miles, trail was OK
Very cool historic village, I will definitely return when I have a little more time.  Glad I stopped in on this fall day.
Noce city park along the Greenway, plenty of benches to sit and contemplate things.  Caves might be interesting if open
Cool place to stop on your to/from the Grand Canyon.  Nice trail amongst the Lava rock as well as a short paved trail.
Not a large area, but a really nice Natural Arch, definitely worthwhile to check out, if you are evwr in the area
Stopped while passing through as it was a great place for a hike with a few nice waterfalls and great views.

Excellent Trail. Well-marked. Easy to moderate. There is a View Overlook along this trail which is a highlight so make sure you check it out. Watch for the sign. There is free parking on both the west and east entrances. There are no restrooms here however there is a porta potty closer to the east entrance. There are areas in the sanctuary which you are not allowed to go into so please respect that. Watch for the signs. There is also a lot of horse dung all along the trail so be careful. Overall good experience definitely recommend.

Very good museum. Not all exhibits were interesting to me. However, one that did stand out was the Hall of Biodiversity where they have an excellent collection of mounted bird species. One of the best. Hall of History was also very good. I especially liked how informative that exhibit was in detailing the history of San Bernardino and surrounding area. Who would of thought the city of San Bernardino was founded by Mormons! Anyways, the admission price was fair and there are even some discounts available.

Very fun. Tram Floor rotates 360 degrees while ascending and descending. The view is amazing. There is a much to do once at the top. There are restaurants, a gift shop, 2 theaters (small), visitor center,  many hiking trails, and much more. It is a little chilly. So bring a jacket especially if you are taking the first tram @ 8 am. Use your AAA membership to get a small discount off the regular price. The only negative i have is the $5 charge for parking.
likes: On-site amenities (restaurants, gift shop, theaters, visitor center)

reviews_attraction.text: Great hike up to the falls. A little steep so be prepared. The falls are impressive for one that is so close to an urban area but don't expect too much. It is so sad to see grafetti on the rocks and trash in some places. Please pick up after yourself when you visit. This area needs to be respected by all who visit. Also, if you have time after the falls visit panoramic viewing area. Excellent views of the mountains in the distance and cities below.

Fascinating place! Wow. I wish i had more time to visit but i was only passing through and had to be somewhere else. But i am glad i stopped even if it was only briefly. The "fort" aka Winsor Castle is mind blowing. I recommend watching the documentary inside the visitor center before touring the historical grounds. It will provide you some background information that is helpful. If you love history this is right up your alley.

Pretty awesome view of the red sandstone cliffs. Initially, did not know this was part of Zion National Park but it is. Don't forget to stop at the visitor center to pay your fee or show your pass. I would recommend driving on this scenic route and coming to the view point at the end of your day after visiting the main part of Zion National Park.

This place is incredible. The Ingenuity of the people that lived in the cliff dwellings is remarkable. I really enjoyed this place. It definitely needs to be on your to do list if you're in the area. The rim trail is okay but I highly recommend the island trail if stairs don't bother you. Otherwise stick with the rim trail which is short and flat

One of the toughest hikes that I have been on. But once at the top you're greeted to one of the best views in the park. I break up the trail in four different parts from Weeping Rock Trailhead: switchbacks, level, more elevation gain, and finally level again then you're there. My advice, start early and take your time

Visited this wonderful museum earlier this month. Truly amazing experience. I really liked the extensive gem and mineral collection, Hall of Birds, and City of LA exhibits. I spent at least 3 hours here. So allow plenty of time. If you are visiting LA, this museum should be one of your destinations.

I absolutely loved this spot. Very scenic and great for photos. But what really annoyed me was other people who stayed in the middle of the road for longer than they should have. What i really wanted to say to them, "What's the hold up? Take your pic and get off the road already! My goodness."

Tough but good hike. There is a point during the hike, maybe half way, where its very narrow, steep, and only room for one way traffic. Be careful. Other than that the views going up are amazing and so is the top. Get to the trailhead parking lot early because it fills up very quickly.

Great place to learn about the event that set off a ripple effect which would be heard worldwide. My only suggestion is there are buildings on the grounds which are not marked so its hard to tell if its a maintenance building or building of  historical importance.

Not bad of a hike. There's plenty of markings to indicate where to go. On a clear day you can see downtown San Diego and the ocean. I think this would serve as a good practice hike for the bigger and longer ones. And please, if you bring a dog clean up after them.

What an awesome place! I got to explore Coronado Cave and i was the only one in the cave! Don't recommend that but do explore the cave with someone. Also, go up Montezuma Pass to the overlook. Spectacular views! So glad i came. A true Arizona gem!

I really liked this hike. It is tough though. Very steep. I even had the opportunity to have my first encounter with a bear! No joke. I was really excited and a little scared but the bear didn't seem aggressive. Be prepared.

Short and easy hike. You may still need to bring water so don't leave without it. They have several toadstools at the end of the trail. Really neat. If you are just passing through like i was this is a hike for you.
This Arch was both stunning and amazing to see. And it's not even in a National Park! You cannot pass this Arch without stopping and seeing it up close. Just be careful on the hike up there.
Great viewing spot. What I also liked about this place is the information displays regarding the history of Emerald Bay and Fannette Island. There are restrooms here in case you need to go.
Wow! This place is amazing! This is the closest you are going to get to what is at Yellowstone. Route here is relatively short from the highway and is made up of a paved and unpaved road.
Nice hike. This is a popular hike so get to the parking lot early. There are variations in the elevation so be prepared for that. Bring plenty of water. Have fun
Wow! What a place. If you want to go somewhere where it feels like you are on a different planet come to this place. It is out of this world!
Good spot for an overlook. There are also other nearby overlook points around the area. This is one of the best and has a nice shaded spot
If you are driving on this road do not miss out on this overlook. The sight that you will see once you look out it's simply breathtaking!
Wow. What a site! The native americans who built this place definitely had ingenuity and resilience. This place is worth checking out.
Great place to ride a bike, go for a walk, go for a hike, or park and read a book in the shade!

This is a National Historic Landmark located inside Petrified Forest National Park. It was built in the 1920s by Hebert Lore. It was a homestead first; but when Route 66 was constructed Lore decided to turn it into a diner and motel for people to stay while driving through the area. This building was bought by the National Park Service in 1930. The CCC remodeled it into a ranger station but also used it an a diner for visitors to the park. It has murals painted on the walls done by a Hopi artist named Frank Kabotie. There is much more historical information available at the Inn if you chose to visit this landmark.

Just east of Sante Fe, this park is unique with a Spanish Mission church ruin in park. I recommend taking the 1.5 hour ranger-led talk through ruins. Very informative. The VC has a very nice bookstore and movie. Pecos village was a trading post with other villages nearby as well as the Plains people accessed through the Glorietta pass. The Pecos River was their water source for their crops and life. Interesting place cross culturally.
likes: Facilities & Services: Informative ranger-led talk, nice bookstore, movie

reviews_attraction.text: Very nice Visitor Center with paved walkway to the ruins. There are a few ladders along the way to allow access into the rooms. An Indian ruin is located at the base of the cliffs. There is a camp ground there but didn't view it. There is also a shuttle bus from town for free that brings you directly to the VC and CG.

This overlook is found in Canyonlands NP at the Island in the Sky section. It is clearly marked on the roadway, about 7 miles from the Visitor Center. The view is incredible. There is a plaque of John Wesley Powell who surveyed and floated this River in 1869 and 1871.

Located in southwest Utah, this is a spectacular park with three lava flows, red and white sandstone rock formations and canyons. Also has a paved trail for walking and biking that parallels main road through the park. Many hiking trails available throughout park.

Fabulous! Both Barrier-style pictographs and petroglyphs. There is a sign by Courthouse wash directing to the path to approach the wall. A little tricky to follow but cairns were in place to climb up the slick rock outcroppings.
