Great Visitor center with artifacts and helpful rangers. Cliff dwelling around spring were in original state as well as dwelling at bottom of cliff face by spring. Nicely engineered stairs to access ruins by spring.

The movie, artifacts and displays are incredible of the Ancient Puebloans. The Pueblo ruins have a kiva to enter if you wish. The area is called Cedar Mesa, where many of the artifacts have been found there locally.
If you are traveling on I-84 thru Idaho, great place to stop to view Malad River Gorge. It is only 12.5 miles long but it does dump into Snake River which you can view at lower end of overlooks.
Amazing place with Indian ruins tucked into canyon walls high above the canyon floors. Stairs travel down into the canyon circling walls where you can enter ruins. Very nice Visitor Center.
Went to this refuge to view sandhill cranes. Thousands of these large birds viewed along with varieties of ducks. Located SW of Tombstone. Beautiful with nice paved walkway through refuge.
Two canyons you can see by the rim road trails or take a Jeep tour. The Jeep guides are Navajos since you are in their territory. This park is managed cooperatively by NPS and Navajos.
This is an incredible fossil repository with fossils locally and nationally. Great place to spend a few hours viewing this finds, plants and animals represented.
Very nice Visitor Center and staff. On display were pelts from different mammals as well as a mountain lion, black bear and bobcat preserved by taxidermy.
Very steep trail leading to lower ruin but worth it. Docent at site to answer questions. The Visitor Center has very limited artifacts on display.
Awesome artist village with galleries and extraordinary cafe. Had a caramel drizzled bread pudding with whipped cream there that was to die for!!
Excellent Salado ruins with incredible view of Roosevelt Lake from the lower cliff dwelling. Visitor Center has small collection of artifacts.
This is a special monument with the dinosaur quarry, petroglyphs, campgrounds and hiking trails. Incredible setting in mountains and xanyons.
This is one of the most photographed springs in Yellowstone. However, to see it from above, there is a five mile hike one way for the view.
Well done ruins with multiple signs with great explanations along the way. However, the last 1/4 mole to ruin is very rough gravel road.
Great national park with two visitor centers and very accessible sites along the 28 mile park road. A few paved hiking trails as well.
Very well marked ruin but dirt paths were confusing. Also much of the ruins are just piles of rocks. There are signs along the trail.
Incredible view of DV badlands, Zabriskie Point, the Panamint Mountains and salt pan in valley. Great for sunrise or sunset viewing.
Accessible cliff dwellings by stairs above the Gift Shop and Museum. Since I was going to Bandelier NM, I didn't climb to see them.
Incredible views of Colorado River. This area is located off Route 313 near Moab, Utah. Entrance fee is $20 but worth every penny!

I was on the cruise today and it was worth every penny, then some. The views you experience from this cruise are once in a lifetime. I would recommend this to anyone who truly wants to see the lakeshore. Because of high and steel cliffs, this is the best way to see the lakeshore. The guides were excellent and were very knowledgeable about history and added some much appreciated humor. The cruise goes up and back so either side of the boat is good. The boats have upper and lower decks for viewing. If it gets cold, head down to the lower deck. Make sure to dress warmer, you are on superior and it can cool down quickly without warning. This is well worth the experience. 1st come 1st serve to board, So get there earlier.

I have a great time visiting upper and lower falls. I'm my opinion upper falls is better because your able to get alot closer to the action. In the summer time your able to rent boats to get closer to the falls. Also we visited in the winter time do the trail had about a foot of snow on the ground. This place is defiantly worth the visit.

What an absolutely amazing park. The views are worth the visit and the waterfalls are a must see. They have there own slide rock that is a natural water slide. You'll need a permit to hike this area so plan accordingly. Overall this was a wonderful day trip while I was visiting family in the area.

Easy to access if your handicapped in any form. The path is easy and the walk is short. If you would like to get to the bottom of the waterfall there is another path that starts where the handicap parking lot is located. It's worth the visit, several people were fishing the beautiful lake.

From the parking lot it's about a half mile hike. We went in the winter time, so we couldn't drive. The waterfall is better in the summer time because you have the option of getting closer on canoe or boat. I'm In the winter time viewing is only from a distance. That is my only complaint.

This is one of the best state parks I've been to. Within a couple hour hike you can see over 20 waterfalls. I recommend parking at lake rose entrance and hiking the trail that way. I recommend this hike to anyone who enjoys the beauty of nature and waterfalls. This is truly a must see.

This is a big and powerful waterfall. The hike is only a quarter of a mile to the waterfall. You get a close up view of the beauty of nature. This is a great place to visit. I was there in winter and it was worth my drive. Upper falls is alot better than lower falls and alot closer.

Great hike back to this spot. There is a trail off yhe sid3 off the road. There was no sign when we arrived but the trail is easy to find and obvious when you see it. Continue on the trail. You won't miss it. The best time would be in spring verse today because of water flow.

What a beautiful spot with a perfect view overlooking the ocean. This is best viewed at high tide as that will affect this area. So look up the tide schedule before you go. Parking right across the street and a short walk. Truly beautiful.

Very beautiful area, hiking here won't do it justice. You need to be in the water, either by kayak or cruise boat which they offer near by.  I would recommend this area to anyone want to explore the UP. I will be back in the near future.

This is amazing and a must do. From the standard parking lot it's about 3.2 mile round trip. It's worth it at the top. The views are amazing and actually walking across the bridge is an adrenaline rush. What an experience.

This is a beautiful bridge with a glass floor overlooking the valley. Absolutely amazing views and a better understanding of the trains that use to cross way back when. What a great piece of history restored.
This is also know as slide rock as you can tell from the video. This area was amazing and a lot of fun. They only give out 100 permits per day so plan accordingly. Overall this is a must see.
This is a great place to experience. We went in the winter time so do the lower bridge and walk way was close but this was still neat to see. The large water fall is worth the trip.
This was a neat stop on my way up to Duluth. 2 really nice waterfalls within a short distance from the parking lot for anyone with issues traveling falls. It's worth a stop.
Park here to access the trail. The trail is about 1.5 miles round trip. This location is the access point for this trail. Don't go to the other area Google maps recommends.
Cliff jumping was the bomb. The cliffs are in the back of the park so don't park near the entrance. Keep going on the road you can't miss it, they will be on your right.
This was a very near waterfall to see. There is a close parking lot and you will take a wooden path down to a viewing deck. This is a very easy hike and worth the time.
The water was crystal clear with an amazing view. This is a view you could look at all day. Mosquitos tend to get bad during the summer months so come prepared.
It's just a rock but the history of the location makes it worth a 5 star. The rock is eroding away with time and worth a quick stop on the way to the cape.
What a great spot. The brew tour was amazing with Gilmore. Overall a great spot with great beers. The tours were the best part. The guy did a great job.
This is a beautiful waterfall. This is the waterfall located under the bridge and the first one you crossover. The bridge is neat too.
What a great stop to visit movie history. It's nice that all of this has been preserved for us to experience. What a great experience.
It's worth taking in a great piece of history for a moment or two. Short detour If your heading to the Cape.
Beautiful little park in the middle of town. This is a little piece of heaven surrounded by a busy city.

This is definitely the trail through the Redwoods to stroll on if you are visiting Humboldt Redwoods. The road is a little bumpy and narrow in parts, but the drive to the spot is well worth it. What you will get is nice mile loop without the noise pollution of the Highway 101 or the Avenue of the Giants. Great campsite close by and some longer trailheads for those who have a bit more time on their hands. Make sure you show up supplied and ready to go.

Pictures do not do this place justice. It is hard to demonstrate how tall the walls are that are covered in a variety of ferns through the lens on a phone. The walls were weeping with water runoff and the overgrowth and mud slides deeper in the canyon showed just how wet this particular season was. Walking into the canyon was simply breathtaking and well worth either the hike from Prairie Creek Visitors Center or the drive into Gold Bluff Beach.

This is our favorite of the East Bay Regional Parks.  We have been hiking here as a family for years and come several times a year to enjoy the changing seasons. The hike to Little Yosemite is favorite along the creek. For those interested in hiking without any crowds, check out McQuirre (sp) look off of Welch Creek Road. This is apart of the park but the access is before you get to the main entrance.
likes: Scenic views (Little Yosemite, McQuirre look off)

reviews_attraction.text: WARNING: Make a reservation before you head out here. We were just out for a drive and followed the signs that took us out here. It was pretty cool to see the dwellings from a distance and appreciate the site itself. However, we did not have a reservation and could not take the tour up into the dwelling. That would have more than likely given this place 5 stars.

Anytime you get to go to a National Park, do it. This one is the closest to the SF Bay and does not seem like it will be much as you drive in. However, once you get out of the car and start on a trail, you are met with surprise and amazement at the geological features that transport you to a Disney ride. Lots of well marked trails, caves, and rock climbing.

Peaceful park, even when busy. Lots of camping available and beach access for those who want to enjoy the lake. Camping is not too close to the water, but the trails are relatively flat and well maintained. Nice visitors center that paints a good picture of what it must have been like for prior generations who used the pass as a path to the west.

Great place to hike and explore when in the area. It was very crowded the day we were there (I feel like this is always the case). There is a nice loop that goes from the parking lot, up the hill, and back along the beach. Wear a hat and bring sunscreen on a sunny day. Most of the walk is in exposed areas.

Great little park in the local foothills. Easy to get to and fantastic views if you are willing and able to walk up a hill. There is nice fishing pond and wide open field along with the many hiking trails that help one explore a little bit of nature so close to the hustle and bustle of city life.

Perhaps it is because I have the SF one to compare it to, but this was a disappointment. Half of the water features were not running and  It was crowded. I imagine that if the water features were on that it would have been a mich nicer experience. I.would not go back for the $15 entrance fee.

How could you not love a National Park? This park has volcanic features, alpine lakes, waterfalls, hiking and much more if you an outdoor enthusiast. If you have the time, this is a great starting point in the Lassen Volcanic Highway and head north past Shasta toward Crater Lake.

I could have spend the entire day here just rock climbing, scrambling and watching the scenery change right in front of me. In fact, that is what we did. Such a great place to enjoy some peace and quiet while getting a chance to do some world class bouldering.

This is a pretty neat park to visit. Looks like a great place to enjoy a stroll and spend time with the family. Like others stated, the bridge floor is pretty cool but can get very hot or slippery depending on weather conditions.

This is a reverant spot in the middle of a residential district. Some great sculptures that tell a story without the need for words. People that were there while we stopped by were repectful as well. Good stop on way to gardens

I meet up with a group of guys a couple of morning a week at the Isherwood staging area to run on the the trails. It is great location and plenty of people are around to keep you safe. No better place for running in Fremont.

Great place to hike and experience the cool breezes of the bay. On a clear day, you can see the Dumbarton Bridge, San Mateo Bridge, the Bay Bridge, San Francisco and Oakland. Be careful of the salt flats (they can stink).

Words cannot adequately describe this gem. Easy hike on well developed and busy hiking trails. Good to go early before the crowds.  A little bit of pain having to take transit, but worth it in the end.

Great place to visit for a walk through time. The Redwoods are amazing and the well marked trails make the stroll enjoyable. Good place to stop while passing through or to camp for a couple of nights.
Fantastic little bouldering area in the middle of the city. Lots of great bouldering and views of San Francisco. Nice to not have to drive 2 hours to get some outdoor climbing in.
This is a great place to run in the mornings. There are several of us who come to the park and run around the lakes a few mornings a week. Lucky to have this so close to us.
This stop capped off our day trip to the Grand Canyon. It was a pretty cool tower to walk into and climb to the top. Pretty neat artwork on the inside to look at.
Great spot to camp at. If you can get up early in the morning, walk down to the beach with a bucket. There will be more sand dollars then one can possibly count.
This is a nice little oasis in the middle of Golden Gate Park. A little expensive to enter if you are not a resident, but it is quite pleasant once you enter.
You cannot go wrong visiting Giant Sequioa groves at this wonderful park. Great place with very well maintained trails and facilities.
This is a small monument to stop over at, but cool nonetheless. It is pretty neat seeing these dwellings in person.
Hard to get a good picture of this place due to the trees and bridges. Kind of a fun little hunt to find.

I have lived in Kentucky my entire life,  and I visited here as a youth and had fond memories of that visit. But I took my wife here for the first time a few weeks ago and the disappointment I have for this place is great.  It seems as though they are trying to be an upscale place.  This is not what this place is. Please don't forget  the heritage of this place. Keep it real.

This is one of the more informative,  educational attractions at Walt Disney World. You are immersed in the actual growing and raising of healthy food.  It is also a very relaxing,  slow paced ride.  If you haven't been on this attraction you need to take the time for it. We try to ride everytime we visit the park.

This place is awesome,  my wife has always wanted to go to Madame Tussauds in New York. Thank goodness they came to Nashville. The figures are so life like we actually fooled our nieces with pictures, having met some of the stars it was uncanny.  The staff is great and very friendly.  Price is reasonable.

My wife and I absolutely live this place. W will probably never get to see Italy, so we enjoy seeing and talking to the cast members that are from there.  The food in the restaurants is outstanding,  and again the people ate phenomenal. We cannot wait until our next trip.

The city has been upgrading the park with the addition of a putt putt golf course, and the addition of a new entrance is nice.  They could benefit from paving these walking path as Mahr park has.  Still a good park just need to continue with the improvements.

I can only rate this place 3 stars because it was closed to the public.  I found out that Georgia state parks are closed on mondays,  very disappointing to travelers.  I believe this would have been a good place to visit. Sorry i didn't get the chance.

If you are interested in our countrys history, this is a must stop for you. You can step back in time and feel as though you are part of what happened at this fort. Look over the water and Ft. Sumter is there. Staff is very friendly and helpful .

This is a real good place to visit . Whether you are traveling the blue ridge parkway and need a break or just want a place to spend the day.  Great wildlife exhibits and the mile high bridge,  bring your nerves,. Would visit this place again.

This is a great place to experience a small part of what the united kingdom is like. They have a great fish and chips place, as well as the Rose and Crown pub. If you are looking for a gift make sure you check out the great shops.
likes: Facilities & Services: Fish and chips, pub, shops

reviews_attraction.text: This is a hidden gem in south Carolina. This should be a national monument.  The state is doing a great job with this property. Take the time to drive here it is well worth the time.  The staff the day we visited was awesome.

If you want to learn the history, and hear a few good stories this is wonderful. The only fall back is the boats are very crowded, they should remove the middle row of seats to make it more comfortable for everyone.
Good place to spend the day,  free zoo is a great place for the young ones. The reason four only three stars is the parking.  We had tho park four blocks away,  they need to invest in more parking.
It's part of our nation's history, I on my wish that everyone that was there realized this. Still its a great place to reflect on the sacrifice that those few haves made to protect us all.
Good spot to stop and visit while traveling the blue ridge parkway.  Nice to stand on the highest point of the country east of the Mississippi River. Great view from the top.
It's a great place but it's a little hard to get around in. The maps can be confusing. Take your time tho understand them before you take off on your adventure.
This is great place for history. I loved the fact that the people that worked there, that I spoke with were actually veterans. Take the time to look around.
Nice scenic spot for a photo opportunity. It is the total journey down route 66, not one spot will make the trip,  you need to experience them all.
Nice trail that leads to a beautiful water fall, just remember you are in nature, you could see snakes, bear, or other WILD animals, use caution.
Very beautiful grounds,  did not actually go into the building, but thr grounds were well kept and the views from thr ground was very nice.
Absolutely beautiful place if you like nature. Couldn't help but wonder what this area was like when Daniel Boone was exploring the area.
this is a great place,  just to know that it has been here since before  we were a country.  Please leave this place as you found it.
This is a great place to visit to see how one of our greatest presidents lived as a child. If you like history this is a must see.
Could spend countless hours here,  don't pass this place up on your way to the canyon. This place is as beautiful if not more so.
The most beautiful water fall we have ever seen,  please do yourself a favor and take the time to go see this place.
Nice place to spend the day, for a picnic, spend the night camping, fish for the day, or just kick back and relax.

Took almost an hour to enter into the parking lot and obviously it was incredibly busy due to spring break. Surprisingly though, there weren’t as many children as young adults. Some of the trails were closed which was a huge bummer for the amount of time it took us waiting to get into the park. Coming from a large population in Chicagoland area, the amount of people in some of the lookout areas was so overwhelming that it made it hard to enjoy the experience. There was photographers, photo ops and people climbing over each other to get the best views, we even saw an middle aged woman fall and get hurt and I truly believe it was due to the commotion of so many people in the lookout areas. We also brought our small dog and I wouldn’t recommend taking a dog to the lookout points for future reference, especially if it’s a busy day. With all that being said, it’s very clear why George Washington chose this as the original place to build our Capital near. There is incredible power coming from the Potomac River but the people that we saw kayaking were the real show stoppers. We also were able to watch rock climbers in some areas as well which my kids thoroughly enjoyed. Overall a good experience but VERY VERY busy. If you’re looking for a quiet trail and peace look somewhere else, but the historical significance far outweighed the foot traffic for our family in the end.

Hadley valley loop is great for working on timing yourself and getting a good walk in, but unless you’re there during sunrise and sunset the views are pretty meh. It has some elevation that’s not too strenuous but makes an impact on your exercise. This is not a hiking area and it’s more like a walking loop. The ground is a type of crushed gravel and some pits are on the trail so watch your ankles and also watch for the horse and bird poop. There are poop bags for your dogs which is good in case you forget to bring some.

Love Starved Rock so much. We went on a day that called for rain. The canopy is already thick enough that when the thunder rolled in and the light rain started we barely got wet. My husband and I bring our kids and furry kid walking about 4-5 times a year and never get tired of the smells and the flowers blooming. I just wish they’d do a better job of keeping the path along the river cleaned up better.

This trail is awesome! When I looked online it says it’s only a 1/2 mile but the trail is bigger than that for sure! We enjoyed going from prairie land trails and tall wild grass into the woods and we eventually came up upon Romeoville’s village hall where there’s a super nice playground for the kids. I will be back to explore more. So happy to find this gem.

Incredible! Be prepared to walk thru the lava rock and wear proper footwear. I wore my keen sandals and although I wear them 99% of the time on my hiking adventures, this is not the place! Can’t wait to come back and show my kiddos the majesty that is our beautiful planet and how nature overcomes anything!

We went here to experience “the bathtub” and it was really quite nice experience. The water level was so low in the river that my kids, my dog and I were able to cross it without it going more than waist deep on my 5 year old. We saw snakes and lots of small fish. A great way to spend a lazy Sunday.

I absolutely love the dunes! Waited 33 years to experience the dunes, the hiking and the beaches and man was I missing out on something! So much to do! People need to follow rules though, and the only way that’s gonna happen is if the park rangers crack down on people not following the rules.

We drove almost 3 hours out of our way to go to this tour. To say the ambiance is weird is putting it mildly. My husband and I are cave lovers so we try to go to one in every state we visit but this was our first “dead cave”. The tour was a bit quick for how long we drove to get to it.

What an amazing hike! This trail take you along the Appalachian so you get to see hikers of all kinds. Not a trail for the faint of heart. There’s some slippery drop offs on the way down but we managed with young ones. The waterfall at the end made this hike even better.

Such a great place to go with or without kids. There’s so much to see! There is a windmill, a light house, a Chinese garden an old boathouse, a flower arch path, a bridge where we saw and eagle and an old rock garden.  Across the street is a hiking path that is unpaved.

It’s an alright place to take the kids in the summertime to blow off some of their energy. They have a charge to get in. They also have a covered pavilion and concession stand. Right next to it is a great playground that you don’t have to pay to use.

Such different plant diversity and friendly hikers on this path. Beautiful and peaceful views of Lake Michigan. I was the only one on the beach. The sand dune on the way back is no joke, so be prepared. Around 4 miles and it’s an out and back trail.

Oh Bell Rock. You definitely feel like you took rocket fuel when you’re there! My husband and I went all the way around the rock and then ended on a ledge that gave us a vision of heaven. My second favorite place in Sedona next to Buddha Beach.

Great walk with a covered bridge going over route 30. A little too much traffic for my liking and it’s completely paved. More of a walking, running, biking trail, not a hiking trail. It’s an out and back trail that connects to I&M canal trail.

One of the few trails that allows dogs. Was able to see a plethora of butterflies on this trail which was a pleasant surprise and the kids and dog got to play in the water as well. The kids thought the bridge was fun too.

This is a great park to take kids to burn off their energy. Very unusual layout with the Pokémon go type interactive game you can download on your phone and play with your kids. It’s also in a very convenient location.

Nice short hike with a trail and a run off. Lots of opportunities for my kids and I to practice grappling and scooting and the kids loved log climbing too. Have to get off the path to do so but it’s fun and worth it.
My favorite place I got to visit in Sedona. It felt so comforting and warm there. Lots of people but you can find a secluded spot here and there. The rock island was an amazing find.
This place was AWESOME! My kids loved trying the zip line and spent a couple hours at the playground. Super clean and open. Absolutely a gorgeous place! Go. Your kids will thank you.
Wish the trails were longer and the park was cleaner. I like that they’ve turned it into a frisbee golf park but it makes us hikers have to keep an eye out for flying frisbees.
This is a great place to take your kids for a quick nature walk and to see all the critters in the nature center. The trails are mostly paved and dog friendly.
Awesome place! Friendly and patient staff. My girls loved feeding the alligators and watching the snapping turtles feast on a live mouse.
One of the few trails in Gatlinburg that you can walk your dog. Wish there were more trails for dogs in this area. I’d visit more often.
This place has an awesome lookout that’s on top of a hill and great walking trails. Nice and green, clean park.
This was a nice peaceful walk with a dog park connected to the trail. You need a permit for the dog park.

An interesting tour for adults and kids. You have the opportunity to climb all over this historic WWII aircraft carrier. Climbing is the key word here. Be sure to wear comfortable shoes. There's a lot of walking and climbing, but it is definitely worth it. There is a nice display of aircraft on board, as well.

You can also tour the USS Laffey, a WWII destroyer known as "the ship that would not die" and the USS Clamagore, a Cold War submarine. Both are interesting tours. However, the Clamagore might not be for the claustraphobic.

The Holocaust Museum is educational, sometimes difficult to handle, and deeply touching regardless of your ethnicity or religious preference. The tour is made very real and very personal when you are given a card with a short biography of a concentration camp victim (or survivor) on it. You cannot help but feel the connection.

Every visitor to Washington DC should tour this museum. You may not enjoy the Holocaust Museum in the traditional sense, but you will grow from the experience.

The changes made to The Henry Ford in recent years have improved the quality of the visitor's experience by leaps and bounds. Years ago it was cluttered and disorganized. There seemed to be no rhyme or reason to the layout. Now the displays are well organized and easy to follow and comprehend. It is truly an enjoyable museum experience for the whole family.

A beautiful church and the people who work there are friendly and knowledgable. The stained glass windows are gorgeous. The main alter and crucifix are uniquely Santa Fe. Be warned, however, this is an active church and you will not be allowed in during funerals and weddings. I would also avoid the area on Sunday mornings unless you plan on attending mass.
likes: Cultural Value: Stained glass, Unique altar
Facilities & Services: Friendly staff, Knowledgeable staff
dislikes: Facilities & Services: Limited access during events

reviews_attraction.text: People need to remember this is not run by our national park service. It is on Indian land, so tribal rules apply. It is a fun spot for a quick picture but is not the type of destination anyone should drive hundreds of miles out of their way to see. Remember to bring sunscreen and water during summer months and be prepared to stand in line for a photo op.

White Sands National Park is both beautiful and unique. As you drive deeper into the park and vegetation gets sparser, you feel like you're in a snowfield. Everything is snow white including the road. It's strangely beautiful. And it's fun for kids. They can go sledding on the sand hills. White Sands is fun and interesting for all ages.

Pine Island is a wonderful little hidden gem on the Gulf shore in Hernando County. For a $5 entrance fee you get access to a lovely beach, play equipment for the kids, a fishing pier, public restrooms, a small beachside restaurant and amazing sunsets. I have been frequenting Pine Island for over 30 years and I love it.

Over a million years ago a giant volcanic eruption created the Valles Caldera. It is now a wild life preserve that is home to elk coyote, prairie dogs, black bears, eagles and more. It has excellent hiking, biking, photo ops and even flyfishing. This a beautiful and serene spot in New Mexico not far from Los Alamos.

A great family park. We went at Christmastime last year and they had a lovely light display. This year we went to the Enchanted Pumpkin Garden. There were cute pumpkin displays, food and craft vendors and entertainment. It's a great place for the whole family. The major problem is a lack of adequate parking.

Bandolier is an excellent park. The main trail winds through ancient pueblo ruins and cliff dwellings and is not difficult to maneuver. I did not have the opportunity to do the 140 foot climb but I have been told it is definitely worth it if you can manage it. Bandolier is definitely worth a trip.

North Bay Park is a lovely, hidden gem in Ypsilanti Township. A boardwalk circles the lake filled with fish and turtles. There are also swans, ducks and two types of geese in abundance. Barn swallows fly over the lake incessantly. It's usually not crowded which is a big plus for me.

A somber and touching tribute to the lives lost in Vietnam. For those of us who lived through that war, to see the names of those thousands of lives lost in battle, is a terrible reminder of the senselessness of war. The Vietnam Wall is a very personal and emotional experience.

An excellent museum dedicated to the art of Georgia O'Keeffe, considered to be the "Mother of American Modernism". She is famous for her iconic paintings of over-sized flowers many of which are housed in this museum. This is an absolute must see museum for art enthusiasts.

Every American should get the opportunity to visit Ford's Theater where President Lincoln was shot and history was changed. Be sure to visit the Petersen house as well where the President died. Both tours are well done and informative. They should not be missed.

Such a lovely waterside park at the end of the battery in Charleston. The best time to visit is in the spring when the flowers are in full bloom. The park is in the heart of the historic district surrounded by fabulous post Civil War mansions.

This is one of the most beautiful memorials in Washington DC. It is striking by day and even more striking by night. It is a touching tribute to the thousands of Americans who lost their lives in WWII.
Lower Huron Metro Park is a big sprawling park with lots of biking and walking trails. In the spring the flowering trees are gorgeous. There is also a golf course and an aquatics center for the kids.
I love this place. There aren't many places where you have to stop to let an alligator cross the road or see a Spoonbill peeking through the trees. No fences. No guardrails. Just nature at its best.
A free museum that gives you a look at the development of nuclear weaponry, plus a look at on-going research. The introductory film is a good place to start. Lots of hands on activities.
A lovely historic home in an ideal setting. Much to see. The tour was informative & the guides are knowledgable. Be sure to tour the grounds and outbuildings around the home.
I love history and Fort Moultrie has a long one. It dates back to 1776. We came across  Fort Moultrie by accident and I'm glad we did. A great way to spend an afternoon.
Kensington was a great park when I was a kid and it's even better now. Rolling hills. Great beaches. Nice picnic areas. Lots of wild life. Good for walking and biking.
Fascinating place. Gives the visitor a good look at the history and culture of the southwestern pueblo Indians. Will definitely return.
This is such a beautiful structure. The mosaics are amazing. People of all faiths will enjoy the beauty and majesty of this church.
A beautiful, out of the way area. A place where you can relax and enjoy the scenery without throngs of people.

Very cool exhibit. We were not expecting the way they had set the acoustics up so that was a fun surprise. And believe me, I get why they don't allow pictures ( because its trademarked) but, I would love to be able to have some photos with it. There is a selfie background set up outside though
Beautiful park. Lots of look outs. There are a lit of locals selling their products at the sites as well. All is very pretty. If you can, take tour inside the canyon with one the tour groups
Lady in store was disinterested and not welcoming at all. Interesting part of history but nothing was open to see. Loved seeing the horses in the back. We heard turkeys but never saw them
There are a lot of famous people from history here. There is no map to let you know where everyone is at though. We used an app about the Freedom Trail that gave us the information though
The history of the area is deep with culture. The rushing river provides for a peaceful lunch spot. Unfortunately,  the park was filthy and there were very rowdy groups there when we went
We didn't get to see the inside because it was closed. The grounds were very well maintained and the opportunity to pull the history on your cell was clever. Great part of history
There are several times if year when there are different happenings going on. Check the schedule on the website to see what is going on when you are there. Great docents
Lots to see. Fortunate enough to go inside the temple as they were setting up for a wedding. Loved watching others practice traditional Buddhist prayers while there too.
It was closed when we were there but, we got to walk the grounds. There is a map for the cemetery and plaques around the building to describe the history
Very nice. There was a lot of information available through displays and staff. Love how this really felt like the people in there were truly interested
A variety of museums to select from and many open spaces to enjoy the beautiful landscape and surrounding areas. A few food carts of different sorts
I am sure it has beautiful hikes. We were there in a thunderstorm so, hiking was out of the question. No roads to drive around and see any scenery
Amazing! Such a fabulous tribute. The fuides were so informative and had a lot of fun facts and trivia. We did the pedastal tour. Beautiful views
Beautiful area. The buildings are well preserved for being out in the extreme weather. Nice walking paths. A few picnic tables down by the river
Wow! Beautiful park! The trails take you to incredible spots. Campgrounds are very well kept and the cave tour was incredible! Great rangers
Amazing!! The docents and volunteers are very helpful and knowledgeable.  They even gave us pointers for other points of interest to visit
Another beautiful nationally park. It is small and can be done quickly.. all of the trails are paved and easy to get around on.
Fun spot. Make sure to check the store hours. It is behind a fence so you won't be able to get up close if they are closed
We have been to many zoo's, all across the US. This one ranks right up there with the best of them. Fantastic exhibits!
We were here too early and it had just snowed so, nothing was open. It looked like a really neat place to take the kids
The zoo, Storybook Land and Playland are here. Otherwise don't go. It is full of homeless people and is very dirty
Lots of history here. There is also a a few historic markers around. The businesses here all have stories to tell
Loved this! We have been to a lot of caves and a lot of lava tubes, this was a great place to experience it all!
So much to see. It was our first time trying "fried dough" which was actually very similar to funnel cake
Just saw this! Wish I had known ahead of time what it was. We seriously thought it was falling over 🤪

Beautiful place to see some amazing petroglyphs and dinosaur tracks. Just 11 miles off I-15 from exit 78 in Parowan.  Follow 4th north out to the west.  Everything is well marked and there are cool interpretations by local Paiute tribesmen.  A stunning place to be. I've also done a lot of road biking through here and it is a nice road to make a loop out of.

One of the funnest parks we’ve ever visited. Best place to play hide and seek with the kids. They didn’t want to leave. We stayed out near Temple Mountain in a free campsite area with some old ruins of the previous mines. Really cool place. Its far enough off the beaten path that the crowds were minimal.

Great tour guide, Andrew Miles, took us through the whole place answering our frequent questions with candid answers. They don’t sugar coat Jefferson’s complex relationship with morals and ethics. Super interesting and enlightening. Our kids really enjoyed it as well.

This review is for the cross-country skiing track. We brought our 3 kids here over Christmas and had a great time. We were the first there in the morning and it was groomed very nicely. Ski rentals were relatively cheap.  Great place to do some laps and very serene.

If your thing is long, hard, solid crystalline logs, you’re in business. They got’em in spades. Fascinating history. The landscape is pretty desolate until you arrive at the park and then it turns colorful and varied. Newspaper rock was also tops. Dogs are welcome.

One of the most underrated parks in the southwest. Views that parallel Zion, but with added heroic/tragic history, still present native culture, and a fraction of the crowds of lesser parks. Don’t miss it.

Literally at the end of the road, this place is amazing. The artist really drew you out into the vast wilderness to have an experience you aren’t likely to have in many places in Utah. Everyone was in awe.

Great museum for families with young kids. Lots of hands on stuff. Exhibits are always changing.  Friendly staff.  Can get busy on weekends and school holidays. Can usually find parking along 5th south.

Don't come to St. George and not visit Snow Canyon. Amazing views. Park just north of the north entrance and hike to the White Rocks amphitheater sand dunes and look down in for one of the best views.
Beautiful place to visit. Stayed at Lucerne campground, which is decent, but the campgrounds closer to Dutch John looked better. Floated the Green, which the kids loved. Sheep Creek area was amazing.
Cool old church filled with local anitiques and historical stuff.  The tour guides, mostly older local lady volunteers, will tell you tons of stories, mostly about their own ancestors.
Excellent place to visit to get an idea of what Salt Lake looked like in early pioneer times.  Kids really enjoy it. Lots of interaction with the animals.  Worth checking out.
As far as animal jails go, this one is pretty decent. I hadn't been since I was a kid and it didn't seem too different. Still pretty small. The bird show was the best part.
We used this park as the start of the Vision Relay. Really nice with a cool skate park and beautiful grass. Would be a great place to chill after a day of mountain biking.
If you want a unique place to see in Salt Lake, this is it. Lots of quirky statues with interesting histories.  Fun for little kids to climb around on too.
No better place to be on a winter day. Huge variety of terrain. No boarders. Albion basin is one of the most serene places just minutes from Salt Lake.
Beautiful hike. Used to be off the beaten path, now the path is rather beaten. Still a lot of fun if you come during the week when kids are in school.
Well maintained trails, although pretty pricey for the distances. They are groomed daily and the views can't be beat.  Skate and classic tracks.
Nice little park just a block from the geyser. Mineral spring water is safe to drink. Picnic area and grassy field nice for group gathering.
Awesome park, few people there on a weekend.  The pioneer homes and school house were cool. Picked apples in the orchard. A real hidden gem.
We ended the 2017 Vision Relay here and the park was really nice. Great place to chill out after a day of biking or enjoying the scenery.
Lots of neat history and very nice Rangers. It is quite out-of-the-way, but definitely worth a visit. Then go over to the spiral jetty.
Awesome views and jumping off point for Wasatch Crest and other trails. Can get very crowded on weekends, so get there early.
Beautiful building in modern style. Very crowded on holiday weeks. Park below and walk up if possible. Great views up top.
Great XC skiing. Groomed daily. 8 miles of course if you do it all in one go. We regularly see moose.

(Translated by Google) I happened to come by here and had not booked a tour before, which is why I was only able to participate spontaneously because someone had canceled shortly before. So I can advise you to reserve seats!
The tour itself is great! The guide is very friendly and explains a lot about flora and fauna, it is often stopped to look at alligators and other animals from close proximity and take pictures. If the boat is standing you can move freely and leave your seat.
On the approximately one-hour ride you get to see dozens of alligators. If you are traveling in the summer months, you should be prepared for some insects, but in the "winter" you will not be bothered.
Only landscape you should not expect too much from the Everglades as an endless flat marshland.

(Original)
Ich bin hier zufällig vorbeigekommen und hatte vorher keine Tour gebucht, weshalb ich nur deshalb noch spontan teilnehmen konnte, weil kurz zuvor jemand abgesagt hatte. Ich kann also dazu raten, sich Plätze zu reservieren!
Die Tour an sich ist großartig! Der Guide ist sehr freundlich und erklärt sehr viel über Flora und Fauna, es wird oft angehalten um Alligatoren und andere Tiere aus direkter Nähe zu betrachten und fotografieren zu können. Sofern das Boot steht kann man sich auch frei bewegen und seinen Sitzplatz verlassen.
Auf der rund einstündigen Fahrt bekommt man Dutzende Alligatoren zu sehen. Wer in den Sommermonaten reist, sollte sich auf einige Insekten einstellen, im "Winter" hingegen wird einem nichts lästig.
Nur landschaftlich sollte man von den Everglades als endlose flache Sumpflandschaft nicht zu viel erwarten.

(Translated by Google) To experience the Kennedy Space Center, you should really bring some time and not only go through the interesting Visitor Complex, but also take advantage of the numerous bus tours offered to various areas of the site. Although these tours have to be purchased separately, making the stay very expensive, they are more than worth their money. Basically, it is recommended to book everything as far in advance as possible online, especially if there is a rocket launch on the day of the visit and the rush is correspondingly huge.
A few souvenirs from the gigantic NASA shop should also be planned!

(Original)
Um das Kennedy Space Center zu erleben, sollte man wirklich einiges an Zeit mitbringen und nicht nur den sehenswerten Visitor Complex durchlaufen, sondern auch die zahlreichen angebotenen Bustouren zu verschiedenen Arealen des Geländes wahrnehmen. Diese einzelnen Touren müssen zwar, wodurch der Aufenthalt sehr teuer werden kann, separat erworben werden, sind ihr Geld aber mehr als wert. Grundsätzlich ist es empfehlenswert, alles soweit möglich im Voraus online zu buchen, insbesondere wenn am Besuchstag ein Raketenstart erfolgt und der Andrang dementsprechend riesig ist.
Ein paar Souvenirs aus dem gigantischen NASA-Shop sollten ebenfalls eingeplant werden!

(Translated by Google) Must-see! Not only but especially aerospace or military enthusiasts get their money's worth here. The impressive aircraft carrier can be viewed almost completely and the backdrop of Manhattan in the background provides spectacular images. Aside from the interior of the Concorde, the General Admission ($ 33 ​​adults) can see everything on the grounds (such as Space Shuttle Enterprise) or the aircraft carrier itself.

(Original)
Pflichtbesuch! Nicht ausschließlich aber besonders Luft-, Raumfahrt oder Militärbegeisterte kommen hier voll auf ihre Kosten. Der beeindruckende Flugzeugträger kann nahezu komplett besichtigt werden und die Kulisse Manhattans im Hintergrund sorgt für spektakuläre Bilder. Abgesehen vom Inneren der Concorde kann mit der General Admission (33 $ Erwachsene) alles besichtigt werden, was sich auf dem Gelände (beispielsweise Space Shuttle Enterprise) oder dem Flugzeugträger selbst befindet.

(Translated by Google) Of the many breathtaking national parks in the western United States, this is one of the most beautiful by far. On the one hand, there are no tourist crowds here, such as the Grand or Bryce Canyon, and you can walk alone on many hiking routes for hours and enjoy nature. On the other hand, there are picturesque places such as the Captiol Gorge Road - a dirt road that leads through a breathtaking canyon. Sensational!

(Original)
Von den vielen atemberaubenden Nationalparks im Westen der Vereinigten Staaten ist dieser hier einer der mit Abstand schönsten. Zum einen finden sich hier keine Touristenmassen wie im Grand oder Bryce Canyon und man kann sich auf vielen Wanderrouten über Stunden alleine bewegen und die Natur genießen. Zum anderen gibt es malerische Orte wie beispielsweise die Captiol Gorge Road - eine unbefestigte Straße, die durch einen atemberaubenden Canyon führt. Sensationell!

20 years ago the doctors told to his wife that she was going blind and she could only see bright colors . He was a veteran and inspired by his travels,especially in India, he started to built the butterfly house with colorful butterflies so his wife could see them...His wife today is blind and she can't see anymore the bright colors but she can touch the butterflies and feel.
He is still working on the house and he did all of it...for his wife.
Such an inspiration!
October 13,2018

°

》The Chapel is located in the heart of what many describe as a vortex bringing gratitude to those who flock there. Sedona itself is well known to many for its connection to new-age mysticism and the purported energy vortices on the outskirts of the city. Despite this connection, the Chapel itself was actually built by a devout student of Frank Lloyd Wright named Marguerite Brunswig Staude in 1956. Staude wanted to create a lasting tribute to her religious beliefs, and was so taken with the beauty of Sedona that she began work on the Chapel.《

★AVENUE OF THE GIANTS★
•The tallest redwood, Hyperion, is 379 feet tall – the height of a 37 story building!  It is estimated to be 700 to 800 years old.

•The widest redwood is 27 feet across at its base – equivalent to two VW bugs parked bumper-to-bumper.

•The oldest Coast Redwoods are over 2,000 years old.  Some of the redwoods alive today sprouted in the days of the Roman Empire.

The majority of interactive booths and displays are geared towards children. Also one floor is nothing more than arcade games that you will need to purchase tokens for if lil Johnny is accompanying you.

The gardens were in a pretty disappointing state during our early August visit. There were lots of weeds, dead flowers and vegetables. I asked a groundskeeper to identify a particular flower that my wife was curious about and he was unable to. A slithering surprise ran us out of one of the areas in a hurry!! The gardens may look much better in spring time but I doubt we would return.,

I had been to Key West a few times in the 90's ,ventured to the buoy on several occasions and it was usually deserted save for a few wino's willing to snap your picture for a few dollars.
Now its a cluster fluck pretty much all daylong,probably due to the cruise ship invasions..
I do know i was not going to stand in line for a pic.
I did a walk by picture....

Church pew style seating,get your tickets online so that you can pick a seat on the end of the row!!All the seats appeared to have good views of the stage.We went to see Carrie Underwood as the headliner but there were some old timers like Ricky Skaggs/Connie Smith and up n comers such as Logan Brill and Charlie Worsham playing on the card as well.

The Alamo is very well kept and a great way to kill an hour in the air conditioned buildings while browsing the various memorabilia/artifacts and listening to the tour guides narrate a little history.
The grounds are what we enjoyed the most,the trees with their huge limbs growing along the ground are beautiful.

The memorial sits beside highway 1 and has its own small parking area. Having spent several years in Florida and experiencing a few hurricanes I had already knew of the hurricane of '35 but I still enjoyed reading the information and walking the grounds,very peaceful.

The wife and I had a blast during our visit t the lazy 5 ranch.
During your drive throughout the ranch beware of the llama snot projectiles aimed at your windows and the bucket thugs that snatch onto your feed bucket and yank it out of your hands.....

Another interesting place for history buffs or those just wanting to get out and enjoy the outdoors in the Sunshine State...Beautiful, well kept grounds along with friendly employees make Fort Clinch State Park an enjoyable place to visit .

We've visited The Ciudad Mitad del Mundo so why not the Center of the USA! Well maintained grounds and worth the drive out to Belle Fourche to see it, don't forget to hit the little boutique shops on the main street and support local.

Nice setting in downtown Lexington and a great spot to sit and enjoy a picnic or sack lunch.
The highlight of the park is the beautifully detailed horse and jockey statues posed as if they were taking part in the Run for the Roses.

The only point of interest I had bookmarked to visit in Central Park.'
I snapped a few pictures and then watched quite a few tweeners and twentysomethings trample the roses and Imagine mosiac to get that purrfect selfie.

Beautiful grounds that are well kept.
We enjoyed walking around observing the various wildlife and narrated tours.Enough here to keep one busy for several hours.
Admission is free if you stay overnight on site!
We had a great time touring the conservation area with Gator Bait air boat rides. Observed lots of birds, fish, turtles and many gators both large and small..Very peaceful out on the water here.
The trolley is the best way to get a feel and layout of the historic/downtown area of St Augustine..The narration by the guide is a bonus....Check localflavor/groupon etc for discount tix.

Attended the arts and craft festival 2015.
Many vendors selling items ranging in price from a few dollars upwards to several hundred.
I picked up a few souvenirs and had a good time.

This was my favorite paid attraction during our Christmas getaway to South Florida.
Nice gift shop,friendly staff, a very nice conservatory that is clean and well maintained.

Awesome alligator Zoo
The park is well laid out and easy to navigate.
Many different species of Alligators and Crocs to go with a variety of birds and snakes on display.
Nice little town and Museum to spend a few hours in, and glad we decided to drive out to Belle Fourche to get away from the mask-less crowds elsewhere.
The Stockyards is my go-to tourist spot when in the DFW area. Good hotels, restaurants and entertainment venues all within walking distance.

It's a small statue in front of the charging bull statue on wall street.
The area is crowded with tourist's such as myself.

We ended up having our picnic in the park at the castle.
Great views all around and the Delacorte Theater is nearby.
Wow, once we got off Interstate 17 from Phoenix onto 179 the views as you drive into Sedona were beautiful.
Tanner was a great guide on the adventure tour. Nice and cool inside the cave on a 90 degree day!!

Legendary birding experience. A must-visit for any serious (or not so serious) bird watcher. There's basically one trail out and back. I didn't see a lot of birds in terms of shear quantity, but every one I did see was something special. Think flame-colored tanager, elegant trogon, rivoli's hummingbird, etc.

Massive place to hike around and see the birds. The wildlife drive is closed to vehicles now, so be prepared to walk. Trails are well marked and border patrol is patrolling all over so it feels really safe. Just don't come without ID 😉

Great little place to stop with about 15 minutes of exhibits for kids and very helpful staff for understanding the wildlife viewing opportunities in the area. She pointed out some mating season turtles for me to see in broad daylight.

Large area with local specialty birds and even more mosquitos. Recommend calling ahead to see when the tram tours are. That's a great way to see more of the park and find more birds. The master naturalist guide was awesome.

We meet here every Saturday morning at 10am for a small dog off-leash walk (less than 20lbs please). It's amazing for the little furry ones and their humans as there's over 100 dogs out on a nice day. 🐶🏖️
It's so fortunate to have such a wonderful dog play area close by. It's a fenced in one, so sometimes you get the less well trained dogs there. But on the whole, it's awesome and great views to boot.
A wonderful walk through a unique former section of the 1 which was closed due to frequent landslides. It's so nice that they opened it as a park and excellent place for bird watching.
Decent small place to walk around for birding. The highlight was their feeder theater which was better setup and stocked than anything I saw at the other world bird centers.
Wonderful variety of habitats that are accessible, yet deceptively easy to get lost in. There are feeders setup throughout and it seems to be a hotspot for rare birds.
World class bird watching... And it's free! I must have seen two dozen species from my car. It seemed like  an individual was every 20ft along this 11 mile drive.
So expansive it's hard to see everything without getting worn out. The recent remodel is definitely nice, although most of the exhibits are still familiar.
Incredible amount of bird life packed into a dense location. They really did a good job making this pretty, accessible and attractive to animals.
Huge area with lots of ponds that you can get really close to the birds. This was the most prolific of the world birding centers that I visited.
Five stars are not enough!! Vincent Arroyo has been my favorite wine country experience for years. You simply won't find a friendlier vineyard.
Truly unique to have a world class zoo with free admission. Despite my ambivalence about the ethics of zoos, this truly is a well done park.
What a beautiful and fun place to spend an afternoon. Sundays and dollar beer and dollar hotdogs. Just make sure not to eat too many dogs 😉
Very well maintained and easy to access. Unfortunately, I couldn't get close enough to anything to photograph well (even with 600mm).
Great place for bird watching and dog walking. Well maintained and varied trail. Just beware the coyotes, especially with small dogs.
Probably the best tourist attraction in St Louis. The free tour rivals that of Guinness and Jameson in Dublin. Plus... Free Beer!
Vast beaches, bluffs and dunes for a scenic stroll while Fido dashes around with the many furry playmates that frequent the park.
Gorgeous and fascinating mansion and gardens. It felt a little pricey at $18/person, but still glad I got to experience it.
Massive wildlife preserve with some of the best birding in the US. Too big to explore in a day (or even two). Enjoy!
Wonderful mission and park. Only wish more of the birds were viewable without a wire mesh between them and the lens.
The birding wasn't quite as good as I was hoping and I got kind of a shady vibe from some of the people around.
I'm ambivalent about zoos in general, but that aside, this zoo is a little small and dated for a city like SF.

This museum is now one of my favorites. Definitely a hidden gem... Rodin, Monet, Manet and other works of art... Beautifully set in amazing architecture. I like that it's not very well visited amongst the tourists. If you pay for admission to the de Young, you get this museum as part of your ticket. It's like 2 museums for the price of 1! A must go!  Parking is free across the entrance. The Thinker welcomes you...  I just bought a membership because to see the special exhibit, you have to pay $28 a person. With 2 people attending, I figured I might as well. Plus membership gets you into the De Young which is a bonus.

There are no signs and google maps takes you to the airport if you put in Prospect Park Scenic Viewpoint. The actual way to get here is off of Mile Marker 6 on Mill Creek Road. There's parking across from Prospect Service Gas Station.  Trail is not marked and you kind of have to trust your gut and listen to the sound of the water. Take a right when you're on the trail. Very short easy hike. Remember there are no signs designating where to go.

The end to Tomales Point Trail. When the marine layer clears you can see more clearly the Pacific Ocean and the other side of Tomales Bay. The trek here is 4.7 miles one way but you'll see Tule Elk and Wildflowers along the way. Bring an extra pair of socks for those accidental slips in the mud puddles  on trail.

Short hike to the Cove. The coastline is so beautiful! The water is amazing. If you keep going past where most people stop to enjoy the scenery, you'll get even a better view. And your reward is solitude! Keep going around the rocks, find a spot and hopefully it is sunny enough to enjoy the rays.

Official parking lot is closer to the visitors center and then you take the buckeye trail which has various elevations and then you cross the street to the actual Blue Hen Falls Trail. Pedestrians are forbidden on the road. But definitely worth the journey!!  It's beautiful!

Rich historical buikding, but definitely a wait to get up to the top of the tower. Surrounding park is lovely with majestic views of the Bay Area. Parking is limited but I didn't have a hard time at the the top of the hill. Weekend parking along the streets are prohibited.

Big Stump Grove is a sight for sore eyes. Sad. Grant Grove is filled with tourists... Wait til summer when you can go to Roads End and hike into the Canyon. Meadows and waterfalls and majestic views carved by glaciers. Kings Canyon is actually deeper than the Grand Canyon.

A magical place! Redwood forests. Coastal Trails. Creeks and Vistas. The National Park is comprised of 3 state parks... Jedediah Smith, Del Norte Coast, and Prairie Creek. The drive down the coast is amazing. Tallest known trees in the world.

Beautiful grounds carefully crafted of themed gardens from Chile to Asia to Australia and so on. I like the Redwood Grove and Ancient Plant Garden.  San Francisco residents get in for free! Wow. Could easily spend hours and hours here.

Love this place!  Watch for cloudy conditions blocking Mount Rainier itself. Snow still on the ground in June as you get to Paradise! October is perfect. Columbus Day no one is there and it was a perfect gorgeous day!
Talk about gentrification between Indians and Whites.  Inspirada is no inspiration.  You can tell it was a community with no character...  Signs of builders everywhere. KB, Lyon, etc...
Hole-in-the-rock dirt road requires patience as one traverses within the least visited part of this National Monument. Slot Canyons await. Be prepared for heat and to get sunburned.
Trailhead to Tomales Point is located here. Parking gets full by 10am. Bathroom are porta-potties which are not very nice. No running water or trash bins. Pack it in, pack it out.
Go through Bear Gulch Cave to the Reservoir. Peaceful place to relax and enjoy sun. Definitely recommend a detour if you're hiking High Peaks Trail thru Condor Gulch Trail loop.
Keep walking... The highest sand dune is actually not that far... And definitely worth the trip. Hike in the early morning to avoid the heat.  The sunrise here is awesome!
Spectacular museum. General admission is free if you Reserve tickets ahead of time online. Amazing works of art... Mostly pop art. Architecture of building is pretty.
A moderate 1.25 mi hike. Slight rise in elevation with sandstones along the way. The end is a picturesque vista of Las Vegas Strip and Red Rocks. Very popular trail.
This is where most people park and view the Lake... But go around as there are better viewpoints and ample parking and multiple pullouts elsewhere.
Spectacular! First waterfall you see as you enter the campgrounds. Keeps getting even more beautiful as you still through the rest of the trail.
Crowds surround this tree... Take a stroll through the short Congress Trail instead... Better pics, views and perspective of the Giant Forest.
Definitely a great place to stop and stroll. Love how easy this accessible trail is... Has stairs along the cliffs to a nice vantage point.
Iconic structure. During the pandemic, it's gated off... So photo ops are kind of better... Except you can't take a reflection of yourself.
After arriving via boat (Island Packers), the coast line of Santa Cruz Island is beautiful. Surprised how dry and arid the land was.
Island in the Sky and the Rim Walk were my faves... Mesa Arch is crowded with unforgiving photographers trying to catch the sunrise.
Great trail capturing forests, clearings, views of San Francisco and Stinson Beach. Can make it a 7 mile loop or longer...

Very cool! We at first got lost on the way here as it took us a roundabout way through the desert. I eventually found the right spot while looking at photos of the mountain so be aware of that! Be sure to bring plenty of water and supplies as it was very very hot out here in the middle of July. If our car got stuck or had broken down we would have been in a whole heap of trouble. Other than that the petroglyphs are super cool! There are tons of them and all kinds of cool designs as well. This place is not well known and there was only one other family besides us. Very neat little place, especially if trying to avoid the crowds of places like Zion and Bryce.

The crater is amazingly spectacular at any time of day! Haleakala is one of the most beautiful places on Earth in it's utter desolation. It looks like Mars or the surface of the Moon. My favorite is when the clouds roll in through one of the gaps, pictures don't do it justice. Sunsets are also exceptionally gorgeous and on clear days you can spot the Big Island with Mauna Kea looming above the clouds. The plants are crazy cool and if lucky, you may even spot a Nene, a very cool goose found only in Hawai'i. Be sure to bring a jacket, it can get very cold up at the top. Other than that, enjoy the views cause this place is unreal!

Amazing!! My new favorite National Park! Truly spectacular with some really awesome views. The hiking there is also insane with so many cool places to get out of the car. The Grand Wash Narrows were truly awesome and a really neat place to hike. Kept getting flashbacks to my time spent in Buckskin Gulch last year. Definitely take the time to visit this spot. The best part of Capitol Reef was the lack of people, it was really awesome to see such a beautiful place and be able to connect with nature. Definitely the best park out of the Mighty 5. Highly recommended!!

I almost do not want to review this place or give it a one star but I cannot. My wife and I love this place with a passion! We found it on a road trip exploring some of the more remote places in Nevada and fell in love! We love to swim here and just hang out in general. The water is cold but amazingly beautiful to swim in with a floating dock for climbing on and jumping off. The surrounding scenery is amazing. This place is like heaven and very well maintained by the State of Nevada. The entrance fee is only five dollars and trust me, it is money well spent!

I love hiking to the Living Room! Nice easy to moderate trails. Especially for newcomers to Utah this trail can showcase what living and hiking in the mountains is all about. Not too hard and very, very scenic. A lot of cool other areas can be hiked to from here including Red Butte and the summit of Mt. Wire. The mountain that the Living Room is on for those who did not know. Fun Fact: The mountain was named after the man who invented the traffic signal! Anyways, this is a fun trail and mountain to explore! Highly recommended!!

The architecture here is unreal! Super cool to see the high ceilings and beautiful murals depicting Utah history. We were there on a Sunday and got to just explore the entire building from top to bottom with no guided tour. It was amazing to see the paintings and sculptures without interference. Really amazing to learn a famous architect built the capitol and other buildings in SLC as well as buildings in France. The Capitol was a cool way to burn a few hours in a day, definitely worth free!

I really like the Leonardo. I have been there to see the Bodies exhibit (animals) and Mummies. Both were awesome and it gave me goosebumps to be so up close to these amazing displays of biology and history. The rest of the museum is kid oriented but me being 31 I throughly enjoyed the exhibits and even wanted to play, but didn't wanna look weird to everyone else. I am always on the lookout for their next rotating exhibit. This place has given me the chance to see some really amazing stuff!

Really cool place to spend a chilly autumn day with someone you love. My girlfriend and I went to get a pumpkin but we also really enjoyed the wagon ride the scenery was beautiful along with all the fall colors. The maze was pretty cool too. My favorite part was the animals, the mini donkey was absolutely adorable and so were the pigs. All the staff were also super friendly. This is a great place to bring kids!! Definitely recommend for some good ol' fall fun!

Bryce Canyon is absolutely beautiful and well worth the when in southern Utah. The visitor center is pretty standard as far as parks go with an informative display showing you the layout and history of Bryce Canyon. There is also a gift shop with all kinds of trinkets and even some useful gear if you came here totally unprepared. There is also rangers stationed there to help guests with finding anything or about conditions present within the park.

Amazing! The beautiful scenery is unbelievable! It reminds me of a smaller Zion Canyon. The 3 mile hike to get to the falls is pretty easy, the sand is really forgiving on the feet thankfully. The water from the falls is ice cold that it takes your breath away. This is a desert in southern Utah so dress appropriately and be sure to bring plenty of water. Make room for tons of photos too, cause this place is amazingly beautiful!!

Really really cool! The history of the area is amazing! The displays in this little museum are well thought out and the entry fee is very reasonable. I loved learning about the way the natives dealt with the desert and lived in harmony with it. My favorite was the replicas of the adobe homes out behind the museum itself. If you are visiting the Valley of Fire or the surrounding area then I definitely recommend a stop here.

I LOVE THIS PARK!!! I often spend time here, whether it be just riding my bike around the loop or sitting at a table and reading a book. The park is very large and has room for everyone to play. Another activity I love is people watching and boy! Do you get to see the latest and greatest of the odd and eclectic Salt Lakers there. I really do love hanging out this park and recommend it to anyone thinking of visiting.

I did not attend a concert here, but looks like a cool venue. I did visit here though to see the beach and walk out to the Great Salt Lake. Very cool. The architecture and history of this place is awesome. The gift shop is quaint and cute with all kibds of historical photos. They had some neat stuff here, worth a visit even if only just to check out a cool place steeped in history!

This place is soooo cool! Totally worth every dollar of the entry fee! They give you a flashlight and a map, then you are on your own to explore. The caves are super cool and it is fun to learn the history of them. The best part is shutting off the flashlight and just taking in the pure darkness. This place is awesome, and shouldn't be missed on a Road to Hana day trip!

Loved this place!! Very cool museum/ zoo/ nature preserve/ etc. This place has it all. Super neat displays and animal exhibits. Although on the pricey side it was totally worth the money. There's so many cool things to look at, so definitely plan to stay a while. Also, it is totally worth it to pay extra to pet the Manta Rays, they are extraordinarily cute!

Amazing! Best National Park I have ever been too! Mainly because it was crowd free but also because the views were absolutely stunning! Going from the valley floor all the way up to 13,000ft is impressive. It is amazing to overlook the desert floor below you from beautiful and pristine green. Truly is an island in the sky. What a beautiful place to visit!

Super cool piece of history! Found this by accident a few years back while driving to Craters of The Moon NM. It was a really cool stop on the way that I was not expecting. I had no idea that remote Idaho was where nuclear stuff started in the US. If you are interested in this stuff then I highly recommend checking it out!

I loved this place so much. The peace and serenity here is awesome. You do not feel a need to talk or make much noise, just walk around slowly deep in contemplation. It is so beautiful here and I especially loved the big Buddha. I left behind a bracelet as a special offering, in the hopes for good fortune on my travels.

Really really awesome!! This museum was totally awesome, full of history, and free to boot! The historical stuff in the basement is unreal and soooo interesting! We loved the old medical equipment, cooking stuff, and the cash register! It was so cool. If passing through Montpellier I highly recommend this stop!

Really awesome aquarium! I loved the different themes in each area and the animals all looked very healthy and well taken care of. I also felt that 20 bucks per person was pretty reasonable. All the staff was friendly and helpful. All in all my girlfriend and I had an awesome day out at the aquarium together!

Amazingly remote and beautiful! Any part of the Sawtooth National Forest is an amazing place to get away from the crowds and the heat of the summer. There are many sections scattered throughout Idaho and Utah and each one of them is uniquely awesome and beautiful. Sawtooth National Forest never disappoints!

Truly amazing! Made me tear up to see the dinosaur bones preserved in the wall. You can even touch them!! Very awesome! There are also some really cool hikes in the area with some neat petroglyphs. Definitely worth the visit!
Super cool! I've never seen so many sea lions up close and with my own eyes! Very cool to see and experience, especially the sounds that they make. Highly recommended!
Meh....not so much a park as a patch of green with a picnic table. Really pretty views of the island from this neighborhood though!
Closed, but still cool. We peeked into the windows. Looks like a fun place! I will be back one day so no worries!

What a place! As a Texas resident, I've been to the Caverns of Sonora and Natural Bridge Caverns. This place feels bigger than both of those combined.

Be prepared to walk. I would HIGHLY recommend doing the natural entrance (rather than taking the elevator down) and walking downhill for about 45 minutes to an hour. The scenery is totally worth the extra distance. I liked that hike down into the cave better than the Big Room, but lots of people would disagree with me I'm sure.

Wear some grippy shoes (flip flops or sandals might be challenging) and take a jacket or pullover since the cave's interior is about 56F.

I highly recommend this tour. The boat ride is fun and quite gentle, so if you're worried about motion sickness, you should be fine.

The food and the show were great. Our kids were glued to the show and wanted to learn more about the dancers and their masks afterwards. All of the food was amazing and we went back for seconds.

The cruise director took a ton of time to explain everything, tell stories, and answer questions.

This is a great park for relaxing or hiking. The Onion Creek trail is one of my favorites and it's the only one you can get through without getting your feet wet.

The maps don't explain it well, but you need to cross a (quickly) running creek by foot to get to the homestead trails. The crossing doesn't look difficult, but the rocks are VERY slippery. Bring water shoes.

There are lots of places to camp, bike, and picnic.

How can you go wrong with this place?

The scenery is not something I can put into words. There's snow, trees, grass, pristine lakes, elk, moose, chipmunks, camping, good roads, friendly rangers -- it's all good.

We stopped with our kids at Sprague Lake and had a great picnic. A thunderstorm came up suddenly and pelted us with heavy rain and hail. Even with all of that, I'd totally come back.

This art museum has a lot of history and it's one of the most unique examples of architecture that I've seen.  The grounds around the McNay are almost as gorgeous as the art inside.

My wife and I had our engagement photos done here. You can pay a small fee to the museum (via the security guard) and receive a pass to take photos all afternoon.

This is a really special place. My son really enjoys it. It's a great place for kids of all ages, whether they have a disability or not. There is plenty of room to play, walk around, and learn something new. Be sure to take some sunscreen with you since a fair amount of the park is uncovered.

Want a unique place to see nature at work? This is the place. Some of the giant rocks appear to defy physics and there are plenty of places to climb and look around. There are multiple parking lots scattered throughout.

Be sure to stop by the HQ to get a map and plan your route.

Want to do something unique with your kids? Take them here! It's a great way to get them out in nature to see flowers, butterflies, squirrels, and ducks. The grounds are expansive and well labeled.

I really enjoy the Japanese tea garden near the front. It's quiet and peaceful.

We had a great time here. My kids are a little too young to know Smokey, but they enjoyed learning about him and how forest fires affect our world. The outdoor walk is really nice and there's a pretty big playground included. The fee was $5 total for a family of four.

I remember visiting this place as a kid and now I am able to take my kids to see it! They really enjoyed seeing the exhibits on life in space as well as a tram tour to a real working building with astronauts. There was plenty for them to see and experience.

Meteor Crater was really interesting and it's worth seeing. However, there's not a whole lot to see other than that big hole in the ground. The hole is REALLY big, but it was quite hot in the summer time and we got there a little late in the day.

This is one of the most unique art museums I've ever visited. It reminds me a lot of the McNay in San Antonio.

Everything is all hodgepodge but it still feels organized. If you're looking for more formal art, head to the MFA next door.

This is the park HQ and it's the best place for you to ask any questions you have. Three park rangers were folding questions like crazy and they gave us recommendations for our children. The gift shop and restrooms were good as well.

This is a really nice park and my kids enjoy playing here. The playground equipment is nice but it can be challenging for smaller children. There's a ladder that goes up to a third story and I've seen kids fall from that a few times.

This is a beautiful area of Chicago and it has a planetarium, aquarium and the Field Museum. The grounds are nice with playscapes for the kids. The views of the Chicago skyline and Navy Pier are really good from here.

There are plenty of playscapes here for kids of all ages. Some of them even have water features, so be sure to dress in something that can get wet. There is a rock climbing wall and mini golf as well (fee required).
This place is BIG. Be prepared to spend a lot of time here or plan to see it on multiple days. There's every genre of art you can imagine here from lots of different time periods. It's overwhelming!
We stopped here on a long car trip from San Antonio to Denver. There are plenty of places to sit and eat. The playground is in good condition, too. The restrooms could use a lot of work, though.
This place was great! It had quite a few unexpected things in it along with many things I expected to see (like robots). It's a great place for kids that are a little older.
This is a really well maintained park! The beach is easy to drive on and it's only $5 per adult. They have showers and bathrooms available, too.
This is a great park for sports. We've played youth soccer with SAYSAT here on the outfield of the baseball fields. Parking is easy.
A big part of history! The self-guided tour was easy to follow and we learned quite a bit about what made the building famous.
Great park in a great location! The playground equipment is well maintained and there is a big soccer field with goals.
What can I say? This is an awesome park. If the weather is good, you could spend a lot of time here. :)
Tons of history in one small place. Take a trip to the top of the monument. It's totally worth it!
