Let me jump right to the best part of my review - Halloween. Yup, Calico Ghost Town is the most awesome Halloween experience in the High Desert. I know of no other attraction where visitors can dress up (or not), trick or treat (the old fashioned way by knocking on doors vs goingvto a mall or the truckbof a car)(anticipation is a huge part of enjoyment for kids, how do you get that from a mall or opened truck?), have a beer, enjoy a barbeque, shop, dine, ride a train, tour a real haunted mine, explore the hills, the school, the blacksmith shop, a house made from glass bottles, Chinatown, a grave yard and so much more. For $8. With free parking. Seriously you can't even go to a minor league baseball game in Adelanto and not pay at least $5 for parking. Calico is free parking. I a world where one has to pay to park at several public parksbin Los Angeles, free parking at Calico is amazing! Is Calico expensive? No. You can buy a chilli cheese burger for $5, Red Robin is around $8. You can get a craft beer for $6, Casino Morongo a Bud Light Draft for $5.75. A barbeque dinner for under $10! Still too much? Bring your own. Yup no silly restrictions on food or beverages. Calico would rather have you enjoy the day and spend money at the shops or such than worry about a bottled water and a sandwich sneaking in. As far as the rides and attractions go, ride the train first for $4 then purchase a package deal for $7 that covers everything else even panning for gold. $11 covers in all. How much is Disneylands parking? Yeah, Calico isn't Disney. But its a heck of a deal and it's real. Real? Yup, ever been to Primm NV? Years back, before Primm, before Buffalo Bills there was Kactus Kates Casino. It was across from Whiskey Petes. Kate as it turns out made her fortune at Calico by operating the House of Ill Repute. Yup Calico made a lot of people rich in its day. Even the prositutes. And there's a ton more history to Calico. Some well known and someblike Kate no so well known. There's also camping at Calico. Now I like desert camping but I like tents and backpacks. Calico is more geared towards the RVer and off road ATV. If that's your thing then this feature adds to the fun. There's also a few cabins available for rent. But they're stuck smack dab in the middle of the RV park. I think it would have been nicer to spread the campground out some more. Give us tent and cabin campers a chance to get away from the ATVs. But hey, camping in a ghost town! On Halloween! Christmas or, any other day is just too cool. Bring a flashlight!

Let me jump right to the best part of my review - Halloween. Yup, Calico Ghost Town is the most awesome Halloween experience in the High Desert. I know of no other attraction where visitors can dress up (or not), trick or treat (the old fashioned way by knocking on doors vs goingvto a mall or the truckbof a car)(anticipation is a huge part of enjoyment for kids, how do you get that from a mall or opened truck?), have a beer, enjoy a barbeque, shop, dine, ride a train, tour a real haunted mine, explore the hills, the school, the blacksmith shop, a house made from glass bottles, Chinatown, a grave yard and so much more. For $8. With free parking. Seriously you can't even go to a minor league baseball game in Adelanto and not pay at least $5 for parking. Calico is free parking. I a world where one has to pay to park at several public parksbin Los Angeles, free parking at Calico is amazing!
dislikes: Proximity to ATVs for tent campers

reviews_attraction.text:
Let me jump right to the best part of my review - Halloween. Yup, Calico Ghost Town is the most awesome Halloween experience in the High Desert. I know of no other attraction where visitors can dress up (or not), trick or treat (the old fashioned way by knocking on doors vs goingvto a mall or the truckbof a car)(anticipation is a huge part of enjoyment for kids, how do you get that from a mall or opened truck?), have a beer, enjoy a barbeque, shop, dine, ride a train, tour a real haunted mine, explore the hills, the school, the blacksmith shop, a house made from glass bottles, Chinatown, a grave yard and so much more. For $8. With free parking. Seriously you can't even go to a minor league baseball game in Adelanto and not pay at least $5 for parking. Calico is free parking. I a world where one has to pay to park at several public parksbin Los Angeles, free parking at Calico is amazing!

Is Calico expensive? No. You can buy a chilli cheese burger for $5, Red Robin is around $8. You can get a craft beer for $6, Casino Morongo a Bud Light Draft for $5.75. A barbeque dinner for under $10! Still too much? Bring your own. Yup no silly restrictions on food or beverages. Calico would rather have you enjoy the day and spend money at the shops or such than worry about a bottled water and a sandwich sneaking in. As far as the rides and attractions go, ride the train first for $4 then purchase a package deal for $7 that covers everything else even panning for gold. $11 covers in all. How much is Disneylands parking? Yeah, Calico isn't Disney. But its a heck of a deal and it's real.

Real? Yup, ever been to Primm NV? Years back, before Primm,  before Buffalo Bills there was Kactus Kates Casino. It was across from Whiskey Petes. Kate as it turns out made her fortune at Calico by operating the House of Ill Repute. Yup Calico made a lot of people rich in its day. Even the prositutes. And there's a ton more history to Calico. Some well known and someblike Kate no so well known.

There's also camping at Calico. Now I like desert camping but I like tents and backpacks. Calico is more geared towards the RVer and off road ATV. If that's your thing then this feature adds to the fun. There's also a few cabins available for rent. But they're stuck smack dab in the middle of the RV park. I think it would have been nicer to spread the campground out some more. Give us tent and cabin campers a chance to get away from the ATVs. But hey, camping in a ghost town! On Halloween! Christmas or, any other day is just too cool. Bring a flashlight!

This is and has always been a very nice park with lots of lakes to fish, paths to walk ride or skate and plenty of facilities. What it lacks is parking and easy access. The large park is fenced and controlled by it own satellite Sheriff's Station. 30 years ago it was easier to get to and less creepy. What I mean is that I personally find it hard to relax and enjoy myself when I'm being watched for even the smallest infraction. I guess it's a necessity evil in today's world.
Still, it was a nice brief visit. We got lucky and found a parking space. A sherrif was nearby in his patrol car to make sure no one created there own space or popped up with a cooler full of beer. Then we headed off for a hike around the lakes. The many waterfowl are very tame and oddly I observed a goose begging. I don't ever remember seeing any bird perform such a display, weird and again, creepy. It was mid afternoon so as expected anglers weren't bringing them in though not for lack of effort. The paths and bridges were clean and easy to navigate. People were enjoying the park in many ways but we did not see any boating or swimming. I took up conversation with some locals and was told the park is used to facilitate community service for criminal violators. The creep got worse. Would I go back with the granddaughter? Yeah sure. But I'd keep my eyes open. For fishing? Probably not. It wasn't stocked with anything special years ago and being that the lakes are concrete lined it alway felt like fishing in a swimming pool filled with green water. I know better lakes with bigger fish.
likes: Clean and navigable paths and bridges
dislikes: Lack of natural feel in lakes

reviews_attraction.text:
I was fortunate and granted a tour with my spur of the moment visit. I'm glad I researched online before I did visit as it made the information I received from the guides much more anecdotal and interesting. Worth visiting.
When the blacktop road ends you are at the 117 acre property and in addition to the signs you'll see 2 steal post poles. To the right a dirt road decends steeply to the temple about 750 feet away. The road is in very poor condition and I don't recommend it to anything less than a 4 wheel drive. I walked it. I recommend you do too because....
To the left of the poles is another road and even though it's part of the property it should be treated as private property. Father  Juan and others live here. This is the road to the Pillars. Walk it too. Ask Father Juan if its OK to visit. The Pillars are about 1000' down on your left.
There is a hiking trail to and from both sites.  I didn't hike it thru (because I wanted to meet Father Juan so hiked the road) but did inspect parts of it and it transverses through some beautiful forest. I found a wooden bridge (two actually) and stairs to and from the road. In 2003 a fire destroyed much and in some places only foundations remain but the forest seems to have recovered well. The whole site is very interesting with lots to see. Serene and quiet. Alive with forest sounds. Glad I visited. Highly recommended.

Interesting but not much to see because the building and parking lot is fence off with a wire fence and many no trespassing signs. There were people there this Sunday but I don't think they were there to worship. Looked more like a gutting crew with a debris truck parked in front of the open door. We were observed several times but not welcomed in.
More interesting was the old gas station across the way. "Gordons" considering the proximity to Edwards I wonder if it might have belonged to Gordon Cooper. That's a reach I know but, maybe. The stations post war construction, it's detail and signage are very photographic. It also was very accessible although I didn't poke around inside.
I plan to return to both places soon but only after doing a little research online about High Vista and it's history and, on a week day when a bit closer examination of the church won't intrude on either worshippers or a recking crew.

I hiked from the truck stop to the hatchery and along the way discovered a nature trail, spoted 4 deer and crossed a rushing stream before entering the hatchery from above and behind. This gave me a unique experience for my first visit to the site. As I crossed through the abandoned and dry brood tanks to the rear of the hatchery I took many photos, all from varying perspectives. But it wasn't until I came around to the front and saw the pond that the magic really happened. The hatchery was closed due to a lack of a volunteer but I still enjoyed the visit and spoted many large trout in the pond (Polorized sunglasses made that possible) and of at least 2 species. I hiked down the entrance to the hwy to return. Overall about 3.5 miles and a very pleasant hike.

Visited the museum with family via a Groupon while en route to Hoover Dam. The experience lasted about 30 minutes including the self guided walk through and a quick look around the little gift shop after. The museum is interesting and well arranged. Its focus is centered around Toms work and his B movie interests. If you're a fan of Tom, this would be an apex trip. If like we were, having never heard of Tom nor having a huge interest in movie monster makeup work and just dropped in because it looked interesting on Groupon, you'll still like it. So check it out. The man does good work and worked hard putting together a unique experience with the museum. I look forward to seeing this grow.

A very nice museum! A friendly, relaxed atmosphere and curtious staff welcomed us out of the heat and into air conditioning, yeah! There was a wide variety of displays and everything was spotlessly clean which for photography buffs like I means good images. Cameras see all so clean displays - a big plus. Wildlife, lifestyle, science and history. Eye candy for everyone and especially so for the very colorful and well organized mineral display. There as also a photographic tribute to the Blue Cut fire damage and Victims. A live animals section. Mining equipment and much more. We had a good time and will be back. Highly recommended. Take the kids.

It took me a couple of months to visit this site after friends who know I'm always interested in exploring told me about the dinosaurs. I'm glad I did, it's unique and I wish I had a solid history for this site. It seems to me that way back when, the property owner, was trying to build a dinosaur inspired miniature golf course. I'll wager the city or county got on him over permit issues or such and either shut him down or pushed him out and, he just walked away. A lot of work went into what was created and it's a shame that it exist today as is. Neglected, abandoned and vandalized. I'll update this post if and when I learn more.

I hiked this trail dozens of times, it's a definite favorite. South of the Blue Ridge Campground the trail has an excellent night time view of the desert and city lights. The trail intersects Hwy 2 near Lightning Ridge and from nearby Inspiration Point it's supposedly possible to view Catalina Island on a good day. I've been looking for years off and on and have never yet happened chance upon a good day thanks to California smog or weather or? So, don't be discouraged if you don't see the ocean - just keep looking, keep hiking.

My visit was business and I did not explore the park on foot but, had a view of the entire park from above from a nearby construction staging lot. The park looked well designed, clean and had lots of open spaces. The nearby train tracks and occasional train or Metrorail added to the parks ambiance and gave a slight rustic feel to the background. I look forward to visiting and exploring in person on day. 4 out of 5 stars because it wasn't occupied and I'm not sure if it attracts or repells visitors based on its location.

Hiked in from the PCT and stayed overnight in the hike n bike area for just $5. The campground is well kept and clean. Bathrooms the same. One electrical outlet at the end of the bathroom building came in handy for recharging the phone. The site was quite by 10pm. The lake was disappointing. Low levels and no swimming. The whole site currently has an ecoli water problem so water, even from the taps, needs to be filtered and boiled before consumption. Wild turkeys roamed the grounds and a single rattlesnake was present.

Obviously a well planned, well designed community lake whose designers considered many different user types. Child play, fishing, swimming and simple lounging around. On Friday eves a farmers market is hosted in the north parking lot. Everywhere I went all was neat and clean. Nearby there are numerous dining and shopping options. Very much looking forward to returning with my granddaughter. Highly recommended.

Awesome! I've hiked the PCT on day hikes in both directions from this trailhead and as always am thankful I did. The various scenery is fantastic. The trail is very well maintained. There are even parts that are wheelchair accessible. Wild orchids are abundant as is poisen oak - neither should be touched. The last time I hiked nobo it rained gently and the trail came alive! A must hike - get out and walk.

A very pretty pine filled forest that has many small trails. Hikes vary in difficulty from easy to moderate and also in distance from short to several miles long. Wildlife is abundant and within minutes of my first visit I eyeballed several white tail dear by the old railroad service yard. Elk sightings are common too.

Very cool. The large parking lot is flat and level ground and it's big enough to get a tractor trailer in and turned around with ease.  Lots of eye candy for the photographer and a few small trails for the hiker. Geocaching is available too. And for everyone else - spectacular views of the river.

Wow talk about greedy. Imagine trying to charge a customer $25 to park so that the customer can gamble in you casino. That's exactly what Casino Arizona tried to do to me tonight. Fat chance. I left immediately and took my business to Wild Horse Pass.

I've been riding the tramway for decades. Always an awesome experience and the summit is amazing. I think I kinda like riding down a little bit more than the trip going up.  Either way its a lot of fun. Great views, hiking trails and fresh air.

I just touched the edges of the park from the PCT and it was awesome. I am very much looking forward to thru hiking next year and exploring the rest of the trail through the park. From what I've seen so far it's been great!

Loved it. Thousands of shoes to choose from. Bring the family. Prices can't be beat and absolutely no waiting in line. I found 2 identical pair of work boots that fit me great and best of all, they were already broken in!

Discovered accidentally while driving by and enroute to the site old the old Mojave Phone Booth. We stopped briefly to look around and found several good campsites nearby as well as a hiking trail. Very photographic area.

A unique and one of a kind place to visit. The best times to explore and experience are early morning and late afternoon when natures light provides the best effects. An ancient mystery that must be seen to appreciate.

We are losing our open spaces to commercialization every day. Or to put it another way... The great American Consumer is consuming Greater America. Do we really need to keep buying stuff? Do we really need SWAG?
Darwin was an interesting place to visit. Was curious after seeing the documentary. The monument is damaged some. Looks like vandalism by axe.
Friendly enough but I didn't stay long enough to try all amenities. Worth dropping in to take a look around.

Gives a nice view of Gerald Ford and particularly his time as President.  It has a full size representation of both the cabinet room and oval office which can give you a real impression of what they are like.  Also thinking through his history of Eagle Scout to the Navy in WW2 and then Congress to the VP and finally the President is an impressive path to think about.  A great few hours in a very nicely put together museum.   My only comment is that this is, of course, giving a very positive view of his time and certainly spot lights the good parts versus the problems but you can expect that at a presidential museum

Went on Thursday morning and had a half mile walk to the trail from parking which was not so bad.  Definitely people on the trail but not too crowded.  Trail itself is nothing special but the views are great.   The trail has its steep sections and lots of rocks so only go if you are in reasonable shape and take good shoes.   We did not have hiking poles but they would have been nice.  Take lots of water-my wife and I both took a small bottle and ran out and were somewhat parched at the bottom.  Overall a great time and we felt like we accomplished something at the end

Went there on a March day so probably not the most picturesque but enjoyed it a lot.  First of all, Eisenhower is a hero of mine.  To think of someone calming from a small town and doing every thing he did is amazing. His  integrity and balance is also wonderful given recent states of politics.   The museum was nice and gave a good impression.  I would definite recommend a few hours here if you make it to Kansas

Very nice visit.   Between the visitor center and a park service ranger who gave a talk you could get a good feel for the Wright Brothers.  The plan in the visitor center is a replica but if they didn’t tell you it probably would pass inspection.  We are off season and there was still a big crowd so I suspect it is very crowded during summer.

Did the Embudito loop on a Thursday morning at 730.  No problem parking and the trail wasn’t very crowded.  A very nice hike but was definitely some work going up and clambering over some of the rocks coming down in a clockwise direction.  It’s beautiful how you see the mix of the high desert plants with some of the trees and forest

Went there on a Tuesday morning and the park was almost empty.  We did the 4.4 mile historic park hike which was very enjoyable though the trail definitely has some up and down and is rocky.  Make sure to wear sturdy shows.  The mining displays were interesting and made you think about people hauling stones from the holes by hand.

I have been coming to the museum and Greenfield Village for over forty years and visited with my wife on a nice fall day.  I love the combination of learning about and seeing history with an outdoors walk. Every time I am there I learn something new-this time it was that Henry Ford worked for Thomas Edison.  Highly recommend it

Really nice hike though a bit of work going up the right side.   We left at about 10 am on a Monday and the parking lot was about half full.  The trail was not too crowded—we passed about five groups over the distance.  Nice view from the top.  The right side is pretty open so make sure you are good with sunscreen and water

Did the Piedra Lisa trail up to Del Agua.  Great hike with wonderful views but the snow on the rocks coming down made it a bit challenging.  Definitely want to bring some hiking poles (at least for us lesser coordinated people).   Road in was a bit rough but didn’t really have any problems but I would avoid it when wet.

Went there on a Saturday in February and it was great. The rocks are amazing and the hike was nice though it was blocked at the end by snow and ice.  It was interesting to learn about what caused them-it seems like the whole west was built by volcanos, wind and water. Rangers we met were very helpful and friendly

Botanica is a nice arboretum with many good features.  They do a nice job in making it friendly though the line for entrance is long (a tip is if you live in Wichita and go at least twice a year get a membership and you can skip the line).  We just went today and the tulips were great.  Christmas is also nice

Went there in the middle of Covid so just walked the two main trails which are very nice and well marked.   The park itself is fascinating with the different climates and areas within a short distance.   Not sure if we will stop by again but a very nice park and very easy to get to from the highway.

A lot of work and some scrambling but well worth it.   Got there around 8 am and had to park in the second lot but the hike itself did not seem too crowded.  There are definitely some challenging areas on the hike so i would make sure you were hiking shoes or boots.  The view off the top is great

Great trail. Had no problem parking.  The first bit was a bit boring along a dirt road but then it started winding up the mountain.  Nice vistas around every corner.  We saw a few mountain bikes but had no issues.  Had some parts that were a bit steep but not too hard.  View at the end was great.

A must go museum in Detroit.  I knew the basics of Motown but the combination of the actual house and a great tour guide gave us a really good feeling for what Motown really was.  Standing in the studio was a really special moment.  Make sure to book in advance and reserve a time

Great place to hike.  We visited Albuquerque for about a week and did several hikes in the forest. Trails are well marked and easy to find our way around.   The view from the top down into Albuquerque is great.    Most of the hikes we went on were between easy and moderate

A nice place for a walk in the center of Wichita.    Our dog enjoyed it and walking the loop gives a decent walk.  Also enjoyed the picnic shelters.   The loop into the woods was a highlight as it was a hot day and much of the park is pretty open.

Walked the trail fro different directions on two days.    Great place to hike whether you want the easier part on the south or harder on the north.  For us non locals not used to the altitude, bring lots of water. Great park and hiking trails

Went up this with my wife on a Thursday in mid December.  Not crowded at all.  The hike is great but definitely some work going up and our hiking poles came in handy.  Some snow going up but not too bad.  Great views from the top.

Great garden and fantastic place to visit both in the main gardens and the related sculpture garden.  This is really a Western Michigan gem and definitely a place to stop when in the area.  I would plan on at least a half day

Nice initiative by the area.  Food trucks are fun and the two we tried were good-Kind Kravings and Nobel Hawaiian.   Ping pong was also fun.   One wish would be for some more shade.  Gets steamy in the summer
Nice family walk along the river and the statue is quite striking.   Wander up close and you can read about the history and get an understanding of the culture
Great hiking paths and enjoyed seeing the convergence of the rivers.  Nice views from up by the fort.  Remember your mosquito spray.
Really neat area and a nice hike but I have to admit it was hard at times to figure out which were Petroglyphs and what was nature
Great place to see birds, nature, more birds and do some walking.   A very unexpected find in the middle of Kansas farming area

A tribute to local corn,, this building has been around since the late 1800's. While the exterior has undergone a few structural changes, an annual theme portrayed in corn husk and cobs (as well as a few native weeds and plants) is very detailed. The borders are painstakingly pieced together every summer with various dried weeds and plants, while the main image is pieced together in fall with 12 varieties of local, dried half cobs. The picture gallery details the themes through the years. The inside of the building has tributes to corn as well with "corn" pillars, a history of the palace and corn, picture booths and many, many photos - all free! There is a basketball stadium inside which is occupied by a huge store selling corn and some local items - foods, trinkets, jewelry, clothing, decorations etc as well as a store selling varieties of popcorn. A corn cam rounds out the whole place. Definitely an interesting place to visit. You can spend an hour there!
likes: Facilities & Services: Free picture gallery, detailed exhibits
On-site Activities: Photo opportunities, shopping for local items

reviews_attraction.text:
A large park with several entrances to walking trails - some paved, some natural, some boardwalk. Plenty of marshy area with water and shorebirds, though on my latest visit, despite very heavy rains a couple of days prior, the water level was extremely low, plenty of oil slicks and algae resulting in a bit of a stench. Plenty of ducks, geese, herons and killdeer as well as plenty of songbirds.
Sadly, the water by the viewing platform is littered with lures, fishing wire and all sorts of plastic debris. I wonder if this gorgeous-when-alive large specimen died from becoming entangled in the lines. It is the one thing I wish this park would monitor.

Lots of material at the center - a museum with a gray wolf and moose (stuffed), native American artifacts, and a twelve minute film on the local history and the Voyageurs. A very knowledgeable lady at the visitor center gave us lots of information on the park. A small store with books, clothing and souvenirs. The building is large and airy with good light and a few chairs overlooking the lake. Restrooms are clean and well--maintained. There is an outdoor seating area which overlooks the ethnobotanical garden and the lake. Access to the Oberhotlzer trail is at the end of the garden. A very cool bark teepee is a part of the garden.

A long drive through gorgeous landscape. The geology and geological features of this place are amazing. I weren't aware that clambering off trail and onto the rocks/hills etc were totally okay at this park (which is quite unlike any other National Park) and I was unhappy that people were doing this. They have a visitors center at just one end of the park, so you won't know until you get there! Lots of bison, deer (pronghorn and mule), prairie dogs, bighorn sheep, cliff swallows and other birds and animals to be found all over the park. The spur road off the west entrance is a must do short drive.

So beautiful, we looped through it twice in one day! Amazing volcanic debris in varying sizes, some places where you can walk/hike/climb though them and the scenery is breathtaking. Sadly, hikers damages part of the trail and it's been since closed. Awe-inspiring to see the area that is covered by lava flow and eruption. Erupted in around 1065 AD. Though not active itself, it's in an area with potential activity. It feeds into the Coconino National Forest. Expect to spend half a day to drive though both with a couple of short hikes, or a full day covering many more of the paths/hikes.

Plenty of parking, several of herds of bison across the park, walking trails all over the place, pull-outs to see nature in all its glory, 3 tours of the caves and free entrance to the park! If you want to do one of the tours, try to get in early as the longer tours happen earlier in the day and sell out pretty fast. The 75 minute boxwork lattice tour has about 8 tours timings and we took one around 6 pm. The others were all done or sold out by the time we got to the park around 3 pm. You can spend many hours just walking and watching wildlife in this park.

A series of small waterfalls, meandering river, lots and lost of observation points at various levels, plenty of small wildlife, several parking lots, an observation tower, a walking bridge, a charming cafe with outdoor seating and homemade icecream, pre packed salad/sandwiches and drinks. Many buildings are made of the local, pretty red and pink Sioux Falls quartzite.  What's not to like? You can easily spend a half day lazing about and enjoying yourself just looking at the birds and water. Definitely a must visit.

A small visitors center with loads of information and a couple of very knowledgeable rangers behind the desk. They also have some native American artists working on the pipestone to make items that are sold in the attached gift store. The bridge across the 3/4 mile looping trail was out as some boulders had shifted and hit the bridge, so we were able to complete just half the loop. The trail is a paved pathway that traverses a gorgeous, green area with the water criss-crossing the trail several times.

Walked from the wharf where we had parked...a mile or more to the monument. Pretty walk. But, you can park and get one free ticket in their paid parking lot. 60 or so stair steps and 100+ ramps of walking will get you to the top for spectacular views and lovely breeze. Interesting information about cities in the state on the inside to bolster you as you walk. Little windowed on each floor have a rushing breeze to cool you off as you walk up an otherwise warm inside tower in summer. Totally worth it.

We looked around the outside, took some photos, saw the outside of her house (where she was born and which was updated to look like it did while she was living in it). There are several cutouts from "The Wizard of Oz" to take photos with. There is $10 pp museum which has a Children's section, a tour of the house an a view.of a large number of dolls from her films. The bathrooms have a set of tiny, useable toilets for children labelled Munchkin. :)
likes: Facilities & Services: Children's section, Munchkin-themed bathrooms
On-site Activities: Photo opportunities, Museum tour

reviews_attraction.text: Swamps, boardwalks, trees, grasses, loads of birds (anhinga, herons, ibis, ducks and geese, owls and other raptors, and songbirds galore), gators, otter, beaver, etc. The boardwalks are fabulous though places are hard to find for a first timer despite the map. You can spend all day and then some! Make sure to bring plenty of water, sunscreen, bug spray, hats and a camera as you walk and look at nature in all her glory!

Beautiful monument, has a combination of steps (about 60) and ramps to climb to the top. Strong breeze in the doorway and on each level at the windows. Town inscriptions along the way help you forget the climb as you get distracted while climbing. Gorgeous view from the top with some seating and coin operated distance-viewing scopes. Museum and gift shop below. One free ticket with paid parking in the parking lot.

Plenty of places to view the falls - the small lake below, at the mid-level where there are hiking trails and from a viewing platform looking down into the falls. There are several trails all over the park, a visitor center and gift shop at the base, a gift shop in a Lodge at the top, and a hike to a hike-in--only overnight Inn. Great place to visit in all seasons

A crowded park as everyone seems to want to see manatees! The line to get into the park was at least 60 cars deep by noon. Over 100 manatees are visible and people walk along the water in the boardwalk and viewing decks to see them. You need time and patience to see more than dark shapes under the water. There is a boat ride available.

A park that is larger than it seems when you drive in. Lots of parking. Dog park up front. Various sports fields, walking trails, pond with many red eared sliders and mud turtles, an outdoor amphitheatre and a mew memorial wall. Quite busy for a weekday, but you don't really run into people.

A fabulous place to watch the sunset over the water. Lots of parking, a boat ramp, a little pier to sit on and picnic or watch the water and sunset, mangroves providing some shade over the pier. You can also walk along the strip of land and watch birds and enjoy the water bodies.

Three waterfalls, intermittent steps. Two falls on one part of the Baptism River a few hours hike away. A more woodland 3/4 mile hike about 30 minutes from the visitors center along the river. Lerge visitors center with a small gift store.

Stagnant water feature with a fountain, picnic benches under concrete gazebos, a short walking trail that doesn't seem to go around the lake, not particularly busy. I think it is more a green space by a school than a park per se.

Parking is a fair distance from the boardwalk, but the sidewalks leading to the boardwalk are tree covered and wide. Fairly busy, plenty of picnic tables, a few birds and some grassy areas along the water.
Spectacular hiking area. Carry plenty of water and a sun hat. Hike into the canyon on a path with many steps/stairs to see the beautiful canyon used as homes by natives in the past.
Large park with a museum and a coffee shop. Great place to sit down and have a picnic lunch by the iconic bear. A must-see photo op location in International Falls, MN
Fun, long walk. Best in day time. Has an upper and lower level with frequent connections from top to bottom. Good views, nice ice cream and novelty shop at one end.
Gorgeous little museum that houses a large collection of artifacts. Some unusual pieces, good information and an interesting live demonstration of glass blowing.
Nice view though you have to pay for parking in a large private lot. Remember thinking it was expensive for the time you spend looking at the view.
A pleasant trail with plenty of cactus and small creatures to see. Great in cool weather, not so great in the heat of summer.

Obviously this is a cool venue for music however this review is focused on the tourist trap non-concert aspect of Red Rocks.  First let me say the trails gets crowded with tourists, hikers and runners.  Second the views at RR are just OK.  Of course the views that are to be had are a bit special due to the red Rock formations but driving a few more minutes into the front range will net some pretty nice views both east and west.  Third, if you are inclined to check out the cool concert venue since it's open to the public you will be over run by a spandex army of exercise culture people people.  The place is covered with stair runners, yoga groups, cross-fitters, MMA/Kickboxing groups, walking groups and more.  Many of which are lead by obnoxious coaches yelling at their struggling students.  Add in the 12 different radios and you'll be motivated to get out of there pretty fast.  Finally, if you really want to see red Rock then drive down to the Garden of the Gods during a week day.

This is a large park near the busy retail area (shops, trinkets, ice cream, dinner, lunch, etc.) of Lake St. and Oak Park Ave..  The main area is a large lawn for frisbee, picnics, gathers, and outdoor concerts in summer.  The send area at the center is a large WWI statue with many benches for relaxing.  The third area is the tennis courts.  Forth and finally is the newly updated small tot park which has the typical features including a sand box.  This park can be quite busy on nice summer weekend.

West Fork of Oak Creek Trail No. 108 is a great summer hike if you want a break from Sedona sunshine.  Parking is $10.  Figure 6 or 7 miles round trip from the parking lot if you go all the way to the narrow water pools.  It is not a fast hike as there are many rock steps through the creek, photo views and other hikers that will slow you down.  Much of this hike is under the canopy of cotton wood, sycamore, maple and some evergreen.

When visiting from Chicago my brother usually takes us here.  Great place for outdoor Adventurers of all kinds.  Hiking, mountain biking, cyclocross for everyone.  We've rode seriously gnarly mountain bike trails, kid friendly trails and done nice family hikes with littles ones.  Something for everyone here.

Awesome park for families.   Playground, workout area, picnic pavilion, sports fields, crushed limestone trail.  The sun sets over the distant mountains also.  The creek is always a summer favorite for wading and splashing around in what is typically shallow water but it does flood sometimes.

What an amazing family farm.  We went on a slow Sunday and there were no lines.  Our 7 year old did the tractor driving school and loved it.  I've been to a lot of family farms and no one else let's kids drive (with instructor) their real tractor!

Amazing little oasis considering it's in the middle of the Quad Cities.  Well maintained mountain bike trails.  Find a map online if you don't know your way.  It's small but the trail layout is very good and they use every inch of the island.

Dunes, beaches, hiking and nature center.  All of which is great for an escape from the city.  The bad news is your still in view if the industrial wasteland that is the majority of the western shore of Indiana.

This is the top spot to take kids in the cold season so they can run around, learn about nature, and occupy patents as well.  Park in the lot or risk your car being broken into as this area is pretty ghetto.

Cute little nature center for families with small kids.  Great destination for a bike ride as the nature center is on the Fox River Bike Trail.  There is a picnic grove and some very short hiking trails.

Great beach with restrooms, showers, concessions, playground, splash pad and clean sand.  The bad news is it's always busy!  Parking cost in 2017 is $6 for Berrien County resident and $12 out of county.
Nice visitors center with a gift shop and museum type exhibits.  The view off the balcony is great.  Do not go on holidays, nice weekends or anytime in the summer as crowds are insane here.
Something for everyone at Glennwood Hot Springs.  There's a hot pool, warm pool and a new kids area with slides and tube run.  This is a great place for families with kids ages 3 to 12.
Fantastic hiking location for families with kids.  Ladders, canyons, creeks, rock throwing, creek wading.... It has it all.  Avoid peak weekends as the place gets very, very crowded.
Amazing new of the valley to the north.  Get there early as this is a very popular hiking/biking location.   Spend a few hours to hike up the side of bell rock for an amazing view.
We hiked the Rainbow Falls Trail with our family and had a great time.  This is a great trail for kids 6 yes and older.  If you hike to all three falls figure 4 miles round-trip.
Nice and quite park.  There's hardly anyone ever there except when there are baseball games going on.  They have 5 baseball fields spread out between Mills and Walnut streets.
Great campground for the Park County area.  Much larger than any of the others.  Try to get a spot near the water if you have kids as there are some great woods to explore.
Nice park with several playgrounds, open space, large pond and a running/walking path around the Waters edge.  Only negative is that it's very close to 55th street.
Great place to take the kids for a quick walk if you can't make it to the mountains.  Throwing and collecting rocks along the river is always a good time.
Small but great place to stop in after a hike to cool of in the summer or warm up in the winter.  My kids love it in there.  Best for kids under 10.
Great place to visit.  Great dune trails.  Avoid at all costs on busy weekends though.  Go all the way to the north lot for the quietest area.
Very nice garden park.  Avoid weekends and holidays if you can.  Great place for kids as long as they enjoy long walks.
Typical cookie cutter stadium.  Eat before you get to the game because you will be raped for drinks and food.
Great trailhead to get you into some great trails.  Not a lot of room for parking so get there early.

20200106- Arrive in the early afternoon, register, drive to campsite #2 and set up. At sunset, I walk down to the waterfront and enjoy an amazing show of color at sunset with a double parhelion.

20171228- First time here for overnighting, but did stop last year on my December drive down from League City and visit the bird blind, CCC structures, and check for the cost for camping.
The ranger told me that there was only three sites with electricity left.
I said that it is probably due to Goose Island state park being closed from hurricane Harvey damage and she shook her head yes.
The campsite has a hot shower but it is one hundred plus yards away. See photo showing the rear lift gate of my blue van.

Closed for building new water treatment plant. May 2018 through Spring 2019.

The sign at the entrance to the beach trail says that the majority of the park will be closed during construction.
The beach, waterfront trail, lagoon, and ballfields will remain open.

However, what has been closed permanently is the shower house, the RV sewer dump, the RV camping w/ electric and water hookups, and the tent camping areas with water.
This part of the park  will be sorely missed.

The sign also says that the park will have several improvement including a splash park, new bathrooms, new kitchen, basketball an pickleball courts, improved landscaping and lawn areas, and a public plaza for community events.

Why is the water Green? I always had this question but could never learn the answer until I came to this overlook and read the answer on a info-board located at this beautiful vista point.
It seems that the unique, intense turquoise hue of the water in this lake is caused by a powder that is suspended in the lake water.
The powder comes from the surrounding mountains covered in glaciers. The glaciers grind rocks into a fine powder, called glacial flour, which is carried down steam in the creeks and rivers to the lakes below and because it is so fine a powder, it stays suspended in the lake, giving the water its brilliant color.

I told the host that "this is the nicest visitor center that I have ever stopped at" and I meant it sincerely. There were many things that made an impression on me, but the one thing that I liked most of all was the compacted dirt walls throughout the building.
Too, the host asked me which way I was driving and when I told her west, she suggested that if I like snow, I should take the Snowy Range highway. She said that it was open because she drove it last weekend.
Wow, I thought, a superior center and a very informative host, what else could you ask for.

Free. I like free

When visiting, the tour guide was with a group so I just followed the painted lines through the center.
In all my days in school, I had never herd about a Breeder Reactor before. However, this examination of EBR-1 helped me to see how nuclear power got it's beginning.
Wow, and to be the first to light a string of light bulbs with electricity generated from a radioactive core, well, I am impressed.

20180529
Fairy Falls trail is now open. I was just there.
Recently, when I looked on line at the location, it was marked permanently closed.
This is absurd because it is a trail in a national park. The road access was closed for maintenance, repair, and enlarging the parking lot, but that is complete now.
This is a must see experience,  at least going to the grand prismatic springs viewpoint.

20181003 - This visitors center is new to me. The last time that I came to this park for a visit, the visitors center was located in the round building at Far View. It was called the Far View Visitors Center. However, that location has been, from what I understand, permanently closed.

20181003 - This is not my first visit here but since it has been such a long time, I choose to stop today and take a few photos.
I think this is one of the best all time gift shops in the west, they even have a bumper sticker for me to add to my collection on my van.

Great place to overnight and it is free.
20190119 - Today, I stop in here to see if Robert is camping here this year.
I find him in the very same space that he has been in for several years. We talk for a while and then I leave for  places upriver.

20180925-
This is an amazing site to see.
The ancients had build a real home for themselves, despite the harsh environment.
Still, when conditions grew worse, they knew when it was time to abandon there home in search of a better one.

20180515 - Arrived in the afternoon and it was closed due to high water in the Gardiner river.
The snow melt is still causing the river to reach the top of it's banks.
So, with the river so high, it would be dangerous to try to soak.

Before arriving at the Quapaw, I looked online and found that it was open. I then dove over two hundred miles.
When I got there, the pools were closed for their annual cleaning. I wish they could have said something on the website.

This site is totally amazing, one of the best I have ever seen. Too, the seep spring in this cliff dwelling was some fifty feet long.
The tour today was guided by Kaily and I ony rate her tour as a 3.5.
Photos will be added later.

I love this wonderful display of indigenous people, especially the beautiful leather and bead designs. I have stopped here on three occasions in the past and can never get enough of the stories of this great people.

20101020 - On a journey down the west coast, I stop here see the fort and light house. I am impressed that the bunker has been preserved an has displays inside. Most WWII bunkers are dark, damp cave like tunnels.

20171015  - One of the many national parks that I have previously visited. Stop here today to change out of my suit after the meeting and talk to several of the people who have stopped to visit the battlefield.

20150508 - Arriving on a Friday and expecting somewhat of a crowd, I find this campground open but completely empty. Except for one couple at the spring, I believe that I am the only one here this weekend.

20180921 -
Returning to Cliff Palace for my second time to take the tour. The last time was in September 2009.
Superb example of the Anasazi cliff dwelling.
Photo will be added later.
I grew up about ten miles from here. In fact, I would walk here from my home in Pasadena when I was in the Boy Scouts so that I could achieve a twenty mile hike for one of my badges.

20180202 - I am really enjoying these Texas state parks, the one is $15.00 to overnight and has all the amenities including WiFi and bird blinds.
I will add photos later.
20180322 - Stop at the visitors center on my drive north. The clerks even check the weather for me which helps me decide to drive ahead of the winter storm
20171019 - One of the best preserved mounds I have seen in the southeast. I have been traveling the Natchez Trace and exploring the Ancient mound builders.
20210317 - Great state park with the best shower  in the northwest of Texas. Very clean and also has hot water. I will come here again!
This place is way too expensive for this wayƒarer. I am allowed to go inside to the gift shop, but even here the prices are high.
I have been watching this bridge for many years and now use it as a mile marker for when I travel the I-5 corridor.

Wow. My wife and I decided to go to Santa Fe, NM for our anniversary trip based off of this place. We had no idea it was also Spring Break, so this place was packed. We went the next day and stood in line before the place opened and we're the fifth people in line.

This place is so unique and wierd and cool and just plain FUN. It's great to see artists and production people teaming up to create an utterly amazing experience.

My favorite art installation was actually on the way to the bathroom. As you walk towards the restrooms, put on your glasses (purchased for one dollar at the front) and stare at the hallway wall. The art piece by Eli Chong really creates an illusion with certain colors, partnered with the glasses, and creates depth. He really brought the wall to life!

Go check out this place. I just recommend you go early in the morning before the crowd. Also, there is some sort of "story" behind the scene they created. I was confused and asked the staff member for help. He told me "to look at the papers on the table" and went back to watching YouTube on his phone. That was only disappointment. Other than that, I will still give this place five stars.

There is a reason why this is one of the premiere national parks in the United States. The trails are well maintained, the views are spectacular, and the services offered are over the top. You won't be disappointed in taking time out if your busy lives to just unwind for a bit.

Make sure you bring water and start hiking on a full stomach. You are going to burn those calories!

My wife and I hiked about 12 miles and that was plenty for us. We underestimated the elevation and we were exhausted by the end of the day. It was worth it, though!

Wow. I "heard" (pun intended) that the Heard Natural Science Museum in McKinney was a cool spot for both kids and adults. My wife and I went for the Christmas lights in December and we were pleasantly surprised.

It was awesome! The outside lights were cool, but are definitely geared for kids. It was cool that they had a live concert at well for the kids.

Now, the inside of the museum was also cool. The natural history part was entertaining and educational. I will be back.

San Antonio has a unique landmark called the River Walk. Tourists came start at one end of the below ground man made river and meander their way through the city. It's a cool place to take the family. (Make sure your kids don't fall in!)

During the hot summers off San Antonio, this is a nice place to escape the heat.

There are shops, restaraunts, a night club (piano bar), bars, and even a mall along the route. If you have a few hours, go check it out!

Well, if you're looking for a cool place to go for a photoshoot.... Every one else will be there as well. Wedding photos (which I was a part of), high school senior photos, quinceneras, couples, etc. This is a cool atmosphere for photos. They have gondolas rides as well. Aside from that, there is really nothing open down here.

It's a cool spot to hang out and take photos before you go to a bar and drink with friends nearby at the Toyota Music Factory.

This is truly the most unique and well executed haunted house I have ever been to. Lucky for me, it's open year around and specializes in holiday haunts. They have everything from Valentine's Day haunts to Christmas haunts and everything in between.

The production is top notch. All of the masks are made in house. The costumes are also made in house.

The actors are great and really know their craft.

I will be back year after year.

First let me say that I am not a baseball fan at all.  However, I was invited to watch a game for $10 and I thought, "Why not?"  I had a great time watching the Texas Rangers.  I could not watch a baseball game on TV because it is too slow paced and boring for me.  However, it was a nice stadium and I enjoyed myself.  Food was cheap and the drinks were cheap, too.  Going to a game is a nice and cheap way to take the family out.

The Arkansas Alligator Farm is a crazy cool place to visit. My wife and I went and the place was not crowded at all. When you think of Arkansas, you would never think about reptiles, birds, big cats, and spooky critters... Well. This place has them all!

You can feed the birds. They will let you hold a live alligator for a small fee.

The staff is friendly and will educate you and your family.

Go see this hidden gem.

The Oakbrook Park playground is great. My wife and I walk the trails around the park all of the time and we see people playing on the basketball courts and kids playing on the playground equipment. The park has a huge green space and a cool walking trail that walks behind a neighborhood.

When my nieces and nephews come over to our house, we always take a walk to this park.

Get out and enjoy the parks of Frisco.

This is a very unique park in the heart of downtown Fort Worth. It's a bit smaller than I remember as a kid. However, there are a few different pools that you can visit. My wife and I took about 30 minutes to walk to whole park. If you have kids, I say you could walk the whole park in an hour.

The rocks are also very slippery. Be careful with younger Ida and watch them closely.

Very cool architecture in the heart of downtown. Not only is this a cool structure, it's actually functional. We left our hotel, we crossed the highway, and we went to the local shopping areas.

This is a good way to cross the highway safely. Watch out for people on bikes, though. They think they have the right of way.

For a county park, this park is impressive. We setup for an event and we had plenty of space. There were food vendors, live bands, corn hole tournaments, and a playground for the kids.

This is a great place to have a birthday party or any celebration.

Make sure you call ahead and schedule your event with the city.

History lesson of the day: The Bridge of the Gods is a cantilever toll bridge that was built in the mid 30's. Indian legend says the natural bridge was cast into the river by Tyhee Sahale (God) when the two sons Wyeast (Mt. Hood) & Klickitat (Mt. Adams) quarreled over Loo-Wit (Mt. St. Helens).

This is a nice place to go for a day to get out of the city.  I got lost on one of the trails because the trail was flooded.  The path was not clearly marked, but I made my own path through the woods.  The beach area was nice.  Lots of kids and lots of trails for everyone.  I would go back.

I'm not a religious person, but this a good piece of architecture. It was crowded with tourists, so I spent about 10 minutes there. The parking lot was horribly packed. While you're up there, check out the huge mansion next door. I think Nicolas Cage used to live there.

First things first... $30 to park?!?!  Are you crazy?  Next, the food is OUTRAGEOUSLY expensive at $12 a small pizza.  That being said, prepare to spend a lot of money.  Now, the track is nice and is nicely maintained.  But, the high prices make me not want to go back.

I went here with a friend when the facilities just opened for the season. There wasn't a lot of flowers b/c of the recent snow. The staff gave us half off our admission and gave us a personal tour that included a close of with the birds of prey! Great place for kids.

I've lived by this park my entire life. When I was a kid, I used to be here every day. The soccer fields are surrounded by a locked fence because people trashed the fields. They have a small plastic playground for kids. There are also four softball fields.

You need to check out this place. Get outside and catch some sunshine.

My pregnant wife and I went during August Days. Admission was cheap. It was super hot. We had a blast!!!

We will definitely be back.
This is the perfect location for a skate park. The weather is perfect here and there are all types of skaters at this park. You have rollerbladers, skate boarders, scooters, etc. Everyone gets along.
Great location. This is where you go to get your tickets for Alcatraz. My suggestion is to get them online and print them before you go. There were really long lines.
Had a great time there this weekend.  We swam around one of the bends and gained access to a private beach.  Was really windy, but the weather was nice.
Definitely not my favorite park in Phoenix, but you have to go here at least once. Decent views of the city. Go early in the morning.
What a cool National Park! Gorgeous views. Make sure you bring a jacket as it gets windy! A must visit!
Very cool place to stop on a road trip.  You can learn a little history and also stretch your legs.

This is a great state park. I came here and was immensely satisfied with my experience. I drove here and stayed the night at the park’s hotel, which was quite nice. I drove up to the hotel, walked into the lobby by, which had lots of comfy arm chairs and a couple tables, and checked in at the front desk. After I checked in, I went up to my room on the second floor. When I got there, I opened the door to my room to be greeted by a nice, clean bathroom and two comfy beds. After I put my bags down in my room, I walked down to the hotel lobby and went in the park’s gift shop, which is located in the hotel. I looked through the store’s products but I didn’t buy anything. After I went through the gift shop, I left the hotel and went to the Maumee Boardwalk Trail, which is a trail that takes in a loop through some on marshes. I walked along the trail (which is a boardwalk due to the fact that the ground is covered in water so you can’t build a trail there) and saw lots of birds. There was marshy water everywhere, and I saw birds, frogs, and storks. After walking along the entire boardwalk trail, which was nice and well maintained, I walked in front of the hotel alongside the lake. After walking alongside the lake for a while, I got to the beach, where I turned around and headed back for the hotel. I would’ve liked to swim in Lake Erie, but I didn’t bring my swimsuit with me. When I went back to the hotel, I sat down in the lobby and worked on a jigsaw puzzle for a bit. When it came time to have dinner, I quit working on the jigsaw puzzle and went to the lodge’s restaurant. When I was at the restaurant, I was seated by a hostess and I ordered a lemonade with no ice from the waitress serving me. The waitress brought me my lemonade soon after I ordered it, and it tasted quite good. When my lemonade came, I ordered some french fries. After I finished my lemonade, my french fries came to me soon after. They tasted quite good, which I liked. After I finished eating my french fries, I left the restaurant and went back to my room, where I fell asleep. The next morning, I woke up, ate breakfast, checked out of the hotel, hiked along the Maumee Boardwalk Trail, and left the state park, satisfied with my experience. I gave this state park five stars because it has a nice lodge and nice hiking trails.

This is a great National Monument. I went here and was immensely satisfied with my experience. I drove into here from the park’s south side, which was quite scenic. The road goes down a hill as it enters the park, so you can see a large, broad, expansive vista of orange ground, which is very scenic. You could see that the terrain in front of you is flat, but there is a sharp, steep decline in the distance. I thought that was the Grand Canyon when I saw it, but I don’t know for sure. After I drove down the hill I went to the park’s visitor center. I parked in front of the visitor center and walked in, where I looked at the park’s exhibits. The visitor center has many exhibits about the history of Native Americans and pueblos in the area. After I looked at the exhibits, I left the visitor center and walked along the park’s sidewalk to the main pueblo in the park (I forgot what it was called). It was very big, orange, and had many rooms. The sidewalk went right by the entire pueblo, so you could easily observe the interior. You’re not able to go into the pueblo. After I looked at the pueblo, I walked to the ball court past the pueblo. I went inside it and it was shaped a large, round, flat circle. After I walked around the ball court, which had a dirt floor, I walked pack to my car and drove to another pueblo. It was smaller, only having a couple of rooms, but I was able to walk inside. I walked inside it and looked around before climbing to the top room. The doorways were very short, so I had to bend down to go through each room. After I finished exploring that pueblo,  I got back in my car and left the park, satisfied so with my experience. I gave this National Monument five stars because it has very nice and well preserved pueblos.

These are some nice caverns. I went here on a cave tour and was satisfied with my experience. I parked at the cave’s parking lot and walked into the building by the parking lot. I bought my ticket for the tour in the building and waited for it to start. While I was waiting, I looked around the cave’s gift shop, which had some geodes and other rocks for sale. Once the tour started, the tour group I was in went into the cave. The cave was pretty level, not having many ascents or descents. The cave had many stalactites and stalagmites, which I thought was very cool. The tour guide knew a lot about the cave, and he walked us through the whole cave. We went through a section of the cave which had lots of names inscribed on the cave’s walls. This is because tourists from the late 1800s wrote their names on rock while visiting the cave. The names were very well preserved and still legible, which surprised me. After we went through that part of the cave we passed by more stalactites and stalagmites until we got back to the cave’s gift shop, where the tour started. After the tour ended at the gift shop, I left the gift shop and walked back to my car. I drove away from the cave’s, satisfied with my experience. I gave this cave five stars because it’s a nice cave, having many stalactites and stalagmites. There’s also a large playground near the cave, but I didn’t go play on it. There were lots of large hills in the area, which surprised me. I thought this area of Ohio was completely flat, but upon doing further research, I found out that the highest elevated point in Ohio is in the area.

This is a nice National Historical Park. I went here and was satisfied with my experience. I drove into here and parked by the temporary visitor center, because the permanent one was closed. I walked up to the visitor center and grabbed a map of the park because I wasn’t able to go I side. Once I grabbed a map, I went on the auto tour of the park. The tour is a road that goes through the park past historical places. I went in the tour and stopped boat the first stop, which had a couple log cabins and a field where soldiers in the Continental Army trained. After I stopped there I drove over a covered bridge before going to Washington’s headquarters. That area had his headquarters along with a log cabin and a couple other buildings. There’s a trail that goes from that area down to the Valley Forge Creek and Schuylkill River, which is pretty nice. I walked along the trail, which was good. After I did that, I got back in my car and drove away, satisfied with my experience. I gave this National Historical Park five stars because it has lots of cool, historical things. There’s also a lot of open land so you can lounge and picnic here.

This is a great National Recreation Area. I went here and was immensely satisfied with my experience. I drove here along the north side of the Curecanti Reservoir from Gunnison, which was quite scenic. While I was driving, I turned left off of US 50 onto a road that took me to the reservoir itself. The reservoir was lower than usual, so I had to drive down to the reservoir over a rocky, dirt plain that’s normally the lakebed. I got to the reservoir and walked around for a while, admiring the view. One thing that caught my eye was that there was a boat ramp across from me at the south end of the reservoir, but it was 6 feet above the water according to my estimations. After walking around the reservoir for a while, I drove back up to the main road and on to the visitor center. I got to the visitor center but it was unfortunately closed due to construction. Since it was closed, I kept on driving along the US 50 to Montrose, thus leaving the park. I gave this park five stars because it has nice scenery and you could launch your boat there when the water level’s high enough, which is cool.
likes: Boat launching (when water level is high)

reviews_attraction.text: This is a great visitor center located at the upper end of Bryce Canyon National Park, being right by the park’s scenic road. I came here before going to the rest of Bryce Canyon, and was very satisfied with my experience. I parked at the visitor center’s parking lot, which was very well maintained but quite full. I walked past the two very large solar panels that moved with the sunlight throughout the day and made my way to the visitor center. I walked in and looked at the relief map of the park they had inside. It gave me a very good sense of where I was and where all of the park’s trails went. After looking at that, I briefly perused the gift shop and glanced at the visitor center’s exhibits, which I thought were quite nice. After that, I left the visitor center and went through the rest of the park before going to Ruby’s Inn to spend the night.

This is a nice science museum. I went here and was satisfied with my experience. I parked in the science museum’s parking garage and went up to the museum. I paid the admissions fee at the admissions desk and went through the exhibits of the museum. There was an exhibit about sea life and the ocean, which was pretty good. There was also a physics exhibit , which was pretty good as well. In the second floor of the museum was a space exhibit, and an exhibit about the human body. After I went through the museum’s exhibits, I went down to the museum’s food court on the first floor. I got some pizza nd sat down at a table and ate it. The pizza tasted okay and I left the museum after I ate it, satisfied with my experience. I gave this science museum five stars because it has nice exhibits.

This is a great show. I went here while I was at Hollywood Studios and was immensely satisfied with my experience. This show is located at a large amphitheater with lots of seating. I walked in here to watch the show and sat in one of the seats at the amphitheater, which had an average level of comfiness. Soon after I sat down the show started. It had the soundtrack of Fantasia and several actors who were dancing. There were also large water displays like that of the Bellagio water fountain in Las Vegas. After I watched the show, which was very good, I left, satisfied with my experience. I gave this show five stars because it has good special effects and large water displays. The sound system in the amphitheater is also of high quality, so the music sounds exquisite.

This is a nice art museum. I went here while I was in Toledo and was satisfied with my experience. I drove here and parked in the museum’s parking lot, which was well maintained. I walked into the art museum and bought a ticket from the admissions desk at the entrance. This museum has nothing but glass sculptures. Glass sculptures are made by blasting a block of glass into the shape of what you’re trying to make, which looks pretty hard. I walked through the museum, which had lots of glass art such as bowls, vases, and random glass shapes. After walking through the museum, I left, satisfied with my experience. I gave this museum five stars because it has lots of nice glass art. Even the museum building is made entirely of glass.

This is a nice monument. I went here while visiting Gettysburg National Military Park and was satisfied with my experience. I walked around this monument and looked at the names of the soldiers inscribed on the walls of the monument. After I did that, I went up the stairs of the monument. This monument has lots of statues and a large one on top, which is pretty nice. There’s a staircase that goes inside one of the monument’s columns up to the top. I got to the top and looked around at the view, where I which was pretty nice. From here, I saw views of the surrounding farmland and hills in the distance. After I looked at the view for a while, I went back to the ground and left the monument, satisfied with my experience.

This is a great trailhead. I walked along the Grand Wash Trail to get here, and it was quite easy to find. The trailhead has a very nice sign showing the direction of the Cassidy Arch Trail and the distance of the trail, which is 1.7 miles. The letters were beige and in a very nice font. The actual sign itself was shaped like an ordinary signpost that you would see in a cartoon and brown, which contrasted quite nicely with the beige of the letters. I hiked up the trail to Cassidy Arch, which was also pretty nice. After that, I hiked back down and left, satisfied with my experience.

This is a very nice park conveniently located at the intersection of Euclid Ave, Superior Ave, Ontario St, and Detroit Ave. It has benches tables, greenery, a nice monument, and a restaurant. You can see the BP Building, Key Tower, and Terminal Tower, which all look really nice. It’s conveniently right by the Tower City Center, where you can go shopping and take the metro to University Circle and the airport. The chairs are pretty comfortable and the tables are quite nice. I gave this place five stars because it’s a very nice park.

This is a nice animal exhibit attraction area. I went here while I was in Vegas and was satisfied with my experience. I walked in here and went to the dolphin pool, where I saw some dolphins. After I went there I walked around the tiger area, where I saw elephants and tigers. Once I saw them, I left because I went through everything here, satisfied with my experience. I gave this animal exhibit attraction area five stars because it’s cool to see a bunch of dolphins swim right by you.

This is a great state park with some very nice scenery. I went here while driving to Capitol Reef National Park and was very satisfied with my experience. I drove in and parked along the side of the road and hiked around some of the goblins. After doing that, I drove to the end of the road and parked at the paring lot. Construction of the Hell Gate Bridge began on March 1, 1912 and ended on September 30, 1916. It was the world's longest steel arch bridge until the Bayonne Bridge was opened in 1931, and was surpassed again by the Sydney Harbour Bridge in 1932.
In 1996 the bridge received a facelift, including its first comprehensive paint job in 80 years. It was painted "Hell Gate Red," a dark, natural red. The bridge would be the last New York City bridge to collapse if humans disappeared, taking at least a millennium to do so, according to the February 2005 issue of Discover magazine. Most other bridges would fall in about 300 years.[6]
