Monterey is always a joy to visit. With the cool temperatures, the ocean breezes, the friendly people, the aquarium, and so much more, I found the lighthouse to be a wonderful inspiration. Having been in continuous operation since 1855, it is the oldest continuously operating lighthouse on the west coast, and the docents will repeat this factoid several times, for anyone who will listen. The lighthouse is open for tours in the afternoons from 1 to 4. The volunteers seem to love their jobs. Situated on the tip of the Monterey peninsula between two fairways, back from the coast a couple hundred yards is a small house with a giant light on the steeple, or whatever you call the part with the big rotating light. The history of the types of light sources, the notes of the keepers, the reports of the issues during the war, make this a very informative stop. Whether you are being self guided or docent toured, there is so much on the wall and in the story to make this an eye opening adventure. I really enjoyed my stop and it takes some time to read the wall postings. I also enjoyed sitting on the second floor and just watching the waves crashing on the rocks, and speculating about watching for ships over the decades. This well preserved site give a glimpse into an era, or even a group of eras unknown or never contemplated by most. For any history buff it is a must. For the curious it is a Pandora's box and for everyone it is a great view.

Well this is a world class science museum. World Class. The breadth of the displays is very wide. there are other museums that specialize in one area that may be larger, it is true. The quality of the displays is down right jaw dropping. The first thing to do is step up and become a member and come back again and again. For my wife and I it was only a few bucks more and we can come back again and again. And believe me after a few hours in the place you brain may explode!  The dioramas are fabulous. They are so clean, new, and just come alive! - They are near the penguins who as cute as penguins can be. The Roof top display is a read trend setter of a type of building that has been lost for a bit and needs to be revived. The Rain Forest is world class and for a good tip do the rain forest before the aquarium - The rain forest is hot and at the end it leaves you in the aquarium that is oh so cool. OK now lets stop for lunch. The cafe is a real machine that produces really nice food and even with a crowd moves right along. Tho Pho and spring rolls were excellent!
now after lunch lets go to the planetarium and see a show. We did and it was about dark matter and very well done.  Well I could carry on and reveal more secrets of the museum and science exhibits, but that would take some of the mystery out of life! So Have fun , Enjoy, Park underneath and it is oh so easy!
in summary WOW!

This is a 6star museum for sure. It is an incredible collection of what some might call junk, that has been classified, loved, repaired and tended to create a historic timeline of electronics, communication, theatre, radio and more. The guided tour is the best, and the guide is so excited, it is almost too much information. These guys know their stuff and are so very excited to share all they have to offer. This place needs to be on the map for all museum goers and history buffs. there is so much that it boggles the mind to start to list things in the review. So I will list a few and there are so many more.
Imagine getting to play music on an original Edison Phonograph. with wax recordings.
Then step up to the second model Edison created in the thirties and listen to the improvement.
Then step up the the next level with thick records and learn how they were created and listen again.
If I only got that part of the tour I would have been ecstatic and happily overwhelmed.
But the history and stories continued about theatre and projection.
the first projectors and the meaning of lime light.
How traveling movies were the rage in the twenties and what got peoples attention.
and on and on and on
Any way I describe it, this is a wow wow wow museum and I loved it.

Dinosaur caves Park in Pismo Beach is definitely one of the most visible parks as one drives up or down the 101 highway. Easy enough to overlook because of the sweeping ocean view dinosaur parks is very worthy of a stop, especially if you have little ones. The dinosaur eggs for the tiny ones to crawl in are beautiful touch.  The swings for those to just go back and forth and let the world roll on by. The large concrete seals and the killer whale are just the right size for the little ones to crawl on and play make believe. Meanwhile the adults can have one eye on the children and one eye on the lovely panoramic view. Many picnic tables make it easy for one to have that beautiful picnic by the beach. The walkways give an easy place to stroll while watching the waves crash. The expansive lawns give a wonderful place for the dogs to run around and sniff sniff sniff . What more could one ask for a park. Is plenty of parking in the park and along the north side. It's just an incredible lovely place to be, to sit and read, to take a walk, to walk the dog, to bring the children, to have a picnic, and to have the 37 other things I didn't mention. It just feels good Dinosaur Caves Park

The Japanese Gardens in San Mateo is quite charming. First parking can seem to be a bit difficult for the out of towner, as the huge Central Park, in which the Japanese Gardens is contained, can be quite busy. That said, park under the tennis courts on East 5th. If you miss it the first time, just lap the block and try again, I know I have has to do that! Once under the tennis courts, you will find shaded easy parking. It may take a minute for you eyes to adjust in the parking lot as it is not brightly lit, but lit enough after a minute of adjustment. The machine for the parking fee is on the end by the entrance and I found the price quite reasonable.  Now exit at the far inside of the lot and presto you are right at the entrance to the Japanese Gardens. The beautiful coy pond is loaded with huge fish! The walk around is so pleasant and it just seems so cool and peaceful as one stroll. Bring a great friend for some wonderful chats, or come alone and let it be reflective and meditative. What ever you choose. This place is so clean, peaceful, well maintained and lovely, I want to come again and again and again ….

This is a museum worthy of your time. I stop whenever I am in Deming, and on my most recent visit, I admit, was overwhelmed by some of the history in this museum. From notes and articles about the Bataan  Death March, to a collection of liquor bottles that numbers probably over a thousand. The Geode collection is extensive. The history of shops and the equipment from long ago is incredible. Wait till you see the old hair salon! The sets of photos of all the locals and their generations is wonderful.
This time I found a photographic collection of The Faces of Deming, that was inspiring indeed!
There is so much going on, yet it is large and spacious. The upstairs is due to be back online in Nov 2012, and that brings another layer to this museum!
Top it off it is free. (you can donate all you want) The volunteers that put this together have a passion that needs to be bottled and sprayed on people everywhere! What a gem.
likes: Activities: Diverse collections (geodes, liquor bottles, photos)

reviews_attraction.text: Fabulous views across LA and more! The place is like ans astronomy museum with lots of displays to study and really learn. Timelines of the universe, a look at each planet and what the gravitational pulls would be like. The ever popular pendulum knocking over blocks as the Earth rotates and more. With a planetarium and shows, both astronomical and and laser shows, and vistas of the city, the mountains, the Hollywood sign view, the James Dean bust and notes of his history, the entrance statue with all the great astronomers of history, and a map of the solar  orbits of the plants set in to the walk ways of the entrance, and if you are not getting it I think this place is wonderful Add in the art deco building and well..... Come on up and enjoy, and especially just after the rain or winds  when the air is clean. Oh yes and the views of the city lights at night are wonderful!

If I carry on too much, you have to know I have been coming to the races at Pomona since 1967 so many of the cars in the Museum I have seen on the drag strip when they were in their prime and at the top of their game. What memories. The displays are fabulous. To have all these machines preserved and in such wonderful shape is a feast for the imagination and the eye. I would be a docent if I lived near by, really. Be aware of some special setups that they have at the museum, special cars that travel around the country to various Museums and car shows. I had the opportunity to take a friend who loved batman so much she had a logo tattoo installed. When the docents at the museum saw it she was allowed to get in the bat-mobile for a photo shoot. How nice. It is a must see for drag racing fans and a good show for everybody else!

The Watts Towers is quite an interesting piece of Los Angeles's history. Made from junk piled, glued, pinned and mortared together over a lifetime this one man has created an icon of Watts and of Los Angeles. It's in a neighborhood that, well, when I see bars on all, and I mean all,  the windows on all houses, when I see tall iron solid fences on every house,  when I see beware of dog signs, over and over and over again, Well I guess I'm not as adventurous as I used to be so visitors beware that you know what you're driving into. It is worth seeing at least once it is worth visiting to understand the nature of what was created here and it's kind of fun. If you live here you better say you visited it at least once.once. I have, and it was enough.

When I made a turn and ended up at the front gate with a guard speaking to me I wondered what I was getting into. The guard asked for ID and if I had any weapons. I said I was not much of a Texan as all I had was a pocket knife. Without a blink the guard said that the museum was closed on Mondays and I could view the tanks and the planes. He said right at the first stop sign, right at the next stop and  I would find things.The plane and chopper collection is small, only a few of each. but when I got the the tanks, WOW! more tanks here than at the Patton Museum in the Mojave. Tanks and launchers and troop carriers and more. An impressive collection. Now I have to come back and see what is in the museum. Next time in Austin, it will be a stop.

The Rex Allen Museum is a wonderful time travel trip into the great era of crooning cowboys dressed in oh so fancy clothes with sequins everywhere and such bright colors. The pictures and memorabilia show a man with a 5 star history. To see the people with whom he was friends, and who supported the museum is very very impressive. However if you do not know the era you will be under-impressed and wonder what all the hubbub is about. As I was with people who had listened to Rex on the radio in their childhood, and seen his movies as youngsters, it was eye opening. For the western enthusiast this is a huge nugget of information and memories. So worth the two dollar admission fee.

I have an affinity for the meditative nature of a well manicured, peaceful park. The Japanese Gardens in Van Nuys is just such a place. The Sepulveda  Basin is driven through by thousands every day. The 101 and 405 take traffic by the tens of thousands daily, and the Gardens sit peacefully amid the frantic pace of Los Angeles. For a quiet stroll, a beautiful afternoon, a contemplative session, or a meditative space, this is a wonderful place to visit. It is always interesting to find local friends who have never heard of the place or given it the I will get to it later excuse. This beautiful park is awaits all in an unlikely location, Van Nuys!

I love little oddities in the form of a big rock painted like a frog - first in 1918, an oddity museum, memorial or shrine. Well this one qualifies! it was a bit hard to find however. with Google map I got it easily. A new fellow has purchased the location from the state and has a small antique store I got an old Eric Clapton record in great shape for 3 bucks) and a trailer snack / burger / chowder kitchen.. It is next to a forest (state park) and is a lovely place for a picnic and more.

I love nature parks, preserves, and the outdoors. This place is hidden away a bit in Los Osos, and definitely worth location. I believe it is a 23 acre piece right on the ocean in the back bay with fantastic panoramas of the Rock and Morro Bay. As the Audubon  Society is closely tied with this place, you would be correct in assuming that there are lots of birds here! Correct! all types of seashore birds are here and just park yourself on any of the benches and they will start coming in to earshot and into view. I was Very excited about the number and quantity of birds I encountered. Bring the camera and be ready for a treat!

This is a gem of a gem. There may not be enough superlatives to describe this one. Unbelievable colors and formations all around. The side road is fabulous. Take all the turnouts and look all around. Come early – especially in the summer – and if you are as lucky as we were you will get to see the mountain goats. The visitor center is a dream. The movie that was playing about insects knocked our socks off with information. Beyond description. Come camp, drive though, hike, chat with rangers and have the time of your life in Valley of Fire. A true top tenner and the First state park in Nevada.

Although this stadium was built in 59-62 (see Wikipedia for all that techno history) it is and continues to be a top notch park with everything one could want from a ball park, The Maintenance is immaculate, the staff is all very personable, I mean all. from the parking attendants, ticket takers, security, food service and guards at the aisles, everybody. Add this in with a jumbo tron TV that looks better than most peoples TV and you have a great experience. I have bee going to the stadium since the 70's and it is still and continues to be a great stadium.

Yosemite Falls - INCREDIBLE! Having been coming to Yosemite for over 40 years I am still in awe, especially when it is a big year for the falls. To view the falls from across the valley is breathtaking. To view the falls from the pathway stunning. To view the falls from the base is inspiring. Come early in the year say May to see the falls really pounding. This year with the small snow, the size of the falls is shrunk a bit. But come again and again and you will always find nature in Yosemite, and Yosemite Falls is one of the crown jewels!
dislikes: Smaller falls due to less snow

reviews_attraction.text: Incredible, breathtaking and jaw dropping. What I can't figure out is how I missed this place for so long. It is a very short drive up the hill to  this phenomenal overlook. The GPS will work fine and there is plenty of signal for uploading the pictures you will want to take. The vista is sweeping, and wide and is a knockout. Just GO! Bring a picnic as there are tables, or a blanket, as there is a lawn. What ever you like. This is one of the best finds of the year. I am calling this a first stop in Ventura to Get the real lay of the land.

What a a lovely park. Hidden at the end of the road on the the north end of San Luis Obispo is a seasonal creek (so sorry for all the drought this year), large lawn, clean restrooms, multiple group areas (for large 50-200 groups), volley ball sand pit with net, 3 horse shoe pits, a fabulous new children's playground for the tots, lots of benches, great sun and good shade - so everyone is happy, and so clean and well maintained. Thank you SLO county. See the Pictures - they tell it all!

Anchor Memorial Park is a very small patch of green, a couple of picnic tables, a small pier, and a big memorial anchor. It is a memorial to the fisherman lost at sea from Morro Bay. It is thought provoking and emotional especially if you know people in the industry. The park has a fantastic view of Morro Rock and of the Morro Bay Power Plant. It is a  place of serene contemplation for most anyone! Stop. Think. Smile, Shed a tear, and Reflect, it will do your heart good.

This monument is such a valuable addition to California and America. The history of achievements and the class with the execution of those achievements make this man a true icon of history for all. To study and learn from the actions of this man is an inspiration. To emulate the actions is divine. His work affected the quality of life for millions. What a lovely find. I really like well maintained, colorful gardens. This is what I consider a nice find on the west end of Golden Gate Park. A beautiful place for pictures with that special background, and when you walk to the center of the garden, the olfactory experience is marvelous. I can sit and watch the flowers grow and simply enjoy the color, the smell, and the peace  that is oh so evident in place like this!

Check the calendar and website to come at the right time of year. This is real important. When you see the Butterflies clustering in the trees it is a sight to remember. The docents are so helpful, and the spotting scopes are so helpful. Bring you camera and binoculars and be ready for amazement., but only at the right time of year.

What a wonderful piece of history!  to experience the grounds of this location is terrific. As a fan of the missions and the history of the California missions this place has so much to see and  study as the grounds have been well attended.  I say come and enjoy and you be the judge. I liked it a bunch.

Of the many small parks in Pismo, this tiny park is just a step beyone incredible. The bird, the seals, the panorama are all between stunning and jaw dropping. I love this park. Bring lunch and pull up to a table. See you there.

(Translated by Google) My favorite ! - July 2016
After a first visit in 2012, back in these places and always as much fun to rediscover this jewel of Arizona.
Big change for 4 years in terms of reception, finished the little hut to wait in the shade before leaving to visit. Now a concrete building welcomes visitors.
Despite a reservation for an early departure (8:40 am), a crowd is already present on the site which will make us a little wait to descend into the canyon.
Departure in a small group with a nice guide, who will not hesitate to stop to take a picture of us.
Despite this feeling of "factory" outside, we had the opportunity on numerous occasions to find ourselves "alone in the world" at the bottom of the canyon .... Very pleasant visit once again!
I confirm, this canyon remains my favorite!

(Original)
Mon préféré ! - Juillet 2016
Après une première visite en 2012, retour dans ces lieux et toujours autant de plaisir à re-découvrir ce bijou de l’Arizona.
Gros changement depuis 4 ans en matière d’accueil, fini la petite cahute pour patienter à l’ombre avant de partir faire la visite. Maintenant un bâtiment en dur accueil les visiteurs.
Malgré une réservation pour un départ matinal (8h40), une foule est déjà présente sur le site ce qui nous vaudra un peu d’attente pour descendre dans le canyon.
Départ en petit groupe avec un guide sympa, qui n’hésitera pas à s’arrêter pour nous prendre en photo.
Malgré ce sentiment « d’usine » à l’extérieur, nous avons eu à de nombreuses reprises l’occasion de se retrouver « seul au monde » au fond du canyon….Visite très agréable encore une fois !
Je confirme, ce canyon reste mon préféré !
likes: On-site Activities: Guided tours, Photography opportunities, Solitude in the canyon
dislikes: Facilities & Services: Crowded during peak times

Breathtaking site that remains etched in my memory and is one of my favorites;)
Go there you will not be disappointed!

(Original)
“Exceptionnel !”
Parc situé à quelques milles d'Alamogordo qui mérite au minimum ½ journée de visite notamment en fin d'après-midi pour marcher dans les dunes de gypse et assister au sunset.
Il suffit de marcher 15mn et vous êtes seul au monde, entouré de dunes....magnifique !
Site époustouflant qui reste gravé dans ma mémoire et fait parti de mes coups de cœur ;)
Allez y vous ne serez pas déçu !

(Translated by Google) Step fun with Page and Monument Valley - July 2016
At Home, stage about an hour on site to perform the walk on the Sandal Trail (no problem) and contemplate Betatakin canyon with its ruins nestled in the cliffs. visible exhibit in the Visitor Center, outside a beautiful dinosaur footprint.
Step fun with Page and Monument Valley, ideal for a picnic break.

(Original)
Etape sympa entre Page et Monument Valley - Juillet 2016
Au départ de Page, étape d’environ une heure sur place pour effectuer la balade sur le Sandal Trail (pas de difficulté) et contempler  Betatakin canyon avec ses ruines nichées dans la falaise. Exposition visible au sein du Visitor Center, à l’extérieur une belle empreinte de dinosaure.
Étape sympa entre Page et Monument Valley, endroit idéal pour une pause pique-nique.

(Translated by Google) “Nice longhorn outing!”
Cowboy atmosphere in this very touristy, friendly neighborhood. Do not miss the exit of the longhorns in the main street every day at 5:00 p.m. to the delight of tourists. Lasts only ten minutes, but remains in my opinion the major attraction of the day.
Many shops and restaurants (H3 Ranch excellent), easy parking.

(Original)
“Sortie des longhorns sympa !”
Ambiance cow-boy dans ce quartier très touristique, bon enfant. A ne pas rater, la sortie des longhorns dans la rue principale chaque jour à 17h00 pour le plus grand plaisir des touristes. Ne dure qu'une dizaine de minutes, mais reste selon moi l'attraction majeure de la journée.
De nombreux magasins et restaurants (H3 Ranch excellent), parking facile.

(Translated by Google) Site steeped in history! - July 2016
Very interesting visit to this site steeped in history, a clean and well-kept place.
Many reconstructed rooms in buildings and houses give the impression that the occupants only left for a few moments.
+1 for the soldiers' barracks ... just superb!
If you are around, a stop is mandatory;)

(Original)
Site chargé d’histoire ! - juillet 2016
Visite très intéressante sur ce site chargé d’histoire, endroit propre et bien tenu.
De nombreuses pièces reconstituées dans les bâtiments et maisons donnent l’impression que les occupants ne sont partis que pour quelques instants.
+1 pour le baraquement des soldats...juste superbe !
Si vous êtes dans les parages, l’arrêt y est obligatoire ;)

(Translated by Google) “For Walker fans!”
Museum that at least has the merit of letting us know the history of the Texas Rangers and honoring Colt Walker. Beautiful weapons on display and showcases representing some facts (Bonnie & Clyde) and “Famous” rangers.
Museum which deserves a visit but also for lovers of arms and fans of Chuck Norris;)

(Original)
“Pour les fans de Walker !”
Musée qui a au moins le mérite de nous faire connaître l'histoire des Texas Rangers et mettre à l'honneur le colt Walker. De belles armes en exposition et vitrines représentants quelques faits (Bonnie & Clyde) et rangers « Célèbres ».
Musée qui mérite une visite mais aussi pour les passionnés d'armes et fans de Chuck Norris ;)

(Translated by Google) “Interesting visit!”
Entire building dedicated to this event, quick passage through the cash register and taking into account the headphones before taking the elevator for the visit.
Interesting visit, documented with an audio guide giving a plus to this historic place.
I recommend this museum, a must do if you go through Dallas.

(Original)
“Visite intéressante !”
Bâtiment entier dédié à cet événement, passage rapide par la caisse et prise en compte des écouteurs avant de prendre l'ascenseur pour la visite.
Visite intéressante, documentée avec un audio-guide donnant un plus à ce lieu historique.
Je recommande ce musée, à faire absolument si vous passez par Dallas.

(Translated by Google) "Very interesting !"
Within the Luxor hotel-casino, a very interesting visit to this atypical museum comprising several rooms, each dealing with different parts of the human body.
Here no taboo, everything is represented and well explained even if some rooms are cold in the back.
Visit that I highly recommend to everyone!

(Original)
“Très intéressant !”
Au sein de l'hôtel-casino Luxor, visite très intéressante de ce musée atypique comportant plusieurs salles traitants chacune des différentes parties du corps humain.
Ici pas de tabou, tout est représenté et bien expliqué même si certaines salles font froid dans le dos.
Visite que je recommande vivement à tous !

(Translated by Google) Nice visit if you have time!
Located in front of a big outlet (Fashion Outlets of Primm), this attraction is located in the main lobby of the casino.
Interesting tour to learn a little more about this famous couple.
If you have a little time after your shopping, or not, do not hesitate to come here.

(Original)
Petite visite sympa si vous avez du temps !
Établissement situé en face d’un grand outlet (Fashion Outlets of Primm), cette attraction est située dans le hall principal du casino.
Visite intéressante pour en apprendre un peu plus sur ce célèbre couple.
Si vous avez un peu de temps après votre shopping, ou pas, n’hésitez pas à venir faire un saut ici.

(Translated by Google) Interesting visit!
Located on the side of the road a few minutes from Lone Pine, do not hesitate to make a stop to visit the visitor center which explains very well the history of Manzanar (reconstituted camp, many photos and videos, workshop ...).
To be included in your roadbook, you won't regret it!

(Original)
Visite intéressante !
Situé en bordure de route à quelques minutes de Lone Pine, n'hésitez pas à faire un arrêt pour visiter le visitor center qui explique fort bien l'histoire de Manzanar (camp reconstitué, nombreuses photos et vidéos, atelier...).
A prévoir dans votre roadbook, vous ne le regretterez pas !

(Translated by Google) “Kitch but fun!”
Not really an obligation to come here but it is still a pretty nice experience especially with family. Smiling welcome, access for a few dollars and here in the very kitsch universe of little green men. A lot of photos to take, certainly the tour is fast but it's quite fun!

(Original)
“Kitch mais fun !”
Pas vraiment une obligation de venir ici mais cela reste tout de même une expérience assez sympa notamment en famille. Accueil souriant, accès pour quelques dollars et voici dans l'univers très kitch des petits hommes verts. Pas mal de photos à faire, certes le tour est rapide mais c'est assez fun !

(Translated by Google) “Exceptional!”
Present on the site at the end of the day or for the sunrise the next day, this place is exceptional!
Good road to get there as in all US parks, large parking and possibility of a very easy hike even with young children.
To do absolutely!

(Original)
“Exceptionnel !”
Présent sur le site en fin de journée ou pour le sunrise le lendemain, ce lieu est exceptionnel !
Bonne route pour s'y rendre comme dans tous les parcs US, grand parking et possibilité d'effectuer une rando très facile même avec de jeunes enfants.
A faire absolument !

(Translated by Google) "Fun!"
Work of art located at the exit of Marfa on the road of El Paso, stop which will take you only a few minutes history to make a little "window shopping" and photos memories.
Fun to see this shop in the middle of nowhere!

(Original)
“Amusant !”
Œuvre d'art situé à la sortie de Marfa sur la route d'El Paso, arrêt qui vous prendra que quelques minutes histoire de faire un peu de « lèche vitrine » et photos souvenirs.
Amusant de voir cette boutique au milieu de nulle part !

Nice place to visit, restaurants to be possibly but beware of the prices!
Depending on your time of arrival, you may have problems parking the car nearby.
To do if you pass in the neighborhood!

A visiter !
Endroit sympathique à visiter, restaurants à faire éventuellement mais attention aux tarifs !
Selon l’heure de votre arrivée, vous risquez d’avoir des problèmes pour garer la voiture à proximité.
A faire si vous passez dans le quartier !

(Translated by Google) If you have some time - July 2016
Interesting archaeological site, many petroglyphs to admire.
Large parking lot close to the premises, stop not necessarily compulsory only if you have some time in front of you.

(Original)
Si vous avez un peu de temps - Juillet 2016
Site archéologique intéressant, nombreux petroglyphs à admirer.
Grand parking à 2 pas des lieux, halte pas forcément obligatoire seulement si vous avez un peu de temps devant vous.

I came here 2 hours before closing time and the guy at the entrance told me I should be not too slow as it takes some time to do the loop drive.

Entrance fee is 20$ per vehicle or 10$ per person and is NOT part of your America the beautiful annual pass.

At first, I thought it was quite a lot, considering I was alone in the vehicle, but I am so happy I did it.

Driving around these incredible rock formations felt so unreal. In the end I did the loop in approximately 1h30 with some stops.

I had a 4x4 which is recommended to drive on the dirt road, but it is also possible with other cars, just be more careful.

Also stumbled upon a street dog.

Coit Tower for sure has the best view in San Francisco. Will cost you some effort climbing the steps at Greenwich Steps, but is so worth it!

Entering Coit Tower you will find unbelievably painted walls all over the ground floor. Once you’ve purchased a ticket, you can admire the beautiful paintings as you wait in the waiting line.

Waiting lines can get pretty big, as the elevator can only take dozen of people up and they try to limit the people up in order to let people enjoy still.

Once arrived at the top, you will find magnificent 360 degrees view over beautiful San Francisco.

They started charging money for the parking lot recently, because of the many visitors. 10$ per car is not a lot, but since I was alone in the car I find it quite expensive.

Arrived here early morning during sunrise, did a small hike down towards Horseshoe Bend and was incredible to see the sun moving every minute.

Stayed here for 10 minutes and walked the way up, which is a bit steep.

Honestly a bit expensive for such a short visit, but you gotta see it once in your life.

Walking from the parking to the visitor center, there are lots of signs with information about Yosemite; trails, weather, general park information,...

Went to have a look in the visitor center itself and there was a huge line to the counter.

There was a nice souvenir shop as well a small free and interactive museum about the erosions that resulted into Yosemite.

This place is a bit overrated to me, as I saw so many likewise streets with painted ladies in San Francisco where I was alone.

At this place, you will find yourself on the hill with dozens of tourists who are taking the same pictures.

What I did like was the view from the hill over the city skyline. Enjoyed the morning sitting on the bench here!

Bright Angel trail is a hike of more than a day which goes to the deepest of the Grand Canyon, but nothing stops you from just taking a short hike down to admire the magnificent views from there.

Honestly, one of the better views were here, just 10 minutes hiking down.

Be careful though, as it gets super slippery when it has snowed.

Near the visitor center you can find big information signs on the hikes of Grand Canyon, describing the length, difficulty and other practicalities.
Make sure to read them before starting a hike!

I went inside to watch the Grand Canyon movie and what an amazing movie it is, absolutely had goosebumps the whole movie.

Awesome!

I was here in November, so the waterfall was rather tiny but I was glad still to see a waterfall though!

The mist trail up to Vernal falls is incredibly crowded, even in November and contains lots of steps.

I would recommend going up the Vernal Falls and going further to Nevada Falls which is much less crowded.

Nice to see the dunes out here in Death Valley!

Can be terribly hot here in summer so make sure you have lots of water with you.

There is parking available just next to the dunes.
Had a short walk here of 10 minutes, personally did not need more than this.

Not the best thing in Death Valley but worth visiting.

Pier 14 quickly became one of my favourite spots in San Francisco!

If you walk all the way to the pier in the end you will find a platform with turning chairs which allows a nice 360 degrees view on the Bay Bridge and the city.

Absolutely loved sitting here, as here is so much silence and not so many people.

Fisherman’s Wharf is a nice but super touristic part of San Francisco.

Have a walk over the piers and enjoy the nice views to the bay, Golden Gate and Alcatraz.

Expect lots of souvenir stores and lots of overpriced restaurants though. For better and cheaper food, walk away from here towards center.

Came to this spot to enjoy the nice view on the Golden Gate Bridge, ended up sitting here for couple of hours.

Lots of fishers here, just loved the calm atmosphere here. There were not so many tourists here, so it was perfect just to watch local fishers, the bridge and Alcatraz in the far.

Amazing!

Great initiative, putting a real life Monopoly in the park.

However, it is not as big as I was expecting and it is not interactive at all, purely decorative.

You cans see it had its best time as the board lost lots of its paint.

This has great potential but could really use a new layer of paint!

Union Square is a super nice district with lots of stores in the neighborhood.

The square itself is not so big, but is nice, surrounded with skyscrapers.
I was there in November, and there was a cute little ice skating rink.

Around the square you can find Macy’s, Apple Store, Cheesecake Factory.

Mather Point is one of the most touristic viewpoints of Grand Canyon and that is clearly visible.

Especially at sunrise it gets very busy here but even at noon in November it was fully packed.

The other viewpoints definitely have more or less the same views, if you want to skip the tourists.

This was probably the place where I saw the most people in November. Cars are lined up here and parked everywhere to have a picture here.

Basically it is a giant Sequoia which fell down, they made a hole inside where you can walk and drive through. It is nice, but a bit overhyped!

Words can hardly describe seeing the Grand Canyon for the first time.

I remember that I was so speechless and having tears in my eyes.
It is truly overwhelming being here and I felt so grateful seeing this nature's beauty.

What a moment this was, I will never forget this, ever.

Wow Moro Rock!

This is quite a short but steep trail, approximately 10-15 minutes only, but it offers one of the most amazing views in Sequoia.

Once up, definitely have a look further than the safety bars, as you can sit there and just enjoy the silence and the nice views!

Walking from Financial District to the piers, you will find this small beautiful park with an amazing art object.

‘Cupid’s Span’ is a sculpture of a bow and an arrow, which is phenomenal with the Bay Bridge in the background!

Nice little promenade in the park as well.

Just like the Monopoly board which really could use a new layer of painting, the park itself could really use some refreshment.

The decoration is pretty old and not in line with the city’s nice and modern look.

Also could use some trees and more benches to sit on.

At first, I drove past this overlook as I saw it too late but I decided to turn back to have a look anyway.

And actually I am glad I did! What a magnificent overlook this is!!

There is even a information sign, explaining everything that you see here. Awesome!

Way less known than the Golden Gate bridge, but the Bay Bridge is definitely not less beautiful in my opinion!

It is huge, and you have many awesome viewpoints if you walk from financial district to  the piers.

Worth it to come to have a look at the bridge.

Enter this place and you will feel yourself like you are in Japan! Decoration is adorable and the tiny streets just feels like Japan.

Lots of restaurants here with sushi, ramen but also souvenir and gift shops with all typical Japanese stuff.

Lovely visit!

Sutro Baths is a true hidden gem in San Francisco and provides amazing views.

Lands End area is not so known among tourists and you will not find too many people here.

It is not allowed to swim in the baths anymore unfortunately.

Must visit place!

Grandview offers such an amazing 270 degrees panoramic view on the Grand Canyon which is truly incredible.

Information signs available on the beginning of Grandview name.

I've been fortunate enough to live here my entire life, and the Columbia River Gorge is absolutely beautiful. Natural beauty wise, it's on par with the top National Parks, except it's right near a major metropolitan area and has a major freeway and railroad running through it. If you're willing to explore and get creative, there are always new views and places to see. What a Wonder historic Highway 30 must have been back in its heyday.

Be smart one hiking though, some areas of which are known to have poison oak and ticks can be found in the area as well, especially east of Cascade Locks. However, don't let that discourage you from enjoying this beautiful. Just be smart when your Outdoors. If this is your first time visiting, check out some of the visitor centers or look into the history of the area. It's really quite fascinating.

Edit: the attached pictures are from when the Columbia gorge fire occurred labor day 2017. This is an absolutely gorgeous area, and unfortunately you can see how bad the smoke was from the devastating fires. The destruction was even worse. If you visit this area or any other forest or national park, do not light fires, throw smoke bombs into a ravine or forest or anything else like that. All the smoke and damage was due to teenagers throwing a smoke bomb into a ravine in Eagle Creek.

Sherrard point is located at the top of Larch Mountain, which itself is an extinct volcano 4,055 feet high. Being from Portland, I have been here many times. You can get here two ways: a seven mile hike with 4000 foot elevation change from the Larch Mountain #441 Trailhead at Multnomah Falls (the hard way), or you can drive the 14 miles up Larch Mountain Road to the parking lot and Hike about a quarter-mile to the viewpoint (the easy way). If the skies are clear and there is not cloud cover, you can see five volcanoes from the viewpoint: Mount Hood, Mount Rainier, Mount Saint Helens, Mount Adams, and Mount Jefferson. Please note this road past mile post 10 is seasonal, it closes due to snow in the winter (usually sometime in November) and the reopens in the late spring (usually late May or early June). Sherrard Point is a Forest Service Recreation Area, so you will either need a Northwest forest pass, a National Parks Pass, or you will need to pay the fee.

Ponytail Falls is a little over a mile up the trail from where it begins next to Horsetail Falls. If you have the time, it's worth the hike up there. If you bring kids on this hike, make sure they understand not to goof around on the trail. Hold their hands as there are switchbacks and some steep drop-offs next to the trail as it switchbacks up the hillside. I've personally never had any issues on this Trail the many times I've hiked there. Yes it's steep so just take time on the switchbacks and go slow if you are a beginning hiker. Once you get to ponytail Falls itself it is worth it as you round the corner you'll get a gorgeous view of the falls plunging over the Basalt cliffs, and as you get near it the trail cuts behind the waterfall itself. Make sure to stop here and enjoy the view from behind the waterfall. It's definitely worth the hike.

Absolutely spectacular National Park. Amazing sunrises and sunsets, with dark skies for night time (when the moon is not out). There are several good look out switch are easily accessible all along the south rim. So even if you are not able to hike down into the canyon there are still stunning views from the top. If you do hike down into the canyon, it's a completely different feeling than the views of above but still worth the Trek down and back. If you do go down in the canyon, don't go down during the hottest part of the day in the spring and summer and early fall, and make sure to bring lots of electrolytes and salty snacks.

Crater Lake National Park is one of the most beautiful places I've ever been. No matter where you going the rim, the views are stunning. There are excellent views from the visitor center and the lodge, no I personally prefer to view it from the edge of the rim. Rim Village is open almost all year long, and less a major snowstorm temporarily shuts down the road in from Highway 62. So you can view Crater Lake from Rim Village regardless of time of year. That said, the amenities up at Rim Village shut down outside of the Peak seasons, so if you're going there in the winter make sure you have everything you need.

This is a full size replica of Stonehenge, and it even lines up with the solstices and equinoxes as it should. It's a memorial to the World War I veterans. Whether you're here to pay homage to the World War I veterans or you're here to check it out simply because it's a replica of Stonehenge, it's worth the trip. It's a neat area with great views east and west of the gorge and the Columbia River down below. If you need facilities, there are none here, but the Pilot Travel Plaza has food gas and restrooms and is just across the Columbia River in Biggs Junction.

Large parking lot with a restroom. It's a great place to stop and rest after going up the curves or before going down them. The farpoint of the Overlook overlooks Panamint Valley, with the part directly next to you overlooking a small side Canyon. It's a nice place to stop, enjoy of you and take a break before heading down into Death Valley or out towards Lone Pine. Also, if you are patient you can sometimes see military jets flying low overhead in the valley below. That's kind of a cool site to see, as it's not often you see military jets flying below you.

Very cool spot, it's a bit of a hike down and back up but nothing terrible. For the most part the beach was quiet and great to visit, there were obviously several people from out of the area (likely the Bay Area) who showed up with a beer for Sunset and decided it was a good idea to climb on the rocks and get loud. Sort of ruined it, and from what I've read in other reviews the place has this problem now. Such a shame, hopefully they pull their head out of the sand and respect the beach here because it's quite beautiful.

A nice little Regional Park with nice hiking trails. Lots of birds here to view and photograph if you're into that kind of thing. Trails can get close to the road at times but not so close as could be dangerous. The south side of the park has some nice artificial Fields if you want to play some sports. It's also near in and out and some other restaurants, so if you're visiting from the Bay Area and want a quick place to have a little picnic or something it's a great place to stop.

Beautiful Lighthouse. The visitors center was very helpful with lots of great information, and the gift shop had a nice selection of stuff l. No admission was charged to get in, c which was nice. So I used that money to buy a stuffed animal for my son at the gift shop. The views of the lighthouse and the surrounding Headlands are amazing. I came back at sunset to take in the views. Well worth the stop.
likes: Facilities & Services: Helpful Visitors Center, Nice Gift Shop

reviews_attraction.text: Beautiful spot along the Point Reyes National Seashore. There is parking near the tunnel, so park there and walk. Do not drive into the tree tunnel. This is a spectacular place to just enjoy a morning, afternoon, or evening stroll. It's also a great place to take pictures. There's lots to do and see along the Point Reyes National Seashore, this place is one you should visit.

Awesome Park. Seriously the best part I have ever brought my son to. I only wish they had Parks like this back home. If we would have let him, I'm sure he would have never left. If you are in the area and are looking for a park to take your kids to come look no further. You will not regret it. An added bonus, there are good views of the sky at Sunset to see good colors.

I love this spot. It has a wife sweeping view of Hat Creek Valley, and you can really see the affects Hat Creek burn. Great views valley My Shasta, Burney Mountain, Sugarloaf Peak and Lassen Peak in the distance. The signs at the viewpoint are nice and descriptive. I've been here several times while passing through, and always love it.

Friendly staff and beautiful area. If you have an NPS pass it is accepted here. This location is open from dawn to dusk, and the lighthouse is beautiful. The Cobblestone Beach down just below it is neat as well. This is an excellent place to stop and bring your family for some great views of the Oregon coast and a historic lighthouse.

You can see quite a bit of this waterfall from the road, but to truly appreciate it hike up the trail to the bridge which crosses in front of the waterfall. It's a beautiful hike and a truly beautiful waterfall up close. If you have time, go further up the trail to Fairy Falls. It's a gorgeous hike (pun intended). You won't regret it!

This is a small but fun neighborhood park in West Linn. There's a playground for the kids, and a water park there for the summer when the weather heats up. There's also a trail around the park and some dirt trails into the forest area. It's not a huge part, but it's a fun park for the family to visit in the kids to play at.

This beach has excellent parking, picnic tables, restrooms and easy beach access. It's a great place to take the family. my father took me and my sister here when we were kids, and my wife and I now take our son here. It's a great, family friendly Beach I've been visiting for most of my life.

Great view of the ocean, and a very short walk from the parking lot. Nice beach and tide pools, and I would imagine in the wintertime you could get some pretty good views of the storms coming in from here. Overall, it was a neat spot and it is definitely worth a stop if you are in the area!!

Spectacular views of the Pacific, and unlike a few miles up the road they don't charge you $10 to see it. Come as early or late as you want. If you are near Monterey, it's worth the stop. Drive this route and enjoy the beauty for free.

This area it's actually pretty nice. It's a nice stroll around of the lake, and the restaurants nearby with outdoor seating is a nice touch. It's a nice place to come and spend some time with your family.

This tree is awesome, and it's a very short walk from the parking lot. If you came to check out cape meares and the views of the Pacific, don't leave before taking the short walk to check out this tree!
This Lighthouse has a spectacular views. It's by far the better of the two lighthouses in this park. I've been here with my family a few times and we've always enjoyed it.
Clean Park. A great place to stop while traveling, stretch your legs, get out and enjoy the scenery. Has public restrooms as well which is always a plus when driving 84.
This is neat because it's a lighthouse, though if you are short on time the other lighthouse in the park is better in my opinion.
I love the beach at this state park. I've been coming here with my family for years and will continue to do so.

The cathedral is a Gothic architectural wonder, you're greeted with a statue of Abraham Lincoln and his immense attachment to the cathedral,the windows all donated from various walks of life is so open that it features space exploration among many other things, there's Woodrow Wilson's tomb, plenty of chapels of which the Bethlehem chapel and the Resurrection chapels underground remains a personal favorite, try to go on the guided tour and if possible visit Sunday afternoon because admission and parking is free .

The national arboretum is a green gem located so close to the city , the area is nearly 1000 acres and you need to spend at least an entire day to do full justice to the greenery on display here for free , the Asian valley , Japanese gardens , floral gardens , conifers , the fern valley are all excellent to watch and the national columns that we're relocated here from the original US capitol is a real icing on the cake in this magnificent vast wonderland

It's a good break if you're headed in a journey along the I-95 . Super small church , seats about 12 people , a few statues outside and plenty of trees around that gives a good shade and feel when you're here, there's also a strange bell just adjacent to it , the purpose of which isn't mentioned anywhere here , good to go in and have a few minutes in silence as you're unlikely to be interrupted by anyone, and also they do have camera, so smile

You'll find tortoise and ducks along the pongs inside the park , the boardwalk is well maintained and offers a brilliant glimpse of the pond ecosystem in general , it's also has a couple of trails that you can jog or cycle , a visitor center , helpful staff and plenty of benches under the trees which make for a aesthetic location and for snacks

An excellent old church with a lot of history in it that's explained perfectly inside the church , the window paintings are magnificent , the way of the cross statues look well built , the dome and the altar is serene and it has plenty of statues that are well done , also free parking in front and the back of the basilica

A must visit memorial around the Washington DC area recording and highlighting the Masonic legacy and contributions of George Washington . It's often skipped by most travel enthusiasts due to a plethora of more popular and rated options , however if you've the time do check this out , it's totally worth the visit

Fascinating views from the top and a majestic Columbus statue in front . The walkway to the elevator queue is full of excellent art work . And the area has a 30 minute free parking ( residential) . Worth visiting if you're on a extended stay at San Francisco , for very short trips may be avoided

Three scenic overlooks and plenty of scenic views there's also a trail which has a dam and it's around two miles long , there's a butterfly spotting point , it leads upto the adjoining state park , there's ample space to park , can easily spend half in it's serene natural beauty

The three giant wings are a fitting tribute as an air Force memorial , with the four iconic air Force men and the views of the Pentagon and the Washington monument from this memorial is absolutely breathtaking, it's a must visit place if you're in and around the DC area

This is serene, quiet and beautiful . It has a mini statue of liberty that overlooks the wonderful town of Richmond , there's a medical museum which has some wonderful volunteers who enriched me with the rich medical history . Don't miss this when you visit Richmond

It has a considerably large cafe , well knowledged people to give everything that's needed as information for visitors of the national Mall , also exhibits some Royal possessions of Smithson , don't forget to see his crypt.
The park has enough things to keep the kids engaged,it's good to walk along the nearby Sligo Creek trail and few benches but mosquitoes are usually on the loose and it's best not to use them
Given the standards set by nps this really needs a lot of work , it doesn't even have a proper access road or parking area  . Certainly needs a lot of work
A national park with several trails most of them above 2 miles long , campgrounds with several spots , mostly secluded , it's really good and often missed

This place was such a fun place to visit. I was amazed that it was there! The last time I came to this building at Thanksgiving Point it was a visitor center/gift store. I'm so glad that they repurposed it to something meaningful for children.
The design of the building took about 3-4 years. The engineers and innovators included the local elementary School in the process of ideation for the new biosphere. They asked the kids what they thought the life of a butterfly would be like. You can see the submissions for their ideas in the hall by the entrance. It was really cool to see things implemented into the building that were inspired by the kids drawings. Like a room of butterflies! Or a 'nector slide.' Sadly the Zipline didn't make it into the building... But hey just about everything else did!
The biosphere itself was really nice. It was like walking into the Amazon rainforest. 85 degree temperatures with misters going off every now and then to keep it humid. Our kids loved it. But there were some other children that were terrified by the flying 'bugs'. They thought they were going to be bitten or stung by the butterflies. You may need to point that out to your kids before you go.
This experience rivals the one at the Loveland Living Planet Aquarium. Though there are definitely more butterflies here, there is more space, the butterflies are bigger, and it feels more like their environment, the aquarium has a more personal feel. This is probably because of the amount of people that were there. It was a bigger room but there were SO many people. It got crowded quickly. The butterflies didn't ever land on us at the biosphere, when they would at the aquarium.
Another cool thing is you can see the butterflies in their various stages of growth behind the glass of a research lab. That is not at the LLPA.
We loved coming here. It was a great experience.

I’ve been a member of this church since I was 8 years old. I’ve never regretted my decision. No matter where I travel in the world I know I’m at home when I attend a chapel of the Latter-Day Saints. Some of the most unique blessings that I receive for living the gospel is peace of mind and conscience, feeling my Savior’s love, faith to move forward in this difficult world, strength to overcome my challenges, friends to rejoice with me or mourn with me, and an eternal perspective that guides my actions every day.

We know we are learning correct principles here. We feel that through the Holy Ghost. (Translated by Google) Worth the trip alone ..... Kings Canyon National Park is a protected natural area in California located in the southern Sierra Nevada, approximately 90km east of Fresno and 250km north of Los Angeles.
Founded in 1940, it covers an area of ​​1,873 km2. It borders to the south with Sequoia National Park, with which it forms a single administrative unit, the Sequoia and Kings Canyon National Parks, managed by the National Park Service. The total area of ​​the two parks is 3,495 km2. The area was already known to settlers in the first half of the nineteenth century, but did not receive much attention until John Muir arrived there in 1873. Muir noted the great geological similarity to the Yosemite park. , concluding that both valleys were created by the action of large glaciers during the last ice age. Muir worked to make the area a protected area, but its future remained uncertain for nearly fifty years. Some politicians and entrepreneurs wanted to build a dam on the western side of the KIngs Canyon valley, which would compromise the integrity of its natural and forest heritage. (Wikipedia)

Cultural center, museum, beginning of tours for Acoma Pueblo Sky City. Good exhibits, clean bathrooms, run by friendly, knowledgeable people. Tours of Sky City are very well run. A short but fun bus ride to the mesa top on the road paved in 1973 for filming the Italian Western MY NAME IS NOBODY, written by Sergio Leone. The walk around the town and mission Church San Esteban Rey (1641) is fascinating, filled with impressive views. The Pueblo was first established after the collapse of Indian culture around 1300, like so many other southwestern cliff dwellings, as an extreme defensive position against attack. It was conquered by the forces of Spanish conquistador Juan de Onate in 1599 and its people treated brutally, but the pueblo was soon rebuilt, and a few Acoma people continue to live in the Sky City to this day. The town is well-maintained, although without most services. The tour is a well worth the cost, a memorable experience, and the tour guides are well informed and helpful.

Remarkable historic southwestern site, steeped in late 19th-early 20th century history, beautifully preserved and maintained by the mostly Navajo staff for the National Parks. The post is packed with collections of rugs, baskets, art, & weapons of the period, as well as current Navajo art and products. The trading post store is a beautiful set out of a movie, and really calls up the feeling of the original and the lives of the people who used it -- and its still in operation! The story of the Hubbell post and the traders who mediated between the Navajo and the larger world, and whose interaction and feedback helped create the worldwide interest in Navajo arts and crafts unfolds before your eyes here. Nice small museum also. Wonderful folks work here, and if it is open, the Hubbell house rooms provide a neat glimpse into a frontier life now vanished.

An LDS theme-park about the Hole-in-the-Rock expedition (see John Ford's WAGON MASTER - 1950) that founded Bluff. I love it! The elaborately reconstructed pioneer cabins and materials are amazing -- almost too much to see in just one visit. Tells many amazing human stories of the pioneers, and life in an unforgiving desert. Great play areas for kids, nice gift shop, helpful staff. Complements the Four Corners area other sites devoted to geology & nature, the Ancestral Puebloans, the modern Native Americans, the cowboys & the trading posts & movie makers, to give a full portrait of the many traditions that makeup the modern southwest.

Great local museum in a classic old schoolhouse. Sprawling exhibits on all aspects of local history, pre-history, geology, etc. Love the room on the El Rio Theater! Jumping off spot for visits to Casa Malpais, the city-owned ancient ruin site in town. Tours take you from the museum up to the site; pretty easy climbing involved. Casa Malpais was inhabited in the 13th century by Mogollon folks, like Gila Cliff Dwellings National Monument.

Truly great and amazingly extensive museum of the movie history of the Alabama Hills and Lone Pine/Eastern Sierra region. Great artifacts, a zillion original movie posters, and lots of fun popular culture items related to Westerns made in the area. Beautifully organized and displayed and labeled. Get a guide to the Alabama Hills here. Knowledgeable folks run it; Lone Pine Film Festival information and publications available.

On route 24, 2 1/2 miles west of the entrance to Capitol Reef National Park turn south onto a gravel/dirt road; pretty easy going for a passenger car when dry; there is a panorama point (nice view of Capitol Reef), then just a mile to the parking area for the goosenecks view. A short climb up the slope leads to spectacular views of the river gorge. Steep drop offs, but with fences and signage. Well worth the side trip!

Been visiting Rancho Sisquoc Winery for over 40 years. Hidden gem north of the Santa Ynez Valley, a bit off the grid, so seldom crowded. Excellent wine tasting room & excellent wine selection, welcoming picnic area, clean bathrooms, super friendly staff. Thank you to the Flood family & descendents for maintaining this homey facility, reminiscent of the wine tasting spots of the old days.

Hidden gem of a museum, that has expanded over the decades into a really fine and educational spot. Covers the history, pre-history and geology of the area -- and what an amazing history it is -- thoroughly, with some great exhibits. Fun for the kids! Outdoor section is great. Loved the special section on the Procession Panel. Lots of parking and nearby picnic tables too.

Landmark and historic Colton Hall, built in late 1840's by Monterey's first American alcalde Walter Colton as a school; largest public building in California at the time. Hosted first California constitutional convention in 1849. Now a small museum, with wonderful front and exterior entry staircases.

Easy to access on the way to Canyonlands Needles section; lots of parking. Short walk to the rock, which seems to combine petroglyphs from all eras (unfortunately including recently). Bathrooms, but the picnic tables were removed when Newspaper Rock got demoted from Utah State Park status.

Just a city park, but magical -- great and quite elaborate children's play area, clean bathrooms, covered picnic area, easy parking, nice baseball field, everything you could want in a public park. We stop at parks all over the country, and this is one of the best, a hidden gem.

Great scenic spot just south of route 24, west of Capitol Reef National Park entrance. Easy short gravel/dirt road to the Panorama Point. Then drive another mile or so -- more easy gravel/dirt road -- to the Goosenecks overlook, with an short hike to a grand view.

Spectacular viewpoint within El Malpais National Monument. Walk up from the parking area to see the panoramic view of the vast lava field badlands below. Mount Taylor, one of the four sacred mountains that delimit Dinetah/Navajoland, is prominent to the North.

V.C. Morris Gift Shop (1948) designed by Frank Lloyd Wright. A miniature of his plans for the Guggenheim Museum in NYC. Amazing space -- the special furnishings are beautiful. Xanadu Gallery lovingly restored it in early 2010's. Great hidden treasure of SF.

The key site in Marfa, artist Donald Judd's ambitious, gigantic project to display the art/sculpture/construction/installation work of many artists. Walk around the outdoor sites under spectacular skies, tour the many buildings with exhibits.

Spectacular bridge over the Rio Grande gorge, seen in several films (Natural Born Killers, Terminator Salvation). Great shaded picnic tables on west side. Whatta view! Steel deck arch bridge, 10th highest in US, finished 1965.
Texas-sized State Park -- huge with many features, great roads and drives, river views, picnic areas, hikes. Pretty remote so uncrowded -- don't miss it after its National Park big brother next door.
Another great, well preserved structure of old Monterey, with that "Monterey" style balcony. From 1835; claims that it is the first California structure with a second story and a chimney!
Very nice recently opened visitor center for the Owens Lake and surroundings; lots on the history of the aqueduct. Good starting point to explore Owens Lake and its new visitor areas.
Fort Point is an amazing spot! Constructed 1853-1861. Fascinating history and well preserved. Remarkable Golden Gate bridge & bay views. Key location in Hitchcock's VERTIGO.

Amazing spot, lowest in North America; recently redesigned for maximum access. You can walk out onto the Basin from here for miles. Great fun and photo ops.

In the spring time this area is really amazing with wildflowers, birds, and reptiles. In the summer is the best time to visit the mines as you get to feel the big contrast in temperature from the dry summer heat to the cool damp inside of the mines. Sand mining and coal mining took place at this site, but only the sand mines are accessible via tours for the public due to air quality issues that occur with coal mines. There is a visitor center inside a large room of the sand mine that you can visit without taking a tour, but a tour really allows you to see what was going on there and the shear scale of it was amazing. In the walls of the sand mine there are fossilized tunnels from ancient shrimp, a really cool transition fault line, and some breathtaking rooms. Aquamarine blue water still flows from grottos in the hill. Most of them have sulfur scent and have had lots of rock work done around them in the past. The forest in the canyon is lush and home to a variety of animals. The canyon is shaded so is a great place to escape the heat.
