What is most impressive, besides the beauty, is that the bay is very clean, I saw people practicing windsurfing and jetski, which is unthinkable in most big cities.
Beautiful scenery of Wahweap Bay and Antelope Island, easily accessible by car from Route 89, with parking and free access.

This place is a Zion National Park postcard!
Let's face it, the road is one of the most beautiful in the world!

A must do when visiting Sedona.  The 4 hour round trip into the Verde River Valley on a restored passenger train pulled by classic 50s era engines.  Cars are air conditioned and have very comfortable seating.  But the real thrill is to experience at least part of your journey in the open air cars pulled along with the passenger cars.  Beautiful scenery, wildlife, and great narration by the train staff make this a vacation priority.  One very important tip - get in line to board early so you can sit in the TWO seat side of the car.  The views are much better there as the other side is mostly next to canyon walls.  Also try the prickly pear lemonade - it is delicious and refreshing.  In first class liquor service and complementary snacks are served on board.
dislikes: Limited views on one side of the car

reviews_attraction.text: An excellent place to start your journey to explore the South Rim area.  Information about the park is yours for the asking including direct conversation with a park ranger.  Considering the enormous volume of visitor traffic, it's a very smooth operation and facilities are clean, open and well maintained.  Of course the parking is a challenge, particularly after 9:30-10:00.  Best to go earlier if possible.   A small "grab and go" Cafe has pre-prepared sandwiches, and other light snacks.  Bicycle rentals are available at the visitor center, sizes for all ages.   The center is also central drop off point for the free bus service that makes round trips throughout the park.
likes: Central location for free bus service

reviews_attraction.text: Built in the 50s, this breathtakingly beautiful chapel is a must see.  The bronze crucifix dominates the interior with a powerful spirituality that you can feel.  The exterior cross seems to project from the mountain, yet as part of it.  Beautiful gardens surround the ramp leading to the chapel as well as the courtyard in front.  In spite of the crowds, you can sit in the chapel for peaceful reflection or prayer.  Limited parking is available at the chapel level, and much more below.  Golf cart shuttles run people up and back for no cost, but tips are appreciated.  Gift shop is on the lower level of the chapel.

An outstanding display of aircraft - both military and commercial.  Interactive displays, very knowledgeable staff can answer any questions you may have.  Do yourself a favor and take the guided tram tour of the outdoor museum, and the aircraft boneyard tour.  Very informative and fascinating.  The museum has 5 large air conditioned hangars of displays including the SR-71 Blackbird and other famous aircraft.  A well equipped gift shop and a cafe completes the tours.  Absolutely wonderful!

Outstanding zoo park featuring several areas of the world, i.e., North America, Asia, Australia, etc, and species native to their habitat in those areas.  Tons of interactive displays for kids, play areas, food and drink, restrooms located all over.  Miniature train takes you around and through the North America exhibit.  A Bob Evans - sponsored barn and surrounding had farm animals for up close encounters.  One of the best zoos we've seen around the U.S.

Jerome is a fascinating place to explore high in the mountains above Cottonwood Az.   An old copper mining town that nearly burned down had been partially restored by artists, merchants and other town folk into a tourist attraction with cool galleries, restaurants, shops of all kinds and an old hotel under renovation.  The views from that altitude are spectacular!   Bring plenty of water and good shoes, and take in the charm of a wonderful little town.
likes: Facilities & Services: Art galleries, restaurants, shops

reviews_attraction.text: Beautifully restored 1800s mission still run as a Catholic church by the Franciscans.  You'll feel calm and Serene as you sit and enjoy the spiritual aura of the church.  Free tours are given hourly and we'll worth your time.  On-site gift shop and on premises, gift shop, snack bar, etc.   Amazing display of Roman, Spanish and even Muslim architecture.   Beautiful murals, statuary a d wood carvings.

Ever since the Metroparks took charge of the Edgewater Park area, it became another jewel in the "Emerald Necklace ".  Building a new multi-level pavilion,  opening up huge space for people to play, cleaning up a former really crummy beach, and providing a safe, family friendly environment has become their trademark for success.  All of us in NE Ohio are fortunate to have them running the show.

A wonderful outdoor horticultural garden and a very well maintained greenhouse.  Outdoor has changing themes spring through Christmas holidays.  Greenhouse (conservatory) is open year round featuring orchid, cacti and bromilads.  The restaurant, Orchid Cafe has fresh salads, sandwiches, wraps, soups, etc, all very good.  Small gift shop too.  A hidden gem in Avon!

A great sunset viewing beach with a wide sandy area, restrooms and changing facilities.  Shelling is ok, not as good as blind pass beach just across the canal.  Can be rough on occasion with strong currents particularly if there are storms in the Gulf.  Water can be a bit murky at times depending on the tides and effluent from Blind Pass.

A very well kept old fashioned green house located off MLK Blvd.   Beautiful gardens in summer with themed displays inside.  Don't miss the poinsettia displays at Christmas.  A favorite spot for holiday family photos.  Maybe overshadowed by the Cleveland Botanical gardens, it should not be ignored.  Oh, and one more thing... it's FREE!

Great place for the whole family.  Plenty of exhibits and animals to see along with farm machinery to enjoy.   On-site restaurant serves the usual casual fare, usually well-prepared.  Can be crowded on weekends especially when themed shows or other organized activities are planned.  Very well maintained and clean restrooms.

It's a great place to get a different perspective of the canyon, although it can be crowded.  The welcome center is filled with maps, diagrams, and more information than you could possibly ask.  There's a gift shop with native American items and the usual kitsch.  Very good ice cream stand.  Fuel also available.

Beautiful ethnic themed small parks along the MLK Jr. parkway in Cleveland celebrating all the different ethnicities that built the city.  Difficult to see as there's no place to park and walk along to read and enjoy the statues, gardens, and messages of liberty and freedom.   Another waisted opportunity.....

A breathtakingly beautiful turn of the century church and surrounding buildings.  Run by Franciscans, traditional masses and ceremonies remain.  The organ will give you goosebumps.  Parking is a bit of a challenge.  Metered parking is available around the area, but must be paid via smartphone app.

Awesome displays and continually changing themes.  Christmas displays shouldn't be missed.  Members have reciprocity agreements with many botanical gardens throughout the country,  including Holden right here in Kirtland.  Spring flowers displays are excellent.

Great examples of lava flows right next to the road way and several loop trails to enjoy it up close and personal.  Although ancient, the a'a lava is well preserved and beautiful.  Cinder cones dot the area.  Watch for cyclists as it is a popular riding area.

Absolutely gorgeous conservatory and themed gardens.  Setting up for fall with pumpkin houses, mazes, etc.  Giant child play area.  A don't-miss opportunity if you have a few hours to spend.  The Chulilly exhibit is mind blowing (no pun intended).

A beautiful well-laid out plan with themed gardens, walking paths, and loaded with information at every stop.  Immaculately maintained and marked.  Nice cafe serving sandwiches, salads, etc.  Wine available.  A must see in the Naples area.

Had the mahi prepared with vegs and brown rice with prickly pear cactus sauce.  Outstanding!   Excellent service with excellent recommendations too.  Overall a great dining experience.  Not to be missed if you go to Sanibel.

A great place to walk around the lake have a little picnic, ride bikes, etc.  Very well maintained but pretty busy in summer.  Probably the best all around park in North Ridgeville.   Certainly could use more like it.

The narrated tours are very well presented and you're given tons of information.  The big house tour was fascinating and fun to ride on the tractor pulled wagon.  Many links to former movie scenes were pointed out.
Cleveland Metroparks is the pride of the area and seem to have the Midas touch handling parks and any outdoor recreation area.  Mill Stream Run is a typical example of their outstanding efforts.
The metro Parks are one of the best things about the Cleveland area.  Run and administrated by intelligent people who have vision, the city administration could learn an awful lot.
Beautiful visitors center with awesome displays tons of graphics, printed material, and informed, helpful staff.  Gift shop has unique articles with a minimum of Chinese junk.

That was awesome!  Nothing beats walking on the edge of a volcano crater.  Budget enough time to explore the entire park, especially the steam vents, lava tubes, and lava fields!  Nothing beats seeing the true power and beauty of nature first hand.  For those with health issues, check with your health professional before proceeding.  Exposure to sulfur is a real threat and can provoke further health problems.  If Kilauea isn't on your 'must-do list,' add it.  It beats tanning on the beach, any day!

I've never expressed emotions at an exhibit, in a museum, until I visited here. The exhibits curator did an excellent job illustrating the raw emotions, pain, and devestation of Hurricane Katrina.  It has a few  #kidfriendly demonstrations but the Katrina exhibit isn't comprehendible by young children.  The Mardi Gras exhibit on the other hand is perfect for children.  I'll always remember this experience and carry it with me forever!  #Letsguide

Maybe I should have done more research before visiting, but it felt like a tourist trap.  Be ready to pay a premium to see the Grand Canyon.  All the tickets and excursions are very expensive!  You're not allowed to take photos with your personal device/camera on the Skybridge.  The highlight of the experience was the drive.  It is visually stunning and offers a plethora of enrichment opportunities.

If you came here for just the turtles be prepared to be disappointed.  The anticipation is real though; every object in the ocean will look like a turtle!  But maybe I came on an off day though....Parking is non-existent so be prepare park on the side of the road then a hike. It's a good beach to spend time with family, tan, or catch a few waves but not an overabundance of turles.

The Meteor Crater is a marvelous geological landmark and it's worth every penny.  Our tour guide was fabulous; he throughly describing the scientific aspects of the crater mixed with his cultural heritage.  Viewing the crater itself is a once in a lifetime experience.  You won't be sorry you took this 40 minute drive from Flagstaff to see the meteor crater!  #Letsguide

This place is a diamond in the rough!  It provides the best view of the Grand Canyon at Sunset.  Besides its stunning views, the Desert Views Watchtower is a Native American masterpiece.  The exhibit, on the first floor, takes you through the Watchtowers history and also contains the gift shop.  Everything about this sight is spectacular and worth the extra drive!

I would definitely recommend visiting this museum if you're visiting New Orleans.  The Merchant Marine is the best and most rememberable exhibit.  I was surprisingly uneffected/moved by this particular museum; unlike the other WWI and WWII museums I've visited in the past.  Nevertheless, this museum should be apart of your New Orleans travel itinerary.

My first time zip lining was amazing!  I couldn't have asked for a better experience from a family owned business.  The staff/family connected with the entire group and even told us unique stories about the poperty.  But moat importantly the zip lining experience was riveting!  It is completely worth the drive to Rayville!!!

Floats are a quintessential element of New Orleans Mardi Gras celebration.  Mardi Gras World allows you to experience these floats up close and personal!  You'll be able to experience all of the classics floats and character which is extremely #kidfriendly.  The tour is phenomenal and jam packed with goodies/information.

An excellent place to whale watch with the entire family for free!  The views along the trail of the lighthouse and the ocean make it worthwhile.  I personally enjoyed the cool breeze and plant/wildlife along the route. Parking can be a little unpredictable, but the path is both accessibility and stroller-friendly.

It's a very unique atmosphere and full of information which is any museum enthusiasts dream!  The museum even allows you to drink on your self guided tour;  I fell in love with New Orleans "Sazerac" drink due to this luxury.  The employees/guides are very knowledgeable and will answer any questions!

This was my second Cirque de Solei show and it was phenomenal!  The stage performers and musicians were immaculate this easily one of the most impressive performance I've ever seen.  My only warning is this particular Cirque de Solei show isn't for children.  The staff is amazing and helpful.

A charming little museum of modern art.  It's an intimate viewing experience perfect for a date and art enthusiast.  The museum might be small, but the exhibits make a significant impact on the community.  Hats off to the curator for always rotating a fresh collection of art to Kansas City.

I visited the National World War I Museum for the first time recently.  I thoroughly enjoyed the experience the museum provides; the museum provides a great blend of video/written media & artifacts.  I would highly recommend visiting this museum if you are blessed with the opportunity.

The museum exceeded my expectations!  The modern art collection was particulary engaging. Ragnar Kjartansson "The Visitors" exhibit in the modern art collection expanded my definition of visual art.  Its "Pay-What-You-Wish" promotion is the best deal museum deal in town!  #Letsguide

The scenery alone makes the drive worth it!  I've never learned so much about plantation owners, sugar cane, and it's impact on slavery in Louisiana;. It was very enlightening. Please give yourself enough time, an hour or two, to walk the entire grounds during your visit.

Arrowhead point offers a great view of The Valley during both Sunset and Sunrise.  The parks trails are a good place to exercise or to enjoy the natural landscape of The Valley.  It's not your typical tourist attraction but an interesting detour if you're in the area!

A fabulous addition to the South Rim Trail.  It's a great place to refuel and enjoy a change of scenery/museum and gift shop along the trail. The building is temperature controlled, has a restroom(s), and also acts as an observation deck.

Very fun and well structured tour of the Warner Bros. Studio.  Our tour guide provide us with tons of history/I information and answered all of our questions.  I would recommend talking this tour if you're visiting the Los Angeles area.

The Bellagio Fountains are absolutely stunning; the musical accompaniment can be heard from any vantage point on the Bellagio Hotel sidewalk. If you're visiting Las Vegas you must this iconic landmark.
Sadly I visited the Atlanta Botanical Garden in December... The indoor green houses/habitats were gorgeous and definitely worth seeing. If you're in Atlanta during the Spring this is specular gem.
Great park!  Thoroughly enjoyed spending time with family and friends here.  It was very well maintained.  There are plenty of playgrounds equipment, fishing, and wildlife for everyone to enjoy.
This experience is very educational and is full of unique facts. The museum is also free and easy access using the Marta system. I was expecting the exhibit to be larger and more interactive.

(Translated by Google) In the beautiful city park Golden Gate Park, next to a botanical garden and the De Youg museum of modern art, is hosted this beautiful
Academy of Sciences, the only "museum" in the world to contain, under the same roof, a gigantic and beautiful aquarium, a planetarium and a rainforest arranged on several floors within a crystal sphere.
For a complete and exhaustive visit, you need a complete day, so it's better not to come here in a hurry. Also because the aquarium is a very varied and intense experience, it makes no sense to visit it in less than 2 hours. The rain forest in my opinion, while beautiful, especially for the multitude of butterflies that accompany the visit, should be improved by hiding a bit 'of too much metal that you see.
There is also a buffet restaurant and cafeteria.
Price quite high but affordable.
Good connection with the city thanks to the various lines of public transport that touch the Golden Gate Park.

(Original)
Nel bel parco cittadino Golden Gate Park, a fianco di un giardino botanico e del De Youg museum of modern art, è ospitata questa stupenda
Accademia delle Scienze, unico "museo" al mondo a contenere, sotto lo stesso tetto, un gigantesco e bellissimo acquario, un planetario e una foresta pluviale disposta su più piani all'interno di una sfera di cristallo.
Per una visita completa ed esaustiva serve un giorno completo, quindi meglio non venire qui di fretta. Anche perché l'acquario risulta un'esperienza molto variegata e intensa, non ha senso visitarlo in meno di 2 ore. La foresta pluviale a mio avviso, pur bellissima, soprattutto per la moltitudine di farfalle che accompagnano la visita, dovrebbe essere migliorata nascondendo un po' del troppo metallo che si vede.
Presente anche un ristorante a buffet e caffetteria.
Prezzo abbastanza alto ma abbordabile.
Buono il collegamento con la città grazie alle varie linee di mezzi pubblici che sfiorano il Golden Gate Park.
likes: Unique combination of attractions (aquarium, planetarium, rainforest)
dislikes: Excessive visible metal in rainforest exhibit

reviews_attraction.text:
(Translated by Google) Beautiful California national park, with different environments to visit, mountains, dunes, Joshua tree forest, ... The main visitor center is that of Kelso, near the railway, where there are also remains of the ancient settlement. In the area of ​​the mountains it is easy to meet herds of big horn, the typical majestic mountain sheep of the USA. Very nice to visit, suitable for everyone. And last but not least ... you don't pay the entrance.
Some advices:
- to see the bighorn herds, enter from Baker (west entrance) and head towards Kelso with the Kabaker rd.
- for a walk in the josha tree forest, enter the Ivanpah rd., and head towards Cima
- to see the white sand dunes, take the Kabaker rd between the Kelso visitor center and the south entrance on road 40
- however always bring plenty of water, in summer the heat is torrid.

(Original)
Bellissimo parco nazionale della California, con diversi ambienti da visitare, montagne, dune, foresta di Joshua tree,... Il principale visitor center è quello di Kelso, vicino alla ferrovia, dove si trovano anche resti dell'antico insediamento. Nella zona delle montagne è facile incontrare branchi di big horn, le tipiche maestose pecore di montagna degli USA. Molto bello da visitare, adatto a tutti. È non ultimo... non si paga l'ingresso.
Alcuni consigli:
- per vedere le mandrie di bighorn, entrare da Baker (ingresso west) e dirigersi verso Kelso con la Kabaker rd.
- per passeggiata nella josha tree forest, entrare dalla Ivanpah rd., e puntare verso Cima
- per vedere le dune di sabbia bianca, percorrere la Kabaker rd tra il visitor center di Kelso e l'ingresso sud sulla strada 40
- comunque portarsi sempre MOLTA ACQUA, d'estate il caldo è torrido.

(Translated by Google) Very beautiful and varied park.
It is actually divided into three areas plus a famous viewpoint, so it can be divided into 4 areas: the "Island in the sky" district in the north, accessible from Moab, with beautiful viewpoints on the river and its bends, and on the famous "dinosaur footprint" (a particular canyon shape) - the Mesa Arch, one of the most striking shots for any photographer, located at the gates of "Island in the sky" - the district of Needles "to the east, where they abound walks for all tastes and abilities, accessible by descending an hour south of Moab, at the entrance to which there is also the famous "newspaper rock", the wall with petroglyphs from various eras - and finally the wild district of "the Maze "to the west, where it is good to venture only if accompanied or properly prepared.

(Original)
Parco molto bello e vario.
In realtà si divide in tre aree più un famoso punto panoramico, quindi può essere diviso in 4 aree: il distretto di "Island in the sky" al nord, accessibile da Moab, con bellissimi punti panoramici sul fiume e le sue anse, e sulla famosa "impronta di dinosauro" (una particolare conformazione di canyon) - il Mesa Arch, uno degli scatti più suggestivi per ogni fotografo, che si trova alle porte di "Island in the sky" - il distretto di Needles" a est, dove abbondano camminate per tutti i gusti e tutte le capacità, accessibile  scendendo un'oretta a sud di Moab, è al cui ingresso si trova anche la famosa "newspaper rock", la parete con petroglifi di varie epoche - e infine il selvaggio distretto di "the Maze"a ovest, dove è bene avventurarsi solo se accompagnati o debitamente preparati.

(Translated by Google) Very nice park, for a short relaxing visit if you pass by in the area.
Here you can walk on the beautiful coral sand dunes, a taste of desert.
The dunes were formed about 10,000 years ago, and since then they have continued their slow movement, which changes their shape and configuration continuously. Recommended the experience of climbing to the top of the dunes and then running down to the base ;-). Parrco also suitable for children.
The park is easy to reach, from Kanab, from Hurricane, from Fredonia - at the end you take a long dirt road, however accessible to all cars because it is kept in good condition - the entrance costs $ 8 per car, it is one State Park, so admission is not included in the National Parks Annual Pass.

(Original)
Parco molto bello, per una breve visita rilassante se si passa in zona.
Qui si può passeggiare sulle belle dune di sabbia color corallo, un assaggio di deserto.
Le dune si sono formate circa 10.000 anni fa, e da allora continuano il loro lento movimento, che ne modifica forma e configurazione continuamente. Consigliata l'esperienza di salire in cima alle dune e poi correre giù fino alla base ;-) . PArco adatto anche per i bambini.
Il parco è facile da raggiungere, da Kanab, da Hurricane, da Fredonia - si percorre alla fine una lunga strada sterrata, comunque accessibile a tutte le auto perché tenuta in buone condizioni - l'ingresso costa 8$ per auto, si tratta di uno State Park, quindi l'ingresso non è compreso nell'Annual Pass dei parchi nazionali.

(Translated by Google) Here nature has truly found a way to make something great eternal.
Very easy to visit even simply passing by car through the view points, and even more beautiful is to walk to discover the giants of the ancient forest.
It is impressive to see the remains of the ancient giant sequoias dating back to the late Triassic ... 225 million years ago! And here man feels small and insignificant, here nature shows us how for her we are only a small nuisance of passage ... here the first human remains date back to "only" 8000 years ago :-) Of the ancient inhabitants, also more recent, there are still interesting petroglyphs.
Beautiful, it is worth a visit!

(Original)
Qui la natura ha veramente trovato modo di rendere eterno qualcosa di grandioso.
Molto facile da visitare anche semplicemente passando in auto per i view points, e ancor più bello è passeggiare alla scoperta dei giganti della antica foresta.
E' impressionante vedere i resti delle antiche sequoie giganti, risalenti al tardo Triassico ... 225 milioni di anni fa ! E qui l'uomo si sente piccolo e insignificante, qui la natura ci dimostra come per lei siamo solo un piccolo fastidio di passaggio ... qui i primi resti umani risalgono a "solo" 8000 anni fa :-) Degli antichi abitanti, anche più recenti, si trovano ancora interessanti petroglifi.
Bellissimo, vale la pena una visita!

(Translated by Google) Tiny ranch dating back to 1888, built by a certain John Wesley Wolfe who moved to this beautiful area in Arches Park following a serious leg injury sustained in the civil war.
It is a main cabin, made of wood, without even a floor, plus a second even smaller addition after the arrival of the daughter and son-in-law who joined John about 20 years later.
The ranch is located near a small stream, which provided running water to the animals.
If you venture on the trail of ascent to the Delicate Arch, it is worth stopping for some romantic photos with a flavor of other times, especially with the colors of the sunset ;-)

(Original)
Piccolissimo ranch risalente al 1888, costruito da un certo John Wesley Wolfe che si trasferì in questa bellissima area nel parco di Arches a seguito di una grave ferita a una gamba riportata nella guerra civile.
Si tratta di una cabin principale, in legno, senza nemmeno pavimento, più una seconda ancor più piccola aggiunta dopo l'arrivo della figlia e genero che raggiunsero John circa 20 anni più tardi.
Il ranch si trova in prossimità dei un piccolo ruscello, che offriva acqua corrente agli animali.
Se vi avventurate sul trail di salita al Delicate Arch, vale la pena fermarsi per qualche romantica fotografia dal sapore di altri tempi, soprattutto coi colori del tramonto ;-)

(Translated by Google) A trading post with an interesting history, which has been kept in excellent condition, and it is a pleasure to visit it with a short visit perhaps during a transfer between parks (I stopped on my way from Monument Valley to Petrified Forest).
Although built in earlier times, its history becomes better known when it was purchased by the Navajo art dealer, John Lorenzo Hubbell in 1878 - its important trade, in fact it allowed the survival of the natives who could thus sustain themselves with their own productions.
The place is still very well stocked with artifacts and agricultural machinery of the time, just beautiful.

(Original)
Un trading post dalla storia interessante, che è stato mantenuto in ottime condizioni, ed è un piacere visitarlo con una breve visita magari durante un trasferimento tra parchi (io mi ci sono fermato sulla mia strada da Monument Valley a Petrified Forest).
Anche se costruito in tempi precedenti, la sua storia diventa più conosciuta quando fu acquistato dal commerciante di arte Navajo, John Lorenzo Hubbell nel 1878 - commercio il suo importante, infatti permise la sopravvivenza dei nativi che così potevano sostentarsi con le proprie produzioni.
Il luogo è ancora molto fornito di manufatti e macchine agricole del tempo, proprio bello .

(Translated by Google) It is a large cave, near Route 66, in the Peach Springs area. In my opinion nothing special, it is fine for children - in fact already at the entrance we receive a large dinosaur ...
However it depends what you are looking for ... for me the charm of visiting the cave is thwarted by how the cave itself has been exploited for tourism ... I do not agree with totally ruining what nature has built in 65 million years, a sort of motel with some suites to spend the night (inside the cave! :-()
In short, it would have been a beautiful cave to see, but they made it lose all its charm ...

(Original)
Si tratta di una grande grotta, vicino alla Route 66, nella zona di Peach Springs. Secondo me nulla di speciale, va bene per i bambini - in effetti già all'ingresso ci riceve un grande dinosauro ...
Comunque dipende cosa cerchi ... per me il fascino della visita alla grotta è vanificato dal come la grotta stessa è stata sfruttata turisticamente ... non sono d'accordo con il rovinare totalmente quello che la natura ha costruito in 65 milioni di anni, vi hanno sistemato dentro pure una specie di motel con qualche suite per passare la notte (all'interno della grotta! :-(  )
Insomma, sarebbe stata una bella grotta da vedere, ma le hanno fatto perdere tutto il fascino ...

(Translated by Google) One of the most impressive places in Arches park. Unfortunately, being very easily reachable from a convenient parking in a few minutes, most of the park's visitors are concentrated here. So forget about being able to take beautiful nature photos in season of tourist influx.
It is possible to climb inside the immense vault formed by the two arches, and from here the spectacle is beautiful.
I recommend using a wide-angle lens (eg 10 mm) otherwise it is difficult to photograph the two arches together being underneath, because they are really big.

(Original)
Uno dei luoghi più impressionanti nel parco di Arches. Purtroppo, essendo molto facilmente raggiungibile da un comodo parcheggio in pochi minuti, qui si concentra la maggior parte dei visitatori del parco. Quindi dimenticatevi di poter fare delle belle foto naturalistiche in stagione di afflusso turistico.
È possibile salire all'interno della immensa volta formata dai due archi, e da qui lo spettacolo è bellissimo.
Consiglio uso di obiettivo grandangolo (es. 10 mm) altrimenti è difficile fotografare i due archi insieme stando i sotto, perché sono veramente grandi.

(Translated by Google) Surely very beautiful outlook, and not by chance here, on the famous rock terrace, many scenes of famous western films are set.
Easy to reach, along the circular route by car ... perhaps a little too easy to reach ... and in fact an annoying amount of people is concentrated here, at least in the months of greatest tourist turnout. In the vicinity there is also a market, many stalls of local Indian crafts, and the possibility of taking pictures on horseback (for a fee).
In short, a great place, but ruined by too much tourism ;-)

(Original)
Overlook sicuramente molto bello, e non a caso qui, sulla famosa terrazza di roccia, sono ambientate tante scene di famosi film western.
Posto facile da raggiungere, percorrendo  il percorso ad anello in auto ... forse un po troppo facile da raggiungere ... e infatti qui si concentra una quantità fastidiosa di gente, perlomeno nei mesi di maggior affluenza turistica. In prossimità si trova anche un mercatino, tante bancarelle di artigianato locale indiano, e la possibilità di effettuare (a pagamento) foto su cavallo.
Insomma, un gran bel posto, ma rovinato dal troppo turismo ;-)

(Translated by Google) Small but interesting Catholic church in the center of San Francisco, in front of the Yerba Buena gardens.
Founded in 1870, therefore of very recent construction, and almost completely destroyed by the 1906 earthquake, it was then rebuilt with the mixed Gothic and Neo-Romanesque aspect it presents today.
Several masses are held there every day.
Nothing special, but also for those who are not interested in it as a place of worship, it is worthwhile if you are in the area for a short visit and some photographs.

(Original)
Piccola ma interessante chiesa cattolica in pieno centro a San Francisco, davanti ai giardini Yerba Buena.
Fondata nel 1870, quindi di costruzione molto recente, e quasi completamente distrutta dal terremoto del 1906, fu poi ricostruita con l'aspetto misto gotico e neoromanico con cui si presenta oggi.
Vi si tengono diverse messe tutti i giorni.
Nulla di speciale, ma anche per chi non ne è interessato in quanto luogo di culto, vale la pena se si è in zona per una breve visita e qualche fotografia.

(Translated by Google) Small church in Chinatown in San Francisco.
The construction work dates back to 1853. From the date of its completion until 1891 this was the city's cathedral, and was later replaced in this role by the most modern Cathedral of the Assumption of Mary.
Renovated in 2012, it appears neat and well kept.
Beautiful tower clock, overlooking the small square of St. Mary's square.
A place of worship and peace, it is definitely worth a short visit if you go by the famous district of the city.

(Original)
Piccola chiesa in Chinatown a San Francisco.
I lavori di costruzione risalgono al 1853. Dalla data del suo completamento fino al 1891 questa fu la cattedrale della città, venne poi rimpiazzata in questo ruolo dalla più moderna Cattedrale sell'Assunzione di Maria.
Ristrutturata nel 2012, appare in ordine e ben tenuta.
Bello l'orologio della torre, che si affaccia sulla piccola piazza di St. Mary's square.
Luogo di culto e di pace, vale sicuramente la pena una breve visita se si passa dal famoso quartiere della città.

(Translated by Google) not easy to find, because the sign is very small and not very evident - this Buddhist temple is on the fourth floor of a normal building where various cultural activities, including a music school, are hosted.
It is a very small room, just a room, very richly decorated. It is a true place of prayer for the faithful of the area so remember, if you go to visit it, that photographs are not allowed here and it is logically necessary to respect the faithful with a silent attitude.

(Original)
non facile da trovare, perché l'insegna è molto piccola e poco evidente - questo tempio buddista si trova al quarto piano di un normale palazzo in cui sono ospitate varie attività culturali, compresa una scuola di musica.
Si tratta di un ambiente molto piccolo, giusto una stanza, molto riccamente addobbato. E' un vero luogo di preghiera per i fedeli della zona quindi ricordatevi, se andate a visitarlo, che qui non sono ammesse fotografie ed è logicamente necessario rispettare i fedeli con un atteggiamento silenzioso.

(Translated by Google) The story told by graffiti on a rock wall, where it seems that over time everyone has enjoyed making their own contribution (unfortunately, even some modern idiot ...).
It is located near Moab (about 80 km south), so it is a must for anyone visiting the Canyonlands area.
It seems that the first petroglyphs date back to the Anasazi (2,000 years ago), then the works of Fremont, Navajo, Pueblo and others were added.
Nice, easy to reach, interesting. Recommended!

(Original)
La storia raccontata dai graffiti su una parete di roccia, dove sembra che nel tempo un po' tutti si siano divertiti a dare il proprio contributo (purtroppo anche qualche cretino moderno ...).
Si trova nei pressi di Moab (circa 80 Km a sud), quindi è una meta obbligata per chi sta visitando la zona di Canyonlands.
Sembra che i primi petroglifi risalgano agli Anasazi (2.000 anni fa), si sono poi aggiunte le opere di Fremont, Navajo, Pueblo e altri.
Bello, facile da raggiungere, interessante. Consigliato!

(Translated by Google) In my opinion this is the most beautiful vantage point that is encountered in the itinerary by car inside the Monument Valley park.
Moreover, in general there is not the same annoying amount of people here, for example, at John Ford or other famous landmarks.
Here the look sweeps over truly immense distances, being the overlook positioned at a good height on the valley, the mitten stand in front in all their majesty.
From the car park you can walk to your liking.

(Original)
A mio avviso questo è il punto panoramico più bello che si incontra nell'itinerario in auto all'interno del parco di Monument Valley.
Oltretutto in genere qui non c'è la stessa quantità fastidiosa di gente che si trova ad esempio al John Ford o altri punti famosi.
Qui lo sguardo spazia su distanze veramente immense, essendo l'overlook posizionato a una buona altezza sulla valle, i mitten si ergono di fronte in tutta la loro maestosità.
Dal parcheggio auto è possibile camminare a proprio piacimento.

(Translated by Google) Main view point of the Canyon of Island in the Sky, easy to reach by anyone in a few steps from the car park.
However, not always from here you can enjoy the best view, the Colorado is in fact very far away and sometimes the mist detracts from the sharpness of the opposite side.
However, from here a beautiful walk of about a kilometer and a half starts, with breathtaking terraces, some even a little dangerous, be careful not to get too close to the rim!

(Original)
View point principale del Canyon di Island in the Sky, facile da raggiungere da chiunque in pochi passi dal parcheggio auto.
Non sempre però da qui si gode della vista migliore, il Colorado è infatti molto lontano e a volte la foschia toglie nitidezza al versante opposto.
Comunque da qui parte una bellissima passeggiata di circa un kilometro e mezzo, con terrazze mozzafiato, alcune anche un po' pericolose, attenzione a non avvicinarsi troppo al rim!

(Translated by Google) If you enter the Valle Dell Morte from the West, this is a first point where it is worth stopping, it is only an overlook, but the scenery is noteworthy, here the natural conditions are extreme, no water, no vegetation, even rare the inevitable crows that are more common in other places. Continuing a few kilometers eastwards you will arrive at the fork with the dirt road that leads to the parking lot where the Darwin Falls Trail starts.

(Original)
Se entri nella Valle Dell Morte da Ovest, questo è un primo punto dove vale la pena fermarsi, si tratta solo di un overlook, ma lo scenario è degno di nota, qui le condizioni naturali sono estreme, niente acqua, niente vegetazione, rari anche gli immancabili corvi che in altri punti sono più comuni.  Proseguendo qualche kilometro verso est si arriva alla biforcazione con la strada sterrata che porta al parcheggio dove parte il Trail delle Darwin Falls.

(Translated by Google) In the wharf area, west of Fisherman's Wharf and a short walk from the famous Pier 39, is this maritime museum. In reality there is not much to see, when I went, the two ships could not be visited internally, but only from the outside. The Eureka ferry is very interesting and interesting, and contains many vintage cars and trucks.
Worth a visit (which still lasts a couple of hours) despite the entrance fee.

(Original)
Nella zona dei moli, a ovest del Fisherman's Wharf e a pochi passi dal famoso Pier 39, si trova questo museo marittimo. In realtà non c'è molto da vedere, quando sono andato io, i due velieri non erano visitabili internamente, ma solo dall'esterno. E' invece ben visitabile e interessante il traghetto Eureka, molto grande, e contenente molte auto e camion d'epoca.
Vale la pena una visita (che comunque dura un paio d'ore) nonostante il biglietto d'ingresso.

(Translated by Google) In the wharf area, west of Fisherman's Wharf and a short walk from the famous Pier 39, is this maritime museum. In reality there is not much to see, when I went, the two ships could not be visited internally, but only from the outside. The Eureka ferry is very interesting and interesting, and contains many vintage cars and trucks.
Worth a visit (which still lasts a couple of hours) despite the entrance fee.

(Original)
Nella zona dei moli, a ovest del Fisherman's Wharf e a pochi passi dal famoso Pier 39, si trova questo museo marittimo. In realtà non c'è molto da vedere, quando sono andato io, i due velieri non erano visitabili internamente, ma solo dall'esterno. E' invece ben visitabile e interessante il traghetto Eureka, molto grande, e contenente molte auto e camion d'epoca.
Vale la pena una visita (che comunque dura un paio d'ore) nonostante il biglietto d'ingresso.

(Translated by Google) A very short walk to get a first view of the famous Delicate Arch. Of course I definitely recommend then tackling the Trail that leads directly to the base of the arch, but it is more demanding (a couple of hours and terrible heat in summer), but it is worth It is also worth a view and some photos from this Trail, which is absolutely within everyone's reach. The arch remains far away, but clearly visible.

(Original)
Una brevissima passeggiata per avere una prima vista del famoso Delicate Arch. Ovviamente consiglio sicuramente di affrontare poi il Trail che porta direttamente alla base dell'arco, ma è più impegnativa (un paio d'ore e un caldo terribile in estate), ma vale la pena anche una vista e qualche foto da questo Trail, che invece è assolutamente alla portata di tutti. L'arco resta lontano, ma ben visibile.

(Translated by Google) One of the many points where it is worth stopping when visiting the Arches park. Nothing special, but the "balanced rock" is certainly a peculiarity that is worth photographing.
A short path allows you to get around the pinnacle in 15 minutes.
Convenient access from the car park opposite.
On the opposite side of the road a driveway leads to a picnic area, with tables and benches in the shade.

(Original)
Uno dei tanti punti dove vale la pena fermarsi nel visitare il parco di Arches. Nulla di speciale, ma la "balanced rock" risulta sicuramente una particolarità che vale la pena fotografare.
Un corto sentiero permette di aggirare il pinnacolo in 15 minuti.
Comodo accesso dal parcheggio di fronte.
Sul lato opposto della strada parte un vialetto che porta a una area picnic, con tavoli e panche all'ombra.

(Translated by Google) A little adventure in Arches park.
Very beautiful route but reserved for excursions with a transit permit and accompanied by a ranger. Here you can get lost and the track is sometimes not easy. In the narrow passages in the canyons, largely in the shade, you don't get too hot, but it is still essential to bring water.

(Original)
Un po' di avventura nel parco di Arches.
Percorso molto bello ma riservato a escursione con permesso di transito e accompagnati da ranger. Qui ci si può perdere e il tracciato a volte non è facile. Negli stretti passaggi nei canyon, In gran parte in ombra, non si soffre troppo caldo, ma è indispensabile comunque portare acqua.
dislikes: Must be accompanied by a ranger

reviews_attraction.text:
(Translated by Google) Nice walk of about half an hour, preferably with the help of a person to take the car from the start to the end parking lot.
The name of the valley is due to the tall tower that resemble the skyscrapers of the famous NYC boulevard.
Relaxing, simple, easy and relaxing walk. In the morning largely in the shade.

(Original)
Bella passeggiata di circa mezz'ora, meglio se con l'aiuto di una persona che porti l'auto dal parcheggio di inizio a quello di fine.
Il nome della valle è dovuto agli alti torrione che ricordano i grattacieli del famoso viale di NYC.
Passeggiata rilassante, semplice, agevole e rilassante. Alla mattina in gran parte in ombra.

(Translated by Google) Very nice area, ideal for many excursions for every taste and every ability. Presence of important natural parks, the closest is the Grand Canyon, just to the north. But a short distance to the south you can also reach the wooded area of ​​Flagstaff.

(Original)
Zona molto bella, ideale per tante escursioni per ogni gusto e ogni capacità. Presenza di importanti parchi naturali, il più vicino é il Gran Canyon, appena a nord. Ma a breve distanza verso sud si arriva anche nella zona boschiva di Flagstaff.

(Translated by Google) a good experience, it is worth doing.
Here you get a taste of the life of sailors and pilots on a floating city.

(Original)
una bella esperienza, vale la pena farla.
Qui si ha un assaggio della vita di marinai e piloti  su una città galleggiante.

Who needs a stairmaster when you can take the 143 steps down to the sand, a super chill spot to hang out, you can stroll miles in either direction on the sand.  Surfing,  boogie boarding is great there, but check the tide tables before you head out... It's a residential area with mansions on the ocean side and Neptune Avenue is also a great place to walk dogs, but no dogs are allowed on the beach there.  Great place to watch sunsets with the locals.  I actually should have given it one star so we can keep it all to ourselves.... raised a kid right across the street from Stone Steps and have zero regrets. There's some vacation rentals nearby, but since it's off the 101 there's really not much tourist traffic there.  There's quite a few budget places on the 101 if all you want to do is surf and have a place to crash. Leucadia has undergone some gentrification, but there is still the vibe and funk feel, a few remnants of the 70s. The Eagles lives and recorded there in the 1970s about a block to the South of the stairway, there's a little plaque that tells the story, and they reportedly wrote Hotel California there.
dislikes: No dogs allowed on the beach

reviews_attraction.text: This is a fabulous concert venue in the Summer months, where you can spread out a blanket and take in musical or theatre events- located right behind the Convention Center, if you are attending an event, think about bringing a jacket after dark or layered clothes, as it gets windy and it's on the bayfront.  Sometimes folding chairs, coolers are allowed and other events prohibited to be sure to check in advance what the rules are as they change based on what's going on there. On a typical, non event day expect to stroll around with great bayfront views, only 5 minutes from the Convention Center on foot so you get a lot of locals as well as people just out running, walking, or fishing. There are a few good places to fish on the piers, and the little part time restaurant is open with good food, mostly sandwiches but healthy choices and burgers...the park wraps around to vistas of the Coronado Bridge, and the megayachts that are sometimes berthed behind the Convention Center. You can catch a ride over to Coronado right at the base of the park by water taxi or ferry.

Idyllic setting with shaded areas and lots of things to do nearby- the library is right across the street, I spend a significant amount of time here. There is a nice gazebo, limited parking, almost 100% local visitors, very chill and mellow spot with events going on all the time on the weekends.  It's well patrolled and safe, there are not a lot of homeless people on Coronado so the usual issues with nice parks are not as prevalent in Coronado- you can't smoke anyplace on the island in public so that's a huge plus and a deterrent, obviously. It's the quintessential stroller park if you have little ones, and it's clean, the facilities and well maintained.  By the way, metered parking on island in most cases is 25 cents, so you will not have to pay much, if you find a spot - If you are looking for a chill spot in Coronado as a base while walking around, look no further- it's near the high school and the Performing Arts Center, so it gets busy on the surface streets during drop off and pickup times.

Panoramic views and access to the sand from just South of Moonlight Beach.  Wooden stairs with a place to rinse off the sand on the way up, and just a short stroll from the stairs to Moonlight Beach and  if you head South it is a lovely walk to the Swami's Beach area along the cliffs.  There is a lifeguard tower manned in the Summer months and no restrooms, so the nearest place with bathrooms is a 5 minute walk North to Moonlight Beach, and it's about a 15 minute walk to Swami's Beach along the sand if the tides are low enough.  Just inland from the stairway a few block is the epicenter of Encinitas Village with all the shops and food, supplies you would need.  Parking is limited, but it is only a short stroll from the center of town- you can hop right on or off the train within a few minutes.

If in San Diego, the 101 bus North from La Jolla UTC gets you there- if coming from the North, then from Encinitas Transit Station you can simply hop on the 101 South and work your way down the coast, stopping along the way at all the nice North County beaches and shops.  It's a very scenic ride from either direction and the beaches are far from the hotels and major tourist attractions- natural cliffs and miles of sandy beachfront, hiking in the trails and running is also very popular- much more to do than just sitting on the beach, but no restaurants or shops are nearby within walking distance.  Parking is ample, but is always limited on this beach in peak visitation periods like Summer weekends.

This is where the old school, serious surfers and the best local waves are. Not too far from Santa Barbara, the little enclave called Mussel Shoals doesn't have food but you can tank up in Montecito, Summerland, Santa Barbara from the North or Ventura from the South if you want to plan ahead, plan to linger here... it's a good place to organize a picnic and stay at the park, with enough grills and places to seat larger groups..

Be sure to check for road construction the upper Park roads are absolutely fabulous because they’re brand new there’s a small section that remains unfinished so in the long run  it is well worth it because the roads are absolutely wonderful not a bump the whole way up everything smooth. Delays could be an hour in one direction or a half an hour and the other it’s unpredictable and even the delays are not unpleasant

out of the hustle and bustle of PB...great views -expansive views of the pacific and the Southern vista all the way past Ocean Beach.
The bathrooms are clean- too much of a hill for the homeless to pass through, it's between PB and the La Jolla Mount Soledad area. Plenty of parking, well partolled and tons of places to chill and picnic- also a great place to watch the fireworks from Sea World in the Summer.

This is a great place to stop and get away from it all I wrote up on my bike I've been here many times there's a little library at the end of the bridge where you can borrow books and leave books right now it's sort of in disrepair and it needs a few good books but the flowers are absolutely beautiful you can stand on the east side of the bridge and see all the way over to the Bay and see the other Bridge

quiet and local park with kid's play area, on a cul de sac, off the beaten path and hard to find. Worth going to if you are looking for relative peaceful seclusion and a nice, fairly shaded play area, or BBQ/picnic tables as literally no one goes here from afar to speak of. Well patrolled by the cops and the neighbors.

The campgrounds and showers are well maintained and the sunset views can be stunning make sure to wear other footwear than flip-flops because the coral is a little rough sometimes when you're walking down by the beach there's lots of birds and wildlife and the park staff is very helpful and friendly.

This is a great park just as you come into Camarillo from Los Angeles just at the bottom of the hill it’s a picturesque rural setting on the way to the park and then it’s a quiet dog friendly park started with oaks it cost three dollars to get in and it’s worthIt they have clean bathrooms

This is one of the coolest places in central California to just chill especially when the creek is running very Serene environment with bathrooms a huge barbecue if you wanted to have a large group it's all so wonderful small children have their own little play place there

This is about an hour's drive from The salted sea and the weather was good I didn't get out of the car at East Chase's but it's a popular tourist destination in an area strewn with litter and garbage and people that are trying to sort things out and some that aren't...

Presidio Park overlooks the city the view is okay it's a quiet spot where you can have a picnic and that's where the Mormons actually first went to San Diego it has sort of sordid history... but it's a very pleasant location to spend the day.

We love to take the kids there and use the high dive, it has a really nice setup for both grownups to chill and the kids to swim. There's loads of sports facilities but the crown jewel is the pool and resort like setting that surrounds it.

I love Chicano Park it's a great place to hang out if you're on your way to and from Coronado now that the village is built up there's a million things to see and do right around the corner so it's definitely improved over the years

There's a few of these across the canyons in the area. Worth a trip with the kids if you go and see them they were built to connect passengers to the trolley system in place as the areas were isolated from the rail service.
I used to own the land at this Trailhead I have a lot of great memories you can hike all the way up to Seven Falls Trail and there's hardly any discernible fire damage in the area now
What a hidden gem I pulled in here paid $6 to stay for the day and just pulled up to a picnic table in my van and worked all day on odds and ends with the most beautiful view ever...
Kind of wonderful day walking around USC. You need to download an app onto your phone in order to get a pass to get on campus but it's beginning to open up.
Perfect venue for a party, we rented it for the kids and they had a really great time at Prom. Lots of interactive games and a small, hot area to dance.
Red Rock is a beautiful place to visit if you get a chance it's a long way from everything but take your best shot
It's a great place to hang out on the weekend has a nice coffee shop out front and it's suitable for any age
Nah... just drive over to CA and 12 minutes from here theres a nicer spot to spend time and money.

This is a great place to start your visit to San Francisco. It is located in the San Francisco Maritime National Historical Park. Right across from Ghirardelli Square. there is 4 Hour free parking to the north of this building. In the front part is the Object Collections it has large parts of sailing vessels and many other items. In theIn the back is another room that has lots of pictures of San Francisco's Maritime history. They also have very clean free public bathrooms.

Very nice place, been here many times.

The Museum houses over 2,500 works of Utah art, twentieth-century Soviet Realist art and American art,comprise the Museum's permanent collection.

It has  over 15 exhibitions annually and a beautiful outdoor sculpture garden.

The Museum is open Tuesday – Saturday 10am to 5pm, Wednesdays 10am to 9pm, and Sundays 3pm to 6pm. Closed Mondays and Holidays,

From Very hot to cold in 10 minuets. The temperature differential between the valley floor and the top of the Tram is usually about 30 degrees. Cars depart at least every half hour
The tram was completed in 1963. Nearly 18 million people have traveled the 2.5-mile ride, from an base elevation of 2,643 feet and ends at the Mountain Station – elevation 8,516 feet.

If you're ever passing through Blanding Utah this is one of the must visit places to go to. It's a Wonderful dinosaur museum it's very large and has a huge collection of many different dinosaurs and fossils. It's one of the best collections of dinosaur relics in any area that I've been in. They also have a nice gift shop where you can purchase items.

Went here with my my wife in the summer and it was very cold and windy so bring a jacket.
Just like Mark Twain said:
“The coldest winter I ever spent was a summer in San Francisco.”

This is by far hands down the best location to take a picture of the Golden Gate Bridge. The view was beautiful. The time around sunset is best.
Took lots of photos.

In April I went to Garland’s Navajo Rugs in Sedona, Arizona.
It is  is one of the best time to go there because of the  weather, not too hot or cold.
I talked to Dan Garland , the owner, he said he has many weavers bring rugs to him he has the second-largest display of rugs next to Richardson’s in Gallup.
Very large selection of rugs.

I went here to this place for my brother's son's wedding. they set up a beautiful tent that was about a hundred by 50 feet wide with beautiful decorations the park is mainly a large golf course with a country club they have really great restaurants with lots of food and catering and golf carts available for rent.

I was Married here in the Oakland California Temple of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.
Great visiror center with lots of information. It is the 15th constructed temple of the Church. The temple dedicated on November 19, 1964, by David O. McKay.

This place says it has the largest collection of Ancestral Puebloan (Anasazi) pottery on display in the Four Corners Region
I also Visited the  Edge of the Cedars Pueblo, a village inhabited by the ancestors of contemporary Puebloan peoples from AD 825 to 1125,

This is one of the new memorials here in Washington DC. I really love this it's very large it has plaques from all 50 states beautiful to reflecting pools beautiful scenery. it's very near the Washington Monument in between that and the Lincoln Memorial.

I took some photos of this place while floating down the route Potomac River on a boat. I've seen this many TV specials on the television on the Kennedy Center Honors tour. there are many different theaters here they are plays music and dances shows.

Stopped here on trip across the southwest. Many interesting things to see here.
This is a 900-year old ancestral Pueblo Great House of over 400 masonry rooms.
Al so see the reconstructed Great Kiva.
Took lots of photos as you can see.

This park is very long and narrow park right along College Boulevard right across the street from the mall in Brea California. It has lots of beautiful picnic tables and lots of shade trees and a nice playground for the kids to use.
Love this place. I come with my family every year. We like to watch the fisherman and the surfers. Lots of good places to ear around and many things to see. You can also rent a bike next to the pier.
We took a drive around  Sausalito  and stopped here by Dunphy Park. One of the best places we visited! I highly recommend if you are in the area, a must-see. Great open space, a wonderful experience.
Stopped to take photos of the Point Pinos Lighthouse It is the oldest operating lighthouse on the West Coast still active today. Open 5 days a week (closed Tu/W) 1-4pm, no reservations required.
Large selection of stuffed animals.   Collections of vascular and non vascular plants, invertebrate and vertebrate animals are maintained. Public exhibits and educational programs are offered.
This bridge crosses the Potomac River in Washington DC and takes you to the Lincoln Memorial on the east side of the river. I took a boat trip and under the bridge to Georgetown University.
I went here with my son and daughter around the  Memorial day weekend. It's a beautiful building with lots of plants glass all around. the plants are from all the states in the Union.

I spent many summer days here rafting down the river with my family.
This is definitely a place for locals. Great open space and popular with the young and old.
We stopped here at Healy hall on our visit to Georgetown University. It is a story building constructed around 1877. took picture of the cannon in front.
Been here this year. They have made many improvements. They have more selling booth and better restrooms. Great Navajo Arts and crafts to see here.
Been fishing and on boat rides here with family many times. Great place to cool off on a hot summer day to have a picnic and play in the water.
Tolls are only collected from westbound traffic at the toll plaza on the east side of the bridge. Toll rate for passenger cars is $5
Nice small park. You can get great photos  of boat coming in the harbor. Walk out the Jetty on the rocks and watch the surfers.

A great quick hike to experience just a small part of the Grand Canyon.  Windy, but of course wonderful views.  We were in decent shape and used to higher elevations when we did it.  We saw MANY hikers who were in dangerous situations from lack of water, inappropriate clothes, or just the lack of fitness to make it back out.  We were actually offering help to people on the trail.  Even though it's a short trail, remember that you go down first, THEN the hard part to come back out happens.  It is very easy to go further than you should.  Make sure to have plenty of water and snacks, good footwear, and appropriate clothes.  There is plenty of vertical relief immediately off the trail, so if you are afraid of heights or not used to mountaineering,  the view from above would probably be safer than the hike.

I've seen a lot of arches in the Moab area, and this one is the most famous and popular for a reason. It's spectacular. The view of the La Sal's in the background is phenomenal, and the arch being on the edge of the bowl and the trail not revealing the arch until you come around the dome just makes it phenomenal.  The hike is listed as strenuous, but it really isn't that bad.  We did it with a 3-yr old, 6-yr old, and 9-yr old and I only had to carry the 3-yr old about half of the time. There's one exposed steep climb on slickrock that could get VERY hot during the summer months, and the final walkway to the arch is a narrow (3-ft) wide path along a cliff, but other than that the hike is fairly easy. Make sure to do this hike, because it's amazing, even with the crowds.

Great monument with amazing views and even more amazing history. It's so close to the highway and the ruins are all over the canyon. You even get to access some of them. We hiked down into the canyon (1 mile round trip, a couple hundred vertical feet) and my 6 year old daughter made the hike fine. However, coming out is strenuous, and if you're not used to the elevation or if you have health issues and do the trail in the summer it could be very taxing or even dangerous. All in all, I highly recommend stopping if you're in the area, even if you only have a little bit of time. Parking was limited, so try to go during off-peak times.

Wonderful place for enthusiasts of natural and invasive weeds and thistles.  Mostly hot, not great views, but it is fun to ride along the trail with your kids for a quick bike ride.  If you want to connect with nature or really get a nice view or feel like you're out of the city, I suggest heading East up into the canyons.  But this is an open area where you might see some birds or wildlife if you get lucky.  I'm not quite sure what people are talking about when they mention you can get away from the noise, because you're always within earshot of the Legacy Highway.

Super fun bike trail.  It's not very long, but they've done a good job with features (optional jumps, small drops, and berms).  When I rode this the trail was fairly new and I still liked it.  The rocks make it a little bumpy, so rocking this on a hard tail might rattle you some, but having a trail designated to one way bike traffic while hikers can still safely use the area is awesome.  All trail systems should try to avoid unnecessary conflict between bikes and hikers like this trail does. Lots of cedar, loose rocks with hardpack dirt, and a moderate climb.

This is a staple and probably the most classic mtb ride of Moab, but I've soured on it some.  Lots of technical climbs and descents, but it can get crowded and is a brutal trail if you're not in decent shape. Like I said, LOTS of up and down portions that really sap your energy and rattle your head loose.  Yes, you have to do this, but there are other rides that are more fun, have higher average speeds, and cover more varied terrain. If you like challenging yourself with very technical super steep climbs, you'll love slickrock.

Awesome park, but can get very crowded. The playground is innovative with great use of the natural landscape.  Several trails through the park, paved and unpaved.  Open area on the north side with multiple pavilions. Creek access for kids to wade and play in Mill Creek. Water features near the playground allow kids to pump, dam, and release water through several water features. Go to the park early in the morning and avoid busy times during weekends. They did an EXCELLENT job with this large wooded and open area.

I love going to zoos and out of every zoo I've visited, Hogle Zoo is one of my favorite.  Maybe it's because I grew up with Hogle Zoo, maybe it's because I know the zoo well and what I want to see, or maybe it's because the zoo is the perfect size to spend a fun day with the kids, see tons of excellent animals, without feeling like you've walked 30 miles.  The only downside of the zoo is that as such a great zoo, it can get crowded.  Try going during weekdays or avoiding early afternoon.

Fun and flowy trail network with lots of different line options and sweeping sudden descents. I wish it had more grade at the bottom to really fly, but it's a very fun biking trail. You actually end up out of breath as you come down because there's not quite as much speed as you'd like to have fun on the features. Bike it later in the year when it gets very hardpacked and rides faster. Too early in the season and it's softer and slower. And go ahead and rip everything. It's all rideable.

Amazing!  I think it's probably the best way to view and feel the power of the falls.  If you're careful like me, you can do the tour and not get drenched.  I even walked up on the Hurricane deck for about 20 seconds.  However, it is very easy to get drenched on the walking tour as well, so plan accordingly. Unfortunately, you don't get to go into the caves or see them, but the close up view of the falls makes up for any of that.

I'd probably give it a 3.5 rating.  Fun place, but the prices were a little steep and there are more involved museums in Utah.  Of course, I might be spoiled because of the dinosaur artifacts in the state, but it still is a fun place to stop.  Kids went through it pretty quick, so I don't think I'd call it a destination, but if you're in the area and looking for something to do, especially when you're craving AC, check it out.
dislikes: Limited involvement compared to other museums

reviews_attraction.text: Great hike for families or those with young kids. It's also a loop so you're seeing fresh trail the whole way. The trail wraps around counterclockwise (stay right).  The tree is big and old, but not that visually different than other big and old trees. Again, it's a fun walk for adults, but a great trail for those with young kids that want to walk.

As a member of the LDS Church, this is an especially meaningful tour, but from a purely historic/secular standpoint it is fascinating to see the recreated and even original buildings that made up life in the early 1800s.  It is also very interesting to see the humble birthplace of a religion that has blossomed into nearly 16 million global members.

As a member of the LDS Church it was very interesting, but I think the historic aspect of the mechanics of printing from the early 1800s as well as the old preserved building was just as interesting as any religious aspect.  If you're curious about history or the region, it's worth taking the tour.

Of course there's the religious spiritual aspect that's wonderful, but from a purely historic aesthetic aspect, this is a beautiful building with gorgeous landscaping and a deep history. Only members of the religion are allowed inside, but others can respectfully visit the grounds.

I've done the tour several times growing up and Minnetonka is a wonderful cave to see.  It's not as well known, but that's part of the benefit.  You're not fighting crowds, the tour guides do a great job, and the cave itself is beautiful, not to mention the drive up the canyon.

A little underwhelming.  Having grown up in a farming community probably ruined the experience for me.  There are more impressive historic farms that do the same thing in Utah, but a nice place to visit and walk around with the kids nonetheless.

Tried it for the first time and I haven't been that nervous for a roller coaster for years.  Super fast, yet surprisingly smooth.  I get sick on rides, but was okay on this one because it is so smooth.
Beautiful terrace/tunnel with great acoustics. Hopefully you get to hear a skilled street performer playing music here. Make sure to tip them if you like the tunes.
Great museum.  The dinosaur exhibit always fascinates me, and they have a floor devoted to temporary exhibits so you can come back and always see something new.
Well preserved petroglyphs from many different ages. Right off the road, but very little parking in the area. Worth stopping and seeing if you're passing by.
Easy relatively safe hike to a pretty pool.  Often busy.  Most young kids (4+) should do fine on the hike. Younger kids will need closer supervision.
One of the biggest parts of the thrill of the "white coaster" is that it feels and looks totally unstable.  It's an ancient ride, but a classic.
Awesome playground.  Climb to the top of the tower, if you're brave enough.  The only issue is that it can get a little crowded.
Great ride.  Short, but very intense.  Not for the faint of heart. Not as smooth as it used to be.

Awesome experience, kids enjoyed the whole drive. We bought animal food(5dlls per small bag) I believe the more you buy you get a discount. We actually went around twice because two baggies weren't enough to feed half way through the path. These animals are so smart they are literally waiting to be fed. Be prepared to have drool on the inside and outside of your vehicle. Take Clorox wipes for clean up... Some of the animals have long horns, so yes did bang our car and even moved our side mirrors a bit, not a big deal but be cautious because some of them don't move or move super slowly. They do have car rentals for 25dlls I believe, that might be an option if you don't want any sort of damage to your vehicle. I RECOMMEND BUYING TICKETS ONLINE a day before, you save about 10dlls, which come to think of it is two baggies of food. I would go back in a heartbeat, family friendly and the experience is awesome. The walk about is small yet has a variety of animals as well. Take a few quarters to feed some of the animals, kids fed the goats and peacocks. It won't disappoint, totally worth the ride.

Amazing, hidden treasure. 15min walk from parking lot. The very beginning lots of sand, a bit steep. After that just a a bit more walking and dirt. Clearly states NO SANDALS, but yet I saw many shirtless and wearing sandals. Personally I would suggest comfortable shoes, lots of sunscreen if going during summer, cap and a bottle of water should be perfect. Parking fills up fast, I went around 10am, parking wasn't that bad. So probably the earlier the better. As well as picture taking of the Horseshoe, after we left there were so many people around the Horseshoe it was hard to get a good pic. Free, no fee, so go enjoy nature at it's best...

This place is Amazing. Totally free, but donations are welcomed. You take off your shoes before stepping in the temple, they have a locker room to place your shoes. If you are wearing clothes too revealing according to their guidelines they will ask nicely to wear a disposable hood. I did feel kind of awkward because I was touring the temple and people were praying and worshipping, I hope I wasn't disrespectful walking around and reading everything about their gods. It so beautiful, the details and marble all around. Pictures aren't allowed. I definitely recommend this hidden gem in Houston.

Definitely a new and colorful experience for me. All the scenery and brightness makes the kids go wild. Wear comfortable shoes, expect to walk around the passages for a good 1hr to 1 1/2. I was wearing shorts, regret that, some places are narrow to crawl into that I did get a few bruises on my knees. But no big deal, that's part of the fun. Try to go early, to enjoy every room without bumping into ppl constantly. It stars getting packed around noon. Have fun and definitely take a camera.

So much to explore, I was amazed as to how big some leafs are, literally my son's size. Expect to spend a few hours, you can take snacks and drinks to make experience with kids easier. Wear comfortable shoes as you will walk side to side, up and down. There's a playground for kids, so yes hand sanitizer is good to keep handy. Overall for the price it was totally worth it. There's a parking fee, but totally doable, we payed 7dlls and we were there for 4hrs.

Amazing guide, Natasha. Had lots of fun, best to reserve before you go, tours sell out fast. You aren't allowed to take any backpacks, tripods, purses, professional cameras. All you can take are hats, bottled water and cell phone. There is lots of walking so best to wear comfortable clothes and shoes. Some spots are kind of narrow, but shouldn't be a big deal. Entering the canyon are a few set of steep, narrow stairs. 46dlls per person, totally worth...

Kids had so much fun. Its included with the all access pass to stone mountain. It's a four lever jungle gym. Slides, different activities and flying foam balls everywhere. Totally child friendly, be prepared to stay there at least 30min, kids had the most fun here. Mainly for smaller kids but saw a few older ones so definitely be cautious letting kids play around the area...

Amazing place. Great for kids, 14.50 gets you to both aquarium and garden. The aquarium could of had more displays, but either way it was fun to see all those sea creatures. The garden was stunning. A lot of walking so make sure you take comfortable shoes. Lots of sunscreen if going during summer. So many great photos can be taken at this place. Simply in love...

Fun weekend road trip. 12dlls per person gets you to both natural formations, Bandera volcano and Ice cave. For the volcano it's a total of 20min walk, amazing views. The ice cave 10min walk total, as soon as you hit the second set of steps, you feel those 31 degrees. Magical, small yet so much history. Staff was super friendly and well informed.

Fun exploring the Caves. There is a 12dll fee. Military get a special card to enter all national parks for free, so ask. Wear comfortable shoes, lots of walking. In my case, I'm always cold so I did take a light jacket. It does get cold as you go deeper. A flashlight might come in handy but definitely optional. Have fun!!!

In the middle of no where, still a fun experience. 5dlls get you in, there are little souvenir shops. Line was long to take a pic, limit of 3 pics per person. There is a little hiking trail, not much to see but had to eat the whole enchilada, meaning was part of the experience. Restrooms are potty johns. A must try...

I am giving a 3 star only because in my humble opinion the aquarium was not worth the extra fee. It was too short and not much to see. The lego statues made it better but I would definitely not pay to go in there again. It does have lots of sea creature facts and my personal favorite the jelly fish display was a plus.

Beautiful downtown plaza. The millions invested are totally worth it. Nice to take a walk and play some chess or ping pong. Little shops and bars around the plaza, very convenient. Right across from Camino Real hotel and the Plaza Theater. Starbucks and the Coffee Box a good place to grab coffee and walk around.

Aztec cave trail. Easy, family friendly. Closed toe shoes, very rocky path. A bit challenging coming down. Probably like 45min back and forth. 5dlls to get in, definitely worth. There's other trails, so if you are planning on hiking more than one, best to arrive early. Opens at 8am, closed at 5pm.

Being so close to the statue of my childhood idol was great. There's a recording of Selena singing and a bit of her background. It is fenced in, but still good pictures can be taken of her. Fun experience, definitely recommended if you are near that area, plus you get to walk around the marina...

Got excited looking at all those bags and Prada shoes. There's a fence around for you to place a personal object, just like Paris. Remember it's a 75mph street so try to be careful when taking the pictures. Super cute, don't forget to wave at the camera...

Fun, walking around the garden trying to figure out the meaning of the sculptures. Going up the buildings rooftop top at night was a bonus, the city looks amazing at night. Definitely recommend, good luck finding parking. Construction work all around...

Such a treat, so relaxing. A must go, can't say no to free. Parking a downside, but most parked on the side to take a quick picture. If staying longer, a hassle to get a parking spot. Construction work all over, good luck...

After a long walk at  the beach, going to the pier a must do. A bit pricey, funnel cake around 15dlls. Yet, should be part of the experience. Lines do get long to ride the games. Live music, lots of eating options.
A bit disappointed, seems like the stars aren't properly taken care off. Some were faded, others so dirty that names couldn't be read. Still a great experience, payed 20dlls for whole day parking.
Drove there. Then walked down those amazing looking rock formations. A bit challenging, but not too complicated nor exhausting. Free, so go on and try for yourself...
Great splash park. Could use more cover seating. Kids had a blast and it's free so can't complain. The public pool just a few steps away, definitely a plus...
I've seen it on TV, so for me a must see. Drove down the hill, cute little street. Does get packed, but definitely a unique experience. Free
A 10 mile park, with wonderful sculptures, surrounded by trees. Such a beauty, even better if you take a bike ride around the whole park.
Speechless, beautiful place for a simple walk or a nights out. Lots of things to do around the bridge, bars, food, shopping...

My 11-year-old son and I were here early on a Saturday morning for the Cactus Flower 6k race (part of a trail series). We were only in town for a few days and managed to find this race on the calendar.

The park itself is pretty plain. The cost to get in ($5 or $6?) seems peculiar to me, since I don't know what the return was on my investment. Maybe that's just how the parks in Arizona/Phoenix work? Either that or I'm spoiled by all of the free parks in the midwest.

We ran on a very challenging course: lots of hills, sand gravel and so forth.

Hitting the trails for a long hike or something? Bring lots of water and snacks. There's not much in the way of shade or anything out there. :)

Just spent the weekend there. I was very happy with our experience. Campsite was nice and not clustered too close to neighbors. River access was convenient. Trails were a nice change of pace. And, after all those activities, the shower in the bathhouse was amazing.

Make sure you bring a heavy duty extension cord if you get an electrical site. The power boxes are likely placed for RVs and we had a tent. Fortunately, we also had a long extension cord.

Park access closes at 10pm every night, so get back in time. Park staff were all friendly. :)

Went here for the first time to camp with the family for the weekend. Even during this zombie apocalypse the campground wasn’t full, including the electric section we put our tent up in.

Showers and restrooms were pretty clean. Only a few miles of trails to hike, bikes aren’t allowed. Walked all the way down to the river but it was rather low, not sure if there’s ever much swimming or anything there.

It’s out of the way here for sure. Campground hosts were very friendly. :)
