You're a jerk if you rate a state park less than 5 stars - it's free outdoor 'entertainment'. ;) Took my kiddo and dog here for a hike, which was pretty adventurous on the rockywood trail since it rained the entire day before we got there.

Rockywood trail was very well-marked and we ended up with just under 7 miles. Roads were nice, lots of parking. Didn't see but maybe 1 port a potty, but we weren't exploring the rest of the park. Add this one to your list, folks. :)

It was kind of neat to say that I had been there, but the site was borderline disappointing. Limited markers at key points of interest - though info stations are less strategically located near the parking lot, random 'strangers' allowed to sell peculiar maps and provide their version of history/facts, and a random piece of tape in the road ("x" marks the spot) where the whole thing went down. Just not what I was expecting.

Came here for a bike ride with my wife. Trail was flooded and closed along the river. We’ve ridden the trail nearest the river before and it’s quite flat but also not very shady. So be ready for sun and limited excitement. We actually parked way at the top of the hill at the new greenway parking lot. Holy cow- it’s all uphill though.

This was our first visit here. Decided to walk a few connecting trails and ended up with just over two miles in total. I'm sure we'll come back and walk again. The view of the Mississippi is pretty sweet. I'd bet the leaves/trees are beautiful in the fall while you're out and about here.

Really nice ball field. The dugouts are in excellent shape. Bleachers are good sized. Bathrooms are one-hitters, though. There is no entrance to the field for the players minus the end of the fence, which makes it tricky for batters who walk of just getting up to the plate.

Detoured through here while riding the Al Foster trail. It hasn’t rained in a couple days but the trail still had several very must spots. One was quite terrible and took us several minutes to maneuver past, as it crossed the creek and become quite slick and steep.

I wanted to give the park 4 stars, but we literally just pulled into the first parking lot we found, hiked 4 miles and then left. Yeah, we were there for about 2 hours, but we barely scraped the surface of what they have to offer. I'm sure we'll be back, though. :)

Quaint, little covered bridge at the end of Old Lemay Ferry road. The area at the site isn't very large, acreage-wise, but is well-maintained and a nice, quiet spot to get away from the noise of the big city. Bring a lunch and enjoy the beautiful Missouri scenery.

Talk about out in the middle of nowhere. Spotty cell phone service, winding gravel road, and only primitive campsites. LOTS of ticks on the trail. We sprayed vigorously and I still got tons of bites. You want to get away from civilization? This is a good option.

Hiked "the mountain" (as my 10-year-old likes to call it) and we made our way over to the main building. We eventually weaved our way down to the dig site near Seckman Rd. Got several miles of hiking in; lots of ups and downs. Nice trails; well maintained. :)

I'm not a religious guy, but this place was pretty cool to see. Hiked up to the top of the steeple for some great views. Narrow, winding staircase. Some spots could use lighting and repair. Signage is a little tricky. Very nice experience though. :)

Way overpriced. Yikes. Plus I’m not a Dr Pepper drinker. But some of the stuff was cool to look at. Parking lot across from the entrance fills up quick. But there’s plenty of street parking on nearby streets. Don’t be afraid to walk. :)

Went there to meet a friend for a socially-distant lunch at a picnic table. We managed to find a few clusters of them here on Google maps and then found an available one when we arrived. Lots of parking , too.
Was fortunate enough to be here for the big spectacle that is the summer music event at the Capitol. LOTS of people watching, lots of vendors. Great vibe. It's a beautiful building
Been here for numerous events as well as just visits to the park (walk, run, etc.). Farmer's market is always nice, in addition to other activities hosted by the city of Arnold.
One of my favorite stadiums. I kind of miss the nostalgia of the older Busch Stadium, but this new one is nicely done. Nearly everyone you meet is very friendly.
This park is much bigger than you think it is. Need to go for a walk/run? The trail is more than adequate. Nice scenery. Lots of places for kids to play, too. :)
I was here recently for a 5k. I've camped here before and ridden the bike trails before, but it's been years. Everything looked to be well maintained though.
Been here several times for races and this visit was no exception. MO cowbell half marathon always starts here and there's plenty of parking and room.
We were here for a league baseball game. Didn't get to check out much of the park. The field we were on was very nice though.
Bathrooms are pretty scary (smell and condition), but the trail head is a great place to rest in the shade.
Braved about 1.5 miles of the steep trail down into the canyon. This was a good spot to try it out.

This was actually a pretty cool place to visit. I honestly didn't expect to actually enjoy myself while visiting this place as it is classified as a museum, however, there is enough to see to keep just about anyone interested. The large Recreation of the Ringling Circus attraction is just amazing and how much work was put into actually setting up for a show for these people. Combine that with all the acts and everything else going on it really would have been a sight to see if they were still in business. They also have them on scene Art Museum which I'm surprised was actually really well kept and a lot of different pictures to see. There is also the Ringling house that they used to live in, but we never went through that. It is surprisingly cheap for this type of venue being $25 for adults and $15 for children and to see the house that is an extra $5 on top of that. Otherwise it was a good time that we had there and I would definitely visit there again to see the house.

Very nice large park in ocean city Maryland. Lots of space to do quite a bit with a lot of fields and grass. Walking paths, fishing, boating as well as playgrounds are available at this park. We go there during lacrosse tournaments and there are a lot of people there, but there still is plenty of room to do things despite that. There does seem to be a lot of parking available so that shouldn't be a problem when there is no sports tournaments taking over the park.

This is a pretty fun place to go when  you have children with you.   The regular lunch food is nothing spectacular,  but the kettle corn and more specialty foods from this type of environment is delicious. The prices are very high with the food and entry,  so expect to spend some money if you come here. Plenty to do and plenty to see when you come here. Definitely check it out if you are in the area for a great experience.

We love coming to this park and camp ground. The grounds are very well kept up and clean and there is a lot to do while you are here.  Biggest gripe is the pets. Despite being a park and outdoors, there are very little places that you can take pets. I get it, they don't want feces sitting all over, but no pets in the lake? Really?

Great experience with a lot to do and look at. Great selection of unique fish and wildlife. There were even a couple of placed where you could touch and 'pet' the fish as well.  The staff we dealt with, seemed very knowledgeable about the fish that they were caring for and the prices were OK in my eyes for something like this.

Nice little stop with plenty of parking to view the beauty of Florida and the ocean. The parking is free and the time that we stopped was absolutely beautiful with the sunset. There is a red light to get in and out of the place so it is easy to get to and get out of and it was just a nice time to visit.

A fun area to visit to be able to walk around and see many many sailboats and other ships in the bay. A lot of little shops all around as well as small restaurants to visit with the family and kids. What are the nicer areas of Salem as well as a big area for the whole witch theme.

Great place to visit and see some of the animal scenery. The staff were extremely courteous and very knowledgeable in the desert life.  The prices wells at the level I would expect and it really does a nice job at immersing you in the desert life of Arizona.

We used to come to this park quite often before they redid it and it was a lot of fun. Now since they redid it everything is nice fresh and seems to be a lot safer. Definitely would recommend you take your kids there any time you can as it is a lot of fun.

Just the place we were looking for. A park that has great hiking paths and has not a little open fields and forest. We like to take the dog here to run around and have some fun. The place is well-kept and the paths, for the most part,  are easy to follow.

This is a nice small park with basketball court, tennis courts, a pavilion as well as a small baseball field that you can come and enjoy the environment and nice days. It's not a really big Park but it's probably sufficient for the Red Lion area.

Very nice, well-kept turn type of fields with multiple restrooms and cknsession stands strewn about. The bathrooms are relatively clean and the lightening is plenty. Nice area to go for various tournaments. We were here for lacrosse.

Nice park with a walking trail next to it. Seems to be plenty of flat land for sports practice and small park is nice for the kids. There is no bathroom but there are Porta potty that are adequate but disgusting.

Overall a nicely built, organized and overall a decent experience.  Includes everything from room, restaurants, carnival games, rides to the expensive food and drink everything a tourist attraction requires....

I cam here with a school field trip. It was a fun experience with a lot of small activities available for both children and adults. A lot of learning to be had and the staff were knowledgeable and friendly.
Great museum in dedication to a very dark time in the history of humans. Weird layout but very nice and well thought out presentations. Food court is in separate building so that was weird.
I like this park a lot. There is a lot of open land to do things with the family and pets. There is plenty to do with picnic stands, various courts, play ground and plenty of parking.
This is a very well-kept park with a lot of different activities from basketball, rock climbing to having a large playground. Awesome to come and play with the kids and family.
We almost always come here when we are in Ocean city. We love to see the wild horses as well as come to the beach as it is one of the few that accept pets to be on the beach.
Pretty cool place to visit when you are traveling.  You can stand in four different states at once! Nicely laid out and plenty of parking for cars and trailers as well.
Nice walking park with great views of the lake. Small swimming hole with lifeguards. Does cost money to get into the swimming hole but overall was a nice day.
We just stopped here for some pictures and memories. At this point there was no race going on and I can only imagine what it looks like when there is a race.
We briefly visited this park when we were visit the fingerlakes in New York state. Small park, nice walking area, well kept grass and surroundings.
Great tribute to the navy if our great country! The fountain of the seven seas was not running but I would have loved to see it running!
A very busy but nice park to visit with a nice little walk around the waterfalls as well as a long walking path for biking and jogging.

Station Road Bridge is one of the oldest metal truss bridges.  I recently found out its listed on the National Register of Historic Places.  I have been coming here for years and have seen the deck slowly deteriorate.  Now the bridge is re-opened with a brand new deck. There are picnic tables close to the bridge. This is a stop for the Cuyahoga Valley Scenic Railroad.
From the bridge, a right turn will take you to the Carriage Road Trail via the towpath.  Turning left will take you under OH 82  that travels over the Gorge. On the way, you will pass the Mudcatcher, and an eagle's nest. Continuing on, you will be on your way to the Frazee House.

Pine Lane to Boston Store is a nice challenging 4 mile out and back hike.  You can start your hike in either direction. The trailhead is easier to find starting at Pine Lane Trail Head. The trail has narrow roads and wider lanes. It can be very rocky with plenty of tree roots at times. This trail is not a loop, but you can get onto the Towpath as you come out of the forest by the Boston Store. Make sure you stop at the Boston Store and pick up some maps or souvenirs.

Nice hiking trails. The "blaze" marker colors coincide with the trail map. The one I would definitely stay away from is the West Oak hickory Trail. This Trail is not well marked and is totally on grass. Lots of holes from the horses made it tough to hike. All the other trails we were on, were well marked. Nice little half mile loop was the adventure walkway. This boardwalk loop gave information about the area. Porta potty on site.

The area has a nice short hiking path. Some areas are paved, and some are forested. Great place to get out and walk by the creek, or through the many Japanese cherry blossoms. Will see deer running up at the overlook. The summer can be very busy as there are baseball fields. At the end of the parking lot there is an access to the Cleveland Zoo. This is the Northern Trek area. Unfortunately this entrance is rarely open.

Great place to go hiking! There are several trails to explore. Some our paved/gravel and others are forest trails. You can also go They have rentals if you don't have your own. You can enjoy a picnic in the area and they also sell snacks and drinks. If you aren't too tired you can hike one of the many trails (paved and gravel). Awesome

A must visit, scenic waterfall in the CVNP.  This cascading 65 ft. waterfall has two spectacular viewpoints. One each from the upper & lower boardwalks. Although the lower view point is closed during the winter, you still can see the falls close up from the lower deck. Also make sure you take the Gorge Trail loop around the falls

Lake to Lake Trail connects Lake Isaac and Lake Abram on an  asphalt path. You will walk under  railroad tracks, and even walk over a boardwalk. The boardwalk crosses over one of many  wetlands in Cuyahoga County.  Check out to see if you can spot any local wildlife. Restroom on sight. Parking is limited

Great place to take your dog for some agility training. A pavilion and restrooms on site
They say that dogs must be leashed at all times, but I find that hard to believe if you are running your dog through the agility course. Mowed grass area around the park for a short walk.

Squires Castle is such a great place to get that unforgettable shot.   A lot of good hiking trails, and bridal trails of all lengths and difficulty Highly suggest it for a day hike or a place to have a picnic. Beautiful open areas in front of the castle.

Next to the Vermillion River, this free park will lit you excape from a busy day. Walk through nature as you see plenty of flowers, lakes and sculptured evergreens. Stay on the concrete path or take a stroll in the trees. Very relaxing

Two parts to the falls split by the road. One side is a cascade and the other is the falls. You can get really close to the falls via the steps. Good picture can be taken on either side. Can get crowded, and not much parking.

Decent sledding hill, with 2 separate ways, around the hill,  to get to the top. This is great because no one can get hurt walking up the hill. The recently finished connecting trail now links up with the Lake to Lake Trail

Starting point to get to the trail leading to Great Falls of Tinkers Creek. Small parking area. After seeing the Falls make sure you continue on a small path leading to the aqueduct bridge. Beautiful in spring and summer.

Need more trees in center loop. Off in the woods trails very nice, with some older trails hooking up with the new ones. Mountain bike trails are for biking and hiking. Please make sure you hike in the proper direction
dislikes: Lack of trees in center loop

reviews_attraction.text: Great place to bring you children. Although this learning center is closed for now, still a great place walk and hike. Can access the Towpath from here.  Also have a bike and hike there. Porta-Potty on-site
Nice area to stroll. 4 different trails totaling around 2 miles.  Playground, fishing, pavilion and even a sledding hill. Nice place to take the kids, walk your dog or take in a relaxing sunrise
Plenty of things to do here in Cuyahoga Valley National Park. All sorts of outdoor activities. Hiking, biking, canoeing, fishing, and just plain relaxing. Cuyahoga Valley can meet your demands.
Always love coming here. Hike separate trails, or put them all together for a 5 miler.  The stairs have been re-done, and they added a connecting boardwalk.  Kids love the Nature Center

Get there early if you're going to the play ground
Nice paved path for walking or jogging. Lovely photo spots of the Cleveland skyline. Great place to see a sunrise or catch a sunset
Awesome place to hike.  Some trails can get a bit difficult. Plenty of wonderful views. Rock formations are gorgeous. Man-made stairs. Trails on both sides of the road.
Nice lake near Berea. Swim, picnic, fish, or just walk on the trails. Head north, about 2 miles on the trails,  and treat yourself to Berea Falls Overlook
Nice wood overlook, can get obstruction in the summer when trees are full bloom. Nice little path where you can get down up and close to the falls.
Nice big parking lot. A nice place to start a day hike to areas like Beaver Marsh Indigo Lake and Szalays Farmers Market
Visitor center now open and restrooms are also open. Starting point for Blue Hen Falls hike via the Buckeye Trail
Great place for a walk, hike, or just take in nature. Nice trails, with rocks to climb, and a waterfall to boot

My friends had their wedding and reception here; it is a nice event space with better-than-expected acoustics for the amount of hard surfaces inside the lodge.

One thing that caught people off guard was the lack of potable water, in the kitchen or elsewhere. We ended up buying several gallons of water elsewhere. The owner should alert people renting the space about the water situation.

Aside from this, the grounds are nice, the ability to have a fire on the patio is a classy touch, and we all left satisfied with the venue after the reception. It's definitely a hidden gem.

I wish that the Rangers hadn't left the Ballpark. I've been to over 20 MLB parks, and this was in the upper echelon; wide concourses, good views, plenty of concession options, classy architecture, and you knew you were in Texas when you were there--moments in Texas history were portrayed on the ballpark's walls!

I know it got very hot, but what would you expect here in the summer? It was a treat when a storm would come through in the afternoon and cool things down for a night game.

A rather enjoyable presidential library and museum. Various displays and artifacts take you through the Bushes' lives and stages of his career. Visitors learn that President Bush was a true public servant. That there was even a TV playing video of SNL's Dana Carvey as he did his 41 impression--and George and Barbara's reaction to it--showed their humility. The gift shop has items for all ages. I highly recommend this museum for anyone in the area.

Fascinating home built above a creek/run in a picturesque setting. It was interesting to hear from the tour guide about FLW's obstinance in the face of questions about materials and reinforcement--I wasn't surprised, as he was notorious for such self-assuredness, even when ultimately proven wrong on other projects. It was a pleasure to visit in the fall, even if the leaves weren't at their peak color.

So much to do here, and close to the metro! Whether winding through the corn maze, playing one of the several games, sitting by a fire pit, choosing a pumpkin, or enjoying the food, there's something for everyone of any age. The owners are friendly and helpful, and they have a nice facility for events and weddings. We've gone here for years, and look forward to it every fall.

Excellent reuse of a sturdy old structure that helps the museum fit nicely into the community's fabric, as well as its location along the river. Both indoor and outdoor artwork is displayed in various media. I like that the museum is comfortable using the building's exterior largely as-is, without the need to make a bold statement that would be out of context for the setting.

I awoke very early in the morning to go out and see the sunrise. I was very surprised at how many people were already there! It's a gorgeous place and definitely worth visiting. Don't just walk to the edge of the lake nearest the parking lot and stop there for a couple of photos; enjoy the trails, too! There is a lot to explore in the area.

An interesting place to explore. A visitors' center, monument commemorating the place Washington and his men crossed the Delaware, and statue of Washington. Associated buildings and signs also tell the story of what precipitated Washington's crossing, and the outcome. Many people were visiting just to relax or swim.

Fascinating rock formations, made famous by many movies and TV shows, in the heart of the desert. Along with saguaro cacti, Monument Valley is emblematic of the American West. While in the area, take time to learn about the Navajo Code Talkers; these men played an integral role in the Allies' victory in WWII.

This was on my list of western art museums to visit, and it did not disappoint. Having several museums with different themes under one roof is a good concept; I also enjoyed the exhibit about the Cody Stampede, and what it means to the town. Definitely worth visiting if you're in Cody!

Nice area of respite amid the many visitors. Park benches, the famous antler arches, and a war memorial. It was a good idea, during the COVID pandemic, to put picnic tables around the square in parking places to keep the restaurants going, yet allow people to properly distance.

Nice, secluded state park that's a good place to get away from civilization. Various campsites, natural areas, places to park and picnic, toilets, and a good overlook from which to view the Missouri River valley. Friendly rangers/staff if you need to call with any questions.

Explore amid the unique Saguaro cacti of the Sonoran Desert. Whether taking a driving tour on the loop or hiking into the backcountry, you'll note that every cactus is unique. The Saguaro, barrel, prickly pear, and cholla cacti all add different elements to the landscape.

Solid art museum in a nice facility. I enjoyed the cafe and its view of the harbor, too. It is a fully-fledged restaurant, and far better than many of the typical museum cafes you find elsewhere. This facility is an all-around good place to visit when in Corpus.

Excellent western art collection; it ranks among the best. As a Remington and Russell enthusiast, this museum was right up my alley. While not as large as many museums, it makes up for this in the quality of the works displayed. There is a good gift shop, too.

Sobering tribute to the brave Americans who stood up to those seeking to harm our nation and its leaders. I visited on a gray, rainy day--yet, the conditions were appropriate for the somber mood the memorial engenders for anyone who remembers 9/11.

The old locomotives are majestic and visceral. They harken back to an age when trains held a more prominent role in American life. Hearing the whistle blast as a train comes into downtown Durango is an unmistakable, and inspiring, sound.

Neat old covered bridge. It is fascinating to see the sturdy wooden beams inside the structure. The red paint looked pretty good. The bridge isn't located in the middle of nowhere, but it's not surrounded by development, either.

Enjoyable hall of fame and museum celebrating the history, culture, and characters of rodeo. Displays of many artifacts, awards, and equipment. Worth visiting whether you're an rodeo veteran or want to learn more about it.

An interesting anomaly. As the title implies, it's literally a large tree in the middle of a four-way intersection out in the country. Not a must-see attraction, but interesting if roadside oddities appeal to you.

Enjoyable museum with many artifacts and art, focused on rodeo and western culture. Good permanent exhibits, as well as interesting rotating displays. I recommend it if you're in Cheyenne or passing through!
Cool vantage from which to take in the cities. You're high enough above things to get a more peaceful, slower-moving view of things, whether the IH-10 traffic or trains.
Pretty place--on both sides of the island--to enjoy many activities, whether relaxing on the beach, swimming, observing wildlife, or spending a day with family.
Cool place to visit year round. Be sure to take the trail to go behind the waterfall. Toward the top, it also affords a nice view of town and the mountains.
Such a touching and classy tribute to a legendary performer. Even the statue seems to have a warmth about it.

BUY YOUR TOUR TICKETS ONLINE BEFORE YOU GO!!!  So many people arrived without tickets and had to wait several hours for a tour time that had spots available, don't do what they did!!! It's very easy to sign up and pay online!!!!  Having said that, the Tour is well worth the price and the wait if you don't buy your tickets ahead of time.  My kids 11 & 14, loved it, the tour was very informative, never boring and so cool to actually get to see it!!  If you have kids look for the Junior Missiler books (FREE!), kind of like a Junior ranger program, the book has lots of great information and is presented in a fun way!!  When they finish or make an effort to finish they get a patch!  A wonderful piece of history, everyone will learn something and have a new appreciation for what was happening during the Cold War.

Absolutely gorgeous! We got to the Bear valley visitor center a little late and the kids just barely finished the junior ranger program.  It is a very good information center and the hikes around the center are great too.  You can still see the fence that moved in the 1906 earthquake on the earthquake trail.  We also drove to a beautiful beach that had huge crashing waves.  We could have explored much more  but it was getting late.  Well worth the visit!! Would spend more time next time!

An amazing and otherworldly place!  So incredible to imagine what this place would have looked like when it was a wetland with trees and water everywhere!  A very easy stop is you are traveling along I-40, just off the interstate to the visitor center and then a out a 1-2 hour loop to see most if not all the park.  The museum at the south end of the park is very nice with a quick hiking trail to see petrified wood in different forms.  Definitely make the stop if you have time!!
likes: On-site Activities: Hiking, petrified wood viewing

reviews_attraction.text: A well preserved piece of history.  We visited in Aug 2020, the museum was closed but my kids were still able to get their Jr Ranger badges.  Seems like most buildings were open, some upper levels were closed but it was nice to be able to view parts of the buildings.  The rangers were very helpful and knowledgeable, a great stop that would take an hour or so to visit thoroughly, maybe a little longer if the museum was open.

A wonderful experience and a neat place to see how people from the past lived.  The dwellings are amazing and different from those at Mesa Verde.  We were there on a fairly hot day and with the heat of the rocks reflecting back it made for a very hot hike.  Be prepared with water and sun protection.  The visitor center is small with a few informative displays.  The junior ranger program is very good.  Worth stopping!

You can only visit the lighthouse at low tide and if low tide happens to be between 10-4pm then the museum is open.  We we're not able to visit the museum because low tide was at 5:20pm but we were able to explore the amazing tide pools around the lighthouse and walk around the outside of the lighthouse.  It is still a functional lighthouse with a keeper.  Great views and well worth going if only for the tide pools!

Wow!! This place is a wonderful way to learn a lot about the history of South Dakota!! So much packed into this museum, well worth a visit by anyone, kids and adults alike!  They have lots of information for the adults and many fun little interactive stuff for the kids.  Admission is free for kids under 17 and adults are $4.  So glad we checked it out!!  The view from this unique building is also very pretty!

A very nice visitor center, a great place to get a taste of the channel islands.  We we're able to get a junior ranger badge without having to visit the islands.  The cost for a family of four is cost prohibitive.  The only way to get to the islands is by a private company.  We learned a lot about the islands and maybe someday we can visit the actual islands but for now it was fun to learn about them here.

A very nice National monument with a great history of the native Americans.  The rangers were very knowledgeable and friendly.  We couldn't spend a lot of time in the museum because we had our dog with us but it was nice from what we could tell.  The circle trail was very nice with lots to see and learn about.  The junior ranger program was great too.  Definitely worth a stop!

It has been over 10 years since i have visited Yellowstone and the new edutcenters are outstanding!  The information is wonderful and interactive for all ages.  The canyon education center focus' more on the geology of Yellowstone, the volcano and the earthquakes.  A lot of great info!!  Definitely worth a stop to learn something new!

Great Beach!! We went here because it had good reviews and they were right!!! Not a lot of parking but the beach is great!  There are restrooms, shower to rinse off and a drinking fountain.  Lots of seashells and there was a lifeguard on duty when we went!  Great place to watch the cruise ships head out too.

Very nice, well taken care of campground.  No campground host, you are pretty much on your own if you need anything.  The bike path is great, the playground is fun for the kids and there is plenty of shade, picnic spots and a brand new frisbee gold course. There is some train noise but not during the night.

A very nice little zoo.  We enjoyed the wide variety of animals they had here.  A few highlights were the sloth bears, wallaby's, goat petting zoo and otters.  The zoo has lots of shade and is a wonderful respite on a hot day.  The enclosures seemed well planned and spacious.  A very well taken care of zoo!

A nice zoo with lots of animals.  We enjoyed seeing one unique animals, especially the two toed sloth!  They were also doing a lot of construction that looks like will be amazing when finished.  Seems like it's an older zoo but the animals seemed well taken care of.  We enjoyed our visit here.

Our family really enjoyed this historical site.  While the visitor center is small, it is very well done and the informational video was great.  The preserved buildings were very nice and worth the short walk to visit them.  Worth your time to see this little glimpse into the past.

Wow! A wonderful look at anthropology, we wnjoyed learning new things about the cultures of the past.  It was also neat to see some artifacts from these cultures, it was engaging enough for a quick stop and we'd protgo back again to discover something new we didn't see this time.

We had a good time, it seemed like it could get a lot busier.  The pools were freezing but it just opened so it might take some time for the post to warm up.  We'll definitely try it out again.  Just right for a day trip and don't forget to find discounted tickets around town!!

A wonderful place to enjoy nature without having to drive far!  The drive through the park is beautiful, we stopped at the beach and also walked over the foot bridge by the marina, all beautiful spots especially on a clear day, but still worth it on a foggy day too.

Outstanding national monument!  We arrived just in time for the guided tour, it was volunteer led and well worth the time.  Very informative and lots of great stories about this interesting piece of history.  A very good junior ranger program and nice gift shop too.
likes: Facilities & Services (Guided tours, Junior ranger program, Gift shop)

reviews_attraction.text: Absolutely amazing and well worth a visit!!  We could have spent twice as much time here!  We spent at least two hours here and that was rushing through some of the areas.  Lots to do and see, something for everyone!

New playground, great trails and frisbee golf.  Up at the top of the hill there is another playground and beautiful public flower gardens. Excellent place to get away from the hustle and bustle and let the kids play!
The kids had a great time here.  They are organized and conscious of safety.  There are things thy like here but the other trampoline park in town is still their favorite place to jump.
We absolutely love this place, there is always something new we discover. Well worth your time to stop and see some real fossils and learn something new about our magnificent earth!!
This was an excellent trail! The information was great, the path was easily traversed and the forest was magical.  Definitely worth the 15-30 minutes to check it out!!
Beautiful museum, lots of hands on activities for the kids.  Great history of the Sioux City area.  Well worth a visit.  Be ready to pay the meter for parking.

The cave tour was worth every cent. I loved it. Even the 20 times a wacked my head on the cave ceiling. I loved the exsperince. Great for a small group. Our tour guide laurel did a awesome job. She was extremely engaged and informative. I took alot away from the tour. I would do it again. The writing on a cave wall in pencil by folks in the 1800s was cool to see still around. Plenty of stairs to climb.

Great time watching Ethen Foote.  As part of its effort to make the performing arts available to everyone, the Kennedy center offers a free performance every day on the mlennium stage in the grand foyer. These performs of music, theater, and dance feature emerging and established artists from the Washington area, across the nation and around the world.

Great for kids and photo ops. You will be diggin sand out of ur draws all day. If you think you not overweight, plan to find out the truth. 30 mins from the car (depending on that cross walk light that takes so long you forget where you are going) to the top of the dune and 4 hours back, dehydrated and disoriented. Smokers need not try.

1 star for the awesome view of the key bridge. Fort Armistead? U mean Fort Landfill or Fort "this is where I clean out my truck bed of chopped up fish". I hope this isn't the neighborhood park. I been in some ruff places in my time but this takes it. So much potential but so neglected. Using caution tape for dock railings won't cut it.

Going kill a fat boy. Nice views at the top of those steps. Killer steps. Nice to see all races of people of all ages working those thighs up that hill. Restrooms at the top. I'm not sure what's up with the cottontail bunny infestation, I have never ever seen that many rabbits in my life. 1 every 10 feet. You can also bird watch.

It's a great parking location if your up for the walk over to the mall. We usually park here for the cherry blossom, thats if we are able to get into town early enough. Parking closer to the tourist area can be convenient but it ain't cheap.
It's nice to see so many people making good use of the park system.

So not to cause any confusion - mvpd can just put up a "Minorities Not Welcome" sign, right outside of the gondola ride into Mountain View. How is the police officer goin follow us to the info board and ask for our ID? I look like many a things,  but a criminal aint one......neither is my natural hair wife.

Can we get a renovation, pressure washer, paint and some trash cans? It's 2018. Time to clean up and update. Put those tax dollars to use. Please send someone to the state capitol in Sacramento (Just in case no one knows where it's at) and take a few pointers. Has so much potential, short on delivery.

Dont drink that dirty water. Fascinating historic stop. It's sobering why it was built and still is in use. I love the museum sharing actuall history of the prison and the work and engineering the prisoners put into the construction and maintenance of the facilities. Guards were very accomadating.

Has to be one of the best downtown parks in the country. On sunny days that is. It's like everybody's there. Parking is a pain but the walk there is worth it. The city is remarkably clean, even with all of the outside rural living quarters found throughout. Everyone loves being out doors.

5 stars for the chili dog, 4 stars for the double cheeseburger and 3 stars for the Guadalajara dog. They have been in that spot for 78 years, where else would you go for hollywood history. They know how to keep the line moving. Parking is tight but they will find you a spot in the back.

Wildlife and flowers aplenty on the 5 mile roundtrip hike from the parking area to border marker 258, originally #1. It's a shame the park has fallen into disarray. This is where mexico, the US and Pacific Ocean all meet. It's ironic, how the ocean gets to live in both countries.

Las vegas with a beach front. Gotta be one of the longest boardwalks on the east coast. It seems it's hay days of excitement and newness have quietly  passed by. Could use some 2018 updates. Much cleaner and normal than many boardwalks out there. Can we get a pisidon statue?

It's an amazing place to visit. Nothing like it on the east coast. It's a wonderful example of creation at it's best. Stout trail very family friendly. They drive up from the south side is an adventure in its self. Plenty of amazing trees to stop along the way and enjoy.

It's amazing the history they have kept. Even though the building have been repurposed it still has the feel of 1800s. True craftsmanship. Parking is tight. Museums, resteraunts, shopping, the river.  Some construction on the west side by the river.

Parking, vistor center and restrooms. You can take the family on the trail to the left a short distance, easy access. To get to some of the best redwoods in the area you need to go in 3 miles or so toward fern canyon.

It's the place to visit if you are any where in the area. Beautiful views. The redwoods are just one of the most magnificent displays of nature I have seen. The road is a little ruff but doable. Amazing hikes.
I guess it was the place to go for seafood back in the day. They could clean the area up a bit. The street fare is overpriced for sitting out in coolers all day. You can always take few nice pics.
I remember seeing this in elementary school - minus the flea market.  The charge booth was closed so a 4 star was easy. Take a 5 min walk out into the middle of desert.
Nice little bit of history documented on the side walk history signage. Didnt see any beavers on my visit, very dissappointed.
They say that some of the best views u get are from climbing to the top of the lighthouse,  I wouldnt know, it was closed.
Great park in the city. Trails and swimming holes.  Kids will enjoy it - they can run wild like the animals they are.
Much more modern, the other incline is where u need to take the out of towners for the historical look into the past.
How is a longer bridge going have a cheaper toll? $4 here and 301 bridge like $60. The state needs a new accountant.
Perfect place to stop and let the kids run wild. After they get dirty u can wash them in the river.

Beautiful National Park just outside of Moab.  This national Park absolutely rivals the Grand Canyon in its scope and beauty.  I am surprised these two parks aren't mentioned hand in hand more often.  I think in Arizona the Grand Canyon is sort of a claim to fame, where as in Utah there are other parks, and other popular areas that steal some of the show.  Lots of great scenic view points, with easy access.  Some parks force you to get on buses, this one allows you to stay in your own vehicle and drive to all the hikes and scenic points.  With the correct permits you can even drive down into the national park, or take your dirt bikes.

Busy, busy, busy.  Get there early if you can, especially if you are coming during a holiday or on a weekend.  The place was swamped, we got there early enough that parking wasn't to bad, but it gets busy.  The visitor center had three Rangers working when we were there but there was still a 15 minute wait for them.  There is a nice video on the grand canyon, and an interesting projection presentation.  Images are projected onto a globe for an 8 minute presentation on how Grand Canyon was formed.  There is food here, and not enough restrooms.  Lady's especially had a significant wait for a restroom.

Walking into this park is like walking into an old western.  The classic cactus, when you think of one, the green thing with three arms sticking up, is the Saguaro cactus, and obviously, they are all over in this park and the surrounding area.  In this park they allow you to hike up a "wash" which is where the water flows, if there is water, but it is such an arrid climate, it only flows after rains.  There are multiple areas to view petroglyphs or stone carvings from native Americans.  Nice park, but generally very hot, bring lots of water if you are hiking.

Approaching the mountains that are home to the Black Canyon of the Gunnison is deceiving.  They are gentle sloping mountains, that are not impressive compared other areas of the Rocky mountains, but once you get up to 8000 feet, at the rim of the gorge, it is striking to see just how deep Black Canyon of the Gunnison is.  Much much steeper than Canyonlands in Utah, or the Grand Canyon.  There are some nice Rim hikes.  If you come in winter there are no fees but most of the roads are closed, so there is not a lot of access to the parks.

This should almost be called a desert zoo.  They have a large variety of animals that are native to the Sonora desert.  The exhibits are natural and you can get very close to the animals.  There is also a big play zone called the packrat play house.  You can walk among the hummingbirds and water them build their nests in the hummingbird enclosures.  And you can touch/feed stingrays.  The Sonora desert extends all the way to the coast where the stingrays are native so they are included in the exhibit.

There are tons of Joshua trees in and outside the park, no shortage to see.  The parts of the branches that were still growing looked like pineapples according to my kids.  They really did seem like some variation of a palm tree.  The rock formations are formed by thousands of years of water infiltration and the following freeze thaw cycles.  Breaking larger rocks apart, and then erroding the edges of the resulting smaller rocks till you get piles of rock rubble that make up much of Joshua tree.

This is a privately run tourist attraction so it is a bit commercialized but they did a very nice job with it.  There are multiple viewing decks with telescopes so you can check out different parts of the very large crater.  You can actually touch what they believe is a small piece of the impacting meteorite.  You cannot walk into or around the entire crater but there are some paths near the visitor center to do some walking.  Adults were $18.  Kids under six were free when I was there.

Very intriguing national park.  The builds of this almost millennia old civilization are well preserved.  The iconic large cities are the most breath taking but there are lots of sites to explore in the vicinity.  The visitor's center is an older one but has tons of material and a nice video explaining the history.  At the time we were there, there were some rock slide fears so we had to go up and down the exit.  Be prepared to climb down some ladders for the Palace cave viewing.

The playground here is great.  One for youngsters 2-5 and one for 5-12.  The ground is the soft recycled rubber, some might baulk, but I prefer it over mulch or pebbles.  It is right next to a school, I don't know if you are technically allowed to but on weekends the parking there is convenient.  It would be impossible to park when school is happening.  The big negative to this place is the public restroom is an absolute wreck.  Avoid it and otherwise the park is nice.

There is a visitor center deeper in the park, but this one near the entrance is relatively new.  Impressive sculpture out-front and very life like wax figures and displays on the inside.  Rangers to help you decide what to do and you can buy your tickets for tours in the park here.  Definitely should spend a few minutes here before you drive all the way into the park to get your bearings on what to do once inside.  Parking has room for big vehicles as well.

I highly recommend doing the hike all the way up to delicate Arch, if you can.  In our case, the weather was miserable and we had youngsters, so we couldn't do the full hike up.  This lower viewing point gives you a clear picture of the arch, and only a few 100 feet from where you park.  If you can't do the hike for any reason, this is a nice place to stop, snap some pictures and still get a good view of the attraction.

This is a very quick hike, .2 miles each way, to a natural bridge that is nearing the end of its lifespan (relatively, still will exist for hundreds of years probably)  The arch is very thing with a steep drop right underneath it with beautiful vistas into Canyonlands National Park.  It is definitely worth the stop as you are driving to some of the other scenic points within Canyonlands National Park.

The miniature golf here was disappointing.  It was strange, all these cool water features, and huge fake trees, and light houses, yet all the holes were basically hit the ball straight with maybe a few obstacles in the way.   With how hard they worked on the ambiance of the course, you would think they would put a little more thought into making the holes themselves interesting.  They just weren't.

A well done visitor center that houses a chunk of what is believed to be the meteorite that created the crater.  Lots of interactive exhibits.  An experience that lets you watch the meteorite hit the ground.  Talks about how we can track incoming meteors and how to avoid them hitting the earth.  Also discusses the moon and the impacts that formed it.  Has an attached subway and gift shop.

This is an understated National park focused on driving.  It's ironic going to a place to look at petrified trees in a landscape that is almost completely treeless.  The visitor center explains how different the landscape was back when the petrified forest was created, compared to the desert it is now.  Lots of nice easy short hikes with tons of petrified rock/tree viewing.

Cool spot with lots of civil war memorabilia.  There was a traveling presentation with an animatronic Lincoln while we were there.  It was interesting, generally well done, but the animatronic Lincoln was terrifying for my 6 year old.  It sounds fun to teach kids about history, but the display was not really good for young kids.  Cool stuff to see otherwise though.

This is not a super modern visitor center but it has everything you need to understand the history of the park.  There is a short video on a small screen talking about the park, and its a good staging ground to figure out where you want to go.  There are plenty of restrooms here although they are pit toilets, they do not have sinks and related amenities.

The up front cost covers all the live action shows you can attend.  If you like old westerns this place is a must see.  My young kids weren't quite ready for the gun fire of the live cowboy shows but there was plenty of other stuff today including tracked cars a train, panning for gold, etc.

Good visitor center with plenty to do, read, research, and interact with for kids.  There is a temperature sign out there if you show up in the middle of summer to get a shot with the super hot temps.  Coming in the winter months the temperature is very comfortable, even a bit chilly.

The visitor center is older here.  Compared to some of the exhibits in the very modern visitor centers it will feel like it's old, but the rangers are just as helpful and the visitor centers are really just gateways to the parks.  Better to go out and see it for real.

Can't imagine living in one of these houses quite busy around the area.  Great Park for the kids nearby there is also the dog park where you can let your dogs run around off leash nearby pretty cool place to hang out.

This visitor center is nicely updated with exhibits on the native Americans, forest fires, and glaciers that helped shape the canyon.  It is attached to the gift shop and not far away from a restaurant.
This visitor center is in the park but far from the main bulk of the park.  We visited in the winter when it had seen heavy snow so hiking wasn't an option unless you bring snowshoes.
This was an extremely busy area but lots of hiking to do.  In the spring the water runs fast and covers parts of the trails.  So be ready to take your shoes off and Wade.
Nice views on the hike of the bay.  Trail is not prepared for rain.  We went after a few days of rain and it was a muddy mess.  Wait for dry weather.

9/2020: 2 stars- After loving this winery the first time we wanted to come back and bring our parents to show up. What a big disappointment. It was really hot and they only had 2 fans. We were dying. Then they don’t give you any water, you have to buy bottles which is fine but it didn’t come out right away. The waitress took her sweet ole time. She also asked us if we were members and when we said no, she left for about 10 minutes then finally came to drop the menu off. After that we ordered and it took another 15 minutes for the wines to come out. The tasting are just flights now, which is cool but you can choose what you like. She dropped off wines and left, no explanation, nada. Another table came and she asked if they were members as well and when they said yes, they got amazing fast service!, while non members waited for days for her to come around. Not a good experience. Definitely treated non members like bottom of the barrel, not coming back.

1/2020: 4 stars- You wouldn’t think motorcycle and wine but hey Doffo did it and people come. It’s kinda cool to see all the display of motorcycle and mopeds. The wines are also really good. Their reds beat most other places. There’s a quieter tasting room and there’s a more like bar area where the wall of bikes are. We bought a bottle and a jar of chimichurri sauce. Both delicious with steak.
likes: Facilities & Services (quieter tasting room, bar area)
On-site Activities (wine tasting, purchasing local products)
dislikes: Facilities & Services (inadequate cooling, slow service for non-members, lack of complimentary water)

reviews_attraction.text: The winery is beautiful. We stopped by and was told we needed reservations but the lady took us in and served us well with her stellar customer service! We ended up buying over $200 worth of wines. They don’t have the normal 5 small 1 oz tasting but instead you have to buy the full bottle. It’s not as bad as it sounds because the wines were so affordable! You actually get more and worth it if you go with 4 people are more. You also get to take home what you don’t finish. Some of the wines are okay, most are average to above average. We liked the Chardonnay and Old Soul the most. Caves were closed when we came. Nice views outdoors. Dog friendly!

The castle is very cool but it’s very commercialized. There’s admission cost to enter the castle, around $30-$40 for either self guided or guided. If you are paying that much you might was well do the food and wine pairing for twice that. We did the food and wine pairing and Mary is the lady for that. She was very knowledgeable. It’s not your normal food pairing (don’t think courses) this was more of small finger foods/appetizers. It was good and she cooked everything herself. But probably not worth it if you think you’ll have like a 4-5 course tasting menu (like St Francis).

Come early! Usually before 8 you can find a parking space in the lot. If not parking on the streets is fine too. This hike is not too hard in my opinion. It’s a long slow descend. The top of the mountain is pretty nice I guess. One or take picnic table. Some cool rocks. In clear days you can actually see the ocean and downtown. Otherwise it’s just a bunch of other San Diego mountains peaks. It’s quite rocky in some parts. Be careful as you might sprain your ankle. Lots of rocks. About a 6 miles round trip. Dog friendly.

I like this park on weekdays- it’s not packed, clean and has a lot of space where if you didn’t want company you can be alone. Has a running path that is cement and about 1/2 a mile. The east side has picnic tables, bathrooms, playground, volleyball net, horseshoe rings, and parking. Big parties on the weekend... so it leaves the weekend kind of packed and trash everywhere after the parties. The west side is more of picnic tables and green grass. Good views of Oceanside toward the back.
likes: Variety of facilities (picnic tables, bathrooms, playground, sports areas)

reviews_attraction.text: Beautiful hike on the coast. Go do Kortum Trail, we started near Goat Rock and head south. It was about a good ole 6 mile walk. Not difficult, just an easy stroll on the cliff. It’s not dog friendly. Go early and go on a nice clear day. The views are beautiful!! So breath taking. The sun was bright and it wasn’t too many people. We came the day after Christmas. Totally recommend if you like trail running or a nice stroll on the cliffs.

Cool iconic stadium! If you are able to watch a Cubs game when you come visit, go for it! The stadium is very packed and the lines for food are long. If you get the Chicago dog make sure you get the pickles fast! It runs out fast!! The price isn’t too bad for nose bleed seats, get a view of the whole stadium. We got some shade too. It’s old stadium so bathrooms are not conveniently located. Hang out in Wrigleyville too!

My husbands boss recommended we come here, and so we did. It’s in Templeton and very small mom and pop winery. The tasting area was quite small, but we felt welcome here. We tried both of their tasting menu- the Zanoli side and Bella Luna. Everything was delicious and we ordered a ton of wine! We love the fighter pilot, and a lot of the zanoli side which had a lot of mixes of Grenache. Friendly service.

Great place to hike! The hike up to the top isn’t hard. One part is quite steep. The trails are maintained except there’s dog poop everywhere. People seriously need to pick up after their dog. Also they allow mountain bikers on the trail, some parts aren’t that wide so you have to move over or get run over by them. Plenty of parking and can enter from various entrances and trails.

This is so cool that a natural spring pool exists. We came during winter so there weren’t many people in the pool, it was cold! There were life guards and staff cleaning the pool. I can already see in the summer it’s a cool place to chill and have a picnic under the trees. Don’t go towards the end with all the moss and the shallow end. It looked pretty dirty.

There’s a troll under the bridge!! It’s a huge troll. Take a picture of him and move on. Watch out for the homeless tents to the right... close to Fremont brewing to go afterwards. We came on a cloudy wet day, I guess he looked even more scary in darker days. Not too many visitors when we came. There’s no parking but cars will pull over and park anyways.

Awesome place! We had a great time. The server was really knowledgeable and friendly. We enjoyed their red wines and bought over 10 bottles and my fiancé’s mom even became a member. Their fume was really good so was their mariness. We loved their Spencer’s hill! Beautiful grounds with some picnic tables! Totally recommend if you are in Healdsburg!

There are many different peaks in Mission Trails... all worth a hike. Some hikes are super easy and some are average. I've hike Cowles, Fortuna, and another one I don't remember the name. The peaks all have beautiful views of San Diego! Cowles is super crowded and Fortuna isn't. Many smaller trails too. Great outdoor playground for adults!

Small tasting room that was recommended to us by an employee of Columbia because we wanted some bold red wines. The reds were very good, wish we could have gotten some bottles but we’re not from here and didn’t have space in our luggage. Atmosphere was very cozy. Staff were friendly and it wasn’t packed at all. Right in the middle of town.

I've grown a liking to LPM... I came when they first opened and was quick to judge as it wasn't as good as what it was supposed to be... fast forward til now... pretty good, more vendors and food vendors. Love the outside patio... love just hanging out and grabbing a drink. It's still crowded. Dogs, kids, babies, everyone is welcome!

Awesome art museum even if you’re not an art lover. It’ll take you hours to see everything! Don’t make the mistake by going late. Go early in the day and take your time. We got the Chicago explorer pass and we skipped the ticketing line, exchange for real ticket at the reception. Beautiful art from all over the world. All originals.

A good walk to get away from the crazy busy streets above. Go down and walk along the river. There are some spots you can sit and watch the boats. At the far end of the strip, there are bars and some food places. They have lawn chairs and some bar games. Fun spot to hang out in the summer. Truly feels like it’s summer.

Cute winery to visit when you’re in town. It was super busy when we came so we just got poured and didn’t learn anything about he wines, which is understand as there was one staff. The wines were good comparable to what you can get in Temecula except without the price point. Big space if you wanna sit and relax.

I’ve been to moshin a couple times now and both have enjoyed my tastings there. Plenty of parking and no reservations required. There was one staff when we came but that’s all that was needed. She was very knowledgeable. Tastings were about $15 for about 5. We bought some wines for the road.

Nice park with a big dog park. There’s a community pool and it’s quite big. The dog park is nice too but it’s bark, wish they had just DG or grass. There’s always something going on at the field. Plenty of space for everyone and plenty of parking. There’s a play ground for kids too.

Gorgeous views of downtown on a very beautiful day! Best part is it’s free! There are m a lot and many tourist (like me) but there’s space for you to see and take pictures. It’s about two miles from downtown. Walkable. Probably one of the best free views, it’s picturesque.

The owner Toni was super friendly and talkative. The wines here were good, we ended up buying a bottle of the Syrah and when you buy a bottle she’ll knock off $5 off from your tasting. The wine dog was a cutie and plenty of space to have picnics and sit outside.

Small park with limited parking, but plenty of parking on the streets. It’s the start of the double peak hike. You can walk around the lake and feed the ducks or you can start hiking upwards to double peak. Lots of families, dogs and people just being active.

Super sketchy on getting down the chain link because towards the end it's all wet and gets slippery. I'm surprised nobody has died or fallen off! But totally worth the water fall and then hike to Beaver. It's amazing!! Wear good shoes and be safe.
Nice park with plenty of parking. There’s a club house you can rent out as well, but no alcohol allowed. Park is well maintained in a new and developing neighborhood.

Oh my God. If you're anywhere near Alamogordo you have to stop at the Space Museum. As I recall there are two or three different screen presentation that they give. After wandering around the missile park for an hour or so I walked in to see the displays inside. It was at the souvenir counter that I was told about the theaters. I thought they were excellent presentations. I thought that I had a better understanding than most about the space program. I learned a lot. If you're anywhere in the area take a few hours go to the space Park, and then sit down and watch the shows. When I was there I was the only one in the theater. LOL of course it was January or February I forget very cold outside so only an idiot, like me would be out driving around looking at museums. LOL love it, love it, love it. I will go back when I'm in the area again.

What an amazing view. To be honest I wasn't certain if I could handle the Heights. The ride was amazing, and very smooth with the exception of Tower 3. There, you will swing back and forth for 20 seconds or so. The rest of the ride is very smooth. And the view was amazing. We were there in June and there was still a small amount of snow up top. There is a bar which I took advantage of at the top LOL liquid courage for the ride down. You'll have a great time

I was told that Palo Duro is the 2ed largest canyon in the U.S.  You can drive to the canyon floor.. DO IT ! the sight of the sun going down over the edge of the rim is....well.... no words
the portion where the info area is is 1/20th of the overall canyon. At least that is what I was told...and judging from the map I believe it... the colors, the sight, the feeling of being so small is ..well... see it and you will understand

We went for the illumination show which was it night obviously. LOL it was rather cold but fortunately it was not crowded. I've been wanting to go there during the day for the five years that I've lived in Texas. After winter is over I'm definitely going to go. Walking around the grounds and seeing the expanse that it had was amazing. I think it's going to be astounding in the spring. I'm looking forward  to seeing it then.

If you are a race fan this place is amazing. There's a lot more here than you would expect. Besides Unser's racing cars there's also a supercharged Duesenberg one of only a few left. Take the time make the stop won't regret it. the cars show 4 generations of Unser's history..I forget the price but I remember that it was a lot less than I guessed

My sister insisted that we see Fort Sumter. I kind of thought okay fort on an island big deal. Well! It was a big deal. The history, the doson's information, the shell impacts still on the walls. The stories. Even the boat ride there and back was amazing. If you're in the area definitely definitely go to see it you will be glad you did.

I enjoyed restored World War II battle ships. It is right near the USS Yorktown which is an aircraft carrier. And next to that is the USS Clamagore Submarine. You really can't see one without seeing the other two because they're right there. In that area there is a place called the Vietnam experience. It's worth a walkthrough
likes: Nearby attractions (as part of the experience)

reviews_attraction.text: Friend of mine took me down to the basic area. I honestly don't know much about the park itself. However, the proximity to Nolan Creek makes it a very nice place to visit. There's a paved sidewalk that runs along the creek and lighting for night time. If you're a couple it's a great stroll.

It is still painted in plaid from the last golf tournament. Definitely stands out as you driving into Harbour Town. Gift shop on the bottom and on the top. Basically it's there to sell things. Recommended? If you're bored. There are lots of stores in Harbour Town. All around the lighthouse

Lot's of information and where you want to pick up the free shuttle to the Grand Canyon. REALLY don't expect to find parking at the visitors center. And even if you can, WHY would you... The shuttle is free !!! Just saying

very beautiful architecture if you have the opportunity to see it at night, do it. It's lit with multi colors. Not quite as intimidating as the Savannah Bridge. Even though they appear to be the same height LOL

Amazing ! Beautiful ! Perfect way to spend a day...So much to see and do... Good variety of animals and foliage. Lots of trees for shade...AND you can bring in your own food ! Figure at least 4 hours there...

If you go to the zoo make sure that you go to the biopark also. For one ticket price you can go to the biopark, the aquarium, and the zoo, and ride a train between the two. There's so much to see there.

Fantastic view... Take the free shuttle from town to avoid the parking lot by the visitors center... then take the blue line in the park. It is also free.. the shuttles will take you everywhere.GO GO GO

The USS Yorktown is located there. Most of the doson's have served on that ship. Their knowledge is extensive. Ask any questions they will have the answers. An absolute must see if you are in the area
Three words. Amazing amazing amazing. I was there in February ( ya I know) there's lots to see. I found the Mediterranean Garden absolutely beautiful. Take the time. Inexpensive and wonderful
It's amazing.... March visit so it was pretty empty and cold.. there is a small hike to the base of one of the falls but worth it...There are so many I can't remember which one this is....
If you love restored WWII ships GO!!! I have recently developed A interest.... I have been traveling all over the U.S. to see them... I think that kids will enjoy also.....simply amazing..
I love seeing old forts but, I don't think we spent more than 10 minutes to get through. Honestly there's not much to see. I couldn't even find anything worth taking a photo
I give it a 5 because thats what I expected it to be.... however the parks were closed due to weather.... it was Jan '18... I don't know what I was thinking ... January lol
It's awsome.. lot's of petrified wood.. Start at the visitor's ( after the toll booth) then do the drive... you won't be disappointed and don't forget the painted desert.
This place is soooooo much fun.. Take your husband or boyfriend or wife ect..... Kids ? that goes without saying... ELECTRIC so no fumes and they scoot !
It was very interesting, I liked it... WARNING when you start to recognize some of the original bottles... it really makes you feel old..lol ouch !!
Very Nice park. Right on Lake Belton... Covered tables, lot's of BBQ's.. It even has a boat launch..Try to stay for sunset you won't regret it..
It's worth a 10 min stop so you can say that you were there.. lot's of tourist shops and a bar....that is "on the corner" (naturally)...

This trail was definitely a lot of fun! If you drive all the way to the trailhead,  I recommend a vehicle with high clearance and 4x4 (especially for the drive back up), otherwise you could rip your power steering lines or damage an axle.

This trail was lightly trafficked when I went on a Wednesday. Only passed 5 other people. There are ropes in place in some steep areas that some kind soul was thoughtful enough to install, I made use of most of them. I used a map and my ears, and continued upstream until I found the falls. This is a treasure! Towering walls engulf the falls area with jagged, sharp shapes that house dramatic shadows with contrasting, vibrant greenery growing out of the rock walls. The waterfall is close to 100 feet tall, and in early June when I went the waters were flowing with powerful force.  I am in one of my photos of the fall, to the left - I look like an ant. I definitely recommend this trail. I can't wait to come back and bring my son!

This is my favorite place in Oklahoma.  There are trails here for all skill / experience levels, and the terrain is some of the most beautiful in the state. The visitor center is really great, with hands-on exhibits for kiddos (and adults too!), Doris Campground has friendly staff and a variety of campsites from RV/ electric sites to backcountry. The showers at the campground are nice, not all camping comes with hot water. Note that drinking water from the campground must be filtered or boiled, but you can B.Y.O.W. too. The Charon's Garden Wilderness Area is a wonderful place to go backpacking,  and for me it isn't far so I can save on gas and still escape into the wilderness for a few days. If you plan to backpack, you must get a permit first.

I went for one purpose: to destroy some crab legs with my dad. We accomplished our goal. This spot has the best crab legs I've had in Oklahoma.  On Friday night for less than $20 you can eat all the seafood you can handle, which includes catfish, shrimp, and yes - crab legs. They are cooked so well, not overly salty, and they are so delicious. I treat myself here about once a year, it has always been good! The only issue I have is the limited seating. I'm patient, and don't mind waiting - and the plus side of that is that the dining area is never super crowded or loud!

This place has been on my bucket list for over a decade. Supai is made up of the stuff of dreams, and Mooney Falls is absolutely magical. Hiked to Beaver Falls, came back, and of course someone proposed to his lady right in front of the falls. It's THAT pretty.
The climb down can be dangerous, even for experienced outdoorsmen / women. Go slow, give one another LOTS of space (if the dude above you falls, you'll be breaking that fall!), and be sure you've got a good hand hold and footing. Totally worth the climb. So happy I got to check this off of my bucket list.

I cannot sing the praises of this museum enough! As a single parent, it is especially challenging to find good ways for my son and I to spend our free time that 1. Are worth our time, and 2. Fit into the budget. I have consistently had a membership here, and my boy and I love it! The fees are very affordable.  The museum itself is really wonderful. Endless educational opportunities,  plus they have some great seasonal exhibits and programs. I love that we can bring friends with us on our membership,  too. No complaints,  we absolutely love the Sam Noble Museum!

This is my favorite place to hike in Oklahoma. I love the boulder field, the bats, the varied plant life and the rock formations.  The water is beautiful. This is a protected area, please be respectful - stay on the trails and leave no trace. No open fires allowed in this area. Permit required to camp overnight. Elk Mountain done 3-6 times in a day is good training for okies sho like to travel and climb bigger mountains. The boulder field is a lot of fun to climb around in. Be careful, bring plenty of water, and watch out for rattlesnakes.

My son got to check off the Grand Canyon NP from his list, and we had the best park ranger to cite the oath for my boy to repeat. Ranger Lance was a lot of fun, and he clearly loves his job! The visitor center is really nice, the theatre is impressive, and the educational film is actually not boring at all. My 6 year old sat through it, and was captivated. Also, I travel quite a bit, and so far the GC has the BEST tasting water at their water stations! Fill up here for free before you hike!

This was a stop on a road trip for my son and I. The staff is extremely helpful, everyone we interacted with was awesome with my  6 year old son, and we LOVED how hands-on this place is. We got to have our hands cleaned by shrimp, we got to pet snakes, lizards, birds, and we got to feed and pet stingrays and sharks! This place gave us some wonderful experiences and lasting memories. Would absolutely recommend,  particularly on a rainy day when you need an activity and can't go outside.

This place reminds me of Garden of the Gods in Colorado,  but it is much larger. Hiking alongside the river on the River trail was nice, but absolutely be on the lookout for rattlesnakes. I came across 4 rattlers and 2 garter snakes during my hike. Just be respectful and give them space to move off of the trail. The rock formations here are interesting and quite stunning. Definitely hike here, there are trails for all skill levels, that everyone can enjoy.

If you like waterfalls, crystal clear-blue water, moss, lichens the size of cabbage leaves, Jurassic Park sized ferns, mushrooms of all sizes and colors, and that delicious earthy smell that comes up from rich soil as you hike along the trail, definitely check this area out. EVERYTHING here is beautiful. I was so high on life hiking this area. I cannot wait to go back again to explore it more! Bring water and snacks, stay on the trail, leave no trace!

We love this place! My son is 6 years old. We have attended the Halloween Party here for the last 2 years. They have such an incredible collection of skeletons,  and the displays are stunning. We will return again and again, and we look forward to attending more educational programs here! If you get the chance to do something hands on, like dissecting an owl pellet, take it! Staff is friendly, knowledgeable, and helpful.

Holy bat cloud, Batman! This was a bucket list spot to visit for my son and I both. We had a blast watching the endless bats stream out from beneath the bridge at dusk. We love bats, and this is the most we have ever seen at once. I love how the local community has embraced these wonderful creatures and encourages others to appreciate them as well. Go watch the bats, you won't regret it. This made a great memory for us.

There were a lot of people,  but this is worth the crowd. Beautiful area for bird and ride pool viewing. Please be respectful of the signs and ropes! These animals are sensitive, and if people are handling them and walking in the tide pools they depend on, they could die. The area surrounding this is peppered with trails that offer beautiful ocean views. I highly reccomend making this a stop on your 101 road trip!

Went here for my son's school field trip. The OKC zoo has really improved a lot over the years. The educational program was tailored well to the age group. The educator our group of kindergartners had was very patient, and did well speaking to the group at their level. My son is crazy about the goats in the petting zoo. We also love the Oklahoma Trails exhibit,  particularly the bats, fish/snakes, and the bears!

Nice place for a day hike, some light climbing,  or a weekend of camping. The scenery is really pretty and unique. This is a particularly great spot to take small children for hiking. The trails are well worn, very easy to hike, and there are some cool plants and pools along the way which keep it interesting for kiddos. Nothing too strenuous here, but a fun place to visit. My son has been going since he was 2.

Such a gem tucked away in the Texas Panhandle. Grateful for the dog friendly policy here. If you will be taking a trip that passes through the Amarillo area, plan to spend some hours here. This is a beautiful location to stretch your legs, get some blood pumping, catch some views and fresh air, and recharge your battery. A road trip worthy stop, as well as a great destination for a hiking or camping trip.

Cool place to see some very temporary artwork! Fun stop on a road trip, bring the kids and let them legally graffiti on something! Fun for the whole family. I dont want to give the place a lower rating because of trash, because it is the visitors' responsibility to clean up after themselves, but there is typically a lot of trash here. Please clean up after yourselves,  folks.

Beautiful oasis in the middle of a city setting. Nice for birding, walking, macro photography,  and portrait photography. If you're into plants, you'll be happy having a stroll here! It smells so beautiful walking through the garden area, with floral and herbal scents lightly wafting through the air. If you're into frisbee golf, you'll like this park,too! !

This lake is absolutely gorgeous. It looks like water from the Bahamas! Not too crowded, amazing spot to spend the day swimming and sunbathing. It can get deep fast, so definitely be careful if you bring small children,  I'd suggest a life vest. Also bring some goggles / snorkeling gear because this is an ideal place to snorkel! Can't wait to visit again!

Underrated, and not talked about enough. This place is beautiful. The highway doesn't cut through this national park, so you really can "get away" once you've hiked out a few miles. Will be returning! My 5 year old son loved hiking here. Rangers were very helpful, and even mailed my son a patch! We love Guadalupe Mountains National Park!

Awesome swimming hole, not too crowded, family friendly,  beautiful water. I also appreciate the police officer that came through to check on things at pretty regular intervals. Very clean, not a lot of litter or broken glass to worry about. Nice place to come for a swim or to spend the day swimming and catching some uv rays.

A really incredible hike in exchange for a low number of miles - and the entire hike is beautiful,  not just the waterfall at the end. My 8 year old son hiked this trail without a problem,  and he really enjoyed all of the cool plants, trees, and river views along the way to the fall. This is definitely a hike to go on!

Had a great time! Such a cool way to experience holiday fun for the family. We walked through the park and enjoyed the mild weather, drank hot chocolate,  took a ride on the "train," met Santa, and had an all around wonderful time.
Well maintained trails, beautiful scenery,  wonderful place for bird watching. My 6 year old had no problems hiking here after a morning spent in the Constellation Trails near here.
Cute park, clean, nice playground. We had a picnic here for Thanksgiving  / my birthday. I can't wait to go back when I have more time, and I'll bring my kayaks!

WoW.  I gave it 3 stars just for the place being so peaceful and quiet.  A nice place to relax.  Otherwise, this Geyser is not that great.  It felt like its a man made fountain or sprinkler in the ground.  In order for anyone not to investigate they placed signs such as "do not enter".  Anyhow, we only lasted here for about 45 minutes.  Nothing special really.  Wish they could have had a wine tasting section, that itself would have made this place an even 5 stars.  They should get this idea from me. LoL

Aloha! The Castle of Love has one of the Best Wines in Napa Valley. Beautiful and Unique place to have Wine Tasting. The tasting room is located in the lower floor and   enjoyed my time. However, as the day went by the place got very crowded. I came when it opened and I recommend being here early. My wine choices are the LA Castellana and Fantasia.  It's a must spot to visit in Napa.

Aloha! Tempe beach park is where everyone hangs out during the weekends. It’s clean and well maintained. It’s the spot of the finish line of many marathons and events. Located just across Tempe Downtown it’s a great place to spend time with family then eat at the plenty restaurants in town. It also has beautiful scenery of the river and bridge.

Aloha! Beautiful museum of art. Lots of interesting paintings and structures.  Not good for kids. Don't bring them. I struggled with mines.
