There are food trucks outside which us the best part of the museum, in my honest opinion . Don't get me wrong, I love art. But the stuff you see here is laughable so it just entertained me... lol

Aloha! One of my favorite spot to just relax. One of the only spots to check out the mounts water and salt water mix. Wow. This place is so magical. I see lots of young people surfing and possibly sacrificing their life if not careful. The waves are so strong it’s not really for swimming. I tried once and I almost lost my sandwich!
likes: Unique water feature (salt and fresh water mix)

reviews_attraction.text: Aloha! Lechuza beach is a Secluded, Beautiful and quiet beach. Beautiful clean sand surrounded by private owned homes. There's Rocks on the north side perfect for taking engagement and family photos.  Beach access is tricky. We parked at the outside the gates to make sure we don't get locked out. So parking can be a challenge.

Aloha! Wow what a place to learn about space and shuttles and rockets. We loved the tour. Loved the countless museums. Lots of things for the kids to do. It’s very educational. Saw Space X and we weee wowed. Overall an excellent spot for the family to spend quality time. The cafeteria has pricy food but they have beer 🤙🏼

Aloha! My favorite ride in Universal Studios Orlando Florida. The aliens stood in front of us the whole time making my score impossible to beat. I’m thrilled to be the best shooter here. Also make sure you had a beer or two before riding here. It would be more fun.

Aloha! A most beautiful park overseeing the city of San Francisco.  Lots of places for the kids to play. Slide, Swings and climbing areas galore. Plenty of grassy spots to hang out. Totally awesome spot.  Restrooms very clean for a public park.

Just a Gorgeous Rock and Beach Formations.  The view is just fantastic and the waves just rocks this place.  People come here to swim but a little risky due to many rocks.  This is a spiritual place and is respected by the locals.

Aloha! If you love ice cream then come here. Lots of very interesting artistic displays. There's snacks and Food given throughout the tour. Not bad. Good to bring the family. I just wished there a more ice cream flavors to taste.

Aloha! Nice park next to the 710 freeway. Facilities were clean and roomy. Enjoyed a birthday party with friends. They have a nice sized tot lot and work out machines. Not the biggest park but nice enough to have family fun.

Nice little library in the middle of downtown. Unfortunately there are a few homeless roaming around. The grounds are fairly maintained.

Loved that it's surrounded by so many restaurants.  Makes this location good to visit.

Aloha! Waimea beach park is perfect for the family and friends to hang out and swim. There's a black Rock where people are jumping off it. Water is good and waves are fairly strong but swimmable.  Parking can be an issue.

Aloha!  I love this beach... you can possibly find turtles here if you are lucky.  My kids loves it here.  Next to our timeshare property.  Walking distance to the Gazebo restaurant.  This area is the best.

Aloha! Very beautiful and serene beach. The waves creates a most peaceful and relaxing sounds to your ears. The water is very deep the moment you jump in. People around are friendly and lots of parking.

Aloha! Very nice and simple place for kids to have fun. Well maintained and staff are friendly. My crazy kids had fun and entertained. That is all that mattered to me today because they were so hyper.
Aloha! Simple the best spot to get the Welcome to Napa Valley. There's another south of this sign but there's no where to park. It has open area and safe. Just across the Castillo di Amorosa.
Beautiful Place. We went when there was 50 mph gust winds 😅 We survived and so much to do for such a simple place. Loves the space ride at their theatre with the Ma. Lopez Rabbit.
Aloha! Nice and simple place to bring the kids to play. Covered playground is the big plus. Plenty of space to picnic. Decent BBQ grills and trails to walk. Overall stand up.
Aloha! One of my favorite spots to take couples for wedding shoots. Close by all the resorts and a small parking lot. Also the sunset is amazing.
Beautiful Pier and it's simple too. Lots of room for swimmers. Not a big parking lot so it's tough to park weekends.  Great for photoshoots.
Beautiful and Angelic. One of the most visited places in a of Arizona. A special place for prayer and to give thanks to God.
I’m here at a wedding and love the large rooms. Our wedding went very well. San Diego is so beautiful. YaY 😀
Aloha! Each time we watch the sunset here it never fails. My kids love to play here. It’s the best 🤙🏼

It depends on what you are looking for -- it can be good or bad
To like Channel Islands National Park, you need to like water.  The beauty and the activities are best enjoyed from a kayak or a boat.  If you like hiking or other land activities, this is not the park for you.  We visited Anapaca island and there really isn't much there.  It's a small island that is basically a large, flat rock.  There is no trees or shade except next to some small buildings.  The entire figure 8 hiking / walking trail is probably 2 miles long.  While the scenery of the coast and the ocean is very nice, it's a very small place and can be explored in a couple of hours, max.  It's hard to get to because you need to pay to get a ferry there, and on many days, it's only one trip out and one trip back, so you have to wait until 3:30 before your ride comes to take you back.  The terrain is very flat so there are no "surprise views" as you come around the bend.  There is no service except for a bathroom and a very small visitor center exhibit.  You must bring any water or food you need to consume during your day there.  In the spring, I'm told there are tons of birds that nest and gather there, to the point of not being suitable for humans.  On the other hands, we saw some kayakers and some in small private boats having an excellent time exploring the shore from below and explore sea caves.  Some were swimming off of the boat.  There are under water marine sanctuaries for snorkeling or scuba diving.  Essentially, if you stick to the land portion, it's not that interesting.
dislikes: No services (except bathroom and small visitor center)

reviews_attraction.text:
We came upon this place kind of by accident just browsing around Google Maps.  It's a hike up rock strewn path for about one mile to a lake at the base of the glacier and another half mile to get to the actual glacier.  The lake is beautiful.  The glacier is small but it's there.  The hike is through lots of rocks that looks like a dried stream bed.  Hiking shoes/boots would come in very handy on this trail.  It can feel strenuous because of the altitude (somewhere around 10000 feet).  To us, it's worth the 2 hours or so we invested in the hike.  It's a nice stopping point for us as we drove from Estes Park to Grand Lake in the "southern loop".
There are no "trail markers" along the way, only some warning signs as you get up to the lake.  Follow "up hill" and stay on the main stream path on the way to the lake, and "down hill" on your way back and you won't get lost, but you can get nervous and doubt if you are going the right way if there are no one else around.  This is not a park so it seems to be private.  It could certainly use a few direction signs.
It's is cool to see and "touch" the glacier.  We visited in late October and the glacier is small and seems to be melting.  I'd imagine it will "grow" through the winter but I wonder how many years it will be before the glacier is gone in the summer / fall time.

Different view of the canyons
Canyonlands National Park is a "tweener".  It's not as grand as the Grand Canyon.  It's not as dramatic as the Black Canyon.  It's not as pretty as Arches.  However, it has its own charm that is best explored with off road vehicles.  There are actually three parts of the park, as defined by the Green and Colorado rivers.  Island in the Sky is the main section with the most number of visitors.  The Mesa portion gets very few visitors and accessible from US24 (not from Moab).  Needles is also less visited and a bit harder to get to.
Canyonlands has a very different feel than Arches.  It is bigger and caters to more hiking and four wheeling.  It has a lot less visitors and you can actually get away from the crowds that mobs Arches next door.  There are several good hikes along the various canyon rims with dramatic vistas that reward the hiking effort.  There are also many day and overnight hiking trails for those that are hardy.

Nice ride on the calm Colorado, with dinner
We concluded a beautiful day by taking a "sunset boat tour" with Canyonlands by Night and Day.  It's called a "jet boat" but it's really just a boat that can go relatively fast.  We went about 20 miles upriver, with the guide/driver pointing out various interesting formations, sights, and rock climbers.  In each case, he rotated the boat so we can get a clear view from either side of the boat.  The water is calm, like a lake.  He had to weave in and out a bit to avoid the sand bars.  At this time of the year (Oct. 2016), the river level is very low, less than 2 feet on average.  The boat is specially designed for shallow water.  The guide is entertaining and knowledgeable.  While it's kind of expensive, it was a pleasant experience.  The dinner was "just OK" with a selection of BBQ style entrees.  The dinner is after the boat ride back at "headquarters".

Bond Park is an excellent city park, with something for everyone.  You like water?  There is a lake and boat rental in season, with ducks and geese.  There is a nice area to let your dog to swimming.  You like playing ball?  There are baseball fields.  You have young kids who like playgrounds?  yep, they have that too.  How about a nice hike?  There is a hiking trail around the lake, some parts paved and some parts not, and it's just the right distance.  Want summertime music?  there is a band shell.  How about just open fields for play?  There is one too.  A nice hill to slide down if it ever snows?  Yep, there is one of those and once a year, they make snow.  There is also a community center and a senior center in the park, as well as exercise trails.  This park has something for everyone, one of the best town parks around.

This is a small (by national park standards) but very nice park. The 2.2 mile boardwalk is wonderful with 20 stops to observe various items. About 1/3 of it is newly renovated (and completed as of late May 2016). The story is interesting. We went on a very rainy day so we didn't explore beyond the boardwalk. Be prepared for bugs. We went on a day where the mosquito meter is at a "2" out of 6. We were not bothered by mosquitos but we had deer fly buzzing around us, which is very annoying. Since it's low land swamp, it will flood regularly so check for conditions before you go to make sure it's not flooded. There is ranger led canoe trip on Fridays for free, as well as ranger led hikes.

The park is FREE! Did I say the park is FREE? It's also only 30 minutes or so from downtown Columbia so it's very convenient.

Worth the money?
We stopped here late one afternoon on our way out of Canyonlands National Park on the recommendation of another traveler we met earlier in the week.  There is a separate entrance fee from the National Parks because it's a state park.  The claim to fame is the overlook at a bend of the Colorado river.  The scenery is pretty, dramatic and you can clearly see the river as it bends through the landscape.  If this is the first scene you see of the Canyonlands, you would appreciate it.  After visiting the National Park, and seeing the Green River / Grand viewpoints, it seems the same.  The visitor center looks like it's seen better days.  The exhibits looks like it needs significant updating and repair.

Small visitor center in the Needles district -- sporadic gas facilities
The Needles district of Canyonlands National Park is the less visited section of Canyonlands.  It's fairly out of the way and it's a long ways after you get off of the main highway - US 191.  The drive in is pretty enough.  The needles district is good if you want to do some all day hikes into the back country.  If you just want to drive and take short walks, there isn't a lot here.  The pothole pointe trail is a short and interesting trail to take.  Cave Spring takes you to some ruins left by the cowboys (and the need to climb a short ladder).  If you have the time, by all means visit but if you are short on time, this is lower priority.

Best single attraction at Canyonlands
If you were to rank the various viewpoints or "attractions" at Canyonlands that you can get to without a four wheel drive, this ranks on top.  The trail is a must to appreciate this park.  The trail is not super easy but it's worth the effort.  You walk along the rim with some dramatic vertical cliffs.  After some uphill, you reach a viewpoint that affords a 270 degree vista of the river / valley below.  It's breathtaking.  The view is well worth the hiking effort.  The trail is not that long.  It can be done in a hour or so.  If you do not want to hike, the view from the parking lot is also OK, but not as dramatic as the hike.

Beautiful panorama of Death Valley - go in the morning!
Your car does most of the work to get you near the peak that is Dante's View where you can get a beautiful panorama of the valley below, including the famous salt flats at Badwater.  It's the best view of the full valley below and appreciate the vastness of the valley.  The morning sun will light up the mountain range to the west, the direction you are looking as you stand on the view point.  You can hike along the ridge to get different views but it's not necessarily better than the closer view points to the parking lot.

Beautiful panorama view
This is perhaps one of the best views in Rocky Mountain National Park.  It also seems to often be the last turn out before the rest of Trail Ridge Road is closed due to weather after mid-October.  Although we were there on such a day, and it was flurrying lightly, I can still appreciate the beauty, especially with a small amount of snow capping the nearby peaks.  The parking area is relatively large with bathroom facilities.  Worth the drive and the stop, even if you have to turn around and head back from there.

Good trail with a large but crowded parking lot
The parking lot serves both the Double Arch trail and the Windows trail, both are very popular.  It's not that hard to do both in a couple of hours and the scenery is beautiful.  This is why you came to Arches National Park, so you have to take the relatively easy hike.  Double Arches, like the name implies, leads you to two arches right next to each other.  It's next to a formation that looks like some elephants lined up.  You can get pretty close to the Double Arch (under one of them).

Good views but better one at Rainbow Curve
If you are coming from Estes Park, you get to this overlook first about half way up the mountain.  While it's beautiful, has OK parking (in two places), a walkway that cantilevered from the road, you get a better view of the same area further up the road from higher elevation.  If you have time, by all means stop here and visit, but if you are pressed for time, stop by the Rainbow Curve overlook instead.

An archway right out of a  movie set
You take a mile or so hike, after a short and bumpy car ride on a dusty dirt road so you can see and walk through a natural arch.  Not too bad but it's not very big and not particularly impressive.  If you have been to Arches National Park or plan to go, this can be skipped because you see far grander arches three.  It'll be hot most time of the year so bring water.  You can get some shade by the cliff walls.

Very pretty scene with a light house and lots of birds.  We came on a day when the actual lighthouse was closed so we can only observe from the observation area above the lighthouse next to the small parking area.  The scene is very photogenic.  It's very relaxing to watch the waves hit the shore below the lighthouse.  Many birds used the trees on the right side, across from the lighthouse, as perches and it made the scene even more magical.

Someone carved a trench in the rocks!
As the name implies, you see the Green River from this dramatic viewpoint.  It looks like someone took a knife and cut a trench through a plateau.  Of course, it's the Green River that carved this path through millions of years.  The view is still "other-worldly".  This viewpoint looks down on a bend in the Green River as it carves a path through a very flat looking plateau.

Beautiful new looking visitor center.  You can get all your questions answered, get your passport stamp, browse the shop, see the National Park movie, have a picnic outside, and get something from the cafe... but the cafe food is lousy and expensive, so keep that in mind.

Next door is Paradise Inn - the architecture is stunning with the "real" national park feel.

Good, informative visitor center with a temperature gauge outside
The rangers are super friendly and informative.  The film does a nice job of introducing the park.  The photo opportunity is just outside with the temperature reading for when it's hot and memorable.  There is a small gift shop for souvenirs.  Good initial stopping point to get your bearings.

It looks great in pictures and the whole idea of a "protected" cove with calm waters is enticing but......  While it's calm and good for swimming and snorkeling, there just wasn't that many colorful fish!!  I've seen a lot more fish snorkeling elsewhere.  It can get crowded with many boats anchoring so you may see more people than fish!

OK visitor center
This is a small visitor center but the major one for Canyonlands National Park.  It pales in comparison with Arches next door.  You still get useful information and the rangers are nice enough, but it could use some expansion.

Nice, but not as dramatic as Grand or Green River viewpoints
This is worthy of a quick stop and it's a different view from the other viewpoints in the park but not the best or the most dramatic.  Skip if you are short on time
Check to make sure the snow is gone before you visit.  We only saw a small part of the park but already loved it.  In 2017, the full loop of the park road was not open until nearly the end of July!!!
This is an outdoor facility where you can see the tip of a mock up of a minuteman missile.  The signs are OK but if you can go when there is a ranger, they bring it to life!
A very nice trail that runs along the ocean.  Great for walking, hiking and biking with gorgeous views.  There are huts along the way to rest and just take the view in.
Nice walk but very buggy on a late spring afternoon.  Second largest tree in the world.  Shorter walk than Sherman tree but just as good.

Nearing 90 years old, this statue is one of the most recognizable things on USC's campus and is monitored by a 24 hour video stream. Trojans are Faithful, Scholarly, Skillful, Courageous and Ambitious. The statue also now has a female counterpart, Hecuba, Queen of Troy. Fight on!

This bridge lives up to its reputation. A huge piece of architecture, it is fun to just watch the several lanes of traffic pass over it for awhile. While you're going over it, admire the water or the Boston skyline. I plan to revisit it at some point.

This place was pretty cool. Yes, it is a tourist trap but still worth visiting for a couple of hours. I almost felt like I was in China because of the sheer amount of Chinese people in this area. You can get a great deal of cheap goods here.

This place is a little dated now but still definitely worth visiting. They have several unique exhibits and it is a great way to learn about science! If you can go on a sunny day, I suggest doing that as well.
There are definitely better Presidential libraries but I still had a fun time touring this place. Not a must-see in Austin but if you have extra time, I'd stop by here for an hour or so.
This giant, red sculpture has been around for nearly 50 years! It makes a cameo in Ferris Bueller's Day Off and is definitely worth seeing in person if you've never stopped by it before.
This is a nice park to walk around for a couple hours. You get a nice view of the lake and the Chicago skyline here. I see myself coming back here in the future at some point.
Sure, there are better roller coasters in the world. However, this one is historic and a great deal of fun. Everyone should stop by here during their time at Coney Island!
An excellent museum, easily one of the best in the country. You can walk around and admire art for hours. Even the exterior of the building has various pieces of art.
There are better museums out there but this one is worth visiting to learn about Iowa's finest athletes. If you have a couple of hours to burn, check this place out!
This place can be crowded and even messy at times but if you've never been to L.A. before you still have to check it out. You'll find at least one star you like.
While not quite as iconic as The Empire State Building or beautiful as One World Trade Center, everyone should still stop by here at some point while in NYC.
Almost 45 years old this building still looks pretty new and shines brightly on a sunny day. I look forward to the next time I'm able to see it in person.
This place is pretty cool. You've seen it in countless films and shows and it actually lives up to its fame. One of the better things to see in Hollywood.
A huge, spacious park in one of the best parts of Chicago. Home to Lollapalooza, championship celebrations, and several other events throughout the year.
A nice park but the place Chandra Levy was murdered at in 2001. It also happened to be one of the last places she was searching on her computer.
This building is somewhat dated now but is still pretty cool and the design is iconic/unmissable. Worth visiting if you've never been here.
This place lives up to the hype. If you're not afraid of heights I definitely recommend checking this out if you haven't been here before.
An iconic, beautiful statue that has been linked with the university since 1903! Stop by and take a selfie if you haven't already!
There are more impressive buildings/views out there but this is a great way to see most of the city if you've never been before.
Not the best water park I've ever been to but still very fun. I'd go here again in the future. They have several awesome slides.
This place is a little overhyped but still very interesting and an important part of American history. You might as well go.
The oldest park in America is also one of the biggest. You can walk around and explore this place for hours. So much to see.
The highest court in the land! If you need something settled, ultimately these guys will have the final say on it.
The Pier to go to Alcatraz Island. In a pretty good part of the city and I enjoyed the tour a great deal.

The play structure is imaginative. And brand NEW! My kids loved all the rope obstacles, "the world" spinning globe like structure, and the large swing. I loved the water views of the bay, the plentiful parking.

I also appreciate Shoreline on the bayside is closed. there is much more pedestrian traffic, it's easy to pop over to the beach.

I don't love the lack of shade structures, but I hear the city might be putting forth a bond to get funding for some shade structures in the future. A girl can dream.

I didn't realize Texas had a slot canyon until I came here. We followed the map we got at the big bend ranch visitor center. Data coverage is spotty so maps functions on our phones weren't super reliable.

It's well marked. The hike begins going downhill and into the canyon. We brought it young kids and they loved hearing thier echoes.

The deeper you get the more chance you have for increasingly difficult scrambling. And then you hit water and can go no further. Overall excellent hike.

It's a beautiful, well-done, big city caliber attraction. And yet. It has a small town feel. We have an annual pass. Employees recognize us, say hi, talk to my kids. There are 5 touch pools, and beautiful exhibits. My son's favorite is when you can touch the jellyfish. The dolphin and bird show are fabulous. We also love the view of the city if you take the elevator/stairs to the very top of the old section of the aquarium. We also always have to say hi to Duncan the enormous grouper.

This hike wasn't listed on the big bend state park map. It was a few pull offs past Closed Canyon. It's beautiful and worth the effort.

This hike starts at a high and then goes downward. Keep that in mind as you budget energy to make the climb back. We went in February and found a few bluebonnets sprouting along the river bank. Our 4 yo and 2 yo were enchanted with the wild flowers and butterflies. The hoodoos or balancing rocks weren't too bad either.

Wow. This center is completely run by volunteers. As of 2016, it has been open 2 years. They've helped rehabilitate and release hundreds of animals who otherwise would've died. Sea turtles, pelicans, egrets, and many other gorgeous animals. Pam gave us a tour. She even showed us some butterfly eggs underneath milkweed plants. I learned so much about local plants. What a gem.

Do the Dam Tour! It's about $8 per person. You take elevators all the way to the base of the dam. Our son enjoyed seeing all the huge equipment. I loved learning about the history, including the watermelon patch that was started on the green space at the base of the dam. Unfortunately it had to be shut down because the dam workers fought over who got the melons.

Low key tour. Our three year old enjoyed jumping in all the puddles inside the cave. Good thing the camp ground has showers so we could easily rinse off the mud. Guide was very knowledgeable about the fossils that are inside, the nestng bats, and the cave formation. Some crouching and about 150 stairs involved, but overall a mild hike. Tour took about an hour

Adding my 5 star review. What a fabulous zoo. YOU CAN FEED GIRAFEES HERE!!! The monkeys were all very active, the staff were all very engaging with my curious kids. We also loved the splash pad and the playground. It's very smartly placed halfway through the zoo. A very enjoyable day.

Magical. I was expecting everything to be at sea level. Surprised to see a bit of elevation change. There are many short hikes along the loop of the park. We didn't have time to visit them all. Need to come back again to soak up this piece of paradise.

Very cool hike and gave a glimpse into native American living I wasn't aware of. Very cool walk through time. Save some energy for the climb back up the stairs. Oh, and the junior ranger badge here is really cool. Made out of wood.

We enjoyed all the playground equipment. There were at least 4 separate play areas complete with shade covers. Our favorite part was the boardwalk trails over the wetlands areas. Lots of huge trees covered in Spanish Moss.

We are astronomy junkies, so we really wanted to see this. It was big and cool. Many of the exhibits were a bit gimmicky. The entrance fee twas a bit steep for the experience. Nonetheless, glad we went

$2 entrance fee for kids 4-12. $4 fee for adults. This is a really nicely done nature center. The trails were well marked and it made for a great day exploring. I particularly enjoyed the frog chorus.
What a well designed park! Separate yet engaging play areas for big and little kids. A splash pad controlled by a button if kids need to cool off. We came twice the first day we discovered it.
What a great stop driving along i-10. We walked the trails along the nature center for 40 minutes or so. Our kids got thier wiggles out and we got to take in the scenery of Sonora.
Great are to let kids run off some steam. I appreciated the 2 separate play structures for big and smaller kids. There was also a well marked walking path to explore.
Free, fun museum with unusual exhbits. The huge walls of taxidermy feel very Texas. My daughter enjoyed during in a saddle and the ranch life hands on exhibit.
Even though the eruption here was over 1000 years ago, the lava flows still look fresh. We enjoyed the 30 minute or so hike around the various flows.
At this time there is a lot of construction at the waterfront. There is a large patch of grass with great views of downtown and the bay.
They have an excellent nature story time for young kids. We caught some insects in nets and learned about the wildlife in the delta.
Lots of wildlife here. Saw wild turkeys, alligators, and racoons. Cool place to get in touch with the wild side of Texas.
Huge playground on the bay. Nice washing trails. Hard to find shade and good views of kids playing in the park.
We came in October and saw THOUSANDS of Monarchs here. Laid back atmosphere and great way to spend a morning.
250k bats! Very cool. Once they emerge it can take 10-20 minutes for all to leave. Go get some mosquitos!
This is one of my go to spots in Corpus. We especially enjoy looking for sea turtles on the jetty.

An easy short hike from the parking lot.  Water optional for this, it is that short and easy.  Nice foto ops.  As of April 2017 the water level is only at about 40-50%.  This is the best water source for miles, a great opportunity for critter watching when the crowds are not there...early AM or some weekdays, if you are lucky.  The wall street mill is a short mile walk away, nice piece of history there. attached are some plant pics....plenty already of the dam.

I hiked the area reached by the Palm Springs aerial tramway, which starts at over 8000 feet, in July. Ambient temperature is a good 30 degrees cooler than Palm Springs, a welcome relief from that 100++ heat!  Trails are easy to follow,  and maps are available from a ranger station, showing easy to moderately strenuous hikes.  A great getaway.  Beware, no potable water available apart from the ranger station and the team station.

Beautiful, quiet area.  We checked out the beach....covered by gnats, quite a walk from the parking area.  Kids enjoyed the easy floating in the lake, but found the water quite irritating to their skin, no idea how common this is, but they don't have particularly sensitive skin, so beware.  Adequate bathroom facilities and informative souvenir shops.

A great view of the Coachella Valley from the north.  Can see Palm Springs, etc as well as the San Andreas fault.  Over 4000 feet elevation, so relatively cool for the area.  Reasonable parking, very short walk, and bathroom available.  About 15 miles from the west entrance of the national park.

A nice place to relax and for kids to play.  Small patch of great grass and big sandbox in kids area.  Parking by library limited, but much more available behind building.  Great grass in ball field.  Occasional seedy folks wandering around...as well as high schoolers looking for things to do.

This is a 3-4 star experience, depending on your love of flowers...fields of them...rather beautiful.  Admission a bit pricey for what you get, which is access to the fields.  Wagon rides are extra.  Nice little kids play area with remnants of Santas Village for them to play in.

Some historic relics,  but more of an ongoing study or commentary on humanity and our culture.   Not really my interest,  and the topics were not my cup of tea.  Basic admission is$13 for adults,  they charge another $19 for an exhibit on cannibals... which i declined.

A small town museum with local artifacts and some live small animals.  Staff friendly and knowledgeable.  The provide a school kids program periodically that is interactive and worth attending, but the number allowed to attend is limited.

Peaceful, open dessert. Dramatic vistas, occasional big horn sheep, rocks to climb, some tenants of early inhabitants. I really enjoy the place.   Only minimal development,  also few amenities... Bring your own water!

Extensive display of model railroading,  clearly involving many dedicated craftsmen and historians. In addition to the many completed operating displays, others are under construction.   This place is huge.
An amazing array of teaching games for pre- and school age kids.  Can easily spend a full day here and not do it all.  Highly recommended for any youngster that is inquisitive and willing to play.
A great collection of vintage and near contemporary military aircraft and a few other military memorabilia. They also have some aircraft simulators,  a library,  souvenir shop, and a small cafe.
Nice facility.   Plenty of parking with easy access to bike/ jogging trails.  Bathrooms good for 2 each.   Large shade/rain-shelter structure with many picnic tables... for picnics or parties.
A little pricey but great family entertainment.  The shows have sadly lost some of their animal acts.  The dolphin arena gets quite hot and there is no shade, wear sunscreen or sun clothes.
Quiet, unspoiled, open spaces in Contra Costa.  Limited facilities, but nice hiking and views.  Amenities...archery, bike trails, horse trails, a few rest rooms and water fountains.
A great example,  if largely rebuilt,  of a native american community from about a thousand years ago... also smaller displays of other decayed structures in outlying areas.
Nice facility...kids play area, play grounds, restrooms, paved trail for biking, jogging, etc.  Worth a visit if near by and you want to burn some outdoor time and energy.
Huge local park in Las Vegas.  Has something for everyone.  We use the various kiddie play areas, but there is way more....a lake, ball fields, dog park, jogging path....
Nice community rec area... play equipment for little kids as well as athletic fields.   Concessions sometimes available, too.  Plenty of free parking.
A nice selection of warm and hot environment animals.   Very good instructional presentations.  Can be rather hot in summer months- go early!
A medium sized out doors museum of actual rail engines, cars, etc.  they also sponsor a Thomas the Train exhibit periodically.  Good times!
A decent community park, with a children's play area, large playing field, a covered picnic area, and restrooms.  Plenty of parking.
Modest sized museum with a nice selection /variety of themes and marquees.  A nice half day visit, currently emphasizing "rat rods".
Interesting rock formation at the turnoff to Keys View in JTNP.  It has an adjoining breathing lot,  but no other facilities.
Extensive California history on display.... but in need of updating.   Didn't make it to the other areas...I will come back!

This place is amazing and scary as hell. Little disappointed since i was the only one of the three of us that went all the way to the top. Make sure, before you pay, that your friends won't freak out half way up. The stairs on the jump outside the elevator are rickety and the rest are open grates. You can see straight down. It sways at the top and is crazy windy. The worst part is the chairlift ride down. It's a great view but it feels like you're going down almost vertically. The whole experience is unnerving but glad i did it!

One of the best home tours in town. Most of all the grounds are intact including the slave quarters and the house is being preserved instead of restored so you get to see more of the original finishes. It's a little more interesting because most houses choose to restore them. The self guided audio tour is nice. Gives you more freedom to skip along so it isn't quite as much of a hostage situation if you end up in a tour group with someone who asks 800 questions.

Beautiful house.  Its such a shame to think the whole street was covered with mansions at one time, and this one was almost tore down to build a parking lot for a holiday inn.  As if that wasn't bad enough, they've had to spend countless dollars undoing awful design choices from the 60's when everyone decided to paint over wood work and wall paper.  Its worth taking a tour at least to donate the money for restoration.
dislikes: Cultural Value: Loss of historical context
Facilities & Services: Past neglect and poor renovations

reviews_attraction.text: We ended up here by accident looking for the lighthouse. Turns out we put the wrong (actually the correct) lighthouse in Google maps. Give yourself more than a hour if you want to go back on the hiking trails. We didn't really leave ourselves enough time and had to do a quick breeze through, which wasn't bad since it's only $7 a person. Great place to visit on the way back from tybee.

Beautiful gardens. It's really easy to walk to as well. The city trails go right to it. The museum was larger than i expected it to be. I thought it would be just a quick breeze-through and we ended up there for over two hours, and that's without really reading everything, just casually passing through. Well worth visiting.

Very nice beach. You can walk a long way out into the water and never be over your head. The water is Crystal clear. Nice and sandy so it's easy to walk on. Biting flies are a bit of a problem. Very long coast though so no problem finding a private area to swim.

Well worth visiting. It's almost an overload of information. Admission was only $4 and you could easily spend 2 hours there if you really take the time to absorb everything. Good for 1 hour if you just breeze through to look at pictures.

Great monument and museum. Well worth the price of admission. And easy to climb. Most of the way up is ramps instead of stairs. One has to wonder, however, what the pilgrims would have thought of such an austentatious(sp?) monument.

It was fun. If you go there about a hour before closing you get a discounted admission. Not a super country nerd so a hour was the perfect amount of time to see everything. Could have spent more time but a hour was enough

Very large museum.  Bigger than I thought it would be.  Certainly worth the $5 admission price.  Unfortunately, the art withered away when we found the ducklings on the roof.  Art Schmart.  The ducks were the best part.

very interesting museum.  Only $5 and quite a bit larger than I expected.  Takes about half a hour if you just breeze though, could spend longer if you stop and read everything.  Worth the price of admission.
Insane.  Completely insane.  Its huge!  Never even knew this existed when I was planning our trip.  How?  This needs to get more recognition because its worth stopping to see.  Completely nuts!
I think I missed it.  Apparently I was standing right in front of it but it looked like every other block.  I mean, the houses are all lovely.  Guess I should have been paying more attention.
Nice park. Interesting choice to have a civil war memorial with Roman gods. Seems like an odd choice. i also liked the replica gatlin gun pointed directly at the houses across the street.
Huge sprawling expanse of a museum. Lots of ground to cover. And it's a national park so your tax dollars are covering the cost of admission, so no excuse not to go!!
Unfortunately, we weren't able to do the whole tour because of time but they have different price options for how much you want to see. Lots of old ruins to explore.
Looks like all the other parks.  its nice I guess, nothing more special than any other one though.  I think this is the one where they filmed "forest gump".
It was fun. Half the exhibits were closed and the tower was closed so maybe a reduced price on admission would have been nice. It's a neat building though.
Lovely park. Everyone has been here and seen the famous pineapple fountain. Not much else to say. Don't drown in the fountains like the sign says
Fun place. Much larger than i expected. Just casually strolling through without stopping can take about 2 hours. Good way to spend the afternoon.
Fun place to visit. The pictures are a tad staged with dramatic lighting, but worth seeing. Cave exploring is always fun.
Cute park. Not much to do but nature, which is nice. Mostly a hiking area. Thought there would be more of a fort to see.
dislikes: Minimal fort遗迹似乎没有完全满足用户的期望，但根据指导原则，我们应该关注景点的核心特征和服务。因此，“Minimal fort”可以理解为用户对景点的文化价值（即堡垒的历史或文化展示）感到不满。让我们调整一下以更符合要求：

reviews_attraction.text: Great place to walk around. Lots to see. There's also a public bathroom at the locks, if anybody is looking for one.
Waiting for the ferry is never fun, but if you can book a sunset ferry to San Juan, do it.  Absolutely beautiful.
More interesting than i thought it would be. Lots to look at and learn. Good for at least 2 hours.

Came here on one of the hot October weeks San Diego was having and it was refreshing because that sea breeze! It made it about 5 to 10 degrees cooler than the inland!
The park was easy to get to and don't pay for preferred parking if you come early as it is just like one row over! So say no thank you to the cash grab
Once you get into seaworld there are many things to do but grab a map real quick!

In front of you will be the explorer's reed which you can touch small fish that literally eat the dead skin off your hand! It feels super weird but i promise they won't eat you alive!
Sesame street bay of play is basically the  where the kids play. They had journey to Atlantis where one employee said they would open at 11AM but when we went back again at a later time, it was even running. Not cool bro

The wild arctic is super awesome. First it's the ride which takes you through the north pole and it's decent but after they lead you into an ice cold area (perfect for those super hot days) where there are narwhals, polar bears, penguins. The setting is like a arctic base in Antarctica. They even had walls that felt like ice! Definitely the coolest place of the park!

Penguin encounter was okay, just a runway that'll take you to some penguins, like SO MANY penguins!!!

We stopped by for the dolphin show becuase that's a must! And we were super hot so we went to the front area in the splash zone, I knew what was coming but boy was I not expecting so much water. Especially the water that flew in my mouth and it just tasted salty dolphin water the whole time but still loved the show!

Turtle reef and shark encounter was cool. In the beginning the Shark encounter had like a pirates of a Caribbean vibe so that was pretty cool and it takes you from the top surface to underneath the sharks.

Then of course to another show which was the sea lion and otter show. It was more of a comedy style and it was actually really funny seeing how the animals and actors work together was fantastic! Not too much splashing.

Fresh water aquarium was nice but kind of meh, not too much to see nor anything of the exciting nature. The Bayside skyride was pretty cool, just a sky lift that loops across the water about 30-40 ft.

I thought Aquariam de la mer was going to be more cool but it was just an octopus tank and that;s it. Another meh area. Aquaria was another meh area where it was just a bunch of different fishes.

Did the Shipwreck rapids and you WILL get wet! So make sure to leave any valuables in the lockers right outside the ride. It's like the tire ride everywhere else has but it was nice to get on it since it was kind of hot.

We went to the bat ray feeding area where you can buy squid for $5 which kind of seems expensive for about 5 small squids. So to feed the Manta ray you must hold the squid in your palm having it flat and putting your hand as low as you can. It's a weird feeling because you will feel like a vacuum which is how the manta ray eats!

Last but not least was the Orca show which was awesome but  it wasn't as great as the dolphins as the whales are more larger. We can clearly tell the Orcas was not happy as two of them had their upper fin sideways which means they don't have a lot of space.

Upon exiting we took a survey and came up with some interesting tidbit. We found out that they might be phasing Orcas soon as it asked us if it was important to us. Upon further reading some articles , we found out that some seaworlds are phasing them out and this one might as well. So of you want to see Orcas, better see them soon because they might not be there anymore which is good for them.
likes: Sea lion and otter show (comedy, interactive)

reviews_attraction.text:
Meow wolf....how to explain what it is and what it has in store. This is where hundreds of artists came to create a fantastic visual, emotional and physical experience. It seems something  like a character in a TV show would hallucinate after taking some bad stuff!

Getting here is easy, parking your car is not. There is limited space in and around the parking lot. You might have to stalk some people to their car. The cool thing about this place is in the parking lot, there are food trucks scattered in every area so you don't have to go far for food. When you finally get to the building, the line runs out the door but do not fear as the line takes about 15 minutes to get through.

Once in, make sure to use the bathroom before heading in. A friendly warning is that there is no backpacks allowed unless it is a camera bag, and yes an actual camera bag! The gift shop is right besides the meow wolf entrance. There is also a area for kids to draw if meow wolf might be too much for them. There are no strollers allowed in the exhibit also. After you grabbed whatever you need, get ready to head inside! Now Meow Wolf is MASSIVE and it'll take a long time to fully see everything! We arrived there at 10AM and got out at 5PM! That's right it took 7 HRS to go through it. Of course that includes taking photo in any interesting location and the WHOLE thing was interesting!!!

Now this area is trippy and it really is like a maze but a fun one! You can either explore visually but if you want to unravel the mystery that is behind meow wolf and the creation, make sure to read the post card in the mail box right next to the entrance you come out of. Now to name a few areas. For those of you that don't want the fun ruined, skip until end spoilers

SPOILERS

The area is a full house built in with letters, clues scattered through the exhibit. You can enter each and every room of the house including the second story. Know that these rooms might connect to another location. For example the room under the stairs takes you to a alien type area! You have about couples bedrooms. Make sure to read everything going to letters, diaries, the TV, walls, posters etc.

Outside the house will take you to a alien spaceship, neon woods, balcony, mirror rooms, tree houses, techno room,  and so much more!

END SPOILERS

That said, Meow wold is a must visit as it is something so unique and different that you cannot compare it to anything at all or even begin to describe it! I recommend that everyone stop by and visit at LEAST once!
likes: Fantastic visual, emotional, and physical experience
Diverse and intriguing areas (e.g., alien spaceship, neon woods, tree houses)
dislikes: No strollers allowed in the exhibit

reviews_attraction.text:
Dear travelers,

Deep within the forest in the most northwestern part of California lies a magical place known as fern canyon. When you get to the end of the gps coordinates, it will lead you to a dirt trail. Yes, this is the place you need to drive through. 10 miles of it!!!! Now don't freak out because this place will have wild elk roaming about and this is their turf so don't mess with them because they roll with their top crew!
Anyways the trail can be completed by a 4 wheel or 2 wheel. We took our Nissan altima to give those of you who need an example what can make it through.
Now don't go all Dukes and Hazard here because this is straight gravel road without any guard rails. Go slow and make sure that you have CASH! The entrance fee over here is about $10 or so. As you drive up and down this road you will come to some really dark areas in which you need your headlights for!
As you head towards the end of the trail you will come across water creeks that, yes you guessed it, travel across. Now take a look before you cross and make sure it is the shallow part of the water. Don't go to slow or you car might just get stuck and sink in or too fast where you lose control. After about 30 minutes of traveling you'll get to the end of the trail where Fern Canyon is.
As you get out and head to the trail, make sure look at the map and see what path you would like to take. There is a simple loop that you can take.
Now if you would love a empty canyon, try coming here bright and early in the morning! You will come to the widest part of the canyon, you will head straight around the bend into canyon and it gets more narrow as you walk past. The best part of the canyon is right around the bend where both walls will be filled with nothing but ferns!
As you head further in you will go about half a mile with ferns all around. Soon you will be able to take a left to go around towards the loop located on your map. This will take you on top of the canyon and you will be surrounded by trees. Head on this path and you will end up at the beginning of the trail! Usually people spend about 2 or 3 hours here.

Do some cool running pictures like you're running away from a T-Rex!!! because parts of Jurassic Park was shot here!!!!!

One of the most beautiful waterfalls in the bay area! Now that being said, you need to put in work to get here! You got about a 4.2 one way or 8.4 round trip to and from Alamere falls. For the most part it is extremely solid path with few elevation gains. Now as you are driving here, you will lose service and that's okay but remember to take all the directions down so when you leave Alamere falls, you will have the directions down as there are lots of turns to get here.
For the first mile or so, the  sea accompanies you and it's refreshing to have the sea breeze follow you and aid you as you traverse through the trail. I'd recommend coming on a clear day because that's when the falls really shine underneath the sun. When it's under overcast, the weather gets a little too cold. Make sure to leave early if it will be warm weather because the heat will be beating on you as you walk. Bring plenty of water on this trip because it is a long one.
You'll walk around the cliffs and then finally into a forest area, where the path starts to ger narrow. You'll eventually come to a open spot and as you hit the curve you will see the seashore right in front of you.

Do not continue but look to your left and you will see a sign and then you will see a little opening. Yup that's in, get in! Now this part will seem like a horror movie where you are cramped up and walking through the path but trust me you will not be murdered here. Walk slowly and be careful for the uneven terrain! pretty soon you'll come out into the open again and guess what? More decline elevation! Walk down and you'll eventually find yourself in front of a path way that is like a mini canyon for you to climb down and no there is no other way.

Head down and you'll see the first set of a mini waterfall. You made it but the work is not finished yet my friend. This next part is the hardest area of the path where it is a heavy decline. Use all 4 limbs and put any loose items in your backpack! Once you get down to this area, then you are at the beautiful Alamere falls!

Please do not leave trash or garbage laying around and take what you bring. Have fun and stay hydrated!

I've been to many many many sand dunes and this was has got to be one of my favorites, right up there with the sand dunes in death valley!
We came here with about 5 hours until sunset so we had plenty of time and we came here when it was fall weather!!!! That's what I'm talking about!!
Anyways when you enter, make sure to stop by the visitor center which has souvenirs. Now the thing about this visitor center is when you walk in, to your right is a gift shop and in front of you is a even bigger gift shop!

Now, since you're here, you might as well sled!!! Now they sell sleds for $15 a pop and used ones for $10. They even buy your sled back at $5 with a receipt. Now for those of you that want a neat little secret, if you manage to get here before hours which will still have the gates closed, visitors leave their sleds behind for free because they don't want to lug it around the whole trip. Stop by and see if they are any leftovers! Now these sleds are more like plastic giant circles instead of the traditional style. It literally looks like a GIANT plastic plate with holes on the side!

Anyways once you grab your gear, make sure to head into the park! Now understand that this park is basically more or so of the same. So anywhere you would like to park in the parking spaces, go ahead park and knock yourself out!

When you get to the sands, it looks like snow, white snow! It is really soft so it feels spectacular on your feet! Fun fact: Even though it will get hot, the sand will stay cool. Now you can see white sands as far as the horizon.

This is the largest white sands in the world and even if you are passing by, you should make time to see this once. I really really love this place and if I'm ever in this area I will come back! Just don't actually start driving without wiping this stuff off your face because you know, white sand. Also they do military testing nearby once or twice a month so make SURE to check with them or online because they shut down the park while they test whatever they like to test these days.

The caverns are tucked in way in the middle of nowhere so be prepared to drive all the way to the top. It's about a 10 mile drive to the top! It's a beautiful location and the visitor center is where you need to go into.

Now this is probably the largest visitor center I have ever seen in my life. When you enter the visitor center, there will be the shop to your left which is massive by the way and also you will have a cafeteria which unfortunately does not open until 11AM so make sure you bring food if you will be coming before then! Oh and the gift shop just has a BATMAN SIGNAL WITH A HEADLAMP socks!!! After you get your cave goodies, head to the visitor desk where you will have to pay $10 per person.

You can take two ways to the save. First is the elevator which I would discourage if you can walk without a hitch and then they have the natural entrance. This cavern will take about one or two hours or so. Make sure bring some warm clothes because no matter how hot it is, the caves will always stay cold.

This cavern is utterly massive and rivals the one we went in Lava beds! There is barely any lighting to light up the whole cave but just enough so you can see where you are walking. As you descend you will come into a flat walkway. This is a giant loop which allows you to see more of the caverns. You really can't take really great pictures here unless you own a professional DSLR so try not flashing a pillar 30 ft away from you. Just enjoy the area!

After you will have to climb back! Just kidding, you can take the elevator which is right next to the rest area/bathrooms. Enjoy this area and head back up. There's not really much to go anywhere except on the path but it will be a great experience and well worth the drive out here! By the way do not leave any trash in the caverns! There are also closures which happens time to time during peak bat season so make sure to check before you arrive on the website!
likes: Unique gift items (e.g., Batman signal socks)
dislikes: Limited photo opportunities without professional equipment

reviews_attraction.text:
Ah Joshua tree, you might heard of the name from the super famous concert but this is a review for the park itself! Now we started at sunrise as the park is usually closed and we wanted to pay the fee before we started driving and exploring. Okay first up, no matter how hard you try, you probably won't be able to explore the whole park before time is up and that is okay. I really wanted to do the oasis hike however that was a shade less 3-4 hour hike which would have taken half of our time there.

We did however did go to most of the areas that's a good photo op! Skull rock is okay, it's pretty cool because as the name suggests, it is shaped like a giant rock. You can even sit in the eye! Be weary though that there is ALOT of people lined up to take pictures with it. Don't be that person to cut in front of the line, make sure you see whoever is waiting in line.

We also went to the arch which was cool because it is a very large arch where you can stand on top of. It's about 20 feet high from the tallest point.

We went to the Joshua forest which is literally all around Joshua tree but there are places with more dense forests than regular.

We also went to the mountain peak which was so much fun. We got to see where they hold coachella at from all the way there.

They also have a cactus garden which is hella cool. It's literally cactus everywhere and be careful while walking around because you can get prickled and not the fun kind.

These areas plus the time it took me to do a photo shoot probably lasted from 6AM to 4PM. IF you don't care about taking pictures as much as I do, then you can definitely see the whole park PLUS do the Oasis hike also!
The weather of course was beautiful because I went in January so we are looking at 65-70 F!

This is a review for the outer grounds of Legion of Honor which in my opinion, is the best part of the museum!
When you arrive the parking is pretty terrible! Not that there isn't enough parking but there are so much cars here!!!! It's not just the parking for legion of honor but parking for the nearby trails, legion of honor, overlook, and golf course.
No after you find parking you will come up to the Legion of Honor and be confused when you first lay eyes on it. How can something so beautiful, so greek be just resting in San Francisco?!
It feels like a roman/greek building just for you to adventure and explore.
First up the front of Legion of Honor does not have a gate around it which means you can come after 5PM and take some pictures here if you arrive too late. Majestic roman type pillars grace both sides of the building. Now if you come here before 5PM, you are greeted with the courtyard which has the pillar walkways on both sides. There are neat statues scattered around and there is also this one awesome half glass pyramid area where you are allowed to sit besides. Perfect for taking some cool pictures.
Then of course you have the museum which is kind of expensive and it is mostly painting exhibition interior, nothing like the exterior museum at all. So don't go in there expecting King Leonidas' house because you will say THIS IS NOT SPARTAAAAAAA

If you are facing the museum entrance, to your right is the land's end trail and an overlook to the Golden Gate bridge. To the left will be the golf course which you need to be weary of golf balls flying.

Mojave desert is one of the most underrated parks that sits underneath the shadow of Joshua Tree. Most people don't really talk about it because it's not the cool thing around social media.
Mojave desert is HUGE and there is so much to do. It has multiple places to offer. We came here and camped for one night....well car camped  and it was perfectly fine and most importantly safe. It definitely feels safer than the city, that's for sure. Even if it is vast, photo opportunities for something different and unique aren't really present compared to what you can find in other parks nearby.

But it deserves a great rating because it's a lot more relaxed than other parks and there is not that much people around which is a definite plus. You have many different geological features from flat lands, sand dunes, red rocks but honestly this was the last stop after Death valley and Joshua tree and as some of you might know, both those parks have everything this park has to offer so for Mojave to be at the end part, it wasn't really fair.

If this is the only park you go to then of course you would be pleasantry surprised. I did go here in the winter so the weather was about 60-72 F which means it felt beautiful! This was in January if anyone is wondering!

Also be CAREFUL while driving on the roads as there are tortoises walking about and you can easily kill them on accident. And make sure you have a full tank of gas because while you are wandering this park, there are no gas stations for miles to accompany you!
dislikes: Less variety compared to nearby parks

reviews_attraction.text:
Chinatown is exactly what you think of it. There is Chinese stuff and it's kinda like a small town.
Anyways first thing is first, parking is ABSOLUTELY horrendous but this is the city so it is expected. Your best bet to park is a parking garage and since there is a abundant of garages to choose from, you should park in the cheapest one you can find! I say this because most of the streets is posted with no parking 7AM-6PM or parking only at 8AM-3PM. They WILL tow your car if you are not parked in the correct spots!
Anyways back to Chinatown! Best place to start is Dragon's gate which is the start of Chinatown!
You have many shops, restaurants and gift shops on this street
Make sure you stop on by some bakeries and grab some Chinese style goods!
Now for the gift shops, they are abundant but some of the items are really cheap as in low quality but that's tp be expected. There's one shop where they sell deformed knock off Pokemon so save your money in that store or you'll end up with a giant squirtle head with a mini squirtle body.
Between the numerous shops are murals hidden in alleyways so make sure you look both sides because you will miss some awesome ones! There is a multi colored steps art, tiger art, and dragon art which is the most popular ones. There are several other ones scattered throughout Chinatown.
It's a really nice place to come and best of all it is walking distance from little Italy so if you want to explored two neighborhoods, it's a plus!
likes: Facilities & Services: Abundant bakeries, shops, and restaurants
Activities: Exploring murals, multi-colored steps art, tiger art, dragon art
dislikes: Facilities & Services: Low-quality gift shop items

reviews_attraction.text:
Came here because I head about the  metal sculptures scattered all around Borrego Springs, so I went to go check it out. Now when you get here, you'll need to get a map where it tells you where to go and where everything is!  This is found in the visitor's center which is at the beginning of the park!

Now this is the desert, so keep in mind most of the time it will be scorching hot so you need to drink a lot of water. The best news is that you can drive to all of these! I would recommend the dragon which technically is a serpent but it looks like a chinese dragon more than anything! Across from it will be scorpion, elephants, grasshoppers and weird human sculptures. From there if you keep heading north/east, it will take you to some dancing raptors and some chief masks!

As you head down south, past the way you came from, you will come across bird statues! Now one of the most coolest sites are hidden in the desert, past concrete roads on a dirt trail. And this isn't gravel by the way, it is rocky road. I would not recommend taking your 2 wheel drive sedan through here or you might get stuck. Best to look at it from a distance or walk to it instead which kinda sucks because it is scorching hot there.

All in all, it was a extremely different and unique experience to see these statues and they are super worth that is if you can stand the heat! Please don't touch the statues when it is super hot unless you want to make grilled serving of you

Ever wondered how it is to drive through miles and miles of trees that cover the sky with the sun peeking through?? Ave of the Giants aka Humboldt Redwoods state park is the one for you. So you can either start from the south or north! Depending on what way you would like to continue! I started from the north side and made my way down south!

Now a few things! When you start, you probably don't where to go but conveniently they have placed maps at the beginning of each location! So matter north or south, you will have a chance to get a map! They are in a small box so no, there won't be any neon signs showing MAPS. After that there will be a couple landmarks you can visit. Everything is free with the exception of the drive thru tree. This is a tree that you can drive through after paying 5 or 10 bucks. Now keep in mind the reason they charge is that this little nifty thing is privately owned. For those of you interested it will be south end of ave of the giants.

Now the place where I would recommend to go to is the big tree. It's this extremely massive tree with the biggest circumference in California! Enjoy this tree and make sure to visit it and the trails around it as there are beautiful trees that have fallen over with massive roots!

Take your time when you drive and if there are people behind you , just pull over and let them pass so you can enjoy the drive!

Mccloud falls is one of the beautiful waterfalls in California. As you get here you will get to a hiking trail. Now the good news is that it's not a terrible hike at all!
You will start in the lower falls which is about 30 feet away from the start of the trail. This is a nice little small waterfall which is a enclosure. Yes, for those of you wondering, you can swim in here. Now onto the second waterfall! This waterfall will probably be half a mile out and to be honest this is the best waterfall out of all three.
Now when you get to the middle falls, there are many places where you can hang out at and chill. You can swim but be aware that the water is really cold but it is mildly refreshing during the summer heat. You can also jump off the cliff to your left into the water but be very careful as it could be dangerous so take the simple precaution when doing this. After you had your fill here you can hike up to the upper falls.
While this one is great and majestic, it is gated off so you can barely see it in person and all you have a view of is just across from the gate. There are picnic tables here where you can hang out and if you head higher, there will be stream which turns into a waterfall which is the upper falls. Although this is a bigger waterfall than the middle falls, I would highly recommend the middle falls to hang out and spend your day in!

SLAB SLAB SLAB CITY, SLAB SLAB SLAB CITY FIIIISH

Located in Slab City lies Salvation Mountain. I Came here on two occasions and it was awesome. First we got here and it was way past closing time and they still let us in as long as we stayed with the last tour group which was free! We saw a little bit since we came late.

Next time we came, we had PLENTY of time so I was super excited for it!
So a couple things, try to go when the sun isn't trying to BBQ everyone on earth and look for a more milder weather but if you really can't, be weary that for most part of the mountain there is absolutely no shade!!!!
Second, when it rains,  you won't be able to go on most of the structures as it is really brittle after rainfall.

Now this mountain was 30 years in the making, it was created by one guy with nothing but paint, clay and his love for Jesus. The mountain is extremely colorful. You can head up the stairs and take some pictures at the top, in the alcoves, and they are creating this large dome which you cn step into and it's colorful everywhere! This is the place where it has shade!!!!! By the way, say hello to the resident cat that likes to chill there!
This is a really amazing place even if you're not religious! The best thing is that it is completely free of charge and the guys running it are really nice!

This is probably the best garden in the bay area! I've been to multiple Japanese gardens within the bay area and I'd say for the price and space, this is Superior. The best time I'd recommend to come when you want amazing pictures is to come during cherry blossom season which is perhaps a two week span. You'll have all sorts of flowers blooming spring time. Make sure to come on a sunny day as overcast kind of kills the luminescence of the place although it is still beautiful regardless.
So as you enter you are greeted the gift shop to the left and to the right the gardens. Buy what you desire and they also have huge bamboo sticks for ten bucks! As you enter you'll see a giant gate with the gardens waiting inside. Straight ahead is the koi pond with a bridge leading to the steps up the garden.
You have the bamboo forest to your left and no you cannot walk through the forest, you're on the pavement. Then you have the Wisteria in two locations. One by the koi pond and the awesome one that is hanging overhead to the right of the building by the koi pond.

All in all you will stay here a couple hours and even longer when you account for taking pictures here! It's well worth the admission!

Such a beautiful place! Alright Let's get down to it!

You have couple different trails to go when you park!

First you'll have a trail that will lead you to a bridge that will take you to "calcutta falls"
I say that because that itty bitty waterfall is not a waterfall. I've taken a tinkle bigger than that. To save yourself time just go down by the river and relax!! Soak it up!!!! Be careful when it's hot though because the rocks will be super hot if the sun has been on them for a while.

If you up for adventure, Let's head the trail on the opposite side! This is the lake clementine trail! This will take you to the dam that looks like a giant waterfall! It's a fairly simple hike and will take you 45 mins round trip! But along the way you'll hug the river and then eventually start heading into the forest just a tad bit. The dam is gorgeous although you cannot go to the top unless you go from the other side of the mountain! Be careful when heading down if you choose to because it is extremely slippery and that's a long tumble down there!

Be careful for snakes and all those fun non house stuff! Bring mosquito repellent!!!

Great place to chill on a sunny day, on a windy, overcast day? Not so much. Be weary of the hours here. You might be able to cast some fire magic here but the cops will dispel it at 9:30pm, no exceptions.
It is a really beautiful place to hang out with your friends are alone if you do not have any friends but hey who needs friends when you have a beautiful beach to walk on? There are douche buckets which litter their trash here like beer bottles, cans and all that not fun stuff so be careful where you are walking on. There also cool sand dunes where you climb on towards the streets. Also this beach is GIGANTIC, probably spreads on for a few miles from the edge of the restaurant to all the way to the beginning of the street down south! So you can pick wherever you would like to be.
Make sure to pick up after yourself and don't be that guy/girl and leave your trash everywhere because last I checked you don't have a personal maid that follows you around.
Like all popular places, make sure hide your belongings as always

Been in the bay area most of my life and I never visited this place until now. Holy moly, this is an amazing display of art! Now getting here can be difficult as the roads are narrow, a specialty of San Francisco. There is quite a few parking spaces available but be wary that since this is a tourist spot, you have a increase of car break ins so do not leave any valuables in plain sight.
Now there is a lot of steps to climb but each step is designed beautifully and there are several designs as you ascend the steps ranging from the ocean, moon and the sun. When you reach the top, if you turn around you are greeted with a bird's eye view of the whole ocean front......assuming it is not foggy.

But wait there's even more! past the hill is even more steps but you can go to the very top of the hill and either swing by the cliff side or even have a better view of almost a 360 view of San Francisco!

Muir woods too far for you? Never fear for the majestic redwood trees reside here also!!! It's actually decently size too! It's a rather amazing place to go and get away from the city! Now to get there, there are multiple entrances and multiple trails to get here. As you are driving up north, you will see parking lots every couple or so miles.
The redwood forest easily envelops you into a beautiful get away.
There are camp sites here and sometimes the trails can become confusing as they start blending in with the surrounding area.
Bring some water although for most of the trail, you will be in shade so it is not too terrible.

I like this redwood forest and kinda prefer it because you don't really pay anything unlike muir woods where it's about $10 per person.
Be careful for poison ivy/oak!!! Don't get attached to this place too much unless you want to look for pete the dragon

This is one of the most beautiful churches in California! There is a lot of areas for photography opportunity. This place is nice as it doesn't have anyone that tries to shoo you out as long as you are being respectful and considerate. Yes that means don't try to do a lingerie shot here!
Anyways you have the front of the church to get right from the get go and then you have small walkways you can walk around the church for different walkways and backdrops of the church. The pure white building makes it so great, On overcast days you kind of have to be careful while taking pictures because it can cause shadows on the models which makes them way too dark to match the church

This place kind of reminds me of a kingdom oblivion for those kingdom hearts fans! Kind of feel like doing a cosplay shoot here!

Came here mid week July for camping. It is pretty decent. Not super pretty or anything. Dry grass is everywhere throughout the whole park. The facilities are actually really clean and I was really impressed. That or I was super lucky no one near us had explosive diarrhea. The campground is almost quiet, the cars by the highway kind of kills the atmosphere.
There are swimming spots which is okay. A lot of people were swimming but the water was kinda smelly and dirty in my opinion but it is a river so that's kind of expected.
The other gripe I have is there are barely any trees so when it's hot then you might be the afternoon smore.
It's not my favorite campground but if you want to get a campground last minute or don't feel like driving too far, it is okay. Just don't expect anything spectacular!

This is a part of the Land's end trail which is the Land's end labyrinth. It overlooks the Golden Gate bridge and the pacific ocean. You can also see the cargo ships going in and out the bay. A labyrinth maze even though it sounds scary, is really a nice slow walk following the maze into the center.
It is know to be a peaceful walk full of positive energy. So don't do back flips or listen to your musics people.
Keep calm, think about the positive things in life and take deep, long breathes and be grateful for what has come and what has yet to come.
As you take this minute long journey reaching the center, leave a part of you as you take the memories of this place.

Also take a jacket or you are going to be the most peaceful icicle in the world

The price of admission is just $5 I believe but we came here for the gift shop and it did NOT disappoint. We bought this awesome customized magnet. So what it is like a cross between a alien face and the new Mexico symbol which looks super rad! The only issue was it is a whopping $25!!! We spent time contemplating it, literally like 30 minutes because it was ALOT of moolah to spend on ONE magnet. But we ended up buying it because this one is super unique and it is locally made by a couple which apparently did really well in the Roswell festival! We wished we had time but we decided to go to the alien zone where they had much more Alieny settings!
But if we had time we would have checked this place out!

Came here ($10) and it's a okay beach. I honestly came here because I was tired from Mt/ Tallac and really didn't want to go too far after I got something to eat. I hung out here and watched the sunset. The parking lot is fairly huge and the beach is really wide and there are kayaks available to rent ! The only problem is you'll have to come in the morning/early afternoon because they don't rent out after 4PM.
This is a okay beach and for the price it's decent. There are also Geese here which run in groups, I call them the Gang dem Geese. They will fight you and you better be afraid, really afraid!

This rolling hills of many trails. It is beautiful with tall grass but honestly that's all there is to it. Just trails with no shade of grass. It is a great place for a photo shoot for those of you wanting tallish grass. But beware that there are alot of mice around so be careful where you step!
And try to come here early morning because there is absolutely no shade!

Took  my kids here as we were driving north on I-75, as we stop by as many National Parks as we can so I can help expose them to things the Public Schools refuse to teach anymore.

We had a travel camper trailer and had a hard time parking.  We did find 3 spots at the far end of the parking lot we could finagle ourselves into

This is a nice facility and we all learned things about MLK that we didnt know.  Kids thought the cart his casket was carried in was neat to see.

It was worth the drive off the interstate.

Excellent place to stop while driving up or down I-90.  Great place to stretch legs and see some history. It's really a gem of an experience knowing you are standing at the confluence of the biggest river in the USA and all of the history that goes with it.

The pay station was unattended.  There is an outhouse bathroom by the pay station.   Recommend walking the mowed trail that goes by the old hotel. .  Kids enjoyed the park. We stayed about one hour total.

I liked the park but I wish there were more signs in the trails to let you know where different intersections will lead you to if you go left or right while walking

Not the parks fault, but there were a few pavilions who had music on too loud where it carried the noise beyond other pavilions trying to have a birthday party etc.   For example, a kids birthday party was drowned out by some Mexican music 2 pavilions away.   I felt sorry for the kids party.

This is a great place for kids to see wildlife up and close. Its like a mini zoo in the front by the building. There are people there to answer questions about some of the birds there, which seem to be under rehabilitation.

There are hundreds of turtles in the pond. There are walking paths and a boardwalk area that leads to the Narrows, part of the Intracoastal waterway.

In summer months bring big spray if venturing into the back trails.

For bicycling on the Pinellas trail, this is a great place to park and hit the trail. They do close and lock the gates around sunset, so plan accordingly.  There is a bike repair station where the park entrance to Pinellas trail is.

Bathrooms and free parking are here.

If not hitting the Pinellas trail, there are a couple playgrounds, pavilions and baseball field.

Watch yourself on the far end (west side) as it is flying disk zone.

The park is nice and the boardwalk walk is open late after dark which is nice as most parks close by sunset.

The dog park section is closed on Thursday. How wierd is that?

There are no signs in the boardwalk to indicate which way is out or to another section.

The mangroves are trimmed nicely and maintained. Park is clean and there are restrooms there. The restrooms echo and people outside can hear everything you do from outside.
