HOLY COW! A bunch of us saw the King Tut Exhibit here recently. We rocked up to the main entrance on Jan 4th at about 10am to join the hundreds already lined up to get in. Without going into too much detail I have to say that seeing hundreds of the boy King Tutankhamun's personal artifacts was one of the highlights of my life to date. Too breathtaking for words! We all stopped for a lunch break at 12.30pm in the huge food court on the ground floor. The food was alright for a gigantic tourist attraction. We then headed to the NASA exhibits and eventually to the Space Shuttle which was just incredible to stand near. I sure wish I could have seen inside it though. We finished up about 2.30pm and gee it was sure worth coming here!
likes: On-site Activities: NASA exhibits, Space Shuttle viewing
dislikes: Facilities & Services: Limited access (Space Shuttle interior)

reviews_attraction.text: My wife and I visited this animal refuge shelter a few days ago.It only cost us $14 each to tour the facility which would normally take about an hour.My wife brought her digital SLR and we hung around a good 2 hours while she took photos of every creature she saw.We saw lots of sharks, turtles, rays, tortoises, all types of eagles, a few owls and lots more.We watched a feeding session for a Golden Eagle and a Bald Eagle.It was amazing to see such beautiful birds up close and personal.It's a fabulous place and everyone no matter what age would find something of interest here.

BORING ! My wife and I were attracted by the nice looking building and while taking exterior photos we were invited to see the inside via a guided tour with other visitors. The center is staffed by young women doing their 2 year Mormon missions. The show dragged on for an hour and there were many not too subtle recruitment attempts along the way. The staff were nice enough to let us take photos inside which we appreciated however it's all about the promotion of Mormonism and much less about history as we know it.

THIS PLACE IS AMAZING ! This was our first time here after hearing from anyone we asked that the market was the best. My wife and I shared a Maine Lobster roll and fries, enjoyed 2 fantastic WestBean salted caramel lattes + a French cake for dessert. We had the best time buying unique shrimp chorizo sausages from Mastiff Sausage Co and some fantastic fresh pasta. We've been back a few times since and there is even more new eateries.

FANASTIC ! My wife and I spent a few very enjoyable hours taking the tour around this incredible facility. I don't like zoos but this place has everything set up like it is in a natural environment. The background scenery is spectacular too.We had a very nice lunch at the restaurant with our daughter and her husband. If you are ever in Tucson this is a must visit attraction !

PRETTY COOL ! My wife and I were out on our Sunday bicycle ride starting in Banker's Hill and we came across this incredible pedestrian suspension bridge across a deep ravine. We parked our bikes and walked across to check out the view from the bridge. The plaque says it has been in operation since 1912. It's certainly worth checking out if you are in the area.

We saw The Police perform here when they got back together in 2008.It still is the best concert I've ever seen. Another time we saw Eddie Izzard....what a genius!The sound system is fantastic and even if you are back a long way you still have a beautiful view of the stage.It is without a doubt the most impressive music venue I have been to.

REAL COOL ! My wife and I spent a few hours walking around this fantastic historic ranch. We were both big Cisco Kid fans when we were little so it was real neat to see this property once owned by Pancho ( Leo Carrillo ) from the tv series. You just don't see real old buildings like this place has except on tv. We loved it !

A MUST TO VISIT ! My wife and I toured this fabulous raptor center when we were staying in Eugene for a few days a while back. It was sad to hear how some of the amazing birds of prey ended up in this refuge habitat. It was a wonderful experience seeing these awesome birds up close and personal !

WOW ! My wife and I were visiting San Francisco and my wife's son thought we would like to check out the Sutro Baths. Just incredible that they were opened in 1896 and operated until 1966. Sadly most of it burnt down in a fire in 1967. It still is a great spectacle worth seeing !

We were visiting San Francisco for a few days while my wife attended a DocuSign conference in Union Square. We had a great time here. Make sure you get a beautiful latte or cappuccino and a bite to eat at the Bancarella Cafe in the square...ask for Lamar.

MIDDLE OF NOWHERE ! My wife and I were riding the bike path to Marina but it was getting a bit late in the day. Not long after we passed the sign for Fort Ord Dunes State Park we decided to head back home. We rode 20 miles so that was a good effort !

GREAT SPOT ! My wife and I were out on an afternoon bike ride along the ocean front in Monterey..not so hot ! We stopped here and there along the endless bike path to take photos and this little park was ideal to get some great shots !

SENSATIONAL PLACE ! My wife and I did the museum tour while on a short visit to Atlanta recently. Everything we saw was very interesting. The Swan House and Smith Family Farm were amazing. Just 12 bucks a head and worth every cent !

JUST INCREDIBLE ! My wife and I took the tour of the Swan House and Smith Family Farm recently while taking a break in Atlanta. We had a grand old time walking through this beautifully designed and restored mansion. We loved it !
WOW ! My wife and I paid a visit to this incredible aquarium not that long back. It's a very impressive structure with lots of interesting and engaging marine life exhibits. We were very impressed !
Wow....my wife and I found this astonishingly beautiful building while on vacation near Santa Barbara. a few years ago.We walked around inside and admired the arches,tiled floors and gardens.
It's a beautiful outlook near the San Clemente Pier and the fabulous La Galette Creperie is straight across the street.We enjoy visiting this area on a regular basis.
We did a self guided tour at the Atlanta History Center in Buckhead while on a recent visit to Atlanta. The Smith Family Farm and the Swan House were amazing !
My wife and I couldn't help but admire this majestic bridge while we were having breakfast in Newport. Such a beautiful location across the bay.
WOW....what a beautiful view up here ! My wife and I drove up here and checked things out for a few hours. It was worth the trip !
My wife and I enjoyed so much riding our bikes over all the lovely bicycle bridges that cross the Willamette River in Eugene.
My wife and I did a tour of this place a few years back. I thought it was very overrated given all I had read about it.
It was a fantastic and unique experience visiting this scenic park and seeing a lot of the art sculptures on display.

I visited for one reason, to fish. Traffic was light though as day wore one I had to work around folks. Good catching with 6 different species. Solid action although the fish we're mostly on small side. Use restroom before visiting as those are the park are nasty.

There's plenty of mowed grass, plenty of area to roam. Other than plenty of parking, picnic tables, fishing, canoe launch, and walking not much else.

I enjoyed the history, although they tend to repeat theirselves throughout. It draws lots of folks and due to the the massive commercialization of the surrounding area parking is expensive and we walked a few blocks even then. Plenty to do around there, especially if you're a city type, which I'm not. Glad we visited, but traffic, crowds and commercialization crowding the area will make it a one time event.

First visit and worth the $6 senior price, $8 regular. Not a huge place but the exhibits are well done and relate directly to Rockport and the surrounding areas. No general Marine exhibits.

However, as pleasant as it was, this is a place to visit if you're already in the area, not worth much travel to see. Allow a couple hours to read everything, sans full reading an hour will do it.

Found this place searching for places to fish. There are three ponds that get regular stockings of catfish in the summer, trout in the winter. I managed a bluegill, catfish and small bass. Not bad for a fly guy. The park has much more with playing fields, picnic areas, trails, playgrounds and more. Looks to be a great place for a family outing.

This place is truly a piece of history. Built in 1667 with additions since. Original has been restored. Plenty on the family history and items from the earliest period on. Truly gives a feel for living at the time of the pilgrims. Cost is minimal for the tour. When in Plymouth, avoid the rock and spend time here instead.

While law enforcement exhibits rarely excite me, this one is well done and covers much of the history of the Texas Rangers, from prior to the Alamo to present day. Many are expressed with the gun collection, which is impressive, but the gun displays support the ranger's history. Well worth the price of admission.

Plan for a full day as it will take that to go through everything. We did it in  half day, missed much and skimmed a lot more. My main dislike was there was more "commercialism" feel about the museum at the start then I care for. Still there's plenty of history and knowledge to be had on America's naval might.

Stopped here to do a bit of shore fishing, a limited commodity in the area. This park has some, plus swim beach, picnic areas, playground, restrooms, and adequate parking. Fishing was great with flies for hand sized sunfish and yellow perch. Down side is the cost of the parking, 15 out of state, 8 otherwise.

We visited on a free day, but would gladly pay for a return visit. Surprised by art galleries and stuff for sale. The rest of exibits were well done and far more than a cowboy museum. The movie was fun, in large part to the pre- and post talks. Rather hope they continue the program. Well worth the time.

This museum has a nice collection of area artists showing subject matter from San Francisco to San Diego. While nothing Earth shattering, it is quality work. Enjoy spending a couple hours viewing all the pieces. Worth your time if you like area paintings, especially water colors. Best of all it's free.

While not the biggest, nor the cheapest it is a delightful place to visit. Focus is on the gulf as it should be. It has a lot of wildlife outside aquarium mixed in. Displays are well done and special features are great for most part. Very kid friendly and highly educational. Worth the price and time.

A dark moment in our history. Home grown terrorism is a reality. This memorable gives the whole story in great detail. We'll worth visiting. Allow a few hours, as it takes time to soak in the full story. While I'll not likely return, if you're in the area, you owe it to yourself to visit.

I visited as it's a community fishing water. The park is multi use with plenty of parking. It also get plenty of visitors, it shows. Not the best upkeep, some trash, and a ton of dogs. Most follow the leash laws. Fishing was slow, one small bass. A few reports of a catfish.

We've been here a couple times. Each visit is better then the last. The granddaughters love it, especially petting the Ray's. Plenty to see and do. This Monday we opened and closed the the place and still didn't see it all. I've no doubt we'll be visiting many more times.

Visited to fish the pond. It's a popular area to fish as there aren't many close. However, catching was disappointing. The area offers other features that I didn't explore. So if you're visiting other to fish it'll likely come across better.

Not a park I'll visit again.

This park gas a lot of interesting structures and history. Problem is we were expecting an event with interpreters. The event was cancelled and not well noted on the website. So viewing a few locked buildings wasn't what we wanted. We'll visit again when it's staffed.

We visited on a free kid's day and were welcome at no charge. That was the highlight. This is essentially a junk yard of past TWA items. While there is some interesting items, they're worth paying to see. Unless you're into aviation history, I'd pass on this one.

This place is a mix of zoo, botanical gardens, playground, museum, natural history and more. There's something for all. We spent the day there and covered most of what interested us. Although, we could have spent more time at all. This is one we'll visit again.

Most, I suspect would rate this much higher. Plenty to see and do. Plus, food and shopping. As I'm not a movie fan, and much prefer nature to man-made it wasn't a good fit for me, the wife loved it. I'll admit the stunt man show was good, if a bit corny.

If you're going to tour the National Park, you need to stop here. Visit a bit before moving on as they have some good exhibits. Plus, here's where you'll was to play as hiking, walking, picniking, fishing, etc. a are not part of the national park side.

Visit if you're in the area, as this all need isn't worth much of drive in my opinion. Lots of history, but the features have a run down feel. Still if you're visiting Tubac and the area for a day then be sure to visit.
Educational and well done. It's her birth place and there's plenty to learn. Worth visiting at least once if you have any interest in early aviation and her story.
A lot lovely place to visit. The walk highlighting trees from all over the country and world. If you're in the Atchison area make the visit.
They have this every third weekend. Nice event with good numbers of booths for a chilly winter day. Worth visiting if you're in the area.
Nice park with lots of history, walking and hiking trails. Lovely area. Worth a visit if you're in the area.

Went here to hike both Aspen and Hayden. Had a great time. $10 fee to enter but I believe if you are a veteran you also get a discount which is awesome. The hikes were beautiful! Not as well marked for Hayden, we ended up just taking the road up to it. All the signs said Hayden trail and we couldn't find it so we found a different way. Highly recommend for anyone missing green trees while in the desert :)

Kind of shorter than I had expected for $15 a person. Fair amount to walk around as long as it isn't raining. I'd suggest going straight to the central parking and parking there to then walk around. We kept getting out of the car and back in and then we ended up at the visitor center anyway. You could really park anywhere and walk to everything.

Yes it is $10 to see a tree... but it's pretty cool!! Honestly, if you're in the area you have to see it! I have a Chevy Colorado and thought it best not to try to fit it thru, and there's a little road to drive around it. An old subaru outback and a corolla fit no problem.

Really pretty views even in february. Not all of the roads were open, but the visitor center still was. The Ranger told us a lot about the park and there was access outside. You could walk to the edge and you can hear the water rushing. There's a great 20 min video too!

Went here at almost closing time and the staff was sweet to let us in and enjoy it until 5pm. They do close and monitor the people in the park, so do not plan to stay and watch the sunset here. Thank you Veterans for your service!!

Awesome place to check out if you're in the area. They are currently working on the road so be prepared to drive on a uneven surface for awhile. We spent maybe 10 minutes here and then headed down to the beach for the sunset.

Wonderful hike down to the falls. Was there during the fall so the trees were really pretty. The way back is a bit of an incline so be ready for that. By the falls is muddy so watch your step. Took me maybe an hour or so.

Really cool place! A must see while in chicago! The Michael Jordan statue is now inside!! They built around it. It took us awhile to find it, but just go into the 'mad house' souviner store and you'll find everything!
dislikes: Facilities & Services: Difficulty in finding the statue

reviews_attraction.text: Unfortunately they didn't change the signs at the front saying the last tour is at 4:10pm. The sign was wrong and we missed the 5:10 because we thought there weren't anymore due to the sign. Really unfortunate.

Super cute place. You can bring your own food here and have some wine. There is corn hole available. Tastings are $10 and you get a plastic cup. Was not impressed with the wines, but it's a really cute place.
Really pretty falls. The stairs to hike down aren't that bad. It looked like you could hike down to the bottom of the falls, but maybe it was blocked off. Such a nice area to sit and have a picnic.
There are many parks in the Albany area to get yourself out of the busy city and enjoy nature. This park is small, but quiet and in a great neighborhood. Great place to walk around or run.
Such a nice place to hike. If you don't want a lot of people, this isn't the place for you. It is very busy even during the week! Absolutely loved every second of it though!
Can walk to here from oak bluffs. Cute little lighthouse with nice views of the water. It wasn't open for us but I guess it is sometimes and you can go up inside
Great place to walk around, people watch, otter and sea lion sightings as well. Lots of little shops to explore and plenty of places to pick from to eat.
Went here to check out the tree. It is $10 to get in and it's pretty neat! I wouldn't recommend driving in it with anything besides a car .
Parking is only on the road here. There was a man and his son who sat there fishing the entire time. Spent maybe 5 minutes here.
Absolutley stunning. Went there during the winter time so we couldn't see as much. Still worth the trip if you're in the area!
The gondola was amazing and it's free. We didn't ski, just took the gondola to Mount Gay. If you're in telluride check it out!
Absolutely beautiful! Went for a little hike on their trail and found lots of lizards and beautiful views with less crowds.
Great place to walk around. Sad how much has broken down from no maintenance for years. Amazing that it's all marble!
Adorable wine bar location ON the pier. Grabbed a quick tasting as we were walking around. The views are stunning !
I love coming here to go for a run! It's beautiful and the trails are really nice and easy to follow.
Great place to watch the sunset! Parking is on the street and even on a Monday night it was busy!
Be prepared for a line of people to take a picture in front of it! A must see on key West.

Africa tram is really great tour. But I didn't like the people managing the queue on a busy day. They may be good in taking care of the animals but the people management is really lacking on the day when it is really needed!!
When I visited the Safari Park, last year December(2017) on a long weekend the park was packed with visitors. My main target was to do the African tram and the Cheetah run. We reached the park in the afternoon and got in the African tram queue by 12:15 PM. The wait time as shown in the board was 90 minutes. But we ended up boarding the tram on at 2.50PM. It was a horrible management by the team out there. More than 1 hour of unaccounted wait time. Totally misleading. I knew the proper time, I could have gone for other attractions instead but this wrong information totally ate my time and money. The staffs managing the line were useless and hardly informed the people that for smaller groups we can go to another line (for singles and two people group). They were more busy with making money by taking photographs instead of informing people properly. At 2.30PM, we were like only 10 people away from the first to board - when all of a sudden we see that they kept on filling 3 buses, one after the other, with people from a totally different line - probably priority people and singles and 2 people groups. This got us delayed by at least 20 more minutes and it was so annoying. They were not even informing any body of what is happening and they seemed to be totally careless about it. This totally ruined our plan to be close to Cheetah at the CHeetah run, because by the time thiis tour ended, the cheetah run had already started at 3.30. My girlfriend and me got only a slit of space in between 5-6 people to see the cheetah run. Worst line management ever!!
The low stars are mostly for the overall experience for the Africa tram tour starting from being in the queue.

Great tour. Must do if you are in San Diego. I loved how Jack, the driver made the whole tour super funny, entertaining but informative about the city.
The seats are not super comfortable and are small to be honest if you are planning to be in the bus for the whole tour.
This  instructions by the staff were pretty clear to us as to where to expect the next bus,  if you plan to get down at any stop.
At the end, when we were waiting for the last bus of the day, the staff at the stop made sure that everybody got a bus to ride and called for more bus when there were more people to get on to the bus.
Overall, we enjoyed our time there. It is worth the price if you plan to start early on not half of the day.
Also, I recommend the riders to get the San diego card for the day (or a customized one) adding Balboa park Museums, USS midway museum etc. because the bus stops at these locations. This way you can save quite a bit of money

You should stop by at this museum if you get down the bus here. Yes, it is not very visible right from the bus stop and we almost missed it.
After checking out the viewpoint, We were waiting for the next bus after a super cold snowstorm in the park. When I spoke to one of the visitors out there, we came to know that there was a nice museum with a great view on the other side. Great that we didn't miss it. Inside, there are multiple exhibits, a gift shop and a Ranger Naturalist who explains the visitors about the formation of the grand canyon and it's history.
Honestly speaking, the naturalist started to sound boring for the kids, young people and the old out there when he started relating star wars, etc. with the formation of grand canyon and I just lost interest in it and started roaming around. The view beyond the glass was amazing. A must visit.

Initially planned to take the Coyote Ridge Trail but found that it was closed. So, we headed for the Slate Creek Trail. The trail is totally covered with trees and this is a backpacking route. The trail looked like ideal for summer hikes. There are some campsites couple of miles inside the trail. The campsites didn't seem to have any fireplace. There is a bathroom inside. At night it surely gets pretty dark out here for the campers as it is all covered with tall trees.
You will come across a lot of narrow paths, redwoods, banana slugs, insects along with LOTS of mosquitoes(which were becoming annoying at times).

The trail will present you beautiful views on clear days.
Car entry fee is $6. You may as well park it in the neighborhood and just walk in to this State Park.

I took the North Peak trail. It looks like not much people come to this Park.
This was my first time here and it was cloudy most of the times. The view got covered at times. But I could still see the coast from various points on trail and the city underneath.

On a hot day, I am going to suggest you to to start in the morning and you will end up hiking mostly in shade. You might get more sun after 12 on the trail.

You reach ligthouse stop by the shuttle on a weekend. You will be charged $7 per head. Usually the bus drivers will give a short history of the place which is interesting - no doubt.
Once you are at the stop, you need to walk for sometime to get the great view of the Lighthouse. Any time is good time to come down here and enjoy the view and the weather. Just relax and take some time to breathe in the nature and the amazing view here. You may also get to see some marine life like dolphins and whales from the lighthouse and the stairs.
likes: Attraction Type: Lighthouse, Marine life viewing

reviews_attraction.text:
Nice tour in the middle of no where and under the ground level. It is recommended to reserve a tour before head so that you don't have to wait in the heat out there. Its amazing to see how these structures got created by flowing water over there. Amazing!!
There will be a couple of guides who will be helping you along the tour.
It was definitely worth spending the time out there and checkout natures art. If you are a photographer you should probably use the photographer's tour. It's a bit more expensive though.

Loved the view of the Columbia gorge from the top of the house.
They have a little museum below, a snack/coffee shop, souvenir, restroom. The Parking is free here which may get full very soon.
You will get great perspectives from different locations - be it from the top of the vista house, or its base or when you walk 1 level down the road.
A must go when you are around. The view of the gorge is breath taking.

On July 4th, people flock around the place to have a view of the amazing fireworks in the city.

You can spend a couple of hours of your morning walking around the garden. All green around you. The park is overpriced for sure. The cafe inside is quite expensive for - not sure why ? There is a gift store inside as well which is expensive as well.
Otherwise, the park is maintained. You can see multiple colorful fishes in the pools inside. Kids will like it for sure.
FOr the entrance, I think, SF residents have a discount.
I won't say that this is a must go when you are visiting SF for couple of days.

It is a beautiful place with lots of flowers blooming around this time. I visited here in mid April, 2021 and the waterfall didn't carry much water. About 3+ hours drive from San Jose. The trail is not well marked, so be aware where you are heading. It took us some time to find and reach the Phantom falls. So people were taking anything path they see and strolling around.
The place offers you a bunch of beautiful views and flora and fauna.

A nice lake with a good view. The Parking space is large. I have never seen it becoming full. While driving in you have to pay an amount for sure. This is a great place to do your morning walks or evening runs.
The trail mostly goes goes around the lake.
There are multiple picnic spots here and people often come here to fish and spend a few hours with their loved ones.
There is a restroom here as well and a drinking water fountain.

I had one of the most beautiful experience while on a 2 day backpacking out here. We were out with a few friends and all the small and large lakes on the trail were just spectacular. The trail had some ups and downs, most of it was shaded with trees.
I like the fact that not much people seem to explore this place. Not sure why though. I have seen horse riders on this trail though.
I loved it and will back here for more.

A nice walk along the streets which goes parallel to the canals. The houses around are beautiful. When you are around surely stop by and spend at least 30 minutes walking along the peaceful canals.
Finding a parking could be difficult. Otherwise just get here stress free and enjoy the walk.
This place also reminded me of many hollywood movies and TV series which were shot here.

This is a great place to spend your time alone, or with your friend or kids. You can just get a book in the park, take a seat on one of the benches out there. Entry is free. There are street parking spaces around the park.
Over here I have seen so many different shades of roses. I never had an idea. It's beautiful and its a mood changer.
This garden is nicely maintained.

Great view of the structures from this location. The road from the highway to this parking lot is not good. It's all gravelly - but drivable.
If you are driving at night or after sunset be sure to drive slow as there will be many night creatures like rabbits running around the road.
There is a parking fee - applicable 24 hours.

The easy, nice and pricky trail through the cholla cactus garden. Expect a lot of crowd here. I am gonna say that be careful where you step because the cactus balls could be on the ground and can surely poke you through your shoe. I got it at least 5 times when I went slightly off the trail.
Enjoy the view.

Hyped and unreasonably priced tour of William Randolph Hearst mansion located in California. The tour consists mostly of walking through some the rooms with its considerable collection of art and antiques.
As far as I remember, they offer multiple tours which covers different sections of the castle.

This park is just by the bay. It's small with free parking. If you are here during winter you will be seeing the monarch butterfly cluster here. I just visited this place for the monarch butterflies though in Jan, 2017.

There is a public bathroom and a small cafe around the parking lot.

Amazing location. Great little place. Great collection of wine. I have been here twice and every time i had a great time out here. I think you will have an awesome time even if you come here alone. Sally was very helpful and was very welcoming.

It was a long drive from the city to be here.
You get a nice view of the hills while walking on the boardwalk. But I wouldn't say you will miss a lot if you plan to drop it while visiting Oregon or in Portland. The trails are maintained well.

There's around 1 mile walk from the parking in the scorching Sun before you get to see this beautiful scene. So bring your umbrella/cap before you start walking towards the view point.
Carry water, cap, wear the sun screen and your camera.

A beautiful lake in the Tuolomne meadows area. Beautiful reflection of the mountain can be seen when not so windy. A number of designated spots at the side of the lake to park your car and walk around it.

Always a good place to be.
No complaints - except the terrible parking space :-(

Its hard to find a parking near the entrance. Even if you arrive as early as 6.30 in the morning.

Never visited the visitor center but have been around this area.
You get to see many elks in the park. Be careful and keep a safe distance.
Meh. Just a point from where you can see the city far far away. Take a break sit down and enjoy the shade on a sunny day.

This is one of the most emblematic buildings in Chicago. Even if you ate not much into history,  the building deserves a visit because of its amazing decoration and architecture. The ancient style mosaics are really beautiful and they are everywhere,  making you feel like you are inside an ancient Roman construction. There are several rooms that really deserve to be visited. And occasionally you can find exhibits.

The cave tour is great. It is just $8. If you go to rubby falls the cave tour is around $20! So it is very cheap here and you have almost the same experience except there is no water fall here. Our tour guide, Garry, was a nice man who explained everything very well. Also, they have good honey in the gift shop. Don't forget to buy some!

A nice park near the Coon Rapids dam, where you can enjoy a nice stroll along the river following one of the several trails available,  including hiking and paved trails. There are alons options for fishing and boat launch. Several spots along the way to enjoy the views of the river.

It's right at the border with Canada. My cellphone was not working there because AT&T carrier was locating me in Canada! I love the trail. At some point you have a good view of superior lake. There are restrooms in visitor center if you need. There is a nice gift shop too.

It is a very nice place for hiking. I don't like it much for biking because the road is narrow and shared with cars. There are shelters and grills and two play ground around. The entrance fee is $6 per vehicle. There is a place to rent kayaks and bikes inside the park.

A really nice state park along the scenic road that follows Lake Superior. Worth the visit. There are dozens of miles to hike,  and several amazing locations to visit. If you only have 1h, visit shovel point,  close to visitor center. The views are amazing

Nice place for picnic! That's right, the name of the island is as should be! Big shelters and lots of benches under the shelters and around them, nice grills, and the breeze from the ocean make this area the best place for barbecue and party.

Very nice camping site. The restrooms are clean and the scenery is stunning. We camped here the first week of September and the weather was perfect for bonfire. It was not too cold for sleeping in the tent and warm enough for the mosquitos!

The garden doesn't have much to visit but there is a honey festival here every year around March which is awesome. You can taste different honey from different parts of US and some other countries. Also, they serve very good food.

Nice park, specially for biking on the paved roads. There are different trails you can try, and several spots for birdwatching and similar activities. They also have a nice beach area ideal for resting or barbecueing.

It is nice to walk here. The trail is good for walking but not for jogging or biking. There are lots of stairs to get down to the fall and the trail so if you have problem with stairs I do not recommend you go there.

I have not tried the boat ride just checked the price and it was $18 an hour for 2 seat boat and $32 an hour for 4 seat boats. We were there on Friday around 11 am and the waiting line was not very long.

It is a nice place specially when clearwater beach is very crowded, it is less crowded in Sand key  beach. Parking is cheap, just $5 for the whole day. There are showers, changing rooms, and rest rooms.

This is one of the places you must go in Miami. You need to walk about for 2 hours to cover most of it so if you are going on hot season make sure you go early in the morning or late in the afternoon.
It's service is awful. We ordered 2 cups of soup and a salad and it took 45 minutes to prepare it! There just 6 more customers at that time so it was not crowded at all. I don't recommend this place.
Very beautiful place for camping. It has very clean bathrooms and showers. Also, it is a nice place for picnic. It has nice shelters and grills and small play grounds near some of the shelters.
It is a very nice old theater. It is one of the attractions in Tampa. It is well decorated and gorgeous. The show special kinds of movies that you can not find in cinema.
This beach is not crowded so for people who prefer quiet places this beach is perfect. There are showers and bathrooms but there is no life guard so be careful!

A small nice park with lots of Pokémons!
We were there around thanksgiving and they were decorating it for Christmas. The decoration was very nice.
A nice beach to spend a lazy day and get sunbathe. The water is very shallow though. You can bring your dogs to this beach.
The trail is beautiful and well maintained. It is shaded in most parts so it is perfect for biking or hiking.
We were not able to see the sunset there because of the bad weather but this place is absolutely gorgeous!
It is a beautiful place with big shelters and nice grills. It is a good place to have birthday parties!
A small area near the boat ramp. It is nice to go  to IHOP near that and then walk around a little.
Water is always cool here. I think it is around 70 F. It is so clear that you can see the bottom.

We saw the sign as we drove by, decided to come back and see what it was like. There's a Park Office with friendly staff, scheduled tours of the arboretum with times posted outside. There's no fee to visit. They have a playground, and tennis as well as basketball courts, and a walking trail with exercise stations. The plants mostly have labels. You can see a Baobob tree, jackfruit tree, miracleberry, strawberry guava, ylang ylang, and many more. There are seats along the trail to enjoy the different areas, and on the half hour the rainforest area has misters that come on. Very beautiful place.

Visiting the Preserve today, I learned many of the pictures posted as being at this location are not- the family in a swimming pool, someone's house, and pictures from the nearby Savannas Recreation Area- when photos are "suggesting locations" between the two businesses they are getting confused as the Park and recreation area are near each other and have similar names. Please accept edits from the Park Service, they keep contacting Google to try to address this. The Preserve has nature trails, visitor center, kayak programs. They aren't a recreation area or someone's back lawn pool party!

Beautiful park, nice walking trails, clean bathrooms and hot showers, recycling program, kids activities and playground. Wish we had found this in the summer, looking forward to coming back during the open season to see the visitor center and the caves. We enjoyed the scenery, tranquility, and it was a short drive to get to any area restaurants or grocery stores- so prepare before you hit the campground. Camping spaces are well maintained, there are sites with electric and reservations can be made ahead of time.

Ten dollars for our van to visit, but totally worth it. They're still repairing the boardwalks on number two and five parking lots, but there's ten different parking lots with bathrooms and stairs to access the beach. Lovely beach, we saw some man o war jellyfish that were beached. We saw a lot of different birds. We also saw an alligator and a large group of coots along our drive. Beautiful and well worth a visit. No pets.

Gorgeous park! I think I have found my favorite place in New Orleans. Beautiful trails, friendly volunteers working diligently to care for the park. Loved Scout Island and the Couture Arboretum. Appreciated seeing well over thirty turtles sunning themselves, having a young white crane casually lead me past an 800 year old oak tree.

Forest Park is fabulous. I love visiting and walking the different trails. The museum's, zoos, history and art in the park are wonderful. I enjoy watching people play golf and other games as I walk. Plenty of bathrooms and shelter areas throughout the park. It takes more than a day to enjoy all the park has to offer.

We loved seeing the manatees, there were 144 sighted Sunday when we visited. The walking trail was lovely, enjoyed the recently repaired wooden walkway, and the gift shop. The park has educational programs, there's canoe and boat rides available on the St John's here. Camping is reasonably priced. Fantastic park!

Excellent park, love visiting the Falls. Can be tricky finding an open parking spot, but the sidewalks and trails are well kept and beautiful. Love getting ice cream there, and all the benches and pavilions for family fun. Bathrooms are usually pretty clean too.

Loved the County Fair-especially the Expo, Treeman, Sand sculpture, grilled meat and milkshake. Great variety of food, rides, shows. Reasonable prices. Clean bathrooms with attendants. The garden was gorgeous! Great displays for landscaping ideas.

Knowledgeable volunteers that were actively engaging, excellent educational displays, great place to visit- and the work they do is wonderful! This is where you go to learn about marine life and to watch the manatees gently play.

I love this zoo. Great exhibits, they take care of their animals and work to help restore wild populations. Great way to spend the day with kids. Plenty of bathrooms, food isn't overpriced. Lots of learning tools. Excellent.

We are enjoying the Manatee festival, friendly volunteers, large variety of venders, Crafters, inexpensive food, cute dog show, good music, rides, free games for kids. Excellent family event, they even have flush bathrooms.

Lovely boardwalk, great information on the signs along the walk, places to sit and a nice shelter half way to the lookout over the water. We saw several birds and a squirrel. The rest area has bathrooms.

Beautiful park, friendly park service. Give yourself enough time to really appreciate the sights here. Well tended, clean and lovely. Bathrooms clean and working. Picnic shelters with tables and grills.
One of my favorite parks, absolutely beautiful. Full of fun from swimming, to trails, nature center, remains of ghost towns, golf course, stables, RV camping, boating: this lovely park has it!
Beautiful park, loved watching the various birds, seeing the golf course and learning from geocaching that there used to be a zoo in the park. Very nice. Plenty of parking.
I went here last summer and loved it. Excelkent and knowledgeable volunteers; great variety of beautiful healthy plants. More orchids than I have seen anywhere else.
I loved watching the sunrise here, seeing the tugs bring big ships in. Beautiful park, clean and public restrooms available. Nice walking trails. Lots of parking.
Beautiful park where the Brevard County Renaissance Festival is taking place the next two weekends. Nice walking trails and facilities. Enjoying camping here.
Beautiful and full.of educational fun! Loved the trail and the hands on learning for the whole family! Thank you! Love the educational programs you offer!
Gorgeous refuge. We had a beautiful walk and saw a variety of plants and wildlife. I would love to see it at sunset when migrations are going through!
Enjoyed swimming here over the summer, never too crowded and free parking. Playground for kids and bathrooms as well as a concession stand.
Beautiful park, clean beach. Playground, lots of tables and grills, plenty of parking- $17/ day during the week, higher on the weekends.
Beautiful, enjoyed our sunset walk around the park. There's a lot of places to park on the street as well as paid parking lots.
It was fantastic, give yourself at least three hours and if you go on your birthday the ticket or at least my ticket was free!

(Translated by Google) It is such a beautiful greenhouse ... The building is beautiful and its interior with plants is magical. Essential visit if you are in Chicago. It is also free and then you can visit the zoo and the park and see the views of the city from there!

(Original)
Es un invernadero tan bonito... El edificio es precioso y su interior con plantas es mágico. Esencial visita si estás en Chicago. Además es gratis y después puedes visitar el zoo y el parque y ver las vistas de la ciudad desde ahí!

This cathedral is beautiful, situated in the nice neighborhood of Nob Hill. It reminds me of the ones you find in Europe although this one is more simple than those. Anyway, it’s a great place full of spiritual meaning. We visited it during Christmas time, there are many concerts available through different days. There was also a beautiful Christmas tree decorated with origami and with written wishes. Just magical!

So beautiful... take the short trail to this waterfall and enjoy the view from below! Easy access walking from the Visitor Center. Parking was almost imposible. I strongly recommend to park your car wherever you can close to a bus stop and then take the bus everywhere (it’s free and has a relatively high frequency)

We had a lot of fun! We went on a Thursday night and it was awesome! No kids around because at that time it’s only open for adults and you can purchase drinks inside. We enjoyed the experience and we are looking forward to going back because we couldn’t manage to visit the whole museum! Totally recommended!!

After reading online many contradictory opinions on where to see the Hollywood sign, we went here and we actually saw the sign super close! We managed to park easily in a designated area (but still had to climb the street for about 10 minutes) and got to see the Hollywood sign from there. This is the place!

It’s unbelievably beautiful and spectacular. You have to park your car at the parking lot (after paying $10 per car to access) and then walk around 15 minutes to get there. Wear good shoes and bring water because there are no shadows and it’s extremely hot out there. Views of the horseshoe bend are amazing!

(Translated by Google) Incredible views of the city and pleasant walk. The wind usually blows hard so you have to keep warm especially in cold weather !!

(Original)
Increíbles vistas de la ciudad y agradable paseo. El viento suele soplar con fuerza así que hay que ir abrigados sobre todo en época de frío!!

Always full of people but if you walk a bit you always end up finding a quiet spot to relax. Views are breathtaking because you see El Capitan from the beach. Water was cold but it was so warm outside that we had a lot of fun. Bring food and sunscreen and raft boats because you will really enjoy that!

AMAZING! Our favorite place in Santa Barbara. Not only the building is beautiful both from the outside and the inside, but the gardens that surround it are amazing! Also, we got to go up to the tower and the views from up there are breathtaking. It’s free and open until 4 or so.

Staff was very kind and explained to us in detail what to do and what to visit during our stay at the park. I highly recommend to go ask them before you start walking around the park because they give you very good pieces of advice about Yosemite!

This park is amazingly beautiful. Breathtaking views of the sea, nature and animals. I strongly recommend to visit it, bring good shoes and water and food to spend at least 2 hours walking around the many trails the park has!
It’s a beautiful place. I went on late February and there was so much snow that I couldn’t even follow the trails to the vista points and waterfall (which was a pity).
Beautiful bridge! You get amazing views when you are driving westbound. Take into consideration that if you are going in this direction you will have to pay the toll.
You will have beautiful views of the painted ladies and the city from Alamo Square Park. Bring a towel or sheet so you can sit in the grass, you will really enjoy it!
So beautiful! Great views of the bay and the palace of fine arts. Usually crowded when weather is nice. Good spot for views and there’s a couple of benches to sit.
Always crowded, sometimes is hard to find a parking spot, but totally worth it. Views are breathtaking. I really enjoyed the beauty of the land and the sea.
We saw the bisons from the distance... they were really far away so it was imposible to see them form the designated area. We will give it another try
This neighborhood is great. I love roaming around discovering the little shops and Chinese signs all over the streets. Nice place to get lost!
The experience was great. Our guide was amazing and the canyon was beautiful. We went on the first tour in the morning and we loved it!
This playground is perfect to bring your kids to when you’re around Venice! They’ll enjoy it and you will enjoy the ambience as well!
Always full of people but it’s beautiful (can’t understand how instagramers manage to take pictures with nobody in the back)
I’ve been here twice and never had to wait more than 5 minutes in line! Great spot for the typical pic but it is a must!!!
Beautiful! I’ve been to the real Venice and honestly this looks so alike! Guess the góndolas are pricey but look amazing!
Views from here were amazing! Make sure you take a jacket with you because it might be a bit cold but is worth it!
Really cool! General tickets are $20. I didn’t get in but it was interesting to see it from the pier!

(Translated by Google) Swimming pool in a very well-kept neighborhood..There are about twenty free parking spaces near the entrance..The backdrop looks like concrete and therefore the water has a nice light color .. The style is reminiscent of the Venetian one, with poles and lanterns ..The locals pay about $ 5. The other $ 15. It is however a structure worthy of note ..

Piscina in un quartiere molto ben curato..Ci sono una ventina di posti macchina gratuiti vicino l ingresso..Il fondale sembra di cemento e quindi l acqua ha un bel colore chiaro.. Lo stile ricorda quello veneziano, con i pali e le lanterne..I locali pagano circa 5 dollari..Gli altri 15$. È una struttura comunque degna di nota..

(Translated by Google) The exhibition area is very nice and divided into 2 locations .. remember to validate the underground parking ticket to pay it $ 1 instead of $ 37 before returning to collect the car! The quality of the photos obviously depends on the temporary exhibition of that moment. The museum, on the other hand, is free.

(Translated by Google) Very large museum (you can also see real locomotives and airplanes) .. it is very nice and there are cars and historic vehicles .. like the American presidential cars .. also nice industrial machines to see the operation of the molds ..

(Translated by Google) Villa furnished with European taste..Precious materials and valuable works of art .. Practically all rooms have gold leaf finishes. Flagler was one of the richest men in the world.

(Translated by Google) One of the free beaches in Key Biscayne .. You pay for the very large parking lot close to the beach and then you can relax under the palm trees or in the sun ..
