Bel trail da fare se avete poco tempo..

Have been going to Leavenworth for I don't know how many years and this was the first time at this park. Hidden way down by the river on the west end of town there is plenty of parking, a ball field, playground and skate park as well as picnic benches. The river trail that goes back into downtown can also be accessed here. I have been on that trail many times but never went that far for some reason. The trail has several river access points where you can get into the river and these were empty compared to the access points closer to downtown. We were confused when we first came in thinking the few spots at the top of the hill were the only parking spaces. Deciding to venture down the curved drive we were pleasantly surprised by an abundance of parking.

I really enjoyed this place. As with many parks along these peninsulas you will have a vastly different experience depending on the tide. When we stopped the tide was super low so that you could walk way out into some of the jettys. Others were digging for clams or oysters, I'm not sure which. What I most enjoyed was the easy, simple loop trail that takes you through the  marshy preserve with views of the water along the way. We entered at a small area that said public fishing which was less crowded than the main entrance to the south.

Great park on the water with nice paved trail, boat access, covered fire pit, picnic area and a beach and play area for the kids. Usually very crowded but not so much now with Covid and all. Ivar's and Kidd Valley are both open and not crowded at all. In fact I've been there twice recently at lunch time and there was no one in line. Went in and ordered and then wait outside until they bring order out. Very easy and safe. Support our local businesses and get a nice walk in to boot!

Park has several small parking areas along the west side, each leading to a trail that winds through the park. The trail also continues up the hill behind the lake and connects with a larger trail aystem. There were several people fishing from docks as well as an electric motor boat out in the lake. The trail has a boardwalk that crosses over part of the lake where we encountered someone taking photos of the wildlife.

Small park by a beautiful river for wading or rafting. Campground sites are fairly open and fairly close together but clean and nicely kept up. The day use area was nice for a picnic by the river. The small interpretive displays have information about the history of the area which was nice. There was some sort of small hall available for indoor gatherings (not currently!).

There is a fabulous park here with plenty of picnic areas, a large playground and open grassy areas. But the real gem is the long flat trail that goes along the river. It runs on both sides (one is mostly paved and the other not) so you can hike or bike along one side and come back on the other by crossing one of several small pedestrian bridges that cross over the river.

Beautiful beach with lots of different areas to explore. There are campgrounds, cabins, playgrounds, fire pits, many different picnic areas and trails galore. We didn't really see any wildlife while we were there but orcas and seals can sometimes be seen as well other land based animals. Right next to Camas state park so that they might as well be one park.

Walking along Cedar River in Renton and looking at the flooded trail below. What's nice about this area is that you have the choice  to walk on the upper level when the lower trail is flooded / closed. We parked by the boeing plant at the mouth of the river that drains into Lake Washington and then walked back along the trail next to the river.

This is a state park with an entrance fee or state pass. Having said that, this park is great with several beaches, plenty of trails and picknik areas and many other options nicely spread out over a large area. Gets very busy on sunny summer days but we were just there on a beautiful spring morning and there were very few people there.

Huge lake with views of Mt. Rainier if the weather is right. Water skiing and other lake activities. Swimming can be done from the main beach but there is also access through the far campground by the dam. From there you can jump from the short rock outcroppings into the lake. Also a nice playground for young kids located there.

This is a fabulous park. It is huge with many trails. There are at least 2 paved "roads" that are blocked off to traffic but perfect for that social distancing hike. You can hike around the upper part of the park but there are 2 trails that go down to different beaches, one with a lighthouse and picnic tables.

Huge park with many different things going on. Lots of fields for soccer and baseball, indoor soccer fields, a rhododendron garden, a small river, a large playground paved trails and some historical buildings. Just don't expect to see a fort, as all that is left is the old watchtower.

A large park with lots of space to roam by the water. There is a long wooded trail at the beginning of the road and a frisbee golf course at the far end. It was very windy when we were there and based on the wind blocks at the picnic tables I'm guessing you can expect wind if you go.

Cute little museum / National Park! It's free and a good place to get out of the rain while you are exploring Pioneer Square. Mostly reading exhibits, so may be a bit boring for some but I enjoyed the bits of history that I learned about regarding Seattle and the Alaska gold Rush.

Worth a stop if you are in the area. No charge for parking or just walking around to look at the old buildings. Everything else has a fee, which varies by activity, but most are reasonable. Ride the train, go to the shooting gallery or grab a bite to eat, amongst other things.

A real hidden gem with a multitude of beautiful areas highlighting various plant and garden scenarios. Small water features and plenty of birds enhance the scene. Not overly large, plan to spend about an hour tops, but there is a lot to take in with the plants well marked.

Small park with a picnic area that overlooks the sound. Trail leads down to the saltwater beach which didn't really hold much interest to us but would be a nice place to relax with the gorgeous view or let the kids look under the rocks for sea life.

Nice shaded park with an easy loop to a bridge that overlooks the falls. Slightly steep but very short, maybe .4 miles round trip. I probably wouldn't go out of my way to visit but if you are travelling by I would definitely stop and take a look.

This place was a real surprise, in a good way. There is a (safe) steep loop trail that takes you down into the canyon where you can walk past some of the ruins along with views of more ruins built into the surrounding cliffs.

What else can be said? Fascinating history of country music that covers it all. Memorabilia, interactive displays and loads of information. I don't consider myself a country music fan and I thuroughly enjoyed it.
My wife and I go for walks here often. The trail between Phantom Lake and Larsen lake is a nice easy walk through mostly wooded areas and is about 2 1/2 miles round trip.
Small out of the way park. Quite place with picnic shelter and BBQ grills perfect for the small group that we had a lunch for. No reservations so first come first served.
As someone else said it's a cute little place to stop and stretch your legs. There is a coffee shop with views of the water and several second hand stores nearby.
Visited here for our son's soccer game. Large expansive park with plenty of interesting walking trails as well as the soccer fields.
If you don't already know this place come check it out. Something for everyone, walk, ride, skate play, swim... on and on.

Bring your walking shoes! This zoo is HUGE in terms of overall acreage. It's not your typical zoo where the animals are very penned in and up close for your viewing pleasure. This zoo is based more along the natural habitat method, with wide open spaces for animals to roam with other species they play nice with. There are some exhibits (penguin, polar bear, birds) where you can see them up close, but most are geared toward watching the animals while they are comfortable in space, from a distance. The elephant exhibit is under construction, which made for poor viewing of the elephants, but the overall concept of watching them in their natural element was pleasurable. We loved the penguin and polar bear exhibits as well as the kangaroos that hop among spectators in the Australia sections. Yes, there are NO WALLS b/w you and the penguins. They mainly avoid you, but it is quite fun to watch them 10 ft away from you.
dislikes: Limited close viewing of most animals

reviews_attraction.text: Perfect park? Dare I say? Hmm...it's got, well, everything a park would need...save for parking. Parking can get ridiculous on weekends. This park has water play, climbing wall, jungle gym, tunnels and a super huge slide! Pair that with great restrooms, seating options for all, dog park, ping pong, foosball, reading and art wagons, community garden, and great food trucks at your fingertips, and you aren't left for wanting. I'm amazed at all they have done with this location and am hoping this park is used as a blueprint for others. Very impressed. We take all our out of town guests with kids to this park...and it is well worth the 25 minute drive for us.

Gorgeous views, fun ride, great history information. Simply a must do for Palm Springs. Throwing snowballs in the desert was a confusing and fun experience. The hiking at the top was tough with the snowfall in January, but worth the views of the Palm cities, desert floor, and surrounding ranges. We wanted to make the 12 mile hike to the top of Mt. San Jacinto, but would have taken too long given the condition and our unprepared choice of footwear. Will have to come back in the spring, summer, fall to make the 10500 peak.

Great for locals it would seem as there are trails all over the mountain and primitive camping options to boot.

This park is well worth the drive. Tom's of space, great parking, large playground, splash pad for those hot Houston summer days. Bonus: disc golf course. My daughter couldn't get enough of the splash pad and playground equipment. I can see the draw. The Quinlan Center obviously has this splash pad beat, but you can't beat FREE! The restrooms are conveniently located b/w the splash pad and the playground. Restrooms as well as the park in general were kept pretty clean. We went early in the day (1030am) and it was pretty calm...maybe 6-8 kids at the splash pad. I would imagine it much busier in the afternoons.

Gorgeous, well kept park nestled right off the highway. My kids love to feed the ducks and pigeons at the pond. Playground is great for the kiddos. Options for big and small. Great seating for parents. Restrooms generally clean and located right next to playground. Parking can be thin on the weekend, but there are garages close by. Children's museum and nearby shops and restaurants really helps make a full day of it.

Play area, ball fields, covered basketball courts, public pool, disc golf. Pretty solid lineup as far as parks go. Execution leaves you wanting though. Brand new (updated) kids play area. Ball parks are fairly well used. Parking lot is falling apart. Pool needs overhaul. The crowd can get a little shady when the basketball courts are hopping. Disc course looks to be well used and fun.

Wow. Went in with basic children's museum style expectations. Left wanting all children/science museums to be this kid friendly. So. Much. Fun. Could have spent hours there!

My only complaint would be the parking fees, but I totally understand the need for them in a downtown setting. I would also say food options for kids could be much better.

Kiddo loves this place. Small park and can get crowded quickly, but tons of stimulation for the young ones. Only a couple of slides and swings, but a large wooden "fort" area with attached "agility course items" keeps them interested. There's also a smaller "fort" for the toddlers. We always leave tired and ready for a nap...both of us.

2.9 mile cinder running trail, golf course, driving range, bike/hike trails, ball fields of all situations, pretty good and fairly new playground. Parking can be tough during peak running hours, after work, Saturday mornings, but fairly easy 90% of the time. This park can accommodate almost any family or individual need I can think of.

Great park, tucked away into a good neighborhood. Two ponds (with ducks), splash pad, playground, large disk golf course. Clean grill/picnic areas. Very impressed at how clean and maintained this park was. Celebrated nephew's birthday and had tons of fun at the splash pad with the kids. Well used running trail through this park.

The green space, park in front is ridiculously beautiful. Great for picnics before or after museum visit. The new glass "maze" exhibit is neat and the 4 seasons are pretty amazing. Can't argue with the content inside the museum as I always seem to get lost enjoying myself for an hour or two. Well worth it if you have the time.

Easy and immersive nature trails. Disc golf course. A cute playground tucked away from the road with ample parking. Playground is super tall with amazing slides. Even the adults had fun.. Feels much more rural and open than its city location. Eight free RV spots for up to a week at a time. Be sure to book in advance.

Pretty nice, quiet little park. Some good shaded spots. Older equipment, but relatively useful/relevant. Picnic tables are scattered about. My one gripe would be the rock, pebbles underneath the equipment. It gets EVERYWHERE and I found a number of ant mounds hidden within the rock area...have the bites to prove it.

Overpriced, but fun for the kids. Takes about an hour to get through the looped trail...and that's with stopping a number of times. $19? Pretty ridiculous for an hour IMHO. 2yrs and under are free. The tiger at the end is fun. Similar to the Houston location. Watching the stingrays eat was also very fun.

Definitely worth a visit. Driven by here 100 times and finally decided to pull over. Man, was I missing out. I don't know how often I'd return, but I enjoyed my time there. The water wall interior area was peacefully loud...almost meditative. The surrounding park was clean and well manicured.

Huge kids play area. Designed around a train that draws the kiddos in for a sure fun time. Lots of slides and size options. Two-person swings!! NO SHADE...bring sunscreen and hats for all. Great parking. Fence surrounding the kids area is helpful for safety.

HUGE park. Older, well used kids play area. Adequate function. Lots of picnic table, covered gazebo options. Well maintained and safe, visible running trail. Area to picnic and play, ball fields, etc. Good parking all around. Well used park.

Good neighborhood park. Standard fare: ball fields, jungle gyms and slides. The splash pad is a nice additional component. Not the best one in town, but very fun for kids...and of course, parent's wallets. NOTE: There are NO restrooms.

Well used, busy park. Large splash pad was great on a hot early summer day for the little ones. The jungle gym is obnoxiously ginormous. The park play areas are large and in good shape. Worth the 15 minute drive out.
Worth a visit if you're in H-town. Well designed. Well cared for. The "spiral-tower" waterfall is interesting as well as majestic. There are many peaceful benches and nooks to take a book and relax.
Huge. Contains the zoo, Miller outdoor theatre, golf course, Japanese gardens and many many walking paths. Very picturesque. The live oaks over the cinder walking path are worth it alone.
Amazing children's museum. We spent at least an hour at the "light-bright" area alone! (Even the adults were playing...lol) You get in with a Houston Children's Museum membership too!
Large park with plenty of useful green space. Picnic tables peppered throughout, with shade. Playground is huge and shaded for the kids. Enjoyed and will be back.
Visited Hermann square for the McDonald's kids fest. Grounds were ok. Fest was a total letdown in terms of costs involved.
Sorry, but a toll is a toll, and a roll is a roll, and if we don't get no tolls, then we don't eat no rolls.

Newer park with something for every age. Kids can play on the playground or water sprinkles, and teens and adults can play basketball, racquetball, wall tennis or exercise. There are even concrete ping pong table for the adventurous. Bathrooms are in the park too, but they seem a bit sketchy.

This park has it all... Toddler and kids playgrounds, swings, putt putt, a tree maze, soccer and baseball fields, paved walking track and fun hills. It also has bathrooms and a snack shed. I really enjoy there is a Little Free Library too. This is a beautiful park for all ages.

For kids this place is great. Yes, most of the inactive exhibits are from the 80's, but young kids don't know that because they love pressing buttons and playing with learning exhibits. Oh yeah, did I mention there is a space shuttle here too. Awesome!

Wow!!! This place is absolutely stunning and it’s terrific the public gets to view this Castle and what it was like in its heyday. There are so many things to do and see. This is a must visit if you can do it. Tip - The outdoor pool is spectacular.

Super cool views of Griffith Park, the Hollywood sign, downtown LA and the surrounding areas. The area around and inside the observatory a great too. A real fun time of your one to be one with the outdoors.

The smell of the ocean and views of coast makes this place a fantastic place to reset or just forget about everything for a little bit. Just stroll down the pier and forget about time for a little bit.
If you are looking for a peaceful hike that isn’t crowded this is the place to go. The grounds are beautiful and the scenery is constantly changing. This is one of Poughkeepsie best kept secrets.
Beautiful park with tons of trails and stunning views. Trails are suited for all stages and difficulty levels. A must do if you are in the area. There are clean restrooms and water too.
What's not better than being on the Hudson on an aircraft that has a space shuttle and planes along with a submarine. I suggest every New Yorker and tourist check this place out.
Spacious park with a baseball/soccer turf field, track, playground and water feature for kids, basketball and racquetball courts, an outside fitness equipment and bathrooms.
Beautiful pier with a skate park, large grassy area, carousel, long pier with lots of benches and space for events. Chelsea Piers is just a stone's throw away.
Small wine tasting room with a large outdoor space. Staff is very friendly and though there is no grapes grown at this location the outdoor space is beautiful.
My advice, skip the restaurant and get food at the cafe. Much cheaper and you can still have views of the water. Portions are large a prices are reasonable.
Great spot to catch a boat and check out some of the sightseeing attractions in NYC. There are also dinner cruises, booze cruises and a lobster boat too.
Public skate park with some green space too. Truth be told there was no one skating so my 4 year old decided to make it her own personal playground.
Outstanding. This is one of California secrets most people do not know about. I highly suggest visiting to unwind, relax and just take in the views.
Clean spacious park with lots of benches and a kids playground. There is also a large open space for kids to run around or play on their bike.
Small coastal fishing town with an aquarium, breweries, wine tasting and other specialty shops. A little disappointed we missed the sea lions.
Great interactive activity for the kids that includes most of the current Disney Junior characters. A must do for the little Disney fans.
Really old lighthouse located in an area that isn't very accessable, but worth the hike. Get ready to exercise to see this beauty.
Large park with two playgrounds and multiple swings. Lots of trees, benches, bathroom and a couple of man made shaded structures.
This place is terrific, especially for the little ones. The Noah's Ark Exhibit is a must see. Your kids will spend all day here.
Home of the Chatham Anglers. Field is beautiful with great views and also a large playground for the little ones to play at.
Beautiful park that is adjacent to the Hudson. Great place to jog, walk, bike or just relax in some of the open spaces.
Beach is beautiful and the rock just makes the experience seem surreal. Must see if you are in the area.

An absolutely fantastic Beach. They have a boardwalk a great beachfront many shops. Plenty of restaurants. The only drawback is in the summertime, parking is really tough. But if you don't mind walking a little bit, you can park on 10th or 11th Avenue and hoof it down to the beach.  Belmar also has a train station that you can go into and from there, you can take a cab down to the beach which is only about a mile. Or maybe a uber.  In the town of Belmar itself there's plenty of restaurants and plenty of stores to look at as well. All in all it is an excellent outing.

Disney Springs is very nice. However a lot of the places inside of it are quite expensive. I suppose it goes with being in the downtown Disney District. The parking is kind of odd. Although they have many garages, they fill up quickly at times. There are a limited number of handicap spots on each level. They seem to fill up quicker than anything else. There is a Footbridge between the garage and the various areas that you're going into. Specifically I parked in the orange garage near Planet Hollywood. I was fortunate enough to find a space.

Just fantastic.  So much to do, hear whether it be picnicking, Sports, just walking around, sightseeing, or just hanging out with a special person. The Park is open even at night so you can go in and do whatever floats your boat. They have a couple of rest rooms that are available. You can picnic. I'm not sure if they allow open BBQs but I'm going to check that out next. It's a very convenient location as well. Easy to find, easy to navigate. Good for kids. I can't say enough about this place.

It's always fun at the horse track. The food is decent, the prices are reasonable. They do have valet parking. For a price of course. If you try to park on your own, it is definitely a challenge. But they do have a big parking lot right across the street from the place. Not only that, during the summer months, you can take New Jersey Transit and get off right at Monmouth Park. It's very convenient and it's a short walk over to the track. Leave the car at home, take the train.

I enjoyed very much showing my fiance around this area. As a native of California I have been here many times. It was fun to go back and reminisce. I enjoy Old Sacramento, always have. My fiance liked it very much too. We really enjoy going to some of the places like Fat City, and Fanny   and of course being a railroad fan, I love the California state Railroad Museum. Have been here many times. Overall it was a really fun time parking can be a little bit tough down there.
likes: Facilities & Services: Specific venues (Fat City, Fanny)

reviews_attraction.text: I was very disappointed that it was not shoveled out and plowed out with the recent snow. Made it very dangerous for people who like myself are handicapped and could not get down there. Therefore I was not able to go. I spent a long time on the parkway driving up to see it, and I could not go. 110 miles round trip for nothing. I'm sure the phones look fantastic. But the city of Paterson has a lot of work to do to make sure that it's safe once you get there

This is a nice park in the Pompano Beach area. There are picnic tables, seats, benches. Nice Beach. Open spaces. There's one parking lot across the street but sometimes it gets filled up to capacity. They do have handicap parking. It's located right on A1A. Easy to find. It's well kept up. And when we were there it seemed pretty secure. It looked as though everybody was following the covid-19 mask requirements. I would definitely go back.

This place is very very nice. I spent about an hour they're walking around in the afternoon a while back. I found the views to be exceptional. It's a good place to walk, people watch, have a quick lunch. Or just about anything that you would like to do. Fortunately I was able to park very close to where I wanted to go. And it was not that crowded on the day that I went. I would go back.

Outside of the parking which can be a challenge, we really enjoyed this area a lot. There are benches, barbecues, tables, and of course the beach. It is a very nice area where you can relax, have a meal, picnic, or just people watch. It's in a convenient location. Easy to get to. Sometimes you will have to sit in traffic, but if you go during the week or at off-hours it should be okay.

This is a great little Park. It has a carousel, baseball fields, basketball courts. Lots to do. Great place to bring kids. You can have a barbecue underneath the overhang. Great place for events. The slight drawback is that sometimes parking can be tough on the weekends. Especially if there's any events scheduled. They also have a field house. I recommend checking this place out.

Great place to walk and relax.   Plenty of benches to sit on.   Nice park.  U can bring your dog.  Or your significant other.  They also have BBQs for grilling.  The only drawback is the parking can get kind of tough especially on the weekends. It's good to go early. The ideal time would be late morning after the fog lifts.  I would definitely go back....with wcwoman!!

I mean it's okay but they have a fence around it you can't see anything. Allegedly they're redoing the entire backyard but you can't tell. It's in a neighborhood that is fairly middle class I would say. I wish them luck with their redesign of everything. Perhaps one day they will allow the public in to take a look once it all gets done.

Absolutely wonderful. Great for the railroad fan. They have so many displays, and so much to do. They offer roundhouse doors and on certain days they actually bring a train in there. The parking can be somewhat rough but you can always take a cab, a lift, or a Uber. I would highly recommend to any railroad fan that this is a must-see.

I have loved coming to Lake Tahoe and the surrounding areas for years. The forest is fantastic. There are so many things to do. Including skiing, fishing, hiking, or just use your imagination. Plenty of spots for a picnic. And backpacking is always good there.  i love mountains so this place will always be top notch.

Have to rate this ski area as average because it's very small. It is conveniently located very close to the freeway. And it is at a high enough elevation that it does get snow. However the parking is kind of strange at times. Overall it's very average

It was an absolutely wonderful experience we got to ride on the trolley and look around the museum. Is something that should not be missed while you're in Scranton. Highly highly recommended and The Price is Right 2

Always awesome.  Even in the fog.   I've been coming up the side of this hill for years. Nowadays it's one way in and one way out though. That's different. But you can still get here and it's still worth it
This is a very nice area. Sometimes the parking can be tough. But we enjoyed it very much. The views are great, and you can have a picnic lunch here or just hang out and walk and enjoy the views.
Very nice cruise.   very informative but narrator was a bit long winded.  However one negative is that the handicap parking is quite a distance from the boat. It really is not convenient.
Great Visitor Center for the National Park. Sometimes a little bit tough to park because of so much traffic in and out of there. But overall an excellent spot
Great great place. Not just a visit, but to actually at end of worship service. Very picturesque. I must see if you're in Jackson Square. You cannot miss it.
This is a very nice park they have a lot of everything. The only thing that was a little bit troubling to me was there was not enough benches or seats.
I have visited this part on numerous occasions and it's really enjoyable. Good location in Bridgewater Township. Easy to get to.
If you want to take pictures of this place good luck finding parking. It's almost impossible. Especially on the weekends.
Took my daughter to the holiday light show.  Pricey and average at best.   Did it, been there, done that.  Once.

One of the best state parks! There’s swimming, canoeing, kayaking, paddle boating, and so much more to do! Walk the well maintained trails for a hike, and check out the store on site: it’ll have everything you need! The campsites are clean and semi private, with water and electric hook up if you wish. Restrooms and well spaced throughout and clean. Check out the shaved ice truck that parks by the lake to cool off in the heat. There’s even a large checkerboard behind the store to play and watch the people on the lake go by. Find the Devil’s Waterhole and jump off its cliff if you dare!

One of THE best parks in San Antonio! Dog parks! Large fields to fly a kite, play soccer, baseball, have a special event, or watch the lunar eclipse! Playgrounds and picnic tables for the kiddos. Paved and unpaved trails for any level of athleticism, with lots of parts shaded by the beautiful trees. Do the blue trail for bikes or walk or run it to lose yourself in the spring blooms. 5ks can be seen taking place here. Deer roam freely and if you’re lucky, you’ll see an armadillo too! Best part: Park Police is visible and it’s safe to run alone in.

The views here are absolutely spectacular.  The trails to crystal cave and old baldy are not for the faint of heart.  Dog friendly! The campsites are comfortable and beautiful.  Come in the fall for the beautiful colors, it’s so worth it. When the new remodeled restrooms open, they’ll be great. The park store has everything you could possibly need, including a microwave! An ice cream store and a shop is also there for your souvenir wants.  Kayaking and floating in the river is possible too. Can’t wait to come back.

Wonderful place when you’re looking to get away and go off the grid for a bit. The summit to Guadalupe Peak is indeed strenuous, so be prepared; the trails are very rocky. The views at the top are totally worth it and spectacular. The visitors center is lovely with all that you need, a slide show, souvenirs, history, and helpful Rangers. Amanda the Ranger was amazing on the guided hike to the top and everyone was helpful and knowledgeable. It’s very rural out here but gorgeous!

A gem of a museum right here in Fredericksburg, Texas! So much history with real artifacts presented in a clear and fun, interactive environment. The USS Nimitz model ship is amazing, along with all the video and items to look at. Very detailed and family friendly. Staff is friendly and you can tell they care about this place. Don’t miss the outdoor memorials and the beautiful Zen Japanese garden right outside!

This park is a tiny place in the middle of the neighborhood but worth the find! The textures are fun to look at and feel, and little strange objects are tucked away to look at and find. There’s a little hidden area behind it with some benches, and an abandoned substation to peer into next to it. Just park in the street and go take a look!

This is a gem of an area right in San Antonio’s back yard. Staff is great and you can tell they care about this park. The trails are rugged, fun and easy to navigate. Dinosaur tracks are mostly currently underwater but it’s still a fun hike. Beware of rattlesnakes! The wildflowers are out in bloom so enjoy them before they’re gone!

DO NOT MISS THIS PARK! Beautiful sunrise, what a way to experience the significance of it in Hawaiian culture. Used a tour bus and it was much easier to not worry about payments and finding spots. Bring a jacket, it’s VERY cold up top. Catch the Milky Way and all the stars and afterward, explore the park and all its wonders.

The renovations this plaza has seen over the past decade have been transformative. It truly is now a main plaza. The cathedral is rich with history and the preservation of it. Please catch the light projection show when you can on Tuesdays, Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays, it is a spectacle not to be missed!

Three cheers for this National Park! Hikes, calderas, volcanoes, the summit of Mauna Loa, the Chain of craters road, holēi sea arch, petroglyphs: there’s so much to do and see. I recommend spending more than one day here to see all the wonders. Use the campsites or the Volcano House hotel to stay.

Do not miss this tour! Take the guided tour on the upper deck, they are so knowledgeable and you’ll learn so much! Tour the decks below which are surprisingly roomy and rich with history. The atmosphere just outside is nostalgic with signage and seating. There’s also a food truck!

This place is worth the stop if you are an art lover. Learn about oceanic artwork from the past, as well as Hawaii’s modern artists showcasing their talents. Cafe is available to eat a bite, and staff is friendly. You will have to check in your bags and backpacks, but it’s free!

Beautiful, sacred historical site to see how the Hawaiians lived. It’s amazing to walk in the place where they once stood. Sled walking tours and the waves crashing nearby. It was raining the day we went but it was still entirely worth it. DO NOT MISS THIS SITE, thank you NPS!

Awesome spring break destination! There was so much to see and do here for the day. Touch and feed stingrays, go to the botanical area and watch the birds fly around you, see a dolphin show, and walk under the immense tanks with sharks! Even on a rainy day, it was the best.

The rangers are super friendly and helpful! They’ll take the time to explain where you can go based on your abilities and time frame. Center has informative displays and small gift shop. Fill up your water bottle with the rain water they collect from the spigot outside!

A gem to have here in Texas! The self guided pace gives you time to see whatever you’d like to explore here. Climb onto cannons, marvel at the planes up top, and learn all about the history of this place. Bonus: it lights up at night!

Super friendly rangers and lots of fun souvenirs. The displays are great for the kiddos, and there’s even a post office next door and and gas station nearby. Make this your first stop when you arrive at Big Bend NP.

This visitors center has everything you will need for this rural, backcountry adventure of a park. Check out the critters that roam the park, and a friendly Ranger will surely help you with anything you need.
Awesome preserved aircraft for you to appreciate. Planes, helicopters, and a beautiful view behind you. Make sure you go to Hangar 79 next door to see more planes and read about the history.
The volunteers here were so knowledgeable and friendly helping to choose the right trails for the day. It’s conveniently located at several popular trailheads and has great souvenirs.
Nice easy walk to see this historical site. Beautiful scenery. A free audio tour and the rangers were exceptional in their knowledge and help! Make this a must stop in Hawaii.
Interesting interactive art installation in the middle of a golden field. Only thing that was unpleasant was the caps of spray paint cans littering the field and the path.
A great opportunity to enter and explore a submarine! Be mindful of tight walkways down below and walking on the top when it rains.  Wonderful experience to see.
Very nice informative center with lots of souvenirs. Large restrooms and a refillable water station for your bottle. Walk the short trail behind the center!
Visitors center had informative rangers who will help you plan your day at the Grand Canyon.  Conveniently located near the gift shop and shuttle buses.

Tons of fun!  I had I idea that you could just walk up and start painting on the walls.  Lots of people were there working on pictures. I definitely appreciated the free hand work over the stencils. The weekend we were there, someone was selling pictures of images on the wall from days past.  Really cool to see how the place has changed over time seeing the pictures.

It is quite a steep walk to the top, so choose carefully if you want to make the ascent.  It was  nice side trip and I would recommend swinging by to see the place.

If you feel like it, bring some cans and put your mark on the wall before you leave.

Nicely done. Not a huge parking lot. If you are driving an RV, come on a day with few people or park elsewhere and walk here.

The movie was good, but they also have videos in the rest of the displays. You can spend a few hours here if you like civil war history.

On the walk up, they have items embedded into the side walk that zig zags up the hill to replicate the zig zag pattern you would run if you were retreating under fire.   The items might be things you dropped or left behind as you fled. Interesting way to get you thinking before you ever even enter the building.

One of the most well done historical visits I have ever had was to Andrew Jackson's Hermatige Home.  If you get the chance, come visit and plan to spend 2-4 hours there.  The grounds are beautiful and everything in the home is original or restored.  They turned it into a museum within about 20 years of his death because his son mismanaged their money and went broke in 10 years.

Peaceful and nice place to visit. We just walked around and read the signs and did not do any audio tour or tour guide, but it was obvious people who did got even more out of the experience.

The loop road is still closed due to weather delays in reconstruction. Can't complain too but, as it is giving the cervils a better opportunity to establish themselves.  Wish the website was up to date on road closures, however

Visitor center sign was missing on road when we went by, again due to road construction, so we had to turn around and go back after we realized we passed it.

Lots of trails, but they are poorly marked to same the least. With all the animal trails it is tough to know which is the real trail. I wish they would have a marker at each intersection, but they don't.

We have been three times now and each time we figure out where we got off the "real trail" and make it farther before getting off again.

We will be back and keep trying

great stop!  They had lots of brochures for all of Texas and Austin and lots of history on the capitol.  It is a great place to start your tour of the grounds.

We parked in the capitol visitor parking garage.  It was large and close by.  A good choice.  The day we went it was free, so I have not idea what they normally charge.

Free museum with a paid 22 min video.  I felt the video did not do a great job of visualizing the troop movements or orienting you on the map. If you are familiar with the area, you will be okay.

Picked up a flyer to do the auto tour while there as well. The auto tour was well marked and a nice drive.

Very short walk to see the outside of the house.. pickup a flyer before going to see the layout of the inside, since it is not open to the public at this time.

Less than a 1/2 mile hike to waters edge to see where ferry was, but currently underwater and blocked off due to flooding.

Took a hike on the four notch loop. Still pretty mucky and wet.  Tough to cross several of the seasonal streams.  Will be great once it dries out just a bit more.

Trails are really well marked.  White for Lone Star Trail and White with red stripe for Four Notches Loop.

Nice little park. They recently opened up their trails to mountain biking so we went to go on a ride.

I would go back and explore some more trails. They are doing some work to improve the trails and grounds.  It will only get better.

Lots of history, great tourist shops, and a cattle drive all in one place.  There are some really high end shops as well on the fringe of the stock yards.

Great place to take kids to see the animals, Do a maze, and watch a gun fight.

Amazing to see some of the roots of America. It was a tiny shot gun house.  Left here in his early teens, but a nice little tribute.  Glad they preserved it.

Parking lot here is decent sized and the grounds are well cared for.

Pretty cool and amazingly big. Enjoyed walking at our own pace.  The recorded guided device you can take along was worth it.  It is a definite hike down into the cave, but interesting.  Just be prepared for a lot of walking.
Pretty rough road driving up to trailhead. Vault toilets at trail head. Easy walk up trail to falls. Plan on getting wet to walk up to see the falls.  Water is pretty darn cold, but beat to see.
Nice place to hike and hang out at the springs. Saw several people fishing as well. They have kayaks for rent too.  You register yourself as you come through the gate, so have exact change.
Small visitor center, but so is this side of the canyon.  The area is neat and lot less crowded than the south rim. Hiking in this area has a lot more trees than the south rim as well.

Nice place to take a stroll.  Grounds are well maintained and there are things for the kids as well.

The koi in the lower pond are super interested in people and they are gigantic.
Not much here. Glad they preserved this much, but it isn't much of a stop.  Literally part of a city block with a monument and a few cannons.  Way to miss it you are not careful

Went for the backstage tour. They pump you through very quickly.  Tours every 15 minutes.  Interesting to see everything.

Don't park at the hotel parking lot, it's $32.
Really neat to see the house and the belongings and hear the stories. It really is neat to see the presidents as people, not just presidents.
Super neat falls. Walk is short, but not well maintained to the bottom. If you aren't sure footed, don't go past the wooden bridge.
Made this stop worth it. Very neat to see how all the foot traffic and natural elements had worn down the path through this area
Nice park with LOTS of camping and nice lake access. You can rent a cayak or canoe, they even have a store there.
This park has limited parking, so don't delay your entry or you may have to wait to get in to get parked.
Pretty cool history here.  Doesn't take too much time to see it, but a lot has happened in this spot.

Wonderful grounds scattered with planes and picnic tables. Lots of history throughout the museum. You can get a Photo inside the Spruce Goose cockpit with up to 4 people. There is a small plane kids can get in for a photo as well. Not sure of the cost for either. Be sure to visit the upstairs deck because it gives a wonderful overview of the planes and has a gallery. Nice eatery and gift shop including a Penny Smashing Souvenir machine. Clean restrooms, water fountain and seating though the museum in the form of airplane chairs. Educational and hands-on activities area for kids. We can't wait to come back! :-)

Huge hands on Science Center! Great Outdoor water park type of play area that the kids can shoot at Targets with the water guns. This park is amazing. There are trails through out the whole park. If you are less mobile, there is "The 5 Mile Loop" that lets you drive through the whole park with view points overlooking the water. This is a great family park as there are tables for picnics, bbq pits, a playground and beach front.
Owen Beach is a rocky beach that has great views of Vashon Island, Mt Rainier and the ferries.
Pt. Defiance Park also includes a living museum at Fort Nisqually. It is a working Fort manned by volunteers showing you how life was in the 1800s.
Then there is the Pt. Defiance Zoo and Aquarium. There is a newly (2019) built Pacific Seas Aquarium that has hammerhead sharks and sea turtles. This park is a true gem of Tacoma. Great place to escape the crazy city life and get back to nature.

Basically, actually grew up within the Bronx Park, and specifically this near by playground, since the age of 4 years.

Have been hiking, kayaking, rock climbing, trekking and even mountain climbing, all across the US and Europe.
And it all began from the lessons learned growing up in this park since the 1960's.

Realistically, what's not love about
the Bronx Park.

Historically,  it ran from the East River, upriver through the (present day) Bronx Zoo, into the Botanical Garden, flowing passed the Old Snuff-Mill.
{Where  the  old-timers would buy the best tobacco in NYC, and always had a coffee and snack store for us children.}
The "River" continued to wind up the rapids, over the falls (really a dam built for the Snuff Mill).
Thus leading, all the way up river, about 25 miles to the Kensico Dam,
by the Valley of the Gods, near Valhalla.

However, shoelace park???
No one, who has ever grown up,
in the Bronx Park, specifically on Bronx Blvd. (Which actually, is the major neighborhood, of the River.)
Has ever, even heard of, shoe lace park,
it is a completely wrong designation of the area.
Erroneously conceived, by the new alliance, which has just recently only formed about 10-15 years, (with mostly all incorrect facts)

There is, however a Horseshoe Park, shaped like a horse shoe, down river a couple miles, passed my old house on Bronx Blvd,
just under Gunhill Rd.
That's where, most of the neighborhood, would gather for late night parties, and
July 4th celebrations.

Most especially, spectacular was the 1976 Bicentennial 4th of July extravaganza.
When many areas, along the Bronx River, were painted Red, White and Blue.
And many stages, were constructed for the politicians and musicians.
With our fireworks display, although small in comparison, was almost as magnificent, as the firework masterpieces, currently held at the upper river, by the Dam at Valhalla.

That is actually, a small part, of the true history of this Bronx Park/ River,
by someone who actually lived it.

I didn't even know El Paso had a tram when I was driving from Tucson back home to Austin and needed a road break and discovered this on the TX State Parks website.

The scenery is overlooking the urban sprawl below, but I was actually disappointed in the tram ride up and the views once I got up there. I mean, I know this isn't the Rockies or Alps, but it just wasn't that impressive for the ridiculously long wait times (each of the two gondolas can only take up to 6 people, though most times it was less and they are supposed to run every 5mins or so, but there were sometimes 10-12min gaps between loads). Over 30mins for a 3min ride? The tram ride was fine, but there isn't a lot to see on the way up. Maybe I wouldn't have minded the wait f there was more than just a few walkways and a perilous "Ranger Loop Trail" at the top. "The best view in the Southwest?" Yeah, I don't think so...they must have meant the Southwest corner of El Paso, cuz there are better views from Mt Bonnell in Austin and definitely better views in several other places throughout the state of TX and the Southwest.

I was wanting to do the Geocaches here, but OMG, where they put them here was a little too "adventurous" for my taste. I did the Directissimo Trail because the line was stupid long and I thought killing 30mins on a trail was a better use of my time. But this trail was crazy! It makes you hike halfway up the mountain and I don't think the geocache was even there because after getting up to the bench where my geocache app said I was within 4ft of the damn thing it was nowhere to be found and I looked for a solid 15mins! The trail going up was bad, but going down was worse. It's a narrow trail w/things that can stab you jutting in on the trail itself, so you really have to watch your footing. But the hike down gets "fun" with all the loose rocks and tall quasi-rock steps. Did not enjoy it at all and to have done all that to come back w/out my geocache punch made it even less enjoyable. When I talked to the ranger at the box office they were just like "oh the girl who put it there said it was there last month" but had no idea if it was at "bench 1 or 2" wtf? Seriously? Then the Geocache at the top of the tram was supposedly next to this brick chalet, but when you see where the chalet is compared to where you are...it is a trek! I attempted the Ranger Loop Trail, but it was more perilous than the Directissimo as there are some pretty steep drops where you need to be super athletic and have longer legs than I did if you are going to make it down and back, so I came back after the 3rd set of chain ropes.

Needless to say, it was not worth the $8 ticket price nor the time. I think if I came back I'd check out the actual Franklin Mtn State Park and seem if it can redeem this experience.

Also, it was annoying with all the crying kids in line and moaning and groaning adults about it being cold. C'mon people...you are going up a mountain in December...figure it out or shut up. Great revenue for the gift shop at the top though, I saw several people in the line to come back down (only a 20min wait...huzzah?) that were jacket-less on the way up w/newly acquired sweatshirts.

Home to one of the largest urban bat populations in the world, the bats of the Congress Street Bridge are like the mascots of Austin. "It's the best free show in town!" was how the experience was first described to me before I moved here.

It initially struck me as odd that a city could be defined by such a "weird" spectacle, but the all female mexican free-tail colony numbering up to 750k that call the underside of the bridge home to birth their pups each year due their part to make sure ATX lives up to its "Keep Austin Weird" moniker.

Having lived here almost 7yrs and now seen these fascinating creatures from every possible angle, I can tell you that, by far, the best way is to see them from the water, right before dusk, from either an individual water bike or kayak. There are cruise options and viewing from on the bridge, but when you are actually under the bridge and they are getting ready to go out on their nightly feeding flights, you can not only hear them as a symphonic hum, but almost feel their preparatory vibrations. It is bat tuning fork and if it doesn't give you goosebumps, you might need to take a certain personality...

My favorite viewing thus far has been on Halloween night when the colony was estimated to be at just over 1.5million (the pups had all be born). I had rented a water bike and just witnessed a gorgeous sunset on Town Lake and made my way to just under the bridge right as dusk was setting in. The hum had reached a fever pitch and the crowds both on the bridge and water were waiting in anticipation as random bats started to flit haphazardly into the night sky. Then, there was almost a palpable "pause" just before three synchronized flumes of bats exploded from under the bridge! Seeing the frenzy up close was like witnessing controlled chaos and it was such an incredible bordering on beautiful sight to behold! This went on for about 15mins. There were a few stragglers that continued in small waves for another 15-20mins afterwards.

I strongly suggest, whether an Austinite native, local, or tourist, to experience this at least once. It really is the "best free show" in the city. Also, the history of how the bats ended up under the bridge is a fascinating read, if you are a nerd like me and enjoy the "origin story" of such things.

A few pointers for first timers:
-Be sure to check the bat migration schedules, as this is not a year around occurrence (usually May to Sept/Oct)
-There is an annual Bat Fest, usually the end of August, worth checking out
-If viewing from the water, be sure to wear a hat, glasses, and look up with your mouth closed...that smell coming from under the bridge is not "perfume" and u definitely don't want it in your hair, eyes, or mouth!

I grew up behind the "White Dove of the Desert" in a house off Valencia, so I have a plethora of memories visiting this historical and beautiful mission on the res just south of Tucson.

But, recently, this place played an important part in a life event. My mom passed away unexpectedly and this was always her favorite place of worship in Tucson. She loved to come light a candle, say a prayer, and bless herself and those she was with w/some holy water. She also used to love to try and lift Father Kino's wooden statue to rid herself of "sin".

I am by no means religious, so my appreciation of this beautiful place is for the gorgeous architecture and decor inside and the intricacy and preservation of the artistry within.

This mission and the grounds it is on is a place of reflection and prayer for the religious and for those of us that aren't we can take it all in with aesthetic, historic, and artistic admiration.

My only concern is that since it is still an active place of worship, I was appalled to see so much disrespect for the sanctity of the interior of the church. People didn't remove their hats or sunglasses, they were using flashes, and drinking from water bottles inside. Even the tour guide giving the history behind the building and grounds had exposed shoulders,was drinking water, and using a laser pointer...she should definitely have known better! So please, if you go inside, be respectful...if you don't know how to behave or what is allowed inside a Catholic church, please be modest and/or ask.

We lit a candle in the little chapel to the left of mission and then hiked up the little hill adjacent to the mission where there is a little memorial shrine and released some balloons in my mother's honor and watch them disappear into the clearest of blue skies. It was a beautiful moment to be sure on a gorgeous spring AZ day and a wonderful way to memorialize someone.

For those that want to experience the touristy side here, there are a variety of vendors w/in the walled "shops" and there are also an abundance of Indian Frybread stands out front under ocotillo shade stands making fresh frybread right in front of your eyes (if you don't know what frybread is, think funnel bread, but better!).

Definitely worth a visit to see a relic of Catholic, Arizona, and Native American history wrapped in a beautiful building and grounds!
dislikes: Inappropriate attire and conduct by tour guide

reviews_attraction.text:
I recently discovered this little gem on their last free admission wknd of the summer. I can't believe I have lived in Austin for 5yrs and never made it out here!

First, let me say, that this place is definitely a place meant and designed for quiet introspection and appreciation of the sculptures, thoughtfully placed and integrated into the landscape and grounds. The water feature at the entrance is especially pleasant and you can walk via a pathway to the top of it and sit and just get lost in thoughts and nature...in the middle of what is essentially downtown Austin!

The sculptures are fantastic and span the spectrum from renaissance to contemporary to grotesque to macabre to religious to exquisite to simplistic...which is just fantastic! You can find one or two or ten and peruse the form, flow, and context, which I love!

The visitor center, which also doubles as an exhibition gallery, was great! The "Shiva and Eve" exhibit they had with various interpretation of the female form was fantastic!

My only qualm was, and in all fairness this may have been due to it being a "free" wknd, that there were 3 separate parents with very young/small children running around screaming and even touching and CLIMBING on the sculptures in the garden. This made it very unpleasant to enjoy the ambiance and environment this place was designed for and I could not believe the complete disregard and lack of respect the parents had for others and these art sculptures. Even if there hadn't been prominently posted signed to NOT touch or climb the sculptures, it is common sense that is NEVER OK! I was honestly appalled that anyone, let alone Austinites, would behave this way!  I even told the docents in the visitor center and they just kind of shrugged and said "there isn't a lot we can do". What a sad commentary on Society and its lack of conscience and courtesy!

Umlauf is a wonderful, peaceful abode where you can appreciate art and nature as one...it is not a playground or free babysitter for parents to bring their unruly offspring! There is the Thinkery in Mueller or, better yet, the grounds of Zilker, for just that!

Please be respectful of this place and those that are trying to enjoy it next time you visit!

I felt like a kid in a proverbial candy store here...

I came w/a big group of "adults" for a friend's birthday and we arrived just in time for their "show and tell" animal show. I was literally giddy with excitement with each and every animal they presented (the presenter was funny and engaging and handled some unruly kids w/authority and ease) and several you were allowed to either hold, pet, or interact with in some way (except the possum, which having lived in Indiana, I was totally fine with). It was just all around amazing! The highlights for me were the gator, the python, the chinchilla, and of course, Art, the sloth!!

Next up, we wandered over to the wolf enclosure where you can actually physically interact with wolves. Many of them, I think by the time we got to the enclosure, were over "playtime" as they were kind of aloof and not into the petting. It was still an extraordinary experience, but I think going early and being the first ones in might have proved a better interactive experience. However, I did end up with an unexpected souvenir...when a friend and I were attempting a selfie, I had my sunglasses on the top of my head and one of the bigger wolves nabbed them right off my head and proceeded to playfully run around dodging attempts to recover them and using them as a chew toy. Thankfully, they were cheap glasses and I left with a very cool keepsake, wolf drool and bite-marked lenses included!

There are several other exotic animals throughout the park, including emus, lemurs, and a kangaroo (who was sitting way back in his corner looking like he was in time out). I think because of the severe heat (seriously, either bring lots of water or have several $1.25 in quarters on hand because the heat is no joke!) a lot of the animals were just trying to keep cool.

They have pigs, goats, and mini-donkeys you can feed as well. Just make sure you are wearing something you don't mind getting "dirty" when feeding the piggies cuz there is a "splash zone".

I cannot recommend this place enough for locals, out-of-towners, or just anyone who wants to unleash their inner-child in a fun and memorable way!
dislikes: Some animals uninterested in interaction due to timing
Potential mess when feeding certain animals

reviews_attraction.text:
After passing this place countless times on I-35, seeing the billboard and thinking it was more kitsch than substance, I finally decided to check it out and wow, it was nothing like I expected! This place was such a pleasant surprise! I have to say going in, I was expecting the dated, hokey, kitsch that one might expect from a commercial cave (and I have visited my fair share) so I had been putting off visiting, even though I used to live relatively close. When I saw their 50% off Facebook promo, I figured $10 was a safe bet...and wow did I get 3x my money's worth!

First off, I liked that it was relatively uncrowded and an easy on/off to I-35. Secondly, the staff is just so pleasant, as in they act like they actually want to be there. Thirdly....they have a zebra!?!? Zoe, the zebra was very lively when I paid her a visit, and though there are signs that say "do not feed/pet the animals" (and righty so cuz she bites!), one of the groundskeepers was feeding her and let me give her some niblets after she calmed down, which I have to say was an amazing way to start my Inner Space experience!

The tour itself was fantastic and that was mostly due to our fantastic and exceptionally knowledgeable tour guide (and resident archaeologist) Katherine! I have been on more cave tours that you can shake cave bacon at and she somehow managed to enlighten me with a knowledge nugget or two! And, per the usual commercial cave tour, you get to experience total darkness (which even as many times as I have experienced, never gets old as it is truly something incredible with the only other natural way to experience it is the deep ocean).

The cave is just beautiful! The formations awe-inspiring and well maintained/protected and the adorable bats were literally just above our heads! The different chambers were all just gorgeous, but my hands-down favorite wass the Moon Lake!

An absolutely wonderful way to spend an hour and 15mins and one of Texas' prettiest show caves with the added benefit of being within a relatively short drive from Austin!

I came here specifically to see the "Woman in Gold" after watching the movie based on the portrait of Adele Bloch-Bauer by Klimt on display here. I also attempted to visit during one of their "First Fridays" where there is free admission from 6-8pm. However, the line was literally 3 city blocks long and I would not have been able to gain entrance had I waited due to the strict time constraints.

I ended up coming back when they opened on Saturday and paid the $20 entrance fee. I thought this was a bit steep for the size of their collection. But, the building itself is beautiful and they had a small exhibition of Edvard Munch's works, including "the Scream" in pastel, which was wonderful to experience.

The galleries themselves are quite compact, so if you go on a weekend, like I did, do not expect to be able to sit and admire and enjoy any of them as they were all extremely packed. They also strictly enforce their "no photography" rule and will make you delete a picture if they find you taking one.

I did enjoy finally getting to see "the Woman in Gold" and Munch's "Scream" in pastel (the poem on wood at the base of the painting that has the poem on which 'The Scream' is based was a neat surprise as I had had no clue of the origin). The other Klimt paintings as well as several other works by various German and Austrian artists would have been nice to peruse, but sadly, with the number of people in the galleries, it was impossible to thoroughly appreciate anything.

I did like that they have a complementary coat-check and audio guide (mine was having playback issues, but I did not want to get back in the long line to exchange for a new one), but I don't know that I would return as there was nothing overly breath-taking or spectacular and the sort of militant attitude conveyed about experiencing the art here was a bit off-putting. Also, for price of entrance, I felt the experience was lacking. For a mere $5 more, you could walk down the street and experience the MET.

I was soooo excited when this placed gained protected National Monument status thanks to Pres. Obama signing into the National Parks Service in 2015! That it took me almost 3yrs to go and finally see it when it was just a 90min drive up 35 and being the National Parks Nerd that I am, is just shameful!

So, if you are expecting something interactive and mindblowing, then you will be disappointed, but if you go in expecting to see the original dig site (which has not been touched since 2001) on a guided tour by a park ranger and do so in about 45mins, then you enjoy your visit!

The covered dig site is small-ish, but to see the bones exposed from above and to hear how they were found and learn about the Colombian Mammoth (and the variety of mammoths that existed) and the history of the dig site and Texas in general is any nerd's dream!

Though, once again this is directed towards parents, if you bring little ones, please either put them on a short leash or keep them in their respective modes of transport. There were a few unruly kids that nearly tripped me running amok and I finally said something to the parents who looked shocked. Yes...I am going to call you out when your miscreant spawn is infringing on my ability to enjoy something I paid for and should be able to despite you thinking your $5 admission equals free child care for 45mins.

That being said, I highly recommend making a stop here whether it is as a destination or just a stop-off while in the Waco area. Don't forget to get your National Parks Passport stamp at the meet-up spot or in the gift shop!
likes: Facilities & Services: Guided tours, knowledgeable park rangers
Activities: Educational experience, learning about mammoths

reviews_attraction.text:
So this place is a great little "gem of nature" in the urban sprawl of North Austin.

I have done a couple of trails here now and have really enjoyed my leisurely hikes through this little pocket of wilderness.

The creek actually had some water, so it was nice to just take a respite sitting on a rock in the middle of the bubbling waters and take a deep breath and forget about the #strugglebus that has become daily life in our ever burgeoning metropolis.

Alas, that moment was short-lived as the 20-something hipsters, 30-something new parents w/their feral spawn, and the array of dudebros and duckfaced barbie-types amongst their packs of unleashed dogs came full-throttle into my little bubble of Zen and burst it with the inconsiderate vigor of entitlement that seems to be the current plague of Austin.  Though, I have a feeling, despite whatever time of day I came, this would be a daily occurrence.

On my hike back to the parking lot, I was almost run down by various mountain bikers who for some reason had it in their heads that they had more of a right to be ravaging the trails than my feet did walking them. They seriously YELLED at me...I guess pedestrian right of way is not a thing here.

I really liked the natural space here, so 5-stars for the haven-esqueness of what could be here, but 1-star for the people I encountered on and off the trails.

Like w/most good things, certain types will always find a way to ruin it and sadly they seem to be en masse here.

This is a definite must see for any amateur speleologists out there or just anyone who appreciates the visual beauty of Nature and Time!

Easily one of the prettiest show caves in TX, Natural Bridge Caverns starts its tours with a view of its namesake right by the entrance. The tour is a little short and our guide was not particularly engaging or overly knowledgable (it sounded like she was reading from the Cave Guide's Discovery Tour Script), but she was really young and honestly, you really don't need a lot of explanation of the absolutely fantastic and gorgeous formations in front of you!

The formations in the cave are just downright spectacular! From chamber to chamber they get progressively more and more breathtaking! The crown jewel is the end of the Discovery Tour when you have a full panorama of the formations from the "observation deck" which creates this sort of layered perspective that is just jaw dropping! One of my fav formations was definitely the King's Throne and the Castle of the White Giants. The petrified bat roosts and rimstone dams are also really cool cave "decorations". And because it is still an active cave, water is dripping everywhere, so it is more than likely you will leave your underground adventure with a "cave kiss", which is always good luck!

Totally worth the money and the drive out there! Also look into combining the cave tour w/a Bracken Bat Flight viewing. You will not regret it!

Finally found the best kept secret in Austin! Seriously, this thing is impossible to find! It is like some weird gap in the Austin Space Time Continuum...you can see it, but you (and apparently no one you know) can't figure out exactly how to get there.

Turns out, it is has various access points, but very few that are within immediate walking distance from anywhere accessible by car. However, if you have an BT@LBL Obi Wan, then all is not lost!

As for the boardwalk itself, it is just absolutely fantastic! There are several "viewing harbors" where you can get off the main path (where the cyclists will run you down if you do not get out of their way fast enough...ahem, pedestrians always have right away!) and enjoy some great overlooks on the water and of the skyline.

There is such great people watching to be had along with wildlife viewing in the form of turtles (they are just so adorable all clustered together sunning themselves on a log) or cranes or Austinites themselves.

Fair warning, there are no restroom facilities or access to water along the boardwalk, so bring lots of water with you and make sure to pee before you trek out!

Also, keep your eye out for what I am guessing is an art installation commentary on ATX's canine per capita in the form of bronze dog collars with funny lil quips along the railings!

What an experience...it is actually really hard to put it into words because the whole thing is such a multi-sensory immersion that verbalizing it would not begin to do it justice!

I had spent two hrs here, but probably could have spent an entire day! The sculptures in the parking lot were just a bit to whet your palate for what was in store. The $20 and $1 for the glasses (which you must get because it definitely heightens the vision experience of the whole thing!) were well worth the price of admission as the minute you walk in you just know something incredible is about to happen!

So, aside from it being an interactive immersive art experience, there is a kind of an underlying "mystery" that you are trying to solve kind of like puzzle room-ish throughout, but honestly, I was so overwhelmed that I was just like "OMG...what next!?". I felt like a kid discovering their weirdest lucid dreams in a weird and colortastic wonderscape!

There were times where i found a secret little nook that i had all to myself and just vegged for a hot sec before wandering onto the next whimsical, jaw-dropping thing.

Do yourself a favor and just come here. Santa Fe is an amazing place, but Meow Wolf is a destination in and of itself!

I was actually disappointed in the caverns and the tour here. I had such high expectations, too, for how much this place is touted!

I have been to several of Texas' show caves and this one was definitely subpar, which I was so confused by since it is a state park and highly recommended by a lot of folks, so I would have expected so much more as far as the cave itself.

There are very few formations in this cave, which I think is due to it being a speakeasy and dance hall prior to a state park/show cave. The tour was somewhat short and lacking and our tour guide seemed to want to be anywhere else but on the tour with us; he seemed to be on autopilot just regurgitating the cave tour "facts" and not really into answering any of our group's questions.

The formations that there were in the cave were not that impressive, especially compared to some of the other caves I have been to and $16, which I initially thought was a steal, seemed to be a bit expensive for the tour and experience you get.

Definitely do not see myself returning here or even recommending it, especially considering the drive from Austin. I'm sorry and sad to say it, but other than its  historical factor, not a lot going for this Texas cave.

This place is the definition of "middle of nowhere" as it is literally not close to anything, so you have to want to want to go here and be willing to invest the time, but the ROI is beyond expectations!

The Visitor's Center here is very nice with several exhibits explaining the importance and history of the bristlecone pines with lots of hands on displays and super informative rangers.

Two trails of ancient bristlecone pines are directly accessible from the VC: the Discovery (just over a mile loop) and the Methusaleh (just under 5mi loop). The Methusaleh is where the oldest tree in the world is located, though it is unmarked to preserve its longevity.

The Discovery Trail is a somewhat moderate (though can be strenuous due to the altitude as you are above 10,000ft here) loop that takes you past some impressively old and photogenic trees. The shale rock part of the backend of the trail is also impressive and has great panoramas of the area.

A must visit if you are into impressive geology and the awe of nature's perseverance!

If you both trails you will need at least 4hrs, but in honesty, 6hrs if you want to truly enjoy yourself and take it all in!
likes: Facilities & Services: Informative rangers, hands-on displays
Activities: Hiking trails, geological features, panoramic views

reviews_attraction.text:
This place is surprisingly beautiful and well worth a visit and price of admission!

First off, the gardens themselves are just incredible and a joy to walk through. They are shockingly vast, so wear comfortable walking shoes!

There is a visitor center, cafe, and gift shop at the entrance as well as plentiful parking, but the parking lot is massive as well, so be prepared to walk when the lot is full.

There are benches everywhere to sit and just take it all in and because the grounds are sprawling, you can find yourself communing with nature without any one else intruding on your solitude, which I absolutely loved!

The tower itself is just spectacular! The artistry is amazing and it is truly gorgeous! It plays every so often and the bells are ethereal and haunting.

There is a little fish moat at the base of the tower that has koi and is neat to walk around.

Definitely make a trek here and see it for yourself, whether you are a FL native or a tourist, you will not regret the experience!
likes: Visitor amenities (visitor center, cafe, gift shop)

reviews_attraction.text:
Discovered this place via the AllTrails app. It is pretty hidden between two apt complexes off the 35 frontage road and the little entrance to the open field which takes you back towards the shores of the Blanco River is not conspicuously marked.

For me, however, this was a good thing. I went just before dusk on a Saturday and there was absolutely no one else on the trail but me. The trails walks through an open field then along some brush obstructing the view of the river, but it breaks up in certain places and you are treated to some pretty vistas of the surprisingly clear Blanco. I only did about half a mile of the trail because the mosquitoes were brutal, but I think the entire thing might be less than a mile to be honest. I turned around at this cool little split that had some awesome trees and I even saw a few frogs.

If you are looking for a nice little walk w/o too many people, this was a neat little find in the San Marcos area.

What a fantastic hidden gem this little park is! Though a little tricky to find at first, it was well worth the hunt! Heads up that parking is very scarce. There is a lot, but it fills up quickly and once it does it is street parking only.

Walking through the park is nice any day, but on a beautifully sunny spring or fall day, it is just fantastic! There is this nice little stone path that goes to this little square with benches and a fountain and little ponds. There is also a nice little walking trail right outside the enclosed garden area.

The icons and stars of the park are of course the feral peacocks that run around the park. They are temperamental to be sure, but whether they are strutting in full plumage display or hiding high in the tree tops or nesting amongst the brush, they are still a sight to be seen in the city of Austin!
#12DaysofChristmasATX

This National Park was a nice surprise! And though it is kind of in the middle of nowhere (the closest town with services, lodging, and restaurants is Ely, which is about an hr drive away), it is worth checking out!

I specifically came for their annual astronomy festival as the skies out here are some of the last remaining true dark ones in the country. They have 3 days full of astronomically themed activities and nightly sky viewing with telescopes at the Lehman Caves visitor center picnic area each night.

The Lehman Caves (surcharge) were the highlight of my visit, but the scenic drive up to Wheeler Peak was also pretty spectacular (you go up 10,000+ft!) with full panoramas of the basin valley below.

The facilities are very nice as well and there is a cafe at the Lehman Visitor Ctr. The NP even has its own very informative app!

Came here for QueensFeast, which is the best menu value this year as it includes wine pairing w/each of the 4-courses! Plus, you get a delicious watermelon shooter w/mint cream palate cleanser!

The property is just gorgeous w/actual vineyards, an expansive patio area and a little gazebo overlooking the pond.

The dining area is open w/a little bar and a couple of hightop tables.

Staff here are exceptional! They made it feel like I was visiting friends, yet were attentive and knowledgeable.

Not only do they have a fabulous menu, but the wines were all pretty good as well! Plus, they offer beer flights from their brewery in Salisbury!

Reservations are required for QueensFeast, but if you can't make it out for that, def check them out for a gorgeous afternoon of sunshine and wine (or beer)!

Wow...so color me surprise!

I usually do not frequent neighborhood pools...the dirty, rude, and usually unattended kids...if I wanted this sort of CDC exposure I'd watch Outbreak and/or visit Atlanta.

But, to my surprise...this free community pool was actually bearable, dare I say, enjoyable?

They have semi-decent/clean changing facilities/bathrooms, a freshwater shower, AND a roped-off-from-the-masses swim lane!

There are two lifeguards on duty and every so often they clear the pool for 5mins. The deep end is an enjoyable 8ft w/a separated @5ft mark "kiddie pool"!

If you live or are visiting the neighborhood (as I was),  check out this rarest of Austin Public Swimming Gems!

This place is an awesome facility to do your Open Water Certification or a refresher course!

The facility has a deep pool to do all your exercises and checkout skills with full equipment rental.

I did my scuba refresher course here with a Groupon for $35 (I believe the reg price is $70) and it was fantastic! The facility is clean and our instructor was very patient and knowledgeable. You get your money's worth in the 4-hr refresher course as well as full on workout!

They also have a scuba club where you can go on different dive trips with your fellow Austin divers.

If you are an active diver or looking to become one this is the place to go in ATX!
#12DaysofChristmasATX

I loved reading O Henry in school, so I was so pleasantly surprised to learn that he had resided in Austin when I moved here. I attended this year’s 40th O Henry Pun Off and it was so much fun! But, the highlight was being able to tour O Henry’s house and learn a little bit more about his personal history. The house tour is free and they have a lot of original items, including some of O Henry’s personal effects. If you are a tourist, native Austinite, or just a nerd like myself, I highly recommend stopping in and checking out this historic house as well as next year’s pun off!

Had a wonderful time hiking across this gorgeous state park!

Jumping across the little water pools and sitting among the waterfalls while dipping your toes is complete bliss!

Parking and finding the trails were not an issue and when we went the park was not as packed as we would have expected on a gorgeous weekend afternoon.

It is an incredibly beautiful and peaceful place so close the hustle and bustle of Austin.
