Whether you are a local or just visiting Austin, I highly recommend a visit here. It is a surprising and wonderful place to soothe your soul (or sole).

Kewl little pueblo to drive through and during the week, especially. The site itself is neat and historical and a quick stop if you want to stretch your legs and learn some area history.

It can get pretty crazy packed with tourists on the weekends, but that is also when a lot of the little pueblo businesses are open. I went on a Tues. and it was pretty much a ghost town.

Stops at the bath house and Soda Dam are a must if you are in the area!

Little park right smack in the middle if the action uptown.

Gorgeous views of the BoA tower and at night is the time to go when it is al lit up and the uptown skyline glitters.

Lots of people walking and playing w-their dogs, and laying on the grass.

Even at night, the park felt very safe, as did that part of uptown.

Also, park was extremely clean w/some of the cleanest restrooms I have ever seem in a city park!

Cooper State Park is awesome because of the available amenities. We camped during a very big storm so the screened shelters came in very handy. We camped at Eagle Point where the shelters were. There was also a big field with a fire pit in the middle. Even better, the restrooms were very close by.

The restrooms were clean considering a public facility or state park. The hand dryer worked, the fan in the restroom worked and even the showers were functioning.

One of the cool things for me was there was electricity in the covered shelter. Even more, the lights worked and there was one outlet inside and another outside. Some of the shelters even had A/C.

The beach area was not so far away and it has 12 covered pavilions, a kid park, a sand volleyball court, a half court basketball court, showers, restroom and a nice beach area. The beach could use a little better and (I'm comparing to Lake Ray Roberts state park).

Overall, a good area and only an hour and a half from Wylie.

I take my scouts here often to hike or to do trail bike-rides. I've even taken a kid's bike trailer that I towed and it fit in all the trails. This is important because while I had an 11 year old passing off his scouting requirements, I couldn't leave my 2 year old at home so he rode along with me in the bike trailer. And the trails were wide enough for it. There were a few difficult spots but for the most part, trailer friendly. Our Scout Troop was also responsible for clearing the trash in 2013.

Update: 5/10/2017: Even after all the rain and flooding a few months ago, the trails are still very hike-able. There were also a lot of trail-bikers there tonight. I love this place, lots of trails and still well maintained. It was a great evening to hike tonight.

Another thing, I've been here several times and have even cleaned up by picking up trash but tonight was the firs time I saw a snake, 2 of them in fact. I didn't know nor even think of having snakes there.

This park is large, lots of open space as well. We were able to put up a badminton net next to one of the soccer fields and there was still enough space.

My 5 year old enjoyed playing in the pirate park which has a large array of swing sets so there's enough room for everyone. There are 4 softball fields (lighted), 2 football fields, 5 soccer fields and two sand volleyball courts.

I was impressed that the sand volleyball courts were both occupied the entire time I was there (2 hours).

There was also a trail around the park. It's also conveniently located next to the Wylie stadium and Wylie HS. Very clean and seemed to be well maintained.

The people here are awesome! They welcomed us, orientated us and then gave us the low-down of the entire area. They were very gracious and friendly. The ranger came out to meet with me because we were doing a service project for them and he was a soft-spoken guy with a welcoming attitude.

This building had clean restrooms, cool decorations and a gift-shop. The outside of the building had some fun decorations as well. We didn't get to see the museum but just talking to the people up front was an indication of how the folks are. Great place, great people and great service!

It was a fun trip, only about 2 hours from Dallas. We enjoyed the scenery enroute there and then taking pictures around the replica of the Eiffel Tower. A fun place. Take the family with your lunch and eat it in the surrounding grass area, the benches or even in your car. The Civic Center is next to it as well.

I especially enjoyed the War Memorial next to it. I did not know about the War Memorial so that was a pleasant surprise. We read the plaques and was very informational. I enjoyed the reverent feeling that permeated the place.

Great place to camp especially for my scouting boys. We used a primitive campsite where there was only running water nearby. It was great and it accomplished our purposes.

The views here is awesome. As flat as Texas is, this canyon is beautiful and is a variation to the great plains that is a part of the Texas landscape.

There are several activities that you can do while at Palo Duro. Just outside of the state park was a place where we got to go ziplining. It cost us $20 per person to do this.

This is the 3rd escape room company I've experienced and each has its own way to differentiate. These guys have a wall to sign when you make it out. The wall is quite crowded. The rooms are well setup, but that's to be expected.

We had 6 teams of 6 and we all fit comfortably. Then we had a gift exchange and they had a large enough room to accommodate all of us.  The hosts were young and gracious. Very inviting and friendly. This is a great place.

Although the beach area is nice, there's a lot of homeless folks that frequent this place. And it is so secluded that I worry about how fast an emergency response can be.

In my latest trip, there were 4 cars with suspicious activities right next to mine and I was stuck there because I was waiting for a tow truck to get my rental. There were men and women just walking around looking scary.

The Port-a-potties were gross and not well kept.

I've been here 3 different times and each time I did something different and it is always a good place to learn about history. This time I took my children and we went on the submarine and that was new for me.

We paid for the digital walking tour so we didn't have a tourguide and it's exactly what we needed because we went at our own pace, sometimes fast and sometimes we stopped to listen to what we were interested in.

We had our family reunion here and it was the first time I've been back for 13 years. Malaekahana State Recreation Area is a great place to camp and have various activities.

The restrooms are clean and well kept for a busy place. The entire area is good and clean. We had approx 100 people from our family reunion at our camp site and it handled it quite well. We even had running water and electricity.

This place was awesome. I loved the lights and the creativity of the whole thing.

The best thing we liked about it was the sledding. They provide simple sleds for free and the lines were not long. We were able to go multiple times.

The entrance and exits were well marked. The inductions on how to sled are quite clear.

The entire experience was fun and spectacular.

Great place to learn about the history of Texas. This marks the spot where Texas won its independence from Mexico. They will give you the history and tour. You will learn about General Santa Ana and others. I thoroughly enjoyed taking my children here.

If you go here, plan to go to the Battleship Texas as it is in the vicinity.

A fun place to hang out. There's a water park and there's a park for the kids to play in as well. There is also a nice open field. I used this place for prom pictures backdrop as well.

Very easy access on eastbound 66. They also have fireworks on 4th of July here. Very versatile location.

We play Ultimate frisbee here and there is a frisbee golf course. There is also a soccer field and a football field. The track is nice. It's a well kept place. We use this place quite often. The only thing to be warned of is it is in a flood area and it will flood in heavy rains.

This is a great place, great park and good location to hang out and just take it easy. This is also where the Arizona Aloha Festival is held every year. There are restrooms and great views of the salt river as well as the Tempe bridge which lights up beautifully at night.

Beautiful and peaceful place. We were able to hang out in Temple Square are. The things we were able to do:
- Go to the Visitor Center
- Go to the former Hotel Utah
- Toured the old Tabernacle

Great place to take pictures and just to feel the spirit of the Lord.

Great place to learn about the history of San Diego as well as the Mormons. Great interactive presentation and I enjoyed the stories that were told. The re-enactment was well done and brought things to life.

Restrooms were well kept and very clean.

I went for a festival put on by the city and I enjoyed the park. I loved the view of the pond and how the park is built around it. The park allowed my 6 year old son something to do while others in my group were able to do their own thing.

Beautiful location and awesome setting. For someone who's never been to Utah before, it was a little difficult to get to in the dead of winter. Luckily, the roads weren't so bad. The Temple itself was beautiful as well as its surroundings.

Loved the history that we were able to learn about. Great Memorial Day Activity for the family. I also enjoyed the grassy area where we had a picnic with my wife and kids. Very nice and beautiful immediate surroundings.

This was a nice park. This was not there 20 years ago when I was living there so it was a nice little area. There were showers to wash off the sand before walking to your car. Good walkway to the car too.
We arrived on a very wet and stormy day and we were happy to find a covered lunch area that we took. The park is big and spaced out and the place we found was quite secluded.
This was an awesome stop. Fun place to take pics and great place to hike or go snow-shoeing. Awesome views and there are well marked signs at the beginning of the trail.
This is a nice park, lots of room to run and a nice pavilion. There was an Asian and Pacific island festival there that I attended and it was very spacious.
A fun place to see and hang out at. Educational as well--there's a plaque you can read up on before entering the vicinity.

There is particular road to go up and very photogenic and good weather. Just wait till you get to a good pull off to pull off and take pictures there's one just short of the top of the dugway.if after going up the dugway you take the very first left you can go to muley point for some additional really spectacular views there's no sign there showing the turn off however. Just take your time and you'll be fine it's not that you can combine it with a tour of the valley of the gods muley point and gooseneck spark for a full day ofyou can combine it with a tour of the valley of the gods muley point and gooseneck Park for a full day of some spectacular touring

Very beautiful area definitely worth a visit and very photogenic. I took the short walk to the cave trail and would not suggested it was particularly worthwhile. Is a little bit uphill but the cave itself not really much to see there. Probably better to do the dripping spring trail if you're going to do some hiking. Keep your eyes open for wildlife saw a deer on the trail as well as some unique birds and other animals

very beautiful State Park. Approximately $6 admission. On the honor system after hours. Combine it with a visit to the Moki dugway as well as muley point valley of the gods for a wonderful day of touring. Nice place for a picnic although not much shelter from the sun. It seemed to be a good place for camping has many people were camping there. Very close to Mexican hat

we went at Socorro fest and with highly recommended. Was on a Friday in a Saturday from about 10:00 in the morning till 10:00 in the evening. Was lots of fun with yummy local food vendors especially the taco vendor is shown in my photos. For five bucks you could get a glass and do wine tasting which is also really fun and enjoy the local bands and music.

not too much to see there. If you go there go early as it's very hot with all the black lava rock. Close to the airport and the energy lab so may want to combine with a tour at the octopus farm or the seahorse farm. They have lectures and classes most everyday in the morning. Also close to the harbor so maybe combined with lunch at the harbor House

Very friendly staff there. Small museum but very helpful and understanding what you're seeing there and then some other Pueblo parks in the area. They have a short 15 minute film that is definitely worth seeing. Free admission and then grabbed one of the pamphlets that explains the short trail that you'll be walking through the ruins themselves

Nice Indian pueblos ruins on the drive between Santa Fe and the Mexican hat area of Utah.very large Grand kiva that's quite impressive to see. Short walk explores the ruins and you walk right through the rooms themselves nice small museum with a nice film that explains what you're seeing well. Definitely worth the stop if you're in the area.

Interesting to visit although it's a long drive from Socorro and the freeway. I visited on the open house which was also the same day that Trinity site was open in October and it makes for a long day but was worth it in my mind. Best to bring a real camera if you want to take pictures as your cell phone camera won't really do it justice

A very enjoyable afternoon particular upside. I would combine it with a visit to the Western Saguaro national Park perhaps for a sunset visit and maybe a little bit of a hiking also. Go early enough so that you see some of the talks and exhibits that you would miss otherwise. For instance The Ray show closes at 4:00 p.m.

Beautiful small spot. Nice to take a few pictures quiet and relaxing in a busy commercial environment. To locate plug in the street address into Google maps pass the location and park in the first parking structure about  $1.75 every 15 minutes. Restaurants do validate should not take long to see it but very pretty

only open to visitors two times a year. Please check out the website for very specific details on how to visit. Was very impressive and can be seen in a relatively short period of time. there really is not much to see there however but is still worth doing at least once in your life.

I really enjoyed this museum and definitely recommend it. Also check out all the outdoor exhibits hopefully when it's not too hot. Definitely worth a couple hours especially if you have kids with you although definitely visit even if you don't

very nice venue. Ironically I live near here for many years but never knew that this playhouse existed. Built 1929 so nice old interior. They have nice fireside concerts here at very reasonable prices in the winter
I visited in the evening when I was dining at Pepper's which is adjacent to the basilica. It was closed at 7:30 p.m. when we went to eat but was lit up beautifully as you can see in these pictures
Sometimes you can snag street parking on Sundays for free with a short walk. Always nice coming here especially on Sundays late when they have a free classical concert at 6 p.m.
Still good after all these years. Was not busy the early evening that I stop by also the ramen place around the corner was really busy. Hot dogs remain good
Beautiful spot at the literal end of the road. Not much parking good for a quick picnic although not much in the way of any formal seating or tables
Beautiful place. Go eat as it can get hot. Some great poppy viewing just before you get to the park. Picnic tables available so bring a picnic.
Not much going on in the off season. Short walk to the bridge site of shot heard round the world....short movie in headquarters house.
Beautiful spot. Love the plantation house for happy hour drinks and sunset. Sensei also great for sushi and late-night discounts
probably one of the best places to park in Yosemite very busy during the summer season. Convenient to food options and store.
Fantastic park. Still enjoy visiting the top even after many prior visits. Can go later in the day & avoid the crowds.
Beautiful especially on a clear winter day. Small snack shop here. Beautiful drive back to PHX or Flagstaff from here
Nice location for some hikes. Park outside the park or a $8 and risk a ticket from the red light cameras
Worth a quick visit if you're in the area. I wouldn't go too far out of the way for it however.

Your experience may vary depending on which tour guide you get to take your around, but this is truly a must see for Phoenix.  To see the raw creativity that Frank Lloyd Wright put into his own house with no client to appease is pretty impressive. It is difficult to not let your own creativity run wild as you stand in the place and see his solutions to simple problems he has to face.  The history and the things to see are very impressive to be a part of, so make sure to stop here.  As said in another review, I now want to go see Taliesin in Wisconsin as well as his other places.

This was a great park to hit up after hours when the lights turned off and play some Friday Night Bee.  Get a light up frisbee and some a bunch of glow sticks. Make a field along the soccer field and then the endzone would be a different colored glowstick. Turn on the frisbee and play ultimate frisbee in the complete dark.  A lot of crashing and fun going on, but a lot of pain too.  Make it less competitive, seriously, and don't keep score.  If one team is dominating, switch up the teams.

It was terrific when it first opened, however it has kind of gone down hill.  They use to pride themselves as being on of 3 aquariums in the world that would house a tiger shark.  Those days are long gone, as tiger sharks don't do well in captivity.  I believe they went through three of them before they stopped.  The tide pool section is fun for kids and the shark tank is cool.  It is probably a half day activity or less, but make sure you eat at some of the restaurants nearby!

This is a terrific park.  Made to look like marshland, it has paths to walk on, select areas of grass to lay down and enjoy the weather, and there is a lack of children running around with the other park down the road with the fountain.  Also, ducks and koi are in the water!  This is a great place for us to enjoy the nice summer days of Portland.  A bonus that it is so close to everything in NW district and is along the Streetcar line

The view was great, but we went in the winter! The skies were clear and you could see Rainier shining in the distance with its snow covered peak.  The view gives you a great perspective about how small this area is as you can see the same mountain that those in Canada can probably see.  Also that that mountain is impressively large.  On a summer day, this park would be idyllic.

This was a wonderful park to walk around.  Going in the Fall, Winter and Spring will mean less changes of mosquitos, but what this place is known for is bird watching.  Look up what birds are around for different times of years. Spring is when we go, as we will see a wide variety of birds out and hear their calls.

As wine goes, Vista Hills is one of our favorites. As a place to visit and tasting rooms go, Vista Hills sets a high bar for wineries in the area.  The building is gorgeous and the rooms are inviting. However, one sunny summer days it can get very crowded and the parking lot can get very full.

This is a very nice square and a great place for the city to come together. Today there was a tuba band playing Christmas songs in the square. The carols and Christmas tree lighting is also another fun event. Take the Portland walking tour and learn more of the history of this place.

A must see on Maui. One of the last undeveloped beaches on the island and it earns its name of Big Beach. Just don't leave valuables in the car.  No showers or bathroom at the beach, so you'll need to drive back towards wailea, but go to Makena Landing for that.

This was the social park for upcountry Maui.  If you lived in Kula and were in a little league sport of some kind, you played here at Keokea park at one point or another.  Also, this is a great park to have large gatherings for birthdays or church/club outings.

This is my personal favorite beach on Maui. We arrive early in the shade of the condo complex to the left, read for the morning, when we warm up we get in the water, dry off and take more sun and before getting burnt we'll go to lunch. Rinse and repeat.

This is an extremely cool thing that Boeing has.  Worth a check out!  Also, they do events so it would be a terrific place to hold a wedding reception or prom!  Unfortunately a prom was there when we wanted to have out wedding reception. Prom won.

This is a terrific tourist spot.  Hanalei is gorgeous for tourists, although if you go during rainy season, it can be very very murky out there.  That can be a drag, but the pier is still cool to see since it is in movies so often!

The clearest water in the Hawaiian islands is here. Go on a boat adventure tour, I recommend Trilogy as you'll get to sail, and come scuba diving or snorkeling. With the amount of traffic here, it can be sparse of fish at times.

The venue was a great place to hold an alumni get together for our college.  I imagine no matter the occasion, it is a great venue.  For people not familiar with the area, it can be confusing and does require street parking.
This is where I learned to surf! We use to come here on Sundays with the church and have a big potluck and all of the old timers would teach the kids to surf. This is a super fun spot.
This is where I learned to surf! We use to come here on Sundays with the church and have a big potluck and all of the old timers would teach the kids to surf. This is a super fun spot.
The park is beautiful and it is a great place to go camping.  As a kid, I loved coming up here for hiking around, and I'm sure other kids would too.  It was a family favorite of ours.
We had a blast doing the Portland walking tour. The guides were very knowledgable and you get a great walk. It last 2 hours and you get to see some great things around Portland.
Amazing place to visit to show respect to those that have fallen. Looking at this from satellite images after having been there helps to see the full scale of this as well.
I love this park. The views from the top on a clear day are astounding. It really let's you see how small of a rock Maui is. Also, it looks like Mars up in the crater.
The view is gorgeous and once you made it this far, go a little further. The reward is great. Plus this is a popular bathroom stop.
Everyone of my reviews here are five stars. This whole area is incredible. You could spend days exploring this place.
This is a great park for the community.  It has some great trails for running or walking and fields for play.
Not a bad bowling alley in North Spokane! I came here for a class during Jan Term while I went to Whitworth.

The Science behind Pixar exhibit is amazing. We spent nearly 2 hours in that exhibit alone- we went at 9 am and for the first hour it was just us in the exhibit so I recommend booking that time slot if you’re interested in listening to and experiencing all of their stations. At 10 am when the next group of people entered there were so many kids and people it was too loud to listen to the videos and enjoy the exhibit.

We stayed at the museum from opening to close and we were able to visit everything that was open except the planetarium exhibit.

The guy who checked us in (he was wearing a Mike from monsters inc mask today) was really friendly and even recognized us when we re-entered after visiting the food court.

The food court food was actually good! We were worried about having to leave to eat somewhere else to come back but the falafel plate was okay and was the most decently priced meal of our trip. We were pleasantly surprised - especially after reading reviews about how the food court food wasn’t that great .
dislikes: Crowded and noisy (later in the day)

reviews_attraction.text:
A sketchy but beautiful  park.  The park is a nice size, with two play grounds, a basket ball court and a couple soccer fields. My friend and I wanted to go for an evening walk outside so we decided to stop at this park. When we pulled up to the parking lot we noticed a lot of parked cars but the park seemed empty. There was a man working on an RV in the parking lot that seemed broken down and like it had been there for a long time. Another car was filled with teens getting high. At the other end of the park there was a tent with someone living in there. We decided to walk up on the sidewalk parallel to the park- big mistake. On the opposite side of the embankment were plenty of homeless tents. We felt uncomfortable and unsafe because there was a teen on a bike who road by us holding a rifle.

The park itself is beautiful but it’s in the ‘hood’. I wouldn’t feel comfortable going alone or bringing my family here.

I loved visiting this museum - many works from some of my favorite artists were featured which was lovely to see.

We arrived early and were parched from our walk and unfortunately we had to wait till 11 am for a cafe at the courtyard to open to purchase water- it was our only option to since all of the water fountains are currently closed and you can’t bring in any of your own water. It didn’t seem right that none of the gift shops or anywhere else had water available.

When you first enter- I recommend watching a short movie in their theatre about Ulysses S. Grant to help set the scene- it was very interesting.
Ranger Shawn gave us an amazing tour of the home of Ulysses S Grant. He also stuck around after the tour and gave us valuable information about what other National Park sites to visit. We weren’t expecting to have such an amazing time. Also I got a cancellation stamp for my National Park passport book.

We went up the arch today - the tickets were $14 each plus a $2 convenience fee- be sure to book online. You are allowed 10 minutes at the top and you are given 2 windows to look through so you can see both sides of the arch.

They also had 2 professional photographers stationed in front of green screens where they photoshop you in front of the arch and various other places in the museum- the complete photo package is $49.

We loved visiting Applewood. We did both the gardens tour as well as the house tour. The gardens tour is everyday at noon and does not require a reservation. We really loved our personalized tour with Becky and I think the other girls name was Wendy but I’m not sure. They are very passionate about where they work at.

Tracy gave us a great tour of the inside of the house and he was very passionate  and informative.

This is the largest national park in the lower 48. It has so much to offer. There is even a Joshua tree forest in case you’re unable to make it to Joshua tree national park.

If you have a national parks pass make sure you stop by the ranger station because they will give you an orange paper for your windshield to show you’ve been verified.  This is also how you can obtain a map of the park.

A creation by the extremely talented and missed Leonard Knight who created what was originally supposed to be a temporary monument and is now a landmark. He created this place with his own two hands and forage what he could from the local dump as well as donations. Today it’s maintained by friendly volunteers. Definitely worth a visit! There’s also a friendly cat that lives there.

We loved visiting this aquarium. It’s good for all ages- fine for people in groups or alone. This place is perfectly set up for social distancing and has markers on the ground so you can go in one direction and be able to see everything. We really enjoyed watching the turtles in the spiral tank swim around clumsily. The workers were also friendly.

It’s a family owned and operated business which is great! We did the Cupid’s escape room (seasonal for Valentine’s Day). I thought it was just okay. It was a shorter and easier version then I guess their hour long rooms. But for $15 it wasn’t bad. I would be willing to try one of their hour long rooms to see if they’re any better.

What a great museum! I wasn’t expecting it to be so large and interesting. It was a rare  rainy day today which made it perfect to visit the museum.
Right now they have a special exhibition for black history month

Tip:Don’t forget your student ID or do what we did and purchase a pass for two people on living social for $14 :)

This park is gorgeous.  We loved walking around and exploring.

I did see some people feeding bread to the ducks- please do NOT do this- not only does it pollute the water but it’s also very unhealthy for the ducks- if you want to feed the ducks please feed them nuts, cracked corn, lettuce, and peas.

This is my second time visiting this museum. We came especially to see the Marvel exhibit. It was very interesting. They are following social distancing procedures and there are hand sanitizing stations. It is mandatory to wear a mask while inside the museum.

If you are silent while standing on the golf course you can hear a metallic ‘clinking’ sound of the salt pinnacles as they reacts to the heat.

Be careful if you decide to walk around  because the ground is hard and rough it is easy to sprain an ankle.

A gorgeous open air art exhibit that’s donation based. The locals that live in East Jesus may look intimidating but they were so friendly, kind, and explanatory. You’re free to touch everything and explore - just be respectful to the exhibits.

Came to Santa Fe but wasn’t sure what exactly to do in this sleepy city. Luckily meow wolf is here! I didn’t know what quite to expect but was pleasantly surprised. Great for both adults and children and plenty of instagramable areas to see.

You can get a nice view of the dam from here. There was a nice large parking lot and a picnic table as well as restrooms.  Be aware- There’s a sign stating that black vultures are known to damage vehicles in the parking lot.

It gets HOT during the day. Wear proper footwear and bring water if you plan on seeing the larger dunes further back.

You’re allowed to explore all over the sand dunes - you do not need to follow a specific trail.

One of those awesome Route 66 finds. I spoke to the owners wife she is so friendly. This place is open to the public so you can come right in- they have a well when you enter that you can drop your donations in.

Pleasantly surprised by what this park has to offer the community. Plenty of picnic areas, benches, shade, play ground, tennis court, skate park, basket ball courts, dog park, pool.

Best of all it was clean !
Came here to relax and wasn’t disappointed. It was nice and clean with many families and dog owners walking around. Lots of ducks, turtles, and a variety of birds hanging around the pond as well.
We came here on a snowy day October 30th. It was absolutely beautiful. Unfortunately parts of the sidewalks were closed so it wasn’t very pedestrian friendly.

It’s a hole in a rock- it doesn’t even look like a skull 💀. Underwhelming but still nature
is beautiful. Don’t go out of your way for this one.
A beautiful park to visit on a date, with family, or alone. The animals all looked very well taken care of. You can even feed a giraffe for $6
Lovely clean place to walk around with plenty of areas to sit. You can view the Statue of Liberty from here.

I like this Zoo. There are reviews that say the food is horrible and expensive.  I had a hotdog and it was good. I know that part of the cost of the food is covering costs of the zoo. I pay because I love zoos. I started coming to this Zoo over 50 years ago. It is such better. The animals have dirt and trees and enrichment unlike the past when everything was concrete. If you don't want to pay for food,bring your own. This is a beautiful area.

The area is breathtaking for a downtown area.  The square is clean and is always in transition.  Different seasons bring different flowers.  Christmas season is amazing because they have several outdoor Nativity scenes. The reflection pool is amazing when there are floating lights.  There are many many lights between Thanksgiving and New Years.  It is cold, but worth bundling up to visit.

My Dad and I spent hours on this building. Many of the pioneer tools used for blacksmithing were the same tools his father used. It was an awesome walk down memory lane for him. He also saw exhibits of floor installation tools that were like the ones he had used, only older. It was awesome. No photography allowed.

I found peace walking around, even though there was construction going around the park. I invite anyone to visit. There are summer and winter  hours posted. I will go back during the spring and summer to capture different faces of the park.

It was quiet. It is not the most modern state park and is is very small, but it was beautiful weather. As for the smell, it was and the bugs... Best time to visit is spring. There is a salty smell because it is a SALT LAKE. It has history.

This is amazing. There are restrictions due to COVID, but so wonderful. Took my 86 year old father and he was able to  tell me stories about the tools he used.  The docent was soooo knowledgeable and freely shared he time and knowledge.

The temple is closed to patrons during the renovations. However, the Visitors Center is open with great information about the initial construction, purpose of the temples and plans for renovations. Very worth the stop.

Must see. Amazing history. I visited in the late 80s and it has improved significantly. Be prepared to climb some stairs, but you will want to see the attic. The original timbers and construction methods can be seen.
This place is awesome.  I didn't take pictures because I felt I was actually in someone's home. The docent was knowledgeable and presented a story that ensured the Clayton legacy will live on.
I love watching the animatronic Lincoln. I was very young when I first saw him. It is always a treat for me to see the show and to watch the movies and read the plaques in the waiting area.
Nothing more to say. This was awesome for us And our canine child. He is a water hater, and we but did get his paws wet. It was his second time in 3 months visiting the ocean. LOVED it.
One of my favorite green spaces in Salt Lake City.  It is clean.  There is a playground for children.  Lots of space for dogs and owners.  There is also a community garden each summer.
The visitor museum has great knowledge about the history of integration in schools. It shares the ugly side of the South's segregation it history. Must see for history buffs.
Enjoyed the ride up the canyon. They have a train that seniors can ride free. Others pay $2. Also have an elevator that makes the Eagle's Nest accessible to everyone.
Loved the story behind the house. SO took the tour and found it very interesting. It was $6.50 entrance. We got there just before it closed. Cute setup.
Stop here for information about canyon lands. Across the street is a view point that you can walk to for a real idea of what the Colorado River can do.
Wow. I was amazed. It is on a dirt road, but worth the trip. It is just a few miles from Highway 7. The turn from Hwy 7 comes up sudden so be prepared.
So clean and well managed.  The volunteer at the butterfly house was knowledgeable and shared her knowledge and experience with us. It was amazing.
Clean and safe. Prices are "Disney" andany like things can be found at box stores for much less. It is a wonderful experience. It is fun and open.
This was spectacular. We enjoyed the majestic views. I will post pictures, but first hand is the only way to truly get a scope of the size.
Love Petit Jean.  There are hikes and a lake.  The lake has been cleaned up and is beautiful. Great for camping and picnicking.
Very nice history of the peoples of this area. Unfortunately, the site was sold for farm land. It is a great little museum
I love this park.  The walk to Bridal Veil Falls is safe and well traveled.  It is also long enough to be a good exercise.
Small museum, but has great atmosphere. People there can tell the history of the fort and the equipment at the museum.
It takes effort to get to this park. It is well worth the trip. There is dry camping available,  but very limited.

I've been going here since literally as long as I can remember. It is a beautiful facility. Very educational visitor center, with lots of little exhibits great for kids. They also have a lot of programs, including a lot that are great for kids. When I was younger, I took several programs while I was still in school. I visited the nature center yesterday, and it bought back do many sweet memories :). Oh, and don't forget to hike some trails while here, if you can. They have a very nice trail system with a variety of habitats. Yesterday I walked the River Walk trail, and it was absolutely beautiful walking along that trout run stream, as well as peacefully resting by the Kalamazoo River. And to conclude, on the way out I bought some of their delicious syrup. Trust me, it's worth the money!

Absolutely beautiful out here! The rocks remind and canyon remind me of being out in Colorado. The boardwalk is wobbly in some places, otherwise trails are easy to walk down. The rocks near the river are easily accessible, so therefore, this is a very photo friendly location. The walk back to the Canyon Falls doesn't take very long, and you can see the beautiful canyon that gives them their name.

It's amazing just looking at the engineering here. I kept imagining how long it took to make "the locks" while I was here. I had no idea how big barges are until I came here. They're massive, a few stories high and hundreds of feet long. It's very fun watching them come in, then find out what ship it is to find out where it came from and what it transports.

I like to explore random areas that I've never been to. Today, I explored this place. It's very nice and quiet, perfect for the nature lover, like me. Lots of hunting opportunities here, as well as hiking and birding. It was a very peaceful trip here today. I think the birding is probably really good here in summer, but even today there was good variety.

It's not a very big place, but it's so nice! Scenic, quiet and peaceful, with mostly well maintained trails. This place is also great for birders like me. I was surprised how many birds were here today: Winter Wrens, Yellow-rumped Warblers, lots of Woodpeckers, and so on. The shrubs, berries and water is what attracts the birds at this time of year.

It's a cool park. There's a very cool little playground with water that comes out. That's a first for me to see in the Kalamazoo area. Also, there's tons of space here to do sports and other recreational activities. Morrow Lake is adjacent to this park. Morrow Lake has always given me the creeps, but it's cool seeing the power plant.

Came to the state park as for a daytrip on the  27th. It has been a long time since I'd been here. On the way out, I had to stop by the beach for old times sake. It brought back great memories. It was super quiet, actually one of the quietest landscapes I've seen in months. Such a clean beach too. Please keep it clean!

The last park I stopped at while in the area. Very pleasant park with a nice bridge and paved trail that takes you from one end of the island to the other. It is very clean too, actually it's nearly spotless! I was impressed! It was nice enjoying an A & W Root Beer Float here :)

This is a very nice state park! I love that you can walk along the river for quite a ways. Also, one thing stood out to me: The trees. There's a lot of Sycamore Trees here, and some of them are massive, the biggest I've ever seen! This alone makes this place worthy of visiting!

I really enjoyed stopping by this place while in the area. I didn't realize how big the Arkansas River is until coming here. It appears to be a very good vantage point for fishing, and sometimes, birding. There's a good sized parking space here thats very convenient.

This is one of the better places in the Midwest to look for birds. It's really stunning how many birds you can find here. There were warblers everywhere when I came here today. The trails are also very nicely maintained. The pier is also very cool.

We drove past this place on the way to our hotel, and decided to check it out on our last day of the trip. This place is cool! The sculptures here are very detailed, it must've taken a long time to get all of these! There's plenty of them to see.

Nice walking area right on the river. There's definitely some nice flowers to see back here, even at this time of year. Could be cleaned up in some places. The best access here is the south end of the parking lot at the Comstock Community Center.
This place is wonderful! Had previously heard about it and decided to come here today. It's a very nice preserve with nice trails and a ton of wildlife, or at least when I was there. Totally awesome!
While on vacation, I stopped by a section of this beautiful forest thats in the Waldron Area. Absolutely gorgeous out here! Very quiet, with an amazing, natural piney smell filling the clean air.
This was my Plan B after being rained out at Don Robinson. Cool state park for sure, beautiful and right on the Merimac River. It was continously raining, but we were still able to walk around.
This place is awesome for birding! There's a ton of habitat for just about any type of bird! Beautiful too! I just love hearing the distant song of a Northern Bobwhite while here :)
Relaxing park right in the middle of Portage with a nice, multi-use paved trail. I love eating a takeout lunch at a picnic table here or taking a bike ride down the trail.
Everything about this place is awesome! The scenery from the lodge and the overlooks are breathtaking! The visitors center is very nice and so is the lodge.
Stopped by whil in the area. Its a very beautiful park! It was very clean while I was here, and the trails were very nice and we'll maintained.
Pretty park. Would be great to enjoy a lunch or picnic at. And if you like birding there were lots of ducks on the lake when I was here today.
One of the coolest parks I've ever seen! It's huge, and it's beautiful, with something to do for everyone. Why can't more parks be like this?
A very pretty, quiet park right on the Grand River. I love the little fish and tulips sculpture. This park would be great for a picnic.
There's so much to see here it's almost overwhelming! The rock formations are so beautiful! There really is no other place like this.
Small beach with good views of the lake. Saw some sketchy people hanging out here which made me leave quickly.

Kansas City was lucky in the old days, when folks like Nelson and Atkins were around.  You just do not see that sort of dedication to the Arts anymore, unless you look to the folks that manage The Nelson.  Recently, it seems there is always something new to discover, and they continue to make improvements to presentation and the type of artifacts on display.

This is a world-class Art Museum right in the MidWest, and a tourist destination if ever there was one... but The Bloch building is still an ugly warehouse.  Who thought that was a good idea, placing such a terribly bland piece of architecture next to such a beautiful old building?

Beautfiul!  Absolutely gorgeous!  This is a fantastic place to enjoy the Gunnison River for fishing, hiking, or just a little boating around the area.  We were only passing through, but we really enjoyed it, stopping for a hike out to Dillon Pinnacles, and then on to the Pine Creek Trail for the Morrow Point Boat Tour of the Black Canyon of the Gunnison.  The Morrow Point Boat Tour was awesome and a must see!

Well kept park and architecture from the 1800s and a great place to learn about the surrender of the North Arkansas Army to the Union Army, and a bit about the inland steamboat history of the region.  The person on post is usually torn between duty at the courthouse and at the gift shop, so if you don't find anyone at one of those spots, check the other!

Interesting place for a quick detour along the route, to learn a bit about the Civil War in Missouri.  Beware though!  Google Maps will steer you wrong, if you try to come in from the East... and their signage is seriously lacking.  You can drive right by it and miss it.  The only sign is at the entrance.

One of the best State Parks in Missouri, with great trails and interesting sites to see.  It is a bit more crowded these days, but if you go for the seemingly less interesting trails, you can avoid much of that.  The castle ruins are no longer accessible, but you can get up close still.

Always a great place to go an relax by the cascades of Collins Creek. It is usually a bit crowded in the late spring and summer, since it is such an easy hike and the perfect spot to get out from the heat without going inside.  1/2 mile trail is wheel chair accessible at a few points.

This is a clean and well-kept park, but really nothing more than a rest stop in the middle of nowhere.  The formations have been ignored too long and are completely covered in graffiti.  The State Park service really should put a little more effort into preserving this spot.

A must-see fantastic piece of art work.  It has become a bit of a tourist side-show in the last few years, but remains and outstanding example of what one man can do when he sets his mind to it.  Always interesting to see what has been added lately!

Quite a hike to the top!  Dropped in here to see this interesting geologic feature, and make the the climb to the top.  I definitely recommend this as an early morning or early evening hike though, as the Texas sun will beat you down any other time.

A great little architectural spot that you can't miss, if you are wandering Michigan Avenue.  Access to the waterfront park below from there, or stop and take a photo with the river.  It can be a little congested in the day time for that though...

I liked it so much, I stopped in twice; once on my way from, and again on my way back to KC!  The waterfalls area fantastic, but be aware of how far you hike up them... you gotta come back under that unforgiving Texas sun.  :)

A great little spot to stop in and get away from it all in the middle of town, hosting an Amphi-Theater, playground, paved walking paths, tennis courts, skateboard court and lot and lots of shade trees, and mostly enclosed.

A great little diversion off the beaten path in Kansas, hosting the 2nd largest electric coal shovel in the world, along with a quaint little museum of artifacts, and various other vintage mining equipment.

Absolutely LoveThis Place!  There is so much great art here, both temporary and the completely permanent (as in architecture).  The building is beautiful inside and out... A MUST SEE if you are in Chicago!

Well-kept little park at a rather busy intersection in the northland.  The only thing to be wary of is the occasional hobo hiding behind the Vet's memorial.  It is a great place for a lunch walk or run.

An interesting stop, but really disappointing that something like this on the National Register of Historic Places is being let fall to ruin... it is probably not one of the more safe places to visit.
Awesome state park in the heart of Texas, with some fantastic waterfalls, if you are up to a relatively easy 2.5 km hike.  Just be ready to semi-repel down to them over that last 100 meters or so.
Interesting National Park, most of which is within the City and comprised of the Old bathhouses with interesting architecture, and a good way to spend an afternoon.
Awesome view of the Pacific and San Diego, well kept and an interesting piece of Portuguese-American History.  If you do nothing else in San Diego, drop in here!
Arkansas really knows how to take care of their parks.  We only hiked down to the falls, and that trail was utterly exhausting, but had a great time doing it.
One of the few places in the Midwest that you can still go get lost in the woods.  Waterfalls, Bluffs, Cliffs, clear running water, and solitude, for now.
Great place to go learn a little about Missouri's past... beautifully maintained grounds, museum inside, and plenty of other historical bits nearby.
Really nice little State Park, with a variety of walking trails from easy to moderate.  Visitor Center is small, but has a nice display.
Lots of sights to see, spread across the area.  Perfect for hiking around in the off season, before the paddlers converge.
Love these little stops along the road.  A great place to get out, walk around, and learn a little history.

stop here 9-26-17 at one of my most favorite overlooks on the parkway is graveyard fields located at milepost 418.8. not only do you have this stunning views but you can do a short hike doing down to the lower falls and a second hike just a little longer to the upper falls. i didn't have time to go the the upper falls but take a left out of the parking lot as just around the bend you can see the upper falls from the roadside. if you hike to the upper falls than the lower falls and back to the parking lot the loop is 2.9 miles. at one time between 500 to 1000 years ago the was a spruce forest that was burned down leaving dirt mounds and the forest did return but fires got it again in 1925. this spot is very popular and there are bathrooms. if you only have time to see one thing on the parkway. this would be an excellent pick

i was on may way to collins creek trail and saw this huge dam said wow. just before the turn to the trail i saw the memorial & overlook sign and got excited. once i got there the excitement left. i really hate to say this but the memorial site is unloved. there was only one small information sign up and that was badly faded. there were framed glass were they put other information and they were empty. the bust was gone. there was nothing at all there that gave you any impression that this was a memorial to one of the greatest presidents this nation as ever had. as a memorial this was the saddest i have ever seen but the overlook is very nice and is why this gets one star. i would be a shamed if this was a memorial in my town.

i stop here this pass january to hike the branch falls trail but had to drive around to check out the ground. it seem like a very nice place to enjoy some camping and lake fun. i stop at the visitor center and was great by a very nice young man that was friendly and fun to chat with. i found 2 bags of chocolate gray and he said that people in arkansas like to put it on their biscuits for breakfast so i had to buy the last 2 bags and bring it back home to NY for my family to try. he said he didn't like it because it made them too sweet but like the american pickers said when you find something different its the time to buy. lol well he and another employee of the park made my visit that more fun. thank you

i did this hike early in the morning and on my way look who i bumped into, YOGI! after talking with yogi i started on the dirt road made you wonder if i was going to find a still. lol. i really like this hike because once you get to the falls you really feel like you are in the middle of nowhere. the gps did help me get there and i used alltrails not mark my trail so i didn't get lost.  i wouldn't do this hike without having plenty of daylight because i feel it would be easy to get lost. the falls was really nice and peaceful watching the sun break through the frog. but you will be surprise on how easy to take a wrong turn leaving the falls. i did so i left on a different road than i came in

i'm not a beach kind of guy so my rating not comparing it to other beaches. its base on the time me and my son had together walking on the beach, trails and the sandbar. watching him enjoining himself on the sandbar is a 10 star rating. walking picking up seashells and feeding the birds was priceless. swing in the late night warm water was the cherry on top. people are pigs. in the parking lot the trash cans were overflowing was what to they do throw it on the ground. not the parks fault but the brainless lazy ass people. so if you are one of these type of people go to a public pool. that's were you belong the beach was clean.

I LIKE SEEING OLD HOUSES AND THIS ONE IS NICE BUT ONLY A 3 ROOM TOUR. ITS A SELF GUIDED TOUR BUT THE YOUNG MAN AT THE DESK WILL GIVE YOU THE HISTORY OF ROBERT AND THE HOUSE. HE WAS EXCELLENT AND NEW HIS STUFF AND IF HE DIDN'T HE TOOK THE TIME TO LOOK IT UP. THE UPSTAIRS TO THE HOUSE ISN'T OPEN UNTIL THEY ADD AN EXIT IN CASE OF FIRE. IF U TIE THE PARK-MCCULLOUGH HOUSE, THE BENNINGTON BATTLE MONUMENT AND THE HENRY COVERED BRIDGE YOU CAN HAVE A NICE LITTLE DAY TRIP ALL WITH IN 19 MINUTES  (7.9 MILES) OF EACH OTHER. BUT CALL OF THE  HOURS  OF OPERATION FIRST. ALSO MAKE SURE THE ELEVATOR IN THE MONUMENT IS OPEN.

unlike NY. CT. values their old homes. CT has so meaning historical house its one of the best states in the New England area. which makes Webb-Deane-Stevens Museum a wonderful stop. not only do you have the museum but the surrounding area is loaded with old homes which makes a great walk around town. the guides are very nice, litrtle gift shop and a very nice historical house that is now a restaurant. even my 12 year old enjoyed it. this in my book is a must to see. i hope you feel the same. in this post there will be a few picture of the restaurant and other homes that are near by.

THIS IS A 10 STAR TRAIL. NOT ONLY ARE YOU HIKING TO A AWESOME WATERFALL THE TRAIL IS FUN AND BEAUTIFUL. THE TREES, MOSS, ROCKS ALONG THE CREEK IS NOTHING BUT EYE CANDY. I HIKE IT ON A COOL, CLOUDY, LIGHT RAIN JANUARY DAY WITH NO SOUND BUT THE CREEK, WOODY PECKER AND MY OWN FEET. THE BEAUTY OF THE TRAIL MADE THE DAY PREFECT. ALL THIS AND A WATERFALL. TO ME THIS IS A HIKERS DREAM.  IF YOU NEED MORE THERE IS A PICNIC AREA SO WHAT ARE YOU WAITING FOR PACK UP THE WIFE AND KIDS AND MAKE A MEMORY IN THIS BEAUTIFUL PLACE THAT YOUR KIDS WILL TALK ABOUT WELL AFTER YOU LEAVE THIS EARTH.

The bald face Mountain Overlook is another long-range view of the valley Valley with the mountains in the background. The day I went the clouds were low and in the distance look like they were on top of the mountains. Kind of cool to see the land meet the clouds. There is an opening between the wall and just a few feet Beyond the Wall is a great Rocky Point which if you take pictures correctly it will make it look like you climb to a summit. This Outlet is located at milepost 61 point zero and is at elevation 3325.

Trade foot Mountain Overlook stop. you get ball hair that the other overlooks offer but I was happy they did not cut down this one dead tree. I know some people hate trees that they feel are in the way when they're trying to take pictures of overlooks. Not me. To me they add character and I'm glad the Skyline Drive left this tree alone. If you would like to add this to your trip you can find it at milepost marker 87. 0 at an elevation level of 2575. Enjoy the drive

Fort Mountain State Park is a super nice park with over 3,700 acres in georgia that is located between Chatsworth and Ellijay in the fort mountain. it was founded in 1938 & named for an ancient 885 foot long rock wall that is located on the peak for and easy trail to hike. there is also a great overlook and a gorgeous stone tower. this park i enjoyed very much last fall and a great spot for a family picnic with sites to see and history.

i love everything about this falls and park. the last time i went was in November on a nice sunny day and it was still pretty. trail to the falls with the leaves on the ground was still a nice walk and there was still a lot pf people there. can you imagine what it would be like during the summer and fall . well, this place is great for the whole family i even saw people in wheelchairs enjoying this trail to the falls

took a 2 month trip down south and i love route 64. the best drive in all North Carolina i have ever been on and i have done some driving. these all these great falls here that i was seeing and i drove pass this place. well who in there right mind doesn't like a covered bridge so i hit the breaks and we stop here for 20 minutes or so. it was a beautiful day and stopping here make it better.

i'll make this simple. this is a must do!!!!! I love everything about this trail. it's a very easy and short hike. Not only is the summit is beautiful. It's that much better from the fire tower. The trail itself is just as beautiful. Great rock formations and tree roots growing over the rocks and trail. The worse thing about this trail is that it's short.

Hemlock Falls Trail is a 1.1 mile heavily trafficked out and back trail located near Trenton, Georgia that features a waterfall and is rated as moderate. The trail is primarily used for hiking, walking, nature trips, and bird watching and is best used from March until October. Dogs are also able to use this trail but must be kept on leash.

nice museum and film. the lady behind the desk was a fast talker and wanted to move on to other things besides talk to me. this was on feb 4th and i was the only one there. so it wasn't like she had other visitor to take care of. anyways i don't take away star for so so employees. this is a good historical place to visit.

stop here on my way to a friends house. what a great place the house were wonderful to see and the trees on the ground surrounding the house were awesome.  had lunch there with i couple i meet and we chatted for 2 hours. great people. but what i found amazing was you could feel the peace in the air. a must see

High Shoals Falls is a tremendous 2.3 mile heavily trafficked out and back trail located near Hiawassee, Georgia that features a waterfall and is rated as moderate. The trail is primarily used for hiking, walking, and nature trips and is accessible year-round. Dogs are also able to use this trail.

another super find. if you take the time you can find gems like this all throughout NY. Knox's Headquarters State Historic Site & Revolutionary War Site.  built in 1754. take the time to look at each old build you see and you'll find something different in each home.

this is an outstanding overlook and trail head. there is a second trail head in the park. either way it is a very easy and gorgeous trail, scenic spot, overlook and a stone gazebo. don't miss out on this gem.
The skyline and all the hikes and overlooks are great. Not one spot I visit I thought wasn't worth while. The drive is a great place to spend the day or a week. There is so much to see
a nice place to eat your lunch and pick up some gifts from the gift shop. talking with the staff gave us a lot of information and pleasant conversation.
i love this tour because you can take all the time in the world to see a great cave at your pace. the tour  guides are at station throughout the cave.
this is a wonderful spot. you have a nice park, lighthouse, beach and a place you can have weddings with a 100 year old carousel.
Canyonlands is my favorite out of the mighty 5. it has it all and so peaceful.  don't miss this national park!

Cornelius Falls is also home to Bridal Veil Falls. You can carefully explore the area above Cornelius by walking dow. The steps and turning right. There you'll see 2 small falls and they have these black shale slopes that are calming to hear and nice in black and white photos.
The paths down to view Cornelius are steep, but there are 2 options.  Steep and then switchback style.  Its slick either way, so be careful. And then getting to Bridal Veil is either a walk downhill around the back of the park or along the streambed walking away from Cornelius then taking a left at the 1st stream merge and walking up to Bridal Veil.  There is a down tree so be mindful and we took to it's right.  And there is just a nice and calm place to sit and enjoy the fall amongst rocks and boulders.  The way out is up the hill to the left of you're looking at the falls.  You can even just go back to the steps or take the path to the parking area.

One cannot Express how cool the Lodge at Mount Magazine is because ots just an amazing, rustic, skyview.  Get a room with a balcony and thank me later!  The food and cocktails are phenomenal and there is an indoor pool and game room.  There are trails, including an easy hike to the highest point in Arkansas. And Cameron bluff isnt very far.  They have bike rentals and that is worth it.  There aren't hard core mountain biking trails inside the park, but they ate close.  And when you go, though its steep, go straight down hill from the restaurant and visit "the Tree."

Mississippi River State Park is 5 stars not because its has everything, but because you dont.  The Visitors Center is a great place to learn about the resource of the river and ecosystem. There is a walking trail there and you can get some provisions without having to go back to town.

You can fish, bring a small boat, camp on the peninsula, bike ride quite a ways, and there is another lake further south.  Kayak amongst the cypress, and there are bathhouses and RV hookups.  And the VC offers interpretive programming, too.  The waterfowl here is dense and glorious.

This museum in McGehee is a powerful place to see how the Japanese were effected inside the USA by World War 2.  The displays are moving and it will cause a silence inside you to see the war's affect on people of Arkansas.  Nearby is the sister site, Rowher, that will also bring it home that these citizens lived an unexpected time unbenonced to us today.  It's all very quiet and, believe it or not, Sulu, from Star Trek lived here for some of his childhood.  And he made it from here all the way to Hollywood.  Crazy and inspiring.

The interpretive exhibits definately help someone understand the history of the area and are top notch and well executed.  There is a projector that shows the history of the geography. There is a video that explains the rivers and how it influences the history of Jacksonport and Newport. The architecture is full of Easter eggs and emphasizes the White River.  The VC enhances the experience of Jacksonport in good ways.  Plus they have a rentable meeting space with a small kitchen and beautiful views.

Beautiful park in Little Rock that has a bit of everything for anyone.  Slightly secluded and large, Allsopp has forest trails, tennis, a softball field, swings, a playground, picnic areas, a pavilion, and parking. Also, having lived in the area, there are no sidewalks in the neighborhood - just along the street. So, this place offers a safe place to enjoy being outside. Plenty of nature and the trails are lengthy for an urban park. You could walk all the way to Hillcrest!

Only speaking about the disc golf course, which is located in the very back behind Dupree lake.
It it a good challenge course.  Definately could use a clean up effort, but it was underwater when we flooded in June of 2019.  Little overgrown and inconsistently marked, so take a photo of the map to gind your way.  Launch pads are concrete and there are fairway details, but need cleaning and touch up.  No trash bins along the way, so leave no trace! But, a good challenge.

This is an Arkansas state Park that teaches and supports and lives coservation. There are camping areas, a Pavillion, an educational visitors center, and trails for walking in the woods. Plus this park was as significant as hot springs at one time. The city of Magnolia is very close, which offer more urban amenities, but the park is enough off the road that your only outside noise is a train off in the distance.

Knopp park is simple - you have to get to it to walk through it and you'll find a unique and beautiful view of downtown Little Ro k once you do. It's a great out of the way place to kick back with a book, hammock, or picnic. It's made from local rocks reminiscent of the CCC era. There are no bathrooms and it is a loop trail connected around the water plant, where there is parking from sunrise to sunset.

Pam's grotto is a boulder haven. This is my second post and I say just walk up the creek directly if you can and there is water, because there are many pools and cascades to greet you on your way up to the big falls. You can even go up and around to the left (if your looking at the falls, but be careful as you do this as its slippery, but you can get above the falls to a pool. Just watch the edge!

This place amazes me and has been there for my entire life.  Just seeing them evolve and make new homes for animals is impressive. They are open every single day! And watching these animals have a great life, training, and study warns my heart.  They do so much with so little, but keep growing for the betterment if the animals.  Kudos to this place and Eureka Springs is a good home for them.

This park is a Nature Conservancy agreement with Arkansas State Parks. There is so much untouched land here and it needs to be experienced.  Luckilly, the park has programs to enjoy the area and there are campgrounds and plenty of kayaking possibilities. It does have class 4 waters, so be careful in your planning.   Do go to the Cossatot campgrounds to see the rocks and picnic.

This Arkansas State Park showcases the cotton industry in central Arkansas.  I learned what boll weavals actually ate and where the terms "high cotton" and "fair to midlan" come from.
It's a great place to go see how a cotton gun actually works. Toltec is north if you want to see how the native Americans worked these soils, too.

This place is fantastic. Sandy beach in Arkansas to relax, swim, and walk with a nice view of the lake...its just really pleasant.  The treeline for some reason stands out to me and offers shade and color.  We also saw one of the best 4th of July firework displays there period. Well, really it's an exclamation!

Nice big park in Heber Springs.  We went for a non existant farmers market, but saw a big playground, 2 arenas, public bathrooms, pavilions, and lots of walking trail.  There is even a little false creek feature that is a nice touch.  Dig friendly and set in a nice neighborhood, so those residents are lucky.

Love seeing Hot Springs from above and afar.  Seeing the scope and looking at the history of the city on a micro scale is a fun addition to the overall experience of a visit to Hot Springs.  Plus, the drive up is nice and there are trails below to explore. Go up to the tower and you'll be glad you did.

The Buffalo National River is the 1st National River and one of the most scenic places in all of the Ozark National Forest.  If you love kayaking, hiking, waterfalls, rockclimbing, camping, horseback riding, or scenic drives - this is Arkansas at its best and most natural state.

This is a wonderful state park that is about an hour west of Hot Springs and has over 100 campsites, several peninsulas with lake access, a nice playground, atv trail, bathhouses, and RV hookups.  It's quieter, calmer, and botanical.

This is such a nice walk in the woods. There are pavilions, playgrounds, and plenty of walking/biking space.  There is a small mountain biking trail at the end of the road   Boyle Park is a quiet spot near UALR and worth a walk!

Lake Chicot is the largest oxbow lake in North America and was created by the Mississippi River. The park is a great fishing park, but it is also a great summertime park due to the pool, Pavilions, and playgrounds.

Quite the historic preservation and information place for Boone County. It is 3 stories and a treasure trove of artifacts- including a room dedicated to Dogpatch. This building was the High School in the past.

Wonderful off-the-road day use historical  park with a view of the Saline river. Pavillion, kayak launch, and picnic tables make this a comfortable place to spend some time as a family or relax in a hammock.
Devil's Den State Park VC is a great resource for park information, a rest stop, or reservations. The Interpretive areas are currently closed due to Covid.
Great for fishing and family day use. Not a hiking park, but they do have some camping sites. And Crowley's Ridge is just 6 miles away.
Really cool military history museum full of neat artifacts. Not much else to do in the area, but this is worth a stop.

We drove around different parts of the preserve and enjoyed all of the beautiful, flowers, trees and nature we saw. Just nice and relaxing during this crazy pandemic. We did get out to have a tailgate picnic at the Turkey Creek unit trail head. Although it was awesome in the parking lot surrounded by a thick amount of trees we gotten eaten by a ton of mosquitos so got out of there. But otherwise it was definitely great to drive through.

What a magnificent state park! The views are breathe taking, the adventure was exciting and unlike the Grand canyon it was really cool to get to ground level in your vehicle and be in awe of the heights of the canyon walls. It was great walking around and enjoying the sites. We had just an amazing day here and will definitely be back! Get outdoors!

I really need more than 5 stars, I just really loved this state park! I loved the Cypress trees, the miss hanging off the trees, the Lily pads, the lake, the visitor center and the beautiful drive around the place. Definitely a must place to check out! Next time I'm going to have a boat or rent a canoe, we really wanted to explore more.

We enjoyed an nice afternoon here. We loved watching the birds and enjoyed the swings along side the water. It was great just to be able to enjoy the outdoors. It was pretty cool getting to watch the water coming through the dam. What a wonderful park. Pack a lunch come and enjoy the day outside.

I really enjoyed the Samurai Collection. Not only was it a free museum it has free valet. I liked that each piece was labeled with the period it came from and a bit of what and how it's made. This is definitely a great place to go for a bit in Texas heat to enjoy some nice cool air and history.

I saw the rock formation on top of the mountain from a distance and had to check it out. Well worth it. I was excited to see we could climb it.  We climbed the the summit trail. I really liked that they had a clean clear path to walk up mountain. This was a very peaceful beautiful walk.

I got the pleasure of going to 4 state parks today and this one was by far my favorite today. Stunning views, lovely flowers, beautiful creeks, beautifully green. I loved all of the limestone, the lilly pads & small little frogs. This is definitely a park to visit.

A wonderful state park to visit. Filled with beautiful buffalo & longhorns. We also got to see deer, different birds & flowers. I didn't expect to be here for so long, but definitely enjoyed every minute there. This is one to check out.

What a stunning natural area. It was great getting to spend sometime here on such a beautiful day. I loved all of the trees, river, hills, views and getting to spend sometime outdoors. This is a fantastic place to go. Love it here!

We loved driving through this refuge. Beautiful trees, flowers & wildlife. I got see see a 4 6-8 point bucks, tiny frogs, beautiful Butterflies and my first live armadillo. What a cool place to check out, just watch for poison ivy.

I don't have words to describe how amazing this place is. I had just lost a loved one and this was a great place to escape to, to reflect, regroup and enjoy the beauty of the flowers, nature and outdoors. 💜💚

What a beautiful state park to just get outside and enjoy the great outdoors. We had a wonderful time here and want to come back during the spring summer time to see the flowers and everything out of dormant

This park was just a treat to get to go to. We enjoyed the stunning views, all of the greenery and especially getting to feed and meet the longhorns. We just had a terrific time outdoors. Check them out!

Had a lovely time outdoors being able to check out the beautiful views, get some fresh air and just enjoy the day. The park has a large walk way and plenty of room to spread out. This was a nice find.
In attempt # 2 and still haven't made it inside. They either close to early or having a wedding. Hope I'll get to see the beautiful kaleidoscope of stained glass some day. 😔
I'm not a Dr Pepper fan, but I love me some Big Red! I absolutely love this place. Fun, history and education, this is a must go to place when you go to Waco!
This park was super sketchy. Got to see 2 drug deals, a disgusting swamp and a lack of serious upkeep! No thanks! Definitely not worth looking for the falls.
Went on a nice walk on the Discovery Trail, enjoyed the paved trail with informational signs on the different plants there. A great way to spend outdoors.
This dam had a nice overlook to be able to see the dam better. Not a informative dam stop. But a nice stop to check out one of several of Arkansas' dams.
I love this place. The roses are stunning, the gardens are very well kept and I love that they label all of the plants. This is a must go to place!
Another great Texas state park! Love the tower & red Rock building. We really enjoyed ourselves. Making great memories and enjoying the day!
I had a great time climbing up the rocks to be able to see this beautiful bridge and views. Definitely a cool place to check out.
We had a wonderful time walking around the state park enjoying the day and learning a bit of history. We had a great time!
Buy the Texas State Park pass. We have paid for it and then some. We absolutely love this park. Had a wonderful time here.
Had a good time here. Enjoyed our flight & cocktail & beer. The staff here are knowledgeable and really helpful.

Tour guide was great, cave was great.  I have been to many caves and this is the first one I have seen with a waterfall which was super cool! Nice rock formations and a variety of cave formations.

Why only 4 stars? The group I was with was the WORST family I have been on a cave tour with ever. The kids were terrible and the entire family was loud the entire time the tour guide was trying to talk. The dad was also very rude to our tour guide defending his annoying child. They all had headlamps and they were obnoxious! They should not allow these headlamps in the cave. The kids were spinning them around and continuously flashing them in my face. It really made it annoying and frustrating. If you have children please remember that other people have also paid for the tour as well.

This place is incredible! There are two waterfalls and soooo many neat “ledges” rock structures. I started out on the blue path and walked it until it curved and then hopped onto the white trail to see Minnehaha Falls and then doubled back to get into the red trail which was amazing. The red trail walks though the ledges structure and is like an obstacle course. Then we took the yellow trail to see cascade falls which is an amazing unique waterfall. There are no signs pointing you in which direction to go but the trees are all labeled one colors. Had a wonderful time here.

Absolutely amazing! Got there at 6:30 am and got to enjoy the area by myself for almost an hour. Was so amazing!
Cute little park that has a playground and a few separated areas with picnic tables and an area to cook.

This is obviously one of the standard Los Angeles places to go, and super iconic. Not only will you feel like you are walking through the history of media, you’ll also have plenty of places to eat and have fun, like the Wax Museum and the Chinese Theater. My only true complaint is that for a world renowned place, it should be a little more clean. A couple feet away, from a star, I could see human feces and urine, just right there on the sidewalk. So look out for that. Also, it’s not too safe. In three days, we witnessed three different assaults. So be careful.

A joint project between the state of Arkansas and the Korean government, this beautiful monument does not just honor Arkansans, but all American soldiers and Korean civilians who lost their lives during the Korean War. It is a wonderful piece of art, though it is ironic that it’s located next to Douglas MacArthur’s house considering that was the war that got him booted from the Army. It’s in a convenient location for students of UALR Law to visit, so I recommend stopping here as well as the adjacent house of MacArthur.

A nice little museum showcasing US military, especially in reference to Arkansan military. This is one of the oldest buildings in Little Rock and is the site of many important Arkansas events, such as the start of the Civil War in the state, as well as the birth of General Douglas MacArthur. It’s got some decent exhibits on all manner of wars where Arkansas citizens are involved, as well as some on the acclaimed general and the suffragettes. Best of all, it’s free admission. Might as well go if you’re in the area.

This is actually a great museum. It’s got two sections. The first is an 1800’s village that you can take guided tours of for a small fee ($1.50), complete with a print shop, pub and some other cabins and houses. The second section is the main museum itself (free), with tons of exhibits, ranging from artifacts from the daily life of early Arkansans, Native American artifacts, Civil War artifacts, early exploration artifacts, and more. Definitely a good stop when you’re in historic downtown.

We used the LA Tour Pass to go here and it was well worth it. You get to see the sets of all your favorite movies, as well as archives of costumes and props from your favorite movies. My favorite part was the real set of Friends. Fun fact: not a single episode or scene in friends was actually filmed in New York. It was all on that set. There’s also a soundstage with all the real Batman vehicles from across the ages. All in all, it’s wonderful. Be sure to see the iconic water tower too.

This is just simply one of those “must sees” of Chicago. It’s a beautiful and unique piece of art. Be sure to go under it as the visual effects are pretty wild. Nearby in walking distance is the Institute of Art as well as many other sights in the park. Be sure to pick up a Chicago style hot dog at a stand while in the park too, delicious.

This is a beautiful and unique little cathedral. It’s situated on a hill, with the only entrance being through the bell tower. It’s actually been featured on Ripley’s Believe It Or Not for that very reason. Considering it’s right across from the Crescent Hotel, it’s convenient to stop by. They’ve got a cute little gift shop too.

While I wouldn’t make a special trip for this, it’s definitely somewhere you should stop if you’re on your way to or from Chicago or somewhere else. You get to step foot in President Lincoln’s house when he was still just a lawyer, not the president we know. And it’s completely free too, though you can visit the gift shop.

This is a place I’ll definitely come back to, mostly because I missed the tour. Was so upset about that. It’s a beautiful place, surrounded by the Boston Harbor with crisp, clean air and a place to eat, as well as several monuments, a walking trail, and a park for kids to play. If you’re in Boston, it’s a must see.

Not my favorite stadium. The staff puppy guards you and prevents you from exploring the stadium (which is my favorite part), so essentially, you’ve gotta stay in your spot like you’re in third grade.
