And the Dodger dog isn’t that great. Otherwise, it’s a super cool location with some charm, it’s still a must see.

This is one of the best and most charming stadiums around. Nothing like the horribly titled and cookie cutter “Guarantee Rate” Field. This is historic and pretty. I recommend a tour, you won’t regret that. You get a close up of the ivy wall and the old scoreboard. You’ll get a great history lesson too.

We visited near winter, so I assume that’s why there were no butterflies and some older vegetables. Otherwise, it’s a really beautiful place for a date. The woman who took our entrance fee was also very nice and polite. No real complaints: a worthy stop.

This is the oldest surviving State House in the US, now a museum. This is the site of the Boston Massacre as well as the building where the Declaration of Independence was first declared from. 7th stop on the Freedom Trail.

A beautiful, if not super duper hot, walk. Right next to the border fence, Tijuana, Mexico is in view. If you’re in San Diego, it’s worth a short trip down. Just don’t touch the border fence! It’s under constant patrol.

Two hundred year old evangelical church and sight of many famous speeches. I didn’t get to go in as it was closed at the time, but since it’s on the Freedom Trail, you might as well stop by regardless.
This is just a cute animated short based on Kung Fu Panda with 4D tacked on. It’s super cute and exciting, and it doesn’t take all too long. The visuals are great, would definitely recommend.
This is now a museum, though it was once a church and a meeting house. This was where the planning and tallying was done for the Boston Tea Party! Seventh stop on the Freedom Trail.
A wonderful museum with wonderful staff. The Director was a very kind woman who allowed us to stay after hours to see the sights, and even complimented me and my girlfriend.
This is a classic place to go, right on the walk of fame. It’s a super nice place and there’s always premiers happening, with celebrities coming to see their own movies.
One of the stops on the Freedom Trail, it’s a must see. So much history here, including a walking tour of Revere’s former house as well as a museum and a gift shop.
A great place to go for astronomy and history, and simply to get a good bird’s eye view of the city. Parking is hard to come by so come early if you plan on going.
Beautiful and historic grave yard, here you’ll find the graves of John Hancock, the victims of the Boston Massacre, Paul Revere, and Samuel Adams.
My favorite of the springs. You’ll see inside a cool refuge from the heat with a small altar that people seem to have melted candles at for years.
This was a super cool little thing to drive through. If you’re going to San Diego, it’s worth a drive. It’s a nice sight.
If you’re in the area, this place is legendary in the music industry. You should definitely stop by and grab a photo.

These waterfalls easily rival Watkin's Glen State Park!  I went here the day after Watkin's, and really enjoyed how not crowded it was on Labor Day.  I was there around 9am.  The hike is slightly strenuous going up (it's one way, so you go along the rim trail right now to go up).  Once you're a the top of the rim trail, make sure you walk along the bridge on the same side of the road and you'll see the stairs down to the gorge trail.  Once on the gorge trail, it's downhill and very easy.  This is the only way to see the waterfalls up close.  The water was running well while I was there, not overflowing, and it was still a great sight to see.

Beautiful area for a nature walk.  The mansion was pretty to briefly walk around, but a little crowded with many wedding photographers (makes sense!).  The hike in this area was pretty leisurely, with only one or two uphill hikes.  Some bike riding on the paved areas, but I wouldn't say there's enough to drive here specifically for biking.  We saw lots of runners on the paths, and everyone we passed put on their mask while passing.

The trees weren't quite turning colors, but I'm sure this place is gorgeous in the peak of fall with all of the colors.

Perfect area for getting breakfast, lunch and dinner while visiting Universal Studios.  It does get really crowded here, especially once the parks close for dinner, so I highly recommend leaving a little early if you don't want to wait a long time for food.  It's a park in itself though, and a nice area for people to go if they're staying nearby at one of the Universal hotels.  The boat rides are fun as well even if you're not staying at a hotel.

Nice park to eat lunch in.  It's right next to the food trucks, so it's easy to grab lunch and walk over.  I wish there was more grass a tree coverage, as it can get pretty windy like the rest of Detroit.  Not a bad place to hang out in though.  Kids may like the sandy area and there are a few games to play and two restaurants in the park.

Enjoyable and quirky museum with a variety of art.  It took us a little over an hour to go through everything.  We were a little bummed because several of the exhibits were closed though, and the pricing didn't seem to be discounted at all so it felt a little expensive.  I really enjoyed the Yayoi Kusama exhibit, which is why we went here.

Great museum to go to in Michigan if you're a fan of design.  The museum was designed by Zaha Hadid, so I drove a couple of hours just to see it.  The architecture and design of the building is awesome in person.  I'm not a huge fan of modern art, so the art displays were a miss for me.  I did like the overall experience though.

This plaza is okay - it used to be a road connecting to Jefferson, and has been transitioned into a make shift plaza.  I would love to see it permanently become something with more greenery and grass, rather than a hardscape like so much of Detroit is.  It is a nice area for food trucks and sitting outside during lunch.

Good art museum with good exhibits. The layout is confusing so I definitely recommend getting a map. They have nice rotating exhibits every year and that makes it worth it to go back every once and awhile. They have a really cool cafe and it's easy to spend several hours here.  Lots of older paintings and sculptures.

Great place to spend half a day while in Philly!  Very affordable, and lots to see.  I was there for 2.5 hours and I didn't get to see and listen to everything that I wanted to.  Lots of rich history here, and very well preserved.  The audio tour is interesting,  and definitely some amazing photography moments here.

A good place to go for a little walk with restrooms nearby if you're visiting the area.  It seems like a lot of locals hang out here.  There isn't much to see though, the waterfront is not nearly as gorgeous as Watkins Glen's.  It is an easy place to park to use public restrooms though.

Good place to stop by if you're in the area, but not worth coming to Belle Isle just for the aquarium.  It's good to pair this with the conservatory next door, as the conservatory has more going on.  The aquarium felt a little drab and sad to me when I've visited a couple of times.

Note:  THIS IS NOT OPEN YET.   Most of these reviews saying it's great are for different areas.  This is not going to be open until 2020.  It does look like the design will be awesome, but the river front is currently disconnected and this is completely under construction still.

Beautiful spot in Pittsburgh, a must see if you're a visitor in the area.  It looked like biking here would be really easy if you don't want to pay for parking.  We were able to lay on the fountain - so it would be a great place to relax with a book or hang out with a picnic.

A very well kept Botanic garden!  It was a little too hot and humid inside of the Botanic Garden for us to enjoy it though, so we just had to speed through.  I'm sure it would be easier to enjoy if it's a little cooler outside, but during early September it was too hot.

Great place to go hiking and to get outside with family and friends.  I always come hiking here when I'm visiting Fayetteville because it's such a short drive away.  There are lots of hiking choices, so anyone can find something for their experience level.

Very clean, simple park right on the river front.  Great place to start biking towards Belle Isle.  Parking nearby.  There's a water play area for kids during the summer and nearby concession stand building.  Generally a good end point on the river front.

Beautiful bridge, well worth walking across because of the views, ease and the bridge itself is nice.  It is just that though, a bridge.  I wish there were more beautiful views of the bridge itself, but in general, worth seeing if you're in the parks.

Beautiful building, one of my favorites in Detroit.  Great variety of plants inside, and the grounds around it are nice as well.  Definitely a fun place to stop by on a nice day, or even when it's snowing to see it surrounded by snow.

Interesting sculptural playground for kids.  It's not an eyesore like most playgrounds, so walking up to it I was definitely intrigued.  It's definitely a sophisticated playground but kids still looked like they were having fun.

If you're looking for a beautiful bridge and area to walk around or bike through, then this is the place.  This bridge is gorgeous, and I love biking underneath it.  Would highly recommend to photographers as a great spot.

We stopped by here while visiting Boston.  We were a little underwhelmed, mainly because we were hoping to see the skyline better.  It is a nice place to stop if you are tired of walking or are just in the area.
This is a gorgeous pier, looking over a beautiful bright blue lake.  The water is really nice around here, great for photography.  This area also has a good place to walk out further on the water.
I recommend going on the goat trail for the best views here, but there are two different paths you can take for this hike.  The beginning of the trail has some very steep rocky areas.
Fun square, although a little touristy like most of Key West.  The last time I visited the area was pretty empty.
Great place to start a long bike ride.  We left our car here and went on a three hour bike ride.

This is a smaller national military battlefield park with representation of a few buildings from this piece of history, but at least the national park service was  able to attain and preserve this much, for all to see and reflect....

It has a nice  visitors center with friendly informative park rangers, interesting artifacts in the museum,  we watched the film about the battle and history and of course got my cancellation stamp in my national parks passport book!  👍🏼👍🏼

Walk or drive the very short self guided driving tour through the park which has the usual pull offs and place marks. Several required walking on paths into the woods to see the locations of the incidents.

We visited March 2019

Everyone loved it here. Reasonably priced admission, it’s not huge, so no long walks to see things, but big enough to see many types of wild animals. (pet the Giraffes!) it’s set out in the countryside. The staff is hands on with some animals and everyone can interact with them. It’s a nice clean open place. We really enjoyed going inside the bird sanctuary, sitting on the big boulders and feeding the parakeets, that actually would land on our arms, the kids were amazed and everyone loved it! We’ll come here again and again 👍🏼👍🏼

These MTB  trails require state park pass since  they're inside Yankee Springs S.P.
Great trails, two mile warm up (next to parking) and eleven mile trail  (starts across road from Ranger station) known for being one of the most challenging. Signing is good. Not To very crowded.
Ranger station next to MTB parking. (There's a restroom and changing area)
We've even taken leisure rides through the rustic campground to reach Deep lake. There's a great long wooded pier with rails, awesome views. Short trail to reach it, very cool 😎

I love it here! Lots of stuff to do. Besides Boating on Gun lake, there are Several Awesome kayaking lakes, clean and clear can see the bottom in most any lake  chosen. No large boat traffic allowed on the smaller lakes makes it excellent. I live the small islands. And Great fishing.
The 11 mile MTB trail and 2 mile warm up trail, are Good challenging and well groomed trails. Parking is next to Ranger station, I like that.
And lots more to see as well

This is a nice clean large park. There's a very  walking path along the waters edge with plenty of benches along the way. There's a nice picnic area and a large children's playground area.  It's between a very nice public boat on one end, a very nice restaurant on the other end that also sets right next to the water, all of this is accessible by boat as well. I must say the city Holland does a very good job keeping their parks clean and maintained.

No worries regarding traffic, the street was blocked the day we went.
Pay to park,. Walk up windows for beer... (Yes, like New Orleans, drinking  while  walking down the sidewalk is OK 😂)

Shops full of souvenirs. The music, the food, the clubs, the street performers up and down the street all night and even all day.

And surround by various landmarks and historic places.

A person should force themself to go through this every so often.

It's very steep, took awhile to get to the top, had to get into sort of stepping rhythm while climbing, which made it easier, all the effort it took to get to the top, only to find out there were several more dunes to cross  before reaching the lake.

But the view from the top looking the other way was still beautiful and worth the climb.

But we decided to find another area to get to the big lake.

Visited at a very busy time, July 2019, traffic was backed up and bumper to bumper before getting to the visitors center . Parking is only side by side up then back down and Parking on the side of the road on the exit side after the parking lot. Visitor center Restrooms closed, but offered 6 unisex vault type instead. Staff was very nice . And Of course the views Great views were amazing.

Get tour tickets at the visitors center (223 N. Main St.) for the ranger guided tour. (Free if you have a National Parks pass).

It was amazing to learn the Truman’s donated nearly every single thing they owed in this house to the American people.

Seeing everything left as it was to the very last day, it’s now like a time capsule.

We visited March 2019

It's very nice, multipurpose trails through the woods.
Easy MTB trails (shared w/hikers), Hiking, and Equestrian trails (across the street) some trails even handicap accessible).  Small picnic area. Busy in Winter months with  lighted Cross country skiing. Even a lodge.

This is a beautiful national park along the northern shores of Lake Michigan. The views are spectacular, the dunes are amazing and a challenge to climb for fun. The water is pristine as far as the eye can see... “Pure Michigan”  at its finest!

Beautiful park, lots of wildlife, nature trails, nice wood walkways, beautiful campground (Not full hook up), boat and kayak launch, friendly and welcoming visitors center ... great place to find quite and spend some time with nature

I like Custer, kayaking is good but it's busier people swimming all over the place and the MTB trail is a good long trail, has several  two tracks, not real technical, shared with hikers here and there, I don't care for that

Very very nice clean quiet well kept state park with beautiful sites that is surrounded by woods.
Most all the sites are wooded and all are paved that we noticed anyway.

Lots to do outside the park also.
Very nice clean park, easy to find, lots of shade, Lake views, boardwalks, large playground equipment, covered picnicking, BBQ grills, three separate parking areas. With short walk to lake.

Get tickets here for the Truman home tour here.
Get  cancellation stamp for your national parks passport book here 👍🏼👍🏼

Friendly informative rangers 👍🏼👍🏼
Visited March 2019
Nice big park, large variety of activities available, picnic/grills, kids play area, small steam, rustic building for renal ... Did not notice a bathroom anywhere ...
We found close parking, and was a short walk to the visitors center,  then we set off on our own to explore this beautiful national park and the history it contains
Nice big  park, plenty of parking on and off street. Plenty of picnic tables and large  pavilion, long walking path,  Nice play areas for the kids
Hard to find , we passed by it several times before figuring out exactly where it was, continual traffic didn’t help as we were looking for it
Very nice clean city park with lots of benches and shade trees, the only parking is parallel around the park otherwise fend for yourself
Beautiful park. Well maintained, great kayak launch into the Pigeon River. List of events scheduled all year for the public to attend
It's a beautiful walking trail,  probably why it's so popular, Parking is good and it's easy to find from the main road. Very nice
Nice park, nice beach but Very separated. It's a "Long" "Hot" walk to get to the beach. I'm not into that.... not necessary
Nice park, nice play area for the kids , picnic area, and offers a skate park and outdoor community pool next door.

This is not a worthwhile destination. I was desperate for a family hike so I took the family here. It is about a 1.5 walk on a crushed gravel path with no shade and no sights. The first bit is through grassland, then under the highway that will be very muddy if it has rained in the last 48 hours to a circle path in a field. Then back the way you came. There are some infographic panels with some history on the area's early residents, but it is nothing worth making the trip for. The mounds they refer to have long been demolished to build roadbeds. Just trust me, and I love parks/hikes, it is a waste of time. Go hike Cooper's furnace, Pine Mountain, or Red Top Mountain instead. Or bike/hike the nearby and much better Etowah Riverwalk.

Small parking lot here for about 20 cars with some parallel parking, but if you can get a parking place, this is the spot to be. From here you have direct access to hike up the mountain, access to the very cool boardwalk that connects to the PATH bike/walk trail, and access to the Animal Rescue AWARE located here. Arrive early, especially on weekends. If the lot is full, you can park at what Google calls the Arabia Mountain Trailhead and walk/bike 0.5 miles to here. There are porta potties and a bike rack.

Small aquarium with about 10 little tanks. Their covid measures are great though. Each family can reserve a one hour time slot and have the aquarium to their self with essentially a private guide. Lots of fish, a turtle, and a few crabs. Nothing crazy like sharks or octopus. Tank designs are simple and focus mostly on fish that can be found in the surrounding area. There is an opportunity to hold and touch hermit crabs, spider crabs, and horseshoe crabs. There is also a lovely nature trail on the property.

Went here on a free day. I was really disappointed by the exhibits. They all feature a heavy emphasis on interactive digital displays, but are often glitchy, slow, and not very engaging. No actual display of college players in the hall like Cooperstown, just touchscreens. Very few pieces of historic memorabilia. The part where you can try to kick a field goal is fun but overall this place was a big disappointment and in no way worth the $20+ admission fee.

Fantastic 3.5 mile loop for hiking or biking. This is not an aggressive mountain bike trail so much as a packed gravel, dirt, and leaves trail you can bike on. There are lots of people walking their dogs on the trail and frequent views of the lack. Parking is $5 and limited to about 30-40 cars. Make sure you look up directions to the trail head on google maps because it is not through the main park entry.

Nice little park with walking/biking trails, frequent views of the river and downtown Chatanooga. This park is located across the river from Downtown Chatanooga and connected by pedestrian and vehicular bridges. My family had a great time parking here and riding out bikes across the pedestrian bridge into Chatanooga.

Great little oddity snuck behind the 7th Day Adventist church. It won't take more then 30 minutes to walk through but there are lots of neat castles and bridges to marvel at. Fun for adult and kids, the admission price of free can't be beat. There are porta-potties on site as well as a wooded 1-mile walking trail.

Beautiful location to walk and bike. The ibis pond was really stunning to see hundreds of the beautiful birds nesting in the trees. Bikes are allowed on the trails, but I'd recommend sticking to the gravel for casual riders, because the grass and dirt trails require a lot more effort.

Very fun concept for locals and tourists alike. Park is filled with outdoor kids toys, free for use. Park could use a "mechanic", lots of the toys are damaged from use and neglect. Park is generally poorly maintained, but the young kids had a blast.

This was such a treat. It's a smallish hike but free and great to do with a date or, in my case, a young family. We loved the Alphabet trail. The kids had a blast following the map and finding all the letter signs that spell out Hatcher Gardens.

Gorgeous park with miles and miles of trails. Hiking options for all ages and skill levels. Biking too around the base. Hiking to the top is a mandatory activity in this party of town. Pretty friendly, but be aware that camping is not allowed.

Simple green space with a pier, great views of the harbor, and two fantastic water fountains. The fountains are kid friendly, so think sorta elegant splash pad. Our toddler had a blast. Excellent place to catch the water taxi too.

Great choice for a morning or an afternoon of fun with a young family. We walked about 1.5 miles on the trail loop, played on the fantastic playground in the woods, enjoyed a picnic lunch, and played in the creek. All for free.
Large, beautiful park with lots of amenities including skate park, playgrounds, green space, and ball fields. Also, there is very convenient access to the Greenway running and bike path.
Definitely go for a show. The shows are best for kids 3+. The museum, particularly the Jim Henson half is entertaining but not big enough to make it worth it without seeing a show.
Small park with two playgrounds, splash pad, amphitheatre, and green space. On the paved Roswell Riverwalk trail, so it made a nice stop on our family bike ride.
The history behind this place is unfortunately more exciting than the sites. Worth a stop, but test or more like a destination for a short hike of a mile or two.
Fun little intra-neighborhood park. No green space but there is a respectable playground, pond trail, and a little deck area with cover to rent for parties.
Overlook is very easy to access with a short walk (you can see it from the parking lot). Very pretty and understandably very popular with campers and RVers.
An art museum for cars. Parking is $13. Plan for about 2 hours to see the museum, 90 minutes more if you are planning to pay extra to tour the vault.
Great public space with something going on most warm weekends. Lots of great places to eat and fun shops located within easy walking distance.
One of the only covered playgrounds in the county. Perfect for rainy or hot, sunny days when the kids still need to run around outside.
Most of the exhibits were tough to experience well with small kids. The General is cool, but doesn't justify the entry price.
Small zoo-like experience with a train ride. Great for young kids. Adults, don't forget your free beer from the beer garden.
Fun trail for a simple family hike. The 3 year old needed a hand held during a few parts but it was a good level for him.

This place was creepy when we pulled up. I was like this is going to be stupid. We traveled to the top floors. It was all history related and movies. I am a history buff, so it was okay. Then we traveled to the basements. The creepiness of the building with the scary props were awesome. I think they should make the whole thing a haunted wax museum. It is worth the ten dollars.

The drive is long but you do not need a four wheel drive!!! There were sport cars and motorcycles at the parking. Plus, parking is limited so start looking for spots early. There is a side road that great for parking, too. There are no bathrooms plan ahead. The trail is well marked, but there are several social trails, so be careful. The trail is easy to moderate.

This is an interesting place to visit and has nice views of ES!!! Do not let the religion detour you from a quick visit!

Went tho see the Christmas light display. Website stated donations, but it is more of an entrance fee. Lights were not impressive, as well.

We went there for the candlelight tour. This was very interesting but the crowds were terrible. You could not walk down the sidewalk/path. The houses are nice and the stories are interesting. However, you could not hear half of the stories due to the crowds.

We came here for hiking and did not have any luck.
There are paved trails.
The one view was not interesting at all.
We could not find the other trails due to lack of communication and maps.
This park could be for camping and other activities.

This was a very informative tour. Could be one of the best tours for a state Capitol buildings.
The building was beautiful.
The top of the rotunda is awesome.
The library is awesome.
Go on a weekday so you can look through the library.

This could be the best winery in Missouri. The service was superb! The wines were delicious. The patio was big and shady. The live music set up was good, as well.

If you are interested....Tables were spread out for social distancing.

Must go when you are in the area.
Our tour guide was knowledgeable and nice.
Please note you will have to duck walk, so if you cannot basically sit and walk you will hold up the tour group. There is a sign warning you about the cave.

Do you want a challenge adventure?
Do you want a nice view?
Do you want to climb rocks on your hands and knees?
This is the place.
The hike is short but you will be challenged.
You will opportunity to see some great views of OK.

This place has ton of free activities. It is kid friendly. Adult friendly. The customer service is excellent!!! The food is overpriced and nasty. The roller coasters are awesome! The interaction with the staff is fun, as well.

The tour was very informative.
The art of the house is a one of a kind experience.
Our tour guide was very nice and direct. You cannot bring food or beverages in the house.
You are not allowed to take pictures, as well.

This was very disappointing.
The information was good.
The building is small.
There was no information about trails.
The bathrooms were clean.
I just had higher expectations, and they were not met.

A nice mile hike.
Views of the Missouri River.
Easy to moderate hike.
Plenty of benches.
The final overlook is boring.
A lot of information about Lewis & Clark and Native Americans along the way.

This was a very nice park and walking trail.
The bridge is spectacular!
The Chinese garden is awesome!
This is a hidden gem in Des Moines.
Wish is was warned to enjoy the park a little longer.

Another treasure in Missouri.
This park offers canoeing, caving, hiking and camping.
The cabins looked nice and cozy.
There are plenty of picnic areas, as well.
You will not be disappointed.

The highest point in Missouri.
The Ozark Trail is awesome!
The waterfall is seasonal or depends on the weather.
Camping is nice on the Ozark Trail. Plenty of space with fire rings.

We hiked the Hidden Springs Trail. The trail was easy. There was an old cemetery on the trail. It was a nice surprise.

There was a nice old cabin with trail information!!!

What an awesome experience.
The staff is knowledgeable and friendly.
The animals do not look sad here like zoos.
A must see when visiting Eureka Springs, Arkansas.
This is a interesting place to stop. The place is awesome. If you believe in God you will love it. If you do not believe in God, you will love it but be judged.

If you like trout fishing, this is your place.
There’s a hatchery.
The visitor center is small.
There are multiple parks.
There are a couple good hiking trails.

This is a very interesting place to visit.
All of the exhibits are replicas.
This is a cash only place be prepared.
There is a lot of reading with this place.

If you have time to kill this is a must stop in Santa Fe.
It is free.
Tons of artwork for sale and art galleries.
A very interesting stop in Santa Fe.
There are many trails to hike. However, there are no maps and the trails are not marked. There are a ton of bugs. There are trees down on the trails.

The wines were good.
The wines are cheap.
The staff was very friendly.
You are able to sample all of the wines.

This is a nice easy trail.
The views are worth the short hike.
The pictures do not do it justice.

Unique rail bridge spanning the Des Moines river.  Just a few miles off of Hwy 30, you drive along a gravel road to the base of the bridge where you can park on the side of the road to take pictures.  Well worth seeing.  I did notice an echo affect on the newer bridge right next to it, so shout down the bridge columns to see if it works for you.

A must see at least once.  Park at the visitor center and pay for your tour.  Grand rooms tour is a good one.  Take the bus to the hilltop.  Tour will likely last over an hour.  You can then roam the gardens freestyle until ready to take the bus back to the visitor center.  Several hour drive down from San Francisco, so plan for the day.

Fun! Fun! Fun!  Worth the trip to dig in the ground for a day searching for diamonds.   Plenty of parking and close camping areas.  They have water troughs available to help sift, and rangers on site to help identify your rocks.  Bring your shovels, buckets, sisters, and other non power tools.  Plenty of space to dig.

Nice state park a short drive from Valentine.  The park has a nice trail to the tallest waterfall in Nebraska, and access to the Niobrara River.  The is a small visitor center, and nice picnic areas.  You will need to pay a fee to access the park, and the road to the main parking area in dirt/gravel.  Enjoy.

This gem of a national park has a visitors center with parking in proximity to central high school.  There are also some Memorial grounds and restored building at the school intersections.  I was amazed at how large the school was compared to the historical pictures.

Beautiful mansion and grounds.  There is a fee, and online reservations are recommended.  It was once considered the White House of the West.  Owned by the Morton family until deeded to the state, it is well worth a stop.  Check out the bowling alley in the basement.

Worth a trip north off the interstate.   A well groomed trail of about a mile takes you to rock formations used for millenia for the creation of pipes.  There is also a beautiful waterfall along the trail.  Allocate an hour or two to see the park.

Wonderful state park for fishing.  The lake is clean and well groomed, and is very accessible from shore via trails with access to the water.  Has modern bathrooms, camping facilities,  swimming area, and trails.  Keep up the good work.

Was very surprised at how much I liked this place.  The gift shop has every thing you could want from the Precious Moments collection.  The crown jewel, though is the Chapel and surrounding grounds.  Worth a stop off the interstate.

Stayed in one of the modern cabins over a weekend.  Probably the best cabin experience I have had.  Clean, large, and easy to book.  The park is well run with plenty of activities and easy shore fishing.   Will be back!!!!

You can tell the character of this man by this house and the story behind it.  Worth a trip from the library.  Yo can park right on the street.  Also, check out the neighborhood with some interesting houses and stories.
The grounds are very peaceful for a stoll to his house and parents graveyard.  Some stunning wooded scenery, and a very informative visitors center.  Perfect stop for history buffs.
Nice park.  Park on the north side to gain access to some trails to the lakes.  There is access to the shore for fishing on several of the lakes in the park.
Small site.  Plenty of parking and very friendly staff.  Take a tour of the house and outbuildings.  The barn has neat information about the site and Grant.
Small historical display overlooking mustard canyon.  Several old machines and narratives of the mining activity in Death Valley.  Worth the 20 minute stop.
Small, but nice, museum plus an opportunity to go into his birth house across the street.  Worth a stop to further understand a very humble president.
Lots of hiking opportunities and to see the historic row of spring houses.  Parking can be difficult,  so bring some walking shoes just in case.
Modern museum focusing on John Wayne.  Nice gift shop.  $15 museum entrance fee which includes entrance to the house. Well worth s stop.
Great trails to see the Mounds and river.  The longest hike will take time, as it is hilly and the trail slowly becomes less groomed.
Small National Park with two visitor centers.  There are about 3 miles of groomed trails.  Be sure to visit the old school house.
Beautiful covered bridge within a City Park.  Parking close to the bridge and several other museum are close.  Worth a stop.
Neat state park.  Make sure to visit the caves and the small historical Cemetery.  Small daily admission to use the park.
Worth a visit when in San Jose.  A bit pricey and touristy, but the house itself along with the grounds are interesting.
Beautiful overlook.  If you look to the west you can see cathedral point.  Worth the hike from Golden canyon trail head.
Beautiful covered bridge about 15 minutes from I35.  Along a gravel road.  Easy access and parking.  Well worth a stop.

This is a very nice little Park located outside of Denver where a lot of people like to go jog bicycle and even ride horses. Has beautiful views of the Front Range and a large part of the trail system could actually be navigated from a wheelchair. My only negative is the fact that all of a sudden all of these little parks in and around Colorado have now gone to anywhere from a $5 to as much as a $15 day-use fee,, undermining my whole idea of a park and maybe having a donation box instead. Colorado has built up over a Billion dollars in surplus money from Recreational(marijuana) usage why not spend part of that on your park system.

This is the highest paved Road in North America. You can drive your passenger car all the way to 14, 000 100 and some feet. I have a park pass but I believe it was either 15 or $20 to enter the park and there are several other fee areas if you choose to stop. The views are absolutely stunning 360 degrees. I recommend during peak tourist season to go early in the morning as the parking lot at the Summit is very limited. There is an observatory and the remains of a building that was once the highest structure on the planet. I highly recommend.

Every trip to Colorado since my childhood 50 years ago has involved a stop by MT's property.  You have to completely hide the politics and simply look at this as an extra ordinary lifetime's worth of art. Art should be art and left alone. I am so thankful that his trust was set up and the Kohler foundation will make this an even bigger attraction for Mullinville.  I highly recommend.
likes: Cultural Value: Lifetime's worth of art
Facilities & Services: Trust setup, Foundation support

reviews_attraction.text: The grounds were beautiful and had a couple of exhibits. The museum itself was free if I'm not mistaken and we wandered through the whole place. Arkansas has spent a considerable amount of money on this building and I highly recommend that you visit if you're in this area. There is a lot to do in this immediate part of town but it only took us about 20 minutes.

This is the centerpiece of Wichita downtown Commons area. This sculpture was done by Blackbear Bosin in the 70s. It is widely used as an attraction for people visiting Wichita for the first time to go see the Confluence of the little and the big Arkansas Rivers, which is also a sacred area for past Native Americans. I highly recommend.

This is just a spectacular place that has now been made into a national recreation area to help preserve it. The East Side belongs to the native Americans and the West side of the gorge belongs to the bureau of land management. Excellent hunting fishing and hiking also rock hounding, beautiful scenery photography I highly recommend.
likes: Diverse activities (hunting, fishing, hiking, rock hounding)

reviews_attraction.text: This is a 501K non profit organization. To help spread the faith of Jesus Christ. The cross was built a 190' tall, 10' short of the FAA requirement for a blinking red light. It can be seen for nearly 20 miles away. And until the recent wind farm installation was the tallest structure for hundreds of miles. I highly recommend.

I would easily give this Visitor Center a 10 star except for the new$15 per day use fee imposed by the city of Denver.  As I also discovered at another park near Boulder had a brand new $5 day-use fee. Even with all of the marijuana tax money Denver is extremely greedy is what I was told by people that live there.

I've been going to this Lake for over 50 years. It's pretty much the same and if you want to get away from Wichita this is where you go.  I just bought an annual pass for much less then normal if you buy it when you renew your car tag. I will be looking forward to driving through Cheney all the time for free now.

These folks have done a tremendous amount of neighborhood cooperation to pull this off. I was shocked and amazed at how many cars were backed up Sunday night to see this block of lights. Shows great respect for the season and obviously makes this neighborhood tighter. I highly recommend thank you for the show.

I commend Wichita for catching up with the times on little things like this park. And we can now actually have a place for food trucks and a very nice public space. I highly recommend. night time security had sometimes been an issue but I for the most part think you should feel safe in this area at night.

This happens to be the closest National Park to my home in Wichita Kansas. This park contains the highest continuous paved Road in the lower 48. Pretty much what the name says Rocky Mountains 360 degrees. Supports unparalleled views from the top of Trail Ridge Road at over 12,000 feet. I highly recommend.

This is an extremely iconic part of Ranchos de Taos.  It is the 2nd or 3rd most photographed place in northern New Mexico. I have never attended a service here on my visits but I hope to someday. Would love to see the interior of this building. Wonderful spiritual place I highly recommend.

This is a cool place to take kids but they just don't seem to change the exhibits enough.. I do however recommend the Boeing cyberdome shows very fun.. The exhibits have gotten much larger and have changed more often. This is just an awesome place to take children and I highly recommend.

This is a beautiful little park that has a short hiking trail there is a small pond there is a shelter building and I believe it is the highest point in Salina and you can pretty much see 360ﾟ from there.   Great place to just get away to nature for a little while.  I highly recommend.

Have been visiting this place for over 50 years it has a stunning view of the plains. The park service recently renovated the wood part of the structure to avoid further collapse. The fact I McPherson allows you to go there for free is very cool. I highly recommend.

Even this late in the year this is one of the prettiest drives in the mountains that I have found. Nice overlooks with beautiful views of the Petitt Jean Valley.  Such a beautiful state. I highly recommend. Get away from the people and get back to mother Earth...

You could not imagine that this park is surrounded by highways and busy streets in the middle of town. It's an extremely nice park it is time sensitive so you cannot visit late at night. The nature center is extremely educational and I would highly recommend.

I'm thinking one of only 2 or 3 places in America where bison have places to roam.. Stunning scenery and beautiful trails. I guess my downfall was trying to get and reserve a camping space they fill up very quickly. I will come back thank you.

It's sad the city won't give this museum more money but I would highly recommend it represents a huge part of what the West was and how Kansas was in the 1800's and early 1900's..   I would highly recommend plus they have seasonal events.

This is an iconic Wichita museum located at the confluence of the little and big Arkansas rivers on sacred ground.  There is a beautiful museum there and also a common space for dances and ceremonial aspects.  I highly recommend.
A big enough of a park that you can still find your own little private place. Offers an array of activities for adults and children alike. Just an excellent place to walk bike or run.
This is a beautiful Park located in the center of West Link. One of the nicest pools in all of Wichita and plenty of room to do whatever. I highly recommend.
This is a great park for the locals, however I go there for the historical content the fact that Kit Carson is buried there. I highly recommend.
I have gone to this museum for decades my daughter displayed art here 20 years ago when she was 7 or 8. I highly recommend.

Very nice zoo with a lot of animals!! I would recommend this zoo to anyone visiting NOLA.

I'm giving it 4 stars though because it's very expensive compared to other zoos I've been to! There is a very cool water park inside the zoo too but that is extra (we didn't go to it). Also the zoo is very spread out and seems more like a nature walk once you get out to the swamp area. This is more of a conservation zoo which is great but some of the animals were hard / impossible to see. The swamp area is cool if you're not from Louisiana but very open and a lot of the zoo seems more like a nature walk.

Also the layout is kind of weird and hard to leave if you want out. We had to walk about half a mile to exit the park because they had buildings in the way and no path through.

I recommend you go see the tiger, jaguar (which is rarely seen in the back of the park), and otters. Very cool! The zebras and rhinos were nonexistent though. :/
dislikes: Missing or rare sightings (zebras, rhinos, jaguar)

reviews_attraction.text:
Amazing and beautiful track! Came here for MotoGP & Formula 1, and had a blast! Tons of seating options & places for snacks. But it’s SUPER expensive for seats and food options. General admission seating is okay if you pick a spot and stick to it for hours, but I recommend buying a ticket for the stands so you have a set seat. Parking all around the track is ridiculously over priced! Needs more parking for cheaper. (Some lots are gravel on the side of a hill).

Traffic coming & going is a NIGHTMARE!! Tiny two lane roads in the middle of nowhere trying to accommodate thousands of cars is ridiculous. Need way more lanes & help directing traffic. (Also, really the only way to get there is to take toll roads that will mail you a bill a month later).

Amazing old Spanish fort! A must see for St. Augustine. It is a national park and there's a fee to go in but it's worth it. Great view of the city / bay and it's very historical. The architecture of the fort and history is amazing. The fort had several sieges in its history, but was never taken by force (only by treaty or FL being taken over by another county).

I would love to go back for the ghost tours they do at night. This location is haunted though. It's been on Ghost Adventures. Hundreds of people lived and died in and around this fort, so that should be expected. Awesome experience for any historian, tourist, or ghost hunter.

VERY nice park and green space between the three major attractions: Georgia Aquarium, Coca-Cola, and the Civil Rights Museum. Named for the inventor of Coca-Cola.

Only problem is there is ONE place to eat around this entire park / area and that’s “Pemberton Café”. Look it up on Google Maps as it might not pop up. This place is HORRIBLE. Avoid at all costs. It’s basically a rip off because it’s the only place to eat close by. Bring your own food, have a picnic, walk a mile away, drive, anything. Complete rip off for horrible food. This park needs more eating options!

Best & cheapest parking was at the Georgia Aquarium parking deck.

HUGE Civil War battlefield with very nice grounds! Shiloh was one of the biggest battles & the sheer size of the park is amazing. If you want to see it all, plan to spend at least 2 hours here. Very good plaques and descriptions of the engagement. Only wish the visitor center / museum was a little bigger. Some more descriptions of the engagement or an interactive map would help. Still pretty huge display of Civil War rifles and pistols (largest I’ve ever seen in a museum). Cemetery was very nice as well. Very important battle in the American Civil War and helped turn the tide for the Union in the South.

Amazing history of the JFK Assassination! Get the audio tour. It is pretty busy and crowded but it is a must see location!

Only thing I don't like about it is they barely have anything about the many conspiracy theories that Oswald did not act alone.. They should have more exhibits / evidence of that. They only support the Oswald theory really. Hello? Grassy knoll anyone?!

Pretty pricey but worth it for all the history and artifacts. I love all of the original cameras they have displayed and the in depth timeline.

Great museum for Memphis music and history! Movie at the start (don't miss it) and then everything is at your own pace. If you read everything, listened to all the audio clips, and listened to half the songs.. This museum would take about 3 hours to go through. Pretty long but great info and music. Good info (kinda short though because it's only in one room) on Sam Phillips, Elvis, Jerry Lee Lewis, and BB King. A must stop for any Rock 'n' Roll or Blues fan visiting Memphis!

Site of Martin Luther King Jr. assassination and Lorraine Motel. Great museum for any history buff or anyone interested in African American history. Really eye opening and inspiring. Love all the exhibits and history. It is located at the original sites as well. Be sure to check the hours before going because several times I’ve tried going when visiting Memphis and it has been closed. Love the store at the end. A lot of great books and souvenirs to purchase.

Awesome history and a must see if you are in San Antonio! It's great to see where American's held out against the Mexicans under Santa Anna during the Texas War for Independence. It's interesting to find out that most of the old fort is now built over. Only a small section of the original fort (but the most iconic) is still standing. I recommend watching the movie on the Alamo before coming to give you some background knowledge.

Great park! Rides, attractions, food, and shows are great and always improving. Prices are pretty high for everything though. Tickets, food, and souvenirs are all crazy expensive! Park is very fun though. Also the cave tours, below the park, are great and included in the park price. Definitely recommend. Only wish prices were cheaper and they had more shuttles to and from the free parking.

I loved the history and all of the real pirate treasure / relics. However this is definitely a place for kids and families, not a museum or for just adults. The kids were shooting off a LOUD cannon over and over on the ship that gave us a headache. Besides it being loud and having kids running around everywhere, it was an awesome stop for someone interested in pirate history!

Great place to take the family or become a kid again. They have tons of all arcade games, mini golf, bumper boats, laser tag, and go karts. The laser tag & go karts are super fun. Everything is pretty expensive here though. Expect to spend a lot of money if you want to experience everything. Overall it’s great though. Highly recommend for some family fun.

Huge replica of the Parthenon in Athens, Greece. The closest you can get to seeing the Parthenon without actually going to Greece. Park surrounding it is very nice. Really nice at night as it has lights all around it lighting it up. Would’ve been nice to tour during the day when it’s open though. Recommend coming here on any trip to Nashville, TN.

Huge museum about Country music. If you are interested in country music at all, come here. You will not be disappointed. Huge museum / gallery of country music from the beginnings to current artists and music. I really liked the store here as well. Of course very pricey to buy things but a huge selection of really nice souvenirs.

Very nice military park, battlefield, and museum. Go through the museum to learn more about the Battle of Prairie Grove. Recommend coming during a reenactment if you can in early December (I think they have one every other year). Markers around the park were very informative. Very scenic and looks almost as it did in 1862.

Very nice mini golf course. I love all the holes and beautiful landscaping. Has two sides to the course with 18 holes total. Recommend coming at dusk because there’s zero shade if you come in the day. It can get pretty hot during the day. It’s located right next to Fastlanes as well. Employees are very nice and courteous.

This is a cool place to visit if you're in St. Augustine! It has a lot of weird and unusual exhibits. We made our hand using wax and that was fun (and kind of painful), but it melted on the way home. I liked it a lot but some of it is a little boring or outdated. It's too expensive for what they have as well.

Very cool concrete memorial to JFK who was assassinated nearby at Dealey Plaza in Dallas. Really interesting and important place to come. Recommend you visit here, Dealey Plaza, and the 6th Floor Museum to understand the historical importance of this area on that fateful day (11/22/1963).

Very big Civil War battlefield & park. Interesting to see and explore.

I only got to see Chickamauga battlefield on this trip. Will have to return to see Chattanooga battlefield as well. I believe it's in Lookout Mountain, TN (South of Chattanooga).

Amazing aquarium!! A lot of different things to see. Love the sharks and seahorses.

Only downside is the very expensive price for admission. It is a positive that you can get a package deal for several Audubon locations for a cheaper price.

Nice history and museum. Arkansas' old Capitol building which played a part in the Civil War in AR. Nice exhibits but in my opinion some of them need an update. Interesting place to visit though. Parking is a little hard to come by.
Nice parking lot area for Lake Springdale and trails. It's kind of a hike to get all the way up to the lake but it's nice. Parking lot is half gravel now but looks like they are going to fix soon.
Great museum and tons of artifacts and exhibits! Best place to go in NOLA.. Only wish it was a little cheaper. You have to spend tons for just 2 people, but overall great experience.

Awesome history & view of assassination spot of JFK. Likely second gunman location behind the fence.

Research witnesses: Lee Bowers, Gordon Arnold, Malcolm Summers, and Ed Hoffman.
Amazing museum about Little Rock Central High School and the Little Rock Nine. A must see for anyone interested in African American history! 👍🏻

I use this area mostly in the off-season (when it is free to park there) as a kayak launching site, or taking out site, and for biking access to the McDade Recreational Trail. The facility is large, with a concession stand and several bathroom buildings. It is also a stop on the Pocono Pony's route so you can park there, put your boat on the Pony's trailer and ride for free to wherever you'd like to put-in (great service BTW!). Crowded on summer weekends as you might expect for a beach close to NJ and NYC.

Every time I've ever ridden this mountain, it has been wonderful! 1000 feet of elevation and some connecting, winding trails make for runs well in excess of a mile in length. Large areas at the top of the lifts where people can gather without impeding those exiting the lift. No high-speed lifts can be both a blessing and a curse. The blessing is when your legs are exhausted and they can recover on the ride up, the curse is when it is cold and windy and it takes FOREVER to get to the top! Love it!

Very nice camp area. The cabins here are interestingly designed, no running water (spigots are between cabins), but there is a flush toilet in each one (only accessible from outside the cabin). Strange design choice, but better than running to the bathhouse every time nature calls! Boat launch into Cayuga is just up the road. Quiet, pretty, and clean, what more can you ask of such a facility?

Pretty stream, kinda rough roads to get there. The water levels in early June, 2018 were very low which rendered the falls almost into extinction. What water was running was crystal clear and refreshingly cool. Folks were swimming in the splash pool below the falls. The picnic area near the parking lot had several families enjoying the sunny day. Well worth the dusty drive to get there.

Pretty park on the harbor in Bar Harbor with a wonderful view of the boats and islands nearby. The park itself is beautifully manicured and seemed very clear of litter and the like. Lots of paved walkways to accommodate anyone with a physical handicap, plus lots of grassy areas to spread out a blanket and just hang out. Plenty of shops just across the street when you finish sitting!

As a place to take young children to spend a day, there's really very little competition in the area. The baby animals and Halloween days were the highlights when my kids were younger. There is an annual craft festival there that is nice to visit. Lots of history and knowledgeable folks to talk to. If you go, be sure to get a loaf of their home-baked breads, simply delicious!

This is a great place to bicycle or hike. The 25+ mile length is a great distance for a day ride. Lots of places to stop and watch the boaters and rafters shooting the rapids on the Lehigh River. Some waterfalls can be viewed directly from the trail and Glen Onoko Falls is just a fairly steep hike away. Great to visit during the fall foliage season.

This park has some of the most interesting boulders in this region of Pennsylvania. There are quite a few of them scattered along the trail and well into the surrounding forest. If the trail were better blazed and easier to follow (I'm a very experienced hiker too!) I'd've given the place 5 stars. What a great place to explore!

An easy 1 mile hike from route 390 brings you to the falls. There are several small cascades on stream the trail runs along that are very pretty too. The rope-assisted trails right at the falls are interesting and quite fun. Can get pretty slippery near the falls, so care must be exercised. Very nice place to visit.

Beautiful place! Only gripe is that the well-blazed trails match neither the map available at the kiosk or the PDF I had downloaded. The blue trail that completes the loop around the lake looks kind of new, so perhaps the updated maps just aren't out yet. Nice trail with only minimal elevation changes.

Lovely park just west of Scranton and north of Wilkes-Barre PA. The hiking trails are not very challenging, but the views of the lake from them are pretty. Paddling the lake only takes a couple of hours, so not a day trip, but it is a very pretty lake. Interesting history concerning the park's origins.

Really only paddled up Wild Creek from Beltzville Reservoir. This is the shorter of the 2 northernmost creeks that feed Beltzville. The falls further upstream, which I've visited at other times, are indeed very pretty, especially in the winter when they are covered in icicles.

The hike to the point isn't particularly challenging, but does involve several hundred feet of elevation. The views make the hike well worth the exertion. As with many hikes in the area, the access is on a ridge and the hikes start with a descent and end with the climb.

Great scenery on an interesting 19th century technology. A bit pricey, but the trains and tracks are expensive to maintain. The running narrative from the brakeman certainly provided more than enough information about the cog railway and the surrounding scenery. Fun.

Parking area allows access to a nice trail. The trail is well blazed in blue and, after a fairly decent amount of climbing, meets the AT. Though it continues beyond the AT, I was time-limited (not to mention daylight limited) and did not do the rest of the trail.

Nice park with plenty of hiking and biking trails for all skill levels. The historical information signs and buildings make for an all-around interesting place to visit. Great for an early morning walk, or an afternoon of bombing around on your MTB.

Better known locally as "the Alice Bridge", though I know not why. Very interesting structure. I forgot my headlamp, but I clambered down a couple of the labelled "Rabbit Holes" and will be back to explore more.

Raymondskill Falls was flowing with a good volume and looked great with the snow covered rocks. The new overlooks allow a great view with the added benefit of deterring folks from doing anything undesirable.
I kayaked New Wawayanda Lake which has a shoreline along this park. Seems like a fairly heavily trafficked park, there were quite a few fishermen along that portion of the shore.
Only saw this from the outside after hiking a nearby trail, nicely preserved historic building. Large imposing place with great stonework and a pretty waterwheel attached to it.
Nice little local park with a pool, skate-park, concession stand (seasonally) and athletic fields. I primarily use it as an access point for the Levee Loop Trail. Nice place.
A bit pricey for what you end up seeing, but the backstory is interesting and the falls are pretty. Taking the longer trail back yields quite a bit more falls and scenery.
Small, but nice county park. Well laid out trail system and even some views. Not really large enough to spend a day hiking, but great for a morning or afternoon.
Quaint little gift shop nestled inside the covered bridge. Prices and selection are about what one would expect. Nice people running the place.
With a solid day of substantial rain on Friday, many of the feeder streams were flowing well. Lots of picture opportunities.

I have to say I was a little disappointed with my visit. The last time I was here I was 8 years old and I remember it being very fun. Now returning 15 years later it definitely wasn't as good. The roller coasters were very fun, but they don't allow purses and they charge you for lockers. When I went they pretty much had half the park closed because it was "off season" but they still charged us full price, and an extra $20 for the privilege of parking on their asphalt. The shamu show was disappointing too, because they pretty much just spent the entire time trying to convince us that keeping whales in captivity is good for them. I guess that netflix documentary really got on their nerves. If you bring your kids here they will probably have fun, but there just isn't really much for anyone who's older.
dislikes: Admission pricing (full price, extra parking fee)

reviews_attraction.text: This is a decent place to visit when you're passing by, but in my opinion it's not the kind of place that I'd want to visit again. Parking can be a little tricky during peak hours, but it's not impossible. They have some fun amusement rides which I enjoyed. But I was really hoping to see a little more of the ocean. There's a small walkway hidden in the back, but not much more than that. Typically with a boardwalk you'd expect to have a walkway made of wood, but you really don't get that at all here. Don't get me wrong, it's still nice, but it's not what I expected. The biggest killer though is the price of everything. $6 for a corn dog. Not a legit corn dog either. I'm talking Walmart frozen section corn dogs, for $6. Pretty much everything is this expensive. Overall, decent place.

Great haunted house. It just goes on and on and on. I couldn't believe how long it lasted. Stay out of the foam at the end though because it lasts too long and just becomes unpleasant. My only complaint is that none of the staff make any noises. No grunts, "boos," or screams. It's obvious that they've been instructed not to do it, but I'm not sure why. It lowers the scare factor. Overall this is a good haunted house to go to for a fun experience and to be impressed by all the work that was put into it. This is NOT a good haunted house to go to if you want to be scared.

Great place to do your tube rental, but expect to spend lots of money! We paid $20 per person to ride the bus from the parking lot to the drop off point and back. A tube rental is included in the bus pass price. We did also have to pay for parking too. If you know what you’re doing you can probably do all your tubing for free but if you’re a noob like us just pay the $20 per person and let Texas Tubes take care of the tube & transportation

What a beautiful place! No gates or fences, so it's very easy to walk around and enjoy the sights and leave whenever you want. It feels just like a public park, rather than a botanical garden. It's also free (at least the outdoor portion). Lots of benches and shade. I love the water. Overall great place to visit.

Superb bayside park! Great views of the water and lots of room for activities. Easy access to shade and plenty of tables to sit at. We came here on a Sunday and there was lots of activity. We played board games on one of the tables and we could smell somebody making bbq on one of the grills. Great place to come.

This is truly a great zoo. It's obvious that a lot of thought and planning was involved in the construction and layout of the exhibits. Everything flows really nicely, and they make pretty good use of their space. They've got a good variety of animals too. I'm also pleased that they don't charge you for parking.

Great baseball stadium. Lots of shade around sunset times, too much further past third base you'll cook in the sun. $1 hot dogs on Wednesdays. Parking is a disaster though. $20 to park in a big empty lot and you'll be guaranteed to be stuck in grotesque traffic when you leave.

This is a very cool attraction, and an awesome activity to do whether you're visiting or if you've lived here for years. They're only open on the weekends, unfortunately. If you're feeling adventurous I highly recommend hiking the trail to the top, then riding the tram down.

Good little museum packed full of history. I was very surprised to find out how small it was. That’s really the only downside of the place. It’s very very small. You can get through the whole thing in about 1.5 hours. Overall still worth coming to learn about the history

This is a fantastic place to come on a Saturday afternoon. You're not supposed to swim because of safety reasons, but every now and then you can find a little pool/waterfall where you can get a little wet. The riverbed goes on and on which makes for a great little hike.

Very cool place, especially since admission is free. Expect to pay for parking though. They have a parking garage, or you can try your luck at a meter on the street. Lots of interesting historical artifacts, rather than just simply art. I would definitely return

This is a great lakeside park to hang out on a weekend afternoon. There's lots of boats hanging around nearby, but I believe the boat launch at this park is closed. There's a small beach (made of rocks, not sand) that you can walk/sit on.

Great place to go for a walk or a skate. Beautiful scenery. The path is paved and well maintained, and it goes on for miles and miles because it connects to other park paths. Highly recommend coming and checking it out!

Great place to come if you're from out of town. So much history. The grounds are really beautiful and you'll learn a lot from coming here. Stand on the star in the center of the dome and you can hear your voice echo.

Awesome place to take an evening walk. The bridge is beautiful. Watch out for homeless people though. It would be great to see more police around here. Also parking costs money so I'd recommend finding curb parking.

What an awesome park! It's built over the freeway, which is such a cool and unique use of space. There's lots going on here on the weekends and tons of people come out here to have fun. Food trucks are standing by.

This is an outstanding park. There's so many things you can do here! If the weather is bad or if you get bored outdoor activities you can go inside to play basketball, volleyball, billiards and more FOR FREE.

I wouldn't call this much of a "mount" but it's the closest thing that Austin has! Great place to visit on an afternoon. It gets kinda crowded on weekends. Go in the morning to avoid the crowd. Good views.
Great scenery! It's really cool to be able to walk across the dam. There's always someone fishing here. Bring your bike, or just take a walk. Definitely a great place to get some fresh air.
Good place to come and take a short walk on the pier. The pier is a reasonable length so you should be able to walk for a bit. You also have a great view of downtown Tampa in the distance.
Awesome place to ride your bike. The trail can get really rocky at some parts, so plan accordingly. There's so much to do. Rock climbing, swimming, hiking, etc. Just get out and have fun!
This is a great place to come. Bring your kids... or don't! There's plenty of stuff for adults to do around here, as long as you like to have fun and have a sense or curiosity.
Great place for tourists. Lots of food and things to see. Great views of the bay. There's all kinds of activities. You can also come here to sign up for deep sea fishing.
Beautiful lakeside park. You could go for a swim if you want. There's usually a couple people in the water on a Saturday.

We had a wonderful visit Monticello! Make sure you plan to spend at least 3 hours possibly even more. You can freely roam about the grounds visiting the gardens that demonstrate some of the vegetation that was grown during Thomas Jefferson's time. You will learn of his great interest and knowledge of vegetables, fruit trees, flowers, and trees. Also on the grounds is the Jefferson graveyard where Thomas Jefferson and his wife and children are buried other relatives. You actually will be led by tour guides through the house and discover many of is developments that were ahead of his time and knowledge even of architecture. The guys are very informative but sometimes we need to speak up a little louder with the groups. They even have special tours to learn about the life of the slaves at Monticello during Jefferson's time.

Luray Caverns were a must see place to visit! You will spend several hours there. Depending on the crowd and how quick your tour can enter. It is an incredible sight to see and you're allowed to take all the photographs if you want. Just an amazing underworld full of stalactites and stalagmites some made with different minerals getting different colors. There's even an underground body of water. Some years ago a man made organ pipes out of many of the stalactites. An amazing feat. This is a guide LED tour and they are very informative. Watch out for the ghost!

I took my grandsons for the Saturday morning package which included two attraction, all the putt putt you wanted to play, $8.50 worth of tokens for the arcade, a box of popcorn, and a drink. Was a great deal we had a lot of fun. You can even add on another attraction like Lasertron for only $7. They have a lot of attractions out there go karts batting cages bumper boats a driving range Lasertron even a virtual roller coaster. But our very favorite was the Hologram is a virtual game. Correction it is called hologate, tons of fun.

All of the overlooks on Skyline Drive are beautiful and breathtaking views! And information guide will help you to choose which ones you don't want to miss as there are so many you can't possibly stop at them all. Mini such as this one it is possible to just drive through and take pictures RC The View from your vehicle. There are some that you will definitely want to get out of the car and follow a short Trail for an even better View.

This is one of Shelby County's greatest assets! It is well maintained calm even occasionals security. Recently when I was riding they even had someone going up-and-down the green line blowing the leaves off the trail so you could see it easily. All of the green line is paved with asphalt and seems to be well maintained. I love the feel of being in the city but feeling like I'm out in a farce sometimes. A wonderful breath of fresh air!

Don't miss this natural wonder! This land was once owned by Thomas Jefferson and even visited by George Washington!  It is easy to make the short walk from the Park building to the Natural Bridge, but not accessible to handicap.   Just under a half mile walk beyond the massive natural bridge is a lovely waterfall. On the walk to waterfall you will pass an ancient Indian Village replica.   Amazing natural wonder!

There is nowhere in the Blue Ridge Mountains that isn't beautiful and this area on The Blue Ridge Parkway is some of the best views with many interest points. There are many overlooks that you can access easily with ample parking. Many hiking trails with some leading to waterfalls! Make sure to purchase a Blue Ridge Mountain Parkway guide so that you won't miss important areas.

We were just driving along on Skyline Drive through the Shenandoah National Park when cars started stopping and people with their phones and cameras out the car windows taking pictures! We stopped and were thrilled to take pictures and watch the bear, who didn't seem to care about us, as she went about looking at things on the forrest floor. A live bear out in the forrest!!!

Who doesn't love Elvis!!! Come visit Graceland on January 8th and celebrate the King if Rock n Rolls birthday!! Many local events and concerts going on to celebrate Elvis. People from all over the world come every year for this event. Many come in August when they recognise the anniversary of his death. A new Graceland hotel has just been open that is quite spectacular!!

An absolutely gorgeous picturesque View! If it's possible you should time this location to sit and watch the sunset! The Overlook is easy to access off the Blue Ridge Parkway side. And it seems as if you can see forever! You will few many mountain ranges miles and miles and miles. It was May and rhododendron around that area would blooming also and we're beautiful!

Beautiful beautiful beautiful!  A little bit of a strenuous hike but doable and a must see.  We enjoyed the beauty on the hike all the way to the falls. This is not something that elderly or handicapped can attempt.  For most of us we just need to stop occasionally and rest. The path is easy to distinguish so there is no fear of not finding it or getting lost.

Just look at the pictures!! Beautiful overlook on the magnificent Blue Ridge Parkway!!  This overlook is at 3830 feet elevation and has beautiful views.  As if you could see hundreds of miles!  Continue on for more spectacular views with even higher elevations.  Be there for a sunrise on the east side views and sunsets on the west sides!!

Beautiful view! Make sure to time your hike through Craggy Gardens when the Rhododendron are blooming. This area had more than anywhere i have seen on the Blue Ridge Parkway.  This overlook has more parking than any of the others. This would be a great location to watch the sunset!! About 25 miles north of Ashville on the Parkway.

There is such an amazing story behind St. Jude Hospital!  The story of it's beginnings and the founder Danny Thomas is told in this area of the hospital. You could easily spend hours viewing all the interesting and nostalgic pictures and memorabilia. There are also beautiful gardens and a gift shop. Truly worth a visit!

Not a very large Visitor Center but sufficient for the area. They have bathroom facilities, water fountains, small Cafe, information desk, souvenirs, and informative displays. A nice place for hikers to take a break. They have books and maps to inform you more of the area so that you're familiar with what you see.

Love this park/forrest!!  It is quite a surprise the first time you visit. Very unlike most of West Tennessee.  A little mountain like, heavily wooded, lakes, fishing, picnicking, 2 great frisbee golf courses, hiking, biking, camping, playground areas, beautiful nature adventure, and more.  Expect to see wildlife!

I don't think there is a bad overlook anywhere on the Blue Ridge Parkway!!  In May and June the Rhododendron and Mountain laurel are blooming and beautiful. In the fall you will see the most gorgeous array of fall colors. From this overlook you will be able to see many mountain ridges for miles and miles!!

This is a beautiful forested National Park. The Apalachee River flows through this forest.  I found large patches where native ferns were growing and also large areas covered in beautiful moss. Deer are plentiful in this area. I also saw a fox. Snakes would be common here also. I luckily didn't see any!

This is a neat overlook. I appreciate the markers to help you find the identified view.  They also have a written explanation of the name and other interesting facts about things in that area.  I learned a great deal about the different vegetation in the area and also some species of animals.

Do all you can to catch a sunset at one of the overlooks on the Blue Ridge Parkway!! These are spectacular views with elevations between 3000 and up to just over 6000 feet.  You can see for miles and miles. I counted up to 14 mountain ranges i could see!!
What an incredible place for outdoor enthusiasts,  family fun,  picnics,  hiking,  horseback riding,  canoeing,  running, biking, ziplining,etc. World's best playground for kids!  Much to do there.
Really took me back to my younger days!  Enjoyed the mixed genres  of music. Left singing all those songs for hours.  Needs a little more interactive displays.
I was quite surprised at what an interesting museum this was.  Both the Asian and Judaic sections were amazing.  Right in the heart of Memphis!
Beautiful mountain state park!  We really enjoyed hiking to the falls. Take a picnic on the hike. That trail is not for small children.
I love how everything is protected and left in a natural state.  Not commercialized!  It was so beautiful and peaceful.

Turquoise blue water and plenty of amenities await you at this public beach park!  There sandpit volleyball courts, toys for kids to play on, plenty of covered eating areas, showers, bathrooms, and even a food truck!  The beach sand was fine grained, fairly clean, and recently groomed.  Watch out - the sand can be very hot on your feet, so bring sandals!  They had also just planted sea oats near the entrance to the sand, and they look very healthy.  And they're installing artificial reef platforms offshore to reduce erosion and attract fish.  The only drawback to this beach was the parking...  Get here early or be prepared to wait for another person to leave before you can park; though there were many spaces, this park is popular and does get crowded!  Enjoy your day at the beach!

Actually quite a detailed museum on one of the greatest battles of the U.S., where over 25% of the current territory the U.S. was won.  Plenty of exhibits on both the Mexican and American sides, including art,  models, and weaponry.  The monument itself is an impressive building worthy of even the Washington D.C. area.  And the murals on the way there were of photographic detail and realism.  The grounds themselves were well kept and clean.

One of my newest favorite vistas and hiking locations in all of the U.S.!  This little rock/concrete house commands one of the most vantage points I have ever hiked to.  The place is solid enough to climb around and on top of.  And the area is so quiet that, when no one else is around, this spot is great for simply sitting still and enjoying the grandeur of the Sandia's and the panoramic views of Albuquerque and beyond...  Very peaceful!

Not your typical RMNP experience, this area feels far more remote while on trail and, in many ways, far more adventurous!  Oh sure, it has well-marked and maintained trails, wildflowers and wildlife, waterfalls and streams, lakes and tarns, and high-reaching ridgelines...  But it all feels more intimate and encompassing, rather than expansive and untouchable.  It's worth your time getting back here, to where RMNP feels so much more real.

Definitely an awesome one-time ride for a beautiful, clear day!  We could see Epcot, SeaWorld, Universal, and the Orlando Skyline.  We had a cab/gondola to ourselves, and the wait time to get on was less than 10 minutes.  Tickets at the desk were cheaper than Groupon, and even cheaper before noon!  And, best of all, one of our kids who says he's afraid of heights, had no problem with the ride at all!

Surprisingly nice beach!  Plenty of amenities including bathrooms, showers, lifeguards, food, etc.  There was plenty of parking ($5/day) and even some trails to walk.  The beach itself was expansive and peaceful, despite being somewhat in the middle of town.  Lots of shells to examine and inlet rocks to climb on.  The sand was fine and easy to lay on with just a towel.  I would definitely return!

Nice facilities and very friendly staff.  Well-organized park with beaches, coves, trails, and plenty of parking.  The sand is sugar-fine, white, and cool on the feet.  The water is fairly clear, though a bit on the green side occasionally (not in a bad way).  TIP:  Watch out for the birds!  One swooped down and snatched bread right out of my hand when I looked away for a moment!

Great forest area right off the road to several bourbon distilleries.  Plenty of open, peaceful areas of grass, forest, and lake.  Lots of fantastic trails to hike and run.  A surprising amount of terrain variability and grades.  Stunning panoramic views for the area, especially from the tree canopy walk!  Loves the art and thoughtful quotes placed around the grounds.

The last surviving U.S. battleship of World War I...  Battleships were a LOT smaller then they are today, and that is interesting in itself!  The ship has been kept up as well as possible, given its age, and the grounds around which its kept have been well maintained also.  Be prepared to pay to board the ship, though entrance to the park and grounds is free.

Great statue to visit during the day.  However, went for 9pm fire lighting 6 nights in a row and they didn't light it once, and there was no way to tell if they would or wouldn't!!  Hundreds of people parked, got out by the riverside and waited around in anticipation each night in the bugs for not...  Put the lighting schedule on a website and advertise it!

Very bumpy road up to the trailhead - only attempt if you hood clearance and confidence on large rocks with a 2WD.  No bathrooms there and parking is limited unless you're along the road.  Otherwise, its a beautiful area with historical mining significance and artifacts, remnants of a ghost town and ore mill, and trails right up Mt. Sherman and surrounds.
