Awesome view!  The bridge is definitely looking old though.  The rest area is also full of people selling various craft items at tables, though they won't actively solicit you.  The bathrooms are decent, and there are plenty of covered picnic tables with great views.  It's worth visiting if you're in the Taos area!

Very crowded with lots of working locals, rednecks, and tourists.  The majority of shops were clothing and restaurants.  There were plenty of specialty shops, and plenty of waterside items to watch near the bridge.  Parking was not free, and cars were roaming for parking everywhere.

When the sun is out and the tide is low, you can walk the sandbars out about a quarter mile into the ocean.  The water is clear and warm.  There are little stands of coconut palms to lay under in the shade.  And they groom the beach regularly.  Great for a big city, public beach!

Fantastic stop along the way to or from Independence Pass!!  Only a 0.5 mile round-trip hike from the parking lot, yet one of the most gorgeous collections of waterfalls in Colorado!  The ice cave is also a lot of fun to explore and easy to access with a little bit of scrambling!

Little kids love this park, and the bigger kids love chasing them around!  Plenty of wooden structures, slides, swings.  There's even a splash park (seasonal)!  Plenty of shade under huge trees, and plenty of parking.  And, plenty of lakefront to watch boats and planes along.

Nice little park right near downtown!  The park was hosting an ice skating rink with warming lanterns, etc.  There were toys for kids to play on, and plenty of seating.  Parking was metered, yet easy to find during my visit.  Easy access to shops and plenty of eateries!

I love coming here first thing in the morning on a any weekday...  The lines are low in the morning and, with an annual pass, I can get on all the big rides across both parks in less than three hours total (plus get in a lot of fast walking exercise)!

Great spot to hang out with your family, or not, and people watch.  Also, a nice location to watch the river flow on by, rippling over pebble and around rock.  Beautiful in all seasons, and the location of some of the town's festivities.
Great exhibits on turtle nesting and coastal habitation.   Hands on and interactive, in addition to auditorium for speakers and video.  Plus, an excellent Sea Glass Festival held every February!
Great rides, heated water (for the most part), good food options, and awesome views!  Very easy to spend all day here, without getting bored.  Highly recommendedď
Average park.  Grassy ground, though watch out for dips in the ground.  They do host a hot air balloon festival there though, which can be fun if you've seen one!
Mostly clean, though quite a few vagrants and panhandlers.  Evenings are lively, though I still get the feeling I should watch my back.
Fantastic views of the Tenmile Range and Breck ski area.  Panoramic views of Buffalo Mountain and Dillon Reservoir around the bend!
Really bumpy and the computer graphics feel a bit cheap.  Definitely not one of the better rides in the park.

Stunning Garden Key Light House was one of three lighthouses slated to be constructed in the Florida Straits in 1824. It's amazing the housing for the keepers. It's a two-story duplex for the principal and an assistant keeper, and a whose top floor served as living quarters for a second assistant keeper and whose ground floor was used as a communal kitchen. Other structures at the station included a two-story, freestanding brick oil house, and two brick cisterns, which collected the rainwater from the roofs of the two dwellings.Visit this wonderful Key Light House""
*****

Liked the nice trail in this park area. It is a concrete trail, basically a double wide sidewalk. I like to start from Shamrock Park, since there is plenty of parking. You can fish virtually at any point. It can be very windy (sometimes it feels like you are going uphill both ways even though it is flat), so be prepared for a good workout. Bring plenty of water, because there aren't many places to fill up except for Shamrock Park. You could also stray from the trail at 41/Circus Bridge to get refreshments, but other than that, you are on your own.
****

It's so peaceful/ serene and natural Park. What a great and relaxing afternoon I've had.  Liked some winding paths, exercise equipment. Lovely place to bike ride or walk in. And the best..  its so cool when the sun is overhead. Enjoy.""Can't beat the view. Near to the beach
Always clean, lots of grass to lay out in the sun, play frisbee, or just sit with lunch.
****

Peaceful and quaint garden.Can't beat the view. Directly across from and overlooking the beach.Always clean, lots of grass to lay out in the sun, play frisbee, or just sit with lunch.

This is a magnificent natural park that seems underused--you should visit it if you are in the area. This beautiful preserve park covers a large area north of Walton Road in St. Lucie county. This is a beautiful place with a fresh water marsh or savanna. Also you can take a guided kayak or canoe around the marsh on Friday and Saturday mornings for $10. Life jackets are provided. This marsh is beautiful all times of the year with different flowers and plants in bloom. Awesome.
****

This is such a nice part of downtown to walk in.  The views are lovely! They also now have water taxis to take you around this area if you don't want to work.  This is a great spot to enjoy the weather and beautiful views of Tampa! You can also run and bike here.  There's lots of attractions around like the Tampa Museum of Art and venues for theater and concerts like Amalie and Straz Performance center.  They also often have festivals in the area.
*****

Great park. Don't come without a blanket. They have restrooms.Too many people are going there but it's still clean. On the north park of the park they have a steep hill where you can also lay down and enjoy even a better view to Manhattan. They have a flea market on Saturday, keep in mind you're not alone and around 2-4 pm could be super crowded. The Manhattan view is great.On weekdays it's more quiet and it's perfect place for a date as well.
*****

Los Robles open space and trail is a short trail shooting off the fire road. I liked this trail.It's pretty rutted out, but is a fast ride. It has some sharp turns at the top, a pretty off camber section in the middle, and some random bridges to play on. So climbing up Los Robles was not hard for me. In fact, it's a pretty easy climb but there are plenty of rocks and switchbacks to navigate making it interesting.
****

Main park in the city of Torrance. Come here for the Farmers Market, baseball games, batting cages, roller/hockey rink, soccer. Really ready for picnics and birthday parties.Everything you will need in a park.  Free parking at every corner of the park. You can also find Street parking along the neighborhood. Currently, parts of the park need more improvements and update facilities as restrooms.
*****

I swam a lot here as this park offers a unique,year-round opportunity for swimming in the Intracoastal Waterway. A guarded swimming area provides easy water access for people of all ages. The adjacent beach lies in the shadow of the Blue Heron Boulevard bridge and offers the perfect opportunity to cool off from the hot sun! It's really worth a visit if you are in the surroundings.
****

Awesome little gem museum. So much information about the area and the settler people. I often go to local museums and rarely be disappointed. This nice museum also talks about the hurricanes, the strength of the pioneer people, the Native Americans, the animals and news articles by professionals. There are artifacts and great staff  to talk with for more information. Enjoy.
****

Quaint and only a few steps away from Wall Street's famous charging bull, this little teardrop shaped park offers quiet refuge from the tourist trap that ensnares dozens at any given moment. The real centerpiece of the Bowling Green is a lovely fountain. This is a highly energetic place. It is the oldest public park in NYC and is really a nice oasis. Plus theres the bull.
*****

This trail lengt has round 8 miles, paved, and equestrian unpaved areas.It's the westernmost state rail-trail, winds through the historic town of Milton. Nice place. There was an enjoyable trip into the countryside where wooden bridges cross several creeks and native wildflowers dot the landscape. The paved trail was it perfect walking and birdwatching.
****

Lushly park!  I feel very safe going there to walk alone and when I go jogging.  Very clean and well kept. A hidden gem located off of the hustle and bustle known as Biscayne.   Best part is that it is guarded by a guard house.It has all of the amenities that you would look for.  I love how you can rent a kayak or even a sailboat for super cheap. Enjoy.
****

Awesome, wild and huge forest.  So many  leisure activities on here. Camping and Lakes. Some long distance trails. Enjoy a nice kayak tour. Wildlife is all around. So be aware of some massive alligators on the area that wander around out of  water. Often these reptiles take a nap only a few steps from you while walking.

Visit  the Key West First Legal Rum Factory to see how rum is made and distilled. Very friendly and accommodating staff. We purchased the rum and definitely did and it tasted just as great as we remembered. The shot glasses we purchased came with a tasting of 6 different items of theirs. Definitely worth the visit.
****

I enjoyed this newly renovated lushly park that houses great sort of amenities as a softball field, basketbal courts, tennis courts, an open area for picnics and family gatherings. Also there is a Boy’s and Girl’s Youth Club where kids can go when school lets out for activities. Visit.
****

Gorgeous place to hike and see wildlife. We had a nice day here.The florida trail was nice and manicured so no trampling thru large tall grass. The managers were able to come say hi too. Highly recommend this reserve! Beautiful place. Free camping.
****

Peaceful area here. Views are unique. Like  being on the water in this pleasant little spot. A great place to relax and just take a moment out of your otherwise busy day.  Often sunny and hot but I like it on summer.
****

Amazing park has lots of ride on toys that are great for toddlers on up.
This park is the perfect place to cool down on a hot day! The twin seals act as fountains in the summer, and are open to everyone. So much fun!
****

I visited JBWR and it's a bird sanctuary with more than 330 avian species living over a variety of habitats, along with other native wildlife. Here I went to a gorgeous sunset tour, and took an amazing hike.
****

Awesome park for Kids. This is a  government spending done okay "The upgrades to this lovely local park include bathrooms, water-fountains, a small parking area and a whole lot more tennis courts. Visit it.
***

What a Great Sledding Spot"" So I entered the park from the southern end to get to the ideal sledding hill  which comes with a view of the New Jersey Palisades. Enjoy.""
****

Lovely small quaint recreation park. It has a nice dog park area. While drinking a beer in the picnic  shelter,  I could saw many well trained pets running on ranks.
****

in fact I just call it the "59th Street Bridge", as do most resident New Yorkers.  The "Ed Koch Queensboro Bridge" is just too many words.
****

One of the most beautifuul parks i've ever seen. There, you can rest, launch, work, study... All this in a quiet an simple way.
****

The Emerald Pools can be reached via the Kayenta trail which starts at the Grotto shuttle stop. Just cross the river from there. The views of the Zion Canyon from that trail are marvelous. The Upper Emerald pool itself is situated somewhat shaded at the foot of a massive red rock wall towering above you. Great place to do a vertical panorama picture with your phone! The hike over the Kayenta trail is moderately difficult - make sure to have decent walking shoes and take enough water.

Sunrise Point is very conveniently located close to the entrance of Bryce Canyon National Park and also very close to the Bryce Canyon Lodge. It offers sweeping views of the Bryce Amphitheatre with great lighting at sunrise obviously, but also at other times of the day. It is also the starting point of the Navajo Loop trail, which descends into the Amphitheatre. If you do one thing at Bryce, is walk this trail to get up close and personal with the Hoodoos.

Bryce Point offers magnificent wide-angle views over the Bryce Amphitheatre from the southern direction looking west, north and east. So essentially interesting lighting during the whole day. Probably best at sunrise when the sun lights up the edge of the plateau. Bryce Point can be reached easily by car from the main park road HW63, but also by walking along the Amphitheatre rim, e.g. coming from Sunset point at the Bryce Canyon Lodge.

Temple Square is where all the key buildings of the Church of Latter Day Saints are concentrated. It is also where the city of Salt Lake City was started by Brigham Young who selected the location to build the Temple. It all looks very clean and well maintained, almost as if it were not real but a really good replica. no doubt the Church pours a lot of effort in this. Pleasant to visit being car-free as well.

The JFK memorial at first appears a bit stern and too much bare concrete, but once you get up close and inside it is actually quite evocative. It is clear America is still very much mourning their most royalty like President and is still wondering how it all could happen. A pity he could not live to see his moonshot become reality, the most significant achievement of mankind in the 20th century.

The Temple was built by the successor to the Mormon prophete, Brigham Jones, who determined its location, therewith starting Salt Lake City. It is not accessible to non-Mormons but there is an attractive maquette in the South Visitor Centre, where young faithful are happy to provide explanation. It is so well cared after that it looks more like a replica than an actual 150 year old building.

Very friendly and helpful clearly some what religious staff will welcome you and are keen to explain about the Mission in Sonoma. It is what remains of the once large and flourishing northernmost Mission to be built along the famous Camino Real. Now some seven rooms are still there including a handsome chapel. Nice displays about the history of the Mission(s) and a small bookshop.

Not sure why this location is called Hausboote "auf Deutsch", but anyway. Unique collection of House Boats, often very nicely designed, decorated and maintained. On at least one pier (A-Dock if I remember well) the public has access or at least it is not explicitly denied as on other piers ... so you can have an up close with the lovely floating residences.

The San Antonio Museum of Art is nicely located in a repurposed industrial facility (the Lone Star Brewing Company) along the famous Riverwalk. It has a rather excellent collection of recent art - in particular very impressive the Asion collection. Very much worthwhile of your visit, on equal footing with the McNay in terms of attractiveness in my opinion.

Great to see the oldest winery of the Sonoma valley alive and kicking after the 2017 bush fire that almost consumed it. They had a wine sale going on, leading to free tasting and and quite good prices starting even at 5 dollars, uncomparable with snobby Napa valley where the prices maybe start at 20 bucks. Overall great experience at Buena Vista.

Moody's Gardens is a really nice nature oriented theme park in sunny Galveston. It features an aquarium, an artificial rainforest, butterfly garden, and expansive outdoor facilities including a really nice pool. This is were you can easily spend a full day or even several days with a family, but it is also attractive for adults alone to visit.

Union Square is always a great place to be in San Francisco, really the heart of the city. It becomes especially nice at Christmas time when the big tree is erected and the skating rink opens. Also the upscale business surrounding the square, such as e.g. the Macys department store, do their very best to contribute to the Christmas atmosphere.

The McNay is a delightful local art museum with a choice of great artifacts from all kinds of heritages and eras but still somehow quite coherent. The building is also attractive in itself. Loved the sign "Please do not pet the sculpture" - almost a work of art in itself. A great place to spend some time in San Antonio.

The tabernacle looked interesting on the outside, but could not be visited on the inside because the carpet was being replaced. Hence the famous choir had also moved temporarily to the conference centre. A bit disappointing although I understand of course that even in the tabernacle the carpet does not renew itself.

The Old Red Dallas Museum is in the former historical Old Red Courthouse ... originally completed in 1892. It is quite a pleasant and richly decorated museum about the history of Dallas including some of the darker sides of that history. Very informative if you are in the city for the first time.

Little Bald overlook is one of the vista points on the highly scenic Blue Ridge Parkway. Definitely worth a stop and a few pictures. On the Parkway, you need a lot of extra time for making stops at the various overlook points. Usually there is enough space even to park a Recreational Vehicle.

Union Square is a great place to be at Christmas time (and Christmas time start early in America, as early as late October ....). There is a very large decorated Christmas tree, and of course the famous ice skating rink. A major attraction for tourist and locals alike.

Parked our car here in the early morning en route to the Zion-Mt. Carmel Highway, but were quickly chased away by the Zion Shuttle driver. However did manage to snap a shot of Isaac, Abraham and Jacob, lit up very brightly in the early morning sunshine.

Hemisfair park was built in 1968 to host the Hemis Fair on the occasion of the 250 year anniversary of the city. It is now a delightful park to spend time in, dominated by the huge Tower of the Americas, very much worthwhile to visit.

Pretty upscale well appointed Museum with good displays, audiovisual exhibits etcetera. Obviously a really big Lone Star on the outside. Pretty good for children and adults alike. Nice gift shop. Not bad to kill some time in Austin.

The Natural Bridge is an archlike feature naturally eroded in the sandstones and limestones of the Bryce geology. It can be reached very easily by car from HW63 which passes through Bryce Canyon park.
At the same time authentic and touristic Chinatown with great choice of restaurants and specialty shops selling Chinese style ornaments. Not to be missed for the San Francisco tourist.
The Android figurines are getting a bit worn out, but still represent a very significant legacy of software development. And are fun subjects for a photoshoot!
Pretty strategic location to place a toilet facility - at the head of the sizable Clingsman's Dome parking area. It gets busy too, in weekends.
A must see in San Antonio for Texas historical reasons. But from a touristic perspective, the Mission San Jose has much more to show.

The best time to take a picture with lights are at night. This is the picture of the entrance of the Los Angeles County Museum of Arts (LACMA).  It is the largest art museum in the US and located right next to the La Brea Tar Pitts & Museum.

Each year, about 1.5 million people visit the museum and take a selfie in front of these lights which have become a popular photo-attraction especially at night when they are lit in the dark. These 202 lights are restored street lamps from the 1920s and 1930s which were once lit in Southern California. Together they are actually a large-scale assemblage sculpture designed by the artist Chris Burden.  Currently a retrofit project is underway by the Leonardo DiCaprio Foundation to replace these incandescent light bulbs with LED bulbs to reduce 90% in power savings as well as emissions of greenhouse gases and other harmful pollutants.

In November'14,  the L.A. County Board of Supervisors approved a $600-million makeover plan which is to tear down the three buildings that made up the museum’s original 1965 campus and to build a 410,000-square-foot new building.  This new building is scheduled to break ground in 2018 and complete construction in 2023.  By then, an underground train station connected to Downtown LA, Koreatown and Weswood will be open at the corner to attract more visitors.

This is the outside of the La Brea Tar Pits & Museum located about 5 miles south from Hollywood, Los Angeles.  This is a historical landmark in California. Inside there is a museum with fossils from 1901 excavation and enclosed lake sized pits filled with tar and gas bubbles.  These pits are 9-23 feet deep.  Before the excavation, animals had gotten stuck in the tar and died inside.  Scientists used the Carbon-14 radiometric dating method to determine the ages of fossils and some  were dated at 44,000 years old, 46,800 years old, and 55,000 years old.

I recently did an energy audit in a nearby building where I intended to add solar calculations since the roof gets plenty of sunshine.  I found out the building is seating on crude oil and the roof cannot handle the load of solar panels. The management pumps out crude oil frequently and disposes as hazardous materials. This info came as a shock to me because that area has several high rise buildings.  Some of the buildings were designed in the pre-computer era and built with strong foundation that has allowed them to stand firm after all these years.

This park is located right next to one of the wealthiest colleges in the country. Still the people in the park are mostly homeless people. There were some kids playing but they too were from low income families. The park is certainly not for everyone to come like the Oan Pacific Park next to the Grove. Educated families will go to thr Natural History Museum next door but won't come to this park for safety reason.

This is probably one of the most visited places in the world!

You can bring kids or just self.  Good place to walk on the beach for a good mile walk on the sand. You'll feel your legs are exercising while walking on the sand.  You can eat there too.  Parking is inside but the best way to get there is by the Expo line which is only a few blocks away where the mall is.

This park is about a half an hour walk up the hill from the APU/Citrus Station. You can see the whole Azusa and the valley from there because it is situated at a higher altitude. Beautiful view! Nice place to have a quiet time! Several beaches are there to sit. Across the street is the entrance of another park that goes under the street. Great place to walk with kids!

Another tiny park in the neighborhood! I came to the area before to see all the parks but couldn't see all of them. Then I went back and barely made this park before sunset. Good place to bring kids! There are clean restrooms unlike most parks in the neighborhood. The area was designed for residents to go to the park as there are 12 tiny parks within a few miles.

The whole community shows up on Sunday mornings especially!  It's nice to see men from all races play basketball together.  They're having a Chinese New year celebration on Feb 1.  For everyday activity, you can jog there. Kids can play and there are also exercise equipment.  Good place to hang out with the family on weekends.

This park has a basketball court where the residents around there get together and play. There is also a fully functioning restroom. There's also a grass area where you can have picnic. Outside the park is the Walk Path that runs for a mile. If you go north, you will see the Summit Park and the top of the mountains.

Best place to bring your kids to and help them get interested in science!  They will see the space shuttle Endeavor and all its parts.  Outside is a beautiful rose garden. The best and the cheapest way to go there is to take the Expo Line train to USC/Expo station. You can also walk from the Expo/Vermont station.

Until you go in, you won't believe something so big can be so beautiful!

The building with the parking is literally one block long.  One side is the train station, Music Center and the other side is the freeway.  Then you go in and see more beautiful interior.  It's breathtaking!

It's nice to see some green patch in the middle of a busy city.

The Park is located across from the Pacific Design Center and right next to the library and therefore I stopped by.  There are benches.  Separate areas for dogs.  Some people were playing basketball in the court.

Great place to jog in the morning!

This is like an island that is connected to the Harbor Road.  You can walk or jog from Hilton to the Convention Center to the park and come back.  You can also have lunch at the Joe's Crab shack or take a cruise by the ships there.

This place is right next to the Universal City train station and few minutes walk from the Universal Studio.  It's a historic place and a landmark.  You'll learn about the early settlers of California here.  They are only open twice a month.

I didn't expect such a beautiful park to be there. It's a block away from the Southwesr Museum station in Highland Park. All the trees are sycamores, and hence the name.  It's also too large to see the other end. Great for the family!

I was in Bradbury area and went through all parks in the neighborhood. The whole walk took 3 hours. This park is rectangular and by the bike path. Nice place for a picnic. The whole neighborhood is beautiful and good for relaxing.

Best time to be there is at night! You'll see a huge bright red building at the corner of Wilshire and Fairfax. You won't see how beautiful this red building looks at night of you don't go there in the late afternoon.

It's short but fun train ride.  You just go up and down.  Located across from the Grand Central Market.  You can eat there and then go for a ride.  The Red and Purple line train station is also right there.
This park wasn't there few years ago. It's nice to walk into some green after a visit from the beach. It's so big that you can walk to through the park from the City Hall to the Pier.
This is a small green patch with trees located in front of the Korean Radio building. It's nice to rest under those tress in an area where there are so many buildings and no green.
I used to go there a lot when I lived close by. People played tennis at 6am. Some where exercising on the equipment. It's a large park with soccer field and tennis courts.
This area is so hot that a park with so many trees can provide the shade and cooling. It's several blocks long. Oxnard side is a little small. The other side is huge!
This place is huge! Two thirds of it is soccer fields. There is a walking/jogging area too. Great place to exercise esp in the morning breeze  and play sports!
It's located right outside the USS Midway Museum and behind the big soldier statue. I would have missed it had I not dined at the restaurant next door.
This was built beautifully with all the good intentions but in an area that is a himekess paradise. It was scary to take pics there.
Up until now, I thought it was a part of the USS Midway Museum since it is located at the parking next to it.

I've visited Seven Falls multiple times over the last few decades and most recently visited for the first time since the changeover in ownership to the Broadmoor hotel & resort.

The park has been renovated and restored to much of its former status, with a few man made landscape items that decorate the walkways. The waterfalls look much as they did before the flood of 2012, as well as the staircases and observation decks.

Still a very scenic place, and great place to sit back and watch the water falls.

My only criticism is the new shuttle service that was introduced by the Broadmoor. First was incorrect information. I was told I would need to walk the .8 miles each way from the ticket office to the falls and that the shuttles were mostly for elderly or handicap use. Because of this I left my camera tripod behind because I already had a heavy backpack of camera gear. I later found out about 50% of people ride the internal park shuttle for $2. The shuttle is included for free on senior citizen admissions but is available to everyone.

In the past you could drive out to the falls entrance and park, now you have to park at the Broadmoor, wait for a shuttle, ride to the Falls park, wait in line to buy a ticket, wait for the 2nd shuttle or walk the .8 miles, wait for another shuttle back to the ticket booth or walk the .8 miles , then wait for another shuttle back to the resort. If your completely unlucky like me and happen to get to the shuttle stop every time its recently left, it can be a 15 minute wait each time, and a 7 minute ride on each of the 4 shuttles.

Waiting 4 times, riding 4 times, and purchasing tickets, I spent about 1.5 hours either waiting for shuttles or riding on them.

Due to this new mandatory shuttle service you need to allot at least 2.5-3 hours for a visit to the Seven Falls. Especially if you plan to walk the stairs and walk the pathways.

Even so, If you've never been to Seven Falls I recommend visiting at least once. The price is very affordable at $16, It just takes a bit more time now than it did in the past.

On a side note, since I had to park at the Broadmoor Resort I took a walk around that property as well for the first time (another place worth visiting).

Decent stop while heading up or down the mountain. Good place for snacks, but some items are a little pricey.

I originally visited the location thinking this was going to be more of an apple orchard store with a huge assortment of apple items. Overall the variety of items inside seemed to be less apple items and more a variety of snacks and gifts. I saw cherry cider at the time, but no apple cider which was what I had come in for, as I remembered buying fresh apple cider from a place out in Arizona as a child.

They carried candied nuts, roasted nuts, and a variety of pies and fudge. The fudge seemed to be one of the more popular items being sold along with the apple pies which were featured on a roadside sign. They did carry an assortment of apple items, I saw some candied apples, and apple butter, and apple pie, but overall the massive amount of other items in the store overwhelms the apple items. I feel like the apple focus was lost in the chaos of the crowd and the huge variety of non apple items.

The store had a country feel to it, but the staff was busy at the time we visited. It was peak tourist season when families were traveling with kids on summer vacation.

We did leave with some snacks for the trip ahead, I cant say I found what I was looking for or that I experienced something overly unique, but I would be willing to return and take another look, I didn't get a chance to sample the apple pie.

Great place to take kids. Its a unique experience riding a steam/coal train over a distance.

While the distance this train covers isn't very far the ride lasts a little under an hour each way, its far better than the short rides you find in amusement parks or train museums. I've only had a similar experience in Northern New Mexico or Colorado. So this is as far as I know the only place to get the full steam train experience in Texas.

The scenery can be great when riding in the fall. Tickets are a little pricey on regular days, but if your willing to spend the extra special event rides can be found via the website. These rides are during peak foliage seasons or holidays and sometimes include a meal on the train.

The train is very photogenic and the areas next to the engine and in front of the engine are completely accessible while the train is warming up and being loaded. This means you can get out there and shoot photos from any angle you want with no fences, obstructions or limits on your photography. Since the train moves at a semi-slow pace about 25mph, many photographers travel ahead of the train by car, setup and shoot photos, then tear down and setup again further down track for another set of photos.

I've ridden the train 2 times, first as a child around 12 years old, and then again in my early 20s. Most recently I've returned to do photography.

Found this place by searching for non mainstream things to do in Colorado Springs. The museum staff seemed partly surprised when I arrived.

I met a wonderful gentleman name Regis, who was my tour guide. I told him about how I was doing a photography trip, and wanting to shoot photos, and he told me that once the tour was over,  I was welcome to go back and shoot as much as I wanted.

The museum had a great selection of historical items detailing the old railroad and electric trolley systems of Colorado Springs. The tour included a model train and toy exhibit, a ride on an antique silver trolley bus, and  he even took me into the areas where the wood cars were being rebuilt and restored.

Regis was overly patient answering any and all questions I had, letting me find good positions for lighting, even stepping out of the way so that I could get great shots of the woodwork and the insides of the street cars with no one in the pictures. Before leaving I snapped the attached photo of him in front of one of the street cars.

This was an experience I will never forget thanks to the excellent tour guide and friendly staff working at this museum. I will return again in the future with others traveling with me.

I highly recommend this place for any history or train enthusiast, as well as those traveling with kids.

Beautiful park with lots of scenery. Excellent place for fishing, walking, photography and getting out into nature.

A historical drive thru an old iron ore mining town takes you through the woods on a dirt road that was a lot of fun. Gave me a chance to exercise the 4 wheel drive a bit. A hiking trail on this drive will take you back to a huge pit where the ore was mined.

In the main part of the park a fish hatchery is lined with a sidewalk where you can see thousands of fish. Wheels and screens help sort the fish by size into holding areas. Fish food can be bought from little feeders in the area.

The sidewalk leads back to a natural spring which has created a lagoon about 15 feet below ground level. Its flowing with fresh water and has bright blue an green colors. Along with fall colors at the time of my visit the scenery was excellent.

Across the way were the many old brick and stone structures that used to be iron ore forges. Historical plaques describe what each place was and how they were used.

The park is an excellent place for nature, history, or a picnic in the park. I spent a few hours snapping photos and didn't see but a small part of the park. I inquired on my way out about camping, which is allowed.

It's always fun visiting Carlsbad Caverns. I've walked the cave probably a dozen times now. Every time I go through a spot little things I didn't see before.

It's a great place to do photography if you have the patience. It takes patience with the other people walking on the narrow pathways. The best time if you're going for a photography is the offseason the spring or fall when people aren't traveling on summer vacation and kids are in school.

The Visitor Center and other areas of the park have had some improvements over the years. But the majority has stayed the same since the 80s.

If you have the time and are staying in Carlsbad for the night I recommend going to the bat flight. It's definitely something different and you will see anywhere else.

Allow yourself at least two to three hours to walk the cave if you are walking down from the top. More if you plan on doing photography. I suggest people start in the earlier morning around 11 walk down, ride the elevator up take a break and eat lunch either in the cafe at the bottom of the cave or the top. Return back down to the bottom and walk the large room finishing some time around 1 or 2 in the afternoon.

Admission to this museum is very affordable. Its a great place to take the kids.

A variety of displays spans many aspects of space exploration. From actual rockets & motors to a Star Trek transporter and actual Tribble from the series the museum offers something for everyone.

If you have kids this place has many displays that are geared specifically for them. A lego area, a place to dress in an astronaut suit and take pictures with a moon background (they have adult sized suits), and all sorts of hands on items.

On my visit a cockpit from a stealth bomber was in front of the building.

In addition to the museum, other buildings are available for visit within the complex. A rocket car track, and a movie theater with additional displays are located nearby.

Also "Ham" the astrochimp's gravesite is located next to the flags near the parking lot.

Plan to spend at least 1-2 hours walking the grounds and the 4 floors of the building.

All in all, its a fun place to visit, it wont break the bank, and no matter your age, you'll walk away feeling it was worth the stop. I wouldnt consider it a must do, but if you have the time I would suggest stopping.
likes: Unique artifacts (e.g., Star Trek items, stealth bomber cockpit)

reviews_attraction.text:
Amazing Experience.

This is one of those must do at least once things. I've ridden the Durango railroad at least 3 times in my life now and will probably do it again. Summer rides and winter rides are vastly different. I've not had the opportunity to do one of the Christmas rides.

I usually opt for the train ride out and bus ride back for the additional fee. Especially since my track record for successful trips on the train has been pretty bad. When I say this, on 2 of my trips the train has broken down. Delaying the one way by as much as 2 hours. But that's some of the fun of riding on an authentic coal powered steam engine.

Riders are given the choice to purchase tickets in different types of cars, the cheapest being the outdoor coach cars with bench seats. At the end of the trip your almost guaranteed to have some bits of coal on your face and hair.

Scenery and the experience of riding the railroad in a remote mountain area are reason enough to do this, but every trip I've taken has been a bit different.

I highly recommend this to families traveling with kids about 10 and older, or photographers visiting the area.

Have visited here many times, many people might think this is a lot like visiting a beach, but its not.

Sleds can be rented at the front of the park, and ridden down the dunes. Evening walks and presentations are offered by park staff at sunset. A boardwalk that travels between the dunes is available for those who want an easy walk.

The sand in the park is actually gypsum, due to its type its not sticky and messy like most beach sand. The dunes are high enough that in the evening you can sit at the base of a dune and get shade.

If you walk across the dunes you will see small bug tracks that leave interesting patterns, as well as wind patterns in the sand.

The park is also great for sunset photography and odd looking photos as colors pop out on almost a solid white background.

Theres always some spots available, even during holiday weekends. However its nice to visit when the park is almost empty and its peaceful.

Bathrooms are available in the park, as well as BBQ pits and picnic areas with roofs.

If you've never visited its a must see. Pack a lunch, or head out to the park in the afternoon for an evening walk.

Stopped here completely by chance while driving around the Albuquerque area doing photography. The property was very scenic and was what caught my eye from the road.

As soon as staff saw we had cameras we were asked if we had been taking pictures outside. We were told photography was not allowed on the property without a permit from the owner. We were also told that the owner was very strict about this because he rents the property for events and had invested a lot into making it look the way it does. For a moment it seemed like they were going to ask us to delete any photos we had while standing in front of them.

We stayed and tried a few of the white wines, none of which stood in my opinion. They spoke highly of these wines, comparing them to wines from California and other countries, but the pricing on the wines was high in comparison to other vineyards. Most bottles started at $20 and went as high as $45 for the Port wine.

Overall we were disappointed by the wine, prices, and photography policies. While its a beautiful property, I don't see myself returning in the future.

I come from Texas wine country and have visited many a vineyard here and while traveling. The customer service received at St. James winery was more than excellent.

I described the wines I  liked and had found at other places in my travels and they checked off a few on the tasting list for me to try. The employee helping me was not only overly accommodating but super friendly. I stood at the counter having a conversation for about 20 minutes. I had originally planned to pop in and out on my way thru town, but was having such a good time conversing and tasting wines I ended up being in the store about an hour.

I tried many of the sweet wines, and some of the seasonal wines they were offering, and found a few I liked, they even mixed a blend of 2 for me, to try and come close to a wine I had found elsewhere.

I ended up leaving with a few bottles including their seasonal mango wine which I purchased for a friend of mine. Overall it was a great experience. I would definitely recommend stopping in while passing by. Excellent customer service..

Not the fanciest of casinos. Pretty minimal on the inside. I've stopped here a couple times while passing through Miami on my way up I-44.

On my last trip I decided to try the snack bar. A minimal selection, and average prices. I ordered the sampler that is your choice of 3 items from the appetizer menu. I had the mini corn dogs, fried mushrooms, and  onion rings. They were out of the Jalapenos, and the mac-n-cheese bites.

The wait for the food wasn't too bad. I sat down at a nearby slot machine while waiting. Was probably about 10 minutes to get my food. The order was a good amount of food for $6.50, but everything being fried and some items a little greasy or overcooked,  it wasn't the best choice for a meal while traveling down the road on an empty stomach.

I've visited the other nearby casino's and prefer the others to this one. I haven't had any better luck as far as the gaming goes, but have enjoyed some good meals at the other casinos.

** This Casino Offers Complimentary Soda Machines **
** Has Some TV Show Themed Machines **

Very nice casino, with decent offers from time to time.

While visiting Hot Springs I wasn't expecting to find a nice sized casino. Hot Springs has now become a stopping point for me while traveling in the area. The casino is very nice looking, modern and seems to be a safe location, with security inside and out, as well as shuttle service to your car.

On my first visit the casino was offering a $2.99 steak eggs and hashbrown special at midnight. On my 2nd visit I tried the frito pie, which was a huge plate, and had OK flavor, but a bit pricey for snack bar food at a casino.

The casino itself though has a decent selection of slot machines, a large amount of penny machines, and several table games as well. Slot club staff was friendly, I visited one time on my birthday, and I've had conversations with them about random things now on my most recent visits.

Its a fun place to stop, a decent plate to grab late night food, and a good evening activity when staying in the Hot Springs area.

Ive been visiting Johnny Nolans for decades now and its always an enjoyable experience. While its not one of the largest casinos in Cripple Creek they frequently have specials going.

Staff here is friendly, I have better luck getting drinks service at the slot machines here, and the slot club even when not attended gets someone to assist you pretty quick. So theres definite perks to visiting some of the smaller casinos on the street.

On the downside many of their promos, drawings and specials require you to return days later. Promos like birthdays and stuff are sometimes only good 1 day. I live over 1000 miles away, so even when I win a slot drawing, I loose the chance to win anything because Im only in town for a day or  two.

I'll continue returning, I sometimes find slot machines here no one else has, but I wish their promos were usable more by travelers. They seem to be more of a locals casino catering to the Colorado Springs area.

One of my favorite parks in Texas. Its a great place for picnics & photography.

I frequently visit this park just to walk around and shoot photos of the scenery and wildlife. A wide variety of animals are present in this park.
Ive seen crawfish, ducks, geese, albino salamanders, numerous types of migratory birds, and what I think were nutria and beavers.

Theres some nice places to take portraits here, gazebos and a river, wooden bridges, its really the perfect spot to brush up on your photography skills.

The park is usually quiet in the off seasons. Theres lots to do here as well for kids during the summer, including a swimming area, train rides, playgrounds, and pool.

No matter what your looking for this park has it.. Ive even gone GeoCaching here. If you've never been to this park its definitely worth a try.

Great park to get some cardio workout. Recently renovated and paved, fresh walking paths wander up a hill to Comanche Lookout Tower.

The park while unknown to many San Antonians was used as a lookpout post by the indians in the 1800's. In the early 1940's a landowner who envisioned building a house much like a castle poured the foundation and built the tower that now stands at the top of the mountain.

The hill is the 4th highest point in San Antonio at 1340ft. From the top long sweeping views of the all areas around can be seen.

The park does not allow motorized vehicles, but does allow bikes.
If you live in San Antonio and have never been to this park you should visit. Its a different experience compared to the many parks in town that are almost completely flat.

The park is especially busy in the evening.

Been to the Living Desert Zoo at least 3 times now. Its easily accessible just off Hwy 285 as you leave the north end of Carlsbad. The zoo is located on a desert hill side and has some very scenic views.

My favorite exhibits for photography are the prairie dog village, and the walk-thru aviary which contains roadrunners and other birds that are just feet away from you.

Staff is always friendly and the park is almost never crowded. Its a great place to take your time without having to worry about your photography getting in other peoples way.

Admission is cheap and the zoo is not so large that you will burn up in the heat trying to see everything. 2 hours will get you thru the zoo at a decent pace.

Its a fun place for kids, and a great place for photography.

Have never been to another place like it. I visited this place as a child, then again as a teen, and again in my 30s. The park has a little something for everyone, from children to adults.

The park ambiance is unlike any other, especially being set in the mountains and pine trees. The ground littered with pine cones, trees covering many areas, with rides popping up into the trees. Many of the same rides that were there when I was a child are still in operation, or a version of them is today. One of my favorite rides as a child was the candy cane spiral slide. I remember going down it in a potato sack as a kid.

The park overall is a great place to take your kids, or even as a short stop while visiting the Colorado Springs area.

This park was recently part of an improvement project.

Brand new paved walking paths, wood bridges, parking areas, and piers were installed into the park. On my visit to the park I walked a full lap from end to end and looked at some of the improvements that were made.

A few people were sitting on the banks, one or two of them fishing, but the park was empty for the most part. The water was pretty murky and dark, but there were lots of turtles sunning on logs and an assortment of large birds including ducks and cranes.

Sadly after only 60 days people have already began leaving garbage around.

I think this place will get busier as the college finishes its expansions and summertime opens the new pool.

One of a kind stop for anyone interested in UFOs. Gift shop has a decent selection of items, but anything you cant find there can be found a short walk away as its surrounded by tons of UFO themed stores.

The museum has a great selection of displays that not only tell the story of the Roswell Crash but also other UFO related topics & cases. In addition to the museum exhibits, there is a decent research library connected to the building.

If you've never visited Roswell before this is the 1 place that you have to visit even if your on a tight schedule. You cant visit Roswell and not visit the UFO museum.

Nice roadside attraction, we stopped in to stretch the legs and use the bathroom, but shopped the gift shop and talked to the employees. We snapped a few photos, and walked inside.

The museum is attached to the gift shop and has many displays a few of which we could see as we entered the building. We were informed that the grave was a short drive from the Museum. Pictures of it were on display in the store.

Because we were on a tight schedule, we didn't tour the museum or grave site, but it might be something to see next time I'm passing thru. The employees in the store were very friendly.

When To Visit: Late March, Early April

Davey park is known for the dogwood trees, which bloom bright white flowers. The annual dogwood festival is held the last weekend of March and first weekend of April.

The park is a nice place to walk, picnic or spend time outdoors year round, but is a draw for photographers and nature lovers during the peak spring flower season. Park is open to the public year round, no admission.

A quick google search for "Dogwood Trails Celebration" will produce information about the upcoming years festival.

Have visited Black Mesa twice over the years now, and the staff is always friendly and informative.

I go to Black Mesa for the variety of wines offered. Both visits wines I have not commonly found at other vineyards were available here. For example, a German hot wine you serve with cinnamon, known as "Gluhwein" which is a spiced mulled wine, and also a oaky chocolate infused red wine.

I always look forward to tastings when visiting and seeing what they have offer. I highly recommend stopping in if your passing by.

I hadn't been to the Hemisfair park in many years, and with all the construction lately, hadn't seen any of the recent improvements made in the last 10 years or more.

Its a nice place for an evening walk, and I was glad to see the area surrounding the Tower of the Americas was a very scenic and modern. It has some nice walkways from the parking area to the tower, with historical markers, cascading waterfalls, benches, and nice tree cover.

Great park to visit, a nice view of the water, sloping grass areas, perfect for sports or Frisbee. Popular spot with people playing Pokemon the last year or two.

Has a skate park at one end of the park and is a good place to go walking. Theres also a nice playground for kids and on a good day a nice breeze coming off the water.

It was finally working! First and foremost: you pay at the top of the hill...so if you are getting on at the bottom just hold tight! They run every 10 minutes and because you are either paying when you get off or when you get on, the boarding process could be delayed. Fare is $1 each way, less with a loaded tap card. The line can be haphazard, people cutting and shoving. Once you are onbaord it is a nice 5 minute ride to the top or bottom.

One of the best preserved missions, surrounded by wonderful eateries. Which means that after a half day of touring the grounds and enjoying, what seems to be unending great weather,  you can relax and eat some great meals. This mission is particularly neat because the original site, the "ruins" resulting from the earthquake are still up and view able up close. This is one worth the trip.

Way out of the way but incredibly worth the drive. I was taken aback by the site. You drive for what seems likes forever through a road that cuts the lush green rolling hills and vineyards. Then you park and as you turn a corner, you are struck by a picturesque site laid against the backdrop of hills that look like they are floating. Careful with the rattlesnakes.

Came out here when I was kid, drag my kids out here too! If you appreciate the old west then this is one of the more hospitable ghost towns: its owner and development are the inspiration for Knotts Berry Farm! A lot of fun, lots of activity! Try panning for gold, walking through a mine shaft, or witness a "bank robbery."
likes: On-site activities (gold panning, mine walking, bank robbery show)

reviews_attraction.text: A spectacular site! It takes a while to get here, and you do have to get close to Fort Ligget for access. The site is being renovated. however, it is so far out in the middle of nowhere that you still get a phenomenal appreciation for the site and what it was like to live there. Well preserved and worth the day trip!

A phenomenal experience. We arrived on a weekday and the place was desolate (except the park ranger) so we go to run around and really explore. You are greeted by a wall of cactus! and then, around the corner, the adobe comes into view. A really neat site and it is definitely worth taking a trip to see it.

As per usual...crowded, nowhere to park, people not paying attention and streets closed for private events in the most ridiculous and inconvenient way possible. Once atop the pier, people are more interested in taking selfies than paying attention which makes the whole proposition difficult to enjoy.

The cottage is one of many sites within the LA Arboretum. It is an expansive park full of beautiful plants, a large pond, and several historical sites. This is worth the visit --either to stroll the grounds, picnic on the lawns, or get tea while looking at the peacocks.

Don't wait to take a pic with the marker...seems nobody is respectful of lines. The marker is about 100feet south of the booth commemorating the end of the road. The vista is amazing. Crowded but worthwhile...stay for the sights, sounds, and food.

Neat site and a wonderful park. Not much to see on the site itself but if you are at the Hollywood Bowl or down the street at Hollywood & Highland you should make your way up. That 1/2 mile will enlighten your understanding of Hollywood.

A little expensive but worth it. When you step of the gondola you are geared with your first glad of wine...the it is self guided but very insightful. There kids had a great time as well, the staff was absolutely wonderful.

Phenomenal! Short ferry ride. Although close to the mainland, the island feels completely remote, and because of its situation there is no wind. it has a lots of hiking and historical sites. Definitely worth a trip.
Beautiful, serene, well preserved and informational. Worth the trip to see it -watch out for the golfers and cross traffic! Incredible docents, and a very fascinating historical site.
Always a fun place to visit. Lots to see and to do. The crowds can be a bit annoying but step right or to the rose gardens and you'll feel as if you are the only one there.
Another beautifully preserved Mission and part of California History. Once you are done with the Mission you can spend the rest of the day walking around idyllic Solvang.
Breathtaking views of the Minarets and falls. Early to get to. Limited parking. There are a couple of picnic tables and frankly you can't beat the view over a nice lunch.
Quaint but fun. The museum is not huge but the history it encompasses and relates is amazing. Once you are done here, make sure you take a tour of the actual Casino.
The zoo is getting better. Weekends are tough given the large crowds and kid generally running around unattended. Viewing the animals is a little difficult.
Could not convince the party to jump on the roller-coaster but it looked fun! Old, rickety, and squeaking as it made its every turn and drop! Good luck.
Wonderful time. Great staff, lovely grounds, wide array of animals. We did the private safari tour and being that close to the animals was amazing.
Sadly, abandoned and under city control to deal with a bad pest problem. This is a California Historical site and its state made me a bit sad.
Nice aquarium, a little on the small side give  the cost. The touch tanks are fun and the kid zone has a lot for them to do. Worth  visit.
A great time for children with plenty of hands on interaction, including a river and rain simulation (bring a change of clothes).
Mono lake. To quote everyone: seems like you are on another planet. Sadly the lake is drying up so I recommend you go soon.
Very fun with a wide display of log cabins and structure. It is not overly large but the docents and site were great.

One of Rexburg’s finest landmarks is the Rexburg Stake Tabernacle, a Romanesque Revival building from 1911.

This was the tabernacle for the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints before being sold off to the city in 1980.

In the basement is a museum for the Upper Snake River Historical Society, with a major exhibit about the devastating Teton Dam collapse of 1976, which left Rexburg underwater and resulted in the deaths of 11 people and the loss of 13,000 cattle.

The total damage estimates are $2 billion and the dam has never been reconstructed. You’ll see a line on the wall marking the high water mark as well as interesting artifacts from the event and the remarkable reconstruction of the city.

Also here is an old-fashioned one-room schoolhouse, home to the Rexburg Children’s Museum, which has lots of interactive displays and activities for kids.

Completely open to the public, Grace Farms is a non-profit center dedicated to initiatives concerning nature, the arts, community, justice and faith.

The main edifice here, called The River, is worth the visit alone: Completed in 2015, it was designed by the Pritzker Prize-winning Japanese architecture firm SANAA.

Radiating a sense of peace, this long, sinuous structure is made from glass and concrete, with a Douglas fir canopy supported by steel pillars.

This houses a 700-seater amphitheater, a tea pavilion, a library, a commons space with an excellent organic cafe and a sunken court for performing arts and recreation.

Grace Farms is in 77 acres of immaculate grounds, navigated by walking trails, around the site you can seek out contemporary art installations by the likes of Teresita Fernández, Olafur Eliasson and Thomas Demand.
likes: On-site facilities (amphitheater, tea pavilion, library, cafe, sunken court)

reviews_attraction.text:
A few minutes west on the Merritt Parkway in the woods of North Stamford is a museum combining art, nature, agriculture and history.

The Stamford Museum & Nature Center is on a former private estate in 118 acres, ten of which are home to the working Hecksher Farm.

The galleries in the half-timbered Tudor Revival museum building are wonderfully eclectic, from paintings by John Singer Sargent, Warhol and Dalí to Native American artifacts, telescopes, vintage local pedal cars, keys and locks by Stamford’s famous Yale brand and farming implements.

Also here are important collections by Stamford-related artists like Gutzon Borglum (famed for Mount Rushmore) and Reuben Nakian.

On Hecksher Farm you’ll find heritage livestock breeds, as well as more exotic animals like burros, llamas and alpacas.

Slightly further out, La Perouse Bay is around ten miles down the coast from Kihei, but merits the trip to see evidence from Haleakalā’s last eruption.

This is thought to have taken place around 1790, when lava issued from the Kalua o Lapa cinder cone over Maui’s southeast coast.

This desolate but arresting lava field can be explored along the King’s Trail, a footpath built during the reign of Piʻilani at the turn of the 17th century and once encircling all of Maui.

Go slow for some amazing photos of the black lava contrasting with the blue ocean and the greenery on Haleakalā’s lower slopes.

You may share the path with dozens of free-roaming goats, and where the lava enters the ocean are tide pools teeming with life. Remember to wear sturdy shoes as the lava is sharp underfoot.
likes: Activities: Photography, Exploring lava field, Observing wildlife
dislikes: Attraction Type: Desolate landscape (if considered a dislike)

reviews_attraction.text:
Walking the Greenbelt between downtown Boise and Garden City you’ll arrive at this delightful riverside park in 150 acres.

It was all planted in the 1950s, and as well as being picture-perfect and abounding with water features, Ann Morrison Park is packed with amenities and interesting details.

You can go birding here, right in the middle of an urban environment, while there’s a series of conservation stations providing habitats for insects, bats, birds and more.

For people with pups in tow, there’s a superb off-leash dog park that has a fenced area for “shy dogs”.

Elsewhere you’ll find a children’s playground, bocce, an outdoor gym, horseshoes, an 18-hole disc golf course and even a cricket field, home to Boise Cricket Club.
likes: Outdoor activities (bocce, gym, horseshoes, disc golf, cricket)

reviews_attraction.text:
As the stainless steel silos visible from West Seltice Way might tell you, there’s a craft distillery on Post Falls’ western outskirts.

Up North Distillery prides itself on producing small-batch craft spirits, with a “farm to flask” philosophy. The selection includes barrel-aged honey spirits and apple brandies, matured for 1-2 or 2+ years.

These are made with 100% local grains, fruit and honey, and every part of the distilling process is done by hand.

The menu changes from season to season and you can visit the bar, mixing up a variety of cocktails and also pouring spirits and beers from around the region. Food trucks on Wednesdays, Thursdays, Fridays and Saturdays.

There’s an intriguing piece of history a couple of minutes from downtown Kailua at this imposing temple site.

Going back as far as the 15th century, the Kailua area was a base of power for the entire island, thanks to its irrigated fields for crops like banana and taro, abundant supply of pond fish like mullet and safe canoe landings.

Kamehameha I for instance lived in Kailua after conquering the island in 1795. The Ulupō Heiau State Historic Site attests to this importance, with a platform measuring roughly 42 metres by 55 metres, and with a height of more than 9 metres.

The stone for this structure was brought from as far as Kualoa, 10 miles up the windward coast.

When it comes to hot vacation destinations, local historical societies often end up at the bottom of the list. But for history-minded travelers without gobs of disposable cash, they’re great community resources that should be taken advantage of.

The Milton Historical Society has been around for nearly five decades and is dedicated to preserving the area’s rich history.

The museum is located in a church from the 1850s and features an impressive collection of artifacts and historical memorabilia.

Operating hours are from Wednesday through Saturday from 11 AM to 4 PM. Those traveling in groups may make special appointments with advance notice.

This quirky attraction in nearby Leslie is thought to be one of the largest telephone museums in the world.

Largely the work of just one man, the unstoppable Tommy C Smith, it was founded in 1995 and has attracted something of a cult following since.

Attractively set within a cotton mill dating from the turn of the twentieth century, there are estimated to be 2,000 items on display relating to the telephone industry.

They date right back to the earliest days of the science in the 1880s, and cover the entire history of a technology that can truly be said to have changed the world.

Leslie is approximately 12 miles southeast of Americus.

It’s not so well known outside the area, but the man who created the phonograph machine that would go on to become the world-famous Victrola was a Delaware native.

The Johnson Victrola Museum is located in Dover and houses one of the region’s most complete collections of original phonographs made by E.R. Johnson. They range from the 1890s to nearly the 1930s.

They’re impressive pieces of machinery, especially by the standards of the day. Now, many of them are exceedingly rare and priceless.

The museum is free to visit, but there’s a donation box by the door. Most visitors choose to leave a few bucks per person to help with upkeep.

At more than 3,000 acres, White Clay Creek State Park is one of the state’s largest natural areas. It’s conveniently located in Newark, just a short drive from Pike Creek.

The park offers visitors a variety of outdoor recreation options. One of its biggest draws is the creek after which it’s named, which stretches for nearly 20 miles through the scenic and undeveloped area.

Hiking, biking, bird watching, and fishing are popular park pastimes, the latter of which draws eager anglers during trout season – especially after the creek has been stocked.

There’s also a nature and visitor’s center, and historic sites as well.

Though San Francisco has more than its fair share of cloudy and rainy days every year, Livermore’s weather is generally sunnier and more conducive to outdoor activities like hiking, bicycling, and watersports.

Del Valley Regional Park is just a 20-minute drive from the city center. It is an excellent option for activity minded nature lovers interested in enjoying the great outdoors without traveling to the larger state and national parks in the region.

For those who’d prefer to spend a night or two under the stars, the park features more than 100 individual campsites, many of which have water and electrical hookups.

With so much to do at Brand Park, it’s hard to know where to begin. Rain or shine, this 31-acre complex situated at the base of the Verdugo Mountains in Glendale offers many things to see and do for all ages.

On-site there are art galleries, sculpture areas and a library. The Whispering Pine Tea House and Friendship Garden is a great place to relax with a hot beverage and some sweet treats.

The Doctor’s House Museum is where you can tour a historic house that was once the home of actress Nell Shipman. Also on site are basketball courts, baseball fields, playgrounds and a series of hiking and cycling trails.

Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory is one of the area’s largest employers. Though much of the facility is off-limits to the prying eyes of nosy visitors, it features a Discovery Center chock-full of unique and educational exhibits designed to engage inquisitive minds.

The Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory Discovery Center is a great place to spend a few hours when the weather isn’t conducive to outdoor activities. It’s generally a big hit with young and old visitors alike.

Due to the sensitive nature of much of the research conducted onsite, you’ll need to sign up for a guided tour in advance.

The ultimate way to discover the full beauty of Lake Coeur d’Alene is high on a zip line suspended in the forest canopy.

This is made possible through Timberline Adventures, which has a storefront in the city and will then take you on an open-air UTV to its massive property on the lake’s northeast shore at the aptly named Beauty Bay.

There you’ll have a choice of seven zip lines; you can ride all seven or opt for a shorter tour, always zooming from one treetop platform to the next.

Timberline has a cute treehouse on the property, which you can also visit to make s’mores, toasted over an open flame.

Spanning the Salmon River in the state forest is the last remaining covered bridge in East Connecticut.

Dating to 1840, it is one of only three crossings of its kind in the state and remains open to pedestrian traffic, although vehicles have been banned since the 1930s.

A decade before then, a truck crashed through the floor, and the ensuing renovation was carried out as a Depression-era employment initiative by the Civilian Conservation Corps.

The main bridge span is covered by a gabled roof, which has the benefit of protecting the timbers below from the weather, and slowing their ageing process.

Public art is common in the greater Los Angeles area but the Great Wall of Los Angeles, only a few minutes away from Valley Glen in North Hollywood, is an absolute must-see.

This beautiful mural, which was completed in 1979 and is more than 2,700 feet long, is officially called The History of California due to its unique historical depiction of the region. It was designed by Judith Baca and was brought to life by more than 400 local youths and artists.

The finished project is a colourful, captivating work of art that remains today as one of the longest murals in the world.

A piece of the Air Line Trail carries you through the Salmon River State Forest, a haven for hiking, fly fishing and mountain biking, or just enjoying a picnic in nature.

The Salmon River is as placid as you can get today, but in the 19th century the banks were teeming with mills.

At North Westchester there were so many factories competing for waterpower that the grist mills had to run at night and the paper mill by day.

The Blue-Blazed Salmon River Trail snakes through the park, and takes you over an important piece of heritage, which we’ll cover next.

Located in nearby Villa Rica, 16 km from Douglasville, this museum is the only one in Georgia located on the exact site where gold was found during the gold rush days of the late 1800s.

It also contains one of very few authentic gold stamping mills dating from the nineteenth century.

Beginning in the 450 square metre exhibition space, visitors are able to explore the remains of the actual gold mines where the precious metal was found.

You can then step aboard the Pine Mountain scenic railroad, which chugs its way around almost 11 hectares of parkland.

Leake Mounds is another even earlier native American site built by the Swift Creek Culture and dating to what is known as the Middle Woodland period. This goes back to the prehistoric era between 300 BC and 600 AD.

The interpretative trail of 18 markers covers around three kilometres. It details the archaeological finds discovered during digs, and what they mean for our understanding of this period of history.

The trail takes in the remains of three mounds, as well as a large semi-circular ditch or moat, and a midden – a prehistoric landfill site.

Perfect for anyone who enjoys the quirky and unusual, you’ll find Barbie Beach around 7 miles from Newnan on the road to Senoia.

This witty roadside attraction features a beach of entirely nude barbie dolls, and so charmed the producers of the hit TV show The Walking Dead that they donated some zombie dolls to the collection.

Their beachside activities are changed on a regular basis, so you’ll never quite know what you’ll come across if you pay the beach a visit. However, scenes tend to echo current events such as major sporting competitions.

Situated in nearby Thousand Palms, the Coachella Valley Preserve is an 880-acre protected wilderness area featuring diverse habitats and an abundance of things to see and do.

This preserve is one of the most popular attractions in the area and as you explore it, you’ll pass through desert wetland and palm woodland ecosystems that are home to a variety of plant and animal life.

There are 28 miles of hiking trails in the park and guided hikes are available during certain times of the year. A visitor’s centre is also on site.

The Museum of Natural History in nearby Bakersfield is a great place to visit if you’re interested in the topics of geology, archaeology, palaeontology, and anthropology.

As you browse the fascinating exhibits, you’ll see a large fossil collection originally started by Bob and Mary Ernst.

Other exhibits include The Miocene, North American Animals, Native American Lifeways, Rocks and Minerals, African Animals, and the Palaeontology Collection. Guided tours are available.

If you’re looking for an exciting night on the town, Aviator Casino is a fun place to spend an evening and you’ll have the chance to win some money.

This casino doesn’t have slot machines but has plenty of card tables where you can join in on exciting games of blackjack, poker, and more.

The on-site restaurant serves delicious meals, snacks, and beverages.

One of the best ways to spend a nice afternoon is at one of Woodland’s green spaces, and Slaven Park has just what you need for the entire family.

Here you’ll find picnic areas with BBQ facilities, a playground, a water-play area, and a large open field. Washrooms are also available.

I purchased two Viper 1 Air Combat sessions, one for myself and one for my father, who was flying in from the East Coast to visit. The Viper 1 session is a specific high-end session which takes a little over 3 hours. It includes detailed training and 3 "flights". First, I want to explain the "above and beyond" treatment we received. Second, I'll go through the experience, and lastly I'll give information on things to be aware of when you go (and I know you will - it's so much fun!) This review is only on the longer Viper 1 Air Combat sessions, I haven't done a shorter session yet (but will in the future!)

I had called FlightDeck weeks before our scheduled appointment, and speaking to their friendly receptionist, I was informed that I could call a couple of days before our actual session to schedule a time. Fast forward to my father now in Los Angeles, visiting me, with this program being the big reason he came all the way from Washington DC. When I called to lock down our date, I was informed that the Viper 1 program requires more of a heads up to reserve a time, as they shut down the facility to focus on those attending the program! I was immediately concerned - she informed me that there really wasn't much they could do, large parties were already scheduled and she couldn't get us in until AFTER my father would be flying home. She kept me on the phone for a while, exploring options, until she let me know she'd call me back.

When she did, she had fantastic news. They would be able to take us the next day. She had spoken to one of the founders/owners, and he decided to go above and beyond and come in to have a special session for us. When we arrived, we were surprised to find out that the trainers we met had all decided to come in - just for us! It was their day off, but they felt it was important to give us the best experience possible. We were truly amazed - not only where they coming in on their day off - they were also the nicest, happiest group we'd encountered in quite some time. We were also pleasantly surprised to know that a few additional pilots had come in to do some training - talk about extra special treatment!

The program is simply awesome. You suit up in flight suits, get your leg boards to take notes, and sit in the briefing room to learn from your instructor. We had "Sockeye", who was a joy to learn from. Photographs are welcome, many times they offered to take our photo, which was very helpful.

Be aware that you truly "climb" into the simulators on small ladders, replicating the feeling of really getting into a fully operational F16 cockpit. It can be a bit tricky to get in and out, just an FYI. My father is 6'7" and fit just fine. Having the cockpit canopy close and hear your flight leader speak to you via headset really adds to the experience.

Pro tips:
-- They do have soft drinks/snacks on site. If you need a break, simply ask for it. You do get breaks between each of the 1 hour training/flight sessions.
-- Ask the instructors anything at any time. Don't be nervous, they're incredibly welcoming.
-- Speak with the instructors after your flights to get candid feedback on your flight. It was really exciting to talk to them and a pleasure to hear their tips.
-- Dress casually. You may want to wear a long sleeve shirt, but no need for a jacket. Although it's cool in the space, the flight suit keeps you warm!
-- Bring your camera! Not only can you get shots of you during the day, at the end of the Viper 1 program you receive a call sign and plaque. It's a great opportunity to get photos with your instructors.
-- You don't have to have any flying experience to enjoy the day. The instructors are thorough, fun, and incredibly helpful.

I have to say this was a fantastic experience throughout. It's a joy to recommend FlightDeck to any and all. A huge thanks to the entire crew that was there that day!

Pretend City is an excellent place to take your kids and spend hours with them as they pretend to be librarians, artists, wait staff, grocery store employees, farmers, firefighters and more. It's a great way to teach values, and even comes fake money to reward "work". It can get a little crowded, especially when there are birthday parties, however on weekends it's manageable. There is a ton of parking, and tons for the kids to do inside. The staff informs parents this is a place to play WITH their children, so they literally ask people don't use their cell phones.

Four stars only because there aren't a ton of employees on the floor, so asking for help with something can be a bit of a challenge. In addition, I've seen a kid vomit onto a small plastic vehicle for riding, and the parent whisked them away but didn't notify anyone. Since there aren't a slew of staff on the floor, the incident wasn't noticed.

Overall though, a really wonderful place to let imaginations take over!

Sand Dune Park is comprised of three distinct areas. The first is what it's name after - the Sand Dune. This imposing dune is a great place to work out. Be aware that it does require a reservation (which is great, as it limits the amount of people on the dune and provides you with a better experience) online with a fee of $1.

The second area is a gated playground, which provides ample entertainment for kids. It has two large features with slides, two sets of swings, and more. A small, but nice (and typically quiet) playground.

The third area has benches, hot box for grilling, bathrooms and a decent sized grassy field. To have a birthday party here, or other events, strongly recommended that you reserve the space through Manhattan Beach.

Parking is limited to the North and South of the park, and be aware that this park is in the middle of a densely populated neighborhood.

It's a great place to work out, spend time with your kids, or eat and throw a frisbee!

Amazing museum with incredible art! A must stop when you're in Los Angeles! There is parking in the building as well as locally. There are two ways to enter the museum, via pre-purchased tickets, or in the wait line. The wait line lets you get in on a timed manner only if people do not show up for their reserved day and time.
