The exterior and interior of the museum are incredible, and have their own stories. Be sure to take your time in the museum, the amount of artwork is amazing. Keep your eyes open, as you walk down the stairs between floors, windows have been designed to provide you with a view/glimpse of other artwork waiting to be put out on display. It's staggering how much artwork is in the building!

Pro tip - there is a large sculpture of an oversized table with chairs. Do not touch this. There are staff (very friendly) who keep an eye on it at all times.

First of all - this is a small museum. Let's get that out of the way. Second, you have membership here if you are a member at the Natural History Museum of Los Angeles. Third, although the museum may be small, it's still a ton of fun and very educational!

The museum is shaped like a circle, and you go through it clockwise. There is an inner circle that is actually open to the outdoors, and is primarily just a place to sit and check out plants and relax. Inside however, are all sorts of exhibits, interactive elements, a play are a for kids, some animatronic (and roaring!) animals, and the ultimately impressive mammoth skeleton!

Once you've gone through the museum, be sure to head outside and check out the tar pits. You'll have a new level of appreciation for them!

First thing - the Woods Hole Science Aquarium is NOT a large aquarium like those in Boston, Atlanta, Washington D.C., Los Angeles, etc. This is a small, quaint location - it is literally the oldest aquarium in North America. it comprises of a small U shaped hallway that has tanks on one side, props and articles on the other. You can also go upstairs and get "behind the scenes" of the tanks, allowing you to see through the top of the tanks and see a few other tanks that house other fish. There is also a small two finger touch pool upstairs that has sea urchins, hermit crabs, starfish and more. This is a "free" restaurant, with a donation location when you enter. Second thing - parking is ROUGH here. Be prepared to circle for quite some time.

The a Brea Tar Pits are incredibly interesting - there are multiple tar pits surrounding the Page Museum, so be sure to explore! The Page Museum itself if fairly small, so it may be tough to spend more than an hour inside, but filled with amazing fossils and recreations. There is even a small "play place" for toddlers, which has books, a few toys, and play mats. The rest of the museum focuses on the tar pits, their history, and the fossils found within. There is a working area inside the museum, where you can view volunteers and experts as they uncover bones and other fossils found in the tar pits. The mammoth skeleton is stellar!

Pro tip - the Page Museum is walking distance from LACMA. Make it a full day excursion and hit both!

Flight Path Learning Center is a great location to soak in a wide range of aviation history. There is a great deal of commercial aircraft memorabilia, including pins, luggage, suits and uniforms. A slew of models show a wide range of plane and planes types. The center is made of of many rooms, making it a delight to explore each and take your time.

They also have a historic DC-3 outside, which you can go inside, sit down in - even in the cockpit! This is a learning center, and to further support that they offer Flight Sim training, with an impressive number of computers to support students.

Pro tip - take some cash with you. Although it's free, they do ask for donations. Take some cash so you can give to this great center.

Two facets to this review - 1st - this IS a real, working movie theater, and in that capacity it is fantastic. Absolutely a great place to watch a movie, and home to many opening nights. Check out a film there if even just to experience the overall vibe of Hollywood.

2nd, the space outside the Chinese Theatre is where the footprints of the stars are. This is a super popular, very fun area to see how large your feet (and hands) are compared to some of our favourite and historic stars!

It can be pretty busy outside, and be aware, there are a ton of street performers here (pay them to take a picture with them). I suggest going early in the day when the crowds are a bit smaller!

This is a massive park, with multiple areas for kids to play, play ground structures, a tree house and more. On the weekends you'll see multiple birthday parties and cookouts taking place in the park, so expect to see bouncy houses and smell food on the grill! Due to the park size, it can sometimes have some trash flying around, and I've spotted unaccompanied adults wandering around that could be a bit worrisome...but overall the park is a fun, enjoyable place to visit. There is a ton of parking, but be aware that there is a farmers market which takes place and takes over one parking lot. To help with these, there is additional parking set aside for it!

To manage expectations - this aquarium is really more of an exhibit. Don't go into this expecting a large, free standing aquarium. With that being said, Shark Reef is a great place to visit. The exhibits are good, the glass tunnel very cool, and the diversity of wildlife solid. There is a fee for entrance, and given that this is an aquarium on the Strip, the price is appropriate. It can get a little busy, so use the Google timeline to see what off-peak hours are and check it out then! A fun place to enjoy some nice AC and snap pictures of sea life!

Pro tip - it's a long walk through the main hotel to get to Shark Reef, so be prepared.

What a beautiful place to get away to! A sprawling mixture of open fields, dense foliage, ponds, flower gardens and more - it's easy to spend hours here simply enjoying the grounds. To top that off there are plenty of activities they host, for adults and children.

Incredible spread of flowers, fauna and beauty! Walk around and gaze at the flowers, go to the children's area and crawl through the secret tunnel in the hedge looking for the frog prince, and relax in the cover of a gazebo as you look over the skyline. It's wonderful.

Pro tip - the temperature can be high here, so bring a hat and water for your stroll!

This stellar facility is open to tours for the public, where they show you incredibly interesting hardware, locations, and educate you with super information on space, Earth, and history. Everyone is incredibly nice, friendly and eager to share. There are different types of tours - ranging from public, to social media and press specific. Regardless of the type you go on, prepare to be blown away by some of the amazing things you'll see! JPL has multiple buildings spread across their campus, so look for statues, plaques, architecture and more.

Pro tip - there are a some great Ingress portals here, hack away!!!

This building is actually known as the Santa Monica Looff Hippodrome, and is a historical building. It contains a beautiful carousel, which you can of course ride (after payment). The ride is somewhat short, the beauty of the carousel is undeniable, as is the history that comes with it. Rarely busy, it can sometimes seem like this lovely attraction is ignored due to it's location (at the entrance to the pier from street level).

My take is that this is well worth visiting and riding when you're at the pier!

A beautiful, other-worldly experience awaits you at Barker Dam. It's a very casual hike with a wee bit of climbing (more akin to steps than true climbing), which makes it perfect for those who don't want to exert themselves, or for little kids. There are multiple paths - but for the most part they all wind up at the dam, where water awaits! Great rock formations, Joshua Trees, cacti and more.

Pro tip - take water, even when it's cold you dry out quickly in Joshua Tree!

This small aquarium is home to a good variety of sea creatures! Comprised of two floors, it even has an education play area for kids, and a touch pool. Although free, donations are welcomed (there is a box right by the door). Most of the exhibits are on the first floor, but there is a good amount upstairs - including their active octopus!

Pro tip - there are often kid specific events happening in the aquarium. If you have kids, check their calendar on their website.

This awesome zip line let's you fly over the old strip two ways - you can either choose to sit (the cheaper option) or lay on your stomach, Superman style (the more expensive option). It's a great experience! The zip line is long enough to be worth the price. Pro tip - if you're wearing a dress the zip line can prove challenging. In addition, you have to put all items in your pockets in a bag for the zip, so no way to take photos/video while you're actually zipping!

Pretty much one of the must stop places for any tourists, it's fun to see this street and the gaggle of people going up and down it. For any visitors, the best view is at the top. There are stairs on the for residents (and tourists) to traverse the street on both sides. It's a fun view from the bottom looking up!

Pro tip - walk down the street for photos vs. driving down it. Driving down it doesn't provide you with great vantage points for your camera.

This beautiful beach house is located directly on the sand! It has multiple spaces for multiple uses, and boasts an incredible view of the Pacific Ocean. There is ample parking, and a clear area for Uber/Lyft pick-up and drop off. Entrance is only on the West Side of the PCH, and trying to u-turn in-front of the entrance if you're going NorthBound on the PCH is dicey - so be aware. A lovely place to hold an event at.

Hard to go wrong with a fountain, especially one dedicated to Yoda at Lucas Arts! Great looking fountain and sculpture, if you're in the area and love Star Wars, then it's a must see!

Pro tip - Note that this is private property. Park farther away (for example near the Social Club) and enjoy a quiet stroll to the fountain instead of trying to drive through the gate to get close to it.

Seeing a machine that took people into space is incredible. The shuttle itself is magnificent in person, and the room it's in allows you to walk around and under it.

I do wish there were balconies or other vantage points, and it's a shame you need to go through the Science Center to get to it, but the actual shuttle itself is incredible.

A must stop if you're in the area!

This beautiful garden is nestled into the grounds of The Getty Center. You'l see many students sitting here, photographers taking pictures, and museum guests sitting back and relaxing. Although there is no shade, the flowers and fauna are quite nice. There are a couple of small paths to walk on - and it is handicap accessible. A lovely place to explore and enjoy!

These large sculptures shaped like dinosaurs are centrally located on the Santa Monica 3rd Street Promenade. The living ivy inside of them gives a great organic quality, and when the sun hits them just right, they're beautiful.

Super easy to get some stellar photographs of these, you can stand inches away and literally touch them if you wanted to!

This is a lovely piece of public art that is situated on the corner of two streets. There is plenty of street parking, but it's often busy, as there are several business in the immediate vicinity. Be prepared for others taking photos and videos at the wall, so you may have to wait your turn. Be sure to look up the artist and their other works!

This awesome space is perfect for parties and events, with ample space and different areas for different venue types. There is a ton of history here, everything from old uniforms to a full airplane cockpit taken from a real 727!  If you get a chance, try out the incredible flight simulator!

The most spectacular waterfall in the Columbia River Gorge, with easy access and stunning views. Parking can be a challenge, as the lot is often full. The path up is a long series of concrete stairs but is not difficult to get up. There is also a lodge and restaurant, but the prices and wait times were too high for me to go in.

The waterfall feels extremely powerful, especially if you get up to the bridge. There are two drops, with the upper one being significantly taller than the lower. The best views are at the main viewpoint, although you will likely have to bump elbows with a hundred people depending on the day. The path to the bridge is also worth the walk, but the crowds can make it a bit difficult as it is narrow in places.

Getting here is an adventure but it's well worth it. The falls are accessed via a long road that starts in a populated rural area but quickly turns to dirt and goes through some very desolate forest. It's very beautiful here, and the road isn't too rough, but it goes on for a while. The trail to the falls itself is quite easy, just be cautious of loose gravel and don't take the shortcuts people have carved into the hillside.

The falls itself is amazing. It's about 70 feet tall and flows year-round, falling in a single drop over a large cliff face. The trail down offers views of it from different angles. I had it all to myself when I was there, and I doubt it gets very crowded. Definitely worth the drive.

A really beautiful hike. The canyon is at the end of a dirt road that, while a bit bumpy, isn't too difficult to drive on. The start of the trail is easy, but it soon opens up into a large exposed wash with very little shade or cover. The trail then goes into an enclosed slot canyon, which is incredibly beautiful.

Do this hike in the morning or late afternoon, when the canyon walls cast shadows onto the trail. Bring tons of water, because it gets very hot and very taxing. It may only be 3.5 miles, but it feels much longer than that.

A great park. It offers great views of the city, especially the Mission. The park is also very large and has more than one peak, with a few trails that go through the grassy areas. The main peak has a large radio tower on it, and offers some of the best views. There is also a swing there, which is surprisingly sturdy and is fun to use.

Just be mindful of the weather, as it can be extremely windy. I've also seen coyotes here before, even on crowded days.

Definitely recommend this trail, and I've done it a number of times. The traffic getting there from the 101-1 interchange on weekends is the most difficult part. The trail slopes gently downwards towards the ocean, and is very wide and in good shape. There are a lot of great side trails to campgrounds, or up to the tops of the ridges, if you feel like doing anything more difficult. The beach itself is great, and the lookout is definitely worth the climb.

Great spot to stop along the Oregon Coast Highway. There's a nice overlook and a trail that stairsteps down to get a better look. The spouting horn itself is easy to see from the highway, so if you don't want to walk down you won't miss too much. Just wait for a large wave to approach the rocks, then the horn will erupt. It ranges from a small spray of mist to a giant plume of water; you're much more likely to see the mist.

Really nice bridge and park and worth a stop. The bridge offers nice views of the river and the mountains around Redding, and the sundial is fairly impressive. The park around it is very nice as well, and there are many information plaques on the history and ecology of the river. There isn’t any shade on the bridge and it gets quite hot in the summer, but the visitor’s center and the area around it are shaded.

Nice spacious green space at the very heart of Berkeley. It's a nice place to stroll through or stop in. While there are a few homeless people here, they're usually not bothering anyone and easy to avoid. It's also the epicenter for a lot of the political activism that happens here (I have seen antifa and far-right protestors clash here before), but this isn't a daily occurrence and it's easy enough to avoid.

Really lovely Japanese garden. It's in a convenient spot in the center of town, right along the greenbelt and river. It's a really nice spot to walk around, but the highlight for me was the clear care that went into assembling the garden. The river water is carefully channelled through the garden, there are stone lotus stepping stones, and stone lanterns are placed around the garden. Definitely worth a walk.

Iconic and bustling, Union Square is in the middle of everything. You could spend an entire day in and around it, because there's shopping, cable cars, restaurants, and more within two blocks of here. Some areas are worth sitting down and relaxing in, while others are always crowded and filled with people crossing the square. At Christmas, the huge Christmas tree and ice rink are always great to visit.

Really nice park right along the lake. It's a great place to stop and sit. There are a lot of tables in an open area at the edge of the park that are an ideal lunch spot. The park is also filled with large oak trees, which, along with the tall buildings and the lake, make it nice and picturesque. Access from the lake is super easy, as it blends into the park area along the lakeshore.

If you're not comfortable with caving and you're in Lava Beds, this cave and Skull Cave are the best to see. Mushpot Cave is well-lit and has many info plaques that describe the formations. The path is easy to follow and there is only one section that requires any ducking or maneuvering. It's very close to the campground and visitor's center, which makes it very accessible.

Great geothermal area. The hike is short and easy, and the features here are really interesting. While there isn't one massive site like there is in the upper or middle basins (Old Faithful and the Grand Prismatic Spring, respectively), all the features I saw here are either unique or really interesting. I'm surprised Google labeled the parking lot instead of the trailhead.

Super nice park. The upper part of the park is basically a town green, and is made up of well-kept lawns with lots of shade. The rest of the park is built around the paved pathway through the canyon. The canyon has been restored with native plants, and feels much more like something in a state park than in the middle of a neighborhood. Highly recommend a hike through here.

Fantastic brewery. The selection is very varied, and a lot of their beers are interesting. The Tip Top and Coconut IPA get special mention as one of the best fruity sours and IPAs I've ever tried (and I say that as someone who really dislikes most IPAs). Staff were super friendly, and the layout and seating of this place are really nice. Definitely recommend a stop here.

A beautiful state park. The park has a number of beaches, hiking trails, and campgrounds. Stump Beach is by far the most prominent and most central beach, and it's my favorite. The Salt Point Trail that connects Stump Beach to the namesake point is also a great hike, as it features a bunch of beautiful and unique rock formations and stunning views of the ocean.

Highly recommend a stop here. The mead is great, and they offer honey as well; I ended up leaving with a jar of honey while my friends got the mead. Best of all is the staff – the guy conducting the tasting was super accommodating and had a great sense of humor. The entrance can be a bit hard to find, but it's more than worth it.

Really beautiful bridge. The scale is something to see. Traffic on it is a bit annoying, as the roads all bottleneck (surprisingly, there aren't many other roads across the canyon). Also great to see the BASE jumpers leaping from the bridge – there are plenty of spots to see them along the canyon wall.

This is one of my personal favorite places. It's a huge and varied park with a wide range of sights and activities. Hiking and camping is great in the southern area, and the beaches vary from cold and windswept to sheltered and enclosed, but they're all beautiful. I cannot recommend this place enough.

Nice museum in the capitol building. It features dioramas and artifacts from all the counties of the state, as well as information on the history of California. There are also portraits of California governors and a period room. If you're visiting Sacramento it's worth a stop.

"Stunning" is the only word that comes to mind about the view here. It offers a great look up the Columbia River across the gorge. Inside the house there are exhibits, displays, and a gift shop. It's possible to walk up to the second floor and look out from there as well.

Really pretty overlook. The overlook is really just a pullout with a couple of info plaques, unlike the overlooks to the south that have actual parking lots with them. Views are worth the stop, but I do wish there was a little more space off the road here.

A spectacular waterfall right on the coast. Can be done as a long day hike or as a stop on a backpacking trip, I've done both. Last time I stopped here I went backpacking up the coast and it's visible very far to the north, making for a great landmark.

A nice stop in Crescent City but your experience will depend on the weather. If it's a cold and overcast day, it's not really worth driving over and walking out. If it's bright and sunny, however, it is a good experience.
The column is located at the top of a hill and provides great views of the surrounding area, even on a cold and foggy day. The artwork depicts the Lewis and Clark expedition and is very well done.

The 5th and last covered bridge I'm visiting on this trip. Roseman bridge is beautiful, spanning gracefully high above the Middle River. It's also farther away from town, so much less people. It was also the only one I've seen with a visitor center and a gift shop. I think this was one of the bridges in Clint Eastwood's movie.

This park has a basketball court on one end a kid's playground and a shade structure with picnic tables in it, with a large, sloped grassy field in between.  Exercise stations all around the perimeter that looks like nobody uses them.  No restroom facilities, no parking.

2nd covered bridge on my trip. This one was nicer, as there was an actual stream under it.  Some guys were headed down the bank said they were going fishing. Other visitors were arriving constantly so had to wait for clear photo shots.

One of the best parks on the East Side.  Fully equipped for families and large groups, for picnics and athletic activities; with many picnic tables and restrooms available.  Nice scenic walk around the lake.  Well-maintained.

A great hiking area; with hikes ranging from real easy to strenuous.  You can go all the way to Garin Regional Park, and even further.  The ridge trail is very scenic, with a nice panoramic view of the East Bay area.

A great, great place for people and pets alike. Off-leash all around. Nice short walk down to the beautiful sandy beach, and lots of room for the dogs to run around in and play with other dogs. Beautiful scenery.

Beautiful, well-maintained park large enough to feel solitude in some places. Very serene views of the lagoon and the ducks and other animals living there. Nice leisurely walk around the entire perimeter.

A large park with many facilities: kid's playground, tennis courts, basketball courts, a beach volleyball court, a full-sized soccer field, clean restrooms, etc. Also lots of open spaces and shade trees.
A large park with a man-made beach park, which is great for families.  Lots of picnic facilities, and trails if you want to walk around.  Also has lots of plums trees and berries on the upper trail.
This is a beautiful park all by itself, separate from the main Golden Gate Park. The flora colors come out very nicely in a sunny day.  Dogs are allowed to run loose, which makes it even better.
A huge, expansive area with much potential for future development.  Currently has picnic grounds, off-leash dog area, bicycle and walking trails.  County has plans for more facilities (7/7/17).
A tiny little park, half of which is taken by the Dog Park.  However it has a large shade tree, as well as a playground for kids, and a picnic area.  Street parking only, no restrooms.
dislikes: Limited space due to dog park

reviews_attraction.text: A very nice place for taking long walks along the shore.  Some sections dogs are allowed free and other sections leash required, to protect nesting birds and other anmals.
A nice beach park with lots of facilities.  Large open areas, clean restrooms, walking and jogging trails, ideal for large family picnics as well as the random passer-by.
A good place for nature walks. Lots of flora. Paid parking, but you can park outside along the street and walk in.  Because of paid parking, doesn't get crowded.
A very large park with many facilities. Playground for kids, walking/jogging track, baseball field complex, open areas for athletic games, picnic areas, etc.
A large, beautiful scenic park.  Great for walking, either just people or with pets. Very serene during the day, as there are no loud traffic passing by.
A long trail that follows the creek.  All kinds of sceneries, from wildlife to flora to other people walking or biking.  Many access points.
A fairly large-sized dog park.  Lots of space for the dogs to run,however there is a large sandy area that gets real hot in the summer sun.
A nice large park, includes a dog park, picnic facilities, clean restrooms, and nice scenery. There are horse trails around the area too.
Good park for families. Not that big, but its great for the neighborhood. Parking lot is small, but lots of street parking available.
A nice park well-used by residents and visitors alike.  Good place to take a break from sightseeing in Chinatown and Little Italy.
A good place for walking or jogging. Clean and the grass looks watered well even in the middle of summer.
A great hike for all levels.  Go as far as you want, as high as you want. Fantastic views to the east.
Not much of a park, and not much remains of the old mill.  Has parking area only, and nothing else.

Loved the snorkeling here, just make sure you bring water shoes so that the rocks don't hurt your feet so much on the way in and out of the water.

Also, you will want to watch out for the glass bottom boats and semi submersible submarines that come through the area every hour so that you don't get run over while trying to snorkel.  The wetsuit rental down the street from here was $15 for the whole day so we felt very comfortable taking our time getting accustomed to the water and our gear.

Excellent experience.  Took the boys here during Spring Break and they had a great time learning about the moving making process and interacting with the different exhibits.  Lots of very cool merchandise to look at and the television sets were amazing!  Especially loved the Friends experience sitting down on the iconic couch for pictures.  Ruby did the presentation about movie sound and it was unexpectedly amazing.

Came here on a field trip with 4th graders and this mission has a great host for their class on making adobe bricks!  The whole mission is very well cared for, pristine gardens and every angle of this place is a great picture.  Kids had a good time learning about how things were done in the olden days.  Kids also had fun learning for themselves from the well labeled displays.

Excellent trail for hill training. Has shade for part of the trail and the hills present a good challenge. Find many older people doing the hills here and felt inspired me to try and train harder. There were some additional signs that volunteers put up so that people don't get lost. I think the city of diamond bar could improve the trail a bit by adding more signage

40 bucks per person, but the kids loved it, was very entertaining and saw LOTS of fish, but it became significantly less entertaining after we learned there are literally only 3 types of fish we encounter on that tour (Garibaldi, Opal Eye, and Calico Bass).  The tour guides were knowledgeable and gave us a well rounded tour of the local waters.

Parking can be a nightmare here, but the sign is a great picture opportunity.  When I came here with the boys there was someone helping other tourists take pictures and it generally made the process better especially because a tour bus came by and some of the visitors were not familiar with how to wait your turn when there is a queue!

Wonderful little modern park with lots of stations for children of all sizes to play on.  Came here during vacation with the boys and this park looked amazing while skating around town so we decided to stop by.  Boys had an excellent time here and it is also well shaded.

Nice collection of skateboarding history, from old decks to wacky skateboarding inventions, from penny boards to longboards, and the art on display is also wonderful.  Very nice place to stop by when you are in town

Excellent 5 mile loop that is welcoming to first time hikers and challenging enough so that fit people can get a decent workout.  There is ample parking and, from what I can tell, all the visitors respect the trail.

Wonderful climbing jungle gym here, but precious few other things for kids to play with here apart from the plastic percussion.  Still, the view was still nice from the park while the kids climbed around.
We browsed through collections of photos with placards that gave good context to them.  The boys enjoyed going through the stories and looking at the pictures. The garden outside was also beautiful
Came here on a field trip with 4th graders and everyone was impressed with the beauty and majesty of the chapel.  You can tell that this place is well cared for and it is a great place to visit
Huge park hidden at the top of the hill.  The boys like this playground because of all the climbing they can do here.  There is also a nice trail accessible from the back of this park.
Beautiful place for a stroll at sunset. Walking along the water side, you can see the great boats and aircraft carriers with the calm waters of the bay. Great place for pictures
Wonderful place to stop and rest along the PCH.  There are multiple places you can walk along the ridges or you can even hike down to the water if you are feeling adventurous!
Huge park that is great for jogging, biking, and skating.  Came here with my workout group and we had an excellent session together with all of the space at this park!
Two playgrounds at this park: one for smaller and one for bigger kids.  Has two tennis courts, hockey rinks turned into basketball courts, and a large soccer pitch.
Beautiful place to ride a bike, go on a walk, or even go jogging.  The temperature was perfect when I visited in the summer and the waterfront was not crowded.
Lots of equipment to do a great variety of exercises with.  Great place for kids to play and nice place for athletic adults to show off their strength.
My boys love this place.  It has lots of different areas where they can pretend to have different jobs from doctor, to firefighter, to postman, etc.
Nice exhibits that show history of mankind from a couple different perspectives like the history of beer and the history of racism.
Great variety at the playground for kids to climb and play together.  There are also adult bodyweight workout equipment available.
Wonderful garden that you can enjoy for free and it is also a beautiful spot for pictures and to practice photography
Wonderful tourist photo spot and fun to drive down except when people are standing in the middle of the roadway!
Came here for the Spartan event and the stadium is beautiful and well equipped to handle such a huge crowd

Such a dope park. Very clean, especially for how large it is, and it can accommodate just about anything you'd want to do. Two full basketball courts and two smaller ones for kids, handball and tennis courts, a baseball diamond, an impressive skate park, a fitness area, a lil stage, playground, I mean it's got it all. That's leaving out the indoor recreation area too! It's a great neighborhood park. Don't go though, it's crowded as it is😋

My wife and I were fortunate enough to be here during the holidays, so we got to see the place all done up with the ice rink and giant Christmas tree. Really happy feel to this place, it was very easy to stop shopping for a second and just stop and take in the wonderful atmosphere. Probably the closest thing to Manhattan's union square that you'll find on the west coast. Absolutely lovely.

In all honesty it mainly gets five stars because of its iconic status (as well as the stellar Los Angeles view). Hiking up here is a bucket list item for any native southern Californian (or at least should be) and whichever route you take is completely worth it. Plus every hike in this area is at least remotely challenging, so you can get up there and feel mad accomplished.

Awesome hike from Grand Avenue Park to Chino Hills Parkway (where you can access ANOTHER great trail if you're feelin froggy🐸). The tunnel underneath Grand that you go through to get started is neat, and the steep hills provide a decent challenge. Great views on a clear day of all the mountains in the area, and round trip will only take a little over an hour.

My wife hadn't been here before, so it was a real joy to watch her wow reaction (which no doubt was my reaction the first time I saw it myself). Gorgeous arrangement of seasonal flowers with spectacular lighting and inventive little flower exhibitions worthy of their own parade floats. It only takes a few minutes and it's very much worth the stop to see.

Great trail, absolutely loved it. Intense at points, what with the steepness here and there, but short enough to where it wasn't absolutely relentless. Hour to the Hollywood sign, hour back, good exercise, and you meet lots of friendly peeps. Bring water, bring a snack, go early to avoid the crowds, and for Pac's sake wear some good shoes!

This hike is like "calves, you mad bro?" Steep and consistent, with great views and a lovely tree-filled area here and there. Lots of paths to choose from, and they go on for a looong while if you're down for that (you can make it to the Puente Hills mall, for instance). Definitely worth regular visits to explore the whole trail network.

Park is perfect. Sweet trees with tons of shade, four tennis courts, three baseball diamonds, two basketball courts, and a huge handball/racquetball court. Add picnic tables, lots of grass, and the most adorable miniature library you've ever see, and you've got yourself a bangin park. Love it here, can't wait to be in the area again!

Great park with just about anything you could want. Softball diamonds, soccer fields, tennis and basketball courts, a playground for the chillins, grassy hills to roll down like you're a child yourself, clean restrooms. Place really has it all. Only thing is it's kind of a nuisance to get to, but you get used to that.

Great example of a more obscure place being every bit as good as the more popular ones. Between the astounding array of artwork and the gorgeous grounds and gardens, the Norton easily stands up to the Getty or LACMA. Lovely, eloquent place, and not quite as packed as the aforementioned museums (can't hate on that)!

Beautiful cathedral that towers over its section of Santa Fe. You can see it from quite a ways down the street, but once inside it's the polar opposite of the bustling city - calm and serene. Come in, absorb the astounding architecture, and leave feeling rejuvenated and ready to get back to exploring.

Staggeringly huge park with tons of basketball courts and baseball diamonds. Lots of greenery! No, not THAT kind of greenery (unless you're talkin after dark, of course).
Ample parking and even the restrooms are clean, as is the whole park, really. Nice neighborhood, too. We loved it.

Definitely for the adventurous type. Like a hood version of Laguna beach, equal parts beautiful beach cliff views and graffiti. The concrete rubble even without the paint is fascinating, and it's such a cool place to walk around or just have a seat and take in the beach air and art.

Nice park with a solid rec area, and a gargantuan play area for the kids - plus the splash pads is a nice touch. One and a half basketball courts plus a fitness area! The equipment isn't exactly top notch but it's nice to see. Lots of homeless but sadly it happens.

Parking is a pain, but you don't really care anymore once you hit the trail. the stairs offer excellent exercise, the views up top are relentless (they really give it to you man, just sayin), and the lil mini-museum up top is fascinating.

Meant a lot to me to come here. You really feel like one with the culture when you stand at that bench and look up at the house (well, the tip of it anyway). A great place to pay respects to one of my heroes.
More for diverse crowds and people watching than actually playing anything (unless you're mad early). Very pretty and calming place, especially considering the bustle.
Very cool place, pretty fountain surrounded by lush greenery and big city staples alike. I'm really glad that Reverend Lovejoy got this fountain named after him.
So happy I got to see this stadium. Not only historic, but you really can feel the spirit of the team in the air around the stadium. I love it.
Absolutely stunning. I felt like I was walking around at the base of a giant bonsai tree at times. Tea place was really good too, worth peepin.
Beautiful views of the river and the bridges, and lots of cool looking people stroll through (people watching is impossible to resist here).
Nice little residential park with a cool lake, pedal boats, and a public pool with a bad ass slide for summer. Ain't much to not like👍
Nice, big park. Great for basketball, soccer, or baseball. Workout area is cool too. The bathrooms are wack tho and parking is meh.
Lovely place for a walk with great views. Watching the steamboats and street cars come and go is a real treat, too😄
Mad majestic and much larger than I thought it would be. Dope place to stop for a minute and people watch.

This place is awesome. I arrived early in the morning and not a lot of cars were parked here. started my way going up on the upper cave. It was so much fun. Took my whole camera gear inside and took great pictures along the way. The 8 food lava wall was definetly a challenge for me with my gear. But I met some great guys from texas and they helped me carrying it up.
Without my gear that wouldn't be a problem. The upper entrance is also a little challenging if you have a bit bigger backpack. You cant have it on your back, otherwise you wont fit through. So much fun to explore the cave and I loved that there was no light installed. That made it even more fun.After I hiked back down to the parking lot, I also did the lower cave. Also fun and not as hard to navigate as the upper one. Make sure you bring good boots and lights.

Awesome place to watch boats going in and out the ocean. You acutally can walk across here and you will walk right on top of the lock gates. Thats very rare that you can walk on the gates instead of a seperate pedestrian bridge. This gives you a heads on view of the boats in the locks. You can get lucky and see harbor seals hanging out here. There is a nice and beautiful garden there as well with lots of shade. Lots of green area for a picnic and views of the locks and canal. Squirrels and ducks are not shy here. We sat down to eat something and they came closer and closer as they would try to grab a bite from us as well. Watch out on the green area, there is a lot of poop from the animals here. There is a small visitor center with some exhibits as well.

Awesome place for people of every age. It is a great place to visit year round to learn more about manatees or join one of their free tours or yoga classes. However to get to actually see manatees it's best if you visit during the winter months. Chances of seeing them are higher then. During the winter months manatees migrate back down south to warmer waters and the outlet of the power plant is a welcoming area for manatees to hang out. Parking and admission are free. Staff is awesome and the visitor center has many programs for kids. Take a stroll along the waterfront. They also have free Wi-Fi. This place should be on your list while visiting the area and especially during the winter.

This place has a great view of the LA Downtown Skyline. When I visited the parking space directly in the park was blocked off. i thought already that some event might be going on and indeed there was a wedding about to be held. They were still prepping everyting. Getting married outdoor in front of a nice skyline is not bad. There are a couple of trails and even public restrooms, kids play area and a mini waterfall. There is also parking available along the street for free. Shouldn't be a problem to find a spot during the weekend.

Wow this is probably the best view of the Seattle skyline. I just discovered this place by accident on early morning and enjoyed the view on a sunny day with some fog through the city. It looked amazing. Also came back the same night to enjoy the view of the night skyline and took pictures. During my night visit I encountered a lot of photographers around here. During the day more tourists. Parking along the street is free. I definitely recommend this place to anyone who visits Seattle. It is a must-see.

a real great place to visit. They tell you how US law making works and you get a peek inside the work of politicians. the admission is free and also the tour which lasts about an hour where you get to hear a lot of interesting things about the history of California and the building. to enter you have to get through a metal detector but you don't have to take off your shoes. make sure you visit the balcony of the two chambers.

Definetely stop here if you are passing through the area. You will see dozens of elephant seals laying around and sunbathing ;). They will throw sand around and move every know and then to a different spot.
Amazing to see and they are right in front of you. You will get a really good and close-up view. Don't forget your camera.

This is an awesome place for a picnic. Bring your family here and enjoy some time out in the woods. Not far from the city but you feel like you are miles away from the next city. If you want to park close to the picnic sites you have to pay a small fee or you can walk a bit and have free parking.

This is a beautiful place and a secret too. Not a lot of people know about this place. I just discovered it, when i was driving along the shoreline to look for some good picture spots. There are some nice trails, which will lead you out in the bay a bit and also lots to see. Really nice place...

This is a really nice place with great views of the beach, fisher island and the miami harbor. You also can watch cruise ships and cargo vessels going in and out of the port here. Really awesome. The closest parking around is all paid parking. After visiting here take a stroll along the beach.

Great place to visit. Hidden literally in the middle of nowhere. There is a marker on the main road but it's easy to miss. Still a cool place to come and visit and take pictures off. Ob one side of the bridge is a little park, great to enjoy an afternoon at the river.

Great little viewpoint of the bridges with placards about their history. Parking here is free and available along the street. This is a residential address, please respect the privacy of the people here and also keep noice down to not provoke unwanted attention.

really nice and amazing place and museum of you are into trains, railroad and such. they have working model trains. reminds me about my youth when I used to build up the model trains in our basement. pretty cool to watch and right next door to a real railroad.

Awesome parks and you can fly your model aircrafts here and meet a lot of other pilots. There is a parking fee from March to including October of 6$. They have a lot of BBQ spots, which can also be reserved for a fee. Nice walking trails as well along the bay.

This trail shows you the vegetation in the everglades. It's a short trail but in the summer time mosquitos hide out here as well. Make sure you wear repellent. You will pass a pond. Enjoy the view. I saw a turtle swimming right next to the boardwalk.

It's a great place, especially on a sunny day. But it seems they charge now for parking and this is ridiculous. When I visited on weekends the lot was almost always empty. Just another way to rip off people.
Very nice park along the river. My hotel was right next to the park. Great for walking, biking, running it just sitting there and enjoying the view.  There are also restrooms and places for a picnic.
This is not a very touristy spot, but it gives you great views of the bay and San Francisco. Locals come here to fish at the pier. You also can watch the harbor operations, mainly during the week.
If you are in Seattle, especially in Fremont, you should consider a detour just to see this gigantic troll underneath a bridge. It depends how busy it is, but you might get parking close by.
Nice statue and one of the many historical markers, which tell you more about the city and history of the country. make sure you check out the wells Fargo museum and visitor center
Great beach with awesome views and some great trails. Unfortunately the water is pretty cold. You can watch surfers all along the coast line in Pacifica.
Great place and great tour. Also missed this on my previous visits in key west. They even have some free exhibits at the check in office and gift shop.
Great place in nature. There are picnic tables and a fire pit and a rope on which you can swing and jump in the river just upstream of the falls.
Nice garden in Miami Beach. Take the talks and explore the gardens. Most of it is very maintained. There are some lanes with fish too.
A great trail and you definitely should take it. You will see a lot of wildlife along the way just watch carefully.

Absolutely loved our visit here. Very beautiful park with great hiking. You can drive up to 10,000 feet and then you can hike up to the 13 thousand foot Peak. Some very pretty lakes in the national park. No entry fee to get into this National Park as it is somewhat remote. One of the lower campgrounds have been recently rehabilitated so was in very nice condition. all of the camping other than the group Campground is first come first serve.

Beautiful although somewhat short hike very close to Furnace Creek. It can be overly popular at times so the parking lot can be full. Don't try to do this hike in really hot weather because it may not be safe. You can get overwhelmed with the heat. You can make a nice Loop out of it by hiking up Golden Canyon over to Gower Gulch and then back down to the valley floor and then North again to Golden Canyon parking lot.

Very beautiful state park on the Columbia river. Lots of green grass and lots of mature trees that give good shade. There is a roped off swim area for kids. Just to the West of the swim area is a little beach with lots of great skipping rocks. The camping areas have lots of grass and are well shaded. Lots of RV sites with full hook ups As well as tent sites and a group site.

One of the many old extinct Cinder cones in the Portland area, this one just south of downtown Gresham. There are a couple locations you can park to access the walking trails. Good place if you really enjoy a tough run since the access roads beyond the gates are pretty steep. There is also a Trail Loop on the south side of the Butte just above Butler Road.

This is a fantastic Limestone Caverns, a really must see. Located in a pretty remote area of Nevada it is definitely worth the drive. It is located in Great Basin National Park which is also really really worth exploring. Our National Park Service guide for the cave tour was absolutely fantastic, her knowledge was amazing and she was quite entertaining.

Very cool historic site in Death Valley National Park. There are some really nice hiking trails in the area. A bit of a drive to get there as it's up in the hills aways but you don't have to drive too far on gravel to get there. There are rustic campgrounds nearby. There are toilets at the parking lot but it is a pit toilet.

Fantastic place with lots of interesting caves and hiking trails. We didn't have much time so just visited the lava tube cave that was lit up inside which was pretty neat. Really nice Visitor Center and staff. Make sure you clean your shoes before you enter the caves so you don't bring in diseases that can kill the bats.

Really large park with lots of paved trails and unpaved trails for walking and biking. There is a large off-leash area for dogs that is not fenced. The rest of the park dogs have to be on the leash. I never saw a playground for kids. There is a new pedestrian bridge that now connects the park to Downtown Salem.

One of the newest Parks in Gresham. Several nice picnic tables and barbecue set ups for briquettes. A short paved path with nice views although in the years ahead the trees might start obscuring the views. You can see the Columbia River Gorge, Mount Adams, Mount st. Helens, and Mount Hood.

Fantastic View from this viewpoint. It's seems like you can almost see forever. Well worth the drive to get up there. You have to drive a few miles on a gravel / dirt road but pretty much any car can do it. A little bit of washboarding but not bad.

If you are into Red Rocks this is the place! Lots of interesting hiking in this state park, a really really beautiful place to visit. We would love to come back here and camp and spend a few days exploring the state park.

Really beautiful Park on the lake. Lots of grass and shade. Lots of great picnic tables. Great swimming beach. There is also a little bit of hiking nearby as well as a section of the park that is great for climbing.

This is an easy family-friendly casual hike that follows the old water pipeline route up the river. The trail isn't very long before it becomes somewhat difficult and eroded so not good for kids at that point.

This is a corps of engineers built park that seems old dated in a bit run down. Good area for free overnight RV parking. there is also quite a bit of free overnight RV parking area downstream of this park.
Lots of interesting historic structures. The dinosaur fossil house is very cool in the staff are very knowledgeable. The fossil house tour and presentation by the state park staff was awesome!
Great campground with lots of shade trees for hot weather. beautiful place to be on a warm fall day with lots of dry leaves around. Nice little bike camp that we rode into and stayed at.
Not much remaining here other than historical signs. Good view of the Towering sand dunes in the distance. We pulled over for the night in our RV and had a very pleasant evening here.
Great deal sunmist newly rebuilt viewpoint of the furnace Creek Badlands area. very colorful, great place to watch the sunset! Also a good starting point for a hike down the canyon.
Really nice city park on the river with lots of grass. Very nicely maintained Park. Includes picnic tables of course and a little water splash pad area for the kids.
Good wines. Nice convenient location on highway. Facility starting to look a bit dated compared to the amazing new places being built in wine country out there.
One of the 7 Wonders of Oregon and rightfully so! Beautiful park to walk, ride, hike, run, and of course climb. Well managed by the State Parks folks.
Large county park with lots of grass and picnic areas. There is a very nice swim area in blue Lake as well. Well-maintained park with lots of parking.
we stopped and did a short hike which we enjoyed but the campground seemed great and I would recommend this as an overnight stop.
A great park with lots of open space to go for nice walks. Very kid friendly with a nice modern playground for them.
A bit on The rustic side but a good Park with some nice modern playground equipment for the little ones.

The Japanese Friendship Garden was designed as an expression of friendship between San Diego and its Japanese sister city, Yokohama.It illustrates two cultures and creates an immersive experience into Japanese culture.The Garden's design is based on centuries-old Japanese techniques adapted to San Diego's climate and florae and seeks to foster a relationship between humans and nature, providing a respite attuned to Japanese simplicity, serenity, and aestheticism.

The Garden sits on a 12-acre plot.It offers a variety of educational programs, exhibits, and festivals as well as accredited horticultural classes to enhance and deepen visitor appreciation for Japanese culture.As a valued community resource, it is well known for its unique setting, stone arrangements, koi ponds, water features, sukiya-style buildings and landscape.

The Japanese Friendship Garden was first opened in 1991.The second phase, opened in 1999, was designed by renowed landscape architect Takeo Uesugi.This phase added the Exhibit Hall, Activity Center, and Koi Pond.The third phase, completed in 2015, comprised. 9 additional acres which included a 200 cherry tree grove, large azalea and camellia garden, a water feature reminiscent of the San Diego watershed, and the state of the art Inamori Pavilion.

日本の友好庭園は、サンディエゴとその日本の姉妹都市、横浜間の友情の表現として設計されました。これは、2つの文化を示し、日本文化への没入体験を作成します。庭のデザインは何世紀も昔の日本のサンディエゴの気候に適応した技術とfloraの複数形に基づいており、日本のシンプルさ、穏やかさ、そして美学に同調休息を提供し、人間と自然との関係を促進することを目的とされています。

ガーデンは、12エーカーのプロットに座っています。これは、日本文化のビジター感謝を高め、深めるための教育プログラム、展示、そしてお祭りだけでなく、公認園芸クラスを用意しています。大切なコミュニティのリソースとしては、それは、そのユニークな設定、石の手配、鯉が泳ぐ池、水の機能、数寄屋風の建物や風景のためのよく知られています。

日本の友好庭園はまず、1999年にオープンし、第二段階1991年にオープンしたrenowed造園家上杉武夫によって設計されました。このフェーズでは、展示ホール、活動センター、と鯉の池を追加しました。 2015年に完成した第三相は、200桜の木立、大きなツツジやツバキ園、サンディエゴの流域を思わせる​​水の機能、および芸術稲盛パビリオンの状態を含め9追加エーカーを含んでいました。

The California Tower is 198 feet (60 m) tall and is open for public tours as of January 1, 2015. The tower's design is Spanish while the details and color are Mexican in style. The tower is composed of three tiers that shift from a quadrangle to an octagon and then a circle. There is a Maas-Rowe carillon in the tower, first installed in 1946 and replaced in 1967. The carillon can be heard throughout the park. It plays the Westminster Chimes every quarter-hour, and a resident carilloneur plays three songs at noon every day. The tower has been described as "San Diego's Icon," the most photographed and best-known landmark in San Diego. As I journey through Balboa Park on my daily walks, it is an extreme joy and pleasure to hear the chimes of the carillon in the background. I love the chimes!

Es gibt einen Maas-Rowe Carillon im Turm, zuerst im Jahr 1946 installiert und ersetzt im Jahr 1967. Das Carillon kann über den Park zu hören. Es spielt die Westminster Chimes jede Viertelstunde, und ein Bewohner Glockenspieler spielt täglich am Mittag drei Lieder. Der Turm wurde als "San Diego Icon", das am meisten fotografierte und bekannteste Sehenswürdigkeit in San Diego beschrieben. Als ich Reise durch Balboa Park auf meine täglichen Spaziergänge, ist es eine extreme Freude und Vergnügen, die Glocken des Glockenspiels im Hintergrund zu hören. Ich liebe die Glocken!

La Tour de Californie est de 198 pieds (60 m) de haut et est ouvert pour des visites publiques à compter du 1er Janvier 2015. La conception de la tour est l'espagnol tandis que les détails et les couleurs sont mexicaine dans le style. La tour est composée de trois niveaux qui changent d'un quadrilatère à un octogone et d'un cercle. Il y a un carillon Maas-Rowe dans la tour, d'abord installé en 1946 et remplacé en 1967. Le carillon peut être entendu dans tout le parc. Il joue le Chimes Westminster chaque quart d'heure, et un carillonneur résident joue trois chansons à midi tous les jours. La tour a été décrit comme "Icône de San Diego," le point de repère le plus photographié et le plus connu à San Diego. Comme je voyage à travers Balboa Park sur mes promenades quotidiennes, il est une joie extrême et le plaisir d'entendre le carillon du carillon en arrière-plan. J'adore les carillons!

La Torre de California es de 198 pies (60 m) de altura y está abierto para visitas públicas a partir del 1 de enero de 2015. El diseño de la torre es español, mientras que los detalles y el color son mexicana en estilo. La torre se compone de tres niveles que cambian de un cuadrilátero a un octógono y luego un círculo. Hay un carillón Maas-Rowe en la torre, instalado por primera vez en 1946 y reemplazado en 1967. El carillón se escucha por todo el parque. Desempeña el Westminster Chimes cada cuarto de hora, y un residente carilloneur juega tres canciones al mediodía todos los días. La torre ha sido descrito como "Icono de San Diego," el monumento más fotografiado y más conocido en San Diego. Mientras avanzo a través de Balboa Park, en mis paseos diarios, se trata de una extrema alegría y el placer de escuchar las campanadas del carillón en el fondo. Me encanta las campanadas!

Il design della torre è spagnolo, mentre i dettagli e colori sono messicano in stile. La torre è composta da tre livelli che cambiano da un quadrilatero ad un ottagono e quindi un cerchio. Essa svolge la Westminster Chimes ogni quarto d'ora, e un carilloneur residente suona tre canzoni a mezzogiorno tutti i giorni. Magnifico!

Nuestra familia ha estado viniendo a este museo desde que mi mamá era un adolescente, mi esposa y yo éramos niños, nos llevamos nuestros hijos y nuestros nietos lo largo de los años. El péndulo en el vestíbulo principal me fascinaba cuando era niño y todavía lo hace, ya que trata de demostrar el movimiento de la Tierra sobre su eje. Ballenas, leones marinos y huesos de dinosaurios están en exhibición. ¡Amo este lugar!

Certainly one of the most beautiful bridges in all of California! Walking across this iconic structure toward the museums provides a fantastic view that of downtown San Diego and the Balboa Park!

Sin duda uno de los puentes más bellos de toda California! Caminando a través de esta estructura icónica hacia los museos ofrece una fantástica vista de que el centro de San Diego y el Parque Balboa!

Sicherlich eine der schönsten Brücken in ganz Kalifornien! Beim Gang über diese ikonischen Struktur in Richtung der Museen bietet eine fantastische Aussicht, dass von der Innenstadt von San Diego und Balboa Park!

Certainement l'un des plus beaux ponts dans toute la Californie! Marcher à travers cette structure emblématique vers les musées offre une vue fantastique du centre-ville de San Diego et le parc Balboa!

Certamente uno dei ponti più belli di tutta la California! Camminando attraverso tale struttura iconica verso i musei offre una fantastica vista che del centro di San Diego e il Balboa Park!
