The Norton Simon Museum encompasses collections from: Asia including; paintings, wood block prints, tapestries and sculptures along with extensive pieces by European sculptures, painters, and tapestries designers. The Norton Simon has a sculpture garden displaying many sculptors' work in a beautiful manner around a large lily pond. The museum also contains the Norton Simon Theater. My wife and I are most fond of the Impressionists pieces available for you at the Norton Simon. The Garden Café is an excellent place to have a snack. Well worth the drive to Pasadena. Parking can be somewhat problematic as the Eastside lot fills up quickly on the weekends.

A little bit Rough on my Dog, but ONLY because the other Pet Partners would NOT control their Aggressive Pets. It seemed that some Pet Partners thought it was EXTREMELY HUMOROUS to allow their Large Dogs to Rough House with much Smaller Animals. Regardless of the Smaller Animals “Yelps”, these irresponsible Pet Partners refused to Step in and dissuade their aggressive animals. Sadly, had this experience been a “one-off”, I would refrain from comment, but this sort of attitude appears to be the norm rather than the aberration.

Beautiful Beach camping, but unless you have an RV, cannot stay over night. NO TENT CAMPING; very strange concept of what plurality of the masses actually means in a supposedly freedom loving society. DON't visit unless you have $50k-$300k worth of motorhome. Doesn't really matter. Park staff allow same visitors repeated visits, hence no reservations available. The so-called "Camp Hosts" programs is just an excuse to let selected persons stay indefinitely.

The Huntington Library and art collection is one the finest art museums in the Western United States. The Huntington[1]) is a collections-based educational and research institution established by Henry E. Huntington (1850–1927). The institution houses an extensive art collection with a focus in 18th and 19th-century European art and 17th to mid-20th-century American art. My favorite piece of art is "The Blue Boy" (c.1770) by Thomas Gainsborough.

Fiesta island dog park is my absolute favorite dog walking area in all of San Diego. My dog Bernie can be off the leash and yet protected from traffic and getting away from me too awfully far. The only thing I would like to see the city do is provide water for the animals. Pass that I would like to commend the fine human pet partners that offer their time and effort, in providing safe drinking water for the animals.

La Jolla Shores is the best beach in San Diego County. Excellent sandy beaches, showers, bathrooms, terrific grassy area for people like my Dad that hate the sand. The San Diego Life Guard Service provides excellent coverage of the water and surf breaks. Been going here since I was a little boy and now I'm 63. All my kids and now my Grand Kids have greatly enjoyed this fine beach.

The San Diego Museum of art has the wonderful collection of artwork from around the globe. I am at big fan of their impressionist artist, particularly Claude Monet and his "Haystacks at Chailly" (1865). The collections include pieces from Asia, the art of the Americas, Europe, modern and contemporary art, photography, along with art of Africa, the Pacific and Native Americans.

Great Park for Families. Excellent Grassy spaces for Weekend Family Activities! Ventures of Bicycling, Skating, Walking, Running, and Dog Walking! Plenty of Room for Family Barbecues, Games, Sun Covers and lots of Fun!. Parking is Abundant even on the Weekends. Excellent watch area for Fiesta Bay Aquatic Activities like the Unlimited Hydroplane Races!

Lovely, well cared for urban Park. I enjoyed looking at the individual art pieces. Was particularly impressed by the memorial to Seattle fire fallen. It was very moving to see that a city had dedicated an outstanding sculpture to our heroes from the Seattle fire department.

Been going to Ventura Cove since I was a Little Boy! I’m 65 now. The Sandy Beach always welcomes the Family. Good place for Everyone from Toddlers to Grandparents and everyone in between! Found my first Octopus friend on the Sandy Bottom of the Cove.

Mission Beach is a community of the City of San Diego. It is known for the boardwalk (actually Cement), the terrific beach, Belmont Park, terrific beach & bay vacation rentals and the boat anchorage at Mariner's Cove.

The Plaza de Panama is a wonderful part of central Balboa Park. Now that the parking spaces have been removed, patrons of the park can enjoy a snack or simply sit at the tables and enjoy the afternoon or weekend.
My Mom and Dad were from the "Greatest Generation" and this statue, in all its iconic glory, epitomizes the experiences that World War II brought to the Military and Civilian Society in America!
Anza-Borrego state park visitor center is an excellent interpretative educational center to explain the mysteries and beauty of the desert. My family and I very much enjoy the exhibits.
Thank you to America's Military Veterans and to the people who honor our brave men and women who have served our wonderful country so honorably!
Our BrVe Tunamen have given so much to our Community here in San Diego. W3 Honor them as they have Honored us!
My wife and I had the opportunity to see the, "age of impressionism" exhibits when they came to San Francisco.

This was my 1st Presidential Library visit and won't be my last. Everyone was so friendly, informative and dedicated from the moment we walked in the door. He was the only President I've ever seen in person. 1968 Ontario International Airport. I was 7 years old when my Mom took me out their. I remember him standing in that doorway of that jet and the crowds of people chanting " Nixon now more then ever, Nixon now" I felt like I was reliving an episode of the Wonder Years in that place. Really not enough time in the day to soak it all in. Really wanted a t shirt but medium seemed to be the biggest size they had. A tour of the presidential helicopter, his parent's house and gardens were spectacular. Full of history around every corner. God Bless America and thanks to all who keep this place running.

A great place to visit and see the life of Elvis. I had no idea, on this 30 day road trip across America, this placed impressed me like no other, including all 5 Presidential libraries, that we saw on this trip. I took more photos then any other place we've been so far. His opulent lifestyle was evident throughout the tour. The number of cashed checks I saw to multiple charities, was impressive and really showed his true colors for his fellow mankind.
I could go on forever but really no need, I think you get the point. I left Graceland with a kinder, gentler heart for my fellow man, and I'm already an RN.
If there is one place you should see before you leave this earth, Graceland should be it. God Bless.

What a great tour, there was no waiting in line, everything seemed well organized and moved along with excellent organization, multiple staff available to assist you, able to answer your questions. The grounds are immaculate, and everything is well maintained. We did the general tour, along with the carriage ride. A shame you can't take pictures inside of the home, but completely understand why. The gravesite here was a sight to behold, makes you proud to be an American, huge amount of history here, God Bless America, the state of Tennessee, and to the volunteers who put in the time to make this an enjoyable experience.

It has been about 2 years since I was there and I remember it like it was yesterday. Anyone can really appreciate the effort that goes into maintaining a place like this. Super educational and a great way to spend an afternoon. Everyone was very friendly. Thanks so much to everyone who made this enjoyable. Have to agree that road is little rough. The answer is not to go but maybe smooth it out a little. Or maybe the guy with the Chevy Impala could start a service transporting visitors.

First off I wanted to say thanks to President and Mrs.Bush for allowing us a glimpse into your museum and some what life is like as a President.  Had no idea what a difficult job you had. I learned a lot through the many interactive videos. I made this trip from California to specifically see the 3 Presidential libraries in Texas. I would do it again if given the chance, have nothing but respect for your family who have served this country well

Amazing experience with multiple aquariums with several species of fish. Unfortunately not labeled, but not going to ding them a star for that. The aquariums were clean, sting ray tank and shark exhibition are cool. Had lunch up stairs. Very friendly and informative staff. Well worth the money. I see some people complaining about the price and size. Remember folks, this is downtown Houston and the price of real estate here is not cheap.

Liked this side tour in combination with the country music hall of fame, our tour guide Greg was very friendly and knowledgeable concerning his job and customer satisfaction. The driver Mike did well navigating the streets of endless construction did an excellent job of getting us there safely. A lot of history there, stepping back in time, thinking of everyone fro Boots Randolph to Elvis Presley. Highly recommend tour.

I have always admired Johnny Cash and this museum does not disappoint at all, there is a lot of memorabilia in a fairly small space, if you take some time to appreciate what is there, easily a 2 hour tour. Saw some reviews about the price for admission, but considering the price of real estate that it sits on and what you're getting, it's really a bargin. Highly recommend and would do it again.

This place is amazing. Arrived early and saw a lot in 6 hours. The trams were not crowded, as previous posters had stated, maybe the overcast weather and threat of rain kept most away. The tour operators were speaking English but heavily accented to the point they might as well been speaking Greek. The admission price was fair and well worth the money, highly recommended.

This place is a must see for anyone visiting Nashville, country and western music fan or not, it was packed today, 8/9/19, but plenty of room to roam around, all day if you like, there is plenty to see and do, and exhibits on the who's who of country music. Could have a few more staff available to answer questions,  but this is hardly a deal breaker.

Bought a couple of tickets after pissing away money at the Galveston Historical Pier. I was offered a military discount and the young lady that sold me the tickets was super friendly along with the tour guide. We did the evening tour, when it was a bit cooler. Very informative and well worth the money, and highly recommend.

Had a great time here reliving my youth. I was stationed here in 1980. 2nd AD at the time, this place is not even recognizable, the only exception being the motorpools are still there in the same place. The museum was great. Multiple items on display and very informative.  Would love to return some day. Thanks so much.

What a great park. Could easily spend a couple nights camping in this park. So many nice trails. Well maintained. Those rock formations are huge. That split rock is huge. A lot bigger then the picture. Staff very friendly. Restrooms clean. Another job well done by NPS. A lot of Joshua tree. A very quiet park.

Great historical place, well manicured gardens and a beautiful building with  historical significance. We spent over an hour in the mid summer day, you have a lot of reasons to be proud Virginia, unlike the state of Californication, keep up the good work, we will be back.

Amazing place in history. The tour of his house was a 30 minute guided tour, very informative and to the point. The self guided tour of grounds and out buildings were a little longer. You can take pictures on the inside of his home. Keep up the good work.

Had so much fun in here. Very informative with plenty of activities for kids and adults alike. Well air conditioned to bring relief from the humidity. 2 hours was not enough time. Honestly need 2 or 3 entire days to thoroughly take in all the exhibits.

What a great place to explore. Some of the trees looked like the belong to the era of the dinosaurs. Beautiful hiking trails. Pay attention to other people's warnings regarding temperature and elevation change. I thought I was in pretty good shape.

Awesome end to our 25 day road trip across America. These bats are so important to our ecosystem and to have them in the city is a bonus. I'm not sure how many there were, probably 2500, well worth your time, price is right...free.

More weird stuff in the middle of nowhere, Thank God this sign is here because I left the folding map at home. Area 52 stuff. Found this weird fruit growing in a wash, turns out to be a coyote melon. See what I'm talking about.

Grat experience, although not being able to take photos of the interior was a let down, becoming more common these days. Multiple things to see and do, tour guides very interactive, well worth the money. Would do it again.
Nothing but 5 stars for this place. Much more then a railroad museum. Easily spent the entire day here. Grounds are well kept. Friendly snd knowledgeable staff.  Highly recommend if your in the area.
Very interesting and informative history. Nice hike if you can climb stairs. Pretty crowded the day we were there. Rather difficult accent. Very peaceful. Amazing people used to live in that canyon
What a shame this place is closing, reminds you of being a kid and who doesn't like that., this place did not disappoint, God Bless Fred, Barney, Wilma , Betty, Pebbles, BamBam and Dino.
This was well worth the price of admission,  military discount also available. A lot of information to absorb and very interactive. Self guided tour at your own pace. Highly recommend
Beautiful park. A lot to learn and very informative. Short nature hike with lots of informative signs. Well kept with nice concrete walkway.

Large but old play area with two playgrounds, swing sets, and some smaller climbing structures. Not that many fun or challenging play elements for kids to play on. There is one large playground with lots of ramps but not a lot to try or do. There is a smaller playground in a sand pit but beware because it gets covered in sand and becomes really slippery for the kids (especially the ones running around at top speed). The only real plus to this play area is that it has a seesaw (which is always packed). There are some large trees around the playground but note that there is not a lot of shade. Word to the wise: Avoid parking in the parking lot next to the golf course as you need to cross the road to get to the playground and sometimes the car traffic blows through the stop sign and the (poorly marked) crosswalk!

A national disgrace. Easily the worst museum on the National Mall. I know the museum is currently (Dec 2019) undergoing renovation but they would have been better off closing the whole museum down to do the renovation work. Hardly any exhibits are open and the ones that are open are worn and dilapidated. Restroom facilities are embarrassing (good luck finding a handicap accessible restroom or a restroom with a changing table). The cafeteria, which was never the best, is beyond sad and embarrassing ... You are better off getting food from a cart outside. Also, there is a ridiculous amount of security at the door (what am I going to do, steal a rocket?) for a museum which creates an unnecessary line and unneeded stress.

A nice park with a number of hiking trails, a large picnic area (with some pergolas that can be reserved for parties), and a small lake/duck pond. The picnic areas are nice but have definitely seen better days and could use a solid refurbishment. The restroom buildings are terrible, but about par for the course for a city park. There are often a lot of off leash dogs in the park (including in the picnic area!) so be aware if you are hiking here or if you have small children. A few scattered homeless encampments (or remnants  thereof) dot the park but overall it's not too bad.

Barnsdall is a nice quite place to sit and relax and enjoy the views of the hills and the city. The great lawn in front of the Hollyhock House is the place to be and is often packed with folks lounging around or picnicking. The Municipal Art Gallery is kind of blah and a waste of space. The Hollyhock House is a interesting but no need to see it more than once. The rest of the park is, honestly, not in the best of shape -- especially the lower park by Hollywood Blvd (the area near the parking lot) and the stairs and elevator at the rear of the park (near the Kaiser Hospital).
likes: Great lawn for lounging and picnicking

reviews_attraction.text: A fantastic museum. Beautifully and purposefully designed. Monumental but not cold. Exhibits are incredibly moving and symbolism of the "journey" from the basement and rising up to the ground level and above was both obvious and important to the experience. The museum (still) gets very crowded (which is a huge problem in the tight confines of the basement level) and the lack of bathrooms in the lower levels is a major problem. Wouldn't recommend this museum if you have toddlers or kids in a stroller (because of the crowds/bathroom situation).

Parque de Mexico probably used to be a nice park to relax and sit and learn about some Mexican history. Alas, this park has fallen on serious hard times. Almost all the statues and busts have been damages or lost (read: stolen) and most of the historic markers are missing (Benito Juarez and his plaque remain!) The seating areas are in terrible condition and the landscaping is barely holding up. Something wonderful could be done with this spot -- it just needs a little love and attention.

A spectacular monument and memorial and in a beautiful setting. A great space to wander through with plenty of small spaces for thought, reading, and reflection. The space is very focused on telling a story of the man and the moments he lived in and less on being "monumental" in the traditional sense (i.e forcing you to stare up at a massive statue or tiny quotations high on a wall). One of my favorite early morning spots in the city to visit.

Beautiful building (what you can see of it that is... come on Autry, get it together) but there really is not much exhibit space here that is open to the public. That said, the one full exhibit that was open was fantastic. The grounds are ok but honestly aren't in very good condition (be careful out there!). You won't end up spending much time here, but its a good place for a quick Saturday visit if you are on the Eastside and its free.

The playground here is terrible. For a park this size, and the number of folks who use it, the playground is outdated, too small, and very poorly maintained (weeds in the sand, graffiti, and faded paint). Basketball courts are crappy and oddly configured. Oh and parking here is a nightmare. The lots are too small, spread out all over the park, and some even have meters (granted, the meters aren't in effect on the weekend).

Easy to access hiking trails that lead deep into the Verdugo Mountains and connect to the other hiking trails up and down the Verdugos. The park itself isn't in the best shape (especially the picnic areas and the restrooms) and the park facilities are a bit run down and outdated. Typically there is plenty of parking, but the lots do fill up when there are activities in the lower park (ballfields, Brand Library, etc.)

Most overrated "hike" in all of Los Angeles. This is a place for walking, people watching, and socializing, not for hiking (or, ya know, seeing nature). The few "trails" here are glorified Billy goat paths that have been carved out across the hillsides over time. Oh and dogs are only allowed off leash in portions of the park ... a rule that a lot of dog owners sadly don't bother to follow.

A great place to stop and stroll if you are down visiting the museums in Exposition Park. Incredible variety of roses and in springtime the smell of the blooms fills the area. There is not a lot of shade in the park (which makes it bad for impromptu picnicking) but there are a few shaded pergolas in the park with benches if looking for a place to sit.

Small park with a (older) playground, shaded picnic tables, a splash pad, and an large open lawn. Park also has a restroom building (which would certainly benefit from more frequent cleanings). Not exactly the most relaxing park as noise from the nearby streets can get a little loud and make it hard to enjoy the lawn area.

Love the Hollywood Bowl. Love to sit back in the cheap sheets and kick it. Game plan is always to park at Hollywood and Highland mall, walk up to the bowl for a pre-game picnic at the park on Camrose, then up to the benches early in order to get comfortable (and claim as much space as possible).

Absolutely beautiful park that, of course, offers great views of the lake. Great place to sit out and get some sun, eat a snack, or get your feet wet in the lake. Love to come here and watch the boats ply the lake and see the seaplanes take off and land.

There is not much to see or do at this park. Just a wide open lawn with a few benches (and little shade).  Oh and there are restrooms available here ... though they are sometimes locked up early (like on the weekends, which makes no sense).

A new small park with a unique children's play area, adult fitness equipment, and a fun "porch swing". Can get crowded, and sometimes dog owners aren't so good about picking up after their pets, but overall it's a nice park.

What a hilarious,  ridiculous, and disgusting tourist attraction. Was, quite simply, an alley where the walls were covered in gum ... Lots of gum. Nice that Seattle would even tolerate "artwork" like this.

Great open space with trails that are almost always empty. A great, but short, hike that is away from the crowds (and off leash dogs) swarming over at Runyon Canyon. Nice and quiet, with pretty good views.
Great trailhead (with lots of parking) if you're up for a long hike either up to the Hollywood Sign or into the heart of Griffith Park. Note: No permanent bathrooms.
The facility is a little run down but it has cheap mini golf. Mini golf! The courses are freeway adjacent, but it is only really noticeable on a few holes.
About the only place to stop along the river and sit and relax. Freeway noise is fairly loud, but you can always pretend it's the sound of rushing water!
A nice, historic, open space and plaza, but the park "users" were just a tad too much for me to really be able to sit and enjoy the space.
Very small park with a half dozen benches and a small open lawn area. Plenty of nice mature trees that provide lots of shade.
A cute hidden gem of a park. Great place for a short stop to sit, snack, and enjoy the peaceful sounds of the waterfall.

We did this hike as a loop of the Nu'alolo, Nu'alolo Cliffs and Awa'awapuhi trails so I have posted the same review and photo on each of these. We did the loop in that order, finishing with the slightly easier Awa'awapuhi trail.
All three trails are well maintained and easily navigable and the views at the overlooks at the end of each trail are spectacular. Neither trail is particularly difficult, just regular hiking trail, although some sections of the Nu'alolo trail can be a bit steep and may be slippery in wet weather. The entire loop took us just over five and a half hours, including stops at the look out points and the 2 mile walk back down the road to the Nu'alolo parking lot.
You get to walk through varying terrain and ecosystems, from tropical rain forest to dry grass land and arid, rocky out croppings overlooking the Nā Pali  coast.
Highly recommend this hike!

First time we went here we had a decent experience. The location is stunning and the wine is okay. The second time about a week ago, we received terrible service. We were made to sit outside in 95 degree weather to taste wine, the taste of which was completely ruined by the heat, and when we asked to move inside to the air conditioning, were told that we should have worn shorts on such a hot day. Considering it is an appointment only venue requiring prepayment, the service should be of a much higher standard. I would highly recommend avoiding Copain and trying one of the dozens of other wineries in the region which have better wine and definitely better service.

Enjoyable trail and a must do for anyone from the Bay Area who enjoys hiking. It is an SF classic and takes in great views of the bay and the California coast. A slight detour through Muir Woods is a bonus.
Definitely start at the traditional start point in Mill Valley so you can take in the Dipsea steps. There is about a mile of urban hiking through some residential streets but you eventually get to the woods. The hike also ends with some even more steep steps and you come out at Stinson Beach. There are a couple of restaurants at the beach where you can grab food and a beer and then go sit out on the beach or go for a dip to cool off.

Headed out towards Amphitheater Lake. Didn't make it all the way as the days are short and there was several feet of snow once we got to the switchback (November). Did get great views of both Taggart and Bradely Lakes.
The trailhead itself seemed well maintained with bathrooms, information signs and trail maps and the parking was ample when we were there in the low season.
The trails seemed well sign posted, but due to the snow at the switchbacks, most of them were covered. Don't think there would be any issue with trail-finding in the summer and even in the winter it was relatively straight forward (just go up!)

I was a bit cautious considering some of the reviews regarding the poor customer service, but I didn't experience any of that. There were repeated cautions about not touching any of the art work, but considering that one of the pieces was a 3rd century mosaic, it really didn't seem over the top.
The tour itself was enjoyable and informative and the grounds of the castle were impressive. It isn't like seeing an opulent castle in Europe, but it's impressive considering it was built in the early 1900's.

Beautiful series of natural ocean pools that vary from benign swimming holes to inlet that get the swell from the ocean. The parking can be difficult as there are only several spaces so if you are staying in the Princeville area, it may be best to walk.
The hike down to the pools can be difficult and slippery in the wet, but once down all the pools are easily accessible with some scrambling over the volcanic rock. Wear sturdy shoes as the rocks can be sharp.

Did a driving tour through this National Park as we had our dog with us and was surprised at how much of an appreciation we could get for the Park. I had very little idea that this park even existed prior to planning a trip to the adjoining Lassen National Forrest and Caribou Wildness and I'm very glad we took this driving detour on the way home. I now want to go back with my crampons for a weekend warrior trip up Lassen Peak.

Went kayaking through one of the sloughs from the Marshlands Road and Thornton intersection. The parking lot and boat ramp had a lot of trash strewn about which was a little frustrating.
Watch out for the mud on the boat launch, it will suck the shoes right off your feet!
One in the slough, it was a much more pleasant experience. Plenty of bird life and a wide passage to paddle through.

Recently joined their wine club and love their wines, service and atmosphere. They are located in the mountains between Sonoma and Napa valleys and the drive out there, long with the view from the winery just adds to the amazing day and trip out here would make. It you want to try a smaller, slightly out of the way place, this is definitely for you!

Didn't see the elk when we were driving through the park, but did see them from the main road. You will almost certainly see the big horn sheep though, usually found on the east side of the southern butte.
Park is open 24 hours if you want to drive through at night, but there is nothing much to see at night.

Great service and amazing Bordeaux style wines. Came here with a couple of friends and had the place to ourselves. Tasted through the entire flight (with cheese pairings) with a few bonus wines and ended up walking away with a case between us and joining the wine club. Will definitely be back here soon!

Quick day hike out from the parking lot to Round Lake. Only a few hours round trip but a lovely hike through the valley, over the ridge and down into the next valley where Round Lake sits. Good lunch spot at multiple locations around the lake and several camping spots too.

Awesome nine hole course right next to the lake. Holes are not super challenging, but definitely not the sort of course you can hit from one fairway and land it on an adjacent fairway. If it is out of bounds it is likely down a coyote den...

Cute winery in Murphy. Only just discovered this wine producing region. Staff was very friendly and welcoming of dogs. Wine was decent with a few very different tasting Zins. Very competitively priced when compared with Napa and Sonoma.

Nice park for a walk or to take your dog out for the afternoon. Park on the eastern side and you can avoid paying for parking.
Path ways are relatively well maintained and there is a lake where you can cool off on a hot day.

If you are looking for this trail head, it is just up from the larger trail head that is supposed to be used by horses. This one isn't marked as well and if you get to Soda Butte (heading east), then you have gone to far.

This trail can get very slippery after any amount of rain and this may have left a more negative impression of the overall experience. The view of Hanalei town and beach are quite spectacular, even through the fog.
So awesome that this was converted into a National Park. Great access from the Bay Area, especially the South Bay. Just wish the park was bigger and we could go on multi-day backpacking trips.
Loved the winery and the tasting tour. Beautiful grounds and expanding with a nice rooftop area and the caves were awesome. And the old style Bordeaux’s and Rhône’s were exceptionally done.
Busy, but it was a holiday weekend. Great views of the South Bay. Only tasted the rosé and it was okay. Interesting color, clean and crisp taste. Slightly acidic.
Delightful wilderness area just west of Oakland. Lots of great hikes, well maintained trails and lots of off-leash areas to hie with dogs.
My favorite park in the northern Bay Area. Great for both mountain biking and hiking with expansive trails and some nice single track.
Very large playground with lots of different play equipment for ages from infant/toddler to older children. I'm there every Saturday!
Not the most picturesque of regional parks but conveniently located and nicely set up for going  a short or medium distance run.
What's not to like. I spend most of my weekends in Tahoe either snowboarding, hiking, kayaking or just enjoying the mountains.

Spent a week camping here and had a great time. Island packers gets you to the pier. Then a 1/2 mile walk to the campsite. Shade covers the site and table most of the day. All sites have a bear box to protect your food from the foxes. There is water at the campsite and pit toilets. Unfortunately, there are flies, bees and wasps which hover around you constantly. The foxes do provide some distraction.

The hikes are fantastic, but no shade along the trails as none of the native trees grow that high. Bring lots of sunscreen and wear a wide brimmed hat.

The kayak trip was fantastic and the caves were wonderful. They provide an optional wet suit and splash jacket in addition to the required helmet and life jacket. Definitely wear both as it can get quite cold on the water and with this protection you feel great.

The visitors center has a massive amount of information from how the islands got to here and the history of human habitation. The historic oven was closed to humans so the bats can roost. It is open the few months they do not roost, so call ahead if you wants to see it.
likes: Provided gear (wet suit, splash jacket, helmet, life jacket)

reviews_attraction.text: We spent 4 hours there at the Old Time Jubilee. We have wanted to get here for years, but the docents only have the houses open on the major events they hold a couple of times per years. Spring is alot cooler than summer so we went in May and the weather was fine. Start at the visitor's center for a video to get up to speed as to why this was settled, how it did and how it ended. Then check out the buildings. All very simple buildings which have been reconstructed on their original locations. A couple are Sears kit houses, the church is quite large, The livery house is original. They have a shed labeled blacksmith and the materials are inside, but it was locked up when we were there. A large number of docents are in the houses on this day and they were the real reason to come on a festival day. You really got a sense of why the residents came and stayed here got getting the different viewpoints. Lots of good food to be had from the festival vendors; bring your own if you do not come  on a festival day. There is a campsite attached to the site.
dislikes: Facilities & Services (Limited Access, Locked Blacksmith Shed)

reviews_attraction.text:
I have been to this garden over a dozen times since it opened. The center where you buy your tickets is in the parking lot to the left of the entrance. It also has the gift shop.
The park has a large central koi pond with paths circumnavagating it. There is also a Tea House, multiple lanterns, bridges, and bonsai. Over a dozen different species of bamboo alone with other grasses. At the end of the walk you can enter the building which is used as the Star Fleet Academy.
Alas,this park is next door to the sewage treatment plant so the smells can be sever if the wind is blowing to the west.

Wonderful to get ideas of what to plant in your garden. Endless wedding and quinceanera parties with photographers. A few homeless sleeping about and carts trying to sell stuff. Great place to sit and eat lunch. The science museum has restaurants and there is a whole bunch across the street to the east. USC is just north. Park in the lot if you are not walking from work. There is little street parking and it is frequently closed without warning for sporting events. Almost got towed a few years back and no longer risk it.

A couple of port-a-poties at the South West corner.

Came here to race in the Luck Dog Auto Race. Great track and massively large paddock.  We were really able to spread out to work on the car and camp out. Easy access on and off the track. Great sign to update the cars place in the race. Wonderful dinner Saturday night. The only downside is a total lack of light at night. There is not one light to direct where to go in the entire paddock. This was not a problem by the second night when everyone was set up, but on the first night we were all lost on where to set up and what was where.

I have been going here for about 50y. Much improved with all the new exhibit halls. From the old north American Mammals to the new one on dinosaurs it is fun to look at and you learn a lot. The gem vault is not to be missed. I was a member when our children were small and we would spend a weekend day just wondering through all the halls. Pay attention when a demonstration is happening as it is not that easy to find your way around. Ask any of the staff and they will direct you. Nice cafeteria in the basement.

Do not confuse the Official Visitors Center with the store fronts labeled "Visitor Center" which try to see you stuff as other reviewers have. The real one is located in the old railroad building as indicated on the map (not the sales pitch one located across the street to the west). Very helpful people with lots of information. The building is packed with free information and they can book tours throughout the city.

The city museum is across the street.

Stopped by here after a week on Santa Cruz. Great place to visit even if you cannot make it on the islands. Exhibits of the flora and fauna, skeleton of a pygmy mammoth, lots of stuff to touch for the children, and aquarium showing the tidal creatures and fish. Very helpful staff to speak with to plan your trip or just to learn more. Also there is an introductory movie, bathrooms, and outdoor exhibit area of each island..Free parking and free entrance.

12/13/2018 closed, for now, due to the fire.

There is nothing left but foundations and low walls to show this used to be a movie site. But as you walk past you arrive in a wonderful oak forest with lots of shade. Very flat so it is a great place for hiking with small children. They can run around all they want as it is too narrow an area to get lost. A block south is a railroad station and museum, also a great time for children.

I have been hiking here for years. Multiple ways to get in and out of this area, long and short hike with lots of round trip possibilities. Main fire road is quite flat, but hikes up the hills and down into the canyon to the river and falls are lots of fun. The main parking lots fills quickly. There is additional parking at the local park with alternative entrances to this area across the street.

The Hearst Castle of the east. A building specifically built like a medieval cloister to house medieval art. Completely built chapels with the European art work making up the parts. Halls filled with tapestries, including the famous unicorn tapestries. Stained glass work in the windows. Fine restaurant as well. We spent the entire day and could go back again to see the rest.

Wonderful base collections and amazing special exhibits. Park in lot 4 and exit the north east stairwell. It is due north from there, no need to go up the famous steps.

I went there for the exhibit on African ironwork. Truly amazing material covering its use in the different aspects of life and from many regions. From daily household items, farming equipment, and weapons.

Truly overwhelming experience to walk under the shuttle. The area starts with exhibits of the systems of the shuttle, from eating to the toilet, etc. Then you walk to the shuttle building and what a massive sight The shuttle is there and you are only about 10 feet from it. many displays in the building of how it is made and what it did.

No food or drink allowed..

Free museum. Very disorganized, racks of material with minimal, if any, descriptions, . Tons of stuff , so if you know a lot about experimental aircraft you may find some cool things to look at. If you do not know a lot already it just does not make much sense. It is right next door to the other museum in town.

Definitely pick a cool day to explore this part of the garden. There is little shade. The variation of species and locations of origin are amazing. Some of the specimens are over 100 years old. Great planting arrangements to see the ideas of what you may want to do. All are labeled.

We've gone here every couple of years for decades. Just saw the Enchanted: Forest of Light. Truly amazing. $9 for entry and miles to explore. Flat lower level for children and up a hill to the house for those with more energy.

Both the museum and the historic house across the street give you a fantastic description regarding how the area was settled and developed. Tons of interesting stuff quite well labeled. I especially loved the mining lights.

Large in size with a great collection of artifacts. I loved the recreated Hunley located outside the front entrance. You really learn how the state came to be, the effect of slavery, and the Civil War.
We just stopped there on our way around town. Having seen what is left of the original in Greece it was great to get an idea if its actual size and the effect it would have made in its day.
There is a 2 large room area for the permanent collection. This was great. The rest of the museum has changing temporary exhibits, which now has shaded canvases of little interest to me.
Went on their Train Days Celebration. A number of the trains are open to take guided tours through. Many exhibits by multiple organizations. Live blacksmith forging demonstration.
One room of the history of New York through the social changes which have occurred which was very interesting. The gilded age exhibit was also great.
Came here for their fall festival. Lots of traditional dancers, food truck for lunch, exhibits for the kids, and access to the historic house.
Definitely worth a stop. 2 floors if exhibits in the old Coast Guard dorm. You get an idea of how they lived and what they did.
It takes hours to go through the ships and the 5 tours on the aircraft carrier. Lots of helpful volunteers

What a great place for a leisurely afternoon stroll with or without a dog.  There are a variety of paths and trails to follows, both improved and unimproved depending on your liking, and the "lake" is rather picturesque on a sunny day as well.  There are an assortment of aquatic birds that frequent the area, all of which appreciate a few crumbs of crusty bread if you have any to spare.

Popular public open space with many walking trails and off-leash dog park.  The scenic ocean vistas are second to none. Perfect place to unwind and watch a picturesque Pacific Coast sunset. Be advised, there are no restrooms for the humans, but there are K-9 waste bag dispensers at the entrance to the park.

Large county park with plenty of open space and picnic tables to accommodate large crowds. There is a big playground for the kids and several horseshoe pits for the adults. The palm trees are plentiful and spaced well for slack lining. The park is also equipped with several bathrooms.

Beautiful well-kept campground with plenty of restrooms spread throughout. There is a large beach area and many picnic areas to choose from. There is a full marina on site with boating supplies, gas, and rentals of both watercraft and self-powered aquatic equipment.

This is primarily a sports complex with two softball field, a baseball diamond, and tennis courts. There are public restrooms, but no playground or picnic areas. The adjoining park, Plaza Del Mar, has plenty of grass and trees, but is overrun with homeless folks.

Large community park with lots of grassy open space, picnic areas with tables and a few BBQ's, public bathrooms, and a playground for the kids. Beautiful sweeping view of the Pacific Ocean and the Channel Islands in the distance.

Located along the cliff's edge of Cliff Drive overlooking the majestic Pacific Ocean, this site serves as ongoing memorial to the surfers who have lost their lives in these treacherous waters in pursuit of the ultimate wave.

Great neighborhood park with a large grassy open space, large playground, a public restroom, along with many picnic tables and bbq's. There is a running creek during the winter months but it's dry during the summer.

Tranquil little grass-covered park bordered by Mission Santa Cruz and Holy Cross Catholic Church. While the old mission is rather understated, Holy Cross is the opposite; it's huge monolith dominates the skyline.

Beautifully landscaped, well laid out park providing easy access to multiple viewing platforms for Shoshone Falls. There are basic toilet facilities available and a small gift shop that doubles as a snack bar.
Not your typical park, albiet beautiful in it's own right. Dominated by oak trees and large boulders. There is a playground but no other general open space or grass. Plenty of picnic tables and BBQs.
Great neighborhood park with a few short walking trails, a small playground, and half-court basketball up top. There are a 6-7 picnic tables, a drinking fountain, and few bbq's, but no bathroom.
Relatively short pedestrian bridge linking Heritage Square Park to Centennial Park. There's quite a bit of swing to the bridge in the middle section so be careful if you have motion issues.
This otherwise beautiful sprawling waterfront park loses a few stars in my book, due to the number of homeless denizens in varying stages of addiction and related mental health crises.
Great spot to view the Snake River, Perrine Bridge, and Perrine Falls. Plenty of hiking trails for the adventurous folks and plenty of grassy picnic areas for the casual observers.
Beautiful sprawling mountain landscape with a mix of trails both improved and unimproved. Plenty of parking at the trailhead. No water or bathrooms. Dog friendly.
Beautiful sprawling mountain landscape with a mix of trails both improved and unimproved. Plenty of parking at the trailhead. No water or bathrooms. Dog friendly.
Great public beach with plenty of paid parking.  There is a large grass picnic area with tables and BBQ's.  There are public bathrooms and a few outdoor showers.
Large community park with a soccer field and a softball diamond. There is also a playground, outdoor exercise equipment, and a public bathroom.
Great local park with lots of open space, beautiful ocean view, large group area with BBQ, a big playground with swings, and a public restroom.
Quaint historic open space to the front of City Hall and home to the annual FIESTA Mercado during the Old Spanish Days celebration.
Located at the mouth of Santa Cruz Harbor, this iconic lighthouse is easily accessible via a short walk along an improved pathway.
With its enormous canopy of leaves high above it's sprawling snake-like roots, the Morton Bay Fig Tree is a unique sight to see.
Small heavily wooded park on a steep slope, with a small parking lot, but with an amazing panoramic view of the city and harbor.
Beautiful beach with great waves.  Hidden in plain sight. It's a bit of a walk from the nearest parking lot, but not bad.

Waking up at 630 to get tickets for this place was well worth it. First, let me impress upon you the scale of this place, because we severely underestimated it when we got there. There are 10,000 pieces on display. There are 3 basement floors and 4 floors in the tower. Between you on the bottom floor and the main entrance on ground level is a mile of exhibits. The bottom floors are full of history, some which you or your kids may have read about in history class, others which expand on it, and still others that will really pull at your heartstrings. The upper floors are more modern history, faster to go through, and more spaced out. There’s a great view from the topmost floor. To get tickets, definitely opt for booking in advance. If you find out too late, wake up at 630, go to the etix website (from the museum) and start refreshing the page at 6:28 (opens at 630). It usually sells out in 5 minutes or so. As a last resort, line up in front of the museum about half an hour before 1PM.

Beautiful and unique view of San Francisco and the Golden Gate Bridge. You can pick out Ocean Beach, Lands End, and the Bay Bridge as well. The drive up to Hawk’s hill is fairly easy, but there can be a lot of traffic in the late morning/afternoons. Parking can be found on the side of the road or in a couple of lots; from there you can hike to the top of the hill and the bunker (0.3 miles, extremely easy walk) to get a spectacular look at the hills of the Marin Headlands. You can also brave a 3 mile hike to the Visitor Center (its deceptively easy going down, but you need to hike all the way back up). There are usually crows and hawks, so bring binoculars to watch for them. Also, there are pretty strong winds up here so a hat/scarf/windbreaker are recommended.

I think this is a generally underrated Smithsonian museum, as it is further out of the way than many of the other museums. But it is extremely kid-friendly, has great staff, and shows a pretty important part of American history. Whether you’re a stamp-collector or not, I’m sure you’ll find the exhibits showing how stamps portrayed monumental American Advances inspiring, or the gallery on the evolution of the postal systems from the Pony Express to Air Mail interesting. A couple other plusses about the location: it is close to Union Station and Chinatown, both of which can be quick lunch stops before or after you go; it is also near the Georgetown Law School, which can be packed into a visit as well.

Holds commanding views of the surrounding area, with great coast lookouts. You want to sit on the left side of the bus going up and the right side going down for maximum coastal views (though the bus turns a lot so you’ll be fine on either side). The tour takes 40 minutes and you’ll have plenty of time to take pictures while the guide talks and can still roam the grounds afterwards. The outdoor pool is currently drained and under renovations but the indoor pool is still extremely impressive (you’ll see it on your way out). There are some nice old tapestries inside if you’re into those. You may also see wildlife like deer on your way up.

If you are a fan of modern art or of the contemporary style, this is the museum for you. Current exhibitions include the visually striking Pickett’s Charge, the psyche-jarring Belief and Doubt, and the contemplation stimulating What Absence is Made of. The sculpture garden around the museum is nice as well. The museum has a Dolcezza on the main floor where you can relax and snack while sitting on some gorgeous wooden benches.

I've gone here over and over again for the great views of the city. There are two routes to the top of the steps, one the tiled steps and two the steps you hit when approaching the area from kirkham/ Lawton. You can hike all the way to the top past the stairs for dual bay and ocean views

Free if you have a SID,th you have to check your bags at the door. Offers great views! The bells ring every hour so watch out for the loudness if you're up in the viewing room at the time! Berkeley students, there IS a class you can take to play the bells!

Ever since the elephants left I've felt driving up to the Oakland Zoo was worth a better experience- they have better rides and more animals, and more consistent weather. Not that this zoo hasn't been catching up and makingi improvements over the years.

Great, beginner friendly hiking trails surrounded with trees and little creeks. Relatively flat with tree roots and easy to follow trails. They have signs that tell you the distance to the destination as well. Very serene, multiple entrances.

Its a long drive up from San Francisco, but absolutely worth the coastline and hills you'll see. We ran into some cows crossing the road on our way up here, but the views were breathtaking. Note the lighthouse might not be open.

Gorgeous views at sunset as the light shines off the pool waters. You can walk out into the foundation remains and enjoy the fantastic rocks jutting out of the ocean. Definitely great to walk around after lands end.

Honestly, a quiet, somber place for reflection. Went here for a middle school field trip, and something about the building really, really moved me. Maybe take a trip as part of a more reflective trip.
A beautiful building with a storied history, gorgeous architecture and cannons. The interior has many lecture halls and libraries. Inside you can find the historic Riggs Library
Bison are animals, and on some days they won't be out! But you can glimpse them in their paddocks. On the nice days when they're grazing though, they are a sight to see.
This is one of the most visually stunning monuments and quite a sight to see when the sun reflects off the water. Really gives a sense that we are a United people.
Great view of the entire city, great to hike up after the 16th avenue visit. Good to go in the afternoon or evening to just enjoy seeing the city settling down.
The better of the Bay Area zoos, it comes with rides, a skyride, elephants, and an afternoon of animals! The lemurs are adorable, and the goats are friendly.
Larger picnic area for gatherings, parties, or celebrations, with plenty of space for kids to run around and to set up your grill and tables.
The showings throughout the day are fantastic, definitely plan to see one of them during your visit! The graphics really are immersive.
Less crowded than the 16th avenue steps but beautiful painted steps. You can also make your way to the 16th avenue ones from the top!
The emotions encapsulated in this piece are haunting and touching. Definitely a must see, either early or late to avoid crowds.
Its a shame you can't take tours to the top anymore, but good food trucks in the area and looks stunning at night.

reviews_attraction.text: Beautiful short stretch of an art piece that makes for good photoes a woodsy trail to the Palace of Fine Arts.
Longer winding trail down to the beach, but you can see lots of stacked rocks on a fairly small, sandy spread.
Pretty waterfront views and a good place to stretch or pause on a run. It's also where the bow and arrow is.

A nice park for camping, if you are aware that you won't be able to sleep due to the birds making a racket all night. You will also discover that there are hidden fees doubling your rates from what you paid online. If you go in April you will have the park pretty much to yourself, and the hiking around the park is great.

Unless you like hysterical children, you'll want to go on a cold, rainy day, when you have the huge place basically to yourself. If you manage that it is a quite extraordinary experience. I have seen better curated zoos, but not in the US.

Extremely long wait for parking, park at nearby Woburn point instead. Note that there's several more bathrooms in the parking lot, no need to wait at the first one you see. The views are very much worth the long drive and crowds.

Too expensive for a museum that focuses on kids that can barely count to ten. Also a lot of the exhibits are out of order. Sadly a missed opportunity and I am embarrassed that Google sponsored this place.
what were they thinking? chrysler built what they thought to be the foremost business offices in the world, for a car company? the painting on the lobby ceiling is interesting but also sad.
Just awful. There's more parking here than park, every few steps you're interrupted by a fence or a highway. Everything is crumbling and loud from the nearby horrendous traffic.
I usually hate video art, but it turns out if it is really well done, as it is here, it is a delight, despite the annoying "influencer" types who are trying to capture selfies.

We went on this trail on April 5, 2017. The waterfall was at full strength from the run offs. It was spectacular. The trail itself was somewhat rugged but very manageable. The fire was evident everywhere, dead trees charcoaled from the devastating heat of the flames. The trails splitted off at some points along the way and sometimes it was difficult to follow. But persevere because the payoff was worth it. The water was very clear and the weather couldn't be better. Not a lot of people know about this trail so it's always very serene compared to other attractions at Yosemite.

Reachable within a 15min drive from downtown Redwood City, this park has fantastic trails for hiking and walking your dog. Really great off leash area. Most o the trails are shaded so day hikes are possible except for the. Hottest days in the Bay Area. Shorter trails like Hessler is nice too if yoh have kids in tow. Beautiful sweeping view of the Eastern part of the Peninsula from the top.

Really nice park with a huge lawn. Dogs are supposed to be on leash but many I saw when I visited were roaming free, which was ok since all of them as far as I know were well trained and well behaved. Plenty of picnic tables. It's in the middle of a residential neighborhood so the surroundings is very nice. It was flooded during last winter's storm, but it has since recovered nicely.

Historical ballpark that's worth visiting even if you don't like baseball or the Red Sox. Usually a player would meet fans in the team store before games, and the photo opp is really great for kids. You have to come very early to get in line though. Plenty of things happening pregame just outside the ballpark makes this a pretty fun place to hangout on game day.

This should be one of the last places you visit in Washington DC, given that it's actually not that impressive as a collection of artifacts, and it costs a lot of money to enter. It's more fun if you bring your kids to do the whole spy hunt thing, but even then it's not that interesting. Skip unless you have nowhere else to go.

Wonderful renovation added a massive amount of gallery space. The pieces now have more room to "breathe" so to speak. Exhibits are numerous and varied. Love the spotlights on artists like Rothko, Warhol and Calder. They seem to have added a lot of staff who assist visitors in a very friendly way. Great improvement overall.

Pretty ragged looking park located next to Twin Creeks baseball complex. On one side you have a lot of drones flying around. Above planes are a constant. The look of the park makes you think whether this is one of many Superfund sites in the Bay Area.

Beautiful and well equipped sporting facilities. The fields are well kept, and the spectator areas provide comfort and plenty of shade. There are two concessions in good locations. A lot of grass for kids to play, and for your dog to walk.

What else can be said about the home of the Champions that have not already been said? Beautiful park, good food and not a bad seat in the house. Excellent atmosphere and plenty of activities before during and after games. Great location.

Beautiful trail at a higher altitude, which means you will likely see snow until early spring. Fairly steep at some places but mostly manageable terrains make this a pleasant 2.5 hour round trip hike. Especially good with family.

Beautiful park in the heart of Burlingame downtown. Large baseball fields and park area for all sorts of activities. Perfect for summer picnic with the family.
Baseball field has off leash hours. Check out signage for hours.

Large park with playgrounds, basketball, tennis and handball courts. The soccer fields are poorly maintained. The baseball diamonds seem to be a little bit better. There's a batting cage for the local little league teams.

Awesome permanent collection, plus a solid variety of exhibits make De Young an inspiring cultural experience. Recently caught the Keith Haring show and that was amazing. Beautiful architecture and interior design.

Windswept ballpark by the bay. On a cold spring day you could get gusts of wind reaching 20+ miles per hour, so be prepared to be sandblasted if you are here to either play or watch a little league baseball game.

Amazing museum even if you are not a baseball fan. A lot of history and great artifacts. A wonderful place for young players to see the narratives through the years about the game they play. Truly memorable.

Really cool museum. Sound lab is a must see. I am a little mixed about the Nirvana exhibit. Seems somewhat of an antithesis to what they stood for. Couldn't really grock the idea of them being in a museum.
Very nice park, well maintained fields and really new facilities. The concession is expensive and choices are slim. You can bring you dog if it is a service pet.
Cheesy fun, touristy place. Avoid talking with the hustling impersonators outside if you don't want to tip them for a photo. Good to visit once every 5-10 years.
Well equipped city park with baseball fields, basketball court and a nice skate park. The wind can really pick up here especially in the morning and evening.

Fantastic new location, same amazing collections. Really cool building with a wonderful view of the Hudson from the rooftop and glass staircase.

Beautiful property and a friendly staff. I came here for a company off site, and the experience was quite nice. The beautiful weather helps.
A national treasure, and a must see when visiting DC. Great exhibits that really enrich your knowledge about the history of this country.
A quintessential San Francisco landmark. The coolest is the Diego Rivera mural. The view at the top of the tower is breathtaking.

Water level is really high compared to other lakes. Excellent for kayaking and cliff jumping. The boat inspection is a bit ridiculous but it's for a good reason. They thoroughly inspect kayaks inside and out, as well as life jackets and paddles. If anything is wet it's an automatic failure. Make sure your boat is dry inside and out!

Absolutely amazingly beautiful hike. Water on both sides. Elk throughout the trail. Massive Elk, at that. Very hilly hike, with regular ups and downs. The last mile is dense sand, making it the most difficult mile to and from the end. Very pleasing and slightly exhausting. Moderate difficulty for sure.

Gets a bit more activity on the weekends. $5 to enter per vehicle per day. I've only played around in the 4x4 offroad area. They have an entire different section for dirt bikes.

Fairly beautiful place. I went today and it's very dry. I'll need to revisit when it is green after some rain. There is quite a big of elevation gain if you hike anywhere. Quite a bit of mining history here!

Awesome place to hike or mountain bike. Excellent trails and plenty of hills to climb depending on the route you take. Large rock faxes, etc. There's nothing else like this in the area. Cool place!

The first thing you should know about The Museum of The San Fernando Valley is that hey are only open Tuesdays, Thursdays and Saturdays 1-5pm. The second thing you should know about The Museum of The San Fernando Valley is that there is nearly zero signage from the street. Trust the address and park anywhere in the (free) lot. There is only very missable sign that can only be seen if you catch it as you’re drink bing in the driveway. As you enter the commercial building filled with other businesses, go to the second floor (elevator is available for those who need it) and find your way to suite 204.

There you’ll find it! This museum is very small, but it has a big heart.  The caretaker I spoke with was VERY enthusiastic, informative and appreciative that we were there. It wasn’t empty as there were at least three other parties. The docent did a great job of making sure everyone received attention. Maybe even a hint too much as I was happy to explore on my own.  She was great though.

There is a room that had wonderful art that I believe is a lot sting exhibit. Then there are some other things to see. I especially liked the Vincent Price head cast!  In the back there is an exhibit in mid century modern houses and they’re working on an exhibit about the dwarf sports teams that used to be a part of SFV culture. Maybe my favorite things were the “Now-and-then” photos and the menus of old defunct sfv restaurants.

I might have given this museum a lesser rating but I make it a rule to never give a free museum less than 4 stars. The people who work here are hard working volunteers who do their best to preserve history as best they can. I hope that we’ll see this grow. I wonder if there could be a collaboration with the much larger Valley Relics Museum.  Where Valley Relics has an infinitely more impressive collection of artifacts, I wonder if The Museum of San Fernando Valley’s historical expertise could help tell the story of those artifacts.

At any rate... this is a free museum with free parking! Check it out!  Maybe organize s trip to several small museums in the area on one day!
likes: Unique exhibits (e.g., Vincent Price head cast)

reviews_attraction.text:
The Workman and Temple Family Homestead Museum is part of LA's "Passport 2 History" program!  If you don't know what that is, please look it up as there are over 80 participating museums, that give you stickers when you go there and there are actually prizes the more you go to.  It's a fun way to learn about museums.

The museums in the P2H program range in their grandiosity, from very small adobes to full scale art museums.  I was expecting the former, but we go much closer to the latter!  They're not fooling around here, and they're constantly growing and renovating.  They had quite an impressive visitor's center where you wait for the tour (complete with free coffee - a part of the history lesson of the community's prohibition ties).  If you get there early, you can enjoy the koi pond (with an impressive soft shell turtle among the large fish and other turtles) and graveyard.

There are two tours - The Workman House and the second house next door (that's name escapes me at the moment).  We only had time for the first tour (each is 45 minutes and we had a 5 year old with us), but it was very cool and informative.  The exhibits are kind of bare in comparison to other homestead museums, where there are more artifacts from the home - but I think there is much more of that in the second home that we missed.  AND there is a behind the scenes tour where they take you in the basement and second floor!  The best part... ALL of these tours are FREE!!!  That's right!  They even have a cute little gift shop that actually has interesting relevant items and toys that are reasonably priced!  So we got some old time candy sticks and a slide whistle because... why not?!?

I know this may be out of the way for many... but make a day trip out of it!  We visited here, The Puente Hills Mall (The Twin Pines Mall from Back To The Future!!! - Be sure to go inside and check out the Twin Pines Mall sign inside the mall!), The Hsi Lai Temple (SUPER cool place that is very welcoming to visitors), a tamale shaped building, the Armenian Martyrs Memorial and more!

I visited the Hathaway Museum with my 4 year old.  We had some other errands to run in the Santa Fe Springs area, and saw this was nearby on our Passport2History Museum Program.  The grounds are large and there is a lot to see.  Watch for the sign as I drove by it the first time.  It's a little confusing where to park, as when I went in I thought just the house on the left was the museum, but the entire grounds are the museums, so you can park anywhere.  Just watch out for the chickens, roosters and cats running around!

The docent was already mid tour, so another staff member caught us up to him.  Full disclosure... by this time in the day, my toddler was in a bit of a mood, so he wasn't in the best place for a tour.  The first staff member had told us there they had 25 baby goats, so my son was eager to get to that part of the tour.  Our docent was very kind and knowledgable and gave a very detailed tour.  It was a bit too detailed for my son's speed, so we had to cut it kind of short, but if you're intro history, I would definitely come back and check this place out because there is a lot to see!  He said we only caught about a third of the place.  There is a lot of cool oil stuff in the big mental oil tower which is now part of the museum.  We didn't make it to the house across the street that I'd LOVE to see!  We did get to see all the baby goats though!

There is a ton to see here, but make sure you give yourself enough time.  I'd go when they open so the kids are a bit more ready for a tour.  I wish this were a bit more self guided so we could still see everything but go at our own speedy pace.  Our docent while doing his best, wasn't really picking up on the cues that we needed the speedy tour.  But if you're adults only, you'll love this!  I hope to get back there!

You can make a decent day trip out this way from LA.  Look up what else is around.  There are some cool historic restaurants, other museums, and King Richard's Antique Center, which is supposedly the largest in CA!
dislikes: Docent not responsive to pacing needs

reviews_attraction.text:
There are supposedly more museums in the US than Starbucks.  I'd like to believe that's true, and if one really dives in and explores... it's not that hard to believe.  We're always on the hunt to visit new museums and this week brought us to the Monrovia Historical Museum.  For a FREE local history museum, they do a great job!  This used to be the Monrovia Municipal Pool since WAY back, and when the pool grew too expensive to keep up, rather than destroy the building, they turned it into a museum!

There are two wings, which were the women's and men's locker rooms respectively.  There are all kinds of exhibits and rooms that show what houses, clothing, storefronts, music rooms, schools and more used to look like.  One wing is more devoted to Monrovia history.  The other currently has a WW1 exhibit and has a permanent Natural History collection that was donated by the owner when he passed.  Even the old wooden boxes that store the items are cool as they are from the 1930s and were made to house the exhibit you're looking at!  The telephone exhibit is especially cool.

We had our five year old with us and they do have things kids can do.  He liked dressing up as a policeman in the police exhibit.  You can play with the phones in the telephone exhibit.  There are a couple of cool touch boxes in the natural history collection... and even a desk set up where kids can color and play with Lincoln Logs.

If you live in LA and are looking for a little day trip... I'd recommend planning a day trip and adding this to your list!  You can visit the nearby downtown area by Liberty Park where there ALWAYS seems to be a festival of some sorts going on.  There are cuts shops, restaurants and even a very cool antique store.  Take a picture with the nearby Mark Twain statue on a bench in the park!  Back to the museum... hedge expectations... this isn't Kidspace or The Natural History Museum or Discovery Cube... this is one of hundreds of small local museums... but they do a GREAT job!  Visit!
likes: Cultural Value: Local history, WW1 exhibit
Facilities & Services: Free admission, kid-friendly activities
On-site Activities: Interactive exhibits, dressing up, telephone play

reviews_attraction.text:
As a full-time toddler father, I try to get my son out of the house at least once a day.  We're always looking for new things to do as I have to admit I get bored just going to a park everyday.  Placerita Canyon Nature Center is a great thing to slip into your repertoire of places to go.

While there is tons of hiking, if you're not going to do the hikes, it's a nice, fairly short trip that you're not going to spend hours at, yet still interesting.  Walking up to the nature center, be sure to check out all the cages that have local birds in them... I particularly love the raven!  They also have tortoises too!  There is an additional hallway that used to have fish and some other things, but that's been empty lately.  You can still check it out though.

Then there is the nature center itself which my son loves!  There are two rooms and a hallway.  One room has panoramas with fake scenes of the outdoors and different wildlife.  The best part for a toddler is that there are glowing buttons to press!  Each button makes the sound of a different bird.  There is also a TV screen that my son loves (for some reason) that shows old black and white movie clips that were filmed around here.  The second room has a bunch of cool taxidermy including a huge bear!  But they also have some live animals like rattlesnakes, a turtles, fish, a bee hive and more!  So while it's not going to take an hour... there's still enough here to make it worth the trip form LA.

Then, you should take the "nature trail", which is a very short hike that takes you past some cool old buildings and around the corner to "The Oak of the Golden Dream" which is the site of the first place gold was discovered in California!  It's not the most exciting thing on the planet, but it's something fun to do.

I highly recommend checking this place out!  We will often also visit the nearby Dunkin' Donuts after, haha.  They have a drive through which is nice.

I discovered the Oxnard Historic Park Foundation in the "Passport 2 History" booklet.  I'm always looking for interesting and different places to see with my three year old.  The grounds are cool and have a nice display of farming equipment, tractors and vegetation.  There was a fundraiser setting up when we visited, so keep them in mind for your next rental.

There are two structures to explore.  The first has some cool artifacts in it and has more of a museum feel.  We enjoyed the cool large safe and admired the player piano, though it wasn't currently working.  Then we were showed where the main building is and were given the okay to self-explore.  It's important to note that they are currently fundraising for the first phase of restoring the house.  Unlike many of the other historical sites and museums we've visited, this one is just being put together.  Upon exploring the second floor, nearly all the doors had spider webs (complete with spiders) across them, and most of the rooms are empty.  There was some cool things, like the piano which my son loved.  There was some cool old signs and historical memorabilia, but I'm more excited to watch this place grow into a place of beauty.  Right now it is fun as it has that kind of "exploring and old haunted house" kind of vibe.  So just note the above and don't let the kids wander too far in front of you as I could imagine injury happening at the moment.

As far as rating, I almost gave this a 3... but since it's a work in progress, it's free and the grounds are lovely... I think it deserves a solid 4.

Here's the key:  There are also TWO playgrounds just next door if you'd like to let the kids play... or better yet, bundle a few of the passport 2 history museums together!  We visited The Pleasant Valley Historical Society Museum & Botanical Garden AND the Reyes Adobe all on the same day!

The Hollywood Bowl is one of the most historic concert venues in America I'd say.  That said, it's not my favorite place to see a show.  Let's start with the good... the history here is amazing.  Every time I go, the first thing I think about is how The Beatles played here.  It still gets amazing acts to this day.  In fact, many of your best shows are going to be here.

One of the coolest secrets of the Bowl is that you can see FREE rehearsals for their non-rental shows (so not for acts like Depeche Mode... but for the LA Phil shows).  You can drive right up to the venue and sit through the rehearsal!  It's amazing and a great thing to take children too!  The actual Bowl events are very cool too.

For the national rental shows... the big acts, I'll be honest... the sound isn't great here.  It's not nearly as good as an indoor venue like Staples Center.  Also, there is a very strict curfew here of 11pm, so the acts can't play super long.  You're not going to get those 4 hour Phish shows you might get at another venue.

The worst thing is the parking and mob scene.  You can park here or you can park at a free lot and take a shuttle.  Additionally you could park at Hollywood and Highland, get some Starbucks and have them validate your parking and walk up.  So there are options... but getting out is somewhat of a nightmare.  Then you'll be in Bowl traffic for a LONG time once you get to your car.  I had heard that The Greek was a nightmare... but I actually had very little trouble leaving the Greek.  There was barely any traffic.  Sure, you waited a bit because of that light in the residential neighborhood, but that was a breeze compared to Bowl traffic.

The parking and sound situation made me consider giving this 3 stars... but the free rehearsals bumped it back up to 4.

My three year old and I visit many local museums as part of the Passport 2 History program.  They range in their interestingness, but the Channel Islands Maritime Museum is certainly one of the best!  It's not huge on the level of a Natural History Museum or Getty... but it's larger than many of these one-room local history museums.  There are two floors that each have a large room or two.

You'll see many ships and paintings of ships... but what makes this even more fun is that they have many things for children to do!  They have a play mobile pirate ship for the kids to play with that kept my son's attention for a LONG time!  They also have a selfie station where you take a picture in front of a cannon, complete with wigs, hats and costumes to try on!  There was no one else in the museum when we went, so we could take our time and really have fun!  Upstairs has other neat things to do, and even better... beautiful views of the water!  They had a coloring station for kids that had a handful of plastic toy whales that kept my son's attention for a LONG time!  They had special lighting that attempted to recreate and "under water" feel, and he had a great time playing with the toy whales there!  They also had some whale bones, which I'm always fascinated by!  Especially the size of a whale vertebrate!

While many of the Passport museums are free... this one is $7/adult.  So that is probably why it's a bit cooler than many others.  We had a great time.  There is free parking, and not far from Ventura, so there are plenty of things to do around to make for a great day trip!

It’s kind of unfortunate google+ puts The Tar Pits and The Page Museum in the same listing. It is absolutely free to visit but it’s in the surrounding park. While the tar pits are certainly not super exciting… They are kind of cool specially when you realize what they have. See the prehistoric gases lives in bubble even to this day and that’s pretty cool. What a lot of people don’t know is that there actually multiple times.. Other than the big one, be sure to visit pit 91. The Tar Pits alone get 4 stars. A nice place to picnic. Even better, visit LACMA just next door.

The museum is much smaller than it looks. You can easily do the entire museum in 20 minutes. So it is vastly overpriced.  You can get in free by reserving tickets with your LA COUNTY library card. But parking is still $12. Next time I’m going to forward street parking… But I thought we would be more than a few hours before I knew how little was in the museum.  Don’t get me wrong... they have some cool stuff. The atrium is nice... it’s just a quick visit. Taking value into consideration I’d give this a 2.5... so mixed with the 4 star tarpits I’ll give it a 3.

If you live in Los Angeles usual absolutely visit the tar pits. But skip the museum. If you are visiting and have heard how cool the Tar Pits are, but I have a limited time… You can skip it altogether. If I was only here for a week there are much more fun things to see in LA than the tar pits. But if you’re here a while, check them out!

The Plaza Firehouse museum is a small, yet free museum.  I'd probably rate it a 3 due to how small it is, but I've recently committed to not give any free museum less than a 4 (unless there was something wrong).  The man who worked there was very nice and informative.  If you want the full experience, come on a Thursday when they have two workers and one of them brings you upstairs!  We missed that part, but I bet it's super cool.

There are definitely cool things here, just not a ton.  While I wouldn't make a day trip to the area just for this museum, this area is CERTAINLY worth a day trip!  My toddler and I literally visited 6 museums!  There are small museums all around here and almost all of them are free!  Start your journey with a walk down Olvera Street!  Catch the Avila Adobe, maybe have lunch or a snack.  Then walk across the way and visit The Chinese American Museum, the Plaza Firehouse Museum and the new Gateway to Nature (which is a nature center full of things for kids to do).  Then walk across the street to La Plaza De Culturas y Artes museum.  Maybe poke your head into Our Lady of Angeles Church.
