I'm very Atheist, but this is historic as it's literally what named and started Los Angeles.  Then continue down Main street and hit up the American Tropical Historical Museum and end with the Italian American Museum!  There are a few other things in there too I think I missed.  A great day!

When I get away with my wife, wine tasting is one of my favorite activities.  While the wines didn't knock my socks off... this is probably the best wine tasting in Julian, which is why I gave it 4 stars instead of 3 (it'd be 3 anywhere else).  The pourer was nice, but a little insulting.  My wife made a comment about a wine tasting sweet and the pourer pulled a "well actually...." and said how "we don't say sweet... we say fruit forward as there is no actually sugar in it".  We're not wine virgins... we've been to hundreds of wineries over the years... we know.  Bet guess what... all that stuff that is written on your menu... taste like apricot, tobacco, roses, pineapple, etc... whatever it is... THERES NON OF THAT IN THERE EITHER!!!!  They are descriptors to describe what it makes you feel and what it makes you taste... and if my wife thought it tasts sweet to her... it tasted sweet to her!  It was just very weird and rude... never been corrected about what we tasted before.  Again... other than that she was nice and gave us an AMAZING recommendation for lunch.

Edit:  You MUST try the 2015 Mourvèdre!!!  Far and away our favorite wine here, and we bought a bottle.  Many times when you try the bottle you got at home, it doesn't always live up to how you felt about it when on vacation... but this ABSOLUTELY did!  I'm going to have to go back for more!!!  Or should I say... go back for Mourvèdre...

We had such a fun time at Jurupa Mountains Discovery Center! We’ve noticed the sign as you drive by the enormous metal Wooly Mammoth up on the hillside, but today was the first time we were able to stop.  There are 4 different sections. The main “office” has a store, live animals and a lot of beautiful taxidermy. They have snakes, lizards, bugs and more. Outside there is a pen with various types of large tortoises.  The gentleman who worked there was super nice and informative.  Oh... I forgot to mention the dinosaur bones!

Across the way is their Earth Science Museum which was actually very cool and had many displays! There are cool things to see for browsers, and even cooler info for those who want to take the time to read!

There is also a “Biblical Garden” with a pond of fish and turtles.  Lastly there is a path through a gnarly cactus garden that is truly impressive and you’ll see Dino sculptures here and there.

Thus far... all of that is absolutely free!!! There is a point on the path that you can’t go yourself and they offer $9/person guided tours... but not on Saturdays apparently. I don’t know if it’s worth that to take the tour... but I haven’t done it so who knows. $10/family might be more like it.

But this place really gets an A+! It’s not Disneyland or the natural history museum, so don’t have too high expectations... but for a free museum, this was simply delightful!

FANTASTIC Museum with PLENTY for kids and adults of all ages to see and do!  This was fantastic for my 5 year old and I could have spent way more time there.  The best part is that it is FREE!!!  Technically by donation - but with zero pressure.

Full disclosure, my review of the Dog exhibit that is currently there would be entirely different... more like 2 stars.  I made the awful mistake of spending nearly $20 to do that, when I could have had a free day at the museum with all the other amazing things!  But we did get to see the Endeavor, if tickets for the Dog exhibit, so that was cool.  Oh!  You need to see the Body Works part!  There is a huge woman that is just strange.  The whole thing is a bit outdated - but the retro ness is super charming.  It evoked feelings of the Diet Coke of 1990's EPCOT Center.

For parents with small children:  There are MANY fun zones that are essentially science based play areas, closer to what you'd find at a play place.  So that is super helpful.  The highlight for us was definitely the aquarium section.  That was super cool.  But we really enjoyed all of it.  I can't wait to go back!

Parking is $12 (so it's not exactly a free day) - but totally worth the $12.  Drinks are expensive, so I'll bring my own next time.  We had lunch there and prices were as expected for a place like this and for museum food, my cheeseburger was pretty delicious!

This is for sure a hidden gem in the valley that is a MUST for all parents with children who need a break from the hot summer days!  This is a GIANT pool complete with two large water slides!!!  I have a 3 year old, so he couldn't do the slides, but the best thing about this pool is that it's almost like a beach where all around you walk in.  It's really wonderful.

And get this... it's only $1 for kids and seniors and $3.50 for adults!!!  I mean, come one!!! That's great!  You can pay extra for cabanas and what not, but we got there early and just go a nice shaded area.

Okay... they are strict for rules here, so check their website.  It's easy to get frustrated by that, but really it's all for safety and their safety record is off the charts!  You have to have a 1-to-1 parent/child ratio until the child is 6.  So if you have 2 kids under six, you have to go with a second adult.  They're also strict about about can go on the water slide.  My wife couldn't where her sun protector and I had to rip out those little metal circles they put in swim trunks.

But all that aside... bring a picnic!  Towels!  Chairs!  Maybe even a table and grill!!!  This is a super fun place to go to save you from the hot summer!!!

The admission price is steep for what you’re getting, so I’d splurge for the VIP pass that gets you into this, Ripley’s and the Hollywood Wax Museum for a full day of fun. Full disclosure, I didn’t do that but bought tickets throughout fundraising auction so I was at a meter instead of at an all day parking lot and I honestly could have used more time here! The first floor has some cool exhibits and a lot to read that is lost on younger children (I was with my five year old)... but they have some fun things for those kids to do like how many hits of a drum can you do in a given amount of time.

The second floor has TONS of fun games! Like an arcade but you can play anything as much as you want without extra fees. I would imagine this would be terrible if super busy but it was just fine for us. We didn’t have to wait long.  The basketball game was my favorite just because I could play those all day. They had a cool movie too.

Then back to the bottom is pretty much the end. I wish it were larger but it was fun! I’d be mad if I paid $26 for just this though! Spend the extra 9 or 10 and go to all three museums.
dislikes: Content not suitable for young children

reviews_attraction.text:
First off, you must check out their parent store, "Bearded Lady Vintage" diagonally across the street.  They're an antique shop specializing in the strange, macabre, morbid, etc.  "Bearded Lady's Mystic Museum", also has some antiques, but there is a lot of artwork and newer items.  You can find a lot of fan merchandise for horror films here.  But their claim to fame is the museum in the back.  It's less a museum and more of an art gallery.  I went when they had their Twin Peaks exhibit open, and while it was AMAZING, I felt a bit weird having to pay $5 to go back there.  Especially where I wanted to buy prints that I can't afford in the first place, haha.  But this is a special place, so if that's what is needed to keep them in business, so be it.  The artwork in the museum gets 5+ stars!!!!  Bravo!!!  The store itself isn't too big.

I think whether or not this place is cool depends on if you like their current exhibit.  However, I would for sure check this place out and DON'T MISS their antique store across the street!

This was our third stop on our Santa Paula "Passport 2 History" excursion.  This museum is fantastic as they have a whole room with things for kids to do!  And we're not just talking pressing buttons...  They have a whole store set up where the kids can dress up, go shopping, put food in their carts, bring it to the check out, pay with play money... and more!  There are toys, games, and many workstations where kids can play!

The rest of the museums has large tractors and stuff like that, and they even had a tractor and horse and buggy set up for kids to go on!  You could definitely spend a lot of time here if you let your kid just play.  There's an outdoors area too.

The gift shop was nice, but what I liked best is that they sell authentic, vintage citrus labels!  The staff here was also wonderful and helpful.  As good as some of the other museums we saw that day were... this was our favorite!

PS.  If you go here, you can get into the Ventura County Museum in Ventura free on the same day!  We're so glad we did!

I finally visited The Greek for the first time and had a very nice experience!  I was nervous when I drove in because traffic was so bad and I was way up in lot G and just imagined how chaotic getting out would be... But you know what... getting out was really easy!  I was very surprised.

It was a little wait to get into the venue, but the line moved.  There are plenty of places to eat if you'd like.  It just seemed very relaxed inside.  Not too crazy.  The sound was actually really good... MUCH better the The Hollywood Bowl.  Additionally, there are NO bad seats (that I could see)!  We were toward the very back and "the very back" here is probably half way up at The Bowl... So it feels much smaller than most amphitheater venues.

Parking is $25... so that was a hit... but shame on me for not knowing that.  Now YOU do!  So plan for i or take alternate transport.  Driving in I thought I'd never be coming back... but after my experience and ease getting out... I'd definitely come back here!

This was our second stop on our Santa Paula "Passport 2 History" excursion!  The building is very nice and I believe the art is constantly moving, so really how good it is depends on the current show.

We began in a smaller room where they had art from your children which was very cool.  Also in that room, there was a project where you could have your kids make their own frog out of paper and part of an egg carton.  I really appreciate when places have activities for kids.  In fact, they're opening a whole new building that I believe is going to be centered around children!  Looking forward to seeing that!

The rest of the museum was nice, but there's not too much to it.  We spent less than a half hour here.  But that's fine because you have two other museums in walking distance, so it actually worked out nicely.  On it's own, it's not much to write home about, but I would certainly make this a stop on your Santa Paula day trip!

This is a museum every parents in LA should know about!  It's a car museum that is absolutely free!  Full disclosure, I wish there were more exhibits for kids to do, so really I feel like it's more of a 4 star then 5 star thing to do... BUT, being as big as it is and being FREE, it deserves 5 stars.

Try to plan your visit right for when they open the train in the back.  We missed that.  Additionally, there are free scheduled tours for adults only to see the collection across the street that is supposed to be unbelievable with mechanical instruments and whatnot.  I can't wait to go back and see that!

If you like old school cars... Packards, Fords, Plymouths, Bugatti's, etc... this place is for you!

If you're anywhere near the area, I would make this a part of your road trip!  This is very cool!  It's a short stop but it's very cool.  Bottles and art made of vintage items completely fill the yard!  Very cool!

No restrooms.  I wish there was a bit more information about what we were seeing.  I'd love to know more about the history of the place!  We passed some antique stores on the way I wish we had stopped at.  Next time.

Since there wasn't a restroom and and 5 stars is supposed to be "as good as it gets", I was going to mark this 4 stars... But then I thought about it how this is a free attraction that someone is doing out of the goodness of their heart... so it gets 5 stars!!!

If you're going to Riverside, and you like strange things... you have NO EXCUSE not to go see The World's Largest Paper Cup!  Not that there is a fence, so you can't get super close.  You have to just pull off the side of the road, which is easy to do.  This isn't a roadside attraction that is going to take much time.  There is no gift shop, museum or bathroom.  Just a giant paper cup that was made when this was the now defunct Sweetheart Paper Cup Factory.  So as long as you curve your expectations (and you're in Riverside)... you have to see it!

ps... note that it doesn't have the stripes anymore.

Small yet cute FREE museum with wonderfully charming staff! They have a nice gift shop but the museum section isn’t large. There was cool info about Balboa Island, Shirley Temple and more.  You probably won’t spend more than 15 minutes in the museum.

HOWEVER! I noticed an empty storefront down the street that said: Coming soon: The Balboa Island Historical Museum... so maybe they’re moving soon and will have more room!

I never give FREE museums less than 4 stars, because anything they offer is gravy. Definitely check this out when strolling down the strip!

This is the jail from the Goonies. There are two parts to the museum. One part has cameras and scenes set up that you can film yourself doing a scene from a film. The other “museum” part is literally just the jail cells with some Goonies memorabilia in it.

I was with a 4 year old who couldn’t do the scenes part so the museum literally took about 2 minutes. $6 NOT well spent. Wish we had done the Victorian mansion next door instead.

We didn’t have time to do the hike, but made sure to seek out Pumpkin Rock on the way home to LA from our Riverside Visit. It’s very cool! Better views are at the end of the street, not just where the gps takes you. Additionally, do some research as to the best place to start the hike. That’s easy to find online. Such a cool thing!

If you went through a pinball phase, you’re gonna love this place. It’s basically a building with rows and rows of machines from years gone by. Drop a quarter in the machine of your choice and play away!

I fell in love with a particular old school mechanical game called Drop-a-Card in the mid 70s. I stopped playing by 1980, and I was not fond of the newer games with all the bells and whistles.

So I was very pleasantly surprised when I found a Drop-a-Card machine. I played about 8 games. Very cool!

Aside from your quarters, the place is free. I really recommend you make a donation though. The place itself is pretty plain. Just a building full of machines. But it’s really worth a visit. It’s about an $8 Lyft ride from the south end of the Strip.
dislikes: Newer games with bells and whistles

reviews_attraction.text: If you're looking for a huge park with tons of space, this is the place.  The grass areas are not ideal for football and soccer - more designed for picnics and fishing.  Great place for long walks.  There is a sidewalk that circles the park that will take you to playgrounds, fishing spots, and picnic benches.  It's very easy to find a nice quiet spot to relax.  There are usually plenty of water fowl to feed if that's your thing.  The facilities are somewhat lacking.  The wind can really howl out here, so if you're heading out on a seemingly mild spring day, bring a jacket just in case.

This is an amazing place. There are several trails that wind along the beach and cut across the point, offering a fantastic variety in a relatively small area. Most of it is very easy walking. The views are simply spectacular. You will likely see harbor seals and California sea lions, as well as many sea birds. The tide pools on the south end are lots of fun too. And stop by and talk to the docent at the whalers cabin on the north side above Whaler's Cove. It's very interesting. And support our parks by paying the parking fee instead of hiking in!

Beautiful park with so much to offer.  Two huge softball fields that are big enough for hard ball, tennis courts, a couple of basketball courts (pickup games on some nights during the week) and a huge soccer field with artificial turf.  Picnic areas and playgrounds as well.  Left it at four stars because no dogs are allowed.  I think Carlsbad is the only city where dogs are allowed in restaurants but not in parks.  So if you don't like dogs, bump this up to 5 stars.  However, I do see dogs there, and I've never seen it being enforced.

Nice park for a picnic or small family gathering.  The playground is very nice.  Difficult to find room for many other activities due to the many trees.  Baseball fields appear to be locked up most of the time.  Two basketball courts draw lots of activity, so this park is a good choice if you're looking for a pick-up game.  Be aware, there's a chance you'll encounter some shady characters here - at least that's been my experience.

Pleasant area with a nice walkway. Fairly small - took us about 30 minutes  to walk all the paths. Not a lot of floral variety, but still pretty. The paths are excellent - they obviously put an emphasis on accessibility. Very little color. It was our first time to the college, so we found the parking a bit confusing. Ended up buying a $5 all day pass in lot 5.

Very pleasant. It's like being in the woods without being in the woods. Any age can enjoy this park. Very knowledgeable and helpful staff. Fairly crowded though. Tip: pay for parking at one state park and the pass is good all day at all of them on the same day - and there are several nearby.

Very pleasant! Provides great views north and south. Extremely clean as well. The adjacent beaches are beautiful, with wide swaths of sand. There are many volleyball courts. There is a life guard station at the onset of the  pier. The nearby pier plaza hosts several restaurants and bars.

Beautiful little neighborhood park. Nice playground encircled by a concrete pathway. A little creek runs by it. There is also a basketball court, restrooms, and ample parking. The grass areas are hilly and small - not useful for much more than sunning and tossing a frisbee around.

Classic Sierra Nevada Monolith.  Great views.  If you're not in great shape, con't ruin your day climbing to the top.  The area can get very crowded.  I prefer some of the quieter trails in the surrounding area, but Moro Rock is really quite awesome once you get to the top.

Very nice little park steps from the sand and the beach. Cool little playground, a small basketball court, and an exercise court. This park has its limitations, but it is a perfect fit for the area. Not sure, but much of the facility looks new.

I went here on a warm summer day. There were thunderstorms about to roll in.  It was an amazing place.  Lots of cool trails to explore.  It was pretty interesting, especially for a Californian.  Creepy looking spiders were EVERYWHERE.

This is a very special golf course. It has several extremely interesting holes, and the entire course is very scenic. My only complaint is the watery sand traps.  Otherwise, one of the top courses in the county, and not too pricey!

Very pleasant, colorful area for a stroll. Lots of interesting artisan shops - photography, painting, ceramics, etc. Most of it is pretty pricey. There is also an ice cream shop and a couple of other food stands.

This review is for the nature trail that begins and ends at Fort Caroline.

Nice area for an easy nature walk. Great views at a couple of spots. Huge bald eagle nest at post 22. Great for kids, dogs, or a jog.
There isn't a whole lot to do here, but the views are incredible.  On a clear day, you can see forever.  Well, at least you can see downtown San Diego to the south and the Pacific Ocean to the east.
Nice little museum with lots of historical information on the island.Probably not much of interest for most folks, but still kind of neat to look at the old photos.  Can't beat the price (free!)
This is one of my favorite places in Lancaster.  Great place for a morning or late afternoon walk.  If you're timing is right, there's a good chance you'll see some interesting wildlife.
Cool little dog park.  Also great for walks, as there is a sidewalk circling the park.  Fairly large multipurpose grass area in the middle, and a playground on the west end.
Neat little visitor's center.  Nice little hike out and back along the lagoon.  Basically flat, so it's excellent for children. Some parts need a little cleanup.
This is a fantastic park for a leisurely walk.  Very pretty area.  You can also connect with other trails, including the high over the hill to Doublepeak Park.
Not bad for a local trail. Some trails are pretty steep. Views of chaparral-covered hills and the small lake. Nothing remarkable or especially interesting.
Very pretty park, but it's very hilly. Nice little playground, dog park, and softball fields. Bummer there's no basketball court.
Extremely long pier with great views north and south.  Very peaceful when I was there, as opposed to some of the other piers.
Kind of neat, and there are some knowledgeable folks here. But it’s not breaking into my top 500 things to do in Los Angeles.

We went to Santa Cruz Island of Channel Islands National Park on this Christmas long weekend. We took Island Packer to get there, we saw a lot of dophins on the way to island, it's awesome! And after getting out of boat, we backpack walked 0.5 mile to Scorpion Campground. This island is an idea place for activities such as camping, hiking, Kayaking, Snorkeling, wildflower and wildlife viewing. We enjoyed it so much! To the best experience the island, camp two or three days will be wonderful, but it can be done in a day trip, I highly recommend 5 miles round-trip to Cavern Point Loop, North Pluff Trail and Potato Harbor Overlook.

We hiked up Red Rock Canyon Trail from Foothill Ranch, the most part of trail is flat and a kind of boring, but the last 0.6 mile  becomes interesting, at the end you will see light color Red Rock Canyon, if you  can manage to climb up to the canyon, the view is quite nice, especially if the weather is in an idea condition, the sky is clear and has clouds flow by or at the time of sunset, the canyon would be turned into bright colors.

It's one of the biggest state park in the country. We camped in Tamarisk Grove Campground, stayed in two cabin. Cactus Loop Trail and Kanyen Overlook Loop Trail are near by this Campinground and are worth to check out. And we explored the west part of the park to see wildflowers as we were short in time, I really like sculptures in the Christmas Circle area, and definitely will go to this park again to explore another areas.

It's located in Whittier right behind Rose Hill, the hiking area is called Puente Hill Habitat Preserve, there are many trails over there, but most of them are steep which makes a good workout ground, so it's not suit for small children, and there is completely no shade, need prevent harm from the sun and bring plenty of water, the best time to visit this park should be spring.

This is my second time hiked up to the peak, it's about 6 miles round-trip with 1300 feets elevation gain, very easy to walk up and down. This time again was cloudy and fogy, i couldn't see surrounding high peaks, it's really pretty.

It's a very popular hiking destination, from there hikers take a rest and have some snacks for fueling them up, for avid and fit hikers they choose one of the multiple trails to explore the surrounding peaks.

It has similar landscapes comparing with Joshua Tree NP and Death Valley NP, but The Lava Tube in the preserve non of national parks mentioned above has it. The best time to visit it is Winter and Spring.

We went there at the middle of November for a short walk on our way to Joshua Tree NP, I saw some trees and most vegetations were withered, and none of birds, definitely it's not right season to visit.
It's a well known landmark near south shore of Salton Sea, created it with Christianity's theme by Leonardo who died at 2011 at age of 82. It is a long drive from LA area, but it's worthy!
There is a hike from the park to misson peak with steep climbing, but no shades at all, the best time to visit the park should be spring and winter.
It's a newest museum in downtown LA, adjacent to wall desney concern hall, exhibits contemporary art, and it's very popular since it's opening.
Only here you can the oldest trees in the world, the Bristlecone Pine trees, it's really worth a visit when you pass by the town of Big Pine.
It is a really cool place to escape the heat from the desert floor of Palm Springs area, and an idea park to all kind of outdoor activities.
It's on the west side of Big Bear Lake, a very easy hike on the wooden deck along the lake, not many birds there when I visited this place.
It's a huge park with hiking trails and playgrounds, especially the Angeles Point there where you can enjoy sunset of downtown LA.
This park is know for camping and just an half mile from lake Hemet, the area near by is burnt to the ground by recent Craston 🔥.
It's a very nice and secluded little high mountain lake, just outside of the town Idyllwild. It is worth a visit and take a walk.
It is fun to hike there, especially in ladder canyon trail where you need to climb multiple ladders, children really like here.
We walked down the site on this memorial day, it's pleasant to see the creek and spring, and it's also a good fishing spot.
It's not worthy of visiting when you need to drive a long way to get there, unless you have a chance to see air craft.
A very nice museum with a wide range of European art from 14th century to 20th century, and with a sculpture garden.
I like this place so much as it is cool when  I go there in a hot day, and there also has so many things to do.
If you walk in a couple miles further, you would see a multiple beautiful alpine Lakes, I highly recommend it.
It's also located at Pelican Cove Park with a trail access to Terrence Resort, shor and easy with senic view.
I like this place as there are cool rocks formation and they are unique in the entire San Gabriel Mountain.

This winery has a large tasting room on the main floor of an old restored farmhouse. Sarah was busy with other visitors but took the time to welcome us and get us started. We ended up buying case of the Farmhouse Red which is a blend. Here both reds and whites were finely crafted. We joined the wine club. Prices are very reasonable for the quality of wine you get. They sell olive oil and reserve brandy as well.

This is wonderful place for plant lovers, hikers, dog owners, and gardeners. Miles of trails in secluded plant and tree groves. Dahlia garden is an explosion of color. Huge blooms in several varieties. The fern trail features shady paths lined with thyme grass rocks and ferns framing bubbling creek. Many wooden bridges provide intimate settings for supreme photo ops.

We enjoyed a fine tour of the best highlights and places of interest within the Capitol building. Our guide was knowledgeable, witty, and personable. I liked best the views of the dome and the restored original offices of the governor and secretary of state. Historic murals decorate the lower level. Paintings of past governors are on display on second level.

I liked the facility a lot it's nice and large inside. They offer meatballs on the weekends that would pair well with their red varietals. Service was good here with our lady offering us some library wines and giving notes about the special characteristics. They have lovely outdoor seating under large umbrellas for enjoying the vast view of the valley.

The museum has a good history of the lighthouse with many original photos. It was remodeled about 12 years old and looks great. We climbed all 116 steps to the very top of the lighthouse. What a fabulous view of the ocean land and mountains! It cost $8 per person. The Point Arena grounds are accessible from Highway 1 along 2 mile one lane access road.

This is where the bats live and play. Under the bridge there is a painting of a huge bat. They replaced the trail path under the north side of bridge with metal walkway. You can hang out on the turnout above the water and watch the lake traffic ok including kayaks and paddleboarding. Hike and bike trail is simply grand and convenient.

Now called Lady Bird Lake, this body of water is actually a river running straight through Austin dividing it into halves. Bats congregate under the Congress street bridge and give off pungent smell as one walks or runs on the Hike and Bike trail which lines the lake on both sides. This urban oasis is truly peaceful and amazing.

I've been to the state Capitol building several times. Each visit i learn or see something new. Like the African American sculpture on front lawn. Much history here and it is displayed with many paintings and sculptures. Rotunda can be viewed from 5 different floors. Both house chambers are accessible. Best to take guided tour!

Large permanent collection occupies most the gallery space. Outdoor sculptures decorate the grounds. Pleasant setting for the outdoor Garden Cafe. Diverse shopping in the museum store. Loved the complete Impressionist paintings including Van Gogh works. Would have enjoyed the artworks more if not for the protective glass!

They have outdoor seating at tables with large umbrellas. Wonderful view of the valley below. Landscaping and plants add drama to the experience. Musician was playing some songs. One has to go to the bar to pick up order. Wine was satisfactory. People were pushing the sangria drinks, good for a hot day.

Beautiful gardens especially the Japanese section which features a lovely koi pond and meandering path through bamboo and waterfall. Another area contains 180 log cabin inhabited by Swedish settlers. Herb and flower garden with lots of shade and trails. Great place to relax learn and get your steps in!

The only bad thing is they charge up front for tasting in amount of $10. Waived if you join wine club of which there are 4 different levels. The wine is quite good. I liked the 2016 Zinfandel and the GPS blend the best. Prices are moderate. Most grapes estate grown. Staff very helpful and friendly.

This is another of the great state parks. Hiking trails lead through huge redwood forest. The Navarro River didn't have a lot of water but it provided nice background with very relaxing ambience. Trial map was a little hard to match to the signs and forks on trails. Signage along trails helps much.

Many shops and restaurants to while away your time. Love the old brick facades and cobblestone streets. There are railroad cars and sculptures throughout the walkways. Street performers perform well without inundating the area. Wine tasting and olive oil tasting venues offer something different.

Server was new and had trouble opening wine bottle. She couldn't answer questions about the wine. Tasting fee is $10 but waived with purchase. Facility is beautiful. Designer bathrooms is separate structure. Tasting room is new and landscaping very tasteful with water wise plants.

I liked the wines especially the library ones with the gold label. This is a longstanding winery that produces a lot of wine for local chains. My favorite is the 2016 Hilltop Cab which is silky with lovely color and beautiful structure. Also good is their 2015 Petite Syrah.

Tons of people go here in summer on weekends. Very family friendly many kids. Water is fairly clean and one can swim laps early in morning. Beware parking is often full even the pay lots. Basketball courts attract rough sort. Runners can run on nearby beach trail.

The view of ocean from rocky outcroppings is fantastic. Hike along the perimeter and all the way up to Glass Beach on other end of Fort Bragg. Good place to bring your dog or to sit in your car and eat lunch. Whale watching is possible during season.

Great place to go running on the paved trail. Many volleyball courts available and they are all set up with nets and lines in place. Plenty of restrooms there at main entrance at Newland. Only bad thing is parking is only all day and costs $15!

Server was knowledgeable but not friendly. It was late in day so maybe he was getting ready to close up. Wines were good, not great, especially for the price. The tasting rooms and facilities had outdoorsy rustic charm, that was the best part.

They offer large selection of both red and white wines. Prices are reasonable and no tasting fee. Different wine club options. Josh our server was friendly and informative. Liked the petite syrah best. Their Zins are popular and robust.

This park in central downtown has a beautiful fountain in middle. No water on this early September evening. Plenty of benches. Trees are abundant. Not too mmay vagrants that I could discern. They have outdoor concerts in the summers.
Many cactus and succulents plus pretty rose garden with fountain. Mansion offers historical perspective. Nice hiking trails.  This is half day visit at most.
Many diverse artists reflecting all types of mediums. The entertainment is fun and catchy. Auction went on too long but it was still quite interesting.
The lady who served me gave me numerous pours and allowed me exchange one of the wines on my shipment that I was picking up

I saw pictures of this cathedral and it didn’t not seem impressive or visually appealing but visiting in person changed my perspective. This cathedral is absolutely massive. The layout is very untraditional with very modern lines and almost and industrial feeling yet very peaceful. The little chapels contain a variety of treasures and artwork. I think my favorite aspect of this cathedral are the murals lining he nave with the plethora of saints facing the alter. This is a place you definitely want to experience for yourself.

Really cool landform surrounded by a wild and beautiful coastline. My recommendation is to pay attention to the tide schedule we went during low tide and started our return when high tide was approaching and it could make the hike very difficult and in some parts impassable. Take lots of water.

This visitors center was small and I was expecting something with more exhibits and information. It’s a very basic visitors center where you can get maps and other brochures for attractions around the park. The rangers seemed disorganized and couldn’t answer basic questions about hikes.

The Denver Art Museum is a wonderful museum with multiple floors filled with many different genres of artwork. We spent several hours here and it's a wonderful place that I highly recommend anyone visit if in Denver. The cafe and gift shop are really nice as well.

Lovely and unique place. I prefer to come in the afternoons because during the light of the day the sands can be blinding. The views are so beautiful here but be careful to not lose your way, the sands can be very tricky to navigate.

This casino is small but has several sections of slot machines and a nice little restaurant with really good prices. I like coming here because it is non-smoking. The only downside is that there are no table games.
This is a great center to lean about the rich traditions of the Hispano people of The United States. There are museums, murals, a performing arts center and a restaurant. It's a great place.
Union Square is a nice park in the city. I especially love the atmosphere around Christmastime when there is an ice skating rink. Lots of shopping opportunities around.
This park is kinda overshadowed by the interstate and all of uptown but it's actually very quiet. There is a playground, lots of hills and views of the mountains.
I've only been on this trail to hike to Nambé Falls and it's an absolutely beautiful high mountain trail. There are aspen groves, streams, and great views.
This monument is famous and beautiful and with seeing up close. There are several information stands with history and detail about the Statue.
This is a beautiful cathedral with a wonderful fusion of European and New Mexican elements. Stay for a Sunday mass when they play the organ.
Incredible nature refuge. It's best in the fall and spring when it is full of different types of animals but it's beautiful all year round.
This is probably one of my favorite parks in the city. It's full of artwork and surrounded by beautiful buildings. Lovely in every season.
The caldera is such a varied place with so many views and trails. Do your research and you'll be amazed at what this park has to offer.
In my opinion this is the prettiest church in San Francisco. It's massive with a beautiful interior and a peaceful mystic atmosphere
Grace Cathedral is an imposing gothic cathedral. The inside isn't much to look at it's quite dark and cold but well worth a visit.
What an experience. Don't waste your time reading reviews just go, explore, and enjoy. I loved this place I can't wait to go back.
This is a beautiful church. Despite the doors being open, people coming in and out it's an incredibly peaceful place.
One of the oldest churches in the United States. Beautiful architecture and art in the center of the old pueblo.
For being a smaller city the Albuquerque Museum of art and history has a good collection and it is well curated.
Great place to take in the views and look at the varied geographic landscape. It can get very hot in the summer.
These gardens are a welcome bit of nature in the center of the city. There are impressive water features here.
This is a small park alongside the coast. It has wonderful views of the ocean and has some very unique trees.
I love coming to this hot spring. It's easily accessible, has a great view, and the waters are so nice.

It's a neat place to go and climb around on the rocks and get some outdoor time, but it's pretty heavily used. It's still beautiful I suppose, but everything has been covered with about 300 layers of paint from all the graffiti and there's certainly no shortage of broken glass. I don't know. I guess that's just what you do when there's rocks. You throw beer bottles at them. Anyways, yeah it's nice but it's certainly seen it's fair share of abuse over the decades, which is really sad.

It was OK. Small, super close to "downtown" but to walk there is sort of taking your life in to your own hands on account of the road and traffic, so I can't exactly call this a feature. It was quiet when we went, but it was also dead winter and it snowed, and there were only two other groups. There were plenty of good sites for tent camping, and a few RV spots too. The ranger was a nice guy and very helpful. Not sure we'd go again, but it's an option for sure.

This is a nice, clean park with a small but good playground and an expansive lawn with shady trees at the edges. We spent hours there with the kids, had a picnic on the grass, and so on. It's a bit creepy being so close to the refinery, but I guess everything around here is technically close. There was a good prevailing breeze and the weather was quite pleasant. We'd go again.

A great escape from the big city if anything. Fresh air, good views of LA and the surroundings, and also a chance to see history up close, not to mention where science is still being conducted. The tours, which run on the weekends I think, are long but thorough, and give you access to the insides of the telescopes, which is way cooler than standing around outside.

Travel town is OK - The price is right. The train is cute and decent to ride, though the Griffith park train is better (the one by the ponies) and the Live Steamer trains next door are SUPER AMAZING comparatively, but still, not bad. Also, they have full size trains you can check out too, and apparently, you can have birthday parties inside some of them.
dislikes: Less impressive compared to nearby attractions

reviews_attraction.text: Great park in Palm Desert. We stopped by to use the EV fast chargers. Could use a few more of those, plus the park really could use some food vendors too. We did go on a week day, so maybe there's a tamale lady there on weekends, I can say. The playground is nice and the pond is full of things for kids to look at.

Yeah dodger stadium is just okay. I don't really know if the experience of going to a ball game is for me. I love baseball, don't get me wrong but there's nothing sacred or religious about sitting 40 rows back and not being able to see anything and paying a million dollars for a beer and 2 million for parking.

Nice walk, but the water is contaminated with sewage and runoff, and last time we went there was a dead rat being eaten by the crayfish. Which I suppose were just doing their job. But don't touch the water for any reason. Do visit the Trails Cafe.

The park is fine. It's big and it sees a lot of use. It's quite loud and close to the road but it's not a bad park I suppose. I just don't feel as though I stumbled across some gem after having come here for the first time.
I'm only an eager spectator. Lots of fun to watch people tear it up with truly world-class skating. Like wildlife, you should respect these dudes from a safe distance, which is BEHIND THE RAIL.
A few interesting artifacts outside, and a whole lot of fascinating history inside crammed in to a tiny space. The woman who was working that day was very knowledgeable and pleasant.
Been going all my life. It's rare that a thing is as fun when you have kids as it was when YOU were a kid. Lots of amazing family moments at this park. I'll go every year if I can.
Awesome for kids, and the distance from the city keeps the idiot factor low. Nice tide pools, neat caves, and manageable waves. Also, the electric car charging is fantastic.
It's a fine park, good for letting the kids ride bikes. Obviously the fun police shut down the playground, but maybe once my kids are too big they'll open it back up.
So disgusting yet so amazing! First time here, it's like another planet.... With beaches made of barnicles​ and bleached fish skeletons! I want to explore more.
Nice park for kids and a picnic, although there was some freakshow of a dude training his off-leash German Shepherd to attack about 50 feet from the playground.
I really enjoy this park because it's a bit wild and unmanicured, not to mention absolutely enormous. We enjoy evening walks there with the kids.
It's a beautiful space and worth a peek if you're passing by and it's open. I attended a wedding there and it easily accommodated a huge group.
A freaking water park in the desert, fun and cheap too! Yeah they might be draining the aquifers, but it's a better use than growing grass.
A gem of a park and so close! Views are AMAZING. Went up there on Christmas Eve day, right after a rain. Could see for a hundred miles!
This is a lovely park with plenty to see and do. The playground is big and friendly to kids of all sizes, and it's well kept and clean.
It's going to be awesome when the trees grow up, but now it's really lacking shade. Also a proper playground would be good.
Good place to watch the sun set, to BBQ, to play in the water a little at the tiny beach, and apparently, to brown bag.
It's a good playground and a nasty little algae filled lake where you can, you know, look at the ducks and stuff.
Yeah it's a fine beach, and the town is "cute" but the campground is bleak and dismissal, and frankly, nasty.

This is a small local Seaport Museum with a big heart and great, caring people running it.  They have many objects that once were commonplace, and are still fascinating.  Like the lenses from lighthouses, charts and maps, nautical instruments, information on marine and terrestrial wildlife.  We attended a lecture on “Celestial Navigation” which was entertaining as well as informative.  There were refreshments including a fruit platter, cheese and meat board, cookies and baked goods, wine and soda – all well worth the admission even before the value of the lecture.  We enjoyed the experience so much, we joined the museum and plan to return for more lectures.

This tour would have been better maybe if i were not the only person on the tour.  The historical store fixtures are vary interesting.  When I tour places like this, I think about what will be left in 200 years of today's special places.  Who thought to keep all the records?  The notes for an order from Martha Washington?  The cabinets still stocked with herbs and the tools of the trade?  It really is quite interesting.

This very remote National Park is 70 miles off Key West.  It has great birding, and a lot of history.  It is the largest and strongest fort the United States built.  Is it worth the 2-1/2 hour ferry ride to get there and then to get back, maybe. [yes, you can take a float plane or your own boat].  I enjoyed the trip and seeing the place, but will probably make the trip again.

This large park has a driving tour and a walking tour - both with informative audio tours via cell phone or mp3. The visitor center has a short video explaining the history of the park and the battles that happened here. There's also information on how this battle worked into the rest of the American Revolutionary War.

This beach varies with the season, rocky in the winter, but sandy in the spring, summer, and fall,  Some of the best surfing on the east coast.  During the season, dog are allowed on the beach before 10 am and after 6 pm.  Off-season there are no restrictions - check the signs for exact dates.

This is an excellent personal space. First this year history of the building and the architecture. Second the public use for art shows and exhibitions. And third the theater Productions which has a lecture series, full theatrical presentations, and other exciting events.

Large safe comfortable catamaran ferry to Dry Tortugas.  Breakfast buffet and lunch buffet are not special, but are plentiful and satisfactory.  There is no getting around the length of time on the boat, but everything is done to make the trip pleasant and comfortable.

Beautiful art in the many mediums of Arizona native DeGrazia. Be sure to see the film that explains his concept and design of the studio. Many of the special touches and meaningful symbolism you probably did not notice, but DeGrazia thought of everything.

Always enjoy visiting any of the theaters here The VIVIAN BEAUMONT THEATER.  A thrust stage, with good sight lines and wide seats with almost enough leg room.  I have seen shows from the balcony and from the orchestra section - all have a great view.

We've been to the gardens in both daylight and evening events.  This time we went for the Las Noches de Las Luminarias.  The illuminated art was very interesting, and the numerous musical presentations added to the festive atmosphere.

This is a great old theater.  The seats are uncomfortable, the show we saw [James Taylor] had bad sound [was it house sound or JT's?? - don't know].  But if the show you want to see is there, you might not have another venue choice.

Good museum and visitors' center for Saguaro National Park EAST.  This NP is special because it has an EAST and a WEST location on separate sides of Tucson.  Both have great trails and scenery.  EAST is best for sunset vistas.

Fun historic area of Fort Worth. Twice-daily Longhorn cattle drives help to explain the historical significance of the area. Great restaurants, souvenir shopping and Western Wear shopping proliferate.
This fun Ferris wheel experience moves at such a speed is not to be noticeable. The large cars are not overcrowded and offer an excellent view of the city and surrounding areas.
This is a great year round hike about the reservoir. With a must-visit at McLoone's Boathouse. Near Turtle Back Zoo this park is conveniently located and has plenty of parking
This is the heart of old New Orleans.  Almost everything worthwhile is walking distance.  Be sure to visit Jackson Square, the Market, and get over to Frenchmen Street.
Newly renovated this historic park maintains the feel of the village. Hawks, squirrels, pigeons, rats.  All the wildlife and local color you could want in a city park.
This fun park has a carousel, fountain to taste the local mineral water, and benches where we were able to have a picnic near the pond and enjoy watching the ducks
Great park with the iconic globe from the worlds fair.  open spaces, weekly NYRR run, shade and sunny places abound... assuming the sun is out!
Good starting point to see the Cherry Blossoms. Parking lot fills up fast in Cherry Blossom season - cannot speak to rest of the year.
Visited this park for the Adirondack Food and Wine Festival,   the park worked well, there was plenty of parking and clean restrooms.
Nice peaceful gardens. Landscape typical of the area with hills and walks up and down.  Be sure to see the butterfly/ flower garden.
This is a great community park with a dog run, a playground, a small gazebo, and a farmers market two days a week in the summer.
We only did the aquarium, it was well organised and very informative.  I look forward to the completion of the new exhibits.
This quiet park and harbor is perfect for relaxing and enjoying the beach, the water, and nature: away from the 'tourist'

What a beautifully maintained garden.  from cacti to palm trees this place has a plethora of foliage from around the globe. They do a splendid job of presenting their collection and labeling just about every species they have. Excellent knowledgeable staff. Their plans to expand and add more to the grounds looks awesome as well! I hope they keep "growing" and bringing in more exotics throughout the years. Great place to bring anyone, shoot i'd come here on my lunch breaks if I could. My father came here as a child and to see where it's at today is breathtaking... I hope to experience the same nostalgia someday! Keep growing!

Awesome fam owned winery 🍷 and one of San Diego's largest! About to double in size to over 300 acres of 🍇 🍇 🍇! Beautifully tucked away on the canyonside just outside Temecula, this picturesque 🖼 place would be great for events and big groups... But also has a nice welcoming family friendly, won't you be my neighbor, feel. Lots of outdoor games and beautiful grounds to walk around and explore. Fantastic service and tasty wine 🍷cheers 🥂.BE RESPONSABLE D R I V E S A F E

Joshua tree national park (its a type of Yucca) is a fantastic preserve of some beautifully different desert scapes.  Soft sands with Joshua trees and other desert life to the giant rock and Boulder formations, miles and miles of cycling routs, hiking trails, camping sites, this place has it all. Beautiful lookouts over the Coachella Valley. Rangers are knowledgeable and always helpful. Surrounding towns are "cute & trendy" the heart of California deserts is here.

Never disappoints! No matter what time of year I visit this area it's always beautiful. I love how much it changes through the seasons. LNT pack in what you pack out. Pretty easy to follow and find trails make sure you download your offline maps! Def going to plan a camping trip here. I've hiked all throughout this area and always see something new or different. Enjoy and be with nature, preserve her, share her, explore all she has to offer. 🏕 🌞🌝🌟🏔️⛰️🏜️🏞️✌️ 💚 🤙

This is NOT a park it should be called a preserve if that. It sits next to waste management, police and fire facilities, as well as other industrial 🏭 facilities. There is a bike path that follows the fence line keeping you from all the industrial parts, you barley see any wet land and there is LOTS of trash throughout the park. Saw some natural boar 🐗 and egret 🐦. The pretty view I posted is found at the end of the bike path on a dilapidated lookout platform.

Great state park 🏞 overall. CA state parks are some of the country's best and the rangers are of another class. Friendly, informative, and always eager to help. Stop into the center to get all the info for the surrounding area, any of the rangers will help ya out. HAVE PATIENCE there are a ton of people this time of year respect it don't neglect it! Have fun, enjoy nature, and stop to smell the roses 🌸 💐 🌹 🌺🌻🌼🏵️💮🐝🐞🐛🦋🐜

Great stop for anyone in the valley to get any and all information about death valley, the lowest point on earth, to Mount Whitney, the highest point in the contiguous (say that 5x fast) United States of America 🇺🇸! Has lots of dioramas, maps, info, gear, and a gift shop. Rangers are there to give you pointers and local info. Located in a beautiful part of the valley with well kept grounds and a CLEAN RESTROOM!

Beautiful easy spot to view the Coachella Valley from. Easy to drive up to with friends, family, & or lovers. Great photo op spot. Sad how careless humans are, throwing rubbish and junk out as if nature was their trash can 🚮 ♻ the amount of rubbish is distracting from the beautiful views. Respect it don't neglect it. Take care of mother nature and she'll take card of you. ✌️ 💚 🤙 🌎

Pretty Rad beach not too crowded, never not busy. Great beach vibes and lots of good lookin people 👙 🕶️. Plenty of lifeguards on duty patrolling the grounds. Be sure to get there early for parking. Peeps the dunes from satélite 🛰 view 🧝‍♂️. Don't forget the sunscreen and stop in the hotel del for some 🍦 or a 🍹. 🧒 friendly 🐶 approved.

Great little pit stop on the way out of Big Bear. I stopped because the weather on the mountain tops made for some pretty spectacular views. There's picnic tables: perfect for a quick sack lunch or snack with good ol mother nature. Well maintained and in such a beautiful spot. Would like to visit when the center is open someday.

Perfect beach 🏖 spot for your day @ the beach! Lifeguard tower right at the bottom of the stairs plenty of sand, sun, ocean and fresh air. Nice shallow waters for a good bit so it's perfect for little ones, skim boarding, boogie boarding, and surfing. Make sure to pack out what you bring with you! DON'T BE A LITTER BUG!

This place is the bees knees. They bring some pretty spectacular exhibits here. I've never been disappointed in the 6+ years I've been visiting the museum. Awesome curators, knowledgeable, friendly and helpful staff throughout. A great museum store. Oh so much more. Def check this place out if you wanna get an art fix!

This was a surREAL EXPERIENCE. Fantastic  collection of Dali and Magritte. Knowledgeable staff who could assist with just about any question on the exhibits thrown at them. It's a very busy museum so plan accordingly (I'd add about an hr to your time) They have self-guided and guided tours. Nice café and gift shop.

Good easy hike. Clean trail pretty decently maintained. Take water! Take water! Take water! Nice views. Quick loop or out n back with miles of other trails to hit if you have time. Be courteous and take out what you bring in. Better yet pick up at least one piece of trash on your way down! #hikenaked #lovelast

Beautiful hiking & mountain biking spot. Miles and miles of well maintained trails through lots of different altitude specific foliage. Canyons, water features, and wildlife oh my! Downside is the lack of respect by humans leaving rubbish and junk all along the way. Pack out what you bring in how hard is it?!

Beautiful light hiking area with sweeping views of the surrounding cliffs. Great place to catch the sunrise or sunset 🌇 no such thing as a bad view here. Make sure you pack out what you bring in!!! LEAVE NO TRACE! RESPECT MOTHER NATURE FOR ALL TO ENJOY PLEASE!

Beautiful lil walking, jogging, biking bridge with some pretty views. Make sure you LEAVE NO TRACE, found lots of trash around this beautiful historic landmark. Wear a mask when in public too please 😷 Keep San Diego clean, healthy, & safe for all to enjoy

Great park overall. Fantastic trails, well marked, maintained and clean! Best part is its pretty close to anyone's backyard in the San Diego area! make sure to download the trail maps from their website. Have fun, be safe, respect nature, and hydrate!

The building itself is 5/5 but the museum seems to have a lot of wasted space inside... minimalism is wonderful if you know what belongs and doesn't but the flow seems too empty here. They sure did stock the shop with things to purchase though.

Great spot and lookout. Quite popular, almost the whole time I was in the area there were visitors around. Unfortunately with that many people there's a lot of litter... Pack out what you bring in people. It's not that hard.

Great one stop shop for any of your on the road travel needs. Fully loaded with snacks, "food" , and drinks... More choices than you could ever get through in a lifetime. Some of the best prices around too!
Great Little park for a nice day at the beach. Playground area for the kids (and big kids 😉) lots of space for a picnic and there are a few charcoal grills around too. Come on down n check it out!
Beautiful park in the heart of San Diego shore line. Great little hikes🏃‍♂️ , biking 🚵‍♂️, running 🏃 paths beach 🏖, surf 🏄‍♂️,and above all natural beauty. Must see for anyone in San Diego. 🌅 🌇
Great community park with lots of activities always going on! Handball, dancing, skateboarding, playground, park workout equipment, picnic area, bring family and friends and enjoy the space!
Great spot for prepping for your hiking adventure. Double check your water and headlamps!make sure to bring SUNSCREEN. LNT and maybe pick up a piece of trash on your way out!

Who hangs out on the Juanita Cooke Greenbelt Trail? Horses, Humans, Mosquitos and Bikes perhaps...

Mountain bikers, runners, hikers and walkers will find a soft, dirt trail underneath tall eucalyptus trees accesible from courthouse on the South side. On the North side, trail can be accessed across the street from Laguna Lake Park. Markers are on wooden posts and trail is bordered with succulent and vegetable private/public gardens. For thrills take Mountain bike trail on left---from courthouse--or right when starting from Laguna Lake.

This is a fun beginner/intermediate trail populated with friendly hikers and after the 1.75-mile marker you will find a fountain and a water bowl for thirsty mammals (see photos). Saw four Horses today and 3 well-behaved riders. Do take notice of the new water wise landscaping and horse/person crosswalk at Bastanchury Road (great feature).

At the mile marker you can opt to go left (from south) or right from north for the shady section of this trail that ends on Euclid Street for a nice 3-mile route. Or you can continue straight under the bridge to Laguna Lake. There are some mosquitos, so deet based spray; hat and sunscreen are always good items to carry in. Juanita Cooke is a scenic trail with peek-a-book views of private estates surrounding trail and has a nice wooden bench at the fork in the trail. This is a favorite place to frequent with groups, family and friends. Great in the spring and summer.
likes: Suitable for groups, family, and friends

reviews_attraction.text:
Trees 🌲 gone.
Initial tour with Mr. Lin and secondary with the delightful Cecilia Lombardi and third with Tony C. Thanks for the hospitality, private tour and answering my many questions. Hi to Michelle! Lovely trees.

1917 La Casa Nueva
Architects: Walker & Eisen
Builder: Sylvester J. Cook
Style: Spanish Revival
Windows by Wallis
Tile by Pedro Sanchez
Blessed by Reverend Cantwell 1923

1870 Workman House
Architect Ezra F. Kysor
Initial home built by William Workman.

F. 1850's
El Campo Santo
One of the finest kept monuments to honor the Workman/Temple families. Notice the detail on the rod iron for the inner cemetery for family. Craftsmanship on the Grecian Mausoleum is superb.

Director of this Museum is Author/Historian/Cal State Fullerton graduate Paul R. Spitzzeri who is an Award of Merit book winner.  The arbor of lovely trees is gone and I am thankful for the stroll, shade and beauty they provided many for decades. Grateful.

Small, green, shady and an overall pleasant park just across from Ladera Palma Elementary School. Terraced cement steps lead you up to the top and give a delightful vista of the valley below. Parking spaces allow for parallel parking right at curb and come in handy for offloading bikes, chairs or even little/big furry dogs.

Large Birch, Jacaranda trees and some pretty Mexican fan palms grow here. They appear to be older than fifty (50) years old. At the lower play area in the south is a play area for grade school children and a tree is in the center for shaded adventure with family and continued exploration in the sand box.

Drinking fountains are located adjacent to the restrooms for cool drinks post bike riding, picnicking or just walking around this park just across Grass here is still beautiful and green. Loma Norte is improving as the school year approaches. This little park is maintained well by the City of La Habra.

RIP...update
Superb Neighborhood Park with baseball fields of postcard quality. Baseball is the game often played here and manicured baseball diamonds prepare one for larger leagues, teams and stadiums. This park is adjacent to Ladera Palma Elementary School.

Enjoyed time watching my little nephews playing baseball, practicing and their proud smiling parents always in the stands. Local caretakers---who have re-landscaped---made many improvements to this park. Great resource for those wanting to enjoy and engage with nature.

In the spring, Jacaranda trees blossom full of purple flowers and provided shade on balmy summer afternoons. Families in Brea/La Habra have watched children grow up and go on to play in the Major leagues. Estelli Park is a ideal place to catch a game, talk a walk or pitch a fastball.

Powder Canyon is a trail that proves challenging or mellow. Straight shot from horse corral to horse stable is approximately 5 miles. Challenging is the black walnut trail  (BWT) from the start is difficult.

The BWT ascends quickly and rewards with views. You can do this trail on a mountain bike as well. Downhill leads to the Powder Canyon Trail. If grueling long and drawn out is preferred try Purple Sage Trail (PST) for a challenge. New seeds in are the landscape is full of butterflies.

Mid way through at crossroads veer left (West) and start the climb, its long with difficult ascents and without hydration---good luck.  At the top, views are 180 degree eye vistas with cool wind and wavy ocean. Hydrate, bring sunscreen and sanitary wipes help to remote the dust.

Green, clean and sounds of a flowing creek overcome the unsuspecting 4 to 100 year old visitor. The play place has sandy goodness where many kid’s size 13 shoes find safety and abrasion in the shade of the towering pine trees.

Notice the views of Mammoth Mountain and Sherwin Range from the park. Desire to run or ride your bike? If yes then this is the perfect push off point for accessing the Mammoth Trail System. Try the town loop for 7.3 miles.

Restrooms are stocked and cleaned regularly and this park has natural granite boulders, monument and a under street tunnel to keep you rolling on your bike, in motion in your Newton’s or just safe from rain, wind or wonderful snow. Delightful!

Review in progress...
Park and the lake are "for ALA members/guests" only. Notice electronic entry system in place for foot and vehicular traffic and ALA does patrol its holdings---they are treasures. Safe/naturally kept area with restrooms.

Park borders Green Valley Lake and the posh Lake Arrowhead Country Club offering views of the luscious greens (nutured by reclaimed water thanks LACSD). Pristine, clean and gated at the time of my visit.

Dogs allowed to play and doggie bags are provided to keep all sanitary. Fishing allowed---with license. Children can play on jungle gym here. Ducks, geese and many varieties of birds spotted and large lake Koi.

This is the only grove of "Red Giants" in Orange County and its located in the city of Brea. Trail is capricious so stay on the dirt while keeping a watchful eye for snakes.

Mountain bikers frequent this trail along with joggers so be alert. Trail is flat and restrooms are nearby. You will need to pay for parking and this includes use of playground, lake, access to "wild animals" eyed some geese and squirrels.

Lovely trails here and the temperture is crisp in the redwood grove (bring a light jacket). Geese looked healthly---as they were waddling to the lake. Well kept and observed Park Ranger on property. Visit!

.

Spacious parking is all around, just to the left past the traffic circle and Irvine is safe as one can get. Restrooms are clean. Baseball diamonds, soccer fields and a full basketball courts are highlights of this park.

Many hiking trails originate from this  QHC park. Easiest is the loop on the west side, in the middle (hiking lite) is the Shady Canyon Trail (gravel trail) and there is paved bike path taking you to Turtle rock.

For a decent workout and +5 miler with rolling hills, critters, and no bathrooms for miles, try the Quail Trail with a significant ascent and a view of estates and the Newport Beach marina.
dislikes: Lack of bathrooms on longer trails

reviews_attraction.text:
This is a quaint little park with baseball fields and located adjacent to City Hall. During the summer they host "Movie Nights" on a screen. Bring a blanket, picnic basket and enjoy a fun family evening.

Trees are large enough to offer shade and playground equipment is well maintained. This is also the home to Little League and the baseball diamond was in top condition like the dugouts, bleachers and restroom facilities.

Parking is ample and within walking distance to the playground. Grass (at time of my observation) was green and the park was welcoming. Richardson Park offers a delightful contrast to the desert.

Delightful park for the discerning residents in love with the rural nature  of La Habra Heights.LHH is a sanctuary for horses, birds, orchards and quiet commissioned estates with views to the Isthmus of Catalina Island.

A horse corral is provided and this is a unique feature in addition to spaces for horse trailer parking. A play area for children is provided (older and younger children) and a community center.

Personally walked along the  sloping streets and observed custom view estates, grasslands, tree groves, riding trails, and panoramic views in a fiscally healthy city. Thank you for allowing me to observe.

Spacious parking is on the east side (north of soccer fields). Restrooms are clean. Shady Canyon trail starts to the west and continues south (up the hill). Quite a scenic trail with healthy wild poppies, sage and lavender.

QH Trailhead starts on the east side.The challenge is here. Bathrooms are at the park and clean. There is an audio tour that may be accessed online. Landscaping is epic!

Be prepared for a significant ascent at the end  and enjoy a 180 degree view of Shady Canyon estates, new construction homes and the Newport Beach marina "vista"  be found at the top. Lovely trail in nature and pristine.

Yorba Linda Regional (YLR) is a wonderful green space and has many trails and outdoor activities for families/couples. Lots of wildlife viewing here and many rangers to patrol and assist park patrons.

Park is located close to Savi Ranch in the "Land of gracious living" aka Yorba Linda.YLR has many green spaces and opportunities for picnics, bicycle riding or just reading a book on a blanket with family.

Parking is not a problem and there are pay/complimentary options. Notice the water bikes, lovingly kept gardens and lakes. Play areas are planned well with safety, serenity and wildlife in mind.Visit.

Heisler's walk ways have an artistic flair and societal views have me pondering of warm breezes and flapping sarongs waving hello in the warm winds of "La Barceloneta." Heisler is close to a "surgeons perfect."

Close parking--bring quarters for the meters---machines take credit cards. Coffee and light snacks on the north side of PCH can be had at Madison Gardens offers outdoor and indoor seating.

Clean restrooms are close and Laguna Beach has many commissioned sculptures throughout this park. Laguna Beach provides an exceptional backdrop for many filmed reality, movie and theatrical productions.

Pleasure meeting historian Russ Keller and snooping around this museum. As a child I was introduced to this area via car trip to Santa’s Village. This is a definite visit and do grab a souvenir from the gift shop.

Theatre presentation of film history of area was a delight while  lounging in the cool air-conditioning. Curious about the “Lollipop Lady” as they named a school after her. Is that true Russ?

Thanks for the card/hospitality. Admission is free and donations are needed. Time in all things and the exhibits are charming. Location has the Historic St. Moritz Lodge sign, gift store at entry.
likes: Facilities & Services: Cool air-conditioning, Gift shop

reviews_attraction.text:
Sunset Ridge Park is quite capricious.This park is green and welcoming.
Victorville was the perfect respite to a long drive and we took a break to sit on the grass and sip Starbucks libations. The surroundings were tidy.

Tennis, baseball and basketball courts were in great condition and in close proximity to the fire station. In the mood for a walk? There is a nice walking/running path here under a mile in length.

Such a pleasant outdoor green experience was lived here for a short while. Do give Sunset Ridge Park a try and be delightfully surprised. Clean, safe and well suited for families.

"Expect Extraordinary"

Members only allowed . All gates require a code for entry and video survelliance signs were spotted at dock houses. Trees are healthy and in an apparent state of bliss and this is a reserve for natures treasures.

Lake Arrowhead is privately owned by Arrowhead Lake Association (ALA) for exclusive use by its members---members family and guests only. ALA holdings include strip and reserve strip.

Other jewels in the ALA holdings portfolio include but not limited to:  Burnt Mill, Tavern Bay Beach Clubs, Marina Peninsula Park, Grass Valley Lake and Grass Valley Park.

For the bargain price of $10.00 you can enter this exclusive museum which houses the private collection of Virgil Elings. This is an expansive collective of fine motorcycles.

Some of the featured items are 1910 FN to the present, and across all makes. Museum is geared toward the racing genre of motorcycles as it is aligned with the particular focus of Virgil and his son Jeff.

A visit to this museum is a delight and is a short trip from Los Angeles area through the drive along the coast to the beautiful Santa Ynez Valley.
Exhibits are diverse and do change as the seasons. Do visit.

Play with the interactive installments in this museum. Onsite is the original house that President Nixon and his family grew up in.  Let me know what little "secret" flying thing was by his desk.

Now you can enter the Oval Office and sit at President's  Nixon’s' Desk. This new remodel is fabulous and imparts the visitor an auspicious view---elevated above Watergate/China scandal.

Did you know in this very office (Oval Office) President Nixon met with Israeli Prime Minister Golda Meir, King Hussein of Jordan and Prime Minister Pierre Trudeau. Play, interact and visit!

Hiking up was wonderful and we brought in some water. Bring a camera, sunscreen and a good attitude, Notice how the soil is? Any guesses on its composition? Hint: D

Hiking in the shadows of giant trees was wonderful and was a great date/get to know each other activity. The shapes and structures of the oldest trees in the world are striking.

We always stop here on our way to Bishop and Mammoth Lakes. Just look for the large bristlecone off the highway and turn left. Parts of the ascent appear as an alien landscape. Elevation is significant, hydrate!

As a child (7 years old) I recall a delightful planet story presented visually, musically and caused us to look up in the theater to see the stars dance on the screen above.

That warm and fuzzy memory engendered a return as an adult. Armed with multi syllabic weapons then ascending steps to this Observatory---what I found within was a secret.

Colonel Griffith J. Griffith said  “If all mankind could look through that telescope, it would change the world!” In operation since 1935 Equipped with telescopes like Solar, Zeiss. Visit and look up.

Formerly this delightful little park was known as "Lone Pine Park." This is a true oasis off the US 395 Highway and has ample parking and clean restrooms for travelers, residents or dogs.

Stream runs through this park. Do take a break under a tree as you hear water passing over rocks. Trees provide enough shade for a picnic or a brief water break.

This park is a friendly place for dogs and owners---who pick up after pets. Check out the playground and do note the nearby fountain---for thirsty little ones and adults. Worth the visit!

Review in progress...
Fluffly Cumulonimbus Clouds hang around here---like chandeliers in the dining room---grow mulch protected toddlers from falls. Such views are phenomenal.

Improvements include a stage, outdoor workout area with artificial grass--snows up here. Bathrooms are clean and this park has a great lookout area on the west side.

Another nice feature is the Bark Park which is an off leash play place for furry friends. This is located north of MacKay Park ( East side) of the park. Fountain and doggie bags are provided.

Crystal Cove State Park is  an idyllic stretch of 3.2 miles of beach, 2,400 acres  wilderness and an offshore underwater area that may be explored with a snorkel and fins. Ruby's Diner is up on the cliffs off of PCH where you can look down and see the Historic District, with 46 vintage coastal cottages available for rent (yet reservations are made a year in advance).

Picture worthy sandy beaches and flying wildlife squatting atop rock formations are great attributes along with paddle boarding, surfing and sunning at this park. For little ones a tot lot can be fun play with parents. Parking is $1.00 at time of this review. Dogs allowed during the summer.

Okay, getting hot is the San Diego region? Then stop by Marian Bear Memorial Natural Park. Just south of State Route 52 near its end at the west. Exit Regent/Clairemont Mesa Blvd, and south. Turn left and you will find the bumpy gravel/dirt parking lot, go under the bridge and find another larger one (east side of road). Both have restrooms and information kiosks, picnic tables and bathrooms. This is a highly wooded park. The trees create lots of shade and bird habitats.
The creek provides water for many types of animals while soothing even the animal in men & women. Many butterflies and hummingbirds are viewable in spring. In summer the park & trails stay cool from shade and constant slow breeze via the canyons coming from the ocean & (SD Mission Bay)bay. Many trails lead up the hill/bluffs into the communities that surround the canyon park. In fact on the eastern side one trail lead under SR 52 to a neighborhood park & school/rec. ctr/pool in University Heights. During summers they have many family events and movie nites here.
On the west side is a nature trail with markers and pamphlet giving descriptions. The trail ends at the another river/creek and breaks off under the SR 52/ I-5 interchange going north to Rose Canyon, another natural canyon I'll review later. This end has a high view path ending at a flowing creek, with meadows and forest on both sides. West side path leads across railroad track, BE CAREFUL!, that goes into a commercial/industrial/retail center. Lunches can be had here on weekdays, you can also smell the waft of beer being brewed at the Strauss Brewery. This is a great place to connect to the path if you are coming from PB, via Santa Fe St. bike path at end goes up to UCSD campus.
There are lots of natural elements here, including Coyotes, Great Horned Owls, red-tail hawks, an occasional perigrine falcon, wood peckers, and fox. Go enjoy your canyons! But women please take a companion to be safe. Mountain bikes can use, too. Just have a bell to warn hikers & walkers, please. Thanks! Enjoy. Walk with Him (fb)
dislikes: Need for caution (railroad track, safety for women)

reviews_attraction.text: Rose Canyon is easy and convenient to access and hike. Near Genesee there is a walking garden space. Woods available on east side of Genesee north of H.S. To the west is shaded area on the south side trail(s). Trails go up into the community on the south portion of the canyon. The end of Regents Road on the North side has north side trail heads. Also at the end of Regents Road on the South side is parking and a shaded trail down into the canyon over the creek via small pedestrian bridge. As you go southwest in the canyon you will see many different types of foliage and environs. Listen for birds, woodpeckers, finches, mockingbird and owls. You might see red tail hawks hovering above. The end of the trail southwest get dry and dusty while going over a hilly are on the east. Trains pass close on the west side. Under the Highway 52 overpass you can enter into Marian Bear Natural Park, a more shaded area mostly. Lots of work has been done in Rose Canyon Open Space, more is being done! So please be kind to the nature, don't litter, and keep the noise to a minimum. We'll all be rewarded by it! Thank you.

So many birds: ducks, geese, seabirds, water fowl. Some from far away. Including BIG White Pelican! Lot of people for Thursday am. Boat/fishing rental shack OPEN again! Sorry no photos, with GF, walking,  talking, necking...she mention bring table top grill and picnic next time!! I say increased walk...halfway around...3.5mi, full is about 7 as you have to reverse at dam and come back!!! Fishing licences required, Horse shoe pits, and dozens of picnic tables, a few docks, and many many soft grassy places to nap or neck(shhh!)
Go enjoy soon @VisitSanDiego twitter

Great City Park with pedestrian bridges...one majorarly Hosrorical, gazebos, stages, picnic areas...and Disc Golf along with ball golf course down the street. They are doing Major improvements so stay chill. Fully done in another year. Along with Recreational facilities improvements. Also no porta-potties are locked so pee in down! Family it up with River fishing too..boat ramp also!!! Library close too!! And great place to plan Employer or group activities!
Can easily be 5 stars when all open.
Sorry no photos...but believe me worth taking a look: 🦆🦢🦉🐦🐣

Good Stuff! Free lunch (donation suggested) Dance, Tai Chi, Zumba, art classes, BINGO fridays (quarter {mornings} & dollar {afternoon} games). Special events, including hosting D-6 Night Market Event early next year!
Many distributions of service, most free...taxes/financial help/advice. Easy parking, green areas, patio space with benches and rose bushes! Also very friendly staff & service. Always keeping you safe & on time.
likes: Cultural classes (Dance, Tai Chi, Zumba, art)

reviews_attraction.text:
Nice, green area with big trees, bushy boundries to private homes 2 sides, school with high clear fencing mostly other side. Very small parking lot about 8 street Pkg space at front, 2 baseball diamond, bleachers, basketball courts, playground, restrooms. Picnic tables. Few drinking fountains. Entrance only in front for visitors.
People walk around baseball fields. Dogs welcomed. Two large Church properties down street.

Great for relaxing, many "sightseers/tourists" swimming beach w/ seals/sea lions wind swept trees, kiosk overlooking ocean, rocky&sandy beaches(not too large). Bathrooms closed{remodel}.
