Bluffs over looking park with Hotels and Luxury Condos. Bluffs with sea birds to water/ocean. On large & deep (sea diving) underwater natural park. Tourist Cave, and many eateries, art galleries, and shops nearby.
likes: Natural features (rocky and sandy beaches, underwater natural park)

reviews_attraction.text: Palisade Park on North PB bluff overlooking beaches: Law St(Fam) & Tourmaline (surf). Residential/Tourist towers overlook. Regular activities on grassy park above beach next to nice restrooms & showers. Life guard south. Yoga in Bluff park daily. Bench, and ez picnic area, as well as road, and foot trails going to Beach. Surf area, but very limited street parking, buses 2&4 blocks away.

Great trails,  more north of here to Del Mar Race Track & San Dieguito Creek area too. @CaStateParkSD by @GolfTorrey ... @USopenGolf June. Open free also! Near by Bus stops for both, not sure about North Trails. Bring picnic and enjoy. No Mtn Bikes! Few romantic places so wine him or her too!! #7footAPARThikes , but gone til June: @PGAtour dream trip!

Excellent..will update later...riding Bus today around Rural Areas toward Austin [comes from Marble Falls: see Brass Hall & Bluebonnet Cafe reviews]
But few pics! Make sure to go Thurs.-Sat. 10-4. Great stuff & history here, large outside cabins and homestead area out back!!! Sadly no BEEMAN Garden Tractors...next time?
likes: Facilities & Services: Large cabins, homestead area

reviews_attraction.text:
Fun, but my day a bit wet...April weather Ft Worth!⛈🌈☔👢🤠🐄🐮
Trains regularly blowing horns...🐎🐄in field nearby. Few FREE parking on top of hill, exit to Paid pkg out back.
Historic in and old town(gone). Added Will Roger's Memorial [see review] pics also...go there if your into cowboy, cowgirl, rodeo, livestock, etc!
dislikes: Facilities & Services: Limited free parking, paid parking

reviews_attraction.text: Didn't get to see much. Full schedule. Even weekdays this place hopping busy. $20 for overnight, $5 less than least expensive on Guadalupe River Canyon City area!! $5 for day-use &/or shower. Heard water can be muddy/dirty after rain..so be aware!!! Support your @Texas @TPWDparks [twitter].

Loved this: 8th Annual Urban Canyons & BRIDGES hike;3 mi.s, 1st Saturday Dec! #7footApartHikes {formerly @WalkwithhimFcbk } NOW San Diego Day Hikers @MeetUp.com weekly hikes!😁✌️🦌approved...next hike the Next Sat started here...some houses before that hike.

Still great with lots of power in art, movement, and culture. Near to new Mexican Grocery Center, other shops, education, and family fun! Because of recent tragic accident, truck flew off bridge killing at least 4, lots of memorials. Say prayer, please.

So great of a place for Kids to play, adults to swim, play tennis, gym too! Also hiking Trail to Marian Bear Natural Park(.5mi). Big fields for concerts/movies during summer. Big public pool, small pkg lot, but lots of Street parking: Governor Dr.

Great lil piece of Art, not far from SD Lindberg Field, Washington Ave, eateries! Good views to North Island, Pt. Loma too! SD Bay!! We SAW on #7footApartHikes weekly hike/Walkabout via San Diego Day Hikers @MeetUp.com by daniel-aka FreedomPlease

Not cheap. And unsure if worthwhile. Price of 2 cheap 🍻for old log blogs? Half block long?? At least good supply of pkg...next to Park, but no restrooms. Or park across S. Univ. Ar least near Panera & IHOP and some local eateries.

Nice linear park, plenty of benches, path around, convient stores nearby...TCP Craigs Ranch Country Club &Golf Course down street! Free parking. Huge set of flags and large Granite Memorials. Think @Hoffman_charley listed there?

Great National Park! Just too bad so remote and far from San Diego. Enter from south or north. Camping, climbing,hiking.Historical places. Town just outside on north side. Easy to hard trails. Petroglyphs & rock art.Tours.

Great design, lots of access points, seating, nature, amazing views, EZ way to just "Chill". Thanks @Austin City Council and Ex Gov. Ann Richardson!! Enjoy!!! 10 miles of trail including both sides of River.
Great, even just to use tables for meal, while closed stand, view into Garden from Above, or Behind via trail below. From @BalboaPark Butterfly Garden, across from Natural Museum, El Prado Dr.
Long, Big,  W I D E  Pier! Bathrooms, Nice Franchise Restaurant at end. Plenty fishing going on!, even Pelicans!! Great view of Coast down too. Advisory, road blockage for cars, and bikes.
Here is little walkabout by the park, starting look into water over inlet bay under pedestrian bridge west of Manuel Park to South of the park near Vacation Island & Crown Point.
Summer Concerts, playgrounds, NO Bathroom 🤔, on bus 11, VIEWS, and Great Walkabout area for Historical Houses. Did with #7footApartHikes SD Day Hikers @MeetUp weekly series!😁✌️🦌
Peaceful place to relax, kiss, picnic, listen to water fountains and view plants, HUGE tree, while listening to CA Tower bells ring hourly!

We took only maze and it was really great fun with kids. Adults also were running around to find all the secrets and place stamps. I'm wondering if at different time of the year bushes are stronger and you can't see through and make shortcuts.
Plantation tour was unclear for us, I still don't know if it was free w/o guides. There is also souvenirs shop and restrooms. Worth spending couple of hours.

Waves are great, but seeing turtles seems like pretty rare event. We spend about an hour walking along the beach (which is beautiful, no doubt btw), very few people, surfers, fishers... Sand is really nice, but you won't build a sand castle there because the beach itself is kind a short in wide and waves takes all the space. There is no wind Wich is also nice addition.

I wish I was able to see the view from that point . You can drive up there, parking lot is about 20 cars i think, but path to the point is very short so people leave fast. You can stop at Taff point and hike from there if you want, there is also beautiful view, but trail is kinda not short. Both views are showing the valley, but if there are clouds you want see much.

We didn't like it. There is no playground for kids, lake is too small to walk around it. There are places for picnic, which is fine, but parking is $6. Trails are with high grass and there were a lot of ticks! There are horse riding so maybe it's good to ride horses there, but I would not recommend to hike here. Views might be good though.

Beautiful and unique place with eucalyptus flavor. One thing for photographers, daylight gives super harsh shadows from the trees so it's not that good as in cloudy day or evening/sunrise. Using telephoto or zoom lens recommend to compress the space and create nice path trail in the background. Kids have fun playing with sticks

I like this place, there is some beautiful scenery, good places for photos, to slowly ride on a bike. Observe nature, birds or just walk. You don't get to this place right away, so you have to park tour car on a parking nearby beach. This is part of coastal trail that goes for few miles from North to South.

I love this beach, it's quite, warm, not super sandy (when wind blows and sand is everywhere). Water have a nice blue color near the beach. I wish it was a more sunny day maybe. There are some wood sticks, so kids can play with them. Seagulls and seals..

Absolutely amazing place for kids where they can build or extend any existing playground elements. Paint, saw, 🔨, nails, magenta for collecting nails and few more tools for fun! Must go with all ages of kids

I was surprised about this place, it has plenty of picnic spots. Trails in the woods are also nice, excep West Ridge trail which is too sandy and  I wouldn't suggest to start from it after Orchad trail.
I love this place!! Views are great and tour to elephant seals was amazing! $7 per person, every 15 min. Please reserve ahead or you will have to wait for an hour or so.
Absolutely beautiful place 😍. Get here around 4-5pm to get a good spot for a sunset and don't forget warm windproof clothes as it's super windy, very strong wind!
Amazing park, beautiful trails, caves!!! Rocks are really rock! And we got lucky to see Condors. Recommended time to visit - spring, might be too hot in Summer.
Absolutely beautiful and amazing place! For sunrise and sunset they're are seats to observe, also you can walk on the short trail, there are a lot of flowers
Views are really great, but it's too windy there to stay for longer time. Water isn't that clean and there are some trash floating in the water
Good place... I wish there was less homeless places, that might scary kids. Plenty of tables for picnic, big green area, playground, river...
Good place to swim there wit kids, or just have a picnic in shadows of trees. Parking is huge, cost $5. You can also take hiking trail.
Great and unusual trail from whatever has left from lava. Good shoes are recommended. Some black goats 🐐 are there and nice views.
Rides are great, dolphins show is so so, orcas are magnificent. Flamingo are great too. Plan your visit early to avoid crowds.
It's good for pictures, but making picnic there is just impossible. Constant wind with sand... You can walk pretty far though
Views are amazing! Although parking issues are problem, you need to get on special bus from a different parking to get there.
It wasn't so nice and flowerful as it described. You should pick a certain time of the year to visit it during blossoming.
High point but views aren't impressive. If you go down by grizzly road there are better view for the bay area and SF.
Nice place and beautiful views here. Probably very good for the sunsets. I wish that sand would be different here :)
Nice place to bring your kids and have a picnic. Playground is big enough for many kids to play at the same time
Good place to visit. You can take shuttle bus for free if you are going to look only outside at the ship

Southside Park is one of the more fun and interesting parks in the city of Sacramento - and I have visited them all. One of the most unique things is the "spaceship" that is first on the end of a curved poll. Nice playground and restaurants here. It's also enjoyable to stroll around the lake in the center of the park. There are Vista points around the lake where you can watch what are fellow frolic and enjoy the wind rustling through the trees. There's also an outdoor theater here.

Peaceful mid-sized neighborhood park. There is a half basketball court, a playground for the children, and a drinking fountain near the entrance. There is also a small flower garden at the top of the hill closest to the main entrance of the park.

Antelope Creek Road behind the park. There is plenty of shady beaches along this small stream where one can relax in relative seclusion.

This is one of the most spectacular views in Death Valley. There is also full restroom facilities in the parking lot at the trailhead. Volunteers have been doing a great job of keeping the restroom facilities clean during the 2019 government shutdown. A private Association is also help funding the maintenance of this particular point in Death Valley.

Pretty cool. This arch can be photographed from both sides, so if you go there in the afternoon you may want to carefully hike to the west of the arch for afternoon lighting. Just don't get to close to the edge because pieces of the lava cliff could break off under you sending you to your doom below.

This park has a large area for multi-sport. There's a frisbee golf around the perimeter of the park. The playground is large with two major climbing structures and all types of swings. Swings for small children and large children there is no restroom facilities at this park.

This is a nice place to launch a kayak or canoe. There is lots of shaded areas for a picnic.
There is a playground, but it is kind of off to the side, so you have to look for it.
There is are less-than-desirable maintained beach volleyball court with well-maintained nets.

This Pleasant Park includes a tree-shaded picnic area, beautiful grass areas, and a monument to Rosie the Riveter. The monument commemorates the women who worked in the factories during World War II. Take time to read the descriptions around the memorial.

Petroglyphs may be hard to notice at first until you get used to looking for them. This short hike seemed longer than it really is due to extreme sun exposure. Probably a good idea to take some water with you.

Wonderful little park. There is two different playgrounds. There's a little Library box. There are covered picnic grounds and a well-kept basketball court as well. There are restroom facilities at the park.

This is a cute little park with a quaint gazebo right in downtown Winters. The hustle and bustle of the small downtown area is nearby. The park is shaded with a couple picnic tables and a public restroom.
Best time for photographs is late in the day.  Called Sunrise Point because you can view the sunrise from this area, but if you're going to visit at sunrise, you'll get better light at Sunset Point.
Nice neighborhood Park with large playground and covered picnic areas. There are paved walking paths and large multisport grass fields There is a handicap accessible restroom.
Really fun place for family outings. Pan for gold.  Explore historic building.  Walk along the river.  Picnic.  Informative visitor center with indoor and outdoor exhibits.
It just an ok viewpoint. The loop is kind of far away, but it's still worth a brief visit. The historical markers include sime interesting facts about the engineering feat.

Really liked all of the geology to the hike here. I failed to grab a trail guide because there were none, but I imagine that sign markers denote where the brochure would tell you about the varying geology here. It is evident that upward crust and mantle thrusts created this valley hundreds of thousands of years ago or more. We really liked all of the things to look at. There was even what looked to be a sealed mine entrance on one of the hill faces. It was completely impossible to get into unless you had some serious welder skills. I wonder if there was mining here or if it was just a person living there. ? Total time took about 2 hours; intersected other trails and put you back onto the gulch rim back to the trail entrance. Bring water, especially for the first mile or so as it has an incline worth noting.

The aquarium is a breath of fresh air, to know more about conservation efforts for wildlife and the environment. This is no Monterey Bay Aquarium, but it's nicely put together and offers a multitude of sea animals from the local area. The cool things: an area where people can touch things like sea snails (in shells), hermit crabs and sea urchins. Also they feed turtles in front of you which was very cool. They've got a large sea turtle and also quite a few nurse sharks in their small pools. Would be 5 stars if these animals in particular had a larger enclosure, as they normally travel quite a bit in their natural environments.

In 1970 I began visiting the mines all around what would later become
Almaden Quicksilver County Park.Later in the early 1980s while a student in Park Management at West Valley College-I did a walking tour as guide around the Senator Mine and Herreshoff furnaces.
Mining began in 1826 in New Almaden-long before the Sutter Hills gold strike in 1849.
Cinnabar was extracted crushed and placed into smelters to cook off mercury in vapor form and fed into  condensers shaped like tubes at many of the mercury production furnaces.
For over a decade along with many friends we enter many of the mines including one on Hicks Road that resurfaces just below Guadalupe Dam as well as a tunnel that was in the Hicks road drainage that exited near Mine Hill.
The area is undermined with dozens of mine shafts-tunnels etc -few had any timber bracing walls or ceilings and many had very dangerous sinkholes,cave ins, and frequently piles of dynamite left behind underground. We were by and large ignorant of the dangers of mercury,lead,arsenic,methane,etc frequently found in mines.
I began to photograph the mines and buildings all around them as vandals began stealing artifacts and using 4x4 trucks to destroy landmarks.
For 7 seasons I also worked as a Park Ranger Aide doing maintenance work and collecting fees at many parks.In 1996 I moved back to Washington State and currently live in Everett.
This is my favorite park in San Jose and New Almaden-long before thousands of new homes would push away all the farms
and close in on the beautiful orchards that once graced the Almaden Valley.
Its my hope that I can shed a bit of light n this grand park!

Welcome to Spencer Island County Park.
Located in North Everett along the Snohomish River
and Union Slough.
This is a beautiful multi-use park.
Despite any negative reviews from "tourists" this is a well visited and loved County Park well worth the effort if you enjoy wildlife.
Its probably not too exciting if you do not enjoy wildlife and yes there is a water treatment plant on Smith Island, but that is not part of Spencer Island!
Tons of birds Winter over on their travels and it makes
for a great day of bird watching and for fantastic views
of the sunrise over the Cascade mountains East of the park.

Well maintained trails allow users easy access.
Its not handicap or wheelchair friendly.
Hunters, bicycles and dogs are prohibited on the South
side of the islands waterways.
In Winter-hunting is allowed for ducks but only on the
North Side of the bridge and in posted areas only.

This is a fantastic place to explore!
A must see for the Everett area.
Beautiful reflections over the waters can be seen
45 minutes prior to sunrise and of course as
the sun sets.
The access trail along the chain link fence
by the treatment plant on the North side
follows the dike on Union Slough.

Great sunrise shots from this isolated part of Smith Island.
Watch for deer,rabbits,fox,mink,otters,weasels and ferrets.
Lots of Butterflies in the Summer!

It is a wetland sanctuary so although it looks like a swamp
but if one looks closer, there is an abundance of wildlife and natural beauty at ones feet.
dislikes: Limited activities (no bicycles, dogs, or hunting on the South side)

reviews_attraction.text:
Welcome to Grand Avenue Park in North West Everett!
It is well maintained by City of Everett Parks crew.
The Park Ranger even pitches in to pick up trash
as he inspects the park daily, provides answers to visitors
questions and points out various landmarks.

The only negative here is the height of the barrier hedge
which blocks too much of the view if you are seated
at any bench or table.

Other than that, its a great location for sunsets and just
relaxing, or having a meal with friends or just solo!
In the last ten years I have captured hundreds of sunsets and
other cool shots here year around!

Though it lacks a bathroom or drinking fountain,
there is simply no room for a bathroom.
The park has historical value also.

As an artist, I love the trees, the shadows,
the scenic views of the
Olympic Mountains and the Port of Everett,
the marina, and Naval Station Everett.
I have talked to many who come there to paint
in watercolor or pastels, chalk or acrylics
the views below and on the horizon.

The park is very popular on the 4th of July
just for watching the fireworks.

Like all City of Everett parks, it is a
Drug and Alcohol Free park as in Zero Tolerance.

It is one of my favorite parks, just for the trees alone.
These are some of my favorite views below.
Enjoy!

Carkeek Park is a family friendly, multi-use park.
Many hiking trails surround the park as it is in a gully.
It has a model aircraft use area as well as trails
along Carkeek Creek and a fish hatchery.
Large lawn areas for hundreds of picnic users as well
as a play area for kids. A larger well maintained bathroom
and bonfire areas are also used frequently.
Trails lead to a pedestrian overpass that
take you safely over the BNSF Railway.

If you choose to cross over the railway be extra cautious
as the BNSF folks have welded all the rails together
and there is no longer the clicking noise as trains rush along
the corridor at speeds of 50 mph plus!
Always cross the Railways safely!

Though many like to walk the rails to photograph
scenery or graffiti along the rails, the RR Police may cite
you for criminal trespass. There have been multiple deaths
along the stretch from Golden Gardens North to
Richmond Beach from careless individuals walking
on the rail road tracks, so, stay off!

Other than that warning and no dogs allowed on the beach,
this is one of my favorite destinations in North Seattle.
Tons of sea life, wildlife, wind surfers and great scenery
from sunsets to sailboat races and the Olympic Mountains.
dislikes: No dogs allowed on the beach

reviews_attraction.text:
I love exploring this park! I took class trips from Saratoga,Ca up to Lava Beds 2 times and visited the area 4 more times afterward.
There are many lava tubes to explore-just watch out for rattlesnakes
in the lava beds and tubes!
One area in the park is set aside for bats! A long lava tube the goes down into the earth has long eared bats living in it!
Lava Beds National Monument is home to 14 different bat species,
largely because this area provides such a wide variety of habitat.

Bats here can find the exact conditions they need and are able to choose between hundreds of caves, cliff faces, and trees. Some species stay here year-round, while others migrate from as far as Mexico and Central or South America. All 14 species are insectivores (they eat insects) and use echolocation to navigate. It is a common misconception that bats are blind; most have fairly good eyesight. Some people may dislike or be afraid of bats, but with a little effort, we can better understand and appreciate these important creatures.

Welcome to the historic Grand Coulee Dam!
This is an awesome facility to visit and take the tour!
Very impressive to say the least.It gives the average individual
a very clear picture of where electricity comes from
on the Columbia River.
Grand Coulee is the largest dam in the Columbia River Basin
and one of the largest in the world. Everything about the dam
is large: it is 550 feet (167.6 meters) tall, measured from its foundation
in solid granite, or approximately 350 feet (106.7 meters) from the downstream river surface to the top of the dam.
It is 5,223 feet (1,592 meters) long, or 57 feet short of a mile.
If you are out for a long scenic drive and want an amazing tour
this may be a great place to visit and bring eager to learn children
along for the tour!

Richmond Beach Saltwater Park is always packed shortly
after sunrise on any day its nice out. So arrive early and
try to park at the top lots instead of the lower ones
due to a number of vehicles being broken into.
It is a great park for stair climbing exercise. Lots of stairs
as well as fitness minded folk working out.
When I lived in Shoreline a few years ago, I frequented
many parks for a great escape, nature and a workout.
Richmond Beach gives you everything you desire
in a park with great beach access!
The beach itself is fairly long, lots of agates, and
driftwood. There are wild roses growing on the North end.
Lots of nice spots on the South end to hang out.
All in all it is a great destination and well maintained.

Over the years I have visited and camped near the Bristlecone Pine Forest
and always enjoyed my stay Ive hiked in November,and all kinds of weather, as we explored the areas many mines, miners cabins and tree line as well as closer to the top of White Mountain.An area well worth exploring.Be prepared for a thin air environment above 9,000 feet.
Take time to acclimate or get use to the elevation by going slowly.
The Road up to the research station is over 12,000 ft and
worth the drive to the observation area that looks
down on Bishop and parts of the Owens Valley.

One of my favorite day use areas in Washington!
Great views for all users and at times Ice Caves form
at the bottom of an avalanche chute.
It can be very dangerous to enter any ice cave
yet many do each year.
Just be very cautious as it can cave in at any time
or a very heavy chunk break off the peaks above.
Still, and awesome destination.
Always respect natures beauty.Pack it in and pack it out!

Be wise and be safe when near the mountain's base for falling objects.

In the mid 1980s as I studied Park Management at
West Valley College in Saratoga,Ca, my class took trips to
Lava Beds National Monument and Tule Lake Sump.
There are millions of birds that stop over here on their journey
North or South. In November the area is packed with
an amazing variety of wildlife!
Since those classes I have visited the area 4 times
and always amazed at the abundance of waterfowl and land
animals from Antelope to Elk, this area is pretty cool!

One of my favorite places to visit in North Everett.
Not only do they have a really nice garden but great staff!
The gardens are well designed and maintained and very good energy.
I enjoy Spring displays the best! But Fall colors add an entire new
perspective to this year around park.
There are many unique sculptures and art in the gardens also.
lots of bees, hummingbirds and other pollinators, and Bald Eagles.
A wide variety of birds for such a small area.

This is the trailhead to the Monte Cristo Mines
and town of Monte Cristo ruins. There are many mines
and tunnels in this area if you follow the animal trails
not far from the entrance gate, or search about.
Always be cautious entering any mine as most are hazardous.
There are tons of marked trails for experienced backcountry users.
Great place to visit and explore!

Welcome to the Pacific Northwest Trail!
This is just part of the 1,100 mile long trail
and this section takes you up to the Blanchard Mountain Overlook
where hang gliders and parasailers leap into the sky from.
The trail also goes up to the Oyster Dome

another awesome viewpoint.The lake has an intense green to it.
It can be very breezy and there are many Chipmunks.
Do not feed them, as they can bite you and carry diseased fleas.
It is a great place to take scenics! And enjoy lunch.

Olympia's best park! A beautiful flower garden, hiking trails,
beach access , picnic areas, group areas!
I spent many a great day bicycling around the park
as well as walk all the trails with friends
and had many great picnics there!

Great walk and amazing when the river is at
flood stages or during the Spring or Summer melting
of the snow pack higher up in the Cascades.
Great exercise but fairly steep.
I tried to add a video of the falls but it was rejected.

This is a beautiful park to have both day use and camping!
Great trails, scenic views and it is the first place
where Spring flowers bloom in the region.Lots of lillies
and native wildflowers can be found along the pathways.

Over the years I have visited the caverns, I have always enjoyed my tour!
It has one of the first welded spiral stairways of its height in the main cavern.Great history behind it as well.

One of my favorite Indian Cultural Centers with lots
of art and history! Its best to call in advance for hours
of operation prior to your journey.

I have visited Mono Lake at least a dozen times since 1971
and I always enjoy being out near the Tufas.
It is a well managed area and great staff!

This is also a great day workout trail.
Be prepared!
Extra water, snack bars,etc.
Was also used as a conditioning
trail for backcountry survival.

This is the city's nicest park, with fishing and picnicking
and where the city has its arts and music , wine festival.
Well maintained.

Just a few small cabins and some other relics
remain at this historic mining camp.
Still, its a great day hike and picnic spot.

I love visiting this place and have taken dozens of photographs
over the last 22 years.It is a fun place to stop over.
It is not just a day use area to fish or watch Bald Eagles but also a great place to camp and be safe!

If you like history and nature you will like this unique park. Visitors Center is full of educational materials on local nature and geology. The gift store has nice selection of books, some fun clothing and crafts by local artisans. They also often have exhibits by local artists, photographers and on weekends host outdoor art and craft events. The area is beautiful any time of year but fall and spring are more colorful. The main house and stables (now Visitors Center) were designed and built by Wallace Neff just before the Great Depression. You can enjoy large grassy meadows dotted with Oaks, the long, winding driveway shaded by Sycamores and Eucalyptus, views of the surrounding mountains, a pond that's often visited by water birds and hiking trails. Free parking and restrooms by the Visitors Center.

The most scenic of all beaches in Malibu, El Matador is often called Mini Big Sur. Steep cliffs, rocks that shoot out of the sand and caves comprise three coves that are popular in any season among not just beach goers, but plein air artists and photographers. High tide makes some of these coves inaccessible. A foot path and stairs take you from the top of the cliffs to the first large cove. Parking lot always opens at 8 AM and always closes when it gets dark, so closing hours depend on the season. Paid parking (machine accepts credit cards and cash) is for about 45 cars, so on weekends come early to assure you get in. Limited free parking available across the street on PCH gets filled fast and is not very safe, because there is no designated pedestrian crossing.

We saw this garden on Google maps,  close to Rancho Los Alamitos where we planned to go as part of our Los Angeles history tour. So we drove out here early and according to Google maps it was open. In reality it was closed due to winter break. Turns out the garden is on the university's campus and functions by that kind of calendar. Since so many people use Google maps to navigate and get information it's important to update your Google maps listing. You would think that colleges and whoever works there would know this.

If you like history and nature you will like this place, Polo field with games on weekends, tours of the ranch house-museum, horse stables and training, large green lawn, hiking trails where dogs are allowed on a leash and Los Angeles city, mountain and ocean views.  Parking is $12, everything else is free. There are bathrooms, drinking fountains and picnic tables. Once a year around late October they hold an art show of representational paintings by local artists who are often seen painting here as well.
likes: On-site activities (hiking, polo games, horse training)

reviews_attraction.text: Always busy with people and no wander. The location, right in the center of the town, and multiple activities like volleyball, basketball and a boardwalk with many benches attract a diverse crowd. The views are worth capturing with cool rocks on one end of the beach and the iconic Hotel Laguna on the other. So that's what I did. I created two paintings wright there, had my supplies on the bench, my Pochade box strapped to a lamppost so it wouldn't blow away, very convenient.

Nice little park with a shady path lined with Sycamores, Eucalyptus and Oaks. Plenty of free parking. Nice features like large grass lawn in front of the ranch house, very clean restrooms, picnic tables under the trees, hiking trails where dogs are allowed make this park particularly attractive for families with kids and pets. Popular with plein air artists, photographers and nature enthusiasts this park is a great setting for your photo shoot or an outdoor event.

It's a good swing hole during hot summer weather. My son swims here all the time and loves it. People are not supposed to jump off the boulders, but unfortunately they do. If you are coming here to swim, please don't jump off the rocks, don't smoke( it's a fire hazard) and don't litter. Keep it clean. Put your trash in the trash bins located right there. I can't believe how much trash gets left behind and right next to the bins.

The Mission is beautiful,  views from the grounds - breathtaking. The disappointment was to see the front entrance and the best view of the building with a parking lot in the foreground instead of the green lawn as their  main photo suggests. The green lawn that is there is on the less picturesque, street side. It's of no use for photography or painting if you are an artist.

Beautiful park with a bit of history was a delight to visit because of the expansive green lawn, huge Moreton Bay Fig trees, Italian Stone Pines, Palm trees, the old light house and multiple gazibos built on the edge of cliff line overlooking the coastline with ships going in and out of the harbor. The weather was perfect to enjoy the day with gentle breeze and sunshine.

You will enjoy spectacular views of the San Fernando Valley, down town LA, Santa Monica Mountains, ocean on a clear day, a little bit of history, clean bathrooms, picnic tables with a view, a choice of hiking trails and the fact that dogs on leashes are allowed. The place is perfect for mountain biking,  hiking, horseback riding, painting and panoramic photography.

Excellent little museum! We enjoyed the tour of the house with a knowledgeable guide, Eileen. Already admirers of Wallace Neff, we checked another one of his creations off of our list. The location is beautiful, up on a knoll with great views. Also enjoyed viewing the Western art paintings and Indian rugs. Definitely recommend it!

Picturesque little beach that doesn't get too crowded even in the summer El Pescador is popular with local artists and surf fisherman. Small paid parking lot and free parking on PCH get full fast, so come early on weekends. A couple of picnic tables and one portable bathroom are the only facilities.

If you need a Gone With The Wind experience, check this place out. Not only it's perfectly kept, but of significant historical value. The tour guide was very knowledgeable and gave us an excellent tour. I would recommend visiting here and the Drum Barracks down there street on the same day.

We took Refugio Rd. all the way up. Lower portion goes by the creek and along side ranch, upper portion climbs high into the oak forested mountains where panoramic views of the mountains, ocean and islands are stunning. Note: only a few little dirt overlooks to pull aside and a narrow road.

It's a nice little beach for what it is and not too busy, so don't expect iconic Malibu here. There is a Native American village set up. Nice vistas from a small trail along the cliffs where I enjoyed painting the view, but forgot to save that photo. All I have to remember is my painting.

Park at Trippet Ranch parking lot, don't go on Cheney to Callon to Penny, private roads with no parking. Topanga State Park, I love this place. I hike here often. Ocean view, mountains,  breeze,  birds. It's a place where your mind relaxes and your body gets a workout at the same time.

This beautifully designed and landscaped cliff-top park has plenty of benches that are art pieces. Beautiful views up and down the coast with Catalina and San Clemente Islands in the distance attract plein air artists. The park is great for walking, people watching and relaxing.

It's not as impressive as other house-museums in San Fernando Valley, but being part of the history of Los Angeles it's none the less, important. I would recommend visiting here and Andres Pico Adobe on the same day since both are relatively close to each other.

One of the best kept secrets in Malibu. Escape the crowd at this nearly private beach with beautiful rock formations. Park in the neighborhood making sure you don't block the residents or damage their landscaping. Walk through a public beach gate access.

Not many parks in Santa Monica Mountains allow dogs, but this one does. It was a pleasure to walk our two pups around the lake and have them check out ducks. The hiking trails are interesting, lots of old sumac shrubs that are now more like trees.
It's a great rural coastal area and not that far from the city. Bathrooms,  lifeguards, a small "dogs allowed cliffy area/ trail, dolphins swim by, what's not to like?
This is a beautiful well thought through park with a playground, other sports and panoramic views of the ocean and mountains. Hiking trails start here as well.
Loved Wallace Neff's architecture, guided tour, artwork and furnishings on display. Enjoyed seeing various animals and sweeping views of the area.
Come to watch the sun set from this beautiful park in a great location with views of the Pacific Ocean, coast line and walking paths.
If you like trails winding through gentle rolling hills doted with trees and shrubs here and there, you will like this park.

All the places we had planned to go were closed because of the recent volcanic activity. Those would have all been fun, but I doubt I would have seen a lot of what I explored today had those areas been open. It was awesome to see the craters, hike the Destruction Trail and see the Sea Arch. Though it is all on lava, there is so much variety from flat lava flow plains to gravel-like mounds to rainforest to petroglyphs. I'm glad I came when I did so I could see so much that I didn't know was here. And by being in the park early, it was like we had the place to ourselves!
likes: Natural variety (lava flows, mounds, rainforest, petroglyphs)

reviews_attraction.text: Awesome hike worthy of its hard rating. There's nothing necessarily technical about the hike, but there are a lot of stairs and the top half has very little shade. There is a lot of gorgeous scenery to take in, but about halfway up you get an up close view of the upper falls. Even if you don't plan on finishing, making it that far is worthwhile. There are a lot of people on this trail-- you decide if that is congestion or subtle opportunities for a quick breather. Definitely recommend for anyone looking for a big hike with a big reward.

We haven't rushed to this park because we've been to Sequoia and Yosemite and thought this might just be more of the same. It is, in the sense that it is a grove of Giant Sequoias, and it turns out that is a great thing. The North Grove hike was perfect for my young kids-- there are 26 markers around the trail and they ran to get to the next one. The grove and surrounding area are beautiful. There was a lot less traffic on a Saturday afternoon than at the big national parks. This is a great little gem in Calaveras.

Probably closer to 3.5 stars. The boat ride out to Santa Cruz Island and back was nice. We hiked from Scorpion Bay to Potato Harbor along the coast and then back on Potato Harbor Road. There is very little shade outside of the campground and nowhere but the ground to sit along the hike. The views of the ocean are great, but the island itself was kinda drab. I think kayaking and snorkeling are really where it is at on this island. If we ever come back, it will be to do one/both of those things.

There's a reason the Monterey Bay Aquarium is regarded as one of the best in the world. The Aquarium had the full attention of the kids and adults in our family for three full hours-- two hours longer than the last aquarium we visited. The displays were amazing, the atmosphere was perfect and there was so much to learn and do. Our kids were tired by the end but still wanted to see some things over again. It was a little pricey, as most of Monterey is, but a very worthwhile experience overall.

Hiked from Bear Gulch to the reservoir through the caves. This was a great hike with lots of variety. The cave ceiling was low enough in one place that we had to take the baby out of his carrier, but only for a few feet.   My other young kids enjoyed the trail and did well on it.

There's insufficient parking, so it's crucial to get to the Park early-- especially on weekends. A number of trails here are unshielded from the sun as well, which I imagine could nake them quite hot in summer.

Not much open right at 10:30. We felt a little like we were making up for a bummer start the rest of the day. It turned out pretty good once we realized that Sea World thought we were there for the animals. The shows were great. We approached our visit just as excited for the rides, but they almost seem intended to be a filler for between the shows. Fun day.

Cool black beach park with good beach access. The Internet said this was a great place to learn how to snorkel. I disagree. There are some cool things to see, but I spent most of the time battling the waves rather than checking out what was there. I did see two turtles after I got out and the black sand is the best.

This was a great one-hour tour of an underground home/resort built mostly in the early 1900s. It wasn't exactly what I expected-- it's more structure than gardens-- but it was still interesting and our guide did an excellent job of sharing the history and details we would have missed on our own.

My kids could have spent the entire day here!  It's great when they are learning while having fun, too. Admission was relatively expensive, I thought, even for a good museum, and beware that parking is extra. It was fun to splurge once but I doubt we will ever go back.

It was below freezing when we stsrted around 8 AM in early October. The hike was very short and easy. The trail is well groomed and could accommodate a jogging stroller or similar-- even had a ramp by the stairs. Great stop for anyone in the area.

Look down the cliff at waves crashing against the steep side of lava and through an arch that is standing strong despite the beating. It's a gorgeous setting and an awesome experience. The arch is visible from about a block away from the road.

Great hike. Not much shade. A couple spots with dropoffs on both sides of the trail that could make those with young kids or a fear of heights anxious. A handful of unique arches beyond Landscape Arch make it worthwhile to continue.

Beautiful, peaceful trail. Moderately difficult but worth every step. Signs lead to one of two lakes; the other is about .5 miles down the other fork in the trail. Can get busy later in the day in summer.

Iconic San Francisco. Parking is tricky and there's not many (legal) opportunities to get out and take a picture or walk the street, but worth driving down at least once if you're already in the area.
Great little hike, but don't stop at Arch Rock. There's a lot of great climbing to do around the arch. The trail isn't marked well, but it's on the right just after the trail crosses the road.
Great hike. Red Cathedral is brilliant in the early morning. The Golden Canyon side is a little more scenic than the other side of the loop, but it was worthwhile to complete the loop.
Great park has seen better days. Much of the park is now faded and showing signs of wear, but it is still a lot of fun and has a wide variety of activities to keep kids busy for hours.
This place is unreal. You'd have no idea just driving by on the highway that these formations are here or that they're so gnarly and numerous. This is a quick stop, but a good one.
On the trail around 8 AM and had it all to ourselves for a few hours. Gorgeous scenery, waterfalls, beaches... hiked about 6 miles and loved every minute of it.
Good, easy hike if you have the time, but not a must see. The best view is from the viewpoint at the trailhead. Parking lot was empty toward mid-day.
Fun place to play on the beach. Sand is coarse, so not good for sand castles, etc., but kids still had fun. Great place to fly a kite.
Fun patch of road that's not too far out of the way, which is good because it's too short to be worth going much out of your way for.
Really neat place with a mix of memorabilia, aircraft and classic cars. They made it fun for the kids with an "I Spy" game.
Water features are very nice to have on warm days, even if it takes awhile for us to drive here.

If you like Pinots and Syrahs, this is the best winery we know in the funk done of Santa Barbara for these. The tasting room is not pretentious but still has an upscale feel to it, thanks to the good taste of the items for sale in addition to the wines. $15 gets you a tasting of 6 wines. The pourer who helped us today was very knowledgeable about the vineyards, the choices made by the wine maker for each wine including the reasons behind the choice of specific clones . He also provided good insight into the tasting notes to expect. The place is welcoming and you can easily  engage in conversation with other wine enthusiasts, as the space is just the right size.

Rangers at this visitor center were much friendlier and willing to answer questions than at the West entrance one. The displays are visually pleasing and you learn the basics about the wildlife to expect. There is a small gift shop that is very popular. In the back there is an interpretive trail but it is still recovering from the fire so we didn't see as much as with previous visits, for example no quail this time although we heard some, but they used to be all over the place. The signs along the trail are meant to be engaging by telling the story of a young woman.

The 5 stars are for the beauty of the rock formations. The experience, however, depends on the time of year. If you go during the peak season, it becomes a zoo where you won't have any photo opportunities and will spend your time wondering how such a beautiful, serene site can attract loud, inconsiderate people. Go in the middle of the summer to fully enjoy. Better yet, take the backpacking trail nearby for more beautiful scenery and where you stand a better chance of observing wildlife.

Because of wisdom this path had changed a lot and can hardly be called a beach nowadays. There is a pier you can walk on, but it is taken over by fishermen who smoke, leave trash and user multiple rods so there is hardly any spot left for you to look down at the water. There  is almost no sand left anywhere, and the gray area had also shrink a lot. A few local families and sorry clubs still have an occasional party and picnic there, and during the summer you can rent kayak's and SUPs.

The views from the ruins are beautiful, but it takes only 5 minutes to walk around. The ruins are only 600 meters from the road, so it is worth it if you are on that road already. Not worth a special trip.
Update: A lot of work is being done. We were told that the owner is planning on having a tea house there at some point. The current construction includes a tower with a gazebo at the top. As of January 2019 you can still walk around the construction site.

The reserve is currently officially closed so visitors are not supposed to go there because the trails are dangerous. Eucalyptus trees have been dying & falling onto the trail. If you decide to go anyway the butterflies are still there in the winter although numbers are smaller. The problem is that since it is closed there are no docents, and some visitors with  children and dogs are making a lot of noise, ignoring the signs that ask you to be silent.

Excellent museum: each piece is accompanied by a very relevant narrative of the context it was created in. The anecdotes are interesting and facilitate the interpretation and enjoyment of the works. There is a lot of space, the lighting is subtle, soothing, and well  adapted to the atmosphere of each room. The outdoor garden  café offers good quality soups and sandwiches at a reasonable price.

The first, very short part of the trail is wheelchair accessible and  shows organized, reassembled petroglyphs all in a circle. For a more authentic experience, continue the trail to an area with huge slabs and many petroglyphs. There are signs explaining what we know, and mostly starting that we don't know much about these. Give free rein to your imagination and to your deductive skills.

Lots of shade and close to the harbor. Unfortunately, it is not family friendly as it has been taken over by boneless people who use the public bathrooms by the parking lot in a way that makes it difficult to access them. Likewise most areas of the park are used by homeeless people. Not a place to sit on the grass or lay your blanket for a picnic.

A beautiful short hike. A lot of families just go half way, to the connector trail. This takes only one hour and you cross the stream a couple of times. A lot of it is in the shade. We like to hike the whole length, up to Camino Cielo, which adds about 20 minutes and is stepper, also far less crowded if you seek more seclusion.

Artful landscaping. You feel like it is totally natural. The trail circles around the pond which has an island with two pine trees. There's also a non viewing platform. The vegetation is a mix of japanese and north western essences. The tea house was closed due to COVID29, I assume.

The pourer was very knowledgeable and friendly. Fun decor based on Area 51. The wines are disappointing. We bought one white blend, mostly to make the pourer happy. One of the red s was so pungent I could not finish it. Still a fun place to visit for the atmosphere.

After exploring all the beaches of the Kohala Coast, this one is probably my favorite one. He doesn't get all the hype of kapuna beach for example but it is definitely as beautiful and the sea is usually dead calm, so the swimming is very easy and pleasant there.

The national Park service has been doing a fantastic job preserving this Jewel. The boat concessioner, Islands Packers, is amazing too. They offer several kinds of excursions and you learn so much while enjoying the scenery!

Small, pretty and secluded even though it is very close to the trail. I was not able to experience the water because it is a big jump and I am told that the water is cold and it is a little difficult to climb back out

It has become so crowded that even when you're able to park the place had lost all it's serenity. You have to spend your time authoring not to photobomb . You are surrounded by people screaming while taking selfies.
We used to live this trail bit now it has become very crowded with hunters and backpackers who speak loud and camp right by the trail. How could such a pristine, quiet trail have changed so fast?
Very touristy. It is horrendous, a scar in the beautiful surrounding landscape, but worth a visit just to see what strange humans are capable of in the name of their religious beliefs.
Nice display, although not very big. The explanation about the two desserts is simple and clear. Good gift shop with all the good books about the fauna, Flora, , hiking and climbing.
Great views, very pleasant trail, overlooking the seals' testing beach. I took off one start because I would like it to be longer and take over the oil company agree.
Crowded and close to the road, do not a very seen experience. It is a convenient beach if you just want to get into the water and be able to park close.
Short walk, beautiful scenery. It gets crowded around sunset as the local campers are back at that time and  walk around.
Beautiful little park. My favorite thing to do there is watch the numerous turtles in the pond by the entrance.
Viewing nature from a loop trail. Dog's are not allowed so you stand s better chance to see a bobcat or coyote.
Lots of places to eat and souvenir shops, candy store for the kids, very cheesy but that's part of the fun

We loved this stop. It has a quiet beauty to it that makes me want to come back. Being in the remnants of a giant volcano is amazing enough for me alone. Add to that the vast meadow/prarie that is full of wildlife and it only gets better. We could have sat down in a lawn chair and watched the prarie dogs for a long time. We saw elk, birds, and a lone coyote. I wished that I had my fishing pole.  The backdrop of forested lava domes reaching thousands of feet above in the distance added to the drama of the landscape. The sky treated us to July clouds that were massive and magnificent. We walked around the island and enjoyed every angle. My short visit left me wanting to come back to explore deeper into this wilderness. I had only planned for a short stop there but I recommend slowing down to enjoy the peace and splendor that lives here. Definitely stop in the nature center, the staff is amazing.

This is the place to spend time with.e in Santa Fe. We visited during July and there was always something going on. Whether it was live music, dancing, or a car show, there was something to see that made life a bit better. We made this our evening walk for the week. On the few times there wasn't an event there was still plenty to see and do. Take your time here. Enjoy the food, beer, people and historical feel of the square. Sit down and watch the people, their dogs, the clouds.  Buy from the galleries, shops, or street vendors. It's a place that makes you want to stop and smell the roses.

The boat ride was good and the two crew members were amazing and friendly. The captain, however, was not. My son got nervous when crossing the rolling ramp and tried to side step it. He made a comment, "there's medicine for that." So instead of remembering the views and experience on the water, we remember the snide comment to an 11 year old boy. There may be medicine for impulsivity but there's no medicine that helps a grown man who says rude comments to kids. Again, the crew were amazing at helping everyone and were super polite and attentive but the captain, not so much.

We hiked down to the bottom of the lower falls in late November on a very warm day. The trail is in great condition, easy to navigate and had very little trash and graffiti.  There are a few nice views of the canyon and a slow trickle of water in the creek. The pool at the lower falls was cold and enough to get waste deep, which was nice on this 80+ degree day.  The trail is only moderately strenuous for about 1/2 a mile as you descend to the bottom of the canyon and again when you ascend out. Don't forget the forest parking pass.

This is a great place to hike. The trails are well maintained and you have a few options for trail difficulty from flat to a tough, long climb. The nature center is great with informative displays about the geology, history and wildlife of the area. They include live and taxidermied animals. The walks and hikes include mine equipment, a shack from long ago, the Oak of the Golden Dream, a tar seep, and the remnants of a long gone ranch. Depending on the season the creek might have water and frogs.

I was a bit hesitant to take my family of four based on the price, but after going I feel like it was a very reasonable price. It was one of the best outings we've done on our trips and will be one we talk about for years to come. It's hard to describe the experience. The best I can come up with is that it's a fully immersive experience into a strange but familiar world that makes you excited to explore every nook and cranny of a maze made through artists' unique minds. Enjoy.

Each time we visit this zoo we love it. It has a quaint feel compared to others mega zoos but still has plenty to see. The feel of the zoo is definitely more like a beautiful park setting. The weather has never been too hot since it's right by the ocean. Our last visit was unique as we did the Safari overnight experience with scouts. It was a great night with behind the scenes tours and a chance to experience the zoo at night. It was worth it and the breakfast was good.

It's a very quaint park with some nice exhibits. On our visit half of them were under construction. I can tell that it's a great park and would be a 5 star stop if all was working. It's tiny compared to Sea World but we like micro zoos and aquariums.  The dolphin experience was very nice. The views are amazing and the staff is very friendly. My favorite exhibit is watching the sea turtles swim.

Great trail. The ground gets a bit uneven in several areas so ankle support is recommended. A few steep spots but manageable for most. Beautiful rocks with lots of climbing and exploring available.  It's in a very quiet area. Kids were excited that it was the same area Mandalorian filmed an episode at. Also interesting to see the Boeing/1957 Nuclear Melt Down site nearby.

This is not a huge museum, but it is a great one. We spent about an hour and a half taking in the painitings and sketches. Some of her most iconic work is in there. You can get close enough to them to see the brush strokes. Along the way you learn about her life and the creative stages she went through. Even my 10 and 15 year old had positive thoughts about the museum.

We had a good time doing the secret island excursion through Kualoa Ranch. Use of the paddle boards and kayaks were included. The beach was like a post card you'd see representing paradise. Lots of shade from the palm trees and mangrove trees. There were hammocks and lounge chairs as well as back yard games to play. I wish it could have been longer.

It's an amazing park to visit. The main walk is not too difficult. Exploring the caves by climbing the ladders was a good time. Being among the remnants of the homes was impressive. The best part was climbing up to the 140 foot high alcove. I'd go here again. We got hit by a sudden monsoon rain storm. It passed quickly but it did cut our day short.

The scenery is beautiful and there's a good variety of trail difficulty for such a small open area. There are flat trails you can stroll on, moderate hills for a view and steep trails for the adventurists. The coyote trail is very steep and easy to slip on. Lots of fox tails. Our dog got several stuck in her paw.

I spent a little over an hour walking around the island near the visitor's center. In that small walk we saw elk, prarie dogs, birds, and a coyote. I left wishing I had brought backpacking gear and a fishing pole. I want to return to explore the back country area of this amazing geological feature.

Putting all politics aside for a minute, this is a beautiful park with plenty of family friendly things to do. The exhibits, shows and rides are fun. The park is well maintained and very clean. I don't like that they started charging for things like the sky bucket ride, though.

Nice hike. Short trail with no serious elevation gains.  Good chance that you will see deer, snakes, and frogs if there is any water.  1.5 miles in is a rock wall that is about 6 to 8 feet high. It's a good turn around spot but you can climb it and go on if you want.

Great park that is well maintained. It has a good.playground for kids and still has lots of open space for frisbee, football, catch, and more. The picnic pavilion is a good size. We held a team party there. Walking is great to do here.

The stadium feels new again. It's a gorgeous setting for baseball. Yes, it's pricey and the food can still use some improvement compared to other stadiums but it's so much better than what it was just 10 years ago.
This dog park has a huge amount of room to run around. There are tons of dogs having a great time. Owners watched their dogs well. Plenty of scoopers were available. It's a park worth going to.
It's a good stop if you are in the area. It's free and has nice views of the harbor and downtown.  You can watch planes take off from the airport and there are plenty of eateries nearby.
Enjoyed the swimming holes. Trail is in bad shape after rainy winter. Very rocky with creek crossings that make wet feet unavoidable. Probably will be dry in a few weeks. Pretty canyon.
A beautiful place that's way too crowded for the Rocky and slick path during this time of year. When dry I would call this an easy hike. Add the mud and this becomes a moderate hike.
It's a great experience to see among the fish. It's a beautiful setting. Way too crowded but I don't know that there's a way around that.
Tucked away in a nice neighborhood.  Good playground.  There's a group of teens who get a bit obnoxious in the parking lot.
I didn't cross to the island but the visitor center was one of the best I've been to. Love the look out tower.

We visited in winter and it was quite disappointing. Place is definitely beautiful, well maintained and original. Visit is really short as it takes not more than 45 min to see everything. Explanations on the map are very light and tours would help a lot improve the experience. Most of the buildings were closed or empty, having some exhibitions or a tea room would be great. At 10$, it seems overpriced in comparison with Filoli (more expensive but more things to do) or Villa Montalvo (free). I guess going there in spring during blossom period might be different.

A must see in Northern California ! This historic state park properly highlights the place Jack London lived with his wife. You can see the cottage and ranch where he tried different techniques to improve agriculture in the area. Then you can do the short hike (0.6 miles one way) to his grave site and the Wolfe house. This is his dream house that got destroyed by fire three weeks before he was supposed to move in.

Great place to visit with young children. The geyser is nice even though not massive. Explanations are simple but clear, the mini museum on the right is great to learn the basics of geology. There is an area with goats and lama that kids will enjoy. Plenty of picnic tables with shades so it is recommended to bring your own food and spend a few hours there.

Very good spot if you are travelling with young kids. They have a large collection of old trains, you can approach them and even get inside. The place also features a few interesting exhibits. There are a few tables inside to you can picnic there. The only inconvenience is that it's close to the highway to it's always a bit noisy

Great small train museum where you can see some old engines and learn more about California railroad history. With Covid, you cannot enter the hangar anymore which means you can observe the trains from very close. The train is still running and you can ride it for 45 min and approx 20$ per person.

We went there early in the morning and it was not crowded at all. While it is funny to see all the stars in the ground, the place is very dirty overall and not well maintained. There is only very expensive parking options in the area so it's better to go there using public transportation or Uber.

Very impressive area and with good amenities, suitable for buggies and wheelchairs. It was really crowded since we were there on Memorial day week end and parking was a headache. The walk from Sherman tree to Moro rock is a nice trail in the forest accessible to most.

Amazing park, this is a must see if you are in the area. Reaching the canyon is a 30 miles drive from the north entrance but it totally worth it. If you are not an experienced hiker just go for a short 3 miles walk around zumwalt meadow till end of the road.

Great area in the middle of Mount Diablo state park. It's a perfect picnic stop with great views over the rock blocks and the valley. Rocks are good for the kids to climb and this is relatively safe as long as there is proper surveillance from adults.

Great parc with great amenities. We did the summit road from Rock City, there was water and toilets every two miles on the way up. There is not too much shade so important to have sun cream and hat for summer time. All the trails were clearly marked.

This should be a mandatory detour if you are driving to Vegas. The visitor center is full of information about the Mojave preserve and also the history of the railway. Kudos to the two rangers who were particularly helpful and friendly.

Great stop on the 395. It's probably better to go there during summer as it gets pretty cold during winter. There is a small film telling the story of the town otherwise it's free exploration to discover the different buildings

A must see if you are in SF especially if you have kids. Just watching the sea lions is a show by itself since they are jumping, swimming and playing together. Place is also extremely respectful of them.
Great place, totally worth the trip if you are in the area. We took the upstairs suits tour and it was awesome. Guide really took a lot of time to answer questions and share multiple anecdotes.
Great visitor center to understand better the death valley history and environment (and also refill your water bottles). It worths planning a 30 min stop there during you death valley trip.
It's not really a "museum" more of a collection and a small store. That being said the collection of old mining tools, tractor etc worth it especially if you are traveling with kids.
Small park around the Coit Tower, it's heavily suggested that you walk up to the tower through the park (if you can). It's a few steps and it gives you gorgeous views over the city.
Awesome viewpoint over San Francisco ! Special greetings to the staff as well who is extremely nice and very eager to help or just talk about their city.
Great stop if you are in the area. You can walkthrough the bridge and also discover some of the short trails around. There are also several picnic spots.
Nice park with beautiful views over the bay. You can start a loop from there of approx 8 miles, suitable for walking, running of cycling.
Great spot to walk. Good views over santa Cruz, some shopping and eating spots. Don't miss the sea lions playing at the end of the wharf.
A good stop if you are in the area to see and walkthrough the bridge. There are also different short trails and picnic areas around.
Great spot with long and quiet beach. You can also get a fire permit with the rangers and then just have your fire on the beach.
Lots of great hikes in this park. I particularly recommend the Oak summit from which you have gorgeous views over the area.
Great park with nice hiking trails. There are no many open areas though so not so many view point to observe the valley.

Wow..wish I could give it more stars.  A very interesting and eye opening experience.   Living in this area many years never knew I had such a very decent museum in my back yard.  The exhibits are interesting and full of information.   The gold watches make me want one.  How time began and from that point until now is truly breathtaking.   I would not reccomend this to children or teenagers unless they fully are aware of this magnificent place.

Best amusement park on the East Coast.  Not sure about the negative reviews I read some and figured out there are people who will never be satisfied.  My word to you stay home.  This park is wonderful and you do not pay for parking.  You do not pay for admission and it is not costly to eat or ride the rides.  They have the best Banana Split in the world.  I love this park.

Tried to make it out to the National Museum ran out of time.  This is the second best.  Has a great selection of static aircraft.  What makes this museum great it is located right beside the runway. We had the opportunity to see a C-17 doing touch and goes and a C-5 taking off.  Just a great experience.

Great information on the Battle of Gettysburg.   We just visited the Museum only paid $9 for entry.  Has many exhibits on the battle decent selection of the weapons used and of the people who participated.   Well worth the money and you can also have a guide show you around the battlefield.

The crypt is amazing.  The fine workmanship and attention to detail is phenomenal.  A must see if your visiting the campus.  This is my third visit to it.  Use to have a honor hard.  But our leadership deemed it unnecessary.  For some reason traditions seem just to be fading away.

I hiked from my car to the pavilion, then gazed out onto the river.  Great view of the Susquehanna River from the Lancaster side.  For some reason the sun was out this day.  A rare occurrence in this area.  The park is very nice a great place to bring your family.

What a great place to visit and walk around.  We were driving around on Sunday and decided to check out the grounds.  Found the entrance and found our way into the Capital.  What a great place of history.

A nice place to visit.  Well off the beaten path.  If your able to the beach you can see many Horseshoe Crabs.  If they are turned over on their back and still alive turn them over and set them free...
Could not wait for the next tour.  Every hour on the hour had the opportunity to look inside very good assortment of his furniture and the story behind it.  Next time I will stay longer.
Doing work on the dam so water is out of the lake.  I actually thought there were more tree stumps in the water.  Nice place to relax and decompress.  Not sure how long it will take.
Great place to visit tourists like yourself.  A must do in San Francisco some great seafood restaurants and I saw the largest strawberry in my life here.  But, photo to prove it.
Washington is a fantastic place to visit so much culture and history.  The Washington Monument Grounds is a great starting place for your journey.
Great view of the Cemetery and of Washington.  I enjoyed the bygone era paintings and furniture.  Cannot believe how we lived over 130 years ago.
I had the opportunity to visit the inside when the Coast Guard was doing maintenance on it.  Very appreciative of them for allowing us access.
Had the opportunity to visit while chaperoning my child's field trip.  Glad to have made the trip and learn the history of this country.
This photo was taken here in  October of 1969.  Shows my love of the water early in life.  Possibly was taken earlier in the summer.
Very quiet and pleasant place to visit great view of the river and a great little spot to walk around and observe the passing ships.
Had the opportunity to visit with my fellow sailors to have a flag flown over the Foundation for one of our retiring Chiefs.
A must see if your visiting Richmond.  The view of the city and river is breathtaking.   I would like to visit at night.
Had the opportunity to re-enlist here back in 06 we had a great tour and the displays around the Pentagon are fantastic.
A great place to either enjoy the woods, lake or river.  Bring your dogs or bikes and enjoy what nature has to offer.
A great place to either enjoy the woods, lake or river.  Bring your dogs or bikes and enjoy what nature has to offer.
Wow so much to do in the Hamptons Roads  area this is a must.  Great exhibits and great static displays for all.
Took way to long for this Memorial to be established.  A great place to visit on your trip to Washington.
So much history on such a small plot of land.  Glad we had him or we could still be using candles.

This is really a beautiful spot, with spectacular views of of Funston Beach from the cliff. There are so many trails, with sand, eucalyptus trees, cypress trees etc. We parked at Skyline Blvd, where there is an entrance to Battery Davis, since many other cars were parked there. It turned out to be a mistake, got $106 parking violation ticket for everyone who parked there. There were no clear no parking signs. Seems like a rip off, with close to 20 cars getting tickets. So be careful about parking.
However we had a great time hiking, trail is dog friendly, in fact dogs are off leash. From the cliff you can view Funston beach to Ocean beach, it's a remarkable sight. Highly recommend this place.

We had a great time visiting Mori point. There are several trails but all of them are short hikes. Some trails have steep climbing to reach top of small hills. You can view Pacifica Pier from here. It is fun to watch waves crashing the shore and rocks in the ocean. Great place to enjoy the sunset. Only downside is, parking lot is very small, fortunately for us we were able to find street parking. Place was reasonably crowded, folks were walking their dogs on the trail. There were few portable toilets near the parking lot. Highly recommend this place for taking stroll along the coast line, exercise or walk your dogs!

Death Valley is a long drive from San Francisco Bay area, where I live. This was a 4 day trip to the National park. With 4 days we had enough time to cover important tourist spots and also do some hiking as well. The view of road to Death Valley is Spectacular, you must capture this shot on the way to death valley.

We did a hike from Zabriskie Point through Golden Canyon. Some of the key places one can visit in death valley: Masquite Sand Dunes, Artists Drive, Dante's View, Bad Water Basin, Scottie'e Castle, Ubehebe
Crater, The Racetrack!

This is a go to hiking place if you live in Cupertino, Saratoga and near by areas. There are plenty of trails here. Place is generally busy. Even though there are lot of parking, it can be hard to find parking in the mornings, since it  is a extremely popular hiking spot. PG&E trail is one of the popular trails. You can bring children to show farm animals, there is a picnic area near the farm as well. Great place to visit if you are a hiking enthusiast.

This is really nice place for hiking. Specially if you go around sun set time, you can see entire silicon valley. Depending on the clouds you may end up catching spectacular sunsets. There is a reasonably big parking lot near the trail head, you will generally find parking there. There are several trails, there is a trail which ends up in view point, where you can see entire bay area, on a clear day you can even see San Francisco and Oakland skyline.

This is a must visit place if you are a tourist in San Francisco. It is fun driving through Crooked Street which has 8 hair pin bends. Street has so many unique and beautiful houses on it. You should visit during hydrangea blooming season, road looks even prettier. Street is always busy, finding parking can be challenging. However, I highly recommend to park and take a walk on the steps on either side of the street.

Very popular place in San Diego. This is right next to USS Midway Museum. Statue is very tall, you can see it from USS Midway as well. You will find lot of tourists taking pictures here. It is a challenge to get a picture without having a stranger in your photo! There is a grass area near the statue where we relaxed a bit after the visit to USS Midway. A nice place to visit!

You can get to here from Lands End Trail. You need climb down the steep steps from the trail. Once you reach here you will find the maze created using stones. You can enjoy spectacular view of Pacific ocean and Golden Gate bridge from here. Place can get windy and chilly, so dress in layers.

This is a very nice hiking area off of 280 on Edgewood rd. We visited during spring. There were lot of wild flower blooms along the hiking trail. We also saw several deer on our trail. It is a huge area, with several trail options. A great place for hiking and enjoying nature.

A great place to take a walk and enjoy several seafood Restaurants, gift shops. You can take Whale watching trips or sailing trips in Monterey bay. There is ample paid parking. You can also find 2hour free parking on the side streets. Must visit place in Monterey bay.

This is a must visit place during Monarch butterfly season. We really enjoyed the visit here. You can walk around the Eucalyptus grove, there were so many monarch butterflies hanging from the tree. Path eventually leads to the beach. Great place for nature lovers.

Very nice place to visit. Don't forget to take your camera. Location is spectacular to photograph. Swimming pools are amazing. Views from here are breathtaking. You need to take a bus from parking lot, depending on the tour you take. Highly recommend this place.

This is a popular tourist attraction. This is where tourists come to visit Hollywood walk of fame. Theater is a place for Movie premiers. You will several people wearing costumes and entertaining tourists. Nice place to walk around and experience Hollywood Blvd.

This is one of two beautiful Windmills in Golden Gate Park. It is well maintained and there is a small garden around the windmill. Best visited in spring, to enjoy the tulip blooms and capture some pictures. Gives a little bit of Holland effect in San Francisco!

Nice place to enjoy nature. This place has several historic buildings. There is a community garden located in this preserve. Nice place to take a stroll in the preserve. There is a parking lot in the preserve, there is ample parking spaces generally available.

This is a very popular trail in Rancho San Antonio preserve. Difficulty is mid to high. There is steep inclination at the beginning of the trail. Slowly keeps gaining height till the 3rd PG&E tower. Once you reach the top you can enjoy the view of south bay.

Located right behind Evergreen College. Very nice place for hiking and jogging. Several high schools run their cross country tournaments here. There are lot of up and downs in the trail. Good for cross country running. There are several trials as well.

Really enjoyed visiting this Museum. Museum is beautiful and well maintained. There is a restaurant inside which also has outside seating.
Also has very good collection of art. Another bonus on Saturday's admission in free for bay area residents.

This is a must visit place on anybodies Las Vegas trip. Lake is huge in front of Bellagio, this is where you can enjoy the Musical fountains of Bellagio. It is fun to watch both during the night as well as day time. Don't miss these fountains!

This is very interesting small town south east of Reno, Nevada. They have an annual event of Camel, Ostrich etc races held in the fair ground here. Town has Victorian buildings built in early 19th century. An Interesting town to visit indeed.

Pigeon Point Light house is located on Hwy 1, 20 Miles south of Half Moon Bay, CA. You can really enjoy the beautiful coastline. The pictures were shot during one of the anniversary events, where light and sound show was displayed.

Beautiful lake in San Francisco city. Nice place to jog/walk around the lake. You can also see several birds here. Only sad thing is people leave trash on some of the trails. Hope people can avoid throwing trash on the trails.

Very nice park where you can relax and enjoy the ocean view. Nice place for picnic. A great place to watch the sun set as well. There are tall palm trees around the park, which enhances the beauty of this park.
One of the beautiful white sand beaches in Northern California. Beach is very popular and it can get very chili even in summer. Very close to 17 Mile drive in Monterey, CA. A must visit place.
Nice little park near Embarcadero, you can enjoy the view of Ferry building. There is play area for kids. Great place for picnic or just relax.

The Grassy Knoll is a scary and impressive place because of the terrible drama that took place there formerly. I have never understood why on November 22, 1963, no one was able to clearly see the killer hidden behind the Grassy Knoll as the Dealey Plaza is really tiny. For proof, to find it the first time, I had to use Google Map.

Malibu Bluffs Park has made me feel good because there is everything we need for a good time - sports fields, a playground or benches to relax. Not to mention the toilets and the picnic table. In addition, this park is really clean, quiet, and has a breathtaking view of the Pacific Ocean.

Cloud Gate is a sculpture opened in 2006 and is probably the most popular tourist attraction in downtown Chicago. As proof, it is almost impossible to take a single photo with it. I would also like to say that the meaning of this work of art is difficult to interpret.

Normally I don't like museums a lot, but California Science Center was really interesting, entertaining, and it was free. Moreover, on the ground floor, there is a restaurant and a gift shop. When it will be possible for me, I will come back for sure.
