The Ernest Hemingway Home and Museum is too small, the price is too high ($ 16), and also the owner seems not polite because in his answer he forgot to tell me hello or thank you, and even when we own The Ernest Hemingway House, we have to be polite.

It was difficult to enjoy my visit to Bryant Park because there were a lot of people due to the Christmas market, but this small park was very nice and conveniently located between Time Square and the New York Public Library.

The Venice Public Arts Walls is the ideal place for an artist who wants expressing his talent in front of a large audience. However, your work will not stay long because the walls are repainted regularly.

Soldiers and Sailors Memorial Arch is an imposing and beautiful monument located to the entrance of the Prospect Park; moreover, in December I especially liked the Christmas tree in front of the arch.
USS Constitution was built and launched in the late eighteenth century. His visit was very interesting and informative for me because it allowed me to discover how the sailors lived at that time.
When I visited this place, Aquatic Park Cove was under construction, so no benches available to take a break here; however, the view of Alcatraz Island and the Golden Gate Bridge was splendid.
Wonder View Trail Head is the highest and most beautiful summit of the Hollywood Hills is at the end of the trail, but beware the trails are in bad shape and there is no way to get water.
George Washington was an American political leader, military general, statesman, and Founding Father who served as the first president of the United States from 1789 to 1797.
National Christmas Tree is the best place to see the President's Park. Unfortunately, this park is currently used by a person not at all recommendable and pleasant to see.
I like Exposition Park because there are plenty of things to see inside: the Rose Garden, museums, the Memorial Coliseum, and USC that is just on the other side.
The Library of Congress was opened in 1800 and contains more than 38 million books, so someone who wants to read them all must have more than one life.
St. Patrick's Cathedral is the most famous and most beautiful religious building in NYC by his high, his size, and his beautiful architecture.
The best things to see at Grand Army Plaza are the William Tecumseh Sherman Monument, the Pulitzer Fountain, and of course the Plaza Hotel.
Soldiers and Sailors Monument was erected in 1877 to pay tribute to Massachusetts soldiers and sailors who died in the American Civil War.
Boston Common is a huge but basic park where there is almost nothing interesting to see. In addition, the lawns are not well maintained.
Corral Canyon Park is now a pile of ash and there is nothing to see because the fire has destroyed everything and I find it really sad.
If you like to skate, Venice Skate Park is the best place at LA for this and maybe in all the USA. In 2014, I saw Justin Bieber here.
The park around The La Brea Tar Pits and Museum could be more maintained. Moreover, the museum seems beautiful, but a bit small.
Venice Sign is the entrance door of Venice Paradise. Tourists should see it not only during the day but also during the night.
The SS Jeremiah O'Brien is a freighter built in 1943 and has participated in the Second World War in Europe and the Pacific.
Excellent place to walk, but I prefer to do this on the beach with my feet in the sea water.

This place is fantastic! Beautiful drive to the trail head, and a mostly paved path till you get to the canyon. Along the path you will come across the cutest, cozy, quaint cottages. I assume they are for rent? I've seen young, the old, and those with very small kids hike this. Large rocks let you know you are getting close to the falls. Its maybe 3 or 4 miles total? A fun way to spend a few hours. Donkeys and goats are near the parking lot, but beware, after hours the owner is not friendly about you petting them. There is a general store also located by the parking lot, but the hours are unknown. Totally recommend going!

Blew my mind! Its Large, extremely clean, and easy to navigate. The $30 entrance fee is worth it ( that pass is good for 6 additional days). Go in the winter and hike with great weather.  Its almost impossible to get lost here and the whole landscape feels like you're either on the moon, or a movie set. Bring food and lots of water as there are no known drinking fountains ( unless you use the sink at the bathrooms. Or stop at the general store in the visitor center). Also, don't forget proper walking shoes, and sun blocking apparel.

WOAH! That was unexpected. You drive up this very narrow road, barely two cars can pass. Up, up, up you go, along the windy mountain. The trees get large and shady. Then.. BOOM. putt over ( because there is no parking lot) and there you are.
The caves are fenced off but you can see past the gate to take a look at some very old art.
SAGE ADVICE: wear hiking shoes. There are MORE CAVES up an extremely seep hill, maybe a 500 yards walk - but flip flops aren't safe, or stable in any way. ( trust me, I tried)

You wouldn't expect something so prized to be a free museum. The collection is very well thought out. First floor is very colorful, second floor has a hidden room that is worth being taken to. The extremely large sculptures are definitely worth taking your time looking at. The fonts are rare for calligraphy. The staff is very passionate and knowledgeable about the how's and why's. All for free! Do yourself a favor and pop on in.

This place hosts a beautiful view of the rolling hills, city scape and flowers. I think I'm even more impressed by the guy in the wheelchair begging for money. He is there often. How did he get up the extremely steep hill? How does he get back down? Does he make better money up here? So many questions. The crowning jewel has been the man with the accordion. He gives the nights a romantic twist with his lovely music.

Sage advice- Go in the winter. It allows to walk to grounds with peace. As a whole, its alright. Some instantiations are clearly not kept up with, so you're left to wonder if this is the original state, or is this just a garbage pile. Others are well crafted and ornate to look at. Loads of political/ racial art to take in.  Don't touch unless you have your tetanus shot.

Tide pools to see some amazing sea life, awesome and colorful rocks to bounce around on, and waves for days. Pro tip is bring tennis shoes to help navigate the rocks. If you walk around the bend of the cliffs, you end up at the bottom of sunken city (bonus for avoiding the sunken city cliffs)
I bring everyone from out of town here and they absolutely love it!

The map makes it look like a flat surface, however, walking to the "lake" (it's small, like a tiny pond) is a steep hill. Not for wagons, rollerblading or wheelchairs. The view from the top is of downtown and the hills. The pond is fantastic if you want to fish. It's stocked full of varying sizes and turtles.

When I went it was packed with a filing crew. The road was extremely congested all the way around. Even if you could stay a while, the water and setting looks identical to peanut lake in Pasadena. Neither have clean water. I'd save your time and just find something else to do.

The grounds are very well maintained. They are open to the public. Sometimes the house is rented for weddings or events so that's a nice venue option if you're looking for one. Aroma of pine trees when walking around. Historic looking house. Just beautiful.

Parking is really hard to find, so be prepared to walk a few blocks. This is a fun place for people watching. It's selfie central. It's a very large and well maintained collection of antique street lights. Looks wonderful at night.

Its like Alice and wonderland, or the Huntington Library... but for kids. Currently the indoor space isn't open, but I'm extremely thankful they have shade, and lots of it with the outdoor spaces. These summers are HOT.

Brand New EVERYTHING! Its beautiful. Bathrooms, basketball court, concessions, playground, and grills. This place is Beautiful. They even redid the dog parks (big and small). Long time  building, but so worth the wait.
It's $5 to go in. It's all out doors so if it's hot out, bring an umbrella for shade. It's self guided so you carry a white book around and look up the info yourself. Lots and lots to at here.
It's okay. Sorta underwhelming. It needs something.. Or feels like it's missing something. I did appreciate how each room is an Asia territory. It's good to go when admission is free.
I didn't expect to get a view like that. One trail leads right up the steep hillside. The view is amazing. The flies that buzz around you are not. Not a bad place to go for sunset.
It's pretty and the dive to this location is gorgeous. The main springs were flooded out due to too much rain that season, but the one spring available was Allright.

Easy to find, and fun to see.
A great mission statement, with a rainbow blast to the corneas. Very cool gift shop  and lounge in the basement.
Parking is tricky, the crowds are thick on the weekends. It's worth a peek into the cement former glory of yesteryears tinsel town.
Great anytime of year. From taking an inflatable tube down the creek, to walking those paths. A must see for out of town guests.
A great place to go to see the well groomed landscapes and climb the tower. All are free to do, and come with stunning views.
Interesting stories, but by the end it was a real bummer. Its a real eye opening experience to see what people lived like.
Pro tip: Go in the summer months at sunset to see the biggest dragonfly that fill the sky for a short bit. Its gorgeous!
This place is cool! Its not open late, but i bet at night it boasts the best views. Would recommend.
For an event it's not so bad of an idea to get the Co workers out to see the twin Cities like this.

There is a trail to ride bikes on, run or walk on.  Tried with a scooter and it was difficult due to the crushed stone pavement.  There are great raised platforms to stop and wildlife watch on, although I did not see very much.  The Bay Trail runs through here, so hop on that to continue on an amazing adventure around the bay.  Great place to come when your kids are just learning to ride bikes because it is not to crowded.
dislikes: Difficult for scooters due to pavement type

reviews_attraction.text: Wear my kids out here.   As of Sept 2019 it is 50% closed due to construction though, so be aware.   Have also seen the staff smoking crack out back several times while waiting to pick up my kids from the dance studio out back, so I would not trust them.  But like I said, the kids love it and they get worn out here.

Great place to explore...very slowly.  It is meant for quiet reflection and peaceful meandering around.   Tuesday nights there are really great concerts to come and listen to with food vendors and beer vendors.  Bring a lawn chair and enjoy great scenery and music together.

Great park for young kids.  Drove 30 minutes to get here and it was worth it, although I probably would not go again.  It does need a little maintenance as the carpets are peeling up and such, but it gets a lot of use, so I am sure they will get to it soon.

Very, very easy hike.  A little to long and boring though.  The kids complained half way through because it was so boring.  Luckily the second half had us run into some horses right on the trail so getting around them and their poop made for some adventure.

Huge, amazing park with so much to do.  Magic Bridge Playground for little ones, pickleball for big ones.  And everything in between.  Tons of room to play and park.  Parking can be busy but there are constantly people leaving so just wait a few minutes.

Have driven by here so many times but never realized how cool it was until now.  The giant banyan tree should not be missed when you are walking up and down Front street shopping or after you eat.  Very cool place.

Lots of sand trails to walk, bike and Onewheel.  Big field for doing field type of stuff.  A drone flying race course and lots of people with RC Cars.  Lots of different stuff going on here make it so interesting.

Can be a bit crowded of a beach since it is the Ritz-Carlton’s beach, but there is always a spot and the waves a really fun to play in.  Hitting the burger shack after is a great way to end the day as well.
This is the hilly side of the trail.  You will start bu going down and down so remember you will need to hike back up.  It is the more beautiful side in my opinion though.  The dam, woods, etc.
It was a fun little hike (.7 miles each way) to the drawings.  But they were not very exciting to the kids...or to me.  It was next to the hotel, so it was worth it, but would not drive to it.
I had no idea this park was here for 7 years!  It is a great spot and a lot for the kids to do.  Great place to have a small get together with other families as well.
Could only park out at the end of the road to take a picture from a distance.  Didn’t realize when it is closed you can not get close.  Go during the week!
After you have a lava flow at his restaurant, make sure you get your picture taken at his statue.  Bonus points if you have the lava flow with you.
It’s a pretty good beach for Norcal.  Only a few days a year that it is usable.  Surfing ranges from candyland on the left to harder on the right.
Great little hike to take with kids.  Gets a bit tricky for the little ones near the end, but just take your time.  We had a blast on it.
Amazing playground.  Best I have ever seen anywhere.  So many things to explore here.  Must stop for those with kids and it is free!
Parking lots are all closed now and everything is really run down and trash everywhere.  Not a place to be visiting for a while.
We get our pictures taken here every fall.  Some great places for photos.  Other than, not sure why you would come here.
This was a bizarre experience that I highly recommend with kids.  We took our 8 and 5 year old girls and they loved it.
Great tiny beach that you earn your way too.  Great snorkeling and clear water.  So glad we walked over to it.
We call this the secret park because it took us so long to find.  Great little park with a water playground.
Tiny little area with a tennis court.  There is a cross country area, but that is not open to the public
A huge place to explore and camp at.  You need to be with a Palo Alto resident is the inly downside.
Decent place to start a Onewheel ride as you can go north or south and there is plenty of parking.

I had to look twice and then again to make sure I was reading the signs right that kept popping up on a highway running parallel to death and directly into something much worse.

"SONNY BONO'S SALTON SEA... " I said to myself frantically trying to figure out a way to roll up the electric window after blowing its fuze because I could taste the sulfur outside start to come in.

"What a strange place to attach your name to. " I thought, as an erie feeling of a time that wasn’t anymore swept through my idea of what kind of place this road was leading us to.

A once hot and heck of a good time was sure to be had during the family vacation for two weeks at the Salton Sea. At least that's what they used to say, until the fish started dying. Some say the water is full of poison out from under the earth where this man made once paradise in the dessert now barely serves as a suitable mirage before checking out. Others subscribe to the belief this is all the ignorant doings of Mexican waste management streamlining an ocean of Hepatitis into our sea to capitalize on the inevitable tourism bucks it's absence would surely have brought.

All of this is part of the reason I'm asking myself the question :

"Sony Bono?... I got you ba--"

"BABE!  THERE IT IS! " Exclaimed my girlfriend with fists gripped under knuckles white gripping that Hyundai steering wheel and turning into a gravel road.

Sonny Bono's nature preserve was down a little further on the road and the last thing I drug us all the way out here to see. Obsidian buette and the active volcanos out in the heart of the sulfuric boggy air is why the next two hours were spent exploring just that and building up quite the sweat and thirst to go with it.

Lucky for us once we made it back to the road and got moving at a respectable MPH again an old friend thought it decent to say hello one more time:

SONNY BONO'S SALTON SEA... NEXT STOP

To make a rediciloiusy long review a little shorter I'll just sum it up by telling you we stopped at his little place in the middle of nowhere past active volcanos and I wasn’t surprised.

Mr. Bono had all the stuff our sweaty body's and thirsty mouths could ever want and the cost was nothing more then having the common sense to know how to use the hose well enough to make it shoot a little water back in return.

You got me babe!

Thanks for the hose water, completely random walkway to most pointless telescopes in World and no visitors so I could pee off the random walkway next to the most pointless telescopes ever.

I got you babe!  Or at least i thought i did...

When it comes to courthouses and my opinion of them I'd have to say that this one is the tops!  I've been to a lot of courthouses so trust me when I say this one's at the top.  The ones at the bottom aren't nearly as open to the photosphere I took that accompanies my thoughts or for that matter, having thoughts or thinking that I matter but before I get off track let me tell you about what matters.

The Landscaping around the Magnificent Spanish influence of the building compliments majestic decor covering the inside.

My first and only visit to this Courthouse where I was able to see the beyond the expensive doors was when being transported from the neighbouring holding cell across the street. Even as I was duck-walking and stumbling towards the entrance in the handcuffs and shackles my future felt swell. When the middle of the day lunch hour rush on neighboring State St. a block away collided with me and began taking selfies using my life as a backdrop I should have hid my head in shame but I  didn’t.

Thank four of Santa Barbaras finest escorts with guns and itchy trigger fingers for that will to be proud of where they were dragging me towards. Life didn't make a difference in the impact the building left on me and that says a lot if it says anything at all.

It's scary to think I would almost not be mad at myself or find a need to break down in repentance on my knees to Joel Osteen on Sunday morning asking for absolvation.

I Love Magnolias,  Palm trees and a forboding police presence around every corner because I am addicted to life and all the living there is to do on this compound when in it.

This is Santa Barbara if you can make it here you can make it anywhere!  Sometimes you just gotta get here even if it the wrong way is what got you here be glad that your here and if you can make it here... Your either a millionaire or just another petty criminal stopped over on there way to Los Angeles.

I haven't been to a natural history museum since the last time I was drug out of a game of spades on the back of a school bus on another field trip to the same boring museum we go to ever year.

Growing up this semed to happen a couple times a year...Every year. That was in Denver where this all happened and during a time where life didn't look nearly as awesome as it does now; the eighties. Keep that in mind ontop of being the Alpha-kid who never let it out to the other kida that I really do like this kinda shi--

... Stuff.

Thet being said; Middle America you gotta' exhibit or two to learn from over here on the west coast to bring you out of the stone age (pun intended) and into what California has to offer.

Starting with their impressive rock and gem rooms with so many different minerals you'll have to rethink everything you thought you knew about this little Planet called earth you've been staying on for the past couple years and get with the real.

"Because, now don't quote me on the other this but there looks like some alien shi---tin there."

The icing on the cake or crack in the rock as a junkie might say it is the huge flawless crystal ball that will change anybody who's only had the Hollywood idea of what one truly is.

And then theres the Dinosaurs and other monsters thay were around in a time when we weren't because we weren't shiii- towering above anything back in those days when out knuckles drug the ground except for when dancing around fire in Caves.

There are two giant rooms showcasing more animals that would love to eat the shiiiii-- tar out of us the first chance they got if ever we found ourselves close enough to watch them in their natural habitat like the museum allows.

To get observe and look very briefly into world's were not able to to do otherwise and hopefully come away with a different take on something old that should feel brand new.

This review could be a little bias and skewed from how good the night turned out so I'll try and see it I can do it in your direction the best I can.

The drive from Culver City to Dodgers Stadium was obviously the worst part of the night beginning at the stand still bottleneck that began a little before getting on the 110,but to be positive about things I should be happy it didn't feel like starting the moment I pulled out of my driveway.

We were on our way to celebrate my dad's 66th birthday at none other than the "Guns n Roses"  concert at Dodgers Stadium and spirits were high... Along with other things but that is irrelevant here in California. I footed the bill for parking along with my buddy driving for parking at a cool thirty bucks which is pretty normal for any event in LA.

The stadium was effective and efficient in moving the cattle through the gauntlet and into our seats without need for much more than the setup already in place. Hands and signs and necks on swivel looking and Bob checking and rechecking tickets.

The entire concert was perfect and crowd around us no different. A couple isles down at one point sparked a fight with security and the people who like to drink more than enough to simply quench their thirst and we're quickly muted out of the venue.

Wisly we thought is smart to leave before the last song and by doing so we're able to avoid any traffic jam whatsoever, making it home in minutes compared to the hours it took to get there ; hence Wisly.

The one annoying part of the night were the random unauthorized t-shirt salesmen who seemed to pop in and out of nowhere in between the slowed down traffic getting in and I saw them prepping up for the same when driving out.

Normally I'm all for people bucking up against the man and earning a little tax free coin but only if the product they are hocking can stand up to the real stuff.

The Greek was a real surprise on how good it left me feeling after I made it home and had a moment to think and reflect about it in bed while waiting for my girlfriend to finish washing all the 'Concords' out from her hair that somehow got stuck in it after first taking flight earlier on in the night during the show of the 'kinda same name that we just enjoyed.

"FLIGHT OF THE CONCORDS"

This was a show that up until they were halfway finished through their opening song was still waiting for Danny Devito to pop out of the bottom of the stage in that black bowling hat and two day old wet brown chewy swisher sweet cigar until it never happened...

Because this wasn't "Its always sunny in Philadelphia!" we were enjoying but something completely different and thank God it was because I can only imagine how much it would suck to have to try and look at Danny devito from the seats we were sitting in.

I digress....

The venue was great, even though it holds 6000 people I got a real intimate feeling that few other places like this have ever been able to give me.

The parking was not a problem either, we came in late like everyone else who consideres themselves hip in the LA scene and pulled right in to a 25 dollar lot that positioned us to be out without a hitch or bumper bent when we were going to leave.

I recommend this to anybody who enjoys to have a breath of fresh air with their enjoyment of life moments because that's exactly what this is and you'll wake up a better person the next day for doing it.

I have trouble giving a Japanese "Friendship" Garden any more stars then two when nothing to do with friendship came to mind while there.

"KANEICHEUA" is not the warm far-eastern greeting I expected to hear from the lady behind the ticket booth and for good reason; as she was preoccupied in helping my girlfriend and her son buy tickets I snuck through unnoticed with my dog Lil' Heis free of charge into the unknown.

Once I was far enough into the garden Lil' Heis and I turned around and copped a quick see at the scene back at the ticket booth. To my surprise I watched the people I was with being turned around and walking back out the front gate, slumped over and now carrying something new with them previously not had before I abandoned then only moment prior...

Frowns!

The frowns on their faces showed me that I was not going to be allowed to finish my quest with a completed mark on this stage due to my compassion towards the ones I was with and the trouble they surly were in.

They turned my party my party away at the entrance because they didn't have the correct amount money on them move forward. Thus putting a damper on in our game of life and the "friendship garden"  bonus stage that includes many necessary powerups and extra lives for the unknown and dangerous Road ahead.

Apart from all that imaginative fun, from what I did see of the place I couldn't reccomend it for any price more then free.

When it comes to views and knowing where on this big Green and blue ball we are all playing on, I must confess that I could be jaded because I've seen so much better.

I'd recommend coming here and living free out under the sun and with the pacific oceans every welcome wave to remind you of the value of life just because it's a break in the routine of our ways that make up most of out days.

There is nothing at all wrong with the sunset past the mandatory pile of you's, them and all the rest of the tourist lump of this and  American life crowded in next to you to share the special moment that only takes place anywhere on earth once a day.

Earth is a place to move around and see some suns set along the shore, over some horizons and outside of the everyday sky playing on repeat nightly. That's why so many when given the chance to hold this remote find solace in the Sunset Cliffs channel--a place where beauty doesn't get taken for granted.

If you are one who has never seen a beach with a sunset over it at least anytime in life this is a must... But...

If you have seen one sunset on one beach you seriously have seen them all and where's the fun in that??
dislikes: Repetitive experience if seen similar before

reviews_attraction.text:
The moment I stepped out of our rental car and took a wide eyed panoramic look around at my new sky line circling the parking lot my mouth was open.
An infinite number of three hundred foot redwoods stood towering above my perfect height for an man at six foot and a half making me feel less adquiet then I really was.

The red skinned wonders peered down at me from so far up-away and above with cautionary eyes if I chose to be one of the unlucky soles to venture off the path into harms way and the dead branches falling from above and ready to kill someone just like me.

They were commanding thick trunks and heavy girth all the way down to the ground and me looking up silently comparing them to why black pornstars are stars-- But that could also be just because I drove up here before black pornstars and our women.

Dwarfed were the whole gang on our brisk but adventurous stroll through the tomahawk Indian scalped redwoods of the late Henry Cowell. We salute you and the gift this place truly is to anyone lucky enough to make it somewhere near wherever hear even is....

We took a wrong turn on the Bang Bus and ended up out in nature and talking to God.

This was a little gem in the midst of a lot of traffic and a nice place to think about a lot more traffic I'd have to fight through when I left.

We arrived on Thursday afternoon and found the line to get in was only three cars deep which was a pleasant surprise.

My disabled veteran's ID had us admitted  free of charge instead instead of the steep $12 stab that anyone who didn't go to war and get blown up a couple of times had to pay.

I enjoyed every part of this beach including the parts that are restricted and dont have easy access to get to them.  Im a big beach person (whatever that means) so it says a lot for me to glam on about Leo's little pile of water and sand.  Normally I have a lot to say about a lot of beaches that can be a little more on the negative side but only to encourage change, not here though.  I only have this to Leo Carrillo about his little beach.

Very peaceful very nice and did I say peaceful? Almost movieesque if they made a movie about this called esque.

Now where is Pam Anderson, the one from 1994 befoee she made that tape.

I didn't even know that this chunk of beauty balled up from a pile of wonderful and jaw dropping amazing was a park until Google reminded me it was.

It doesn't matter what label or name goes in front of this place because there is only one world universally understood that could describe what this place really is;

Envious.

For that reason alone that apart from the few in America who are able to take it for granted everyday because they live right across the street, the word Envious is a perfect one to tell the feelings of all who step foot on it and maybe end up catching a sunset or rise while there...if there lucky.

There is nothing about this park which isn't the most picturesque spot in town next to Camel and pebble beach and everywhere else in Monterrey and ....damn they lucky.

It's a beautiful place that is free to get in and will load your empty head with a pile of juicy memories that will be sure to last long after your out. Or until you make the next stop anywhere around here and they are quickly replaced.  Ciao!

I came here with my brother and his two little ones, my nephew and niece for a little time outside of the usual and home that comes with it.  I would have thought of so much more they could have made a place like this into shine but nobody told me they could have used my help and I had to figure it out on my own.  Don't get me wrong,the kids are not going to complain about the content this place has for them to play with and on but what does that say? Not much considering most kids are just as happy to get their hands on an empty bottle or unguarded dumpster full of trash...so why not try to shine through j to something so much more which any place of this stature in a town as big as Chicago should have little problem doing...so let's get it do a donde and we can be on to get with our gone and move on.

I visited here during the anti-trump protest post his election for the express reason of getting to see people at their worst believing they are doing their best and enjoying the chuckle that would surly follow.   MacArthur Park was well equipped with the necessary space and amenities it took to carry all these bolt-cutters along on their journey to be heard that morning, all ten thousand of them.  Which says alot about a park that can handle that many counter-culture individuals ontop of the usual bunch of dope dealers and crack heads milling about.  Oh and this park was mentioned on the movie Training Day for anyone who likes a bit of Hollywood nostalgia to mix up their thought a bit.

The Canals are quite the random site to see if you are used to Los Angeles and accustomed to seeing and sharing the beauty of our other canal, the LA River for the reason that they make no sense in comparison to everything else in this city.   The Canals are quite beautiful and even a little bit magical as you will find when walking amd weaving in and out what can feel like something of a maze of them.  They are also like everything else of substance in California,  heavly populated with tourists and all the selfies, group photos, team planks and Asian whatever's so don't plan on having any time to play with yourself... It just ain't gonna happen.

Manhattan Beach in itself is one of the great places to go with the family on a weekend and make you wish it was Monday from the amount of people who thought the same milling around all the off in your day.   The pier on a Tuesday on the other hand is just swell and nothing short of nostalgic for anybody who grew up next to the water... For the rest I couldn't begin to speculate on the feeling it might give to you as I only know mine.   Not the greatest of piers and like most men in America,  too short but you wouldn't know it until standing at the tip and looking down telling yourself : "meh"

Sutro Baths one of the most memorable places I could ever go in my life and for some reason it has been 30 years since last visiting. I can never seem to find time to take a bath until I was did and once I was within the Sutro Air I felt like I needed anothdr bath from all that Nostalgia my past had crashed into, on and all over me covering my senses  like one of the waves off the pacific can do here if not careful. I was left soaked, smiling and sound. I'd recommend this slice of sweet American life to anybody who has a taste for the living that can be done in it.

The landscape complements architectural piles of awesome that seem to be everywhere in San Francisco. Another thing that seems to be everywhere are people who appear to be of the street Urchin nature sleeping in parks and ruining anyone who might prefer a bed at night to grass and rot gut in the middle of the day's time planned on being spent there.

There are far too many people spread amongst this not big enough plot of park to even have a chance to try and enjoy anything about it past the eyesore homeless shik has its way of leaving on me everytime I smell it.

I had found myself sitting across from Brad Alan Grey, one a rising television and film producer responsible for co-foundeing the notable Brillstein-Grey Entertainment agency, if that says something about the man.

He kept offering to validate my parking to the lot acting a step above the rest choosing not to hear my response that I came by Uber... Or was it Lyft?

He looked at me and waited for a response that would properly thank him for a piece of paper he handed me that was in fact validation for my Lyft... Or was it Uber.

This gets an easy 5 Stars in my book for a couple reasons and both of them being part of the View and how wonderful it really is to...

Number one : Access:

The view, which unlike other places more popular with the fans of the Sun going up and down eg. Griffith Park;  Baldwin Hills doesn't make it pain in everyone's ass to get to the top of it and have a smile.

Number two:  Panoramic Beautiful.

The 360 panoramic view of Los Angeles from my location that couldn't be any more sensual.

5 out of 5 on a bad day!

A good place to stop over if one ever might find themselves in a position of expression that can only be satisfied by letting go of all that is and everything which isn't or should have never tried to be...

Beginning first with the letter P.

Exit off the half-highway Road you are probably white knuckling your way through and relax when putting it slowly I to park and exhale a sigh of relief.

Bathrooms are fully stocked and waiting to be refreshed with the letter of the day you most surly will bring onto it.

A diamond in the rough normally filled with Bloods or conflicts internally that finally is OK to take home and talk about without the LAPD knocking down my door or the Crips shooting through it ia how I would describe this place.

This is Nature in Los Angeles and the cleanest air I've huffed outside Griffith observertory in four months, take it all in and keep it for a time like this when Google will help you share the experience.

(It's a good little park for talking walks or winding down the little ones)

Everytime I end up here is another time I can chalk up  as a piece of well spent chalk written on the board of memories from my life I hope to never forget.  The cliff wall is really something to look out on in either direction and in all of its crumbling away glory as a reminder to who calls the shots on this planet; man or ocean.   I'll put my money on ocean -

Up until just  now if someone were to question me on how I'm able to do what I do everyday and fall asleep at night... My answer would be much less eloquently put after that person comes to out of the kinda daze being hit with a two by four hacksaw Jim Duggan style cirqa Wrestlmaina 2.  When Andre still had the glory at the top of the hill.

This is a great place to just come on your day off or lunch break and have a walk around the center and surrounding parks if you want a slice of peace with a smile in a day that otherwise probably lacks.
Great beach if you like to see very few people to the left or right of you and awesome views of the constant airplane show going on overhead.
I had a great time getting to take in a load of culture here and the price can't be beat at a cool free!

A last minute purchase from Groupon and my family and I set off for a day trip. On the Web a first impression is 5 stars. Great pictures, great marketing, easy to use.

Before taking off I knew that this place was located in the desert. So I was prepared for the 1.5 hour drive. What I didn't expect was the dirt road leading to the sanctuary from hwy 395. When I called they didn't mention it when I asked if there was anything I needed to know. For someone in a smaller vehicle expect a semi rough ride. Despite the surrounding area of abandoned shacks and automobiles, upon arrival it still remains a 5 star rating. The grounds are very well maintained and updated.

If you purchase guided tour tickets the last one ends by 2pm. If your visit is like mine, then be sure to arrive a little earlier because they may begin sooner then what is to be the presumed tour start time. In addition when purchasing tickets online for a tour (my suggestion) they should list tour times. I was not provided any of this information and it would have been a little more helpful. As for the tour, from what I observed, tour guides were very knowledgeable about the animals. I like how they were able to share their day to day accounts of the animals with guests. There are signs posted indicating rules and warnings. Hand sanitation is available if you have an opportunity during the tour to touch a reptile.

The outside habitats for the animals are well maintained. You will see Tigers, leopards, bobcats, falcons, llamas, alligators, piranhas, primates and other reptiles during your visit. They are sectioned off reasonably in my opinion which allows for the safety of their guests. I just wish the other tigers within the sanctuary were better placed in the sanctuary. There are some animals that are visible in the back but a much further distance.

My children had an opportunity to feed both the leopard and a bobcat. It was the best $10 spent. This part of their extreme package was worth the experience, even if it was over within 5 minutes. Although you feed the animals behind a double enclosed fence, my kids loved sharing their experience with friends and family. Overall, it wasn't a bad experience. A bit unorganized by staff but I think that was due to the lack of staff availability.

The duration should last about an hour to be fair but guests are welcome to stay longer after the tour which is a plus. At the moment, I feel like this is a place you can say "yea, I did that and it was fun!" but im just not certain it is something that I'd return to in the future. I gave this place a 4 star rating because of their negligence to communicate necessary information and because I feel it could use a little more to increase the awe factor of their establishment. I will definitely recommend this place to friends and family but perhaps my criticism / review can be used to help perfect the experience that future guests may have.
dislikes: Lack of information on tour times

reviews_attraction.text:
Pretty cool! The 6.5 mile round trip hike from Warner Springs is well worth the trip. Begin your hike along side fire station #52. From there you'll pass "The bee tree", within 10 minutes of your hike and continue along oak creek for about 1.7 miles. If you continue on about another .5 of a mile, you'll find yourself overlooking the valley where the California poppy usually highlights the landscape. For the last mile you will begin to see a variety of rock formations; continue on pass them, through the open area and no sooner will you notice the "Eagle Rock" in the distance. The 500 ft elevation gain is considered to be an easy to moderate hike. This trail is definitely kid friendly. My youngest being 5 years old, trecked 5.5 of the 6.5 miles. So any kid should be able to hang. You will see the wild turkeys, blue jays, deer or poppies during your hike. Take pictures and enjoy the view. It is well worth the hike along PCT (Pacific Crest Trail). Btw, parking is free along side the hwy. If you have time to visit the information center before your hike, then you should grab a bite to eat. They are very helpful to newcomers. Oh and don't forget to plan ahead and pack plenty of snacks and water for your hike; you will need it! Can't wait to visit this hidden treasure again.

NOTE:
One last thing for future hikers; Please be sure to discard of your trash appropriately.  This place is beautiful and I saw not one item of garbage along my hike. So lets keep it that way!

I recently revisited the 3 acre, Pio Pico Historical State Park. I was pleased to see that minor improvements to the Adobe Mansion, that once belonged to the first Mexican Governor of California, were made since my last visit several years ago.  The exhibit provides a wonderful example of how such structures were made. There are limited hands on activities that are available for children. Tours are offered when in attendance.

This park is well maintained and park Rangers are eager to greet you when noticed.  There is plenty of parking and drinking fountains can be found throughout the park. Expect to spend about 30 minutes tops, inside the exhibit and another 20 minutes walking outside the grounds. It is free to visit unless you choose to make a donation. Literature is also available in English and Spanish when touring the exhibit.  They open at 10a.m. and close by 3:30p.m. It's also great for a picnic,  exercising or walking your dogs.

This place is horrifying! It really deserves no stars but that isn't an option. This unfinished park has nothing "park" like about it. My wife and I were out Geocaching with our four children and decided to try this spot out. The following is a list of what we ACTUALLY found: 3 kids smoking pot and drinking beer, an actual drug deal and 2 prostitutional acts taking place!! My wife was terrified and we all tried to escape the "park" and found ourselves trapped behind a chainlink fence. Trash and graffiti were everywhere.We eventually escaped and walked along Idaho St. back to our car. Please trust me this place is a dangerous neighborhood blight! NEVER bring your children here!

I've been taking my kids here for years! It's a great place for toddlers. There is a variety of exhibits and lots of hands on activities for kids. Great for any imaginative and unimaginative child. The entrance fee is reasonable but the yearly pass is a better deal and worth it. Staff is great!

The museum covers a wide range of interests as their content is not limited. (I.e. - Automobiles, Theater, Archeology,  Science,  etc...) They have a revolving exhibit that is designated to one room.  The Dinosaurs outside are pretty cool!

You won't regret your visit. Enjoy!

For being a smaller museum they have been fortunate to obtain funding and donations from many which have allowed them to brings such fascinating exhibits like;

The terra cotta warriors
Egypts mummys
And many others.

This place is worth every penny. It has made our family experience enjoyable.  A very clean and well maintained museum that offers additional programs for children and adults alike.

I enjoyed our membership here. The kids liked that green screen. The presidential bedroom was neat and the guns were awesome.  There are lots of stairs, not really recommended for the disabled.  Any kid or enthusiast will love it! There are plenty of photo opportunities and the crew members are very knowledgeable about the ships history.  Definitely worth the time.

A great zoo to visit. It is small but expect to see beers, deer, American Bald Eagles, Golden Eagles, Owls,  Foxes, Wolves and more. The facilities are maintained well but I will advise being cautious of where you walk. The paths pose a risk to injury as some are unstable. Overall expect not to exceed visiting the zoo between 1 and 2 hours tops!

I rate it a "B".

By far one of the best spots to enjoy an endless amount of time playing I•Spy with your kids! There are many things to see. The light that shines through many of the bottle tree's and its objects are absolutely beautiful! I highly recommend this place to anyone traveling route 66. Make memories and have fun because you can't beat FREE!

A great park to enjoy during 4th of July for free! You can't beat that. There is plenty of seating so as long as you bring a lawn chair or blanket.  The play area is both padded and has wood chips. The equipment has been updated and is in good condition.  The restrooms are near the play area and are well maintained.

It's a great place to run, hike, walk your dogs, or mountain bike. It is tucked away in the hills behind La Serna high school. No restrooms are available but there is a drinking fountain.  There is not much parking but enough for those who frequent the park. It's an average park with few trails to take.

It's an average size park where the local youth soccer league come to practice.  The play area has both a padded area and sand around the equipment. The equipment has been upgraded in recent years. It is centrally located between a small community. The restrooms are in average shape. It is dog friendly.

I decided to try some place new a few years ago. I took the family here and they enjoyed the moderate hike to the beach. On a good day you can find seals along the buffs and plenty of starfish and eels. The caves are cool but educate yourself before heading out. Check for the tide times. Parking is $5.

I never knew about this place until a few years ago.  There is plenty of parking available.  It's really nice here and I enjoy all the coverage it provides during the hike. Definitely an easy to moderate hike depending on the trail you choose.  Duration is between 2-3 hours.

A fairly new sports park with great fields. There are several baseball and soccer fields, a few basketball courts and a small play area which is located adjacent to an elementary school.  The facilities are well maintained. Overall a great place to watch a game.

A great little park that is centrally located next to FIDM. It provides plenty of shade. Interesting lawn art and a play area for kids. It is always supervised and police frequent the area for breakfast,  lunch and diner. Restrooms could use improvement.

A well maintained park. The play area has wood chips but very clean.  It is dog friendly. The baseball and soccer fields are in great shape.  Restrooms are clean.  Kids will enjoy it as it has lots of play area access with minimal crowding.

I've always enjoyed this place since I was a kid. Lots of jelly fish and other marine life. Although the beach is not what it was 25 years ago, my kids still enjoyed it. Donation is suggested but not required. Plenty of parking.

The park has well maintained fields and play area's. The play area has wood chips but the toy equipment is updated.  The restrooms are clean. It is dog friendly.  Plenty of parking is available.  A friendly community all around.

The park is very well maintained.  It was rated #1 in one magazine for top O.C. parks. Your kids will love this cool pirate ship themed park. They will have hours of fun.  Dog friendly,  basketball court and clean bathrooms. A+

A great place to take the family. It is inexpensive and the 55 acres provide a wide array of trains to look at as well as ride. A wonderful idea and a great place to enjoy old electric, diesel and steam locomotives.

A++++

I enjoyed my first horseback riding experience here and it was fun. From what I remember service was good. No complaints other then having sore inner thighs after riding.  They take you to the Hollywood sign.
I've been here twice to watch a hockey game and a circus show. I sat in a similar area and must say that I was pleased with both performances as well as experience.  A++
They always seem to have some decent exhibits that will interest your children. A hands on place but is subject to overcrowding.  Overall a good stop!
A great place to visit! Especially during the new year celebration. It is full of fun activities such as Mexican paper cutting - Papel picado.

This place is amazing.  Kilauea's crater is massive.  It is almost impossible to overstate how large and imposing it is.  For me, it was like seeing the Grand Canyon the first time.

Also, don't miss the hike around the rim and through the crater of Kilauea Iki.  There is a self-guided tour of this hike that you can download off of the internet that will explain what you are seeing at different points of the hike.  This made our hike even more informative and interesting.

Finally, there is a lava tube near the Kilauea Iki hike that is worth seeing.  It is a short hike, and we enjoyed it.

Our first visit to this park was today.  The road to the park is mostly gravel and bumpy.  Once you get to the park, you will find palm trees, nice sand beaches and a couple of historic old beach houses.  It was; a nice place to walk on the beach and watch the waves.  It did not appear to be a good place for swimming because of the rough conditions.

11/13/2018 update (one year later):  visited another beach at this state park:  Kua Beach.  It is a beautiful, sand beach with fun waves for boogie boarding (for novice boogie boarders).

We were heading toward Hawaii's Volcanos National Park when we saw a sign that said "South Point".  We decided to explore the 12 mile road that was one lane or one and a half lanes for most of its length.  We were hoping to see what the coast looked like in this volcanic region.  Our efforts were rewarded with 50-60 foot cliffs plunging into the ocean.  This  coastline was spectacular.

Also, there is a green sand beach nearby.  We didn't go as we had time constraints, but it was about a mile from South Point.

We visited the Kilauea Visitor Center today.  It is just inside of the gate to the park, and it is well worth the stop.  There are numerous fine displays that show where things are located in the park as well as telling the history of the park.  There are, also, friendly Rangers on hand to answer question that you may have.  This is a great park, and the Visitor Center helps to make sure that you know how best to enjoy it.

Beautiful and historic church.  This is the oldest church in Hawaii.  It was established in 1820.  The exterior and interior are in good condition and interesting to observe.  Admission is free, and photos are allowed both inside and outside of the church.   There is a small area at the very back of the church where a short movie is shown talking about the church's history.

This is a very popular snorkeling venue.  There are many colorful fish, and sea turtles are often seen here.  There is a sea wall that, generally, keeps the water calm in this area.  When the conditions are right, you can also enjoy watching surfers out by the end of the sea wall.  Nice sand beach, bathrooms, lifeguards, and food trucks make for a relaxing experience.

We love this place.  The history and the scenery is amazing.  The ranger's talk explaining the history of the area is excellent.  You should attend this first before touring the grounds if possible.  The park brochure contains a self-guided tour map that makes the experience considerably more interesting.  Also, right next to the park is an excellent snorkeling area.

This area covers two of the Big Island's National Parks: Kaloko-Honokohau NationalHistorical Park and Ala Kahakai Historic Trail.  Kahoko_Honoohau National Historical Park features fish ponds, lava fields, and the historical trail.  We had walked the Ala Kahiko Historic Trail in the Waikoloa area, so it was interesting to see what it looked like in this area.

I was hesitant at first about going, because it was $20 per person.  This botanical garden was fantastic and totally worth the money!!  We went to Akaka Falls State Park and to Rainbow Falls the same day.  Both of the waterfalls were excellent, but the botanical garden was the unanimous favorite for our family.

We have lived in the area for 28 years, and this park has gotten nothing but better and better as time has passed. It is a wonderful place for a walk or to just sit and watch people enjoying themselves.  Also, it has the Seymour Botanical Conservatory in it which is a wonderful place to visit.

Great hike.  We started at the Fairfax Bridge (trail leading down from the east end of the bridge).  The hike was flat (follows the river) and there are remnant of Melmont to be seen (foundations and such).  We thought that it was well worth our time.
This lookout and the hike down into the Pololu Valley are remarkable, but you need to be in pretty good shape to do the hike as it is a steep descent/ascent in and out of the valley.

Great zoo.  We loved taking our kids there when they were young.

12/18/2018 Update:  we went the week before Christmas to see "Zoo Lights".  It was awesome!!
This bridge was built in the 1920's.  At the time it was built, it was the tallest structure in Washington.  Pretty amazing view of the river gorge below.
Great place to walk your dog or to go for a walk around the lake.  The most popular park in Puyallup - yet, it almost never seems overly crowded to us.
We had the privilege of visiting Mission Santa Cruz on our last trip to the area. It was very interesting. The ranger on staff was very informative.
Wonderful place to sit, enjoy a nice bottle of wine, and relax while appreciating the spectacular views (and, hopefully, spotting a whale or two).
Great hike around the rim of the crater and down into the crater itself.  Downloaded a self-guided tour for this hike which was really helpful.
Great place for a short - but difficult - hike up Mt. Peak (or Mt. Pete or Pinnacle Peak - I've heard it referred to by different names).
Nice, little parking area and bathrooms. A perfect spot to stop, stretch your legs, and enjoy the view of this beautiful, little canyon.
Hawaiian history, great beach, very nice showers and bathrooms, great shelter house, and the snorkeling was fun  (not great but fun).
Awesome views... the  hike to the bottom of the valley on the access road is steep (one of the steepest roads in the USA.
We had a dog with us, so we stayed to the west side of the highway. The trail was great. The beach was wonderful as well.
Love the portion of highway 410 that passes through Federation State Forest (it's like you are in this tunnel of trees).
My wife and I enjoyed the short hike to the waterfall.  Bridal Veil Falls was beautiful and well worth the stop.

For my list, I've created a bucket list of places to go. And they've been to all the zoos beside Oakland zoo. In December, one of my friends went to the Oakland Zoo with her 2 year old and family. She cognizant that Oakland zoo is not huge and not that many animals to see.  Although her reviews were stuck in my heard, I still sought to see for myself.
Entrance- At the zoo parking entrance, you have to pay $10. There were signs posted on the windows of the entrance, credit card system temporarily down and cash accepted. I pretended as if we didn't read the instruction and gave my credit card. They guy said you don't have cash. I replied, no. Then he swiped my card. I guess to speed up at the entrance, they posted those signs.

We purchased the tickets at the  zoo entrance and I kept saying to myself that should have purchased the groupon deal. It was expensive, $19 per adult without tax and for 2 year and up they charge.  I think best time to come to the zoo is in the morning. We reached the zoo at 10.30am and the parking lot was almost full. At the entrance, make sure to grab the map so you don't miss out anything. Once you enter the zoo you'll see the gift shop on your right and the flamingos directly in front of you. Near the gift shop are the restrooms and on the left is the restaurant where we ate.  The gift shop is small but remarkable,  great educational toys, t-shirts, hats, sunblock, puzzles and etc.

Outside the zoo is the Outback Express Adventure Train.  They have a train ride for adults and children that go around the zoo. Every time my daughter see the train, we have to ride. And she loved it. Our conductor did not give much information.
After paying the zoo entrance, we paid additional for the train ride. I felt everything was adding up very fast.

Wear comfortable shoes because there are steep hills in different portions of the zoo.
For the sky ride, you have to pay $ 3per person. I have 9 months old and they charged $3 for the baby. You can see most of the animals through the sky ride and it was totally worth it. I loved the newly opened Gondola ride. It had a beautiful view of the bay area. We saw elephants, giraffes, zebra, turtle, lemur, lion, buffalo, tiger and etc.

Overall, this was a great zoo and I would definitely come back when the new area is opened.
dislikes: Additional costs for train and sky rides

reviews_attraction.text:
The Japanese garden was 3 star. It's smaller than expected and you can easily walk around in less than 10 minutes. Highlight of the garden were the big koi fish.

It was the memorial weekend and they charged us $10 parking. I inquired at the entrance about the high cost. Usually it's $6, they said it's special holiday even though it was Sunday and memorial day was on Monday. Not worth it if you plan to go for the Japanese garden only.

And the Japanese garden opens on certain hours. Tea house  is located in the heart of the garden. It was closed.

1 check-in

The park is outdated and understaffed. The staffs were friendly and if they saw a line on a certain ride, they would jump  onto that rid to operate. Most of the time you'll notice the ride is ideal.You'll have to wait until the staff is available to operate the ride.

My daughter was excited to go on the rides. For a two year, all she cared was any rides. At the fun town, the first ride she wanted to go was the train ride. She kept complaining it's going slowly. But she had fun.

Rides were $2. And if you get the package deal which is 10 rides for $18.

On the carousel people had to make sure the weight was even otherwise hard for the carousel to move.
The rose garden is very relatively small. But they had beautiful roses. I wish they had more roses. My favorite roses were the pink ones..
dislikes: Limited operating hours (Japanese garden, tea house)

reviews_attraction.text:
It was my first time at this park and my kids enjoyed it.  We live in Elk Grove but after our Nimbus hatchery play date we decided to take the kids to the nearest park in Folsom. And my friend recommended this spot. This place is similar to the one in Elk Grove but infrastructure is much nicer.

The park doesn't have a big shade area or lots of benches but you can bring your picnic mat and enjoy the nice and clean playground. The park is designed to resemble the castle. It's suitable for all ages of kids.

My 9 months old son enjoyed the baby swings while my daughter enjoyed the slides and older swings. They have lots of shades at this park. The kids can play hide and seek in the park or adults can host picnic or birthday events here.

Highly recommend to those parents who are looking for nice and clean playground for their little ones.

It's a 3 star zoo because it's very small and not enough animals..

We had to pay $10 for the park entrance because they counted the day before memorial day as special day not holiday ( I guess they don't know memorial  day is a holiday)and then entrance fee for the zoo separately. You can go to the Japanese garden, fun town, zoo which is accessible with the parking entrance.

In the zoo there were no Lions, giraffe, monkeys. We drove from Elk Grove to Lodi to check out the zoo. My daughter kept asking where is the lion? Are we going to see soon. There were lots of turtles. The restroom needed cleaning.

At the end of the zoo, I asked her whether she had fun. She replied yes. Mommy where is the lion? My little two year old's zoo adventure was surely incomplete.

Here's a review on behalf of my little babies.

Great place for kids 2 and up. Well kids six months and under are free. And if you have a toddler, as a parent you'll want to burn  off their extra energy. Perfect spot for children and to host kids birthday event. You'll exhaust them.

The crafting room was perfect for my daughter. She's into art and craft. They have a area for calligraphy, kitchen area, dancing space, train room, outside bubble, hula loops and etc. If my kids were given the choice, they would have stayed here the whole day. ❤️

Today we stayed for 4.5 hours. We had to leave because the  museum was closing otherwise my kids wouldn't have left. 😊😊

Bring our wear warm clothes. This place gets cold.

The Adler Planetarium is a public museum dedicated to the study of astronomy and astrophysics. It was founded in 1930 by Chicago business leader Max Adler. It is located on the northeast tip of Northerly Island at the shore of Lake Michigan in Chicago, Illinois. The Adler is America's first planetarium and part of Chicago's Museum Campus, which includes the John G. Shedd Aquarium and The Field Museum.

My sister and I had a great time exploring and learning about planetariums. And they have interactive stations. If you have the city pass, then you can come here as well.

The have beautiful beach outside to walk around and  gift shop.

A great educational place to bring kids.

On Sunday, we went to the fairytale town for a birthday party. It was in the garden area. The kids had so much fun watering the plant. Another fun activity they did was color the paper and paste outside their pot plant. And they grew some type of pea ( the young girl helping was unsure what type of pea exactly it was). Anyways, the kids had tons of fun and they had a chance to explore the fairytale. If you read fairytale stories then you'll be visit this place. We ordered chicken tenders from the food court and it was horrible. Take your own food.

It's a small little train town but my 2.5 year old enjoyed a lot. She thought it was the best thing in the world. And she enjoyed all the rides even though my husband thought it would be scary for her.

You can easily spend 3 hours with the kids here. And they have a train ride that takes you into the woods and let you feed lamas. They say the train ride is 20 minutes but I think it's only 5 to eight minutes ride and mostly spend time with lamas. But kids don't know the time when they are having a blast. Highly recommend if you are in the area.

The Vista House was built in 1917 on one of the most beautiful scenic points on the Historic Columbia River Highway. It was constructed to provide travelers a place to rest and refresh themselves as they made their way down the magnificent Columbia River Gorge. The view of the Vista House on a clear day is beautiful, along with peering out into the scenic view of the Columbia River Gorge! Inside, there you go through a historic timeline.
Definitely a fantastic place to stop on your travels along the Columbia Gorge.

If you going to Maui, add this place on your itinerary. It's a special place vibrates with stories of ancient and modern Hawaiian culture and protects the bond between the land and its people. The park also cares for endangered species, some of which exist nowhere else. Go visit this special place, renew your spirit amid stark volcanic landscapes and sub-tropical rain forest with an unforgettable hike through the backcountry.

Going up the mountain, my son and I had ear pain. Stunning view from the top.

This was my favorite beach. View were the greatest here.

Goat Rock Beach is located between Goat Rock Point and the Russian River along the Sonoma County shore near the town of Jenner. There are two parking lots for Goat Rock Beach. One is at the north end of Goat Rock Road with easy access to the sand spit at the mouth of the river and the other is right below Goat Rock itself. The ocean here is part of the Russian River State Marine Conservation Area so fishing is prohibited.

One of the best Art museums here in Sacramento.  The first time I visited this museum as part of a paper for my class. They change art often.

Parking:  street parking which is metered. Don't forget to add money to increase time otherwise you'll get a surprise waiting on your windshield.

Floors : is 3 floors and they have a cafeteria. So take your time exploring

Free days : if you have BOA card on certain days. If not, pay $10.

Overall the place is clean.

If you've been to other zoo's like SF or San Diego then you'll find this zoo small. Although for adults we think there is not much to see or it's small but from a little kid's perspective it's big. The facilities look well maintained

I'm happy to have this as our local zoo to take our children. They have lions, giraffe, flamingo's, etc. They also have a small little café area.
They have street parking and the zoo offers membership

I felt like a little kid here, I was amazed with all the sea animals. My daughter loved the fishes.

Some of the unique fishes were the frog dish.

The Shark tank has a tunnel which is beautiful. Great places to take pictures.

If you are from California and have been to Monterey bay aquarium then you'll be disappointed. This is very small and no as many sea creatures. And the price is almost the same.

The painted ladies are Victorian and Edwardian houses and buildings painted in three or more colors that embellish or enhance their architectural details.This is a landmark of the San Francisco.

One of the houses were used for the TV series, full house. A popular tourist destination.

Parking : street parking but it can difficult to search for an empty spot.

We took our kids and they loved it. They have observatory area, my daughter enjoyed examining the rocks and sands, watching the boats from the big windows, experimenting different objects. Although the entrance fee is expensive but it's worth getting the membership. There are so many things to see and try out. I loved this place and we'll be coming back soon.

The beach is beautiful and lots of parking here. We saw several families doing BBQ, kids birthday party. My daughter loved the beach. The waves were great here. And I loved the view of the ocean and we did our sunset watching here.

My daughter loved it. She wanted to go on it again. We paid $3 since we went to the museum. Otherwise it's $4.

Highly recommend this carousel for parents whose kids are crazy about Carousel. Beautiful view at this place.

I love this zoo. We were going to the Japanese garden but ended up at the zoo. One of the best zoos in the San Jose. My daughter loved it.

There are so many things for kids to do at this zoo. It's like a mini Disney.

Educational place for kids. You can easily spend all day watching fishes, planetarium show and etc. my second time there and we love it.

They have a Cafe too

Try the earthquake section. Awesome

Aloha!!!

Polo beach is very small.

It's a nice spot to hang out with friends and family and it has a great view.

And they have limited benches and tables, advisable to come early.
This is a big open park to hold picnic, private parties and etc. For big events, you need to get a permit. Beautiful park and close to fairytale, zoo and funderland.
Beautiful gallery. And they had summer love and there were lots of kids activities. And the view of bay is great at the observatory.
Small little park located near the apartments. It's good to bring the kids in the daytime. The play ground area is pretty big.
We went on the wrong time of the year. No flowers. We'll go back in future and update our review.

Did a tasting here recently a week after dropping off clients (I’m a wine Guide in the Willamette Valley) and wanted to know more about their wines and approach to the tasting room experience. We were greeted at the entry way, questioned if we had reservations (we were there just as they opened on a Saturday morning) and shown to a table near the bar, facing the huge window that faces south and east. Ashley introduced herself and got our tasting flight started. Nice pacing of the tasting, not too rushed but attentive. Their wines area quite exceptional, as would be expected from such a name and historic background. While the wines are very good, including a 2014 Pinot Noir (tasted side by side to the same wine, but a 2016 vintage) the prices are at a premium level. Not to take anything away from the impressive tasting room and excellent staff, the beautiful vineyards and well maintained grounds, but the experts know what they are talking about and it all comes at a price. If you want an “way above average” tasting experience, then this is the place to go!

Interesting place to go for indoor go-karts. Building is new in a neighborhood of Amazon warehouses and the like. First time visitors must create a profile on their computers to get started. WARNING; this is not an inexpensive place to go to, but for those millennials who have lots of disposable income this is your place. My 30 year old son and I stopped by mid day on a Monday and had the place to ourselves. Friendly staff and a reasonable sized track fir racing. Races are 12 laps (but for some reason our first race was stopped after only 8 laps). My son went on to do his 2nd race by himself (trying to improve his time) and got the full 12 laps. This is an event for the young at heart and body. If you’re over 55, stay on the sidelines and watch and drink beer! Getting into and out of the carts is a challenge for any one over 6’ and if you are prone to motion sickness, then come prepared (I didn’t unfortunately). Overall it was a unique experience for father & son.

We have been Wine Club Members for a number of years and I have been a customer since 2002. The tasting room has expanded over the years and now is just the right size for the business. Dave & Mary are always so gracious and the tasting room staff are very knowledgeable and friendly. The range of wines that are available for tasting and purchase are the perfect representation of the AVA & Dave’s skill as a wine maker. I have attended numerous events over the years and have enjoyed them all, from intimate tastings to lunch and/or dinner with 140 of my closest friends!

When I became a wine guide for A Great Oregon Wine (2 years ago) I started to bring my clients here and they always have a great experience!

Come taste Arborbrook’s wines, enjoy the vineyards and buy their wines to take home...you will not be disappointed!

COVID-19 UPDATES: Reservations are required and they are very accommodating to the needs of the customers & staff.

Parking is in a small lot well below the center (don't forget your parking pass) and then a short walk up a steep path to get to the facility. Well worth the walk & entry fee to explore a great exhibit ( see the movie too) to learn more than you can imagine about the Lewis & Clark expedition!!

The displays and material are well laid out and it is presented in a clear and logical chronological way. The kids will love this place and the views are not to be missed!!
Take your time to absorb the scope & scale of what Lewis & Clark accomplished.

Recently rebranded to TOC, this classic venue is wonderful for anything that goes on there. From classical to jazz to indie music, TOC is the place to hear it. Weekly free Sack Lunch concerts every Wednesday are a great way to hear music (mainly classical) from local musicians. Get on their email list & join as a member to get regular updates on upcoming shows. The new seat cushions are comfortable & the building is beautiful, especially the restored stain glass window on the south side of the Church. One of Portland’s best places to see!

Attended a Gala Fundraiser for Profile Theater on Friday evening (as a volunteer & a guest) in the newly opened Irving Street event space. The space is amazing and I throughly enjoyed myself (even though I was volunteering my time & energy) and I highly recommend this location for any nonprofit (or any organization for that matter). The room is great and there was plenty of room for our catering staff and our 140+ guests. Located on the NS Street Car line, there is also plenty of street parking. Ecotrust is a great company to work with!

Interesting place to visit and especially good for families with children. The “artwork” made from willow and dog trees is in its final year of standing (created in 2017 with a 3-4 year life span) and two of the three sculptures are starting to collapse. The paved path over the bridge is a good place to start and then you can take the small gravel paths that work their way along the creek and up through the canyon and wind up back in top near the huge lawns and playground. Covered areas with tables are closed off due to the pandemic.

One of the 16 museums in the park, this is a great presentation of a wide range of art in a historical building. They have a series of regular galleries with art from around the world and a rotating special collection (Bouguereau & America during our visit). The building is a great host to these collections and they are all presented in a very nice way. Plan on spending 2-4 hours to take in what they have on display.

Also check out Panama 66 next door for food, drinks and Jazx on Wednesday evenings!

One of Washington County & Beaverton’s hidden secrets!! A must go to place for a long walk(s) along the two paved paths or go off into the gravel/wood chip paths to explore all of the books & crannies of this wonderful park in the middle of Beaverton. Open from dawn to dusk, this is a beautiful park & educational experience for the whole family. Great interpretative center too. Would not know that you are surrounded by the bustling city when you are in the middle of the park! Plenty of parking too.

Had a great tasting experience here as they opened on a sunny Thursday morning. We shared a tasting ($15 w/o tax) and throughly enjoyed the range of wines they had to offer. We learned about the history of the owners and the vineyards. They have a huge wine club (by Willamette Valley, Oregon standards) & have developed the tasting room and winery into an event venue, including an area that is family friendly (under 21). Stop & try these wines and take some home with you (we did!).

The only bridge of its kind on the West Coast of the USA, this is a beautiful example of what a transit only bridge can look like. A great place to bike or walk on a clear & sunny day (which in the fall & winter is a challenge), the Tilikum is a Native American language (Tilikum” is Chinook Wawa, an international language used by first Oregonians, and later spoken by explorers, fur traders, settlers and the first few generations of Portlanders).

One of the most unique presentations of this medium I have ever experienced! As a photographer, I appreciate the range of what can be presented and MOPA goes way above what you might expect. They did have one of the three galleries closed, but the other two had amazing displays of photography that really made an impact.

Please take the time to see this small, but intense museum while visiting Balboa Park & you will not be disappointed!

Had a great time with family from out of town and loved the “new” gardens as we had not seen the renovations until now. Got there just as they opened, so had the place to ourselves for the first half hour. The improvements and upgrades were nice and other than missing the colors we see in the spring we enjoyed the experience. A “must see” for visitors as well as locals who have not been there for a while.

Great place for the entire family with 4 levels of places to explore and learn. Great exhibits with lots of information (take your time). They also have several movies that explore different aspects of the museum and of natural history, so make sure you take in one or more of them.

You can explore the exhibits at your own pace which is really nice and even with children, you can have a fantastic time!

Small location just off the highway, but reasonable size parking lot. Took the Art Walk just off the parking lot & enjoyed the whimsical art along the way. You can also take the more adventurous 2/3 mile loop trail that starts near the end of the Art Walk. A lot of up and down, but gorgeous views of a pristine wooded forest, a couple of creeks. Take your camera to capture the views!

A wonderful place to escape your worries and concerns. Great hiking trails and a wonderful place to learn about what the Audubon Society does. A local gem that is hidden in the west hills. Parking can be a challenge with a small parking lot near the gift shop & education center and street parking along the main access road. They are busier on the weekend, so try a mid week visit!

Always an experience at this place as the Mission Theater is one of the local gems for music (PDX Jazz specifically). Staff is always available to help out with one of their local brews and a bite to eat.

Update as of 1-2-19 for Cascade Blues Association monthly meeting. A new venue for them (an upgrade from Catfish Lou’s) and lots of room for these events.

One of the collection of 16 museums in Balboa Park, the Museum of Man is housed in this amazing building (see picture of from entry). Great displays throughout the museum and it’s a wonderful place for families to learn about our ancestors. DPEV enough time to read the information at the displays to get the full educational value of the experience.

The square and the Banyan Tree look pretty much like it did 20 years ago when I last visited. Unfortunately we were there the day when the cruise ship unloaded it’s thousands of passengers, so the town was mobbed and the streets almost impassable. After checking out the tree, we only spent another 30 minutes in town before we made a quick exit.

What a great place for the entire family! Multiple displays show the range of what model railroading is all about. You can ask questions of the volunteers that man the different displays and they are only to happy to discuss their passion! While you are in Balboa Park, please take the time to check this museum out!

The “place” to stop for pictures of Crater Lake! Still had snow in the parking lot & around the edges of the viewing areas. Gift shop is full of stuff for the tourists. Check out the views of the lake & then drive down the road to the Visitor Center.
dislikes: Snow in parking and viewing areas
