reviews_attraction.text: Small tasting room with some outside seating. Limited selection of wines for tasting, but a very nice mother & daughter team that was knowledgeable. Check out the chocolate shop on one side & The Rouge Creamery on the other side!

An amazing place for wine & lunch outside. Cat was a fabulous wine guide & server and answered all of our questions with a smile. If you are anywhere nearby, you must stop by & enjoy the wine and the view!
Always a great place to participate in a demonstration! Was there to support the teachers in an effort to get the state legislation passed for full school funding.
One of the best places to go to to pay your respects to those who served and made the ultimate sacrifice.

From downtown Wilmington, drive and drive and drive some more to find the  Cameron Art Museum on the edge of town. We visited in early 2020 for the Isamu Noguchi lantern exhibit which was amazing. This was a side of the artist we had not seen before. The Cameron's permanent collection is one of the largest collection of prints by abstractionists. Many of the names are famous in other media, so the prints are a new twist: Calder, Giacometti, Nevelson, Matisse, etc. The staff was super friendly and there's a sculpture garden outside.

We tried to visit "The Great Dismal Swamp" on the VA side but that visitor center was closed. By accident we discovered this visitor center in NC and enjoyed the exhibits and gift shop.
George Washington was part owner of a company that tried to drain the swamp, and where he failed, others managed to harvest the trees (twice over), and shrink the swamp with many drainage canals.
The swamp's lake water is brownish but was said to be healthy. In colonial times it was put in kegs and stayed "sweet", never going bad.

One of the smaller state capitols we've visited but worth a trip. Many states have modernized or created new capitols but this building predates the Civil War and the ground floor is still used by the governor. A self-guided tour upstairs has exhibits on the building's history.  The state legislatures have moved two blocks North, just past the State History and Science Museums. That building also allows self-guided tours.

I'd give 5 stars if the permanent collection were free to the public. Instead they make no distinction between special exhibitions and entrance. One ticket gives access to everything. The displayed collection is small but still impressive. Nice collections of African and Latin American Art. Nice use of technology for virtually changing the colors on statues or for reading the pages of a Medieval manuscript.

This was my 2nd visit, 1st for my wife. We arrived early morning and did not have a long wait. There's a museum inside at the base to keep you entertained until your ticketed time arrives. And while in line for the elevator, a guide tells stories so you're never bored. The ride up is fun - the "elevator" has to zig-zag: side step, up, side step, up. The view at the top is awesome.

When old trains are retired (or rescued) they end up at the NC Transportation Museum near Lexington. There's also planes, trucks, and old cars. This is truly a marvelous museum complex. Our only complaint is that they need better signs. Some vehicles have no label or descriptions. The path to walk is not always clear when halls end in unlabeled doors.

When we visited in 2016, the exterior looked like your typical tourist trap promising all kinds of amazements and wonders. But to our surprise the place delivers. It's enormous inside with collections of Rocks & Minerals, fine glassware, hundreds of lunch boxes, Indian artifacts, stuffed animals, farm equipment, and more. We were quite impressed!

We visited with a family with several children and the kids were all fascinated by the exhibits and cool items in the gift shop. The museum does a great job of explaining the how & why and what happened in each war. It's amazing what the army airborne is capable of and what a significant role they've played in times of war.

The Page-Walker is a great community landmark with a public garden, two indoor art galleries, a tiny museum of Cary town history,  and frequent public events like plant sales and concerts in the garden. The art works are usually changed monthly with new local artists for Cary's 4th Friday Art Loop.

We were super surprised by the great time we had at this little museum. We've been to many of the great art museums of the world, but this gem we found to be charming. Not stuffy or dark. Nice variety in the exhibits. Interesting modern and temporary works displayed. We spent two hours here.

Expected this to be very campy but actually had a great time. The Titanic is treated seriously with a look at the lives impacted and the sacrifices made. It's interactive. Trying to climb the ship deck at different degrees of tilting was eye opening.

Free tours on the hour about life during the beginning of the 20th century (1900's) for a affluent family in Fayetteville. The guild was cheerful and knowledgeable about the family and servants and the new technologies that changed how we lived.

It's a house, it's an art museum. You can enjoy either or both. The house is lovely and quirky with a bowling alley and bar in the basement, and an indoor pool. The quality of the art exhibits is also outstanding.
likes: Unique facilities (bowling alley, bar, indoor pool)

reviews_attraction.text: Like all of Eureka Springs this church is on a steep hillside and, as reported in Ripley's Believe It or Not, you can enter this building from the top of it's bell tower. Lovely building, nice gift shop.

Wow! I had not expected the old jail preserved inside a new building. Or the historical figures and history lesson broadcast/presentation. A must see for any Mormon and interesting for non-Mormon also.
What happens when you get a new hobby and it takes over your life. The topiary work is amazing. And he's self-taught so there's hope for all us to accomplish art work like this with bushes and trees.
This is a large garden park with sculptures everywhere, a zoo, a restaurant, gift shop and more. Keep the ticket, it's good for more at least 2 days and you'll need time to see everything.
Ridiculous expensive to visit, but I'm glad I came. There's the house, multiple museums with cars and outfits, hit records and Elvis history. It takes many hours to see everything.
What an amazing town built alongside a steep slope. A "stairstep town". Everything is on a slant with stairs to and between buildings. A destination worthy of the journey.
Great little museum about a man who could not sleep at night so he started sewing, then gluing, buttons on everything. He appeared on all the talk-shows back in his day.
Fun day trip of a very unusual house. It doesn't look all that big on the outside but the guided tour twists round and round on the inside with lots of beautiful rooms.
Worth a side trip for the widest tree I've ever encountered. Not tall like the redwoods but rather giant branches stretching out like you've never seen before.  Free!
Strange that one of the most visited tourist sites in MS is the ruins of a mansion, but the columns are incredibly beautiful and photographic.
Had a great time at the Farmer's Market . There were lots of vendors and we found several items to bring home.  Parking was not a problem.
Had a fun visit learning about the Walton family and the history of Walmart. Get some Ice cream at Walton 5 & 10 next door.

Restrooms and a small picnic area with a few tables are next to limited parking. The trail is paved from the lot towards the pond and then you will find paved and non-paved sections circling the pond. Very brushy along the edge of paths and near the water. Plenty of leaf litter and branches are in need of removal. There are even some very large trees knocked over. I bet this was after all the fierce wind storms this year and hopefully cleanup will continue. There are four platforms/docks on the west side of the pond. Two of the docks are ice-bound at the moment, and the other two were being used by anglers. Nobody seemed to be catching anything today. The trail goes all the way around the pond, but the south and north sides have tall chain link fences that prevent you from reaching the water and block your view. Probably to give the ducks some safe cover. I saw Canadian geese, Wood ducks, and Mallards in the water. Also saw some small bass. Overall a pleasant but small area to enjoy.
dislikes: Blocked views and access due to fences

reviews_attraction.text: Great place to for hidden groves, ponds, and shady trails. I especially enjoyed the birdhouse trail. Actually, I was blown away by the sheer number of clever and beautiful bird houses. There are several kinds to explore and if you are lucky you might see a turtle, or three. The Bird of Prey area was also very enjoyable. Such gorgeous owls, hawks and eagles to see. There is a great playground for the children, with pails in the sand and a water pump to add to the fun. There is even a children's library near the playground with some interesting books to read. There are shady chairs to rest on and fantastic sculptures for the kids to climb on. About a mile and a half of trails to wander and even a hidden "mouse hole" to find. Spend a pleasant day enjoying nature and support the wonderful educational programs in this unique getaway.

This access gives you plenty of trail choices to Taylor canyon. You cangcan above the canyon, into the canyon, or check out the cool little pond nearby. There are chances to catch some shade along the way, which is welcome in the summer months. In spring you can enjoy the stream. Today I heard the plop plop sound of ripping acorns falling off the trees. It is often crowded on the trails, but people here are cool and know how to share the trail. Great views of the peaks near Snow Basin in the distance. If you like to climb, you will find many excellent boulders on the Northside entrance to the canyon (labeled as the School Room Climbing Access). Wildlife is abundant in the early morning.

This historic, working farm is a peek into the not so distant past. Several places to view animals including horses, cows, donkeys, peacocks, chickens, rabbits and more. Lots of picnic tables spread out across the property to enjoy a snack or a meal. The old Icehouse and ponds are a special place to experience. You can milk a cow or take a tour of the lovely farmhouse.  Very well kept paths take you from the main barn out beyond the creek and into a large nature area. So much to see that I will have to come back again to see it all. Clean, brightly lit bathrooms.

Way out in the middle of nowhere. The drive takes a lot longer than you might expect. But then you are rewarded with an amazing piece of artwork to interact with. Nice parking area and room to explore. Pro tip #1 - Bring bug repellent. I didn't, and the flies and no-see-ums really tore me up. I would have stuck around longer but I got tired of being bitten. Pro tip #2 - there is a nice hiking trail behind the parking area which goes up the hill and give you a spectacular view of the Spiral Jetty from up above.

Nice walking loop of just under a mile. Lots of birds. We saw bluejays, robins, doves, hawks, jays and blackbirds. Nice playground for kids including a small splash pad. The park covers an area of 57 acres which can be accessed via a paved path around the entire park. There are several benches along the way if you want to birdwatch or catch your breath. At the East end you will cross a small spring-fed creek, with a marshy area full of cattails.

A wonderful place to spend the day. Plenty of opportunities for wildlife watching. Some really challenging hiking trails. I saw dozens of Pronghorn and Bison, especially near the Buffalo Point area. Don't miss the historic Fielding Garr Ranch. I loved all the antique farming equipment on display. All the Employees and Docents were knowledgeable and cordial. Be prepared for swarms of insects, and bring some bug repellent along with you.

Amazing scenery. Campsites were full. Kind of a pain, because it's a long drive off the freeway to find that out. I'm not a fan of first come first serve campgrounds for that very reason. But if you just want to see some incredible rock art and geological formations, this place is well worth the side trip and price. One of the most beautiful parks for a hundred miles. Plenty of trails, caves, and historical sites to explore.

A good place to spend an hour. Don't linger anywhere or the mosquitos will get you. Not a lot of interesting rocks on this trail, but there are plants and animals in abundance. The trail could use some maintenance, especially when it enters the scrub oak. I saw 4 deer along the South side of the loop. There are actually four trailheads which access the park. Nice place for kids.

You will find spectacular views down Emigration Canyon and South towards Mt. Aire. You can also take a hike from the parking area and see some awesome vistas of Little Dell Reservoir. Plenty of wildlife including several deer. This is the road to Zion, so follow the Pioneers to the last summit on the trail. The rest area has plenty of parking and clean restrooms.

Scenic place to stop and enjoy the gorgeous red poppies.  Please be careful and don't trample the flowers trying to get that perfect shot. Some of the hills are a bit steep, so watch your footing. It's a narrow road with no turnoff parking. Traffic is high, so watch your kids and your dogs. June is the best time to visit this attraction.

Mind blowing historic site. The ruins of over 800 ovens lie scattered on the landscape. The unique back to back beehive design is truly unique. Walk around the old railway station and other buildings and be careful not to disturb anything. There are also several ATV trails near here to enjoy.

Good place for a family gathering or for walking the dog. Two excellent playgrounds for the kids. Covered picnic tables, benches, and shady trees.   Access to some great trails including Gibb's loop to Waterfall canyon. Plenty of parking and friendly folks who kept their distance.

Quaint neighborhood park with all the fixings. You will find covered picnic tables, several charcoal grills, and a playground and swings for the children. A gently sloping hill is just perfect for rolling down or taking a barefoot stroll.

What an enchanted place. Frisbee Golf, Fishing, and a splash park for the kids. Have a picnic by the pond and walk over the creek on tiny bridges. Lots of Mallards that are almost tame and don't seem bothered by visitors.

A large green park with a pond, small waterfalls, wooden bridges across the stream, and a playground. Plenty of shade trees and gently sloping hills. Bring a blanket and lunch and enjoy a cool summer picnic by the water.
Pretty little place. Historic building and hot springs on the North end of the park.  few homeless folks around but they won't bother you. Plenty of space to walk the dog or toss around a Frisbee.
Birdwatching is fabulous and exciting along the road. Several trails and interesting places to stop. Don't miss Goose Egg Island. Several places have signage describing historic people and events.
Great access to "The Ledge" and Eagle Cave. Trails in great shape and uncrowded. Get high real quick and get stunning views of Fremont Island and South to the Great Salt Lake. Saw some deer.
A cool place to check out. Not all the buildings are open to visit, and that's a shame, because it's a very interesting farm. There is a picnic table near the barn, so bring your lunch.
This cozy park has a picnic area with tables and barbeque grills. There is a small playground area for climbing and sliding. Great place to exercise the dogs or yourself.
Hidden Gem. Very old but cute little neighborhood park. I've been coming here since I was a wee lad. Love the access to the Ogden River and covered picnic areas.
Climbing wall! This little park has plenty of room to run and play some Frisbee. A large covered pavilion with several picnic tables for your gathering.
This arch can be visited by taking one of the car tours at Golden Spike State Park. Always uncrowded and we'll worth the drive.
The buildings and grounds are chock full of amazing historical relics. A great place for kids to learn about pioneer history.

This is one of the most active residential parks I've ever visited. I used to live in the nearby apartment complex, and it was awesome to see people using the soccer field and tennis courts every single day. I think the splash pad is closed in the off season, but the small fountain was filled with children most days too.

I only ever saw homeless people a couple times - I would be more worried about the numerous Grandma's power walking around the pathways at night!

The park is on the south side of town, so the views to the south over the lake bed are beautiful. There are walking trails separated from the roads, which is nice for cyclists and pedestrians.

For the Pokemon Go players - yes, there are probably around 20+ pokestops in a row on the south side of the park (on Veterans Memorial Dr). If you hop on your bicycle, you can totally hit all of these from the walking trail!

Most people just drive through the forest on 50 to get to South Lake Tahoe and never see more than the tress by the highway. There are tons of hikes and little towns off the main drag, and it's easy to find a place to hike or camp. Backpacking requires permits, so always contact the ranger station when planning a trip! I recommend the Ralston Peak area. It's close to Tahoe, but feels like the back country.

My favorite memory of stopping here was in the middle of a big thunderstorm. It was only 20 minutes from start to finish, but it blocked the mountains completely! It was raining sideways so hard, even the big shade shelters didn't protect us.

That said, there is normally no water here. The bathrooms are just pit toilets.

Tons of backpacking possibilities along highway 4 and 108. Watch out for weather conditions and seasonal closures. Always contact the ranger station before heading out into the wilderness!

The key to an enjoyable experience here is finding places to camp away from the clouds of mosquitoes...

A lovely park in a quiet neighborhood. I have never seen so many memorials that were so well kept.

The Pokemon Go craze has taken over the park these past few weeks, but for the most part people are considerate. It's cool to see so many people out and about in the evenings!

I did not know what to expect coming in to the EMP for the first time, but after spending almost 5 hours there, I can say it was totally worth the visit! The museum is divided into separate exhibits, so you can skip or spend time on the things that interest you!

Not very well lit after hours unless there is an event or game scheduled. Lots of parking and entrances on both sides of the block!

Pokemon GO players - this is currently a Shellder Nest, but they're pretty slow to spawn in my experience.

The trailhead for Mission Peak is out here, but you can keep heading out further into the hidden peaks and valleys beyond. The preserve is open for backpacking, but double check permitting and access privileges before heading out.

The parking lot is always full on weekends. The group picnic areas are often in use as well.

There is a split between casual visitors and climbing enthusiasts here, but the area is a great (free) alternative to Red Rocks!
likes: Suitable for both casual visitors and climbing enthusiasts

reviews_attraction.text: The paid parking is a bit annoying, but worth it if you plan to stay all day. Lots of community activities and the atmosphere feels like you're up in San Luis Obispo instead of being right in the middle of LA.
Lots of parking, but the park is a little stretched out. The main areas with the facilities are easily accessible, but the dog parks, bmx areas, and trails are all way in the back down a steep hill.
Very well kept grass here! There is also a surprising amount of mature tress in the park as well. Entrance is a little hidden, but you can keep circling around the roundabout if you can't find it.
There's a surprisingly big parking lot here, and the trails can be a little busy during summertime. Camping happens at the trailhead, but the good spots are just down the trail a couple miles!
I used to stop by here on my bicycle before heading back to San Luis Obispo. The area is set aside from the main road, and has nice views of the ocean.
Sunset park has always been one of the popular local hangouts. It's huge, well maintained, and hosts many different events/fairs throughout the year.
It's a rainforest! The Pacific Northwest is an awesome place to visit, but don't forget how far away destinations can be. The peninsula is huge!
I've only seen the western side of the forest, but the drive through to Mt Lassen is beautiful, even with some of the older fire damaged areas.
Lots of hiking and riding opportunities. Busy on the weekends, and the campground can get filled early as well. Beautiful place for day trips!
I usually just bicycle through the park and stop for water, but there is a cool looking bike park and a ton of baseball/softball diamonds!
Lots of hiking and mountain biking. Double check the maps before heading out, you might go down a hill and get stuck at a dead end!
This park is on the north side of City Hall. Lots of employees walking around and using the gazebo as an outdoor lunch spot.
Nice little green space next to City Hall. There's usually shade parking nearby, and the grass feels cool even in summer.
I haven't used the facilities in the back of the complex, but the park has TONS of shade and usually isn't very busy.
Lots of climbing opportunities here. Few facilities in the park, but Vantage is just a short drive across the river.

Probably the most popular hike in the Santa Ynez Valley during the Spring. You just have to make sure you go after the rains and catch the wildflowers while they are popping. It's truly a sight unlike any other I've seen. An entire mountain more orange and purple than it is green.

As for the hike, it's pretty steep. Going halfway up is pretty feasible for most anyone, but if you want to get to the top of the mountain then you'll want to be sure to bring lots of water and lembas bread because the last half is like scampering up Mount Doom. It's well worth it though to make it to the top.

About a six mile round trip hike. Not too strenuous but definitely something you'll have to block out most of the day for. Once you're up to the Punch Bowls it's gorgeous and a great place to spend the whole afternoon (especially when it's hot). There are three separate bowls to jump into which can sparse out the crowds a little bit. Certainly a popular local spot so you can't expect to be the only person up there, but the fact that you need to work to make it to the top means the crowds get thinned out along the path.

Definitely bring more water than you think you'll need.

One of the more accessible hikes in Montecito. The trail offers a great view after very little hiking but you got the option to keep hiking farther up and in for more panoramic views. It can get difficult if you stick with it the whole way but very worth it. The mudslides blew out the bridge so the best way to get there now is via Olive Mill to E Mountain Dr. The trail says its closed but its been well used recently with an easy trail path to follow. Give it a go and you'll be mindblown by the destruction that the mudslides  caused.

Wilamette gives you the full breadth of PNW beauty. From tiny creeks to massive peaks and everything in between, you get the whole array of Oregon's green and wet climate. More spots to visit than you likely have time for in a summer, and certainly a place that will draw you back. Perfect for the most extreme of outdoorsman to the first time car camper. It's first on my list for anyone who is looking to get into the Oregon backcountry.

One of the great hikes of Santa Barbara with a low barrier of entry. Easy to get to, easy to get to the top, low time commitment and a panoramic view. The trailhead also connects you to some more extensive trails leading farther up the mountain and even over to Rattlesnake Canyon. Parking can be tough on Saturday mornings so the earlier the better, but if you're fine taking a few more steps than it's no matter of where you park.

Definitely some of the best hiking in the area. You can take the trails up and turn around whenever is convenient (there are great views along the way that make it easy to hit a good "turn around" spot) or you can keep following them up until they connect with the Inspiration Point or Tunnel trails. Easy parking and a broad array of difficulty make it a great place to hike for just about anyone.

The epitome of Santa Barbara architecture and style. The historic courthouse has it all. The history, the Spanish Colonial Revival architecture, the gorgeous sunken gardens and a view of the entire city from its tower. Small weddings are held here, community events and countless lunches on the lawn in addition to it still functioning as a court of law. It's a truly special place.

One of the best theaters in California. Incredible location, awesome history, the best performers and open air seating. They'll rip your eyes out on the concessions (as per usual with theaters) and the parking is a little nightmarish but overall its a great place to attend a concert.

Holy nuts! The sunrises from up here with the hovering fog above the lake are unreal. A perfect place to watch the sunrise or scope out a hike on the surrounding peaks. Great climbing nearby as well with some awesome intermediate pitches.

The park has a series of light walking paths that are pretty mellow. The real reason to show up is to look up at the sheer cliffs and the Needle.

Avoid the $5 parking fee by parking outside the gate and walking a few extra feet.

One of the great places in the Valley just to sit down. From here you can see all the big rocks and waterfalls. When your feet are tired, just make sure they can get you here before you take your shoes off for a good rest.

Dinky Creek Wilderness is pretty magical. The trailhead has a couple of route options but regardless of where you end up you find yourself in some gorgeous country. A good place to start a beginner backpack trip.
One of the most beautiful views of Santa Barbara belongs to the Mission and its grounds. A great place to spend an afternoon, set up for a picnic or play lawn games in an open public space.
Great hiking and driving. It has one of those raw beauties to it that you don't get a whole lot of nowadays. One of the few spots in the Bay Area that feels untouched and clean.
The park connects to a ton of trails that can take you a decent way up and down the coast. Great for a long walk or run past some of the best of the California coast.
The hike to the top is one of the more challenging hikes in the Valley but has a stopping point at Lower Yosemite Falls... but the glory is all the way at the top.
The hiking up near Giffith is honestly better than the museum. The trails are really extensive and capture some of the most iconic scenery of the LA area.
One of the few spots for the citizens of LA to get a taste of the outdoors. Hikes for all calibers of fitness and surprisingly good views from the peaks.
A killer view of the Golden Gate and the North Bay. The batteries are a great historical reminder and the city has kept them preserved relatively well.
All the views.The Pacific and the entire Bay. A pretty special place and it's much more remote than a lot of the tourist attractions in the City.
It's one of the better vantage points of the north side of the island. A good blend of the beautiful products of both humankind and nature.
likes: Blend of human and natural beauty

reviews_attraction.text: A gem of a park with killer view of Portland dispersed around its peak. One of the prettiest places within the city limits.

As a place for walking: excellent.
As a planetarium: epic
As a culturally relevant place: Whatever La La Land has made it
Pretty mellow hike down to the waterfront with plenty to do once you're down there. Kayak, hike, swim, SUP, etc.
Stop and walk a little! Landmarks like this invite you to get out of your car and check out the Coast!

This small working museum that incorporates both the central cable power station and the car barn for the cable cars details the history of the San Francisco Cable Car including details of how the system actually works. You can watch the cables thrum through the giant motors that propel the cable through the system lifting cars up and down the San Francisco hills. There are displays on how it all works and a small souvenir shop which as drinks and snacks too. The upper part of the museum is accessible. The best way here is is either by Cable Car or by foot. The museum is free to enter and explore. #LetsGuide

The wave organ looks like ancient ruins but was actually made in the 1980s. It seems that very few people know about it and those that visit don't realise they should listen to the pipes. The most amazing oceanic orchestral noises come out of the pipes as the waves do their thing. This is well worth a visit and the choppier the sea the more noises you get. I lived in the Bay Area for ages and had no idea it was here until another local pointed it out. Some of the Wave Organ is accessible but most of it needs bodily movement ability. #LetsGuide

I quite enjoyed this place but would like more freedom especially to visit the engineering spaces of the ship because that's my interest. I could find any volunteer that knew anything about it. All I got was you can't go there. Not overly helpful. The place gets quite crowded and on weekends there are massive queues. They've done their best to make it #accessible but a chair bound person has limited options. The food is simply well like a school canteen. Not appetising. At least the prices were ok. The best bit is the submarine.

Fort Point is a civil war fort which is available for public exploration. There are a number of interpretative displays within the fort and there are volunteers on hand to explain things including a very entertaining lady who would not be drawn out of the 1800s character she was playing which was highly amusing. The fort has a considerable number of spiral and traditional stairs and needs some stamina to visit it all. I recommend seeking out all the nooks and crannies of this fascinating building.

Amazing waterfall well worth the effort to climb up those stairs. They're on the Mist Trail (if you go on the John Muir you won't see them) on the way to Nevada Falls. There are toilets above the falls. There is a huge mirror pond and waterslide (rock) at the top. They are signposted for not swimming but there were plenty of people in both when I went. The stairs are uneven, wet, slippery and difficult. Take your time. Take plenty of water and food for the climb and of course your camera.

I love the Guggenheim. A lot of it was closed due to a new exhibition, but it is more the architecture than the art that attracted me to the place. That said you could certainly see the new exhibition from the other side of the ramps where you could go! The building is somewhat smaller than I expected but is absolutely gorgeous design. I really enjoyed my time here. It was like a peaceful oasis in the depths of New York.
dislikes: Limited access due to new exhibition

reviews_attraction.text: It seems strange to review a place like this... The grounds are immaculately kept and the sweeping lines of white head stones receding into the distance backed by dark trees and surrounded by green lawns are magestic as well as sad. They remind us of the futility of war. The thousands of lives lost giving service to their nation. Definitely worth a visit for a moment of quiet reflection.

Known from the story as The Great Grey Bridge the George Washington bridge spans the river and states of NY and NJ. The bridge is an interesting open lattice design and has elegant draped suspension span. Very similar to its more famous west coast cousin. Well worth a visit. You can bike or walk over the bridge if you want to look. It is accessible from The Greenway.

The modern counterpart to the adjacent Brooklyn Bridge. The bridge allows travel (car, bike, foot) from Dumbo, Brooklyn through to China Town in NYC. The access is easy. The Manhattan bridge is a much quieter walk than the Brooklyn bridge as it doesn't seem to have the tourist influx that is enjoyed by that bridge. It has interesting rooftop views at the NYC end.

Coit tower is a great vantage point above the city with strong views in all directions both from the tower and from the surrounding Pioneer Park. You can drive up to Coit, catch a Muni bus or simply walk. The tower has a number of interesting origin stories, perhaps some of them even have a grain or two of truth. It costs $7 to get to the top of the tower.

I really enjoyed wandering through both the Mickey mouse special exhibit and the main rooms in the other building. I do wonder if the people are trained to be infinitely polite and smiley though... It was worth the time and the cash. The are accessible restrooms and the entire exhibit is accessible with ramps and elevators.

Language of the Birds is an interesting public art piece on Columbus Ave. It is illuminated at night, but I actually prefer it during the day highlighted against a bright blue sky.  It can be visited 24 hours but be aware that there are a lot of sex clubs nearby that attract interesting people at night time. #LetsGuide

Statue Cruises are efficient at what they do which is transporting thousands of people to and from Statue of Liberty and Ellis Island. They're fairly impersonal but that happens when you deal with so many people day in and day out. They get the job done quickly and safely.

Not just trains lined up. This museum tells the story of each exhibit well with each within its diorama. Full sized and model collections are displayed. I'm betting you've never seen train hung from the roof before...

A small but quiet park adjacent to the 9/11 Memorial. A good place to get an overview of the memorial and to see The Sphere contained within the park. There are no facilities and several different monuments here.

Awesome spot for iconic photography of the Golden Gate Bridge, Foreshore buildings, Alcatraz and San Francisco. Good place to bring kids to simply run around. Easy access to recreation and tourist facilities.
Good visibility of the GGT bridge and over to North Beach. Parking is easy. Quite a few bong smokers the night I went. A bit far away for fantastic photos. Might be good when the fog rolls in.
Awesome park for kids with water play and playground. Equipment is a bit dated but functional. Bathrooms were ok. Lots of trees and shady areas for the hot days. #kidfriendly #letsguide
Simple stone structure with some interpretive information. Great views across the valley but do go right out to Glacier Point itself for the best view and photo opportunities.
The people on this visitor centre are really helpful. I preferred to get my souvenirs here as the money goes into the park. Found the very hard to get Photographing Yosemite.
Great little waterfront park. A nice place to relax on the grass and catch a little shade at the hotter parts of the day. The giant bow and arrow sculpture is interesting.
The zoo was remarkably crowded on the day I went and this reduced the enjoyment of wandering the grounds. Apart from that its well, a zoo and there are animals.
I love visiting this place. There is so much to see as you wander the grounds. The friendly volunteer staff are generally happy to show you around.
Accessible and beautiful granite cliffs. Would be amazing when there is a lot of water. Get to the fall via board walks and trails.
This is a really cool set of displays to help learn while consuming time at SFO. I loved the insect display.

They did some upgrades and the visitor center is well worth the trip, you get to see what exists even if you might not be able to visit the seals.    Highly recommend signing up for the hike,  reservations required from november to april at least on weekends, you can sometimes find openings during on nonbusy times during week days.   But best to reserve on web site if you really want to see the seals.    We were able to see some young males on the beach below visitor center, but these are not the big boys.

Interesting, little small as art places go, usually has some really good temporary display.   Not a kids place, although they try.
But not much room for too much.   I get bored here quickly, so can imagine kids would.   Would say check current exhibit and if it really sounds great go, if not don't.

One of the california gems.   The tours are always differrent, depending on guides, but just to see the place and see the views from the castle are worth the admission.    If you get a good guide you will know it,  by how much more you want to know about this place.

Not sure of this park, little dirty, smelly and maybe visited at wrong time, a large meeting was happening and well i didnt feel comfortable, and wouldnt feel so with children playing at what appears to be nice playground.   Not my place.

Very nice waterfall, but this is a really painful place since no public parking exists, and what paid private parking is very limited.   Very worthwhile hike if you can get there.  No  handicapped parking and trail is muddy and narrow .

Nice place, extremely crouded and a tourist trap.   Did have a dolewhip which was excellent, but at around 8 dollars, well not sure.   If in area drop in.  You can see a pineapple field for free, but it is only free part.
Very protected Beach area and a sandy swimming area exists.    Not very deep and just ok for snorkeling.   We were on windy day with 20 swells breaking and it was calm inside.    Great for kids.
Nice park, has kids playground and exercise stations.   Trails along Creek, but hiway 17 noise is really loud, making a really pleasant trail is walking on freeway.     Bike trail looks great.
One of the best scenic points in yosemite, a required stop if its open.    You will have unbelievable views of the whole valley, a very different perspective of everything.  A dont miss.
The nature center is nice and people pleasent.   Trails little confusing out to River, loop isn't clear.  Maybe more inpressive at different time of year,  little depressing.
Very isolated, Rocky beach.  Maui not visible today, covered picnic tables and potapotty.  Has shower's, water access not for me, although was calm but lava rock crossing.
Nice beach next door and really interesting park.    Great snorkeling at beach.   The historic displays and knowledge on the docents is great.   Well worth the trip.
Well it's free.  Has history of the mission santa Clara, and local indians and a changing art exhibit.   Little small. Worth a visit if at Santa Clara mission
This is a great beach when not too crowded, and where else can you hear the history of a concrete ship.   It too bad the pier hasn't been repaired.
Fun place for all, right now lots of exhibits are in change and really bad when crowded like on this visit.   Takes away from normal experience.
It is an interesting place and has lot of information regarding the past and current eruptions.   Too bad some areas are currently closed.
Great beach, would love them to finish restrooms.   Wasn't that good for snorkeling, cloudy water but very calm nice beach on my visit.
Love this place, although we are at end of season.  Surprised by vandlized displays.  And recent weather has downed some tree branches.
Nice park, great playground.  But lot of homeless and trash as result.   Some may find uncomfortable, I was not bothered by anyone.
Interesting, worth a trip if you enjoy California history.   The Adobe is nearby, and also a good place to check out.
Interesting story and place.   Worth a trip to see.   They also offer transport for those unable to make the walk.
Great place hidden a few feet from main streets.  Is a great recreation of the mission and has plenty of history.
Great place for a quick walk to see redwoods.   If on limitted time this is great place to see some redwoods.
Great place to take t he kids for a walk near the ocean.    The buildings are great during the celebrations.
Great beach, but have to be early or gets crowded and no parking available.   Flat and Sandy, easy to swim.

I recently took the kids to the science center to see the space shuttle and the dogs exhibit happening right now.  The center itself is pretty big and dialed in.  The staff were super friendly, helpful and fantastic with the little ones.  The shuttle exhibit was really cool to see up close, but would be nice to have a overlook to see it from a higher angle.

The Dogs exhibit was also cool, with lots of interactive stations and tons of great info.  My little ones enjoyed running around touching everything, but the exhibit is really best suited for middle school and high school aged kids.

The LA Science Center was super impressive and I would highly recommend checking it out, especially if you have kids. The Space Shuttle exhibit makes it a place for all ages to visit and marvel at what humans can do when they put their minds to it.

This beach is nice in alot of ways and not in others.  Located right off the bikepath and near shops and eateries in Playa, this beach has nice facilities, bathrooms, parking, fire pit and more, but has to be one of the dirtier beaches I have ever encountered.  Tar from boats literally everywhere, trash as far as the eye can see and people disrespecting what is actually available.  It really is sad because there is tons to offer, it just needs to be cleaned up an maintained differently.  I do see tractors combing trash and whatnot, and I ever see volunteers constantly picking up, but alas...too much trash.

Just a Los Angeles classic music venue with incredible views, fantastic acoustics and the ability to bring in your own food and booze! What could be better?!  I have been to the Hollywood Bowl many times during my years in the city and can't recommend it enough to locals and visiors alike.  If you think the shows are great, the people watching is even better, depending on who's headlineing of course.  If you are in town and looking to experience the crown Jewel of the LA music scene...look no further.

This was my first experience at The Greek and it was awesome!  The venue is basically a smaller, cleaner more intimate version of the Hollywood Bowl.  We brought a picnic and ate in the park before the show and just walked right in, couldn't have worked out better.  The seats were comfortable for the small amount of time we were sitting, the drinks were expensive, but not obscene and best of all, the aucustics were fantastic! I will certainly be looking for a reason to return sooner than later!

A spiritual experience, set in a unique and beautiful New Mexico landscape. This place is rich in history and has an almost overwhelming energy, regardless of your faith and/or beliefs. The place is set up like a campus, with each building having its it's own unique story, purpose and style.  Walk around, buy some fresh spices and enjoy the views, but most importantly, take in the beauty of what this place is all about.

Ok folks, Pinks Hotdogs, are they all that they are cracked up to be? The short answer is no, but they are still some really good dogs! We stopped in because the line was short as we passed by. The dog itself was fantastic...love the pop! The cheese was some kraft singles thrown on top...wait what?!  They lose a star for that alone...get some real cheese up in there!!!

Joshua Tree National Park is gem in the national park system.  It offers many completely unique landscapes, hikes, exhibits, reserved campgrounds and so much more!  Endless views in every direction and something for everyone, from car hikers to hard care backpacker's. Just make sure you bring enough water and I highly recommend bringing in lunch.

Lafayette Park is a lovely sprawling greenspace located in the heart of San Francisco that offers picnic tables, gathering areas and a playground that rivals any top playground you've ever seen.  A perfect place to lay on a blanket and soak up the panoramic views, throw around a ball or anything else you can think of in a huge recreational space.

Hidden Valley Nature Trail is a good easy/moderate hiking trail located in Joshua Tree National Park.  The trailhead offers bathroom facilities, a picnic area with a bunch of tables and BBQ's as well as ample parking.  This is a great spot in the center of a bunch of exibits to rest, grab some lunch and take in some beautiful scenery.

The Rose Bowl is a special place for Angelenos for a variety of reasons.  It is home to THE ROSE BOWL, tons of concerts and events, a fantastic park that surrounds the area and one of the countries most famous flea markets.  It's pretty easy to find a reason to go, now just pick one and check it out!

A fantastic playground for children of all ages to run, jump, climb and play.  Tons of great equipment and structures to play on and a wide range of fun stuff for the little ones  to get in to.  If you are in the area and looking for a place for the kids to run wild, this is your place!

We stopped by Candy Cane Lane on Christmas Eve and were blown away by all of the fantastic decorations and festive vibes. Everyone was having a wonderful time and we can't wait to go again next year. We can't recommend checking this place out to get in the mood for the holidays!

A fantastic park with a pirate theme playground.  The kids ran around and had a ball climbing and playing on all the structures.  Safe, fun and a great design for hours of fun!  If you live or are visiting  Santa Barbara, put this place on your list for the kiddos!

I've been wanting to hit this spot for years and finally checked it off the list. The flowers were incredible and the surrounding area is beautiful. I recommend coming towards the end of the day as the crowds can be sizable and do make a reservation online!

Culver West Alexander Park has tons of greenspaces, shade and a fantastic playground for all ages.  There is also a community center with basketball and handball courts, bathrooms and the benches are available to reserve for parties.

The Big Morongo Canyon Preserve is a great spot to hike and take in endless high desert landscapes. Home to many critters and native plants, stop by for a great alternative to Joshua Tree National Park, with far fewer people around.

We loved this trail! Plenty of space for the kids to run around and features nice wide trails with plenty of shade trees throughout. The parking lot can fill up, bit be patient, someone typically leaves every 5-10 minutes.

Fantastic park with tons of stuff for kids of all ages.  The splash pad is awesome for the little ones along with the adjacent playground while the greenspaces and basketball courts are perfect for older kids and adults.
Stop into the Country Music Hall of Fame for some serious music history and see how it all began. I love visiting this place and brushing elbows with some of the greatest performers of all time!
Burton Chance Park is a nice park with tons of green space and endless views of the boats floating around in the Marina.  It's also the hub and perfect viewing area for the holiday boat parade.
A great little park in the sand for the little ones! A good variety of things to do and close to picnic tables, bathrooms, a huge greenspace and the cement park to ride bikes and scooters!
A fantastic park with a variety of facilities.  The playground is impressive and perfect for kids 3-12. Tons of greenspace to run around and throw/kick a ball.
A great park on the westside of LA with tons of greenspaces, a great playground and a super cool tower to get a bird eye view.  Great for kids of all ages.
A great spot to take a walk, set up a picnic or just let the kiddos run around on the grass.  Lots of picnic tables around and a trail head to local hikes.
The best theme park for kids and home of Daniel Tigers Neighborhood. If you have kids 2-10 years old, i can't reccomend this place enough.

Sacramento Zoo may not be the best, cleanest, largest or most animal friendly or ecologically responsible, but it's certainly trying hard to be a 'good' place to house some representative examples of the world's great animal (and plant) life. I gave it a 4-star rating because it's close to my heart (my granddaughter goes there often since my son bought a family membership (3 family members can enter for free for a year).  I can't say that there is that ONE great animal exhibit that everyone who visits Sac Zoo MUST see, but it's the entire zoo itself that creates a special Northern California animal habitats in the confines of a large state capital city.
If you're an out-of-town visitor (with or without kids in tow), you can probably see the majority of animal exhibits and have time to enjoy a  meal and the shuttle train ride (all 300 yards of it) in about 3 good hours.
Those who live in or near Sacramento might enjoy breaking up their visit to the zoo into several shorter trips, which is what my son does with his 3-year-old daughter.  I've been in a coolish March spring and in scorching August  heat to Sac Zoo, and you can still see quite a few interesting species regardless of season.
It may not be a big reason to visit Sacramento, but if you're spending time in the State's Capitol, you should allow at least a couple of hours to visit a fine example of 19th century-style zoo -- kind of relic of a past century, but like many old (and old-fashioned) things, it's good see how animals were once kept in cages for human amusement.

Kakino-Honokohau National Seashore and Wildlife Refuge is a great stop for an hour or two to explore one of the pristine beach parks on the Big Island. It is well-known for the chance to see Hawaiian sea turtles sunning themselves on the beach and in the shallow rocky tidal pools. It’s located just near To Honokohau Boat Harbor, which is where you can park after entering from the highway and then turn right at the first turn, continue about 400 m to reach the parking lot on your left. There is a gate on the right leading to a pat that enters the National Park Reserve, snd follows along the shore northward.
You can park for free in the Honokohau Harbor parking lot and walk into the national park to reach the beach. There is at least one public restroom inside the park —about 400 yards along the path going north. If you walk far enough, approximately 1.4 miles, you’ll reach the ranger station and a small exhibit of the park’s features.
If you’re lucky, you’ll see more than one sea turtle sunning itself on the sandy beach as you walk about one kilometer ( or more) along the park’s shoreline. It is a national park and rangers take their job seriously—to protect species from human harm, so don’t get too close to those magnificent sea turtles. Of course, don’t touch them or feed them either.

Diamond Head Beach Park is one of the hidden gems that is not too far from Waikiki, but far enough to leave it in relative isolation from the typical hordes of tourists flocking to Waikiki's beaches. It is about 1 mile or maybe longer from Honolulu Aquarium, turning right and following DH Road to Beach Road, that descends on the right to the shore. Typically, it is not very crowded and almost deserted at certain times of the week and the day. There was a time a few years ago when homeless people were starting to take over this beach, but now they have been moved out. There are men and women who sunbathe in various stages of undress since it is apparently not illegal to be without even a bathing suit on Honolulu city beaches. There is a shower at the far end and an inclined pathway that leads back up to Diamond Head Road.

San Onofre State Beach is a very large State beach park, just off Interstate 5 by taking the Basilone Rd exit and cross back over the highway to reach the park entrance, and it is located  just north of Camp Pendleton., if you came in from San Diego.  After exiting, you will need to drive about 2 miles back south on the access road to reach the state park beaches. There is plenty of parking. You’ll pass the now closed, double breasted nuclear reactors as you head south to the beaches. Formerly, the section around Parking Lot 6 was traditional a clothing optional section of the beach, but that has changed for now.

It is not too difficult to walk down the steep paved road to reach the shoreline on the floor of Waipio Valley, but remember you’ll have to work your way back to the top—45 minutes to get down and another one and a half hours to get back up. You can possibly drive, but you’ll need 4-wheel vehicle (most rental cars do not have it). However, once down you’ll swear you’ve reached heaven on earth. Going right,  you can see one of the waterfalls (in season). I prefer instead to cross the shallow river and head out walking along the wide beach extending at least a half mile further north.

A visit to South Union Shaker Village is more than an educational tour. It is a open window view into a once very prominent and an advanced secretive religious society known as the Shakers. In many ways, the Shakers had a society that was bound by staunch religious beliefs,  but also was an economic and technological powerhouse.
Years ago, the Shaker Village put on an annual musical play for about a month during summer vacation that reenacted the story of the Kentucky Shaker Village at South Union, and I was a part of the cast for a couple of summers back in the day.

Kapi'olani Park is a great place to spend leisure time, eat a picnic lunch. take a interesting walk, and do some great people watching as it is not far from the western end of Waikiki and is on the way to the lookout on Diamond Head Road (the road in front and far below the crater's peak).  There are some interesting trees and landscapes along with the beauty of Diamond Head Crater in the distance.  There are restrooms in a couple of places, and you'll pass by the  old Natatorium which has a legendary history, and where you can shower and also use the restroom.

The trip to Volcanoes National Park was done well before the 2018 Kilauea Lava Flow, so things were pretty quiet. It was great to explore that park and see evidence of its enormous natural volcanic activities. The best place to start is at the Visitor Center, so you can get your bearings and find out about the original history of the National Park and about the recent activity of the volcano. Then you can stop at various points around the huge caldera to get to see the special geological effects created by the volcanic activity over the years.

When my uncle and aunt lived in Ventura, while he was the general manager of a Mexican food factory, we would see Two Trees when visiting them, standing as a solitary pair high on a hill and remark on their beauty and solitude:  “At least they have each other.“ So it was a sad day when we visited the city and found that one of the trees was gone. All things change, of course. Let's just hope that someone has been forethoughted enough to plant another set of trees that will inspire the next generation as Two Trees did for ours.

The fountain provides a great backdrop of wedding photos. Almost any time of day, you can see a couple dressed in wedding clothes nearby having their photo taken as part of a commercial wedding package. Most of the couples are Japanese, as coming to Honolulu for a wedding is actually cheaper and easy to manage than the typical Japanese wedding event inside Japan.   The fountain also makes a great site for a photograph because Diamond Head peak can be seen in the background.

Hobson Grove is located in the city where my parents lived the longest and where I went to high school and university. So it was fitting that we hold a small family reunion at Riverview At Hobson Grover a few years back. During that time, there were some enactments of life back in when Riverview Mansion was in its heyday. The highlight was the appearance of a man who impersonated MarK Twain, and performed some excerpts of his literary pieces.

Fort Mason Park is an oasis of greenery and grass lawns, great views of San Francisco, and a great place to see the San Francisco Bay with views of the Golden Gate Bridge. It’s bordered by huge pine trees and is an easy walk to Fisherman’s Wharf, and even walkable to more central parts of the city. It’s a national park in actuality and there is also a hostel located right on the park grounds with a fair amount of parking available.

While still a teen, I got to get inside Churchill Downs for the Kentucky Derby race because my dad was working for a factory in Bowling Green that made a type of folding chair. We went to the Kentucky Derby in order to sell those chairs, which actually was quite a lot of work.  So much so that I don't remember much about the race or the horse that won the race that day.

You can view the Diamond Head Lighthouse from both the Diamond Head Road just above it, and also from Diamond Head Beach about 75 meters below it. There is no access to the lighthouse as it is off limits to the public.  Just below the Lighthouse, there is a steep hillside and from this elevation, you get good views of the surfers and of Waikiki Bay.

The Aquarium of the Bay is a densely packed, well designed assortment of living marine animals, mainly fish and invertebrates that makes a very informative excursion for visitors to Pier 39 on San Francisco’s Embarcadero. While not huge, it is certainly packed with interesting and attractive exhibits. My granddaughter was enthralled.

The Salton Sea is like visiting someplace on an alien planet, except is has the laid-back country feeling to it as well, so it has got to be on Planet Earth -- after all. I've been here in all seasons - and it's true it can be seemingly excruciatingly hot, But at least it's dry heat.

When you are in Hawi or Kapa'au,  there aren't  many places to actually reach the water at the coast. So Keokea Beach Park is one of those few places. In addition, you've got all the basic amenities to make your picnic or day at the beach fun and comfortable.

If you descend to Diamond Head Beach and them continue walking, you will eventually come to Kuilei Cliffs Beach Park. There are generally surfers off shore about 200-400 meters on most any day, but especially on weekends and holidays.

When my son lived in Mountain View, he often took his family to Shoreline Lake Park, and also brought me there when I was visiting (the granddad) from out of town. It's a very nice park. I enjoyed seeing the Canada geese (in season).

While I prefer a little less people than the way Waikiki Beach is packed on the typical day, you can't beat Waikiki Beach for the weather, the ambiance, and access to some great places along its great length.

We reserved one of the picnic pavilions and held a family reunion for about 40 people one summer. The park itself is not very big, but there is a city golf course adjacent to it, so it seems a lot bigger.

The entrance to the Makalei Beach Park is very inviting. The park is bigger than how it first appears from the street. There are some interesting older homes in the immediate area surrounding the park.
Even before I became a freshman student at WKU, I used to visit the Kentucky Museum as we lived just a short ways away on the Old Morgantown Road.
It's a very beautiful part of San Diego County. Except when there are brush fires (or worse), it's a great place to go hiking and camping.
When the other bars get too crowded at certain times of the day (4:30-7:30pm), then give Duke's Canoe Club a try.

First I would like to thank the staff for the kindness and consideration they showed us during our visit. They were wonderful in sharing their extensive knowledge of the history of New Almaden Quicksilver Mine and park.
The Mining Museum is housed in a building called Casa Grande, and was built in 1854, and renovated by the county five years ago at a cost of $6 million. It sure looks great and houses many mining artifacts. Casa Grande is a three story building with the top story dedicated to offices for the park, the bottom floor houses conference room and the ground floor is where the museum and gift shop are. Some of the rooms are furnished with mostly donated or loaned period furnishing that were not from Casa Grande, but fit right in. Furniture that was here are a book case in the office area and some other pieces, but most is donated. There is even a square Steinway piano that was donated. The floor in the left side room is original, but the floor in the right side rooms is a modern replica. Beyond the gift shop on the right are the exhibits, and they are excellent. Using mining artifacts collected by Constance Perham, the museum give you a sense of what life was like for the miners. These artifacts that were used by the miners give a sense of authenticity to this museum. Realizing that the Ohlone Indians were using cinnabar, which contains mercury, Mexican Cavalry Officer Captain Andres Castillero made the first mining claim in California in 1845. Mercury being crucial to the mining of gold and silver, New Almaden soon became and important factor in the California Gold Rush. Due to it's location, New Almaden soon displaced mercury from Almaden, Spain. Mercury was also shipped to other countries, including China,  because of it's location to coastal ports.
New Almaden Quicksilver mine was therefore a huge money maker and important economic driver for California. The museum also has an extensive archive of unique photographs because one of the managers and doctor were photographers, and they documented underground mine work as well as everyday life of the miners and their families. This archive is available online for free. The entrance fee is FREE, but if you want to contribute $2 to support the museum, there is a mailbox where you can put in some money, but this is completely voluntary.
Go see this museum, it is situated in a small valley where the company town was located. You can take a walking tour and see homes were the skilled workers lived, or visit the period cemetery. There are hiking trails that lead to mines and equipment used when the operation was active (now cleaned up and safe), and will give you a good workout. There are views that are awesome and relaxing. Casa Grande has a landscaped garden in the back with picnic benches. You can get married here, have a company meeting or just walk in and enjoy being in a building  166 years old. This is a historic place off the beaten path and worth your time to visit. So close to San Jose, this is a hidden gem.

The last mission and the only one built by the Mexican government. All the other missions were built by the Spanish government. The docent this afternoon was very knowledgeable and really made the history very interesting, she was awesome. Today was Children's Day and had many interesting activities and period crafts for kids and families. The docent let us know to check out the California Buckeye tree that was blooming with large white flowers. We were lucky to see this tree today because it only blooms once a year, and the flowers would be gone in ten days. The California Poppy flowers were blooming in front of the mission and the ranger had a friendly burro for kids to pet. I was greeted by the 2016 Alcalde of Sonoma, Mr. Patrick Garcia who was nice enough to introduce himself to me on his way into the Children's Day event, and what an interesting gentleman he was. I learned from him that he is a direct descendant of a member of the DeAnza expedition that founded San Jose, CA. What an interesting coincidence, since I live in San Jose.  On exhibit are artifacts of the mission period and water color paintings of all the missions as they were in the mid 1800's. The mother in law of General Vallejo is buried  in the chapel. This mission was in operation for only eleven years and unfortunately has some dark history in that over 900 Native American men, women and children died of disease they had no immunity to. These people were literally buried under your feet in unmarked mass graves. A plaque was placed in 1999 outside the mission in memory of these local people who died here. Like many parts of California, the history is not all pleasant, but it happened and we deserve to know about our past. This place is fascinating and I encourage anyone in Sonoma to go see it and enjoy learning about California history. Very recommended.
likes: Facilities & Services: Knowledgeable docent, Interesting exhibits
Activities: Children's Day events, Period crafts, Educational opportunities

reviews_attraction.text: All of the roses are blooming today and I purposely parked on the opposite side of the park so i could walk toward the sight. I got a subtle smell of the blooming roses as they came into view of the fountain. This place is so relaxing. You can sit near many varieties of roses and admire the colors and smells of them. There is a nice blue fountain in the middle with benches to sit on. Then sound of the water is relaxing too. There are some strategically placed redwood trees that look majestic in this this park. Come, walk around and see the many different roses in this award winning rose park. Sit in the grass or on a bench and relax during lunch. Walk or jog around the park if you want to get some exercise. The neighborhood is upscale and the homes are worth looking at too. This is a very safe area. There are water fountains and restrooms too. Kids love walking or running around. There are many people with cameras here and everyone has a smile on their face. It's a very unique park and right now April 25, 2016 the roses are in full bloom. This is another gem of a park in San Jose. Come here now and I promise that you will leave relaxed and happy for the experience.

This is a nice little park, and it has some interesting history behind it. Basically all of Communication Hill was owned by the Vieira family, who were  Azorean Portuguese immigrants. The family still owns, and I believe, resides on 30 acres of the hill. Communication hill has been developed in conjunction with KB Home, and there are a variety of housing types here. Since it's not a large area, this is the only park up here and it happens to be very nice, and has a view South. There is a play area for kids with a grassy field and benches around the park that make it nice to spend some time here. The kids play area has a soft rubbery surface, which is safer for kids if they fall. They also have swings, seesaw and a structure to climb on for the smaller kids. There are usually some kids for your child to play with and the parents are friendly. The park is quiet, and the noise from planes on landing approach into SJC is minimal. This is a nice place to stop and rest of you are on a walk up the hill for exercise. Definitely recommended.

WOW!!! It has been years since I have come here and I am still stunned by the opulence, the art and the wonderful views. This place is stunning. You pay $25 for adults, $12 for children and it gives you a bus ride up and a docent led tour of only part of the castle. We chose the upstairs portion of the castle per the recommendation of the ticket vendor. No matter where you go on this property, the view of the castle, grounds or landscape is stunning. The sheer opulence and wealth of this place and the people who built and lived here will amaze you. Yes, the Hearst family were wealthy beyond what we can imagine. They lived a life of leisure and freedom from toil and labor. They had many notable guests to their castle for their entertainment. You must go see this castle at least once in your life, because where else are you going to be let in to see how the super rich live. This is also a California State Park and your entry fee goes to support other state parks. Exceptionally Recommended!

What a nice place for a short gentle hike. I took the San Andreas Fault trail and it was easy and educational. This trail has minor elevation gain and loss, so even people who are not hikers can enjoy seeing the San Andreas fault. There are wildflowers here as well and a few good views. The trail is mostly in shade and in a canyon area, so views are a little limited, but it is still scenic and pretty. Obviously, there are many more trails and views in the rest of the park. This trail was only 1.1 miles, but there are other, longer trails here. Parking is good, and the information board is good and has trail maps for you. There is a bathroom across the street. There is no water, so bring plenty. Cell phone coverage is spotty on the trail. The drive up is scenic and you will see many huge mansions. Go and enjoy a day out, but wear insect repellent because there are ticks here. Recommended.

Crowded and expensive, but you must see this aquarium, it's worth it. It's one of the best in the world. The exhibits are educational and informative Great for kids and families. There is a gift shop and cafe. You will spend hours here, and if you want some air, just walk outside and enjoy the view, but if you leave the aquarium get your hand stamped for quick re-entry. Monterey itself is beautiful and you will enjoy the city and the restaurants they have. The bay and wildlife are right in front of you, you will see sea otters, sea lions and even whales. Gorgeous place and you should see it at least once in your lifetime. Go! Preferably on a weekday when the crowds are not as huge.

A nice place to walk along the river, but be aware of your surroundings because there are many homeless people with mental health issues living here, who are single men. Obviously, not all people who find themselves homeless in San Jose have mental health issues, some people are families that have found themselves in dire circumstances, but they are not usually here. It is best to not walk here alone, or at night. Otherwise, it is a nice place to walk or ride a bike because of the paved walkway. You are in downtown San Jose here and not far from restaurants and other attractions. Be safe and enjoy a nice walk here.

They close at 3 so just be aware of that. Getting onto the base requires the driver to show a driver's license. The museum is OK, it has a lot of uniforms, models, medals, pictures and some plane parts. Outside there are a few planes that are cool to look at. Since we arrived near closing time, we did not get up close to the planes. The giant blimp hangar is next to the museum and it is impressive too. It's a nice museum, but you have to be a hardcore military history buff to enjoy it. Kids won't really get into it, and there aren't any exhibits geared toward them, so they will quickly get bored.

Nice walk for kids and disabled adults thanks to the wooden walkway loop trail that runs along the creek and returns to the parking lot. The trail has several benches to sit along the way as well as some observation platforms. This is one of my favorite walks because you can leave the wooden walkway and continue on a dirt trail. It's really peaceful here with few tourist taking the short graded dirt road in. It's worth it, drive down and have a relaxing walk, but please take water and a hat because you are in a potentially dangerous heat. There are a couple of tables and a porta potty here.

This is a decent city park next to the Hayes Mansion, that used to be part of the property and later a small amusement park called Frontier Village. There is a playground for kids with swings and other features, some fake rocks for them to practice climbing, tennis and basketball courts. There isn't much green grass here, so don't expect to lay or play in a grassy field. There is a lot of dead grass and dirt, except for an area near the Hayes Mansion where there is a nicely kept lawn. The park is good for walking or jogging. Kids also skateboard here.

A nice place to go to the beach and see some tidepools, elephant seals, or just go for a hike. Some days can be windy, so dress warmly. There is about a 1/4 mile walk from the road to the beach on a well marked trails. Large "sneaker" waves can wash you out to sea and kill you, so do not turn your back to the ocean and be ready to run for your life. Also, watch your kids closely. The water is cold, so I would not swim without a wetsuit. There are not many services here, so be aware of that. Bring food and water and enjoy the beach. Be safe!

Free to enter, $3 to see the shuttle (parking $12). Great exhibits to inspire any kid or adult. This museum is a gem and a resource for the kids of Los Angeles and beyond. The space craft exhibit has scale models of space probes and space capsules. These exhibits are well done and lit very well so you can see a lot of the detail these modern artifacts have.
I have always loved this place since I was a boy, and it still impresses me as an adult. Go, take your kids and enjoy this wonderful museum and Exposition Park.

Monument to a genocidal freak who set up his own gulags for California  Natives. For real, those missions have mass graves.
They don't mark the path and they let nature grow a little wilder here. That is really good because most people will not see this ugly statue to Serra behind the trees. In time, nature will wipe this nasty stain from the history of decent people.
The views from here are nice, but there is no reason to have Serra here. It's the past now, we have moved on to the future.

The Sonoma Overlook trail is an easy hike, even with a chronic illness. Great views. Lots of people wearing spandex tights. Flowers and places to sit. Trail is in partial shade. I was told the trail was 1 to 1.5 miles to the top. The trail is not steep, but it is somewhat rocky and uneven so wear decent shoes, but even then I saw someone in sandals walk up. Bring water because there is none on the trail Beware of ticks, they carry Lyme disease and the trail sign warns of this.

Used to be a five star spot, but then they put fencing around it.
In the past you could drive through the streets that are now fenced off, and park and watch the planes or the sunset or the ocean. Now it is all surrounded by fencing and you can't see any blue butterflies or anything.
So this is just an area surrounded by chain link fencing. Nothing to see here, that is all in the past.

$3 to see one of human history's greatest technological and engineering achievement. Give your kids the benefit of seeing this, it might inspire them to reach higher.
The Shuttle exhibit is a really well done and for the price, there is no reason to miss this. They have a gift shop in there. Don't miss the External Tank outside. Excellent visit!

Nice view at 2,000 feet. Trails for hiking, trash cans, information board. Small parking lot and no bathroom or water. What do people do when they need to go to the bathroom? Bushes are not very big and trees are sparse and small. I guess you have be daring on the trail to relieve yourself. Watch out for ticks and stay on the trail.

Excellent placer to bring the kids. The California Science Center is free and seeing the Space Shuttle is only $3. Exposition Park is a gem from my youth. I spent a wonderful few hours here. It is peaceful and relaxing to walk around the exhibits and seeing so many school kids enjoying this great resource.

Free. One of my favorite places to daydream as a kid. The flowers are beautiful and smell great. There are gazebos to sit under, benches to sit on and a fountain. There are also water fountains. This is a great place to relax and it is next to the museums in Exposition park.

Easy hike that goes through Mountain Cemetery for a short section. All uphill until the loop at the top. Partial shade, no water, potential for infected ticks. Great views. Well worth the short hike. Doable in less than an hour at a slow pace. People run up in less time.

Great open space preserve, but not a lot of shade. Miles of trails and beautiful views while on your walk. There is ample free parking and bathrooms that are a little stinky.  There are water fountains to quench your thirst. I recommend you go early while it is cool.

Ahhh, depressing. Many homeless people camp around the park by the freeway. They are harmless poor people. There are also gentrification hipsters here and they are the worst. The park is ok, they have restrooms and water. Not a great park but one from my youth.

Free entrance. Excellent art galleries and historical exhibitions on the history of African American people in LA.
Highly recommended. The space is really nice, they have kid activities.
This museum deserves a visit if you are in Exposition Park.

A nice little park great for kids because of the playground. The Almaden community center and Almaden branch library is there too. Benches and tables are available for you to sit and eat. A nice little park.

Historic house in mountain view. Worth the visit if you are going to see the lake anyways. They have several tours going on every week. Several times a week you may tour the house and learn about the entrepreneur rengstorrf and his family. Several times a year they do environmental tours as well around the bay. Also check their calendar for other annual activities. You may event rent this venue for special occasions.

Medium size wharf with great views. Fishing is allowed. Worth the visit to the fish market and watch huge alive crabs to sell. Many sea lions wander around. There is a restaurant that offers food and drinkson site and to go during lunchtime on weekends and a beer place with a terrace. A free trolley goes from here to the Outlets in Pismo Beach during summertime but with a reduced schedule.

Awesome regional preserve that features species of special concern and threatened species. The artificial lake gives a romantic flare to the site. Birdwatching is a very fair activity to do here.  There is a restaurant, recreation facilities and a playground shaped as a boat. Since this is an old landfill BBQ are not allowed. Check the historic rengstoff house.

They have interesting species I have never seen before. But other than that I think is overpriced. It is small and don't have many animals. It is the oldest zoo in California and they have been trying to shut it down for a while now due to the animal conditions. It is great to see also the Sequoia park close by and its lake.

Nice playground with structures for almost all ages. There is a labyrinth and great slides similar to magical bridge playground. It has water fountains and restrooms. Nice sculptures and real old train at the entrance. Downside is dirtiness of the sand. So shallow that it's difficult to play with it. Need more maintenance

Free parking but little spaces. Beautiful walking hikes for the whole family to enjoy. Every spring docents offer free walks to see flowers during their blossoming. If you want to see the flowers on your own, they normally post outside their office pictures of the flowers you may encounter. It is a hidden jewel!

Great hikes to enjoy with kids, family and friends. Their lake is feed with trouts so besides your regular fishing license you need to purchase their daily fishing license for another $5. Entrance is not free. They have an small cafeteria that supply some foods and drinks.
