Inside the university you see this mission that contains a church, a cemetery and a museum with some artifacts like the previous bell gifted by Charles the third from Spain. There are better missions around California but if you have opportunity it's a good idea to visit.

Selected collection of items from a broad number of places and times. It's worth it to visit for whoever appreciates art. They hold permanent and temporary exhibitions. The outside Rodin sculptures remain always open unless there is an special event going on.

A great venue for children of all ages to learn about marine animals and see and touch some. Still I find that it's a bit pricey for what they offer but still worth to see at least once. Their volunteers are great. They hold a full blue whale skeleton.

Beautiful spot but way too crowded. Many people taking pictures including professional photographers. At walking distance there is a wave organ that it is very interesting as well but you have to go when tide is high and you wouldn't hear the music.

Interesting artifact that has been there for no more than 30 years. It is better to visit when the tide is high so you hear the music played by the sea. Views are good and close by you can see the palace of fine arts.

Beautiful and well maintained natural area. It has picnic tables, bbq, playground for infants and children and a splash park for Summer. Lots of grass and shady areas. Tennis courts and restrooms​ are present too.

Very complete outdoor recreation area. Contains a playground, a soccer field, restrooms, water fountain and a swimming pool. Close to downtown and walking distance to the library.  Also it has a parking lot.

Relaxing outdoors area that has hiking trails, a fishing lake and playgrounds for several ages. Birding isca great idea to perform here too. There are picnic areas with restrooms and a quiet environment.
Big outdoor park with many amenities for children. It has a magical bridge playground and also a splash pad. It has several restrooms, ball fields and the new library. There is also a cafe nearby.
A lot of old machines from the 40s. This is the old house of a doctor and has plenty of antiques mostly from office days. Interesting way to see how was technology almost 100 years ago.
Nice panoramas of the bay if you walk all the way to the Meadows. Many different flowers.   They have a small but nice environmental education center. Totally worth it.
A but pricey but could be a great venue for a  very​ special occasion or as a conference room. It's not exactly the original Adobe building but a replica.
The best thing they have is the train model upstairs and the recreation of Californio people dwellings. Great small museum to go with children.
Liked the location and the big parking lot. Has restrooms and water fountain. Playground is pretty cool and kids enjoy all the areas.
Small compared to the Monterey one but still worth it. They have special discounts for locals in their website. Children love it
Great beach to relax, play and enjoy. Not really crowded. Awesome view. Parking lot is half sized now due to construction.
Iconic place to eat, go for a walk or watch the sunset and the sea lions. Very beautiful panorama from here. A must-see.
Small but nice. You can walk it in 5 minutes. Interesting to see the origin of the name of Palo Alto and its Sequoias​.

One of the better County Parks in Santa Clara. Many people mention it's $6 to enter, but look at what you get for the whole family: lakeside gazebo with BBQ pits, big lawn area for picnics and all kinds of family sports, beach volleyball field, horse shoe throwing area, a massive dog park, hang glider field, tennis courts, and many family friendly animals you can see and take pictures with.
The highlight is the hike to the peak, many people take that challenge as the incline can get steep for the unmotivated. But the view is breathtaking along the entire way, and you will be surprised to find huge cows lying around the summits, motivating you to climb further.
Pro tips: the hike is mostly uncovered, so bring sun protection and water to rehydrate.

Very easy to walk park. Their trail is completely paved, and even strollers can be pushed through out the entire park. This ranch is located right next to all the buildings where they house small animals they have rescued or found within the ranch. The ranch houses a community garden, along with some pretty rude owners who think they own this place (note the word "community").
Try walking a bit further and you will find volleyball courts, bocce ball courts, playgrounds, and a golf course with horrible players who can't keep their balls on the fairway.
Despite all the horrible golfers, patrons, and garden owners, this place is pretty awesome to visit.

Relaxing and pretty place for families of all sorts to come and enjoy. This park is from San Jose's sister city, Okayama-Shi, located in Japan, and everything in here preserves the Japanese serenity and traditional beauty.
What's not beautiful are some Instagram girls and wannabes who come here and hog the small walkways so they can take 470 pictures of themselves under the changing leaves.
Insider tip, parking and entrance are free during Covid, so there are plenty of people visiting this place. The best autumn leaves Kodak moments were between Nov 19-26. Don't forget to walk around the surrounding park and Happy Hallow if you have the time.

What a nice short trail to walk around with everything being nicely paved and labelled. The trail is only 0.25 miles, so it's a great trail to go on with your little ones, and because you are on an elevated boardwalk, you won't get your shoes dirty and the trail is even perfect for wheelchair access. I suggest driving up Little Airport road to park in the parking lot right next to the trail instead of hiking 6 miles from the Van Damme park entrance. If you are interested, you can also hike on the 1.2 or 2.3 mile trail to the Fern Canyon in the same park.

Just a historic sign for people to take pictures with in the middle of the road. Now the sign has its own parking lot, a long wait to get to the front for pictures, and hustling camera men vying for your business. Not sure what the hype is all about, I used to drive by this sign and it would stand all alone, in the middle of the road. It has unfortunately turned into a huge tourist trap since then.
Good thing that this place is still free as of last visit. That may not last long once locals realize the revenue they can generate off of it.

Nice light house museum to visit when you are in the area. There is a nice parking lot with plenty of spots, free Wi-Fi, and charging stations (2 level 2 chargers) for EV's. After this, you take a short hike of 0.5 miles to the light house. There is also a cool aquarium to visit with more information about marine life. Then you get to the main attraction, the light house museum. The light house is still in operation, and the museum below has plenty of cool information about shipwrecks around the area and souvenirs to buy.
likes: Facilities & Services: Parking, Wi-Fi, Charging stations

reviews_attraction.text: Massive park with lots of green grass to sit on and picnic areas with BBQ grills for parties with reservations. During the weekend you can see families grilling BBQ Meats on the park provided grills scattered around the park, and kids running around on the trail with their scooters or bikes, while their parents pass football on the grass. I really enjoy this park much more than other smaller parks. Bring a Frisbee and picnic basket with you to enjoy a Lazy Afternoon with your loved ones in this massive Park.

I have been to Alviso Marina Park many times, and it is a beautiful place that's always empty. You can feel like you have this whole place to yourself.little did I know, they have a free Salt Marsh Safari Guided Boat tour periodically when the tide is right. You do have to go online to sign up, but trust me, the trip is totally worth it. Great ranger talk, comfortable cruise to ride on, and good company, everything is going well for this place. Sign yourself up, you won't regret it.

Great park close to the Bay Area for a weekend getaway for the real camping experience. Unlike the crowded and expensive national parks that's further away, Mt. Madonna provides a good balance of proximity and sleeping among the redwoods in California. Of course, hiking is a must do in the park, and discovering all the harmless insects along the way is an added benefit. Book early to reserve a campsite, and stay the weekend to take in the beautiful scenery in this fantastic park.

When I arrived here in December, I guess the rain has caused the campsites and trails to be flooded, so many areas were closed. Aside from that, the ranger at the entrance helped us find a viable route that we can go in and walk around. There is no fee for day use purposes, but if you choose to stay here or camp, then there is a fee associated. The boardwalk and the beach are the main attractions here. Everything was clean and well labeled. I would come back again.

A nice free museum in San Francisco that's suitable for the entire family. The men can enjoy the grease smell and the mechanics of the cable car engineering, the women can shop to their hearts delight in the gift shop, and the kids would be fascinated by the loud cable noises and the photo ops with the many actual working parts of the cable museum. This is what makes SF unique and we need more of these attractions to keep people coming to the Bay.

A really busy park located along San Tomas/Montague. Due to its convenient location, it's a hub for family and friends gathering for picnic and BBQ. The large field and grassy area is good for kids to play on, or adults to show that they can still play soccer. The picnic tables allow the groups to gather and host birthday parties.
They also have play areas for different aged kids. They removed the sandpit a year ago due to sanitary reasons.

A quiet tourist trap that warrants one visit on your lifetime. If you are in the area and have little ones to entertain, this is a good place to stop and spend a couple of hours watching the geyser, and playing + feeding the small animals. The geyser is not as impressive as the one in Yellow Stone, but consider this as geyser-lite, then you will be OK.
It is a little expensive, but you get the whole place to yourself, so that's good.

Big tree loop is an easy 0.1 mile loop, but I would also recommend the Circle loop (0.3 miles) that is attached to the Big Tree, so you can get away from all the crowd at the Big Tree. You can also get a little more of that stroll through the forest experience. Big Tree parking lot is also nicely equipped with bathrooms and explanation placards. I guess this trail is also wheelchair friendly as most of the way is paved.

Fun castle built in 2007 equipped with everything a castle has: a moat, drawbridge, cellars, a torture room, and a dungeon. It's a family fun experience for an afternoon. I suggest taking the guided tour (a little pricer than the self-led tour), which is 1 hour long, and then tag on another 45 mins of wine tasting. With the guided tour, you get more behind the scenes look and entrance into restricted areas.

Hidden gem in the outskirts of Fort Bragg. This was used by old trains to carry lumber down to the cities in the old lumber days. Since those days are long gone, this trestle has been converted to pedestrian use only. The Pudding Creek Beach is a hidden treasure where you won't find anyone else on the server beach with you, and you get to enjoy the same million dollar coast view as any other tourist points.

This is not the traditional Disney experience for the kids. Quite a bit of awards and the old Disney drawings from yesteryear's. Very cool to learn about the history and the printing process from the first Disney publications and how far they have come to today's success. Once again, don't bring your young kids here expecting a good time.
P.S: very friendly staff. Disney sure knows how to train them.
dislikes: Attraction Type: Not suitable for young children

reviews_attraction.text:
In my opinion, the prettiest and finest beach in the Monterey area. There are plenty of other beaches around, but the sand is not as comfortable, the beach is not as wide, or accessibility is not as convenient.
This beach is hidden among residential neighborhoods, but it is a gem not to be missed. I will make sure I come here every time I visit Monterey.

Always a tourist destination to represent all that is wonderful about Monterey. The place is so pretty, basically all the tourists have to come here to indicate that they have visited Monterey. Try the secluded beach that's hidden from the popular park and the big beach, this is where you will find amazing tide pools and wild life aplenty.

A rare swamp conservatory in the middle of Silicon Valley. Very cool that they had the foresight to carve out this piece of land just for this Natural purpose. Kids and adults alike will enjoy this place by walking around and taking in the various information printed on the side of the paths for your reading pleasure.

Small neighborhood park hidden among the houses and apartments nearby. Despite its size, it still has multiple play structures for different aged kids, and benches for the adults to sit and wait.
They used to have a sandpit for kids to play in, they must have removed them for sanitary reasons.
Big pretty park with bad logistics for parking and exit. Great location and I hope they can work out their routing issues to ensure smooth visits by all.
A very crowded Plaza with high end stores and hotels around. The only time people visit this place is during Christmas in the Park around the holidays
One of the nicer baseball stadiums around. Overpriced food and products as expected, and Giants happen to be one of the better teams on the roster.
Interesting place for kids to learn how to build things. We walked away with two custom built shelves for the kids.

The worst part of Saltair is that they are a big concert venue that attracts a lot of great acts because really, the other reviews are right. Their customer service is dismal. Parking is an absolute nightmare. They have an indoor and outdoor venue space and despite sketchy forecasts days and hours in advance, they have repeatedly held shows outside and then cut them short when the weather became too severe and never offered refunds or to move the show inside. I love a lot of groups that perform here, but it's getting harder and harder to suck it up. Especially when the facility itself needs so much improvement and you just know the owners are sitting on piles of cash. It's a real shame because it has so much potential.

The Living Planet aquarium is pretty decent for a desert state. They have a lot of room to grow in their new facility and I'm hopeful for the future. As it is now, I think it's overpriced and lacks some key exhibits. They changed their pricing to include the old separate cost of watching one of their films, so make sure you watch at least one because you're paying for it now either way. I did think the staff was knowledgeable, attentive and accessible. The penguin feeding is insanely crowded so go early to get a good spot. You can also watch it from below, but I don't think you'll be able to hear the presenter.  It's definitely a fun one time thing, but I am hopeful for future growth.

Seriously, don't forget to stop by the Alamo. And don't let it's small size turn you away. The history of this hallowed ground maintains "Everything's Bigger in Texas". The gardens out back are beautiful and you should definitely visit the barracks along the perimeter before you leave. You can't take pictures inside and outside they will let you take pictures, but will stop you if you make gestures like the peace sign. Also the perfect spot to watch the battle of flowers parade each April as each entry leaves a bouquet with the guard to place on the front lawn of the Alamo. Alas, there is no basement.

The home of the Mormon Tabernacle Choir, numerous cultural events and a world wide General Conference twice a year in April and October for members of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. There is a beautiful waterfall, free tours, and a huge Rooftop garden with native plants and a river. Inside there are several amazing pieces of art and a Hall filled with busts of all the Prophets of the church in modern days. They also have a "Little Theater" where they host a Christmas production each year on the life of Christ.

One of the best parks in all of Utah County for sure. This huge park has fields, tennis courts, and a brilliant playground of adventure and "Discovery". Everyone's favorite is the volcano or rocket ship. They also have really cool swing sets and tire swings. It's a great place to bring the kids and let them run around and use their imagination. If you're not up for running around with them, you can sit at the front where the only entrance/exit to the playground is, so you can catch your kids before they run out.

This park is particularly expansive. Do your research before heading out if possible. There is much to see in every zone but getting from place to place, could take all day, even if you drive. I've been to the Needles and Island in the Sky and loved both. Bring a good camera. You won't regret it. Bring plenty of water and food and blankets in the trunk just in case. We had to be towed out of here once and it was a huge ordeal. Be prepared.

First, be careful. There's the future dad in me. These are ruins right on the oceans edge and there are signs warning of people getting swept off and out to sea. But second, go visit this beautiful place at sunset. It's a truly spectacular place to take photos and enjoy the view of both the Golden Gate Bridge and the Endless Pacific ocean. And head up to the visitor center and learn a little about this places unique history.

I feel like when you hear National Portrait Gallery, it may sound a little boring compared to dinosaurs or space shuttles, but I was in awe at the variety of portraits representing hundreds of people from throughout American History. Presidents, social activists, athletes, performers, religious leaders, all woven together in a beautiful museum that really exemplifies the melting pot that is America.

Beautiful, sprawling park in Orem, UT. Water features, a giant lake, ducks, a rose garden, playground and tons of open grassy fields make this one of the prettiest spots in Orem. Definitely popular for picnics, family reunions and easy afternoons in the park with the kids, this place has something for everyone. Bring your camera. Bring bread to feed the ducks. Come enjoy this beautiful space.

Slate Canyon Park is rather small currently, but now has a paved parking lot, pavilion and seating and official trailhead for Slate Canyon. The views of the city are spectacular, especially at Sunset. As far as I know, there isn't a grassy green space yet, but it's a huge improvement over the "side of the road" that used to be the starting place for adventures up Slate Canyon.

This is the most serene, peaceful, beautiful acre of all of San Francisco if you ask me. There are beautifully ornate pagodas and structures, a huge bronze Buddha, lovely water falls and koi ponds and masonry. There's also really cool bridge you can take pictures on. They have a lovely tea shop and gift shop as well. It's totally worth the cost of admission. Go go go!

The Museum of Art has been a staple for high quality art from around the world for over a decade. From exhibits featuring the Etruscans, The Imperial Tombs of China, the religious works of Christ from cathedrals and palaces in Europe and more, there is always something beautiful to see and experience at the MOA. Plus they have a great café.

I think this is a beautiful park under the Bay Bridge and next to AT&T Park with the famous bow and arrow statue. It's right along the waterfront and provides a great view of the city and bay. There are often homeless people sleeping along the edge of the park, but if you're in San Francisco this is true of almost every park.

I love it because it is iconic. But San Francisco is a city of Iconic architecture and landmarks. That doesn't make these houses any less special. Plus you get a stunning view of the financial district and downtown skyline. So come take some pictures and throw them up on Instagram and be a part of the cool kids.

Usually a homeless hangout spot during the week. On the weekends they kick everyone out for the farmers market. During the late summer it's also the home of the Twilight Concert series each Thursday night. Concerts are only $5 in advance and have featured Death Cab For Cutie and other national and local acts.

One of the most Beautiful buildings architecturally speaking in Auburn. It's great place to take a few minutes to explore while you are on I80 traveling back and forth across the country. It's right off the freeway and you can snap a picture of the giant gold digger at the same time. :-)

Beautiful space full of art, culture, history and amazing water features. Home of the Tower of the Americas, it's a lovely spot to hang out on a summer afternoon or come visit one of the festivals or watch the fireworks on the fourth of July. Lots of historic buildings onsite as well.

A wonderfully unique Temple. A place of refuge in a traditionally dangerous and divided city. The view of San Diego from across the bay is unparalleled. The Temple grounds also include a public visitors center and a stake center for conferences and special firesides.

The museum to go to in San Antonio. Huge variety of anthropology and natural history displays. Great art. Awesome interactive features for kids to make learning fun. The San Antonio river runs right through the back park. And I believe Tuesday afternoons are free!

Fun park with a playground, splash pad and huge fields. Several pavilions for parties and picnics. During the summer the splash pad is always packed and in the evenings there are some fun events. The playground is massive, covered and great for kids of all ages.

This is the most beautiful part of the National Arboretum.  The bonsai are masterful and creative. Very beautiful. Plants in bloom throughout the year.  There are several different pavilions and cultural areas, make sure you check them all out.

Beautiful gardens and greenhouses featuring plants and flowers from across the country. They also have a cool set of replica monuments in the front area. There are also beautiful outside gardens across the street. And it's all free.

They took all the original sandstone columns from the United States Capital and replaced them and put the original ones here in this garden. Great place to take photos and see a piece of history. And admission is free.

Quaint little neighborhood park. Small playground and a few structures/features for kids to use. Several trees provide some shade. It's nothing special but nice for the local kids to have a little green space to play
This line is a little slower, but it's a beautiful lift and fun ride. Not too scary. Good speed. Classic coaster.

we stumbled upon this little garden by pure accident and i was ecstatic that it was open to the public. the sculptures are so nicely made and the actual garden feels secluded from all the hustle and bustle just a street away. if i'm in the area again i'd really like to make my way inside the gallery and see what they have to see. if you want to enjoy a quick 5 minute break from walking the city, i highly suggest stopping by here to enjoy the art.

they absolutely need to lower the price of admission. this is a real quirky and weird museum. you will more than likely not be familiar with anything inside as most of the works are strange or other wordly. they need to work on their A/C as well and some of the 'buttons' to displays did not function properly. it's worth it to come and visit but it's definitely not the best museum by a long shot. it's a strange place overall to be honest.

i accidentally stumbled upon this park only because i was in the general area. there was another park near me but i chose to come here as it looked bigger on the map but i am so glad i visited Smith Park. there is a small skate park which i spent some time watching the skaters. the rest of the time spent here i made it all around the park on my own while skating my own board. there is a lot of parking which also was a plus!

it was an incredible experience to drive out here and visit this temple to see it in person. it's not the biggest by size but it's definitely worth the trip. i was lucky enough to show up right before a prayer ceremony took place. i stood in the back while the actual followers of the religion followed along in their own language with the prayers. it's a great place to visit even through this whole CoViD lock down.

we were sad to see that the maze and train ride were so expensive. we ended up spending that money on gifts instead. the line for ice cream, dole whip and food items was extremely disorganized and was all over the place. i'm surprised that hasn't been addressed or taken care of. the bathrooms were clean. if you pass by the location by the roasted nuts make sure you get some, they are delicious

this place is absolutely worth the price of admission and the time that you spend here! 5 stars! it's a self guided walk through with little informative videos (i highly suggest you watch them) there is so much to know and learn about martial arts that you wouldn't even realize it. if you're in the area or even have minimal interest in martial arts, you should definitely stop by

there are a lot of winding trails in this park and different routes to walk around through. the trail is well maintained and pretty busy the later in the afternoon it gets. i suggest get here early and leave early as well. overall, it's an easy to get to location and it's close to home. there is somewhat of a difficulty when it comes to finding and parking there though.

We arrived at around 10am just before the huge rush of people @ 11. There is a terrible parking situation and signs posted all over for towing (we saw a car get towed) just be careful and read signs properly. I would highly suggest to come early and leave early. It gets very crowded and you are stuck at certain points behind people or a big group along the trail

do not underestimate this hike! you will need to pack water and dress comfortably. you will be tired if you are not active prior to visiting. i suggest you stretch and prep yourself. it's a grueling uphill battle but the reward is so worth it once you are up there. if i were to come back to the islands, this would be one of my top 3 things to come back and do!

i actually really liked this park. i was driving home from a day spent out in LA and decided to stop by here and skate a little just as the sun was going down. there were only about 2 cars in the parking lot but about 20 people actually in the park. it seemed like where some of the locals liked to gather around. it was very clean and well maintained as well.

this arena was great! the staff is professional and helpful everywhere I went. i came here for a Blackhawks hockey game and was in the 'standing room' only section. i felt like a real fan with everyone around me drinking and having a good time! if i ever come back to Chicago i know to come and see another hockey game! that's for sure!

what else would you expect but the best from here? if you are thinking about coming here... stop thinking about it and go! in some cases there are long lines but it is always worth it. i would highly suggest putting nacho cheese and bacon on your fries it goes great and it's not overwhelming. i love coming here for a bite to eat.

i guarantee that you'll be here for 15+ minutes trying to get the best picture you can. it's actually really great that they blocked it off due to CoViD which doesn't allow people to just crowd around it. it's tough to find a parking spot close but once you're here it's worth it to really enjoy this art piece and look around.

the remains of the "castle" are hardly any. take a good look at the pictures and decide if you want to go or not. it's currently under construction and fenced off. i don't know if someone purchased it or they are fixing it up but i wouldn't suggest coming up here as the leftover ruins are barely worth talking about

this is a great pier and i really liked it because it doesn't really have a gimmick besides it just being what it is. it's got a restaurant at the beginning and a small gift shop near the end. it's simple and it has really nice views. my favorite part is leaning over the edge and being able to see a train go by.

awesome place! great value! i got the seasonal pass and had a blast on the mini golf courses! they are well maintained and really clean! it was a little busy for a sunday afternoon but the good part about that was having a bigger group for laser tag! a good sized room for laser tag too and a lot of fun!

this has always been a great spot to come and take a walk around in. a couple years ago they shut it down and remade it which was a great idea. they should more with it and make it even better. you have a great view of the city and are only a couple steps away from the metro light rail

the parking here is a bit slim and it gets packed. this is an extremely easy trail. i enjoyed it for a nice break and good scenery. there is not a lot of people and the actual trail is well maintained. i would definitely suggest to come here because most people don't know about it

i enjoyed this street art at the end of this dead end street. there was nowhere to park so you might have to walk down the street but it was a pretty nice area right by. make sure you go down the street and grab a bite to eat somewhere! i'll be coming back to walk the stairs

there is plenty of parking available here which was awesome to see when driving up to the location. i noticed a ton of people with picnic baskets and blankets to just lay on the grass with. it's a great spot to spend some time in the sun enjoying the views.

huge park! there's a lot of parking and so much space to play. the grass seems kind of patchy with dirt in the middle of the soccer fields but nothing too crazy. the skate park also draws huge crowds and there is a YMCA here.
probably the best view of downtown that you can get on foot. i highly suggest to put this on your itinerary and make the trip for this. there isn't much else around so just enjoy the view
beautiful. make sure you go down the stairs and make it down to the shoreline it is quite a walk but so worth it for the view of the cliffs and ocean.
awesome park, great view of the river and buildings around. always worth the walk down to kind of get away from the hustle and bustle of the city.
great museum. the staff is also knowledgeable if you have any questions. would like to return when they have a new set of art!

Our first time here was amazing. The staff and trainers are so friendly here! The experience I had with my family was just wonderful. My daughter got to touch a dolphin and she was just blown away. She interacted with them, and learned so many things, and so did we. This park offers things Orlando didn't. The orca trainers are just great people. Shout out to Tom who helped me meet Corky, a whale I never thought I'd get to see. They do so much good for the animals that live there and for wild animals alike. I'm glad I had the opportunity to go here as often as I did!

This place is truly amazing. Most of what you do is driving, pulling over and walking. The views are beautiful, and there is so much wildlife to see. The gators that are gathered around the old rice field is pretty awesome. I saw eagles, several species of waterfowl, gators, lizards, all sorts of things. I didn't even see the whole place. But it is worth going again, and again if you love birding and wildlife viewing.

I love this place! It can get EXTREMELY busy, especially on the weekends. During the week, it is much more manageable. You can walk your dogs, and take your kids to play, and when you're done, have a picnic. It's along the bay, so you can get some beautiful views of the water and SF in the distance. It's always clean, and it's nice to see rangers actually here and making sure everything is in order.

This is a great place to take your dogs for a walk off leash. There is at least 3 miles worth of walking here. They are making a disc golf area so the back part is being worked on. It doesn't stop me from going. The picnic area is surrounded by pine trees and there is a trail to walk through them. It's nice to feel like you've gotten out of the city for a minute.

I love it here. You can walk around for hours. The local bald eagles are awesome, and the hundreds of birds that live around there too. You can also take your horse and go riding on the trail that extends around the outside of the marsh. Trails are well marked walking and riding. I'm sure I have places I haven't seen yet there.

This place really promotes conservation, and teaches people to be aware of what they put out into the world and how it can harm animals. It was busy, but the exhibits were awesome. The kelp forest and the deep sea were  amazing. I enjoyed seeing the types of jelly fish under human care as well. This place is worth a visit.

If you want to get away from the hustle of the city, come here. You can walk five miles...and then walk some more. The landscape is amazing. You can do some hiking, or just leisurely walk along the boardwalk. Biking too is popular. I don't see dogs here, so I assume they are not allowed. Excellent place to look at birds.

We have had a great time, each time we've gone. My daughter loves the animals, and learning about them. It's a smaller zoo, nothing huge and fancy, but it's well cared for. It's clean, the enclosures are nice and nothing looks horrible. I do hope they are able to update more and more as they've been doing this last year.

I love this place. The trails are a work out! But the view is amazing. Access to the beaches along the way, and I haven't even seen the full park. Lots of people on the weekends, and parking at the lot by the Cliffhouse is usually not very successful. Hard to find parking around there. But it's worth the view.

This place has great views, and if you want a work out, go for it. One of the few places that is off leash for dogs, but be warned that not all dogs here are friendly. A few went after a dog and tried for mine the other day. I'm a dog lover, but it really ruins it when people can't control their dogs.

Coming here in the morning is totally worth it. Seeing the harbor, and all the ships leaving, catching a glimpse of some dolphins...lots of birds. It's really nice. Going for a walk through the garden is nice as well. I like this part of the city. Mostly all of Charleston is beautiful though

What's not to like about this place. You can watch people fish all day, and watch the egrets try and steal all the bait. You can watch the dolphins and manatees come in, and you can go do a little shelling not far off the beach. I come here every time I visit, or at least I try to.

I love this place! Nice walk, the pier is wonderful. My daughter loves the park. It's nice to be able to stop and get some coffee and a bite to eat as well. I love coming here. The gift shop is cute as well. It is clean, and everybody there is usually extremely nice.

There is a lot of history here, and that is what I love about it. The gardens are beautiful and the swamp is pretty awesome. I love all the different animals you will see. It is also extremely peaceful. It is worth coming to at least once while visiting.

The mission of this place is so wonderful. The work they do is amazing. It was awesome to meet Winter and Hope...and see what they do behind the scenes. Definitely worth the money. I am excited to see the new building once it's all done.

The wildlife here is amazing. So many things to see. I haven't even walked the whole swamp yet and I've seen a variety of animals. It's definitely worth your time to go slow and explore, there is so much to miss! Can't wait to go back.

I love it here. It is so beautiful. Views of the Cooper river, and the gardens are lovely. There are alligators here, and usually the ponds are blue which makes it all so wonderful. I love coming here to walk after a long day.

Dolphins! Birds, crabs, fish, all sorts of creatures. We met some awesome people there too! I love this place. It's enjoyable to just walk and see the wildlife and the shrimp boats. Can't wait to go kayaking here.

This place is pretty freaking awesome. Parking can be a pain, but this whole park is definitely worth it! You can have parties here, a picnic, it's also clean. Lots of walking trails. My daughter loved it

I'd say this place is worth at least a visit. They do a lot of conservation work so that's a plus. Pretty expensive though. They could have more exhibits. But my daughter enjoyed it so that was worth it.
When is this place not awesome. I am so happy to see that they are working and expanding. Can't wait to see the finished project. The bear cubs were amazing. Never seen one before. What a great place
This park is right next to my daughter's school, and it's very convenient. It's well maintained, clean, and welcoming. A nice place to have a picnic.
I loved this park, and I totally miss it. Lots of walking trails, a small cafe and it is dog friendly. Not very expensive to get in.
I love this place! You get great views of the lighthouse, and there is so much walking to be done! Once it warms up I am going back.
Awesome farmers market, and easy parking. I love how nicely located it was to so many othwr things as well.

The legion of Honor is a sister museum The deYoung and Golden Gate Park. If you go to both of these museums to see there temporary exhibits the price of the ticket roughly is $28. To just go into the basic parts of the museum for their long-standing exhibits the price is $15. it is very cost-effective if you go very often to buy an annual pass. So I got the annual pass at The de Young for $119 which emits one person plus a guess. You could buy a family pack that allows for people in annual pass but that price increases.
So this may be like a fourth and fifth time I've been to the Legion of Honor.  They had their museum set up where the special shows are down the stairs and requires a special ticket. The upper floors has their main collection which is usually there year-round though it can't get rotated with other collections.  Do take the time to walk around and enjoy the museum. You can actually get through the whole museum probably in two and a half hours including the special exhibit.
You have to be mindful of where you're allowed and not allowed to take pictures. It's especially busy on the weekends of you're seeing a special exhibit it's going to be crowded and parking may be a little difficult.  also be mindful of what you leave in the car because there has been break-ins in the area.
They have a cafe downstairs and a food is moderately priced and actually pretty good.  I'm a very nice day I enjoy eating out in the patio.

So 19 of us headed over at different time, thinking the final show was 8:00pm, so we took our time eating dinner at the Ferry building before heading over on the F train.  Some of our friends got their earlier and found out we needed to be there by 7:00pm for the final show.  So in a great rush we headed down that way.  This place is next to the wax museum, the signage gets all mixed in with all the flashing signs.  We get in and were rushed through the photography done in the beginning because they wanted us to start the tour ASAP.  So we got one group picture taken and sent on our way down a stairwell.  They tell you to use the bathroom before starting the tour.  You go through different rooms with different themes, it's quite fun because they were using people in the audience, but twice they used their own staff member.  We were laughing really hard at our friend who got picked from the back of the room.  The whole process took a little over an hour, at the end, we got a chance to buy our group photo.  We only had the option of a large print for $20 which will hang at the office.  I didn't find it scary at all and it was way more fun to go with a group of friends.

If you're going to the Statue of Liberty, it's best to pre-order your ticket rather than waiting for day of.  I wasn't paying attention when I ordered the tickets, but they also included Ellis Island.  When ordering online, you pick the time you want to go to Statue of Liberty  We didn't want to walk up all the steps to the crown so we only ordered tickets to the pedestal.  I did will call tickets, remember you need your confirmation number to pick up your tickets.  The buy day of line is really long and they might not have crown tickets available day of.  Buying tickets ahead really made planning the visit easy.  Will call line was pretty quick to pick up tickets.  Then you go through security before boarding, so leave those bags with wheels, knives, and other things at home/hotel.  Treat it like airport security.

Parking is across the street along the road.  when I drive by, I missed it the first time because I was looking for a parking lot.  This place is a groove of trees which is a home to Monarch Butterflies colony from November to February.  It's always good to do a bit of research before coming here.  If you come too early or when it's cold, it might be hard to see any before because they don't become active until it's a bit warmer.

There's volunteer docents who come and provide information.  Check the website for the schedule.  Bring binoculars or a telescope because they can be way up high in the tree tops or flying high above.

The Sutro baths was San Francisco's giant indoor swimming pool using salt water from the bay.  What we see now is the remains of the building after a fire that destroyed the building.  If you didn't know about the building, it's hard to figure out what was there, but seeing old pictures you can picture the place just by the outline of the stone walls.

We like going here and walking along the beach and on parts of the wall that look safe.  It's a  great to explorer (carefully explorer) and enjoy the view.  From here you can hike to Lands End.

Crissy field is a big green field, but there's many things to do here.  Grab a cup of something hot at the warming hut and then go check out what people are catching at the pier.  You'll probably want to take some pictures on the pier, but watch your step.  Sometimes you'll see people board paddling or dolphins swimming in the water.

Update 10/13/2016 - This is a Federal park, now you have to pay for parking 7 days a week.  You'll see patrol cars ticketing.  Parking isn't very expensive, but find a pay station because they will ticket.

This museum catalogs different times periods of Ferndale's history.  they change the display in January when the museum is closed. The mission for the museum is $2 a person. Additional donations are optional as it keeps the museum open. There is also a lower level room which contains more Hardware and tools use during the time. Such as saws, hammers, buggies, even Bob wire.  They also have twice-monthly blacksmith demonstrations of the days do vary so you might want to call in advance to ask.

This places has about 1000 kids running around, well maybe not 1000, but there's a lot of kids running around.  If you bring your kids here, be proactive because theirs 3 different areas to play in and there's a lot of people here, it's easy to suddenly have a missing kid.  There's also not much shade here so bring sunscreen and lots of water.  This is a great place to let kids burn off excess energy because there's plenty of kids for them to make friends with.

Scotia is an old logging town when they were still allowed to cut down trees.  You'll noticed that many of the buildings have large tree trunks as part of the building design and look like pillars from afar.  This museum documented the history of the town, the lumber industry and the old mill (which is still in production until all the wood have been processed and sold).  The various types of saws blade used (lengthy, width) is displayed through the museum.

This museum covers both old and new forms of media.  We had just missed the Batman exhibit and the new Jim Henson exhibit wasn't up yet.  They had a whole Mad Men displayed, though I don't follow the show, the set up was impressive.  Some of the displays are interactive - game of old school donkey kong anyone?  Or want to do a voice over?  Then there was models, clothing, and props on display.  This does take a few hours to go through and it's so much fun.

I think this is something you have to do once in your life if you live in Nor Cal.  The awesomeness of the trees that are hundreds of years old stretching so high you can't see much of the blue skies above our heads.  The road isn't crazy busy, we hardly saw any cars going in either direction.  This is a side road, the main road is about 5 miles shorter while this one runs through the redwood forest.  We got some amazing photos.  It's so peaceful here.

All I can say is Wow to the newly remodeled SFMOMA.  The space is a lot easier to move around.   I suggest going early,  but noon on a Saturday it was starting to get crowded.  Remember to hang on to your ticket stub because they'll need to scan them before you enter.  Give yourself plenty of time to walk around.   We were there for almost 3 goes and still doesn't get to see everything.

There's a lot going here in these buildings.  There's dance, music, and art with limit showing times.  Where can you go where a whole art display is created around vinyl records which you can spin on record players.  Or write message on a wall?  Watch beautify dance movements.  This is the place, you have to keep track of the calendar because there's a lot going on here.

This is part of the Alvisio Park, we just walking from one side to another.   It's vet peaceful here.   Great place for bird watching/ photography.   We came early morning which is prefect toner of day.   Bring sunscreen and a hat.   There's no shade out here and obey the signs.  You wouldn't want to be trapped if the water rises.

I like it when the art is created around the neighborhood. And by this I mean that the used books in a sense that they are birds in flight. But I feel like it is also a nod to City Lights bookstore. The fact that this has been here for a long time but it also shows that it's been well-maintained and kept up.

This beautiful bridge leads to several walking trails, Mediterranean garden, and underside of the bridge.  Many people come here for an evening walk. There's lots of parking in the evening.  The only thing I would be worried about is rattlesnakes, as they have warning signs posted.

There's always fun stuff going on, it can be art, a gathering, cultural events...  This is a nice place where the weather is nice, grab some food or a drink and enjoy the sunshine.  Don't forget to take pictures of the heart art on the corners of the square.

This is the more recognized-able building in the park.  You can enter the castle through the side door and walk into small coves to read the story of Sleeping Beauty.  This space is small and can be difficult to enjoy the displays when it's crowded.

It is so beautiful here.    People take photo walks here or ride their bikes.   Watch the signs as they direct you what trails are open to the public.  You also may want to plan early morning hikes because it can get warm here and there's no shade.

Going a bit further west past Crissy Fields, is Fort point.  Just below the Golden Gate Bridge you get a mix of weather, sometimes its bright and sunny and minutes later a blanket of fog will roll in.  Many people come here to take pictures.

The zoo is cute and very small.  You won't get a giant variety of animals here, especially the exotic type.  It doesn't take very long to go through the whole zoo, but it's good for young children.  The place was pretty empty.

This is a tourist attraction for sure.  This is a take off the 80's TV show Off the same name.  You go though rooms/displays of fascinating discovery around the world.  It's fun to go through for entertainment sake.

At the end of fisherman's wharf sits this beautiful park facing the water.  You see a lot of people here just sitting and enjoying the sun.  The sidewalks have many artists with their crafts for sale.
A bit of green hidden down town.  There are children playing, couples soaking up the sun, other sharing a picnic or reading.  Sometimes you can catch some live music or another performance.
This plaza is used for many events throughout the year.  I've come here for sumo wrestling, soy festival, and other festivals.  Other times, it's a great place for photos.

Excellent fairly strenuous hike with amazing views of Vandenberg airforce base to the South (On clear days you can even see the oil platforms off the coast near Goleta) and Pismo and Avila to the North. Stay on the trail as the beginning of the hike is on private property and at the top of the hill is Vandenberg property. No facilities and be sure to bring lots of water especially if you decide to go all the way down to the beach as coming back up the hill can be quite difficult especially at midday, I have seen bikes here but am not sure if they are allowed. Dogs can be on leash. As the parking location is a bit isolated be sure to not leave any valuables in your car or carry them with you. My car has been broken in here and I think it happens pretty often as I have seen window glass several times.

There are a ton of trails in this preserve and you can choose whatever suits your endurance level. Biking is allowed and horseback riding with permission. Provides a great view and is a perfect spot to watch the whale migrations that happen every year. Dogs are welcome and bags are provided at the entrance to the trails so there is no excuse to pick up after your four-legged friend. I have seen skunks, foxes, coyotes and of course lots of deer.

Went here on an early misty Saturday morning and felt like I was driving through the Scottish Highlands. Got here around 10 and besides a few people fishing near the parking lot, the place was deserted. There wasn't a lot of people on the beach and it felt good to get out of the hustle and bustle of the city and just have some peaceful time with the sound of crashing waves. A bit of a drive from the city but the views are worth it.

I enjoyed my visit (my ticket covered both Liberty island and Ellis island and didn't regret not purchasing a ticket to the pedestal at the Statue of Liberty. It seems like everyone comes to the statue of Liberty for the selfie opportunity but the audio guide is really informative too. I enjoyed the free your at Ellis island as well provided by a park ranger. Not a lot of food options at either location.

This place features prominently in my childhood memories. It is a very large park and I have attended my fair share of birthday parties and soccer games here. Lots of barbecue facilities that are first come first serve and the park also features a large disc golf course which can be fun with friends. Several vendors sell shaved ice and other treats but there are no real restaurants here.

My friend and I visited this museum after a visit to the statue of liberty. The museum is located near the water, next to Wall St and the ferry. The museum consists of two levels and has items from some of the major native american tribes from the Americas. I enjoyed the collection as I'm an archaeologist but the museum is not very interactive and many of the displays feel quite dated.

Beautiful spot with a stunning view of the Santa Ynez valley. You can get here via Camino Cielo. Just park on the side of the road and take the dirt road to the old house. There isn't much left but the fireplaces and some stone masonry but it makes for a dramatic backdrop. You can also hike from the valley floor from Cachuma though you will probably need a day pass.

Really enjoyed my first visit to Angel Island. Tons of great trails and nature to experience along with some epic views of San Francisco and the East Bay. Ferry ride from San Francisco's pier 41 takes about 30 minutes and its beautiful with some excellent views of Alcatraz. Bike rentals on the island and lots of water stations to fill up your canteen.

Excellent little walk with some beautiful unspoiled views of the Pecho Coast. Springtime is amazing when the flowers are in bloom and the hills are green. But it is a nice level walk (takes about 30-40 minutes) to get to the beach where you can explore the coastline. Cliffs are steep and prone to erode so stay back from the edge.

This is a great little hike located at the top of the Cuesta Grade on Hwy 101. Just follow the road up the hill. You can go for miles. There is a stand of rare cypress if you go far enough and you get a pretty spectacular view of the seven sisters, with Morro Rock on a clear day.

Went during the holidays on a Saturday night and I really enjoyed the experience, very romantic spot. The lights are really beautiful and the castle is decorated for Christmas just like in the 1930s. It was cool to see some of the docents dressed up in period costume too.

Great beach with twenty parking spots a picnic table and two pit toilets. It's a pretty isolated beach with only the bravest surfers heading out due to strong currents. Great walking along the beach but it gets windy. Usually some folks are fishing from the shore.

Small little park where lots of people from Berkeley take their dogs. Beautiful views of the city and bridges on a clear day. Excellent sunset vantage point. There is a lot of parking but I imagine on the weekends it probably fills up.

Beautiful spot with a nice view of Harmony and a nice peaceful setting. Small outdoor area and small gift shop located inside. Do a tasting then head down the hill to admire the ceramics and glass blowing activities in Harmony proper.

If the sunset looks like it might be good one, this a lovely place to come and chat with a friend or someone special (maybe bring a wine bottle in a paper bag. Not really much of a walk but In the summer the roses are in bloom.

The drive provides great views and the pictogryphs are really beautiful. A metal grate has been placed to protect the site from vandals. There are very few parking spots and the road is very windy so be careful.

If you are over 18, wait until Thursday night, for their after dark event. it's a great date spot to let out your inner child and have fun. During the week it can get pretty crazy with all the school groups.

The museum is very small and if you are looking to while away a few hours here you might want to pair this with the MoMA next door. The exhibit on Carnevale was interesting but again not very extensive.
The zoo itself was pretty sad. Grizzly bears looked the happiest. Maybe an alright place for young kids but the animals didn't look particularly healthy. Especially the polar bear and komodo.
The walk here is pretty nice but definitely not my favorite beach in Santa Cruz. A lot of beach glass finders here. Keep walking South to check out the old pier.
This is a small park with a baseball field, barbecue facilities and playground equipment. Lots of seating available here which lends itself to large parties.
Free parking and nice little beach with bathroom. There are a couple restaurants on the southern side of the beach. Play equipment and picnic facilities.
Beautiful spot to sit and watch the sunset in your car and watch the sunset or have a picnic. The view of the city are incredible!
I went here for a conference and was blown away by the facility and mission of the Academy. What an exciting institution.
Park stays open until 12pm and I spent a nice warm evening here playing guitar with some friends. No lights though.

Relatively easy place to snowshoe in the winter with accessible routes even for beginners. However two big caveats: 1. the road is super icy, and our Jeep skid and did a 360 two times! Make sure you have absolutely good winter tires or chains in the winter. Despite the fact that there wasn't a lot of snow during the day, the ice is super slick and potentially dangerous for driving. And 2. make sure you don't store any important belongings in your vehicle. I saw a tinted SUV whose trunk was broken into at one of the Mt. Bachelor trail heads (despite being heavily trafficked!).

There's a lot there. In fact, the MoMA has so much art, some of it stays in storage most of the time! But it's worth a visit. When I was there, Sol Lewitt had a piece at the entrance which was great. There's also an outdoor sculpture area with some great artists like Louise Bourgeois and Lawrence Weiner. It is a great place for contemporary art. I haven't been impressed with the rotating exhibits, though. My favorite has been more of the newer, contemporary faces on the top floor.
likes: Specific artists (e.g., Sol Lewitt, Louise Bourgeois, Lawrence Weiner)

reviews_attraction.text: Beautiful place with views of Los Angeles. The best place to come to get a panorama (this or the Getty). Parking can be a pain. Dedicate a full day to getting there. Parking is at the base of the hill, and a bus is required to go up. Last time we were there, it was $2 per person - cash required. The observatory itself (inside) is all right. It's really the view that you're going for.

This is one of the few memorials where people walking through are very quiet. Family members frequently visit, standing in front of the wall with flowers. Respect is given in silence. 'Architecture' of the memorial was controversial because it seems rather simple for the war that was fought and the lives that were lost. Nevertheless, worth a visit to pay respects.

Beautiful place to take a stroll. Very cold with a breeze in the winter. Google reviews routes to the road. To access parking you either have to park in the residential area in the north part, or there's a small lot in the south part, but it seems to have limited access to the park.

Had a wonderful time at the Opera House. Sergei Prokofiev's R+J was magnifique! Brooklyn Mack performance was excellent. Ticket purchasing, parking, seating were all relatively smooth despite the large crowds. Would visit again and recommend to others.

Small little park, mostly for people waiting for the bus on 4th street - major intersection and stop for transit. Sometimes there's a decent food cart present; otherwise it may take a bit of searching to find a decent meal around the area.

Not enough people know about this stunning little museum, tucked away in the Presidio. Beautiful architecture; interesting changing exhibitions. Small compared to other museums, but worth the visit. Great views of the bay as well.

Friendly rangers, well-maintained roads during winter weather (chains required), great views throughout. It's not as big as one would think (i.e. compared to Yosemite), but still a great place to get a view of glaciers.

Really wanted to like this museum because the architecture is so special, but the inside exhibitions are focused on a lot of the 'costumes' worn by this community, and aren't particularly as engaging as one would hope.

Beautiful park to relax and walk around. It has the best view of downtown Seattle including the Space Needle. View of Union Lake is stunning on a sunny day. Families love to sled down the hill during winter snow also.

This place is huge, and it's certainly beautiful, but the landscape is relatively homogeneous. I guess that's to be expected, but if you're looking for some more variety, the cascades are great WA destination as well.

Beautiful place to stop while driving thru the area. A nice, beautiful creek, and bathrooms available. Pay attention to your maps or you'll miss the exit. Enough parking during the holidays when we drove thru.
Not enough people visit this beautiful park. There's a lot of greenery here, but I would recommend coming with a friend. It's frequently isolated. Great place to have long conversations while hiking.
One of the most stunning areas of Washington; definitely worth a visit during reasonable weather. It gets super cold out this way, so have plenty of layers and tough jackets ready.
Small but clean and quaint. There's a bike station adjacent to this park that has a vending machine with bike repair accessories. The free bike pump doesn't work that well, though.
Mt Tabor isn't my favorite park in Portland. The trip up is steep, and there are a couple of reservoirs but for better views, you're better off making your way to Powell Butte.
Great architecture. You can take the elevator up to the top to get a view of GGPark and see the top of the Academy of Sciences. Contemporary art space is great as well.
Nice place to relax during the summer; tons of parking; people like to swim in the water during the summer, but it's best to wear some shoes because it's very rocky.
Beautiful park to picnic and ride your bike through, but beware of parking your vehicle around there - parking tickets given out regularly upwards of $75+
An absolute must for any visitor and Seattleite; architecture by Frank Gehry is one of the most spectacular and stunning in the world. Definitely a must.
This is an OK state park. Trails are not that well maintained. Steep declines and inclines. Can be dry. Make sure to take plenty of water with you.
This amazing space is not visited enough by locals and visitors. There's amazing art within, but requires patience to walk through and appreciate.
People like to shoot their guns in this park. There's some trash around as a result. Otherwise a nice place to hike/stroll about.
Despite all the crowds, they have very efficient staff that help keep the lines moving. A must-see for visiting Philadelphia.

Salvation Mountain and Slab city, a very unique part of California.

I really recommend researching Slab City and Salvation Mountain before going there.  Theres a lot of interesting facts, history and other oddities that you can discover that you would probably miss if you didnt do your research.
Slab city was created when the government abandoned Fort Dunlap near Niland.  The buildings were dismantled in the 50s but the concrete foundations were left.  Eventually hippies and other people migrated to this area.  Part oddity, part hippy commune, tons of interesting art especially for photographers and people interested in social sciences.

Salvation mountain was created by Leonard Knight who passed in 2014.  The art installation is made of adobe, straw and thousands of gallons of paint.   Many people traveled through and stayed at the mountain, Leonard is featured in several books and films about these people as well as some really interesting documentaries.

There was a very interesting book/ film called Into the Wild in which the protagonist passed through Salvation Mountain and Slab City.

There are some locals who sort of curate the area but its free to enter and enjoy. bring something to leave at the site in memory of Leonard.

Death Valley is ALIVE:
If you have never been here, its a must see at least once in your lifetime.
I have traveled here many times, ten or more I would say, I still havent seen everything. Theres always something new to see or believe it or not, things change.

I usually stay at Furnace Creek but staying in a near by town like Beaty is a great option.
Make sure to stock up on supplies before you come because it can get very expensive here.

Some of my favorites spots are Bad Water, Scottys Castle, the Painted mountains, Furnace Creek, Beatty Candy shop, Rhyolite to name a few.

Definitely worth spending at least a long weekend here.

Great place to get away from it all.  Wonderful trails. Off roading roads. Spectacular views.
This forest is great. Its very convenient to get to. You can access it from Oretega Highway.  I usually come up and eat breakfast at one of the main spots like The Lookout or Hells Kitchen and then make my way to the forrest.
There are a plethora of great hiking trails just be prepared. Dress for the weather, make sure you bring water, its a good idea to prep an emergency backpack and let people know where you are going.
Fun for the whole family or a great place to get away from it all.

Great VIP
Saw Lilie Mae and Jack White.
VIP area is legit. Lots of fun people. Backstage is awesome

ive never seen either perform live wow what a show.

Lily Maes stage presence is incredible. What a voice and great fiddle player. Frank was on Guitar wow that guy can play. Totally shredded the acoustic guitar. Sally was on the mandolin wowowowoow.

Really impressive performance by Jack White. Such energy and love for his fans.

Being back stage was quite an incredible experience. Free tacos were great by Hell Yea Taco!!!

Great night. Also saw a coyote in the parking lot.

Iconic LA Landmark-
Funny how some of these reviews state that there are no coffeeshops, nothing to do and no place to sit around the sign.... its a SIGN people. lol.
You can see it from all over Los Angeles YOU are the one that decided to hike all that way to get close to...the...big...large.... sign..... Maybe you should prepare a little, you know, bring your own beverage and maybe a chair? Im not sure how many people bring a chair and demand a coffee shop on their hikes or when they look at a sign in general but ok ...nice story bro!

I really love coming to sanctuaries.  Its a very educational experience.
Farm Sanctuary is a really great place to visit with your family and friends. A great organization to  come out and help out by your visit.
Its very important for children and adults to  get up close and personal with animals, learn a bit about then and what they go through on a day to day.  We have visited here a couple of times and always really enjoyed our visit.
Parking is easy and the staff is friendly, helpful and informative.
Great way to get more informed.

Dodger Stadium.
Iconic LA. If you are a local or if you are traveling you have to go to a Dodger game now and again.

Parking, relatively easy but somewhat chaotic. If you can take a train, an uber... much better situation.

Dodger Dog, nothing beats a Dodger Dog and a beer on a warm day.

The Fans- REALLY DEDICATED. You will find no other fan as dedicated to their team as Dodger fans. Be warned and play nice heheh.

The Beer and stadium food is pretty pricey so just be aware of that.

Great family park, great place for the community.
There are numerous places for the kids to play, and the family to gather.
Additionally many people come here for a bit of exercise. Walk, run, hike, theres also a number of people who do yoga and other fitness regimes.

The best part of this park is the view of Los Angeles from the top. You really cannot beat it. Its a spectacular view overlook much of the city.
Great place to take photos or watch the sun rise or set.

Great park great community center
Lots of things going on. Small children can play at the playground. Lots of people exercising. There are two nice size basketball courts.
Some transients but the park feels safe although it smells like human waste in some sections of the park.
Overall a nice little park insanta monica.

***as im writing this i witnessed a park employee shovel human poop and walk it to the restroom an flush it

This is a must see for families.
If you have young kids you should bring them here. I think a lot of the experience at the Great Moments show with Mr Lincoln are very important for our youth.
This is a really touching and amazing part of disneyland.
This show has been around for a long time and is pretty much unchanged.
I remember coming here as a kid and was in total awe.

Easier, safer and probably more legal to approach going southbound on PCH.  Ive been coming to this point since i was in the WOMB.
Great memories here. I almost proposed to my wife here.

This Rock means so much to local people here, not only as a landmark but with such fond memories.
I know its just a rock but its a special place for many.

Beautifully spectacular views

If you have never been in a cave like this and you are in the area, you MUST go to this.
Beautiful cave with tons of stalagmites and stalagtites.  Pretty easy for anyone with average mobility.
Be sure to book your tickets in advance.

This is a great cave and fun for families or individuals. the tours are really interesting and something you dont experience every day

Awesome Wax Museum.
This is one of the iconic Hollywood and Los Angeles things to do.
If you live here, youve probably been, if you are passing through or just moved here you have to go. Really great experience.  You will probably be in and out in an hour or so. TOns of parking near by. Great places to go after, eat, shop, drink etc.
Check it out!

Parking is terrible, the seats are very uncomfortable. Tickets are still expensive even for the nose bleed section...whats not to love?
Lol.
Very disorganized venue with silly security rules but we still had fun.
The parking situation is grossly disorganized which is on of the big reasons we dont come here near as much as we used to.

Really awesome park. Great for families. I really enjoy the programs and events we have at this park. Remember the old shuttle playground. That was a blast. Fiesta La Bologna is a wonderful even for the community. I love running into and meeting up with friends here.
Also love the California Rare Fruit Growers events here.

Spectacular view.
Great place to have a picnic, enjoy the views, spend some time with family and just enjoy a little peace.
I love taking strolls along here. The park is really peaceful and quiet.
We have had some friends here for a nice picnic, parking was easy and finding a spot even more so.

Not a fan of waterparks but I had a blast.
Really great time with the family this day. Great place for families, birthdays, groups of friends etc.
We came on a hot day and it was a great way to beat the heat.
It was crowded as heck but didnt feel too crazy.
Fun times!

Great place to spend the day.
Definitely come here to check out the ocean. Spend a bit of self time, spend some time with your loved one or come with a family.
Great spot to check out the crashing waves and the ocean, the sunset or the sunrise.  Great place for photos

Great place to spend time.
Not as crowded as the most photographed tree (The General SHerman) but still plenty to do and see here.
The trees are spectacular. One of a kind and once in a lifetime experience for most who come through here

Nice place to visit with a family or in solace.
Great place to chill and check out the scenery.
I love coming down here and taking photos.
Parking is pretty easy.
The lagoon is very unique and cool to check out if you are in the area

Really love this place, great place for kids and always new happenings here.  This is a very easy place to take your family and have a great day.  Theres so much to see including the rose gardens.  Exhibits constantly rotate.

I was basically dragged here and then I didnt want to leave.
really great museum. tons of great things to see.
Very fun for the family. the kids can get up close and personal with the trains.  Great exhibits

Great place to people watch. theres always a number of gymnists here doing various practices.
Lots of yoga and other happenings going on.

Really cool to check out if you are here. always seems busy

Really amazing museum. Great to see with friends or family.

The tours are great and its right across from the LA Zoo so you could do both.

Tons of rich history and artifacts here

Nice local park for the neighborhood.
Generally pretty quiet and great for a family picnic.

Just a short walk from Titos tacos

If you want your cardiovascular endurance and hamstrings get tested these trails are for you. I hiked Jones Peak that has an elevation 3,375 ft. The recommended route begins at the Bailey Canyon Park trailhead, also known as Grove Park. Getting onto the trail you'll go through the turnstile gate west side of Bailey Canyon Park. Jones Peak is great hike with a distance of 6.5 miles (round-trip) with narrow trails & sharp corners which took me 2 hours to reach the summit. It's degree of difficulty was from easy to moderate. I love the smell of fresh wild plants, flowers and ogling wild animals (e.g., lizards, birds). They should be venerated and handled with caution. There were few benches and signs getting to the peak. Going down was relatively easy and faster but be careful there were sharp corners which you'll go straight to a deep ravine. If you're planning to hike I suggest bring plenty of water, mask-ppe, and sunscreen. Overall I was very ebullient that I did this hike and appreciate the pulchritudinous view from top.

As a hiker I don’t say this lightly that the Tuna Canyon Park has the most spectacular and stunning views. TC Park a mountainous park with 1,255-acre in the western Santa Monica Mountains above PCH in Malibu parallels more than two miles of the Pacific Ocean, and provides dramatic, 360-degree views of the San Gabriel mountains to the Santa Monica Bay. Furthermore, it links over 18,000 acres of contiguous protected open space from Topanga State Park west to Las Flores Canyon. We drove up to the trail head from PCH via narrow Tuna Canyon road. There’s only dirt parking near and/or at the trail head. The entrance to the trail is somewhat hidden. The hike is about 2 to 5.1 miles (out and back) with elevation change of 900 to 1,500 ft. The trail head has two main view points: the West vp (Hearst Tank) and the East vp (Big Rock Lateral). Both view points are not interconnected albeit offer a magnificent view of the park. Street parking only. Overall, I highly recommend this hidden gem park.

This trailhead is easy to miss because it’s right next to a house. Rubio Canyon-trailhead is steep and rugged 3.4 mile hike (out and back) with elevation change of 1,410 feet. This trail is unmaintained, however, offers a great view of the canyon mountain. Moreover, the trail is very rocky with narrow path and rated difficult (see photos). Trail is for experienced hikers only. Be very careful not to slide/trip and fall over the sharp rocky ravine below as you ascend. There is no clear trail path once you’ve reached the gigantic wall of sedimentary rocks; you have to climb over it which can be treacherous. Furthermore, this trailhead has multiple zigzags which was challenging. I wouldn’t recommend this trailhead, if you want to go to Mt Lowe Railway. Ample of free street parking. Great upper middle class neighborhood. Overall, I had a challenging and heart pounding hike.

Heritage Square Museum is a living history and open-air architecture museum located beside the Arroyo Seco Parkway in the Montecito Heights neighborhood of LA. The museum focuses on interpreting the years 1850 to 1950, a century of unprecedented growth in Los Angeles. I visited on a Saturday and took the 2 hr guided tour. Admission is free but the tour cost $10 bucks. Grounds are self guided but inside the houses are not.
I love the Victorian style architectural houses. Each of the houses were rich in history. My favorite was W.Hayes Perry and Hale's house because of their unique interior design and layout. Our tour guide was very knowledgable and friendly. Parking is very small and limited. However, residential street parking available. Overall, I enjoyed visiting HSM and I highly recommend you visit at least once.

Bailey Canyon Wildreness Park is a 1.7 mile moderately trafficked out and back trail located near Sierra Madre that features a waterfall and is rated as moderate. The trail is primarily used for hiking and dogs are also able to use this trail but must be kept on leash. Moreover, it has multiple trails that lead to Jones Peak and Mt Wilson that can reach to 3,376 ft and 5,715 ft respectively. Getting onto the trail you'll go through the turnstile gate west side of Bailey Canyon Park. Easy study (loop) trail in oak woodland area, approximately an eighth of a mile. BCWP has a small free parking lot with trees around to provide shade. Overall I highly recommend this park as the base trail for anyone trying to get their cardiovascular endurance and hamstrings.

Hike to panoramic views of the pacific. This 5.4-mile out-and back trail takes off from the end of the residential area of Paseo Miramar. Stretch your legs on this ~400 feet of elevation gain. Once you hike a little less than a quarter mile in, you'll connect with Los Leones Canyon Trail. Continue on Paseo Miramar Trail, which in another 2.5 miles, will connect you with the Parker Mesa Overview. The trail is very narrow with almost single file occupancy; not to mention some wild plants and flowers on its path. It took me roughly 30 mins or so to reach the top viewpoint. It's a very easy hike going down which took me another 30 mins. Parking lots and side streets are available. Overall, it's a short trail hike with spectacular view.

For years, I have always called it the White Candle Stick because it does look like one. Coit Tower, a slender white concrete column rising from the top of Telegraph Hill, has been an emblem of San Francisco's skyline since its completion in 1933, a welcoming beacon to visitors and residents alike. It sits on top of Pioneer Park in down town San Francisco and provides 360-degree views of the city and bay, including the Golden Gate and Bay bridges. Furthermore, there are tower viewers (binoculars) around the place so you can see other landmarks in the bay area. Parking at the tower is very, very limited, so I suggest park on the surrounding street. Overall, I enjoyed my visit and the free self tour guide.

Eaton Canyon Nature Park is a190-acre zoological, botanical, and geological nature preserve situated at the base of the beautiful San Gabriel Mountains. We went here on a Sunday morning. The hike to the 40-foot Eaton Canyon Waterfalls can be summed up to: 1.1 miles of wide flat, relatively uneventful dirt trail, followed by 0.65 miles of single track up a narrow canyon that is adventurous and fun (forming a 3.5 mile round trip hike with 375 feet of elevation change). Free parking is available. Dogs are welcome in Eaton Canyon Park and on Eaton Canyon Trail to the waterfall. No fee or permit is required. Overall, I enjoyed my time hiking. It is an easy trail so anyone can do it.

I finally crossed it out on my bucket list. The famous Cypress Tree Tunnel of Point Reyes. It is hard to beat a spot this beautiful as the Cypress Trees do grow into a tunnel over the road. This scenic spot is heaven for photographers (professionals and amateur), locals and tourist. The driveway though the trees leads to an old building that houses the Point Reyes National Seashore North District Operations Center and the KPH RCA Radio Station.

The best time to visit it before sunset but it will be busy. No parking lot, however, you can park on the side road. Overall, this place is a hidden gem and I highly recommend you visit if you're in the bay area.

Willie Mann Memorial Chair (34°13'11.5"N 118°17'27.9"W) is a permanent art lounge chair situated at Verdugo Peak-3,126ft. It was dedicated to Willie, an avid musician, artist, and nature lover.
