He worked for the film industry (25 years) as a freelance film production. Anyways, there were several trailheads that one can take that leads to this memorial chair. I took the hardest, most rugged and challenging trail called Vital Link Trail. Despite the arduous challenge reaching the chair, I gotta say it’s definitely worth it because it provides a majestic view of LA and surrounding mountains. Overall, I enjoyed sitting on this chair and the view.

My favorite museum😍 in Pasadena. I wonder here and walk aimlessly to feel the rich art history. Norton Museum has copious art collection from European art (14th-18th cent) to Asian art to Rembrandt to Cezanne. Each gallery is organized, spacious and well lit. My two favorite arts are Adam and Eve c.1530 by Lucas Cranach and A Sleeping Woman c.1544  by G.Pencz. Staff are friendly and professional. Admission price is cheap. Audio guided tour available for $3 bucks. Members, child and students are Free! Parking is spacious and free. Overall, I highly recommend NSM and you will ♡ it.
likes: Specific artworks (Adam and Eve, A Sleeping Woman)

reviews_attraction.text:
MOLAA is a museum dedicated to Latin American Art in Southern California in Long Beach; the only museum in the US to exclusively feature works by people of Latin American decent. It is relatively a midsize museum, impeccably clean, well curated, air conditioned and wonderful exhibits.
Parking lot is huge. Admission price is relatively affordable; Sundays are free!! Staff are friendly and competent. Museum store is small and souvenirs are tad pricey. Overall, a good museum that every family or individual should visit and enjoy Hispanic Culturas y Artes.

Wilson Creek Winery is the most popular winery in Temecula. We had a great time at WCW. I'm no sommelier but their wines are of high quality. Staff are very friendly and competent. Prices are very competitive.
It's a wonderful place to hangout, bring a date/spouse and people watch while you sip wine. Indoor is very spacious with lots of full bar to choose from. Moreover, the outdoor grounds are spectacular. Parking lot is huge facing the vineyard. Overall, we had a great time and I highly recommend Wilson Creek Winery.

PSAT is the largest rotating tramway. The ride is twelve-and-a-half that begins in the Valley station (2,643 ft) and elevates all the way to the Mountain Station at 8,516 ft above sea level. We came on a weekend and the ticket line was not long. Tkts have time schedule going to the tram. Prices were reasonable at twenty-five bucks. They have cafeteria, a small souvenir shop and a tiny historical museum. Parking lot is huge and has a shuttle. Overall we had a wonderful time. I highly recommend visiting PSAT.
likes: Facilities & Services: Reasonable prices, Time-scheduled tickets, Shuttle service, Large parking lot

reviews_attraction.text: LA MAG is a small gallery in the heart of Hollywood blvd that exhibits local arts and artists of Southern California. Staff are friendly and informative. Admission is FREE! Donation is highly recommended. Visitors can complete the exhibits in less than 30 minutes. The best part of this LA MAG is it view of the Hollywood sign, the Holly Hills and Griffith Park. If you're in the neighborhood go check out this gallery; not too many people knows about this gallery exist in the Barnsdall Park.

Palisades Park is a 5-acre park linear park overlooking the Pacific and its a wonderful place for walkers, bikers and people watchers, and exercise workout. Park is located between Colorado Avenue and Adelaide Drive above Highway 1. The PP is organized and well kept.  Street metered parking available. Overall, I highly recommend you visit this park in Santa Monica.

The Vessel is an architectural wonder situated at the Hudson Yard. Its perfect for photoshoots for the family and a great tourist spot. It has 8 floors with impeccable view of the surrounding neighborhood and the Hudson. Parking ticket is fair. The Vessel is near Hudson Yard station. Overall, its a great architectural structure.

The price of admission is as good as the exhibits. PMCA has free midsize indoor parking designed with kosmic art. The museum's galleries showcase breadth of art and design by different artist across the country from abstract photography to colorful canvas. Visitors can easily breeze through the art exhibits in an hour.

Library Park is a beautiful huge park with plenty of amenities include tables, free parking, open grassy area and outdoor drinking fountains and playground equipment. Furthermore, Monrovia public library is situated at the middle of the park. Overall, it’s a cool park to chill, workout and read a book.

Palm Springs Sign is a must stop for quick photo op. Great view of the desert. Parking is available at the visitor center or by the dirt where the sign is at. Overall, its still a wonderful area with a majestic view of the desert mountains. I highly recommend this place to all visitors.

I like all forms of art including this brightly colored 30-foot-tall totems that light up the desert sky which is just outside Las Vegas. This is a cool place outside of the city that’s worth the drive. I recommend going very early when it’s cool and there are less tourists.

Barnsdall Park is a good park with lush green grass. Its a nice place to hangout and enjoy the view (hollywood sign and griffith park). Parking is limited. Downside is some homeless peeps tend to hang around the park. Overall, its a nice park for picnic.
Rosemead Park is a huge park with aquatic ctr, basketball court, kids area, picnic area, two soccer field and running path. Parking lot is available. Overall, a great park for outdoor activities.
I love going to Cali Science Center. Admission is free for the Space Shuttle Endeavor is awesome. It's a fun museum to bring your family or significant other.
Cool little lighthouse surf museum at the edge of the park. Fun facts bout surfin history. Great view from the beach.

This is different place in Big Bend National Park. Mountains/ Hillocks are different & in slabs. This is also dusty place. Driving from road to this place is on rough road & only for small vehicles. After parking bit of walk on trail gives good view of river. Lot many old buildings are around but not in operation may be used earlier. Hot springs area is small & not have any facilities near by. Only touched the warm water but couldn’t take bath. River is also nice place. Should have some more time to relax here. Do not forget to take bath towels & other set of clothing.

Yesterday visited zoo, though it is very cold & majority animals were in shelters & all eat outs were closed, we enjoyed the visit with very less people around. It’s claimed worlds one of the largest penguin habilitation centre which is excellent. I am very much impressed with zoo layout. We have walked through entire zoo, & enjoyed lot. Butterfly garden is also beautiful. All animals which we could see are very healthy . You should have above 3 hours to see the zoo, may be more time if with family & friends. Must visit place in Detroit

Simply great place for visit & observe / understand various space related information &  programs with help of exhibits. It’s nice place to spend day. All facilities like food court, accessibility to all & gift store are available. Visit to training centre & rocket area gives us some idea about how scientists worked for various space programs. Display & information is amazing. Must take younger generations to create space awareness amongst them

Excellent museum I have ever seen. Simple old things of town are displayed very nicely. Have different sections- old city shops display, post office, hall of fame for sports, old vehicle, industry in town , old dentists shop & so on. Enjoyed visit to museum & entry fee is negligible only one USD pet person. Certainly recommended for visit. Staff is very cooperative

Beautiful concept of stairs at public place. We enjoyed it very much. Cactus garden around staircase is also amazing. Not much rush. Careful in parking to avoid theft. Must visit place in San Francisco. Tiles concept is also well thought, the Sun - The Moon - water reservoir (sea) , water flow (river), water animals & then land all are beautifully presented

Great place, excellent nature exhibits on display. You can touch & feel different animal parts such as skulls, skin(furr) horns etc. nice decor & children play room. Bird house outside center is very nice & many birds & sparrows are taking shelter. Small but beautiful place & without visiting this place your visit to island is not complete

Excellent Hindu holy place . Nicely carved temple. One will feel really calm & becomes fresh after visiting the temple. Good Indian food is available in cafe. Gift shop has very nice Indian & traditional articles & food stuff for sale. Must visit place after visiting NASA centre . Temple is open in early morning & evening also.
likes: Facilities & Services: Nicely carved, Good Indian food, Gift shop

reviews_attraction.text: This is place where artists fair is arranged in Tulips festivals. This reminded me my towns (India -Asia) Yatra. Good to have round in fair. Things are bit costly but enjoy ambience & crowd. Dutch couple dance was beautiful & added much spice in visit. Enjoyed day in Tulips festivities & round in town was simply great

Very nicely planted Tulips. Great ambiance. Enjoyed walk & photography in Tulips. As from Pune India pleasantly surprised to see good Indian (Asia) food stall at this place. Must visit place during Tulips show. This is 90th year of show great going Holland, keep it up

Very nice & compact rose garden. Nature/ flower lovers will enjoy the visit. Thousands of roses are planted in neat & organised way. Entire area is colourful & aroma in atmosphere is really beautiful. One can spend quality time with family & lot many photos

Excellent place visited in Austin. Very easy access to main assembly of government. You can easily watch the proceedings from gallery. What a architect of building & surroundings. Must spend good time to have round in & outside the building.

This is close to glacier point. Highly scenic place. Just seat on valley side & watch amazing valley, peaks, snow topped tips, wonderful waterfalls. This is open only in summer. You can see half dome from this place just across the valley

Excellent well presented road in San Francisco. Nicely decorated roadside area & enjoy full car ride on this road. People are walking around & lot many photo points. Near by roads are full of ups & downs
Very nice Aquarium. Good amount of fishes on exhibits, good information with proper photos of each spice of fish. Enjoyed visit very much. Few photos & video explains well about this nice place
Excellent place to spend the time with family & friends. Good scenic place. One will really enjoy the walk/ cycling on the river side. Good places for relaxation are created alongside the path.
Beautiful spot on scenic 17th mile drive, lot many cypress trees. Lonely cypress tree on rock in sea is simply great. This is also used as symbol as logo by pebble beach resorts.
Very beautiful site on 17th mile drive. When Spanish came first time they camped here. This is very scenic site & in May you will find beautiful pink flowers on all across
Nice park. Many facilities within park such as community centre , dog park with two different sections for small & big dogs, skating area good trail. enjoyed visit here
Total view of lower & upper Falls is simply great, I recommend first go to lower falls by trail & come in round trail to see total fall, you will enjoy more.
Other side of Big Bend National Park. Offers different type of Canyon. Couldn’t complete the trail due to lack of time. Might be offering good views.
One of the scenic spot in 17th mails drive. Very good view of sea shore as sea has lot of rocks it’s having good waves & looks like restless
This is place we briefly visited on way to Yosemite National Park from San Jose. This is scenic place & good for family & friends picnic
Excellent holy place in Auburn Hills area. You have good holy atmosphere around. Many programs going on through out the year.
Good place to visit & spend time with family. Couldn’t visit the museum as it was closed, had good scenic spot also
May be good museum but couldn’t see as we reached the place after office hours. Few photos taken from outside

Famous large hilltop park with unbeatable views and an exuberant urban vibe.
The panoramic view of the city from on the east side is fantastic, especially during sunrise. Even if painted ladies were not in the picture, I would still consider this one of the best and most easy-to-get place to appreciate the city's skyline. On the other side of the park is a big dog play area and green space where people gather and picnic on the grass. The park always emits a playful, cheery vibe. Moreover, it is just a few blocks away from three business areas (Divis, Lower Haight and Hayes Valley) so it feels very urban and central.
Yes it gets very touristy but to be honest I think many tourists just come grab a picture and go.

Huge natural area with gorgeous redwoods and tons of different trails to explore.
The east edge of the park is a multi-use paved trail parallel to Terwilliger Boulevard, no more automobile traffic for runners and cyclists as they pass through the park.
Other trails are unpaved, foot-traffic only and often undulating up and down little hills and valleys with occasional stairs. There are many intersecting trails so it's a bit difficult to navigate, some intersections are marked with signs that are super helpful. Definitely not the easiest trail to run on, if you prefer a more straight forward run, take the trail along Terwilliger which is easier to follow and has better terrain/surface.

Tons of trails to hike and run! If you are new to this area, navigating the trails can be a little daunting, so pay close attention to the little trail signs. I really appreciate how comprehensive and clear these signs are, they are at almost every intersection (though sometimes pretty small) so once you know which trail you want to follow or turn to, it's not that easy to get lost.

Great spot in Washington Park. For here you can go north to check out the redwood observation deck and cross Burnside to climb up to Pittock Mansion; or go south to the Vietnam Veteran memorial and Oregon Zoo.

Steel Bridge doesn't possess a lot of physical charm, its color not as vibrant as Broadway, its design not as majestic as St. Johns, but it's very practical and means a great deal for the community. Its double decks are frequently used by cars, buses, light rails, pedestrians (on both levels!) and cyclists, and even those slow moving, loud honking cargo trains. You can't find another bridge in Portland as versatile and well used as Steel Bridge. Sadly though, the surrounding areas of the bridge on both sides are a bit sketchy.
likes: Multi-use (cars, buses, light rails, pedestrians, cyclists, cargo trains)

reviews_attraction.text:
Beautiful waterfront green space with views of the Richardson Bay and Strawberry, as well as the city on a clear day (you can see Sutro Tower and Golden Gate Bridge). Great place to go for a stroll, jog or dog walk.
The northern part is a big field that can get quite busy and lively on the weekends. It's quieter on the south side where there is a playground and public restrooms. The old rail trail passes through the park and goes all the way to almost downtown.

I’m a runner so the review is only about the track, which feels like a little bit of a let-down. It’s not a standard track (more rectangular than oval) with only four lanes. It feels a little out of maintenance as well, with some uneven spots here and there. On top of that, the whole complex feels too dense with different facilities crowded into one public space. As I ran on the track, an off-leash dog barked from the little park right next to the track.

What a gem! This is truly a park for the people. You can run or cycle around the park (one loop is a bit over 2 miles), you can come fishing, taking a boat ride in the lake, playing outdoor games, or having a picnic with family and friends, or you can simply chill in the shade and read a book. Great infrastructures and facilities around the park as well.

Wash Park is my favorite during my visit to Denver, it's always so lively and makes me feel alive.

* This is a review for the Lakewood Gulch Trail, not just the park.
The trails is quiet and easy to navigate. I started my run from Confluence Park and ended with a loop around Sloan's Lake, by way of Lakewood Gulch trail. It's a nice and chill10 miler. Several light rail stations along the trail makes it even more accessible. Not a sight or attraction itself but definitely a good connector between downtown area and the East side of the city.

I love running on Broadway Bridge, its vibrant red color brightens my day and definitely reminds me of the beloved Golden Gate Bridge. There are designated and protected lanes for pedestrians and cyclists on both directions and wide enough for to make passing safe and easy.
Awesome views of Fremont Bridge and Steel Bridge from here (especially during dawn).
p.s. Broadway Bridge has the longest span of its bascule design type in the world.

Great park occupying four city blocks with quite some stuff to offer, including a big playground with fun play structures, open green space and quieter wooded area, a dog play corner (not really a dog park though) and tennis courts hidden behind the trees!
It's up the hill like many other SF urban parks, with decent city views, not the best but open and soothing. A nice place to take a break and get some fresh air if you are around.

A pretty big park with lots of amenities yet also feel like could use some more maintenance. There are several big sports field including a stadium. The fenced football field looks great, on the other hand,  the tennis courts are definitely long deserted. There is a jogging loop however the trail surface is way too soft for running.The park is a block away from the I-205 bike trail which is sort of taken over by tents...

Situated in the very heart of the city where the Cherry Creek joins the South Platt River, this little park is an ideal place to start an exploration of the city. While it's close to Union Station and Downtown Denver, it's usually fairly quiet. You can take any of the long river trails to run or cycle for miles (10+ if you wish); or spend a few hours in the LoHi area, where shopping and dining options are abundant.

Sadly it's only accessible to automobiles so I can't run it. But you can get a good look at the bridge at the foot of its tower on Front Ave. During sunrise and sunset time the color is even more magic.
Seen from Broadway Bridge, the elegant long arch of Fremont Bridge even reminds me of Sydney's Harbour Bridge. Seen from Overlook Park, it adds a beautiful curve to the otherwise uninteresting view of Portland.

Short but beautiful tiled steps. It's really short though, much shorter than the similar colorfully tiled 16th Ave steps, or the Lyon street steps which has no tiles but offers great views and is a fantastic spot for stairs exercise.
I wouldn't recommend people to come here visit just for the steps, but this is a good entry point to Lands End. The opposite view of California St is kind of cool too.
likes: Good entry point to Lands End
dislikes: Less impressive compared to similar attractions

reviews_attraction.text: There are a lot of things packed into this one little park! Trails, a tiny pond, benches by the bushes, an undulating sculpture wall made from 99 railroad tracks. It definitely feels like there are a lot of thoughts put int planning this park. There is even a sign that explains how this contemplative space represents the natural history of the Pearl district.

This is exactly how I imagine a modern bridge in a metropolitan: elegant with style, easy to recognize and differentiate from its older siblings; environmentally friendly and conscious, prioritizing public transit and self-powered commute. It's the most runner/cyclist friendly bridge in Portland and I always enjoy the view as I cross the river.

A nice, multifunctional park in the geographic center of the city with a lot to offer. There is the Museum of Nature and Science taking up the west side of the park, there is a beautiful lake for the walkers and runners, a zoo for the young families and some tennis courts at the northwest corner. Lots of green spaces for people to enjoy.

Great park in SE Portland on the riverfront that I ran passed by many times. It's on the longer waterfront loop along the river and you'll find it a good change of scenery after a stretch of trail in a residential area.
There are some benches, a small dog park, and I believe public restrooms as well so that can come handy sometimes.

Nice little trail along the Clackamas River that connects trails between Gladstone and Oregon City. Half of the trail is in the woods and the other half unshaded with river view.
I came from Portland along Trolley trail and then crossed the river and this trail led me to Clackamette Park before reaching Oregon City downtown.

Small park by the South Platt River with lots of green spaces. Ideal for taking a walk or jog. While the park itself isn't that spectacular, it's nice that there are several parks like this one along the South Platt River trail and they form a really nice green belt for runners and cyclists.

Peaceful little deck in the park, a nice stop for hikers and runners to appreciate the handsome redwoods. Sometimes people even come here for wedding photos.

Pretty easy to access as you follow the trails. It's always shaded even on a sunny day, I hope there had been more natural light.

Charming little square with a nice view of the Lakewood Bay on one side and a shopping / dinning village on the other. A great place to hang out with friends, walk around, grab a coffee or snack. The restaurants nearby are a bit pricey but I guess you pay for the great atmosphere.

Little urban park in the Pearl district. Feels a little deserted every time I pass by despite being in a really nice and lively neighborhood. There are no kids playing, no people reading, leaving the stairs and benches empty. Maybe it’s because of the current pandemic.

Beautiful park and during the fall its color is legit! I enjoyed running through the park on my way from Kelley Point to downtown St. Johns. There is a dog park and across a bridge over the railroad is Pier Park–a bit weird that they are actually two parks.
Tiny city park next to the ferry with an elephant statue. It's very lovely but the fun doesn't last long.

Disney Springs (previously known as Lake Buena Vista Shopping Village in 1975, Walt Disney World Village in 1977, Disney Village Marketplace in 1989, and Downtown Disney  in 1997) is an outdoor shopping, dining, and entertainment complex at the Walt Disney World Resort in Lake Buena Vista, Florida, near Orlando. The complex opened on March 22, 1975, and has been expanded and renamed over the years. In 2013 plans were announced for a three-year renovation and expansion of the complex, and on September 29, 2015, the name officially changed to Disney Springs.The 120-acre complex includes four distinct areas: Marketplace, The Landing, Town Center, and West Side. Buses and water taxis  operated by Disney Transport provide transportation between Disney Springs and other areas of Walt Disney World.Characters in Flight observation balloon ride
The Lake Buena Vista Shopping Village, which opened on March 22, 1975, was originally envisioned as an area shopping mall. Two years after its opening, the complex was renamed Walt Disney World Village. With the advent of new management under Michael Eisner in 1984, Disney began looking for ways to keep vacationers on Walt Disney World property longer, and prevent them from leaving for entertainment beyond Disney's borders.To compete with the popular Church Street Station clubs in downtown Orlando, Disney announced the addition of Pleasure Island, featuring nightclubs showcasing Disney's quality and creativity, to Walt Disney World Village on July 21, 1986. Construction began the following August and Pleasure Island was opened on May 1, 1989, the same day as the Disney's Hollywood Studios theme park. Later that year, the complex was renamed Disney Village Marketplace.In the mid-1990s, the growth of Walt Disney World created the potential for further expansion, leading to a $1 billion investment in projects across the resort. The first World of Disney store opened October 2, 1996, in Marketplace.On June 20, 1995, major enhancements and expansions were announced for the area, with the Disney Village Marketplace and Pleasure Island being combined into a newly branded district named Downtown Disney. The re-branding was introduced on September 7, 1997. On September 15, Downtown Disney West Side, a 66 acres (27 ha) expansion, opened as a third shopping, dining, and entertainment area featuring venues such as La Nouba (the former Cirque Du Soleil show in residence which closed at the end of 2017), DisneyQuest, and Virgin Megastore. Major changes to the complex also included the conversion of Mickey's Character Shop into the World of Disney, becoming the world's largest Disney store, in addition to the expansion and upgrade of the AMC Pleasure Island Theatres, as well as the opening of Rainforest Cafe and Planet Hollywood. On September 27, 2008, the Pleasure Island nightclubs closed.The Downtown Disney complex gained a sister district in California on January 12, 2001, with the addition of Downtown Disney  at the Disneyland Resort. Similar complexes also exist at other Disney resorts: Disney Village, which opened on April 12, 1992, at Disneyland Resort Paris; Ikspiari, which opened on July 7, 2000, at the Tokyo Disney Resort; and Disneytown at Shanghai Disney Resort.

The Golden Gate Bridge is a suspension bridge spanning the Golden Gate, the one-mile-wide (1.6 km) strait connecting San Francisco Bay and the Pacific Ocean. The structure links the U.S. city of San Francisco, California—the northern tip of the San Francisco Peninsula—to Marin County, carrying both U.S. Route 101 and California State Route 1 across the strait. The bridge is one of the most internationally recognized symbols of San Francisco, California, and the United States. It was initially designed by engineer Joseph Strauss in 1917. It has been declared one of the Wonders of the Modern World by the American Society of Civil Engineers.

The Frommer's travel guide describes the Golden Gate Bridge as "possibly the most beautiful, certainly the most photographed, bridge in the world."At the time of its opening in 1937, it was both the longest and the tallest suspension bridge in the world, with a main span of 4,200 feet (1,280 m) and a total height of 746 feet (227 m).

Ripley's Believe It or Not ! is an American franchise, founded by Robert Ripley, which deals in bizarre events and items so strange and unusual that readers might question the claims. Originally a newspaper panel, the Believe It or Not feature proved popular and was later adapted into a wide variety of formats,including radio, television, comic books, a chain of museums, and a book series.The Ripley collection includes 20,000 photographs, 30,000 artifacts and more than 100,000 cartoon panels. With 80-plus attractions, the Orlando-based Ripley Entertainment, Inc., a division of the Jim Pattison Group, is a global company with an annual attendance of more than 12 million guests. Ripley Entertainment's publishing and broadcast divisions oversee numerous projects, including the syndicated TV series, the newspaper cartoon panel, books, posters, and games.

We went on the first Sunday of the month (free admission) so it was crowded! At noon the parking garage was already full, so we parked by the civic center. The museum was huge, with a variety of local art, cultural history, and natural history.  We had lunch at the Blue Oak Cafe. Long line and we were told the food would take 25 to 30 minutes but surprisingly it was ready in about 5 minutes. We stayed for a few hours and could easily have stayed a few more if we weren't so tired. Lots of interactive exhibits that the kids really enjoyed. We didn't check out the special exhibit this time but it was the artwork of Burning Man. Nice little gift shop too.

This place is AMAZING. If you love Disney it's a must see. I would say it's not meant for kids, more adult oriented. They tell you it'll take about an hour and half to get through, I was there for three hours and probably could have spent more time. There is so much history, lots to read and fun stuff to interact with.It's a great journey through Walt's life and by the end I nearly cried...no joke. They also have a Cafe that serves coffee and food and some adorable Disney inspired pastries. Yum! Come spend the day, have lunch and check out the gift shop! If you're lucky the volunteer named Mark will be there, he's wonderful!!

This is a stunning museum with beautiful architecture inside and out. We paid extra to see the Early Rubens exhibit and we were glad we did. The paintings are incredible! And huge! Throughout the rest of the museum, there is a lot of beautiful art all very thoughtfully displayed. We saw some Monet, Rodin, Cézanne, and so many other famous artists.They have a lovely cafe with really good food. It's a bit pricey ($18 for sandwiches), but at least it was tasty and we didn't have to leave.

This is the best dog park in the Bay Area.  Hike for an hour or more in the off leash area.  Throw sticks into the surf and watch your dog gleefully crash into the waves.  Watch your dog run around with other dogs in a large enough area that they can easily sustain a full sprint.  I've never seen a dog fight here, nor abandoned poop.There is no easy access to fresh water at the parking lot, so it's good to bring a five gallon jug and extra towels to rinse off the dog before you leave.

Stunning & beautiful!!! I absolutely love public art; having a public garbage can, a transformer box, or the support beam of a subway stop painted by an artist just makes everything more beautiful, but these stairs are on another level! The mosaic tile art is so colorful and beautiful - I've attached pictures so you can see for yourself. And the stairs themselves are shallow, so they're easy to walk up without getting winded.

I would not describe Clarion Alley as a tourist attraction at all. It is a space for the community to make art and send positive and influential messages through art. It warms my heart that San Francisco and the Mission District welcome graffiti and murals and see the beauty in them. I love and appreciate the meaning behind the murals and it is so pretty and enjoyable to look at as you walk through the alley

Visitors can expect 18 miles of sugar-white beaches and equally pleasant water temperatures at Pensacola Beach, located on the Florida Gulf Coast (on the western part of the panhandle). The beach is an ideal getaway spot for families and offers everything from restaurants and bars to various water activities.
Getting there: Pensacola Beach is a 30-minute drive from Pensacola International Airport.

Totally drab, uninspired collections. Visitors can and do powerwalk through the exhibition spaces. The art is such pap that I was more impressed with the spaces under renovation. (Perhaps they're exhibits in disguise?) I will chuck in an extra star for the lovely building -- it's spacious, well structured and flooded with natural light, all of which make it entirely too good for its contents.

The Hollywood sign, which debuted as Hollywoodland in 1923 to advertise a real estate development, was rebuilt in 1978 to mark the iconic industry that makes Los Angeles a company town, even today. For the best selfies, park along North Beachwood Drive off Franklin Avenue and look up Beachwood Canyon, or get nostalgic at Griffith Park Observatory, where “La La Land” was filmed.

Phenomenal beach, awesome sunsets, beautiful dunes with a boardwalk, white sand, peaceful, clean and serene.  Great people watching.  Good for family fun or a romantic picnic.  The sound of the surf crashing on the rocks is very lulling and magical.  Parking can be a bit of a chore, so have patience, it is worth it.  Enjoy!

Beautiful place to visit during your stay in Chicago. It is really big so be prepared to walk a lot. If you're visiting in the summer, make sure to use sun screener and bring your water with you. Restaurants near the place are amazing! The best thing about it is the view of all the buildings.

We strolled down the wharf on our visit.  There is a great fish market at the end.  Great place to get fresh fish and seafood.  Very good prices. There's a restaurant that is a definite locals spot.  We didn't get to dine there. The menu looked great. Definitely would go back and try it.

This park has everything. There's a grass sports field, gated children's playground, restroom, activity center, and miles of trails with beautiful greenery and views. All this right in the middle of the city, and only a few blocks from shops where you can get picnic supplies.

Nice wide clean sandy beach that's never crowded. Parking is easy and free. The beach seems to go on forever toward the south. To the north it ends at the entrance into the harbor at Moss Landing. There are no businesses on the beach so no food etc. There is no lifeguard.

Must-do if you’re in Chicago for sightseeing and amazing views of the river. This is the best option to appreciate the beautiful architecture of the city. Try walking at night to enjoy the sight of lit-up buildings and its reflections on the river!

Went to see the Blue Angels. Great place to watch anywhere along the pier. Take public transit to avoid the traffice. Lot's to see eat and do. Mostly tourists..
Went to see the Blue Angels. Great place to watch anywhere along the

Before leaving San Francisco you must to go Chinatown and visit this interesting place. Also, this is the best place to buy gifts for everyone! There are a lot of shops stores at good prices! Enjoy it!
Very interesting landmark in Marina neighborhood. You need to be there at high tide to hear “the music”, but just the walk to the organ is special, with awesome city view, and right next to marina.
One of the prettiest in the way of city parks that SF has to offer. Dogs everywhere to play with, people in a great mood, grass green, nice playground, well kept and taken care of by the community.
What's the point of buying tickets online if you still have to get in line in order to get ur ticket scanned to get a paper ticket and then get in another line to be able to enter.
Easy access to beach from parking lot, and easy access from freeway as well. A beach with bathrooms is a def bonus.  Enjoyed my time here, will definitely return.
Great tour with Gael Gallagher who can weave a tale with the finest Irish wit and a wink. She makes Carmel and it’s people come alive. Highly recommend.

New playground, with great aesthetics - has a tall, yellow, metal play structure & rocky stairs leading up to a wood bridge. Lots of equipment for kids of various ages. Hard to keep track of your kids unless you get up on the bridge for a good vantage point. Surrounded by fancy buildings and great trees. Cleanest playground restrooms I've seen.

Surprisingly good, with lots to see. A moving sidewalk takes you through a long tube under one of the aquariums, with saw fish and other scary creatures swimming close by. The kids enjoyed the costume box & the tanks you could crawl under and into the middle of. The dinosaur exhibit seemed out of place but was fun nonetheless.

Beautiful new playground. In addition to the more typical play structures, it has natural areas with thick grassy berms that the kids liked to explore - I hope they stand up to use. It's sad that they would not put restrooms into a new park, but there are some at the Spark food truck court a few blocks away.

Easy hike 1.3 miles each way (with about 300 foot elevation gain) to a nice waterfall. Also saw some bears sleeping on a ledge 50 feet below the trail. The train is paved, but in poor condition, so strollers aren't a good idea - signs also advise keeping control of children due to the steep edges.

Wild, rustic hilltop park has steep unpaved trails and paved paths with tree roots busting through. A few charming old stone fences are skattered around. Top of the hill has picnic tables, a BBQ, and views through the trees. A small fenced in area has an old, tiny play structure for little kids.

Huge aquarium was great fun, but super-crowded on a holiday weekend. There were lots of helpful staff around to answer questions. The exhibits had a good combination of things you can look at and things you can do. The cafe served food fairly quickly, but it was hard to find seats to eat.

Newly renovated in 2020, it has an expansive rope structure over an artificial turf base. Also has a sloped climbing wall, concrete slides, and a three-level swing. Only a few things for toddlers. Plenty of benches for sitting & eating, and restrooms nearby

Small playground with 3 play structures and no shade. There are shade trees outside of the play area, and the buildings provide shade in the afternoon. Restrooms can be found a little bit of a walk away on the second floor of the Embarcadero center.

Formal looking square with basketball courts on one side and a playground on the other. Surrounded by brick apartments that are unusual for San Francisco. Playground is newish with rubber surface, two play structures, climbing ropes, and more.

The ground floor is grotto-themed, with a waterfall, pond, bridge, and island with a tree house (for looking only). Upstairs address the galleries, mostly Asian art, about half paintings and half sculptures that look like icicles or roots.

Windy sand & grass beach with great views of the Golden Gate Bridge & Marin. Enjoyed the Mark di Suvero sculptures from SFMOMA On the Go. Muni only goes to the edges of it, but there's also the (hard to find) PresidiGo.

Nice looking pool. Playground has old wood structures, complete with an arsenic warning - sand surface. Kids restroom adjacent to library. 3 tennis courts, bocce ball, basketball court and large paved open area.

Enjoyed the ride on a century-old steam train. There wasn't much of a view, but it was pleasant and relaxing going through the forest with the chugging and whistling of the engine & the smell of the steam.
Big park with lake and trails. Playground had old wood play structure over sand, a concrete slide, and a roller slide that didn't really work. 4 tennis courts. Restrooms. Hwy 1 is kind of noisy.
Park has an expansive playground with great views. Little and bigger play structures, climbing dome, and other small pieces. Has a rubber base and is in good condition. Restrooms.
Renovated in 2013. 1.5 basketball courts, 1 tennis court, restrooms. 2 play structures, one of them with a pirate theme, over rubber surface. Slide built into the small hillside.

A little dated, but an enjoyable car-free street nonetheless!

Has a couple of playgrounds, a block apart - one for older kids & one for younger. Could use a sand cleanup.

A grassy area surrounded by high rises, it feels like a mini version of Central Park.
Privately managed, so has a more controlled atmosphere than other parks.
Small, free museum. Has a few exhibits, a bell kids can ring, a video playing, gift shop, and an overlook of the machines pulling the cables. Restrooms.
Big grassy circle surrounded by trees and benches. No playground so the kids get to run and use their imagination. Nice view across the Hudson as well.
Italy St playground has an old wood and metal play structure over sand. Newer larger playground is listed separately as Purple Park Playground.
Busy urban playground in Chinatown. Tennis and volleyball on one level, basketball on another, and play structures on a third!
Cute farm for kids to visit & see a few cows, sheep, a pig, and some geese. Bring celery and lettuce to feed the animals.
Cute children's museum with lots of different activities for various ages. Small snack area but no other food on site.
Children's play area is pretty small. Just one play structure for smaller kids, and part of it was broken. Sand base.

Last I went on this tour I was a tween. Back then, there wasn’t much furnishings and there was a limited area that was part of the Mansion tour. I remember the tour wasn’t that long and it was hot.

Now there is a Visitor Center, Store, and a place to get something to eat and drink.

All of the antique furnishings are period base, not owned by Sarah Winchester. They give a better sense of how she would have lived.

Some of the rooms are still left as how it was after the 1906 Earthquake, which I found fascinating because she did not have these rooms repaired.

She was under 5 ft all and had arthritis. Her mansion was customer built to her size and her ailments. Lots of narrow hallways, staircases, and very short steps. The last rooms on the Daily tour (mansion) was her dining room area. The ceiling are very low.

The outside grounds are free to walk around before or after the tour.  It is funny to now look from inside through the mansion''s windows and to be outside her mansion to see “21st century San Jose” surrounding her estate, including how busy (and noisy) Winchester Blvd now is, plus Santana Row is across the street!

The Winchester Mystery House is beautifully maintained and clean inside and out. Our tour guide was amazing. She had the right amount of eeriness in her voice and her period piece costume uniform.

Can buy tickets advance online and in person.  Best to go with a group so you can talk about your experiences after the tour. The maximum tour size is 27.

NOT Accessibility or Kid Friendly: If you use a wheelchair, walker, or stroller, visiting the Winchester Mystery House is not for you. The house is not retrofitted for this and, unfortunately, you will not be able to take the Mansion Tour.

Cool education place to bring babies and young children, especially when it's cold and rainy. There is always a "talk" by one of the volunteer wildlife ambassadors educating the kids about the local wildlife and the differences between wildlife and pets.  Beware: The volunteers do feed the birds dead mice and other things while speaking.

In the Exhibit hall is on one floor and is small. You can easily see everything in one hour. but can stay longer for each "talk" (one per 30 minutes to an hour). There is a bird area that there are live birds and owls sitting above the glass enclosed bird habitats, which you think are stuffed because the birds don't move at all.

Lots of interactive exhibits for kids of all ages to engage and learn from. The active bee hive is very cool by the window - the bees come in and out from outside and go into the clear "hive" to made honey.

There are live snakes, bunny, guinea pig, mice, rat, possum and a tarantula to look at. Lindsay is also an active wildlife rehabilitation hospital for the East Bay and offers wildlife education programs and camps starting at the age of 2 through teens throughout the year at very reasonable rates.

Another great value, become a annual Lindsay member and you can also get in free or get a 50% discount to visit six Bay Area science attractions, including Oakland Zoo, and more than 300 across the United States.

Diaper changing table in the women's restroom. Tiny-sized elevator to get up to the Exhibit Hall. In a residential neighborhood, Lindsay has access to additional free parking across the street at the church's parking lot.

Best place to bring your dogs and let them roam off leash in the San Francisco Bay Area. It's quite a sight to see for the first timer. Small, big and everything in between. My two get so excited when we get to the entrance they are both whimpering and snorting so loud it's to the point of hyperventilation.

Fort Funston = Doggie Nirvana. Lots of paved trails. You can take the trek down the cliff to the beach and really watch all of the dogs running, tails wagging, tongues slobbering with glee. The views of the Pacific Ocean and the San Francisco coast and skyline are beautiful when it's not too foggy. Bring a camera and be sure to bring a jacket with you because the weather can be unpredictable.

The Park also has a hand gliding area where the glider jump off the cliff and they are gliding all around and above us. My little one gets spooked and starts barking when a glider is above her, she sometimes runs after them.

Dogs are well-behaved here. My two will start to follow others. Lots of friendly sniffing happens here.  On the weekends, it seems half the City's dogs are out here, especially when it's warm and sunny. So you and your dog will never be alone!  Owners do pick up after their dogs.

Parking in the lot can get a little stressful during the weekends because once you bring your dog(s) here, it's hard to go to another park after you see the pure joy in your little one's eyes. The public port-a-potties are clean. Your dog will crash from  all this happy hyperstimulation in the car as soon as you pull out of the parking lot guaranteed.

The main park for San Mateo. It has a rose garden with gazebo, large playground and choo choo train ride for the little ones (weekends only), tennis courts, the almost 50 year old Japanese Tea Garden (free, designed by landscape architect, Nagao Sakurai, of the Imperial Palace of Tokyo), picnic tables with BBQ grills, large open grassy areas for volleyball, frisbee, and to picnic and listen to the annual outdoor Thursday night Summer music concert series.

There is a Recreation Center in the middle of the park which is also the Senior Center during the weekdays which the seniors in the area come to exercise, socialize with one another and eat lunch. In the mornings, you will see groups of seniors exercising and groups of mothers pushing baby carriages.

No matter where you turn, you will see a happy dog with its owner. Very dog friendly (must wear leash). Poop bag dispensers are throughout the park. There is a large baseball diamond with good size stadium bench seating and a bocci ball court in front of the baseball diamond.

Many families use the park during the weekends. During the warmer months lots of kid parties are being hosted in the picnic tables area and the kids are playing in the playground or riding the train.

Central Park is beautifully maintained by the city. There is something blooming throughout the year.

There is metered 1 story parking garage underneath the tennis courts and metered street parking.

This Japanese Tea Garden is one of the best kept secrets in San Mateo. Tucked inside a section of the main urban, city park called Central Park, the San Mateo Japanese Garden is free to the public and can be crowded during the weekend with so many people walking, sitting and enjoying the tranquil scenery. For those who are planning to have a party or a wedding, the city of San Mateo will rent this lovely Japanese garden for a fee.

The almost 50 year old San Mateo Japanese Garden was designed by landscape architect, Nagao Sakurai, of the Imperial Palace of Tokyo. This strolling garden features a granite pagoda, tea house, koi pond, waterfall, bamboo grove, walking bridges and many bonsai to admire at every corner. This Japanese Tea Garden is beautiful throughout the year, especially during the late Winter and early Spring when the cherry blossoms are in bloom.

It takes about 10 minutes to walk leisurely the entire perimeter to gaze and enjoy every vista. You can watch the park staff feed the koi at 11:00 a.m. and 3:00 p.m., Monday through Friday, during Spring and Summer (fish are not fed during public hours November - February).

Metered street parking Monday - Saturday. Free parking Sunday.
likes: Scenic elements (pagoda, tea house, koi pond, waterfall, bamboo grove, walking bridges, bonsai)

reviews_attraction.text:
Wonderful place for the whole family to go explore, learn, and have fun together. There is the zoo, the panoramic gondola 🚠 ride in which you can see the Bay Area (strollers and wheel chair friendly), and Adventure Landing (Kiddy amusement park for toddlers to 8 year olds).

Can easily see and experience the zoo and Adventure Landing in less than 6 hours.

#LetsGuide Tip: Be sure to ride the gondola as part of your experience, the panoramic Bay Area views are spectacular - can see all of the East Bay, Oakland Airport, San Francisco, etc.— there are bears, mountain lions, bald eagles, etc. to see, a cafeteria with self serve outdoor dining area a “multimillion dollar view,” and a zip line for kids to enjoy.

The zoo itself is hilly (many rolling hills) so if you are pushing a stroller or wheel chair it can be a workout.

Restrooms have diaper changing tables. Lots of outdoor dining areas that you can either purchase food or bring your own and eat.

Besides zoo ticket costs, parking cost is $10/car.

During the week, the place is filled with school groups and summer camp attendees besides families. There are certain areas where there can be a lot of kids in one place because of this.
dislikes: Hilly terrain (challenging for strollers and wheelchairs)
Crowded during weekdays (school groups and summer camps)

reviews_attraction.text:
Neighborhood park in the Schaefer Ranch development. Trees that were planted here will not protect you or your kids from the elements - wind, sun, or rain. It's going to take years for them to grow to give any kind of protection.

The only protective covering / shelter is big enough for a good size kids party to keep you from the hot, glaring sun or wind. Plenty of picnic tables and space.

The public restrooms are clean. The only issue is there is NO changing table in either the womens or mens restrooms. Huge strike against the builder's part since if this is a park for kids and their families where do you expect parents to change their babies diapers?! I was there long enough to change my babies on top of a picnic table and on a picnic bench, near was safe for them. Other mothers were changing their babies on the concrete floor under the huge cover structure. Again, not safe or clean.

Plenty of street parking around the park. Local tip: Most come to the park either early morning or later in the day to avoid the heat and the sun.

One of San Francisco's oldest Roman Catholic Churches. In front of North Beach's Washington Square Park, the church inside is dimly lit, beautiful, serene, and majestic with a beautifully polished Italian Carrera Marble Altar. There are traditional confessionals and real candles to light for a donation of $5. Feels very Old World inside with all the dark carved wood work, benches and stained glass windows.

Has English, Chinese, Italian, and Latin Sunday Mass Services.

Love the bells going off throughout the day that can be heard throughout the North Beach neighborhood.

Free to visit during the day and worth the time to visit even if you are not Catholic or religious just to see and appreciate the magnificent architecture and beautiful religious art work and decor.

Mt Diablo is one of those SF Bay Area sites you can see in many parts of the Bay Area, but you never think about actually visiting it. You should!  Lived here all my life and never knew you could actually drive up and take in the panoramic breathtaking views at the very top of the Summit, 3,849 ft up! The cloud porn is amazing up here.

Besides hiking, camping, picnicking, horseback riding, and biking, also fun to visit for the whole family for a few hours. $10/car entrance fee. Plenty of designated disability parking throughout the park and at the top of the Summit’s parking lot.

Summit Visitor Center has an automatic disability door button to get in and within the Learning Center / Museum, each of the exhibits have Braille descriptions.
likes: Accessibility (disability parking, automatic door, Braille descriptions)

reviews_attraction.text: The largest park in San Ramon. Every year, the city provides a great free summer concert series, annual Art and Wind Festival, and July 4th Fireworks show for the community to enjoy here.  Family-oriented. Groups of picnic tables are available to rent for kid and family parties. The public restrooms are clean! The park is kid-oriented. It has soccer and baseball fields, tennis courts and Community Center. The kids love the expansive play structure area with the splash pad fountain. Plenty of dogs and their owners use the park during the weekends. Decades in the making, the new massive City Hall (and eventually the future downtown) is currently being build on the left side of the park.

Came here to attend a late afternoon wedding in Na 'Aina Kai's teakwood forest and wedding dinner afterwards at the former residence of the Dotys (the house has a 360 degree view of Pacific Ocean). We had a private tour after the wedding through the different areas of the garden.

Everything about the garden was designed (or envisioned) by Mrs Doty, the original owner of the garden, including the lake and waterfall in the middle of the garden and the hills where the Japanese Teahouse is at. There are custom life-size bronze statues (think Norman Rockwell or Thomas Kinkade-inspired) throughout the garden. Be sure to use bug spray if you plan to be anywhere outdoors here.

This is such a awesome place. The big, expansive playground is awesome for kids as young as 2. It includes disability-friendly swings for kids who need to be securely strapped in. The playground can be very crowded at times.

There are picnic tables and park benches around the playground with overhead sun canopies to protect from the sun and and shade.

Lots of green grass and trees. Dogs and their owners walk around the park and go to the dog park at the back of the park.

Lovely rose garden with gazebo. Great spot to take wedding photos and also get married at. There is a community event building to rent out which has a fully equipped kitchen and outdoor grill.

Free to park and see everything in 30 minutes.  Easy to get to from the parking lot, but you have to walk through the Flea Market (souvenir stalls) area to see the Spouting Horn.  Flat, paved walkways from the lot to either push a stroller or a wheelchair or have a person use a walker or cane.  The viewing platform is safe, with a high enough chain link fence to have toddlers run up and watch for the waves to rush in and watch the horn "spout."  You are close enough to see and talk photos from your phone.

There are public restrooms and picnic tables with panoramic ocean views with lots of wild chickens running around.

Best kept secret in San Francisco. Next to Crissy Field is Torpedo Wharf which is a pier that you can walk on. Besides locals fishing off the pier, you can stand and take a 180 degree unobtrusive view of the Golden Gate Bridge. This pier is the closest thing to take photos and videos of the Golden Gate Bridge for free!

#accessiblity - You can easily walk, roll (Wheelchair or stroller), run, or bike from the pavement (next to the Warming Hut Bookstore and Cafe - access to public restrooms too) to this pier. If you have a young child, be sure to hold their hand tightly. There is no guard rails or railing.
likes: Accessibility for all (walk, roll, run, bike)
dislikes: Lack of safety features (no guard rails)

reviews_attraction.text:
Cute, quaint downtown. Easily walkable in a few hours to window shop and get something to eat or drink or both. Sidewalks are #accessible for all - nice and flat for strollers, wheelchairs, and walkers.

There is a free historical museum with a jail cell to visit. The Welcome California Visitor Center is a part of the Truckee Transportation Center (Greyhound Bus Station, Local bus, and Amtrak Station).

Parking meters are now 7 days a week on both the Main Street, side and back streets.
dislikes: Parking meter fees 7 days a week

reviews_attraction.text: Next to Monte Vista High School. Great, clean park. Ducks and geese are in and around the man-made pond. Lots of well-maintained lawn. Good size playground area with bucket swings for under 18 months old. Community Center can be rented out. Nice wide walking paths for both walkers, strollers, and dog walkers. A War Memorial area in the far right corner of park. Plenty of benches to sit all around the park. Public restrooms. Free parking lot.

If it's your first time visit to San Francisco or to Chinatown, you should come here and take your photo /selfie of this iconic SF landmark or start your walk into Chinatown through Grant Avenue all the way to North Beach.

It's a fun walk and lots of photos to take as you go through Chinatown - places to eat and shop. Visit Old St Mary's Cathedral and see the Chinese Virgin Mary, Baby Jesus, and Joseph too.

Simply amazing! Martial arts choreography, Cirque acrobatics, French comedic humor, and fantastic sets and costumes all rolled into one 90 minute show. There are built-in speakers in each of the seats so the music surrounds you. Worth every penny spent. Better than Mystere. However, the only time you see a Chinese dragon is at the front entrance of the KA theater.

Fun place to visit if you are interested in knowing the history of cable cars in San Francisco.

It’s also a working station to see how the cables work to pull (move) the current cable cars up and down the streets of San Francisco for all three cable car lines.

Free to visit and walk around and see the glass display cases filled with cable car artifacts.

One of the fun, free things to do in the heart of downtown Livermore. Great gathering place to socialize, enjoy the view, and/or be like the many kids and run through the water fountain.

Plenty of benches to sit and drink a cup of coffee from the nearby Peet's or eat a pastry or two from French bakery Casse Croute.

Beautiful park in the middle of downtown Healdsburg. Lots of benches to sit and enjoy with large, mature shady trees to stay cool. There is a fountain in the middle of the plaza with a large gazebo.

Interesting to note this park has lots of trash cans and recycling containers throughout the park.

The Mission is one of the warmest, sunniest districts in The City. Lots of room to walk with your family (baby, dog), up and down the rolling hills. When you walk to the highest parts you have great views of the downtown skyscrapers. Amazed to see people sunning and picnicking during the weekday.

Interesting small museum for maritime buffs and people interested in knowing the maritime history of San Francisco / West Coast run by the National Parks Service.

Free to see. Exhibits are self-paced. Staff are friendly volunteers.

The other Bay Bridge that connects the East Bay with San Francisco.  The cool thing about this bridge now it has walking / bike lanes.  And has synchronized LED twinkling lighting at night on the San Francisco side to admire.
White, powdery soft sand. Beautiful, not crowded. Great place to walk the long beach and enjoy the breathtaking views of the beach and mountains while eating a Island Snow shave ice.

Great state park with nice camping areas.
Hiking:  Know that the Año Nuevo trail is steeper then others there, the canyon trail was closed when we visited for a land slide (April 2016) and that is only marked on some (not all) of the connecting trails; wish the grumpy entrance ranger told us that, you get to see a lot of varied environment, mostly shaded and some pretty windy due to being close to the pacific.  This SP is very particular about leave no trace (good practice but their approach to it hear seemed overboard or deficit based).  The remote trail camps (5 or so miles in) have an outhouse... good if you need it at that point in your journey.  Hiking sticks recommended.   MANY banana slugs and red CA salamanders too; watch your step.  We hiked early as well as late and didn't see/hear much else wildlife.

Camping:  Reservations fill up fast but I was able to get one of the walk in (about 100 yards) sites which was great as there isn't the sound of cars, was under amazing tall redwoods right next to our fire ring, big bear box for food/gear, and tent.  Water and toilets near by but not too close.

Great State Park for hiking.  Some busy days can fill up the parking lot and even the surrounding road-side pull offs fast.  I've seen it in hot summer days (beware some trails can be pretty exposed near Goat Rock) and in the winter mornings (where you can see great fog banks roll in).  Well maintained trails.  Depending on season might not see much water /water falls (I've been there in the summer of drought).

Free parking is available if you park outside the official lot on the road.   The only downside of this park is that a nearby gun firing range can be hear depending what side of the mountain you are on.  Never been to the campground but excited to check it out sometime (its a hike in not a drive up experience).

Castle Rock (which the park is named for) is a quick walk from the parking lot and great for people with actual climbing gear.  The moss covered rocks to your left before you arrive at Castle Rock [formation] is just as beautiful as the name sake.

This was my first time to this side of Big Basin along the coast line.   After camping in nearby Butano SP we stopped her for some mid-day hiking.   You park along the coastal highway as the entrance/parking lots is for the horse camping folk (although some parking is at the History Center which was closed during its marked hours of operation).  No visible maps in the map container but we figured it out anyhow.   This section of the Skyline to Sea trail give off a whole new set of views and environment then the upper portion of Big Basin and there is a nice 3 mile loop you can do.  A small 0.7 mile "marsh" trail is okay and can end you in the history center where there is a free build-in binoculars to view waddle beach the the air surfers.   No clear entrance fee from this side of the park.

Great park.   I almost don't want to share how great of a time I had so I can keep it to myself.   A small parking lot will start your journey (although some roads connect to trails and you can find other ways in).  NO facilities, water supply, restrooms, paper maps, or fee collection- be prepared.  A good mix of hiking trails for those that like more of a nature walk there are a few not far from the parking area and if you want to go explore I'd suggest heading towards Big Ben Tree.  Some steep climbs with a mix of redwoods and other trees; a flowing creek and nice shade.   The park is clearly dog friendly although official signs posted reflect otherwise.   I did about a 10 mile loop which was a great day.

I'd give it 10 stars if I could.  This NP has so many different environments to explore and with each change of the season they present themselves in a new manner.  I first entered the park in the SW entrance (great visitors center worth stopping to see what is closed, recommended for this time of year, etc) and I also camped at that spot too (great sites, quieter better for singles and couples).   Even in June we had multiple trails closed due to snow pack, frozen over lakes, and the first signs of flowers in some spots.  Be sure to go to the other park entrances too (they don't all connect and expect long dirt roads).

Must Sees:  Paradise Meadow,  Cinder Cone, and the Boiling Lake.
likes: Unique attractions (Paradise Meadow, Cinder Cone, Boiling Lake)

reviews_attraction.text: The trails here are very well maintained and at first look do not appear to be a challenge as the are more like back country dirt roads for vehicles, but while you might not face rugged territory here there are many miles of path with nice gradual elevation climbs, nice views in the distance and clouds gentling rolling over top of the mountain.  The tall cement 'cube' (a former military site) on the top of Mt. Um looks like a creepy X-Files left over looming while you hike.  There are two parking lots which do get busy with bikers.  A good amount of tree cover so should be good on hot days too.  There are restrooms at the parking lots; no water sources that I saw.

Well marked paths for hiking, great views to watch the fog/clouds roll over the mountain.  Don't be fooled by the CA drought... you will see moist lush environments with moss on tress, mud on the path, and wild life all around.   The park contains pet friendly (on leash) trails, picnic areas, horse back paths and more.  Great place to bring the kids or for couples on a romantic stroll.   I suggest taking a map (and returning it at the end) as some paths seem to dead end).

The Saratoga Gap Trail is nice, good views, covered by tress most of the time so good on a hot day, cool in the winter/spring.  Small parking lot at the top of Hwy 9 & 35.   The main trail connects to a few others in the area and you most likely will find yourself in a neighboring park or open space preserve.  The big downside of this hike is that you will hear traffic from a nearby road almost the entire time (even though you mostly won't see it).

Decent size local part with great views.  Many trail options can get you away from the crowds.  Most will flock to 'Eagle Rock' for the view and to sit on top of the iconic area.  Birds of prey will fly right past you front that point. In May I had a front row view to a brush fire during the drought.  In March muddy trails from recent rains.  A good place to see some wildlife... including deer and turkey.

A nice little free (parking it $6 flat) park in the city.  It would be nice if they had some more benches... I mean seems like a good calm place for reflection.  The water is still there even during the 2015 drought... although its kinda green.  Bring your family, a date, or well-behaved children and watch your step around the bird excrement.

Great park for a short hike... pay attention to your distance traveled as there are clearly paths that are much longer in distance than the 'loop' which isn't on any state park maps.   Lots of mosquitoes too.  The trees are beautiful so if you are in the area its worth a trip; not sure its worth a trip if you aren't already around.

A nice hike on a mostly well groomed path.  One are can be a little steep for weekend hikers so just pace yourself.  There are 2-3 benches to rest/relax along the way.   Be sure to go to Pfeiffer Falls too as its not that much more of a hike if you've already gone to this point.   Views are pretty far but no amazing sights.

Amazing hiking location with multiple well defined trails.  Even at 2,500 the trails were easy to find and had amazing views.   Bring water and flashlight.  Ur phone flashlight tool is fine but don't drop it.   In two days I hiked 18.64 miles and had a great time.  I used the west entrance for my starting points.

Great trails, multiple options, easily connects to neighboring Saratoga Gap Open Space Preserve.  The only issue is that some of it you are close to highway 35 and hear a lot of traffic.  Portions are in wide open spaces and give no sun protection.  Good vistas, some of which you can see the pacific.

Good place for easy-mild hiking.  Most of the hiking is open air on hills (not tree covered or shady areas... be prepared with sun screen).  Was a bit muddy when we were there in end of December.  The view from top of coyote peak is very nice (if you ignore the radio tower up there).

Amazing NP.  This park has a lot of small trails which are nice if you are there during the desert heat.  It might be best to find a spot with out trails and just sit out and observe the landscape; lots of open vistas.  Saw a good bit of flowering plants including catus.

Great garden open to the public for free in San José.   A great place to have a picnic or take a small stroll.   Many people take their wedding photos and such here.  Note this is not pet-friendly but many people run/walk their dogs outside the fenced area/perimeter.

This privately owned and operated cavern is in great condition compared to others I've been at.  For $18.50 you get a 45 minute tour by a staffer who knows this history of the area, the cave, and was great with our small group during some Q & A. Worth a visit.

This place used to be amazing until the recent redesign. There are few classic pieces still here and the sculptures /art are still good but the layout of it as a 'garden' lack a lot.  You can see everything from the parking lot which diminishes the experience

I really should say this place is bad because I don't want to let the secret out.  However, this place is a park not far from where I live that is great for a short hike.   Dog friendly, moderate in difficulty, and filled with redwoods.

Great place to relax or take a bike ride.   Yes some parts smell a bit but you get used to it. Running g here might get boring cause the views on the levees are similar.  No parking fee.  Full outer path is about 9 miles

Well maintained and dog friendly trails.   Park has a large off leash area too.   No water, trash/recycling, or restrooms so plan ahead.  Some of the park clearly shows remnants of a old/failed housing development.
Surprisingly big visitors center with extensive book collection, maps, and other items highlighting the Eastern Sierra region.  Super clean restrooms too.
The zoo is okay the park is good at the conservatory is amazing. I must stop and all free!   Support them by leaving a donation
Great experience really telling the rich history of the area. Watch the movie "Minneapolis in 19 minutes flat". It's great

Great service by the park. Based on the maps available a couple of trails are suggested. You can take some additional brochures for a small donation that actually provide quite some helpful information. The store doesn't sell bear spray, so for this you need to go somewhere else

Great hike where there's quite an incline in the beginning. When the weather is good you have a great view on the Grand Teton, but unfortunately the weather changed while hiking. Also the wild-life wasn't home today. But the view remains amazing over the Taggert and Bradley lake

Great point to see the amazing lower falls of the Yellowstone river. You can either take the look-out point, but personally I recommend to also visit the Red Rock trail. It's only a couple of steps down and is less crowded and gives you also a great view of the fall

Another great visitor center of Yellowstone. This one focusses on the fires (and consequence, as well as the positive ones!) that happen within Yellowstone. Especially the fire of 1988 gets lot of attention for the right reasons. Definitely a visit worth!

Amazing building and venue. It basically consist of two parts: (1) Pop music and (2) SCI-FI and Fantasy. Especially the pop-part we very much enjoyed! The location is very easy to get to. We recommend the City-pass that also includes the Needle.

One of the best spots in Death Valley, especially when the sunset takes place. Walk all the way up to the view point to have the full view of Zabriskie. If you want to go for a trail: this will meet at some point the Golden Gate Trail.

Nice trail, that can be really hot so bring enough water and protect yourself (and your head) against the burning sun. Walk all the way down to the cathedral where you have to climb and go to narrow tunnels to get an amazing view

Great place to get the latest information about the park. Opens at 8AM. Maybe even more interesting to do is to visit the exhibit about Yellowstone and the connection with the volcanos and wildlife. Very interesting!

One of the most amazing drives I've ever done (maybe the best). After paying $10.25 you can drive along the most amazing sceneries. Just take you time to see all the high lights by following the signs along the road

An amazing spot along the 17 mile drive. There are some parking spots, but I can imagine that during the summer it will be full. Definitely worth a visit. Especially to get there with all the great view points
An amazing park, that is much greener and 'lively' than I expected. Especially the rock structures and boulders were impressive. The park is not that big so 1 day is more than enough in my opinion
Most amazing waterfall I've seen, including the look-through into the canyon. Breath-taking! Very simple to get to. Just follow the trail and descent for a while until you get to the platform.
An absolute must if you want to see the city of San Francisco, with an amazing view of the docks and the Golden Gate Bridge. Also the lower ground is nicely decorated with wall paintings
Fantastic valley with a lot of wildlife. We were lucky to see 4 black beers by taking the Trout Lake Trail. But even without the wildlife the scenery is amazing with all it colours
Nice view on the Gibbon river falls. If you're heading towards Mammoth from the west entrance it's an easy visit. Walk down the walkway to have a very nice outlook of the fall
Go around sunrise or sunset, otherwise it will be too hot. You might have to walk 1.5 - 2 miles to get to some more quiet dunes with less tourist. But definitely worth it!
Very beautiful spring with unfortunately not a lot of water making it even more interesting. The colours are amazing and all is very accessible via the walkway
One of the biggest surprises I had in terms of visits to places. What can be great glass... Well, just visit this museum. Both indoor and outdoor are great!
Very nice and short trail with information along the track. We were lucky to see quite some lizards. Especially the rock formations were astonishing to me!
Amazing view point to see San Diego from, but also to understand more about the history of the United States and the Spanish invasion in 1592 by Cabrillo
A very nice hour and of you're lucky with the weather it's even better. Our guide Billy was very pleasant with some nice and funny fact about Seattle.
Honestly not really impressive. It was just a nice walk, but way to short to give it a name. Just look around and enjoy the nature I would say
Great visitor center about the hot springs and geysers. The building itself is already phenomenal and the gift shop is also great
I understand it's pretty impressive how it was 'created', but honestly it's a simple rock in (a much more interesting) landscape
Marvellous location where we got the information we needed. Also a giftstore is present where you can buy the bear spray

The Monterey Bay Aquarium is a contender for the best aquarium in the world. It’s also very kid friendly, but if you have no kids in tow you’ll find yourself skipping a number of the attractions. The giant tank with the swirling ball of fish is absolutely mesmerizing and can be watched for hours. Don’t miss the otter feeding either, plan out your day to get there a bit early for a window spot at the top level. The jellyfish are a sight to behold as they lazily puff through their environment. Expect to spend a minimum of two hours here if you zip through all the exhibits and don’t eat at the restaurant inside. This place is also very pricey and it’s tough to get discounts - but your money is ultimately going to sea life conservation and learning so it’s well worth it. There is parking nearby and cannery row is next door so you can easily spend an entire day in this little area.

Prepare to spend at least a few hours here to truly appreciate it all - or all day to really get your money’s worth. Entrance to the 17-mile-drive costs $10.50 and is very worth it. They’ll give you a map of all the attractions at the start and there’s usually parking at each one with signposts explaining the history. The only truly crowded attraction is the Lone Cypress, so prepare to wait for parking if you plan on stopping there. There are also a number of hikes/walks you can take, so both beach and hiking shoes are a good idea. Some attractions have picnic benches for eating, but not all. Bathrooms are rare, and there is no gas station on the drive either.

A great place to learn about Hawaii’s plantation history. The train ride is about thirty minutes and is very educational, and you’ll see real tropical plants you wouldn’t see anywhere else. The garden tour is fairly short but there’s a neat pond with wildlife. However, the maze can be tiring and there’s little shade. We gave up fairly quickly, as it’s pretty tedious even with the map. Overall we spent about three hours here. The shop has pretty good Dole Whip and the food is not bad for a tourist trap. Overall, this place is a must on your Oahu visit.

This place far exceeded my expectations- I went in thinking it would be a cheesy tourist trap but it’s actually an incredibly beautiful piece of Bay Area history. Would highly recommend the extended tour of the basement and spires. The guides are very knowledgeable and can answer pretty much anything you ask about the house. It’s amazing to see just how much work was done on the place, and it’s all been preserved or restored to perfection. Places like the rooms damaged in the SF quake are accessible and very interesting to see.

Great tour - this is a no-frills and highly educational tour of a real decommissioned military sub. All the levers and knobs still work and everything is in great condition. There are very few restrictions on this tour - most things are hands on. If you want to touch something, you can. Nothing has been removed. Takes about 30m to see it all. A bit pricey but thoroughly enjoyable. Can combine with your visit to the USS Arizona. Doors inside are very small - at 6ft I felt like I was at risk of a head bump all the time.

Don’t miss this on your NYC visit! Awe-inspiring monument with a rich historical background. It’s absolutely worth the extra $$$ to go up to the crown - book your tickets well in advance. Expect to spend 3-4 hours here to see it all, including the ferry rides. You’ll need to pass through security multiple times so leave sharp objects at home and account for that in your scheduling. There’s a restaurant which serves decent food at the monument so you don’t need to bring a meal.

Lots of military history here - show up early so you can read all the info before you hop on the boat. It’s kind of amazing that the memorial itself is on top of the actual sunken ship - it’s one thing to read about it but another thing entirely to stand where the ship was sank. Very amazing and sobering experience. If you come to Honolulu and have any interest in history, make sure you check this out.

Take a date or just sit and meditate while the sun sets. Fantastic views of the bay, great place to sit and just talk until it gets dark and you have to stumble down the stairs. It can get chilly here on cold days, but nice and warm in the summer. Parking is usually pretty available nearby, much to the local homeowners chagrin.

This park is right next to NYU and is so full of life and activity. There’s a good amount of homeless but they are friendly and harmless during the day. Lots of live music and college students just relaxing and enjoying the trees. This park is not kid-friendly and is pretty dirty, but great for a mid-afternoon walkabout.

Long walk with stars in a not-so-nice part of Hollywood. Parts of the walk are very touristy and dirty - it’s not really maintained very well by the city. Prepare to deal with homeless and beggars selling trinkets. Parking near the Chinese Theater is expensive, it’s worth it to park a bit farther and walk.
