Neat little art sculpture under the bridge. Can combine with a stop at the nearby brewery if you don’t want to come all the way out just for a troll photo op. One tip, the city does not appear to clean the area and we saw a couple dead animals and trash - watch children and animals.

The Lone Cypress is where everyone stops. Parking is plentiful but usually it’s all occupied. If you stop anywhere on the 17-mile-drive, make it here and snap some photos. You can actually walk down and get pretty close to it via a stairs and a catwalk which has been installed.

Incredibly detailed and informative museum. Probably the best museum in Vegas. They don’t hold back any grisly details. Very interesting trip through Vegas history and the history of organized crime in America. Parking is easy here and expect to spend 3-4 hours to see it all.

Don’t miss this beautiful white-sand beach! There’s a hiking trail at the end of the parking area which runs for a mile or two and leads to more beautiful views and beaches. The hike is easy (really more of a walk) and is mostly flat and occasionally on sand.

Unless you come during an event, it’s a pretty plain landmark. There are celebrity hands and feet beyond the roped off area but you can’t get to them, unlike the stars. Looked like a pretty dirty and touristy place, not much to see or do here.

It’s exactly what you’d expect - a wall of discarded gum. For best results on Instagram, wear your best hipster outfit and blow some bubbles. Be sure to get bubble gum, and of course, help it find a home once you’re through.

Bring a camera - incredible views of LA here. There’s also a little museum place inside with some interesting astronomy tidbits. One hour to see it all, it’s a good idea to combine this with a trip to see the Hollywood sign.

Neat art installation in the desert. Good photo op, nice place to stop before the long drive home. For best photo results, come in afternoon and have your subject face into the sun and shoot against the desert background.

Incredible mountain and lake views. Great place to start many hikes. If you go here, be sure to also stop by nearby Vikingsholm. Bring a camera, because this is where you’re going to want to take your Tahoe photos.

A really beautiful little park. Has the occasional homeless person in it, but they keep to themselves. Has a nice new fountain and sitting area. Grab a coffee or bite to eat and sit here to people watch.
A must-see for your next Seattle visit. The glasswork is beautiful and very creative. Sometimes the big greenhouse room is closed for weddings, so go early in the day to make sure you see everything.
More beautiful views - if you aren’t tired of having your breath taken away by the views at Pebble Beach, stop here and prepare to gasp once more.
Free for students! Don’t forget your student ID like I did. The bells at the top are mesmerizingly complex. Good views too.
Bird Rock appears to be covered in ranch dressing. Not sure how it all got out there, but it makes for quite the view.
How do you let all your friends know you’re at UC Berkeley? Take a photo in front of Sather gate, of course!

hidden gem of a hike behind the suburbs of glendale! free parking near the library. i saw two trailheads, my friend and i took the "seven trees one." it is quite steep so beware. wear proper shoes, bring sunscreen, and water for sure! the path is dirt/gravel so can be slippery at times. the views of glendale/burbank are pretty neat! unfortunately, it was quite smoggy today. there are many forks in the road, with not too much signage. my friend and i ended up going higher up the mountain and traversed along the verdugo motorway and the brand motorway, until finally making it back to the parking lot (7 miles). more signs/maps would be helpful... we were scared we got lost a few times! there were not too many people on the trail, which was nice. also water fountains/restrooms would be great additions to the trails!

this hike is fun! not too grueling... to the falls and back is 3ish miles. it's generally shaded and being by the streams keeps it cool and not too muggy. we started at 8am on a saturday and fortunately snagged a spot in the lot before it quickly filled up. be careful if parking along the stone wall because we saw a car ram into it too fast... puncturing its front tire and damaging its bumper! back to the hike... it's definitely crowded, and we maybe encountered 3 groups of people with speakers blaring out of the backpacks. also lots of dogs along the way. overall a fun way to get outdoors and get some exercise while enjoying the scenery!

i really liked this venue! a great spot for a summer concert. my friend and i got to the show about an hour early and managed to find a street parking spot (saved 30 bucks on parking! look out for street signs though because some areas are tow away after 8pm). the venue itself is clean and intimate... similar to the hollywood bowl but smaller. the band was super fun and i would definitely like to come to more concerts here in the future. the only thing was that there were a lot of people in our section smoking weed so it smelled pretty strongly throughout the evening.

came here for a giants dodger game on a friday night. parking was $17 if you purchase online. we sat on the loge level and the atmosphere was very safe and fun. fans in our area were respectful and not too rowdy. food was mediocre... not too many options on this level (mostly just dodger dogs and sausages and one pizza stand). food and drinks are pricey but that's expected for a ballpark. ballpark is one of the oldest in the nation, but still pretty especially when sunset hits. overall a fun experience and something every one living in LA should try!

so awesome!! this hike is a little out of LA on the 14 but so worth because it’s gorgeous and not crowded at all. there is a parking lot with ample parking. the visitor center has a display of different reptiles, a mini gift shop, very clean bathrooms (!) the hike itself has a little for everyone... it’s not too challenging but does have some hills. you can even do some rock climbing if you’re up to it! i had a great time :) one thing to beware of... it may be windy so dress appropriately. dogs allowed on leash!

this was a little pit stop on my drive from SLO back to LA. really enjoyed walking around, going up to the tower, seeing the view, and taking in the beautiful architecture. someone was getting married and it looked really pretty! would recommend if you're in the area. there's lots of street parking around the area that's not metered.

i love joshua tree national park. definitely come
visit in the winter. lots of hiking and nature trails and rock climbing and exploring. the afternoons get busy and it can get tricky to find a parking spot but you just have to be patient. make sure you download a map or have a paper copy because there’s no cell reception.

a hidden gem in los angeles! tons of parking, no entrance fee. you can spend a decent amount of time wandering around the property and admiring the architecture and garden. there's .a cute little pond with turtles too. you can't go inside but you can peak. lots of movies were filmed here dating back to the 50s fyi!

really nice facility with tranquil and clearly marked trail heads. nothing intense, but makes for a really enjoyable stroll on a quiet saturday afternoon. not too many people about and people were good about wearing masks and keeping distance. there is a parking fee, but it looked like not everyone paid?

really nice trail!! lots of parking (dirt turnouts) along the main road, was not difficult at all. the trail is easy to follow and the top vista point is pretty impressive! the decline (mystic canyon) is very steep so be careful. also would recommend bringing water since it gets hot in the summer.

beautiful gardens to escape the busyness of los angeles. entrance fee was $25 (reserve online ahead of time). i loved the asian gardens and the desert garden. tea room currently closed because covid. also the gift shop was super neat — also very well curated. would love to come again!

played course 3 on a saturday afternoon. prices were reasonable and it wasn't too crowded! we reserved online a week in advance ($10 deposit that you get back). ample parking. covid precautions followed. a nice way to get outdoors and enjoy time with friends safely!

beautiful spot on the sand dunes to watch the sunset. a hidden gem that a cal poly student brought me to. there's quite a walk to get to a spot where you can see the sunset, but it is well worth it. fyi there are no bathrooms, only a porterpotty.

gorgeous view, tons of parking, bathrooms available. gets busy depending on time of day. there are also some hikes (badlands loop) that you can explore. be sure to bring water because (obviously) there is no shade and it gets toasty mid-day!!

a pretty easy nature stroll/trail. cool landscapes and the dam sure is an interesting feature. there is a big lot and even if it’s full, there are always people coming and going. also connects to echo t trail and some neat petroglyphs.

this is more of a walk/stroll. not stroller friendly because gravel. it brings you from jumbo rock campsite to skull rock and back to the campsite. signage is a little confusing on this trail but it’s a doable 1.7 mile loop.

i can't believe this place is free! so much to see and so much nature to enjoy. parking is easy and there's a little nursery where you can talk to the arboretum volunteers and also buy a plant baby to take home!

i love this hike!! it's kinda .hidden gem. beautiful views. can be a bit chilly and windy on an overcast day, but on a clear day, the views of the ocean are seriously stunning. parts can get a bit steep fyi!
great views and trails. lots of signs and maps so you won’t get lost. not super shady so be aware and bring sunscreen and water on a hot day. also lots of mountain bikers and some rattlesnakes!!
okay park for the area, there are some homeless people hanging around and bathrooms were super nasty. but there were also some families with kids and people walking their dogs.
a little slice of nature in a bustling city. the turtles are my favorite part. the botanical gardens are surprisingly big so definitely give yourself some time to explore!
huge grassy area for picnic-ing or just hanging out. other people were playing frisbee, walking their dogs, etc. nice when it's not super hot out. safe area!
the nutcracker is such a treat! beautiful venue with gorgeous architecture... love the christmas decorations. a must see for the holiday season.
likes: Facilities & Services: Beautiful Venue, Gorgeous Architecture

reviews_attraction.text: one of my favorite hikes in the bay area. can get crowded/touristy. but it's always a treat checking out the labyrinth or sutro baths.
i love their saturday morning deal! only $3 and not crowded. my favorite is course 1. always a fun time at sherman oaks castle park

Beautiful location. Really a must visit. When we were there (early April) the weather was windy and there were amazing waves in the water. But the weather was sunny too we could see gorgeous colorful water and surrounding views. Park your vehicle in the separate parking area provided, which is a very large area and very well maintained, plus some roadside parking is also available. There's a restroom too. The island is beautiful filled with trees and the whole area in general has lots of trees and greenery. So many people come for walking, jogging, biking and hiking and much more to explore. It's a lovely place, would definitely come again. Thanks.

A great historic landmark not to miss while on a walking tour of the financial district in New York. We visited here on a cool morning and it wasn't crowded. The architecture of this beautiful building catches our eyes from far away.  Grand from outside and grand from inside. It's really decorated and maintained very well. Such a peaceful place to be at amongst the hustle and bustle of the busy city of New York. We were here for about half an hour but someone can spend more time based on how much leisure they have. Would like to visit again and spend some more time there.

This is such a great place with a variety of beautiful views and places to walk, relax, camp.  Lake Winnebago and Sherwood views from the wooden observation tower are well worth to climb that tall structure.. Don’t miss it. Also people were launching their boats at the huge boat launch. Butterfly pond trail is beautiful too. And the family camping grounds are amazing - personal spots to park your vehicle and have fun, eat and enjoy the nature right there. We will visit again for sure.

Amazing place to just take a drive, slow and relaxed. It is right besides the Fox river, and there are good parking places everywhere around the drive loop. We like the spots near the river, there are little swings at different places. Just sit back on a cute swing, relax, watch the river, people boating and the nature. This is our go to place to spend time. Just that if you need restroom it might not always be open.

Beautiful scenery!! Colorful beach atmosphere. There’s a lovely trail walk besides the magnificent beach. It’s so much dreamy to walk leisurely while watching the awesome waves in the Pacific Ocean. In spring there were pretty pink little wildflowers everywhere near the trail. Those were adding a special beauty to the beach scenery. Kissing rocks and the crashing waves, are just surreal to sit and watch. Great !!

Great atmosphere. So many people come here and enjoy their time. Trail walk alongside the lake is awesome. Evenings here are superb, especially summertime and the beautiful warm vibes. Lively, clean and safe place. Many people play on the lawn, make music, play guitars, read books, sunbathers are relaxing, picnic tables are available and families come to enjoy weekends too. It's an awesome park, really !!!

Great place. Nature is exceptionally beautiful. Awesome location for hiking and camping etc. Obviously as the name suggests Voyagers National Park, it's superb for all types of water fun like boating, kayaking etc too. Maintained very well, place is clean and roads are nice. Restrooms are good. Beautiful lake views and thoughtful overlooks and trails too. Overall it was a great experience visiting here.

This is my go to place to have a quiet walk in nature. Have been here on different times of the day morning, afternoon, evening. It’s always beautiful and well maintained. I love the trail going through the woods. And the children’s play areas are so good. The swimming pool is amazing too in summer. The picture is taken on a spring day. In summer the trees are lush green with greenery everywhere.

Definitely a must visit place if you are around this area. In winter it's beauty is stunning with the frozen icicles on the rocky lakeshore. Just keep in mind that it's always crowded, and finding a parking is a bit difficult on more crowded days. So if possible visit on a weekday. We have visited here thrice in different seasons of summer, fall and winter. I liked it best in winter.

Beautiful beach atmosphere. Walk on the beach, watch the waves and feel the beauty of magnificent nature. Loved our time here. Took a lot of pictures and videos. This place is very near to the 17 miles drive so don’t forgot to take that scenic drive if you haven’t already. Also see the nearby beautiful places too which could be off the beaten path but really worth the visit. Thanks !

Superb experience to walk the trail amongst the golden and orange limestones mountains. Such a magnificent place. It’s really hot during day times though. So preferably don’t go too far during daylight, try to hike before 10am or in the evenings. And carry enough water and wear proper clothing and hats, sunglasses etc. It’s a great experience if done carefully !!

We went here on a beautiful spring sunny day. But weather was still cold. While entering every vehicle needs to buy a daypass or yearly pass, like other State parks. The trails are really neat and give awesome nature views. Liked the calm and quiet atmosphere near the bay. Park staff was very helpful too. Want to visit again.

Just. Parking spot but has great views. Lake looks really pretty on a sunny day with blue skies. When we went there prior to that it had been raining for a couple days so the soil was very wet there and it was too muddy and soft. There's basically nothing much. Just great for spending some leisure time with nature.

Views are simply great. We went here in summer so the mountains were perfectly covered everywhere with greenery and lakes were filled with pure water. Wildflowers were in bloom and there were literally thousands of colorful butterflies everywhere  !! It's a nature lover's paradise  !! Truly. Thanks so much  !!

This drive is really beautiful. And a very famous thing to do if it’s on your bucket list. Really worth the visit. There’s an entry fee to take this drive about $10. But the view points are simply stunning and the beaches and ocean is superb. Highly recommended. We loved our day out here !!

A beautiful quiet park to walk around and have pictures taken. There are nice children play areas. It’s close to the city and still have that calmness of being out of town. The Duck Creek flowing through the park offers beautiful views to photograph.

A nicely maintained small park. We sat on a bench near the bay. Enjoyed our time and the beautiful views of bay and harbor and the huge ships nearby. The restrooms were locked, donno why, mostly because of the still so cold weather in early spring.

Harbor Park: Beautiful quiet place. Maintained very well and clean. Good to take a walk alongside water. There are many ducks, geese and seagulls when in migration. Parking is available. Nice atmosphere. We have visited here many times. Thanks.

The park educators are really welcoming. We talked with Andrew. The trails and other areas are maintained very well. We saw so many birds including geese, baby geese, northern cardinal, woodpeckers, etc
Serene and quiet place. Beautiful lake views. Lake is frozen during winter and some of the spring season. Great for little walks and spend some nice time in nature alone or with family and friends.
Beautiful area to hike, be in nature and having high cliffs naturally. Observation tower offers great views. Roads are nicely maintained to drive inside and good parking spots.
Beautiful and great historical location. Maintained very well. Clean premises. Great for a walk and also for spending some leisure time near water. Thank You.
Yet another beautiful place on Blue Ridge Parkway. Great for a nature hike and feel the nature’s sounds around us. Loved the experience!!
Beautiful place. We stopped here while driving the complete stretch of Blue Ridge Parkway this summer. Was an awesome experience!!
A great place to enjoy outdoors with trees and nature around. It’s a dog park. People come here to walk and play with their dogs.

This is a one time experience but not more. There is a hidden fees which is the parking. You must pay it because you are no where in the wood. The tour is 45 minutes because of the good theatrical performance of the staff. However, it is really 5 min of illusion. There are so many people that when you pay you may have to wait 2h before your your start. The problem is this is very grateful from everything. It means that you are stuck to wait which is not great at all if you have kid. I went with a two years old and it was borderline.

Nice but when we went 75% were under heavy construction. Parking is not free and some homeless wander around. It is small. You can do the whole park in 30 minutes if you walk at a normal pace.

Edit: I went back in August 2018 ( more than 10 months later ). No water, barely anything to see, nothing advertise the bad conditions. I even saw a broom with her wedding dress in the parking lots who was about to get desappointed. It is not worth it at all. Always under maintenance. Also, a lot of animal feeces in the sidewalk.

You better pay a day pass and spend the day there. We finished the afternoon and paying 5$ per ride is way too expensive. Lot of rollercoasters require a minimum of 36 inches so I'd say that it is more adequate if your kid is above 3 years old. The pier is nice but you must wear shoes or sandals because it is made of wood. I saw someone on the ground with people trying to help to take of splinters. I would come back for more than an hour.

Best place to ride a train with a 34 inches and more kid. The ride is long and fun. The price is a donation and it was strongly pushed to give. I didn't like the pressure first but it is worth it. For 2 adults and 1 kid it costs 9$. The waiting line was about 15 minutes and the ride about 8 minutes. They have many trains hence it goes fast. The only thing I didn't liked else the pressure was the parking which is a war zone

Nice parking, lots of place on the beach to settle. There is a strong fishy smell that might bother some people. The ship is sank and it is hard to see anything anymore. The pier is not accessible more than half of it which is owned by seagulls. Still one of the best beach around because of the parking (10$) which is at 2 min walk from the beach. There is free restroom and a lot of picnic tables.

This place is free but if you want to ride it will cost you about 3$ each. Reasonable price. The trains are old and awesome to see. They are huge and you can go in few of them. The place is crowded with artists but it is okay. Lots of family come this place which is great if you have kids. There is place to have picnic and you can organize party. The parking is big and free.

Great park, lots of grass, picnic tables, good amount of playground structures, restrooms. Parking is on the street but plenty of space. Few swings, about 6. There is a basketball court and plenty of space to run. The park does not have sand pit, neither water structures. Two main areas, one with a fake train, one with a fake tree house structure.

Nice place, but a lot of people. The park is nice for kid but not the greatest. You must follow your children very close because of the amount of people. Parking is very challenging. It can take 20minutes to find a spot and it can far away (plus 15 min walk). The view is great. Worth a one time but I do not plan to come back.

Park is awesome. Lots of well maintained structures. The only downside is the parking with 7 slots.

The theme is the sea and is divided in two which is for toddler and for older. Each part are covered and have several palm trees.

Restrooms available, basketball field and limited table to eat are available.

Parking in the streets. 3 concrete slides which are very steep. You must use cardboard to slide. Lots of swings. The park was a little bit dirty with many papers and trashes on the ground. It is a nice park but not the greatest around. There is 5 tables to eat and no restroom.

Nothing to see but a place to enjoy looking around. You can sit and enjoy the city. Lots of homeless people. It is the place for several bus tour as well. There is a limited number of table where you can sit and eat. No public restroom, little shade but mostly under the sun.

Huge park with many tables to eat (around 12) and it has restrooms. No water park but two areas: 5 and under and one 5 and up. The 5 and under has a fence and animal are prohibited. There are basketball courts, bowls field, swings and many place with grass under huge trees.

We went there a Friday at 1pm and it was jam-packed. Couldn't park anywhere, even far away on the street it was impossible. We had to leave. From what I saw, it looks good but the lack of possibility to actually leave the car is high. I cannot imagine during the weekend.

Nice park with a great parking and restrooms. Only two swings for adults (no seat for young). The sand is okay, but lots of branches in it. Many rocks and sound objects to play with and few slides. The location is in a residential project, loved the calm atmosphere.
Water fountains, parks divided in two with one with full Gates and smaller slides. Four swings for baby, three for toddler. Lots of green space, free parking, small restroom.
Great park with a small parking that is payable and no gates for small kid. Has a train and swings. Has a fake plane and lot of grass. Nice place to take pictures.
Huge park with east access with bike to most area. It has soccer fields, parks, tennis courts and some plain area. You can eat on place since it has picnic tables.
Next to the botanical garden, this park got an area for kid to play. Like the botanical garden, this is free. Lots of tree so possible to get some shade.
0.8 miles to walk , can take 30 to 1 h depending if you take the time to look around. Parking is not free. Restrooms at the start and half way.
Interesting museum. Some time can be free. 2 years old toddler was not very cooperative for this kind of museum. I suggest above 5 years old.
Great beach, low parking but the sand is great and clean. Waves are great and the view is a mix of houses and the boats at the wharf.
Great sandy park with many trees to cover. There is restrooms, and grass. No water game, no parking. You need to go on the street.
We went October 1st around 10am. The sanctuary is 5 minutes walk with a toddler. Probably better later in the season.
Small beach, not very deep, more large. Water is not blue but it is okay. Like that it's near and has free parking.
It's a nice place since it's near of Redmond heart, but there is a lot of horse poops on the ground.

Nice place to walk through a Japanese style garden. There is currently some work being done on one of the ponds. Went on a spring weekend in the afternoon and the line for tickets took about 15 mins, but didn’t feel too crowded once inside. There is a nice, small picnic area to eat at before exploring the garden. Not much food onsite, just a few snacks in the gift shop, so bring your own food.  It’s a lovely place but not huge, taking your time it takes about an hour.

We arrived around 9:30 and while the tasting room doesn’t open until 10 the gate was open and we could explore the gardens before it got busy with people taking pictures. By 11 the parking lots were filling up and the tasting bar was busy (a Saturday). I didn’t do any wine tasting as I really wanted to see the lavender. Bought some lavender honey which is great! Not a huge place but nice to sit and relax in the shade for a bit. There are areas to picnic.

Lovely place for a hike. So many trails to choose from. There are 3 park entrances. Parking is free. It’s never too busy. Make sure to take a map and view the topography as some of the trails and quit steep and are not for all fitness levels. Some trails allow horses and mountain bikes. There are lots of wildlife to observe such as deer, birds of prey, and gophers. Good place to see spring wildflowers.

Really beautiful hike. Of course most people focus on the short boardwalk around the geological features. Those are really neat, but the hike also has spectacular views of the valley, surrounding mountains and meadows of wildflowers. Much of the hike is in the sun so prepare. The parking lot of the trail head gets very busy. You can also enter at the less busy Kings creek picnic trail head too.

Beautiful location that was different in scenery than the 2 area National parks. Because this is a state park the national park pass won’t get you in. There were very clean, flush toilets here. Also a snack stand and a large interesting visitor center. The trails are nice and not too steep. It gets busier around sunset as it is an amazing place to watch the sunset.

Nice large campsites near the lake. Clean facilities and helpful staff. Only downside for me was that you could hear traffic at times and in parts of the campsite you could see people’s backyards so you didn’t really feel like you were in a remote area. That said it was great that we were in close driving distance to museums like Mass MOCA and The Clark.

Amazing national park. Views here are incredible. Also less busy than some of the other area parks which was very welcome. There are pit toilets but only a water fill up at the visitor center. No place to buy food so bring everything you need with you. Trails are great and there are levels to suit everyone.

Beautiful during the peak rise season. Lots of people, like wedding groups, come to take pictures here. It’s free but can be hard to find street parking nearby. Here you can also catch some great views of the bay. Not wheelchair accessible to go down but views from street level are still impressive.

Great park- lots of parking. Some lots are free but some of the lots further in are $6. Great education center. Has a variety of trails both dirt and hilly and paved and flat. Some great interpretation panels about the park history as a tourist spot for the mineral springs there. Lots of restrooms

Nice for families with small kids. Flat, paved walkways and a large playground. Holiday lights in December. You have to pay for parking inside the park but just outside there is usually plenty of street parking. Can be very busy, not a great place if you are looking for a quiet spot.

Amazing views of the bay. Bring sun protection as there are not trees at the top and is quite exposed. While there is a paved road around the island in order to get to the summit the trail is narrow and dirt. At the top there are a number of picnic benches.

Great local museum near downtown Los Gatos.  Family friendly. Had a great exhibition of artwork from local high schools. Downstairs there was a small exhibition dedicated to the history of the town. Would say it would take about an hour or so to go through.

It wasn’t for me. You wait in line to take pictures in brightly colored rooms. Expensive, not much to do or ice cream to be had. If you are into selfies I guess it could fit the bill but expensive ticket to take pictures. Really about the hype.

There is a $15 fee to enter. The national park pass doesn’t work here as it is a state park. Facilities are great. There is even a cafe during the day which was ok but the only option around. People come here to watch the sunset.

Come early on weekends, parking can get very busy especially during whale migration season. Great, knowledge docents were on hand to help explain the history of the site. Some small flat trails are nearby. Can be super windy.
Incredible place. There are many different sites in this park. I would review before going or at least stopping by the visitor center. There are beaches, campsites, trails, a mammal center, etc.
The most incredible views on my 6 National park trip was at this location. The trail was very easy. Get there early to beat the crowds and to get your pictures without people.
Curved, steep drive up. Good amount of parking and a bathroom. Not the most impressive overlook but itself in the park, but I went just in case I could see a jet. I didn’t.
Museum part was closed due to COVID but the shop inside was still open. You could see most of the exhibits from the shop part. Very small but packed with information.
Lovely garden, very nice staff. One docent walked us around like a private tour. Interesting collection with free admission. Easy to walk to from main shopping area.
Lovely area. Clean bathrooms. Rolling hills but not too steep. Dogs allowed on lease. Not many benches or trash bins along the way. Small parking lot.
Lovely, family friendly park with farm animals and orchards. So many places to have picnics. Restrooms and a hall that could be rented for events.
Small park. City has had activities in the park over the summer to enliven the park. Feels safe overall but not a destination itself.
Great place for a day of fairly easy trails. Visitor center and bathrooms available. You have to pay for parking
Such a beautiful spot to spend a morning. Weekends can get busy in nice weather. Such a huge variety of plants.

Local Eval.:  Mysterious ancient surreal "Dali-like" twisted Oaks, almost drowning in huge beards composed of Spanish Moss, in a dreamy moist microclimate, punctuated by the distant road noise.

While it seems straightforward at first, and the multiple short trails converge at points, it is quite easy to wind up following dead end paths.  Since the road noise never really goes away, you can always head toward a direction where it gets louder.
Since the trail map & trail heads all indicated loops, I picked the Chumash loop.  While one can always backtrack, the far ends of the trails do not obviously interconnect, nor are labelled, so I can see why people get lost.  Fortunately, it is a rather small reserve, which is a mixed blessing.  As you progress, you go through some interesting terrain changes...from sandy beach like brush to very moist Oak/Spanish Moss humid twisted tree dense surreal forrest.  It is rather otherworldly and I have not seen anything quite like it before in my travels...so it is well worth a brief easy hike. The provided pamphlet is informative.

BUT BEWARE OF SOME STEEP HIDDEN SUDDEN DROPS TO A CREEK BED!

As many others have noted, it is a relatively unknown preserve, easy to pass by on the road unnoticed, and rather devoid of people.  My wife became a bit scared when I reviewed some tips on what to do if we happened to encounter bigger mammals [which I doubt live here...but Los Osos means "Bears"].  The last thing one wants to do, is to run from either a Mountain Lion or a Bear.  She was ultimately spooked by a human being!  She was right....human beings are the most dangerous.  She actually asked for me to buy her a Pepper Spray for the future.

Other than two other humans, I only saw a small lizard, and did not notice any Poison Oak/Ivy, nor Stinging Nettle [which I had a horrid very painful run in with at Arroyo Grande's creek].

While I may have seen "Pele's Hair" [AKA invasive Spanish Moss in Hawaii] while hiking in Oahu's Tantalus forested area, I had never before seen, nor really appreciated, overwhelming volumes of Moss.  They are not a form of Lichen, as others have noted, but are relatives to other so-called "Air" plants, which get their nutrients from the air, and even leaching minerals from Oak trees.

According to Wikipedia: "...This plant's specific name usneoides means "resembling Usnea", and it indeed superficially resembles its namesake Usnea, also known as beard lichen, but in fact Spanish moss is neither a moss nor a lichen. Instead, it is a flowering plant (angiosperm) in the family Bromeliaceae (the bromeliads) which grows hanging from tree branches in full sun through partial shade....Spanish-moss is an epiphyte which absorbs nutrients and water through its leaves from the air and rainfall.
While it rarely kills the tree upon which it grows, it can occasionally become so thick that it shades the tree's leaves and lowers its growth rate....the plant seems to show a preference for growth on southern live oak (Quercus virginiana) and bald cypress (Taxodium distichum) because of these trees' high rates of foliar mineral leaching (calcium, magnesium, potassium, and phosphorus) providing an abundant supply of nutrients to the plant..."

The Discovery Day hike today was fantastic & free.
BTW- We have been longtime local contributors to support the development of the preserve, but this is the first time we had the
pleasure of hiking here!
We were picked up by the last free Shuttle right from the front of Lido's Restaurant at the Dolphin Bay Inn (a kind sponsor) & we were the only ones in the vehicle. The driver was super-nice & so were the volunteers at the Preserve.  We almost made it to the Avila Lookout, but we had tons of great views of Ocean vistas all thru the hike.  The hike for us out of shape types took about 2.5 hours. We then regained out calories at Lido's with an extensive dinner including a bottle of Champagne, Whale watching from our ocean view table, & Choc. Mousse for desert! An amazingly fun afternoon for us local Shell Beach residents.  Thanks to all who sponsored the event!

From the KCOY TV News Website on June 10th 2017: "

Lifestyle
"Pismo Preserve discovery day draws hikers from near and far"

The Pismo Preserve was open to the public for the first time as part of a discovery day. (Michal Colaianni/KEYT)

PISMO BEACH, Calif. - In the hills above Pismo Beach, hikers were given the chance to get a new and unique view of the Five Cities.

The Pismo Preserve was open to the public to hike the more than 11 miles of trails unsupervised for the first time Saturday.

"This is the first chance for the public to get out and enjoy these trails on their own," said Kaila Dettman, Director of the San Luis Obispo Land Conservancy. She says while this area is known for the beach, they noticed a need for hiking grounds.

"There's no upland hiking and mountain bike trails, so we saw a real need for there to be access for people to get up in the hills and into nature."

"I'm always amazed by all of the different little vistas around every corner," said Dyan Theobald, the conservancy's Stewardship Manager. "It is really nice to see the general public come out here and enjoy, especially after all the hard work the community has put into this project."

The conservancy raised more than $10 million to buy the preserve property from the previous owners, who were considering developing the land. Organizers hope to have the preserve fully up and running in 2018.

The preserve will be open for two discovery days a month until it opens. The next chance to check it out is June 25.

"All you have do is hop on a free shuttle," Dettman said. "It's a short drive from City Hall, and in south county we have some stops as well. Then anyone can come out here and hike, and mountain bike, and enjoy themselves."

OK playground for kids...but you need to watch
them & others to prevent a fall off the cliffs!
Nice for a walk.  During the summer they sometimes
have arts & crafts festivals.  Parking is usually not
a problem. Does have restrooms.  A good break from
driving on the 101.

As far as the photos here, some are for other nearby locations
or totally off.  Many are taken from the nearby "Inn on the Cove",
or the "Hidden Cove" that I added (which is beach accessible
only by either a fairly risky path from the Inn, or by boat).
Part of it also lies under Dinosaur Caves Park, but it is not accessible
via DCP. Other pics are from the nearby Margo Dodd Park & the
Conservancy area.  All are beautiful.  Regardless of all these
nearby areas, there are no easy access to "Caves"...except
by Kayak or by a hazardous path thru partially filled
natural tunnels at low tide.

The "Cave" collapsed & the artificial Dinosaur was
destroyed long ago. What remains is mostly a flat
plateau that runs from Shell Beach Rd. to Cliffs
with a step drop off. There is no beach access here,
but there is past Margo Dodd Park....where there is
a stair case.  Here at low tide you can carefully explore
the hazardous rocky shore.  The rocks are unstable, which
when combined with the incoming
tide, rogue waves, & slippery moss, do make a hazardous
milieu.

As far as the history of DCP,  there is a sign posted
that describes the strange history of this Parks
name & creation.  Greed, accidents, erosion, &
community input all played a part in its history
& likely still does.

Anyway, there

NEVER was any dinosaur fossils found
here (it was a actual named after a fake headless
partially completed dinosaur "statue" that burned
down long ago) and there are

NO safely accessible "caves", except by Kayak...
and those would be shallow, at best.

Regardless of the above, the views & playground
are worth a stop.

I am giving it only four stars, because the name
is misleading to most people, who may stop to either
see Caves or Fossils.  Ironically, the only things
that are related to Dinosaurs are small models
of them & (enormous, not to scale) eggs in the
kids playground.

At least these ones have the heads on & the kids
can play on them.

The city does try to maintain a fair amount of native
plants on the grounds & it is pleasant to walk the paths
to various outlook areas, many with benches.

Again, you & your kids need to be extremely careful
not too stray too near the cliffs edge, as the fall
would mostly lightly result in a fatality.
Be cautious & watch your kids!
BTW- No photo is worth your life!
dislikes: No actual caves or dinosaur fossils
Risk of rogue waves and slippery moss

reviews_attraction.text:
This preserve is great for views & for limited beach combing at low tide.
When it is high tide...forget it....and also do NOT let yourself get stuck when the tide comes in.  You will have to pay for the rescue.
The staircase down to the water is safe, but not the rocks on the bottom. Most are slippery & are unstable.  It is all too easy to slip & break something.  I have seen many a tourist walk with sandals like idiots. It is not worth it.  The small beach that is beyond the corner is no great shakes. Do not drag your kids over the hazardous rocks to get there...it could be grounds for a call to child protection services.  The rocks are that dangerous.  Pic wise, there are fairly good pics of the birds, the rocks, & the surf...depending upon conditions.  While people do Kayak here, it does not mean that the water is safe...it is not.  BTW- there are far safer & nicer beach for the kids nearby...such as Pismo, Avila, Grover, Morro Bay, and so on.  Locals can always tell who the tourists are...the ones who take ridiculous risks.

A pleasant little diversion as you explore the Bayview & Los Osos area.
The term Elfin Forest is really a euphemism for the tiny dwarf Oaks that live here....so load up on Sun Screen.  The walk is easy, but is not ADA friendly off the boardwalk.  You do need to walk over a couple hundred feet of sand on approaches from the side streets.  Parking is limited to 1-2 spots in some areas & can disturb the residents.  Your will find few tourists & lots of dog walking locals here.  The boardwalk is fantastically well made with pseudo-wood, looks great, but is limited in length.  The view of Morro Rock & the surround water is serene & quiet.
It is a good diversion for about 1/2 hour. The does not seem to be any facilities here. You need to go into nearby Baywood for eats...or check out the "next door" bakery that is in someone's house.

Amazing somewhat hidden nature preserve! Well worth a brief stop to chill & gaze upon panorama s that include Morro Rock. Lots of birds & even some Monarch butterflies. Few tourists off season.
No facilities, but a nice short walk & cool views.  There is a stream on-site as well.

It is right near "downtown" Baywood which has a Monday afternoon
Farmer's Market & some eats.  It is also near other beaches/parks [e.g.
Pasadena Park or Elfin Park.]  It is also on the way to the Golf course
which has eats/bathrooms & close to the huge amazing Montaña de Oro State Park which you need to drive to.

Of course it is not far from the center of Los Osos town, which also has some modest eats, gas, pit stops, & markets....and even a discount market [Grocery Outlet].

It is yet another one of the few beaches that you can wade in.....but watch for hypothermia. The water in this area of CA, is super-cold and most will use wetsuits.  Due to prior extensive oil pollution in this beach, I would also research.  They had to replace the top few feet of soil in Avila town due to oil residue.

The views here are nice & it is pleasant to walk barefoot on the shore.  Food & hotels are right here & the 101 is just a few miles away.
Prices are rather high for what you get here.
There are lots of wine tasting places a few blocks away.
People can tend to clog the area when there are reports of Whales to watch.

Cute local park that has a little something for almost all.  The Chumash Artwork is quite interesting, so there is a bit of history here too.  They have a summer pool for locals.  There is a little kids playground right next to a muddy banked brook, which is easy to slip on into the water, so be careful.  They have a picnic table with BBQ area and enough grass to play around.  The park is split by the street, so on one side you have the tennis court, pool, restrooms, artwork, and on the other you have more open space.  Of course most people gravitate to the beach area nearby, rather than here since there is not much of a view.
likes: Facilities & Services: Summer pool, Picnic table, BBQ area
Activities: Playground, Grass for play, Tennis court

reviews_attraction.text: Nice little playground area for kids, but it more of a "pocket park".  It is good for both locals & visitors since I think there are only about two playgrounds in the immediate area.  The interesting part is actually the "extension" of the park toward the ocean front.  There you have no beach access, but quite nice views, among some local coastal plants.  Obviously, not worth a special trip, since the main beach park is only a few more blocks away.  Of course, it is really nice to break up the unrelenting overdevelopment with any kind of greenery.  It is especially nice in the off-season.

This cute tiny little beach park is right between Dinosaur Caves & the Conservancy Beach area.  There is not much here, except great views.  Beach access via stairs (& at low tide) is about a block down, but is not apart of this park.  Some people get married at the little gazebo on the grounds.  This park is one of many small or large beach parks all along this area.  Many are popular with locals & surfers.  While this one is cute, it is more for tourists that also stop at DC Park.  It is good for a Pizza picnic from the nearby Del's Pizza. BTW- watch the UV & steep drop here!

Not much of a Park, despite the name.  It is more of a Bay side walkway that extends from the very end of the buildings on the Bay to the Morro Rock area.  The views are kind of ruined by the electric plant which stand out like a sore thumb.  For most, it is better to drive on and park in the main area around the rock...or choose a much nicer beach area.  While there seems to be tennis court here, it is not very useful since your ball can easily fly into the water.  There are few plants here and mostly dirt and some scrub.  It seems to be a pseudo-park in search of a purpose.

Great for kids, dogs, etc.  It is one of the few beaches that you can wade in.....but watch for hypothermia. The water in this area of CA, is super-cold and most will use wetsuits.  Due to prior extensive oil pollution in this beach, I would also research that as well.  They had to replace the top few feet of soil in town due to this.  So even if it looks nice, it may not be healthy...but what beach is?
Anyway, the views here are nice & it is pleasant to walk barefoot on the shore.  Food & hotels are nearby & the 101 is just a few miles away.

Very pleasant place to stop by [pre-C-19 anyway]. Pleasant people, nice grounds, scenic drives both up the mountain [up Tepusequat road which while beautiful is not for the faint of heart] or down the valley toward many other vineyards & then Solvang, and good wines.  Well worth a stop as part of a scenic drive. Who knew behind Santa Maria there was such an amazing area.  That area has old towns, old oils fields, vineyards, out of the way side roads, but the beaten tourist vine area is best done off season.

Local eval for locals: Cute small park & playground for the kiddies. Lots of safety rubber materials on grounds. Has picnic & BBQ area.  Good stop off on the way to Pozo or Carizzo.  Can get food for picnic right on the main street in town.  A bit close to the railroad so please keep an eye open for stay kids.  There is also a dry or semi-dry creek which could cause a fall. All & all quite pleasant.

Ira Lease Park is the "companion park" of the similar one across the street. The main difference is the presence of a kiddy playground. Either is a nice break from the noise of the downtown area.  Either has some picnic tables for a snack, but just a short walk away is the beach area.  There are good views of the creek and you can spot various birds, and sometimes ducks as well.

This super tiny cliff park overlooks the tidal beach, but only boasts some good views & a few benches.  There is not beach access here.  People houses line the back of the park, so it is uncomfortable here with people watching your back.  You do & feel like you are disturbing them.  Rather strange that they have this awkward park here.

Likely the best Chinatown in the USA.  While not as large as NYC, it is far less hectic & more serene.  It is a pleasure to wander around, take in the sights, shop, & eat Dim Sum!  It sure helps to have someone who speaks Chinese with you.  Do not be afraid to check out all the back alleys & tiny streets..at least during the day.

AKA Dry Creek Park is an Oasis in the center of
dreary Modesto. Great for long walks, biking, &
all kinds of exercise. It runs thru the middle of
Modesto from Claus to downtown.  The entire
walk is alot of fun.  Be especially cautious as
you get toward the downtown end...or when
you are alone, for obvious reasons.

A fairly mediocre Zoo,  but better than nothing.
Animals look rather sad.  Limited fun things
for kids...like swings. Food is the usual fast
food junk.  Older kids & adults will get board.
Younger kids will be a hassle to get to walk around.
Better to head south to the Aquarium.

A fairly mediocre small Zoo. Not worth a trip from the
Major Cities. Limited number of animals. Some kids
will get a kick out of it....likely the 6-12 yoa crowd.
Lacks water & does attract homeless.  The park should have been placed by SLO in old Chinatown proper....instead of on the near forgotten periphery.

Really great for easy hikes by the ocean
for the whole family.  Really beautiful
sunsets. Close to the hotels in Monterey
or Carmel.

Unique, or very close to it.  One of the very rare original drive-in movies
that still exist!  It should be made a historical site.
Niece loved this place. Playground, pond with ducks, swings, etc.  Nice large grassy area to play frisbee & ball. Kid friendly.
Nice calm park. Kids playground is large & safe. Small easy trail in the back. Good for a quick picnic break. Bathrooms too.

One of California's most recognizable private homes, now belonging to the people in the form of a beautifully maintained museum.  William Randolph Hearst built his "La Cuesta Encantada" ("The Enchanted Hill") on the highest spot of his families ranch.  A spot where the sun shines even when there is fog along the coast.  The views are without comparison.

There are many different tours available, I took the Grand Rooms Tour.  About an hour in length, this one takes you through the rooms on the ground floor.  Also included is a tour of the grounds from where the shuttle bus from the Visitor Center drops you off, up 165 stairs to the front door.  Passing by the Neptune Pool (under reconstruction during my visit) and ending with the Roman Pool, both are pools like you've never seen.

Our guide Shawn was amazing, a fount of Hearst knowledge.  His tour guide style is like walking through the property with a friend who know a lot.  Very friendly and casual.  Asking what we might be interested in knowing about.  This is NOT your standard canned tour.  I highly recommend making the trip out here to see it.

A collaboration between the county of Santa Clara and the State of California, this public park is situated on 287 acres.  The property was donated by Mr Walter Cottle and family. The idea here is to represent the farming past of this part of San Jose. There is a working farm, a Master Gardener's plot and Our City Forest.  additionally there is a very nice visitor center, great children's playground and many barbecue areas. Parking is $6 a vehicle or you can bike and ride there for free. Extensive pass around the perimeter of the park and through the recreational areas make for a great place to bike ride. Family friendly and flat although afternoons can be very windy.  It is a farm that has become a new park so there is not a ton of shade trees but there are some shaded areas to picnic.  #SanJose #BlossomHill #Park #FamilyFun

Torrey Pines is one of 14 (out of 279) state parks in California designated as "natural reserves".  Absolutely beautiful and kept as close to natural as possible because of its reserve status.  Miles of beaches, sandstone cliffs carved by the constant wind, water and sand.  Beautiful!  Free parking along the roadside in designated area is extremely limited.  There is paid parking ($20 on weekends) but it can be a bit of a hike.  Drop your beach gear and passengers off at the roadside parking (if full) and then park the car.  Bring everything you need, there are no businesses out there to sell anything you've forgotten.  There is a couple of vending machines on the edge of the paid parking (next to the bathrooms) that are stocked with some basics like water, snacks and sunscreen, if you need them.

Something that I've been wanting to do for a long time, finally done!  The hike up from the Stanford Ave entrance is scenic and supposedly the shorter/more shaded trail up.  There are zero trees anywhere along the trail so the only shade is from the mountain as long as you're on the trail before the sun gets too high in the sky.  Parking is minimal, approximately 25 spaces.  With up to 2,000 hikers each Saturday and Sunday, those spots should not be counted on.  There is limited parking in adjacent neighborhoods just be sure to read all signs.  There are parking police on permanent duty there.  Bring water for yourself AND your dog.  This is a challenging hike.  There is a bathroom near the summit.

Conceived as a place to keep her personal collection of art by Isabella Stewart Gardner, this home has not changed much since she passed. It is still an incredibly beautiful place to visit.

The interior courtyard alone would be enough to make me wish to visit. The art collection is rather unusual with a heavy lean towards religious art which she seemed to enjoy.

Curiously, there are several pieces that are missing from the collection as they were stolen and never recovered. Part of her will stated that none of the art would ever be replaced or hung other than the way she wished it to be. Therefore the missing pieces remain missing and where they were only empty frames exist now.

Wish I could give a better rating but I can't. Was there during their Dia delos Muertos celebration, The Tasting Room was very busy. I paid my $10 for myself and a friend to taste. The pours we were given were about a teaspoon of wine, not nearly enough to form an opinion about whether or not I even liked their wine.  I would say that it was not a standard pour because I have worked in the wine industry and know what that looks like. Also, the patrons standing right next to me were getting normal pours from another employee who was working there.  There are over 18 wineries on my list for downtown Murphy's, it will be a very long time before I give this one a second try.

Coit Tower is a beautiful Art Deco Memorial to the firemen of San Francisco. A gift from the Lillian Coit who was child in the 1906 earthquake. Much of San Francisco burned and she idolized the fireman that saved so much of the city.  Some think that the murals in the lobby were painted by Diego Rivera but they are only represented it up his style. They were actually painted under the auspices of the Public Works of Art Project, one of the New Deal federal employment programs for artist at the time.  Tickets for the elevator ride up to the top cost $8 and are available in the lobby. On a sunny day, the view is well worth the price.

Park has some lovely parts but much of it is a home to San Jose's homeless population.  The children's park is lovely but if look it over before letting my kids run and play on the equipment.  The biking paths wind along the river making the park accessible to many looking for somewhere to pitch a tent.  There winter rains and flooding caused a lot of the garbage that comes with a homeless population to be deposited in the trees along the river.  This park has great potential to be a good place for the people of San Jose.  As it is now, I don't consider it a safe place to recommend you go.

Locally grown wine!  The sparkling wine (Rose) is one of my personal faves.  Warm and inviting tasting room.  Excellent staff, they can tell you everything you might want to know about their wine.  they also make an effort to get out into the community so that their wines can be tasted in areas closer to the population centers. The drive to the winery is a bit on the twisty Mountain roadside. It is beautiful getting there though. Worth the trip!

The beauty of this building in real life does not disappoint.  I've seen pictures of this structure so many times.  Always wanted to go and visit it, walk the Aerial Walkway.  Those walls are like polished steel canyons.  Go at dusk and enjoy the orange colors.  The Blue Ribbon Garden and the Rose fountain in it are especially peaceful.  All of these can be reached on the Aerial Walkway that circles the building.  Open to the public.

Gorgeous place to go hiking or riding mountain bikes. Plenty of choices on trails and level of difficulty. View from the top is unparalleled. On a clear day you can see all the way to Moffett Field! When out there hiking you will want to be careful keeping an eye out for mountain bikers coming down hill. Some of them are a bit fast but the park rangers are also out there using the radar gun to warn those cyclists to slow down.

Highly recommend this Museum on the strength of their special exhibition on the history of hip-hop and rap. Really well done and gives the visitor a chance to participate in the art form. All of the pieces exhibited are fascinating to stop and really look at but my personal favorite was a handwritten poem on lined notebook paper. Written by Tupac Shakur this piece could not be more timely and relevant than it is right now!

Nice little oasis of green set smack dab in the middle of the Hayes Valley neighborhood.  Home to a few art installations.  The permanent ones like the Ghinlon/Transcope by Po Shu Wang OR the temporary like the 10th Anniversary Temple by David Best.  Plenty of nice benches in the shade, a few with tables at the north end. Park is kept clean and nice, a great place to take your kids.

One of the most beautiful places along the Northern California coast.  Hiking trails, nature and history are all within easy reach here.  The volunteer docents (retirees mostly) are amazing.  They live to pass along knowledge to park goers of all ages.  It is a long hike if you start out from the front gates so be sure to dress in layers with comfortable shoes and plenty of water.

Sunny bit of green down by the piers!  This is where you'll find "Cupid's Span" an outdoor sculpture by married artists Claes Oldenburg and Coosje van Bruggen.  The 60-foot (18 m) sculpture, commissioned by GAP founders Donald and Doris F. Fisher, depicts a partial bow and piece of an arrow.  The best views of the Oakland Bay Bridge are found here.

Beautiful tree covered park in the center of Willow Glen West! A popular place for Sunday picnic or taking your children to play on the playground equipment. There are also tennis courts, a bocce ball court and softball / baseball fields on which to play. In the summertime, there often are performances of Shakespearean plays in the park.

One of those hidden little spaces in San Francisco that not too many people know about. Any Star Wars fan would consider this a must swing by stop. On the campus for Industrial Light and Magic in the Presidio. The grounds surrounding are beautiful and worth a stroll after checking out the fountain.

What a treasure trove of technology they have here!!!  So many fascinating bits and pieces of our history.  You'll want to allot a fair amount of time to wander through.  So many wonderful displays detailing the history of the modern computer starting with the ancient beginnings 2000 years ago!

Hidden (in plain sight) treasure!  Located next to the world famous Ghirardelli Square, this one is overlooked by most everyone.  It's mesmerizing to see the displays from San Francisco's long maritime history.  Serves to highlight, even more so, what an incredible and unique city this is.

Beautiful replica of a Spanish style cathedral, this was built for the 1915 Panama-California Exposition.  One of only 3 of the original structures.  Buy the ticket that includes the tour of the tower, an additional $13 for a 40 minutes tour yup to the 8th floor.

Awesome way to spend a sultry summer evening!    Lots of open air dining and drinking along the way.  Take a seat in one of the colorful Adirondack chairs at Bubba's Love Shack or grab a table overlooking the water at any one of the restaurants linking the walk.

The History of California follows the Missions and Carmel is one of the most beautiful of them.  The surrounding gardens are beautiful and well maintained.  The mission itself has quite a history, all on display in this museum.
Impressive soccer fields!  They have lighting to support night games.  Picnic areas next to the parking are clean and well maintained.  Parking is limited in the area so plan for a little extra time.
Absolutely amazing museum.  Went there for a private event but I'm going to need a return visit to see it completely.  Beautiful restored aircraft of every kind in an airy and modern space.
Nice beach for a weekday visit.  Gets super crowded on weekends.  Parking lot always full, surrounding neighborhoods have some street parking but are very narrow.

This is a nice drive along the ocean offering some great views. Lots of nice ocean views, big homes and overall CA coastal beauty.

Suggestions:
* Weekends (esp Summer) can be crowded (goes without saying)

* To get the best part, start at the Pacific Grove gate entrance (instead of the main Hwy 1 entrance) and get off the Carmel exit.

* The Inn at Spanish bay is a nice place for lunch (it's right at the start if you follow this route). But if you are on a budget, pack some food from the town of Pacific Grove (just before you enter) and eat at the picnic tables. Overall the food along the 17-mile drive is great but very pricey.

* The beaches along the drive are nice, but Carmel beach is nicer. So if you want to get into the water (it's cold no matter where you go on this coast), just view the beaches on the drive and once you get to Carmel, go to the beach there. It's much nicer (less sea weed too).

* End the day with some shopping and dinner at Carmel-By-the-Sea. Its a cute little town.

This is a great park - it's huge with miles and miles of paths. Great for biking or even bringing the dog along for a walk.
There are easy stroller friendly paths and steeper paths, lots of water sources and small hikes around the smaller ponds or go upto the bay. Lots of little hills with great views.
The possibilities are endless.

Parking inside has a fee ($5), but if you want to bike or walk a little more (about a mile more), park at road that turns into the park on Paseo Padre - if you come early, there is enough parking. If you park inside, the gate closes at 8 (summers), but if you park outside, you can stay longer. There is not too many places with shade. There are several picnic tables around the area. Good views of the bay from several trails.

Overall a wonder nature lovers park.

Best snorkeling esp with kids. This place is well maintained and has two super shallow areas that are blocked from the sea by rocks - making it safe to go all around without worrying about the tides, and pretty shallow all over. The best part is that the water is literally teeming with fish - all colors, shapes and sizes - best snorkeling! Never saw so many fish, even in an large aquarium - floating right by your feet.
The park has a nice walking path along the beach. There is a lot of driftwood that gets cleaned up regularly. There are benches, plenty of space to camp out and a kids play area closeby.

One of the MUST dos when in Yosemite.
The road to Glacier Point is only open during the warmer season (and gets shut down after snowfall begins).
This place offers spectacular 360 degree views of mountains, the valley below, water falls (including imo the best view of half dome) that can't be beat anywhere in Yosemite.
It does require an hour of driving up to get there (30 miles from the valley), or for the athletically inclined, a good 4 mile (one way hike).
Sunsets are amazing to view here.
It does get crowded on busy weekends - plan accordingly (imo the best time to go to Yosemite are weekdays).

The end point of the drive to Hana (though this is past Hana) but worth it. Most people come here in the evening, but come in the morning to avoid the crowds.
The pools are closed for swimming sometimes but when not raining, it should be ok. It is truly lovely to see though. There is a nice beautiful and short trail that takes you to the pools. The other end of the trail (long trail) goes up the Pipiwai trail to the large waterfall via the bamboo forest.
Definitely a must do on the Hana trip.
The ticket to enter the park ($25) can be re-used to visit Haleakala crater within 3 days.

This is a lovely place - and seems like not very well known because most of the crowd was at the Emerald bay (which had no parking) but this place had plenty of parking and hardly any crowd.
There is camping and other things to do here - but we spent most of the time in the quiet and serene beach with clear (but cold) water far from the boats. There are picnic benches on this small 'beach' which is a short hike down the road from parking. Entrance cost $10.

This is as Spectacular as Cirque de Soleil gets. The multi million dollar gigantic set itself is breathtaking and Cirque puts on a visual delight - combining a multitude of acts and acrobatics. Don't pay too much attention to the story line - just let you senses feast.
There are some parts that are a little slow, but the performers are talented and some parts of the show just wow you. An overall wow experience and must do for Vegas

Great place to connect with nature and farm life. Park close to the 280 bridge, and walk in to a system of small stroller friendly hikes leading to a farm with goats, chicken and other animals - that kids would love. There is a small picnic area too (restrooms are smelly).
If you want a more strenuous hike, there are trails that lead all the way up the mountain (or around it) and provides some good views from the top.

Beautiful well maintained arboretum with plenty of trails offering flora of all kinds from all over the world. There's peacocks and ducks mostly for kids, a nice bamboo grove with bamboos from all around the world, beautiful trees, flowers, and overlooks, some very nice views of water falls and the valley. A great place to stop and spend some time on the road to Hana (MM10.6). Costs about $15 but worth it.

An easy but beautiful trail. Easy enough for bikes and kids, wide enough for social distancing, decent amount of parking at the trail head.
The views are spectacular - views of the bay, Lake Elizabeth, 360 views of the mountains. There are plenty of cows around on the trail (and some manure too).
There is hardly if any shade so be sure to bring some sun protection and hydration. Overall a beautiful trail.

This is a nice large park with a pretty big lake in the middle. Lot of play areas for kids, base ball court, tennis courts but what i use the most is the nice walking path around the lake.
There's even a water park that opens in summers.
Several entrances from Stevenson and Paseo Padre. Now that the BART construction in this area is over (or most of the debris is gone), this park is more accessible.

This is a must do in Palm Springs area. The tram goes straight up and offers some spectacular views going up (or down). You go from desert to pines in a short time.
On the top there are restaurants, visitor center and some nice short hikes with good views from the top of the mountains. Get a jacket because it does get much colder than the desert below.

Fun and beautiful place for kids and adults alike. Lots of things to do - walk around. Lots and lots of greenery, water and tropical vegetation all around with some spectacular views.
The restaurant on site (Mill House) is amazing.
There is a zip line on site too which we didn't get to try. You could spend some good family time here.

Cute little aquarium right at the touristy Pier 39. It's not as large as the one at Monterey Bay but has plenty of nice exhibits, especially the underwater tunnels (which was packed with Sharks, Rays and all kinds of fish). Kids will have a great time here - esp with petting the Sting Rays, Little Turtle. Otter  and other exhibits.

Very nice, neat museum! I was here for a corporate catered dinner - so didn't focus on visiting the entire museum. But there were a lot of planes from different eras, flight simulator, hands-on exhibits.
It also provided an interesting backdrop for the dinner. Will return with family to explore this place.

Lovely little beach area with great views of the Hudson. The parked up the hill - where is large green picnic area.
A short wooded hike down gets you to the view and beach area. Great views, lots of shaded hiking trails (and biking trails). Great place for a family hangout and connect with nature.

Lovely beach and pier area. Close to Hanalei town, plenty of parking. The beach is nice and has a mix of warm and cool water. Great for kids surfing. Had a blast here - there are a few picnic tables and an area to clean yourself. Head on to Hanalei town for a nice meal after

Right off the 89 is this short but must see spot for great views of Emerald bay and Tahoe.
Parking can be tight on crowded days, but wait a bit and you will find parking (people don't spend too much time here). But the vistas are gorgeious

Short road up from the 101 past the Golden gate and you get to this point with lovely views of the golden gate bridge. Drive a little further up for a network of trails and views of the bay and the golden gate.
This is a nice not hard to do trail along the road to Hana. There is a short and long loop. Lots of greenery and views (not waterfalls). Can get a little muddy and slushy when raining.
Nice old banyan tree with lots of seating under. Surrounded by lots of shops and eateries. Free parking can be tough to get, there are lots of smaller paid parking lots
Nice and main lookout point for the Waimea Canyon from the road. Well maintained with restrooms. $10 fee gives you parking in all the lookout points upto Koke'e park
A worthy slight diversion on the road to Hana. Sights of waves crashing along the lava rocks, get some food at Aunty Sandys (dont miss the banana bread there)
This is a must do for thrill seekers in Vegas. Your are shot up with G force at 1000 feet from the ground and freefall 60 feet. The views are amazing
Nice falls past Hana (MM45) on way to Oheo Gulch. We did it early in the morning and there was no one there. Nature at its best.

This is great park from all points of view!
There are good views all around (Lower Manhattan and Jersey City), huge grass field to play, one of the best playgrounds I've ever seen, and all is close to WTC ferry terminal.
The playground is really awesome, it has few sandboxes, few water places, and a lot of usual playground activities.
In the summer rush hours it is a bit crowded but you can always find free space to play.
On the weekends there are also special tools and games shared by recreational staff and even some children books.
Great place for family rest.

Great museum located on the piers line of San Francisco. It has lots of activities for kids and big enough size to fit all the people going into.
There are number of experiments with liquids, electricity, light, and all of them have quite clear description nearby. It say what's happening and why in short and easy to understand posts.
There is a parking lot right across the street. When you pay for it, mention that you are going to go into the Exploratorium, and you will get more than 50% off the cost.

Excellent place to spend the whole weekend with kids!
It has everything you will need for this: Lego sculptures, huge playground, lots of different Lego blocks to build here and there, 4D cinema, even carousel.
And all this at the same place.
As far as this is placed in shopping center, there are few food places so you will not be left hungry.
The parking is really cheap: I paid $3 for more than 6 hours.
The music is too loud. A felt like I've been to rock concert after 6 hours inside.

Wonderful scenic view point with great Golden Gate bridge and bay and ocean views!
And it is not only about the bridge: there are old buildings if a battery Spencer that had been used to protest the entrance into the bay.
You still can see the the buildings with chimneys, places to store the weaponry, and the places where artillery had been placed.
Also there is a wide trail going down close to the water that is nice to walk, run, and bike.
Great place to spend morning or afternoon.

Great playground with lots of unusual and non-standard equipment. Some of these rides I did not see anywhere else.
There is a windmill, and couple of sculptures with wheels to swing their wings.
The parking is a bit small for busy times so be prepared to look for additional space.
The sculptures are very nice and realistic.
In summer time there are few water attractions to keep kids cool.
It is so close to SJC airport that airplanes are flying right above your head!

It's an incredible place to have family fun!
Lamas are running near your open window, elks and yaks are standing in the center of the road to stop you to get bread, buffalos are trying to get inside filling all space inside the car.
Do not forget to take a look at requirements for bread on the website, not everything is appropriate.
Bears are sitting and waving you back, they also can catch bread in the midair.

Great science museum with awful lack of parking.
There are life discovery, space, water sections and other. IMAX shows are awesome. Take few minutes to visit gift shop, there is some good stuff in it.
The place is donation-based so be prepared to estimate how much you can leave (they do have recommendations though).
The parking is paid and awful, we spent at least 30 minutes to find althe spot.

Wonderful park with variety of hiking routes and great views.
On some routes you can even see the ocean that is beautifully combined with green mountains.
There are multiple starting points with parking so you can always find the spot. And on parking lots you can find park maps.
Restrooms are located in few places along the routes.

This park is one of our favorite.
Zoo, train, carousel, three big playgrounds for different ages, water splash point in the summer and skate ring in the winter, grill, parties, and the park itself.
You can find what to do here for all ages.

Definitely if you do not have plans for weekend this is the place to go anytime.

Me and my son love this place, it has two good playgrounds nearby and wonderful pond.
Also the is a great long path running through all the park alongside the Saddle River.
You can walk or ride to the old water mill to checkout how people used to work earlier.

This is a very good place for family evening.

This is an incredible playground though looks simple at the first glance. It is surrounded by rocks from one side and has direct bridge to them.
In the hot days they turn on the water that is running all over the playground and there is also a sand nearby. So kids have everything they love.

It is a good park for kids to play and run around. The playground is big and has few parts for kids of different ages.
There is a plenty is sand to play with too.
The grass field is big and there are walking paths too.
Parking onsite an on the streets nearby is enough.

Great huge playground in the Mitchell park that will keep kids busy for few hours in a row.
There are all sorts of tools and things one can imagine for playground.
It is well built and well maintained, always clean and has space for parents to watch their kids playing.

Great huge park with big field, lots of paths, few good playgrounds, and tennis courts. This is nice place to have a kid's birthday party.
The playgrounds are fit for kids of all ages, and the field is big enough to have people playing different games at once.

Great place to spend the weekend with family! It has all you need: picnic areas (big ones for huge companies), fields for all sports, water park and sand shore of the lake.
For bad weather there are tented tables.
The parking is very tight though.

It's rather a large park with few things to visit: couple museums, golf course, Japanese friendship garden, Happy Hollow Park & Zoo.
The territory is well maintained and clean.
Parking is paid which is ok since it is big enough.

Wonderful place with small zoo, great playground and few attractions.
There is puppet show my son loved and the playground is really big.
You can ride a roller coaster and have some lunch in little cafe that is quite good.

The huge wonderful park with great lake and beach. The lake is not deep near the beach so you could count it will be warm even in the morning. In fact at our visit it was even warmer than the air outside.
Wonderful place to spend time with kids. My sons loved the place from the first visit. There are a lot of activities to do: big playgrounds for any age, nice small lake and huge fields to walk.

This monument remind us that for war there are no right or wrong sides. It kill anybody.
Monument has full description of the tragedy happened on it.
Worth seeing if you are nearby.

Wonderful park for spending time with kids or alone.
There is big playground and sand to play on.
And the walking area is big enough.
The park is always clean and nice to be in.

It is a good place to walk and have lunch.
In the morning and evening the lights on the trees makes it glow beautifully.
It has granite benches and few tables.

Great place with wonderful views on Manhattan and the statue of liberty.
It has grills and great playground.
The parking is big enough.

On the Friday midday the park was completely deserted except for at least 5 homeless people.
The parking lot is a one huge pothole.
Great park in the lower Manhattan where you can walk and have some rest. There is a big refreshing fountain on the middle.

It's been awhile since I last visited the San Francisco Zoo yet there were several exhibits closed to the public the same situation the last time I came. Unlike the zoo of my childhood now most of the animals are free range in their natural habitat with the exception of monkeys and some birds there are no cages. The Zoo is divided in several sections based on their geographic origins. There can be a section of African animals seen in a Savanna trail or another section with a Amazon Rain Forest theme. They done a good job transforming this zoo into a place that is above average as far as zoos go. The bears were out today on a warm September day and the Aviary is opened as well.

The new transportation center is impressive so spacious and bright that it warrants a visit by itself. The park on the top levels could be accessed by escalators, elevators, or a tram and I found all three efficient and scenic ways to reach the park above which was in a word fantastic. There were plants and succulents to the perimeter and plenty of benches along the trail which spanned several,  blocks.
