In the middle where there was grass and groups were enjoying their picnics, birthday parties, board games which were provided by the park in a case on a first come basis. There was even a yoga class going on in the amphitheatre. Worth a visit for sure.
likes: Efficient and scenic transportation options (escalators, elevators, tram)
Recreational activities (picnics, birthday parties, board games, yoga)

reviews_attraction.text: We went by the 76 Muni Express that we caught after our matinee nearby. The bus trip itself was very scenic across the Golden Gate Bridge and thru a scenic winding road to the Marine Headlands. It was like going back 200 years into unspoiled wilderness flanked by mountains to one side and seascape avroac the other side. There are trails that wind up the unspoiled wilderness to the casement of the giant gun that once provided protection from would be invaders. Down the trail there are beaches and lagoons stretching out for miles. Fort Cronkite is located near the waters but seems deserted due to the ongoing budget debate.

We went up the Filbert Steps and it took a bit of exertion to traverse the 400 steps to the summit on a cold crisp San Francisco day. But the air was clear and the views magnificent making the trek well worth it. The restored murals looked new as hundreds of people lined up for the elevator ride to the top where we were greeted by a blast of cold wind that made us pull on our hats or hoodies. But the view of our great city made up for all that in spades. Coit Tower is a must see for San Francisco is and tourist alike. A flock of wild parrots flew overhead to salute us.

The place was immense and will take several visits to immerse in detail the many special exhibits. From the huge digital mural called The Chronicles of San Francisco which depicts the daily life of a cross section of over a thousand residents to the wonderful comprehensive exhibition of Andy Warhol which spans several level there is no way see it all in one day. We spent most of the day on Warhol's impressive 40-year career and barely scratched the service. It will be worth every penny to consider an annual membership. Highest recommendation.

It was truly a panoramic drive up to Vista house and you are rewarded at the summit with breathtaking views worthy of postcards. The Vista house itself is impressive sitting on top like a crown jewel. If you go to Portland this is a must see destination. Bring a jacket in October because it gets quite windy atop here. There is a nice store inside the Vista House and there is a museum on another level of the natural history museum on another level. It is worth a visit. In fact visit the Vista House with your family the kids will be happy here.

This place is still a fun place to go to a ball game even as it is about to enter it's third decade in a few years. The fans have abandoned the team which is now reeling but the true fans that come out enjoy themselves and cheer or jeer at every opportunity. There are continuous improvements every year to make coming out meaningful. The new scoreboard with all it's bells and whistles is a prime example. On this night on July 6 the Giants had a pinch grand slam by Slater to beat St. Louis 8-4. Still a fun place when team wins.

A smaller Catholic Church but very beautiful and serene with a very welcoming staff that beckoned
me to come in brother although I was hardly dressed for church and hadn't shaved this morning. Nevertheless I came inside and was impressed by the rich woods and impressive glass. Other worshippers smiled at me a total stranger and I felt their compassion as I settled into a pew to say a prayer for a friend who passed recently and felt much better when I went back to the the cold cloudy street.

We had to see this waterfall one of the highest in the United States. Unfortunately due to the wildfires we were confined to the lower levels of  nevertheless it was a great experience. The waterfall is a vestige of the last ice age when the ice melted this small section was blocked producing Multnomah Falls. Multnomah Falls never goes dry giving visitors all year to enjoy its splendor. This is because it is fed by streams from the nearby mountains a local told me. Come and be awe.

We rode up the mountain in the wee hours but hundreds of people were already lined up against the railing to watch the upcoming sunrise which was an experience of a lifetime. A masterpiece by nature in glowing reds and oranges against the dawn. Hundreds of people huddled in the chill on an absolutely clear windless day was a miracle in itself with views of other Hawaiian island visible on a clear morning. It was magnificent.

Watch the boats come in loaded with Dungeness that will soon turned into cocktails at one of the outdoor stations and served in paper cups with cocktail sauce. There is an arcade of classic games that still draw many families introducing the classics to the next generation to love as they did and still do. There are a historical ship popular with kids and adults to explore and much more around this place to discover.

An oasis in the busy downtown area where one can wander along the paths and enjoy the plants and people taking a break from the rat race and breathe in some fresh air and feel the refreshing wind on their face. Very invigorating. The Martin Luther falls is a good place to reflect on the struggles of Dr. King and panels detailed out important events in the life of this great civil rights pioneer.

Very nice selection of magazines and pamphlets on travel and trips throughout San Francisco and California. The staff member was very cordial and answer even the stupidest of question. A great resource for travelers and natives alike to unlock new places to experience beyond their usual hangouts. The place is big enough to explore with a great view of the yachts berth outside.

It was a challenging trail to the North Peak but the views along the way were breathtaking and well worth the task. The air was cold and crisp and the views were clear after the recent rains over the weekend. The waters were as blue as a picture and relaxing to see and soak in. Better wear layers as it get rather chilly at the top. Good shoes are helpful too.

A place to meet friends for an Al fresco lunch to get away from the hustle and bustle inside the busy malls. Often the site of celebrations such as The Cherry Blossoms Festival where there are stages set up throughout this plaza. During those events it can get pretty crowded but all in good fun.

Beautiful beach with bright blue green waters filled with scores of surfers, swimmers, snorkelers, and just people soaking up the sun. On this day there was at least a dozen turtles resting in the sand to our delight.

I brought my kids here and they had a blast with all the animals. They even had a tarantula crawl up their arm cringe worthy but exciting. Best of all it is free and the views outside are breathtaking.
Though compact this place is full on stories of the history of railway transportation in San Francisco. The exhibits, pictures, and miniatures were very detailed and had me absorbed for quite awhile.
A great place to discover the sailing vessels that were an important part of the early economic development of San Francisco. So much to learn for adults and so much to enjoy for children.
Fun for kids with rooms for arts and crafts with plenty of ice cream to sample but at $40 not cheap. That said the sprinkles pool at the end was amazing making it all seem worth it.
Chinese history told with artifacts and a very congenital guide who answered all my questions enthusiastically. Two short movies made by Thomas Edison were especially informative.
A historic brick church stand out among all the modern buildings that flank it on all sides. A good place for prayers and reflection in a busy section of the city.
A contrast to the busy malls to either side this concrete five tier structure gives one a pause from the busy shoppers inside and to take a breath of fresh air.
Really not much on this end but a good place to walk, jog, or bike but watch out for faster moving people on the trails.
A nice park with great views of the city. Eat your lunch here before ascending to the top of Coit tower.

One of the best hidden gems in Far North Dallas. I absolutely love the jogging trail that leads to a massive trail system running along the cliffs of White Rock Creek. Most people have no idea its even there.

There's a playground, plenty of open green space, park benches and good landscaping and maintenance. Clientele is mainly working and middle class families and children, with a few young adults doing morning and evening exercise on the trail.

The extensive trail system is perfect for biking, jogging, exploring and hiking. Plenty of shade throughout the trail system, but be cautious in the evening as it can be easy to find yourself lost once the sun starts going down. No restroom facilities or water fountains so be prepared.

The neighborhood is fairly safe and secure, no beggars or shady individuals hanging around the park area. Most of the visitors are locals living in the apartments or gated single family homes next door. Highly recommended.

This was my childhood neighborhood park for twenty years, and I love it. Huge open green space, a nice jogging trail, a small playground and picnic benches throughout. Great for dog lovers and a softball field for the kids and adults to get a game in. Occasionally frequented by beggars, trash diggers, shady characters and a few drug addicts. Relatively safe, but as the years go on, its getting worse, which is in tune with the rest of the rising crime and low class people in the East Contra Costa area. Be cautious, and definitely leave before sun gets low. Wildlife, weirdos and addicts come out at night.

Terrific place for family and couples fun, right on the water with amazing views and great atmosphere. Prices are expensive, but it is an amusement park, so it is somewhat expected. Plan ahead for that. Surrounding area is full of great bars and restaurants, galleries and shops. There is plenty of food and snacks on the Boardwalk, and it gets crowded during the summer, especially on weekends. Dress comfortably and casual, and prepare to have a great time. Highly recommended.

This place has a tranquil setting and beauty that cannot be ignored. Dallas residents have the Arboretum, and Fort Worth folks have the Botanic Garden. Such a wonderful, lush park with trails, superb landscaping and friendly staff. Always clean and maintained well. A perfect place for weddings, romantic day trips, trail walking and relaxation. Plenty of shaded areas and hidden gems to find here so feel free to explore. Highly recommended.

I absolutely love this place. The beach, the views, the park green and the pier itself are breathtaking. There's nothing like watching the sunset here. Easy access by cable car, bus or street car with a short walk. Parking is a nightmare and extremely expensive, so don't bother. Popular with locals, tourists, families and couples alike. Great place to people watch, read a book, work on your tan or just enjoy the views. Highly recommended.

This is a beautiful, well planned and modern dog park with plenty of parking and great open green space and a pond for your furry friends to enjoy. Safe and peaceful, with lots of young professionals, middle class families, singles looking to mingle and empty nesters mixing it up together for conversations while admiring their pets. Jogging trail of half mile track wraps around the park. Highly recommended.

A must see while you visit San Francisco. The views, the history, and walking along the ruins with deep dark waters on narrow walkways and crumbing stones. The dangers are also the magic of this place. Very popular with tourists on the weekends, especially during sunny weather, so plan accordingly. Breathtaking beauty here. Don't miss the gift shop and cafe at Land's End. Highly recommended.

Great shaded green space and playground in the wonderful Northwood Hills neighborhood. Connects to White Rock Trail for walking and jogging along the creek. Parking is somewhat limited. Great place for picnics and gatherings. Safe and peaceful, Dallas PD regularly patrols and keeps less desirables out. Needs restrooms (instead of portables) and water fountains. Otherwise, its quite perfect.

Absolutely breathtaking views and vistas here. Wear very comfortable shoes and clothing, and bring plenty of fluids as you will get a good amount of exercise walking the trails in the area. Magnificent views of the Bay, Golden Gate Bridge and Pacific Ocean. Over 100 years of history for military historians and fans as well. Highly recommended and well worth the drive.

Amazing views overlooking Hollywood, Downtown L.A. and the entire Westside and to the ocean on clear days. Limited parking, gets extremely crowded on weekends with tourists and some locals. Definitely a must see on your Los Angeles vacation. Surrounded by jaw dropping mansions and hillside view homes, lush vegetation and the aura of Hollywood. Highly recommended.

A very nice, shaded and calm green space and lake that's been ruined by the overcrowding and apartment dwellers that litter and loiter everywhere. Lake water is dirty, park is poorly maintained, dog poop everywhere and there's always beggars, thugs, shady characters and low class people or crazy bad and loud kids running everywhere. Not really recommended.

Absolutely breathtaking views and vistas here. Wear very comfortable shoes and clothing, and bring plenty of fluids as you will get a ton of exercise walking down and even more so on the way back up. Magnificent views of the Bay, Pacific Ocean and Golden Gate Bridge. Highly recommended and well worth the drive.

Very serene and nice, but not once in almost ten years have I ever seen the swan paddle boats working, or even an attendant or staff in the area. Otherwise this would get five stars. I've made special trips during the hours they have posted, but never once were they ever open or in operation. Very frustrating.

Large and well designed urban park with plenty of shaded trails, open green spaces, playgrounds and pavilions to explore. You can walk across the San Antonio River via a submerged road and lockout system here, which is an experience well wroth doing. Clean and well maintained. Highly recommended.

Monterey's version of San Francisco's Fisherman's Wharf. Excellent seafood restaurants and wine tastings here. Prices are touristy so be prepared for that, but the cuisine is top notch and always fresh. Plenty of gift shops and stores to drop in and browse as well.

A very nice smaller neighborhood park in an older area with mature trees and blue collar working class families and households. Tennis courts and playground is popular, could definitely use some updates but all in all is a decent park to bring pets and kids to.

A wonderful gem in the heart of Walnut Creek. Lush greenery, shade and plenty or park benches and a gazebo to relax yourself. Hugely popular with dog walkers, families with children, walkers, joggers, and a great place for a picnic. Highly recommended.

Beautiful art from all over Asia, friendly and knowledgeable staff, and impeccably maintained galleries. Calm, relaxing atmosphere and lovely garden for catching a breath of fresh air and conversation on the upper level. Highly recommended.

Wonderful views and an amazing view of the skyline. Bring water and snacks, and enjoy on cooler days, especially mornings. Not much shade, so prepare for that. Easy access to Trinity River and Trail. Highly recommended.
likes: Easy access to river and trail

reviews_attraction.text: A very romantic. beautiful walkway overlooking the lake and downtown Austin skyline. Popular with walkers, joggers and photographers, as well as couples and college students looking to relax. Highly recommended.

Very small but nice aquatic experience for small children. Stingray petting tank was great, as well as the many exhibits of fish and reptiles. Was clean and even when busy the staff was nice and courteous.
Wonderful place full of Texas history and impeccably maintained. I could spend hours and hours in here learning and educating myself and standing in awe at some of the exhibits. Highly recommended.
Spectacular views, challenging steps and trails to climb, and nice green space up top to relax and take in the sights. Dress comfortably, maybe bring a bottle of water as well. Highly recommended.
Great place for people watching, sitting by the ocean relaxing and catching some sun. Popular with walkers, joggers and people just wanting to chill and take it the views. Highly recommended.
Very cool place and essential stop for military historians and veterans. A small duty station but with a lot of very cool facts and stories to learn about.

One of the best tasting rooms we visited on a recent trip to Napa, specifically in the Silverado Trail area. The setting of the place itself is beautiful - green, forest-esqe atmosphere, heavy wood, dim lighting, even a fireplace. The staff was very friendly, very patient, and incredibly professional. They specialize in cab sauvignon, and have quite a history behind them (check out the movie "Bottle Shock"). Two flights to choose from, for $15. Again, far and away the best service of any vineyard in that area.

This museum/gallery generally has a good variety of exhibitions, as well as interactive sections which can really get visitors involved. The sculpture garden left much to be desired, but hopefully with the upcoming renovations, SFMOMA can take it to the next level. One of the coolest spots here is the gift shop. So many cool art/SF books and nick-nacks!

We came just a couple weeks too early for the lavender bloom (happens at the beginning of May, I learned) but this secluded winery was still beautiful. The tasting fee is $10, and for that you'll get a minimum of 6 pours (more if you're nice) and plenty of education on their wines. We ended up taking home a bottle of their excellent Sauvignon Blanc.

I was surprised by the amount people here (lots), as it's a bit out of the way. There a plenty of recreational opportunities here (fishing, kayaking, paddle boarding, boating, etc). At the main end of the reservoir, there are picnic spaces on both sides. The crowd was a little rowdy, but still was a fun place to be during the summer heat.

An understated icon of San Francisco. Perched on a rocky hill in the middle of the city's core, this art deco styled tower has impressive views from both it's base and it's viewing platform. Well worth the hike up the hill. Parking anywhere nearby is not going to happen, so take that into account.

Decently-sized, kid-friendly park, with baseball fields, basketball court, modern playground, picnic tables and barbecues (which do get snagged early on weekends - apparently they can be reserved for a fee). Biggest negative is the restrooms at the park... gross.

Cool little wine tasting room, with the owner and his son running most of the tastings here. Very friendly, very knowledgeable. Glad we stopped by. Also, on a side note, the coffee they sell (from their family farm in Kona) is very good, despite the high price.

Really surprised how busy this place was. There were definitely a mix of locals and tourists, leaning more towards locals. Had live music, DJ, several bars, and plenty of tables to play. I'd say, overall, this is the best option for nightlife in North Tahoe.

Even during a poor snow season, we enjoyed Mt Rose. Its slightly cheaper than other Tahoe resorts, is usually less crowded, and has some pretty good terrain. Hopefully the snow comes back in force after the drought.

The tourist heart of San Francisco, Union Square often has events and festive decorations abound. Art galleries in the summer, and lights and ice skating in the winter. Worth a walk-by, if nothing else.

If you're looking to go out of your way to see this attraction, don't bother. The houses aren't overly impressive, and there are better views to be found in the city. Certainly worse photo ops, though.
A beautifully landscaped urban park, with good stores/dining on-site. Lots of good entertainment options too (for all ages). Looking forward to attending events there during the nice Summer weather!
Can be pricey to get in, and for the drinks themselves, but the all-ice experience is unique, and the crowd is fun (you might even catch a celebrity hiding away here, if you have good timing).
Stunning scenery! Had just the right amount of solitude without being in the middle of nowhere. Be careful, some of the dirt paths can get pretty sloppy here within a few days of it raining.
Great little city park in downtown Mountain View, surrounded by the library and city hall. Lots of tree-covered benches and a walking path, if you're looking for somewhere to relax.
Nerds! But hey, its all good. The late night Thursday events are a great idea, and pretty fun to go to. The exhibits here are also very interactive, and in good variety.
Great, medium-size neighborhood park, with plenty of open grass, barbeques, tennis courts, and more. Come early if you want to grab a shade-covered BBQ grill.
One of Reno's "local casinos" where you'd rarely stumble on a visitor here. Everyone seems to know each other. The drinks at the bar were cheap and stiff.
Excellent "island" park in the middle of the Truckee River. The stage and grass area provides for a great venue for community events. Can get crowded.
Small in size, but with plenty of stunning panoramas. Mount Rainier, the space needle, the bay, and Olympic National Park in the far distance.
A grand, clay-colored capitol building, with a very prominent and tall central dome. The grounds of the capitol are very nice to walk through.
Beautiful ballpark! Looks like what a classic baseball stadium should look like. Great sports venue to have right in downtown San Francisco.
Minus the heavy carpeting of goose droppings, Idlewild is a very nice park. Good place to have a large BBQ/Event.
Not quite as impressive of a view as we were hoping for... don't go out of your way on a hike.
The name is appropriate - it is a grand view. It's a little bit of a hike, but well worth it.

A great little state park that is far enough away from Boulder to feel removed but still a short drive. We did the Eldorado Canyon trail and were not disappointed. The views were great and the trail itself wasn't too crowded, compared to Royal Arch and other trails around Boulder. Parking is pretty limited which is a good and bad thing, helps keep the crowds down. All the picnic areas where take when we got back from the hike but we just snagged some rocks by the creek for lunch. Overall, definitely worth a trip up there, we will go back.

The Oakland zoo always leaves me feeling mixed. Their elephant exhibit is great and there is tons of small play areas for my toddler. Problem I have though is there is always trash everywhere, even when we are first ones through the door. Also, some of the animal pens seem too small, specifically thinking about the giraffes and elands. It is easier to get to and park than the SF zoo which is a big plus and tends to be less crowded.

Great venue for catching free local shows. I took my daughter to go watch the local ballet perform and she loved it. Keep an eye out for upcoming shows. One downside, like most Boulder parks, is the large semi-perminate homeless population. Usually the groups there are fine but a couple times they have been more crass and rambunctious, mainly loudly yelling profanities I don't want my 3 year old picking up.

Beautiful gardens. We spent about an hour just roaming around with my family. Great spot to bring kids, with koy fish, turtles, and a healthy bug population. I lost count of the number of water falls around which gives the space a very serene and quiet feeling. Lots of small hills and dense plants often left us feeling like we were the only people there, even though the parking lot was full.

Wow, this place blew me away. They have done an amazing job with this museum, I only wish I had more time to spend in it. This museum is definitely designed for adults, though teens and older children will have fun. The detail and storylines they have throughout really engage you. Favorite part though was the miniature Disneyland model that they built before the park.

This is what happens when for profit casino companies own an aquarium instead of a non-profit looking to improve public understanding of aquatic environments. There is shameless advertising, nickel and diming, and inadequate pens for the large cats. I didn't give it 1 star because the shark exhibit is impressive, though that was about it.

Go for the Africa, lemur, and grizzly bear exhibits. These three are amazing. The rest of the zoo is good and it's well laid out. Ample places for kids to play and have fun. Their playground is really impressive, we always had to end their with my daughter. Downside is parking, it is awful there and expensive, even if you are a member.

Fun place to take kids though might leave anyone looking for a challenge wanting. The trails are all flat and short but there is a decent amount of wildlife. We were only able to see bison from the visitor center's telescope which was a little disappointing. My 3 year old loved the hands on exhibits at the visitor center.

Great event venue with a view. I went to a multi-day event here and it was a fantastic experience. The views look out to the Bay bridge and Treasure Island. The A/V was very well done and the staff working the venue we're professional and courteous. Only downside is that it was very cold.

We loved this short hike and cave exploration! It's a bit of an odd drive and I imagine Google isn't leading to the main parking area but still fun. The caves themselves were really cool, filled with bats and breaks so light can come in. I would still recommend bringing flashlights.

Great public beach with fire pits and volleyball courts. Fire pits are first come and the volleyball courts you need your own nets. In the summer there are kayak and paddle board rentals. It can get busy on warm days and parking is limited. Great views and the water is pretty calm.

A fun trail that you can catch from North Boulder or downtown. For the non-local it has pretty decent elevation gain so fair warning. It's a beautiful hike with great views both out towards Boulder/Denver and the Rockies. Not a ton of shade and it can get busy on nice weekends.

Walden ponds is an easy, scenic hike close to Boulder and Louisville. My daughter loved the raised walk way through the marsh and reeds. I knock it a star because the maps were not very clear leading us to get on the wrong trail. Not a big deal since it is short hikes though.

Great ball park, just make sure to bring a jacket! It doesn't matter if it was 80 out today...bring the jacket. I highly recommend getting the garlic fries, they are delicious. There are no bad seats in the house so buy what is available and have fun. Go Giants!

It's a great, pay what you want, museum to take your kids to. Their selection of dinosaur skeletons is impressive for the small size of the museum. They also have a rotation exhibit that tend to be interactive.  Definitely worth a visit.

Nice small park near downtown Boulder. Good play structure for younger children and a lot of shade. Like most Boulder parks there is always a large number of homeless there. Right next to Arapahoe so it can be a bit noisy.
Good views and a fun little hike for my 3 year old. Good facilities and looks like they have some good programs as well though we haven't made it to one yet. Downside is that is gets busy up there.
Little nine hole course right on the lake. It could use some love though. Course only has a few holes that are interesting. It is a cheap, mostly fun, round though that you can walk on in Tahoe.
This place is spectacular but it gets crowded. Definitely head up to the Alpine visitors center and do the short hike up. It gets you to just over 12,000 ft (3657m) with amazing views.
Easy, beautiful but crowded hike. For us though, it was worth it. The scenery is pretty spectacular and our little girl loves to watch rock climber so this was a big hit with her.
Great art museum for families. Every exhibit has its own interactive area for kids to play and explore. First Saturday of every month is free too! Definitely worth checking out.
Great little museum that is very hands on. The staff is amazing, very knowledgeable about local wildlife and history. They have a scavenger hunt and fossil dig for the kids.
A cool old WWII fort that you can actually go inside. The area we were in was pretty small though and busy. Still worth a visit just knocking a star.
We love this park. Tons of trails to explore, the beach, and a nice playground. A popular place for running and dogs as well.
Beautiful views and easy hike down to middle and lower falls. I just did it with my three year old.

5 stars for the normal Roaring Camp Railroad that I've loved over the years. It is a spectacular railway with routes to the Boardwalk and, my favorite, the narrow gauge steam train trip up Bear Mountain. The routes are beautiful and the steam trains are the real deal. Then my entire lifetime of memories of this place came crashing down with our most recent trip….

The Thomas the Train event was one of the worst nightmares of my entire life. It was a complete cluster-f beyond description. Hoards of people overcrowding the place and traffic jamming the tiny road in for over an hour, all in honor of a phony Thomas car that is pulled along by a real locomotive on the other end of the train. We missed our train after the excruciating traffic jam and were forced on to a train three hours later. Much of our three hour wait was spent in line for a snow cone in a desperate attempt to quell the relentless, sweltering heat, followed by a visit to the packed store selling all the same Thomas crap you can buy on Amazon from the comfort of home sweet home (which sounded so good once we were in the midst of this train wreck). And then, after missing the opportunity for the Thomas photo due to the impossibly-long line, we rushed to cram aboard our assigned car. When the train finally started rolling, they queue up the ear bleeding-loud Thomas soundtrack that repeats over and over. Most of the kids looked miserable by this point. After the brief out-and-back journey, we missed the photo opportunity again afterward due to the understandably contemptuous Thomas crew kicking everyone out. And believe me, everyone wanted to get out of this miserable abyss by the end of the day.

My recommendation: enjoy a "normal" day at Roaring Camp and avoid the Thomas weekend like the plague--words cannot describe how hellish an ordeal it was.

I practically grew up in the Exploratorium. I didn’t realize it when I was 7 years old, but I was already grasping the fundamentals of physics, biology, geology, thermodynamics, and botany. I could solve binary arithmetic problems and explain to my friends why a bicycle stands up. Things like computer programming and physics were a breeze later on in high school.

Although it’s no longer donation-only, today’s Exploratorium is better than ever. I’ve had a family membership for years and bring the family in often. This is one of the best places around to bring kids--they will have fun and can’t help but learn along the way. When the new location first opened, I missed the old dark, dank, cavernous feel of the original location, but the location, capacity, and overall atmosphere of the new location seems natural now. The food and waterfront view aren’t bad either.

I’ve been to hands-on science museums around the world that have followed the Exploratorium’s model, but the Exploratorium is the original and still the best.

Once a staple destination for my elementary school fieldtrips and YMCA summer camp outings, the old Chabot had its charm, but it was always the same routine: you unload out of the school bus, the guy in the lab coat bangs the little rocket on the cable with his hammer, then they file you into the tiny planetarium.

This is not your father's Chabot anymore. The new place is a state-of-the-art facility with much more to do. The exhibits are always interesting and the kids love it.

But the best experience at Chabot is on those clear Friday nights when all the amateur astronomers are set up and the big scopes are locked and loaded. There's no better place in the Bay Area to go stargazing with plenty of experts to explain exactly what you're looking at!

This is now called the LeRoy King Carousel. We went to the grand reopening ceremony and that LeRoy is quite a guy!

How cool it is to have an original 1906 Looff carousel right in the heart of San Francisco. Not just any Looff carousel but the original carousel that spun at Playland At The Beach for 58 years.

It was recently completely restored and is absolutely beautiful down to every detail, from the shiny lacquered hardwood floors to the polished gears and rods that run so smoothly once again. The only thing missing is the old band organ.

You might walk right by it, but don't mix this historical machine up with a cheap Pier 39 merry go round because this is the genuine thing. And it's worth a ride by both the little kids and the big kids.

Sure it's no tropical Hawaiian beach, but it's our beach and I love it. The water's cold but refreshing on a hot, sunny day. Ocean Beach is also great for dog swimming and kite flying. A walk over to the Beach Chalet or up to the Cliff House for a beer (or two) and bite to eat is always in order after a day trip to the beach.

But the beach comes alive as the sun dips into the Pacific and the pastel houses along the Great Highway glow. I've been to and even set up a few bonfire parties on the beach, which never fail to be good times. Just keep the flame height lower than the beach wall or you get a visit from the friendly ranger.

I have to admit, I liked the old CAS better than the new one, but the times they are a changin' I suppose. There was something about that old custom-built planetarium projector with all the little doodads  protruding out at every angle. It was a one-of-a-kind mechanical marvel. I hear it's crated up somewhere in one of the Smithsonian warehouses now. The new Morrison Planetarium is really a movie rather than a true planetarium show, but they always have a good show.

Nevertheless, I've been a member since opening day and we enjoy the member's nights and other special events.

As much as the zoo has changed over the years, there are plenty of old 1930s depression-era WPA buildings still intact which are always interesting to explore. And the Little Puffer steam train, the hardest working machine in all of San Francisco, is a must-do on each visit. And the 1921 Dentzel menagerie is one of San Francisco's three antique carousels, but is eerily quiet with no music playing.

The animals themselves are the standard zoo assortment. Of course, the birth of the American bald eagle named Stephen Colbert in 2006 was the zoo's all-time biggest star!

Probably my favorite bike ride in the entire Bay Area is to the summit of Diablo, even though I'm far from a being a climber. I've ridden up 100+ times from both sides and hiked up a few times too. After an hour of climbing, there's something about that final 150 yard, 16% gradient stretch to the summit that puts the body through unthinkable excruciation, making the view from the top so much sweeter.

I like the mountain so much I was Race Director for the annual USA Cycling-sanctioned Mt. Diablo Hill Climb for a number of years.

When I was a lad, this seemed to be the default destination for the YMCA summer camp when they couldn't come up with anywhere else to go. We spent so many days fishing on the lake, rowing, and playing capture the flag in the poison oak-infested hills. I lost count of how many times the camp counselors had to dig fishing hooks out of kids' arms from wild-casting. We'd camp for the night every once in a while, with plenty of Kumbaya to go around.

I usually head up here now for a change-of-pace jog around the lake.

Great for a Sunday drive, or better yet, a bike ride. Killer view when the fog isn't in. There's a long, dark, dank tunnel to go through (with some pretty awesome "cave drawings") and Nike Missile Site SF-87 up above to explore.

I've come up here dozens of times with my telephoto lens and tripod to get one of those bridge-tower-popping-through-the-fog shots, but after years of trying, I've just come to the conclusion that it's not gonna happen for me. But who cares, plenty of other people have gotten the shot.

Coyote Hills has trails with some beautiful sweeping views of the lower bay wetlands. It's a great place for wildlife spotting. It's great for a long walk or loop around during a bike ride.

If you walk the trail, leave plenty of time and take plenty of water. The loop around is deceptively long and, although I had ridden around the trail plenty of times, we were dehydrated the first time I ever did it on foot.

I don't mind paying the parking fee because I know the funds go to good use.

Fort Funston was a WWI-era defense installation to protect San Francisco Bay in the early 1900s. Today it is a National Park. It's a great place for scenic trail walks along the coast and exploring the old defense batteries. Fort Funston is also the best place in the Bay Area to watch hang gliders up close. You can hear the whooosh when they fly over close above. I haven't gotten into hang gliding yet, but this is the place I'll go when I'm looking to get started.

There are traces of 265 Nike Missile sites around the US, but SF-88 is the only restored site in the country. Every part of this complex, from the launch computers to the elevator ride down to the missile bunker is fascinating. The best time to go is on first Saturdays of the month when the Nike veterans volunteer to tell stories and explain how things work down to every detail. Every time I visit, I leave with the sobering reminder of our Cold War past.

This is a must-see place for any rail fan or street car fan. It's a small half museum/half store with plenty of unique things that you can't buy anywhere else.

I'm a sucker for the limited odds and ends they sell here and I have a growing collection of things like cable car track pieces and genuine Muni rollsigns that have retired from service.

And don't forget to pick up a calendar. My photos have been featured in it for several years.

When you alter the blueprints for the world's greatest bridge to throw in a steel arch in order to avoid demolishing a place just because it's beautiful, it must be a special place.

Good old Fort Point defended our bay during the Civil War--no invasions were even attempted thanks to the intimidating might of the fort.

I've never grown tired of trips to Fort Point. It is packed with history and always fun to explore.

Best ballpark in the country, hands down. There's nothing like the atmosphere, views, and location of AT&T Park.

Aside from countless Giants games I've been to, I've been to football games, corporate parties, and other events here. It's one of the best venues around.

Unless you're making an entire day out of tailgating, it's ridiculous to even consider driving here. There are plenty of public transit options.

A great easy-paced day hike smack dab in the middle of the bay with spectacular views in all directions.

The island is rich in history, including the sobering reminders of our country's darker times of years past.

The only downside to an Angel Island visit is the inevitable last-minute rush to make it to the departing ferry. I have no idea what happens when one misses the last ferry off the island.

Huge steam trains in the Bay Area! This heritage railway runs a short out and back track through beautiful Niles Canyon and transports you back to yesteryear. The holiday train is always fun but my favorite special event is the photographer's special where they drop you off at picturesque spots along the track and "pose" the trains and run them back and forth for photo opportunities.

Point Reyes is one of the natural jewels of the Bay Area. Our big 5th grade trip was in a camp in Point Reyes where we learned to appreciate the majesty of tide pools, beaches, and trails. Although I've only camped in Point Reyes a few times since, there's plenty to do during a day drive. We never miss the lighthouse and beaches and occasionally indulge in some fresh oysters.

The Oakland Zoo always makes for a fun few hours. My favorite animal from when I was a kid was the Siamang Gibbon who had the loudest voice I've ever heard. He was always our first stop on any visit.

The zoo seems to be keeping up with the times and modernizing when money allows. Luckily the zoo will be allowed to expand into Knowland Park.

A paradise for dogs and dog lovers. On a sunny Sunday afternoon, you'll find the number of dogs hitting quadruple digits. The canines seem to fall into their instinctual behaviors and form packs with the other dogs.

There are miles of path, beaches, a water inlet that water breeds love to swim, and spectacular views for the humans to enjoy.

It's always sunny in Dolores Park! When Karl the Fog has you down, you can escape the freezing dankness of the rest of the city and come to the miracle spot where the sun always seems to burn through. And while picnicking or basking in the sun, you get a great view of the fog rolling over the rest of the downtown skyline.

One of my favorite mountain biking spots as long as it's not mid-afternoon in the middle of summer. Great place to just set out on a hike too. There's plenty to explore, including the old graveyard up on the hill. And, of course, a tour of the Hazel Atlas mines is a must-see at least once.

A must see for any Disney fan, the WDFM has a treasure trove of artifacts from the early Walt days all the way up to the creation of Disneyland. I can gaze for hours at the massive and detailed Disneyland scale model.
The Bay Area's go-to epicenter of mountain biking in my opinion. After all, Mt. Tam was the birthplace of the mountain bike and the trails and views are spectacular.

Phantom Falls is one of the most unique waterfalls I’ve been to in CA.
Don’t forget to pay for a lands pass online.($5).
When I arrived at the trailhead,
I found out there was no trail at all.
I needed GPS and the All Trail App to help me and my cousin.
It is flat with rolling green hills and some wildflowers.( very pretty,amazing).
We followed an old fence and crossed over the fence.
There are 2 ways to get Phantom falls.
They are both the same distance and incredible view.
Getting down to the swimming pool of Phantom Falls was big adventure for us but it worth it.( we were using rope).
The view around Phantom Falls were spectacular.(you have to go down to the pool if you are here).
Some parts of the trail are muddy with a lot of small water  crossing.( hiking shoes with water roof is the best).
We were able to visit 4 waterfalls on our trip.
We didn’t have much water flowing but enjoy Landcape and wildflowers.
We will try to come back here again for wildflowers and the falls after few rains or sometime in early April.
(2/16/2020).

My first time hiking at Henry. W Coe State Park.( January/3/2021).
My hike started from head quarter to China Hole Creek.
It is 11 miles out and back, 1,717 feet of elevation gain.
It starts with downhill all the way and obviously uphill all the way back.  it’s mostly narrow trails which make it unique and fun.
This was an absolutely beautiful hike: spectacular views, awesome creek, and not too difficult.
The view at the top of each hill was fantastic , the sign of green went on for miles.
I saw only 5 hikers,1 bicycler, few coyotes, hear several woodpeckers, and some deer.
It is secluded quiet, but very mighty area, those rocks and ferns wall does look nice and has good potential.
China Hole is Kelly Lake,since it’s not enough rain, so not much water left at China Hole. But still worth to spending sometime to hang out, it’s very pretty and peaceful, perfect place for picturesque.
Good hiking shoes, snacks, water, walking sticks,dress up warm since it’s winter.
Great scenery, definitely come back this park for different hikes.
dislikes: Low water level at China Hole

reviews_attraction.text:
I was visited this park on ( July/6/20).
There is $ 10 for parking fee, clean bathrooms, and very nice staff working in here.
But because the parking in the street was empty, so I didn’t have to pay for parking.
I Loved the trail, I had  done it before.
The Saratoga Gap loop’s trail, it is around 5 miles with a little bit over 1,000 feet of elevation gain.
AllTrails rated it as moderate, I think it is right.
The waterfalls over looks is closing right now. There are one way noted everywhere, because the COVID-19, but it makes much easier to hike.
The first half of the trail  was hiking down hill with dusty and sunny cliffs, but it has panoramic view of the canyon, it is breathtaking.
Awesome rocks formations, with little caves.
a large bouldees. There is decent climbing on the way out.
At one point you will have to hold a steel rope.
Hiking shoes, hat, water, bug spray, are needed for this trail.
Highly recommend it to everyone love outdoors.
Happy hike folks!

It is a beautiful hike, about 5 miles RT.
There are 2 ways to hike these falls, either from the top of the mountain hiking down to the Alpine lake, or from the lake up to the mountain.
I 've done this hike 2 times in both directions.
It's fine in both directions, though the top of the mountain is an easier drive.
The top of the mountain also has more parking spaces but no restrooms.
Today we were started at Alpine Lake and climbed uphill through a shaded of forest covering 1.7 miles to Laurel Dell picnic area. The route had so many waterfalls and was very peaceful and refreshing.
We didn't stop at Laurel Dell, and continued hiking up almost half of the mile to the top of the mountain, where we had a breathtaking view of the mountains and the ocean.
I love this hike. It's a good work out with 1,150 feet of elevation gain. I will surely come back if I'm around Mount Tampa again.

If you looking for something very  easy and super pretty, this is the PLACE.
I was here on 6/9/20.
The park is open back, very clean area, restroom in both sides, limited parking.
We did 3.6 miles RT, and  435 ft gain.
It has a lot of benches.
My thoughts... It’s not a hike, more like a cliff side walk.It is very treacherous.
We walked from this side of the bunker and walked back.
It is incredible view of the ocean from high up, the ocean so calm and so blue.
The mixed between those rocks, pave road and the ocean gave me very special feeling,
It is the mixed between human and Mother Nature.
It is amazing photo spots.
I took a lot of landscaping pictures from Tom Lantos  tunnels and the bunker.
I went here with my three sisters.
They were agree with me this is the place to walk with your lover and family.
It will be a lot of fun and relaxing.
Happy walk folks.

It is Beautiful this time of year to hike at Almaden Quicksilver. (3/21/2021).
The park has so many different trails and well marked.
An amazing history of the mine, Guadalupe Reservoir, Almaden Lake, and very spectacular views of San Jose  Bay.
I was used Mockingbird Hill Parking, with no entrance fee, it has a bathroom at the trailhead.
I was hiked  16 miles, and 2,500 ft of elevation gain.
My hike was not easy because it was a long-distance but it was not too difficult since it was not steep.
It’s nice rolling hills with some great views of the valley, and not too crowded.
Tons of fun!! Lots of shade and little sun.
Good balance of incline and decline.
During early spring, the park offers one of the most spectacular wildflower displays.
The secret of happiness is to discover all the marvels of California.
Happy Hike Everyone!!!

I have been here so many times,but I’m always feel like my first time.
I can heard and see Burney Falls the moment I arrived.
It is $10 fee.
The falls are absolutely amazing. Definitely a target spot for camera.
The trail along to the river was closed down.
I hiked only 2 miles, it was easy for me, but I was happy with that, since I had traveled far for the falls.
I was taking most of my time,sitting around the falls, trying to feed  my eyes with the beauty and my ears with the loud sounds of the falls.
But my soul was filled up with awesome of Mother Nature.
The falls are majestic, stunning, power,breathtaking, spectacularly .                                             I was living in the heaven at that moment.                                      I will come back to this falls again and AGAIN.

I was hiking at Windy Hill Open Space today July/27/2020.
Free parking,no entrance fee, basic bathroom, few benches.
The Hamms Gulch to Spring Ridge  loop.
The trail is 6.8 miles, almost 1,500 FT elevation change .
It is beautiful view. So many trees and shady, and very friendly hiker.
I was started at Hamms Gulch trail, passing  by Sausal Pond.
The trail has a lot of  switching back and steep but not bad.
When I came to Spring Ridge, it was hot and sunny, I didn’t want to hike with the heat and no shade.
I got out by the same way I got in.
I made my hike around 7.8 miles but most of time I was hiking in shade.
I didn’t have a good view from Spring Ridge.
But because of that I will come back to this hike again.
Next time I will start much earlier or much later.

Hiked in this trail for the first time, November/22/20.
The trail starts right in the middle of the campus.
There’s no parking fee, no entrance fee, I didn’t see bathroom at the trailhead.
My hike was a loop 7 miles, around 1,200 feet of the elevation gain.
I was started at something very interesting, those architecture graveyard projects, it was fun, I enjoyed a lot.
Following the dirt, rock, straight up  trail, it leads me to the Serenity Swing, (tree of life).
The views of the canyon from the peak is truly breathtaking, it’s spectacular place to take a break.
I was ended my hike at the ranch.
It is not too difficult hike, well maintained trails, no shade, hiking shoes needed, plenty of water, hat, sunblock, snacks.
Happy Hike Everyone!!!

Mt. Diablo Rock City has some of the most surreal- looking sandstone formations you’ll find in the Bay.
It is fun place, adventure for young-age and family.
I wished it has cable to climb up and back down for safety just like half dome. So I don’t get thrill with a hazy wind across the valley.
the Rocks are very cool, but they are also covered with so many initials, names, numbers.( You mind able to find your name too).
The formations at Rock City are remarkable, it has quite view from the top.
While you’re here, stop by Mt. Diablo’s Summit Museum, Art Gallery, Observation Deck or overlook.
You won’t regret for that 13 miles driving up,
Enjoy your trip.

I had visit this place on December/27/2020.
Spoony me.....I was looking for the garden with a lot of flowers but after about 1.5 miles hiking in, and I found out....
The name Garden of Eden is a misnomer.
There is no garden but a beautiful forest and scenery river flowing through it.
It was a bit confusing because no sign board or gate.
It is a small pool and boulders, very awesome spot if you love water holes.
The hike along the train tracks is lovely and a lot of fun. 99 percent of the trail is shaded,super easy, and not many people.
Wish I had gone when it was warmer to enjoy swimming!
It’s totally worth the effort.

I was here on December/15/2020.
No parking fee and basic bathroom.
The trails  were burnt in the recent fire so it’s not over grown.
The trail follows alongside of the lake almost entire way and it feels absolutely isolated in nature.
There are few down trees but it is easy to get over.
I Just hiking along the water.
Views are spectacular and the trail was not crowded, since it is not safe to hike.
But if you still want to challenging yourself, this trail is waiting for you, just watch your steps on the traverse.
Shoes with good traction and waking stick recommended.
Definitely will come back to try again in 2022.

“Exploring the art in Albany Bulb was fun for one day trip since I’m living not too far from Oakland City.
It is dogs friendly, and popular spot to explore (though there’s not enough parking space).
A lot of great graffiti artists, wildflowers , pretty cool urban art towards to the end.
It has many miles of hiking trails. ( I hiked a little over 2 miles).
Hiking along with Albany Beach is very peaceful, I was able to see Bay Bridge, San Francisco Bay, Golden Gate Bridge, and much much more.
I left a lot of footprints at the trail, and took home a lot of pictures.
I will comeback when I’m in Berkeley.”

I was here on October/25/20.
The road to get in to Hot Creek is rough but not too bad.
The parking lot has decent amount of spaces.
From the parking lot...  I’m already be graced by the excellent views of the Eastern Sierra.
At the top view... I was able to see 2 hot springs connected with the creek.
Followed the trail... it leads me to a steep path down to geyser.
Walked a long with the creek... it is a little smelly but it is something to learn about Mother Nature.
So sad... Hot Creek Geologic Site no longer allows human contact with the water.
Hot Creek Geologic Site is still well worth the trip.

I visited this place on July/9/20.
I made my dream come true when I was here.
It is so quiet and peaceful. It has a lot of nice art works from the vet.
They are so meaningful, thoughtful,and so lovingly.
Those art works trying to tell me.
1. They was tough when they were younger.
2. They were smart when they grew up.
3. They did not grow old enough to enjoy their retirement life.                                                     Especially the POW MIA sculpture.                                                        Folks please stop here show some reflective and give thanks for those who served.

Hiking in Mendocino is on my list.
I did it yesterday (Nov/24/2019).
I got lucky, weather so nice. I took Mendocino Headland State Park. The trail on another side of Mendocino town.
It is more like walking and play. I saw a lot of couples, kids, dogs.
Plenty of place to sit. Watching the wave is my favor. I thought I having whole place for myself.
I love  ocean air, it smells so fresh, it heals my soul.
A nice place to be,Wish I did not have to leave.
But I’m heading to mountain ( Russian Gulch State Park).

From Potato Chip Rock ( Ramona)to Torrey Pines Beach just a little over 20 miles, but very beautiful view,
It's usually super busy, early birds get worms ( parking).
quick and easy hike, 2.3 miles RT, a little steep, ( 321 feet of elevation change)
Hike down to the beach and then up back to the trail is the best.
Ocean is good for all ages and dogs, temperature of the water is nice to get wet, happy place to stay ...
Will come back if I around for sure.

I was here on April/4/2021.
I was hiking up to Jack Peak, it is a loop about 6 miles, 1,000 ft of elevation gain.
it is super nice trail, not many people, very peaceful, and a lot of shady.
It has a benches, picnic tables, bathroom.
Nice view of Carmel Valley, Watsonville,Santa Lucia mountain, and Monterey bay.
Everything in this trail are so green,
I would love to invite everyone come out, enjoy Jack Peak and support Monterey county park.

This hike is good for all skill levels. But some parts of the trail was closing for the construction. It is no shade, but it’s nice to walk along the bay, listen to the sound of the nature, and get some fresh air.
No need hiking gear, hat is needed.
But it can be windy, check with the weather before you go is the best.
Happy hike.

It is on the way to Yosemite from highway 140, small museum with amazing artifacts and a lot to learn about the history of the area during the gold rush.
Uniquely displayed related to post 1849 gold rush and massive migration into Mariposa County and state of California at that time.
I’m highly recommend everyone to visit it.

I was here on 10/3/2020.
Easy to find and park, street parking.
Residential neighborhood, it is super bright.
There is a lovely story about PG butterflies house.
It’s so sweet and true love.
I can not wait to share the story and the house with my daughters.
It is easy Walker or driving from Pacific Grove.
Worth a detour.

It is small garden but it’s so amazing.
Those sculptures are very uniquely caving.
There are so many different pieces of  wooden, stone, and some oak artists.
The landscaping and sculpture from across Polynesia and Pacific Rim are just perfect together in this garden.
This is such of treasure to me!

I am falling in love with this garden, it is small but beautiful flora and cactus.
It has very unique walking distance and
So many different kinds of cacti.
Most of cactus in this garden are big and healthy.
They are stunning and gorgeous.
it is amazing spot to take pictures.

Great hiking loop, easy to find parking lot,
4 miles round trip, gradually climbed up hill for the first halfway and all down hill for another half.
Awesome view of the valley, easy hike for everyone, very peaceful,
I love this trail, nice for work out...
I will come back.

I was here on Labor Day weekend 2020.
It was the most busy time at the park.
We had to waited over an hour for those pictures.
It was unforgettable and fun time ,I will do it again if I’m at the park.

You can spend an entire afternoon if not a full day reading and learning from all the exhibits they have here at Fort Missoula. They're also picnic tables and Greengrass to have lunch on so you don't even need to leave the premises. There's Fort history Native American history. Lots of exhibits on farming equipment logging equipment,  Railroad and mining equipment. Many many of the buildings have been restored and have exhibits in them others are restored just as they were. They also quite a few waiting for restoration and of course accept donations to further the expansion of exhibits in the museum. My favorite is going inside the smelter and looking up it's pretty cool then go climb the fire tower.

I visit a lot of state parks. Farragut State Park is the first one I visited in Idaho. It was fantastic. Spent the night in my car in a public ranger station lot. Got there too way late to get a campsite grow through and most of them looked  occupied. In the morning I went down to this overlook to boil some water and make coffee and have breakfast. Other local camper started walking and jogging by around 7 a.m. . Use caution if you're up at this time there is lots of Wildlife hanging around the roads. An excellent Park I will reserve a campsite next time. Great spot to take the kids to the lake lots of open areas. And the Beaver swimming area is completely awesome what a great spot!

I've been to many vortexes throughout the USA this is by far the best tour it's way more Hands-On they actually have three different vortexes a massive gift shop the guides are super friendly very inviting and it's a hands-on experience so be prepared to participate it's a lot of fun. I can't recommend this enough. All are welcome here! Vortex lovers and naysayers. They welcome questions and they have scientific proof to backup the area. The best part is after the tour they don't take you out you're free to wander around the grounds and eventually exit through the gift shop! A lot of fun bring the kids

This historical landmark is a great place to explore relax and unwind. It's not as well maintained or fixed up as some of the other historical forts. It needs your help and support! Help keep this piece of American history around in thriving for future generations to learn how hard it was back in the first and second world wars for America to protect herself without the current innovations that we have now. Words can really not describe the feeling you get walking around here and imagining what it was like to be a young 18 or 19 year old American sent here to help protect your country.

Beautiful park with many trails and a AWESOMELY historic lighthouse! FYI It's open for tours during summer months be sure to visit then it's worth it. Also check out the octopus tree watch out for Steep drop-offs near some of the trails!...

Some dummies shot out the glass lens in lighthouse when I was here to visit last. Big thumbs down to you little boys. Very uncool hopefully you get the maximum punishment available and then some from your parents.

Play structure,  restrooms, plenty of parking soccer field, basketball court,  and lots of trails. Plenty of trees left for a cool park.

There is a small patch of trees left from before they developed 136th, the road ended and the whole area all used to be covered in trees with a few trails throughout. Many kids playing with BB guns, motorcycles and making bmx jumps in the dirt! Only the airfields where nearby.... it was a great place to grow up.

I found this place while searching Google Maps had stumbled upon another fort on a road trip. It is super fun with lots of stuff to explore. Minimal vandalism which is nice. Kudos to the public on that. Great camping facilities with pretty warm showers and decent toilets, campgrounds are a little bit close together but that's the way it goes at state parks. Overall a great experience lots of History wish I had more days to explore I'll be back

Great park ....multiple lakes lots ( old water cooling pools for nuclear reactors ) Lots geese and goose poop! No bathrooms really.. theres one outhouse.. half the park is closed till next memorial day and the restrooms are behind the gate. I asked the roaming guards why the closure of that end of the park? They said to hard to keep an eye on people that far back...vandalism and stupidity win.  A few of societies FINEST ruin it for all of us!

A fantastic experience! Weather it sunny or raining this is a beautiful place! I love to come here when it's raining because there's less people . Bring lots of water if you plan to hike very far.  I bring an aquamira bottle it's refillable out of all of the streams and Creeks up here less weight in my backpack I highly recommend it

A little bit hard to get to since they've allowed people to build houses all around and they don't want you to park anywhere near their house. Best accessibility for taking pictures and viewing from a distance is the beach. It's sad that the local area would allow development all around this beautiful icon of Washington State

A fantastic wide-open space right on the Columbia River with plenty of room to enjoy a day with family and friends. Or just to take a walk by yourself. Plenty of trash cans to pick up after yourself. Clean restroom facilities. Lots of parking. There is also two playgrounds and two picnic structures  with barbecues.

Well maintained, friendly staff great location. You are a little bit close to your neighbor as with most state parks. So expect to be friendly and smell what they're cooking for dinner. Luckily our neighbors were super cool and we ended up making some new friends and drinking buddies!

Awesome trailhead. Lots of History make sure you read the plaques! Also just a great spot to park and walk out look over the edge quick and easy walk for a beautiful view. Completely wheelchair-accessible! Except for the trails. There's also a vault toilet here yay

I love this place! Cable cars are awesome and this place gives them the respect they deserve. Everybody should stop here! It was busy but the staff was still kind to me. I had all my questions answered and had a really good time.

Great place to break away from the drains of society and just take in some beautiful nature maybe see some wildlife. Also a great place for Enduro or snowmobile riding plenty of logging roads and lots of fun to be had.

A great Park all the way around I love the koi ponds and the conservatory! Plenty of room to get out and do activities pretty much any sport is doable here great place to walk. Or just let the kids play!

I had no idea there would be a zoo in North Dakota! Our family visited it was a lot of fun. Great zoo, lots neat animals to see and great meeting rooms. Bring your sunscreen if it's during summer time
A great place to visit especially for those that are into minerals obviously. But also the science of local geology and Mining. And those just with curious minds. Located on the Montana Tech campus
This is one of the best blocks in downtown Portland! Super awesome always loved this fountain... could use more police patrols to run off the whiskey saturated bums and crackheads though.
Unique park. Very dry. Biking, Walking paths. Nice spots to repell. benches throughout the park. No restrooms! Stunning views from most angles....the rim rock ARE A BILLINGS TREASURE!
It's amazing there's no bums in here. Beautiful natural area with very little litter. If this was in Portland Oregon it would be packed full of squatters, tarps, and heroin addicts!
Ice skating, swimming pool, walking path, restrooms, large beautiful shade trees lots of well taken care of lawn and ample parking on most days. What a great Park!
Very fun stop! Low level of graffiti and vandalism too, which is pretty neat for such a large city there is still a lot to see here! Definitely bring a camera
I'm not a fan of little kids or little kid movies but I had a fantastic time here! There is definitely stuff for adults too
Nice park right down by the water lots of stuff to see. Probably a fun place to let the kids run out some energy

The expanded Exploratorium at Pier 15 is a five star experience as the previous reviewers agree, but can wear you out. To get the most bang for your twenty-five bucks, you need to pace yourself and relax. Did you get hot running around the exhibits trying to keep up with the kids? Go outside and cool off in the fog exhibit on the walkway between the piers. Go upstairs and outside at the Bay Observatory. You can lunch at SEAGLAchose toSS restaureant or picnic outside (but remember to get your hand stamped). I was hang out in the cinema room watching the short films, taking a weight off my feet. Want to take a break standing up? There's a pinball machine with the insides exposed so you can see how it works. Still tired? There's an expresso bar and and espresso cart.

This review  the gardens and the ecological exhibits, not the State Museum. OK, it gets hot here but the car park has a misting system so you don't experience oven conditions on departure. Tip: come early and wear a sun hat or you will want to lie down on top of your vehicle and enjoy the misting. For me this was a zero $ not a $$ experience. Just ask for gardens only tickets. The garden includes the desert living and unlv desert solar house but not the butterfly habitat. The gardens are nice. You'll enjoy the air conditioning as you play recycling games inside a very clean garbage truck within a rammed-earth house. For me, the unlv desert solar house was the star attraction.

I biked here on an Indian Summer day. Agua Vista Park is well-named. I hung my hammock, climbed in and had a thoroughly relaxing time looking out on the water, the dry dock, the  gulls and the passing clouds. It's an easy walk from the Muni T-Third or the UCSF shuttle. It's right on the bike path, too. There's a fishing pier. Although there is no official camping (camping AND fishing right by the bay, who knew?), there do seem to be some mostly friendly car-campers with shopping carts here, who may ask you for a cigarette. Agua Vista Park offers excellent viewing for fireworks at AT&T Park or Ka-Boom.

Why pay over the top to stay in a box when you can enjoy the 'penthouse' suite (site #1) at Limekiln with a panaramic view of the coast and cove, hot showers and, well, cold showers under the waterfall (think non-tropical). One caveat: check out the Marine forecast, 40 mph gusts forced us to take down our 10-person tent and relocate into the redwoods. A hike to the lime kilns is recommended. Here is where the lime was manufactured for those 19th century brick and mortar buildings in San Francisco. Now that this review is published, all the more important to reserve in advance.

Andrew Molera State Park has lost its Woodstock vibe since they have restricted the free-form camping in the meadow. The water quality reports vary; I brought my own. This time we camped in the more developed Pfeiffer - Big Sur State park and enjoyed the beach at Andrew Molera free. It's a relatively short hike to the beach for you and your picnic. Too hungry to wait? There's some nice creek-side spots. Even hungrier? There are picnic tables right by the parking lot. You'll some of that red-ish "purple" sand on the beach, just like Pfeiffer Beach.

Nike Missile Site SF-88 is only open one or two days a month. I've toured here twice. The first time they let us go down into the bunker where the missiles are stowed. I think this is the only site where you can see the actual missiles. They have the radar rotating, too On my last visit a missile was top side keeping us safe from that 1950's attack. Even though the guard in the sentry box is a dummy you get a feel for cold war ambiance. Did you know, the perimeter fence was patrolled by attack dogs back in the day?

BTW, it really is a vista point not an insurance agency as categorized. You can get here on your Mountain Bike by taking the fire road to the top then a short distance down and here you are with an excellent view of the downtown or the fog. You'll remember the immense cross at the top of Mount Davidson from Dirty Harry but did you know it commemorates victims of the Armenian genocide? Reticent to get to Mout Davidson on your own power? You can arrive on Muni 36 Teresita from Mission district or Glen Park BART.

Both the exterior of the Museum and the theater across Main Street feature what looks like Doric columns fashioned from redwood trunks, if you accept Doric columns with square capitals. An eclectic collection of exhibits awaits you within the museum, and in the park outside you'll find a locomotive that originally hauled excursion trains up Mt Tamalpais. Tip: SF Bay Area residents seeking affordable housing will find single family housing in Scotia for $100 - $200 K.

This small, pleasant museum recently re-located to the rapidly-growing Dogpatch neighborhood. The location is excellent, handy to chocolate, ice cream, cheese, and the Illinois Street bike lane. Coming from the Mission? Take the 22 Fillmore. Coming on CalTrain? Get off at the 22nd Street station.
I was here last week for an extremely well-catered event. This place is big enough to accommodate your event and cozy enought everyone will feel at home

Having tried both, I far prefer Montana De Oro State Park over overpriced stucco egg-crate motels in SLO or Morro Bay. It's delightfully undeveloped here, so I stocked up at the Ralph's (Kroger) supermarket in Los Osos. The Bluff Trail is a must, and the beaches and tidepools are very pleasant. Disclosure: no showers here but you can fetch water in a bucket and have your significant other slosh it over you farmhouse style.

Sonoma Coast State Park stretches for some 11 miles along highway 1 between Bodega Bay and Jenner. I went hiking here on Bodega Head just when the fog was clearing -- beautiful views. You'll hear the barking of harbor seals in the distance. Did you know, you can visit the Bodega Head section free? Just drive in and there's lots of parking. You can warm up after your hike at Spud Point Crab Company. So get out there!

I was here for a performance of the Marriage of Figaro the other night from 7:30 until about 11pm. The time went by very quickly during the lively performance. This is one of the top opera houses in the world. The acoustics are excellent, the performers are amazing, the seats are comfortable.
Tip: bring some sandwiches and snacks so avoid the rush at intermission

On the plus side, it's a rare opportunity to see and learn to understand the interaction of dune and Franciscan rock that formed San Francisco. You can look out over row on row of Doelger housing streets in the Sunset and visualize them reverting to a vast dune field. On a clear day, that is. The minus side is: on a foggy day there's no view from Grand View.

If you want to stay in the wine country and save money for your fermented beverages and ever-increasing bridge tolls, Skyline is a good camping choice. I've been here three times. They have more hot water in the shower than many state parks. There's plenty of trails for maintain biking or hiking to Lake Marie. Yes, you'll see lots of deer and birds.

Hanna Winery is family owned, and I think this contributed to my enjoyment of a summer wine-tasting experience. Hannah has a second tasting room in Alexander Valley; this Russian River location is the original operation and the origin of the Hannah pinot noir. A leisurely lunch on the patio was a pleasure. You'll feel welcome here.

What's not to like about Balletto. Cool tasting room. I enjoyed listening to the blues while tasting the very fine pinots and a dry gewurtztraminer. The patio is nice too. Very friendly, here, none of that pretentious wine snob stuff.  Tip: if you show them your Visa signature card, your tasting will be free.

very nice to relax on the benches with maybe some take-out coffee from Ritual or Blue Bottle. If you have time, you might like looking through the kaleidoscope style sculptures her and along Octavia but watch out for traffic on Octavia or you might see stars in an unexpected way.

what a fun place to hang out on a clear day or to shelter behind the rock ramparts and watch the fog roll in. you can relax in the middle of the round former tank emplacement and visualize yourself being evacuated by helicopter from the roof of SF

There are some pleasant trails here with good views of downtown. It's a convenient option if you don't want to walk all the way to Buena Vista park or Tank Hill. Got kids? They'll like the nearby Randall Museum.

This is the OTHER San Francisco Conservatory, and quite a gem it is. Even if it's closed you can enjoy the landscaping. You can combine this one with Mt Davidson (remember Dirty Harry?) on the same  trip.

Pluses: A great place to relax and enjoy a BBQ or a walk on the recently improved shoreline trail.
Minuses: Some vandalism, early closing time. Easy to walk or bike to Heron's Head Park.
Lovely vistas day or night. Great place to watch red tailed hawks. Sometimes I bring my hammock to relax and observe the #SanFranciscp Bay
It's a restful oasis right above Moscone with live music in the summer. Nice butterfly garden. There are chess tables on the East side
There is an impressive number of special exhibitions here. The building also houses a cafe and the Pacific Film Archive.
No tasting fees and wines that go down well if you like dry whites. Just avoid the peak traffic on 101 if you can.

We had an amazing time on our Jet boat ride! The Jet boat guide we had was amazing! He was very informative, humorous, filled us with information about himself & made us feel like family which was nice. I think it’s great he is a boat guide and a fishing guide! What a great life to have! We met his wife and red headed child along the banks of the river. We dropped the dog off with them. I loved his joke that he had told us “my son has red hair, not sure where he gets his red hair from. Some people think my son looks like the UPS guy,” he paused while we all laughed. Then he says “well, it turns out he is the UPS guy!” Haha! My son told him he wanted to get wet, while boarding the boat, after our delicious lunch at the lodge. On the way back, adventure got better! We got wet, boy did we get wet & we did more spins! We saw an abundance of wildlife along the trip- Bald Eagles, Osprey & their giant nests, ducklings, deer, and even a Harbor Seal (named Super Glue- on the river for the fish!) and a Black Boar or pig (I forgot! Oops!). We originally booked the longer trip for my birthday. Then my sister could only go to the early & shorter one so we changed it. We were a little bummed because we wanted to do the whitewater trip through the canyons and didn’t think that in the “relaxed” trip we would be doing spins or getting wet. I’m so glad I was wrong! We also had our 2 & almost 5 year old with us. The shorter trip- mail route was just the perfect  amount of time for the little one’s attention spans!

This place is located right over the Oregon border. My research reported there are 700+ caves in this National Park. We explored a bundle of caves with our young ones but did not see 700 caves on the map. We went only as far as we were comfortable with. We went straight to the visitor center to speak directly with the park hosts/ rangers. You can buy a National Park passport book (if you don’t have one yet) for around $10, which we did and had our son stamp it. After we went to the visitor center to get their advice, knowledge about the caves and cave closure information we went on our adventure! There was a cave closer due to a Rattlesnake hanging out in one and other caves were closed (had to do with bats). We spent a whole day driving to the different caves but it would take 2 days or so to explore all of the marked caves. The map shows locations of caves and which caves are least difficult to most difficult. There are even painted caves. To hike into those it is .7 miles to the first painted cave and another .22 miles to the painted bridge cave. The first painted cave- the paintings have warn off mostly. The bridge cave has painted symbols in two sections that we saw, painted by Native Americans years and years ago. It is very spiritual being inside a cave and thinking of the Native American history and what they may have done inside that cave! Our family enjoyed exploring these Native lands and it left great opportunity for teaching.
likes: Facilities & Services: Visitor center, park rangers
dislikes: Facilities & Services: Limited cave access due to closures

reviews_attraction.text: This is a fun place to stop if you are in the Bend or Sunriver area. There are places for RVs or oversized vehicles to park as well as regular vehicle parking but it fills up fast in Summer. It is free to explore the caves which is wonderful. Before you go inside the caves the park rangers do a brief speech asking if you have visited any caves before. They let you know about disease that can spread from other caves to bats. The caves are at a lower elevation and temperatures drop in the 40 degree range, so bring a coat if that is cold for you. Wear headlamps or bring flashlights because the caves are very dark. The caves are also longer than we expected. They are about a mile long. We brought our kids along for the journey. They enjoyed the cave. We had a guy say out loud “this isn’t a place to bring your baby!” I thought that was rude but I didn’t say anything. My daughter, at 16 months old and son at almost 4 years old did great. There are some bumps on the trail to watch out for, handrails everywhere but nothing too dangerous. There were other kids in there and a baby younger than ours being perfectly protected in her mother’s carrier. The cave may be too long for some. I would recommend checking out this cave but if you don’t hike to the end you aren’t missing much if you turn around early. The cave looks pretty much the same throughout but there is one spot that the cave narrows for a few steps so you have to duck down for a bit.
