Mission Bay Park East is about a one mile long Park on the east side of Mission Bay. Quite a few of the reviews are not actually of this side of the bayfront park; many of the photos are of Sea World and other parts of Mission Bay and it's gorgeous Park areas. With that said I will share the good news. This Bay is man-made and it is huge extending for miles. This Park is really a great addition to all the areas that it extends to. A good Park to visit when in San Diego.

The Eastside of Mission a Bay Park includes the grounds around the Hilton Mission Bay. The park itself is narrow, well treed, a great boardwalk follows the shoreline and there are plenty of recreational activities throughout. This Park was originally the area for the SD Visitors Center which was great for getting info for your San Diego visit.

Many areas to park for free. Great place to have a picnic and play ball.

You will like Mission Bay Park!

Newport Pier is a stately pier that was built in this configuration in 1940. The Newport Lifegaurd Bldg at the front of the pier is a beauty. The pier has long been popular for a stroll, fishing, taking in the coastal view and also dining at the restaurant on the end of the pier (Newport Grill & Sushi closed in 2012). Nestled to the side of the pier is Dory Fishing Fleet a coopertive that was established in 1891.

The pier extends out across a wide white sand beach that is the playground of the locals and tourists (6.9 million visit Newport Beach each year; the pier is central to this lovely beach town). Newport Beach is usually very crowded yet the area has a serenity about it. The beach is well maintained by Newport Beach government. The pier is a real asset to this gorgeous community!

Crown Point Park is a wonderful San Diego spot for a great day on the bay in a beautiful Park. I love the winding boardwalk (popular with runners, bicyclists and people going for a walks). The Park's boardwalk goes on and on around many parts of Mission Bay (for miles this boardwalk skirts the whole of the bay; it wraps around the bay all the way to Mission Beach.... a great bike ride.. perhaps 5 miles).

Crown Point Park is very green and well manicured, great trees and sandy beaches of the man-made Mission Bay; it is a great enjoyable area!  The park provides fire rings set in sand, many picnic benches on green grass or on the sand, public facilities and the park is in close proximity to stores, restaurants, bars and much, much more.

This is an historic lighthouse. You will find photos of the Long Beach area posted on the exterior of this structure. Gorgeous area (park) with views in every direction. The lighthouse shots atop a hill that overlooks the famous Queen Mary, the Marina, Shoreline Village and the Long Beach Skyline.

The park itself is exceptionally picturesque, green grass and gorgeous trees, winding boardwalk, beautiful blue water, many specialty restaurants, candy store, souvenir shops, boutiques, gift shops, Aquatic Park, street vendors, The Pike Mall, and much, much more...

Horton Plaza is great fun; a feel good fantastical mall! I love the dizzying wild architecture in this multi-level mall and the variety of stores. It reminds me of Alice in Wonderland with all my favorite stores.

Horton Plaza is the Crown Jewel of San Diego's lively Gaslamp District. You can spend hours and hours shopping in a miriad of stores and then have a great meal in one of the many food establishments. Also you can catch a movie in the malls theater...

Parking is abundant and free for first three hours (last time I visited).. You should ask.

Have fun!

cmilton111   6.2017

Vacation Isle Park; a small but beautiful setting, a special San Diego Park. Great location on Mission Bay right adjacent to Paradise Point Resort and Spa. A relaxed feeling of nature within the city limits.  You will love Vacation Isle Park..

They have plenty of space for family or events, a great pond for miniature boats, boardwalk for walking and bike rides, fishing in Mission Bay, fire pits, plenty of shady trees or open green grass areas, great views and loads of serenity (double dose).

Very small but special park.

The park is named after Kate Sessions who is the one person that influenced the beauty of San Diego as she brought in trees from all over the world. Thank you Kate.

The park is gently slopped toward the coast with beautiful views of Pacific Beach and the ocean. Favorite of many locals to walk their beautiful pampered La Jolla doggies. Also a great place to picnic or chill on the green well cared for lawn.

Very small but very enjoyable!
likes: Facilities & Services: Well cared for lawn

reviews_attraction.text:
This is a small Park that is popular with local people. The park does have some vandalism issues which would give me concern of recommending although I love parks with ducks and geese as well as fishing.

I would recommend going in a group to any member of my family or anyone that I know. The park is maintained through citizen contributions to a local Lodge which is adjacent to the park (that was pointed out to me).

Fanuel St Park is set right next to the famous Mission Bay. The well traveled  Mission Bay Boardwalk runs through this small green park so there is a lot of interest for those who like to watch people or have fun as recreation includes: sunbathing, volleyball or paddle ball for the athletic, Frisbee, catch football, sailing on the bay, bike riding, skating, photography and picnicking. Nice place to spend casual time with a great view and your crew.

Mission Beach Park (MBP) is a favorite destination of people from all over the world. The beach is very popular and extremely crowded during the summer months. MBP is an amusement park, a beachfront park with picnic benches and plenty of grass, restaurants, bars, plenty of shops and people, people, people. Close to a lot of shops, a great park, the gorgeous Mission Bay, miles of boardwalk and sand.  You will love MBP!

Soledad Park is set atop Mt Soledad. Spectacular views of most of the area including Clairemont  and San Diego to the east and south respectively; then also La Jolla, the Pacific Ocean  to the west and the coastline to the north. Worth the drive through parts of upper La Jolla (some of San Diego's finest homes are on Mt. Soledad... you may also enjoy driving through the neighborhood and viewing the homes). Have fun.

This is the bridge from downtown Long Beach to get to the Queen Mary...

I rode my bike across bit I don't recommend it. I took the north side of the bridge and that meant I had to carry my bike down a long set of stairs to get to the street level. Still all in all I enjoyed my time there and the view of the area from the bridge.

Cabrillo National Monument is a spectacular park with great views overlooking San Diego, Coronado and the Pacific Ocean. Much of this park is preserving the natural California landscape. Paths wind through the park along the cliffs all the way down to the water which surrounds the Point Loma peninsula.

Very small but packed with dynamite views! The park is in view of the beautiful cliffs of lower La Jolla and sit atop cliffs about 50 ft above the sands of Pacific Beach. Great place to relax and take in some sunshine, sunsets and the views are great always. Popular spot!

This is a really beautiful park, perhaps the best in Knoxville (I am only in Knoxville for 10 months at this time).

Great for quiet time by the river, family time and recreation, walks, bike rides, fishing, and much more...

Bixby Park is small but it has a lot to offer. Is proximity to the Long Beach shore (park sits on clifftop overlooking the beaches). Lots of beautiful trees,
green grass, and many recreational and community attractions.

Nice small park. I am told that Anaheim has a lot of parks and that they keep them very clean.

I talked with the recreation director briefly; he was very friendly.

People that I talked with were friendly.
This is a very nice additional Park just north of Point Fermin Park. It stretches for several beautiful blocks on the cliffs of San Pedro. Walking path is great. Access to the beach below.
White Point Park is set on the San Pedro Cliffs. Children's play area and a great view of the Pacific Ocean. There is also a baseball field, walking path and nature center.

Manhattan Beach Pier is very, very nice. The beach is pristene white sand, blue skies most days, friendly atmosphere and nice views!

Nice walking trail. Plenty of green grass, trees galore, a children's area, friendly approachable people; makes a nice place to enjoy yourself!
9.26.2019
Gorgeous park on top of Laguna's beautiful cliffs. Great place to visit and take in dynamic views and of course sunsets to dream of..
Laguna Art Museum is a beautiful museum and it is in a great location. The exhibits change every few months.

I love this place! My destination was little yosemite, and the trails I hiked were Canyon View Trail and Ohlone Rd. Canyon View Trail is narrow, but it's high enough that you can see the beautiful scenery of mountains in the distance, and it's less crowded. Ohlone Rd is a wide trail without elevation changes that is easy to walk and also accessible to the river that runs beside it. The little yosemite area has a river with many rocks and you can climb on the rocks and have fun. The entry fee was $5. Pay attention to the gate hours (may vary depending on the season). There is plenty of parking and some picnic tables as well.

I visited there in May. I enjoyed changing scenery throughout my walking. There is an open space of meadow hills with a great view around the Monte Bello Open Space Preserve Parking Lot. As I went down, I got in the forested area.  There were many trees covered with lots of moss on their stems.
I walked down Stevens Creek Nature Trail, then returned walking up Canyon Trail.

I’ve also hiked Grizzly Flat Trail which extends from Skyline Blvd. I kept walking down and down until I met Stevens Creek. This is more wild than the trail above. Be careful of the bed bugs.

There are some beautiful view points where you can see small towns and blue ocean.
The trees in this place were unique because they had smooth trunks.
We walked up Brooks Creek Trail and returned by going down Montara Mountain Trail. The view from the end of Brooks Creek Trail was so nice. I found a caution though, that I was in mountain lion territory. Some notices are written.
There is a waterfall viewing point, but the staff said that is for a limited season only and we couldn’t see it that day.
The vehicle entry fee is $6.

Ridge Trail has the best view. I want to visit here again. From the main parking lot (located on the corner of the Skyline Blvd and Alpine Rd's intersection), I walked a loop consisting of Ridge Trail, Bo Gimbai Trail, and Ancient Oaks Trail. When standing on the Borel hill, it offers a spectacular 360-degree view. A sea of clouds could be seen in the distance from there. I think this trail is great for cyclists, too.
The restroom in the parking lot was clean and had automatic sanitizers.

It is a nice place to hike.
I started walking up Mayfair Ranch Trail and headed back down Longwall Canyon Trail. It was a mild uphill and downhill hike, I also found two small creeks. Once I arrived around the 1 mile mark, there was a great view of a huge open field with dry grass. A gentle breeze made it relaxing.
There were many sunny parts, so it can get very hot in summer.
This was the only one-way trail when I visited here in May, due to the COVID-19.

The trail is along side the stream down in the valley. We walked over fallen trees and across a shallow river. It is difficult in some places, so you could fall into the river. Wearing trekking shoes or boots will prevent you from getting wet. The walls of the canyon are covered with ferns, which makes for a wonderful space and gave a unique experience.
We had to go off-road to get to this place, and on the way we crossed a shallow river by car!

A very beautiful coastal trail, the best I've ever seen. The main trail is a paved road, on top of the cliffs, which are covered with sand and succulents, we walked along them with a wide open view of the ocean. You can also go down to the sandy beach. The trails here are relatively crowded compared to the other places. There were also many people with dogs. The parking lot is very large, but it fills up quickly on weekends.

I visited here in November. You need to apply for a free permit more than 24-48 hrs before. This is the best place to enjoy the huge redwoods trees. Due to the limited number of people, you can enjoy the great wilderness at your leisure. There is an abundant and variety of plant life. The trail here is 1.3 miles all the way down, then a 1 mile flat loop track.
Note: It's a narrow 30-minute off-road ride to get the trailhead.

A famous spot here is Bear Gulch cave trail, but the roadway that accesses the trail was closed when I visited here in June. So I parked at the Visitor Center and headed there by foot, but unfortunately I couldn’t because it was too far for us to walk, and the temperature went up 91F with no shades. If it were cooler, I could’ve enjoyed the view more. I want to try other trails, anyway.
Restrooms were by the Visitor Center.

A beautiful place to visit. This is a poetic hike because you can find poems on wooden signs along the trails. A grove of redwood trees make the trails highly shaded.
I walked up Lookout Trail and reached Lookout Point. From there, there was a great view of the city and mountains. I liked this trek very much.
Other than trekking, there are nice gardens and grass fields to visit around the Montalvo arts center.

I hiked down the McClures Beach Trail, which is in the northern part of the park. It’s an easy trail to get to the beautiful beach. The waves were high and there was sea foam along the sandy beach. The drive to the trail was also beautiful. The meadows were spectacular. I saw some elks roaming freely.
Bring a jacket as it can be chilly.
Next time, I want to go to Tomales Point.

I visited here in November. To get here, you need to take a narrow off-road track by car. The trail here is easy and flat with lots of huge redwoods. Some of the trees were overturned and showed their bare roots, while others had been struck by lightning and charred with their top half missing. Ferns were densely growing everywhere.
There is no restroom.

I went camping there last August. It's not crowded even on the weekends and has a dry grass field
I could enjoy the comfortable sound of the insects during the night. And the stars are absolutely beautiful!
I found various insects hanging out there during the day such as bees in the morning, flies in the evening and mosquitos at night.

I went camping here. The place was very nice and comfortable. The temperature was just right. I saw a beautiful sunset.
You need to go down the steep slope to the beach, but the scenery from the top of the hill is so wonderful. I wanna go camping here again.
One bundle of firewood is available for $8. There were very few bugs.

You can hike with a view of the meadow mountains in the distance.
I walked along the Oak Tree Trail and the Woodland Trail, stopping at Meadow Pond on the way. The pond was dried up when I visited here in April, but the view from there was great. The Oak Tree Trail had little shade, but the Woodland Trail was mostly shaded.

Great place to visit. I went there in May. The trails around Picchetti Ranch Parking Lot are relaxing. Although there was quite a steep part before the Stevens Creek, the Zinfandel Trail was almost flat, so it was easy to hike. In the middle, I saw a great view of the mountains and Stevens Creek Reservoir.

From the starting point, you can see a large hills covered with green grass all the way up to the top, so you can enjoy the wonderful green scenery while climbing. There is no shade, so be sure to hydrate well during the hot season and be careful of sunstroke. The trails are wide and easy to walk.

It was the best view I'd seen lately.
I walked the Anniversary Trail and climbed up the Windy hill summit, which had a great view of the city and mountains in the distance. As the name suggests, the wind is always blowing. You can walk the Anniversary Trail and I admire this great view.

I visited here in November. I walked around Manzanita lake. A lot of idyllic natural scenery can be seen. Part of the lake was frozen over and I saw some small gray fish swimming under the ice. It was breathtaking to see the beautiful snow-capped Mount Lassen reflected in the lake.

These coastline trails are very scenic. The view of the cliffs and the ocean from the headland was especially great. The trails have some steep uphills and downhills which are slippery, so hiking boots are recommended. At sunset, pampas grass field was in a golden glow!

A very beautiful trail with views of the cliffs and the ocean. Succulent flowers were blooming. This is also a popular paragliding spot. You can also go to a wide sandy beach, but you need to go down a narrow, rocky slope. Be prepared because there are no toilets.

I visited there in March. I loved the idyllic scene of meadows as far as the eye could see.  Also, there is a city over the meadows.
We parked Sierra Vista Point and walked the Kestrel Trail and Sierra Vista Trail.
There is no shade and  no restroom.

I parked at the main parking lot and climbed up to Edgewood Park Vista, where you can see the grassy hillside. I liked Old Stage Rd, which goes through an open grassland, and I saw some deer. The trails were smooth and easy to walk, but narrow.

I walked from Sears Ranch Parking Area to Harrington Creek. It was an uphill and then downhill track. There were few changes in the landscape, it was a peaceful scenery with meadows, cows, and mountains in the distance.

It's an idyllic scenery and the path is paved.
I wish to walk there again in spring, when the field of green grass can be seen.

Whether you are a tourist looking for the best things to do in LA, or just a local looking to make something of an afternoon, the La Brea Tar Pits is one of the best attractions in the city.

The La Brea Tar Pits is a group of asphalt seepages that are located in the middle of West LA. There are multiple pits, each one fenced off and  all open to the public for free. There are currently two digs going on, though only one is working at any point in the year. Well made signs detail anything you would ever want to know about the pits, and guides are available in the kiosks if you have more questions. If it is during daylight hours, you will most likely see actual workers excavating, which is pretty awesome. The LA County Museum of Art (LACMA) along with the Petersen Automotive Museum are right next door - I would highly recommend making a day out of going to all of them if you are planning a visit. Parking is limited due to the high number of visitors - street parking is metered and the parking structure is $14 for the day, however if you are willing to walk a little parking shouldn't be that big of an issue.

I would insist on if you are visiting the tar pits that you visit the museum. Admission is $12 for adults, $9 for students/seniors, and free for teachers with ID. If you want to see the IMAX movie it's a few dollars extra. The museum is one loop around - small, but chock full of information and interesting things to do. I would say it is definitely worth the price of admission with all the time I spent in there (2 hours, but I was engrossed in everything)

The museum basically details the entire history of Los Angeles from 50,000 BC to now. They have animated dioramas and TONS of skeletons of animals they've dug up. It is truly mind boggling the number of animals and plants that they've pulled out of the pit, and really makes you appreciate how much of a gift this place is to the paleontology field in general. The coolest part of the museum has to be the part where you can watch the scientists sort through and categorize items found in the pits. They have progress sheets that they fill out so if you come back you can see how far they've progressed on whichever skeleton they are working on. There were multiple guides sprinkled throughout the museum, and every single one was incredible and elevated the experience (shoutout to Zwi and his lecture on ancient bison and the multiple theories of extinction for large megafauna in North America).

The gift shop has some hilarious shirts and some really cool gifts (one day I'll purchase that full size replica Sabertooth Cat skull!). I'm not usually one for museum gift shop crap but the person who designs the stuff has a sense of humor and knows how to make stuff look good. It's a little pricey but the proceeds help the digs (and sometimes there are some good sales on T shirts), so at least there's that.

Overall, it's a great place to go, whether you have kids or are just going on a fun date - The La Brea Tar Pits are one of the highlights of Los Angeles to be sure.

Hell on earth during the summer, but great secret spots if you know where to look.

It's a very desolate beauty - I'm of the opinion that CA desert is very ugly in general (as a local), but Anza Borrego is definitely one of the top. During the rainy season the blooms are some of the best in the entire world. People come here in the spring expecting flowers - don't. Flowers only come in the weeks following rain (Fall, Winter, Spring) - and then they will disappear until the next rain - which can be a long time. If you don't time it right there will not be any flowers to see. The stargazing is second to none, and there are not a lot of people here so the place has an otherworldly feel. Borrego Springs is a nice small town and there are plenty of places to stay. I would recommend camping if it isn't during the summer, and there are some great trails for offroading and RV camping. The State Park center is very nice and all the rangers know their stuff. Asking them for the best hiking trails for your level is your best bet. Bring PLENTY of water and hats/sunscreen.
likes: Great trails for offroading and RV camping

reviews_attraction.text: There is so much to do here that it is hard to put into few enough words for a review. First off, cars are allowed to drive on the beach here. If you have two wheel drive and low clearance - think twice about taking your car on the sand here. Even if you have 4WD or AWD, remember to AIR DOWN YOUR TIRES before you attempt to drive on the sand. Keep to the speed limit and have a good time. Campsites are plentiful and cheap ($20 bucks and make a reservation online at the state park website). Primitive camping - only portapotties are available. If you are brave enough to haul your RV trailer on the sand here you can do that too. ATV rentals are plentiful if you don't have any to ride the dunes. Fishing and clamming will need a license - be sure to read all the rules associated with them. The beach is very long, so there's plenty of space to get away from the louder folks at the dunes if you want peace and quiet. When you are done, be sure to rinse off your undercarriage to get all the salt off and prevent rust.

Nothing short of incredible. I've been to more than my fair share of National Parks, and Olympic National Park is definitely in the top 5. The unbelievable scenery and the fact that it seems like this place doesn't get inundated with visitors makes this a treat to visit. There are so many things to see and places to visit within the park, that a week here is still chock full of things to do every day. The park is remote - and feels like it. People can get lost here easily because the park is so huge. My advice would be to go to places like Hurricane Ridge, camp in the Hoh Rainforest, visit the beaches of La Push (remember, the coastline is part of the park too!), and go kayaking on Crescent Lake. You could also visit a Salmon Hatchery and explore Forks (for the Twilight fans) if you want. Overall, this area has a lot to offer, and anyone travelling to Seattle should honestly skip their trip and just come here - it's that good.

Meh. Maybe it's because I've grown up with ugly CA desert that Joshua Tree doesn't interest me in the slightest. The only things here are rocks, sand, and the Joshua Trees - that's it. I wouldn't take my family here for fun because the most trails don't lead to scenery of any note and there's nothing really to do. Rock Climbing holds some interest - some of the rocks are excellent for bouldering, but other than that there's little to do here that involves any sort of scenery/animals/reasonable temps under 100 degrees. If you are thinking of stopping, either drive right and look at the millions of Joshua Trees on the side of the road by or just stop by the visitor center and then leave. The only reason to stay here for any longer period would be to boulder OR to stargaze - for which the dark sky is second to none and is the main reason why I'm even giving it 3 stars

Stunning, I believe, is the word. Wherever you are from in CA - or out of state - it's worth the drive. The flowers and colors are 2nd to none and the amenities provided by the park are very adequate for a normal day. Notice at midday when the crowds are heaviest at peak season (March-April) it can get quite unenjoyable due to chaos of everyone seeing the flowers, but there are more than enough places to find in the many trails that weave through the park where you can get some peace and quiet. Remember STAY ON THE TRAIL, AND DON'T CRUSH THE POPPIES!!! If you have a vehicle with an sort of moderate clearance (i.e. not a ferrari) your car will have no trouble on the dirt roads that surround the park when it is dry as they are all fairly flat.

The best aquarium one the West Coast, perhaps in the United States. The amount of things to do is worth the hefty price of admission many times over. Plus the aquarium is on the forefront of sustainability and methods taking care of the animals. Can get crowded during the tourist season, so plan wisely. Parking is VERY limited, and you will have to walk quite a distance to get to the aquarium - my advice? Park and make a day of strolling through downtown and learning about the history of the city. Plus you can cap it off with a dinner at the first Bubba Gump's, which is right next door.

Overall, if you are visiting the city, you should definitely visit the aquarium.

Nice little center to learn the basics about the eruption. Admission is 5 dollars and there is a gift shop - hours are limited during off peak seasons, but they are open during the winter. The center itself is small - but if you've never seen anything about the eruption before than you could easily spend an hour or two here reading everything. There is also a movie to watch (which I would recommend). Overall a good little experience, and very good for kids.

If you are wondering whether the long drive was worth - I can assure you it is. Incredible views and a great experience. The bus out to the lighthouse (the only way to get there) costs 7 dollars, runs every 15 minutes from the lot, and stops at 5pm. Totally worth it to get out there as the combination of views, wildlife, and farm history is unparalleled. Definitely a once in a lifetime experience if you are just visiting the bay area for a short time.

Never knew this was here - great place for recreation hiking and camping. There is an RV park and large shaded groups of campsites that can be booked by large groups. Lots of parking, and all the roads can be easily accessed by all vehicles. There is no offroading allowed in the area as evidenced by all the great trails shut off by iron gates :( But overall a great resource for those in orange county that may not know it is even here.

Easy parking, great racing, and cheap admission - also there are lots of historical places of significance within the track itself. Makes for a wonderful day out. Food is expensive in the way that ballpark food is expensive - they have deals every week however for cheaper food, so paying full price can be easily avoided

Great hike - stellar views all the way round. Will take a while to complete (8 miles total) but it is worth it. If you don't want to take it all the way round to the falls I'd recommend the taking to boat to the lower part of the falls trail to save some time/distance).

Really great place - we went here every year with out school and it never gets old. They have a huge furnace where you can watch them make glass, and then a museum of artwork to accompany it. I’m not a super Texan by any means and in no longer live there but it was still great to visit the capital building. Great architecture to see. As for the monuments, yes some are being looked in a harsh light, and I don’t agree with them but they are there and yeah I took pictures of them. I would recommend anyone who loves music to come here.

Could be bigger but I think that museums could be bigger.

The pumpkins were amazing. Absolutely will go back again to experience more of the garden on a day when it’s not raining. Expect the rain ads something special to everything.

When I went it was not too busy which is nice. The staff was really nice and everything was presented in easy to see way. It’s a must part of the Hollywood experience.

This may seem like just a normal gate but it does have a rich story behind it. I thought it was interesting. Can you imagine that this was in front of a house once. That’s crazy. How many people just walk past it without giving a single thought to what it is. It’s a grand opening to the garden.

A great small green spot that is a reminder of a dark moment in human history. The city has such a connection to Ireland. It’s a great place to come and reflect. Some great views of the freedom tower and the surrounding area which a bonus. If you happen to be near by you should stop by.

Love coming here to the longhorn walk, it’s such a different event that you will see in most places. Lots of great places to eat here. A real must see if your from out of Texas or even if your from Texas. And it’s free. Lots of parking and places to take lots of photo memories.

reviews_attraction.text: Great national park with amazing hikes. Must visit the less known areas in the Northeast and Warner Valley. The main park area has developed roads and easy access to the attractions but not so much in the eastern sections so be prepared. Stop by manzanita lake for fun kayaking, hike to waterfalls, and definitely climb up a volcano. Dont forget to stay late to catch the night sky. Also check out Lake Butte area and Devil's kitchen in Warner Valley. It's all worth it and best part...it is never crowded!!

They are connected to the ocean, they take care of animals, there is a research center, they are helping injured animals and have hands on activities. It's such an educational place for the kids.

Enjoyed our hike here. We parked near Fisk Mill Cove and hiked to the Cove area for some amazing views.
I mean,  is just OK. You can take pics and experience driving through a giant tree but that's about it.

There is so much to do here.  I've been to DC many times but usually did not have a car or was not wanting to spend money so I've never been here before.  Let me tell you, you will not regret going here.  You can easily spend all day here.  My wife and I got there at 1pm and left when the museum closed at 6pm rushed through it and we didn't even see the gristmill or distillery!  We could have easily spent 8 hours here.  When you get in make sure to look at the calendar for the day so you can plan when to be where.  If you want to see the weaving for example, it's a walk from the mansion so make sure you're in that area when it starts.  Do not miss out on the museum either.  There are multiple movies and tons of good information there.  In the museum alone expect to spend almost 2 hours.  If you've been to Monticello this place is much bigger, highly highly recommend this as something to do outside of the normal National Mall activities in DC.

It is truly a beautiful garden!  There are places to picnic and Florida's own version of rolling hills are in sight.  My wife and I didn't do any of the hiking trails because it was too hot (June).  The visitor center has a nice video and small museum.  The tower is impressive with a spectacular bronze door.  We did the house tour which was nice.  You can walk around the outside of the house without a ticket if you don't care to see the inside.  It's a self guided tour but there are volunteers throughout who provide some commentary.  Overall Bok Tower and Gardens is worth the cost of entrance.  It's a ways south of Orlando (over an hour drive) but one of the top gardens I've seen.  You can easily spend 4-6 hours here.

Last item is I don't recommend this trip in the summer.  There is some shade but Florida heat is too much and you won't get to take advantage of all that there is to do.

We spent 2 days in ONP in mid July: 1 at Rialto Beach and the Hoh Rainforest and the other at Hurricane Ridge, all while staying in Port Angeles. I would skip the Rainforest next time and visit Crescent Lake because the Rainforest wasn't too impressive for someone who sees ferns and mossy trees all the time in Florida.
ONP is known for it's varied regions. Certain parts are very distant and can only be reached one day at a time. Recommend you research extensively ahead of time so you don't waste all your days driving. Lake Crescent area with Marymere Falls is a nice single day trip. Hurricane Ridge gets packed in the summer afternoon so be prepared that you might just have to wait before you can drive up there. Victoria is a nice day trip from Port Angeles too

The grounds are gorgeous.  You have the option of a guided tour or a self led audio tour.  I agree with the other people and recommend the self led tour for a few reasons.  First it's go at your own pace.  My wife and I were able to stay at certain spots longer if we like it.  Two it's your own timeline versus having to start on the hour.  Third it's cheaper.  Overall we enjoyed the time here learning about these two men.  For those that don't know you don't actually go inside the house but can side the inside of various rooms through clear plexiglass.  There's some shade but it's outside go earlier in the morning if possible.  I would say 2 hours is how long to expect to spend here going at a leisurely pace through all the audio stops.

I've heard about Monticello before but never really thought of going.  After enough people recommended it, my wife and I finally went and I'm glad we did.  Recommend to try and go early in the morning because it does get hot during the summer.  Make sure you do the slave tour which provided good information, and if interested, the gardens tour.  Both tours are included in the price of admission.  There is a museum with a video which we did not get to see.  We walked the short walk to graveyard and then all the way back to the entrance.  Expect to spend about 4 to 5 hours to get the full experience.  The grounds are beautiful and people super nice, it's worth the price and you'll learn some history (good and bad) about Mr. Jefferson.

Every one of the staff we met here seemed so happy to be working here.  It's the only Florida State Park with no cost for an entry fee.  We weren't planning on going here but we went here while we waited for our boat tour.  I'm glad we did.  This park has a ton to do.  There is hiking trails, camping, fishing, bikes for rental, and canoeing for rental.  The main trail is nice wide and well marked out path, it's easy and don't need hiking boots or anything.  A note to buy food ahead of time as there's not much there or nearby if you plan to stay for a bit.  Overall a great park and worth the visit.  We didn't experience too many mosquitos but still recommend bug spray and going early

So the Alamo itself is free but the audio tour really is worth the extra $12/person.  I knew nothing about the Alamo when I came and after about the 9th audio stop I was starting to put the pieces together.  In the back courtyard there is a nice 20 minute video which will help with getting the timeline and finally the exhibits in the long barracks help you to see how the Alamo shaped not only Texas but the United States and Mexico.  An absolute must when visiting San Antonio.  Plan for about 3 hours to really soak up all the history.

If physically able you have to do this trail. It is very strenuous both down and up and make sure you have good hiking sticks. It's not too long but in the summer you will be hot when you get to the bottom (and I'm from Florida!). Bring a change of clothes and towel and be adventurous and jump in. People jump from the high rocks but you can also jump in from a lower area. You'll warm up shortly after you get out. The 3 bathrooms at the bottom are pit toilets. When you head back up you'll be happy to be a little wet.

This is the iconic and most well known waterfall in Oregon.  Because of that it is also PACKED on weekends and holidays.  If you are heading here in the summer go early in the morning.  Parking is terrible and there are so many people, I felt like I was at Disney.  That said, it is a huge and gorgeous waterfall.  The trail to the top is very strenuous and not for the faint of heart.  Even if you don't go all the way to the top (we didn't), go at least a little beyond the bridge for some great views.

Staying near the airport, I was looking for any nearby parks and this is one.  It's a very nice park (better than the pictures on Google maps would have you believe).  It's open sunrise to sunset with lots of parking and free.  Great place to watch the sunset by the bay.  The park has a kids playground, grills, pavilions, benches, "beaches", even disc golf.  If staying at the airport you will have to drive or Uber over because it's too far to walk, but if you get a chance I would check it out.

This is a great trail, with hiking for all sorts of skills, but it is generally steep.  There is a fire road that is pretty well paved and wide.  There on the west side is an off road type hiking trail where some sort of boots are recommended.  The trails all intersect so I recommend taking a picture of the map when you start because you'll have no cell service and you don't want to be hiking in endless loops.  Plenty of people on the trail but parking is limited for sure and they do ticket

We were staying near the airport and made the trek to Ballard Locks via public transit as we dropped off our rental early. It was an easy Metro, bus, and walk there which was half the fun! You can spend maybe 1-2 hours here (or longer if you love boats) just watching the boats pass through the locks. Don't forget to stop by the visitor center and watch the movie so you can gain some insight on to why and how they were created. Also check out the salmon ladder down below. All for FREE
likes: On-site Activities: Boat watching, Salmon ladder

reviews_attraction.text: Visited Mt. Rainier NP in mid July. It was rainy both days and wildflowers were not in bloom yet. Despite that, it is a gorgeous park. We did a few trails and saw bits and pieces of the Mountain. It is one of the more stunning parks even in the rain. Would recommend multiple days as getting from one location to another is lengthy. Also the weather is a variable. Both days the forecast was supposedly clear and both days it was rainy and overcast.

Great side trip in the Columbia River Valley. It did not have very many people when we visited on the day after July 4th holiday. It made it great for just driving right near the river and spending a half hour here. Great place to relax, picnic, or if you are adventurous wind surf. $5 entrance fee was well worth it.  I did not notice it being too noisy as some people complained.  I could have stayed here hours admiring the sights.

Some gorgeous views at the north of the park. Really cool black stone beach south of the lighthouse. Be very careful near the tide pools. I slipped and really hurt myself. There's a trail to the top of a little mound which we didn't do, but probably had great views. Only pit toilets here with no water but awesome. Skip the visitor center and head to parking near the light house first.

This fall is not too impressive but it is nice. The most difficult part is finding parking because there are only about 10 spots in the immediate vicinity. On a rainy or cloudy day it's a good idea however if you are headed up to Paradise early hit this on your way back out of the park. Also bring a hiking stick it's steep and can be slippery when wet.

This is a cool place to spend about 2 hours. Visited here after visiting Crater Lake so the water was not as beautiful, but it was neat to see all the impacts of a volcanic explosion. This is also a good place if you want to see a lot, but not have to do a lot of hiking. We drove to multiple stops and then just took less than 0.5mi round trip hikes.

Went on a Friday afternoon and it was a pleasant time walking seeing the natural beauty mixed with man made architecture.  We ate around 3pm and had no trouble getting a table right on the water.  However we came back at night and it was packed!  Be prepared.  We missed the boat tour which everyone recommends, maybe next time.

This is a short very easy loop hike.  Like some of the other trails here it shows it's just a short loop but some other trail intersects with it so make sure you look at the trail map before departing so you don't end up on a longer trail.  It was an okay trail, but nothing you couldn't see from the parking lot.

If you have never seen the after effects of a volcano this will show you. It is not pretty but quite stunning. Pictures don't do justice to the desolate feel that exists. You can walk as far as you want in the area. We walked just a short ways in and enjoyed it. Spent maybe 30 minutes here.

Easy to get to and from Victoria via the Coho Ferry. Ride was smooth and had a few options for food purchase. Plenty of room to find a decent seat. Can't beat the price if you walk on (vice bring a car). You can bring food just make sure it's prepackaged! No fruits allowed

All the talk in St. Augustine is about Castillo de San Marcos, but don't forget about this free fort.  A nice little ferry ride and a half hour at the fort is worth a visit.  There is a quarter mile boardwalk nature trail too with some history to learn as well.

Pretty intense drive up but nice overlooks.  Spend about 10 to 15 minutes.  Go to the Big Obsidian Flow first and get an idea what it's like from the ground then go up to the overlook and see from an eagle's eye viewpoint what you just saw down there.

Beautiful free park in the Museum District.  Just a nice place to relax for a few hours, no activities just sitting and seeing the garden there is a rose garden and I don't know which months the roses bloom but they were beautiful in mid-November!

Gotta plan it right for high and low tide for the full effect.  Watch out for the water when it hits!  You'll get wet.  You can walk from the Cape Perpetua visitor center if parking is full right by this place.

What else can be said about a visit to the Redwoods National and State Parks in California? It is definitely a must-do, especially since you will get a chance to experience and explore the largest trees on earth.

Walking through the groves of trees there is the extreme sound of silence. And it makes you almost think of Jurassic times.

Seeing the roots of these trees is just as impressive. They form elaborate patterns and shapes and can form unique shapes that you can show your face through (see photo)!

It is hard to imagine the size of many of these trees until you see them in person.

And even then, they can only be put into perspective when either a person or even a vehicle is placed next to one.

The picture with our car in it is taken in front of a single tree (Cal Barrel Trail). That is the massive size of its trunk. Unreal!

DOG OWNERS: I POSTED A PICTURE OF THE PARK RANGER APPROVED TRAILS THAT YOU CAN TAKE YOUR FURRY FAMILY ON.
We did Cal Barrel trail and it was phenomenal!

P.S. The Rangers are so friendly and amazing!

We just hiked Elk Mountain and it is a challenge of the body and will. It is straight up, start to finish.

**********
If you are looking for that hike that will challenge every fiber of you both physically and mentally, King’s Mountain is a great one. This is the second time I’ve hiked it and so knew what to expect which didn’t necessarily make it easier. I could just appreciate the true challenge that it is even more.

The main official sign  lists it as VERY DIFFICULT.....and it is. But It is also doable, just prepare with knowing your own abilities, the right type of shoes, plenty of water, a walking stick, and energy snacks. As you see in the video: A WALKING STICK IS A MUST. Just a note: my Apple Watch measured the distance from the parking lot to the summit as 2.75 miles with an elevation gain of 2400 feet. NOTE: When you pass the wooden picnic table you are 0.17 miles to the summit. On clear days you can see Mount Hood (see photo). Take the challenge! I give the fullest credit to those who have hiked it in snow, etc.!

At over 27-Acres, Tualatin Community Park is a fantastic local park.

The three phenomenal cities of Durham, Tigard, and Tualatin have worked together to create a local recreational network that includes walking, biking, jogging trails as well as great places to walk your furry family including off-leash parks.
And boat ramps for SUP Boards and Kayaks.

Accordingly, there are multiple options for parking to reach the park.

The Community Park has a phenomenal skate park as well as sports fields & courts, playground, boat ramp, and great off-leash dog park.

The meandering trail along the Tualatin River is a fantastic way to step away and get back to nature.

Overall it’s part of an incredible local Tri-City resource.

My family and I visited Battery Point Lighthouse during part of our summer road trip from Tigard, Oregon down and around through Northern California.

Our children really wanted to see the lighthouse so we ventured over, a close drive from our motel (Quality Inn & Suites, which I have also reviewed).

We really lucked out and found parking directly in front. It is very easy to get to by using Google Maps. The whole area is very rustic and scenic.

NOTE FOR DOG OWNERS: Dogs are not allowed on the grounds so we had to make it a very quick trip. Fortunately it was really cloudy and cool that day.

Definitely worth a visit for the history and the views.

Excellent learning and nature preservation reserve that focuses on the local ecology while stressing the ability and importance of mankind and nature living in harmony.

There are countless wonderful animals that you can interact with while being able to hold or touch many of them. In the process you learn about their natural abilities and how they fit into the ecosystem.

We were able to hold a huge snake for a family photo as well as pet wolves and feed pigs with baby bottles of milk.

This is truly a hands-on one of a kind experience that is perfect for anyone of any age. Hopefully more parts of the country will follow suit.

Bridal Veil Falls at the right time of day is an easy drive from our home in Tigard, OR. Once you get there you will be overwhelmed by several things:
1. The 1000 shades of Green that exists there.
2. The plentiful amount of breathtaking waterfalls, some of which are a fairly short walk to get to.
3. All of the vistas to stop and meditate on the serene beauty and listen to the power of the water as it flows over the Falls.
4. And it is a great place to bring and bond with the family, so close to the Metro area. There are always others around to ask for that group family photo.

It’s a wonderful gem so close to home.

Bridal Veil Falls at the right time of day is an easy drive from our home in Tigard, OR. Once you get there you will be overwhelmed by several things:
1. The 1000 shades of Green that exists there.
2. The plentiful amount of breathtaking waterfalls, some of which are a fairly short walk to get to.
3. All of the vistas to stop and meditate on the serene beauty and listen to the power of the water as it flows over the Falls.
4. And it is a great place to bring and bond with the family, so close to the Metro area. There are always others around to ask for that group family photo.

It’s a wonderful gem so close to home.

Looking for good local hikes my wife and I decided to try the Four T Trail. We parked at Council Crest Park and started out from there.

Not being familiar with the Four T we chatted along the way with various passers-by. And so hiked the “urban shortcut” across the streets on the way down. This was an interesting and unique experience.

We stopped at Marquam Nature Park which is a really nice park to visit. And then we hiked back along the forested Marquam Trail and back to our starting point.

Overall it was a fun time. But if you read the Four T sign, there is a lot more involved and sounds like it would be fun.

Since moving to Tigard a few years ago, my family and I have been making day-trips to the White River West Sno-Park, OR-35 at Mount Hood, OR 97041.

We have gone for hikes different times of the year but we especially like to go during Winter.

This year in fact, thus far, has definitely been the snowiest we have encountered the Park!

Along side the upper paths I would occasionally step into a 1-2 foot snow hole, showing just how much fresh powder it received.

There are ample places to sled and tube for the kids and the whole family.

Plus our furry family acts like a pup in the fresh snow!

Horsetooth Mountain, Horsetooth Reservoir, and Horsetooth Rock are the iconic landmarks standing in prominent view in the Foothills just west of Fort Collins.

It makes for a wonderful area to explore nature and see some fantastic beauty.
Camping sites are available to rent.
And the lake makes for a lot of fun in the heat of summer.

By boat, kayak, SUP, etc. it is a great place to enjoy the water.
And for a true mental & physical challenge the area provides for some rigorous routes on bike.

The north end of it adjoins Lory State Park which is definitely worth checking out as well.

It’s just 90 minutes away from the Portland area and everyone there is so incredibly friendly.

Face coverings are currently required.

At more than 2150-Acres of skiable terrain, Mount Hood Meadows definitely offers a great variety for all skill levels.
It’s easy to enjoy a solid day of skiing or boarding.

It was super-fun to be involved with my daughter’s high school ski team as they competed in downhill & slalom!

They offer lessons & rentals and even post-season purchase of equipment.

We caught a couple of days of fresh powder and it was pure gold!

LET IT SNOW!!!! ❄️

My family and I really enjoy Barkland Dog Park and our dogs love it too. What a great local dog park serving Parkland.

Any given day you can meet many friendly people and large varieties of different dog breeds.

It is spacious, wonderfully designed, has nice paths to stroll, has a couple of drinking fountains for the dogs, and has plenty of shaded areas.

There is a nice dog wash station in between the large dog side and small dog side which makes it convenient to rinse off any mud if need be.

Our Vizsla would sometimes obsess in trying to find the lizards in the trees!
likes: Separate areas for large and small dogs

reviews_attraction.text:
These iconic row-homes sit directly across the street from Alamo Square Park and were some of the few things left standing after the fire of 1906.
And they were the location of the T.V. Series Full House and the movie Mrs. Doubtfire.

If you’re driving, you may have to look carefully for a spot. But you just might be able to hop out of your car just long enough to take some amazing photos!

There are some phenomenal panoramic views of the amazing city of San Francisco from the area too.

There are some area-restrictions on tour-buses and large vans.

We are so lucky living in an area that has such magnificent bridges!
Portland is definitely unique and wonderful.

Crossing the Willamette River, St. Johns Bridge stands tall with the highest boat clearance at 205 feet. It’s two Gothic Towers, that influenced the naming of adjacent Cathedral Park, stand at 400 feet!

Either side of the River has great areas to visit, whether it is Cathedral Park or Forest Park.

It is only one of three suspension bridges in Oregon.

It is unmistakable, very beautiful, and quite stunning to see.

Durham City Park is a fantastic local park that is part of a Tri-City Park system.

The three phenomenal cities of Durham, Tigard, and Tualatin have worked together to create a local recreational network that includes walking, biking, jogging trails; picnic areas, as well as great places to walk your furry family including off-leash parks.
And boat ramps for SUP Boards, Kayaks, swimming, etc.

There are multiple options for parking to reach the park.
The most direct is to take to SW Rivendell Dr off of SW Upper Boones Ferry Rd.

We are so lucky living in an area that has such magnificent bridges! Portland is definitely unique and wonderful.

Crossing the Willamette River, Steel Bridge  carries some amazing distinctions. Since it carries almost all types of traffic, I think the biggest distinction is that it is one of the most multimodal bridges in the world! Which certainly fits with Portland being such an eco-conscious City.

And it is the only double-deck bridge with independent lifts in the world!

And overall it is very unique looking.

Portland is definitely the City of Bridges and something that I truly appreciate since my family and I lived far from any bridges while living a long time in Colorado.

I crossed the Fremont Bridge while heading to Sea-Tac for weekend work training.
It carries I-405 over the Willamette River.

It feels tight while driving over it, but if you are a passenger you can certainly catch some some amazing glimpses of Portland.

What is really cool is that it is the second longest tied-arch bridge in the world!

ECSP has great trails to hike and it’s a great place to bring dogs (must be on leash) and to let the kids explore some caves.

No doubt our favorite time of year to visit is in the Fall when you can catch the Autumn colors starting to shine.
And it’s not too far to get to the Peak-to-Peak Highway from here.

You can even see some reds dapped in with the standard Aspen gold/yellow.

This is a fantastic place for the whole family plus it’s close to Boulder which is always a fun city to visit.

Excellent conversation center focused on local ecology, especially in understanding and aiding Sea Turtles.

Pretty amazing to see all of the different hatchery rooms and rehabilitation rooms and all of the hard work that goes into it.

Great boardwalks meander through forest-like areas. And eventually lead to an open area with beautiful views (photos).

Cool aquarium in the entrance building as well as a fun gift shop. Useful poster on Florida’s venomous snakes for anyone interested!

Cooper Mountain Nature Park is a local park nestled between Beaverton and Tigard. At 230 Acres it offers three and one half miles of trails.

Dogs are not allowed.

The trails are very well maintained and with easy and gradual elevation making them ideal for most.

There are some great views of the Tualatin River Valley in the distance.

The day we went there was decent patches of frost and fog in the lower levels and this is evident in the photo I took of the deer.

BLSP is a fantastic outdoors-recreation area sitting in Loveland right near the border with Fort Collins.
There are beautiful views of Long’s Peak in the background.

There is just about something here for everyone.
There’s a beach & swimming area, areas for boating, fishing, camping, picnicking, hiking, etc.

And all types of powered watercraft are allowed.
I’ve spent many a summer enjoying jet skis with family and friends.

It’s a true gem in Northern Colorado!

How much better does it get???!!! To be able to allow your 4-legged best friend to frolic, splash, and play in wonderful warm waves and on a vast soft-sanded beach!

Either alone or with you by his/her side! Well numbered markers designate the dog beach boundaries. And the many times we went, the Rangers were nothing but friendly, helpful, and professional.

If you are in or going to be in that area you have to take your dog here. You won’t be disappointed!

What a great park! Centrally located in the Portland Metro area and very easy to get to from all directions.

It was easy for us to get here from Tigard.
And it is perfect to bring our furry family.

There are many different trails to take. There is one with a suspension bridge that looks fantastic but I’m thinking my dogs might be skittish to walk on it.

The Visitors Center is closed due to the pandemic.

Face coverings and social-distancing is ideal.

Great downtown area to walk, window shop, and buy cool and unique things. Plus a lot of great eateries offering something for everyone. Bend, OR is 100% dog friendly and many shops have water bowls out for our furry family! 🐶 Also, it is a really easy walk to Drake Park which sits right at the Deschutes River and Mirror Pond, which offers natural beauty (see photo). DOWNTOWN BEND IS A MUST DO!!!

Drake Park is a very comfortable and easy walk from Downtown Bend and should definitely be checked out.

It is abundant with natural beauty and offers a chance to see families of ducks and geese.

There are great “photo ops” here with the majestic Mount Bachelor rising in the background. Especially with Mirror Pond.

Great for the whole family, furry family included.

Beautiful and amazing art! People from all over Earth come to visit the Art Institute of Chicago to gaze at the art! Students get discounts with school/college ID. Illinois residents get free days throughout the year with proof of residency. Check the Art Institute's website for free days.

As a courtesy to visiting guests:

You are NOT obligated to give any money to anyone standing outside of the museum. They are not affiliated with the Art Institute of Chicago.

If you want to give money to people in front of the Art Institute, that is entirely your right. I have tipped the drummers on several occasions. I even included them in my YouTube video, "Ketchup Bottle Challenge Chicago Featuring Matthew Hussey."
I really do like those guys!

But understand that there are other individuals standing on the sidewalk who claim they are in need of financial assistance but are not being entirely honest. Again, it's your money & you can choose to do whatever you want with it. I'm just asking everyone to please be cautious. Thank you!

Honestly, I didn't know if the Snow White Cottages were available for public view or if I was trespassing. There's a gate but it wasn't locked, it was only closed. I let myself in and started taking pictures only to notice that people actually LIVE in the Snow White Cottages.

I tried to be respectful and as quiet as possible to not disturb anyone (and to not get LAPD called on me in case I was trespassing). I took my pictures, let myself out, and closed the gate- that was it!

The Snow White Cottages is a really small area so you can see them, take pictures, and leave in under 5 minutes. Again, I'm not sure if it's open to the public so cross the gate at your own risk.

*Don't say that you read my review and I recommended that you go there. People live there so treat the place as you would ANY place of respect. If the residents call the cops- that's on you! Don't call me to bail you out because I'm going to pretend that I don't have any money.

Head's up: No photography allowed in the home. Personally, that defeats the purpose of my visit, if I can't take photos of places I've visited in my life. But you can take photos of the outside of the house and get up close to the windows and take photos of the living room as you stand on the porch. There's also a visitor center, where photos ARE allowed and you can learn about Elwood's history.

Staff was pretty nice. They greeted me & told me where the restrooms are located & then they went back to work in their office. They just let me walk through the visitor center like a ghost walking through the halls. That's fine by me! I rather be a ghost than have staff drill me with questions like I have in other museums:

Where are you visiting from?
Where do you live?
How did you hear about us?
Have you visited our website?
Have you visited us before?
Where are you going after the museum?

I'm JUST passing through... Dang!

Beautifully preserved, historical Chicago landmark! The fountain is on view all year but the fountain is only operational during the warm seasons, usually end of April through mid-October. Chicago Police often patrols the area, keeping it safe for visitors.
At night, the fountain lights up and music plays in the immediate area. Again, this is only during the warm seasons. It's a nice place to just chill out. Please keep Chicago clean & utilize the garbage cans when visiting, thanks!

Quick Story: When I was little, I first saw Buckingham Fountain on the show "Married With Children" and told my dad that I wanted to move from Los Angeles and live in Chicago! He laughed at me and said, "Kid, you don't know what you're talking about!"  Several years later, after my time in the military, I stayed true to my childhood wish and moved to Illinois.

Who's laughing now?  ;)  LOL

I came here to watch The Great American Solar Eclipse. I loved it! There were many areas throughout the park where there were no street lights so that I could view the eclipse without light pollution. I'm glad I came here because Carbondale had light pollution and several people complained about the eclipse being clouded over in Carbondale.

Not at Giant City State Park! I had clear skies! I loved the eclipse! I was so thrilled, I shouted, "My life is complete!" at the amusement of fellow eclipse watchers! Afterwards, people hiked the trails or visited the restaurant to get out of the heat for a little while. The next solar eclipse is coming back through this area.

Makanda, Illinois: X marks the spot!

The museum is currently under renovation (as of 3/16/2018) but I still got to see the exhibits that are open. "Paper Gowns and Photography" was beautiful and the photos were thought provoking. "Freedom, Resistance, and the Journey to Equality" had historical artifacts on display and audio-visual historical clips that you can watch. One of the security guards, Mr. Hill, was present throughout the museum welcoming visitors and answering questions. I even got to speak to him about the racial challenges that other social groups have faced apart from African Americans. Go upstairs and watch Harold Washington. It's a life-like robotic representation of Harold Washington with moving arms and blinking eyes!

Great experience visiting the planetarium! You even get to touch a moon rock! There are exhibits that cost an addition from your entrance ticket but are well worth the price if you are interested in astronomy. Check out their website for current exhibits, events, and schedules before planning your visit.

Tip: Wear comfortable shoes. There's a restaurant with a beautiful view of Lake Michigan that's worth eating at for the experience. If you plan to see a solar eclipse in the near future, buy your eclipse glasses DIRECTLY from the planetarium, available at the gift shop. You risk buying fakes online as many people did with the solar eclipse last year.

Love! Free entrance but you do pay for parking. Staff is welcoming. Animals appear healthy and well looked after. Wear comfortable shoes. Check out their website for any special events.

* The website does mention free parking for the first 30 minutes, if you plan to make a quick stop. I don't know anyone who visits a zoo for 30 minutes but if you're just stopping by, you don't have to pay for the first 30 minutes. Also, the website says there is "free parking" nearby.

Folks, if you find a free parking spot around Lincoln Park, Harambe (the Cincinnati Zoo Gorilla) IS LOOKING OUT FOR YOU!!!

Paws up for Harambe! LOL!!

Your guess is as good as mine when it comes to describing what this sculpture is but use the base of this sculpture to slide down it! You have to slide down it- AT LEAST ONCE! Don't feel you're "too old" or "too mature" because that mentality ages you and robs you of living your life to the fullest! And while you're there, go check out the eternal flame that honors troops! It's just feet away from the sculpture enclosed in a metal fence to keep people from stepping/falling into it.

* Don't mind the bums! They're always hanging out in downtown Chicago looking for people who are willing to give them money.

Gangster tour with a side of comedy.  You do not get off the bus during the tour, you remain seated inside the bus the entire time.  My advice, sit on the LEFT side (the driver side of the bus) so that you can get a good view of the bullet hole in the Holy Name Cathedral wall and a good view of the Biograph Theater.  This way, you can get good photos of the top 2 locations of the tour without heads/people in your way.

The tour guide was wrong about the Chicago fire being caused by a cow.  Even the Chicago History Museum has disproven that claim (check the museum's exhibit). Stop spreading fake news.

Park is open to the public. Many people with dogs were out walking their pets. There is even an area for kids to play on the swings and basketball courts. 4/5 because the restrooms were locked but I can imagine they were locked for safety reasons (i.e. to keep bums and addicts out).

If you are driving, make sure you are parked along the street where parking is allowed. There is a parking lot by the tennis courts where a permit is required to park your vehicle. Stay on the right side of the law to avoid getting parking violations or a boot on your tire. Boots can cost you $140+ to have them removed.

I came to Washington Park to see the Fountain of Time. While there's no water in the pool during the winter/spring, it gave me the advantage of stepping into the empty pool and walk right up to see the sculpture for closer photographs. Walk around the backside of the sculpture as you get to see more figures and expressive images on the back that you can't see from the front of the fountain.

* Remember to keep Chicago beautiful and place your trash in the garbage can and scoop after your pets.

Thanks for reading my review!

Love! Zoo features different animals but is not so large that you get tired of walking all day. Miller Park Zoo offers discounts to students and Veterans and even offers free days throughout the year. Miller Park Zoo offers events for children and families. Follow them on Facebook for prizes, like free movie passes and free hockey tickets, etc. I especially like that they just put a Free Library in the building with the tiger. I can pass on books that I've read to others in the community. It's a form of recycling.

I followed "Google Maps" on directions to this park but it didn't take me to the park. Instead, it took me to some apartment complex. I felt I was near the park, so I drove around to see if I could find my own way. Nope- I just kept going up & down streets, over the bridge, unable to find the park. I give 3 stars because Google didn't get me there. I'm sure it's a nice park. The other reviews say it is & I'm going to take their word for it.

Museum is well worth a visit but I will throw caution at anyone with a weak stomach.  The old OB/GYN medical tools were sick!  We've come a long way from devices that look to be more pain-inducing than pain-relieving!

As far as parking, I parked at the Chicago History Museum Parking lot and walked across Lincoln Park to get to the Surgical Museum (about 10 minute walk).  Show your school or military ID and get a discount on your ticket.

Been here on several occasions! Everything I've done here has been absolutely FREE- including the bus tour to Wisconsin to walk through Frank Lloyd Wright landmarks. Anywhere else, I would have been charged entrance fees, transportation fees, etc. The Chicago Cultural Center only asks that one arrive on time & give a courtesy call/e-mail if one can't make an event to allow another guest the opportunity to visit. CCC, I love you!

Can't do it all in 1 day. I would probably need a second day just to get to tour the museum and see everything- it's that huge! I especially liked that the day I visited, there was a band playing outside.  So while I had my sandwich and Coke from the little restaurant, I got to jam to some live music!

Kids, don't climb on the street lamps- security will yell at you.

Free 2-hour parking on the street. Museum offers guided tours (check website for schedule) or you can tour the museum on your own. Staff was welcoming and answered my questions. Worth a visit!

I also want to give a shout out to museum staff member Don- he provided me with information about local museums and local landmarks/attractions to visit.

Spent the afternoon viewing the Saturday Night Live exhibit. The staff was courteous and informative. The second floor had collectables from old shows and viewing areas with chairs to relax. Great way to get out of the heat this summer! Students receive discount on tickets with school/college ID.

Love! I came here to pass a Saturday afternoon and had a positive experience! It was FREE to enter the museum, the staff was courteous and answered my questions about the art work on display. The museum gift shop was beautiful and worth a look!

Thanks for reading my review!
¡Viva Mexico!

Free museum (donations appreciated). Exhibits rotate but you can check the website to see what is on display at the time of your planned visit. Air conditioned facility, friendly staff, and just a walk away from the Wabash Corridor to see huge murals. A+

The tours were OK. Be prepared, there's no food/drinks allowed once you leave the visitor center. You aren't even allowed to take a granola bar out of your purse to feed your child as you walk through the gardens. Just letting you know!

I walked here last year in August. It was a good place to take a walk. You can hear sea lions at a distance. Bring a camera and depending on the weather, you may need a sweater or light jacket because it does get breezy in the evenings.

Visited just before Halloween and got to see the trees as they were changing colors- beautiful! Take the tram ride, it's worth it for the information! You can also take yoga classes among the trees (check website for more information).
If you're in the area, it's worth a stop. It's a quick 5-minute stop. There are restrooms available on site, which is awesome because the next town isn't for miles.. LOL!

Great park nestle between Moro Bay and beach. Plenty of wild life all over this place. I got to see seals and sea otters. Lots of squirrels as pelicans in and around the area . Plenty of free parking and clean restrooms. Had a great time since there’s so much to see and do. Nearby restaurants and shopping will keep you busy. Enjoy and be respectful to all the wildlife. Please pick up all your trash and throw it in the trash can. Keep this place beautiful for all to enjoy.

Charming collage town. Plenty of free parking and public restrooms. So many shops and restaurants. Patios all over the streets so don’t worry it’s open here. Take your masks and hand sanitizer and you are good to go. The mission is closed but you can see it outside and enjoy the gardens all around it. Enjoy locale artists at the galleries and enjoy the San Louis obispo creek running through downtown.

Great pier off the Monterrey bay. We were able to see sea otters and seals . Great shopping and dining with great views of the bay. There’s plenty of parking near by and clean public restrooms. Best part is the charm of the locale people . Sunsets are spectacular and worth taking in.  Arches nearby with seals add to the nautical charm. I definitely enjoy coming here and will be returning for sure.

One of many iconic bridges along Carrillo beach highway . This roadside attraction offers great views of the surrounding cliffs and bluffs. The golden coast does not disappoint. Couldn’t get enough of the great views of the stunning coast line. Definitely a must see but do use caution as the cliffs do give way. Stay at least 4 feet distance from the edge . Parking is limited so get here early.

During the week is free to come do enjoy it Monday through Friday . Plenty of parking and clean restrooms. Great place to picnic or walk your dog. Feed the ducks or just enjoy the outdoors . Hiking trails with awesome views of the city also make this place worth the trip.

City park located south west of the downtown. Accessible from expo train line . Across the the street from USC. Lots of museums and venues located here. Rose Garden , Natural History Museum , Memorial Colosseum and California Science Center to name a few.

It’s a feast for the eyes for sure. Lots of different exhibits and plenty to learn from. IMAX theater with knowledgeable movies is a plus. King Tut exhibit is on currently but they have rotating exhibits year round.

Great vistas and just a perfect place to to cool down from the summer heat waves. Must say if yuh haven’t been I would highly recommend coming and enjoying nature. Plenty of parking and clean public restrooms.

Great park overlooking the bluffs. The trail to the ocean is nice. It’s a very rocky beach but looks great. Parking available along the street and picnic tables on top. Great to take in the scenic vistas.

It’s been a long time since I’ve been here. It’s a lot bigger than I remember so bring comfortable shoes your going to be walking for while. Special exhibits year round. Definitely a feast for the eyes.
Massive museum so bring comfortable shoes and energy. Plenty of places to grab a bite and also clean restrooms around. Museum also has free wifi and maps to get around this labyrinth.
Massive park. Great place to be if board of quarantine. So many fields to try something . Basketball, baseball, tennis, softball, soccer and volleyball all are first come first base
Great winery with amazing grounds . The peacocks that are all over are stunning. Not only are the wines great but there’s great art works here to buy. Left with three bags of goods.
You can go upstairs to the top floor when they are open . The observation deck isn’t very highly but it offers great view of the Los Angeles Skyline and grand park views as well.
Very interesting current exhibit on display. Great location in downtown with great rooftop views of the city. Your entrance fee also gets you into the sculpture gardens.
Great place to visit and enjoy the panoramic views on this peninsula. Plenty of open space and parking. Several landmarks to check out all walking distance from here .
Great exhibits and had plenty of different types of paintings . Great location with nice views of the state capital. Parking free with student ID.
Loved our late afternoon stroll here. It’s was peaceful and serene. Very scenic and not overly crowded. It’s not far from the boardwalk either.
Venice Beach is ready for Saint  Patricks Day. Lots of pubs are having special events this weekend get here early parking will be an issue.
This building and nearby buildings are phenomenal. It's like going back in time when detail and passionate architecture was being built.
What a unique and pleasant place to come visit. It has several to choose from all great. I highly recommend taking a look for yourself.
Glad I came. It was a treat to be here in autumn. Great location and very educational. There’s a movie Night coming up for Halloween.
Going in a weekday is much better. They have all kinds of cars. Movie cars , racing cars , vintage cars luxury cars and sports cars.
Sunday’s the museum is free to all. Has great exhibits and the gift shop is a must. Great location with plenty of parking near by.
Enjoyed our tour of the behind the scenes of the media giant. Lots of places to take pictures and great locations available.

Awesome little hidden gem most people don't know about. It has two spots you can park. The smaller one which is just two or three spaces gives you access to the little board trail and also takes you to a longer hike to the Eagle Crest trail. The bigger parking lot which is just up the road a fee yards more is where I prefer to park. You then have a less then a mile hike to some amazing views of Eagle Creek. That path consist of two piers that are rarely used but give you great views. It also gives you access to the board walk trail which leads to the Eagle Crest hiking area.

I just happen to have a job in Paducah which is across the river and seen this advertised and thought I check it out. Glad I did, the statue is pretty unique because where else do you see a giant superhero in the middle of a small town square. And the museum/gift shop is a great add in bonus. It has lots of goodies to buy for your kiddos and the museum is kinda run down looking a bit but still well worth checking out all the  Superman collectables.

Way bigger then I thought. The beach area gives you great views of the lake and is a pretty nice spot to have a picnic. The trails are nice and laid out so you won't get lost and they have differnt levels so you can go from easy to hard hikes. The cemetery was a pretty interesting site. Not many parks have a cemetery right smack in the middle of it. I highly recommend checking this place out if your into the great outdoors

This is by far one of my favorite nature areas to visit when in the New Orleans area. It has rows of beautiful and very big cypress trees. One in particular that is massive and is well worth it if your into photography. It also has the only sand beach I know of in the New Orleans area.  It gives you amazing views of Lake Pontetrain and has a few trails you can walk on to get a view of some of the wild life.

This place is amazing! You'll get lost for hours into all the different videos and displays they offer throughout the museum. Way bigger and much more in detail on each major event of the war then I thought which was a plenty surprise. I took my kids 11 and 15 and even they loved it so great place for the family.

Took my sons there and had an amazing time. Went during the fall when they had the field maze which I thought was really done well. Beautiful trails to walk on and the employees that worked there were really nice. They went out of their way to be educational and fun at the same time to my kids.

This place is really amazing. The boardwalks make it truly unique for Indiana and also it's a beautiful walk that let's you see areas you normally don't hike through. The viewing areas are worth hanging out at and taking in the wild life. Any level of walker or hiker would be ok on this path.

This place is a bit out there by itself but I love that. You can't access the inside but you can still roam around the outer parts including a few old bunkers that are underground. Also gives you stunning views of the water. Since it's a bit out by itself, it's normally never busy.

Beautiful place and much bigger of a place then it gets credit for. The trails are amazing and the sights will surprise you how beautiful they are. From the old saw mill, to the playgrounds, to the great rock walls, and Cliffside over looks. This place truly has it all.
