I have a special love for this park since I've gone to it since I was a kid. It's a bit worn down and people tend not to pick up after themselves but it have a lot of great qualities to it. Has a park, two little hiking trails, and plenty of areas on the lake go fish.

Over the years they have really developed this park into a great place for the local kids to go to. It has a good size splash pad and the playground is really unique. It also has a few paved walking trails. Good for kids of all ages.

To the suspension and covered bridges and to the trails that weave through the ravines. This is one of Indiana's most popular spots. You can spend a whole day out here. My personal favorite is the punch bowl, it's a must see.

I'll admit the price scares a lot of people away but once you get inside you'll see why it's a bit pricey. So much to do and see that you can spend all day here exploring the various displays. The staff is super friendly

I thought it was a bit odd having to walk across a field in order to access it. The Prairie part had a bit high grass on the trails but other then that the trails weren't to bad. It's a bit bigger then you would think.

Takes a bit of a hike to get to but well worth it. Has a few parts that are kinda rough so I wouldn't advise bringing kids or pets. Devils backbone is really unique but use caution crossing it and enjoy the view.
I wasn't able to take the tour but still interesting to see where Indiana got it start from. The building sits in the middle of Corydon so you'll have plenty to walk around and check out.
I hate to rate it so low because it does have some really beautiful spots. But the main trail was a bit high and they didn't have any maps or fact sheets about what the area was about.
Wonderful place, very friendly and knowledgeable staff. A lot of pieces from local artists. Not the biggest place but still very much worth checking out. Admission is free.
The trails are well marked and nicely done. None are very difficult so very kid friendly. Gives you great views of the river and also access to the Rail Trail.
It doesn't look like it's much of a hike but the trails are a bit longer then expected. I enjoyed how you could walk up to the river at a few different spots.
Nature center, beautiful trails, playgrounds, and even some pretty cool structures. This park packs a lot into it. Great place to take your kids.
Has everything that you would be looking for. Great parks for the kids to play at and long paved trails to walk or ride your bikes on.
Kinda a hidden place. Not many people know about it so it never gets to busy. Really nice trails and a nice lake to fish off of.
Great little place to visit when in the LA waterfront area. It host all type of cool little ocean creatures.
Truly special and one if a kind. A place to take your kids each year to admire the beauty of circle.

This is got to be the most beautiful water fall near boulder Ut. Beautiful scenic hike 3hr round trip, ofcourse you can do it faster, but we were amazed and kept stoping for pictures and videos but the hike is definitely worth the walk up there for the waterfall and beach is simply breathless. I recommend early morning hike if your here during the summer, by 9:30am the heat is already strong. Lots of water and maybe some snacks for the hike. The water is cold but its worth to dip in after the hot and long hike, you will feel very refreshed, the blueish water area close to the waterfall is the deepest maybe 9 to 11 feet deep or something like that.
There are clean restrooms at the parking lot, water and picnic areas are available, there are also 1st come 1st served camping spots, some big enough for rv's  no hook ups and others for tent only 15$ per night with 2pm checkout. #1 and #2 are the biggest with more tree shade but only suitable for tents, there is also the creek near the parking area to dip your self in.

Your Welcome.

This is one of the Best parks i've been to, "an oasis" is the only word to describe it, beautiful panorama with sandy beach area to soak in the water which by the way had the perfect temperature for the summer heat,fishing,kayaking, boating and swiming. BBQ on your own propane grill. No open fires or charcoal use during the time we were there as the Fire Danger was Very High. Camping area and RV is available but plan ahead because this place packs up on weekends and holidays. Watercraft rentals are also available and the bathrooms were clean with flush toilets, so no ditch pot and smelling others peoples happy💩🤢😒.
I highly recommend it here for camping and day use its worth it.
dislikes: No open fires or charcoal use

reviews_attraction.text: We stayed at Indian Bay Campground, almost all of the camp sites are great, but the best ones are the ones near the shore with a spectacular view and quick access to the beach area some are big enough for rv's and others for tents only, no hook ups at this campground, vault restrooms that were pretty clean. Fishing, paddle boarding and all your other water sports are sure to be fun here. The only issue was the trash bins were overfilled and trash scattered around the camp grounds, maintenance can do a better job at this and so can we, pick up after yourself and keep this place as nice as it naturally is.

Here on the last days of Summer with a Spectacular view of surrounding mountains.
Very very nice park with multiple gazebos picnic tables and BBQ grills, beautiful green grass with scattered trees all around and a very nice sidewalk that goes around the park for an evening stroll, this park is very well maintained right next to the park is the provo river, but you cant really see it as it hides downhill from your view, there is also access to the provo river bike road and if you hike up hill next to the parking lot' you will find another dirt road than can be used for hiking or bike riding.

This park is pretty nice, picnic area right next to the beach are nice. Not too many camp sites maybe like 11 or so and it's 1st come 1st serve. Bring your own propane grill during the summer, this weekend we were there the Fire Danger was High so no open fires or charcoal use. The water temp was good, about 76 so it was perfect for a soak for the heat was at 106. Boating, kayaking and fishing are perfect here.

Very nice scenic drive heading there, many camp spots to stay in. The Devils trail is paved and very short, easy trail with a very great beautiful view of the mountains and standing rocks. A few picnic tables and restrooms at the entrance. Nice place to relax with the family. A small creeck runs down from the montains no fee to visit here.

We were here for the 4th of july weekend, it is a very nice big lake, picnic areas and a beach area and boat launch. Really refreshing water in the summer heat. It is very popular lake and can get very very crowded on summer holidays, to get a picnic area i would recommend getting there super early hours in the morning to beat the crowds.

This was a very cool experience, never been on a battle ship before but i can definetly appreciate everything about it and its history, had a nice day here with my family on the tour, this ship is massive and has different levels of tours, gift shop has a good souvenir variety and friendly staff. I recommend visiting the ship.

Very beautiful colors in the fall, pretty good decent size park for a day picnic with camping on the other side of the parking, picnic tables and 1 huge gazeebo can fit several family size party. Provo river right next to it, lots of matured trees with shade. View of mountains all around the park, perfect for a day trip.

This Cave is very nice just like the trail hiking up to the cave, very beautiful scenery and the cave itself is very awesome, highly recommended, and very inexpensive. a good meal before the hike might be a good idea,  water and maybe a light jacket or sweater. it's very cool inside. Very friendly guides. :)

This was a very relaxing and fun trip with my family, very nice scenic view along the whole way. And nice train attendants, including the cowboy robbers whom were nice enough to let us go after surrendering the duck, we will be back in summer for the full trip.

There a lot of activities in this area for the entire family..spent the day here and had so much fun..CornBellys, museum of ancient history, the movies theater...and the garden behind was a very nice walk, perfect for family pictures
December is the best time to visit for the Christmas lights decoration all around the temple square very very nice but can be very very cold. enjoy your late evening walk with a cup of hot chocolate.
Very cool and educational observatory, we spent all day here and was fun, they got a cafe' on the second lower level. parking can get very limited depending at what time you get there.
Very educational and interactive activities for the kids, it's free admission, but donations are appreciated. They even have a Beaver Dam, Sponsored by' The Beavers.
Beautiful Short Hike, awesome view, i can see why it was named Goose Neck, very scenic view, breathless landcape, easy short hike, did it with my sandals on.😎🙃
Wow...you must come here and take a dip in the nice cooool water...had fun with the family here. If u want a more warmer water then head the the beach side
This was very fun and very educational. Great for the family, the whole experience was great, i'v never seen so many sea fishes like this. RECOMMENDED.
Beautiful Water Fall, hiking trail is moderately easy, best time to go is during summer for you will be able to refresh your self after your long hike.
This is a very sophisticated museum, with a great variety of historic artifacts and ancient bones. Great learning and fun center for every age.
Nice park with a big pond, playground and volleyball court,you can see the frozen bubbles if you come at the right time during winter here.
It's a very big beautiful bell hanging under a very artistic traditional design, nice place for a walk and get a view of the ocean
Very Great trail takes you into the canyon, lots of cool climbers around and nice for an evening hike or morning jog. Very scenic
Ice fishing. Great place to go day picnic or camping, boat ramps and zip lines..perfect place to spend a day.
Friendly trail with view of the ocean, picnic  area ontop and trail ziz zags down to the beach. Very nice

Riverbank has lots of big boulders.  Water is so clean. We saw so many little fish. Lots of shallow areas for families. We think this crossing is better than Bridgeport Crossings, which is more famous.  There is a short but level hike from parking to various river access points.  A bit of a climb down but very manageable even while carrying a toddler.

The unpaved parking lot is small. When we arrived at 9.30am on an Aug weekday, there were plenty of parking. In fact that's when some folks seem to be leaving, perhaps overnight campers. But by the time we left at 11.30am, the lot was full and cars were parked on the dusty road before the bridge where the No Parking signs are.  The last few miles is narrow, bumpy and unpaved. Drive slowly - 2 way traffic.

This is a first rate park right behind the Mountain View Public Library.  As a mom, I love that there is NO play structure here and the kids have to use their imagination and remain in tune with nature.   The child-sized bronze statues by the library exit always have curious kids playing pretend or exploring around.  The gently undulating landscape, framed by curving foot paths, accented by beautiful old trees, invites exploration by kids all too eager to freely roam around while parents relax on picnic blankets have clear view of the little ones.

In the nicer months, there are frequently events here on the weekend, and of course, the popular Summer Concert Series (for preschoolers) run by the excellent Friends of Mt View Library.

Beautiful inside. A great building to introduce lower elementary kids to grandeur, architecture, and government. We didn't take the free tour because of the crowd. Walking around the various museum rooms, we chanced across a rare books display (great big beautiful old books), saw a vault with super thick doors, climbed up 3 tall flights of stairs and found the Senate and Assembly galleries. They were not in session so were quiet but still invokes a sense of awe.

They also have displays on the hallways highlighting each county in the state. Some are more well done than others and feature nice models of local attractions.

Afterwards, my 5 1/2 year old daughter mused at how beautiful the inside of the building was.

Everyone told us to visit this crossing of the South Yuba River. True that parking is aplenty,  it's shallow, and lots of easy access points for families.  However it was nowhere as spectacular as the other crossings. Maybe that's an Aug thing,  I don't know.  Did hear that Buttermilk Trail which starts here is a great spring wildflower hike.

We like that the South Yuba River Conservancy League was here for outreach about taking out your own trash. They were even collecting a little at the closest access points to the parking lot.

Also note that parking is $5 even by the road. The self registration station was out of envelopes and we had to drive/walk to the next parking lot where the Ranger kiosk is, to pay.

Called the city using the phone number on this page, a few days before visit, to check if water feature is on, specifically due to drought.   Was told it would be on sunrise to sunset.  So I organized a water playdate thinking summer is almost over.  After psyching up the kid, when we got to the park, there was a notice that says, due to drought, the water is off until further notice, due to the drought.  Come on, city employees!  Please check your fact.   Luckily my child did not throw a fit and happily played with other park feature.  Probably would have ruined the playdate if child was a year younger.

Saw big and little koi fish today.  Koi fish food available for a quarter from a machine -- don't feed them anything else!  Lovely park for watching water running and taking in the serene design.

But no picnicking allowed within this park.  You have to go outside and there are plenty of grass and picnic tables right behind this park.  Signs say to keep off grass, which is a bit sad given this is a park.  Might be a hassle with little ones as they just run anywhere.

Unfortunately the beautiful design is marred by cheap looking chain fences on the perimeter.

All the young families I know frequently come here because it is great for so many reasons.  It is good for all the reasons reviewed by others here.

Beware no food allowed at the play structure area.  A "ranger" actually patrols the park and will tell you to stop.  If picnicking with young kids, head first to the picnic tables by entering from the southern parking lot because they won't see the play structure first.

The reservation for the BBQ areas fill up quickly when registration opens.  Can fit large parties.
dislikes: BBQ area reservations fill up quickly

reviews_attraction.text:
Vast open space that makes you forget you are within a few minutes of densely populated Silicon Valley.   I've seen so many interesting natural things here on my various strolls, and the landscape is varied from area to area.

Most walking trails have little to no shade, and the grassy areas aren't quite suitable for picnicking (due to unevenness or geese poop).

Parents with strollers beware!  Lots of geese poop around the lake areas.  Use your baby carrier instead or be prepared to wash off when home.
dislikes: Geese poop in picnic and lake areas

reviews_attraction.text: There is a spot that is great for bouldering with kids who are 5 years old or older.  You enter through the Route 9 main entrance.  At the parking lot, there is a trail that heads left.  It zigzags uphill for a bit, not a long walk, and you get to these giant boulders that are between 1/2 a storey to 3 storey tall.  There are quite a few formations, some lower, some higher, some easier, some more challenging.  Our young kids loved it.  Forgot the trail name, but the formation is called, the Castle Rock.

We went for a hike this spring, to see the wildflowers.  We only did the trail that went from the parking lot, somewhat along the creek since we had little ones.  The elementary kids in our bigger group really enjoyed climbing up the slope, full of wildflower and knee-high grass.  Everyone enjoyed hopping across the rocks on the shallow creek, and the kids loved going into the shallow creek to play.  There were tadpoles, frogs and backswimmers!

Very well worth the time.  The mine shaft and metalsmithing stations are good. The ground is quite beautiful. Quite a few machinery from gold mining days.

Just a note that the Bourn family roleplay tour of the house is 1 hour long after a 15? min presentation. It's not suitable for younger children as it is mostly talk, very little walking, and not much of visual interest to them. It's a decent way for adults to experience life in 1905 though.
dislikes: Lack of visual interest for children

reviews_attraction.text:
One of my favorite parks for the kids.  "Mariposa"-themed, i.e. butterfly in Spanish, so look for all the butterfly motives.  Two play structures, one for young toddlers.  Sand-pit has built-in water saving faucet (spring-loaded) which is so fun for the kids.    Many sitting areas for adults, and picnic tables too.  Large lawn area for spreading out.

Parking is tricky as Mariposa Ave is narrow and some residents also park on the street.

If you have a toddler who is capable of climbing up the tall structures at the back, be aware of there is a rock climbing wall connecting both structures without side barrier.  This is a really fun wall for older kids, but once my active 2yo walked onto it without me realizing it existed (I was behind another structure chatting) and I barely reached up to hold her hand to walk across safely.

In the summer there's no sea lion in the caves. But the experience was still interesting to see a sea cave, the view of the walkway down was beautiful (which you can get for free elsewhere nearby). They marked our tickets as rain check for future visit although we won't be passing by for a long long time if ever again.
dislikes: Rain check not useful due to infrequent visits

reviews_attraction.text: Nice wooden play structures. A nice spinny thingy that is safe even for 3 years old. Flights coming down the slope next to parking lot it's pretty fun. The slides are not that long. There is a trail connected to this park that is pretty busy. Easy parking.

Always clean, well-run, lots of activities to entertain the little ones.
Amazing jungle gym climbing structure.
Just big enough to tire out everyone for a good nap afterwards!

The $80 annual parking pass is good at all City of San Jose Regional Parks.

Go during high tide.

We didn't see this geographic feature in action because of low tide. Still, the nice pathway down is easy for the kids and the igneous rocks harbor interesting tidepools. Reminds me of Point Lobos in California.

Gorgeous views.

Nice big park with great structures for kids.  Nice that the most advanced structure here is suitable for upper elementary kids; this is rarer in most parks around here.

Note there are two parking lots, and on-street parking all around.

I think this maybe a neighborhood park that you're supposed to walk to.  Couldn't find where to park,  not even on street, after circling around for 5 minutes.  It's next to an apartment complex and a residential neighborhood.

One of the best parks around.  New, unique, many different areas, some natural areas. Gets super duper crowded on Friday afternoon or after work due to the high density of apartments surrounding it.  Not very diverse at times.

Quite a few structures for kids in separate areas.  The one with the ramps is really fun for the very young.  It's big.

Generally the equipment seems dated, and the paint is peeling.
Tourist trap and not worth the $6 per car. Our 2014 Honda Odyssey (non Touring) minivan barely made it. Someone's Touring model didn't make it causing a traffic jam.
Just the right size. Lots of slopes, a little tricky with stroller.  We enjoyed the cable car and train a lot. Those have amazingly good views.
So near to Silicon Valley towns. So peaceful. Rather easy trails for walks. The little interpretive center is informative for all ages.
Majestic. Quite a few of the attractions are a bit of a drive off Hwy 101 so budget your time accordingly.

I echo most of the good things said about this historical and well-maintained place. The house tour and the exhibits at the Visitor Center are informative (the former was quite chatty, more on that in a bit). The overall narrative presents Jefferson as a noble and accomplished man who had his own share of shortcomings, especially with regard to his owning of slaves.

The two stars is for the prohibitively expensive ticket and what we got out of it. In hindsight, we could have booked the basic $23 tour covering the first floor of the house. But we didn't know better and booked the behind-the-scenes tour for $49, which really was just access to the upper two floors and basement of the house, sprinkled with chatty explanations from the docent to make the two-hour tour somehow worth it. Everything we saw and heard is covered in the official guidebook sold at the museum store. The place is not a castle in terms of size or grandeur and if not for Jefferson and his legacy, it would have been just another colonial house for a wealthy landowner. And finally, I don't understand why photos are prohibited, including photos of the natural surroundings taken from inside the house.

I feel that doubling the price so people can see the other parts of the house was a way to limit access to the upper floors, which I doubt are designed to handle the foot traffic they see today. Of course, they won't explicitly say that so they packaged it as a somehow magical experience worth the cost. After our visit, I strongly felt that they should not only limit access but discontinue upper floor tours altogether because the structure may weaken over time. They could build exact replicas off-site if they want visitors to experience what the floors were like back in the day.

We also missed out on visiting Jefferson's tomb as the shuttle didn't stop there on our way back to the Visitor Center. It may have been because it was rainy during our visit. The driver could have asked if we wanted to stop by, and we actually would because we came with umbrellas in anticipation of the day's weather.

We enjoyed the three hours we spent here. Start your visit at the Visitor Center, which has exhibits on the life and times of President Coolidge and his wife Grace. It's interesting that while the President spent most of his political career in Massachusetts and DC, he held a life-long affinity to Vermont, where he was born and raised.

From the Visitor Center, there are a few buildings to visit, all Coolidge-related. There's the small house where he was born, which is attached to the General Store. Next to it is the church he attended growing up. Across the street is the house where his family moved when he was four and interestingly, where he was sworn in by his father to be President, after the untimely death of President Harding. If you like cheeses, there's a store built by his father in the late 1800s that sells locally produced cheese at reasonable prices.

The President's gravesite is outside the historic site but is only a short drive away along Lynds Hill Road. Check it out if you have time.
likes: Facilities & Services: Visitor Center, informative displays

reviews_attraction.text:
The ferry ride from Manhattan took 15 minutes and a roundtrip ticket costs $2. Weekend ferries are available from Brooklyn. There are no admission fees in the island.

The entire island is car-free and walkable (expect at least 20,000 steps). Being mostly flat, it is also wheelchair accessible in most places. If you want a faster way to get around, bring your own bike or rent one for a fee at four different bike stations, three of them operated by Citi Bike. However, the bikes are not cheap and expect to pay upwards of $12 for an all-day use.

The island has plenty to offer. For scenic views and outdoor photography, head to Outlook Hill. For history and architecture, check out Fort Jay, Castle Williams, and Liggett Hall. For green spaces, there's Nolan Park, Parade Grounds, and Play Lawn. There is a restroom near Soissons Landing, where the ferry from Manhattan docks, and portable toilets around the island.

Definitely visit this site to see the tomb shared by Benjamin Franklin and his wife Deborah. I must say though that the experience was underwhelming mainly because the tomb does not stand out, calling into question what the people behind the 2017 restoration of the tomb were thinking when they planned the effort. I was told that maybe they wanted something modest but IMO, the plainness of the tomb does not really honor the Founding Father and his legacy. By contrast, the gravesite of Mr. Franklin's parents at the Granary Burying Ground in Boston is quite notable. As are the gravesites of two US Presidents at the Hollywood Cemetery in Richmond, Virginia. And those sites do not charge an admission fee the way they do here. Yes, the fee is minimal but with the prestige that this site brings, I wonder why they cannot raise the funds required for maintenance and upkeep.

Beautiful, well-preserved buildings, some dating from the Dutch colonial period.

It is free to walk around and take pictures of the buildings, but guided tours are not, although it's pay-as-you-wish every Friday. The guided tours, which can be booked at the Visitors' Center, allow guests to go inside the buildings and learn about their historic and cultural significance.

I like that they do not try to touch or renovate the buildings unnecessarily in order to preserve their authenticity.

My guide, Ain, was friendly, knowledgeable, and very patient with questions. I did not feel overwhelmed with information.

The place is a bit difficult to reach by public transportation from all the other New York City boroughs, including Manhattan, so those without a car might want to reconsider. From Manhattan, it takes at least an hour to reach the place by bus.

This National Park is the site of quite a few of Edison's actual workshops. The buildings are very well preserved and give the visitor a sense of the creativity that came from the mind of one of America's most prolific inventors and businessmen. The staff are very friendly and welcoming, and the large multi-story warehouse serves as both time capsule and museum. From his workshop and laboratory, Edison could build just about anything his mind could dream up!

Be sure to check out the replica of the Black Maria, an early movie studio that rotated to capture the light of the sun, as well as footage of some of the first movies ever made.

We visited on Memorial weekend so the place was busier than usual. The museum chronicles the history of Memorial Day in Waterloo, presents the key figures who started and promoted the event, and discusses what led to Waterloo receiving official recognition as the birthplace of Memorial Day. It was interesting to learn that various other places around the country vied for the same recognition, but that Waterloo provided the most compelling and comprehensive set of evidences. There are some related exhibits on the second floor, one on the subject of Vietnam War.

Admission is free. A visit should not last more than an hour.

Small museum with exhibits on Brooklyn’s geologic, industrial, and political history. The exhibits on Brooklyn’s 19th century waterfront warehouses were particularly interesting, especially since the museum is housed in one of those warehouses. The short film was also interesting as it tells the story of Brooklyn through the words of some of its most famous residents.

The museum staff are all very friendly and helpful, just like the ones on the main BHS museum in downtown Brooklyn. If you haven’t yet (and if you want more Brooklyn history), I suggest visiting that other museum too.

It’s not a museum although they do have small exhibits. You can come here to watch TV shows from years back and browse their comprehensive media archive. When we visited, we saw the first few episodes of the 1977 miniseries ‘Roots’, about the African slave trade. We also looked at vintage cigarette advertisements from as far back as the 1920s.

Admission is free but donations are welcome.

The next time you remember a rare media event or piece and wonder where you can see it, you know where to go.

I'll rate this 5 stars because I'm sure the bisons would be a real treat to see if (and that's a big IF) they are around. They weren't when we visited, but that's fine. I'm sure they were someplace safe and sound.

Be aware that this spot is in a nondescript location with no road signs to help you find it. If the bisons aren't around, chances are you'll miss the spot. There is a designated area for parking but it was snowed in when we visited.

A good place to start a visit to historic Batsto Village. Grab a map to help you navigate the place with ease. Be sure to also check the small museum within the Visitor Center to learn about the history of the once-thriving industrial community and the attractions on-site. There are restrooms and a souvenir store. Admission is free but donations are welcome.

Vehicular bridge with walk paths on both sides. Scenic views guaranteed! The bridge is named after the classic 1940s movie, "It's a Wonderful Life", a Christmas movie-watching staple. Interestingly, the movie wasn't filmed here and there is no definitive evidence that the bridge in the movie that was the site of an important scene was inspired by this one.

Small, well-maintained park surrounded by buildings of remarkable architecture. Like many parks in Manhattan, the terrain slopes in places, allowing for good cardio workouts. The park hosts the relocated home of Alexander Hamilton called Hamilton Grange, which also functions as a museum that showcases Hamilton's personal and political achievements.

We walked the entire length of the bridge, which took maybe 20 minutes. More than half that time was spent taking photos. The views are amazing, especially on the side of the bridge facing downtown Boston and MIT. Vehicular traffic can be intimidating and  the guardrails should be higher and sturdier to prevent accidents.

Stop by and learn about this sacred burial ground, unknown to many until the recent discovery of the site. Because the entire site is fenced off, visitors can only see and take pictures of the memorial from the street, and read the plaques with information about the history and significance of the place.

Beautiful place that can be really busy in the summer, especially on weekends. Hessian Lake and the Hudson River were particularly scenic. There's picnic spots, hiking trails, a pool that's popular with young families, and even historic sites. Come early for a convenient parking spot.

This is one of the best spots to enjoy sweeping views of New York City, including the famed skyline of Lower and Midtown Manhattan. Come between early and late afternoon for the best daytime photos. There is a public restroom here but I have not seen it in use.

Interesting modern building that stands out for being too thin, even by New York standards. Stayed for half an hour to visit their small but fascinating art gallery. Admission is free. The guy at the reception was pleasant and helpful.

Neat park in the center of Newark City that used to be a military training ground, hence its name. It has a few notable landmarks, such as a sculpture of JFK and an Episcopal church that is more than 200 years old.

Small but scenic park next to the Brooklyn Museum and Public Library. It is a bit elevated, allowing for good views of the vibrant street below. A good place to while away time and do people watching.
5 stars for the beautiful and eye catching building and the great photo-ops. Must be quite an experience to be here when decisions on landmark cases are announced.
Sobering place commemorating the native Brooklynites who fought and died in World War II. Great stop for those exploring Brooklyn’s historic district.
​Nice place to take photos of the famed Flatiron Building, a somewhat obscured Empire State Building, and the modest skyline.
A very busy place during the day. Great for people watching, if you enjoy that. Also, very easy to get to from the subway.
One word: photo-ops. Let loose, be creative, snap, share, repeat. You'll never know what new pose you could pull off.

Absolutely amazing tour. Our extraordinary guide, Alex, was engaging and personable. I really felt more connected to our great city and especially Over the Rhine, after this tour. Though centered around out cool history of craft beers, I learned things about Cincinnati I'll never forget. Alex had heaps of super cool information, accessible right off the top of his head. I'd give him, and this tour, 10 stars if I could. #teamalex #localguides

Awesome little park in front of city hall. Heavily wooded so it almost doesn't feel like you are right in the middle of Manhattan. There was auditory art playing, which was sort of weird, but that only lasts until early July. I suppose it did help drown out the street noise, making it a bit more tranquil. Pigeons and squirrels were totally cute, and with one guy feeding them all, there was a virtual army crowding him.

Beautiful church and grounds. Most of inside was closed off for repairs/renovations, but the chapel you could see is beautiful. Cemetery on the grounds is surreal, the history there is amazing. Saw graves for Revolutionary War veterans. Graves date from all centuries of our country (minus possibly the 20th and 21st).

Can't believe I haven't tracked this down until now. The story behind this monument is one of true Valor and heroism. The photo this is based off of is the most go famous war picture in history, and the monument dedicated to it doesn't fail to impress.

The scale is breath taking, it inspires awe.

So glad I paid to get the boat tour to take me here. So often seen in movies, tv, and media, but seeing Lady Liberty in person is indescribable. Every American (IMO) should see her at least once in their lifetime. What she represents is ageless, even if it is forgotten at times.

I do not have the proper words to describe the feeling that comes over you when walking though this museum. This is a history, a series of events, that should never be forgotten. I encourage everyone to experience this and take something meaningful from the lessons learned.

I wish we had shown up in time to spend the entire day on this. Great way to see entire city, I wanted to jump off at ALL 20(ish) stops and spend time. Also some nice free additions if you buy a pass (free boat tour was included)

Cheapest way to get to Ellis and Statue of Liberty. Long lines for ferry, but with them leaving (at least) every 20 minutes it wasn't too bad. Would pay the $18 bucks to go back the next time I visit NYC.
Only 4 stars because they seriously need to fix up the original Andy (arms broken off). Otherwise, loved this little (open to public) area and there's some great stuff in the Google Store!
Worth a trip to DC just for this. Amazingly powerful, paying reverence here created feelings I can't describe. This experience is why my daughter joined the service I believe.
First time ever seeing an aircraft carrier. Was awestruck my the magnitude of it all. You could spend hours and hours exploring below decks of this floating city.
The Smithsonian Castle is not to be missed or overlooked. Beautiful architecture, with a rich history all in its own. The building itself is the exhibit here.
Still one of the most beautiful parks in our area. Lunch picnic style on top overlooking Covington and Cincinnati has the best views in the area.
Awesome memorial we searched out due to Daughter leaving for navy this week. I adore the globe on the pavement. Need one of those on my driveway.
Well lid out and th lady at ticket booths was SUPER helpful. This is a must stop for any catching the sights. So many great tours to choose from.
Great park with something for everyone. Awesome lawn, food and coffee booths, ping pong tables, nice restaurant on one side attached to library.
Part of the Ellis island experience, do your self a favor and explore this monument and surrounding area. You won't regret it, time well spent.
Great park with room for everything. Multiple lakes, fields for a bunch of sports, and great areas to be rented out for family get togethers.
Beautiful and quiet park, even during the lunch craze. Views of NY Supreme Court and Federal Court, which are marvel's of architecture.
An absolute must see. Knowing this is the site of the Boston Massacre, and truly understanding what that meant are worlds apart.
Beautiful park, lake, recreation area. Has a great looking water park, though it wasn't open yet (2 weeks before memorial day)
There is nothing about DC I don't love, and Washington's Monument is one of the best, especially with its colorful history.
Amazing experience at this park. The walking trails are second to none, and tour all the caves available would take years!
Loved the sea life and the walkthrough giant tank. $100 bucks for 2 adults and 2 kids seemed a bit too much though.
The setup of this memorial is breathtaking. You can almost imagine you are there with them, fighting for your life.

We were looking for a place to camp near Charlotte and ended up coming here for the weekend. It's conveniently located about an hour and a half from Charlotte which is pretty convenient (it's also right outside of Columbia).

We camped at a group campsite at the Longleaf Campground. The campsites were huge and each had a fire pit. There were vault toilets at the front of the campground. The parking lot was right by the campground. The sites were close together and unfortunately we had loud neighbors, but I can't blame the campground for that.

The weather was ok, but not great. It sprinkled on and off a couple of times on Saturday and was a little chilly, but we made the most of it.

We're used to hiking in the blue ridge mountains, so this was something different. We did the Winston Lake Loop Trail which was around 5 miles. We really enjoyed it. It was quite scenic to see all of the trees in the marsh/swamp. The trail did get quite muddy at different parts, so definitely be prepared with waterproof boots if it has rained at all recently.

In the afternoon we went kayaking which was my favorite part of the park. They do free canoe tours some days, but other than that you need to bring your own kayaks or rent from somewhere in Columbia. We started at the South Cedar Creek Canoe access. The parking is close to where you put your boats in so that's nice. The river moves fairly fast, so starting upstream is probably a better idea. We paddled for a while in both directions. It was incredibly scenic along the river and cool to be that close to the trees in the water.

I'm really glad we checked this place out. It's a great place to spend a day or a weekend!

We were looking for a place to go hiking where we could see good fall colors. We found a guide that said this would be the perfect elevation for the weekend we wanted to go.

There isn't much parking, maybe 5-10 spots, but tons of cars park along the road. The last few miles to get there is a bumpy gravel road.

I had read that it was a 1.5 mile round trip hike, but it ended up being around 2.3 miles. It was a pretty short hike to the summit, but it was a decent climb.

It's not marked all that well. At the first split, take a left. There is a sign that points you back to the parking lot which you can use in reverse to figure out which way the summit must be. There's another split close to the top. We were told that both ways will take you to the summit with the left being shorter and steeper.

The views at the summit are breathtaking. You can get a view from the left side, but the actual summit is to the right. You can get 360 degree views that are stunning.

It was incredibly windy at the summit. The hike up wasn't because of the trees blocking it, but it felt like you might get blown off the summit. We were a little disappointed because the views were still almost completely green, but leaves changing is probably happening a lot later than normal this year because of the warm weather.

You can also drive a couple of miles down the road and hike to the Table Rock summit. We decided to call it a day after Hawksbill, but might come back another time.

If you're looking for a short hike with awesome views, I would highly recommend this one!

This is a pretty nice state park with good views. I've been here twice now and it can get pretty crowded on nice days.

There is a visitors center with restrooms which is a good place to stop before you get started. The rangers can give you more information about hikes and help you decide which is best for you.

Both times I've come, I've done the Hanging Rock Trail which starts from the visitors center parking lot. It's not a very long hike — 1.3 miles each way. The beginning is a little steep, the middle flattens out a bit, and then the end has quite a few steps. I would say it's moderately challenging. You can see the summit you are going to climb to at the beginning of the hike. With our stop at the top, it took us about an hour and twenty minutes.

The view from the top is really pretty. There are a lot of rocks to climb out onto to get a good view, but there are several different viewpoints. I wouldn't compare the view to what you'll see over in the mountains, but for the Piedmont area, it's really pretty.

I'd like to come back sometime and do some of the waterfall hikes. From pictures they look like pretty falls.

While you're in the area, Pilot Mountain State Park is only a half an hour drive away and is a pretty unique mountain.

If you're looking for something in the Piedmont area that's a little different than your Blue Ridge Mountain views, this is a good place to come.

In my opinion, this is one of the most underrated national parks. You won't find tons of people here, but you will find a stunning canyon.

I've been to the Grand Canyon and I thought this was more impressive. Don't get me wrong, the Grand Canyon is amazing, but the sheer drop offs into this rocky canyon will take your breath away.

Most people only go to the south rim. Don't make that mistake. You need to go to the north rim. My favorite view in the park was from Exclamation Point. It's a 3 mile round trip hike that's pretty flat.

We also did the north rim drive and stopped at the handful of overlooks. It's about a hour and a half from the south rim, so you could squeeze them both in one day, but it's probably better to do it on a separate day.

On the south rim we did the south rim drive and stopped at Pulpit Rock Overlook, Chasm View, Painted Wall View, Cedar Point, Sunset View, and Gunnison Point Overlook (all roadside overlooks). At the end of the drive, we also hiked the Warner Point Nature Trail which was about 1.5 miles and easy.

There's not much hiking at this national park, it's more overlooks, but there are a handful of hikes you can do.

If you're in Colorado or anywhere near it, this national park is for sure worth a stop.

This trail is located right off of the Blue Ridge Parkway.

We did the loop hike that started at the parking lot, went to second falls (lower falls), then upper falls, and took the loop back.

The trail is pretty moderate. It's not very steep overall, just a few minor hills. It was very muddy when we were there. There's one turn off at the end where I think the trail could have been better marked. Luckily another hiker told us the trail on the right was a spur and the falls was to the left.

Second falls was really pretty. Upper falls was nice, but kind of hard to get a good view of with the trees around it.

You'll get better mountain views on the parkway on your way to and from the hike than on the trail.

I think it was supposed to be about a 3 mile round trip hike but we added on a mile or two attempting to find another waterfall unsuccessfully.

I think there are better hikes along the parkway, but this one is still worth doing.

I was looking for interactive art museums in NYC and stumbled upon this one.

My husband and I came with three of our friends and had a blast.

There are a handful of different color themed rooms (maybe 10?). They have snacks throughout including mochi ice cream, macarons, raspberry soda, gelato, and gummies.

The rooms are all interactive and are a lot of fun. They also give you a card with a qr code to scan in the different rooms to take pictures of your group. They then email you the pictures. The pictures are pretty low quality, but it was still fun.

At the end, they give you a map of different color themed activities throughout Manhattan.

Make sure to get tickets in advance because they're usually sold out day of (we got ours a few weeks ahead of time).

I'm really glad we came here and would definitely recommend it.

I visited this valley on both of my trips to Hawaii. It's one of my favorite spots on the big island.

The views aren't the best from what's considered the lookout. You should really hike down to the valley.

It's a very short hike, maybe half a mile. While it's short, it's very steep. There are great views of the cliffs for most of the hike down.

Once you get down there, the valley is beautiful. There's also a black sand beach. Unfortunately, most of it seems to have washed away. It was a pretty big beach the first time I was here, but there was very little beach left this time.

There are rope swings and lots of shade to relax and enjoy the peaceful valley.

Parking is very limited. Cars park down the side of the road as the lot becomes full.

This is a must see while on the big island.

The views are great, but the crowds aren't so great.

We came here after hiking to Taft Point and Sentinel Dome. It's about 10 minutes further down the road past those and a little more than an hour from Yosemite Valley.

We were able to get a parking spot just fine, but I can definitely see parking being a problem in the summer (we were there in October).

It's a short walk to get to Glacier Point from the parking lot. We brought sandwiches with us to picnic, but there were some very aggressive bees so that wasn't very enjoyable.

We definitely enjoyed the views of Half Dome and the surrounding area, but it was a little crowded for me. We tend to prefer hiking that leads to views and is less crowded.

If you're coming to Taft Point/Sentinel Dome, it's definitely worth stopping here.

If you like hiking and are in Maui, you should definitely check out this trail.

There's not a ton of parking, but we were able to get a spot around 9:30. There's also more parking down the hill (but who wants to walk all the way up the road before a hike?).

The hike starts out incredibly steep. After that, it levels out a bit but is still uphill. It gets pretty steep again at the end.

The views are gorgeous from about the halfway point until the end. Make sure you do it on a clear day or you won't see much. There were some clouds blocking part of our view, but it was still pretty.

It was about a 4 mile hike round trip. I would probably rate it as moderate to strenuous depending on how good of shape you're in.

This was one of my favorite things we did on Maui!

We came for a morning hike while visiting San Jose.

We arrived around 8:30 on a Tuesday morning and the first parking lot was already full. Luckily we were able to get free parking in the Eagle Rock parking lot.

From the parking lot we started on the Penitencia Creek Trail and took that to the North Rim Trail. We turned right on that. We took a couple of additional trails off of it—the Eagle Rock Trail, the Weather Loop, and the Todd Quick Trail. We turned around at the end of the North Rim Trail at the other parking lot.

Our hiked ended up being about 4-5 miles. Much of it was easy with a few steep sections.

The views were gorgeous and the trails were well marked and well maintained.

This is a great place to come hiking in San Jose!

This is a nice park to go for a walk on that's conveniently located close to my parents house.

We've come here a couple of times. The trails are probably only a couple miles or less total.

We usually take the path through the seven ponds that's across the street from the parking lot. You start on a path through the woods and then it meanders through the ponds to loop back.

We usually take the short trail from the parking lot to the eagle's nest lookout. We saw the eagle's nest on our most recent trip but no eagles.

It's a short and flat walk that would be good for all ages. It was a little muddy last time but not too bad.

Check it out if you're in the area and looking to get outside!

This used to be a Girl Scout camp, but it closed 10 years ago and now it's a public nature preserve.

This happens to be right across the street from my sister's house. We went on a great hike here with her. I think we covered almost all of the trails here in about 4 miles/2ish hours.

It's all very pretty and mostly shaded. There's a lake and the second lake has been temporarily drained. Seeing all the old Girl Scout buildings is really cool.

It's not crowded. We saw maybe 5-10 people there the whole time we were there and my sister said that's the most crowded she's seen it.

This is probably my favorite place to hike in the Cleveland area now!

This is a small state park and a quick stop.

Parking is pretty limited. The lot is small. If you get a spot in the lot, it costs $5 for the car. Otherwise, it costs $1 per person to walk in. Cars are parked everywhere on the street outside. It's kind of hectic.

Even though it seems crowded, it's not terrible on the trail. There's a short loop where you can walk through the bamboo first. Then you come up to an awkward view of a falls (I forget the name).

The last viewpoint is of Akaka Falls which is what you're here to see. It's gorgeous. The whole loop is maybe half a mile.

This is a quick stop close to Hilo that is definitely worth doing!

We got food down the street at Burgers and Barley and brought it to this park to eat.

When we drove in, I noticed many signs about social distancing. People seem to be completely ignoring the signs because the park was incredibly crowded and no one was social distancing.

Luckily, we were able to find a secluded picnic table to sit at and eat our lunch.

It seemed like a nice park and I would have loved to stay and walk around on some of the trails, but I wasn't comfortable doing that considering how crowded it is.

I'd recommend trying to find a less popular park than this one if you're just trying to spend some time outside.

This is over of two casinos on the strip where I can reliably find $5 table games no matter what time of day it is. It's still a nice casino, but it's much more casual and laid back than most of the others on the strip. They play good music as well.

The big downside is that it's a very small casino so it can get really hard to find a spot to play blackjack or craps, especially if you don't get there right after they open. It's worth waiting around though if you prefer cheap table because they aren't easy to come by, especially at night.

I'd definitely recommend checking out this casino!

We came to Chagrin Falls to get Jeni's and had to stop by and see the falls.

There's street parking, but we opted to park in the big parking lot by Heinen's (and even that was packed).

The falls is cool to see. My husband commented on how muddy it is. It's usually crowded by the falls, but people must have been focused on the street market going on because it was empty when we were there.

Take some time to walk along the river on the other side of the street. It's really pretty and I like it even better than the falls.

It's a neat thing to stop and see when you're in Chagrin Falls.

This is a tiny little nature preserve hidden in a neighborhood in Ballantyne.

There's no parking lot for it. We just parked on the street in the neighborhood.

We explored for about half an hour before it started to rain. You probably wouldn't spend more than an hour here though.

The huge rocks are fun to walk through and you can even climb on them.

There are also some trails down by the creek to walk on. We did this for a bit as well.

If you're looking for an easy place to enjoy the weather on a nice day, this is a good place to come.

I love the botanical garden! Funny enough, I still haven’t made it in the spring to see the flowers. They host a lot of cool events here. Most recently, I came for the Chinese Lantern Festival. It was absolutely incredible. It was packed because it was so popular and sold out when we were there, but it was definitely worth it! The lanterns were gorgeous. I also go every year for their holiday lights exhibit which I really like. It’s my favorite light display in Charlotte. Maybe next spring I’ll actually make it there to see the flowers!

This is one of the first things you'll drive past as you enter King's Canyon National Park.

If you've never seen sequoias before, this will be a very cool experience.

It's a short walk around this grove. We spent around half an hour exploring. You'll find the General Grant Tree here which is what the grove is known for.

You can also walk through a tree that has fallen down which is pretty cool.

It's flat and paved, so not really a hike, but more of a stroll.

I think it's definitely a place to check out in the park.

I've walked past this park before, but just spent some time here for the first time during Charlotte Shout.

The location is very conveniently located right by 7th Street Public Market across the street.

The festivities here during Charlotte Shout were awesome. I hope they do more events like that here in the future.

The park is small, but nice. There's a splash pad which the kids love. There's bathrooms as well. Google Fiber is right next to the park.

Overall, it's a nice place to hang out for a bit.

We visited the zoo recently for Wild Lights and we enjoyed the visit. They do a good job decorating everything you can imagine with lights. My favorite part was the light show at the pond that was synchronized with Christmas music.

If you're going to see animals in the winter, don't expect to see very many. We were able to see koalas, elephants, tigers, and matetees though.

Overall we thought it was a good display, but I'm not sure if we would go back again now that we've seen it once.

This is a fun place to stop in San Francisco. We stopped by twice on our recent trip.

The first day we didn't have a car so we walked down it. This isn't quite as fun because you just go straight down on the sidewalk. You can get a picture of the crooked street from the bottom though.

The next day we drove down it. This was more exciting. You have to drive up some really steep hills to get to it and then it's a steep zig zag down.

This is a must see while visiting San Francisco!

We've come here a couple of times now to go on a walk or hike while in Columbus.

The parking lot can get crowded on nice days, but we've always managed to find a spot.

It's pretty easy to meander through the different trails. There are quite a few interconnected ones, so it's fun to string them together.

We most recently walked on the dog path which is nice, but I prefer the hiking trails in the middle of the park.

This is a great place to come to get outside close to the city.

This is my favorite park in Charlotte! It’s a pretty big park with tons of great trees, benches, and picnic tables. There’s also a large pond with a bridge and island on it. On the island there is a stage for performance. If you’re bringing kids, there’s a playground and baseball fields as well. Make sure to come in September for Festival in the Park - it’s a large arts festival held here every year. There’s also plenty of parking.

This is a small little park on the top of a hill.

I enjoyed the views of San Francisco from the park. You can see both downtown and the surrounding neighborhoods.

On one side of the park, there's a great view of the Painted Ladies.

There's not much to do since it's so small, but it's a good place to relax for a bit.

Best buggy ride offering in town. Truly authentic! Loved that each tour is private, meaning you only ride with those you're with.

My mom and I had an absolute blast on the hour long ride with Sam as our Amish guide. He even let me take the reigns for quite awhile! He seemed to know everyone we saw on our route, and was an amazing guide.

We stopped at a cute bake shop on our ride and picked up some tasty goodies.

You can't go wrong with Abe's! I highly recommend them!

Perhaps my favorite place I've visited associated with the National Park service. The exhibit is beautiful, fun, engaging, inspiring, and modern.

From a great book and gift shop, to stautes you can pose with from the women's movement, there's a lot of goodness here.

The upstairs exhibit is full of colorful displays of history.

I wish I could have spent more time here! Make sure to check the outside area behind the building for a neat water feature they built.

The Turtle Back Zoo is an amazing gem in New Jersey. I went for my first time this weekend, and I wasn’t sure what to expect, but it was amazing.

The zoo is clean, there’s a lot of different exhibits and animals to see, and there’s many places to just sit and relax.

I had a wonderful time visiting and loved getting to see a wide variety of species, from big cats like lions, to cute little seahorses!

It’s a must visit location for anyone of any age!

It's a cute aquarium right off the main strip in town. I recommend using the self service ticket machine to speed up the process.

The highlight for me was the moving walkway that went under the main aquarium tank. You got to watch sharks and fish swim above and around you. The walkway was slow but that really made it a great experience allowing you to really see everything around you.

The penguins at end are super cute too! One of my favorites!

A large historic center where you can see a ton of the inventions. My favorite part was visiting Thomas Edison's personal library. It was extremely ornate, beautiful, and inspiring. You truly felt he could walk in any moment and get to work.

It was awesome to see how much space and items they were able to save and preserve. Definitely worth a visit and you can then drive down the road to see his actual home in a private community.

Not a lot to see on the grounds and the house tours sold out which was disappointing.

The scenic walk in the woods was nice, but one of the bridge areas to the beach was flooded so we didn't get to walk all the way to the water.

The visitor center is super nice and is like a mini museum. The store is also quite cute with a lot of unique items.

A surprisingly cute and well put together local museum. I really enjoyed the Native American and textiles displays.

While it’s a small museum, there’s a lot of neat things to check out, from machinery to gemstones, there’s something for everyone.

They could use some ac, but it’s a small enough museum that it’s bearable.

Great park with lots of areas to walk around and many attractions to check out! Love the mini golf course.

For kids there’s a playground, a zoo, and a fun little train to ride.

Make sure to take a ride in the paddle boats!

Look Park is also a great spot for picnics and cookouts!

Lots to explore and enjoy!

Great park to walk around, enjoy the water views, relax and go for a bike ride.

We had a lovely afternoon just walking the paths, and renting lime bikes to explore the area more. Lots of geese with their newly born babies to watch.

Definitely worth stopping by for a fun weekend activity!

Not the most exciting national park historic destination. Not a ton to see and tours end early.

The folks who work in the main visitor center are very friendly and there's photos and stories you can read about Harriet and the underground railroad here.

A quick visit kind of place.

Large park on the Hudson. Great views of New York City and the Statue of Liberty. Lots of walking trails, an area to have cookouts, a park for kids, and tons of green space to walk around and rest in.

Really love the walkway along the water. It’s a beautiful spot for a long walk.

Beautiful spot to visit. The first part of the museum is based on photography and seems to have revolving exhibits. However, for the real cool stuff,. Head to the far end of the museum to see the actual estate and home of George Eastman. It's beautiful and over the top elegant!

Beautiful nature reservation with a ton of trails including the Appalachian trail.

Some of the hiking can get pretty tough with lots of rocky areas and steep inclines.

Once you get to some of the peeks you'll be treated to a beautiful 360 view of the area.

Fun spot to spend the afternoon. Make sure to bring a light coat or hoodie because it will get cold! Take wait times with a grain of salt. We were wanted it would be two hours but we were on the tour within an hour.

Great national park with lots to explore. Here you'll find bikes to rent, beautiful scenery, fun areas to explore, seating with water views, food stands, and picnic areas. Lots and lots of green space to explore!

Great place for an afternoon hike through the woods.

It was very quiet, clean, and peaceful. We didn’t see a whole lot on our hike, but still had a fun time. Keep your eyes peeled for deer and mountain bikers.

Great old lighthouse and visitor center. Here you can watch a video about the lighthouse, check out the shop, go up in the lighthouse if available, and learn about the beach and military that was posted here.
Large museum with multiple buildings and exhibits. The outdoor exhibits, such as the big rock you can walk under and the lamp posts, are fun for picture taking. Be prepared to do a lot of walking!
A fun escape the room type of location. We did the Sherlock room, which was several "rooms" and very tricky! The ending was tough and hard to follow, but we had a lot of fun!
Great nature reserve for hiking. You’ll find many different trails throughout. I found the place to be extremely peaceful, quiet, and clean. Great spot for summer weekends!

Clean visitor center with friendly staff. You can enjoy a little video or check out the fun items for sale in the shop area.

Buy a state park passport and get it stamped!
Nice place to walk through and see the old tracks, but there’s not much to do or see beyond that. Take a walk along the water for a more scenic time.
Great park by the water. Here you'll find a cute playground, dog park, several sports fields, and even a little wooden walkway over the water.
An ok boardwalk with a clean beach. Not the most exciting boadwalk, as there was limited things to do and not a ton of shops.
Quaint park that gets very busy mid day. I enjoyed the beautiful flowering trees and watching artists paint in the park.

One of my favorite spots on the strip. The Bellagio spares no expense with their amazing ⛲ fountains and pools that are choreographed to lights and music, and free for all to enjoy. The fountains stretch 1,00 feet across and shoot almost 500 feet into the air. You may recognize thee are they are featured in many films including Ocean's Eleven. Multiple restaurants also feature spectacular views of the fountains from your 🍽️ dining table. The fountains have ♿ handicap accessible views as well.

Timing:
The show is every 30 minutes from 3:00 pm to 8:00 pm Monday through Friday and every 15 minutes from 8 pm to midnight. On Weekends and Holidays the shows start at noon every 30 minutes and change to every 15 minutes from 8:00 pm to midnight.

The best playground in the Triad North Carolina area. It is state-of-the-art, brand new, composite materials, rubberized ground, and fully ♿ accessible playground. They have structures for older and younger kids. One for older kids with ramps, a 🏰 castle, multiple slides, ladders, tunnels, and more. They also have swings for younger kids with bucket swings, swings for older kids including a tire swing, and wheelchair capable swings. They have multiple rock climbing structures and merry-go-rounds as well. They have picnic areas and seating for adults as well.

Great park with a paved track to run around the tennis courts and baseball fields. Great location next to the Y with playgrounds for the kids in the heart of the West End of downtown Winston-Salem. To review the playground only, this structure has some of the biggest slides in town that can be a bit scary or rough on younger kids. They also rely on both stairs and ladders to climb the 3-story structure. They also have a separate smaller playground with a slide for small kids and multiple swing sets. Not an accessible playground.

Great park off of Silas Creek Parkway that has great tennis courts, Greenway access, fun ship-shaped playground, restrooms, and soccer fields. Great for a nice day out with kids or active adults. The playground has mulch all around it, multiple slides, and a great boat structure for small kids to crawl in and around. The also have a wall to keep kids away from the parking lot and to add safety. They do have a ton of climbing structures that can be advanced for small children. Not an accessible playground.

Fantastic tourist destination that shows the very interesting house of the Winchester widow. So many cool features like doors to nowhere, stairways to nowhere, hidden compartments, and many state of the art features for someone very very short. They do state it is not very handicap accessible to make it through the house tour but they do have ♿ handicap accessible parking, restrooms, and features among the grounds and gardens. Great gift shop for souvenirs as well.
dislikes: Limited handicap accessibility in house tour

reviews_attraction.text: Such a touching memorial to the lives lost, the terror attacks, the first responders and survivors of September 11th. It is at this pool that you understand the size of these buildings and impact they made when the fell. I recommend just standing quietly and have some time for introspection. It can be very quiet here and should be so please be respectful as you visit.

The bean is the best. Great photo-taking spot even though it is overdone. Try and go before 8 a.m. when no one is there and capture the sunrise and the skyscrapers in the reflection. SO peaceful and beautiful. With the Bean and all the other artwork near Millennium Park, you are sure to see everything you need within a half of a mile.

if you are passing through the Las Vegas airport and have a little bit of time to spend please stop at the aviation museum. They have really fun yet small and compact exhibits with even some old planes on display. It is handicap accessible and there are plenty of video, audio and literature postings near the TSA precheck.

Great place for a short or long hike if you want beautiful views of the city, canyon, or lake. Bring some water and good shoes as some areas can be difficult to climb. Check the signage and history markers out as well.
Great public restrooms, gift shop, cultural areas and wonderful playground for kids of all ages. Well-maintained with plenty of parking and nice shade from the heat and sun.
Great public park with a picnic shelter, public restroom, boardwalk and trail over the pond and a great playground with slides, ladders, and interactive elements.
This makes a great stop when near Park City. Even in the summer you can see people testing ski jumps or visit the bobsled area and have a go. Great experience!
Love the public fishing pier with great views of the bridge and boats and wildlife. Also love the gift shop and swings/covered areas on the pier.
Nice facilities, great play sets that are Gates and safe and the picnic areas are great for rentals. Nice shady spots during the summer months.
Beautiful views of the Hudson, the skyline, and wonderful place for a walk, or a meal shared with some peace and quiet on a weekend or workday.
Great place for families. Good running trails, places to ride your bike, a dog park and playgrounds as well. The staff are helpful as well.
Great spot for camping, hiking, a picnic and more. Parking area for the Delicate Arch hike but it is a long hike to get to the real thing.
Used to be great place to find peace downtown but seems to have fallen into disrepair and the fountain seems to be off half the time.
Fun sound, cool and laid-back staff and a great place to see a live show in Winston even though the drink selection lacks a little.
Great park with a performance stage, gazebos, benches and ample space to lounge in the grass on a nice day. Very clean and safe.
Great park in the heart of downtown. Always clean and safe except late at night. Look for cool events and Sawtooth events here.
Beautiful park and facilities tucked right in the heart of Winston. Not the safest place at night but great during the day.
Great water feature in the heart of Millennium Park. Love the lights and changing scenery as video plays on the structures.
Beautiful park at the tip of Charleston. Surprisingly quiet with a nice view of the boats and water lapping on the shore.
Check out the very cool Rocky statue and run up the steps like a boss. It is shocking how many steps there actually are.

A great place. I was here during a chilly day during fall to do some hiking. There are some unmarked trails with a medium - medium plus degree of difficulty, as well as trails which are much more comfortable and suitable for the whole family. I guess the views and the surrounding would be more appealing during summer, but still, the views from the top of the mountain is beautiful. There are many picnic tables all around and many places to see around the lake. Very recommended for a fun day out at nature.

This state park is the best I've seen around. It is meticulously kept, clean all throughout. There are tons or good trails, picnic tables everywhere, grills, lots of parking and more. There is also a nice snack court by the lake and there are restrooms in many locations across the park. Oh, and the lake. Simply beautiful. During summer you can swim and hang on the sandy beach and enjoy nature like nowhere else around. The trail that surrounds the lake is also beautiful and has good views.

It's a very simple park with nothing special in particular but has some pleasant and easy hiking trails. There is plenty of parking throughout the park road and at the end of the road there is a Nature center that is open on weekends. Nearby there are also great views from the top of the hill. With Manhattan being visible in good weather. The reservoir at the bottom of the hill is unfortunately not accessible and has a fence all around it.

Hey, it's a free museum so why not give it a try.
It is fairly small, and I covered it all in 30 minutes. You can find here exhibitions about clothing and its design. The exhibitions are changing and when I was here it was about late 1800s and early 1900s dresses, as well as uniforms throughout time.
If you love design and clothing then definitely check the place out for some history and inspiration.

A great park for a fun day out that is very well maintained. There's a nice little local wildlife exhibit, followed by lots of well maintained trails and bridges along tje water and waterfalls. Hiking level is suitable for kids and is not very difficult.
There's also a snack bar, souvenir shop, playground, paddle boats and more.

Awesome place. The views at the top of the lighthouse are worth the $8 per adult and the short climb upstairs. Be careful there, it's extremely windy at the top so hold your stuff!
The trails around are a delight and have a lot of birds, and the beach here is beautiful, good for seabirds watching. Just a great experience

A very nice place for modern art. I was able to see the whole place for less than two hours, so it's not very big, and the collections are not as large as in some European galleries. There's a small square outside and has a nice seating with a café/bar which is very nice to sit at.

A delightful and large park, suitable for the whole family. The are some really interesting sculptures here and the park itself is very beautiful to walk in and is very well kept. Be sure to check out the exhibitions at the main building which are changing from time to time.

A pretty big park with some big flags. The views are very nice here and it is located ay one end of the Freedom Way promenade, so you can have a beautiful walk with views to the statue of liberty and lower Manhattan. There is also a playground here and public restrooms.

It's really impossible not to visit this cathedral which visiting the city. Not as impressive as those you can find across European countries but definitely a special structure, especially in the very modern surrounding architecture.
dislikes: Less impressive compared to European counterparts

reviews_attraction.text: Nature nature mature! Love this place. Beavers, beer, loons, rabbits, foxes and more and more. Come at a quiet time and you will have a better chance of seeing wildlife. The trail around the lake is great for running or bicycling.

The best escape from the city chaos you'll find around. I come here just for the incredibly cute dogs and squirrels that run around all over the place. Just seat on a bench, breath in and listen to the wind in the trees. Perfect.

A nice park with some pretty imposing waterfalls. There are a few view points and the park is not too big so you can see everything even if you are tight on time. Restrooms are available in the visitors center across the road.

Tiny park. But hey, I'll take any piece of greenery in this concrete jungle. There are benches all around and a small fountain in the middle, and the sound of water makes all the difference. Greater spot for a breather.

You can park your car for free here if you come to see the waterfalls. There is additional parkin across the road, at the visitor center. This spot had also some nice views as well as a couple of statutes.

It's basically an outdoor museum with some very detailed street artworks that are very interesting to look at and are quite complex to make. It's completely free and is a very nice to spent some time at.
Clean, modern facilities and an overall awesome experience. What can I say? It's the Madison Square. If you get the chance, definitely go to a game or a concern here, it can be out of this world.
Located in the large Holmdel park this farm is a very nice place to bring kids to. Cow, horses, sheep and more make it a real farm experience. The cow goes mooooo
Beautiful and delightful place to visit, full of interesting shops and cafés. The charming Boston atmosphere is everywhere here, definitely check out this area.
Lovely park and surprisingly quite when you think of the highway close by. Lots of shade and ‫picnic tables and restrooms make it ideal for kids and families.

Located along the Freedom Trail, this old city hall is quite a beautiful building to look at.
It is also surrounded by great places to eat so don't miss it.
A nice little visitors center where you can get information about the park and its history. There is also a souvenir shop inside here, and public restrooms.
If you love Google and if you love Android, this place is an absolute must for getting some cool pictures with the statues. Do not miss.
Sea Lions! Lots and lots of noisy sea lions! This deck is great because the sea lions are always here so you're not going to miss them.
Not that if a big park at all. Barley a park to be honest, but it does have some benches to rest or have lunch, so better than nothing.

It is good in general, only few things that I should mention. Parking is a problem here. It is quite small. There are some additional parking a bit far from the lake, but these are golf club and restaraunt parkings. So, I am not sure if it is a good idea to park there. Another problem is bird dung near the lake. So, it is not much fun to look at this stuff when you just want to walk near the lake.

Good for walking. Partially ok for biking. First few miles of bike trail is very uneven with many ruts left by cars wheels. The rest part of the trail is fine. But if you have lightweight road bike with thin wheels, it will not be very comfortable ride.
A lot of water around makes walking and biking comfortable even if day is hot. Restrooms were open when I was there last time (May 26th).

Not much entertainment like in Universal park. Tours in WB studio is more informational. 3 films were mentioned many times during the tour: Friends, Harry Potter (looks like that every major studio in US was involved in shooting of this film :) ), and Batman. I'm not a big fun of any of these movies, so some parts of the tour were boring for me. But it was good in general.

Nice park for walking. And it seems pretty cool for biking. There are many trails, some of them are gravel, some of them are covered by asphalt. Very few trails that go up to hills. Nice view to San Francisco Bay and even to the city, but it's very far away ;). There are two parking lots that are big enough. I also saw one overflow parking.

Good place to walk. There are few trails of different kenghts. The one near lake is shorter, the one near the bay is longer. There is a rental station there you can rent bike, boat or catamaran. I saw many people who make picnics. Restroom. Parking might be a problem if it is a sunny day since this place can be popular at weekends.

Good museum that has several different expositions: native Americans history, geology, inventions, game industry, weapons, mining, and some other. Mining section is very interesting. These guys made a small copy of mine that demonstrates different types of miners activities.

Well, this attraction is a bit disappointing. A lot of stars with names of the people you know nothing about. It is a bit dirty there, many strange people who tries to sell you some useless stuff like CDs with their own music. And it is always a lot of people there.

Nice place to visit,especially if there is some event here. We visited few concerts here it they were good. Many parking lots around this place. 5 minutes walk to light train and bus stops. Many people bring their own chairs here to sit, relax and listen music.

Nice park. Trails are not very complicated. Beautiful views. Staff is nice and helpful. There are several camping areas in the park. Parking should not be a problem. There are few parking lots in the park, not very big though.

Good place to visit. Great views to San Diego and ocean. If wether is not sunny, it might be chilly here. Visiting this place is usually not free (about $10 per car) except major holidays. Parking lot is quite big.

Parking is a huge problem here. You need to go here at about 7am to get a parking spot. Otherwise you will have to park somewhere on shoulder far away from park entrance. Park itself and views are great.

The place is usually crowded by tourists, especially at Summer. Very good ocean view.
Finding a parking spot might be a problem here. Parking price is $1 per 20 min, $24 max day limit.
