Must visit place for all people who work in IT area :). It is It is amazing to see the history of modern computers and learn about ancient devices that people used to do calculations.
It does not look very impressive. Few houses, few rusty cars. Airplanes looks a bit surprising. It is more interesting to read history of this place rather than visiting it.
Huge aquarium with many interesting showpieces. Entrance fee is quite pricy, though. Parking is also should be paid separately. Place is very popular, so be prepared to it.
View is nice, but this place is mostly used by fishers. So, not much free space here. Smell of fresh fish also does not make you happier if you do not really like it.
Place is beautiful. But the road to this place is very narrow. Parking is also a problem - since road is narrow it is not always possible to park on the shoulder.
I have not visited the golf course itself, but ocean view point near it. And it was amazing. Worth too see if you visit California and especially Monterey area.
Trail to the waterfall is white nice - long enough for a non professional hikers and not complicated. Waterfall itself is small, but located in a nice place.
Nice place to have walks. There are few things to do here: biking (there is bike rental), boating (boat rental is also here),  walking around lake, picnics.
Good park. It is very easy to get here. There are few trails there. Bus tour is also available. There are few cafes there, not sure about quality of food.
It is very unusual to see the piece of Chinese architecture in the middle of SF downtown. There is not much such places in Chinatown.
Interesting place to visit. Tours are a bit expensive, but it is interesting to see how superstitions can affect people's life.
Excellent view to the lake. It is better to visit it early in the morning since not much people visit this place at that time.
It was not good idea to visit it January :) - garden was closed and there were no flowers. Will try one more time soon.

ABSOLUTELY WORTH IT. The price is high, but it is seriously worth the experience. No other VR experience is as immersive and realistic as this...they truly have a winner here with the Star Wars experience here at The Void. Pro tip is to buy tickets online to ensure you get a spot, and be aware there are restrictions for the younger ones. Can't recall exactly but there is an age and height restriction. The cue line can take quite a while, and if you're too early they may force you to come back at your set time. Did not like this part, but the actual experience makes it all worth it. Even if you're not a Star Wars fan, you'll find yourself so into your role during the experience. It is better if you have a part of four or you may find a random person in your group or vice versa. The staff inside is also very personable, energetic, and witty and helped make everything run smoothly. There is also some great merch after you are done. Hopefully they bring more experiences to The Void!

Gorgeous ski area with a number of different slopes for all levels and skill types. Came after a blizzard and thankfully were able to drive up considering the road conditions and were not disappointed. We arrived late in the afternoon and parked far, but there was a shuttle that took us to the main area, which was nice. Having never been on the slopes before, our instructor, Tim Stroh, was an absolutely understanding and accommodating gentleman who made the kind-of-scary first-time experience all the better with his professionalism, encouragement, and sense of humor. Their skiing and snowboarding lessons are the best prices, no doubt. They also make the check-in and rental process easy and seamless too. Once you're done on the slopes, there's a gift shop (one of the best I've been to) and eateries as well.

#skiing #snowboarding

Such a great find of a park in the most unexpected area. The walking path is spacious and provides a great walk or jog as a loop from and to the parking lot, which had many spots available. The nature here is beautiful and there has been a ton of great work done here to keep the park calm and leave the animals unbothered in their natural habitats. I did notice a park ranger in the area making rounds so the grounds are relatively protected but use best judgment and recommend locking your car, etc. Also, there is no shelter if weather gets bad and no restrooms either. A ton to learn and explore about this preserved piece of nature.

Thought this was just a great spot to see the Golden Gate Bridge up close and personal, and soon realized you could take a time machine (not really) back into history within the main historic site itself. I found myself in awe at how much I learned about the use of the fort by servicemen and how the Golden Gate Bridge came to be. You'll see a lot of artifacts in a number of rooms with great signage to guide you along the way. You can even climb to the top/roof to get some amazing views - it does get pretty cold up there, though. There's also a gift shop. Thoroughly enjoyed this experience.

Excellent use of outdoor space for mixed-use including great retail and dining options in addition to the casino and race track. Even when it is relatively busy there seems to be enough space for all. Although it may not be flashy or as updated as some other nearby entertainment venues/facilities, it is a great time with options for many, including families. Parking is relatively abundant due to the parking spaces within the internal roads and the edges of the complex and the stores, restaurants, and facilities are very accessible due to ramps and elevators.

Came for the NightGarden experience and was amazed. The theming of the grounds and the interactivity made it an enjoyable night. Parking seemed like a bit of a hassle but being that it was a popular event I think parking is usually better during normal hours. The grounds themselves are absolutely beautiful and truly seem like an escape from reality. Staff was very polite and helpful as well. Will be returning for normal operating hours to see what else Fairchild has to offer!

Incredibly immersive - once you enter Diagon Alley, you're no longer in Orlando. Every bit of detail and every touch put into the shops exterior and interiors and the structures themselves are beyond incredible. The Wizarding World truly comes to life and being able to experience it through riding "Escape from Gringotts," eating at the Leaky Cauldron, and feeling the heat of the fire from the Gringotts Dragon makes a visit to Universal Studios more than worth it.

You'll get lost in the maze of classrooms and other academic suites and areas in this amazing structure. You'll feel like you transported to another era. It is truly a work of art, and it's interesting reading about the building on the interactive screens as well. Beautiful grounds surround this building as well, so there are tons of photos available to take from the interior and exterior. Would highly recommend visiting at night.

Visited this area at night and was very surprised at how populated the beach was in the evening. Parking was actually pretty easy to find considering it was a holiday weekend. Was able to park close to the sand and enjoy the park a bit. Would definitely recommend securing your vehicle and valuables as it can get pretty dark depending on where you are and may attract vandals. Will likely give this park a visit during the day.

Great all around experience. Short trip from the city and an exhilarating drive up. Whether you're a beginning or expert, you'll have a great time here skiing, snowboarding or even tubing. There's also a cool lounge to get some r&r before hitting the slopes again. Staff was very helpful and polite. As a Miami local who's never dealt with snow or any sort of winter sports, they made the visit very comfortable.

A quick stop at the most as the location itself only provides a small look into the surrounding waters, but it's definitely pretty cool to get to see this landmark as it is a must do for anyone visiting the keys. Lines for photo ops may vary, wasn't too bad when I visited but do be prepared for a wait. Make the quick visit and continue seeing the rest of what Key West has to offer.

Excitement and adventure lurks around every corner at Islands! Between the super hero rides, water-based rides (amazing for summer days) and one half of the Wizarding World of Harry Potter, there's so much for those young and old to get into. Each area is perfectly themed to immerse you entirely. Utilize the park map and explore every corner or you may miss something!

Visited early on a weekday and was very impressed with the facility. A bit difficult to find but once we did, it was really cool to see the work put into the interior design. Was able to quickly get my racing license and hit the track. They have two tracks available and very fast carts. Definitely a cool place to go with a group of friends or on a date.

Really loved this park and it's proximity to Navy Pier. It was freezing but still had a great time playing with the interactive art pieces and grabbing some great photos as well. Great for families, especially the little ones. Parking around was bit of a hassle to find - had to park a bit out in an affordable garage but the trek over wasn't so bad.

Love the amount of trees and green space at this park! Found parking to not be an issue at all and there was ample space to socially distance while jogging or taking a stroll. The basketball courts are well kept and reflective of the park in general. Only downside was dogs weren't allowed at the time but not sure if this is permanent or temporary.

Small but immersive art museum with a variety exhibits, many of which are changed every so often so there's usually something new between visits. For more bang for your buck, visit during the Lowe After Hours (formerly LoweDown) nights - admission includes two drinks and small bites, and you get to enjoy the various exhibitions and galleries.

Very pleasant and beautiful grounds - great for the young ones. Tons of varying events periodically throughout the year, no matter your level of interests. Perfect on a cloudy day or when humidity is low. Lots of land to cover and a lot to explore. Very historic and will take you to a time long ago. Definitely a Miami-Dade gem.

Not a large museum, but tons of interesting facts and unique items that really bring you into the reality of those affected. You will come face to face with many of the stories told through art and interactive pieces, and you'll undoubtedly leave with a greater knowledge of AIDS, especially in South Florida.

Great little shop with tons of different flavored fruit wines. Lady doing tastings wasn't as polite as I had hoped, so just browsed the products and purchased items. They also have cool little wine pouches (like an adult Capri Sun) if you'd rather not have the entire bottle. Decent prices.

Whether you're a local or a visitor to Miami, you must take a visit to the gardens. As a local, life is always moving quickly, but this place is great to relax and take in the beauty and serenity of Miami's history. Price is affordable as well and location is not far from other hot spots.

Nice gateway to the beach. Very relaxing in the early mornings before things get busy with direct access to the beach and lots of space for strolling around or a light jog. If driving over, there's a parking lot and quite a few street spaces available as well. Beat the late morning rush!

So much to explore and see and you can actually feel and experience the tranquility of being so far from modern civilization. Love the exhibits and the more than friendly staff. A wonderful gateway to addition areas of the Everglades. There's a lot you can learn just on your stop here.

Pretty expansive art collection, including a few modern exhibits and pieces as well. Aesthetically pleasing and very beneficial to the pieces and works being featured. Very quiet environment, not as fun as the history museum but that is another completely different setting.

Fantastic views of Crissy Field and other landmarks such as the Golden Gate Bridge and Alcatraz in the distance. Best explored and experienced by foot and by bike as roads are narrow and traffic is usually always moving.
Amazing views of the river and some of the skyline from this bridge. Quick to cross to get to either side, makes for quick and easy exploring of the area.

Amazing park. I like that it’s not as crowded as some of the other national parks, yet offers great hikes and beautiful vistas. The park is free (at least I didn’t have to pay when I went in October) but has great amenities like campgrounds and public restrooms. There are some sources of water and places where you can fill up with potable water but bring your own to be safe.

Iconic, but super crowded and the food is way overpriced. There were some cool street performers when we went in the afternoon. The sea lions were fun to look at, but if you’re not an animal person then I guess you wouldn’t enjoy that. Also, there are a ton of people wanting you to sign petitions and/or donate money to their cause, which is super annoying.

This is a small museum with fascinating ruins in the back. It costs $5 to see both the museum and the excavations in the back. For a small museum it has a lot of cool things: artifacts, videos, interactive stations for kids, and a gift shop. The ruins in the back are really cool, there’s also a replica of an Anasazi structure that you can go into.

I don’t know if this is an accurate image of Mr. Harvard because I never saw him in real life, but it’s a nice looking statue. He seems comfortable in his seat. There are steps that you can sit on next to Mr. Harvard and enjoy some snacks. It’s not as comfortable as his seat though, don’t get your hopes up.

It’s a fun place, but it’s super expensive. I like to go in the summer because the water rides are some of my favorites, but I’ve heard the Christmas lights in the winter are pretty as well. Expect to pay a lot of money for food and drinks as they don’t technically allow outside food or drinks.

It’s a great park with lots of cool places to explore. There are hikes that require a wide range of skill level, so there’s something for almost everyone. I think the price is a bit high for the size of the park, but it is well kept. One park ranger was very friendly, and another one was not.

As far as beaches go it’s not pretty. There are a ton of shells that make it painful to walk and the water is very murky. But there’s a fun water fountain area that’s great for kids and the grass and wooded area is good for a picnic or a barbecue. And you can’t go in the lighthouse.

Beautiful views, great fishing, and some exciting rafting on the Green River. I would spend at least three days here, there’s so much to see and do. For rafting go with a friend (2 cars) so that you can shuttle the rafts and not pay an  exorbitant fee for someone else to do it.

Very beautiful place in all seasons. My family loves going to see the Christmas lights in December, they’re not fussy but they’re also some of the best lighting in the area. The sister missionaries are friendly and there are lots of resources available for foreign tourists.

It’s a nice playground with lots of things for kids to play with. There are percussion instruments, slides, ropes and lots of space. There’s also a track/trail that goes on the perimeter of the park that you can walk/run on. Plenty of parking spots.

Soooo why are there penguins here? I thought they escaped? And even if they didn’t escape, then where’s the lion, the zebra, the hippo, and the giraffe? The movie Madagascar was very misleading. The red pandas are absolutely adorable.

There were some really cool exhibits, my favorite being about handmade crafts in Atlanta/Georgia. Emory’s Laney Graduate School hosted its annual gala there and the setting was good. There were lots of places to take pictures.

The Spanish moss and the trees here are breathtakingly beautiful. The museum is pretty whitewashed and does a poor job of highlighting the stories of the slaves (and later poorly-paid servants) that lived on the plantation.

Lots of fun things to do around here. The attractions can be a little pricy and parking can be tricky if you’re looking for free options, but overall this is a fun place. A must if you’re visiting Atlanta.
I went at Christmas time and they had their regular steelwork exhibits as well as some Christmas exhibits. Small, but nice. Good bathrooms. They were also having a Christkindl market there.
The buildings look old, rusty and historic. There’s a nice visitors center where they have a few exhibits. They also have a Christkindl market there during the holidays.
A significant historical site for both Missouri and The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. The sister missionaries do a good job with the tours.
Easy access to the beach. We went on a Saturday afternoon and parking wasn’t too hard to find, and it was free. The beach is huge and flat.
Beautiful hikes and views. You can also do the AT Approach trail from here. Fishing’s allowed in a small pool but it’s catch and release.
It was a bit busy on the Saturday morning that I went. It seemed like most people were there to bike or to float the river.
This park has a long, clean beach that you can watch the sunset from. It wasn’t crowded when we went on a Friday evening.
You can look through the windows but can’t go inside. If you’ve seen other old schoolhouses there’s no need to stop here.
Leave your car here if you don’t have high clearance. Plenty of space here and not too far from the trailhead.
The grass is very green. I heard they have a farmer’s market on Saturdays but it wasn’t there when I went.
Finding parking close by can be a pain but it’s a nice park. There’s events on weekends which are fun.

We really enjoyed this park. It is very clean and the bathrroms are well kept. While there we saw the Mora Sherifs, the park rangers and the fish and game ranger.

We went during the week and it wasnt very busy but started to get really busy on Thursday and by Friday morning all the spots were full. There are also lots of people who drive in around 7pm and fish until 9pm.

The fishing was really good we caught lots of smaller trout and a few bigger ones. There are crawfish and frogs in thr lake that are very amusing for younger children. The boat loading area is a nice place to swim.

I was skeptical at first because from the town it doesnt look like much. You might think that it will just be a boring dessert or there will be nothing to see and you would be wrong. I ry enjoyed this park. The rock structures, views, plant life and animal life were very interesting. There are short and long hikes that you can take to explore the area. The Joshua trees are fascinating and there are whole "forests" of them at a certain elevation.

We came here at 10am in July it was 95 degrees outside and we werent expecting to be able to do much. However, unlike many parks, this park has very good shade. It is designed so that at least half of the playground will be shaded at any time during the day and it really didnt feek hot in the shade.

My only complaint is the fake grass ott really hot on our feet.

This is my favorite chidrens museum of all time! I have been to many from West to East coast and this one takes the cake.

My favorite section was the math/physics section. I am a math teacher in CA and i wish i could bring my students here to explore.

There is also a really great water area and air area.

This place is good for ages 2-100

I love this place and so do my kids. There are  big trains, small trains, old trains and trains you can ride. Take your kids here. It is free and they will have fun. You can reserve spots for parties. They have a model train area that runs on weekends and they will let you kid check out a toy train to play with on the wooden tracks.

Fun place to bring the kids and get away from the city. They have a nice visitor center with some interesting exhibits. There are bugs to see and some inside glass to look at. They also have pine cones, pieces of wood and antlers for the kids to touch. The walk around the park is also very relaxing and informative.

This museum is awesome! My daughter and I got in free because IM a teacher and she is <3. The animal exhibits were my favorite. They make it seem like they are actually in their natural habitate. There was a dinisaur show that was exciting and the bugs and spiders were fun

Lake is super low. It takes a long walk to get to the water and the bank is super muddy. This makes.it difficult to fish and swim. The camp sites are pretty nice an upscale. There are bathrroms, drinking water and hot showers all of which are included in the camping fee.

It is a nice looking park but has some flaws. Dueing the day there is not enough shade and all of the playground gets super hot and impossible to play on. There are also lots of ants near every seat. Other than that the park is nice and the water area is great.

This is a very fun park. It has a water area and a normal playground area. It makes for a good transition from the heat to cool off in the water. There is also a lot of grass areas for parents to sit or have a picnic and there are tables and benches.

After parking, a short walk takes you to the top of the hill for some spectacular views. The day we went it was pretty smoggy and we.couldnt see Palm Springs. We could just make out the Salton Sea. I definitely would come back for the sun set.

This was one of my favorite short hikes. We took the path next to the stone house and down into the arroyo. Their were some really awesome large rocks to climb and the rock cliff above was fun to explore. Our kids really enjoyed the sand.

Super fun play ground with lots of activities. This is the first park I've seen that has the zip line swing that goes full circle. The kids 2 and 4 love it. I also like how the play structure is Temecula themed.
Prett good playground for kids. They have several tyoes if swings, different levels of slides a spinner and plenty of shade. The only negative is the bark flooring. I really prefer sand
It seems like a nice place for running and special events. However, it would be nicd to be more kod friendly like a playground or something. If you park inside you pay alot.
My kids had a really good time here. They spent over 4 hours. They have lots of educational activities for kids. They do charge an entrace fee but trust me it is worth it.
It is fun and all but there are much more interactive childrens'  museums out there. There is not much to do here. Most exhibits are watching and are not interactive.
Great place to take the kids. So much to learn and see. You could spend a week here and still have plenty oglf things to do and most of it is really affordable.
Really nice area with many really good restoraunts. They do special events on weekends and holidays, its not unusual to see karaoke in the middle.
Really cool place for the kids to play after the beach. They have interesting clmibing structures, push button water fountain, and fun slides.
Best museum EVER! Webt on Thursday night and had a blast. You have to come to appreciate it. So many fun actuvities to explore and learn
We have a yearly membership and come several times per month. The zoo is very fun. Our daughter lokes the carosel and the dinisaurs.
I really enjoyed this childrens museum. I have been to several and this was by for the.most interactive, creativr and fun.
I am not a huge fan of museums and i visited this place for a class i am taking but this museum was very interesting.
Our school did prom here. It was a spectacular location. It's a bit of a drive to get here but it's mostly freeways.

The park has some amazing views that doesn't exist elsewhere such as unique looking plants and incredible rock structures.
My 6 & 9 year old kids were able to do all the hikes with Ryan Mountain trail being their favorite. They also enjoyed climbing all the rock formations that were all over the park.

When we went in November, the crowds were fairly light so we never had any issues with parking or overly crowded sites.

This is the most popular hike at the Volcano National Park for a reason.
There are 2 main parts to the hike and both are amazing. The first is walking through the forest that has many different species of plants. The second is walking across the crater.
Due to the high elevation change between the forest and crater areas, the hike is extremely steep although they did a nice job of putting in stairs where needed.

My 6 & 9 year old kids had a great time here. The hike is relatively short around the loop (~1/2 mile).
There were plenty of fallen redwoods where the kids had fun climbing. In the middle of the loop, there is a river where many kids were swimming.
The parking area is small but it's easy to find spaces near the trail entrance off the side of the road. There are also restrooms at the main parking area.

My 6 & 9 year old kids enjoyed the relatively short hike across the hardened lava landscape. We went during a light drizzle so didn't experience any of the heat others mentioned.
The petroglyphs themselves were pretty interesting, but if you must see them and don't prefer hiking, there are other areas on the island where you can see them with less effort. Apparently, they aren't that rare.

This was the highlight of our trip. The scenery is so unique and hiking is fun while trying to navigate through the shallow streams.
Bring extra shoes or wear sandals or aqua shoes. It's difficult to avoid water if you want to fully explore the area.
Also, to get to the nearby parking area, the car will need to drive cross a stream. We had a Mazda 3 that rides low and we had no issues.

Seeing the gigantic trees is amazing... photos don't do a good job of showing how large they are.
There are many hiking trails for all levels. If you didn't plan or research ahead of time, the rangers at the visitors centers can help decide what's best depending on your time of stay and preferences.
Most parts of the park are free but some areas require the usual National Park fees.

It's a relatively smaller beach with very mild waves. It was great for my young kids.
The parking was free and there was a restroom available. It also seems to be a camp ground since there were many pitched tents.
Also, this is a great location to view the sunset and doesn't seem to get as crowded as some of the other popular locations for this viewing.

It's a lava tube that has lighting installed allowing guests to walk through without any preparations. It takes less than 30 minutes so worth the visit.
If there's wet weather, water will be dripping from above and there will be puddles on the ground.
Parking space is limited so you may need to park 0.5 miles away at a nearby trail head parking area.

It had some nice views but nothing to go out of the way to see.  They have a  ferris wheel type of attraction which we didn't go on but others might enjoy (seemed like a waste when the Space Needle provides much better views).
If driving, there is paid parking nearby but it's a bit of a pain to get to since they are on a busy one lane road.

The kids had an awesome time here especially at the sand dunes.
We spent 1 full day here which seemed like enough time to explore all that was on our list (sand dunes, natural bridge, badwater basin/salt flats, zabriskie hike).
The food options were minimal inside the park so we picked up some sandwiches before heading into the park.

The vista point provided great views of unique land formations.
Even better was the 2.7 mile hike that circled the area. It allowed us to see some of the rock formulations up close and scenery that couldn't been seen from the vista point.
We had 7 & 10 year old kids and they were able to hike this with ease and also stay interested.

Hoping they expand this area to include a museum that explains his history. Right now, it's just some sculptures and his most famous quotes engraved in stone which doesn't seem to do him enough justice.
But still worth a visit particularly if you are already planning to walk along the lake to the FDR and Jefferson memorials.

The rangers here were able to suggest which hiking trails and other activities to do based on our length of stay and preferences. There was information shared that weren't available on any website.
You can also pick up the trail maps here.
Finally, they provide guided tours occasionally starting from this point.

The tree is simply a cone shaped net with designs on the outside covering a tree. I was expecting a much grander tree like the Rockefeller one in NYC but this one was very underwhelming.
The supporting props were nice like the model train and trees for each state and territory.

The lake at the end was beautiful which the kids and a fun time playing in. Along the hike, the kids also had a great time playing by the river banks and getting a treat to see some deer close up.
It took about half a day to go in and out and most of it was forested and shaded.

This was a fun hike for my 4 & 7 year old daughters.  They enjoyed climbing down the rocks to the river bed and hiking up the trail to get closer to the top of the waterfall.
The parking area at the bottom of the falls had a water fountain and clean restrooms.

This is an easy trail for viewing gigantic redwoods. It is mostly flat with a wide dirt path. Signs are clearly marked where there are splits in the trail.
There were people of all ages from toddlers to older adults who seemed to enjoy this area.

Great for first time visitors but loses its appeal after several viewings.  The show runs every 15 or 30 min depending on the time of day so if the area is too crowded, your can always catch it at a later time.

The kids had a great time climbing all the rocks and the tail was very easy. There is very limited parking near the trail entrance so people may have to park on the street and walk a few hundred more feet.
In photos, it doesn't look as big since it's shown along with the Washington Monument which is super tall.  However in person, it is extremely grand and a great site to see.

It's a nice neighborhood park with a lot of green space.
Update on 4/30/2017 - the playground structure area is closed due to construction.
The visitor center provides a good overview of what's at the park. the rangers are helpful if you have questions about your visit.
Come early in the morning to avoid the crowds. It's well worth visiting if already here to see the more popular Lincoln Memorial.
This area has really nice restaurants. It's also a convenient way to walk along the strip while avoiding the hot outdoors.
Fun place for kids to pose with giant Android statues.  The nearby Google merchandise store is only open on weekdays.

You go to Crater Lake to see the lake not these falls.  Off in a wilderness all by themselves they would be a sight, but caught in the middle of this park, they are ho hum.  If your walking, biking, skiing, or driving by, take the time to stop for a few minutes and consider where in the heck does that water come from?  Then you will take in the marvel of what is happening and enjoy the moment.  This is not worth the effort to go out of your way for, but if you are at this point on the rim, you are probably in for the full tour and you should take 10 minutes to enjoy.  If you are driving by, please slow down as many people mingle on the edge of the road here.

One of many stopping points on the rim drive that take your breath away.  If you visit in the summer make the time to drive the entire rim and take in as many overlooks as you can.  As you drive around the rim the people will be more disbursed than at the visitor center.  Each stop creates a unique view as the angle of the sun hitting the lake and the change of the sky clouds reflect in the water.  Google and I done agree on the location of Dicovery Point.  There are three or so stopping points in this general area that fit the bill for checking the box for stopping at Dicovery Point.

This was a nice tour.  I was a bit disappointed with the display and access to the actual trail.  The signs of stay on the path and look at the sign that says it was here did not do the trail justice.  I think there should be a 400 yard hike in the soil right on the spot. I am all for preserving history, but what is happening here is the growth of sage brush.  Can you imagine going to the Pacific Crest trail and not being able to walk on it?   Why not let people feel the history of the Oregon Trail in the souls of there feet?

The experience of taking in Spring Creek by way of kayaking from Collier Park and back is special. Please respect the sensitive environment here especially as the popularity of this kayak location begins to grow. I am a regular here and it never gets old. The clarity of the water is amazing.  Just as amazing is how frigid cold the water is as it comes out of the springs right under your watercraft.

This is an easy access point to the Pacific Crest Trail as it crosses the road here.  There are no toilets or water.  It is just a place to park for access.  In the winter it is plowed and you need a snow park permit.  There is a well marked trail (PCT) that leads to a snow shelter in just under 2 miles; to the north.  Bring your own fire starter but there is usually wood there.

There is something magical about this fall. When I close my eyes and think waterfall, this is the first to come to mind.  The width, volume in summer, and the colors of the rocks, water and surroundings make a postcard image.  Going up the Mist Trail gives you the best experience.   Going down the Mist Trail can be slow going and very difficult when it is wet.

5 stars for the fact that the public gains access to a wonderful piece of river. Downsides. There are pit toilets use at your own risk.  There is a place to launch a boat but it takes some creativity to get it down to the river.  I won't call it a boat ramp more like access point.

I was told this is the highest elevation paved road in Oregon.  It is way up there and very windy.  Based upon the shape of the trees and the interpretive signs the wind blows regularly here.  Tie you hat on and enjoy a bird's eye view of the lake.

An easy stop on the valley loop. You will have a hard time driving by it as your eyes are drawn to the top of El Capitan. The colors change with every angle of the sun and passing cloud. Each time you drive by it looks different.

We stopped here for a great walk by the river.  The adjoining walking and biking paths are well maintained and of appreciate width to accommodate runners, walkers, and bikers.  Bikes are allowed on the paved paths only.

For the price this is a one star attraction.  If it was prices accordingly I would rate higher.  About a 30 minute tour of the facilities is what you are getting.  The large tanks were impressive, but WAY over priced.

I don't think I would plan a vacation around this as the feature attraction, but I would never drive down Highway 26 without allowing an hour to sit and watch the colors change each time the sun goes behind a cloud.

A great well maintained trail. There is a picnic table near the falls if you wish to pack a lunch. Just under 1 mile one way. There are good educational markers along the way identifying various plants.

A great place to get away for a few hours. Lots of mountain bike trails and some other easy walking trails.  Many good picnic spots and a playground.  Disc golf is also available as the season permits.
We stop here regularly as we pass through for a road trip stop.  The bathrooms could be a bit cleaner but I do appreciate that the city or county provides this convenient stoping place.
A beautiful bridge over the river. The bridge is a testament to the commitment of the park to have a piece of functional art as opposed to a piece of steel to walk over.
This is a great place for a picnic meal. There is less traffic here than in places with less of a view up the valley.  We always have a very enjoyable time at this beach
A good .9 mile hike in to a beautiful waterfall. The trail continues up the hill to view the upper tier. The side trail to the Job Rock Garden is a wasted effort.
dislikes: Side trail to Job Rock Garden

reviews_attraction.text: If you are going to stop and look around, it is well worth your time to make sure you stop at this visitor center.  Very good exhibits and a knowledgeable staff.
If you put politics aside, it is a great place to take in views.  There are many hikes to vistas that look over the Ashland and Medford area that are stunning.
A nice little park to relax.  There is a nice open grass area opening up to Lake Ewauna.  There is a small boat ramp with limited parking.
A great set of static displays and 30 minute videos in the theater.  There is a gift shop and rangers there to answer questions.
A great hike among the majestic sequoias. It is downhill on the way in and uphill coming back. Well marked trail.
Super helpful rangers to help you find the best places to see on the given day. A small gift shop is here too.
A good staging area to hike the Crag Trail or just go to the Vista point.  Good parking and a pit toilet.

One of my favorite places in Mill Creek. The forest loop takes away the noise pollution as best it can. And the birds and smell of the cedar and salmonberry takes over! Little trails cut in and out of the entire loop. Don't be afraid to go off path, although there are a few dead ends. But it's small enough the turn around and isnt a big deal.

Only four stars because there is quite a bit of trash and the occasional sketchy/inappropriate person. They keep to themselves. And mostly stay in or behind the A frame party rental shelter. There are tons of people around. A lovely playground. A stream that rolls through occasionally. And people leave gifts along the path for kids to find.

The DUI wall is intense if you stop and really feel what it's about. I hope it makes an impact.

Another awesome place in Washington. You really can't go wrong here. Google directions didn't quite get me there. Make a left on high bridge and go over the river.

There is a pull out shortly after this on your left with signs that say public fishing. It does have small spots with access to the lake.

But continue on down high bridge rd. Stay left at the fork. And on the bend will be a driveway and parking lot.

I have been here twice on week days. It was relatively quite. One person and a dog the first trip. The second trip a semi truck came through!? Bazaar. All the way down and tried to get though the forest trail. And on my way back a Ford F350 came through, as well. So not only keep an eye and ear out because it is a hunting area - also keep a look out for automotives.

I originally went to the animal park but quickly saw that was not for me and my pup.  Luckily grace cole.is nearby and was just what we were looking for.  We - my 11 year old border collie and my self - went on a Wednesday afternoon mid January.  It is the 3rd day of snow and people in this state flock to the snow - it's hard to find a quiet area.  But Grace came through. One other car in the lot.  The minis one star is the fact that it's so short.  There are two areas to explore - the forest and the boardwalk.  Worth the drive from Mill Creek on a snowy day but we also stopped by. McCollum on the way home because it's always a hit

Gorgeous crystal clear lake ! It does get busy but the lake is huge and has plenty of access points for everyone to have a quiet spot to themselves. Dogs are allowed off leash but must be kept in control. But honestly it’s not the dogs you have to worry about .. it’s the people. This place is beautiful and there is so much trash lining the shore. I saw 4 diapers within 100 yards of each other. Not dog poop bags. Not beer cans/bottles. Diapers, cheese it boxes, towels, Sunscreen bottles... from Lazy people.

Not what I was looking for. I have a senior dog and we like to stroll around the local parks. The reviews rave about this place and I suppose if you are looking for a playground - heck ya!

I was here for the trails. Everything is really steep!! Really steep! I would have loved to come here for the snow! Not only is it steep but a lot of the trails are next to the street. I might be back to bring my nephew to the Animal Farm, though

Endless amounts of fun for everyone.  There is a pretty nifty play ground, but my nephew raved about the sandbox with the excavators you can actually use! We went back 3 times because of this.  It doesn't end there - farm animals, endless trails, a lake, beautiful covered picnic areas.  SO much space it makes it enjoyable for all.  OH! Did I mention the master gardeners and their orchard! Yeah.. super thankful for places like this

Dog park was nutso. So glad I went down to the beach. Although the dog had to stay on a leash there was tons and tons and tons of space it did not matter. Gorgeous green grass near a playground. People out flying kites and there was still room to walk the dog around. Beach follows you everywhere - through the trees over the pristine pond - you can't go wrong here.

Not as bad as some of the reviews say. There are sketch areas that look sketch from far away. Just don't go in those areas. There is plenty of room to explore elsewhere. Lots of water access. The trail is wide enough to accommodate traffic both ways with no one squeezing.

It is a Sunday in July and I saw about 12 people. All of them had AT LEAST one dog.

This is a beautiful gem that has taken me a year and half to find! Please follow the directions - it's not an off leash dog park.  There is plenty of space - let's be respectful and keep it that way.  Trails interconnect. You. A. Stay as long as you want.  There is a farm and it is very horse friendly.  My senior dog and I will be back.  Twas delightful.

Playground is pretty average but the setting is serene.  Walk past what is supposed to be a splash pad... Pfff... And walk past the owl totem and stumble upon mini waterfall streams that the kids will surely love.  Frisbee golf continues behind the park. Lots of great shade and beautiful magnolia trees crossing the bridge

Trailhead parking is directly off the old 99 hwy on your left side.  There's a sign as you approach maybe 3/4-1/2 a mile to the trailhead. The trailhead parking is a one way loop parking lot just above and off old hwy 99. It fits about 10 cars with off street parking for maybe 4 more cars at the bottom.

Lots of options. Park at the top and gave a steep walk to and fro. Park at the bottom and have an easy stroll to the beach. Winter time it becomes an off leash dog beach. Lots of dogs here even mid week and blistery weather. Found pink sea glass. Great views. Worth the drive from Bothell

Not worth the drive... for a day hike. Beautiful lake, of course. But the trail is about 2 miles of switchbacks. When you get to the lake there is only one real spot - so no privacy. There are other pokes but no real access. And lots of bugs because of the swampy area!

Stay away from the south side parking lot and it is spectacular. The south parking lot is empty and great for solitude but always has the evidence and feel of vandal.

Also note lots and lots and lots of horse poop on the trails. And, as always, snakes in the grass

Aside from "swimmers itch" (but you can get that almost anywhere) it's perfect.  A nice easy but challenging small short game frisbee golf. Also has a concrete BYOP ping pong table. Birds and views are the cherry and whipped cream on top!

Great place to take the kids. There’s a huge park with lots of trails. 2 playgrounds. And of course the lake. You can swim or rent water crafts. Dogs must be leashes and are not allowed on the beach. Discovery pass required or $10/day

Great park with water access.  There is a boat ramp and a small beach to let the kids/dogs play and fish.  There are 1 inch spikey balls that can get caught in dogs fur. But other than that it was a fantastic place to let my dogs dip

You just have to see it. Fremont is such a cute little off shoot that must be explored. Tons of coffee shops and breweries.  Very artsy and fun. Very little parking so if you see a spot snag it and walk the rest of the way

Just a square inside a neighborhood.  And it is well used by the neighborhood. Fantastic for them because it's like a dog park in your front yard, but not what I was looking for.  We drove to Grace Park nearby instead

One of my favorite Washington hikes. Steady climb for a "wait, this isn't a painting!?" reward. It is rooty and rocky but that should be expected. There was a toddler who charged this ahead of me in a dress and vans.
It's like cape faltterys little sister.  Or a tiny slice of Ireland.  Or a tiny slice of big Sur.. all within an hour of Seattle.  We stayed in this tiny area for an hour and a half.
Sure is a treasure ! But I bet in good weather and sunsets it gets crowded.  It is right next to train tracks without a fence
Great family friendly trails.  And awesome off leash dog area!!!! There is a falls you can jump off of into a swimming pool
Worth the drive. Lots of areas off the path to dip in the water. Water is beautiful and clear. Turquoise in the sun!
Perfect small zoo in a super cute beach town! Perfect walking steps for a small child. And cooler weather, too!

Accessible camping for the Bay Area.  The Bay area is just blessed with so much natural beauty that even this average park in the Santa Cruz mountains offers great camping. We camped here in April mid-week.  The place is deserted and of the 20 available sites, only four were occupied.  The campground is in the middle of a redwood forest. Clean bathrooms! There are some short hikes that takes you to a nice swimming hole (too cold and swift in the winter though) and a 1600 year old redwood tree.  Very impressive for a small county park.  Supplies can be had either at Loma Mar or in Pescadero.  You can reserve a spot for the summer or weekends from the San Mateo County web site.  Mid-week or off-season you can pretty much just show up.

The Dipsea should be on the bucket list of everybody who lives in the Bay Area. The 7 mile hike out to Stinson Beach starts with three grueling flights of stairs. After that you're not done. You still have a some climbing to get to the first ridge, at Windy Gap. Then you drop into Muir Woods. You can take a little break here before the long climb to Cardiac Hill. Then it's a steep downhill to the beach.

Pro-tip: you can avoid the Muir Woods reservation system by parking in downtown Mill Valley and hiking to Muir Woods

pro-tip 2: once you get to Stinson Beach you can take the Marin transit bus back to downtown Mill Valley for $1 (price as of 2019)

There are several parking areas. The trail gets progressively rockier as you ascend. Most would feel more comfortable with high clearance. I saw a Subaru at one of the higher parking lots. 4wd not necessary unless the road is wet. The road is wide enough in many places to turn around.

The hike up to the lakes is awesome. It's a short 2 mile hike from the upper lots. Maybe 1.5 more from the lowest lot. About halfway there is an awesome waterfall. Great example of Alpine Colorado hiking.

From the parking lot, hike about 1 mile to just past the fenced off section to reach some beautiful dunes.  The fenced off section is to protect the nesting area of birds.  The dunes are huge and you can climb quite a ways.  We were there in March and many of the plants were flowering.  Sand Verbana, etc.

There is no water at the parking lot.  So remember to bring water if you plan to be out for awhile.

This is a wonderful place to see a large selection of California native plants. It's well organized. Most plants have a label colored coded to indicate it's native region of California. All the major regions are represented: desert, mountains, coastal.

It's also a very serene place with a creek running through. There are lots of benches where you can sit and just enjoy the peace and quiet.

Spending some time here is a great way to relax after a good hike or several days backpacking in the mountains. Some of the exhibits are pretty cheesy but fun. Don't miss the film on the history of movies shot in the Lone Pine and Alabama Hills area. After that you will start recognizing the Alabama Hills scenery in many of the film's you have seen and also will see in future film's.

An easy snowshoe to this lake just past the turn-off to Bear Valley Ski Resort on Highway 4.  You have to park on the side of the road just before where they don't plow the snow any more.  There is a gate there.  Hike for 3/4 of a mile on or next to the snow-covered road.

In the summer, the lake is just as beautiful, offering some very nice kayaking.

I love California Poppies. We visited in late march. And the blooms here are just jaw dropping. You stand in the field and there are orange flowers in all directions, sprinkled with a few purple and white and yellow flowers. Amazing. Best time to visit is march and early april but depends on winter rain and spring warmth.

Old fashioned family oriented ski resort! Not fancy but good for kids and a good place to practice basic skiing. The runs are not challenging. For cross-country you can ski up the road  all the way to glacier point, a 11 mile trip one way. You also have huge swaths of Yosemite backcountry to explore by ski or snowshoes.

This is where you come to pickup your wilderness and Whitney hiking permits. To climb Whitney you should enter the lottery (April) and win a permit. Then you pick it up here the day before. But if you don't win, you can get try your luck and get in on a cancellation.

Plenty of parking, clean bathrooms. Nice gift shop.

Excellent location for a family hike and easy trail runs.  A little bit of climbing but at the end you'll be rewarded by nice views of the bay area.  The trails are pretty easy and smooth.  Beware of the copious coverage of poison oak.  Don't touch anything green if you aren't sure.  Learn what poison oak looks like.

The hike is 5-star but the parking sucks. Because Mount Bierstadt is one the "easiest" 14er and it's proximity to Denver the trailhead gets crowded. We arrived at 730 and the parking lots was full. People parked on the shoulder for a mile on either side of the trailhead. I recommend arriving before sunrise.

This marvelous Beaux Arts structure with a stunning blue reflecting pool celebrates the waters of the Hetch Hetchy as it streams into Crystal Springs Reservoir.

Located halfway between Edgewood Ave and highway 92 on Cañada Road, a popular biking route, this temple makes a wonderful lunch or watering stop.

Stop here and get an amazing panoramic view of the panamint valley. And if you're lucky you might get a fly by from military jets. They often fly here and sometimes very low for practice.

While you're here notice the geology. The rocks here are mostly volcanic but further down the road they're not.

A medium size museum!  Honestly I haven't seen much of their permanent collection but I have seen several special exhibits.  All excellent.  The museum isn't large and feels very intimate.  Make a trip up to the top of the tower and get a great view of San Francisco (on a no fog fall day!)

One of the popular trails in death valley because it's so close to the main road. The colors are awesome and in the late afternoon sun it looks golden. You can hike all the way up to zabriskie point, or do a loop via Gower gulch. Or you can just explore up canyon to red  cathedral.

I love the spaces in this museum. I like their permanent collections but their special exhibits are excellent. A wonderful place to come on a quiet weekday and just, well, do nothing and get inspired by the art. On weekends it can get crowded.

Cool place to stop on your way in or out of Death Valley National Park. If you get here you probably also saw the art work at the museum down the road. It's hard to imagine that there was a sizable town here just over a century ago.

Do the tours of Balcony House, and Cliff Palace.  They fill up fast in the summer, so arrive early and get the tickets.  It's just mind boggling that the natives managed to build such cities with only stone tools.
Small parking lots that fill up quickly on weekends. From there it's a short walk to the beach. There is a much longer bluff hike to another entrance to the South.
This is one of the best National Park Visitor Centers.  Nice museum area and a nice gift shop.  It's also a very nice, airy building.  Lots of parking.
Haunting sculptures at this museum. Very fitting for an old ghost town. I would like to come back here in a full moon night. And on Halloween.
Easy accessible beach where you can ponder life and universe. Just watch the waves and forget yourself for a little while.
A pleasant hike for a great view of SF, especially after a nice lunch in the Mission. It gets pretty busy on the weekends.
The eye of the storm! A wonderful serene spot isolated from all the activity of the bay area only a short ferry ride away.

The Nashville Zoo may not be the biggest zoo in the South but it’s perfect for the Middle Tennessee/Nashville area, which has so many outdoor activity options for families. They have an Andean bear, tiger, cougar and other species that you’d want to see. Parking is so spacious that you’re never fighting for a spot.

They have timed entry with the COVID-19 pandemic, which is not a big deal. When the indoor wildlife exhibit hall is open, that’s a real treat for the kids. Put this on your list of places to visit when you’re in Nashville.

Wonderful child-friendly museum with a great set of hands-on exhibits and displays that introduce kids to music, science & engineering, animals and the human body. Definitely one of the best places to take your children on a rainy day if you live in the greater Nashville area. Prices appear a bit steep at first glance but buying an annual membership is the way to go. Some of the stations or activities are a bit dated but the museum is undergoing a long-term renovation that’ll only improve the experience for families.

Spacious and beautiful park that's used for all kinds of festivals throughout the year. Great place for a photo shoot. There are different kinds of fish in the pond for those who love to fish. There is also a pathway for people to take their canoes or kayaks to a launching spot on the Harpeth River.

Last, but not least, the wonderful K-9 Korral Dog Park is located at the northern end of the property for those want to unleash their dogs for some exercise.

Not a great number of parking spaces here at the base of the bridge or at both ends. Nevertheless, the view from the bridge is absolutely beautiful regardless of the season. It definitely gets more crowded with warmer weather.

Be careful as you walk along the bridge as the railing is extremely short, only 35 inches tall, and it could get dangerous on a windy day. All in all, the bridge is a beautiful part of the Natchez Trace.

A huge surprise for us when we visited the TN Aquarium. Didn’t know that there was such an awesome location to view some of the most beautiful local and international aquatic creatures right here in Tennessee. The price of admission was well worth it. Parking is not free as the aquarium is located on Downtown Chattanooga’s riverfront. Totally recommend visiting this place to others.

Great expansive center for young children to learn and have fun at the same time. So many different topics of learning are available to kids through unique activities. A fantastic option to spend a few hours on a rainy day. I would recommend purchasing an annual membership that allows you to come back with your family as many times as you want.

Nice challenging public golf course with a high number of holes with doglegs and uphill/downhill tee shots. Almost every hole is lined with trees so driving the ball reasonably straight is important. Greens are in good conditions and have a fair amount of undulations. Definitely worth playing if you're looking for golf with elevation changes.

Closed during the winter for good reason but a fairly cool area for the kiddos to play during the hot Memphis summers.

The only downside is that the designers went overboard in trying to make the sprayground look as natural as possible by placing boulders near areas where kids could slip on wet ground and hurt themselves.

This location on the east end of W.C. Johnson Park is fantastic as a part of the Collierville Greenbelt system with a boardwalk that extends further into the forest for walking and biking. Plenty of opportunities for bird and wildlife watching as well. Never gets too crowded.

Recently built park with long walking trails and a bathroom. The biggest plus is the massive playground area with multiple sets with different activities for children. Definitely a plus for anyone in the Brentwood/Franklin area with kids who need to burn off some energy.

Massive beautiful public park on the Mississippi River that’s also dedicated to hosting major festivals during the warmer months of the year. More parking would be great but it would encroach on the park, so you just have to make do with finding a spot.

Expansive park in Spring Hill with a walking trail, modern playground and plenty of parking. The free splash pad here is the key attraction that keeps the kids cool during the hot summer. Also has a basketball court and grills.

Downtown Franklin is a great place for families and for tourists and very pedestrian-friendly. Lots of shops and restaurants to visit. The festivals and celebrations held throughout the year are great.
Beautiful park behind Woodland Middle School that contains the massive wooden Brentwood Community Playground for kids to enjoy, an amphitheater for concerts and several fields for organized sports.
Almost like the Times Square of the South with the crushing crowds of people during the warmer parts of the year. Bars, music lounges, restaurants and gift shops galore. Good luck finding parking.
Nice park with playground green space for the kids to play. Has an enclosed dog park with separate spaces for small and big breeds. Also has a football field and plenty of ballfields.
Beautiful park across the street from the Brentwood Library with a basketball court and access to the Greenway. Safe low-lying playground set is great for toddlers.
Wide open park with a walking trail along the entire perimeter. I wish it would have a few more trees on the trail for shade during the hottest days of summer.
Great place to park your car and go on a energetic hike up a historic set of hillside stairs inside Percy Warner Park to get your heart rate up and running.
Small but very informative train museum. Staff are very knowledgeable, friendly and willing to give you a tour even if you’re only a small group of people.
Spacious green space within an urban area. I love the extensive walking trail that circles the entire park. So much room that it never feels crowded.
Best new park in east Shelby County! Lots of open space with fun play areas for children. Just needs more covered spaces for the summer heat.
Great aquarium with a wide variety of fish and sharks. I definitely recommend to anyone making a trip to the Smoky Mountains.
Great place to start a ride on the fabled San Francisco cable car. Much smaller crowds than the one on Market Street.
Very quaint green space in a busy area that allows you to reflect on those who struggle in order to overcome cancer.

This island is so beautiful! I'd start with biking the perimeter, then go to the fort since the pass covers several attractions. With those two you get both the history and the natural beauty of the area. After you finish those two wandering around and hiking the area is awesome. If you get off the bike trails and slow down you see a lot more. This place rewards those who are willing to get off the beaten path, plus the forests and water are much cooler in the heat of the day. I bet renting a kayak would be a blast, too!

This place was beautiful and surprisingly untouched; I would expect a lot more people given how close it is to major cities like San Francisco. There were a lot of secluded areas where you can enjoy some quiet time on the beach. The lighthouse is currently closed for renovations, but there are still a ton of places worth seeing here, especially if you enjoy hiking.

This place provides a great vantage point for the nearby coast but is worth seeing for its own sake. The mountains here are beautiful and there are many campsites available in the area. It would be a great budget alternative to staying in Santa Barbara, which can be pricey. The picture shows the view from my campsite.

This place was very cool but very popular. I would go early in the morning or later in the evening to avoid crowds. There are a lot of nice hikes in the area if you're not afraid to get lost. If you bring plenty of water and a map it's pretty hard to get really lost because you can't wander off an island!

This trail makes a beautiful bike ride on a warm day. Some areas were rocky, so you have to watch carefully. The views are beautiful, but I liked biking it better than hiking it. Some areas are forested, so you don't always have views. When there are clearings you can see for miles!

This place was cool to see. You have to look through a telescope to see the butterflies as they are small and camouflaged effectively. I also recommend listening to one of the experts before you see the place; I couldn't find the butterflies until they showed me where to look.

I loved walking around this area and appreciated that there was no charge to enter. I was hoping to see wildlife, but the seas were rough that day and might have scared them off. There were not many other visitors, so it was nice to enjoy some peace and quiet.

It's a nice free gallery in an expensive city. The designs are unique, so I'd recommend taking a few minutes to explore. It's not a large exhibit, so you wouldn't need more than an hour unless you live for fashion.

The park is a prime place to see the bridges and enjoy the skyline of Manhattan. It's popular but beautiful enough to be worth braving the crowds. Walking across Brooklyn bridge is an priceless experience, too.

The views here are incredible! This area is beautiful in spite of recent fires and natural disasters. You do have to pay for parking within the park, but it's worth it if you want time to see it in detail.

The falls here are gorgeous! I would definitely give yourself plenty of time to walk around and explore here. There are so many beautiful angles of the falls, so you need to take time to hike the area.
There's a lot of space to wander around here. You can get away from a lot of the crowds and bugs if you hike away from the main attractions, especially on the east side with the sandier areas.
This a great hike with plenty of switchbacks at the beginning of the route. The creek makes some beautiful  waterfalls, and the canyon is especially pretty in the fall with all the colors.
I loved the ocean views here and especially enjoyed the cypress trees. It was a bit crowded that day, but it was a holiday. There was a nice walking path that I enjoyed strolling along.
This was a beautiful beach and seemed to be a popular area for watersports. There were surprisingly few visitors considering how close it is to major cities in southern California.
The Sacred Grove is well worth a visit. People may argue about all aspects of a faith, but my faith depends on what happened here. Even on a busy day, it's a peaceful place.
This place has some beautiful coastal areas. I've also heard it's a great place to spot wildlife, but the seas were rough when I visited and may have scared them away.
This park is gorgeous! I love how much red rock is in this area; it's like Moab but closer to home. There's a good hiking trail, a campground, and water access.
This has got to be one of the nicest beaches near LA. It's just close enough to the city to be convenient to see but far enough to not be too busy.
I loved the public art, and you can catch ferries or boats to the Statue of Liberty nearby. I especially loved the immigrant statue.
I was here close to sunset, and the views were amazing! I loved the most on the lake and how the lighting reflected on the water.
The views here were awesome, and the ranger program was quite informative. I only wish I'd given myself more time to explore!
This park was scenic, and I loved the coastal areas. It was a popular place to visit that day, but it was a holiday.
It's an amazing view! I'd try to come during a less busy season, though. There were a ton of visitors that day.
It was cool even though I wasn't able to get close due to the government shutdown.  I love cypress trees now!

Great park that has everything except a basketball court??
But more than makes up for it.
They have a popular pool that is great for the summer.
Next to city hall, police, AND fire department.
They have a baseball field. An outdoor auditorium. A covered sitting area. Bbq spaces spotted throughout. A little hall for city help courses like dancing. Even tennis courts. Great place to run and jog. Smack dab in the middle of MPK. They do lack calisthetics areas along their walkways. It’s a great park for checking carnivals and festivals.
And of course a kid playground. On 4th of July the place fills up for fireworks.

Great little park in Monterey Park.
They used to do dirt bike races in the 40’s. Next to reservoir.
Has two baseball fields. Two children playground areas. Town museum that has models of all the California missions. Even has a working observatory you can use to see the sky Wednesday nights. Great area for having parties. 2 gathering areas. Large grassy areas. Great park in this city.

Good looking castle with moat and all. They best part of the castle is the walkthrough. You go through old stairs through the castle to dioramas of the sleeping beauty story. It got a makeover and it was sad because the previous dioramas were very cool and old school style.For folks with disabilities there is a little room with a video of what it looks like going through.

Just a gorgeous mission. You can easily take a train from Los Angeles here and spend the day. The old mission church itself is just a structure now but the grounds are well preserved with lots of activities for kids to learn. Pan for gold. Make bricks. Tour the museum. Right in the middle of a nice town. Great day trip.

Another of these spooky memorials. During the day normal. But during the night, and if its raining you really get the feeling of what the area must have been like. The ponchos they wore giving away the terrible weather they faced.
Ghosts walking in the darkness. How do I salute while typing?

Great beach. My child went here for Boy Scout camping. Cold but nice. Very peaceful ... yes there is a train that passes by but that’s side noise to me. It has spaces for camps and mobile camps so lots of folks here give it a great community environment.
Also great area for biking too.

Where our most important documents are stored. The declaration and Constitution. You must go just to see that paper. There is more to do in there as well. A museum and lots of other documents to see. The mural is amazing that sits over the documents.

A great little place to take nature walks. There is this nice little 1.5 mile walk that goes a bit into the forest. And little walkways arou d the parking lot. Can be done in a hour but still a nice place to relax. Will have to pay for parking.

Another of those missions that no longer has a lot of what makes it a mission. Church and museum with a small cemetery. Swallowed by the city. But the mission style around the church gives the neighborhood a great style.

A great mission located in the lush San Gabriel area. This one has a great garden and one of the few missions that still has those soap vats. You can still ring the bell too.
The church is very popular for weddings.

Similar to other aircraft carrier installations like midway. But it has extras that make it stand out like the Concorde and the enterprise shuttle. Go for the military history but please go to see the shuttle.
sad walk. Mainly because you can still see living vets from this war visit and breakdown. Its tough to watch but the least we can do is walk the wall and pay tribute to these men.
It was a castle. A castle in the distance. We had to stop. It looks so majestic. Bought a wine sampler package and enjoyed some nice tasting wine. Left with a bottle (or two).
Another amazing well kept mission. Final resting place of Father Juniper. About as fine an example of well kept mission there is. Worth the drive. Church, museum, grounds.

Just visit. What can I say that hasn’t been said before.

Just plan for base tour and plan a year before if you want to go to the top.
And exercise on a stair master.
Small little mission that did not survive to have a complete campus. The church is there and small museum and grounds. Nestled in a small town it is a fine mission.

I love miniatures so its such a treat to see everyday america and great scenes of our country. Love it.
I wonder the work it takes to keep clean and sun damage.
Drove here on the way to Solano, Had a wine taste and loved it. The grounds are very awesome and in the right weather carry a solemn feel. Lovely place.
There is a lot packed into this space museum. Because its small it can only fit so much. But there are some great pieces here. Rockets. Planes. Nice.

Cool submarine. Love ship tours,
Not for people who are claustrophobic.
But fascinating to be in. Worth a trip if you have never been in one.

A quick visit museum. A lot of fine example of maritime history. Lots of model for the engineer enthusiast.
Great little fine.
Just this cool little ghost town in the middle of no where. Go for the mystery shack and to take a quick rest and break
Came when there was no water. This was a good thing because we got to step up close and see the structure. Awesome.
Can book early or just go. But book if you want to be sure. Do not go for the politics. Go for the architecture.

A great aquarium.
They have this huge glass wall to see all the fish.
Good place to go while visiting.

We entered from the south and stopped at the visitor center. We got a Jr. ranger book for my 9 year old. On our way up we completed the book...like a scavenger hunt.  Lots of exhibits off the main road to stop and take a photo or read a info baord. Short hikes are also off the main road as well as some campsites. The terrain changes as you head north which is really cool to see. We exited at the Joshua tree exit in the north...stopping at the visitor center to show the ranger our book and collect our badge. Without stopping it may take 2 hours to drive thru...but you'll want to get out explore some...my son loved climbing on the rocks.

We made the drive up from San Diego just for the Tut exhibit. I didn't realize what a massive museum this was! Included in our special Tut admission was the Endeavor exhibit. O highly recommend both! It was beyond amazing to see all of Tut's treasury even though the mummy wasn't there. And to see the shuttle up close was awesome. And these were just the 2 additional exhibits.  The entire museum has so many different exhibits! We barely scratched the surface.  We also did the IMAX movie about Tut which was great . Parking was additional. On

We came here on the 1st Tues of the month which happened to be $1 day. Kids were free. This is a small but well done museum.  We learned the science of the wave, the history of surfing in Vietnam during the war and the evolution of board size and shape. There was a even display with Bethany Hamilton's board and several other famous surfers. What really made our visit was the older gentleman who took us around to each display and explained to my 8 year old all that he was seeing. Excellent one on one tour!

This is a beautiful museum. The bigger than life scuptures in the entry are amazing. Upstairs the art is displayed in an uncluttered arrangement giving each piece it's proper space for maximum enjoyment.  Don't miss the short movie which highlights the artists.  They do have a twilight afternoon price which is significantly less expensive.  The staff was friendly and helpful. The gift shop had unique items.

Our homeschool co-op visited all 7 historic bridges around Balboa park. We had just finished up a unit study on bridges. This was a perfect way to be outdoors, see some beautiful history of San Diego and many types of bridges that we had learned about. This one sways a bit...but is over a cool canyon with a trail...we even saw a coyote!

There is a small Beach and playground area. There are restrooms and There is a place to rent Kayaks. A grassy area for picnics with a few picnic tables, A boat ramp nearby,  And sharp rocks that can cut your feet. There was no lifeguard on duty ...we came during the week. There are also lots of stingrays so shuffle your feet.

San Diego's only National monument, this is a great and popular tourist spot. Beautiful visitor center with bathrooms, a movie and exhibits. Views go one for miles. Lighthouse is cool and the tidepools are great at low tide. There is a hike you can take along the cliffs which can be steep in spots. Excellent spot for photos!

This park is curently undergoing renovations. The restroom has been torn down and one of the playground structures has been removed. Hoping they fix it fast. The library is adjacent. There is a large grassy area and some playground equipment that is still usable. Plenty of parking and picnic tables.

I have been here twice before and it is amazing. This trip was a holiday weekend and it was crazy! Two hour wait to get up and nearly an hour to take the tram back down.  Call me spoiled from my first 2 trips which had zero wait. But of course the view is spectacular and the hiking is challenging.

Great place to hang out with friends or family. Playground structure for littles...workout structure for adults (although kids think it's a playground😜) Basketball court. Bathrooms and showers. Picnic tables and benches. Beach access. Parking is limited...you may have to walk a bit.

Excellent history tour outlining the beginning of the city. Very informative. Wish more of the underground were included as part of the tour. There is an above ground portion and walking is involved. Our guide (Dave) knew his history and welcomed questions from the group.

Plenty of parking...lots of different areas to visit. We were at the end of DeAnza road...playground is still closed 😒...but there are bathrooms and an outside shower. Also a lifeguard tower. Grassy areas with shade trees as well as sandy beach for sitting.

Beautiful park one block from the beach in the middle of a round about. Shady magnolia trees and benches surround a flag pole and military gun installation. A quiet place to sit and reflect, sip some coffee or chat with a friend.

Beautiful and peaceful park. We picnicked here. There are playgrounds and bathroom facilities.  The lake is serene. Nice place for a walk. You may consider bug spray. Parking and admission is free and easily accessible.

Beautiful park. Raised boardwalk trail to an overlook tower.  Lots of wildlife to enjoy. You can hear the hum of traffic which disrupts the mood a bit. Bathrooms and picnic tables. Free to enter and free parking.

This is such a beautiful and majestic place. The views are amazing especially at sunset...pinks and purples. Just gorgeous.  The hikes are a bit of a challenge due to the rocky terrain bit well worth it.
Absolutely beautiful during the spring bloom! It is a must see! Trails you can walk or bike on. A great visitor center with interactive displays. Ample parking and Bathrooms . Also a small gift shop.

Beautiful park...so much to do. A relaxing walk...playground for the kids
Public pool. Beach area. Volley ball nets. Barhrooms and shower facilities available.  Parking is plentiful and free.
Small slice of green grass right on top of a cliff in Pacific Beach. Benches and a few trees to sit under and relax. Rest rooms available at the top of the Law Street beach access ramp.
Loads of trails to explore. Pretty flat. We came during peak flower bloom and it was amazing. Trails for walking/biking/horse back riding. This has been our lock down hike of choice.
Lots of picnic tables and Pavillions, playgrounds and sports equipment. Bathrooms. Parking is plentiful. Weekends are busy. Beautiful spot to sit under a tree and relax
Pretty little park in Santee.. Playground for the kids...covered picnic tables.  Tennis court, short trail to walk on. Sufficient parking and restroom facilities
Great beach...lots of sting rays! Two girls in our party got stung today! Shuffle those feet. Lifeguards are helpful. Parking is for a fee. Facilities are ok.
Small visitor center with restrooms and a sink to refill your waterbottle. A small gift area and 2 rangers to answer any questions.
likes: Facilities & Services: Visitor center, restrooms, water refill, gift area, rangers

reviews_attraction.text: A very strange oddity of Seattle...if you're at the market worth a short walk to see it. But really...it is just ABC gum🤪

Miami seaquarium was an enjoyable experience. I came for the dolphin encounter. Got a chance to swim touch and interact with the dolphins. The park itself is a bit smaller than what I anticipated. One of the female dolphin trainers. The shortest one of them all wearing a greenish outfit was somewhat nasty and unfriendly at times. The other staff were superb and friendly. Also the photos of you and the dolphins they offer to sale you after the dolphin encounter are way to expensive. So its safe to say they price gouge. I only went along because a one time experience, but they should not charge so much for photos.

I sooo loved this place. Admission is 5 dollars to enter this small museum for adults. Staff were friendly and  knowledgeable. They have a small aquarium on the first floor and displays and artifacts all throughout. They have a second floor with more displays. I came upon this museum by accident but I learned from this museum the hard work and sacrifice these people made during that time to save other lives. Hard work that was not easy during all kinds of storms and weather. Five stars for this place and those heroes who helped others and rescued lives.

Loved this place. The cruise was about 1 hour long and they travel on elliott bay. The staff was awesome and the captain narrates the voyage. He gives a good description of the city and other sites during the tour. They sale refreshments on board. You can go upper deck, in front of the deck or stay inside. You can use the seattle citypass to save money as this is one of the included tours. Great place near pike place market and the ferris wheel.

Had a great time. I had shaquiro as my tour guide ( sorry if I spell her name wrong ). She was awesome and very informative. I enjoyed seeing the inside of set stages and got close to items worn by some of my favorite actors and actresses. I loved going inside the ellen degeneros show set as I love her show and she makes me laugh. That was a highlight. All in all I give Warner Brothers Tour a Thumbs Up! Awesome!

This place is awesome. They have artifacts and a replica of an indian village and a pilgrim village. They have people playing the role of the villagers.
