You can interact with the villagers and ask them questions. They have some animals on site and you can enter some of the huts or homes. Great place for the kids. You can buy tickets at the admissions office for the mayflower ship if you choose.

Lol...this place is super cute. The artist who made this troll was very creative. I got here and a small crowd was here taking pictures. A great place to take memory pictures of your stay in Seattle. If you go the hill from here you have a small community garden which they grow some produce....I saw spinach. Up there you also have tbe bus stop that can take you back downtown.

Betsy Ross house is a small house located in philadelphia where she stayed at and created the American Flag with the 13 stars. The house is very old and small. Upstairs is betsy ross's room where she knit the flag. Very beautiful place to visit and you get to see some old items. In the basement they also have some in display. A must see place if you come philadelphia.

Great iconic movie theatre that was updated from its original form. Came to see Star Wars and place is awesome. They have many other screen viewing in here. Would definitely come back again. They also have a 4D movie viewing section where you actually have the seat move and you smell scents whole viewing the movie in 4D.

This park is both peaceful and beautiful. Good to come early hours and take pictures of the area. Has a statue in the middle and a nice crowd of people. Very upbeat energy with merchants selling different items on the side of the park. Park is on front of a cathedral of great architecture.

Beautiful old castle structure used years ago against the british. Not much inside, but its a valuable important piece of American History. They have a gift store inside and the staff here were super nice and can give you a run down on the history of this place. When I came it was open.

Very beautiful designed piece of architecture with stairs and elevator. Sadly it is currently closed because some people were jumping off the top committing suicide. They might however, rebrand it, so jumping off will not happen in the future and probably reopen to the public again.

Historic open air place where many hollywood stars made their impressions of their hands and shoe prints on cement. In front of Graumanns Chinese Theatre, this is a MUST place to go in LA where you will see many imprints of your favorite past and present celebrities.

Oh my gosh! I loved this place....one of chicagos best buildings. They have a ride called the tilt that you hold to and tilts you facing down the steeet....not for the squemish. I enjoyed it and great atmosphere and beautiful views of chicago.

Very nice ride and the car has temperture control to keep warm in the cool season. The ride lasts a few minutes but gives you pretty views of the elliott bay and the city. Great ride to take kids and your family.

Beautiful area very peaceful. Very elegant historic lighthouse. Definitely best to come at sundown or evening to see the full display lights emanating from this lighthouse. One of my favorite sites in cape cod.

I came here but unfortunately it was closed when I got here. But you can still take some selfies and pictures on the outside. But its a cute lighthouse but the sorrounding area is a bit cringe worthy.
Cute little historic park in provincetown. Nearby is a small beach and a long jetty with large rocks where you can tread upon. Be careful if you decide to walk on the jetty. Beautiful views out here.
I LOVED this place. Such a beautiful location in the florida key west. Beautiful view and a great place to come and relax and enjoy the warm positive energy. Roosters and chickens walking abound.
This was a house where edgar allan poe lived at one time. House has a sad energy and they show a short film about his life. Although he was a famous poet, his life was short and challenging.
This lighthouse is awesome. A must see when your in the key west. When you get up to the top it is very breezy and you get a beautiful view. Very serene location in the key west.
Very serene beautiful place. About 30 minute drive outside main Las Vegas strip. They have parking area and restrooms. Offers a beautiful view of the natural setting.
I did not go inside this museum, but looks like a great place to take your children to. On the outside, they have mechanical dinosaurs thst move and make sounds.
Came to see the magical flute play. Very nice show and well done. Staff is friendly and helpful. Great venue for theatre plays etc. Very elegant arena and place.
Very beautiful garden with historical significance. Right near fort ticonderoga. Great to spend awhile in leisure and enjoy the flowers and garden here.
Beautiful park. When I was here in July they had the chinese lantern festival. Beautiful Chinese exhibits and the fountain is breathtaking.

I first visited a California Mission while in high school many years ago. I still visit them for two reasons: beauty and heritage. Most of the missions are still beautiful almost three hundred years after being built. If you were born in California, the missions are part of your heritage, so you need to understand their impact on our history. Whether the missions’ history repulses you or you celebrate them, you need to see them to truly understand them.

The Mission Basilica San Diego de Alcala is very beautiful but ii like a few others better.

I first visited a California Mission while in high school many years ago. I still visit them for two reasons: beauty and heritage. Most of the missions are still beautiful almost three hundred years after being built. If you were born in California, the missions are part of your heritage, so you need to understand their impact on our history. Whether the missions’ history repulses you or you celebrate them, you need to see them to truly understand them.

IMO, Mission San Juan Capistrano is the most beautiful of all California Missions.

We went to Hearst Castle and were very surprised by two things. First, people in wheelchairs cannot go on standard tours. Second, people in wheelchairs cannot use the tour buses to get from the visitors’ center to the castle.

A State Park official told us they would give us an individual tour that might join up with other tours when possible. So, when a standard tour went somewhere inaccessible like Neptune’s Pool, a tour guide took us through other rooms. To get to the castle, we just followed the tour buses and parked near them.

While driving up Interstate 680 and crossing the Benicia-Martinez Bridge, you can look across Suisun Bay and see our Reserve fleet and reflect on a little bit of our Navy’s history. On one hand, the ‘Ghost Fleet’ is slightly depressing because the fleet represents a response to external threat, but on the other it represents our willingness to protect. Sad that we get placed in a position where we have no choice but build these ships, but I am very thankful to every man and woman who served on these ships.

I love seeing the Giant Sequoia Groves in Kings Canyon National Park. I had the coastal redwood on my place in Bonny Doon California. All sequoias are beautiful, but the bigger they get the more beautiful.
Kings Canyon National Park is my favorite national park because of the giant sequoias and because you can hike down into it from Florence Lake where my family stayed every summer. Until I broke my neck, I had intended to solo hike from Florence Lake to Kings Canyon National Park when I turned 18.

Even though we lived close to Yosemite National Park, we only went there once or twice a year. Most of the time out-of-town visitors would asked us to take them there. Until I ended up in a wheelchair my favorite thing to do was hiking to see the wildlife. Now, sightseeing with short jaunts to see falls are the extent.

All our guests wanted to see Yosemite Falls. Most of the time, they only saw it in the summer, but it is much more beautiful behind Fall colors or with a soft blanket of snow.

On one hand, I wish Alfred Hitchcock had used another edifice in The Birds, but by using Saint Teresa of Avila Church in Bodega, he immortalized a beautiful church. An Aunt and Uncle lived near Bodega on Joy Road, so every time we drove through Bodega, at least one of my cousins had to remind where The Birds was filmed. Why? Because I hated all Hitchcock films. I do not like horror films, and to me that was Hitchcock’s genre. By using this church, he ruined any chance I might attend it.

Visiting the Dole Plantation was lots of fun, and very informative. Lots of tour options, but the cost of each is minimal. We learned a lot on the plantation garden and pineapple express train tours. Reserving the tours on-line was easy and very helpful. With so many people at the planation, I am not sure we could have gotten the tours if we had waited until we gotten there. After the tours, we ate wonderful deserts at the plantation grille.

Avalon is a very beautiful island town but getting around to se the sights in a wheelchair presents many obstacles. Fortunately, the road going to the Catalina Island Casino & Avalon Theater is flat, so getting there is just a matter of pushing down Casino way. We were never there for an event, but we did tour it. It is a beautiful dance hall that would have been fun to dance in when it was built.

The Byodo-In Temple is the largest Japanese temple I have seen and when you realize it is only ½ the size of the Byodo-In Temple in Kyoto, Japan, it quickly becomes amazing.  While we were there the bird man invited us to ring the peace bell. That bell sounded so amazing.

Note: some web sites claim ‘the Byodo-In Temple is a non-denominational temple’, but this is not true. It is Buddhist.

I think you can drive out on the Santa Cruz Wharf, but I have never investigated the requirements. It is such a nice walk, it dies not make sense to drive. Fishing from the wharf is fun, and does not require a license, I think. Last time I went fishing there, I did not need a license.

I have eaten at all the wharf restaurants, but I would rather eat fish bate.

San Jose’s Happy Hollow Park & Zoo is a fun place for day with the munchkins. You can let the older kids run wild and guide the younger ones through the park. The crooked house is fun for kids of all ages but help the youngest through it when older kids are not pushing them through. For some reason, the crooked house frightens the youngest kids.

Lake Tahoe’s Emerald Bay State Park is very beautiful. During the summer, Vikingsholm makes Emerald Bay even better. Visiting Vikingsholm is like stepping back into European history. Once you finish the twisty steep one mile hike from Highway 89 to Vikingsholm, you will be in one of the most beautiful [laces in the Sierra Nevada Mountains.

Lighthouse Field State Beach in Santa Cruz has two things that are attractive to me. First, it is away from the wharf and boardwalk area. Second, it is centrally located on West Cliff Drive, so it is an easy walk to almost everything. Sometimes the drummers come here for an all day and night drum fest, but otherwise, it is a quiet beach.

Waimea Bay Beach Park is obviously next to Waimea Bay. Be very careful surfing at Waimea Bay; the waves get huge and treacherous. Waimea Bay has lots of room for having fun though, climbing the rock, jumping from the rock, volleyball, BBQ, swimming, and snorkeling. Waimea Bay is very beautiful, so just come and have fun.

Wawamalu Beach Park is next to Sandy Beach. Sandy Beach gets crowded but mostly it is locals. Just a word of warning: Sandy Beach waves can be very dangerous. If you’re not an expert surfer, don’t do it here. The shore-break us not normal, so this is a great place to brake your neck or back.

One of my grandmothers took my sister and me to Forestiere Underground Gardens when we were very young children. I still remember that trip to Fresno as one of the most fun days growing up. Even after visiting Forestiere Underground Gardens many more times, I never get tired of the place.

Applegate Park is one of the nicest places in Merced. Sitting alongside Bear Creek, it has a very relaxing environment with tall shade trees. Whether you want to spend time with family or friends, have an outdoor wedding/party, or visit the zoo, Applegate Park has everything you need.

The Santa Inés Church at the mission is very beautiful. There is a daily Mass at 8:00 to get your day started. After Mass, Solvang has a lot to do from museums to vineyards to gambling to Danish celebrations with lots of dancing. Regardless of what you do, you will have fun.

The de Young Museum permanent collections are wonderful, but some of the temporary exhibitions allow us to see works of master or learn how art intersects our lives in new and wonderful ways. One of my favorites was the temporary exhibits of the Impressionist Claude Monet.

Just after moving to Bonny Doon, we saw signs for Beauregard Vineyards Tasting Room and Winery. When we stopped in to check it, it was unfortunately not wheelchair accessible. Hopefully, this oversight has been corrected. If it has not been corrected, please do so.

Monterey Bay is huge and beautiful, IMO, the most beautiful bay in the world. Monterey Bay Aquarium may be a tourist attraction, but it also teaches us how to ensure we have the bay in the future. A visit to Monterey Bay Aquarium should be mandatory for everyone.

Drumheller Fountain is a great place to relax and watch the ducks and fish. On clear days, it has one of the best views of Munt Rainier on campus. In the Spring, flowers around Drumheller Fountain enhance its beauty. Bring your lunch and relax for a little while.

Thomas F Regan Memorial City Beach is one of the best beaches in South Lake Tahoe. Also, it is the best location for watching the Fourth of July fireworks. Get there early for a family BBQ and let the munchkins play in the playground.
San Francisco’s Crissy Field is a great place for a family picnic, an afternoon run, fly kites, or just sitting watching people.

My husband and I always wanted to ride a train so where better than Georgia. We drove from Warner Robins and made it just in time at 10:30. We were lucky to find parking right by the train so I recommend getting there early. We preordered tickets online with military discount for $38/person for Closed Coach 332. It’s air conditioned with fans also but after a while I decided to sit in one of the open air coaches because the weather was nice and the breeze was cool. I didn’t like the smell of the closed coach although it had nice seats. The staff was very nice. There’s no mountain views, but one side of the train gets a view of the river at some points. We stopped in McCaysville for 2 hrs and walked around. I recommend the Toccoa River Park that’s on the map they give you in the train. It’s pretty expensive for what you get, but you’re paying for the experience I guess.

We had trouble finding this place on Apple Maps so we ended up parking in the parking lot of a park next to it and walked through a field. It’s a neat little museum. My husband loves Civil War history so he enjoyed it. Like other reviewers said, the price is a bit high for how small the museum is. It’s $6.50 for military, $7.50 for the public. We spent about an hour here. Unfortunately, the ship replica displayed outside wasn’t open for visitors which was a shame since it looked neat.
Word of caution if you have young children: the exhibit USS Hartford has a scary lifelike wax figure laying on a table wrapped up in a blanket inside the ship replica where the officers’ mess and quarters were. I don’t know if the figure was suppose to be there but it gave me the creeps.

This visitor center is nicer than the Beaver Meadows Visitor Center at the other gate. There’s a souvenir store that is huge. This gate is also less busy than Beaver Meadows. The staff are nice. I came to get the passport stamp and the stamp is severely disappointing. It doesn’t even have the date on there which is pretty much the whole purpose. It only says 2021. I’ve been to several national parks during the pandemic and they’ve all been actually stamps or stickers of the actual dated stamps. I’ve included a photo of the Great Sand Dunes stamp that I got that was a sticker but it was still very well done. The one at RMNP is just pure laziness.

This place is a hidden gem! I would’ve never known it existed until I got the National Parks Passport book and wanted to get my stamp here. It wasn’t crowded at all when we went on a Saturday afternoon. We enjoyed exploring all the rooms. The horses and cats on the property were adorable. You can touch everything. The parking lot is a short walk to the fort. There are nice, modern restrooms in the fort (don’t use the ones by the parking lot). They have a water dispenser to fill your water bottle at the fort restroom as well. The bookstore/gift shop has unique items I haven’t seen anywhere else. It’s also pet friendly! We spent 2 hours here.

This place is very cool to see in person. It’s like a kid’s castle drawing come to life. We couldn’t make it all the way to the top since we’re scared of heights and the stairs can’t handle 2 way traffic so it was too cramped, but anyone can easily make it to the main floor with the chapel. There are some holes and tough steps here and there so watch your step. Kids seemed to really enjoy it. There’s only roadside parking but there were plenty of space to park on a Saturday afternoon. There’s a little gift shop with stickers, magnets, and Tshirts as well as a little refreshments stand with hot dogs, snow cones, etc.

We came here before in April during winter and it’s much more beautiful right now in September/October during fall. You can drive to see the whole park on one main road and pull out at overlooks. Overlook trails are dog friendly. During COVID, the visitor center is closed and they have rangers with a table outside; they close at 5. You can get your passport stamp at their table until 5pm. The gift shop hours are 9am-4pm so no souvenirs or passport stickers after 4pm and they only allow 1 group at a time which is pretty ridiculous. Other national parks have a better layout strategy for their gift shops.

You must see this park if you’re in Colorado! The drive to the park is absolutely gorgeous. Entry cost $8. There was no attendant so bring cash for the honor system. It takes 30 seconds to get to the waterfalls from the parking lot. The Coyote Trail behind the waterfall will take you to the caves and to the top scenic views. It’s not strenuous but there are stairs. It took us about 1.5 hrs, we stopped for a while to enjoy the views. I would highly recommend visiting Harvey Gap State Park while you’re in the area. It’s very close to Rifle Falls and has a breathtaking lake with mountain views.

It was a decent tour and our tour guide was good, but overpriced for what you get to see. I enjoyed the Archives with the Aquaman, Wonder Woman, and Harry Potter movie costumes as well as the Batmobiles. You also see the set of Fuller House. However, that’s pretty much it. For $69/person and $15 parking, it seems a little outrageous. You don’t get enough time to read any of the plaques about the details of the movies. They rush you to get out of there for the next tour group so you don’t even get 10 minutes with what you paid to see.

Good park with great views and wide trails. You can see the Broadmoor from the trail. There is very limited parking, maybe 15-20 cars can fit into this lot so recommend getting there early or go on a weekday. The trail map is horrendous so we just took the trail on the farthest left and kept following it and it led to the reservoir at the top. Took us an hour to get to the top and back down. There were lots of dogs swimming in the reservoir and it was fun watching them all. Definitely don’t forget the sunscreen!

Beautiful state park with lots of trails. It was $8 for the entrance fee. We went on the Lake Gulch trail which has nice views of what used to be a lake. It’s really icy around the curve in winter so bring hiking sticks or wear traction cleats. We crossed the stream and took a left onto the Dam Trail. You can walk onto the dam. There’s mud, slush and ice so be careful. It wasn’t too strenuous and wasn’t too much of a walk. We did it with our dog and was fine.

This is a beautiful, nice park in the city that makes you feel like you’re in the middle of nowhere. If you take the full loop around the valley, it’s a good hike. If you want the best views, take the trail next to the porter John in the parking lot. It’s easy to get lost when you’re deeper in the trail since most of the trail doesn’t have a map and the trails aren’t marked. Take a picture of the map in the parking lot and you should find your way.

I’m sure the trails are beautiful but we didn’t get to hike it because it was so congested and there was no parking available. The quarantine made everyone want to go outside I guess. We found a pull off but it said we needed to pay for a parking permit but we couldn’t find anywhere to pay it. We kept driving and ended up going outside the park and found the Walker Ranch Homestead trail. There were a lot fewer people and tons of parking available.

None of the facilities are open. The Ft Pickens store, discovery center, etc are all closed. No rangers available. No national park passport stamps available. I wish they would update that on their website at least so people don’t waste their time. You can still go on the beach and into the fort. Ft Barrancas is the same way too, all closed. Hopefully saves someone else the trouble.

A friend introduced me to the Sunday market at the Temple and I’m so glad I discovered it! The coconut rice cakes are to die for (they’re 5 tokens/dollars)! I also love the noodle soup served by the nice man with the cool mustache (it’s 7 tokens). The fried potatoes are also delicious. Bring cash to exchange for tokens. This place is so peaceful to visit.

Wonderful museum with 2 hangars of aircraft. There was only one or 2 others here besides us on a Saturday afternoon. In Hangar 2, you can climb into the cockpit of 2 aircrafts! We spent a good 2 hours here. It’s free for active duty military members (not dependents) and $10 for adults. I think it was well worth it.

Nice park with a big open field and playground. There’s only street parking. There’s a nice pond with lots of ducks and geese. The only problem is there’s droppings everywhere. You’ll get it all over your shoes, and if you’re walking the dog, they’ll get it all over their paws too. Don’t let them roll in the grass.

I just moved here from Georgia and let me tell you, we didn’t have anything as good as this park. This is a wonderful park and it’s so large with trails and huge dog parks for pups to run around. It’s well-maintained and clean. I went on a Tuesday morning and there were tons of dogs there to play!

Great little museum. It’s very interesting to see the jail cells and the history it holds. They give you a booklet that corresponds to numbers on each exhibit to read about it. It took us about an hour to go through the main floor and downstairs. $8 for military and $10 for regular adults.

Great trail with beautiful views and so much history! Starting at the parking lot, you can go to the trail on the right for the historic houses or the trail on the left for the mine. Either way, it goes in a loop back to the parking lot. There’s a few hills but it’s an easy hike.

We really enjoyed the tour. The guide led us through each room and it didn’t feel too rushed. The house is beautiful and original. My favorite part was the Egyptian mummy which was unexpected but exciting to see. We spent about an hour here and would definitely come back.

I only stopped at the Elk Creek Visitor Center to get my passport stamp. The gift shop was not open so no souvenirs or passport stickers. The ranger was very nice and even gave me a free poster! He said the visitor center is temporarily closing very soon for renovations.

Nice lake with great views of the mountains. There’s 2 parking lots that get pretty full on the weekends. There were lots of people fishing around the lake and on the piers. There’s a dirt loop trail around the lake that’s about half a mile as well as a playground.

Very nice park and trails. They have 2 spacious, well-maintained dog parks, one for small dogs and one for large dogs. The trails are paved and shady. The park is in a nice neighborhood. The playgrounds look fun for kids.
Nice little neighborhood park with playgrounds and a big field. Only downside is there's no parking lot so you have to find space on the side of the street.
Great park with some good trails. There's a large open field, picnic pavilions and a playground. Well kept and clean.

My experience had a lot of factors that were beyond the control of the venue. It rained and our tent didn't do it's job but because it's an island there was no refuge. On top of that, we had forgotten a few items for dinner and the store wouldn't sell us uncooked hotdogs nor would they cook more because it was too close to closing. I get that it's a rule but when stuck on an island, it would be nice to have an option.

You must remember I'm not big on camping in the first place. This will be my last tent camping if I can help it. If you are good at camping, you'll think the place is kept well and the rangers are nice. The island is neat in idea. Because of our night, we didn't take advantage of canoeing and kayaking so I can't speak to those services.

We had fun and the price was right for what you get. We have been to larger courses in the past but this was good starter course. They use hand breaks unlike some of the higher end courses. Nothing too tall or fast but at $40 per person and around 14 lines made it feel like a proper value. The guides were really nice and we had fun chatting and joking with them. I'm not sure I would go back myself but I would still recommend to others if they want a good first experience at a low price.

The bridges and bits of the terrain can be challenging to walk on if you have back or leg issues, but I would say most courses up in the mountains are like that, just be aware.

We tried to go 10 years ago but one of our kids was too short, they gave us a free pass to come back...10 years later they honored the pass.

Bev was very knowledgeable and had a great chat with my wife. The area was very clean and staff friendly.

There is 219 steps, up and down, so be prepared. The whole experience doesn't take a long time so $15 pretty person might be steep but we had fun.

We were at the Beer Bourbon and BBQ festival. It was a good time for hanging out but... You basically had to stand in line constantly. You could only get small samples of the drinks, which are included in the entry fee, but couldn't but a regular sized version. Good was all for extra, and not included in the admission.

Not sure I would go back again, but wasn't a bad time.

The park is nice for picnicking and convenient parking. The beach front has lots of shells so you probably want to wear flip flops. Lots of seaweed too, but still beautiful. There are better places to let the kids play but there wasn't many people out and my outing preferred solitude over play.

Though I'm not a fan of church and religion, this is a pretty place to visit. A bit sad to see misinformation about how natives were treated by the settlers but I suppose that is pretty standard in the states. The grounds were nicely lit for the holidays making it nice to visit after sundown.

Fun for the family. Make reservations for the Old Sugar Mill but be prepared to cook for yourself. Water is cold in the springs, 72°F year round. There are a couple hiking trails but we only walked a little ways. Was muddy since rained day before, so good to have proper shoes.

Really fun experience that we stumbled upon. We did the tour with three zips. There is another with more but we had one over 3000ft long and 60+MPH. There was also small hikes between zips. Staff was nice and funny, was perfect day, perfect weather, perfect time. Loved it!

Not sure if it's worth the money but it was an interesting place. Grounds weren't as big as I expected but I think I was comparing to the Biltmore, which really isn't a fair comparison. We had a nice time and with the weather being so awesome, heightened the experience.

Had to pay for adults and really nothing adult there. Kids had fun but price ruined it for me, if they only charged for kids would be better. Lastly, the fire alarm went off and we had to leave. I was ready to go but for people who just got there, I feel bad for them.

We have done the tour many times and the trolly can be a great way to get around. I feel like it is kind of expensive but we keep doing it so must not be too expensive. Troy was our primary driver. He was knowledgeable and spoke clearly so we could all hear.

The maze is fun but these things always seem to cost twice as much as I think they are worth. The hay ride is not worth the money. Shooting corn was pretty fun and only $1 for three shots, probably the most affordable part of the day.

Theme park, so it is pricey but fun. We love roller coasters and theme park living. We can walk to the park and have season passes. We go all the time. So much so that my son gets "bored" with going to the theme park.

Parking is actually pretty easy if you come in off of Universal Blvd. Number of restaurants to walk to. Yard House is good stuff. I'm not a huge fan of I Drive but if I have to go, it is usually here or point Orlando.

Laguna Beach is one of my favorite places. There were some homeless around, which I've never experienced before but still some beautiful views. The town is cute with lots of good places to eat dinner and treats.

Great playground with an old school carousel. Kids had lots of fun. There were a few unofficial vendors so if you are willing to eat at a flea market, you'd probably go for the options available at the park.

Fun and educational. Vern was full of information and great story teller. Wish my dad could have visited with us as he was an aircraft quality control and mechanic, he could have shared so much insight.
I could do without the cross but I get why people want it there. Lovely memorial with great views. There were some slick spots since it had rained recently so be careful and watch your kids.
The facilities were pretty nice and it got really dark for some good star gazing. Only downside was they happened to be doing a controlled burn that night, so too a while to clear up
We visited during the kite festival which was really fun. You can drive onto the beach, there are restrooms, and restaurants all right there. We had a very enjoyable day.
It's a very short ride, only 3 cars at a time. Lines can get long. Island has amazing homes so be prepared for jealousy and envy. You do get a great view from the water.
FYI, costs $4 pet car. Its a nice park with a number of activities from the lake, to camping, to farm animals, to playground, camping, and picnic area.
Such an odd painter but amazing at the same time. You can find yourself sickened and amazed at the same time. We bought the Matador for our house.
It's a lovely place for a walk. We witnessed more wildlife here than Little Big Econ State Forest earlier in the day.
Not a lot to it but just a cool place to hang with the family. People who like history will enjoy it for that.

The history of Purisima Mission at Lompoc is the other side to the history of the region, seen from a greater perspective of Alta California, the Chumash Indians, King Carlos of Spain, Mexico, and rivalry with Britain and Russia over otter pelts and territory. While Lompoc today is famed for Rocket launches from Vandenberg Air Force Base, and its reputation as the city of flowers, according to our guide in times past it was a stage of conflict between Mexican authorities and native Americans (the Chumash), with the peace being kept by outstanding Franciscans -- such as Padre Payeras who learned Chumash and negotiated not only with the secular Mexican and Catholic religious authorities in Santa Barbara, but also with Russian leaders further up the coast. If you visit Purisima be sure to go on a guided tour where you not only have access to private parts of the mission, but will learn the rich history of Purisima.

Most of Kelly Park is open but not the history center or Happy Hollow. Parking is abundant for drivers. We cycled to the park and meandered slowly along the winding paths being careful of pedestrians. Bicycles are not allowed inside the Japanese Friendship Garden, so we could only peek in from outside. The water features looked mainly dry but the grass was verdant and the trees looked healthy. Kelly Park is a fabulous space for families where kids can run and explore.

We found this beach a little before sunset on a warm yet breezy, fall day. It is isolated -- 19 miles down a winding country road off California Route One. It is rewarding, far from the hustle of LA, half a dozen family groups flying kites and catching waves, a splendid sunset, gulls overhead and sandpipers scuttling along the shoreline. Wrap up against the breeze, and wear solid shoes, enjoy the wind, waves, scenery and sunset!

If you want to find a place in San Jose where you can get away from it all, Quicksilver Almaden Park is the place to go. Originally a Mercury mine exploited in the late nineteenth and  early twentieth century Quicksilver is now a sprawling natural park in South San Jose where few folks visit. About one hundred miles of trials that are great for walking and running, and also good for biking, but beware of the pedestrians!

Like most State Parks, Castle Rock is a little off the beaten track, but we'll worth visiting for either hiking or climbing. Serious climbers go here for both bouldering -- in the morning they are scrambling all over the rocks - and for rope climbing (all the climbers wearing helmets). Unfortunately due to the towering trees there is little view, but the achievement of climbing to any summit is reward in itself.

The Fairlie Poplar district is growing, and there are several student friendly eateries, but it needs to both increase in size and accessibility to become a great Atlanta feature. The potential is there, but so are many lifeless, shuttered buildings. If there was a downtown community (right now it's the homeless, and they need a community) that could support local business, then Fairlie Poplar could develop.

Hans Christian Andersen Park is very cute, tidy and organized, nicely laid out. It's a green, relaxing space in a hot, dry place, perfect to get away from the town, to eat a picnic, to saunter around, to let the kids play in the children's playground. We picnicked in the outdoor gazebo on the bend in the river. It's a small river, but it was peaceful and refreshing, a good place to take a break.

Would you like to hike a trail that is both close by to South San Jose, and where hardly anyone else is about? Then pick the El Sereno Open Space Preserve. Parking is limited and you will probably have to hike 200 yards up a steep hill to get to the trailhead, but it is totally worth it. There are several trail possibilities, and the steeper and longer the climb the more rewarding the views!

Surrounded by artistic buildings, from the church of St Patrick's, to SFMoMA, to the Contemporary Jewish museum, to the Martin Luther King Jr memorial and waterfall, Yerba Buena Gardens is always fun to visit, to sit back and relax, to enjoy the tranquility with the homeless folk in the midst of the metropolis.  Yerba Buena is an oasis of culture within this artistic city.

The San Jose Museum of Quilts and Textiles is a.small.passive display of the works and collections of locals.. Although the space is circumscribed, with a little imagination it could be used in a far more interactive and interesting way. What they have on display is interesting, but it is a  small and umimmaginative exhibition with limited appeal.

Drove and hiked up Frazier mountain. Fairly barren for a SoCal park / wilderness area. Watch out for the hunters all carrying loaded rifles / shotguns, although there is barely anything to hunt. View from the peak is moderate -- huge telecoms towers dominate, and the forestry lookout tower is crumbling,and.potentially dangerous to climb.

The Elizabeth Gamble gardens, donated by the Gamble family of Procter and Gamble renown, are a splendid community center piece in suburban Palo Alto. Flowering plants, vegetables and trees around.. The beauty is.in the details. My favorite part is the cool,. covered brick patio that houses this potted ferns.

The Rose Garden is cared for year round, and most pleasant on a sunny afternoon. You can smell the roses, spread out your blanket on the lush grass, watch the children play around the fountain, and enjoy this spot of well tendedl beauty.  A great place to unwind and feel good about life.

The Presidio's Main Post consists of Large, open, flat lawns sloping towards the Bay, next to the Golden Gate Bridge. Strong breezes are a challenge for kite fliers, and lend a healthful fresh air feel to this community green. Fabulous on a sunny day, wrap up warm when it's colder!

Spacious and beautiful park with amazing trails, particularly around the lake. Parking is free, there is swimming in the summer, and you can hike either one hundred yards or ten miles. Just over the hill from Kensington, El Cerrito, and Berkeley, easy to find yet away from it all.

St Mary's Square is an oasis of fresh air and peacefulness next to the heart of Chinatown. It's a great place for a lunchtime break away from the hectic busyness of the office, and also a pleasant spot for quiet reflection when you need to clear your head or chat with a friend.

Unpretentious yet serene, a haven for family and friends to hang out. The lawn is shaded and green, picnic tables abundant, parking extensive, and a different band plays weekly during the summer in non pandemic times. Food trucks also show up when the bands do!

A 220 degree panaroma of gentle mountains, and the trail head for walks, either up to a vantage point, or down to the waters edge of the meandering reservoir. Great for either sunrise or sunset walks. Avoid the heat of the day because there is little shade.

The aquatic park is good with both lap and recreational swimming, but it is only open from June to Labor Day because the pool depends on student lifeguards (who are only available during summer break). It's and it's outdoor pool and pleasant to swim there.

Shoreline Park is always a peaceful retreat whether you want to walk, jog, bike, boat, play volleyball or just chill. You can run or cycle for a few hours, six miles in one direction, ten miles in the other.
The limiting factor for Shoreline Lake Boathouse is the size of the lake. Renting a water craft here is fine for beginners, but if you hope to sail any distance the lake is just too small.
A sun filled day in Chinatown, San Francisco, gently mascerating fresh steamed char siew bau, each morsel of fluffy pastry and creamy savory pork delighting my taste buds.
I love this park. If you want to go somewhere quiet and open that's nearby, Rotary Park males for a great outdoors socially distanced meeting place when the 🌞 is out?
Los Gatos creek park connects Campbell park with Vasona Lake park along the Stevens Creek trail. You can jog and cycle for miles! It's a fabulous outdoors area
There's some construction activity going on right now, but you can still walk around and enjoy the open air setting

I hardly give anything a 5 star but I am giving this place a 5.
Since the time i read about this place i wanted to go here and it turned out to be better than my expectations. It gives you a venice kind of a feel and its actually a small locality . Its not a tourist place or  something so its very less crowded. There are these small channels of water running betwee the houses and its pawed with pedestrian path all along. If you have a baby you can carry a stroller. Then there are these bridges which connect the two ends.. Its a beautiful place. The houses are very beautiful too. There is also a small park for kids to play.. I visited this place with my wife and kid and they too enjoyed it a lot. Hard to find such a peaceful place in LA. You have some parking on the street nearby.

One of the biggest and unique of the metro parks of the city. First thing first. They have a great nature center with lots to explore and look around. Live stream and species preserves being a few from kids standards. Then they have a big creek to look out for just half a mile down the nature center. Canoeing is a huge fun there. Then the wetlands and bisons are worth watching for and of course lots of trails for everyone. They also have a nice sand volleyball court.

Great place if you like being amongst nature.

1. Parking was full and i had to park down the road
2. One of the most picturesque hikes i have done with view of mt rainier on one side and wild flowers all along the way
3. The entire loop was 3.9 miles per my recording and was pretty easy. Did it with my 3 year old on my shoulders.
4. People were considerate and wore masks
5. Do it clockwise for good views of rainier
6. Lot of bugs so carry bug spray or full sleeved clothes
7. There was slight snow patches but easy to cross with regular shoes

If you are a travel freak and looking for something different , other than the beach all the time in california then this is the place to be.

Its a vast stretch of desert, but beware that there are no springs as such as of today.

The landscape is amazing and the cacti growing are a good sight for the eye.

The temperature is quite a lot so take plenty of water and stuff to eat because you might not find any stores open between vast stretches of land.

Overall enjoyed it

Its a beautiful place to be with your family.. Just loved it. I had a family picnic here near the waters in the sand and all of us enjoyed it. An impressive site.  It is out of the way, away from the main tourist attractions of DC, but a very important story for all Americans to know.  The home is high on a bluff overlooking Washington, above the Anacostia neighborhood, across the river in South East DC. The concrete visitors center is dug out of the side of the hill.  You start your tour here with quotes from his writings and a timeline of his life followed by a video of his life story.  The house can only be seen by guided tours of 10 people so call ahead to make a reservation.  The house is very large and decorated in the late 19th century style.  Since the home stayed in the family it has many of the original family artifacts. The National Parks Service needs to make a new video and make sure their staff are more thoroughly trained on the story of Frederick Douglass's life.  Definitely worth a visit. Makes me want to know more about this important man's life.

Mush trail and the fire road both lead up to eagle rock. Its about 5 miles roundtrip. Mush trail has more shade and its nicer. Amazing views of the hills and get a glimpse on the ocean on a clear day.  State park, keep it clean please and enjoy.

Another getaway from the city, just a short drive out near Altadena/Pasadena.
Easy and short trail, mostly shaded and nice waterfall. 20 minutes each way.
Parking is with a prepaid park pass. Alternative to park on the side of the road.
Entrance to trail is passed the millards camp ground. Just follow the water stream all the way up.
Keep the place clean.
Follow me on Instagram @ happy_explorer_2

A must visit while in New York. Free to walk around. They never built over the original spot of the twin towers building. There a north and south pool with all the names of people who died that day there. Museum has admission fee. Below, underground is the Westfield mall. Park area closes am hour before sunset.
*Strict covid19 rules.. only one entrance and exit.

Known as the best arts museum in the West coast. Several buildings showcasing on rotation various arts from ancient historic paintings to Modern Arts. Year Memership for a student is $23. It's centrally located on Wilshire and la brea. Nearby is the Wilshire lights and tarpits museum. It's a nice area even to walk around which is free.

Huge park. Plenty of parking, $11 for day pass per car , $5 for senior citizens.
Seem like summer had camps passing thru here.
During the week it wasn't crowded.
Lake has small swimming area. picnic area with  few shaded areas. Bathrooms on site.
Lake seems like it was built from a dam..
Nice place to take photos.

I drove up to the parking lot. Small fee to park. Watch out for hikers/joggers. Free parking on the street level.
Great views of the city from the top. Option to walk,jog or bike up/down the hill.
Museum on top with history of the place. Clean  bathroom on site.
Follow me on IG  @happy_explorer_2

Famous route 66. Right on ocean ave is the entrance to the peer. Many parking garages in the area for 2$ after the first hour or park on the peer for $15 flat. Enjoy the arcades and mini amusement parks, street performers and souvenir shops. Great spot to see sunset.

Trail is very narrow and unkept and can be dangerous. It's mostly a loop but you can find a trail or 2 veering off.
Looks like it had once a stream of water but it dried up.
If u like a challenge u can try this.
Not much views besides for trees.

Several Hiking trails with beautiful views of the nearby mountains. Plenty of parking. Office/info room with WiFi . Bathroom on site. Bring plenty of water as there is no safe from the sun and watch out for those snakes. Enjoy the walk.

6/21. Sunday. No crowds and low water level. Free street parking until 8 pm. Medium 3 mile roundtrip. About 2 hours. Mostly shaded and quite nature sounds. Had to climb some boulders and use ropes to get to the falls.
Free admission. Small museum which explains the history of the liberty bell and the Independence of the USA.  Also houses the liberty bell Itself. Can spend 20 min in there.

Right on the side of the road.
Visited in mid August. Trees and plants weren't alive and fresh, certainly didn't see the butterflies. Gotta go spring or summer time.

Bike along the river and stop by here. It's like a destination. Right under the bridge. And the only lighthouse remaining in NYC.
It opens once a week for 2 hours.
Nice small park with volleyball, basketball,baseball and tennis courts, play area for kids. Lots of green grass to sit and picnic. Parking meter on the block.
Big park. Lots of tourists and locals. Watch as people play live music, performances or street vendors. Take a photo sit on a bench or grass and relax.
Haven't seen or been on the trail. Tbis location given on Google maps isn't correct, u need to continue driving down the road. Find out if it's opened.
Nice public county park. Rent canoes. Museum about the local history. Boardwalk along the watergrove. Tower overlooking the waters. Free parking.
Beautiful valley, its privately owned by the local tribe there. one can walk or take a tour bus down there. If u have a 4x4 car thats ok to.

Fun for all ages. Roller coasters, Ferris wheel. 5-10$ a ride, combo or all day pass. Arcade games, good prices.
Free to just walk around.
Beautiful place to visit in Hilo. Its like its own small island. Lots of coconut trees and palm trees, picnic tables.

Believe it or not, we went to the Bronx Zoo for a wedding. One of the premier zoos in America.

It is a huge zoo next to the Bronx Botanical gardens.

The ceremony took place in the elephant house since it was raining and we couldn't seat outside which was already set up until the rains came.

The reception was held in the Madagascar building, very nice setting.
likes: Facilities & Services: Indoor ceremony option, nice reception setting

reviews_attraction.text:
Very nice small estate winery producing around 8,000 cases. Located in Sonoma near the Carneros area producing mainly Chardonnays and Pinot Noirs that are natural  without fertilizers and pesticides.
The wine are nice but pricey. The only way to buy their wines is through their wine club or at the winery.

You can't go to San Francisco and no ride the Cable Cars. Since 1873 , they have been running and are the only moving historic landmark.

There are 2 lines, Powell-Hyde and Powell-Mason. It is better not to board them at the turnaround but walk a few blocks to catch it.

Right in front of Ghirardelli Square overlooking the bay. There are historic working boats docked at the Hyde Street pier where you can view them , they go back to 1886.
the Hercules.
For $10, you get aboard the Balclutha, the Eureka, and the Hercules.

A beautiful museum that has several building in a campus like  setting. They charge $16 to park in their parking garage.

They have an incredible art collection, especially modern with quite a few Picassos.

They also have a large Asian collection.

Sitting on top of Telegraph Hill offering great views of the both the city and the bay. just below is Washington Square park. It is a San Francisco landmark.

You can ride the elevator for $9 but admission is free.

Parking is a major problem.

An amazing wetlands in a very tranquil and serene setting. Attracts a lot of photographer who are into nature.

There is a long boardwalk extending into the wetlands. Great for viewing all kinds of birds, alligators, rabbits, and turtles.

The statue of Sun Yat-Sen is here, he was the leader of the rebellion that ended the Qing Dynasty and was the founder of the Republic of China.

There  benches and a small playground. It's a nice break from the main street of Chinatown.

Across the street from Washington Square Park in the North Beach section.

Built in 1924, best known for pictures of Joe DiMaggio and Marilyn Monroe after their wedding at City hall because he never had his first wedding annulled.

A landmark winery that is huge. Fortunately they serve reserve wines in their tasting room that are only sold there. The creator of  white zinfandel.

There is a very nice gift shop in the tasting room with wine related items.

Yerba Buena Gardens is a 5 acre park just south of market Street and across the street from SFMOMA San Francisco Museum of Modern Art. Also houses the Yerba Buena Center for the Arts.

They have beautiful wall fall.

Not a big fan of casinos but Seminole has some very nice upscale restaurants. Sorrisi, Italian and NYY Steakhouse.

Even though they allow smoking on the 2nd level. you still can smell it in the main casino.

Built in 1847 and is one of the first parks in the city. Unfortunately it is currently closed because of renovations.

It sits just below Coit Tower and across the street from Saints peter and Paul Church

Very Impressive,. right in the heart of Boca.

Picnic areas, tons of sports fields, a carousel, science museum, and roller hockey rink.

There is a playground with many fun activities for kids of all ages

We were there years ago before it underwent a major expansion.

This time they had an Andy Warhol exhibit that was fantastic in addition to their contemporary permanent collection.

California's first building built expressly to be a cathedral in 1854. It was gutted by 2 major fires, one being the 1906 earthquake.

Look at the clock tower on top of the church.

An oasis in the middle of civilization. A great place to see Japanese nature at its best.

A very calm, sincere setting. Unfortunately the museum was closed for renovation.
Great park sandwiched between I-95 and lake Ida. A long narrow park with the dog park at the end. They have 2 playgrounds and lots of picnic tables overlooking the lake.

Called Suicide bridge by the locals because of the number of people who have jumped from the bridge.

They have very interesting street lamps on the sides of the bridge.

Located at the end of Atlantic Avenue bordering the Everglades. A huge park that really has only 3 venues.

Archery, radio-controlled planes and boats.

World Famous

Great view of the world famous Hollywood sign from the Griffith Observatory.

Perched on the mountain with nothing around it.
To celebrate it's 75 anniversary, an artist created the world's largest LED light sculpture dancing on the bridges' cables at night.
Another iconic landmark that symbolizes San Francisco and was it's tallest building until 2017 when the Salesforce Tower was built.

Located in a park which has a golf course. Right on the outskirts of Pasadena.
. Unfortunately it was closed for a private event.

Don't waste your time or money. They had a temporary showing of a local potter, fair.

The rest of the museum was non existent.

This Museum home is well worth a visit if for nothing else than to say that you've been to Graceland and saw where the king lived. The tours are well-organized but but can make you feel a bit like cattle when you're going through them. Parts of the two are bottleneck and it can become very crowded. I would recommend going early and trying to be in the first group of the day.

What a wonderful day trip with family, friends, or kids. The trip into the red woods is beautiful and a great length for the price of the ticket. At the Midway point of the trip you can get off and explore or use the restroom during a ten minute break. Roaring camp itself has food and entertainment, along with a shop with souvenirs. I highly recommend a trip to Roaring Camp!

They said we wouldn't know what we were in for when we showed up that night and they were telling the truth. Our lineup had five artists including Rascal Flatts and Keith Urban. However during the performance we also had The Oak Ridge Boys and Blake Shelton show up for surprise performances. It was a great night at the Opry and one my mom and I will never forget.

A wonderful beach to walk and spend time on. My husband and I like to walk from this beach to the Monterey wharf and back. It's usually relatively quiet and a pleasant walk. Big Little Lies has an ad out which shows this beach as a set location. I hope this beach keeps it's charm. Not a lot of parking, so be aware. No bon fires.

When I went they were very busy. The views and location were gorgeous do I was excited to try the wines. They have only Syrah and Petite Sirah, which is not my cup of tea. They served bread while we tasted which was awesome and we were able to sit outside and pet several winery animals.

This is probably one of the most beautiful places in the world. As a local, I always find myself wanting to return. Great hiking trails and views including a handicap accessible trail! Point Lobos is amazing. This is one of the best places on the Monterey Peninsula.

Large clean park that is well-maintained with lots of interesting places to stop and smell the flowers. Also there are several exhibits or statues to stop at for entertainment. Between the fighter jets and the suffragettes I was will entertained in this park.

Garland offers lots of hiking, biking, and riding trails. At the info station you can borrow or buy a map which is nice. It can get hot at Garland so be sure to bring water! Hiking can be flat or uphill depending on your preference.

Clean facility with helpful staff. Compared to other casinos in the area, this one seemed to have better ventilation and was less smokey. I enjoyed the range of slot machines they had and was easily able to find my way around.

This is a small little Museum but the sound booths downstairs with all the different Hall of Fame artists was a lot of fun to sit in and play with. The history and music is amazing and is well worth the price of admission.

Beautiful location with great seating options. Food truck on Saturdays. I love their late harvest wine, but their prices have a bit of a range on them so double check the prices on the bottles you fall in love with!

Great facility for a conference. My only complaint is that the bathrooms are freezing! The center is well maintained and staff are helpful when you're lost and not sure where to go. Great artwork on the walls!

So. Many. People. This is by far the most crowded rating room in Paso. But it's also completely free. They have something for everyone and will help you find what you like. Great staff and a great location.

There is no place quite like it, and it is the place to go in Monterey. Highly recommend. The temporary exhibits are amazing and definitely worth going to see even if you've been to the aquarium before.

Great hiking, great trails. Big hill is worth the hike! Be sure not to leave things out and visible in your car! So many people leave things so that they can easily be seen through a window! Be aware!
Beautiful location for a relaxing stroll. It's currently under construction and all the water has been let out but I could still get a sense of what it would be like if I hadn't gone during winter.
One of my favorite hiking spots! The trails are usually perfect but can get muddy after rains. Not overly popular but also well used. I love the red woods and the water! Such a beautiful place!
Lots of interactive exhibits for those of all ages. Even if you're not a fan of country music there is a lot of history to see and here in this Hall of Fame. Well worth the price of admission.
So many wines at great values! I love the Distraction and their sweet dessert wines. Pear Valley has a beautiful location that is hard to beat. Everytime I'm in Paso I have to stop!
Great place to get a sense of old California history. It was well worth the $6 to get in! There are hiking trails as well as historic sites to visit.
Amazing place to hike! Great views and scenery! Parking can be tricky if you going a busy day. It may be worth it to figure out the bus system.
Beautiful secluded spot to start a long walk along the recreational trail. I love coming here around sunset, great spot!
Free tasting! Very good wines around $35 price point. The tasting room is clean and has lots of cool swag you can buy!
Beautiful location with lots of places to pull off and park. Mornings may be cold but there is no better time to go.
I got married here! I love this park. It's small and near the water but it's also right by the road.

This review is for the building / grounds only. Simply beautiful - you would think this was a statehouse instead of the city hall of a suburban city. Some of you may recognize the facade as part of the opening credits for the NBC sitcom "Parks & Rec" . To the right of the entrance, there is a statue commemorating Jackie Robinson and his brother, both Pasadena natives. Walk inside the building to see the central rose garden. Just a beautifully executed municipal building.

Out beyond the Western edge of Grand Junction, a nice monument run by the National Park Service. I recommend driving to Fruita and starting on the Western end then driving back towards Grand Junction. You are closer to the visitor center that way, and also end your trip nearer to Grand Junction. Took away one star only because a road closure lead to a detour (which is fine) but the detour added THIRTY minutes of driving and was very poorly marked.

Nice wooded area near 610-West and Memorial Park. Easy access and ample parking, but the parking is metered. The system is not use-friendly. If you can park for free at nearby Memorial Park and walk over, that might be better.

There are many trails but not all are well-marked. While this is a unique spot within Houston worth visiting, it pales in comparison to other arboretums of similar size or even smaller cities around the US.

Lovely garden just outside downtown Dallas. We went around Christmas and they had large Merry go round type displays with each item from the song 12 Days of Christmas. There are many trails and gardens to walk. There is also an adjacent children's garden which is an additional charge. Basically there's something for everyone. Plenty of parking available but it costs $10 (free for members). Would definitely visit again!

Beautiful garden next to Hermann Park. Hours vary by season but generally 9-5p. Free parking adjacent. Great place to take kids. Could easily spend 1-2 hours strolling around and exploring. Towards the back, there is a statuary with statues of internationally important figures. Nothing else quite like this place in Houston.

Easy access by T, but streets around get congested very easily. Lots of dining options in Kenmore and in Fenway itself. Most seats have good viewing angles. Plenty of concessions available, but prices are (unsurprisingly) high. Still, no substitute for experiencing one of America's classic ballparks!

Nice park in the heart of Downtown. Next to George R. Brown Convention Center and close to the Toyota Center. While there is parking directly underneath the Green, you can easily find street parking on off peak hours. The light rail is also close by. A nice spot to spend a weekend afternoon.

Terrific park just outside Colorado Springs! Drive through and see the unique rock formations, or park and take 15-60 min to hike the many trails nearby. The visitor center has a lot of information and a nice cafe / views. Many runners and bikers are also active in the park.

Great State Park about an hour west of Austin! Start early with the hike to the summit as it is the hardest and most sun exposed. Make sure to take lots of water and wear sunscreen. The trails around the park are nice too. We saw many hawks and other wildlife. Fun day trip!

Interesting site in the heart of LA where fossils are still found in the outdoor tar pits. On a random day, it's tough to make see the dynamism of the site by just reading the static exhibits. Keep an eye out for special exhibitions to get the most out of your trip.

Nice Houston park near the Heights. Several fields and open spaces to enjoy. Ample parking. Adjacent to White Oaks Bayou with its trail, about two miles from downtown / Buffalo Bayou trail to the southeast, and adjacent to MKT trail through the Heights on the west.

The main entry point to Harvard's campus, the square itself isn't much to see. The T stop dominates the spot, as Massachusetts Ave curves around the campus. Many stores worth checking out are a short walk away, as is the Charles River.

Outstanding neighborhood park - a hidden gem. Nice grounds, tennis court, walking/jogging trails, and rose garden. Ample street parking outside. Look out for hours for residents / non-residents. Weekday evenings are open to all.

Great classic ballpark! Easy parking just outside, nice seating with great views across the ballpark. Access to concessions is pretty straightforward. Just remember where you parked b/c it can get confusing in the crowds!

Went during Sail Boston. Great place to visit that's right on the Freedom Trail. The USS Constitution should be out of dry dock soon, but you can still see it being worked on. The museum is well done and very educational.

Great stopping point to learn about the Collegiate Peaks and get a great vista! The cost is $7 per car (self-pay), but they have multiple benches, outhouses, and picnic tables. Well worth a stop if you're in the area.

Excellent neighborhood park! Tennis court, tennis wall, basketball court, playground, baseball field (which can be used for soccer, etc). A 1/3 mile gravel trail surrounds the park, which is great for quick strolls.
Well-designed museum right on the Harbor. Interesting art exhibits, although some are a bit too abstract for my taste. Check the calendar for events, which may be hosted outside in the summer time.
Great little concert venue right off the Charles River on the Esplanade. Hosts the Boston 4th of July concert every year. Be mindful of extra security measures for big events, including bag checks.
Nice community park along Lake Houston. If you like walking, there is a 3 mile trail around the perimeter of the park. If you have time and want more of a hike, check out Eisenhower park next door.
Lovely art museum and sculpture garden within walking distance of the heart of Pasadena. If you're an art lover, a definite must-see. The Rodin sculptures near the entrance are particularly nice.
Fantastic venue for sporting events and concerts! Many great outdoor activities also nearby, including a 5k running loop around the stadium and adjacent golf course. I love running around the RB!
Small neighborhood park next to an elementary school. Covered Basketball and open tennis courts. Ample parking. Direct access to Lady Bird Lake trail.
Nice park just outside of Boston. Explore the old fort, fly a kite, or just walk along the shore. A great place to spend a summer afternoon!
Terrific public garden in the heart of Boston! Just southwest of the Common. One of the oldest such gardens in America.

Went here on Wednesday, June 26 at 8:30 pm expecting it to be pretty empty. I even checked the K1 website to see if there were any events going on and nothing was listed. When I showed up, it was packed with hundreds of people. After maneuvering through the crowds, I reached the front desk to see what was going on. It was some party for Vidcon or something. With the wait being over 1.5 hours, we decided it wasn't worth it to wait.

If you have a section on your site for events going on at different locations, at least update it so people don't have to drive out there for nothing.

Prices are high, so it's only worth coming here if you can find a deal on Groupon or something.

This park is great for car camping, hiking and backpacking. I've been here many times during Boy Scouts for the backpacking. Camping at the top of the hike was great. You're far enough away from everybody to really get the nature-y feel, but it's just a short hike back to the bottom. They have porta potties up there too so you don't have to dig your own hole.

You always hear about how the parking here sucks, but it wasn't too bad. My friend know where to park where it wasn't too crowded. We also left just before the game ended so we beat the traffic leaving the stadium. Sat in the AYCE pavilion area and it was great. I didn't end up eating that much, but the endless water was helpful on a hot day.

It's far enough away from the pier that it's not crowded with tourists. Great place to park and explore the beach and the accommodations along it. I parked here and went for a run, came back to my car to get my beach stuff and just relaxed on the beach. $3 per hour to park here.

A good beach with fire pits, but it also get really packed here. Fire pits are hard to claim unless you get here early and parking can take forever to find. The beach is clean though and it's fairly large (sand distance from the parking lot to the water).

This could be really nice park if it was better kept, but it's more of an area where homeless people reside. The lake is filled with colorful balls which helps to liven up the park, but they still need to do more to make sure it stays clean and safe.

Stroll down the Hollywood Walk of Fame to see all the celebrities being honored with their own star. It's neat to know that the celebrity was once there even if you don't get to see them in person. Who knows, you might be able to spot one by chance.

A nice, long stretch of beach that has fire pits. Get here early if you're hoping to get a fire pit though. People will come here at 8am or early just to camp out a fire pit. The beach is clean and usually doesn't get too crowded.

If you're even the least bit interested in cars then you have to check out this museum. They have everything from vintage cars to super cars. They even have movie prop cars. Check out the underground garage if you have time too.

If you're showing some out of towners around, this is one of the places you should bring them to. Everybody associates Hollywood with LA so they'll be thrilled to see all the signatures and hand prints of all the celebrities.
Large sports centers with fields for all kinds of sports. Just be careful on the fields. There are lots of holes and uneven dirt so you might twist an ankle. That's what happened to me there.
The park has been getting better and better. The library is really nice and there's a recreation center here too. There's a large field in the back and a full court basketball court here.
I haven't been here since I was a kid and this place is still awesome! I had so much fun interacting with all the different exhibits. I just wish I had more time to explore everything!
Very large Japanese garden with lots of running water. There was a bonzai tree exhibit you can peruse. Plenty of spots for photo ops and just a nice calming feel throughout the garden.
The Infinity Room was really neat and they had some nice artwork. I don't know if it's worth the long wait though. Hopefully the hype will die down and wait times will be shorter.
Downtown Disney has tons of restaurants, bars and retail stores. Everything is a little pricey since it's Disney, but if you look around, you can find something worth the price.
Lots of interested exhibits and artworks. There's something for everybody. The last time I went was to see Metropolis II which was a really neat art piece.
Nice Japanese garden to walk through and enjoy the sights. The price to get in is a little high for what it is though. Still, it's a beautiful garden.
It's a nice place to get away from the chaotic parks. They currently have a Frozen show that's pretty good, but I still liked the Aladdin show better.
When you see the smoke stacks, you know you're in right place.Great beach that's not too crowded. They also have fire pits which is an added bonus.
Large sports park with fields and courts for all kinds of sports. Parking is hard to get whenever there's a league game going on.
This park has it all! Plenty of playgrounds, tennis courts, basketball courts, large fields and even a horseback riding place.
Nice little Japanese garden located at CSULB. Pond has too much algae in it though so it's green and it's hard to see the koi.
Great place to get one of the best views of LA. This place is perfect if you want to bring a date here. Lots to do and see.
Great place to get a view of all of Los Angeles. You can see from the ocean to downtown LA.

A great open and under-the-sky memorial to US navy, the Plaza has several historic buildings and tiny monuments all around. It's sort of 'on your way' in Washington as you move from one side of the city to another, jumping from some history to other history! Parking can be a challenge. I recommend the city's absolutely fantastic subway instead. There's an out nearby.

Get off and walk around. Take in the surroundings. There's several government buildings of note within a two-block radius. There's also a few eating option for you or your kids, if anyone's hungry.

A word of caution, however: The area teems with homeless persons. Some of them can be drunk (even during daytime) and can be aggressive. It's best you stay away - far away or to another side of the street. Cops are never too far but they only intervene if called upon. So, note where the cops are and remember to signal to them if someone tries to get money off of you.

The Park is centered on Lake Hope, a relatively small sickle-shaped lake in Southeastern Ohio. It's larger cousins nearby steal all the limelight. However, that also means relatively fewer people frequent the Park. Therefore, the Park is closer to pristine, untouched nature than its counterparts.

This is not to say that it lacks for facilities. Access roads are good. There is a nice camping ground. The Park includes a really, really great mountain lodge-like resort. Do check that out.

You can quickly descend from the highway or the Lodge down to the pretty Lake Hope. In that sense, the Park offers the quickest access-to-realization-of-expectation that you can imagine!

Head on there if you want to get to a really pretty lakeside quickly and then want to enjoy nature in its natural habitat: NATURE itself!

Parking can be a huge hassle. However, remember, this is DC. Public transport is just great. The subway works great. Everything is very walkable - Even if you have little kids with you. Or, better Uber around. Plenty of restaurants in the vicinity and literally dozens of food trucks for cheaper options. Major food districts are never far from here.

Now, the good stuff: It doesn't work simply to go up to the Capitol building and take a pic. It's the whole area. The grounds, the little monuments all around, the eclectic blend of surrounding buildings. Look, it's all history. You can't just snap a shot of history. You have to 'walk through it' and 'experience' it. So do that. WALK. Walk around the building. Look at the little things - The water fountains and the lamps. This place is an experience.
likes: Attraction Type: Surrounding monuments, eclectic buildings

reviews_attraction.text:
There's really two ways to see and photograph the actual White House. One of them is through the iron railings of this park. The other option is to circle round and get to the view area next to the Lafayette Park. This view gives you a rounder view of the White House and you can spend more time taking pictures. On the Lafayette Square side, you get the more iconic, columnar Athenian architecture side - Even as that side has more tourists hogging the viewing area.

My recommendation: Do both!

While here, look to your back: There's the terrific Eisenhower Building and the gorgeous First Division Memorial.

If you're in Boston, you have to see it's Central Park! Is it better than NYC's Central Park? Maybe not. However, it's smaller, tighter and in some ways more complete. An absolute treat to be in, the place is riddled with monuments and sculptures. There's a great couple of ponds in the middle with an iconic iron bridge over them. Nearby are some fabulous stone fountains - each with their own sets of sculptures. To a nature and architecture lover, this place is a delight.

Enjoy your picnic lunch here or just stroll about. Hardly will you find cause to be disappointed.

Although this sculpture celebrates women in war, it still restricts women's role to that of nurses! Some tribute!

Anyway, the sculpture is well-made. Definitely one of the better ones on the National Mall. It's made in an suspended-animation kind of way. Alot of movement. You come upon it by exploring the National Mall area. It's on the side of the Lincoln Memorial. Google Maps will help you find it! So, Google this!

Definitely worth your time and effort because it's the only memorial that celebrates women in war - Amongst the countless that celebrate men!

Just the best eat-out district in DC. Google or Google Map the HUGE range of eateries that line multiple streets in a several-block area. From underground bars to roof top restaurants. From Chinese take-out to classy fine dining options. Chinatown has it all.

Interestingly, barring the Chinese gate in the middle. Very little else has anything to do with China! Not many Chinese either! :D

Parking will be a huge challenge. So either take an Uber or take the amazing DC metro. There's a major station quite in the middle of Chinatown. Easy breezy!

Go party!

There are several parks and monuments around the White House. This war memorial is perhaps the most gorgeous one. It's a nice and tall stone monument with golden sculptures up top. Great to look at. Great to learn about. Great to photograph. You can get the Eisenhower Building in the background. It's esp worth your while to visit it while you're on tour to visit the White House. Many people miss it because it's not exactly next to the White House. Just a hop away. Therefore, visiting here will make your visit stand apart and also be more comprehensive!

You simply cannot be in Monterey and not visit this place! This is the main show to the whole place! The Wharf is part of the historic district area. Has the single largest concentration of eating places and great bars. This is seafood paradise. Try to get your hands on something locally sourced. Help the local community and enjoy better taste!

Parking can be a mini-challenge. You basically have to find a spot somewhere along the streets. It's metered - So, don't forget how much you put in!

If you have any amount of interest in art, you HAVE to visit the Sculpture Garden. Walk around and explore all the various sculptures and installations. Esp the metal tree - if it's sundown - Watch the last sun rays gleam and glimmer off of the metal!

As spring transitions into summer, the Sculpture Garden turns into an open-air event spot - Multiple events happen here - Including musical performances. Nothing like enjoying one of those with a glass of beer and the sun!

Recommended!

Score: 10/10!
Why: Just the best space museum in the country.
Exhibits: Terrific. Informative. You learn ALOT!
Public Restrooms: Yes. Several.
Food: Nice big cafeteria. Many food trucks etc around. Cafe can be a bit more expensive.
Access: Google Metro and bus stations and timings. Very accessible.
Parking: There. But hard to find a spot. Not recommended.
Kid-friendly: Definitely.
Time needed to see all of it: Your whole sunday!
Recommended hours: 10.00 AM to 4.00 PM.

Santa Cruz is known for many things. But I would say it should best be known for the Wharf. It's a brilliant place to be. Great dining options. But the view of Santa Cruz from here and the sea is great. If you have your partner with you, you'd want to take a nice long evening walk here. Watch the old men teach the kids how to fish; The sea gulls fly about; And the sun break into a thousand shimmers on the sea!

This historic building has been dwarfed by skyscrapers, so you come upon it almost as a surprise. It's on a little triangle between busy thoroughfares. Yet, it retains its 18th century elegance and sense of history. This is where the Boston Massacre happened - the guides will tell you. Here's to the guides - They do a fantastic job. I've taken two separate tours with two separate guides. They're all fantastic!

History lies buried here. Not a place for the uninitiated. If you don't know history and do not respect America's founders - There isn't very much for you to do here. This is a historic graveyard. Many notable revolutionaries. But not Washington or Jefferson - The most commonly known ones. You have to know your history to honor those who lay buried. Kudos to City of Boston for preserving this.

After the Old Fishermen's Wharf, this is the second most important place in Monterey. There used to be an old canning factory here. This has since been converted into a great mall. The road that runs past it is the Cannery Row. It still retains the look and feel of a 1920s/30s America. Alot of eating options; Some shopping; Some great bars! Walking around in the windswept streets is amazing!
likes: Facilities & Services: Diverse dining, shopping, bars

reviews_attraction.text: If you're a sculptures fan and you're in Boston, might as well go check this one one. It's in the Boston Common. Plenty of history all around. The Common provides a terrific picnic spot and peaceful environs to stroll through. The ideal time to visit would be Spring or Fall. Spring - To enjoy the sun without getting sun burnt. Fall - To enjoy the many colors of the leaves!

In all of the bay area, this is perhaps the best place. It has some great places to eat by the sea - esp if you come upon it at evenfall. Nearby, often, you can see seals. Plenty to do here. Nearby, you have a museum, navy ships and guided tours. If you're a tourist or have kids to show around, this is the place for you. Totally worth spending an entire weekend day here!

One of those things you come to after having walk across the Maritime National Park and Jefferson street, and having crossed many piers and such.
