This place seems like a state fair in perpetual motion. Great eating places and bars nearby. However, it's especially good for children. They'll have a blast! Go there at night when the lights come on!

One of two main monuments in Washington that celebrate women in war. While the other one near the Lincoln Memorial casts women as nurses, this one is a more general tribute to women's services during wartime. In this way, I find this one to be a far better one.

We need more memorialization of women and the services they're rendered!

History thy name is Los Angeles! This is a really old establishment and looks quite like a Mexican pueblo. Great experience visiting here. One of the lesser known LA attractions. Los Angeles by the way was Mexican territory before the US took over and many parts of the metropolis retains its Mexican influence. Cheers!

The Church has iconic status. Architecture is wondrous. Totally worth your while exploring the building. But anyway, this is church you'd see in postcards. So go ahead. Create your own postcard. Go there especially in spring and fall. Snap a few pictures. You'll have your wallpaper by the end of the excursion!

As you're walking through the National Mall and arrive at the Washington Monument all tired from all the walking - Drop down on the green. Good place to rest. Take in your surroundings and the experiences you've had. All the while remaining in full view of the Washington Monument!

This National Historic Site can well be referred to as 'Historic District'. Multiple historic buildings, monuments and sculptures. It's a good idea to get off your car and just walk about for a bit. Keep your camera on hand. You're gonna want to use it very often!

This is the iconic Harvard Statue. Take a guided tour. They'll tell you. The statue doesn't depict the real Harvard. Heck, Harvard didn't even found Harvard University. This and much more you will learn from the student guides! Kudos guys!
Absolutely historic! Walking around it is like living all those movies you've seen that were shot here! Think: Rush Hour.

Captain’s Walk is a true first rate winery (not like the touristy wineries you’ll find in Door County). And if you’re thinking, “there are no fine grapes grown in Wisconsin”, well, they source much of their grapes from the west coast (premier grape growing areas like the Columbia Valley). So the juice they start with is first rate.

Being a small winery, they put passion into each barrel (I’ve listened to their chief winemaker enthusiastically talk about winemaking and noted this first hand)!  The awards they’ve won attest to their success.

The low price of tastings at Captain’s Walk is unlikely to last since similar west coast wineries charge upwards of $20.  Don’t opt for the basic tasting, spend the extra few dollars and sample every wine on the right-most page (they will let you “revisit” wines if you are polite).

Although they do produce a fair number of “every day wines”, they have some real winners worth the price.

(8/2020) If you can find the 2012 Sangiovese, GET IT!!! I just opened my last bottle - 98 points; a true classic! Pay what it takes, you won't regret it (this is what money is for).

The last half mile is probably the most enjoyable.
The first half mile offers minimal views, but is fairly easy (and can be muddy).  The trail then becomes moderately easy, becoming moderate leading to the first two main viewpoints. The second viewpoint has a bench for enjoying the views.  Most hikers turn around here, as the trail becomes significantly more difficult and more muddy after the bench.  However, the last half mile is probably the most enjoyable (though moderately difficult) portion of the trail.  The view at the end is also worth the hike.  Shorts and sneakers are adequate, but long pants may be helpful (for the last half mile).

This winery is the place to come for more refined wines. Their wines tend to be finer than those from other Door County wineries. The focus seems more on traditional dry varietals rather than the sweeter wines prevalent in this area.  Prices for these higher tier wines seemed correspondingly high, especially for this area

I was quite pleased with the quality and taste of the wines I tasted, but disappointed with the apparent lack of knowledge about the wines from our tasting staff (although she did inform us that all the grapes are sourced from California).

A pleasant and scenic trail to Susan Creek Falls. The trail is only about a mile long and  a very easy walk over mostly flat terrain (very accessible).

Various signs point out featured flora.  The waterfall is very pretty and well worth the 15 minute walk (each way).  Parking with restrooms at the trailhead and also at the day use area across the road (much nicer restrooms with running water in the day use area).

There is poison oak in many places, but one of the signs points it out so you can recognize it.

A pleasant, easy walk to an old picturesque stone dam.  Mostly along a flat gravel road thru a mahogany forest.  The most picturesque part is the very end. Totally worth the 5 mile round trip walk, which can be done in an hour and a half. Turn left at the first fork (trail sign will point to the right) to go directly towards the dam if you want shorten the total walk (maps along this well marked trail show the way).  Recommend for repeat walks.

Nice, albeit somewhat neglected, aircraft and missile display. And it’s FREE.  About two dozen static displays in a small park for closeup viewing.

Many of the placards are completely faded, which leaves you guessing as to the item being viewed (fortunately, google lens has arrived to save the day).

Convenient access from the PCH (Highway 1). Definitely worth a visit if you’re passing thru. Did I mention that it’s free?

The first half mile of this trail (to Waipo’o Falls parking lot) is just a down and up thru mediocre woods with no views ( and usually very muddy). Just skip it and start hiking at the Black Pipe trail head (corner of Koke’e and Halemanu Roads) down the 4x4 road towards the Waipo’o Falls parking lot.  Definitely take the short diversion up to the Cliff Trail Lookout (signs mark the trail). The views are totally worth it.

A top tier Smithsonian affiliated maritime museum. Flagship exhibit is the USS Cobia, the most fully and accurately restored World War II submarine in the world. Guided tours are excellent. If you can get a behind the scenes tour (nooks and crannies), do so. Totally worth the price of admission. Very nice museum store, which can be accessed without a fee. Highly recommend.

The wine quality is what sent this to 5 stars. Not pretentious; ambiance is merely ok; but the wine quality trumped all that. This is where to start your Santa Barbara wine tastings and move on from there. This sister winery to Santa Barbara Winery is where the premium wines are to be had. Enjoy the tastings here and then move on to Santa Barbara Winery for the ambiance.

Pleasant and scenic park with a stream running thru it.  There is a partial dam across the stream that makes a good fish watching spot as the fish fight to get across.  There is also a scenic footbridge across the stream.

This is a very popular wedding venue for both indoor and outdoor weddings.  The outdoor venue features a nice gazebo.

The Two Rivers Community Center (colocated here with Parks and Rec - city hall is across the street) is a great recreational facility. Includes a gymnasium with a basketball court, a stage for live performances (including dance recitals), a racquet ball court, and a nice workout center. Very pleasant senior center as well.

Pleasant park with nice paved walkways along a small slowly flowing stream. Typical city park “wildlife” (ducks, loons, squirrels, rabbits, etc.).  Moderately wooded, providing shade for walkers and runners.

The park is especially nice for this area because it is essentially an oasis in an otherwise semi-arid region.

A quaint little museum spread out over a small meticulously restored “fishing village” (several buildings, boats, and a light house). Just walking on the dock along the river is worthwhile, and doing so doesn’t even require an admission ticket. Museum staff is very devoted towards maintaining this little jewel.

Very nice zoo; about what you would expect for a mid-sized metropolitan area.  Reasonably priced.

Although the zoo is of a modest size, several of the exhibits are quite impressive.  The butterfly habitat is one of the better ones and is a must see.

Many helpful staff and volunteers to assist you.

Spectacular waterfall, especially if you climb to the base of the main falls (easy).  Look up at the wispy spray and feel the downdraft. Small parking lot, but this is along the gorge trail so you can hike here from nearby areas. Worth a visit just to see this alone.

Easily accessible navigation marker on the north pier of Two Rivers Harbor. Parking lot and access from behind the coast guard station at the end of the beach. Pleasant walk and lake views from the pier.

Also a favorite fishing spot, especially during salmon season.

Truly a worthwhile arboretum. Extensive paths, notable topography changes, and majestic trees. Great for fall foliage enjoyment.

Many trees labeled. Detailed trail markers help you navigate around. You could spend the entire day in this extensive park.

Small park on the Manitowoc River used primarily for launching boats onto the river. Nice facilities. Has a paved walkway along the river leading to the nearby neighborhoods. Well maintained paved parking lot. Picnic pavilion and restrooms.

Excellent winery in a scenic location off the beaten path. The ambiance is great, the service pleasant and attentive. Above average wines.

The three ports I tried were especially good, which is one of the reasons I’ve returned here.

Very nice art museum. Quality collections of European, American Indian, and contemporary art. I especially enjoyed the Mt St Helens pre-1980 art.

The collections are extensive and need multiple visits to do them justice.

Pleasant park with several interconnected meandering paths thru it. Lots of beautiful wildflowers. Some territorial views of the nearby suburban hills. Very pleasant and relaxing for walking (a few benches are provides).
Fairly large city park along the river with many wooded hills and extensive trails. The National Ice Age Scenic Trail passes thru here. Very good cross-country skiing. Minimal facilities

This is a basic small city park. Has a grassy area, a kids playground structure, and a ball field.

Best for those local residents who live closer to this park than others.
Probably the finest Japanese Garden outside Japan.  A must-see on any visit to the area.  Best enjoyed at a slow, leisurely pace.  Very popular.
Pleasant park with very nice water views and a lighthouse. Ample benches for enjoying the views or reading a book. Public restrooms.

Great panoramic views from the top!
There is parking available at the top of Hetzer Rd for $6. There is no attendant, you just leave your $$ inside a small metal mailbox type of envelop drop container at the entrance of the parking lot. Parking can also be found on Jefferson Blvd, the north side is free parking and the south side has meters. Depending on the time and day you visit don't be surprise to find it very crowded and hard to find parking at times.

I suggest to park on Jefferson Blvd closest to Hetzel Rd. Walk up and follow the trail that is to the left o the entrance sign, this will lead you right t the bottom of the stairs. Be aware to bring water, and comfortable shoes. This stairs are a very good work out and will leave you tired.

Once you've reach the top you can go back down on the same stairs or take one of the many alternate trails that lead to the bottom right where you had started.

Be mindful of the animals, plants and nature.

With a ton of parking areas, you won't have to worry about driving around trying to find a space to park. Once you are inside, you get a sense of the history within the walls and is noticeable that this place has been around for quite a while.  You'll find restaurant, bar, lounge and the view towards the mountains that gives the race track a great backdrop.

The horses come out and you can get a view before they enter the race track and be able to place your bets. once the race starts it a high adrenaline and excitment time with everyone cheering and waiting to see the end of the race.
Before fun and exciting time

5 benches and 3 tables is the only things you'll find at this very small park. There js a tiny parking lots for 5 cars and 1 handicap and one water fountain. There is a small bridge connecting the 2 small sides of the park and a dolphin statue. Most importantly to know is that there is no shade at all anywhere.

From the 3 tables that are available you can get a good view of Catalina island as well as a clear view if the sun as it sets.

The park was dedicated after Marilyn Ryan who was instrumental in the formation of the city of Rancho Palos Verdes in the early 70s.

You can not miss out on trying the Original.. PInk's Hot Dog's.  Expect a big line, and be sure to bring cash. as you approach the conter you will tell the attendants what type of dog you want and with what toppings. I like getting the Guadalajara dog with wrapped bacon, chopped tomato andonions with mexican crema.  As you turn the corner the chasier will ask what would you like to drink , from ther Soda selections. make your way back to the sitting room or the back patio area , space is limited.
If you are in the area, you can not miss out!

Visited this place fro the first time recently and was very interesting learning the history if the house and the many stories behind it. We where only able to do the daytime tour during hour visit but the night time tour sounds to be very exciting! I like that the staff that was there was very knowledgeable and sharing details as you where there and we where able to take tons fo photos as well. no supernatural occurrences happened while we where there but I would like to come back again and visit during the night time.

Very cool area to go for walks, the pathway around the perimeter takes you all the way around from the gate and following the fence all the way around. You get nice views of the water, flowers, plants and you might come across some wild life that lives there.
At the time of my visit there was many different colorful flowers and plants.
Parking is available at the visitors center  where you can also find a gift store, classes and various other educational things great for kids to visit

Nice moderate hike and easy way to the water fall. I wish I lived a little closer to this place so I could go. More often. I specially like when the water is high and runs down the stream. Always be aware of your surroundings prepared and alert. Pack water and light snacks just in case.
All together makes for a wonderful and relaxing hike. Good for kids and others with light hiking experience.

I enjoy walking looking for names that I recognize of artist I know of and coming across other named who I had forgotten. Depending on what area of the street you are be aware that some part might not be as safe as others just be aware of your surroundings.
I'm not sure but there must be a map or guide that shows where all the stars are and how to find the ones you are looking for
dislikes: Facilities & Services: Lack of map or guide

reviews_attraction.text: Build in 1818 by Francisco Avila known as the oldest standing residence in Los Angeles  it is open to the public and is a registered historic landmark, one of the very first settlements of the Los Angeles. The architecture is made of adobe and you can still see the rooms and areas of the house as they where back when the house was occupied. very nice things to see and experience

I was surprised how big this park is! There is two playgrounds for kids walkways to tale a long walk a small lake with ducks and plenty of green area to sit. There are also tables and benches with BBQ areas to cook. Parking is on the street there is no parking lot so keep an eye out to park towards the side of the park you want to be near.
Very nice locarion and plenty to do.

A Santa Cruz classic since years and years ago and its absolutely a must! A wooden coaster that has a whole lot of history top speed is about 50 mps or so. There are posters along the area where you wait in line to board with facts about when it was made back in 1924. I just hope they never tear it down because it should be a historical landmark if its not already

Big park area very big! plenty of room to enjoy your time. my only thing I disliked about this location a whole lot is the bathrooms. It was by far the worst bathrooms I have seen. I can tolerate bath bathrooms in bad situations but when i have to go I have to go but in this case it was soo bad that I actually turned back out and left. This was absolutely bad!

$9 entrance fee and free parking. This place is so large that I was not able to finish seen all the exhibits in one day. There is a nice koi pond near the entrance and lots of different type of plants, flowers and other natural stuff to see.
The day I attended there where hosting a Ferrari car show  which was part of the entrance fee.

You will be able to find everything outdoor fun to do here. walking, hiking, bike path, running, exercise benches, soccer fields, basketball courts, Kids playground, golf , fishing, BBQ grills. there is so much to do and soo much area to explore is like I can never explore the entire place because the area is so large.

Although is jammed packed with tourists, it's nice taking a stroll down the steps from the top to the bottom seen the nicely decorate flower gardens as well as the very nice houses which I imagine must cost a fortune.  Nothing much to really see other than a street with lots of turns with a really big downgrade angle

Beautiful place to have an amazing view of the ocean, see surfers ride waves and enjoy the beach. Is a very well known location and the light house makes it looks very impressive and nice as well. You can bring your dog and just relax getting some sun. and the view of the surfers doing some high skilled riding .

So many things to see! Depending on what they might have at the time of your visit as a feature exhibit, some with hands-on experience and learning.  My personal favorite is the area dedicated to space  program. Bring your kids and be sure to see the Space shuttle that is an amazing experience just by itself

Relaxing and nice space overlooking the beach with benches, shade from trees and a small playground for kids. there is a open space in the center where people can do activities, and play. Meter parking is available on the side and nearby street, there is also a community center and a Historic library

This is a very nice Park very hidden from the main road and with a lot of this to do.  Playground for kids! Trails for hiking benches to have picnic sports fields and most of all surrounded by a lot of nature making it feel very relaxing and quiet.

Tiny little area of grass that is called a park,  it's very close​ to the busy street and there are not playgrounds and only a few benches available. I guess is more of a decoration tot he street cus there isn't much to do or anything on this park

Very nice area to enjoy a walk, photo views of the USS Midway and other ocean views. parking is a bit hard, there are meters and some parking lots as well. I really liked the sailor and nurse statue and the bob hope tribute area as well.

I like hiking thru this place that is not crowded with all the typical daily hikers. Option to see the original bat cave from the old TV show. Parking is very limited and be sure to read the parking restrictions.
Very nice location with a park,  walking path and clean restrooms.  Plenty of parking and the beach is very clean as well.  I like going to this place for the calm atmosphere it provides
This place is very cool with stadium bench seat facing the water makes a relaxing and nice time to spend there watching the ships passing by and later catching a nice sunset.
I enjoyed seen the airplanes they have on display and the history showing how and what things are. They space is very nice woth a lot of well put together displays

Be careful on the hike if it rained the day before, because the trail has steep areas and they will become muddy if it rained. There were ropes to grab on the side near the fences, but there are also alternate paths along the way that lead to the same place.

If you plan to sit on the pillbox, then prepare to go even earlier. If you get there right before sunrise, you probably won't get a spot. Headlamps are your friend.

Beautiful views all around. The worst part is probably getting back to your vehicle with muddy shoes.. Bring other shoes to wear on the drive back and bag the ones you went up the trail on.

Parking wasn't that difficult to find early in the morning. You'll be able to find some residential spots. Do not pull up all the way to the hike entrance since there's no spots available there. No bathrooms anywhere along this hike.

Get here early if you want to avoid the blazing sun!

It gets real busy throughout the day, so you'll be sharing the railway with other people. Make sure you bring water since it's a long way up. There is a certain part of the trail where there is no ground, but there's also an alternate side trail you can take if you are afraid. I see people take the side trail on the way down during this part.

With multiple water breaks, this trail took maybe 1 hour to get to the top. If you put some hustle in, you can probably get it done in 30-45 mins.

The top of the trail has very little shade, so be prepared for that if you need. No bathrooms available.

If you are a fan of cave exploration, then this place is for you. Headlamps and flashlights are a requirement if you plan to go in since there is no light. Inside the caves will be wet and slippery. You'll have to do a bit of crawling to get inside as well. Saw a bunch of roaches crawling when I turned on the light, so expect to find some of those when you're there.

Don't bother bringing camera equipment unless you have you have your own lighting or you have faith in your low light photography. It won't come out good otherwise.

Don't go if you aren't willing to get dirty!

Parking available across the street.

If you're interested in Hawaiian culture, then this may be a stop for you.

There is really not much to see here, just a little walk through the area inside. Could probably be done with the whole walk in one hour, but you might as well take your time and just enjoy the views since you came this far and paid to get in.

No point parking before the park because they charge individually, so two people walking in costs the same as just driving in. Only worth walking in if you are alone.

Bathrooms available inside.

This is a paved trail! As easy as it gets. Can be done with flip flops. Alternate side trails available for those who are adventurous, but those would need shoes.

Possible to see whales at one of the lookouts even though I didn't see any.

Sunset is blocked by the mountain if you plan to get to the top of the pages path to see it, so don't come just for the sunset.

Small parking lot available, which is not an issue because people don't stay that long and this trail isn't extremely popular.

Definitely a view to behold and enjoy. The view is much better at night, but that also means that everyone else is coming back at the same time. The area can get a bit chilly, so wear extra layers. Be prepared for all types of photographers, all types of flash, and all types of people! Low light photography is king at this spot.

There is ample parking at this area. The museum is a quick visit as well.

Only downside is that you can't get any closer than the allowable area.

Be sure to sign up for the infinity room early. We were a bit late and wasn't able to check it out, but I bet it would have been cool. Be sure to reserve your museum tickets online. You'll only have to pay for parking when you get there.

I also had the chance to be at the museum during the free tour slots and the tour was definitely worth it. The guide helps you to see what the artists were trying to convey. Definitely join the tour if you get the chance.

If you needed to see just how small we were in this world, then you have to stop by these redwood trees. Amazing sights to behold and admire. These trees will probably outlive us!

Redwood trees along the entire Avenue of the Giants. Ample time to enjoy your own area. Off-road trails leading to many different hikes. There's a certain path you could follow as you drive along the Avenue, but the signs were too small in my opinion.

Get here early or the close parking spots will be taken quick! Then you'd have to park along the driving path before the entrance. No big deal.

The views here were awesome. Trees galore. Big trees everywhere! Went on the trail that cut through a tree.

Unfortunately, one of the trails that I went to were really muddy, so we had to turn around. Either way, prepare to walk a lot and enjoy yourself!

Not sure if I should be disappointed by what I saw, but you'd have to drive for a while to get to this point. The drive down was pretty cool since you get to see the different terrain getting to this point. The actual arch was formed by lava and sculpted by the ocean. Won't last forever!

Since you're already at this point, you might as well visit 'Lava Taking Back The Road'.

Nice place to check out that won't take up too much time of your day. Parking is easy to find in this area. Steps seemed to be well maintained. There wasn't much people at this location when I went, but large groups seemed to tour at this spot as part of their itinerary. Be sure to head up the 16th Ave tiled steps that isn't too far from this location.

Come here for everything pineapple, but get your pineapples from Costco if you can.. much cheaper on the island. Grab some Dole whip while you're here. Skip the diner food in the back, watch the demonstration, and take a walk outside. The pineapples on the island are much sweeter.

The dried fruits were overpriced.

Parking lot available.

One of the famous landmarks of San Francisco. Shown in the latest Ant Man movie and is the destination of many many people. Expect all your photos to have other people in it.

Expect to be behind cars lining up to go down. Expect cars to be behind you. Expect to be going very slow down this street. Lastly, enjoy the ride!

If you've never seen elephant seals, then you're in for a big surprise. These animals are huge! They lounge around and you get to see them along the boardwalk. Definitely a place to visit.

Big parking lot available so that everyone is able to see these wonderful animals.

P.S. The seals do not smell good.

A really short walk to check out the Devastation Trail.

Once you see the area, you won't even know you passed it since it was so short. A quick visit to see how the eruption changed the surrounding area that used to be filled with green trees.

Parking available.

Museum was okay. They don't allow pictures. Only bad thing seemed to be the distorted glass which made it hard to see and read the descriptions. Bathroom was available and it was spacious and clean. No divider between the urinals. Bring student id for discounts.

Extremely short hike. Drove 2 1/2 hours just to get here, paid the entrance fee ($5/person, $20/annually) and only hiked a bit over a mile. You also get a bit of climbing when you go below the rocks. It's near Sam's point so maybe you can stop by there too.

A bit of a long walk to check out the petroglyphs. If you're interested in Hawaiian culture, then by all means, take the walk since this is along the way on the Chain of Craters road. There is no shade in this area, so get that sun block ready.

Very close by to the entrance of the park. You get to see steam coming out from the ground as well as smell the sulfur. How often do you get to see that? Take a walk along the trail to get the Sulphur Banks. This area is windy.

$10 per person for the tour. Very informative tour for their product, but pretty much the same general information as other tours if you can get a free tour elsewhere. Coffee is pretty pricey here. We'll see how it tastes.
Expected much more from the great reviews. This tube won't take more than 10 minutes to get to the other side. Extremely short, but still nice to see at least once. Bring flashlights if you have.
Great place to get the sights of the surrounding area. Many people came to get the views during sunset. The tower could be full of people. Parking wasn't too bad when I got there.
Parking across the street from the beach. Ignore the signs telling you not to park since apparently no one follows it. Was disappointed since I didn't get to see any turtles.

Wish there was a bit more shade in this place.

Not sure if there is a real parking lot here, but the spots outside the park are going to cost you.
Another quick stop along the Big Sur. The views here were nice as well. Paved paths towards the beach area.

A decent, small sample of the railroad experience.  Note: my review is based on a general visit with a regular train excursion.  For a couple bucks more, special excursions for the young and old are planned throughout the year.

Generally, kids will enjoy it, but if attention spans are short, the *regular* train excursion may seem a bit too long.  If you have kids, consider visiting when train excursions geared for kids are available.

I enjoyed viewing the railroad memorabilia... especially the working model train sets... very nice.  The train excursions run from New Haven, KY (the museum location) to a stop at a general store in Boston, KY.  In peak season, they run two trips which opens up the option to board at the general store in Boston.  I boarded in Boston on my trip.  Basically, everyone in my party road the *second* leg of the first excursion.  We actually purchased our tickets when we arrived at the museum in New Haven.  After visiting for a while, we then used those tickets to return to our parked car by catching a ride on the *first* leg of the second excursion of the day.  That's how it works.

Note:  If you begin your visit by boarding the train in Boston:  It is a small town.  You will park at this small general store.  Though the train tracks pass next to this store and cross the main road, the signage was very limited.  I parked in the small gravel lot behind the store and for a while I wondered if I was in the right place.  It turns out... I was.

The old passengers cars used for the excursion are vintage... very cool... and probably enhanced my enjoyment of the ride.  The route is pretty much a straight shot without curves.  The countryside is pretty, but nothing more than you will see from your car on your way to this place.  In short, this is a few notches better than a train ride at an amusement park, but probably several notches less than the experience of catching a ride on Amtrack out west.  It's a good taste of what it was like to travel by rail... back in the day.

I'm glad I visited this place.  Though once is probably enough for me, I may return to try out one of the special or themed train excursions.

This park has everything you need:  Streams, trails, tennis courts, basketball courts, pavilions, playgrounds, and historic features. I give nearly all parks are good, however, I will award a top score if they have a little something special.  For me, the special part about Cherokee Park is Big Rock.  This area wraps around the bend of a stream that has cut into the side of a hill leaving a chunky cliff-like wall of various rock ledges.  Hundreds of years ago, heck--maybe thousands, a large chunk of rock broke away from the cliff and landed in the side of the stream... and Big Rock was born.  The rock is easily accessible, climbable, and has a large, flat top where one could have a picnic (of course, one shouldn't bogart the rock).  The surface has been worn smooth from all the human paws that have gripped this hunk of limestone over the years.  OTHER COOL STUFF:  Historic Baringer Spring, the teepee-style shelter at Hogan's Fountain, and a Spanish-style shelter at Big Rock.  I like that there are park roads utilized to make a complete one-way loop for vehicle traffic leaving the other side of the road only for those on bikes or on foot.

GOOD:  Free.  Surreal landscapes in this area are beautiful and amazing.

CAUTIONS:  As others have mentioned, it is a rocky shore and it can be dangerous.  However, it's not as if anything will really sneak up on you.  The entire landscape is wide open and you can get as close or as far away as you'd like.  It can be hard to find as there is very little signage.  I found the place by knowing exactly where it was on the map and by seeing a large pull-off area (like a "dirt parking lot") by the side of the road.  There were a few of these pull-off areas in the same vicinity and I actually pulled off at a couple before I found the right one.

SUMMARY:  Waters crash into a rocky and "cliffy" shore and some of the water sprays up through a hole in a rocky ledge.  Sometimes there is some action every ten seconds and sometimes only every ten minutes... just depends on the water.  While the blowhole was pretty cool, I was more entertained by walking around the shoreline.  There are so many varying landscapes packed into this tight little area.  It's a freebie and the views are spectacular... I highly recommend.

GOOD:  If on the east side of the island, this place is a very short drive and offers up some beautiful views without taking up a large chunk of your day.  Asphalt or concrete trails with steps.  Very easy to get around.  Restroom facilities.

BAD:  Nothing.

CAUTIONS:  There is a parking fee, but just a few bucks for the car.  While the trails get you to those beautiful views in a very short distance, some segments are steep.

SUMMARY:  This place is a "must see" in my opinion.  Again, if visiting the east side of the island or the Kahului area, it is so easy to get here and see so much without investing much time.  The views include mountains, the "Iao Needle", botanical gardens, rain forests, and mountain streams.  Even after seeing it, I would visit it again on a return visit.

*GOOD*  Pretty awesome experience for those in a car, on a bike, or on foot.  This place is one of the most stunning displays of giant, colorful, natural rock formations... absolutely beautiful... and it's all so easily accessible.  *CAUTION*  It is touristy, so if you are looking to experience nature a little more remote, this place may not be for you (but it would be crazy not to check it out if in the area for the first time).  *SUMMARY*  Though this park is the "garden" of the gods, I feel like it's more of a "playground" of the gods.  Instead of swings and see saws, there are natural formations to walk around, climb on, sit on, etc.  A person could hike around all day or just drive up for a picnic.  Very cool place... definitely a "must see".

Good:
- good number of trails with easy to moderate difficulty levels
- many unique features including waterfalls and remnants of an old reservoir
- there are both intimate, secluded areas and wide open lawns
- great for archery, picnics, hiking, walking, and taking in some nature or infrastructure ruins

Cautions:
- no playgrounds
- there is parking available at the top of the hill and bottom (separate entrance); the lot at the bottom is small and fills up easy leaving absolutely no where to park; the lot up top is bigger

IMO, this is the best park in town!  Definitely should be visited often by locals and park-lovers passing through town should stop by for a visit.

Great park with so much to offer.

Good:  Nice trails especially around either of the small lakes... offering some unique configurations.  The dam areas provide some great views of the lakes.  If you like to climb, this park offers a fire tower which is something that is normally off limits at most parks.  Great views from the tower.  If you don't like to hike, the driving along the roadways is enough to showcase much of the park.

Caution:  There is an entrance fee, but this is common at most state parks.

Overall, this is a great park with a lot of offer.  Many have called it a "mini-Smoky Mountains" and I agree.

Quite a mystical place.  The mountain in the park, a volcano that almost was, towers above the surrounding, flat landscape.  There is plenty of atmosphere candy to absorb just sitting at the trail head at the foot of the mountain.  The trail toggles from easy to hard, but I would say leans slightly toward easy.  It is deceiving because it does take longer than it looks to reach the summit, but with wide open views the entire length of the trail, it's not really difficult for a hiker to guess his/her location in the journey.  I found this to be such a rewarding, relaxing hike.  Highly recommended.

Nice park.  Rivers, creeks, ponds, fields, and trails.  It has all the essentials for a good park, but there is a bonus or two.  There is an observation tower for those who want to climb several flights of stairs to enjoy a great view.  There is an amphitheater and a wonderful looking covered bridge.  Some of the playground equipment is unique and includes some features I have not seen before--especially one area where the equipment is more for an adult who wants to exercise or work out.

Overall, a very neat park.
likes: Diverse natural elements (rivers, creeks, ponds, fields)

reviews_attraction.text:
This place is a groovy oasis right in the middle of the congested city of St Matthews.  It's a piece of green carved out in ways both natural and contemporary.  Pathways follow the winding Beargrass Creek one moment and than rise above swampy wetlands via steel grating that angles around like something out of an abstract art painting.

It's a small park, but it has all sorts of places to hideaway.  Come here to walk, jog, meditate, relax or picnic.  Do not come here to bike, hike or look for a playground.

Beautiful, historic property and grounds.  Certainly a must-see, but mostly because of its fame.  Combined with other nearby attractions and sightseeing, it is very easy to wander onto this property and stroll around the grounds (one should not pass this up if in the area).  The only reason I gave a rating slightly less than perfect was because, aside from fame, I found some of the other missions in town to have more interesting grounds and beautiful architecture.
dislikes: Less interesting compared to other missions

reviews_attraction.text:
Good:
* the historic, tiered reservoir system provides a unique feature that provides lots of eye candy
* solid network of trails providing a great variety of atmosphere from city park to secluded mountain climbing
* great views overlooking the city

Bad:
* nothing bad to report

IMO, this is THE premier park in Portland.  Locals should visit regularly and if a visitor can only visit one park, this one is highly recommended.

Hosting a segment of Rapid Creek and the parallel walking/biking path, this park offers up a great place to have a picnic with a small or large party.  The scenery is great and other eye candy includes a few monuments and art.  Large lawn area good for a variety of outdoor games.  It's a good 'home base' to enjoy some hiking or biking at adjacent parks.  (Caution for the kiddos:  No playground equipment at this park.)

On my visit, most people were flocking to the adjacent North and South Window arches, but IMO, this arch was far more grand and interesting.  Nonetheless, there will still be other people around as this arch is part of a cluster of short-trail arches all tied to a single parking lot.  No seclusion, but very easy to see.  If dropping anchor in this parking lot, it would be a crime to not get a close look at this arch.

Connecting downtown to the river, this park of more of a 20-block plaza that is great for viewing the river in about a million different ways.  It's a great long stretch for walking or biking, yet there is plenty of green space to relax and soak in the ambiance.  This park is a great "catch all" for a wide variety of vendors in case you want to eat or have a little entertainment.  Overall, a great place to hang out.

Good:
- wide variety of landscapes; some carved deep into the earth and some rising into the air
- hikers should be pleased as there are plenty of trails of different lengths and difficulty
- plenty of paved roadways taking any driver to a front row seat for some of the most spectacular views

Bad:
- nothing bad to report

This review based on the Island In The Sky section of the park.

Good:  Beautiful park.  Unique structures (old log cabin, silos, etc.) that adds a little curiosity to the place.  5-mile trail around the lake.  Really nice pavilions available.

Cautions:  Some of that 5-mile trail needs a little TLC.  There were some eroding, wide-open spaces where there appeared to be nothing controlling draining rainwater.  Not a terrible big deal, though.

Good:
- beautiful property including a rocky shoreline and peaceful lawns
- super-friendly staff
- free to explore ground; very affordably priced to visit top of lighthouse

Bad:
- nothing bad to report

Highly recommended if visiting the Sandusky area.  It's a short trek and the investment in time can be as short or long you like.

IMO, one of the best National Parks because of (1) it has plenty of 'wow factor,' (2) it has a variety of trails in varying lengths and difficulty--all offer big rewards in the way of surreal landscapes, and (3) it's a spectacular drive--this road trip winds from high vistas to canyon floors offering so many different perspectives.

Good:
- really great water fountains for walking around or sitting/relaxing
- variety of green spaces and artistically-designed concrete spaces
- really fantastic playground for the kiddos
- was previously the site of a world's fair (causes some good vibes)

Cautions:
- pay to park (nearby lots or garages)

Grade "A" park with everything you could ever want at a park.  Fields for sports, playgrounds, picnic shelters, fishing holes, paths of various surfaces from dirt to concrete to please hikers and casual strollers.  The landscaping also varies from natural to artfully designed.  Overall, terrific park!

Good:
* pavilion provides rooftop access with great views of the park
* Heekin Overlook provides great views of the Ohio River and valley
* beautiful fountain and gardens
* great place to catch a sunrise or sunset

Bad:
* trails in wooded area are mostly unmarked and need some TLC

So many trails, but what makes walking or hiking at this park so great is the uniqueness of the trails.  Many are elevated and send hikers over swinging bridges.  Really cool place.  My review is based solely on hiking, but there are many other amenities at this park.

Great place for walking and/or relaxing.  The dam and 'Gazebo Island' are nice features.  Parts of the park have a big city feel while other parts feel a bit more nature.  Very clean and beautiful park.

Not the most spectacular, but still grand in its own way.  I recommend only because it is adjacent to another spectacular arch (Corona) and together, they make a pretty great end-of-trail destination.

One of the best viewpoints in the Bay Area. If you can, avoid the summer season when you usually can't see anything through the fog. Just follow Conzelman Road up to the top of the hill. There are several parking areas along the way, but when the road starts leveling out and you see a lot of cars parked on your left, that is the place. There are a couple of trails through the tunnels and up to the top of the hill for the best views.

Porta-potties here are disgusting. If you continue down the hill (one-way street), you'll eventually get to the visitor center that has much nicer restrooms.

Hawaii has an immigrant history that is different from the rest of the USA and is poorly covered in American history lessons. This village is a recreation of the immigrant life during the late 1800s and early 1900s, using many original artifacts that were donated by or bought from immigrant families. Hourly docent tours are included with your admission and well worth taking. If you have an interest in history and culture, this fun and educational place to visit.

The square itself is kind of underwhelming. It's a large concrete space with an tall monument in the middle that is covered in bird poop. Most people come to Union Square as they travel between the many high-end stores, hotels, and restaurants that surround it. Occasionally, there interesting free concerts or other performances here. During the winter there is a (not free) ice skating rink here.

Really cool little lighthouse with a great view of the Golden Gate Bridge (on a sunny day). Summers are really foggy out here, so avoid those months if you want to see anything. There are free docent tours of the lighthouse on some days which are interesting. Lighthouse hours are limited, so make sure you check the schedule before walking down here. Parking is tight on weekends.

Beautiful hiking trail within a big city. Start at the Lands End visitor center and walk all the way to Sea Cliff. If you have more energy, continue through Fort Baker, up the sand ladder, then continue on the Batteries-to-Bluffs trail to the Golden Gate Bridge. Then catch the bus back to the start, or back to home.

Extremely beautiful state park with well maintained trails and beautiful scenery all around the peninsula. Lots of different wildlife, especially marine wildlife swimming in the coves. There are several small parking lots throughout the park. They don't fill up on weekdays, but I advise coming early on weekends.

This is a large scenic park next to the ocean. Pretty views along the coast towards Waikiki and Diamond Head. Lots of picnic tables and open fields. Unfortunately, the park was closed when we tried to visit in November 2017. News reports say it may reopen in January 2018.

Large city park with a swimming pool, picnic areas, open lawns, and a variety of sports courts. South San Francisco is always cold, but will be colder on cloudy or foggy days, so dress appropriately. Several parking lots and public restrooms spread around the the park.

For some reason, the park is called McNee Ranch, but the main attraction within the park is Montara Mountain. If you want to hike up Montara Mountain, you came to the right place. The hike is somewhat of a slog, but the views are great from the top.

Not much of a park. No restroom, no parking, not even any park benches. Just very steep and sandy/slippery trails up and down the hill. Nice view from the top, but the view from Grandview Park (a few blocks to the north) is much nicer.

Small quiet very clean neighborhood park. A few paved trails through the forest. Small children's playground. No public restrooms. No parking lot and very limited street parking. Mostly intended for nearby residents who can walk here.

As you walk or bike along the scenic shoreline between Fort Mason and Fisherman's Wharf, you pass through this park area. It's not really a destination park unless you're going swimming. There is a museum here that I've never visited.

Pretty beach park near the island that used to be called "Chinaman's Hat", but was called "Frenchman's Hat" in the Magnum PI TV show for PC reasons. Nowadays, the island is again called it's native Hawaiian name Mokolii. Free parking.

Pretty forest on a steep hill in the middle of the city. Mix of paved and dirt paths through the forest. View from the top of the hill is somewhat limited because of the trees. Great place for getting some quick exercise.

Small park across the cove from AT&T Park. Nice statue of Willie McCovey.

There used to be a Chinese fishing village at this location. Then it became an office park. Now they have a big parking lot and this little park.

Beautiful and historic beach on the windward side of Oahu. Far less crowded than Waikiki. Beware that this side of the island gets more wind and rain and rougher ocean conditions than the south side of the island.
Magic Island is the eastern side of Ala Moana Beach Park. A short walk from Waikiki and just as beautiful as Waikiki, but far less crowded. Lots of free parking and public restrooms.
Beautiful art museum. Regular special exhibits keep you coming back. Come for the morning, then have lunch in the cafe and explore other parts of Golden Gate Park in the afternoon.
Beautiful museum covering the history of the Hawaiian islands and Hawaiian culture. Regular free docent tours are worth the time and give you a great overview of the material.
This is the second most crooked street in the city. According to city engineers, the crookedest street in the city is much less touristy Vermont Street on Potrero Hill.
Years ago, this was a lively shopping mall near downtown Honolulu. Now it is mostly abandoned. Elevator ride to the top of the tower is free for a nice viewpoint.
Interesting place to see the locks in action. Also a draw bridge and fish ladder (salmon season is June-August). Free public parking lot on the south shore.
likes: Attraction Type: Locks, Draw bridge, Fish ladder

reviews_attraction.text: Large public park with open fields, children's playgrounds, and lots of other stuff. Restrooms and parking lots around the north end of the park.
Easy hiking trail leading to a beautiful waterfall. The Marymede waterfall trailhead is nearby, so you can visit both on the same day.
Pretty park with a children's playground, grassy field, etc. A large reservable picnic area is on the other side of the parking lot.

This place totally changed for the worse. It use to be so nice to stop by this location. Now its different and nearly gone. I'm not so sure that this place was saved or preserved. From a cultural perspective it was needed as an anchor to show where we have progressed to as humans and specifically in this region of Los Angeles. Highland Park always and will be ghetto. It's in the neighborhood that honestly has nothing high-end and still is ugly. You see changes being done throughout the neighborhood but in reality it is doing nothing. Streets are still dumped and consumed in graffiti drugs and homeless people no matter how hard the authorities may try to reduce the appearance of morbidness in the streets of Highland Park. North East Los Angeles has a reputation and has been constant keeping it. You still find out about horrible events here that could bring anyone down. Consumed by sadness that follows with countless tear drops. Highland Park can't and won't be messed with. I grew up in these streets and you find out about the truths that many don't want to know about but they matter. It's always good to know what's going on around your surroundings. This museum was closed to make it a storage. The Autry museum now own the main artifacts. The location should be well intact with the artifacts. It makes sense to keep the artifacts at home. This Southwest museum needed to be saved. Very few stood up when they needed to speak up and to be heard, but Highland Park and the Latinos will prevail.   -Sergio Antonio De La Torre

I really enjoy this location for lots of reasons what can be that they play great music and all the spots nearby so get ready and bring your favorite dancing shoes. Some locations have pool tables so you don't necessarily have to dance they also have arcade games so we can get our game on. Most of the locations on this street are closing at 2 a.m. don't drink and drive. Please drink responsibly. There are checkpoints and cops everywhere on the streets and if you are too drunk they will arrest you. You have been warned keep that in mind, have fun.

Let's go Dodgers! I love this place. It's a ton of fun whenever I get a chance to go. I've been here for stadium series and I was able to see the Kings on ice here. The staff is really helpful and the place is kept clean. The food and snacks are great. I was helped out by Edwin Q. He was friendly and got me my food. I enjoyed the food and my snacks for the game. Dodgers won in the end of the game. Great place overall with tons of photo opportunities so be sure to stop by and check it out for yourself. Let's go Dodgers!!!

The place gets busy here with long lines and orders, however the lines tend to move fast. By the time it's your turn your order should be said perfectly. Pinks has been around for so long now it's no wonder they are still respected for their food and style. I recommend this spot to everyone I know. The choices are near endless, so there's something here for you too. Enjoy!

Aloha everyone. This is a very beautiful place to come and stop by and take a couple pictures please remember to respect the land. This place has really clean water and I hope if it continues to stay that way for many years to come. I do recommend everyone I know to come check out this beach. Mahalo and aloha.   Sergio DEE

It's a nice beach overall, however the rocks on the beach floor are so sharp you will get hurt. Be careful and stay aware of where you're stepping. There are so many nice stores nearby to shop at in case anything is missing or forgot. The spot to fish is on the rocks. A bunch of tourists here everyday. Good luck.

I was born and raised in Los Angeles California and I love LA. Once you see Los Angeles in a whole new way it's always going to stay with you no matter what. I highly recommend this place to everyone of all ages. It's amazing and breath taking. Enjoy and don't forget where you are from.   -Sergio/Tony De LA Torre

So much history. R.I.P. Duke. Thank you Duke. His name will always ring in Hawaii often. This is a great spot for his statue and to continue to spread awareness of his journey in Hawaii. Accomplished so much in his life. I always stop by when I'm in Oahu for Duke. Please be sure to check out this location. Enjoy.

Dark, ghetto, and ugly. Highland Park for you all. I've seen numerous times fights and gun shots gone off here. I don't like the location. The grass is even kept unevenly cut. Bunch of times I've spotted out used condoms on the grass, pills/drugs, and gun shells littered. I don't recommend.

Great location with lots to see and to do. You really are able to value natural beauty and the life all around it. Waimea Fall is very well preserved and kept. I hope this place stays like this for years to come. A short walk to get to the water fall and it's worth the wait. Enjoy.

A nice place to make you mind go wind with imagination. I've been here a couple of times. The tree is not always on at night but it's a good experience seeing this huge tree filled with lights and light. The area is a neighborhood so please keep that in mind. Please be respectful.

Very nice beautiful location. I wish I could live here in this wonderful place. I hope to be back soon. Pictures only show so much. In person this is bliss. I recommend this location to everyone. Bring the kids because they will love it too. Get ready to have fun.

I like this place because it is not as crowded as one would think and the beach is nice. The paths can be slippery, dangerous, and broke down. Wear good footwear is a must. Get ready to get covered in sand also parking is very limited.

I'm a fan however the jumbo screens still really haven't been to use. I saw Morrissey and Billy Idol 2017 back to back days. Both times the didn't have a camera man catch this and project this.   -Sergio/ToNY DEE
This park is nice at times can be nice just don't stay out here to close to night fall. I've seen countless gangsters smoking and doing drugs here. It can be nice for a picnic though in the day.
Great location that has so much to see and do. The hike is light and I find easy to do. Been coming up here since I was about 7 years old. Please be sure to check it out for yourself soon.
5 stars and it's a park. I was comfortable enough to sit on the grass and have lunch. The place is nice and all the people going by were nice too. Be sure to check it out soon. Enjoy.
This is a okay Beach to go and just relax. I don't go in the water and I don't fish here either. This spots is rarely visited by me I don't recommend it
Great place to hike and take a ton of pictures. Good for kids and hikers. This place is beautiful, so please be sure to check it out for yourself soon.
A nice tree that's been here for a long time. I hope this tree sticks around much longer. This tree is truly a gift to the world just like many others.
It's packed with mostly tourists and the lines are long. They're fast workers and lines move quick. It's Nice to check out for the kids too.
Dope spot be sure your 4×4 wheel drive is working and have fun in this place. My brother Rick got us stuck in mud once. Be safe. Enjoy!
It's a good workout. No doubt about it. It's fun and worth it. Take good shoes water and sunglasses don't forget the sunscreen.
I don't like it. I know for a fact that its dangerous here. I've known and been here for years. It's crazy! I hate it.
5 starts. You witnessed American history here and and most of the veterans from ww2 are almost all gone. Go.

(Translated by Google) I do not agree with the opinion that the Yosemite Valley is known only for its waterfalls and cliffs.
The vast territory of forests with tall trees no less determine the face of the national park. The freshness of the air is incredible. The recreational power of staying in Yosemite cannot be overstated.
In addition, there is an excellent transport infrastructure, shops, centers, places for recreation and information.
The roads are very winding, therefore, it is worth stocking up with chewing gums and possibly pills for motion sickness.

reviews_attraction.text:
You could get lost in here. This museum is full of history and has a lot to offer. Their exhibitions are always interesting and the architecture of the building is gorgeous.
The museum staff is rude, especially staff at the store. I said hello to the woman ringing me up for my things when she started grabbing my stuff to ring them up, she didn't even look up at me. So I said HELLO! 😁 (Eagerly with a smile) a little louder, and she continued to ignore me and told me a total and didn't even look at me, extremely rude!!! Avoiding the store when I come because interactions like that suck and are draining. Hire people who care or at least train them in customer service.

I love this place! I've been here twice and the views are phenomenal. I love that it's indoors, I feel it's just as enjoyable especially if there is inclement weather. My second time here we basically had the entire place to ourselves. The staff are great and I love how there are so many areas to create jobs for people in the building. The observation deck has so many fun activities! It's impossible to be bored and when it's not crowded it's easy to spend a good deal of time here

This pier is a great Philadelphia landmark and park. Super great spot to relax, enjoy coffee, hangout, take photos, or run/walk. There are so many incredible views here and the breeze from the river is perfect. I love bringing friends here or coming to just check out the pier. I did yoga on the pier here for the first time last week and that was fantastic as well! I cannot think of a better spot to exercise or do community yoga

Very cute museum with so many things to see and do! You have to go in one direction only so you cannot go backwards, you have to enjoy each attraction only once. The service is very happy and upbeat! The tickets are very expensive and there is no way to avoid the service fee when you buy tickets, in person or online. At the end the woman in the gift shop was registering people to vote and gave me a free ice cream scoop!

Awesome ice and roller skating rink! They play fun music. The rink can get reeeeally crowded so if you want to go fast you will probably get annoyed. It's a great view and great for families! I'm thankful that BCBS card holders get to skate for free (4 people per card!) This is a great way to spend time along with all the fun things to to at Winterfest or Summerfest. Lockers are only a dollar (pay with quarters)
likes: Free admission for BCBS card holders

reviews_attraction.text: I would not describe Clarion Alley as a tourist attraction at all. It is a space for the community to make art and send positive and influential messages through art. It warms my heart that San Francisco and the Mission District welcome graffiti and murals and see the beauty in them. I love and appreciate the meaning behind the murals and it is so pretty and enjoyable to look at as you walk through the alley

What an amazing park!! I came here early to watch the sunrise. The park was not crowded at all during this time. It is a small hike to get to the top and the view is gorgeous. You can see the entire city from every direction. The view surely is "grand" and breathtaking. There are places to enter and exit the park at multiple directions. It's super windy so be prepared.

I was able to come here with a ticket to the Art Museum. It's awesome that they dedicated a museum ro the work of Rodin. They are very interesting to see and read about as well. I came after walking in the museum for hours and then walking here so by the time I came I was kind of exhausted, I feel I would've enjoyed it more had it been by first stop.

I love Dilworth Park! Especially in the wintertime, there is so much to do and explore! Ice skating is super fun and they have an indoor "cabin" where you can relax and get drinks afterwards. The deck the hall lights show is a phenomenal show that goes during Christmas time. And in the summer it's a great park to relax and walk around in!

We came here not knowing this was a giant ferris wheel, but once we got in it was so fun. The pods that you ride in are quite roomy, they are enclosed and have huge windows and the view is fantastic! The ride also takes you around several times so you have a long time to enjoy yourself!

Perfect overlook park with an amazing view of the bridge. When I came in the late afternoon there was only one other person here. It is so peaceful and you also have a good view of the mountains to the west of the bridge. It is a good place to rest mid-hike, relax, or take photos

Great plaza area with plenty of parking and space. There is a huge open field with a great view of the city and a sidewalk that connects the World of Coca-Cola, the Aquarium, and the National Center along with having some great food/coffee places and some sculptures.

Great museum that demonstrates history so well. They have free movies showing and a large exhibition that I feel everyone would benefit to see and understand. The way that this museum displays and explains history and true life examples is powerful and impactful.

Huge open park with fantastic views! This park has a few giant open grassy areas, benches, pathways, and even a playground. There are beautiful big palm trees as well. It is so spacious that when filled up with people it is still easy to find a zenfull area.

Came here for the first time (outside of ArtPrize) when I had some time to kill and it was a very delightful experience! There is a lot to see and take in. The museum is quiet and relaxing and the art isn't overwhelming, so you have time to enjoy every work.

I love the Schuylkill banks trail. This park is very well maintained and the views are amazing and refreshing!! This is an amazing place to go on a walk/run/bike ride and it is also a good place to meditate or relax. I love coming here

Beautiful walking trail and park with many sights to see. It's great for running,walking your dog, and even a picnic or just lounging. A great place to go for a walk and see the city sights! It never gets old
This is such a peaceful and clean park, it's a great place to stroll through and get a good view of the city and the grand river. The park is also host to many great events
Great for tourists to see the steps and for anyone to come hangout, take photos, or climb them. Good exercise too! And they lead to a fantastic view of the city
likes: Facilities & Services: View of the city
