reviews_attraction.text:
(Translated by Google) One of the icons of San Francisco has been its famous "tram", which is actually a CableCar, and in this museum, which is actually the operational center from where the cables that allow the carriages to move are explained to you. while you can see it through your eyes.
If you come to this beautiful city, you must go through here. The visit is free and in a few minutes you will see and understand one of the things that allowed this city to advance in history.

(Original)
Uno de los iconos de San Francisco ha sido su famoso "tranvía" que en realidad es un CableCar, y en este museo que en realidad es el centro operativo desde donde se mueven los cables que permiten el traslado de los vagones, te explican su funcionamiento a la vez que lo puedes ver por tus ojos.
Si vienes a esta hermosa ciudad,  debes pasar por aquí. La visita es gratuita y en unos minutos verás y entenderás una de las cosas que permitió que está ciudad avanzara en la historia.

(Translated by Google) It could be defined as the center of the city, an emblematic point from where many tourist Tours start and where the main urban transport lines of the city pass, being a place where you can do route transfers.
Surrounded by different prestigious stores and hotels, it gives it a special touch.
At Christmas they install an ice skating rink and the respective Christmas tree creating a somewhat magical atmosphere.

(Original)
Se podría definir como el centro de la ciudad,  punto emblemático desde donde se inician muchos Tours turísticos y por donde pasan las principales líneas de transporte urbano de la ciudad, siendo un sitio donde puedes hacer transferencia de rutas.
Rodeado por diferentes tiendas de prestigio y hoteles, le da un toque especial.
En Navidad instalan un pista de patinaje sobre hielo y el respectivo árbol de Navidad creando un ambiente algo mágico.

(Translated by Google) Emblematic NY city building which is not only admirable from a distance, especially for its termination on the heights, but also for its facade in general.
The reception is spacious, the details on the walls and ceilings are worth stopping to observe as well as the information panel about the occupants of the tower.
You can take photos inside, but they do not allow videos or panoramic photos.

(Original)
Emblemático edificio de la ciudad de NY el cual no sólo es admirable a la distancia, sobre todo por su terminación en las alturas, si no por su fachada en general.
La recepción es amplia, los detalles en paredes y techos vale la pena detenerse a observar al igual que el panel informativo acerca de los ocupantes de la torre.
Se pueden tomar fotos en su interior, pero no permiten ni vídeos ni fotos panorámicas.

(Translated by Google) Small park on the banks of the Halifax River on its eastern bank, at the foot of Granada Brigde (Granada Avenue Bridge).
Highly recommended to go at sunset, well you can see the sunset inland with the river in between, as well as being able to observe it from some wooden paths that go into the water as it was a small dock.
Recommended if you walk through this area to end the day.

(Original)
Pequeño parque a la orilla del río Halifax en su ribera este, a los pies del Granada Brigde (puente de la avenida Granada).
Muy recomendable ir al atardecer, pues se observa muy bien el ocaso tierra adentro con el río de por medio, además de poderlo observar desde unas caminerias de madera que se adentran en el agua tal cual fuese un pequeño muelle.
Recomendable si paseas por esta zona para terminar la jornada diurna.

(Translated by Google) Emblematic place in NYC history and the US in general.
It is small, it takes really little time to visit it and you do not need guides, it is well explained with some posters. Despite being in a tumultuous area, its interior is rather calm and isolates you from the bustle outside.
Its staircases face the street where the NYSE is located and give you the best perspective for a good photo.

(Original)
Lugar emblemático de la historia de NYC y de EEUU en general.
Es pequeño, tardas en realidad poco tiempo en recorrerlo y no necesitas de guías, está bien explicado con unos carteles. Pese a estar en una zona tumultuosa, su interior es más bien tranquilo y te aísla del bullicio exterior.
Sus escalinatas dan hacia la calle donde se encuentra la NYSE y te dan la mejor perspectiva para una buena foto.

(Translated by Google) One of those surprises that await you in San Francisco, due to the variety of world-class works and artists in different areas, painting prevailing.
He also has one of the original versions of Rodin, the thinker, in his front yard.
Although far from the city center it is very well connected by public transport.
It is worth approaching and investing time in touring it.

(Original)
Una de esas sorpresas que te aguardan en San Francisco, por la variedad de obras y artistas de talla mundial en diferentes áreas predominando la pintura.
Posee además una de.las versiones originales de Rodin, el pensador, en su patio de entrada.
Aunque lejos del Downtown de la ciudad se encuentra muy bien comunicado por transporte público.
Vale la pena acercarse e invertir un tiempo en recorrerlo.

(Translated by Google) Excellent museum of modern art, one of the most iconic in the world.
It is spacious, pleasant rooms and spacious corridors, a good variety of works and artists from renowned to emerging.
If you want free access, you can do it one day a week from 5pm (in my case it was a Friday, but I don't know if it could change).
Offers cloakroom service.

(Original)
Excelente museo de arte moderno, uno de los icónicos del mundo.
Es amplio, salas agradables y pasillos espaciosos, buena variedad de obras y artistas desde renombrados hasta emergentes.
Si quieres acceder de forma gratuita, lo puedes hacer un día a la semana desde las 5pm (en mi caso fue un viernes, pero no se si pueda variar).
Ofrece servicio de guardarropa.

(Translated by Google) Small park at the back of the Natural History Museum for acidity When you get off the subway (depending on the exit you take).
Small external opening to what you will find once you have access to the museum spaces.
As everything in this city is worth walking and observing in some corner you can always get a nice surprise.

(Original)
Pequeño parque en la parte posterior del Museo de Historia Natural para la acidez Cuando bajas del metro (según sea la salida que tomes).
Pequeño abreboca externo a lo que posteriormente te encontrarás una vez acceder a los espacios del museo.
Como todo en esta ciudad vale la pena ir caminando y observando en algún rincón siempre te puedes conseguir una bonita sorpresa.

(Translated by Google) Small park in Manhattan, where you can stop to rest when you find yourself walking down Broadway down to the financial district.
From this park is where you can take good photos of the famous Flatiron building and not miss the decoration of the store that is located on its ground floor and the narrowest area of ​​said construction.

(Original)
Pequeño parque en Manhattan, donde puedes parar a descansar cuando te encuentras caminando por Broadway bajando hacia el distrito financiero.
Desde este parque es donde puedes tomar las buenas fotos del famoso edificio Flatiron y no perderte la decoración de la tienda que se encuentra en su planta baja y zona más estrecha de dicha construcción.

(Translated by Google) Small square with very good communication with the rest of the city as it has a subway station where several subway lines connect.
In their spaces, markets of fruits and vegetables in general are assembled to a market that sells everything.
It is surrounded by different restaurants and varied cafés to meet all tastes.

(Original)
Pequeña plaza con muy buena comunicación con el resto de la ciudad ya que posee una estación de metro donde conectan varias líneas de metro.
En sus espacios se arman mercados tanto de frutas y vegetales en general hasta un mercadillo que venden de todo.
Está rodeado de diferentes restaurantes y cafeterías variadas para cumplir con todos los gustos.

(Translated by Google) One of the oldest lighthouses in Florida, whose name is due to the discoverer of Florida, the Spanish conqueror Ponce de Leon.
Close to the mouth of the Halifax River between the border of New Smirna and Ponce de Leon Inlet, it offers interesting views and on occasion see animals such as manatees, dolphins or sharks.

(Original)
Uno de los faros más antiguos de Florida, cuyo nombre se debe al descubridor de la Florida, el conquistador español Ponce de Leon.
Cercano a la desembocadura del Halifax River entre la frontera de New Smirna y Ponce de Leon Inlet, ofrece vistas interesantes y en oportunidades ver animales como manaties, delfines o tiburones.

(Translated by Google) Place where you can see the famous sea lion colony in SF. The reason is unknown, but it is the only port site in the city where they stay, on this side of the iconic Pier 39.
You can see them in all their facets, from playing to fighting and defending their space on top of these large floating blocks.

(Original)
Lugar donde se pueden observar la colonia de leones marinos tan famosa en SF. No se sabe la razón, pero es el único sitio del puerto de la ciudad donde se alojan, en este lateral del icónico Pier 39.
Los puedes ver en todas sus facetas, desde jugando hasta peleando y defendiendo su espacio encima de estos grandes bloques flotantes.

(Translated by Google) Small park in lower Manhattan near the headquarters of courts and municipal offices.
You can walk and take very good pictures of the nearby buildings, it is an open space that contrasts with the height of the buildings a few streets away.
To spend a few minutes enjoying the walk is pretty good.

(Original)
Pequeño parque en el bajo Manhattan cercano a la sede de tribunales y oficinas municipales.
Puedes pasear y tomar muy buenas fotografías de los edificios cercanos, es un espacio abierto que contrasta con la altura de los edificios a escasas calles de distancia.
Para pasarse unos minutos disfrutando la caminata está bastante bien.

(Translated by Google) Small church next to the World Trade Center, small but very beautiful and cozy. It has its own cemetery which if you see it in winter and with snow it acquires a somewhat mysterious aspect.
Inside it is simple, very well maintained and does not have great luxuries, but it is definitely worth visiting.

(Original)
Pequeña iglesia al lado del World Trade Center, pequeña pero muy bonita y acogedora. Tiene su propio cementerio el cual si lo ves en invierno y con nieve adquiere un aspecto un tanto misterioso.
Por dentro es sencilla muy bien cuidada y no posee grandes lujos pero definitivamente bien vale la pena entrar recorrer

(Translated by Google) Building located on a plot where two avenues meet tangentially so that the area remains triangular, being the corner where a Heras corner of the building is located with very little width, hence the name of the building that originates from Flat.
The best angle to see it is Madison Square Park.

(Original)
Edificio ubicado en una parcela donde se juntan dos avenidas de forma tangencial de forma que la área queda triangular siendo del vértice donde se ubica una Heras esquina del edificio con muy poco ancho de ahí el nombre del edificio que se origina de Flat.
El mejor ángulo para verlo es el Madison Square Park.

(Translated by Google) One of the great surprises that Florida has given me, close to the city of Orlando.
Park where in winter in one of the arms of the St. John River, whose waters are warm, the manatees come to take refuge to escape the cold waters of the sea. Good worth it

(Original)
Uno de las grandes sorpresas que me ha dado Florida, cercano a la ciudad de Orlando.
Parque donde en invierno en uno de los brazos del río St. John, cuyas aguas son tibias, vienen a refugiarse los manatíes para escapar de las aguas frías del mar. Bien vale la pena

(Translated by Google) Excellent building from an architectural point of view, the temporary exhibition hall revolves around the main corridor. It has permanent exhibition rooms that are sometimes found in other museums in cities around the world.
A must see.

(Original)
Excelente edificio desde el punto de vista arquitectónico, la sala de exposiciones temporal va girando alrededor del pasillo principal. Posee salas de exposición permanente que en ocasiones sus obras se encuentran en los otros museos de las ciudades del mundo.
Visita obligada.

(Translated by Google) Small but very beautiful Japanese garden, well kept down to the smallest detail with very good ornamentation.
The architectural part is very well designed, with nice roads and places to go resting or just stop to relax and enjoy the moment.

(Original)
Pequeño pero muy bonito jardín japonés bastante cuidado hasta el mínimo detalle con muy buena ornamentación.
La parte arquitectónica muy bien diseñada, con caminerias agradables y sitios donde ir descansando o simplemente parar a relajarse y disfrutar del momento.

(Translated by Google) Nice park located in the old facilities of a sugar mill. Ideal to spend part of the day on the banks of hot springs, or watching nature.
The restaurant located in the sugar complex specializes in pancakes, being high-priced.

(Original)
Bonito parque ubicado en las antiguas instalaciones de un ingenio azucarero. Ideal para pasar parte del día a las orillas de aguas termales,o viendo la naturaleza.
El restaurante ubicado en el complejo azucarero está especializado en panquecas, siendo de alta factura.

(Translated by Google) It is simply the replica of one of the garages that were used when at the beginning of the 20th century cars were racing on Ormond Beach.
In the park there is a series of signs where the origin of this event is explained.

(Original)
Es simplemente la réplica de uno de los garajes que se usaban cuando a principios del siglo XX se corrían las carreras de autos en la playa de Ormond Beach.
En el parque hay una serie de letreros donde se explica el origen de este acontecimiento.

(Translated by Google) Japanese garden of medium size, very well organized and careful despite being all snowy on the day we went. Recommended and warm if it is winter

(Original)
Jardin japones de mediano tamaño, muy bien organizado y cuidado pese a estar todo nevado en el día que fuimos. Recomendable y vayan abrigados si es invierno

t's a nice place for take some picture of the war's ship in this site.
In winter you must go with a good coat.

Must see during spring season. You could see flower blanket in all direction. Small parking lot but can park road side. Washrooms are there near the entrance site so use it. Not stroller or wheel chair friendly place. Ups and down , rocky and muddy areas on the way so dress up for the weather and the landscape. Wise to carry water bottle and light snacks. Trail towards Phantom falls  is good for young kids but not the other side which is steep and bit dangerous for toddlers. Best scenic place for spring flower blooming. Hike untill you see Phantom falls. Breath taking view. We went during third week of April. Good breeze and nice weather for hiking. Make sure you have first aid kit especially if you go with kids.  Camera is must. Sure this place will add good memories in your heart about California.  Roads are pretty good but when you getting closer to North table mountain Ecological Reserve its windy, Drive as per the instructed speed.
dislikes: Steep and dangerous sections for toddlers

reviews_attraction.text:
Quarry park is a hidden gem. It's pretty close to Pillar point harbour. Easy to reach my b
Using Google map.  10 cars parking lot. Lot of street side parking. Opposite to the parking lot there is big size kids at area. Washroom is clean. Best place for family gathering. Nature lovers best choice to admire mother nature. Birds chirping , dry leaf and eukalyptus trees  smell make you to forget city noise. Safe trail. Pack up lunch and drink. Hiking involves uphill area so water bottle is must for the day. Highway 1 to quarry park take 5min. Best part is when you come out of highway you can find convinient stores and good restaurants to fill your back pack.

It's on Cabrillo hwy. On a regular day it will take 25 min to reach this place from San Francisco. One of the scenic place. Huge parking lot. It has hiking trails too. No washrooms. Kids friendly. Small place but beautiful. Best place for ocean lovers.
There is a swing before yo our to the beach area. Picture perfect place. It's only 15 min from Halfmoon Bay. Get food and drink before you reach the beach. Windy road . Lot of pull over places to take picture of majestic Pacific ocean. Week days are good to explore this place. Week end is super busy. Take extra care before you cross the road .

Alameda is a small town near Oakland. It does have ferry service from San Francisco and Oakland. Bus service is also available from Oakland and San Francisco. This festival is well organised. Kids friendly. Best for family outing. You can see creative art work. Picnic tables are also available. There is a huge parking lot.  Less than half a mile distance you can find dog park and a play ground.  Shady area is nearby. Clean washrooms and water fountain is nearby.

Must see place near golden gate bridge. Its open only on sunday and Monday.  Make sure you check the map before going as its a loop between from free way to Bonita light house.  Lso check the light house time.  Pacific ocean looks beautiful as well as if you go there on a sunny day then its an added bonus to eyes and mind.  There are several arking lots and has two washrooms.  Have water as well as some snacks.

Best for one day trip. It's 1hour drive from Oakland. Easy to reach. Several parking lots are available. Picnic tables make our meal time easier.  Park your vehicle based on the location. Lake side pretty crowded. So choose week days. You can walk around the lake. Boating is possible. Good to go with bike. You can see different birds and squirrels. It has washroom in different area of the picnic area.

It's a perfect beach for family.  Mori point parking lot is not big one , mostly street side parking. Carry water with you. Make sure phone is with full battery. You can't stop taking pictures. Good to have quiet lunch while enjoying sea breeze. Wheel chair can go without any problem. Black sad add extra beauty to the beach. Majestic waves and cypress trees make you feel as if you are in monterey bay.

Quiet place. Spring has added extra beauty to this trail by blooming 100%. Small trail so fun to have kids. You can see turtle, squirrel, pelican, Canada geese etc. Birds have their orchestra (close your eyes and listen for 1 min).  Wild mustard flowers are pleasing to eyes . Clean washrooms. Wheel chair accessible. Lake to challenging your fishing skills. Huge parking lot. $6 entrance fees.

We had visited this place during Halloween time. So place was decorated with pumpkins , It was pure thrill and fun for kids. It has restaurants and washroom. Small gift store near the entrance and it has edible bugs. They have tours to take people in small groups. Really unforgettable experience. Glad that visited this unique spot. Big parking lot. Kids friendly.

One of the best place with 90 min drive from San Francisco.  Rail journey is for 90 minutes.  You will fell like its very short.  Great customer service.  Yummy food.  Lot of gmes for kids.  You cn purchase ticket online and get the tickets from front desk.  During rail journey very good hear details about red wood tree.
For sure will go again.

One of the must train in northern California. Not kids friendly. There is a small parking lot. Scenic place. Untouched mountain area. Need enough water and some snack. Good to start before 2pm . Sun set is beautiful on the top of the mountain. Best to go with friends. Narrow path. Cyclist and hikers have to share the same path.

National shrine of saint.  Francis Assisi competes with other  churches in SanFrancisco . Devine place in the heart of the city.  Street side parking is challenging but cheap.  Parking lot cost $15 to 20. Lot of restaurents near by.  Small park is only one block away from the church.  Best place to spend for 1 hour.

Sea Lion center is a family friendly place.  Lot of open sace to watch the aea Lions.  Beautiful while sun set time.  Restaurents and near by so grab food  watch the bulky sea Lions.  Public transport is the best to reach this place. Ferry ternimal is 100 feet away from Sea Lion center.

Habitot museum is a fun place for kids. All activities are safe for all age kids. Painting
, shopping, water table setups are awesome.they change the theme so in a year you could see different setup. Washrooms are there. Wheen chair access is a plus.
Can spend one to two hours.

Must see in north California.  Unique place.  Rough path so keep kids closer to you. First aid kit and water bottle are must.  Dress up for the day weather.  Long walt before you reach the falls.  Beautiful place.  There is a parking lot as well as road side parking available.

As of now , you can park on the road side. Open space. Closer to bay area. You can see Oakland airport take off and landing. So kids really like this place . You can find place to have group activities. Picnic table are also available. Good to go with stroller and wheel chair.

It's one 90 min drive from San Francisco. It is 3 miles from freeway. Easy to find in google map. It has a big parking lot. It does have a washroom. Very clean. Left side of the trail has sharp incline. But right side  path is good for kids. Need  solid two hours.

Pretty close the golden gate park.  Huge parking lot.  Sand dunes are the amazing place for kids.  Good restaurent opposute to the beach.  Worlds first mobile Gym awesome.  Beach is not crowded.  Best location to go crazy with family.  Washrooms are there.

Its a small quiet place.  Easy access by public transportation.  Beautiful place.  Treasure for history lovers.  It has washrooms.  Small gift store with unique art collection.  Self guided tours are good.  So many reataurents near by.  Can spnd one hour.

Must see place in California.  Roads are windy.  Mke sure that you know the parking lot.  Better to take shuttle bus especially with little kids.  Clean washrooms are there.  Wheel chair parking is available.  Amazine tree.  Worth to see this giant tree.

Nice view of the falls.  But should have a good hiking shoe.  No stroller or wheel chair can go. Washrooms at the entrance location.  Lways keep n eye on your kids.  Bit rough surface.  Have a water bottle nd dress up for the weather in layers.

Best place for hiking near Berkeley.  Slight windy road to go to the top.  But one you reach the top there is roadside parking.  The view of bay area from the top is amazing.  Quiet place foe hiking.  Not many people.  No washrooms.

Must go with kids.  Washrooms are nearby.  Snacks available. Big arking lot. Kids will enjoy this place.  Scenic location.  Easy to find.  Make sure you have the camera. Fun place for kisds and resting place for parents.
It's a gem in the middle of an residential area. Good size parking lot is there pretty close to the garden. Kids friendly place. It's has good photo shot place. Turtle and Koi (fish) attract kids.
Beautiful church.  Can be seen from road side.  Huge parking lot.  The church os huge and spacious.  Church Alter will occupy a space in your heart.  Church involved in many community activities.

Great place for vintage airplane buffs.The museum itself is inside Travis AFB (an active air force base). To get to the museum, you have to stop at the visitor's center and provide your name, address and SSN (yes, your SSN...) Once admitted, a van/truck will come and pick you up, driving you through the base to the museum.

The museum features an indoor display of airplane history, including airplane systems, cockpit, bomb shells, airplane guns, engines of all types, aircraft replicas, and a few complete vintage aircraft. History buffs will spend quite some time reading the displays and appreciating the historic details behind the artifacts.

The "plane lot" outside is a blast, and has a number of aircraft most of us will immediately recognize, such a a B-52 bomber, a B-17 bomber, helicopters, and many others.

Overall, a good place to bring the kids or just bring the kid in you. Call in advance for times and information.

Beautiful desert park, with all the pluses of your typical desert: solitude, silence, beautiful skies. The park has tons of rock formations, which can be climbed without a lot of effort. There are also good hiking opportunities for all levels. I'd recommend Joshua Tree over the Mojave National Preserve for people after a more "tame" experience. There are campgrounds here, with bathrooms, etc. If you prefer a more "authentic" experience, visit the Mojave Preserve. The park can get pretty crowded (and noisy) during the weekends, so I'd recommend visiting during the weekdays. Avoid the "overflow" camping and parking lot outside the park if you can -- rules are not enforced there and people make noise and raise all kinds of ruckus all night.

The entire preserve is a must for desert lovers. There is so much to see here: from the restored Train Depot (Kelso Depot) to sand dunes you can climb all the way to the top (Kelso Dunes). There are nice hiking trails (Teutonia Peak trail, all the trails around hole-in-the-wall campground), campgrounds (Afton Canyon campground, hole-in-the-wall, mid-hills, or wherever you want), Lava tubes, Volcanic craters (Amboy Crater, others), abandoned mines of all kinds, old mining artifacts, etc. It's a wilderness, so don't expect amenities, gas stations, or cell phone signal. Late winter to early spring and late fall to early winter are the best times to visit. For stunning night skies, choose your visit so it matches a new moon.
likes: Natural features (sand dunes, lava tubes, volcanic craters)

reviews_attraction.text:
Nice trail system for hikers, bikers, and horse riders. The park has two almost distinct sets of trails, forming a "figure of 8" of sorts. The lower part of the "eight" has a bit less than five miles and is suitable for an easy to moderate hike. The upper level is far steeper and recommended for intermediate hikers. Mountain bikers have the option of doing the lower loop a few times or going for the entire course, which can be demanding.
There's also a flat 0.8 mile loop next to the parking lot, for those with children or getting back into shape. Parking is free, but watch for park closing times to avoid getting your vehicle locked inside the parking lot.

Nice place for an easy/moderate hike in Portola Valley. This park is very easy to access from most of the bay area and features a relatively large parking lot (that gets full, be warned), restrooms, and a nice trail system for hikers and bikers. There's a relatively long climb if you hike/bike the trail in the counter-clockwise direction, but it doesn't start right away and by the time it starts to really climb, you'll be warmed up. Also, note the name "Windy Hill" -- it is *really* windy at the top and it can get chilly in the winter months of the year. There's also an upper parking lot for those who just want to enjoy the nice views from the summit.

This is a nice park near Morgan Hill, and just 30 minutes or so from downtown San Jose (with good traffic). The preserve opened in June 2015 and features a 4-mile loop for hikers, bikers, and horse riders. Despite the relatively short total length of the trail, its hilly nature makes up in climbs for what it lacks in distance.

The preserve also offers the usual amenities found in other Open Space Preserves (parking lot, bathrooms, park benches). In addition to that, there's also a parking lot dedicated to people with equestrian trailers, and some picnic spots along the trail. Admission is free.
likes: Trail for multiple uses (hiking, biking, horse riding)

reviews_attraction.text: This park is a little known gem in Northern California. There are hikes for all levels and a "whole loop" around the park which is something around 10-12 miles. The park has attractions for everyone, including hiking trails, peaks, caves, lakes, and climbing routes. Caves close during certain times of the year so the bats can do... bat things and we can have more bats. There are also campgrounds for regular campers and RVs. I'd avoid the hot months of the year for hikes, since it can get seriously hot. Note that there are two main entrances to the park, but you cannot drive across them.

Nice place to bring your kids. The camp is well maintained and themed like an old Western town. The main activities are the trains, and there are two distinct possibilities: A steam train (with open cars for people) which takes passengers through the forest, or a Diesel locomotive (also with some open passenger cars) which takes passengers all the way to Santa Cruz and back, through the redwood forests. The Diesel train will depart Santa Cruz back to Roaring Camp Railroads one hour after its arrival there, allowing passengers some time to enjoy the Santa Cruz boardwalk.

Calero has an extensive trail system, and shares some of those with the neighboring Rancho Cañada del Oro Open Preserve. Despite the miles of trails, this is far from my favorite park given the nature of the trails, lack of interesting views (for most part), and constant and steep climbs and descents. If you're visiting, try to get to the higher elevations, where things are better and you'll have a nice view of the reservoir.

This is an absolutely amazing place inside Lassen Volcanic National Park. The place is not reachable by vehicle, and a short and easy hike is required.
Bumpass Hell is at the end of the trail and easy to spot due to the many steam vents and strong smell of hydrogen sulphide. There's a catwalk over all kinds of interesting volcanic vents and boiling mud ponds and visitors should be safe as long as they don't step out of it.

Beautiful aquarium, with a lot of variety. There is no private parking, so you'll have to find parking in the streets around the place (hard!) or pay for a whole day parking and walk a few blocks. Their annual pass is worth it, but our kids didn't want to go there more than three times per year. Also, once they have your phone, they'll keep pestering you for renewals and donations, which is not ideal.

This is one of the main entrances to Almaden Quicksilver and the best overall entrance if you're biking the park. There's a large parking area with spots for trailers, and an overflow area for really busy days. Bathrooms are usually clean and well kept. There's zero phone coverage for most operators at this location, but they recently started offering free WiFi, which is fantastic. Parking is free.

Beautiful views of the ocean here. The place is large and has lots of parking spots, but also lots of visitors, so come early. We visited during the week (in July) around 11am and the lot was almost full. Try to come here on a day without fog (I heard they're rare). Also, the fog apparently tends to dissipate around 4pm or so. Leave ample time to explore the place on foot.

Nice hiking and biking trails. This preserve is a bit unusual in the sense that it already starts pretty high in the mountains, and most of the trails are on the side of the mountain, offering great views of the city below. Mountain biking is allowed, but you'll start at the top and descend. Make sure you have energy left to come back to your car (the trails are steep).

Nice park with a lake in a suburban neighborhood. The lake, unfortunately, is polluted with Mercury from the old Almaden Quicksilver mines, so fishing and swimming is a bad idea. Not a very large place, but good for a short stroll or for those with children. There's a good play area near the Almaden Rd entrance. Paddle boats are available during the weekend.

Very large park with ample hiking and backpacking opportunities. You can make multi-day hikes in this place (not something you find easily in the bay area). Bikes are welcome, but trails tend to be very steep and poorly marked. Avoid the place during the summer months if you can, as it tends to be *very* hot. Ticks are a constant problem here.

Small and nice neighborhood park. Small kids will love this place. There are play areas for kids with interesting toys (including a "spinning" toy that will make your kid puke -- guaranteed). It's a nice and quiet setting to spend an afternoon with your kids. The park has no bathrooms.

Fantastic place for a short (and easy) mountain bike ride (10-mile loop) or hike. It is also possible to connect to Rancho Cañada del Oro for s much longer and interesting ride. Keep in mind that Rancho San Vicente is just an entrance to the Calero   County Park trail system.

One of the many nice places along the 17-mile drive. This place offers a frontal view of Bird Rock and a small beach with some rocks. Parking is bigger than I expected, but could get crowded very quickly with tour buses. Prefer the late hours of the day to avoid the fog.

Nice place for geeks and people who like computers and technology in general. The younger crowd will see stuff they never thought could exist. The older crowd will vividly remember some of the exhibits when they were the state-of-the-art in terms of computing.

Nice and secluded regional wilderness. A bit of a ride if coming from the South Bay, but interesting place. Plan ahead since it tends to be really hot. When coming in the summer months, prefer the late hours of the day. Entrance fee is (as of July/2019) $5.

Nice little place for a walk near Anderson Lake. There's a few somewhat steep but short climbs, but most of the terrain is otherwise gentle. Some really nice views of the reservoir at the back of the park. Bikes allowed.

Fantastic views of the valley below. This place is a mandatory stop for anyone visiting death valley. Temperatures here might be 10-20 degrees lower than in the valley below. It can be very windy at times.

Great place for a short/medium hike or mountain bike ride. The place is about 50% shaded, 50% under direct sunlight, so hats are recommended during the hot months of the year. Nice views from the trail.
A nice preserve right in the middle of the city. Good trails and good views. The place is a bit too crowded for my preferences, but still worth a visit.

The state beach at Torrey Pines isn’t the most picturesque beach in the world, but for the price, it’s not bad. Parking can be incredibly hard on nice days, even in the early spring, and may require a lengthy patient wait for people to leave. The same lot serves the reserve trail with great views, so it fills up quickly. The beach itself is a pebble beach, so not the most comfortable to sit out on, but it can be done. The surfing is not bad and lessons are run from here as well. Lifeguards are periodically on duty, but not that often, so check the schedule if it matters to you. The sunsets are pretty great here, but again you’ll need o plan ahead to get a parking spot.

The old Wall Street Mill is a deserted gold stamp mill in the middle of Joshua Tree park. The building was constructed in the early 20th century to press gold from other materials mined from the desert and still stands today largely the same. You can’t go inside due to a fence, but can get a good idea of the entirety of the structure from outside. The path to the mill is easy and flat, but bring water as there is no shade and it gets very hot under the sun. Along the way are a nice variety of plants including the Joshua Trees and desert scrub. There are also several abandoned old cars along the path and a wind powered water pump.

Phenominal restaurant with one of the best atmospheres in the world. All tables have a view of the row boat lake which is so unbelievably pretty in the Spring. No wonder so many bridal parties come here. Watching the fish and turtles swim around is also wonderful. The food was quite good as well, from the exqusite crab cake to the most delicious and tender fish and chips I've ever had. Desert was also good and the home made ice cream and espresso was delightful. The staff was a bit off, but helpful and relaxed which was nice. Don't expect a quick meal but in the atmosphere, why would you want one?

Torrey Pines reserve is a beautiful slice of preserved land along the water with awesome views of the cliffs, ocean, and even all the way down to La Jolla. The parking is interesting with a free section under high demand due to the beach, but the paid section for the park is more than large enough. The walk up can be a bit intense in vertical climb, but reaching the short loop around the cliffs with awesome views is worth it. Beware the crazy bikers dying down and the runners and stick to the side trail. The hike up which can feel like it will never end is definitely worth the view.

Mount Mitchell may be the highest point east of the Mississippi, but it is very easy to get to from the parkway. A short drive up non-treacherous roads makes it easy and the parking lot is huge. Be wary of the huge temperature drops while climbing as we went from 55 to 36 in mere minutes and it even began hailing quite hard when we got to the top. From the parking lot, it is a very short, moderate hike to the summit which has an overlook and a sign marking the summit for pictures. The short balsam wood is also very cool and smells like Christmas. A must stop along the parkway.

The forest is a great place to take a hike, whether you are looking for an easy family stroll or a more challenging hike. The main trail loop goes around the perimeter of the lake and is easily accessible from the upper and lower parking lots. There is also a great trail that is a bit more strenuous that goes to the ruins of an old mansion on the top of the mountain. There are also great trails up the side of the mountain that are pretty easy to get lost on, but you are never really far from a road. Great place for a walk with a four legged friend as well.

A cool and unique working attraction maintained by the army core of engineers. The park itself is quite nice with a variety of trees and flowers and makes for a nice walk. The locks are way bigger than expected and watching a boat go through is awesome. It is a bit inconvenient when boats are going through as you have to go all the way around to cross, but it's nice to be able to get so close. Walking across is recommended for the views and the salmon ladder, especially when they are spawning. A one of a kind sight to visit in the city.

This great aquarium houses a wide variety not only of fish, but aquatic birds too. There's plenty to see and explore here, especially for young kids who love seeing animals. There's a massive tank with sharks, turtles, and rays, tons of fish, and a touch tank with rays too. There's even a bald eagle in rehabilitation and a turtle hospital to walk through. The aviary upstairs and outside is also a nice unique feature. For any animal lover, or even kids who are just building up a love for animals, it's a perfect spot in town.

This wreck is a testament to why building boats of concrete never caught on. One of several experimental boats built of the more readily available material during the First World War, it survived the war and was bought to be used for a pier for the Cape May Ferry. While being moved to its dock location, it broke apart and sunk. Now, half of it sticks up out of the water and acts as a sanctuary for birds a few hundred feet off the beach. It definitely makes for an interesting set piece while enjoying the beach.

A dream for the child inside and the nerd outside. I enjoyed my trip to the Intrepid as much at 27 as I did at 7. The addition of the space shuttle makes the visit all the more interesting. I'm not a huge fan of the arcade games and non-educational junk in the main deck now, but there is plenty of opportunity for learning around. The price is a bit steep, but discounts abound online, so do some research first. We got in for half price thanks to a couple from PA ho had an extra coupon.

You may expect more beautiful lighthouses around Portland, but this one definitely stands out among the other smaller ones. Portland Head has an interesting history from being commissioned by Washington to being immortalized in Longfellow poems. This is what you picture as a lighthouse and it looks great from every angle. The cliff walk also in the park is very nice as well and gives dramatic views of the rocky coast with waves crashing.

This view point that comes up fast when you enter the valley is one of the best panoramic views of the unique landscape. The rocky landscape here is different than the flat terrain of most of the rest of the valley. From here you get a stunning view over the rocks and little valleys as you enter the park. The short walk up to the viewpoint is definitely worth the stop.

This large park that stretches along the water just North of downtown is a great place to get outside and take a nice walk. There are nice paths that wind along the water and pass beautiful scenery. It's also great for large events that take place here as they can spread out along the water. It's work a nice walk out of the bustle of downtown to explore.

Not a great place to see a concert or event due to the claustrophobic, yet somehow vertigo inducing atmosphere. The bridge seats are very distracting with people constantly walking across your field of vision. The history is great, but the old building can't keep up and it gets very warm when packed. Also the single escalator means slow entrances.
dislikes: Facilities & Services: Poor ventilation, Limited escalators

reviews_attraction.text: A great expansive square in downtown Portland. Great place to take a picture of the scenic courthouse or take a break on the stone benches around the square. When we visited there was a flower exhibition going on which was a lovely addition to the square. Great place to regroup when taking a walk around the city.

A very inspiring and beautiful view of downtown Providence and the capital building that feels a bit like a Parisian park. Great tree cover makes for a great picknic spot. The views even draw artists and classes from the nearby schools. Great place for some good photos of Providence as well.

Discovery Green is a nice park in the middle of Downtown Houston. There is a nice large pond to sit around and fountains to run around in. Unfortunately the view isn't awesome now with a ton of ugly construction around. They also do concerts in the park in the summer which is nice.

Very unique monument to the Polish soldiers from this battle. Stunning with the backdrop of the Freedom tower and lower Manhattan behind it. Right in the middle of the river walk way right outside the exchange place path station. Worth a quick walk by when in the area.

Beautiful park on the site of an old gas work site. The views of Downtown Seattle, SLU, and the space needle are great from here. The old rusty metal buildings grant great character too. Great place for a picnic, walk, or just relaxing.

The mineral museum is a pretty nice stop along the parkway. Great spot for a bathroom break while driving the parkway. The museum part is small but free and pretty interesting. It's a good diversion from too much driving on the parkway.

Nice park with good paths for a walk and some beach front areas. Very pretty on a sunny day though the rest of the crowds will have figured this out as well. Nice place for a walk or jog. You might even catch sight of whales from here.

A nice, fairly low key park in a great location. A fairly quiet hide away in midtown where you can relax in the shade or get some work done at one of the cafe tables. The Christmas market is also pretty nice though crowded.

A small but nice block park in Bushwick. Not a ton to do here, especially in the winter. The area is nice to explore with lots of street art. Not the cleanest or safest feeling park, but decent for getting some fresh air.

Phenomenal park with tons of space and fields. Great dog park that is absolutely huge. Too bad many of the dog owners are not good owners, but there is enough space to get away. Great place for a walk.
What's the deal with the troll under the bridge. Part of the local art work, it holds a vw bug and eats goats that pass over the bridge. Watch out for children hanging from the nose too.

This is a beautiful park surrounded by smiling children playing in the water, beautiful view of the new York city buildings. Great for photos and just hanging out , also getting a tan on a sunny beautiful day. Overall my favorite park and you get to see the Pepsi cola sign, beautiful apartment buildings.

Nice park for kids to play in the playground. Always see smiling kids jumping around, playing, laughing. They also have basketball courts and handball courts. Also got a field for baseball or football. Usually in a hot summer day the water is on. Overall great park for all ages.

Nice place for kids to play and enjoy their time in the park. Surrounded by beautiful NYC and NJ buildings and the water of course. Best of both worlds and great to shoot photography. Overall great place and will return soon, lots of good restaurants around the area too.

Great museum for all ages, the atmosphere is cozy and lovely. I suggest bring a light jacket because it get pretty cold inside. Lots to see and very educational. Staffs are knowledgeable and friendly. Overall amazing experience here and good for the kids.

This park has great views of the Manhattan bridge and NYC buildings. Also pretty good park just to hang out and chill with a friend or have lunch outside. Pretty good area for photography. Overall nice place to enjoy the weather when it's warmer outside.

Great park for all ages. Good stop and sit to have lunch or a snack on a beautiful sunny day. This park has lots of tourists from all walks of life, every where in the world. Great park for photos and videos. Overall awesome park for everyone.

This is properly one of my favorite museum. It's small, manageable to get around and not too big. The art here is just amazing, I wish I had some skills like that. Staffs are friendly and knowledgeable. Overall great place to visit.

Great old stone house, couldn't believe it's still up through out the years from the war this is a historic gem to look at. Even great for photo shooting the house. If you haven't seen this old stone house your missing out.

Radio city is a classic venue that will never go out of style. The seat are comfortable with good sight lines from nearly any seat. Overall the place is super iconic and worth to watch any show especially the Rockettes.

The church has been in st. Marks forever. The church is also pretty historic. Great place for photos or even just hang out and eat while sitting on the bench. Overall great landmark for st.marks and the neighborhood.

Wonderful park to bring kids and dog walks. Beautiful view of new York city buildings. The park is beautiful and nice walk in warmer weather. Good to photography the city buildings. Overall great park for everyone.

Good park to relax and enjoy the weather. Also good park to enjoy your lunch or take a break from work. Overall great area just to chill and there is was a lots of bars and restaurants surrounding the park.

Pretty big park with handball courts and soccer field. Usually you see people playing soccer and old people doing thai chi. Overall this is a pretty good park to relax and enjoy your lunch and outdoors.
Place is awesome with high end stores and restaurant inside it. Usually you see mostly tourist. If you guess it right, it also a tourist destination. Overall great place but too rich for my blood.
This museum is super nice, cuny students get to go in for free. The arts are nice and staffs are friendly and attentive. Atmosphere is cozy and comfortable. Overall great museum and lots to see.
Great oval park to relax and enjoy the sunlight. Also you get wifi that's a huge plus for me. Usually see people relax and eating their lunch. Overall great park to relax and chill.
Great small Italian museum. Right in the heart of little Italy in Chinatown. Good things to see in the museum. Staffs are friendly and helpful. Atmosphere feels laid back and relax.
Lots of interesting thing to look at. Staffs are friendly and knowledgeable, also helpful in showing you where to head too for the special things to see. Overall great museum .
Nice and relaxing park to sit and enjoy great company with friends and enjoying the weather. Great restaurants around the park and huge church across the street from park.
Great location for photos of different court buildings. The architecture of the building look pretty cool. Overall great place for tourist visits and photos.
Beautiful park surround by buildings.great to take photos. Could just relax and take in the sun. If you hungry there is a shake shack kosik to get food.
Nice park for a walk. Also great for photos. During the winter the ice skating rink is open. Also great park just to kick it and relax.
Nice area to relax and enjoy the weather and clouds. Good place to eat your lunch and sometimes there the entertainment in the park.
This garden is beautiful, great for photos. Tip: if your a student you are able to get a student discount and not pay full price.
Nice place to hang out and relax. Great for taking pictures of the arch. Good place to see different characters of people.

(Translated by Google) Background: The Los Angeles Township Building was completed in 1928 and upon completion was the tallest building in Los Angeles.
The sand used for the building was taken from California's 58 counties.

In 1998, the building underwent a massive renovation, so the building could withstand a strong 8.2 magnitude earthquake with only minor damage.

Observation floor:
At the top of the building is a free-standing observation deck.
The lookout is open Monday to Friday from 8am to 5pm.

To get to the observation point, enter the town hall from the entrance on main street (the side of the building that does not face the grand park).
At the entrance you must present an ID card and pass a security check.
After the test, you will receive a guest sticker and explain how to ascend to the observation floor.
In order to ascend, you have to climb two different elevators and one more floor (see explanation in one of the pictures below).

One floor of the observation is a closed space with windows.
In the space are pictures of Los Angeles' former mayors.
The second floor has a balcony around the entire building that gives a 360-degree view of Los Angeles Downtown.
The scenery is particularly beautiful on clear days.

The Hollywood sign can also be seen, but it is far away and you see it quite small.

(Original)
רקע: בניין העירה של לוס אנג'לס הושלם בשנת 1928 ועם סיומו היה הבניין הגבוה ביותר בלוס אנג'לס.
החול ששימש לבנית הבנין נלקח מ58 המחוזות של קלפורניה.

בשנת 1998 עבר הבניין שיפוץ מסיבי, כך שהבניין יכול לעמוד ברעידת אדמה חזקה של 8.2 בסולם ריכטר תוך ספיגת נזקים קלים בלבד.

קומת התצפית:
בראש הבניין נמצאת קומת תצפית שהכניסה אליה חינם.
התצפית פתוחה בימים שני עד שישי משעות 8:00 ועד 17:00.

בשביל לעלות לתצפית יש להכנס לבניין העיריה מכניסה ברחוב main (הצד שלהבניין שלא פונה grand park).
בכניסה יש להציג תעודת מזהה ולעבור בדיקה ביטחונית.
לאחר הבדיקה תקבלו מדבקת אורח והסבר איך לעלות לקומת התצפית.
בשביל לעלות לתצפית יש לעלות בשני מעליות שונות ועוד קומה אחת ברגל (ראה הסבר באחת התמונות המצורפות).

קומה אחת של התצפית היא חלל סגור עם חלונות.
בחלל תמונות של ראשי הערים הקודמים של לוס אנג'לס.
מהקומה השנייה יש מרפסת מסביב לכל הבניין שמקנה תצפית של 360 מעלות על הדאונטאון של לוס אנג'לס.
הנוף יפיפה במיוחד בימים בהירים.

אפשר לראות גם את השלט של הוליווד, אבל הוא רחוק ורואים אותו די בקטן.

(Translated by Google) A redwood tree park that is really recommended. There are several recommended routes in the park.
We did a short track (about a mile) without ups and downs and no steps, which greatly facilitates trip with small children. The track is clean and very well maintained.
We saw a lot of wildlife and it really excited the kids.

The place has a steam train station like it used to.
There is a train that travels in the woods (we did and highly recommended, though not cheap).
And another train that goes to Santa Cruz and back (we didn't).
The train ride was really lovely especially for the kids.
The train travels slowly through the woods and even takes a break that you can get off to the right for a short ten minute walk in the woods.
It is highly recommended.
So long journey accompanied by explanations and can ask questions of the conductor, dressed exactly like the days of steam locomotives were common means of transportation in the world.

(Original)
פארק עצי סקויה שממש מומלץ. בפארק ישנם מספר מסלולים מומלצים.
אנחנו עשינו מסלול קצר (כקילומטר וחצי) ללא עליות וירידות וללא מדרגות, דבר שמאוד מקל בטיול עם ילדים קטנים. המסלול נקי ומתחזק מאוד יפה.
ראינו חיות בר רבות וזה מאוד הלהיב את הילדים.

במקום יש תחנת רכבת קיטור כמו פעם.
ישנה רכבת שנוסעת בתוך היער (עשינו ומאוד מומלץ, למרות שלא זול).
ורכבת נוספת שנוסעת לסנטה קרוז וחוזרת (לא עשינו).
הטיול ברכבת היה ממש מקסים במיוחד לילדים.
הרכבת נוסעת לאט ביער ואפילו עושה הפסקה שתוכל לרדת מימנה לטיול קצר של עשר דקות ביער.
מומלץ מאוד.
כל זמן הנסיעה מלווה בהסברים וניתן לשאול שאלות את הכרטיסן, שלבוש בדיוק כמו בימים שרכבות הקיטור היו אמצעי תחבורה נפוץ בעולם.

(Translated by Google) The World Trade Center observation is very different from the other observation floors in other tall buildings in the world. The elevator that ascends to the observation floor radiates the view around the tower from the first settlement in the city to the construction of the tower.
The elevator rises to the 102nd floor in just 52 seconds!

The observation box is closed (without a balcony) and has huge windows for a 365 degree view around the building.
Because of the height of the building you can see the curvature of the earth that looks over the landscape.

There is a lookout on what to watch on the street below. Of course, these are TV screens and not glass floors, so don't be afraid to mount them.

You can rent a tablet that explains the view from the building, quite nice but a bit expensive.

The lookout is open seven days a week from 9:00 am to 8:00 pm.

The price is expensive, but it is a very invested experience.

(Original)
התצפית ממרכז הסחר העולמי שונה מאוד משאר קומות התצפית במבנים גבוהים אחרים בעולם. המעלית שעולה לקומת התצפית מקרינה את הנוף סביב המגדל מהתישבות הראשונה בעיר ועד בנית המגדל.
המעלית עולה לקומה ה102 ב52 שניות בלבד!

קופת התצפית סגורה (ללא מרפסת) ולה חלונות ענק לתצפית של 365 מעלות מסביב לבניין.
בגלל גובהו של הבניין ניתן להבחין בעקמימות כדור הארץ שמביטים על הנוף.

בתצפית ישנה במה שעליה צפייה ברחוב למטה. מדובר כמובן במסכי טלוויזיה ולא ברצפת זכוכית, אז לא לפחד לעלות על זה.

ניתן להשכיר טבלט שמסביר על הנוף שנשקף מהבניין, די נחמד אבל טיפה יקר.

התצפית פתוחה שבעה ימים בשבוע מ9:00 בבוקר ועד 20:00 בערב.

המחיר יקר, אבל מדובר בחוויה מושקעת מאוד.

(Translated by Google) An amazing museum, not just for aviation enthusiasts, and kids in general will love the place.

The hangar under the air-conditioned deck and there is also a movie theater with movie on the ship.

On board are a number of planes, one of which is an A12. There is also an Israeli Kfir aircraft, and many aircraft from around the world, but mostly American aircraft.

From the deck there is a spectacular view of Manhattan.

In the back there is an air-conditioned building with a new space shuttle, the shuttle was a demonstration of technology and did not really perform space missions.

Recommend to save for a visit at least two to three hours.

Those coming by public transport should note that there is no nearby subway stop, but there are taxis and a nearby bus stop that will take you to Times Square in a few minutes' drive.

(Original)
מוזיאון מדהים, גם לא רק לחובבי תעופה, וילדים בכלל יאהבו את המקום.

האנגר מתחת לסיפון ממוזג ויש גם אולם קולנוע עם סרט על הספינה.

על הסיפון ישנם מספר מטוסים שאחד מהכוכבים שבהם הוא מטוס A12. כמו כן ישנו גם מטוס כפיר ישראלי, ושלל מטוסים מרחבי העולם, אבל בעיקר מטוסים אמרקאים.

מהסיפון נשקף נוף מרהיב של מנהטן.

בחלק האחורי ישנו מבנה ממוזג עם מעבורת חלל שמורה כחדשה, המעבורת הייתה מדגימת טכנולוגיות ולא באמת ביצעה משימות בחלל.

ממליץ לשמור לביקור במקום לפחות שעתיים עד שלוש.

למי שמגיע עם תחבורה ציבורית יש לשים לב שאין תחנת רכבת תחתית קרובה, אבל יש מוניות ותחנת אוטובוס קרובה שתיקח אותכם לכיכר טיימס בנסיעה קצרה של מספר דקות.

(Translated by Google) Union Square: The park in the center knew many popular demonstrations, and today is also a popular place for such demonstrations. In the center of the square is the statue of George Washington, made by sculptor Henry Kirk Brown. The statue was inaugurated in 1856. In 1986, the statue of Mahatma Gandhi was added to the square.

On Monday, Wednesday, Friday and Saturday from 8:00 to 18:00, a farmers market square is held where farmers from New England and New York bring their produce. The market mainly sells vegetables and home foods such as jams and sauces.

On the northwest side of the square (across the road) is the "Dylan's Candy Bar" candy shop a little expensive but an attraction for sweet lovers (and food colors).
Nice place for a short stroll with the farmers market open.

(Original)
כיכר יוניון: הפארק שבמרכז ידע הפגנות פולטיות רבות, וגם כיום מהווה מקום פופולרי להפגנות מסוג הזה. במרכז הכיכר נמצא פסלו של ג'ורג' וושינגטון מעשי ידי הפסל הנרי קירק בראון. הפסל נחנך בשנת  1856. בשנת 1986 נוסף לכיכר פסלו של מהטמה גאנדי.

בימים שני, רביעי, שישי ושבת בשעות 8:00  עד 18:00 נערך בכיכר שוק איכרים בו מביאים איכרי ניו אינגלנד ומדינת ניו יורק את תוצרתם. בשוק נמכרים בעיקר ירקות  ומוצרי מזון ביתיים כגון ריבות ורטבים ביתיים.

בצד הצפון מערבי של הכיכר (מעבר לכביש) נמצאת חנות  הממתקים "Dylan's Candy Bar" חנות קצת יקרה אבל אטרקציה לחובבי המתוקים (וצבעי המאכל).
מקום נחמד לטיול קצר במיוחד עם שוק האיכרים פתוח.

(Translated by Google) San Francisco's Chinatown is the district in which the former San Francisco Chinese residents used to concentrate.
Unlike Newtown's Chinatown, the place remains much more loyal to the original and much less commercialized.

The main reason why Chinatown in San Francisco is so big is that after the big fire that hit the city, many Chinese immigrants from the area flocked to it knowing that they could claim to be legal immigrants in the city and all their documents were burned in the big fire.

It is true that Chinatown is very well-toured, but there is still little feeling like you are in China and not in the US.

In Chinatown many shops and restaurants, I highly recommend choosing a good Chinese restaurant and having a good meal and most often it will not happen.

(Original)
הצ'יינהטאון של סן פרנסיקו היא הרובע שבו התרכזו בעבר התושבים הסינים של סן פרנסיסקו.
בשונה מצ'יינהטאון של ניו יורק המקום נשאר הרבה יותר נאמן למקור והרבה פחות ממוסחר.

הסיבה המרכזית לכך שהצ'יינהטאון בסן פרנסיסקו כל כך גדולה היא שלאחר השריפה הגדולה שפקדה את העיר נהרו עליה מהגרים סינים רבים מאזור מתוך ידעה שהם יכלו לטעון שהם מהגרים חוקים בעיר וכל המסמכים שלהם נשרפו בשריפה הגדולה.

נכון שצ'יינהטאון מאוד מתויירת, אבל עדין ישנה הרגשה קטנה כיאלו אתה בסין ולא בארה"ב.

בצ'יינהטאון חנויות ומסעדות רבות, אני ממליץ בחום לבחור מסעדה סינית טובה ולהנות מארוחה טובה ולרוב לא יקרה.

(Translated by Google) Siegfried and Roy Memorial: A duo of German-American entertainers, who were made famous for their circus performances, which included lions and white tigers.

Their show at the Mirage Hotel, was the most popular and observable show in Las Vegas in the 90s and early 2000s. Over the years, the pair has appeared about 5,750 times, most of them at the Mirage Hotel.

In October 2003, Roy was severely injured in the neck by the Montecar tiger during a duo show. Roy went through a lengthy restoration period, where he returned to talk, but the show at the hotel was discontinued, and 267 crew members were fired. Mirage lost about $ 50 million from ticket sales following the show's stoppage.

(Original)
אנדרטת זיגפריד ורוי: צמד בדרנים גרמנים-אמריקאים, שהתפרסמו בשל מופעי הקרקס שלהם, שכללו אריות וטיגריסים לבנים.

המופע שלהם במלון מיראז', היה המופע הפופולרי והנצפה ביותר בלאס וגאס בשנות ה90 ותחילת שנות ה2000. לאורך השנים הופיע הצמד כ-5,750 פעמים, רובן במלון מיראז'.

באוקטובר 2003 נפצע רוי באורח קשה בצווארו על ידי הטיגריס מונטקור במהלך מופע של הצמד. רוי עבר תקופת שיקום ממושכת, בה חזר ללכת ולדבר, אך המופע במלון הופסק, ו-267 אנשי הצוות של המופע פוטרו. מלון מיראז' הפסיד כ-50 מיליון דולר ממכירת כרטיסים בעקבות הפסקת המופע.

(Translated by Google) Holy Trinity Church: Established in 1846 on the ruins of the two preceding churches. The original church was destroyed in 1776 in the great fire of New York, the second church was destroyed in the winter of 1838-1939 from severe snowstorm damage.
The church steeple was the tallest building in New York until 1890!

The entrance is recognized for two films filmed in it:
1. National treasure: The treasure is hidden under the entrance.
2. Spiderman: One of the important scenes in the film takes place in the church's bell tower.

Adjacent to the entrance is a historic cemetery where a number of important people are buried, according to Alexander Hamilton of the seven founding fathers of the United States.

(Original)
כנסית השילוש הקדוש: הוקמה בשנת  1846על הריסות שני הכנסיות שקדמו לה. הכנסיה המקורית  נהרסה ב1776 בשרפה הגדולה של ניו יורק, הכנסיה השנייה נהרסה בחורף 1838-1939 מנזקי סופת שלג קשה.
צריח הכנסיה היה המבנה הגבוה ביותר בניו יורק עד 1890!

הכניסה מוכרת בגלל שני סרטים שצולמו בה:
1.אוצר לאומי: האוצר חבוי מתחת לכניסה.
2.ספידרמן:  באחת מהסצנות החשובות בסרט מתרחשת במגדל הפעמונים של הכנסיה.

בצמוד לכניסה ישנו בית קברות היסטורי שבו קבורים מספר אנשים חשבים, בינהים אלכסנדר המילטון משבעת האבות המייסדים של ארה"ב.

(Translated by Google) The famous sign that started as a temporary sign in favor of promoting a residential project in the area, and is now one of the famous icons of the city of Los Angeles.

Reaching the sign itself is not possible, but getting close to it in favor of photography is possible, but not as simple as one might think.

Note that the masses of tourists who came to be photographed with the sign created a hustle and bustle in an upscale residential area, so today there are parking restrictions for tourists in the area so as not to hurt local residents, beware of fines for forbidden parking.

The sign is not lit at night so a picture with it is only possible in daylight.

(Original)
השלט המפורסם שהתחיל כשלט זמני לטובת קידום פרויקט מגורים באזור,  וכיום מהסמלים המפורסמים של העיר לוס אנג'לס.

הגעה לשלט עצמו אינה אפשרית, אבל הגעה בסמוך אליו לטובת צילום אפשרית, אבל לא פשוטה כמו שאפשר לחשוב.

שימו לב שהמוני התיירים שהגיעו להצטלם עם השלט יצרו דוחק באזור מגורים יוקרתי, ולכן היום ישנם הגבלות חניה לתיירים באזור בשביל לא לפגוע בתושבים המקומיים, תיזהרו מקנסות על חניה אסורה.

השלט אינו מואר בלילה אז תמונה איתו אפשרית רק באור יום.

(Translated by Google) A nice park in the center of Solvang.
Park There is a statue of Christian Andersen, author of the Little Mermaid.

Incidentally, according to the original legend, unlike the familiar version of the Hippie Hand, the mermaid must murder the prince she loved, and will not become foam. But in the end she does not murder him and becomes a light daughter instead of Bat Yam. We agree that the familiar version is nicer.

The park has public services at a reasonable level of cleanliness plus. In front of them there is also a drink for four-wheelers.
At the edge of the park there is a monument to the fallen of Solvang in the wars of the United States.

(Original)
פארק נחמד במרכז העיירה סולבנג.
פארק ישנו פסל של כריסטיאן אנדרסן, מחבר בת הים הקטנה.

אגב לפי האגדה המקורית בשונה מהגרסה המוכרת עם ההפי הנד, על בת הים לרצוח את הנסיך שאהבה, ולא תהפוך לקצף גלים. אבל בסופו של דבר היא לא רוצחת אותו והופכת לבת אור במקום בת ים. נסכים שהגרסה המוכרת יותר נחמדה.

בפארק ישנם שרותים ציבורים ברמת נקיון סבירה פלוס. מולם ישנה ברזיה גם להולכים על ארבע.
בקצה הפארק ישנה אנדרטה לנופלים של סולבנג במלחמות ארצות הברית.

(Translated by Google) Madison Square: (across from the Flatairon) The square bears the name of the fourth President of the United States, James Madison, the Madison Square Garden building adjacent to the square in its first two incarnations. In the park is a large branch of the famous "Shake Shack" burger chain (highly recommended).

In the block on the southwestern side of the square, Eataly NYC Flatiron has a chain of Italian delicatessen and ice cream parlors. It is highly recommended to have a light breakfast here with good Italian coffee. Adjacent to the complex is a Lego chain shop recommended for children.

(Original)
כיכר מדיסון: (מול הפלאטאיירון)  הכיכר נושאת את שמו של נשיא ארצות הברית הרביעי, ג'יימס מדיסון, המבנה מדיסון סקוור גארדן שכן בסמוך לכיכר בשני גלגוליו הראשונים. בפארק נמצא סניף גדול של רשת  המבורגרים המפורסמת "Shake Shack" (מומלץ מאוד).

בגוש הבניינים בצד הדרום מערבי של הכיכר שוכן סניף Eataly NYC Flatiron רשת של מתחמי מסעדות מעדניות וגלידריות מאיטליה. מומלץ מאוד לאכול כאן  ארוחת בוקר קלילה עם קפה איטלקי טוב. צמוד למתחם ישנה חנות של רשת לגו שמומלצת לילדים.

(Translated by Google) North of the fantasy land is a small world devoted entirely to Mikey Mouse and his party.
The real deal here is Mikey's house, Gopi's house and Donald's boat.

Mickey's house can be photographed with Mickey Mouse with a park photographer to upload the pictures to the application (worth the most).

In the southwest part of the complex there is a gadget train which is a roller coaster for small children. From a height of 89 cm.
The fountain is also really cool for kids.
In the courtyard of Gopi's house there is a place for playing even for really small children (under two years).

צפונית לארץ הפנטזיה שוכן עולם קטן שמוקדש כולו למייקי מאוס וחבורתו.
האטקציה המכרזית כאן הוא הבית של מייקי, הבית של גופי וסירה של דונלד.

בבית של מיקי אפשר להצטלם עם מיקי מאוס עם צלם של הפארק שיעלה את התמונות לאפליקציה (שווה ביותר).

בחלק הדרום מערבי של המתחם ישנה רכבת גאדג'ט שהיא רכבת הרים לילדים קטנים. מגובה של 89 ס"מ.
המזרקה במקום גם ממש מגניבה לילדים.
בחצר של הבית של גופי יש מקום משחק גם לילדים ממש קטנים (מתחת לשנתיים).

(Translated by Google) World Trade Center Building 1 (Herut Building). The towering structure in New York City dominates the skyline of the city, much like the twin towers it was before. The building is built in a modern style and there is considerable investment in its construction.

The height of the building is 1,776 feet (541.3 meters), as the year of independence of the United States.

Please note that, according to the New York Police Department, the building has been removed from the road (unlike the Twin Towers originally) and its lower floors are built without glass due to fear of injury.

בניין מרכז הסחר העולמי 1 (בניין החרות). המבנה הגובה בניו יורק ושולט היטב בקו הרקיע של העיר, בדומה למגדלי התאומים שהיו לפניו. המבנה בנוי בסגנון מודרני וניכרת השקעה הרבה בבנייתו.

גובהו של המבנה 1,776 רגל (541.3 מטר), כשנת העצמאות של ארצות הברית.

שימו לב שלפי דרישת משטרת ניו יורק הבניין הורחק הבניין מהכביש (בשונה ממגדלי התאומים במקור) והקומות התחתונות שלו בנויות ללא זכוכית בגלל החשש מפגועים.
dislikes: Lack of glass on lower floors

reviews_attraction.text:
(Translated by Google) A very comprehensive and invested car museum.
The showrooms and even the toilets are clean and tidy.
The vehicle display is very interesting, and in my opinion one of the factors that sets the museum apart is the display of vehicles from films such as:
Batman, Back to the Future, Thelma and Louise, etc.

There are also very nice games for children, so those who come with small children can leave them there (under supervision of course) and walk around the museum without the children.

The museum has adjacent parking (for a fee) and it is recommended to park there.

(Original)
מוזיאון רכב מקיף ומושקע ביותר.
חדרי התצוגה ואפילו השרותים מצוחצחים ומוסדרים.
תצוגת הרכב מענינת מאוד, ולדעתי אחד הגורמים המיחדים את המוזיאון הוא תצוגת רכבים מסרטים כגון:
באטמן,בחזרה לעתיד, תלמה ולואיז וכו'.

ישנה גם משחקיה מאוד נחמדה לילדים, אז מי שמגיע עם ילדים קטנים יכול להשאיר אותם שם (בהשגחה כמובן) ולהסתובב במוזיאון ללא הילדים.

למוזיאון חניה צמודה (בתשלום) ומומלץ לחנות שם.

(Translated by Google) Great place if coming with small children.
The bottom of the fountain is a (rough) surface with lots of small fountains.
The water is about 3 cm high, and kids are really happy to run there and play in the water.

There are chairs and tables around the fountain for the parents.
Instead, the Star Bucks branch also serves public services (in good Nikon mode I was there) and an ATM.

Do yourself a favor and make a coffee break here, and let your kids go a little crazy in the water (under your supervision, of course).

(Original)
מקום מצוין אם מגיעים עם ילדים קטנים.
החלק התחתון של המזרקה הוא משטח (מחוספס) עם המון מזרקות קטנות.
המים בגובה של 3 ס"מ בערך, וילדים ממש שמחים לרוץ שם ולשחק במים.

סביב המזרקה ישנם כסאות ושולחנות לטובת ההורים.
במקום גם סניף סטאר באקס שרותים ציבורים (במצב ניקון טוב שאני ההיתי שם) וגם כספומט.

תעשו לעצמכם טובה ותעשו כאן הפסקת קפה, ותשחררו את הילדים שלכם להשתולל קצת במים (בהשגחה שלכם כמובן).

(Translated by Google) Garden in Central Park named for the famous song "Forever Strawberry Fields" by Lennon and Paul McCartney.

In the center of the garden is the famous mosaic, with the title Imagine as the name of the famous song, which is ranked third in the list of Rolling Stone magazine's 500 greatest songs of all time.

The place serves as a memorial dedicated to John Lennon's memory and on his birthday and his murder day is filled with fans singing his songs.

In my opinion from the duty points for a visitor to Central Park.

(Original)
גן בסנטרל פארק על שם השיר המפורסם "שדות תותים לנצח" של לנון ופול מקרטני.

במרכז גן ישנו הפסיפס המפורסם ועליו הכיתוב Imagine כשמו של השיר המפורסם אשר דורג במקום השלישי ברשימת 500 השירים הגדולים בכל הזמנים של המגזין של הרולינג סטון .

המקום משמש כאנדרטה שמוקדשת לזכרו של ג'ון לנון  וביום הולדתו וביום הירצחו מתמלא מעריצים ששרים משיריו.

לדעתי מנקודות החובה למבקר בסנטרל פארק.

(Translated by Google) Ramble: A complex that has been simulated by architecture and nature walks.

A trip to the complex makes you forget that you are in the heart of one of the busiest cities in the world!

There are many ways to get from Ramble to anywhere, in my opinion the most fun is just to walk around and feel what it is like to do a nature walk in central New York.

Kids will love running around here, just notice that some paths also have (not much) stairs which makes it difficult if walking around with strollers.

(Original)
הרמבל: מתחם שבא לדמות על ידי אדריכלות סביבה טיול טבע.

טיול במתחם גורם לך לשכוח שאתה נמצא בלב אחת הערים הסואנות  בעולם!

ישנם דרכים רבות ברמבל להגיע ממקום למקום, לדעתי הכי כיף סתם להסתובב המקום ולהרגיש איך זה לעשות טיול טבע במרכז ניו יורק.

ילדים ישמחו להתרוצץ כאן, רק שימו לב שבחלק משבילים יש גם מדרגות (לא הרבה) דבר שמקשה אם מסתובבים עם עגלות.

(Translated by Google) A promenade overlooking a beach filled with sea elephants.
There are two roads south and one north.
Each way is short (a few hundred meters).
When I visited the place it was recommended to go north.
You can see countless sea elephants, some of them sleeping in the sun and some of them quite active.
Parking on site does not cost money.
It is absolutely forbidden to feed the local inhabitants.
It should be noted that there are no toilets or even cans.

(Original)
טיילת תצפית על חוף שמלא בפילי ים.
מהחניון יוצאים שתי דרכים אחת דרומה ואחת צפונה.
כל דרך היא קצרה (מאות מטרים בודדים).
שאני בקרתי במקום היה מומלץ ללכת צפונה.
במקום ניתן לראות אינספור פילי ים, חלקם ישנים בשמש וחלקם פעילים למדי.
החניה במקום לא עולה כסף.
אסור בתכלית האיסור להאכיל את דירי המקום.
יש לשים לב שאין שרותים ואפילו לא פחים.

(Translated by Google) Horton Park: A new park built on the site of a park with the same name.
Today it is a large and well-kept park with a large amphitheater, and a beautiful fountain named after the street that borders the park to the north.

Nice place to sit for a cup of coffee and let the kids run a little.

(Original)
פארק הורטון: פארק חדש שנבנה במקום שבו עמד בעבר פארק בשם זהה.
כיום מדובר בפארק גדול ומטופח שבו אמפיתאטרון גדול, ומזרקת יפה על שם הרחוב שתוחם את הפארק מצפון.

מקום נחמד לשבת לכוס קפה ולתת לילדים לרוץ קצת.

(Translated by Google) Federal Hall: A national monument commemorating American independence. George Washington was sworn in with this structure, and the first US congressional meeting was held here.

The interior of the building is of no interest to anyone who is not an American or an American history lover.

(Original)
הפדראל הול: אנדרטה לאומית שמנציחה את העצמאות האמרקאית. במבנה זה הושבע ג'ורג וושנגטון וכאן גם התקיים אספת הקונגרס הראשונה של ארה"ב.

פנים המבנה אינו מהווה עניין למי שלא אמרקאי או חובב היסטוריה אמרקאית.

(Translated by Google) A garden found inside a bellagio hotel.
The garden is small and can be completed in a few minutes (10-20 minutes).

The exhibition in the garden is changing, and not permanent.
Most of the exhibition is highly invested and worth visiting for those who are walking around.

Admission is free.

(Original)
גן שהמצא בתוך מלון bellagio.
הגן קטן וניתן להשלים סיבוב בו במספר דקות (10-20 דקות).

התערוכה בגן משתנה, ואינה קבועה.
לרוב התערוכה מאוד מושקעת ושווה לבקר למי שמסתובב בסביבה.

הכניסה חופשית.

(Translated by Google) The Bridge Bridge, built of iron, was the largest bridge in Central Park, and is a famous focal point for photographs in the park.
Do not be surprised if you see a couple of couples on their wedding day come to be photographed there.

(Original)
גשר "Bow Bridge" שבנוי מברזל היינו הגשר הגדול ביותר בסנטרל פארק, ומהווה מוקד מפורסם לצילומים בפארק.
אל תופתעו אם תראו מספר זוגות ביום חתונתם באים להצטלם במקום.

(Translated by Google) A really lovely place to look at the mammals of these days.
You can see some swimming in the water if looking for good.
In my opinion, it is a mandatory place for anyone who casts in the area

מקום ממש מקסים להתבונן ביונקים הימים הללו.
אפשר לראות את חלקם שוחים במים אם מחפשים טוב.
לדעתי מקום חובה למי שמטיל באזור.

I think it blends in nicely with the downtown environment.
Did not go inside.
