לדעתי משתלב יפה עם הסביבה של הדאון טאון.
לא נכנסו פנימה.

(Translated by Google) Windmill like Denmark.

Beautiful background for a souvenir picture from Solvang.

(Original)
תחנת רוח כמו בדנמרק.

רקע יפה לתמונה מזכרת מסולבנג.

A very nice hiking trail. We were there with kids (5, 10 and 12) and they all did really well. We didn't get to the top (the kids were getting tired) but reached several points on the hike with beautiful views. There is a mixture of sun and shade. Sun screen recommended. It's a narrow steep path so not good for strollers. No dogs allowed on this trail. We came midday on a weekday and found parking easily. There are several lot spots and some street parking as well.

Nice wide playing area with some interesting equipment. There's a sand pit, swings, slides, climbing equipment, sand pit and a few more options. It's a great space for hide and seek. There's also a basketball court, soccer field, tennis courts, dog park and concrete path for scooters and skateboards. They are currently doing construction on the open field, so no space to play a ballgame at this time.

The science center is a L.A. treasure! Parking is $12 (CASH ONLY) and entrance is free. This is a whole day, hands on, educational and entertaining spot for kids of all ages. You must keep a close eye on your little ones, because it's usually crowded. From a simulated earthquake to an aquarium with sharks. There's SO much to do and see. This place never gets old for my kids (2-13).

This is wonderful as a beach option. It's not at all nerve wracking because the water is shallow, there are lifeguards on duty, it's a gated area and everything is in close proximity of each other. It can be fun for all ages, because there are sprinklers, slides and a big area for the big ones to swim. They also have fun digging in the sand, so don't forget the sand toys!

Love this place! So many options that keep the kids entertained for hours. The famous Noah's ark is always fun and the art room has great supplies. There's the archaeological dig on the third floor which is cute. And the exhibits are always interesting, but I usually don't have time to visit them since my kids spend most of their time at the other areas mentioned above!

A beautiful small park, in a residential neighborhood, with a magnificent view of the beach. There are many benches to just relax and take in the beauty. There is a cute playground adjacent, but distant enough as to not disturb the serenity of the benches/grassy area. There are a couple of fun climbing trees. Great to come with or without kids.

Great experience for the whole family. The tour guide was knowledgeable, friendly and answered all questions. The building itself is a piece of architectural art! Every where you look are intricacies. And it's free! Just show up and enjoy the tour.

Tiny park in middle of the Venice canals. It was a great spot to take a break, but only 1 climbing area with one slide and 2 swings and no area for big kids to play around. It was a nice place to rest our feet, but wouldn't come just for the park.

This park has it all. The weather is perfect, the views are magnificent, a playground for the kids, large grass area for picnics, an amphitheater and a century old lighthouse tour that'll being you back in time. I could've stayed there all day

It's always fun at a Dodger's game. The seats are great, the stadium is beautiful. Parking can be long wait to get into, so uber if you can. As with all stadiums, the food is outrageously priced, but it's part of the experience.

Its an awesome trail. I carry my 2 yr old in a back carrier and it takes just under one hour to take the trail up and down. Its not too busy and has wide paths. Beautiful views of the Hollywood sign, downtown and all around.

Came here for a pre-screening of a movie. The grounds are beautiful and everyone is friendly. Wish I could've had more time to walk around, but they were very careful to only lead us to the theater and back out.

A quiet Oasis. The red and blue hike was difficult, but worth it for the view on top! Recommended for ages 8 and up due to some steep areas. After the hike, the kids enjoyed some time by the beach at the lake.
Friendly staff, lots of options and reasonably priced. It's a great place to bring a family of different ages. The only complaint I have was the facilities we're a little old and there were wasps.
Breathtaking!  A short hike down to the lake.  You can go to the beach area, or find a more secluded spot where there are scattered picnic tables and entrances to the lake.  It was so beautiful.
This has a playground with swings, sand and a small climbing area. All with little shade. If the weather is not too hot, it's a good spot for change of scenery, but not a full day park.
Great park with a fun splash pad, sandy play area, cool climbing for older kids, a basketball court and a library. You can easily spend a few hrs without the looks being bored!
Love this hike.  It's shady,  quiet and a good workout.  It's about a 45 min hike depending on how fast you go. Be aware as bicyclists come here occasionally.
This is a small playground. There are some grassy, shaded areas. There is also a library on the property. Nice spot to let the kids let out a bit of energy.
For all your little train lovers this is a great spot. Free entrance and a cute train ride, with a minimal fee, to end the tour of the trains.
Beautiful grounds. The splash pad is great, except it's hard to enjoy due to the swarms of bees. We had to leave because of them.
Was not impressed. The actual exhibits were well done, but lost it's flavor by being in a run down, poorly lit facility.
Great hikes with awesome views. Very kid friendly. Gorgeous grass area perfect for a picnic and throw around a ball.
The people who hang out here a bit shady, but the equipment is fun and there's a gated area for the little ones.
Small Oasis in the heart of Beverly hills. There are tables and chairs to eat lunch or go for a date.

This is a great park. It has sufficient activities to keep you occupied for the better part of the day. there is a wonderful playground for the younger children with a sand pit, a wooden boat, sprinklers, swings for both the babies and the older kids and lots and lots of climbing things. the older children also have a basket ball court and baseball. there is a pond in the park and lots of trails to walk / scoot / bike on and of course plenty of grass to picnic on. there are no barbecue stand and i am not sure if it is allowed. as an added bonus, there is a farmer's market on Saturdays so you can get your lunch / breakfast there and enjoy the park for the day.

They have a new exhibit -  Medieval Jewish History which was very interesting (also small) - I thin it's on exhibit until January. It's in the lower level leading to the garden.
If you are a Ny resident,  you can pay whatever you want which is so nice because we were only there for about 45 minutes. There are tours which are good if it's your first time so you can get a sense of the exhibits. There's always a lot of information to read so it can get overwhelming- so with children,  short visits are great. Also, if you are going with children,  they have a scavenger hunt throughout the museum which makes it so much more fun.

Really nice museum. A little small but it's perfect to manage in a hour with kids.
There is a room that has an optical illusion- you're supposed to go in on your own but kids freak out on there by themselves(it's not scary, you can just get a bit disorientated), so I would recommend an adult go in with the younger kids 6-8 - kids older can go in together they should be fine. There are a lot of fascinating artifacts and the interesting history of Chinese in California.
Quite a few of the exhibits encourage you to slow down and have some quiet reflection time which is also great for the kids as they automatically calm down.

This place is busy and hectic so much going on. It's just like Time Square but by the ocean. Take your water and don't buy anything - over priced. There are plenty of places to eat if you want tho. Walk up and down the wharf and you can see street performers, people watch and just look around. DO NOT park here - the prices are insane. On the weekend it can get over $60 for the day - that's just wrong. Park somewhere else or, if you're in Oakland,  take the ferry over it's a lovely ride. Give yourself about 2 hours here - any more and it can become overwhelming.

Amazing place. It's a bit pricey- they charge per person in the vehicle (as opposed to per car) but worth it. The space is so vast and wide - and it wonderful to walk from piece to piece. Even if you were to spend the whole day here you wouldn't see everything.  Apart from the art sculptures,  the scenery itself is a work of art. Just stunning. Autumn(fall) and spring are the best times to come here as there is not much shade and summer would probably be too unforgiving.  You can come with blankets and a picnic and just chill for the day.

This is an amazingly designed playground. If you have little kids it's very difficult to sit and keep an eye on them you have to run with them. But for older kids who like to explore it's amazing. There is so much to keep them entertained - the regular play structures or the natural rocks that they can go rock climbing on!
2 things that bothered me as a parent - 1)there were not enough drinking water fountains and 2) you have to walk around the park to look for the garbage bins! Not nearly enough for that huge space.

Beautiful. We happened to come during an event and it was spectacular.  Kites everywhere. There was a kite workshop where kids could make their own and the go fly it. There was a section where more serious kite flyers were and they had these amazing ones with tails! There were some vendors - food, drinks, snacks etc... the grounds are beautiful and there are hinking trails. Just keep an eye on where you park and if you move your car, just be aware that each section has it's own parking code.

What a beautiful place. You could easily spend half a day here. The drive up to the information center and monument is through a naval base - there is also a huge cemetery on the way up in a beautiful location overlooking the ocean.
So much to see and do at the monument. There is a small exhibit that is very informative. And the reenactment performers are really great. The lighthouse is wonderful to see and so cool that you can go into the house. The grounds are wonderfully kept as well.

What a wonderful discovery. There are paths that you walk and all sorts of nooks and crannies and little side streets. The houses are part of the scenery and are really beautiful. The people who live here seem to be amused by the tourists but are kind anyway. There are so many bridges and it looks like you can take a row boat out as well. Take lots of water with you. Try to keep track of where you are it seems easy to get ost there. You can either exit Venice beach side or the street.

This is a great museum if you live in the city. Do not make a day trip with this the main feature. In summer there are more activities here as they open up the outside and have the water activities. But overall, you can be in and out in under 2 hours. Good for children up to age 6. For the older kids the best floors are 4th floor and basement. The basement has different exhibits every few months. 4 stars because it's pricey... $14/person.... toddlers included.

Beautiful quintessential picturesque views with lots of benches and green space. You can walk or sit and just take in the ocean view. Bring a blanket and sit on the grass with a little picnic. There are hiking trails that go all around. In the evenings there is a community orchestra that plays chamber music. There are quite a few places to park all around. It gets chilly so bring a long sleeve something.

Wonderful little lighthouse with a delightful park. There are quite a few benches to sit on and admire the view and enjoy the fresh air. The path to the lighthouse are original laid stones that are beautiful but uneven so be careful when walking. You can actually walk all around the lighthouse. People are so nice, they stopped to talk to us and gave us tips on what to see and do in the area. Lovely.

This is a fantastic place to come for activities. They offer tons of classes for kids and adults. The facilities are great and the recreational grounds are offer a lot too. In summer you can enjoy wonderful picnics and the beautiful view and in winter you can just come ice skating and take advantage of the indoor swimming. The only down side is the smell as the whole park is built on a land fill.

Nice little museum. There is a lot of information in a small space. In the canal room there are some interactive things for kids and fun exhibits. In each room there is a lot of information to take in. This museum can easily be done in an hour.
Right next to the museum is a ferry that you can take rides (they are 2 hours so we did not take a tour as that is way too long with kids).

It's a bit of a walk to the beach, but it's a nice walk along a trail. The beach is not so sandy - more rocky but there are lots of shells for collecting. There is also quite a bit of seaweed.  There are some protected areas that are roped off so look out for these. Quite a bit of wildlife which is so wonderful to be around.
You have to pay for parking

Its like a party - you can't help but have a great time. The MC, dj and other staff are so professional they rope you in and make sure you have a blast. Amateur night on Wednesdays is fantastic and so affordable - date night or just friends poonight out its fun. The other shows that are put on there are great too.

Wonderful museum. This has been on out "to do" list for a while. Its great for children of all ages and adults. We spent the whole day there and saw the majority of what the museum has to offer. Coming from NYC tho, this museum does not warrent membership but it would for local families.

This is such a great neighborhood place to come. In the summer they have tons of activities and events and it's just fantastic to come and just enjoy the grounds. The cobblestone is so wonderfully unexpected in upper Manhattan.  Chris was great as were all the rest of the staff

Beautiful views. There are chairs to relax and enjoy the view and atmosphere.  You can walk down to the dock (there's a ramp/incline)and see the boats and do a bit of fishing. The restaurants in the area adhere to social distancing and there are lines and wait lists

The walk down to the Hudson, with the bridge right there was spectacular.  The paths are easy to follow for a comfortablehike or bike ride. Wear comfortable walking shoes. Picnic tables to sit at fun for kids to run around

Went to see WWE. As huge as this place is, you can still see the stage/arena pretty clearly and they have the TVs too. There are consession stands on every floor. Going high up you can easily get vertigo.
Beautiful place. Lots of activites. Boats. Fishing. Swimming. Hiking and more. All in a beautiful setting. The pool is huge and perfect for kids of all ages and adults.
Went ice skating. Very very affordable, the staff is amazing and if you go early it's not crowded. Great activity to do with the kids.
This park is an oasis in the city. Beautiful green with serine spots and busy areas depending on what you're in the mood for
The gardens a peaceful.  A bit stark in early spring but you can still enjoy the budding flowers and view.

Unfortunately I didn't get to visit Keeneland during the racing season, but visiting it a few weeks after a major auction was still exciting.

We toured the facilities with Fred, who was very knowledgeable and friendly. We learned that Keeneland is open all year and is primarily an auction house, and then a race track. Touring the facilities on a crisp Fall day was perfect and it was great to take a peek behind the scenes, walk through the paddock and see where celebrities and millionaires bid on horses.

I would definitely recommend taking a tour, though the gift shop is quite disappointing. But then again, I was there to learn, not buy Longchamp bags.

I finally had an opportunity to stop by the Federal Hall National Memorial on a rare weekday off and I can't wait to return.

Entering the Rotunda, you'll see a lot of "dioramas" (or displays) of the city's geography and buildings from way back when.

Stepping to the rear, you'll see a replica of the Constitution, as well as various other exhibits that give you chills as they relate to the founding of our country.

Don't miss the vaults off the Rotunda, which housed valuables and now hold air conditioning units.

AND, don't forget to get your National Parks Stamp!!

The Skywalk Observatory on the 50th floor of the Prudential Center is by far a must-visit when in town, whether you're a tourist or resident.

Tip: From the main shops floor, you have to go down an escalator to take an elevator to the 50th floor where you can purchase tickets before entering. The skywalk itself is pretty empty, just the perimeter of the floor but it offers breathtaking 360 degree views of Boston and surrounding areas, even further on a clear day. Definitely worth the admission fee that's around $15.

A great museum for adults and kids alike, with interesting, interactive displays for each exhibit. I think the highlight of my visit were the turtles though the dinosaurs in the side room with a skylight (and visibility from the floor above) gave them a run for their money just for being a great photo opp!
It's absolutely free, not what I expected, but love it! That leaves more money to enjoy the cafe on the top floor, which smelled delicious and was packed, though I did not stop by to dine.

This was the second stop on our vineyards tour and we enjoyed a tasting flight in the main tasting room. The larger, open area, which was being used for groups, looked lovely and I almost wish we sat in there to sample our wine. But, if we did, we would have missed out on John and Judy's extensive discussions on the differences between their lovely wines.

While mostly a white wine person, their BBQ red was AMAZING and I wish I grabbed a bottle to go!

This is a gorgeous beach that I totally didn't expect to find after the initial approach. Along the causeway, cars are parked with people fishing and sunbathing in the spots. We arrived at the main beach area, which was pretty packed for a Tuesday afternoon but then again, it was winter break. The beach is clean, the facilities are decent and I just love that there are areas in the shade if you need it.

Be sure to pay for parking, wherever you park!

I arrived here an hour before it was posted to be closed (both on Google Maps and their official website) but they had a sign posted that they closed earlier, which was so unfortunate as it's a six hour drive from where I live in NY. I only got to see the outside of the original Harriet Tubman home, the outside of the visitor center and her actual home. They were lovely but it would have been nice to be able to learn about while touring, too.

This is definitely an obligatory photo opportunity when in Key West and you're more than likely to see a line when you stop by to take a photo. Avoid this by coming just after sunrise in the morning and/or by keeping an eye on the cruise line arrivals. Whatever time you do arrive, be sure to bring sunglasses and a flash on your camera. Also, look around to see the historical plaques for interesting information about the buoy and area.

I, too, came here at the end of the holi/phagwah parade and was just overwhelmed at the size of the park! I expected a small neighborhood park, but this park has it all: basketball courts, handball courts; two jungle gyms/playgrounds, baseball fields and a comfort station. As Zia mentioned, the comfort station and water fountains aren't turned on until it's warmer out, so make sure you come prepared.
dislikes: Comfort station not available in colder weather
Water fountains not operational in colder weather

reviews_attraction.text:
I'm not a fan of modern art, but MoMA has a nice combination of classic artists with the more ridiculous artists. (Sorry, but it has to be said). While one exhibit will make you scratch your head, you can move on to another exhibit that will just have you speechless.

Sort of expensive admission but try to get there on a night where it's free so you can spend more money at the amazing gift shop(s).

This zoo is perfect for small kids and big kids alike. Not exactly the place to spend an entire day, but if you get there early enough, you can do the entire zoo in a three hours without crowds. Make sure you check out the sea lion feeding schedule and my personal favorite, the gopher holes. Sure, adults may be a bit big to be squeezing in there but you won't want to miss out on that photo opp.

I only just recently discovered Bush Terminal Piers Park on a recent walk on the waterfront and was pleasantly surprised to discover a green oasis in such an industrial area. There are clean public restrooms, bike and pedestrian lanes in addition to great viewpoints to admire the NYC skyline. If you're a baseball or soccer fan, check out the fields for both pick-up and organized games.

Fearless Girl is a beautiful bronze statue that, like the Charging Bull, is a piece of art installed without permission from the city.
At basically any time, you'll likely face huge crowds, people standing in the way of images of the bull and a complete inability to take a photo of the girl staring down the bull as intended but seeing the statue with the crowds is quite the experience.

The pavilion itself is a sight to see (especially if you're a Men in Black fan) but don't expect to get any closer than taking photos this Worlds Fair piece of history as tours are offered very, very infrequently and only during special occasions, if at all. The nearby Queens Museum has a World Fair memorabilia exhibit which nicely complements this pavilion.

Number one reason why this park rules? Because the annual pillow fight is held here.

Seriously, it's a gorgeous little park in the middle of everything. Nothing like going to Crocodile Lounge then stopping by for a little people-watching on a bench.

I've never purchased anything from the vendors, but they do have cute things and a little Winter market.

Whether you're in the area or you have to travel to get here, it's worth it to visit an American legend. You can explore the outdoor tar pits without paying the price of admission but to tie your entire experience together, do visit the museum first. It's just a really cool place and seeing what they've discovered in the deep tar pits is fascinating.

I attended a corporate appreciation party here and enjoyed going through the eight floors of the museum, even if all the exhibits weren't up my alley. I'm not really a fan of modern art though I did find the 1930-40s and 1965+ exhibits most interesting. The Whitney has lovely outdoor space including a nice rooftop area with shaded seating options.

I've seen a number of shows here over the course of my life and nothing beats the grandeur of the theater and its restrooms, though they are looking a bit tired as of late. I prefer to view any show from the mezzanine — especially with the Rockettes — though orchestra seats are also fair for concerns. Prices are pricey, as expected.

Garden Key Lighthouse is a part of Dry Tortugas National Park on the main island and is on the top floor of of Fort Jefferson, accessible via stairs only. It stands out from the rest of the fort as it's black and the fort itself is made of brown bricks. It's a beautiful lighthouse and you must visit if you're at Dry Tortugas.

I'm with the other reviewers: it's a must-visit place if you're a tourist and a must-go-to place to people watch. Ever since they finished the renovations, the park is even more vibrant than before and nothing beats sitting around the fountain. You'll catch an impromptu concert, dancers and a million dogs on any given day.

As a New Yorker, I have to admit it, this park is exactly what baseball stadiums should be! Great views no matter where you sit, wide outdoor decks to catch the sun while enjoying a cold beer and great food.
Note: Sneaking onto the Green Monster isn't possible without tickets though.

We may have everything in NYC but In-N-Out and the San Diego Zoo, but I consider this Zoo the San Diego Zoo of the West Coast.

It's a huge zoo and there's something for every age group. Definitely worth a day trip but start early and wear your sneakers!

If you're lucky enough to know an employee, you'll be able to take a tour of this place on the weekend as I was. While the cafeteria isn't open on the weekend, both the bookshop and gift shop are open. Huge selection of goods at fair prices can be found.

The views of Manhattan and back on Brooklyn warrant a five star rating. Soaking up the older fisherman vibe here is a plus, but the lack of a bathroom and the fish pieces everywhere (not on the designated cutting boards) is a definite minus.

You must visit if you're a history buff to learn about Brooklyn's wonderful past, as today you'd never imagine such a simple life. It's great for adults and kids alike, with special programs throughout the year.

(Translated by Google) Liufang Garden is a tourist attraction on the outskirts of San Marino, California. The project is built on 12 acres of land in the Huntington Library, Art Collection and Botanical Gardens.

On the outskirts of San Marino, California, there is a tranquil garden that connects plants, poetry, and scattered overseas Chinese with elegant and great ancient Chinese civilization. On February 17, the Los Angeles Times published an article entitled "The Huntington Library Completed a New Chinese Garden", introducing the window of Chinese culture opened in California.

After more than ten years of preparation and construction, the largest Chinese park in North America, "Lifang Garden" officially opened its doors to the public on February 23, 2008.
The first appearance of the poetic and picturesque "Liufang Garden" attracted a large number of people to visit the park. “Yu Yu Tang”, “Sanyou Pavilion”, “Love Lotus”, “Shuiyun Gallery” and other buildings full of Chinese traditional culture charm make visitors stop to take pictures and take pictures. A young Chinese couple told reporters that they came to the United States from Hong Kong when they were children. They used to travel to China and watched the gardens in the south of the Yangtze River. They saw that the Liufang Garden felt very cordial and very Chinese. They will often come with their families in the future. Garden.

Liufang Garden, which follows the architectural style of Suzhou, China, is located in the Huntington Library in San Marino, near Los Angeles. The planned area of ​​Liufang Park is 12 acres. The first phase of the completed project covers an area of ​​3.5 acres. The first phase of the project cost about 18 million US dollars. The water fountains, pavilions, arch bridges, promenades, leaking windows, rock formations, etc. in the Liufang Garden...The architectural elements of traditional Suzhou gardens are all available. Seven pavilions and five stone bridges were built around a five-acre artificial lake. The garden is green and the flowers are overflowing. The exquisite and beautiful garden architecture and the surrounding natural environment form a charming landscape full of poetry and painting. Liufangyuan respects the principle of Chinese garden layout of “stepping to change the scenery”. When tourists walk along the garden path between pavilions and pavilions, every corner can see new scenery.
In order to let Liufangyuan maintain the authenticity of Suzhou gardens, the design and construction personnel are mainly worked by skilled craftsmen from Suzhou Garden Construction Company. The main building materials are purchased from China, and more than 100 containers of construction materials are shipped from China before and after. The stone is as high as 850 tons. In the most critical stage of garden construction, more than 50 Suzhou garden designers and engineers have built this authentic Chinese park after more than six months of construction.
“Liufang Garden” is located in the famous Huntington Library in the United States. It is a collection of rare books, manuscripts, art collections and botanical gardens. It was founded in 1919 by the famous American railway king Henry Huntington. . In the 1990s, the Huntington Library launched the China Park Project, which raised a total of about US$27 million. In 2005, the first phase of the “Lifangfang” project was officially started. As of 2005, six Chinese-style gardens have been built in North America, and Liufang Park is the largest one.
"Liufangyuan" is a poem from Cao Zhi's "Luo Shen Fu", "steps are thin and flowing." It is designed according to Suzhou classical gardens and lasted for 10 years, costing 20 million US dollars. The “Liufang Garden” now covers an area of ​​3.5 hectares and will be expanded in three phases in the future. The total area will reach 12 hectares. The park includes pavilions, arch bridges, promenades, rockeries and other attractions, and has a name that is rich in Chinese culture, such as "Yu Yu Tang", "Love Lotus", "Yu Yuqiao", "Luo Yan Chau" Wait.

The founder of the library, Henry Huntington (1850-1927), was a visionary industrialist of that era, and was known as the "king of the railway" in the United States. When he was 21, he began to help his uncle to run the railway company. After that, he settled in Los Angeles to run his own business, repaired the railway in California, and bought a 207-acre San Marino estate. Now he has used about 90 acres, and a large part of the land has not yet been used. Development.
Huntington, who is passionate about collecting the best of culture around the world, retired at the age of 60 and is dedicated to the collection of books, manuscripts and art. The Huntingtons signed a contract in 1919 to transfer their manor and collection to a non-profit educational custody, creating the Huntington Library, Art Gallery and Botanical Complex and contributing to society. When Huntington died in 1927, he left $8 million in cash assets for the management of the library.
The Huntington Library has a collection of 6 million rare books and manuscripts, mainly British and American literature and historical works, some with a history of five or six hundred years, and many maps of China in the 16th century. In the Jane Pavilion, the reporter saw a map of the southern part of the English-Chinese map translated by Portuguese in 1547 in Goa, India, and the first version of the map of China by Marco Polo.
The Huntington Library has been open to the public since 1928. It has been free until 1972, but as the cost of the library has grown, it has begun to make ends meet, so charges began. The library can accommodate 1,800 scholars to study here, with 23,000 regular member readers and 500,000 visitors a year.

The Los Angeles Chinese community pays special attention to the Huntington Library because it is building a 12-acre Chinese garden, which will be the largest Chinese garden outside China.
Huntington [1] I am very yearning for the ancient oriental culture. He always hopes that his manor can have some connection with Chinese culture. In 1912, Huntington bought a tea house and later added some buildings to form his Asian garden. A wooden bridge in the park was originally painted in a red Chinese bridge, but in the 1960s, the red paint completely fell off into a log color, and the style of the garden was also fixed into a Japanese garden, so the library was built. The idea of ​​a Chinese garden.
Ms. Moss, assistant deputy director of the library, said that the establishment of the "Chinese Garden" has always been the dream of the library, but it lacks starting capital. Later, the library received a donation of $500,000 from Aetna Insurance Company of New York. From then on, the library had a formal idea of ​​building a Chinese park, and signed a contract with the Suzhou Garden Architecture Design Institute of China, and hired Chen Jin, who graduated from Shanghai Tongji University, as the chief designer. Huntington's "Chinese Garden" design strives to fully express the Chinese classical garden art, blend the elegance of the Jiangnan gardens with the style of the northern royal gardens, and let the American people appreciate the poetry and painting of Chinese gardens. Shullman, director of the fund and public relations department of the library, said that we are proud to build Chinese classical gardens in the museum. Huntington's "Chinese Garden" overall design is divided into spring, summer, autumn and winter seasons, a total of nine gardens and eighteen scenes. After the completion of the "Chinese Garden", the Mid-Autumn Festival can be used to enjoy the moon. The Spring Festival can be used to watch the lights. 流芳园是位于美国加利福尼亚州圣马力诺郊区的一出旅游景点，该项目建在亨廷顿图书馆、艺术收藏馆和植物园的12英亩土地上。

在美国加利福尼亚州圣马力诺郊区，坐落着一座宁静的花园，它用优雅而伟大的中国古代文明，将植物、诗歌及散居的海外华人联系起来。美国《洛杉矶时报》2月17日刊发一篇题为《亨廷顿图书馆落成新的中式园林》的文章，介绍了在美国加州开启的这座中国文化之窗。

历经十余年的筹备与建设，北美最大的中式公园“流芳园”2008年2月23日正式向民众敞开大门。
充满诗情画意的“流芳园”初次亮相即吸引了大批民众前来游园。“玉茗堂”、“三友阁”、“爱莲榭”、“水云廊”等一个个充满中华传统文化韵味的建筑令游客驻足欣赏、拍照留影。一对年轻的华人夫妇告诉记者，他们儿时就从香港来到美国生活，曾经到中国旅游，看过江南园林，看到流芳园觉得很亲切，很有中国味道，以后会经常和家人一起来游园。

遵循中国苏州园林建筑风格的流芳园坐落于洛杉矶近郊圣玛利诺市亨廷顿图书馆内。流芳园规划面积十二英亩，已建成的一期工程占地三点五英亩，一期工程耗资约一千八百万美元。流芳园内水榭、亭台、拱桥、长廊、漏窗、怪石等等……传统苏州园林的建筑元素应有尽有。七座亭台楼阁、五座石桥围绕着一点五英亩的人工湖傍水而建。园内草木苍翠，花香四溢。精致优美的园林建筑与周围自然环境共同构成充满诗情画意的迷人景观。流芳园尊崇“移步换景”的中国园林布局原则，当游客沿着园中小径在亭台楼阁间漫步时，每到一个角落都能看到新的景致。
为了让流芳园保持苏州园林的原汁原味，设计施工人员主要由来自苏州园林建筑公司的能工巧匠担任，主要建筑材料都从中国采购，前后从中国运来一百多个集装箱的建筑材料，仅太湖石就多达八百五十吨。在最关键的园林建设阶段，五十多名苏州园林设计师和工程师历经六个多月的打造，终于成就了这座地道的中国园。
“流芳园”位于全美著名的亨庭顿图书馆内，该馆集珍奇图书、手稿、艺术品收藏和植物园林艺术为一体，由美国著名“铁路大王”亨利·亨廷顿于一九一九年创建。二十世纪九十年代亨庭顿图书馆启动中国园计划，先后共筹款约二千七百万美元，二00五年，“流芳园”一期工程正式动工。截至2005年，北美地区已建成六座中式园林，流芳园是其中规模最大的一个。
“流芳园”一名来自曹植《洛神赋》中的诗句“步蘅薄而流芳”。它按照苏州古典园林设计，历时10年，耗资2000万美元。“流芳园”现占地3.5公顷，今后还将分3期扩建，总占地面积将达到12公顷。园内包括亭台、拱桥、长廊、假山等景点，并且都起了富有中国文化韵味的名字，如“玉茗堂”、“爱莲榭”、“赏鱼桥”、“落燕洲”等。

图书馆的创始人亨利·亨廷顿（1850—1927）是那个时代有远见的实业家，当时在美国有“铁路大王”之称。他21岁时开始帮助叔父经营铁路公司，后定居洛杉矶经营自己的企业，在加州修铁路，并买下总面积为207英亩的圣马力诺庄园，如今已利用约90英亩，还有很大部分土地尚未开发。
热衷于收集世界各地文化精华的亨廷顿在60岁时退休，致力于珍版图书、手稿及艺术品的收藏。亨廷顿夫妇在1919年时签署了一份契约，把他们的庄园及馆藏转给一个非赢利的教育托管会，由此创建了亨廷顿图书馆、艺术馆和植物园综合体，并贡献给了社会。1927年亨廷顿辞世时还留下800万美元现金遗产，用于图书馆的管理。
亨廷顿图书馆现藏600万册珍本藏书及手稿，主要是英美文学与历史著作，有些有着五六百年的历史，还有不少16世纪的中国地图。在珍版馆，记者看到了一位葡萄牙地图专家1547年在印度果阿印制的根据葡萄牙文翻译的英文中国南部地图，还有马可·波罗的第一版中国地图。
亨廷顿图书馆从1928年起对外开放，1972年以前一直免费，但随着馆务费用日渐增长，开始入不敷出，于是开始收费。图书馆可接待1800名学者在此研究，并有固定会员读者2．3万名，每年接待50万参观者。

洛杉矶华人社区对亨廷顿图书馆格外关注，因为馆内正在兴建一个占地12英亩的中国园林，这将是中国境外最大的中国园林。
亨廷顿 [1]  本人对古老的东方文化十分向往，他一直希望他的庄园能与中国文化有某种联系。1912年时，亨廷顿买了一个茶馆，后来又增加一些建筑，形成了他心目中的亚洲园。园内的一座木桥原为漆成大红色的中国桥，但到了上个世纪60年代，红漆完全脱落成了原木色，园子的风格也定格成了日本园，于是图书馆又有了建一个中国园的念头。
图书馆助理副馆长莫斯尔女士说，建“中国园”一直是图书馆的梦想，但却缺少启动资金。1999年，图书馆的一位董事潘纳克先生辞世，他在遗嘱中留给图书馆1000万美元，并指名用于造中国园，后来图书馆又得到纽约安泰保险公司的50万美元捐款。从此时起，图书馆才有了建中国园的正式构想，并与中国苏州园林建筑设计院签订了合同，聘请毕业于上海同济大学的陈劲为总设计师。亨廷顿“中国园”的设计力求全面表现中国古典园林艺术，融会江南园林的淡雅和北方皇家园林的气派，并让美国民众领略中国园林的诗情画意。图书馆的基金与公关部主任舒尔曼表示，我们很自豪能在馆内兴建中国古典园林，庄园的馆藏涉及英美文学、历史、法国油画等，中国园林的建成将是亨廷顿庄园的典范。
亨廷顿“中国园”总体设计分春夏秋冬四季，共有九园十八景。一期工程将建夏园、峪园以及湖、池、廊、桥、亭、塔、茶室等景点，并以中国的桃、荷、桂、梅等林木展现四季不同景色。据介绍，夏园是完全按苏州园林风格设计的，园林的许多细部工艺，如雕刻、窗檩、木梁及瓦片等都将在苏州制造，以保证原汁原味的苏州风格。一期工程中亨廷湖里的石头要用真正的无锡太湖石。“中国园”建成后中秋可以赏月，春节可以观灯，还将开办茶艺等研究会，吸引各方人士前来学习，中国文化在美国的传播会得到更大发展。

Nice place to bring family to visit the rain forest, ride the classic boat, and watch the 3D, 4D movies, and many more....

They have it pretty well organized. The train ride is interesting, and the maze is in the Guinness book of world records as the largest in the world. The day we were there the people were giving out these little keys that fit this treasure chest they had set up. My girlfriend's key opened it. There were a bunch of different color origami paper dragons. You pick one, and unfold it to see your prize.  She won a chance to find a pearl by selecting a live oyster in a little tank. Hers contained 2 beautiful rose colored pearls about 1/4 inch in diameter.  Wow! She was thrilled to death. Those pearls cast a lovely glow over the rest of our vacation. May your visit be as lucky as ours!

Interesting little side trip worth taking. I was surprised to see the stark difference between a 1950s garden tractor and today's version. The one from the 50s looks just like a cute little scaled down Caterpillar D2. Are they serious? Tracks and  everything! Must have been a little tough on the lawn,  I can't even guess the weight of this thing. That is just one example of the interesting and well labeled implements sprinkled around. There's also a historical village that unfortunately we did not see. It's worth going back soon to finish checking this place out.

We have been to Old Hickory's place twice now, and we took the docent led tour of the mansion both times.  Very interesting and priceless items from the revolutionary war and the period just after. Then you walk or take a carriage ride to tour the grounds. One very cool thing to see is the spring that was used by Jackson's slaves, it just wells up right out of the ground. Never seen that before. What a trip that it's still that way with clear water just coming up out of this big hole. You better allow 4 to 5 hours for the Hermitage if you come.

Ah, memories. We would come here to surf when I was in my 20s (in the 80s) and back then the Amtrak stopped right at the end of the pier and people disembarked right on to the planks, right in to that bar that has one half on the left side of the pier and the other half on the right. Back then both sides were the bar, now one side is a restaurant. They had the best grilled Mahi I've ever had. Wow. On top of that the surfing is still great! Nice point break. Tube rides all day!

Whenever I visit these Pioneer memorials it always just takes me right down to the ground. Because you get an inkling of what they had to endure in order to open up the West. The whole story is laid out here, of the way their endurance was pushed beyond the limits and you can see from the writings of a TWELVE YEAR OLD GIRL which seem like the words of an old sage just how impossible it was for them to come back from the experience. Prepare to be moved.

This is a great way to beat the desert heat and also spend some time with nature. However,  you are going from the desert to 8500 feet altitude, so I highly recommend those little oxygen shot cannisters they sell in the gift shop. It's very scenic at the top with no undergrowth between the trees. Great for hiking.  The trees are numerous and very large. Nice place for a drink at the bar also.

It's a great place to get away from the Bay Area's hustle and bustle, close enough to get there in an hour or less. You can tell by Denise's smile that it gets her full approval! What impressed me most was how quiet it was. The small stream that runs through has little minnows if you look for them. Plenty of Redwoods and hiking. There's an abandoned airfield back there on one of the hikes.

Avenue of The Giants is a must see for every Californian, but possibly even more important for everyone else. The feeling of peace you get from the quiet majesty of the forest of ancient trees simply cannot be communicated with mere words. The entire forest is pristine. The peace and quiet is almost surreal. I feel like pleading with people to come here. Just come here. Please.

Extremely informative and we enjoyed it very much.  They hit you with so much information it's hard to take it all in so try to allow at least 3 hours for your visit. I especially liked all the stories about how the musicians modified those old guitars to get a particular sound. What a trip. They wrote the book that defined the part that goes 'this is how it's done '.

Trippy and cool place to stop, about 1/8 mile from the road. The tube goes for about 1/3 mile and brings you back to the parking lot. Make sure you bring a flashlight! Flicking a bic lighter is just too dramatic. I didn't see any bats. But very interesting geology and how often do you have a chance to walk through a lava tube? 5 stars.

The best thing for me is they let you bring food in, which can save a lot of money.  Besides the great views, the game is visible from almost everywhere on the Promenade and that in itself is something to do during the game. I always try to make at least one trip around.

It has actually improved since the demise of the stadium,  they have added some landscape enhancements and graded the area around some of the picnic tables to make numbered campsites. Peaceful and quiet here,  always good for an afternoon walk.

It's a great track and the crowds aren't bad. This track runs thoroughbreds just like Del Mar. However the weather is much better! The view from the Turf Club is excellent. We had a bit of luck, and a great afternoon. So will you!

Go for the beauty and swimming more than the snorkeling. It gets packed early but there is another opportunity around 11:30 a.m when the morning people leave. If you've never been it's worth it to go and see.

A great view down the beach! I am disappointed with the vandalism going back decades that has damaged just about everything left except the foundation of the old house. Still worth a look and we will be back.

A lovely piece of historic San Francisco, this grassy field was part of a cow pasture belonging to one of the first settlers during Barbary Coast days and has never had a building on it. Hopefully never will.
We always go to #3 The Wharf, Sabella and LaTorre, for fresh fish and crab. I highly recommend the blackened swordfish and the crab cocktail! They also have one of the best Bloody Marys on the Wharf.
Interesting history of the power station that was here. There's a history of the covered bridge posted also. Nice day use area near the river. Great place to stop on the way to or from Yosemite.
I very much enjoyed the museum and exhibits. The 9 minute movie at the beginning is compelling. The full size replica of Casey's engine 382 helps to put the scale of the crash in perspective.
If you go you HAVE TO jump off the rock at Waimea, there will be a line of people waiting that goes right through the water up to the beach. Lots of fun! Try to do a cannonball!
Great place for whale watching. Lovely view of the beach. And a nice trail that starts right across the street from the Moose lodge. Round trip is a little over a mile.
It's a very well preserved Old West town and the Saloon stays open late.  A lot of things to see including a working blacksmith shop.
Beautiful area, there's a couple of places to pull over and check it out. Good stop for photos! On your way around to Kaneohe.
A great place for a stroll and to see what everyone is using for bait and fishing rigs. Nice to walk along the beach here.
Beautiful scenery and fantastic views are the hallmark of this stop along hwy 101. Also a great hike down to Agate Beach.

The highest natural point in Manhattan. This used to be home to a fire spotting station (a tower) which looked downtown over Manhattan to ring in fires. Unfortunately as that method of emergency service got outdated Mount Morris (the hill in MG Park) was been taken over by drugs, prostitution and gangs.
Today it has been cleaned up substantially. You can see the little league playing, street basketball, the old timers playing chess and concert in the amphitheater, but degenerates still roam free, their stench, discarded alcohol containers and manic voices heard day and night.
Much of the problem is the fact that this park is split by two police precincts, neither willing to overlap their border for the sake of keeping this beautiful park clean.
Visit in the day, bypass in the night.
dislikes: Facilities & Services: Poor maintenance, safety issues

reviews_attraction.text: Just love this place. The building itself is beautiful and well layed out and easy to navigate, it's the art you will get lost in. There's 1000s of beautiful works to gaze at, and many will capture you for longer than you think. You need to visit this place 4 or 5 times to see it all, but by that 4th or 5th time there will be something new, so it's ever-evolving.

The westside river park is a welcome refuge from the city. I love the bike path running all the way down Manhattan. This makes for a great day's ride for those energetic enough to pedal.
The park in midtown gets a little sparse, and the noise and grime from the city is impossible to escape. but overall this is a great feature for Manhattan.

These paths that run in the valley behind Harlem Hill, along the little streams, are some of the the best escapes from New York you can find in Central Park. You're truly in the woods here, the sound of traffic very distant, and the birds and squirrels can be seen properly enjoying the trees.

A treasure that most visitors will pass by. Head long the paths behind the archway, that follow the stream uphill along the series of waterfalls to the west side of the park. An amazing escape from the bustle of New York, and even the bustle of the park. You truly get into the woods here.

Slowly getting restored to its former glory, this is an excellent escape from New York city. The tours are free and entrance is only $5 and its well worth it! The landscaped gardens are gorgeous. The interior has some really interesting artefacts.
likes: Facilities & Services: Affordable entrance, Free tours

reviews_attraction.text: One of the cleanest beaches within a day's drive of Manhattan. Clean sand, clean water, just enough amenities nearby to make it easy. Further east is nudist and LGBT, the west end is more not nudist and a mix or multiple societies and cultures

I've been here 3 times and never paid to go up the tower, but I come here for the beautiful views from the base. It's quiet, nestled in the heart of the city but feels a world away. Relax on the grass beneath the majestic eucalyptus trees.

Wow. Huge. You can really escape New York here, walking among the trees and the forest they have created, touring the glass house, enjoying the sun and the flower displays. Certainly worth the day trip and the money.

I did a crash course in Japanese here and got great results from the course. It's a very difficult language to learn but in only 4 days i was able to form a basic conversation useful for visiting Japan as a tourist.
A spot largely missed by visitors to the park. This archway leads to a path that will take away from the bustle of the city and into the woods. This is a beautiful pathway at all times of the year.
A secret garden in Manhattan. The Garden is lovely and normally empty. You wouldn't expect to find this kind of escape in this neighborhood. The house is run-down and in need of repair.
Beyond stunning. This natural beauty is hard to find and the way that Hawaii protects and nurtures is parks is fantastic. Get here well before the sunrise to get the full experience.
Amazing. The tours are a must. The guides are so knowledgeable and funny. The grounds are amazing and hopefully the woman selling healthy bakery stuff in the courtyard is there.
This is a great NYC attraction that even the locals love. Don't bother getting to the lighting unless you have tix. Drop by any other night, grab a drink and go skating.
One of the best places for a romantic and unforgettable experience in New York. Great food, decent wine list and friendly service, but it's all about the view.
becoming pretty dated in parts but the machinery on display is great, as is the IMAX theatre and the flight simulators. To Space! And Beyond!
Forget the religious symbol. This is a good spot to come just for the view, and also to start the perimeter walking track through the woods.
Open sunny park in the Italian neighborhood. Not as many homeless sprawled around as the other parks. Often part of festivals and events.
Great spot in CP but very popular. Can be too packed with sceney new yorkers sometimes. Get here early if you want to kick the footy
Fairly well maintained public park on the edge of the east river.l The Skate park was decent quality and the running track was good.
Classic NYC mix of history and an ok design of public space, and neglected homeless people, beeping traffic and trash on the street.
Beautiful bush walks. A lot of people just come for the breakneck Ridge climb and miss the relaxing walk to Beacon or Cold Spring
Awesome views out to Catalina islands. Parking is basically street parking only and it can be hard. No public restrooms

A phallic testament to US nationalism!

Best viewed at dawn in winter or spring, if you can brave the cold

Holo Holo Charters was a fantastic experience. I suppose that weather is a big part of the success of each trip, but our weather was fantastic and so was our trip. Captain Drew, Emily & Shankit were great hosts for a trip from Port Allen up to the Na Pali coast. They began by warning us of all the things that could go wrong and I was fearful of getting sea sick, given that I have a weak stomach from motion sickness on planes. However, I never had a moment of sea sickness. Captain Drew made extra effort to keep the boat steady and knifing through the waves. Once we were on the boat, Captain Drew and his boat mates served us drinks and food while describing the beautiful items along the Na Pali coast line. Eventually, we made it up to the coast which had spectacular views. Captain Drew was such a great driver that at one point, he was able to nudge the boat under a waterfall from a cliff and allowed some willing participants to enjoy a 'waterfall dunk'. His precise driving and negotiating the caves and coast line really made for a great trip. On the way back from the Na Pali coast, we enjoyed a very good dinner and sunset. I began my trip worrying about sea sickness, but enjoyed every minute of the trip and the hosts' great service.

I came to the Hall of Fame with high expectations. I enjoyed my visit, but it could have been so much more. They have some interactive video displays, but it was not as good as a simple Google search and some of the audio speakers were broken. The kids loved the pop-a-shot, but one of those was also broken, so there was a line. Grant Hill was running a team drill the day we were there. Shaq's shoe is unbelievable. However, the threshold to make the HoF has diminished significantly (e.g. George Raveling was voted in). They allow you to announce some famous plays and they play back the recording.All in all, there are some great parts, but several parts that are broken. There has to be someone out there to lead the HoF and take more pride in the Hall. It could be so much more.

This place is a beautiful bay full of incredible snorkeling, but half ruined by government incompetence. The parking is a disaster with incompetent attendants who tell you the parking lot is full, when you can see with your own eyes that it is not. I recommend to arrive early before the workers and wind and waves start. Alternatively, arrive after 230, which seems to be the departure time of the inept parking lot attendants. Once you have overcome the parking, the beach is very nice and so is the snorkeling. Try to avoid windy, wavy, turbulent days. We were unlucky and visited on a day where the wind and waves churned up the sand and made it difficult to see anything. This place has potential for a great day, but be selective on the time/day you visit.

I like Pier A park a lot, when it is open. It is a beautiful park on the Hudson River, built on a pier extending from the Hoboken Riverfront. My only gripe with the park are the hours and the upkeep. Oddly, this is the only park in Hoboken that closes. They close the park early and open it late and don't upkeep the slides for the kids. Weird. Every other park in Hoboken is open 24 hours. There is nothing different about this park than the others. The opening and closing of the gate has the feel of the old communist dig-a-hole-in-the-morning and fill-it-in-the-evening jobs program.

Telluride is beautiful. It is a bit like Big Sky in the sense that it is not close to any large cities and a pain to get there, but once you are here, you get to ski a beautiful mountain without many other skiers. The town itself is a quaint old mining town where ramshackle homes have turned into high end art galleries. There are many fancy restaurants as well. The town is very expensive due to its remote location and high end clientele. All in all, I really enjoyed it.

This is my favorite of the Washington DC museums and monuments. The rooms are huge and spacious and as a result, they can fit entire planes, including the original Wright Flyer. They have a whole room devoted to just this plane and the Wright Brothers struggle to get this first plane off the ground. Also, you can see spy planes (U2), rockets, old commercial planes, etc. If you see just one museum or monument in DC, this is the one.

I was a little worried about this being a tourist trap, but it was fantastic and so unique. I have been to Mammoth Cave in Kentucky, which is also amazing. While this is not as big, I think Natural Bridge Caverns is even better. The stalactites and stalagmites here are second to none. The cave descends quite far into the ground and the water is still dripping creating new formations. The place was worth the trip.

The Thomas Edison Museum is pretty amazing in that it has a lot of old tools and projects and work from 100 years ago. There are phonographs and light bulbs and examples of Thomas Edison's work and life all over. I just would have liked it more if there were more demonstrations, although I realize it is difficult to get things to work that are 100-125 years old.

This is the worst Museum/ Memorial/ Monument in DC. The building looks interesting from the outside, but that is the end of the positives. Most of the inside sits empty. This Museum is a waste of time. Clearly, the Indians did not care about it when they set it up. Much of the space is just devoted to selling trinkets and such. Don't waste your time here.

If you love gardens or irises or peonies, this place is amazing. It is an old rich guy's house and property who passed away and willed his property to the local town. They are known for their Irises, which are amazing, but they also have an incredible group of peonies by the front door. Great place to just walk around and take time to "smell the roses".

Stanford University is obviously an incredible place of learning and one of, if not the best university in the world, but their Rodin Sculpture Garden is not worth the visit. The campus is a bit of a let down as well. Spread out and not really a college town like some others. School is fantastic, but the area around it is just a generic open space.

We were on a long drive with kids going down I-77 and looking for a park. This park had good reviews. The park was as pleasant as the photo attached to the description. It was clean, safe and fun. The kids loved the slides, monkey bars, shaky sticks, swings, and walking path. It also had basketball and tennis courts. Just what we needed.

Alta is a Utah ski resort with 15% green circle (all from one lift), 30% blue square, 55% black diamond runs. It only has 5 lifts. Given the number of locals & tourists that visit Alta, this recipe of lots of skiers and only 5 lifts means longer lines. I liked their runs, but the lift lines were annoying. Good, but not great.

The Hudson River Front Walkway is quite pleasant and quite long. You can even go through the Hoboken Train Station and continue on south through Jersey City. It also has beautiful views of Manhattan. On the mainland side of the walkway facing towards Hoboken, there are a variety of restaurants, bars and office buildings.

This reminded me of the Liberty Bell, in the sense that you expect something epic, but it is actually quite small. Nevertheless, I still enjoyed it. The diagrams and stories behind the Alamo were very interesting. Travis' letter asking for help 'Victory or death' is inspiring. Worth the trip, but not an all day event.

The Tabernacle was fantastic. The pianist sat at one end of the arena and dropped a coin. The acoustics were so perfect, you could hear every clank of the coin as it bounced in the opposite end of the arena. Similarly, she ripped a piece of paper and you could hear that as well. Beautiful place to listen to an organ.

I enjoyed the Cave of the Winds. It should be named Cave of the Winds and the falling Water. I loved it because basically you are walking into the edge of the falls. You can avoid getting wet if you wish, but you can also get completely soaked if you wish. Bring a water proof camera.

The Franklin Institute is nice, not great, but the price is a joke. $150 for a family of 5 to walk around. They have a few nice features on the brain and sports, but nothing worth $100, let alone $150. If it were free, I would give it as try.

I am not sure exactly what it was about the World War II Memorial, but I found it quite moving. There is a pond in the center with a jet of water and a statue to each state that gave citizens to the battles of World War II. Well done.

The Old Town Trolley is very dependent on your host. We began with a fantastic host, Gonzo, but then transferred trolleys and had a good, but not great, host. The trolley is a convenient way to get around town at your leisure.
The FDR Memorial is nice because it is not as gaudy as the other DC Memorials. They have different sections for his 4 different terms and even a statue of his dog. I enjoyed it. Out in the open air.
The Boston Public Garden is a pleasant open space in the heart of Boston. The best part is the Make Way for Ducklings tribute in the northeast corner by the pond.
Sinatra Park is a great park in Hoboken for a beautiful view of the city, an occasional concert, or a movie night with other Hobokenites.
Lombard Street is worth the trip because there is nothing else like it, but don't plan on spending more than 10 minutes there.
The Black Sand Beach is appropriately named. It is a bit remote and a nice place to hang out for some time with nature.

Seattle's Chihuahua Garden and Glass is a monument to glass as art and features a large portion of Chihuly's work. The long term exhibition features a Glasshouse,  an Exhibition Hall containing eight galleries and three drawing walls, and a lush garden that serves as the backdrop of glass sculptures made up of impossible shapes and unbelievably brilliant colors. If Seattle's famous overcast skies leave you feeling washed out, then Chihuly Garden and Glass will surely adds a splash of color to your day.

Visiting Bodie is the most authentic way to see the real life setting of the Gold Rush. With the gold mining days a distinct memory with abandoned wooden buildings in a state of decay to photograph and explore. See in the windows of the church, school, barbershop, saloon where bottles, desk and other relics remains.

Be Warned: Leave everything exactly the way you see it. People have been known to experience a string of nightmares after helping themselves to a souvenir.

Very scenic beach with a gorgeous mountainous background. The beach is fairly big. The sand is soft perfect fo walking or to just chill out and lay down. The water was perfect shade of turquoise blue. We went on the last weekend of April and it wasn't crowded at all. Plenty of locals hanging out, surfing, swimming and boogie boarding. The waves was mild, great for swimming even for the kids. Will definitely come here again and highly recommended place to visit.

The bridge was officially named the DuSable Bridge in 2010. It is considered the gateway to Chicago. The bridge is the symbol of the Magnificent Mile. The DuSable Bridge is all at once a beautiful work of public art and a great feat of civil engineering. Like most bridges over the Chicago River, the DuSable Bridge is movable, which allows boats to pass underneath. Its double deck allows two levels of vehicular and pedestrian traffic.

The crossroads of the Los Angeles community. It's more than an urban park with outdoor recreational activities. Exposition Park is a collection of world class museums, educational and sports facilities and entertainment venues. With the landmark Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum and the Los Angeles Football Club Banc of California Stadium on the background.

Old Kona Airport Beach is a nice place to hang out if you just want a quiet escape from the crowds, provided it’s not a weekend when many locals fill the pavilions for picnics and beach parties. Find a picnic table in the shade along one of the wide open stretches of sand, relax on the beach right next to the water, or wade through the tide pools.

Great place to sit and watch the airplanes take off from LAX. So if you are an aviation buff, you will appreciate this place.The beach is big and expansive. You can park your RV and camp out. Plenty of parking. The firepit is a great addition. Electric hookups, bathroom and showers are plentiful and clean.

The Byodo-In Temple is located at the foot of Ko'olau Mountains. It is a smaller scale replica of the Byodo-In Temple in Japan.

The temple is a non practicing Buddhist temple which welcomes people of all faiths to worship, meditate or simply appreciate the beauty of the lushly landscaped grounds.

I'm not a fan of contemporary arts at all, however I can appreciate the artist perspective throught arts. The Museum of Contemporary Art Chicago is worth visiting is a great venue. Wonderful time looking at the Seeing Chicago exhibits. The grand staircase with the webbing was very interesting.

Very spacious venue perfect for a big party and a stage area big enough for a big performances. You have to use their own catering company. Parking gets very tight especially if there are several parties going own but street parking is available and a gravel lot across the street.

Visiting the Grammy Museum was an experience. It's full of amazing collections of Grammy memorabilia. Love the exhibits, interactive displays and the amazing collections of artist performance costumes. A also loved the behind the scene process to put together a successful show.

Malibu Pier is a Southern California icon in an area once called the Riviera America. The historic landmark is located in the heart of California's surf culture. Restaurants offering classic seaside dishes to complement the pier's beautiful coastal location and rich history.

Close to the center of Downtown Seattle. Provides access to green space and water. It is just a quick 20 minute walk or you can take the streetcar ride from downtown. Wonderful place to stroll, get on a boat, or take a moment to just catch your breath.

No visit to Las Vegas is complete until I visit this place at least once during my stay. Every season the theme changes and it is always stunning. The details and the sculptures using flowers is so beautiful and breathtaking. Best of all its is Free!

Great outdoor space. You can jog, run, walk around the park. They have a basketball court, as well as tennis. Also a place for skaters. Big field for baseball, softball and soccer. I come here for the Farmers Market. Plenty of parking.

One of the best Baseball Stadium in the country. The location is picturesque. The stadium is very well laid out. Plenty of bathrooms. Good selection of concessions stands. However, prices are expensive. Parking is very well organized.
likes: Facilities & Services: Well-laid out, Ample bathrooms, Good concessions

reviews_attraction.text: The scenic drive on the Hamakua Coast is a MUST do drive. The road twist and snakes through a lush tropical rain forest lined with streams. Several stops allows for breathtaking views of the ocean coast.
Scenic coastline situated north of Hilo. Breathtaking ocean panoramas, crashing surf and lava rocks surrounded by lush vegetations. Relatively secluded, perfect place to relax and unwind.
When you travel to Waipio Valley today, you not only step into a place steeped in the history and culture of Hawaii, you are entering one of the most beautiful places on earth.
Beautiful and elegant Neo Gothic style architecture. Don't miss and admire the many stone works from all over the world that's embedded in the exterior walls of the building.
A small, sandy beach with locals and visitors. Not a good beach for non experienced swimmers. The waves are pretty strong at times. This is perfect for bogey boarders.
The lake boasts a recreational lake enjoyed by water enthusiasts. Walkers, runners, and bicyclists regularly enjoy the view. It had a large covered picnic shelters.
The collection is outstanding and is very well laid out. A stellar museum with an extensive collection of paintings and exhibits. Definitely worth a visit.
Excellent. Well maintained park with plenty of shades and picnic tables. Great place to hang out with your friends and family for a Beach day.
Perfect for families with small children. Calm water. Clean and very well maintained. Parking lot could get crowded on weekends.

Kaloko-Honokōhau (fish traps) was the exact picturesque beach I had in my mind when we came to Hawaii. We went to every other beach on the island first. The sand was fine and white. The water was shallow, crystal clear, and full of sea life. The potential for instagram pictures was oh-so-very-real but the mile-plus hike over hot, uneven, sun-soaked volcanic rock meant that this beach was not overcrowded at the perfect parts of the day.

There is a small gift shop at the beginning of the trail. Pick up anything and everything you might need here. When they say no services, they really mean NO SERVICES (except for a single, rustic bathroom). Wear good shoes, sunscreen, hats and bring lots of water. The trek across scorching hot black lava rock is brutal, especially when you are tired and sun-worn.

For my fellow tourists feeling misled by the semi-professional turtle photographs of non-specific beaches posted all across the Big Island, they are actually here. Stay at a distance and do not bother them, PLEASE. So many places on the island which are said to have turtles have been overrun by people who are not respecting the wildlife and it is heartbreaking. Even at the Fish Traps, the turtles have gone off to other areas by midday due to the volume of visitors.

There is an amazing hike that stretches along the shore for miles. Bring water. It is longer than you think it is, and there is no clear way to see if it is a shorter hike turning around or going forward. I spent the final 20 minute trek toward the road fantasizing about whether or not I could get an Uber to meet me that far off the pavement.

Consider helping #LocalGuidesCleanTheWorld - bring an extra bag in with you and pack out as much as you can from the shoreline.  #letsguide

The Denver Botanic Gardens was the perfect place to spend a warm afternoon. I enjoyed the exhibits, although I was a bit heartbroken to find that the upstairs of the tropical area was closed off. There were so many beautiful things to see! I went through at the fastest pace I felt I could, and I was there for 3 hours. I will be going back soon!

#oneaccessibility note: The gardens have mobility-impaired options for the majority of attractions, including sight-impaired and hearing-impaired adaptions on many of the more museum-exhibit style areas. Everyone can enjoy the Botanic Gardens.

#letsguide

I loved walking around the steam vents! Some sections of the trail feel more like a suggestion than a formal pathway, but compared to my experiences in other national parks (like Yellowstone) it wasn't difficult to figure out where to go. There were plenty of interesting plaques, and the trail was easy to traverse. I saw lots of families with strollers making their way through here easily. If I brought children with me, I would keep their hand in mine. There are areas where you could clearly fall into things that might not be easy or possible to get back out of.

The wines at Torii Mor were quite delicious. I enjoyed the Japanese theme of the grounds and the tasting room. As our first stop of the day, it was a lovely place to begin our journey through wine country. The desk staff was passionate about their particular wines, and were more than happy to discuss with us the wines in our flight as well as several others. We were lucky enough to be offered a taste of their port, which was sumptuous and rich.

Gallagator Trail is one the easiest stretches of "Main Street to the Mountains." It is usually easy to walk, even during the winter months, and has a few outlets into main roads that lets you access restrooms, shopping centers, parks and more. During dry months, I would even venture to say the train might be wheelchair friendly, especially since the trail has heavy traffic in case of trouble. #oneaccessibility #letsguide #onlyinbozeman #walk

Peets Hill has one of the best views in Bozeman for the brief 5 minute walk it takes to get to the top. Don't miss this place in the fall! (Do make sure to wear good shoes and take the long route down. It is steeper and much more slippery than you think, even when it is dry.) Also, do not come here alone at night - there is virtually no light and it is dangerous.

I really enjoyed my afternoon at this beach! There was pickled mangoes for sale in the parking lot, and lots of locals. The beach is more pebble than sand, and other than right up against the shoreline it is all lava rock. Wear good shoes! There is very little sun protection, and the surf is pretty strong. #letsguide

What an incredible show! I had the time of my life here! I came on my own, but not for a moment was I able to notice it. Everywhere you look something amazing is happening. I would have to go five times to even begin to see what is going on on the various parts of the stage (which encompasses the entire theater!)

Having come here for years to use this building for many years for various reasons, I can only recommend it. There is plenty of local flavor, halls to wander, classrooms and studios to rent or visit, and usually a source or two of delicious food and coffee. #letsguide #art #onlyinbozeman

Kaumana Caves were pretty neat. We wore shoes meant for the activity and brought headlamps (thank goodness), but did not venture very far into the caves. it is a very steep descent down, and unless you are willing to go into very dark spaces you can only step a few feet inside.

My children and I spent a pleasant morning wandering around Dundee. This park was one of the hilights. It is expansive and full of more than few different little play areas. The park itself was clean and open, with plenty of space for social distancing rules to be observed.

While it may seem quiet and unassuming from the outside, this museum if filled to the brim with fantastic exhibits and materials. I can spend the whole afternoon in here as an adult, and my kiddos stay occupied for a long time too! Admission prices are on a donation basis.

My group had SO MUCH FUN at Tunnel Log. We went through once, then circled back around for a second go. We found that we could leave one person in the car and send the rest of our group around the back to stand on top of the log, which made for some amazing photographs!

The petroglyphs were well worth the short walk in. Each area of markings around the island have unique styles and I enjoyed comparing them. They begin to show on the ground before you even reach the boardwalk, so keep your eyes cast down! #letsguide

I often take guests here when they are visiting. The museum is fascinating and fun for all ages. It makes for a great afternoon! My boys especially like pretending to be prisoners in the cells which are still accessible.

What a surprisingly wonderful walk! Devastation trail wound in and around several other attractions, and while there are intermittent closures for safety reasons, it was still an easy and delightful walk.
Parking is a couple of dollars. The walk is short, but the vista is lovely. There were restrooms. We did not find the hike to the falls, but it was a SUPER hot day and we didn't look very hard.
I came here to see the DaVinci exhibit and wound up doing a total run-through of the whole museum afterwards! I loved everything I saw and should have allotted a whole day (or two) to be here!
Common sense required - the boardwalks are fenced for guidance more so than protection. I saw an alligator from less than 3 feet away, with nothing between us as a barrier.
What a lovely place to wander and spend the afternoon! There are so many delightful places to explore, and plenty of shade and shelter to use, depending on the weather.
My group spent the better part of a hour simply wandering around the beach, enjoying the ocean, the pebbles, the wildlife, and the views. It is a lovely little area.
This is a spectacular view, and the perfect end to a meandering drive. It is really breezy, which feels nice after so much heat on the rest of the island.
I used to bring my children here all the time. They always loved their time at this park, and we would bring a picnic lunch to make a day of it.
Beautiful and well kept. Small, but easy to loiter. Good price, especially with the local coupon books you'll find laying around everywhere.
If you are taking the time to come up to Rainbow Falls, set aside a bit more time to explore this little park. It is just lovely.

Best motivation to quit smoking. Tell yourself you can have a cigarette once you get to the top. After climbing those 300 steps on an 88F July day, I was craving oxygen and water way more than any nicotine product. Too be fair, it is a mostly shaded climb, there are rest platforms and benches every 40 steps or so, and a terrifically rewarding view from the top. Platforms look north and south along Kzoo river and there is an abandoned cold war era radar tower perched stop the dune. Be advised if you head back down the dune towards the lake, cell/data service almost completely vanishes and your lucky to get a roaming signal which may prove valuable to call the medivac helicopter when you realize there is no way in heck that you can climb back up that dune to get back to your car. If your an oversized sand-sinking slug like me, be smart and take the paved road back to your car to avoid the inevitable heat stroke. Seriously it was a very pretty and worthwhile climb, just know and respect your physical limitations, and bring water, especially if it's hot out.

Showed up on clam chowder day and they were sold out. We were pretty bummed, but next time we will call ahead because broccoli cheddar is really the best day to go, just get there early.
Seriously though, this is a 5 star hike from the trailhead at Hall's Lake it's under an hour on foot. Once there you can follow a loop around the bowl, or descend 100 feet or so down below. You will feel a temperature drop at the bottom, but besides that not a ton to see. This is actually a geological feature caused by receding glaciers called a kettle. After the soupbowl follow trails to Graves Hill, Hall Lake or Long Lake.

Great site to check out for some cool instagram photos near DT San Diego in Banker's Hill neighbirhood. Part of a a couple really fun walks you can do, google seven bridges walk SD or banker's hill stroll to get maps and routes. Check out the Quince St. bridge a couple of blocks away while your here if you don't have time to do the complete walks. This is a suspension bridge and it does move, can be a little disconcerting when it says, but is completely safe. It traverses a verdant canyon(winter spring) with lots of great photo ops.

Absolutely gorgeous beach and huge dunes. Unfortunately the stairs have seen better days. I doubt they will make it through the next winter as the dunes have already reclaimed significant portions of the steps. The other big issue is parking, there are less than 20 legal spots, and the county sheriffs often patrol and ticket illegally parked vehicles. However if you can time your visit right, you will have one of the prettiest beaches and dune ecosystems in the country to enjoy swimming and sunsets.

Great spot to take pictures and relax to the soothing sounds of the Flat River cascading downstream. Seems like a revered fishing spot as I always see lots of dudes wading beneath the dam with extra long fishing poles, but no one ever seems to catch anything while I'm there, kind of like Pickerel Lake. Gorgeous fall colors and a nice memorial area with flags. Also cool sculptures, landscaping, sitting areas and a gazebo. Neat spot to relax, go fishing or take creative pictures in downtown Rockford.

Terrific example if Frank Lloyd Wright's prarie school design here in Grand Rapids. Free tours on Tuesday, Thursday and Sunday. Fully restored and maintained by a generous gift from Steelcase. The free tour lasts about 90 minutes, including a brief movie. There is another partially FLW associated property just a block east on Logan on the SW corner of College called the Amberg House, that's worth checking out. This is a private residence but there are some nice views from the street.

Stunning state park on the shores of the big lake. Remember to get your state parks pass when you renew you license plate tabs at SOS for only $12, otherwise you'll end up paying $17 with convenience fee to get in. Out of state visitors can pay $9 daily access fee. Incredible trails to Big Sable Lighthouse and Lost Lake. Also there is terrific dark sky star viewing, especially near the lighthouse.

Great spot for sunsets, people watching and getting fresh air. Nice to set up along the north bank of the Macatawa inlet and watch boats go by the big red lighthouse as the golden hour transitions to sunset . You can park less than 100ft. from the waters edge on either the river or lake. Remember to get your state parks pass when you renew your license plates at the SOS and avoid parking tickets.

Beautiful trail, about an hour out and back. Try to hit it close to sunset to get some amazing colors on rock formations. Go up on north side first and follow creak through he fan palm oasis and then cross the foot bridge to return back down trail on south side ridge to see cool rock out c, unusual cactus and wigwams. Great easy 1hr hike. Bring your camera. Tons of Instagram worthy shots.

One of the top 3 parks within 30 minutes of Gran Rapids. Incredibly scenic nature preserve with top notch sunsets, incredible assortment of wildlife, easy to moderate hiking trails and good fishing. Bring your camera, your trail runners, your fishing poles, you binoculars or hammock and enjoy one of West Michigan's natural treasures. FYI...No dogs allowed.

One of the best sunset spots in GR. Sweeping views of the west side, the Grand River valley below. There are a few benches and a nice park to relax in while waiting for the sun to go down. Pick a night with a few clouds in the sky 30-50% cloud cover at a medium height and you will be rewarded with a beautiful array of pinks, purples, reds and oranges.

Pretty cool tram ride to the top of Mt San Jacinto. It rotates the whole ride up which can be a little vertigo inducing far some. If that's the case try to grab one of the bench in the center by where the operator stands as the center does not rotate. Great views from the top, bring a light jacket at it is 20-30°F cooler and windier.

Hard to add to previous reviews, all spot on, but parking can be tough. Park in city lot on Venice Bvld. a few blocks north for $10, walk to the beach, enjoy the boardwalk, go to Hinano Cafe for burgers and beer, walk back through canals to your car, and then hit Abbot Kinney on your way home. Great day in VB.
