Wow, world class sculpture/botanical gardens hiding in West Michigan. Incredible facility with very well orchastrated plantings both indoors and outside. Terrific trail that reveals different sculptures as you round each turn. Also a nice stage set up for outdoor concerts and events. Very impressed.

Four Seasons is an enlightening mosaic by Marc Chagall exhibited in Chase Bank Plaza. Well worth your time to stop by and enjoy. While your at it try to see Picasso's sculpture in Daley Plaza, Miro's Chicago at 69 W. Washington, and Calder's Flamingo in Federal Plaza, all within a few blocks.

Great spot to view the sunset over Mt. Baldhead, see fireworks, or just watch the boats come in. The lighthouse isn't much of a reason to stop, but it makes for some nice backdrop in photos. Parking listed as private so don't stray too far from your vehicle as there are towing signs posted.

Still in awe of these magnificent trees. $10 entrance definitely worth spending time amongst the giant costal redwoods no and other wildlife in the park. Great self guided loop to take for those with limited time, filled with lots of great photo ops. Nice store and visitors center as well.

Best state park in West Michigan. If you don't have license plate pass you can park at Dorr E. Felt Manor/Shore Acres Township Park and use connector trail. Look out for patches of prickly pear cactus that grow wild on dunes by disc golf course, usually bloom in June along with yuccas.

Neat location near downtown Grand Haven wedged between an old cemetery, a upscale residential neighborhood and the lakeshore. Beautiful mature trees including Beech, white pines, and red oaks. Nice parking and access to other nearby trails by hiking extensions. Great asset to the city.

If your the type of person who loves bugs, I'm talking swarms of mayflies and midges, this is the place for you. I likely inhaled several on my walk to the lighthouse. But putting the bugs aside this is a beautiful spot at the end of the peninsula, with several cool photo ops.

Great local park for beginner disc golf players. Just watch out for the goose poop on the holes by the pond. Good walking track around the pond with some cool ducks that you don't usually see. Also historical one room schoolhouse and basketball courts
Nice casino. Rather small compared to Nevada casinos, but there are lots of slots and the table games. Good selection of food options, and everyone who worked there was friendly and accommodating.
Great public art in the plaza. Nice to photograph during the blue hour on a summer evening. Don't miss the Tire Swing sculpture in the corner of the plaza as well.
Amazing hikes with waterfalls, fan palm oasis, split rocks, hummingbirds, and ruins. Great adventures awaiting and a terrific day trip from Palm Springs.
Cool rotating team to the to. Sit in the middle on part that doesn't spin if you get sick. 84° in Palm Springs, 40° and snowy atop the mountain.

We were lucky enough to get a private tour thanks to a GHA/Omni Local Experience and really enjoyed meeting its Director, Patti Clark.The Zoo has the admirable mission of 'not existing at all' since without abused, injured and abandoned animals to rescue, it wouldn't need to be here.

Patti could relay every story of each animal on our tour, and although many of its inhabitants were transfers from closed pet stores and zoos, the majority were exotic pets from owners who never considered what happens when a bear, panther or alligator grows up. This zoo is the final destination for these animals where they get to live out the rest of their days without transfer.

While there are no giraffes, polar bears or theme park rides, there's an enthusiastic and friendly staff caring for several hundred animals that otherwise most likely would have been euthanized. This non-profit is continuously building new enclosures and facilities and hosts daily programs and talks for kids and adults alike, in its effort to house animals from the 40-50 calls they get every month.

Austin Zoo is not a flashy place and doesn't have multi-million dollar enclosures and exhibits. You can see your entrance fee and donations in action, and the focus is on providing the best possible support for rescued animals. I'd strongly recommend visiting - kids will always love a trip to the zoo - but for adults the ethical mission is the real draw.
dislikes: No large, popular animals (e.g., giraffes, polar bears)

reviews_attraction.text: I admire anyone who tries to make wine in Central Texas - the brutal weather here is a huge barrier for producing balanced wines. But Becker does a good job and a number of the wines are surprisingly unique although a little expensive. My major criticism of the $10 tasting is that the pours are very, very small compared with other wineries but then the free glass is probably worth nearly the cost of the tasting. We went during the Lavender Festival and enjoyed the grounds and vendors and had a thoroughly relaxing afternoon. Unfortunately the lady serving the tastings knew really nothing about the wines (and I quote: "I don't care if it's red or white I just look at the alcohol number"). Hopefully this was because of extra staffing at the festival and the usual tasting experience is more informed. Otherwise it's a beautiful stop along 290, very reminiscent of the sort of facilities you would find in Napa or Sonoma.

I'm a big kid at heart so it's hard not to get excited about a visit to Sea World. While this one is tiny compared to the one in Orlando, there is still a small selection of good rides and a wide range of animal attractions. It's a theme park so you can literally feel the money leaving your wallet for every little thing and the food available is nothing too spectacular.

The last time I saw the Shamu show they'd raised the cheesiness level considerably to the point where the entire pool might just turn into cheddar. I was literally crying with laughter at the "Believe" show that's now so incredibly corny I almost videoed the whole thing for later generations to enjoy.

That aside, it's still a great place to spend the day - it's a good mixture of roller coasters and dolphins that should put a smile on your face.

It's expensive for a relatively short ride where most of the gators were no-shows. The wildlife show is really an excuse to tease an alligator and scare the audience with scorpions and a skunk - kids may enjoy this especially since you can hold a small alligator (for $3 more). I didn't like being pressured into a tip after dropping ~$50 on two tickets for the airboat. There's no way it should cost more than $15 per person. The airboat experience is fun but with the water levels so low it's not what it used to be.

It's bad when the best thing about a museum is the cafe (which has a really pleasant outdoor seating area). I've been here twice and there won't be a third time. The first was for the King Tut exhibit which was $35 per person to get a timed ticket to stand in a line to join a herd of people streaming through very few exhibits - it was a total rip off. The last time was a general tour for the museum that generally wasn't very inspiring. If you want to see world class museums, go to New York or Chicago.

It's easy to underestimate the insane amount of work that goes on here to make the displays. I watched one being built over a 5-day period during a conference and was amazed at the number of people, artistry and hard work needed to put it all together. Anytime you visit Vegas, this is a different display with a totally new theme. The conservatory is free to visit and if you get very early in the morning, you can walk around completely alone and avoid the (massive) crowds that come later.

Something of a hidden secret in Napa, Schramsberg provides the kind of winery tour that doesn't really exist in other places that are now swarmed by tourists. You have to make an appointment quite far in advance but it's absolutely worth it. The groups are kept fairly small and it's an extremely informative presentation about the techniques and history of sparkling wine. The caves are fascinating, the wines are excellent and even walking through the gardens adds to the experience.

Make sure you get a coupon online (or from a soda can or a tourism brochure) since they can cut the admission by 50%. There are some excellent coasters here from the traditional old wooden type up to the latest steel inverted tracks. We went on New Year's Day when it was surprisingly quiet and managed to get around the whole park with very few lines. Parking is very easy and overall it once of the best maintained theme parks I've visited in a long time.

Expensive to get into ($15 with the $2 coupon on their site) and not so enjoyable when it's very crowded. The best time to go is early morning when the animals are hungry and haven't been fed by the masses. You can see everything in about 60-90 minutes. There are giraffes, rhinos, camels, zebras, ostriches, buffalo and all the animals outside cages are very tame. The restaurant on site smells pretty dire so I'd recommend bringing your own food.

This provides quite an insight into the history of Texas though would benefit from a little more interactivity. The films were okay. I managed to get in trouble twice for attempting to take a picture and then drinking a soda from their gift store - I guess that's my fault by the staff are like rule-enforcement ninjas. The IMAX is really impressive - I look forward to coming back and seeing a large format film some time.

One of my favorite places to visit in the keys. The staff here care deeply about the dolphins and share their enthusiasm with visitors - it's hard not to feel inspired and in awe of the work done to help the animals here. Aside from the visit, you can also feed and swim with dolphins depending on the package you buy. Overall it's an amazing not-for-profit operation that you'll love if you're a dolphin fan.

If you ever plan to do the picturesque Highway 1 drive from San Francisco to Los Angeles, the Hearst Castle is an essential stop on the way through San Simeon. It's a spectacular building on a beautiful site. There are a range of tours, all of which cover different areas and history of the property. If you have the time, spending most of the day here would be highly recommended.

Excellent for kids though the appeal starts to fall down the curve as the age increases. Some of the exhibits are interesting, some are educational and some look pretty dated. Admission is relatively inexpensive for San Francisco and there's enough here to keep an adult entertained for 1-2 hours. The cafe is bad even by museum cafe standards so get fueled up before you arrive.

A great way to spend a Sunday morning or afternoon - it's $5 per person to visit where you will get to enjoy the waterfalls and swim in the river. The falls are a little light right now due to the lack of rain but it's still a beautiful place to visit. There are facilities here to have a picnic and barbecue too.

Famous for its role in Sideways but you should really come here for the decently-priced wines that stand out from many in the area. The tasting room is spacious and staff are more than happy to tell you everything you ever wanted to know about wine. A great place to stop in the wine country.

It's definitely significantly higher when you're looking down. Although a little pricey, it's a thrilling way to spend a couple of minutes enjoying the view and trying to hold down the booze from the night before. If you're a roller coaster fan, you will have had better - but try it anyway.
dislikes: Less exciting for roller coaster fans

reviews_attraction.text: I had a great time floating down the river! Just tie everything into a bag, attach it to your tube and don't lose your flip flops like I did. After two hours on the water, a one-way shuttle will bring you back to the parking lot. It's hard to find a better way to spend a couple of hours.

It's a slice of Texas history so a must-visit for out of town visitors but it's smaller than you might expect and easy to get through in 20-30 minutes. Apparently one of the common comments from visitors is "Why did they build the Alamo in the middle of a city?". *Sigh*

Spectacular views from the top of Mount Washington with a hair-raising drive to get to the top. Save your brakes and take the guided tour instead to learn more about the fascinating history of the toll road and the area. There is a new hotel opening at the base soon.

Definitely worth seeing if you're driving passed - it's not something you're going to come across very often. If you've never seen a ghost town before, it's quite amazing to an entire functioning town just vanish. Best to visit when the weather isn't too hot.

It's a relatively new ball park, though you wouldn't know it from the cleaning. The game is fun but the parking is horrific ($70 at a local lot), it can get cold in the stands and the vendor pricing is beyond a rip off even for San Francisco prices.

I highly recommend the self-guided tour around one of the area's most extraordinary buildings. Even if there are no concerts on the schedule, the tour provides an insight into the design, structure and day-to-day running of this amazing landmark.

There's nothing really more authentically Austin than Barton Springs Pool and perhaps unsurprisingly it can get very busy. Still, bring a picnic and some sunblock and you'll have a blast. The water is pretty cold so be prepared!
One of the more touristy wineries, the tram is overpriced and the tasting room can get very busy. But if you're a fan of Sterling wines then don't miss the opportunity to go to the source.
An extremely small collection that can be viewed in minutes with nothing really of note. One of the most disappointing museums I've ever visited anywhere.

Great views and architecture. Easy parking and free access around the property.And, it's one of the few things that's free in Beverly hills.
It is located in Beverly hills, is one of the original millionaire mansions.We are free to walk around the buildings, the gardens, and get a beautiful view of Los Angeles, especially good at sunset.

Dozens of movies and TV shows have been shot here, and the Mansion itself is just what you would want a Beverly hills mansion to be. Grand. Old-world elegant, on a lot of land. A must visit attraction in LA

It's located in Malibu just off Pacific Coast Highway #1.  One of the top five most beautiful beaches in all of Southern California, gorgeous sunsets and breathtaking views.The Photogenic rock formations on a nice sandy beach. Very relaxed, great scenery, and not too crowded. Parking is limited and it's a hard hike up after the fun. Definitely worth visiting

It's located in Malibu just off Pacific Coast Highway #1.  One of the top five most beautiful beaches in all of Southern California, gorgeous sunsets and breathtaking views.The Photogenic rock formations on a nice sandy beach. Very relaxed, great scenery, and not too crowded. Parking is limited and it's a hard hike up after the fun. Definitely worth visiting

we have been going to this park since this summer. They have 5 Tennis court, Big other ground and children's playground. They maintain the park so clean. Weekdays evenings are always busy for tennis court. Its First come first serve basis. They have good Trails for walk and Jogging.
Its a public park with no parking or entry fee.

Highly recommended .Located in National Mall. So much to learn, see, and do and it is all free. As it saves time
Car parkings available but it's difficult to drive in traffic. Best to rent bikes/scooter or take a walk to quickly get around. If you like photography visit early morning to shoot/ capture with no people around.

MAGICAL and HEAVENLY feel.
It was busy during the time i visited but it was totally worth.
They have a wonderful trails, lakes and This is the state park where the Michigan's own spring Kitch-iti-kipi is located
There are concession and picnic area located in the park

Key Attractions in Boston. A must vist place. You can enjoy morning and evening walk and people watching.
It consists of  visitor & information centre, pond, avilion, fountain, monuments and gardens, biking. You can find many local artist and talent doing some show.
likes: Variety of features (pond, pavilion, fountain, monuments, gardens)

reviews_attraction.text:
On of top attraction in LA downtown. Since it's a tourist spot it is crowed all the time.  The architectural style is amazing & relates to Chinese culture with a long history
It is located near to walk of Fame
We can see the hand & foot prints of Hollywood Stars.

Love this museum It is very photogenic and even interactive.
The 3D exhibit is also available, as well as the graphic design exhibit. You can spend 2-3 hours over here.
Genaral entry $25, Students& local LA residents gets discount
Street parking available at $3

One of key place when you visit DC .Amazing monument & architecture works. Love every single thing about this and outstanding rich history of makes one learn a lot and meet people from all walks of life.
Free guided tour available ,
Remember Sunday it's closed

It is a one of the key attractions of Louisville. The museum is well maintained and show us all the history about the races and horses Ticket price is $14 per person.They show a 20 mins video with a Tour inside the racecourse area. I spend around 1 hour

A must see attraction in LA with many beach performances, Muscle beach, I would recommend to rent a Bike/scooter as Parking is difficult
It is near from Santa monica, busy area.
Avoid going after 8 pm as i find many people were drunk and dangerous.

One of the main attraction in Detroit. This place is AMAZING and HUGE!
Nice place to bring family and children to learn more about history of Ford.
Some interactive tours available.
You could have easily spent an entire day in just the museum

A good place to checkout when you are visiting Boston. It has a great history about the soldiers who gave their life for the country.
This would be part of stop if you choose a city tour.
There is no charge to look around.

Beautiful area in Hines drive, with a small pond view by right side.
It would be great area to spend quality time for cycling, running, pets allowed. It is a calm and quiet environment.
Free parking available

Great Relaxation place and beautiful environment, calm & quiet
Well maintained and clean area
Best for Hiking and running. No Bike trails available.
No play area for kids
Usually can spend 1-2 hours

The place is beautiful and huge.. Enjoyed taking photos and walking around the columns and good hike
Many nice garden are located in the Arboretum.
Make sure to see the 200 years old tree

One of the key attraction in San Francisco.
Best time to visit is morning before 10 am, where there are less people on road. After that it's over crowded with lots of people/ traffic.
A must see spot in Las Vegas. You can spend time click some great pictures and shots. It's located in between deserts on the way to red Rock grand canyon.
It is a must spot if you visiting Boston. We get to watch entire Boston city from every angle. Ticket price is just $50 ( if students 10% discount)

I did a hiking to the Hollywood sign (found from Airbnb). It took us 2 hours to complete.
Parking is difficult, recommended to arrive early

Nice location, it was just 5 miles away from Google headquaters.
we can spend roughly 30-50 mins.
One of best places to get pictures

It's a key attraction in DC mall. Located by side of lake.
Recommended to take bike/ bus tour which is cheap & saves lot of time.

It's located in Arboretum , a great place to take a hike / drive & capturing great pictures
Entry is free for all.

Awesome views of Las Vegas strip from here.
A good time to go is at night and day and capture great pictures

I wasn't impressed with this museum. I like to wander and get lost in a museum. In this museum, I saw everything in about 20 minutes. They have a few rooms with particular exhibits like Horror movies and pearl jam, the band. In their indie video game exhibit, happy the hand didn't even work and the controller was sick l stuck and you couldn't or the button... They don't have have a permanent collection of popular culture though the ages, which is what I have enjoyed. Then they want to charge you extra for the marvel exhibit... I wasn't happy and I would never come back here.

This park occupies four city blocks. It's a plateau so it has really great views of the Manhattan and New Jersey skylines. There are hand ball courts, soccer fields, basketball fields, volley ball fields, outdoor swimming pool, and even an indoor weight room and ping pong tables!!! There is a fenced doggie park too! And there is an outdoor electric charging station.

It can get crowded and it might be hard to find shade. But it's very diverse and a great place to hang out if you live in the area.

Great 360 degree views, and the slide was so much fun! I actually recommend going first thing when it opens in the morning because there are no lines what-so-ever and you have the whole place to yourself.

Don't be nervous about the slide, it's over in a second. Just go slow and take in the view! Great place to go with friends and take photos together. Worth seeing at least once. If you buy tickets online, you also save a lot of money.

It was a great experience. Lasts one hour, very interactive and funny. Get ready to be in pitch black darkness! The actors are funny but also scary. Then there is a drop at the end which was short but fun. It's scary in a good way, so you can bring kids. Just enjoy the show. I recommend getting tickets online to save $5, you can even purchase them on your phone.

This park is mostly for someone who needs to pass through it because they live farther away from the train station. There are a ton of steps, and there is also a basketball court. I saw some people sliding down on the snow yesterday. It's nothing extraordinary, but at heart going through the park is better than going through traffic and busy city streets.

Very secluded area, you get to pass by lots of boats that are docked at the harbor. It's a bit of a hike, that's for sure. The view is pretty. I don't know know effective the organ is, but it's definitely a cute sculpture. I did take a seat and just listened to the waves of the water. Good place to get away from it all.

I like this park. There are basketball courts, a playground, and wide open green spaces. There is even a cute stream with bridges to walk across. However, when I was here the bathrooms were still under construction. The park is a bit secluded and there are not that many stores around.

This is my favorite bridge in New York. It's like NY's best kept secret. There is a pedestrian party and a bicycle path. It is much less crowded than the Brooklyn Bridge. The only drawback is that the trains pass by so it can get noisy.

It's super expensive - $30, and you have to book a tour with a tour guide who will talk the whole time. I like exploring by myself, not being stuck with a bunch of people in a room listening to a lecture like back in school.

Fun place to visit, and it's free! Make sure to bring some gum so that you can stick it on! It's s very colorful wall, and people do really creative things with their gum! Check it out! And it's on the way to the acquarium!

It's free to go inside. You can only go in the lobby but it's definitely worth it. The architecture is very unique and very nice to look at! It's also close to the theaters on Broadway and to Angels Flight!
I enjoyed looking at all the bikes, and there are over 500 here! If you do visit, make sure to come on a Saturday because that also includes admission to the bicycle museum nearby!
Really awesome museum! The exhibits are amazing and it's free!!! The garden on the ground floor was really something. I love the art frames by Buddha III on the second floor.

The doggie park is fantastic. The dogs and pet owners there are very friendly.

The park does have a lot of steps but the view is really nice, especially at night.
It's a free museum, for goodness sakes! Definitely worth checking out! It's small and cozy, but still bigger than a lot of other small museums - and cheaper too!
It's a nice little museum. You can see Edward Hopper's bedroom (recreated), his high chair where he sat as a baby. Most of the art here is not Edward Hopper's.
Very nice park with a dog run, interesting sculptures, can sit on benches or the grass, and selection of food is available. There is also free Wi-Fi.
It's a very modest museum with a small collection. It's nice that as native new Yorker, you can pay what you wish and visit all three met museums.
Benjamin Franklin was here! During the revolutionary war, September 11, 1776, the king tried to arrange for a truce here at this very building!
It's free! This is the place where Edgar Allen wrote The Raven. It's also close to Silk City if you want somewhere cool to get a bite to eat.
Pretty! Magnificent views and the house is really cute inside. It's definitely worthwhile to come and learn the history behind Alice Austin.
This is a huge and beautiful building but the exhibit is pretty small and limited. However, the saving grace is that it's free.
Great museum with a lot to see. I liked the recreation of old Tokyo, Japan and the art from all around the world was pretty.
It's a nice pier, but if you want a cheap boat ride, take the ferry at the Seattle Ferry Terminal ;-)
It's a bit small, but it is donation based and worth a visit, and it's in a central location too.

Best thing about this place is the boat ride which takes you through the swamp which is living place for alligators. You will go so near to them. There are couple of shows including gators and snakes. You get to touch small gators and snakes. There are lot of alligators all throughout the farm. Do not miss how they jump on the prey during their feeding time.

This is all 3 sea, air and space museum located at one place. This place has real sub marines, aircraft, space shuttles etc. You can also go inside some of these and explore the things inside it. Could be very chilly during winters when you go out to see the aircraft otherwise most of the exhibits are enclosed in big room.

This is one of the most famous temples in USA. It's very big and has ample parking space. Temple has idols of many Hindu Gods. They also perform many pooja's like Satyanarayana Swamy Vratham, Car Pooja etc. There is a food court as well in the temple campus which sells delicious South-Indian snacks.

They have very well maintained aquariums. The animal shows are highlight especially Shark Attack, Dolphin show etc. Will be usually very crowded during weekends. Reach the spot where they will have conducting these shows very much earlier than time to get some good seats with nice viewing.

This is a very large zoo compared to any other zoo in NYC. There are lot of exhibits. You may not able to cover entire zoo in a single day. They have trams to take you to different parts of the park. You will see a lot of varieties of animal species. Food is bit over priced.

This is a museum dedicated to Ripley's believe it or not facts. These facts are represented in the form of artifacts. There is a small motion picture right at the end of the museum. I would recommend not to miss it. This museum is right beside Madame Tussaud Wax Museum.

We wanted to halt somewhere before we reach Niagara falls and trust me we should thank ourselves for choosing this place. It's a great place to spend with family. There are couple of good size waterfalls here. I believe so people halt here before going to Niagara.

If you haven't experienced Gondolas or haven't been to Venice then this is your chance. It's so beautiful and pleasant to ride in the Gondola. The guy or lady who gives you ride sings songs for you, take photographs, tells some jokes etc. It's so entertaining.

Visited this park to see cherry blossoms. Thought instead of going to Washington DC or New York City parks, lets give it a try and I was surprised to see so many trees looking so beautiful with cherry blossoms. The park is maintained very well.

It's a museum and there is a ship as well into which you are allowed to enter. You can see how it is like inside a huge ship and also there are many artifacts inside it related to it's history. Best part of entry is free.

It's a museum of modern art so not every art or painting is easy to understand. If you like modern art then this is the perfect place for you. The artifacts are arranged properly. Photography is allowed but without flash.

This is located away from all the Newport Mansions and is part of Mansions maintained by Preservation Society of Newport. It had lot of topiaries in the shape of various animals. There is a house as well to check for.

It has an amusement park with some good number of rides, beach, lot of food options etc. Will be very crowded during evenings. You can see many people enjoying games like beach volleyball, throw disc etc.

Love the architecture of the building. Although not many but you will find  various good number of regular and modern art pictures here. People go here first for it's architecture. One of a kind building.
This is the place where any Hollywood star would like to have their name printed on one of the stars. You see so many stars on the floor with the names of many famous Hollywood celebrities.
It's a small size animal park with lions, tigers, leopards etc. Best part is the dolphin show. Ticket is bit pricey. It is located inside Mirage Casino. There is a gift shop as well.
Had been here long time back. It's a good size art museum with so many art exhibits at one place. Was initially reluctant to go but after visiting this place, have enjoyed a lot.
Good size park with awesome views of Manhattan Skyline. You get ferries here to reach Statue of Liberty and Ellis Island. Good place to spend some time with family.
Although weather wasn't that good when we went there, it was still amazing experience with the views you get to see here. The monument itself is very well built.
It's a good size science center where kids will learn a lot through science demos. They show some 3D movies as well. Ticket and food prices are pretty high.
Mystic aquarium is good size aquarium. It is famous for Whales, Sea Lions, Penguins etc. Do look for big size whale which is very interactive.
One of the oldest 4D rides which still exists. It's fun for entire family. There could be long wait times as this is a very popular ride.
Had been to one of their tours which covers almost all the bridges in New York City. It was very knowledgeable and pleasant boat ride.
It's a small size zoo located inside central park. Kids would love it. As it is located within huge park, it feels different.
There are lot of trails here for hiking. The mountains provide great scenary. There is a lake to sit and relax.

A good variety of sea animals and some big big sharks. I am really glad i visited Shark Reef because i have always wanted to see sharks. When you see them in person you love them more. Also i had a great experience “petting”  a stingray. Never thought i would do something like that.

You can even camp here via permits online over the weekends. Theres a few nice places to have a picnic with the family. My favorite is down by the lake because the kids can feed the ducks and the fish:) only thing that would be better is more bathrooms closer to the lake area

The Photoshopped beach and sky I've ever seen. Really enjoyed the perfect shade of blue in the sky and water. The fact that it's so close to the hotels (including mine) really made it all the more special. If you've ever wanted to see photoshop in real life, come here.

Started with little fear But when it started I was flying, screaming, posing superman, Happy & there's Audience below you. Fifth floor to single floor height. At the end there's strong jerk, like very strong. But you dont have to worry about it. It was FUN.

Hands down one of the best children's museum I've ever taken my child to. It's under $14 which to me, is a steel when in Boston, NYC they charge upwards of $25 per person. There are so many things to do, your child will be busy all day. Love coming here!

one of the Only place in California where people always go for something great with a lot of expectations, but there is not enough parking. And all one does is to reach closer and take a picture. That’s it. But that is what is a lifetime experience.

A great spot to get a beach front view of Waikiki, and you can sit on the Jeti and watch one of the prettiest sunsets you'll ever see.  We also watched a large sea turtle mulling around near the Jeti popping up for some air every few minutes.

We went as a tour and had a wonderful guide, Bob Snyder who was extremely knowledgeable about all the aircraft's and their history.  This was one of the best tours I have been on and I highly recommend it for anyone visiting Honolulu.

She allowed me to stay super excited which i totally appreciate. Adrenaline is pumping through your body like crazy. It is AWESOME!!!! I recommend going at night because the city lights are beautiful when making that jump.

I arrived in a bad mood but left with a humbling sense of awe and inspiration. Art can change a person and this museum is full of priceless wonders from nearly every corner of the world. I now visit every chance I get.

If you have half a day open I would recommend it. They do have regular feeding times posted for some of their animals and had someone there to tell us about the animals and answer questions while they were being fed.

We  stopped in and got the chicken sandwich, delicious! Their fries were as good as I remember as a child, but after I left I realized I had forgotten the pastrami! "Don't forget the pastrami!" It's the best.

Enjoyed watching and feeding the sea turtles. It was a nice touch putting a play area for the kids.  Dolphins were amazing as well as the sea lions.  We didn’t try the restaurant, but it sure looked busy.

If you're driving by but don't have time to spend the whole day, at least take the Avenue of the Giants. It runs parallel to 101 for about 30 miles and has an auto tour pamphlet available at either end.
The workers were very nice and full of energy. They recorded our whole ride and it was very funny to watch. If you look on Groupon they have deals for 2 pictures and a go pro it was only 50 dollars.
but it's pretty dirty and it's very rocky right when you start walking into the water. It is a nice beach to lay out and tan on though, that's usually what I end up doing if I go to the beach.
one of the most beautiful parks I've ever been through. I couldn't look away from anything in the forest, or the incredible coastal vistas. You're dazzled rounding every single corner.
This is an awesome park. We didn't have that much time unfortunately but we still had an incredible experience  hiking. We even saw some horned animals which was the cherry on top.
Nice place...parking is  small. You can walk through it in 45 min. Awesome place for partys and private functions. Awesome summer time Hawaiian music concert series.
learned about the connection between plants and humans.  This place is free but I gladly made a suggested donation to keep the garden and research ongoing.
very professional overall good experience you get what you pay for and workers make it fun from the bus ride there all the way to the last zip line !
My kid loved seing peacocks and ducks. Lots of trees and grass around. And the are few places for groups to have a picnic with a barbecue.
Always looking for something different to do. This fit the ticket. Really enjoyed it. Tiny was our instructor and he did a great job.
View of the water Hooters and the Tennessee bar have a great happy hour. The taco stand has good food. Parking is validated.
The ponds are lovely and pathway is clean.  They could clean the filters of the trees debris a little more!

I really enjoyed the New York Historical Society Museum.  All of the exhibits were great and very interesting.  I especially liked the Tiffany lamp exhibit, the Asia Society Museum collaboration exhibit and the Oval Office exhibit.  My favorite, though, was the Bill Graham exhibit.  The music, provided by a device that the Museum provided was just great.  It triggered songs as I proceeded thru the exhibit.  The artwork (concert posters) and photos were awesome.  Bill Graham was such a prolific concert promoter.  The exhibit really details this and his great impact on the music world.

This was a very interesting museum.  The exhibits were very diverse.  They're are exhibits on early wireless communication, early radio & TV, electronic warfare and jamming, early computers & PCs and a huge collection of Jeeps and other WW2 vehicles. There are also a lot dioramas and models ranging from WW1, WW2 & 9-11.  There were many docents/tour guides on hand that provided a lot of interesting information about all of the history and artifacts.

I really enjoyed Kittatinny Valley State Park.  This was my second visit to the park.  I took my kayak out on Lake Aeroflex during this trip.  The views were pretty scenic with the spring foliage around the shoreline.  The planes taking off from the airport were interesting, as well.  After the lake, I went on some of the walking trails including the Shale Trail.  They were very good.  I especially liked the Ruin off of the Twin Lakes Trail.

I really enjoyed the museum.  A docent gave me a tour of the exhibits in the lobby area which was very interesting.  I also enjoyed the special exhibit "Machines of Interest".  The permanent collection was great.  There were a lot of interesting machines, artifacts and films to see.  The signage throughout the museum was very informative.

This is a great museum.  I especially liked the Seeing America exhibit.  The Native Artists and Ancient Mediterranean exhibits were also interesting.  I also enjoyed the Arts of Global Africa collection.  Finally, the Ballantine house and the exhibits on display there, especially the "Sterling" silver exhibit were great, as well.

I really enjoyed the museum.  The Countryside exhibit was very interesting especially the top floor with the robots.  I also enjoyed the Brancusi exhibit and the Abstract Expressionism related exhibits.  The Thannhauser Collection was also great.  This was my third time at the museum.  The building is a work of art in itself🙂

Those was a great park.  The views of San Diego from the Visitor Center are spectacular.  I'll never forget them.  The exhibits in the Visitor Center were also very informative and interesting.  The Old Point Loma Lighthouse, Cabrillo Statue and Kelp Forest & Whale Overlook were also interesting.

This is a great museum.  The exhibits were excellent and interesting.  They detail the history of submarines and the crucial role they played in our military history.  The self-guided tour of the Nautilus was also great.  The audio device that was provided worked well and was very interesting

This is a great museum.  It's provides an interesting and clear overview of all the events of the Revolutionary War.  There are many interesting artifacts on display including Washington's tent.  I also liked the films that examine key points during the war.

This is a great museum.  I enjoyed the Natural History (Dinosaurs) and Bird Gallery.  The artwork on the 2nd Floor was also good.  I liked how the artifacts and artwork were arranged.  The special exhibit, Lock and Key, Home was also great

I enjoyed Harkness Memorial State Park.  The grounds and buildings were interesting.  The mansion wasn't open due to the Coronavirus.  However, it was nice to walk around the site.  The views of Long Island Sound were great.

I enjoyed Wave Hill. The grounds are very scenic.  Many of the trees and plants have name signs which were helpful to identify them.  I also liked the Woodland trails, the Gift Shop and the views of the Hudson and Palisades.

I really enjoyed the museum.  The illustrations by Howard Pyle and others were interesting.  I also enjoyed the Pre-Raphaelite gallery.  The Layered Abstraction exhibit and the Julio daCunha exhibit were great, as well.
This is a great place to visit.  The ship and the museum exhibits are very interesting.  The planes on the flight deck are very diverse.  There are also great views of Manhattan from the flight deck
This is a great museum.  I particularly liked the exhibit from the Palace of Governors Museum in Santa Fe.  The artwork in their standard collection was also interesting, as well
This was a great casino.  All of the slot machines were new and up to date.  I ate dinner at the Taqueria.  It's was very good and the personnel were very friendly and efficient
I enjoyed Evansburg State Park.  I was only there for an hour and walked along the Skippack Creek Trail.  It was scenic and I liked the interpretive signs along the way.
This was a very interesting zoo.  I enjoyed the Amur Leopard exhibit and all of the indoor exhibits.  The rattlesnake collection was very extensive and impressive.
This is a great museum.  Numerous historical trains are on exhibit with many from the old PA RR.  The exhibits and signs were also interesting and informative
I really enjoyed the Botanic Garden.  There were many different environments to explore.  I especially liked the Sasebo garden and the Koi pond and waterfall!
This is an interesting site.  The signs leading to the tower provided a lot of interesting background information about the tower and Fort Miles in Delaware.
I enjoyed the self-guided tour.  The accompanying audio device was very good, as well.  There are docents around the ship who are available for questions.
This was an interesting park with great views of the Delaware River and Phila.  There were a lot of interesting plants and trees in the park, and well
This was an interesting historical site.  The buildings weren't open due to the Coronavirus but the interpretive signs were good and descriptive.
I liked Hoffman Park.  It was scenic and peaceful.  I walked along Darby Creek.  From there I rode my bike throughout Lansdowne and the area.

It is easy to spend an entire day at this museum and leave feeling as though you've only seen a fraction of what it has to offer - and that's probably the case. Absolutely massive selection of high-quality exhibits; some modern and high-tech, some fascinating simply because they're so dated. The price of entry is relatively steep, but the quality is well worth it.

Gas Works Park is an appropriately beautiful, hipster-y place to spend a lazy afternoon in Seattle. Lots of room, a fantastic view of the city, and the gas works themselves add a very cool vibe to the whole place. A little out of the way, but you wouldn't get the skyline view without that.

The Olympic Sculpture Park is a great place to wander around and have a quiet stroll. Convenient to downtown, usually not too crowded, and an easy walk to Pike Place. Good views all around and benches throughout the park. The art is nothing to write home about, but still very nice.

The Ca' d'Zan is a gorgeous place to visit, and a highlight of the shockingly wonderful Ringling Museum. The exterior architecture is beautiful, and the views of the bay -- especially at sunset -- simply can't be beat. The tour is unnecessary, but definitely visit the building.

This is a nice, small little visitor center for Cuyahoga Valley National Park. Stamps are available here, as well as pins and patches. The store section is small, but there's some nice porch seating and very friendly staff and park rangers. A good stop to take a breather.

Nat Geo loses a star here because the quality of this museum -- which has priced admission -- is SO dependent on the frequently-rotating exhibits. I've seen some of the best exhibits I've ever seen in this building; I've also seen some of the worst. Check before going.

The FDR Memorial is surprisingly extensive, and makes for a lovely walk along the water. As always, the memorial is better, in my opinion, when lit up at night. Very close to the Martin Luther King, Jr. Memorial, so make sure you stop by that one on the way as well.

One of my favorite national park visitor centers so far. Very helpful park rangers, lots of good material, and centrally located. Spacious, clean bathrooms. Very good gift shop with pins, patches, and the visitor stamp. Great place to begin your Glacier adventure!

The Ringling rose garden is a labor of love and really is a sight to behold. Dozens of varieties of rose, meticulously maintained, in open air for people to wander around, smell, and just generally enjoy. Centrally located on the gorgeous Ringling Museum grounds.

All politics aside, the U.S. Capitol is an amazing piece of architecture and a great place to visit. Gorgeous rotunda and halls, although my personal favorite parts are the underground tunnels to the office buildings. Email your representative and ask for a tour!

The Smithsonian American Art Museum is the other half of my favorite museum in DC. Some amazing pieces of less-traditional art from American artists, a great layout to the museum, and the courtyard is the best spot to relax in the city. Absolutely worth a visit.

The Village Green in Bar Harbor is a lovely area right in the center of town. It has a great gazebo, easy access to tons of nearby shops and restaurants, beautiful foliage in the fall, and usually isn't too crowded, even during peak seasons. Great spot to relax!

Lake of the Isles Park is a gorgeous park to wander around or walk a dog. It's not quite as multi-featured as Bde Maka Ska or Lake Harriet -- not fantastic for cycling, no bandshell, etc. -- but it's wonderful for what it is: great views and a nice walk.

The Washington Monument is still an impressive sight to behold, even when you've lived in DC for a while. The scale doesn't really register until you get right up next to it -- the thing is absolutely massive! Well worth a visit, especially for tourists.

The Cal Neva is a good addition to Reno's lineup of old-school, no-modern-frills casinos. There's some really good, cheap food inside, as well as a wide selection of slot machines. Near a bunch of the other casinos, so a convenient place to visit.

One of the best rides I've ever been on -- thrilling, just the right amount of scary, decently long, beautifully-designed. Also has one of the best ride queues in the world -- walking through Hogwarts itself! Absolute can't-miss among theme parks.

The Smithsonian Castle is well worth a visit, especially for a newcomer to the National Mall. An eclectic series of small exhibits and history of the Smithsonian itself, as well as a (relatively new!) interactive map of the Mall that's very neat.

The Buckingham Fountain is a nice leisurely stop for tourists or locals on a walk. The fountain performance is fun, and doesn't happen so often that it's too annoying. The park is nice with plenty of seating, and it's very centrally located.

The Cinderella Castle is the central landmark of the Magic Kingdom. Great to wander around or just walk through, and a fantastic piece of scenery for the regular fireworks. Also has several great family photo locations scattered around.

Good roller coaster for kids. Lots of nice Harry Potter theming, cute design on the ride. The ride itself is a bit bumpy, pretty short, not too many exciting bits for adults. Check it out if there's no line or if you brought your kids!

Had the good fortune of joining a cruise run by LeBarge Tropical Cruises. The boat was very clean, the captain was friendly, and everything about the experience was generally enjoyable. Thanks for a good time!
This is an absolutely lovely place to walk around, especially after a long day at the Museum of Science and Industry. Great places for picnics, lounging, sunset-watching, and general happiness.
An amazingly good museum. Beautiful architecture, incredible selection, great exhibits, extremely convenient access to everything around it. One of the best in the country.
The Japan Pavilion is beautifully-designed, with some good food and good shopping. One of my favorites among the pavilions at Epcot.
This is a small museum, but a beautiful collection. Lovely stop for a short visit, especially if you're a Duke student.

Absolutely stunning Observatory with beautiful architecture and breathtaking views of L.A day or night. Parking is free and there is a shuttle that will take you right up to the Observatory, however you can do as we did and take a nice stroll to the top and enjoy the twists and turns of the mountain. The deco style building is stunning and can outshine the views of L.A and the Hollywood sign, inside are a ton of exhibits that are interesting for the whole family. There is a cafe and gift shop, I high recommend checking this out... its one of the few times I wished I had bought a souvenir and didn’t.  Take your time and enjoy the history of the Observatory you’ll be glad you did!

Absolutely stunning Manor, easy location to find with plenty of parking. Tours start on the half hour, but in the meantime you are able to walk the gardens and check out the self guided exhibit. The Manor inside is beautiful and full of interesting artifacts from America, England, Russia, Germany etc. Tour lasted around an hour but it’s great info. for the price. Photos are not allowed inside but you are free to take photos all around the outside of the Manor. Our tour guide was so sweet and had so much useful information, she is a Historian and was able to answer all questions thrown her way. Child friendly and If we ever come back to Richmond we will definitely stop by again!

Absolutely great place to come and check out art from some local artists. Two stories filled with different mediums of art, friendly staff aimed to help you make a purchase or just give you information about the pieces your looking at. Also on of the best perks of coming in is the diner located to your right, they have hot dogs, sandwiches, burgers etc. and some of the tastiest deserts for an affordable price. Located right in the heart of AVL, it’s a definitely must do when you visit.

TCL Chinese Theatre is a historic landmark located right on Hollywood Boulevard in Hollywood, CA. The architecture outside the theater itself is stunning, the many features inside were "one of the first" including AC, and is also one of the largest IMAX screens in North America. Wether your going to see a movie or a landmark its definitely worth a trip, keep in mind the popularity of the theatre and the Hollywood Walk of Fame because it can be busy at times.

Beautiful visiting center located right off the Blue Ridge Parkway, friendly staff and rangers with a large assortment of souvenirs. Clean restrooms and water fountains, plenty of space to stretch your legs.   I was allowed to bring my dog into the visitor center (I asked first) so that was a huge plus, I also noticed they have State/National passport books for only $10 compared to $25 on Amazon. Overall it should be a definite stop just for the views alone.

Small state park with a lot of character, the visitor center is small, more like an office, but the staff is polite and helpful about the area. We took the boardwalk trail and saw a nice view of the lake. Further in we came across the plantation, although closed on our day we were able to walk around the grounds. There were a handful of plaques and information about the property and owners of, it would be nice to go back and observe inside the homes.

Beautiful home full of history and intrigue, great stop during our visit to Columbus. The staff was polite and helpful, and gave us a quick layout of the house, we chose the self-guided tour with audio guide. I highly recomend the audio guide for two reasons, without it, it is highly possible to breeze through the house because it isnt that large. And second, it gives a large amount of information about each room, and the artifacts inside.

Chimney rock is one of the most unique state parks in North Carolina. The work that has been done to accommodate foot traffic is amazing, the summit to the top is no joke, but the area is clean and well maintained. I highly suggest visiting the park when the weather is nice, if your going during a rainy or foggy time there won’t be much to see as far as views go. Plus with the steep prices for admission, you want to plan accordingly.

Very interesting state park, the Fort is preserved and restored in an impressive manner. The visitor center was full of exhibits, gift shops, and information rooms with videos too. Animals are not allowed inside the visitor center or within the Fort walls, be aware and possible bring someone with you. The Fort is full of history and information, the staff is ready and available with any questions you might have.

Medic Mountain was large state park with beautiful trails for all hiking styles. The visitor center was clean and spacious, different exhibits throughout, the staff was also extremely nice, showing our son the different telescopes and stuffed animals. We did a short 2 mile hike, the foliage was beautiful and it was pretty tame. Great spot for a picnic, or to lounge out on the grass.

Beautiful lake and nice area, the lake looks amazing in the morning. We decided to take the full loop around the trails but unfortunalty due to the hurricane it was near impossible. We were recommended by the park ranger  that it could possibly be flooded out. We took our chances and were compltely drenched in mud by the end of it. Overall really great park with amazing views.

Great place to take the family, there are a lot of trails spanning from beginner to the more advanced (biking and walking). There are locations for picnicking and camping, as well as plenty of parking. The scenic waterfalls and rivers are a great place for tubing... if you forgot to bring one there are plenty of places to rent one for cheap.

Really interesting historic lighthouse, learning about its past and the fact that the lighthouse was moved almost a mile away is insane. Staff was friendly and helpful, the campus itself is stunning and spacious with shops and smaller exhibits. Come and see one of the largest lighthouses in the U.S while having fun with the whole family.

Great place to relax and enjoy nature, we came here to kill some time before the Kelton House opened. I highly recommend stopping by, they were maintinaing the grounds and we were able to see the hard work that is put into Topiary Park. There are restrooms and a small gift shop, we were able to find free parking nearby.

Crowders Mountain is a nice well maintained Park with many areas to start. Trails are wide and well maintained, the visitor center was exceptionally clean with plenty of exhibits for education. My only downside would be it took us 15-20 min. to find a parking spot, we went to two parking lots and it was slammed full.

The trail is a fairly easy, family friend path... it’s only a .75 mile hike till you reach the falls. The elevation does change consistently, there are man made steps and bridges. Parking can be scarce so be aware that you may have to wait or park further, there is an information plaque at the beginning of the trail.

Nice quite state park, we came around 9:30am and probably ran into no more than three people. The visitor center was nice and well kept, the staff was friendly and helpful. Once on the trail it was cool and easy, we walked around 2 1/2 miles, the trails are wide and some are sandy. I would highly recommend!

Great state park with beautiful trails to explore, we took the wooden plank trail and it was a fun and relaxing walk. The draw bridge is pretty cool to trek across, it’s interesting to see boats go by. The visitor center is clean and tidy, cool exhibits for the kids as well, would definitely recommend.

Great place to stop and take a breather, with camping, hiking, and swimming, it’s a well rounded park. The staff was polite and the visitor center was spacious and tidy, the exhibits were up to date as well. Spacious grounds with covered picnic tables, nice place to stop and have your lunch too.

Really cool place to spend a few hours and bring the family. I was pleasantly surprised of the vast dunes and sand that covered the park, the view from the top isn’t to much... but for me the best spot is at the base. I would love to come back and try to hanglide.

Well maintained state park, staff was friendly and helpful when accessing park stamps 5 min. before closing. The trails were well covered by trees maintains a cool l, breezy experience. Most of the trails are wide and mild, three miles in didn’t feel too harsh.

Nice park to visit and relax, we took a 10 min. walk by the river and it is truly one of the more peaceful spots in Columbus. There are alot of plaques and iron made statues, you can also walk close to one of the train bridges and rent bikes for cheap.

Great state park to relax and take a walk, the visitor center was very clean and the staff was helpful. They had a nice exhibit for the kids, there are a few trails that are mild and enjoyable... parking can be a bit scarce on the weekends.

Beautiful spacious park filled with large areas and walking trails. Very close to Eno River, we didn’t see a visitor center for Occoneechee, but we were able to receive our park stamp at Eno River for our passport.
One of the best parks in Asheville, trails are easy to navigate and the Disc Golf course is unique. Great for solo/family hikes!

Wonderful area with pristine beaches and picnic areas. Would definitely recommend to anybody who wants to visit a nice natural area with good scenery. It can get a little sketchy towards the evening but otherwise is a pretty safe spot. This is also the best place to walk too goat island. If you visit please be mindful of wildlife, especially any nesting seabirds you might come across. Only go swimming here if you are an experienced swimmer. Swells can come in suddenly and unexpected, especially during the winter.

Ho'omaluhia is a very special place. Definitely worth seeing. There are a lot of various plants that are interesting to see. The lake is gorgeous and very picturesque. There are so many Koi fish swimming in the lake, it looks like there are large orange spots from far away. The tall surrounding Ko'olau mountains make it complete. Definitely stop by for a visit and be sure to leave everything as clean as you found it.

Dam seems like it would be a lot better with a decent amount of water. We were there in late may and there was little more than a puddle. The hike there was amazing, but the dam it's self was underwhelming. There was trash floating in what water there was. People really need to learn to clean up after themselves. It amazes me that even in national parks some people lack the decency to pick up their own trash.

Joshua Tree National Park is a surreal experience. We visited during the early summer before it was too hot. There are so many places to camp and hike. There is something here for everybody. All that being said, there are not any good placed in the park to get water so be sure to bring a lot of water with you. As always, be sure to pick up after yourself so that this natural wonder can stay so pristine.

The drive and destination were both fantastic. Be sure to give yourself at least a few extra hours to check out all of the little pull-offs and stops. Lots of scenery. At the end of the road there are toilets but there is no running water so be sure to bring a water bottle. As always be sure to clean up any trash that you see so that the park can stay clean.

Trail is a nice short walk that can be taken from either a parking lot off the main road, or from the nearby campground. Arch rock itself is pretty great, however the trail there is pretty great and just as good as the destination. No toilets at the main parking lot, however the nearby campground does have a pit toilet. Be sure to bring extra water!

The views here are simply stunning. Dead Horse point is certainly worth a stop for anybody visiting Canyonlands' Island In The Sky district. The Dead Horse Point visitors center has a great gift shop. Staff are very friendly and helpful. There is running water both at the point and at the visitors center. There are flushing toilets as well.

The visitors center has a lot of good info about the park. There are displays and interactive activities that help educate people about things like light pollution and fault lines. The film is really educational about the park. The visitors center is definitely a place worth visiting for anybody going to Bryce Canyon.

The trail was amazing with great views of rock formations. The trail had lots of wildflowers and different varieties of cactus when we visited. The dam it's self was less than spectacular and was practically empty. People really need to pick up after themselves. Parking was convenient and the trail was not too busy.

This is a must do. I have been twice and there is still so much I haven't done. Chain of craters road is amazing as is the Kiluea iki trail. There are good camping options and the park rangers are very helpful. Even with the Jagger museum and crater rim drive closed there is so much to do.

This garden is beautiful and enjoyable for everyone. Free entry and very well kept. The paths are ADA accessible and very well kept. There are great places to sit down and enjoy  plenty of exotic plants. The Garden is located next to a city park that is a great place to go as well.

Truly an amazing place. The rangers are kind and helpful, there is a nice viewpoint right across from the visitors center. Great little displays about the park and it's history. This visitor center isn't quite as fancy and grand as Zion or Bryce, but it's well worth your time.

Hau'ula loop is an amazing trail. This trail is easy enough for the whole family. Parking can be difficult so plan ahead. Bring water and try not to hike right after rain because the trail gets quite muddy. Be sure not to leave any trash behind an keep our island clean!

Definitely the best place in the park. Spectacular views of the canyon. There is a large overlook that is great for pictures. Parking lot is large, however it can fill up on bust days. The free shuttle is a great way to get there and not have to worry about parking.

It's a good park, it's just way too busy during the summer. There are definitely better placed up the canyon to spend a sunny afternoon. The park is well kept and is very accessible. The Provo Parkway River Trail is a fun thing to do when things aren't too busy.

Beautiful structure and grounds. Definitely a must-see for anybody visiting Salt Lake City. Check to ensure that it is open to the public when you visit as hours vary. Plenty of great exhibits on the lower level. Street parking is easy and convenient.

What a view! We never intended to stop here but we had to because it is simply amazing. The landscape stretches on for miles. Bring a good camera and be sure to park fully off the road to avoid any accidents. It's hot so bring water for the road.

Beautiful state park with great trails and stunning views. The lookout is breathtaking and it's typically not too busy. Be kind to the land and pick up any litter you see. Stay on marked trails and don't leave rubbish behind.

Decent well-kept beach park conveniently located right off the Highway. Good snorkeling and coastal views. As expected the beach park restroom has no soap and is poorly kept, this is the case with all Oahu beach parks.
A great place to go and see the birds but the trail there has been ruined by so many off-road vehicles. That should close it to all motor vehicles.
Great park in a great community. Playground is covered to protect from the sun. Large open fields for various types of sports are well maintained.
Beautiful view, definitely the best in this region of the park. Not very busy when we went. Parking lot well maintained, great trails in the area.
Great views. On a clear day you can see Molokai and Maui. Paved trail all the way too the top. Arrive early to find parking.
An amazing experience. From the summit your can often see the other islands. It's a long drive up but 100% worth it.
A great place for a scenic walk. Bring a water bottle though, none of the facilities have working running water.

Beautiful city gardens.  The light over xmas was amazing. Saw the exhibit of fuschia. Very lovely indoor show and the trails are very well kept. Visit March 2019 during Dahlia tuber sales. Lots of spring flowers daffodils,  daphne,  iris etc. Tried Kettle coffee bar inside. Very nice view of the garden. Visit in June 2019, a pleasant docent tour and very interesting walk with experienced guide.

Beautiful trails and nice view at several places.  Discover pass required for parking.  Lots of interesting plants and vegetation.  Perfect for a short day hike or a trail run..
Most recent visit: may 2018. Beautiful weather and very sunny. Hat and sun screens recommended. Reasonably easy hike for most people and dogs.

Was here for East Lake Sammamish Half Marathon.  Very scenic as the finishing line of the race! Quiet and serene on Sunday morning. Friendly staff.
June 2018 visits: a cool morning jogging started here. Very pleasant to circle around and run along east lake Sammamish trail.

A giant ferry wheel that offers grand view of the sound and the high rises depending on which bench you choose to sit. A fun 10 minutes ride or 3 rounds to be precise. Print the vouchers if you purchase online. The online purchase enables skip the line feature.

Arrived here unfortunately on a rainy day. Very misty. It is very family friendly. Restrooms reasonably clean, better than the one cross the street at Cedar Falls trail head. Picnic tables around. Display your discover pass.

Was a part of my running route a bit small but beautiful. Look for street parking. There is a public BBQ grill and several tables and benches.  Bring your own picnic blanket! Open view of Puget Sound across the street!

A cool bridge that connects Mercer island and Seattle. Very popular among bikers time ride i90 trail. Not as pleasant to cross for the runners but very doable distance and a great way to explore Seattle from Bellevue.

Very friendly park with lots of parking space and it's got a soccer field and a play ground. There's Robinswood house for special occasions. Looks very interesting! It's a part of my lake to Lake trail running route.

A very large park with plenty of parking space, including a dog run.  This location is where many sports events occur and is the starting/finishing line of many Half Marathon races. Bathrooms are clean.

A fun place for families and school field trips. We attended several birthday parties here. Very interesting. Parking can be a challenge, budget some time for looking around. The lot at times is full.
A hidden gem to many tourists. It's got a nice trail for a good two hours of walk. Most recent visit in April 2019. Serene and peaceful during weekday with joggers and walkers. Clean bathroom.
Very educational.  My 5 years old nephew really liked the visit.  He enjoyed looking at the T-Rex skeleton, the fossils.  I like the gem and mineral collection.  It was a very pleasant visit
Beautiful and scenic.  Suitable for a 5 miles or 5K loops.  Many hills and stairways for cardio training.  Very fun for a 2-hour walk too.  Be sure to take a picture of the light house!
A pleasant park to walk and enjoy the waterfront. It's the beginning part of Mercer Island half marathon route.  Very scenic. A few picnic benches, public restrooms and playground.
A wonderful place to enjoy seeing variety of plants and flowers.  Lots of parking and convenient bathrooms. There are trails nearby for walking and jogging. Excellent place!
Beautiful park.  Very large with eclectic collection of plants, a Japanese garden, lots of trails to explore.  Very beautiful during the cherry blossom season.
Very scenic for a walk or run on a cool day. Playground for children as well. Ran here in October 2018. Chilly foggy and scenic run  along lake Washington Blvd
Always a fun visit.  Some part of it reminds me of Stanley Park of Vancouver. Beautiful view of ferry and Puget Sound. Very family friendly and a public pool.
The park is where many half marathon races took place. Very popular among hikers, runners,  and cyclists. Advise having a discover pass for ease of parking.
A relaxing community park with playing fields for local residents. Parking available or street parking.  Bring your own picnic blanket on a sunny day!
Beautiful neighborhood park with summer concerts, BBQ areas,  a lake for boating and swimming with life guards. Trout fishing requires license.
Tucked behind Lake Hills green belt park. Very pretty and serene when I ran by it. Very friendly staffs and clean bathrooms. Bravo
A tunnel over the trail. According to Wikipedia it was a former harbor defense. Was called Lake Merced military reservation.
Great park for running and walking.  Scenic  view of lake union. It's the location of the seattle 10k race finishing line.
A fun place to run and walk.  The lights are pretty and creative. The line to get into the garden can be long

Why are you reading the reviews, get in your bike, car, or bus and head right over. You get a wonderful view of San Francisco and miles and miles of rolling mountains. It’s a wonderful place to bike to, a quick escape from the city. I saw wild deer once. Also check out the black sand beach.

I often stop by this pace before I bike over to Palo Alto. It’s has a small hill that over looking Palo Alto area across the bay. The area is well maintained even during the government shut down. You get a nice 360 view of the surrounding cities and the bay. There are parkings too.

This is an iconic location for LA, beautiful beach, always lots of people, beautiful sunset. The transportation isn’t that bad, you can take the light rail to the city pretty easily. They have lots of small and big shops near by for pretty much any shopping needs.

The architecture is unique and really works with the surrounding nature. Great art collections, new and the old. You don't need to check your bags in, just carry it below your waist. There is a restaurant, with pretty good selection of food, and out door seating.

The caves were amazing and nicely done. They did everything they can to prevent slippage. The temperature in the cave could get pretty warm so no jacket require. Everything is well lit and beautiful. The entrance fee is a little much, so is the gift shop.

Yosemite Falls is very different depending on when you go, it will look different all year round. It's very easy to get to from the visitor center and there is also a bus shuttle. It's a must check out location if you are at Yosemite for the first time.

It was a good experience, very unique collection of horror and Si-fi exhibition. There are also music rooms and machines that teaches you different aspect of music creation! I wish there is more for the price of the ticket, I hope they expand.

This park is iconic to San Francisco, with painted ladies and views to all around San Francisco. Sometime they have coffee trucks there. There is a pretty well maintained restroom, water fountain, and dog play ground.

Lovely little park, lots of food options around the area, great view, could be some what dirty at times. Some parts of the part is under construction. Usually you would have access to limit bike in the area.
One of my favorite spot in San Francisco, not a lot of tourist, lots of nature, the hike is not intense, it’s a nice nature walk for anyone who enjoy the ocean, the wood and fresh air.
This area is very easy to bike to, there is a small park right next to it. The view is pretty nice, you can watch boats coming in and out. Some area are still under construction.
This is a pretty unique little park, it’s well maintained, with a great view of the down town Seattle, lots of green grass, and big open space by the old gas industrial plant.
What a well nicely maintained park. You get the green trees, glacier, snow, large mountain, easy and hard trials, camping sites ... there are so much to look at and do here!
This is the pier that you would come to board  the Alcatraz island ship. There is a restroom to the left before you board. The line has shades, so it doesn’t get too hot.
This is a great park for watching the sunset. They have one path for bike and one for the runner or pedestrians. They have several large sculptures by famous sculptures.
If you are new to San Francisco, Dolores Part is the epic center of relax and hangin out with friends. You got the J train, Tartine bakery and bi rite ice cream near by!
Right after sunset it’s when people started to make fire. Some people might not be using firewood and might creates a lot of smoke. It’s relaxing and beautiful sight!
Nice little garden, great for picnic and hanging out. There do have a small bike rack in the parking lot. The garden is pretty well maintained and it’s free!
Great and complete collection of computer artifacts. Not a lot of interactive installation or history of programming.Take the guided tour to learn more!
This park has a long stretch of sand beach, lots of parking and benches, you can easily bike from down to here, there are bike path along the way.
Great place to bike to, clear pool, beautifully maintained garden, tree and lawn. There is a water fountain and restrooms for visitors.
Beautiful location, you get great views from pretty much all directions. There is a restroom picnic table and bike parking.
likes: Basic facilities (restroom, picnic table, bike parking)

reviews_attraction.text: This is a great area at night to check out the stars, there is also a flat sandy area near the bridge for people to chill.
Lovely park, easy to bike to, has lots of Porter parties, not too crowded, and huge open outdoor, what’s not to like.
The forest is pretty much flat, easy to walk or run around the trail. The place is well kept and not usually crowded.

This was one of the "must sees" I was told I had to go to. When I arrived I was so overwhelmed by the massiveness of it's size and how overcrowded it was. The line to purchase tickets was too congested and you would need an entire day to check everything out. The only thing I really wants to see was the Rain Room exhibit and I was told it was sold out, and if their was any chance of getting in I would have to wait in the huge line to potentially get to the front and find it was still sold out. You also couldn't purchase the rain room tickets online so that was very frustrating. There were several cool free things to look at, so we checked out the famous map posts and the levitating rock which were neat and then we left. I would recommend if you're interested in touring the entire museum for a day and you're not particular about just seeing one specific thing.

This place is such a neat touristy spot that has a lot of interesting history and mysteries surrounding it. The standard tour was 65 min long and we found a Groupon that saved $10 off each ticket. The tour guide was very well rehearsed and knew what she was talking about. She was able to answer questions, know her facts, and make everyone laugh. The tour itself was very interesting and it felt like I was in Willy Wonka- with rooms getting smaller and larger, and people potentially getting lost or left behind. It was a great experience and the home was beautiful, along with the property it was on. The gift shop was also full of a lot of cool things. I wouldn't go again but I would totally recommend it!

The Wonder View Trail is a beautiful and scenic trail to enjoy during the day. I hiked up the trail about 40 minutes before sunset and it wasn't the smartest idea. It takes about 35 minutes to hike up to the wisdom tree and by that time it was dark and I was very winded. I had to race back down the trail as it was getting very dark and didn't have time to make it to the Hollywood sign. Head up the trail closer to the morning or middle of the day. Expect to take at least an hour to get to the sign and plan accordingly. The journey back downhill is very dangerous and deceivingly slippery at night. Otherwise beautiful hike for people who want to climb!

This farm is so adorable, and great to go with a young family or for a fun hike with your pup. It is free and you were able to wander through the farm where they have goats, cows, chickens, and other animals, as well as educational areas inside of different buildings for young ones. They also have park equipment for kids to play on and trails behind the animals that go into the woods. What a great location for a couple hours of outdoor fun!!

Such a windy and quick trail to followed that has a lot of entry points. The trail is easy to access from different parking areas at the park. It also has an old building that is neat to observe from the outside if you’re interested. This is a good hike to take kids or dogs, with a lot of open area to run around and play fetch where it is off leash, or frisbee on a nice day!

The parking here is a little tight when they’re busy, but it’s so accessible to the entrance. The exhibits are really cool and it’s a great place to bring young kids because everything is right there so there’s really no way of getting lost or walking too much. There’s also a nice playground in the middle to let your kids run off some energy for a little while.

I camped here for two days and I love it! The hike up to Castle Dome was much harder than I was expecting. It is rated moderate but I would say difficult. The entire trail is uphill and it's about 4 miles up. Bring plenty of water. There are gorgeous views on this hike and the campsite is so comfortable with very friendly and helpful rangers!

Very cool ride if you aren't afraid of heights. This trolley takes you above the ocean next to SeaWorld, and the view is beautiful. It's probably a 15-20 minute ride total. The line is very easy to find and fairly quick to get through. I am personally terrified of heights, so one time was enough for me.

Beautiful hiking area with a comfortable breeze, and mostly shaded trails. This place had so many trails to choose from, whether you're there to run, hike, or bike. The water is also nice and cool, so if weather permits, dress appropriately to take a quick dip if you're up for it!

There are so many trails and breathtaking views at Alum Rock Park! It's a fantastic place for a quick hike or a good long workout in nature. Some of the trails are daily easy and others are quite difficult. Would highly recommend going for some good views with good company!

I like the historical value of the place but how much they charge is utterly ridiculous. Visiting Memphis, I don't know how families can afford to pay $40/person for a couple hours in Elvis's home. It's cool enough seeing the house from the road.

BEAUTIFUL!!! This is a must go if you have a day to spend outside in the water, climbing through rocks and sliding with waterfalls. The water is so clean and clear and the views are breathtaking! Highly recommend!!
Such a fun and inspiring place to visit for a beautiful hike. The views are spectacular and the feeling of awe is deafening. Would absolutely recommend to spend some time here if you have the chance!
Such a fun and naturally beautiful place to spend your day! I've loved visiting with small groups and big groups. Great place to go if you have a day! Would totally recommend 10/10.
