Mojave National Preserve located in the Mojave desert in Southern California is a terrific place to photograph,video, explore,camp,hike,RV,ATV,see railroads and trains and watch the sunrise and sunset.
It's vast,historical,scenic and great for family and individual adventure.
Our family had a great time!
Google search info about this land and come and visit!
likes: Diverse activities (photography, exploration, camping, hiking, RV, ATV)

reviews_attraction.text:
The Cleveland Script Sign at Edgewater Park,just west of downtown Cleveland,Ohio- is a terrific place to spend a morning or afternoon or for a scenic walk at dusk.
Overlooking Edgewater harbor, many individuals and families enjoy the park along the lakeshore and relax.
When you visit be sure to plan your visit at dusk for the most stunning of selfies!

Lookout Point Park located above Port Of Los Angeles,California,is a great place to see panoramic ocean views of The Port of Los Angeles,Port Long Beach and coastal views and beyond! Above It All !
.
.
.
.
#lookoutpointpark #portoflosangeles #portoflongbeach #oceanviews #waynesalvatti #nineteenth #ilovela #cityviews #ilovelongbeach

Great fun and educational Japanese cultural community near downtown Los Angeles.
Lots of Japanese restaurants-the REAL THiNG!
The Japanese Cutural museum is there to make it a complete family or date day or evening.

Euclid Beach Reservation near Cleveland Ohio is a great family location to walk,spend a day or have a picnic.
Lots of free parking too!
Dont forget to take a selfie at the Cleveland sign too!
Edgewater Park in Cleveland,Ohio is a wonderful place to see the City of Cleveland,the lake,and relax with friends,family or solo.Plenty of free parking and pet friendly!

A terrific place for families to explore and to learn.
Displays are first class and the staff is very friendly!

This place is so awesome!!! You can either drive up to a close parking lot or do the hike. I recommend the hike.

My girl friend and I did a photo shoot up here as the fog was filling the valley and rolling in. So my photos are crispy clear of the water below, but I hope they inspire you to still head up to this outlook.

I cannot wait to see this in the fall when the leaves chance or in the summer when it's clear. The lake/river below goes as deep as sea level in some areas also, which is crazy to think about.

The Wright brothers single handedly changes the world. It's amazing that they flew before the Titanic sunk, and that during Orville's lifetime he saw both world wars and a pilot break mach 3. Traveling to these places genuinely makes me interested in the history of this world, and the amazing people who shaped it.

The park ranger staff were super friendly and have an amazing presentation on the Wright Brothers. The entire area is a wonderful walk and the memorial is quite impressive.
likes: Facilities & Services: Friendly staff, Informative presentation

reviews_attraction.text:
One of my favorite places to run! There is about a mile loop in the front of the park but if you park near the end you can run along the lake/Dam/Creek around the loop to get an enjoyable five mile loop :)

Plus the pancake festival is always a super fun time in the spring. There are a ton of back trails to run and hike on. People in the area are super friendly too :)

Be sure to check out the ice skating as well. They are open to public on some days and times.

A fantastic beach and place to hangout. Although you cannot have beach fires in this area, the beach is absolutely wonderful and is in walking distance to the lighthouse and Buxton woods. As a runner and local, I run often here and in the Buxton woods just a tad down the road.

It's a great place to spend the day or weekend, camp down at cape point and enjoy the island!:)

This place is just Incredible. Wow....the sober feeling is very eerie over this landscape. I cannot wait to see the Bell tower having all 40 chimes activated here in the future. For the time being it is still a work in progress, but you should still take the trip up to the tower.

We almost missed the actual memorial down the road from this tower. Be sure to check it out!

Okay....so this place should be very neat. If you know the history of the massive ship that hung off the side of the mountain then you appreciate it. However now there is just this empty pull off that over looks a few counties. In the winter you can see through the trees. In the summer it's over grown.

You must stop if your driving through! You can grab some beautiful photos and it's nice to get out and strech your legs. I did a side hike when I drove through (added an extra two hours, but was nice to put driving aside for a while) to a trail called Long Point for the cool photo of the bridge.

Such an awesome wonderful rail road! We traveled here from Ohio for a weekend trip. The train ride was very nice and it is amazing to think they refurbished all the old train cars.

The history of this rail line is interesting. We would love to come back and do the dinner car for lunch :)

Such an exciting beach being able to watch the massive waves crash into the rocks. I could sit here for hours listening and watching them.

Definitely not a beach for swimming as the waters to rough. The park it's self is super clean with a clean tiny restroom.

This a great neat little museum. They have some great automobile treasures. Amazing to think how cars and engines have evolved over time.

We did the railroad in town then walked down town afterwards. Well worth the stop :) Highly recommend for family trips:)

Well worth the tour! Not a super crazy Elvis fan before I went, but I was blown away. The audio tour with the iPads is a great idea as well! I was a little skeptical at first, but it's well worth the price and time. I highly suggest visiting Graceland!

Wow what a great way to spend the afternoon! Rather your a visitor to saint louis or a local, this zoo is a great addition to the city. Then afterwards, head over to the boat house for dinner and rent out some paddle boats! A perfect date night!

Such a wonderful state park! A great loop around the lake for jogging and hiking. You can rent kayak or  canoes or bring your own. Beautiful mountains and a wonderful damn.

Definitely a great place to spend a weekend afternoon :)

If your visiting Atlanta or live here, it's a great place to see the city. I parked downtown and ran 2 miles out here to see it. But there is super close parking too. One of the best skylines of the city
Incredible! Drove through Dayton and decided to stop and check out the museum. 110% totally worth it! It is free, and very fascinating! A huge selection of older aircraft and modern marvels.
Awe this park is so neat! I feel as if it would be a great place to run. Little trails and it extends out to the Bay. Parking is easy and the people tend to be friendly here.
Simply amazing, totally worth the drive out of the way from hocking ans old man's cave. I highly suggest people coming for hocking hills visit this place
A great little park full of nature trails hidden inside chippewa. The longest trail is a loop a little over a mile with a bunch of smaller trails.
Wonderful experience and place to visit! It is A LOT more touristy, and is more like a large "park", but it is very cool. Nice, groomed trails.
Incredible!! Saint Charles is such a historic town, so both tourists and locals should check this out. It's cheap and you'll learn a bunch!
Good place to train for a marathon or just for a long hike. The trails are long gravel roads and area connects up with the Katy Trail.
A great little park to start a run when running into the city. We ran from here to the bridge but this park was nice and we enjoyed it
A beautiful stop! A mile north is preacher rock, make sure you check it out! This spot has a bothroom and trash but no running water
This is a wonderful, good work out hike! It can be relatively flat by splitting into other trails, or you can climb up to the peak.
A beautiful look out. We actually parked and took a nap here for a bit. A good place for a break!

This is one of my favorite spots in New Mexico. It is beautiful year round and the sound of the wind in the grass and trees is wonderful. New Mexico is such a desert state that it amazes me each time I go there and find a prairie. This is definitely a place to go if you want to do some landscape photography. There aren't many trails, but the grassland is open for wandering. And since it's high elevation it doesn't get as hot as the rest of the state. Well worth the visit. Plus if you like the show Longmire his house is in the Valle Caldera and the park rangers will sometimes drive you there. Just one other cool thing.

This place was a surprise. It's really easy to miss on the highway (the entrance is on the west bound weigh station on highway 550). The first mile to mile and a half is a well kept trail and after that the trails just follow the geography. It's possible to wander too since it looks to be BLM land. The views are lovely and deeper in the trail are great spots for photos. One thing to be aware of is that it's used and maintained by an off road motorcycle club. I didn't see anyone when I was there, but if you're hiking there just keep an eye out.

This place was alright. For myself it was a three star visit. It had interesting old boats to wander around and old cars in the boats. As a piece of history it is very interesting. If I had kids I think this place would be so much better. There were classes of kids being led around by two actors dressed as sea captains. They kept making the kids yell out things like, "Aye Captain!" They were tasked with the things that people on the boats usually would have. It was adorable. So for a kid this place is awesome. For an adult it's just cool.

I've wanted to visit this place ever since I saw/read Contact as a teenager. The dishes in formation is awesome to see, and that part of the state is beautiful. The VLA itself though is kind of just okay. It's an active science center and they'll give you a tour, but honestly I had more fun wandering around taking photos outside. It takes awhile to get here, but it doesn't take that long to explore it. I think it's worth the trip, but I would plan another place to go after it because it won't take you that long to be done with it.

I went during the summer so I don't have much to say as far as what the skiing is like. I will say that it was fun going out there for hiking and there are tons of great views up there. If you hike far enough up you can see the lakes at the peaks. On the way up there's a lovely little stream. Parking was free and we were allowed to just walk up. I don't know if it's always free during the summer, but it was the day we went and that was wonderful. As far as we could tell there weren't any open restrooms during the summer.

It's a nice trail that looks to be pretty well kept up. Looking at the maps I thought it would have more views of the river, but there was really only one spot that got all that close to the river. When I went it was during the monsoons and parts of the trail were flooded and very muddy. It was still a nice walk. The road to the spot is pretty easy to miss and it's a bit on the thin side of things. The road is maintained it's just something to keep in mind with larger vehicles at busier times.

This one is tough to recommend based off the cost. It is $25 per tour per person and the castle is split into 4 different tours. You have to buy all the passes ahead of time because you can't buy additional tours from the castle itself. All the tours give you the chance to wander the garden and see the indoor pool and really those by themselves are worth visiting. It's just hard to recommend the tours considering the cost. $25 to see an cool building and great garden is pretty worth it though.

This forest is great. It's a quick drive from Albuquerque, the views are amazing, and there are tons of places to hiking. I haven't ever used the tram to get to the top of the Sandias, but I have taken the road from Placitas and the one from Edgewood and both are wonderful. The one from Placitas is considerably more rough and higher clearance on your car would be great. Sunrise and sunset from Sandia Peak is worth the trip by itself.

The views from here are top notch. It is a bit crowded and the roads to get here from South Tahoe are a bit terrifying, but the trip was worth it. The hike to the beach is not too bad going down, but it can get a bit tough on the way back up. It's 2 miles round trip, so bring some water, and if you aren't in the best health you might want to skip the hike itself. If you're up for the hike though it is completely worth it.

The views are lovely from here. The pier itself is in terrible shape. Truly awful shape. Half of the pier was falling apart when we were walking on it. It had to be walled off because it was literally falling apart. The entire place smelled like piss too. On those two things nearly ruined being on the pier itself. The views were worth the trip though. I just wish they would clean the place up.

I liked this area, and I got some cool photos from it. But it's more of a walk than a real hike. The trail is paved and the grade on it is pretty chill. If you aren't much of a hiker it's one of the best spots to get near an old NM building, if you are into wandering the wilderness this isn't going to hold your attention for very long (but is still worth stopping by at least once).

My husband and I have gone here a few times. The garden is always worth it. It's really well kept and the cost is quite nice. There are some downsides. It's part of the water treatment plant and has a bit of a scent to it, and everything has concrete near it so it makes photography a bit difficult. All in all though it's a great place to spend some time on a slow afternoon.

It still strikes me as odd that there's a an aquarium in the middle of the desert. That being sad the types of fish and animals they have here are pretty cool. It always smells pretty fishy and it is always crowded. The price is a bit high too because it's not very big. I think it was worth going to once. I haven't really felt the need to go back.

I like the hike at this location. The worst part is that sometimes the dirt roads to get there are a little rough. The views from this location are lovely. There's plenty of places to wander and if you stand in the right place you can get an amazing view of the Rio Grande Valley. Taking photos sunrise is great, a little less impressive at sunset.

This is a great place for a hike. There are lighter trails to wander and there are more advanced trails to wander around on with plenty of surprises. Heck I found an old Ford Mustang in a ravine out there. I'm not sure how it got there, but it was a neat find. The trails go all the way up to the mountains. Awesome spot to go!

I'm not a fan of rides, so when I was invited to go here I wasn't so sure. I had a good time though. It's like going to a state fair that's going on all the time. Everything is a little bit cramped and the layout is odd, but for the price and it's location near the free way make it a fun place to spend an afternoon.

For the longest time I thought this place was a made up movie set, and then my fiance brought me here. It's not the biggest park in the world, but it is super fun to wander around in. The rocks themselves are pretty easy to hike up and the view from them is great. Now I can say I stood in the same spot as Spock.

Any time that I go to Old Town I make it a point to also come here. I don't know how they do it, but every show I've seen at this museum has been top notch. Heck I even saw a student photo show here once and it was amazing. The Albuquerque Museum is a real gem in town and completely worth the visit!

This place is fun to visit. Incredibly crowded, but the views are so nice. Especially at sunset. It's a very fun spot to wander and take photos. There are a couple of restaurants near there as well that have a second floor that let you just watch the pier, beach, and sunset at the same time.

This place can get pretty crowded. It makes the hike trickier because of all the narrow passages. That makes taking photos more difficult too. Going on an off day is a good idea. Pack light too. It's not the hardest hike, but light climbing is required to get to the top.

I really enjoy Santa Fe's plaza. It's just a nice place to wander and take photos. The biggest downside is how hard it can be to find parking and how crowded it is. There area  bunch of good restaurants and the area around the plaza is really nice to.

Admittedly we went in the winter so most everything was still closed. The views were very nice and even with quite a bit of snow still up there it was pretty easy to get there and wander around parts of the lakes.
We missed the chance to hike here the last time we were out that way, but we made it in time for some amazing sunsets. It was a lovely place and I plan on getting back out there one of these days.
The view from here is wonderful. I think I missed prime poppy season when I got there, but it was still a wonderful place to wander. It was definitely worth the drive.
It's a little expensive and crowded, but it's always a good time, the gardens are lovely, and it's great for taking photos.

This place sits along the Connecticut River and is adjacent to Harbor Park. They have live music here with both indoor and outdoor capabilities. It is nice to sit outside, eat some good food, and enjoy a drink while watch a musical performance from a band (or solo act). For example, you may enjoy dining on the Lobster Mac & Cheese. For lighter fare, they have French fries, Eggplant fries, or the recently trending Sweet potato fries.
Prices may be a little high, but not ridiculous. Part of the charm here is this place's ambiance and surely waterfront property comes at a premium..
Boats sometimes come in off of the river, which is pretty cool.
I have actually arrived here by boat after a cruise down the river.
This is a nice place to go out for a good time. The bartenders and rest of the staff are nice.
The only downside to this place is that it is susceptible to flooding inside if the river swells and gets too high.

While on a duck boat tour of the city, we went passed here and saw a huge crowd with a couple of bands performing on different stages. We decided to give it a closer look after the tour.
What we found was, there was free admission. The next thing we discovered is that it was some sort of hemp fest. I actually asked one of the many police officers what was going on. After he told me it was a hemp fest, I asked him where to go for good Italian food in Boston.  We didn't stay, but instead, cut through, on our way to the north end of the city, which is some sort of Little Italy.
The festival looked like everyone was being respectful. There were lots of police officers there, providing security. There were many vendors offering lots of food options as well as other merchandise. The park looked nice.  There is a lot of history associated with it.
If you are in Boston, you should check out the Boston Common.

Nice park. Lots of people walk around the track. Good view over the city from the monument at the garden.
Fun fact; The location of the garden was a wading pool back in the late 60's, maybe early 70's. Also, back then, there were many more ways to drive into and through the park (before they made the road into more of the so-called track).
The Shell is a nice spot to watch free outdoor concerts at night during the summer...
When there are no shows, sometimes kids will skate board in front of the Shell stage. Some of them are pretty good...
They have baseball fields and tennis courts here. As you walk around the loop, there are various exercise stations with different apparatuses set up along the way.
There is a small hill in which kids sled on that is nice.  It is located nearby the playground.
The playground is nice. It was redone a few years back...

I was passing through the area the other day and came across this bridge.  I will be coming back in the semi-near future to explore the trails, but I did take a moment to go to the observation platform to take in the view of the merging rivers.  If you arrive here via route 7, there is parking before you cross the bridge. Yes, you can drive across it, but there is no parking on that side of the bridge. The no parking side is where you need to go to take a short walk out to the observation platform where you can see the two rivers merge.
I will update after my return visit at which point I will hike the woods. This place is a real beauty!  More to come in the future...
Side note;   Someone from the area told me legend has it that George Washington crossed that bridge... I can not confirm or deny this.

Nice park with plenty to do. There is a public pool that is fairly new. A nice walking trail runs through the woods behind the pond. It isn't usually too crowded, so it allows you to be able to enter nature while still being close to the rest of the city.
Update; There is now an entrance at Village Square Drive, off of Hartford Road so you can enter from the backside. The trail has been tarred over and looks like it is a bit busier than it used to be... It is still nice, just more crowded.
Picnics areas are available for large groups from the city for a small fee.
This park is a fun place for a kid to explore...
Over the years, I have seen crayfish, snakes, eels, and fish in the park, not to mention birds in various locations throughout the park.
It is also the home of the New Britain Little League.

We went here just before sunset one evening to check out the lighthouse. We climbed down into the rocks to get a great view of the lighthouse itself and we spent a little time watching the sun go down. You need to get there early because as we were leaving, it looked like the local authorities were no longer allowing people to enter the area. This is purely  speculation based on the squad car blocking half the road when we were leaving.
Anyway, it is a cute little lighthouse and a great spot to watch the sunset.
Very picturesque...
We purchased tea in Bar Harbor and this lighthouse is on the back of the packages.

I went here last season to see Seven Bridges Road, an Eagles tribute band. There were a lot of people that attended the show, but the area is big and the flow of traffic was handled well. The band was very good. There were multiple food trucks there to offer food and beverages for reasonable fees.
There were plenty of garbage cans to help keep the place clean. The crowd was well behaved and pleasant. I understand they have several shows here annually. I would recommend watching a show here and I'd certainly come here again for a future show.
Good times!

I like this place a lot. As you spiral up, you get a good look at the sea creatures that are what is essentially a giant aquarium. Once you get to the top, you can look down into it.
I remember going here as a kid with my parents and grand parents. It was great, until father picked me up and acted like he was going to toss me in. It scared the poop out of me knowing there were/are sharks in that water...
As an adult, I took my own kids here. They really enjoyed it. I did not terrorize them as my father had done to me. lol
Good times

The wife and I went here for a night time trolley ride. It was nice. The length of the ride was good time wise, not too short, but likewise, not excessively long.
The night we went it was a little cold waiting while we were waiting in line, but we enjoyed a delightful, hot chocolate to keep us warm.
This would be even more fun to go to if you were to bring kiddies.
We had fun and if you have never tried it, I would certainly have no reservations in recommending this place.
Good times

I last went here some time ago while chaperoning my daughter and a few of her friends on a class field trip. We all had a great time here checking out the animals. I liked this zoo much better than other zoos I've gone to. The layout was good and there were many cool animals to see. My favorite of the day was the gorillas. Although I do really like the big cats...
The facilities were clean. The staff was friendly and helpful.
If I had to pick a favorite zoo, this is it!
Good times

This place is a shadow of what it once was... I remember a time when you could go here and set up a blanket in the sand on the beach and spend the day. There was parking and  lots of people would go here. Now, it is mostly a waste of space and resource...
I have gone here for water skiing competitions in more recent times, but those events are far and few in between.
At one point, years ago, people were able to use the pavilions and set up a grill.

This is a must see location in San Francisco. You can walk this area, but driving is another option. During the day, it gets backed up with a line of cars waiting to make the short drive.
We were still on east coast time and were up and here bright and early and there was no line. We drove down, parked, and then walked on it too.
It was cool to see it in person after seeing it on film so many times over the years...

This Zoo is nice. I took the kids here years ago to see a dinosaur exhibit. The dinosaurs were animated and looked very realistic. One kid, not mine, was so scared, they wet themselves...  lol
I will also mention, it was very hot outside when we went, so many of the animals were not doing much, if anything at all.

This is a scenic area along Memorial Boulevard in Bristol, CT. They have some nice things in regards to war memorials here. In the past, I know they had the Moving Wall here tool.
If you drive through here, the Boulevard is for automobiles only. Your vehicle must have passenger plates on it to drive through.

Very cool place to go, especially if you have a kid that is into dinosaurs. The building covers the tracks and you can see the pathways and strides of the dinosaurs too. The outside area is nice as well.
It isn't the biggest place, but then again, we are lucky to have this sort of thing at all...

While in Newport, we decided we wanted to tour one of the mansions, so we chose this one since it was owned by the Vanderbilts (and we recognized the name).
We did the audio tour. The place was amazing. You want to talk about well to do? Parts of this place are layered in real gold.

Attended a Holy Communion here for one of my nieces here. The place is very big. It was a nice ceremony, but took a long time due to all the people that were there for the same thing - multiple people received their communions on the same day.
It is very nice looking inside.
likes: Facilities & Services: Big place, nice interior

reviews_attraction.text:
This is the end of route 66. There is a sign there to mark it.
We took pictures next to it.
We learned people that drove the entire route and documented their journey check in here. Pretty cool...
Perhaps some day, we will drive this entire historic roadway.
K-Lap

This park is just gorgeous... So many flowers to see. It is known for the Rose Garden. Obviously the best time to see this park in all it's glory is when the roses are in full bloom.
There is a little restaurant here too...
Very nice place

Talk about historical. The USS Constitution, aka "Old Iron Sides" is still afloat and you can actually go on it and take a tour (for a fee).
This is another must see, Boston attraction, even if you're not a history buff.

This is one of the nicer beaches in Connecticut. Being in CT means the ocean is Long Island Sound, which means no significant waves. Long Island New York blocks the waves. This beach is in the lovely town of Madison...

We enjoyed our trip to see the Statue of Liberty, including the boat rides there and back.
I will say, the statue looks bigger in the movies and on television.
There are some great views from the statue...
We drove over this bridge we came across while exploring Arlington. When we drove to the other side, we were surprised to find a former home of Norman Rockwell. It is a very nice area...

I like the aquarium, but it is a little too expensive for what it is.
My favorites were the Beluga whales and the penguins.
It does get very crowded at times.
Beautiful place for a stroll. Very pretty. You can see Taylor Swift's house from here. Lots of people fishing here

This is a fun place to take kids that need to burn some energy. There are different themed areas for the children to play. Places like tractors, grocery store, water play, theater, and trains and cars. There is also a craft area and clay building area. On nice days there is a large outdoor exploration area as well. On weekends it is much more packed with people than on week days. My children have a blast each time we have been.

Although I cannot pronounce the name of this park correctly, it is a great park to relax or bring the family to for a fun afternoon. There's plenty of grass space to lay in. There's a great toy structure to play on. The skate park has both easy and difficult sections to play on. My children loved riding their bikes around the park, and in the skatepark. People seem to be very friendly here and make space for the little kids.

This is a fun park. The play structure is huge. There are swings, a rope structure climbing area, and a sand play zone. The big structure has tons decks at various levels, lots of slides, and balance obstacles. My children enjoy this place so much. There are picnic tables, benches, rocks, and concrete walls to sit on. The park is well kept. There are bathrooms right near the play zone.

This is such a fun place to go with the family. Lots of rides for all ages. The new roller coaster looks awesome, we did not ride it on our last trip as we had our little kids with us. There is lots to do and so many fun attractions. The park is not so large that you have to walk forever to have fun. When you buy unlimited rides bracelets you also get into the roller rink as well.

I was slightly disappointed by this area. The view is good. The weather seems to his stay cold even on a hot sunny day. The water is murky. In the trails are very Brushy out to the water. Perhaps it was just a few times I've been here, but each time there was a sketchy vehicle in the parking lot. The owner loitering around. And made me feel uneasy about leaving my vehicle there.

This is a huge awesome park. Lots of space for walking, playing, and relaxing. The toys for children are brand new and exciting. It is not your averages slide and swing set lind of park. There is a water and sand zone, things to climb on, a very large hillside slide, a skate park, soccer field and a great energy about the place. This is a wonderful place.

We visited White Pass Ski Area in the Gifford Pinchot National Forrest. We have been here many time before, but we brought our 5 year old son this time. Staff at the ski area was great and accommodating. The National Forrest was stunning and beautifully dressed  in its winter whiteness. The clear day made for fantastic views of the surrounding valleys.

We had a great time here fishing. My boys lov e catching fish after fish. They may be tiny little things, but it's tons of fun. It is an active park with many people walking on the trails and enjoying the relaxing scenery. It's a great spot to take a relaxing walk too. The trails are well kept and maps are located along the trails for easy navigating.

Great community park. There are paths and trails to walk on. The park is medium sized. Enought for a light walk with a few laps around. Not a great spot for a jog. It would be a good place to pass through on a jog. The toy structures are in good shape. The grass is kept trimmed. Much of the park it unkept and just has small trails throughout.

This was a very relaxing park. I visited during a super busy day at this park. Literally hundreds of people. The park handled it nicely. People were napping, relaxing, sitting in the grass. They had brought in some extra portable restrooms that had long lines, but that was really the worst of it. Everyone was having fun. Glad I could visit.

This is a nice large city park. It has a little bit of everything. There is an area for kids to play and park toys and swing. There are lots of trails for walking, jogging, or riding bikes. Tons of green space available for laying in the sun and relaxing or enjoying a picnic. There is also a large pond with ducks swimming around.

This park is very large. We went in the springtime so the river was very high. It appeared there was more part to be explored when the river is lower. The play structure here is nice not very large and simple. There are several fishing docks. There's also a boat launch dock You may not fish off of that one.

It is very interesting to just walk through the cemetery. There are some very old graves. The family plots have some wide ranges of years and life spans. The buildings are very cool to look at. There is a calm quite feel here. It lacks an eeriness that some cemetery locations have. Its clean and well kept.

My family love to visit here. There are nice trails for a relaxing walk around two ponds and some marsh like wetlands. You are guaranteed to see some duck or geese while on a walk. We have been fishing of the shore and a few docks that are present. We have had a good time reeling up small fish.

A fun tractor and equipment museum. My kids enjoyed looking at toy and real tractors. The exhibit is way larger than it looks from the road. They have lots to look at. There are many trinkets and things for sale. A fun place to spent several hours, walking, looking, and reminiscing.

The pier was nice. It was a little cold on the first week of January with the wind. But just long sleeve shirt kind of cold. The little shows are fun. Ruby's at the end of the pier was nice. People fishing. Kites flying, surfers surfing. Lots to see. The sun set was stunning.

The Westport Tower offers up good views of the ocean as well as the whole town of Westport. The harbor looks amazing with all the boats. On good days there are large ships to view. I would recommend bringing binoculars and a camera to the location. It is a spot to remember.

Nice little park along the north shore of the nightly Columbia river. The beach is sand and the current is calm. There are great views of the sun rise and sun set. You can also see the Portland airport across the river and watch planes take off and disappear on the horizon.

Such a cool park. There are some beautiful little beaches. The trails are nice and well kept. The light house is wonderful. The ocean is majestic from the view decks. My family had a wonderful time here. The 7 dollars to get in with a small vehicle is totally worth it.

Many fun times are had at this park. I remember playing at this park as a kid, and now I bring my kids here. It's a pretty big play structure. If you are over 6 feet tall it's hard to keep with with the kids.
The hikes is is not bad. My 5 year old made it. The falls is pretty. We took a picnic and sat off the trail on some fallen. Trees and it was very fun.
Quiet calm neighborhood park. Good views and relaxing. If the main road was a little further away it would be even better.
A park hidden in the neighborhood. Takes a while to find. Always has a few kids playing here. Stays quiet and relaxing.
Good place for lake side entertainment. Swimming area is nice. There is a play structure that my kids really enjoyed.
The hike is nice. The park spots are nice. It can be very hard to find a spot to park on weekends.

(Translated by Google) Waimea Canyon has spectacular colors, in fact the red-orange of the rock blends with the green of the vegetation. In addition to the colors, the dimensions are also striking, in fact it is very large and from the road that runs along it there are various points to admire it from various angles. We saw it both in the morning with a bit of mist, and at noon where the colors were more alive. If you have some time, you can also do some small trails so as to immerse yourself even more in nature. In particular, this is the main lookout where you have a view of the entire canyon

(Original)
Il Waimea Canyon, ha dei colori spettacolari, infatti il rosso-arancio della roccia si fonde con il verde delle vegetazione. Oltre ai colori anche le dimensioni colpiscono, infatti è molto grande e la dalla strada che lo costeggia ci sono vari punti per ammirarlo da varie angolazioni. Noi lo abbiamo visto sia alla mattina con un po' di foschia, sia a mezzogiorno dove i colori erano più vivi. Se avete un po di tempo fate anche qualche piccolo trail così da immergervi ancora di più nella natura. In particolare questo è il Lookout principale dove si ha la vista sull'intero canyon

(Translated by Google) The Waimea Canyon State park, has spectacular colors, in fact the red-orange of the rock blends with the green of the vegetation. In addition to the colors, the dimensions are also striking, in fact it is very large and from the road that runs along it there are various points to admire it from various angles. We saw it both in the morning with a bit of mist, and at noon where the colors were more alive. If you have some time, you can also do some small trails so as to immerse yourself even more in nature.

(Original)
Il Waimea Canyon State park, ha dei colori spettacolari, infatti il rosso-arancio della roccia si fonde con il verde delle vegetazione. Oltre ai colori anche le dimensioni colpiscono, infatti è molto grande e la dalla strada che lo costeggia ci sono vari punti per ammirarlo da varie angolazioni. Noi lo abbiamo visto sia alla mattina con un po' di foschia, sia a mezzogiorno dove i colori erano più vivi. Se avete un po di tempo fate anche qualche piccolo trail così da immergervi ancora di più nella natura.

(Translated by Google) Wonderful park with "alpine"-like views. In addition to the intrinsic beauty of nature, it is necessary to consider the spectacular organization of the park, with clear indications for trails and well-kept roads. The full visit would take several days. Pay attention to the height in fact with the car you get to about 3600 meters above sea level, so when you move on foot if you are not used to it, be careful.

(Original)
Meraviglioso parco con panorami simil "alpini". Oltre alla bellezza intrinseca della natura bisogna considerare l'organizzazione spettacolare del parco, con indicazioni chiare per i trail e strade ottimamente tenute. La visita completa richiederebbe più giorni. Fate attenzione all'altezza infatti con la macchina arrivate a circa 3600 metri sul livello del mare, quindi quando vi spostate a piedi se non siete abituati fate attenzione.

(Translated by Google) For an airplane enthusiast like me you could not miss a visit to this museum. Structure divided into two large areas; the first traces the attack on Pearl Harbor with reproductions of the war environments of that time, the second a large parking lot of planes and helicopters with historical pieces such as F-14 and F-15. The museum lacks a pinch of vitality to be able to take full marks

(Original)
Per un appassionato di aerei come me non poteva mancare al visita a questo museo. Struttura divisa in due grandi aree; la prima ripercorre l'attacco a Pearl Harbor con riproduzioni degli ambienti di guerra di quel tempo, la seconda un grande parcheggio di aerei ed elicotteri con pezzi storici come F-14 e F-15. Al museo manca un pizzico di vitalità per poter prendere il massimo dei voti

(Translated by Google) The most beautiful beach on the Big Island and among the best of all Hawaii. Deep beach with light and fine sand. Crystal clear waters and little moves. We took a bath with the mantas that swam around us. Presence of lifeguards and services. Parking is on payment, it is recommended to arrive early in the morning so that you can enjoy it with a few people. Magnificent

(Original)
La più bella spiaggia di Big Island e tra la migliori di tutte le Hawaii. Spiaggia profonda con sabbia chiara e sottile. Acque cristalline e poco mosse. Abbiamo fatto il bagno con le mante che nuotavano attorno a noi. Presenza di bagnini e di servizi. Il parcheggio è a pagamento, consigliato arrivare la mattina presto così da gustarla con poche persone. Magnifica

(Translated by Google) Perhaps less touching than the cemeteries in Normandy but with the same historical and emotional value. Excellent choice to limit access, it allows a quick but very private and touching visit. The wall remains impressed with the names of the dead boys and the oil that continues to rise from the wreck despite 70 years have passed

(Original)
Forse meno toccante dei cimiteri in Normandia ma con lo stesso valore storico ed emotivo. Ottima la scelta di limitare gli accessi, permette una visita veloce ma molto riservata e toccante. Rimane impresso il muro con i nomi dei ragazzi morti e l'olio che continua a salire dal relitto nonostante siano passati 70 anni

(Translated by Google) Nature show that looks like the geyser even if technically it is very different. In fact the jet of water comes from the waves that pass under the rocks and come out forming a jet of water. Intensity and duration depends on the sea conditions, it takes patience to see a nice jet

(Original)
Spettacolo natura che assomiglia al geyser anche se tecnicamente è molto differente. Infatti il getto d'acqua deriva dalle onde che passano sotto gli scogli e fuoriescono formando un getto d'acqua. Intensità e durata dipende dalle condizioni del mare, ci vuole pazienza per vedere un bel getto

(Translated by Google) The oldest public building in Manhattan continuously in use is a small episcopal church immersed in the skyscrapers of Low Manhattan. Also resisted by the collapse of the twin towers that were nearby, it is now also a meeting point to pray to the victims of terrorism.

(Original)
L'edificio pubblico di Manhattan più antico continuamente in uso, è una piccola chiesa episcopale immersa nei grattacieli di Low Manhattan. Resistita anche al crollo delle torri gemelle che si trovavano nelle vicinanze, è ora anche punto di ritrovo per pregare le vittime del terrorismo.

(Translated by Google) A well-kept park where various government buildings overlook, such as that of the "municipality" of Denver and that of the State of Colorado. In addition there is also the Museum of contemporary art with some sculptures exhibited right in the park.

(Original)
Parco ben curato dove si affacciano vari edifici governativi, come quello del "comune" di Denver e quello dello Stato del Colorado. Inoltre si trova anche il Museo di arte contemporanea con alcune sculture esposte proprio nel parco.

(Translated by Google) Coming down from Rainbow point there are various panoramic points which, however, do not reserve the same emotions as the first although always beautiful and with unique peculiarities. A short stop is a must.

(Original)
Scendendo da Rainbow point ci sono vari punti panoramici che però non riservano le stesse emozioni del primo anche se sempre bellissimi e con delle particolarità uniche. Una breve sosta è d'obbligo.
dislikes: Less emotional impact compared to Rainbow Point

reviews_attraction.text:
(Translated by Google) Well-kept Japanese-style garden with some very suggestive corners. The size is small and if you consider the admission price it is quite expensive. Either way, it's an interesting experience

(Original)
Giardino in stile giapponese ben curato e con alcuni angoli molto suggestivi. La dimensione è ridotta e se si considera il prezzo di ingresso risulta abbastanza caro. Ad ogni modo è un esperienza interessante

(Translated by Google) Medium-easy trail where the only difficulty is the ascent by a ladder that makes this trail particular that goes into these spectacular mountains. Allow about 1 hour to travel completely.

(Original)
Trail medio-facile dove l'unica difficoltà è la salita per una scala che rende particolare questo trail che si addentra tra queste montagne spettacolari. Considerate circa 1 ora per percorrerlo completamente.

(Translated by Google) The first panoramic point that is located shortly after the park entrance. From here you have a spectacular overview of the valley and the surrounding mountains. Not to be missed

(Original)
Il primo punto panoramico che si trova poco dopo l'ingresso del parco. Da qui si ha una panoramica spettacolare sulla vallata e sulle montagne circostanti. Da non perdere

(Translated by Google) Located near Old Faithful, this area contains 3 swimming pools with unique colors not to be missed. To visit it takes about 30 minutes being quite small.

(Original)
Posizionata nelle vicinanze dell'Old Faithful, questa zona racchiude 3 piscine con colori unici assolutamente da non perdere. Per visitarla servono circa 30 minuti essendo abbastanza piccola.

(Translated by Google) Two pitches for the view of the Canyon, on the first you have a beautiful view, unfortunately from the second you do not see anything because of the dense vegetation grown.

(Original)
Due piazzole per la vista del Canyon, sulla prima si ha una bella visuale, purtroppo dalla seconda non si vede nulla per colpa della vegetazione fittissima cresciuta.

(Translated by Google) Waikiki Bay is very famous all over the world for the unmistakable skyline it offers, very high beach and palaces. Beautiful view from Diamond Head, not to be missed.

(Original)
Waikiki Bay è famosissima in tutto il mondo per l'inconfondibile skyline che offre, spiaggia e palazzi altissimi. Bellissima la vista da Diamond Head, da non perdere.

(Translated by Google) Beautiful scenic spot in the Badlands national park. The colors and shades of the mountains acquire an even stronger charm during the sunset.

(Original)
Bellissimo punto panoramico del parco nazionale di Badlands. I colori e le sfumature delle montagne acquistano un fascino ancora più forte durante i momenti del tramonto.

(Translated by Google) Beautiful beach, famous for both surfing and windsurfing. Very strong currents make it very dangerous to swim but to admire those who surf is spectacular.

(Original)
Bellissima spiaggia, famosa sia per surf che windsurf. Corrente molto forti rendono molto pericoloso fare il bagno ma ammirare chi fa surf è spettacolare.

(Translated by Google) For being a mountain road it is beautifully maintained and it is fantastic to drive. From here you can admire the road that goes up immersed in the forest.

(Original)
Per essere una strada di montagna è tenuta splendidamente ed è fantastico guidare. Da qui potrete ammirare la strada che sale immersa nella foresta.

(Translated by Google) Beautiful panoramic point in an area of ​​the park where the conformation of the mountains is different. Here in fact the predominant color is yellow.

(Original)
Bellissimo punto panoramico in una zona del Parco in cui la conformazione delle montagne è differente. Qui infatti il colore predominante è il giallo.

(Translated by Google) Castle located in the center of Central Park. From an architectural point of view nothing to report, good view you have from the top.

(Original)
Castello posizionato nel centro di Central Park. Da punto di vista architettonico niente da segnalare, buona la vista che si ha dalla sommità.

(Translated by Google) The statue reminiscent of Alice in Wonderland is one of the most famous Central Park points. A passage for a photo is a must.

(Original)
La statua che ricorda Alice nel Paese delle Meraviglie è uno dei punti più famosi di Central Park. Un passaggio per una foto è d'obbligo.

(Translated by Google) One of the most popular pools in Yellowstone. Reachable on foot, it allows you to admire unique colors.

(Original)
Una delle piscine più famose di Yellowstone. Raggiungibile a piedi permette di ammirare dei colori unici.

(Translated by Google) Lookout point on Lower Falls. Easily accessible, it allows you to take incredible photos.

(Original)
Punto panoramico sulla Lower Falls. Facilmente raggiungibile permette di scattare foto incredibili.

(Translated by Google) Beautiful Lookout, if you pass by the road you have to stop to admire the landscape

(Original)
Bellissimo Lookout, se si passa dalla strada bisogna fermarsi per ammirare il paesaggio

This is one of the best museums I've been too. It's very exclusive and pretty hard to get tickets for because you have to get tickets 3 months in advanced and they only release tickets on the first of the month. What I loved most about this museum is the architecture. It's incredible how it's built on the water, so much glass and natural lighting. The way that they stagger people into the museum makes it feel like you're alone walking through this big building observing art. It's hands down my favorite museum in the area.

A hidden gem in DC. This is a very nice art museum. The layout is great. It features sculptures indoor and out door. It has a ton of nice art paintings. One of my favorite things about this museum is the outside area, it has a path you can walk through that is a shaded and features very cool sculptures. It also has a really cool fountain where sometimes there is live music playing. This is for sure a low key place with not a lot of parking. They also change the art out having different themes every few months.

This art gallery is absolutely incredible and free! It has a great array of art and sculptures. Even work from Picasso. The museum is open and huge with a lot of natural lighting. There is a terrace with great views of DC and sculptures. They have an underground walkway that goes between the east and west ends of the building with gift shops and a full cafeteria. One of the coolest things about this underground tunnel is the waterfall that comes down and crashes into a glass wall.

The sky deck was a really cool tourist attraction. Being from south Carolina and living now in Washington DC I don't get to see very many tall buildings. Being up that high in the clouds was just amazing. A view of the city. Not being able to see the ground at certain times, looking down only seeing clouds was very cool. It was very organized and didn't take too much time. I went on a weekday so the lines were very short.

This is a great place to come and observe the Golden Gate bridge. It's cool to watch the traffic from this vantage point. If you're a photographer it'd be great to get a time lapse here along with all other kinds of icon photos. It was pretty crowed when I came here, so if you want photos without a lot of people in them you'd want to come at off hours. Either really late or very early in the morning.

This Museum was very interesting to me, I have always missed the ball pits but I was able to make it for the LAWN exhibit. The LAWN exhibit was very cool a manmade turf hill with a ton of hammocks to lounge in. Other exhibits were really cool as well, if you're into architecture. The secret cities and the Hoops exhibit were among my favorites. I recommend stopping by if you're in the area.

This place is incredible. So many businesses, shops and restaurants located inside. This building is also huge. One of the coolest things I saw when walking around was they had this huge projector that was displaying the news and had red cushions on like big stairs where people were sitting eating their lunch. I thought that was very unique.

This park was pretty cool, I enjoyed the giant cupid bow and arrow. The views here are great no matter what direction you look. You have the bridge and the water, the cool architecture of the city behind you and of course all the people passing through the park. It's a great place to get some take out and just hang out and eat.

This park seemed to be very cool. The light arches is what I went to go see. I do street photography for a hobby so I ventured all the way to this park to try and get a cool photo. I was very disappointed to know upon arrival that the lights were off. I got there a little after 9PM. The park was nice from what I could see.

I thought this was a really unique artistic fountain. It's really cool how it doubles as art and sort of a water park for small kids. One thing I really liked about the Crown fountain is that the faces that were projected onto the towers were all actually people who lived in Chicago. That's just a very cool concept.

This museum is incredible! It really is filled with amazing art. It's very clean, the layout is very well designed and I love how it has windows that have incredible views of the city. They also have a restaurant inside and outside displays for when the weather is nice! This is a must see if you have the time.

A pretty cool area to see for sure. It's not as big as I thought it would be but it's surrounded by stores, a ton of stores. There are always a good amount of people here doing varies things. Street artist, photographers & even people playing music and things. It's a great place to hang out and people watch.

This area is a lot of fun if you're into photography. You can do so much in your photos with the water reflections and stuff. The national Capitol columns is also a cool historic place where Abraham Lincoln gave his famous second inaugural address. I'd say check it out for sure if you're in the area.

A nice park, I'd say it on the bigger side of parks in Washington D.C. It has a couple of parks for the kids, open grass/field for dogs, maybe kicking a soccer ball around, catch. All sorts of room for activities. It also has a good amount of pavement running through the center of the park.

This is a great museum. The exhibits rotate so it's always good to come back. It very nice inside and the staff is great very patient and knowledgeable about things in the museum and other things in the city. It's not too big but I'd say three hours is adequate to explore the whole thing.

This is a phenomenal park with a lot of things to do and see. It's a fun place to take pictures. You can walk, bike or even drive from
Place to place. There are a lot of pathways you can walk down to get lost in nature. This park is pretty big at times you forget you're in the city.

Being a space geek this is for sure one of my favorite museums in DC. It has great replicas and audio tours. One of the coolest things is they have an IMAX theater inside of this museum. If you like air and space flight this is a stop you should add into your schedule.

A very cool street. It's a marvel to see in person. It's going to be really crowded. If you intend to try and drive down this street you will have to be very patient. It's worth recording of you do take the time to wait in the long line to drive your car down Lombard.

One of the staples in the city. It is the highest structure in the city. Through out the city you can see the monument. The way the city was designed it provides amazing views of this monument you can see daily just going about your day to day life.

I'm pretty sure everyone knows about the two popular photos i took below. Even though you've seen these pictures everywhere, nothing beats actually seeing these views in person. There is a reason they are so popular. The views are amazing.

Eastern market farmers market is a great place to spend your mornings. Nice areas around to eat and a lot of cool vendors and local artist. I ride my bike down here at least once a month to check out some of the cool unique boutiques.

Growing up watching full house I couldn't come to San Francisco and not come here. This is a cool spot to see in person and also a great spot to have a picnic if you don't mind all the tourist hanging out and snapping photos.

This is a great park. It's huge. I went here for curlfest and it was a phenomenal event. This park has great views and with it being on an island even on the hotter days the breeze from the water keeps it bearable outside.
Not exactly sure what this building is or its purpose but it is very cool to look at. It has a nice out door seating area for lunch and its a cool place to take photos as well.
Nice area with a nice view. A great place to have lunch outside. Walking distance to restaurants and ice cream.

The Yorktown is the second carrier museum we have visited. We’ve also been to the Midway in San Diego. This is very similar. You can go throughout the ship and the deck has various aircraft.

One thing different here is the memorials to carrier losses which I don’t recall the midway having. Important to remember those lost on carriers. During covid, operations are pretty much unchanged as the indoor spaces are generally large. It was pretty sparsely attended the day we went. Masks required.

It’s a lot of walking all over the ship. Wear comfy shoes.

Also, the onboard restaurant is closed due to covid but they have a snack bar, we just brought our own sack lunch.

Saw littler turtles and sting rays on the walk along the pier to the ship.

Great zoo and aquarium. We’re yearly members so we go often. The zoo is worth the price if you’re visiting and if you’re local, the membership should be your go-to gift for birthdays or holidays. It’s a great value with guest passes and unlimited entry. Here’s what I find...when I travel and go to zoos with my kids, other places zoos aren’t really any better than pdza. Went to San Diego this summer and without pandas which have been returned to China, there isn’t many animals you can’t find at either pdza, woodland, or Oregon zoo. Pdza is stellar when compared to other zoos. On par with the best. Friendly staff. Decent food options. Monument to ET the walrus. It’s a good place.

Great views from the end of the road of Waimea canyon. The problem I have with these locations, many along the road, is the lack of facilities. I don’t think there was a bathroom up here. That’s the only reason for the docked star. If places do have bathrooms, they are sometimes not well maintained. Aside from that, it’s remarkably beautiful. You’re at the mercy of weather as it can be cloudy up here and it was on and off cloudy here in mid February. It’s a pot-hole filled, twisty road up but that’s part of the fun. Just take it easy. Hike down the trail a bit for additional views, it can be steep and muddy. Sturdy shoes recommended. Definitely worth the drive. At least once.

A great monument/exhibition. Beautifully constructed with immersive experience of walking behind the waterfall to displays about MLK and elegant quotes along the wall. It's relatively quiet here aside from the cascading water which does have a roar to it. A peaceful place in the midst of the bustling city. We went over MLK weekend and it wasn't crowded (which might be a sad truth). Was able to take a good amount of time and slowly walk through all the parts of this place. I enjoyed reflecting here and exposing my children to the importance of MLK and the movement he was a part of and that continues to be necessary today.

Limited parking at this water’s edge spot but basically the only public access on this side of the lake at least. Paddleboarded our from here. There’s a little rope swing for the kids. Can see little fish in the water. Boat launch is small and steep but everyone seemed to be able to make it work. Lake’s great. Once in the main body of water there’s a small island to explore and then under the road bridge which gives view of rainier. Pleasant paddle even on a weekend. Boat traffic was present but not overly annoying.

Nice beach and pier in Hanalei. Protected bay keeps waves down and nice for beginning surfing or wading. Nice sand here, maybe imported as it’s not full of coral. Lots of families for the kids to play with and they made fast friends. Parking can be an issue and the bigger problem is the bathrooms. Honey buckets without toilet paper and unserviced. They are building bathrooms that should help but the current situation is really tough. Be prepared. Knocked a star off for that issue.

This was one of my favorite stops in Waimea canyon. It is pretty early in the drive. When we were here in sept 2010 I don’t think it was flowing but this time in feb 2020 it was and it was really stunning. The landscape is mars-like. Lots of good photo opportunities. Be careful not to slip and get the soil on your clothes as I’ve heard it can stain. Definitely a great early stop on the road. We hiked all around it. Please be careful to not leave trash or destroy any plant life.

It’s a little pricey but there are offers available variously to reduce the costs. We had a deal where adults were free with paying child. The tram experience is great with many animals around and their playground is second-to-none. We really enjoy the otter area with the other small mammals. They are fun to watch. It’s a good distance out of town so plan for a long drive both ways but it’s worth it!

Longtime members of pdza. Great zoo and new and improved aquarium. Tons of different animals and regions to see. Enclosures are decent. You’re not as close to the animals like the San Diego Zoo but still good visibility. Highlights are tigers, elephants, budgies you can feed, new aquarium, walrus, polar bears, red wolves, and roaming peacocks. Great play area for kids as well.

There is a lot to do at the museum of flight. They have special events for members and lots of great displays and interactive presentations. The air park has lots of big planes to check out and the new b-52 is pretty cool. Was lucky to see the red arrows stop here. Kids love it. I love it. Connections memberships for kids is big plus.

Nice viewpoint lookout spot with trails that lead to i don’t know where. More signage about those paths would be helpful. Stopped here to stretch legs and place was deserted. Saw grey whales from here in the distance. Shady parking lot is nice and it’s a few blocks off the main highway so it can be quite quiet here.

Great part of the museum. It’s a bit of a walk from the main buildings but it’s pleasant. Great to see the Concorde and only Air Force one. Ww2 bombers and planes both commercial and military. There’s a small kids play area in the very back past the Dreamliner. They love playing there - it’s like a little airport.

Very nice beach park. You have to pay to park inside the park but we found street parking a block from entrance and walked in. Quietish during covid and most people keeping distance. Pleasant water and waves here. Wonderful soft white sand. Facilities are down towards the end of the park where the car lot is.

Very interesting feature to visit on the coast. You can walk under this thing! Then you can play on the beach. Parking located not too far and facilities available. We stopped here on an around the peninsula 2 day drive which is maybe pushing it a bit with kids. 3 days would be better for that long haul.

Nicely kept historical site. Free to walk around and read placards. It’s where the hunley launched from and a few other important things happened here. Walked around and then out to the beach. Do not recommend this beach. Got bitten up by small bugs there. Cool cannons around the fort. Worth a stop.

Cool place to visit. Excellent views and a workout to boot. Very steep, straight walking path with stairs either side of the curvy roadway. We took the cable car from fisherman’s wharf up to the top, walked down, then up again. Fun for the kids to see the curviest street.

Beautiful place but difficult on holiday weekend. Came over Memorial Day and it was so packed they had to let cars in one at a time as visitors left. Nice hikes/walks and info at the center. Friendly enough staff. Decent facilities. Worth a visit during a quieter time.

Very cool park with lots to do. Be advised if you’re going to a beach, it’s a hike down because the park is up on a bluff. Beautiful though. Great sandy beach at agate beach and rocky shores at cannonball beach. Will visit here again. Day use fee is 8$.

Went here for free covid test. Long line. Drive through. Health workers were nice and gave the kids stickers and licorice. Person with mental health issues ranting at corner.

Nice looking park.
dislikes: Person with mental health issues ranting

reviews_attraction.text: Nice city park that is well kept. Bathrooms, play ground, nice walks under the bridge. Playground is themed with the Yorktown, bridge, and lots of Charleston specific landmarks.
Really nice sandy beach with decent public access. I really enjoy the walk between wailea and polo beach. Nice views between two nice beaches. We always enjoy sunset here.
The pic is of just to the north of Thor’s well. Cool spot. Short hike down to the rocks and the well. Saw grey whales just off shore! Lots to explore in this area.
Nice park with play area for kids, facilities, and water access. Pleasant atmosphere and generally pretty quiet here. Lake is nice to be out on.
New bridge is nice but the stairs are STEEP. Beach is rocky. We launched kayaks and paddle boards and went across to ketron. Pretty cool.
Nice little park and beach. Lifeguard on duty. Not much in the way of facilities here. Nice walk along the tracks.

(Translated by Google) The largest neighborhood in Chinatown in the world and where the concept of this type of neighborhood originated, mixing Western architecture with the Chinese's own details.
It is impressive not only for its size or for the amount of details but also for the whole history it has, for how to conserve the identitary houses of powerful families ... it is worth it and I recommend visiting with a guided tour to have an experience completely different
On one of the streets you can find the store where the lucky or fortune cookies are made, you can try them and see how they are made and can also be purchased in different formats.
If you go to San Francisco, you must visit Chinatown!

A un d’els carrers es pot trobar la botiga on es fan les galletes de la sort o de la fortuna, pots provar-les i veure com les fan i també es poden comprar en diferents formats.
Si vas a San Francisco has de visitar Chinatown!

We only saw a small whale called Minke whale, and we saw it from afar, but apart from that we had the experience of seeing Risso's dolphins close by and short nose even closer.
The whole crew of the ship is wonderful not only with the clients, also with their way of treating animals, how they respect nature and how they try not to interfere when they know that animals that do not like them. A great experience.
Now just browsing with them is fun enough.

Només vam veure una petita ballena que es diu Minke whale, i la vam veure des de lluny, però a part d’això vam tenir l’experiència de veure dofins Risso’s de molt a prop i dofins de nas curt encara de més aprop.
Tota la tripulació del vaixell és meravellosa no només amb els clients, també amb la seva forma de tractar els animals, com respecten la natura i com intenten no interferir quan saben que als animals que hi ha no els agrada. Una experiència genial.
Ja només el fet de navegar amb ells és prou divertit.
