(Translated by Google) I found Guardian Building, Fisher Building and especially the "abandoned buildings" like Fisher Body Plant 21 much more interesting, therefore only 3 stars. In addition, of course, "The Henry Ford" in Dearborn.
This beautiful view of the GM Renaissance Center, "RenCen" for short, can be seen from the ballroom on the 32nd floor of the Guardian Building.
At 221 m high, the GM Renaissance Center is the tallest building in Detroit. It consists of 5 interconnected towers and was opened in 1997. In addition to the GM Global Headquarters, there is also a 72-story Marriott hotel and the "Coach Insignia" revolving restaurant at the top.
Free entry: on the lower floors, all 5 towers are connected to form an atrium with surrounding shops, cinema, the entrance to the GM office wing, etc. There both the history of Motor City, i.e. Detroit, shown, as well as that of General Motors. The urban development is surprisingly clearly in the foreground. GM itself is illustrated by gigantic LED displays and vehicle exhibits.

(Original)
Ich fand Guardian Building, Fisher Building und besonders die „abandoned buildings“ wie Fisher Body Plant 21 deutlich interessanter, daher nur 3 Sterne. Außerdem noch natürlich das „The Henry Ford“ in Dearborn.
Diesen wunderschönen Blick auf das GM Renaissance Center, kurz "RenCen", hat man vom Ballsaal im 32. Stock des Guardian Building.
Mit 221 m Höhe ist das GM Renaissance Center das höchste Gebäude von Detroit. Es besteht aus 5 miteinander verbundenen Türmen und wurde 1997 eröffnet. Neben dem GM Global Headquarters ist noch ein 72-stöckiges Marriott-Hotel und ganz oben das "Coach Insignia" Dreh-Restaurant darin.
Eintritt frei: In den unteren Stockwerken sind alle 5 Türme miteinander zu einem Atrium mit umgebenden Shops, Kino, dem Eingang zum GM-Bürotrakt, etc. verbunden. Dort werden sowohl die Geschichte von Motor City, i.e. Detroit, dargestellt, als auch die von General Motors. Die Stadtentwicklung steht dabei erstaunlicherweise deutlich im Vordergrund. GM selbst wird illustriert über gigantische LED-Displays und Fahrzeug-Exponate.
dislikes: Less interesting compared to other buildings

reviews_attraction.text:
(Translated by Google) The Norris Geyser Basin is one of the hot spots of Yellowstone NP, including many interesting volcanological phenomena: Echinus Geyser, Steamboat Geyser, and Emerald Spring, just to name a few of Topp's attractions.

The Echinus geyser is very, very unreliable as far as the frequency of its eruptions is concerned, but you want to see the colorful iridescent colors around its lake. It is a so-called acid geyser, which gives its shores the colorful colors: iron, arsenic, manganese, aluminum, and many other substances are in its water, which then oxidizes in the air. and the rusty colors arise. After being inactive for 70 years, he has been active again since 1948. Even in the 1990s, water fountains shot up very regularly, but now, for decades, it has been erupting only very, very irregularly, sometimes every hour, and then again for many weeks.

Unfortunately, just as we were at Steamboat Geyser despite all the waiting no eruption was on. We would like to have taken that too

(Original)
Das Norris Geyser Basin ist einer der sehenswerten Hot spots des Yellowstone NP, u.a., da viele interessante vulkanologische Phänomene hier zusammenkommen: Echinus Geyser, Steamboat Geyser, und Emerald Spring, um nur einige der Topp-Attraktionen zu nennen.

Der Echinus Geysir ist sehr, sehr unzuverlässig, was die Frequenz seiner Eruptionen angeht, aber die bunt schillernden Farben um seinen See will man gesehen haben. Er ist ein sogenannter saurer Geysir, was seinem Ufer die bunten Farben verleiht: Eisen, Arsen, Mangan, Aluminium, und viele weitere Stoffe sind in seinem Wasser, was dann an der Luft oxidiert. und die rostigen Farben entstehen. Nachdem er 70 Jahre inaktiv war, ist er seit 1948 wieder aktiv. Noch in den 1990er-Jahren schossen sehr regelmäßig Wasserfontänen hoch, aber nun bricht er schon seit Jahrzehnten nur sehr, sehr unregelmäßig aus, mal im Stundentakt, und dann wieder über viele Wochen hinweg nicht.

Leider stand gerade als wir am Steamboat Geysir waren trotz allen Wartens keine Eruption an. Die hätten wir gern auch noch mitgenommen

(Translated by Google) The Lower Terraces are far more exciting than the Upper Terraces, so I would only visit them in the future. Overall, the Mammoth Hot Springs are beautiful, but they can not compete with the top attractions in the Yellowstone NP.
The Mammoth Hot Springs are lime sinter terraces, similar to Pamukkale in Turkey. The predominant color is snow white, but there is also a lot of yellow, red and brown. You walk on a wooden boardwalk (board walk) with very many and steep steps, and is therefore safe from burns. We liked it a lot, and the sinter terraces are also on the way to the northern exit of the Yellowstone NP at Roosevelt Arch in Gardiner, so you'll inevitably get past it. Even from the parking lot you can see a lot of sintered terraces, so that walk-disabled can here. I was struck by this interesting, clinking sound that comes when the water flows down the rock formations.

(Original)
Die Lower Terraces sind weit spannender als die Upper Terraces, daher würde ich nur diese künftig besuchen. Insgesamt sind die Mammoth Hot Springs sehr schön, aber mit den Top-Attraktionen im Yellowstone NP können sie nicht mithalten.
Die Mammoth Hot Springs sind Kalk-Sinterterrassen, ähnlich wie in Pamukkale in der Türkei. Die vorherrschende Farbe ist schneeweiß, aber es gibt auch viel gelb, rot und braun. Man läuft über einen Holzplankenweg (board walk) mit sehr vielen und steilen Treppenstufen, und ist daher sicher vor Verbrennungen. Uns hat es gut gefallen, und die Sinterterrassen liegen auch am Weg zum nördlichen Ausgang des Yellowstone NP am Roosevelt Arch in Gardiner, sodass man zwangsläufig dran vorbeikommt. Auch vom Parkplatz aus sieht man schon sehr viele Sinterterrassen, sodass auch Geh-Behinderte hierher können. Mir fiel noch dieses interessante, klirrende Geräusch auf, das entsteht, wenn das Wasser an den Steinformationen herunterfließt.

(Translated by Google) 1925 created at 600 Biscayne Boulevard Tower, 17 floors, 78 meters high. One of the most high-rise buildings in Miami, when extremely low from today's perspective. Designed in Mediterranean Revival tower was modeled after the bell tower of the Giralda in Seville. One of the landmarks of Florida!
He was the headquarters of a newspaper, which was inaugurated the tallest structure in the city. After the newspaper publisher had moved, it was rebuilt in 1962 by the State for the opponents of the Communists under Fidel Castro in a refugee camp and used as such until the 1974th From that time the name "Freedom Tower" is due.
In 1997, the tower was sold for 4.1 million US dollars and extensively restored. Today it is home to, among others, the Miami Dade College Museum, as well as offices and is often used as an art gallery.
About the College Museum can be visited for $ 12.

(Original)
1925 am 600 Biscayne Boulevard erstellter Turm, 17 Stockwerke, 78 m hoch. Eines der schönsten Hochhäuser Miamis, wenn auch aus heutiger Sicht äußerst niedrig. Der im Mediterranean Revival entworfene Turm wurde dem Glockenturm der Giralda in Sevilla nachempfunden. Eines der Wahrzeichen von Florida!
Er war das Headquarter einer Zeitung und bei seiner Eröffnung das höchste Bauwerk der Stadt. Nachdem der Zeitungsverlag ausgezogen war, wurde es 1962 vom Staat für die Gegner der Kommunisten unter Fidel Castro in ein Flüchtlingslager umgebaut und bis 1974 als solches genutzt. Aus dieser Zeit rührt der Name „Freedom Tower“.
1997 wurde der Turm für 4,1 Millionen Dollar verkauft und umfassend restauriert. Er beherbergt heute unter anderem das Miami Dade College Museum, sowie Büros und wird häufig auch als Kunstgalerie genutzt.
Über das College Museum kann er für $12 besichtigt werden.

(Translated by Google) Architecturally interesting and part of the overall arrangement of Downtown Chicago!
From this bridge, a double-decker bascule over the Chicago River, one has an impressive view (or photo subject) of the skyscrapers on the shores of the Chicago River and, most notably, the 423-meter Trump International and Hotel Tower, or Trump Tower, inaugurated in 2009 which was built in the style of the Burj Khalifa.
The road bridge over the Chicago River is part of Michigan Avenue and connects the northern and southern parts of Chicago.
As you can see, I was there on St Patricks Day, where every year the river turns green. Attention: If you want to experience this, you have to goog in advance, when exactly the "River Dying" will happen in the respective year, so that you are not a weekend too early or late there.

(Original)
Architektonisch interessant und Teil des Gesamt-Arrangements von Downtown Chicago!
Von dieser Brücke, einer doppelstöckigen Klappbrücke über den Chicago River, hat man einen beeindruckenden Blick (oder Fotomotiv) auf die Skyscraper am Ufer des Chicago River und vor allem auf den 423 m hohen, in 2009 eingeweihten Trump International and Hotel Tower, kurz Trump Tower, der im Stil des Burj Khalifa errichtet wurde.
Die Straßenbrücke über den Chicago River ist Teil der Michigan Avenue und verbindet den nördlichen mit dem südlichen Teil Chicagos.
Wie man sieht, war ich an St Patricks Day dort, vor dem jedes Jahr der River grün gefärbt wird. Achtung: Wenn man dieses erleben will unbedingt vorher googlen, wann genau im jeweiligen Jahr das „River Dying“ passieren wird, damit man nicht ein Wochenende zu früh oder spät dort ist.

(Translated by Google) Not a park as such, but rather a huge lawn interrupted by flower beds between the beach and Ocean Drive. But this is exactly the ideal way to walk parallel to the beach and street. There is always something to see here - seeing and being seen is THE motto: The restaurants directly on Ocean Drive are of course overpriced, but it is worth just watching people and cars.
Bikini girls on the long beach of South Beach, lifeguards keep watch in their colorful pastel-colored beach huts, and body builders lift weights in an open-air gym in the park. Chic and expensive cars, especially cabriolets or classic cars, keep gliding up and down Ocean Drive with V8 babble.

(Original)
Kein Park im eigentlichen Sinne, sondern mehr eine riesige Rasenfläche unterbrochen von  Blumenbeeten zwischen Strand und Ocean Drive. Aber genau das ist ideal, um parallel zu Strand und Straße spaziergehen zu können. Hier gibt es immer was zu sehen – Sehen und gesehen werden ist DAS Motto: Die Restaurants direkt am Ocean Drive sind natürlich überteuert, aber es lohnt sich, einfach nur Leute und Autos zu beobachten.
Bikini-Girls am langen Strand von South Beach, Rettungsschwimmer halten Wache in ihren bunten in Pastellfarben gestrichenen Strandhütten, und Body Builder stemmen Gewichte in einem open air Gym im Park. Schicke und teure Autos, vornehmlich Cabriolets oder Classic Cars, gleiten immer wieder mit V8-Gebrabbel den Ocean Drive rauf und runter.

(Translated by Google) We crossed the Golden Gate Bridge with the 32-foot camper. A unique experience. The Postcard View, however, we have omitted.
Be sure to drive through the Moore Rd below the Lime Point (see google reviews) to the Lands End. You can usually park well there. We drove here very early in the morning when the bridge was still in the fog. One parks very close to one of the bridge piers, but just below the bridge and therefore sees it from another, unusual perspective. We then made our breakfast in the motorhome, and as fog and clouds cleared, we had unique views. Although in the summer, only a few local fishermen were there, no tourists. THE insider tip!

(Original)
Wir haben die Golden Gate Bridge mit dem 32-Fuß-Wohnmobil überquert. Ein einmaliges Erlebnis. Den Postcard View haben wir allerdings ausgelassen.
Man sollte unbedingt die Moore Rd unterhalb des Lime Point (s. google-Rezensionen) bis zum Lands End durchfahren. Man kann dort meist gut parken. Wir sind morgens ganz früh hierher gefahren, als die Brücke noch im Nebel lag. Man parkt sehr nahe an einem der Brückenpfeiler, aber eben unterhalb der Brücke und sieht sie daher aus einer weiteren, ungewöhnlichen Perspektive. Wir haben dann im Wohnmobil unser Frühstück zubereitet, und als Nebel und Wolkenfetzen sich lichteten, hatte wir einmalige Ausblicke. Obwohl im Sommer, waren außer uns nur ein paar einheimische Fischer dort, keinerlei Touristen. DER Geheimtipp!

(Translated by Google) The Grand Prismatic Spring is the largest hot spring in Yellowstone NP and the third largest in the world. It has an oval shape of 75 x 91m, is 49m deep, so really gigantic. Approximately 2,000 liters of 71 ° C hot water flow out of their interior every minute. The colors from blue to yellow to red at their edges come from microorganisms in the water or underground.
It has its own parking lot, from which you can walk around ½ mile in an irregular circle on a paved wooden boardwalk (board walk) around 5 large geothermal wonders. This makes the whole thing harmless nowadays. This area is next to the Old Faithful certainly the most volcanologically interesting in the park.

(Original)
Die Grand Prismatic Spring ist die größte heiße Quelle im Yellowstone NP und die drittgrößte weltweit. Sie hat eine ovale Form von 75 x 91m, ist 49m tief, also wirklich gigantisch groß. Minütlich strömen etwa ca. 2.000 Liter gut 71 °C heißes Wasser aus ihrem Innern. Die Farben von blau über gelb bis rot an ihrem Rand stammen von Mikroorganismen im Wasser oder im Untergrund.
Sie hat ihren eigenen Parking Lot, von dem man ½ Meile in einem unregelmäßigen Kreis auf einem befestigten Holzplankenweg (Board Walk) um 5 große Geothermalwunder herumlaufen kann. Dadurch ist das ganze heutzutage auch ungefährlich. Dieses Gebiet ist neben dem Old Faithful sicher das vulkanologisch interessanteste im Park.
likes: Size and depth of the spring

reviews_attraction.text:
(Translated by Google) This pool is rather small, but a must for visiting Yellowstone NP, especially for its intense blue color. The colors come from microorganisms in the water or underground.
The pool belongs to the Midway Geyser Basin. From the Grand Prismatic Spring Parking Lot you can walk around ½ mile in an irregular circle on a paved wooden boardwalk (board walk) around 5 great geothermal wonders. This makes the whole thing harmless nowadays. This area is next to the Old Faithful certainly the most volcanologically interesting in the park.

(Original)
Dieser Pool ist eher klein, aber besonders wegen seiner intensiven blauen Farbe ein Muss eines Besuchs im Yellowstone NP. Die Farben stammen von Mikroorganismen im Wasser oder im Untergrund.
Der Pool gehört zum Midway Geyser Basin. Vom Grand Prismatic Spring Parking Lot kann man ½ Meile in einem unregelmäßigen Kreis auf einem befestigten Holzplankenweg (Board Walk) um 5 große Geothermalwunder herumlaufen. Dadurch ist das ganze heutzutage auch ungefährlich. Dieses Gebiet ist neben dem Old Faithful sicher das vulkanologisch interessanteste im Park.

(Translated by Google) The Dragon's Mouth Spring was not that impressive, but the Churning Caldron in the same geothermal area was fine.
The Dragon's Mouth Spring is a kind of cave, from the hissing sound hot steam or smoke comes out, just like from the mouth of a dragon. Otherwise, this natural spectacle is rather unspectacular.
The Churning Caldron is a boiling mud hole (mud pot), from which mud masses are thrown up a few meters. This is really interesting to look at, and the Caldron is also quite large, s. my review.

(Original)
Die Dragon’s Mouth Spring fand ich jetzt nicht so beeindruckend, die Churning Caldron im selben Geothermal-Gebiet aber sehr wohl.
Die Dragon’s Mouth Spring ist eine Art Höhle, aus der unter lautem Fauchen heißer Dampf oder Rauch herauskommt, gerade wie aus dem Maul eines Drachen. Ansonsten ist dieses Naturschauspiel eher unspektakulär.
Die Churning Caldron ist ein kochendes Schlammloch (Mud Pot), aus dem immer wieder Schlammmassen ein paar Meter hoch geworfen werden. Das ist wirklich interessant anzuschauen, und die Caldron ist auch recht groß, s. meine Rezension.

(Translated by Google) 1930s and 40s art deco architecture, beautifully preserved and fully in use. In this district between 5th and 23rd Str, every street looks like an IG motif.
In just 2 square kilometers there are over 900 historic buildings in the well-known Art Deco style: fronts in delicate pastel tones, soft curves everywhere, and dazzling neon advertising signs. The Miami Beach administration wanted to demolish the old buildings when they were in poor condition and make room for new ones. Fortunately, that was prevented.

(Original)
1930er und 40er Art-Déco-Architektur, wunderschön erhalten und vollständig im Gebrauch. In diesem Stadtvierel  zwischen 5th und 23rd Str wirkt jede Straße wie ein IG-Motiv.
Auf nur 2 Quadratkilometern stehen über 900 historische Gebäude im bekannten Art-Déco-Stil: Fronten in zarten Pastelltönen, weiche Rundungen überall, und schillernde Neon-Reklameschilder. Die Verwaltung von Miami Beach wollte die alten Gebäude, als sie im schlechten Zustand waren, abreißen lassen, und Platz für Neues schaffen. Das wurde glücklicherweise verhindert.

(Translated by Google) On the trip from Seattle to San Francisco, we visited many of the crazies of nature, including Van Damme State Park, because I was simply interested in the Pygmy Forest. The Pygmy Forest is definitely a very crazy one. Due to the ingredients of the soil, the trees, some of which are hundreds of years old, have remained dwarfed.
The trail is very well developed with wooden walkways that lead across the swampy areas. Sure, like everywhere in the USA. Finding the forest was not easy.

(Original)
Auf der Reise von Seattle nach San Francisco haben wir viele Verrücktheiten der Natur besucht, unter anderem den Van Damme State Park, weil mich der Pygmy Forest einfach interessierte. Der Pygmy Forest ist sicher ein sehr verrückter. Durch die Inhaltsstoffe des Bodens sind die z.T hunderte Jahre alten Bäume zwergwüchsig geblieben.
Der Trail ist sehr gut ausgebaut mit Holzstegen, die über die sumpfigen Flächen hinwegführen. Sicher, wie überall in USA. Einzig den Forest zu finden, war nicht so einfach.

(Translated by Google) I'm not a type to look at poignant, sad places. Still, this monument has mesmerized me completely. It is a place of rest in otherwise busy Miami Beach. Of course, the psychedelic music in the tunnel from the outside to the inside does the rest. If you are in Miami Beach for 2 days, you will see the Art Deco district on Ocean Drive, maybe the Wynwood Walls and Calle Ocho in Miami itself, but then this Miami Beach monument should be one of them.

(Original)
Ich bin eher kein Typ dafür, mir ergreifende, traurige Orte anzuschauen. Dennoch, dieses Monument hat mich voll und ganz in seinen Bann gezogen. Es ist ein Ort der Ruhe im sonst so hektischen Miami Beach. Die psychodelische Musik im Tunnel vom Außen- zum Innenbereich tut natürlich ein Übriges hinzu. Wer 2 Tage in Miami Beach ist, wird sich das Art Deco Viertel am Ocean Drive anschauen, vielleicht noch die Wynwood Walls und Calle Ocho in Miami selbst, aber dann sollte dieses Monument in Miami Beach eben auch dazu gehören.

(Translated by Google) A photo can hardly describe this beauty, especially since the trees hardly fit in a photo!
The whole area along the HW 101 is impressive with the ancient trees. You drive in the semi-darkness with bright sunshine, because hardly a sunbeam passes the tree giants to the streets. For me, this was one of the many highlights of a road trip from Seattle to San Francisco.

(Original)
Ein Foto kann diese Schönheit kaum beschreiben, zumal die Bäume kaum auf ein Foto passen!
Die ganze Gegend entlang des HW 101 hier ist beeindruckend mit dem uralten Baumbestand. Man fährt im Halbdunkeln bei strahlendem Sonnenschein, weil kaum ein Sonnenstrahl an den Baumgiganten vorbei bis auf die Straßen trifft. Für mich war dies eines der vielen Highlights eines Roadtrips von Seattle nach San Francisco.

(Translated by Google) 10USD is fierce to see a tree that you can drive your car through. Still, we're in the sequoia area, and that's how we want to see this spectacle. In my opinion, it was worth it. Cars and mid-size SUVs fit through, full-size SUVs or even RVs don't.
The Chandelier Tree is 96m high, has a diameter of 6.5m and is said to be more than 2400 years old.

(Original)
10USD sind heftig, um einen Baum zu sehen, durch den man mit dem Auto hindurch fahren kann. Dennoch, wir sind hier im Gebiet der Mammutbäume, und so wollen wir auch dieses Spektakel sehen. Aus meiner Sicht hat sich das gelohnt. Pkw und Mid Size SUVs passen durch, Full Size SUVs oder gar RVs nicht.
Der Chandelier Tree ist 96m hoch, hat einen Durchmesser von 6,5m und soll mehr als 2400 Jahre alt sein.

(Translated by Google) He is worth a visit because of the hiking possibilities. Definitely one of my highlights in Yellowstone NP.
The Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone is regarded by many tourists as a miniature version of the original Grand Canyon in the southwest. This is wrong, because this canyon is very well visible, and you can walk here much easier than in the hot, dusty southwest.

(Original)
Er lohnt wegen der Wandermöglichkeit einen Besuch. Definitiv eines meiner Highlights im Yellowstone NP.
Der Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone wird von vielen Touristen als Miniaturversion des originalen Grand Canyon im Südwesten angesehen. Das ist falsch, denn dieser Canyon ist sehr gut einsehbar, und man kann hier viel leichter wandern, als im heißen, staubigen Südwesten.

(Translated by Google) He is worth a visit because of the hiking possibilities. Definitely one of my highlights in Yellowstone NP.
The Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone is regarded by many tourists as a miniature version of the original Grand Canyon in the southwest. This is wrong, because this canyon is very well visible, and you can walk here much easier than in the hot, dusty southwest.

(Original)
Er lohnt wegen der Wandermöglichkeit einen Besuch. Definitiv eines meiner Highlights im Yellowstone NP.
Der Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone wird von vielen Touristen als Miniaturversion des originalen Grand Canyon im Südwesten angesehen. Das ist falsch, denn dieser Canyon ist sehr gut einsehbar, und man kann hier viel leichter wandern, als im heißen, staubigen Südwesten.

(Translated by Google) Worth seeing! The procedure is like so many attractions in the USA: You drive by car or RV, runs max. 300 m and calls this the "stern hike".
The skull rock and the rock formations around it are very beautiful. We found the entire Yoshua Tree NP great. It is ideally located on the route between San Diego and the Grand Canyon.

(Original)
Sehenswert! Das Proceder ist wie bei so vielen Attraktionen in USA: Man fährt mit dem Auto oder RV hin, läuft max. 300 m und bezeichnet das als „strenious hike“.
Der Totenkopf-Fels und die Fels-Formationen drum herum sind sehr schön. Wir empfanden den gesamten Yoshua Tree NP als toll. Er liegt ideal auf der Strecke zwischen San Diego und dem Grand Canyon.

(Translated by Google) Alamo Square Park is visited for "The Painted Ladies", a beautiful 19th century row of houses. The Victorian houses are strikingly different in color, which earned them the name. From the park you have a beautiful view of these wooden houses and on SFO.
After half an hour you usually move on again.

(Original)
Den Alamo Square Park besucht man wegen „The Painted Ladies“, einer wunderschönen Häuserzeile aus dem 19. Jhdt.: Die viktorianischen Häuser sind auffallend unterschiedlich gestrichen, was ihnen den Namen einbrachte. Vom Park aus hat man einen wunderschönen Ausblick auf diese Holzhäuser und auf SFO.
Nach ½ Stunde zieht man meist schon wieder weiter.

If you are in town, make sure you either buy tickets online or you just turn up and bis. USD 22 for Illinois nonresidents, USD 11 for residents. Its platform is on 94th with panoramic windows all around. Spectacular scenery down there to watch. There is a smalll but nice exhibition explaining the building's history. The coffee shop at 94th offers hot and cold beverages, sweets and saveries.
I skipped the Tilt, which is said to be the highest altitude moving ride  attraction in the US. I simply found it not worth the extra cost for just leaning onto a glas panel sliding out by ca. 30 degrees.

(Translated by Google) In the Ground floor everyone finds the sights very fast. Cathedral-style! But definitely drive up to the 32nd floor with the lift. There is the Great Ball room. View from there u.a. at GM Headquarters or Ambassador Bridge, s. Photos. Unique!

(Original)
Im Ground floor findet jeder die Sehenswürdigkeiten sehr schnell. Kathedralen-ähnlicher Stil! Unbedingt aber mit dem Lift in den 32. Stock herauf fahren. Dort befindet sich der Great Ball room. Aussicht von dort u.a. auf GM Headquarter oder Ambassador Bridge, s. Fotos. Einmalig!

Excellent! The Fountain Paint Pots are for sure one of the top 5 ranked attractions you will visit, once going to Yellowstone NP.
The trail is very, very short. Whereever you look, there are gas bubbles coming out of mud or waters. The sulfur smell though maybe awful at times. The walk is very easy. Park your vehicle at the Fountain Paint Pot trail parking lot and with very few steps you are there, where all this action is. I specifically liked the bizarre looking remains of the trees killed by the sulfur.

(Translated by Google) The Bean, officially called Cloud Gate, must be seen. It's definitely worth a hike.
There is always a lot going on here. Unfortunately, far too many Gen Y tourists who take nonstop selfies.

(Original)
The Bean, offiziell Cloud Gate genannt, muss man gesehen haben. Die ist definitiv einen Fußmarsch wert.
Hier ist jederzeit ganz viel los. Unglücklicherweise auch viel zu viele Gen-Y-Touristen, die pausenlos Selfies machen.

(Translated by Google) The Norris Geyser Basin is one of the most interesting hot spots in the Yellowstone NP, among other things, as many interesting volcanological phenomena come together here.

(Original)
Das Norris Geyser Basin ist einer der sehenswerten Hot spots des Yellowstone NP, u.a., da viele interessante vulkanologische Phänomene hier zusammenkommen.

25 USD pp is a quite high entrance fee, however it was worth it.
We were impressed by the stories around these 2 personalities. The premises looked prestigious as expected. Rarely one woudl have a chance to see how they lived and what kept them going towards their missions.
As well we liked the banyna tree right in front of the buildings.

the LARGEST! permanent​ folk art collection in the world...100,000 items strong.
all thanks to the tireless efforts of eccentric collecters, Alexander & Susan Girard. connections to Herman Miller, and the Eames brothers. how ya' like me now design afficionado's? this place never fails to impress. always dynamic travelling exhibits, of course. pack ya some lunch, this could take all day...

came here for Jennifer Lynch art exhibit in Fechin Studios/Museo Store which is a separate building/seperate experience. Studios = free entry. saving next visit for Fechin House. both are world class examples o' architecture/human ingenuity and integrity. can't recommend more highly, don't leave Taos without a visit!

werth it fer de African Arts Collection upstairs alone! the soul and juju o' de masks still shines thru. perhaps even more relevant in our multicultural surroundings... the Renaissance old guard paintings downstairs bore me, make me sleepy.

late summer magique at AfreekaSF: FelaFest! celebrate de Nigerigian AfroPop legend, wit musique all day, bean fritters, curried goat, and sunshine beamin' out de NM/African ladies. Cameroon, Ghana, Nigeria, Sudan, Mali, Algeria represent!

primitive. thas' how we like it in this neck the woods. primo spots fer gratis overnight camping. some roadside pulloffs wit facilities like pit toilet, by design no electric! best part maybe close proximity to backwoods country roamin'!

please donate a few bucks to honor dem folks who've graced us wit this blissful lil spot. lovely dedication to creativity inna out de way spot o Carrabelle, which is refreshingly real/not overdeveloped/ full o rich boring pasty folk

came here fer Standing Rick exhibit.
WATER IS LIFE y'all. ya can't drink oil... will be returning fer de masterpieces o Pueblo pottery. that'll be an all day deal, gladly seaux! de knowledge n collection here is non parallel.

world class facility, I went to the 'Making Africa' exhibit, fell more in love with African matters/issues than I already was! 😘can't wait to return for modern contemporary art, civil rights exhibits, so elemental to life!

incredible spot fer creative reuse o space that becomes a park, enjoyed by all. perhaps a sign though of gentrification? as dem hipsters roll in, we shall see. thankfully de park is free fer Joe & Jane Big Easy!

lovely lil mountain lake. come fer de crispy air, fishing or... white pelicans! was here late June, bring yer wooly, free trade organic, adobe colored, handknit sweater, cuz night temp was 45°. muy yum_yum muy!

great spot rite by water. super close parking, family friendly, never crowded, super clean, lotsa gull wildlife, near giant live oaks, firerings fer fires, convenient to downtown OC. omg awesome sauce.
only wish I had mo' time. next time! wonderful space, lovely folk in the public sphere. impressed by book section in museum shop. call me envious! can't wait to darken their door again.

Storyland was probably 100X better than I expected. I have spent most of the later part of my youth living near Disneyland, and most amusement parks are pale in comparison; but not Storyland. In fact, it reminds me of a nicer version of Fantasy Land (a section of Disneyland). I was spoiled for a good part of my life as I was able to spent lots of time visiting multiple amusement parks throughout Southern California. So when I compare this to Disneyland, I am saying that as someone that is very particular when it comes to places like this. Storyland is really that good.

Storyland is such a great place for families to bring their children (all ages). It is very clean, the staff was extremely friendly, the rides were surprisingly well done. I was surprised by the attention to detail, and how well laid out the children's play area is... There is so much to do for a family with children.

We took our two children there today (3 & 7), and since we drove from the seacoast, we were there pretty late and didn't expect much from our visit. At first we spent a good part of our time in the kids area, where kids could roam and visit tree houses, meet Cinderella, etc. We thought that was great, and didn't realize they have so much there to offer. Whether you are going for simply a relaxing trip to walk around and let the kids loose, or you want to go on a few thrill rides, Storyland truly has it all. I will break down all the reasons this is such a great place to visit...

There are so many reasons to love this place:

1. They have a dog kennel. It's free to use, it's secure, and we had no problems leaving our Labrador Retriever there. It was easy to come out and check on her, and take her potty. This was one of the reasons we decided to go. We hate leaving her at home along when we go on trips. Since this is almost 2 hours away from us, it means our dog would easily be alone 8 hours or more, depending on how long we stay. Since she can come with us, it's less stressful for her, and convenient for us.

2. They offer tickets to come back if you get there a few hours before closing. This is a very generous policy and they have no reason to offer it, and I hope they continue this policy. It demonstrates that they care about accommodating guests that arrive late. I was very impressed by this.

3. The staff all seemed professional, and friendly; something I didn't see as much at other amusement parks in NH or Maine.

4. The food was not only very reasonable, but had great portion sizes, and very good quality food... Even the grilled cheese and fries were restaurant quality. I could honestly say, this was my first experience enjoying fast food at an amusement park. Did I mention the prices? They are more than reasonable.

5. The rides are great. Whether you are going simply to go on a few roller coasters, or want to sit around reading while your kids run around various playground or the water area, this is place to go for many different experiences. The park is very large, very clean, lots of area to cover, many rides, and is completely worth the price of admission.

I hope they never change... At least not very much. This has instantly become a family-favorite destination, despite the fact that we were only there for about 2.5 hours. It truly is that impressive of a place for families; which is exactly who this place is geared towards. We look forward to our next visit (sometime in the next few weeks), and I will very likely add to this review at that point to share my experience then. If you are thinking about where to go this summer, I can wholeheartedly recommend you choose Storyland.

This is by far, one of my favorite places that consistently impresses whenever I have visited there. When Iw as young, we used to go there for class trips. Later, when I was in college, I regularly would stop there anytime I was in Los Angeles, Hollywood, or simply on my way home from the beach.

For years, we lived fairly close, and had a membership (to support it), and would visit on a regular basis, a few times per month. My favorite time to come is about an hour or so before dusk, and stay until it's very dark. I could spend hours in this place, checking out the exhibits, watching the planetarium programs, or simply talking a stroll outside. This historical place will always be a fond memory for me, and a pleasure to visit when I['m in California.

Coming from California, this was one of my best experiences at a national park. If you are not from the area, be prepared for endless green trails, ponds, and gorgeous scenery. This is far less crowded than many of the other national parks I have been to out west.

There are lots of wildlife, and for those of you that want to experience nature, but don't have the ability to hike, there is the Kancamangus Highway, which is about an hour long drive, with plenty of scenic stops along the way to experience the marvelous scenery.

Make sure to pack plenty of fluids, and I'd recomend having some permethryn, and possibly deet or picaridin to protect you from the insects. Ticks are a major problem here, and lyme disease is not uncommon in these parts.

Joshua Tree was a wonderful experience when my wife and I visited a few years ago. We camped at a local event in Pioneer Town, and spent the entire day hiking through the trails of Joshua Tree. One of the greatest things was the serenity; though there was lots of rattling noise, which we assumed were bugs, or locusts, which we later discovered was rattlesnakes... That made our hike back into town a little more stressful, but fun nonetheless. :-)

If you're going during the hot months, be sure to have plenty of fluids, it is extremely dry, and if you are not in optimal health, it could be dangerous. In fact, even if you are in great health, be prepared to avoid any problems.

Great park for families. Like some of the parks of the area, the locals feel that they own the park. For example, I lived right down the street, nonetheless, if you went there and you weren't from across the street from the park, and people didn't know you, some people were a little snobby. My children were playing with some other kids and the parents actually said, "you don't know them, or where they live, so don't play with those children." Anyway, some of the parks in this area people can they get a little territorial, which is sometimes understandable.

This used to be one of my favorite trails, really convenient to get to if your local, and usually lots of parking. It seems the more people that know about this, the more crowded it gets, and the more likely you are to see Cheetos wrappers and water bottles throughout the trail, on the ground. This became far less appealing the past few years because of that. Nonetheless, it's a good trail, and there's not many other options anyway.

Nice place to visit, and support. Learn a little about history, engineering, and what Navy officers that rode this had to go through. Great staff and gift shop too. Word of advice, if you're visiting, take your time, and relax. If you try to rush and push through, you're going to make the experience less enjoyable for yourself and others.

We love visiting this place. They have great events for kids, and it's fun letting the kids go off and explore; there is so much to do for kids of all ages. It definitely ranks as one of our favorite spots in New Hampshire. It's clean, the staff is friendly, and though occasionally crowded, we have never felt it was unbearable.

Big open park, with a playground, and a large fountain area that kids can even go in. This is a great place to spend the day. There is a very historical area that we have enjoyed each time we have been there. It's difficult to find the bathrooms though, and you really got to be careful and remember where you parked.

Beautiful scenery, with the area to walk on the rocks, overlooking the water between you and this historic lighthouse. Like others have said, it would be great to be able to go inside, but that being said, it would lose its appeal, once it was ruined by unlimited foot traffic of tourists.

We had a great peaceful walk there, and spent a good portion of our walk with a family of peacocks. It was definitely a great place to walk, and enjoy the scenery. I would definitely recommend a stop here if you are vacationing in Hawaii.

This has always been a great park with lots of space, some playgrounds, and some trails. Sometimes gets crowded and people tend to not understand what trashcans are, but... that's pretty much southern California.

This park is great, lots of great activities, and one of the best places in the area to walk and enjoy the scenery. Figure out where the parking lots are before you get here, and you will have a much better time.
Excellent spot to stop by on your way to and from the pier. A large playground area, and plenty of bathrooms. There's also Hot Dog on a Stick, which is I think, the first one ever.
Great spot for climbing, exploring, and enjoying one of the best scenic areas in L.A. Nothing like an ocean breeze while you enjoy sitting on the rocks and looking into the sunset.
This was an amazing place to visit. We assumed we could get through the whole thing in one day, but quite honestly, it's one of these places that's worthy of an annual membership.
I remember we were not able to do the train tour, but I forget why. We did enjoy our time there, including the maze, and were happy about the whole experience.
Great park with amazing views of the ocean. Kids will appreciate the modern playground. As always, parking is limited. Park in the first spot that you find.
A bit overpriced, but you really can't experience this anywhere else. A great place to go with the family, or on a date with a loved one or some friends.
Fun place to stop, and lots of time can be spent exploring the Rocks, the river, and taking in the wonderful views of New Hampshire's White Mountains.
Great spot for a romantic walk on the beach, a bonfire with friends, or some time to walk and reflect on life. One of my favorite spots in San Diego.
Great Beach, was always one of my favorite places to go when I was younger, and especially enjoyed living there for years as an adult.
Fun beach with lots to do; keep in mind this is a touristy beach. Nonetheless, it is beautiful, and enjoyable as a tourist.
Nice Beach, but I wouldn't recommend it so much if you're a tourist. However, if you hate crowds, this is a better spot.
Great place to go. I've only been there for a few events, never did the tour yet, but looking forward to it.

Okay, first of all, how could you not write a four or five star review of this place?! This is definitely a world-class aquarium, and one of the best I've ever been to (You can't beat Shedd Aquarium and Georgia Aquarium, plus I gotta stay loyal to my local, aquarium, The Florida Aquarium).  This is a very unique aquarium, featuring pretty much only animals inhabit Monterey Bay.  I HIGHLY recommend that you purchase tickets online ahead of time because I feel that's important to be as efficient as possible when visiting this place.  Also, they do have a lot of feedings, trainer talks, and other programs throughout the day which are probably all very good, but I feel that if there's a time constraint, skip them because walking around yourself and seeing all the exhibits at your own speed are more than enough. The best exhibits at the aquarium for me were The Open Sea, featuring the ocean sunfish (A.K.A. Mola mola), hammerhead sharks, and a whole lot more, the Puffins exhibit is also great (I can never get enough of those cute puffins!), and the aviary.  For those of you who said in your review that you had trouble viewing exhibits up close because of the large crowd, for my experience, I first of all either waited 60 seconds or less for someone to move over or I just maneuvered my way through the crowd to get as close as possible.  Something that I didn't expect was to see so many wild animals outside from the Wildlife Viewing Station. I saw multiple sea otters, seals, could hear sea lions, and I even say a seagull with its chicks.  Overall this is a great aquarium and a MUST when you're in the Monterey area.

This museum is what I would consider to be modern, clean, and a good example of the kind of science museums we'll be seeing in the future. Why? Well first of all, this museum has a mix of live animals and taxidermy animals, as well as interactive science exhibits. So this place is kind of like a science museum/natural history museum/zoo/aquarium hybrid. Also, the museum is pretty open with high ceilings and a lot of natural lighting. The museum is primarily two floors, the main floor having views of the underground aquarium from above, and the African animals exhibit, which is mostly taxidermy with some live animal exhibits such as the penguins. The aquarium part, which is probably around half of the museum, was great, but not incredible like the Monetary Bay Aquarium, for instance. The museum part, which is mostly like natural history-type stuff is also great, but not as good compared to the Museum of Natural History in New York City. The rain forest exhibit was good and unique. It features all live animals native to fain forests and as you walk through the fain forest exhibit you go from the rain forest floor to the canopy. The special exhibit they had at the time of my visit (July 2014), Skulls, was done very well and featured skulls from a HUGE variety of animals.  As a quick recommendation, I suggest purchasing tickets in advance online just you can walk right in and avoid the line, even though when we went there was no line... Overall, I was glad that I chose to go this museum rather than the Aquarium of the Bay at Pier 39 or the San Francisco Zoo because like I said, this is kind of a mix of both.
likes: Hybrid experience (science, natural history, zoo, aquarium)
dislikes: Aquarium not as impressive as others
Natural history section less extensive compared to major museums

reviews_attraction.text: There is no need to look further for a good coastal park in California.  Point Lobos State Reserve has everything you could possibly look for.  They have trails more inland if you want to walk through the woods, steep trails and leveled trails, fantastic views of both the coast of Carmel and the Pacific Ocean, and wildlife everywhere.  We went here in mid July so the sun set at 8:30 and we got there at 8:00 - just in time for sunset.  As we started to drive deeper into the park we already started to spot dear on the side of the road in the woods.  Our first stop was at the Whaler's Cabin area and on the west side of the Whalers Cabin is the Cabin Trail. We started to walk up the hill through the coastal scrub.  It's mostly uphill and has a lot of stairs but the beauty is worth it.  From here you could see the Carmel coast.  Next, we got back in the car and headed over to the Sea Lion Point Trail. By then, the sun was getting a lot lower in the sky so it was difficult to see the sea lions off shore on the rocks but you could easily hear their barking. We could actually hear it the minute we got out of the car and started walking.  Here we were able to get excellent views of the Pacific Ocean and just as a warning, it was very windy.  Lastly, we drove over to Sand Hill Cove area located on the south side of the park.  Of course there were more excellent views and from this view we could see the coast south of Carmel and to the right the Pacific Ocean.  By then, it had started to get dark so we started heading out but we could have been there for hours.
dislikes: Difficulty seeing sea lions due to low light

reviews_attraction.text: I love Central Park Zoo. There are a few key things that make this zoo great: it's not too big, it's conveniently located in the middle of Manhattan, and most importantly, this zoo doesn't have your typical zoo animals. Now you might be thinking: Why is the fact that this zoo is small a good thing?  Well, most zoos I would say are pretty large and take up a large part of your day because you want to see the whole zoo and get your money's worth.  But with the Central Park Zoo, it's smaller and you can see the entire zoo in about an hour - as long as you don't see any of the shows and just walk around at your own pace. At a typical zoo, you'd probably see lions or tigers, at the Central Park Zoo they have Snow Leopards. Think about it, when was the last time you saw a snow leopard? If you're reading this and live in the mountains of Nepal, you don't count! Rather than Chimpanzees or Lemurs or Spider Monkeys, they have Snow Monkeys.  They're very cute and you don't see those too often! The penguin exhibit is good.  First of all it's extremely air conditioned - can you guess why? Also, it seems that almost all zoos and aquariums these days have the South African penguins but this zoo has multiple species of penguins from Antarctica. Also, this zoo has a great rain forest exhibit with a free-roaming sloth and lots of exotic birds and a really cool tree-cutter ant exhibit.  Also, throughout the zoo's many exhibits they have many species of exotic ducks!

This humble "museum" was truly a highlight of my trip to California considering that I'm very interested in the mystery of Bigfoot.  I first discovered this place from watching an episode of 'Finding Bigfoot' on Animal Planet (spoiler alert: they don't find Bigfoot!). Anyway, I already knew that we were planning a trip to San Francisco and Monterey and so after seeing the museum on TV I knew that we now had to go to Santa Cruz too. Boy was I happy that I went.  I really liked look at the old Bigfoot memorabilia that this guy has collected over the years and I liked talking to the guy who worked there. It was pretty funny because when I asked him if he personally had ever seen Bigfoot he said yes but then when I asked to share his experience with me he wouldn't.  I liked the souvenirs they were selling. I bought two pins a t-shirt, and a 11" by 17" poster of the history of Bigfoot.  I was very interested about what the guy was telling me about Bigfoot and how people in other countries accept the fact that we're living along side an ape-like man.  I honestly could have stayed longer to look at everything and talk to the guy more.  Two things I recommend you look at while there is the casts of Bigfoot footprints (they're very cool) and ask to see a model of the supposed Bigfoot tooth that was found.  Also, I encourage you to donate some money because this place does not charge admission.  This is definitely a place that I would return to.

I would say that this is a top five in terms of things to do in San Francisco. In my opinion, it's the best way to get a good view of all of San Francisco. Because it's circular, and windows go around the tower, in one direction you can see the downtown office buildings, another way you can see Fisherman's Wharf, and another way you can see The Ferry Building. To get to Coit Tower, I took the Filbert Steps.  It can be strenuous to walk up all of those steps, but just take a break to breathe every few minutes and it's especially not too bad considering that the weather in San Francisco is always cool and breezy. Speaking of breezy, most of the windows at the top of Coit Tower are shut so you're just looking behind glass. One or two of the windows though did not have the glass windows blocking so you could stick your head through and feel the super refreshing breeze. Coit Tower doesn't have a roof so while you're up there you can see the clouds moving really fast from the sea breeze. We did have to wait on line for about a 30 or so minutes, not only because there is one elevator, but there is limited room at the top, and because Coit Tower itself was very crowded with what seemed like almost all tourists. I wasn't too bothered by the long line because you got to look at the nice murals of San Francisco's history that wrap around the side and even though there's no air conditioning, San Francisco has usually cool weather.

This place has so many good reviews that it doesn't even need my review - but what the heck!  This zoo is so huge that I don't think it's humanly possible to do the entire zoo in one day. I guess you just have to prioritize on what you want to see the most. I'll start your prioritizing with my favorites:

The most unique, not your everyday zoo things include:

A great, indoor aviary with lots of exotic birds

A Madagascar area with many interesting species of primates, etc. (From what I remember it had an odd smell in there - you get used to it in a few minutes).

They have two other aviaries as well and they aren't as big (Dang they have a lot of birds there!)

The Wild Asia Monorail is a MUST DO because not only is it relaxing to just sit and be in the shade, but you get to see a lot of animals you can't see otherwise - once when I rode the monorail there was a Red Panda in a tree right at the same level as the monorail - so cute! :)

The Mouse House is great - they used to have a nocturnal building (which was one of the ultimate things there) but it closed due to budget cuts so they have some of the animals from the nocturnal exhibit in the Mouse House plus the cute little mice

By the way - make sure to ALWAYS be on the lookout for freely roaming peacocks walking around - they come pretty close to you because they probably get fed by the guests (even though you're not supposed to

Disclaimer: I was only here for about 25 minutes

When driving up the coast of California, one of our stops was here, at New Brighton State Beach.  We drove straight to the parking lot near the water and went down the stairs to the beach.  We didn't plan on staying long.  We just wanted to check out what the beaches were like at this area.  This beach overall is very nice.  It sits on Monterey Bay so the there were minimal waves.  It was like the Gulf of Mexico or a lake.  Looking to your right or left, you're greeted with mountains and trees and nice, mostly natural, scenery.  Opposite the water are these extremely large cliffs that we are at that the bottom of. At the top of the cliffs are trees and where the parking lot is.  The cliffs were the most unique part of this beach because you could see some of the trees' roots going down the side of the cliff.  The main negative with this beach and the reason why I probably wouldn't choose to spend the whole day here is because the sand had a TON of seaweed/kelp and some dead seagulls (ew!). Overall though it was nice to make a quick stop to check out this beach especially considering that it's right off the highway.

This is one of the best and biggest zoos that I've ever been to. They have such wide variety of animals that practically you could name an animal that you've seen at a zoo before and most likely the Los Angeles Zoo will have it. I went here in the summer of 2010 when three major areas of the zoo were closed for construction: The LAIR (indoor reptile area), the elephant exhibit, and the the Rain Forest of the Americas. Despite this, I still saw more than enough animals. I was there for hours and couldn't even finish seeing everything. Some of the highlights of the zoo for me were the seals and sea lion exhibit exhibit because of the large underwater viewing, the gorilla exhibit because they have two troops in multiple viewing areas, the chimpanzees because they were performing tricks because they used to be in the circus, the koalas because you don't see these too often in zoos in America, the aviary because it feels like you're walking up the side of a mountain in a jungle, and the meerkats because you can see what them through the underground burrows. I highly recommend the LA Zoo to both locals and visitors, and if you're a zoo/animal lover this zoo is a must!
likes: Large underwater viewing (seals and sea lions)

reviews_attraction.text: It's a little difficult to think of what to say about Lombard Street because well, it's a street. But, Lombard street isn't just any street, that's why it so many reviews - and is one of San Francisco's most popular tourist destinations. The best part about seeing Lombard Street when you're on vacation compared to anything else is that you can be at Lombard Street for 20 minutes or less and be completely satisfied. The curvy part of Lombard Street is one block and can easily be walked in about five or less minutes. I recommend starting at the bottom or top - does matter which is first and then walking up or down. Make sure to check out the view from different angles as you go up or down because you can see in the distance you can see both Coit Tower (which is only about a twenty minute away walk) and the San Francisco - Oakland Bay Bridge. You definitely could drive down Lombard Street (one way only) which is a fun experience but walking it is much better because you can stop to take pictures at the top, bottom and all the beautiful landscaping along both sides.

What a great park!  Covering such a large area of land with so many trails you could easily be here for days and still not be able to explore everything.  Because we were only here for a limited amount of time. We did the circle that goes around the redwood grove near the gift shop.  It was so nice. It was nor crowded at all, especially compared to Muir Woods. We were alone on the trail most of the time. Be on the look out for banana slugs and deer. We saw deer but no banana slugs. But when we went to the Fall Creek side of the park we saw banana slugs and make sure to check out my review for that as well. The trail is very shaded. It's so amazing to look at the immense size of the redwood trees.  There's so much to see and do in this park.  You can on a train ride and maybe even spot some locals riding their own horses throughout the park. Even though you have to pay to enter the park it's worth it goes towards a good cause and don't forget - if you go to another part the same day you get to go for free!

How can you not like MOSI?!?!?!? I've been going to MOSI since before I even started kindergarten, and I still like going there today. The best part of MOSI to me is the IMAX dome theater, which is like no other movie theater that I've ever been to. Because the screen is curved and is from floor to ceiling, it makes it feel like your actually in the movie. They have a lot of hands-on, interactive exhibits that are also educational and interesting. MOSI always has special exhibits, over the years they've had a lot of good ones, including the Titanic exhibit, the BODIES exhibit, and lots of others. Once a month, MOSI has a "Sky Watch" at night in which people bring their own heavy-duty telescopes and point them at various groups of stars and planets - it's very interesting, and the best part is that the "Sky Watch" is free! While you're there, I also encourage you to check out the butterfly garden, which is really nice.

This park is so big, I was only there for about a half an hour so I don't even know if I have a right to write this review but here it goes... First off the parking lot I used which was on Felton Empire Road was pretty small and almost full when I was there.  When you start walking it goes down hill and then levels off. We walked for about 25 minutes.  The entire time I could hear the rushing water of the creek so we walked till we could actually see it.  On the way someone pointed out a banana slug to us and then on the way back I spotted one.  When you're by yourself at this park, it really makes you feel like you're in the middle of nowhere with zero civilization and if you waited long enough you would encounter Bigfoot. Overall the park was nice but if you're only visiting the Santa Cruz area I recommend the main Henry Cowell Redwoods State Park rather than the Fall Creek side.

I had a great time on Delray Yacht Cruises.  I was researching online for something like this in Delray and this is the only one around. We went the same week as Christmas in 2013 so the area was definitely crowded. We were told to make reservations ahead of time which was a good idea because it was packed.  The cruise was very nice.  You could hang out on the second floor's air conditioning, or you can hangout on the top floor's scenic, 360° view. The cruise I went on was about 2 and a half hours and went south on the intercostal. For the trip south, I guy talked through the speakers and was very informative. It was pretty nice to see all the AMAZING mansions and pools that all these people have on the water.  Unfortunately, we didn't see any dolphins or manatees but we did see some nice birds.  The staff were very nice and attentive.

I can't believe that I'm giving a park a three star review but to me, this park isn't really anything special. The two main issues for me is the fact that there is little to no shade, and that the park isn't very natural.  What I mean by "natural" is that the park doesn't have much foliage or wildlife.  This park is pretty centrally located so it's good for festivals and other kinds of events. It have a nice view of Hillsborough River, but this part of Hillsborough River is not the prettiest to look at. I guess the best times to go to this park would be for a walk when it's either cloudy or cold out, or if there's some type of event going on, but don't go out of the way to come here.

This design of One World Trade Center is one of my favorite tower designs in America. Its shape of the tower is iconic and at the top is the spire which can light up any color for special events, holidays and more. One World Trade Center is home to One World Observatory which is one of my favorite observatories and is a fantastic experience to do. One World Trade Center is home to a large space for private events. It's difficult for me to think of a more impressive venue in New York to have a private event. The views from One World Trade Center are spectacular - no matter the direction or height the view is outstanding.

Mini golf is good for any age, and Congo River is no exception.  Probably the best part about is that when you're walking around it feels like your in the jungle.  You're provided with a scavenger hunt and if you find everything at the end they give you coupons for next time.  I also like always seeing the alligators.  You can feed them but I prefer to just feed the fish and turtles because it's less expensive and just as fun.  Congo River is the type of place that you could go to more than once but because it's entirely outdoors, it can be pretty sweltering most of the year (even though it's mostly shaded).

This is probably the most unique thing that I've ever seen at a park in my life.  As an animal lover especially, this was one of my "musts" when going to Golden Gate Park during my trip to San Francisco over the summer. When I was there in the middle of the day, the bison weren't too active, but I still enjoyed seeing them. If they want, the bison can come right up to the fence and be very close to you. I read that the San Francisco zoo maintains and cares for the Buffalo Paddock here. Overall, I recommend checking out the bison even for just a few minutes because of the uniqueness of this.

The Clearwater Marine Aquarium is much more of a rehabilitation center than an aquarium. It's very small which is why there is plans for a new multi-million dollar new aquarium in a new location nearby. The dolphin presentations are every half an hour which is good but still not worth it. I suggest going to Mote Aquarium in Sarasota, The Florida Aquarium in Tampa, or even Lowry Park Zoo in Tampa.

I love going to zoos and seeing wildlife.  Naples Zoo is no exception.  I've been coming here for years and they have definitely expanded.  The zoo is planning another big expansion so expect even more to see here.  The shows are also great here to see some animals that are not always on display.

Though admission is pricy, the Chihuly exhibit is definitely worth checking it out.  I've never seen any thing like Chihuly's artwork.  There is a movie at the entrance about him and his artwork which is interesting and worth seeing.

Miami Seaquarium has a lot of potential. The facilities are very out-dated and the exhibits need to be expanded to make the animals more comfortable.  Not the best aquarium.  If you're visiting Florida, SeaWorld is much better.
The Seabird Sanctuary is free and always different. It's right on the beach and also has a gift shop. I love seeing the variety of birds but sometimes the enclosures can be a little dirty.
My all-time favorite beach!  I could spend days here! Go down to the north most part where there is an inlet. The sand is nice and soft. The beach is clean.
This museum is much larger than it used to be and has a wide variety of art work. The museum also has some good traveling exhibits and a great gift shop.

Clean. I chose a disabilty site. Picnic table, campfire pit, and separate standing grill. I like the paved part to the picnic table from the pad which an rv'er (excellent dump and water filling area but need own hoses) would stay at. This provides more stability while walking. It's smoother with my rollator. Sites are arranged so neighbors won't look into your site. Open tall trees. Nice privacy in back of #92. Trails hook up at campground. The showers are all located in a separate area. One disability type shower can easily accomodate a wheelchair. There is a fold down bench in the shower. Separate dressing area bench. Two hooks on door. Token payment machine is on the wall away from actual shower. Small trash can on the wall in the dressing area. Rubber mat in dressing area. Large mat could accommodate wheelchair for further stability. Very nice.

I enjoy this area I access from the frontage road next to I-680. It's not only a refuge for birds and other local wildlife it's a portal for duck hunters. The hunters actually help manage the duck population. There are different types of ducks they are allowed to hunt for. The quantity caught varies from one type to another as well. I like this hunting idea of management so I don't have to try my abilities of crawling through mud for a bird for Christmas dinner. I've talked to some of the hunters. They love it. Too many ducks we might be killing them in commuter traffic as they go splat into the car windshield. OMG.

The OHV staging free Blackwood Campground is primarily a beautiful tent campground. I stayed in my 23' RV just fine. I came in the last day of Race 200. It was snowing in September! Those diehard racers wouldn't give up! It was very quiet when they left. There is no cell signal there. You have to drive out from Blackwood Campground back to the lake. There is a park lakeside of the highway. One building of two vault toilets. No water. Trash disposal available. Single lane road from main road to campground.

It's now the site of Bodega Bay's farmer's market. Also trails to explore. We actually had lunch in the truck in the parking lot. We had a bit of shade. It was a nice enough stop as late afternoon there was a bit of traffic on hwy 1. Good to see people out. But, COVID counts may go up. Stopped at the head too for a nice sunset. My cat, Skipper, was with us too. He was trying to chase flying seagulls through the auto glass. Lol

I came over across the hwy from Sugar Pine Campground. I was tired, but I managed to take in the generator building. From a distance I thought the water tower was a carriage house. It looks like a simple house with a pitched style roof. I managed a distant peek, from a distance, at the circular part of the mansion. I'm going back in the spring as I believe they close for the winter.

Actually on old Highway 1 which was repaced because it was sliding into the ocean. Even some sites are no longer usuable due to erosion. The greatest thing is being right next to the crashing waves of the ocean. Sturdy tables. Two vault toilets. Many camp sites. We saw tents, cars, small RV's, and huge motor homes. Parallel parking. No trees. Enjoy the vista!

Use the campground. Seen lots of people use the trail to day use. I'm handicapped and use a cane or rollator. Some camp sites are good for RV's as then have water and power. Two dump stations. Draw back I find in most camp ground showers is they are sheltered, but open to the elements. I want lots of hot water from their free showers.

Excellent info about history of Donner party pioneers, Chinese workers struggles, other local history, and some artifacts. Excellent gift shop. Kind and knowledgeble rangers. Protection rangers carrying firearms are not orientated to friendly directions for park guests. Only to enforce rules they believe are applicable.

I really loved this place. Crashing waves. Easy trails. I laughed at a donated bench in honor of a volunteer because it sits at the edge of the cove alone. I sat and felt the breeze on my face. I heard the crashing waves below me. I wondered if it had been used as a doghole during the very active logging late 1800's.

I grew up going to Donner as a kid. I liked the campground. I had my space and privacy even though there are no barriers between sites. The day use was nice. Several picnic sites by the lake. Small boat rentals. Swimming area set aside. I hadn't seen since the late 1970's. Some changes were made. Enjoy.

Spent most of summer 2019 in the area. North of Truckee off hwy 89 at Cottonwood campground and Sage hen which is a ways back. Blackwood Campground off of Lake Tahoe at hwy 89. I really enjoyed sage hen even though it's down a bumpy dirt road. My camp site was next to a beautiful meadow.

Several beach areas to access. One requires one lane road access. Go slow. Watch for other cars. Wait for the road to clear as there is a clear view to the other side. It is well worth the effort. Two beaches across from each other offer closeup variety. Beautiful sunsets. Enjoy.

I enjoy this park especially for the ocean breezes coming in off the Carquinez Straight and the awesome view with beautiful sunsets. There are many benches, flushing toilets, boat launch, fishing piet, playground, walking paths, picnic table, and two small beaches.

Nice local city park with pool. Pool has indoor year round pool. Offer classes for fee. A Summer outdoor pool features large shallow pool with slide and other features in pool which kids enjoy. I think there is an outdoor lap pool too.

We had a great campsite. There are drawbacks. No water for restrooms. Portable toilets available. Good camp store. Fun gift shop. Enjoyed despite not physically able to hike. Busy park. Many groups camping from schools and others.

Nice park for short perimeter walk with older exercise stations. Good picnic park with concrete tables & benches. Small playground which kids live. Lots of dogs walked. Owners are good with poop p/u. Next to school.

Nice all year round. Redwoods are comfortably enveloping. Quiet at night. Usually good people. Clean bathrooms and coin operated showers. Nice day use. Several trails. Nearby are several vineyards. Near Cloverdale.

Nice place to relax among the oaks. Has been used as an environmental teaching facility. Can see those areas of class area next to picnic tables. Small garden. Trails. Local peacocks are nice attraction too.
I like going here for weekday midday picnics. Decent public restrooms. Good parking for even a small rv. Some shaded spots. Clean picnic tables. Trees. Birds. Play ground. Ball park nearby.
Nice. Access to long trails. Clean gravel parking lot has some picnic spaces. Clean handicap vault toilets. Have to pay to even stop in parking lot for picnic and to use the toilet.
It is even nicer at twelfth street park if you know the shipping history of Benicia. I like to imagine the ship building going on 100 years ago. Beautiful sunsets. Nice dog walk.
Beautiful place to explore nature from the fishing bridge to Rush Ranch on down to the boat launch. Awesome sunsets. Birds of prey to deer to lots of cows.
The coast is always awesome. Northern coast has more crashing waves. Several pull overs along the way. Several historical interest spots.
Last time the water had receded. The boat launch was open. Time before the rains were raising levels enough for a great release of water.
Being a baby boomer I got to see this in it's hey day. It's a nice place to stretch your legs and gather a bit of history.

There’s PLENTY of stuff to do at this park.  Enough to stretch out to 3 maybe even 4 days and still not get bored.  Cabins, tubes for sale, grilling meats, LOTS of stuff available (all within the park) if you forgot something.  There’s also a convenience store right outside the front gate.

They even have mini golf and a permanent food truck inside the park for crying out loud!

The check-in experience is a little different than most state parks I’ve been to.  You go inside the office, take a number and stay in an enclosed waiting room until they call your number.  Then and ONLY then, may you enter the room where the staff take your payment.  I visited in December, and it took about 10 minutes to get in, so I can only imagine it’s much slower during the busier spring and summer months.  It’s a large park, but the road signage is decent and does a good job directing you to the different camping areas, attractions, trails, etc.

Now, on to the hiking experience!

I must say the trail marking is decent.  I never got lost and always knew which trail I was on.  They use yellow shoe prints painted on the rocks every once in awhile to let you know you’re on the trail.

Highlights - you MUST check out Old Baldy Summit. It’s a short but challenging hike.  Expect a 600ft elevation increase within a half of a mile - so that tells you it’s pretty steep!  But the views from the top are SO worth it!

The Crystal Cave Trail - challenging in a few areas, but it leads to a cave. The cave isn’t that impressive though.  It’s about 30 feet deep and wide.  Easy to get in and out of - I even saw a couple of 8 year old kids in there.  I’m claustrophobic when it comes to caves but I was able to handle it for a couple of minutes.  Just not a lot to see there.

The Bridges Trail is also considered challenging and includes a few ledges that might make you a tad nervous.  But if you just finished the Old Baldy Summit, it gives you a good vantage point to see view what you just accomplished.

Old Horse Trail - wow.  It’s pretty rocky and on narrow ledges a couple hundred feet above the trail below.  It’s pretty intense.  This is the kind of stuff that makes me nervous and gives me nightmares, LOL!

Old Entrance Road Trail - it’s paved, and parts are a little steep, but don’t waste your time on it. Based on the map description, I was expecting to view some awesome old stonework built by the CCC back in the 1930’s.  I hiked all the way out there and wasn’t impressed at all.  Take the Old Horse Trail above this trail instead.

Pro Tip - the ONLY place I got cell signal was at the top of Old Baldy - and not even for miles around the park perimeter.
dislikes: Disappointing historical sites (Old Entrance Road Trail)

reviews_attraction.text:
Everyone knows of the tragedy that happened at Pearl Harbor that early Sunday morning on December 7, 1941, but the devastation REALLY hits you when you visit the memorial for the first time.

Entrance to the visitor center and tickets to take the quick boat ride out to the memorial are free.  You can reserve your tickets online the day before you visit but you cannot reserve them the day of your visit.  It is first come, first serve.  I was there on a weekday so luckily, I was able to walk up and get my free tickets.  The time printed on the tickets is the time that the short documentary movie starts, it is not the time your boat leaves.  Go watch the movie first, then walk out the back doors and get on the boat to the memorial.

Once you arrive at the actual memorial, you will see a solemn tribute to the 1177 crewmen killed aboard the USS Arizona and the remains of over 900 are still entombed in the sunken ship.  The names of all killed are inscribed in a large marble wall.  An interesting fact is that a few dozen survivors from that day chose to have their ashes interred with their former shipmates when they passed.  U.S. Navy divers actually bring their ashes down to the ship and drop the urn into an opening in the ship.  This tradition began in 1982 and continues to this day.  There are less than 10 survivors still alive.

The waters in the harbor are only about 40 feet deep so you can see several parts of the USS Arizona above the water line and some just below the water line.

This is a very sacred memorial, so please respect it and keep your kids in check.  There really isn’t much to do out here for the younger kids, so you might want to think twice before bringing them out there.  It is very moving and a great thing to teach the young ones about but just keep in mind it is a memorial and everyone needs to be respectful.

Out of the four missions on the south side of San Antonio that make up the World Heritage Site and the National Park System, I would consider this one a medium sized one, just a little smaller than Mission San Jose.

Just like the other missions, this one is still a fully operational church.  Take your time looking at all the details inside the church.  Remember, these were built in the wilderness frontier in the first half of the 1700’s.

The sanctuary has a beautifully arched ceiling, and if you take a look toward the ceiling at the back of the church, you will notice a small window.  On a certain time and day of each year, the sunlight shines through this and is directed on the painting of Jesus Christ which is hung above the altar.  Yes, they knew enough about astronomy way back then to know when the sun would be in that certain place and enough to build the church, so the window and the painting were in exactly the right place.

In one of the side rooms, take special note of the painting on the ceiling and the tops of the walls (see my photos).  The red lines and blue lines represent the “Red Path” and the “Blue Path” that the American Indians of this region believed they has to follow (Google for more information).  The sun with the face of the moon within it also has a good story behind it.  Notice the face in the moon is the face of a Spaniard.  Remember, it was the Spaniard Franciscan monks who built these places with the intention of converting the American Indians to Catholicism.  This painting had something to do with that.

Lot’s of paved and natural “rugged” trails within our city limits.  Some of the paved trails are steep, so beware in case you are using a wheel chair.  Very clean park and very natural.

The Red Oak Trail is a MUST-DO (not paved) – the scenery changes so dramatically on this trail.

Finding the trailheads is confusing.  When you first drive in, you are drawn to a large pavilion area, but the trailhead is not there. Head west just a bit and look for the kid’s rock wall playscape and the bathrooms and find the trailhead there. Walk in a few yards and you can get a trail map – or you can print a better one from the SA Parks and Rec website.

Cell coverage is available pretty much everywhere in the park but the signage letting you know which marker you are at, etc. is lacking.

The Hillview Natural Trail and the Red Oak Trail are really awesome, but some areas are pretty rugged and steep.  I would not take pets on the entire loop.  Parts of it are ok for pets, but not if you are doing the entire loop.

Lowest area is 852 feet above sea level and the highest point is 1233 feet above.  Each of these points are on the Hillview Natural Trail.

Two story wooden observation tower locate on the Cedar Flats Trail just off of the Hillview Natural Trail.

Restroom located near there as well (no running water but it is a permanent structure and was clean).

Near the park entrance, there are several pavilion areas available to rent and also rest rooms with running water.

They have a small playground and rock climbing wall near the entrance.

This review is for the hiking trails only.

I’m not going to complain a whole lot, considering it’s only been four years since the wildfire that impacted this park.  I’m impressed that they have almost all the trails open for hiking, and they are in good shape.

You can hike anywhere between .1 mile and 6 miles if you get imaginative with your trail selection.  Although the trail map indicates Pine Gulch is “challenging,” I would rate as “moderate.”  It’s not rocky at all; there are a couple of inclines that might be challenging for some, but they’re not too steep, and not rocky.  You can do all of the trails out here with regular tennis shoes, and you probably don't need a hiking stick.

Trails are mostly dirt, and just a *little* rocky.  Northern sections of the Pine Gulch Trail are sandy, but it’s tightly packed, so it’s not like you are trudging through sand on the beach.

Most of the trails are in full sun, so be cautious if hiking in the summer.  There are a few sections in the southern section that survived the fire and have some tall pine trees.

As of November 2019, the lake is low.

All in all, not a bad place to hike in the fall/winter if you are nearby, but I wouldn’t drive out of my way to hike here.

Pro Tip – part of Pine Gulch Trail has been closed since the 2015 fire, so it’s no longer a loop.  The park maps are updated, but if you are using an online hiking app, it might still show it as a loop.

Yet another well-kept secret San Antonio Park (this one is actually a Wilderness Park).

Located near UTSA, this is an awesome park to walk through the wilderness without driving for an hour.

It includes several paved walking trails with benches along the path, but you can also go off the beaten path and try some more challenging trails.

This was my first visit, so I stuck to the Main Loop Trail for the most part and although it had a few rocky inclines, it wasn’t overly rugged.  I’ll try a more challenging trail next time.
