There are two working windmills pumping water that are cool for the kids to see.  One of them is a short easy walk for the kids.  The other one is way on the other side of the park – probably too far for the really little ones to get to.

Make sure you have a QR code scanner on your phone before you go. They have marked LOT’s of native plants and trees with QR codes, so you can find out more info about them.

Some picnic tables, a pavilion, and a bathroom with running water near the parking area but don’t expect anything after you get on the trail – take plenty of water!

Free Wi-Fi also available at the main trailhead and in the common areas near the parking lot – kewl!

No pets or bikes allowed and don’t try and bring a stroller if you are going to get off of the paved trail. I saw someone carrying their stroller – it’s just not possible to roll it because of the terrain.

WOW!  At 505 acres, it is one of the largest AND the newest parks in the city of San Antonio.  I think it is only about two years old and is in GREAT shape.

There are two full court basketball courts with a nice surface, a large splash pad, a very nice skateboard/inline roller skating court, bathrooms with running water (also a couple of port-a-potties), a large pavilion available, plenty of walking trails (some paved some gravel) a couple of playgrounds, some stationary workout stations along the trail and so much more to do (including a zip line!)

The walking/biking trails are about 5k and take you up to two hills with GORGEOUS views of the Alamo City. You can even see the downtown SA skyline from one of the hills.  One of the hills has a couple of picnic tables and an art sculpture that is partially shaded (see photos).  The trails to get to the top are steep but smooth, easy walking.  I saw many bikers walking their bikes up the hills because of the steepness.  Might be a good workout for the runners and bikers out there.

Dog park right next door but not sure if it you can get to it from within this park. You might be able to but not sure. Also, a frisbee/disc golf course and a connection to the Leon Creek Greenway trail – although it is a short trail.

Free city provided Wi-Fi in the main areas of the park.

Plenty of stuff to see and do here.  The three paid attractions are the Pineapple Express Train, the World’s Largest Maze (it’s a hedge maze), and the Plantation Garden Tour.  You only have to pay if you choose to do one of those attractions.  Otherwise, you can hang out and do a little tourist shopping, or grab a bite to eat.

The food - I only had a pineapple ice cream cone which was REALLY tasty.  Lots of other ice cream choices too.  Check out the picture of the $26 pineapple split. I think it’s big enough for 6 people to eat! The rest of the food looked on par with what you would get at a theme park (overpriced and mediocre) so I skipped that.

The lines for food and the ice cream are really long but they move at an “OK” pace - not too terrible.  The inside of the shops are extremely crowded.

If you need to take a nap, I recommend the train ride.  The gentle rocking to and fro coupled with the easy listening music is enough to put you to sleep for a good 15 minutes - I had a great nap!  There isn’t really a whole lot to see on the train ride anyway.  It takes you near the pineapple fields and some sugar cane.

The maze is the best part - there are 8 landmarks that you must find and mark off on a ticket they give you.  It's best to pair up in teams and see who can find all of them first.  It's so much fun!
dislikes: Long lines for food and ice cream

reviews_attraction.text:
Don't forget about the other trails in the park. There are several more besides the Summit Trail to the top of the rock that everyone does.

The Loop Trail is about 4 miles long (the Summit Trail is .6 (6/10) of a mile but STEEP) and takes you all the way around the rock and also Turkey Peak, Little Dome, etc.  It's good for a really great view of the domes from a different perspective that I had never seen before.  Most of the trail is pretty mild, wide, and even, but about a quarter of it is actually single person wide and a bit rugged.  A couple of places are even confusing on where the trail actually is so be careful on the the Loop Trail if you are taking kids or pets with you.  Several water refill spots on the Loop Trail and a couple of bathrooms even - but don't expect flushing toilets or sinks, etc.

I know they are trying to keep it natural but the trail signage could really be improved.  I wanted to try a couple of different trails that were on the map that I was given but the signage and the printed map were conflicting and confusing so I stayed on the Loop Trail.  Do some research before you go if you want to be adventurous.

There is a playground, primitive camping spots, camping spots with grills and tables, etc.

BEAUTIFUL, BEAUTIFUL area that we are so lucky to have!

I bought tickets online for a discount and they had a pickup and drop off point right in front of my hotel in the marina area. It couldn't have been more convenient.

The drivers are very friendly, and the buses are very clean and comfortable. I never had a problem getting on a bus as others have said. They seem to run on time, and although most of the buses were almost full, I was never turned away and always managed to find a seat.

The tour covers a decent area of San Diego and will also get you out to Coronado Island and back.  The only downside I have for this tour, is their operating hours.  If you are trying to squeeze as much as possible into one day, you will not get to see a lot.  I recommend a two day pass if you want to take your time. The buses don’t run very late. I think the last one left Coronado Island at 4p or 5p.

Pro Tip - if you want a dollar discount, open up a chat session with one of their support agents. Just ask some random questions, and you’ll get a coupon code for $1 off each ticket.

What I didn't like -  they made you wear a sticker on your shirt to get on and off of the bus.  I got off at one stop near Petco park and wandered into a seedy area to check out a brewery.  I wasn't overly thrilled to advertise the fact that I was an out of town tourist.

It's a nice nature preserve, and well managed.  If you are looking for an easy peasy stroll through the woods with a couple of views of a small pond, this is your place.  When I visited, the only trails that were open were Blackjack, Cottonwood, Cicada, and Green Dragon - cool trail names, right?  :)  You should be able to squeeze 4.1 miles in on these trails.  Not sure about the rest of the trails since they are closed until sometime in February 2021.

The trails were EASY PEASY and flatter than a pancake.

Things to do:
- You can bring your own kayak and paddle through Beaver Pond.  There's a kayak launch site near the road at the trailhead for what's listed as the "Paddling Trail."

- Near the intersection of the Green Dragon and Cottonwood trails, there is a pretty cool historic log house and other outbuildings to check out.  You can go into most of the buildings on your own, but the main log house is furnished with artifacts from the late 1800s and is only available for pre scheduled tours. (check llela.org for the deets!)

- Even if you aren't kayaking, you can get a sweet view of Beaver Pond by hiking along the Cottonwood trail

It's currently $5 per vehicle to get in and they are not accepting cash at this time.

Porta potties at each trailhead.
dislikes: Limited access to main log house

reviews_attraction.text:
It’s been about 10 years since I have visited the zoo and although the admission price is more than I recall, they have definitely made a LOT of improvements. I didn’t even recognize the place!

The giraffe exhibit is really cool because you can now walk onto a deck that is as tall as the giraffes and you can actually feed them.  Even if you don’t pay extra to feed them, you are able to walk on the deck and see them face to face – it was AWESOME!

The Lory exhibit is also pretty cool.  You walk into this aviary and if you pay a couple of bucks, you can feed the birds – they will actually land on your shoulders and arms to eat.  One in our group didn’t have any food but 3 or 4 of the birds landed on him as soon as he walked in the gate for some reason.

Parking is the same as it always has been – kind of tough to park in the lot in Brack Park, but don’t forget there is parking under the highway on the opposite side of the zoo.

Signage could be improved – it’s hard to find your way to the exit when you are leaving.

A very awesome tour of a wonderfully kept WWII era battleship.  It is moored in Pearl Harbor, but it was not there during the December 7, 1941 attack.  However, this historic battleship is where the Japanese Instrument of Surrender was signed in Tokyo Bay on September 2, 1945.

The ship is actually located on the base, so if you have military ID, you can drive to it.  Otherwise, you can take a shuttle from the “World War II Valor In The Pacific National Monument” (AKA Pearl Harbor Visitor Center AKA USS Arizona Memorial).

Cost to tour the battleship is $5 which includes an informative guided tour around the deck.  You get to see and stand at the exact spot where General MacArthur and other officials signed the Japanese Instrument of Surrender.  Very historical spot.

After the tour of the deck you are free to venture below deck by yourself and see the mess halls, the sleeping quarters, officer’s areas, and more.  The ship is in really great shape and is well worth the $5 to check it out.
likes: Access to historical sites (surrender signing spot)

reviews_attraction.text:
It’s smack dab in the middle of the city, so don’t expect lush landscapes or anything like that.  Although there are trees and some grass.

There are plenty of picnic tables to eat at, and lots of benches to hang out on and enjoy being outdoors.

There’s a crushed granite walking trail that goes around the edge of the park, but the park only sits on two city blocks, so it’s not really a great place to hike.  More of a hang out and have lunch and enjoy the day type of place.

Also a decent playground for the little ones.

You can read some historic info about Ben Milam here, and check out one of the oldest former burial grounds in San Antonio.  Check out the blue bench area on the east side of the park and read the information and memorial for all those that were buried there.

It’s literally across the street from Santa Rosa Children’s Hospital and within walking distance from the courthouse and city hall, so it’s a good outdoor lunch hangout for those that work in the area.

#SA300

Beautiful park, but very difficult to navigate the trails for the first time visitor.  Trail markers are EXTREMELY lacking.  I came across more than one split in the trail where there was no signage, and then another split in the trail that had a sign with arrows pointing toward each trail, but it didn’t have the NAME of the trails.  It’s like, “duh, I see that the trail splits in two.  Why do I need a trail marker to show me this?”

Most of it is wooded and shaded, so that's a positive.  There are a couple of places where you can cross the creek and get to the other side - the water is only a couple of inches deep on these parts.

Parts of it are an off leash park, so your dogs can run free.

If I had the time to wander around I would have, but I didn’t, so I ended up cutting it short because I was concerned I would get too far out and not have time to get back to the trailhead I parked at.

I'll try it again when I don't have time constraints.

Really a lot more fun than I thought it would be. A very intense and well designed set of mirrors in a maze dimly lit (but not scary for the little ones). They have flashing lights that change colors on the floor. You have to find your way from the entrance to the exit and it is more difficult than you would expect.  I was VERY impressed by whoever designed and built it.  The mirrors REALLY play tricks on your mind.
You can go through it as many times as you want for the entire day since they stamp your wrist.
Price includes unlimited access to their laser vault where you try and move over and under laser beams without setting off an alarm before getting to the other side.

They have a coupon on their website but you have to PRINT it out, they will not take a picture of it from your phone. It's only a dollar discount per person but every bit helps!

Unbeknownst to me, water lilies don’t bloom in the winter, so I only saw four or five blooms, and not many lily pads either.  According to signage, the best times are March through November.

Even though my visit was a bust, the online photos look like it’s an awesome place when they’re in bloom.  The areas for the lillies is quite large, so I think you’ll be impressed if you visit during the right time of the year.

It’s a small park with a couple of short trails to walk along the creekside, but the trails have a bit of trash on them.

Park in the Presbyterian church lot across the street (but not on Sundays you heathens!).

P.S. - there’s a rose garden in the same park, but apparently those don’t bloom in the winter either, what was I thinking???

There are paved trails, natural trails and some biking trails that are maintained by DORBA.  Bikes are not allowed on the natural hiking trails, so they have to stick to the “designated off-road bicycle trail.”  Dogs are allowed on the paved trails and the natural trails, but NOT allowed on the DORBA biking trails.

If you are hiking as a pedestrian on the biking trails, you should walk against the bicycle traffic so you don’t get run over.

Some parts of the hiking trails cross the creek, but as of January 2021, only one of the four bridges were open.  Lots of construction going on here - mainly for erosion control, so have some patience with them folks.

Hiking trails are considered “easy” with very minimal elevation changes.

Pretty decent natural area.  The Red Oak Trail is pretty much paved but if you want to get on the natural area, go out to the Bear Grass Trail.

All the trails combined are probably less than 2.5 miles, so don’t expect a whole lot. But the Bear Grass Trail is really good for bird watching and listening. Also, very natural, so you get to see Texas like it was way back in the day!   Just don’t expect a rugged hike if that is what you are after.  It is fun, but not challenging.

All in all, it’s a great park and not too busy – kind of a hidden gem in SA – so, SHHH, don’t tell anyone else about it!

Water fountains and bathrooms with running water can be found at the trailhead.

Awesome, breathtaking views like you wouldn’t imagine. It’s very rocky down below at water level, so lots of waves crashing against the rocks and spraying water in the air.  It really makes for a good scene.

There are several opportunities to be a daredevil and crawl out onto some of the rock bridges.  Parts of the trail are rocky, but it’s not grueling if you stay on the main trail.

There’s also an albatross habitat at the point, but I didn’t spot any the day I was there.

Even though I missed out on the albatross, this was an AWESOME experience.  Pictures don’t do it justice - you have to hike this trail in person to experience it!

Really great place for bird spotting and other wild life such as a couple of alligators if you are lucky, water snakes, and turtles.
It is FREE to visit and mostly consists of a decent boardwalk type peer that walks you out over the water and the marsh.  There is also a three story tower at the end of the pier with telescopes in the top.
On certain days early in the mornings, they have guided tours - but I have never attended one.  I have just done the freestyle tour.

VERY large park – maybe the largest in San Antonio. Plenty of sports fields (baseball, soccer, etc.) and plenty of paved jogging/walking/biking trails.  Also, many off road trails for mountain biking.

Plenty of trees and shade on the trail we were on today.

Picnic pavilions available some grills, etc.

Lots of deer in the park. They are very used to people so you are usually able to watch them from about 20 feet away and they don’t run away.

Beautifully maintained buildings and grounds.

Make sure you go into the church if mass is not being held.  This church is open all the time.  It’s a smaller church than the rest of the missions, but it is breathtaking inside – don’t forget how old these missions are.  It’s really incredible that they are still standing and more importantly still a working church with regular mass schedules.

Beautifully maintained buildings and grounds.

Make sure you go into the church if mass is not being held.  This church is open all the time.  It's a smaller church than the rest of the missions, but it is breathtaking inside - don't forget how old these missions are.  It's really incredible that they are still standing and more importantly still a working church with regular mass schedules.

A short walk south from the Pearl riverwalk entry point or you can also enter from street level at the Camden Bridge or Newell Bridge. Take some time here and look for some hidden items. Look very closely into the waterfall.

Amazing point to see military jets fly low through the valley! I witnessed the same F/A 18 fly by 3 times. It was worth the wait, you just have to be patient. You won't see a military jet fly lower than you anywhere else in thee world. The road driving up from Panamint Spring is legendary too. There is a rocky trail that you can walk or drive your car to the farthest point with even better view of the valley. Be careful with your cars though, it could get damaged due to the extremely rocky trail.

A must-visit if you are visiting Mount St. Helens National Volcanic Monument. There are plenty of parking spots at the observatory. Plenty of interactive information that talks about the 1980 volcano eruption. Remember to buy your day pass or annual pass for national park at the visitor center. There are daily ranger talks and a short film that talks about the volcano every half an hour. If you are hiking at the park, remember to take a trail map from here.

Unless you are a hardcore aviation, missile or military buff, it takes quite a bit of effort to get into the Museum. You need to do a background check at the entrance of the active military base. It could upward to 1 hour to get it done. However, the museum has a lot of information on missile history and development since Rattlesnake anti-air missile is developed here. However, it is a great little museum you won't see anywhere else.

Amazing view but be prepared for traffic jam and wait for parking spot. You have to be very lucky to get a parking spot in this crowded place. There are usually volunteer stationed here to help answer questions. There is also restrooms, gift shops and a coffee shop at the basement of the Vista House. I also recommend walking up to the upper floor and also walk down the path to the side. It is very beautiful here and a must visit.
likes: Available facilities (restrooms, gift shops, coffee shop)

reviews_attraction.text:
The drive to this location was not too difficult. There was ample of parking spaces and the hike down was not too difficult. This place is extremely windy so be prepared. It was a nice place to sit and just view the scenery.

The road east from here will get very difficult with lots of one-way and pulloffs.

Very tough hike due to elevation gain. If you have weak body or knees, I don't recommend it. There is a secret spot that gives you the best view of the waterfall. Go right when the trail splits into two. Once you start going down in elevation, you are just a few steps away from the viewpoint.

Beautiful area but very crowded. It is impossible to find parking if you are on the Historic Columbia River Highway. I recommend sticking or driving on the I-84 and just park at the Multnomah Falls Park on I-84. There is plenty of parking there and it is just short walk away to the Falls.

A must visit and most popular spot in the park. Regular parking is above this spot so you will have to hike down from the parking lot. There are shuttles from nearby visitor center that will drop you off closer to the tree. Disability parking lot is also closer.

Awesome spot to visit during the day to see the valley and night to see the stars. Bring fleece and long pants as it gets cold and there are bugs that bite. Check with local visitor center to see the time of free guided star talks.
Must visit if you are in the area or you are interested in history. One of the great tragedies and injustices in the history of our country. It is important that everyone visit and learn about it.
Not much to see and it gets unbearably hot without much shade. Be careful hiking this trail. I had to tell people to go back to their cars as they didn't bother bringing any water with them.
Much more interesting than the submarine. You don't get to see or even be on a working ship from WWII! This is a must visit for military fans. There are lots of see on this ship.
Beautiful scenic trail that can be driven the entire way. Don't forget to get a paper map and guide at the entrance. There are many spots to stop and take a look along the way.
A must stop for visitors to the Death Valley park. There is free water refill station here. It is also important to get an idea of the park from Park Ranger to stay safe.
Good luck finding parking around the beach. There are several walkways that will bring you to the beach from the town. Beautiful and legendary beach. Water is very cold.
Parking is extremely limited but you can park on nearby road and walk to the hiking spot. The hike up isn't too bad. The steps are well paved. The view is spectacular.
You can drive up to the summit with two wheel drive car. I did it with a Nissan versa. However, if there is ice or snow. You better have 4wd and snow chain or tire.
Amazing National Park. It's a good change of scenery from your maui beaches. Highly recommend visiting for everyone. You get to see another side of Maui.
A must visit for Death Valley National Park. Great for stargazing too. Remember to visit when it is not full moon to see all the stars.
Nice little National Historical Park to visit if you are in the Bay Area. The world's oldest National Park Ranger works here too!
Not as crowded as Yosemite or Sequoia so it is a great getaway place. It offers great canyon view and plenty of trees as well.
Be careful of road condition as I got a flat tire because of it. The beach is vast and very windy. Beautiful place to visit.
Important to stop by and ask questions. It has great exhibits that show you how Yosemite was created by natural forces.
A little bit disappointed with the view. Not much to see as there are more interesting places to visit in the park.
The most famous and best vista point at North Cascades National Park. A must-visit if you are in the park.

Absolutely love the trails. They are paved and mostly shaded so it's really nice when you have the kids or dogs with you. The little lake has a fishing pier and the park has bathrooms that are pretty clean. The only complaint I have is parking. The lot is fairly small so most people have to end up parking on the dirt road, which can be a headache on busy days.

Stunning!! Everything about this place I love. My daddy told me how much he loved it when he was young and used to come with his parents. I didn’t get to go with him before he passed but better late than never. The elevator had just started working again so we didn’t have a long hike to the top. Come early and see everything!!

Absolutely a hidden gem. I went in just for a visit but left with a TON of information. William was my guide and he was VERY knowledgeable. I learned a lot and even got recommendations for future visits to places of my interest. The fort was still in construction, so I look forward to visiting again when it is completed.

This place is amazing! We did a day trip from Charlotte. Lots of parking, we got there around 10am. Bathrooms at the beginning but aren’t in use right now due to COVID. The first part is easy and flat, and then becomes more moderate. My five year old did great. We had lunch on a big rock near the top.

We really enjoyed our camping weekend here. It was our first time on Keowee and the views are definitely worth the trip! However, there is a lot of rocks in the water on the edges which makes it hard to swim easily, especially for my little ones. Well maintained though.

Love this place!! It is a very naturalistic walk/jogging area with a beautiful lake in the middle. It also has a fenced in dog park area for the furry friends to play! There's no playground but you can fish in the lake, so bring the kids and make it fun!

This place is fantastic. It’s an old bridge turned into a long walkway of some beautiful displays of plants and flowers. I LOVE the creativity of the gardeners, it’s really well put together. It’s definitely worth the stop if you’re in the area!

This place is a must visit!! We parked along the street and walked in. They have boat rentals, which I thought was cool. Lots of beach shops and restaurants. We especially loved the sea lions at the end sunbathing on the lower level. So cute!!

LOVE! I do wish that they had bike trails but the hiking trails are beautiful! There are picnic tables around the pond and in the open area with big trees, but no grills. I love that they have signage informing visitors of history. 💗

Loved this place!! So much to see, we have to come back because we didn’t get to it all. The outdoor displays are so awesome, and it’s totally kid friendly. You won’t regret spending the day here with the fam.
A hidden gem!! The falls are gorgeous and we happened to stop in while the water wheel was on. It made for some great photos. They do have restrooms but not food. So pack a lunch and enjoy the view!
Such a beautiful place, serene and well maintained. We stopped in with our boys and they loved walking the trails with all the maps and historical info about the Revolutionary war.
The falls are absolutely stunning! But know this, be prepared for a hike! There’s lots of stairs and incline so wear good shoes. Gorgeous natural falls, definitely worth the trek.
Most libraries aren't this fun! My toddler had a blast and family storytime was so fun! They even have plays and stuff for pre-teens too. We will definitely be back again.
The castle is insane!! It’s so immense and beautifully created, it’s worth the visit alone. The Tasting was a bit pricey for me, but the wines were delicious.
Beautiful place! A great mix of history and nature. We didn’t camp, just came to visit for the day. Lots of spaces to picnic or fish around the lake.
What a gem. We ate lunch down by the waterfall and there we many other families taking advantage of the area. I loved the old ruins and garden.
What a gem! The building is the original and it’s packed full of history and cool items from the past. Staff was knowledgeable too.
The beach area is nice, wish it was bigger. They have clean restrooms and changing areas so it's worth the few bucks to enter.
Absolutely love this park. The sprayground is so much fun for the kids and they have tons of different playground equipment.
The walk is perfect and the scenery is beautiful. Something for everyone here, especially for the nature lovers like me :)
Lots of little shops and places to eat. It was very relaxing scrolling through the little town. Love the waterfront too!
This view, man!! It’s super cool and unique add to the nature scene. Good little hike to get there, but it’s worth it!
Love this place. Toddler Tuesday is where it’s at for a good price, and every display is touchy-feely. We love it.
I have never seen a view like this. You can see so much!! Plenty of parking, so don’t miss this!!

This place is a true hidden gem.  It's hard to imagine any other park in California with Sequioias more accessible than this one.  Pull off highway 4, pay entrance fee, drive a very short distance, park the vehicle, take a few steps and you're there on the trail.  If hikes are more your speed, they have that too at the South Grove.  Drive the park road for about 15 minutes, park the vehicle and start hiking.  It's not the hardest hike, but it's not the easiest hike either.  It's much more remote, so very few services are available.  Additionally, there are campsites available for those who like to wake up in the outdoors.  A pretty awesome State Park...

The smell of their restaurants cooked meats from the outside was marvelous.  I ordered a 2 meat BBQ platter, and I was disappointed with just a 3 bone spare rib slab, and a brisket slice the size of a thick piece of bacon for around $14.00. Yes it came with 2 sides and I selected coleslaw which was not dressed (raw cabbage mix right out of the bag), and potatoes salad (which was pretty good).  I don't think I would order The platter again, and I would stick to the brisket sandwich instead.  The casino is what you would expect.  Slot machines and the smell of cigarettes.  Lots of cigarettes.

It is truly an out in nowhere type of place.  Very few signs of any kind of life, but if you look hard and careful you will see a different story.  The visitor center is very modern and nice.  The staff there are real friendly and helpful.  Not too large, but good sized for the area.  It can get very hot in the Summer, so if that is not your thing, try Spring or Fall.  Be aware of the road conditions where portions are just a gravel road.  The Southern entrance road is all gravel and would be ideal for dirt bikes and 4 wheel drives.  Use the hwy 373 entrance instead.

Very nice centrally located large city park.  It has fountains, statues, open space, views of the city, public artworks and many other things of interest.  The only knock is, in the center of the park where the commuter train system runs right through it.  It seems very practical to have it here, but it is not that pleasing to the eyes and ears compared to the other nice things at the park.  Helpful hint - If you go to Buckenham Fountain as it gets dark, you can see the fireworks at Navy Pier on every Wednesday and Saturday between Memorial Day and Labor Day.

I would say, if you're near Houston, the space center is a must.  Not too many places around the world have anything like this (maybe Russia and that's it), so it shouldn't be taken for granted.  The tour of the facility is interesting, but seeing the Saturn 5 rocket is the highlight of this experience for me.  The Saturn 5 at Cape Kennedy is displayed in a much better way, but at Houston it's still very impressive.  Something that big flying into space with only a little more than 60 years since the Wright Brothers first flight, is mind blowing.

Of all of the Presidenial libraries I've been to, they tend to promote the positives and down play the negitives, and this library is no different.  That being said, I found it an interesting place.  With his childhood home on the premises, it gave perspective on President Nixon's upbringing.  The general setting is not too much over the top for the most part.  It's location is isolated from much of the comotion surrounding it, and the library didn't feel like a farce,  which is something that can easily happen.

This zoo went through a recent expansion adding what is known as the California Trail.  Basically more than doubling the previous Zoo size.  Bald Eagles, Condors, Cougers, Black Bears, Grizzly Bears and more.  Keep in mind this in addition to what was previously there, like Tigers, Lions, Elephants, oh my and more.  With the expantion comes a higher price too, but you get to see so much more as well.  An added bonus is the views of San Francisco are pretty awesome from this new portion of the Zoo.

A novel approach to a restaurant.  5 Dollar, 10 Dollar and 15 Dollar menu offerings.  Meals at 10 Dallors or more come with a drink.  For some of their offerings, it's a pretty good deal, like the Parmesan Chicken with Fetichinni is a very large potion and worth the 10 Dollars.  However, items like the Chicken Fried Stake sandwich was somewhat small for the price.  The building is split into two sections with the bar and gambling hall on one side and the restaurant on the other.

As beaches in California goes, it's not what most people would expect.  No blue/green water, big waves or fine powder sand.  Instead, it gets you a pretty nice view of San Francisco area, and a nice place to cool off on a hot day.  The surrounding grounds are spacious enough to stake out your claim of independence for you and your family.  It can get very busy at times, so there can be a level of frustration to finding parking related to this place.

This is one of the most premier aquariums in the country that's located near one of the best rugged coastlines in California.  It has many exhibits, with some sea life you might expect and some you would not.  You can touch the rays, and watch the sea otters play.  However, their deep blue aquarium is the most unique.  It makes you feel that you're viewing through a glass submarine in the deep ocean.  Pretty spectacular.

The cavern and waterfall are interesting, but with the volume of people being processed, it becomes obvious Ruby Falls wants to make as much money as possible, and not provide the best experience to the visitor.  It's difficult to hear what the guide has to say while you're trying to understand what you are seeing.  Rush you in to see the falls (which is very nice) and rush you out to the gift store, just like Disney.

For those of you who are not into fine art or who would rather spend your money else where in the city, the de Young Museum has a hidden treasure for you.  Their observation tower, which is free of charge to anyone who desires to go to it.  Just simply tell the attendant at the entrance that you want to go to the tower.  You will be pointed to the elevator, and off you go.  The views are very nice.

A smaller place than you might imagine it to be, but it's nice as a piece of history.  The fact that it is right in downtown makes this more enjoyable with easy access to the River Walk and places like restaurants.  I found it very interesting that a very high percentage of the caualities from the battle of the Alamo were from Europe and not North America.  Not what most people would expect.

If in Waco, this place can be interesting.  They have small arm artifacts and other items as well.  I did find it interesting that their photo hall of fame of agents past, were not too diverse.  Very white male centric.  I guess the Texas Rangers aren't as diversified as the baseball team in Arlington with the same name.

This city park has almost everything.  Water park, little kid play ground, soccer fields, skate park,  baseball diamonds with fences, Bocce ball court, basketball courts, walking paths and even cricket field and practice area.  Yes, I said a cricket field.  This park has picnic areas too.  Like I said, almost everything.

A modern take on an outdoor public fountain.  Where Buckingham Fountain is spectacular to see, Crown Fountain is much more interactive.  Kids and adults playing in the water on a hot day.  Not too bad if you ask me.  It's located right near the Bean (Cloud Gate) art display, so it's easy access from mass transit.

We walked the main trail to the top and back.  It's about a mile and a quarter each way with an incline most of the way to the top.  Is it strenuous?  Not for people that are active and their bodies are acclimated to hiking.  For those who are not, yes it can be a little strenuous.  The good news is it's short.

A very exclusive location to see and hear nature.  At the visitor center there are only 50 parking spaces to limit traffic, so if you can get into it, you should feel very fortunate.  It is a very special place, and I'm very greatful to Laurence Rockefeller for this gift.

Located in the middle of downtown, where open spaces are NOT unique in this area, but it is still a welcome sight.  It's basically  an open area covering underground parking that has a few statues and some grass areas as well.

A nice little museum with an eclectic artifact collection.  There are out buildings that are interesting too.  I can't imagine spending more than an hour or so here, but it can be an interesting hour or so.

A fun place to visit when in Las Vegas.  It's not fancy, but fun for sure.  Games of all types, and you don't feel ripped off when you leave.  If only you felt the same way at the casinos on the strip.
It's not very large, but the grounds are kept up very nice.  I can see why people might like to have photos taken there, like wedding photos and other portrait style photos.
Really nice State Park with people dressing in period clothing, old style crafts, activities, food and drink.  A great place to take kids, so they can explore some.
A little pricy for what you get, but it's Monicello.  An iconic place after all.  If in the area, I would say it's a must see.
A phonomemnal art glass museum and showroom.  Some of this work is hard to believe that it's glass at all.

We've been here on several occasions for both fun and birthday parties.  Overall, the place is a lot of fun with tons to do for the kids.  They have mini-bowling, which is great for the younger kids, full size bowling with child bumpers and ball ramps, a climbing wall, laser tag, a bouncing room with inflatables, and a large arcade area.

The inflatable area is great for the kids --they simply love it (yes, so did I --well, I had to take my daughter on there, I had to ensure it was safe.  The outcome of that? --it kicked ass!!).  There are around 6-7 large inflatable devices all of which have ramps, slides, and other obstacles.  There is also a smaller enclose one for younger children.  At the end of the large room there is a small area  where you can sit and watch the kids from the outside while eating/drinking --which is nice if you don't feel like being in the trenches.

The mini bowling is only $2 which I thought was very reasonable.  I did think the full sized was a bit on the expensive side, though.  If I remember correctly, it was $40 for 2 adults and 2 kids both under 5.

The location has a small cafe inside that serves a variety of food from pizzas, salads, and hot dogs to coffee, pop and alcoholic beverages.  The food isn't priced too bad and it almost tastes like food.

As you can probably imagine, this place can get quite loud with a ton of kids running around like lunatics.  Whenever we've been, we're typically there 2-3 hours on a weekend afternoon, which is plenty of time for the kids to exhaust themselves and enough time for you to loose your sanity.

The venue is very clean.  When you use the arcade or other activities, it doesn't look and feel like that nasty Chucky Cheese on the off side of town that probably hasn't seen a good cleaning since its grand opening.  Everywhere is kept neat and tidy by their army of staff.

If you've never been here, and have kids, give it a try; its a lot of fun.  I will disclaim that this review is only for the fun 'kid side' of the place.  There is also another side to this that has a huge fitness center what I haven't ever used.

This was a pretty cool trail. First impressions were this why is this a moderate rating?!? It starts off with nice flowy trails, slight inclines and just a nice walk in the woods. That was the Chestnut Oak trail --just a pleasant walking spot. The the other connecting trails are where the moderate rating comes. The Occoneechee Mountain loop was pretty cool, better inclines and a bit more strenuous. Literally, all the trail systems were pretty rocky, though well defined and nicely maintained.

It had rained hard for two days prior to my walk and the trails were as dry as can be, they have a great run off so it wasn't muddy at all.

If you're looking for more adventure, there is some fun scrambling around the over-watch. There are many 'strong' warning about doing so, but if have any scrambling experience, they aren't that challenging. It's predominantly made up of shale so it's not all that stable, and the granite is extremely slick --I may or may not have attempted it :) That was clearly the highlight of the walk, and pretty much why I went. Overall nice trail system. Easy parking, outhouses at the trail head, and very few people.

I thought this place was pretty cool.  A nice restaurant tons of parking and picnic spots, and beautiful roadway up to the summit.  Cool gift-shop at the top, and the mile-high bridge was pretty cool to experience with stunning, panoramic views.  Definitely a great place for large groups, family outing and the like, though it's certainly a tourist trap.  Now, that said, the entrance fees were ridiculous, and that's the only reason this is being marked a two-star.  It cost $90 for four 5 of us, two of which were small children.  I don't recall the cost per-person, but it's not per car.  Is it worth seeing, yes, but you can get better views up at Table Rock and it's free.

Defiantly one of my favorite trails on the east rim of Linville Gorge. Hike isn't too bad, but can get tricky toward the summit with packs and the narrower trails. Without packs it's a quick, heavily wooded hike and a decent incline as you rise. Amazing views of the gorge on a clear day and a eerie feeling when is summit are engulfed with clouds and you can only see 10 feet ahead of you. Limited camping spots but plenty of trees for the hammock campers.

Place is pretty decent.  Well planned and designated by floor, telling a cool story.  The layout can be somewhat confusing, though they have some pretty awesome artifacts, stories and belongings to some great African Americans.  Extremely nice restaurant in the basement, with incredible food, though pretty pricey.  Couple gift shops, and cool building architecture encapsulate the  experience.   Enjoyed he museum, but not on my next list for a DC trip.

Nice location with plenty of parking.  Has portable bathrooms and easy to get to.  Can get quite congested on soccer game/practice days.   The fields aren't that great, and certainly not as well maintained as other area fields.

There are four fields at this location. The fourth being located behind the very back parking lot, number two to the right as you pull in, three back by the woods and one running parallel with he back parking lot.

This is a pretty cool pier and great spot for watching the sun go down.  Been here several times and love it.  It costs $9 to park which seems a bit excessive, though that does give you a single admission to the pier.  You can rent fishing gear from the local store which also includes the fishing license if you don't have one which is cool.

Great spot, not overly busy and worth paying even though I complain about it.

Wow.  Such a well designed museum.   It starts off lighthearted and intriguing, and gradually tells an incredible story of rise to power, failures, successes, and eventually goes into the atrocities which occurred during this time.  The story is so well told using mediums of all kinds —artifacts, video, still images, recordings, letters and much more.  Very well thought out and delivered.  Must see.

I'd heard so many incredible things about this place so we finally visited last summer.  It was a pretty cool place.  Several soccer fields, nice lake and a beautiful pathway around, small amphitheater, tons of benches and places to pitch a blanket, and a lot to do for kids --parks, etc.  There are other trails leading off the park which we didn't explore.

Absolute fantastic memorial.  The layout and design in wonderful.  The attention to detail in the soldiers faces and bodies are just incredible.  You can’t get too close, but you honestly don’t need to, he larger than life-size platoon easy easy to see from he boundary.  Frank Gaylord truly did an incredible work of art.

Awesome spot —just love this place.   It’s free to get on pier if not fishing which is awesome.  Staff are friendly and polite, awesome gift shop, and fishing passes with gear and licenses available at gift shop.  Awesome views and great spot to catch an early sunset.   Love it!  Easy, free parking immediately at pier.

Very cool place.  I was extremely impressed with the size of the park, beauty of the red rocks, and cool layout of trail system --very well thought out.  Great parking, awesome photo ops, climbing with permit, and bathrooms available.  Perfect spot for a quick walk, not strenuous at all, and fun for the entire family.

Great location and tons of fun.  Zip lines, climbing and bouldering wall, great white water rafting, kayaking, paddle-boards, mountain biking trails and so much more.  This is a great place for anyone who loves outdoor adventures.  Great restaurant, cool store, and great staff.

Really enjoyed this place.  Walked around and had a lot of fun.  The lighthouses were cool, and park in general was nice.  It wasn't overly crowded in July.  there is a side beach with rocks which was fun for scrambling exploring.  Easy parking and clean restrooms.

Had an opportunity to go here recently and was pretty cool.  I was quite surprised. I've known about the falls for some time, however,  didn't' realize how pretty they were.  Fantastic spot to go grab ice cream and a coffee and enjoy the water.

Great trail.  Walked several times and always love it.  If you keep going 3 miles or so longer, you'll reach the Golden Gate Bridge.  It's not clearly marked, but use Google maps and you'll find the way, it's a great walk.

Absolutely incredible.  They did an amazing job of this memorial.  He attention to detail is fantastic, and tribute just beautiful.   Simple, but extremely powerful.   Definitely worth a visit if in he area.  Incredible.

Played here a few times and loved it every time.  Fun for all ages, and never all that busy.  Reasonable price, and very well designed.  Extremely well maintained and great atmosphere.  Easy parking, and polite staff.

Yet another awesome memorial design.  As always, great representation and meaning of the location, and incredible views.  From this spot you can see the Washington monument, and Jefferson memorial.   Cool spot.

Pretty nice trail.  Very short, though really nicely done.  Perfect if you're looking for somewhere to walk a dog.  This location has several picnic tables, ample parking, water fountains, and bathrooms.
Awesome facility.  Extremely well maintained, clean and well planned.  Soccer fields are fantastic.  Has a small cafe/food bar which is cool, nice restrooms and plenty of parking.
Such a cool place.  Amazing for kids of all ages, and adults alike.  Fascinating exhibits, most pertinent to the local North Carolina area.  Highly recommend for a fun day out.
Cool and fun place to visit for all.  We took the water taxi over and explored around.  Fun place for kids to experience the carrier and sub in additional to some cool history.
This was a nice little spot.  Not too busy, and a ton of fun.  Fantastic views from the top and fun to boulder.  Great place to bring entire family.
Great beach, probably the best on the island I’ve found.  Beautiful in the morning. So quiet, hardly anyone around.  Love it.

(Translated by Google) Rival Red Rock canyon, to him from the Strip 20 minutes drive, and in this Valley Park 1.5 hours drive (which och wounds). 50 million years ago there was a sea on this place! There is a visitor center where they tell how this canyon was recreated! At the entrance you need to pay $ 10 per car, they give out a card with all points of interest! A lot of rest area and furnishings (toilets, eria picnics, everything is there).
It takes 1.5 hours, if you go through the canyon almost without stopping !!! Altogether takes 3 hours! Views while driving through the canyon change every 10 minutes! Of the minus -None of the cafes in the canyon itself or in the district-so sandwiches and water with you are required!
There were a lot of police officers, so you need to monitor the speed (35 miles per hour - speed during the whole movement at the entrance to the canyon)

(Original)
Соперник Red Rock каньону ,к нему  от Стрипа 20 мин езды , а в этот Парк Вэллей 1.5 часа езды(что оч уматывает ) . 50 млн лет назад на этом месте было море ! Есть визитор центр ,где рассказывают как воссоздался этот каньон ! При въезде надо заплатить 10$ с машины ,там выдают карту со всеми точками с достопримечательностями ! Много rest area и обстановочек (туалеты,пикники эрии-всё есть ).
Времени занимает 1.5 часа -это если ехать через каньон почти не останавливаясь !!! В общей сложности занимает 3 часа ! Виды во время проезда по каньону меняются каждые 10 минут ! Из минусом -Ни одной кафешки ни в самом каньоне ни в округе -так что бутерброды и воду  с собой -обязательны !
Полиц машин встречалось оч много -так что надо следить за скоростью (35 миль в час -скорость во время всего движения при въезде на каньон )
likes: Facilities & Services: Visitor center, rest areas, picnic spots, toilets

This place East Rim Overlook, Steens Summit Trailhead is just an amazing place. The High desert is just an awesome place to ride through. Roads are great for traveling “a little narrow, (for me) in some spots but the sights are just unbelievable. Wear sneakers or hiking shoes, etc., going up to the summit, anything else could be a bit challenging. Great place for all, the air is definitely a bit thin at over 9700 ft. An absolute must see. The Quaking Aspen trees driving thru this area are none other than striking, and lovely to hear whispering in the wind.

Returned here after 37 years. Death Valley is an amazing place to visit, whether it’s Badwater Basin, furnace creek, StovePipe Wells, the artists pallet Scottys Castle the sand dunes or Dante’s view. The views of the valley are spectacular. Scottys Castle was closed this time, but we thoroughly enjoyed it our last time. It will open again soon, and perhaps we will return to this amazing place and see the renovations.

Great place to just hike. Trails are easy to walk nothing to horrible and the views are spectacular. I’ve taken my camera for a walk they the forest on several occasions, however this time our tag along friend “my daughters chihuahua”, joined us. He was enough to watch along our trip, so no photos to share this time. Great picnic area and a public restroom available as well.

Beautiful morning spent at the Tracy Aviary and Botanical Gardens. It’s a great place for family, children can easily get around and view each of the showcases. The bird show is well worth going to, you may even get called upon to assist, the kids usually get a kick out of that. Great place to spend a Sunday strolling around and relaxing.

Fantastic waterfall. Great place for a hike. Great place for families. A little walking involved but you can really decide how far up the trail you want to go. Great gift store before you head up or after you’ve viewed. Clean restroom and also a kiosk outside for coffee with several tables and chairs for sitting and just relaxing.

Spectacular views today at Hells Canyon. The cloud cover cleared over the canyon so that we could enjoy the vibrant colors. Beautiful place, great experience for young and old, family or just by yourself. Picnic benches located here along with some trails. We came and just took in the view from the overlook.

Sunrise Trail was a nice trail to hike, it was a bit muddy in some spots but it could have been much worse, and frankly what’s a little mud When your here to enjoy the hoodoos and spectacular views. So we made the best of it. 2nd time in six months, and hopefully we’ll be back.

Glad we took the time and meandered today in Salt Lake City. What a spectacular city. Went into several buildings including the Tabernacle. Quick stop into the conference center which seats 21,000 people. Salt lake temple is a marvel as well as Assembly Hall.

Fantastic spot to stop and have a bite to eat or just a quick snack while visiting Kings Canyon National Park. I’m a huge fan of water falls and this spot was just terrific. Walking was not bad, and rock climbing wasn’t to bad near the falls themselves.

This was such a beautiful spot to just stop and enjoy. Just admiring the bridge from where we stood was beautiful. It was raining, but none the less breathtaking. The Oregon coast has much too offer, the sights no matter where you stop are marvellous.

Wachusett mountain was spectacular today. Who says you have to ski, I spent half the day just sitting on the deck outside looking at the mountain. Relaxation at its best!!! My family had fun on this glorious day on the slopes and I enjoyed watching!

Great place for hiking, saw many people hiking the trails. There were even people climbing the rock. You can actually see people in my photos. Which I find very fascinating to watch. Nice place for a family picnic. Restrooms were clean as well.

We had a delicious bite to eat at Tony’s a crab shack and then did some touring around Bandon South Jetty Park. The sights are great, mesmerised with the waves and strength of the Pacific Ocean. Seeing another lighthouse was a treat as well.

Great place to visit with family and friends. A limitless walking involved but well worth it. Thanks to places like this, as these raptors from the wild deserve a chance at life. Thanks for the work you do! If I lived here I’d visit often.

The Arches National Park is a must see for all. The trails are spectacular and the views are breathtaking and outstanding. Some trails are more difficult than others, wear comfortable shoes “sneakers” and bring lots of water.

It’s a short hike, with a lot of stairs. Well worth the hike because when you get to the falls they are beautiful. There are beautiful spots to stop at along the way with a few benches to just sit and take a breather.

An interesting overlook in an area in Canyonlands National Park, Island in the Sky where mining existed. Road is used, for off road vehicles, but we didn’t see any while we were there. Spectacular Views.

Great place for hiking. Trails are pretty easy to walk and you walking along the river. The white water (River) is just crazy fast. If your an avid kayak fan, this would no doubt be a great place to go.
Saw a falcon here today! Pretty cool. I have never seen one up close, and this was the closest I was getting to this one.  Great place to do some walking and catch some amazing sights.
Beautiful area along the Oregon Coast. The sights are just magnificent. Haystack Rock was just another one. This 235 foot rock is very accessible by foot at low tide.
Great place for a hike with kids. Trail isn’t too bad, a little steep but really not awful. The falls are beautiful to watch. The water is so powerful, yet soothing!
Great area to tour around, sights are fabulous whether it’s the observatory tower or taking a stroll thru the beautiful garden. Great historic site for family fun.
The Moab, just amazing. I honestly can’t wait to visit this area of the United States again. These amazingly tall rock formations are so spectacular.
Glacier Point, my favorite spot, the eastern entrance In Yosemite Valley, breathtaking views, just unbelievable. Half Dome is just a must see!
Loved taking a selfie with Humphry Bogart. The closest I’ve been to a movie star. Great place to visit. Displays were very well done.

The beach hikes from the parking lot are the best.   Roughly 4 miles of beach to hike where there is no driving and thus very few people.   If you hike north to the point, it is very likely that you will not see anyone for the last couple of miles.   If you can time your hike for low tide the tidal flats at the point are expansive, but when exploring keep track of the incoming tide.

Note: There are white poles marking the Snowly Plover nesting area in the dunes.  The plover is listed as endangered.  This means one must stay down by the shoreline during nesting (Mar-Sept).

I just completed the hike (Jul 2018) and the eagles are numerous.  Not sure how this effects the snowy plover recovery?  Noticed quite a few of lost crab pots from the winter season and sand dollars.

Being alone on the point feels, how I would imagine it, to being on the moon (except for the sand dollars and driftwood).  If you are not one to hike 8 miles round trip but want to see the leadbetter point for your self, it  is possible to drive to the point during clam digs (but you will not be alone).

The museum does a good job of providing the full context for the JFK presidency and this event in US history.  The museum was full when we were there and the reaction of the patrons added to the experience for my children.
It was nice to show my kids this part of US history to provide them the context.  I think they left understanding that JFK was the boomer version of their Obama.  I hope my children will not take public service for granted nor the impact of the alteration of a US presidential election result.

The fish viewing center sits inside the Wildwood Recreation Area.  There is a cascade streamwatch trail of which it is part.  The trail is paved and winds along the Salmon River with lots of view points, secluded picnic areas and bathrooms.  The fish viewing center is not on the Salmon River, but rather a small creek feeding into the river where juvenile Salmon can be viewed.  The river watch trail would be a good place to view spawning salmon in the fall.

Very nice urban park with northern and southern entrances.  It is bisected by a creek that can flood the trail in the winter.  It has paved, gravelled and bark chipped trails so there are all-weather options in the winter.
There are several interesting trees in the park.  I have shot graduation portraits in this park using its scenic backdrops.
There is also an eastern trail in a utility right-of-way that in the summer can offer some variety.

This park located in Chinook and is run by Pacific County and has the potential to be so much more.  It is day use only, with some very nice picnic spots situated right on the Columbia river.  When open you could drive your car to a spot. The park has been closed to cars since Covid so you must park and walk into the picnic area.  The bathrooms are also closed. There is a boat ramp that you may access, but it is unusable during low tides.

Kids love this place.  There is so much strange stuff to see. Get your picture taken with Jake, everybody does.....  Or the shrunken head... Or the two headed calf...  It is free unless to find a souvenir that you can't live without.  They handout small shells to everyone as a gift (really small shells).  It is the thought that counts.
I enjoy the old school baseball game, when it is working.  Look for it on the back wall.

One of the best dog parks I have visited.  It is large with lights and undercover areas.  It has a big and small dog sections.  Double entry and exit gates so no one escapes without supervision.  Portions look like they floods from time to time so check to make sure it open in the winter before heading over (there is a phone app for this).  It is also closed for maintenance from time to time.  Features nearby parking lot.

We went after the season ended and the visitor center was closed as was the road up to the butte.  It was snowing. The parking lot and trails were open so we hiked the trail of molten land.   Interesting views with the snow covered lava flow.  Very good signage on the trail.

If you want to see the butte in winter you will need to hike it (about  1.8 miles).

It is kind of confusing, but Loomis Lake state park is on the beach side of Hwy103 and has restrooms, picnic area and beach trail.  The access road to Loomis Lake is 1/4 mile north of the park on the otherside of Hwy 103 with restrooms and boat launch.  The boat launch is best place to launch at the lake as there is very little public land around the lake.

Nice urban park.  Small paved loop with a couple of bridges and some feeder gravel trails that can be explored. I remember when the area was a flood plain.  Nice that THRPD has been able to utilize this unbuildable land so that it can be used during the summer months.  Judging from the activity this evening it is well used by the community.

I like the improvements made recently to the lighthouse, access path and overlook.  Because of the views from the trail, the lighthouse and belle's overlook it is first class.  I wished I had seen some whales today, but you can't have everything.
A tip of the cap to Friends of the Columbia River Gateway for the improvements!

HIked with Angora hiking club to cape disappointment lighthouse. Hike was guided by a very knowledgeable park ranger,  Stephen Wood.   Nice folks and a nice hike.  Visibility was good, wind calm and weather dry.
Could see shipwrecks on Jetty A with binoculars, but no whales...

This clear winter day was windy when I stopped to check out this  roadside historical marker.  Lots of information about the native Americans that lived in this area.  The wild strawberries growing in the middle of the observation platform was a nice touch.

Nice place to walk the dogs when it is hot.  Long flat trails, with interesting sights.  Parking and Bathrooms are reasonable.
Make no mistake this is an industrial area park so if you are looking for a natural experience you should look elsewhere.

During my visit, I learned that George Vancouver named Mt. St. Helens after a friend, Alleyne FitzHerbert, 1st Baron St Helens.  It pays to have an explorer for a friend.  Luckily Alleyne had a title or we would have been visiting Mt. FitzHerbert.

I have driven past the signs for this park many times, but never stopped.   I picked a nice day to check it out.  Cullaby Lake is much bigger than I expected. The park has full services with a play area, boat ramp and boat dock.  Lots of parking.
I am happy to report that the tree of life is still thriving.  Easy access from the Kalaloch campground.   I remember a visit 10yrs ago where it looked better so I am happy I got to see it again.
My father was quite amused by this museum and vouched for its authenticity.  It a nice break from the shops in Palm Springs.  Admission  is $1 per person and you can spend 10min seeing it.
Sizable urban park with playground, courts, ball field and open space.  Bring your own chairs because there aren't a lot of picnic tables.  Our Natalie gives the playground a thumbs up!
We had fun this weekend exploring the forest.  It should be noted that google street view has surveyed many of the roads in this forest making it easier to find road side vistas.
Arrived in the evening and all the structures were closed.  Nice evening to just walk around.  Even though everything is a reconstruction it was still interesting.
I have driven by this many times and finally stopped.  Very nice day use area with lots of room to explore and picnic.  Note: there is no overnight camping.
The bathrooms are closed for the season.  Lots of parking and the pines offer a secluded park out of the wind.  There is a trail that goes out to the beach.
Took a detour through the garden.  Would love to see it in the spring and fall.  Squirrel activity was high.  Good thing the squirrel bridge is nearby.
Great view of the Columbia River from here.  Easy access with well maintained grounds.  Great place to watch the sunset.

Fresh! Clean! New!  Although it was cold outside when I went, it was nice inside - and not smelly or steamy as some aquariums seem to be.  The Shark complex has a nice flow to it and seriously interesting set up wherein the fish and whatnot swim over your head!
There is an outside turtle tank with one of those reallly big ones!
I didn't get to the 4D experience movie. not sure what that was all about.
It wasn't crowded when I was there - but they are SERIOUS about their closing time...don't dawdle.
Bonus!  two penny squishing machines (one was out of order).
Gift shop had lots of fuzzy creatures to take home (and some nice glass ones, too).
If you are at Coney - why not stop by?

NOTE: at $25 per adult, it is not cheap.

Really interesting little museum dedicated to the Kellogg sanitarium (of "Wellville" fame.  Not only do they have items from the times, but you can try them out.  An example is the foot vibrator.  Mmmmmmmm!
Our guide was a volunteer intern from PR.  She didnt always use the right terms which was misleading at times, and fed us her slightly "modern" attitude (judgement) about some activities/practices she discussed. Some of the informational signs were not accurate either (using modifiers of most, often).

But!  It was reallllly interesting!  Do glad we went!!

WOW!  This museum is so very very cool.  So glad I found out about it.  Walking distance from Inner Harbor, Federal Hill, Science Center - well - lots of stuff.
This is a museum that will make your head THINK  - you aren't just going to look, you are going to THINK about who made the art, why it exists, could YOU be an artist yourself.
It is not cheap (what is these days) but   - -  if you are going to pay a pretty penny, it might as well be here.

NOTE: they DO NOT HAVE a penny squishing machine, but maybe they will consider one!

worth a detour if taxidermy your thing. very cool place filled to the rafters with "stuff"....you almost dont know where to look!  The lady of the manor was really ljvely and informative! Dont forget to make your donation!

i almost gave one leas star: I dont think kids will necessarily like this place. the kids kn our tour were ....uncomfortable.

I know LOADS of artists, goths, alt kinds of folks that ISIS the right place for.

keep your eyes out for the various mermaids!

So much under one roof.
It would be easy to simply write this off as a Y (as in YMCA) but it is so much more - from the beautiful theater space, to the amble changing rooms, to the reasonable and tasty cafe (on the third floor).  If you live near (or it's an easy commute) there are so many classes and benefits to joining this Y (including readings and orchestra - not just gym "stuff.")

Note:  There is security at the door.  The security is VERY friendly and helpful.

What a great treat the new york historical society is!  Such diverse exhibits which are always changing.   Some of the permanent collection is always on display.   From the George Washington portrait that is the basis of the George on your dollar bill to the gorgeous glowing glass of tiffany lamps  to shows through the ages and bill Cunningham there  really is something fir everyone.  Pay what you want on Friday.

A nice gathering place...a bit quieter now with the whole CV thing going on - but you can still sit on benches throughout the park, hear some buskers, and enjoy being outside of your 300 sqft apartment or hotel or whatever cage you live in.  Very central for subways...I always feel like it is the heart of the lower part of the city.
when it is popping - double dutch, chess, skaters....dancing even.

Don't get lost!  While maps works in the park...it is easy to wander and become turned around.  There are plenty of benched, trees, grassy areas.  There are playgrounds and of course, the zoo.  Please don't litter  - take your trash with you.
Oh!  and it is easily accessible from several train stops.  Nice in any weather.

Well!  If you are going to do a whole "thing" about your name and being buried and fame and stuff....Jim did it right. What a cute town, nice monument, and peaceful setting.  Check out all the various sports and writeups that are at this memorial. The grounds seem very well maintained.  Good job, Widow Thorpe!

A little plaza  - away from but close enough to the bustle of Chelsea Market and Hudson Yards.  We were treated to a large scale art installation of STained Glass Houses (there through April, I think). The chairs were locked up (it was 9pm) but I imagine this would be a fabulous place to just sit, day time.

Triennial, part 2:  fascinating, diverse, thoughtful, just right.  Two pieces brought me to tears.

Many mediums are represented, styles, and comments on the world both as it is, was, and could be.

The space itself is elegant.

I spent about an hour- conscious of my time.
Just go! (timed tickets)

It's FREEEEEEEE!  If you can take this bridge instead of the tunnel - it's FREEEEEE.
It is complicated when you get off to figure out which way you need to go (in both directions).
As a bike rider - it is very steep on one side. The air quality is not good.

BUT - it's freeeeeeee

A pitchy little museum that is bigger than you would think.   It is a roadside attraction!  Fun events sprout from here, too.
If you are native, you need to go to learn more stuff and to say: oooh!
If you are a tourist, you need to go because THIS is really NYC stuff.

Seriously.

Beautiful location for a picnic ..or wedding.   The grounds sweep to the river.  The out buildings of another time.   Lovely views, backdrops for photos, simple benches for reading and pondering.
Tricky to...get to without a car.   But trsin to Yonkers station is close- ish.

An interesting plave, both modern and yesteryear.  Items you couldn't find anywhere else.  Tricky layout.  Staff doesn't go above and beyond....just as much as they need to (a bit....abrupt with a smile). Changing exhibits.   Feels fancy when jazz group is playing.

Herald Squste is more than a little square - it is s meeting place, an eating place, a reading place.  The Bell Ringers statue is ag Jane end and little cafe tables and chairs are there.

so, why 4 stars on this convenient meeting place?   crowded and bird poop.

A lot of reading:  wall placards and such.   Interesting if not easy for our modern brains.  it would be grand if they got some more physical items.  I enjoyed what was there regarding famous players of old palm springs. clean.  donation.  Closes early(ish)

the exhibitions are always changing and always very well curated. there is a bit of a library feel to the space.  good placards of explanation are posted throughout and often (always?) a video bonus.
the hours are tricky to hit
..so plan your trip.

SUPER INTERESTING...but was very crowded when we were there.  Loads of wacky and weird medical related stufff - skulls, Civil War photos, fetuses of the abnormal.  It is in a house, so the feeling of the place is a bit Victorian - in a good way.

I should be glad for any outdoor experience these days, but j always sn wary of astoria park. Over the years there have been tons of reports of illegal activity after dark.  I also feel just...uncomfortable there.
Just a feeling.....

I like the gallery - big, clean, white.  It seems well staffed and organized BUT I don't like the lines for some of the shows.  grrrrrr. (and some of the security/line guards take their jobs a littttttle toooooo seriously.)
Enjoyable tour representing  a time that changed music.  You really feel you are with the "spirit" of the time and people - with so many artifacts.
Lots of space in this park - which is right off the main drag (31st street) with seats and tables and statues.  It is an almost hidden gem
Peaceful, pretty, clean.  A very nice respite if you have ocme from any urban area. Just take a nice stroll and forget it all.
A fun sciencey kind of place for kids eith dinosaurs!  They also have a squished penny machine *out of order today.

Incredible Park, just down the road if you're staying in Calabasas. If you come here, you'll recognize many things you've seen over the years in movies and television shows. Mash was filmed here and there's a trail that leads right to the outdoor set where they filmed, there's some old abandoned Jeeps left from the show and they have everything mapped out so you can tell where they were filming. There's also Century Lake and The Rock pool. All five of the original Planet of the Apes films filmed here. Park is loaded with trails and every direction there are golden Rolling Hills and grassland. Easy to see why they film so much here, it's gorgeous and looks like a giant outdoor movie set. I don't think I've ever been in a more pretty Park. Place is huge, easily you could spend a day or two here. There's also an information center Ranch House that tells about the history of the place. If you're in Calabasas or Malibu area, this definitely has to be on your list. I waited a long time to come here and see this, and it absolutely did not disappoint.
likes: Activities: Hiking trails, Exploring film sets
Attraction Type: Scenic beauty, Large park

reviews_attraction.text: Very nice looking and well-maintained Waterfront Park in the Newcastle Renton area. This place is much larger than you would expect, nice walking trails that go on for a considerable distance past the General Park area. There are also two main large swimming areas with Docks. They have a huge boat launch area and there are plenty of places to sit and enjoy the view and watch all the action. For food, they have a kidd Valley hamburger restaurant here as well as an Ivar's Seafood Bar restaurant. The Landing shopping center is close by with more food as well. They have a lot of parking here for both cars and boats, plenty of restroom stations as well. Great place to roam around and enjoy the summer day.

Golden Gardens is probably the best park and Beach area in all of Seattle and it's certainly the most popular during the summer. If you come during the summer on weekends, the earlier the better as the parking is ample but it fills up fast. Great place just to hang out people watch walk your dog or whatever. They have BBQ Pits, covered seating areas, children's playground area, volleyball area, a fishing pier, a snack bar store with food items and soda. Plenty of places to explore and wander around. The perfect place to go in Seattle on a hot summer day.

you have to come here and see this place at least once in your life. The inside is incredible and very interesting, but for me the view of the city below, especially at night time, is something magical right out of a movie. Incredible. There's a long winding drive to get to the top, and you may have to Circle a little bit at the parking lot to find a spot. There's usually a lot of people here.. but it is well worth it to see this place.
likes: View: City view, especially at night

reviews_attraction.text: What used to be an old oil refinery was turned into this wonderful downtown park in Seattle . Perfect place to come during the summer or any time of year  to wander around  walk the Dog climb up hills  and enjoy a 360 degree panoramic view of Seattle one of the best in town. Gas Works Park is of course the perfect place to watch the fireworks show Over lake Union on 4th of July. The only one drawback is I wish there was more parking.

Very nice park in downtown Juanita. Ample amount of parking plus there's a spillover lot across the street. It can get a bit crowded on weekends during the summer, but there's still room to roam around. Covered picnic area with grills Etc. Nice playground area for kids to play. There's a walk-around dock in the marina, so good place to go for a walk after you've eaten. They also rent kayak and paddle boards here too.

This is a great Pier and Beach to hang out at all day, Lots of atmosphere. Several snack bars underneath the pier and other restaurants are close by. There were a lot of fishermen on the pier having a good time and there's a Ruby's Diner restaurant at the end of the pier. Very cool looking place. The beach itself is very long and there's a harbor area with boats down at the North End.

Nice little secluded beach, good place to hang out or go swimming or just chill out, you can also rent canoes and kayaks here. It's sort of right under the bridge to Mercer Island, you could drive past it and miss it it's kind of hidden. There's also a dock here and they have lifeguards on duty. The parking here is limited but hopefully they'll fix it soon.

Very nice park at the North End of garrapata State Park area. Accessed via Highway 1, there's a parking area alongside the highway. No fee to go in. There's a set of steps down to the rocky Beach below, lots of waves and a cave with a rope ladder to explore, good walking Beach, quiet and peaceful area. Lots of colorful nature around to explore.

The Palos Verdes Heritage Museum Castle was once the setting for the classic film it's a mad mad mad mad world. The entrance to the park was filmed here at the front Gates and the Big W palm trees we're inside. Unfortunately the trees no longer exist. It's still a very cool place and it's worth the drive down the coast to check it out.

Robinswood Park is a very nice park and it is well maintained year-round. Lots of walking and hiking trails here in a wooded area plus they have two full-size soccer fields, baseball diamond, playground equipment area for kids plus there is a dog walking Park here too. Ample parking, good place for walking around quiet and peaceful.

This is the Bixby Creek Bridge and there are some truly amazing views of the coastline here. One of the best spots in all of Big Sur. There is a parking spot off the highway just before you get to the bridge and another spot off to the other side where you can park slightly above. Stunning Vistas with crashing waves below.

The Newport Pier is a very touristy type of place, nice but a little rugged around the edges. The pier itself is nice and there's a Ruby's restaurant at the end of the pier. Lots of souvenir shops and knick-knacks and such. Best place to park is in the pay lot right by the beach and the prices are surprisingly Fair.

Nice shaded Park along Holmes Point Drive with excellent view of Lake Washington. good place to have a picnic, covered area with BBQ, lots of benches and picnic tables here, playground for kids, lots of room to roam around and good place to walk your dogs. There's parking in the park and directly across the street.

Huge Park out at Sandpoint, a great place to just roam around in peace and quiet along the shoreline. They also have a dog park here as well. Also a huge field for soccer and Outdoor Sports, a dock system with boat launching and there is even a tennis center here too.

Fun place to spend the day walking around sampling clam chowder and Seafood , taking in the sights and sounds and visiting all the restaurants, candy and fudge stores and t-shirt gift shops. Perfect place to stroll around and kill a few hours.

This nice little park in West Seattle has great views of downtown Seattle across the water and is hardly ever crowded. Perfect place to unwind with some free time or walk your dog . Come at night time for an even better View of the city.

The lone Cypress is located inside 17 Mile Drive, you have to pay to get in its cash only. Very nice looking place this amazing one-of-a-kind scenery. Better to go earlier in the day in the morning rather than later it gets crowded.

Pretty much near the start of the 17 Mile Drive, this white sandy beach has a very large nature area with trails to walk along and observe the scenery. The parking is ample so shouldn't be a problem to find a spot.
Nice quiet park along Lake Washington.They have a concession stand,covered grill area,bathroom facilities,lifeguards on duty in summer.Nice place to hang out for some quiet time.
This is a nice quiet and peaceful area to get away to down in Juanita in Kirkland. Nice long walking trails and wetlands area you may see some Wildlife as well.
Nice long stretch of beach, very remote quiet and private. Perfect place to go for some quiet time, do some fishing or just enjoy the scenery.
Pretty cool park/boat launch/Seafair HQ! Good place to hang out and check out the scene.The Mt. Baker Rowing/Sailing Club is here also.
