Great beach in West Seattle, go to spuds for lunch and your set. Lots of traffic during the summer time on weekends, so be prepared.
One of the nicest spots along 17-Mile Drive. Gorgeous scenery. Ignore all the rich guy houses here, just money spoiling The View.

A stunning museum for museum lovers of any kind. Not a huge number of exhibits but it’s packed with information that really helps pique your curiosity for locomotive transport. The central stunning pieces are the multiple full sized locomotives that are still in working order and used seldomly on a yearly basis. Step up on the multiple display to get a close look at all the engines and conductor compartments. Got a sneak peek at the inside of one of the conductor compartments in a rare occasion. Come support this museum through an awesome train ride a couple miles away which run every hour or two. Considering the entire museum is absolutely free, this museum shouldn’t be missed whether you’re a local, or a visitor from any corner of the globe. Easy enough to get to on public transport and take advantage of the river walk trails nearby.

An extremely lovely showcase of all the animals that Florida has to offer in a safe environment run by the state mostly helping nurse injured animals either for rehabilitation back to the wild or to act as ambassadors for the species if they are too injured to return. Had a fantastic experience and if you want to explore every nook and cranny, read every description card, etc. you could easily spend 1-2 hours here. Some highlights that you should catch are the manatee feedings, hippo feedings which occur at set times throughout the day, there's a schedule posted at the entrance. Really love the jumping fish that greet visitors right near the entrance/exit. If you time it right, you catch a string of jumping fish. A great experience, low cost place to have some fun for both adults and children alike.

Beautiful hikes and conveniently located in the bay area. Relatively easy trails with multiple different paths throughout. Ended up doing a round trip of around 10 miles without any issue. Relatively few visitors on each trail and some trails are extremely wide allowing plenty of space while others are not frequented by many visitors. Parking does cost money and they do enforce a 1 car in and 1 car out policy when it starts to get full but if you aren't opposed to a little extra exercise, park outside the park in the community for free and make your way in with a short walk. Unfortunately there's no sidewalk between the park entrance and the community that I could find so I did have to share the road with vehicles for a short distance.

Great museum pretty close to downtown easily accessible via public transportation. A museum that contains an immaculately maintained home with many artifacts that were handed down for multiple generations and still flawless after many years. The tour guides give a rich history and have in depth knowledge of the many different artifacts around the house.

Went during Denver arts week which happens during the first Saturday of November where multiple art museums graciously open up their doors for free between 5-10pm.

Museum admission is not expensive on most other days and it’s a fantastic way to explore some history and immerse yourself in the life of someone with a house built almost 150 years ago.

This place should 6 stars if I could. Far and away exceeded all of my expectations. Easy access to the trail, plenty of parking in the community, no adventure pass required, cell signal throughout the hike for easy communications, beautiful beach scenery and lovely greenery. This hike doesn't offer many tall trees or shade but when I came in the afternoon a couple hours before sunset, it was absolutely perfect. With just enough sunshine for a clearly lit path, stunning sunset colors splashing over the mountainside leading to the ocean, it was an absolute joy for all my senses. Not to mention, extremely secluded and only passing a couple people for the 2 hours on the trail.

Great spot that has the mixed feeling of a grand library and a museum. Lots of exhibits and showings here on a wide variety of subjects concerning Chicago from modern art to modern film. A little bit of historical information used for setting the scene for the needs and plans for the future. Unique exhibits covering modern art, to easy-to-understand graphical public notices. Some of the special exhibits are also quite unique with one on Brazil’s São Paulo region’s housing costs and how micro apartments are being created to lower housing costs and make it more affordable for the vast majority of low income residents. Completely free so there’s no excuse to not swing by.

Absolutely amazing place to come and learn more about the famous locks that connect the Puget Sound to the Lake Union.  View the fish ladder in the underground structure that gives clear glass views of the fish ladder although depending on time and season, you may not be able to see any fish jumping up the ladder. Seeing the locks open and close is a real treat and there's constant traffic no matter when you come. The sunset is also beautiful and lots of seating to have a snack and enjoy the waterfall sounds in front or behind you.

Quite an expensive museum to visit with high admission prices but it's worth every penny and they participate in Bank of America's Museums on Us program. The submarine is the coolest thing ever and the staff do a great job explaining how different parts of the sub work. The aircraft carrier is beautifully restored with lots of amazing aircraft and information. Going up to see the island of the carrier was awesome and the 1:400 Lego carrier is extremely impressive.

Beautiful trail along the old US-1 route which means it’s extremely wide as it used to fit 2 single lane vehicle roads which is now replaced by the tunnel just off to the side. Clearly marked pedestrian and bicyclist lanes. Lookout points and rest areas with benches sprinkled throughout. Came before noon and was met with a dense fog which started clearing out in the afternoon. Even with the limited view of the coastline, it was well worth the visit.

Great spot that’s relatively close to the downtown and easy enough to reach by public transportation for a little taste of nature without having to leave too far. Lots of trails flipping back and forth that’s not super clear where one ends and one starts but if you have extra time, it’s easy enough to wander around and enjoy the scenery and the views. Not a huge amount of people allowing for enjoyment in relative serenity.

Good museum but felt the galleries and artifacts are a bit lacking. Museum was not very large with the entire gallery on one floor. Half was split in to a large permanent collection and the other half is a smaller collection. Staff is friendly and the admission prices are reasonable although a bit higher than I would have expected for the small space. They do participate in Bank of America's Museums on Us program though.
likes: Participates in Museums on Us program
dislikes: Higher than expected admission for size

reviews_attraction.text: A really nice park with a lot of trails but be prepared, some trails contain surprisingly steep up and down hills so bring water and a good pair of hiking shoes. For an easier time, start from the North end and make your way south for a most downhill descent. For a workout, just head South to North. The trail is also a loop so feel free to start on either end and take both sides of the challenge.

Stunning place to relax with a little bit of shade offered by the many large trees along an easy and wide dirt path. Was able to find a nice secluded corner and sat on a fallen tree branch in a corner next to the shoreline which was a great place to stretch my feet, eat some food, take in the beautiful coastline spotting surfers and the ocean currents underneath while feeling the ocean breeze.

Absolutely amazing museum filled with all of the quirky and unique cars many you've never heard of or seen. This place is like Disneyland for children and adults alike. They have many sections and they try to have a few examples in each collection to present a cohesive exhibit. The crown Jewel is a massive amphibious military vehicle parked outside that weighs over 100 tons.

Beautiful beach allowing visitors to enjoy the ocean waves crashing along the shoreline. Seldom crowded with plenty of parking along the parking lots and metered street parking areas alongside the main road. It costs $2.50 an hour during the peak summer season which includes parts of spring and fall. Sometimes you may even be able to catch a surfing competition as well.

Absolutely amazing way to spend an afternoon. Diverse and substantial collection that is very well organized. The guided tours are very informative. Don't forget to take advantage of the Bank of America Museums on Us giving free admission on the first weekend of the month.

Be sure to check out the observation deck up on the 9th floor of the towers. Amazing views.

Really beautiful mini park located along the lake cheshiahud loop and the shio canal trail. When the season turns the leaves a golden color, come here to enjoy an absolutely beautiful view along an absolutely serene river to relax and take in the peaceful ambiance. The trail nearby also makes it super easy to come here by walking or biking.

Great spot to be able to walk around and see lots of cool flowers and plants from around the world. Not many flowers outside during the winter however the green house contains a ton of colorful tropical flowers and even cool animals like poison dart frogs. Lots of space and outdoor area and great for a peaceful stroll.

Great spot to spend a few hours learning about some old pieces of news and some of the most recent news. Admission prices are slightly high but currently part of Bank of America Museums on Us program. Has a great looking terrace with a view right over the middle of D.C.

Beautiful views along the riverfront with a lovely Riverwalk that stretches over a mile. Nice wide sidewalks and not too crowded. Passes by lots of shops and restaurants allowing you to grab a quick bite. Also lots of river cruise and taxi operators.

The museum is good with lots of exhibits but it is definitely geared for younger children. Be prepared for long lines to every exhibit on weekends and parking takes a long time. Try to get there early and buy tickets online to avoid the lines.

Fantastic museum that's not as large as it might look on the outside but full of little surprise and fantastic pieces from many artists. Friendly staff and they even participate in Bank of America Museums on Us.
Park offers amazing views over the Hudson river and has great views of NYC and the Tappan Zee bridge. Great spot to hang out and watch the sunset.
Really small museum but be sure to take advantage of the staff inside the house. They love to explain all of the little details and history.
This place is an absolutely fantastic way to spend some time over the weekend especially when the weather is good.

Really bizarre and unusual place. Was really hoping for the Portuguese experience, having loved what the country and their wine offers.  It's absolutely amazing in their wine country.

This place is akin to a Vegas style faux Portugal inspired locale. It can be considered perhaps a bit campy. I get what they are trying to do, and they almost pull out off, but there are sections that fly in the face of the essence of what they are attempting. They have statue water fountains galore. The most unusual part is the section that has a military vehicle and farm equipment for kids. If you have kids this could work.  For those looking for a special event they do have a chapel.

The wine was reasonable. The almost vhino verde was okay, but lacked the quintessential bubbles. As you go toward the dark and more robust wines, they hit their stride. With the tasting, they provide a plate of chocolate, cheese, crackers, and sausage. It's a nice touch, but they are light on the quality, which is fine for their purposes.

What the what? When I first started going to wineries in VA many moons ago, this was one of the places. Recently while being there, the place feels really run down. The men's bathroom was destroyed. Seriously, it felt like the bathroom from Dan's Cafe in Adams Morgan, not a winery.

Another disappointing part was how they're serving now. Your tasting comes in the little round plastic cups with tops that are used for salad dressing cups at Whole Foods.  I get the one use during this era, but most of the wineries are using glass - and simply washing.

That all said, the wines were decent. Perhaps this was an off Saturday.

Always feel free to reach out to me on Twitter @joerazz

Really? It's a huge cement marker colored in red, black, and yellow defining the "Most southern point of the continental United States.  The line this day to get your own picture was 30 people deep - though I hear this grows to several hundred over the weekend. That will be an hour wait. Geographicly speaking, I'm not 100% it's really the southern most tip, given land around it juts further out than the marker - just saying. Want to see a video in 360 degrees - see it on YouTube for more information.

Always feel free to reach out to me on Twitter @joerazz

Beautiful, huge, well designed, clean, and very good wine. The place is massive inside and out, but feels like a high end winery with an indoor barn-like tasting room and an outside venue. They also have multiple decks and covered outside seating. In addition they have a long wide field with picnic tables and umbrellas. Really wonderful venue.

Always feel free to reach out to me on Twitter @joerazz

The entire "coastline" of this stretch of the Potomac that looks towards DC is perfectly picturesque. This is one section. You can take the trail from Reagan Airport all the way up to Rosslyn and marvel at the scenery.  It's typically traversed by locals and cardio enthusiasts, but should be on the docket for all from out of town.

Always feel free to reach out to me on Twitter @joerazz

I am really impressed with this museum. The eclectic nature of this place beacons nearly any dilettante or expert to appreciate this massive private collection of art.  I would highly recommend visiting this place if you are even partly interested in the last 2000 years of history or the arts.  Oh, and it's free.

Always feel free to reach out to me on Twitter @joerazz

Beautiful location, basking in the sun, this winery is unique. It's tiered landscape has a multi level plateaus for vines, and at various points, ponds. Trees surround the hillsides.

A sampling of the red wines were a bit underwhelming. They seemed very sweet across the board. Clearly the primary appeal here is the landscape and feel, which is outstanding.

Tight, two level museum, packed with information about slavery in Charleston and beyond. It's a very good glimpse into what happened at their historical sight. It's a rather small exhibit, but filled with information and some AV. It's worth a visit if you're in town for a few days.

Always feel free to reach out to me on Twitter @joerazz

This should be on your list when you visit DC. One of the classic museums in DC. I've been going to this one since I was 5 years old. They do a fine job of rotating new work into their standards, they may have been there since I first went. It has been renovated recently.

Always feel free to reach out to me on Twitter @joerazz

It's so hard to describe this place. A flat short golf course that looks over the entire DC Capitol area. It's got more promise that Agusta with its views and landscape, but is public funded so it's more like a run down local park in Detroit. Nice oasis in the DC area.

Always feel free to reach out to me on Twitter @joerazz

Shocked with how untouristy this pier was recently. It has exquisite views from the end of the pier at sunset. The two restaurants that bookmark both ends of the pier are real.  No Bubba Gump here - yet. ;)  That is, the food isn't slapped together for the masses.

Always feel free to reach out to me on Twitter @joerazz

Fantastic local treasure!  During the summer you can pack a full picnic basket with food and any beverage and attend a full range of performances on their lawn.  The parking is usually easy, though it can be a test of your will to get out after the performance.

Always feel free to reach out to me on Twitter @joerazz

It's the center of Old Town, which is generally quaint and worth a stop. While some of it is touristy, they have some gems where stores sell some local crafts and arts. The church is the centerpiece and is also a place to check out.

Always feel free to reach out to me on Twitter @joerazz

Street art is everywhere in this part of the city and this location is the epicenter. The color, spectacular imagination, and scale is absolutely worth a visit to see the murals. See a few 360 degree pictures I've posted.

Always feel free to reach out to me on Twitter @joerazz

I really liked this place. The grounds were charming and fun. It's a working farm with horses, goats, and other animals about, but penned.

The red wines were quite good, but interestingly, no matter the blend or grape seemed very similar. I'd definitely come back.

It's $5 to enter. You have two buildings conjoined and the rooms are period pieces in what you would have seen when Thomas Jefferson visited to eat and sleep over. It's small but a nice museum to get a feeling for what the early days of the country was like.

Great piece of Georgetown history. The guide was a PhD and knew a load of local lore. It's worth a quick trip through if you're in the area.

Always feel free to reach out to me on Twitter @joerazz

Here after hours for a wedding. Very cool space to have special engagements. Lots of well done buildings covering the history of the area.

Always feel free to reach out to me on Twitter @joerazz
You can come here most times of the year, but no better time is during the middle to late July when most of the lotus plants are in bloom. It's amazing and definitely something to do in DC.
Very walkable trail for all ages. It's pretty and the grades aren't too steep. If you're lucky you may see an owl. We saw a huge one in the middle of the afternoon in the old woods.

Great little park to launch your boat or watch the geese along the waterway. They also have a few fields to play baseball.

Always feel free to reach out to me on Twitter @joerazz

If you're a Potter fan this is your Mecca. It's pretty amazing what they have created based on the movies and books.

Always feel free to reach out to me on Twitter @joerazz
Quite a nice beach! It's clean, can be quite, or not,depending on the time of the year. This section of the beach does not have a lifeguard.
Loads of wonderful art. Make sure you get to all three plus levels. The third floor gets to your more modern angle.
Another charming bridge in VT. The water nearby is active and you have a few rocks to enter if you so dare.

You can’t beat the entrance price of three dollars per person. It was definitely interesting. I wish I could’ve taken pictures, but understand why you can’t because people would know was in there and they would lose  business. Some of the stuff is definitely real and just Autre rare. Some of the things may or may not be authentic, but still cool to see. One thing there was the remains of a mermaid, for example. Probably not real, but bizarre and cool nonetheless.  They also had lots of skeletal remains, antique embalming instruments, jars with specimens, shrunken heads, antique circus/freak show displays. Definitely worth seeing.

I loved this section of the park better than the section Sherman was in (Giants Grove).  General Grant tree is in an area with lots of huge sequoias. There are several of the largest trees in the world in this grove. We also preferred this growth over the Giant Grove because the hike to get around was much easier. The hike from General Sherman back to the parking lot is pretty much uphill all the way, which makes it difficult for some people including children, less fit folks and those with disabilities. It seems anyone can do the hike to the General Grant tree. Easy and very pleasant hike. Amazing!
dislikes: Difficult uphill hike (to General Sherman, not the attraction in question)

reviews_attraction.text: The museum is very nice and was a fun experience for my daughter. I don’t like the parking situation. You have to park in the deck and pay for that and then when you come out of the deck, it’s hard to tell which way the museum is.  Then when you go  back to your car, there’s more than one parking deck. I guess this is an a problem if you live nearby but for people coming from another city, still in North Carolina, but not living in Raleigh, it’s confusing. Then there are the one way streets… Basically, we like museum, but not the location.

I had gotten discount tickets on Groupon and gave it a try since it was pretty inexpensive. We were pleasantly surprised and we all had a great time. We especially love the tamarins and lemurs. It’s mostly indoors but there’s a section outside with sheep, goats, a few lizards, turtles and a couple of monkeys. You can feed the goats and sheep right out of your hand. It’s funny because they follow you around and almost fight each other to be the one to get fed! So cute! We spent about an hour there.

Amazing! I will say that I enjoyed the grove where the General Grant tree was better because it seemed that there were more of the largest trees in easy walking distance from the parking lot. There are several of the largest trees in the world located in the general Grant Grove. The hike around the trail at General Sherman was more difficult and mostly uphill back to the lot. This may be difficult for children and some adults. Both well worth the visit!

There is a nice welcome center with beach access and great views.  When you drive a little further up the road, you get to the four and the museum. The museum has lots of historical information and is nicely organized. There is a mini theater where you can watch a documentary.  The fort is very well preserved and has great views and lots of rooms were you can walk in and see where soldiers lived and worked.  Great experience!

It’s amazing to look upon a historic landmark with that much history. The lighthouse is beautiful. It’s quite a hike to make it to the top, but there are landing spots where you can stop to catch your breath. The stairs are narrow so sometimes you have to stop to let someone come down anyway and that’s a great opportunity to rest for a quick minute. It’s definitely worth climbing to the top. The view is amazing.

We did a workshop for Girl Scouts that taught us about sea turtles and how to help protect them. The facility was nice and it was a great program. The kids had lots of fun. We took the ferry from Southport, which is $11 for kids and $23 for adults. There are no cars on the island except for special permits, so they had a tram. to take us across to the Conservancy. It was a great day and fun experience.

Carrot Island offers a nice, relaxing, family nature adventure. We saw the wild horses and they were beautiful. The hiking trails are nice, but there really is horse poop everywhere. That is to be expected when you go to an island with wild horses. Fun and relaxing. I would definitely go back sometime. It also has a nice view of the historical Beaufort waterfront.

Very informative and the audio tour was really cool. I’m a Titanic fanatic, but I thought this would be cheesy and it was really great. We were even told they change the exhibits periodically between the other locations and they get very valuable pieces on loan from the owners. We saw an actual violin the band was playing the night it sank. So cool!

There’s lots of information to be found here. It’s free and they have a nice gift shop where you can find unique gifts. If you’re interested in history, I would recommend taking the time to stop by. If you’re not really interested in history, you’ll probably find it boring. There’s not a whole lot to see but there’s a lot to read and discover.

Very enjoyable experience. Daniel Boone only actually lived here when he was very young, but it was still the homestead of his family and, therefore, has significance in his life. The scenery is beautiful and it is very peaceful just to stroll the grounds. It was a little hard to find, but once you find it, you’ll be able to find it next time.

All three of the North Carolina aquariums are different. They have some similarities, but also unique. I like this one because it’s organized by region of the state and it flows nicely.  It’s very educational and relaxing. I love the outside walkway and it’s great views.  The kids love the climbing nets and the tire swing on the playground.

I love the butterfly house! This was very beautiful even in early spring. I know the prettiest time is yet to come later this spring and early summer. We got free admission because of reciprocal membership at another garden. It was very peaceful and relaxing here and there were great views of Hershey from the parking lot.

Breathtaking! I had always heard of this place but I’ve never been before until this year. It’s amazing and I will definitely go back. It’s one of the prettiest places I’ve ever been and I’ve been a lot of places. It’s a beautiful and peaceful. You can just sit and enjoy it for a long time.

This is a very nice zoo with lots of animals exhibits. The animals are grouped by their habitat and continent. It’s a nice hiking trail that leads around to all of the exhibits so you get to experience some other nature too. They have food and snack bars.  Highly recommend visiting.

Fun and great learning experience. I loved seeing this historical home. They don’t allow photos inside the home which stinks because I like to remember it. It was very informative and definitely worth doing. The grounds are beautiful and you are riverfront. The view is amazing.

We really enjoyed our visit. The site is very well-maintained and has some beautiful scenery in the area. There are lots of informative exhibits in the house and if you didn’t know much before your visit, it’ll tell you everything you want to know.

There are three floors full of cars. There were all kinds of unique and beautiful cars. We thoroughly enjoyed our visit and highly recommend to any one who likes cars.  They even had antique buses and an old food truck diner! Very cool!

I’ve seen the museum before when I visited Cherokee, but never went. I’m glad we took the time to stop by today. It’s a nicely laid out, very informative and interesting museum. You can learn a lot about Native American history.

There’s a trail with gardens, small garden ponds and places to sit and relax. There’s an observation tower with really nice views of the mountains. We really enjoyed it and it’s very relaxing and beautiful there.
We visited the farm museum while at the Oconoluftee Visitors Center. I enjoyed it because it was cool to see actual structures still in good condition. It was free and interesting.
This was a very beautiful and nicely kept park. I really enjoyed my visit and I would love to go back and spend more time there and do all of the trails.
This was a very nice and interesting stop. There’s lots of informative exhibits. It’s a small museum and gift store inside. Definitely worth the stop.
I love seeing this icon of American history. I thought the grounds were very well-kept and the displays of historic information was great.

A fabulous dinner show!

Sometimes when you go to these kind of shows, the food is not that good. But here it's excellent! Felt pretty full after the dinner and the selection was great!

And the show itself was very well done! Quality entertainment and in partic-ular the musicians were first class!

When you wait for the show, you queue in the gift shop which could bother you if you are claustrophobic as they pack everyone in , but you get to see the 'wares' which is probably deliberate.

Also it's worth stopping by before the show or even if you are passing by to see the farmyard animals they have outside!

Highly recommended!

This museum is fabulous and huge!

I can't say that I am a tank enthusiast, but when we found out there was a tank museum in Danville we set of to be underwhelmed, and we were so wrong!

The collection extensive and the facility is very big. In addition to the tanks, they have military uniforms, regalia and the like.

Plan on spending several hours if you want to see everything. You can take as many pictures as you like but make sure you switch off the flash.

Parking is plentiful and the admission price is great value.

Highly recommended!

Nice get away as soon as you cross the Bridge Tunnel. The visitors center is a little dated but still has some interesting exhibits about the area in general.

There are a few walking routes and some overlooks where the view is stunning! There are quite a few stairs if you want to get the best view from the overlooks.

There is no cost for any of this, and there is plenty of free parking. It can be a little tricky to find where to turn from the main road, but it's worth it when you do!

A nice little park right by the New River in the heart of Radford.

Plenty of walking trails and places to rest up and enjoy the day. On the times we have visited, parking has not been a problem and the shelters are clean and tidy. They even have bathroom facilities which were OK.

You can book the shelters here too, as I once attended a corporate event here.

Stop by if you are in the area on a lazy Sunday!

Fabulous museum!

Gives a real insight into coal mining and the local area and the challenges it faced.

The highlight of the tour was the trip into the mine itself, a decommissioned mine. The mine remains cool regardless of the time of year so make sure you bring a jacket.

Plenty of places to park, and the folks working there were friendly and knowledgeable.

Highly recommended if you are in the area.

The Castle is Disney, at least in the hearts and minds of people who have never been to the park.

It uses 'forced perspective' to make it look taller than it actually is but it's still iconic.

The Castle show at the end of the day is amazing! The Castle changes color, dances and even takes off at one point! Get to the show early though because standing room is actually sometimes limited!

My Wife found this place online, and it was the perfect respite from the hustle and bustle of the Orlando attractions.

The gardens are beautiful, and the tower is spectac-ular when you see it in person.

The tower plays music at reg-ular intervals and we were treated to a reading of 'Stairway to Heaven'!

The visitor center has a small museum, and the who facility is well worth a visit.

Fabulous quirky roadside attraction near Natural Bridge!

Union Soldiers battling Dinosaurs with Mr Slimes seeking out gold!

Some of the Dino's are looking a little tired, but it was fabulous hour or two taking it all in.

Incredibly creative works by Mark Cline, and the Disney style statue at the end was the icing on the cake.

Recommended for everyone!

This is a really nice aquarium, and one that I have visited multiple times.

The variety of fish on display is stunning and the touch pools are fun!

There is a Penguin exhibit which costs extra to visit, but you can see some of the Penguins from the main part of the building.

The location is right in the middle of downtown and is well worth a visit.

We had a great trip to see where the legend of John Henry took place.

The statue used to be located on the road, but it's now in its rightful place near the tunnel.

Plenty of parking near the statue. Don't forget to play your favorite version of John Henry as you drive up to it. I highly recommend Joe Bonamassa's song 'The Ballad of John Henry'

I loved visiting the Hemisfair Park!

It's a large area to walk around with where you can really get a taste of how great the Hemisfair was years ago.

The centerpiece to the park is the Tower of the America's which gives amazing views of the San Antonio area.

Also worth visiting here is the Institute of Texan Cultures.

Fabulous park in the middle of Downtown Roanoke.

They hold many events throughout the year and this is always a great place to come.

The Ampitheater is the centerpiece to the park and has hosted numerous concerts from many great artists. Prices are generally reasonable and the view is great regardless of where you sit.

A real piece of history that every American should visit.

The tour of the house is the centerpiece to the visit, and you have to join the tour group to see it. When we visited it was extremely busy and we had to book in almost at the end of our day.

The grounds are interesting, and there is plenty to see and learn.

Disney's answer to Universal City Walk.

Lots of shops, restaurants and a nice area to walk. It gets very busy here, but it's a good place to start your Disney adventure.

Parking can be a nightmare depending on when you visit, and some of the lots a good way away.

As you would expect 'attraction pricing' applies.

Having been to both the real Eiffel Tower and this one in Vegas, this one is probably more exciting!

Once you get up there, especially at night, the view is stunning!

You can stay up there for as long as you like and sometimes you even feel the spray from the Bellagio fountains!

Recommended for any Vegas trip!

This museum is a hidden gem!

We were in town for a show and found this place online, and were so glad that we did!

This is a very modern museum, and it was free to get in!

They have many attractions, and the Dinosaurs are a very fabulous indeed.

Highly recommended!

On of the most classic Vegas photo opportunities!

There is now parking at this site, but the spaces are limited.

Often there are Elvis impersonators and pan-handlers here but they are not official so you don't have the engage with them unless you want to.

This is a small car museum on the same site as Luray Caverns. Once you have paid the fee to see the caverns, the car museum is free.

Not an extensive collection, but one that is well kept.

Best part are the mannequins! Scary and creepy in equal measure!

This is a very impressive bridge!

There is a very well done visitors center which allows you great views of the bridge and the surrounding area.

The visitors center has a small museum and gift shop and is free to get in.

The iconic dancing fountains that you will have seen in films and TV.

Best viewed at night, this is one of the few free attractions in Vegas that is worth seeing.

Arrive early to get the best spot to see them!

Beautiful building that greets you as you approach Avalon by sea.

The Casino is in excellent condition and a must visit if you are on the island. There is no gambling here though, it's not that kind of Casino!

A very peaceful place for a walk in very well kept gardens.

There are some interesting exhibits here and lots of things to read and learn.

We had a great time walking with 'my feet 10 feet off of Beale'!

Lots of of bars, resturants and lively establishments in this area.

Fabulous piece of street art cast in Bronze.

I am pleased to report the Bull is anatomically correct in every way!

A monument to a most important man who seems to get forgotten by the history books.

Tesla is not just a car....

Visited Johnston Ridge Observatory 7/15/19 to hike to Loowit Falls. Only 2 other cars in the lot when I arrived at 4am. Started hiking at 4:30am. 15 miles in 9hrs 49 mins total, 2hrs16 mins stopped 7.33hrs moving with 2416 elevation gain.

Hiked the boundary trail (a little overgrown in places, but otherwise trail is in good condition). Saw some chipmunks here.

To truman trail (a couple kind of sketchy area and a little overgrown in places, looks like there has been some trail work done in some of the bushy areas. Otherwise trail is in good conition). A beautiful colored lake/pond.

To Willow Spring Trail (in good condition) beautiful lupine fields here.

To loowit trail (in good condition) saw 50+ mountain goats here with 4+ large herds scattered all over the mountain. Everywhere I looked I saw mountain goats. It was a great first time experience to see so many. A lot of baby goats as well.

To falls trail (in good condition) I hiked to the end of the official falls trail, not very great views of the falls as there was thick clouds and it was sprinkling there, but on the other side of the canyon there was a mountain goat and a baby goat, so I did enjoy watching them while taking an hour break. It looked like there is a sketchy looking trail going closer to the falls, but I did not check it out as I was hiking solo.

Saw 12 other people on the trail, all on my way back.

If you have a NW forrest pass or America The Beautiful just display it in your car and you can hike and leave, but if you want to go into the observatory, you have to show them your pass.

May 2018
Went up there today. A little busy for a Monday. Beautiful day to see mt st helens! The gates were open so I decided to go up. Very informative. It costs $8.00 to go in the observatory when it is open.

Had a cheeseburger at the food truck, save your $$, the food isn't great.

9/15/19 arrived at the hummocks trailhead on Sunday at a little over 1pm only 2 other cars in the lot on a rainy weekend day. Didn't see anyone else on the trail. Handicap parking is available here, but the trails are not handicap accessible. There is no bathroom here, but there are bathrooms at coldwater lake and that is very close. Hummocks loop trail is a easy hike beautiful area for a sunset hike.

Also did the boundary trail to Johnston ridge which has some sketchy parts with close to 2000ft elevation gain. Great choice for a rainy day hike. Some mud and puddles on the hummocks trail along with overgrown areas. Huckleberries and wild blueberries are in season on the trail right now. Saw a bunch of shrooms on the boundary and hummocks trail including a big pile on chicken of the woods. Saw birds, small frogs, deer and a heard of elk in the valley below and even heard them calling out to each other, beautiful sound.

The road in is suitable for all vehicles and the parking is spacious enough at times I have seen the lot full and also a school bus or two in there.

Hummocks loop and Johnston ridge via boundary trail.10.38 miles with 1943ft elevation gain in 6hrs total time and 5hrs 27mins moving time.

Hummocks trail loop is a great place to bring kids with low mileage, interpretive kiosks and a phone learning app activity. Plenty of benches on the hummocks trail to sit and enjoy nature.

The least amount of people I've ever seen at the observatory during open hours.
likes: Wildlife (mountain goats, chipmunks, birds, deer, elk)
dislikes: Lack of bathrooms at some trailheads

reviews_attraction.text:
Visited here Monday 7/20/2020, arrived at 1:50 am, there were 9 cars. There is no parking area for this TH, you just park on the side of the road. No bathrooms here either unless you drive to one of the campgrounds.no handicap parking and not handicap accessible. Might be ok for young children there are steep drop offs at the rim and on parts of the trail, as well as some rocky areas of the trail close to the TH. Trail is in good condition. Make sure you have an America the beautiful pass ($80), Northwest Forrest pass ($30) or pre purchase a day pass ($5) before you arrive as there is no fee box here. Make sure you also have a map of the area. No cell reception at TH. Road in is gravel, potholed, rocky and washboard, any car can make it with cautious driving.
Had the rim all to ourselves for Sunrise. Beautiful Sunrise up there. We continued on to see if we could get to no name lake. Make sure you have a map of the area.the trails can get a bit confusing. At one point you have to scramble over boulders. There are 2 snow fields before broken hand that are not hard to pass, the 3rd snowfield before broken hand is steep, you can go around it or cross it. Might need micros. The snow was pretty soft when we were out there. We saw a backpacker before the scramble camping in the middle of the trail.
At broken hand there is a large, steep looking snowfield to get to before no name lake the access to snowfield looked a bit sketchy. My friend and I checked out the trail that goes around the east side of BH, but it ends with trees smashed up to the rock wall and we did not feel safe getting through with our big packs on. We decided not to cross the snow field as my friend was low on energy, so we turned around here.
Bring sunscreen and bug spray. There's not much shade here and there were bugs up high (mosquitoes).
Bring plenty of water as well.
Think we saw 30 people total most of them at the rim or heading up to the rim. Got back to our cars at 1:30 pm and it was busy. Lots of people enjoying the lake on a hot day.
10.35 miles w/1816ft Elevation gain.
Campgrounds were open when we went.

Did a one night backpacking trip 5/19 to 5/20/19 on this trail. It was my first backpacking trip ever!
25.33 miles total 17+ hrs on trail and 2,995 ft elevation gain. Lots of blow downs, bushwacking, washouts and creek/stream crossings on trail. Hiked in 14.02 miles.
Trailhead is paved road, parking area is gravel. Bathroom is a vaulted toilet. No TP in bathroom and stinky trash. Must have a northwest forrest pass or America the beautiful pass to park here as there is no self pay station. Must sign the log for a self issued permit.
Cool little grave across from the biggest most flat camp spot along the raging creek. Where Fred Erickson lies one of the original builders/owners of Ingalls Creek Lodge.
Saw two deer in the forrests on our way out.
Found ticks on ourselves, I had one and my friend had 3, 2 of which were Dog Ticks (ticks on steroids!). Saw a Rubber Boa on trail on the hike out.
Make sure you have some sort of navigation as there are plenty of places where you can loose the trail.
Most of the creeks and streams are raging right now from all of the snow melt. Lots of waterfalls on the mountains.
I would not recommend this trail for small children as there are some steep drop offs, the trail can get pretty narrow, overgrown, ticks and big blow downs.
Only encountered a tiny amount of snow on trail where we hiked but heard from 2 female backpackers who hiked further up that the trail turned to soft snow where postholing, slipping and sliding was common, so they turned around.
Saw a big college group of hikers, a backpacker and a couple hikers on 5/20/19 all on our way back to trailhead, saw no one at camp. 5/19/19 saw 11 people. And some campers along the river.
5/19/19 when the weather is more warm all the bugs are out, including mosquitoes and ticks.
Numerous trail junctions along this trail.

Hiked this trail on Monday 10/15/18. This was literally one of the most difficult hikes I did this year! The roots, rocks and obstacles on the actual trail are relentless. This trail starts off easy on the road gradually going up hill on forrest road 63. There are 3 major washouts on forest road 63. Once on the trail it is all up hill and steep switchbacks until you reach virgin lake where it flattens a bit. There is a white rock wall that you must climb up to continue on the trail to virgin and blanca lake. After virgin lake you will be going down even more difficult terrain than the initial climb to virgin lake and you won't even see blanca lake until you're right on top of it. The day use trail is tiny and has more than a few scary parts. I would not suggest this trail for small children. Blanca lake this time of year had icy grounds, so take care in your steps. Lots of places are roped off for regrowth. My legs were freaking exhausted before I hit blanca lake. The climb up and then back down past virgin lake took everything in me not from buckling legs and tumbling down the mountain. It took me 10+ hours to complete this hike including all the breaks. My moving time was 9 hours and 35 minutes. I was hiking for a total of 10.6 miles. The bathroom at the true trailhead is closed due to the road washouts. This trail also feels really long when you're hiking it. I saw 2 trail runners, 8 hikers and a dog and a backpacker w/dog. I started on this trail at 6:30am and didn't finish till 5pm. The road in starts out paved and then turns to hard packed dirt with a lot of potholes, top speed I was driving was 20mph.

Hiked here 7/8/19 1167 elevation gain in 3.43 miles in 3hrs total time 49mins stopped. The road in was riddled with potholes so use caution when driving on the gravel roads. Google maps directed me to a different trailhead that was not the high rock trailhead, continue up the road till you get to a wide parking area at the top. You can see trail info across the road and a shutter leaning against a tree. There are no restrooms here and no fee pay station here. There is also another smaller marked trail not sure where that leads. I would rate this as a moderate to hard hike with maybe the final trek up to the lookout being the hardest (on steep rocky surface with cliff edges that seem to come out of no where, use caution). It was drizzling when I started at 4:31am, a few muddy and puddle areas on trail. Got to the end of the dirt trail at 6am. Didn't go all the way to the lookout as I was hiking solo and did not have my pack on me. Even with the cloud cover it was still beautiful to see this fire lookout through the earie mist. Numerous flowers to see on this trail as well. There are a few blow downs on the trail to maneuver around and several side trails. Saw not a single other person the whole time I was here, not even on the gravel forrest roads.

Visited 9/9/19, not many people there. Huge parking lot. Bathrooms are gross smelling and I'm pretty sure one is closed. Someone left their trash outside the bathroom doors even though there are trash cans inside. Hiked white river canyon trail to the timberline cutoff (saw a tent camper here). Trail is not well maintained after you climb the hill, there are several blow downs on trail. Beautiful area. Have been here multiple times and will def be back for more.
3.85miles with 725ft elevation gain in 2hrs 32 mins total time.

Visited Sunday 3/7/21, the sno park was groomed alot better than the previous year. There was a thin dusting of snow on top of icy pavement. The bathrooms are still stinky (strong amonia) but were a lot more clean. The park was not as busy as when I visited 2020, same time of year. Only two big groups training at 8am. Around 12pm the families were out with their kids, etc (not a lot of masking up going on), but the parking lot was still less than half full. Avy Danger (pinwheels and cornices) make going up to timberline from white river impossible right now. The trail on the way back was icy (a couple of us had accidents when our snowshoes hit the icy snow the wrong way). 3.3 miles with 615ft elevation gain.

Visited 9/17/19 saw no one on the trails, but did see multiple tent campers (probably people hiking the pct). Dry creek falls via pct 5.80 miles in 3hrs 20mins total time and 50 mins stopped time with 1071ft elevation gain. Picked up 6 bags of dog poo, please leave the trail better than you found it.

Maybe 10+ parking spots here with a couple handicap spots. Bathrooms are clean (flushing toilets), covered picnic area with a couple trash cans. Large grassy area under a canopy of trees.

Started at bridge of the gods trailhead (open 24/7), trail is right before you cross bridge of the gods. There are a couple street crossings that can be confusing in the dark.

Trail is in great condition. Hike to the falls via pct is easy. Saw a frog. Dry Creek falls gorgeous and a must see gorge hike!  Go up hill on dry Creek road till it dead ends then go across the cement walkway/bridge for best views of falls.

You need a NW Forrest pass/America the beautiful pass to park here or can get a day pass online.

Hiked Hardy Loop trail and a mile or more on the top of Hardy 5/7/19 10.3 miles with 2,091feet of elevation gain. No snow, but lots of bugs. Lots of flowers blooming on the trail. A bit windy, but I like it that way and trail is not as overgrown as the last time I hiked it. Only Saw 5 people close to the start, but did see a bunch of people in the lot getting there around 10:30am. Started the hike at 4:45am and finished at 10:30am. Saw a deer running across the entrance to where I was parked at on the way out. First big game I've seen at beacon.

Hiked 10.4 miles 4/16/19 from equestrian trailhead to bridge trail to upper hardy trail (blow downs on trail, debris and snow) to I named trail (to gate), to Hamilton mountain (little bit of snow on trail), to equestrian trail.

Endless adventures here. My dad and I hiked this morning for 8 miles and 3.5hrs and we did not even see everything. The trails even go up to the houses on prune hill, which is where we parked. We saw all the falls and all the lakes. 2017
Hiked this trail again 3/18/19. Some blow downs, but mostly in good condition. Bathrooms by round lake are locked in the winter and the porta john had trash all around it so I didn't even want to try it out, but the bathrooms by the community center across the street were open and clean with running water. It was a beautiful Monday morning. We did an urban hike from my dads place in washougal to round lake to lacamas lake to fallen leaf lake to mill ponds/ washougal river greenway and back to my parents place. Hiked 11.1 miles in 6hrs.

Visited this small park at 11:10am Sunday 2/21/21. Accessed this park via a trail on the North side of Andresen after Burnt Bridge Creek trail going south. Beautiful access trail that makes you feel like you're out in nature. You can access both Van Fleet Park and David Douglas Park via this trail (not handicap accessible, but great for small children). Van Fleet Park has no designated parking and does not have a bathroom. There is a green space with 2 picnic tables, a small playground (saw a father and his two children and a couple walking their dogs), several benches, a trashcan and a water fountain. This park is great for young children and handicap accessible. There is no gate here so you could access anytime. Clean park in a nice neighborhood.

Easy trail. I came from steam boat at the beginning of the levy and did the loop in the refuge back to the levy. Saw a deer, a rabbit, an osprey, a bittern, yellow bellied little birds and plenty of other birds. This is a must trek. I will visit this place again after 6am of course. The refuge doesn't open till 6am and close at 830pm. There are gates at the entrance so you cannot drive your car in till they open. Plenty of benches to have a sit on and a little bit of shade here and there. Mostly in the sun though. Only gnats and they weren't too bad at the refuge. It is gravel on the walkways. Very peaceful and beautiful  place.

Visited Meadowbrook Marsh at 12:20pm Sunday 2/21/21. Saw over 20 people walking, riding bikes and walking dogs. Some wearing masks, but mostly not. Lots of trash here from all the homeless encampments within. Saw three homeless tents very close to Andresen. There is street parking available from where I accessed the Marsh on NE 19th Circle. The Burnt Bridge Creek is stinky here. Beautiful big birds and bridges here. This path is Handicap accessible and great for young children. There is a small parking area on Andresen before the hill. Looked like there were also bathrooms available there. Beautiful lilly pond close to Andresen.

Visited Sunday 12/6/20. Beautiful park with tall trees, several parking areas and bathrooms on site. Burnt Bridge Creek Trail runs through this park and you can make a small loop of it if you want. There are several picnic tables, large covered party space, trash cans, bathrooms, small playground and softball field. Beautiful views of Burnt Bridge Creek and lots of small bridges. I did see one homeless encampment under the large bridge below NE 15th avenue. I didn't see a whole lot of trash. Saw 7 people at around 9am.

Visited this park Friday 10/16/20 at 10:08am 6 cars parked (the main parking area). 2 handicap plus 18 parking spots,bathrooms (4 stalls), water fountain, picnic tables, benches, trash cans, bike parking, lots of big 🌲 and grass, 2 small playgrounds, lots of beautiful walking paths, several entrances, big covered party space with 2 grills, ash dump, horseshoe game area, rose garden. I walked around the big loop in the park. This park is close to the highway and homeless people.

Vista house was close when I went there yesterday 11/26/18 due to weather (high winds) Beautiful viewing area and learning area. Beautiful building. I could see it from the 84 as I was driving up in the early morning. I would recommend a visit if you've never been. This place is open from 6am to 10pm, there is plenty of parking and it's free (not sure if you have to pay to do the observation deck in the building).

Saw this waterfall while I was hiking the Angel's rest to devils rest loop trail. This was a very beautiful area and I hope to be back to get a better look. One of the side creeks in this area had beautiful red rock for a bed. Visited here on 11/26/18. The trails have recently been re-opened on 11/23/18 after the fires. Saw 5 plus people in this area in the am.

Visited here Friday 5/8/2020. There are two handicap spots. Parking for 5+ cars, no bathrooms and a small trail area that goes through the power line area and on the side of the road. Easy to spot from the road, just look for the red barn. The playground is closed right now. Cool little park. Saw about 6 people total at the park at 12pm.

The viewpoint is really easy to get to. The parking area is tiny, so get here early unless you want to circle it a time or two to find a parking spot. The bathrooms are vaulted pit toilets and can smell pretty bad later in the day. The falls are beautiful and can't wait to go back on another day. 8/13/18

Small picnic area with a bathroom, bbq pits, rocky river access that's a bit over grown and a walking trail. From the 1900s to 1950s it was a vacation ranch for the cloud family who had an apple orchard. The apple orchard is the only thing left of the vacation spot. I visited here 7/17/18.

Beautiful forrest and views of the mountain ranges. Hiked at Mt Si via Teneriffe Rd 9.5 miles in 7.07 hrs. Elevation gain 3459 on 4/22/19. Also visited rattlesnake lake 4/22/19 and hiked to Rattlesnake Ledge 4.8 miles, 1211 elevation gain, 3hrs16mins hiking time.

This trail was fairly difficult in the beginning the trail was very small with steep drop offs. Its along the highway so you never really get the feel you want to get while you're hiking, noisy. I didnt see any other people on this trail.
This hot springs is temporarily closed till April first due to covid-19 and is not clothing optional. Seems as though you cannot Car camp either. Either pay to tent camp per person or get an RV site.
Great stop, we visited in 2017 in the off season (everything was closed), still lots of historical information and an interesting stop.
Gate was closed at new parking area when we arrived at 5am on Monday 4/22/19. So we parked at Mt Si parking area.
Beautiful big forrest with plenty to see and do. I did a hike, the cispus pass loop trail on 9/24/18.

This was honestly just an okay park, there's a kids jungle gym area right when you first pull in. Some beautiful trees surrounding the trail area, which lead you to believe your walking into something beautiful, yet instead your met with disappointment on a slightly moving bridge that leads you out to a field of grass which is on top of the pond. You may hear a few noises in the tall grass, each option you choose on the trail leads to a dead end. This place is great for the elder and small children,  several picnic benches and the trail is about 1.6 miles.
likes: Suitable for elders and small children

reviews_attraction.text: In the entrance area there are clean restrooms, a map and layout of all the trails, a breakdown of the plant life and animals that can be spotted. I absolutely loved how well kept this trail is, several rest stops such as benchs, restrooms and even picnic areas, all well maintained.  This is a great hike for all ages the further you move up the trail the increase of difficulty, but honestly if your a regular hiker its a breeze.  Beautiful views of running water throughout the trail and of course a huge waterfall in its natural stages.

I honestly find it hard to put into words, how beautiful this place really is, so i will definitely show you with my videos and pictures.  This is a great place for all ages, several different levels of hiking trails, great places to go fishing. There are places to camp and near by cabins to rent. You will honestly feel like you walked into a fairytale, full of mystery and ahh. The water is so clean, the birds chearp to a beautiful melody, while you gaze at every shade of green you could ever imagine.

This is a small desert zoo there are a variety of animals/mammals.  Excellent staff, now this is the desert so bring water, sunscreen and snacks maybe even an umbrella.  Weather ranges from 87-115 degrees Fahrenheit. Theres also a really cool butterfly cage. Now if your with a child or elder please bring a mobile chair or comfortable seating. This zoo is excellent for their holiday events. There are extremely helpful to the community and children.

As you enter the park you will get to gaze upon a beautiful tree arch entrance that gently touches the sky allowing the sun to shine through. Throughout the park are several trails, one leading up to a lake, creek, softball field and much more. Surrounding the park are several places to park and a near by restaurant and small shops. Downside to the park you can still hear the noise and construction from the surrounding city.

Okay this is a great spot for Instagramming or possibly running into a celebrity.  This is a hike where you'll actually want to dress nice. Now this spot can get crowded and parking is no joke. Really great trails that keep you in shape also great to take the dogs. There are fountains but do take water. Yes there a bunch of hotties at this spot Male and female.

It was a truly beautiful Japanese garden and an actual pretty cool maze like setting,  easy to navigate around and beautiful to stubble upon random little waterfalls. I would recommend going for a stoll either for a romantic setting, clear your mind or to take super cute photos with friends. Love the Zen of it all, this is a great spot for pictures.

Beautiful park with smooth trail and steep throughout.  There are a couple of trails quite short in distance that lead to: the creek, park, bench area and the beach.  You may see a few homeless routed throughout the park, but honestly it's very well kept and clean overall, with a few dog bag dispensers. The beach area is well kept.

This was a lot of fun, good safety instructors. You'll meet at the bottom of the hill they'll show you how to properly put on the equipment and then take your group along with others in the van. Once your done they drop you right back where you started. There are great little shops near by and good food.

Very small museum,  absolutely loved the shout out to womens rights. It was really cute and clean, very informative and discuss the discrimination done on asain America's in the US.  I suggest stopping by here, i do wish all the pull out drawers had something and maybe a few things outside would be nice.

This is a really unique little spot. I absolutely love the local shops, the food is decent. Great spot for a little romantic weekend or a nice hike with the kids. Beautiful lake and great little trails. It can get a little chilly so bring a jacket. The roads up to idyllwild can be a bit narrow and steep.

This is such a great trail for a good workout,  your abs will love you. This trail has some steep parts, but also a lot of smooth trail you can run through. You will feel very grounded here, nature surrounds you, rock staors throughout the trail. All small hiking trails, you can do a few at a time.

This is a great walk for seniors and children or if your wanting a light jog unders some shade. A beautiful arched trail, with peekaboo creeks and a beautiful architected bridge,  sadly graffitied on. So the reason for the 2 stars is this place literally smells like sewage waste.

A great park area by the waterfront, wonderful place to jog, have a picnic and gather with the family.  They have a beautiful tennis court and a few jungle gym areas for the kids. Great place to take your dog on a run or just to have a little quite area for a romantic kiss.

Wow, just wow this is absolutely beautiful for everyone. There's is a tree where you can sit surrounded by water, and so many shades of blue. A great place for a picnic,  or just a nice swim on a hot day. There is a trail near by and also restrooms located on the premise.

Excellent trail, this was honestly so much fun!! Besides having gorgeous views, the pathways are easy to access really great for either an all day trip or just a quick run. I absolutely loved running about and they even have a couple cool benches randomly placed.

Great park for all, beautiful spot to go on a stroll, kayak, bike or take the kids out. There is a cute little museum and restaurants near by. The kids park had a pirate theme, you can learn to kayak or paddle board.

I mean it's the Dodgers stadium. Dodger dogs do suck the come out cold an the bun is way to small. Soda is 7 bucks water 6 bucks, so definitely bring your own. Always bring a hat its Los Angeles it gets hot.
Ah it reminds me of the titanic,  it's a beautiful building inside. Great spot to take a picture,  since it's so small dont bother with a tour guide you can usually just listen in to someone else's.
A fun spot for children. Its quite small, sometimes free on sundays.  Food trucks usually near by on the weekend.  They have a cool spot inside where you can watch staff working on projects.
Good collection of modern art, great spacious design to be able to view the art at every angle. Can get busy some sundays for the free museum day, please check calendar for times.
Beautiful little trail,  with 1800 style housing along the water.  Beautiful bridges placed over a beautiful huckleberry like waterbend, a really simpleton type of trail.
Great place for families and single mothers. Lifeguards located by swimming area, beaches and near by parking.  Very small area that gets populated quickly in the summer.
Highly recommend this hike, right from the beginning its beautiful. I absolutely love how the water is trickling down the rock path. This is an easy hike for all.
Great spot to go for a girls getaway, bachelorette party, date or fun with friends.  Great wines cute animals and after a fun celebration.

Huge park in the south-metro.  Miles of hiking, biking, and even horse trails.  The entrance off of Johnny Cake Ridge Road (near Cliff Rd) is for mountain biking, the entrance off Cliff Rd. (just west of Robert Trail) has the visitor's center and free beach.  Visit the center to learn about the park, nature, or to rent canoes, paddle-boards, or snowshoes.  Rent a canoe and portage the several lakes wthin the park, or just putter around Schulze Lake near the center.  There are also (at least) two other entrances - Jensen Lake (on Pilot Know and Carriage Hills Dr.) and Holland Lake (off Cliff Rd. and Lexington Ave. S.).  Beautiful in the fall, but accessible year-round.

Nice, big, new playground with all the accoutrements (big slides, swings, tire swing, climbing walls).  Has a new splash pad, drinking fountain, wifi (so the sign says, but I've never tried the wifi), picnic and volleyball area, and soccer fields.  The trail that went over the railroad tracks and through the meadow seems to be blocked off now, maybe because it is near the power plant.  If you are there long enough the kids may see a train go by too.

Includes all the Marvel rides (the Hulk coaster is awesome), and the Dragon Challenge and Hogwarts rides from Harry Potter.  Also has Dr. Seuss land (if you don't have kids under 10, this part may wear thin quickly).  Also, if it is not warm out, do not go on the back half that has all the water rides - you will get wet!

Great for the kids - if you live close I would encourage a season pass for the family.  The kids learn interactively, get tired out, get to play in the water, sand, or other environments, and they always have special exhibits.  The Halloween Party was a special favorite when our kids were younger!

Drove up to Paradise point, 5400 feet above sea level. Beautiful scenery, harrowing drops, from rain to slush to snow during the drive (be careful near the top). Your ears will pop, but you'll be treated to some great views. Pics all taken in one day in mid-October.

What can I tell you that you wouldn't already know?  The iconic statue representing America, donated by the French, cast in bronze but now in its known patina-green.  Audio tours are included in your ticket price, and, of course, you end at the gift shop.

It's diverting for 15-maybe-25 minutes, if you go forwards and backwards.  The kids will love it for sure, but I would not pay full price.  We went went there was a Groupon, and if you look on there (or Living Social, etc.) you'll probably find it.

Just visiting, but the architecture is historic, and the campus is beautiful.  I cannot speak to the actual academics, but if you were looking for that, surely you'd check a professional source and not Google Reviews before you chose a college.

A simulated jungle river cruise, with animatronic animals and natives.  The guides will spount many, many, many puns which may make adults groan, and may go over the heads of the smallest children.  An oldie but a goodie Disney ride.
dislikes: Puns may be unsuitable for young children

reviews_attraction.text: Nice big playground, with a good-sized splash pad as well.  Free concerts during the summer too.  Prepare for the kids to get wet!  When they get all tuckered out, head across Galaxie Avenue to Culver's for some frozen custard.

Great little park with trails leading into the woods, a small playground (with a zip line for the kids), and the Eagan Art House that offers classes.  Within walking distance of retail, restaurants, and grocery to the south.

Fun to look at all the sealife and walk through the underwater tunnels, and even pet stingrays.  Look for the coupons that are stationed around the mall, because even being wondrous, I don't know that I'd pay full price.
It's a nice little neighborhood park - best if you happen to live nearby.  It only has one playground and a large empty lot.  Nice playground, but there is not much to the whole park.
A look at frontier / wilderness life, with a fully restored and working riverview fort.  Displays and demonstrations run throughout the day, and the summer camps are fun for the kids.
Great place for families, dates (who are into that), and, of course, stamp collectors.  The rarest are here, as well as histories, exhibits, interactive tools, and it's all free!
Art from all over the world, throughout history, and special exhibits all the time. Check their website for free admission days, and there are lots of good places to eat nearby.
If, like us, you didn't get your reservations in early enough to go on the White House tour, stop into the Center across the street for the closest experience.  Totally free.
Historic part of history, from JFK's eternal flame, to Medgar Evers' grave, to the Iwo Jim a memorial and many more. Free (unless you do the tram) and a big slice of history.
Nice, well-maintained park - very short walk from Psycho Suzi's (which I would also recommend).  Right by the river with decent views, and the occasional homeless residents.
Great quirky park in the south metro. Regular open hours, lots of art, neat walking paths, all free. Parents go for a different free outing, kids go for all the pokestops.

Decent park - features:
1. 4 tennis courts
2. Good-sized playground
3. A good disc golf course with varying terrain
4. 2 ice rinks
5. 1 soccer field
6. 1 baseball diamond
likes: Varied terrain in disc golf course

reviews_attraction.text: Not really a playing-at park, more of one for reflection.  A little historic pocket of Summit Hill, with a small shelter, a fountain, and a green space.
Tons of exhibits, lots of interactive stuff for the whole family, one of three space shuttles to have gone into orbit, aquariums and special shows.
Shelter, tennis courts, baseball diamond, soccer field, and off-street parking.  Also has a paved walking trail going around the perimeter.
Pleasant park adjoining the waterfront, lots of trees, and the point at where you take the ferry to Ellis and Liberty Islands.

We thoroughly enjoyed our full day tour of this magnificent Mansion,  Meadow Brook Hall, which is a Tudor Revival style mansion that took 3 years to build (1926-1929). It was by Matilda Dodge (Wilson) the Dodge Automaker Heiress and her 2nd husband, Alfred Wilson, a lumber baron. This huge home has 110 rooms and is the 4th largest historic mansion museum in the United States. Plan plenty of time to tour the grounds and building. You must purchase a tour ticket and follow your guide. Public Restrooms and plenty of parking available. The Mansion is also available for special events, weddings, etc.

Too add to my above comments: There were two Dodge Brothers, both contracted Spanish fever and will die from it. John Dodge in 1920. Well John's 1st wife had died from tuberculosis, so he secretly marries his maid then divorces her couple years later, then marries his secretary Eleanor and he dies. His wife Eleanor and sister-in-law sell the Dodge auto company for today's equivalent of $ 2 billion! Eleanor remarries a lumber baron Alfred Wilson and will inherit his fortune as well when he dies! They build this 110 room mansion and it's a doozey! Eleanor was making $ 40,000 PER DAY in the 1920s from her investments! Check out the Tiffany lamps, light fixtures. Uranium based glassware that glows in the dark, liquor cellar with all bottles from Pre-Probition. So much wealth! Got to meet the President running the place. Neat. A lot going on here! A must visit!
Kindly click the like button if this review or my photos are useful.

Was able to visit this Museum in Castine, Maine and see the wonderful collection of my college buddy, Maynard Kufrovich, a local resident.

The Wilson Museum is a museum in Castine, Maine, United States. It was founded using the collection of Dr John Howard Wilson, a geologist.
Wilson lived in Philadelphia, Brooklyn and Nantucket during his youth. He arrived at Castine in 1891 with his mother, Cassine Cartwright Wilson. He received a PhD in geology from Columbia University.

In 1921, Mrs Wilson gave the western part of the land she owned to build a museum for John Wilson's collections. The building was designed by architects Milton See & Son of New York.[1] Three other buildings were added in the late 1960s, the Blacksmith Shop, Hearse House, and the John Perkins House.

Rocks, minerals, shells.
Pre-historic artifacts from North and South America.
Exhibits from Europe and Africa illustrating the development of tools during the early Paleolithic, Neolithic, Bronze and Iron ages.
Six dioramas constructed by Ned Burns of the American Museum of Natural History in 1926.
Cultures of Africa, Oceania, North and South America.
Early weapons and firearms.
Local history.
Ship models.
19th century carpenter's tools, farm and household equipment.
Reconstructed kitchen of 1805 and a Victorian parlor.
Special exhibits every summer using the museum's collections.
Archival material on the history of Castine.

We paid our respect to our 25th President, yet another assassinated, President William McKinley, who died 9/19/1901, 8 days after being shot in the stomach by a crazed anarchist. He is buried here with his beloved wife, Ida, and sadly his 2 young daughters, eldest living to age 4. He is remembered as an above average President the last to be a Civil War Veteran. Once again the American people are outraged as they remember Lincoln (1865) and Garfield (1881). 6 months later the assassin was executed by given 3 jolts of 1,800 volts through electrocution. The warden then had sulfuric acid poured on the body which dissolved the body within 12 hours. Unlike today's punishment.

Nearby is and inside President William McKinley Library and Museum including his death shirt, a talking wax President, chair hat, etc. Just so sad his life was taken.

Free Admittance to McKinley's Tomb but must pay to enter the Museum. Free, ample parking on site. Kid and Disability Friendly but many steps to walk up to the tomb would be difficult for some.

We wound down our visit to the Motor City as we took the Ford Rouge Factory Tour, the world's largest manufacturing complex at one time employing 100,000 workers. Few photos allowed inside and absolutely no photos allowed of their assembly line! We were really impressed at their efficiency, where they build their Ford F-Series Trucks. They currently have  4,000 workers, 2 shifts a day of 1,000 workers, four 10 hour days, with 3 days off, 1 truck is built every minute or 60 per hour, 600 per shift! 7,200 trucks per week all are pre-sold and built per the customer's specifications. Ford Built Tough! GO USA! Well worth the cost and your time to tour! Manufacturing is still alive and going strong in America!

What a wonderful opportunity to learn the living history of the Amish sect.
We took the fabulous tour last August and thoroughly enjoyed ourselves. I was surprised to realize how modern civilization has encroached upon the Amish, with majority no longer farming but accepting retail and other work among the laymen and living in regular homes with a propane tank,  barn and horses in the back. Included is a bus tour stopping at different Amish locations. Our guides were very knowledgeable, pleasant and willing to answer every and all questions from our group. The Amish School House was very interesting. Highly recommend taking the tour.  Kindly click like if you find this post and my photos to be helpful.

Our tour of this magnificent was part of our vacation through upstate New York and New England. We enjoy visiting so many historic homes of the past and Gilded Age. This one is no exception. Although some of the architecture needs some upkeep and maintenance the overall expanse of this huge property makes one wonder how they can manage such an undertaking. Obviously management should be commended. So neat to slip back into time and let your mind wander as you walk the grounds and tour the mansion. We were blessed with a had a picture perfect day. There are gift shops, wine shop, greenhouses, fish ponds and much more to enjoy. Please like my post if you find it coupled with my detailed photos helpful.
likes: Gift shops, wine shop, greenhouses, fish ponds

reviews_attraction.text: Taking the tour of Graceland is the culmination of growing up in the era of the legendary  Elvis Presley. Very impressive how Lisa Marie Presley, Elvis' daughter mainly with the help of her mother Priscilla preserved Elvis' residence where he lived up to his untimely death. He along with father members are buried on the property. We took the VIP tour last fall on a beautiful sunny September day, having stayed at the very nice Guest House while making our bucket list mecca trip to Memphis and Graceland. Elvis like many of us had his own idiosyncrasies. And be aware that there's a whole lot of shaking going on here! And here Elvis has officially NOT left the building.

We toured this facility last summer during our vacation in the area. There is a required fee to tour. Perry's Victory and International Peace Memorial commemorates the Battle of Lake Erie that took place near Ohio's South Bass Island, in which Commodore Oliver Hazard Perry led a fleet to victory in one of the most significant naval battles to occur in the War of 1812.  With replicas and commerative antiques to view. We were blessed with a beautiful, sunny day to take outside photos.

This was the 4th of 5 Mansions we toured one day a couple of October's ago. Another elaborate Manion of the Guided Age, the Elms was built as the summer residence of Mr. and Mrs. Edward Julius Berwind. Edward Berwind was a Coal Baron of his day and the money he accumulated was in part used to construct this marvelous place in 1898. Well worth the admission price, you are given headphones for a self guided tour. Partially wheelchair accessible, public restrooms available on sight.

A must stop if traveling through the area for the historic importance of the 1980 Winter Olympics, especially when considering the USA Hockey Team beat the Russians for the Gold Medal. With 40 years of age, the place is a shadow of its past glory. We were amazed how small the ski slopes actually are. For fun, you can boogie board down a couple of the slopes into a wade pool. We stopped in the gift shop, used their rest rooms and purchased our souvenir tee-shirts.

A highlight of our New England vacation a couple of October's ago, finally got around to posting my review and photos. Need to congratulate the owners for continuing and keeping alive this historic train, the industry which played such an important part of American History. Although an era gone by, everybody should experience this mode of transportation that was an everyday even generations before us. You'll be glad you did.

A nice salute to the legendary Bob Hope, the plaza and sculpture overlooks the waterway and was dedicated on July 8, 2009. It was a joint effort by Bob Hope's family in conjunction with the port of San Diego and the Navy veterans who fought at the Battle of Leyte Gulf.  Very nice. He gave so much of  his time and talent for the enlisted military men stretching through the Vietnam War.

We had a memorable event as we were in town last September and able to partake in the Spirit of Ethan Allen's Harvest Moon Evening Dinner Cruise. We we able to watch the moon rise and set over Lake Champlain. The buffet dinner included  roast turkey with mashed potatoes and apple crisp.   Highly recommend taking any cruise with them. We have a memory that will last a lifetime for us.

Located at 15 2 Lights Terrace, the Two Lights Light House is also known as the Cape Elizabeth Light is at the southwestern entrance to Casco Bay, Maine. The is no physical access allowed at the Light House but can be seen from afar at the near State Park. We were blessed with a beautiful sunny day a couple October's ago when we visited the area.

Built in 1882, this is yet another quintessential New England Covered Bridges deserving a visit. We visited here a couple October's ago while vacationing in the area. Located 1 mile east of NH Rte 12A on Root Hill Road at the foot of Dingleton Hill in Cornish over Mill Brook. It originally cost $ 812 to build the original bridge.

We visited this local tourist attraction as part of our tour of the Heineman Winery as we vacationed here last summer in the area. Very nice to walk down the steps into the cave of minerals. Was not overwhelming having visited much larger caverns in other parts of the country but nice way to spend part of an afternoon.

Genuinely nice walking trail we took advantage of while we visited our daughter and son-in-law a couple summers ago when he was stationed here.
