They rented a place right below the trail on Komo Mai Drive, so it was a short walking distance to here. Glad we hiked it a couple of time. Too bad I forgot to bring my camera.

They proclaim to be the World's Largest Maze, it was fun to walk the grounds and savor the beauty of this area and the islands overall. Well worth the trip here. We did so a couple summers ago when visiting our daughter and son-in-law who was stationed here. This is truly paradise. You must try the pineapple ice cream!

We visited here a couple years ago with our grandson's cub scout group. We walked the loop and enjoyed the huge display of animals inside. Make sure to bring water as it can get very hot along the trail. There is shade along the way but not everywhere and is still hot. Well worth the effort.

The Portland Head Light House is the quintessential of all Light Houses along the North Atlantic East Coast and is adjacent to the Fort Williams Park. We were blessed with a warm sunny day a couple October's ago when we visited here. A must visit when in the Portland area.

We visited President Chester A. Arthur's Memorial Tomb, located in Section 24, Lot 8 to pay our respects to our Nation's 21st President becoming President after James A. Garfield was assassinated. A man with a history filled life, we salute you. May you rest in peace

One of our most favorite beaches in all the Honolulu Area! Was quite busy when we were here quite a few times a couple summers ago when were we visiting our daughter and son-in-law who was stationed here.
Simply beautiful, we stopped along along here as we drove this wonderful Kancamagus Highway a couple October's ago. After days of intense rain, made for some great shots of the high and might river.
Well worth visiting this natural wonder here in Virginia. Visitors from Thomas Jefferson to today we visited summer Pre-Covid and enjoyed our time here.
Beautiful scenic view along the Blue Ridge Parkway near Peaks of Otter. About 30 minutes from our home, we love it every time we drive by here.

I give this National Park 5 stars and I didn't even get to see the cave because it was closed during the COVID-19 pandemic.  This park has a lot to offer beyond the cave.

If you enjoy watching animals in their natural habitat and are willing and able to do a little hiking this is a great park to visit.

In six hours at the park I saw hundreds of prairie dogs, three dozen bison, mule deer, a bobcat, a bunny, a few types of birds and a red squirrel.  I also saw a dozen pronghorns just outside the North gate off 87 at dusk.

I visited in early March and did the the Centennial Trail to Lookout Point Trail loop, Rankin Tower Trail and drove out West on NPS5 (unpaved road) toward Boland Ridge Trail for Bison viewing.

Experiences will vary of course but I highly recommend this park.

A reminder, please do not feed the animals and be sure to keep your distance, especially from bison.  My closer range bison pictures were taken from inside a vehicle driving on the road to a destination.  Bison can run over 30 mph and close in on you very quickly.

I had a great time hiking this trail in early March 2021.  It was nice to feel like we had the trail to ourselves as my partner and I saw less than a handful of other people on the trail.  It was sunny and in the 50s with a mixture of mostly snow with some mud and ice mixed in.  I wore hiking boots most of the way and utilized crampons for a portion on the way down. We took route 9 up and route 4 down (clockwise).  I really enjoyed walking through the pines on the snowy surface and it was fun to see Harney Lookout Tower on the way up to Black Elk Peak.  There are several great views on this trail on the way up and down.  The view from the peak did not disappoint either.  I highly recommend this trail (in off-season late winter conditions).

I struggled between giving this trail a 3 or 4.  I'd probably give it a 3.5 if I could.  The trail had decent views on the way to the destination but nothing all remarkable. There were a lot of wildflowers when I went in mid-April.  The window view at the terminus was cool but sort of underwhelming. The deer that slowly walked across the path ten feet from me on way back was arguably the highlight of the trail.

I'd recommend starting at the small parking lot next to the trail in the campground instead of leaving from the Chisos Visitor Center.  The trail is supposedly great for sunsets.  It is over 5 miles round trip with 800 feet elevation.  It starts off going downhill so be prepared for most of your effort to be on the way back.

This is where tour tickets are acquired to get you inside the birthplace homes at the corner of Presidents Ave & Franklin St. as well as their Peace field home at the corner of Adams St. and Newport Ave.  A wonderful place to go for people interested in history and/or John Adams and John Quincy Adams.  The tour guides are very knowledgeable and the Peace field home is almost all original.  You can bring your camera but no pictures are allowed inside the homes.

I enjoyed the 200+ steps to the top of the monument even though the view from the top was less than spectacular with the small windows and crowded room.

For those of you not sure whether you are up for the climb, there is a railing but  the steps are fairly narrow, there is traffic coming both ways and there are no benches.

You need to get a time slotted ticket from the Bunker Hill Museum (43 Monument Sq) in order to be allowed to climb.

They have convenient parking, close picnic areas, restrooms accessible from outside the building and free WiFi.  Indoors they have an exhibit on the wildlife in the area and typically two rangers present to answer questions.  The ranger I spoke to was pretty noncommittal regarding trail recommendations and did not seem as knowledgeable about the park as I would expect/hope.

Decent trail mostly along the Rio Grande.  There is a restroom at the start of the trailhead but it was locked when I went.  You will most likely get to see burros toward the end of the trail.  I got to see a couple turtles bobbing their heads up out of the water as they floated down the river as well.

Sometimes a great place to sit, relax and enjoy tulips, roses and crab apple blossoms.

Unfortunately over the years a greater number of people come here to swing in their poorly supported hammocks, disturb the quiet with music and let their kids destroy the crab apple trees.

Unfortunately over the years a greater number of people come here to swing in their poorly supported hammocks, disturb the quiet with music and let their kids destroy the crab apple trees.

It's not cheap but it's not just a skyline view either.  Besides the great 360 degree view, especially at sunset, the interior walls are adorned with Boston history.  An audio tour is also part of the price of admission.
There is also a small room with rotating videos.

A short, paved and potentially crowded destination trail to the lower pool.  Maybe it was the time of day/year but I was not as impressed as I was hoping to be.  The view from the bridge over the Virgin River at the start of the trail was arguably a better view.

Visited during the pandemic but even then the Visitor Center was nice.  Beyond the park info on the walls, there is a nice size gift shop.  The park Ranger was very friendly and gave us great hiking advice based on our interests and time available.

Bedesen Park is a nice place for a walk any time of the year.  It can be especially nice on a windy day as you are decently protected by the trees.  Potential wildlife spottings include turtles, ducks, muskrat, geese, owls, squirrels and deer.

A nice short hike with some hoodoo views.  I suggest staying to the left and doing the loop clockwise as it's easier to follow the trail that way.  You can also get a good view from the overlook without walking down to get a closer look.

It is an easy, short jaunt on a boardwalk from the parking lot.  There are a couple informational signs and you can go down a set of steps into the Badlands to hike at your own risk.  The view is definitely worth the short walk.

A short but fun destination trail on the Ross Maxwell Scenic Drive.  There were a healthy amount of blooms when I went and quite a few reptiles.  There are attractive mountain views along the trail, especially at sunset.
It was definitely worth a stop on my way to Capitol Reef from Moab.  The rock formations are fascinating and fun.   If only it was feasible to play hide and seek or paintball amongst the goblins.
A place where you can see great distances on a clear day.  There is a restroom.  If you are fortunate, you will see plenty of live deer along the road the way to and from this point.
Tulips, lilacs, crab apples, roses and more.  Great for a wedding, a picnic, watching the sunset, taking a walk or just a relaxing chat while you take in the view.
Many well organized exhibits packed in a relatively small space.  They have an excellent variety of aquatic life from around the globe.  I enjoyed it thoroughly.
Great place for a hike, especially during sunset when you can often see deer along the treeline of the prairie, great sunsets and brilliant fall color.
Sol Duc is a nice destination trail.  The waterfall at the end is worth the trek.  At the trail head there is a large parking lot and a bathroom.
Fenway is a living museum and a great place to experience a baseball game.  If you are so inclined I recommend a tour of the park as well.
The hike itself wasn't that scenic and when I went it was wicked windy but you go for the destination and it's a really good one.
Small but nice conservatory with a variety of plants and some koi fish.  The periodic butterfly exhibit is very cool.

Joyce was very friendly & informative.
The 2nd floor is available for events with a modest rental fee. The basement is still under construction. The deck (all floors actually) have wonderfully stunning views.
They have a good interactive corner for kids where they can touch things & it's ok! Lol as a parent, this is always wonderful in a museum. The visit can be as quick or slow & laid back as desired.

Do only see myself returning for an event or special showcase/display though.
dislikes: Limited return interest (only for events or special displays)

reviews_attraction.text:
Well marked trail that is just over 2 miles. Depending on how far back you park & how much exploring, it will be about 5 miles of walking. The trail can get muddy, but is doable for families. The youngest with us was 4 years and he did well.

Parking is parallel on side of road entrance. There is pit bathrooms before starting on the trail. There are ups and down on the trail and when getting to Blue Pool there are plenty of rocks to sit upon.

This has been on my bucket list. The hike was not as long as imagined, but there is definitely an incline to it. A full circle is possible, but bottleneck is created abive one of the arches and can be tricky to cross. Do not recommend for children at that point.
We made it down (up to that point) with a six year old girl. A three year old with another 7 year old stayed further back not going down the decline where the bottleneck forms.

Love that there is a trail that takes you to the foot of this waterfall. It also is a round trail, so you don't have to hike back the same way. There are a few spots where people can get good views of the waterfall without walking all the way in (those with difficulty walking or simply tired), but it is an easy trail that is flat (accessible) all the way around.
There are public restrooms near the parking as well.

This is a house converted museum with self-guided tour of local history. It is on three levels, but is made accessible with an elevator. They have many pieces from old ski gear, signs, art, and documents. There is no entrance fee, donations accepted & it also includes a small gift shop. Lady is informative and keeps to herself unless engaged. Good for those who don't like super enthusiastic people on you.

The lighthouse was a great stop to take a picture & hike down to the beach for a bit. However this last time (Nov. 24, 2018), there was no lighthouse & no sign in sight stating why its removal &/or if it is temporary.
The trail going down to the beach also needs some maintenance. The benches along the way are nice for those not going all the way down to the beach & to take a break given it's a bit steep.

Lovely place for a day outing. Worth every bit of going that extra stretch past Oceanside, into the woods, past the spacious/nice parking, down the slope, and finally to the lighthouse. All the views are stunning. There are few benches sprinkled around, two large viewing decks, a picnic area, public bathrooms, more trails heading to the Octopus Tree and another ocean viewing area.

Nice smaller waterfall. The road into it closes during snow season. There is still parking available by the main road (89) and the walk in is about half a mile.
When road is open, you are able to park practically next to the waterfall. There is a view area with benches. There is also a couple pit bathrooms. On the otherside is a campsite and two other waterfalls upriver.

Nice, paved trails around for walking/jogging. Plenty of field space for different games (soccer, baseball, basketball, open space). Small kids playing area & picnic tables good for a birthday party. Wish the trails & parking were better lit for evening/dusk walks. At least to finish without rushing to beat the dark.

Good, clean beach with good sized parking & public bathrooms. Handful of services at walking distance. This part of the beach gets more crowded for the same reason, but hasn't been too bad. If you keep walking south toward Symons State Park (same beach stretch), it gets less crowded. Plenty long to walk and wide.

Little oasis especially in drier season. Bathrooms were good, some picnic tables, few areas to relax for longer, & a good viewing area from above where everyone can enjoy the waterfalls. Getting to the bottom may be difficult for some, but view is gorgeous.

It would be best when all the flowers are blooming. Also plan ahead and make a reservation for hiking, otherwise there isn't access to She Who Watches. There are still other open areas, but make for a shorter stop. Petroglyphs were definitely a bonus.
dislikes: Shorter experience due to restricted areas

reviews_attraction.text: Beautiful spot, wasn't very busy although we weren't the only people there. There was plenty of space. Water is very cold and you can see fishes swimming by. There are good spots to have younger children without them getting into shallow areas.

Great gated playground for kids with two entrances in opposing sides. Well kept and with cameras. It has multiple things to play with for a large age range, but mostly geared toward 3-10 yrs.
There are benches, picnic tables, & bathrooms.

No one else was there and it mostly looks like a spacious area along the road to pull over, not much else.
It is a two minute walk into the creek and waterfall and is worth the stop. Was happy to have all to ourselves.

Easy hike on paved walkway. Has two paths so you can see different things each way. Picturesque lighthouse with amazing views.

The lighthouse is closed during winter months, so I'll need to be back when it does open.

Good, easy, well maintained trails. Wish there was more at the end of Two Rivers View trail even a bench to enjoy reaching the just over a mile hike to get there. The trail does have a few benches along it though.
dislikes: Lack of amenities at trail end

reviews_attraction.text: Great kids playground. It's fenced in with one entry making it more relaxed to let the kids run around and play w/o a hawks eye over them. There are restrooms, picnic tables, and water fountain inside.
Beautiful place with many short and easy trails and a beach. The views are amazing and relaxing. It's a great place to bring small children. Campsites available too.

Great place for a walk, jog, bike ride, or simply go up in car & enjoy the view. It has a nice incline with paved or dirt paths.
There are public restrooms.
Nicely maintained trail. Plenty stairs, but not difficult & the waterfall is stunning. Wish the trail went down & the fence were wood for better aesthetics.
Definitely a magical place with plenty of beautiful spots for peaceful relaxation, trails, picture perfect spots, and more to discover.
Well maintained. Wish the play structures were more shaded considering the vast amount of trees. Plenty of open fields for games.
dislikes: Lack of shading on play structures

reviews_attraction.text: Beautiful stop. Has decent amount of parking, it also isn't a very long stop. It shows a good view of road and curves up ahead.
Nice bridge that is also lit at night. It leads to a nice paved trail with benches and trash bins every so often.

Holy cow, this may be one of the most difficult trailheads to find.  We tried to find it once and gave up, then I came back by myself and finally found it.  The Maunawili Demonstration trail starts off this small pullout parking lot, after the tunnel when traveling towards Kailua on the Pali highway.  After a short walk away from the parking lot, you will find the start of the trail.  The trail takes you along the mountainside with great views.  Part way through the trail, there is a branch that you can take to the Maunawili falls, but if you want to continue, it is almost 9 miles one way.  It is a very lonely trail, only saw one other group during my entire 17 mile round trip (had to turn back because there was a good stretch of trees that had fallen and blocked almost the entire trail for a good 50 years or so.  Also at the beginning of the trail, there is a warning about explosive hazard.  Saw many of these signs around, but I didn't have a problem as long as I stayed on the trail.  Not five stars because it's basically a long hike with mostly the same view, but it is there for people who enjoy long hikes.

Great snorkeling experience, try to get there super early to get the parking and when there is less of a crowd.  Unlike other snorkeling places around the island, there is an admission fee, but it is well worth it.  They also make you watch a short film about how to protect the preserve (e.g. not standing on the coral).  Even so, we unfortunately saw many people standing on the coral.  The best thing to do is find a pathway to the deeper end of the preserve, closer out towards the ocean.  The water is a lot clearer the farther out you go and there are less people you have to swim around.  You are better able to see all the fishes and coral the further out.  Also you might run into other more species such as sea turtles, who you won't get to see when you stay near the beach.  One last thing, several days after a full moon, the jellyfish come out.  Make sure to check the calendar and don't go snorkeling when this event comes up.

Crissy field offers some great views of the Golden Gate Bridge.  There are also several activities nearby that you can participate in (there was a trampoline place, rock climbing place, the Wave Organ).  There is ample parking around as well.  I was there for a group activity and you have to make sure you have everything in your car stored out of sight.  Two different cars very close to where I parked had their cars broken into with a large crowd literally just a few hundred feet away.

Great park with a lot of great views.  We were impressed with the beach, but then we walked around a little bit and discovered the Moli'i Pond, which offered fantastic views of the surrounding area and cliffs.  Also it gave way to a small mangrove forest as well.  It was just very cool to see all these different views in one place.  It was also less crowded as we headed south and west of the park.

Awesome to see the old, but still operation brewery.  There is a free tour that you can join that includes 2 free beers.  You get to see the Clydesdales which is awesome.  There is a restaurant inside that serves decent beer.  Did I mention the free tour and free beer?  It includes one at the end of the tour where you can choose from the numerous brands that are owned by Anheuser-Busch.

The state park area is nice and seems well kept.  There are many trails around, but I feel like the trails are a little overgrown and it is not quite clear which way the trail runs in many locations.  There was a loop trail that we were trying to hike, but we lost the trail and had to head back the way we came.  It does offer some great views of the ocean as well as the valley.

Great place to hike.  The first part of the trail is mostly paved with some interesting bridges that you can transverse over.  You can continue hiking after the paved trail ends (about 3 miles in), however it quickly becomes overgrown and difficult to hike.  There is a small parking lot for you to park in and some restrooms at the beginning of the trail.

Very beautiful beach, it was surprising how we had a great stretch of the beach all to ourselves one day.  There is a nearby Goat island that supposedly you can wade to on a good day, but the day that we were there the waves were rough and it looked too iffy trying to get over to the island, so we just spent time exploring the beach.

The trails were ok, but probably not enough to justify the crowd and the difficulty parking.  We arrived at 8:30am in the morning on a Sunday, and despite four large parking lots, could not find a single place to park because it was so crowded.  Then on the trails, it was filled with even more people.  It was just too crowded.

From the parking lot, it is a short trip to the cave.  It is very cool and dark inside, you should definitely bring a flashlight (I saw many people trying to use their phones, which didn't provide adequate light).  It as a great marvel to look at and explore.  There are small signs inside giving details of the cave.

Awesome botanical garden, very well organized and well kept. There is so much variety here and there is always a rotating exhibit. So much to see that you will easily spend a whole day here and not see everything. The rose garden is definitely worth a visit as they have so many different varieties of roses.

This trail probably can get pretty hot during the summer months.  Some of the trails are closed due to construction and it was not immediately clear so we had to change plans mid-hike.  The dreaded hill is decently steep.  There are also a lot of mountain bikers around, so beware if you are hiking.

Awesome gardens, lots of great variety.  Worth the trip if you are in town.  The tickets are cheaper if you are a St. Louis resident.  Also they host some free music events during the summer that is worth checking out.  Parking can be a little tricky as it can get full quite quickly.

Nice secluded park, a bit of a walk so less people make it all the way out.  We got to see several albatrosses.  Supposedly you can see monk seals sometimes on the beach, but no such luck for us.  It is fairly far from any facilities and water, so make sure you plan ahead.

Some great trails here to hike.  We took the Matt Davis Trail to the Steep Ravine Trail to the Dipsea Trail which went through some great change of scenery and was a decent length hike.  There are a ton of other trails that we didn't try in this large park.

Long arduous hike up the mountain, about 3.5 miles up with about 2000 feet elevation gain, however the top is well worth the hike with stunning views of the valley as well as several waterfalls. Bring plenty of water, food , and a sense of adventure.

Great trails available, however some of them are not very well marked and we got lost a few times and had to turn around on trails that were supposed to be loops.  The shut ins are really cool, try to get to them in the morning before all the crowds.

There are so many different and beautiful plants here. It is also interesting how they have a rotating exhibit that changes. When I went, it was plants from Hawaii. Some of the flowers are so colorful that you think they are fake.

A lot of long trails here, however it almost seemed featureless.  One trail we took just went on and on with the same scenery.  Nevertheless, if you are into long hikes, this place has many trails for you.
Very nice coast line with spectacular views.  Apparently it cost money to go visit the lighthouse so we didn't go (we had already visited another lighthouse on the same day).
Nice park to walk around, includes a small but beautiful Japanese garden. Many areas with park benches to sit down and enjoy a picnic. Close to many restaurants as well.
A lot of good trails as well as variety. There are a ton of signs around, marking all the trails so navigation is fairly easy. Some good variations in sights.
One of my favorite beaches on Oahu, the sand is very fine, accessible with dedicated parking lots.  You can rent a kayak nearby and go explore the waters.
Quite a few interesting trails to take around here, can link there several open space preserves together to have a very long hike.
Quite a few interesting trails to take around here, can link there several open space preserves together to have a very long hike.

(Translated by Google) If you are interested in military history and the Pacific War, then visiting the Missouri Battleship Memorial is an essential trip for Pearl Harbor! Adult tickets are $27/person, and children between 4 and 12 years old are $13/person. The Pearl Harbor package is extra. Tickets include the round-trip fare of the Pearl Harbor Visitor Center to the Missouri Battleship Memorial Shuttle Bus and the Chinese interpretation of the 35-minute Missouri Memorial Hall deck provided by the staff. Before the ticket is checked in, there will be a staff member to take pictures of you, which can be accepted or declined. Finally, they will print out your photos. If you feel satisfied and like, you can choose to pay for it or not. After going to the battleship, there will be staff to ask if you are Chinese, and then arrange a Chinese tour guide. After listening to the explanation of the deck, you can follow the arrow to the inside of the battleship and go up to the top of the battleship. It is highly recommended. Just pay special attention to safety, the space inside the cabin is small, be careful to bump into the head, and pay special attention to the stairs. There are toilets on the battleship and on the shore, and there are gift shops and dining car hawkers on the shore to provide food. The Pearl Harbor Visitor Center offers free parking, but parking on the holidays is tight! It is forbidden to carry bags in Pearl Harbor, so please hide them in the car in advance, or go to the storage at the right side of the gate! The camera can be brought into Pearl Harbor, allowing you to take pictures wherever you go without problems! Before entering the gate, there will be staff to check whether there is a carrying bag. There are three service desks in front of the entrance door. The middle one is free to receive tickets for the Arizona Battleship Memorial Hall (by the time on the ticket to watch the 23-minute documentary. Then take the barge to the Arizona Battleship Memorial. The right desk is for tickets to the Missouri Battleship Memorial, the Pacific Aviation Museum and the Puffin Submarine Museum. You can purchase a package or purchase tickets separately, as appropriate! The left counter is a rental audio guide, available in Chinese for $7.5/person. It is highly recommended to rent a visitor center and the Arizona Battleship Memorial! Because the Missouri Battleship Memorial and the Pacific Aviation Museum are located on Ford Island, it is a military area. People's vehicles are not allowed to enter without permission. Therefore, after purchasing tickets, you need to go to the right-hand station to take the bus to the Memorial Missouri Memorial Hall. The staff will check if the ticket is purchased, although there is also a ticket window at the Missouri Battleship Memorial Hall! Remember that the first stop of the shuttle bus when you stop is the Missouri Battleship Memorial, the second stop is the Pacific Aviation Museum, and when you return, you will also pick up the shuttle bus; you need to remember the shuttle bus when you return. One stop will be the Pacific Aviation Museum. Don't get off the bus (unless you want to get off the bus and visit the Aviation Museum or go to the dining area inside). When you get back to the Pearl Harbor Visitor Center, all the tourists will get off when they get off.

如果你对军事历史以及太平洋战争感兴趣，那么参观密苏里号战舰纪念馆是珍珠港之旅必不可少的行程！成人门票$27/人，4到12岁儿童$13/人 。珍珠港套票另计。门票包含珍珠港游客中心到密苏里号战舰纪念馆接驳车的往返费用以及工作人员提供的35分钟的密苏里号战舰纪念馆甲板中文讲解。检票后上舰前，会有工作人员给你拍照，可以接受或者谢绝。最后她们会把你的照片打印出来，如果你觉得满意和喜欢也可以选择花钱购买或者不买。上到战舰后都会有工作人员来问你是不是中国人，再给你安排中文的导游。听完甲板的讲解后，可自行顺着箭头指示下到战舰的内部以及上到战舰的顶部深度参观，非常推荐。只是需要特别注意安全，舱内空间狭小，小心磕碰到头，上下楼梯也需特别注意。战舰上和岸上都配有厕所，岸上还有礼品店及餐车小卖部提供食物。珍珠港游客中心提供免费的停车场，但在节假日停车位比较紧张！珍珠港内禁止携带包袋进入，所以请提前在车内藏好，或去大门口右边的寄存处寄存！相机可以带入珍珠港内，允许你能去到的地方拍照也没有问题！进入大门前，会有工作人员检查有无携带包袋，进入大门后正前方有三个服务台，中间那个是免费领取亚利桑那号战舰纪念馆门票的（凭票上的时间去观看23分钟的纪录片，再坐接驳船去亚利桑那号战舰纪念馆），右边个服务台是购买密苏里号战舰纪念馆、太平洋航空博物馆及波芬号潜艇博物馆门票的，可以购买套票或酌情单独购买门票！左边个柜台是出租语音导览器的，有提供中文，费用是$7.5/人。参观游客中心及亚利桑那号战舰纪念馆的强烈推荐租一个！因为密苏里号战舰纪念馆和太平洋航空博物馆都位于福特岛上，是军事区域，民众的车辆无许可不可驶入，所以购票后需要前往右侧的接驳车站乘坐大巴车前往密苏里号战舰纪念馆，车站的工作人员会检查是否购票，虽然密苏里号战舰纪念馆处也有售票窗口！记住去时的接驳车停靠的第一站便是密苏里号战舰纪念馆，第二站是太平洋航空博物馆，回来时也在下车地点等接驳车；需记住回程时接驳车停靠的第一站会是太平洋航空博物馆，不要下车（除非想下车顺便参观这个航空博物馆或去里边儿的就餐区进食），等回到珍珠港游客中心全部游客都下车时才下车。

(Translated by Google) Located on the western end of Oahu, Kaena Point is backed by the Waianae range, to the south is the scenic Leeward Coast, and to the north is the famous North Shore. Legend has it that the souls of ancient Hawaiians will enter another world from here and gather with the souls of the lords. In addition to the rich plant resources, the Hawaiian Monk Seal and many species of seabirds live happily here. In the evening, sitting quietly with the people I love, watching the sunset, is a happy thing.
However, the infinite scenery is far away, and it is not an easy task to reach Kaena Point, because it is not accessible by road and can only be reached on foot. There are two hiking trails here: one is from Kaena Beach State Park on the Leeward Coast in the south and arrives via the Kaena Point Trail for a total length of 2.1 miles. The route is more rugged, close to the sea cliffs, and it is dangerous to climb over several landslides. The other is from the end of the North Shore Farrington Hwy, which is about 2.5 miles long. The road is relatively flat and there is a certain distance from the beach.
A few days ago, I saw on the map of Hawaii published in Japan in 1943. It turned out that the railway was here. The sugar cane produced by Kahuku on the north bank was transported to Honolulu via this railway. The railway was built in 1899 but was destroyed by the 1946 tsunami. However, the government has not repaired the railways and built roads here. It may be for military purposes. It does not want to let too many people come here. The military is in the vicinity of the Waianae range. base.
In 2011, the government spent money building a wall at Kaena Po int to protect the flora and fauna that inhabit it. Although many people criticized the wall for destroying the natural beauty here, the number of seabirds that have been inhabited here has increased significantly over the past few years. When playing here, remember not to disturb their comfortable life, otherwise you may violate the laws of the State of Hawaii. Remember to never bring a dog into here, because the dog will attack seals and seabirds, and there will be warning signs at the gates.
Hiking here requires a pair of comfortable sports and leisure activities, prepared food and plenty of water, and of course, anti-mite measures. If you want to watch the sunset here, remember to bring a good headlight or flashlight, there is still a certain danger in the night, and it is best to choose the north line. In addition, there is no wind and wave. Kaena Point is also a very good snorkeling spot (you can see a lot of beautiful fish in the pond on the shore), but the wind and the terrain along the line are more complicated, it is best not to carry out Water Activities.

Kaena Point位于欧胡岛的最西端，背靠山脉怀厄奈岭(Waianae range)，南面是风景秀丽的利华德海岸（Leeward Coast ），北面则是著名的北海岸（North Shore)。传说中古代夏威夷人的灵魂会从这里进入另外一个世界，与先主的灵魂相聚。这里除了生长着丰富的植物资源，夏威夷僧海豹（Hawaiian Monk Seal）和诸多种类的海鸟也幸福的栖息在这里。傍晚时分，与相爱的人静静地坐在这里，看着夕阳西下，是一件夺多么幸福的事情。
不过无限风光在远方，到达Kaena Point也非一件易事，因为这里不通公路，只能徒步到达这里。到这里有两条徒步路线：一条是从南面利华德海岸（Leeward Coast ）的Kaena Beach State Park 出发，经过Kaena Point Trail到达这里，全长约2.1英里。该路线道路较为崎岖，紧临海崖，且要翻越几个塌方点，具有一定危险性。另外一条是从北海岸（North Shore)Farrington Hwy的尽头出发，全长约2.5英里，该路线道路较为平坦，离海边也有一定的距离。
前几日在日本1943年出版的夏威夷地图上看到，原来这里是通铁路的，北岸Kahuku 出产的甘蔗经过这条铁路运到檀香山。铁路建于1899年，却毁于1946年的海啸。不过后来政府再未在此修复铁路和修筑公路，可能处于军事目的的原因，不想让太多的人到这里来，紧靠的山脉怀厄奈岭(Waianae range)里边上各种雷达站等军事基地。
2011年政府花资在Kaena Po int修筑围墙，以保护栖息在这里的动植物。虽然很多人批评围墙破坏了这里的自然美景，不过这几年栖息在这里的各种海鸟数量明显提高。在这里游玩时，切记不可打扰它们惬意的生活，否则您可能违法夏威夷州的法律。切记万万不可带狗进入这里，因为狗会攻击海豹和海鸟，围墙大门处有警示牌。
到这里徒步远足需要一双舒适的运动休闲，备好食物和充足的水，当然还要做好防嗮措施。如果要在这里看日落，切记记得带好头灯或者手电筒，走夜路还是有一定的危险性，并且最好选择北线进出。另外没有风浪时Kaena Point虽然也是一处非常不错的浮潜胜地（在岸边的水塘里就可以观赏到很多漂亮的鱼类），但是沿线的风浪和地形地貌都比较复杂，最好不要进行水上活动。
dislikes: Restricted Activities (No Dogs, Limited Water Activities)

reviews_attraction.text:
(Translated by Google) The long and narrow beaches under the cliff are Diamond Head Beach Park, Kuilei Cliffs Beach Park and Cromwell's Beach from right to left. Due to the rocks and waves in the sea, it is not suitable for swimming in the water. Tourists rarely visit this beach, but it is Surfers' paradise. As the beach is relatively long and narrow, there are three entrances. First of all, you can walk to the beach under the cliff through the trail of the first viewing platform. There is a shower facility at the entrance of the trail beside the road. It should be noted that although the three long and narrow beaches under the cliff are called beach parks, they do not have toilets or changing clothes. Room, lifeguard, etc. The shower facility near the beach at the end of the trail is currently in a state of disuse, so the only shower facility in this area is located at the entrance of the trail next to the road. You can also enter Diamond Head Beach Park through the end of Beach Rd. Beach Rd is a short end-of-head road. You can park on the side of the road. However, the road is relatively narrow and needs attention. In addition, you can also enter Cromwell's Beach through the end of Kulamanu Pl, but you cannot park on Kulamanu Pl. You need to stop at Kulamanu Street next to it.

Diamond Head Beach Park is located under the lighthouse and is mainly a rocky beach. You may encounter people who are illegally basking here, or there may be some tramps who set up tents on the cliffs. However, there is a relatively large tidal pool here, which is good for taking pictures in the water. Many Japanese models have taken photos on this beach.

The sand at Kuilei Cliffs Beach Park is green, and it gleams in the sun due to calcite crystals. When British sailors discovered gleaming things on the beach and on the mountain, they mistakenly thought they were diamonds. This is also the source of the name Diamond Head Mountain.

The sand on Cromwell's Beach is white, and the neighboring houses are multi-million or even tens of millions of dollars. Therefore, the homeless people who set up tents on the cliff behind Diamond Head Beach Park do not spend a penny, and the same sea breeze blows every day. , Looking at the same sea view. Haha.

Except for a small area at the Kuilei Cliffs Beach Park trail, this beach lacks shade of woods. You need to pay attention to sun protection, and it is not recommended to swim in this beach.

©️Hawaiian guide photographer Youli Zhao WeChat: HiHonolulu

(Original)
悬崖下狭长的海滩从右到左分别是Diamond Head Beach Park、Kuilei Cliffs Beach Park、Cromwell's Beach，由于海里礁石以及海浪的缘故，这里并不适合下水游泳，游客比较少造访这片海滩，不过却是冲浪者的天堂。由于海滩比较狭长，一共有三个入口。首先可以通过第一个观景台的步道走到悬崖下的海滩，公路旁步道的入口处有一个淋浴设施，需要注意，悬崖下三个狭长的海滩虽然叫海滩公园，但是并没有厕所、更衣室、救生员等配置。步道尽头海滩旁的淋浴设施目前处于废置状态，所以这个区域唯一的淋浴设施便位于公路旁步道的入口处。也可以通过Beach Rd的尽头进入Diamond Head Beach Park，Beach Rd是一段很短的断头路，路边可以停车，不过道路比较狭窄，需要注意。另外也可以通过Kulamanu Pl的尽头处进入Cromwell's Beach，不过Kulamanu Pl这条路不能停车，需要停在旁边的Kulamanu Street。

Diamond Head Beach Park位于灯塔下，主要是一片礁石滩，可能会遇到在这里非法裸晒的人，也可能有一些把帐篷搭在悬崖上流浪汉。不过这里有一处比较大的潮汐池，在水里拍照挺不错的。不少日本的模特都在这片海滩拍过写真。

Kuilei Cliffs Beach Park的沙子是绿色的，由于方解石晶体的缘故，在阳光的照射下会闪闪发光。当年英国水手发现沙滩上和山上闪闪发光的东西，误以为是钻石，这也是钻石头山名字的来源。

Cromwell's Beach的沙子是白色的，相邻的都是数百万甚至上千万美元的豪宅，所以Diamond Head Beach Park后边悬崖上搭帐篷的流浪汉不花一分钱，每天也吹着同样的海风，看着同样的海景。哈哈。

这一片海滩除了Kuilei Cliffs Beach Park步道处的一小片区域外，缺乏遮阴的树林，需要注意防晒，也不推荐在这片海滩下水游泳。

©️夏威夷导游摄影师Youli赵 微信：HiHonolulu
dislikes: Lack of facilities (toilets, changing rooms, lifeguards)
Presence of illegal sunbathers and homeless people

(Translated by Google) It is currently a very popular hiking trail! Koko Head is located in the eastern part of Honolulu, Oahu, Hawaii, next to the famous snorkeling resort Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve. They are two extinct craters, but the former is higher than the latter. The latter has been covered by sea water to form a bay. In the Koko Head District Park, an abandoned railway track leads to the top of Koko Head, which was built during the Second World War for military personnel and facilities transported to the top of the mountain. There are 1,048 sleepers. . However, it has become a popular destination for locals and tourists on foot. Some people can reach the top of the mountain in 20 or 30 minutes, while others will take more than an hour or even give up. The reason is that the railway is straight up and down. It is mainly divided into two parts. The first half is relatively flat, and many people are still acceptable. The second half of the slope makes many people fearful, and I am full of the momentum of my heaven. At the junction of the first half and the second half, there are tens of meters of aerial railways, and the lower is a gully of three or four meters deep. Many people dare not pass the upper side and can only bypass the small road next to the road. After arriving at the top of the mountain, there are many military facilities such as the abandoned Bunker Observatory, where you can enjoy 360-degree views of the eastern part of Honolulu. Beautiful scenery such as Makapuu Point, Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve, Sandy Beach, and Hawaii Kai are all in sight, and you can see the distance. Diamond Head and Waikiki. At the top of the mountain, you need to pay attention to safety at the same time, try to stay away from the cliffs, and sometimes blow a lot of wind. When I first came to this place, I was not greedy, but when I was gradual, too many brawny were tired on this railway. Both the upper and lower mountains need to pay attention to the sleepers on the railway to avoid being mixed. In addition to this abandoned railway, there are a few wild roads, but it is not recommended. Safety first, do what you can! By Youli Zhao

(Original)
目前是一条非常热门的徒步爬山路线！科科角（Koko Head)位于夏威夷欧胡岛檀香山东部，紧邻著名的浮潜胜地恐龙湾自然保护区（Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve），它们同是两个死火山口，只是前者比后者海拔要高，后者已被海水覆盖形成了一个海湾。在科科角地区公园（Koko Head District Park）有一条废弃的铁路轨道通向科科角（Koko Head)山顶，这是二战时期为山顶的军事人员和设施运输物资所建的，共有1048条枕木。不过这里现在已经成为了当地人和游客徒步健身登高望远的胜地，有的人二三十分钟便可到达山顶，有的则需要一个多小时甚至中途放弃返回。原因是这条铁道直上直下，主要分成了两部分，前半段相对平缓，很多人都还可以接受，后半段坡度则令很多人生畏，大有我天朝华山的气势。前半段和后半段的结合处，还有几十米的空中铁道，下方是三四米深的沟壑，很多人不敢从上边经过，只能绕道旁边的小路。到达山顶后，有许多废弃的碉堡瞭望台等军事设施，在这里你就可以360度的尽情檀香山东部的美景了。玛卡普吾点（Makapuu Point）、恐龙湾自然保护区（Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve）、桑迪海滩（Sandy Beach）、夏威夷凯（Hawaii Kai )等绝世美景尽在眼前，还可看到远处的钻石山（Diamond Head）和威基基（Waikiki )等。在山顶欣赏美景的同时需要时刻注意安全，尽量远离悬崖，有时会吹很大的风。初次到此徒步切莫贪功冒进，当循序渐进，太多壮汉累趴在这条铁道上。上下山都需要注意铁道上的枕木，避免被拌倒。除了这条废弃的铁道，另外还有几条野路上山，但是不建议你尝试。安全第一，量力而行！by Youli Zhao

(Translated by Google) If you are interested in military history and aviation aircraft, then it is still worth it! Tickets for 13-year-old adults are $35/person, and children from 4 to 12 years old are $22/person. The Pearl Harbor package is extra. The Pearl Harbor Visitor Center offers free parking, but parking on the holidays is tight! It is forbidden to carry bags in Pearl Harbor, so please hide them in the car in advance, or go to the storage at the right side of the gate! The camera can be brought into Pearl Harbor, allowing you to take pictures wherever you go without problems! Before entering the gate, there will be staff to check whether there is a carrying bag. There are three service desks in front of the entrance door. The middle one is free to receive tickets for the Arizona Battleship Memorial Hall (by the time on the ticket to watch the 23-minute documentary. Then take the barge to the Arizona Battleship Memorial. The right desk is for tickets to the Missouri Battleship Memorial, the Pacific Aviation Museum and the Puffin Submarine Museum. You can purchase a package or purchase tickets separately, as appropriate! The left counter is a rental audio guide, available in Chinese for $7.5/person. It is highly recommended to rent a visitor center and the Arizona Battleship Memorial! Because the Missouri Battleship Memorial and the Pacific Aviation Museum are located on Ford Island, it is a military area. People's vehicles are not allowed to enter without permission. Therefore, after purchasing tickets, you need to go to the right-hand station to take the bus to the Pacific Aviation Museum. The staff will check if you are buying tickets! Remember that the first stop of the shuttle bus stop is the Missouri Battleship Memorial Hall. The second stop is the Pacific Aviation Museum. When you return, you will also pick up the shuttle bus at the drop-off point. The trip back to the Pearl Harbor Visitor Center is over. There is a dining area in the museum, so don't worry about getting hungry.

如果你对军事历史以及航空飞机感兴趣，那么这里还是非常值得来的！13岁成人门票$35/人，4到12岁儿童$22/人 。珍珠港套票另计。珍珠港游客中心提供免费的停车场，但在节假日停车位比较紧张！珍珠港内禁止携带包袋进入，所以请提前在车内藏好，或去大门口右边的寄存处寄存！相机可以带入珍珠港内，允许你能去到的地方拍照也没有问题！进入大门前，会有工作人员检查有无携带包袋，进入大门后正前方有三个服务台，中间那个是免费领取亚利桑那号战舰纪念馆门票的（凭票上的时间去观看23分钟的纪录片，再坐接驳船去亚利桑那号战舰纪念馆），右边个服务台是购买密苏里号战舰纪念馆、太平洋航空博物馆及波芬号潜艇博物馆门票的，可以购买套票或酌情单独购买门票！左边个柜台是出租语音导览器的，有提供中文，费用是$7.5/人。参观游客中心及亚利桑那号战舰纪念馆的强烈推荐租一个！因为密苏里号战舰纪念馆和太平洋航空博物馆都位于福特岛上，是军事区域，民众的车辆无许可不可驶入，所以购票后需要前往右侧的接驳车站乘坐大巴车前往太平洋航空博物馆，车站的工作人员会检查是否购票！记住去时的接驳车停靠的第一站是密苏里号战舰纪念馆，第二站才是太平洋航空博物馆，回来时也在下车地点等接驳车，回到珍珠港游客中心行程便结束了。博物馆内有提供餐饮的区域，所以不用担心饿肚子。

(Translated by Google) Look at Dinosaur Bay from another angle! The Hanauma Bay Rock Bridge is located in the eastern part of Honolulu, Oahu, Hawaii, next to the famous snorkeling resort, the Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve, which is eroded by sea water. Although it has become a popular secret walking place for locals, the area where the entire hiking route passes is not open to the public, but it is not explicitly prohibited. Not only can you enjoy the different angles of Hanauma Bay along the way, you can also see Koko Head, Hawaii Kai, Maunlua Bay and the Diamond Hill in the distance. (Diamond Head). The beginning of this hiking route is the asphalt roadside, followed by several different wild roads leading to the seaside stone bridge, and the route planning needs to be done in advance. Because you have to make a few steep slopes, you need to pay attention to safety, especially the sections near the cliffs on the sea. There will be several different geological and geomorphological areas. There is a section of road that has a special feeling of being outside the planet. The rocks near the sea are white, because the upper side is covered with sea salt. After arriving at the destination stone bridge, I suggest that you do not try to take pictures on the stone bridge. There will be a big wave at any time. The danger level is too high. There is no chance of surviving when you fall. My favorite level of this route is currently rising to No.1, where you can park your car on the parking lot of the Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve for $1. By Youli Zhao

(Original)
换一个角度看恐龙湾！恐龙湾石桥(Hanauma Bay Rock Bridge)位于夏威夷欧胡岛檀香山东部，紧邻著名的浮潜胜地恐龙湾自然保护区（Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve），石桥由海水侵蚀而成。虽然这里已经成为了当地人热门的秘密徒步地点，但是整条徒步路线经过的区域却不是对公众开放的，不过也未明令禁止进入。一路上不仅可以欣赏到恐龙湾（Hanauma Bay）不同角度的美景，还可以看到科科角（Koko Head)、夏威夷凯（Hawaii Kai)、玛鲁阿湾（Maunlua Bay）以及远处的钻石山（Diamond Head）。这条徒步路线开始的一段是沥青路边，之后则是几条不同的野路通往海边石桥了，需要提前做好线路规划。因为要下几个比较陡的坡，所以需要注意安全，特别是临近海边悬崖的路段。会经过几个不同的地质地貌区，有一段路特别有在外星球的感觉，临近海边的岩石则是白色的，因为上边铺面了海盐。到达目的地石桥后，建议你不要尝试到石桥上去拍照，随时会有大浪袭来，危险程度实在太高，掉下去绝无生还的机会。这条路线我最喜欢的程度目前上升到No.1，到这里徒步可以将车停车恐龙湾自然保护区（Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve）的停车场，停车费$1美元。by Youli Zhao

(Translated by Google) The Banzai Pipeline is located on the North Shore of Oahu. There is also a name called Ehukai Beach Park. It's just that Banzai Pipeline is too famous, so everyone only remembers it. The giant wave of the tube is a description of the huge wave here in winter. The long live pipeline is the literal translation of the Banzai Pipeline. Every winter, this place is known as the most perfect surfing place in the world. It has the most ferocious and biggest waves in the world. Of course, it is also the most dangerous. Many professional surfers and photographers on the beach are buried here. But it still attracts the world's best surfers to show their talents, and the world's most famous surfing competitions will also be held here. Due to the special geological structure at the bottom of the Banzai Pipeline, giant waves will form a tube here, and surfers will rush into these tube-shaped giant waves. If you travel to Hawaii in winter, you must visit here, but you need to stay on the beach honestly and be alert to sudden waves. In summer, it will look calmer, and the area of ​​the beach will become larger. There are public toilets and shower facilities, and parking spaces are sometimes tense.

(Original)
筒状巨浪（Banzai Pipeline）位于欧胡岛北岸(North Shore),这里还有个名字叫伊胡凯海滩公园（Ehukai Beach Park)。只是Banzai Pipeline太出名，所以大家都只记住它了。筒装巨浪是对这里冬季巨浪的形容，万岁管道才是Banzai Pipeline的直译。每年的冬季这里被誉为世界上最完美的冲浪地点，有着世界上来势最凶猛以及最大的巨浪，当然这里也是最危险的，许多专业的冲浪者和沙滩上的摄影师葬身这里。但它还是吸引着全世界最优秀的冲浪者前来大展身手，全球各种最知名的冲浪比赛也会在这里举行。 由于Banzai Pipeline海底特殊的地质构造，巨浪在这里会形成筒状，冲浪者会冲进这些筒状巨浪里。冬季到夏威夷旅游一定到造访这里，但需老老实实呆在沙滩上并时刻警惕突如其来的巨浪。夏天这里会显得比较平静，沙滩的面积也会变大。有公共厕所及淋浴设施，停车位有时会比较紧张。

(Translated by Google) Kaiona Beach Park is located on the southeast coast of Oahu Island, and the adjacent Waimanalo Beach Park and Bellows Field Beach Park form the longest beach on Oahu Island. Kaiona means fascinating ocean in Hawaiian, and it is indeed worthy of its name. When the weather is clear, the sea is really beautiful and very charming. In particular, there are some remaining seawalls in the sea here, which block the waves. The seawater in the seawalls is very clear, and the sand at the bottom is also good. It is especially suitable for swimming and relatively safe. In the seawall is the pond where the former chiefs raised sea turtles for food. The park is equipped with parking lots, toilets, changing rooms, picnic tables, and shower facilities. There are also many trees on the beach to provide shade, but there are no lifeguards. There are usually fewer people here, and tourists rarely visit this beach, but on weekends and holidays, there are all nearby residents, and parking spaces are tight. In addition, Obama has a mansion behind the seawall under construction, and the Obamas will be residents here in the future.

©️Hawaiian tour guide photographer Youli Zhao WeChat: HiHonolulu

(Original)
Kaiona Beach Park位于欧胡岛的东南海岸，与相邻的Waimanalo Beach Park以及Bellows Field Beach Park组成了欧胡岛上最长的一个海滩。Kaiona在夏威夷语里的意思是迷人的海洋,这里也确实名副其实，天气晴朗时，海真的非常的漂亮，非常的迷人。特别的是这里的海里还有一些残存的海堤，它们阻挡了海浪，海堤里的海水非常清澈，水底的沙也不错，特别适合游泳，也相对安全。海堤里是以前的酋长养海龟来食用的池塘。公园配有停车场、厕所、更衣室、野餐桌以及淋浴设施，海滩上也有许多树可以遮阴，不过没有救生员。这里平时的人比较少，游客很少会到这个海滩，但一到周末和节假日就全是附近的居民，车位比较紧张。另外奥巴马有一栋位于海堤后面的豪宅正在建设中，奥巴马夫妇未来将是这里的居民。

©️夏威夷导游摄影师Youli赵 微信：HiHonolulu
likes: Equipped facilities (parking, toilets, changing rooms, picnic tables, showers)
dislikes: Tight parking on weekends and holidays

reviews_attraction.text:
(Translated by Google) Laie Point is located in Laie, North Shore, Oahu, Hawaii. The detailed name is Laie Point State Wayside. Close to the famous Polynesian Cultural Center and Brigham Young University-Hawaii, transfer to Anemoku St at the intersection of Laie Shopping Center and transfer to Naupaka St. The wind and waves here are very large, not too close to the cliff, the rocks are undulating and very sharp, walking on the top, remember to pay attention to safety. There are several small islands next to it. The ancient legend of Hawaii was formed by the remains of a corpse of a samurai who killed the lizard. The sea is not dry and the stone is rotten. The island with an arch near is called Kukuiho'olua l., the other is called Mokualai l. Laie Point is not only an indispensable attraction for visitors to the North Shore of the North Shore, but also a destination for local fishing. Sometimes you can see that there are many local youths jumping on the cliffs next to the sea, which is very exciting. Pay attention to safety when playing here, and the unreliable cliff is too close.

(Original)
拉耶点（Laie Point）位于夏威夷欧胡岛北岸（North Shore)的拉耶（Laie)，详细的地名是Laie Point State Wayside。紧邻著名的波利尼西亚文化中心（Polynesian Cultural Center)和杨百翰大学夏威夷分校（Brigham Young University-Hawaii),在拉耶购物中心（Laie Shopping Center)的路口转入Anemoku St再转入Naupaka St便可到达。这里的风浪非常大，不可太靠近悬崖边，礁石起伏不平且非常锋利，行走在上边，切记注意安全。旁边有几个小岛，夏威夷的古老传说那是以前一个武士杀死蜥蜴神后其尸体残部所形成的。海未枯，石烂了。近处有个拱门的那个小岛叫Kukuiho'olua l.，另外一个叫Mokualai l.。 拉耶点（Laie Point）不仅是游客到北岸（North Shore)大环岛不可缺少的一个景点，也是当地人海钓的一个胜地。有时你还可以看到有许多当地的青年在旁边的悬崖上往海里跳，非常的精彩。在此游玩需注意安全，万不可靠悬崖太近。

(Translated by Google) Kailua Beach Park is also a very long beach, about 4 kilometers long! The waves here are small all year round, suitable for swimming, and the sand is very good, white and delicate. There is a small island called Popoia Island nearby, which can be landed by kayak. The beach park is equipped with parking lots, lifeguards, toilets, and shower facilities, as well as a special estuary landscape. The river flows to the sea sometimes is not connected to the sea and is blocked by the beach, thus forming a visual inflow river. The beach park has many woods and is a great picnic spot! The Kailua community is the largest town on the Windward Coast of Oahu. It has beautiful beaches and various seaside luxury homes. Former President Barack Obama returns to Hawaii every Christmas to live on this beach. villa. In addition to water sports such as kayaking and windsurfing, many Japanese tourists will go cycling in Kailua. There are various supermarkets, restaurants and many other shops near Kailua Town Center. But the influx of tourists brought a lot of annoyance and disgust to the local residents! by Youli Zhao

(Original)
凯卢阿海滩公园（Kailua Beach Park）也是一个非常长的海滩，约有4公里长！这里全年海浪较小，适合下水游泳，沙质也非常好，洁白细腻。近处有一个小岛叫Popoia Island，可以划皮划艇登陆。海滩公园配备了停车场、救生员、厕所及淋浴设施，还有一道特殊的河口景观，河流流到海边有时却未与大海相连，被沙滩阻隔，从而形成了视觉上的内流河。海滩公园有许多树林，是不错的野餐地点！凯卢阿（Kailua）社区是欧胡岛向风海岸（Windward Coast)最大的一个城镇，这里拥有着漂亮的海滩、各种海边豪宅，前总统奥巴马每年圣诞节回夏威夷也是住在这边的海边别墅。除了皮划艇、风帆冲浪等水上运动，很多日本游客会在这边骑自行车游也是凯卢阿（Kailua)。凯卢阿小镇中心（Kailua Town Center）附近拥有各种超市、餐厅及其它诸多的商店。但是大量的游客涌入，却给当地居民带了不少烦恼及反感！by Youli Zhao

(Translated by Google) Solvang is located in Santa Barbara County, north of Los Angeles, 130 miles from Los Angeles. In Danish, Solvang means “the field of bathing in the sun”, but Solvang has only nearly 100 years of history. In 1911, several Danish immigrants bought this unremarkable land and built a school to allow their children to receive traditional Danish education while they were engaged in farming. There are more and more Danish immigrants living here, and around this school, this Solvang, which is separated from Denmark, forms an exotic town with a typical Danish style today.
From Los Angeles, all the way to the north through the 101 high-speed, 154 and 246 roads to Solvang. Today, Solvang is already a famous tourist attraction in central California. The residents of the whole town are basically engaged in tourism-related work and have considerable income. It was said that the Danish king visited the United States that year.

(Original)
Solvang位于洛杉矶以北的圣塔芭芭拉县境内，距离洛杉矶130英里。在丹麦语中Solvang的意思是“沐浴在阳光下的田野”，不过Solvang只有近100年的历史。1911年几位丹麦移民买下了这块当时毫不起眼的土地，并在建起了一座学校，为的是让他们的子女在从事耕作之余能够接受传统的丹麦教育。渐渐的居住在这里的丹麦移民也越来越多，围绕着这所学校，这个与丹麦相隔万里的Solvang就形成了今天具有典型丹麦风情的异域小镇。
从洛杉矶出发，一路向北经过101高速、154公路和246公路便到达了Solvang。如今的Solvang已经是加州中部著名的旅游景点，全镇的居民基本从事旅游相关工作，收入可观。话说当年丹麦国王访问美国也曾造访过这里。

(Translated by Google) Located on the southernmost tip of the Hawaiian Islands, the island is the largest of the archipelago, so it is also known as the Big Island. The island of Hawaii is a magical place. In addition to the polar climate and desert climate, it has all the world's climatic zones and the world's largest active volcano. On the same day you can surf the sea off the island of Hawaii or go skiing up the mountain. The cow is hurting.
South Point is located at Ka Lae, the southernmost tip of the island of Hawaii, and is the southernmost tip of the 50 states of the United States. Blue sky, white clouds, sea, pasture, here is one of my favorite places. However, the wind here is really big. I accidentally dropped a piece of rubbish on the ground. It was too late to go and smashed. So I took it with a hat and picked it up here.
These cows live true TMD happiness, this is a five-star home, living in a sea view room.

(Original)
夏威夷岛位于夏威夷群岛最南端，是群岛中最大的一个岛屿，所以又称大岛。夏威夷岛是一个神奇的地方，除了极地气候和沙漠气候，其拥有世界上所有的气候带，还拥有世界上最大的活火山。在同一天你可以在夏威夷岛下海冲浪，也可以上山滑雪。牛逼疼了。
而South Point则位于夏威夷岛最南端的Ka Lae，也是美国50个州领土的最南端。蓝天、白云、大海、牧场，这里是我最喜欢的地方之一。不过这儿的风真的很大，不小心掉个垃圾在地上，根本来不及去捡，就被吹跑了，所以戴帽子啥的在这儿就摘了吧。
这些牛生活得真TMD的幸福，这就是一个五星级的家，住的都是海景房。

(Translated by Google) Weimea Bay Beach Park Located on the North Shore of Oahu, Weimea Bay Beach Park is very calm in the summer and fierce waves in the winter. There is also a Waimea River that enters the sea from here, so there is also a unique landscape. Sometimes the river will open the beach and connect it to the sea, sometimes it will be blocked by the beach into an “inflow river”. There is a large rock next to it. Although it is forbidden to jump from the rock to the sea, the old Americans and the locals are generally not very obedient. Whether you are lying on the beach or in the water in the summer, or picnicking on the picnic table on the lawn, watching the sunset and watching a group of people performing cliff diving are good experiences. There are public toilets and showers, and parking spaces are sometimes tense.

(Original)
Weimea Bay Beach Park 怀梅阿湾海滩公园(Weimea Bay Beach Park)位于欧胡岛北岸（North Shore),夏季这里海面非常平静，冬季则是凶猛的巨浪肆虐。还有一条怀梅阿河（Waimea River）从这里入海，所以还有一道独特的景观，有时河水会将沙滩冲开与大海相连，有时则会被沙滩所阻行成一条“内流河”。旁边还有一大块岩石，虽有明令禁止从这块岩石上往海里跳，不过老美和当地人一般都不怎么听话。夏季在这里不管躺在沙滩上或水里，还是在草坪上的野餐桌上野餐，看着日落，看着一群一群的人表演悬崖跳水，都是不错的体验。有公共厕所及淋浴设施，停车位有时会比较紧张。

Children aged 3 and under are free 4 to 12 Older children (must be accompanied by an adult) $5/person 13 to 64 years old adult $12/person 65+ older or disabled $5/person Hawaiian 13 to 64 year old resident $8/person can book tickets in advance on their official website You can also use the cash or bank card to buy tickets on site. Margaret's Way Trailhead is a hidden gem in the Issaquah Alps. Unlike the other area trailheads, Margaret's Way Trailhead has a large parking lot and several structures from its past life as a campground.

Some of what you'll find includes an old office building, tennis/basketball court, a clubhouse with a filled-in pool in the back, a sign welcoming you to the "Issaquah Highlands," and the remains of several other unidentifiable structures. Buried under straw, or hidden under a beautiful canopy, you'll find even more remnants of the old campground, including level camping spots, power connections and water taps (dry). NOTE: Camping is no longer permitted at this park.

Back on the main trail, you'll be taken up the mountain via a combination of old campground roads and new trails. As you near the top, you'll find a remnant of the mountain's logging past, vast areas of new growth trees. Continuing onward, you can take an unmarked side trail (built trail) to an outstanding panoramic view of the valley. Continuing on the main trail connects you with the rest of the Squak Mountain Trails, including Debbie's View.

The Cougar-Squak Corridor is an amazing area for a hiking, and Margaret's Way Trailhead is an excellent place to start your journey.

Annapolis Rock and Black Rock are amazing viewpoints along the Appalachian Trail. For those thru-hiking, Annapolis Rocks offers first-come-first-served campsites and a couple composting privies. A pipe stuck into the mountainside provides access to a fresh mountain stream. Rock climbing on the face of Annapolis Rock is popular. Black Rock is a couple miles down the trail and provides a similar view, but without the campsites and privies.

The scenery is beautiful, but the ease of access has made it especially easy for those that could care less to pollute the area and damage the environment. Please do your part and pack out any trash you pack in, follow the other leave no trace principles and, if possible, help the Potomac Appalachian Trail Club out by taking out trash left by other, less considerate, visitors.

Rattlesnake Ledge is a great hike that everyone who can hike should do at least once. It's a short hike with only 1100 feet of elevation gain and panoramic views across the region.

The major downsides include the narrow trail and crowds of people hiking, many of which have no concept of trail etiquette and can significantly degrade the experience. The parking lot is always packed, which I suppose is a positive indicator that so many people in the region want to get out on the trails, but the journey to find a parking space can further degrade the experience.

Nevertheless, the views, lush forest, and relative isolation make it worth it. If you're not up for hiking, there are picnic areas down near the lake.

Mitchell Point has a sweeping view of the Columbia River right from the parking lot. It's also right off the highway, so it's easy to get to. If you want to challenge yourself, head up the trail to Mitchell Point. The trail isn't very steep, but a lot of it involves switchbacks across a scree pile with an unmarked, flattened, trail. The rocks are loose, so watch your footing. There's also a substantial amount of poison oak surrounding the trail. It's everywhere you look; try not to step off the trail. Even if you stop before you reach the top, the views along the way are still amazing.

Park:
Beautiful park with well kept trails. Relatively low elevation gains and the possibility to loop back at several points via an easy service road make this park great for families and solo hikers that want to error on the side of caution.

Trailhead/Parking Lot:
Easy to get to trailhead with a mostly paved lot and two pit toilets. I've found parking on rainy winter days, but this lot isn't too big and probably fills up quickly on summer weekends. There isn't a good overflow area, so you might want to have a plan B if you're heading here mid day on a warm summer weekend.

Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest encompasses a massive area with unequivocal beauty and access ranging from groomed trailheads and trails to deep wilderness. Pristine lakes await those who dare to climb to the top of peaks just to see what's there. Whether you want to ski, hike, bike, swim, sunbathe, picnic, rock climb, meditate, etc, this forest offers it all. No matter what your adventure entails, remember to always carry the 10 essentials and practice the leave no trace principles. As John Muir once said, "The mountains are calling, and I must go."

Beautiful park with a lot of trails to choose from. The park is set up for hikers, mountain bikers, and equestrians. Lots of intermittent streams across trails can make it a muddy trip, but then again, was it really a good hike if you don't go home with your boots covered in mud? I liked the name of one trails in particular, "Ear Therapy," which starts/ends in a peaceful field with a pond created by a beaver dam and a stream under a bridge.

A beautiful spot for a picnic. This park is very busy on a regular basis, so come early to get a parking spot and remember that everyone is there to have a good time. Remember to leave no trace and, if possible, leave the park in a better condition than you found it (e.g. pick up trash). If you're up for a hike, check out the trail up to Rattlesnake Ledge which overlooks the park below.

Marina Park is a hidden treasure. It has a soft sandy beach for playing in the water, a large picnic pavilion, public artwork, close proximity to great restaurants and shops, and a public restroom. Occasionally you'll find a local producers market set up in the grassy areas. Free parking is hard to find, and paid parking fills up. Park nearby and walk into the downtown area if you can.

A great launch point for countless of hikes on Tiger Mountain. The main lot is big, but the gravel road leading up to it has a lot of very deep pot holes in it. Parking is also unofficially available along the road just outside the gate. Do the right thing and get a Discover Pass anyway. The main trail head has pit toilets, an information kiosk, and an educational pavilion.

Henry Coe State Park is a huge park with an extensive trail system that's open to a wide variety of uses, including car camping, picnicking, horseback riding, and mountain biking. During the summer, the temperatures are much higher than the valley below, and water sources you can purify on the trail are scarce, so make sure you pack more water than you think you'll need.

Wonderful park with a huge amount of open space. Sports fields, playgrounds, and jogging trails provide recreation options for most people. Parking can be tough and often overflows into the streets of the nearby neighborhoods. If you have to park in one of the neighborhoods, please drive carefully and park responsibility in legal spots.

Nice park that's easy to get to and typically has plenty of parking. There are a few different routes you can take, but your choices are limited. The trails are mostly exposed. There's western poison oak in every conceivable spot off of the trail, so don't do any bushwhacking here.

Beautiful centerpiece to Leavenworth's downtown. There's always something going on in the park. You might find music, bounce houses, a car show, an art show, or all of them at once. This park is also a wonderful spot to rest for a bit and enjoy the scenery.

Wonderful park with fantastic views. The terrain isn't challenging, so it's great for jogging. Since all of the marsh areas are protected, wildlife is plentiful. The only downsides are the terrible smell from the salt marshes and the lack of shade.

Bridle Trails State Park is a beautiful park tucked in behind horse farms. The park is small, but feels endless. Watch where you step, the park's primary users are equestrians. Also remember to yield right of way to equestrians if you're on foot.

Welcome to Ichetucknee Springs State Park

The crystalline Ichetucknee River flows six miles through shaded hammocks and wetlands before it joins the Santa Fe River. In 1972, the head spring of the river was declared a National Natural Landmark by the U. S. Department of the Interior. From the end of May until early September, tubing down the river is the premier activity in the area. In addition to tubing, visitors can enjoy picnicking, snorkeling, canoeing, swimming, hiking, and wildlife viewing. Scuba diving is available daily in the Blue Hole only (you MUST be Cave Certified). White-tailed deer, raccoons, wild turkeys, wood ducks and great blue herons can be seen from the river. Picnic areas, equipped with tables and grills, are available throughout the park. A full-service concession offers food, refreshments, and outdoor products from Memorial Day through Labor Day. Tubes plus snorkeling and diving equipment can be rented within the park or from private vendors outside the park located four miles northwest of Fort White, off State Roads 47 and 238.

Directions to Park

Ichetucknee Springs State Park is located four miles northwest of Fort White, off State Roads 47 and 238. From the south, take I-75 north to exit 399. Take US 441 north to the city of High Springs. Take US 27 north to Ft. White, stay on US 27 north approximately 4 miles to the South Park Entrance.

Click Here for Summer Tubing Instructions

The South Take-Out gate is closed to traffic during peak visitation times and during the summer months (Memorial Day to Labor Day). It is accessible from the river for tubers/paddlers- use the Concession Tram service or hiking trail to get to the South Entrance Parking Lot.

During the summer months (Memorial Day to Labor Day) you may experience longer than usual wait times to enter the park.

Ichetucknee Springs State Park is featured on the Firsthand Florida Fun Blog. Experience this park with Erika Z.’s YouTube video and check out past blog posts from other Florida State Parks.

Henry Morrison Flagler Biography
Henry Morrison Flagler was born on January 2, 1830 in Hopewell, New York, to Reverend and Mrs. Isaac Flagler. At the age of 14, after completing the eighth grade, Flagler moved to Bellevue, Ohio where he found work with his cousins in the grain store of L.G. Harkness and Company, at a salary of $5 per month plus room and board.
In 1852 Henry Flagler became a partner in the newly organized D. M. Harkness and Company with his half-brother, Dan Harkness. The following year, on November 9, he married Mary Harkness. They had three children, Jennie Louise, Carrie, Henry Harkness. Unfortunately, only Henry Harkness would survive to have children, one of which would later establish the Flagler Museum.
In 1862, Henry Flagler and his brother-in-law, Barney York, founded the Flagler and York Salt Company, a salt mining business in Saginaw, Michigan. When the Civil War ended however, salt, which had been in heavy use as preservative by the Union Army, was no longer in high demand and Flagler and York Salt Company collapsed. Heavily in debt, Flagler returned to Bellevue, Ohio - his initial investment of $50,000 and an additional $50,000 he had borrowed from his father-in-law and Dan Harkness were lost.

Located at the headwaters of the Wekiva River, the beautiful vistas within this park offer a glimpse of what Central Florida looked like when Timucuan Indians fished and hunted these lands. Just one hour from most central Florida attractions, Wekiwa Springs offers visitors the opportunity to relax in a natural setting, enjoy a picnic, or take a swim in the cool spring.

Thirteen miles of trails provide opportunities for hiking, bicycling, and horseback riding. Canoeists and kayakers can paddle along the Wekiva River and Rock Springs Run.  Canoe and kayak rentals are available from the park's concessionaire.  Options for camping include a full facility campground and primitive camping areas.

This is a very popular park, particularly on summer weekends. To ensure entrance, we recommend arriving early; otherwise, the parking area will be full and you may not be able to enter.

A stroll down Savannah’s Riverwalk is not only pleasing, it’s truly serene. Walk along the Savannah River; stop in for a bite at any of 21 restaurants or simply enjoy the scenery as you head towards the adjoining River Street, just a short distance away. On River Street, in the heart of historic Savannah, you’ll find everything from sweets to teddy bears, Harley Davidson apparel, and art galleries housed inside restored Cotton Warehouses. The working harbor—filled with ships of all kinds, horse-drawn carriage rides and street performers add to the enticement of this idyllic waterfront locale.

The Okefenokee National Wildlife Refuge was established in 1937 as a "refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife".  The Okefenokee is like no other place on earth, where natural beauty and wilderness prevail.  The vision for Okefenokee National Wildlife Refuge is to protect and enhance wildlife and its habitat, ensure integrity of the ecological system, and embrace the grandeur, mystery, and cultural heritage that lead to an enrichment of the human spirit.

I saw many time some family came for only free food and without any donation they went out i really felt very bad.

The Ernest F. Coe Visitor Center is open 365 days a year. It offers educational displays, orientation films, and informational brochures. Special collections by local artists are often displayed. Books, film, postcards, and insect repellent may be purchased in the adjoining bookstore. A series of popular walking trails begin only a short drive from the visitor center. Restrooms are available.

Today i went first time take visit in park.. Really its very very convenient for all  ages. Play ground for children's , BBQ and picnic spot, benches.. And also free parking :-).. Shower for after beach play, Public restroom and also life guard on duty. I did not see any negative in this park. Defiantly tomorrow  i will go with my family for BBQ picnic.

This is first time i saw this type of natural garden...You can see plant and tree of vegetables and fruits. Lots of variety of another plant.. Small lake and in lake you can see orange and black fist and tortoise even you can feed this animals..  Garden is too clean and maintain.. You feel like you are walking in small jungle.:-)
likes: Small lake with fish and tortoises

reviews_attraction.text: Oceanfront park beach is open 365 days a year from sunrise to 9:00 p.m. Lifeguards are on duty from 9:00 a.m. - 5:00 p.m. The staff is certified or licensed as First Responders or EMT’s. . Designated surfing and skim board areas are located at the north and south end of the beach.

I was went first time in 2011 in Diwali festival. Its huge prasad "CHHAPAN BHOG" its very very beautiful manage. I saw first like this. and after pooja they arrange cafeteria for fast food. it is very delicious dishes typical gujrati snack. I did lots of enjoy.

Its a amazing tubing experience.. i had never been this type of experience.. i went many times and every times i got new good experience it is look like water rafting :-). I loved this place and good for all ages people.

Great Place For Fellow Naturists In The Am. Beautiful Nature Trails. A Great Place For Those Who Live The Clothing Optional Lifestyle.Please UseCaution As Most People Arent Used. To The Clothing Optional Lifestyle.
Great place for yoga, medication and walkie-talki . Great place for soccer the fields are all turf. Tennis is great 4 courts and two basketball cats. Kids playground.
It's a nice temple. Well-equipped. Has most of the Hindu gods. Hosts may volunteer events and free yoga classes and some literature classes for kids over the weekends
likes: Facilities & Services (Well-equipped, volunteer events, free yoga classes, literature classes)

reviews_attraction.text: It's a small park BUT nice sea view and deck. Some time live music and showing movie .Lots of free parking space and good for marina

This place was great. They had a lot of things to purchase like presidential cards, food, drinks, books, etc. etc. etc. There were so many little things being sold here that were cool that it was hard to choose just a couple things to purchase. The person checking us out was super helpful, friendly, and inviting. They also have a lot of history information in this little area and it made our time here even more worthwhile. Glad we stopped off here. They had way more to offer here then I imagined they would and they're only a couple blocks away from the incline and right next to Point Park.

we had an extremely informant docent who told us everything we could possibly learn about Susan B. Anthony. I learned a bunch of valuable information and she reinforced the things that should be taught more in history class. definitely a place to check out if your visiting Rochester, it’s in a convenient location and they do have parking. The prices aren’t that bad, either. Pictures are permitted too. You get a tour of the whole house and learn so much. they also have nice souvenirs you can get at the gift shop as well.

This is a very unique ride and a fun experience. It is especially nice when it is all decorated for the holidays because they do a very good job with it. It’s a very educational ride, a pretty long one and you definitely get your worth since there is a lot to see. The greenhouse is very fascinating and it’s cool to see how they grow all their vegetables. It’s very organized and interesting. The lines generally are not long for this ride at all. Definitely recommend!

To me $7 seems like too much to visit such a small area. The history is interesting of course but they give you the same information inside pretty much as they do outside of the park. If you're a National Park Pass holder then you get in for free but unfortunately we did not have that at the time. The view here is iconic though and absolutely stunning from above. That in itself would make it worth visiting.

Visiting the U.S. Capitol is an experience that should not be passed up. There's incredible views, picture taking opportunities, and much history to learn. Unfortunately, our tour guide was quite rude but it didn't get in the way of having a good time. Even had the chance to walk right by Speaker of the House Paul Ryan. That's certainly not something that happens every day!

There is a great selection of restaurants, shops, and rides inside Epcot’s World Showcase. They have festivals going on every now and then in here, including the arts festival or the food and wine experience. There are many places to stop and relax as you are walking around. It’s nice that it’s in a big circle so you can get through the whole park easily.

They have some interesting pieces here. I think I would've enjoyed it more if it were more engaging, and it's a little smaller, and not as much to see as I had originally expected. Their collection was vast and unique and the outdoor section was pretty. It's a neat experience to check our, but I don't know if it would be worth visiting several times.

Very lovely site right along the water, perfect location. Nice place to come and visit and camp at. The only concern I had was that I noticed several wasps around the camp site which was troublesome considering allergies within the family. Other than that it’s a good find and worth visiting. The said is orange there too, so fascinating.

It's a nice little park. I'm not from the area and I just needed a rest stop, essentially. It's a lively little area. The one Thursday afternoon I was there, there were a lot of people and children, running around the park, but not in a bothersome way. It's a quite and relaxing area.

A definite place to stop and visit while in Chicago, but really not much to do and see here other than the Bean. A great place to take pictures, but I suggest finding other things to do in the area but this will not take up much time. Incredible views of the city from here, however.

This is a great ride to try out at Epcot. I love how they give the aroma of each of the countries you soar through. It is a very unique experience and a fun ride for kids too. The lines for this generally are not bad and there are several other attractions in this same location.

Beautiful zoo lights during the Christmas time, and great location in the center of the city. The best part is... it's free, so you can't ask for much better than that! Definitely worth checking out during christmas time to see all their light shows and festivities. Cool stuff!

It's a great place to go in the San Francisco area. There's a lot to do, a lot to eat, and a lot of walking you shall prepare to do. It has great views and in general is likely unlike where most tourists are from. I'd definitely go back if it wasn't across the country for me.

Beautiful views. Rather expensive for what you get to do and see at the top. The ledge is cool, but weird location, could've been more on the city side. Overall, beautiful, places to eat and places to shop. Definitely a great place to get incredible views of the city.

It was an absolutely incredible experience to go here. They have more than you can ever possibly imagine and it's absolutely gorgeous. There's good views from upstairs, and there's a lot to see. You can't get bored here. Plus, it's great to go during election time!

Lots of delicious restaurants to choose from. Lots of parking too, but it's a bit of a walk. Then of course you have the attractions. If it starts raining, that will be unfortunate, as there's not a lot of overhang. They have a good candy shop and entertainment!

I liked it here but lines were long to get into some exhibits and it's not set up like a lot of other museums are, so it was pretty confusing to find things. definitely a place worth checking out, however.
A pretty place to stop if you're just going for a drive. Gorgeous views of the sky and water. Not a whole lot or parking available and there is usually quite a bit of people here, even in the winter.

It's a nice park with a lot of open space and room
to have a lot of activities whether it be a birthday party, just to go to the park to play, to play soccer, etc., whatever it might be.
There's so much to do in this area. There's Fishermans Wharf, Ghiradell Square, and the lovely cable car. A great place to go with your family: just watch out for the bikers.
It was a really great adventure to do as a family. They had a little show that was very fun to attend and it was a good experience. It gets hot out there.
not a whole lot to see here. if you go at night I guarantee there will be a lot of annoying knats flying around you if you're anywhere near a light.
It takes such a long time to walk up to the spot where you actually get on the ride, even when there's absolutely no wait. It's fun though!
Absolutely gorgeous. It's nice for a walk around or drive. Seems like whenever I want to go, they're closed however. It's pretty neat!
it’s a nice view, but if I’m being honest.... I thought the water would look more cleaner. It was green 😶

The tour actually starts at the education center. You need to take the time to read us and understand the role the Fort played before going. I was surprised at how small it seemed but after the pounding it took during the Civil War, I shouldn't have. Take the ferry after visiting the education center and listen to the history in the ride over. Walk the grounds and enjoy the history.

Start off the visit by heading inside and watching the movie. Its an old movie and a bit hokie but its informative. Walk around the museum and read some of the history and see the artifacts. Walk across the street and walk through the tunnels. Walk around the outside and look across the bay. This is where they shelled Fort Sumpter to start the Civil War.

We've been here for a few years and only now came here. We drove through before but didn't stop and walk around. Big mistake. Beautiful area. Glad it made it through the fire. Yiu can still see how close it came. Not the easiest walk with the rocks and roots, but definitely beautiful.

This is an amazing museum. The displays and artifacts are historically accurate, relevant and interesting. Easily one of our highlights of our vacation, and it was an unplanned one. Read about the Bar Pilots and then saw a transfer in action afterwards.

Caught the last tour of the day by chance and truly enjoyed it. Learned a lot about the distillery process and tasted the product in process. Good tasting stock. Signed up to be a Ranger so I can be involved in the process and can taste future products.

Came here for our daughter's wedding in the Hoh Rain Forrest.  The sun was shining and the scenery was absolutely lovely.  Service was short and sweet.  Will definitely come back again to visit more of the Park.
