This was perfect for our dog. Was able to get him in a less populated area and had lots of room and met a few others who were looking for the more quiet areas. Finnegan met a few friends and ran, ran, ran.

Her to drop off our daughter at the DNR program. They do a great job keeping the park clean and maintained. Staff was friendly and helpful. Rooms were clean. One of the beter State Parks we have been to.

Brought family here for a stay-cation. Set up awning, brought chairs, food, music and spent the day. We had a great day. Kids played in Whoa Zone and paddle boarded. I enjoyed a quiet day. Will be back!
Lovely park. Took the green 2 mile loop with the dogs. Bit muddy but managed. All was good until we found a tick, then another.... Lots of ticks. All is good now but a bit stressful for a while there
Stopped in to find a few bottles of wine for friends. They were very helpful and accommodating to non-wine drinkers. Shipped them home for us and our friends loved them.
Beautiful day with beautiful views. Walked uo with our puppy who loved both the snow and the sand! In my younger days I would have walked to the bottom, but not now.
Had a couple of the best sandwiches ever here. Ordered and sat down on the overlook and enjoyed the scenery. Will stop in and grab some tomorrow as we pass through.
Beautiful park that is over shadowed by the rest of the beautiful surroundings. If you drive through the Smokies, this is a great place to stop and eat lunch.
Very nice park. We walked down to the beach (rocks) and enjoyed the view and quiet for a while. Didn't take the trail but it looks perfect for another night.
Nice open beach to bring your dog and walk. Not as many shells, but still worth visiting. Showers, bathrooms, grills... Everything you need to spend the day.
Very busy today. Full parking lot with some rock hunting, some playing and some eating lunch. Bathrooms are open. Narrow beach but lots of rocks.
Nice park no matter the season. Sledding Hill in the winter, nice walking trails, picnic area and playground. Ample parking and good facilities.
Probably the most interesting thing we did today. Drove a bit out of the way to get a look. Quick photo opportunity and back on the road again.
Here for Bark in the Park. Our puppy loved it. Lots of dogs to see and more importantly, people to talk to. He loved the attention and treats.
Beautiful place that is probably overlooked.  Drove through on the way in from Seattle and came back to do some geocaching later on our trip.
Beautiful area. The stacks and the beach were a different kind of beautiful and enjoyed waking up in the morning and walking.
Wonderful place to bring the kids. Look for fossils (not huge but cool), bike, jog or walk the trail. Even geocaches here.
Drive through here every time we are here. The $5 goes to a good cause. Stop and see the sights while here.
Wow. This is great. Reminds me a lot of Fort McHenry. Love the draw bridges and the view is awesome.

So many beautiful butterflies. This is a great place to relax and get away from the hustle and bustle of everyday life. Bring your camera as you will want to take lots of pictures.

The gift store is also nice. It is the perfect place to find some unique gifts for your friends and family.

One of my favorite Parks!  Lots of shade trees throughout and plenty of nice playground equipment for the kids to climb on. There is also a basketball court and a big green grass area for the kids to run around on. Bring your fishing poles as there is a nice pier to fish from.

The Jacksonville Zoo and Gardens in Jacksonville, Florida is amazing.  The Jacksonville Zoo is unique in that it not only provides a home for animals but it is also listed as a Botanical Garden.

Our favorite exhibit was the Land of The Tigers.  You must see it!

Such a unique area! Be sure to take the guided tour so that you can learn about how the tufas are formed and how important the lake is to the birds that flock to the area.  You can swim in the lake but you should know it is about 2 times saltier than the ocean.

We had a fun time touring the museum. There is lots to see and two fun simulators for the kids. Admission is free and donations are always welcome. During our visit jets were flying overhead and my kids really got a kick out of that!

We really enjoyed visiting this museum. Lots of hands on exhibits for the kids and adults. I recommend taking the tour led by the docent as you learn a great deal about the history of the island and the state.

Fun stop to check off the to do list. We visited in July and it was hot!  There was a line so plan accordingly. There was a day ed ice truck just up the street which was nice after just standing in the sun.

We visited the dog park during our visit. Our dog is large so that is the part we stayed in. The dog had a blast exploring and meeting other dogs. A water hose is available for your pet if they get thirsty.

We drove through the reserve as one of my kids were sick. It's a nice, free preserve. I'm looking forward to exploring more with my kids. It can get quite hot so we will visit when it cools off a bit.
My kids really enjoyed visiting this museum. They loved the Navy Seal course and exploring all of the boats. After visiting the museum enjoy a packed lunch and visit to the beach.
Great place to learn about Amelia Island and how shrimping affected the area. It's a small museum, but if it is raining like it was when we visited it's a nice place check out.
Nice visit. We did not enjoy the your during our visit, but we did enjoy the items that were on display. Great place to learn about our history enjoy a little A/C and shade.

Such a fun experience.

Hubs and I took our 10 year old son and we had a blast. It is a great way to get a different perspective on the zoo. You will have lots of fun!
My kids love this park.  The ground is soft and the there are misters on site where your kids can cool off.  It caters to those with special needs but is open to all.
Pretty amazing, especially for this Florida girl to see.  There are a lot of huge pine trees in the area as well.  I wish I had more time to spend here.
Great place for the family to explore. I recommend taking the guided tour of the stamp mill. Bring snacks and drinks as there is not much there.
Great place to bring your little treasure hunters! It took us about an hour to walk through. My boys as well as myself had a fun time learning.
Beautiful! Really enjoyed hiking to the waterfall and visiting Vikingsholm.  The water in the bay is crystal clear and gorgeous!
One of our fave parks! We love to fish and relax by the pond.  There is also basketball and volleyball areas for you to enjoy.

Beautiful place to explore a unique picture of nature.
Be prepared for a little hike down the sand dune to get to the beach.

Great place for both young and old to stretch their minds while having a ton of fun!!

The staff are great and very helpful.
My kids love the playground! The fort and guided hands on exhibits were great for immersing us in the history of the fort.
Crystal clear water.  Another amazing view and a great place to take pictures! There is a lot of hiking around the area.
Nice, relaxing place to visit. Be sure to check out their website prior to your visit as they routinely host fun events.

Nice clean beach with lots of picnic tables.
When we visited the bathrooms were not the clean but they were usable.

The park that is available is huge and amazing for any age. There is multiple fields and courts for any sports (Basketball, baseball, volleyball, soccer ball). There is also a very cool and modern park with new obstacles and games that I like and I'm a college student. With that there is a lot of empty fields wrapped with walkways and bike paths which is nice because you get a taste of what everyone is doing in the park. Basically, everything is alive with people and activities to do.

I historic beauty in Chicago. It used to be the old Chicago Public Library before turning into the cultural center. It is just beautiful to see the architecture inside, including the two beautiful glass domes. The center also has multiple art exhibits and events. The best part is they are all FREE. I always stop by if I am around to see the place as well as to stay cool in the summer and warm in the winter.

The building is one of the newest building on campus and follows the architectural style of the rest of the buildings. With that, I do beleive its function was not thought through because the biggest space in the building is not used as much as the basement which to some extent looks like a dungeon. Personally they put so much money in the building they should have found a different style for the function.

I was really excited to see this musuem, but it was not as nice as I thought I would be. The place is defrosting from the inside out. Many important artifacts had visible damage because of the environment. None the less it was important to visit to recognize African American history. To remember that this country is built on the help of many and to recognize our diversity.

The Planetarium is rather small compared to its neighboring museums. The museum really focuses in the history of astronomy which is really unique to read about. Other than that, there is not much to do, especially because astrology should be seen not shown in a building. That's why they hold very fun events all year long to view the stars under the telescope.

A jewel hidden in the middle of Chicago. It is a nice pause form the busy city life as you get to explore the history of Chicago. The mansion is very well kept, and is beautiful. The staff are super nice and are more than happy to answer your questions. So make sure to ask away!

Grant park is one of the best barks in Chicago. It has great views of the skyline. Plus it is a two minute walk from the lake shore. The Buckingham Fountain is beautiful and a must see. What is also great about the park is many events are hosted in it, and many are free!

A great place for all ages. They have many activities ranging from tock climbing to ice skating in the winter. There is many open areas for picnics and sport games. It is a very clean park with very unique architecture. Especially the playground, it is very interesting.

This museum is large and amazing. Has many different styles and eras of art to see. The building itself is nicely put together, but there is some sections that should be remodeled. There is a lot of free days for Illinois residents so keep a look out on their website.

This place is huge and nice. There are many activities all year around. There is a nice park for the kids. There is huge field to take the dogs, play Frisbee, and of course soccer. Also a community center for art classes. Came here as a kid for picnics, and still do.

Has a great path through the woods and many fields for picnics and BBQs. I run through herer throughout the week and really enjoy the scenery. Plus, you never know what animal or critter you will find lurking around. It's always fun to discover new things.

A great place to hangout and end your day. The park is alive all night with a bunch of performances. I even got to attend a great play that was super unique. The arch and fountain give this park an enlightened feeling which is why I enjoyed chilling here.

Came here through the Los Leones Canyon Trailhead and ended up at the Mesa overlook. It was a long hike, but very worth it. The whole time while hiking you can see the ocean and are surrounded by green luscious mountains. I highly recommend a visit.

Great place to have fun and learn. I came here throughout my child hood and still visit. There is always new and interesting exhibits. It is a must visit if you are visiting Chicago. It is very interactive with many activities for the kids.

A great place to sit down, unwind, and relax. It is a huge open field just waiting for a picnic, even for some people a great place to tan. You get some clean fresh air and almost forget your in a busy city with the surrounding trees.

Great bike trail to run on with beautiful scenery, it's very nice since it turns along the river I also was impressed by the obstacle courses they had set up for famialies. It's nice to see the space be used for more than one thing.

It was a nice park in the city. It was on the quieter side with no events, but it did have a stage ready for what seemed to host large events. There is a bunch of mini cafes and nice places to sit and unwind.

A tropical place to escape the cold. It's nice to see some green when all of your surrounding is white and brown. It is well maintained with a few ponds and fish. Just a nice place to unwind for a bit.
A wide and clean path to reach Mesa overlook. One of the nicest paths hikes I have take in California. I went after heavy rains, so everything was super green and luscious. I enjoyed every moment.
Great museum. Has many famous and important art pieces. I loved their Southwest Asian exhibit. Overall really enjoyed my visit.  Best part was that students are for free.
It's nice to see the original water tower, especially how they use it as a small museum exhibit. Make sure to visit it at different times of the year to see what new.
Wow. I didn't think such architecture and art existed in Manhattan. This place is beautiful and magnificent and is a must visit. It is free admission.
An awesome and short hike. It is pretty rocky, but you end up at a nice waterfall. I reccomend this for all ages and a great idea for a family hike.
A small parking lot in the middle of the Cal Sag Trail. It's new and clean, and usually never full, so there is always a spot to park.
Beautiful place to unwind if the weather is favorable. Plus, great place to take pictures of the city. It has marvelous views.

I have done hiking in multiple national parks all over North America and the hike from this Trailhead to the loch is one of my favorite hikes in the world. Do yourself a favor and get to the parking lot by 7 a.m. or it will be full. Don't be a sheeple. Most of the people only hike to Alberta Falls or around Bear Lake and the true beauty of the park is about 4 miles back past where most people will ever travel.

There are plenty of ponds here for your dog to swim in. The water might be questionable. It is a large area for your dog to run wild and free. The place can get in very busy with hundreds of other dogs on the weekends. There's not a lot of shade in certain parts. The only disadvantage is that you have to pay the state park entrance fee in order to access it.

During most of the year this area is littered with homeless people and drug addicts. If you've never seen human feces laying out in the public you might get to see it here. It's kind of disgusting and sad that Denver has allowed to dilapidate. In the winter time... around Christmas they light the building up and hide away all the transient people.

This place can get busy. There is a small parking one so get there early if you want to use the space. There is a easy single track mountain bike path that's approximately a 3 mile loop. It is a very easy but still fun and because of its Western exposure you can ride year round and in almost all weather conditions

I hiked this with my wife and two small children. There are a couple of spots where you have to scramble on some rocks and it could be a little unsafe for small children if it were wet and slippery.  It's a bit challenging for two small kids. The only disadvantage is that the Stanley Lake / Reservoir is drained.

The beach is very long with powdery sand. It's shallow for a long ways so that bigger children can easily play. We visited in the middle of the week in the springtime and it was uncrowded and underutilized. There appears to be a handful of people who tent camp on the beach. Lots of seaweed.

This place is so crowded and overused it should Boggle your mind. It is one of the only lakes in the world with a traffic pattern due to the high volume of boats. I have frequently boated in Minnesota and Iowa and I have never heard of a lake being full but Chatfield gets full.

The hiking from this location is not that impressive however it is a quiet underutilized area to be able to access the national park. There is a great little Campground right there by this Trailhead called the East portal Campground I would definitely recommend camping there.

The place is a bit pricey but it is my favourite Zoo. Be prepared to do a lot of walking because the zoo itself is on the side of a mountain. It is a smaller zoo so most of the animal enclosures are small...that allows you to have an intimate contact with the animals

This is a really interesting park it has a sled built into a hill a giant Treehouse overlook some obstacles to climb upon a soccer field. My children have been going here for years and really enjoy it because it is unique equipment to fool around on

You can park here and it's not as congested as other areas of the park there's a bus stop right here but the bus stop only runs during peak hours in the summer time. There is also a way to connect to a trail system that loops around the valley here.

This place is crazy busy on the weekends. During the middle of the week it's pretty underutilized it's got a nice modern play structure Open Fields for volleyball or playing catch. It's also right next to the river that you can float in a tube

This place is insanely crowded. The grounds are well maintained. There are opportunities for self-guided and guided tours. They have a few actors dressed up talking about the time. It's amazing to believe that this place is free to visit.

We come here at least two times a year. In the summertime there are two small water slides. In the winter time you can hang out in a gigantic pool that's bathtub temperature all day long while it snows on you. My kids love it.

It's a bit spendy for a big family....you might as well buy a membership. Compared to museums in other major metropolitan areas it's not that impressive but it might be the best of its kind for 300 miles.

It is worth the entrance fee to pay to come here and hike for a day. Get there early cuz it gets very high use. There are some campgrounds in the area that appear to be well shaded with nice restrooms.
There's a reason it's a national park. The views are amazing the hiking is amazing. The only problem is that has become so popular it's often crowded and traffic jams can occur on the weekends.
This is a memorable hike to an iconic location in Yosemite. The path is insanely busy. It is a significant elevation gain but an easy hike as the path is paved and has stairs.
In the fall there are lots of photographers who take people here for family photos because of the nice backdrop and foliage. I can't see another reason to come here
The views are amazing. This is one of the best concert venues in the country. It's pretty awesome that you can come here on weekend mornings and workout.
This is a great little Park there's a baseball diamond a soccer field a playground and has great access to a number of easy mountain biking trails.
This is a great place to take your kids so that they can get a real world experience of what a cabin was like a hundred years ago.
This is an exceptional place to be on a softball league because the facility are nice and clean and the grounds are well-kept
There are some great simple hikes in this area. Nothing breathtaking. All the hikes in this area could be done by a family.
This is the easiest place in Colorado to see a mountain goat. Get there early because it's insanely busy on the weekends.

This is a beautiful museum with well educated and friendly staff. I recommend getting a tour and checking out The Panorama of the City of New York. Don't forget to take a picture of the Unisphere, the largest globe in the world, in Flushing Meadows Park. It's directly behind the museum. It's a great place for the entire family to go and enjoy.

An incredible 60 second journey to and at the highest point in the Western Hemisphere for a reasonable price. Plan to go around sunset and you'll be blown away by the stunning views of the city that never sleeps. If you plan to dine at One, be sure to make an OpenTable reservation in advance. Plan a Summer visit since Winter hours are reduced.

This park has one of the best views of Manhattan. It's a great loop for walking after trying one of the many great restaurants in downtown Hoboken. Bring a blanket and lay out on the grass while you enjoy the breathtaking view of the river and Manhattan.

It's quite underwhelming but a great replica of a piece of history. If you're in the area, it's worth stopping by. There are some tour guides on site who can share the history and answer any questions you may have.
I highly recommend the Best of NYC tour. Spend the extra money for the premier experience. Joe's a great tour guide. We learned a lot in the 2.5 hours and saw all of the beauty that NYC has to offer!
This is a nice park with plenty to do and a great view of the George Washington Bridge. People are always around to make it feel safe. It’s a great place for a picnic or playing some games.
A beautiful park with a great playground and Shake Shack. You can sit on a bench and people watch or lay out in the sun. There are plenty of shops and restaurants in the area.
A great place to go for a swim or workout. If you plan on using the pool, they strongly encourage you to bring a lock. The staff are pretty strict about following the rules.
Even on a rainy day, there's still so much to see. I recommend going for the full experience package in the Spring and Summer only. Beautiful animals throughout the zoo.
I attended two weddings here and saw nothing but beauty. From the wandering peacocks to the rustic scenery, it's a gorgeous ranch. I highly recommend checking it out.
Such a beautiful view of the pond in Central Park. The waitstaff is really accommodating and the food is worth the wait. It's worth visiting after a walk in the park!
A great park with a beautiful view of the river. If you want to find peace in a big city, this is the place to go. There are so many moments worth photographing.
I recommend going when the weather is nice. The unicorn tapestries are absolutely beautiful. Plan to stay for lunch, with a beautiful view of the gardens.
likes: Facilities & Services: Lunch with garden view

reviews_attraction.text: A fun place to explore trails and see Lake Michigan. We encountered the small pier, a beach, and a yacht club that look out on the lake. It's beautiful.
A fun place to walk around and view incredible artwork. Don't miss Peter Tunney's gallery. So many incredible sayings turned into art around town.
The tour was very entertaining. Josh is hilarious. The tour is a great deal and a fun experience. The food is good and the atmosphere is great.
A beautiful park with a view of City Hall. There are plenty of places to sit for people watching. The fountain is a great meeting spot.
A beautiful place to watch the sunset and people watch. I recommend going when the weather is nice. Bring a blanket and have a picnic.
Only in town for a quick visit? Get an experience in Atlanta with a view to remember. Stay warm while viewing the incredible skyline.
A beautiful space with so much history. Take what you want from the experience. There's something for every unrepresented group.
This place is impressive. The security is tight but it's worth going for a tour if you can get access. There's so much to learn.
A beautiful statue for an incredible late public figure. It truly resembles her courage and strength. I recommend waking by!
An aquarium that's worth a quick visit. There are more great views right outside the doors. You may learn something new.
A busy park that's great for people watching. There's plenty of shopping around the area. It's a nice meeting spot.
One of my favorite hikes. The hike and falls are beautiful. Plan to take your time and spend an afternoon there.

It's only recently when we visited the Balaji Temple for the first time!

An incredible place to worship & find peace of mind. As you arrive here, you'll enter the massive parking lot. There are multiple accessible parking spots too!

Now entering the temple— the first thing you do is take off your shoes, place them in the designated area & move inside the premises.

Once you are in, an officer would gently ask you to create an account on your phone & scan the code at the register. Now there will be only one account for the whole family/group. Every time you visit the temple simply scan the code.

It's time to move in, see the real magnificence within the temple, the deities. Mostly there are no restrictions as to what you should wear but be mindful of the fact that shorts n all won't be appropriate. It is to show respect towards the culture & spiritual sentiments.

Now, spend some time inside, observing the grandeur of various gods/goddesses. Walk around maintaining the distance & I am certain you will obtain peace of mind.

Also, no photography/videography is allowed inside the premise.

Once you're done, you come down to the hallway where there is a food court too. You can enjoy South Indian delicacies like Vada, Idli, sambar, and sweets at a very reasonable price. Don't miss that.

Outside there are multiple picnic benches installed around the pond. Enjoy the surroundings as well as delicious food.

There is a play area and a park on the backside too! The temple has accessible parking, entry & restroom.

Waste of time & Money!

We’re currently on a Rod Trip to NaperVille from Florida, we decided to visit Science center in Nashville TN.
I’m so disappointed with this place being called a Sceince Center, It’s a Science Mess instead.

My daughter is 4— She is exposed to Science to a certain extent, however, most of the sections/rooms/Games are for older kids.

In order to play or use the area at its best, they must understand the Know-how & 4 I beleive is too young to understand what’s going on in there.

My daughter & I didn’t find anything amusing in there except for the planetarium.

I’d say- refrain from this Science Mess unless ofcourse your purpose for visiting is make your child(6+) aware about Science, Astronomy, so they may atleast comprehend what they’re seeing.

Contrarily, Do Not waste your precious time & money here, rather take ‘em to an outdoor play area, they’re way better in every sense, mostly free of cost!

Not so absurdly crowded like this one. Kids were literally crashing into each other especially in the play areas.
The Cafeteria was full to the Brim.

My friends have been seeking for some place to spend a few hours. I recommended them turtle back zoo since we had visited it last year.  And i had very strong reasons why i suggested them to see this zoo.
This zoo has such diversity of animals as well as birds. My friends couldnt have been happier after experiencing this place.
They have animal feeding, bird feeding activity, farm animals, animal safari, pony ride a saperate playground, carousel and what not.
Additionally, there’s a boat ride too however thats located at a saperated area.
We were lucky enough to see albino wolf which we never thought of having experience of.
Besides all this, theres tree top activities too but thats for some older kids. Our kids were too young for that activity.
My daughter was so amazed to see the peacock flaunting its feathers and dancing for atleast half n hour.
Their cafeteria is good, organized and tidy. Face painting is available for the kids which is great.
So we spent around 4-5 hours and totally worth it. We came back only after the zoo was closed entirely.

My entire family loves going to this park. this place has way too many options for you no matter what age you are.
Mini playgrounds for toddlers and kids, swings and slides. my toddler doesn't wanna come back from the park ever. we usually visit the park after the office, and walk around the place while my toddler play at the swings and slides.
There's a beautiful long trail too equipped with exercise apparatus that includes instructions on how to use it. it feels so nice to walk along the river and its an instant stress buster activity.
this park has a swimming pool too which we haven't used it yet but i heard its nice and clean. so will be planning on using it soon on a nice warm day. The restrooms here, i wont say are sqeaky clean instead i’d rate them as 7/10 on the basis of cleanliness.
plus there's a football ground, a separate bicycle way and amazing views. Thousands of colorful trees, lots of green grass and happy people working out. Overall, a great place to enjoy nice breeze, greenery and fitness activities.

One of the best Aquariums!

If there were a list of top aquariums in the US, this aquarium would most likely be there. Ripley's Aquarium has that vibe, that ambiance which will certainly pay-off & you’d want to revisit it.

Some rare sea-creatures like Sea Dragons, sharks, hammerhead, enormous turtles, were exclusive to this aquarium, you won't get to see them everywhere.

Exhibits like touching the jellyfish, experiencing the sting-rays, the penguin exhibit, also, under the sea spectacle where we hover on the slow-moving belt and observe all the sea creatures in their natural environment, were thrilling all the way.

The cafe inside the aquarium is decent, the impossible burger tasted fresh/delicious.

Although Glass Boat Ride can be a unique experience for some, It didn't really interest me.

Public parking lot—near the aquarium.

#SensoryFriendly #RoadTrip5 #Gatlinburg

Migrating from Florida had me thinking—I’m leaving behind Abundance of Nature parks waterfront parks & trails, but Naperville proved me wrong.

I’m so glad to be able to locate multiple parks in here for the city being a Park District, it’s highly likely I’ll stay close to mother nature.

Today, I stumbled upon Knoch Knolls Nature Center/Park, a perfectly warm day for a visit to a place such as this.

It’s a gigantic public setting offering— Multiple Trails, Picnic areas; some include fire pit & other rest areas, Kayaking, Playground for kids alongside engaging exhibits, keeping them busy for hours.
My kiddo simply didn’t wanna return home. Need I say more?

P.S— Ample Parking Spots, Accessible Parking available too!
I found this park to be pretty Accessible for ECV & Strollers.

#Nature #Park

It’s been a week since we relocated to Naperville from St Pete Florida. My family & I love going outdoors, undoubtedly, parks are one of the best places for Fresh Air in abundance & lots of fun—

So, on this Freezing though beautiful Sunday Noon & Mothers Day, My family & I planned on visiting Lilacia Park in Lombard.

Luckily, there was an event going on in there, amazing Live Music & Colorful Blanket of Flowers everywhere around the Park, it was worth a visit.

One of Park members passing by was distributing flowers to all the Mothers on the occasion of Mothers Day.

Also, this historical park is huge, though there was an array of Spring Flowers, Tulips, Lilacs, Spring Mix, there’s no Play area for kids so we headed over to another park a mile away.

#Spring #LetsGuide

Although Lincoln Park Zoo is virtually free to visit, you have to pay for parking and other exhibits inside the zoo.

Starting from Naperville, it took us about an hour to arrive! We parked at Belden Center and walked a few steps to the zoo.

My family and I had been to multiple Zoos in the past, however, surprisingly, in here we got to see a giant yet playful Gorilla Tribe, a Polar Bear and unusual species of birds which was plenty to perk up our day.

Besides, Nature Boardwalk, Safari Train, Face Painting, a Carousel, a Souvenir Shop fulfills the purpose of the visit.

The food here is good—multiple food joints to choose from.

Lincoln park zoo is accessible to a larger extent including the Gift Shop and the Lionel Train.

#Zoo #Chicago

Oh boy! Not for faint-hearted.

Forewarning - I do not recommend going with kids/toddlers. It might be a horrifying experience for them.

I made the mistake of accompanying my 5-year-old, & trust me it scared her like anything.

They won't warn you beforehand so it's at your discretion whether to proceed for a super horrifying adventure & history lessons. We started off with a group of 8 people for a 60-minute session.

The actors perform excellently & stay in the role no matter what. They won't touch you but dark rooms & scampering will create panic for sure.

Be prepared to scream and/or hear screeching, yelping sounds.

Finally, the drop ride concludes the session & you feel thankful for coming out alive!

#Day2

Even after residing close to NYC, I never got a chance to visit Madame Tussauds. For that reason, I didn't want to miss the opportunity in SF.

This accessible museum is such a fun place to be, exhibiting numerous wax statues of celebs from various genres could be seen & few of them were unrecognizable for some reason.

Of all the rooms, the flower room remains on top of my list, the prison set up and then the Camping site.

Besides the intricate details added to the rooms not to mention the statues, I love the provision of extra costumes & tiaras for a more decent photo-op.

We purchased combined tickets online for Tussauds & The Dungeons at a reasonable price.

This wax museum is suitable for all ages!

#Day2

This enormous State Park, located in the town of Mt Morris, is a terrific place to be! Beautiful campsite for a weekend getaway.

White Pine State Park allows nature lovers to Hike, Camp, Picnic, Hunt, and Fish. Need I say More?

Multiple Trails having varied difficulty levels, welcome everyone to hike through the forest and cross over the Creek. The trails, we hiked through, were so peaceful that the only thing, we could hear, was the sound of water flowing through.

Tall Pine Trees gazing the sky could be seen all around the park. My 4-year-old loved accumulating Acorns in her tiny backpack.

PS- Some of these trails are accessible. Bikes, not allowed on the trails.

#hiking #StatePark

If you are looking for more natural charm in Smokey Mt national park, turn your vehicle towards this spot and praise mother nature. That's what we did during our visit to the park in Tennessee.

The Sinks is one of many scenic spots in the Smokey Mountain National Park and is definitely worth a visit.

Unlike other waterfalls in the park, you won't have to hike a lot to arrive at the location, simply park your car, enjoy the beauty, click pictures & relax.

There's a small parking space at this location including accessible parking & no restrooms.

PS- Most likely no network coverage around here so better download the maps ahead of your visit.

#RoadTrip5 #SmokeyMt

My 5-year-old loves carousel, the moment she realized there's a carousel at this location, we had to get a ride on it.

This may, at times, go unnoticed but I believe it suggests how family-friendly Pier 39 is, welcoming everyone regardless of age.

Also, this fun ride doesn't only welcome kids but also grown-ups. Hint- it's super fun.

Tickets can be purchased from self-helping kiosks too near the carousel. If you're coming here with a child, there is just no way you can overlook this fun ride.

The best part is that this carousel is two-tier, lower level & upper level. So you get to choose the spot that suits you the most.

#Day2

If you're visiting SF and fancy seeing what real SF is like, Fishermans Wharf located at Pier 39 is the place for you.

I, as a vacationer, visited Fishermans Wharf last week & cannot deny the fact that this place is lively, super entertaining. Locals, as well as travelers from all over the globe, can be observed here.

This place can be accessed by public/private conveyance. There's a parking garage (Beach St) available at this location.

Applebees (restaurant at Taylor St) based on the first floor provides the best view of the activities taking place at the Wharf.

PS- Be sure to get a ride in the Cable Car.

#Day2

Not many people realize but the best way to capture the enormous Golden Gate Bridge is from a distance. Golden Gate Overlook makes the job easy breezy!

Locals can be seen running/biking/strolling here.

We were lucky enough to click a handful of pictures from this site for the moment we arrive at the Golden Gate Bridge, it was out n out Foggy!

It was pretty underwhelming at first, for dense fog kept playing all the while.

Parking- We parked our car at a nearby parking spot called ’Langdon Court’—absolutely free of cost.

It's about 10-12 minutes' walk from the parking spot to the bridge.

#Day1 #SFO

Big beautiful park comprised with every possible amenity you might ask for in a Public setting.

Two seprate play areas for infant, toddlers & kids.
One huge grass ground for free play, running, jogging or just meditating(if you wish) plus, a few picnic benches.

I could see how clean & well taken care of is this entire facility.

The washrooms on the setting were, though dated yet highly clean & decontaminated which is great.

Also, the location of the Park is very nice, surrounded with apartment buildings.

My 4-year-old loves going outdoors which is why every other weekend, we track down a park in our neighborhood and spend some time playing, walking and relaxing.

Country lakes Park—A small park offering Play area, covered picnic benches & a softball field.

The Play area stands in seemingly decent shape, the site is all nice and clean.

Entry to the park is through a residential community, I'm unsure if this park belongs to the same building.

Separate parking space available too!

#Outdoors #Park #PlayTime

If you’re visiting Old Sawmill Park—fenced in by residential area, keep in mind there’s no designated parking space.

We realized it right after arriving at the park, so we street parked and walked a few steps.

Given that, this park appeared to be fairly new and unharmed, the Play Area in such good condition. Definitely a great place for kids.

This Park offers Swings, Slides, Climbing Frame, Benches, Covered Picnic Area, and a great view, basically everything but a Parking Lot.

#outdoors #Playground

I went there exactly 3 days after Hurricane Michael. I could clearly feel the effect.
A strong toxic odor everywhere with some dead fish scattered over the shores. You can check my pictures for a better understanding. I Was a bit skeptical about going there for the same reason.
Otherwise, this White Sand Beach is serene and calming with some spectacular sunset views.
The parking ($2/hour) can be an issue during peak hours. We arrived here after 5 in the evening so wasn't an issue for us.

Last Weekend while passing by the area, we noticed Chromatic Shapes In the sky which later turned out to be Kites of All shapes & Sizes during a Kite Festival in the Frontier Park.

I’m fairly new to the neighborhood, so was delighted to be able to discover a Beautiful Park here.

Couldn’t see the entire park, I could track down a Kids Play Area with several exhibits.

Apparently, this Park is Huge having ample parking space too.

#Outdoor #Playground

We planned on going to the beach at around 5 in the evening. Arrived at the location at 6 around, the beach isn't far from the road.
Unlike a Few beaches that I had been to earlier, had a long way to walk from the parking lot to the beach.
This beach is extremely busy & fully commercialized with amazing beachside shacks n bars.
You can even rent a bicycle or a covered cycle for multiple people.

Located at West Bailey Road, Winding Creek park invites people of all ages and abilities.

The play area is a decent size and has multiple apparatus to play with. A climbing frame, slides, swing, and two separate areas to accommodate kids of all ages.

Additionally, this park offers a baseball field, trails, and picnic shelter.

PS- No restrooms at the location.

#outdoors #playarea

One of the cleanest and spectacular beaches I've ever been to.
Millions of shells on the ground, big n small.
Clean n cold water, I could hear the sound of the waves, it was so peaceful being there.
Just Lovely.
Since I was traveling from NJ to Florida, I'm not used to seeing empty spaces. This beach was not at all busy, it felt like we're the only one at the Varn Park.

Wonderful public setting for anyone who loves Hiking, Biking on long peaceful Trails no matter if you’re visiting Solo or with family.

Enormously stretched Grassland on either side of the Road, this preserve includes a Model Aircraft Area, Several Picnic Benches & an Off-leash Dog Area.

Ample parking spaces & Restrooms available.

#Hiking #Trails #BikeRide

Would you believe if I say its one of the most amazing Trails in the neighbourhood.

With wildlife around the lake, Greenary in abundance & Peacefulness, this Nature Trail is second to none.

I make frequent visits to the Trail for a jog or a peaceful walk, away from hustle-bustle of any kind.

We primarily come for the playground area for my kids. There is a decent sized sandbox to play in that will fit many kids. There are 2 main playgrounds for different age levels that are separated by fences which is really nice. Typical swing sets that are on all playgrounds.

The really cool part is that the playground is next to a school that has several basketball hoops and lots of open space for play with lines pre-drawn on the pavement. When school is over, the school's marked pavement is like an extension of the playground for other games.

This was our first time to visit Sea Life Aquarium. My kids didn't want to go. Once we arrived, they got really excited to see the sea creatures. This is an extremely family-friendly aquarium specially designed with kids in mind. Almost all of the tanks can be seen by small kids. Lots of interactive things for the kids to do and not just in one spot. Lots of educational information about the sea animals and keeping our oceans and rivers clean. Near the end, the kids can touch some of the sea creatures. Excellent place to visit!!

You get to enter a battleship and submarine from WWII. Both vessels played significant roles in the war. You can sit at the gun stations, visit bunks, kitchens, and the torpedo bays in the submarine. There's a war memorial in the museum grounds. They have the best portable bathrooms I've ever entered.

Parents of little children: These are warships made for adults. Stairwells are narrow and steps are thin in some areas. Please watch your small children carefully when entering and walking within the vessels.

Nice historic land that has been converted into a family park. We only visited the playground area. It has a well-designed playground space, zip line, cycling track, large sandpit, wide slide and hill, plus restrooms.

My only concern is that kids of different ages and sizes go down the same aluminum slide and most adults are just watching. I saw a lot of close calls with a larger kid about to slide into a smaller kid who didn't have time to leave the bottom area.

The museum is small but packed full of nice displays and real artifacts, fossils, and other historical findings from around the world. Great information and explanations of scientific evidence into creation.

While it may be generally unpopular, the findings in this museum must be considered by real scientists if they consider themselves real scientists at all. Lots of information to read on the walls that includes quotes and where to find the references.

This place is pretty amazing. Very relaxing to walk around and explore the predominantly Chinese themed garden with other styles as well. There are little hidden gems to look for throughout the gardens. Lots of things to see like waterfalls, ponds, koi fish, maze, fountains, flowers, sculptures, architecture, and more. They host weddings and other large events. This is one of those hidden treats in the DFW area that doesn't get enough publicity.
likes: Variety of attractions (waterfalls, ponds, koi fish, maze, fountains, flowers, sculptures, architecture)

reviews_attraction.text:
There is a beautiful children's garden with a stage area, maze, climbing structures, and more. Plus, it's free to enter.

On the property, there is also a carousel, outdoor auditorium, bridges, fountains, walking areas around a pond filled with Koi fish, turtles, ducks, and geese.

All this and we didn't actually make our way into the actual greenhouse area. Really well designed overall. You also get a nice view of the tallest building in OKC.

The Miniland sets are truly amazing with famous cities like Washington D. C., San Francisco, Las Vegas, and New York, and famous monuments/cities in the foreign countries like the Taj Mahal, the Eiffel Tower, and Big Ben. The attention to detail is very special. There's also a Star Wars Miniland area nearby. The boat tour of the different sets is nice and relaxing and gives you a closer look at some of the pieces around the pond.

It was really great to see the canyon and drive down. We hiked some trails and explored some of the areas. Unfortunately, it was the weekend after Christmas 2020 and there was a hunt occurring on the same day. So, we could not see half of the canyon, which was disappointing. Lots of places to pull over for photo opportunities. This is definitely a Texas treasure that everyone should visit.

This is a neat museum with a unique exterior. There are a bunch of artifacts and displays of the culture of the local natives and those from around the world. There are some large selfie photos around the back exit of the museum. There's a skeleton statue of the Oklahoma dinosaur that was excavated. There are other interesting statues and paintings inside. Admission is free!

This is just an amazing place to visit with all the different pools and fountains. It's hard to describe this place with numerous water themed parks. There are some dangerous walking areas. We had engagement photos taken at night here so I have fond memories of this place. You really just have to see it for yourself. And it's free to visit! Parking is a bit of an issue.

A fun place to walk around with the family. Unlike theme parks, you can enter the boardwalk and walk up to a ride before deciding if you want to pay for the ride. You can get an all-day pass for all rides. The restaurants in the area are real establishments like Saltgrass and Bubba Gump... Not theme park food. There are several rides for little kids.

This section of Legoland is really exciting for the kids with the various rides like driver's license cars for little kids and older kids, first responder rescue, helicopter patrol, and more. I really like that they separated the driving attraction to kids 3-5 and 6+ years of age. They have some amazing famous statues in FunTown like the Thinker.

This is not the big Legoland theme park in San Diego, but it's very nice and condensed. There are 2 rides and one city area for kids to drive around in electric cars. There's a large play structure, some Lego exhibits of the DFW area that are very well done, and a build-a-racer section. The slash pad is outdoors and a huge hit for the kids!

We mostly come here for the playground which has very uniquely themed play structures and slides. They have a nice zip line too. We also got to run around with the kids at the soccer field with 2 real soccer goals and try to score some goals. Very impressed with this park.

They also have a decent water park and tennis courts.

A nice park with a wonderful playground for small to big kids. It's pretty large and can accommodate a lot of children. This playground is good for kids with disabilities or special needs too.There are numerous picnic tables and areas for activities like basketball & volleyball.

There's also tennis courts and a swim center.

Much like Cadillac Ranch, this is a smaller version with less fanfare. People spray paint the half-buried VW Beetles, so it's always changing. There are buildings nearby that are also spray painted. It looks like there used to be some businesses here. A motel is nearby, but does not look open.

Great hands-on activity center and museum for kids and adults displaying ingenuity and engineering that touches all the senses... lights, sounds, etc. It's humongous since it fills an entire pier. Food is available in the pier, but it's very expensive.

Beautiful state park with multiple nature trails. There is so much to do inside... heritage center and museum, beach, paddle boats, kayaks, campsites, nature center, train ride, restaurant, etc. You can spend several days here and have plenty to do.

This is a great family water park that is part of the city of Grapevine. Very kid friendly with a few things like a 12-ft deep pool and diving board for older kids and adults. I only wish they had a lazy river, but still a very nice park.

This park is very spacious and has plenty of picnic tables and bench areas. Play structures include zip lining, musical instruments, dinosaur dig site, climbing structures, and more. Everything looks pretty new here.

This is a great place to hang out with the family. Hammocks, an area for games and sports, tables/chairs, large mural, swing chairs... and a beautiful Ferris Wheel that is affordable! Nice view of the OKC skyline.

This is a good sized park with several pavilions/picnic areas, playgrounds, and trails. One of the trails leads to the Falls near the highway. There is a Disc Golf Course and is near the Nature Center.

Lots of nice nature trails and enough landmarks to make stops interesting and have things to look forward to. Ponds allows for fishing. There are future plans for an educational center and new trails.
A quirky little leaning water tower that is not being used and has the name Britten, USA, which is not a true town in Texas. The backstory is fun to read. Another interesting landmark on Route 66.

Is a large will maintain botanical garden in the heart of the Chapel Hill area. Very easy to fine, and a great facility with a lot of educational resources for teachers and students. They also specializing  in native plants for the North Carolina area and a lot of's sustainability practices.

One of the best parks in Greesboro, lots of historical interest scattered all around and easy to walk to. Nice for bikes, dogs, family and tourists. Good for recreational hot days in summer, lots of shady trails and connect to Country Park and Greensboro Science Center

If you need to get away from the city...jest a short ride from downtown and the airport is Library station park. Surrounded by water front walking trail, play grounds, shops and great market place. Wonderful atmosphere for families, walking or jest sitting and reading.

A bit of a hidden gem, Behind the Friendly Shopping center at Harris-teeter is a wonderful escape from concrete and into the natural woods, waterfall, boardwalk and trails of the Bog. Lots of plants and animals life to observe.
A great natural resource to visit to learn about the ecology of the Florida waterways, wonderful educational opportunity for kids and adults, a great place to get away from the noise of the beach.
A wonderful botanical garden, with lots of unique planting, paths, seating and great walking trail. Great location to bring your lunch with lots of playgrounds lots for kids of all ages.
One of the best museums in the Southeast, really great exhibits wonderful campus easy access. Great to visit inside and out with large sculpture installations surrounding it.
The beach is fun but the pier is one of the best thing to do. Lots of artists showing off their wonderful work, people fishing and the sunset is what most people gather for.
And I space to get away from the traffic and the crowds and get down to the water. With kayak rentals, bike rentals and boat tours, seating, nice views and nice walkways

A top destination for Greensboro and the Triad. Fun learning experience .
Great for all ages and beautiful location surrounded by City and National parks.

Very nice beach, clean white sands blue green waters
with lots sitting options and ball courts for playing
jest across from shopping and restaurants.

Make you feel like you are in the old country.
Wonderful atmosphere with restaurant,shops and colorful people.
Lots of seating and great views 360...
Very nice and educational museum centrally located downtown Wilmington in historic area, excellent exhibits of trains and history, a nice experience.
In the center of downtown Greensboro, NC is a lovely respite from busy city life. Great for lunch, reading or jest sitting with cool water features.

A family park in the middle of triangle.
Lots of trails for hiking, walking and biking.
Plenty of reaction opportunities. Great for cook outs.
And wonderful new park in the center of Greensboro, built around family and fun and eating and community great place to visit in Greensboro
In the heart of town, a great green space to enjoy lunch, sitting, kids playing and just relaxing. Great views and just off the train line.
A well designed and maintained garden. Really great history and lots of tropical flora. Wonderful for kids nice cafe and lots to purchase
One of the best beach piers that I have been on, well kept and far reaching. Good fishing with shopping and dinning closely available.
Nice...at the center of the city with lots to do and up coming events. Playgrounds, music stages, green spaces, and nice seating.
A very nice visit, I was there a bit early in the season but all the camellias were in bloom. Will revisit later in spring.
Aesthetically pleasing, multi functional space for visual art, theater and dining with some of the best views in the city.
The zoo was kind of sad but the bog trail was great. Boardwalk and cement walkways that are handicap accessible.
The other beach in VA beach, quite clean and a great place to get away from the madness of the boardwalk.
Nice park to spend the day, cycling or paddle boating on the water nice walks or just flying a kite.

(Translated by Google) It's worth a walk through Miami Beach's Art Deco District. There are 3 styles represented mainly on Ocean Drive: The Modern Streamline, the Mediterranean Revival and the Traditional. It is said that there are over 800 perfectly preserved buildings. The best known are Cavalier Hotel, Colony Hotel, Breakwater Hotel, Clevelander Hotel, Leslie Hotel and Cardozo Hotel. The motifs are usually tropical and pastel colors. They use a lot of neon, bas-relief, curves and lines. The ideal tour for lovers of beauty and architecture.

(Original)
Vale a pena um passeio a pé pelo Art Deco District de Miami Beach. Há 3 estilos representados sobretudo na Ocean Drive: O streamline Moderno, o Revival Mediterrâneo e o Tradicional. Dizem que há mais de 800 edifícios perfeitamente preservados. Os mais conhecidos são o Cavalier Hotel, o Colony Hotel, o Breakwater Hotel, o Clevelander Hotel, o Leslie Hotel e o Cardozo Hotel. Os motivos são normalmente tropicais e as cores pastel. Usam muito o néon, baixo-relevo, curvas e linhas. O passeio ideal para os amantes da beleza e da arquitetura.

(Translated by Google) Small park with a good beach of calm waters. Ideal for families to spend the day. There are tables and benches for picnics. The beautiful view of the disabled bridge is an incentive to take pictures. Bathrooms clean and fully equipped. We paid $ 9 to get in and park. When we visited the park it had a beautiful construction of sand. I found the sand full of algae but a poster explained to me that the algae were part of the ecosystem of the park and therefore were not removed.

(Original)
Pequeno parque com uma boa praia de águas tranquilas. Ideal para famílias passarem o dia. Tem mesas e bancos para picnic. A bela vista da ponte desativada é um incentivo para se fotografar. Banheiros impecáveis e totalmente equipados. Pagamos $9 para entrar e estacionar. Quando visitamos o parque tinha uma bonita construção de areia. Estranhei a areia cheia de algas mas um cartaz me esclareceu que as algas faziam parte do ecossistema do parque e que por isso não eram removidas.

(Translated by Google) Fort Jefferson is in Dry Tortugas National Park. We can reach the park by boat or hydro-plane. The first is more economical but it takes longer to get there. Whatever the choice, it is worth visiting this park and Fort Jefferson built there. The fort is the largest brick structure in the Americas. The park is 109 km away from Key West.

(Original)
O Fort Jefferson fica no Dry Tortugas National Park. Podemos chegar ao parque de barco ou de hidro-avião. O primeiro é mais econômico mas demora mais tempo para chegar lá. Qualquer que seja a escolha vale a pena visitar este parque e o Forte Jefferson nele construído. O forte é a maior estrutura feita com tijolos das Américas. O parque fica a 109 Km de distância de key West.

(Translated by Google) Beautiful building that is part of the World Trade Center complex. On the elevator ride to the One World Observatory, a film is shown on the elevator walls that shows the growth of the city over the years. The view from the observatory is beautiful, but perhaps not the most beautiful of all. A visit for a reflection on rebirth and overcoming.

(Original)
Belo edifício que faz parte do complexo do World Trade Center. Na subida de elevador até ao One World Observatory vai passando um filme nas paredes do elevador que mostra o crescimento da cidade ao longo dos anos. A vista que se tem do observatório é bonita, mas, talvez não seja a mais bonita de todas. Uma visita para uma reflexão sobre renascimento e superação.

(Translated by Google) Wonderful place where you can swim with dolphins and snorkel with rays and countless fish of all sizes and colors. Neoprene clothing, fins and diving goggles are provided on site and are included with the entrance. Ditto for the sunscreen that is ecological. Beach chairs and shade at ease. Restaurant just reasonable.

(Original)
Lugar maravilhoso onde é possível nadar com golfinhos e fazer snorkel com arraias e um sem número de peixes de todos os tamanhos e cores. Roupa de neoprene, pés de pato e óculos de mergulho são fornecidos no local e estão incluídos na entrada. Idem para o protetor solar que é ecológico. Cadeiras de praia e sombra à vontade. Restaurante apenas razoável.

(Translated by Google) Dry Tortugas National Park can be reached by boat or hydro-plane. The first is more economical but it takes longer to get there. Whatever the choice, it is worth visiting this park and Fort Jefferson built there. The fort is the largest brick structure in the Americas. The park is 109 km away from Key West.

(Original)
Podemos chegar ao Dry Tortugas National Park de barco ou de hidro-avião. O primeiro é mais econômico mas demora mais tempo para chegar lá. Qualquer que seja a escolha vale a pena visitar este parque e o Forte Jefferson nele construído. O forte é a maior estrutura feita com tijolos das Américas. O parque fica a 109 Km de distância de key West.

(Translated by Google) St. Patrick's Cathedral is very close to the Rockfeller Center and was built in the late 19th century in neo-Gothic style. It has recently been restored and has been visited by several Popes. It is considered a National Historic Landmark. Highlight for the panels and stained glass inside.

(Original)
A Catedral de São Patrício fica bem pertinho do Rockfeller Center e foi construída no final do século 19 em estilo neogótico. Foi recentemente restaurada e recebeu visita de diversos Papas. É considerada Marco Histórico Nacional. Destaque para os painéis e vitrais no seu interior.

(Translated by Google) Very beautiful place. It was James Deering's winter residence from 1916 to 1925. Deering made several trips to Europe to draw inspiration from European buildings and thus build his residence in Miami. More than 1000 workers from the Caribbean and Europe were used in its construction.

(Original)
Local muito bonito. Foi residência de inverno de James Deering de 1916 a 1925. Deering fez várias viagens à Europa para se inspirar nas construções europeias e assim construir a sua residência em Miami. Na sua construção foram usados mais de 1000 trabalhadores do Caribe e da Europa.

(Translated by Google) I wanted to do a tour of the Ca 'd'Zan at the entrance but I was informed, in a way somewhat rude, that the tours would only be made over the weekend. It was a shame because for some time I was wanting to make this visit. I just took some pictures of the entrance.

(Original)
Queria fazer uma visita guiada à Ca' d'Zan mas logo na entrada fui informado, de um modo um tanto rude, que as visitas guiadas só seriam feitas no final de semana. Foi uma pena pois há algum tempo estava querendo fazer esta visita. Limitei-me a tirar algumas fotos da entrada.

(Translated by Google) Pier 60 is widely used by fishermen trying to catch one or the other fish. If they succeed, soon pelicans, herons and seagulls appear who take advantage of the distraction of the fishermen to make a free mouth. It is a spectacle in itself associated with the beauty of the place.

(Original)
O pier 60 é muito usado por pescadores que tentam pegar um ou outro peixe. Se conseguem, logo aparecem pelicanos, garças e gaivotas que aproveitam a distração dos pescadores para fazerem uma boca livre. É um espetáculo por si só associado às belezas do local.

(Translated by Google) After a walk through Sun`n Fun I went to visit the Florida Air Museum. Small museum for the number of aircraft that are inside. Such a collection would deserve a larger space. I saw some models that made history and some interesting curiosities.

(Original)
Depois de um passeio pela Sun`n Fun fui conhecer o Museu do Ar da Florida. Museu pequeno para a quantidade de aeronaves que estão no seu interior. Tal acervo mereceria um espaço maior. Vi alguns modelos que fizeram história e algumas curiosidades interessantes.

(Translated by Google) Lighthouse at one end of the island. Very well kept and still operant. The beach next to the lighthouse is dangerous for swimming due to strong currents but is very used for fishing.

(Original)
Farol em um dos extremos da ilha. Muito bem cuidado e ainda operante. A praia junto do farol é perigosa para banho devido às fortes correntes mas é muito usada para pescarias.

(Translated by Google) Beautiful museum that shows a little of the history of Henry Flagler and Florida. This 55-room mansion was a gift from Henry Flagler to his wife Mary Lily Kenan Flagler.

(Original)
Belo museu que mostra um pouco da história de Henry Flagler e da Flórida. Esta mansão possui 55 quartos e foi um presente de Henry Flagler a sua esposa Mary Lily Kenan Flagler.

(Translated by Google) Beautiful boat trip through the interior of the Mexico pavilion. Highlight for the Mayan and Aztec culture, for the beaches (Acapulco among others) and for the music.

(Original)
Bonito passeio de barco pelo interior do pavilhão do México. Destaque para a cultura Maia e Asteca, para as praias (Acapulco entre outras) e para a música.

(Translated by Google) Beautiful pavilion with replicas of some monuments of Venice (Doge's Palace, Belfry of St. Mark's Square, etc.). It has good restaurants for Italian food.

(Original)
Belíssimo pavilhão com réplicas de alguns monumentos de Veneza (Palácio Ducal, Campanário da Praça de São Marcos, etc.). Tem bons restaurantes de comida italiana.

(Translated by Google) Fair tribute to a woman who stood out for her contributions in the field of literature. This statue is one of 5 that exist in Bryant Park.

(Original)
Justa homenagem a uma mulher que se destacou pelas suas contribuições no campo da literatura. Esta estátua é uma das 5 que existem no Bryant Park.

(Translated by Google) Beautiful pavilion with emphasis on oil (which is extracted in the North Sea in extreme conditions), for fishing and of course, for Vikings,

(Original)
Bonito pavilhão com destaque para o petróleo (que é extraído no mar do Norte em condições extremas), para a pesca e claro, para os Vikings,

(Translated by Google) Very good beach for swimming. Clear water and calm sea. Optional nudist on left side of beach. Huge paid car park.

(Original)
Praia muito boa para banho. Água limpa e mar calmo. Nudismo opcional do lado esquerdo da praia. Enorme parque de estacionamento pago.

(Translated by Google) Beautiful tower that is attached to the Museum of Man. It is in Balboa Park and is one of the many attractions of this park.

(Original)
Belíssima torre que fica anexa ao Museum of Man. Fica no Balboa Park e é uma das muitas atrações deste parque.

(Translated by Google) After crossing Central Park from end to end, we sat on a bench and were treated to the sight of this statue.

(Original)
Depois de atravessarmos o Central Park de ponta a ponta, sentamo-nos em um banco e fomos brindados com a visão desta estátua.

(Translated by Google) Beautiful pavilion representing Japanese culture well. It has a good restaurant and a fantastic souvenir shop.

(Original)
Bonito pavilhão representando bem a cultura japonesa. Tem um bom restaurante e uma fantástica loja de souvenires.

(Translated by Google) Impossible not to be moved. Beautiful monument that honors the victims of the Holocaust.

(Original)
Impossível não se emocionar. Belíssimo monumento que homenageia as vítimas do Holocausto.

(Translated by Google) Beautiful castle. It was inspired by Germany's no less beautiful Neuschwanstein Castle.

(Original)
Castelo lindo. Foi inspirado no não menos bonito Castelo de Neuschwanstein da Alemanha.

(Translated by Google) One of the many museums in Balboa Park. The facade of this museum is magnificent.

(Original)
Um dos muitos museus do Balboa Park. A fachada deste museu é magnífica.

(Translated by Google) Long wait time but worth it. Perfect attraction in the smallest details.

(Original)
Tempo de espera longo mas vale a pena. Atração perfeita nos mínimos detalhes.

Davy Crockett State Park is a fun park. The visitors center is the first building when entering the park. We stopped at the visitors center to pick up some maps of the area. We parked by a playground next to campground 1. From there we hit the trailhead for the Shoal Creek trail. The trail follows Shoals Creek to Davy Crockett Falls. Its not much of a falls but a fun area to play in the water. The trail was 3 miles round trip. We drove through campground 1 and it seemed like the sites were spread out fairly well. Most sites were flat but a few requires  a lot of leveling.  Campground 2 was shut down for improvements . There is a covered bridge over  Shoal Creek.  We visited Lake Lindsey where you can fish for bass, blue gill and catfish. You can rent a jon boat or a small paddle pontoon boat that seats four.  Boat rentals were 2.50 per person for 30 minutes. We rented a paddle boat and floated to the dam and spill way. Just beyond the spill way is a fairly nice waterfall. From the lake you can view an eagles nest.

Cummins Falls is one of Tennessee's newest State parks. The is a trail to an overlook of the falls and it is spectacular.  The trail to the falls is about one mile and it's fairly easy to get to the bottom. Once you are at the bottom you must plan on getting wet because you will cross the river at least once. There is a small water fall on the right before you reach Cummins falls. Cummins Falls is amazing and the swimming hole is probably Tennessee's best. I think there are up to 7000 visitors per day during a summer weekend. Weekdays are not as busy. There are life jackets provided at the base of the falls, but are not required. There is also a trail to the top of the waterfall. It is best to get there early and get a parking spot close to the trailhead. As it gets busier you may have to park at the entrance making it a long walk to the trailhead.

We stopped at the visitors center to get some information since it was our first time at Chickasaw. They were very nice and helpful. The bathrooms at the visitors center were very clean. Near the visitors center there is a residential owl and hawk that you can get a close up view. There are cabin rentals that are very cute. There is a RV campground that appears to be very nice and partly shaded. The tent camping area has some beautiful sites near the lake. There is also a wrangler campground for horseback  riders. You can fish on Lake Placid for crappie, bass, bream, and catfish. There is a swim area on the lake and a playground nearby. You can rent a kayak, canoe, pedal boat, or jon boat. There is a beautiful walking bridge that goes across Lake Placid. The best thing about Tennessee state parks is there is no fee to enter the park.

The drive to the state park is beautiful so be sure to explore all the roads around the park. As you enter the park you drive across the dam which is just one lane. There is a picnic area below the dam with a small playground.  There are restrooms below the dam. Just above the dam you can rent Jon boats, kayaks, canoes, paddle boats and paddle boards. All were inexpensive to rent. There is a visitors center down the road from the dam. A four mile trail goes around the lake. There are several CCC structures.  The campground was very nice.  It wasn't too crowded when I was there. It doesn't look like the sites are too close together.  The campsites were shaded well.

Sycamore Shoals is a very nice State Park. The visitors center is very close to the entrance . We stopped at the visitors center to get maps of the park. There is a lot of history of the frontier life displayed inside the visitors center. When you go out the back door of the visitors center,  there is a life like fort that you can explore. Behind the fort is an amphitheater. Behind the amphitheater is a gravel trail along the Watauga River. The trail is very nice without any hills. It a an easy hike and I think it's a two mile loop. It's hard to judge the river because it was flooded. I think it would be a good river to kayak.

There is a lot to see in this small state park. The campground is beautifully shaded and the sites are spaced out fairly nicely. The visitors center looks like it has been recently updated.  You can walk on top of the visitors center to view the dam and Big Duck River. There are two nice waterfalls on Big Duck River Blue Hole Falls and Big Falls. The Little Duck River has one nice waterfall named Step Falls. The two rivers come together on the backside of the state park to form the Duck River. It doesn't cost anything to visit Tennessee State Parks.

We stopped at the visitors center to pick up some maps of the area. The visitors center is in the back past the swimming pool. The river was flooded so we couldn't play in it at all. I am sure is fun when the water level is down. There is a trail along the river giving you easy access to it. Up river is a creek that flows into the river. Down stream are some rapids or small waterfall. The campground was packed in tightly. I think there are 88 camping sites. The campground is only partly shaded. If you want a camp site you need to plan in advanced.

This is a beautiful, clean and well groomed state park. They are doing a lot improvements on the campground. There will be full hook ups on all sites soon. The sites are not too tightly packed together.  It is lacking shade though. The campground is close to a small lake. There is a small campground store. Paddle boats can be rented there. There is plenty of picnic areas and playground.  There are a few easy trails along the lakes. You can fish for bluegill, bass and catfish.

Rocky Fork is Tennessee's newest state park and it is going to be awesome. You will drive along the river for a good distance on your way to the parking lot. There are several places along the way to stop and enjoy the beautiful river. I am sure that I saw someone trout fishing in one of the pools. There was a parking lot for access to the trails. There is a lot of potential for this new state park. The best thing about Tennessee State parks is there is no fee to enter.

The drive to Roan Mountain State Park is beautiful. You will see the visitors center as soon as you enter the park. We stopped there to pick up some maps. The Doe River flows in front of the visitors center. There are over 100 camping sites for tents and campers. The Miller farmstead is very interesting. On the way to the farmstead is a beautiful overlook. While there you can enjoy hiking, biking, swimming, fishing and much more.

I can not say enough about Sleeping Bear Dunes. It is an extremely beautiful place. We drove down Pierce Stocking Road which is a very scenic drive. We stopped at point 9 and 10 to watch the sunset and it was amazing.  The views of Lake Michigan are gorgeous. We were at the top of the dunes and watched a bald eagle fly below us at lake level. We also did the dune climb which was a little difficult. It was an amazing experience.

Very nice park. There was beach access on the gulf side. The gulf side was beautiful. You could have a very private spot if you don't mind walking just a little. The water was great. On the bay side you could kayak. They have kayak rentals if you don't have your own kayak. There is a little store bit did not have much to offer. You could swim and snorkel on the bay side also. There was a boat launch on the bay side.

Cove Lake State Park is a beautiful park surrounded by mountains.  There is a paved trail that takes you along the lake and swamp areas to view wildlife.  Don't bypass the observation deck on the trail. There are plenty of picnic areas, a swimming pool, tennis courts, kayaking and fishing. The paved trail can also be used for biking. The campground appears to be packed is tightly but shaded.

Tent campsites are on the river and they are awesome. We really enjoyed camping here for the weekend. The camper sites are not near the river but they are also nice. We have never camped in the rv area but we did drive through it. There are nice bathrooms on the tent campsites but you have to go to the rv sites to get a shower. There is easy kayak and canoe access at the tent campground.

Foster Falls is one of Tennessee's most beautiful waterfalls. It is very easy to get to the overlook of the falls. Getting to the bottom is a little difficult . The view from the bottom is even more beautiful.  There is a fairly nice swimming hole at the bottom. There is a trail going across the top which gives you a different view of the water fall. There are many trails in the area.

Fort Loudoun is a beautiful state park. We stopped at the visitors center to learn more about the park and we got our state park passport stamped. Everyone there was very friendly and helpful. We walked behind the visitors center to explore the fort. There is a boat ramp to launch kayaks and canoes. Great access to Little Tennessee River.

Quickly became one of my favorite trails. It isn't very difficult to get to the falls. There is a primitive campground with about 8 sites. All of the camp sites are spread out to provide a little privacy. There is also a group site. There is a port a potty at the campground. The waterfall is not of the best in Tennessee.

Burgess Falls is one of the most beautiful waterfalls in Tennessee. The trail th the bottom is no longer open because of damage from flooding. You can kayak to the bottom of Burgess Falls from Center Hill Lake if you don't mind paddling for a few hours. Be sure to explore the area, and don't miss out on anything

We took the tour of Dunbar Cave and it was amazing.  The park ranger did an excellent job describing the cave and its history. There are hiking trails and a small lake for fishing. There is no fee to enter the state park. There is a fee of about 15.00 to tour the cave.
Beautiful river walk. Awesome bridge across the river on the way to the gravesite. The river is great for fishing ,kayaking ,and canoeing. There is a lot of history to be found at the visitor center.
Beautiful place to just walk around. I loved the large granite map of Tennessee.  There are a lot of restaurants in the area to grab a bite to eat.
Part of Rock Island and is a beautiful waterfall. It is a man made waterfall caused by the dam just upstream.  It is best just after a good rain.
This is a very nice state park. The water was beautiful and hiking was nice. The water level was too high to walk to the island.
This is an awesome campground with access to Tim's Ford Lake. I believe it is now part of Tim's Ford State Park.
This in kind of the entrance to Slab City. It has very unique art and a very interesting background story.

Monticello is a different experience now with Covid. There used to be a live tour guide that took you through the house which was nice because you learn something different from each guide. Now, you swipe a QR code with your phone in each room to hear a short summary of the room and you can read additional facts on your phone. The benefit of this is that you can take your time and move at your own place. Another change is now you can take flashless pictures which is really nice! The gardens were lovely with lots of blooming bulbs, Bluebells, and Redbuds.

Smith's Fort Plantation is one of the most fascinating historical places in Virginia! It is certainly one of the oldest with the earthworks dating back to an attempt to build a fort by Captain John Smith in 1609. The property (before the house was built) was part of Pocahontas' dowry upon her marriage to John Rolfe. Take a tour from the amazing tour guide to learn the rest of this properties history. The period pieces in this house are particularly old and unique! Not to be missed if you love history!

Reds Meadows and Devil's Postpile is a lovely area and worth the trip down there if you are in the Mammoth area. With a few exceptions, you will need to ride the shuttle bus down (there is a fee) but it does run frequently. Besides seeing Devil's Postpile; Rainbow Falls and Minaret Falls are all on the same trail and are very beautiful! Several campgrounds are available also but usually require a reservation during weekends.These pictures are from dusk at Minaret Falls.

Excellent zoo and botanical gardens! Good information is posted on signs about the different animals.
Lots of feeding events and talks scheduled throughout the day. On the botanical side, more signs posted with botanical names would be helpful, especially with the Salvia. The hiking trails were beautiful but the biggest loop was fairly strenuous. The views on top of Eisenhower Mt. were well worth it though! Spent 6 hours here and never sat down, highly recommended!

Lovely lake and trails galore! Douthat is one of the first state parks and has beautiful log cabins, lodges, equestrian corrals and three campgrounds. The lake itself has a beach with a lifeguard in season. Douthat has one of the largest trail systems that I have seen at a state park, 43 miles worth! Two of the trails had waterfalls which were nice. The other trail we took was Mountain Top which had a nice view as you might guess. Well worth the trip!

The new American Revolution Museum replaces the old one in the same location. It is amazing and beautiful!!! It is huge and has lots of exhibits, statues, and several theaters. Our favorite part is the Siege Theater which is experiential, you feel like you are really in the middle of the siege! We spent 3 hours in there and could have stayed longer. It was very cold so we never got to the outdoor exhibits, good excuse for another trip!

Point of Honor is a beautiful Federal home built in 1815 by Dr Cabell who was a physician to Patrick Henry. The tour was excellent and they have done a fabulous job restoring the home. Great view of the James River from the second story. The rooms are enormous with lots of large windows and intricately carved mantel pieces. The dining room and the receiving room are particularly nice.
