The Visitor center was open for ticket sales, gift shop, and restrooms only. Displays were covered up and there were no paper maps,  only QR code for your phone. Because of limited tours and almost no restaurants open, ticket price was reduced to $27 per day. Another victim of the virus! The docents in their costumes (along with modern masks) were great though!

Provides easy access to Mono Lake. There is also a board walk to a lake lookout point and a trail, 1.2 miles, that goes up to the Mono Lake Visitor center. Along the dirt trail you can see the Icebox Tufa. Very interesting! The informative signs along the trails are well done. Also, the only part of Mono Lake open in the forestry shutdown!

Bodie State Historic Park is always fascinating,  we have been there four times now over a long period. Park service has done a good job of maintaining the town  and preserving the buildings. The walking tour booklet they sell for $3.00 is well worth it. Allow at least 2 to 3 hours to see everything! Dogs allowed on a leash.

This is a wonderful museum! I didn't allow enough time so I will have to back again, didn't realize how extensive it would be! Besides the history of the Carson Valley, they also cover the Washoe Indians, the wild mustangs, and more on the bottom floor. The book store has a great selection of books! Can't wait to return!

Fabulous museum!! It covered a much broader spectrum of subjects than we expected. Everything about this museum was very well done; the artifacts, the presentation, the signs and interpretations and especially the tour by Mike! Mike has a wealth of knowledge and gave a very detailed and enthusiastic presentation!

The Governor's Palce is magnificent, decorations inside represent the period beautifully! My favorite room is the entrance foyer with cleverly arranged swords and rifles! Downstairs only at this time, there was still plenty to enjoy. The gardens, the maze, and the bridge over the canal should not be missed!

This is THE place to go to for sunset pictures in the Moab area! Go the the end Dead Horse Point, it is very large and allows for many people and many views of the incredibly vast series of canyons and cliff's! Incredible!! This state park has 7 miles of hiking trails, along the rim only.

The Art Museum was huge- period paintings, furniture,  sterling silver, and every other form of art! Enjoyed it immensely! The Cafe downstairs was not so good. Maybe the virus is to blame but the sandwiches were very cold, tasteless and prepackaged.

Excellent visitor center with knowledgeable staff. They have a short but informative plant nature trail around the building. The longer hike from the center looked good but we didn't have the time. We picked up a lot of good hiking ideas from here.

Fascinating tour! Seeing and smelling the various medicinal herbs really added to the experience. They also had original surgery tools and live leaches! It felt like stepping back into time, wonderful!
This is a hidden gem in Richmond! Beautiful furnishings, many which are original. The tour guide was excellent! If you enjoy history, this should be at the top of your list in Richmond!
It was a very short, easy hike.to this famous arch. Great view through the arch too. The trail is a loop and on the way back are lots of plant ID signs with interesting facts.
The Capitol building has a very interesting history that was presented well by the docent. Tour was downstairs only now. Tour was about 10 mi minutes long.
Beautiful views! Just be aware that the roads are very steep and winding over the pass and it took about 40 minutes longer than anticipated to drive this.
Huge selection of wines to taste in a beautiful tasting room. The tour by Bill was outstanding!! The best wine tasting experience we have had in Virginia!
A very beautiful park, underrated I think. Some arches and lots of canyons to view. Hike to Mesa Arch was great and so was Upheaval Dome!
Lovely marsh area known for its bird and other wildlife watching. There are trails for hiking and kayaking is possinle in the marsh.
Steep hike up but worth  it! Very popular,  you will need to wait in line to have your photo taken under the arch.

Raven Rock is a popular state park to go to that has easy to moderate hikes great for family and escaping into the wilderness for a bit. You'll want to try to get here around 9 am because the park gets packed around 10-11 am and isn't worth worth waiting for if that's the case. They will usually post it on Facebook when the parking lot is full.

The namesake trail 'Raven Rock Loop' is 2.6 miles and takes you to a large rock wall that has an abstract imprint a raven with the Cape Fear River lazily flowing near by. Along the way, you'll pass an 'overlook' that shows the Cape Fear River from a higher view point too.

The Fish Traps Trail is another sight worth walking to that isn't too far. It has the river close up and you'll see some triangular rock beds that act as 'fish traps.' There are some large rock platforms along the way that you can stop on if you don't mind getting a little wet.

Another notable trail is the Lanier Falls Rapids. At the end of the hike, you can walk across the river about 10 feet to an island that is pretty neat to be on. The water goes about waist deep for an average adult (I'm 5'8") so you'll definitely get wet if you decide to go on it. Worth it though!

All in all, this is a decent park to check out if you have time to do some light hiking. You'll probably see a few critters along the way too (squirrels, birds and possibly snakes and/or spiders). I recommend wearing some bug spray and some sunscreen.

They are starting to allow seating to those who are vaccinated so it's a step towards normalcy!

The Dodgers are the 2020 World Series Champs and have a nice home stadium. There is plenty of parking so driving is a decent option since public transportation is a bit inconvenient to use for getting here. Tickets are a bit pricey ($80-100), but what would you expect especially in LA?

Alcoholic drinks are also in the same price point ranging from about $15-20. I got their namesake beer and the Blue Margarita for the same price of about $20. The regular beers are around $15. The food is a much better deal with Salted Peanuts and Dodger Dogs for about $7. They have one stand that does sell wine though for $10 which I think is the best deal over on the right field side.

The Dodger Dog I got was nothing special in my opinion. It was unfortunately a bit overcooked and the bun was stiff from being on the warming plate for too long. It just came with mustard and ketchup as well.

Overall, love the sport and this stadium, but you'll definitely spend a pretty penny if you want drinks. Food isn't too bad price wise though!

The Cocoa Beach Pier is touristy, but if you do go then I'd recommend Rikki Tiki Tavern because you'll have fantastic views of the Atlantic and will be able to watch the surfers do their thing on the waters. Try to go when parking is free (usually after 4:00 pm M-F and 5:00 pm weekends) otherwise you'll end up spending about $15-20. It's an additional $2.00 to get into this area, but you'll get a token to receive $2.00 off of a drink at the bar. You could avoid this just by staying on the main pier area, but something about being underneath a thatched-roof and having a cold one seems so right in this area.

They have food for purchase and every now and then will have some live entertainment to add to the atmosphere. The food is simple, but tasty and comes from their main kitchen to your location in a covered plastic container. I ended up getting their Grilled Pineapple Chicken Wrap with a side of potato salad (other options include chips, fruits salad, or slaw). Overall, it was exactly what I wanted and had a good amount of chicken in it compared to the vegetables and wrap itself.

There is a good amount of raw talent here. It almost has an underground kind of vibe that definitely makes a statement. The current exhibit is "Robot Love: Prove You Are Human" and they have some pretty thought provoking pieces.

There is a mix of local and some national artists. The musuem itself is a bit cluttered in some areas and may not be as organized as your typical art musuem, but I think it's part of its charm. It's a bit of a disarray with some incongruent pieces mashed together which makes it interesting. I really enjoyed it and found a lot of pieces that resonated to me.

Best of all, it's free for the most part unless there is a special event going on. There is free street parking and plenty of restaurants and boutiques near by. I recommend grabbing a cup of joe at Anaya's and fresh pie at Joan's Perfect Pie right across the street! There is also a nice open brewery a few minute walk away called Intercoastal.

Pretty much just park and wander around the Historic Eau Gallie District area!
likes: Mix of local and national artists

reviews_attraction.text:
Just went here this past weekend and they are doing temperature checks and have limited entry points too. Masks are required when not eating or drinking. It's pretty packed in the late afternoon and evenings so I would recommend swinging here in the mornings to help avoid large groups of people or on the weekdays.

The ferry is not available unfortunately and the dole whip station was broken when I went. Super bummed about that!

Anyways, I really enjoy making a half-day trip down to Disney Springs because it's always full of life (crowded, but free people watching entertaining) and there is always something going on.

It is one of the few 'free things' to go to that is owned by Disney--free parking! It is hard to resist spending money here because it is literally filled with stores to shop at and restaurants to eat at. With that being said, it is a good place to test your will power against material goodies if you aim for just window shopping or wandering aimlessly.
dislikes: Crowded in late afternoons and evenings
Masks mandatory (except when eating or drinking)

reviews_attraction.text:
This is a great park with a beautiful reservoir, hence its name! Definitely good for paddle-boarding or kayaking. Parking at the main location can be a pain especially early in the morning when all the early-bird runners are getting their workouts in. However, they have three other parking spots for access to the other trails: Elizabeth Rounds Park (570 Pee Dee Rd) or Whitehall Trail (490 Pee Dee Rd) and up north at Nick's Greenway (7200 NC 22 Hwy).

The main loop (David R White) is about 2 miles long around the lake, but they have plenty of other trails that you can mix and match to add to your run. There are also little work out challenges through the path so you could end up doing a circuit-like workout as well. They also have a disc golf course going on too if you're into that.

Overall, it's a lively park with a lot of people and is a trail runner's paradise with all the paths to take. So grab your running shoes because there is much to explore!

I have always wanted to do an airboat tour over the swamps and encounter some wild gators and I finally got to do so at Boggy Creek Airboat Adventures! This place is about an hour from the Orlando airport and is perfect to take family and friends to other than the usual theme parks.

I ended up doing the half hour tour for about $30 per person, but they also have hour long tours for $50 per person and other variations as well (sunset, private, you actually driving the airboat, and night tours). The tour guide is knowledgeable and knows all of the good spots to see wildlife and you will absolutely see a gator. The one that we saw was definitely about 10 feet long... Definitely do not want to get close to that one!

This location also has a mini zoo where you can see baby alligators and even feed them too. Overall, I enjoyed my experience at Boggy Creek and would take other people here since it is pretty unique ecosystem being a part of the south.

The wheel looks a lot cooler passing and seeing it from the highway than being on it. It's mostly because there really are no breathtaking "views" making the top of the wheel a little underwhelming. It's touristy for sure and it's not a bad thing, but living here for a few years have made me wary of what it was going to be like. However, for a person visiting here for the first time, it'd be something to check out.

It does a good job at describing key things about Orlando through a narration that accompanies the ~20 minute ride. There are also two interactive tablets that you can use to get more info on key attractions. There are also seats at the center of the gondola. You can also purchase drinks beforehand and enjoy it on the ride.

Overall though, it's a straightforward and simple ride that kiddos and first timers would really enjoy.

Today (Sun, 3 Jan) is the last day of the 'Points of Connection' display by Filipino-American artist JEFRË! Opened from 12 pm to 4 pm Sunday. Definitely do not want to miss this exhibit as his statues, art, and story are captivating. I found myself staring at them almost endlessly because of their modern and sleek design. If you like huge steel works of art then you have to see them!

The musuem overall is well put together with some great pieces that are eclectic enough so you'll most likely find something that will resonate.

It's located near the Orlando Science Center and the Mennello Art Museum so you can hit those two as well. It's also a quick car ride to some of Orlando best restaurants as well. I recommend Black Bean Deli, which is what I went to, or Hawkers Asian Street Fare!

I'd say that this is museum was a bit smaller than I was expecting, but currently has some iconic and historic work from the Florida Highwaymen (mostly self-taught African American artists) that is worth checking out. It should be opened until about the end of March 2021. They have a few other collections as well and currently they are featuring that and Ancient Heroines. It's their 100 year anniversary and they will be undergoing a remodel of sorts so that's pretty exciting too!

Admission costs $15 for adults and $7.50 for seniors, military, Florida educators, and professional artists. Students are $5 and children are free!! There is also a small cafe with a gift shop right next to it as well.

Also, it's right next to the riverwalk so you can have a nice stroll afterwards!
likes: Facilities & Services: Affordable admission, discounts, free for children

reviews_attraction.text:
Admission is $10 for adults and $5 for children (free under 5). The winter hours are 10 am to 4 pm Monday to Saturday (and 12 pm to 4 pm on Sundays). For summer, it's 9 am to 5 pm. They have group rates (more than 25 people) for $8 for adults and $4 for children.

Overall, it's a pretty large garden that has multiple trails for a nice walk. The longest loop is over a mile. This place makes a great place to host a reception or other event. I came here in the fall so the garden wasn't as booming, but I was still able to capture some beautiful greenery and flora!

There is a pond that has some koi fish that you can feed. A bag of fish treats are only $1 at the gift shop so pick some up before heading out to explore the garden!

The COVID-19 hours for the musuem is from Tuesday to Friday 10 am to 4:30 pm. So unfortunately, it's not opened on the weekends. However, admission is free so donations are greatly appreciated.

It's a very well organized museum that focuses on airborne and special ops from the 1940s to present day. A lot of history and action displays that bring the stories to life.

There is currently a GWOT (Global War on Terror) Memorial Flag Exhibition that will pull on your heart strings from the sacrifices made. It is made of around 7,000 dog tags and makes a lasting impression. This special exhibit should be here until the end of the year.

Don't forget to hit up the gift shop! A lot of really neat memorabilia to check out.

This memorial is worth checking out because of the emotionally driven artistry it invokes while seeing it up close and allows you to take a moment to reflect on humanity. Although it can be quite somber, it helps put things into perspective and is a reminder of history, which is important to have. What makes this structure even more special is that it was established by Holocaust survivors in the South Florida area.

Visiting the memorial is free and there is also a self-guided tour brochure available ($2 suggested donation) that'll take about an hour to go through. If you happen to have a larger group (10 or more), you can make a reservation before visiting the memorial on their website 2 weeks in advanced.

With all that is going on in the world, it's good to take a breather amidst nature to decompress.

This is a good park to take a leisurely stroll since they have a ~1 mile paved trail (~2 mile round trip) that also acts as the disc golf course with benches throughout. There is also a dock that has calming views on the Glenville Lake. You may encounter some wildlife as well such as bunnies that I saw on my first trip.

At the other end of the park are some tennis courts that has a separate parking space. If you were to walk, it would take about 10-15 minutes to get there.

As of June 3, 2020, the park is opened until 7 pm, but should get back to regular hours once things are more stable.

The Coconut Vendor here made my trip. No official cost, but rather just tip what you think he deserves. Such a good person with an easy going vibe that's genuine. Super fresh coconuts too. Literally coconuts still on the branch that he uses a machete to whack off. Watching him do it and wracking it again is quite the sight too!

Aside from him, there is a plethora of entertainers doing their thing from acrobatics, bag pipers, jump scares, and more!

It's free and they only downside is that it can be crowded. However, if you manage to get a good sunset view it makes it all worth it.

Crazy, colorful, beautiful...
likes: Facilities & Services: Coconut Vendor, Fresh Coconuts

reviews_attraction.text:
Glass artwork can be mesmerizing as this Chihuly Collection will show. The craftsmanship and elegance of some of these pieces is mind blowing or should I say glass blowing?

Admission is $20, but it also includes entry to the Morean Art Center across the street and a glass blowing demo around the corner at the Morean Glass Studio. A very great deal if you ask me!

Dale Chihuly is very well know up in the Seattle, WA area so it's cool that he as an exhibit right in St. Pete. Definitely worth a visit if you appreciate the art and especially this one since there aren't many that specializes in glass sculptures.

This is a small art gallery that has some unique pieces. I just wish it was a little bit bigger, but it features some local artists which is nice. They were undergoing some renovations when I went so hopefully it's done by now.

You can get free admission to this gallery from purchasing entry to the Chihuly Collection right across the street. It also includes a free demo of glass blowing around the corner at the Morean Glass Studio that starts every hour!

Overall, I probably wouldn't visit this place by itself, but would incorporate it with others activities.

Between this view or the Shipwreck Musuem view, I'd choose the latter. This one doesn't really have a nice view of the ocean, but it does have a decent view of the quaint town of Key West. The cost for this is a bit overpriced, but it does keep the crowds out so it's easy to get to the top of the lighthouses without too much of a bother.

They also have a small museum that you can enjoy with history of the light house. I wasn't particularly interested in it, but it has good info.

Other than that, they have a gift shop that you can get to for free.

This house is dedicated to the other Edgar Allen Poe (not the poet, but a local businessman). He was an important figure in Fayetteville's history by owning the Poe Brick Company and was significant to the economy of the area.

They have tours that should be resuming starting 12 November 2020, but check with the Museum of Cape Fear to verify. Suggested donations is $2 for adults and $1 for children.

If you want to catch it with some Christmas decorations, they should have some wreaths and bows starting 28 November until 9 January.

Pretty cool glass work, but definitely on the pricier side. It's great for almost treating like a gallery to see some unique glass pieces. It's really neat to know that it is locally made because some of the sculptures created are ridiculously done by some talented folks! Be careful though because if you break something you're liable to pay for it.

They also do glass blowing demos on the hour. If you purchase admission to Chihuly Collection around the corner, you get this for free and access to the Morean Art Gallery as well!

A nice little relaxing pier to take a stroll on. It's near the Key West Garden Club so you can hit both for a unbelievable peaceful time. It has great views of the ocean too and is nice to visit after a night on Duval.

It also has an Aids Memorial with some quotes ingrained on a wall that will give you some contemplation.

There aren't any stores or cafes really near by, but if you walk over to Higgs Beach Pier there's a simple restaurant and a playground for kids.

Definitely worth adding to your Key West itinerary!

Yes, I like to take long walks on the beach...to Southern Pointe Park Pier!

This is a good destination to hit up in South Beach. Some great views of incoming yatchs, rocks, and for you to take some shots! (Double meaning intended. :P) You can fish at the end of the pier as well if that's your thing too, but you have to bring your own equipment.

Oh! And sunrises/sunsets here are beautiful too!

There are also some fantastic eats a short walk away! The Lobster Shack or Joe's Stone Crab to name a few!!

I went to their 'To The Hoop' exhibition last November and really enjoyed with how well everything was laid out and how they were able to do so many artsy things with a basketball!! It was part modern commentary and unusual interpretations at the same time. A very interesting collection and can only imagine what their other exhibits must be like.

Admission and parking is free so definitely must do if you're in town! Nothing to lose and you'll get to see some interesting art pieces!

Eno River is a great place for trail running that goes along the river that has nice variety of woodland plants and animals. I was able to get some pretty good nature shots from my time here.

The Cox Mountain Trail is about 4 miles round trip and is perfect for a workout. It's usually not too crowded compared to some of the other parks so parking isn't a hassle. Overall, a nice park worth visiting at least once.

Forsyth Park is the main park within Savannah, but all throughout the town you'll find plentiful of mini parks that will most likely have a statue recognizing a notable figure. It's ridiculous how photogenic everything is and it almost feels like a movie set, but it's not!

There's a farmers market that takes place on Saturdays as well if you're able to catch that!

A good hike with great views.  The first part is pretty steep and can be rough for us flatlanders.

There's no way to know how much further and whether the steepness continues.  Once you reach the sign pointing to Lily Pad Lake, the terrain gets less steep and you have 30-40 minutes left to reach the lakes.  We have up last year just before the sign.

We walked a bit slower than most.  It took 80 minutes to get up to the lakes and 60 minutes to get back down.

We saw an old Male moose with large antlers not far from the trail on the way up before the sign.  He was apparently used to hikers and didn't pay us much attention.

Good views of Frisco and Lake Dillon at certain points on the way up.

There are plenty of places to sit and enjoy nature at the lakes.  There were a bunch of squirrels and some ducks at the lakes.

Sept 2020

A great place to gather a group for an enjoyable afternoon.  I invited family and friends to come to Haak for my wife's birthday.  They were very welcoming, everyone enjoyed the place and wine, it was a simple and great time together.  Good wine, good place, good time together.

I enjoyed helping with Pruning Day for the second year in a row.  I appreciate Raymond bringing in the consultant to teach us about pruning and propagating from cuttings.  I have three vines in my yard from last year's cuttings and I took more cuttings this year to try for more.  Pruning Day is enjoyable - almost as much as Harvest Day.

After pruning we stayed for good music, great wine and good food.  The burgers and fried fish were super.

A terrific place that delivers a great experience.  We arrived just after a bus load arrived and they went out of their way to give us a great spot and make us feel welcome.

A beautiful facility and they clearly have plans to expand and make things even greater.

The Cuvee was very good.  The Pinot Noir started soft like other Pinot Noirs, but ended with some good spiciness and depth.  The cheese and meat tray was good and looked nice, but was sparse on contents, especially for the price.

We will be back to enjoy the place and drink more wine.

A great park with lots of well marked trails. You can easily spend hours walking the paths and checking things out.

The obvious first choice for everyone is the Summit hike that  takes you to the top of Enchanted Rock. It is a highlight, but wears you out for other, simpler hikes. We arrived soon after the park opened so wer could do the hike in the cooler part of a hot August day. They read a good merging. A good breeze was blowing on top of the Rock that made it comfortable.

An amazingly diverse spectrum of wines considering that they only have 20 acres and everything is estate grown.  We tasted only reds and there were 2-3 varietals I had never even heard of.

I was impressed with their red blend from their 120-year old vine acreage - enough to get a bottle.

Don't expect a fancy place.  The tasting room has unpainted plywood walls and ceiling.

The free tastings, personal attention and quality of wine make this a great winery to check out.

Terrific place to hang out with multiple porches, patios and nice areas to enjoy.  Very friendly and welcoming family owners.  Well worth the remote drive.

The Tempranillos had an off flavor.  The Lenoir was better but still not great.  Their Sangria was flavorful.  We didn't try any whites or the other reds.

I hate leaving this wine review since they are such nice people with such a nice place.  We wil try to go back and try some of their other wines.

Nice place with lots of comfortable spots to hang out inside and outside. Friendly staff that wants to help you find what you would like.

We like dry reds and found that is a wine category outside of their wheelhouse. The Lenior is the driest red they have but it was earthier and softer than our liking. We also tried their Merlot & Rose and found them to be similarly off our palates.

We didn't try their whites or sweets, which seem to be their focus.

Quaint winery with very friendly staff.  Lots of interesting wines so this is a good place to do a tasting.

The chardonnay is not packed so it is crisp and clean for a good summer wine. The gewurstaminer was very good but not too sweet.

The dry red wines are very dry but are not at all astringent. The sangria is very fruity and sweet. The blueberry is a great dessert wine. The prickly pear is very interesting and not at all wild tasting.

A terrific family winery with great wines, interesting stories and a fantastic view.  Definitely worth the drive.  The remoteness keeps.it from getting too crowded.

Their reds are all great.  The HSV Estate wine with co-fermented blends are the most interesting wines I have had.

The owners and staff are present, ready to befriend, and actively keep an enjoyable and friendly atmosphere.

Great views and a large wine selection.

The rooftop has great views and looks to be a good place to hang out.  We looked around and then went down to the first floor since it was a chilly windy day.

Not many Texas wines.  The Trapiche Malbec from Argentina is good.

Lots of residences to rent on the property.  The Lighthouse looks to be a great place to stay.

A terrific place to visit.  Very interesting to see and tour the castle. Definitely a place to see.

Pretty crowded and certainly a high volume place.  Not a place to focus on the wines, but instead a great place to visit.

The wines were okay.  The tasting was a bit rushed and inattentive since the server had to be busy with many guests coming and going.

A terrific winery to visit.  The red tastings were delicious and informative.

Walking through the vines in the front that displayed the major grape varietals was very interesting.

The culinary gardens in the back were impressive and beautiful.  There were some plants I couldn't even identify.  The walnut trees were full of fruit.

Nice winery with two sides. One side offers food pairings while the other side is a comfortable place to share a bottle or two with friends or family.

We enjoyed the Barranca red blend.  We would get it again.

We stayed inside because the weather was off.  They have outside facilities that look good for nice weather days.

They open things up for a free walk on on Friday nights in September. I'm glad they did because it gave us a chance to go see what it looks like so we could consider bringing our grandkids in the future.

It's surprising how much they can pack on this little pier. They always have specials going on.

A terrific place to visit with some of the best bourbon around.  Fully Texan in the heart of Texas Hill Country.

They give the best tour I've ever had from any distillery, winery or brewery.  They walk you through and explain each of the steps and give you tastes of each step.

A terrific job at putting together this museum!  Very interesting and the buildings and displays really put you back in that time.  Very easy to spend hours there.

Nice big yard and gazebo next to the museum that is used for concerts and other activities.

Friendly servers and comfortable porch to enjoy their wine with friends.

Tempranillo was good.  They had an even better tempranillo we tasted that wasn't on their menu sheet.  The Cabernet Claret was a bit soft for me but others in our group liked it.

A nice park with a bunch of good hiking trails.  Nice to have the trail that leads to the Rio Grande River.

The Towers with bridge between them are fun to climb and give good views.

Good water fountain with cold water at Welcome Center.

Nice little park for the kids to run around and play on a train-themed playground.  A nice set of vintage engines and cars with the ability to walk through a caboose and look into a box car.  Very well done and all free.

Really good wines at a very comfortable winery with a terrific view.  It's great to enjoy the outside patio and be served instead of having to go to a purchase counter. The outdoor fidelity is comfortable on cold days.

7/2018 - Dropped a star since there are no benches or seats for parents around the Splash Pad.

7/2017 - Great playgrounds for kids with lots of space for lots of kids in a wide age range.
Great fun for the kids and all.  The conductor give a good talk on the front let of the ride.  They were short on seats when a new group boarded at Georgetown.
Fantastic frisbee golf course.  Lots of good biking and hiking paths.  Available water fountain and restrooms.  Very well done facility and park.
Nice park, but it is really just a holding area for people in the ridiculously long lines for the Ellis Island Ferry.
Fun Frisbee golf course. Signage isn't up to date so it is confusing at times where to go for the next hole.

It's a free public beach and how could anyone complain about that?

With something like 700 miles of beaches in Florida, sure, there's many better ones but hey, you're in the Keys.  Expect almost all beaches south of Miami to be fraught with rocks and or i.e coquina and seaweed and whenever you do have nice clean sand you're very likely at an expensive poshish hotel with exclusively well manicured private beach.  So there's that.  Options for beaches are limited due to private ownership excluding the public.

... but this one's free and they do rake it up some mornings, so I've seen. And it looks like there's some concessions and toys for sale or rent.  I'm only ever out here first thing in the morning.

I remember back in the '90s, one of my bestest highschool buddies sold everything he had, quit his job, and took the bus down here planning on making a life in the Keys ...starting on this beach.  Don't do that! - I picked him up a few days later after he'd been robbed and gave up.

Lucky for him, he was able to find work in a  restaurant somewhere for a few days to earn enough keep for foods and lodging until I came to the rescue. I'm not so sure you could do that these days but I admire his courage and sense of adventure.

Wherever you are Paul, I miss you.  I'm sure you're swashbuckling somewhere else!!!  Best of luck!

Free Florida fun!

So Higgs is a pretty good beach so far as Keys beaches go, seagrass and such, they do a pretty good job of keeping up with it and people seem to Love it.

It's got a really cool art deco Southbeach like vibe though it probably helped invent it.

There's bathrooms, a pier, a pavilion, a pretty good children's play area, volleyball courts, tennis across the street.  Vendors pop up, including a really cool coffee hippy chick and then there's Salute! on the beach which is really nice if you've got the scratch. West Martello Tower and gardens are adjacent as well and are worth exploring as is the Edward B. Knight Pier, African Refugee Cemetery (very respectfully important), the ever small County beach nobody ever pays any attention to in between, and the Aids Memorial, all of which are cool and interesting and very well worth fleshing out any Keys trip if you're into robusting up your time here. The Martello Tower gardens is worthy in and of itself; lots of great photo ops there. Lots of things to do in a relatively small area.
likes: Adjacent attractions (West Martello Tower, gardens, Aids Memorial)

reviews_attraction.text:
Turkey Crick's another free fantastic Florida resource.

It's basically an L-shaped boardwalk trail that runs along Turkey Creek sporting various launches for swimming, tubing, kayaking or whatever along the way.  There's two entrances, most people use the one over on John Sims as there's also a large pavilion over at that entrance that people always seem to be enjoying. Sports a large fireplace which is nice.

I've been coming here for years and years visiting family in the area and usually try to get in a few walks whenever I can. It's about a mile one way.

There's on-site security and video surveillance if that makes you feel any better; and they're usually very friendly when you ask them whatever.

While it impresses as serene, you're never really far from earshot of the wooshing highway nearby or the startling crack of heavy military and domestic air traffic overhead.  So there's bird watching of another variety.

Nevertheless, this is a solid five Star Park for all it is.

Small free Florida fun worth having a look at. It's basically two short boardwalks under shady canopy a couple hundred yards apart that pass through some wetlands and bottom out at two narrow beach segments separated by the Casa Caselles condos. Hey folks, this is what Key West used to look like. Not unlike other Keys beaches, it's narrow and rocky and full of seagrass and do take good care to watch out for the sea glass, not the good kind. There's lots of sharp broken glass on the beach but give it a good ten years and it'll probably be an attraction. It's my guess campers, hobos, and tramps used to make good use of this quasi private quiet slice of Key West after sundown but it looks like the city's working hard to clean it up or err at least keeping up with the waves of trash and litter left behind except on the beach in the surf itself.  Such said, be careful there of glass and shady types.

Quirky Florida fun's Always a five!!

Though I think these curious trails are worth exploring not everyone will agree.

So what?  These lands were saved from development years ago and have been allowed to be reclaimed by the environment.  So don't expect well manicured gardens or trails because this isn't that though you wouldn't entirely be wrong for thinking so from the name and impressive Jurassic Park looking gate!

Unsung heros saved these hardwood trees and habitat where the Key Largo cotton mouse and wood rats largely make their home from massive sprawling concrete jungle development in the late 70s, early 80s. And though it may not seem like it to some, this is what success sometimes looks like.  Who would have thunk?

Most any all evidence of that has been raised including parts of an old radar base leaving only few curious features to explore. Fun fun.

Solid four or more, really a five but since Irma so many years ago, so much of the park is closed. Not just closed due to Irma, but if you're not a registered camper a lot of the park is off limits which is sort of a bummer. Hell, even half of the half of the bridge is closed.

Was fun to explore what's open, took us about 20 minutes to walk about the whole of the park.

There's some really cool picnic areas if you're early enough to score one. And plenty of typical Keys beaches, if you know what I'm talking about. Seagrass. Bayside Beach looks manicured which is why I imagine a lot of people come here.  Great place to play.

Really, sort of a quintessential Keys park. Everybody should visit here once or twice in their life.

Gift shop's open. There's plenty of parking. Clean bathrooms. And lots of photo ops.

What a wonderful place.  We totally enjoyed our day walking about.  Snack shop/gift shop is very reasonable, socially conscious, and delicious.  Lots to see and do.  They're working on building one of the best wet bars I've ever seen coming with the new children's play area for events, tastings, and such.  I really hope they include an awesome splash park.  Lots of trails.  The tower and the history and the Pine Wood Estate are all very interesting for young and old alike, I think.  Concert from the tower was meaningful and we were lucky enough to see a wedding prepping up, nervous groom and all!  We really enjoyed ourselves and we're thinking maybe next time we'd picnic with a bottle of wine.  Walk the trails.  ...and and...
likes: Facilities & Services (Snack shop, Gift shop, Reasonable prices, Socially conscious, Delicious food)
Activities (Walking trails, Concerts, Weddings, Potential for picnics)

reviews_attraction.text:
Key West's signature public beach. Everybody should visit here at least once in their life. Nominal entrance fee.

It's really a two-fold experience. You have the interesting history and the fort to explore as well as the beach affords a fantastic place to enjoy yourself some fun in the sun.  There's even some trails.

Goes without saying, about Keys' beaches; narrow, rocky, and rife with seagrass but this IS one of the better ones unless you're at a resort. What's especially nice is the large canopy of shade trees running up to the beach with plenty of neat picnic areas to enjoy.  Love, love, love that.

Lots of parking. Nice clean bathroom amenities.  Looks like there's concessions and beach rentals.

Fun, fun.

Key West's signature public beach. Everybody should visit here at least once in their life. Nominal entrance fee.

It's really a two-fold experience. You have the interesting history and the fort to explore as well as the beach affords a fantastic place to enjoy yourself some fun in the sun.  There's even some trails.

Goes without saying, about Keys' beaches; narrow, rocky, and rife with seagrass but this IS one of the better ones unless you're at a resort. What's especially nice is the large canopy of shade trees running up to the beach with plenty of neat picnic areas to enjoy.  Love, love, love that.

Lots of parking. Nice clean bathroom amenities.  Looks like there's concessions and beach rentals.

Fun, fun.

Good small fun. A handful of curious exhibits, some arty sculptures, the fort itself is interesting enough, and of course the real reason most people will come here, Robert the haunted doll.

Was sort of creepy for me because I was the only one in the place besides the employees and I didn't want to breathe any life into Robert by paying him any attention other than walking by.  I've had a frightening experience with a haunted doll many years ago and that's all I'm going to say about that.

Having the run of the place alone really made the experience special except for wandering off into a closed area by happenstance and unexpectedly surprising some construction worker in the dark. Yipes!! Lol

Lettuce rejoice for this is the best $2 you might ever spend on a park! Of all the fun Florida parks, this could be one to remember.  With a footpath circling about and boardwalks along the wetlands and water front there's plenty of opportunity to run into some wildlife.  This last time out there was a 6' gator encounter, large gopher tortoise, gaggle of rabbits, ibis, anhinga's, among other notable birds for birders and wildlife aficionados.  Several majestic old growth cypress trees abound older than us, our fathers, grandfathers, their fathers ... you get the idea.

Canoe rentals look interesting enough though I haven't done.  When in the area, I'm always looking to come.

One of Florida's best little known public spaces.  Trails, park, dog park, all very nice.  I've been walking and biking here for years and generally speaking, everybody's friendly.  Every now and then, there's some DnD Lotro ring gang battling it out, but I look the other way after laughing at the energy these people put into their fun.  Laughing in an appreciative way, btw.  Several springs, rental areas, camping.  Several nice, wide fields for football, soccer, flying a kite, or whatever.  Footpaths for the occasional hiker.  Thank you Volusial County, and Florida for making this public.  Democratic socialism at work.  lol

This superlative (donation based) free Florida history museum's been excellently well reviewed by fellow yelpers ad nauseam so I'll keep it short.

Free garage and street parking on the weekends!

You could blow through in a few hours or if you're like me, could spend the whole afternoon and want to return again and again.  Was especially tickled with the Central Florida bits I could find and really appreciated the artifacts and write ups on our Indigenous peoples.  Lots of Civil War stuffs.  The Silver Springs diarama's impressive.  And of course, Love the cars.  :)

I don't even have the words to describe how wondrous walking among these trees was.  I just don't.  Curious drive in as well.

Wholly recommend parking at the front lot and walking in for free and arriving early, very early.  And if you're lucky, you'll have much of the park to yourself to enjoy it in all its serene majesty.  Its something very different, magical, when its quiet enough to hear the unfettered sounds of the forest.  Awe inspiring. Thought provoking. Magical. I think you could hear them talking.

Green Springs is rich in history and one of Volusia's best natural resources.  The sulfury emerald green spring is as green as can be with two absolutely beautiful oak trees growing curiously above it.

Connecting the Spring to Spring and Rail Trials this park's seeing lots of renewed interest.

There ought to be security though.  Revelers, young and old, profane teens and skinny dipping seniors like to make this their own personal private watering hole despite rules against it, signage and warnings.  Sucks.
likes: Attraction Type: Natural resources, Green spring, Oak trees

reviews_attraction.text:
What beautiful fun, the drive up.  Running past orchards and farms and wineries and wonderful rustic road side stands selling all manner of curious wares.  Oh my.  Absolutely beautiful fun.

So the lighthouse and primitive cabin were closed up for season but at least they still let you run about the grounds and beach.  Small fun definitely worth the trip for the beautiful Sunday drive on up.

Plenty of port-o-potties for those in need; clearly they've addressed this issue from other reviews; as if.

Good small fun. Was enjoyable exploring the Geiger family's old house, the gardens, and a fantastic Audubon collection if you're into that sort of thing.  A little bit of curious history, a little bit of art.  We blew through it in an hour but you could easily spend half the day enjoying the beautiful and quiet grounds.

And they've got cats, two of them so I'm told, though only one made an appearance.

There's also a short narration, clean bathrooms, and of course, gift shop.

Put them on your list of weird Florida list of things to do on a tankful.

Free fun.  These gardens are a hidden local treasure with many different vignettes carefully manicured by volunteers centering around the sugar mill ruins, which are a sight to see in and of themselves.  We spent half a day here having fun.  There's also cuttings and small plants for sale on donation and one of those littlefreelibary's so bring your extra books to donate.

An affordable area attraction with seven floors including observation deck perfect for rocket launches or cruise ship sail aways.  Smallish learning center with floors focusing on Port Canaveral and the Space Coast.  Neat virtual reality piloting experience.  There's a movie too, gift shop, coffee shop, and you can even rent space here for whatever.  It's an ultra modern contemporary building with awe inspiring bathrooms perfect for photo ops.

Spectacular spectacular to walk among the giants!!  Wowee wow wow.  Absolutely loved walking the foot paths around North Grove.  Wow.  Was absolutely wonderful.  Driving down to South Grove, hitting the overlook, was fun too but didn't have the time to walk it.

Nominal fee to get in.  There's an information desk, small gift shop, and  bathrooms at North Grove.  Fun fun.

Was good touristy fun, learning about shipwrecks and salvaging. America's first millionaires were salvagers from the Keys, who knew?

A menagerie of interesting things, Keys bits and shipwrecker's baubles, all worth taking in. Definitely a sight to see.

We didn't get to hike up the tower because it was too windy ...but I wasn't exactly looking forward to it either ;)

It's a park. It's free. Lots of people are having fun. You can run or walk or jog about the park circumnavigating the water rife with ducks and water foul of many variations. With little one in tow, we were worried about aggressive ducks but this was nonsense.  What a wonderful free local resource. What a nice respite from the world around.

A small but beautiful Park with boat launch along boggy bayou in Niceville.  It's a great place for sunsets or simply relaxing the day away. Sports several table areas and enough green perfect for frisbee or other lights sports without being too much in the way. It's clearly a beloved spot as there's always people about.

What fun! Plenty of beaches and well manicured trails and a board walk to explore. Lots of gorgeous views.

Nice, clean facilities is always a plus. Nominal entrance fee.

Worth noting the camping area's all closed up due to hurricane Irma back in 2017.
Wowee wow wow.  More like an automobilia campus of museums with a period Cadillac dealership, gas station, diner car, and numerous exemplary out parcel collections in tow.  Amazing.

Great hike. Plenty of parking and bathrooms. We did not complete the entire loop. We were there in June of 2020 and we already did another long hike that morning and was getting really hot under the desert sun. We took the trail to the left and went to to landscape arch then up to Wall, Pautition, and Navajo arches. The way up was much easier than the way down. Definitely not a hike for beginners. Also, bring plenty of water. We saw someone carrying a Poland spring water bottle, the person looked exhausted. Bring proper water carrying bottles for desert hiking that keeps cool in a backpack, totally worth the extra $. If you like our pictures follow us on Instagram @redwanderers

We park in the Ringwood  Rec. department field parking lot across the street. There is a house across the way and the trail begins to the right of the house. Be careful not to miss the red trail. If you stay on the red triangle and green trail it is a longer and more strenuous hike.  The red trail is hard to find, it’s spray painted on the trees not the typical metal rectangles you see on most trails.

But the view you get is breathtaking! We saw two bald eagles, chipmunks, and woodpeckers along our walk. It’s definitely a hard trail so be prepared for very steep terrain and loose rocks on the way down.  The top is flat, we always bring a snack.

What an amazing place!  The kids enjoyed trying to climb up the dunes. I thought they were simply beautiful. It was a cold day in August, we started at 105 and by time we got back it was 108 and we were happy the ac in the car kicked in quickly. I wish we went at sunrise or set. Bring plenty of water and sneakers. Even though there was obviously sand everywhere, the sand was too hot to touch and if we had sandals on I don’t think we would have made it as far as we did. If we went in the morning we could have easily made it to the highest dune.  Would love to come back in the winter or spring. We also saw tracks of many animals.

Amazing! We really loved this national park. We only had about 7 hours and we were pretty satisfied. We visited June 2020 and during the covid 19 pandemic. We were not allowed to go see the palace, it was closed, but driving around and stopping for the small hikes was great. The kids enjoyed seeing the pit houses and the cliff dwellings from afar. The park is beautiful! Sometimes not a car in sight. Great time to travel.

What a fun location. We walked the entire pier.  Our kids were very curious about what the people were fishing and the fishermen were polite and answered their questions. We were there in the morning so not too crowded. The only downfall were the homeless people who lived under the pier. Though they did not pose any problems it smelled like a mix of urine and weed when walking up the stairs.

My 11 year old son and husband had a blast here. My 8 year old daughter, not so much. It really was a cool place with movie vehicles. There was also a video game spot that you could race a car. I wish we brought our daughter to the art museum across the street because she never watched most of the movies that these vehicles were in. Very well laid out, and super clean.

A bit small but it was super cool to see the tar pit!  Tar pits were in the park for free, but the museum explained it and why so many fossils are found in them. My kids, 8 and 11, loved the area were they had paleontologist with pieces of bone. One of them talked to us a little bit through the glass pointing at things to try and show us what was going on. Super cool.

We were fortunate to get the last tour of the steam train shop.  The building is beautiful.  Our kids really enjoyed the looking at the artifacts from long ago, like old scales for weighing luggage, type writers, and old phones.  The model railroad upstairs was a little outdated.  Everyone was very friendly and it was a nice stop on our way to Yellowstone.

This place was so cool.  Stopped by for about an hour and a half, which was just about right for my 7 and 10 year old.  They had an area for kids to dig in the soil/dirt to find critters.   Try to go when they release the new butterflies, it was amazing!   If my kids were a few years younger we could have spent ours there, but we still loved the place.

I am reviewing the parking lot. The lower lot was horrible. Low cars would have a hard time driving and could ruin or puncture the bottom of their car. I’ve never seen such a bumpy parking lot and we road trip all over the country. It was at the edge of the walkway over the Hudson. Also had electric car charging station.

We gave our kids the choice to float down the Colorado River In a tube or to take the hour jet boat ride and they chose the jet boat. We had a blast! We were soaking wet. We had fun and got to see down the Colorado River. All staff members were happy and knowledgeable. Would definitely do it again.

This was our first impression of Yellowstone.  We came in through the southern entrance after we visited the Grand Tetons.  Our kids were amazed.  There was a a short walk to the boardwalk.  We spent about an hour here before moving onto the next Yellowstone attraction.

This was my favorite part of Sequoia NP. I wish it was a little less crowded. I felt at peace, in fact I think many people felt that way because it was quiet for the amount of people who were up there. In August, we were able to see snow in the mountains.

We got here after sunrise.  It was a little over a mile to the end of the path and back. Be sure to bring plenty of water, colder the better.   It was amazing to stand in the middle of the vast field of salt crystals and stare into the distance.

Great hike for smaller kids or someone who can’t do hills. Mostly flat, easy hike. Good for someone who has an off road wheelchair too. Bumpy is some places but for the most part smooth, dirt path with some rocks. Nice views of the lake.

Perfect to see the sunrise while staying at Yosemite Valley Lodge. Short walk. You might see deer and other animals. You can also see upper and lower falls. Beautiful! Great for small kids, older people, or handicapped people.

One of the best places for sunset pics and to sit and admire the landscape. This is one of my favorite places in Arches National Park. Go on the night of a new moon and view the Milky Way. It’s such an amazing place.
Great place for a sunset. It was walking distance from our hotel and beautiful at sunset.  There are boats in the background and the large rock makes it look so different from other places.
So cool. We were here in mid August and lots of elephant seals. They make the most amazing sounds. Definitely worth a stop to get out enjoy some wildlife and stretch those legs.
Great quick stop. It’s all in the shade. Our family loved reading about the pit houses. It was very simple and our kids were able to understand how these houses were built.
We were passing by on our way to Great Sand NP do stopped for 2-3 hours. Great views. Park rangers were very informative. AND...we got another NP stamp!
Even though there were no tours because of Covid it was a great experience. My kids loved imagining what it would be like to live there. Great views.
Great flat trail until you get to the slot canyon. The kids had lots of fun climbing up the canyon.  We saw a sea snail on our walk back to the car.
Great place to stop. Beware that it is an unpaved Road. But not many people so cool to see the salt crystals and take pictures.
Great viewpoint! We were unable to do the tour due to covid restrictions. But happy they had this viewpoint to enjoy.

I have visited many state parks across Texas and was not disappointed with Mother Neff. There is a wide variety of well maintained trails with water features along with noticeable changes of vegetation and terrain. The highlight for me was the cave. My only complaint is that the park was packed. If you are interested in solitude and serious off-trail hiking, this is not the place for you. For more remote and primitive hiking get an access card for the Fort Hood area. However, if you have children or are going for a family get together this is the spot. I still rate a 5/5 because the park itself is beautiful. Definitely visit if you find yourself in the vicinity.

I visited the Kiwanis Cabin for the first time in November of 2018 and thoroughly enjoyed the hike and the destination. I took the tram up the mountain and hiked the remaining mile and a half or so. Even with strong winds and some snow the hike wasn't too bad. I live close to sea-level so I definitely noticed the difference being at such a high elevation. Nonetheless, it was all worth it. The cabin itself is very solid and perfectly situated at the pinnacle of the mountain. This is a perfect place to take photos or just enjoy the breathtaking views. I certainly recommend visiting if you're in the area.

Whether you're a local or from out of state I highly recommend coming to Kemah Boardwalk. There's an eclectic mix of shops, a water taxi, amusement rides, and several restaurants. My favorite ride here was the wooden roller coaster and the platform that rises high above the park and rotates. Located immediately nearby there is also plenty of locally owned shops and bars that are casual and fun to explore. Also not far is Galveston Island and downtown Houston is about 30 minutes away depending on traffic. I would certainly put Kemah on your list of summertime stops.

En route to Houston my partner and I decided to stop at Bastrop State Park and hike for a couple of hours. The ranger station had plenty of reasonably priced souvenirs and the rangers themselves were also very nice. Despite the fire that happened here, this state park is still beautiful. There are plenty of trails and several scenic viewpoints. My only complaint is the excessive highway noise. I typically prefer more primitive and remote places, but I wasn't disappointed with my visit. If you're coming with family this would be a great spot for an outing.

The revamped pedestrian only Ronald Kirk Bridge is a fine addition to the Dallas city center. I'm pleased that the city of Dallas took the initiative to turn an old bridge in to an interesting urban oasis. When crossing, one will see an eclectic mix of people. I enjoy visiting at night to admire the skyline. Before the adjacent Margaret Hunt Hill Bridge existed I used to drive my car across this one. Regardless of when you visit, it's a great place to take photos or bring a date for a walk. I highly recommend coming here when in the area.

I recently visited Battleship Texas for the first time in March of 2019 and thoroughly enjoyed everything there is to see. This place is a great attraction for families and history buffs alike. Admission is also reasonably priced, I think I spent around $24 for two adults. I can spend hours marveling at the all of the manual dials and controls that were designed in a time before the pervasive use of computers. That fact alone is impressive in itself. Whether you're a local or visiting, I highly recommend making a stop.

This is a very nice place to walk to and enjoy beautiful scenery. There were far fewer people than Twin Falls. I'm not too confident of the cleanliness of the water however. The water appeared clean enough though. I still recommend looking at the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) website (or other applicable regulatory agency) to determine if bacterial levels are within acceptable limits. Even if you don't swim the rock features are worth it.

Hermann Park is a beautiful urban oasis. There are quality running trails, an obelisk with adjacent reflection pond, a natural area, amphitheatre, zoo, etc... there's something for almost everyone. This urban amenity is certainly something for Houstonians and visitors alike to enjoy. It's a great public space, but I do wish there was more and better night lighting and features.

I recently discovered Cameron Park while visiting Waco. I didn't expect a park this large and developed to be in the area. There are a couple of scenic vistas along with numerous hiking trails. This would be an ideal place to bring your family or have a picnic. If you live nearby or have time to kill I certainly recommend dropping by.

I visited this park for the first time and I was not disappointed. The entry fee is only $5 for day use, the staff was nice, and the grounds clean. The trails were surprisingly nice, but my only complaint is that many of the informational signs were faded and unreadable. I'll definitely be back to visit again in the future.

Every time I visit Chicagoland I make it a point to walk the riverwalk. There are spectacular views of many famous structures and monuments. I highly recommend taking the Chicago River cruises, they are fun and informative. For being in the heart of downtown the grounds are very clean. I know I'll be back for sure soon.

I recently visited this park for the first time and was very happy with the trails. I visit parks in San Antonio to go hiking because Houston is flat as a billiards table. This trail system is definitely worth a visit especially if Government Canyon is closed due to inclement weather. Make a day of it and pack a lunch!

This is a beautiful park, but I give it two stars because I don't feel safe leaving my car alone in the parking lot. There are a lot of automotive break-ins here. I've also heard multiple gun shots while on the trails. Overall, I don't think it's worth risking my vehicle and it's contents. I'll stick to another park.

As a native New Mexican I'm happy I was finally able to visit the state capital building. The round layout reminds me of a kiva but it is unique for sure. When I visited in November of 2018 the trees along the main entrance had vibrant, beautiful fall colors. This would definitely be a nice place for photographs.

I lived within short walking distance from this park for several years and definitely took advantage of it. There's a nice pedestrian bridge along with bike trail access, and several nature trails. If you're in the area it is definitely worth a stop.

Cathedral Park is truly a beautiful place to visit. I especially loved the Statue at the center with all of the detail. There are plenty of benches to sit as well. I wish I could have seen it with snow. Stop by if you find yourself in the area.

Buckingham Fountain is most certainly a bucket-list item in the Chicago area, many would remember it from Married With Children. Unfortunately the fountain was turned off for maintenance when I visited. Hopefully it will be turned on soon.

Agora is definitely an interesting collection of sculptures right in downtown Chicago. It sort of reminds me of dementia or mental illness, I'm not sure why... On a lighter note, If you find yourself in the area it's surely worth a stop.

A few people suggested that I visit Elena Gallegos Open Space for the view of the city lights after dark. There were plenty of trails, facilities, and a nice nighttime view. Next time I'm in Albuquerque I'll visit this park again.

The Sandia Peak Tramway is definitely worth the wait. There are stunning views of the Sandia mountains and vistas of over 10000 square miles of the New Mexico landscape. Be sure to dress warm, the top of the mountain is COLD.

Japhet Creek Park is a nice hidden gem in East End Houston. There is a nice walking trail that winds through a wooded area and along Japhet Creek. If you're in the area this park is definitely worth a stop.
I've  visited Wyler Aerial Tramway a few times  through the  years and have always enjoyed it. If you are in the area, I definitely recommend visiting. You can see for miles in all directions.
Green Acres Park has always been a nice place to visit. The walking trail is a nice addition, as it didn't exist when I lived in Clovis. If you're in the area visit for sure.
Trammel Crow Park is a great place to park and enjoy some nice views of the skyline from atop the Trinity River Levee (if it's not flooded).
This is a nice place to visit when its not packed. I recommend walking a bit further to Sculpture Falls because there were fewer people.

This place had lots of things to do. Even the scenery around the cave was awesome. The mountains in the background while my son climbed the rock climbing walls and the obstacle course made for awesome pics. The guide in the cave was cool and the experience was fun. The food wasn't that great and we waited in line for awhile to get in. That's the only reason I don't give a 5.

The price was high and u have to take a pretty long shuttle ride there. Our shuttle didn't have air conditioning but I can't vouch for all of the shuttles. The falls have a lot of stairs to climb and it could be scary for ppl who are afraid of heights. That said, it was a pretty area but it might not be worth the price for some.

This is the best and biggest outdoor park I know of in the Metro Area. It is pretty clean and there are sitting areas with huge umbrellas for shade. They have two bathrooms and they sell food and water. They have mist coming out of pipes so you can cool off as well. There's usually lots of kids to play with.

Definitely get a CityPass for the cruise. We got awesome pics of downtown and even the pics of seals. The staff were friendly and it was a nice smoothe ride. They don't have a problem with u standing up and taking pics either.

I was surprised at how much there is to see and do. You could easily spend more than 3 hours in this place. It's shaped mostly like a rectangle so it would be hard to get lost. There are things to do for almost all ages.

The museum looks huge on the outside but there wasn't that much to do in the inside for an eight your old. If your children are 4 and under I think the place is ok but still pricey. The best part for me was there food.

This is one of the most unique places to take a pic of the bridge. At the right angle you can take a pic that looks like your holding the bridge up with one hand. Be careful of the sun. There is no shade.

This is a cute little aquarium that has a fun staff and a good location. The juvenile otter was the best. My Son took off his hat and waved it my the water tank and the otter followed the hats movement.
You can get a pic of the painted ladies with a part of the San Francisco Skyline which is awesome. It's to far to walk from the financial district to the painted ladies but it's worth coming anyways.
This place is one of the most unique places I've been to. It has big screen TV attached to a skyscraper, food, and an awesome view of downtown Philadelphia. It's a must see when visiting.
This is one of my favorite parks. I liked the iconic statue and the ping pong table and other games. It's a really good place to take pics and its clean with lots of staff.
It was very interactive and the actors and actresses were really good. It's more than just walking through the ship. I would say more but I don't want to ruin the surprise.
This is the largest tower in Seattle and the price is cheap. You can see the Space Needle on one side and Mount Rainier on the other side on a good day.
I have been to quite a few Chinatowns and the size of this one is pretty good. It didn't smell bad either and was pretty clean from what I could tell.
The facility is pretty small but they have more things then butterflies. U can have a spider crawl on u and they have a peacock shrimp mantis.
This is a good place to relax and enjoy the flowers and the Waterall. Snap a few pics and enjoy the sound of the water while reading a book.
Compared to other towers I'll been in it's not super expensive. It has an excellent view of different places and u can even see Fenway.
This was probably the most beautifulest part of Boston in my Opinion. The musicians that play in the park topped it off for me.
The guide was very nice and knowledgeable and it's a great place to learn about history and it includes Ben Franklin's grave.
The views and the fountain are great for the most part. There were some homeless ppl sleeping on the benches when I went.
I would say that it's a unique experience but definitely not a must see. If you really love to jog and then go for it.
It's a decent place to spend some time looking at the running water and taking a walk but I've been to better places.
This is the oldest alley in the US and it's worth getting some pics and vids there is u have the extra time.
This is a nice park to walk around and relax. It's a pretty huge park in a pretty homey neighborhood.
This isn't the best Aquarium I've been to but it's the only one I've been to that has a tiger.

One of my favorite state parks in the middle of the state to visit. The wide open views are outstanding. Bring a boat or go exploring the potholes to the south. Also numerous fruit farms in the area with fresh produce right off the vine or tree. The campground is very green and full of shade. You can not go wrong here on a hot day. Full hook-ups and plenty of space between the sites. Nice metal picnic tables and fire rings set back from the RV sites. Will keep coming back!

This memorial is so easy to miss, a small sign and gravel road lead to an unexpected find. We expected a small memorial but found a lot more. Definitely stop here and learn about Japanese Bainbridge Island residents who were sent to internment camps during WWII. In the future they plan to build a big visitor center. Nearby are paths to the beach which is part of the neighboring park.

This seems more like a regional park than a state park. Tons of picnic tables, bathrooms, and playgrounds for the kids. The trails are mainly feeder trails to the beach area from the neighborhoods in the area. The best thing about the park is the scenery and kayak access to the lake. I-90 freeway noise is very loud, grounds are very wet and flooded in places during the winter.

An out of this world place to hike amongst 5000-8000 year old trees plus some only decades old. One of my top 10 hikes in my lifetime, do all three hikes at visitor center, you wont be disappointed. Very friendly staff and great gift shop! A must see for you bucket list. Just dont drive anything bigger than a car or truck, road is very windy and steep with drop offs at edge.

Really fun state park. Unfortunately the skywalk access trail was flooded along with a lot of the side trails. Walked to boat tours area from entrance, 3 miles each way. Food and drinks were excellent, especially the beer! Boat ride or tram rides available, $20-25 each. Saw alligator, deer, armadillo, and lots of birds. You can also rent bikes.

One of the best museums in LA. Consist of half a dozen buidlings next to the Le Brea Tar Pits. Easy to spend 5-6 hours here. Parking is on site and less than $20. The Grove is 8 blocks to the north, also worth going to along with the Farmers Market shops and restaurants. Cafeteria has reasonably priced food along with a decent selection.

The holiday lights are one of a kind. Very fun place to go and only $5. Get there before 4:30 if you want to park in the botanical garden lot. The gift shop is very nice and they also sell a variety of coffee along with cookies and other deserts. $5 to park and they only take cash for that.

Great little park with approximately 20 camping spots, 2 with rv hook-ups. Also has 2 boat docks and a restroom with flush toilets and showers. The place was extremely quite and peaceful, I could easily spend a few days here camping and sit around a fire or play horseshoes in the nice pits.

Love the variety of shops and food here, probably around 20-25 total. One of the few markets in San Diego that reminded me of Pike Place in Seattle. I wish downtown San Diego had something bigger that had more flowers, crafts, and fruit and vegetable stalls.
dislikes: Fewer flowers, crafts, and produce stalls

reviews_attraction.text: My second time here, just as windy as the first time! Bring a jacket and walk up the 368 some steps to the viewpoint. Apparently dogs allowed as several spotted so bring Fido! Looking forward to a return trip someday and some serious hiking in the area.

Awesome hike, we did the 4.2 mile loop which followed the lake shore and then entered the forest. Multiple bridges and boardwalks, a huge diversity of scenery which made the hike go extremely quickly. Tons of access points so easy to get a parking spot.

Great place to hike or mountain bike. 29 miles of total trails, 3-4 miles if you do the outer loop. Not very busy during the work week, i saw 3 hikers, 1 biker, and 2 equestrians on my 90 minute visit. Lots of shade so not to warm even on a hot day.

Great park to camp at if you want to bike on the Olympic Discovery Trail or put an ocean kayak into the water. Road noise during the day is definitely noticeable. See YouTube channel "Explore Your World Today" for video of park and campground.

Great path across the narrows on the Tacoma Bridge. Watch out for bikers and strong winds that might blow your hat off. Traffic noise is loud but the views are amazing. Great place to see Mt Ranier in the distance or a fantastic sunset.

Great place for a picnic and a hike. Also has overnight boat morage and 82 camping sites! Washington and Florida might have the best state parks in the country. For video of park see YouTube channel "Explore Your World Today".

Great state park located along the water. The trees in the tent part of the campground are huge, if in an rv try and get one of the spots adjacent to the water. Bring your fishing pole or chair and a book!

Nice little park but not a ton to do. We spent about an hour hiking a loop trail. The campground looked nice, also beach access in 2 places. See video of park on YouTube channel "Explore Your World Today".

Amazing place in Death Valley. It was in the 80s on the valley floor but 30 on the hike we did to a nearby peak with snow covering the ground. A 4 wheel drive is definitely needed to get to this trailhead.
A state park to harvest clams or fish in hood canal, not much else here other than a beach and views! With wind coming off the water to the north it can be chilly. Only restroom is a port a potty.
One of the best National Parks in the NW. Fewer people than Mt Rainier and a ton of options for hiking. Also has multiple visitor centers that do a great job of showing off the park.
One of the best state parks in California.  Many trails of varying length allowing one to see the redwoods. Lots of camping and lodging choices close by.
Great place to see the town of Westport or winter waves crashing onto the rocks! For video go to YouTube channel "Explore Your World Today".
Great unexpected museum in a small town. Stop by if you have an hour and see the exhibits, movie, and gift shop. Cost is $5 per person.
Amazing views of the water and mountains. Plenty of parking and a bike path/lane to downtown Port Angeles. Bathrooms are at the end.
Best place to park if hiking or biking in 360 trails park. Also has a playground and picnic area. Room for trailer parking.

Historical plaque inscription:
First Commercial Oil Well In California, Pico #4.
On this site stands Pico #4, California's first commerically productive well. It was spudded in early 1876, under the direction of Demetrius G. Scofield, later to become first president of Standard Oil Company of California, and was completed at a depth of 300 feet on September 26, 1876, for an initial flow of 30 barrels of oil a day.
Later in the same year, the well was deepened to 600 feet, using what was perhaps the first steam rig employed in oil well drilling in California. Upon this second completion, it produced at a rate of 150 barrels a day, and is still producing after seventy-seven years.
The success of this well prompted formation of the Pacific Coast Oil Company, a predecessor of Standard Oil Company of California, and led to the construction of the state's first refinery nearby. It was not only the discovery well of the Newhall Field, but was, indeed, a powerful stimulus to the subsequent development of the California Petroleum Industry.

Note: After producing oil for 114 years, the well shut down in 1990.
This is California State Historical Landmark No. 516, placed in 1953.
The location is a 1.5-mile walk up a paved path from Mentryville.

History:
Tongva, 10,000 BC.
The first people of Los Angeles used this river as a source for food, materials for daily life, and spiritual renewal.

Spanish, 1769.
The Portola Expedition.

Rancho San Rafael, 1784.
The Verdugo family grew crops and raised cattle along this stretch of river for 80 years.

J Hartley Taylor, 1890s.
An ambitious entrepreneur opened a grocery store on San Fernando Road at Elm Street. He raised chickens, hogs, pigeons, and grew grain on this land. He founded Taylor Milling Corp., producing animal feed and flour for nearly 50 years.

Railroad, 1920s.
Taylor gave up part of his land for a railroad maintenance facility. Taylor Yard employed thousands of local workers until 1985.

Coalition, 2000.
36 community organizations united and fought to reclaim this river land for shared recreation and habitat restoration.

Rio de Los Angeles State Park, 2007.

(The above information is on a park bench located at the back of the park)

Hilltop Gardens sign:
Private estate becomes public treasure.
Newspaperman E. Manchester Boddy (1891-1967) purchased the land that is now Descanso Gardens in 1939. The 165-acre Boddy estate became a public botanical garden when LA County acquired it in 1953. Boddy's passion for camellias, roses and lilacs is still evident throughout the Gardens.

Boddy House: A lasting legacy.
Soon after purchasing this property in 1939, E. Manchester Boddy hired architect James E. Dolena (1888-1978) to design his dream house. The Boddy family lived here until 1953, when LA County acquired the estate.

Our Storied Past: Echoes of World War II.
Our camellias include plants purchased by E. Manchester Boddy from local nurserymen F.M. Uyematsu and F.W. Yoshimura when Japanese Americans were forced into government-run "War Relocation Centers"* during WWII. Hundreds of these camellia plants still thrive at Descanso Gardens today.

Historical plaque inscription:
Arnold Palmer took a 12 on this hole.
On Friday January 6, 1961, the first day of the 35th L.A. Open, Arnold Palmer, voted Golfer of the Year and Professional Athlete of the Year, took a 12 on this hole.
As an inspiration to all golfers, the Los Angeles Junior Chamber of Commerce dedicates this plaque on January 3, 1963.
Rededicated on May 17, 2017.

How Palmer Made His 12:
After hitting a fine drive, he proceeded to hit two shots into the driving range and two more onto Patricia Avenue. He hit his sixth shot to the green and two putted. These eight strokes, plus four penalty strokes, added up to 12.

"Golf is deceptively simple and endlessly complicated; it satisfies the soul and frustrates the intellect. It is at the same time rewarding and maddening - and it is without a doubt the greatest game mankind has ever invented."

Arnold Palmer
1929 - 2016

Listed in the National Register of Historic Places in 2017, the Great Wall of Los Angeles is one of the largest murals in the world. Depicting the history of California, it is 13 feet high and 2,754 feet long, stretching over half a mile. It is located in a section of the Tujunga Flood Control Channel parallel to Coldwater Canyon Blvd, between Oxnard St and Burbank Blvd. It was painted by hundreds of young people and artist supervisors between 1976 and 1984. Muralist Judith Baca, working with the Social and Public Art Resource Center (SPARC), was primarily responsible for the design.
Plans to continue the history of California beyond the 1950s are in the works. The mural will be a mile long when sections for the 1970s through the 1990s are complete.

Historical marker inscription:
The world's first circular office structure was designed to resemble a stack of 45 rpm records.
