Artists recording in its studios since its completion in 1956 have included such luminaries as Frank Sinatra, Nat King Cole, Peggy Lee, Dean Martin, the Beatles, and the Beach Boys. The rooftop beacon flashes "Hollywood" in Morse Code. The architects were Welton Beckett & Associates.

Marker erected by Hollywood Chamber of Commerce.
Note: This marker has a mistake. The building was not designed to resemble a stack of records.
The photo on the marker features a scale model of the building presented by Frank Sinatra.
This is Los Angeles City Historic Monument No. 857.

Historical marker inscription:
El Rancho Simi (1795).
This is the site of the headquarters of the Spanish Rancho San Jose de Nuestra Senora de Altagarcia y Simi. The name derives from "Shimiji," the name of the Chumash village here before the Spanish. At 113,000 acres, Rancho Simi was one of the state's largest land grants. Two prominent Spanish and Mexican family names are connected with the Rancho: Santiago Pico who first received the grant, and Jose de la Guerra who purchased the Rancho in 1842. Two rooms of original adobe remain, part of the Strathearn home built in 1892-93.

California Historical Landmark No. 979.
April 9, 1989.

Built by the Watchorn family... As did their friends the Smiley brothers, Robert and Alma Watchorn contributed greatly to Redlands’ cultural life. A labor organizer, Commissioner of Immigration at Ellis Island, and oilman who experienced the American dream, Robert as a self-made man identified with Abraham Lincoln. He shared that interest with his only child, Emory Ewart. Ewart’s impaired health led to his death at age 25, the result of his service as a pilot in World War I. Devastated by the loss, the Watchorns decided to memorialize their son by erecting a museum in Redlands honoring Lincoln.

This 1,325-foot-high peak is known for its 12-foot white cross at the top. There are numerous trails leading to Mount McCoy, which sits in a 200-acre nature area operated by the Rancho Simi Recreation and Park District, while the cross and its immediate surroundings are owned by the Simi Valley Historical Society.

In 1813, the cross on Mt. McCoy was a landmark for the Friars and others in the Simi Valley.
Another cross was erected by Robert E. Harrington in 1921.
The concrete cross was erected in 1941.
In 1986, Mount McCoy was designated Ventura County Landmark No. 106.

Historical marker inscription: Stoney Point Outcroppings, natural site considered one of the most picturesque areas in Los Angeles.
Los Angeles Historic-Cultural Monument No. 132, declared 1974.

History: Stoney Point was the site of the Tongva Indian village of Momonga. A sulphur spring, believed to possess spiritual properties, runs adjacent to Stoney Point Park on the Eastern side. It is said that Shamans would visit Stoney Point in preparation for the Winter Solstice celebration that drew native people from as far away as Temecula.

This was originally Lawry’s California Center, a showcase of restaurants and shops to promote Lawry’s seasoning products made here. The Lawry’s center, completed in 1953 and expanded in 1961, opened a dining area in 1970. The production facility was a popular place for public tours and school field trips. Lipton purchased the Lawry’s property in 1979 from its founders, the Van de Kamp family. The center, which was never profitable, closed in 1992 and was sold. The production facility was demolished to make way for Home Depot.

The Hollyhock House, as part of the 20th-century architecture of Frank Lloyd Wright, has been inscribed on the World Heritage List.

Inscription on this List confirms that this property deserves protection for the benefit of all humanity because of its outstanding universal value.

This property is one of eight that collectively demonstrate the qualities of what is known as "organic architecture” developed by Wright, which was a singular contribution to global architecture in spatial, formal, material and technological terms.

This area served as the City’s Zoo from its founding 1912 to 1965, when the Los Angeles Zoo moved to its current location about two miles north of here. Many of the walls, grottos, and other enclosures you see today were built in the 1930s by County Relief workers and Works Progress Administration (WPA) crews. Once, bears, lions, monkeys, macaws, goats, elephants, reptiles, and turtles, among others, lived here and sounds of their growls, roars, calls, and clamor filled this canyon.

Many of the walls, grottos, and other enclosures you see today were built in the 1930s by County Relief workers and Works Progress Administration (WPA) crews. Once, bears, lions, monkeys, macaws, goats, elephants, reptiles, and turtles, among others, lived here and sounds of their growls, roars, calls, and clamor filled this canyon.

“Father of the Marina” Burton W. Chace, 1900-1972. This park is dedicated to the memory of Fourth District Supervisor Burton W. Chace whose faith in the future converted these formally mosquito-infested mud flats into the Marina Del Rey small craft harbor. Mr. Chase, whose long and distinguished public career tragically ended in an automobile accident in 1972 a few months before his retirement, served on the Board of Supervisors from 1953 to 1972.

Old Santa Susana Stage Road was an important road linking Los Angeles and Ventura County.
To slow down their descent, drivers would use a wooden timber placed through the rear spokes to lock both wheels. Hikers can still see the deep ruts made by the wagons on the 'Devil's Slide' section.
The road is Los Angeles Historic-Cultural Monument #92, listed on the National Register of Historic Places, and Ventura County Historical Landmark #104.

Old Santa Susana Stage Road was an important road linking Los Angeles and Ventura County. To slow down their descent, drivers would use a wooden timber placed through the rear spokes to lock both wheels. Hikers can still see the deep ruts made by the wagons on the 'Devil's Slide' section.
The road is Los Angeles Historic-Cultural Monument #92, listed on the National Register of Historic Places, and Ventura County Historical Landmark #104.

The most lavish of four Hollywood Blvd theaters designed for live performances, it opened in 1926, featuring stars such as Buster Keaton, Clark Gable, Henry Fonda, Jason Robards and Will Rogers. It was renamed the Paramount Theatre in 1942 and became a movie palace. "Citizen Kane" premiered here. Its original name and appearance were restored in 1990. The exterior is Spanish Colonial style and the interior is East Indian.

San Francisco businessman William T. Coleman built this plant to refine the “cottonball” borax found on the nearby salt flats. The high cost of transportation made it necessary to refine the borax here rather than carry both borax and waste to the railroad, 165 miles (265 km) across the desert.
Workers refined borax by separating the mineral from unwanted mud and salts, a simple but time-consuming process.

Inscription: Originally located some 200 yards to the north, the Stagecoach Inn was built in 1876. Its redwood lumber came by sea and was freighted up the steep Conejo Grade by multi-team wagons. From 1887 to 1901, the hotel served as a regular depot for the Coast Stage Line, which carried both passengers and mail. In 1965 it was moved to its present location.

Open 1-4 Wed-Sun.

The building was completed in June of 1934. It stands 232 feet wide, 180 feet deep, and 130 feet high from the bottom of its circular stairway to the top of its main 80 foot tower.
This building was constructed as nearly as possible from Catalina materials. Aggregate stone, all of which was quarried and crushed in Catalina, was the principal building material.

Opened in 1918, the $800,000 depot was the largest west of the Mississippi,  designed as the Gateway to Southern California. It was a bustling passenger and freight center with a restaurant, living quarters, and offices, and thanks to a $15 million rehabilitation, the Santa Fe Depot has been restored to its former beauty.

Interpretive sign:
This large wiry creosote bush (Larrea tridentata) before you, the only creosote bush in this woodland, is about 10 feet high and 20 feet in diameter; it has been estimated to be nearly 800 years old by botanists. This may be the oldest living organism in Lancaster and the entire Antelope Valley.

The Holocaust Monument has six 18-foot tall triangular black granite columns with inscriptions covering the Holocaust period, 1933-1945. Construction (in 1992) cost $3 million. Located in Pan Pacific Park outside the Holocaust Museum, it can be visited any time.
Garden of the Gods was part of the Iverson Movie Ranch which flourished from 1912 until the late 1960’s. Over 3,000 movies and television shows were filmed here, more than any other filming location.

Great day trip for family or solo. Giant lava tubes from a past St Helen's eruption. Lower flow is .8 mi down and back, fairly easy walk in a wide and tall cave. Nearly anyone, including kids can handle this hike. Upper flow is a bit more challenging and requires scrabbling over some boulders. Either way, be sure to bring multiple flashlights and good sturdy shoes, as well as layers of clothing. The cave is quite chilly and water(cold) drips from the ceiling. Ape Cave is on the south side of the mountain, so the typical crater us not visible. Quite a drive from the north side (typical tourist views) to the south side where the cave is. Well worth the trip if you are in the area.

Tallest waterfall in Oregon. Very popular tourist spot. If eastbound on interstate they close a gate when lot is full. You can go down to next exit and come from the east heading west may have better luck. Still may have to circle like a vulture for a parking spot. Fill up definitely on the weekends. Old historic highway still closed near the falls as of November of 2018 due to fire. So is the trail up to the top of falls. Bridge is now open for viewing the falls. Worth the trip and wait if u are in the area.

Have to admit I was sceptical, but we really enjoyed this place. There are several educational exhibits and hands on learning. A lot of it is occupational based and let's kids learn about careers while pretending. I was concerned that my 11 and 12 year olds would be too old to enjoy it...but they had a blast! Probably helped there was no one else there so they could let out their inner child. Price is very reasonable as well.

Very nice park with with access to bay area. Lots of drift wood on rocky beach. Very nice park with playground and picnic tables. On a clear day can see Olympic Mountains and Mt Rainier. $10 is a little pricey for a visit to a park, but they may have yearly passes that would make it more affordable. And beware they do have rangers that patrol the area. It is a county park and also has a primative boat ramp and fishing pier.

Nice hike to get the blood pumping. Moderate to easy. Could be done with older kids if they are adventurous. Nice views at the top but not much to look at on the way up. There are lots of trails in the area si it was a little difficult to find the correct one. Recommend using a trail map or GPS, or ask the other friendly hikers, it can be a very busy trail. Parking is along the road at the trailhead.

This was better than expected. Just an impromptu trip and found out there is a free museum. Exhibits on the 2002 Salt Lake Winter games. Definitely worth a visit with interactive exhibits as well that the kids liked. And the price is right...free! There are guided tours and other paid services that we did not take part but looked reasonably priced.

Very good WWII sub near pier 39 in San Francisco. Good audio tour taking you through the whole submarine ship. $20 for adults and $15 for youth. They give a pretty significant discount for military. Lots of good history. Kids really enjoyed it(age 11 and 12) as did I (age...older than 12) Worth the money in my opinion.

Nice photogenic spot in San Francisco. Adjacent to a nice park which is worth a visit. Free to visit and take pics, but not unlike a lot of other streets in San Francisco. Does have a nice view of downtown over the rooftops. Best views probably in afternoon when sunlight highlights the paint jobs.

Nice ski Museum located at Utah Olympic Park. Not much there, but the price is right...free. there is a cost if you want a guided tour or any of the other adventure packages they have(bobsledding) . Also a 2002 Winter Olympic Museum. Definitely worth a visit for adults or kids.
dislikes: Activities: Additional costs for guided tours and adventures

reviews_attraction.text: Beautiful forest. One lane roads throughout. A little lacking on the signage, so a little difficult to locate where you are. Definitely secluded. Check out maps ahead of time. Most trails tend to be for ATVs but hiking also an option. Large forest with lots to see.

Very comprehensive museum with many aircrafts. Great exhibits on WWI and WWII. Great place for kids and adults. Be prepared to spend a few hours here and even then may not see it all. Best for multiple exhibits. TIP: First Thursday of the month is free from 5-9pm.

Beautiful park. Great views of Mt Rainier and thick beautiful forests. Lots of trails and other ways to visit this park. Visitor centers and parking lots can get full, so go early in the day or late in the day if during the peak summer season.

Great little museum in Fortuna CA. Lots of local history. Definitely worth a trip. Staff is very friendly  and knowledgeable. 11 and 12 year old enjoyed it as well. And the price is right. Donations appreciated.

Multiple visitor centers with great exhibits and information. Large parks with lots of trails and beaches. Wildlife viewing (mostly elk) and of course really big trees. A must see if you are in the area.

Very nice nature area in Seattle. Lots of trails and walking paths. Restrooms available and parking. Pets allowed on leash. Did not see a playground area...more of open grassy areas and wooded trails.
Great place for kids and adults. Very nice play area, lots of room to walk, plenty of shade. Fishing as well. Great place to spend the day. Pavilions also available to rent for parties big and small.
Open with restrictions. Must buy tickets in advance and schedule a time. Had a good visit here. Lots more than just fish. A little pricey, but save $5 if you go on a monday after 4pm.
Very popular tourist attraction, so be prepared for crowds on weekends and holidays. Short trail to bottom of falls is very well groomed. Very beautiful falls and nice hike.
Nice quiet small lake for fishing. Primitive camping available as well. Facilities are scarce. Pit toilets only. Small boat ramp and dock on North side of lake.
Iconic Seattle skyline views! Tourist spot right in the middle of a residential neighborhood. On a clear day you can see Mt Rainier behind the city skyline.
Nice moderate hike to the falls. Very beautiful and picturesque. Lots of photo ops along the way. Popular hike so come early during weekend or peak season.
Great beach. Lots of military aircraft overhead. Traffic can be rough so plan accordingly. Parking is free along road but fills fast on warm days.
Nice little zoo in Eureka California. Giant Redwoods make a great backdrop.  Not a lot of animals but the price is reasonable. Good for kids.
Beautiful views of Mt St Helens. Great displays about the mountain and a gift shop as well. Need park pass or annual NP pass to visit.
Beautiful overlook and beach and bay access. Road to end of jetty is a little rough but doable even in a car.

An awesome and memorable train-riding and mine-touring experience with the folks at the Georgetown Loop Railroad company. The train ride is enjoyably comfortable (on a sunny day!) even in the open air coach carriages and the train moves at a good steady pace to allow you to enjoy the views near and far. It was very neat to see the coal powered steam engine in operation with the sight and smell of smoke, along with the sound of the whistle from the steam being release. Our Extended Lebanon Mine Tour was led by the fun yet charasmatic Sophie. She was funny and comedic, yet did not sacrifice her delivery of the historical information. Very fun and could not recommend this destination any more!!!

While the roadway to Mount Evans was closed off, I still had a memorable experience up at Summit Lake Park. The park includes multiple hiking trails (one of which to Mount Evans) leading to different terrains and scenic views. Take caution that the terrain here is mountainous and rocky, but the views are always rewarding whichever direction you take. I came late afternoon and was rewarded with the changing colors in the landscape caused by the setting sun. Happy exploring!

Lamar Valley is a fascinating landscape quite different from the rest of the park. Drive through the many fields and witness the majesty of the mountain ranges in the far distance. This is also the prime location for animal watching during dusk and dawn. Our visit occurred during midday, and while we only encountered multiple herds of bison near and far, it was still well worth the visit and drive.

While known as a venue for exhibiting drawings, The Drawing Center serves secondarily as a space for greater learning and education. The interior itself is warm and welcoming, and at the time of my visit, was hosting a workshop while featuring an exhibit that communicates current social issues and community outreach. Check out the website for program schedule, and come in for momentary respite!

After living in the city for more than a decade, I finally made a day visit to the Bronx Zoo. What a delightful visit featuring many animals and creatures from around the world to learn about. Fortunately most walking paths are under the shade making for an enjoyable walk on a hot summer day. Be sure to arrive early in the day if you plan to cover all areas as the grounds are expansive.

In comparison to the Lower Terraces, the Upper deck is a much quieter area that is approached and explored in a vehicle. There are no sidewalks for pedestrian navigation. The springs are more scattered and activity is relatively dormant. I would go so far as to skip portion if one has already explored the Lower Terraces which offers a more intimate and varied experience.

Magnificent permanent exhibit featuring the glassworks of Chulihuly. All of the art pieces have been thoughtfully put together, and their individual placement from dark interior spaces to the open air gardens is well curated. This is a visitor destination not to missed, and definitely purchase your ticket with the Space Needle admission for discounted rate.

Truly breathtaking experience with its changing landforms depending on your elevation and area in the park! While known for its abundance of the eponymous tree, the park is situated at the intersection between the Mojave Desert and Colorado Desert, thus offering one will be able to see magnificent rock formation and wild habitat.

Fairly small (due to the current building closure from the architectural expansion) yet engaging art museum featuring rotating exhibits both traditional and contemporary. The architecture, both inside and outside, makes for an interesting engagement with the various lobby and gallery spaces. Perfect place to spend an afternoon.

And easy and enjoyable trail that takes you along the Colter Bay water body. The trail includes a peninsula like island and offers unobstructed views of the Grand Teton mountain ranges in the distance. The short trail also crosses through different terrains including woodland and stone shores.

Cool rock formation located just off the side of the roadway. Make a stop, and explore this around all sides -- there's something interesting to see at every angle. Views of the valley, and mountain ranges are also beautiful! Well worth the trip out in the Lamar Valley.

Lovely spot in the valley area of the park for an easy stroll along the bank of Snake River with scenic views of the mountain ranges on the back. The stroll itself is marked by a well defined trail path. Tranquil, peaceful, and very enjoyable; only wished it was longer.

One is greeted with eye popping views of the rugged mountain ranges set behind the calm and pristine Jenny Lake water body. Soak it all in before embarking on your hike around the lake and up the hills. Absolutely glorious and surreal to the eye and senses!

Awesome lookout situated inside the Alderfer / Three Sisters Park. Not hard to get to as long as you have the park map with you on hand to follow as there are multiple trails inside the park. The views are rewarding and is a perfect spot for a picnic!

Manhattan Bridge crossing gives you an awesome view of Lower Manhattan and the neighboring Brooklyn Bridge! No worries of overcrowding with the tourists and cyclists mowing you over. It is the underdog of pedestrian bridge crossings in the Big Apple!

Take the scenic drive up to Signal Mountain summit and take in south facing views of the park. Breathtaking valley landscape and Snake River on the east side juxtaposed with the rugged mountain ranges on the west side. Well worth up the drive up.

The place for respite in the Flatiron District, away from the hustle and bustle of the city! Plenty of trees, lawn, plenty of benches, dog park, a water fountain — and oh, and there's the original Shake Shack on the south end. Perfect!

An easy and pleasant afternoon hike and stroll in the valley to the waterfall. Careful what time of year you come to this waterfall; I came at a time when the fall was dry... Oh well, another time I suppose!
Swung by this overlook on my way down from an afternoon hike at Runyon Canyon Park. The timing couldn't have been more perfect, overlooking at Hollywood Bowl, the 101 and Downtown LA in the distance!
Perfect place to pass and stop by during my night time run. This side of the waterfront is less crowded compared to the adjacent Jane's Carousel and Brooklyn Bridge Park further down.
Elevated park with gorgeous open views of the city as well as the mountains in the far far distance. Best to come here during dusk or at night when the light is in transition. Enjoy!
Small overlook with scenic view of Tower Fall. Note that the overlook only allows for partial view of the waterfall and there is no access for full view at the base of the hill.
A good museum to spend an afternoon at, showcasing a private collection of classical and modern art pieces -- a bit of everything for everyone's taste! Go see for yourself!
Awesome views of the river flowing along the rugged valley floor. You can make out the Lower Falls in the far far distant. Wow!
Beautiful falls cascading down the valley! Follow the trail from the parking lot to the view point for straight on view.

The first time I came to LA, I wanted to visit, but I forgot to make reservations for tickets ahead of time.  They do offer a wait outside type of system, but the line can get very long and by the time you make your reservation for the infinity room it might be hours before it is your turn.
So when I was coming back to LA, I made sure to reserve my ticekts for the very first session.  If you reserve online you cut the long winding line and get to go straight in.  Once inside, the first thing you should do is go to your left and reserve a slot for the infinity room.  At opening it was about 45 minutes for our slot to be called.  In that time, we were able to explore the whole third floor.  There are a lot of famous pieces up here including Jeff Koon's tulips and balloon dog.  Along with Andy Warhol's campbell's soup can, Cy Twombly's the rose, Robert Therrien, Under the table, and Yayoi Kusama's longing for eternity.

This top flood should keep you busy for awhile, but we had to leave because our time slot was being called for Kusama's The Souls of Millions of Light Years away.  It was a very fun infinity room.

Overall, there is so many iconic pieces and the best part it is completely FREE.  Well you do have to pay for parking, which you can save by getting a validation pass from the gift shop area.  The building itself is really cool to look at also.

I've been to a few different presidential libraries, and this one has a special place in my heart.  LBJ's library sits on my alma mater's campus.  Sadly, for all the years that I attended school and even the years directly following it, I never knew about the library nor had an interest to visit.  However, after visiting Bush's library at SMU was inclined to visit LBJ's.  First off, there is FREE PARKING! This is unheard of at UT, but they have their own private lot right next to the school/museum.

Once inside, if you have a student ID it is only $3 per person.  You can start the tour off by viewing a short video.  Afterwards you can follow through the floors so see his accomplishments along with his wife's.

The building itself is beautiful, I was a little bit sad not to be able to sit in the replica oval office.  But it was unique to see the aged technology vs the more recent Bush's office.
dislikes: Facilities & Services (Restricted Access to Replica Oval Office)

reviews_attraction.text:
This was our first stop in New Mexico.  I had recently visited the caverns in San Antonio, and was told that these put those to shame.  It truly is something that you must see in person as pictures just do not do justice.  It is a HUGE! After you pay you can either walk the natural entrance or take the elevator down.  We opted for the elevator as we were pressed for time.

The caverns themselves are remarkable, it was a bit cool, mid 50s, so remember to bring a light jacket.

They have very well thought out paths that will bring you from the start to the finish.  The lighting is designed well to highlight certain big or unique formations.

We were able to walk through the whole cavern in about an hr at a leisurely pace.

This was my 4th visited presidential library.  Ever since I started this quest I’ve found each one well done.  For the presidents that was before my time you only know a little bit from the history books and if you’ve tried you can read more about it.

However, this library does an amazing job to focus on the other aspects of Nixon’s life and political career outside of just watergate.

I also really enjoyed this library because they have the actual helicopter that is shown in his iconic departure picture.  You even get to board it and take pictures.

This location allows you to sit at the presidential desk and take pictures too!

I gave my wife a mini history lesson.  So we started out at LBJ library and followed it up by showing her Lady Bird's center.  I would recommend visiting in spring or summer vs the winter.  It was a bit sad looking at all of the dead flowers.  However, the space is great and the history behind Lady Bird was amazing.

It's a great place to take the kids, as the family garden has so many activities to keep them busy.

The observation tower does provide some spectacular views.  The admission price is a bit high, but definitely worth it to support green spaces.

I doubt I will ever make it to Africa anytime soon so this was a nice and safe alternative.  I do feel bad for the animals being in captivity but it does look like they are being treated nicely.  The area is spacious, so it does give the feel of a safari vs just a zoo.  Also, the animals are some what free to wander so while we there a few giraffes got really close and we had to stop for them.  The driver does give a very informative tour, and it does feel more like a guided tour than a "ride".

This is one of my top attractions for Yellowstone.  Why? because it's different.  All of the colorful geysers, get a bit redundant inside of the park.  You do stop getting amazed after the 5th or 6th one.  Not to mention my wife and I saw some other variations in New Zealand, but we had never see anything like Mammoth Hot Springs!!! This thing is massive.  You can see it from far away as you're driving towards it any direction.  You can park at many different areas including from the above.

This is literally what the name says.  It is a rest stop halfway on the road to Hana.  We didn't think we needed to stop, but after the trip we were so grateful that we did.  It's a good place to get some rest and pick up some banana bread.  The banana bread was delicious, but there are not many other food options on the drive.  We did not pack snacks, drinks, etc.  That banana bread was all the nourishment we had for the whole 2nd half of the day!

This by far was my favorite ride on my whole trip to Disney World.  It is a 4D ride, but it is very thrilling, they also have water mists they hit you and flower scents being sprayed on you.  They did an amazing job on the execution of this ride.  Also, the wait here is LONG, we waited about 2 hrs coming a little after opening.  However, there is a lot of stuff to see along the wait.  It actually went by fast, if that is a thing.

While at Animal Kingdom, you MUST see the Lion King show.  It's a show that goes on throughout the day and you know it's good when they offer fast pass as an option and people pick it over a ride.

The production value is high.  Think a mini cirque du soleil show, except with better music (lion king classics).  The costumes, dancing, and acrobatics are what'd you expect.  The seating is all around so not a bad seat in the house.

I can't believe I missed out on this landmark all the previous times I went to San Antonio.  On this particular weekend, I made it a goal to visit this spot.  We were super lucky because it happened that Fiesta Fiesta was hosting a night market right at the base of the Cathedral.  In addition to it being a beautiful place, we got the bonus of celebrating with thousands of people.

This is probably one of the most iconic photos floating around instagram these days.  It's a cool permanent installed in front of the LACMA.  It basically is a bunch of light posts.  The best part about it? It's completely FREE.  You do not have to pay admission into the museum, you can just come and visit this exhibit.  It is located in front of the museum and easily accessible.

When we got our magic bands, it allows us to pick certain rides for "fast pass", I really wanted to get Flight of Passage, but it was completely booked, so I was excited to see the other Avatar ride was available.  The Journey ride is similar to the animatronics that they have in Magic Kingdom, it's OK, but I was expecting more to utilize one of the Fast Passes.

The hike down is a bit rough, but totally worth it.  So the water slams against the rocks, and because there's a hole, the water flows up and out like a whale's blowhole.  Don't get too close as it's not safe.  But the views from the edges are amazing.

A must when you disembark from the Jamestown Ferry..the begins of English dominance in the New World and eventually the beginning of democracy...but only for white male gentry. 1607 they landed with little thought for their safety or the future. They were a lazy bunch of wealthy men who chose the most unhealthy location on the James River and where fresh water was not available. They starved, turned to cannibalism, regenerated with further shipments from England and after 90 years of plowing and fuming and dying removed the capitol to higher ground.

This is a visual piece of art from the grounds of the museum to the facade to the interior to the art. It sits at ground zero for downtown St Pete nestled between the water and the multiple restaurants and high rise condos. Escape from civilization and enter a world of first class art forms from the old masters to free wheeling folks determined to express themselves visually. Take time to muse over the reason people created what they did. Don't rush through the museum or you'll miss the tranquility and peace it offers.

It's a must see. Oldest standing plantation building in Florida. Largest number of extant partial slave cabins. Made of tabby as excellent material for cool in summer and warm in winter. Shells removed from Timucuan Indian mounds crushed and molded into blocks. Over 200 years old. The best thing about this site is that the enslaved are finally being lauded for their contributions to the economy and the cruelty is visually documented. A wonderful historic site. Maib house dates from 1798 built by John McQueen.

It was the worst of times; it was the best of times. Slavery. Cruelty. Wealth. Power. And the writing of the Constitution and Bill of Rights. Madison's will explicitly stated for his wife Dolley to free the slaves. Coward that he was Dolley was worse. She sold them. History is generous to her but you learn if her dark side, no pun intended, by how she treated people of color. Montpelier is dedicated to unearthing the history of the enslaved and for this I applaud their setting the facts upright and correct.

If you admire Andy Warhol then this 7 story museum is a must see. Start on the 7th floor and walk your way around his early life exhibits then move down each level to view his move to adulthood. Yes he had talent for sure. But being the great Warhol seems to me to have been promoted by his vulgar and outrageous behavior. His predilection for the bizarre and outlandish and his wealthy and wild friends promoted an unhealthy and very public lifestyle which in turn captured a curious public.

This is one of the most undisturbed and peaceful places along Florida's east coast. I'm 74 and a native. I  know.... But wait! When it's time for Cape Canaveral to do its thing...blast away...the place is jammed with sightseers. The location is perfect to watch a launch. The vehicular assembly building is within site and many launch pads are visible. But the history of the pioneers brings an appreciation to their endeavors when one visits the old homestead and rocks on the front porch.

Come here every few years and stay in the original overseers cottage. What makes me really proud is this is the only plantation that deeply recognizes the contributions of the enslaved. On their backs the Roman Family lived a luxurious life. The names of the enslaved are printed in one of the reconstructed slave cabins. They are FINALLY HONORED and treated as God's children too. BRAVO OAK ALLEY!!! We're it not for those people this magnificent building would never have been built.

It is a tranquil place where once the Seminole tribe roamed. Of course we know what Andrew Jackson did to the Seminoles. There are over 20000 acres if wildland and water bogs. Remnants if Spanish horses and bison roam the area though rarely sighted. It had observatin decks and hiking trails. Located a few miles of Gainesville it is the perfect place to gain peace and equilibrium especially if you have a loved one at Shands Hospital. And here you can truly communicate with God.

Great site to get a feel for the last battle of the American Revolution. 1803. See General Washington's tent and camp desk. Walk the redoubts especially #10 so invaluable in beating Cornwallis. Drive the various dirt roads as they meander through woods and fields. The museum a must see at the national park. Interactive exhibits grab the attention of both child and adult. The film is fact based and thrilling. The gift shop worth a purchase.

I've always loved this place and taken my grandkids there over the years. But two days ago this organization held a camp for around 25 kids and 5 counselors. They had a picnic at the Lighthouse Park then boarded a boat to  tour the river. NO ONE HAD A MASK. NO ONE WAS WEARING A MASK. This organization has endangered the lives of all those children. SHAME ON YOU. I didn't have my camera as I was going on a jet ski. But this happened.

Peaceful setting on the black river. Stephen Foster never visited Florida but sent his brother south to find a river to use its name for a song he was writing: Way down upon the ??? river. His brother returned with several choices and Suwannee won. The park has cozy cabins with fireplaces. Hiking and canoeing and an abandoned bridge I traveled across via car when I was a child. I LOVE THIS PLACE.

Interesting displays of plants and of course the delightful well cared for animals. The hospital is impressive. 25,000 sf!! Yummy food stop, a great gift shop, and multiple places to sit in  the shade.

Pray for those who shed their blood that future generations might be free. Thank those who protected this historic structure for future generations.

Beautiful plaza named where Indian killer Andrew Jackson was sworn in as territorial governor. If any statue should be removed his bust should be busted. He hated the Indians and originated the Cherokee Indians Trail of Tears. He tried to kill the Florida Seminoles. He is a disgrace to hunanity.

Great if only the evil trump rump had been tossed from this impressive presentation. Chills run down my spine and pride fills my heart when the music and story rolls across the screen. But despite a liar in the white house America will persevere.

Amazing vistas and untouched land surround this one-of-a-kind ocean blowhole that is carved into the rocks. What you need to know: the drive may look like it is not that far from close-by hotels, but it is a windy up and down road with hairpin turns and only a few turnouts. Be respectful of the locals that live there, they will leave you alone if you leave them alone.

There is a parking area at the top with plenty of spaces, and an easy walk out to a bluff where you can see the spray from above. If you are going to hike down, you need to know a couple of things. One: no ambulance is going to get to you anytime soon, so don't be stupid. STAY AWAY FROM THE EDGE OF THE ROCKS AND THE HOLE ITSELF. Right after we walked away a sneaker wave annihilated the entire area and someone was almost swept away. Two, it looks closer than it is. Plan for some time getting down and back up. Three: bring water!

The best advice is bring sturdy shoes and make your own path up and back- traversing is the safest and will not tire you out. If you aren't going to hike, bring binoculars! Lastly, plan on arriving around 2 or 3pm for two reasons; one, there will be wind that will both create waves AND keep you cool, and the morning rush will be over. Stop by a beach on the way back home.

Worth the drive, and it's free!

With so many options, I won't be coming back here. Had a group of 5 which was WAY too big for the small tasting room. We went out back to a nice barn area for service - suggested by the staff. We had to go back in twice after waiting 20 minutes to get our first sample. Meanwhile, many other groups were getting great service. Eventually a staff member came out and was inappropriately talking about his life experience (doing too many drugs, getting drunk at his last winery) and was obnoxious. The wine was young and unrefined with many tasting very thin. We ended up buying a bottle because it actually saved us money. It is still on the shelf.

A nice stop off the highway for some learning, a few trinkets, and some spectacular views. The staff is knowledgeable and you will learn a lot from the various posters and videos showing. The views are what makes this place a good stop - windows allow you to be inside from weather while enjoying some spectacular coastline. The shopping is nothing to write home about but kids will like some of the trinkets. A good stop for all ages.

Insider tip: take the Otter Loop road from 101 south and this will be the final destination after a few pull outs for scenery.

Beautiful, safe, and healthy hike. Park in the police department's lot; how many hikes do you get that level of security? Then walk downhill through a shallow valley filled with fir, maple, yew, and other NW native trees with s cool ocean breeze coming at you from the water. When you reach the bottom there are some interesting plaques about what used to be here then enjoy the Puget Sound with quiet views. The hike back up will get your blood pumping, but won't make you sweat through your clothes. Male sure to visit the facilities before you head out!

Not the most clean facilities, or the best beach, but by far the BEST ACCESSIBLE SNORKELING for travelers. Don't bring a bunch of stuff, just your gear, and walk right into the water. There is a reef/breakwater that creates a calm bay. Bring your kids, grandparents, etc out to see it in real life. Be careful of Vana (urchin). They are all over the reef, and a misplaced foot could ruin your vacation.
Also - for the caring people out there - choose a mineral based sunscreen.  Oxybenzone, a common ingredient, is killing coral. Thank you!

Great river beach access with parking, covered picnic area, and public restrooms. This is the perfect place to take a stroll and check out some seals that rest on the opposite shore. Generally protected by the wind, it attracts a large crowd in the evening for beach fires because you can stay close to the car. Why 4 stars and not 5? It is too crowded and it is actually a longer walk to the actual ocean. There are miles and miles of beaches to explore. This one is worth a visit but not ideal for a beach day.

One of the better beaches on the coast. Small town, and a bit of a drive to get here means less people and more focus on the beautiful surroundings. There is a really interesting tunnel blasted through the rock you can walk through to get to the other side with a completely separate beach! Great beach walks, facilities available in parking lot (though very dirty when I visited) and dramatic scenery with rocks out in the water. I would choose here over cannon beach every time if coming from Portland.

This is a quieter beach to go to if you are looking to get away from crowds. The bathrooms are often dirty and the walk down to the beach can be treacherous. The fence line facing the ocean is overhanging a the beach cliff with posts in mid-air, so beware of kids running around or getting too close for a look at the waves. There is also a shore-break here, so do not swim!

A great hidden gem. It can be difficult to find an entrance from the road, especially those who are trying to find a sports game being held at the field. Your best bet is to park and walk in, or turn East off of Dosh onto 33rd avenue then take a right onto boundary. The most popular sports field for games is in the NW corner, but only accessible by walking in.

Super Cool, even for adults! We went for the LEGO exhibit and ended up spending as much (if not more) time in the other exhibits. There is definitely something for everyone here, and I would recommend going at least once if you are in the area. A super fun "touristy" thing to do with out-of-towners, or to take the opportunity to be a tourist in your own town!

Beautiful park with large green space, old structures from gravel companies of the past, and a gorgeous bridge connecting a beach to the park. Come around sunset to enjoy spectacular views on a nice day and bring a picnic to have as you sit on drift wood down at the beach. Park up top for a healthy walk down and back up!

An amazing park in the making! Great play area with water pumps, sand, a rope climber, and swings. There are four bathrooms to use, and wide open spaces being prepared for more fun. There is an awesome sculpture exhibit right now made with natural materials. A must see park on the west side of town.

A surprisingly good museum for where it is located. Willamette is able to draw major installments and they often staff with knowledgeable, friendly staff. Great place hidden away with other major attractions but a positive experience waiting to be had.

Beautiful vistas and a nice looking lighthouse. Lots to see around here, and lots of hiking trails to take. Bring a light rain jacket at all times around here, it can rain quickly and a cold wind off the water can cool you down quickly in the shade.

For those of you visiting from off Island, pull of here on your way to or from the ferry boat for a great view of the inlet. Also a good stop off on a bike after climbing the big hill, or good to strap everything down before you go flying down!

Worth taking the walk down to this site. You will find a deck built into the hillside nestled into a grove of redwoods, even one growing through the decking for an up close view. It isn't too far from the top and totally possible for all ages.

Really cool experience that is not to be missed if you are in the area. Bring a flashlight and a warm layer or two if you are planning ahead and you can literally walk into the earth until light becomes scarce.

One of the best walks in town for spectacular vistas and a good workout. Park up top for better exercise or down below for the option. You can see a lot of the course and the Puget Sound all at the same time.
Great interpretive center, beautiful walks, and interesting things to see around every corner. Cost is $7 per car unless you have a forest pass or walk in, but worth it for sure.

An amazing view that will remind you of the classic movie shots you see of a tropical paradise in the middle of the ocean.

Have been meaning to visit this place for months and finally got a chance to stop by. I originally decided I would peruse their website to educate myself because I could not make it during their open hours, but I'm glad I did stop in. Reception was very friendly and welcoming. The museum itself coders a lot of historical facts that I never knew that helped me understand the present much better. There is also a library with a suggested reading list available. I really got a lot out of my visit and would happily recommend it for anyone interested in cryptology or language and mathematics and how they are used together to create a new meaning.

I was very excited to see this gallery for the first time. The long lines, no photos and the miscommunication about the pricing cost this gallery one star on my review. I really enjoyed the movie and the story of the factory. I learned a lot of new info I would not have been exposed to otherwise. As far as the size of the exhibit, I wasn't disappointed but I did have different expectations on pricing as mentioned previously.
dislikes: Facilities & Services (long lines, no photos, pricing miscommunication)

reviews_attraction.text: Well worth a drive. I saw their ads in Ft Lauderdale but they're actually a few hours from the city. I really enjoyed how interactive the museum is. Was also cool to see the living village, refreshing after mostly spotting ghost towns while traveling. The area itself is just very clean, from the convenience store to the gas stations. Highly recommend, especially for those who are visual learners.

Don't rely on Google maps to get there. It was showingme a round about way saying the road was closed but I was closer to the Three Rivers route and everything was actually open and clear. Yes, they make you carry chains but no one had to use them (January 13 2019). The park rangers that are still working despite not getting paid are my heroes!

Absolutely loved this place. Best time of day to view is early morning, right around 🌅. For someone who spends most of their time in the city, this was especially breathtaking. Everything from the trail layout to the safety of this place have definitely been well thought through and are maintained with care. ❤

This is by far one of the best parks I've ever been to. I love the display where they show all of the Northern Florida wildlife. Place is well maintained and looks gorgeous. You can't find anything like this next to any other library anywhere in the world.

I thoroughly enjoyed my visit to this museum. I went on the Smithsonian Museum Day but was still able to see all the exhibits without it being overly crowded. The gift shop is lovely. Everyone that I sent the gifts to from here was happy with them.

Interesting place to visit. They have really cool books in the gift shop - Buccaneers of America should be a school required read over Canterbury Tales or Moby Dick. Hated reading those. Pirates are much more intriguing.

I was surprised at the quality and the volume of this collection. Did not expect anything extraordinary but this was a great place to visit. The sketching pop up every last Friday of the month is a very nice touch.

Nice area although you have to keep an eye out for odd characters. I had someone at Piedmont Overlook tell me (not ask, actually tell me) he was planning to sit out the rain in my car because he was on a bike.

Great museum. Visited it on behalf of my sociology class. I really enjoyed the exhibit that focused on the architecture of the city as well as the interior design. It's not overly crowded which is nice!
I would like to return after doing the walkthrough. The property is very well maintained. The scuba diving prices are very reasonable. Can't speak for the quality yet. It is very crowded, however.
Fun park with a cool spring and an awesome trail but a bit overpriced if you're just there to walk through. Plenty of parks in Florida that don't charge just to park there.
Very friendly, always give you a few extra minutes to actually pick a pike if you're renting one. Many birds to see in the morning and croc babies are out in December.
Fantastic views, friendly people and helpful volunteers to guide you through the area. I believe parking was +/- $5 (worth it). It's a really great photo op place.
Beautiful park with breathtaking views. However, in the 10 minutes I've spent there, a lurker showed up and a loudly gossiping couple so it did not feel safe.
The Lights are one of my favorite things to see during the holiday season. I love the originality of this event. $15/per car and $3/3 pairs of 3D glasses
Pretty and good for a walk. The volunteers are a bit pushy about donations. Too much pressure for something that's supposed to be genuine.
Only in passing & now it won't drop off my Google Maps no matter how many times I click on "dismiss". Beautiful architecture nonetheless.
Never knew Oregon had dunes. This was a nice quick stop even without going on a trail - worth pulling over and checking out the view.
This is one of the most unique and wonderful places. It's breathtaking. You can easily spend an hour there watching the water spout.
Our tour was led by Robert Kuskin. This was a very worthwhile, interesting walk through the historic town. We learned so much!
The snorkeling beach is better than the regular beach. It also has a cute butterfly garden. One of the best places to relax.
Wonderful drive through park where you can see deer. It also has a few short trails to look at birds and alligators.
Worth checking out! This is a massive tree. There is also a train on display right next to it. Very impressed.

I was not impressed at all with this park as so many others have been. To be honest this is the first bad park experience I've ever had. To start the staff was rude and seemed a bit hostel/uptight. This was my first visit here and because its on a good size lake I thought that the fishing might be good so I brought my  14' aluminum fishing boat to give it a shot. Let it be known I've been to a large number of parks in Michigan so I'm no stranger to State parks or local parks and the general rules. As soon as you enter the park you have the option to go right toward the boat launch area or veer to the left to continue on to the park. As I always do with my first time visits I wanted to go get a lay of the land first so I tried to go left to see the rest of the park. There was a park ranger on golf cart that just about had a heart attack and started getting very upset at my choice of direction. After I explained to him this was no way for him to talk to me(with my wife and son present)he calmed down and explained because I had a boat I could not continue into the park. What???... Please note there were no signs or at least none I had notice(and I looked) that stated this info. My only option if I wanted to see and enjoy the rest of the park was to leave my boat unattended in the boat launch parking lot. Until now I've never been to any park that puts such limitations on its boating guests. If I had a huge boat then I would easily understand but my boat is very small and has never been an issue even at the smallest of parks and to be yelled at like I'm stupid was completely uncalled for. Once I got on the lake it was way to crowded to comfortably fish and when I was heading back in, I was again yelled at by the Park Ranger for making a "wake" that I wasn't making. For god sacks a pontoon boat was passing me port side going faster then I was but they just wanted to make their presence known and I was the closest one to send this message that they were there doing their job. I honestly do not think I will ever go back based on my bad experience but I don't think this should prevent anyone else from doing so unless they plan to do as I did and spend sometime on the water and in the park without being forced to leave there boat unattended and vulnerable. I think the Park should either reevaluate this decision or at the minimum put up some clearly marked signs before entering the park, at the boat launch intersection as well as on the website to avoid unnecessary future problems with patrons.

I think the best and fairest way to review this place would be to say your experience will most likely be hit or miss and come down to just dumb luck. There is a single large viewing platform where you can potentially get some wildlife sightings but from my experiences to date hasn’t really panned out well for me at least for taking photos. The frustrating part is that there is definitely plenty of different bird species and waterfowl here, but unfortunately aside from the one platform, your only other real option is driving slowly down the gavel road and crossing your fingers you see something. The problem lies in the vegetation being so thick, and with most of the clearings where the waterfowl take refuge in are deep within this vegetation and out of sight. Even though I haven’t done this myself yet, a kayak would definitely come in handy here. Considering the size of the refuge and it’s limitations in sight, It would be nice to see additional viewing platforms put up in multiple locations.
My other complaint about this place is, for it being a wildlife refuge which I’ve always been under the impression was to offer a place to protect the wildlife, it sure seems the DNR is only really concerned in the interest of hunters. I came here during the fall migration when the chances for sightings are at there best but was chased down by a yelling off-duty DNR officer who was hunting and who was less then friendly and threatened me with possible arrest and citations for hiking on a trail I didn’t know was closed except to hunters. He stated this was clearly posted on signs however the route I took had no such signs unless it was hidden in the vegetation. I understand for safety purposes they close trails to non hunters and I even understand issuing tickets if they have to, but 2 things that bother me about this. The first was his over the top aggressive attitude like I was this big time criminal, and the other is the conflict in interest of a DNR officer hunting within his jurisdiction while policing it at the same time. I most likely will never go back.

This is one of Stony Creek's best kept secrets. Not many people know about it or realize this is actually part of Stony Creek park because unless you hike to it from the Nature center trails you can't get to it from inside the park(via driving) but you can drive to it from outside the park. For years the park leased out this property to a company and I guess it was a grave pit for a long time. After the company stopped leasing the land it sat unused for many years and mother nature slowly reclaimed the land to its rightful state. Now its officially being used as an extension to the park and in my opinion a the secret jewel for nature enthusiasts of all kinds. One reason is because there are a breeding pair of Bald Eagles that nest and breed here every year. Please note, they are protected(Federally)and the park monitors them closely making sure that no one disturbs either them or their nesting area which again is protected under federal law. This is also a prime time location to find an Eastern Massasauga rattlesnake which is also protected by the State laws and under "special concern" status. You can also find Minks here as I did around the streams if your quite and looking(and with a little luck!!). All in all, this is the true Nature area you'll want to come to if you visit Stony and want to witness nature at its best hands down!! Enjoy as I have so many time!!

As a park goes its awful. Only reason this gets good reviews is solely due to the cider mill located across the street and the fishing. What this park doesn't have is a playground or anything of that nature for the kids, a pavilion or any form of shelter, and basically anything else found in a real park. There's some picnic tables and some grills and that's about all you get here. Another reviewer stated its a launch site for kayaks and yes you can paddle off here but its not an official launching point and offers no info or maps typically found at designated sites. Now it may sound like I dislike it here or have some personal vendetta but that isn't the case at all, I actually really enjoy coming here when I go to Yates Cider Mill or to fish from time to time. I'm sorry If my review seems harsh but it's just the facts. If you enjoy places that basically offer nothing as far as entertainment or activities, piles of dog crap, and garbage from lazy, ass self-absorbed people who enjoy nature enough to fish but not enough take their empty worm container or fishing line w/ them then you will love it here. Seriously what is so hard about taking you garbage w/ you and why do you feel so special that you can just leave it for someone else to pick up? Enjoy!!

Of all the Metro parks Stony is at top of my list. Tones on awesome trails and paths to choose form. Whether hiking, to Mountain biking this place has you covered. In the winter you can cross country sky or head over to anyone of the many hills and go sledding. The fishing here is great but I suggest doing so from a boat/kayak as shore fishing may not land you what your looking for. You can't go wrong here regardless of your activities. I've heard at some of the other Metro parks that the park police can be less then friendly, I can tell you first hand that's not the case here. Every run in I've had I can say has been nothing but pleasant and I've had a few cause I'm that guy they have to track down and kick out at closing time. Now if your drunk and belligerent then of course they will treat you like such but come on that should just be expected. They do have a campsite here and I can tell you the sites are place in a wooded area near the lake shore. I have never camped here because it's just way to close to home and would be like camping in my backyard but it looks like ideal spot for pitching a tent for the night. Enjoy!!

Nice, well managed park. It has a playground, 2 volleyball courts side by side, basketball courts, soccer fields and paved walking paths. Though I did not need to use them the bathrooms are in a fixed structure and not port-a-potties which is nice. If you happened to noticed the large pond that appears to be included as part of this park in the overhead map view then I regret to inform you that it's not. This was the main reason I scouted this park in the first place thinking that it was. That's not to say you can't gain access, which you can very easily throughout many of the breaks along the fence and despite the fact no one seems to police this and I saw no signs stating to "keep out" or "no trespassing" I would still imagine you would be if you ventured in as I did. With that said, fishing here didn't seem to promising. I saw many dead fish and a oil base residue floating on parts of the water near the shoreline. Also I found it a little strange the limited amount of waterfowl that were here for such a tucked away little pond. Personally I would fish elsewhere if that's your motivation.
dislikes: Misleading map (pond not part of park)

reviews_attraction.text: The Detroit Zoo has unquestionably had a very troubled financial past nearly being forced to permanently close its doors on a few occasions but thanks to large private donations and sponsors whom have made very large contributions along with the many successful fund raising efforts it can now be said the zoo has made a complete 360 turnaround. Over the last 10/15 years or so the zoo has been transformed undergoing some much need improvements, renovations and adding new additions hosting new animals like the Grey wolfs. For those of us old enough to remember the zoo back then before all the positive changes and who can recall how desperate it once was, it wouldn’t be fair to give anything less then a 5 star rating now. The Detroit Zoo is another wonderful testament to the efforts being made towards making all things Detroit the greatest comeback story the nations ever seen. Obviously we still have a long way to go but it should still be noted that success stories like the Detroit Zoo are proof we’re on the right track to one day making that a reality.

This bridge has so much history and yet most will never know it. Some of which is its dark history with suicide and death. The Detroit Free Press' Detroit Almanac, stated that in 1935, 87 people had leaped from the bridge to their deaths, a sum no doubt aggravated by the Great Depression, which hit Detroit especially hard. The problem was so acute that the Detroit Police Department instituted a "suicide squad" to scout the bridge for potential jumpers. In 1938 alone, 15 would-be jumpers were saved. Another hotly debated historical moment for the bridge's history is when Harry Houdini jumped from it back on Nov. 27th 1906 as one of this famous stunts. The jump happened, but it's the details over whether he was trapped under the ice nearly dying seem to be just fiction as reported by Detroit News and many other sources. There is plenty more fun facts and hopefully this will intrigue you to do your our research. Best part about this bridge is where it takes you to regardless of the direction your heading.

Trees are beautiful and the one trail we hiked was well maintained. As for the entire park my experience was brief but from what i saw along this road in the park I wasn’t overly impressed. Not as much to it as I was expecting and not much info posted to go off of while your here. The ranger station was closed at the time and most of the side roads were also closed and locked. Aside from the first main trail you come across at the beginning not a lot to see unless you research before hand or already know the area well. Also you need permits to hike and camp here but I wasn’t able to obtain any online because you are required to do so weeks in advance even though there wasn’t soul around in the hole park. Do your research in advance and get permits setup long before any impromptu visits to save yourself from wasting your time. Personally I’d just recommend going to some of the other nearby redwood locations instead because they seem much better.

Absolutely beautiful area. You have to go down a seasonal dirt road to get here and to the campsites. Its a bit of a bumpy ride but people make it w/ huge RV's so its not to bad. The river access is by foot traffic only because you have to go down a pretty steep foot trail to get to the river. If you have a boat you can launch boats at Tippy Dam down the road. There maybe a closer spot I'm just not sure. This is a good spot for Steelhead and Salmon when they make their runs. Like I mentioned theres a campsite located here but I didn't pay much attention to the over all size but its not very big and spots may be limited during peek times. It's $5 for a day pass due to it being a National forest "fee area" which you'll need pay to park here but its well worth if you ask me. Not sure how much camping fee is. Enjoy!!

Great place to go if you want to enjoy the beauties of downtowns  riverfront property. The path is very long and runs along side the Detroit river. If taking pictures is your thing then I promise you won't be disappointed. This area has really been cleaned up over the last few years. It's about as safe as safe gets for being in Detroit. It's Under 24hr police video surveillance and has 911 call stations all along walking path, not to mention this area is pretty heavily patrolled as well. What's also nice about this locate is its hill which is unique for being downtown.  There's an awesome little Splash park for kids, and parking isn't normally bad unless there's a big event going on. All in all great place to go and enjoy a hot summer day along the Detroit river front. Enjoy!!

Great spot to view the night Sky w/o all the light pollution that normally would prevent you from seeing much of the stars/sky that you would say if you were in the UP. It Obviously doesn't take the place of being in the UP but its a great alternative w/o the long drive. Please note for obvious reasons experiences may very due to weather conditions, the time of year, and the amount of human contact you have at time of visit. If conditions are right then you should have no problem getting a decent view of the Milk Way belt. This park is blacked out(now lighting) for this very reason so make sure to stay respectful and try to limit headlights and any other lighting to an absolute minimum. I recommend using Red LED lights in place of your normal flashlights. Enjoy!!

Rural and tucked away from plan sight this is a great alternative to a long drive up north. There is some great historical facts to be learned here, as well as plenty of access to fish, hike, bike, picnic, and everything else that a park would draw you in for. Pet friendly but dogs must be on 6' leash when hiking. Though I didn't spend much time near lake it seems quite large and I am looking forward to a future fishing trip. My visit was over the winter months so I wasn't able to see much of the wildlife, however it is extremely obvious this is a prime location once warmer for plenty of furry and feathery encounters. Elevation various so for my fellow eastsiders this will be a nice little treat from our flat parks we know and love so well. Enjoy!!

I had so much fun watching and photographing these guys(and girls) skateboarding. Extremely chill crowd where everyone was just having fun on a beautiful California day down at the beach. I look forward to my next trip out!!
Update 7/12/17:
Went back and hung out here again for 2 days and experience was the same. This time I saw this little boy that couldn't have been any older then like 6 skateboard who just blew my mind how good he was. He had like no fear at all and he was skating vert to top it off. This is by far one of my favorite places to visit whenever I'm in LA area. Highly recommend!!

This is a beautiful park and I'm envious being that I'm from the east side of the state. As much as I am pure Michigan kinda guy it kills me to say that compared to a lot of other states it seems to me Michigan falls short of the care, maintenance and atmosphere you find elsewhere. Slowly I'm starting to notice a change in all that with the new additions of parks or the renovations of existing parks with the west side of the state leading the way which I hate saying but it's true. Awesome park and I hope the locals here appreciate and take care of this wonderful place.

I love coming here and watching the climbers and just pondering what an awesome experience that must be and how perfect it also must be if all you had to do to get away from the world was climb to a place where nobody could reach you. The thought of that always takes me back to being a kid again when I climbed to the top of every tree in the neighborhood and now I find myself looking back wishing I wasn’t to old and unskilled to be up there also. Oh well that’s life and you’ll never get anywhere staring in the rearview crying about the turns you missed!!

Nice nature area with lots of well traveled trails on a hilly environment. Ironically I didn't see very many birds but there is definitely no shortage of squirrels or chipmunks to say the least. Too many people come here for my liking but I'm the type that likes places where you don't see anyone. Parking outside the gate where we entered was limited but there are plenty of other spots to park if full. All in all the entire area is beautiful and should be visited if you enjoy hiking as I do. Enjoy!!

As far as State parks go I feel it is lacking. Maybe it's just cause Its to close to home for me but I feel it's a little boring and limited. I've camped in the "wagon wheel" many times as a teen and was always a good time but that was about as good as it ever got for me here. The hiking trails leave very little to the imagination and the landscaping seems to go on and on with very little noticeable change in scenery. Again my opinion is biased and should probably be over looked this time.

Great park to visit for some family fun. I love all the free games, especially the giant connect 4. Year round this is another great addition to the city of Detroit and I hope to keep seeing more and more improvements like this that revitalizes the city’s image and brings people from all walks of life back together again in the spirit of Detroit. One love

Really cool place!! This is a good spot to go if you want to see Detroit's creative side. If you enjoy'd Eastern Markets artwork then you'll appreciate the array of street art here considering a lot was done by  some of the same artists. My favorite was the dinosaur constructed out of junk odds and ends but it's been dismantled. RIP Jordan(aka TEAD)

My visit here was peaceful and relaxing while here in November for my first time and in search of rocks and simply enjoying my birthday alone. This stretch of beach is perfect for rock hounds offering a plentiful variety of all types and shapes. Time can easily get lost here if you’re like me and lose yourself in the hunt. Highly recommend

I love the hiking trails here. Plenty of wildlife to see as long as you don't advertise your coming in advance. The overall park itself is nice and well kept but at the same time seems a bit boring to me but again I come here for the hiking trails so as far as I'm concerned its perfect. Enjoy!!

Had a brief visit here which was really nice. Beautiful area along the Huron River. It's within walking distance to Bird Hills Nature area which to is very nice place to visit and hike. I plan to visit again at a later date and will update my review with park details.
One of my local favorites I regular often for wildlife/ bird sightseeing. Has a pretty extensive trail system with even more improvement on the way. great spot. Enjoy!!
View is amazing and not a bad seat in the house. From concerts to games I always leave satisfied. Go Tigers!!

This is a wonderful place to visit. There is a visitors on one of the roads leading into the park that has a shop, video, park rangers, a store and shuttles to the park.

You can either drive into the park and park and walk or park at the visitors center and walk into the park. The park is free and it is a wonderful pace to visit.

There are several parking lots but this is a popular Co Springs destination so the lots fill up quickly. The road is one way and you share it with people riding bikes, walking, on skateboard and in cars (sometimes stopped) so pay attention and rive carefully.

For the center part of the park most of the main pathways are about 4' wide sidewalks that are easily traversable.

There are excursions that you can take, like rock climbing and bicycle riding, for a fee but you can just walk the park and get some great pictures and see some beautiful views. We visited this park twice, once when it was overcast and once when the weather cleared. There is a walking path on the southern end of the walkway that allows you a better view up near to the top of one of the rocks. I highly recommend taking this as it is a very pretty view.

Definitely recommend for anyone in the area to see this national monument.

A must-see on the space Coast. COVID update Sept 2020
This is the heart and soul of the space program and one of the places where America launched, and launches, people and items into space. It is open with specific COVID restrictions. There is plenty of parking. Costs for tickets to enter are $57 with an annual pass about $90. There is plenty of parking. All personnel must wear masks and get a temperature screening to enter. There are at least 4 things that you probably want to see while you are there: The IMAX, Shuttle, Memorial and gift shop. The IMAX is open with spaced out seating. There were at least 2 different movies that were showing when we went. The shuttle experience was open and well worth going. The movie presentation and display is very original and well done. The memorial is tucked behind the IMAX theater closest to the road. The gift shop is in the center of the complex – hard to miss. There are definitely other items to see but those are the ones that I liked the most when I visited. Overall, the complex is a must see to see the past and present of the American space program. Enjoy
likes: Facilities & Services: Parking, IMAX, Shuttle experience, Memorial

reviews_attraction.text:
A must see show at EPCOT
This is located on the far side (south side) of the lake in the American of the park. The shows are on a regular schedule so pick up a brochure to find the times. You may want to give a few extra minutes since there is typically a room with a display of culturally apropriate material. The day that we went there was a tribute to Native American music and culture. It was very well done. They will announce when the doors open. You will proceed up the stairs and escalators to enter the back of the theater. All cast members are wearing masks and maintaining social distance. The seating is marked off for groups to stay together but be separated from other groups. The show is about 20 minutes with the American story told by a combination of the animatronic historical characters (Twain, Jefferson, Bell, etc) and various video display presentation. It is an inspiring and well done presentation. There is an added bonus that it is well air conditioned, the seats are comfortable and the theater is beautiful. A must see for any visitor to the park.
likes: Facilities & Services (comfortable seating, air conditioning, beautiful theater)

reviews_attraction.text: A great piece of Florida history. This historic site is inside the Canaveral National Seashore park and so has a national park entrance fee for the vehicle. After entering you travel about 1.25 miles (just past the Apollo Visitor’s center to the River Road turnoff on the right-hand side of the road. This road will take you by the parking areas 7 and above. There are signs for the turnoff for this site. I believe that it is about parking lot 8. Parking lot for this location is a fair distance (about 300 yards down the road) from the physical structure and the river. It is a beautifully restored house to museum for the time period. Upon entry we were greeted by a park ranger. He offered and we watched a 13 minute video. Following that we looked at the displays in the first two rooms of the house. The staff member was very friendly. Outside the house there is a dock to the north and a walkway and trail to the south. We did not go very far along the walkway. If you are a Florida history fan, this is a must-see!

This is a must ride for EPCOT.
I have ridden this often both before and after COVID. It is located in the Land pavilion at EPCOT. GO early as it is a very popular ride and fills up early. It is one of the best rides in the whole park. There is a long walk down the concourse to get to the ride but it is low stress and very enjoyable. You are seated in three rows of chairs about 10 chairs wide. They have added dividers for covid spacing both in the waiting areas and in between the seats. You sit down, buckle in and then the seat move so that the row 1 is at the top, row 2 is in the middle and row 3 is at the bottom facing a large screen. Your feet are dangling and you are transported to various places across the world that are absolutely beautiful and breathtaking. Once complete, the seat return to the ground and you exit. It is a wonderful must-see ride for anyone wanting a pleasant experience.
likes: Facilities & Services: Seating arrangement, safety measures

reviews_attraction.text: Wow – Beautifully done museum – Must see! I visited this museum many years ago but it has undergone a major renovation. It was good, now it is great. It is located next to the beach and has plenty of parking. It has the actual museum, lots of static displays, a store and an obstacle course. The cost is very inexpensive for what the museum is showing you. It is really beautifully done by years going from the most recent as you enter the door to the WWII at the southern end. There are interactive displays on computers as well as lots of very well done displays throughout. Outside there are displays to show the various craft that are or have been used. Some are viewing only and some you can actually go onto. The entire museum and grounds is one of the best that I have seen. If anyone is interested in military history, this is a must see.

Outstanding site explaining the Fort in its heyday

This is a drive off the interstate but worth it. The site was free and there was plenty of parking. The visitors center was open. It is pretty much in the middle of the site. The visitors center is great. ½ of it is a bookstore and shop and ½ is a series of historical displays. The staff was great and very helpful. You walk around the site on a self guided tour. Each building and location has waist high informational panel that tells the details about the location. Some buildings are just shells that have been maintained. Some have been fully restored and you can walk through. I highly recommend walking through the restored ones. The restoration is wonderful. I was especially impressed with the Cavalry bunkroom and dining hall. This site is a must see for any fellow travelers.

What a cool place. I did not even know that this existed or that it was in Lousiana. It is a self-guided tour. That has several stops. The story of the McIlhenny family and the hot sauce history is fascinating. It is the only place, in the world, that makes this every sauce that you see on tables everywhere. We went on a day when the factory was closed but it was still worth it. You could easily walk all the stations within about 1-2 hours – more if you want to get more detail. The staff was very friendly and professional. The prices were reasonable. They have a tasting bar at the back of the git shop that allows you to try all the sauces. I did not have the time to see the jungle gardens but hope to visit again soon. I really enjoyed it and highly recommend it.
likes: Facilities & Services: Self-guided tour, friendly staff, reasonable prices

reviews_attraction.text: A very nice Japanese garden in Saratoga. There are about 30-40 parking spaces directly in front of the entrance. You pay for the entrance fee at the shop next to the parking lot and across from the entrance. It was a modest fee for what you can see. They have done a very nice job of maintaining the park.
