There are many sites for a small space and be apprised many of the upper paths are thin dirt paths up a step hill. There are several buildings that you can get to and around, a bamboo garden, a small pond with koi and a rock garden. Please get the brochure that has the highlights of the gardens and the story behind them. I really liked this garden and think it is worth the stop and the fee. Enjoy.

Mormon structures – interesting from historical perspective.
This site is not as interesting as many of the other pullouts and turnouts from my perspective. But I believe that others would find all of it interesting due to the structures being maintained in their original look and place for many years. There are, I think, 5 sets of structures. One is close to the paved road and the others are a little farther off. We only went to the closer one. There is a board with a map and an explanation. You can walk around the area and I have heard that the barn is the most photographed barn in America and, maybe, the world. The backdrop is the Grand Tetons so the pictures come out very well.

What a cool little museum.
This is not a massive structure. It is a small building located just off the interstate. There is pleny of parking. It is dedicated to the Minuteman missile facility that were located nearby. There is a small walk through museum that is very well done highlighting the arms race, why the silos were built and how they worked. It is a neat little museum that anyone and everyone should see to understand what the country went through during those times. There is also a small gift shop. If you are interested, they also have self guided tours of 2 of the delta facilities (missile facilities) nearby. A good historical stop if you are in the area

A great place to see the seals. This is the southernmost of the two parking lots but there is a trail that connects them. We parked in the northern parking lot that is listed as the Boucher trailhead. The walkway is pretty easy to navigate and is elevated above the beach and so the seals are easy to see from the trail and the southern parking lot. When we went there were about 40-50 of them in a pack near that southern parking lot. Be on the lookout along the trail because we found several that were far away from the pack of seals near to the northern parking lot. It is a great place to stop and see the seals that is right of the road with plenty of parking.

We like hiking so we decided to try this park.
There is a cost to enter the main part of the park.
Once there (at the water) There is a fair amount of parking, bathrooms and a concession stand.
We arrived after 1 pm and the place was very busy so if you are going to visit you may want to go early. We hiked the upper falls trail and then walked down to the waterfalls. The falls were nice but even though people were not supposed to climb on the rocks or be in the water at the falls there were a lot of people in both places who had no respect for the park rules.
My suggestion for anyone visiting this park is to take the trails away from the main area.

True to its name – Easy stop.
This particular stop is right off the South east side of 240. It is an easy pull-off with about 25 parking spaces for cars and a lane for about 2 or 3 RV’s. It is very true to its name and gives a view of the hills off to the South of the parking lot which are a lot of yellow and whitish hills. It is a very nice view of the colored hills. You can climb on some of the hills next to the parking lot for a better view. There are trails that seem to start from this location although we did not go on any of them. A pretty and easy stop to see pastel colored hills.

Beautiful building and very nice display even with COVID
This site is well marked from the road and easy to get to from the main park road. There is a large parking lot with plenty of parking. They have managed the COVID arrangements very well. They have arranged it with one entrance and one exit . Dots on the floor to specify 6 foot distance. The 3 d map, gift shop and ranger booth are all open. The view out the window looks directly out onto the Tetons. This is a great first stop for seeing the park and I highly recommend it for people to prepare to see the park.
likes: Open amenities (3D map, gift shop, ranger booth)

reviews_attraction.text:
A good place to get souvenirs.
This location is located off the Moraine Park entrance. There is a parking lot with about 50 spaces. The restrooms were in a separate building from the main building but were functional. The main building did not appear to be open but there was a Park Ranger under a tent by the entrance. The gift shop is a modular building set up in the parking lot. It is small and can only fit about 5 customers at a time. The staff was very friendly and helpful. If you want to get some souvenirs then this is a good place to look.

Nice park, boat ramp currently under construction. This property is on the point of land with easy access to the water/river. The boat ramp is still being rebuilt and is expected to be completed in early 2020. This means that there is no trailer access at this time. The grounds are well kept. There are several covered pavilions with tables and a set of restrooms on the grounds and the water is easy access for kayaks and paddleboards. There is limited parking while construction is underway. Overall, nice park with limited access.

Fossil exhibit trail – 5 stars
A great walk with Plenty of exhibits
This is right off the road travelling through the park. There is a large parking lot with plenty of space for cars and RV’s. There is a short boardwalk that seems well maintained right off the parking lot. There are many signboards and displays to explain the various fossils found in the area. You could spend 10 minutes or an hour there looking at displays and walking beyond the boardwalk. Very nice, easy, pleasant and informative stop. A must see for the park.

Very pretty view and an easy stop
This is an easy pull-off stop on the east side of the road. There is a large curved parking lot. The walkway is a short wide path to a larger platform at the end. It is an easy stop and gives a good view of all the hills surrounding the east side of the park at that area. We saw this on an overcast day but I think this stop would be wonderful on a sunnier day because even when we saw it you could see the various levels in the sand structures. Very pretty and worth the short stop.

Lots to see – worth the stop!
There are several parking lots and a driving loop for this attraction. We parked on the side of the road on the beginning part of the driving loop. There is a boardwalk and stairs around most of the sights. We alked down and around the Minerva Terrace and back up. This is not an easy walk back up. Lots of steps and a steep asphalt walkway with a serious crown. Beautiful sites, lots of sites to see from one location. Well worth the stop!

Easy to get to but you’ll have a difficult view from the parking lot due to the trees.
This is one of the first overlooks that you come to after leaving String Lake parking lots on Jennie Lake Road. It seems to be a fairly popular stop and was almost totally full when we stopped. There are some paths but you will have to move toward the lake or to the end of the parking lot to get an unobstructed view of the lake and the mountains.

This is a wonderful exhibit that shows the actual tiger in his enclosure. It is near the stadium and on campus to that it is easy to get to. There is plenty of parking nearby and it allows lots people to see Mike. It is one of the best places to see a tiger up close. Both times that I stopped by the enclosure, Mike was outside and sitting on the rock making picture taking easy. I think this is a must see for anyone in the area.

Easy to get to and a very pretty view.
This is an easy but steep drive off the main highway that is paved for part of the journey and a rock road passable by regular cars for the last part of the journey. The parking lot at the end has some paths, a restroom and a great view by the river and across the valley to the foothills of the Tetons. We went in October and the foliage colors were stunning .

Great flat turnout with a wonderful view of the Mountains
This is a flat turnout right off the Jenny Lake Road. There are parking spaces for about 25 cars all facing the mountain view. It allows a stunning view of the major peaks of the Tetons. Great place to relax and enjoy the view.

Easy pullout, Great View
This is a large flat pull-out off the Teton Park Road north of the lakes complex. There is plenty of parking and unobstructed views of the mountains. Great place to pull off and enjoy the view.

this should be a great park, but it is an example of how the immediate area residents are somewhat allowing the place to be pulled down by undesirable activity by staying away.  If you stay out of the boat launch/park parking area you will avoid most of the bad stuff.  Another  truly unfortunate thing about here is, although having a great waterfront with views/wildlife etc. you cannot safely swim since there is no separate area from the boat launch/marina, there also is signs about sewage outflow after storms and the fuel/oil that comes from the marina.  Maybe if enough people started taking this place back it would become what it should be, a gem along south lake washington.

probably the best option for trampolines as of right now.  like all trampoline places, they have gotten more strict to avoid lawsuits but you still can flip in the main area and they allow a fair amount of stunts in the foam pit.  there area other activities available inside such as a kid playset and a laser room and a basic game area.  food is available but nothing spectacular, best bet is use your time and head to one of the local food spots afterwards, say the drive inn just down the road.

Update- the new flying circus in Kent now kills this place.bigger better tramps, more options and far less rules.

fun,cheap and lots to entertain for the day.  when you are sick of the weather in seattle head over here for almost guaranteed sun and much more warmth.  wind can get high here so consider a rash guard to stay a little warmer when out of the water.  water slides are basic but fun and high dive boards are very popular for those wanting to show off.  the surf rider is awesome and usually not to busy since it takes some skill.  give it a go and you will probably pick it up(as long as you don't care about crashing and burning in front of others)after a while.  They do sell food inside.

Although this place is free to the public and their intent is noble in trying to educate the public on conservation it doesn't seem to offer much.  Other than a nice bridge over the tranquil creek and holding pens for public fish viewing, i am not sure if this place is truly serving the best public interest for the  large amount of taxpayer money it requires to operate, especially when there is some evidence that non-hatchery methods may produce better results in salmon spawning.  Were it not free, I would give it 2 stars.

great mtb trails.  be aware that you start at the bottom and have to go up up up before you can come down.  trails are mostly very long, requiring commitment and can be confusing for new visitors.  Do not go without a map or someone who knows the area.  Potential to get hurt far from the trailhead is very possible, so bring your own first aid gear and do not ride alone.  Hiking is only suggested on certain trails to avoid conflict with fast   downhill riders.  plenty of parking but entry /exit to hwy 18 can be dangerous.
dislikes: Need for a map or guide

reviews_attraction.text:
incredible waterfront park.  Only drawback is that it is adjacent to hwy 97 and the railroad is very close(don't know how often the train runs).  I am not completely sure why the hoards travel so much farther to chelan when you can have a complete experience here without the crowds/cold water of chelan and high prices of the city of chelan.  lots of parking/boat trailer parking and launch, camping(both tent and rv) right on the water.
For some reason this place does not seem to have been discovered, it is vacant.

i will admit it is very unique, much like northwest trek except in your own vehicle.  The downsides are: very expensive for what it is and honestly, it seems like the animals do not have a very good quality of life.  It is understood why this place existed originally but now it seems to be just a cash cow for the owners and not much about the animals.  We probably will never return.

based on the description and pics we were expecting a spectacular park.  Once we got there we saw that it was very similar to most community parks, a fairly nice play structure and a lot of new landscaping.  We heard that there was a huge play structure that was very tall with climbing elements and parkour area, not so.  Probably fun for very young ones and live close by.

great for walks.  paved path goes through the entire park, feels pretty secluded and quiet.  at bottom there is a nice basic play area with a small spray park in the summer.  Not really much flat grass areas for sports.  parking is on two sides of the park and is shared by the ymca and library but if that is full drive to the other side.

There aren't many parks around with the view this one offers.  The city maintains this place better than most anal homeowners keep their own yard.  if you are in the area come take a walk around the .52 mile paved trail or head into the paved trail along the adjacent park and probably see the elk herd.

this is a beautiful park but main offering is baseball.  There is a nice creek running through the lower section.  Parking in two lots seems to be a little insufficient on busy days.  Not a ton of shade with exception of one field so bring your tent or umbrella on a hot day. nice little snack stand.

beautiful area, not sure about the review stating poop and gross water.  the swim area is very nice.  overall a well maintained park with great views and very few people.  big downside is no camping, but there are water access sites nearby that allow overnighting(no real campsites or utilities).
dislikes: Limited facilities (no real campsites or utilities)

reviews_attraction.text: pretty distant from the city but that gives you a dark sky at night for stargazing and plenty of seclusion in a beautiful viewing site for the canyon and the abundant raptors along the cliffs.  you can camp here but much better places exist 5 miles further down by the river that are also free.

this place is cool.  We had our first visit after living here almost 40 years.  getting to the water is a bit of a hike but on a nice trail through a peaceful forest.  no real swimming area but still a fun place to go in summer.  lots of other stuff to explore here.  lots of parking.

if you have not been for a while go.  the park has been much improved lately.  probably one of the best skateparks in seattle.  incredible views, huge play area, water spray area, zip line,tons of play fields and enough parking most of the time.  one of our favorite seattle parks.

very fun, not a ton of rides but enough.  suggest getting in on the afternoon pricing to save your money, you will still get enough done to satisfy everyone.  There is a public pool next door that is separate cost(cheap) but warm and worth hitting afterwards if you are cold.

this place is fun for adults and kids alike.  You could spends hours here and still not take in all the information.  just the structure alone is amazing.  check out the boats outside(floating museum).  worth going back multiple times.

boat launch is easy and not crowded, a fair amount of parking.  seems to be a hangout for some shady people but never had a confrontation.  check out the rowing/sailing center. lots of good classes offered. great 180 degree views.

I can't hate on the beach with this view and sunsets but don't go there with kids expecting to have tons to do.  you cannot swim(too cold and rip currents) but there are some areas of tidepools at low tide.
you learn something new everyday. i have lived in bellevue for 40 years and never really explored this park. largest in bellevue and it seems like you are somewhere remote. great trails.
parking is not free but easy to find.  city did an exceptional job at renovating what was a wasteland.  so much more to do here than meets the eye.  explore and take at least one hike.
you will be amazed.  Kind of a hidden oasis.  Not just for rock climbers.  Gets very busy and parking can be a problem and is not free unless you already have a pass.
go out of your way or make this a destination trip, it is that cool.  the hike to the top looks scary and is a little but not as much as you would think.
tons of orv trails great place for beginners and experienced alike.  If you are not an orv you may not like it because you will have encounters.
so fun, how can anyone rate it poorly.  Obviously best time to visit is in winter otherwise you are better off hitting silverwood waterpark.

This garden is on some extensive acreage.   There are excellent botanical displays, in a variety of formats.   There is also a stage venue.
The highlights are the world- class sculptures, presented in a variety of natural settings, most notable the DaVinci giant stallion.
There is a tram ride that takes you around the majority of the vistas, allowing you glimpses of some statuary, which you can eaxily visit on foot.
There is a neat children's area.  The Japanese gardens are fairly new, and it will be interesting to watch the development over the years.
Make sure you take water with you, as there are limited places to grab a bite or beverage.

The Blue gate restaurant is in the heart of the Amish shopping district in Shipshewana.   There is a theater in the building as well.
The menu can be ala carte or family style.   All the food was excellent, with the sampler platter being a way to try lots of things.   The ham was especially tasty.  The meatloaf was good.   The chicken pot pie was bland but for the fact that the gravy was extra salty.
The real reason to come is for the pie.   There are a multitude of possibilities, all of which are very tasty with excellent flaky crusts.   I highly recommend the sugar cream pie
Stop by, even if it's only for some pie.

The Ruthmere mansion offers tours on the hour during the season.
The building is in excellent shape, and contains a lovely variety of decor in the Beaux Arts style.  The tour starts with a video about the building and family.  There are stairs to climb, but you get a very thorough overview of the way things were in the early part of the 20th century.
Our tourguide is also the caretaker, and provided a very knowledgable insight into the life and time of the building.
One of the best historic house tours I have ever been on

Coit tower has recently undergone some renovations.  (Thanks National Trust for Historic Preservation)   The WPA murals on the ground floor are freshly cleaned, and present interesting visions of life in the 1930's SF.   The stairs are out of commission, so you have to take the small elevator up.   The views are spectacular, particularly on a clear day.  The view from the ground level parking area is also not bad.   On the way down,  try the steps toward the Embarcadero,  very great insights into lush backyards.
dislikes: Facilities & Services: Stairs out of commission

reviews_attraction.text:
We recently stopped to see the Ansel Adams exhibit.   The museum building is reminiscent of an adobe pueblo, and has many interesting plantings on the grounds.   It abuts the canal walking district.
The exhibits in the museum itself are interesting, but once you are partway through the second floor exhibits, you are fairly committed as the exit areas are limited.   The photography exhibit upstairs about the gay rodeo was also interesting.
A good introduction to First nation lifestyles and western art.

Neat brewery tour.   Very large beer hall atmosphere.    There is good service at the bar, with the draft list posted on a board.  There is also some root beer available on draft.
The tour shows some of the aspects involved in brewing, and provides tokens to imbibe along the way.  There is also some memorabilia stuff--such as the bottling line, and Bernie Brewer's original mug and hut.  The guides are well-informed and personable.
A fun atmosphere.   Just be sure to reserve tour tickets.

The Arboretum is on a lake, a short drive from downtown Dallas.   There is a separate children's area with an additional admission fee.   The garden currently has a pumpkin town, and there are displays for the 12 days of Christmas erected, with only a few on view.   A portion of the garden is closed for renovation, but the rest has meandering trails,  different atmospheres and scenic vistas.  A must visit place, if only for the calming beauty.
dislikes: Additional admission fee for children's area

reviews_attraction.text: Giant bat and walk of fame outside.   Good tour of an actual working bat factory.   The guides seem very  glad to share their knowledge.   You get to see some of the old hand-turned methods, as well as the latest modern carving.  The exhibits have some interest to the baseball history fan.   You can purchase an engraved bat (not carry-on legit), as well as other Slugger memorabilia.   I liked it even though I am not a baseball fan.

Great experience located near the convention center.   There are distinct zones, including a mountain encouraging climbing, a mist filled pool, and a quiet, below ground level meditation pool.  The major site is the active pool, where you can descend some steps and experience the sound and thrill of rushing water.   A great postmodern piece of architecture.  Worth a stop for some quiet introspection.

This show presents a fountain with colored lights,  that change in coordination with the music.   The playlist varies by evening, and the show presents some interesting effects.
There is bleacher type seating, or bring chairs or a blanket.   The fountain is across the river from the stands, which are smack dab in the middle of downtown Grand Haven.
Harkens back to old fashioned family amusement.

Neat lighthouse in the Lakefront park.   The building is open only on weekends.   The staff is very knowledgable and eager to give a tour of all the displays.  The tower actually has an older portion on a newer base.   The tower is not to bad to climb, and there is a ladder to get to the very top.   There is also a greenhouse effect at the very top.   The fog can roll in very quickly.

The Burbank home and gardens is a lovely place to spend some time in Santa Rosa.   The gardens are open daily, with the house being viewable only through a tour.   The gardens are nicely manicured, and are subdivided into planting groupings.   There are some lovely mature trees, and a gigantic cactus.   An interesting insight into this horticulturalist.
Street parking available.

The Dana Thomas house has classic Frank Lloyd Wright architecture.   The space is filled with wonderful period pieces and furniture, all appropriate for it's original purpose as a house for entertaining guests.  The tour takes you throughout the buildings, with a lovely meandering route as is common in FLW buildings.
On of the best FLW experiences I have ever had.

This state park is around the town of Mendocino.   There are some walking paths on the clifftops, as well as down to the 2 beaches.   The views of the ocean, as well as of the town are fabulous.  There is a blowhole and the sunset views from the parking area are quite phenomenal.   A great wander when staying in or just visiting the town of Mendocino proper.

The glass beach in MacKerricher consists of 3 separate areas, all part of a former trash dump.   The amount of glass is minimal, but there are tidal pools containing interesting creatures.   The walk on the clifftops is nice, and there are numerous areas to stop and enjoy the view.   Also check out the fox squirrels in the coastal prairie.

All sorts of interesting artifacts and video displays, with a carousel that you can ride.   Nice location on the river, with interesting architectural elements.   Make sure you check for special exhibits.   Great place to learn about history and science, since there is a sky show as well.    Must see in downtown Grand Rapids.

Old school horse racing experience.   The box seats are well worth it.   Enjoy seeing the horses in the paddock and the post-parade.   The food is adequate, and there are several places to get a mint julep.
The only thing that would have improved the experience is a betting primer.
A fun day out with family and friends.

Neat re-use of a former train track.   There are entrances about every 2 blocks (1/4 mile).   There are a few fountains around California.   No bathroom facilities and not enough places to sit.
Bustling with people walking, cycling, etc.   Use it to wander, get off and explore a new neighborhood.
A work in progress.

Lake park was designed by Frederic Law Olmstead.   There are nice paths to walk along, a lighthouse, bridges overlooking 2 ravines, a golf course and a waterfall with access to the bottom of the bluff.   A good example of using open land to create something that the community utilizes on a daily basis.

This tasting room and shop is in the old mill complex in Cedarburg.   They offer a free tasting of 4 of their varietals, and provide listings in order of sweetness of the wines.   A good selection made from local grapes and fruit.  The staff was very helpful.   A good experience.

All the art in the fabulous mansion references birds.  There is a lovely sculpture garden.   The new addition is right in character with the old building, which still retains some of the room flow indoors.   And the whole thing is free.   Worth a visit when you are in Wausau.

This park is adjacent to the arts district.   The park was bustling with activity, and interesting promenades.   There were also food trucks providing an interesting selection.   The people watching was excellent--there was a couple practicing their acrobatic skills.

The Kentucky state capitol building rests on some nicely manicured grounds, with the Floral clock in the neighborhood.   Tours are available during the week and early on Saturdays.
There is a great overlook on the west side of town.
Nice place to browse around.
The Governor's mansion is right next to the "new"  State Capitol building.   The grounds are very lovely.   Tours are available 2 days a week, so check if you want to tour the inside.
Covered bridge with wooden peg connections.   It is in a park complex with picnic tables that is located on the north part of town.   A nice stop to reflect on the olden days.

The George Eastman Museum is a cultural trifecta offering a world renowned photography and film exhibition; an incredible architectural oasis complete with manicured gardens; and finally an unrivaled venue for all sorts if events.

The exhibits are sure to please visitors of all ages. During my last visit we got to see the Warner Brothers Cartoon exhibit which provided an insider's behind the scenes look at the mechanics of producing these historical cartoons. This exhibition came complete with the opportunity to relax in the theater and view about two hours of the best of the Warner Brothers cartoons.

The gift shop offers a variety of souvenirs and learning materials for photography fans and creative types. Although 99% of the products were geared towards film enthusiasts,  the educational material was quite appropriate for digital photographers as well.

The cafe was an absolute surprise as the salads, gelatos and sandwiches are made to order immediately after ordering.

A very underrated museum destination located just a few blocks from the National Mall and the Capitol.

Inside you will discover exhibits about the history of news media as well as current events and special exhibits.

As you approach the exterior of the building be certain to check out the encased newspapers with today’s headlines. They have at least one representing the topics on the forefront of each city where the paper originated. They also have international papers represented. The display continues inside and if I remember correctly they get about 800 newspapers sent every single day for this endeavor. It truly is fascinating to see not only the commonality, but the unique issues and topics selected by many of the newspapers.

Kaaterskill Falls is one of the most picturesque destinations throughout the Catskills.
There are multiple ways to get on the trail, but my favorite is via Route 23a; where 23a meets Haines Falls. This starts the trail with a moderately steep hike that is safe if you stay on the trail and where appropriate footwear. Along the trail you will find multiple places to stop and picnic, catch a breather or even picnic. If you do picnic, please take all garbage out with you do as to leave the trail as clean as when you arrived. The trail is also accessible from the top of the Falls where there is a nearby parking lot.

A recent walk through Chinatown left me standing in front of the largest Buddhist Temple in New York City. I've always seen this from afar but as I stood there I realized that they encouraged visitors of all walks of life. So I entered and was blown away by the 16-foot Buddha poised at the altar. The space eminated a feeling of peace and quiet that is a stark contrast to the streets of this bustling Asian neighborhood.

The history and background on the construction of the temple are posted on the walls in English for visitors interested in learning more about this fascinating place.

A beautiful bridge to drive across from Queens into Manhattan. Architecturally, it certainly has a wonderful style that is more unique than the other New York bridges. There are many places in Manhattan, Queens, Long Island City and Roosevelt Island to admire it from, by way of park, roadway or tram.

The only thing stopping me from giving it five stars is the mess of a roadbed. During my last marathon run I sprained an ankle up there, due to potholes, as did many others. I even witnessed two bikes of handicapped athletes get mangled due to the potholes.

Beautiful sculpture depicting the Irish famine known as The Great Hunger. Many of the Irish boldly took to the seas to travel to America in hopes of finding a better chance at life and opportunities.

The statue is quite poignant and the artist did a fantastic job depicting both the face of burden and celebration among pride.

I hope to update this review with additional photos of all sides of the sculpture. There is much more to this work.

Took a drive upstate to visit the Forest and do the 3 mile round trip trail hike to Red Hill Fire Tower. It's not a very challenging hike, but the rewards come by taking in the beautiful forest terrain. Those not afraid of heights are welcome to climb the 60 foot tower to take in the wonderful Vistas. If you visit with children, have them do the scavenger hunt and review the trail markers for interesting history and nature notes.

Great local park serving the community during the Pandemic. Owls Head offers plenty of trees, benches, hills, paths and flowers for all to enjoy.
The park staff is totally dedicated to making this park a gem. It is usually spotless and social distancing Unfortunately,  I removed one star due to the inconsistency in the time for opening restrooms.

A recent complete renovation of the waterfront has resulted in a unique and breathtaking destination. The team of Parks and Recreation that keep this place running and maintained need be highly praised for their commitment to the job and the community. The restrooms are always clean and the staff is constantly tweaking the grounds.

A bustling seaport that serves as a museum and entertainment/dining destination for all in the city. The area is peppered with very interesting educational and historical signage. The waterfront is clean and admission passes to the museum will also get you access to some of the maritime vessels anchored along the waterfront.

A beautiful destination for hiking. Start at  the southern approach to take in the Bastion Falls before ascending to the Kaaterskill Wild Forest and Waterfalls.  Explore a large network of Bring your camera to capture the beautiful scenery. When the weather permits you can take a dip at the base of the waterfalls.

A safe and serene beach experience without the hustle and bustle of Coney Island or Brighton Beach. Spotless restrooms, shade covered benches, open air bbq areas and plenty of playgrounds and sports courts for the entire family. My only complaints are the limited parking and food concession options.

Lincoln Center is a massive venue that plays host to an eclectic range of international acts and performers. Although there is never really a dress code for public performances, this is the place where most New Yorkers insist on wearing black tie. Bring your camera to take pictures by the fountain.

This gem of a state park is constantly evolving with new amenities and surrounding businesses. If you have not visited in a year, I am certain you will discover more than during your previous visit. The views are outstanding day or night, rain or shine, so bring your camera.

Plenty of options for hiking and taking in the spectacular views of the surrounding areas. Hudson Highlands is centrally located and is really the gateway for a whole new way of getting healthy during these pandemic times.

Outstanding photo opportunities that are constantly changing due to all of the Lake George waterfront activities.
Even at night it provides for a perfect place for a stroll or perhaps some night sky photography.
Considering the fact that it's supposed to be a centerpiece for the town, it's actually a little sad looking. I can't imagine wanting to sit here after walking among the beautiful main street shops.
This waterfront park offers great views of the Manhattan skyline. Standing on the beach you can see from the Manhattan Bridge to the Queensborough Bridge. Visit at night to take in the city lights.
Rain or shine this museum destination never disappoints. Check out legendary aircraft, including a space shuttle. Kids will love the interactive displays as well as all the learning activities.
Stopped by here to do the hike to both the cliff and the ice caves. I was not disappointed. The parking lot proved ample and the trails were clearly marked and well maintained.
Formerly known as the Hayden Planetarium. The planetarium is now part of a larger collective which includes the Scales of the Universe Walkway, and the Hall of Planet Earth.
A great meeting place where you can engage in Chinese culture and activities. The park even gas an eighth of a mile track in the interior. Great photo opportunities abound.
Oceanfront state park with incredible views and great facilities.  Enjoy barbecue grills, picnic tables, trails, restaurants and the historic  Montauk Lighthouse.
This historic fort is on the register of national landmarks. I recommend searching for a park ranger to learn about the free and enlightening  guided tour.
This is a beautiful and tranquil space in a busy and sometimes hectic neighborhood. Visit on Saturday or Sunday for the meditative organ hour.

You can meet the strangest people in places like this. I decided to jaunt down the road - I don't live very far from it - and check it out. It has nice big jumps, smaller ones for the lesser experienced, and even step ups that one must bunny hop to even use the trail. The trails are marked advanced, intermediate and Pro, so pick wisely. I found the advanced trail a little bit less than riding a bmx track, and since I was on a bmx bike, it was rather a simple ride comparebly. I met a friend of mine who I rarely see, riding the pro trail, and he seemed to enjoy it. Overall, everyone I talked to said it was a good set of trails that you can be pushed to try harder, but only if it suits you. I recommend anyone who enjoys a good ride in the dirt with obstacles to get through, go visit Draper Cycle Park.

The skatepark needs some repair work for a skater to enjoy it fully; there are cracks in the flat. A bmx freestyler would enjoy it more than skaters in the condition it is in.  Other than that,  it would be a very nice park with transitions that are big enough to scare you if you are a beginner,  and large enough for a pro to reach a good height. It is a pity the county or city have decided not to repair this park, as it must have been very fun once. Scooters also might not enjoy the point of impact as their wheels find the cracks in the cement unexpectantly.

Such a strange mystery surrounding this old house that you have to see it to believe it.  It does get hot in the house so prepare before you enter.  I asked a few questions that were outside of the tour guide,  but she answered what she knew and gave opinion at times to help things mesh on the why things were done the way they were.  I had to hold my kid the whole time and though it was hard,  the guide was quite nice about trying include us though we're had to stay in the back.

Bright lights on almost every single tree add you walk around a complete block or two in the city center of salt lake city.  More than the normal crowd attends to the Christmas lights. This read my umpteenth time to traverse the beauty as I headed from one end to the other to get to the conference center for the tabernacle choir performance. Still cold,  still a sight to behold, even if walking at mach 2 to make it in time for the concert.

My kid had a report to do on Box Elder County so we figured we'd go for the most natural thing that is popular for and that is for the last Spike that connected the Transcontinental Railroad. This is place to go if you need to know that information on it and they have movies & certain presentations that indicated what they were and what was it about and how it happened.

The water was shy today.  Only a week ago it was 8 ft higher up the beach according to others. I'll have to check back another day,  but swimming was not an option. A nice walkway around the entire pond was accommodating for joggers, skaters and walkers. Sand on the beach was good for digging holes according to my kid. Ducks enjoyed it as well.

Animals,  yep they have them.  During the summer months it is a regular zoo, but in the fall they have a Halloween thing and Christmas a light show thing then too. Don't expect animals unless in the summer or you'll be disappointed. Off season openings are for the light shows and booths lined up along the zoo paths.

Covered pavilion allows people the needed shade for all sorts of events. The park has a lot of room to do a plethora of sports and events.  I usually attend three park to go skating and biking.  The park is nice Anna's large enough to give everyone room without bumping into each other too much.

Having lived down the block literally,  it was nice to see the colorful hang gliders and parachutes filling up the sky overhead.  Plenty of space to park and watch people take off if you just wonder how one just walks off the cliff and sails into the sky.

Went to the amphitheater area and had no problems with cleanliness and shade was nice, no birds nests or their excrement that you would find on such venues.  The rest of the park looked well- maintained except a very vacant swimming pool at 4:30.

What a great skatepark.  There are 10 out so different bowls and various transitions.  Skaters are not afraid of catching air out of the bowls. Street riders will have less to ride on,  but they could have enough to ride.

This park needs a lot of help it have been doing it from years that I've known it and it's gain little bit better each time but the lack of the forested area it really made said not af fun,  but more safe to visit.

Good playground?, but parking is hazardous to your health, not much of it at peak times.  With 6 tennis courts and baseball fields they need more parking. The mist sprays at the kids discovery land thing is nice.

Well built auditorium and good looking if you have good eyesight, which I am lacking, so the choir was a pretty blur of white and blue.  The chenoweth girl did very well and added just the right touch of humor.
dislikes: Poor visibility for those with eyesight issues

reviews_attraction.text: There is a lot of different attractions to choose from in the park and the surrounding areas. An average size water park/pool exist on the main southern side with a few slides included.
The submarine was intriguing and the ship was big.  The history was there as well.  The telescopic lens platforms were broken so we got a good look at Alcatraz without paying a cent.
A decent amount of shade to sit under while watching the kiddos play in the water fountains.  Went here for a church activity and it was just the right size and not crowded at all.
There is not much in this park but a playground and basket ball court and a lot of grass. A nice grade down to the park would be nice for sledding in the winter.
Luminaria is a pleasant visit when it gets cold.  Otherwise,  the gardens is where it is at for beauty. Kids still enjoy the museum,  dinosaur and curiosity.
I go here for the skate park.  Met some great guys who have gone pro, congrats to them. A nice park with a little bit for all kinds of bmx and skating.
You are not allowed to park in front of resident's homes, so park at the top of the hill by the temple if you don't find a place at the bottom.
Ended up here for a great view of the fireworks on the July 24th celebration looking out to the valley seeing explosions all over the place.
Pretty cool place to visit to see all of the butterflies flying around,  colorful blurs when trying to take their picture.
A lot of history in the tour.  They preserved what they could, and other stuff is not original but to the correct years.
A unique experience. Not the easiest to work with a child trying to sleep on your arm, but we made it work.

Snoqualmie casino is pretty close to Seattle, making it convenient to get to. It has a lot of table games and even more machines on the floor with a wide variety in selection. You have to pay for your drinks since it's not Vegas, and they like to jack up table price minimums at the most inconvenient times, including when groups of people are looking for a smaller minimum table. The restaurants are OK and the buffet, especially king crab night, is phenomenal. The buffet staff however, especially the ones at the front, tend to be pretty sassy and not too knowledgeable on things encompassed around the buffet. Make sure to get a players cars, they usually have some event or free play on your account if you tend to go every once in a while.

Melakwa Lake is about 4 and a half miles with almost 2,000 feet of elevation gain hike. The trailhead is not marked very well since it's meant for Denny Falls, however follow the trail to get there and continue through it to get to Melakwa Lake. Gradual and sometimes steep gains for the first 4 miles basically so make sure to be prepared, but once you get to the lake, it's totally worth it. Parking at the trailhead can be annoying since Denny Falls gets so busy, and make sure to have your Northwest Forest/National Parks pass, not the Discover Pass. They have a campground there too (for RVs and cars), but you drive past that closer to the bathrooms near the Franklin Falls entrance as well.

The Franklin Falls trailhead is very easy to get to off of I-90, with plenty of parking both inside of the camping parking lot and along side the roads. During the winter months, the snow here can accumulate pretty quickly, so please make sure you are driving a car that is built to go through the snow as plenty of cars get stranded here often during these months. There is a bathroom and some garbage cans near the trailhead, which is actually a split for a few other trails as well (Denny Creek, Melakwa Lake and Hemlock Pass to name a few) so it is very popular. It's a good mix of difficulties too so you will see all sorts of people hiking/walking these trails.

Green Lake is a staple in Seattle as one of the getaway from the city places. It's always full of people, walking around the 3+ mile lake loop, biking around, or sitting out on the grass fields. It has many entrances from all over, and parking would just be anywhere you find a spot. There are a few fields and courts to play sports on and a small playground area too. During the nice weather months, they have a good stand open and you can watch the row team row on the lake. There are tons of shops, restaurants and bars on the outskirts of the lake too, which is nice to go for a walk before or after.

Marymoor Park is a beautiful plot of land on the northern edge of Lake Sammamish. It is a very large park with many different types of fields within it including baseball, soccer and cricket. They hold various events here year round which is nice, however the only unfortunate part is paying for the event and for parking at the same place. The off leash dog park is usually pretty packed with little and big dogs so it's fun to watch them all run around after the same ball. The south end has some nice views on the water, but you could spend a few hours walking around and still not cover it all.

Alki is a great place to go and hang out for all different types of days and groups of people. Although it has sand, don't expect to come here and find killer waves. At night time during the summer, there are plenty of spots to have bon fires. There are a ton of rentable bikes along the sidewalks and plenty of bars and restaurants to go to. There are a few bathrooms scattered towards the end of the beach towards the miniature sized Statue of Liberty as well. You can also catch some wifi from the various shops on the beach in case you want to "work from home" during some nice weather days.

Grandview Off-Leash Dog Park is a larger park meant for all sizes of dogs down in the Kent area. It has many different placea for your dog to explore, lots of benches to sit, and a few spots with water and poop bags which is really nice. While exploring the park, it's basically a big circle you can walk or go to individual areas. There is an agility course area at the bottom, fences all over and always lots of dogs everywhere. The views here of Mount Rainier are incredible as well so I would recommend coming here if you haven't before.
likes: Availability of water and poop bags

reviews_attraction.text: This park is more of a beach as the park itself is very small. It has a lot of parking on the lower area and the bridge over the tracks and the stairs to get down create quite the view. The right side is the off leash area for dogs and the left side is the off leash area for humans. It goes pretty far down which is nice if you want to sit away from others or go for a walk along the water. The beach is also really clean, even though it's so close to places like the ferry where sometimes it can get dirty quick.

Apgar is one of a few visitor centers in Glacier National Park. This one is a bit smaller, but at the front of the western park entrance so it's easily accessible. The parking lot is pretty large, so if you plan on carpooling with people, you can drop one off at the back of the lot. The rangers here are pretty quiet though, not very chatty and stand back almost like they don't want to talk to people. Right now it's got a pop-up shop outside because of COVID, so check it out past the center itself.

Smith Tower is a pretty neat little historical spot in downtown Seattle. It has some interesting history behind it and you can find out all about it through the tour they have (which also allows you to go to the top). The elevators are super old which is cool, but the view from the top is great, and it has a little bar up there which is nice (you can also order food depending on the time of day). If you haven't been up there, it's worth the few bucks to go see the view.

The Ancient Lake trail is a nice flat, small distance, easy hike. The parking lot is pretty big, although lots of horse trailers show up and take up a lot of spots, so you may need to park on the road. About 2 miles in you'll hit Ancient Lake, which is a great spot to camp out. Underneath cliffs and in the middle of a canyon, the views here are surprisingly great for it being in eastern Washington. I would recommend everyone going out here, even if it's for a day hike.

Sunset Hill Park lives up to its name at night, a clear unobstructed view (barring any cloud cover) of sunsets going down over the Olympic mountain range. This park is very narrow running along side the road, doesn't have any bathrooms, and parking can be a pain sometimes since it's in a smaller neighborhood. With a few benches, you may be able to find a seat, but I recommend bringing your own chairs if possible just in case.

The Statue of Liberty is easily in the top 3 on the list of things to see while in NY. The history behind this is fascinating and it's a great place to bring the kids to learn. The views from here are great, and you need to take a ferry from Battery Park if you are coming from the NY side. The more expensive tickets include potential tours and even to let's to go up into the base or higher.

Magnuson Park is one of the biggest parks in Seattle. It has many fields and is on the water, so it has great views all over. Lots of parking all over the place, and a few buildings and courts where they hold various events all year long. The dog park in the back can get pretty packed and at times doesn't get cleaned by dog owners, so make sure to be careful when bringing your dog around.

Drake Park is a pretty large area along side the Deschutes Rover going through Bend. You'll frequently catch people sunbathing, tubing, swimming or just plain hanging out during the nice times of the year. This is an awesome place to go and picnic and spend some time in the sun and just in the river during those hot days. Rent some bikes and ride around too so you can catch it all.

Castle Clinton is the starting point for your journey to see the Statue of Liberty and Ellis Island from the NY side. This is where you buy tickets to get on the ferry. I recommend getting here early since lines get very long and the waits for ferries can get insane quickly in the middle of the day. This place is nice for a bathroom break too, as it has nice facilities.

One of the National Parks locations, Fort Vancouver has a lot of history behind it, but it is also a great scenic drive. The visitor center is a bit smaller than some of the other National Parks visitor centers, but the rangers inside are very knowledgeable and friendly. Make sure to stop off here if you have a National Parks Passport to get one of your stamps.

Incredible views all around. This trail can be deceiving though, so be careful. When there is inclement weather, you want to take it slow as it gets very slippery with all the run off towards the end. Lots of parking at the trailhead, and a ton of switchbacks at the beginning can really throw you for a loop, but the rewards at the end are completely worth it.

Discovery Park has many beautiful views of the surrounding areas of Seattle. It is a very large park with many amenities. Parking lots are scattered all over the place, so it's easy to get to any place quickly. Lots of trails all over and so many dogs walking around. This is a great place to watch the sunset on the sound side and can be a wonderful photo op.

Visit Bend is the information hub for Bend and a place you have to go to if you're visiting. They have a great and friendly staff, combined with amazing stuff for sale that all benefits the town and parks. They also are the last stop for the Ale Trail, visit 10 breweries in town and get a SiliPint, 110% worth struggling through 10 beers on a hot day in town.

A small little park on Mercer Island, this plot faces the Seattle side. There is a good amount of parking on the street right outside of it, and there are some benches and lots of places to throw down a blanket. It has water access for kids or dogs to jump in as well. Nice and quiet most times, so great to go read or have a quick lunch type of spot.

These statues on the dunes next to the beach have some interesting history surrounding them, literally. There are a bunch of signs up in various places telling the history of Long Beach, the local lighthouses and the town itself. Worth a walk if you plan on going to the beach anyways as these are on your way to it.

Maple Leaf Reservoir is a great park. It has a huge track to walk or run around, lots of field space, baseball fields at the bottom and tons of parking all around. They have great transportation from all over that leads you to the park, and it is well maintained as well.

What a cool little park in such a tight city. This has great views almost all around. Parking is a pain since it is always so packed, but there are always people there and lots going on. Great place to throw down a blanket and have a lunch with some friends.

Camille Park is a super clean area with a playground area, a few picnic tables and a few tennis courts. The layout is perfect, giving people space in all spots. There is a parking area on the east end with some toilets.

Was not even on my original travel plans, but I had some additional time. I would have regretted not stopping, once I got there it's an amazing sight. Well worth the small parking fee (lasts for the season). Be prepared for some stairs if you want to climb the column...and they are spiral so balance is required.

Stopped here to take some photos. Although you can't access the seminary it still is veiwable from the outside and is a rather impressive building. The trail to the shoreline e is a great walk offering really lovely scenery.

Small musuem tucked into First Hill, brings old world and new age together. Well worth the visit. Especially because admission is free, but do try and make a donation. Staff are very welcoming and helpful.

The tour through the building is well thought out and put together. Original Otis elevators add to the experience and take you to the lounge in the tower. Wood lined and intimate. A great place to stop by.

Really a great museum in Astoria. I began my Astoria adventure here and wasn't disappointed. The museum offers a wide range of interesting exhibits about maritime history and it's impact on the region.
Columbia center is a great stop if you want an amazing view of the city. Travel to the top on a clear day and it's amazing. While in the area enjoy some of the great architecture, from old to new.
Yes you have to go up the steps and pretend you're Rocky...just kidding. But a really good.museum with themes rooms. Take some extra time and walk around the grounds and see the water works.
Amazing. Be sure to go to the ticket desk and inquire about a tour. I got a one on one tour from a cast member, complete with behind the scenes detours. Definitely worth it.
Go on Saturday (once a month) and see the original equipment and take some really cool photos. You are on your own to explore but volunteers are on hand to answer questions.
If you're at Seattle Center make a stop off to see the fountain. Seems to run most days but is definitely more of a warm weather site if you want to play in the fountain.
Very informative. A full history of organised crime in the US (and somewhat abroad) all the way to the present. Added experiences are available like a crime lab.
A really beautiful place to connect with nature. Gets busy during peak hours. But if you are a photographer be on the lookout for special photography times.
Great trail, well maintained. Hiked down to the lake and it was well worth it. Be prepared...its not steep but its a long constant gradient up.
Great place to hang out, gamble, and enjoy the atmosphere. Always on my list to stop by. Lots of restaurants, and access to shopping and more.
Amazing views and down the road is Alki. Be prepared to look for parking. Or if you are there to catch the sunrise, you won't have a problem.
A great show, that’s free, that you must see. Crowds gather fast so be sure to stake out your viewpoint, especially for the nighttime shows.
Such a gem with old world charm. Definitely one of the better museums in Astoria to stop off at. Be sure to start at the carriage house.
The outside observation decks are really the draw. Interior has the history and science exhibits, but let's face it...you want the view.
Something that you have to stop by if you're going to Fremont. Consider stopping by the locks or the Nordic museum while in the area.
Amazing museum expierence. Well worth the visit. A great historical and current view of Nordic heritage and it's impact in Seattle.
A nice mix of installations. Good rotating exhibits on the top floor. Had a membership but not quite enough draw for me to renew.
A developing area, there are a lot of recreational opportunities. I always stop by for the craft fairs they have in the hanger.
Maybe I’m just not a die hard contemporary art fan, but I came away like I was missing context for a lot of the pieces.
dislikes: Lack of context for art pieces

reviews_attraction.text: Such a cool setting. Went up to get some photos and the weather broke just enough to explore the old fair buildings.
An amazing example of the gilded age. The tour was informative and revealed why and how such opulence came about.

The International Rose Test Garden is one of 24 official sites where 200 new rose cultivars are tested every year. Limited paid parking. Late spring and summer are the best times to photograph the gardens --  a living history of rose cultivation. The original rose plants are next to the tennis courts. Portland is the only city to award Gold Medals to the best new introductions each year. Pack a lunch and a blanket to enjoy the outdoor ampitheater on the grass next to the garden. Enjoy a birds-eye view of Portland, the Shakespeare Garden containing botanicals mentioned in his works, and visit the Rose Garden Store for a box of rose tea or other rose-themed items. An ADA accessible childrens play structure park is nearby.

Hillsdale City Park, hidden right off of Hwy 10 just west of the Town Center, features an enormous off-leash area for well-behaved dogs and their owners, as well as rigorous and sometimes steep walking trails through a forested area and along a creek bed. The park is open from 5 a.m. to midnight every day, and is adjacent to Robert Gray Middle School. Bowls of water are positioned around the park and kept full for furry friends.  The park is maintained by a small crew and many neighborhood volunteers. A bridge goes over the creek to the forested area. Wear your hiking shoes and take water with you. Parking is available in the back of the Portland Christian Center lot. Great escape from the city just minutes away.

Named by British sea captain James Cook in 1778, Cape Foulweather Observatory and Gift Shop is the best place for whale-watching on a clear day on the Oregon Coast. Now a state park and on the National Historic Register of Places, it was briefly a coffee shop before becoming a successful tourist gift shop in 1937. Located on a cliff 500 feet above the ocean, picture windows and telescopes allow visitors to view the whales in season and pick up a souvenir on the way out. Worth the trip.

Because there is limited parking available, it's best to walk or bike to this 12-acre park nestled in the middle of a neighborhood on the west slope of a hill in the Glencullen neighborhood near Hillsdale.  Good place for children and dogs to run free. Part of the original 1850 land claim of pioneer Albert Kelly, the park area was sold by descendents to the city in 1956. Restoration Creek had recently been restored. Access to field and play equipment is only available from SW 35th.

One of Portland's newest neighborhood parks features all-access play structure and a water feature, in addition to a trail down the hill in a natural setting. Nestled in the Multnomah neighborhood, it features a panoramic view of the West hills at sunset. It also has a Portland-style sanitary station. There is a picnic area as well as a lawn next to the water feature. Great place for a party, lunch, or evening stroll. Side-by-side slides are the grandchildren's favorite activity.

Tasting estate wines in a beautiful setting, aided by a friendly and knowledgeable staff, makes for a perfect outing any time of year. Because all of the original grapevines were removed during Prohibition, it wasn't until 1965 that Oregon wine pioneer Charles Coury planted what are now the oldest vines on the estate from Alsace and Bergundy root stock. Coury also planted an assortment of Gewürztraminer, Sylvaner, Semillon, Pinot Blanc, and Riesling.

Point Park is a primitive woodsy park with vast meadows surrounded by giant shoreline trees, where the Willamette River enters the Columbia River. Lewis and Clark explored this area. Picnic tables and viewpoints. Watch out for serious potholes on the road. Don't enter the dangerous water surrounding this park. Powerful currents, steep dropoffs and changing riverbed conditions make it dangerous and has resulted in a number of drownings.

This park is the hub of the Southwest waterfront. It is surrounded by businesses and an easy walk for residents and guests. Three blocks east is the Willamette River. The park features a water sculpture with soft tiles, performance area, plenty of lawn, and wheelchair accessible trails through the native plants areas anchoring the corners. Sound sculptures and bocce ball courts make this a relaxing and fun destination.

Pack a lunch and head out to Doran Regional Park, featuring picnic tables, restrooms, and two miles of flat beach to walk, swim, surf, fly a kite, or build sand castles. Kid and dog friendly and easy drive to Bodega Bay area. $7 day use fee per car. Drive all the way to Doran Beach at the end of the spit, then choose one of the parking areas to start your  beach adventure. Overnight camping available.

Small 3-acre park includes recently improved trails and steps that lead to a creek and a wheelchair accessible bridge where you can view the natural area. There is a another entrance for wheelchairs just north of the main entrance, but it has 15 degree slope. The improvements make SW Trails 3 and 6 accessible from Bertha Blvd. No parking on Bertha but you can park on SW Chestnut, or better yet, walk.

Smith Rock is an outdoor adventure playground. We hiked the Homestead Trail which, once you go down hundreds of feet, follows the Crooked River. Then we had to hike back up. We started at the turnaround and the views just became more amazing. One of the many must-see natural wondered of Oregon. Be sure to start your hike with plenty of water and pace yourself. #LocalGuides #OnGoogleMaps

We walked the Indian Creek Trail from the Mitchell Drive Trailhead, which was a fun, scenic and easy walk. More challenging trails, especially up to the ridge top, are also available. The Shell Ridge Recreation Area is a wonderland for locals and visitors who love hiking, biking and running with their dogs in a beautiful, inspiring setting. Be sure to pack water.

Summer and fall showcase everything Lithia Park has to offer. Stay cool under the tree canopy on a hot summer day, or enjoy the splendor of the changing colors of fall. Playgrounds for children, a lake with benches to watch the ducks, and nearby eateries -- and a play or two -- are great ways to pass the time when in Ashland.

On a clear day you can climb the 360 steps to the top of the column and see the convergence of the Columbia River with the Pacific Ocean, the state of Washington across the bay, the mountains to the ready, and the Oregon coast to the south. Parking permit is five dollars and is good for the whole year. Store located onsite.

A serene combination of formal gardens surrounding the old Kerr home, now the Episcopal Archdiocese of Oregon, and nature trails to a ridge overlooking the Willamette River and Elk Rock Island. Great for a family outing or out-of-town guests. No restroom. #LocalGuides #OnGoogleMaps #LetsGuide

Excellent soccer and baseball fields for league play, and great outdoor trails, shelters, boat launch area, playground, and picnic areas. Tigard's hidden treasure. Parking is always at a premium, and if you can park up by the football field and walk in you will save time getting out.

An oasis in the middle of Laurelhurst, this large, hilly, tree-covered park with a pond had nice trails, large open grassy spaces, and picnic tables. We attended an annual company picnic here -- the perfect spot to enjoy an evening with colleagues and friends.

A shelter offers respite from the wind to enjoy whale watching and ocean views. A beach cliff trail is wheelchair accessible. This is a great spot to take in sunsets by the beach after catching an early dinner at one of the excellent nearby restaurants.

Great fun for kids of all ages.  Explore Portland's rail yard history and see locomotives that helped settle the West. Don't miss riding the train down to Oaks Park and back. Check out the gift shop specializing in railroad merchandise.

Great meeting area for the preschool set along a walking path that encircles the park. Plenty of picnic tables, trees, basketball courts, and restroom. Baseball and soccer fields are nearby. Easy access to Vermont street.

Pioneer Courthouse Square is Portland's living room. The people and the things they do are constantly changing -- and often caught on camera from the KGW studio on the square. There is also a Starbucks on Broadway.
Great place for a picnic, and a launching point for a visit to the bamboo garden nearby, and a short hike to the Vietnam memorial, the zoo, the forestry center, and more trails.
Nice little neighborhood park for the kids to burn off some energy before heading into the library across the street. Some library events are held in the park during the summer.
See coho salmon spawning area through an underground window. Wheelchair ramp and walkways. Illustrations help you identify the species of fish on the other side of the glass.
Excellent views of the Oregon coast on the hike up to the lighthouse. Nice Beach. Great place to watch the sun set.

When going to Statue of liberty and Ellis Island Immigration museum, the only way is to take the ferry from Statue Cruises at one their locations. They have ferries going to Statue from Battery Park in Lower Manhattan and Liberty State Park In New Jersey.

Since millions of visitors visit Statue every year, it is always advisable to buy tickets. The last time we went here we bought our passes online though even then one has to go to the counter to get the actual tickets. The wait to get tickets wasn't that bad even though it was a weekend. After one has to wait in the line after collecting the tickets. The line at security moved fast.

The ferry itself is very comfortable. Even though the ferries are huge it sometimes become difficult to find a seat to sit down. The view from the ferry of lower Manhattan are very nice. They first take the ferry to Statue of Liberty and then one can wait for the next ferry to take them to Ellis Island museum.

So for $17 per person, the ride is worth checking out two of the most touristy spots in NYC!

Well I just love Governors Island , this is one few really good perks which NYC has to be offer. There is so much one can do at this island family picnics, biking or maybe just relax. I would recommend getting a bike to explore the island, there are few vendors on island which rent out bikes and surreys.

The island is very well maintained and offers amazing views of Statue of liberty, Downtown Manhattan and Brooklyn. Best way to enjoy here is to come for a day picnic with family or friends and bring your own food. We had a great time last weekend here on a day picnic. There are few food vendors on the island in the food court area though the options are limited.

FYI - To avoid buying $3-$4 bottles of water at the food court, bring your own water bottle and fill it up at the water fountain right at the island entrance, that's probably the only water fountain we were able to locate.

This is an absolute gem when it comes to museums in the city. I really adore this place. I was here for the first Target Saturdays with my friends.

There is so much to see in this museum. One should definitely arrive early to enjoy the different art works on display across different floors. There might be some lines on some floors to get into a specific section of the museum.

The DJ that night was so good. It was so much fun to see the crowd with different age groups enjoying the music. This reminded me of first Fridays at the Museum of Contemporary Art in Chicago as they used to have a similar event like this. They also sell some snacks and drinks within the premises during the event.

FYI- Arrive by 6 to get a smooth entry to the museum,when we went people were not let in after 7 due to over occupancy.

What's not to like about Whitney, nothing...this place is awesome. We came here recently to see the Andy Warhol exhibit and really enjoyed the exhibit.

We came on a friday and there was a long line to get in but the line moved fast. After making suggested donations, we checked the exhibit which is spread across multiple floors. Each floor has a different theme and we loved all the different themes. There is a small cafeteria on the top floor and there is a restaurant attached to the museum on the ground floor as well. This is perfect spot for a date night or a visit with friends.

Whitney is now one of my favorite museums in NYC and we will be back here very soon.

I know it's just a bridge but I can justify my five stars here. It's an absolute miracle of the human effort. I always admire the amount of foresight the architects had when they were building these architectural marvels. Unlike Brooklyn Bridge(BB) this bridge offers much more to the pedestrians. Separate lane for pedestrians and bikers is a big relief for pedestrians. At BB it was a constant struggle for bikers and people jogging juggling for space.

The bridge gives awesome view of the city skylines which is definitely worth watching. Hopefully coming summers I will be a regular at WB with my bike or just jogging.
likes: Separate lanes for pedestrians and bikers

reviews_attraction.text:
An absolute adorable place with so much rich history attached to it.It is located across the southern tip of Manhattan Island in New York City, the park some breathtaking views of New York Harbor.It houses the statue of John Ericsson and also the the sphere.

One can spend hours just relaxing , reading a book and taking a jog around the park. Though it is always bustling with tourists, one can definitely find a quite space in this green pasture. The name battery comes from artillery batteries that were positioned there in the city's early years.

Definitely worth visiting when one is in the hood.

A must see fountain nesteled in the heart of Grant Park. This fountain is one of the landmarks for the city of chicago and is one of the largest fountains in the world. It is built in a rococo wedding cake style and inspired by Latona Fountain at the Palace of Versailles, it is meant to allegorically represent Lake Michigan.

Every hour there is a water show which lasts for approximately 20 minutes and is really nice. It is worth enjoying the water show in the morning and late evening after sunset . The water show with the lights and music is one of the best highlights of this fountain.

A perfectly calm and serene setting nestled in the heart of village away from hustle and bustle of the city. I just simply love that. NYU students are pretty lucky to have this in the vicinity of the campus.

I love such places which help us to relax away from the concrete jungle in which we live in. Since it is close to NYU campus, it seems pretty safe too. I sat on the fountain steps which reminded me of The Millennium Park (Chicago) which also has a water flow and one can soak the feet in the cold water.Looking forward to becoming a regular visitor at the park.

An absolute awesome place to enjoy all the nice events all along the summers sponsored by the City of Chicago. Have attended some really nice events such as Ballet shows, Bhangra performance, Musicians from Nigeria and so many more. There are ample seating available for the visitors to enjoy the live performances. The event calendar is planned in such a way that they have artists from different countries and regions all across the world.

Thanks to Mayor and the City for organising all those nice events every year.

Things like Transmitter Park remind me that there are so many gems in the city which I have not yet been able to experience.

I did not even know that place even existed. My buddy  told me about about this park. While biking back from Brooklyn Bazaar we decided to check this out. This by far is one of the most non touristy spots as most of the people don't know that it exists.

It was so nice to sit by the grass and looking at the skyline. The view is really nice.

Come here and enjoy the views (tourist free) :)

Located at the tip of manhattan this is probably one of the biggest public parks in manhattan. This park is pread across 67 acres and offers some really nice views of the George Washington Bridge, New Jerey and harlem river.

The park is so huge and there is so much to see and explore here, one definitely needs a couple to visits to properly explore it. It is very well connected via public transportation. Definitely a perfect spot to bring food and spend some quality time with friends/family ona weekend picnic.

I adore this park, the green pasture surrounded by the concrete jungle.

There is so much to do/see in and around union square park. I have coming here for a while to visit the farmers's market. There is also the Christmas holiday market which surprises every year. I can spend hours sitting in this park. There is always something happening here right from artists displaying their skills on paintings and people playing some kind soothing music.It is located very conveniently close to public transportation.

One of the most sought after and best looking structures on fifth avenue!

I really love the architecture of this place.Both the exterior and interior look of the church takes one's breath away.It is a decorated Neo-Gothic-style Roman Catholic cathedral church and it is the seat of the archbishop of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of New York. This place is serene,calm and just awesome. Though it is always crowded with tourists the best time to explore this church is early morning or evening.

Even though I am writing the review after visiting it after a couple of months. But the feeling is yet to sink in. The view is so dead awesome.
Please make sure that you visit it on a day with bright sunlight. I fully agree with the fellow reviewers, this view is so much better than the one experiences at Willis Tower.

Secret : The elevator is so damm fast, it just takes you at the deck in a very short span of time.

What an awesome museum, nesteled in the most diverse part of  Queens. I really really loved Museum of Moving Image. It is such a dope spot and is very chic and beautiful.

It was a very well organized and planned museum space.Though it is not a huge museum but they have really interesting modern art pieces on display across the 2 floors.

I would definitely come back here to see the new art installations.

A great place to enjoy the modern art display. Specially the artist not be missed is Calder.Every first Friday of every month they have a social gathering. It's more fun because there is also a dance floor with DJ.

The outdoor terrace is great to strike a good conversation.The food was good.We enjoyed the  dance floor with couple of young hip hop dancers, they were just simply amazing.

Definitely a must visit spot when in sfo. Famous for having a steep, one-block section that consists of eight tight hairpin turns, it was really fun driving down Russian Hill neighborhood and onto the Telegraph Hill neighborhood. This spot is easily accesible through the cable car but I would definitely recommend driving on this street as it is one of kind experience.

One of the most sought after spot in the Millennium Park. It's a pretty damm interesting steel sculpture which attracts so much attention. Though it's name is cloud gate but it is known more as the steel bean. It looks like a steel mirror to me and it's fun to take pictures around it. The bean is designed by the world renowned sculpture artist Anish Kapoor.

It's one of the best places to enjoy the modern as well as the traditional art.There are some many things to see here right from paintings to sculptures.Modern art wing is a must see.The coffee shop is also nice.
If one does not want to spend money to go to art institute then try visiting on Thursday from 5.00 PM to 8.00 PM since entry is free on this day.

Discovered this green pasture after completing my morning jog on Williamsburg bridge.It is a great asset for Greenpoint and Williamsburg hoods in Brooklyn.It is a place where one can engage in kickball, soccer, baseball, handball, basketball, football, and tennis. It is quite big and is spread across couple of acres and is always bustling with people.

What is not to love about this epicentre of shopping, hotel and theatre district. All the major brands and also the upscale boutiques, gift shops, art galleries, and beauty salons are in Union Sqaure. The best time to come here is during the Christmas when a giant Christams tree is erected in the park with the whole squre decorated like a palace!

One of the few spots to enjoy the awesome views of GGB. Make sure to carry a good camera to capture the bridge in the background. One should be lucky to see the bridge with sunlight as most of time bridge is surrounded by fog, i was able to enjoy the view with sunlight and fog both on the same day!

Amazing views of NYC Skyline, Statue of Liberty and miles & miles of lush green park. I love riding my bike here specially till the end of boardwalk. Compared to other parks specially in NYC this is still relatively less crowded. Definitely a must visit place for locals as well as tourists.

One of the best spots city has to offer :

* Bring a sheet
* Make sure to bring Frisbee
* A great spot for people watching
* Bring food and then eat it for next few hours(lazy afternoons) :)

One can never get bored at this spot!

One of the most touristy spots in SFO boosts -

* A lot of decent seafood restaurants
* Good views of the harbour
* Lot of shopping spots
* A great place to visit with family and friends

Overall a decent place to visit in town!

The Apollo Theater is legendary. Do make it uptown to Harlem. It's actually not very far as you can take an express train there and most shows start early. One to definitely catch is Amateur Night on Wednesdays. It's just like what they used to show on tv but live in the flesh. Expect a range of talent from singing to dancing, all ages, and some not so talented. It's pretty funny and the energy will get you pumped. The theater itself is old, but restored, and in great shape. Lots of history in the place. You can feel it. Stay in town for a late bite. The whole area is pretty much gentrified and there is such great soul food around.
likes: Activities: Amateur Night, Variety of Talent, Energetic
