reviews_attraction.text: Washington Square Park is one of my favorite parks in NYC! It's gorgeous with the arc and fountain. On the weekends it is full of life with street performers and people lounging. Actually during the week, it is pretty bustling too with all the students. I like to grab a falafel from Mamoun's and eat it in the park. The place has cleaned up greatly in the last 10 years. Sure the fountain moved and there is still quite a few homeless and dealers roaming around, but crime is down and security is watching. Did I mention it is possibly haunted?
likes: Cultural Value: Street Performers, Historical Elements (arc, fountain)
Facilities & Services: Food Availability (falafel from Mamoun's)

reviews_attraction.text: Visiting the Statue of Liberty at least once is a must! Bring all your tourist friends and family here because it is New York. I have been a few times in my life and have never went up to the crown. They are letting people go up there again but you have to reserve months in advance. I also just finally went to Ellis Island for the first time. Usually I bypass it to save time. Well worth a visit. Tickets for the ferry is a short line but waiting to get on the boat could take hours. Dress warm because it is cold. Go as early as possible.

The Queens Museum is such a hidden gem of NYC. This museum is a must see if you are going to spend the day at Flushing Meadows Corona Park. Set aside an hour and a half for this museum. It recently went through a renovation and the new layout is fantastic and perfect for events and parties. Nonetheless, it is still a museum and the panorama and World's Fair memorabilia is so important to the history of NYC. There are also small exhibits and other maps to check out.

Longwood Gardens is ranked high up there with Butchart Gardens and Keukenhof. It is a must see. There are many parts to the gardens, a little something for everyone from waterfalls and a conservatory to towers and tree houses. I was really surprised at how well everything was kept. One disappointment I had was that there was just more grass than anything. Wish there were more flowers. Buy an extra ticket for late night concerts and water fountain shows.

If you have one chance during the Summer to go to Governors Island, take it! Hop on that free ferry and have a little break from Mahattan. You can even take your bike or rent on on the premises to take a ride around. The island is small enough so that you can walk it. There is plenty of lawn to relax or have a picnic. This is an excellent date idea. Also, every weekend there is some sort of activity on the island.

Sutro Baths are a must see if you like urban exploring. It's part of San Francisco's history and you could see the ruins. Wear good shoes when you come here as the hike is steep and can be slippery. The views are lovely and on a clear day you can see the Golden Gate Bridge. If you keep walking you will eventually find yourself walking through a cave. Hear the ocean waves crash and you might even get a little wet.

Ground Zero is so moving. You could just stand there and feel something in the air. It can be emotional. The fountain is really beautiful. All the victims names are etched into it. You have to get a reservation for the timeslot you are visiting. It’s very organized and easy. Make sure you go to the bathroom before you visit. There is none onsite and you will be in line and going through security for awhile.

I love Governors Island and the fact that New Yorkers get to visit it for free every Summer. The ferry ride is quick and lots of fun. There is plenty of room for bikes and strollers, just get there early. There are always different events happening every week, so check the calendar. They just opened up the new slide area and have a working farm now. Bring a ziploc bag because they give away their herbs.

You gotta use Flushing Meadows Corona Park in order to love it. Do you play soccer? BBQ? Picnic? Bike ride? I bike around the park for an hour or so every week in the Summer. Lots of trails to zig zag around in. It's a great work out. Flushing Meadows Corona Park is full of life. Usually there are festivals, parades, and marathons. Keep a dollar handy so you can buy an ice cream from one of the vendors.

We visited the Edgar Allan Poe house at the request of our 15 year old. The house turned out to be a great little museum. There was a short movie in the beginning, an informative timeline of Poe's career, and we were free to roam the house. The best was the creepy basement. Use your imagination. This house is free to enter and the rangers are very knowledgeable and friendly.

Monterey Bay Aquarium has so much to offer. If you are every in the Bay Area, make the drive and check it out. The town is relaxing and slow paced. It will be a nice break from the city. Be warned, the crowds come out in droves. Tons of children so have patience if you want to see the fish. If you don't want to pay for parking, park a few blocks away in the residential area.

The New York Hall of Science is an excellent place, and not just for kids! It's very educational and the grounds are state of the art. Great overhaul of the building. I visited during the Maker Faire and everything was very organized. Carve out a good three hours for this place. You will be mesmerized and then your brain will start to hurt from all the coolness.

Who knew NJ had waterfalls? This is a great stop of you are passing through or just want to appreciate some nature and forget about the city. The area is small but we'll maintained and the viewing area is plenty big for everyone. The falls are loud and spray water everywhere. It's part of the fun. No need to drive all the way to Niagara. This is good enough.

If you like exploring, go to Fort Tilden. It's far so if you have a car it'd be ideal to travel here. The beach is lovely. Went in off peak season so I am not sure how the Summer crowds are. In the winter, you could get lucky and get some sunshine. The grounds are desolate and empty but the abandoned buildings and fort are really something to wander about.

Battery Park has great views of the water. It's the meeting place to catch the ferry for Statue of Liberty and Ellis Island. There are a few play areas for children, some volley ball courts, and lots of walking paths. Unless you want to go to the Statue or live in the area I wouldn't exactly call this a destination.

I was a tourist for the day and took the NBC Studio Tour. It’s actually very cool to see the behind the scenes. I would have loved to see things while filming and what not but you basically tour when everything is closed. See the studio of Jimmy Fallon, SNL, Dr. Oz, etc. My favorite is the Jim Henson muppet corner.

Everyone should make it a point to visit the Cloisters. What a wonderful day trip. Pack a lunch and spend some time at Fort Tryon Park. It’s very easy to get to on the subway. The Cloisters is a magical place. It’s like going back in time. My favorite is the garden in the middle. It’s very peaceful.

Gorgeous park in Long Island City with views of Manhattan. They have really done a great job in renovating this area and they are still building it out more! There is a fantastic playground for children, lots of hammocks in the Summertime, and tons of adirondack chairs. It's actually quite fancy!

This is the people's bridge! Brooklyn Bridge is for the tourists! Manhattan Bridge connects Chinatown in Manhattan to DUMBO in Brooklyn. You get gorgeous views of everything and it is quite a walk and workout. Make sure you walk on the pedestrian side so you don't get run over by the bikers.

Excellent park in Brooklyn. It's comparable to Central Park and there is much to do from view a fireworks show and attend a concert to ride your bike and have a picnic. Lots of people take their wedding photos here. I don't blame them. It is a nice park.

I love this art filled park. There is always something going on. The park is not so big, it's more of a walk through park but if you are passing by and need a break there are many benches to rest on. Also, this is the home to the original Shake Shack!

Perhaps the Brooklyn Botanic Garden is most famous for their Cherry Blossom Festival. Even without the Cherry Blossoms, the grounds are kept very nice and are beautiful. Lots of picture taking opportunities and space for kids to run around in.

Roosevelt Island is a residential island and park. There are also hospitals and a few restaurants on it. It is fully functioning accessible by F train subway and the Roosevelt Island tram. Great place for a bike ride and bbq.
Madison Square Garden is so New York! It's a great place to watch a concert, hockey game, or basketball game. It's huge. Prices are expensive but worth it.

Nice little trail! Could use some upkeep in some sections though. This part is free to access even though box canyon waterfall charges $5. You might have to park somewhere along the highway if the box canyon parking is full though. Some of the stairs on the trail are a little rundown. Ice is all melted for the season but still a beautiful little hike through the rocks with a view of the mountains! Dog friendly too. This is a loop hike that leads to a bridge that crosses the creek where you can see the dam too. Supposedly the  loop trail on the west side is closed at some point due to fire mitigation but the nicer part of the trail with the views is on the east (highway side) anyways! If you have time, take the detour and follow the signs for the ouray perimeter trail. It will cross highway 550 and take you to the other side and take you up even higher for even nicer views!

$7 for a day pass but there are miles and miles of trails ! We did a 6.5 mile loop (many trails connect and loop to each other). Pretty creek in the canyon . Trails along the creek at the canyon bottom and rim trail along the edge of the canyon . Old dam you can hike to as well! Many nice lookouts . Enjoyable hike . Playground for kids near parking area. Some restroom. Dog friendly and rock climbing areas too.

Definitely a must do at least once ! Pricy but worth it . Property is extensive and there is a lot to see . You can get through the house tour on a self guided tour within an hour but if you do the extra museums and car rooms and planes you will need an extra few hours! So much to see!

Not sure why they would still charge when the part of the trail to even see the falls is closed for construction. You can hear the falls and see them partially and still walk into the canyon on the trail, but you cannot get up close to the falls or see the part hiding behind the rock.

Loved this state park! Only $8, well maintained,picnic areas, nice campsiteson the river, restrooms. Easy walking trail to falls and caves! Can hike to top of falls and do some longer trails to fish hatcheries if looking for more of a hike.  Lots of people were fishing too!

Amazing service, great selection, yummy wine and cheese! Your tasting can even include slushies, mead, and other non wine choices! The servers there are always very friendly. Vibe is great! When weather is nice, patio is lovely! I have been twice with their groupon now!

Awesome place to learn about the grist mill and see how it worked in the past . They have it still running with actual corn so you can see how it produces cornmeal and flour  . They use it now to feed animals ! Beautiful area with historic buildings . Small store .

Awesome park . Beautiful in the months after winter when the park is driveable but you can still see snow everywhere . Be sure to do the cinder cone hike at the other area of the park ! Bumpass hell area closed until December but sulphur works area was cool!

Pretty area right downtown for some nature time . 11.2 miles of trail alongside the river. One side is for pedestrians and other is for biking  and roller blading . All paved . Pretty, clean creek and dog friendly ! Walk alongside the city skyline!

Super easy hike . Much less distance than the 3/4 mile distance posted . There is a ridge hike at the end too if you want to extend your hike . Currently the middle falls lookout and stairs to the base of the big falls are closed due to damage !

Best dog park ive been to in the springs yet! Huge, great for walking on trails. Nice creek through the middle.  Beautiful park compared to just dirt parks i have been to. Water provided. Training area for dogs here too. Small dog area also!

Fun to support a local place by eating pies and other goods while experiencing some history within a national park! Everything is made local from the orchards on their land! Nice picnic area out front near horses to enjoy the view and food.

Awesome hike varieties! We did the 9 mile hidden passage loop with lots of random other pff trail sections. Good mix of cliffs, rocks, tunnels, caves and waterfalls! We got soaked in the rain the whole time but pretty wooded hike
likes: Natural features (cliffs, rocks, tunnels, caves, waterfalls)

reviews_attraction.text: Pretty area! Lots of trails , but not much walking to the actual painted hills if you don’t want to walk far. Be careful walking around on the actual rock areas because it’s slippery with loose rocks .
Great little dog park. Mostly sand, no grass. Some dog training items . Size is great though and always lots of dogs ! Nearby a playground for kids, walking path and frisbee golf course
Awesome place for a walk! Plenty of parking and so many trails so there’s no problem with crowding . Beautiful views  of pikes peak and garden of the gods ! Easy to get to as well
3 trails. 2 mile loop, .6 mi loop,  2.1 mile one way ridge trail. Nice and wooded. Lots of leaves. No viewpoints or anything but nice peaceful trail and dog friendly
Definitely great place to go to get a good look inside a piece of history. Great knowledgeable guides and not touristy so you get a good small tour.
Easy 1/4 mile hike to the waterfall. Completely frozen in the winter so you can walk directly on frozen creek to the frozen icefall, super pretty !
Easy 1/4 mile hike to the waterfall. Completely frozen in the winter so you can walk directly on frozen creek to the frozen icefall, super pretty !
Awesome park. Dog park area, kids playground, grassy fields, frisbee golf course, nice walking path, bmx course! Nesr the high school
Great park by the beach for kiddos! Lots of grass, great for pets and picnics ! Paid parking until 5pm, either meter or pay by space
call for open skate hours because the calendar online isn't accurate. we had a blast ! groupon deal online is great.
My favorite dog park! So big, bags for waste, water, lots of trees, trails, creek, lots of dogs/people to meet!
Closed when we went due to flooding :( if it rains , they need four hours for flooding to clear up.

(Translated by Google) St. Patrick Cathedral in Manhattan Middletown. The style is neo-gothic. If Trinity is the oldest, this is the largest. Moreover, it is the largest in the United States. It was completed at the end of the 19th century over nearly 40 years. Stained glass with beautiful vertical saints was properly photographed. It's a classic New York sightseeing 😀 The steeple is cool. It's the only place in New York that feels strange and familiar to us ... a strange space between buildings. St. Patrick is an Irish saint who, as you know, promoted Christian missions through the integration of Celtic and Catholicism. March 17 is St. Patrick's Day for many Irish land.

マンハッタン・ミドルタウンのセントパトリックカテドラルです。様式はネオゴシック。トリニティが最古なら、こちらは最大となります。しかも全米最大です。40年近くをかけて19世紀末完成しました。聖人たちの姿が縦型美しいステンドグラスはきちんと写真に収めました。ニューヨーク観光の定番中の定番ですね😀　尖塔がかっこいいです。ここだけがニューヨークの中で異彩な感じでもあり、馴染んでいるようでもあり…ビルの狭間の不思議な空間です。セントパトリックはご存知のようにケルトとカトリックの融和によりキリスト教布教を推し進めたアイルランドの聖人です。アイルランド系の多い土地では３月１７日がセントパトリックスデーとなります。

If you have money, you will be happy to live comfortably in low-rise condos in Roosevelt Island than Manhattan ~ (^. ^) The rich are likely. Black decoration is given to the upper end of the bridge, and it is a chic and elegant impression.

ご存知、マンハッタンからルーズベルト島そしてロングアイランドに至る橋です。有名なブルックリンブリッジより日本人観光客は少ないですが、トラムもあり中々の観光スポット。お金があればマンハッタンよりルーズベルトアイランドの低層コンドとかで、ゆったり暮らすのも幸せですね〜(^｡^) お金持ちがおおそう。橋の上部先端に黒い装飾が施されていて、シックでお淑やかな印象です。

There is no help for it, because there is not 200m… Is the observatory lower? This is 270m. It will be about the same height as the observation deck of Abeno Harukas in Osaka. You can see everything from Mount Rainier to Elliott Bay because of the 360 ​​° view.

701 5thアベニューにあるコロンビアセンタービルディングです。シアトルの展望台はここが一番高いですよー。はるか向こうにスペースニードルがめちゃ低く見えます。それもしょうがないですね、200mありませんから…展望台はもっと低いかな。こちらは270mあります。大阪のあべのハルカスの展望台と同じぐらいの高さでしょう。360℃ビューなので、マウントレニアからエリオット湾まで全部見えちゃいますよ。

(Translated by Google) Take a leisurely stroll through Charles River Esplanade. You can see this hatch memorial shell in front of the lagoon if you walk while looking at Longfellow Bridge on the right back. MIT is on the opposite side (front). It ’s the best environment. The shell type has a structure with good sound. I want to listen to something with good melody, not noisy music.

チャールズリバーエスプラナードをのんびりと散策。右手後方にロングフェロー橋を見ながら歩くと、ラグーンの手前にこのハッチメモリアルシェルが見えてきます。対岸の先（前方）にはMITが。最高な環境ですね。シェル型は音響がいいような構造になってるんでしょうね。うるさい音楽じゃなく、メロディのよいモノが聴きたいところです。

(Translated by Google) This is an observation deck with a 360-degree view. Located on the upper floor of the Prudential Center building. The name is also good, Skywalk. The Prudential Center itself has a mall so you can eat home on the way home. I came in the daytime, but the night view seems of course wonderful. The observation deck space is on the 50th floor of the building.

360度ビューの展望台です。プルデンシャルセンターのビル上階にあります。名前もスカイウォーク、いいですねぇ。プルデンシャルセンター自体がモールがあるので、帰りにご飯も食べて帰れます。自分は昼間に来ましたが、夜の景色はもちろん素晴らしいようです。ビルの50Fが展望台スペースです。

The nearby pedestrian crossing was a rainbow. Is this neighborhood an LGBT friendly area? There is a luxurious tomb at Greenwood Memorial Park. Let's match the fans!

Brick Art Materialsという店の前にあるジミヘンの銅像です。多分この店が作ったのかな？銅像はかなりエキサイトしてイナバウワってます。近くの横断歩道がレインボーになっていました。この辺はLGBTフレンドリーな地区なのかな？Greenwood Memorial Parkに豪華なお墓があります。ファンは合わせていきましょう!

(Translated by Google) Park Street Church where a beautiful white tower shines in the blue sky during the day. Although it is a small church, it is a venerable church next to Boston Common. In 1829, it will be the memorial place where Garrison made the first speech against slavery before the United States. The church itself was completed in the early 19th century.

白く美しい塔が昼間は青空に映えるパークストリートチャーチ。小さな教会となりますがボストンコモンに隣りあう由緒ある教会です。1829年、この前で合衆国初となる奴隷制反対の演説がガリソンにより行われた記念すべき場所となります。教会自体は19世紀初頭に竣工したものとなります。

(Translated by Google) This is the Broad Art Museum that just opened in September 2015. Eri & Edith Broad's private property was invested, and admission is free. 2000 pieces of contemporary art are on display. In Japan, companies sometimes have such museums, but usually they are charged. This is what true social contribution means.

2015年9月にオープンしたばかりのブロード美術館です。エリ&エディス･ブロードさんご夫妻の私財を投じたもので、入場料は無料。現代アート2000点が展示されています。日本も企業がこういったミュージアムをする場合がありますが、たいてい有料。本当の社会貢献とはこういうコトを言うんでしょうね。

(Translated by Google) Coit Tower on Telegraph Hill. We can come even if we walk, but think that it is a little bit. There seems to be a bus. I came in the night with my friend's car, but the lights were beautiful and shining white. Please note that the observation deck closes in the evening. It's pretty big. There seems to be 64m.

(Original)
テレグラフヒルの上に建つコイトタワーです。歩いても来れますがちょいシンドイと思います。バスがあるみたいです。わたしは友人の車で夜に来ましたがライトアップが美しく、白く輝いていました。ただ展望台は夕方にクローズするので、ご注意ください。結構デカイです。64mあるそうです。

(Translated by Google) Old South Meeting House. Local people seem to be connected with Old South simply. I think it will be the oldest structure in America built in 1729. It is not a church but it is a gathering place for puritan. There is also a museum. A great staple of Boston tourism (o ^ ^ o)

(Original)
Old South Meeting Houseです。現地の方はシンプルにOld Southで通じるみたいです。1729年に建てらたアメリカでは最も古い建造物になるかと思います。教会ではありませんが、ピューリタンのための集会所です。ミュージアムも併設されています。ボストン観光の大定番(o^^o)

(Translated by Google) Of course, the scenery is good and the height is high, but there is no personal impression. Ashizuri, Muroto, Cape Shionomisaki have a great view. There are two reasons why I came here. It was this that I was looking at the Golden Gate from here and that it was the shooting location for various movies.

もちろん景色は良いし、高さもありますけれど、さほど個人的には感動はなし。足摺や室戸、潮岬の方が絶景感は大きいです。私がココに来た理由は二つ。ココからゴールデンゲートをながめることと、いろんな映画の撮影地になっていること、これでした。

I think it is a popular spot. I felt relieved that there was a little oriental gravestone atmosphere in the western cemetery. Easily.

It ’s not bad, but it ’s the difference between China ’s glaring and hectic shape.
It's nice to see it from nearby, but when you can see it from the streets of Lower Manhattan, it feels like the beauty stands out.
I like it more than Empire State (o ^^ o)

悪気はありませんが、中国のギラギラしたヘンテコな形のビルとは雲泥の差。
近くから見るのもいいんですが、ローワーマンハッタンの通りからチラッと見える時に、美しさが際立つような気がします。

(Translated by Google) This is Trinity Church in Boston. Although it is in Copley Square, a small green area, it is in the middle of the city, so it is already surrounded by high-rise buildings. It is next to the famous John Hancock Building and Boston Library. Completion is said to be at the end of the 19th century.

(Original)
ボストンのトリニティチャーチです。小さい緑地のコプリースクエアにはありますが、街のど真ん中にあるので、すでに高層ビルに取り囲まれてます。有名なジョンハンコックビルとボストン図書館に隣あってます。竣工は19世紀末だそうです。

(Translated by Google) It is a magnificent city hall. In Japan, there is a debate about rebuilding, but since the United States has a strong desire for old things, it will cherish such things. It's already a valuable building, but another 100 years? Do you have it? Over time, cultural value will increase.

(Original)
重みのある立派な市庁舎です。日本なら建て替え論議がでるところですが、アメリカは古いものの憧れが強い分、こういうものを大切にするのでしょう。すでに価値ある建築物ですが、更に100年？もつかな？経つとさらに文化的価値も高まります。

(Translated by Google) This is wonderful. It seems to be terrain made by past volcanic activity. There was a cave, but it was not a limestone cave, but a hollow due to water erosion. It seems that the day has been shallow since it became a national park. A full day drive is possible from San Francisco.

(Original)

When coming from Commonwealth Avenue it was directly in front of you. It seems to be just in the center of the park.

(Translated by Google) Painted lady who appeared in Baymax. I was thinking about it now, but it was nice to come. Everything is just colorful at sunset. There were many other tourists. You can take the best shot from Alamo Square.

(Translated by Google) It seems that at the end of the 18th century copper was affixed to the dome, but later changed to gold leaf. Shines beautifully when illuminated by sunlight.

(Translated by Google) This historic park was built in the first half of the 19th century. There were many statues and it was a wonderful atmosphere. I can spend a day here.

19世紀前半に整備された由緒ある公園です。銅像もたくさんあって素晴らしい雰囲気でした。1日でもここで過ごせそうです。

(Translated by Google) If you are a Bostonian, you must come here. It seems that the amount of water is adjusted at Charles River Dam near the river mouth.

The John Harvard statue is most certainly the most photographed at the University.  You will even see crowds waiting for their chance to stand in front of the statue.  It is easy to find located just inside the gates to the Harvard Yard.  The campus is beautiful so you may want to expand your walking tour to see some of the other sites including a very impressive library where you may be able to determine who John Harvard actual was or was not.

The Key West was an unexpectedly fun find.  On a clear day you can have 360 views standing outside the lighthouse beacon.  For those who have a fear of heights, this may not be your thing as there is very little room to maneuver.  Also, the only way up a through a spiral staircase which requires some exertion.  However, the reward is worth it.  You can also tour the museum which has some history on the lighthouse and its operation.

Here is something different.  When in Key West you cannot spend all your days in Sloppy Joes or the myriad of other bars.  The Key West Butterfly provides for a pleasant moment and break from the usual.  I was surprised at just how many butterflies were in the green house some a beautiful color blue as well as orange.  It is fun to walk around and see these creatures on various flowers.  Not too expensive and a nice diversion.

Pompano Beach has a nice Pier.  It feels sturdy and is wide so you do not feel like you are crunched against all the walkers.  The pier offers decent views of Pompano Beach and from a distance the lighthouse.  There is no charge for people just walking on the Pier.  You will also find some fishing for which there is a charge.  Parking can be difficult but there are limited metered spots.

This Club is sandwiched between the White House and  George Washington  University.  It is a private club but open to the public during certain hours.  The historic building is worth the visit and you can visit certain rooms that have art hanging on the walls.  You can also use the facilities for events.  If you enjoy art and a quiet atmosphere this is a very nice venue.

The Hemingway House tour should be a required part of any visit to Key West.  I particularly recommend the guided tour as you learn some much more about the author.  Much like Hemingway’s life, the house is quirky with its cats and a basement in Florida where they do not exist.  The house is an oasis and the yard alone is relaxing.  This is worth the cost of a tour.

Tucked just steps away from the White House the Renwick Gallery is a gem of creativity.  Outside you may find many protests and tourists, but inside the gallery creates artistic exhibits that very depending on the show.   The gallery building is interestIng to walk in by itself.  It is not so much a traditional paint canvas gallery but focused on exhibits.

The Hillsboro Inlet Park is a tiny park offering some of the best views of the lighthouse.  From the park you can look across the water and view the skinny lighthouse which dates back to 1907 or so.  Parking is very limited and it is metered.  Tip:  Go early if you want parking.  There are some benches to sit on if you just want to enjoy some sunshine.

There are a number of reasons to like the International Spy Museum.  First, it is in a brand new building which feels so much more spacious than the old one.  You are also able to get some details on spy incidents that you have heard about such as some big double crosses!  It’s a fun way to spend the afternoon esp if it is hot and humid outside in DC.

If you are looking for a Florida fine sand beach you will need to go there.  Mowry Beach offers the Maine Coast and the pebble filled beaches.  Most amazing are the tides which are some of the strongest in the world.  When low, the beach looks like a mud flat.  You will see the local clammers in force during the low tide.  The scene is quite unique.

Boston has such great history and the Paul Revere House is part of that history.  It is on the North End and the house is unique.  It is wood and not very large located around other buildings.  You may miss it if you are not paying attention.  Nonetheless it is worth the visit and the sense of history that will come back when you seek t.

While the museum may be closed inside, the grounds and gift shop are open.  This is truly a grand house and appears to be well taken care of as a museum.  The mansion is a brownstone built in 1860 and it initially served as a summer home.  It was made of Italianate brick.  I enjoyed the large windows and scale of the home.

This is a great light house to visit. More importantly, it is the easternmost spot in the United States.  This is a spot where you want to place your toe or entire foot on the ground.  There is a plaque to mark the spot.  Nearby, is a very scenic state park.  Of course, you can enjoy  the lighthouse which is red and white.

I did not visit Lubbock with the intention of going to the Wind Museum, but I am very glad I did.  This visit was a great education on the role of windmills for farming, trains, mills and power.  I had no idea.  In addition to the windmills they have a huge related model train display and intricate doll houses.  Who knew!

Beautiful grounds with interesting art objects on the national mall.  I am sure there is a theme but you will find everything from tin trees to rabbits with very large ears.  It’s right off the mall and very accessible.  If you are visiting the mall this is a pleasant place to come by and relax from all your walking.

This park adds to the City feel in a very positive way.  You have a performance center which would be great for outdoor music.  You have plenty of grass to relax on during your visit.  I wish they had some more benches because I had to complete with the homeless to find one.  On a nice day it can be very relaxing.

The Air Force memorial is on a hill with some decent vista of DC.  The sculpture has three spires in the sky which is inspiring.  There is not much beyond that but the memorial is fun to see up close.  Of course, you can also visually see it from the road.  There is a grassy hill to sit but no formal seating.

With all the hustle bustle in Bar Harbor, Village Green offers a green respite in the middle of the central commercial corridor.  There are some benches and some memorials to view within the park.  You may just to sit down and soak up some sun.  You cannot help to run through the park if you are in town.

The Portland Observatory is of historic significance.  The observatory was built in 1807 it served to communicate with ships providing two way communications.  There were both a telescope and signal flags that were used in the day.  The observatory is worth a visit as it is iconic to Portland.

The Cathedral is a towering structure in Portland.  The Cathedral was build in the 1860s and serves as an example of Gothic Revival.  You can develop an appreciation for the sheer size of the building during a walk on the grounds.  Note the many windows, which I found to be interesting.

There is something profound about this memorial.  It seems understated, but as you walk in the wall keeps going and going.  Name after name after name.  If you are visiting the Mall this is one memorial you cannot miss.  It is within easy walking distance from the Lincoln Memorial.

What a great way to get your exercise done!  The shore path offers excellent views of Frenchman’s Bay.  The path is easy to navigate and offers several different locations to take photographs.  It is also located near the harbor so there is easy access from the town.

The World War II is a grand monument combining a statues with water.  It is almost a lesson just walking around and noting all the states involved in this war effort.  The monument is closest to the Washington Monument when you are touring the Mall area.

Who would not like a seal like Andre protecting the beautiful Rockport Harbor.  Andre you will find surrounded by flowers (though I believe the seal would prefer fish).  It makes for a nice stroll if you are down in the harbor.

Davenport House is a great chance to see a historic building right in the heart of downtown Savannah.  The house also has some decent gardens and a gift shop.  You can get a feel of what the old south may have been in its time.

Great hike/bike trail that runs just over 10 miles one way with a place to camp in the woods. Park had a nice designated, paved bike path which flows over hills making for a nice ride or walk. Tons of grassy knolls, places to BBQ, and play the day away. Also a nice, clean Marina and loads of places to explore by water via boat, kayak, paddle board. Great stop! Watch out for the racoons though we saw at least 5 (4 in a pack and 1 solo). Also, watch your speeds in and out of the park...tons of deer!

Eugene could be a mecca of awesomeness but there are just too many homeless lounging around, living in all the parking lots and open areas. I was amazed to see vehicles on cinder blocks in the park parking lots in the area. It ruins the entire grounds. The trails would be so amazing if they just cleaned this place up! Maybe I just got tired of being approached by beggars and people trying to sell me things from jewelry to fake arrowheads. Either way, just not for me.

Easy rental or BYO board, some days setup for kayaks, other days surfing..or just have fun and play. The water is cool which feels great on a hot day or bring a wet suit if you got one or don't like cold water. I recommend water shoes of any kind because it is a bit shallow and you can scrape up your knees/legs/feet. Some kids had on PFDs but not required use your own common Sense on that one. Awesome fun to play or watch!

We went not expecting much with a plan to spend the day and ended up spending 4 days. Great mountain biking if you have the courage to brave the annoying people stopping in the middle of the road to take photos of the buffalo. The bison were rather chill if you respect their space. I recommend the ride down to the ranch museum. The bugs are a nightmare so bring bug repellant or long sleeved everything!

The locals call it "the ditch" but we had a GREAT time out here. Not super crowded, great wind for kayak sailing. Sometimes not great wind perfect for kayaking, kayak fishing, or SUP. Quiet. Nice place to swim and cool off. Worth the $6 to get in if you plan on spending the day! Clean area, picnic tables, and well manicured. Also, nice place to watch the sun set.

This is more a review of the entire Row River Trail. WOW. What a treat! We had a great ride from the Trailhead Park in Cottage Grove and rode to Harms Park. If you ever have a chance to experience the trail, it is a MUST! Fairly flat, super easy, and one of Oregon's best kept secrets!!! Will do again if we are ever in Oregon!

Great place to kayak and explore all the water ways, bike on one of the trails (intermediate/advanced), hike, there is a mountain bike skills course, ATV/dirt bike trail, lots of fishing opportunities, outdoor galore! Also RV park (minimal amenities) but nice spots. Overall, great place to spend a weekend!

Much to crowded for my taste, but a beautiful hike in and water bluer than blue. We hiked in from Sahalie Falls which made it roughly a 10.5 mile hike (round trip). Fairly easy terrain. The trail was flooded in 1 area but a downed tree helped us to get across. Great place if you can beat the rush!

Shooting range, so if you're looking for peace and quiet, it can get annoying. But the area itself is fantastic with lots of places to explore. We've taken our bikes out here several times to just get lost in nature. Gets a little soggy after a few good rains so beware.

Awesome views. Great picnic spots-moderately private with fantastic views of the ocean. Not a lot of spots though, so you'd need to get there early! Lots of trails in the area. Did I mention...BEAUTIFUL views!

GREAT stop. Pleasantly surprised by the St. George Desert Garden. Nice walking paths showcasing native flora. Next to the St. George Narrows and Red Rocks. Lots of seating and places to relax. Loved it!
Nice beach, not too crowded. Could drive down, put kayaks or SUP in, and then park. Nice views. Looked like there were tons of trails (biking/walking/hiking) in the area as well. Beautiful drive.
Possibly one of my favorite parks ever! Wonderful place to bike, walk, enjoy the water. I went during the week and it was not crowded. Stunning views and a great way to enjoy a day out in Boise!
Something for everyone. Very popular place for skateboarding, soccer, picnics, racing your remote controlled car, accessing the Bear Creek Trail, baseball/softball and much much more!!!
Great place to get lost and explore. If open, devil's icebox is a must on a hot day. Nice for stair climbing or hiking up the rocks. Perfect for hanging out with family or friends.
Friendly volunteers who taught us a lot about the area and birds. Thank you Larry and Jessica! Excellent place to take a stroll, birdwatch (of course!), or take a short bike ride.
Beautiful building and grounds, I'm not allowed to go in, but the area is quite beautiful in the fall. A nice stop on the way to Red Rocks and the main drag off Main St.
A nice place to wander around, read/listen about Anne Frank (listening is available in multiple languages), meditate, get lost in a book, have lunch, and be peaceful.
My favorite area on campus. Play Frisbee, meet new people, nap in the sun. This spot has it all. A must visit section of campus if you're visiting from out of town.
An endless outdoor paradise. PLEASE STAY OFF OF THE TRAILS WHEN IT IS WET AND MUDDY!!!!! Understand your role in helping to maintain the condition of the trails!
Nice two tiered parking, bridge to link forum traffic to MKT and perfect to choose from going left to Katy Trail or right into downtown.
Nice place to unwind, people watch, read, throw out a hammock, or climb on the rocks by the creek. Nice place for young or old alike.
Nice place to hang out, people watch, enjoy the local biking and walking trails, have a picnic. Dog park and skate park area nearby.
Great experience! A must see if in Boise. Fantastic photo ops, interesting history, inexpensive, and more fun than I ever imagined!
No matter what you believe in...the Temple Square is a must stop if you're in the area. Absolutely beautiful at night!

Great nature center with many exhibits of live animals and plants as well as interactive exhibits focused on simple (and fairly advanced) aspects of local environment. Friendly staff are always willing to help and teach at learner's level. Especially recommend the live bee hive and tadpole touch pond. Wheelchair and stroller users will appreciate then powered door; there is also an elevator and accessible bathrooms. The library is great for an indoor view for reading or writing. A large activity room hsots events throughout the year. No fees beyond park entry. Several trails take off from here and there is foot and small boat water access at this location as well. Would recommend allotting 45 minutes to 3 hours to explore the exhibits depending.

Danville's city park is popular for it's kid friendly creek, swimming pool with slides, and concerts at the amphitheater. There are several playgrounds throughout, basketball courts, little league and adult diamonds, and little league football fields. Strollers and wheelchairs users will find the paved loop around the park a good way to get near to most features. A trail system into the woods provides more rugged adventure. Bring a change of clothes and towels because your kids will definitely find joy in the ankle-to-knee deep (typically) creek. The park connects on the north side via unpaved path to the Blanton House and Retreat Center grounds.

A one block nature park with birding view porch, 2-3 trails, a creek, and gravel parking lot. There are two trail loops which are district and of quite different character. The linger is an infrequently shaded,, mowed field grass, flat, wide trail suitable to walkimg, jogging or the stoller pusher willing to put their back into it. The more northern trail is over a creek, shaded by tall trees, single track with risk for poison ivy appropriate for walking, jogging. The trailhead has a gravel lot and a small hut with birding and local park info. The park is well maintained, has little traffic, and even less litter.

One of the most popular Indiana State parks, largely because of the most rugged trails. This park is split by a large creek and features a suspension bridge, nature center, outdoor pool with slides, lodge, and trails requiring ladder climbed and Creek stomping. Would highly recommend for families, birding, and weekend adventures. Campgrounds are typical gravel drive with fire ring and dirt for a tent. Wheelchair and stroller users will find most paths unaccessible but there are a days worth of paths for each. Remember to pack-in-pack out your trash and don't bring firewood across county lines!
dislikes: Inaccessible paths for wheelchairs and strollers

reviews_attraction.text: An amazing little local gem with hands on (yes you can touch the sea life!) exhibits and engaging viewing tanks suitable for 3yo and up. Adults won't be dissappointed either with an underwater robot, microscope viewings, and knowledgeable / engaging staff. Wheelchair and stroller accessible, though no power doors. Small area so probably best to park the stroller at the entrance. No public bathrooms, though there are some just down the street at the docks.

The zoo has surprisingly high quality engaging exhibits including interactive spider monkeys, crawl-underwater river otter tunnels, and a feed-the-farm-animals area to name a few.

The park has subsections suitable for varying ages perfect for sending a troupe of kids off to each while keeping everyone in eyesight.

And an ice cream and sand which shop right across the street, too. Certainly a half day of fun if not a full day.

Excellent family park with playground (upgraded circa 2012), long walking loop, baseball field, and small amphitheater.  Parking is along the residential street and not usually a problem except nicest weekends of the year.  Visible fire department, police station, and church add sense of safety.  Stroller friendly.  Bathrooms and water fountains open only seasonally. No grills available.  Few picnic tables. One shelter.

Well appointed community park with bathrooms with water, well built wood, enclosed playground and mature trees surrounding. Playground has a toddler / pre-school section and an older section. One accessible swing. Base of wood chips make wheelchair / stroller access more difficult but can get up to the entrance and over grass to many surrounding areas for viewing. Picnic tables are available.

Make the drive around the peninsula, planning half to full day excursions inward at several areas to experience the many biomes of this dramatic landscape. Gate fee as of 6/2019 is $30 and is good for one vehicle at any entrance for 7 days. Would recommend for those with strollers or wheelchairs as has a surprising number of accessible trails leading to beautiful sites.

Splash pad is amazing! Lots of open spacer perfect for football, ultimate.  Shelter with approximately 10 picnic tables.  Jungle gym appropriate for 2yo-13yo.  Jungle gym and splash pad are far enough apart one could not watch kids on both at the same time.  Often trash blowing around due to limited trash cans.

Largest and best in the world. Prices fairly steep so only takes 1-2 visits before the membership is worth it.  Something for all ages. Nice mix of Indiana-focused history and hands on physics lessons.  Special area for under 5 year olds.  Makes a surprisingly fun date for high-school and college couples, too.

Paved accessible 4 minute trail (with 2-3 spots a little inclined) to a beautiful waterfall bathed in green light reflection off of lush surroundings. Look for slugs along the way. Wheelchair and stroller friendly. Gravel parking area enough for 30 cars. Pit toilets available. No water.

Quaint, quiet park with playground (2-7yo), swings (infant and regular) and a shelter (appropriate for party of 20 or so) and lots of running area.  Parallels the Monon Trail for great people watching and making the park a great destination when cruising the trail.

Clean and with a variety of amenities, though short on playgrounds. Especially recommend the sunken garden and connected pleasant run trail (paved). Much of the park is stroller / wheelchair friendly, though several walkways traverse fairly streep slopes.

Park benches, area of shade, and interesting playground make this a great respite for any age or any family. Playground appropriate for 2-10yo. Wheelchair and stroller friendly with no steps into Park area but only minimal walk way area.

Splash pad , basketball courts and three playground equipment setups for ages 1-15 years old. Minor trash drops the stars. Wheelchair and srtroller accessible. Toilets and picnic tables. Two shelters each about four picnic tables big.

Picturesque, tranquil lake with swimming area and rentable kayaks situated at the top of an hill. Campsites are near water, some on the water. Hiker / biker spots x2 available also. Coin operated showers. Nice loop around the lake.

Riverside park with jungle gym, large picnic shelter (15 picnic tables or so), 5-10 RV hookups, 2 port-o-pots, and large field areas. Squirrels seemed genuinely surprised to see me, belying the quaint nature of this community park.

Self pay tent sites for hikers / bikers.  Has food locker, table, fire ring. Near the noisy highway but quiets enough for sleep eventually. Clean bathrooms. Kind SP employee checked in on us cyclists. Cell phone service spotty.

Family friendly walk-able park with paved and mulched paths and many distinct garden areas like pre-historic plants, rose garden, etc. Water features, wide open running spaces, and a small cafe make it fun for kids, too.

Splash pad and skating area park with jungle gym and small gazebo perfect for family leg stretch off the interstate. Parking area not likely to be full. Splash pad with zero entry for strollers / wheelchairs.
Home of the greatest spectacle in racing, this Indiana must see hosts a golf coarse, museum, and 3 major racing events yearly. The museum is quiet and worth the cheap 5$ entrance fee.
Beautiful, feature rich park with nice, quiet though dense electric campgrounds. Established trails with wide variety of difficulty and now with wolf cave reopened as of August 2017.
Hilly trails through prairie, woods, and along the river. Well kept park. Playground with swings, rock wall, slide, and climbing area. No bathroom in the off season.
Old building with large room of glass case exhibits and materials. Adorably invested personnel excited to help me see the area.

Editing my review as we spent a few hours hiking the dunes succession trail, one of the most beautiful trails according to me in the newest NP of the country. While the bath house is not open year around, the NPS facility just a  quarter mile away hopefully will be open year round. Should go back there in winter/spring to view the migrating water birds.

Though not much artifacts from the native cultures, but I think the focus of the place is more to highlight the contributions of various native people to this country even though they didn’t get much in return and a frank attempt to show how the initial people & governments treated them. Disclaimer: My wife, daughter, and I got to go to the National Aquarium for free thanks to a good friend who is a VP there. After going through the aquarium, we realized our 1.5 hour stay there would have costed $105 ($40 per adults and $25 per kid). That's EXPENSIVE!

Despite the price tag, it's worth going to for sure at least once. It's one of the top aquariums in the nation and for sure the best on the East Coast. It's centrally located on the Inner Harbor. The building itself is beautiful (and smaller than you'd think). The staff are very helpful and friendly. In addition to the usual aquarium suspects (fish of all kinds, sharks, etc), here are highlights:

1) The open pools are beautiful with the dark lighting and decorations. It makes for amazing photos!

2) Petting pool: You can touch and pet sting rays!

3) Harbor view: There's a spot where you can get the best view of the Inner Harbor.

4) Rain forest: It's on the top level and has many plants and fun views of the city.

5) Family rooms: Ask a staff member to take you to a private family room to nurse (And the have Finding Nemo playing in the room and complimentary water).

6) The large tank of sharks as you take a winding walk way down and down. It's breathtaking!

Other things to note: 1) They have a food court/cafe inside for food, 2) You can check your stroller/car seat for free, and 3) They have many shows for kids with GREAT staff leading it.
likes: Cultural Value: Top aquarium, nationally recognized
Facilities & Services: Beautiful building, helpful and friendly staff, family rooms, stroller/car seat check, food court/cafe
Activities: Open pools, petting pool, harbor view, rain forest exhibit, large shark tank, shows for kids

reviews_attraction.text:
The largest of the Fairfax County parks, Huntley Meadows Park is a dream for families, photographers, dog walkers and nature lovers.

My toddler and I went on a Monday morning around 9:30am during the summer. As we rolled into the free parking lot, we noticed a number of photographers trekking back from capturing the sunrise off the wetlands in the middle of the park.

Once parked, we followed the sign to the wooded trail. We hiked for about ten minutes passing the nature center (it's closed during the pandemic) and markers leading the way to the wetlands. The majority of the ten miles of trails are in woods and shaded (very important during hot D.C. area summers). Dogs on leashes are welcome on these trails and we saw a number of dog walkers.

We then hit the boardwalk over the wetlands. This is where the trails become more stroller friendly, but also very hot. The wetlands go back a half-mile, but it's not shaded. Plan accordingly.

The wetlands are beautiful with the boardwalk emerging from the greenery. Slowly walk along the boardwalk and look into the water to see frogs, turtles and maybe a beaver or two. Further in the distance, you can see butterflies and heron.

If you go, stop by Historic Huntley afterward to learn about the history of Huntley Meadows and see a historic house.

Disclaimer: I am writing this review as a DC resident. DC is a city known for their hundreds of museums and many of them are free. Museums in our nation's capital are big!

Spark Museum is a decent small town museum. I went on a Thursday afternoon and paid $12 for general admission and the spark show. The museum has two floors. The first floor is a mix of items on display (with a few historical items) and interactive exhibits that keep you entertained for 4-5 seconds. The second floor is fun and games for kids.

The spark show was just under an hour and not really fit for younger kids. My nephews ages 6 and 7 thought 20% of the show was exciting and 80% boring. The man who runs it knows his stuff, but he talks a lot without explaining what's going on so it's easy for kids to lose interest.

A few highlights from the trip:

1) In the record section, a museum staff member showed us how each player works. He was engaging and fascinating!

2) The second floor offered us the opportunity to make a fun quiz using electrical wires to show what answers matched with what question. My nephews enjoyed that!

If you're looking for things to do, stop by, but don't expect to come back more than once.
dislikes: Spark show not engaging for young children

reviews_attraction.text:
Chapman State Park is a state park 30 minutes south of Southeast DC along the Potomac River. Here's why it's worth the drive:

1) Family-friendly: If you have small children, it's perfect. There are two trails and none are longer than 1.5 miles long. It's easier for children. There's also a wildlife preserve where you may find turtles, lizards, bald eagles, and other animals. The trails lead to the river with small sandy beaches for children to hunt for seashells.

2) History: The property belonged to the Chapman family since 1751. The family has ties to several Founding Fathers. There's a historic mansion on the property restored (tours are offered). There are several old buildings abandoned and worth exploring.

3) Architecture: The mansion is beautiful and was used during the Civil War by the Federal government. The back porch offers stunning views of the Potomac River.

There's one thing to be warned- ticks! Bring repellent and stay on the marked trails. We went in May. Venturing off the trail for literally 15 seconds resulted in three ticks on my ankle. Ugh!

If a museum costs money amidst a sea of free museums in DC, it better be darn good. At $25 a pop, I was skeptical, but after several visits to the Newseum, I can say it's the best paid museum in DC. Here's why:

- Content: Not everyone thinks the news is exciting and they do a great job of creating each exhibit to be interesting, interactive, and engaging. From the Berlin Wall to the photography to the hall of historical newspapers, it's so fascinating. Definitely check out the social media hall.
- View: It's just off the National Mall super close to the US Capitol by the Canadian Embassy. On the top floor, you can go outside to snap a photo of a very cool view of the Mall.
- Store: It has one of the best museum stores in the city.
- Outside gallery: Outside of the museum, the front cover of each state's major newspaper is on display and they switch it out daily. You don't even have to buy a ticket to see it!

If you're visiting DC, the Newseum is worth the investment.

If you love abandoned places, run to The Old Zoo. If you don't, still go to use the picnic tables for lunch, but skip the exploration part. If you are a thrill seeker, budget 45-60 minutes to explore all the old, empty cages. There's a lion's den, bird cages, monkey cages, etc. Most of the cages are closes, but a few are open for people to crawl throw and see what it was like to be a zoo animal decades ago. The highlights:

1) Lion's den: There's one you can crawl up into and see the crawl spaces and the graffiti art now in it.

2) Monkey cage: Behind the main area, hike up and keep going until you come to another cage that you can go in and walk on top of.

3) Back den: There's a large area that goes on and on. In the very front is a water way with a dry tunnel you can crawl through if you're brave enough.

If you like unique things or taking unique photography, go here! It's in Griffith Park, which is fun to explore on its own.

The Glenstone is a fascinating FREE museum in Potomac, Maryland funded by billionaires as their way of giving back to the world. Here's why you should visit:

1) Art: They celebrate art, design, and nature by creating several buildings of unique, post-World War II art and an estate of art out in nature you can explore and stumble upon. Photography and phones are discouraged so you can truly connect with the art.

2) Design: Everything is simple and beautiful from the buildings themselves to the staff uniforms. It's all so nice.

3) Exploration: Spend hours here getting lost and exploring the woods, boardwalk, and all the art found outside.

4) Food: The cafe is gorgeous and an award-winning chef whips up locally sourced meals.

The museum is free, but you need a ticket you can get from their website. Parking is free, which is good because really the only way there is via car.

Washington Monument State Park is interesting for two reasons:

1) The Appalachian Trail goes through it proving that there is natural beauty in Maryland. The views in this park into the valley are beautiful.

2) The OG Washington Monument. More than 50 years before the Washington Monument was built on the National Mall in Washington, D.C., the people near Middletown, Maryland built a stone tower on a hill called the Washington Monument. 500 people built it in one day and it still stands as the very first monument named after George Washington. As you walk up to the monument, you can learn about key dates associated with the first president.

There's a small visitor's center that walks people through the history of this state park (note: the center is closed during the winter).

Many parents speak praises about Clemyjontri Park. Located in McLean, Virginia just off the highway, it's easy to access. There's a small parking lot, but we found a spot on a Saturday morning easily.

The park itself is large. There's a carousel in the center, bathrooms (with stools for kids to reach the sink), a maze, a running kid train, and two areas with slides, monkey bars, etc. It's pretty awesome in terms of things they have.

However, our daughter was unimpressed. She got bored of the park after five minutes when she LOVES playgrounds. We think maybe it was because the equipment is centered around younger kids (she's 2.5 years old).

If you live close by, it's amazing, but I wouldn't drive out of your way to go.

Built around the same time Columbia, Maryland was founded, Wilde Lake is a man-made reservoir with a 1.3 mile trail loop around the lake. Here's why you should visit:

1) Nature: The scenery is beautiful and as you walk the trail, you'll see ducks and geese. Also, many of the trees have little signs by them explaining the type and significance. There's a man-made waterfall and little docks offering beautiful water views.

2) Amenities: There are plenty of benches around the lake offering quiet places to reflect, journal and read. There's a playground by a barn used for events.

3) Parking: It's easy to find with several lots around the lake.

If you are looking for a family-friendly spot, go here!

Fort Dupont Park is one of the most underrated parks in Washington, DC. You have the National Mall, Meridian Hill Park, Lincoln Park...all amazing parks, but if you want a true escape from people, go to Fort Dupont Park just across the Anacostia River just off of Pennsylvania Avenue.

It's a fairly large park full of trails, picnic tables, an indoor ice skating rink, an outdoor amphitheater, and Civil War ruins (truly!). There are pockets to park in and enjoy nature. Ypu'll escape the sounds of the city and won't see many others if you do during the day on a week day.

Grab your lunch and enjoy the many picnic tables scattered throughout!

Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum is a hidden gem in Boston. It's a historic building south of Fenway with a gorgeous indoor courtyard that spans three levels with fountains, plants, etc. In addition, there are several galleries in the new building, many galleries in the old building, a restaurant, reading rooms, theaters, and a gift store.

It's $15 to get in as a regular adult, so budget several hours to enjoy the art and sit and relax in the indoor courtyard. If you go on the third Thursday of the month, the museum stays open until 9pm with music, poetry reading, etc.

There are bathrooms and free lockers to store bags in the basement.

I work with musicians for my job (connecting them to the work of International Justice Mission in helping to end slavery and human trafficking) and I frequent all of the DC area's music venues and Wolf Trap may be my favorite. It's only a 25 minute drive from the District and is uniquely built (like a tree house). Lawn seating is the best since it's the cheapest and they let you bring your own food for a picnic. The sound is amazing even with this venue being entirely outdoors.

Recommended: If you have seats on the lawn, bring your own food as the food and drinks there are pricey and not the best.

The most Austin thing to do in Austin is hike up to Hope Outdoor Gallery in West Austin. It's a hill completely sprayed in paint...layers upon layers of it.

It's literally concrete that you can spray paint. As you hike to the little hill it's on, you'll see a few stands with spray paint for sale. Grab a can or two and go crazy!

Snag your camera as it's one of the best places to take photos in Austin and not just of the graffiti backdrop. Once you get to the very top, it's the best view of the city skyline (and Texan State Capital).

It's such a fun experience and not to be missed when in Austin.

Gulf Branch Nature Center & Park is a great neighborhood green space. There's a small parking lot by the small nature center that does programming in non-pandemic times. Attached to the center is an outdoor terrace with chairs and a caged area for an owl.

Just outside of the nature center is a small pond, a 1871 restored log cabin and an old blacksmith. This is where the trail starts that takes you into different Arlington neighborhoods and to an area with picnic tables and tennis courts. Benches are along the way and a small bridge over a creek.

If you're a traveler, Alki Beach Park will remind you of the coastal towns in Italy meets Ocean City, Maryland. It's a beautiful beach with a great view of downtown Seattle. You can walk along the beach dipping your feet into the cold Pacific Ocean. Once you need a break, just go to the strip of restaurants. Find a place that sells seafood (not hard to find) and order a clam chowder soup and watch the sunset. Once done, drive up the steep windy streets back into downtown Seattle. For a second, you'll think you're in Italy.

The Netherlands Carillon is a tall bell tower in Rosslyn, Virginia near the U.S. Marine Corp Memorial. It was a gift to the U.S.A from the Netherlands as a thank you for their aid during and after World War II. The bells perform daily and even do summer concerts for the public for free. When they are in season, a tulip field surrounds the tower. There's a small wooden bench nearby with the best view of D.C. where you can see the Lincoln Memorial, Washington Monument, and U.S. Capitol in a row.
likes: On-site Activities (Daily Bell Performances, Summer Concerts)

reviews_attraction.text: A garden that isn't a destination, but once tourists stumble upon it, it becomes one. It's a large garden behind the Smithsonian Castle (not the most interesting Smithsonian museum). There's one large garden in the center with plenty of benches for reading/resting. But don't stay there. There are smaller gardens to the left and the right worth exploring especially during the cherry blossoms. If you like gardens, this is one of the best in DC!

Going into Discovery Park, I thought it would be Seattle's version of Central Park or Stanley Park. If you have that in your mind, erase it. Discovery Park is not as developed as Central  Park and Stanley Park. As you hike, you feel like you're in the middle of nowhere. You take the path down to the beach and walk along the water until you get to the lighthouse. It's beautiful views and it's a great break from the city.

Crispus Attucks Park is a true neighborhood park. It's in Bloomingdale surrounded by rowhomes. If you didn't know it was there, you'd easily miss it. Once inside, you'll see a large green space with benches, gardens, and a space for dogs. They sometimes host neighborhood events as well. One of my favorite parts of this park is the guestbook under one of the benches for visitors to sign and share wisdom/thoughts.

Fort Lincoln Park is a fascinating place! It's on the Maryland-DC border in NE DC near the city's only Costco. It's a large park with plenty of street parking nearby. They have benches, courts, and play areas throughout the park. They also have these large wooden huts connected by a network of wooden bridges. It's old, but such a unique park in DC. It's one of my favorites!

I'm giving this a 4-star rating only for history buffs. It's a free museum and if you like history, it's worth the visit. It's one of the oldest homes in DC and this is where the White House was set up after the White House burned down in the War of 1812. It's a self-guided tour through three of the four floors and will take you only 20 minutes to see it all.

The Indiana War Memorial is THE monument to see in Indy and it's hard to miss. It anchors the downtown and can be seen from all parts of the city.

The architecture of it is impressive and you can even go inside and up during on season.

My toddler loved climbing the steps up to it and I enjoyed photographing it.

Hovander Homestead Park is an excellent public park in Ferndale. There's plenty of parking and much to do once on property. There's a playground, an old barn, a historic home, gardens, a lookout tower, and several farm animals like chickens and rabbits. Our toddler LOVED visiting this park and so did we!

Meadowlark Botanical Gardens is a massive park in Vienna, Virginia filled with all types of gardens from around the world. It costs $6 for adults and kids under five are free, but it's a small price to pay for a day trip. You can spend hours wandering the trails and spending time in each garden.

Living on 23rd Street and working as a clinical psychoanalyst on 26th means that--for many, many years--I've had the privilege of walking through Madison Square Park...sometimes (often two times/day). And, because I've been doing so, modeling in, around and through Lower Manhattan for the last couple of decades, I've witnessed the increasingly loving care that has been put into the upkeep of this park. When I got here (NYC) in 1997, that was simply NOT the case (in fact, it had the reputation of being a place not not be traversed after dark). Now it is anything but...it has Shake Shack, amazing art installations (most of them super fun and interactive), and all kinds of kid-friendly and music events. Most recently, a red-tailed hawk has moved in! What a blast!!!

What a place to, for all kinds of reasons, walk through regularly in the course of simply living our lives as residents--often referring to ourselves as "resident tourists"--of downtown, NYC!!! For years when my girls were young (younger than they are now), on the afternoons that we'd be moseying around together, we could count on Union Square to provide some kind of lively activity--concerts, protests, all kinds of entertainment, green markets, etc., etc. Anyway, we're all quite grateful to have the privilege of walking through Union Square as often as we do.

Love tis place! Most Saturdays after surfing, I run over to Friends Seminary--where my kids attend Japanese school--and spend some time (either before school's out or after) hanging out in this beautiful park. There's always something going on--film students shooting something, skateboarders skating amok, parents chasing gnarly little kids. Well kept and pleasant...a nice place to sit on a bench and take in what downtown is like when (other than the occasional frenzy, as mentioned) quiet.

WOW!!! What an exhilarating place for a 5, 10, or whatever, K run!!! I mean, gotta young daughter who wanted to train to make the track team at her (grammar) school, and so we signed up for a few races all over the city to prepare her. Her dad--Yours Truly--had been a cross-country runner in high school and done OK on PT in the US Army, and--whoa--Riverside Park was a perfect challenge for this duo! Not to mention the beautiful view of the Hudson River and whatnot--but, man, what a run!!!

Such a lovely place to pull over -- with the whole family -- on a bike ride along the East River bike path! So hot this summer, and, yet, an immense need to be out and about as we've all been cooped up in our x-square-foot apartments for months, and this beautiful park seems to be situated in a way that captures the perfect mix of wind and shade to refresh one's self (and family) so I -- so we -- can get back on the path and enjoy the Lower Manhattan sojourn...out and among our community!

Grew up 🏄‍♂️🏄‍♂️🏄‍♂️ on the Balboa Peninsula -- lived at 118 Sapphire and took the Ferry as many days as I could to either surf at Blackies (off the Newport Pier), The Point (17th Street) or body-surf t
The Wedge!!! What a life...a grommet growing up on Balboa Island, Newport Beach, SoCal!! A dream come true!!! I love NYC--where we're having our Grrrrrrrrrrrrrrls (Kata and Uta!), but my 💓💓💓 is still crossing that ferry...And I take my wife and kids there every chance I get!!!

Always love it here. From the first time I visited in 1997 when a colleague invited me to the Kirov Opera at The Met to, more recently, when my co-author (of "Relationship Sanity" ) and I celebrated our most recent publication by attending all four operas in the "Ring" cycle, I am in love with this place. Big Apple Circus, free open-air concerts at Damrosch Bombshell (including last year's tribute to Lou Reed [with an appearance by Yo La Tango]), this place has it all!

23- Skidoo! What can I say? This building is the shining symbol of a district that stretches between itself and the Empire State. Flatiron District is how I describe to clients where my office is; how to find me. And though I've been in New York City for 22 years (as of July 2019), I still get a thrill out of having a Broadway office address, and claiming the Flatiron as my professional home! I ❤️ here, and this building in many ways symbolizes here.

What's not to love, eh!? Amazing exhibitions (for instance the David Bowie) and what could be better than that Target First Saturdays!?! I mean, really, we have had blast after blast at this joint Saturday after Saturday for years! In fact, the night that I got the call from the woman who was to be--still is--my wife called me while I was partying down at First Night---so, you gotta know I've got some gold standard associations to this place!!!!

What a place! Awesome place to see a concert, or an event. There is often, in the summer especially, so much going on here. It has been the place, for years, where the Run 10 Feed 10 race started and finished--and that was a great event. I'm not sure if that is over for good (???), I sure hope not. This is a wonderful place--right along the Hudson River bike path--to pull over, find some shade, and share a meal.

I really like this little park. My younger daughter and I often mosey over to this park for some empanadas (Las Nunches) and people-watching. It's located right at the center of what, for us, constitutes what we experience as "Home"--downtown New York City. And, we wind up there all throughout the year. There are times where you'll find us munching away in our winter gear right in the depths of the cold season.

What happened? Where's that lovely vibe, etc.? Remember seeing all kinds of rockin' bands (like Xiu Xiu and Deerhoof playing Joy Division's "Unknown Pleasures"!!!)! Seriously good Pickens!!!

Super blast, Carrillo National Monument!!! We were on our way to San Diego (proper) when we saw a sing for this amazing--seemingly hidden away--little stitch of sea, where the kids could frolic in the tide pools, observe various sea creatures (quite an experience for New York City Girls!), and wrap ourselves all up in sea weed! We'll be back to hit it every time we're in SoCal!!!

Love love love it here....what's not to love? Yet another NYC-scape that has all the compelling features that hundreds of years of historical/mystical resonance is inevitability going to result in. A blast for friends and family when visiting -- as well, of course, for is so-called resident-tourists here in the lovely, lovely NYC!!!!!!!

Super blast, Carrillo National Monument!!! We were on our way to San Diego (proper) when we saw a sing for this amazing--seemingly hidden away--little stitch of sea, where the kids could frolic in the tide pools, observe various sea creatures (quite an experience for New York City Girls!), and wrap ourselves all up in sea weed!

We love this place. I first visited this place in 1991 when I met a dude who would become a lifelong friend. We more recently visited the Exploratorium--that dude and me--with our partners and our kids. It was fun to visit as young adults ourselves so many years ago, much more fun to visit all these years later with our kids!

WOW!!! To get a chance to kick back, take a rest while peddling away--all 42 miles of--that Five Burroghs Bike Tour with your (my) True Love!! Quite a moment...I mean, yes, Staten Island is the short cut to the Jersey Shore for the serious all-year surfer in all of us...but, to stop, take a breath, take a photo...WOW!!!

Man, Oh Man--this is the last stop to some serious thwalpinin' waves out in the Atlantic!!! As the bounce-point to the rockin', gnarly waves, the Long Beach Boardwalk is the a New York version of a yellow brick road...off the boardwalk, onto the beach, paddlin' out to happiness-- Cowa-Cowabunga, Dudes!!!

Awesome park....saw one of the all-time best (FREE!) Concerts here ever--Laurie Anderson--with a pal in from Hawaii who turned me onto her in, what? Maybe 1987! Sheeeeeeeeeeeeeesh!!! Having that kind of experience here--I have to say--really makes this park one of the best (to me) in New York City!!!

Lovely, lovely spot for a late afternoon stroll! We ride our bikes up from downtown (Eastside) when, throughout the summer, there are these wonderful performances put on along the banks of the wonderful Harlem Meer...what a lovely spot, and a really quite compelling destination for us downtowners!!!

We love it here..especially the Dinosaur Safari--I mean, come on (!!!), we've got two little dinosaur-lovin' Grrrrrrrrls who were thrilled (a little too thrilled, didn't want to go home!) with the animatronic creatures--T. Red, Bronto, Steger, etc.--t'was the real deal blast for these NYCers!!!

We love it here! Ice skating in the winter, concerts and wonderful events all summer long (like the amazing Roots picnic with an assortment of awesome bands and guests such as Wu-Tang Clan, David Byrne and Deerhoof)! We love to stroll through this park on the way uptown or down!

Awesome place!!!--what a wonderful adventure to sojourn out from Manhattan to hit this extremely compelling and infinitely enlivening place! We've seen such wonderful exhibits and shows here, and are always happy--and grateful--to take the chance to hit PS 1!!!

The Museum at Eldridge Street, while an impressive place to begin with, outdid themselves by sponsoring the wonderful Empanada, Egg Roll and Egg Cream Festival---combing and celebrating various cultures of downtown NYC! What a blast!

I have lived in the DFW area for 10 years but never visited before. It's a huge place to go and relax in nature. The entrance fee is $5 per person which is a bit steep and would be better if per car but it's not breaking the bank. I visited during the end of winter and the spring colors were just coming out. There were a lot of birds, mostly cardinals. The paths they have setup are really nice and depends on your skill. Some are easier on your feet than others. Fishing isn't allow so the noise of boats won't bother your visit. They have a kayak and canoe launch and course which looks cool and would be something to try during the spring and summer.

Very nice place in the center of Downtown Dallas. It was meeting point for local tour of the area. While here I saw many people walking their dogs and just enjoying the day. The grass area was restricted because of some construction but it was still nice. You get to see many buildings and admire the views of the old city hall building.

A very nice park and its huge. Lots of paths to walk, run, bike, or walk your dog. It's right in the center of the city and they are doing many upgrades to make it look nicer. The Buffalo Bayou flows right through the center. The park has lots of sites like the Police Memorial, Spots Park, and Eleanor Tinsley Park.

The museum is very nice, lots of planes so the little ones will be amazed. Lots of interacting displays and games. The planes and helicopters on display are well maintained and the staff if very knowledgeable. Its also a working airport so you can see planes taking off and landing on the runway.

This was my second time coming here and it was great. The first time was about 9 years ago and I was rushed but this time I was able to take some time. Free admission to their regular exhibits and you can explore at your own pace. Great way to spend the day especially around the Arts District.

The park is a great place to view the river and go for a walk. Best times to go are during the wet season so the river path is full. Except when the river is at flood stage it's nice. As for the view, it's okay. Not the best view of downtown and at night it's too far.

I visit the place on Saturday because it's free on the first Saturday of the month. I highly suggest you take advantage because the regular $10 fee is too much. The center is small but is well maintained. Interesting sculptures in the lawn and also inside.

A very nice place to hangout and walk around. Bring your dog so they can enjoy the little park and get lots of attention. They have lots of activity and they offer a sort of market some nights. They also have movie nights.
Great local park to visit and walk around. They recently completed the expansion and you have more trails. They also put new disc golf holes and they expand across the street to the other parts.
This is the West portion of the park. They have the Soccer and baseball fields here as well as some basketball fields. Nice place to take a walk, ride your bike, walk your dog, or just relax.
Nice place to get an overlook of the eastern half of the city and primarily downtown. Only issues are there is not enough parking and too much trash. You will find beer cans and bottles.
A wonderful place to take a walk and enjoy the city. The sites and sounds are awesome and the weather is very nice. Right along the water front, you get the breeze from the Bay.
A great park to take pictures of the Seattle skyline. Day and nighttime shots are a must. They have lots of people and sometimes there is a band or quartet playing some music.
Nice cruise service that takes around the bay to get a view of the waterfront. Good price but the recent construction makes it pain to go there. If you can, Uber to the place.
Very nice place to visit. Attended the orchid society show and the butterflies in the garden exhibit. Lots of educational programs and the staff is very friendly.
Nice plaza buts been under so many remodels that you never what it looks like year after year. Mostly a bus terminal but still nice during the holidays.
A beautiful Ferris wheel located right on the piers. When we visited there was a lot of construction so getting to it was a pain as well as the parking.
Beautiful place and the landscape is gorgeous. Very tranquil place. The garden is well maintained. Perfect place to take a stroll and just relax.
Very nice place when I visited Seattle. When we visited they had part of the beach sealed off because a sea lion was sleeping on the beach.
This is one of the hardest trails I have ridden in the DFW area. It was fun but come prepared and keep an eye for the loose rocks.
Drove by the Los Angeles County Museum of Art for those street lights. Just a quick stop before calling it a night.
Great park to visit. Nice place to walk or take your bike. They also have a dog park for your friend to have fun.
This is nice neighborhood park to visit. It's across a middle school so be careful and keep an eye out for kids.
Always love visiting this place. It is very relaxing and during the summer months, a great place to cool down.
Cool place to stop by a wander around. Lots of nice sculptures to see and amazing how they made them.

I love balloons as much as the next guy, but the Balloon Classic is a snooze fest at best. I saw 3 balloons in 4 hours and they all looked the same. Probably could of seen them for free from a parking lot in town. Lots of nothing to do time. Jason Brown put on a concert, but whose Jason Brown ?? The food venders were the highlight of the night, as was going home. It’s a balloon festival, there should be 20 balloons in the sky at any given time. And maybe someone periodically jumping out of one. I know how to put on a Balloon Festival, I am the 1999 Balloon National Champion !!!
🎈🎈🎈🏆🏆🏆🥇🥇🥇

What better place than Temple Square for review #500 !!!  WOW !!! Let that sink in for a minute. Beautiful gardens and buildings tended daily by 500 Mormons. The Mormons have been around for 500 years give or take. I'm not 500% sure about that.  If your Mormon, you can have up to 500 wives. Deffenitly sure about that one, 500% x 2. Totally unrelated yet just as interesting , I have $500.00 in my 401K and my house is 500 square feet. Beautiful place, everyone should see it once. Temple Square, not my house.
⛪⛪⛪⛪🕍🕍🕍🕍🕍
