Fun at 1000 feet. Buy your ride tickets with your tower ticket for best value.  I HATE  heights, but my daughter wanted to do the rides and no one else in my family would man up. Not even my wife ??  So I mustered up all my courage and rode them with her. Oh, I thought I was going to die the whole time. And my courage has not replenished itself as of yet. 🤢🤢🤢 The view from the space shot will blow all your senses into the "Stratosphere". Good one. Still terrified of heights.🎢🎢🎢🎰🎰🎰

I would have gave it 5 stars if I would have seen more than one ghost. The one I did see wasn't scary at all, she was working in the gift shop. Props to her in making the world a better place instead of spooking visitors. Although not haunted at all, the house tour is really cool and the story behind the house is very interesting. The staff is friendly if not a little over infatuated with Sarah Winchester. Don't ask if Sarah was crazy. A tick pricey.
👻👻👻👻🔫🔫🔫🔫🔫
dislikes: Staff over infatuated with Sarah Winchester

reviews_attraction.text: Life jacket required. I think Sergeant Floyd was once the mayor of Sioux City or something, like in the ealy 1960s, his name is all over the place. Neat paddle boat museum along I-29 and the Missouri River. Surprisingly, they cram a lot of intetesting things in that boat to look at. It's not on the river, so no need to bring your sea legs.There is also a rest area on site. Who do you like better Lewis or Clark ??  🚣🚣🛶🛶

A different view of Rushmore. Great views of the Black Hills. The best part is piloting a alpine sled down the hill at 120+ mph with no helmet. ☠☠☠ I'm kidding, it's 95 mph. I'm still kidding. Its not dangerous fast.  The only downside is the price. 💰💰 The ride down last maybe 90 seconds. I'm being generous with that time. After paying for my family of five, we had no cash for meals the rest of our trip. 😵😩🤑😫🤐

I have to quit setting myself up for disappointment. Or do better research before I drive 600 miles to just be let down. Paul is not real, you can't talk to him. Did you know that ?? Babe is fake as well, no rides. They are so tall that picture taking is useless. With that heartbreaking story, Bemidji is a very beautiful town. The Lakefront is nice a  place to relax. Check it out for yourself. 🐂🐃⛏⛏🗿🗿

The world's greatest museum. I actually mean it this time.  ⛴⛵🚤 I never get tired of it. It's so interesting and unique. It's also, are you sitting down ?? FREEEE !!! For all the countless times I've been there, I still don't know what "Maritime" means.  I wanted to ask a museum worker, but I was afraid they would laugh at me. I am shy. I suppose I could look it up on Wikipedia. 🛳🛳🛥🛥🚢🚢

I was a little disappointed in this stop. Oh, it’s quiet, peaceful and pretty being right next to the river, but there are no signs of a shootout anywhere. You can read about it and use your imagination. No thanks. I want to see a bullet ridden car, I don’t even care if it’s not period correct. It can be a Pontiac J2000 that was shot up in Detroit last week...
🔫🔫🔫🔫🔫🔫🔫🔫

Bridges Of Madison County feel just a mile from I-35. You've seen one bridge, you've seen them all. No need for a long boooring  drive to Winterset. I get the other bridges have more scenic backdrops, have cooler names, and get torched more often.♨♨ But your friends will never know from your pictures that your at the red headed step child of the Covered Bridges. 📸📷

Bill May have been born in Le Claire, but he called North Platte Nebraska home. But don’t we all ?!?! I’m guessing it’s a nice museum, but it was closed when we were there. But it’s right on the river, who wants to go inside and read when the scenery outside is so beautiful ?!?!  Grab a park bench by the water and Wikipedia Buffalo Bill. Or enjoy nature...
🤠🤠🤠

This is the premier state park in the country,  makes all other state parks look like a landfill. Better than some national parks. Too much to do to list, it's just one big adventure after another.  Bring lots of bread to feed to the donkeys, you will be a hero to your kids.  Wild life and natural beauty abound all 70,00 plus acres. Yeah, it's big. 🌲🌲🐴🐴🍞🍞

Only YOU  can prevent forrest fires. Wow, that's a big responsibility. How did you get suckered into that ?? Glad he wasn't talking to me, I can start all the fires I want. No accountability.  Seriously, nice and quiet city park thats great for relaxing or picnics and whatever else people do in parks. Enjoy. 🐻🐻🐻🔥🔥🔥🌲🌲🌲🚒🚒🚒

Its like looking down on The Black Hills from Heaven. If you only do one thing in The Hills, do this. It's freeeee !!! Well, it does cost to get in the park. So that begs the question, is it free ??  Don't forget gas, plus wear and tear on your car. ⛽⛽🚘🚘 Maybe, it's not such a great deal.🤔🤔🤔 Enjoy !!!

World Renowned museum. 🌎🌍 By world I mean a 3 block radius. We visited before they charged admission. I think now its a nominal fee. Still a great deal. It is a very interesting museum with some neat exhibits. Learn about local legend Fly Speck Billy. That will take all of 3 minutes. Have fun.🏛🏛🏛

Life begins at 12,000 feet......Maybe it ends. I mean no trees grow here, no Taco Bell or cell phone signal and it's like you have Stage 9 Asthma. What animals are here........aliens. Very busy during peak season. Still a cool stop.  🎶Rocky Mountain High, Colorado🎶   Bob Denver 👽👽👾👾

What is it ?? I think it’s a tomb for E.T’s dad. Often touted as the 9th wonder of the world, people always ask, did aliens build it ?? Or did the railroad build it ?? We may never know. What I do know, is that it is a cool and quirky stop off I-80. Good luck finding it. ☘☘☘👽👽👽🚂🚂🚂

Westbound only. No Eastbound access. Maybe if you park your car in the median ?? Neat little tower to view the Missouri Valley. 1000% guarantee you will be the only one there. If I'm wrong, which I won't be,  admission is on me. I like those odds. Handy restroom on-site. 🗼🗼🗼🗽🗽🗽

We stopped here for a picnic on the way to St. George.  I wanted Hardee's 🍔🍔🍟🍟back in Salina, but the Lil General  🌟🌟🌟🌟 insisted on a scenic stop with great views and fresh air !?!?  There were some hiking trails, but who has time for that ???  🕐🕜🕑 Clean restrooms.

Nice and quiet, extremely small city park that pales in compression to it’s next door neighbor, Custer State Park. But it has one advantage over CSP, no entry fee !! But as the old saying goes, you get what you pay for. And this could never be more true than here.

Awesome collection of Shelby Mustangs. There is a viewing area to watch ho-hum Fords being transformed into fire breathing Shelbys. I would have gave it 5 stars if they Customized my Stang for FREE !!! Seems fair to me.😁😁😁

It is very cool, from the road. You can see all you need to see from the road. And your wallet will thank you. Spend your money somewhere else. Somewhere more fun. Which is everything else in the Black Hills.
😎😎😎

Fun for kids or small people. Lots of things  for you to explore and climb. Neat and historic building to look around. Enjoy it. Take a car you don't care about. Better yet, take a cab. It is St. Louis. 🤸🤸🤸🚕🚕🚕
Quiet, tranquil  stop along I-80. People who go to church in glass structures shouldn't throw stones ?? Seriously, it's a neat church. I think a F.000005 tornado would wipe it out. 🌬🌬📿📿🕇🕇🕇
Quick stop off I-29 with a great view of Sewer  City. Looks just like the Washington Monument in D.C. minus all the crowds and  fanfare. Odds are you will be the only one there.🗼🗽🚽🚽💩💩

One of Chicago's best attractions. It's free to enter (though you pay to park, so take public transit if you can) and each exhibit is better than the last. It's not huge and it doesn't have any extremely modern or catchy exhibits, but it has everything you'd expect from a zoo. And, you're in the middle of the city which makes it that much cooler. The "farm" is great for little kids, and they really have something for everyone.

Beautiful lookout over the island and the lake. The fort itself isn't really much to see - it's just a recreation of an old fort, and the design doesn't really make any sense. There are no stairs to the 2nd floor. Not sure if that' s how it was originally or not, but in any event, an explanation on a placard would be nice. Definitely worth checking out while you're on the island, however.

Very nice beach. It's incredibly clean and well kept. The staff is very friendly. There's a fun playground for kids. The shoreline is a bit rocky, but not too bad. The lake is obviously very cold, but it's very refreshing on a hot day. You only pay to park, but you can drop people off and then park at the Ravinia train station for free, which is about a mile away. Then everything is free.

Huge park with many different playground areas. There's a sand area, several play structures, a park district building with facilities and water fountains, and plenty of open space. It's a great place to spend a few hours on a nice day. There is also ample parking if you're driving there. The grounds can get quite muddy when it's been raining, so dress appropriately in the spring.

Phenomenal place to see a show. It's small and intimate, yet you're surrounded by Chicago's best buildings and skyscrapers. The acoustics are great, and there's not a bad seat in the house. Viewing angles aren't great from the grass, but the pavilion seats are all great. Be sure to use spothero or something similar if you're driving - the millennium park lot is a ripoff.

Fun playground for younger kids. The metal slides get too hot in the sun, so be careful on sunny days. The maze-like play structure is very different and unique, so kids will love it. There are a few water features for hot days. and there is a sand box as well. It's clearly a destination for kids in NYC. I'll be taking my kids there again next time I'm in town.

Really nice zoo. It is massive, so you likely won't be able to see everything in one visit. They have so many different exhibits and things to see. It can be very crowded, so plan accordingly. On very busy days, getting in can be a pain (long lines to get into the parking lot). It's also a bit pricey. But, the high price is totally worth it.

Whether you're a tourist or a lifelong Chicago resident, you will love this place. It has something for everyone. The scale model of the downtown is great, and their tours/boat rides are even better. Of all the river cruises, this is the best. The walking tours are awesome as well. Be sure to check this place out.

One of Deerfield's best parks. It's rarely crowded, but there are plenty of things to do: lots of open green space, 3 different playgrounds for different aged kids, running path, exercise equipment, baseball field, etc. There's also plenty of parking. Facilities are very well kept-up. There are bathrooms here.

The depot itself isn't anything special. It's too boring for kids and not interesting for adults. However, the train set next door is awesome. And, the miniature train ride (which is like $7 per person for unlimited rides all day) is super fun and kids will love it. This makes for a fun few hours with kids.

This place is great for kids who love trains. We were last here for their annual Day of Thomas event, which is really incredible. But, even without that, there are tons of fun train-related activities for young kids. It's a bit of a hike from Chicago, but it's an easy drive and definitely worth it.

Great park with plenty to do: playground for little kids and older kids, basketball courts, baseball diamonds, open fields and running/walking/biking trail. There's plenty of parking if you need to drive, and it's rarely crowded. This is another one of Deerfield's phenomenal parks.

Great spot for a day with the family. They have something for everyone here, and the large digital wall is very engaging for little kids (and adults  as well, for that matter). The staff was very friendly as well, and their kids activities were a blast.

Great park with a lot to offer. The playground has different areas fur different ages, and each section is fun and unique. There's also a dog park, open fields and a baseball diamond. The facilities are nice and the pavilion is usually clean.

Nice museum but overpriced and overcrowded. Parking was very expensive as well. All of the exhibits were nice, but it's not very large, so it only takes an hour or so to see everything. Tar pits are cool to see, however.

Fun spot for children. It was perfect for my 3-year old. I was there on a Sunday afternoon, and it was surprisingly not too crowded - we didn't have to wait for anything at all. It's a great way to spend an afternoon.

Fun and approachable zoo. It's the perfect size for young kids. Boat cruise (which is no extra charge) was great. Feeding the giraffes (which cost $5) was great as well. Great time for the whole family!
My 16 month old had a blast. It's a little pricey for what it is, but you'll have no problem finding something that your kid likes to do. They have something for everyone.
Really great park. Several different play structures. Water features. Exercise equipment for adults. Fun vibe in the area. Plenty of parking. Plenty of open space.
Very nice public park. There's a splash pad for kids, a fun playground, a roller hockey rink and lots of open green space. There's plenty of parking as well.
Beautiful large pier. Lots of space to walk around and see the sights. Free little aquarium at the end. Nice place to kill an hour on a nice day.
Beautiful theater with not a bad seat in the house. It really is a beautiful as you would expect. See a show here if you ever get the chance!
Great site to see while you're on the island, but there isn't much there. It's just a cool rock formation plus great views of the lake.
Great park. Many different play structures for different ages. Plenty of parking. Skate park. Basketball and tennis courts. Fun vibe.
Nice little beach. Not the nicest beach in town, but it's convenient and there is parking and clean bathrooms. Beach is small.

A must visit place if you find yourself in this part of the Key West, and especially if you're the reader or the writer type. I didn't really listen much to the docents doing the guided tours, which happen almost regularly. But I heard some of them, as the place was packed that weekday afternoon we showed up there.

I love the cats, and you'll see lots of different colors and sizes of them there. They even have a cemetery space there.

I'm also impressed from seeing the biggest private swimming pool when it was built then in the 1930s outside of Miami right by the property. You'd get an idea on how big these people lived their lives and pursued their dreams from visiting the site. It's worth the fee, even if for a brief time and it's hot and humid. Inside the house, it's cool because of air-conditioning.

I like their service, considering all the troubles. They picked us up from near our hotel & brought us back much later in the day. They try to make it easier for you in more ways than one to have a great 15-hour day trip from Las Vegas Nevada to the Grand Canyon South Rim in Arizona. Tiresome trip but very much worth it, especially because given the time, we have accomplished much. I won't do such distance driving, as I know it's hard work. Kudos to our driver Ric ( I hope I recalled his name right). I will try to do the helicopter option next time with them.

This park always looks pretty and clean whenever I get to visit it.  Not really that big in size, if I will recall Central Park in New York City. This park can definitely be seen as among the best looking parks in Philadelphia. I have been there almost all seasons, except on winter. But it is generally quiet even if you see many people around. This is true even during the last time I went there with a friend on a weekday and where many paintings and other artworks were on display and for sale to the curious public. It still didn't look and feel crowded.

This is an interesting concrete spot to come by and wait for your turn to have your picture taken next to it. When we showed up, there was a long line of visitors patiently waiting for their turn. In the meantime, I was surprised to get reminded that the point is really at least 90 miles from Cuba. Wow, I wish they have trips by boat from that marker to Cuban island itself. I am sure, I will avail of a ride on it.

A must visit art destination here in Beacon. Huge, spacious, and very interesting. I just think the guided tours discriminate by design against people with disabilities. I was with my friend who had a walker but I felt the artist who was doing that guided tour on a Saturday at 12:30pm didn't really want to deal with us in her group. Oh, well, she will grow older & I am sure she will get what she deserves.

One of the must see places in NYC if you are into museums. It's literally the cloisters originally somewhere in Europe but were carefully moved and placed in this part of Manhattan up in Inwood. When you go to the main building of the Metropolitan Museum of Art on 5th Avenue, you can actually use the same ticket on the same day but you got to travel from 5th Avenue to Inwood. Enjoy!

What a lovely small museum of art that is worth visiting if you find yourself here in Atlanta, Georgia. Didn't really plan it, and I had some difficulties locating it after exiting the subway station, as it's not exactly on Peachtree Street. But I persisted, and so I found it after some time. The architecture of the display buildings themselves are very notable!

I like this well-maintained, good size park. I wasn't expecting something like it in this part of Florida during a recent visit, as I was thinking the whole state has long given up protecting nature places as this one from development. It's in a city near Ft Lauderdale, and I look forward to visiting it again next time I am around.

I was here lately with my 2 friends visiting from abroad. It was cold and a bit wet due to the rain. We didn't see that many usual people. The arch still looked great. The very park itself was quiet that time when we showed up at past lunch time. I didn't even see musicians that day, as they're here normally doing their gigs.

A beautiful, new-ish section of the south side of Las Vegas strip. I prefer to walk by here rather than being in a car, unless when the heat outside is too oppressive. Lots of things to look, admire, check out, and consider. I don't feel it's too crowded but I can imagine the whole place can be packed.

A must visit place, even in the pandemic.  Some sculptures need the mood to better appreciate them. I had fun too looking at the peacocks and the big fish. Come when it is about to grow dark, so many of the sculptures look very interesting and more appealing with the play of lights.

This is a very pretty old and well maintained park in Savannah. I love its fountain, the other squares don't have fountains. This square has plenty of dramatic settings that are perfect for picture taking. You just need your imagination to get the best sites.

If you're in Miami, find time to come here before the whole place is built in with tall buildings almost right next to the beach. It's beautiful, peaceful, all about nature and I am grateful there's still a beach place like this in Miami.

We were here even on a rainy winter weekday and had fun just the same. The arch is looking great especially if you have guests to bring around NYC and get everybody's pictures taken by or near it. It looks simply grand as a background.

This is a must visit place if you are into museums and modern art and when you visit NYC. The last time I was here I enjoyed viewing Dorothea Lange, Donald Judd, and other artists' works. Awesome feast to the eyes.

I have been to these exhibits at least twice, and they continue to fascinate me. Certain displays and artworks have been changed but it just means the art has evolved. Good opportunities to take selfie shots.
Looks quiet  but there are people coming here even on pandemic time. Just across the river is New Jersey. Looks industrial in the background. Maybe  in a few years, more visitors will show up.
It's always a good feeling visiting art galleries. Some were closed that day. We talked with gallery owners and artists. We got a piece that caught our fascination. Visit the area if you can.
Nice place to visit, especially after you've been to the New York Public Library on 5th Avenue. They have movies screen on the lawn during summer. Nice experience with so many other people.
A tiny park where even the buses turn around on their way back. Well kept and maintained for some reason, which is not the same with all parks in NYC.
Interesting place. I am just surprised it's almost always without a crowd when I find myself in the area. Of course, I see people walking, passing by.
It's a nice park to hang around. Convenient and near the subway stops. Nice views of the water. They even have Shakespeare plays in summertime.
If you're going to downtown Atlanta, this should be included among the list of must-visit places. It's a very interesting park.
This is good playground to spend time in if you find yourself in the area. Across is a big public hospital.
Small park but it's a very nice place, at least during most of the time that I have been there.

One of the premiere shows of the area. The place was filled to capacity for our show. However, they move people effectively. The group picture taking slowed the process.
The pre-show was a nice diversion as the capacity crowd was brought into the facility. We were then ushered to our shoe seating area.
The meal was cooked very well and served hot, as finger food. The staff was particularly well trained and cordial. This was first class country.
The show itself was thoroughly entertaining, especially if you like horses. The Christmas theme was dynamic. I would return again to this theater and recommend it to anyone.

Compared to other show opportunities in the area, this one needs work. It wouldn't take much to go from good to great.
The show itself was flat and predictable. It is built upon a series of old cliches. I could have written a better script. The music was good, but not unforgettable.
The food was alright, but slightly cold. The food handlers were excellent. The seating was nice.
There were eye catching distractions during the entry. There were at least two vehicles that dramatized that Era. The barnyard pen also entertained while we waited.
Trust the show is better next time, if there is one.

As so get older, history means so much more. Visiting the birthplace of flight brings history alive. Have spent time in Dayton OH; this compliments the Wright Brothers story.
Recommend bringing your walking shoes for intermediate tourist hike. Plan to spend at least two hours.
The ocean view is also fabulous, as this is a promontory point. Bring something warm on cooler days because the humidity is high and slight breezes can bring on a chill factor.
Read the markers carefully. The park rangers are fabulous. It's all good.

There is an unmistakable connection between the NSA and this museum. If you are anywhere near Ft. Mead this is a must see.
The staff are very knowledgeable and helpful to visitors. They have free materials for both adults and children.
I would make it a point to visit their library to see their unique collection and possibly chat with the librarian
The visit provides a unique glimpse I to the careers of men and women who assess the secrets in our nation's security. I thank them for their service.

Visited for the the first time, on the last day of Art in Bloom. This was a challenging first impression because of the crowds. However, they did a superb job of getting us parked and inside the exhibits.
It was difficult to get the pictures that I wanted, free of other camera readied  visitors.  Most were polite.
The collections are varied from paintings to sculpture and it will take several trips to fully apprecoate the exhibits. Thoroughly enjoyed and plan to return on a non-event day.

Enjoyed the commaraderie of several servicemen,, including WWII vets. This museum is a jewel that serves both the local community and savvy visitors.

Volunteer staff and friendly and willing to share their history. The collections are well organized an properly authenticated. They add ti their collection rwgularly.

This is an archive of military history. Visitors gain a great sense of our military past achievements by visiting this treasure trove.

The winery was a little difficult to find on maps, possibly due to a poor signal in this area. We were delightfully successful.

The staff proved generous in our wine sampling. They offer a unique range of wine. We found selections to mail directly home. They delayed shipping to coincide with our arrival; our shipment arrived about two of our return.

This is a nice excursion for adventurous tourists while visit the nearby national park.

Enjoyed the drive up the mountain, which has scenic rest stops. There are places to picnic along the way.
We traversed the suspension bridge and I enjoyed taking pictures of the vistas. So.e climbing around the top is permissible at your own risk.
We stopped at the gift shop before departure. They offered a nice selection of clothing and collectables at fair prices. Highly recommend this location, if you like the outdoors.

An overall excellent facility and experience. We reserved a tent site and were very satisfied with how it was laid out with a picnic table, grill and water source.
Bathrooms, with shower were with a few feet. We could park immediately in front of our space. The staff proved always helpful and knowledgeable. A short drive up the gap takes you to a Trail head for the Appalachian Trail. We will definitely return.

Beautiful half mile hike on a well built trail, for ease of access. Parking proved ample for a steady stream of visitors.
The end of the trail was filled with roots. Access to the Falls requires adapting to wet slopes of bare rock.
The recent rain gave us a spectacular experience of bountiful flows of roaring waters, living up to its namesake. Overall a great visit.

Miles of trail along the Neuse River enjoyed by the local community. The system connects much of the Raleigh area for both bikers and walkers. Its accessed easily from many vantage points.
Enjoy the occasional park benches for a quick rest. The bridges provide splendid views of the river. It's a wonderful trail to enjoy nature at its best...within city limits.

Excited that the state parks are finally open  They tend to be less busy during the week, but there was still foot traffic on the trails.
Most trails are rated easy. We did a loop of four miles, that includes one medium difficult trail.
Enjoy the trails that parellel the namesake Neuse River. There are some real photo opportunities in this park.

Have enjoyed classes at the community center. They offer a good variety of offerings at affordable prices.
The center is clean and well maintained. The staff seem willing to help in any way possible. Our draw for commuting remains the class offerings. There are strategic facilities throughout the Raleigh area.

Be sure to check the list of provided items. We were there a few minutes early, to ensure our appointed seating.
The trip begins with instructions and a  film. The craft was piloted by able Navy personnel. It must be quote the honor to serve in this capacity.
Slow Salute to those lost. Never forgotten.

Perfect weather to enjoy the plants and trees of this state treasure. Plants are clearly marked with informational markers, for novices such as myself.
There are many places that invite you to sit down and relax amongst the growth.  Trust to return at various stages of plant life. Taking photos today!

Elmira College does a great job in preserving all things Mark Twain. Visitors are welcomed to their holdings. We arrived before the traditional summer tourist season.
Amazed to see the dwelling where Samuel Clemmons created his later works. Found central to the campus.

The entertainment was worth the trip. The food was good, but some tables were served very late. The boat had a romantic feel, even though we had a full riverboat. I took some interesting photos of this one of a kind view of Nashville. Very good experience overall.

Quiet spot for dog walking with a direct view of the lake. Be sure not to by pass the oldest building known for these parts.
Really nice area for family time or a place to walk on your own. Great place to view migrating birds.
We walked the lake trail. The information signs provide geological information. We watched both swimmers and boaters having a great time. We will return at a later date.
Great facilities to appreciate the Navy's finest. The movie seemed to drag on, there were multiple 'endings.' It is a must see to appreciate our military heritage.
The trail was quite muddy on the back end, perhaps from re ent flooding. It is a heavily trafficked park. We saw several deer feeding about 25 ft. from the trail.
A community park that is extremely well priced for families. The location boasts: paddle boats, train, walking trail and a consession stand. Glad we visited.
Very well maintained park. It is quite accessible to greater Raleigh region residents. The trails offer modest challenge to hiking enthusiasts.
First time visit to this garden. It is well designed with botanical surprises for all interests. I especailly enjoyed the ponds.
Unusual historical and faith center. We did not wait for the tour. We shopped for great books and gifts here.

If you're in Balboa park, this museum is probably worth checking out for a bit. The exhibits themselves are a bit of a hit or miss at times. Despite anthropology being a wildly interesting subject, I would myself at times questioning why certain exhibits were there, and definitely left with the impression that this wasn't entirely worth my time. The Maya section is fascinating, and the recent Cannibalism exhibit is interesting, but at times frustratingly vague and thin on details. Kids might enjoy this, while hardcore history buffs might not.

Free art visits, and fantastic exhibitions on a regular basis. If you come on a weekday you won't have trouble parking. Great for all ages. Good lighting and really some truly incredible pieces in the collection. You could spend an afternoon here without getting burnt out. I really enjoy the 1600-1890s era paintings, lots of landscape paintings, abstract, modern, antiquity, you name it.

There really is something here for everyone. Go relax in the park after reveling in the collective creativity of humanity.

There really is no place quite like this. The ethos of this church is pure and inspiring. The custom artwork really ties the place together. The owners/members are very kind people that were able to answer any questions we had. Very cool gift shop/rec room on the first floor.

They are doing something very different here. You really get the sense that the members of this community care for each other in a deeply spiritual way. This community is paving the way for the mindfulness revolution.
likes: Facilities & Services: Custom artwork, Kind owners/members, Gift shop/rec room

reviews_attraction.text:
The Denver Art Museum has something for everyone. The installations right now are a very inspiring collection of themed works, as well as an installation by a famous Native American inspired artist. The fee is reasonable to get in, and the curation of the art is great.
A big chunk of the museum isn't open due to construction and renovations, thus the 4 stars. It'll be better than ever once the place is back up and running. Great for kids, and artistically unrealized adults!

A beautiful church and complex. The visitors center is warm and inviting, even if you are not a practicing Mormon. The people working here truly are kind and understanding, and were very friendly and excited that I was there to see the church. Visiting for the architecture alone is worth it. The church was closed on a Monday, so I recommend coming on other days or calling to see if the interior is open. Absolutely a must see in Oakland.

I loved the layout, the choice of animals, and the design of the Zoo in general. The modern design had a flow to it that other older Zoos I've been to have lacked. It's smaller; I was in and out within a couple of hours, but I liked that. The food is pricy, definitely, if you want to feed a family of four here seriously reconsider. The animals appear well taken care of, and the giraffes are truly the best and goofiest part of the Zoo.

Wow, what a place! Definitely a must for anyone in the area, and anyone visiting. The entirety of the gardens are worth viewing, with an incredible attention to detail and lovely walkways. Checking out the library is a must, and everyone should see the Gutenberg Bible. There's loads of activity places for kids, and there's no shortage of parking. And there's cafes here! It's got it all. The architecture alone is worth it.

Came in from out of town and knew I had to see the Da Vinci exhibit. Was not disappointed! Great exhibits and very oriented around kids. Friendly and helpful staff and lots to see and do. Took a star off for parking. Parking was definitely a nightmare, and that might just be a result of Denver's exploding growth. Tickets here are also not cheap. Prepare to be surrounded by kids.

Wonderfully creative and awe-inspiring. Free to see with the possibility for donations if you're willing. Quite a few metal found object sculptures, and the owner/creator is often outside working on projects during the day. You could come here to take a picnic, or just to see these creations. This is worth coming to just to see what he's created. Truly a gem. Recommended.

This is definitely a museum for motorcycle fanatics! They've got so many interesting, jaw dropping motorcycles. Take time walking around, and take some photos. Pretty great attached bar, restaurant, and hotel next to this place. They host events, too. The Mac and cheese fest we went to was super fun and very entertaining to say the least. Worth a weekend visit for sure.

A must see experience in San Francisco. The story of the ship and simply being on this vessel is an incredible experience. The volunteers are absolutely awesome people, and they were delighted to fill me in on anything that came up. Make sure to check out the engine room and the crew quarters...and everything. See everything. Great for anyone interested in history.

Great views, and an appropriately sized museum and exhibits detailing what NCAR does and why it's important. Special area telling the history of the architecturally significant building and layout. Area describing the computer sever racks/mainframe. Given that it's free, this is an incredible experience to see inside this important institution.

I might be more critical of this garden if you had to pay to go inside, but parking and seeing this is free. It's a beautiful little place that's tended to very well. Definitely a worthy Japanese garden, and the nicest free Japanese garden I've ever been to. Beautiful and great for a walk with a loved one, or just alone. No dogs allowed. 🐕

Really beautiful park and setting. Great trails to walk, albeit a tad unkempt in some sections. The scenery is worth it all. The camp grounds aren't as well maintained as they should be. That said, worth many trips for bike rides, or hiking, or just walking around. Can't speak to anything inside, since it was the weekend.

The crown-jewel of art museums in KC. Extensive and impressive collections-- Greco-Roman sculptures and artifacts, Egyptian, Hindu, an incredible stained-glass collection from the medieval era, etc. Too much to list. It's incredible and free. A great example of a truly remarkable museum inside and out.

It's hard to imagine a more thorough and detailed exhibit and museum to showcase this unique historic unearthing. The artifacts are remarkable given the circumstances, our guide was knowledgeable, and the layout is thoughtful and detailed. So much to learn and know about this. Great gem in KC.

So glad I took a chance on this museum. Truly a wonderful gem in Pueblo. The volunteers know a ton about the history of the contents here, but the tour is self guided. It took me 2 hours to get through everything here. Lots of little fun pieces here that'll make you go 'woah, they have THIS?!'

Definitely a must for Estes. Expect at least an hour long wait for this. Easiest way to get up the mountain, presumably. The top is worth it for the view. The cafe at the top is also great and has some very friendly staff. Probably a fantastic experience for kids and adults.

Make no mistake, seeing this glorious beetle will take about 10 seconds. That said, it probably will make for a decent photo op, and you can tell all your friends that you saw the world's largest beetle. I wish I could get closer, but I have to love from afar.

The Escher exhibit opening was completely fantastic and exactly the kind of thing this space was made to hold. The Hall of Fame otherwise has a good amount of detail and history for the main attractions as well. Very well put together place. Classy and clean.

Although this place is only open one day a week, it's completely worth visiting. Such an incredible collection of Shelby cars, and other artifacts and pieces. The staff is friendly and enthusiastic. You'll probably spend an hour here or so. Worth the trip!

A beautiful beach and park with places to park and enough space to really enjoy it all. Not as crowded as I might have expected. Lots of nearby motels and restaurants, and the goofiest squirrels you'll ever meet. Worth a trip for the views and photography!

Truly a great experience. We walked around for a while and took in the fantastic scenery and mindful curation of flora. Clearly great attention has been taken to every aspect of this garden. Great for kids and adults alike. Sit and appreciate this beauty.

One of the best botanical gardens I've been to. Very helpful staff, very well curated gardens, and I love the additional art in the garden. Every part is worth seeing. Pretty busy, so I recommend going when it's less so.
A beautiful place with some of the world's most beautiful plants. I have a membership and I love going to all of the member exclusive events.

TOURISTY BUT FUN = The ceiling to floor windows wrap around the whole 103rd floor allowing bird-eye views all around the Willis Tower. According to a sign on good days you can see areas from four different states! The windows were mostly clear allowing great pictures of the city below. Staff members constantly walk around the floor making sure people aren’t going past the railings. I imagine this place can get packed during tourist season because it didn’t seem like they could cap the incoming flows reasonably. THE SKYDECK = there were three available stations were you could walk out on the glass floor and be surrounded on three sides. Creative selfies ensue. The glass here seemed clearer than the windows. With no one actively patrolling this area (probably because it was off-season) us guests were left to share and luckily no group hogged the areas for long times. OTHER THINGS TO DO = There’s only bathrooms and a small gift shop up there. Not really any chairs. Pay-per-use binoculars are affixed to the floor. Back on the floor you pass at least TWO Skydeck gift shops and small Café.

“I don’t feel like I’m in Naples anymore.” With wide paths, a handful of themed areas, large landscapes, and nice use of water … this place is huge! Windy paths and green borders also help to further shield the true size of the place and make you feel transported. While not every area was breathtaking, there are definitely some wedding-prom-jumpshot-photo inducing spots. Most areas have beautifully manipulated nature and presented them in a manicured way. With long, walk-through arches, waterfall hub, zen garden, statues—it seems a little bit of everything you see in a stereotypical themed garden is placed here. Although each plant is nicely labeled, there’s still more explanation that can be done on behalf of the landscapes. This is still a very pretty place to keep ALL ages interested. And due to the size, come prepared with water. There’s not many little shops (if any) midway through this vast garden to provide thirsty and hungry travelers with sustenance or a shaded rest.

COOL IN SUMMER=This nature park is especially great during the sunny months because of the abundance of thick trees that shield out most of the harsh sun. ACTIVITIES SURROUND EXPLORING= Although you’re over the water, I haven’t seen anybody fishing. There actually is a large clearing towards the center which is a gathering for birthday parties (in surrounding pagodas), soccer games, and other impromptu team sports. There’s a launching area for kayaks/canoes (and rentals). And of course there’s many casual bikers as well as joggers. ANIMAL WATCHING= Of course there’s the paved trails and boardwalks, but some dirt trails shoot off from those and really put you among the trees. The best boardwalk (near the education center) borders the Hillsborough River where it becomes very easy to see many bird varieties and gators/crocs. I’ve also encountered eagles, owls, turkeys, and armadillos.

SKIP THIS TOUR. Even for the relatively low price it WASN’T WORTH IT. Yes you get on a bus that drives you to the location of haunts around the town. You disembark to get a closer look at two particular locations. But before and after those two locations the BUS JUST RACES PAST THE LOCATIONS from its stories (going with flow of traffic). You don’t have time to stare at any site to search and be a little afraid. Our guide knew her stuff, BUT HER AGE WORKED AGAINST HER (a definite college girl reflecting the stoic “like… like… like” used by her generation). THE STORIES DID NOT COME TO LIFE through her telling (which is almost essential to a supposed ‘haunted’ tour). But the story teller who took over at the Old Jail by pretending to be a former prisoner and told the haunts in first person narrative played his part (insane, crazed, schizo emotions) very well.

[Warning: Young adults from Central Florida in for vacation] Free admission. A visitor center sits at the top of the hill with amenities. Those with WALKING DISABILITIES WILL FIND IT VERY DIFFICULT TO DESCEND into the ruins area. On it’s own, the Bath Ruins aren’t much; The largest remaining structure of the Ruins is COVERED WITH SOME PRETTY COOL GRAFFITI, but most of the ruins just look like short, stone walls peeking out of the water. It was pretty FUN TO WALK ATOP THOSE STONE WALLS, and you’ll see even kids doing it. The visitor center was closed when we visited, so we had to research the history of the Ruins on our own since there aren’t any history signage down there. Surrounding the ruins are GREAT TRAILS ZIG-ZAGGING ALL THROUGHOUT Land’s End that provide even more beautiful views (and make you feel like you’re away from the city).

It’s crazy to think I was still in Florida—but this is the REAL Florida! Although there’s a lot to do here (after the car entrance fee) such as canoeing, hiking, and experiencing nature up close, I went here for the cave tours. You NEED to book a tour to enter the caverns which is an additional fee. Our young tour guide was very friendly, bubbly, and relatable to the kids in the group. The tour is only an hour long but felt much longer as you move between six different ‘rooms’ underground. The Florida Caverns can easily compete with more popular American caves like Lurray and Mammoth in beauty albeit a smaller size. TIPS: the temp is a constant 65 degrees under there. What began as a welcome reprieve from the summer heat became chilly after 45 minutes. Hike a nearby tour too—there’s mild elevation changes and very well-kept, dirt paths.

(Warning: Young adults from Central Florida in for vacation) There’s NO REAL SIGNS POINTING OUT THE PATH or saying where to park, so the little crowd of people you’ll definitely run into are there because of good ol’ Google. A relatively short, uphill hike away, you’ll get to TWO FANTASTIC AREAS FOR PICS with the sign. As someone who was there because my relatives live within the sign’s shadow, I understood the neighborhood’s frustration at the wandering tourists and wanna-be models, but I also know this is not a ‘gated’ neighborhood either. The walk from Lake Hollywood Park - where many cars park to the back of the sign can take almost an hour up. There’s NO BATHROOMS OR WATER FOUNTAINS in between. Plus, you’re hiking through people’s neighborhood - so please be respectful.

During our Saturday early afternoon visit, there were only one or two others. I attribute LOW ATTENDANCE TO ITS LOCATION IN DOWNTOWN ORLANDO- an area still working on getting weekend visitors. Front desk worker Tre was very CHATTY AND PASSIONATE ABOUT THE PLACE which features a continuously rotating cast of local, young and hip artists. CITYARTS IS ROUGHLY THE SIZE OF A SUBURBAN HOME with each room featuring an artist. Most of the medium is paint but it shows up in murals along the hallways, staring back at you from the water fountain, and within many frames. This place OPERATES ON A SUGGESTED DONATION of $5 (and they’ll validate a portion of your parking at a particular garage). I’m definitely interested in returning and seeing what new, local talent is on display.
likes: Unique artwork placement (e.g., murals, water fountain)

reviews_attraction.text: CENTER OF IT ALL = This is one of those iconic-Chicago-things-to-do-selfie spots. You can’t visit this city without visiting “The Bean.” With its location in Millenium Park, there’s many other things to do and see nearby—it’s a short walk to many other of the Park’s wonders as well as many food and shopping places in the surrounding city. THE BEAN ITSELF = There will always be a crowd trying to take advantage of the interesting photos that can be had from the reflective, curved surface—even during the cold weather. The area immediately surrounding Cloud Gate also offers great views of the city buildings—more great selfies! Even though it’s very ‘touristy’ I totally recommend visiting this art installment because it’s so ‘Chicago-ish’ and its location is perfect.

This place sums up all the quaintness of Downtown Lakeland through one circular walkway. Although there are no swans in this Lake, you admire the lake from the walkway bordering the Lake and pass by several sights along the way (little signs along the way instruct you further)
The Lake itself is simple and beautiful to look at. It’s not surprising to run into many people jogging, strolling, or taking photos on the spacious path. Along the way you’ll run into the Hollis Gardens (Attack of the bridal photo ops), Barnett Family Park (kids will act like monkeys all over the playground), and a handful of artistic sculptures. Luckily there are several public areas to have a picnic or use the bathroom yet the entire walk revealed nothing but clean ground.

I guess all the tolls and admission just to enter the park help deter some of the wild, annoying young’uns because although it was busy during my weekend visits, it never felt like a Spring Break party. Sure almost every square foot of the thin beach sand was staked by a family, but trash tended to stay in the trash bins, bathrooms were decent, and drunken laughter didn’t fill the parking lots.
I prefer the ‘non-beach’ activities where it’s possible to escape most crowds (some not all). Kayaking the open waters (there’s a rental place) walking/biking the trails (not really scenic because it follows the road), and exploring the relatively young fort. Even without a dog it’s fun to watch the popular Dog Beach for all the cute pups.

Mind you, THIS ISN’T A VERY LARGE PARK but I did wonder why there was NO PLAYGROUND FOR THE KIDS while one parent is shopping around. Nothing made me want to play Frisbee on the grass or have a picnic on the side… it just didn’t seem like the type of park to do that at EVEN THOUGH THERE WAS PLENTY OF SPACE. After passing all the cute, northern-styled homes and shops to get here, I expected the park to reflect more of that—BUT IT WAS RATHER PLAIN.  The old Train Station is not visually impressive however the ease of TAKING PHOTOS ON THE TRACKS can bring a few of the photographers out. Even on a gorgeous day it SEEMED MOST OF THE VISITORS WOULD RATHER BE AT THE SHOPS or the benches on the outskirts of the park instead of in it.

Although this is a VERY SMALL PARK, its location along with several unique charms still make it stand out to other also-beautiful parks. Demen’s Landing gets an outdoor stage for theater productions in some parts of the year. It’s also a GOOD LAUNCHING POINT FOR THE 20+ MILES LONG PINELLAS TRAIL  (great for biking/jogging) and one of the lots offers FREE PARKING. When the sun gets hot but I still want to dine outside, (I think) Demen’s Landing is the only place nearby where there are PICNIC TABLES UNDER A SHADE! (Plus great WATERSIDE VIEWS with dolphins playing) Plus having BATHROOMS NEARBY is great. Unfortunately it’s a bit small for kids to run around—the playground is pretty small plus the waterfront offers no railings.

I totally recommend taking the free “tour” because you can superficially see the whole fort in less than an hour. It’s not a tour at all but begins with a cannon demonstration by period actors. From there each one delivers storytelling speeches about young America entering war. While the acting was very convincing, children may become restless. In wandering the fort, there are signs and plaques in various locations delivering explanations for certain points. Personally I would’ve preferred even more signs delivering more about the background of the areas. There’s not a lot of scenery change within this fort, however the small second floor has great views of the Savannah River as well as cannons to touch.

(Warning: young adults from Central Florida in for vacation) After a great week at BBNP, we entered a rainy weekend in Alpine. The Museum was INDOORS, NEARBY, AND FREE (donations welcome)… yet it FAR EXCEEDED OUR EXPECTATIONS of just another way to escape the rain. The museum itself is probably just a little larger than a three-bedroom home yet somehow SO MANY EXHIBITS COVERING A VAST AMOUNT OF TOPICS ARE DISPLAYED- and very organized as well. We saw fossils found around the parks, the history of its geographical formations, historic sites around Alpine, typical goods for sale from stores long ago… the accompanying signs were very informative and there are MANY VISUALS TO CAPTIVATE CHILDREN.

I was very surprised to find this free, natural paradise hidden behind a handful of boring business buildings. It’s definitely not a big park—don’t expect fields for footballs—but it’s location along the Tampa Bay waterfront make for some nice panoramic views of the Causeway Bridge (the future includes having a bike path start from this park and connect to the Causeway) The main hub contains a few small pagodas and small picnic tables for eating as well as nearby bathrooms. The ‘beach’ is rather thin (three feet or less wide) but it wraps around most of the park. Following that beach around all the overhanging bushes leads you to some pretty secluded, visually calm areas.

(Warning: young adult visitors from Tampa Bay in for the weekend) Thankfully THIS PICTURESQUE LITTLE LAKE has a sidewalk (not the widest thing) that encircles the whole thing. THE DISTANCE AROUND IS ONLY 0.6 MILES. There’s also several features to make this little walk more enjoyable such as a land pier that juts into the center of the lake allowing 360-degree views, random MOM-AND-POP SHOPS housed in cute buildings to one side, and public bathrooms. Unfortunately, this lake is also marred by some SEEMINGLY SHADY CHARACTERS who like to loiter by the shady picnic tables. THE BATHROOMS WERE A MESS INSIDE and I left after I heard lots of random groaning from inside a stall.

This is a beautiful and relaxing park in the bustling Downtown Naples area, but it can be active if you want it to! Although the official ‘sports courts’ are tennis and baseball, there is a nice shady field which is the site of many concerts, entertainment, and art shows. The nearby playground is also huge and will keep kids distracted long with its artsy wood look and lots of hiding places and obstacles.  My favorite part is its proximity to 5th Avenue (just cross the street)—not only is there a nearby free parking garage but when you want to relax away from the touristy 5th Avenue, it’s easy to just go over here and plop on a bench.

It’s tempting to treat this place like a playground with its stairs, thick walls, and maze-like areas… but luckily the strict staff knows how to sweetly approach rule-breakers because this place CAN GET PACKED WITH UNCARING KIDS. As you enter the rooms, MOST CONSIST OF INFORMATION STANDS and only the OCCASIONAL AUTHENTIC HISTORY behind some glass. I would’ve liked to see some rooms fitted to look like how they did back then. Climbing to the top reveals FANTASTIC VIEWS OF THE WATERFRONT as well as the site for their DAILY CANNON DEMONSTRATIONS. NOTE: you don’t need a ticket to enjoy the beautiful, waterfront grounds of the fort.

[Warning: young adults from Central Florida here for just a visit] Since we wouldn’t be in the area long, we took a crash course of PIEDMONT PARK BY BIKING through it-- via the Relay Bike Share bike rental. I love parks with MANY BUILT-IN ACTIVITY AREAS such as dog parks, tennis courts, bocce ball, gardens… and all of those were spread out among the huge Piedmont Park space. YOU ALMOST THINK YOU’VE ESCAPED THE CITY. There’s a plethora of bathrooms and water fountains-- always a plus. My favorite part was deep into the park - the northeast area - where the crowds disappeared, and we had the paths to ourselves.

AWESOME PLACE FOR PHOTOS! Relaxing place for AIRPLANE WATCHING. Those are the two biggest reasons to visit this little strip of a park. On a good day I’ve passed photo sessions at the entrance (so you can get the flashy, blue dome of the Dali Museum as well as the steps of the Mahaffey Theater in the background) and ALONG THE WATERFRONT (capture BOTH THE ST. PETE SKYLINE AND the little yachts). And since it’s right against the airport you can watch the planes wheel around and take off. Just to round things off there’s AMPLE PARKING (metered), PLAYGROUND with an airplane theme, and CLEAN BATHROOMS.

With the convergence of the three rivers and great views of the skyline and other sites, this is a great breather AWAY FROM ALL THE CONCRETE as well as a GREAT PHOTO SPOT. But you’ll also find MANY LOCALS HANGING OUT here enjoying the fields (when the weather is nice) or the college-aged groups hanging out at the overlook near the Fountain. FUN, CLEAN AREA  with little areas to explore. There’s NO PLACES TO RENT bikes or kayaks on the grounds yet you’ll find plenty of people using them around here.

(Warning: Young adults from Central Florida visiting for the week) This was actually the first trail we attempted at BBNP and it was a GREAT INTRODUCTION FOR HIKING- great VIEWS OF BOTH THE RIO GRANDE AND THE CANYON, mild elevation, and it was a short hike. PERFECT FOR FAMILIES. Everyone- especially children- will like the trail’s end where a large bed of smooth, whimsical rocks push right against the water.

This is a nature lover’s park but also a great place for parties in the huts! Bring your small boat and launch it here into the bay—for everyone else there’s a lot of water side views to enjoy. I enjoyed walking among all the trees and shoving children off the rock climbing wall in the playground (j/k… I think) This is also a clean park with scattered restrooms and pretty trash-free.

This is a very clean and well-designed park combining… 1.) art (bronze statues scattered throughout)… 2.) exercise (many sidewalks to jog and a nice “exercise playground”)… 3.) activities (community center on-site, wide empty field, seasonal events)… 4.) kids! (one of the BEST PLAYGROUNDS in the Bay—lots of moving stuff and things to climb—adults welcomed)

Beaver Brook Watershed Trail was a happy find. From the ample parking lot, follow the service road a short distance through a beautiful meadow, but make a left when you see a small foot trail going into the forest. Keep your eyes open for old homestead ruins and an old Model A Ford rotting where it was abandoned, who-knows-when. A number of lean-tos are in the area where people occasionally camp, and the forest is... simply... stunning. Listen for owls and watch for northern flickers.

The hike is beautiful, about 2.75 miles to the falls, and although they say it is moderate, it is tough, man. But worth it, if you can tolerate all the irresponsible dog owners. You will encounter 10 to 20 unleashed dogs, some growling and barking at each other. AND  you will see 8 to 12 plastic bags filled with dog poop, where these irresponsible dog owners have left the pet's poop, thinking that YOU will pick up after them.

If you visit Haleakala NP in Maui, the hike into the valley ("crater") is a must. However, hiking back up is a pain in the... whole body. You can hike down though, to a Hiker's lot, and catch a ride back up to your car from a fellow traveler. So! If you see hitchhikers in the designated pullout lane on your way up, consider picking them up... they just hiked for miles, and are not likely escaped convicts.

The hike that goes through the Maxwell Falls area is stunning. This hike goes through several ecologically unique sections that you just can't miss. Also, just a few yards off this trail is my secret hiding place where I often go to write. (You'll never find it!) :) I've sat under "my" pine tree while two huge herds of elk walked by on both sides of me. First the females,  then the males. Fascinating.

The Arapahoe and Roosevelt National Forests are not things you can see in a day. It takes many trips, many hikes, and only a small amount of curiosity. The environments and foliage vary greatly, and never ceases to impress. Keep your eyes and ears open for wildlife... we've seen deer, elk, bear, fox, coyotes, moose, raccoons, northern flickers, owls, woodpeckers and more. Take it all in!

We love Barr Lake. It's changes all year long so it's rarely quite the same. We've been watching the family of Bald Eagles for years. They raise their young and teach them to hunt the Canada geese that flock there every year. Fascinating to watch. Bring your camera! Deer, coyotes, fox, owls, fish jumping, ducks, geese, eagles, fall leaves, winter snow, spring flowers...

Great for kids! All kinds of outdoor activities and playground regulars like things to climb and ride. They even have a modern day see-saw that is safe! (Remember how danderous the old see-saws were? Not any more... pretty clever!) It doesn't stop there, either. The designers added some features that get kids thinking and wanting to learn and explore. I was impressed!

If you just want to get in a quick hike in cool weather, this hike is fine. There is a lot of traffic noise though, little shade, and keep in mind that it is for Highlands Ranch residents only. Also, the trail is closed the first quarter of every year for animal migration. You can still walk the East West Trail, but that just goes along the busy street (Monarch).

Getting to the lookout point on Eagle's View Trail is hard work, but worth the effort. The views are fantastic. The forest is peaceful. The air smells sweet from blooms you may have never seen before. Deer might want to hang out with you for a bit. Sit on a fallen tree for a few minutes and rest easy knowing it is downhill all the way back. :)

Great tour, fantastic crew, delicious breakfast and lunch, AND a worthy Catamaran. Some of the best snorkeling on Earth, too. The good ship Leila plowed through medium rough water without slowing a knot. Despite the choppy seas, the captain navigated through the waves expertly, picking out the smoothest path possible. Highly recommended!

We were impressed with the stunning beauty of this canyon. There is nothing else like this in our entire solar system. We took the time to explore every point of interest, and go on at least part of every hike. We were glad we did, too! There was something different on each hike. Bring plenty of water and good hiking boots. :)

I'm not trying to put any ideas in anyone's head, but my wife and I got married at the top of Mt. Evans. On top of the world! We go back every year and we are never disappointed. The M. Walter Pesman Trail is one of the best hikes in Colorado, and the 1000+ year old bristlecone pines simply have to be seen and admired.

Giant redwoods in Maui? Yes, although they are not there naturally. They are part of a conservation effort, along with other trees, still, the forest is beautiful, as is the hike to get to them. The drive there is treacherous, not for the faint of heart or those with fear of heights or mediocre driving skills.

That first 1/2 mile or so does look appealing, and it is as it looks, boring with road noise. However, when you get over that first hill, your soundings change for the better... Stunning Colorado scenery. We've heard or seen owls and woodpeckers and walked among small herds of mule deer. Get there early!

One of the best hikes in Colorado. The ecosystem changes several times along the trail, so it feels like you walked 3 or 4 different hikes. Somewhere a few yards off that trail is also a favorite place for me to write. It's that beautiful and peaceful.

If you enjoy beautiful Colorado, and hearing busy Interstate traffic a couple hundred yards away, and hearing trains rolling by a couple dozen feet away, this trail is for you. Leave dogs at home, because there are no dogs allowed.
Fascinating place! If you make this drive, take the hike and pay attention to tiny details in plants and lava rock. You'll see species you've likely never seen before.
Creeks, ravines, meadows, views, pines and junipers... Beautiful hikes, perfect picnics. And nearly all the dog owners keep their little friends on a leash.
Fascinating glimpse into two or three hundred years into the past. If you visit Maui, I highly recommend taking an hour or two and seeing these Petroglyphs.
This place is underrated. I took two of my grandsons to Legoland and they LOVED it! One was 5 and the other was 15, and both were equally entertained.
I rode the Miniature Train over 50 years ago, and now my kids and grandkids are riding it. Hats off to the maintenance crew and efforts.
A great local jewel! If you're in the area and have children that love dinosaurs, the Rocky Mountain Dinosaur Research Center is a must.
Aspen groves, a variety of evergreens, fern-covered forest floors... Elk, deer, bears, foxes and owls... beautiful. Nature at its best.
Elk, deer, bear, eagles, rivers, lakes, mountains... want to take an award winning photo? Point your camera anywhere and click it. :)
My 5-month-old was thoroughly amused! The colorful fish moving around in the tanks seemed to mesmerize him. Money well spent!

Camp Ondessonk is an amazing place! I have been there many times. I have slept out in the treehouses and I am here to tell you that during a thunderstorm these are the place to be! Some of the best sleep I have ever had. I have also stayed in the St. Noel Center. The rooms are cozy and comfy.
We have taken guided and unguided hikes on the property. The trails and waterfalls are beautiful. I love walking out on the swinging bridge. When we stayed and used their meal services the food NEVER disappoints. I highly recommend this location for church retreats, camping weekends, family outings, scout troops and whatever your outdoor fun may be. Fishing, hiking, canoeing, kayaking, archery, horseback riding. You should check out all the events and special weekends they offer along with summer camp for the kids.
likes: Variety of activities (fishing, hiking, canoeing, kayaking, archery, horseback riding)

reviews_attraction.text:
I have been here a few times for events. I am always pleased with my visit. I was able to fullfill a lifetime dream and see the Rockettes at Christmas here. The show was AWESOME!! We were not allowed to take pictures which made me sad, but at the same time it helped me to totally focus on the experience and enjoy every moment. We sat in the balcony and it was a perfect view.
Last year I was able to participate in an Audience Company of Nashville event and be a part of the CMA Country Christmas on ABC. This was an AWESOME event as well. We enjoyed ourselves and would definetly take the opportunity to do this again.

What a great place to visit. We took the riding tour of the planes out on the field. I highly suggest paying the money to do this. We were able to view all planes, helicopters and such. Being able to ride on the tram was much better than walking the whole place. We also were given information via our guide of all the aircraft.
We spent time touring the museums inside and looking at all the interesting facts provided. The kids enjoyed the many interactive areas.
If you love history and aircrafts March Field Air Museum is a great place to go!

A great little jewel hidden in the desert. Our guide had much knowledge and was very informative. We all truly enjoyed this place.
There are alot of museums to tour so make sure you have alot of time when you go. You can walk around on your own, but I highly suggest waiting for a guide and listening closely. So many neat trains and lots and lots of history to see and hear about here.
Staff was friendly. We went during the day on a weekday. They were not busy and we had plenty of time to tour.
I highly suggest visiting this place!

My husband always loved the the story of Paul Bunyan and Babe the blue ox. When I found out this town was his home I got excited. We were on a quick trip here so we didn't have time to explore, but we visited this park and can't wait to come back to see everything else. What a neat little place. The lady working was kind and full of information. She actually had friends that were in our how town visiting. What a neat coincidence. There were lots of neat things to look at too.
Restrooms and facility was clean.

This is a clean and nice public park with beautiful views. The boys rode their bike and scooter down to the park and the ladies walked.
There are lots of things for the kids to play on and the surface under the equipment is really nice. Slides, climbing things, huts to crawl in, little picnic table, big picnic tables.
We love going over to the park and relaxing while the kids play. Thank you City of Perris for such a nice place to go and for the kids to play!

AMAZINGLY BEAUTIFUL! We only drove over Trail Ridge Rd to Estes Park for family pictures but the drive and scenery were like none other that I have ever experienced. My only concern was not enough guardrails along the "scary" (to me) parts of the drive. I would love to go again one day and really take time to stop and photograph the scenery. We made brief quick stops and drive by pictures because we were meeting the photographer at a certain time.

This was our first time coming to Afton Alps. The staff were all friendly and the resort was beautiful.
My 13 year old son had never snowboarded before and had to get fitted for all the gear. I wish the staff would have came out and really helped him in more detail. They didn't really explain any of the gear.
I enjoyed our time at Afton Alps and hope my son tries snowboarding again one day, sadly he got discouraged quickly and quit.

The falls are beautiful, but there were SO MANY people here. I am from Southern IL and when I hike even in a State Park I never encounter so many people. I enjoy being more alone in nature. If you are looking for beautiful pictures and a peaceful experience go super early in the morning. Wear good walking shoes, light comfortable clothing and take a water bottle as the climb back out is harsh. Nice trail, but steep!

Christmas at Cheekwood was Absolutely beautiful! I truly enjoyed walking the gardens and seeing all the lights.
They do not accept cash at this time so make sure you have a debit or credit card with you.
Layer allot and dress warm. We used hand warmers and toe warmers and that made a huge difference!
They have S'mores pits, but you have to pay to make them.
The blown glass is beautiful as well!!

A must see when in Metropolis. The history of Metropolis is rich with Superman and his legend. There is a Superman festival every year. There is also a Super Museum you can visit at Superman Square. There are cutouts to have your picture made with and a Lois Lane Statute at the other end of the street. Visit our Chamber of Commerce it is a nice place to buy souvenirs.

Great museum! Staff were all very friendly and helpful. My husband, son and I all enjoyed walking through and reading/looking at the exhibits. Well worth the time and money to stop by. My son had just studied this war in school so he was spouting off facts and information, makes a momma happy to know her kiddo listens in school 😁

Great place for a retreat. The dorms are clean and nice. Bathrooms are clean and the water is so nice and hot. There is a playground for the kids, disc golf and softball field. Dining hall is large and the food is good. The gym/stage area is nice as well. The lake is pretty.
I would definitely look forward to coming back here.

We have hiked here for years. As long as I can remember this has been a high priority place to take people when they were here visiting. Truly God's handiwork on major display. It's a must see if you are in Southern Illinois. ALWAYS be CAUTIOUS and CAREFUL! Many accidents here from falls.

I am rating this according to what my son-in-laws family say about it. I was there briefly while visiting Bagley but they weren't open yet. They love this place and stay here often.
I keep trying to remove it from my Google timeline and it keeps popping up so there we go 😁

Woodway Park is a great place to take your family. I attended an early morning boot camp with my aunt here and let me tell you I was worked to the edge of exhaustion. If you ever want to get fit you should join the boot camp that gathers here. It is no joke SERIOUSLY.

Amazing experience. If you lived during the Elvis era or like musical history this is a must for your to do list. Make sure to put on the headphones and listen to the information on the iPad they give you. I truly enjoyed the stories from Lisa Maria.

We love hiking and picnicking here. It is a beautiful park. I want to try out the camp grounds here. They look really nice.
I have used this park for photography and it makes wonderful pictures.
I highly recommend this area for lots of family fun!

We were passing through Van Buren on our way to Branson and stopped off to see Big Spring. What an wonderful display of God's handiwork. Beautiful bubbling underwater spring and gorgeous rocks to climb on. A MUST SEE if you are in the area.

What an enjoyable place. We were here for an Audience Company of Nashville event so we didn't do allot. I would like to come back sometime and do more. It's a beautiful building inside. I enjoyed the parts I was able to see.
The kids and adults both enjoyed this experience completely. Make sure you have plenty of time to spare when visiting here. It is a process that takes time. Well worth it and lots of fun.
We spotted this place as we were coming up the mountain and decided to make a quick stop, so glad we did. Beautiful place
We only looked at the outside cars. Not sure what the inside was like but we enjoyed listening to Mater talk!
A great historical places to visit. You need lots of time to tour this and really take it all in!
My 11 year old is a car nut and he loved this place!! He made me take a photo of every car.

It is bewildering why this institution is named the way it is, because in this context, the word "History" would generally be the main adjectival noun to modify "Center", with "Colorado" used as a supporting adjectival noun, thus should appear as "Colorado History Center." As it is, History Colorado Center does not roll off the tongue, and is in grammatical disagreement with the generally accepted adjective order in the English language. In any case, this place offers a selection of Colorado-specific history exhibits (Or are they history-specific Colorado exhibits?), and is a fun destination for kids.

The bike and pedestrian trail is a great way to get through this part of the city without much interaction with vehicular traffic. The sections of the trail are well marked and it connects with other trail systems, including the Platte River Trail on the Eastern end. There are several RTD light rail stations along the route. A disc golf course is along the parallel park. There is room for improvement, with perhaps better maintenance and expanded facilities, but is in general a great example of how a corridor centered on a trail should be implemented in an urban area.

As one of the guards told me when I asked about the location of the museum while I was in the Capitol building, "the whole building is basically a museum." That's about right. Several exhibits are sprinkled throughout, along with painted portraits of past governors. The gift shop is great for finding something California specific to bring back to kids at home when visiting on a business trip to Sacramento. In all, well worth the minimal effort of going through security to get into the Capitol.

The South Suburban Ice Arena is a terrific community resource, offering ice skating lessons for all ages, hockey leagues and games, and open skating times. It can get quite busy on weekends and holidays. The arena features a snack bar and a full service skate shop, where you can buy equipment and get your skates tuned or sharpened. There are a couple of ice shows hosted here each year, in which kids of any skill level can participate.

This state park is a terrific and easily accessible place to see some old growth coastal redwoods. It's a short drive from Santa Cruz and other nearby communities. The trees are so immense and block out so much light that at the forest floor, it is in perpetual shadow. This place is an amazing experience, and well worth a visit. Don't miss the easy walking loop to see some of the oldest trees.

A terrific place to visit with kids, and requires most of a day to do it right. Vast amounts of sea creatures and engaging, interactive exhibits. Tickets aren't cheap, but little is in Monterey. Regardless of price, the experience is unique. Truly a premier aquarium that is also a science and research center. Park your car in the public parking garage and take the free shuttle trolley.

Well worth a visit if you are interested in Western and/or railroad history. A few miles to the west of this site was the location of the Dale Creek Crossing, one of the highest railroad trestles ever constructed. Near the monument was the town of Sherman, where steam locomotives used to fill up on water and fuel at the highest point along the Transcontinental Railroad.

A key piece of Laramie history, the railroad depot is a gem. Built of locally quarried stone and little changed in more than a century, it is a popular site for weddings, parties, and other celebrations. Unfortunately, it's not in regular passenger service anymore, though vintage locomotives such as the UP 4014 Big Boy make the Laramie Depot an occasional stop.

Terrific, interactive museum/living laboratory. Lots of fun and thought provoking things to see, do, and explore. Kids and adults of all ages will experience new and unknown discoveries. It's a bit expensive, but a good value if you spend much of the day there. Who knows, your visit may inspire a family member to become a future scientist!

A world treasure of some of humankind's most amazing technical achievements. As impressive as everything in the museum is, the space exhibits are easily my favorite. Learning about what can be accomplished through science and engineering, and a committed societal focus toward a lofty goal can inspire young kids to shape the future.

Even more fun and informative today than it was when I first visited on a field trip as a kid decades ago. Some exhibits stay the same, and others change over the years, but there's always something new to see on each visit. The UW Geological Museum is an iconic part of the campus, and gem for people of the state.

An amazing resource and place to visit. Enjoyable and inspiring exhibits for the kids. Be sure to visit the animal landscape dioramas, many of which were constructed and painted more than half a century ago. They are truly amazing in the ability to trick the eye, especially in the current age of digital imagery.

Huge museum with a wide range of artistic styles to explore. A terrific choice to bring kids to introduce them to the world of art. Everything from classical paintings of the West, to indigenous art and historical features. Many opportunities for interactive engagement, and rotating featured exhibits.

Amazing outdoor recreation area, with a variety of challenging trails that beginners through experts can enjoy. Excellent scenic views of wildlife, the hogback, foothills, and the Denver metropolitan area. The location can be a bit too sunny/exposed on a hot day, so plan accordingly.

Terrific museum with engaging exhibits and rotating features. Nice gift shop. Easy to find and close to the Capitol and convention locations. If you're looking for gifts to bring back to your kids while on a from a business trip, this is a good choice.

This park has a nice playground, but a lot of the fun is in wading in the nearby stream and exploring the wooded area and trails. We stopped for a break on a trip across the state, but could have easily spent several hours here. A really great park!

Crowded and touristy, but that's Chinatown. The Dragon's Gate and surrounding neighborhood is something every visitor to San Francisco has to experience at least once. Great place for people watching, and exploring art and food.

A beautiful gem of Wyoming. Lots of places to explore, and easy to find camping, even on holiday weekends. Helpful staff at the visitor center. The road from Centennial to Saratoga is scenic, with pristine views.

Great place to ski with kids. Affordable lift tickets and food. Not as big as many ski areas, but just about right for skiers or snowboarders of all ages and abilities who aren't aiming for the X Games.
likes: Suitable for all ages and abilities

reviews_attraction.text: Huge park that is part groomed, part open space. Has a playground, sports fields, adjacent trails, and lots of room to run around. Terrific vistas of the foothills and mountains beyond.
Terrific beach to watch the sun set, as the name implies. Wide expanse of beach that isn't too crowded. Great views and lots of things to see and explore. Nearby camping.
Nice park, but be aware of protruding bolts on the underside of the playground equipment. My kid required 4 stitches to the forehead after running under a play structure.
Exemplary art deco industrial design. The bridge is fascinating to walk across in order to see details of its construction. Great views of the historic surrounding area.
Excellent place to visit with kids. Be sure to climb to the top of the block houses for a sweeping view of the Missouri River. Lots of history to see and experience.
Amazing historical site that is largely unchanged from more than 100 years ago. The annual rendezvous is a great event, and worth a visit.
