I had high Hope's for this luau, and unfortunately was disappointed, it was only okay. The schedule was communicated incorrectly numerous times. When booking or talking to staff beforehand, they always mentioned to arrive at 4pm and the luau would start at 5pm, guests dont even get to enter until 5pm and are given basically credits for all drinks including nonalcholic and sodas or out of pocket once done. The location was great giving a great sunset view, but the area seems to large for the programs provided. The food wasnt bad, buffet style, but you had to make sure you got as much as you planned to eat beforehand because food ran out quickly. There are dances that occur before the show while you are eating, but most people thought this was the actual luau performance. The show itself was what I'll call a more variety show than typical luau. There were way too many breaks in the show asking for guest participation and allowing odd events like a proposals occur. Alot of people actually left early. Favorite luau in the islands is still Old Lahaina Luau on Maui, this was something else entirely.

Went here for a private company event and it was alot of fun, but I can tell that it would be pricey if I had to pay my on way. Its located near the gondolas and food court. You get a parka and a set of gloves and then get to go inside the ice room, and it's cool to see all the ice sculptures and decorations and drink at the bar. But it will get cold even with the jacket, you really need to wear long pants and closed shoes, and even then you're going to feel cold from your exposed head, its roughly the same temperature if you were going to go skiing. The drinks are pretty good and the glasses are made of ice, which is recommended to hold with 2 hands. As for the food for private events, it was actually pretty good, with pasta and slider selections.

I came here for a corporate event so they closed it down for us. It was a great experience, they provide parkas and gloves to go inside. Please be aware, you really need to wear long pants or Jean's and wear totally closed shoes, my friends with shorts or sandals couldn't last more than 10 minutes before they had to go out. Also even if you do wear appropriate clothing, your head is still going to get cold. The drinks are good, alot of pina colada style drinks inside and shotskis are available. We had pasta and sliders for the provided dinner. Great experience overall if you want to feel like your going skiing inside the Venetian.
dislikes: Dress Code (requires long pants, closed shoes)

reviews_attraction.text: Been to here in the summer and in April, don't come in April. It's too cloudy to see the sunrise. For a trip from Kaanapali (leaving at 3:30am), only go in the summertime. It's a great experience. Important to note, that you need to get an advance reservation ahead of time, no exceptions (about $1.50) because they only allow about 60 cars in every morning. And there is another fee to enter the park per car. Also, dress appropriately for cold weather, you can see alot of people wrapped in towels without the correct clothing. Don't miss traveling a little further up from the summit parking to the higher observatory.

This is a must visit for any Disney fan. You get to learn so much about Walt Disney and the origins of what we know as the Disney company today. You can spend an entire day here and marvel at all the amazing facts and displays available. Currently there is a Mickey and the World special exhibit, which is great, but not as large as you'd expect and located in another ancillary building. The museum also includes a nice cafe and gift shop. Parking is fairly easy, but you still have to pay.

This is a great place to visit that a lot of people don't know about. The area is really rocky, so make sure if you bring kids to make them really watch their steps. The scenery is amazing and the waves come right over the rocks in a lot of places, there is also an odd flat maze that kids will love. Photographers will also love the unique scenery. Would recommend coming here and then going to Sansei for happy hour on the same road to get to the trail head.

Best part of Monterey, everyone will eventually stop by for a visit. It's not quite as large as other aquariums, but it does a fantastic job with the space it has and its exhibits. It's not cheap, about $50 for an adult, but it is well worth the money. Plan to spend 2-3 hours to see everything, more if you have children. The must see exhibits include the sea otters, penguins, and local sea life. The weekends are obviously busier than weekdays.

Great park, includes a playground, beach access, docks, dog park, etc. The tennis courts are undergoing refurbishments in summer 2018. Good place for kids and adults. Parking is a bit limited though so you'll have to wait until someone l leaves usually. Parking is also available from the community center located next to the park. Kids will love the playground and the beach especially. There is also a theater built into the grounds.

This is a great park with 3 main playground structures next to one another. There is also a great dragon sculture/play area slightly further from the main area. Kids will love coming here. There is also a small shelter with picnic tables and benches for parents to sit or hold items. Parking is a bit limited, but the main lot for island crest park is just slightly down the road a few minutes away with plenty of parking.

Great place to see Seattle and greater Seattle history, love the exhibits showing off the history of the area. The temporary exhibits are a bit underwhelming, it's currently on pets which really doesn't make sense and the exhibit looks like it was hastily thrown together. You really only need to visit this place once which is great, but with diminishing value each time you come back.

Great place to visit on Maui, interesting concept and great farm to table restaurants. A lot of the produce is destined for the on site restaurants. Tram tour lasts about 45 minutes and comes with pineapple at the end, there is also a zipline course that runs through the property.  Even has a great ice cream place on site that sells ice cream, gelato, and popsicles.

Iconic park with great skyline views of Seattle. Usually filled with tourists and local families using the playground. It's a great place to take photos and see all the old machinery, often there are alot of people taking professional photos using it as a backdrop. But keep in mind, it's not the cleanest park and mind the geese droppings that are everywhere.

Great state park. Has picnic facilities, beach access to Lake Sammamish, baseball field, etc. Even has stand up paddleboard rentals in the summer. Playgrounds is great for the kids to spend hours on. Parking requires a discovery pass otherwise you can purchase one from the front booth or park station on site. Often has activites and fairs in the summer.

I was actually a little disappointed with the show, it's certainly interesting and impressive in it's own right but doesn't quite live up to its reputation. The show is rather short and is a bit repetitive. Shows start at 3pm and beginning at 8pm run every 15 minutes.

Great place to take the kids, but it's basically the same as when I was a kid so the exhibits are becoming really dated. The kids will still have a great time though and it's a place to take the kids when you can't be outside. Butterfly room is still a favorite.

Amazing cultural experience highlighting ancient polynesian history all the way to modern Hawaii. Very educational, and alot of great exhibits. Parking is $5, and lasts all day. Kids should have a good time, but might get bored relatively fast.

The new location is good, but the pricing structure has changed so now membership is per kid, adult, there is no more family plan so it's really expensive now if you want to include the whole family and grandparents . Not enough places to sit.

This is perfect if you know what you're in for. Park anywhere and walk all the trails, but dont go off the marked trails. Entry fee is $10 and a guide is another $2, but they'll let you borrow one if you dont want to pay for one.

A very nice community park. It has 2 large soccer fields and a small playground along with bathrooms and plenty of parking. If you want to use the park primary for the playground others nearby are larger and just as convenient.

Great park, mostly for the playground which is shaded from all the tall trees nearby which makes it a bit different from the other playgrounds. Includes a baseball field and right next to the railroad train station.

Fun place to take the kids for a few hours, like people have said this is more of a kids playcenter and not a museum. Like the international sections, but like the rest of the museum, it's becoming dated.
Best part is the location is closer than Tulalip and Muckleshoot to the Eastside. Pretty normal for the local area casinos, restaurants aren't bad. The more you spend the better the food.
Great small zoo that people rarely know about since it's hidden in a residential area but easy to get to. They don't have a lot of animals, but they have reindeer during the holidays.
Great park, but unless you live or are visiting the Talus neighborhood, not sure why you'd want to come here instead of lake Sammamish state park.
A nice small little park right off of downtown. A great place to take a rest and see the river.

One of the most iconic parks in NYC and one of it’s most notorious. Currently going through a massive renovation, but that hasn’t kept the people away!

One of the newest dog runs in NYC complete with a small fountain! Bring your pup there to relax and have fun.

Beautiful place to visit in the summer. You'll usually spot a wedding party taking photos there by the main house, as it's a photogenic area. Take a walk by the back of the house & see the rose garden.

The most fun and different way to travel here is the tram - amazing views of Manhattan. You can also get here via the F train. The island is small, peaceful and very manageable if you want to walk it.
So many activities we love to do here...running on the track, walking our dogs, sledding, biking, roller hockey, and more. This park is absolutely gorgeous in the fall as the leaves change color.
Let your pooch run free in this large 2+ acre park with natural wood chips. Dog/human water fountains available for refreshments during the warm months and a separate gated area for smaller pups.
Go off leash & let your pup run free between 9pm-9am. Our suggestion on where to romp in this 585-acre park? Long Meadow where there's a small dog beach for cooling off during the warmer months.
Take your pups here for a taste of an agility course run at the Canine Court. The first public dog playground in the country! Walk along the running path after agility training for a cool down.
This massive sports complex has seen it’s ups and downs, but nothing can compare to a 7:30am swim in the outdoor lap pool for only $3 – evening sessions require the $30/month membership.
Make a point to visit the upper floors of the castle (only accessible by narrow winding stairs) and enjoy the best views of the park from the park. Call ahead to check if they’re open.
Line up early for Target Free Friday Nights when admittance is free from 4-8pm. Open until 8.45pm on the first Thursday of the month. Closed on Tuesdays. Grab lunch at Café 2!
On Wednesdays it's a "Suggested Donation" day which includes everything but a camel ride. So take a personal day and spend it exploring the wild wonders of the Animal Kingdom.
Break out your cross country skis and enjoy a wintery jaunt through the park. Skiing is allowed only when there is a base of snow of at least six inches - or so we've heard.
Be prepared to wait in line after line for each exhibit in this beautiful and modern gallery. Check out the view from the rooftop. Free admission every Thursday from 7-9pm.
Get the audio tour and head straight to Morgan’s library. The entire museum can be seen in just a few hours. Afterwards (or prior to) grab a bite to eat in the Dining Room.
You can’t fathom how large this pool is until you experience it. As with any public pool, make sure you bring a lock, wear appropriate suits and follow all the rules.
An increasingly popular place to see live music, especially famous DJs. Catch a ferry out here, and you'll be rewarded with amazing views of downtown Manhattan.
If you need a break from the city, you don’t need to go far. Visit this immaculate park with a date and a bottle of wine (hush hush)…its romantic and inspiring.
Be sure to buy tickets online beforehand so you can avoid waiting on a massive line on a nice summer day. We love to come here to watch the sea lions be fed.
Visit Williamsburg's wood chipped dog run for some fun and go out for brunch at one of the many neighboring dog-friendly outdoor restaurants in the area.
One of the most peaceful and tranquil museums in NYC – you’ll swear you heard the chanting of monks. The medieval tapestries and architecture is divine.
Relax and enjoy lunch or a good read a in this beautiful “secret garden”. Best to go when all the springtime flowers are in bloom. Fido is allowed too!
An inviting oasis that is a perfect spot for a picnic, people watching, a leisurely stroll or to take work outdoors as there’s free Wi-Fi here.
Has it all: hiking, canoeing, kayaking, fishing and biking. Great primitive campgrounds are available on segments of the Florida Trail.
Make sure you get on one of the red or blue swinging cars for the full experience. The yellow cars are for the less adventurous.
The pool gets overly crowded because it’s not that big. However, it is clean, not overly chlorinated and has great lap hours.

Park was fantastic. There were artists performing all around. Park was clean but full of small dogs but that was ok. We had fun enjoyed picnic here. Northern area of park was somewhat not cleaned but that doesn't matter a lot because people usually don't go to that side. It was all good. I will give 5 star for cleanliness.

This place hardly warrants a review, But since asked- Breathtaking appeal! Unlimited fun. Hikes aplenty. Freshest Air, greatest natural aromas! And waterfalls, lots of beautiful waterfalls. Almost guaranteed to see wildlife up close, Deers, Bears etc..

This park has lots to offer for everyone. There's lots to see within easy reach of the car and plenty of day hikes as well as multiple day options for backpackers. It's a rare day when you are overwhelmed by crowds. Enjoy your trip.

This beautiful place is adjacent to the Bayside Marketplace with several  interesting monuments and sculptures. Best thing to view here is electronically controlled Pepper Fountain. You can run or walk on the paved trails too.

This Park is nice place to sit down for a minute. It's also the highest point which is neat. It's filled with history. It also has plenty of benches to sit on and relax or read. There is a nice playground for children.

Beautiful, fun experience. This park is amazing to visit. The park rangers at each station are incredibly helpful in guiding you visit and keeping you safe. Would definitely visit again for the amazing views.
One of the best parks in Miami close to the airport. I love the greenery all around and the amazing views it has. Clearly I would say that I enjoyed my visit. It's really the best time we had here.
Nice place. Park is silent enough to relax during the weekends. Loved it. Sat here for 3 hours under the tree in the sun. Birds were chirping. There was total silence all around. Enjoyed well.
Went on a weekday, had nearly the entire park to ourselves.  Really enjoyed the hike we took.  My advice to those going hiking would be to take plenty of water, as it does get warm quickly.
Lovely park with loads of seating. I spent a little hour here with a coffee soaking up the sun after a busy morning exploring. The seating was surprisingly well kept and looked after.
Love sitting and watching everything that goes by. It's a good place to read a book, drink coffee and just sight see. I could spend hours sitting here and just thinking about life.
This is a great place to go for a long walk or bike ride. You can stop for dinner along the way at a few different places near this park. Best of luck for your visit.
Park is open enough. Very quiet and nice square. Also has some kind of installations for holidays. Nice place to take a load off while shopping or walking around.
Great Park! I love taking my dogs here. They have large and small breed section so it helps my little guys not get stressed. They keep the park pretty clean.
It is very well maintained. Nice size. Larger area for large dogs. Places in the shade for parents to sit. Place has many areas to sit and enjoy all around.
Park is fantastic. It has great views and cool environment. It's clean and green all around. Park authorities have maintained it well. Good one to explore.
This place is really fun. Liza is such a great and helpful employee here. The city should reward her for that. The elderly enjoy her attention and care.
Flowers. Music of all kinds at appointed times. So clean. Benches to seat. An oasis in the city. Lovely people oversee the activities. A gem.
Fantastic community green space, lots of activities every weekend. Good for yoga and meditation. There is a nice playground for kids too
We really enjoyed our visit. Beautiful park. Hike to the rocks and spend the day exploring. Best in spring or fall. Very hot in summer.
Beautiful place. Incredible opportunity to commune with nature primary. I've never been in this park, it is worth to come.
I've always lived this park. The city keeps it nice and clean. Close to everything a person needs! My son loves it too
Shockingly beautiful views of the park and the waterfall. You can admire it from high up. Best of luck for your visit.
It's a nice open space park with good seats and shade. It's a quiet place to relax. Just visit and enjoy the silence.
Nice park, I love to visit this place. This is a  big place and can do different activities. But always crowded..

Edgewater Park is the place to be! Since the Cleveland Metroparks acquired this into their system, Edgewater Park has moved up several notches! Edgewater LIVE is a wonderful event every Thursday on the shores of Lake Erie. Featuring food trucks, live music, and a beautiful sunset to cap it off. I can't wait to find out what else the Metropark System has in store for Edgewater! Making CLE proud Metroparks!

What beautiful architecture! I love the fact that this plantation is preserved in its original condition. There aren't many museums that can make that claim. The staff is very knowledgeable about the history and make the tours very interesting. We were so very pleased   that we stopped here!

This is such beautiful architecture and a wonderful historic remnant of Cleveland's past. If you haven't read the history of Squire's Castle, you should! There's hiking trails around the castle as well. But, the castle and its history make the visit well worth your trip.

One of the oldest public buildings in the United States and the oldest public building in Boston. The Declaration Of Independence was read from the balcony of this building and still is every 4th of July. It's a true historic landmark and well worth the visit.

Very interesting tour! Our tour guide was very knowledgeable and informative. The history of this building is fascinating. I never realized how many uses this building had throughout history. What a great historic asset this is to the city of Charleston.

This was one of our stops on our spontaneous Lake Erie Winery Tour. We're so glad we stopped out. The staff was very knowledgeable and courteous. We loved the cozy sitting areas to relax and drink our wine. We're looking forward to coming out again!

A peaceful park in the heart of Oberlin. What a relaxing place to be! It’s a great spot to bring lunch or to sit under a tree with a cup of coffee. We also enjoyed a concert on the square this past summer. What a great asset to the community!
What a wonderful Cleveland landmark! I've been there many times and the historical value to our city is unsurpassed. If you have the opportunity, take a guided tour. You won't be disappointed!
What a fantastic find!! The trails are well kept and beautiful! The house, stable, and gardens were an added bonus. What beautiful property with such a rich history. A valued community asset!
We had a wonderful time wine tasting! Buckeye Red was our favorite. The staff was very knowledgeable and courteous. We loved the cozy atmosphere and we're looking forward to coming out again.
Once home to the Shawnee Indians, this park is a hidden gem. A beautiful setting rich in history, hiking trails and a gorgeous lake. It's worth the visit and to stay awhile and explore.
We had a wonderful tour by a very informative host! This was a very interesting piece of Cleveland history. I’m so glad it’s so well taken care of and open to the public for tours.
What a great find while working in the Toledo area. The trails are beautiful and full of wildlife. It was so relaxing to just sit along side the Maumee River and enjoy the scenery.
Beautiful park! Great trails with interesting reasons to stop and explore along the way. I could spend an entire day here! What a wonderful, and historic, asset to the community.
I took the build a bird house class and was very impressed with the nature center and staff. I'm looking forward to coming back for another class and in the spring for a hike.
It's a great spot to search for beach glass! There's also a fishing pier, small beach area, and picnic area. Amazing views of the sunset too! What an asset to the community!
The oldest, continuously operational lighthouse on the U.S. side of the Great Lakes! A wonderful spot to enjoy the Lake and to tour this beautiful historic lighthouse.
What a beautiful historic location! A very peaceful park and trails to wonder through and enjoy nature. I look forward to walks there whenever I'm in San Diego.
Bring in your favorite take out and enjoy a great wine selection and relaxing atmosphere. Cute gift ideas as well! It's one of our favorite local Winery stops!
What a beautiful park! There's plenty of well kept trails, beautiful lakes, and some spectacular densely wooded areas. It's a great asset to the community!
What a wonderful find! It's such a peaceful setting with picnic tables, trails to explore and boat rental. What a great asset to the community!
What a beautiful park right on the shores of Lake Erie! We love the beach and watching sunsets from the pier! A true asset to the community!
The oldest continuously operational lighthouse on the US side of the Great Lakes!! You absolutely want to visit this historic gem!
What a beautiful walk in such a peaceful setting! Birds,  alligators, a lake and the swamps. We absolutely loved it here!
A beautiful public beach with plenty of picnic areas and an ice cream shop. A wonderful place for summertime family fun!

It was my first time at Fort Sumter and glad I finally made it. So interesting to see a site that is so integral to our history. I can only imagine what it was like back when it was fully built and functional. It was quite a bit smaller than I expected and to see that only one channel was really navigable. It must have been terribly loud when all those cannons erupted in those very small spaces. The park rangers were quite helpful. I was there with a third grade class and even they were impressed by the site. I fully plan on coming back later with my family and spending more time there.

What a treat this place was. For years we've been in the area, but never visited grandfather proper. A clean nice entrance with friendly staff. Numerous attractions to include an animal area, museum with gift shop. Fudge shop. Numerous walking trails, picnic areas, lastly, the bridge I've heard so much about. Wasn't as scary as my wife thought it would be. Once you cross, a rocky area that you can walk out to. A view that literally, goes on for Miles. We will certainly visit again.

I was pretty astounded that the zoo was free. It was every bit as good as many that I have paid to visit. It is easily a full day visit. Numerous, Lush exhibits. A wide variety of animals to see. Well located restrooms and concessions. There were indoor and outdoor exhibits. Animals from a wide variety of locations from hot to cold environments. We were all very pleased with the visit. Too bad we did end up getting rain and had to leave early

How can you put a rating on a place that looks like God took extra time to make with it's infinite beauty. We came in on the first day that Trail Ridge Road had opened. We saw bear, moose with babies, marmot, elk, deer and so much more. There was abundant snow pack with waterfalls and lush trees. I could write for hours on the beauty of this place. It will be the best $20 you will spend in your life. We can't wait to go back.

Loved this place. From the Visitor's Center you can see the lush meadow, mountain tops and the old halfway house. As we left a red fox darted across the road. We traveled the road to the lake. Numerous beautiful views along the way. The lake was beautiful, people canoeing as we watched. There are camper spots, small cabin and canoes for rent. You can walk around the area and lake if you desire. For free it's hard to beat.

Didn't realize a 200-year old bridge was so close to us. It's naturally beautiful and the setting offers trail hiking, walking in the river and enjoying the scenery. Kind of hard to imagine that was a main thoroughfare from Asheville to Greenville. Would be a great area for family photos.

Very positive experience. I really liked their focus on indigenous creatures. A nice variety of small and large animals such as bear, coyote, wolves, foxes and birds. Numerous play area to distract the children for a moment. Buy an annual membership for an even better deal.

It's hard to get a much better view than the Alpine Center has. If you're traveling through on the route, just make sure that is going to be open. They're course or no other bathrooms in the immediate area, but there are some more primitive rest areas along the Route.

I am not a connoisseur of wine, but I did enjoy my time in the winery. The host was very friendly and offered numerous suggestions to help me explore new Friday's of wine up. Is very well done and offers many selections for those who and enjoy wine more

Lots to do on Magnolia, the house for me was not the highlight. Beautiful grounds, boat rides, and numerous walking paths. It can get very hot in the summer with many mosquitoes so be ready. When in the animal area don't forget to look below and above.

We live in the neighborhood that borders the Cottonwood Trail. It's nice, with numerous wide paths, bridges, rivers and more. Do watch for the numerous wildlife, especially the deer that wander out in the evening as you drive through.

A historic ship with plenty to see. That day a lot of Veteran's to speak with and sign autographs. Plenty of planes, a snack bar and helpful staff. Great views of the harbor, bridge and downtown. If you're in the area it's a must see.

It's not as scary as some people would say, but it wasn't windy on the day we went either. Once you continue across across the Rocks, the view just goes on for miles. It is simply beautiful in all directions. Well worth the effort.

Such a great place to have. My wife's brother lives in the neighborhood we can simply walk to Grant's Farm. You can see the history of the area. Wandering through the paths and seeing the sites. It's hard to believe it's all free.

A nice combination of pools and golf. The club house is conveniently located with a bar and grill. The courses well kept with water features. Don't forget the occasional alligator that hangs out in the bodies of water.

We happened to stumble upon the location. It is 200 years old and hard to believe that was the main way from Asheville to Greenville years ago. It was nice to walk the bridge, the path and even into the creek below.

A nice setting with a really large pool. We stayed at the adjoining hotel and just walked over. The family liked it, but it made my skin very dry and hurt. Then again I have sensitive skin so your mileage may vary.

Went with family to see the train and flower show. Very beautiful and the kids enjoyed it all. A scavenger hunt for the kids and they loved it all. When we got back again we'll assuredly visit the garden.
It's quite a beautiful place. To be in the middle of city, it's hard to be beat. Many animals and other attractions. Plenty of walking spaces. Beautiful foliage. Please don't Miss it.
Quite the upgrade since I lived there. It now has a new playground, a covered picnic area and ample open space to play. Right in the middle of town with plenty of free parking.
Nice park near downtown.  Nice kid splash area,  covered Hut and amphitheater. Grounds well kept and mostly gated. Not been but they do have performances at the theater.
Nice visit today. They had a Revolutionary War battle reenactment.  Surprising how small the house  truly was.  Lots of buildings,  graveyard and a nature trail too.
We love this little park when we go to Montreat. Plenty of slides, swings and apparatus to climb on. The kids favorite is to stand in the cool running streams.
Nice break from the parks. Some restaurants allow you to use the dining card so check it out. Maybe do Animal Kingdom as a short day and then come here.
Very well kept and illustrated historical site. You can see the home, view the barns with lots of historical notes and travel the grounds.

So glad that I took a detour and stopped by Mardi Gras World.  Let's be honest, how many people can actually visit NOLA during the actual Mardi Gras week?  Even if you did make it during Mardi Gras week, how good of a view do you get of the floats at the Mardi Gras parade?  Solution: visit Mardi Gras World! It's essentially a giant warehouse where the Mardi Gras parade floats are actually made and stored.  Doing the facility tour allows you to go behind-the-scene on how these colorful paper mache creations comes to life. I didn't quite have the patience to go through the entire place with the guide, but they didn't seem to mind you helping yourself going through the warehouse at your own speed and pace.  Yes, this place is a giant tourist trap, but if it's not clear, I'm the definition of a tourist in NOLA, and I definitely enjoyed getting "tourist trapped" at Mardi Gras World.  The parking lot right next to the warehouse is slightly expensive, but I found plenty of free street parking on Tchoupitoulas St. just 2 (longish) blocks away.

Easily the best place to visit while in the museum area of Cleveland, the Crawford Auto and Aviation Collection has an eclectic collection of mostly cars and a few small planes.  What was confusing for us was this collection has a lot more reviews and photos on Google than the main museum (Western Reserve Historical Society) that this collection was part of.  To visit this collection, you will need to purchase a ticket to the main museum that also grants you access to other interesting collections found in the museum.  The place does remind us of a smaller version of the Henry Ford in Detroit.  Initially, we were disappointed at the very few number of cars visible on the main floor, however, we soon discovered the treasure trove of vehicles found in the basement level.  The collection is well curated with a descriptive sign for each vehicle displayed.  When we visited during the off hours, there wasn't too many people, which really helped with getting great photos of the vehicles.

A beautiful Catholic cathedral in the middle of NOLA's French Quarters.  I really shouldn't have gone on the ghost tour the night before.  The image of Place de Henriette Delille being lit at night behind the church keeps popping into my head as I was visiting the cathedral.  Adding insult to injury, the striking black and white tile flooring inside the church triggered the "Beetlejuice" vibe for me.  Regardless, there is a nice plaque commemorating John Paul II's visit back in 1987. Otherwise, St. Louis is a relatively small cathedral by Catholic cathedral standards. This is a fully active/functional parish, so be sure to check mass times from their website (and posting on the front entrance) before barging into the church for photos. The area in front of the church is constantly occupied by arts people, adding to the cultural flare of NOLA.

Upon reading the reviews, I've discovered that I had failed to pay the parking fee while visiting the Quinsigamond State Park... It was the middle of night and there wasn't anybody to take my parking money.  Anyways, there was a very good view of the bridge across Lake Quinsigamond to the south of the park.  The bridge was lit beautifully at night.  There were also some houses on the other side of the lake that made for some pretty night shots across the lake.  There was a sandy area, but I didn't really get a chance to go on the sand since the park was so dark at night.  There seems to be plenty of street parking available nearby, so if you're just trying to get some exercise at the park, consider parking for free in the nearby small streets.

The giant Christmas tree at Rockefeller Center gets EXTREMELY crowded after the lighting ceremony shortly after Thanksgiving.  The crowd of people trying to get a photo with this giant tree can be pretty ridiculous, especially at nights.  NYPD does a reasonably good job at controlling the massive crowd, but this is definitely not a location you will want to visit if you have claustrophobia.  During the rest of the year when the giant tree is not around, there is a nice bronze plaque on the floor that marks the location of the tree, which makes a great photo opportunity.  There are plenty of photographers for hire hanging around the outer edge of the tree if you find the selfie from your cellphone isn't quite good enough.

Downtown Disney is literally the best way to visit Disneyland and getting some Disneyland swag without having to paying for the exorbitant admission ticket prices.  The shopping district of the Disneyland resort offers numerous shopping and dining options, all which are better and cheaper than dining within the actual parks.  We were quite disappointed to see both ESPN and Rainforest Cafe having closed during our most recent visit, but we're sure Disney will replace the empty buildings with something else soon.  Parking is free if you can get validation (not difficult given the high prices for souvenirs), but the parking fees for Downtown Disney is actually quite reasonable compared to the surrounding structures.
dislikes: Closure of ESPN and Rainforest Cafe

reviews_attraction.text: The Edgewater Park is really a great place to visit while in Cleveland.  It's quite a different experience from the rest of the attractions like museums and professional sports.  There is a beach to the West, a pier to the North, and a marina to the East of the main entrance.  All 3 areas offers a unique experience.  The best part of visiting the Edgewater Park is the fact that the parking is completely free and there are plenty of parking.  The place looks like it may potentially get busy during weekends, but there are so much parking available, you might just end up having to walk a little bit further, but not forced to leave frustrated due to not being able to park.

Probably the second best location for viewing cherry blossoms in Central Park (best is Cherry Hill).  There is nice row of cherry blossom trees right at the entrance to the obelisk.  The obelisk itself is eroded on 3 out of the 4 sides.  Only the side facing the Met is still intact (and visible from the Egyptian wing inside the Met).  There are benches surrounding the obelisk, so really a nice location to sit and enjoy the cherry blossoms in spring.  As other reviewer has mentioned, you will need a wide angle lens to capture the entire obelisk along with the cherry blossom when you're close, so take your selfie on the footpath leading up to the obelisk.

My favorite time to visit Bryant Park is finally here!  During the holiday season (November thru January), Bryant Park transform into a Christmas wonderland.  There is a beautiful ice rink with the Empire State Building in the background and a bunch of pop-up shops that appears at the Christmas market.  A giant Christmas tree also gets installed around Thanksgiving and stays lit all the way until after New Year's Day.  I actually prefer visiting Bryant Park over Rockefeller Center simply due to the avoidance of massive crowding from tourists.  During the non-holiday times, Bryant Park is a relaxing space with plenty of seating.

Cherry Blossoms! The reason that this location in Central Park is called "Cherry Hill" is because of the cherry blossom trees planted on this hill.  Literally the best place to view cherry blossoms in Central Park.  There are other locations in Central Park with cherry blossoms, but this is the only place with a waterfront view along with probably the prettiest light pink cherry blossom tree that I have ever seen.  Even though the cherry blossom bloom is now over, be sure to mark this place as a must visit for next spring in Central Park.

What an awesome museum! There are so much to see and do already, but it seems that the museum is still expanding. My favorite building of the museum is the Boeing Center, but probably because I have a strong affinity for airplanes.  Seeing World War II from the different perspectives (America, Europe, and Asia) really broadened my appreciation for the magnitude of events that took place.  A huge perk of visiting the museums are the volunteers that tell their personal story from the war.  This museum is a must visit for anyone in NOLA.

This iconic sculpture of 4 letters on the Southeast corner of 6th Ave. and W 54th St. in midtown is a popular location for tourist.  Having been made famous by being featured as a stamp for the US Postal Service, people really enjoy having their photos taken with this giant sculpture.  The line for photos is usually not that bad and people are quite patient waiting for their turn with the sculpture.  There has been the installation of a new 4 letter sculpture, Hope, on the Southwest corner of 7th Ave. and W 53rd St 2 blocks away.

Better known as "Little Tokyo" in Los Angeles, Japanese Village Plaza is the center of the Japanese themed area in Downtown LA.  The plaza itself has numerous stores that sells Japanese goods, Japanese food, and even a Japanese supermarket.  If you're lucky (or unlucky, depending on your mood), there's usually some sort of gathering of cosplayers in the plaza.  Street parking is available, but nearly impossible to find, and nearby structures all charges an arm and a leg.  Definitely worth a visit if you can make it here.

Broderick Park is a small park on the southern tip of Unity Island to the West of downtown Buffalo.  The park essentially is a large parking lot to allow people to park their vehicles to walk along the pedestrian walkway lining the western edge of Unity Island that connects Broderick Park and Unity Island Park.  The walkway is quite popular on the weekends when the weather is nice.  There is a nice view of the Niagara River and the Peace Bridge to the south.  Oh yeah, there is also a view of our neighbor, Canada...

Located just under the Bethesda Terrace, the Bethesda Arcade has an iconic ceiling that's been line by 49 large panels of Minton Tiles.  Due to the design of the arcade, the acoustic is very ideal for string instrument and singing.  As such, there are often musicians playing inside the arcade.  The arcade is also a great place to seek shelter during the summer heat.  The dim yellow lighting on the ceiling helps with photographing of the tiles no matter what the lighting condition may be outside the arcade.

This famous fountain inside Central Park has been featured in many films like Home Alone, Angels in America, and most recently, John Wick.  The Bethesda fountain is only functional during the summer months and gets emptied as soon as the weather starts getting cold.  During the summer, the fountain is usually populated with kids running in the fountain to get cooled off.  There is a very good view of The Lake and the Loeb Boathouse from the northern end of the fountain.

Mutual Park is a well-kept park along the Buffalo River.  Its location provides the perfect photo shooting angle for the silos along the river.  It also has a small canoe/kayak launch for those that want to row their way through the silos.  The park itself offers some green space for picnic and also some signage explaining the history behind the park and the silos.  Street parking is available close by the park, but the park itself does not actually have a parking lot.

Yes! I finally got the chance to visit the Cherry Esplanade inside the Brooklyn Botanic Garden when it's blooming.  It's a great location for taking photos, granted you find a quiet spot to take a photo without people.  Needless to say, the place is extremely popular around the Sakura Matsuri event.  The 4 long rows of cherry blossom trees make a very impressive backdrop, and thus making this the premiere location for photographing cherry blossoms in NYC in spring.

Supposedly there are other Cleveland Script Signs around the city, but the sign found in Voinovich Bicentennial Park is probably the most photogenic given the background of downtown Cleveland.  The sign is also easily accessible by car with the ample amount of metered parking on the 9th street pier.  The sign is also within walking distance from the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame.  Definitely a good place to visit to document the fact that you've visited Cleveland.

If you've watched enough movies/TV, this bridge is instantly recognizable.  The whole area is really pretty, especially during spring when Cherry Hill is in full bloom.  Although you can get some nice long shot on the bridge itself, IMHO, the best location to capture the bridge along with Cherry Hill is from the west bank of "The Lake" (there is an unlabeled boat landing).  From there, you can get a nice shot with some people rowing themselves on The Lake.

Not sure why this pier has so many reviews, but the Edgewater Pier is just a short pier that extends into Lake Erie.  The pier itself is quite well designed with a ramp for wheelchair and plenty of benches for seating.  There is also ample amount of free parking available.  Most of the people visiting the pier were just snapping a few quick photos and immediately left.  Otherwise, there really isn't much to see or do at this pier.

Across the street from the Des Moines Civic Center, most people have probably walked/drove by this place while visiting Des Moines.  There is a really cool structure at this park that gets lit up with different colors at night.  Otherwise, it's just an open space in the middle of downtown Des Moines that sometimes get booked by political candidates while visiting Iowa during campaign season for rallies.

Miniature Trains! Too bad, the place is only "open" on Saturdays and Sundays.  Despite the trains not being in operation, it's nice to see all the efforts that went into building the miniature replicas of the various sights from New Orleans.  There are some really intricate buildings and really cute scenes setup around the main track.  My favorite building was the ghastly looking St. Louis Cathedral.

Even though this place is a national monument, people rarely visit Castle Clinton for the actual purpose of visiting Castle Clinton.  Instead, they're just in line to pick up their ticket for the Statue of Liberty Cruise.  This circular fortress does contain a few attractions for tourists, but it mostly serves as a resting shelter for tourists waiting for their turn to get onto the cruise boat.

Spoiler Alert: The Singing Oak sings because there is a bunch of wind chimes installed onto a big oak tree.  Some of the wind chimes are incredibly large and produce such beautiful sounds.  This is a great spot to relax and chill out while traversing through Zemurray Trail around the Big Lake.

It is one of my favorite damn parks in all of Seattle. For a park in the city it has some sprawling trails and abandon roads to walk on (it was a former military base). There are some unique buildings left standing, including a radar tower, from it's previous use. And of course there's some beach to enjoy as well as a few areas of open field. I would definitely recommend checking out this park on a nice day, I love it there.

A great park for playing some frisbee! It's good for other things as well though. There are turf soccer fields, a baseball field, playground, walking trails, basketball court, dog park, and large open grassy field. There isn't a copious amount of parking but between the two lots there's probably plenty. There's really no place to get food or drinks terribly close by, but it isn't far from anything.

This was definitely a fun and unique experience. Not only do you get to see some unique animals from close up, but you can feed them as well! It's a humorous sight to see a bison trotting along side your car hoping for a piece of wheat bread, or a llama wandering out in front of your car to stop you from driving off. 10/10 would recommend visiting if you're in the area.

Definitely a great ride, and I'm not even a roller coaster nut. I definitely recommend grabbing  a fast pass for this ride and giving it a shot. This is one of the few rides in California Adventure that we road more than one time, and it was just as enjoyable the second time as the first. Do it once during the day and again at night, totally worth it.

I love this park! They have a good series of walking trails, a ton of pecan trees, even some camping spots, and two donkeys! There isn't a ton of parking, but there is enough, and it's pretty beautiful most times of the year. I would recommend visiting during pecan season and joining the hoards of old people and children there to collect pecans.

A great park for taking a walk around a large water feature. There's a giant playground, a pretty big parking lot, and a lot of benches under trees. The lawn is big enough for many games of frisbee, volleyball, badminton, and many other sports you may or may not see in the olympics. Plus, I had my first date with my current girlfriend here.

To be perfectly honest, it was a little smaller than what I expected and slightly underwhelming. However, that might just be because I had my expectations of all museums set so high by friends. The building itself is very cool and they have a great atrium. I enjoyed the space portion the most, even if it was a bit small.

This is a pretty cool spot to stop by if you are in San Diego touristing like we were. Probably good for some pictures, especially on a nice day, as long as you don't mind the wind-blown-hair look. There's a little shop/restaurant halfway out in case you need some nourishment to make it ALL THE WAY BACK to shore.

Excellent place for a run, a swim, a bite to eat, or a drink. Or all of the above (but preferably not all at the same time). It's usually pretty busy here but there's parking on the roads that circle the lake and in some of the neighborhood streets. It gets very busy in the summer, so just keep that in mind.

Avery Park is pretty great. They've got a rose garden, some weird dinosaur bone looking artwork, and an old locomotive you can climb around on. There is also trees that produce shade, which can be very important in the summer. It looked like there was a reasonable amount of parking as well.

Even though it was very windy, and raining (and a little hail), then very foggy. And we never actually got to see St. Helens, or much of anything, it was still a great time. Also the observatory is mostly closed because of Covid, so we didn't get to go in there and look around much either.

Great park for short walks around the water. There's a few trails and it connects to a shopping center and another park, both which have extra parking. There's a boardwalk over the water where you can check out some of the wildlife, and I believe there is a bathroom as well.

Wilburton Hill Park has a couple baseball fields, a place ground, and a few walking trails. It's a nice park that is usually pretty clean and has plenty of parking. It also has a trail that connects to the Bellevue Botanical Gardens which is just a 5 minute walk away.

This is a nice little park in a neighborhood that's off any real main roads. It's quite, there's a play set, a few tables and chairs, and some trash cans. It was a nice spot to eat some pizza from Deru before we headed north on the Kirkland Corridor trail.

Feels much less depressing than most casinos. You'll still smell like an ashtray for a day or two after visiting but compared to most it isn't very smokey. The food is overpriced, as one would expect, but pretty good and there's plenty of free parking.

This park isn't huge, but I do like it. It has a few volleyball courts, a playground, and some bathrooms. There is also a a boardwalk type thing that is fun to walk on, and you can apparently swim here in our 3 months of summer.

Great place for a hike. It gets busy so carpool and get there early if you can. There's not a ton of views, but there are a couple good ones, and of course the falls look nice, especially with all the rain we've been having.
It's a bit expensive for how long you get to ride it, and the wait can be rather ridiculous at times. That said it isn't a bad time and there's a good view even on a cloudy day.
Pretty great science museum with a lot of interactive exhibits and things for the children. They also have 2 IMAX theaters that are pretty awesome (especially the Boeing one).
This is a very excellent park. It's so large it is easy to find a place that isn't crowded, even on a nice day, and it turns out it's a wonderful place to watch some LARPing.
Nice big park, some trails and walking paths, and a off-leash dog park. Also some fun playground equipment that was probably supposed to be for children.
Excellent place for people watching and just generally hanging out. The fountain seems to be a fun magnet for children to play in, so there's that.
Great uphill trail with a couple excellent view points, even on a cloudy, cold day. In a nice day, you can watch people hanggliding.
This is a popular trail with limited parking so make sure you get there early, really early if it's a nice day.
Very cool building. I took a tour many moons ago but it is also nice just to wander the ground.

Wow! Amazing tour. We had an exceptional tour guide and felt like we learned so much about Anheuser-Busch, beer in general, and the city of St. Louis. We've done countless brewery tours but this one was one of the best. The Clydesdale horses were beautiful. Their stable is fancier than my house. We were able to try a new product that was not yet released to the public which was fun. We also visited during the time that their "Dilly, Dilly!" campaign had just begun, so we were able to experience that!

Really great Metropark. We have always went to Stony Creek and St. Clair Metropark but we decided to have our wedding at Indian Springs due to the beautiful Environmental Discovery Center. We're so happy that we did because we now look forward to returning to Indian Springs each year for our anniversary to do a round of golf, a run on the trail, or a visit to the EDL. Joe Fulton is an awesome staff member that we also look forward to seeing on future trips.

Brought water shoes per everyone's comments. Ended up going barefoot as the mud was up to our ankles. It had not even rained an extraordinary amount leading up to our visit, but it was still treacherously muddy. The view was okay, but to us it was not worth the muddy hike. There are plenty of other "baths" in Hawaii that are much less of a hike and even more beautiful.

Pretty but we found the cost of entry to be a bit steep for what they have to offer. We’re huge flower and plant enthusiasts but found this place to be just okay. Was nice to have a public bathroom offered. Was disappointing to see that so many people have defaced the trees with their initials.

This is a pretty intense uphill 2.1 mile hike but well worth it for the views. My husband and I did a half marathon in the morning and then foolishly thought this hike would be easy. I highly suggest you plan on doing the hike with lots of water and sunscreen on hand as much of it has no shade.

Wow. This experience was amazing. The staff were exceptional and helped to make this my favorite activity we did on Maui. Kalen, Alec, Justin, and Stevens were awesome. They went out of the way to make sure we were all enjoying ourselves. The views were stunning and I’d do this again.

Intense hike down. Even after a slight amount of rain, the path was extremely muddy and steep. I do not suggest bringing bags or anything unless you're positive that the path is dry. There are also a lot of rocks in the water, so I recommend water shoes (See attached photo).

Woo-wee was that a hot climb up those stairs! We went during October and it was very humid. The journey up the stairs was worth it for the beautiful view. I recommend you do this attraction without a back pack. We had a backpack and the journey up is very cramped.

We loved our tour with Praline as our mule. We did a tour of the St. Louis Cemetery. The guide had a ton of interesting history to tell us about on the way to the cemetery, within it, and on the way back. We really enjoyed this part of our trip.

Beautiful zoo but is on the smaller side. It was extremely busy, to the point where it became difficult to see a lot of the exhibits. Some of the animals, specifically the macaws, looked so miserable in their cages that it made me sad.

This stop was our favorite in New Hampshire. The Flume Gorge hike is a very easy and beautiful one. The gorge itself is one of the most beautiful places I’ve ever been. I felt like I was walking through a fairytale forest.

A lot of the museum was closed during our visit. There was not much available to see but since it was free, we didn’t mind. We were most impressed by the local high school art. So much talent within their community.

Absolutely perfect wedding venue. The room holds 200 guests and has two walls covered in floor to ceiling windows. You do you have to use their exclusive caterer. We could not have asked for a better wedding venue.

The fountains are by far the best free attraction in Las Vegas. I try to catch the show as often as possible when visiting. You can find the current playlist online to get an idea of what the next song up will be.

We spent about 2.5 hours going through the exhibits. We loved how much we learned about Mississippi’s ecosystem and history. Most of the exhibits are aimed towards children but we still really enjoyed ourselves.

I'm not a huge baseball fan but I LOVED the Fenway Park Tour. We had the most amazing tour guide who really knew how to get us excited about the park. This was one of my favorite tours I've ever experienced.
My absolute favorite State Park in Michigan! A campsite on the water is a must. Perfect ship-watching location. Park is very well maintained. Nice running trail goes right through the park.
The Detroit Zoo truly cares about animal conservation. They make sure that all of their animals have proper space and a clean environment. I love supporting their effort.
This was our favorite stop on the Freedom Trail! The staff were very kind and accommodating. It was raining, but that did not make this attraction any less fun.
We felt that the botanical garden was slightly overwhelming for the price. I hope that it is more beautiful during other seasons. We visited during February.
I was pleasantly surprised by how beautiful the conservatory was. It is an awesome free attraction. I highly recommend checking it out if you enjoy flowers.
We really enjoyed this park but it is very small. The needle is very beautiful to look and and the river was pretty but packed with swimmers.
Beautiful and expansive park. We rented Bublr's and cruised the park during the kite festival. The park provides awesome views of the city.
Peaceful and beautiful. Unfortunately when we visited in early April, not much had bloomed. We'd love to go back when in full bloom.
Very interesting cemetery full of history. I enjoyed learning about how the tombs actually work and are still operational today.

World class collection of 20th century sculpture. Much of it was commissioned by the Pepsi CEO, installed by the artist, and landscapes designed expressly for the work. It’s completely lovely and worth the 60-90 minutes it takes to walk the loop path to see the 35-40 works. Open spring, summer, and fall weekends only (check ahead). Excellent audio tour using their app, with commentaries by curators and the former CEO who chose all the works for the benefit of his employees and the community. A wonderful community asset thanks to PepsiCo.

Jewel of a town park. The peninsula has sweeping 360 views of Greenwich, Manhattan, Stamford, New Rochelle, Long Island, and the sound. Great for the beach, a walk, a picnic, fishing, learning to sail, flying a kite.

Challenging access via downtown Old Greenwich's traffic laden one lane roads. Great amenities, especially deck and bathrooms at newly restored Old Barn.

If you don't have a Greenwich resident park pass, stop at the civic center (follow signs) to pay the fee before you get there.

Loved the circus museum with our kids (didn’t make it to the art museum). The model recreation is rather amazing and the rest of the displays really fun, a celebration of circus arts like nothing else.

Beautiful grounds great for kids to explore. Mine liked the playground. Lunch from the outdoor cafe was adequate but rather chaotically understaffed during our holiday visit. Good for long or short visits with kids. We’ll be back to explore more.

Very enjoyable tour of Boothbay Harbor and lighthouses, islands, and coves east of Boothbay. Large boat with outdoor seats in sun and shade, plus many indoor seats. Descriptive narration of landmarks and wildlife (birds, porpoises, seals, tourist on land). Wish the snack bar wasn’t trapped in the 1970s (chips and cocktails only). Overall we were surprised we loved it. Will try a different tour next time (they run 3-4 tours at 5-6 times per day)

Wow what an amazing science museum. My ten year old spent four hours exploring it on a weekday morning when it was mostly deserted. Fun for anyone all ages. Don't miss the amazing giant parabolic mirror and the excellent outdoor exhibits on the pier. One visit is not enough to see/do everything. We'll be back!

Really fun place to bring a kindergartener. Endless fun in every direction. A little pricy for what it is, but it is NYC area. Rides were the highlight but beach looked nice too. Live entertainers an unexpected surprise. Easy parking, short lines the Saturday morning/afternoon we visited.

Fun for kids. Could have done without the political discourse during he show. Also wish they got to the big cats faster (kids didn't need the warmup acts...). Seemed to have adequate care of animals to me. Birds and lemurs were nice in addition to the big cats.

Great little park about to get better when the new pool is completed. Already has beach, marina, and Ray Dalio-refurbished playground. Gorgeous panoramic views of Long Island Sound. Only marred by I-95 highway noise and ugliness of the park's marina.

Wonderful park. Great amenities, always lively, love the tables. Very clean -- great cheery staffers clearing table when I was there. Has bathrooms, food, and that amazing lawn. Thank goodness they moved the fashion week stuff elsewhere.

Really great beach park for families. We loved the bridge over estuary, walking paths, live bluegrass in the amphitheater, and secluded feeling. Couldn't believe the sparse crowd on a holiday weekend during peak season. We'll be back!!

Fine small Museum conveniently located in central Greenwich right off I-95. ~10 new exhibits a year and many programs are reasons to return again and again. A really community asset. Fine for quick visits, easy parking.

Just a great museum for young kids. We visit on every trip to the area. The new Wild Walk is quite fun (especially the giant spider webs and eagle's nests). We love the various movies and hands-on activities.

Fun rocky beach with gorgeous harbor view. Rock outcroppings fun but slippery to climb for improved view. Tight limited parking lot. My kids loved an hour here. No services, bring whatever you need in.
Tiny private park. Waterfalls dull the city noise. Heated in winter. Small snack shop. Perfect spot to eat you takeout lunch on a nice day. Go now before updated zoning permanently shades the park.
Brand new. Great small shop with snacks books and water bottles. Short film. And tickets for the walk (but much better to book in advance). Bathrooms and spring-feed bottle fillers outside.
Really fun. Quick stop. Really well organized on a day when it was packed. Touch a ray and shave ice we’re nice surprises. Not sure I’ll be back, but glad we brought the kids there once.
Fantastic dinosaurs, interactive exhibits, and views. My first grader explored uninterrupted for three hours (as did I) and we were both entertained and thrilled. Nice gift shop too.
Small but mighty. Loved the snow leopards, the black and white lemurs, and the penguin feeding. Grizzlies were surprisingly active (hope they can't get out of there!)
Great kids attraction for couple hours on a nice day. Ours like the flamingos, bird show, and reptile show. Convenient and the small scale is a feature.
We didn’t go in but really enjoyed visiting the grounds, outside , and nice waterfront views. Will return without kids in tow to tour the inside!!
Amazing gardens and walking trails for our young kids. Doesn't take more than 60 min to see the highlights, but you can spend a lot longer there.
Great place for a short walk in the woods. Recently built story walk for kids (a girl scout Gold Award project). Bring bug spray in spring!
Really fun kids rope course and zip lines. Museum small but nice for parents. Bring a picnic and watch the athletes practice jumping.
Small waterfront park with unusual rock cliffs. Former WWII battery to protect Gulf of Maine. Nice picnic areas. Fee for entrance.
Worth the short 15 minute drive from Main Street to take in one of the area's best panoramic views. No winter access!

Truly one of the best scenic train rides. There are many ways you can do this ride at different price points or one way. We did a round trip in the Yankee Girl car and we had a wonderful attendant, Charlotte who guided us with her knowledge of the railroad and historical facts. Her exuberance made the trip so enjoyable. We had access to snacks and beverages with comfortable chairs. I highly recommend doing this train ride and remember to book it early when you know your travel itinerary as it sells out.

One of the most fascinating and tragic natural disasters. I would suggest watching the movie. The film captures the essence of the magnitude of this eruption as told by the locals who knew the topography of the area so well. I remembered this day from 1980 and for me it was so amazing to see the regeneration of the forest and the rebuilding of this incredible park. The museum does an excellent job of documenting this event. Definitely go to this Visitir Center

We always go first to the VC of National Parks and this one proved to be very valuable. We watched the video which gave you tips about how to view the park.it suggested to go to the furthest point and then hit all the points of interest on the way back. The reasoning is that all points of view are mostly on the left and easier to turn into. Personally, I feel that it helped with traffic flow. The park is truly astonishing.

The architect, I.M.Pei designed a stunning building located overlooking Dorchester Bay. The grounds are astonishingly beautiful. The video presentations & film are extensive throughout the museum. Personally, I wished there was more about his love for the sea with establishing Cape Cod National Seashore. There is a beautiful painting by Jamie Wyeth of JFK sailing.  The museum is beautiful and a great historical experience.

On a road trip to Cannon Beach, when we pass by Lewis & Clark NP. It is truly an astonishing part of history and the museum offers an accurate portrayal of the historical journey. I am glad we stopped in as it was a nice group of NP that were super friendly and offering some suggestions of what to see.  Nice welcome into Oregon.

The most amazing NP with so many different climates and terrains from alpine, a rainforest, tidal pools and Monoliths. Truly astonishing. Must go to the top of Hurricane Ridge. My favorite was Cape Flattery. If you go there, you must buy a pass and limit of 20 parking spots so go early.

Being a National Park Fan, I enjoyed my visit to Rocky Mountain National Park.  We went to see the aspens and the views.  Check the weather always first as it can be tricky. Been here with complete fog on top, but on this September day it was nothing but blue skies and golden foliage.

We were driving from Jackson, Wyoming to Steamboat Springs, so we decided to explore this area and follow the Green River. Extraordinary scenery and seems less of a tourist place which pleased us immensely. We got to experience a beautiful night sky. Just loved the area!

Bryant Park has a beautiful skating rink and Christmas pop up shops filled with crafts and gifts. The Bryant Grill is a gorgeous place for a holiday lunch. Bryant Park is located behind the NYC Public Library. One of my favorite places to enjoy the city in any season.

Stunning part of NYBG. It was originally built in 1916 and restored in 1988 by David Rockefeller to be the complete design drawn up by landscape gardener Beatrix Farrand. The best time to see this is June 7-10. For a gardener this is a must do.

A magnificent place to walk and hike. During the pandemic it is a great place for some outdoor excercise with no entrance fee for now. You must observe social distancing and it is clearly posted. A little slice of heaven in Westchester.

One of the most extraordinary artist of our times whose installations are incredibly vibrant. I have seen his work many places but the Chihuly Garden & Glass exceeded my expectations. It is a must see in Seattle.

A beautiful place to hike and enjoy nature.  The museum has amazing art and a connection to Stanford White. The buildings the gardens  and surroundings are rustic  We love going there for walks and a picnic
It is truly a stunning place and represents an important part of the history of Texas. We enjoyed our tour. We went early in the morning and the crowds were not yet there which I highly recommend.
Just breathtakingly beautiful and so many places to enjoy the views and water. If you go to Lone Rock, do not go down to the beach unless you have 4 wheel drive. ( experienced getting stuck)
While visiting Colorado Springs, we decided to go for a hike here. Amazing trails and views. A plus is that it is close by to Manitou Springs for the others who like to shop and have lunch.
The charm of this town just captures you with this historic museum. The buildings are log cabins and very informative. With the holidays approaching, it was a nice welcome to Frisco.
Honestly, it was magnificent and we almost didn't go because we thought it was just a movie.  We laughed and screamed on this ride and it has 100% stunning scenery of Washington
A majestic octagonal building but in 1918 that is located above the Columbia River.  I would say it offers the most stunning views and really a must see kind of place.
Astonishing geological canyons. Went to the South Rim Visitor Center and other stops. Magnificent views. The Black Canyon is so breathtakingly beautiful, so go!
This was an exciting museum with an area for glass blowing. Loved the outside display of Chihuly vases. The architectural element of the museum is outstanding.
Truly loved it here. We hadn't planned a stop here but very glad we did. The lush forest was incredible. And then we discovered the Salmon River. Amazing!
A must see kind of thing and if you are lucky to experience a low tide you will see a. Incredible tidal pool and a sea garden.
If you are looking for a nice location for a picnic and some ocean views, then this park is a perfect place.
Lake George is a gorgeous place to visit and the village has lovely places to sit and enjoy the views

Wonderous world of attractions. Geared for families, but easily enjoyed by couples, singles, and the elderly alike. Closest thing to Walt Disney World in this part of Texas. Rainforest and Aquarium pyramids are the stars here. Each has its own price of admission, but you can easily spend 2 or more hours in either one. Discovery pyramid tends to be ignored and is usually only worth it for travelling exhibits so don't feel like you need a Value Pass just to see it. 3D IMAX is fun, but 4D ridefilm and Colonel Paddlewheel are skippable. It's a magical park, and I love going back here time and time again.

PROS: Heavily air-conditioned, wonderfully restored, audio tour available. Cool woodworking and stained glass. CONS: Few works of art and furniture remain, much restoration work left to be desired, nothing much to do or see after 45 minutes, no exceptional information to be gleaned from audio narration. It's like visiting the house of a stranger you never knew or even heard of and hearing that they liked to sit upstairs during the day. Huh. I think it looks cooler on the outside, tbh.

It was okay. I guess I was expecting more. They tried really hard to make the exhibits interesting. They didn't gloss over the slavery issues or the Native American angle or whitewash anything. They had videos and interactive exhibits. It just felt kind of stale. Like the privateer ship-- I know what they're going for, but it looks like something from a playground. Some exhibits (eg, contemporary accounts and letters) are a bit dry. I'd go and see for myself if I were you, though.

Major points for theming and keeping things faithful to the TV show. Unfortunately, it's only faithful to the dreaded later years of The Simpsons. Really pulls you into this crapsack world of unsafe amusement parks, poor customer service, and unrestrained capitalism. Unfortunately, the writing isn't stellar, the jokes and plot are forced, and I didn't find it that funny. It's amusing enough on its own, though, if a bit nauseating, so yeah-- it's good.

Trackless ride. Wild side has more spins, but is not exactly Mad Tea Party. Fun light effects but nothing extraordinary. Not exactly a compelling story... A penguin chick hatches late and goes inside an ice cave for shelter... and DANCING! At the end, you stand in your Florida shorts in the same room as the 32F penguins, so you can leave quick or get hypothermia and frostbite. You will die in under an hour.

Easily the cruelest attraction at WDW. You will be sprayed with acid, farted on, blasted with bug spray. Your children will be terrified as giant spiders leap from the ceiling onto their heads. You will be stung, buzzed, tickled, and screamed at by a giant grasshopper. Children under 5 will not last through the whole show.

Perfect for a childless millennial who loves listening to kids scream, though. A-

If they turn this into Jurassic World, I'll cry. Needs an upgrade on the animatronics, the day I rode the ultrasaur looked like it was trying to drown itself. Still looked way better than a mosasaur on a screen. Ride itself works as always, though maybe less intense than it used to be. I do NOT think it would be improved by Chris Pratt or Bryce Dallas Howard, just needs some TLC.

I don't usually go in for galleries, but I loved the collection of historical pieces from around the world-- artifacts collected from medieval Europe, Tibet, China, Japan that take up entire rooms and have to be seen to be believed. You could spend all day taking it all in. My favorite painting is Charlemont's "The Moorish Chief"

I like this coaster not because it has a lot of inversions (only one), nor because it's particularly fast (60 mph, compared to 70 or 75 for usual launch coasters), but because it has style and grace, flowing fluidly through the park. The way it leaps through the canyon halfway through is a great touch.

It's okay. Line was long, even with Express Pass it takes too long to board and get through. There's really only one scene of interest and it's a giant screen ripped directly from a tram ride at Universal Hollywood. Queue is really cool. Not nearly as awful as Fast & Furious. Animatronic is cool too.

Fun little ride with good theming.  You go forwards, then backwards, then spin because of an evil god's curse. Definitely more intense than a standard kiddie coaster, but not nearly as intense as Montu. Good views of serengeti. For an intermediate coaster, this is the gold standard

It wasn't quite what I was expecting-- I was thinking more picturesque scenery and cool terrain (photos show trucks plowing through water) but I'm glad I went. Maybe it was the fact that it was raining when I went on. Apparently Little Red and his mama don't exist any more.

I did this on an EMH morning, having arrived early to the park. Waited 20 minutes in line, don't regret it. Wouldn't recommend waiting 45 minutes, an hour, etc. Thought it was pleasant and fun. If you're expecting an e-ticket or something "worth the wait," bail out now.

It would get 5 stars just for being so awesome and still being free. Bonus for the toboggan ride, Phoenix, Impulse, and classics like the always-marriageable 1001 Nacht, Flyers, Haunted House... worth the trip out to Elysburg. Prices for food were fantastic too.
likes: Classic attractions (1001 Nacht, Flyers, Haunted House)

reviews_attraction.text: It's a late 70's looping coaster, but it scores extra points for me for really exploring the terrain and dipping into the treeline a bit. I also liked how packed in it was with Coal Cracker and Great Bear. Impressive use of space.

I liked that the zoo has so much history, and I liked a lot of the new things that had been built. Zoo is going on a good direction. Still some areas that could use a facelift (eg, monkey house). Everyone was sold out of pretzels.

I'm cosmically average, but this is a fun ride with great shooting segments. 20 years old, so a bit dated but I love that it's got physical models instead of screens, great theming, and Will Smith. Better than Buzz Lightyear.

I loved the intense racing aspect more than the actual ride. It really gave the impression that we were running a steeplechase. In our case, Team Thunder won because Team Lightning's train wasn't as full

My wife loves B&M inverted coasters for their smoothness and intense inversions. This coaster is her favorite in all of Hersheypark. We did FastTrack to bypass the line and it was worth it. Fun coaster!
This may be the best dive coaster in the US (tied with Griffon). Love the way it goes through, in, and around the Zambia Smokehouse. Great views! Worst part is the shoulder restraints (I'm 6'2").
The only revenge was on my groin. The track would be fine as a floorless coaster, but as it is, I'm taking major g-forces in the babyzone. Please convert this ride before someone becomes sterile.
Fantastic, the ultimate version of the Spider-Man ride. Won't spoil it, but everything about this is exciting and perfect. Don't drink butterbeer immediately before riding, though.
Love our big city park, so much to do outdoors, from running trails to picnics to volleyball to golf. Always being kept clean and landscaped.
1940's wooden coaster is still in great condition. Not too bumpy, nice speed, and no computers here-- still uses friction brakes. Cool!
I've been on several flying coasters, but I think this is my favorite. Great views flying over water and zooming around.

(Translated by Google) This museum will be of interest not only to males. We went to the museum with my girlfriend and she was absolutely delighted. We took a lot of great photos and learned a lot of new and interesting things about the history of aviation.
Many historic aircraft dating back to 1914 and older. Military fighters and bombers, helicopters and even retro cars. The number of exhibits is gradually increasing.
Affordable price. Through the Groupon app, we purchased a ticket for 2 people for $ 13.
A great place to bring your kids with you. They will be delighted.
All the necessary amenities are provided. Completely convenient for people with special needs.

(Original)
Этот музей будет интересен не только представителям мужского пола. Мы ходили в музей с моей девушкой и она была в полном восторге. Сделали море отличных фото и узнали много нового и интересного об истории авиации.
Множество исторических самолетов, начиная с 1914 года и старше. Военные истребители и бомбардировщики, вертолеты и даже ретро автомобили. Количество экспонатов постепенно увеличивается.
Демократичная цена. Через приложение Groupon мы приобрели билет на 2 персоны за 13 долларов.
Прекрасное место, чтоб привести с собой детей. Они будут в восторге.
Имеются все необходимые удобства. Полностью удобно для посещения людьми с особыми нуждами.
likes: Facilities & Services: Amenities for special needs, affordable pricing

reviews_attraction.text:
(Translated by Google) A very small but very cozy historic center of the Dallas suburb, the town of Carrollton. You can walk around in 15 minutes. Free public parking is available at a distance.
Of the sights, I would like to note the antique shop, which was very interesting to explore due to the HUGE amount of old things for sale. During the walk, you can enjoy the "old style" delicious ice cream and look into the sweet shop, popular not only in the whole city, but also in the whole district.
We enjoyed spending a couple of hours there!

(Original)
Очень маленький, но очень уютный исторический центр пригорода Далласа, городка Carrollton. Обойти вокруг можно за 15 минут. Чуть поодаль имеется бесплатная общественная парковка.

(Translated by Google) This is a very nice park. The entrance fee is $ 8. Parking is sufficient. Further up there is a beautiful beach and at the end you can walk along nicely. There were quite a few anglers there. We saw some raccoons, a manatee and little lizards. Unfortunately, we have sighted the large specimens. In any case, the park is worth a visit.

Es waren etliche Angler dort. Wir haben einige Waschbären, einen Manatee und kleine Echsen gesehen. Die großen Exemplare haben wir leider gesichtet. Auf jeden Fall ist der Park einen Besuch wert.

(Translated by Google) We have been to this beautiful place a few times. There is always something new to discover. Unfortunately, the park was closed this year, when we were there in June. You can observe many animals, enjoy nature and just listen to the sounds. We can definitely recommend the park. The best time to visit is in winter.
