Man kann viele Tiere beobachten, die Natur genießen und einfach den Geräuschen lauschen. Wir können den Park auf jeden Fall empfehlen. Die beste Zeit für einen Besuch ist im Winter.

(Translated by Google) It is worth walking up the path. You can enjoy a wonderful view over the Pacific. We were there at sunset. Unfortunately we had a cool day and the wind whistled around our ears. The view was still beautiful. We were lucky with the parking, because there are very few parking spaces. But they are free.

Leider hatten wir einen kühlen Tag erwischt und der Wind pfiff uns um die Ohren. Der Ausblick war trotzdem wunderschön. Wir hatten Glück mit dem Parken, es gibt nämlich nur ganz wenige Parkplätze. Sie sind aber kostenlos.

There was a swivel on every incline and the platform rotates while driving. You have a fantastic view. The fun costs almost $ 26 per person, but it's worth it.

Das muss man unbedingt gemacht haben. Die Fahrt dauert je 11 Minuten. Es geht ganz schön steil hoch. Nach oben macht es mehr Spaß als runter. Bei jeder Steigung gab es einen Schwenker und die Plattform dreht sich während der Fahrt. Man hat einen fantastischen Ausblick. Pro Person kostet  der Spaß fast 26 Dollar, aber lohnt sich.

(Translated by Google) Admission including parking costs $ 6 per car per day. There are plenty of parking spaces and toilets are also available. It is best to drive to the end, because it is particularly beautiful and you can still walk a nice arch along the sea. Nature and the sea are particularly beautiful to look at.

Der Eintritt inkl. Parkplatz kostet pro Auto 6 Dollar für einen Tag. Parkplätze gibt es reichlich und Toiletten sind auch vorhanden. Am besten fährt man bis zum Ende, da ist es besonders schön und man kann noch einen schönen Bogen am Meer entlanglaufen. Die Natur und das Meer sind dort besonders schön anzusehen.

(Translated by Google) This is a beautiful park for an exciting nature trip. It stretches a beautiful landscape with a variety of animals. You drive by car quite comfortably through the park. And if you feel like running, you just get out.

(Translated by Google) The beach is nice, but it's not worth the effort. Parking is quite expensive and the shells are small and there is a lot of breakage. There are really nicer beaches in Florida. When visiting, don’t forget to wear slippers.

(Translated by Google) We were here for the second time. Although we did not take our dogs on holiday, it is still funny to watch other dogs romping. The beach is ideal for this. The water is very shallow and spacious.

Hell's Revenge is a "difficult" rated trail and is not for the faint of heart. However if you have a vehicle that can tackle it, even one of the locally rentable Jeeps or other off-road vehicles, then this is a must do! The trail itself is manageable to the experienced and competent driver and there are always others on the trail who can come to your aid if needs be, but be prepared with water, sunscreen, and emergency supplies if needs be. Drivers looking for more of a challenge can do the additional (optional) obstacles such as Hell's Gate, The Escalator, and Tip-Over Challenge that really put a person's skills, wits, and vehicle to the ultimate test. This is one of the most iconic and famous trails in Moab. Definitely run this one if you can.

The largest marina in the park. Unfortunately since the illegal introduction of the lake trout into Yellowstone Lake by unknown means, the historic numbers of the local cutthroat trout have been greatly bombarded and now fishing is nothing like it was back in the pre 2000s. The park is working every year to cut the lake trout numbers down through netting operations to help retain the endangered Yellowstone Cutthroat trout. Still, this is a great place to launch a boat or get a boat rental for the day. They also do wonderful tours of the lake on a large boat. The lake is beautiful and large and has lots of history surrounding it.

A little hidden gem of the park! Getting to swim here is one of the best parts of the trip to Yellowstone. It is not always open since some years the waters are too high and it is dangerous but there is a calm section of river great for families and then there is a little more rough and rapid section that is fun for avid swimmers to play in. The river here unlike others in the park is warmer because of the flow of heated water from geothermal features upstream. It is very enjoyable and fun.

Nice little museum with cool taxidermized animals found in the park, mostly bird species that can be found in Yellowstone. One of the simpler museums, nice place to briefly drop by and check out. The actual "Fishing Bridge" is nearby and is cool to check out. Historically fisherman used it for fishing but because the bridge happens to be right on top of the endangered cutthroat trout's spawning grounds it is illegal to now fish from here. Great place to spot trout though and other wildlife.

One of, if not the best train rides in the entire country. Riding this railroad is like truly taking a step back in time. Not only do you get to experience a historic train ride up to Silverton just like folks would have done starting in 1882, but the scenery of the Animas River, the mountains, and the canyon you travel up is breathtaking. A very fun adventure for folks from all walks of life! And a bucket list caliber experience for those who love trains and railroading!

Great off-roading trail for those who have substantially capable vehicles. Some stock high-clearance 4x4s may make it unscathed but the trail is not for the faint of heart. There are a few tricky places where a spotter could be handy. Beautiful rock scenery and backcountry. Be sure to bring water and emergency supplies in case of complications. My Toyota FJ Cruiser did well and I know others who have done it in stock FJs or Jeeps. Canyonlands N.P. is awesome!

Very neat little museum that highlights the railroad history in Ridgway as it was the center of the very famous and now abandoned Rio Grande Southern railroad that went from here to Durango via a narrow gauge rail system. Lots of history is preserved here with books full of railroad documents, a selection of many many photos, small diaromas, and full sized rail equipment including a replica of Galloping Goose #1 sitting outside!

Nice little place to visit and learn about some of the early Mormon pioneers that trekked across Utah known as the Hole in the Rock Pioneers. I enjoyed their new main visitor center building and the "fort" they have established there which shows what life for the pioneers would have been like when they settled in Bluff. A great book to read about these pioneers in named Undaunted, I highly recommend it!

Amazing place to visit if in this corner of Colorado. Superb tours through fascinating Pueblo Indian cliff dwellings as well as lots of places to lead yourself and discover what an ancient yet mysterious people have left behind for us to uncover. Their new visitor center is a wonderful addition and their museums are really cool. Being a local I really have taken this place for granted.

Wonderful place! Glad I stopped by. Huge selection of artifacts and memorabilia related to the history of the Montrose area, the D&RGW railroad, and life in the late 1800s to early 1900s. Large amount of old farming equipment and even a full sized Union Pacific caboose you can go into. Small fee to get in but worth keeping the place going.

Not for those with a weak stomach! The smell of rotten eggs is prevalent here but that is what a sulfur releasing hole in the ground will do. Haha. Love visiting this section of the park since it is one of the few places with so many muddy thermal features. Nice loop you get to walk/hike on and often there are bison in this area.

Seems like a nice little museum! Showed up on a day they weren't open but I got to walk around the yard and see the old train cars, artifacts, and locomotive #5. Hope to make it back and see what is inside. Big narrow gauge railroad fan from SW Colorado and they even had a D&RGW stock car there!

Love going here! Not much to do in this small town but visiting the Dinosaur Museum is always fun. Filled with neat, one of a kind exhibits makes it a real treat. Great for kids and adults alike. Never very busy and the people are always so nice. Make sure to drop by!

Love love love Lagoon! Fantastic theme park, especially for being in Utah. Love their coasters like Wicked, the Spider, and Colossus. Great family fun. Be sure to go with a season pass if you know you can go at least twice. It pays for itself.

Got to ride this awesome stretch of railroad up the gorge and back and wow was it beautiful! Super cool experience especially if you walk out onto the open car so you can look straight up the canyon walls at the huge bridge high above.

Little Moab is a great place to go that isn't far from Provo to mess around off-road. Lots of trails in the area and cool rock outcropping so similar to Moab that allow you play around with your 4x4. Had a good time in my FJ out here.

Amazing museum! Largest and most intricate model railroad I've ever seen! A must see if you are a railroad or model train fan and especially of you have small kids. Worth the price of admission to help keep this place running!

Very cool museum if you are a Toyota Land Cruiser fan or even just a fan on unique and vintage vehicles! Check it out as they have the largest collection of Land Cruisers from around the world that you'll ever find!

Wonderful park for sure! And the recent addition of a small, rideable railroad is definitely something to check out if they are running on a weekend! Check out Utah Live Steamers on Facebook for info!
Great hike and beautiful arch! Probably the most iconic arch in the whole park and dare I say it, the world! A must see if visiting Arches N.P. And if you are physically able to do the hike.
Super cool museum! The best one out of the Smithsonian's. Be sure to try the jet simulator and plan to spend lots of time here since there is so much to see!
Really powerful museum. Great place to visit and wonderful representation of the Holocaust and commemoration for the people of the events that occurred.
Nice museum! If you have a national parks pass you get in for free and the exhibits as nice. They even have a small theater and some hands on stuff.
This is the trailhead for the Fairy Falls hike. It is a nice back country waterfall and is a nice, easy hike if you don't mind distance.
Really cool wax figures! First time to a wax museum and I was impressed. So many iconic figures that look so real!

Morgan Run is a small, out of the way State Park, situated across several stream valleys surrounded by wooded hills. It is an old agricultural land, so you can see an occasional ruins of old farms. The park has a convoluted network of trails, not all of which are on the map, so watch your path---it's easy to get lost, and trail shortcuts are quite hard because they have a lot of thorny ground cover. Use OpenStreetMap (OSM) or AllTrails, at least, and if you find trails that are not on the map, please crowd-source it to OSM.
We've heard that in the spring and summer there are lots of ticks.

This park has many entries so it is a little bit confusing: it is all centered around the South Mountain on the Appalachian Trail, but it's divided by Interstate 70, with separate entries. Depending on where you park, you'll be closest to the Washington Monument,  Annapolis Rock or the Greenbrier State Park. They are all connected by the Trail, of course.
This location is closest to the Annapolis Rock overview after a nice hike.

Washington great falls is the best kept secret and fantastic destination for hikes and sightseeingin the metro DC area.  Besides the official park there are several unofficial access points,  usually at the old C&O canal lock houses. The canal row path is just perfect for hiking and biking. It extends from far upstream of the Potomac river to DC downtown and even to Mount Vernonoon the other side of the river.
likes: Canal row path for hiking and biking

reviews_attraction.text:
You just HAVE to get to Glenstone. A modern art museum on par with the mainstays of large capitals of the world, in my opinion.
The pavillions surround a beautiful lily pond, reminiscent of Monet; the individual rooms contain collections of well-known 20th century artists like Pollock, Warchol, Rothko, Twombly et al., plus very interesting open-air art installations on the large museum grounds.

South Mountain State Battlefield Park is adjacent to Apallachian Trail and it contains the Washington Memorial. The hiking trail branches off onto several vistas, overlooking both sides of the ridge. There's a beautiful view onto the Catoctin range. We came here in late February, with couple of feet of snow on the ground, but the trail was well trodden so the hiking wasn't too hard.

Is Charleston the prettiest city in the US? Quite possibly so---the downtown district is just astounding, with historical charm that is clearly well maintained with  care to this day. We recommend walking the cozy streets and admiring the varied architectural styles, from New England to Spanish Collonial, as well as the beautiful parks and waterfront.

It's a very nice hike to a beautiful vista. A perpendicular hard rock layer, eroded by the Deer Creek creates two rock pillars on both sides of the valley. I hear it's a popular rock climbing location. When we visited, we saw a wedding party with ladies in long dresses and high heels climbing the rocks like there was no tomorrow.

The entire C&O canal and adjoint areas between Potomac and River road/McArthur boulevard are a wonderful resource. From the Anglers Inn parking and C&O towpath access point, to the Great Falls, up to Penny Lock and Blockhouse park is just a wonderful opportunity for hikes and bike rides.

A beautiful waterfront park around the Pineapple Fountain, within a walking distance to the Battery Street and Rainbow Row historical district on one side, and a wide open water view onto the suspension bridge, USS Yorktown and sailboats.  Charleston is wonderful!

Great hike from the parking lot off State Road 40, with several easy climbs and descents on the forested path. Watch for the turn-offs to several scenic spots on the way to the main one. We had a very nice sunny and clear weather so the view was magnificent.

There are several park entrances to this area that borders Camp David near Thurmont. This one is right off Rt. 15. It has several trails; we took the uphill trail heading towards the Cunningham falls and stopped at the picturesque overlooks along the way.

We were here on a beautiful April Easter Sunday. The view is great: clear blue sky, open water with sailboats and ships, USS Yorktown museum ship and the suspension bridge in the distance. Everyone looked happy and we enjoyed our picnic very much.

This is an amazing piece of history---the church was established in 1660 in this beautiful location, overlooking the meandering Potomac. We were blessed with great weather and visibility.
Check out the outdoor chapel on the other side of the road!

Beautiful park and hiking area near Monticello in Charlottesville. The trails aren't visible on Google maps but exist in OpenStreetMaps, which I definitely recommend for serious hikers. I use Maps.Me android app with OSM maps.
dislikes: Trails not visible on Google maps

reviews_attraction.text: It turns out that Maryland is quite hilly and beautiful. Within minutes of our suburban home we can enter several parks and hike in the forest for miles. Lake Needwood and lake Frank are one of our several favorite locations.

Seriously, Smithsonian is one of the Seven Wonders of the world. I love the National Gallery---both wings. We've been coming here for thirty years and we feel at home. I hope I will be visiting it with our grandchildren.

great community park; nice and clean, and has the Bladensburg water park facilities, from which you can rent kayaks and paddle the Anacostia river up to the National Arboretum. We had a great weekend there.

The awesomest museum in the Smithsonian and maybe in the US or even the world. Just walk here and touch the spaceships and Moon rocks.
Ah and don't forget to visit the Udvar hazy annex near Dulles Airport.

Wheaton Park and Brookside Gardens are our favorite weekend destination in the suburban Maryland. The gardens and the conservatory are beautiful for walks and hanging out. Too bad they do not allow pets.
Awesome Aventine Mount mansion, with a beautiful view over the Potomac and a nice landing. I really liked the story of a Hungarian princess breeding the war spoil Hungarian horses here.
Bohrer Park is a local Gaithersburg attraction, with a water park, skate park and minigolf, right next to the community center and Gaithersburg High School. Also, early voting station!
There's not much of hiking here, but a nice combo of a fairly big marina, an arts center and a campground. Interestingly they both rent pier space, and have a dry boat storage area.
Very nice hikes on a surprisingly large wild plateau. Hard to believe that this area is in the middle of pretty urban development, with West Baltimore just few miles away.
Sullivan Island has a  pleasant small place feel and we liked it better than Isle of Palms, which we found to be crowded, commercialized and touristy.
Las Vegas has everything. But don't forget to visit ZIon, Bryce and Grand Canyon---it's a long drive but still possible for a day trip.

I'll start with a word of caution,  the trail at the north end of the parking lot that looks like an ATV trail is the correct trail for those looking to do the Battle Creek Overlook trail.   I saw a smaller tail just to the left that said, Bonneville Shoreline Trail.... don't go on that one as it added a mile to the hike fortunately I still had signal and used location on Alltrails to find the right trail.   Saw 13 deer and 7 squirrels on the trail and was blessed with great views of snow-capped mountains and of the valley below.   The trail was better than I expected.... make sure to follow the map to the overlook which gives you a great ariel view of Battle Creek Falls.

We took a trip up to Ogden and let me tell you,  this place has jumped near the top in places my kids love to go.  To be honest,  they had way more fun here than they did at Disneyland earlier this year.   There are so many things for kids to play with,  create with,  and simply do.  I love the layout with the tree in the museum and the little homes from other countries.  They have trains to play with that won over my son.  There was something for everyone.  Fair warning, I got in free (blue star museum), otherwise the price may bring down my rating by one as it's not cheap if you have 5 kids.  I think they should have a family package deal...

For the price, I didn't feel like the place lived up to the hype.  They do have a peregrine falcon that they show you (though they don't allow it to fly around) if you go to the class and they have a nice exhibit for their California condors, but that's about all of the highlights.   The rest of their birds (not many) are kept in jail like exhibits that just make you feel sad for them.   The "play room" was also very disappointing which is saying something as I have 4 children under 7.

This is a beautiful picnic spot up Spanish Fork canyon...its like a little trip to arches just in our backyard of utah county.   The picnic site has a few tables though these are not shaded at all.  There's also a toilet.  I'm not a rock climber,  but there were several lines already in place in the rock and often there are people there climbing for those looking for some thrills.   All and all, it's a cool place to go and check out.

Great,  short hike up to the "G".  This particular hike is not quite as steep as the "Y", but the path is far more narrow and slicker making it a bit sketchy for small children.   I went early April,  so the foliage is limited but was still a pretty hike that gets you out of the city.  It shares the start point with battle creek falls,  so knock that one out while you're here as well due to their short distances.
likes: Proximity to other attractions (Battle Creek Falls)

reviews_attraction.text: OK, let me first warn that this place is expensive, especially for a landlocked aquarium...but the place is impressive.   One of the best aquariums I've ever been to and I used to live in California.   The exhibits are incredible and make you think for a second you're seeing the animal in its actual environment.   Make sure to get over to the otter exhibit during feeding time as that was the coolest feature.

This is the epitome of a tourist trap.   You pay an entrance fee per person and that gets you just that... entrance to shops to buy stuff.  There are obviously a few buildings to check out, but you have to pay more, per person,  to do any of the attractions that should be included with the gate price (panning for gold, touring the mine,  house of mirrors). Next time I'll stay on I-15 and forgo this stop.

It's a lovely hike for the area that can be enjoyed by all, but compared to many up in the canyons this left something to be desired.  The trail has very little shade making it an oven if you try during the summer afternoon and the end you're just rewarded by a bridge.   Again, great family hike near the city,  but misses when compared to mountainous hikes in the area (ie. Bells canyon)

Cute park that has a little of everything from basketball courts,  to sand volleyball,  to a splash pad,  playground,  amphitheater,  and more.   They even had a concession stand open this past weekend when my family was there.   Also, there is a lovely pond stocked with wish and beautiful memorials to veterans.   Great family oak next to the Village in Meridian.

Don't let some of the reviews scare you,  took five children under 10 with one only 18 months and this was ver doable for them.   As others mentioned,  go during lowtide and you'll be blessed with quite the treat.  We saw lobsters,  anemones, various crabs,  and even an octopus!  This little hike was one of my family's highlights during our trip to San Diego.

OK, without a parks pass I'm not sure I would feel the stop would warrant the $5 admission, though the view is breathtaking that's literally all there is to do at the park...you park and walk out over a bridge (OK there's also a small walkway to a second viewpoint).  As with most scenic water locations,  visit earlier in the year for a more spectacular view.

Great family activity when the weather doesn't permit outdoor fun.  Lots of butterflies in the dome that fly all around the patrons.  I love that they have food areas where the butterflies seem to congregate.  Besides the actual butterflies,  there's lots of learning activities for the young ones to include an indoor playground!

Great easy hike that kids of all ages can do that puts you down by the river.  Kids played in the water for hours despite the water being extremely cold to me towards the middle of April (as such if you're early in the year be prepared for frigid water).  The place also has great trails for horseback and mountain bikes.

Absolutely beautiful view up Nephi canyon that brings back memories of Bryce Canyon.  There is a short paved trail thats about a half mile round trip that takes you out to the lookout.  The trail is easy for all ages.  There are picnic tables at the site as well as bathrooms.   A great stop on your way up the Nebo loop.

Even going near midday at the beginning of September when you wouldn't expect many birds were we able to see a few thousand.  I was impressed with the number of pelicans that frequented the location.   The water was low enough that you could actually see the tops of fish as they swam in the mucky water.  Kids loved it!

I love this lesser known hike just about a half mile or so up the Provo River trail.  You need to look out for the graffiti building as there are no trailhead signs.   I've been up each of the past three years... this year an avalanche spilled out at the falls making it sketchy to get to the base of the falls.

Park has the only "splash pad" in Middleton, but I'm hard pressed to even call it that.   This park houses some of the festivities during the year (firework show, harvest festival,  etc); otherwise the park doesn't offer much to do except provide recreational soccer fields for kids.  No playground or tables.

Awesome zoo up by the University of Utah.   Great place to bring the kids.   They have some great polar bear and sea lion exhibit.   I've been going to this place since I was a kid and is only gotten better.   The only thing that I miss is that they removed the kid play area that my kiddos loved.

Lots offered at this park from tennis courts, to several playgrounds, to Tracy Aviary.  There are great paths for running though ut can get busy some mornings.   Many units at Fort Douglas use this park to do their 2 mile APFT.  It is a beautiful park with something for everyone.

Perhaps the best playground in Utah county....just be ready for A LOT of other kids/families to be there with you.  There is so much to do with something for everyone.  My kids spent two hours there and would have spent the rest of the day there if we hadn't made them leave.

Best park in Middleton!  Playground area for all ages,  tennis courts,  basketball courts,  restrooms,  picnic area,  walking/biking path, and more.   If you're looking for a park in the area then this is definitely one to remember.
What a beautiful park in the heart of Boise, ID that has everything from playgrounds,  to green belts, to paddle boats,  to even a zoo in the middle.  A fantastic family adventure awaits.
There's so much to do here from playing in the ponds, feeding the ducks,  to playing on the playground or starting the SF river trail.  My family loves this park....highly recommended.
Wonderful, family friendly park that everyone can enjoy.   This park is centered on science and affords kids the opportunity to learn while they play.  A must see playground in PG.
Awesome nature park full of activities from a nature trail,  to a playground,  picnic tables,  and water fun.   Definitely a great family fun spot.

Definitely an underrated Seattle experience, for both out-of-towners and locals alike. Being in the north end of the Sound, we dont make it to Seattle very regularly, but were done for the day to celebrate a birthday. We opted for Sky View's evening sunset VIP option, which included a reserved window-side table overlooking the waterfront and city, flatbreads and drinks. This is an incredibly great value option for any kind of celebration. The flatbreads were very good, and we appreciated the drink variety. At the cafe, Mary and Jesse were absolutely awesome to interact with. Both were very friendly and personable, and they took extra steps to make the birthday night even more special. Huge shout out to both of them for all they did! Cafe aside, the view from the top is unbeatable, since you're at the highest point in the city. Admission is cheaper than other similar attractions, such as the Space Needle, and the experience up top is far better. The location is also great, as it's close to the 5th Ave Theater, the Convention Center, and much more. This is definitely on our "return to" list!

Spacious park with a lot of activities available. Easy access to the Iron Horse Trail fir walking or biking, a spacious swim beach, a boat launch, large playground, grassy areas for sports and ample parking. Reasonably close to Cle Elum and Roslyn, and a few minutes drive from several great hiking trails.
The campground has several portions. The loop closer to the river features a bit more private sites, plus less freeway noise than the sites near the ranger station. Bathrooms are newer and convenient, with several showers. My biggest complaint (as always with Washington State Parks) is the falsely advertised 3-minute show time. I used all 4 different showers at our specific restroom building, and time the water on my phone's stopwatch, and only one was close to 3 minutes (2:48). The worst was 2:10. All 4 took between 15-30 seconds to be warm enough to tolerate as well.

The visitors' center has an extensive display of educational and informational materials, detailing the work of the foundation, and providing opportunities for thoughtful discussion, community input and especially education for younger generstions. It is laid out in 4 main sections, and has both enough material to satisfy a long visit, while also having concise enough displays to be conducive to short stays. Joining one of the guided tours is a great way to learn. Perhaps best of all, admission is free!

Finally a garden space designed for kids! Too many gardens lack enough kid interest or features, and too many parks don't incorporate enough plants or garden art features. Gateway finally combines the best of both, geared toward kids. What a great place to get kids interested in plants and gardening, while providing great spaces to play, sit, and interact with others. This model should be repeated in communities nationwide.

Beautiful park with a scenic gorge, waterfalls, and hiking areas. The gorge trails take you deep into the rocks all the way to the river, providing multiple great viewpoints. Much of the trail down and back up is dozens of stairs in a row, so be prepared to work up a sweat and get your heartrate going! Crossing the bridge by the dam is a little harrowing with highway traffic so close by, so keep kids close!

Beautiful old estate with expansive gardens, great areas to stroll and several old greenhouses. The gardens were of course hibernating for winter during our visit, but I can only imagine how beautiful they would be in spring or summer. We still were able to pick up a few ideas to take home for our garden at home. Be aware it can be soggy/muddy in winter, and there is a bit of new work being done currently.

One of my favorite camping spots for the summer. Very close to downtown Winthrop, great fishing, swim beach, and play space. Many of the sites are lacking a bit in privacy, but if you can score one along the water, it makes up for it. The west side is currently undergoing some kind of upgrade or renovation, and I'm glad the state is investing on improvements.

Beautiful grounds to wander, with an incredible amount of unique and uncommon plants, along with some of the more common favorites. The gardens are structured nicely into many individual as l outdoor rooms, showcasing different themes and ideas. Even if you are not a gardener or plant enthusiast, the beauty and colors are worth a stop!

Fun place to stop if you're a fan of street art, graffiti, murals, etc. I don't exactly consider myself a graffiti supporter, but have to admit the variety and amount of tags and colors here is impressive. I also appreciate the fact that "allowing" street art here keeps tagging and graffiti away from other areas in town.

Fun but spooky experience going through the tube! It is completely dark, so bring a good light source, and quite chilly, so wear long pants and a sweatshirt! We were there when the outside temperature was 80° but the cave was in the 40s! You can go quite a far distance in, but we turned around after about halfway.

Beautiful, lesser-known spot to hike/walk in the fields and woods, and an excellent place to enjoy Autumn color. The full loop hike is not terribly long, but there are intermittent steep areas, so it still provides some good leg work. Overlooks at the ridge are perfect for a snack break or picnic lunch.

Excellent place of history and education, especially if you're not able to make it out to Fort Sumter. The grounds are scenic, and there is a great display of various cannon across the battery. The self-guided tour is easy to follow, and contains all of the critical points of interest in the fort.

Another lesser-known historical place to visit. The grounds are beautiful, especially the gardens, ponds and farm area. Lots of trails allow for great walking, and dogs are allowed on some of them. The house is open for tours at select times, and the goats are always up for a visit too.

Such a neat place to experience pivotal history of this country! Seeing the old buildings, bridge and other sites of critical clashes between the two sides really gives a great opportunity to stop and reflect on what the colonists and Founding Fathers believed in and fought for.

Beautiful place to wander and enjoy a wide assortment of plants and crops. The rose garden is spectacular, as are the dahlias, artichokes, gladiolus and much more. Also a great place for kids and young gardeners to learn about Luther Burbank's horticultural contributions.

Great out-of-the-way spot to learn some history not taught in school textbooks. I had no idea any Revolutionary War action took place in this area, and it was interesting and surreal to walk the exact paths the two sides took and envision the clash.

Scenic, short and simple hike makes a good, quick way to get a little exercise. The river and falls nd rapids are all picturesque and powerful. It's a but down the road from the main visitor entrance, so not too many cars or people to deal with.

Another essential historic stop on a trip through the region. Nice to have far more info and background on Roanoke than we learn as kids in school. The NPS staff on site were very friendly, welcoming and happy to share their knowledge as well.

Fun winery with a laid back approach. There are multiple wines to choose from on your flight, and many of them deserve a full-glass or take-home bottle. Pricing was reasonable, and our server was friendly and attentive.

Beautiful trails with great views of the mountains. The woods and marshes are excellent for bird watching. Kids will love the Hobbit Trail. Somewhat secluded location means it is usually not super busy.

Beautiful park full of geological history and science. Great place for kids to learn about volcanic processes, and see volcanic features up close, such as a lava tube, obsidian field, and cinder cone.
The tour to the top is $5 per person. Our tour guide was full of interesting facts and history about the lighthouse. It was fun getting to see the lens up close and learn all about the light station.
likes: On-site Activities: Lighthouse tour, lens viewing

reviews_attraction.text: Great spot to walk around and learn some local history about a lesser-known but influential leader of old America. The giant trees covered in Spanish moss are absolutely beautiful.
Another great spot to see the natural springs, popular both for swimming and for divers to check out the underwater cave system. Also some walking trails through the woods.
Fun spot with lots of family friendly options and reasonable prices. Mini golf goes right by the river, and has good views.

I would give this park a higher rating, except that you cannot park near the entrance. I don't mind a walk, but the only place to park is fairly secluded which means it's easy for people to break into your car unnoticed, and it looks like that happens fairly often since the small parking lot was absolutely covered in broken auto glass. I couldn't really enjoy my time at this park solely because I was worried about my car being broken into (I was lucky and my car was fine). The trails themselves were nice, mostly paved, and I enjoyed the views and birds. It is also next to a water treatment plant, which I can imagine could get rather pungent, although I did not smell it on my trip. I think that if the parking situation was improved this could be a wonderful park that I would visit often.

Not a huge park, but some decent trails along the water, and plenty of waterfowl. Restrooms are actual flushing toilets and there's a real sink to wash your hands. Water fountain next to the restrooms. Pretty water views with a long dock to walk along. The kids playground looked like a nice one, with seperate equipment for the smaller kids. There are picnic tables and benches, and even a bike repair station. I had to take away a star because the water by the wooden picnic table nearest the playground was incredibly littered (I'll post photos), it was very sad to see ducks foraging for food among the trash floating in the water.

I followed the directions from Google Maps to get here, but they either didn't take me to the main park, or this park has seriously gone downhill since the last time I was here (over 10 years ago). It is very pretty, but I constantly heard gunshots nearby and people talking, so I don't know if hunting is allowed in this park, or just very close to it, but I wasn't wearing bright colors so I was worried I'd be mistaken for an animal and shot so I left after only a few minutes. The parking lot was empty except for my car and I usually feel safe in empty parks alone, but the sounds of hunting very closeby worried me.

I have not camped here, I have only spent an hour here so far, but cannot wait to go back. I parked in the lot by the amphitheatre and covered picnic area, then took the trail down to the beach area. I was stunned by the beauty I saw! The blue water, the beautiful rock formations, the changing leaves on the trees (I came here in October). I felt like I was standing in a postcard! I only saw three other people the hour I was here. It made me want to explore the other areas of this park, one hour wasn't even enough time for the small area I saw. Very clean, very relaxing, stunning beauty.

We were there this afternoon and very much enjoyed our visit. We weren't there long as we we're catching a show and dinner at Cafe Nordo, but we enjoyed the views and the totem poles. There's also a memorial to Seattle's fallen firefighters here. It has a unique atmosphere, a bustling cobblestone square, surrounded by tall buildings. Be aware of the people around you though, we were practically chased by a very aggressive unstable man yelling. Other than him, the other people were nice. We walked back through after dark and it was filled with a lot of sketchy people.

One of the best aquariums I've ever visited. The employees were very knowledgeable and super friendly, happy to answer all of my questions. The exhibits are fantastic, I love the kelp forest, I'd never seen an exhibit like it at any other aquarium I've visited before. There were lots of people there, but it didn't feel overcrowded, I like the layout, enough room for everyone to see all the fish without feeling claustrophobic. I'm very glad I decided to visit. I will say that the price of a ticket shocked me a little, but it was worth it!

I very much enjoyed my visit to this park! The pedestrian bridge is well maintained and easily accessed from the good sized parking lot, it takes you over the railroad tracks and right to the beach. There are picnic tables next to the beach. The beach itself is fairly rocky, but beautiful, with old dock pilings sticking out of it in spots that the birds like to perch on. Quite picturesque, with beautiful views of the blue water and islands. Very clean park. I also saw some harbor seals out in the water. I will visit again soon.

My first time visiting here and I enjoyed it quite a bit. I only took the Sares Viewpoint trail, but it was a pleasant little hike. It was very easy and didn't take long at all, I don't think it's even quite a mile in length, but it takes you to a beautiful rocky area with a bench and lovely views. There's a restroom at the trailhead/parking lot, the trails are dog friendly, but not horse or bike friendly, and there are several areas with very uneven ground so it isn't wheelchair friendly either.

An incredibly beautiful location! Photos cannot possibly do justice to the sheer majesty of the mountain, cliffs, waterfalls, and glaciers here. A Northwest Forest Pass is required for the parking lot, and can be purchased at the Verlot ranger station. There are restrooms at the parking lot (non-flushing, but in permanent structures) The trail is paved for part, boardwalk for other parts. The trail is just over one mile long with approximately 200 foot elevation gain.

A clean, relaxing park. Beautiful beach with lots of Driftwood and tons of picnic tables, I also saw one BBQ grill next to a picnic table on the beach. They have life vests available at a kiosk next to the beach parking lot. Several restrooms located throughout the park. As well as the beach, there are also several parking areas and pull offs located on the forested road, with trails that branch out into the forest. Beautiful park year round. Discover Pass required.

My first time visiting this park was today (February 20th). I didn't have much time to explore, so I only saw a fraction of the trails here, but I enjoyed my brief walk through this area. The trails were nice, not overgrown, and not terribly muddy. I also enjoy finding parks that are still green in the winter, and this is one of them. I look forward to returning in the spring when flowers are blooming and leafy plants have sprouted again.

I love visiting this place, it has a very unique vibe to it. This is the site of the old Northern State Asylum farm. The farm buildings are deteriorating and not safe to enter, however many enter at their own risk. On clear days there is also a nice view of the mountains. If you go on a day where there are few people visiting it's a great place to explore, also many people walk their dogs here. This is one of my favorite locations.

I only visited part of the beach area today, but it was beautiful and sandy, surrounded by gorgeous forests. There were 3 picnic tables here, none too close together so you could still have some privacy. The trails were narrow, but well kept. There's a bathroom on the way into the park, and I think I saw a sign near this area for another restroom. I saw 3 deer along the roadside as I was driving out.

Small park, but lots of local historical value. When I stopped by all of the buildings were closed, so I wasn't able to utilize this park to its fullest, but I still enjoyed the historical buildings, restored rail car, and beautiful grounds. I only spent about a half an hour here, but I got some nice photos and really enjoyed my visit, I will be stopping by again when the buildings are open.

My favorite park. Beautiful year round, very crowded in summertime with people swimming and hiking, but it's still my favorite time to go. There are enough evergreen trees that the forest still looks green in the cold months. Plenty of waterfalls, not just the big main waterfall. I live an hour away from here, but still make the drive at least once a month to visit this incredible location.

I love this park. Well maintained and clean, nice trails, easy access to the river, and there's an abandoned train track and bridge that goes through the forest! I got some very unique photos here and spent a good 2+ hours just wandering the trails with my best friend, and we still only saw a small portion of what this park has to offer. I am looking forward to visiting again.

Great place to walk the beach, and beach comb. Also within easy walking distance of the lighthouse, and there's great views and a beautiful rock beach there. Also fun to walk out to the pier and take in the ocean views. While we were out on the pier we saw plenty of harbor seals and a few sea lions playing in the water. It appears to be dog friendly as well.

A nice, quiet little park. A flat, grassy area with picnic tables and benches, plus a paved walk way that circled the grassy parts of the park. There is a Marina off to one side, and a nice Sandy beach as well. Dogs are welcome as long as they are on leash. Everyone here was nice, but keeping to themselves.

A pretty little rocky beach area, but a bit loud because it's right next to the ferry dock. I still enjoyed myself, there is a bench on the trail that overlooks the water and a picnic table at the very beginning of the trail. It was nice, but I won't be back unless I'm there for the ferry.

Much cooler than I had expected. A great gift shop, and a wonderful experience taking the tour. During the tour you get to see a touch pool, an aquarium with cool fish including sturgeons, a chance to pet a live leopard shark, and a seal and sea lion show! I highly recommend it.

I only visited a very small area of this park. It was very clean, plenty of parking and a nice trail along the lake, picnic tables as well. Nothing spectacular or anything, but if you're looking to take a nice scenic stroll it would be a worthwhile stop.

I enjoyed this park quite a bit! Great views of the San Juans, Cascades, downtown, the marina, the oil refinery, and Seafarers Memorial Park. A very peaceful place, and it was very relaxing watching all the boats go by in the bright blue water below.

It's a small zoo, but it was clean and tidy, the animals seemed happy. Staff was friendly. I went by myself as a quick detour to stretch my legs on a long road trip and I'm glad I did. There's even a little free library here!
Tiny park with a paved trail, basketball hoop, and covered picnic area, with stairs that go down along a terraced hill to a small grassy area below
A very pretty bridge over a very pretty river with a cute little corner park right next to it. Right around the corner from the town of concrete.

Beautiful campground! Warnings...
1. Mosquitos are crazy vicious even with spray. Bring a screen enclosure, citronella candles and benedryll/calamine lotion. These buggers could be a new genetic form of vampire mosquitos? 2. Smokey - Pyro convention with high pressure system and no wind; campfire smoke is thick at ground level.  May require fireman masked ventilation system by peak burn hour! (Cough-cough)  3. Alfred Hitchcock would be impressed with the number of screeching birds (crows) at pre dawn hours! Do they really need to talk so loud? Bring several pairs of ear plugs.

Great sites with mostly private spaces. Gracious rangers and volunteers. Flush toilets and a shower (mosquito bar).  No power all basic sites. Bring extra levelers and chocks as this campground is on a hill!

Bzzzzzzzzzzzz-ack! Darn skeeters!

Tenting area is not private and has the grossest bathroom which is unfortunate because tenters use it the most. Art in the park and cedar tree was lame. Fish station is broken. Burn ban in effect and tons of campfires. (Cough cough) Hike to interpretive center is too steep for a significant portion of population-poor planning. Interpretive center closed but Walmart is open? Garbage cans are nonexistent.

Nice view of ocean and non-tent sites look delightful. Appreciate the yellow phone for credit cards.

Fantastic science center! Lots of hands-on activities teaching a wide range of concepts. Appreciate the opportunity to read instructions, observe and then read for further understanding (avoid misconceptions). Large portion of building dedicated to space exploration. Section for those 7 and younger. Automotive theme section. Small cafe. Unimpressive gift shop. Recommend looking into NARM or ASTC reciprocal option for free or reduced entry. Take hand sanitizer to curb germs!

Kids and Dad enjoyed touring this visitor center. Took about 2 hours for movie, tour and completion of Jr. Ranger packet. Not much shade at center. Dogs must be attended to at all times. Center has great visual aids of archeological records, working research area, screening room, hands on kid opportunities with a kiddo room. Small gift shop. No food here so bring a lunch or grab a bite before you head this way. Free entrance. Nice restrooms.

Kids and Dad enjoyed touring this visitor center. Took about 2 hours for movie, tour and completion of Jr. Ranger packet. Not much shade at center. Dogs must be attended to at all times. Center has great visual aids of archeological records, working research area, screening room, hands on kid opportunities with a kiddo room. Small gift shop. No food here so bring a lunch or grab a bite before you head this way. Free entrance. Nice restrooms.

Great place! Based on size and price this amusement park is worth a stop! There are plenty of kiddie rides, a couple wet rides and a mix of rollercoasters for the wild at heart. The waterpark is much bigger than what you can see. Water was warm. Tough to find a chair. Kids under 48 inches must wear a life vest. Only qualms would be cleanliness of swim dressing rooms, slow ride transitions and grounds are not zippy. Please like if helpful.

Understand the need for security and supervision, however, one young gal was on sphincter police mode and doing so inconsistantly. Made the experience uncomfortable and unpleasant. Example would be she told my child and I the "rule is to stand 2 feet back" and pointed to a imaginary line.  No art pieces were touched! A couple nearby were way closer to the artwork and nothing was directed to them. Just odd! Current exhibit was interesting.

Surprised the family enjoyed this museum as much as we did! Would not recommend for kids under 10 unless you prep them! Museum needs a kids' scavenger hunt to earn a coin to play pinball game or small souvineer! Not much is current (obviously) so they aren't as invested. Loved videos to relax feet. Wonderful cafe (try the philly steak and cheese) but a bit pricey. Recommend NARM or ASTC reciprocity program for free or reduced entry fees.

A boat tour is the only way to really see this park! Dress in layers since the wind from traveling and cooler water temps make it chillier than land! Sit on top right (passenger side if car) on trip out to get best views. To do this you need to be in line early. Also, the 1 o'clock tours tend to have the sun hitting the rocks for better colors. Covered area seating if you are too cold. Bring snacks for kids! 2.5 hour tour

Fantastic resource to the Tri-Cities! You will find weekend activities, a gift shop, guest presentations and a relevant museum. The museum is small but packed full with a pluthera of information on Hanford and its WWII connection, geological history and the Columbia Basins' natural resources. Plan to spend at least 2 hours. Buy a family pass and support the museum then visits hundreds of other reciprocating museums FREE.

Not art fanatics but enjoyed the visit. The greeter was hoity toity and made it clear she had no time for us sweat shirt wearing folks! Missed an opportunity to impress a family on the art world and the Stanford campus. Came to see the Golden Spike! The YO out front is "art" so don't touch it! (The same letters at the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame can be climbed on...just say'n)

The museum is way bigger than it appears. The entry fees are really high IMO. (Should have some roller coasters at that price!) It is definitely a museum on Walt and if that's what you want to see then this is your place. Totally enjoyed the miniature Disneyland and the Still Motion Movie activity. Not a lot to eat in this area. Car break-in so leave valuables at home.
likes: Activities: Miniature Disneyland, Still Motion Movie
dislikes: Facilities & Services: High entry fees, Limited food options

reviews_attraction.text: Not open Friday, Saturday, Sunday. Hmmm. Seems like a missed opportunity with the general public. When they are open they do have an amazing taxodermy collection.  There isn't a whole lot of memorable hands-on kids items. Nice employees. Bird viewing hut never has birds near it. Best to see birds from road. Nice 1.3 mile loop hike.

Free admission! A must visit even if you aren't a fan of art! What an amazing resource to the community and visitors. Wear comfortable shoes! Not a place for wild or unruly children, however, they do have a room for kids to touch and interact with art. The gun and armor collection is pretty impressive. Take a chance and visit!

Not based on tour. Bathrooms were gross and no toilet paper. If you cannot climb a gravel hill, you will not get to the bathroom. Sink had broken faucet. Not sure how this passed health standards? No ranger for 30 mins in info area and gals in gift shop didn't seem to know basic National Park info either. Cool gift shop!

Considering it's smaller size the amusement park has a little of everything to offer! Clean grounds and restrooms. Short lines on a Sunday morning. Honest folks as I left my credit card and they kept it safe. Lots of seating around rides. Gorgeous grounds with snoopy theme and tons of flowers!

Must see! This visitor center was amazing, fun and educational! Both indoor and outdoor viewing opportunities and both are recommended. Start with the video! Awesome Junior Ranger patch upon completion of their packet. Bring a coat and stable shoes for the outside portion. Plan on 2+ hours!

Great park for the kids! Bring a blanket, towels, sunscreen, bikes, trikes, scooters and a tennis racket. You'll find hours of fun on the grass lawns, playground equipment, tennis courts, pool or along the Columbia River. Park has bathrooms and concessions in the summer.

Above average campground with power, showers and paved level campsites. Shooting range and model airplane airport nearby. Yakima River sits to the east of this park. Would be hot here in summer! Closed during winter. No playground so bring scooters, bikes and frisbees!

This is rating the NP visitor center. The ranger was not friendly. The information is minimal. This location is a big gift shop. Lots of neat gifts wish the artifacts were equally neat. Parking lot warns of frequent vehicle break-ins so leave valuables home.

CDA well done! This kind of parks sets you out as a family destination! Absolutely beautiful park. Kids loved the toys and splash pad. Clean restrooms were available in two locations. Lots of picnic tables-wow! Locals are so lucky to have this available.
A large field with wild flowers and tall grasses. You will see a shed with a nearby catapult only. Enjoyed road out with trees canopying the road. If you don't stop here, it's not a deal breaker.
This map location is not the national park's official visitor center! You must go another 2 blocks to the Calumet Visitor Center. Well worth a visit!
Loved the butterflies and huge potted plants! Not really into the rest of the gardens. I really tried to like it. Great gift shop.
Awesome NPS gal working the front desk today! Kids enjoyed the small museum. The front had a fun hands on parachute model.

I've been in St. Louis for the last eight years, but this was my first time up in the Arch. We had family in town and therefore an excuse to be a tourist in our own city! But we decided to do this kinda last minute. Apparently, if you decide in advance, you can not only buy your tickets online, but you can also schedule your time and date. We arrived around 3:15p on a Saturday in June and the earliest available time was 4:35p. We killed time exploring the couple rooms in the old building that had some great historical information.....and then we went to Starbucks across the street.

We were allowed to enter at 4p, so we headed over and went through security around 4:15p. We probably didn't get on the elevator to ride up until around 5:20p. The time in between was spent standing in one line, then standing in another, then receiving a number, then having our picture taken, then standing in another line, then standing in ANOTHER line and then standing and waiting outside of our assigned elevator. And these elevators are pretty darn small, as you might imagine. For any of you who might be worried about feeling claustrophobic, there is an elevator on display next to where you by your tickets. You can even step inside and see how you feel. Make sure you do that before hand if you have any concerns.

The ride is 4 minutes. Our ride was pretty smooth. The only problem I had was that the elevator door is clear, so you can see the insides of the structure falling down behind you, which made me dizzy to watch. My husband, on the other hand, said it made him feel better.

Once you get up to the top, it's pretty darn tiny - go figure. But you can get some pretty neat photos!

One of my fears was that I'd be able to feel the Arch swaying (as many people told me you could). But unless I was standing and leaning against a wall, I really didn't feel it.

The ride back down was 3 minutes and for some reason it was a little bumpy and clanky....I can't say that was very encouraging.

Over all, this was a fun excursion because I was with my family and having a great time. I had no idea that getting up to the top would be the huge process that it was. But I'm really glad that we did it together!

What an amazing place to have so near my in-laws. Military families get in free, so we take our son basically every day that we're in town when there's spare time. On our most recent visit I think we went three days in a row. And every time, my two year old boy was very entertained and wouldn't have left if I hadn't carried him away.

I think his favorite parts were the firetruck (with buttons, lights, costumes and a fire pole), the red truck (an actual truck that they can sit in and press buttons and they look under the hood where all the parts are labeled) and the grocery (with mini carts, plastic produce and a register to check out).

We also took out 9 year old niece on one visit. She absolutely loved the house with a full play kitchen. I'm pretty sure she stayed in there for the whole hour.

There are many other entertaining options, a stage (with costumes), a shelf full of books), a closed off area specifically for those 2 and under, trains and train tracks, a water play area with plastic fish and fishing rods, an area with large, soft building blocks, arts and crafts and an oversized light up board.

Just a note, no liquids allowed. So you'll have to leave your Starbucks sitting at the counter.

Boy, this is a great park! And the neighborhood certainly knows it! At around 4p on a Saturday, this place was absolutely mobbed. But my little boy still had a great time, so that's all that matters, right?

I think his favorite part was feeding the ducks and pigeons at the lake (even though there's a sign not to do so, EVERYONE is doing it. Someone gave us their left-over bread). And don't worry about that lake - there's a gate surround the playground so your little ones aren't likely to make a fast escape to the water.

I love that they have those swings that are meant for parent and child - an adult swing on one side and a supportive swing for baby that move together. But on a busy day, expect a wait as there are only two of these.

I think hubby was most impressed with the "elevator" for the kids. There's a pole with a small platform to stand on that they can ride from the second level back down to the ground. You can't ride it back up, but when it's empty it moves back up on it's own for the next child.

There's a section that I think is meant for slightly older kids. It looked like an awesome spider web/ropes course. If I weren't huge and pregnant, I would've been trying it out myself!!
likes: Unique play structures (elevator pole, spider web/ropes course)

reviews_attraction.text:
What a beautiful way to spend my last day in Colorado!! We'd stayed the night before in Colorado Springs and drove up to the Denver Airport. This was the perfect place to stop on the way! Although the google maps tried to take us the to golf club, the man at the gate let us turn around and pointed us in the right direction.

You pay $7 for a sticker to put in your car window so you can park for the day. Be careful! This sticker REALLY sticks and didn't want to come off in one piece.

After paying for our parking, we looked at a map with someone working the desk. We told him that we wanted to do a hike that would take about 2 hours. And since we'd never visited before, we wanted the trail to be one of the prettier/more interesting ones. He suggested a couple options, but definitely recommended the Fountain Trail. It was just what we were looking for! It was mostly flat and very open - the trail was wide and mostly covered with gravel. And the views were beautiful! We passed others on the trail, but it wasn't crowded by any means.

My sister brought us here years ago when we visited. It was a fun place that she’s drive all the way down town to visit so my niece could play and have fun. I remember that we fed baby goats a bottle of milk (hubby absolutely loved that!). I also remember buying eggs at their farm store.

This time we were in town for a wedding and needed to entertain ourselves and our little one during the day before evening festivities. So we brought him here. Parking is free and it’s only a few bucks to get in. We opted to pan for gemstones because my almost-two-year-old loves to play in water. It was $5 for a small bag or $8 for a large. We went with the small. It was a pretty decent size as we didn’t use it all at once. And we actually found a good amount of little stones. My boy also loves rocks, so he was totally into it.

We walked around and saw a lot of animals. But I think my boy’s favorite part was simply the playground.

We will definitely return on our next visit as this is definitely a place that’s great for all ages.

Garden of the Gods is absolutely beautiful! We recently visited for a second time and I am happy we did. There are several places to pull off, explore and take pictures. This would be lots of fun for all ages - the kids can run and climb and adults can relax and enjoy the view.

The visitors center is a great place to stop, as well. The gift shop has some great shirts among many other things. And if you need a coffee or a snack, they've got that (I recommend the cinnamon sugared pecans)!

Also, if you leave your car in the visitor parking lot after it closes, no worries! Apparently, a lot of people make this mistake. Our friends left their car so they could ride with us. And by the time we came back, their gates were closed. Luckily, we tried more than one gate and the second one hadn't been locked. When they got to their car they found a printed note telling them that the gate had been left open for them and to simply please lock it behind them when they left. Thank goodness!!

I give this place a 5/5 because it’s beautiful! So beautiful that we saw two separate groups working with a photographer on the same day (both were maternity photos). So this is obviously a popular place for such things.

My husband somehow found this place while I was working and loved it so much that he brought me back the next day. We brought the baby and our running stroller. Be warned that none of the paths are paved, so don’t bring a stroller that can’t handle it.

The parking lot had plenty of spaces when we visited on a Sunday evening. It’s right by a big, beautiful stream of water. There’s also a large sign with a map of all the paths as well as pictures of the different locations.

We walked the whole park in well under thirty minutes. The paths are mostly flat, so there’s nothing strenuous.

I loved the sign telling about the old trees - about five hundred years old! I’ve never been to a park like that. It was like having a mini history lesson. Very fun!

This is one of the most beautiful buildings in the city and definitely one of our major landmarks. They were closed last year in order to do some major renovations. From what little I’ve seen, they did a fantastic job! The original architecture was respected and everything is still incredibly classy and ornate.

I suggest that when you attend an event that you arrive early and park across the street in the back at the KET lot. On a Tuesday at 2:30p it cost us a flat $3. While the lot right next to Music Hall was $15.

I used to love coming here for Cincinnati Pops Concerts. They would bring in amazing guests such as Kristin Chenowith, Martin Short, Audra McDonald, Patti Lupone and many more.

What a great park with multiple different play grounds. Each more unique than the last. The first we drive by upon entering had a few large porch swings for lack of a better name. It also has Owen’s place. Instead of the usual climbing structure it was a wide and long ramp system that included a handful of little houses (decorated with chalk drawings), slide, climbing wall and a little “elevator” the kids can ride down. There was also a spinning pad near here and quite a few large instruments.

The next playground we came across looked brand new! And it looked like a jungle gym crossed with a kids rope course.

So fun! We will definitely be hitting up this park a lot this summer!

Our go-to beach in Holland. It can get busy for sure, but it’s worth it. Park across the street where it’s free. The kids will love the playground. And there are plenty of picnic tables and grills if you’ve brought food.

A huge dune prevents you from walking straight onto the beach. But there are two ways through here. By the playground you can climb the dune or take a set of stairs. Or I’ve by the restrooms, you can simply walk through the tunnel. We like to switch off because both options are all part of the experience.

Once you’re done with the beach, there are water fountains by the restrooms so you can rinse off the sand.

I can’t believe we waited so long to check this place out! When I found out that military could get BOGO Free tickets for the summer, I knew we needed to give it a shot. After two minutes inside we decided to get a pass. This will be the perfect place to stop after school on rainy or cold days. There’s an endless amount activities that are perfect for my three year old - water area, puzzles, climbing and slides, tree house with a bee hive, a vet, a pizza shop, trucks in dirt and the list goes on.

Just a heads up that while strollers are allowed, I found it much easier without due to there being multiple levels.

This great little park is super close to my son’s preschool and was the perfect place for the school picnic. The playground was a decent size, so there was plenty of entertainment for the kiddos. Not to mention tons of green space for running around. There’s a shelter that you can rent and it has about four grills. There were plenty of tables for us to spread out and enjoy the evening. The only problem was the small parking lot. I’m sure on a normal evening, that wouldn’t be a problem. I hope we have another get together here soon!

Now that we’ve moved to a different part of town, this is our new go-to Park. My husband and I love all of the paved trails as it provides a nice walk in the evening. There’s a gazebo and a swing that makes things feel evening a little romantic. Also, how fun is it to see deer everywhere?

My little boy loves the playground near the main parking lot. I’m sure he will be happy to explore the other two playgrounds that this park features.

The only downsides? Very little shade, wandering skunks and no swings for the kiddos.

It was our last night in town, we’d enjoyed some ice cream in the sun and then we went for a little drive just to enjoy the scenery. We stumbled upon this park and thought it would be good to let our little boy run off some energy before returning to our BnB for the night. While the playground was a little hike through the field and up the hill from the parking lot, that was probably best for energetic son. Lol. On a Sunday night in mid June, don’t expect it to be very busy. I think we saw two other people.

We had some time to kill and I wanted my little one to burn off some energy before nap time. This was the closest playground, so we came here. It’s a huge park with a large pond. Great for walking with friends, family or the dog.

But as far as playgrounds go, it was only so-so. It was certainly pretty unique, but not very big or entertaining for a toddler. Also, bonus points for a playground with ample shade. This didn’t have that either.

What a peaceful place to sit and visit. There are benches throughout and plenty of tall bushes and trees that help you to feel very tucked away which is nice. If I lived or worked in this neighborhood I would enjoy eating my lunch here and enjoying the peace and quiet.

There is a sign saying no talking on cell phones. Most people seem to respect that. The quiet is so calming. It would be a shame to have to listen to someone's phone call.

What a great park! Especially for my almost three year boy who LOVES trains. There are quite a few trains to see and a great playground next to it. I will warn you that there are signs asking you to please not climb the trains....but literally everyone was ignoring those signs (yes, even parents). So not sure if that’s actually ever enforced or followed.

This park is very near the Main Street and is definitely one we’d visit again!

My favorite thing about this park? It’s completely in the shade! Perfect for a hot summer day. Mom, dad, just sit and relax at the picnic table. This place has a nice size playground and swings (toddler and adult) for the kiddos. My little boy is particularly a fan of the stationary car.

The only downside is there’s no close parking lot. Only street parking in the neighborhood. Which makes me feel like I’m invading their space.....

I didn't get to spend much time here, but I had a nice little visit the other day! I had no idea that this little gem was tucked away, just across and down the street from West County Mall! It had a beautiful little pond, a soccer field and a great playground! According to the little map I looked over, there seems to be plenty of trail worth walking or running! I look forward to stopping by again the next time I'm in the area!

Come up here for a beautiful view of the city! There’s not much parking, so that could potentially be a problem. But it never has been for me!

Bring the kids! Because there’s a great little play area with a jungle gym for them!

Also, if you’d like a steep adventure, there’s a little trail off to the side that leads you straight up through the trees and to another lookout!

What a good find. Check this place out!

This is our go-to place for hiking! We like all the up-hill action first, take the steps down and then cool off with the flat trail through the field and along the river. You get a some shade, some sun and some pretty look-outs. When we went this past weekend, there were lots of families - most of them enjoying the water! On the busy days, it can be hard to find a parking spot!

Another park we always have to stop by when we’re in town. Especially now that we have a kiddo who loves playgrounds! Because they’ve got a great one. We’re usually in the area because we love Main Street Holland, so this is easy to do in the same afternoon. There’s a lovely view of the water and there’s an outdoor theatre/stage that occasionally has live music!

Beautiful! This is definitely a place you'll take a few pictures! The building is gorgeous outside and in. I'm a particularly big fan of all the beautiful tiles. And don't forget to go all the way to the top so you can look out over the city! There's only one small elevator, so plan on waiting if there's even the slightest crowd.

I grew up at this park, so it will always have a special place in my heart. There is a shaded sitting area, there are swings and there is a jungle jim with a slide. This is a great place to bring your kids and wear them out!
This park has two playgrounds, swings and a splash pad. I love it because it’s not too far from home, it’s never too crowded and because it’s easy to visit with the kids after working out at the Y.

Love this trail. You can make it short and easy and stick to the first section which is a wide groomed path, handicap accessible, to the first lake lookout. The walk through the woods is beautiful and in the spring filled with more wild flowers than Pete's Woods trailhead! If you take the paths further you can single file hike up the woods to Old Baldy Dune, an over 300' high dune. Spectacular lake views. Breathtaking. There is a pair of port-a-potties, , so that's always helpful. A little more out of the way, so usually not busy like the main Sleeping Bear turn outs, which is wonderful. Highly recommend.

Went to outdoor Art Fair on the grounds. Nice to be at an asset fair with some shade! Lovely trees, lots of space for artists tents. Have to believe that having the artists in view of a main road like that bumped up attendance immensely. Win/win. Betty's food truck was on hand with the best nachos I've had in ages. The center building bathrooms were a nice plus as opposed to port-a-potties...I'll happily stand in line for a few minutes in exchange. Show was supposed to be over at NW College, so I missed not going into Dennos Museum while at the show, but this location was wonderful.

The Mart in Chicago is an institution. Phenomenal block-sized building, chock full of anything you might need for your home. Grab a designer and have them take you. Need flooring, beautiful tile, fixtures, wall coverings, furniture or just about anything else? You can find out here. Couple times a year the One Of A Kind Sale takes over a floor. Fantastic event full of known, and new, artists, jewellers, designers and foodies.

Wow! Low on iron??? This is the right place. Yikes, you can smell the metal as soon as you approach the pergola. Took me back to my aunt's farm and her well water. Several people came to fill a thermos or jug. Two from our party drank from the fountain head. No ill effects ;) It's right on the main drag, so take the time to stop and run over to it. Worth it just to read the history posted there.

Beautifully secluded and off the beaten path. Short walk from car to water. Wheelchair friendly if you don't mind unpaved paths. We saw a beautiful pair of Peliated Woodpeckers very close to the path on lower trunks of trees, totally ignoring our presence. Pond is lovely, last summer it had two rocking chairs on the platform to sit and watch the goings on. Total peace & quiet.

Beautiful historic site. Old log cabin along with the Light House itself a bonus. Beautiful beach. Quaint Lighthouse,  only 35 steps to top. Well worth the $4 adult/$2 child fee to climb to the light! Lovely views. Or totally free, walk around first floor and see how they lived, see photos from the past, listen to a video presentation and go to the little gift shop.

Green Point Dunes is a beautiful winding hike through the woods. Two parking areas. Stairs to beach access closed right now, but hopefully will reopen in summer as long as water doesn't rise much. Two high viewing platforms and another down by the lake. Gorgeous. I'd recommend yak traks or something similar when there's any snow as steep ups and downs get slick.

Old Baldy is a beautiful hike. Highly recommend. Even wheelchairs can go up to the first look out site. Past that it is a single file trail through the woods and up the dune further to the actual Old Baldy Dune. Spectacular. Over 300' high. Breath taking views. In the late spring the wildflowers in the woods are even better than at Pete's Woods trailhead.

Whether hot and sunny, windy, rainy, snow and/or ice covered, the views from Sleeping Bear (like the wooden platform at Pierce Stocking Drive #9) are worth going to see. This October visit we were sand blasted and numbed by the first real cold winds of the season, but it was still a great visit. Highly recommend any time of year. Just dress for the temps!

Much less crowded beach with beautiful wooded trails. If you're a rock hound, this is a fantastic find. Well worth the drive to get to it. Not too long a drive from TC, & VERY close to Torch Lake. Single portapotty type relief station, no running water, so be prepared. (Bring some toilet paper just to be safe, have been there when there was none)

The Commons is a great place to visit, and these trails bordering it were wonderful. Creek running through entire area, couple little waterfalls, well marked. I was doubtful, but The Hippie Trees are actually pretty magical. Short loops, long trails, hilly but not difficult, something for everyone. Highly recommend.

Beautiful shoreline & wooded trail. Love it in the winter. Snowshoe, hike when the snow is low or just add some Yaktraks to those boots. Now that you can hike all the way up to Petobago Pond, it's even more beautiful. It's a very important watershed, and it's great that it is being protected from development.

Always gorgeous in the summer, different kind of beautiful in the winter on a nice day. Hardly anyone else there. Great views of the shore and ice fields. Highly recommend. When really snowy take your snowshoes, if icy put some YakTrax on your boots. Steps all disappear and it's all drifted snow.

This hike is strenuous, but just beautiful. Recommend hiking boots instead of sneakers, and take lots of water, especially if there a heat advisory like there was the day we went. Photo op once you get to the Chip is incredible. May be a line waiting, but it's worth it.

Steady climb but not difficult. Beautiful look out points. The hike through the words is great on hot days as you are in the shade a great deal of the time. The abandoned kilns at the base of the trail are fascinating, if not a bit spooky. Highly recommend.

Southern most tip of the island. Quaint old lighthouse and keepers buildings. Really nice fishing pier also and beautiful beach. Usually Osphrey nesting on building (nest on chimney this past week). Like a step back in time. Always recommended.
Great lighthouse with gorgeous vistas. Worth the long drive up the peninsula. We went on a very blustery cold day and had the place to ourselves. No matter what the season, it's beautiful there.
Beautiful views, long winding climbs up into the cliffs. Go at own pace, go as far as you want. Watch the surfers, further to the south you can see the hang glides taking off. Just spectacular.
It's gorgeous in the winter. The ice. The snow. You can hike down to the very point and see both East and West Bay at the same time. It's beautiful. And swinging in snowshoes can't be beat!
Beautiful area. No challenging hike here. Beautiful woods, lovely shoreline, some picnic tables, and most of the time, relative solitude. Sleeping Bear has something for everyone.
Went in February, and it was closed as far as the buildings go, but even so the view from the lake front is gorgeous and definitely worth the stop.
Gorgeous lighthouse right in the shadow of the great bridge. Well worth the stop. Lovely views of the bridge and of Mackinac Island.  Recommend.
Little cool still, but great picnic area. There were Sand Hill Cranes in the area today, so nice opportunity to watch and take some photos.
This is such a cute little light house tower....right near the Point Trail, so very convenient. Nice beach here too and parking.
If you love lighthouses, and are in northern Michigan, you definitely need to stop here. It's well worth the scenic drive.

This is a fun place to walk and do a little people watching while you marvel at the fabulous scenery. The actual pier is only open partway out before they charge you to walk the entire length. There are lots of little pop up shops selling jewelry and souvenirs along the free part. There is a public bathroom at the beginning of the pier and lots of blow up toys you can pay to use. The beach itself was very busy when we were there. The parking is a challenge. There is a garage close by which is what we ended up doing. Free parking would require a long walk. The sand is so pretty, very fine and white.

This park is truly astonishing. The mesa arch is one of the most photographed arches in the world. You can expect a lot of photographers at sunrise which I found really interesting to see them all at work. The views are quite unbelievable.
