My husband thinks it's better than the grand canyon, I don't know if I'm quite there but I see his point. It's an easy hiking spot with these little stone markers that help you find the path. You do not want to skip this park is you're in the area.

The Strong is an amazing experience. Be prepared to spend a lot of time, if you expect to cover the whole thing. I would suggest you plan on needing two separate days to get through all the different areas. There are so many unique things to experience. It will be difficult to keep your kids moving to the next exhibit. Don't expect be to bored as a parent, there are a lot of interesting things you will want to try and experience as well!

We walked into the beach and paid the $2.50 per person. It's a bit of a jaunt to get there from town. The beach was not as nice as I'd expected. The top part was filled with coral. The sand was nicer closer to the water. There were interesting rock croppings that you could swim to and sit on. The color of the water is a lovely turquoise. We had a toddler with us and because the waves were so slight, it was perfect for her.
dislikes: Sand quality (implied, only nicer closer to water)

reviews_attraction.text: Amazing to see all the siege lines that were dug hundreds of years ago by both the British and the Patriots.  The signage gives you a good idea of how it all happened but the visitor center has a movie or two that will set the context for you.  It's so easy to forget how much others have sacrificed. It gave multiple examples to talk with our kids about the importance of character and courage.

Several different areas to explore outside. I really enjoyed how far back in time it took you.  The old armor and houses almost made me feel I was in an old English village. The museum is great and covers a large time spectrum.  I felt at ease asking the living actors questions and they always had answers and additional interesting information.

If you get out and stand under the monument next to the battlefield, there is a audio you can push and listen to while you look out over the battlefield.  It's easy to imagine the soldiers from both sides and the amount of emotion involved must have been astounding.  It's a great stop as you are touring the encampment area.

Nice part of historic old key west. Lots of touristy shops mixed with old architecture. The water is close and the boats we saw docked were the nicest I've ever seen. Huge yachts along with fishing charters. It's an interesting people watching spot for sure. The tour we had gave me an appreciation for the history involved.

You can't go wrong visiting the largest living thing in the world. These trees are one of a kind.  You can understand why people thought they were a hoax years ago. Well worth the drive up the mountain. Take advantage of a few of the hikes to lookouts. You won't be disappointed.

It's clean and the animals seem well cared for. The zoo gets a lot of criticism because it's animals are getting older and some have been dying.  I find this unlikely since, I'm sure the zoo is desperate to keep the animals alive in order to keep the zoo profitable.

There is a lovely hike through the woods and you can walk out onto the beach at the one end. We had a little picnic lunch overlooking the beautiful water and could see the lighthouse in the distance plus watch the sailboats go slowly by. We had a lovely afternoon.

Disney is one of those places people love to hate because there is nothing bad to say about them. They took temperatures on the way in as per covid safety. It snowed the night we were there but that just increased the magic. Be prepared for lots of people.

Nice to wander down and to realize this street has stayed so much the same for two hundred years. It's really fabulous to realize people still keep their homes on the street. If you're a history buff or just a lover of beautiful places, don't miss it.

It's a pretty walk to the top. Be prepared with water if it's hot outside. The entire trail is very exposed. We were there in December and saw five other people total on the trail. If you don't like crowds or heat, consider visiting in the winter.

This is a super busy trail with both people and four wheel drive vehicles up and down the trail. After you get to a certain point, obviously, it's not an issue because they can't climb the rocks 😃. The view is spectacular at the top.

You'll be delighted when you pull into the parking lot and realize how many little goblins fill the valley. It looks like they are having a huge goblin festival. Surprisingly fun to walk through and watch your kids climb.

It's a national park for good reasons! I especially loved the road leading into it. The views of the mountains are astonishing against the gigantic fortress stones. The Hickman bridge hike was our favorite.
This is a pretty hike with a great payoff. We were there in winter, so no swimming for us. But, I imagine in winter it's amazing. Although, there were only two other people on the trail with us.
Watch for the Cairns all along the trail that leads to the view point. Even if you miss them, you can still find your way. A gorgeous view that is hard to duplicate anywhere on the planet.
The docent was very helpful answering questions and the house was well appointed to the time period. It was very easy to imagine the officers meeting and making out their treaty terms.
If you've never been, you should go! Just beware, the roads are so twisty and not many guard rails. It's a little terrifying worth it.
We went to get a rapid covid test. They were very friendly and organized. Hardly any wait, it was all very efficient and painless!
Right off the Erie canal with lots of trails,a playground, a dog park, and shelters. A well maintained pretty park.
A great walking park with a large pool for the summer months. Good camping spots. A lot of deer. Watch out!
If the line is super long, you can always go around to the side and look in through the glass very easily.

Such a great place to day hike.  The distance from this trailhead to the top is about 2.3 miles give or take. Majestic views of the Bremerton valley and Seattle from the top. Picnic tables available to take a break or eat lunch.  Trails allow horseback riding and motorbike riding. It is not difficult but there a tons of loose rocks along the path so be careful to avoid twisted ankles.  Hiking sticks recommended.

Such a great place to hike or camp. Well-marked trails of different distances and degrees of difficulty. Parking is free. Some entrances cost $25 per car for access. Parking is otherwise free. Overnight camping is $20 per day. Campsites are clean and easily accessible.  Bathrooms available at the bottom of all trails. The park is great place to stay for the week or weekend.

Simply worth the price of admission.  Really well done.  The staff is great.  Well-kept up park and educational signs everywhere. The museum is terrific, including the feature short movie.  Just love the place.  Discounts for multiple days or a combo pack for Yorktown and Jamestown. You can see the entire place in one day so plan to be there awhile. 5 stars!

Very nice winery right on Lake Chelan. Super friendly staff. Great location, just minutes from downtown. Outdoor and indoor seating available. It offers lunch and dinner.  Happy hour 3 to 5 PM. $12 samples of 3 wines. Huge discounts on older wines. Good views of the vines. Plenty of parking.  Summers are super busy so get there early. Enjoy.

Really well done.  Brings you back in time and gives you an appreciation for life back then.  Super friendly employees. Lots to do and see.  Definitely worth visiting.  A visitor's pass is required for some events.  Bring your walking shoes.  Plan to spend at least a half a day there.  Open 9 to 5 PM.

I thought it was just fantastic.  You could spend hours there and still not see it all.  There are so many displays and historical notes.  Definitely worth visiting and taking your time to see it all.  Well-organized museum.  Admission required but there are discounts available.

Great place to spend the day or night.  Large beach area and large camping and picnic sites.  Discovery Pass required for day trips.  Reservations required for overnight stays.  Hook-ups available on some sites for RVs and trailers.  Definitely worth visiting during the summer.

Beautiful views at the top. Easy drive to the top. About 7 miles from Dosewallip State Park in Brinnon. 2.5 mile hike up from the base off the main road if you enjoy hiking. Fairly steep switchbacks.  Good place for a day hike. No camping allowed.

Very small park. There are a few benches. It's not well maintained.  Easy to cycle through with a mountain bike.  It is usually quiet and peaceful. I suppose you could eat lunch at one of the benches.  There is only room for a few cars.

Wide open community park. Great for walking, biking, skateboarding, and volleyball. Large covered area with tables for eating. Raab Park is really nice. Great for kids and picnics. Permanently mounted grills are available for cooking.

Just 10 miles up the mountain from Chelan, WA, this trailhead offers majestic  views of the mountains and lake. There is an upper and lower trailhead.  There's plenty to do year round.  Definitely worth visiting even for a half day.

The Governor's palace is spectacular and 100% worth touring.  The gardens are well kept, including the maze out back.  Wonderful to see history presented so well.  Face mask required for entry and during the tour.
Great place to walk around, jog, or bike along the paved paths. Super clean and safe.  Great views. Had a spectacular time and can't wait to visit again.  Outdoor bathrooms on and near the beach.
Really nice waterfront, eateries, and shops. Dined at Scales, great seafood and steak restaurant. Parking was $5 for a few hours. Area was clean and patrolled by security. Had a good time.
Fantastic place to bike, walk, jog, kayak, and more. Really well taken care of. Plenty of nearby parking. Picnic tables available to reserve. 3.9 mile trail around the lake. Great times.
Good sized park with play area and a couple of miles of walking or running trails. Not usually crowded.  Good scenery with a creek that runs through most of the park.
Nice place to relax and view the mountains along the Columbia River.  Discover pass required.  Trails for walking are available down to the water.  Enjoyable scenery.
Fabulous place to visit. Definitely worth going. I could have spent 2 hours there and not been bored.  Magnificent views.  Well-preserved historical property.
Great shop in downtown New Bern.  Lots of history.  The staff was friendly and courteous.  Many Pepsi souvenirs obviously.  Nice place for a quick visit.
Excellent place to get away for the day or weekend.  Nice scenery for biking, running, or walking. Good for a day picnic or overnight camping.
A spectacular place to visit - full of naval history. Concerts on the Avenue with the Secretary of the Navy...priceless. Open to the public.
Great place to view the bay and walk around. Close to shops in downtown Poulsbo. Many activities are held here.
So many place to hike or walk. Well covered areas for views, picnics, etc. So much to do if you like outdoors.
Great place to take the family or to just find some peace and quiet. Beautiful views of the Hood Canal.
Clifton Days - had a great time. The atmosphere was great.  Fun things to do for people of all ages.

Gorgeous place to visit, the scenery with all the plant life, along with so many different kinds of birds to keep track of. They have a nature trail to hike, so you can admire the scenery. It is also one of the best fly-fishing places in the world, for you along with a friend or loved one, to out smart some of the biggest or smartest fishes they have to offer. So have at it, take your chances on catching a monster trout, it is only opened for the fly-fishermen with the skills to land one.

Great wine selections offered by them, they have an outstanding staff on hand to assist you with their wine selections. The bonus for them is that they are located off the Green Belt facing the Boise River with great views, so you can just ride your bike to them, along with burning some calories off on the way back home, kudos for that.

Beautiful place to take the family for a visit or camping trip, they have two ponds to fish for Bass or Blue Gill, or you can enjoy hiking the sand dunes, or renting some boards from the gift shop. They also have a Planetarium for people to come visit to check out our solar system.

Out standing place in the mountains filled with pine trees in the middle of nowhere, with three different temperature pools to choose from for relaxation. A great friendly environment along with the price to use the geothermal pools, also you can bring your own goods.

Another place in Boise Idaho to take family and friends to go float on the Boise River. It is about 2.5 hour float trip down on the river. Ps; not enough parking, so just take the city park bus up, then float down to where you parked your vehicle.

Awesome place to visit with your family the scenery along with the views not to mention all the hiking you can do around the Sawtooth areas. Also the rafting along with fishing on a Salmon River one of the most beautiful areas in Idaho to visit

Great place to visit in East Idaho, especially if you love to fly fish, also for families or with whom ever you choose to be with. You can also go over to Yellowstone National Park to view the wildlife or the beautiful scenery they have.

What a beautiful view from the top looking down and across, the marine life is picture eristic, you will love all the different species of fish that can see. Bring your water proof camera, you won't regret it that's for sure.

Great park to take the family with kids to enjoy the water hydrants during the summer heat. They also have two fishing ponds stocked with trout, Bass, also catfish for kids and their grown up parents to fish in.

Great, place to run, walk, bike ride, kayak, sunbathing, fishing  or just having fun with mens best friend or ladies if you are not into the other things I mentioned. Also they do have some gorgeous views.
Bring your camera to take lots of pictures to this truly great place to visit, or take your family for vacation on the island of Oahu. It is truly a life changing moment for you or the family.
Another great place for you to visit, or with family members. To ask the Rangers question about what there is available to see and do, along with places to go visit while you are there.
Love this isolated beach on the Naval, also Airforce base for active duty or retired military, you can swim, snorkel, relax to the waves, or do some fishing, or fly fish like we do.
Been here so many times, I just can not say enough great things about this gorgeous place of a National Park, except everyone needs to come visit once in their lifetime.
Beautiful golf course, even better now that it is no longer a private club. Now anyone who wants to golf on it can do so, just call to reserve your T time.
Outstanding place to take your family, they have barbecuing Pitts with tables next to the beach for the family to enjoy and have fun on or off the water.
One of the cleanest camp sites around, they even have flushing toilets to go with running water. The camp host are very friendly people to talk to.
One of the most spectacular views of Oahu, not to mention all the WW11 history objects they still have there for tourists visit and touch.
Great place to visit or take family members to ask questions and find out about information there is available in the park areas.
Pretty nice place to take the family to see the wild fish like trout, salmon, sturgeon or steelhead behind a viewing glass.
Definatly one of the places to visit on the island of O'ahu, if you enjoy snorkeling or diving this is the place to do it.
Love this place, for the ocean views, you can do some swimming or snorkeling, also some fly fishing if you are into that.
Awesome place to visit and get lots of information about the park, along with hiking trails, books that they offer ther6
Awesome, place to take friends or family on camping trips or what ever you choose to do in the great outdoors.
It has some of the best views to see the Saw Tooths Mountain range at a distance from the summit overlook.

Sarah P. Duke Gardens are always a lovely visit. Even when the parking lot seems crazy, there are some great hidden corners that you can have all to yourself. They continue to expand the gardens and recently they have added more walks and a waterfall area in the Asiatic garden. The main formal garden is also frightful and filled with the seasonal flowers that make these type of gardens beautiful. The native garden area is also beautiful especially in winter when the camellia are blooming. There is also plenty of lawn to sit on for picnics,  playing frisbee, etc. My only real complaint is that the parking meters take users too long as there are no signs posted indicating that you need your tag info in order to pay. A mobile app driven meter would work much more efficiently.
dislikes: Lack of signage for parking payment

reviews_attraction.text: This national park is absolutely amazing so if you're in Maui, you must make time to visit! A major issue to keep in mind is if you are not staying in Central Maui, it takes about 1.5 to 2 hours to reach the entrance because of all the switch backs you must navigate from Kula. Also a car with a tight turning radius is also a great idea because of the tight turns here and On the Road to Hana. There is an entrance fee per passenger car as at all National Parks. Definitely go to the smaller visitors center along the crater and see the observatory. On a clear day, you should be able to see ther Big Island in the distance. You can also walk down into the crater from the rim. Parking at the top is limited so the earlier you go, the better your chances of getting parking.

The Philadelphia Museum of Art is a fabulous museum. The permanent collection has some great pieces as evidenced by the exhibits that are bright together from within the museum as well as special exhibitions that are really fantastic. They are currently renovating parts of the museum so I look forward to seeing what it looks like when they are complete. If you live locally in Philadelphia and enjoy at museums, I would highly recommend a membership as it also allows access to the Rodin Museum down the street and also access to other museums across the nation. Parking is available in the deck behind the museum and is underground. Very convenient.

This is a beautiful botanical garden in the midst of St. Louis. There are a number of gardens and features. The Climatron is not to be missed and houses the desert plants add well as the tropical plants. The water garden right outside of the Climatron is chock full of water lilies and right now there are Chihuly glass works in the water. There are various Chihuly pieces scattered throughout the gardens. I'm sure that the iris and daylilies are amazing in the spring. The Japanese garden is tranquil but certainly not totally organized like those in Japan. Free parking lot in site. Definitely a must see.

So Wailea Beach is really a very nice beach. BUT in order to get there if you're not staying at one of the resorts that line the beach, then getting to this beach is painful. So the resorts do not have public access lanes available to access the beach and in order to find the walkway to access requires Google stealth. (Yes, use Google directions to go the back way through the resorts to access the walkway.) Then you walk through the endless resorts to get to the beach. The equipment is for guests only and the showers, faucets to clean off with are very limited. So no parking.

This lookout has a beautiful view of the north shore or windward side of Oahu. You can see Kailua and Kaneohe in a sweeping vista. When we were three in November 2019, they were working on the ramp to the lookout parking lot so you have to turn around if you're coming from the north (driving south) and take the ramp off of the highway going north. You do have to OSU for parking which is what funds the lookout but it's a nominal fee and totally worth it. Keep valuables out of sight as we saw car window glass on the pavement while we'r were there.

What a phenomenal landmark in St. Louis! This cathedral is located in the Central West End near Washington University. The claim to fame for this building are the numerous mosaics that line the ceilings. It took the artisans 80 years to complete all of the mosaics. It's a magnificent cathedral and incredibly grand. There are also tours of the cathedral as well which meet in the back of the main hall. Parking can be had in the nearby parking lot which is not next to the cathedral. Definitely a must see if you are in St. Louis!

Impressive falls with a really nice view from Pont Renne. The trail is also cool since it gives the history of how multiple businesses used the power from Genessee River to their advantage including the forge. The Race where they harnessed the dead drop from the top of the falls was also interesting. Would definitely walk around to look at the different parts of the trail to get a sense of the history surrounding the falls. Parking deck on ther outside of this historic area or on street parking is available.

Very nice recreation of the first governor's mansion in North Carolina. It is very nicely done and as historically accurate as possible. It is unfortunate that the original mansion was demolished, but this is great and the guides are fantastic and know a lot about the historic context and provenance of the location. Ther gardens and side buildings are also beautiful and worth a walk through. They run a shuttle from the main building to the mansion which is also nice. Lots of parking so easy to visit.

This is a great arboretum that is free to the public. Early morning visits are very tranquil. They have an extensive saucer magnolia and conifer collection so visiting anytime of year is rewarding, but spring can be spectacular when the magnolia trees are blooming. The Japanese garden is also very nice once the Japanese maple trees have leafed out in the spring. There is also a learning and visitors center. The arboretum closes fairly early especially for summer so check the hours before you go.

Great ferry service that will take you to Shackleford Banks and also to Cape Lookout. The boats run on time and they are prompt and also make sure that everyone is safe. Service is supposed to be slower off season and they will customize pick ups a little.  They also have a fun tour that takes you to the Point at Cape Lookout that is a nice trip as well. Make sure to bring a lot of sunscreen though since you're really out in the open on the islands. Plenty of parking at the launch in Beaufort.

This is a great stop especially if you catch the waves at the right time so that they are large enough to produce a plume through the blowhole. It is a very popular stop so it may be difficult to get a direct view, but we enjoyed the stop. There is a pretty treacherous drop of though if you wander out past the railing and there were swimmers in the sea at the base of the neighboring point, but the waves could launch you into the rocks so be warned. Parking is pretty good if not crowded.

What a great beach on the windward side of East Oahu! This is a great beach with beautiful soft sugar sand and not very crowded when we went for a stop. There are also many picnic tables so you can sit and have a meal. There are fields between the picnic tables so you can play games also like frisbee, football, croquet although I wouldn't fly a kite since there are many beautiful local pine trees that flank the fields. Great family beach. Spacious parking lot as well. Hidden gem!

Very scenic and definitely with the short hike to the falls, but definitely a couple of detracting factors. First the parking lot was totally packed since it is the first stop off on the road to Hana so that can be tough and deter people from stopping. Three big sign out front was helpful to tell you which falls out was, but a bit tacky. Finally probably due to natural variation, unfortunately it was not Twin Falls that I got to see, but Single Falls. Still with a quick stop.
dislikes: Natural variation (Single Falls instead of Twin Falls)

reviews_attraction.text: Very interesting historical site that tells a lot of the local history and gives the visitor a flavor of what life was like around the time of the founding of Beaufort. There is a printed guide or you can download the app so you can locate and see who is buried and what role they played in this town. They also ask for a nominal $1 donation per person which I think is quite fair. Be warned though in the humid and warm months that there are a lot of bugs that will bite.

When visiting Center City, taking a rest and sitting in one of the many benches at Rittenhouse Square is always a good idea. Great for people watching, also have spotted a falcon or hawk before, Saturday mornings they have their farmers market and Sunsets bathroom dancing when the weather is nice. Very convenient to the area shops and restaurants and beautiful especially during the fall. They also have art shows about 3 times a year.

While the park is stunning and is 5+ stars, this particular NPS Visitor center (at entrance) was kind of sparse with not really a lot of information. The visitor center at the crater rim was better with more info and merchandise. Weirdly not much merchandise overall which is usually a major way for each NP to make money to cover expenses. Also the parking at the crater and the visitor center at the entrance are rather small.

This is the most amazing lookout along the coastline along the windward side (northern coast) of Oahu! The turn out is easy to navigate and there is a nice, but small parking lot. The views are simply amazing and none of the pictures are Photoshopped. The water is so blue and the distance you can see on a clear day is simply amazing! While the North Shore is appealing this past of East Oahu is breathtaking! A must go!

The Eno River State Park has multiple entrances and parking lots that allows access. The hiking trails are well marked and there are some very nice hikes from flat trails as well as hilly areas. Some trails follow the Eno River while other parts are on the hills overlooking the river. There are also some nice small falls and rock formations. Very close to Durham and Raleigh and well worth a visit.

A very large square with nice lawns and benches. There is also a building where there are restrooms. Flanking the plaza are buildings in all 4 sides where the are many interesting stores, boutique stores, and cafes/restaurants as well as few tasting rooms. There is also parking all along the plaza as well although this is still not likely enough especially during high season in winter country.

Love the Farmer's market and glad that they prohibit dogs in the market. The Hunt Street market is also fun with food trucks and some crafts booths. Wish there was a prohibition on dogs here as well since I would enjoy my food more if I didn't have to worry about being approached while eating and the occasional dog fight is also not fun. Great playground for kids also.

What a beautiful state park! Great fields where you could play games like tossing a frisbee, throwing a football/baseball, etc. Also the mountains in the background are absolutely gorgeous. The beach is pretty good, but there are definitely nicer beaches on Oahu. Plenty of parking so no worries there. Definitely a must stop on the way to the North Shore.

This point and lookout is beautiful and the water is gorgeous. There is a small parking lot at the end of the road and it wasn't very busy when we stopped to look. There is also a sign there that tells you the legend behind the name of the point: Laniloa. Definitely a 10 minute stop to take in the view and hear the waves crashing against the rocks.

Really terrific fountain with sculptural movement and different levels of water cascading off of the fountain. Again would have been 5 stars but was surprised when the sleeping homeless man on the lawn woke up startling me.

A very good playground for children and large fields for frisbee or other field sports and a small creek for children to explore in as well as restrooms. Otherwise small parking lot and not many other amenities.

The park is beautiful. I went to a picnic and enjoyed the amenities. The park is shaded and nicely maintained. The pavilion was large and furnished with a barbeque pit. The bathrooms are very clean. The park features numerous walking paths and a large playground for the children to play on. I highly recommend the place. Go and enjoy it.

The house is a remarkable structure with 2.5' wide walls. It was actually built by Daniel's son Nathan. The grounds have a number of imported homes to create a pretend town. It takes away some of the authenticity. The views are beautiful. Daniel Boone died here, but his remains were originally placed 13 miles away in Warren County.

The Saint Louis Zoo is recognized as one of the best in the world. The zoo's charter mandates it remain free for all to enter. Saint Louis city and county fund the institution. Come here and then visit another metropolitan zoo. You will agree the Saint Louis Zoo is the best. Hands down this place blows away any pay for zoo.

One of but a handful of remnants leftover from the 1904 World's Fair. It's a stunning structure and the bottom of Art Hill lies a fully restored lake with ornate ornamentals and complete walking trail surrounding it. The artwork is wonderful inside. And it's free except for the occasional traveling art shows.

This was a fun park. The vista's were beautiful overlooking the Mississippi River valley. The waters were high after the recent floods due to the spring rain. The park has a way cool lodge that can host events and weddings. We were there on a day trip, but it would be fun as a weekend getaway.

Within this establishment is an authentic replica of Lewis and Clark used. It's not unusual for it to be missing. The typically means a movie is being made and the boat is on loan. This at least what I have come to understand. I do know it's been lent to Disney for movies.

The riverfront is a nice walk by the water. It contains a veterans memorial of all the major wars of the United States. The town of Milton, Florida is small. It contains the county court house. It was a fun visit although it did not take too long.

St. Ambrose is a beautiful structure. The building is very ornate and features an altar of columns. The music was great to hear. The organ has a deep bass that can be felt in the music. The church is worth visiting if you enjoy architecture.

The facilities were impressive and very educational. There were numerous birds on display (stuffed) native to the area. The outdoor views were also cool. Bald Eagles are present mostly in the cold months. There are binoculars available.

There are over 30+ lakes here. It's fun to put a bell on the end of the rod and  doze off on a lazy afternoon. Hunting is open, but is based on a lotto system. There is a self-guided tour. You can pick it up at the visitor center.

The pier is a nice amenity and offers wonderful views of the coastline. There were a number of people fishing and catching fish. There were a large number of bull sharks present. It does cost a couple bucks,but it is worth it.

The best of St Louis is viewing it from within the Arch. The monument is staggering standing next to it. Impressive as it is, just north of the area is the nation's most violent region. Stay close to the downtown area.

I'm far from a civil war buff, but the spans of this park is overwhelming when reflecting on what took place. It's sobering to think of how war was fought and the bravery it took. The self-guided tour is outstanding.

I enjoyed the show overall. I'm not a country music fan, but it was fun to see a few celebrities. The structure was beautiful, but if you don't like heights it is not a good idea to go to the upper balcony.
dislikes: Not suitable for those afraid of heights

reviews_attraction.text: This is an unusual facility visually but stimulating simultaneously. I'm not really enthused about contemporary, modern, or the minimalist movement. The pool is cool. You'll enjoy and won't be disappointed.

Wonderful place to hang out with your lover, friends or yourself. The Katie Trail is cool if walking is your thing. The park gives great access to the river and can even challenge you to a bit of fishing.
Beautiful scapes, beach was slightly covered with ocean vegetation. I wanted to record the sunset, but the the sun went behind low clouds on the horizon. Too bad there's not a complaint department.
This is a remarkable structure. One can have a lunch sitting on top of a nuclear waste dump. Now that is a rare opportunity. The size is impressive. It's a modern version of the Cahokia Mounds.
The historical significance of Grant's house is less than a "must see." Grant married a Busch family member and basically lived at the farm for a short while and moved on never to look behind.
This is one of the true classics of St Louis, MO. Free to get in and two free beers. Unfortunately, descendants of the Busch legacy are selling it to cash in. I can give it only two stars.
I went here when I was 9 and thought it was so cool. It is well taken care of and true to the period. Kids will learn some stuff. It also served as a post for goods.
This is a sobering and educational experience. What started as a curiosity quickly changed to compassion for the suffering. This is a "must see."
Escape is a good time and a wonderful way to spend with friends. We did the dig. It was tough. We won the challenge. Only 30% win the challenge.
The place was closed when we arrived and we discovered it was $6.00 just to see two rivers converge. It is free on the Missouri side.
This structure is a St. Louis relic. It has exhibitions regularly relevant to the region. Touring exhibitions are hosted as well.

Having plenty of experience with plenty of forms of camping and having been to most of the state parks in Indiana, Chain O' Lakes State Park gave me the opportunity to visit another park I had never visited while also providing a very unique and fun new form of camping at the canoe campground. Going earlier in the season, we had the entire canoe campground (4 sites in total) to ourselves. It would have been a different experience otherwise as the site are pretty close to one another.  After paddling in from the boat ramp at Miller Lake, we setup camp before exploring the chain of lakes, which really was a unique paddle unlike anything I had done before. The next day, we hiked around 10 miles through trails that provided a little bit of everything in terms of lake views, deep ravines, pine forests, a one room school house, and more. The trails were also the best marked of any state park I've ever been to! Coming early in the season where many of the trees still had no leaves, I'd love to come back again later in the summer or even better in the fall when the leaves were changing.

I had heard friends talk about the park and the disc golf course, but had never been there until today and I was not disappointed. The park was very well maintained with all the grass nicely cut except for the intentional areas of the rough on the course. The course was the primary reason for me coming so I will address that first. As an intermediate player who came with a beginner, it was a perfect course. Most of the holes are pretty wide open, but also contained enough trees and areas of rough to add some challenge. Overall, it felt like the course had more variety than some others I have played at. There are some holes with water hazards (a pond), but those holes can be simply skipped by beginners, played conservatively by intermediate players, or more aggressively by those with advanced skills and experience. Overall, I definitely plan on coming back here to play more rounds in the future.

Besides the disc golf course, it is also a very nice park in and of itself with nice paved trails, open fields, and beautiful scenery.

On the way back home to the Indianapolis area from a state park even further north, I primarily stopped here to check out the mountain biking trails I had read about. I wasn't sure exactly what to expect, but didn't have the highest expectations compared to my normal riding locations of Town Run Trail Park or Brown County State Park. However, I was very pleasantly surprised with the Kintionki trail. It's not the longest at around only 4 miles, but it had plenty of features for intermediate and advanced riders alike, which some fun berms, steep down and ups, log ramps, and overall just great use the limited topography that they had to work with. While here, I also noticed they had a disc golf course, so I made sure to check that out as well since I had brought my disc set with me. It's only a 9 hole course with gravel tees and relatively short holes, but it was a fun additional activity to do if already there (I wouldn't make the drive if my only goal was looking for a disc golf course).

Did this suddenly become one of my favorite places to hike in Indiana? No, but it's a nice area that is less crowded than major state parks like Turkey Run or Brown County. We did the Blue Heron trail, which was relatively flat and offered some great picnic spots and views of the lake via some spur trails. The disc golf course was also a highlight. It started off easy, but quickly opened up into some very long and challenging holes - offering more than just the par 3s I've become accustomed to in courses around Indianapolis. On the negative sides, almost no one was wearing a mask, not even the gate attendant, which is something I hadn't experienced at any of the other state parks or recreation areas I've been to recently. And if you want to check out some really unique rock formations nearby, you should check out the Seven Pillars Nature Preserve which is less than 15 minutes away.

I was looking for a new place to go kayaking and decided to check out Raccoon Lake. I was originally planning on launching from Portland Mills Boat Ramp and going up the creek, but that ramp was closed. So instead, I launched from the main ramp (Raccoon Ramp) and went around and up the west side all the way to the US-36 bridge (it gets too shallow quickly after that). Going on a day that was windy, the water was pretty choppy and going back into the wind was a challenge in the more open sections of the lake. There also is some boat traffic that you have to keep an eye out for, as well as the wake they generate. Overall, it seemed like a nice park and kayaking was fun and improved once reaching the no idle zones, but I wouldn't describe it as the most scenic or best place for kayakers. For that, I'd recommend checking out Yellowwood State Forest.

An amazing place that is truly a unique hidden gem in Indiana. Echoing the comment of another reviewer, Portland Arch Nature Preserve offers the beauty and uniqueness of Turkey Run (one of my favorite state parks) without the crowds (there wasn't a single car in the parking lot when we arrived on a Saturday around 11:30am)! The trail itself isn't very long at coming in at just over a mile, but there are plenty of places to explore and downloading the trail guide ahead of time was very informative in learning about different features as the trail had numbered sign posts along the way (although some were in need of repair to make the number more legible). For those wondering about whether this trail is closed based on other reviews, it has now reopened after repair work was done on the boardwalks.

Great place for kids (and adults as well). I had fond memories of this place growing up, but had not been there in over 10 years, so I did not know what to expect. The CineDome was converted to the Dinosphere, which was an improvement. The water clock, carousel, race car, and many of the other things I remember we're still there. New exhibits such as DC comics and Hot Wheels show a desire to be current with the times. The new Sports Legends experience looked really fun, but unfortunately was rained out when we were there. My main disappointment came with the apparently recently rennovated Science Works, which had been my favorite. Gone was the rock climbing, tunnels, and water exhibits that I always looked forward to.

More than just beaches and sand... Having been to many state parks across Indiana (with my favorites including Turkey Run and Shades), I had never been to the Dunes as I thought it was primarily just a beach with sand. However, I found that was clearly wrong and the Dunes has much to offer with trails through a wide variety of ecosystems from deep woods to marshes along with the dunes, which offer very scenic overlooks of Lake Michigan. We even saw a bald eagle on one of our hikes, which was cool. One of the trails did lead us through the crowded state park campground. If you don't mind more primitive, I definitely preferred the more secluded and spacious sites we we're staying at in the nearby Dunewood campground.

Nice state park close to the city, which is it's main advantage. It's not near the top of my list for best state parks in Indiana, but does offer a lot of different options, making it sort of a jack of all trades, but master of none. There are mountain biking trails, but foot traffic often lead me to ride elsewhere. There's hiking trails, but nothing scenic compared to Turkey Run. There's paved trails for biking, but nothing terribly long. There are also open fields great for a pickup game of Ultimate Frisbee or something else. Overall, it's a great place where everyone can find something to enjoy, but just not a top destination when breaking it down into specific categories like mountain biking or hiking.

Amazing place with such unique and diverse flowers, plants, and trees. And at only $2 per person, it's an incredible value. While it may not be the largest conservatory, we ended up spending a good hour walking through and taking in all the sights. I also felt very safe during this covid era as it was nice to see everyone wearing masks inside (which is required), one way traffic, and a cap on the maximum number of participants for a given time slot. I would highly recommend everyone checking out this place and I want to go back myself during different seasons to see what other plants might be in bloom at that time. And next time, take my macro lens for even better photography.

It's hard to believe this is a city park as it feels much more like a state park, boasting of many miles of trails and a reservoir great for kayaking or just watching a sunset. Unlike other city parks, there is an admission fee (and additional fees if you bring your own boat), and a state park pass won't get you in (it'd be great if a combo pass could be created). If you want more rugged trails, drive west across 56th to the Great Bear statue, which are some of my favorite trails and views of the park.

Truly one of the best parts of Zionsville. It offers miles of dirt trails for running that can't be found in many other places around. Wildlife is abundant as I frequently see deer throughout the park on many runs. And the park staff does an excellent job at maintaining the trails, reflected in both can absence of any trash or litter as well as downed trees blocking the trail being cleaned up very quickly. They have even mowed wider side paths and short detours to make social distancing even easier.

Great park for a lovely stroll through very well kept grounds. The Sunken Gardens are a perfect place for enjoying the weather, beautiful landscaping, or even bringing a picnic lunch. Outside of the gardens, there are nice walking parks that go throughout the park. And while you are there, make sure to check out the conservatory as well ($2/person, currently requires getting tickets in advance). It offers amazing diversity of flowers, plants, and trees and is well worth the price of admission.

Great place to park to go hiking east towards boardwalks and overlooks of the reservoir or to head south towards Eagles Crest, where there are many trails to choose from once there. The trails are more primitive so don't expect anything like toilets, but a positive is you can often go for miles without seeing anyone else. The only negative of this parking area is the slope getting off the road into the lot is somewhat steep, so make sure to take it slow and at an angle.

One of the best state parks in Indiana. The trails offer amazing beauty that makes you question if you are still in Indiana, going through gorges and past waterfalls. The trails also present a fun adventure with ladders on certain parks and jumping across rocks when going through sections of the water filled gorge. Sugar Creek also offers a great place for a refreshing dip in the summer time. Check out this park and I can guarantee you won't be disappointed.

A fun place to check out Christmas lights that is not too far of a drive from Indianapolis. It is probably the most Christmas lights I've ever seen in such a small amount of space. And with tons of different types of decorations, it's great for the whole family. My only complaint is that I wish some of the pathways were marked as one way, specifically in the age of covid. Also, despite signs saying masks were required, compliance was definitely a mixed bag.

A very nice place for a stroll through nature, passing along the way various unique sculptures.  The lap around the lake is nice with side paths down to both the lake and the river. There are many picnic tables scattered throughout to find a nice secluded spot for a picnic lunch or dinner. The reason for the loss of a star is that there was one area where someone had definitely been smoking something illegal.

I wouldn't make the drive from Indianapolis just to see this park, but if you are already coming up to check out the lights at We Care Park, it's worth an additional stop. When checking out all the different lights, there is a side walking path, but it seemed like it would be a very long walk and would recommend driving through here and spending time walking around at We Care Park.

A beautiful park that is one of the fewest places in Indiana with rentals for cross country skiing. The trails are great for beginners and there is a nice mix of different types of forests and some scenic overlooks of the river. The rentals were setup in a way that was simple and also felt safe with covid precautions being followed.

Great park in the middle of the city that has something for everyone. There are paved paths, dirt hiking paths that go down to the river, playgrounds for kids, large open fields, unique ruins, and so much more. If you have never been here before, I highly recommend checking it out.

If you want great views without any hiking, this is a great option! While I would probably choose Glacier Point if forced to choose between the two, Washburn Point can definitely hold it's own with great views of Half Dome, Vernal Falls, Nevada Falls, and even Illilouette Falls.

Beautiful state park with many opportunities for hiking and exploring. Wolf cave is a definite highlight, but be aware the exit is a little tight and maybe require crouching or crawling to get out. Walking the creek is also a lot of fun with a nice waterfall at the end.

An easy to miss entrance leads to a mountain biking trail that is close to the city and offers a fun ride with jumps and technical obstacles. It does take a while to dry out after a heavy rain, so make sure to check out if the trail is open first.
Mountain biking trails, rock climbing opportunities, scenic trails along the river, and a nice campground with spacious sites makes this a great place to visit.
Beautiful place, but more parking is needed and at peak times, you may have to wait a long time to find a parking space.

They were overwhelmed for the amount of people that wanted to appreciate the Kusama exhibitions, but they handle it so well that I gave them a high five! All the employees are extremely nice and kind, and they help you to enjoy the very cultural and amazing art experiences that you will have here. Therefore it is organized so great that you wont have any regret visiting it.

Amazing scape point in UES. The park was very beautiful flowers and the view for the river in astonishing. In summer they have jazz concerts and you can dance in the concrete. Also, you may bring your special one, and I am talking about your pet, to enjoy the relaxing posh glamorous pet friendly zones. i am very grateful to have this park so close to my house  #givebackNYC

The Picasso and Dali are the best! but do not forget the Diego Rribera+ Frida Kalo, and some Rothko and Pollock. it has a very cool photography expo (as always), the Magrite "wait for ever in line" exhibition on the top floor is a must! free on fridays after 4 until 8 pm. Tip: go to the top floor and then go downstairs floor by floor.

amazing acoustics for concerts, and even if it is a huge place it feel cozy and home-related with the performers. the quality of the musicians is always exceptional and the international variety makes this place great for all the kinds of music. last time I saw an Argentinian opera singer who was outstanding

i love or hate this place depending of the exhibition, so far the Koons one is great and worthy to see it. They have some very weird art sometimes, but go to the top floor first so see the Calder, Hopper and other american modern artists famous nice art and then walk your way down to the surprise expos.

When the midsummer swing is happening this is best place to dance the nice off in summer! from swing to salsa you learn all the rhythms and have a blast with friend or a romantic date. Plus the wine, food and the arte of the gelato are ready to sell all their amazing food.

this place has a great open minded direction, so it always depends on the expo that they have if i have a blast or i just feel i waste my time. The here and there exhibition has some nice photography and movies worthy to see. go tot the 7th floor for the sky room view

The best time to visit is in summer with the amazing warm ups parties! you can dance all day long and visit the really modern art exhibitions. The other good time is monday when is pay as you wish! the basement is worthy to visit to see the original equipment.

This place is very small. It is cozy and charming, but it looks very old and derelict. The expo about donas is interesting but there is nothing too crazy about it. I guess it is a good spot to take a look in you are in williamsburg and it is only 5 bucks.

great museum to visit with kids, a lot of fun stuff to play with or just touch, like the space capsule. Plus everything is very well organized and easy to follow. They have free movie screening fridays night.

One the best parks in summer time to watch the other side of the Hudson. They have a nice garden and a cool bar. It is nice to visit the castle and see a theater play outdoors, or just grab some of the tours.

beautiful historical island, great for the art events and the jazz party with live music and 20s outfits. Also the ferry is free and easy going if you have your bike. The only problem in the ferry schedule
This historical theatre is still a great place to watch from a New Orleans band to Pharell Williams. They also have the amateur night on wednesdays which is very fun and worthy the trip to Harlem

This a very solid children's museum if not a great one.  There are a lot of activities and areas and each one is done well.  We spend most of the day there and my kids were entertained throughout.  The only downside is the parking is a bit of a challenge, since there is no direct parking area.  There was also not a really good place to have lunch at the museum- it was raining the day we were there so outside was not an option.  Overall, highly recommend.

The museum as a lot of items.  It is has a great depth and breath to the collection also.  I really enjoyed the President's Cars and the Rosa Parks Bus.  They have a great selection of places to eat also.  However, it is NOT EASY TO FIND.  You would think there would be signage for the place- there really isn't.  I got lost driving down some neighborhood roads and such trying to find the place.  Henry Ford evidently didn't believe in road signs.

Great hike for the Petroglyph Monument.  This is my favorite of the hiking trials in of the group.  The trial sets up like a journey back to an area with many Petrogylphs.  Definitely an easy hike, some up and down rolling hills like areas ,but mostly flat.  You can go at your own pace.  The trail is well used and many people are out.  Dogs on leash are allowed. reviews_attraction.text: This is not the San Diego or LA Zoo, however it is very good.  The animals are fine and the zoo is well kept.  It is not on par with other "major" city zoos, but it probably does not have the resources to do so.  Overall it is a great family time and the kids love it.  It suits ABQ's needs perfectly! The Penguin Chill is a good addition. The new COVID-19 set up is about the best you could ask for in the facility.
dislikes: Not on par with major zoos

reviews_attraction.text: It was a great facility.  Definitely for tourists.  The facility gives you a behind the scenes look at the making and maintaining of Mardi Gras floats.  Our tour guide was solid.  We got into a tour with a larger older tour group, so it was not as "intimate" as I would have like the tour, but such is life.  Overall it is fascinating to see how the whole thing is put together and what is actually accomplished.

This is a great place. They have so many programs/tours and things going on for a smaller park.  They have a lot of programs and volunteers and do a great job with everything.  The site is very easy to access and walk around.  Highly recommend the Battlefield Tour, since it is really the only way to access the battlefield due to preservation issues.  A gem of a place outside of Santa Fe.

Truly amazing.  There are hundreds of foot prints here.  The set up is as best as it can be.  We were camping at the park and ended up going three times to the tracks- each time we saw something new and appreciated something new.  Definitely was better in the morning than the afternoon- just with the light the tracks stood out more.   Definitely if you are in the area worth the trip!
likes: On-site Activities: Multiple visits, new discoveries

reviews_attraction.text: First thing, this is not officially part of the NPS, so you have to buy your own admission and such for it outside of the other historical items in the area.  It is neat.  Definitely trying their best to keep it going.  They have a lot of good information and there is a lot of history in the house.  Not a must see, but a worthy look.

There is not one thing that stands out here- not in a bad way.  It is just beautiful.  It is a great area to enjoy nature and the beauty of Northern New Mexico.  I was blown away with just the stunning beauty of nature here.  I am glad to see it is now federal land and protected.  Highly recommend going to spend some time there and

Very good tour.  Enjoyed it a lot.  You have to buy your tickets at the Henry Ford Museum and take the bus over.  The second film was very loud which actually distracted from the information given.  I would highly recommend it though if you are in the area.  It was a great way to see how things are made and done with Ford!

Sky City/Old Acoma a special place and unique to New Mexico.  It has a proud and strong history.  The tours are solid and the experience is a must. The Acoma people are amicable and have a great deal of pride in sharing their home.  A lot of history and culture to soak up at this place.  The drive there is scenic.

The Museum is very well done and put together.  It has a lot of items.   Definitely make sure you go over the annex area to check out some of the cars and trophies there.  Overall very good.  The museum has a "no touch" policy so much make sure to watch little kids if you bring them.  Overall good experience.

Great little museum and walking area.  Really gives you a feel for the time and place of the Manhattan Project and what was going on.  Overall the place was worthy of a stop and the time I spent there.  Would recommended.  However, I think it is a place you will get out of the museum what you put into it.

Very Unique New Mexican Tourist attraction!  The Ice Cave is impressive and a good place to cool off during the summer.  The hike to the cave is very short and easy.  The caldera hike is a bit longer, but nothing crazy.  Enjoyed our time and experience.

For a town the size of ABQ, this museum is amazing.  It maximizes its resources and really does a great job.  It is free to NM residences the first Sunday of the month.  They have a dinosaurs and other materials specific to New Mexico.  It is a great.

Great for families and young kids.   A lot of young kids- a lot of families.  There is the general chaos that ensues with that crowd.  However, very family friendly.  Can get hot and steamy, bring some water to wait in line for the tram.

Great Kids Museum in Philly!  A lot of different items and exhibits.  Very well done.  Definitely appreciated the selection and diversity of exhibits.  Overall I hope it continues to be there and remains successful.

Beautiful park in the heart of the tourist area of NOLA.  It is maintained well.  Definitely a spot you can stop sit and just relax for a minute amid the hustle and bustle.  Well maintained plants and tress too.

The Albuquerque Children's Museum essentially.   It has a great mix of science, arts and fun.  It is a great museum.  A lot of things to do and play and all with a learning basis.  Definitely recommend it.
Great Ballpark.  Did not get to explore it as much as I thought I would.  Definitely has a lot of things I did not get to check out.  Hope to go back sometime.  Good layout, great fan experience.
This was a great way to spend the afternoon.  I was impressed with the place.  Basia was my tour guide and she really made the whole experience.   Great way to spend a few hours.
Solid place to walk around and appreciate the plants and such.  Good place for kids and a picnic.  Went during the early spring so not a lot of stuff really blooming.
How can you really say anything bad about a National Monument.  White Sands is unique.  Very special place, highly recommend the sunset stroll!
Good little nature trail. Could see in the summer it could very hot and uncomfortable- no shade.  However, well done and good little walk.
Cathedral of the Archdiocese of San Antonio.  Very historical.  They appear to have a nice cafe and bookstore next to the Cathedral.

(Translated by Google) On November 22, 1963, the sixth floor of the Texas School Book Depository became world famous because Lee Harvey Oswald fired the fatal shot at President John F. Kennedy from a window on that floor. An event that had a huge impact on many people. Although still young, I have consciously experienced this. I thought it was very special to be where it all happened. Quite an experience. A must for people in Dallas who love history.

The Sixth Floor Museum at Dealey Plaza is located on the sixth floor of that building, which is now the Dallas County Administration Building. In the museum, various aspects of that day are highlighted with film material, photos and eyewitness accounts. The museum also contains many documents detailing the aftermath of the tragedy, the findings of the Warren commission's investigation, which has been questioned to date, and its implications. It is very interesting to read that the picture now is that services such as the FBI and CIA were not involved in the murder, but did make mistakes in the protection (for example Lee Harvey Oswald was known as someone with communist sympathies). Covering up these mistakes has probably helped create so many conspiracy theories.
The reason why Jack Ruby probably shot Oswald a day later is also sobering. Ruby thought he was doing well and expected to be honored as a hero. A spontaneous action. No conspiracy.

(Original)
Op 22 november 1963 werd de zesde verdieping van de Texas School Book Depository wereldberoemd omdat vanuit een raam op die verdieping Lee Harvey Oswald het fatale schot loste op president John F. Kennedy. Een gebeurtenis die en geweldige impact had op hee vel mensen. Hoewel nog jong heb ik dit toch bewust meegemaakt. Ik vond het dan ook heel bijzonder om op de plaats te staan waar het allemaal is gebeurd. Een hele belevenis. Een must voor mensen die in Dallas zijn en van geschiedenis houden.

Het Sixth Floor Museum at Dealey Plaza bevindt zich op de zesde verdieping van dat gebouw, dat nu het Dallas County Administration Building is. In het museum worden verschillende aspecten van die dag belicht met filmmateriaal, foto's en ooggetuigenverslagen. Het museum bevat ook veel documenten over de nasleep van de tragedie, de bevindingen van het onderzoek door de Warren-commissie, waarover tot op heden twijfel bestaat, en de gevolgen daarvan. Heel interessant om te lezen dat het beeld nu is dat diensten als FBI en CIA niet betrokken waren bij de moord maar wel fouten hebben gemaakt bij de bescherming (men kende bijvoorbeeld Lee Harvey Oswald als iemand met communistische sympathieën). Het in de doofpot stoppen van deze fouten heeft er waarschijnlijk mede voor gezorgd dat er zoveel samenzweringstheorieën zijn ontstaan.
Ook de reden waarom Jack Ruby een dag later waarschijnlijk Oswald heeft doodgeschoten is ontnuchterend. Ruby dacht dat hij goed deed en verwachtte te worden geëerd als een held. Een spontane actie. Geen samenzwering.

(Translated by Google) The Cathedral Basilica of Saint Francis of Assisi is a Roman Catholic cathedral located in the center of Santa Fe, New Mexico. It is the mother church of the Archdiocese of Santa Fe.
The cathedral was built by Archbishop Jean Baptiste Lamy between 1869 and 1886 on the site of another church. A small chapel on the north side of the cathedral is still a remnant of the old church.
In contrast to the surrounding adobe structures, the cathedral was designed in the Romanesque style. The cathedral has characteristic round arches separated by Corinthian columns and truncated square towers. The large rose window in the front and that of the twelve apostles in the aisle windows were imported from France. The towers were originally to be crowned with 49-meter-high towers, but due to lack of funds, they were never built. The left tower is a single row of bricks larger than the right tower. The cathedral is built of yellow limestone blocks carved near the current site of Lamy. An addition to the cathedral's facade in 2005 is a small, round window with a dove, the symbol of the Holy Spirit. It is a stained glass replica of the translucent alabaster window in St. Peter's Basilica in Vatican City.
The Cathedral of St. Francis of Assisi was officially elevated to Basilica by Pope Benedict XVI on October 4, 2005, making it a cathedral basilica.

(Original)
De kathedraalbasiliek van Sint Franciscus van Assisi  is een rooms-katholieke kathedraal in het centrum van Santa Fe, New Mexico . Het is de moederkerk van het aartsbisdom Santa Fe .
De kathedraal werd gebouwd door aartsbisschop Jean Baptiste Lamy tussen 1869 en 1886 op de plek van een andere kerk. Een kleine kapel aan de noordkant van de kathedraal is nog een overblijfsel van de oude kerk.
In groot contrast met de omringende adobestructuren, werd de kathedraal ontworpen in de Romaanse stijl . De kathedraal heeft karakteristieke ronde bogen gescheiden door Corinthische zuilen en afgekapte vierkante torens. Het grote roosvenster aan de voorkant en die van de twaalf apostelen in de zijbeukramen werden geïmporteerd uit Frankrijk. De torens zouden oorspronkelijk worden bekroond met 49 meter hoge torens , maar door gebrek aan geld fondsen werden deze nooit gebouwd. De linkertoren is een enkele rij stenen die groter is dan de rechtertoren. De kathedraal is gebouwd van gele kalksteenblokken die in de buurt van de huidige plaats Lamy zijn uitgehouwen . Een toevoeging in 2005 aan de bovengevel van de kathedraal is een klein, rond venster met een duif , het symbool van de Heilige Geest . Het is een glas-in-lood replica van het doorschijnende albasten raam in de Sint-Pietersbasiliek in Vaticaanstad .
De kathedraal van Sint-Franciscus van Assisi werd op 4 oktober 2005 door paus Benedictus XVI officieel tot basiliek verheven,.Het is n u dus een kathedraalbasiliek.

(Translated by Google) This is a very nice museum. It is actually 5 museums in 1:
. Buffalo Bill Museum
. Plains Indians Museum
. Whitney Western Art Museum
. Draper Natural History Museum
. Cody Firearms Museum

They are all visiting where. One is of course more interesting than the other. But the collections have all been carefully put together.

The Buffalo Bill Museum stands out. As a European, I know Buffalo Bill, of course, but I didn't know what kind of celebrity the man was in the US and what impact he had on the experience of Wild West history. A close second for me is the Plains Indians Museum and then the Draper Natural History Museum. All very interesting and very beautiful exhibitions.

The least part I liked was the Cody Firearms Museum. I have nothing to do with weapons only exhibitions. They can close that for me. But that will not happen with great certainty. In fact it is being expanded.

But we spent a great many hours there.

Dit is een heel mooi museum. Het zijn eigenlijk 5 musea in 1:
.	Buffalo Bill Museum
.	Plains Indians Museum
.	Whitney Western Art Museum
.	Draper Natural History Museum
.	Cody Firearms Museum

Allen zijn ze een bezoek waar. De een is natuurlijk interessanter dan de andere. Maar allen zijn de collecties zorgvuldig samengesteld.

Het Buffalo Bill Museum steekt er bovenuit. Als Europeaan ken ik natuurlijk Buffalo Bill, maar ik wist niet wat voor beroemdheid de man in de US was en wat voor impact hij heeft gehad op de beleving van de geschiedenis van het Wilde Westen. Goede tweede voor mij is het Plains Indians Museum en daarna het Draper Natural History Museum. Heel interessant allemaal en hele mooie tentoonstellingen.

Het minste deel vond ik het Cody Firearms Museum. Ik heb niks met tentoonstellingen van alleen maar wapens. Dat kunnen ze voor mij sluiten. Maar dat zal met grote zekerheid niet gebeuren. Sterker nog het wordt uitgebreid.

Maar wij brachten er een groot aantal uren door.

(Translated by Google) Norris Geyser Basin is the hottest and most active thermal area in Yellowstone. Strolling through this place is beautiful. As you walk along the landscaped wooden footpath you will see spouting geysers, small hot springs and you can view the organisms in the water.

The walk starts at the museum. At Porcelain Basin see a lot of volcanic activity. The steam then rushes to the surface. The Back Basin is also worth a visit because it is where the Steamboat Geyser is located.

Steamboat Geyser has an irregular timetable with long breaks between major eruptions (longest was 50 years). During large eruptions, the geyser bursts more than 90 meters into the air. Between the major eruptions, there are small eruptions of about 12 meters. Unfortunately, however, we have not seen an eruption.

(Original)
Norris Geyser Basin is het heetste en meest actieve thermale gebied in Yellowstone. Een wandeling door deze plek is mooi. Terwijl je over het aangelegde houten voetpad loopt zie je spuitende geisers, kleine hot springs en je kunt de organismen in het water bekijken.

De wandeling begint bij het museum. Bij Porcelain Basin zie veel vulkanische activiteit De stoom raast dan naar de oppervlakte.  Ook de Back Basin is een bezoek waard want daar bevindt zich de Steamboat Geyser.

Steamboat Geyser heeft een onregelmatig tijdschema met lange pauzes tussen grote uitbarstingen (langste was 50 jaar). Tijdens grote uitbarstingen barst de geyser wel meer dan 90 meter de lucht in. Tussen de grote uitbarstingen, zijn er kleine uitbarstingen van ongeveer 12 meter. Wij hebben echter jammer genoeg geen uitbarsting gezien.

(Translated by Google) Sometimes you come across things that feed you 'How can it exist'. In our opinion, this is also the case with the American Founding Fathers Exhibit.

Driving on the highway you suddenly come across a replica of the hall where the agreement in principle of the American Declaration of Independence was taken (the actual signing took months after that because of the distances).

Inside, based on the famous painting by John Trumbull, all the players are arranged in the form of life-size dolls.

Almost a must for American history buffs, especially since it also provides a lot of detailed information about all the signers of the statement. For example, did you know that some of the people in the painting were not present at all at the meeting?

Rijdend op de snelweg kom je ineens een replica tegen van de hal waar het principeakkoord van de Amerikaanse Onafhakelijkheidsverklaring werd genomen (de daadwerkelijke ondertekening duurde daarna vanwege de afstanden nog maanden).

Binnen staat op basis van het beroemde schilderij van John Trumbull alle spelers in de vorm van levensgrootte poppen opgesteld.

Bijna een must voor Amerikaanse geschiedenisliefhebbers, vooral omdat het ook nog veel gedetailleerde informatie geeft over alle ondertekenaars van de verklaring. Wist u bijvoorbeeld dat een aantal mensen op het schilderij helemaal niet aanwezig waren bij de vergadering?

This is a surprisingly interesting and detailed museum. It has a wealth of information about the industry, the people it employed, the whales and the products made from them. Importantly, it does a good job justifying itself: it acknowledges that whaling was a cruel and unsustainable practice, but nevertheless critically important to the history and culture of New Bedford—and therefore worth remembering.

It’s a great zoo for its size; the environments for the animals are really well put together, and they have nice plaques explaining where the animals came from and how they are involved in conservation efforts. If you’re willing to spend $18 to go to the zoo, though, it’s really worth it to go to the main location in the Bronx—which is massive and (I think) not much more expensive.
dislikes: Admission cost relative to main location

reviews_attraction.text: This is a great big park, certainly underutilized because of its location. It’s on the site of the 1964 World’s Fair, and it’s kind of funny to walk around and every so often pass by some hulking futuristic eyesore that nobody would ever build today. Some of them, particularly the big globe by the Queens Museum of Art, are pretty attractive, and there’s lots of picnic space too.

There are a few fun things in here, including scale models of lots of famous skyscrapers on the second floor. The highlight, though, is definitely the building-by-building model of the city in the back of the ground floor. The detail is excellent, and there are interactive screens that allow people to choose data overlays that are projected down onto it. I had a lot of fun.

I saw a concert here; the seats are well arranged and the production capacity is great. They were able to do some pretty amazing light work to support the music, and I was kind of surprised I could make out a lot of the words in a hip hop show, despite the huge space and the echoing. The concessions aren’t anything special, but I guess we don’t expect them to be, right?

While the main museum is under construction there’s not much to do here, but it wouldn’t be fair to penalize that too much in the review. (It claims to be opening soon.) There are some outdoor exhibits, mostly old farm equipment, that are kinda fun to look at, and the setting is beautiful, but I think the whole place will have a lot more life to it once it reopens.

A very distinctive museum, partly for the quality of the art but mostly for the uniqueness of Isabella Stewart Gardner’s vision to not just build the collection, but design a home for it as well. It’s like a real-life memory palace. At times her taste is odd and doesn’t match mine, but nevertheless it’s unlike any other museum I’ve been to.

The exhibits are similar in quality to the excellent New England and Monterey Bay aquariums, but there isn’t as much to see—particularly during off-season renovation. We felt like we had seen pretty much everything in a half-hour, though the tickets were not that expensive so I don’t feel bad.

Not my favorite part of the Botanical Garden—probably least favorite, actually. The roses are really pretty, but it’s always so hot! Bring an umbrella or something if you’re planning to stay more than a few minutes: there’s no shade and the heat can be pretty oppressive during bloom season.

This is a pretty park, I think a recent development of what used to be a dock or loading zone or something. It doesn’t have a ton of character (yet), being a recent development surrounded by high rises and office buildings, but it’s still peaceful, with a nice walkway along the riverside.

Radnor Lake isn’t all that big—it’s a manmade lake that you could probably walk all the way around in an hour, with a couple of side trails in addition. It’s very pretty, though, and the main paths are paved, which makes it one of the best bike paths/dog-walking routes I’ve ever seen.

This is a good park with some fun, not-too-long trails. The views of the Puget Sound and Mt. Rainier from the beach around the West Point Light House are really lovely—especially at sunset, where the sun sets behind the Olympic mountains in the distance.

This tour was really great. The Boeing factory is just so impressive, and the tour guides so full of interesting stories… it was hyped up a lot for me, but nevertheless I was amazed. If you’re going to Seattle, you really shouldn’t miss it.

I wouldn’t call this a tourist attraction, so much as a kinda nice place to jog or walk your dog. The waterfront views are pretty in the right weather, and there’s a nice amphitheatre; the sculptures didn’t really grab me, though.

Apparently Bryant Park used to be sketchy? It definitely isn’t now… small, but really pretty. The big lawn in the middle gets put to good use for concerts, movie screenings, yoga sessions—and an ice-skating rink in the winter.

They have some pretty cool stuff here, especially samples of pre-Civil War currency and military money through the years. There are also photo ops with a million dollars in each of three denominations. Fun place, and free!
You know, it’s a nice park. The view of the Space Needle and the monorail reminds you of what people thought the future would be like in the ’60s, and also the consequences of hosting a World’s Fair.
It’s a beach… pretty much indistinguishable from the others along the ocean side of the National Seashore to me, except it doesn’t have a fun beach bar to go with it like Cahoon Hollow does.
The original escape room chain, as far as I know. Note that puzzle designs are repeated between locations, so e.g. the Office room is the same between the New York and Boston branches.
Pretty cool place, with glassblowing demonstrations and some very cool artifacts and historical exhibits. I don’t know if it’s a thing to do every year, but fun once at least.
Excellent collections, and the architecture of the building is a big part of the attraction. It reminds me of the Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum in Boston in some ways.
Probably the best aquarium I’ve been to, though the New England Aquarium comes close. This one is bigger, and also maintains really high quality throughout.
It’s funny to give this a rating, but it is actually a great park: big playground with basketball courts and a baseball field, all well maintained.
It’s pretty odd to build a full-sized replica of the Parthenon in a major urban park, but Nashville pulls it off.
You have to stay for a while to make it worth the admission fee, but it really is a great place.

Free, picturesque, garden collections, historic, open space, *GASP* plenty of parking (in DC?!). The National Arboretum is a treasure trove of everything you could possibly want in an arboretum/botanical research center. It covers over 400 acres and has 9 miles of roadways winding through and connecting the various gardens. It's both walkable and drivable for your convenience. There are multiple parking lots within walking distance to each garden collection, making it easy to visit them all. However, you can also walk (or bike) all the exhibits if you want to get some exercise in.

Here are the various collections/exhibits:
+Asian Collections
+Azalea Collections
+Dogwood Collections
+Fern Valley
+Friendship Garden
+Gotelli Dwarf and Slow Growing Conifer Collection
+Holly and Magnolia Collections
+National Bonsai & Penjing Museum
+National Boxwood Collection
+National Capitol Columns
+National Grove of State Trees
+National Herb Garden
+Perennial Collections

I just want to highlight a few of these collections, mainly the Azalea Collections, Herb Garden, National Capitol Columns, and the National Bonsai & Penjing Museum.

For the Azalea Collections, the time frame is generally between mid-April to June. You can check the Azalea Blossom Watch on their website for the current projected peak bloom dates and current conditions before you come. During the spring/early summer months, these azaleas bring an array of color.

I love the Herb Garden. It is the largest designed herb garden in the nation and includes annual, perennial, and woody herbal plants.Just past the entrance of the Herb Garden is a circular plaza with a small pool and fountain. Between the grapevine-covered arbors is the Knot Garden which features evergreen plants in a contemporary geometric design. To the distance, you can see the National Capitol Columns. There are ten themed gardens such as the Dye Garden, Culinary Garden, Asian Garden, Fragrance Garden, etc. The Herb Garden features over 100 varieties of roses, more than 50 varieties of peppers including the habanero and ghost peppers, and huge collections of lavender, rosemary, basil, scented geraniums, and much more. It's a beautiful motley of color and mix of fragrant aromas.

You can cross the meadow from the Herb Garden to walk up to the iconic National Capitol Columns. The columns were actually first part of the East Portico of the Capitol in 1828. However, the dome of the Capitol couldn't support these columns, so they were moved here in the 1980s. There's a reflecting pool in front of these columns (although it was dry in August 2015). These columns are easily the most photographed part of the National Arboretum.

The National Bonsai & Penjing Museum has one of the largest collections of in North America. It all started when the Nippon Bonsai Association donated more than 50 bonsai and it has steadily grown since then. Currently, the National Bonsai & Penjing Museum houses 150 plants. Very calming and zen here.

In the past, the Administration Building housed a beautiful aquatic pond with lilies, lily pads, other aquatic plants, koi, and frogs. You can even purchase some food to feed the koi. The pond is currently under construction.

Anywhere else, an arboretum like this would cost an admission fee. But because it's in DC, it's free.
