Beautiful scenery early in the morning, you can see the signature reflection of the Rocky mountain as you walk around the lake; easy walk around Bear lake for the entire family.
This is one of the greatest museums in Queens for fans of classic films and television. Costumes, toys, props, storyboards, film screenings, interactive exhibits, and more!
Beautiful park with a good assortment of trails including an easy one around the incredibly picturesque lake. Ample parking, picnic tables and grassy areas to relax on.
A must see for everyone! The observatory tower was spectacular with the views of the city, the museum very well laid out and the entire park is clean and picturesque.
Carousel amusement closed during covid19. Can wait until they open again, one of the oldest rides. There it's also one in Central Park.
There's so much to see. Its very serene and peaceful. Its a good place to escape from the hustle and bustle of the city!
The church is being renovated at present. However, it is a beautiful building. It is situated by the financial district.
Spectacular views of The park on your drive to see the Clift Dwellings. We really enjoyed our visit and the drive.
Huge park. So many things to do here from a walk along the lake, to the museum, theater, barbecuing, picnics etc
A nice spot to enjoy some greenery while in the city. Next door to the NYC public library which is fabulous!

We stopped here on a layover on our way to London. This is a guaranteed must see that I can't recommend enough. Make sure you line up to do the tram tour as soon as you get there, preferably when they open. You'll see the Astronaut training center, Mars Vehicles, ISS Control and Rocket Park. The exhibits in the actual Space Center are probably better for kids, but most adults will still take an interest. That 747 outside you can actually go inside and learn the history of ferrying the space shuttle across the country.

We didn't get to go down in to the caverns due to arriving too late. But this place is still pretty cool. We bought some mineral bags and panned for shells as well as minerals. They have a large zip line course that was pretty amazing. To enter is free and its a fun place to just to hang out and explore the shops. The food was pretty good as well. I am sure the caverns were good as well, we just didn't get to see them.

Excellent animal sanctuary. Yes its pricey, but its private and worth it. You walk on a cat walk about 30 feet or so in the air with animals all around you and beneath you. It can get warm and windy. It takes roughly 2-3 hours to see it all, bring sunscreen and water. It is a 3 mile walk, so bring comfy shoes. We saw several animals and got some excellent pictures. I highly recommend it.

The History Colorado Center is a pretty museum with a bunch of interactive exhibits where you can let your kids pretty much run free. It does have 4 floors of exhibits so it can take several hours. It covers everything from farming in the east to mining in the west to native peoples. I wish it had a few more exhibits and a little more depth to some subjects, but I really liked it.

Excellent zoo, a little pricier than most but well worth it. It's not open like most zoos, more linear, which is a good thing. Its on the side of a mountain and you start at the bottom. You can hand feed giraffes as well for a fee. Their are a few rides, including a sky ride to a play area. Don't miss the Will Rogers Shrine that's included in your ticket.

The history of this place is pretty incredible. While the actual Alamo is mostly an empty building, the history exhibits around it are really cool. Theirs also lots of living history going on, we got to see a weapons demonstration. Its free and a must see. Definitely check it out on your way to the river walk.

Theirs a lot to see here: good dinosaur exhibits, a great children's hands on play area, beautiful animal exhibits from Colorado and the world, a good outer space area, and a small but entertaining Egyptian exhibit. The grounds outside and park are nice to walk and the city zoo is nearby as well.

Awesome, free to enter, hand built castle. It truly is amazing to see. The drive is also very scenic. The castle is a little steep and you will be standing over grating very high up. If you have a fear of heights or tight spaces I would avoid it. Can be muddy if it has snowed or rained.

If you want an excellent place just to walk around and people watch, in a peaceful environment, look no further. Good food, good night life as well as day life and just an amazing place to look around, take the boat and show. Can get pretty warm in the summer but otherwise its great.

Great spot to see the mountain when their isn't any clouds or fog. The parking lot does fill up quick. Their are several great trails nearby that have good views as well as waterfalls. Some are very steep but they are worth it and all are paved.

Excellent and gorgeous national park. Taking the drive alone is worth it, driving up the mesa with gorgeous rock formations and canyons. Their are several hiking and biking trails as well. The one we did was excellent.

We really enjoyed our time here. The staff was very friendly, even though we were probably their only visitors that day. The wine is excellent and they have super friendly cats. Definitely recommend if your in town.
Great place for children. Several small buildings children can get inside, a playground, plenty of restrooms, ice cream and a good 9 minute train ride. The price is the best part, very reasonable.
Probably one of my favorite parks in Colorado. Plenty of parking, nice trails, a splash pad, picnic pads and ball fields. It also has one of the largest and nicest playgrounds I've ever seen.
Nice fort with a lot of history. The Rangers their are very friendly and helpful. Just walking through and reading the self guided tour is excellent. I'd recommend it if your in the area.
Great walkable area, dog friendly as well. Afterwards take a walk around downtown. It's not as amazing as San Antonio but still pretty neat, decent but not a whole lot of restaurants.
You can't see much from the drive but stop at every over look and hike the small way in. Absolutely beautiful. Haven't tried any camping but for a day trip this place is incredible.
Beautiful, easy falls to get to from the parking lot. Great hike for kids. Their is a staircase at the end that is fairly steep, but anyone can do it if they pay attention.
Good free museum with an excellent selection of rocks, ores and metals from around the world. The bottom floor has a great exhibit about mining techniques and history.
This is a great small museum with a lot of skeletons and a ton of information. You could probably kill an hour hear, my 3 year old enjoyed the children's area.
Excellent place with beautiful formations and Good easy hiking. Please respect the rules and stay off the formations so others can enjoy them as well.
Beautiful area with excellent hiking trails through an alpine forest and the alpine itself. The Ranger at this station was very nice and informative.
This is a must see Museum for fans of Shelby, Ford vs Ferrari or racing in general. They have some rare cars and for the price you can't beat it.
Probably the best place to just lose yourself in the Rockies. Great drives, lots of wildlife and over 300 miles of hiking.
Great museum full of cars, trains and motorcycles mostly pre 1960s. Not the best for small children, better for adults.

Smaller but it feels more intimate than Canyonlands.  Got some great shots though I wish there was more hiking.  This is a better option for people who are looking to drive to a photo op rather than hike there.  Busy but not crowded.  We didn't spend a lot of time here since we had just come from Canyonlands, maybe 30 minutes.  Pretty much the same price as Canyonlands just smaller so we regretted it a bit.  But the pictures were great and the toilets were clean!

Whether you are a local, in-state, or out-of-state tourist there is no better way to spend the day in the city. Get there early and beat the heat and the crowds. Also, try to do some of the longer trails, none of them are hard and they get you away from the road for a more intimate Colorado hike. A place you will never forget, young or old.

Not easy but not hard I just love trails that run along a stream or creek. With lots of shady places to have a snack or catch your breath Be sure to take the time to enjoy your surroundings. Get to the parking lot early or you will have to park far below or pick another trail. Definitely worth the addition to the summer hike schedule.

Absolutely breathtaking views!  We went in March and it was not too hot, comfortably warm, and we spent about 3 hours just in the Islands in the Sky district.  Hiking was easy, trails were short and not too crowded, and took some amazing photos and made amazing memories.  If you love the outdoors this is just something you have to do.

Uncle Wilbur's fountain in the summer is really the highlight of this park.  In winter they have ice skating outside.  I can't ice skate but my family can and we have a great time.  I wish they had more jazz or classical shows in the summer to drive out the homeless.  With all the homeless there the park is kind of a waste.

I never get tired of this place! I’ve seen some great special exhibitions here and can wander around the North building for hours.  Packs a great variety in a space that will occupy a full day. I’ve been to museums all over the world and the DAM for its size can compete with them.

Family really had a great time here.  Bigger on the inside that it looks on the outside it was well worth the admission.  We spent about an hour here and saw a lot of plants that we then saw again in Costa Rica.  Can highly recommend for an entertaining and educational afternoon!

Cooler than most roadside attractions this castle is huge, as big as some castles I’ve seen in Europe. Be sure to climb everywhere and see everything. I climbed to the top and had no fear as it is very sturdy. Great photo op and fun for the family. A must if you are in the area.

I grew up in the neighborhood so I have been coming here for years.  Nice big grassy field is plenty for all, the playground is decent, and the walking trail around the park is nice, if small.  If you live in this area it is the best open space near by.

Hell of a nice little hike! Lots of hummingbirds and cool shade and aspens and the sound of the creek beside you. I got up early and hardly met anyone in the hike up. If you need to hike for 6 miles or so someplace convenient you can’t do much better.

Affordable parking and easy to hike trails. Conveniently sited for a quick get out of town go in summer and enjoy the wild flowers and butterflies. Archery range, playground, and visitors center round out a park that is a perfect way to spend a day.

Had a great hike with my mom. Perfect for all abilities as what it may lose in difficulty it makes up for in scenery. We got there early and saw no one till we were headed back from pancake rocks. This would be an awesome hike year round

Such a beautiful trail.  Easy enough for all abilities but interesting enough for those who hike frequently.  We followed Sporting News trail till it ended where it was no longer maintained and enjoyed every minute, even in late spring.

An enormous museum that will either take a good half a day to see or multiple trips. Everything was presented really clearly, concisely, and interestingly for both history and non-history buffs. Price is steep but ultimately worth it.

Really cute park with lots of locations for picnics and light hiking. The lake itself is gorgeous, like a postcard. We saw that plenty of people fishing and fish jumping. We ended our day here after Mount Evans and it was perfect.

Cool neighborhood park perfect for a walk around on the trail, fishing, kayaking, or paddle boarding.  Decent sized playground and a basketball court to round it out.  Perfect place for families on weekends.

Great photo opportunity and a quick breather from the vendors and performers who surround the park. Sit down, enjoy the fountain and sculptures, then head back into the craziness that is the French Quarter!
Right by the highway so not a place you want to do more than park, get your bike of the truck, and hit the trail.  Bike trail is easy and pretty, perfect for families.
Doesn’t have the name or the sights like Garden of the Gods but this a fun group of trails that are good for all ages. Bring the kids and the dogs and get outside.
Great for families or those just looking to drink a brew and watch the world pass by. Be sure to stop by for Halloween as it’s the perfect family day
Decent venue and I have seen Riot Fest here which was a lot of fun but parking is atrocious and buildings are bland and out of date
Long hike but definitely worth it.  My favorite thing I did on my trip to arches.  Bring water, sunscreen, and comfortable shoes.
So cool and huge! We loved that it was free, detailed, interesting, and informative! The highlight of our trip to Frisco.
Neat little spot that was better than expected. If you are interested in local history then this place is a must.
Cool arch, easy hike.  Get there in the early morning or the late evening and beat the heat and the crowds.

Knowing every rock in this park over 35 years, i wanted to take the oppertunity to tgank the volunteer s and Rotary International for the extraordinary design and implimentations that have turned this little wild wonder ibto a pet, kid, and senior friendly expedition. Not only does tgis organisation do remarkable work for the youth of the state, sponsoring srudy abroad, Boys and Girls State- (changing my life) but they make all of thier neighbors richer for knowing them with this remakable park. Picked up in the 1930's, the garden creek park has been on a steady climv to becoming one of the crown jewels in the region. Observation decks, benckes, and miles of trails that have assended in the past few years. Thank you for your service rotary. . .so many wonderful experience s at this park i get all mushy thinking about it

Crown jewel of denver history and heritage. Cinsider you rodeo ticket every january or april as a tythe to your pioneer ancestory, where ever in tge world they come from. It may be that political correctness and cultural sensitivity training training had to start with a little less arguing, and a lot more fun. Take your kids to the fair, not to pet a bunny, but to join 4-H. By golly you live in denver not new york city. Pin a little volunteer perspective on the ownership of being a local, even if you just got here. The organization is a marvel, running the largest volunteer staff for any event, likely anywere in the country.  We all need a little can do spirit, and its not hareditary, we get it from the right kind of friends- you will make them from the bleachers to the barns at tge NWSS

what an outstanding venue to bring a little one. My two-year-old was on static blow out of excitement to the entire time. I saw a few things got me pretty excited too. a lot of press had people thinking that this place was closing in the next two years, and it was quiet, for a rainy October Tuesday afternoon. turn from the front desk there will be at least 3 years before can you slow down at this facility. I really enjoyed the outdoor trails, the giant sea sailbug, and the bees! I hope more mollusks are introduced into the exhibits. Kind of a fair amount of showboating teen getting large crowds for feedings camera did actually reduce the value of getting the kids up close

These days every comunity park has stepped up a notch in weekly family friendly entertainment. . .  but i feel tge personal need to send some kudos out for the wednesday evening concert in the park series. . .so great to see everyone i just never make rhe time ro check in on. . .makes a little grange love out here in the burbs. Particularly for families new to the area. So much international flavor to the demographics of our little rown these past 5 years, its neet to see some of the audiance effecting the musical selections. . please support the broomfield auditorium and library in appretiation for this pleasant weekly event

Actualmap looks like tgis. Google maps has it wrong. East enterance often closed due to a locked gate but ME street access trail is an empty olt no one ever uses even though the "you are here spot" is alwaus packed. Recomend this trail to break in your low lander friends and relatives to catch them in a mile hike with lots of evac points rather than som mountain waterfall trail. . . just saying great warm up for anyone, great trail running espesially qt south acces to summit as there are very few steps there. Would be nice if they let is climb to tge top like we were allowed 30 years ago. . .old people. . sheeeze

It just keeps going. . .shady creek walking with plenty of troutlets and soft pkaces to take your running shoes off for a pleasant soaking. I found the network north of this park with a halfmile patch if residential streets particularly useful and inviting to all of east boulders causeways. Offers a variety of wild flowers paved and dirt tr@cks with inviting a little fold of seclusion if you really want to find it. Parking area rarely overburdened is unusual for this town. Please help keep that a secret if it is to stay that way

A crown jewel of Denver tourism, outstanding concert venue, and reasonably priced. Beauty must recommend a membership to go along with your sketch pad box of watercolors. there are special benefits to those who invest in their communities pride and joy, ask your front desk for details on a key fob program. I have volunteered with this institution maybe five years of the past 29. really wish I could do more as this place takes my breath away and what gets accomplished and built on each year. Please support the good stuff

Every kids slice of heaven. Swimming holes,, rocks to be tossed in a perfectly good Creek, the chance of seeing a real live rattlesnake. This place is ingrained in the childhoods of every Wyominite. Picnics, reunions, dates, and the chance to relive them with the next hopeful generation. this is one of those happy places I go when the rest of my life isn't working out. _od bless the fine folks who keep this place up. It is such a powerful place to revisit from time to time

Best routes are hiking into golden via the trail between the two south gates. Micro biomes for critters and fauna I don't see anywhere else. Golden hour photography spots shooting down the high back is cool on gate three road. Best not plan on getting any shared rides out of nearby golden till really late as the gates for automotive access to that town are closed for hours during and after the big shows to discourage folks from choking off the town for free parking.

Alright Colorado, answer me this,, why is this the first stop out of towners who just got off a plane from sea level. For goodness sakes, drink lots of water, give him a little time to balance their eardrums. Highest paved driving road America is best appreciated without headaches or exhaustion. An absolute must stop for any lowlander, just give me a little time to acclimate. it's nice to see people respecting the wildlife a little better than in years past.

In the offseason this is the end of the line, as road conditions and visibility suffer from ice. Yes, that makes us a wonderful place to visit all by itself in the colder weather, I also like to use this as a staging campfor the full extent of Mount Evans when we have folks from out of town.a better place to address headaches or hydration issues than The summit . Also recommend you follow the trail to the South to get it cracking view of the valley

On first glance a good deal of the displays read like tourist brochures than content heavy museum displays. I found some displays invigorating, and others sparse. The building is beautiful, giftshop superb, staff welcome and accommodating. I hope a multi media feel will expand the conciousness of this museum to its former grandeur. I love the ABC and artifact rooms. Hope to see more archeology and cultures in conflict presentations in the future.

Premier premier location for out-of-town guests. Approach loop from the north for more privacy, this is the high Life. Observe how the reservoir filled such a vast area. South loop offersrestrooms, Stone pavilion which attracts weddings, family reunions, school boards, and is it pleasant place to sit watch both ice and summer breeze alike. The entire loop at a brisk Pace doesn't take more than 15 minutes to complete

Beauty and convenience stones throw from the traffic that will make you appretiate tge 8 dollar cover. Particularly happy with the access from some of the more advanced trails on the otgerside of tge hogback. Lake facilities, archery range, equestrian facility, yurts. . . damn! Been tempted more than once to detour out of the commute and spend a few days here. Tempting as a staycation destination par excellance.

Ohhhh, nice when you learn a new grape, credit is now on my profile radar. Really enjoyed the comfortable ambeyonce, well merchandised lighting, and most of all a rebounding respect for how much these syrah grapes are loven that west side sun. Several balanced marketable selections, with the silverware to back it up. Really enjoy the idea of a wine club based on purchasing power, good business sense

Spending so much quality "self care" time in this area has been a delight. Watching the seasons roll through and showing my son how to become as much of a naturalist as possible. I like places like this but you can still get muddy. Well enough off the beaten path, metro forget your proximity to industrial duties, perfect for a lunch break when you actually work in those duties

Getting better by the year. Like the new playground installation to the northwest, and glad to see it clean and free of permanent residence. This park hgv as been through alot of dark times, what an impressive transition. A true uh e credit to the hard working city planners and grounds crews. I might even walk here late (not looking over my shoulder) some day really soon

We call this the pirate playground since the equipment feel a great deal like ship. Ralphie's "original pizza" and the broomfield firehouse engine 2 *(I think)make this a sublime location for a picnic or event gathering space. We like the bike path connecting this playground to no less than four more parks with on a quarter mile

Cultural hotspot for boulder. The kids kind if take the place over every summer. Great tubbing, shade, and playground. Facilities folks always get too much work as so many people here litter constantly, but that's part of how I prefer raising my kid, we pick up for the practice, hope that catches on. This is a great park

Great museum and interpretation center. I like chilling with the buffallo and the best inner city pond layout i have ever seen on any city. Board walk over the cattails is fenced enough to take your littlest fisherman out for a cqst or two. Just lovely

Among the best playgrounds in the state of Colorado. A real treat for the Little ones. Especially the proximity to a great little ice cream shop, a Creek, and the Lake. This remains one of my favorite rest stopss on any I 70 dumpster fire trFfic
Catering at the denver museum at natural history for annual breakfast fundraiser went extremely well. Knowlegable professionals who keep tgings rolling nicely with excellent fair
Great fun! Our favorite are the jellyfish and the sharks! Baby sharks were found too, and tunnels, and dinosaur bones, and a tincy little otter

A big problem I have with this site is there really isn’t much to see. Although the rangers were nice and helpful and told an amazing story I feel like this house could offer a lot more. It is also a very far drive from a lot of things, minus the town of Xenia or Yellow Springs which are very pretty towns to see if you’re in the area. That is not to say you shouldn’t see the site, especially if you’re a park enthusiast, I just feel like more should be offered.

If you’re into zoos then you should check this out. Lots of fun animals to see. Festival of Lights is also well worth visiting. Little on the pricey side though for food and admission but worth it if you’re into that kind of thing. If you don’t have very long the Reptile House, Insect House ( not sure what it’s called), and the Night Hunter exhibits are the places you should see while here.

Very unique museum, wished we had a full day there. The place was so huge and had so much to see and learn. The man who we bought the tickets from was a very nice man and made our stay even more worth while. Great museum. I will say the one thing that is not great about it is it is far away from all the other places. But either or it is enjoyable.

I'm only going to give it a four because for the time being we couldn't go inside and I couldn't get a good look at it which was unfortunate but I really enjoyed walking around the outside and going into the museum's. It is a unique site seeing the outside walls of the fort. The park ranger staff was also very nice and helpful.

One of my favorite Presidential homes that I’ve visited ! The area it’s in is very scenic and takes you back to older times. The Rangers were excellent and made the experience even greater. It’s wonderful when you get to see the home if someone so important in history. Well worth a road trip to Springfield to see!

Beautiful national Park to see ! If time allows you def have to see Brandywine Falls, the ledge outlook and one of the visitors center. But you can’t go wrong in picking any place to see at this wonderful park! It’s great the history behind why it was created as well !

One of the best and most informative museums that I’ve ever experienced. It’s very touching to find yourself there. The location of the place is also convenient. Loved how there were many ways of going about experiencing different aspects of world war 2

Very fun art museum if you’re in the CBD of Cincinnati. Easily walkable from fountain square, Carew Tower, and many other places. Although there isn’t a large amount of stuff there ( at the current moment) it is definitely worth seeing for free !

Very small low key battlefield that has a great museum and wonderful mountain view and battlefield view. Anyone in the suburbs of Atlanta must stop here. It was great to be in this location. They make history really come alive.
Always a place I love to come and you get to see how history comes alive in this beautiful fort. It is well preserved and is presented quite nice and to me it is the top thing to do in St. Augustine.
Alright Contemporary Art Museum with some unique pieces. The staff is very friendly and accommodating. My problem is for the money there should be a lot more but it’s still cool to check out.
Great place to get views of the Mississippi River. Also the building itself is in this architectural wonder. Checking out a play was also a very fantastic experience during my stay here.
Very empowering museum to see if you happen to be in Cincinnati ! You will leave questioning a lot of the actions of the world ! So if you want a great museum to see check out this one
They fit a lot of unique artifacts into one little museum and it is breathtaking. The art pieces they have are quite impressive. Truthfully one of my favorite small museums to visit.
The 3 dune challenge was quite unique ! Great views from the trail. It also has a nice mix of Forrest, beach, and dunes so I have no complaints about the time I spent here today.
It is for sure one of the better contemporary art museums I’ve been to. Had a mixture of both thought provoking artwork and then straight garbage. But you can’t beat the price.
Not a big sports guy but it was cool to see this iconic landmark, sure I would’ve enjoyed it more if I actually went to a game. But it had a cool aesthetic to it
Great Art Museum to visit with a lot of unique art pieces to look at ! Also it’s free and the staff is just wonderful. One of my favorites I’ve been to!
This Art Museum is well worth your visit if you are in Forest Park. The museum itself is huge and filled w so many interesting artifacts and pieces.
Truthfully one of the best museums you can ever visit, especially for free! So much history in a great building. Also a very friendly staff
The team store workers were very kind and polite. Can’t wait to come back to Detroit to watch a game at what looks to be a beautiful park !
Too expensive and overhyped. Cool to look through but not worth paying mass amounts of money for. Kind of overrated place to go.
I think we all wish we could live in Fallingwater /: but we can’t /: but we sure can enjoy going and admiring it’s beauty
If you ever happen to be in Scranton Penn. stop here because there is so much history to be learned about trains !
The emerald lake, bear lake and Alberta fall trails are wonderful ! Wish I had more time to spend there !!

I've never seen anything like this place, which is basically like an outdoor adventure amusement park. We've gone at least once a month since moving to Charlotte earlier this year and don't remotely regret getting the annual passes.

Bottom line, even if you're not too outdoorsy, you need to come visit if you haven't already. There's always events like jam bands over the summers,  fireworks, yoga, runs and the list goes on. Of course there's also endless rafting, ziplines, high rope courses, rock climbing, mountain biking and stand up paddle board on flat water!

Plenty of my DC friends claim this is their favorite museum in the area. It's huge (6 floors) and has tons of great exhibits, so I definitely put it high on my list as well. You could probably spend most of your day here, but I love that it never feels too crowded even on busier days because of the amount of space.

I really enjoyed the FBI and Berlin Wall Exhibits, but there are so many others to explore too. Maybe I missed them, but I'd like to see more interactive exhibits.

A gem in the middle of VA. Worth a visit, although I would suggest avoiding popular days as there will be long car lines in the park and you may have less animal encounters because of it. Other than that the safari is fun for the whole family as you can choose to feed the free roaming animals right from your window. The walk thru portion of the zoo is small, but still fun. You can get close to kangaroos, feed giraffes and have birds perch all over you in the sanctuary.
dislikes: Long car lines on popular days
Fewer animal encounters during busy times

reviews_attraction.text:
$5 per head admission/parking fee...This is a great option for a beach day trip if you live in the DC metro area. On busier weekends it's good to get here before 10am or after 2 or 3pm because they close the gets if it gets overcrowded.

If you get in okay, there's plenty of places to grill, play basketball/volleyball, or just lay out. The water isn't too bad considering the location and is generally very warm in the summer.

Not the best aquarium I've ever been to (especially for the price), but it's still worth the visit...First thing you notice is a very unique layout - the majority of exhibits surround one giant cylinder aquarium about 3 stories high. Other than that, the penguins and the seals outside were my favorite exhibits. I was, however, very disappointed in the lack of sharks!

Great park with soccer fields, basketball courts, tennis courts, a volleyball sand court and a kids playground. A lot of this has been newly renovated in the past year-ish, so there's still not too much wear and tear on all the equipment. I'd like to see a fenced in area for dogs in the future, but it's still a great local park for the Pentagon/Crystal City area.

I've only come to here for the dog park and it's a solid option for any dog owner with an energetic pup. Plenty of room and usually other owners there - plus you don't have to worry about any water fixtures or sand/gravel terrain like in Clarendon.

On a side note - the tennis courts and basketball court look nice too, I just haven't used them...

Short exhibits that are hit or miss here. Considering there's so many other free museums in DC, you can probably find a better way to spend your time.

I will say, however, that when this place hosts events, they don't mess around! Had a blast at the last Greek event they had, so keep an eye out for Nat Geo events.

Took my 5 year old nephew here and I could only imagine that this place is a godsend for most parents. Plenty of arcade games, huge play place and really fun side activities like the lazer maze  (this was a favorite!), bowling, and trampoline basketball.

So easy to tire out your kids for the day here.

It's hard to find this much green space in the Clarendon area so I like this park a lot. Plenty of sports options with baseball and soccer fields, and tennis and basketball courts (although I'd love to see more than 1 basketball court). There's also a kids park, which I'm sure parents love.

A short, but very pleasant & easy trail hidden away among the DC city area. The trail weaves in and out of a small river for about a mile until you get to the Potomac River. My dog loves exploring this area as well and I haven't passed anyone along the trail who had an issue with dogs yet.

I always bring visitors from out of town here on our down time. It's a great place to grab some fresh air and check out some interesting flea market type items. I haven't explored the food options too much, but it looks like a pretty good variety of produce, meats, and other local eats.

This is a great hiking trail (and dog friendly) if you're from the DMV area and you don't want to drive more than a half hour to escape the city...Huge expanse of trails and great views of the river. I haven't seen the falls yet, but will definitely be visiting again soon.

Came here for an interactive digital exhibit, which was definitely worth it in terms of it's uniqueness. There were only a handful of things to play/interact with, but it made for a fun quick date night. Would definitely recommend if the exhibit returns!

I'm lucky I live so close to here. It's a great park to walk around, take a nap, workout, play club sports (mostly soccer), or take out your dog! Clean area filled mostly with turf soccer fields, but has a couple kids playgrounds on the side too.

Fun, free and educational Samurai Museum. It's a fairly small exhibit (read most of the displays in under 30 mins), but it's still a unique attraction if you're visiting Dallas and struggling to find other things to do.

Probably my favorite winery in the area - the smaller venue felt more comfortable and welcoming than Cana or Quattro Gumba. The staff was also really nice and the wine was solid. Bonus for having live music midday.
Awesome network of trails just off of the Parkway on the Arlington-side of the Potomac. No big views or anything, but a great city 'getaway' without actually having to travel outside the city.
Kids playground, 2 Tennis Courts and one basketball court. A small but nice park overall, but would like to see nicer basketball hoops. Great lighting after dark.
Definitely one of the more interactive museums in DC - I would put it in the 'must-try' category if you're visiting and find yourself in the Downtown area.
One of my favorite places to run/workout in Richmond. It has a looped running trail (maybe a little more than a mile long) and a few workout stations.
Awesome, open park the size of about 3 or 4 baseball fields. Played here for my kickball league, but only drawback is the lack of shade...
Love this park both to walk around and enjoy the outdoors but mainly for the giant dog park that's the size of about 4 football fields!
Pretty much every bit as amazing as it looks in pictures and then some. Very much worth the visit if you're in the Denver area.
$20 gets you a tour of one of the most iconic stadiums in the US. What more could you ask for?

Tons of great hikes in this area, very close to town easy to get to from just about anywhere.  There are clean restrooms at the main trailhead, and all the trails are well marked and easy to follow. If you are looking for some amazing views of Red Rocks and a change to make a great loop I would recommend taking the Red Rocks trail and the Dakota Ridge trail to make one large loop. I would definitely recommend this area to new hikers. Lots of great views everywhere you look and most of the trails can be hikes all year long.

There are only a couple trails in this park, but they are both beautiful in the warmer seasons. The main loop trail runs through some beautiful wetland areas and the forest is thick with small pines. The parking lots are large and the main lot has some handicap accessible areas. The restrooms at the main parking area are very nice and super clean. This is a fantastic place to spend the day with the family, bring a lunch and enjoy the great covered picnic areas.

Very nice park, Jefferson county does a great job maintaining all the parks in the county. Lots of trails with something for everyone here. Great place for a family picnic, but the park is very busy so parking can be an issue.

If your looking for more hiking and camping info check out my guide on Amazon.

Colorado Front Range Hikes: OneSunChaser Guides - Volume 1 : Morrison, Ken Caryl, Idledale, Kittredge, Conifer, Aspen Park, Indian Hills and Evergreen Areas

Beautiful park with several easy trails. Most hikes in the park have little tree cover so bring protection from the sun. If your looking for a good workout climb mount Morrison for great views of the whole park.

If your looking for more local hiking and camping info check out my guide on Amazon.

Colorado Front Range Hikes: OneSunChaser Guides - Volume 1 : Morrison, Ken Caryl, Idledale, Kittredge, Conifer, Aspen Park, Indian Hills and Evergreen Areas

This is a fantastic hike very close to Denver. Depending on the time of year you go there may or may not be a waterfall. But the hike is definitely worth doing.

If you are looking for local information on hikes and camping, check out my guide on Amazon.

Colorado Front Range Hikes: OneSunChaser Guides - Volume 1 : Morrison, Ken Caryl, Idledale, Kittredge, Conifer, Aspen Park, Indian Hills and Evergreen Areas

Views go from great to spectacular in this park, all the trails offer a chance to capture some mountain beauty. There is lots of parking at the main lot along with very clean odor free restrooms and several great covered picnic areas. If your riding your mountain bike through the park and find yourself needing a repair there is a nice bike station at the bitterbrush and antelope trail junction.

Hikes are all easy to moderate, some trails are popular with mountain bikers. Most trails are short, but all hikes have great views. Great place for quick easy hikes. Picnic areas are nice, and the bathroom at the more northern parking lot has flushing toilets. Water is available seasonally as well.

Tons of trails in the area, some lead to amazing views. Most of the trails have a creek near them, and mushrooms are found everywhere in abundance and variety. The parking lot is huge, but there are no restrooms, picnic tables, or names to the trails. This is a great place to go get into nature.

Fantastic place to hike, there is a good amount of parking, clean restrooms, and picnic tables to make for a nice outing. The trails start to get very beautiful and void of I-70 noise within 1 mile of the trailheads. Trails are well marked easy to follow and absolutely gorgeous.

Great place to hike even if there are only a few trails. Views from the trails are great and easy to traverse. There is a very nice picnic area and lots of parking. The restrooms however, are amongst the most pungent I have been in, it kind of sticks with you.

Came for the trails which are great for children or those with mobility issues. Good place to get outside and enjoy nature. The trails are nice and very easy to follow, but traffic noise and the sight of transmission lines in the park distract from the views.

Great hikes in this park, there are no service like pit toilets or picnic areas. Camping right off the creek and the falls are great depending on the time of the year. Park at the upper entrance if you want a short hike 1 mile in, 1 mile out.

Great hike up the hill, steep and not super long. Your reward for your efforts are some amazing views far into the mountains. The porta poti at the trail head can be a little dicy, I would plan on forgoing that adventure if at all possible.

Great park for the kids, we had a blast playing at the park and on the soccer fields. There are a lot of paths in the park it looks like a great place to take a walk. Picnic areas are clean and plenty of seating so lots of people can enjoy.

Great place to hike, there are lots of places to camp, and plenty of parking. Trails are easy to follow, and the scenery is beautiful. There are no facilities available at the parking areas so plan appropriately.

Fantastic park, lots of hiking trails, very close to town. Nothing super strenuous but will definitely get your heart pumping. Amazing views on all of the trails. I would highly recommend hiking in this area.

Great place to go boating, sailing is interesting here due to constant wind shifts. Dog park is nice, great bird watching here as well. There are nice looking camping areas here, but they are  always full

Great trail with a fair amount of wildlife activity. Hike is moderate with a good waterfall depending on the time of year you visit. I would definitely recommend this trail for the natural beauty alone.
Great park, there is something for everyone. Great playground and skate park for younger children. Soccer fields and baseball diamonds for spots and a great lake with paved path and fantastic views.
Great little park with amazing views. There are plenty of picnic spots and quite a bit of parking for a park with one hiking trail. I love the drive up to the park with all its twists and turns.
Great park with lots of equipment for the kids. Also a great place to beat the heat as there is a very fun splash pad for kids. Huge parking lot and lots of other fun activities very close.
Not much in the trails department, but panorama point has some great views. There are a few decent picnic areas as well, but most are very close to the road.
Very beautiful mountain lake with Mount Massive looming in the distance. Great place to spend the day exploring, fishing, hiking and enjoying nature.
Good hiking and mountain biking close to the highway. The bad part is you will hear the highway the entire time you are hiking.
Great place to hike, bike and run. Plenty of parking, and the restrooms and other facilities are in good shape.

Beautiful historical landmark. There are signs posted, "no trespassing" the owner(s) are usually present, please observe and respect from the viewing point.

The small town of Crystal still exists up the path, with only a handful of residents, be mindful these are private residences.

Great hiking/4X4 area, do NOT attempt this trail without a proper vehicle (high clearance) and tools in case of a tire blow out, or worse! People are friendly along the way as they would help, willingly, but don't assume everyone will have what you need. We encountered an entire family of 5 broke down with a tire blow out, the 10 people that passed, no one had the correct tools. We couldn't stay all day, hopefully he was able to get towed, (I couldn't imagine what that would cost would be on this narrow, extreme 4X4 trail). Total of about 9 miles round trip. Enjoy, but come prepared with everything you may need to hike or drive.

Very small oceanside, beach front park. Boat dock available for small watercrafts, kayaking,  paddle boarding, etc. Maybe half mile loop through the jungle on a wooden path, lots of wildlife to see, and a lot of people fishing (not sure what the catch was). Bathrooms could use some cleaning, but overall great park. Peace River animal wildlife is also on premises, please donate to this worthy cause if you saunter through to check out the refugees.

Not at all a youthful experience, food is bland, beer/sodas are flat and not very flavorful.  The 1800's environment, outfits, zero music, and less than attentive staff do not make an enjoyable atmosphere.  Customer base is on average 80 and older, on the weekends standing room only. I get that it is a historical location, given it more than one chance, not impressed,..

Interesting story that Buffalo Bill was part of the circus/carnival act and killed buffalo for sport. I'm not sure why we commemorate him? Steel drive up to the top of the mountain, about a half hour drive. Beautiful view from the top of the mountain anyway. Great shop with souvenirs, hand crafted native American made gifts, snacks, and ice cream.
likes: Facilities & Services: Souvenir Shop, Handcrafted Gifts, Snacks, Ice Cream

reviews_attraction.text: Absolutely breath taking! Views for miles located in Estes Park. Grab your hiking gear, camera, and get outside! Be prepared for all elements, ice/snow in late April, so dress accordingly. Definitely would have been more helpful with spikes and hiking sticks. We took a hike in 60°F weather and it started snowing on us!

This man is a 'mad genius'!  What an eclectic atmosphere of homemade, refurbished/repurposed junk.  He literally made someone else's garbage into a treasure and is sitting on the jackpot!  Fun, family, tour, food, live music, and gift shop.  A veteran, but doesn't do military discount?

Easy on and off experience.  Car was ready when we docked.  Small state rooms, 2 twin sized beds.  Very old ship!  Definitely feels like the 1950's.  Set your alarm a half hour before docking or you will be shocked awake by the hard banging on your hollow steel state room door.

Everything you want under one roof, many dining options, from buffets to fancy, bars to ballrooms for events, spa, gambling, and rooms.  Although I have never stayed here or used the spa/fitness area the biggest downfall is smoking is still acceptable in certain areas inside.

Beautifully maintained, dog friendly park in Denver. We attended the, "Bunny bolt" on the Saturday before Easter, a 1K for kids. 5K and yoga offered same day, prizes, costume contest, photo booth, and a giant Easter egg hunt. Peddle boats offered in season.

This place was amazing, beautiful, and well kept up.  I could imagine it only gets better with warmer weather, (half of the tour was closed due to bat hibernation) they have outdoor activities too. Zipline etc.
The 4 stars was due to customer service...

What a cool abandoned, historic silver mining town. We enjoyed walking around the trail and through the houses. A lot of them have been restored at this point, so please leave donations to keep up on maintenance, for other visitors to enjoy!

It's pretty grown over, trails aren't too maintained. Small loop, maybe 0.5mi round trip. Wear appropriate hiking gear, ie. long pants, hiking boots, and take a stick, in case of possible alligator encounter.
Love the Thursday farmer's market! What a great selection of local and organic items. Great for a quick fill up on goods, or to browse and spend all day! Bring your own shopping bags and go green!💚
Beautiful view of Seneca lake!  Large craft beer selection, great wines, and small plates.  Pulled pork sandwich, ballpark style nachos,(processed cheese) and delicious spinach filo triangles.
Awesome park to gander at wildlife! Always clean. Please pick up after your dog. Love the hike through the woods or around the lake on a pretty day. Free outdoor concert during the summer.
What a beautiful establishment, feels so NYC in our small town.  I absolutely love this theater and the performance of 'Kinky Boots' was fabulous!  Not a bad seat in the house.
Beautiful State Park, $7 a day admission, or $70 for all the states parks. Well maintained and beautiful wide trails. Please clean up after your dogs and they must be leashed.
Beautiful manicured gardens, have fun spending hours here! Military discount or yearly rates available. Pack your lunch and SPF, or try something local from their grille.
Amazing scenery.  Breath taking views.  Surfers go out even when it's chilly.  If you're lucky you can see deer in the woods.  This used to be a zoo, in the 80's I heard.
Well maintained, open space, flat hiking trails, horseback riding, and fishing. No admission cost. Dogs permitted leashed, and picked up after.
Went for the Dior and Rembrandt exhibit which were amazing! Beautiful museum, definitely need to return and check out the standard displays!
A great big, green open space in Denver. We attended the bunny bolt here for Easter. 5Ks, yoga, prizes, Easter egg hunt, and so much more!
Loved this place, great for hiking.  Make sure you keep navigation running it's possible to get lost, not a lot of signs for directions.
My review is strictly because it wasn't open. They open on weekends only starting May 5th and open up 7 days a week starting the 27th.
Great place to check out the rescued wildlife. This kind of facilities cost money to run, please donate if you walk through!

We have tried a mid-level difficulty room, and their most difficult room, and have enjoyed each experience. During our first visit, we were paired up with two other couples who were reckless with the room, and ended up knocking down one of their cameras. At the end of our hour in the room, the staff pulled me aside and offered to comp our next visit due to our unruly teammates. They definitely did not have to do this, but the gesture was very much appreciated!

This place is beautiful and FREE!! What more can you ask?Upon arriving you will see a million prairie dogs which if you don't live here then you will be amazed! You will see deer, hawks and you most likely will get lucky and see bison which is the coolest thing!! They roam in herds and even have little babies with them. Butttttt you might not see them until the very end of the trail that you drive on

This is a great place. You have many different paths. Beautiful view. Lot of history in this place so be prepared to find lots of old homes with lots of history. Great place to bring your pets. If you hit the right spot. You can see and hear Red Rocks.I can't think of a better way to spend a bachelorette than having Mount Falcon on the agenda.  First off, I want to give a gigantic shoutout to Robin,

This open space is just beautiful. It is diverse in that you walk through open meadows and pine forests as well. In the spring there are little streams that cross the path. We didn't have long enough to spend here. There are many trail options and some are accessible for horses and bikes in addition to foot traffic. Lovely vistas. Bathroom facilities. You can find a map at the start of the trails.

From questioning it appears that the sales points are managed by the tournament organization and there was some doubt by the facility staff whether they could open the gates for storms.Also it appears that the parking access is managed by the tournament organization. However I would surmise that any legal action for "reasonable accommodation" would be directed towards the Sports Complex.

You know when you go on a road trip and you find those hidden roadside attractions that is Instagram worthy? This is one of them! The Swetsville Zoo is a collection of sculptures made out of junk! I guarantee that you will find one you love with a quick 15 minute walk through the park. Not only is it a fun place, it's peaceful, and a good spot to stretch your legs during a long drive.

Baseball fields are on the north side, west of the in-line hockey rink.  Because the heart of any park is all about playing, the awesome playground is in the center.  In the summer there is a water park next to the giant lake and in the winter, the large hill serves as a sledding hill.  They even put hay bales around possible obstacles like trees and metal poles of the picnic shelter.

This place is very cool. The married couple that owns it designs and hand cuts all their pieces from steel. They make everything from refrigerator magnets and Christmas ornaments to picture frames and wall hangings. We had a hard picking something out because there is so much. They are very friendly and polite while helping you look at the vast selection. We'll be back!

It's listed as a moderate trail, but someone with high arches, a torn ACL and meniscus, this is hard. But I kept my eye on the prize, and it was extremely worth it. It's beautiful and breathtaking. You can get to the top, and sit there for as long as you want. Grab some snacks, and definitely bottles of water. The summer time is brutal, but it is definitely worth it.

We saw many large groups that brought their own tables, grills, and chairs. I don't think that it was within the park rules to bring a grill; however, the park rangers didn't police it. They seemed to be on the look out for more egregious offenses.A parking space (the parking lot was completely full and we had to circle it a couple times for someone else to leave).

Also, if you made the unfortunate mistake of not bringing enough water with like I did, there is a nature center at the top with water fountains and bathrooms. We parked in a space which were all located right next to the road after you pull in a tiny bit. I had to use the restroom after driving for so long. I was happy to see some available.

The staff memebers are so friendly and great with the children. We always have fun. My daughter loves coming home to show her dad and brother what she made. The cost is $3 for the child and adults are free. Read and Seed is for ages 2-4 but they have programs for all age levels. I would definately recommend checking this out!

Great experience! Visited Wings Over the Rockies while visiting Denver. Located approximately 10 minutes from downtown Denver. Friendly staff and a whole lot to do for people of all ages. Checked out several airplanes, helicopters and memorabilia from different eras. Tried out the flight simulator for $7 and was super cool.

This is our favorite park and playground for the kiddos. Something for toddlers thru teens. Much of colorado is dedicated to parks and recreation for young and old, and Ft Collins is my favorite so far. I just saw a couple families walking with inner tubes from nearby waters here at the park, that will be our next plunge!

It's my home away from home. I can bike, walk, or drive here- it's wonderful the access- the bike trail runs right into it. The paddleboats are neat in the summertime. Avoid the geese. Playground is lovely and the park is well-maintained. Lots of cool festivals and things to do on weekends. Pokémon Go hunting is FIRE!

My idea of fun is laying down in the shade on a comfortable recliner while people bring me food and drink but my responsibilities yank me back into place.. Today I dropped my organizational urges with a THWACK, like a heavy platter of meatballs in a thick sauce, that rolled over my clean wood floor in every direction,

Stayed at Boyd Lake State Park for 2 nights. Campsites are pull through and level. Fire ring and picnic table are provided at each spot. Must buy firewood locally to bring in.Sites are electric only. There are 2 water spigots on each row and are there for you to fill up your rigs. Dump stations are available on site.

Hike was moderate with lots of beautiful flowers and grasses along the way. The end is steep and mostly rocks. Tons of chipmunks at the top! The falls were very pretty and I would recommend taking the trail that allows you to go to the top of them, it gives you a great view and there are very cool pools at the top.

From the greeting that we got, to the presentation of the room, and the bathroom, to the kitchen and how willing everyone was to make the experience.  amazing as possible was astounding. The bed and the sheets were some of the most incredibly soft that I have felt in a long time coming from a bed-and-breakfast.

I came upon this park just by happenstance one day one my bike ride and was amazed by the sheer size of the place. A huge park with a gigantic lake right off to one side. The whole lake has a path encompassing its perimeter for one to walk or bike around with ease. there were also outcroppings for fishing.

View from the parking lot is gorgeous. There is also a trail (believe it's pretty short) that leads to the Lookout Mountain Nature Center. I didn't check it out as it was starting to rain.The museum was also kid-friendly. There were some interactive exhibits as well as a dress-up area (cowboy gear).

We had our daughter's birthday party there in lower part of building with one of the art instructors and they had a great project to do and we had the usual cake/ice cream afterwards.  Wife thought of an original and creative venue here.  Too bad I was under the weather, but still enjoyed the event.

The drive to this location is absolutely breathtaking thanks to Horsetooth Reservoir. I enjoyed every second of it. We drove through the park to hike up to Arthur's Rock. Once we got near the area to check in and park, the roads were not paved and it took awhile to get to the destination.

Basketball courts. Baseball diamonds. Barbecue area with tables. Bike lockup areas at each smaller area. Nearby dog park that's pretty awesome. Own Yelp listing and everything.Think the kiddie playground is probably the main attraction. Huge slides. Swings. An army of smaller jungle gyms.

I enjoyed the ripples and bones. I wish they would identify more of the bones on the other side. I would have liked to learn more about the animals there. Even a sign with pictures of them would be nice. Like the side with the tracks, showing the three dinos who made the tracks.

This is a really great place to visit. First only 4 stars because of the  tremendous crowds today and the impossible parking. But the walk up was nice although there are shuttle busses to the observatory from parking. The view from the top is fantastic o a clear day but on this day the smog was not good. The observatory itself is very interesting with great exhibits including movies in the auditorium and a planetarium. The is even a Foucult's pendulum. Did not try the cafe dye to all of the negative reviews. This is well worth a visit and a place to bring children.

This is a great place for kids and parents. Something happening every minute from shows (cat in the hat tour of the planets) to imax to tortoise training. All hands on exhibits for kids from dinosaurs to water room to weather station to science projects. Feel the hurricane wind is popular. This is an expensive but wonderful place to visit. Plan to spend hours. Kids will not want to leave.

Not easy to see the wild horses but the beach was nice but more so were all of the hiking trails. A lot of varied ecosystems worth seeing. Lots of birds and even a couple of deer and a woodchuck! The walk to the lighthouse was short but really worth it. Nice lighthouse if you are into lighthouses. Plenty of parking sites and none of the trails are difficult.

An absolutely wonderful place to visit. An old home from the early 20th century with beautiful appointments and interesting architecture. The gardens are amazing with many different species, well kept and manicured. Over 7 acres of gardens and pathways built on a couple of steep hills. Hard to get into so mke reservations well in advance. Parking available.

Really fun place to visit with lots of sculptures large and small. Nice walking paths and chairs and benchs to rest and look. Parking lot at end of road where it turns to left...pay lot. There are occasionally 1 hour free spots on the street. This is a beautifully cared for, clean, and well kept exhibit. Easy to find in a quiet neighborhood. Worth a trip.

This is a  great park for families. From Storyland to Put Put golf, from Coterie Woods to the golf courses, from the stadiums to the amphitheater, it has everything. Boat rentals near the Museum of Art and fishing off Harrison Ave. Food at the old casino, driving range off Filmore. What a wonderful park. Only problem: avoid fire ants!

This is an interesting place to visit. Entrance fee, but for seniors discounted. Stairs up to the battlements. During part of the year they shoot off the cannon but not now due to COVID. View from the top worth the stairs. A lot of history here in a beautifully preserved structure. Lots of parking.
likes: Facilities & Services: Senior discount, ample parking

reviews_attraction.text: Really enjoyed visit here with the grandkids. Plenty of room to run and play. Nice place for picnic on clean benches.dog lark in the back. Plenty of parking and not too crowded during the week so great place for smaller kids. Nice hill to run up and down and even some clover to look for flowers.

Circumnavigated the island for the fishing. A great place on the entrance to Tampa Bay. Lots of fish if that is your goal. Easy trip by boat. Some interesting ruins and a nice beach Gulf side. I dont know about the facilities on the island but apparently there are rangers here most of the time.

This is a pretty nice park. Just know that you must enter the park from either the East or West entrance. Nice trails and plenty of birds especially in the morning. No dogs allowed but plenty of people jogging and hiking. Parking lot cost $1 per hour. Clean and neat.

Lots of restaurants and stores. Interesting  place to visit and shop. Can be very crowded because it is very popular. Every kind of Japanese restaurant you could want. Oriental market, stuffed animal store. Shoe store and tennis shoe repair store.

Small park with nice sand area under swing set and climbing apparatus with 2 slides for small and larger children. Fences in qiet neighborhood.  2 and 4 year old grandkids love it but not for older kids. No restrooms. No real dedicated parking.

A beautiful old building but a little small for a 250 guest wedding. It is a charming space and beautifully maintained. All old wood. Enjoyed our visit. Wedding here was beautiful but I would recommend no more than 150 guests in this space.

My grandchildren loved it. Lions and tigers and bears and ponys and you can get up close and really see them. Children love it. The bird show was a little weird but interesting. It is an interesting place ti visit with kids.

This is a really cool building wirh an interesting history. If you are in the area well worth a quick stop just to see. Very interesting interior. The meeting place for Untapped Tours is out front at the entrance.

Great park adjacent to the airport. Plenty of sports fields and play grounds for smaller kids. Even area to learn how to ride bicycle! Picnic tables and concrete benches. Well maintained and clean. Parking nearby.

Nice park with access to beach, Big Sarasota Pass, and the bay. Places to kayak paddle board, picnic, hike, and just have fun. can be very busy at holidays! Plenty of parking at both ends of the park is free.
Great beach with facilities but parking is not easy as the lot fills up quickly. Watch out for the tarballs. Water is cold but wonderful. Beach is cool all day. Go to 27th street and there is a lot.
great park on the lake with $9 18 hole par 3 golf course, lawn bowling, free parking, bile and hiking trails. Very pretty spot. Beautiful view of the lake. Great stairway up to the Bistro.
Great hiking trails inside of neighborhoods at base of mountains. Plenty of parking lots of trails if varying difficulty. Breath for exercise. Good view especially at sunset.
Visited from the water only. Fishing around the island  was very good for speckled sea trout, lady fish, and a few small snapper. Not a bad ride by boat and worth the trip.
Nice hiking trail through the neighborhood. Actually plenty of wildlife to see. Mule deer, quite a few birds. Heard but didn't see coyotes. Very dry this time of year.
Nice little alley where artists have painted murals. Interesting little place to stop. Park on the street. Great micro brewery around the corner.
Great facility and St. Petersburg boat show was really good. Right next to the Dali Museum and a beautiful boat basin and sn airport!
This is a surprisingly fantastic museum. Bird exhibit alone is worth a trip. Children of all ages will enjoy this museum.

This is a beautiful place to visit. There is a ton of walking through great paths between exhibits. I kinda am here for animals not so much a walking trail. Don't get me wrong it is a good place and the animals deserve the best. I am a zoo advocate. I have a membership to the Denver Zoo. Some people there complain that the animals don't have enough privacy or space. Having done many behind the scenes experiences I can say they have plenty of room and are treated so well. Today in Tacoma we saw elephants, a tiger, the walrusses were amazing as was the polar bear. The red fox has a great story here. They are currently off exhibit due to construction. This is a good thing. What it comes down to is an okay zoo. Would I drive 2 hours again to come back? Probably not. Would I say go at least once. Of course. Support your zoo and the work they do. The hamburger was amazing.

AMAZING! We took Spirit and Ghost out. The way they have this adventure set up is phenomenal. They have 1 volunteer who stays by the cars to protect against break ins. 1 volunteer who checks the path for other dogs. Especially off leash dogs. 2 volunteers who walk with the clients. And Peggy who runs the operation was also with us. These guys know what they are doing and take every safety precaution they can. The walk is approximately 1 mile round trip. They have a volunteer who takes amazing pictures in the most beautiful spots. I am excited to see those. They give you a thumb drive after the walk. You are also free to take your own pictures and videos. It took us awhile to get in to do this adventure. 100% worth it. They also send you very detailed instructions on where to meet them. This adventure is by appointment only.

Maybe it's because I am used to aquariums along the ocean. This place was not a good experience. Maybe it was the line to get in, the line to have them put your bracelet on because you may not know how, the line to take your picture BEFORE you enter even if you don't want it taken. Don't ask if they can "click" you into the aquarium to bypass the 2 pictures they take of each person. Then you get inside. Wow, the noise is loud. There are tigers,  that is kinda funny to me. Now if you want you can guide a camera through the water for an extra dollar. At the end, to a very short exhibit you can play carnival games. Yes that is why I came to the aquarium. Again maybe because I am not from a landlocked state. I will not be back. Ever.

What a great zoo! This would be a little difficult to navigate go anyone who has issues walking. Even with a scooter or wheel chair. If you have the patience you can do it. Totally worth it. Bring cash to feed the giraffes. $3-$5. You can touch them if they choose to let you when you are there. I posted a picture of one kissing my daughter. You can also do last minute behind the scenes with the rhinos, elephants, and a few other animals. They have an Australian walk about with wallabies. We had pizza there that was really good. Not like we expected. Fun for the whole family.

Where is the best zoo around? I'm not sure there is one answer. This zoo is amazing and did not disappoint. We took the 102 mile drive for the Red Panda Experience. Totally worth it. The staff were so friendly. All of them. Brittany, who was the lead in the Red Panda Experience was extremely good. Some of the animals here are old. Kaya, the Canadian Lynx. What a beautiful cat. There are way more animals to see here than I expected. It can be gone through in a couple of hours. This is an AZA accredited zoo. The only kind I go to.

This is my first time here and can I just say "WOW!" It is so beautiful. The price to get in is very reasonable AND if you really love it you can upgrade your day fee to an annual membership. This is a great place to come and stroll around. Find a bench and read a book. Bring a lunch or buy lunch here. The conservatory is amazing. They also have an elevator in there so if you can't do stairs you  an still enjoy the beauty. I am betting that there is beauty here in any season. This is a MUST SEE. Parking is FREE.

A great place with amazing views. A little spendy to get in. Worth it if you have the funds available. $14.50 for adults. Under 2 is free. Add $2.00 per person if you take the tram up to the base of the falls. It is 8 tenths of a mile to get to the base. You can climb 150 steps on one side or take the elevator the view from that side. Or go past the restaurant and take the 224 steps to the top. There is also hiking beyond that point. The view is beautiful.

I brought my  family here to drive through the park. We also did 2 animal encounters. I will tell you I paid full price for them. It wasn't too expensive until I found out that they have AMAZING Groupons out. I could have cut the cost by more than half. They are worth it. You can drive through more than once. It's a great thing to do as animals are active at different times. Most of the staff was friendly.

Beautiful day to go here. Loved the walk. We saw Prarie Dogs, Bison, Geese, Birds, People, Lakes, and more. The walk was relaxing not too many people. There were benches along the way if you need to rest. The floating bridge was awesome. It looks like you can drive and see some of the things that we walked to. Great for people who can't walk very far. We will come back.

5 stars for the High Tea. So much fun. Great selection of teas. We loved the mango tea, chai tea, and the chocolate cherry tea. The scones with Devonshire cream, mmmmm yummy. The castle tour was also very nice. The views from some of the windows is amazing. Don't forget to say hi to Chuck the dog.

This is a beautiful place to visit. I love people watching here. The views are magnificent. The natural rocks are gorgeous. The colors are vibrant. Full disclosure I have not been here for a concert. I think the traffic would be horrible. I do bring all my guests here for the beauty.

We had an amazing experience at Wallaby Ranch. I flew in from Colorado and we drove from Portland to here. It was so fun. The tour is family friendly and we learned so much amazing information about wallabies and kangaroos. I highly recommend adding this to your list of things to do.
Wow! What a great day. The hike was no too bad and we are still getting used to going up that elevation. The view was worth it. Lake was frozen and fun to walk across. Met great people and pups.
We had so much fun at the dinosaur exhibit! Totally worth the trip. We learned even more about dinosaurs than we knew. There are live exhibits to see. The exhibit on babies is phenomenal.
This was a cute little park. Nobody ever wanted to stop here with me and finally my friend did. Please make sure to bring a little cash to donate. Cute little gift shop too.
I am giving this 5 stars simply because you were able to walk up to it. So many of them you can't.  Not a large lighthouse, still beautiful and very well maintained.
Easy walk. If you are walking to explore take the dirt path not the gravel one by the bike path. We saw ducks, rabbits, birds, dogs, and people. Beautiful views!
Great place to go to see and hear about history. Friendly tour guides who really know what they are talking about. Great for the family. Beautiful gardens.
Cute place. I would have probably enjoyed it more had we been able to enjoy the outside section. It was pouring rain that day.  I loved the petting area.
Great park. We will be back to walk the 6.8 mile loop. A little more time needed for altitude adjustment. Sea level to this level. The problem is real.
Great BIG dog park. Charlie loves to come here. My daughter and son-in-law bring him 4-5 days a week. I come too when I am in town. Charlie loves it!
What a great park. Perfect for a walk. Woth or without a dog. Need a FREE DOG WALK? Download the Wag app and use code DEBRA1018.
It is a great little park if you want to play Frisbee, catch, walk a dog, or sit in a bench and think. No playground for kiddos.
Great little local park. There is always some kind of fun community event going on. Today was "Pets in the Park."
I love this park. The pond is great in any season. I love all the geese and ducks around. Great walking paths.

To begin with I feel that 4 stars is actually a little bit generous for my experience here during the summer. But let me explain why. When I first started to go here during the summer I had a blast, slides, a climbing wall, a basketball hoop, and a lazy river. Basically all a kid can hope for right? But as I got older, I am now a teenager, even though I do enjoy the park still there are a lot of flaws that point out that the Oasis is primarily focused on attracting a younger crowd. This is not a bad thing but I feel that teens should be aware of it before planning to attend.
The reason I feel that the Oasis is geared for younger kids is this, the life guards are much more strict on the older kids compared to the young ones. Even when completely respectful and follow the rules multiple times the life guards made sure to comment to be nice to the kids. The snack bar is also very expensive for a teenager to try and plan to spend a full day here. For an adult who is bringing thier kids the cost is not bad but for those of us getting minimum wage? It hits hard.
Other complaints regarding it is that there is no where to actually swim around, lazy river your required to have a tube and the other pool deep enough to swim is occupied by the climbing wall.
My final complaint is that there is not a whole lot of area to sit for parents or anyone trying to eat lunch etc.
I feel like I have made the Oasis sound bad but by no means is it a bad destination for kids under 12 or thereabouts. It just isn't geared towards teenagers.
Make sure to bring plenty of sun screen, there is a lack of shade as well.
I would recommend ☺

Filled with all varieties of plants, animals, and veiws this is definitely one of my favorite places to visit that is right in the center of the city. When your on the refuge you have an amazing veiw of the mountains with the spectacular addition of the Denver sky line. While driving through you can spend either a short 25 minute trip here or up to several hours. If you enjoy photography this is a great destination for you. There are a lot of birds, deer, and buffalo that are all great to photograph.
The park is open sunup to sundown all year long and does allow fishing from around memorial day weekend to veterans day. Other information you should be aware of is that hunting is not permitted, and fishing does require a special $7 day pass as well as a Colorado fishing license as well as special rules including only catch and release, barbless hooks only, and no live bait.
I would recommend this to all age groups but especially the elderly and young children as it is a short drive from the city but still is great for both. Taking young kids or trying to drive far when your old is a hassle so this is the only reason I would especially call those groups out. However it is still a great destination for all! Highly recommend!

Nice lake with good fishing for rainbow and cutthroat trout. Nice tables that are shaded  as well as a nice pavilion beside the lake. There is a trail around the lake which in some areas is a boardwalk, however the trail and boardwalk are not super maintained but still very easily walkable. There is very little shade except on the west side of the lake so be prepared for heat. It is busy, mostly with fisherman so it is not loud and still very peaceful. The small admissions fee of 7 dollars was already covered by our camping pass in the area which was nice. The people running the booth were helpful and friendly. My biggest complaint is that the lake does close at 7:30 and they start getting people out around 7:00 or 7:15 (pm) which is slightly annoying when fishing as that is when it is cool and the fish bite. However they do open at an early 6 am which is helpful. I would like to go again.

This is most likely the most underrated tourist stop in Plymouth. The statue itself is a work of engineering genus, art, and history. There was literally no one there but my group when we showed up and it's really cool. A ranger stopped by and gave us some great information about the Monument and I did notice that you really gotta give it a few minutes. There are SO many hidden meanings and everything has a significance. I cannot recommend this enough! The parking is free and easily obtained and the information was awesome.
It's truly a shame more people don't see the Monument, I do think it may have the fact that it could be taken as far too political and Christian for many groups. It talks about the fundamentals this country was built on, including God. Myself being a Christian this was really inspiring as an American as well. I highly recommend this to all people.

Went to see the Dead Sea Scrolls exhibit as well as the Imax. Very pleased with the size of the exhibit and the amount of information contained. The Imax was also very interesibg and informative. I did stop by in a couple other exhibits including the Mummy exhibit which is also very informative and packed with interesting artifacts and facts. The only exhibit I went in and was thoroughly disappointed by was the creatures of light exhibit.  Not very interesting and much more geared to very small kids. The museum itself was clean and had plenty of benches throughout, there were tables for eating that appeared clean. The restrooms were nicely cleaned and easily accessible. The gift shop has an ok selection but was so overpriced it's not even worth stepping into. The staff were engaging and friendly. I would recommend you visit.

Absolute must see while in Boston! This is such a huge piece of history that is so cool to see completely for free. The staff on board, who are active service men and women, know their stuff and are very happy to help! I learned a ton of fascinating things from them and was glad to have asked as many question as I did, and they seemed to not mind as they were bored anyways.
Just for anyone looking to go make sure to bring an ID of some kind! There is security and a metal detector to go on the ship and they do require an ID when you go through.
This is of course great for all ages and the museum attached is certainly geared for younger kids. I would recommend this for everyone that enjoys history or ships!

The views alone are worth making this location a bucket list item! Add music and any person is hooked. While attending a concert here is absolutely amazing, going when nothing is happening can be just as cool. It's completely free to go and walk around the amphitheatre and even up on stage. A cool event for kids and adults alike. There are several trails in the area to take advantage of the gorgeous rocks in and around the amphitheatre. I highly recommend this place to anyone passing by or looking to attend a concert here. It can be a several hour event to see a concert or a 25 minute stop on your way past. It's all up to you, regardless this is definitely a jaw dropper. Pictures just don't do it justice.

Stunning views, a range of difficulty in hikes, and lots of company! This is an amazing state park, however, there were a lot of people there when I visited, even during January.
