I see lots of reviews saying that 4 wheel drive is needed, but I saw a '98 Toyota driving with no trouble, I was with a group in a minivan which had no trouble. If you are an experienced driver and will patiently take your time to avoid tricky dips any car should be more than adequate.

This is a great place to bring the family and take a hike over the weekend, I wouldn't recommend it for camping or staying an extended amount of time. If you are a rock climber this is one of the best spots in Colorado.

While the history of the church fantastic, architecture impressive, and the grounds well maintained, I can't say I really enjoyed my experience here.
The fact that they now charge 8 dollars per person to enter is rather insane. First off, this is not worth 5 bucks to see. The inside, while amazing, is just not worth paying for. Any average Catholic church looks the same. In all honesty it was just as busy even with charging to get in, so there are no pros to this new change.
I recommend this place to everyone to stop at and look at, make sure to get a photo of Paul Revere on the back. However I don't recommend actually going in to anyone, it's a waste of time and money.

3 words can describe this place. Not very impressive. For this reason it only deserves the 3 star rating. Even though the visitor center is great, parking is a little tight but ok, and several miles of trails to hike, I can't say this State Park Impressed me. There are some nice red rocks which are a nice veiw, and some cool wildlife to see but the trails are very boring and completely flat. For older hikers or adults with children this is probably a good place in summer because of the easy trails and low elevation. But there is very little challenge to the hikes and barely any cool views. Tons of mud on the trail I hiked as well.

Museum is loaded with information and has a lot of cool bits and pieces of history inside as well. Definitely worth checking out.
The gift shop had a great selection including the typical gift shop items such as coasters, ornaments, and magnets.
I would be lying if I said the staff were top notch, the gentleman at the information desk was rude and not very helpful. However the girl who helped me out at the Monument was great, very friendly and knew what she was talking about.
I most certainly recommend the museum to you, it is free for those wondering, whether you plan to climb the tower or not.

Really cool, lots of history, very well preserved. There is a person there who answers any questions you may have. It is also completely free and no to let's are required so it is not time either.
Only complaint is that because it is a free self guided tour it is very crowded and can be difficult to get the full experience because of this.
Highly recommend this to all people and you will find that young kids will find it really cool. Don't plan more than 30 minutes for this stop, my group made it through in about 20 and even that was a little excessive.

If your on the Oregon coast this is a must see! When the tide is just coming in the sound of it can't be compared to, and the splash is awesome as well. I could, and have, spend hours here watching it. It is such a peaceful place to just sit and watch, but also super powerful and just cool. Getting out to it is a little bit difficult so I would recommend anyone who has small kids or any kind of a disability keep this in mind. You have to go down a lot of stairs as well as over a lot of rocks.
I would 100% recommend this to anyone who likes the ocean.

I did enjoy the state park and it was great that they had ample picnic tables and that the restrooms were open during the winter. The hike I took was quite easy and very boring. For much of the hike you could see the road if you looked for it, as well as being able to see parking lots and buildings occasionally.
I can't guarantee all hikes follow this trend in the state park but the particular one I took was somewhat disappointing.
I would definitely recommend to anyone looking for an easy hike to get away from the stress of life.

This tricky spot to find is well worth the hunt. Located just off of 101 it is a little bit tricky to locate the spot but after that you will have no problems. Don't plan on a long visit, count on taking between 10 and 30 minutes here depending on how many pictures, information, or time you want. The walk itself is really peaceful and super easy to do. It's all on a raised boardwalk around the Cobra lilies so there is no chance of getting your feet wet. If you have a few minutes to spend on a unique spot this your place.

This lake has gorgeous veiws and a nice hike around it. There are a lot of different types of birds that frequent the lake which is cool. This is basically where the greatness ends.
There is trash everywhere very poorly maintained, the lake is super unhealthy looking when you get close because of the amount of trash. The parking is a nightmare and constantly dangerous to get into and out of.
I would recommend this anyone who has a pet or just wants to take a walk. But not if you plan to fish or do anything in the water.

Super cool statue with an amazing view of the Old North Church in the background and  a very peaceful area to sit and take a break.
Very tricky to get a nice shot because of the amount of people, however if you truly wanted one than simply use a tripod, take about 15 photos not moving the camera at all about 1 minute apart for each photo. Then go to Photoshop and blend them together with the program removing anything it finds different in each photo. This gets you a sweet picture of the statue with no one in it 🙂

Not highly priced at only 7 dollars for a day pass it is well worth your money. The visitor center is nice and has friendly staff. There is one little trail in particular which goes beside the lake and into the feild a bit as well that is really peaceful and a nice easy walk. The fishing is really nice, however I personally have not had much luck. A really great place to go for a nice afternoon. Only complaint is that the picnic tables are not super well maintained and has several wasp nests in them.

Wonderful park for kids and teens alike. The actual playground of the park is awesome and can entertain ages 3-11 without difficulty. There are also wonderful restrooms, tennis courts, a skate park, and basketball court. These all beside a lake with a long path leading all the way around it. Only complaint I would have to say is that at times the park is crazy busy, but that only proves that it is one of the best for miles.

A nice little lake with a path around it which is great for a jog or dog walking. Tried a bit of fishing and was disappointed that the pond is more polluted than it appeared in photos. No luck fishing sadly.
I recommend it to anyone who lives in the area but it's not worth more than a 5 minute drive to be honest.

The staff were not very engaging but did get thier job done. Prices were rather high and there isn't a great selection in the gift shop. They did close early the day we went in at only 4 pm. The view itself is phenomenal however, hosting the coast in both directions as well as the occasional gray whale.

Really pretty, peaceful green space. An amazing history and some cool memorials. Definitely a necessity to check out, there isn't actually much information as to the history on it there. But there are several museums around about various aspects of the history of Lexington and Concord.

This is considered one of the most historic ballparks in the nation! And in a recent visit I saw why. Fantastic design, great experience when a game is going, and wonderful history. If your in the area it is a must see whether there is a game going or not!

Gorgeous gardens with fantastic views. I really enjoyed my time here and thought the various memorials in the park were very cool. Only complaint is that the park has got MAJOR drainage problems and it was very muddy. Even on a hot day.
Plenty of open space, some nice ponds, and a cool rec. No fish are in the ponds for anyone wondering. Though an enjoyable place to walk or play some individuals may find it boring.

TAKE A STREET CAR - to this amazing city park.  That's right get a breather from the quarter and venture out here.  Some beautiful sights about. Old trees, fantastic and as unexpected strange art.

Out here is a sculpture garden, Botanical Garden, Train Garden, Cafe Dumond, Art museum and soon to be Childrens Museum just to name a few. Along with that, a wonderful place for a picnic.

Only down side, is the park could use a few more covered spaces to protect you from the rain or a brief respite from the sun.
likes: Diverse attractions (Sculpture garden, Botanical Garden, Train Garden, Cafe, Art museum)

reviews_attraction.text:
Cannot say enough great things for Bayou Country.  Looped out here from New Orleans to let our kiddos explore.  Makes for a good day trip that the staff can blend into a full day for your rugrat.  Stop by in the morning, skooch out to lunch then come back in after that for another hour or two.  Plenty to do inside for a couple of hours then weather permitting explore a bit outside.

A local officer did a puppet show for the kids.

Awful Camp Hosts!  They are rude and arrogant. Hopefully they pick out better people for the 2018 Season.

That being said, the recreation area itself is great!  So much to do there and see.    We really do love the place. Beach area, Picnic tables, Hiking trails, fishing spots.

Make a reservation if you are camping, or the camp hosts will make you think you are stupid for even asking about availability.   Otherwise, enjoy!

Easy to find, just follow your navigation to a large open parking area that is on the edge of the state park, at the end of the road, just before the bridge.  Quite a few other stops before the water before the point within the state park that requires no entry fee.

Eagle watching is great out here! Easy walks to vistas that you can see with three sides of water surrounding you. Picnic, swim, boat and easy walks abound.

This is the spot to test the break in run for your new camper.  Large pull through spots, just far enough from town for you to pick up additional supplies for and set it up. Decent walk paths, swim beach, boating.  Campsites have fire pits with 50% of them being shaded.

Pro tip: Make sure you make a reservation during the summer, it gets pretty busy

Nice park that could use some patrols during the busy hours.

All the facilities are great and in tip top shape like the playground equipment, picnic benches and gazebos.

On the other side, had kids begging us for treats while thier moms sat around a full picnic table.

Keep a close eye on your kiddos, this park gives off a creepy vibe.

Be forewarned, you have to pay the entrance to the Botanical Gardens to enter the train garden.  Then weather permitting, this is a great place to hang out with your kiddos.  Our boys enjoyed exploring the train garden and the gentleman running the operation that day was kind enough to show them around behind the scenes.

If you are traveling skip the rest areas and stop here.  Great place to stretch your kiddos with clean bathrooms.  Lots of picnic tables and parking. It is a touch harder to get back on the freeway, but worth the stop.

The park is clean with well groomed grass that is pet friendly.

At the time of this review - COVID times, Silver is working hard to bring things back to normal, but like everything in this time, it is just a bit off of perfect.  Overlook that 25% that would have taken you to perfection and you will leave with a smile at the end of the day.

Awesome little park in town right next to Little Man Ice Cream. Well fenced from the street to keep your kiddos safe. Trash cans were full in the middle of a weekday. Playground equipment was in good shape.

Bonus - No obvious syringes lying around the playground!

What a fun place to get out and test your vehicle.  Terrain is from mild to wild depending on how much you want to push yourself and your vehicle. Bathrooms with running water available, lots of terrain to spend at least a half day meandering.

Great place to get out to for a short day trip.  Entry fee is appropriate to activity.  Lots of history is on display here with more to come.  Ride on a small train is included.  Bathrooms are clean and the staff is super.

Room to grow.  A truly macabre look at death, with some areas to improve.  Not for the faint of heart.  It truly fits into the city of New Orleans.

Interesting to see a brochure for volunteering at the local hospice.
Fun half day trip.  Good to hear some history, drinks were tasty, and friendly staff everywhere.  Band was nice to hear as we meandered our way along sipping on some select beverages.
likes: Facilities & Services: Tasty drinks, Friendly staff

reviews_attraction.text: Peaceful stop as you pass through this area and let your heathens out to run.  Bathrooms are rough, campground looks like it can be cozy but the play area and views are fantastic.
What an amazing park. Beach access with sand for your sensitive soles. Public bathroom and even some food if you hot it up at the right time of day. Lots of activities!
Great park situated just north of Moscow.  Fun place to get the kids outside and exploring. Picnic tables are spread out so you get some privacy for your day.
Fun park!  Folks love to Frisbee golf, so even in the middle of winter there are people here.  There are some fields for the kiddos and a few gazebos as well.
Tasty drinks. But it seemed like a bartender broke a glass over the ice bin and did not clean up the mess very well. I suppose I'll risk it again sometime
An anchor park for the City of Post Falls.  Great tree cover, lots of picnic tables and it is right on the river.  Clean bathrooms and park grounds.
Easy walk up from the car with some great photographic moments.  Not too crowded when we stopped, which made for great picture opportunities.
Fun ride for a 4-5 year old!  Kids love it for all 50 seconds... Good thing we were fortunate enough to use a Fast Pass on it.
Beautiful park in the middle of town!  Great for families as it is pretty far away from traffic and fairly flat.
So much to this park that is tucked away past the hillside.  A great stop as you come through this area.
Great park in central Denver. Walk close by for the Zoo and Museum. You could easily be here all day.

Look, I'm as red blooded American as your gun toting neighbor with the fading Romney bumper sticker on his battered pickup, but the American Pavilion is a mockery of the USA and volatile history our young country boasts.  From the massive 5 story building masked by three stories of oversized windows and doors,  to the joke of a summation of the history of our states and the good and bad we've committed  as we molded this experiment of democracy.  Considering the number of foreign visitors to EPCOT, it would have been nice to have a better defined slice of American life and lore than this embarrassment.  One star given to the robotic stars of the history presentation; they do hold up to the test of time.

Incredible, immersive park area that goes above and beyond the best of Disney.  Working close with JK Rowling and original film set designers, Universal Studios spared no expense in recreating one of the most memorable film locations in recent history.  Kids and adults will love exploring all the nooks and crannies of the alley.  The shops, bars, and inns are all represented.  Gringots Bank hosts a 3D motion ride based upon the seventh film.  If you purchase a wand from one of the shops located here or in Islands of Adventure's Hogsmead, you can interact with many of the props and displays throughout Diagon Alley.  Be sure to hunt for unmarked hidden "magic items" your wand will also interact with.....

An excellent sample of an African safari for the many of us who will never get the opportunity or funding for such a venture. The "ride" utilizes real diesel trucks to take you out in the savannas, forests, and river ecosystems across the African continent. You will see crowd favourites like the elephants, lions, and giraffes, but also endangered gazelles, wildebeest, and other less know species. Early morning and 17:45 in the evening gives you the most animal activity.  Truly the crown jewel of Disney's Animal Kingdom.

PS: Go on it again at night.  The animals move into defensive resting herds groups and the predators wake up to hunt.

The world's premiere outdoor concert venue, crafted by mother earth over millions of years.  Words do this place no justice...just go.  Even if you cannot come for a concert, the whole area is a park and open daily to the public.  Many of Denver's citizens use it for a fitness playground, with it's extensive staircases and sun kissed, wide seating areas perfect for exercise.  In fact they offer seasonal yoga classes along with other community activities.  The summer season offers classic film showings in the evening.  Be sure to tour the Visitor's Center and take in the Denver skyline from row 55.

Wonderful state park area smack dab between North America's two greatest waterfalls.  Currently undergoing renovations with the visitor's center and Cave of the Winds ticket booth, the overall park area is still very accommodating.  Don't forget the fact you can view both the American/Bridal Veil Falls as well as the Horseshoe Falls right from the edge.  Check out the monument to Tesla and his immense contribution to the area and civilization in general.

Unique setting brings a 18 degree Fahrenheit bar to the hot climate of Orlando.  The Fire bar has an Euro techno feel, and oddly enough good tapas style food.  The actual ice bar is a frozen club where even the glasses are made of ice.  The interior changes with new sculptures and furniture carved from ice.  A unique experience through and through.

Jackets are provided with admission, with an up charge  for faux fur "pimp coats."

Quite a bit of the ship is accessible, in this unique glimpse of history and this pinnacle of the military industrial complex. The ship was empty when I came (afternoon on a school day Monday) and still took 2.5 goes to traverse.  Though smaller than the Iowa class warships on display throughout the country, the North Carolina gives you more views of the life and mechanics of such an incredible vessel.

Part of a series of coastal parks with beaches, Little Talbot strikes a great balance between natural and accessible development.  Less known than it's larger brother just north, Little Talbot has a more traditional beach. There are pavilions with charcoal grilles, restrooms, changing rooms, and outdoor showers.  Bike and walking trails wrap through the island park.  A great place to spend the day.

Massive cybernetic organisms made real by massive 4k, 3D projections.  Enter the kinetic world of Michael Bay with this thrilling motion ride that puts you in the heat of battle between Decepticons and NEST's Autobots.  Utilizing the original voices, the intricate CGI renders of the robots, and cast members from the films, this is as close as we will get to a world of waring robots.

With its subdued cultural nature, the Japan Pavilion is a breath of fresh air compared to most of the World Showcase.  The staff is friendly and refined, and the main restaurant serves premium Japanese inspired cuisine (at premium prices).  Throughout the year the pavilion celebrates different Japanese holidays and events with ceremonies and entertainment acts.

One of the most unique parks in the country, complete with sandy key beaches, a lagoon, green hiking spaces, air conditioned nature lodge, and a part of the historical Flagler bridge system.  There are camp sites with cabins, RV space, tent space, and even a marina.  Full bathroom and shower facilities, and a food booth.  A must see place.

A hidden gem of the Florida coastline.  A rocky beach continually carved out by the Atlantic causing incoming tide to blast through natural blow holes.  Combined with the dense vegetation, large crabs, rare birds, and other ecological marvels makes this a beach completely removed from what one expects in Florida.

An extensive look at the history of the region, from prehistoric times to early civilization to the explosion of culture in the 20th century. Housed in the former Orange County Court House, the eras are laid out in unique modern exhibits. This is a fun, inexpensive activity for both tourists and locals alike.

If the safari next door is the crown jewel of Disney's Animal Kingdom, this takes second place.  Originally called Gorilla Falls (and some signs still show this nomenclature), this is a half mile shaded walk through showcasing duikers, okapis, a meerkat clan, gorillas, and more.  Well worth your time.

An aging ride, but with so much going for it.  A great concept, well fitting in the world of Jurassic Park. A video presentation by the late Sir Richard Attenborough! But I can't give it five stars when the robotic dinosaurs are failing, or in the case of one...entirely missing.

A dark "hidden" area of Harry Potter's Diagon Alley that faithfully replicates the more sinister shops of the wizardry world.  Complete with a faux foreboding night sky and unique places to test your wand spells, one must give props to the designers of this park experience.

Fantastic scenic walk on a closed down parkway that leads to numerous dinosaur fossils and track sites, all viewable from the trail.  You also have spectacular views of Red Rocks and Denver.  There is a guided bus tour available at either visitor's centre.

Once you get through the kitschy history of American farming and ecosystems robots, you will be treated to a showcase of cutting edge farming techniques and technology actually used by the park to feed its patrons.  Well worth the journey.

This charming little neighborhood park is both a community art project and a tribute to the power substation that was once operated on the property.  Though small, the park's unique sights make this a great place to visit or hang out.

Spectacular nature park with extensive hiking trails across great expanses of wilderness and upon the glacier ice.  Be prepared for a day of rough hiking and incredible views.  A real gem of an area near Idaho Springs.

Nice strip of land across from "downtown" Winter Park.  Numerous weekly and avian events are held here, including the farmer's market.  Plenty of parking and a Sunrail train station makes it easy to access.

Any well maintained city green space is worth five stars, but Lake Highland Park also boats great views of the Orlando skyline. If your boat is small enough to carry, a fun place to lazy the day away.
Wonderful local park on the top of the mountain.  Hiking trails, a small restaurant, store, and the grave & museum of Buffalo Bill.  Incredible views of the Rockies and Denver.
Run down house covered in beer cans inside and out, in the middle of a swanky part of town.  Bet the neighbors hate it.  Free to see the outside, pay to get inside.
Incredible modern ride experience involving 3D immersion screens, moving truck, and live action animalectronics.  Definitely a must for park visitors.

Overall a great time. We hit the park on Grad Bash... Very cool event for graduating high school seniors. You should know that this will close the park to regular patrons about 3 hrs early. (Not a big deal if you plan on it) The part that made our day less then optimal was it also closes a sizable chunk of CityWalk to the general public. Some restaurants are simply not available. Those that are will tell you the wait line for a table is 10-20min... We waited 40+ before being told it would be an additional 40+ before we could even be seated. Other patrons said it was taking 45min to well over an hour after sitting down to get their meals. Unless you're involved in gradbash or simply can't visit at another time don't come then.

Also be aware that you can't ride the rides most of the time without locking your belongings in a locker. Some rides the locker is free... Small (can hold a cell phone jacket and maybe some very small park swag) but usefull. The medium to large are for a fee. There are also specific rides where the only way to get a locker is to pay. After $$ for park tickets $$ for hotel and express passes it's a real kick in the shins to have to shell out even more for a locker to ride rides you've already paid for....
dislikes: Mandatory paid lockers for some rides

reviews_attraction.text:
Bit of a hike... The road is a fun adventure of a drive. The pools are surreal, tranquil and perched on the edge of the mighty Pacific ocean. So don't be stupid. Check the tide charts. Low tide is best. A big high tide and you might find you'd self in trouble. Watch the surf. If it's big be smart.

Last little bit of helpful warning. Don't poke around the really cool olivine encrusted rocks to much. Teh ones that look like they are full of holes make great critter homes. (Sometimes really angry critters with wings and stingers...)

So I should say bad things to keep people away... But that would be dishonest. We visit in the winter when most of the camp and picknick areas are closed. There is great snowshoeing and cross country skiing to be had. With little to no crowds. Keep in mind if you get lost back here there is a minimal number of other folks around... And really no cell service. Be smart tell someone where your going and when you'll be back. Roads are not well traveled and can get slick unexpectedly.

Yeah so this is an odd one... Historically this is one of the site's where the US manufactured triggers for nuclear weapons. Now after a stint as a Superfund cleanup site the land has been dedicated back to nature. The history here is rich and haunting. It's worth a brief visit but there is not much to see and they actually limit you time.

Absolutely love this section of Epcot. Bittersweet that WDW is now the primary owner. The old school vibe was spectacular with a very refined unique take on dining. One of our all-time favorites, we will have to see how the transition goes. At our most recent visit the section was closed for a paint job and face lift. Fingers crossed.

Grab a daily rental bike in the hot summer time there is a station at the spray park on the west side... Or if your in Iowa on the east side tucked under the bridge. Lewis and Clark landing in Nebraska is a find and a great stop. The massive park on the east side is great for large get together and a lazy day enjoying the river.

Shhhh don't tell anyone how nice it is here.... Huge beautiful vistas. The fishing is apparently top in the nation... I won't disagree that there are big fish here. I will add that I have never tried to catch a more finicky lot... Being lots of options if fishing is your game and be ready to share the waters.

Spectacular! Busy mid day but very manageable. The wand fitting show is worth the extra 5min of your day. If you want to dive right in wands can be bought online or in your resort gift shop as well as at other shops through out the park. If you get in early do breakfast in at the leaky cauldron.

Really cool experience, the tour is a must. Currently remodeling the team USA store and Visitors center. Will be spectacular when its done. They are still open now but many of the exhibits have been moved or are under construction. Might want to call ahead to see where they are at.

If you like trains then you must pay this place a visit. They run a small scale model in the basement a lager steam model on the main grounds and then they run the real thing on the weekends. The special events are well worth it from day out with Thomas to Polar Express...

Amazing place to go if your from out of town... Even better if you live here. The rotating exhibits are spectacular. Concerts in the summer are great. Wonderful cafe and endless opportunities to get lost in nature while being in the center of an urban landscape.

Wonderful park, lived here all my life and some how missed this one. A few areas are closed for flood restoration but the out buildings are all open and the trails are in great shape. Oh and if your lucky you might snag a little fish or two.

Limited facility but overall very nice. Ramp and docks are in good condition. There is limited space and the channel is tight just off the ramp. Mind the markers with winter low tides or you'll run out of water fast.

Nice boat ramp. Long run to the beaches however. Plan accordingly. There is a small marina about 1/4 of the way out with some basic service and a restaurant, gas and occasionally live bait. $5 parking fee required.

Great little park.... Though... We do call it goose poop park. Yup not a typo. The rather large group of year-round Canadian geese, though friendly tend to leave a little more behind than you'd expect.

The state park system in Florida is great. Concession stands, equipment rental, friendly and knowledge staff. If they'd let me is live there.  Great boat launch with good parking and a very nice dock.
Great, relatively secret spot for a wonderful hike. The area is rentable for special events. Bring a picnic or a fishing rod. Great camping spots with tent pads or pull ins for trailers.
Must see if you live her or are traveling through. Go to a show. Any show. Come do yoga in the morning or run the stairs.  Make sure you visit the visitors center and get the tour!
Very well done micro national park site. If you in Omaha and downtown you MUST come check this out. The park staff is great. Super helpful and friendly.
Great state park! Clean and super helpful staff. Plenty of space for everyone and a beautiful environment to spend a day hunting shells along the beach.
Simply WOW! If you don't go here you are seriously missing out on one of the best botanical gardens our country has to offer.    Yes it is that good.
Quiet little park with a launch. Good facilities for a picknic and grilling. Small fish cleaning station. Overall very clean and well maintained.
Wonderful peaceful bit of nature tucked into an urban setting. Worth the visit. Lots of trails for biking and hiking. Good watersports as well.
Nicely kept little piece of paradise just 20 min from the metro area. Can be an bit crowded from time to time but week days are great!
Wonderful staff and a great state park so close to home. Tons of trails and camping. The visiting center is a must see.

Great for walks and even better for relaxing on the dunes or beach, with a view of the Lake Michigan coastline.

From the parking lot there is a wooded trail that goes up and over the dunes and down to the beach. The trail splits off in several spots, making it great for walks/runs. Once you reach the beach, there is plenty of space to set up for swimming. There is also plenty of little trails that go up and down the dunes, along the beach, that provide excellent photo opportunities.

Although our group doesnt disc, the park also has a pretty nice disc golf course at the entrance.

The only con to the park seems to be a small lack of maintenance on the trails and beach, both are a little less cleaned up than other beaches in the area (PJ Hoffmaster, Muskegon State park, etc).

To start off, there really needs to be a minimum age to ride the bus through the trails. There is a little off roading and its MUCH too bumpy for small children. A couple on our trip had a really difficult and semi scary time trying to hold their infants head still while going through the trails. There is also a moment where the bus stops inside a building that smokes out with no air conditioning, which caused all of the children to start coughing.

With that said, I still give it a five star review. It was a very fun and entertaining little thing to do while on vacation. Alot of effort is put into behind the scenes work to keep the ride fun, my niece and nephew both genuinely believed bigfoot was near.

My family used to visit Duck Lake every summer growing up, and now as an adult I always make a point to stop out a few times each year. The beach and dunes stretch along the coast as far as you can see, with plenty of spots to set up for the day, whether it be towels on the beach or hammocks up in the dunes. Every year the beach on the Lake Michigan side changes, so it's always a cool little surprise to see what the beach is like after the snow melts.
On busy days the parking lot fills quick and often times people park along the road, so be prepared for that.

Boat launch, picnic area, and beach are always well maintained, very much recommended.

Easy walk to an absolutely beautiful Waterfall. We took the Gorge trail from Inspiration Point, past the upper falls, and to the portage bridge and back. The views of the Upper Falls and surrounding scenery along the way are amazing. We found this to be one of the more busy paths and the view points stayed a bit crowded for the most part; if you can get past that, its well worth the walk.

Highly recommended.

Nice little park with several fields (baseball & soccer) on one side, and an outdoor park and volleyball court on the other. There are two parking lots, one for each side, so be sure to map to the correct one. There are plenty of covered picnic tables near the playground for lunch, and a loop of walking trails on the back side of the park. The public bathrooms are also usually well maintained.

Lots of trails throughout the park that offer great views of the city and pikes peak. The late hours make it great for sunset and night hikes as well as day hikes. Lots of rock formations that offer natural seating, and the park has a very peaceful setting, perfect for picnics. Animals are allowed as well, and there is a fenced in animal park along the trail.

Great little park for just about everything. Theres a large handful of picnic tables with a couple grills under a gazebo right at the entrance. Small hiking trail, seperate running trail, as well as a paved bike path next to the river. Beach at the end of the running trail. Some pretty good views, great for pictures.

Always very well maintained. Lots and lots of parking, shaded picnic area,  and beach that spans a long distance. There's also bathrooms, vending machines, and a spot to wash off near the parking lot. Plenty of dunes to climb in both directions; our favorite spot is at the top with a great view of lake Michigan.

Nice little set of trails; lots of paths to cut through to change things up. Paths are well maintained; mowed and cleared of branches regularly, but are not paved and are not wheelchair/ stroller accessible. Many view points/ benches along the way. Highly recommended for anyone looking for a light nature trail.

If you're visiting Chicago, the Museum Campus should be one of the first places you visit. Make sure to plan a full day or more and get to the museums early. The museums are well put together, have many articles, and take quite a bit of time to look through. Buy tickets online to save some time and $$.

Visiting NOLA without seeing City Park would be a mistake. Set aside a full day or more, it's worth it. The sculpture park, art museum, and much more. Perfect place for all ages. Plenty of spots for grilling and the park is also set up for biking. Well worth the money for the things that do cost.

An experience you wont want to miss. You can tour both the museum and lighthouse, which has tons of historic items and some pretty cool stories. Great for families or couples on a trip. There is also a viewing deck over lake michigan that makes for great pictures of the lake shore and lighthouse.

Nice little park with 2.5 miles of well maintained paved trails. There are benches and trail markers showing distance along the way, as well as pet stations and  several wheelchair accessible observation decks. There are also trails outside of the parks 2.5 mile paved trail for longer walks.

This iconic fountain is a must see when visiting Chicago; both day and night. During summer there are events, such as the switch on event when the fountain is actually turned on for the season. Outside of events, the fountain is a very nice and peaceful area to relax while enjoying the city.

Great place to walk or run and take in the city. Beautiful slice of nature right in the city with amazing views of Chicago architecture. There are kyak and other boat rentals right off of the riverwalk, as well as many resturaunts and businesses in the nearby area to stop at along the way.

Absolutely beautiful. The pictures taken from here are post card worthy. Very easy to get to on a well traveled path. If you visit mackinac island make sure to make the small trip over and stop for pictures. Our group walked, but biking or getting a ride over on the tram are also options.

Nice little set of trails with many benches along the way. I would say the trail is of moderate difficulty, terrain wise; but on the lighter side of moderate on the inner loop. The outside loop is around 3 miles, and the inside loop is around a mile total. Well worth the visit.

Very much a must see. Be sure to put away more than just a couple hours for this museum. One of my favorites along with the Smithsonian. There are many, many authentic displays that show stories, rather than just a bit of general information. Highly recommended.

A++ bear sanctuary. Great for all groups; families, couples, and solo travelers. If you're in the area and dont stop at Oswalds, you're missing out. Everytime we go to the UP we try to stop at the ranch.
Absolutely beautiful views at both locations, the upper falls is more popular. The park itself is also beautiful and well kept. One of the more picture worthy spots in the Michigan U.P.
Great little view point overlooking the start of the mountains and the city of Golden and Denver in the distance. We stopped to have lunch with a view and were not disappointed.
One of the many beautiful scenic stops in Canyonlands National Park. Not as busy as you'd expect for being such a short walk to such a great view overlooking the canyon.
Short half mile round trip walk thats worth the stop. As a warning, the arch is very busy and families like to take it over for photo sessions.
Easy hike to a stunning view of the city with peaks peak in the background. The rock formation itself is also something worth not missing.
Unfortunately we didn't get to go into the arch because of the government shutdown. It was very much still worth the visit.

This is a pretty interesting and educational museum on all sorts of medicinal, historical, and scientific information. It did feel a little underwhelming but it has enough to keep you entertained for a couple of hours, nothing too out of the ordinary here. Wouldn't really recommend it for kids as it doesn't have too much for them but if you're studying or practicing in the medical field, you will have a lot of fun here. Also, the admissions office can easily be skipped here as there is no one that works here that checks if you actually paid to get in or not so I don't know how they overlooked that here.

The Hemingway Museum is spectacular and has been very nicely preserved throughout the years. The museum has a lot of great and interesting bits of information about Hemingway himself, being displayed in a very orderly manner. There are free tours here as well and our tour guide Sarah was great and did an excellent job. There are also plenty of cats roaming the property, some with six-toes,  that are very friendly so cat-lovers will heavily enjoy coming here. You MUST come here if you come to Key West as we had a lot of fun.

The gift shop here is really nice and so are the views from the top of the mountain. You can see all of Golden from here but the best part about this place is the fudge and the hot chocolate. This is easily the best fudge and hot chocolate that I have ever had. The drive to the top of this mountain is worth it for the fudge alone, as it is all house-made. Keep up the good work, as the quality in the food and drinks were phenomenal. This place is definitely a strong recommendation from me.

This zoo is much better than the Miami Zoo.  Unlike the one in Miami, this one actually has shade throughout the park, making sure you're not walking directly under the hot sun. There's not too many large exhibits so don't expect any elephants or lions but the ones they have are great and focuses more on the smaller animals in the world. The restaurant in the back of the zoo is overpriced and you should bring your own food. I highly recommend this place.

An absolutely beautiful monument that most people will never have heard of in Miami. The Vizcaya is amazing with a heavy emphasis on European design and architecture. You will honestly feel as if you are in Europe once you're here and think you're in Versailles. You also won't find a better photography spot than here. I would skip Miami Beach and just come here instead. Plus, they filmed parts of Iron Man 3 here.  I highly recommend.

A pretty cool museum dedicated to Key West's history but the main standout point is Robert the Doll. Besides Robert, the museum has a lot of other Civil War-era displays and exhibits that everyone should love. Just don't go in October as they move Robert to another museum in Key West.  Plus, its far away from most of the other tourist spots and isn't as packed.

One of the very few beaches in Key West, it is pretty nice here. Since it is man-made, there is more gravel in the sand than most other beaches but the park itself is well maintained and also has an old Civil War fort. There is an entry fee but it is worth it to help preserve these areas that are operated by the National Park Service.

This is easily among the most beautiful parks that I have been to in the country and the hiking trails are relatively short, making it accessible to everyone. It is also entirely free, making this park a must-go place in Colorado Springs. I'd definitely recommend this place, especially for fans of mountain climbing and hiking.
likes: Suitable for hiking and mountain climbing

reviews_attraction.text: One of the many things representing Chicago and it is simply amazing. Underneath the Bean, it looks really cool and the odd architecture makes it look very trippy and makes for a cool photo op. Its free and there's no line to take pictures so check it out as you can't say you've been to Chicago without coming here.

What a beautiful landmark in the country's oldest city. They have not commercialized it and it stands out in such a great way without being ruined by tourist attractions. You're free to walk around the castle at night as well. If you visit St. Augustine, this place should definitely be visited.

A beautiful park with amazing views and fun trails that anyone can do. The mountain itself isn't very high but is still very fun to hike up. Parking is fairly limited. I'd recommend going around the evening, the views from the top at night is phenomenal. Definitely worth a visit.

This is a really fun experience in Ft. Lauderdale. I would highly recommend as the boat does a good tour of the city, explaining what everything is. At the end, you get to an island where they have an alligator show with very talented people. A must see.

A gorgeous swimming pool located in the heart of Miami. This is regarded as one of the greatest swimming pools in the world and for a good reason. All of the water is naturally cycled and filtered which makes for a great experience.

This is a signature building of Chicago that must be visited if you are in the city. Even if you don't watch a game, seeing the scores from the outside of the building along with Cub's fans, is really fun. Definitely worth a visit!

During the day, this park is great and well-kept. However at night, there are a fair amount of homeless people hanging around here, some of them talking to themselves. Nice place but I'd avoid at night.
Pretty interesting place that is worth a visit. A lot of weird things but the best part is the spinning tunnel at the end and the 2-way mirror. Those alone were worth the admission.
An interesting piece of Civil War history that should definitely be seen if you're going to the beach. Not a very large fort so don't expect too much but its been well preserved.
What a beautiful park with all of south Florida's wildlife congregated into one area. Admission is only $5 and is worth it for the nature center, fishing, kayaking and hiking.
Its the beginning of the most famous road in the US, whats not to love about it? Go check it out and start walking as it ends all the way in Santa Monica, California.
If you're in Key West, you have got to check out the local monument. There is usually a line but takes no more than 15 minutes to take a picture. Worth every shot.
The Seven Mile Bridge is beautiful and makes for a great photo shoot.  If you have time, they do private boat tours out to Pigeon Key and it looks really cool.
Homeless guy attacked me here, saying he was the 2nd born of Castro, but a mcdonalds employee saved me. Wouldnt recommend but theres a nice bench here.
There's a reason why this place is called the Sunset Pier. If you visit Key West, you have to come here to view the sunset at least once.
Cool view at the top of the city and is another museum in a city chock full of them. Admission was high but worth at least one trip.
Not much to see here, just a free little art gallery in one of Chicago's oldest buildings. Worth a check if you're passing by it.

Nice escape from the normal beaches with skeletal trees littering the beach and slowly eroding away. Connects to the other trailheads and beaches of Big Talbot Island via the paved Timacuan Pathway. Entrance fee is $3 per vehicle and on the honor system. The Shoreline Access Trail is a 0.3 mile sandy and flat trail through the woods out to the boneyard beach and bluffs.

Resting place of Buffalo Bill atop Lookout Mountain. Great views can be had here, but it was foggy with zero visibility during our trip. The museum charges an entrance fee but the store and fudge/snack shop along with the gravesite and rest of the grounds are free to visit. Large parking lot can accommodate buses and other large vehicles.
dislikes: Foggy conditions (Note: This is about the weather, but included here as per the review's focus; normally, it should be excluded based on the given criteria)

reviews_attraction.text: Great state park with lots of history and hiking. For a small fee you can enter the park to visit the deserted beach or enjoy wildlife at the marsh or on the trails. Bring some extra money to access the fort or buy souvenirs at the gift shop. The pier was a wonderful place to spot marine wildlife like sea turtles or dolphins.

Beautiful area to explore with multiple waterfalls of all sizes, hiking trails, and historical info. Trails are wide and usually not too steep, with flat observation areas for the best views of the falls. Nice Visitor Center with historical info about the area and public restrooms right off the highway with plenty of parking.

A quiet loop trail just over 2 miles long that follows Sims Creek, sneaks under the Blue Ridge Parkway, and wraps around a meadow. Parking and access to the trail is available both ends at the Sims Pond and Sims Creek Overlook. Though I've not encountered them, a wise person told me to "beware of bulls in the pasture."

It's just a short, mostly flat walk under half a mile to the waterfalls viewing platform. The path is wide and mostly dirt/small gravel and the falls are beautiful. Lots of flow after a lot of recent rain but the trail was in good shape with some mud near the falls. There's a gravel lot off the main road for parking

Nice state park with amazing sunrises and sunsets and great beach access along the Nassau Sound. Restrooms were clean and the entry fee is not too expensive. Good fishing there off the the George Crady Bridge. I can see the small paved parking lot filling up quickly and you probably need 4WD to drive on the beach.

Great place to just hang out and relax. Calm waters along the inlet allow for easy snorkeling for younger or inexperienced swimmers. There's a good selection of sealife including large angelfish and eels to be seen, plus you may get buzzed by a manatee swimming in from the inlet. Plenty of parking and restrooms

Huge park with lots to do: around 10 miles of hiking or mountain biking, fishing, volleyball, playgrounds, ball fields, and a dog park. There's a bike-share with great trails of various lengths and difficulties. Many restrooms scattered about and a nice, easily-accessible place to get into nature for a bit.

Nice park in heart of downtown Asheville, with a small stage and restroom building. Close walking distance to many shops, restaurants, offices, and the YMCA. There are parking sports on the nearby streets and also a large covered garage right across from the park, with decent hourly and special event rates.

Hiking along the Linville River in the gorge or along the mountain ridgelines high above, there are amazing views and adventures to be had. Waterfalls, swimming holes, nature's beauty, and plenty of wildlife. There's camping and the Mountains to Sea Trail in what some call the Grand Canyon of the east

Only a few spots for parking and they will fill up quickly on nice days. Trail is rocky and is a flowing stream after heavy rains. Tough hike up to the top of Shortoff Mountain but well worth it for the views of the Linville Gorge and Table Rock. Connects to the MST and access to the Gorge loop

Great views of Grandfather Mountain one way and the Linville Gorge the other. A short uphill hike from the parking lot leads you to the smooth rock face which is great for a relaxing picnic or some stargazing. And it's large enough you can space out if there are a bunch of people up there

Free visitor center with great information about the area and educational activities for adults and children. There are short walking trails and also a drive through the preserve that cost a few dollars, but offer scenic overlooks and stops to observe the surrounding nature and wildlife.

Small park with picnic areas, waterfall, and a water mill just outside of downtown Valdese. Plenty of parking, decent restrooms, and a pavilion for rent. The walk to the top of the falls is easily accessible and short while going to the bottom is a little steeper down a gravel path.
likes: Easily accessible walk to the top of the falls
dislikes: Steeper gravel path to the bottom

reviews_attraction.text: Friendly and informative tour guides with nice customer service. The tour is around a half hour but a good overview of the cavern system there. Large gift shop with many local crafts and items. Picnic tables along the Linville River are great for lunches when the weather is nice.

Awesome boardwalk in Ft. Myers. Easily accessed and a small parking fee thtat pays for the great maintenance of the park. Good restrooms, benches along the boardwalk for resting, and wildlife. We actually didn't see any Gators on our visit but we did run into a raccoon.

Drove up on a warm mid March afternoon but the park was still closed for the season. Great views of Boone and surrounding areas from the top, but parking can be scarce during busy times in nicer weather. Worth the short drive up when in the area for the views alone

Great history of the Waldensians in Valdese. You watch a video then walk through the trail listening to their histories and stories as you tour. There is an outside amphitheatre where they host a drama in the summer that should not be missed
Amazing lighthouse on the eastern tip of Sanibel Island. Unfortunately you can't climb this one. Pier and beach access all around, with paid parking for a small rate.
Nice beaches, a cool bridge, clean facilities, camping sites. A great place to stay the weekend or spend a quick stop for a picnic when  driving through the Keys.
This mirrored bean-shaped landmark is an interesting piece of design art. Plus this is a great place for views of the Chicago skyline.
Convenient to downtown Hudson, the greenway, and 321, lots of room for the kids to run and play and frisbee golf for the adults.
Nice park with trail around the lake and good facilities. Even though here are a lot of spots, parking can be tough on nice days
Nice short walk from parking lot but it can fill up quick, which leads to parking alongside the dirt road.

As a local, this is my go-to area during the summer and winter. The cost of entrance is only a few dollars. The park is relatively large includes picnic tables, barbeque grill area, fishing area, boat ramp, kayak and paddle board rentals and much more. It is also walking distance to Dania pier and Quarterdeck.

If you enjoy snorkeling and the water is flat, easy way to check water conditions ahead of time is by looking at the Dania Beach Pier Camera. I suggest checking out the Dania Jax, an artificial reef located at the inside the park between Dania pier and the first parking lot.
The reef starts about 500 feet offshore depending on water conditions, and a dive flag is required. The artificial reef stretches for about 1500 feet until it touches the first reef.
Please help protect Florida marine life don't touch the reefs or leave anything behind on the beaches.
We have seen, turtles, eels, nurse sharks, tons of fish, stingrays and manta rays at this location and much more.
likes: Diverse facilities (picnic, BBQ, fishing, boat ramp)

reviews_attraction.text:
If you have not guessed it already, shark valley does not have any sharks.. my first advice would be arrive early because parking lot is small for the crowd it attracts. The second advice is bring water and sunblock. Thier is no shade. You could walk, bike(rentals are available ) or take the tram. if you do take uber here remember that's it's located in the middle of nowhere so getting a ride bike if arrangements are not made going to be hard..

Because it's got poor data service I suggest downloading google maps area.

If you walking it's a long walk! Bring water,

My advice for park is maybe have more benches available with shade along the path if possible.

Better maintenance on bathrooms would be nice too

I loved the park and would come here again.

You $25 park fee is good for 7 days

This is a nice little park with some wildlife. It's got a long Loop for biking or rollerblading. The road is newly paved, the park also has plenty of trails. Being this close to the water I would recommend long sleeves and pans unless you want the mosquitoes attacking you. The park offers paddle board rentals jet ski rentals and kayak rentals. The restaurant in the park offers drink and snack options.
likes: Water activities (paddle board, jet ski, kayak rentals)

reviews_attraction.text: Great location for a quick dive or for snorkeling,  if your snorkeling plan to spend about 1 hour here. The water feels cold because the spring does not get sunlight,  I recommend bringing a wetsuit or renting a wetsuit. During rainy days the spring is more cloudy. If you have a underwater flashlight bring it. Visitors are not allowed into the cave without snorkeling or dive gear.

Visited the park in January, The sunset from the mountain was amazing. We did see deer and elk. The restrooms are rustic but clean around the park.  I would suggest coming with a full tank of gas and bring food and water since you could easily spend the whole day hiking and driving. Hidden Valley has a little area for sledding and a clear path that people ski. Park map is below

I enjoyed this place very much, I found a great Groupon deal online. The staff had been very friendly. I like the open concept for the zoo. I think very kid friendly. The place looked in good maintenance. I did watch the show they had at 1pm and found it enjoyable. I did not have the opportunity too try the food offered. I would visit again.

I have been coming to Brooklyn botanical gardens for years. Once your inside the gardens the people and atmosphere is more relaxing. The staff are always friendly and helpful. The park stays clean. Would highly recommend this park. I also recommend Tom's a few blocks away for nice quick breakfast or lunch.

We had a great experience here it's a 50-acre property with plenty of paths and goes near the lake. We had found this Garden on a rainy day. The fee for adults is $10 and for kids for 4-17 is $5. The park also does offer discounts for high school students. Check out their website about special offers.

The light has offers a really amazing view, its a narrow walk up the stairs. The walk is worth the view. I would suggest coming up the lighthouse when the park is not super busy they normally only let 10 people up at a time. The area around lighthouse makes for some amazing photos.

This a little hidden gem of a park, They have kayak rentals, volleyball court, basketball court, tennis court, handball court. They have great paths for walking or jogging; the park is dog-friendly. During the weekend a lot of families do picnics and birthday parties.

This is a nice little park at Dania Beach Boulevard near the casino. The park has a decent playground for kids, it also has batting cages a skateboard ramp section. Along with mini workout stations. There are drinking fountains and bathrooms available as well.

Great location for a swim,  the water is beautiful. We normally park at KP hole a few miles down river and paddle towards the head of the spring. Its awesome to than drift down the river in kayak or SUP. Lots of fish, birds and turtles.

A local hidden park, offers a great boat lunch area, along with a nice observation tower, fishing area bathrooms, Its nice and quite perfect for  walk around and relax, they also have a local rowing club located inside the park.

I like K.P because it's got a clean boat ramp. I could park in the outside parking lot and stay on the river as long as I want. I always found the people friendly here. You could rent both kayaks and tubing here too.

This park was such a great find!! The staff and volunteers are A class.  its really a wonderful experience.  Its not a zoo but people who seem to really care about the local wildlife! i would visit again for sure!

It's a great education center on the beach. The staff are amazing and loaded with information about turtles and local marine life. The entree is free and if you enjoyed your visit I do recommend donating.
I spent about 2 hrs driving and walking thru this forest. It's pretty rural location and the park entrance works on a trust concept. I would come here again for sure during the summer
I like the park, has lots of areas to park. On the weekend people do birthday parties and grill. It's really not expensive considering how much space you have here.
Offers a few different areas for lunching your boat.  The location also had a kayak rental vendor. The place was clean during day. Easy access to sunrise.
Free pier, however bathrooms are in poor repair,  the pair has seen better days, I would suggest for city to keep better repair on pier and bathrooms.
The signs for overlook are a little misleading and its easy to pass it. We actually passed it the first time. Its always cool to see wildlife.
Had a great time here did a little snorkeling using Nemo battery powered hookah from BlU3. Becarful when anchoring ⚓ so not to harm the reef.
A great park for walking,  running and hiking.  A large park with endless trails with some elevation going through the woods.
The elk refuge is beautiful during the winter, if your staying in jacksonhole drive around the area for beautiful wildlife.
Very nice park in Hollywood, free parking. On the boardwalk if you look at the trees you'll notice the small crabs

We did a self-guided tour of the observatory site during the day, then a Special Viewing Night (SVN) of the 36" telescope.  The site itself is fairly spread out so you will drive to the different domes, but there are informative markers throughout.  Right now the enormous HET telescope is being upgraded.  You can still go inside and see it, though. There are a few hiking trails around but the telescopes are the obvious draw for most people.  The SVN was capped at just 10 participants plus your astronomer guide. Our evening started on time at 7:30pm, but the clouds were getting thicker.  We were shuttled up to the 36" dome anyway, and everyone sat inside on folder chairs placed along the inside wall.  It was cramped but not uncomfortable.  Our astronomer managed to find a few objects to look through between clouds. He offered to extend the program by an hour (to 4 hours), to which we all agreed. Thankfully the clouds started to dissipate and we were able to view about a dozen objects. Unlike the larger two scopes this one still has an optical eyepiece so it was neat to step up to it each time.  I was a little less than impressed with the sights, though. They weren't what I would call 'awe inspiring'. I am not an astronomer, even an amateur one, so perhaps I just couldn't appreciate what we were seeing.  I suspect our guide used the powerful scope to see objects are too faint with a small backyard scope in order to impress the knowledgeable ones in our group, but too me most of them looked like regular stars.  I was able to see a nebula and a star cluster, which looked neat.  Overall I'm still very glad I went, and it was worth the money ($65/pp). Next time I'll try a star party for greater variety.

The "no nudity" sign in the restroom surprised me. Is this something that you normally need to tell people?
Paid $3 to park and $5/person (honor system) to enter. I felt that was a little high for what was a simple park with a handful of monuments, but then again all parks need our help and I probably would have donated that anyway.  I was also surprised they prohibit picnicking - it would be a great place to enjoy a snack.  The perimeter walkway wasn't entirely fenced, which contributed to the amazing views but made it a little more precarious with two toddlers.  Otherwise, it's an attractive park with interesting Civil War monuments and worth a visit, if only for the views.

There isn't another Texas state park like this one. The draw for most folks is the large area of "active" (e.g. unvegetated) sand dunes. The visitor's center rents out plastic snow sledding discs for $2.5/2hrs, and gives you a small block of wax, and you can slide down the dunes just like it were snow. Well, almost - you really need to put lots of wax on to help, and only the steepest dune faces work. But just like snow you will find yourself huffing and puffing to walk back up the hill to do it all over again. DO NOT FORGET sunglasses, sunblock, hat, and water. It's easy to get disoriented in the dunes; we heard some real horror stores from the rangers.
dislikes: Steep dune faces required for sledding

reviews_attraction.text: Six stars! This is not a huge zoo, and not really in the typical sense with large outdoor animals. It is billed as an "invertebrate zoo", so it focuses on insects but also has marine animals, too. But it really excels at providing meaningful kid experiences and our 3yo and 5yo really enjoyed it! Many of the terrariums have a kid-height platform so they can see the occupant up close. You can also hold "Rosie" the tarantula! The butterfly exhibit is obviously the biggest draw, and is really well done - not as large as Moody Gardens in Galveston, TX, but equally high-quality. Tons of opportunities to see large, colorful butterflies up close.

We got lucky and had nice weather in late February, which meant the place was practically deserted. We had seen this on The Daytripper so we knew what to expect as far as the depth and clarity of the water, but it really has to be experienced in person! We brought our own snorkel gear and were able to leisurely swim around the pool by ourselves. The fish are so friendly it'll make you laugh. This really is a special place and every Texan owes it to themselves to visit at least once. Bathrooms and changing facilities were large and clean. I could see shaded areas being in short supply in the summer, so be prepared with sun screen.

A large museum with extensive exhibits detailing everything about the West, but particularly focusing on Pecos history (e.g. Pecos fire fighters, cowboys, teachers, statesmen, etc.)  The setting - a three-story historic hotel - is as interesting as the artifacts inside. The exhibits are dated and showing their age (literally, with peeling paper and dust).  However, if you can look aside from that there is enough here to spend 4-5 hours reading everything.  Instead, skip the exhibits that don't interest you so there is more time for the stuff that does.  $5/adult entrance fee.

Ok, I'll be the grump. This place really wasn't my cup of tea. Crowded, intentionally confusing, and no maps! It's clear the folks who built it have put a lot of heart and effort into making it what it is, but what it is isn't for everyone. I think it would be too frightening for toddlers (and parents trying to keep an eye on them!), but pre-teens and teens would probably have a blast.  I might have even allowed myself to have a bit of fun if it hadn't been so crowded.  So, I guess see it but be prepared for experiencing something like you've never been to before.

Glorious trails set among the trees and Ocoee River. The building is surprisingly spacious with excellent photo opportunities all over.  A nice paved path follows the river and it's easy to picture in your mind's eye all the Olympic competitors and spectators many years ago.  If you're driving the scenic two-lane roads around here this is definitely worth your while to stop, even if only for a short while.  I would have liked to have spent a half day or longer exploring the trails.

An amazing park! It's quite large so we didn't feel like it was crowded although it's one of the most visited parks in the state. There's plenty of trails to hike, bike, and ride horses. Lots of wildlife! We saw 8 tarantulas, a dozen turkeys, a bull snake, mule deer, and several barbary sheep during our stay. Research weather first, though - it can be very hot in summer and snow in winter. This is one of those parks you will never forget visiting.

Free, clean, air-conditioned, and slightly quirky - but still worth a quick visit even if you're not into chess.  The first and second floors are more of an art gallery of whimsical chess sets and pieces. The third floor is the actual hall of fame, with interactive TV screens, plaques, and info on chess leagues. Overall I came away with a better impression of the game of chess, and was pleasantly surprised how professional this center is.

Rugged canyon wilderness - you've seen the pictures and it's more majestic in person. Lots of prairie dogs that you can photograph quite closely (10' away!). We barely saw any of the bison which was a bit disappointing, but the ranger said yesterday they were all hanging around the visitor's center, so clearly it's hit-or-miss if you'll see them. Enjoyed a nice hike, too, but be sure to take plenty of water!

Our two kids loved spending the day here - it was nearly the highlight of the whole trip! Lots of varied exhibits, and everything is interactive. Activities to challenge both the body and mind. The workshop area was especially impressive, given that the kids are allow to use real tools.  This is the kind of place we would seriously consider getting an annual pass to if we lived in the area.

Come for the mosaics, stay for the air conditioning and quiet ambiance.  The staff are friendly and encourage you to take as many photos as you like - what a difference from many other places of worship around the world! After you walk around, take a moment to sit in one of the pews and just take in the sights. Then, walk down to the basement museum to read about the construction.

Wish I had done more research and saw that most of the cars are in muddy puddles. Only one car you could actually go up to without getting your feet in muddy water, and that car was crowded with people. Bring boots and you will have access to paint cars that others can't! Also, lots of trash around, so carry out more than you brought in to make it nicer than you found it.

A wonderful place to spend the weekend with your family. Great nature trails throughout and plenty of opportunities for amateur anglers to fish from the banks or a dock. RV sites are pretty close together so choose carefully. Bathrooms were kept spotless (cleaned 2x day) with plenty of hot water and pressure. The sunsets behind the lake are magnificent!

A not-quite scale replica of what a complete Stonehenge would have been. But unlike the real thing, you can actually get right up to the "stones". Definitely worth a stop, especially since there are other sights to check out here on the grounds of the Hill Country Arts Foundation.

An interesting (if dubious) backstory about how this building came into existence. When it's closed - as it was when we visited - there's not much to do but take a picture and drive on. Worth seeing if downtown but no need otherwise.
dislikes: Facilities & Services: Limited activities when closed
Attraction Type: Not much to do

reviews_attraction.text: As with most free attractions, come early to avoid crowds. But there is still plenty to do here and keep the kiddos entertained. The temporary Apollo exhibit was particularly fascinating, with the actual capsule on display!

Large park with plenty to do for all ages and abilities. Miniature train rides and (seasonal) quarry splash pad are musts for the kids. Lots of hiking trails in the back part, too. A real destination park!
Worth doing to rest your feet, take in some sights along the river, and hear some really corny jokes. Be aware that it only makes stops southbound, but you can hop aboard at any location.
Peaceful park to camp. Boat ramp is on the far side from the camping spots. Easy access to hiking tail. No primitive camping at this site - just RV/tent sites with water and electricity.
Highly worth a stop if you have kiddos! The playground is HUGE, with things for all ages including wheelchair ramps. The park is a gem of the city.
Shaded playground! Clean restrooms! What more could a traveling family looking for a picnic spot want? Perfect pit stop. Thanks, Gonzales!
A great place to walk around, with lots of living exhibits and friendly, knowledgeable volunteers in period clothing. Excellent for kids!
All the painted churches are wonderful to behold, but this one really is the "queen", as they say. More ornate than the others.

Top notch rangers that are willing to take the time to help you plan your backcountry trip, day hike or provide advice.

Nicole W. Was so helpful, friendly and professional. This is the second time we have been helped with back country planning, the first by Robert.

Before you head into the park, make a stop here for some solid advice and seek the knowledge of the pros. It really should be your first stop before entering the park!

To get the best out of your visit I recommend you stop a the WIC first (Wilderness Information Center).  It really becomes important if you only have a short stay that way you can maximize your time in and around the Park.

The Rangers are really helpful and can assist you.  Get ready to describe the things you want to see and your objectives that way they can make suggestions curtailed to your individual goals.

The visitor center has maps, a small theater section and if you plan on backpacking, the back country office to assist in permitting and planning.

The museum is small by larger city standards but very well laid out and has a unique architectural personality. It's clean, well lit with large expanse areas that easily guide you through each art exhibit.

It will really depend on what exhibit will be showcased which of course appeals to individual taste however I do not think you will be disappointed in the museum layout or design.

Another treat to see is the evening lights on the museum and how they flow through color changes cast on the all sides of the structure. Very relaxing to sit in Curtis Hixon Park and observe at no cost.

The museum has a small cafe serving drinks sandwiches and gelato it overlooks the banks of the Hillsborough River and can be visited by all visitors through an admission-free entrance. The café has indoor and outdoor tables/seating overlooking the river.

Set in Point Defiance is the Point Defiance Rose Garden. The entire park has plenty to do however with  the rose garden (as mentioned), zoo/aquarium, science & math institute and living history museum on the park grounds.  The place is big!  There is also five mile road if you want to just drive around the natural setting of the point and observe the different views of Commencement Bay.

We visited the Rose Garden and it was a fabulous way to spend 1-2 hours observing a very well maintained flower and rose garden in the heart of the park.  The attraction is no cost (free) and provides a very relaxing leisurely walk among some gorgeous flowers.

You can complete the circuit in about 1-2 hours and some will find getting done in >1 hour but it all depends on your pace.

One of the best trails in the hillsborough Paul system of nature preserves. There are no facilities at Rhodine and access is via Steven J. Wortham Park.  To gain access there is a very easy short stream hop, a child can handle. The trails are 60/70% shaded but still remember to bring your water and bug spray.  Despite being DecemberThe mosquitoes were still out just not that bad.

The trails are very flat in compacted and easy to navigate and walk through. You will go through pines oak Forest and scrub oaks. During our visit we didn't see any type of wildlife which was a bit disappointing.

his place is pretty cool. Something for everyone at this gathering place in the middle of downtown Dallas. It's has stuff for families and  20/30 something's. It just really depends on what type of event is being sponsored. Nevertheless, it's a great venue with a restaurant bar located in the middle of the park, plenty of covered outdoor seating to relax and enjoy the sites.

This place gets really crowded on the weekend, especially when the weather is great almost to the point it looks like a theme park.  Can get a bit too much and takes away form the experience.

If you are visiting Austin, this is a definite stop - don't leave without visiting.  The architecture is magnificent and it was constructed Texas style, big!  Upon entering I would recommend taking the free tour.  It's about 20/30 minuted in length but really gives you a lot of information about the capital and Texas history in a short period of time.

It's also very interesting to wonder the capital halls and check out the legislative rooms.  You could spend hours but I'd say the typical visitor will spend about 1 -2 hours.

Fantastic oasis in the heart of St Petersburg. This is an excellent venue to relax and look at the garden variety of palms and other fauna/plant life. It's set up very well and has a nice winding shaded path through the garden area that you can  stroll under a shaded canopy.

A splendid activity for the entire family. Probably can be completed in about 1.5 - 2.5 hours or longer if you really take your time. Keep in mind this is all outdoors so when it is the middle of June and July it will be hot with probable mosquitos.

Hands down this has to be one of my favorite nature and science museums I have been to. Reasonably priced and many exhibits.  It's not just the number either, it happens to be the quality of exhibits and also the size.  There big, it seems everything they do is big here.

they have a souvenir/retail shop and cafeteria area as well.  They move people well in their ticketing area.  Parking can be a bit hectic, especially if you want to grab a space close to the entrance (so arrive early-this museum is popular).

Definitely worth taking a few moments to check out this gorgeous Catholic church.  There are only 2/3 of these fine examples of stunning cathedrals in the Spokane area.  Beautiful stained glass windows and stations of the cross along the perimeter walls greet you as you enter through the heavy brass doors.

You can spend about 20-45 minutes and the walk will take you to a center tree lined street that will not disappointment especially if you are there during the fall time.

The beer here is pretty decent, nothing spectacular but good (9 beers on tap). They serve a basic menu of snacks and sandwiches should you get hungry (but selection is limited).

The interior space is pretty nice, very welcoming,   gives you a warm feeling inside, definitely inviting and laid back. They have a small outside seating area that's nice and intimate, very cozy feeling. They have two seating areas, the wine tasting area and beer tap area, both are nice.

Love the Suncoast trail.  The bathrooms at the Lutz Lake Fern trail head are two port-a-lets.  For port-a-lets they are pretty clean and don't smell that bad but remember they are what they are!  The trail rangers keep the water stations pretty full however during the heat of the summer there are some periods time that they are empty but never that long.  Just make sure you bring adequate water and do not rely on the stations.

You might as well make the trip and say you saw the grave and cemetery with other native Baltimore notable citizens buried there.  Other than that it is a bit deflating. Like saying, is this it, well yes it is.

There are interpretive plaques  along the walk that inform you about the other notable people interned there. So it is pretty informative and for no fee involved it's a nice place to kill some time.

If you are in Golden make the 10 minute trip up to the museum and grave. It is some fantastic artifacts and tells the story of William Cody's traveling show which is a part of American history.

The museum does a fantastic job with showcasing the artifacts in the exhibits.

The grave site sits on prefect vantage point and I can see why Cody wanted this to be his final resting place.

It's a small park with not much to see here unless you want to people watch and in that case it does offer some nice seating and vantage points to watch pedestrian traffic stroll by.  It also offers a decent location to eat outside.

There is bench style seating on the perimeter of the park that is shaded by medium size oaks but no covered seating.

Not many sites to see but an excellent hike among prairie view's with tranquil silence (when the parachute jumps aren't occurring).  This is a great look trail and a fantastic cross country run. Plan on bringing your own water as there is none along the trail. It's also not frequented so make sure you tell someone where you are at.

Definitely worth walking by if you are in the area.  It's an urban park located close to the capital.

Allows for an educational experience via many kiosks located throughout the mall area.  There is no actual "attraction" in the mall it makes for a nice walk and informational learning about the history of Tennessee.

What a great experience. The movie is no frills with basic Indian cuisine. The prices are very reasonable. It's cafeteria style ordering, place your order at the register and pay. The menu listing is on the white board, no paper menus.

This place is off the beaten path but we'll worth the visit.

We tackled this hike on our way completing the Hiking Spree challenge. It has been one of the most enjoyable this season. It has about 50% shaded trails and as expected is flat. There is enough scenery change to keep your visually stimulated.

It's an enjoyable hike with not much wildlife.
