Apply a generous coating of sun block lotion over exposed skin and bring plenty of water. The wearing of hiking boots or other sturdy footwear is recommended since this is a rocky and narrow dirt trail. A round trip hike to the top and back will take approximately two hours for the physically fit. The parking area is very small, so arrive early!

Alamo Placita is one of the oldest parks in Denver. Commissioned by Denvers first mayor, Robert W. Speer in the early 1900's. Before the advent of motion pictures, Alamo Placita Park was once known as Chutes park where a team of trained Elk would run up a 60 ft high platform and dive into a tank of water.  Today, the grandeur of this park can be clearly seen amongst the beautiful and carefully crafted rows of flowers and fields of lush green grass and is located on the north side of Speer Boulevard between Ogden and Emerson Streets. In  2000, This park was designated as a historic district by the Denver Landmark Preservation Commission.

The Adams County History Museum is a great way to learn about the early history of Adams County. Historians will love the detailed displays of what life was like back in the early 1900's up to present day. Kids will love the interactive displays of the geological history of the area and the dark room that shows the florescent colors that certain rocks display when a black light is presented. The general museum is free with a more detailed guided tour offered for a modest price. Located next to the Adams county fair grounds makes it a convenient and easy place to find and enjoy. Check their website for museum times and tour prices.

To climb this trail one must call upon their inner mountain goat. This is a steep, rocky, rough terrain but the views are phenomenal. From the NCAR building to the cave its about 2.7 miles and there is an elevation gain of around 850 ft. When I went the last portion of the trail and the cave were closed due to some bat disease. But this is a good trail overall. There is plenty of parking at the NCAR building parking lot. Make sure to wear study shoes, comfortable clothing and bring a couple of bottles of water per person. Total round trip hike time is around  1.5 to 2 hours depending on expertise and fitness level.

what an amazing trail. This is an easy 21 mile paved and mostly flat trail that goes to/from Greeley to/from Windsor with plenty of stops in between. A portion of this trail is within the city but the majority is out in the country and you are surrounded by beautiful views of mountains, open fields, lakes, trees and farmland and all that you can hear is the wind rustling through the trees and maybe a small critter jumping into the water. I would say the best time to go is in the spring or fall when the air is cool and crisp, or in the early morning hours of the summer.

Community Park is a great benefit to the city of Broomfield. walking, biking, playing on the playground, having a group gathering or family picnic and even free tennis courts can all be done and had here. Take a walk and have a quiet moment of silence and reflection at the 9/11 memorial or enjoy a free outdoor concert at the amphitheater. Ive even seen hobbyists sail remote controlled mini sailboats on the pond. Plenty of open grassy areas to play sports or just lay down and soak up some rays. This park has plenty of off street parking and even restrooms.

The Kirkland Museum is a wonderful gallery full of amazing art of all different types, styles, shapes and configurations.  Many of the art pieces were of furniture and there even was a bathroom complete with toilet, sink, and a rack of clothing that was roped off and displayed as art. The main attraction was of the dot style paintings where the artist dipped a paintbrush into paint and instead of paint strokes, dotted the entire canvas with little dots of paint. Very interesting, unique and explosive in design. Truly a must see gallery.

This is a small park situated on a hillside and it sure lives up to its name. A walk or ride up to the top will reveal a inspirational view of the whole city that on a clear day can be seen for miles and miles in all directions. This park has old growth pines trees that early in the morning you can smell their fragrant aroma and its like you are magically transported out of the city and into the middle of the mountains. The roads on either side of the park are very steep and offer good climbing challenges for cyclists and hikers.

This really is a hidden gem for the city of Longmont. Tucked away from the busy city streets is a lush oasis filled with beautiful lakes, rivers and even a waterfall! There are plenty of places to stop and have a peaceful picnic lunch and there are many miles of trails to bike, hike, or walk your dog on. Very picturesque and tranquil views of the lakes, trails, wildlife and mountains will make you think that you traveled hundreds of miles far off into the mountains, when in fact this treasure was in your backyard all along.

This museum is a interesting place to see, I went for their Star Wars exhibit. It was a large exhibit that featured all types of Star Wars toys both new and from the original movies that first were shown in the 70's. This museum is in an old house and there was no air condition, so it was hot and stuffy. Plus many of the other exhibits were in the hallways of the house which made walking past other people a tight fit. If you like miniatures, dolls, and other toys, then this place is definitely worth a look.

Garfield Lake park is a medium sized park on the southwest side of Denver. It has a nice little trail that surrounds the lake thats used by walkers and cyclists. This park also has a playground, a pool, restrooms, a water fountain, basketball and tennis courts and large open fields to play football, baseball and soccer.  When I went the park was mostly quiet with a few people walking around. Good place to visit if you're in the area.

Cool little museum in the heart of the CU Boulder campus. Mostly has exhibits about the history of Boulder and the surrounding area. When I went they were having a Native American live exhibit that you could participate in. They had cutouts of various different animals and you could throw spears at them as if you were a Native American hunter gathering food for his tribe. Nice place to visit while in the Boulder area.

It was a beautiful late September day, the sun was shining, a cool breeze was in the air and everybody was happy and in good spirits. The hike started easy but the trail became steeper and steeper with each step until we reached the glorious summit and each person achieved their victory over the mountain trail. The views at the summit are well worth the hike as one can see for miles and miles in each direction.

A unique collection of contemporary art is housed in this three story building. When I went it was sparse but interesting nonetheless. If you never been to the MCA I recommend going at least once, they have different showcases every few months and the first Saturday of every month is called penny day since they only charge an admission price of $0.01 on that day for Colorado residents. Worth checking out!

Ive been to this park many times, mainly because its on one of my bike trails. Its a good place to rest since it has a big covered picnic area and I believe it also has a water fountain, which is helpful in the hot, dry summer months. Its more of a general use park filled with bike, hiking trails, playgrounds and picnic areas, The dog part is only a fenced in patch of ground in the corner.

I walk over this feat of engineering marvel and architectural beauty  every time I go to the 16th street mall. in the summer this bridge is decked out in flowers and offers very photogenic views of lower downtown, plus it connects you to the new RTD mall station which offers free bus rides. The stairs on this bridge have tracks near the edge that are designed for bicycles.

A unique and interesting gallery/ venue space. Many of the installation pieces at the time of my visit were digital animation shown through a projector and displayed on the wall. The whole building has that artistic and creative vibe that makes you want to stay and examine each piece. Its great that Denver has so many artistic outlets, I want to explore them all.

This is a fun place to go and learn about natural history and science. It has many exhibits about the earth and dinosaurs; About outer space and caves filled with gems. Take an extra trip with Imax and the health expedition. This place gets busy quickly, so its best to go early in the day.

There is never a bad time to visit when you come to Rocky Mountain National Park. The alluvial fan provides hours of hiking over rocks and kids will love it! The spring is the best time to visit if you want to see very active waterfalls as the snow is melting at a good rate. But the trails can still be covered by snow which can make hiking a challenge. Wildlife is abundant in the park and you are likely to see moose, chipmunks, elk, deer and many others. Summer is great for hiking as all of the snow is gone and there are many lakes to visit. Also during the summer Trail Ridge Road is open which is just an amazing drive through high country. Be prepared to stop and take a lot of pictures no matter what part of the park you visit. Each visit is a new adventure and you are guaranteed to see something new each time. Camping in the park is top notch and you will sometimes have close up adventures with wildlife as we found out with a deer who decided to hangout next to our tent.

A very fun place to visit, it is hard to get photos in the caves to turn out well, but the tour is fun. We had a good tour guide, but you could tell she had said the same script over and over that her jokes all fell flat. There is a really nice gift shop to look around in while waiting for your tour to start and a large area to sit and eat concessions. Since the last time we went there, they have added a lot of extra money makers such as a zip line and a ropes course. Of course we fell for it and had to do both. The ropes course is actually a lot of fun and part of the course extends out over a cliff which gives an even greater feeling of danger. The zip line is laid out over a steep mountain slope giving more excitement. They also have a ride called the Terror-Dactyl, but none of us were brave enough to try it, check out the website for more details.

This park has a nice long paved trail that encircles it and now connects to a longer set of trails that cover miles of territory. The park sees a lot of activity, from soccer to flag football, the grass fields seem to always be in use for kids activities. There are also several softball/baseball fields that are well maintained and also see a lot of activity from youth and adult sport events. There is an excellent playground right next to the soccer fields and this provides great exercise for the younger ones. On the south side of the park is a very shallow, wide creek which provides hours of exploration for any adventurous kids. A pair of boots will allow for walking in and around the creek, but never go near it if it looks like it is going to rain as it fills up quickly. But on a clear sunny day, it is a blast!

This place is great for older kids and younger kids. There is so much to see and do here and new things are added all the time. They have horseback riding and fishing. Bottle feeding the goats is always a fun activity as well as riding the pedal tractors right next door. The dairy barn is a great place to pet some calves as well as watch a live demonstration of a cow being milked. There is an old school house to tour as well as a blacksmith demonstration, a barbershop and an old bank. There are paths to walk through in the forest and an Indian encampment to learn about how native americans lived. There are tons of play areas for the kids both inside the farmstead as well as out. There are fish to feed as well as large goats and sheep that are always accepting of handouts.

Excellent little park just off of Grant St in Overland Park. The park was remodeled in 2017 is really looks nice. There is a walking path and bridge to explore for the more adventurous older kids. The little creek is fun to explore also. The bathrooms as mentioned before have been remodeled and are in very good shape. The picnic area is in a covered area and can be booked for events. The playground area has some really unique play equipment is and geared towards younger kids who will find hours of playtime here. There is also a small spray park area that is operation during summer hours. The parking lot is a little small but this park is kind of hidden near a neighborhood and school, so parking might not be an issue as you can easily park at the school and walk over.

Great park with lots of wide open space. The park has a lot of features for a variety of activities. There is a well maintained tennis court (actually two courts) with a nice high fence around it. There are two half court basketball courts in the park. The playground has lot of slides and is large enough to keep any kid busy for a while. There are only two swings though, one is for infants and the other for older kids. The park features four historical makers telling the history of the surrounding area. There is even a small section of train tracks in the park near the historical markers. The park is right behind the Johnson County Central library, which is another great place to spend some time. There are a few restaurants close by if you need food.

A family favorite, we have been here more times than I can count. One complaint about the zoo is that it is so spread out, but this is actually a good thing as this allows for many of the animals to be in a more "natural" habitat (an open field), as compared to some zoo's that have their animals in concrete cages. We usually break up our visits each time we go. One time we will go over to the Africa section (if you don't want to walk, a tram can take you there) or we go to the Asia/Australia section. If you live locally, the season pass is the way to go as just a couple of visits will more than cover the cost. The zoo is constantly adding and upgrading their attractions so it is always fun to go and see what is new.

This place is excellent, so much to see! Many, many trains to climb on and explore in. The trains are displayed outside and can get pretty warm in the summer, but some of the trains are under a canopy which helps cut the heat. There is also a display of cars inside of an air conditioned building. This is a fun place to cool off and hang out for a while. The main building has a lot of great history and displays to explore. It is quite a walk from the main building to the trains, but luckily they have a shuttle that runs back and forth. The kids will love this as much as seeing and exploring the trains. There is also a large tug boat you can climb around in, but aren't allowed to go inside. Fun time!

Nice little park that extends from Meadowbrook Elementary to the south for quite a ways. This 14 acre park is located at NE 60th Terrace and N. Michigan.  It features a basketball court, sand volleyball court, picnic area, playground, picnic shelter, a creek with a nostalgic walking bridge and a drinking fountain. If you decided to walk the length of the park (North to South) there is no walking path, but the grass is cut short so it makes for a fairly easy walk. The park also features an abandoned tennis court, you used to be able to go in there and hit tennis balls for fun, but now the gate is locked no longer allowing access to the court. Great place to send an afternoon!

Always a great place to visit! The zoo is large enough to have an incredible variety of animals, yet compact enough to get around in one day and see most things. They have really done a lot of improvements over the years to give the animals better environments and it is worth going back over and over to see what has changed. The zoo is free, which you can't beat. You do have to pay for parking unless you are willing to walk. We always manage to find a free place to park in Forest Park and then hike to the zoo. If you ever get a chance to go on a cold day when the giraffe's are inside the building, do it, it is amazing to see them upclose.

Perfect ski resort of any skill level. The beginner slopes are perfect for those who might need to sharpen their skills and there are bowls to challenge even the most experienced skier. Getting to Copper is super easy as it is right off of I-70 not far from Dillon, Colorado. The high speed chair lifts make it a breeze getting to the top to take run after run. There are also plenty of places to rest and warm up if you need a break. Haven't tried the condos at the base of the mountain, but from what I understand they are really nice. Had a season pass here one year and never got tired of skiing at Copper!

Great park with a lot of features. This is a great place to fish, as there are two fishing docks. The park has a .42 mile walking trail and there is exercise equipment placed at different intervals around the lake. There is an awesome playground for the kids, so much to do it will keep them occupied for hours. Many picnic tables are spread throughout the park, many of which are underneath awnings for shade and protection from the weather. Bar-b-que grills are also numerous around the park for those who like to cook. There is also lots of open space for running around in or walking your dog.

Excellent park featuring one of the most iconic water fountain's in the Kansas City area. During the summer there are wedding photographers at the fountain, in the spring prom pictures are taken in front of it, no matter the time of year there is photography going on. During the winter, the city continues to run the fountain and the water freezes into an interesting display. The park also features bike/hike trails and has lots of green open space. The Clay County Veterans Memorial is also located in the park and is worth the stop if you are in the area.

Excellent place to takes kids of all ages (and adults)! Everytime we go we discover a new area we've never seen before. Just an amazing variety of things to do, from slides to mazes to caves and tunnels. Go early in the morning when they first open because it gets very busy very quickly. The roof is an extra few dollars but is worth visiting if you haven't done it before.

Great place to camp. We found a fantastic spot this summer and really enjoyed the time we had at Mark Twain Lake. There is also a good variety of hiking trails. Many miles of adventure with lots of them near the shore line for a great view of the lake. There are also cabins to rent that look nice. Haven't tried boating yet but it is on the wish list.

Great park for young children. The park features a Pirates Ship that kids will spend hours on. Swings are nearby as well as a park shelter with picnic tables. An added benefit is that the park sits next to the Gladstone Municipal Pool and the Community Center. Even features a small baseball field that isn't well maintained but is usable.
likes: Proximity to community facilities (Pool, Community Center)

reviews_attraction.text: One of the worst state parks I have been to. Horrible layout design. If you like walking and lugging your stuff for miles and miles from the parking lot just to get to the trailhead then this is your place, otherwise there are so many better places to go than this waste of time.

Great park, lots to do.  A very good playground for kids, two baseball fields, a football field and a basketball court. The lake is a great place to go fishing and there is a nice bike/hike trail through the park.
One of our favorite places we visited during our trip to Colorado. The kids absolutely loved it, lots of great examples of how weather works and the short movies are very interesting to watch.
A great place to spend the day! Seeing the Clydesdales up close is amazing and your kids will love all of the animals in the farm. Highly recommend!
Excellent hidden gem in Denver. Take the bus tour if you can, it makes it easier than walking up the ridge and the tour guides are knowledgeable.
So fantastic to see the Statue of Liberty! Got to go up in the Crown, an amazing experience. What an amazing monument to see!
Some truly amazing things to see here. There are a few exhibits that might disturb young children (and some adults).
Very awesome spot to hike to. Worth the trip if you are traveling along I-70 and want a little detour.
Very fun visit, excellent views of the city. Had to wait about 45 minutes to step out on the ledge.

Fairly recent (1972) National Park in the Trans-Pecos region of Texas that protects, among other things, the highest point in Texas.  A unique area in the surrounding Chihuahuan Desert, the park encompasses a world-renowned example of a Permian-age reef, the highest mountains in the state, the renowned McKittrick Canyon, and a massive salt flat, as well as important examples of Native American, Hispanic, and Anglo habitation and use.  Dozens of miles of trails, both vertical and horizontal, that range from the lowest Salt Flats to the highest point in Texas, the summit of Guadalupe Mountain.  Excellent backpacking opportunities with well-marked trails and backcountry campsites.  Nice but limited camping facilities, seasonal crowds, high winds and monsoonal rains in the ummer, and occasional snow in the winter, so plan accordingly.

One of the crown jewels of the Texas state park system, Davis Mountains State Park lies along Limpia Creek north of the village of Fort Davis.  Multiple camping areas for all types along the creek bed.  Full service lodge with restaurant and swimming pool.  Trail to nearby Fort Davis National Historical Park (NPS).  Newly developed hiking trail and primitive camping area north of Limpia Creek.  Short scenic drive to bluffs above the park with views of Fort Davis below.  An area of considerable natural beauty in a unique area of Texas.  Lack of other public camping facilities in the region makes proper planning a necessity, since there are no real second options if the park is full other than Balmorrhea, itself a very popular park.

Developed Colorado State Park on Lake Trinidad, a Corps impoundment of the Purgatoire River immediately wast of Trinidad on Co. HWY 12.   The main area off the park is located on the northern shore of the lake, near the Project Headquarters, and contains camping loops and restrooms.  While the area is very nice and the facilities modern, the loops are on a ridge high above the lake.  This placement, plus the wildly fluctuating level of the lake, which is often very low, really doesn't give the impression of a "lake park."  Nice, if pricey, facilities and areas of geological importance around the lake makes this a nice diversion, but the lack of water access makes the park less of a destination in itself.

National Park Service facility in the village of Fort Davis, protecting a once vital cavalry fort in the Trans-Pecos region.  Located near the intersection of TX 17 and TX 118, the park contains a visitor center and a large number of buildings (barracks, hospital, etc.) spread beneath a long, striking mesa.  This is a FEE AREA and a DAY-USE ONLY area, meaning there is an entrance fee, there are no facilities for camping, RV's, etc. and the gates close at 5 PM CST.  Camping and lodging can be found in nearby Davis Mountains State Park.  Whatever your mode of transport, the Trans-Pecos requires reasonable adult preparation and reasonable expectations, so plan accordingly before you visit.

Very large National Recreation Area located along U.S. 50 between Gunnison and Cimarron.  Composed of three reservoirs, Blue Mesa, Morrow Point, and Crystal, on the Gunnison River, this enormous area offers developed lake access to Blue Mesa, with marinas, public boat ramps, campgrounds, group facilities, trails, and limited primitive and boat-in camping.  Both Morrow Point and Crystal and smaller, more remote, difficult to access areas, with limited lake access and facilities.  Despite occasional seasonal and fiscal closures, this is a year-round park that offers something for all types of visitors, from day-visitors to dedicated fishermen and rock-climbers.
dislikes: Limited access to Morrow Point and Crystal

reviews_attraction.text: Limited-service state park SW of LLano protecting the massive granite dome known as Enchanted Rock.  A Hill Country landmark for generations, the dome remains a very popular destination for both locals and tourists, who flock to the area to climb the rock.  While the area is mainly a day-use joint, there is a large walk-in camping area near the HQ and a trail system around the base of the dome with primitive camping areas for overnight visitors.  Can be MASSIVELY crowded at times. so much so that the parking lot is often closed to new arrivals for long periods of time.  Plan ahead, check for possible restrictions, and have alternate plans--just in case.

Developed state park on the southern shore of the Pedernales River east of Johnson City.  Perennially popular among natives and tourists alike, the park has welcomed generations of visitors eager to see and experience the cascading falls on the wide, quick river.  While the falls are the main visual draw of the park, the area also contains traditional camping areas, picnic areas, a swimming area, numerous trails, and primitive camping.  Backcountry area is very popular among mountain bikers.  Very close to Austin, the park can be very, very crowded, so visitors should always check TPWD for information on access, construction, and temporary closures.
likes: Diverse activities (camping, picnicking, swimming, hiking, mountain biking)

reviews_attraction.text: One of the many National Monuments established in the 1930's throughout the Four Corner region, White Sands protects a massive white gypsum sand field at the base of the Organ Mountains.  Accessible via US 70, the park is west of Alamogordo and offers a scenic loop drive, picnic areas, nature trails and access to the dunefield.  Though a backpacking trail and primitive camping area have been added in recent years, the park is mainly a day-use joint for picnicking and fun on the dunes.  Special events offer unique opportunities to enjoy the dunes at night.  Myriad camping options around Alamogordo and Cloudcroft for longer stays.

One of the only developed areas on Morrow Point Reservoir, one of the three reservoirs that make up Curecanti National Recreation Area, this small trailhead, picnic area, and launching point for hand-carried watercraft is immediately west of Blue Mesa Dam and can be accessed from US 50, west of Sapinero.   An area of outstanding natural beauty, the area is composed of a parking area, restroom, and scenic views.  A stone staircase leads down to the water's edge, offering access to a short trail and an area for launching small boats.  The NPS offers motorized boat tours of Morrow Point on a seasonal basis from this area.

Full-service state park west of the town of Meridian with primitive camping near the lake shore, tent and trailer camping, and three screened shelter area--one on the lake, one in the woods near the camping area, and one on a high bluff above the lake.  For day use, there are a number of trails, including a trip around the lake, as well picnic areas, a swimming area, and a CCC-era bath house on the lake shore.  Scenic park without the crowds of nearby Cleburne and Dinosaur Valley, with excellent screened shelter options--though areas south of the lake do suffer from traffic noise from the nearby Hwy 22.

Long, narrow developed state park spread out along U.S. 64 between Cimarron and Eagle's Nest. A number of camping and picnic areas along the Cimarron river in a beautiful, heavily-forested canyon bound by high jagged mesas, such as the "Palisades."  While the scenery is nothing short of spectacular, small recreation areas separated by 1 mile + distances, and few trails or other amenities makes this park best suited as a fishing camp or a base camp for day trips to Eagle's Nest, Red River, Angel Fire, etc.  Seasonal closures during winter months shouldn't dissuade campers from winter camping.

Full-service state park north of Tyler, accessible from I-20.  Beautiful pine forest scenery with cabins, screen shelters, and multiple camping areas ranging from tent to full trailer sites.  Large trail system for hiking and mountain bikes.  64-acre spring fed lake with park store, bath house, swimming area, fishing pier, and canoe rental.  Historically, a favorite weekend escape for residents of the Dallas area, the park is heavily used year around and can be crowded.  Regardless of this, the park is still a jewel of the TPWD system, with excellent facilities and wonderful scenery.

Large, sprawling state park in the legit mountain range that divides the city of El Paso.  Originally a smaller day-use area on the NW side of El Paso, the park has grown over the last decade into a more full-service park with camp sites.  Four distinct areas, the larger of which, the Tom Mays Unit, offers small RV camping area, a larger walk-in camping area, and two group camping areas.  Myriad trailheads and trails in all four units, with paths ranging from the foothills to the top of the mountains at Smugglers Pass.  Awesome in winter, particularly on the rare snow days.

Large greenbelt park and trailhead on the West Fork of the Trinity west of Loop 12.  A part of the County Preserve system, it is accessible from Hunter Farrell--bit of a travail to get there at the best of times.  Normal park amenities, playground, etc., paved trail near the water.  Is the southern terminus of the Campion Trail system, which runs east under Loop 12 and then north along the border of Twin Wells Golf Course to Shady Grove.  The part of the river the preserve borders is brackish and can be pretty rank, so reasonable expectations are a must.

Developed Forest Service trail-head and parking area on Hwy 12 near the southern edge of the village of Cuchara.  Composed of a parking area, 3 picnic tables, and a restroom.  A seasonal area, the trailhead offers access to the Dodgeton Trail (#1302), a multi-use trail that travels west from Cuchara to junctions with the longer Baker and Indian Trails.  While it makes for very easy access to the trail system, a $7 daily fee, seasonal closures, and wicked crowds in summer mitigate its utility.  Look for free areas to park nearby, such as the old ski area.

Massive, sprawling, and remote state park west of Big Bend National Park near Lajitas.  Much less formally developed than other TPWD parks, the Ranch nevertheless offers traditional, backcountry, and equestrian campsites, hundreds of miles of multi-use trails, and 70 miles of high-clearance vehicle roads in a stunning desert environment.  While this area has grown in popularity over the last few years, particularly among mountain-bikers, this is a very remote area, with no water/elec. campsites, no dump stations, and no cell service--so plan accordingly.

Small full service state park east of the town of Daingerfield in far northeast Texas.  Beautiful East Texas setting with dense pine forests and small spring-fed lake.  A mix of older and more recently constructed areas, the park has tent and trailer camping areas, a small number of cabins, and a bath house on the lake with a fishing pier. A trail around the river and several smaller trails in the woods north of the lake.  A quiet, beautiful park, particularly in the fall and spring, with smaller crowds than other parks in the Piney Woods, such as Tyler.

Unique developed state park on US 180 immediately east of the town of Mineral Wells.  Built around a central lake, the park has three distinct areas--the western shore of the lake, which contains screen shelters, camping areas, and a trail system with a small primitive campground, the Penitentiary Hollow area east of the lake, with picnic areas and trails on a high bluff above the water, and a central area at the south end of the lake, with the park store, fishing area, and canoe rentals.  Excellent facilities for both campers and day use patrons.

Full-service state park east of Commerce on the southern shore of Cooper Lake.  Individual loops for cabins, screen shelters, trailers, tent camping, and equestrian camping.  A small peninsula at the west end of the park is set up for walk-in camping.  Day-use facilities include a boat ramp, picnic areas and a short trail.  Excellent facilities in an area of gently rolling woods and miles of lake shore.  Lake level can change drastically throughout the year--so boaters and fishermen should plan accordingly.

TPWD-administered Day-Use Area south of the Pedernales River and accessible by US 290 west of Johnson City.  Visitor Center and Store, Restrooms, Historical Displays, and Living History area.  Many nice picnic areas, both near the Visitor Center and along the southern shore of the river, take advantage of the beautiful Hill Country landscape.  Best in the spring, when wildflowers abound, and of course, during peach season, when nearby Stonewall becomes awash with fresh peaches and related items.

Large, full-service state park on the western shore of Lake Brownwood.  Multiple camping areas of all types, large screen shelter area near the water, and almost 20 cabins scattered throughout the park.  Usual lake park amenities, i.e. boat ramps, etc. and several day-use areas. A number of overnight buildings for groups of different sizes and a beautiful cliff-side dining hall that is a masterpiece of the CCC era of park building.  Lake levels can fluctuate greatly--so be advised.

The site of the original park office, this scenic overlook offers spectacular and occasionally terrifying views of the deep canyon and river below.  On a seasonal (May-Oct) road.  During winter, when the road is open to ski and snowshoe traffic only, this area marks the beginning of the area open to primitive camping.  While open and flat, this area has little to no cover, so over-the-snow campers may want to camp further west or on the south side of the road.

Small overlook area on Lake Joe Pool, accessible from FM 1382.  A traditional feature of many local Corps of Engineers lakes, the Overlook is a combination scenic viewing area, picnic area, and restroom near the Project Office.  Nicely wooded area with expansive views of the lake and trails down to the water.  Offers access to the eastern end of the dam, which is topped by a two-lane state road--closed to traffic but open to walking and bicycles.

Small developed trailhead/parking area in the NE area of the park.  Near the intersection of the Fall River Rd. (west of the Fall River Entrance Station) and the Endovalley Road, this area is adjacent to the Sheep Lakes area and along Fall River itself.  Offers access to a number of trails, some leading north into the mountains and others leading south into the Sheep Lakes and West Horseshoe areas.  Generally open in winter.

Small State Park Unit on the north shore of Cooper Lake.  Smaller than the sprawling unit on the south side, the Doctors Creek Unit has more day-use facilities, such as larger picnic areas, and more trails.  A single camping area accommodates RV units, making it a better RV destination than the south unit, with its long winding park roads.  A large boat ramp and adjacent pier offers access to the waters near the dam.

We had the chance to visit the site with family. We had our grandkids (2 1/2 & 1 year old). Our 2 1/2 year old did get excited seeing the animals coming up to the car. Each car is given a bag of food pellets for the animals. Our 2 1/2 was having fun tossing the pellets out the window to the animals. Just pay close attention to the Zebras and ostriches. We got there early thinking that the animals would be hungry, but a truck was going around dropping hay. Hay or pellets the animals choose hay. So we got to the petting portion of the park and they just loved this area.

We went on 12/31/2018 very cold outside, but nice inside. It was a great time with the grandchildren. Lots of families so that means children running everywhere. It was fun, but all the little ones look alike. So much to see not just fish. We ate here because of the convenience, but it’s a bit pricey. Food wasn’t bad and the staff was friendly. Note....it’s humid so going outside in the cold is even more cold ❄️

01-24-2020 We went at 6:30 and there was all ready a large crowd. Once inside it didn’t appear to be that many people. It had snowed off and on which just added to the great experience. Plenty of hot chocolate and fresh from the oven cookies. Kids laughing and parents calling out children names. Just a fun time for the families.

Sandstone Ranch Park is one of Longmont’s bigger parks. I think it’s the biggest park within Longmont area. It’s located on H-119 east of Longmont. It has bike trails on the south end that go all the way to town. Many grass fields for soccer games. Baseball fields, playgrounds, spray water feature and covered picnicking areas.

We just visited the park last weekend 9/15/2018. They had an event for vendors to show their goods. It was more like a flee market just no one asking to take less. It was hot and only a few of the stands where in the shade. Nothing to eat or drink made for quick visit. Also very few people most was at the farmers market.

Great place for the little ones. We took the grandkids here (ages 7,9,11) and they had so much fun. They climb on the ropes ran over the bridge came down the slides. I have to say that the silo slide about three floors high was really cool. Lots of kids young and old were enjoying themselves.

11/09/19 The weather man said that this will be a warm day with winds around 5-10 miles per hour. That was in the parking lot once I got on the trail it all changed. I didn’t bring snowshoes and I paid for it. Post holed all the way up to Lawn Lake and on the way down my legs were smoking.

St Mary’s Lake and Glacier are two great things to see. You get both in one visit. It’s a short hike ~ .5 mile up a rough road with some large boulders. The payoff is worth it once you see the lake with it’s glacier. Lots of people come here and they all want to slide down the glacier.

03/03/2018 Bear Lake trail will lead you to a few others lakes. 1st will be Two Rivers Lake, 2nd Lake Helene, 3rd Odessa Lake, and 4th is Spruce Lake. This is scenic hike all the way. It does climb a bit, but it’s well worth it. This is a very popular area, in the park so come early.

Great part of this grand Rock Mountain National Park! So much land and wild life to see. I see each time I am up there why people come from miles, and from several countries to visit this park. Each person visiting want to be there to experience this beautiful part of this country.

05/24/2020 It was an overcast day with rain in the forecast. What I got was snow and lots of it nearing the top of the ridge. I only saw about 6 other hikers and not dressed for snow. It was great to be up in the woods after staying at home for 5 weeks(social distancing).
dislikes: Lack of proper attire among hikers

reviews_attraction.text: 1/13/18 started out at 6:30am with lite snow falling. Was able to record the sun coming up through the falling snow. Didn’t have snowshoes on till about 2 miles in, then the snow went from 3-4 inches to well over 12 inches. I didn’t make it to the lake, but I got close.

4/20/2018 I hike this area a lot. Great area to take the family or just get outside alone. You will have to hike a distance right now as they have the road closed. You may just turn onto Hessie Trailhead as it’s a lot closer to where you’ll be parking.

09/28/2019 I did the loop clockwise from the parking lot to Bridal Veil Falls then to Balanced Rock and down to Gem Lake. The Aspen trees are changing to that bright yellow. The loop took me about 17 miles around. Great hike got one hell of a workout.

I live just down the road from here so I come here a lot. Great area to bring out of state guest. Great area to just get away and enjoy nature. Note- get outside alone, or with family and friends and enjoy the parks before someone gives it away.

This is a great place to take the kids. Longmont’s older parks have matured trees and this is one of them with lots of shade. Plenty of space for the kids to run and play. If your planing a summer family picnicking this would be the park.

Big park many areas...ball fields, soccer fields, play grounds, and a skate park. Kids love this park and lots of parking spaces. There’s also a trail that starts out by the Sandstone Ranch Visitors Center and goes back towards town.

Great park to take the little ones. This park was in the path of Longmont's flooding just a few shot years ago. Those big ants actually moved all the way up to higher ground during the flooding. Glad to see they survived.

Really great park with lots of trees and restrooms. Golden Ponds starts the trails that connect the two together. You can do so much here as it’s a big park. Room for the dogs to run and for you to run or bike ride.
06/13/2020 it was very warm to hot day. Lots of young people going for a swim even some sunbathing going on. This is a great hike and the view (s) are always great. Still had a lot of snow around.
Great place to bring the little ones. Lots of people use this area to bring their dogs. Many people will run, walk, bike and just site see. Watch out for the geese droppings, enjoy this park.
During the Christmas Holidays it is beautiful. We went Nov 26,2017 it was warm out. The lights come on right after Thanksgiving and go off Jan 2.  Cost is $12 for adult (2 and up).
Started on Hessie Trailhead and went up to Woodland Lake. Had to post hole in some areas already (10/22/17). It was a windy day, but well worth the hike no one was up there.
It starts out in the trees and gradually as the trail turns at Lake Isabelle you start to move out of the trees. The views on the way up just keep getting better and better.
It was very smoky when I was here not sure why. It may have been the fires in California. I love being outdoors so there is nothing I will say bad of this area.

PAISANO RANCH. Paisano Ranch, fourteen miles southwest of Austin in the Hill Country, was the country retreat of J. Frank Dobie until his death in 1964. He had previously owned a larger place, Cherry Springs Ranch, near Marble Falls. In 1959, after a severe illness, he sold Cherry Springs Ranch and bought the 254-acre Paisano Ranch, which had been called Shady Creek Ranch by the previous owners, George and Pearl Turney. The first owner of the land was James S. Burton, who surveyed and received 160 acres of it about 1860. On August 14, 1863, Burton sold the property to Frederick and Lucy Kunze, who built a log cabin on it. The cabin is hidden within the walls of the present house, though a part of it can be seen since renovation in 1979. The property was sold on September 15, 1865, to John Daniel and Mary Wende, who increased the size of the ranch to its present acreage, built additional rooms on the cabin, and built stone walls that still crosscut the property. Wende died in 1897, but his wife lived there five more years. The ranch was uninhabited for the next twenty-six years. In March 1928 it was sold by the Wendes' son, John Charles, to Anton and Minnie Holm. The Holms sold it in 1943 to R. L. and Dicy Springfield, who in turn sold it the following year to George and Pearl Turney, the last owners before Dobie. A few items from the Turneys' tenure-a clock Turney made from a cast-iron skillet and some wood-burned plaques of dubious artistic merit that amused Dobie (pictures of a grinning sow and a playful longhorn)-are still at the ranch. Dobie first thought of calling his place the Wild Gobbler Ranch, but decided on Paisano, a name of Spanish origin used in the Southwest to denote the roadrunner. Dobie was also familiar with other regional meanings of the word-"compatriot," "native," and "rustic." The roadrunner image, the symbol of the Texas Folklore Society, became Dobie's personal symbol, and he used it on bookplates and elsewhere. Originally, he kept a few cattle and sheep at the ranch, but he later sold them, preferring, as acquaintances recall, the deer and wild turkey and other wildlife found in abundance on the property.
likes: Facilities & Services: Log cabin, stone walls

reviews_attraction.text: This is a rare gem in the Rio Grande Valley. The park currently has a small developed area with much room to grow in the future. Thus far they have walking trails and many viewing sites from which you can see both a wide variety of migratory butterflies as well as common local birds and migratory Birds. Unfortunately, the canal that passes across their property is slated to be the site of the much opposed border wall. This will effectively shut down the capacity for this private park to grow and preserve much-needed Butterfly habitat that is ever shrinking along their migratory corridor. Please get out and support the center. There is a rally to stop the wall at the Santa Ana National Wildlife Refuge on January 27th 2018 from 11 a.m. until 1 p.m. This will be in the field adjacent to the park. Speakers, music, food, and opportunities to take action will be presented to the public. These are beautiful areas and The Last Vestige of the indigenous habitat that the valley once offered before it was plowed for citrus and tract home development.

Nice, well maintained state park nestled in the Davis Mountain Range. Campgrounds fill fast so reserve earlier than you think you need too.  Bathrooms with running water, hot showers.  RV hook up sites with electric and water.  Sites are close together but with the electric access, no one was running generators- my pet peeve.  You do have all the traffic noise funneled into the valley however.  The sky is incredible at night, almost no light pollution.  Javalinas roam the grounds so be aware and clean up after yourself.  Current burn ban at this time, have just finished a prescribed burn.  Do have ice at the bathrooms for donation of $2. Lodge is being renovated so no accommodations there.  Easy hikes throughout the park, completed with the kids in sandals but again, not  14'ers here.  Overall an enjoyable time

Very unique place built by the Civilian Conservation Corps in the 1930s. They have a essentially 3 different pools in one.  the 1st is 3 to 4' deep, the 2nd 25' deep and the 3rd is 20' deep. Several diving boards multiple picnic tables showers changing rooms. Campground is closed you buy a sewer issues. If you want to swim you must show up early otherwise you have to wait for people to leave to get a parking spot. Definitely a must see while you're in the area.   Just heard that there was a significant structural collapse of one of the walls of the pool, requiring draining and only picnic are is open at this time, repairs pending 12-18 months
likes: Multiple facilities (picnic tables, showers, changing rooms)

reviews_attraction.text: This is an amazing gem to still have in the center of McAllen. Preserved from the 1920s, this historic house and property are filled with botanic specimens from around the world primarily South and Central America. The grounds are filled with a wide variety of sculptures. The historic house has been well-preserved. Rooms are filled with artifacts and informative displays perfect for visitors of all ages. A side shop has some reptile specimens and Taxidermy specimens. Fun for all ages, staff was well-informed everything was very clean. A complete departure from what you normally find in the valley.

Surprising zoo for Brownsville. They had a diverse collection of exotic and endangered animals. 1800 species most of which are the last remaining pairs of their kind. There are bathrooms and shade breaks everywhere come in and the giant loop is broken up into multiple air conditioned buildings for when it is 103ﾟ outside. The kids had a great time, some of the enclosures were small in sparse and definitely in need of environments to simulate natural ones. Over all, it looks like they are doing a very good job. Would definitely return.

Nice . Small children's museum in Brownsville. Nice park directly outside. Price is reasonable $8 for anybody over the age of 1. There is also a museum of clothing of the Americas next store, admission is free on Sunday and free with admission to the children's museum. Most of the play is food centered and the kids really seem to enjoy that aspect. Just 1 room not extensive as the doceum in San Antonio or the Thinkery in Austin. However it's nice and close as well as being close to the zoo. Would definitely recommend.

A very interesting Park. Like other reviewers have stated there are more law enforcement officers here than visitors. You can see that Mexican side of the Border clearly and two floating dry docks Mark the international boundary. Expect to see fast Department of Public Safety boats intervening when craft attempt to cross the line. Did not see much in the way of wildlife but there are several playgrounds for kids and a boat dock plenty of people fishing lots of tables and grills. Plenty of public restrooms.

A surprising Hidden Gem in the City of Edinburg. Well laid-out and Landscape pads Meander through a myriad number of Botanical specimens. Feels like the resource of a very much larger City. Unique with in Edinburg. Teaching Center has a variety of exhibits. Standard gift shop with books and stuffed animals for the kids. Will allow you to rent binoculars if you exchange your photo ID. To holding ponds and canals are good viewing spots for wildlife. Overall an enjoyable experience with children.

Have multiple programs for the public both during the day and at night.  We signed up for an hour long informative talk in the auditorium prior to the star watch portion outside.  Unfortunately, sky occluded with clouds.  Staff were quick to offer alternate learning activities or offer people a chance to reschedule or a refund.  A great resource for  anyone with an interest in astronomy.  Kids really enjoyed the activities.  We will reschedule and hopefully be back when its not so cloudly.

By far the most diverse setting and highest concentration of animals Ive seen in the birding center network in the lower RGV. Awesome botanical specimens, labeled. Restroom. 5 entry for adults, children are free.  Very nice boardwalk system takes you out over the largest wetland habitat in the network.  Trails are easily accessed and wide.  Bikes allowed. back side has alligator pond with viewing platform. The state has done a very nice job with this park.

Nice hidden little gem within the city. My understanding was that this was a former for tanical gardens, however due to funding and what not it was let go in now is just a nature preserve. One and a 1/2 or so miles of crushed granite gravel trails, great to get out for the family, all the local Flora and fauna you'd expect, functional bathrooms, over all a pretty nice place

Always wanted to stop and finally got the chance. Definently some abnormal thought process going into this one. Beautiful though. So sad to hear the tower named after the baby died in 1984 And anyone who stands for themselves deserves credit,this guy has dealt with just about everything m

It is a mixed bag that this mural has been re painted. Part of the charm of art like this is its ephemeral Quality. Making it a landmark that will be there for ever and ever takes away from the original strength of the composition I believe. But whatever, lots fun super cool

Water park is old and worn out. Resort is a misnomer.  From to mold growing on ceiling to to bathroom door that touches the toilet, you can do much better for a much more reasonable price. Waiting for a hurricane to clear this one out

Nice park, easy to access. Raid off the road in monument. We visit often. Will continue to do so. Park maintenance is spotty. But monument as a whole doesn't seem to invest much in maintenance of infrastructure.

Awesome amenities,  variety of traits. If its warm enough bring the inner tubes. Every thing was clean and well maintained. Helpful campground hosts. Watch for the wild turkeys. Great time for all ages
Only in city parks can you watch entire drunk families have hot dog fights while arguing if grand child is pregnant with number 6 or seven. The water is great and the spill over a lot of fun
Not the wild west but every building has a story to tell.  Touristy now but get out and walk the alley ways. The taste of the dust hasn't changed in 200 years. Same with character of people
4 dollars an adult, minimal  history presented. Attendant rude but it was hot so... Whatever. Would be  nice to see further info on role it played in civil and Mexican American wars.
Great technical rock. Some north shore elements out there if you find them. Tons of fun. Protect the trails and watch for others who don't know basic trail rules. Shin guards!
Nice older park. City park on one side of river and county on the other. You can see the debris in the trees from flash flooding. Park was nice. Town has a lot of potential
Classic Colorado springs. Preferred it 20 years ago before it was really upgraded. Super crowded, if you want to hike or run go really early or when therescsome snow
Very cool park. A little of something for everyone. Easy to access and the kids had a great time on the playground equipment. Will definitely return.
Some of the most technical riding in the area. Lots of rock gardens, hair pins. Be polite and share the trail. Whomp whomp!

Lots of work and investment needed to make some of the older rides more state of the art. Jurassic Park ride needs a major facelift with more interactive dinosaurs. What's the point of the Poseidon ride -- no clue! People actually left in the middle of the show and shouted "lame". The Harry Potter area and Kong Skull Island are the real attractions. The rest is fluff with little value to most. Seuss land is good for the very young tots.

Excellent tour guides who are passionate about explaining the historical struggle for civil rights in the United States, particularly the South. Educational journey explains the context and the aftermath of the Greensboro sit-in in 1960 and the impact on the bigger movement. Photography is restricted and limited inside, so bear that in mind. Groups can be large but guides do all they can to accommodate large tours. Highly recommend.

Excellent Presidential library in the heart of Dallas. The amount of visitors underscores how much President Bush was loved and is still admired. Knowledgeable staff, so much so they are almost too much -- kind of like the grandparent that can't stop reminiscing. I did find admission cost and refreshment costs excessive. Also, no leniency when closing time comes -- they will escort you out.

You shouldn't have to worry about your dog's safety when you go to a dog park, but unfortunately, here you do. On several occasions, an abundance of aggressive dogs, particularly pit bulls, have hurt or terrified my dog and other dogs and their owners. It's an area way from the main road so little policing, and the owners of the aggressive dogs show little concern.

Beautiful, well-maintained fields that attract a lot of visitors. Do come early to avoid crowds and heat. Several varieties are planted from multi-branching to dwarf to mammoth Russian sunflowers. Expect to spend 40 to 60 minutes or more exploring the many rows and paths. Lots of good picture spots. Watch for bees and please don't pick or destroy any sunflowers.

Excellent, well-tended gardens next to WRAL studios and NC State. The size of the gardens is astounding, and one has to wonder about the investment of love and labor for the many beautiful plants and bird feeders. The gardens attract a lot of photographers, amateur and professional, so plan ahead to come at an off-peak time during the week.

Fantastic, modern museum on the Baylor campus with interactive exhibits for visitors from young to old. Really affordable as well at $8 for adults and $6 for children (12 and younger). The mammoth dig site recreation is very realistic and check out the village behind the museum for a glimpse of life a century ago.

If you a geeky science type, this is a great museum that helps explain the complexity of splitting atoms and how Oak Ridge played a central role in atomic energy and the first A-bomb. Lots of interactive exhibits and educational diagrams. I do miss the larger space of the previous location.

Wow - clean bathrooms and friendly gate staff! A nice, local state park near Wichita Falls. Crappie fishing just starting to pick up in early March with high water levels, and you cant beat fishing for free in Texas state parks. Don't miss Prairie Dog Town, just down from the fishing pier.

A beautiful, historical state park that has personal significance to me. Note the need to hike several miles to get to the falls. Many steps so be prepared or plan to take some aspirin afterwards. Beautiful year round but expect large crowds in the summer. Knowledgable park staff.

Great place to understand the US history in space flight. Staff fairly knowledgeable. Only issue was confiscation of a fingernail clipper -- not sure why this was not allowed! Long, long wait for shuttle simulator which probably isn't worth it. Revising rating to 4 stars.

Terrific exhibit and ranger presentation on the mammoth and animal find at this site. Short, brief tour but worth the time. The biggest issue is parking -- very limited, especially at busy times. Site averages 350 people per day but can exceed 800 visitors on busy days.

Great docent and park ranger interaction despite the constant stream of tourists and repetitive questions. They obviously love what they do. Definitely take time to listen to longer walking tour to understand the connections to famous people and events of the Civil War.

Pretty lake and park spoiled by visitors who don't pick up dog waste after their pets and like to throw rocks and trash onto the ice. Needs to be more closely monitored. Otherwise, trail is nice and wide and cir les the lake. Some drone users in the park.

History lives here on the old Chisholm trail. Learn how thousands of cattle once crossed this bridge on the way to Abilene, Kansas. Roebling helped build this bridge before building the Brooklyn Bridge. Nice statues commemorating this landmark.

This is a nice museum but several exhibits closed or not available. Seems like a waste of $7 per adult with roughly half of the museum with inaccessible. Plus, there's the cost of parking. What was available for touring was nicely presented.

Even on a snowy day, it's a nice place to visit. First parking lot is under construction but there are other lots further up that are open. Trails can be slippery in the snow, so bring hiking boots and walking stick.

Nice aquarium, even if small. I would like it more if the nickel-and-diming for photos and trinkets wasn't as intense -- the kids working here shouldn't be high pressure salesmen but focused on marine conservation.

Great place to gather for 4th of July fireworks. Family oriented and nice lake to fish. Near Womble Park. Expect crowds for fireworks and have plenty of patience upon exiting. City police do their best.
Very comprehensive museum of the Titanic that doesn't feel cheap or exploiting. Staff are well trained and polite. You can truly learn about the ship, the crew, and the passengers.
Really like the audio tour by cell phone. Nice historical battlefield with walking tour. Informational placards. Have some insect repellent handy for mosquitoes.
Best place to get a great view of Big D. Don't count on going up to the restaurant unless you have a reservation. Generally clean and staff accommodating.
Much history here with the church and surrounding grave stones. Well kept but not always well respected by visitors. Take some time and breathe it in.
Beautiful national monument with good hiking trails. Snow cover can make it challenging but it's worth it. Careful on one lane road coming in.
Great place for a walk. Lots of nature but I-40 nearby can be noisy. There is fishing but a warning sign says don't eat them.

We took our little one here.  Great experience for a young one.  Shamu show was different from when I was a kid.  The pool seems so small for the several orcas they have.  They should build up the lake and turn it into a sea life exhibit.  Would give the large orcas more room.  Otherwise get rid of the orcas.  Little one loved the sea lion show, one guy tried really hard to be Chris Farley.  Otherwise it was entertaining.  All the rides in the Sesame Street area are perfect for little ones and the water pad was a hit.  Prices for drinks and snacks were not as bad as I thought they would be.  Free refills for plastic cups.  SeaWorld really should add filtered water stations around the park to fill up your personal water bottles.  Especially since they are running on the "SeaWorld cares" theme.  Lots of plastic in use.  We rode the Rescue coaster, line was fast, ride was fast and there were videos of SW rescues to watch while you wait.  We walked right up the Steel Eel.  Not too fast of a ride but still fun.  We missed a few areas and will probable return.

Kiddos can go crazy in the enclosed park area.  Running and jumping all over the place.  Nice rubber ground all around the play area.  Lots of room and I love the bridge for a different perspective.  Would be nice to have an ice cream truck or snow cone stand nearby.  The smoothie truck did not go over well with my little one.  People with dogs really should stick to the dog area.  I saw a dog in the kids splash pad and then I saw another dog use the beautiful flower areas to do their business.
dislikes: Lack of ice cream or snow cone stand
Presence of dogs in non-dog areas

reviews_attraction.text: The coolest place in Houston on a summer afternoon.  Walk into the stadium portion and you feel like you are being transported to another dimension. I kind of got motion sickness staring up to the sky with the water flowing down.  If you get close enough, you do get damp.  The green space in front is lovely, the kiddos have a great time playing.  We parked at Williams Tower visitor parking and paid a small fee, you can park for free at the Galleria but you have to deal with the traffic.

Large park on Hammerly near the Beltway.  Three pools, one for children, one for diving and a large pool for adults with a pacing lane.  There are outdoor rinsing showers.  Several lifeguards on duty.  The restrooms have several stalls and one changing room.  Very basic facilities.  Bring a chair for the pool area.  There are not many seating options.  The park has a covered basketball courts, very well attended when we were there.  There is a play area for the kids and disk golf.

Park is large and would be lovely to visit if not for the neighborhood and the interesting people in the parking lot.  Reviews for this park are not positive as far as safety, so I was on edge the time we were there.  Several men were sitting alone in their cars throughout the parking lot.  Lots of families were there, but they did not stay long.  I may return again if there is an organized event.

Artsy park off of 45 and near the Orange show.  Three large swings for the family.  Interesting artwork all over.  Love how they up-cycle pieces that would otherwise be thrown out.  A great way to spend time looking for hidden objects in the art walls.  Not a lot of parking.  There were not restrooms when we went, those with children may need breaks before and after visit.

The kids will go crazy with excitement running around learning about space travel.  The parents will enjoy themselves as well.  Lots to see definitely need a full day.  We are making plans for our next visit.  The facility boasts its available space for parties and other events, hopefully I'll be invited to experience what looks to be a fantastic and unique event space.

Discovery Green is the best outdoor park in downtown Houston.  We visit several times a year for outdoor movies, holiday lights, splash pad and the play ground.  We really enjoyed the summer music program hosted by UH this past summer.  It is a great place to pack a lunch/dinner, grab a blanket and let the kiddos run wild.  Beautiful art throughout the park.

Historic train ride through the mountains.  We did the half day option.  Open sided cars available as well as enclosed.   There is a stop at the end to get out take pictures and view the engine and caboose.  The engineer is knowledgeable and gives a narrative throughout most of the trip.  Lots of information was given.  Beautiful scenery.

We like visiting Donovan park, just wish there were restrooms available.  Across Heights Blvd are several restaurants and shops for a quick restroom run and break.  Kids love all of the wooden play areas.  The train is a hit with all ages.  Plenty of shade.  Very well attended.  Gates to keep the kiddos in.

Too many "tour guides" around bothering you.  We were having a conversation about the history of the area as we know it but someone kept bothering us trying to sell us tours and newspapers.  There are markers for the events that took place there in the middle of the street.

Fun little park in downtown Houston.  There is a dog walking area.  Water falls/tranquility area.  The Niko Niko's is delicious and offers patio seating.  The city offers Friday night events and movies.  Within walking distance to other venues and restaurants in downtown.

Large park near 610 and 18th street.  Lots of play ground equipment and a splash pad for the kids.  Disc golf facilities, tennis, basketball and baseball field.  There are port-o-potty's for use.  Lots of parking.  We enjoyed Jaycee park and will return.

Really nice size park in west Houston/Energy corridor.  Plenty of playground equipment, 1 side for smaller kids and other side is for larger kiddos & both are fenced in! Nice walking path around the large park.  Pavilion and private area for parties.

Fun Casino.  Lots of different gaming options.  Staff is patient on the off hours.  Will give you pointers if you are a novice.  Free drinks are ok, better off buying your drinks.  Loved the Walking Dead seated game.

Large park near Memorial drive and Stafford high school.  Early voting location.  Fun kids playground.  Water area that sometimes work.  Picnic tables and walking loop.  Parking lot and curb parking available.

Nice facility.  Museums are well staffed and provide lots of information for Texas history.  You have to pay extra for the Star of the Republic but it is worth it.  Nice grounds at Washington on the Brazos.
Lovely Park in Oak Forest.  Lots of families playing at the playground.   Nice size community room that can be rented out for events.  Lots of parking available.   Restrooms are not always available.
Beautiful views.  We went when it was extremely windy.  Great area to see marmot and elk.  Nice hike, it was only rough due to weather conditions and altitude otherwise it was a paved trail.
One of the best parks in Houston.  So much to do, from the paddle boats to the train, to just walking around the grounds.  You could easily spend a full day at the park and not get bored.
Beautiful cathedral in the heart of downtown.   Everyone is friendly and inclusive.  Private free parking located across the street.  Beautiful architecture.  Beautiful music and organ.
Lovely farm area and living history tours.  The Barrington farm is a great place to spend the day away from the city.  Large sized area and usually not a lot of people.
Love the updates.  Reminds me of other city's central gardens.  Clean restrooms.   Beautiful views of the museum district.  Rental areas for weddings and events.
Cute public park located in midtown.  Right next to the metro train.  Swings and play area for kids and grow ups.  Large parking facility below, cheap parking.
Great neighborhood park.  One of the only parks we go to that has open restrooms.  Playground area is enclosed which is appreciated.

This is an amazing place. We have stayed here overnight at least 3 times and it has been the experience of a lifetime. The staff is super friendly and helpful with any questions. The place is beyond creepy and confirm without a doubt it is haunted. The lights go out and spirits come out. Worth a stop! Always book in advance this place is very busy. Get their early on the overnight tours the shop is only open before your tour.
Make a trip!

Awesome overnight investigation. This place is so creepy and has a very amazing vibe to it. It is well worth the overnight tour if you have time. The staff was super helpful and friendly. It was one of the creepiest places I have ever been to. We experienced so much paranormal creepiness. If you are a non believer or a believer this place will change your view regardless.
Great job!

This is a very nice place to spend some time. There is a lot of neat animals here and they seem to very well taken care of. I do wish the zoo was free like some others we have visited. It is worth every penny, since the overall experience was amazing. The staff was super nice and the place is very well maintained. If you are in this area, it is well worth the small admission fee.

Such an amazing place that gives you great views of the city. The view is almost even better and night and you are able to see how far the lights of the city reach and view over the lake and navy pier. It such an amazing experience. It is best when it is not peak time as it took over 2 hours to get the tour completed. But it was well worth it in the end.

We took the tour here and it was an amazing experience. It was well worth the money to see the history and the legend behind the Kentucky derby. If you are ever in Louisville I would stop by and take the tour. You would not regret it. The ladies giving the tour were also the best in the business and were super professional.
Good job!

We took the tour here and it was an amazing experience. It was well worth the money to see the history and the legend behind the Kentucky derby. If you are ever in Louisville I would stop by and take the tour. You would not regret it. The ladies giving the tour were also the best in the business and were super professional.
Good job!

We had an amazing time here. The kids really enjoyed this place. It is well worth the time spent here. If you are on a family vacation this is one of the stops that you need to make. Your kids will thank you. The staff was super friendly as well. It was kept very clean and they are very interactive with the guests.

This is one cool sculpture. While I had it known as the bean, it is a masterpiece all of its own. It is very easy to go to and there is lots of other things in this park to see as well. You have to make you take the picture here. This place is always crowded so be quick and see a great piece of Chicago.

Place is very crowded. It is an amazing place to see and we learned a lot of history here. We even got a space suit for my toddler son to use this Halloween. It was so adorable to pass up.  A lot of exhibits were closed when we were here which was disappointing but overall it was an amazing experience.

Very nice place. The art and the design of the building is superb. It has a lot of history while still being able to be modern. The old state capitol is also a good place to visit if you wanna see another piece of Illinois History. Easy parking and very nice staff.

We had such a great time here and we got to see some amazing things. This place is amazing for families and being around lake Michigan helps with view and makes it all even more amazing. Parking was a breeze and was very easy to get thru. We enjoyed out time here.

This is such a neat place with lots of things to see and the view from the top is amazing. I have a new phone so I did not get all my pictures but I can tell you it is a view of lifetime. The ride up is a little small and tight but it is well worth the time.

We went here while we were in Louisville and it was amazing and glimpse of what this city has to offer. The person giving the tour was professional and the drinks that were made were amazing as well. The staff overall was super friendly and helpful.

Amazing place. You can even save on parking by the planetarium. It is free but it well worth seeing it from the other side. The staff is super helpful and there is a lot of things for the kids to see. Well worth a visit.

We took a tour here and it was an amazing experience. We learned so much about the history of Lincoln and everything that happened here. Would recommend to anyone looking to learn a little more about our 16th president.

There is some great history here. The location is so iconic and it brings up so many of the things you learned in history. It takes you that step back in time. If you are visiting here, this is a go to stop.

Very nice place. It has so much to offer here and the overall experience here was excellent. Well worth the stop. Thanks everyone for the service. It is very well maintained. The staff is super friendly.

Very nice place to visit and see. It offers great views and it gives a look to all Hannibal has to offer. If you are walking from the bottom going up might be the hardest part, but it is well worth it.
We had an amazing time. The service was excellent and we ended up seeing so much stuff. We were presently surprised. It is super clean. The staff did an excellent job at answering our 100 questions.
This is a very nice piece of Illinois and US history. You get to step back in time and get see what Lincoln had gone thru. It is a very good place to bring the whole family!
Place was closed when we were here last but when we did go a couple of years ago the place is amazing and give you a look at this beautiful capital of America.
Beautiful park in historic downtown Quincy. It has nice scenery and a it is a good place to take the kids. There is so much to do around here
Always love coming to this place when I come to Louisville. It is amazing to see this history. Also to see the amazing relics. Awesome staff
Neat place! And it is amazing to see and the view is incredible. Plus place is haunted which is a plus for me.
Haunted as can be. The place is beautiful and it is a must see if you are in the area.

They have gotten super elaborate and high tech with their props but have lost some of the scare factor in the process. They need more attractions to spread out the crowd or they need to sell less tickets. The lines are way too long and $25 a person is too much to pay to skip the line after paying $40 already. It is not worth $65 it is barley worth the $40 these days. If you are worried about COVID don't go at all. There are no precautions here at all. Thousands of people standing in line with no distancing full carts on the hay ride including people in the middle. The hand sanitizer stations were empty. Due to bottlenecks on the trails and in the houses a guests are right on top of each other and the actors yell in your face and touch you quite a bit. I personally don't care but lots of people do and should know this before they decide to pay for a ticket.

This is a super fun place to go. Feeding an interesting variety of animals is a  riot. The little birds are our favorite. They sit on your hands and eat the seeds off the little sticks. We could do that all day . The giraffe feeding feels like feeding a dinosaur. The drive through gets way too crowded so you spend a lot of time just sitting in traffic doing nothing. Hold on to your bucket tight when feeding the lage animals because the go for the bucket instead of the food to try and pull it away from you. Llamas and alpacas spit if the get mad so give them food or put your window up to avoid a very stinky surprise. Try to save some food for the animals towards the end they are less aggressive and are still hungry later in the day because most people are out by that time.

Best observation deck in the city. The I Pad we got with our combo ticket was worth the extra couple of dollars once we figured out how to use them. This view is much higher than the empire state building or Top of the Rock plus it is in lower Manhattan so you get a good view looking back at the city. The elevator ride was super fast so if you have ear problems beware it might be a bit uncomfortable. There is a video played on the entire inside of the elevator that makes the ride pretty cool. Enjoy it is a great experience!!
dislikes: Uncomfortable for those with ear problems

reviews_attraction.text: The house is in pretty good condition complete with original furniture. The tour guide was very good and loud enough for the large group to hear. The cats are  bonus.  Not all of the cats are friendly but many are and love the attention. Just approach with caution and let them decide. The gift shop is small but there were a few items worth looking at. Not too expensive to enter so worth doing at least once

Parking lot is very small. The sand is not that soft but If you can find a spot it is a pretty nice beach. We found lots of good shells just off shore in the shallow water. We also saw manatee dolphins and starfish. There are a ton of fish large and small around the rocks. You will need snorkeling gear to see them and find the shells. We really enjoyed it

This is a nice beach. White sand not too crowded. You can walk the beach for a really long way. Snack bar food was good and not crazy priced. Bathrooms were pretty clean and there are showers to rinse off. The fairy ride was smooth and the crew was entertaining. You do only get 4 hours tho wich is kind of short but definitely worth a trip out there.

This is a well built challenging course  that is very inexpensive to play. The rockwall was super fun as well with a ton of interesting elements for all skill levels. The ice cream shop had a large variety of flavors to choose from and was the perfect ending to a fun night climbing and golfing. I wish we had something like this closer to my house

Nice place to shop and eat while on your beach vacation. The stores sell an interesting mix of items that you might not find other places. If you are looking for gifts check this place out. Everything closes fairly early so don't wait to go late in the day and you have pay to park so keep track of your meter time.

Great stop on any trip down skyline drive. The Rangers have the answers to all your questions with fliers and maps that they highlight for you to show whatever you want to do. The museum is pretty informative with a nice short movie. The store is kind of small but it has all the basics

This is a fairly small aquarium but the little sea turtles are worth the visit all by themselves. The staff is very knowledgeable and answered all of our questions ( we had a lot of questions) definitely worth the price of admission and does not take that long to complete.

Very well thought out and put together. Challenging but not so hard that you give up trying to figure it out. We did get a little help along the way but solved all the puzzles in time to escape. Always a fun time for a small group of your smartest friends 😄

The overlook was beautiful with a great view of the dam we have heard so much about. My wife was impressed with the cute women's bathroom inside the round building. The visitor center was however closed so we did not look around at anything else
