The zoo is small and expensive but you do get an up close view of all the animals. The aviary is the best part of the zoo because there are a ton of birds in a small area so there is activity all the time
Beautiful view from the overlook. The parking lot is a bit treacherous to exit. It is on a curve in the road and the traffic moves at a very high rate of speed so when you leave hit the gas and pray.
Due to some ongoing renovation a large portion of the fort cannot be viewed. The areas we were able to see seem very well preserved. We will probably come  back when these areas reopen
Gorgeous beach with powder white sand. There is however a lot of standing water around the park so bugs can be an issue. Bring bug spray if you are visiting early or late.
This is a super cool place filled with hundreds of butterflies and beautiful little birds. We could spend all day here just watching them fly around and eat
Crowded and lots of seaweed but the beach is long and the water is clear and beautiful. Very shallow so you can walk out pretty far before it gets deep.
Nice park with a small beach boat ramps and activities you can book. The snorkeling trip to the statue   was fun. It can get crowded so get there early
Parking is $2.75 an hour. The beach is narrow but long. There is no public restroom. The sand is white and powdery. Water is fairly clear and calm.
Not a ton to see but what they have is fun and interesting. The observation deck has an amazing view. Worth a stop if you are in the area
Great place to view the sunset. Great street performers. It is however super crowded so that takes away from the enjoyment a bit
Nice park but parking could use an upgrade. The lots are small so when they are full you have to park in the muddy field
It's a bit expensive but there is a lot to see and do here. Use a coupon to save a few dollars
Kind of cheesy but still a fun picture. The line can get long so try to go early or late

Love the sights, sounds, smells and food on the main drag here.  Dodeconese Blvd is  full of great shopping and eateries from Greek to seafood.  Boat excursions on the Anclote River are available too.  The side streets near Momma's Restaurant are full of great places to buy authentic Greek food and spices to take home.  We always eat at momma's and follow up with coffee and dessert at Hellas bakery.  Love to visit Tarpon and bring all of our visitors there when they're in the area.  Be sure to get some of those amazing sponges.  There really is a difference!  I only use the natural sponges after trying them.  Don't miss the Tarpon Springs sponge dock experience.
likes: Facilities & Services: Shopping, eateries, boat excursions

reviews_attraction.text: Loved this park because of the great views of the Statue of liberty and Manhattan.  There's also Ellis island and tours of the area by boat.   A must see for descendants of immigrants who entered the country through the island.   A boat ride to and around the Statue of liberty is a great experience for anyone of any age.  Lots of parking space and many amenities nearby including a marina and the Liberty Science Center.  You'll feel the history in the air here!

Great location and plenty of eateries nearby.  Go for a stroll in the park,  have lunch and return.  Beautiful plants, birds and fish.  Numerous exotic trees and turtles.  Photo ops galore! Gift shop has some unique and unusual options.  There's even a water bottle filling stations and clean large restrooms.  A nice place to stay in the shade and enjoy some peace and quiet in the middle of the city.

Great small town park with a playground for the kids. There's a perennial garden for your family.   Many plants are designed to attract butterflies and there were lots there.   The park is surrounded by a trail and makes a good hike that's not too long.   You can join a community garden that has a waiting list.   Look but don't touch the vegetables and flowers grown by local people.

Absolutely do not miss this place! What an amazing experience in the sphere- a 3D movie experience.  You feel like you can touch the whales in the movie! Tons of great other stuff to see too! Many viewing stations under ground and even a glass tube you walk under the ocean as manta rays and other fish swim over your head! Another must see place for visitors! Don't miss it!

Never can get enough of this place. Mackerel Cove is one of the most picturesque places in Maine.  This park is small but it's a public space that allows you to park, picnic and take in the fantastic views.  Also a wonderful perspective to photograph the the cove with an unobstructed view at water level.   So hang out for a while and enjoy the open public space

We really had fun taking pictures here. Parts of the park were closed due to ice.  We'll have to come back when we can go on the bridges and get some more great photos.  The park is located in the middle of the city and is quite unique.   There's a visitor center and some statues.  Overall it is an interesting experience and like a window to the past.

Amazing ferry features a beautiful view of the pictured rocks.  Lots of photo ops.  Friendly staff.  If you're prone ro motion sickness you may want to check out the weather reports and medicate! Wet weather gear is a great help if you're planning to sit up top outside.  A great experience if you plan ahead.  Our tour was about 2 and a half hours.

Beautiful place to spend time together with family and friends. Many photos ops and beautiful gardens to enjoy. The tower is impressive and so is the mansion. Beautiful vistas from the hilltop by the tower. Great selection of food in the cafe (pricey but good) and we enjoyed the day there

Nice way to spend some low key time in the Charleston SC area.  Enjoyed the visit and the gardens.  Best of all- it's a national park service site.  Feel free to make a donation since there's no charge for admission.
Nice place for an evening stroll.  Last time I was there I saw 4 Manatees.  There's a pier and it's equipped for fisherman with gutting sinks etc.  Public bathroom is usually clean.  Great photo ops.
Great skate board loops, curls, jump and tunnel, among other things.  Attached to a ballpark and a great kid's park with swings, slides and jungle gym among other things that kids enjoy playing on.
Large fort and great sites and views.  The whole island is picturesque and offers plenty of choices for shopping, food and drinks.  Overnight a accommodations are available if you plan ahead.
This is a county park and charges$5 to park.  If you're a resident you can buy an annual pass.  Great Beach and has bathrooms and changing rooms. cabanas and chairs are available for rental
Lots of activities here.  Part of the national Park service.  Revolving exhibits and beautiful grounds.  River Walk along the bank provided some terrific views and photo ops.
Great place to visit with your family and friends.   There were over a hundred manatees the day we were there. Well managed site with great views and amenities
Great location on Indian Shores beach. It's a country park covered by the Pinellas county park pass.  Free access to the beach.   Lots of parking.
Great Beach and picnic areas.  Close to tarpon springs.  Parking is covered by the Pinelas Country Parks pass or $5 a day at electronic kiosks
Location on the bay is good for walking.  Nice picnic areas with tables.  You can reserve a pavilion.  Has bathrooms and hiking trails.
Beautiful waterfront park.  Numerous photo ops.  Walk on the pier for free.  Sit on a bench and sip coffee while you enjoy the views!
Large land preservation with lots of different types of plants trees animals and birds.  Hunting by permits at certain times of year
Great venue for food drinks and music.  Lots of great choices for places to eat and then shop!  Music was interesting...
Part of Phillipe park great hiking trails and picnic facilities.  The bayfront park area offers a view of Tampa  bay.
Beautiful centerpiece of Morristown!  Sit and watch the people go by.  Take a break from all there is to do nearby
Fun island that some tours out of Tarpon Springs visit.  You can also get there with your own boat or jet ski

Came in on a Saturday evening in our 28 ft. Heartland Wilderness.  This is our second time here.  We brought hybrid Giant bikes so we could do some trails for the first time.  301-303.  Trail around the Lake was good.  Since we were camping in the Creekside Campground we decided to take 303.  We discovered we were going straight up the whole time.  Had to push our bikes, but came down on the highway--super fast🤪  We love this state park.  BTW everyone GREAT about social distancing in campground, not so much beach/picnic areas.🙏

Beautiful! Totally worth the $8 entry fee.  This doesn't feel like a State Park though without campsites.   The Natural Bridge pictures do not do it justice.  We also liked the Native American living history.   The saltpeter mine had an interesting history.  On the walk to Fancy Waterfall we were fortunate to see a Blue Herron "fishing" for his lunch.  He was successful.   The cascading stream to Fancy Waterfall was beautiful.   This park has ample benches to sit to rest or reflect. Highly recommend if you have never been.

Deep Lake Campground at Yankee Springs Recreation Area

Vault toilets "stank"
They need to be emptied or some kind of solution to take care of smell.  Other Michigan recreation areas do a much better job with their vault toilets.

Site #6 not level, but we made it work with our 28 ft. travel trailer.  Sites 1, 3, 5 wete flatter..  Vault toilet located other side of #5.  We like recreation areas because of more privacy.

Covid rules in place.  Camped for 3 nights in nice shady spot next to bathhouse.  Bathhouses need remodeling, but clean.  Plenty of shade. Sweltering hot.

Limited on what kids can do because of Covid 19.  No access to playground.  Grands rode their bikes, went swimming (no beach or diving or paddle boats), played putt-putt (bro't own clubs & balls), campfire pizza and smores.

Loved this state park.  Nice wide sites (tent pad with tt/rv spot).  Can totally disconnect and go hiking, see wildlife and fish.  Bathhouse maintained and clean.  Only 2 handicap sites have full hook up.  The rest is water and 30/50 amp electricity.  Highly recommend.  Hiking trails are nice and wide and maintained.  Loved falls, Stone Mtn vistas and Homestead.  Cool & shady.

Stayed at Elk Creek campground from Sunday before Labor Day until Friday.  Once the Labor Day crowd headed home. We had no neighbors for 5 days.😁😁😁 flushed toilets,  no electric or water hookups. We visited Black Canyon South Rim,  East Portal,  North Rim every day we were there. GREAT time hiking, picnicking and taking tons of pics.

Love the shady sites.  Bathhouse needs major renovations.  Also, we came in after 5 and had a very frustrating time finding where the green post were.  We had to totally come out of the campground and start all over.  Our 29 foot trailer made it impossible to make turns.  The map is way too small.

BEAUTIFUL fall colors along Lake Ontario.  Sites around 248 have more space between campsites.  In the rest of the park the campers are on top of each other.  Between colors and our site privacy, this was a perfect weekend.  Behind our campsite you can walk to the cliffs that once had a beach.

Love the large, flat sites, and clean bath house.  Wish there was heat in the bath house, but the hot water for showers helps.

Our site #1 is a corner site with water and electric.  It is only a very short distance to the bath house.  The campgrounds are perfect for running.

Very humbling and saddened as we listened to 40 bios of the crew and passengers of Flight 93.  This memorial to these brave individuals was inspiring and heartbreaking as you listen to their calls to their loved ones.  So many precious lives taken too soon and so brutally.
likes: Activities: Listening to bios, Calls to loved ones

reviews_attraction.text:
I LOVE this campground.  Nice, clean big bath houses.  Very shady and great place to see sunset on Lake Michigan if you can catch it not cloudy.

Our 28 ft. trailer fit nicely on #A11.  Was concerned road on 3 sides of our site, but during the week no problem with privacy.

Just visited the lighthouse.  Road to lighthouse and lighthouse was worth the 2 mile walk.  You can also bicycle it..  Must have Michigan sticker to get in..

Vault toilet stunk.  Needs cleaned and pumped out.  Walked thru campground.  Sites are on top of each other.

Just arrived today.  Sites are flat with pea gravel, picnic table, fire ring, water, electric and dump station are provided.  Most sites have vegetation/trees between sites.  Not on lake and not a very pretty park compared to NC/SC/GA state parks, very large park.
likes: Provided facilities (picnic table, fire ring, water, electric, dump station)

reviews_attraction.text: Bathhouse needs updating, but nice and clean.  Beautiful campground with beach area right on Lake Huron.  We loved the bike trail from Presque Isle Lighthouse to Roger's City.  We also enjoyed 40 Mile Point Lighthouse Park and Ocqueoc Falls nearby.

We camped at Muskegon State Park just down the road.  Some locals recommended Duck Lake for some nice hiking.  They were so right.  Wish we had brought our bicycles.  Nice well maintained trails and the leaves are starting to change.

Mr. Klein & family, the resident on one side of the lighthouse, was very hospital and informative.  Love how they have made it their home with a vegetable garden and chickens.  Also, the remnants of a shipwreck was very interesting.

BEAUTIFUL!  Just hate our camping schedule didn't coincide with Maroon Bells in the Fall.  Took the free bus to Asphen Highlands and then bought Sr. $6 shuttle passes on ip to Maroon Belles.  Enjoyed the short hikes and beauty.

When I went, filming for a movie had some of the rooms unavailable.  Would have been a nice substitute to see some "behind" scenes rooms.  Pam, our guide, was very knowledgeable and accommodating.  5 stars.
Muddy sites.  Need more gravel to be added.   Site #9 picnic table and fire ring too far from travel trailer--too heavy to move.  Can hear traffic from nearby highway.  Very clean bathhouse.
This is such a unique national park.  Recommendation all the 3 Cliff dwelling tours @$5.  Very knowledgeable rangers!  Now when I look at mesas I look for possible cliff dwellings.

Sites right on lake need paving, mud puddle when rains
BEAUTIFUL sunset and sunrise
no privacy
due to cars having to park next to road hard to get 28ft in and out of site
It was good, but nothing like Mammoth  Cave in Kentucky or Carlsbad Cavern in New Mexico. A little pricey . . . Loved the young lady who was our guide--jokes were good.
Great place of fun for the family in the Fall.  Plenty of activities, food, music etc.  Ask about when Grandparents Day is.  They get in free.  Highly recommend.
Serene, just what we needed to totally  relax.  Extra nice and clean bath house.   Flat easy to  maneuver backend site#15 with full hookup.
Love visiting historic sites especially lighthouses.  Wished it was open to the public, but it was beautiful from the outside.

This small riverside park is a host to some very interesting industrial sites on the southwest side of Chicago. Canalport Riverwalk is a simple paved walking and biking trail in the Pilsen neighborhood of Chicago. It covers only one side of the river, so if you’re hoping for a looped path, seek a different route. I have only visited this path during mild weather and I’m not sure if it is cleared of snow in the winter. Looks to be wheelchair accessible and the trail is in good shape. There is an overlook where you can watch the metal processing/ recycling center move pieces of scrap metal into piles. Sounds a little bit boring, but it’s actually kind of interesting. There is no boat launch on the riverwalk. Across the way you will also notice the Chicago Yacht Yard. There is no parking for this riverwalk, so it’s best to access by foot, bike, or public transit. I do not believe there are lights along the trail and I did not note any open hours. The park likely closes at dusk. Path was clean and well-maintained, would be a fun place to learn how to ride a bike or roller skate because it is not very busy.

This is the most marvelous park! Came here every morning to ride bikes while we were visiting. Quiet. Beautiful. Peaceful. You can rent bikes at the shop near the rangers station. Snacks, water, etc. can be purchased too. Definitely take home a bottle of the Honeybell orange juice, you will not regret it!!!

This park is such a treasure! The staff is kind and knowledgeable. The park is sparkling clean and easy to access. $10 fee to drive on the blackpoint car path. Loved visiting this area. It’s an absolute must if you’re in the area. Very neat to be able to see the nasa complex from this park.

Incredible park. Didn’t see any buffalo, but also didn’t have the time to hike the entire park. Make sure you have bug spray- with all the beautiful tall grass- the chance for ticks is high. The crushed gravel trails are great for walking, strollers, or bikes. Can’t wait to come back.

This is park has seemingly been closed for years and years. Despite living in Chicago for 6 years, I hadn’t visited this park until recently. I believe the water levels are high and are probably wreaking havoc on the grounds. If you’re ever on the south side, this is a must visit.

This is my favorite park in the city. It’s really clean and there’s bathrooms available in the REI boathouse. Neat walking trail and the park is located next to some really awesome bridges. You can catch the water taxi here too! A must visit!

Great park with lots of covered picnic areas with tables. Small beach. Nice playground. Very clean. Lots of available trash containers for garbage. Benches by the water. Neat birds. Love this park, it’s really pleasant!

Such an amazing park! Parking was tricky on a Saturday afternoon- get there early if you want a spot close to the park to leave your car. Highly recommend visiting, the trails are awesome and kid friendly!
This spot is an amazing resource for Chicagoans. The building itself is gorgeous and the galleries they curate are very thoughtful. Be sure to go to the top floor to be amazed by the ceiling design!
This awesome riverfront park has a community center, playground, exercise equipment, boat launch, and fishing area. Great spot to come and relax and watch the water. Beware: Lots of goose poop.
One of the most amazing botanical gardens. Olmsted really did a great job with this one. The tower is of course the star of the show, but the whole park is charming and clean and lovely.
Absolutely magic space for reflection and art viewing. The museum is free and hosts a variety of events for the neighborhood. Important resource for the community. I love this place.
Very small beach with limited parking. lots of benches. The small piece of beach surrounded by buildings on both sides makes for an intimate space. Not a good spot for swimming.
BEST PLACE IN THE ENTIRE CITY. Provides a much needed space of calm and warmth, especially during the winter months. This place is an invaluable asset to the Chicago community.
One of the best things about Chicago is the 606 trail. An absolute must for anyone that likes being outdoors or loves walking/cycling. Can be crowded on the weekends.
This spot was one of the most magic parts of living in northwest Indiana. Clean beach area and often very busy in the summer months. Large parking lot available.
This beach is great in the summer time. Parking can be tricky during the summer- so if you can come here via public transit that's recommended.
Great resource for the NWI area. This water park is expansive and offers a variety of activities for families with children of all ages.
This is my favorite building in Chicago. It's stark white, a stretched in a way that makes it look like an optical illusion. Very cool!
Such an amazing park with a cool view and quarry that’s been converted into a pond! Highly recommended for picnicking and exercising.
So grateful for this huge green space in downtown Chicago. Love the music I've seen here and the picnics I've had on the grounds.
Nothing beats free! The Zoo lights that they do every year is a favorite holiday activity. Great staff and beautiful grounds!
Super special place. Perfect for super hot days. Seating around the perimeter for those who don’t want to get wet.
Great outdoor space with multiple playgrounds. There's a lot of squirrels at this park and it's fun to watch them.
Iconic sculpture of the Chicago loop- this is a spot you'll want to bring your friends and family for photos!

If you don't want to hassle with parking, you want to learn something about St. Augustine, and you want an easy way to get around, the Old Town Trolley is a great way to do it. Your ticket allows you to ride as little or as much as you want for three days. We ended up waiting, at the most 15-20 minutes, to pick up a trolley at one of our stops, but we found the stops were in very convenient locations and were able to get on and off close to where we wanted to be.

The tour takes about an hour to an hour and a half and allows you to see the main sights (23 in all), including: Ripley's Believe it Or Not Museum, the Shrine to Our Lady and the place where the first Mass was held in North America, the Basilica, the Presbyterian Church build by Flagler, Flagler College, Castillo de San Marcos, and a lot more. Like the other reviewers, I'd recommend getting on the early tour (it begins promptly at 9 am) and taking the entire tour so you can learn the lay of the city and see where everything is. Then you can plan your later excursions accordingly.

The tour guides are each unique and make the ride enjoyable, sharing history, quirky jokes, and even singing. Davey Jones, one of our guides, serenaded us. Marshall, another guide, had great accents that he used in portraying various characters.

Just be aware that the trolley stops running at 5 pm. Many shops and things close then. It's just good to know so that you don't get stuck somewhere with no transportation back to your vehicle. If you're staying at an area hotel, there is a shuttle service that will bring you from your hotel to the trolley visitor center.

I'd highly recommend this for any first-time visitor to St. Aug's.

I almost don't want to review this park so that it stays quiet and the way it is.

Stumbled across this treasure with the family. What a beautiful park. If you like the woods and the river, you'll like Crosby. Named after a historical farm that once sat on the location, this park has picnic tables beneath a shelter, decent bathrooms, and a large fire pit. In addition, you can walk the paved trails (or dirt trails along the Mississippi River). There's also biking trails (Mississippi River Trail system).

We sat along the river's sandy edge and watched worms (Army worms, perhaps) drop down on strands into the river and be gobbled up by fish. It was amusing. We met a fellow hiker and her dog and had some nice conversation with her.

It's hard to believe, when you're in the park, that you're right next to St. Paul. It feels like you're in another, magical world. There's a path along the river; one through the woods, and another that is a wetland trail. Your children will love this place.

One word of advice: stay on the paths. As this is the Mississippi River flood plain, the woods are filled with wood nettle, a plant that will give you a stinging rash if you walk through it.

Warner Lake is a county park that offers a lot. There aren't a lot of nice lake beaches real close to St. Cloud. This park offers a great trail that goes around the small lake - perfect for an afternoon hike with the family. Along the way, you'll discover a creek with a walking bridge, the outdoor center, and enjoy the scenery. There's also a large picnic area, with a couple of shelters, picnic tables, and grills. The lake itself is nice. It has one of the most awesome beaches locally as it's all sand, with many trees to offer some shade from the hot sun. On a nice weekend, it's common for the beach to be packed, and for there to be lots of people floating on the lake in their floaty devices.

On the backside of the park are primitive camping sites that are quite nice, and settled in the woods, away from the activity on the other side of the lake. We stayed here once and were among the only campers.

For a county park, this park is kept up very nice. I'd highly recommend checking it out and spending an afternoon.

This beautiful and peaceful park is located in suburban Ocala. I'm guessing that a lot of people don't know it even exists. We had a woman who lived nearby tell us that she lived nearby without realizing it existed. It's tucked away, on the edge of rural Ocala.

It's a peaceful oasis where you'll find flowers, a koi pond, a forest path, a labyrinth path, and lots of flowers and trees to look at as you walk the paths.

There is a bathroom on site, and many strategically placed benches. In the koi pond, you'll find koi and lots of turtles. There's a small covered deck near the pond where you can relax and feed the fish.

We thoroughly enjoyed our time here, finding refuge in the cool forest during the heat of the day, enjoying the flowers and the sounds of the many birds.

If you live nearby, or are just passing through, take some time to visit this wonderful garden.

Can you really review a bridge? Yes. Yes, you can. The Duluth Aerial Lift Bridge is the city's iconic landmark. There are many ways to enjoy it. You can enjoy the view from a distance, during the day or at night, watching it lift for passing ships. You can walk out on the piers. You can cross it onto the peninsula. You can enjoy the view from restaurants nearby, such as Grandma's rooftop dining. You can take the Lakewalk. No matter how you enjoy it, spending time near the bridge is always a memorable occasion when you're visiting Duluth.

This has to be one of the three lamest rides at Epcot. It's an embarrassment to the people of Mexico. You hop in a boat that goes along a waterway on the backside of the Mexico Pavilion. Along the way, you're treated to some irritating commentary by The Three Caballeros as you pass by pictures of Mexico. The ride designers really failed on this one. It could have been so much better, and more respectful to the people and land of Mexico.

Simply a stunningly beautiful Church, and stunning that it was just built in 2010. It's filled with artwork, stained-glass, statues, shrines. Get a tour, or pick up the booklet that explains all the detail that went into this worship space. It's quite a sight, and proof that gorgeous churches can still be built. If you attend Mass here, you'll find an active parish with many young families.

Located in an old Church, the Russian Museum of Art has rotating displays on three levels that are very interesting, as well as guided tours that are excellent. There's also a wonderful little gift shop inside. Currently, the exhibits include Faberge items, a Russian impressionist's paintings, and underground, dissident artwork. This museum is well worth spending time at.

You really can skip this visitor center and head on into the park. There just isn't that much to see - a movie playing, a gift shop, and a few small exhibits about the wildlife and history. It's a great place to use the restroom before you head into the park, but other than that, I'd skip this visitor's center.

Awesome views are available from the Foshay Observation Deck, which sits atop this art deco historic skyscraper. There was a time when this was the tallest building in Minneapolis. Visiting the museum and outdoor observation deck will take you back in time.

A truly stunning place to worship and visit. The acoustics can sometimes be a challenge, but it's so worth coming to see the artwork, the sculptures, the dome, the shrines to the international saints, and to pray.

How can you beat a free zoo and the amazing Conservatory and its gardens and fish, the large park, and amusement park rides. Como is one of St. Paul's gems, and an inexpensive way for a family to spend a day.
Great historic building that used to hold offices, but now is used for historic events. If you're downtown and want to see an interesting space, stop in and look around. You'll enjoy it.
Wonderful suburban park with children's play area, amphitheater, walking/biking trails around the lake, fishing pier, observatory, picnic tables, and the bathrooms are being renovated.
Perhaps one of Minnesota's (and Lake Superior's) most iconic images - Split Rock Lighthouse. It's fun to visit this historic site and learn about the use of the lighthouse.
The Navarre Beach had very few people on it, which was nice. It's a white sand beach where you'll see lot of bird activity and find all kinds of interesting shells.
A nice urban park with a small lake that's perfect for paddle-boating, children's play area, a small stage for concerts. The lake is great for a short walk-around.
One of the most picturesque stops along Highway 61, it's fun to walk the trails and see the different falls here. Our children have always loved it.
Awesome views, trails, elk, glaciers, mountain lakes, bathrooms, exhibits, and a restaurant, all at nearly 12,000 feet up. Bring your coats.
While expensive, we thoroughly enjoyed our guided tour of the Glensheen Mansion and estate. This historic home is well worth visiting.
Home to railroad "king" James J. Hill, this is a beautiful old home to tour. They also hold special events, which are worth attending.
Wonderful little French Church, with a beautiful Winter Chapel located on the backside. You can find daily Mass and confession here.
Mini-golf, go cart racing, a water slide, batting cages, bumper boats, and more. It's a fun place for a family for some summer fun.
Small but enjoyable museum that looks at the Minneapolis flour mill history, and the explosion. Our family enjoyed visiting here.
If you, or your children, love trains, this is a must-see. They have a variety of trains that you can take a look at. Fun!
likes: On-site Activities: Variety of trains to view

reviews_attraction.text: Haven't rode the train but chased it several times. Beautifully maintained Engine #98 provides weekend service up the Red Clay Creek Valley. Destinations include Mount Cuba, Ashland & occasionally Hockessin. Very scenic...you wouldn't think you were just a few miles from Wimington.

Forsythe is a refuge you keep coming back to. Most recently, we saw snow geese in dozens and then shortly thereafter, hundreds came in for the evening. The wildlife drive is the perfect length to spend an hour or two and see what the seasons have to offer.

The High peaks of the Adirondacks you will continue to revisit. The best area for me was Algonquin Peak, the second highest in NY. Heart Lake is a beautiful starting point but so is St Huberts for the Great Range.

A beautiful boat launching area right next to a sheltered ruins and Captains BBQ. Palm Coast is a nice Florida beach town. Not too big, but just minutes from beautiful Washington Rocks and Washington Oaks Gardens

Interesting old spa buildings and a unique trail along a sulfur creek with springs. I recall a nice restaurant in premises. Also the Sunday farm market at Lincoln baths offers a variety of local goods.
Parvin is a beautiful lesser know New Jersey State Park with hiking bicycling and paddling opportunities. Unfortunately, lack of funding has allowed many of its facilities to fall into disrepair.
Amazing hiking opportunities. So far, I have only visited Round and Twin Ponds, but this area is less traveled than the Great Range and High Peak regions. Solitude abounds.
Features the Anhinga Trail, an excellent boardwalk usually good for alligator viewing. Also, the Gumbo Limbo Trail, which guides you through a different ecosystem.
Very crowded. The blow hole is only active during certain tide and surf conditions. But Sandy Beach to the north is a must stop, if you can find a parking space.
Very crowded especially for sunrise. Beautiful views but recommend Kalahaku overlook for a more interesting less crowded view of the crater cinder cones
Did not see turtles but they frequent this location. There is a small secondary beach to the south just past the rocks. But watch for broken glass.
A nice self guided tour through the historic sub should take about 45 minutes. Located at the main Pearl Harbor historic sites visitor area.
Great view of Philly and the planes landing as well as the Navy Yard. The old estate in the park is picturesque. Nice short walking trails.
Beautiful walk through the jungle with large variety of species as well as two natural waterfalls and ocean frontage. Worth the cost IMO.
Nice place in any season to view wildlife at McCarthy Ponds. Unfortunately 4 wheelers often break in and ruin the paths and make noise.
Fresh Pond Park is another beautiful Gardiner's Bay beach. The Fresh Pond and its outlet are an interesting natural feature to explore.
A 2 mile walk to the point will expose you to the tidal lands and pools of the New Jersey barrier beach coastline. Abundant wildlife.
Just outside of Hilo. Bring your flashlight. Exploration takes about 30 minutes for each cave. Tropical plants greet each entrance.
Very crowded. Could not go to the lighthouse. But the views to the north are stunningly gorgeous. A must stop on the scenic drive.
Very cold and rainy when we were there. But in nice weather you can imagine a lovely view that you will share with many others.
Fairchild Oak is a nice spot to take a break and admire this majestic live oak. The trails look interesting as well.
A bit flooded in the spring. Interesting emerald colored lakes in the summer and fall. Noisy from nearby Route 55.
Nice ruins and the put in/take out for paddling the Great Egg Harbor River. Very crowded in the summer months.
Disappointed that the area was gated off so you are limited in viewing and must share it with the crowds.
Excellent place to take a nature walk, bird watch, relax, at the beach and explore an old WW II bunker.

What a wonderful Park. And it's free parking, if you want to see the sights on Lake Apopka one of the largest lakes I've seen. Beautiful Park, beautiful grounds, Wildlife abounds, and they have Pavilions if you want a picnic. There's also a campground if you want to camp out.

This is an all natural park with a spring that turns into a lazy river about a half a mile long. They have restrooms also concession and it's handicap friendly. Plus they have showers although you might not need one because this is fresh water Springs. 72 degrees year-round.

Very easy to get around with the one-way streets and very beautiful all the buildings are clean streets are clean Etc lots of businesses especially Banks of every sort. You can walk or bicycle with a $1 rental. Most Street side parking is free on the weekends

It's a beautiful well-kept Park that has security all the time it's open. Nice walkways to walk or bike and it also has playgrounds for children. Also soccer fields and baseball fields. I believe starting next week it stays open until 9 p.m.

Wow what a great Park with restrooms for handicapped as well as a great place to swim in 72 Degree water. Lots of children and adults be sure to bring your goggles and snorkel so you can see where the spring comes out of the Earth.

This is a wonderful Park to take children because they have a giant playground they have tennis courts they have many fields that they can run around Ball Diamonds Etc and have restrooms and it's handicap friendly
It's a small Park but very well maintained. Don't look for a place to go swimming because the alligators are out there. You can launch your boat though and they do have free restrooms that are clean
This is a wonderful place to visit any day you want to relax and just enjoy the surroundings. Beautiful walkway all the way around the lake and even boat rides available on the floating swans
I like it because it has parking and sidewalks you can walk or ride your bicycle you can run on the grass. There's lots of wildlife around small ponds and plenty of handicap parking
Plenty of parking spaces and they have kayaks for rent and canoes also to be able to go out onto the lake. Pretty well-kept as Olive Florida state parks are
This is a peaceful place to take a walk and enjoy the beauty all around you. Plants as well as animals and creatures I've other sorts are all along the walk
Nice park for walking jogging Etc no bicycles though. There was an art festival when I went there so that took up about half of it. It is very large
Very nice park with about a half a mile sidewalk all the way around it. Several benches to stop and relax, restrooms handicap parking Etc
What a nice park, they have tennis courts for free as well as playground for children and an exercise Park, one of the best I've seen.
It was good. Very soon after Hurricane Irma so it wasn't totally cleaned up yet. But they did give us a better rate for all three.
Blue Springs is a wonderful clean place to go swimming, when you can get in, because it gets to be busy and filled up early.
It has about eight or ten exercise stations throughout the park which I enjoy also has a boardwalk through the nature bath
Wonderful place, very clean and up kept, handicap friendly. They also have a restaurant there. A great place for children
Lots of trails and places to go fishing. I saw two fawns on the entry and many other birds as well as a gopher tortoise.
The city of Orlando closed all of the exercise stations along the Route Around the Lake. I think that should be illegal
Very nice park with walking trails bicycle trails and frisbee golf as well as camping. This place is well kept
You can go here in the winter time and see manatees trying to stay warm in the water from the power plant
Lots better than Sanibel where the parking is $5 an hour. $8 here get you a whole day free parking
A very nice and up kept Recreational Park for anyone who wants to come and see it. And it's free
I'm sure it's a good one there were many dogs there. But I don't have one so I didn't go there

We came here to celebrate my birthday, having read about the museum in the Atlas Obscura and seeking to experience the unique attraction for ourselves.

We thoroughly enjoyed our visit, starting with a friendly welcome by a very enthusiastic staff member who took us on a brief tour and then gave us a copy of one of the founder's books. We enjoyed all of the exhibits, particularly the interactive ones, and really appreciated all of the historical information and rare memorabilia that was on display.

We had a chance to meet Don, who very happily showed us around some of his favorite pieces and have us some amusing stories and anecdotes, as well as a second book.

Overall, the museum is a unique and interesting treasure with a rather eccentric spin that makes it enjoyable for people of all ages. I would recommend it to anyone who is in the area and has the time to stop by.

The Devil's Punchbowl is a beautiful, scenic destination just outside of Menomonie, Wisconsin along the Red Cedar River, a natural pit in the Earth carved by so many thousands of years of erosion and water flow, maintained and made available for all to visit and appreciate.

It is a wonder to behold in all seasons, dripping and bustling with life during the spring and summer, colorful and calm in the fall, and lined with massive ice walls during the frozen winter.

I would definitely recommend that you take the time to visit if you should find yourself in the area.

The Minneapolis Institute of Art is a beautiful diverse and sprawling curation of artwork from all over the world, featuring artwork from a variety of different cultures and time periods. There are many friendly and knowledgeable staff members who are happy to answer questions and provide insight into the pieces.

The periodic exhibits are always interesting and filled with rare/unique pieces ranging from modern expressions of creative intent to historic discoveries. I always come away having learned about the world of art and history in general.

Beautiful park with plenty of scenic views and winding trails. There are plenty of places to sit and enjoy the space, and the history of the space is interesting for new visitors. The only reason this is not a 5 star review is the quality of the trails - they aren't really maintained that well, and tend to be in pretty rough shape. I would also not recommend coming to this park after dark - it is perfectly fine during the day though.

The Minneapolis lookout features a one-of-a-kind view of Minneapolis, from a park filled with beautiful trees and sprawling prairies. The winding trail is nice for a bike ride or a walk. My first kiss with my ex-wife was at this spot, though don't let that stop you from visiting; I've been here with others since and have not experienced any such disaster, leading me to believe that the park was not to blame.

This is one of my favorite locations to visit, not only in the Duluth area but in general. The sprawling beach stretches out in all directions as the lake crashes on the shore (or the ice, depending on the time of year!).

Scenic, natural, and filled with opportunities to learn and explore, this park is definitely worth a visit if you are in town and arguably worth the trip if you are not. 😊💙

Como is a lovely park for walks along the lake, quiet time with friends and family, or events at the pavilion. The waterfall is very pleasant and meditative, and there are many other small elements of the park that bring contentment. The bike trails are pretty simplistic and a bit frustrating, but overall, the park is well maintained.

Mills Ruins park is a historic, intriguing staple of downtown Minneapolis that helps to provide a visual example of how the architecture of the city had evolved over time and the beauty of preserved structures. The nearby bridge is also a lovely walk, and there are plenty of nearby attractions to make for an engaging day out.

Crosstown park is a lovely, well maintained park with a winding trail that leads around a small pond with a gazebo in the center. The walkways are perfect for taking the mind off of a long day at work, and the many benches and tables are a wonderful respite for the walker.

Definitely a park worth visiting and maintaining!

This park is always a favorite part of the annual MS150 fundraiser ride. It is the last rest stop along the ride back from Duluth to Century College, a d alongside being a symbol of having almost completed the ride, it is also a very nice park with a beautiful view of the lake and a nice pavilion.

Crosby Farm Park is a beautiful, sprawling system of trails and paths, rambling along the Mississippi River through forests, wetland, and floodplains. The park is well kept and accessible by both car and bike. Definitely worth a visit for a walk in the fresh air. 😌

Battle Creek Regional Park is a sprawling park with bike and hiking trails, forests, winding creeks, and a variety of activities for all to enjoy.

This is one of my favorite parks in the area, as there are just so many things to do.

Definitely worth a visit!

A beautiful, sprawling park with plenty of outdoor activities, such as trails, a lake, climbing equipment, and even a zip line! There is something here for people of all ages. The nearby art center is a wonderful option for indoor days as well.

A very nice local park with a playground, tennis courts, and plenty of open space. Sometimes it could use a little bit of TLC in terms of debris and garbage, but overall Carty (or the People's Park) is a nice resource.

The bandshell at Lake Harriet provides a nice outdoor space for events and concerts, complete with facilities for food and a lovely lake with ample space for walking, biking, and other recreational activities.

This park had well maintained facilities, but the trail is really just a few hundred feet of nice lake front, which becomes roadside sidewalk in either direction. Wouldn't be my first choice of parks.
Wisconsin Interstate State Park is a beautiful park with views of the river, plenty of trails along the bluffs, and various centers to learn about the park and history. Definitely worth a visit.
A sprawling park full of trails, fields, and plenty of water to explore. We have come here for picnics and bike rides most often, but have also brought our canoe to explore the waterways.
Not the most welcoming place. The park itself is nice, and there are some great people in the area, but you definitely have to be aware of yourself and your surroundings here.
Our local park - poorly maintained trails and grounds, but always full of decent folks from the community. Wish the city would take care of it... Could be a nice park.
Phalen is a beautiful, open, and multi-functional park with beaches, trails, fishing, and more. We love coming here to explore and always find something new. 💙
Well kept (by a local group of volunteers) and well maintained little block park in downtown. Lots of benches, a meandering brook, and a band shell with music.
Swede Hollow is a beautiful urban park with a great deal of history and many activities for families and individuals. Definitely worth a visit!
Very interesting and unique tours of a beautiful old house with a mysterious history. Worth checking out if you have the time.
The Large Green Chair is a very fun place to take photos and spend some time in the beautiful outdoors!

A beautiful location near the top of Trail Ridge Road featuring views of a glacial cirque (glaciers not included during warmer months) overlooking Old Fall River Road and the valley leading to Horseshoe Park. Occasionally you may spot a herd of elk in the valley too! Not uncommon for clouds to run through the area making it foggy which is very cool! Hard to visit Rocky Mountain National Park and not visit the Alpine visitor center!

How often do you get to stand at the highest point anywhere? It may not be the tallest mountain in the world, in North America, or this country, but it is the tallest in the state and for that distinction, it is worth it especially if you have a desire to visit the highest point in each state!
Camping is primitive only and hiking takes you to the Ozark Trail and to Johnson's shut-ins via backpacking trail! Definitely worth a stop!

Formerly Times Beach residential community, Route 66 State Park explores America's famous highway and the culture surrounding it. Also learn the fate of Times Beach before walking through the park grounds were the community once stood. Great historic location providing boat ramp access to the Meramec River as well as fishing from the banks!

Found along Colorado 36, Beaver Meadows visitor center is the place to stop at the main entrance of Rocky Mountain National Park coming from Estes Park. Take a look around, hike the nearby trails, browse the gift shop, and talk to the friendly rangers always happy to take your questions!

One of Missouri's many historic sites exploring the history of native Americans and their culture from the surrounding area! Van Meter also features hiking, fishing, boating, and camping!
Great please for all ages to learn about the history of the state!

Missouri is known for its many caves and Onondaga is well worth the visit! The park offers access to the nearby Meramec river, features camping and picnic areas, and tours of the cave! Plenty to do to spend an afternoon or a full weekend!

Great way to cool off and beat the summer heat! Plenty to do when the crowds pile in (and they will pile in) if swimming is not an option!
Hike the scour trail and see the destructive power of water from the Ameren reservoir failure.

General Pershing's boyhood home offers a rich history to one of America's most prominent generals who is also a native of Missouri! Also take the time to stop in at Pershing state park which features hiking and a great picnic area!

Absolutely beautiful park! Take a relaxing weekend floating the river, swimming at the rock beaches, explore Fisher cave, or hiking the many trails!
Plan accordingly though as it is a very popular park!
Stop in and learn of America's rather harsh history with the native Americans. There are also many hiking trails and both basic and electric campsites with access to the Mississippi River!

Unstaffed park featuring several trails that take visitors around the Grand Gulf area. Interpretive signs along the trails detail the history of the area.
Great way to spend an afternoon!
One of the last four covered bridges left in Missouri! A beautiful display of architecture and a great picnic area where the kids can run around a play or splash in the creek!

One of the state of Missouri's many historic sites that dive into the history of the native American culture of the area!
Great history and learning experience for all ages!
Wakonda features several lakes which are accessible for small boating and fishing. The campgrounds are placed near and around the lakes making a very scenic campground!

Great place for hiking and mountain biking! Trails take you along the Meramec River with plenty of scenic views!
Not too far from St Louis and adjoining cities either!
Beautiful undeveloped lake in North Central Missouri! There are swimming beaches within the park and boat ramps for launching personal boats for a day on the lake!
Crowder state park features many miles of hiking, bicycling, backpacking and equestrian trails and is a very beautiful place to spend a day or a weekend!
One of four remaining covered bridges in Missouri! Union covered bridge is by far the largest of the bridges and a beautiful display of architecture!
One of the last standing mills in Missouri! A beautiful location to visit and walk around; stop in and enjoy the picnic area before touring the mill!
Beautiful park offering camping, hiking, fishing, and floating along the river! Great way to beat the heat and a very popular summer location!
Right at the edge of the Missouri River in the state capital! Fantastic views and within walking distance of the Capitol building for tours!
Great campground, beautiful hiking trails, and all close to the city without feeling too close! Great place to spend the day or weekend!
Beautiful lake with plenty to do from hiking, camping, kayaking and fishing to boat rentals allowing easier travel all over the lake!
This site offers many scenic hiking trails as well as a great museum offering a look into Missouri's prehistoric times!
Beautiful area on the East side of Rocky Mountain National Park and a great place to view the elk as fall colors!

This place is way better than I expected. They have a big variety of animals to look at and they have a cave tour that comes with your admission. If you do the cave tour, and you go to the other 2 animals shows, plus look at all the animals you will easily spend 3-4 hours here. We were hear almost 4 hours. All of the people working here were really nice as well. My favorite part was the kangaroos, you go into a big fenced in area, and you are free to roam to pet and feed them. There are lots of kangaroos to pet as well. So you don’t have to worry about waiting.

Very fun zoo, my son had a great time here. They have a big variety of animals to see and you can also pet some of the animals throughout the zoo. There were only a few negative things. We went on a Wednesday morning and it said on their website that it wouldn’t be busy. But it was pretty packed and it made it hard to see certain animals. Also as with most zoos their was some construction and some of the animals weren’t out to be seen. The parking is $10 dollars as well I thought that was a little excessive. But It’s definitely worth checking out

As for the scenery I give this place 5 stars. Very pretty lots of streams, places to fish, hike etc.  The problem I had with this place was the people, there were a lot of loud trashy people here. Multiple times while walking in the woods and checking out the streams I heard rap music blasting, people arguing. It just ruined it for me, it's hard to enjoy nature when it feels like walking through a Jerry Springer show. I went on a Saturday, maybe that's why it was so bad, it might be more peaceful during the week.

I had a lot of fun here with my family. My 2 year old son loved looking at all the fish and penguins. We got there early because at 11 am they bring a penguin out into the theater room for everyone to see up close. The aquarium is pretty big, it took us about 3 hours to get through it.  I’ve been to several aquariums and this is probably my favorite. We also went on a weekday and it wasn’t crowded at all. So it was really easy to get around and see everything.

I didn’t know if I was going to enjoy this museum. I like history but I’m not that into trains. But this museum was way better than I thought. The train depot itself is very big and is well maintained. There are two floor of exibits that are self-guided and then a tour guide takes your through the five train cars. Our tour guide was very friendly and informative. I’m glad they have preserved this depot and these train cars. Very cool part of local history.

I have been to a lot of museums and this  is definitely one of my favorites. It’s not the biggest, but it’s well maintained and it is very detailed. They have 3 floors of exhibits. My favorite was the top floor which is all about Bourbon. Very interesting and they have a impressive bourbon collection dating from the early 20th century to modern bourbons. They also have a really nice gift shop. It has a little bit of everything and a lot of local products.

I was really disappointed with this place. It looks very big, but it’s filled with a lot of empty space and the dining area covers a lot of it. Also it’s expensive, especially for a family. They had a Pixar exhibit there and of course they have to charge extra for that. Also instead of having a lot of different things to look at. They just went really heavy on a few things, I like museums. But I found this one extremely boring

The grounds here are very nice, and this place does have a cool history to it. I have to say I was a little disappointed, I’ve heard a lot about this place on tv and online, but it was fairly small compared to other botanical gardens I’ve been to, and didn’t have as many species of plants as I expected. I thought I would be here for hours, but I was done in a hour and a half and that’s me taking my time.

This place has the potential to be a cool little museum. I remember going here as a kid and it was in a lot better shape. They have some cool exhibits, but a lot of the activities for the kids on the second floor don’t work and the whole middle part of the floor is just empty. The floors were dirty and the employees weren’t very friendly either. Hopefully they can get this place back into good shape.

A pretty nice park for a walk. There is  a paved portion and a unpaved portion. There are some great views of the river and I went during the week and I only saw one person so it was pretty peaceful. The only thing that would improve the park is if it were marked better. Some parts of the unpaved trail. I wasn’t sure if it was just for bikes or  if it was a shared trail.

I wasn't really interested in doing this. But I bought the combo tickets for ruby falls and rock city gardens and this came with it. It was fun riding up and down, but that's basically all there is to do. They have a gift shop at the top and you can walk to a civil war battlefield. But I wasn't interested in that. Also we had to wait quite awhile to go up.

This park is ok. It’s good if you want to go for a short walk. Most of the walking trail is shaded, which makes it good for walking on a hot day. If you park at the Nashville rd entrance, it’s a little confusing because it’s connected to a church parking lot. So I guess you just park in the gravel section. That’s what I did.

Very cool place to visit. The tour is very fun and informative, it’s about 30 minutes long. They have a lot of really cool memorabilia from baseball legends like Babe Ruth, Hank Aaron, Mickey Mantle that you can look at. You can also get your own custom bat made. The gift shop is very nice, with a lot of cool items to buy.

Pretty nice little park, a small walking trail. The old church and meeting house, the graveyard was well maintained and it was cool to see the graves of the revolutionary war soilders. The only problem was we came on a Sunday and the gift shop was closed, be nice if they kept it open everyday like the rest of the park.

This place has some very cool activities for kids to expierence and learn about art and science. The major problem with coming here is that it is super crowded. You're constantly bumping into people, and you have to wait a long time to do certain things. I went really early on a Wednesday and it was still crowded.

Very pretty grounds. They have a good variety or trees and plants to see. The art museum was really interesting. I lived in this area most of my life and never heard of Joe Downing until recently. So I think this is a good way to celebrate a great local artist, and give him the exposure that he deserves.

If you're in Colorado Springs you should definitely check it out, it is very cool to see. I think this place is a one and done though. When I visit family here I get dragged here over and over. I don't get the hype. And now it's gotten so crowded, it's hard to even find parking or enjoy walking around.

Very beautiful place, plenty of stuff to see and do. You can, walk, hike, kayak, drive and see the sights. I didn't have as much time as I wanted to explore, it will take you a couple days to explore everything. So I'll definitely have to come back when I'm in the area and see the stuff I missed.

I love going here. Been here so many times I can’t count. The cave tours are really fun and informative. My favorite tour is the frozen niagara tour. I also enjoy the hiking trails. They have a lot of different trails to hike and the trails are never that crowded.

Pretty cool place to visit if you're in the area. For the general admission ticket you get to walk the trail with all the dinosaurs, tour the museum, and they have a kids playground.  I liked it, but it needs more attractions to bring people back a second time.

This was a fun little place to visit. I like things that are different like this. It was cool to see all of the different kinds of cat figurines, toys and artwork. My 3 year old son had a fun time here as well. I would definitely recommend This place.

This is my favorite zoo to go to. They have plenty of animals to see and it’s never over crowded. You never have to wait that long to see any animals. They also have other cool things for children like the carousel and train rides.

The rangers and employees here are very knowledgeable and helpful. The center is small, but they have some cool items.  Also the craggy gardens pinnacle trail is one of my favorite hiking trails. Very beautiful
Really fun place to go, even if you're not into bourbon. It will keep you entertained, you can take the tour, get a tasting, eat, walk the grounds, and look through their gift shop.
Definitely a place you should make an effort to visit. So much great music history and memorabilia. The building itself is pretty cool and its right on the lake.

Bushkill Falls has some amazing views and waterfalls, there are many different hiking trails for all levels of hikers. The only issue to me is the high ticket prices. I don’t think I should have to pay to see nature, I would be more than happy to donate, but the price to get in is much higher than it should be.

UNCLE GERRY'S TIP: My friends go hike Rickett's Glenn, Watkins Glenn, or even Buttermilk Falls. They are just as beautiful without the entrance fee.

Amazing place, kind of like a live action game.  You can go up against, mummies, dragons, spies, and aliens. It is hard to explain, but trust me experience this for yourself. It is worth the price of admission.

UNCLE GERRY'S TIP: Buy all the different quests at the same time it's much cheaper and you can come back and play them at different times as long as it's in the same day.

The best state park for waterfalls in the area.  The trail is very challenging but worth it for the beautiful views.

UNCLE GERRY'S TIP: Wear hiking boots and bring a walking pole!!! It is better to be safe than sorry. Trust me on this, my friends.

Adorable little park, inexpensive, very homey... Lots of good roller coasters and water rides. A great way to spend a day in the summer.

UNCLE GERRY'S TIP: After a great day at the park head over to Bill Gray's for some burgers and ice cream.

Nescopeck is a great park with lots of different trails for all levels of hikers, snowshoes, and cross country skiing. The river is also a great place to fish. An educational center is located in the main part of the park near lake Frances.

Beautiful views and lots of different covered picnic areas and restrooms makes this a nice place to picnic.

UNCLE GERRY'S TIP: There are a few two person swings that looks over Athens if you want to swing and enjoy a beautiful day.

Great views of the NYC skyline.  Alice Austen was one of the first female photographers so the museum has a lot of her pictures.

UNCLE GERRY'S TIP: Go early on the Fourth of July for an amazing view of the NYC Fireworks.

This is a great state park. They have a section in the gorge where you can safely swim with lighguards. The trails are pretty easy to hike and beautiful. There is also really nice playground and camp store and snack bar.

This is a great park with a huge lake. The park offers lots of hiking, biking trails and picnic spots.

UNCLE GERRY'S TIP: They have a well taken care of single track mountain biking trails at all skill levels.
My daughter loves these museums and we usually visit one whenever we vacation in a place where they are located. They are all basically the same but they are fun to visit the different ones anyway.
Waverly Glen Park is a lovely community park. It has  hiking trails, a waterfall, a playground, picnic areas, and tennis courts. A great way to spend a weekend day or even go for a hike after work.
The experience was amazing. I was so happy I was able take my daughter to this. From the pre flight training, to the flights the instructor was great and who can beat floating on air like superman?
It was nice with a lot of history and memorabilia that covers the beginning of Rock N Roll till today. However, it was  much smaller than I thought it would be and the entrance fee is high.
Great views of the NYC skyline and on the Fourth of July its a good view of the fireworks.  Alice Austen was one of the first female photographers so the museum has a lot of her pictures.
Very pretty hike and lots of natural beauty.  The main hike is about 2 miles and is either straight up if you go to the left after the bridge or a easier hike if you go to the right.
Beautiful views, great river, hike, bike and kayak.  When the water level is good you can have a few day paddle and just make camp on little islands or right on shore.

Beautiful park with lots of history and a great bike path.

UNCLE GERRY'S TIP: While you are here check out the museum and go for a ride on an mule drawn canal boat.
My wife dragged me to this and I found it much more enjoyable than I thought I would have... The huge real iceberg at the end is worth the visit.
This is a great place to come and enjoy the day on the cheap. You even get some free chips and the ability to buy others at a deep discount.
Great park with beautiful views. The is a bike trail that goes around the whole city and is wonderful in the Spring, Summer, and Fall.
This is a great park to walk, bike, or even rollerblade.  The beach is nice and it has beautiful views of the ocean and the marina.
This is a great launch when you are either  putting in at "White Haven" or if you are going to take out at Glen Onoko.
Don't waste your time if the wait is over 30 minutes. It's still breaking down all the time and totally not worth it.
This was a very nice little Garden and was a good way to spend about an hour or so. It is also free admission.
If you like beer, this is the place for you. Plus the food is very tasty and the prices were right.

During our recent visit to the Colorado Springs area, we decided to book a train ride at the Royal Gorge Railroad.  I booked tickets for 4 adults ahead of time for a 3:30pm ride on a Saturday in August, 2017.

We arrived 45 minutes early as suggested, got our tickets, and boarded our train on time.  We booked the Vista Dome class of tickets because we wanted the best views.  But upon entry into the Vista Dome car, we noticed that it was very hot and stuffy.  We were also seated directly across from the cashier desk where employees could be heard communicating via walkie talkies.  We were seated at a table for four on the river side of the car (odd numbered tickets).  This is the best side to sit on because you have a better view with the river (as opposed to rock).

The Vista Dome windows are nice enough for a good view, but ours was dirty from the outside, which was definitely a distraction.  The biggest distraction, however, was the lack of adequate air conditioning.  The vents above barely circulated air, and the air was not very cool at all.  It was so stuffy that we decided to go out to the Open Air car shortly after the train departed the station.  We had to walk through the Coach car on the way to the Open Air car, and WOW what a difference!  The Coach car was probably 10 degrees cooler and seemed to be less cramped.

When we made it out to the Open Air car, all of the distractions didn't matter anymore.  The Open Air car is wonderful with perfect views and plenty of space to hold a good number of people (though it does get busy out there, and the river side railing is preferable).  We ended up staying out there the entire time because of the stuffy Vista Dome car.  Since we rode in mid August, the weather was terrific with warm sun and plenty of air keeping us cool as the train traveled along the route.

And the route through the gorge is fantastic and breathtaking!  You start out at the station and begin to see rafters floating down the river, who will often wave at the train passengers (and one even mooned us).  But when entering the actual gorge, the views truly take your breath away.  I took a ton of photos and videos.

The train travels along a route through the gorge that lasts about 50 minutes.  Then it stops for a few minutes until it begins to travel in reverse along the same path.  I wish the train actually traveled a different way back to the depot, but it's a gorge route so it is what it is.  On the way back, the train will stop for several minutes under the bridge so that you can take photos and hear a bit of history.  The bridge itself is very cool to see from underneath, but the rock formations are actually more interesting.

The entire round trip (including stops) takes 2 hours.  I would NOT recommend the Vista Dome upgrade, as it was $25 more per person and it MUCH hotter than the Coach cars (at least on the 3:30pm ride... it may be okay in the morning or evening).  But I WOULD recommend the train ride itself, especially getting out to the Open Air car as soon as you get a chance to get a good spot.  I cannot comment on the food as we did not end up ordering anything since it was too hot to stay in the car.  We did end up telling a manager about our experience and they said they have upgraded the air conditioning in the coach cars but not the Vista Dome yet (which is odd since it's a higher class of travel).  Also, the bathrooms at the train depot are small and stinky.  The only reason I'm giving this 4 stars instead of 2 or 3 is because of the fantastic views and the open car.

We drove a little over 3 hours to Milwaukee with the main purpose to visit the zoo because a friend gave us some tickets (two adults and two teens).  The first day we spent driving, some time at the beach, and at our hotel.  The second day, we visited the zoo and got there right at the 9am opening.

Upon arrival, we actually waiting in line with our car for about 10 minutes before zoo opening.  We were surprised to discover that you pay for parking and admission to the zoo right at the gate when you enter (whereas in most zoos, you pay for parking upon entry and then admission at a separate gate after you park).  There was ample parking and we did not have to walk far.

It seemed like a lot of the zoo doesn't get going until at least 10am.  The zoo seemed pretty dead at 9am, and we visited on a holiday weekend (Labor Day weekend, though it was a Sunday).  Not much was going on, and some of the animals weren't out.  But it was pleasantly cool for early September, and we enjoyed just walking around a bit.

When reviewing zoos, I always rate them comparatively, based on other zoos we have visited.  The zoo we have in our own home location is very small and boring, so this was definitely better than that.  But compared to some of the nicer zoos we've visited, this one falls short.  Specifically, there are several other zoos that we've been to that are a considerable step up from the Milwaukee Zoo:  Henry Doorly Zoo in Omaha, Columbus Zoo, and both zoos in Chicago (Brookfield and Lincoln Park) are more fun in my opinion.

On the other hand, there are some nice exhibits and a relatively unique rope climb and zip line.  Our teens enjoyed both of those, even though they aren't extravagant like you'd find at a dedicated zip line establishment.  The zip line is basically just a 10 second zip across two points you can see simultaneously, so don't expect a multi-point zip line or anything fancy.  The rope climb is part of it (though you can pay for one or the other or both), and they enjoyed that for at least 45 minutes.  The prices are relatively affordable.

We spent maybe a total of 6 hours at the zoo and then we left because we were a bit bored.  There's not a whole lot that is unique to this zoo, though I can't complain too much because it's a pretty nice zoo for the locals to visit.  I would not suggest an out of town visit unless it's the closest one and you aren't interested in anything a bit more out of the way.
dislikes: Fewer animals out in the morning
Less engaging compared to other zoos

reviews_attraction.text:
We visited Milwaukee in early September of 2018, but the beach was not our primary destination.  We were looking for something to do towards sunset, so we looked up beaches online and this one popped up as slightly more secluded than some of the busier beaches.

Atwater is definitely not secluded, but it also wasn't crazy busy or a tourist trap.  It's a beautiful park and beach with a very cool view from above as you descend down several flights of stairs to get to the beach itself.  Alternatively, you can walk a spiraling pathway that takes you down to the beach that is lined with flowers, grasses, and a nicely paved trail.

There are many overlooks from the top and from different places on your way down.  When we first got there, there was a mist blowing in from the lake and it looked like we were up in the clouds.  It eventually burned off from the afternoon sun, but it was still pleasantly cool and refreshing.  Always expect the temperature to be a bit cooler on the lake (and especially down below right along the water).

The beach itself is not huge and there are signs on both sides warning you where the beach ends.  There are a couple of boardwalks that are blocked off, but they have a neat look.  There's a nice playground at the top and bottom of Atwater for the kids.  The sand is pleasant to walk on, and the sun was shining on the entire beach and water from behind the park as the sun started going down.  It's the perfect place to get some photos or portraits late in the afternoon (though I'd imagine it would be nice in the morning too as the sun rises above the water).

We didn't get in the water because the temperature was too cold, but we didn't come to swim anyway.  We just came for some late afternoon relaxation and pictures, and Atwater was perfect for that!

Our first visit to Seven Falls was fantastic!  I was pleasantly surprised by how beautiful the entire area is - not just the falls themselves, but even the short hike up to the falls base is gorgeous.  The landscaping is immaculate, maintained well, and adds a great deal to the atmosphere.

To get to the falls, you have to park some distance away near the Broadmoor Hotel.  Then you hop on a free shuttle that takes you to the entrance to the park itself, which is about a 10 minute drive.  You purchase tickets and then decide whether to walk to the falls themselves, or take a tram for $2 (we walked, and it's a beautiful walk).  I couldn't stop taking pictures the entire time on the way to the falls and at the falls themselves.

At the falls, you have a choice of walking up 200+ stairs to see all of the falls OR take a mountain elevator that only takes you to a look-out point some distance away from the falls.  If you only do the elevator, you will miss out on seeing the falls close up, but you will avoid the very steep stairs.  There are TONS of photo opportunities, and the entire area is just lovely.

Note that these aren’t gigantic waterfalls anything like Niagara, but they are surrounded by beautiful mountain rock formations and great landscaping.  I think it was well worth the trip and we spent about 4-5 hours there (though you can do it much faster if you didn't stop for photos as much as we did).

HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!

My wife and I stopped here with our mini Aussie on our way home from Door County in July of 2019.  It was a long drive home and we wanted to find a place for our dog to get a bit of exercise, so I looked on Google Maps and found this place.  We are so glad we found this place because it was truly awesome!

To call it a "dog park" would not do it justice because it's more of a wooded refuge for dogs with two off-leash areas (for small and large dogs) and another on-leash area with a creek.  We did not visit the leashed area, but the large off-leash area is huge and wonderful!  The terrain is interesting and exciting with hills, a bridge, plenty of benches, and even a couple dog agility fixtures.

The latches on the gates to get into the park are perfect because you simply life up on them to open and then they automatically lock when they swing shut.  The entire area is shaded, which keeps the dogs cooler.  I'm sure it can get muddy when it's wet, but it was nice and dry when we visited.  Our dog had an amazing time and we really wished we had something like this back home.  We would definitely stop here again if we went through Green Bay with our dog.

The $2 donation admission charge was well worth it, and I would definitely get the annual pass if we lived in town.  HIGHLY RECOMMENDED.

A very nice dog park that is heavily utilized.  They have doggie water fountains,  bags for cleanup, and plenty of space!  The experience can vary depending on the quantity of dogs and courtesy of the dog handlers,  but for the most part, it's usually harmonious.

There’s three segregated areas for the dogs:  one called “The Spot” for smaller or older dogs that need a more laid back area to hang.  Then there are two larger areas that are rotated so that they can be maintained.  One has more shade than the other, but they both have plenty of space for the dogs to run.

Dog parks are not for every dog, but I’ve been here quite a few times now and for the most part, the dogs get along well and the owners are respectable.  The best part is being able to talk with other handlers about training, behaviors, etc.  I learn something new every time I go here, and I get to appreciates dog breeds I’ve never had a chance to see in person before as well.

Sunderbruch Park is arguably the BEST place to mountain bike in the Quad Cities, and riders come from out of town just to ride here.  The trails are many and varied, and maintained well thanks to QC FORC.  There are two main beginner trails (Comlara and Farmdale) that are connected to each other in a loop, but the best way to get to them is via an intermediate climb, Kickapoo Up (it's a little steep, but pretty short).

Once you are on the main beginner trails, there are many intermediate and black diamond trails that branch off and return to the main loops.  The signage is clear, but it isn't too difficult to miss a turn and end up on a trail that you didn't expect, so pay attention!  One of the best, in my opinion, is Jubilee, which has a cool wooden berm section and is still fairly mild compared to the expert trails.

There is plenty of parking in the main lot, and I greatly enjoyed riding here a few times now.

I'm reviewing Dorrance Park explicitly for its mountain biking trails, maintained by QC FORC.  There are three main MB trails:  Oakley Dokely (beginner), Loam Ranger (intermediate), and Uncle Rukus (expert).  I am a beginner and have completed the beginner and intermediate trails, but abandoned the expert trail about half way through when I discovered it was a bit too much for my current skill level.

At any rate, the trails are flowy and very nice to ride with plenty of features and variations in elevation (but nothing too extreme).  The beginner and intermediate full loop is a LOT of fun and takes less than 20 minutes at a fairly slow speed.  Even better, Dorrance Park is right off of the main river trail that goes all the way to the Quad Cities (which is where I ride from if I don't drive).  And Illiniwek is less than a half hour ride from Dorrance as well.

One of the finest places to visit in the area.  The campground is fairly small, but very nice and very close to the caves.  The facilities are decent, including firewood by donation, showers, restrooms, water pumps, fire pits, picnic tables, and both electric and non-electric camping sites.  On the weekends, the rangers are amazing:  very knowledgeable, helpful, and pleasant to talk with.  The caves speak for themselves, and range anywhere from very easy to excruciatingly difficult.  Some of the caves are spacious and accessible to all, while others require squatting, crawling, and climbing.

PRO TIP:  If you plan on spelunking in the more difficult caves, definitely wear hard-hats, knee & elbow pads, pants, and old shoes.  Helmet lights are very helpful, but at least take a flashlight.  You will get dirty - more than likely wet and muddy!

Typhoon Lagoon has one killer attraction and that is its gigantic WAVE POOl that cycles between a 6-foot wave (which is awesome) and bobbing (which is boring), so definitely check it out during the former period.  It also has quite a few slides, a kiddie area, and a large lazy river that goes around the park.  I personally prefer Blizzard Beach because of the theming and because it seems to be easier to get around (Typhoon Lagoon is confusing and more complex to maneuver around in).

Typhoon Lagoon does seem to be the busier water park, and I'm sure it's because of the world-class wave pool.  You hear the sound the machine makes at the start of the wave and everyone in the pool screams as it makes its way from front to back.  It's truly a sight to behold and experience.

We stopped by here on a recent trip to Adventureland, and we were pleasantly surprised!  While not as big as some other botanical gardens, Reiman is just a beautiful, well-maintained place to visit.
