The kids especially loved the butterfly exhibit, and I think every one of them had butterflies land on them.  The outdoor exhibits are also very nice, and even though the gardens is very close to the road, you'd never know it walking through it.

TIP:  When walking along Lake Helen, be careful near the cattails because there are birds nests in there and the birds will likely fly over your head.  Or in my case, a bird swooped right by my head, likely warning me to get further away from its nest.

Yes, the sunsets are beautiful, but the park is very small and gets pretty crowded at sunset (duh).  We stopped her on a beautiful Saturday evening in July and it was indeed very pretty.  It's not really a "park" though, since it's basically just an overlook with a wall and a bit of grassy lawn.  There is a better "Sunset Park" in Sturgeon Bay with trails and more things to do.  But if you are in Fish Creek and just want to walk to the end of Main Street to watch the sun set, this is great!  My wife and I plopped down on the grass with our dog and stayed for about 45 minutes until the sun was fully set.  It was very nice, but don't expect an actual park, trails, or a "beach".

Decided to visit here instead of Starved Rock for Columbus Day weekend, and I'm glad we did!  Though Starved Rock is more spacious, this park is definitely for the adventurous.  Lots of cool little waterfalls and wading pools if you are so inclined to get wet and muddy.  Great views, bridges, stepping stones, dams, and rock formations abound.  We spent over 5 hours in the Dells area and did not have time for the River area, but we did a lot of picture-taking and the teens all had fun climbing, wading, and just being adventurous.

Definitely being old shoes and a change of clothes.  We look forward to coming here again to visit the other area and see it in a different season.

Toy Story Land is a ton of fun, especially for the younger audience.  The theming is some of the best in all of Disney, with loads of imagination and details that you could never see all of in one visit.  Slinky Dog Dash is a fun, but short, ride that is a great first coaster for the little ones.  It has very cool theming with voicing and lots of color.  Alien Saucers is your typical tilt-a-whirl type of ride with mild turning and fun Toy Story music.  The new Toy Story Mania incorporates an old favorite into the new land.  Overall, it’s great fun but definitely either go to the rides during EMH or get Fast Passes for Slinky.

Located just off of i80, this is an extraordinary place with lots of hiking and camping.  There's a very nice visitor's center, a lodge with rooms, dining, and cabins, a small campground, and a plethora of hiking trails.  Starved Rock itself requires a hefty climb of stairs, but has a spectacular view of the river.  This place changes greatly with the seasons, with waterfalls in the spring to colorful foliage in the autumn.  Personally, I find it less enjoyable in the heat of summer.  There's also plenty to do along the river with boat rides and rentals.

John’s Pass is a nice retreat in contrast to the bustle of Clearwater Beach just up the road. Here you can enjoy a quieter, more family friendly location on the beach with lots of unique shops, plenty of water activities, and a very nice beach just under the pass.

You can watch the pass open up fairly frequently and you can even enjoy the shade beneath it.  You’ll see visitors doing everything from fishing to parasailing, swimming, lounging, and shopping.  Parking isn’t too hard to come by either.

I think this place is a gem along the Gulf coast!

We visited Disney Quest as a family of 5 for our first time in July, 2013.  Admission was included with the water park option of our Disneyworld vacation package.  It's definitely big, and the enjoyment is dependent on your love of gaming.  Pushing 40, I really enjoyed playing some of the classic arcade games without having to use quarters!  My kids all enjoyed some of the larger attractions.  If you have time to add this to your itinerary and you have family members that love videogames, I think it's a great diversion from the main Disney parks.

Wow, what a nice campground that is a great alternative to the busier ones like Starved Rock.  There may not be as much to do, but there are some trails and boat rentals.  They also have plenty of bathrooms, including a main one with sinks and showers.

The campground is quiet and peaceful, and we enjoy the smaller turnaround areas that have tall pines and more shade than the larger main camping area.  There is also a camp store with firewood, rentals and a restaurant with limited hours.

A very nice recreational area, but closed to pedestrian access as of summer of 2013 due to structural issues with the pedestrian bridge.  While the island is still open to the public, hopefully walking and biking access will be restored.

The island had historical value and is a nice place to walk, bike, fish, or just enjoy a bit of nature in an otherwise urban location.

EDIT:  As of December 2017, the island is open to pedestrian traffic again because of a newly built bridge!

A great stretch along the Moline / East Moline riverfront with walking / biking trails, plenty of parking, picnic tables, benches, and playgrounds.  There's even bike pump / tool stations along the route for riders to use!  The area does flood almost every year these days when the river is high, but they do a good job of keep it maintained.  The trail extends beyond the park in both directions if you want to walk or ride up or down the river.

We loved our visit here, and it was free to visit and park.  Beautiful rocks and cliffs line the shore, and there is a nice trail as well.  We saw lots of kayakers down below.  Didn’t see a good map and the layout didn’t seem intuitive at first, but we didn’t stay long enough to check it all out.  We brought our dog too and she had a great time walking with us.

This is an awesome area to visit, whether you're on foot, bike, or boat.  There are bike / hike trails going both directions down the river, as well a boat ramp and plenty of picnic tables and benches.  There's an awesome view of the i-74 bridge, including a walk under the bridge if you want.  One of my favorite places in the heart of the Quad Cities.

Awesome place to visit or hang out on the Illinois side of the Mississippi Riverfront.  There's a very nice playground, plenty of places to sit, a good sized slash park for the kids, and a spectacular view of the river, downtown Davenport, and Centennial Bridge.  Lots of events take place here as well, including a 4th of July celebration.

Known locally as "Rocket Park" because of it's theme, this is a very nice park that is maintained well.  There is a very large area for kids to play with soft turf and many activities.  The location is right off of i74 and is frequented by both Iowans and Illinoisans alike.  Ample parking, shelter, and bathrooms as well.

I come here to mountain bike, and the trails are awesome!  Great for beginners and intermediate riders alike. Nice flowy trails with minimal elevation changes but still some fun features (especially on the 206).

I second everything in Jodi Anderson's post. Nice if you are looking to beat the crowds and have soft prarie ground under your feet. Sure some of the trail is a mowed path through the woods, but that part connects the amazing lake/marsh system in the more center of the area. There aren't trails but are paths in which others have slightly worn and can follow if paying attention. Was the only person there for 3 hours!

Not too busy for early June. Trail that starts at the beginning of the air strip is well maintained and goes through a thin strip of old growth forest - with a 20 min walk to the remnants of an old lighthouse, gated off now for safety =( .  Beach walk was nice too but apparently it used to not have sharp dropoffs but there was a recent storm that washed out the sloping edges.

Take the path via the beach and rocks on the north side of the area if possible (clockwise), as there are mpre birds, prarie, and wildflowers that way. I crossed with a bit of a swell but its still doable. The lighthouse is only open about once a month apparently but at least they leave the stairs open! Very well maintaining and excellent view. Lots of art on the rocks!

Worth it even if just going to dry falls (less than a mile) which has a great little jump in spot and "pool" to sit in! Terrain is varied and fun. Some of the "scenic overlooks" aren't impressive because trees are in the way but not a biggie. The campsite are legit looking and I plan on using one in the future!

Wanted to love this park because of the diverse floral arrangements and musical instruments in the playground area, but there was so much trash. It was spread throughout but most concentrated by the dumpsters. I bet I could have picked up 2 full garbage bags full, but I stopped when my grocery bag was full :(

A 3 1/2 mi out and back trail that is sponsored by The Nature Conservancy and full of possibly more bird sounds at one time than I've ever heard! Stesp toward the end but a legit view and the prarie is pristine.  The last quarter of the hike is a bit shaded in a more woody area which is nice.

There was a Karen who pulled up in her SUV drinking a White Claw and not giving a hoot about social distancing. Also,  saw a decent amount of plastic litter and a rock wall separating the "private condos"...but the sunset was mighty good!

One if the better lake side parks surrounding Lake Mendota. Has a legit playground, volleyball court, and although it's not incredibly wide it's big enough to throw a frisbee without fear of it going in the street.

Only checked out the disk gold course, which was alright. The concessions and grill area had about 20+ people gathered/partying despite COVID group restrictions and the poor park ranger had to go break that up =/

Adjacent to the Aldo Leopold Nature Center and accessible from it. Many of the trails are dead ends but that is OK. There is a long land bridge between two marshy ponds and for me that is the highlight
Very spacious and lots of parking. Great view of the hydro plant. Its a shame the beaches are kind of dirty and when u go of path there is a lot of trash. I tried to pick some up but there was a LOT
Hiked the whole loop, but I recommend starting at the NE most lot and checking out the hill (Frederick Hill) and then jaunt over to Frederick Springs, as they are the highlights in my opinion!
Coolest nuns around are the Franciscan sisters of perperual adoration! We may not overlap on politics all the way but these particular ladies have nothing but love in their hearts!
The staff and volunteers were so genuinely friendly. Surely the most eco-conscious botanical garden I've ever been too - which I appreciate. The trails are A+.
Small but quaint and u great view of the Capital from here. Lots of area to lay out kite-surfing equipment in the large field nearby.
Worth a couple hour stop. This seems like a legit non profit doing amazing work without exploiting animals unlike the bear center.
Often crowded bit the trails are wide most of the way. The staircases are cool. Some geology and history. Trail ends at the river
According to the park site they own a lot of the land that the Leoplold Center uses and they lease it to them, which is nice!
Ran into the very friendly park ranger in the parking lot on my way out and was very full of good info. What a unique park.
Awesome open space close to C.Springs. Stop here for sure after a day at manitou or the Inline and you wont be disappointed
Wow, what a little gem! Got a cool pic where a monarch flew through my shot and a few close up of a cardinal taking a bath!
Many of the best trails begin from the nature center. Be sure to check out the eagle scout bird project (see pics)
Very eclectic and cute park. Parked here to walk across the cool boardwalk that goes across the edge of the lake.
Walked the visitors center in the winter. Still sooo many birds and so much beauty within just and hour walk
Lovely trail. Its one way for COVID and they let a group in every four minutes, which is just right

Completed the yellow waling path today in this large preserve.  The best place to park for the path is at the village hall which is in the middle of the 3 mile path.  You can go either way then return.  The path is all crushed limestone and is about 50% covered so plan ahead.  There are tremendous views and lots of wildlife.  There are a few large hills that you will encounter but not bad at all.  The path was somewhat busy at 4pm on a Sunday but not out of hand.  Everyone was very friendly today.

Great park to play ball if you are in soccer or baseball. The fields are well kept but sometimes flood with heavy rain. Parking sometimes is an issue and needs to be expanded. A fruatrating thing is that this park was renamed to Gbur a few years ago but the signs still say Hamilton. I guess this is typical governmental "it's not my job".

Jewel Cave offers a few different tours that sell out fast.  This is about 20 miles West of Mt Rushmore and is well worth the trip.  The visitors center has an elevator that takes you to the beginning of your tour by knowledge rangers.  Plenty of shopping items await you as you finish your tour.  Pricing is reasonable.

The Dells are the main attraction of the area and it is worth spending money to visit the river and area.  There are several options to view the river and nature.  The Original Ducks are great and they will shuttle you from the downtown area to the main launch.  This is a tourist area so be prepared to spend money.

This is one of the oldest homes with a lot of history in Palatine. In April 2016 they celebrated the 150th anniversary of Palatine and buried a time capsule out front.  For those who will be around in 50 years, they are planning on opening this up.  Great place to visit and learn of the history of the site.

This mountain is 14,115 feet in height and has a 19 mile road to get to the peak.  They are currently remodeling the top and have limited parking so they are offering shuttles from mile 13 and mile 16.  The COG was also being rebuilt while we were there.  Overall this is a great experience and visit.

Today I jumped on the equestrian trail which is on the South side of Ivanhoe road which has a small sign. This trail is great as it was not busy and there are miles of trails to pick from. There were several riders on horses so watch where you step. Everyone was friendly and there is a lot of shade.

This is a kids play area within the Royal Gorge Bridge and Park area.  This is on the West side of the gorge and you have to either take the bridge or the gondola over.  This provides a great area for the kids to hang out and play while the parents can site and relax or check their phones and email.

Camp Kane is a historical park just South of the downtown area of St Charles.  It is a large park and played an important role in the Civil War.  It was a training camp and today the reenactment people were there on horses and were practicing.  The Fox River Trail runs just West of this park.

It's a casino and the house is not in your favor.  Great place to lose your money but they have good restaurants. The atmosphere is friendly and active at any time of day or night. There is plenty of parking at the garage or out front in the main lot. There is no charge to enter the building.

Maggie Rogers Park is a small park in Inverness on the corner of Bradwell, Baldwin and Ela Roads.  There is parking on the West side for when you visit.  This is not a very busy park but great for the youngsters.  There are some trees for you to rest under or have a picnic with the family.

Great National Park to learn about the history of where Abraham Lincoln was born and spent some younger years.  They have a museum and grounds to walk around on.  The spring where young Abraham played in is onsite and there are many other things to see. Make time to visit some time.

Hidden and often missed gem in the beginning of Mammoth Cave park.  There is a lot of history with Floyd Collins.  The trail ends at the top of the cave entrance but you can make your way around the fence to follow the trail to the cave.  Read up on Floyd before hitting the trail.

This is the original residence of the owner and founder of the park. There are tours available and you can stroll thru the hallways.  This house is on the North end of the park and only takes 10 minutes to walk to it. The house has a lot of history that is explained by the guides.

Nice park next to Harper College. There is a large lake to fish at and a couple small piers to watch. Next to the lake is a dog park and play area for the kids. You can reserve the picnic Pavillion for larger events. In addition there is a nice grass and paved walking path.

I used to take my boys here when they were younger and they had a full day of fun. This is great for kids under 10 years old with many options of learning. You can bring your own food and eat at the food court or order from them. There is plenty of parking for many cars.

Great park for the entire family. There are multiple baseball diamonds to play ball at and play grounds for the kids. On the South end the Community Pool sits. The park is well maintained and is open year round. In the winter they set up a temporary ice skating rink.

This is the museum on the majestic Cantigny Park grounds. They are open every day except Mondays. There are two tours in the building that are for free. The tours cover some history and details of the Cantigny Battle. This tour is great for all ages in your group.

This town square is in the middle of Woodstock Illinois. They have parking all around the space and the street is lined with various shops to spend money at. They have a gazebo in the middle area where they have summer concerts and plenty of space for a picnic.

Great park to swim at or rest at.  There are several benches and about 25 parking spots.  Several informational signs are posted to read about the history.  The bathroom was pretty much destroyed today by someone.  Not sure how often this is cleaned.

Hidden park witg tennis courts and playground. There is a nice paved basketball court with nice rims. Behind the tennis courts is a large field to play in. The playground equipment was changed out recently which is a nice improvement  from the past.

Great place to relax and have a picnic.  This is in a convenient place and holds the Palatine Christmas tree.  For those who know Palatine, this was the original home of the Taste of Palatine before it moved and renamed Streets of Palatine.
Looks to be a man made lake with a running path around it.  It was in use by a lot of people.  Free WiFi was also available in the area.
Explored this forest via car and came across the dam recreation lake. I need to come back to discover more.
Great place for younger kids but it is stuck in the middle of Navy Pier which is an overpriced location.

This park is HUGE! New Orleans City Park has been a 1,300-acre public park since 1854, making it one of the nation's oldest urban parks; and is the 87th largest and 20th-most-visited urban public park in the United States. The City Park is approximately 50% larger than Central Park in New York City!  Definitely something to hit up when your in New Orleans!

Today's park is renown for the crowning claim of having the world's largest stand of live ancient oak trees, which includes a grand oak that dates back nearly 800 years! These unique trees are known for their distinctive sculptural shape - some of the oldest trees have limbs that are twice as long as the oak is tall.  Home to modern art; a museum and the beauty of a live performances, 160 years in the making.

We would recommend to go to their website when you choose to go there to get a grasp of all the things there are to do at this enormous, yet enchanting park! For starters there is an equestrian area with stables of horses to ride. Beautiful botanical gardens, a Mini golf,  Story land-the amusement park, A renown sculpture garden, a children's playground, the museum of art, and an old style classic park cafe that serves up classic New Orleans sandwiches and beignets, and a huge golf course. The park accommodates its guests with bike rentals and boat rentals at the lake to explore this massive park in! If your feeling a bit romanced by the park, you'll be surprised to find gondolas boats for rent that comes with their very own gondolier to sing their bird songs while you enjoy the day at the park with your very special someone!

The oak trees are simply stunning and mesmerizing. after a full day at the park their shade simply begs you to take a comfy nap under them!

WOW!!! This botanical garden is the BEST one I've been to yet! Amazingly beautiful; so large that it contains all sorts and types of gardens ranging from French Renascence Gardens, Elizabethan Era Gardens, Water Gardens, Shady Gardens, to Gardens of the West,  Internationally Inspired, Ornamental flowers and foliage, Herb, Cactus, Ornamental Grasses, Alpine, Tropical Jungle Conservatory,  Oak Groves, South African, Victorian, and "Romantic" Gardens! That's just to name the few that comes to mind! :D
The entire park is a romantic getaway that you wouldn't think you would find right in the center of Denver, you simply forget where you are while your strolling through this place. We saw a handful of families that were on-point when they planned their visit with a full picnic. WE definitely are looking forward to taking our picnic with us next time, too!
I recommend this place for everyone, even if someone isn't crazy about nature... These gardens showcase nature in such a way it will mesmerize you and take you back to simpler times!!! Just set aside plenty of time for your day hike. We went thinking to set aside 2 to 3 hours for this and after 5 hours realized we want to come back to properly enjoy this with a picnic. Its hard to get tired of all the beauty, scent's, tastes of the edibles, and the feel of some of the most velvet like foliage!

Simply a Fantastic park that runs about 9 miles through town from north to south. It replaced an old rail road line that was in its place. Prior to the rail road being laid down it actually followed a historic trail that was once famously used by both American and Mexican Soldiers during the American/Mexican War over escalating conflicts over Texas.
Today, the park cuts through a range of  our beautiful local ecosystem of resacas, thorn brush, grass fields, and chaparral that exists all along the trail. Whether your there to beak sweat or to do some nature watching, you'll be in for a treat. The trail is lined with local plants, birds, and aquatic life! Additionally, the trails are loaded with info stations that display photos and information related to the history, flora, and fauna that can be found all along this historic trail.
You'll be surprised how quick you'll be slicing through town utilizing the old direct rail path! You'll find trail users of all ages. The trail is equipped with lights that keep the trail lit up all night. All major intersections are lined with traffic lights to cater to the safety of trail users. And rest assured that you'll find plenty of drinking fountains to keep you hydrated.  Weather your in town visiting or your from town, this trail is well worth a visit!

Looking to do something off the beaten path?! This park might just be for you! It's a great location to go enjoy this historic mill and the beautiful flora and fauna that surrounds this beautiful location. Simply put, its peacefully isolated.
It has an accessible mill house to explore the manner these mills were laid out. its built on a beautiful ledge next to the falls where you get to see the cascading waterfall empty into the Chunky River. You'll know your in the wild by simply listening to the sounds of birds and rustling trees above. The park some short nature trails that are long enough to wind through the woods where its home to birds of the region, including wild turkey, squirrels, and deer. You're more likely to run into these jittery critters here  than the parks closer to the city because if it weren't for this mill, there would be nothing but nature and a beautiful clear river running through this area. You can swim, fish, and even canoe in this stretch of river. Up on the edge there's some picnic tables and grills for having a beautiful family outing. It is certainly quiet out here and for those that truly want to get away!

The Last Refuge for the endangered ocelot.
Laguna Atascosa is the largest protected area of natural habitat in the Lower Rio Grande Valley.  It is a large refuge of 98,000 acres out in the countryside right by the bay!.
It is well known for having a small family of ocelots living near the park as well as the rare Jagurundis. Its a rare find simply because of their keen senses, plus they are nocturnal. Best chances of spotting them is early in the morning or during sun-setting hours.
Also very well known for their bird varieties; from the colorful Green Jays, the elegant Great Egret, to the stunning Raptor birds of prey such as the Caracara Falcons!
To get the best sightings we recommended to get there early in the morning! You'll catch an eye full of white tailed deer, havalinas, rabbits, bobcats, roadrunners, coyotes, rattlers, alligators, and if your sightseeing party is quiet enough, you may even catch a glimpse of the mystical Nilgai.
Remember, the key to seeing all this rich wildlife in its natural habitat is being as stealthy as possible... Whisper and be vewy quiet! And most importantly, HAVE FUN!!!

Home of the largest ranching operation in Texas in the 18th century during the Spanish Colonial Era of Texas.
The beautiful Goliad State Park earns an extra star, in our view, because not only for its scenic views of the San Antonio River that flows through these campsites but because it is chockfull history ranging from Spanish Colonial Era up to the Texas Revolution Era! It's full of interest for the history lover due to the historic significance that exists here. One is able to enjoy the serenity of this Spanish colonial church and surrounding buildings and view exhibits that explore the history and daily life of the missionaries and Indian converts.
Interestingly enough, Goliad State Park is located across the "Presidio La Bahia" Fort that played a major role in the Texas Revolution. Here, Colonel Fannin and his ill-fated men were held prior to being executed at Santa Anna's order, an act of infamy later recalled at the Battle of San Jacinto with the cry, "Remember Goliad! Remember the Alamo!"

We had the pleasure of visiting Fiesta Texas during Fright Fest 2015! This place is decked out in Halloween Décor to the brim! THE WHOLE FAMILY LOVE IT! My little girl of 14 even cried with one of the scare zones! :D. Get there early and you'll be surprised how short all the lines to the park rides are. If your into completely blowing your mind on extreme rollercoasters we'd have to recommend the Rattler. During Fright Fest, all the ghouls arrive at the back train station (by the Rattler rollercoaster), and if you want to get a glimpse of them all together be there to catch them. Its a great time seeing them perform and creep through out the park. The rest of the night you'll be able to catch them in their confined Scare Zones. And the park is covered in a thick mist. They have out done themselves and if you are to go anytime of the year, Fright Fest would be the time!

The Cathedral Basilica of St Louis King of France is the most iconic landmark of all the French Quarter!  The city's center of worship for over 280 years, the Cathedral Basilica of St. Louis remains the oldest active Cathedral in the United States It is a very well kept historical landmark!  The art work within its walls... impeccable.  Stop by any given day and watch a litany of street performers rustling up the change from spectator pockets! Art vendors selling their art and wares outside in front of the square where the Cathedral stands!  There you will find iconic restaurants and cafe's, also known as respectable icons of New Orlean's French Quarter!  For the city square... the Cathedral-Basilica of St. Louis is the head of that square!  At night you will find ghost tours talking about the mystery of this building... its worth a drop of a peek!  Go check it out!!!

Garner state park is one of my favorite state parks in Texas and happens to be one of the most visited overnight state parks in all of Texas!!!  If you and yours are lookin to camp over the summer, Garner State Park is ganna be the spot. The Frio River stays a cool 60 degrees even during the summer which makes for a heck of a refreshing swim during the heat of a Texas summer! During windy afternoons, even the breeze is kept cool by swooping through the river valley.
One can camp, hike, paddle boat, go tubing, picnic, canoe, fish, play miniature golf, ride bikes, and enjoy the community dance during the summer evenings at the pavilion!  Whatever you choose to do, make sure you go up river some and set yourself up with one of the outfitters to enjoy yourself a lazy float down one of Texas' favorite river stretches down the Frio!

This has got to be one of the most unorthodox and most beautiful sculpture gardens I've ever been to!  The art is out of this world and the wonderful garden that surrounds each piece has been so methodically blended in with the art.  You can't tell if the art has been blended in to the garden or if the garden has been manipulated to support the art!  You have everything from classical sculpting to out of this world, eerie like wonders, that will have your mind racing!  Definitely, the kind of art that will make you stop and ponder!
This is the kind of Sculpture garden that even if your not an aficionado, it will capture your interest!
The Sydney and Walda Best of Sculpture Garden is just one of the many things to do within the MASSIVE Nola City Park! Drop on by, you'll be happy you did!

San Fernando de Bexar Cathedral is the oldest cathedral in the state of Texas! Its a work of art to say the least. A lot of detail went into the design of the Cathedral. A style that was so pronounced in the past.
Within these walls a casket is displayed in it's own room in one of the entrances to the cathedral. In the casket lays the bones of the "heroes" of the Alamo... David Crockett, James Bowie, and William B. Travis.
Although this Cathedral is a work of art as it stands, during some evening you can see it come to life as a laser light show paints the face of the cathedral with moving images and colors that turn into an illustrated story of Texas History! At the very least this is an impressive light and sound show that shouldn't be missed!

Gladys Porter Zoo is a world renown wildlife preserve! Because of its location it takes advantage of the natural subtropical climate that exists in the region. This climate makes it ideal for harboring the worlds exotic animals in open air exhibits! And for those of you that love exotic flora, the Gladys Porter Zoo is a contained botanical garden that showcases some of the worlds flora specimens as well as its fauna!
Located in the heart of Brownsville, its stands as one of the city's iconic attraction! A Clear winner for the whole family! Certainly not to be missed if your in town!
FunNote: Sit with Americas National Bird at the aviary and enjoy some ice cold beers to cool you off while you enjoy the magnificence of the American Bald Eagle.

The Broadway Vegas Strip populated by drifters, dealers, old cowboys, drunks, and homeless people. Showcases the best and worst humanity has to offer! You've got your super heroes along side the blvd putting on their performances for some jingle, the winners racing from the casino to the shops to spend their money, the raving/rolling party as they leave a trail of mayhem in their wake, pick pockets, hustlers, falling midgets, angry pimps, and the many homeless and no talent "rappers" on the catwalks trying to scam a quick $20 by selling blank CDs.
Grab yourself a bottle and walk down the blvd because this bozo circus nightmare is always kickin and a great place to freak watch!!!
dislikes: Presence of drifters, dealers, and homeless

reviews_attraction.text:
The "Old Morgue" of Fort Brown was built about 150 years ago. This lab was one of the first places yellow fever was studied via autopsy. It was here, Dr Gorgas discovered treatment and prevention of Yellow Fever.
The tree in front of the morgue was said to be used to hang criminals before conveniently depositing the bodies at the morgue.

An interesting side note:
The Old Morgue building is infamous for being haunted and many reports of apparitions have accumulated over its history. Ghost hunters have been known for frequenting this building and have observed anomalies and carried out studies of oddities present around said building.

Ripley's Haunted Adventure Rocks! It had been one of the first Haunted Houses of its kind. I really enjoyed this one because unlike seasonal haunted houses this one has actors year round that have perfected the art of surprise and haunt! Get into it, let yourself go, and awaken your inner adventurous self! The Vertigo Room is a MAJOR TRIP!  I would keep going through that room alone if I could. Whenever you get to it, let all the other guests walk ahead of you until they are no longer visible in the Vertigo room to best "feel" the room. Without other guests standing in front of you, you truly feel like your getting pulled in! :D

One of the nicest parks I visited while I was in Mississippi. A lovely state park with a tall beautiful forest on the edge of the Bienville National Forest. Has plenty of cabin accommodations as well as full hookups and primitive campsites. Plenty of wildlife to be found in these forests. Not to mention it has beautiful trails that maze into the nearby forest!
It also has an open field for baseball, basketball, and even a pool area with a large slide to enjoy with the kids! A place for the whole family!

These caves are awesome! It looks like another world down there! Dress as if your heading out to the beach and wear tennis shoes. I've been to a handful of caves and this one really takes the cake. It has tall and wide rooms that have some marvelous stalactite and stalagmite sculptures! Some of these sculptures are larger than life and out of this world!  Next time we're definitely going on the Adventure Tours!!! It's a whole new ball game for those who want to truly explore the caverns! :D

A nice park to take the family. Practically every location is accessible via car and lots of paved trails. Plenty of drive up camp sites. There is no Primitive camping sites so if your trying to rough it, this wouldn't be the park. It does have a nice stream to falls to enjoy a good swim in. Don't forget to walk the coolest trail, which is an ancient native American hidden trail that still survives in existence today. Check it out & enjoy!

I really enjoyed reading the info bulletins of every animal there at Animal World. The info wasn't your standard bore of stats. These bulletins explained that I was looking at the worlds smallest marsupial, worlds largest rodent, worlds largest owl, etc. Overall it had a great collection of animals. Both in number and in interesting facts that was displayed about these animals!!! Great for the whole family no doubt

A good stop to get acquainted with Mississippi. This great, heavy stone, intricate, architecture is astounding! It's a shame not to see this kind of quality work anymore.  It's an easy walk through museum. Most of it is "interactive", meaning its equipped with sound speakers and some videos that tell you summaries of the history that revolved around and/or associated with the state capitol.

It's Brownsvilles main sports park in town. its large. holds major city events during the year. The 4th of July, Independence celebration is a must to goto if your in town for it!  Tailgating is a must! Plus they have stands, entertainment and music! Plenty of trails and designated bbq pits!

Easily one of the best museums I've ever been to. Outer space, flora & fauna, Ancient Egypt. & Egyptian mummies, dinosaurs & prehistoric earth! Simply put, it has redefined what  a museum is and should be! Never thought a museum was THIS cool!!!

Its a beautiful park right inside the city. Although you wouldn't know it when your standing in the center of it all. It is an oasis of nature right inside town! Perfect for when you want to getaway without leaving the city! :D

The southern end of linear park! It's where most of linear parks events are held... Right across the all famous Gladys Porter Zoo... Next to the museum of fine arts... Home of Brownsville's farmers market!
Great park to learn how such a beautiful real estate was once a brutal historical battleground. Great for picnics and jogs

This park is absolutely amazing. I have never seen anything like it. Endless things for children and adults. It is not your typical park. It is your typical park times a million. I also loved that they had plenty of wheelchair accessible activities for the children who may need to use them so that they are able to enjoy the park with everyone else. I am 24 and I feel like a kid when I step onto this spectacular playground. It is also very clean and all the equipment is in very good condition. Even the bathrooms get a five star. I love telling people about this park, it is a great conversation starter on things to do.

I absolutely love every single mile of the cape harreras national seashore. I love having the open beach, nothing but sand, dunes, and water. No houses, no hotels, no stores, just nature. I like that during off season ( with a permit ) you can drive on the beaches. Its definitely my favorite beach to visit. I have found so many beautiful shells, sand dollars, and sea glass while exploring the beautiful coasts. It's almost like a fairytale, it seems like endless beauty. Great place for vacations, camping, fishing, photography, and most of all Solitude.

I grew up going to the park. Whether is was playing on the playground or playing in the river I've always enjoyed it. The furnace itself is huge and amazing to look at and hear the stories. They have it gated off but you can still walk around the outside of it to get the full view of each angle. It's really pretty in spring and fall with all the trees, plants, and flowers that surround it in the right season. I love the steps that go down into the Dan river that allow for easy river access and no nice seating if you just wanna relax with a view.

Absolutely breathtaking views around every turn. So much to do. Harrah's casino, Santa land, so many different shops. They have a lot of awesome Indian shops with amazing little trinkets. I love all the wood work and dream catches. They have several parks, rivers, waterfalls. So many different places to hike. Plenty of restaurants and hotels. Definitely perfect for anyone that loves the outdoors and Indian culture. They have an Indian museum that makes the perfect day trip and learning experience. I always have a great time in Cherokee.

I love this little Pitt stop when I'm cruising the blue ridge parkway. First off it has nice and clean bathrooms when it is open. The museum itself is very neat. It tells you about the states rocks and where some of are found. It goes in to detail of course with all kinds of pictures, diagrams, and of course rocks to touch. I think it is a very neat and informative little place and I like stopping there and testing my rock knowledge. I highly recommend it for any NC rockhounders and also just for fun.

I absolutely love this short trail outside Bryson City. The drive to the trailhead is amazing. Winding curves, colorful farms, variety of farm animals and wildlife everywhere. Even the parking areas have lots to look at. Plenty of benches and picnic tables. Lots of parking. Bathrooms during the warm seasons. The trail is very easy. Slightly uphill on the way there. The fairytale bridge is a huge bonus. The falls are beautiful and long. They are even better after a good rain. Highly recommended.

I absolutely love taking a day trip to Moratock Park. It has two sides both directly across from the road from each other. The side with the Furnace is historic and beautiful especially in the spring and summer. There is also a river access here and a playground for young children. On the other side of the road is more river access with multiple picnic tables and benches to relax and enjoy the view and crisp mountain air. I definitely love visiting this area.

I've been going to Bogue Inlet Fishing pier since I was a young child. I always enjoy a stroll along this pier. Fishing off of it is also really fun. The store you cross through has everything you'll need to fish in case you forgot something. It does cost to fish. I like how that have a double deck at the end of the pier for better views without being in the way. It's a really fun experience at this pier whether you are just walking or going fishing.

I highly recommend this trail. Its is stunning from the moment you get out of your car and then for the entire mile hike up to the falls. There are many places to stop and rest and take in the amazing beauty of this forest. I love that the trail follows a creek all the way to the falls. It is a very moderate hike that leads to some very choppy stairs. It is literally breathtaking, the hike and the view. 2 mile round trip, totally worth every step.

I absolutely love this overlook. It is very easily accessible from the winston-salem/stokes county area. Its straight up highway 52 past mount airy. It has a very clear over view of pilot mountain and downtown winston salem and is perfect for cameras with good zoom. Plenty of people have signed the wooden fense over the years. This isnone of my favorite eastern NC blue ridge parkways overlooks. It is beautiful during all seasons.

A beautiful place right outside the city life. Short and long trails for every stage hiker. You can also walk across the waterfall just be careful and cautious. There are plenty of rocks to jump on and water across on the opposite side of the park. They have old buildings including a mill and much more open on Saturdays and sundays 1-5pm. They have port a potties but they were locked today. Also shelters and picnic tables.

I always enjoy making a short trip out to shacktown falls. The placement is perfect, its right off 421 and the location itself is only a skip and a hop from the road so there isn't much walking/hiking involved. Ive only seen it packed in the summer time, typically when I go I am the only one there. The trail is very wide and easy to navigate. I like that it also goes anobe the falls with lots more to see.

This place is absolutely fantastic. It's fun for all ages even the adults. There are so many different things to look at and explore. It is very hands on and makes learning very full. Its takes several hours to get through the entire thing. The shop is very nifty with lots of cute things. They have snacks. They also have events at the location and on the website. Definitely an amazing and cheap day trip.

I absolutely love visiting this trail. It is always beautiful. I love catching it around sunset because you can sit at the top of the stairs and watch it fall behind the mountains and still have enough daylight to make it back to the parking lot. Its also nice in the winter with the icicles and such. There are amazing views from the falls to toris den to the surrounding mountain range off in a distance.

I really enjoyed my time at South Mountain. I took the High Shoals trail it's about a 2 mile round trip. The hike is fairly moderate up until the stairs. I loved walking by the river and catching all of its beauty as well as the falls. I highly recommend this trail and to bring water and snacks. I look forward to going back and seeing what the rest of the park has to offer.

I loved it. Free admission but they do have a donation box. Plenty of things to see. Learn all about sea life. Pirate ships. Boats and more. They also have shows and events posted on the boards outside and also on their website. They have a movie theater and they play different films. The staff was very friendly. The library was absolutely amazing. I had an amazing time.

I absolutely love every visit to this place. They have an amazing little country store and restaurant. They have a working water wheel. Informational posts on all the old equipment. They have camp grounds as well. Public bathrooms during open hours. Plenty of nm parking. Hidden little waterfall. Amazing walking paths with incredible views. All around a lovely day trip.

Absolutely amazing. Not much parking. It is literally right off the road but they do have some signs. The parkway is right up from it as well. The trail is very interesting. Cliff side and then a guided rope walk down to the falls. It is a rather rough trail, lots of slick spots. The falls are absolutely beautiful. Its nice how two come together and form one.

Everytime I place by Creswell I always stop by this place. They have an amazing set up with some very beautiful views. They also have an amazing back story and is definitely worth a tour. They even have trails that lead over to Lake Phelps with spectacular views of the lake. It also has benches to take a rest and enjoy the view. Swimming is prohibited.

This place is absolutely beautiful. Even though it was cloudy the garden was stunning. I really enjoyed the variety of plants, herbs, and flowers. It has plenty of little sitting areas they are just to cute for words and extremely calming and relaxing. They have little hidden trinkets everywhere and they were super neat. I really enjoyed my time there.

The nature of the park is beautiful. The bathrooms were absolutely replusive. There was no soap or running water in the woman and no running water in the mens. The floors were trashed and the toilets were discolored and full of feces and urine. It also smelt like a cow pasture. It needs a lot of tender love and care and also lots of tax money.

I love this little overlook off the Blue Ridge Parkway. It has a few picnic tables with nice views. During season it has a public restroom. The cascades trail is to the left behind the bathroom. It's very short but beautiful. Ot has little bridges and runs beside a creek up to the falls. The falls themselves are amazing.

Sweet little park with many trails and sights to see. The cave was awesome. I look forward to going farther in next time. The stairs ain't terrible but there are a bunch. The bathrooms were very nice, clean, and well stocked. The Rose's were in bloom and looked gorgeous. I like this amazing state park.

Absolutely beautiful views. I love the little visitor  center/ store. They have tshirts and maps and other things. The staff is always friendly and ver helpful. The parking can have its moments. Some days it's full and some days it's not. It has wonderful views on all sides. It also has bathrooms.
A very cute and educational little stop. They had many different crops growing and they were in full bloom and beautiful.

The only national park in Rhode Island (and the smallest one in the country), this place doesn’t look like much upon first glance. It’s a nice park, well-maintained and picturesque, but it’s very small for a national park and for the most part looks like any other park in the city.

The cool part about this park is the history behind it. This is pretty much where Providence was founded, and Roger Williams lived very nearby. There’s a historic well, plenty of informational signs, and a wonderful visitor’s center.

If you’re looking for a breath of fresh air or a stroll through a park, this is an alright option with plenty of better alternatives. If you want to learn more about the history of Providence and Rhode Island, there’s a lot to discover here.

Very cool mansion formerly owned by a coal magnate. They are one of the two Newport Mansions that are open to yours during covid. There’s an app you can download that will give you a very in depth history of the mansion, or a pamphlet that is a little more surface level but you can move a lot quicker. Or you can choose to just take in the beauty of the place! It’s crazy that people lived like this, and really gives a good insight into the inequality of life in the Gilded Age, especially if you take the Servant Life tour. After you work your way through the mansion, you can hang out in the enormous courtyard and explore the trees, fountains, and statues. Well worth the cost of admission, which I believe was $18/person.

One of the most unique state parks in Rhode Island, Beavertail is all about the rocky shoreline. Pretty small compared to the other state parks, there’s not much in terms of open space besides a small field near the lighthouse and the areas that are used as parking. But with all the nooks and crevices on the shoreline, there is still plenty to explore. The lighthouse is one of the oldest in the country, and eventually they will be open for tours again. Plus, Conanicut Island is a really cool, rural area uncommon in RI, so the drive out here is nice even if it is a bit out of the way. Highly recommend to tourists and locals alike!

My favorite state park in RI (at least so far), this park has a little bit of everything. At the north end along the bay there’s a nice, but small, town beach surrounded by a playground and a lot of sports fields. As you walk south along the water, you come across a picturesque lake, a dock, plenty of picnic tables, and a trail into the woods. Further on, there’s a barn that’s been converted into a museum, although I didn’t stop in. Great place to relax on a weekend and get a nice view of the bay. It also seems like a very popular place to get professional photos taken.

Beautiful beach looking out onto the bay. It is a little on the smaller side when you compare it to some of the oceanfront beaches like Wheeler and Scarborough, but it is just as beautiful, and you have the added bonus of Iggy’s being right there. There’s a nice park as well, and sometimes people will sing/perform right by the historic gazebo. The sand is free of rocks and shells for the most part. Not the best place to catch some waves or search for seashells, but it is a fantastic place for a quick trip to the beach, especially if you have kids.

Love this beach. A lot of people come here year round, and if you’re a surfer this is the beach to come to in RI. Has a nice, long, sandy shoreline, all the way from the Towers to the Narrows, where the river runs into the ocean. There are some rocks on that end that birds like to nest on, so if you bring binoculars you can get a pretty good look at them. Lots of people come here to walk their dog, and even if the weather’s bad it seems like people just come and chill in their cars. Can’t blame them though, it really is a beautiful beach.

One of the best parts of Pueblo, City Park has a lot going on. The Parks & Rec department does an awesome job of running events in the summer, there is always family activities available. From the zoo to the kiddie rides and the dog park to the frisbee golf, there’s something for everyone. There’s also access to trails down by the river for runners or dog owners. They even have several softball fields, tennis courts, a public pool, and a skate park. If you’re wondering what to do on a nice day, spend some time at City Park.

Pretty nice beach near Quonset Point. The water didn’t look too great, definitely doesn’t seem like a great place to go for a swim but is a good place to take a walk along the bay. A lot of pretty cool shells around here too. Might even see a cargo ship coming in or out of Quonset. Also has a nice paved bike path leading up to it and a short trail through a wooded area. Pretty unique beach in RI with some nice natural areas, residential neighborhoods, and an industrial zone all right up against each other.

Makes me miss Colorado. Great hiking spot for Massachusetts, especially for the eastern half of the state. We went when it was really foggy, which made for a very surreal experience on the summit, but look forward to going back for the views. There’s a ton of hiking trails, but if you’re not feeling it you can drive your car to the summit, too. Parking is $5 if you have Mass plates, $20 if not. Also a ski resort in the winter, although I’ve heard the slopes are nothing to write home about.

One of two parks on the shore of Lake Quinsigamond, this is the one that I would recommend. Regatta Point is great if you have a boat. Otherwise, come here. Parking is free and there is an extensive walking path as well as a small beach. There are plenty of trash cans around and there are even bags to pick up after your dog. Unfortunately, there are no bathrooms and the area can get a bit muddy. It’s a great place to skip rocks in the summer, or to throw rocks out on the ice in the winter.

Intriguing historical site in Newport, a seemingly simple stone tower with a lot of debate on its origins. Some people claim it was built by Vikings during the Leif Erikson expeditions, while others believe it is the remnants of a Portuguese or even Chinese built structure. There’s even a small group of people (my mom included) that believes it was built by ancient aliens! Whatever its origins, it makes for a wonderful place to sit, think, and enjoy the day.

Spacious dog park with plenty of room for them to play. I’ve only been here a few times, but each time the other owners have been very friendly and responsible with their dogs. There are separate areas for small and large dogs, and both are fairly large and open. Unfortunately it’s almost completely dirt, but the dirt is pretty sandy and doesn’t stay muddy for long. I wish it was a little greener, but regardless it’s always a good experience.

A very nice, relaxing park to come to for some peace and quiet. The Woonasquatucket River runs right next to it and provides some great views. There are often a lot of geese and ducks around the park, which is nice except for the fact that their poop is everywhere. Not much you can do about that though. There’s a nice bike path that runs right along the river, and a lot of open space for activities. Overall, a great park!

The view coming into Fall River is super cool, the industrial style bridge matched with the view of the city is actually really beautiful. Because Fall River is on a hill, you can see a lot of the buildings, and the churches really stand out. I also like how you can just see the top of the battleship when you’re driving out. I’m from Colorado so I’m weirdly obsessed with bridges, but I especially like this one.

Beautiful spot with some scenic views, but unfortunately it’s not very accessible and there’s not much in the way of hiking trails around here. I also went when the water levels were low, I think, so I didn’t even get a good view of the falls. If it were made more accessible to the public, it could be a lot better. As it stands, though, there’s so many better places to experience nature in RI.

Beautiful ball park, great ticket prices and the concessions are not as bad as I expected. This was my first visit to Fenway and I had a great time. I’m from Colorado and Coors Field is pretty hard to beat, but Fenway was at least very close. Very easily accessible by public transit, I would recommend parking at a station on the green line. It’s cheap and you avoid the worst of Boston traffic!
likes: Facilities & Services: Great ticket prices, reasonable concessions

reviews_attraction.text: A nice little beach/park with great views and awesome seashells. It’s in a perfect location to view the whole Narragansett Bay, if you walk out to the point you’re basically right in the middle of it. Dogs are welcome anywhere but the beach which is a big plus for me. Only downside is how hot the sand gets, bring beach shoes!

Huge field, great place for dogs to get some energy out. Would definitely be better if owners would pick up after their pets but unfortunately that’s a problem everywhere. Decent trail by the lake but potential for more if time and energy were invested in it. All in all a good park but could be better if there was more to do.

Really nice zoo with some great exhibits. The elephant enclosure really stands out, but all of the exhibits are large and well put together. Zoos can be a little depressing in my opinion but at their best they are meant to educate people on how we affect wildlife and I think this zoo does a great job of that.

One of the first outdoor excursion I went on in New England, Arcadia did not disappoint. I went in early fall of last year and the views were amazing. There’s some awesome trails, a great place to see the seasons change or to take your dog for an adventure. I look forward to coming back in the near future.

Nice beach, fairly rocky though. Decent place to look for shells, a lot are smashed but if you look closely you can find some good ones. Provides a good view of the Jamestown Bridge. There’s only one trail that does through the woods to the beach. It’s pretty but nothing spectacular. Watch out for ticks!

One of the few parks in Rhode Island that is just as beautiful during winter as it is at any other point in the year. Very nice, clean beach with a great view of the bay. The surrounding area has a small playground for kids, and dogs are welcome. Good place to come read a book on a nice day.

Nice park, especially if you have dogs or kids. Cool statue, good view of the Armory, and exercise stations throughout. Also has a bocci ball court and chess/checkers boards on some of the tables. Great place to enjoy a day off.

This park is awesome, it’s got hiking and equestrian trails in addition to an amazing beach on the bay. Very beautiful, it’s really cool how you can from being in the water to the middle of the woods in a couple minutes.

A really beautiful bridge, especially nice because it’s free. A lot of attention goes to the Newport bridge, and although this one is a little smaller, it is every bit as beautiful and makes for great pictures.

We enjoyed our family evening. Kids and grown ups laughed and had fun!
Yes, it was a drive from the city and you do drive through an industrial area to get there. With all that said- we enjoyed the show very much - beautiful and talented female dancers, handsome and skilled male dancers, friendly staff, very welcoming, gorgeous sunset photos, with palm trees, tiki torches, sandy ground, fun atmosphere with crowd.
Buffet All-You-Can-Eat included- pork, beef, chicken, salads, toss, macaroni, cole slaw, rolls, fresh fruit, light desserts, more.... The pork was our favorite. Unlimited soda. Our package had three Drink tickets from the bar also.
The show was fun and interactive. The fire show was our favorite.
I will say - The announcer spoke very fast and was challenging to understand at times.
Wear casual clothes and shoes. Relax and have fun!

Quaint- and well cared for facility. Geese were enjoyable. Beautiful landscape. A small waking trail on museum site. Good to stretch your legs. Great stop! Coming back to visit. At the museum Tony was so helpful. He give us information on surrounding activities. Great history- look forward to the PowWow in September. There is a small gift area, gallery, museum and beautiful music was playing. Clean restrooms. Nice break on a long trip or a destination if visiting Ponca and spending time in town. And it was all FREE!

Amazing! The museum was worth the admission. They did an excellent job displaying items, honoring the memories, depicting the timeline, and the grounds were beautifully and tastefully designed.
The tree of life was stunting that itself survived the many changes from the 1920's.
So glad we can and spent the afternoon. Nice family time. Parking was a little tricky because the area is very busy so give extra time to park and walk. We parked at the memorial parking and paid $5.

Great stop- a bit challenging to see but so worth the effort.
Clean restrooms inside, easy pull in and turn around for larger vehicles.
Absolutely gorgeous view of Lake Michigan and the Mackinaw Bridge.
Nice rest stop before your bridge crossing.
Inside a video of the building of the bridge is running and you can read about the progress of the construction.

Great family day at this historical site, enjoy boarding the battleship and walking through the ship. We attended during an Anniversary event, navy band and army band were playing, dancing, food vendors, gift shop. Photo opts. Cost of tickets supports the program and upkeep of the ship. It was $ well spent. Many volunteers help also.

Family perfect! We spent the day with 2 and 3 year old and it was great. Playground, restrooms, shower, picnic tables, small beach, wading area is perfect for toddlers, shade trees, across the street from farmers market. Great day at a family friendly beach. Limited parking.

Nice family day, enjoyed pleasant atmosphere, beautiful landscape, visitors center, art exhibit from local artists, restrooms, staff was extra helpful.
Camping, picnic area, lake with ducks, fishes, mongoose, wild pigs.

Great way to spend the day with the family. Exhibits are spaced out and nice walking paths, gift stores, snacks selection, restaurants- salads, soups, sandwiches, fries, desserts, fruits. Wear comfortable shoes. Check out the NEW penguin exhibit.

Historical - if you are a history buff then you are sure to enjoy this.  It was a nice afternoon. Relaxing and fun time, gift shop, nice restrooms, educational area for school groups.  Well cared for and beautiful yard.

Large grassy area and beach. China Man’s Hat view and easy access. Large parking lot. Restrooms. Beautiful view of mountains and ocean.
We enjoyed collecting seashells. Picnic tables and a water fountain.

This is the first place where Mormons settled. It was also the place, where Occupy Salt Lake movement spend their time. It was the place where homeless people live, and the center of Operation Rio Grande to drive homeless people out. All of this make it to me, a person who is interested in local history, and culture a very interesting place. It didn't feel very safe though unfortunately, which is especially bad for homeless people who spend their time here..

On the contrary for example, looking to Mexico City, or Istanbul from a high place can be much more depressive, the second one being where I was grown up. Bring some water, or a legal drink, maybe some food, and spend some time here.

One of the best places to visit in Utah. Read the history of railroad building but especially the actual golden spike ceremony which was really fun. So in the end even though the owners of the company take credit for putting the last spike in, the actual last spike, both golden one and iron one was put in by workers, Chinese-Americans, Irish-Americans and Mormons.

Small park, but one of the best parks in Salt Lake City, in my opinion. It isn't a park being over-promoted like Liberty Park. It is not too small, and dangerous like Pioneer Park. It is not too large and overwhelming like the Sugerhouse Park. And I love to watch people who skateboard here.

An interesting natural area to walk certainly. But not one of the bests in Salt Lake City. Jorden River Parkway, Ensign Peak, and trails at Red Butte area as well as Bounville Shoreline Trail are better.

Now it's just Headquarter of the Passaic County Historical Society. No more Monet, Rembrandt, Renoir. Today only four of Lambert's original paintings remain in the Castle. The very best time to visit is when the wildflowers are in bloom. The park is very beautiful any time of year but I really enjoyed the wildflowers more than I thought I would.  One of the main reasons I really don't care about flowers much is because I can't identify them like I can trees.  The park did a really nice job of periodically labeling some really stunning flowers.  Thank you for that! Also don't miss the mineral springs. We were able to make a nice big loop from several trails.  We tried to hit at least part, if not all, of every trail.

First overlook is breathtaking. This is a fairly hard trail with some awesome views. Best advice is to go clockwise.  Get the big hill with the great view out of the way first. Then the second hill is out of the way and you can enjoy the scenery as the day starts to get hot.  We hiked the loop in June.  There are a few parts that are quite steep but overall it is very enjoyable.  The map listed about 10.5 miles but at the end of the day we had gone a total of about 12 miles.  We ran into some nettle at the end so I wish I had not worn shorts.

The mill was closed for the season when I was here but the often give tours in the summer months. Walk the road from the parking lot to get down to the mill. Be careful as the road is steep.  There is some parking near the mill but the lot at the top is much larger and there are bathrooms there. You can make a nice loop out of the Slippery Rock Gorge Trail and the Kildoo Trail and of course check out the covered bridge.

This is one of my favorite PA state parks. Probably because when we went, we were the only people there on the trail.  There were a few people near the lake..  It was chilly but a perfect day to see the great view from the overlook with the leaves off the trees.  We found some ticks off trail but that was not surprising.  We also saw a porcupine along the way.  I hope to make it back here someday.

Hells hollow is a short hike, about 1.2 miles out and back that is a part of McConnells Mill State Park. There is a good sized parking lot that is fairly easy to find with google maps.  There is also a left fork in the trail to Slippery Rock Gorge Trail that runs into N County Trail that leads to Eckert Bridge then on to the McConnell’s Covered Bridge. This is 15 miles out and back.

Laurel Hill SP is one of my favorite PA state parks. There are many nice trails you can make a loop out of each with different terrain.  Very fun any time of year but summer, spring, and fall are best. Make sure to check out Jones Mill Dam.  Fall is the best time when all of the fall colors are in but any time of year is beautiful.  The Hemlock interpretive area is gorgeous.

This is one of my favorite PA state parks. There are many nice trails you can make a loop out of each with different terrain.  Very fun any time of year but summer, spring, and fall are best. Make sure to check out Jones Mill Dam.  Fall is the best time when all of the fall colors are in but any time of year is beautiful.  The Hemlock interpretive area is gorgeous.

Hiked to Beam Rocks from here on a series of trails.  It was worth the hike even though you can drive to the parking lot of Beam Rocks and start a lot closer but what fun would that be? The short section actually called "Loop Trail" seems like it would be popular for cross country skiing in the winter as it looks loopy and flatish.  We had a wonderful time here.

The 2.4 mile trail around the lakes is really beautiful.  It is a heavily used park so I like to avoid it on weekends in the summer. It's nice throughout the year. There are tamarack trees which are hard to find. They are pines trees but the needles turn yellow and fall off in autumn.  They also have paddleboats here in summer.

The Cedar Creek Gorge Area is really cool with a really neat bridge to cross and a few trails that wind around a small area that includes a hill side. A little steep but not too bad. Hard to get lost as all of the trails in this area are in a area that is visible from almost every part of the trails. Nice little gorge area.

This is a beautiful natural area but it is nice to go when it has not been raining a lot.  There are a lot of stream crossings so when the streams are higher, you are going to get your feet wet.  We have done this trail a few times and it is much more enjoyable with dry feet. It is really nice either way though.

Fall spectacular overlook!  There is a nice trail plus a stunning overlook.  This is one of my very favorite fall spots every year.  If possible, don't just get out for the overlook and run back to your car.  Get out along Baughman Trail and enjoy the fall ness and spooky ghost looking sassafras leaves.

I like to hike so in my opinion, the best time to visit is when the pool is closed.  There are fewer people.  This is a very beautiful park with a lot to see along the trails, waterfalls, a furnace, wildlife, a hearth, etc. We worked out a nice loop hike, a very nice way to spend the afternoon here.

I have visited many covered bridges and I tend to like them all. This one is in a very pretty forest setting, it is very accessible to walk in and around, and you can easily park close by. Just be careful of the traffic. It's fun to visit on days when the park is not busy, lots of time to explore.

Lake Trail is a nice loop around the lake. I also recommend taking at least one of the trails trough the woods.  The trees are beautiful and the trails are wide for some of the more used trails. There are more strenuous trails too if that is your thing. Overall, a very pleasant park.

Love this place. To our surprise, the day we were there you could earn a pickle pin from the gift shop if you walked up the stairs to each floor and got your "passport" stamped. We did indeed earn our pickle pins and got a nice workout. Pittsburgh is an interesting place.

This is a beautiful wooded park in Lancaster Co with lovely well maintained trails through the woods that occasionally lets you get a glimpse of the Susquehanna River below. When I was there, the park was quiet and not crowded at all.

The fitness walking trail is stunning in the snow. It is a one mile paved walking trail that looks fairly well maintained in the winter. There are quarter mile posts and vaulted toilets plus port a johns there.

Interesting piece of Lancaster history if you have already done a lot of other things in the area. My tour guide was knowledgeable and enthusiastic about the subject which made the tour very enjoyable.
Enchanting, easy to follow trails through a wooded area. It is not a very large park but it is heavily wooded which is rare so close to civilization. It’s especially nice when it’s not too crowded.
There is a gift shop and several nice hikes to some gorgeous views. Lookout trail is the one we chose. It is about one mile from the Visitor Center to the last overlook.
Gorgeous, easy, relatively short trail if you just go around the lake but it goes longer. Parking lot fills fast. My favorite trail in RMNP.
Beautiful in the fall. Small lot that fills up early though. Luckily people don’t stay too long so you can usual wait for a spot off season.
Nice, short trail that ends at a waterfall.  The only annoying thing is that parts of the trail are near the road.
I only go here to walk the grounds.  I have never gone inside but plan to some day.  The grounds are lovely.

What makes this experience so wonderful was that our guides and wranglers, the staff don't insist on a cookie-cutter experience. This is not a trail ride where all the horses ride single file so that you see only the person in front of you. Instead, We set off across the Island and crested a ridge above a herd of bison. We had to cross gullies and climb inclines, and that brought us to where we could see about 40 bison with week-old calves. And then, to top it all, it was pointed out a pronghorn for us to see. The staff are gracious, knowledgeable, and friendly.

I really enjoyed my visit there. They play a 20+ minute introductory video in the gift shop that contains all the details. Then I would suggest visiting the adjacent museum prior to the cellular tour of the battlefield.  The park ranger captivated me with his lecture reenactment of the battle that took place at Little Bighorn. He had taught courses in his local high school and college, as well as, advised programs for the Discovery Channel about what happened that fateful day.

The Albright Visitor Center is one of the more interesting visitor centers in Yellowstone National Park it has really cool displays and when you get a chance to talk to one of the Rangers and they can really provide you with a lot of valuable information about the park plus be very careful because this is also one of the hangout for the local elk herd remember all the animals in the park are wild and can be dangerous so keep your distance.

When traveling to the Grand Teton National Park area you have to start here at the national park headquarters.  the staff here are wonderful and have a true interest in helping visitors learned about the park and the best places to see the best things.  plus they also stress that you have to be careful especially around the animals that are in the park because they are wild and they can be dangerous.

This is an incredible place to have the opportunity to see any of the concerts or events that the Tuacahn Center for the Arts puts on. I try to make it down once a year for one of their Productions I've never been disappointed but one thing you need to do is make sure that you get your reservations ahead of time because they are very busy.  But it is worth it.

I remember growing up and taking the hike down to the Morning Glory pool back then it has been several years ago the pool had really great colors in it but as of late because of the mistreatment of Park visitors and all the foreign objects that keep getting thrown into the pool I've have noticed that the pool is losing its colors and dying.

As I visited Yellowstone National Park I always make it a point to stop in the mammoth Springs area over the years I've noticed that from one year to the next the area changes dramatically because of all of the water that comes up that has all the minerals in it it really changes the formations one year to the next.

Every year I take a group of Seniors to see the Christmas Lights on Temple Square.
The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter Day Saint does a really good job of Decorating the Grounds.
There are several close by restaurants to eat at.
I would recommend the Nauvoo Cafe, they have a Turkey Pot Pie the is just Wonderful.

Whenever I'm traveling thru this area I always make it a point to stop at the Cove Fort historic site I really enjoyed walking around and seeing some of Utah's history there are LDS missionaries on hand that will answer any of your questions you might have about the fort so make sure you ask some questions.

I love the Ogden's dinosaur park I have a friend that works there during the summer and she helps disadvantaged kids learn life skills and she's really good at it and this is one of the areas that they practice at. They have really realistic dinosaur replicas and the grounds are always very clean and neat.

The Norris geyser Basin is one of the longer hikes in the National Park when you do this hike make sure you take plenty of water and stay hydrated plus take your time and look around. Plus make sure that you stay on the established trails and do not travel off because it is unwise illegal and dangerous.

If you make it this far north into the Yellowstone National Park you have to stop grab your camera and take a picture of the Roosevelt Arch.  The arch has some interesting history behind it so when you get a chance look up that history and learn a little bit more about Yellowstone National Park.

The park is a large park located along the Sevier River. It has a collection of some of the best Pictographs and Petroglyphs I have seen.  Picnic tables outside and cold water & restrooms available.   Make sure to bring binoculars, or even better, a camera with tripod and telephoto capability.
likes: Facilities & Services (Picnic tables, restrooms, cold water)

reviews_attraction.text: Growing up many many years ago I remember coming to Yellowstone National Park and actually having my fishing pole hanging off the side of the fishing bridge this is back when you actually could fish off the bridge, now you get to take pictures of the fish off the bridge which is cool too.

This place makes for a nice drive with amazing views and great photo opportunities.  I love red rocks. Look to your right and look to your left  and up and and all around. Stop at the overlooks and absorb the beauty of this monument.   The rangers at the Visitor Center were also friendly.

I grew up going to Lagoon Park as a teenager and as a young adult and every so often I go with friends to reminisce about the old times we used to have at lagoon it's always been clean the staff is always been Pleasant and I've never been concerned about the safety of the rides.

Such a relaxing and beautiful natural environment . Lots of picnic tables with shade trees and areas for camping.  Don't lose heart as you travel the narrow, winding paved road several miles through seemingly endless open country.  The scenery is absolutely gorgeous!

Beautiful scenery abounds. An excellent place for photos or to just meander and enjoy the beauty.  Visit with family, children, adults or alone...you will have a great time in any situation. I have been there at all times of year and I loved each and every time.

I've been in this building several times over the past twenty years.  This is a beautiful place for artistic enjoyment of all kinds! There is a great staff to answer all questions.  Their gift shop was small but held many treasures by local artists.

This is such a beautiful park!  There are lots of picnic area and biking/walking trails go explore. This place is great for walking at all times of year and watching the ducks, birds and wildlife. A good place to walk the dogs and take photographs.

When you're traveling through Yellowstone National Park you do need to stop at the Lewis Falls pull off, get out of your car grab your camera and walk up The Path a little bit and you're going to get some fantastic pictures of the Lewis Falls.

Beautiful area adjacent to Ogden. Canoes to rent, great camping, lots of cool events. Right behind the fort is the River walk which extends in both directions and is a fun place to walk or hike.  The dog park area is really great.

This review is for the Grill. I ordered a Pizza and a Salad, both were great. The view of the surrounding area is fantastic. This is at the Terra Blanca Winery, so there is no signage indicating that there is a restaurant.
The Grotto picnic area has a great spot to stop and have a bite to eat plus it is also the beginning of the trailhead area and this area of the Zion's National Park.
The Golden Spike National monument area is a really interesting place to Learn a little bit more about Utah's history.

With a name like "Jungle Gardens" I didn't have a lot of expectations, but I was totally wowed by this park created by Edward Avery McIlhenny. You can walk or drive it, but is would be a very long walk. The breadth and depth of flora and fauna was amazing to see. McIlhenny had deep passions for certain plants. He favorite was Camellias and collected them from around the world. Azaleas were also a passion. He helped the government research varieties of bamboo and many still exist in the park. Live Oaks are plentiful and magnificent. His passion for Egrets, cultivated on his first Arctic expedition, led him to create a have for them. Perhaps saving the specie. BTW keep an eye out for their alligator and stop in the gift shop before you leave. That's the location of the only restrooms in the park.
