This unpretentious looking house serves up a fabulous tour. The tour guides know an incredible about about John Marshall and his time here from the 1780's until his death.  At least half of the objects in the home are original to the family and the house.  It is amazing to be so up close to the very items that this famous family lived in day and night. I would heartily recommend this tour if you have any history in our country, the constitution or the Supreme Court. Marshall's rulings changed the way the Supreme Court worked and established it as an equal third branch of the government.

I visited because I have an ancestor buried here. We stayed and visited again because of it's beauty and serenity. No. 3 is much quieter, safer and better kept than some of the other cemeteries you can visit in NOLA. There is an office with minimal staff. No bathroom. They do not have a flyer of the many famous people buried here, like Leyah Chase, Queen of Creole Cuisine and her husband Dooky Chase. So you'll have to discover them on your own. And no, Paul Prudhomme is not buried here, despite the rumor. There are some Prudhomme's buried here, but not him.

This museum is a little gem - if you can find it. You have to pass through guardhouse security right off the road to get it, but it is sure worth it. The museum was completely renovated after Hurricane Katrina and is more exhibits are being added. They do a tremendous job in two areas. First is the   Louisiana National Guard's response to Katrina and second the LNG's involvement in each war time effort of our country. The men and women of the National Guard are truly unsung heroes. Thank you for your service.

I had the pleasure of spending three days in the Martin F Schmidt Research Library researching the genealogy of my family. Since the stacks were closed due to COVID-19, the library relied on running the desired books to the researchers. The system worked well and I discovered a surprising amount of new information about my ancestors. They also practice Safe Library Practices by wiping down all surfaces and placing all books into a multi-day quarantine.

We arranged for a private one-hour tour with Royal Carriages. We had Lori and her mule Lagniappe. Both were spectacular. We wanted a history oriented tour and Lori filled the bill. We learned so much about the various cultures that have ruled and lived in New Orleans and what they brought to the area. She was extremely knowledgeable about the building styles, major fires and how the living situation evolved over time. We loved the tour and our guides.

We almost passed the site due to it's unpretentious entrance; so glad we didn't. This site is low-key, but does a wonderful job of telling the story of two of Louisiana's favorite sons, White the Governor and his son White the US Supreme Court Chief Justice. They also do a wonderful job of of explaining White's sugar cane operation. Fascinating stories.  And don't mist the magnificent 400 - 450 year old live oak trees around the house.

While they've done a very good job or telling LBJ's story, the museum is tired looking.  You can tell it's been up for a long time and needs modernization. I was a teenager when LBJ was president so I wasn't glued to politics, so it was very helpful to see his accomplishments.  They also do a nice job of reviewing Lady Bird's accomplishments as well. Caution the Library is hard to find behind the administration buildings.
likes: Coverage of both LBJ and Lady Bird

reviews_attraction.text: A great spot for the family. Take a break from skiing and do some tubing. Tickets for tubing are timed by the hour to limit crowds. They have a large lodge area with a small snack bar for warming up. If you are into tubing, one tip is to buy a hour of tubing, then rest in the lodge, and do another hour of tubing. Make reservations online to avoid having to wait when you arrive.   Great fun an exercise for all.

Nice botanical garden, but I wouldn't go gaga over it. Areas include a large children's Storyland, lovely statue garden near the entrance, greenhouse with a living fossils exhibit (w/prehistoric plants, and a tropical rain forest. Lovely garden paths. And a certified Monarch butterfly feeding station. No senior discounts. They do have a nice gift shop just off the entrance. Ample parking on the street.

An amazing museum! Didn't know it existed until we arrived in Ft Pierce, then had to go. Spent most of a day here and were wowed. Their exhibits, with they type of Seal memorabilia and stories you would expect were fantastic. Their collection of vehicles makes it real. Their Memorial Wall is deeply moving and beautifully done. We owe so much to the brave and selfless few who become Seals.

We visited in the winter and much of where we wanted to hike was flooded.  That said it was beautiful and we could see it would be a lovely hiking part to visit again.  One surprise to us was hearing a wild boar grunting in the brush.  Needless to say, we stepped a little more quickly after that. Staff at the visitor's center was wonderful explaining all of our permit and camping options.

This park was purchased by the state when the owners wanted out. Spacious sites with reasonable privacy. Good amount of trees for shade. Nicely landscaped and maintained by camp hosts. Great hiking and biking trails right within and from campground, not to mention the beach. And if you don't want to walk, there is a tram that will take you down to the beach as well.

What a great bonus for Kerrville. This concrete trail is very well maintained. You can access it from multiple locations along the Guadalupe River in downtown Kerrville all are good.  The trail runs on both sides of the Guadalupe. Good signage for the areas you're going through.  Look for signs of the heavy flooding that can happen along the Guadalupe.

This is a little known but fabulous museum. Gliders played an important role in WWII and they have done an outstanding job of laying out the timeline and role played. The exhibits are fantastic, and don't miss the short move.  Them museum has one of the remaining glider on display. Great for all ages.

After visiting a good number of Presidential libraries, this is second only to President Reagan.  You have full access to the Oval Office.  The timeline of his presidency especially the events of 9/11 are deeply moving.  His daughters have done a wonderful and fun exhibit.  This is a must.

Outstanding location.  Having a volunteer give background on the chapel is well worth it.  The museum does an excellent job of of interpreting the school and Robert E. Lee.  Highly recommend a stop here. A good place to learn about the links between George Washington and the Lee family.

We visited here while camping in the area.  Even though it was early in the season our granddaughters had a blast running in the sand and searching  for special rocks. Beach was nice and clean, easy to sit down and watch freighters go by.  Good family destination.

We thought an hour or so here would be fun, instead we spent half a day and it was worth every minute of it.  Being from the mid-west we had no clue about the history of ranching, now we do.  They've done an amazing job of telling the story of western ranching.

This is a lovely nature center with boardwalk trails, well-marked greenery, lovely ponds with many turtles. Excellent for site seeing, casual walks for anyone. Children will squeal with delight at the many turtles and fish in the ponds.
Great facility. Their PT boat exhibition is fantastic. Its moving to see the actual atomic bomb that was built, but not used over Japan. Well worth taking the time to go through it slowly.
Very well done.  Exceptional presentation of his life and time in office.  Brings the family in. Important to see the rose garden and pavilion and their cemetery.
As disgusting as the concept of chewed gum stuck on walls is, you still have the urge to go see it. Do go, it's worth it. Just don't touch anything.
We've taken our granddaughters here many times and always have hours of great fun and joy.  Be careful around the bubble room, it's often slippery.
OK, how much can you learn about windmills?  ALOT.  This museum was just fascinating.  People of every age will love it.

It's a statue... But that's it, a statue in front of a courthouse..... Parking can be an issue especially during the week during court....and really all there is a statue nothing else downtown at this time but the way things are growing,  that will change but not in the near future.... If you like looking at singles statues then it's worth the stop.

Been to many aquariums...... And outside of SeaWorld this one is very nice..... It's compact..... But has a little bit of all the sea creatures..... And the location is actually great because you can walk out and then go downtown Gatlinburg we're all the shops and other activities take place....... It's worth a visit.

Most cities have a decent park....I rated this one a five...because you have a walking path, waterfall, a great view from the gold sphere when taking an elevator to the observation deck(free)....and your a little walk away from market square where you can have your choice of eatery options or an ice cream...

For Florida this is a pretty cool place... Your hike is about two and a half miles but you could go 4... It is a loop so that's cool and there's plenty of trees and privacy... There's no unique water or Cove type areas...but it's a nice level hike wide path plenty of room and it's easy to get to.

Was a very nice nature hike... multiple trails, all flat and wide...they have a large boardwalk into the marsh, you will see birds, squirrels, wide variety of plants, majestic trees, such as Oaks...their is a small lake to fish, horses to ride....pack a lunch, it's worth it!

Very nice place lotta options and things to see... From nice hikes to water to kayak... However I recommend visiting off-season... Because everybody knows about this... It gets extremely busy... Won't have a nice nature unless you like a lot of folks on the trail.

Flippin home run... If you like waterfalls this has the most volume of water outside of Niagara falls in New York..... Just minutes from downtown Cookeville Tennessee this multi-level waterfall.... Is stunning... It's only a short walk to see such great beauty..

5 stars, because it does have the best foilage canopies for hiking in hot sunny days! The shaded hikes are great..along the streams.... waterfalls are average, but with all the trees and shaded canapy trails...this place is a home run.... really cool!

It's nice little stop it's quiet on the top not much for views but there's a nice little Trail that's a mile to walk and maybe have lunch... they do have a pavilion....... You can go camping there if you like.... And you do have a view of the dam....

I was thrown off with the $20 charge....HOWEVER....worth it....if you not only walk the 1 mile boardwalk(4 star)....but as a couple or with your children...check out the little caverns, the crevices.....it's a neat worthy experience......
Good views of the gorge the waterfalls the rocks of pools of water.... however, their are over a 1000 steps to climb....bring a sandwich, a bottle of water and a good pair of legs!   WORTH IT!
The whole area is fantastic....all within 20 minutes....cane falls(here), falls Creek falls around the corner.... swinging bridge, rock formations, cabin,villla and boat rentals...
Has everything but waterfalls...big open spaces, curvy treelined trails and roads,  nice lake to boat...they have rental paddle boats, creeks and little nature nooks all over
Neat, history in view....you can look and imagine what it was like back during the war...it makes you pause and reflect ones life and how our country and history was shaped!
Is a nice walk, easy... It does have rocks on the path so you may trip if you're not watching..... Going through the woods not a lot of scenery but we still worthy to go...
Hold on!!! You want a memorable day? Get on, it's safe, but bring an extra pair of shorts just in case.......I'm kidding, you will be glad you went on it.
Good 3 mile hike.....close to the road but.....it has ups/ downs, woods...a little water... worth it....we were surprised by the different terrian
Nice hike, easy to moderate....can see the  top of falls a short distance from your vehicle.... bottom of falls....is a  1/2 mile trek down.
Alot of private areas.... Plenty of water foul....For a southern nature Park area it has good views and adequate nature stops and trails.
We like hiking and this place definitely is worthy of a stop... The views are good bring an extra pair of legs for a good stretch walk...
Panaramic view that is excellent with the river down below...plenty of trails and views...a great stop if you want to see far vistas.
Great place to hike, see great views and nature.....going through this part of the country, then this place is a must see!
Unique building, great open field park to walk, kick a ball or fly a drone....the large Greek structure is impressive!
Very nice view and open area....the scenic depth is one of the best.... plenty of parking and walk around area
It's a nice place to stop I love the nature I love the little hike I love the Falls you'll enjoy it too

It's not about "seeing fish" (to those who say just rent a mask and fins). It's about learning about the ocean and seeing the many animals that aren't 10 feet from shore. Yeah, you can see 20 foot tiger sharks in the aquarium or in the ocean, but I feel a lot safer seeing them at the ocean center. And there's no guarantee you're going to see sharks or eels or octopus or the hundreds of other animals the ocean center has on display UNLESS you go to the ocean center. the ocean is a huge place and there's no signs to read underwater that tell you about everything you'll see. I love the ocean center.

This place, long ago, was once a dairy farm. In fact, you can see where the old dairy used to be before it was burned down. Now it's a coastal refuge for engangered animals. It's free to visit any time. You just have to have a car with some clearance to get to the parking area in front of the beach (or walk from the other beach's parking area). Once you're in, it's a quiet, green, costal loop trail. Very nice. Also, at the far end, you can keep going along the beach and across Waihee stream.  Eventually I turned around, but the little trail seemed to go on forever.

When friends from off-island come to visit Maui, and we have plans to run around in Lahaina, I'll usually pick up lunch somewhere close by and we'll come here and eat it at the Banyan tree. It's a very nice, friendly place to sit down and relax in the shade. I still remember the days before all the shops, when children could run around and climb the tree. Much has changed, but the banyan tree itself is still the same awesome tree. It's also fun to take 5 or 10 minutes to check out the historical sites that surround the tree courtyard.

I really like this beach. it's very shallow and you can walk out pretty far. the waves are always small so it's great for children. You can also go back by the pier and keep walking thru the grass to get a close look at the bird sanctuary as well as the birthplace of Queen Kaahumanu, for which there is a landmark that has been erected. If you feel like breaking the rules, you can also jump off the pier, but just be careful and don't get caught doing it. There are showers here, by the way, and a food/snack establishment.

This was a great haunted museum. There were a lot of rooms to look thru and plenty of things to see. My favorite part was the cabinet in the hallway with the petrified chihuahua. Very odd!

Pros: LOTS to see, friendly staff, water misters outside to keep you cool, scary at some parts, fascinating history of the house

Cons: LONG wait to get in, expensive even for locals, rushed thru the tour due to the necessity of moving people through the house, insultingly expensive gift shop, no photos allowed in tour

I camp in the crater at least every other year. I love Haleakala. It's the most beautiful thing to see on Maui. The best thing about it is that what most people see is just the top, but the real beauty is INSIDE. 10 miles inside. Meaning there's rarely any tourists. Just last year I went with my grandfather to Haleakala to watch the sunset. it's way better than sunrise. No need to get up early or struggle with parking.

Short, beautiful hike through the woods. This one is great for kids, because it's not very technical. Also good now during coronavirus because the walking trail is often wide and you don't have to get too close to people. There's a waterfall and spring to see if you want to go the extra distance, but it requires for vertical hiking, so bri g water and a snack if that's your plan. You'll want the extra energy.
dislikes: Vertical hiking required for some features

reviews_attraction.text: I mostly only come to sunset park to take my dog to the off leash dog park. It's a nice spot, but can sometimes be crowded. The dogs are separated by size, so there's no fear of having my little one trampled by a bigger dog. Most people keep to themselves, but some people are happy to socialize, we could all take lessons from our dogs though on how to be more friendly to strangers though. lol

I absolutely loved coming here. It's basically an interactive museum! Most machines are 50 cents per play, but some older ones are only 25 cents, while the really fancy ones are 75 cents. Aside from pinball, they also have other popular arcade games such as hockey, baseball, skiball, and some classics such as Pac-Man and Space invaders. I spent over an hour here for only $2. I will be back!

A Beautiful spot. Sometimes it's crowded, sometimes it's empty. You just have to get lucky. The trail, thankfully, is easy to find and easy to climb down. I like it best when the surf is huge. it's really fun to sit in the pool while the ocean is exploding on the rocky cliff, spraying the tidepool. It's completely safe.

There's a water fountain here that kids can play in, a lake, a little boardwalk, and lots of grass. Parking here is free as long as there's no special events going on nearby. I usually bring my dog and walk over to the river where some other dogs are also playing around in an off-leash area.

This place is sometimes referred to as "cardiac hill". It's talking about the hike back up and out, not the way in. It's brutal, especially when it's been raining, but that's when the waterfall is going, so it's so worth it. Great hike, great swim, great jumps, great photos. Bring your dog.

It's pretty far out of the way, and I have definitely been to bigger better waterparks elsewhere, but for a half day of cheap fun, it's a good place to go. Last time I came here I had a blast. I recommend buying your tickets online. It can be cheaper, and you skip the line at the entrance.

This is more of a walk and less of a hike. But the views are stunning and sometimes you'll see animals (such as goats). It's about 8 miles roundtrip walk to the hoover dam and back, so make sure you start early because they close the gate at sunset and you don't want to get stuck inside!

Hali'imaile is such a tiny village, so to have their own park is a treat. It's not much more than a grassy field, but there is a basketball and tennis court as well. I think the big building in thr back is a gym, but I couldn't see an easy way in. Gotta do some research and find out.

I love taking my wife and dog to the park here. It's a good place to walk the dog and give her some exercise. There's some shady benches to enjoy a packed lunch too. I often see kids playing on the play set. I wish I had that near me as a kid. Looks like they're always having fun.

I've been coming here since I was a baby. I really enjoy swimming in the stream on hot summer days. Someday I hope to do the hike from Olowalu Valley to Iao. There's lots to explore aside from the normal boring paved walking path.

This hike is a really beautiful place. You can actually walk up REALLY FAR into the jungle here, and find some pools and some ridges and some irrigation canals. There's also a lot of native birds to listen to and see in the trees.
Great boat ramp for the Kihei area. Has room to launch multiple boats at once. There are also wash stations for washing your boat (bring your own hose, soap, etc). There's bathrooms here as well.
Lots to do here. basketball, baseball, walk in Pittman wash, play with your dog... There's always enough parking, and it's close to lots of food and snacks at the corner of Pecos and Windmill.
I took my now fiance here for one of our first dates over 8 years ago. Such a pretty place. I've also seen people get married here, I'm pretty sure. Or at least were taking wedding photos.
I love coming here and catching waves. Hookup is world famous for surfing. There are also a lot of turtles in the water. Good facilities as well, and friendly lifeguards.
This park has beautiful views of Central Maui. I love taking my wife and son here all the time. The hills are great for cardboard sledding, too.
Did a good 5 mile in and out hike up the ridge on the left of the bike track. Heard some birds, saw some trees. Was a good time. 🌱🌳🌿🍃🏃
such a beautiful place. waterfalls around every other turn, green trees as far as you can see. hundreds of hiking opportunities.

Lovely place to spend the day.  It took us about 2 hours, we did explore some of the side trails.  If you walked around the lake with few side trials you can do it much faster.  The drive in is very small, so do not miss it.  At first we thought that it was just a walkway.  The lot filled up on the 4th weekend, but I imagine that was one of the busier days.  They collect the fees right in the parking lot.

We walked the trails and side trials.  Great water and sculptor combinations.  Running water, great rocks, buildings and sculptors all combined into a great combination.  Many great trees, blooming and not) and blooming bushes.  The water lilies were in bloom right now, so it is a great time for a visit.

Good place to walk, but it is a great place to ride you bike.  The trail connects onto River road so you can ride it all the way up to Gaylordsville.   Great views of the river and many places to stop and look at the river.  You could at that point ride to bull bridge and continue up to Kent on the West side of the river.  One day maybe they will add the connector so you can do this without getting onto 7 ( I guess you could go back east on normal roads to come out at bull bridge and avoid 7 right now using normal roads).

A nice place.  You can use the picnic areas for free, but need to pay to access the trails down to the waterfalls.  These trails are the highlight of the trip and not to be missed.  They have several streams falling down the mountsides and forming many waterfalls.  We walked down one side and up the mountain then back to the starting area.  The whole way we have many points that we could stop and rest.  Plus, many great vista of the falls.  Many great views along your walk, so make sure your camera is fully charged.

I love this park.  I have visited it many times over the years and find something great every time.  I love the old building that is Washington's old headquarters.  The old covered bridge on the backside of the park.  It is a large park that you drive from location to location or ride if you brought your bikes.  Some places are overlooks others are stops with history.

Around every turn you look you will find someplace that you love.

A great hike.  The old railroad path is clear and a gentle walk, but when you hike up the hill toward the old donkey trail it gets a bit rough.  Near the Quarry Bridge back to the top of the dokey trial is about a mile and then 1 mile more back to the furnace area and the parking lot.  The parking lot fills up fast so best if you arrive before noon to find a good place on the weekend.  The old furnaces are great to see.

A great place to walk.  Paved trails and a nice dirt path along the river and rapids.

The entrance and exit are poorly marked on Google so be careful.  Plus, most people park out near still water drive off the old Lanesville Road, but you must enter that part of Lanesville Road from Still Water Rd since the bridge is closed to traffic.

Waterfall, nice swimming area near the bottom of the falls.   The water is cool, but nice on a hot day.   We went on a late june, weekend afternoon and it was not hard to get a place.  The water was still cold, but many people were swimming.   I imagine  August is much busier.   Great place, with easy parking later in the day.

At first we thought it seems small for the price, but start the walk and you will find it is a good size.  Not too big and not too small it really was a great size for getting out of the car and doing a great walk.  Nice views of the coast and waves.  Great flowers and trees.  Many great displays.

This is a great location that you can see the waterfall over the damn, walk a great section of the Appalachian Trail, see a Covered Bridge, a great section a rapids.   You can see so much here and they have a small parking lot to help you visit the spot.

Great string of falls down the hillside.  Mostly smaller drops, but quite a few over a large area.  Great walk down the hillside; you can take an easy walk along the main trail or a harder walk along the falls.   Better views close to the falls.

What a great location.  In the city and easy to walk path.   Great Waterfall in a great location.    We went on a June weekend and it was not crowded and found easy parking just right across the street from the historic area of the falls.

A great place to walk.  You can choose several locations along the roads and the main house.    Look over the maps and you can choose a few locations.  We loved the pond with the boardwalk around it.  Great fall colors and many birds.

A amazing beach and we timed so we could stay for sunset.  Wonderful place to watch the sun set.   The rocks and area has many sea-life in rocks and pools around the main rock.   Walk around and see what you can find.

Nice parking to see the beach and walk around the area.  A small pier to walk out on and look around.   We stopped for an hour to walk and rest while we drove on 101.  Some small shopping and takeouts.

This place was nicer than i expect from driving by many times.  Great lake views and some nice spots for swimming and fishing.   Room to walk around, plus a few trails that I have not checked out yet.
These are good trails during wet weather.   The southern section of the trail is cleared before the northern section so better place during winter.   The trail is paved so easy to walk after a rain.
A nice walk, good trails.  The rocks were beautiful and not too hard to reach.   Entering the cave requires a little balance, but not a great amount.     Most people should be able to reach it.
Nice place to stop and see the falls.  We saw the main falls.  Did not see other trails.  Plus, not much markings on where to go or to see.   The falls are tall and very nice.
I  loved this place I encourage everyone to visit and see a bit of history.  You can walk around and see some gardens; flowers and vegetables.  The house is amazing.
We loved this place large fort nicely redone.  Marching and guards; great entertainment.   The gardens close to the forts were also very good to walk around.
Nice waterfall great place to stop if you are staying in Hilo, but not worth a long drive to see.  We like it, but wish there was more to see in the area.
Great place to hike.  Good trails and even a bird watching stand.   You can choose different trails to match the distance you want.
An important stop along the freedom trail.   We loved this old church.  It has been well maintained and contains a lot of history.
A great view, if you do not have much time for the walk down into the valley you can stop here.  We loved the overlook.
This place is great!!!!   Nice walk, good views always something new to see.   You can not go wrong walking here.

This area has recently change the structure of the landscape. A new dike has been built and several old ones are removed so Leque Island is mostly flooded now at high tide. This change is to help young Salmon have a place to grow and get bigger before heading to sea. They will now be in saltwater but protected from predators in the ocean until they get larger.

This is a strenuous hike to the top but the views of Mount Rainier are spectacular. Get there early on the weekends because parking fills up quickly. Also remember this area gets a lot of fog so the views can suck lots of days but still a nice hike.

My plans are to head there this summer when the gate is open along  the forest road which will allow you to drive up close for minimal hiking. The views of Mount Rainier from this old fire lookout area spectacular.

A beautiful falls but my suggestion for best pictures is to come on a weekday and after 2:00 pm so the sun is shinning on the falls. If you come before then the sun is in your face and the falls is in a shadow.

Have hiked here several times climbing all the way up to the PCT Trail. Best time to hike is first two weeks of October during the Larch Madness. The beauty of all the Larch Trees be changing is spectacular.
Love this place. Hiked the Heather/Maple Loop Pass Trail. It's 8.2 mile loop trail with spectacular views especially in Fall before the first big snow falls. It's a must for all hikers.
Went to see the fireworks. They were nice. This is a city park so it was nice for the cities folks but I am not a fan of cities so I was glad to leave and I am not likely to come back.
Short but step hike the first mile then the last three quarters of the way it smoothed out. The views from the top on Lummi Island looking out over the San Juan Islands was fantastic.
Major changes to the landscape. The island is mostly flooded at high tide and has creating small pool areas to help young Salmon to thrive in saltwater as they get larger.
Nice little park but lake is contaminated with a toxic algae bloom and off limits to all humans and animals. Don't let your animals or kids get in or touch the lake.
Loved the gardens but I went here when temperatures we're reaching triple digits so be aware of Sumner months when it can get very hot. All and all a nice garden.
Beautiful trails to hike on the southend if Whidbey Island. Everytime I have hiked there it's been very quiet and I was always alone except for lots of wildlife.
A small hike up hill to a nice little falls that does not have real good views but if you cone at night if and when they turn on the lights it's nice to see.
Very small park that is not taken care of. Kind of run down for such a small park. Nice to park car here to launch kayak and see views of Guemes Island.
There is no other spot in Washington State as beautiful as this spot from a major highway pull off. It is a must for everyone to see once in their life
Love the local park. Great views, camping and hiking. Just a nice local place to go to get out of the house. Love the views of the San Juan Islands.
By far the most spectacular falls to see on the east side of the Olympics especially in spring with the least amount of work getting there.
Nice deep forested park but due to root rot on trees camping is suspended in the park. Nice trails in the forest just below Sauk Mountain.
The views at the top are well worth the climb. If you like the outdoors and hiking you will live this place. I have hiked here ten times.
This is a beautiful place for a short hike on the beach. Up here there's not a whole lot of sand but still worth it just for the views.
One of my favorite local hikes. Beautiful views of inner Puget Sound and surrounding islands. Trails in good shape and never crowded.
This is a nice little State Park that borders on the west by Puget Sound. A nice place for a walk on the beach or with your pet.
Very nice state park. Very clean, camping spots are plenty and we'll organized. Has a large beach section to hike on.
Always wanted to come here and finally did. Beautiful views but lit of traffic but still worth seeing at least once.
My favorite local hike to get me out of the house in Winter. Beautiful views from the beach of Mount Baker.

It was not so nice experience for me and my kids. First of all its takes 2 hours to get there by public transportation from Brooklyn. Second ground administration is $15 per adult (NYC resident) which doesn't include tram & exhibitions.  And without tram you can see something interesting. They have free admission on Wednesdays but the same problem - you can get a tram for additional prace. If you want you supposed to pay full admission, which is $25 per adult. But it's good place for nice and peaceful walking.

Nice experience even heat waves and Covid restrictions can't push it down.
It's great to mix up aquarium and Zoo together.
Overall it's not big place but very cozy. They have a lot of big spices like giraffes, elephants, tigers, gorillas and even polar bear!
In the aquarium they have small shark exibitions.
Sad that Jumbo restaurant was closed and your can just order online and pick up.
Take a lot of water or be ready to buy $4 bottle and enjoy!

Very cozy place. You can spend 1-2 hours and enjoy to be a part of amazing bird world. They have different exebitions with live birds - tropical world, rainforest, tiny birds and so on. Resample prices - $17 per adults and very well maintained place. They  practicing social distance and have a lot of sanitizer stations.
I would definitely recommend this place to visit specially with kids.

It's awesome place. Meanwhile the museum is under renovation but trails are open. It's kingdom of the birds in the middle of rush downtown Fairfield Life and busy roads. But it's really great and can visit for free. But donation is appreciated. I will definitely recommend for everybody specially for family with small children.

Tiny museum which requires a house tour. A lot of history but too little information about Walt. They have parking lot but it can be closed for no explanation. My expectations were not meeting. Not good for visiting if they host same events.

Really great place to visit. Beautiful river shore walking and a lot of space for relaxing.
Even in that covid time this place is great.
A lot of trails still closed but Breezy Island is open now and this is stunning place.

Good small spot specially for the kids. Closed to the train station and downtown Greenwich. It's a beautiful playground and park just on opposite side of the road.
And just keep in mind - Tuesdays are free admissions.))

Good place for a long walking or bike riding.   But if you don't want to do both this place is probably isn't yours.)) You supposed to bring food with yourself - no food in the park or place close to the park.

Must to see in the city. You can walk inside of battery completely free and enjoy connection between historical and modern times.
If you wish to visit Statue of Liberty don't forget to buy tickets here..

Small & cozy Zoo.  Animals trail is great,  even in hot weather you will be fell not bad because a lot of trees.
Price of the tickets are very appreciated - $10 for adults and $6 (or $7) for kids.
Good place for refreshing. Small but cozy. You supposed to be local to enjoy this place completely but if you come by Metro North train from NYC out of beach season you can enjoy relaxing here.
This is an amazing place with a lot activities for entire family - a beautiful lake with a boat rental station, very nice playground, an interesting zoo and many more. ;)
Really great place and so closed to NYC. The falls great. And walking trails are good enough. They have a lot of parking lots and picnic tables as well. Nice experience.
Great museum - very well maintained and on the top of hill which has breath break view. 4 stars just because I am not a fun of war museum even very special ones.
Not bad place - good for children but the problem is - too close an elevated D train line does too much noisy... But the biggest issue is that no restroom here.
Good place for relaxing, picning and walking. A lot parking lot and picnic tables. You can enjoy nature and keep social distance at the same time.
Really great park. They have a pool, kids summer meals, two stages playgrounds & fitness corner. Very clean, a lot of trees & flowers.
It's a really great place to walk and refresh your mind. It feels like you are in wildwood but still you are around a beautiful town.
It's a public park and you can enter for free but if you want to visit Cheese garden and pound your supposed to pay $5 per person.
It's so funny to see so small park which is called Central Park, especially if you are compared  to Central Park in NYC. ;)))
It was awesome! So beautiful pass and lake, and birds! I will definitely come back again. Really easy to get there by LIRR.
Great place to go. It has nice barbecue area and clean restrooms as well. The boardwalk is very nice and ocean looks great.
Impressive view from tram. Just use your Metro card & you can get free ride if you used your card in the subway.
Small but cozy beach, water is shallow & and not clean enough. But there are a lot trees and tables for picnic.
Beautiful grounds. Very nice to spend an hour or few to enjoy beauty of nature in combine with man made art.

Can’t say anything even close to bad about this place. It is a gem. Amazing staff so knowledgeable and wants you to enjoy and experience all of the stuff they have to show and know. One of the best museums in the state. Really come out to check it out. You will not be disappointed.

This museum is outstanding. great information stories and experiences in railroading. You get a joint ticket for the memorial railroaders museum and make sure to check out the turn table and wheel house there. Check for the train schedule seeing that is amazing.

Great little museum of the path. Great information and story about the labor movement. It’s an amazing place to check out in the area. Totally worth every minute. The tour guide was amazing women that made and gave the place so much life and importance.

Really cool national park. Shows a often overlooked and important means of transportation west in early America. The preservation and history at the site is outstanding. Really worth a visit especially on a nice day the scenery is great.

It’s a really cool Historic Site to check out. The tour is really informative. The interpretation center has great information and a fantastic gift shop to grab a text to read. Beautiful site worth all the time to enjoy you could spare.

Great museum and grounds to see. It’s a ton of space outside to enjoy even when it’s cold. The US life saving exhibit is great and the small craft building has a ton of boats and information. Staff is amazing. Totally worth a visit.

Great small zoo that has enjoyed yuh to see and enjoy that it is a must see in Springfield. The staff was so nice and inviting. The path was really easy to follow and a really good morning or afternoon especially for kids.

It’s such a great place. So interactive and a huge amount of information and clips to go back into Comedy. It is continuously growing and is worth every penny and time to visit. It is such a great experience.
Howard have a fantastic tour. Really knowledgeable and friendly. Made the experience so much better. A lot of stuff to see but really close together and definitely worth every penny and all the time.
It’s an outstanding living history house that is worth a trip and the tour guides are amazing. Steve was so informative and engaging. It’s outlook is some of the best views in the Adirondacks.
This state park is truly a hidden gem. The walls and the bird preserve is amazing. The fly fishing school and activities look fantastic. Great afternoon to enjoy the outdoors.
A great museum that really shows off one of America’s best artists. It is on great beautiful property and highlights all the things that are amazing about Rockwell’s art.
It has a ton of information on the War of 1812 and Lake Erie maritime history. The video is great to start. Make sure to ask the staff to check out the boats. Loved it.
An amazing set of museums and worth an entire day to see. The art museums are great. Dr. Suess exhibit and garden are outstanding and the History museum is fantastic.
Outstanding lighthouse, life saving station site and national seashore. The staff is amazing. It is a gem to visit. The history beauty and architecture is worth it.
To bad about the no stadium seats but got to see the Worcester Bravehearts. It was great. Loved the love of the game and dedication to the live sports and fans.
It’s an underrated site that is beautiful and has tons to see. The tour is great especially Joan. Love the artifacts and walking paths. Video is great to start.
Really great small museum and animal spot. Awesome for kids. Great exhibits for the history and environment that is covered. Highly suggest as a quick stop.
Outstanding place for a great experience. Great exhibits with a great staff. Well worth the time and effort. Awesome for kids and adults.
Great views and a nice breakdown of the battle on the plaques. The monument on the hill is really cool and the campsites all look great.
It was a great visitor center in Boston center. Then taking the tow path is a great trail. Heading up to Brandywine falls is a must.
This was a true hidden gem. Outstanding exhibits and so much history and legacy of motorcycles. It’s a great visit. It’s also huge.
Great park. Trails are nice and a great place to get some peace from the hustle and bustle. Carousel is a must if it’s open.
Really nice place with great staff. Has the ability to do more but needs more funding. Is a great place check it out.
It is the Grand Canyon of the East and worth every penny and the time for the entire visit. It’s amazing.

This is a great museum that’s packed with information. The lower floors have exhibits from the slavery era to the civil right movement era and the upper floors talk about more contemporary topics such as music and art. The exhibitions are very dense, there’s a lot of information to absorb so take your time to explore. There are a lot of visitors in the museum so it can get quite packed, it’d recommend booking an early ticket to enter to escape the crowds. Everything is wheelchair accessible.
Ticket information: I visited in May and had to book my tickets in February, so make sure you plan ahead of time! I had some trouble with ordering my tickets because the online service froze when the sale started. I refreshed for 30 minutes and suddenly was able to get tickets, so just be prepared for a non-smooth sale. Trying to get in without any tickets is very difficult, there’s a line that wraps around the building for walk-ins.

I went on a successful whale watch with this company, they took us 2.5 hours out to Canadian waters to see whales and we did! The guide explained everything very well and pointed out wildlife. A part of your ticket fee goes go being able to take a researcher on board, which is really cool and important. Do think ahead about where you want to sit, if you’re outside you’ll have a great view but YOU WILL BE COLD. I sat outside and was wearing a t-shirt, 2 sweaters, a windjacket and a blanket and I was still freezing. So beware! Sitting inside means you’ll be warm but the view won’t be as good. Just make sure you’re seated where you wanna be at the start of the trip, the boat gets packed and after a while there’s no seating space inside anymore.

A must-do when you’re in Provincetown! The tower is not that hard to climb as there are walking ramps and not that many stairs. It’s doable with kids but not with strollers or wheelchairs. The views from the top are amazing, you have a wonderful 360 view! The museum is very interesting as well, take your time to walk through it. It costs $12 to enter as an adult, but if you park there you get one free ticket.
Also interesting to know is that the parking is free between 5PM and 9AM, so perfect for overnight parking in the otherwise expensive Provincetown.

I've taken the tour 3 times and I always see new parts of the building which is nice! The tour guides are very friendly and are happy to answer (reasonable) questions. Security is stringent but friendly. The appointment confirmation always says you have to be there an hour before your tour, but if you get there 40 minutes before you're totally fine too. And oh, it's usually quite cold in the building (even in the summer) so make sure you bring a sweater!

It’s great fun to visit the vessel, beautiful architecture in a beautiful spot.
The tickets are FREE but I think it’s best to order in advance. We were able to get a walk-up ticket but it was already in the late evening. So if you want to visit during the day, do plan ahead.
There is an elevator inside.
There are no restrooms in the structure itself, but there is a mall super closeby.

This is a unique museum, a must-see if you’re in Philly! It’s not exceptionally big but there’s a lot to see so make sure to reserve at least 1 hour for it. Kids seem to get freaked out so consider whether this is a good place to take them. Bags are not allowed in the museum, but there are lockers where you can store them in addition to a coat room.

This park is okay. The footprints are very impressive and you can make molds of dino teeth and footprints, which is a lot of fun for kids. The exhibitions are old though and some parts of it were out of order. It’s a good place to take your dinosaur crazy kids, but do warn them they won’t see any bones or anything, it’s just the footprints.

If you’re visiting DC and want to do an art museum, I would definitely recommend this one. It’s beautiful, both the collection and the building itself. They have a little bit of everything for everyone and honestly, you can just wander around for hours or just pay the museum a quick visit. It’s so worth it!

This is such a beautiful and spectacular place to visit, I definitely recommend it. Although it’s quite expensive ($28 for an adult), it’s definitely worth seeing. The tour takes about an hour and you walk a mile and a half from one spectacular sight to another. Not wheelchair accessible.

This is a beautiful park, I definitely recommend spending some time here if you enjoy nature! It has a lot of interesting plants, flowers and trees and it’s perfect to stroll around, do some hiking or just go for a picnic. Unfortunately it is quite far away from any public transportation.

This is a great museum for every train fan, they have a lot of authentic locomotives and train carts that are preserved wonderfully. The signs are very informative as well and the staff is happy to help. It is quite expensive though, $20 for an adults and not a lot of discounts.

I really enjoy coming here, it's good for a quick visit and you'll always discover new plants! They have a lot of unique flowers too, for example the corpse flower. During Christmas time they have really beautiful decorations too, definitely worth going!

Very interesting and impactful museum. You can only take tours but there are tours almost every 15 minutes. Most tours take about an hour, but keep in mind that it might take longer depending on the amount of questions. It’s $27 for an adult.

Beautiful hiking area, there’s a lot of trails with  great views. There is not a lot of parking though, so make sure to get there early or wait until someone leaves. You cannot park on the side of the road, many people get tickets!

It’s a great state park, perfect for hiking, running, walking your dog, swimming,... There’s a paved road you can walk on and also forest trails. There’s usually enough place to park and there are enough restrooms in the park.

The Renwick Gallery will always add some wonder to your day. You can find quirky art here that you will not find anywhere else. It’s good for a quick visit or a longer exploration and kids usually love it as well!

Very much worth the money ($16 for adults)! It’s a beautiful hike with a lot of variety in scenery. It’s family friendly but not pet friendly. During COVID-19, you need to book a time slot online in advance.
Definitely worth paying the $5 for. It’s a rather large area with some diverse ecosystems and a lot of wildlife. I walked around for about an hour and a half and saw many birds, squirrels and deer.
A great place to hike to and to visit. We received a lovely tour of the lighthouse which was very interesting. There’s not really a price to enter but they do appreciate small donations.
I saw the New York City Ballet here and it was amazing. The venue is beautiful, the stage is big, you have a good view from every seat so even the cheaper tickets are still great!
likes: Facilities & Services: Venue aesthetics, Stage size, Viewing quality

reviews_attraction.text: Definitely one of my favorite museums ever! Whether you’re a child or an adult, this is a fun and informative museum that you can roam for hours or just visit for half an hour.
If you’re visiting Plymouth, don’t make this your  main stop. Although it has a great historic value, it’s underwhelming and you can barely read the year on it.
This is a beautiful trail off the beaten path. Not too difficult at all! There’s a small parking lot but you can also park on the side of the street.
A good spot to stop during your hike or drive, the staff is very friendly. There’s no indoor seating which is unfortunate during rainy days.
I came in here to see the building, which is beautiful. You can walk in for free and roam around a bit without being reprimanded for it.

Salt Rock State Campground is a public recreation area that preserves one mile (1.6 km) of wooded riverfront along the Shetucket River in the town of Sprague, Connecticut.  The state park offers RV and tent camping sites, swimming pools, and river fishing. The state curtailed camping services in 2016, reinstating them in 2018. Facilities include tent and recreational vehicle (RV) sites, some of which have utilities. There are also restrooms, a dumping station, showers, and 2 in-ground swimming pools.There is a swim school (Bubbles to Butterflies) that uses the pools for swimming lessons from 10a.m. to 5p.m. during the week days. However, during this time campers are more than welcome to use the pools.  Reservations must be made at least 2 days in advance. 11 month reservation window. The maximum length of stay is fourteen consecutive days. If you have a 14 day reservation, all members of your camping party and your camping equipment must leave the park for 5 days before you can return. In an effort to protect Connecticut's forests from the introduction and spread of destructive insect pests - in particular the emerald ash borer and Asian long-horned beetle - the Connecticut Department of Energy and Environmental Protection is taking the following action:
Prohibiting the bringing of firewood into state of Connecticut campgrounds and state parks from other states. As an alternative, firewood can be either purchased at the camp stores within the state campgrounds or at local retail sellers of firewood.
The Department of Energy and Environmental Protection greatly appreciates the public's assistance in helping to protect the state's natural resources and apologizes for any inconvenience this initiative may cause.   One vehicle per site limit. Parking available for second vehicle in visitor lot.            Campers must bring their own equipment for recreational activities (horse shoes, swimming tubes, sport equipment, etc). Also, we do not provide each campsite with a grate/grill. Campers need to bring their own.
dislikes: Limited swimming pool access (due to swim school)
No provided recreational equipment or grills

reviews_attraction.text:
New section of the Canal. 11.17.18🍁The new section of Cheshire trail is great. We decide to visit today, after the first snow-day.
The mile-long section goes  from West Main Street to Cornwall Avenue to the Main Street.
🌲Along with foliage and a paved walking path, the trail  include a two-stall bathroom facility, a 12-car parking lot, a bike repair station with tools, and a water fountain. There is also  benches and small picnic tables scattered around the area. 🌲The new section also include three butterfly gardens. One of the gardens is dedicated to Michaela Petit, who was killed in the 2007 home invasion. 🌲Several local nonprofits and businesses, predominately the Cheshire West Community Butterfly Gardens organization, have come together to adopt the space. Volunteers will help maintain it in future years. 🍁

Beautiful view. 🌲Horse Guard State Park 🌲245 W Avon Rd, Avon, CT 06001🌲 Horse Guard State Park is listed as an undeveloped park, but work over the last few years has turned it into a park worth the stop.  It had remained relatively unchanged since its acquisition in 1964.  🌲Now thanks to local scouts and volunteers there is a small parking area with a legitimate trailhead.  The trail here is an out and back from the parking lot to the ridge overlook that’s about 2/3rds of a mile one way (though the sign at the trailhead says .41).  There is also a connector to Wyngate Drive that adds about a half mile, but isn’t worth exploring.🌲 The rocky climb to the ridge is a nice surprise and the overlook provides an expansive view west. 🌲History:Established as a park in 1964, it is named for the Governor’s Horse Guard.🌲

Located in Burlington, Connecticut, Sessions Woods Wildlife Management Area is a 700-acre tract of natural land set aside for wildlife that also serves to introduce visitors to wildlife and natural resources management through educational programs, demonstration sites, and self-guided hiking trails and displays.🌲Managed by the Connecticut Department of Energy & Environmental Protection (CT DEEP), facilities at Sessions Woods WMA include an education center with an exhibit area and a large meeting room, as well as interpretive trails, habitat management demonstration areas, and a backyard wildlife habitat area. 🌲The trails at Sessions Woods meet up with the Blue-Blazed Tunxis Trail, which winds from Bristol up to the Massachusetts line with a separate section running through Southington.🌲

Blackledge Falls

Located in East Glastonbury at the Hebron Town line, this 80 acre parcel of open space is largely wooded. It contains hiking trails, a pond and a streambelt.
Directions
Route 2 East to Exit 8 Hebron Avenue. Take a left an end of exit onto Hebron Avenue and go about 10 miles. Black Ledge Falls will be on your left (if you see the Hebron Town Line sign, you have gone too far).

Route 2 West to Exit 10. Take a right at end of exit ramp onto Manchester Road. Follow Manchester Road (about 3-4 miles) to the intersection with Hebron Avenue. Take a right at that stop light and go about 6 miles or so on Hebron Avenue. Black Ledge Falls will be on your left (if you see the Hebron Town Line sign, you have gone too far).

THE FALLS

Bailey's Ravine (sometimes called Ayers Gap or Ayers Falls) is a quiet but very special place. 🌲The main attraction, a 10-foot plunge, is preceded and followed by several smaller drops and waterslides. 🌲The falls here is pretty and the hemlock-surrounded ravine is rugged and secluded. While the main falls is the popular attraction, those seeking a more memorable experience can hike through the entire 0.5 mile ravine. 🌲A portion of the hike through the ravine involves actually walking through, not along the edge of, a tight gorge. Some would argue that the experience of hiking through the gorge is more rewarding than visiting the main falls itself.

Beautiful place to hike and explore.  🌲 Pachaug State Forest was established with a 1,011 acre land purchase from the Briggs Manufacturing Co. in Voluntown in 1928.  In 1933, the first year the Civilian Conservation Corps began, Camp Lonergan was established in the Forest. 🌲  As funding became available, the forest quickly grew, totaling 12,000 acres by 1937.  The actions of the Resettlement Administration, in 1937, acquired an additional 9,000 acres and leased the land to the state for forest production.  Eventually, this land was deeded to the state.

Beaitiful Hiking place. 🌲I love it! The parking area today was full. 🍁 I'm happy to see families and friends enjoying the outdoors. 🌲 West Rock Ridge State Park is a public recreation area located in New Haven, Hamden, and Woodbridge, Connecticut. The state park is named for the 400-to-700-foot trap rock West Rock Ridge, which is part of the Metacomet Ridge extending from Long Island Sound to the Vermont border. 🌲Love this place. A lot of hiking trails. 👣👣you can ride your bike🚴‍♀️🚴‍♂️ of the old road from the area gone by. 🍁

Beautiful place to walk.  Barn Island Wildlife Management Area consists of more than 1,000 acres and a pleasant mix of salt and freshwater marshes, hardwood forests, fields, and a boat launch. Moderate trails are suitable for hiking, dog walking, cross-country skiing, and snowshoeing. Hunting allowed in season. Bring your camera to take some scenic pics!

Open sunrise – sunset. A few parking spaces are available at the entrance to main loop trail. Otherwise there is large paved parking lot at the boat launch.

The North Haven Trail Association welcomes all recreational hikers and bird-watchers to take a leisurely stroll on the Tidal Marsh Trail, a short but extremely relaxing and educational walk along the Quinnipiac River. Starting high
above the river’s edge, with stunning views of Sleeping Giant, lower Hamden, and the river’s marshes, the trail turns left, meandering south through stands of different species of trees between the water and abandoned Cedar
Hill Rail Yard train tracks. I love this place.

Beautiful view🍁 Swimming, natural history displays, nature trails, picnic grove, bird sanctuary and an antique carousel are highlights of this 82-acre park on Long Island Sound. Season runs: April 1-November 1. Gates open 7 a.m.-sunset year round. Carousel, weekends & holidays noon-4 p.m. Parking fees: New Haven residents free/$20 CT vehicles/$30 out-of state-vehicles. Carousel rides: 50 cents. Pricing: Parking fees, carousel 50.Other Amenities: ADA Compliant, Bus Parking.🍁

Beautiful place to visit and walk around.  Saturday is our day to relax and enjoy nature.
Exposure to nature not only makes us feel better emotionally, it contributes to our physical wellbeing, reducing blood pressure, heart rate, muscle tension, and the production of stress hormones. 🍁🍂❣🌲👣👣🍁Being in nature, or even viewing scenes of nature, reduces stress, and and increases pleasant feelings.

Seven Fall, Bear Hill, and Mattabessett Trail is a 8.4 mile moderately trafficked loop trail located near Middletown, Connecticut that features beautiful wild flowers and is rated as difficult. 🌲The trail is primarily used for hiking, walking, nature trips, and birding and is best used from March until October.🌲 Dogs are also able to use this trail but must be kept on leash.🌲

This is a great place to visit. Peoples State Forest is a Connecticut state forest occupying 3,059 acres along the West Branch Farmington River opposite American Legion State Forest in the town of Barkhamsted. It is managed for forest products, wildlife habitat, and recreational uses that include hiking, hunting, fishing, and snowmobiling

Beautiful área for hiking. Naugatuck State Forest is a Connecticut state forest consisting of five separate blocks in the towns of Oxford, Beacon Falls, Naugatuck, Bethany, Cheshire, Hamden, Seymour, and Ansonia. The five blocks are the Mount Sanford, East, West, Quillinan Reservoir, and Great Hill blocks.

Easy hike and beautiful falls. Wadsworth Falls State Park, or simply Wadsworth Falls, is a public recreation and preserved natural area located on the Coginchaug River in the towns of Middletown and Middlefield, Connecticut. The state park's 285 acres offer trails, fishing, swimming, and picnicking

We had a fantastic walk. Amazing place to visit.  There is benches around if you need to take a break. Picnic table if you decide to bring a bite. And a little playground for the kids. A perfect family destination. I love it!

Dennis Hill State Park is a public recreation area located in the town of Norfolk, Connecticut, that was once the estate of Dr. Frederick Shepard Dennis. The state park offers hiking, picnicking, and scenic views.

Beautiful view 🌞The Soldiers' and Sailors' Monument is a war memorial located on the 366-foot summit of East Rock in New Haven, Connecticut. It is visible for miles from the surrounding area and Long Island Sound.
Norwich, Connecticut. Yantic Falls is a 0.3 mile lightly trafficked out and back trail located near Norwich, Connecticut that features a waterfall. ... Michael Fischer recorded Yantic Falls.
The Pine Knob Loop Trail is located in Housatonic Meadows State ... The trail is accessible from the state park's campground and group camping area via unmarked trails. Visited 121120
I love this place. We try to go there as often as possible.  There is a great picnic area, the playground close by is well maintained. Parking is near by, for residents only.
Perfect day for a walk. The air is fresh, some of the trees are changing color and the white trial was deliful to follow. I love it!
I love the beach. The sound of the water, the air, the sand, the people...it's all part of the great experience of the outdoors.
For evrybody to the park is closed. Please next time post anoncnent for people to know the place is closed

Had an amazing Sunset tour trip and I also did the northern circuit inbound and it was awesome the general manager of the Rhode Island Division Rachel also overheard my friend and I needing to get to the bus stop so they made sure we got there on time to make the bus by making sure one of the crew members gave us a ride in one of the crew cars that they use. The customer service at this place is awesome and they made us feel appreciated and provided great service and made sure we were safe on the tour I definitely would do the northern ramble again but go outbound since I did inbound this time. I also recommend the sunset tour for the southern circuit.

This Art Museum had more than I thought. Not only was it a museum it was a famous historic house as well where we got to see all of the rooms. I spent much more time there than I thought I would and I'm glad I did because I got to see everything the museum and the house have to offer. It just goes to show you that there are many things you can do out there at no cost or for donation if you choose.

This Cruise was an amazing Cruise. I wish we could do all 8 lakes in the chain but that's physically not possible so we did the best for including fourth Lake which was the biggest and the best. Looking at all the houses on the lake was amazing along with hotels as well. I hope when I go to Old Forge for the weekend I will get to do the cruise again.

Very good Museum and I enjoyed my time on the trolleys it gives me an excuse to go back there more often to ride the various types of trolleys that they operate. I just wish it was closer to my house so I can have more time there more than just a couple of hours because of the length of time it takes to get there To the museum.

This was a beautiful place to go walking in to take pictures of streams rivers creeks and the Hudson river. The temperature was also great for walking as well and to visit such a great place with such awesome views and open areas and being able to social distance with ease and learn about the history of the place as well.

I enjoyed my experience at this Museum and I enjoyed the video that they had and seeing all the old school train cars that they had. I also enjoyed my trolley ride to Kingston Point Park and my walk around that Park as well. I would love to go back to this Museum if they were able to get a newer trolley car to run.

I have walked down this block in this area many times and didn't know it even had a name to it the things you know by just looking at your history in Google maps based on places you have been in and didn't even know there was a history behind it or any historical references or purposes.

I enjoyed my rail Excursion and I look forward to doing the ones in Rhode Island but I have a feeling this one will be the better of the two. I also wish it was longer because there is more track to make the Excursion longer then what it is.

Overpriced for what you get it's one of those things that you do once and that's it it's mainly for tourist who haven't seen New York and don't know what the area is and looks like and all the attractions and historical landmarks.

I enjoyed the event that I attended at this pier this weekend and the same as last year and I look forward to making it a yearly tradition to go watch the AVP volleyball tournament when it is in New York City.
A very nice park that I never knew existed. I look forward to coming back here again in the future of a nice walk on A-day that has one lever and good walking conditions.
I always love stopping near and taking pictures of history I just wish that they opened up the walkway to go on to where the lighthouse stands at is located offshore
I enjoyed going to this park and seeing the statue and the flagpole and the memorial at the top of the climb. I also enjoyed the view from the top as well.
I enjoyed my visit to the State Park and was able to walk by the bay and the ocean and hopefully next time I'll be able to do a tour of the fort.
Loved going for this area and I love taking pictures of all the great views in viewing all the great views that came with going on this walk.
I enjoy go kart racing and I love racing on indoor tracks and I really enjoy my time at this race track and I wish I could go more often.
I enjoyed my time here at this Zoo and enjoy the activities that they have along with the sea lion feeding which is the highlight.
It was amazing to witness a piece of History. It is amazing what you learn just by going to a place and finding out what is there.
I really like the grounds the place and the house itself. I can't wait to go back to do the full tour and see the Full House.
This is a nice state park that I look forward to visiting in the summer when the weather is warm and everything can be used.
I love the fact that they had a vintage and a model train there and they preserved a part of the old Greenfield station.
I love coming here for a volleyball tournament but the tournament got bigger than the location and had to move.
I have not been to this park in a while but I always enjoy walking around this park and being by the fountain.
Very nice place to go to in the spring and summer time and maybe even fall depending on the temperature.
This was one of the better science centers that I have bed too and I really enjoyed my time here.

Amazing!  Come early to get tickets for the lower viewing area.  They cost $5 (cash only, exact change necessary, limit 70 people).  While you wait, walk over to the Alamo Springs Cafe for dinner.
The walk down the path to the lower viewing area is not for people unsure on their feet.  A volunteer will tell you everything you ever wanted to know about bats in general, Old Tunnel State Park history, Mexican free-tailed bats, and more.
As soon as the bats begin to emerge from the tunnel, he stepped aside and let the show commence.  We were there in mid-June (said to be the low point, population-wise).  He estimated half a million bats were there and it took about 7 minutes for them all to leave.
Don't miss this!

The Commonwealth Museum first landed on my radar around the time of the Big Dig.  I had heard that they had an exhibit on some of the items found when excavating.  Unfortunately, I never got there while that exhibit was being shown, but I assumed that they had a curator that changed out exhibits periodically.  Unfortunately, that isn't the case.  The exhibits that we saw seemed very static.  There was such a large amount of reading that I can't imagine anyone reading it all.  Perhaps the highlight was the historic documents in the furthest room.

Always a pleasure to stop here while we're out on a motorcycle ride.  On this day, we borrowed one of the picnic tables in the parking lot for our lunch and then wandered over the bridge to take a few photographs and check out the monuments for the ump-teenth time.  We found a large number of painters spread around painting mostly landscapes, but also one did a character study of the costumed minuteman stationed by the bridge.  We chatted with him a while before continuing on our ride.

We had a very interesting time here.  Don't underestimate the amount of time you might spend.  There are many exhibits and the costumed "reenactors" are happy to interact and answer questions.
There is still much of the fort that is in disrepair and off-limits to visitors.
Note to motorcyclists: the parking lot is not paved and can be a little tricky, especially when crowded.
Admission included a token to get through the gate leading to Mount Defiance.

We visited as part of Free Fun Friday.  What a pleasant surprise!  It isn't a large place and I had prepared myself for a huge crowd.  The way it is designed the crowd was spread out and seemed much smaller than it was.
There were a number of interesting animals.  My favorite was the elephants.  We spent a few minutes chatting with one of the keepers and learned quite a bit.
There are a good number of tables around to have your picnic lunch.

Many of the pieces on display were made by relatively local artists.  Many of the subjects are of local interest (local buildings, etc) as well.  Many art museums I've visited become exhausting after a few hours.  Fitchburg Art Museum is nicely sized and kept my interest throughout.  The docents with whom we interacted were both friendly and knowledgeable.  Tucked back where it is, it can be easily overlooked.

Wow!  We've visited a lot of automobile museums, but this one is something special.  Not only did they have a lot of things that I've never seen or heard of before but they were presented in a new and different way.  Focusing on a story for each car in the museum made each and every one of them fascinating.  I wish we lived closer.
We had lunch in the diner.  The hot dogs were very tasty.

Very interesting collection that chronicles the history of Attleboro industry.  Lots of machines and examples of the jewelry-making businesses that once thrived here.  We went on a weekday.  There weren't any other visitors and the staff were extra friendly ... we were given a partial guided tour of several areas.

Lots of free parking and beautiful grounds to enjoy near the lake.
When we visited, it happened to be one of the days you can pay to climb the lighthouse.  We decided not to, but my wife got a stamp in her lighthouse passport since there were staff there.
The foghorn house had a bunch of souvenirs for sale.

There are two great things about this museum.  1) the film they show describing the history and building of the bridge and 2) it's free!  Most of the rest seems to be hard hats and models people have built of the bridge (luckily the real bridge doesn't have the angle of entry on some of these models.

It's a beautiful building with a very knowledgeable staff.  We visited on Free Fun Friday and took their (abbreviated?) tour.  We didn't hear much about Rose and her family during the tour.  A perfect time to chat about them would have been while we waited outside for the next tour to begin.
dislikes: Limited information on Rose and her family

reviews_attraction.text: We took the "classic" cruise.  It is the perfect way to see the Pictured Rocks.  The staff were all very friendly and knowledgeable (well, the ticket saleswoman wasn't exactly helpful).  You do have to put up with terrible jokes by the tour guide, but, I guess that is to be expected. :-)

While I am not a die-hard Star Trek fan, I completely enjoyed my tour.  The tour guide was knowledgeable and entertaining.  We were not rushed at any point and encouraged to take as many photographs as we wanted.  If you remember the show at all, you have to check it out!

Very interesting museum.  We came to get a photo of the CCC Worker statue (why doesn't anyone working the front gates ever know where these are?  Don't they actually go inside the parks where they work?).
It was a short, pleasant walk from the visitor's center.

An interesting place to poke around in.  Note: the parking lot is behind the building, but they expect you to enter the front.  We tried several times and finally found the bell at the back door.  The staff was very friendly and answered all our questions.

Even in winter, it is a beautiful place to walk around and view the birds.  The staff at the visitor's center were friendly and helped us try to identify the species we saw during our visit.  We were surprised at how wide and flat the trail system is.

A somewhat dry look at the events that led to US independence from England.  We visited as part of the Free Fun Friday program and were given "identities."  Unfortunately, they weren't used for very much along the way through the museum.

We had a great time on a snowy Saturday morning.  Despite the weather, we still had seven people on the tour.  We were shown everywhere except the basement and the housekeeper's quarters" (said to be offices and storage now).

This place is incredible.  I've visited twice and always find new and interesting things.  Some of the exhibits change and are always fascinating.  If you are a car/truck/motorcycle person, you have to visit this place.

We visited on Free Fun Friday.  The museum is small, but very interesting.  The views from the very top floor are terrific!  The employees and volunteers all seemed very knowledgeable and were quite enthusiastic.
Very interesting collection.  The roaming volunteer was very knowledgeable.  Our favorites were the early navigation device and the Reading Standard motorcycle just like my grandfather had.
Very well done.  The library and museum includes all of LBJ's political career as well as exhibits highlighting Lady Bird and the rest of his family.  We thoroughly enjoyed our visit.
The wines were OK.  The tasting was pretty pricey and you didn't even get to keep the glass.  Tip: be sure to ask for a taste of the chocolate sauce made with one of their wines!
What a beautiful place.  The staff member that conducted our tasting was very friendly.  The wines were some of the best we tried of the few vineyards we visited.
We stopped in to visit at 1:30 on a Wednesday.  The place was closed.  The hours on the window indicated that it was supposed to be open.  Very disappointing.

Seaside State Park is nice, but has a few issues which aren't bad. No swimming allowed, which you wouldn't, because there's seaweed everywhere, The park isn't ideal for little children, because to get to the beach, there's a big step from the grass to the beach with not many safe places to go down from it, and there are a lot of abandoned buildings. There are no signs anywhere for this place except for the one at the entrance, that all state parks have, with the shield hanging from a pole by chains. So why should you go here?

If you want to sunbathe, there is almost no one on the beach.
If you want to play fetch with your dog, again, no one is really here.
If you just want to take a walk, there are a few trails that you can walk on.

Hope this was a helpful review. I recommend coming here, just for the experience.

The easternmost point in the United States is right here! The lighthouse is great, and has good charm, and it still works! There are some trails, which are nice, and a visitor center, where you can learn about the history of the lighthouse. If your looking for souvenirs, go to West Quoody Gifts. There is a Maine state park stamp in the visitor center. It's definitely worth the trip to this lighthouse! The best time to go is on a cloudy, cool morning, but not too foggy. You get the essence of what it's like to be a lighthouse keeper. It's about half hour from Rte. 1, but worth it.

This was a great place. This place had a nice beach, with views of the bay, and you can watch ferries going back and forth. You can also see the Cape and Islands Korean War Memorial. This memorial was very nice and impressive, with a wonderful statue in the center. The one thing that was an issue here was the geese poop, so just stay on the walkways. Also check out Little Poseidon's Adventures on Google Plus, where he provides pictures and information about his journeys.

Very pretty here. In the past few times I've gone, both on weekdays, no one has been in the ticket booth, meaning they're letting you in for free! But this is as of August 2016, so I don't know if they charge on weekends or if this will change. Walk through the many gardens, take your bike and ride along the paved roads, see a 100 year old tree, go out to the flagpole to watch the ferries come in. Great place to go!

Definitely come here. The drive is a little long on the way down, but is scenic and is worth it. There is a little aquarium that the state park set up, with sea horses, pipefish, and a horseshoe crab. The museum is great, it doesn't only focus on the lighthouse, but all the other Rhode Island Lighthouse there ever were. After, climb on the rocks and get the breeze in your face. Great place to go.

The views are absolutely amazing up here! You can see all of Provincetown and most of Truro. There's a small cottage at the bottom. The climb is mostly a series of ramps, with some stairs at the beginning and end, making this an easier climb.  Also check out Little Poseidon's Adventures on Google Plus, where he provides pictures and information about his journeys.

This memorial was great. There was a nice pool in a serene area overlooking the bay. The memorial itself is very neat. There are benches as well so you can sit and take in your surroundings. This is a very nice place, minus the geese poop. Also check out Little Poseidon's Adventures on Google Plus, where he provides pictures and information about his journeys.

Nice exhibits, with a variety of different animals, including seahorses, octopuses, sea urchins, penguins, seals, eels and so many more. The giant tank in the middle that is 4 stories tall is my favorite, especially when we saw the fish take pieces of food from the diver's hand! The gift shop is OK, but overall a great place. Recommend 3 hours to do this.

It's a 40 minute drive from Bar Harbor, but SPECTACULAR views are here that capture Acadia's beauty. The lighthouse is closed to the public, since it is an active US. Coast Guard Lighthouse, but the view is great. Next to the bathrooms, there is a trail that goes down to the  rocks to get an even better view. Please go here on a visit to Acadia.

This is just like all the other Rhode Island beaches, which are absolutely wonderful. They're huge, so lots of room to spread out, and the have big waves, which are nice. This also has a very easy acsess, and a restrooms building, a few nice things that make this place stick out from the rest. Good beach to go to.

This place is basically New England in a nutshell. You have a beautiful lighthouse and a wonderful beach on the Atlantic Ocean. This place speaks for itself. It is just beautiful. I suggest checking out Little Poseidon's Adventures on Google Plus, where he provides pictures and information about his journeys.
