This was a pretty good museum. It was very interactive and hands-on; great for little kids. There was a lot I learned from this museum, including information about his life, his inventions, and historic Philadelphia. Overall, a pretty great museum about the person on the $100 bill.

There is some nice overlooks and an observation area here. Unfortunately this place is open from April 15th to October, so we didn't get to go in here. Also check out Little Poseidon's Adventures on Google Plus, where he provides pictures and information about his journeys.

Fort Knox was great, it's not the one they keep gold in, but it's still pretty cool. If you're going to the observatory, I suggest going to this too. There are some cannons still in the fort, which is really cool, but be warned: it is very easy to get lost in the fort.

This place is awesome! The water is freezing, even in the summer, and the waterfall current is strong, but this is great! There are dozens
of little pools the waterfall makes that you can swim in! I saw fish in one of these! Such a great stop and don't miss it.

Great place to go for a day hike. Slightly challenging but lots of fun. Plenty of viewpoints to look out from. Be prepared for lots and lots of people, and come early if you go here on the Tower Toot weekend. Otherwise there’s usually not a lot of people here.

Views are fantastic. Have lunch right on the rocky shore and watch the ducks float in the waves. 10 minutes from Portland. Many view points above rocks give you good views, but is it often foggy here. Overall, I recommend going.

This was a good art museum of portraits of important people from the Revolutionary era. The bank has been turned into an art museum, so if you want to find bank artifacts, head to the First Bank of the United States.

So much to do here. 3 floors jam packed of hands on, informative learning for all ages. I suggest planning to have half a day to be able to see everything, because there's so much! Great attraction in Boston.

Great place for an evening hike. Good viewpoint at the top; you can see Hartford and some of the suburbs from there. The hike does go right by some houses, but otherwise it’s a beautiful natural place.
Very interesting museum, with art from around the world. The museum includes Greek, Islamic, Asian and other art. We visited in July, so it was rather hot inside, but overall a pretty nice place.
Panoramic views of the city, harbor islands, the suburbs, and beyond. You can see Fenway Park, The Bunker Hill Monument, The Museum of Fine Arts, just to name a few. Definitely worth it.
The bridge is walkable, so you can go on a stroll and get some good pictures. It is 1 3/4 miles one way, so plan a good amount of time to walk the whole thing.
This was a nice cute historic alley, and close by to all of the attractions. There's a little back alley where you can here stories as well.
This is a nice, quiet, serene place on the water. You can get good pictures of the bridge here as well.

The first sign which greets you is one in the unpaved spacious parking lot which says that any car found after sunset will be towed without notice to the owner... ‘cause there’s nothing a lost hiker in winter needs more than to return and discover that his vehicle’s been stolen! Luckily the waterfall is not far off, maybe ten minutes hiking. There is an overlook fashioned with a fence so that you don’t gawk your way to a watery grave. There is a bridge with handrails, a cobbled staircase, some benches, and causeways spanning channels in the hillside through which spill-off runs in voluminous rivulets during torrents. At the trail’s entrance is an archway and a bulletin board.
likes: Infrastructure (bridge, handrails, cobbled staircase, benches, causeways)

reviews_attraction.text: Great place to spend a day with the family. Lots of fun and learning activities. There is a 3D theater with several shows a day. Butterfly exhibit is very enjoyable. If you are lucky, a butterfly may just land on you. There is a separate fun playground-like area where the kids can play with the water-based machines. For the water activities, there are rain covers available of various sizes. I would recommended that the parents bring a pair of water-proof shoes for the child since the feet do get wet. There is a food court offering a variety of sandwiches and pizza. There is a tea and coffee stand, a snack vending g machine and a Frozen yogurt stand.

Science made fun and understandable for children. Mini Gold and a didactic playground on-site. Movies of education and entertainment for children are screened several times a day in the theatre upstairs. Throughout the day there are interactive educational performances. The gift shop has many interesting offerings, discounted for the Hall of Science's members. Likewise members get discounts in the cafeteria, which is clean with lots of natural lighting, though its selection is scant. Bathrooms are well maintained, and parking is plentiful. For public commuters, the Hall of Science is a short walk from the 7-train's stop at 111th Street.

Short but cute covered bridge, with breadth enough for one car at a time. A pedestrian walkway approaches the bridge, but does not traverse the bridge since there is insufficient space. Therefore be careful when exploring the bridge on foot. Spooner Pond slowly passes underneath the bridge. Nearby are antique gear works in display, and a unpaved parking lot for roughly ten cars. A beaten up wooden archway frames the road leading to the bridge, so that vehicles can determine whether they have the headroom for clearing the covered bridge.

Straddling the border between Connecticut and Massachusetts, this park has two halves on opposite ends of the Whiting River. Present review was conducted solely in the southern half mostly encompassing Connecticut. Two border markers are erected there, one vandalized. The footpaths are well-trodden, with pine needles either manually or naturally strewn underfoot for greater traction. One can cross Ginger Creek for steeper trails towards the crest line. The waterfall itself is gorgeous!

Refreshing use of space and catchy industrial designs. Located in the Belly of the Beast which is modern Long Island City, yet mercifully distant from the worst of that urban jungle. The playground equipment is in good repair, and the sprinklers are especially refreshing in the summer. Bathrooms were functional during this review. Free wi-fi (if you trust New York City's government enough to let it plant cookies on your device). Ample seating for the supervising parents.

A challenging but rewarding hike in the freshest air imaginable! There are about three different routes of varying difficulties, with the steepest cresting the ridge itself. Crystalline water. Two plaques recount the Stone Church's bloody history. Access to the Stone Church is through a private driveway (with public easement granted), which is disorienting, especially given that directly next door is a funeral parlor with intriguing "church-like" masonry out front.

Wide-open park space along the waterfront. Clean and well-mowed. Bathrooms on-site in season, and free streetside or metered parking nearby. The park features a playground for younger kids. Many options for eateries around the park ranging from lower to high end. MetroNorth is directly adjacent, which is a mixed blessing insofar as it makes the park very accessible, but disrupts the park's tranquility with screeching train whistles every thirty minutes or so.

Being that Queens is populated and visited by so many people from different countries, this steel sculpture represents everybody in some way. Perfectly spherical and iconic, the Unisphere is a marvel of engineering, set in symmetry to the park's other structures. Used as the backdrop of many local cinematic and photographic productions. On September 16th, 2020, the Libertarian Party of Queens hosted Larry Sharpe directly in front of the Unisphere.

Ruins of a mainstay of industrial production in this region. This blast furnace and smithy were owned and operated by a family, the Pomeroys, who arrived from Massachusetts. Remnants of their trade’s equipment are on display in the museum on-site, including an ore-crusher patented by Eli Whitney Blake, grandson of Eli Whitney, famous inventor of the cotton gin. There are also ruins of the coal shed used in the iron smelting.

A memorable destination in any season! Snowmobiling, sledding, ice skating, ice-fishing, fly-fishing, cross-country skiing, swimming, camping, hunting, biking and boating all available (permits may apply through New York State's Parks & Recreation). Cabins for rent. Sheltered beachfront and concessions of decent quality nearby at fair prices. Bathrooms with showers in the center. Sizable parking lot by the beachfront.

Not all that impressive, but hey, when you’re getting some fresh air after living couped up in one of these surrounding matchbox Woodside apartments with a bong-smoking room mate, this small parklet must seem like Yosemite National Reserve! Little confusing that this place is also identified as Lawrence Virgilio park, but he was probably the area’s city councilman who grafted this park into existence.

Undoubtedly better in fairer weather, but still a relaxing destination for a stroll. There is also a playground, basketball courts and picnic tables. The curious feature of this park are its acoustics. You hear the diffusion of sound as at a beach (with the surf’s sound nearby), yet the cobblestones allow for some reverberation, which makes for an intriguingly eery combination.

Maybe this review caught Found Land Park off season, but it was not in the best shape. There are faint, infrequent markings on trees to indicate a trail, but underfoot the trail is scarcely blazed, which leaves hikers just trudging over brush. Nor were any landmarks sighted, or anything distinctive, leaving an unchanging landscape. The park is serene, though.

Idyllic playground (sawdust flooring) and park with basketball court (four hoops). The playground’s equipment is in good repair. Two sets of swings and many benches. Two picnic tables. Receptacles for trash and recyclables. Evergreen screening out the baseball diamond next door. There is a community garden, but nothing was growing during this review.

Visited off-season, but clearly a lovely park. Crystalline lake (unsure whether swimming is permitted), picnic tables, stationary grills and hiking. A rivulet flows nearby underneath three small bridges. Bathrooms are available, though there were closed during this review. Parking lot sizable (around sixty vehicles). Grounds well-maintained.

The re-enactors' fluency with and enthusiasm for the subject matter is contagious! Thoroughly impressive reconstruction of the fortress and collection of artifacts. The only incongruence are the surrounding modern businesses like Mini-Golf and Para-Sailing on Lake George, which detract from the fortress' somberness.

A rehabilitating excursion from anywhere! Majestic views in all directions, with nearby West Point and distant Manhattan visible on clear days. Frequent events like vintage car shows, custom motorcycles and Oktoberfest (2-hour wait on the line to the bathroom, so drink accordingly!). Parking plentiful.

Anything... and I mean anything related to motorcycles and motorcycling, will be found here. Prototypes, flops, successes, concept bikes, vintage discontinued models, artisanal builds like Indian Larry's work. This museum is a pilgrimage which every motorcyclist must make at least once in a lifetime!

As with modern art, it can be very hit or miss, but the curation is thought-provoking, and definitely there are some awe-inspiring, unconventional works on display in mediums of sculpture, video, illustration and architecture. No visit is complete without a trip to the M. Wells Dinette on site!

Specimens gathered from all over the world, including some which are very rare, such as the Red Panda. The local high school's students do most of the zoo-keeping, which makes the exhibits even more impressive. A webcam displays activity at the zoo, in certain cages.

A lovely park with a war memorial which is not overly maudlin, tastefully proportioned and positioned. What is mystifying though is that most of the many people who come here mourning lost veterans are eager to make more of them through endless foreign engagements.

Gorgeous monument to our veterans which has not yet been toppled by Ant1fa. Cobblestones and benches which see their fair share of freaky-deaky at night. If you take toddlers here, just remind them that those things discarded by the bushes are NOT balloons!

A delight to the senses and intellect, engaging children in those subjects which they usually avoid in their homework! Hands-on learning at its finest. Wonderful curation! Tickets purchased on-line and last up to six months.

Lovely public park in the middle of the town of Hudson. Monuments with plaques, railroad tracks, laminated maps, benches and a street clock. All around are restaurants and smaller shops, including a Citgo gas station.

Great Place to Bike-About.
This coastal park was next to our Hilton Garden Inn and they provided the bikes for free.  Great paved bike paths and a cool playground structure at the south end.  Many beach photo ops and panoramic shots too.  Park is free with easy access and ample parking.  Make sure to check out the 1750 Hawaiian ruins at the north end of the park into Wailua State Park.

Nice Walk-About with a Happy Ending.
I entered the park from the CT side.  Note the trail head is to the left.  It's a 20 minute walk to the falls base, about 2000 steps.  It's very nice walk-about and the waterfall is very cool.  Not a single bug was encountered along the way.  There is a gravel road that overlooks the top of the falls.  This is a must-do whilst visiting Norfolk.

Must See This....
This is a must do drive-about.  There are many lookouts along the way.  The main lookout has fairly good parking capacity with quick turnover.  There is a fully stocked fruit stand and clean restrooms.  The views from the main platform are incredible.  There is also a non-guardrail section that will really test your fear of heights.

Best Kept Secret Walk-About.
This park offers a great walk, run & bike about.  Ducks and Geese.  Very clear water and fish.  The tall pines that surround the reservoir make it pop.  The parking is very tight but I see it's the norm to park on RT 202.  This is must go-to spot for all.

Great walk or bike-about loop trail.
The nature center is very cool for adults and kids.  The staff is very laid back and friendly.  There are native on sale for cheap.  The loop trail is good for walking or biking but only in the dry season.  Dog friendly too.

Canadian Geese Rest Stop.  Neat pond just off Sullivan Avenue.  Good place to see wildlife.  Short walk from the small parking area to the deck on the pond.  There are tons of Geese here and a few ducks.  There is a bench on the deck.

Great Beach Park, Arrive Early
The water is excellent here. The view from the bluff at the western end of the eastern park is awesome. Great spot for kids to learn how to surf.  Make sure to check out the dry cave across the street.

You can do this in just over an hour.  Some well written storyboards.  The Baldwin Locomotive was the centerpiece and informative.  Great paid parking next door.  The only negative was, there isn't a AAA discount.
Great Blue Trail Trail-head.  Plenty of parking behind the Wilbur Cross Dunkin Donuts.  There is also a canoe launch here.  The trail meanders along the Q and there is a good chance to see deer here.

Great place for a walk-about with camera.
Nice views along Indian River.  Good boardwalk. Free entrance. Lots of squirrels. Nice breeze and plenty of shade trees. Easy access and ample parking.
Cool CT river find in Cromwell.  Well off the beaten path so not many folks around.  Lots of bird activity and one drone.  Plenty of parking and several park benches / tables and a pavilion.

Meeting Astronaut Story Musgrave was an Awesome Experience.
Great small town Air Museum. 3 buildings chalk full of aircraft displays. Very good story boards. Great for all ages. A must see.

Cool Park
Found this park during the evacuation of hurricane Matthew and needed a place to let the dogs do their thing.  Note the real park is east of the mapped park. No entrance fee.
Pre-hurricane Irma drive-by.  Whilst evacuating Irma we did a quick pit stop here.  Would have liked to spend some time here exploring.  I wonder how it fared in the storm.

Cool Spot to Watch Aircraft Takeoffs.
Also a good spot to clean out your rental car and change into your travel clothes.  Good views of pounding surf.
Very nice preserve.  Short walk to the St. Lucie River.  Parking is tight but there is usually an open space or two.  Good story board and map.
Nice park.  No surprise the brook was not roaring in December.  Looking forward to more walk-abouts here in the spring. The parking is tight.
Great townies park.  $20 for non-townies.  Groomed sand.  Ample parking.  Clean bathrooms.  The friendly staff let me do a Google Drive-By.
Must see Refuge.  Great drive through park.  Lots of bird life.  Plenty of places to pull over and walk-about.  Observation and boardwalks.
Nice park with a summertime water feature.  Dog friendly.  Lots of Canadian Geese on the lower pond.  One large white swan on the upper.

Great Waterfront Dog Park.
Well maintained.  Nice sidewalks.  A separate dog park with chain linked fencing to let the dogs off leash.
Exceptional historic site.  Great walk about loop trail.  Much to see.  Good story boards.. The Tree lined tunnel drive is very cool.
Quiet Park.  Nice end of the road park .  Lots of winter bird activity here.  Large parking area.  Free access.  Open 8AM to Dusk.

Cool Park on the Salmon Brook.
Well maintained park.  Canadian geese hanging out in the water.  Easy access and ample parking.
Great park along the Connecticut river.  The park is free.  There is ample parking.  Nice place to watch the water craft.

Went to the Halloween train ride and my son loved it.  The old train and locomotive are beautifully kept.  You can tell they care about the train very much.  Each detail down to the stain of the wood is done with care.  The train takes you down the tracks about 6 miles with little displays on the side.  There is an open air trailer where you can go out and see everything with the air whipping through your hair.  The passager car as mentioned was very well preserved.  There is a snack train and store which they maintain.  The staff was very helpful and nice, and any questions you had about the train or the area was answered.  They are running a Christmas train ride which we are looking forward to going.

The redesigned Shark Park is amazing.  We loved the old park but it was starting to show its age.  We miss the wood character of the park though.  The new park though is just as good.  They added a ton of new areas for the kids to climb around and play along with added features like the bells.  They added a dedicated small kids area with easier to climb on rides .  Lots of swings were added, and the park looks great.  They did a fantastic job.  They also take donations as it was all privately funded.

Small aquarium with lots to see. There is numerous exhibits inside with large tanks for fish, jelly fish and crabs. There is an ampitheatre to watch sea lion show. There is a small penguin exhibit with underwater viewing and a whale exhibit. The shark 4D movie was ok which leads to the animatronic dinosaur exhibits. Only complaint is the price is a little high for the size of the aquarium and the food court food wasn't the best.

Very nice aquarium. There are numerous exhibits and layed out very well. A large part of the aquarium is an enclosed tube underneath the large tank which let's you see all the fish from below. The penguin section was great and allows the kids to crawl under the tank and come up with the penguins. The layout is very linear so if you miss a section you will need to walk through the whole aquarium again.

Beautiful nature preserve and beach. Only way onto the beach is walk up from Clearwater, sail in or take the ferry over.  Beach was not packed when we went but they said during the holidays it does get packed but there is a large beach for everyone. There is changing room building on the path up to the beach and chair/umbrella rentals once you get to the beach.

This casino is sad and I've been to Mount Airy Lodge. They abandoned everything in the casino. What was once filled with slot machines is now open floor for people to mindless wander around in and look lost. The buffet is completely gone. There is a bro pit with beer pong and an arcade but the arcade is sad too. Guess there is live shows on the weekend.

Great Family Fun.  There are some really great rides in the park and the food is awesome.  Best amusement park around.  You pay per ride and there are no gates around the park.  You can wander in at 8 AM, and just check everything out.  There is a ton of rides and stores.  The food is fantastic, and there is something for everyone.

The playground is large with lots for kids to play on. There are tennis courts and basketball courts along with a very clean and inviting dog park. The community center is on site with a gym, indoor basketball and community events. It's nice to see this available for everyone. The community pool is also on-site and is very clean.

Very expansive train layout with night time display. Shows are 30 minutes and run every hour on the half hour. Lots of detail in the train set up. You can tell they put a lot of care into the details. Lots of cool things to find in the displays. The display is very popular around Christmas so try to go not during the holidays.

Very nice park. Very clean and well maintained. There is a playground at the entrance near the covered Bridge along with tennis and handball courts. Jordan Creek runs through the park and it is accessible from anywhere in the park. There is an 18-hole frisbee golf course throughout the treeline.

Small little covered bridge park. You can tell someone cares for this park very much. The park is well kept and the gazebo is maintained. Some nice walking paths are around the park and the bridge itself is very well kept. There is no parking space but there usually isn't anyone here.

Excellent zoo and well worth the visit.  Its great that it is donation admission and not a set price.  The park is very clean and presentable.  Lots to do here.  Concession stand is not overly priced and seagull free (unless they walk in).  The zoo its is great and fun for kids.

The Halloween train was a lot of fun. They stopped off at the farm and there was a lot to do then. The Easter Express was not as good. We had to get off the train so they could swap the engine and there is nothing to do at the train station other then a small train table.

Nice easy hiking trails and very well kept paths. Beautiful scenery of the Bushkill stream. The main eastern trails is easy to walk and relatively level but there is a hill to climb.  The western trail does get a little a steeper. There are facilities at the entrances.

The chair and view are awesome. Whomever made the chair did a great job on it. The view is beautiful and you can see all around the valley.

The dumping ground of trash over the ledge isn't that great. Can't believe people would drop their junk here.

This park is awesome. Take your kids here and they will have a blast. There are a ton of kids specific rides and there is no wait. Only complaint is they charge adults the same price as kids even though they can't ride on a majority of the rides.

While not the best aquarium I've been to the facilities are small, but the exhibits aren't bad.  Its very underfunded in a town know for the casinos and not the family attractions.  Its good for a rainy day when you need to get out of the casino.

The park and its walking trails are great.  The fish hatchery, the covered bridge and the Native American Museum are great to explore.  The bathrooms are very rustic, but none of the horse owns clean up after themselves.

Beautiful state park. Numerous beach, boat docks and hiking trails adds to the park. Even off season the park is open for walking the trails. If you are looking for unique smooth rocks this beach is the place.

Great place to take the kids and walk around the fort. Lots of displays and information to take in. They have demonstrations during the day on fort life and weaponry. The view from the top floor are fantastic.

Fun place to bring you kid if they are into geology and rocks. The dig area is fun and look for rocks and other minerals. The tour is closed right now due to Covid so we didn't do that but everything was fun.
Nicely kept park with a beach on the ocean. There is no swimming as it's a rock beach. The mansion grounds are we'll kept and the flower garden looks like someone cares for it.
Beautiful park with a large lake and swimming in the summer time. Park was very well kept and trails easily accessible.  The boulder field is definitely something to see.
Beach was amazing. Easy access parking lot with reasonable prices with an on-site bathroom and water vending machine. Beach is very clean and beautiful.
Wonderful park. Lots of walking paths and a nice clean beach. The lighthouse is great if you want to spend the money and walk the steps.

Lovely fountain in the heart of Cincinnati city. A happening place with many social activities going on. A must place to visit if one is in Cincinnati. As I was about to click  a photo of the fountain, a clown jumped in and posed in the photo.

I could view and photograph it from Fort Constitution ( a somewhat restricted view). The main access through an active Coast Guard base ( which was not open the day I visited). Seems this access is open only for restricted times.
Wonderful place for taking long walks. Reasonably well maintained trails. A working dairy farm and ice cream parlor is added attraction if accompanying kids. Ample parking place ( with parking fee).
Very scenic, relaxing and calm place. Good place to spend a day or half for walking/hiking or picnic. As the reservoir is for public drinking water supply, restrictions on going close to  water.
Very nice memorial with a beautiful gate. Ideal for photo shoot. The memorial is located in green Hill Park, which itself is very beautiful with sprawling green lawns and a couple of ponds.
Very well maintained and clean park. The trail around the pond is very relaxing. Ample benches to enjoy the scenery and take rest. Fountains add to the beauty of the pond.
Nice park with a beautiful small pond. Ample benches to relax and enjoy the scenery. Lots of geese, which are not scared by people. Goood place to spend a couple of hours.
Very nice rocky shore. Parking space is limited ( around 6-7 cars). Very close to other tourist attractions like Magnolia pier and Hammond Castle and Coolidge reservation.
Very nice place for a hike with a view of sea. Well maintained trails. A couple of hours are required to explore the place. Parking is limited so it gets filled fast.
Very nice place to go for hike. Ample free parking and lot of trails. Trails are comparatively easy. The place has lot of bugs during summer, so come prepared.
Nice small place. The sea view is very nice and relaxing from top of the rocks. Free street side parking on Ocean Avenue ( at the entrance of the park).
Very nice place to spend a day with nature. Has sandy beaches, rocky shore, boardwalks, trails, watchtowers etc. Excellent place for bird watching.
Very scenic place to hike with lot of well maintained trails around pond and in the woods. Good place to watch wildlife. Dog friendly place.
Easily accessible  well maintained landmark of Rockport. There are several gift shops and food places for tourists in nearby Bearskin Neck.
Trail to waterfalls very well maintained. Falls are every impressive and beautiful. The trail is a bit steep from Mass. side trail head.
Very nice and refreshing walk along the lake in Meredith. Several artworks to enjoy and ample benches to take rest and enjoy the view.
Very nice and well maintained trail for walking or biking. Trail is mostly flat and shaded. Benches along the trail for taking rest.
Very nice park in side Worcester. Has a beautiful pond, with walking path around it, and bright colored bridges to cross it.
Nice light house on private property. Can be viewed and photographed from pier of another lighthouse ( Dog Bar Lighthouse).
Nice looking castle by the sea. Went off season so it was closed, but could walk around the premises which is accessible.
Ample parking with a small fee. Lot of trails and natural beauty. My favorite trail is the one along Merrimack river.
A small but very beautiful garden, with plenty of roses of various colors. free parking and free admission. Love it.
Very nice and picturesque place to take a walk by lake. Ample free parking and sprawling lawns. Dogs are welcome.
Nice spot for awesome view of Quabbin Reservoir. Minutes walk away from main road. Good place for a short break.
Very cute fun place with live music in the evenings. A bit crowded, but everyone seemed to be having lot of fun.

The Seacoast Science Center was one of the places we decided to visit during our vacation. Admittedly, I thought the center was much bigger than it was. However, the center is utilizing most of their space with exhibits and or historic information. There is also a rather comfortable ocean front view with nice open hallways.

NOTE: This place is much less expensive to visit, let's say, the New England Aquarium. We spent a fraction of the cost to the Seacoast Science Center. Of course, this is different than the sea creatures found at the New England Aquarium but still has the same vibe. Also, may I add, there was so much more room here as opposed to the New England Aquarium. If you want to visit a center filled with ocean creatures and don't want to be within shoulder space between someone else, this is the place to go.

There is also a fun interactive boating area for children. My daughter had such a fun time fishing and sorting her daily haul. There are other activities through the center for children and curious adults as well! Although, there were a couple of things that appeared to be out of service or not working correctly on our visit. The microscope appeared to have a bad connection to the monitor it was connected to and the scale appeared to be out of service.

We visited during what I would call an off season. I read many reviews and I see many people complaining about the cost of parking. I believe those parking costs are only applicable between Labor day weekend to Culumbus day. So if you have never been here before and would like to visit without paying a parking fee, I would suggest visiting mid September to mid May.

We had visited on a spur of the moment type deal while we were vacationing in Connecticut. Upon arrival, I was a bit sticker shocked at the price of admittance plus the extra fees to do special exhibits. We were concerned that our daughter would be too old for this science center (age 6) but we were so wrong! There are 6 floors of amazing things to learn, even for adults! The CT Science center leaves nothing out! The have a rooftop garden and a butterfly exhibit you can walk through. Admittedly, it is not the most amazing butterfly exhibit I have seen, but for the amount of room they have to work with, I understand. Our daughter was able to program a life size robot to talk and move around. They have a floor for engineering, an area for saving energy and how the things we use everyday effect the power we use. There are live reptiles on display, though you have to be really small like a child to see some of them. Pretty cool though how they designed it all for kids of young ages to see such cool creatures. They have a HUGE section on space and another HUGE section on AI technology. Another room completely dedicated to mazes and puzzles. Everything can be easily accessed for those with disabilities and wheelchair accessible.  Absolutely incredible the way this place is designed to teach everyone all these things! So, if you feel like I did and were unsure about the price or if maybe you child might not be interested, just know that it is WELL worth the trip for anyone of any age. I wish I could go back everyday!

This museum was a fun educational place to take our daughter! We had never been here before and it was quite a surprise for our daughter. She had a blast! We got there early, shortly after they opened. There was hardly anyone there at that time. I was able to go around and take some pictures. We were able to try a lot of what the museum had to offer so that was fun! We loved the USPS letters throughout the museum. My daughter loved delivering mail! It was just such a fun time.

We did visit on a weekend so we had a feeling it would be a bit busier than a weekday, but we didn't expect a party to show up. It got a bit overcrowded by 1pm so that was a bummer. (Super packed) Too many kids hovering around exhibits by that time. So we ended up leaving much earlier than we wanted to.

I think the cost of admission would have been fine had we been able to stay longer. But it was so over packed with people it made it not feel like the price was worth what we paid. We were told we could leave and come back that day, but there was absolutely no parking available. People were lined up hoping to catch a spot from anyone leaving.

Again, it was great before it got overwhelming busy. I would say this museum is great for kids 5 and under. If we paid this price on a sunny Tuesday, we would have probably had the best time where it wouldnt be over crowded. But when you take a busy cold Saturday and throw a kids birthday party in the mix, it's not the best.
dislikes: High admission cost relative to experience

reviews_attraction.text: Submarines great and small!! Look at the size differences between the USS Ohio and the USS Holland! If you like to learn about submarines, this is the place for you! This was our second visit here. Some things have changed since the last time we were there. Santa is gone from the museum. There's a new NR-1 exhibit moving right along. One subtle thing noticed was the change made on the USS Nautilus. So, the USS Nautilus was the first ever nuclear powered submarine. It's so cool that it's right here on display for people to walk through, but obviously we won't be experiencing any nuclear one on ones with the submarine. So, last time we were there, we could walk through and basically half way through the submarine and the door would be closed so there would be no access to the other half of nucleur end of the submarine. The difference? Last time, we could peer through a tiny round window on the door. This time, the tiny round window was plated up. Glued down. Alarm on the door. A lot of extra precautions to keep people from looking at anything directly related to nuclear technology. When asked about the change on the way out and the gentleman wasn't really sure how to answer the question other than saying, even though it's old technology, there are still countries out there that would love to get their hands on certain information. I found that interesting.

Great for walking around and learning a lot of cool facts! You have to be physically able to maneuver around inside the submarine. If you are not physically able to go through the submarine, you can learn a lot from inside the museum from videos and various plaques.  Nice air conditioning inside of the museum, not so much in the submarine, but hey, what did you think? They do have some fans inside the submarine to help keep the air moving! During the past year, there has been a remarkable amount of renovations made to the location! They now have a great draining system and have cleared up a lot of the debris that the submarine was sitting in which was causing corrosion. It looks amazing now!  When we were visiting, there was someone mowing far out all the way to the road so it's all cleared out now. It looks amazing! Remember that it is run on donations so when you visit, donations are super important to help contribute to keep this place looking great!

Our family had a wonderful time here. It was quite educational as well, even for my young daughter. The wind was blowing, but not too bad. The sun was out and we were above the clouds. I just have to add this  because it is something I will never forget: Cell phone service is of course poor up there, but there is wifi. With that said, I found it absolutely hilarious and awesome that there were 2 pokemon go gyms atop the mountain. So, if you want a pokemon to stay in a gym for more than a day, there you go. It was just funny that it was there. I am glad there was wifi because our emergency phone rang while we were at the top of the mountain but we could not answer it. No one has our emergency number so we knew it was serious. And it was. Other than that, I would have never even checked my phone because the day was just so amazingly perfect without it.

What a great place to explore! Tall trees, the chirping of the birds and the long winding walking trails will have you wanting to stay forever. If you keep walking, you can make your way to the Jackson Falls dam. Our adventure went a little like this. So, we went to Lincoln Park which is right in with Mine Falls Park. We wanted to go by the dam and watch the water fall /flow from all the rains we've been having. Overall it was a fun day. There was a family who was trying to cross the water over small rocks protruding from the water. I was like PFFFFT I can do that. So on my way back to the car, I decided to do it. Let it be known that during my crossing, I lost my stepping twice, and yep, I left Lincoln Park with pretty wet feet and pants. Would recommend!

2020 Update
Wildcat Falls Conservation Area is a beautiful place and has become quite a popular attraction this year  for more than just our locals. Many places still remain closed and now Wildcat Falls is one of the places closed. My heart is so broken to see how people have treated this land. The behavior some people have displayed are atrocious. I hope that when this area opens back up people can use the common decency to respect the land. Carry in, carry out. Please drive slow. Please respect private properties as well. This is really just such a sad situation considering this was one of the few places that /was/ open to the public. Definitely more than a few bad apples created this mess. ☹

Lovely park for entertainment mainly but also beautiful just to enjoy the day. There is plenty of room for sitting or chairs if you are attending a concert or an event. (Sorry, it's all grass so bring a chair or blanket as no chairs are here permanently.)  They did have food trucks there but I am sure thay varies between what events are happening. The park was incredibly clean. There were people who were picking up trash the second it hit the ground. Very attentive park staff. I think they could have done better with supplying enough bathrooms because those were not clean at all. Just opted not to use the bathrooms. But my experience here was great and fun for the whole family.

We absolutely were delighted by the beautiful flowers all throughout the park! All the right flowers and plants in all the right areas and they were all thriving! I can definitely appreciate a park with the right garden atmosphere. The park is very well maintained and the paths are clear. The only issue we had was the amount of people hanging out under the gazebo during the rain, and they were not friendly and they were unwelcoming. I'm not sure if this is normal that people just huddle here? But the park itself was beautiful. We did end up departing when the crowd under the gazebo began yelling and swearing because we just were not sure what was happening.

There is so much to do here! We actually didn't even have the energy to see the whole place. Wish we could have. We noticed a playground when we first came in. They have trolley service / tours. There are fields and fields of room to basically do as you please! People were flying kites, having picnics, grilling, and just enjoying their time being with one another. The views are incredible! We did do some rock walking. I would recommend wearing some good sneakers.I went in flip flops and it was easier to walk the rocks barefoot. They have some incredible lobster rolls of all kinds! It is a must to visit if you are in the area!!

Nice day spent with the family here. Staff was friendly and knowledgable. Spider monkeys coming soon. Seemed to be a lot of construction through the park with new exhibits coming. It was just strange to see construction workers during the zoo hours, considering the zoo closes early enough daily where the construction workers could work on the new exhibits after the zoo closes. Lots of animals to see. Food was good, although it was a long wait (about 20 minutes) for a BLT. The otters were incredibly cute! Otters definitely on the top of my list for this zoo!!

I cannot stress this enough, buy your pass online before you get there. When we showed up, they were not taking payments at the booth and gave us the information for purchasing a pass online. Unfortunately not all phone companies have service in this area. My husband did have service with Verizon but it was slow. Anyway, PLEASE plan ahead.

Once you get in, check EVERYTHING out! Place is amazing. We spent the entire day here and we loved it! Bathrooms are available too. Lots of history here and lots of family memories to be made here as well.
dislikes: Poor mobile service for on-site ticket purchase

reviews_attraction.text: I was very disappointed. I saved many light houses on my trip to Connecticut along the east coast. However, once I got to Connecticut, it was impossible to see any of them! Drove here just to find it is intended for Connecticut residents . Such a let down for the whole family. Do not waste your time coming to this light house. If you are not from Connecticut, avoid going to really anything along the coast in Connecticut because none that we went to were free. Insane prices for out of state travelers to visit.

The parking situation was a bit hectic but perhaps it was just because of the day and time we had visited. You can spend all day here trying to walk all the trails or you can break it up into sections and come back at another time. Some of the trails are nice easy and flat where others are fairly steep (for walkers, not hikers). But of course, my opinion is the best art is on the harder trails. Great for a family fun day outdoors that has pretty open trails. There is always something fun to find here!

Generally a good time. Tickets to the games aren't too expensive but you can expect to pay an arm and a leg for food and drinks. That's pretty typical though. Seats are pretty good and better protected. Not stroller friendly. Please don't try and shove your strollers in the isles. Transportation to and from here is very easy too with easy access to cabs and the train station not too far away.

Lovely piece of history. Well maintained land and Mill. We would love to come back during of hours of operation. I believe I read those hours are the 2nd and 4th Saturday from 10am to 4pm. It certainly would be amazing to see how it all happened in person. Even though we visited while they were closed, it was still so beautiful to just visit and enjoy.

Lovely day to go out with the family. We were on an adventure to do all new things we had not yet done together as a family. Decided to come here and check out this state park. Place was beautiful and kept well clean. There was plenty of room for all types of family gatherings. Looking forward to coming back in the warmer days!

Wonderful time with our family. There was plenty to explore! The weather was rainy that day, but that didn't stop us. We had such an amazing time with the rain wind and all! I can't imagine how amazing it must be in the summer. We would love to go back next summer so we can visit in a warmer nicer day.

Miller State Park is a BEAUTIFUL place to visit in New Hampshire. There are many great things you can do outdoors here. There is plenty of parking in a well maintained area. This is such a great place to take kids or pets because they are nice easy trails in my opinion. Great for the whole family!

It was hot. We had a blast. We left soaked!

Plenty of seating. Super clean. I could really smell the chlorine, though. Overall it was super fun! We really enjoyed the variety of water displays it had. Everyone was having a great time! I will definitely bring the family back again!

Great park and access to trails. People here are incredibly friendly and helpful. Park is VERY well maintained, all the way down to the lines on the pavement. Awesome place to bring kids and enjoy the whole day outside. We will definitely be back again soon to do more exploring.

Small little lighthouse very much on land and not really near the water. However, this is truly a beautiful little place and markers placed around the lighthouse. The parking was a bit tricky. Many people were in the area and we had to do a bit of walking, but it was worth it.

Amazing place to visit ESPECIALLY on a hot day after the sun gleaming down on you. The lower falls has plenty of water and flat like rocks that allows many visitors to all enjoy a bit of water. So come and enjoy the view of the trees, rocks, and while you relax and unwind.
An absolute incredible site to see! Very well kept grounds. Bus/trolley tours and lots of room for doing outdoor family activities! It is a must visit place if you are in the area!

(Translated by Google) The entrance is between two houses, it does not have a sign so you have to be careful, it is a very beautiful, relaxing hike, the experience is incredible, you can take dogs 🐩, you have to do the walk. If you have a car 🚘 you have to find parking because you cannot park on the avenue, they close at 6:00 pm, there are slippery rocks, the rocks move, you have to be careful. Wonderful local park. Loads of picnic tables with built in barbecue grills. An enormous pool, soccer fields, playgrounds, mini-golf.  For me the best part is going on a quiet day to walk around the lakes and enjoy this swath of nature in the middle of yonkers. On a summer weekend, it's going to be crazy, but honestly if you go off-season there are people around but its generally quiet and a great place to take your kids and family for some outdoor time.

A small-ish picnic area on the edge of lake Kanawauke.  It probably parks about 40 cars, but there are maybe a dozen pinic tables and some benches along the lake. There are some paved trails that go through private cabins and if you cross the road you can head off towards the Bald Rocks. The boat launch is nice, you'll need a PPC sticker to launch your boat.

Generally quiet off-season, but expect it to be packed in the summer.

Pretty nature preserve with about 10+ miles of trail. Most are 1-3 miles, but you can combine to get some distance in.  They are definitely not "technical" trails, but they're also not groomed, so expected rocks and roots and a touch of rolling terrain. All in all its a pretty forest oasis where you can have a nice hike and enjoy the outdoors. Parking is $5 and the lots are fairly small, so keep that in mind.

During the sunmer they do super loud lawn work every weekday. Beware, it's insane since it echoes off the dam. Don't expect and peace.

A park located at the terminus of the Bronx River Bike Path. There are some great views from the top of the dam, and regularly scheduled events throughout the summer and around christmas.

Fun place to spend a couple of hours with young kids. See the pigs, goats, cows, turkeys and a few other animals. Great backdrop for some nice family photos. It's linked to a fairly long section of trails that goes into the surrounding hills.

Also check for kids events or the farmers market which is really nice.

Nice park, with a few miles of trails that connect to the Colonial Greenway.  If you're a runner,  you can string together a nice run without crossing any roads (follow the white star in blue circle if you want to take the Colonial...its about 13 miles long and has maps posted at access points)

Pretty nice beach, with large grass section for picnicing. It's definitely not the most peaceful, and there can be a lot of goose poop in the sand. The whole time we were there we heard very loud engine noise which may have been the boats just past the swimming area.

A nice park with three separate but connected sections that gives each one a cozier feel. There is a handicap friendly playground, baseball and basketball fields and some picnic tables nestled in small clearings to give you a touch of privacy

Surprisingly diverse if small nature preserve. Trails are mostly rough (that's a compliment) and you've got forest, a quarry, scattered benches, and some cool structures. Downside is parking is very limited, so you may have to wait

Beware coming on a weekday...always some kind of lawn work and loud machinery.

Very nice waterfront park. Some nice picnic spots and huge fields if you want to kick the soccer ball around. It can get pretty crowded.

A local treasure. Nice trails that aren't too easy or too hard. You feel like you're deep in the woods. Do the blue loop and add an out and back across the road next to the Charles and you can get 3-4 miles easy.
Small old school, very old school, arcade. Small kids tend to enjoy the carousel and some of the games. They make you pay for adults to accompany children on the carousel, which is a bit of a scam.
dislikes: Additional charge for adults on carousel

reviews_attraction.text: A pair of cute lakes with about 2 miles of trail surrounding. Walking the dam wall is kinda fun. I've seen both deer and fox here in the mornings, so if you're lucky you may have an encounter.
Pretty trails overlooking the river. A little over a mile to hook into Croton Aqueduct trail, and a bit farther to Rockefeller Preserve. Bikes are not permitted and parking is VERY limited.
Huge parking lot with a few trailheads to get you into the hills of Harriman Park. Not lots of picnic area and gets packed during festivals. Paid parking during the summer season
A small hidden gem with great playgrounds for the kids, farm animals (and bald eagles!), as well as some simple hiking trails. Great place for an afternoon with the kids.
Small parking lot on Lake Sebago, with a boat launch. You cab access a couple of trails here. Not good for picnic space. Swimming not allowed and boating by permit only.

Cute little nature walk tucked at the end of a dead end street.
Should be peaceful but the sounds of leaf blowers permeate the whole place on a weekday.
Nice spot with a gorgeous view of the harbor. Beach is somewhat small but if you want picnic tables, some shade and a patch of sand, you're good to go.
Fun nature center to bring the kids. Everyone is lovely and helpful. Trails are easy but accessible and nice for a leisurely stroll.
Small, kid friendly park with great views. The riverwalk is nice for a stroll and its been pretty quiet whenever I've visited.
Great park for hiking or trail running. Trails are technical in a running sense, but no massive climbs, especially for hikers.
Fantastic family friendly beach. Non locals pay a high daily rate, so be prepared.  Great movie nights in the summer as well.
Small local aquarium, but lots of fun for younger kids. Parking is a couple of blocks away. Worth a few hours of your time.
Small preserve with about 8miles of marked trail. Two peaks to climb with great views of the lake from Cat summit

The oldest continuous operating art museum in the US.  The museum buildings and grounds reflect the gilded age of the area, when industrialists who built factories, brought wealth and arts back to their towns for their people.  May be the proximity to Boston, this museum is often overlooked.

You will find European and American arts over many periods here in its permanent exhibits.  Most of the important periods are well presented.  The rolling contemporary exhibits are well thought out  and laid out beautifully throughout the years.

The museum location is conducive for exploring many other attractions of the area.  Family can easily spend 3-4 hours exploring this museum.  One of a must stop in Hartford.

Good museum in the heart of Philadelphia.   Its permanent exhibit is quite extensive cover both Eastern and Western parts of the world.  Many exhibits are transported from the distance land to be rebuilt and restored on site.

One can spend at least half a day here to cover the main building and the other two buildings nearby.  On a nice day, the steps of the museum attracts many tourists running up and down pretending to be Rocky in training for the Heavyweight championship.   There is a statue of Rocky on the bottom of the steps for selfie and picture.

First Sunday of the month is "Pay as you wish" day.

Staff is very helpful and well informed.   One of the must see of the area.

The hallowed ground of the American Revolution war, where Washington won the decisive battle against the British.  It is a battlefield, devoid of large buildings and grandious monuments, left like what it was, empty space for all to take in of that fateful January 3 in 1777.  The field is quite suitable for walking and running.

The colonnade memorial was very solemn and symbolic as it was transported from the house of General Mercer who died on this field, and in the back of this memorial was the mass grave of both British and American soldiers.

The vastness of the place captured the spirit.   You can easily spend an hour here.

One of the nicer state park in New York state or perhaps in any state.  The view along the river is breathtaking, the trails along the river are well marked and maintained.  All three main falls are easy to get to.  At the middle fall, there is a nice inn, people can take a seat on its veranda or wander around on its front lawn.  The middle fall is only a few steps away.

It is a big park with numerous entrances.  All trails are easily accessed either by foot or by car.  It also have campgrounds and lodges for rent.  Many pavilions around for picnic or family gathering.

A truly nice park for everyone to enjoy the outdoors.

A small museum featuring the works of three generations of the Wyeth family.   The collection is very extensive,  showcasing the illustration style of art that the Wyeths are known for.

Beautiful layout, one can go through the permanent exhibit in three floors with ease.  Special exhibit in the same style is quite good and well presented.

The museum is situated along the bank of the Brandywine river, gives it an airy feel.  A family can spend a few hours here very easily.   Children can burn off their energy by running around on its ground.

Staff is knowledgeable and attentive.  A must see in the area.

If you like Norman Rockwell, then this is the museum for you.

The museum has most of the important works from Rockwell, laid out in chronological order.  It also has all of the covers of the Saturday Evening Post in exhibit in the lower level.  A very small exhibit devoted to contemporary artists that operated in the same illustrate world.

The museum has such a beautiful ground.  The illustrator's studio is relocated nearby.
Staff was so friendly and helpful.  Its admission is high for what it provides.  We breezed through in such a short time, and may not be back anytime soon.

One of a better science museum in the country.  It has an IMAX theatre, a planetarium, and numerous open "lab" areas for live demonstrations and experiments.  Its rolling exhibits are top-notch.  We have enjoyed the terracotta warriors last year, and this year the Vikings.  Food court is clean and spacious, you can also bring your packed lunch there.  Parking is a bit pricey, as its location is in the heart of the city.  Families can easily spend half a day there.

A "twin" with the Natural History museum.  It is also beautiful, but may be not in the same league with his twin.  Nevertheless, it has many exhibits about human development/progression.  The Mayan exhibit is well done, and the "world we live in" exhibit is great as well.
The neat thing about having a joint building allows one to move seamlessly from one museum to another.  It did break up the monotonous for us, and make the trip quite interesting.
likes: Specific Exhibits (Mayan, world we live in)

reviews_attraction.text:
Excellent arboretum, managed by University of Pennsylvania.  The trees and plants are being built in the landscape.  They are well marked by common and scientific names, making it a pleasure to walk around and learn about plants.  The ground is well kept.  The staff is helpful.

The "out on the limbs" exhibit is popular with young children and adults alike.

Family can spend 3 or 4 hours to explore.  A place to spend with children on a nice day...

Beautiful park with multiple entry points.  Many trails along the Galena lake, suitable for walking, running, and biking.  The trails are paved and well maintained.  There are plenty of shades for rest and picnic.  Boat rental would allow anyone to get on the water to fish or just simply enjoy time in the open air with some cool breeze from the water.
Clean bathrooms, plenty of parking.  Good place for a family to get out and enjoy the outdoors.
likes: Suitable for various activities (walking, running, biking)

reviews_attraction.text:
Museum built on the boarding house of the American impressionist painters in the beginning of the twentieth century.  The house has some paintings of the resident artists and their contemporaries.  There is also a modern gallery that houses the rotating exhibit.

It is a nice and compact museum.  Have some activities for children year round.  Pleasant environment for a family to visit and have a nice walk along the river.

Good science museum in the New England area.  Many in-house exhibits, like electric and mathematics are outstanding.  The annual special exhibition is often grand and elaborated.
Staff is nice and attentive.  Museum store is very nice and well-stocked.   Food court has a variety of foods for adults and children alike.  A family can easily spend a few hours here.
Good location.  A bit pricey due to its location.

Small but a well kept aquarium.   Only aquarium with beluga whale in the area.  Good place for a family to spend a few hours in the afternoon.  The mini theater has a short movie for an additional fee, "free" for members.  Its 4-D movie is quite good and entertaining, especially for young children.  The seal show is interesting and is a hit for most.  The staff is friendly and helpful.

Battlefield of the American Revolution War.  Beautiful ground with many landmarks and monuments to tell the story.  Self guided tours are available.  Tours are better by cars or by bikes as this is a very large battlefield.  Many came here to use the ground for recreation, i.e. walking, running or biking.  Good place for families to enjoy the outdoors or simply taking in a picnic.

Great state park, having many things for families to do at a minimum cost.  One can go swimming, hiking for free, and camping is available for an affordable fee.  Day trip can be had for free.  Swimming in a spring-fed lake or hiking along the water edge to the falls and to the boulder field.
A worthwhile trip for families who want to spend their time outdoors...

Nice park in a natural setting.  Large rock formations scattered over a large swatch of land.  Good walking trails, taking through the woods with many rock statues and formations.   Good place for recharge and enjoy the nature.
Trails are well maintained.   Nice picnic benches and quiet nooks in many areas in the park.

Nice museum in the middle of the old fashioned New England village.  The structure is quite small.  You have to pay a small fee to get in and see the inside.  The ground is free.
It a well maintained light house on a nice well kept ground.
A good find, and a pleasant stop for all ages.

Quite good small museum.  Having permanent and rotating exhibits.  Interesting artifacts about Soviet Union space program.  Some paintings of the eighteenth and nineteenth European painters.
Large ground, good parking.  Good place for a stop in Greenwich area.

Good museum for children under 12 (my opinion).  Many hands on activities for the kids.  Sufficient bathrooms and "rest" places for parents.  Decent food option.  You can practically spend a whole day here.  Lots of activities to keep active kids busy.

Historic canal boat ride and canal historical museum.  Nice park along the river and the canal.  Good walking and bike path.  Plenty of parking and rest area for family picnics.  Nice playgrounds for little kids.
likes: Activities: Walking paths, bike paths, playgrounds

reviews_attraction.text: Nice modern exhibition building of the Mystic Seaport.  It is the main building to be used as a main entrance and exhibit the main attractions of the museum.  Beautiful lay out.
Nice area, good blend of historic sites with commerce.  Plenty of places to see, lots of restaurants to grab a bite to eat, and many stores to browse and shop.
Nice walk along the beach.  Walk path is about 1.25 miles long.  Very popular in the winter as the concrete gives up heat, takes the bite out of the cold.
Well run museum, showing the extensive works of Yale educational staff.  Its dinosaur exhibit is quite impressive and worth a visit alone.
Good place to go for a walk in town. Some buildings in various stages of restoration can be seen here.

Naval Air Station Wildwood is a great take.  A beautiful old hangar with some amazing planes. The kids loved touching the planes and sitting in some.  A lot of the planes and helicopters had stairs that let you either see it up close or walk through.  Nice short video about the history of the Air Station, which helped put it in perspective for everyone.   The kids also loved the simulators.  I would suggest setting up more photograph opportunities to help advertise NAS Wildwood.  There are plenty of opportunities. The kids love getting into the cockpit and putting on helmets.  I would have liked to take home a NAS Wildwood challenge coin, but they are only for members and we were visiting from out of state. Short of that, it would have been great to get a magnet or another keepsake that said NAS Wildwood. Maybe a patch or something. Overall a great place to visit with a lot more potential. All three types of planes used in the shooting of Top Gun are there. On top of the military history, I think the pop culture angle will also be appreciated if you point it out in the hangar.

Great indoor water park with 5 water slides, a lazy river, a surf simulator, an indoor and outdoor hot tub, a pool with basketball hoops, plenty of seating, a retractable roof, a bar, lockers, cabanas and an attached arcade.  The kids loved running from pool to pool and the lifeguards were very good. The indoor temperature was incredibly warm even when outside was just about freezing.  There was about a 15 minute wait to ride on the surfing simulator while we were there on a weeknight during Massachusetts school vacation.  The only complaint I had was that I saw many people carrying carriages over the bridges that went over the lazy river. I'm surprised that there was not easier access. There was also a lack of decent food close to the waterpark.

Visited with two kids (8-9). The building is beautiful and it's has a very nice layout. Everything is brightly lit. Lots of history to soak up. The kids for bored quickly with the displays, but loved the interactive displays. They liked the jump measurement and the virtual basketball video game and the pretend sportscaster set up. By far, they liked the shooting baskets the best. They could have played for hours shooting at all the different style baskets including the peach baskets. They also enjoyed the slam dunk area. There's a couple of burger places close by that are family friendly. The kids probably spent half a day in the museum.

Great park with many different routes for running, walking, biking, fishing.  Some of the paths are paved, but others have a bit of rutting with some roots and a few steep sections with stair-like areas.  We were able to bike most of the paths, with a few sections that we had to walk the bikes up, but if you are experienced mountain-bikers, you could stay on.  Saw many people fishing in the canal. The trails aren't marked really well, but you are never at risk of getting lost in the park. Found plenty of parking and a few port-a-potties at entrances.  Well-maintained.

Beautiful campus designed by Frank Lloyd Wright.  They offer different length walking tours of the campus, with visits inside some amazing spaces. Like most of Wright's buildings, these are starting to crumble and are in need of maintenance. One of the gems is a brand new Wright building, built from his plans and to his specifications.  It was one of the only buildings by Wright that allowed you to touch everything and sit on chairs.  The campus gets a bit hot over the summer with not a lot of shade.  It would be great to see the central fountain in action.

Amusement park with many great roller-coasters for the 48" and taller kids. Free soda all over the park sounds good, but the bees were out in force.  The waterpark was a lot of fun, but the odd arrangement led to confusion over the entrances.  The amusement side of the park is very consolidated, so it was easy to walk from one side of the park to the other.  When we were there, some of the games were under-staffed.

Great hiking very close to Boston. Multiple entry points along Route 93. My favorite trail is the skyline trail that has many elevation changes. The kids enjoy going to Wright's Tower, which is an observation tower that has views of Boston. Plenty of different routes to keep you interested. Sheepfold even has an old soapbox style boyscout track that is no longer in use.

Great little museum.  Fun for young kids and adults. Inexpensive to buy a self-guided audio tour.  Fifteen minute video explains why the sub is there, then you get to walk through the submarine. Beware, there are a lot of tight spaces and climbing through some of the portals is tough if you are taller or need assistance walking.   A nice stop on the way to Portsmouth.
dislikes: Difficult for those needing walking assistance

reviews_attraction.text: The group taking care of the house has done an incredible job with the visitor center, the rebuilding of the secondary buildings and the preservation of the original building. This was my second visit and first time seeing the completed kitchen restoration.  The guides are very knowledgeable and the one hour tour accommodated older kids (7-9) extremely well.

Fun day for the kids. Plenty of Gators up close. The price is a bit high, and there are many things inside the park that cost money, but once inside, there are plenty of things for the kids to do. The kids love the splash park. There are a few nice observation towers. Beware that the back of the park gets hot and doesn't have much shade.

Great park that we didn't realize was there.  The kids wanted to see Lady Liberty, but we were running out of time. We stopped at the park and got a great view of the city and Lady Liberty right at sunset.  The park is very open, with lots of lighting and a broad stretch along the water for walking, biking or picture taking.
likes: Suitable for walking, biking, and photography

reviews_attraction.text: Small inexpensive ski area that is nice for kids that are learning. Lessons weren't that expensive and were easily booked. Most of the paths were visible from the bottom, which was good for us to allow the kids to ski freely without us. Small lodge, but food was decent and a small bar was open part of the day.

The museum has restored a few rooms in the original house back to the time that Emily lived in the house. The tour is more about the story though. The grounds are a nice stroll also. If you are a fan of Emily, you will enjoy it, but kids are quickly bored and there isn't a lot to see.

Very nice playground for kids of all ages. Large, with plenty of open space and completely fenced in. It is tough to find the entrance because you can't park at the hardware store, but instead have to travel up Andover road and park between the baseball field and the playground.

Self guided tour, with a few nice historic displays. Good explanation of the process on the walls with accompanying videos. Kids moved through relatively quickly, only stopping at the interactive experiences. The most boring part was the viewing of the actual minting process.

The kids enjoy the rotating events that are held at the museum including train events and lego events.  The space has some fun areas for the younger kids to play all the time.  The downstairs has a permanent train set up that the kids enjoy.

Great experience. Friendly and knowledgeable guides. Awesome collection of firearms with historical information. Difficult to get to since it is located on the campus of a technical institute and the signage is not clear.

Easily accessible after 5:00 without a timed ticket, the bell is in a beautiful glassed in room overlooking independence hall. Knowledgeable staff were willing to answer any questions and interact with the guests.

Well maintained small zoo. The tropical forest was especially well done and the penguin exhibit put you up next to the penguins, although it did seem like it was too small an exhibit for the penguins.
Beautiful museum with some great pieces. Surprisingly large and we'll laid out. Some great rotating selections also. Located on a beautiful wooded campus. Spacious and a great space to walk through.
Good experience. Appeared to be listed as a difficult room, but wasn't as difficult as some others. Very nice room to share with the family. Tweens had fun. Owner was very nice.
Great aquarium. Much more than I expected. More similar to a sea world type park, but smaller. Very interactive. A bit expensive, but the tickets are good for three days.
Beautiful cars. Amazing Frank Lloyd Wright Gas Station.  I'm glad I happened upon it. Definitely stop in if possible. You shouldn't miss it for the price.
I haven't been here in many years. It looks like they have grown. The place is extremely busy. Relatively organized, but still too hectic.
Very spacious park with a few elevation changes. A few nice long slides for children. Picnic tables and some trees for shade.

Great park! Lots of unique spots for kids and adults. Our favorite was the yellow slides, but also seesaw, sand area, rope climbing things, and our activities.  Also basketball courts, grass fields, ample benches. Street and garage parking. Also, across from an elementary school with even more play ground equipment. Short walk to the trail.

This is one of our favorite parks! It is a working farm, so there are several barns with animals (pigs, cows, sheep, goats, chickens, horses, peacocks, etc.) And old farm equipment. There is also indoor and outdoor horse /equestrian trails and rings. Lastly, there is a nice playground, restrooms, and ample parking. Highly recommend!

Beautiful park. There is a nice path through the woods that goes into the marsh. Several places to stop and rest (if needed) along the path. There's also a nature center and pavilions (though closed at time of our visit due to covid 19). We saw lots of animals - turtles, frogs, birds, butterflies, and even small lizards.

We had a lot of fun earlier this week on a pirate cruise!  We got there about a half hour early, which allowed for face painting, tattoos, and dressing in pirate gear. My kids had tons of fun - especially with the pirate battle and the treasure chest at the end. Crew was very entertaining for kids and adults.

Great park, lots for you to do!  We bought train tickets in advance and did that as well as a nearby playground and ice cream treat. Theres also a carousel,  marina, mini golf, driving range, and golf course, as well as lots of other options. Lots of signs to help direct you, and ample parking throughout.

Very nice park down by 4 mile run and the bike trail.  Big picnic pavilion with bathrooms, two play areas with slides, swings, sand box and benches tables. Close to the dog park too. Some limited parking is available near the park. Other parking is available at the top of the hill, or near the dog park.

Great park with pretty new equipment!  There are two play areas- one designed for kids 2 to 5 and another 5 to 12. There is also a rope climbing area, as well as swings, balance type logs and toys. Also a big beach volleyball court, picnic pavilion,  and lots of trees and grass to run around in.

Huge park in the heart of Arlington.  We spent our time in the fenced in kids area, but there are also beach volleyball courts, baseball field, and huge soccer field. Also areas where you can just hangout under a tree to read or nap. Small parking lot and street parking is available.

Great neighborhood park!  The play area is self enclosed, with 2 climbing structures. There are also picnic tables and benches. Public bathrooms and parking spots are available.  Theres also a basketball court and baseball field and picnic tables and structures. 5 stars for sure!

There is a great kids playground at this nature center! Nice parking lot. The nature center itself has about 10 display cases with turtles, snakes,  etc. We also walked around the pond (nice walking path) and explored the woods a bit on some well marked trails.

Nice park with a basketball court, 4 tennis courts, and a baseball field. There are also picnic tables and grill, and a new play area for kids 2-12 years old. No bathroom, though there was a portapotty there today. Park on the street.

Great community center! Open and free. Recently renovated library with displays for adults and older kids, and a beautiful kids area. Highly recommend visiting! Theres also a super cool boat pilot simulator in the kids area.

Great park, with a big play area for kids. There is also a baseball field, bathroom, basketball court, creek to throw rocks in, and lots of picnic tables. Lots of shade so perfect for a warm or sunny day.
Great park. Nice lake - you can rent kayaks and paddle boats for a small fee. There are lots of park benches, picnic tables. There's also a small playground with swings, mini golf, and a carousel.
Great park!  There's a big open field for soccer or running around. Two to three at areas for kids of different ages to climb and slide, and a nice picnic pavilion. Ample street parking.
Great museum!  Only a few steps from the White House, and two short blocks from the metro station. Lots of food options nearby and there is a small museum store on the ground floor.
Fun neighborhood park. There are swings, basketball court, and two play areas for big and small kids. Also lots of shade and benches/chairs for adults. Highly recommend this park!
Very nice nature center. Several live frogs and snakes to look at. Other interactive exhibits with animal fur, sounds, bones. There are also costumes and toys for the kids to try.
This is a great play ground and park! Lots of benches in the shade. there's also a picnic pavilion, t ball field, and a couple different swing and slide combinations.
Lovely park with several different play areas and structures for kids. Including slides, swings, picnic area, climbing stuff. Lots of street parking too.
Fun park, with two big play areas, two sets of swings, a big picnic pavilion, soccer field, trail through the woods, big parking lot and port a potties.
Beautiful park. Very nice soccer field and pavilion, with tennis courts and a kids play ground.  Nearby dog park as well. Lots of parking nearby.
Fun playground with a lot of unique climbing items for kids - rock walls, ropes, slides, and built in hills. Lots of benches for the adults too!
This is a great spot to watch boats and people. There is a small parking lot that fills up. People like to come here to fish.
Three baseball fields and a nice open space for soccer and running around.  Plenty of parking. Portable bathroom as well.

This is a true gem.  It is off the beaten path and doesn't seem like a likely location for an outstanding museum.

The stained glass collection is incredible.  Every piece has a lot of information that helps appreciation.   Kids were encouraged to touch the glass.  We all learned a lot about the glass.

The time section is equally incredible.  My family didn't have the background to truly appreciate the depth of the collection. I will need to do more research and return.  The time pieces were incredible but ultimately the shear number overwhelmed my smallest children.

Wow.  We have now visited Chicago twice specifically to visit this musuem (and eat pizza).  My kids and I have spent 3 days in this museum and have only scratched the surface.

I highly suggest you get a membership.  The tours and activities are not to be missed.  The WOW tour is a great way to start.  It gives you an overview of the entire museum.

The baby chicks are my kids favorite.  The weather exhibition is exceptional in explaining key phenomenon.

My entire party agreed this was the best escape room experience we have encountered.  My children and I tackled the conspiracy room and despite the 3 of us not finishing the puzzle we had a great time. A party of 5+ would increase chances of completing all the puzzels.   Each puzzle was well though through and was challanging but solveable.  Hints were available when necessary.

Run was well run.  Thank you.

We will return.

I didn't have enough time to begin to do this place justice.  I also was traveling with a six year old.  I had heard amazing reviews but given constraints hesitated. In the end decided to take my little one.  The museum was incredible and exceeded expectations.  It was able to engage my tired daughter.  I will return and spend several days here.

We are from out of town but decided to visit today and became members.  This is a well managed science museum.  My son's favorite was the aquarium.  There is a good mix of topics and thoughtful displays. Many of them supplemented the items my son was studying in school.  The museum was clean and seemed to be following good covid protocols.

Amazing collections.  An encyclopedic collection.   We spent an entire day but only saw a small fraction of the exhibits.  The free guided tours were exceptional.  They were not crowded.  Food options were limited and long lines and limited seating.  A new dining option is opening soon on the second floor that might mitigate that some.

This donate what you can afford entrance is a great musuem for children. It has a lot of hands on activities for children that help them contextualize the content.  Staff was helpful and knowledgeable. The exhibits were  relevant and well maintained.

This was a much better way to understand this history than the national park nearby

A nice place ground and green space by the parking area.  The highlights of this park require a nice trek along a well marked path (a little under 2miles) to a beach.   It isn't a very big beach since the cliff sides are off limits to the public but the main section is a nice place to play and Fi do shark teeth.
