In any other country this would be a cathedral.  Inside is an incredible space.  Soaring columns. Amazing high celing.

We have been members for many years.  Kids enjoy the building activities and the leading stations and packs.

Many of the exhibits are well done don't appeal to all ages.

this was a highlight of my trip with my 6 year old daughter.  she loved it.  she got to feed and get close to many animals that she had only seen from afar.   Make sure you budget buying the biggest set of feed.  Being able to feed the animals dramatically increases the experience.

The national park ranger made the experience.  We asked about ranger led talks and while there were none scheduled the ranger volunteered to give one.  Offered a talk, a QA session or hybrid.  We choose hybrid and learned a lot.  Helped us understand what we saw in the exhibits.

A very cool museum. We spent a half a day learning about natural history.  This museum has a good selection of exhibits.

The second largest egg collection in USA was a surprise.  Good shell exhibits.  A few dinosaurs.

Kids enjoyed.  Not a lot of hands on.

Amazing art. We especially enjoy the children programs.  Yesterday my kids spent hours reproducing masters.  They enjoyed coloring and studying each of the great works.

We are members despite living in Maryland and only getting there periodically.

Family loved the nativity sets from around the world as part of the festival of lights.

The grounds are beautifully decorated.  The staff are extremely friendly.  Parking can be a challenge but people are there to help and direct you
likes: Attraction Type (Festival of lights, Decorated grounds)

reviews_attraction.text:
An amazing small museum that has impressive collections.  Good specialization and comprehensive exhibits.

Children room is lacking but a major expansion has been announced.

Good sculpture garden.
an amazing monument with a great set of history to understand.   Also one of better spots in DC for Pokemon go.  Saw rangers leading groups and the rangers and the groups all playing.
My kids had fun here.  The museum has great bones.  Lots of fun areas.  The museum was crowded when we were there.  Also several areas were not functional.

Beautiful place.  We were here for family pictures.

In addition when the park is having field days they have wonderful activities for the  whole family.

This is a gem.

Limited parking but it looked like they open a field for additional parking when busy.

The trails were well maintained and marked.
This is small park that maximizes it's useful of space.  Has a extensive (for its size play area) and benches.  Multiuse field and tennis court
Great museum.  Another gem that allows a good mix of interactive and informative displays.  It has a lot of unique items    my kids enjoyed it.
We enjoyed all the staff pop up areas.  The special exhibits were interesting but expensive.  Museum is showing its age and lack of maintance.
Great place for kids.  Lots of levels of fun. Many different type of play. My favorite are the staff lead projects or activities.
We are regular visitors from dc. Lots of fun learning for the children.   Not huge, but big enough for lots of fun.
It was wet and rainy but that didn't decrease the fun of the BBQ event.  While there we found a Geocache.

The Museum of The City of New York is an educational museum for anyone interested in the history and future of New York City.

There are 4 floors of exhibits encompassing everything from the rise of New York as a Dutch trading colony to the near collapse during the Great Depression to the aftermath of 9/11 and Hurricane Sandy. Includes throughout is everything from the founding of Wall Street to Jackie Robinson and the incredible rise of the jazz scene in Harlem.

There is also a great exhibit on public art throughout the city and all of the installments throughout the years. My favorite was the field of wheat that was planted near the base of the World Trade Center Towers in the 80s.

The South Street Seaport Museum is a small but quaint little museum that provides the history and evolution of the South Street Seaport. While the museum shouldn't take you more than 30 minutes to peruse, the best part of the museum is touring the WaverTree and Lightship Ambrose tied up to the nearby docks.

Touring the ships is not handicap friendly due to the tight passageways and number of steps on each ship, but is a great experience for those interested in maritime history and the history of New York.

This museum/experience is a nice surprise. Though it may not look like much, this museum is about the tour and the experience.

Our guide was amazing and brought the gangsters to life through her storytelling and charisma. I learned details about Pretty Boy Floyd, John Dillinger, Baby Face Nelson, and several others that I never knew.

The tour ends in a functioning speak easy below, so if you're of age, come thirsty.

Incredibly engaging and informative tour, great for all ages.

On the tour, you go through each of the steps necessary to produce a bottle of Kentucky Bourbon. You even get a chance to bottle your own bourbon complete with your thumb print in wax on top of the bottle.

There is also a great exhibit for the Independent Stave Company on the production of these new white oak, well charred, bourbon barrels.

Best concert venue on planet Earth! Nothing beats taking in an epic show at Red Rocks on a nice summer night under the stars. Something about playing Red Rocks causes artists to perform some of their best sets and play outstanding sets.

Even if you're not taking in a concert, go visit to take in the beauty of the venue. This place is also great for hiking and workouts.

The Butterfly Pavilion is a magical place. This is a great place to bring the whole family.

They've got insects for everyone! From spiders (caged), to a live bee hive, to the rainforrest wsquw pavilion, there's something for everyone.

The highlight by far is the hundreds of butterflies that foot around you as you walk through their makeshift habitat.

If you enjoy art, then MoMA is a must! MoMA is a well laid out, easy to navigate, space with incredible works from Van Gough, Picasso, and Warhol among many others! If you're into art, I would leave yourself 3 to 4 hours to visit.

Don't forget to visit "The Starry Night" and "Gold Marilyn Monroe" while there.

The Morgan Library is worth a visit. As a New Yorker, it's fascinating to learn about J.P. Morgan's extensive collection of antiquities, many of which are used in other New York museums.

The library is amazing.  Make sure you identify the secret passageways by which books are displayed.

incredible experience for those seeking deep powder and fun terrain in Steamboat!

The guides are always great and now the terrain like the back of their hand. Booking a private snowcat for a large group of comparable skiers/boarders is the way to go if you can fill the snowcat.

Make sure to look to the skies the week before September 11th and the evening of September 11th.

This tribute is beautiful and moving. If you get the chance to visit the staging area, make sure you do so. There are 88 8,000 Watt lights (44 per tower) that make up the tribute.

This iconic New York landmark is great for running or biking in between China Town and DUMBO. It's significantly less crowded than it's southern neighbor, the Brooklyn Bridge and provides unobstructed views of DUMBO, the Brooklyn Bridge, and Lower Manhattan.

Great fun for the entire family. Late fall is ideal for Apple Picking, though their cidery and distillery are worth a visit any time of year.

After picking apples, go try their Chai Vodka with some of their delicious cider for a great fall adult beverage.

Incredible views of the Brooklyn and Manhattan bridges as well as of Manhattan.

Great place for picnics, strolls, romantic evenings, and taking a moment to enjoy this beautiful city.

Summer weekends can get crowded, but still a great place to check out.

This museum shows what life was like for Jews during the holocaust. I would recommend starting at the top and working your way down.

Don't forget to check out the Garden of Stones, a living memorial on the second floor.

Bryant Park is a fun reprieve from the hustle and bustle of New York City. Make sure you check out the park midday Wednesdays during the summer when various Broadway show companies perform songs from their shows.

If you're a baseball fan, this is a must visit.

The second floor shares a visual history of the game and all of the amazing stats and records of the game.

The hall itself is filled with some amazing players!
Dirty park with nasty water in the heart if downtown New York. This park does provide a fun little oasis from the hustle and bustle of the tall buildings and Brooklyn bridge nearby though.
I would recommend a minimum of 2 hours for the Intrepid, but would suggest 3.5 if you really want to see everything and fully learn about the ship and all of the exhibits.

Beautiful views of lower Manhattan and plenty of space to enjoy the outdoors.

You can get there by taking the yellow ferry from the WTC Ferry Terminal (Cost is $7)
The Rock Center Tree is always crowded, but worth the visit. I'd recommend sneaking in from 49th or 50th instead of trying to get in from 5th ave.

Great place for a run or a walk. The outer loop provides you with decent mileage.

I'd recommend going before dark or running with a buddy.

Great little park with plenty of grass, benches, and beautiful flowers.

Great place for a picnic of live in Battery Park City or FiDi.
This is a great space to gather, play tennis, kickball, ultimate frisbee, soccer, or just enjoy the park at the base of the foothills.

Great location, easy to get to, and always an incredible atmosphere no matter the event.

Plan ahead as beer and food is pricey.
Go later in the evening during the week when most of the crowds have dissipated. Worth the walk to the top.

Very nice place to drive around and see the wildlife and scenery.  One of the best birding areas to go, we always see something amazing, unusual or rare. The visitor center is nice inside. Best to go when the bugs aren't swarming or else your stuck in your car.  We couldn't get to any of the towers without getting bit up, it's expected this time of year. Definitely will go back in the fall.
dislikes: Limited access to towers due to insects

reviews_attraction.text: Old Pinnacle Road is mostly closed off in sections.  It’s a nice place once you walk to the top of the hill to overlook the dam. We also saw some Eagle nests on the islands there.  Not many places put razor wire on power line supports to keep people from climbing, probably why the gates are closed. There’s trails that go around up there as well.

This place is amazing. The visitor center is the nicest place I’ve ever visited of any parks. Lost of taxidermy, info and a great indoor bird blond setup with lots of Nikon binoculars. The wildlife is plentiful, the walking trails are nice and they have Snow Geese almost every year.  They do a great job maintaining everything.

The tower was closed to anyone not using the elevator for the Maid of the Mist boat tour. We couldn’t even walk out on the regular part unless we bought a ticket to the boat tour and waited 2-3 hours in a very long line. Next time were doing the tour, during the week, off season. Looks like a lot of fun.

What a spectacular place to see the sunset over the water.  It’s an easy walk to the beach and they have picnic tables under pavilions. Parking is limited though. Seeing the boats go in and out are fun, and the dolphin watch tours tend to attract dolphins so I got to see them from a few feet away.

Nice if you’re a local, otherwise it’s $10-$20 for out of state visitors. There is a barbed wire fence around most of the perimeter to keep people out or in, but what about lost hikers trying to find a way out?  Otherwise it’s a nice place with lots of trails and areas to boat and fish.

This is a great place to visit. Nice gift shop with really good coffee and very nice knowledgeable people working there. The trails are wide to walk around with lots of information stands and lots of different stuff to see. It connects to other trails as well.

It’s $8 to get into the park, another $15 to walk around the Fort, if you can get in before they close at 4pm. It’s a nice size park to walk around or ride a bike. We were there on a weekend and it was empty. The town is quaint and nice to walk down as well.
Nice place for local residents but $10-20 for us out of towners to visit. Camping looks cool, beach area looks nice and looks like plenty of water to boat around. Only a couple of trails to hike.
Nice little park to walk around on the trails, take the dog out or just chill. Not too many people around and the benches by the water is nice. Pavilion next to volleyball court is nice.
Some of best maintained trails I've seen in the region.  Everything is well mapped and marked. Lots of different type of trails too. We rode for hours and missed quite a few trails.
This place is amazing, make sure you get there early enough to see everything inside and out. I'm amazed that's it's free and the staff there are very knowledgeable and friendly.
Love this place, it’s worth the drive to see the 22 waterfalls, walk the trails and see the lake. They have kayaking there and don’t allow gas boats, electric motors only.
I loved the walking trails around this park. It's scenic around the water and right across from market commons, where you can rent bikes to ride all the other trails.
We love this place, the staff is great and very involved in the community. They're always changing up exhibits which makes getting a membership work the purchase.
Neat place to hike and see the tubs under the waterfalls.  A little hidden and usually not very busy there, although it can attract the wrong crowd at times.
Has some nice trails to walk around, a few pavilions and an interesting history lesson. Very nice landscape.  Can get busy, but always plenty of parking.
Very cool piece of history.  Nice walking trail around with a field of Blue Bells. Just seeing this structure and what remains around it is amazing.
This place is amazing! Reminds me of Bombay Hook a little. Can get buggy at times. Well worth the trip to drive around and see the sights.
What an amazing place inside and out, and it’s FREE!  Didn’t expect it to be this nice, clean and organized. Easy access, and lots to see.
Lots of local talent on display here. It's worth stopping in and seeing everything, I enjoyed it. The people there are nice.
Very nice park with a cool walking trail around the reservoir. The trail connects to other local trails and  to white clay.
This place is great, lots of walking trails and a driving tour. The beach on the south side is very nice.
Neat park, like people mentioned, easy to get to. Wish it wasn’t so dry when we were there 3 weeks ago.
We frequent this place a lot for the different events up there and just in general to see the stacks.

The village was spectacular, complete with a young bride to be, a shrewish older woman, and a lot of men with fun tools and great costumes.  Most had great dialogue-we learned many things.  Heft one of those muskets!
Hot and dusty, would do it all over again!  Loved it. Well worth the price.
Suggestions:  go early in the day to the village.  The heat is intense, shade mostly in the homes.  Spend time in the Native American area asking questions,  poking into all the bags and bins, and watchingthe work.  These folks don't "stay in character", which is so great.  They can tell you about their costumes and who made what.  Those loinclouts are freaking awesome.  They make meals and eat them.

Blue star family discount. Thank you!
Not easy for wheeled conveyances, we saw a wheelchair struggling going down the hill that is "main st" in the village.  Paths are gravelly.  Lesser slope outside  the palisade, smoother surface, but hot in the sun.  Lots of walking.
One of the best historical experiences we've had in the USA.

Native American folks were the best part, and I grew up in the West with lots of tribal experiences. Really informative and spontaneously willing to share information.  And handsome people!

The crafters are knowledgeable and mostly kind.  One apparently forgot we were paying to be there.   Talk to the Roach makers!  Delicate and exquisite products, fun to find out their quills come from my home state bc our porkies have longer quills!

We did not explore the farm fields and shore area, but wish we had. Definitely worth the trip!
likes: Facilities & Services: Blue star family discount
Activities: Interactive experiences, Costume details, Craft demonstrations, Knowledgeable staff, Native American area
dislikes: Facilities & Services: Inaccessible for wheeled conveyances, Gravelly paths, Limited shade

reviews_attraction.text:
"Lake" is a generous word.  This is a large pond. It is lovely, but small.  I don't believe gas motors are allowed, and there was a burning ban in effect.  Probably smart because in just our short visit, we saw 2 spots where idiots had dumped used charcoal.   The picnic area is first, with a small jungle gym, large grassy areas, picnic tables delightfully tucked among the trees, and several shelters.  We saw wheelchair accessible tables and toilets, but not much pavement other than the very steep hill to the beach and the campground loop.
The campground is gorgeous and offers very nice cabins as well.  Lots of foliage separates sites. But this is a BUSY place.  Most sites had at least 3 cars in them!  That's a lot of folks.  There are camp hosts.
The beach is small, roped off, and fairly shallow.  Not much "sand", but grassy area, picnic tables, and native plants line the shore area.  There's a boat launch, and plenty of space to fish.  We saw translucent green fingerlings eagerly approaching every rock thrown in, but no one had large fish today.
There is a lovely trail around the lake.  It was a cool day, so no swimmers, but I had just read online that the water quality was suspect.  Check before you go.
We had the state park pass, so no fee, but there's a charge to use it.
The air smelled fresh and lively, but at least one of us reacted to either the cedar and/or the moulds in the air.

Recommendation: go early, make reservations if you want to camp, avoid weekends, and take ready to eat food or a gas grill.

Excellent park, built on a hillside near Old Downtown Sherwood.  Large, beautiful play structure near top of hill (and the street)was recently redone (summer 2018) and is now wheelchair accessible, a major plus.  Lots of access for those with vision, hearing, sensory disabilities as well.  Note pictures in older reviews are obsolete.
Bathrooms are near it, including a family one.  A macadam walkway curves down the hill to the bandshell, where there are tables and a picnic shelter. Nature trails lead through a wetlands, along a creek, depending on rainfall and time of year.  Parking lot is across the street.
Would give 5 stars if the lower park had toilets, hillside was developed more and had level,shaded spaces.
dislikes: Lack of toilets in lower park

reviews_attraction.text:
Fabulous place!  Grab a clipboard with questions...we were 6, so did both the easy and hard ones.  Now you have a focus for each area of this well-organized museum.  The navy member found all the military answers, the youngsters found the vehicle and toy ones, but it took a committee to find the newspaper price!  They actually do have a prize, too.  Make sure to wander down to the point and read plaques, too.
Don't forget to shut the front door and climb the tiny steps to the lighthouse.  There is a short, scary ladder at the top. The view is great.
Nice clerk, some art and souvenirs for sale.

Fabulous park.  Leave food, pets, noise, etc in the car.  Control your children.  A Japanese garden is a special, serene setting.
Dont think I've seen it the same two yrs running.  Bridges, entry, paths, pond all change dramatically from year to year.
My grown kids like to remember the Spirit-hindering bridge, the turtles, sitting under the falls, the perimeter path.
Be respectful and if taking formal photos, get permission first.
Last visit was level 4 air quality, but sitting under the leafy canopy one felt they could breathe. Truly one of Spokane's best elements.

Fabulous historical site.  Not a battlesite...important part of local history.  Reenactors are top notch, esp the blacksmiths.  Listen long enough and you can come away with an item they make on the spot.  The day we went the fur trading gal roughly told our 3 kids NOT TO TOUCH the furs...then stood there stroking the furs over and over.  Weirdst spot.  Carpenter was interesting, and our 8 yr old boy did not want to leave the cannons in the tower.  Well done, fun, beautifully kept.

Vista House offers great views of the Columbia, volunteers who are knowledgeable, history in words and pictures, gift shop, coffee, and time trzvel to the olden days.  Don't forget to check out the marble bathrooms!  Sunny days are best, but even rainy days are great.  On the historic waterfall route, parking might be a challenge, but well eorth the stop.
Climb the stairs to check out the views, saunter thru the tunnel in the basement to look over the rim.

Be ready to climb!  Gorgeous historical site, tiny silly gift shop, $5 gets you in for a year, but you can share the ticket.  The outside ofthe column depicts historical events, the inside holds winding metal stair.  Not for the noise-intolerant!  We had fun making loud yells.  Meet visitors from all over, have a picnic on the lawn, use the binocs to peek afar ($.25), or gawk at the bridge, Saddle Mt., etc.
Well worth the price.  Impressive.

Hidden gem of a park!
Google maps doesn't take you there easily, so look behind the Marriott.
Creative climbing, sliding, banging!
Sweet water recovery nature area to west, then the tiered grassy area.
Bathrooms and benches.  Lots of sun, some shade.
Won't tell you all that's here so your kids can explore and be surprised.
This is currently my favorite park for kids in Vancouver.

Great family activities for all ages.   Went on a rainy day and spent hours with elementary school kids and adults highly entertained.  Brain puzzles, science, things to build, animals, engineering, tons of things to do.  We bought the basic tickets and avoided special exhibits.  Memberships save you money, don't get you in free. We didn't get to all the stations or rooms.

Well worth the 5 buck entry fee.  Lovely blooms. Baby ducks and goslings, hawks, songbirds, etc.
Waterfalls, ponds, creeks and features abound.
Parking across the street @Reed College bc lot is small
There are gravel paths, so wheeled chairs might be challenging.
Restrooms with running water in center of park.
If you take food for the waterfowl, make sure it is healthy.

The OMSI exhibit was excellent.
Loved the bird viewing and feeding station.
Picnic area at rear, fountain out front.  Park nearby.  Lots of parking.  Loved the toads.  Younger kids might be easily bored, but older ones should like, especially if their adults act interested.
Was hard to know what was on loan and what belonged, but we will return.

Last winter we walked from the Fort side across, turned around just before the end.  Plants were leafless, you could see quite a bit of the area.
Late August, we walked from the river side up and over.  It was very hot, little shade, and hard to see much.  It's a lovely walk, but would prolly be more fun on a scooter or bike.

Nice grassy areas, small and medium kids playstructure, splashpad that works on 2 of 5 jets for about 30 seconds.  Big rock to climb (fake), tables and a semishade structure.  Didnt try bathrooms. 2 basketball courts.
Always some shade, walking path.
Would give more stars if waterpad worked and the missing swing was repaired.

We hit high tide and this geologic feature was spectacular.  My companions walked down and stood on the little ridge near the well.  They got fabulous photos.  I stayed atop the feature and enjoyed all the features simultaneously.  No whales in fall usually, but we saw one later at Depoe Bay.

Fabulous, has everything!  Except a pool.
Great splashpad, multiple playground structures of varied sizes/ages.
Playfields, nature walk, some shade, easy access for wheeled chairs.
You HAVE to give it a visit, and then return again and again until you've seen every little bit!

Lovely, shady.  Equipment geared toward the under-5 crowd, so if you take bigger kids, remind them to be courteous to the little kids.

Benches for adults, restroom bldg.  Woods to run around, with lots of sticks on the ground.  Small but pretty fab.

Homage to an ingenious thinker who liked rodents with fluffy tails.
Large wooden squirrel by locomotive has plaque with the basic story.
Turn the way the squirrel is facing and walk to intersection.  The Nutty Narrows is overhead.

Zingo, Zip!  Great food, fine beer. Plentiful quantities and decent prices.
It was so easy to eat GF and Dairy free, too.  Will definitely be back.

Outdoor seating under heaters and tent, but we ate inside.
Can be Fun to find!
likes: Outdoor seating with heaters and tent

reviews_attraction.text: Wow!  Gorgeous and peaceful.  This is unexpectedly now one of my favorite places ever.  Plan for a day or two,  bring hiking gear and water. Catch the singing volunteer at the North Bridge. Kayaking the river looks fabulous.

Fabulous!  Lots of parking, seals and starfish and waterfowl and agates.  Also a nice enough public restroom, with handy water sprayer on side to clean sand off.  We hit exceptionally low tide and had a blast.

Fabulous!  Tiny tourist town.  Parking is angled, would give 5 stars if it were easier to extricate the car on this busy highway.  We've been able to see whales here year round, sometimes more than 1.

Great little gem of a downtown park.

Many features for kids and adults, tons of special events all yr long.  Bathrooms are only reason I give 4 stars, not 5.  Farmers market on weekends.
You need to schedule the 45 min tour ahead of time.  Grounds and gift shop are lovely.  Will go back someday when we have more time. Staff were lovely.

Lovely park with stages and etc for events.
primitive bathrooms
Great play structure for kids.
Nice integration of art, nature, and play.

Growing up in Washington DC Martin Luther King Jr. was one of my childhood heros and it was very moving to see the Memorial. Make sure to take the time to read the wonderful quotes on the wall.

One of King's quotes that I love is: "An individual has not started living until he can rise above the narrow confines of his individualistic concerns to the broader concerns of all humanity."

I personally loved that the statue was facing the Jefferson Memorial across the tidal basin considering that I was named after Martin Luther of the Lutheran Church (as was King) and I was born on Thomas Jefferson's birthday. My parents told me that they also considered naming me Tomas because of my birthdate but choose Martin making me the III. I am so glad they picked Martin.

I'm so excited to be able to get in. I went down as an individual alone on a Saturday, unable to get tickets and was able to get in. Lucked out. The downstairs history exhibit often has a line that's about half an hour long so if that's important to you, go there first. I recommend it. You go all the way down to the basement starting with the slave trade up to the present day.  Make sure to go to the restroom 1st because it is about a 1 mile walk to the next bathroom. As far as parking I would just not try it. Take some form of transportation. The dining area and gift shop on a Saturday had long lines. It was a place of beauty, healing and hope. Both the building and the exhibits are well worth the visit. The staff was great too and the people visiting it.
dislikes: Long Lines (Dining, Gift Shop, History Exhibit)

reviews_attraction.text:
Growing up in DC one of the exciting things I did was walk up all the steps of the Washington monument and look out the small window from the top. I don't believe you can walk  up it anymore for obvious safety reasons. The wait is long to get to go up it but if you have the time it is worth doing. When I took a tour of Egypt it was exciting to see the originals that this monument was patterned after.

Most people know it, but the building of the monument was stopped during the civil war and when they restarted its construction after the civil war stones from a different location causing a texture change  in the rock that is clearly visible today.

Not that easy to find but well worth the effort  there's a little bit of everything here. Great for family, great for hikers, great for bicycles, great for walking your dog, great for people wanting to kick a ball around in a field.

My first time here was on the Saturday and it was amazingly not crowded it was 89 degrees outside but plenty of shade to walk in it was cool. The trails seem to be well maintained there aren't a lot of benches on the trails but they're playing shelters and picnic benches in the main area to sit down on. Camping is available for organized group with the rangers permission.

Only had a little time but still wanted to get on board and did. They let you explore a lot of places and if you have not been here before it is truly very impressive and worth seeing. You don't get the full perspective until you walk the deck. Quite a piece of history. I was amazed how steep the steps and would not recommend doing down into the engine room if you have a challenge getting around. I added some more pictures from below deck that I took and next time want to have more time and see the upper deck area. I felt proud for all those that served on this ship.

I remember as a kid first coming here and it is just exciting today at 55 years old. In some ways more amazing to realized what we did with the technology of the time.

From early flight to the space program this show the amazing capability of humans forces working together. The IMAX is always a blast if you have time and they have a nice cafeteria as well.

I loved the walk through of the early pan-am airplane and remember traveling in smaller plains as a kid that were similar.

Take about 1/2 to a day to visit and bring your camera.

The real Birthplace of Pepsi Cola. A delightful little place to sit down have a pepsi, learn about the history and visit the gift shop. I did not know it was here and just saw the sign while walking around down town. It also was created a tonic to start. Must make a stop into it and hear the story. What is so interesting is watching the video of how the brand of Pepsi was built. What I realized is that it was the celebrities and fans in ads that truly built the brand recognition. It's people not "the brand" that builds the brand.
likes: Facilities & Services: Gift shop, Video presentation

reviews_attraction.text: I stopped in on my way to Marion NC to teach and was pleasantly surprised. It is a bit area and look a while to find the public park area but it was worth the effort. I love the little beach area with picnic tables and hiking area I found. It is wonderful mountain lake shared with park areas and residential homes. I am so glad I got to take the time to visit. The local Chamber of Commerce recommended it to me. Good choice.

This the review about Wiseman's View Old nc 105, Linville, NC. 1st know it is a 4 mile dirt road to get to it, safe but windy road and about enough room for one truck. 1nd you park then hike on the trail past the sign that says watch out for kids on the rocks. It is worth the trip and a beautiful view without many people (dew the drive) .toe see the sun rise on 10/22/2015 and it was worth the effort. See the pictures.

The full name today is: Penelope Barker House Welcome Center. It is a information center, historic site and gift site with a living room.  I have had the pleasure of training  in the living room overlooking the Edenton Bay.

Penelope Barker was an activist in the American Revolution who in 1774 organised a boycott of British goods known as the Edenton Tea Party.

A nice piece of history in downtown Edenton NC.

1st know it is a 4 mile dirt road to get to it, safe but windy road and about enough room for one truck. 1nd you park then hike on the trail past the sign that says watch out for kids on the rocks. It is worth the trip and a beautiful view without many people (dew the drive) .toe see the sun rise on 10/22/2015 and it was worth the effort. See the pictures.

Everyone in America to study and learn about Fredric Douglass. Especially read "Life and Times of Frederick Douglass" his Autobiography. I was a volunteer docent for the Fredric Douglass museum in DC as a youth. I also recommending taking the time to learn about his dialogue with Lincoln. So please to see this place.

We use to go here in my youth in the 70ies. We would rent cabins that are still here with my Uncle Ed and his kids. I am so glad it is still here and is in such good shape with a few of the items I remember from my youth. May may generations enjoy it as well. Hope to come back sometime soon. Just like walking around.

Great view for the Sunrise and especially cool if the clouds are in the mountains.  Sufficient parking and good visibility to pull of and on the parkway.  It is located at milepost 376 just north of Asheville, NC. and Elevation 3175 feet above sea level.

What an amazing place! Mutiple rooms with differnt levels of difficulity. Amazing thought and creativity when into these rooms. The rooms are spectacular just to be in. Great customer service, fun for anyone and look forward to coming back!

Local art galore with working artist onsite. Wood, pottery, paintings and more. Large collection with a wonderful diversity well displayed.  See the artist working mixed in with their art. Amazing place. I posted a few pictures.

An outstandingly creative "escape rooms". I got a private tour and was blown-away by the amount of thought, creativity and work that goes into each of these rooms. Must see and good for families or business team building groups.

Came out with my friend and scuba instructor Kevin. It is not only a beautiful place to dive but just a beautiful place to see. The water is clear with a number of things to see both about the water and below the water

Wow what an amazing place. A husband and wife team created this business with over 30 years of collective experience in the game and puzzle world. Available for parties, groups, and corporate teambuilding.
It is so exciting to have such a progressive and beautiful Museum of Art in the RTP. The only challenge is sometime very big events get too crowded and you need to find off times to go.
Well kept lawn and area that set off nice as a view from downtown. I like the statues and  cannons around it (for show of course). I plan on getting a tour soon.
Nice little hidden dock and the place where I proposed to my wife a number of years ago. Drove up north Raleigh still like to stop and see this place
Wonderful park with nice walkways along the creek in Hickory and plenty of parking. Good place for kids families bicycle and hiking and picnics.
Well maintained and well loved parks in this area with wonderful trails. I was in the area on business and love walking the trails.
It was not open when I came with a beautiful view of the river with nice areas the picnic.In the nicest work downtown. To walk in

I took a free walking tour and my guide explained that when the slave trade originated and agriculture business was booming, the horrible and disgusting practice of buying and selling humans was practiced outside at the historic market and various places around the city. Once the Carolina Golden Rice, which was the #1 export and 40% of profits, declined in sales the demand for labor forces also declined dramatically and the main place for human trade was at the indoor slave mart. The first person sold in this mart was a 20 year old female named Lucinda. If it alrighty wasn't f'd up enough -the practice and brutality of kidnapping, transporting, selling and forcing people into labor, splitting up families, raping and torturing- they were sold at auction, naked as the day they were born- humiliating.

Super awesome aquarium! Fair price. I love that it is not only an aquarium, but an aquatic rescue and turtle surgery spot. It also supports or acts as an educational program in the community. The aquarium has indoor and outdoor touch pools, a bird area, reptiles, an alligator with albinism, bald eagles and more. You can go on a "Behind the Scenes" tour, which is free, but must be mentioned at the ticket booth to arrange. There are lots of kid and educational activities and feedings throughout the day. Animals are well cared for. Mostly volunteer staff, including many of the divers! The food spot is small, but okay.. Great view of the water while eating.

A Charleston must-see attraction!!! Good for kids, adults and families alike!

I enjoy the architecture and the exhibits at this gallery. There is a small, but diverse permanent collection as well on the second floor. The third floor has a small exhibit and the largest floor is 4. The staff always does a great job with the exhibit layout and the descriptions are really informative. I always leave having learned a lot. I tend to visit on Bank of America Museums on Us weekends which offers free admission to Bank of America customers.

Staff is nice, taking pictures is encouraged, restrooms are clean and beware the gift shop is expensive.

Great first time safari experience with your own vehicle or wagon. On popular days like weekends or school holidays, reserve wagon spots ahead of time. Safe environment, animals approach but are gentle. Safari includes many types of cattle including long horns, water buffalo, emus, ostrich, llamas, deer, pigs, zebra, giraffes, etc. There is a petting zoo which includes sheep, goats, ponies, horses, camels. Then there are enclosures with peacocks, birds, turtles, the animals that start with the letter "L" from the movie Madagascar and more.

Beautiful, manipulation of several trees that have grown together into one enormous tree.
I visited on a Sunday before the opening hours of one o'clock and arrived to find that the area encompassing the tree and gift shop has a high gate and is monitored by a burglar alarm system. However, we were still allowed to sneak peeks through the gate at varying angles to see the whole majesty of the Angel Tree.

Next time I visit Charleston, I plan on visiting again when it's open (M-Sa 9-5, Su 1-5) to spend more time and enjoy it fully!

I was so excited to see a beachy shoreline from the bridge crossing over the Potomac River. I was even more excited that the turn in to the beach was directly accessible after getting onto the Virginia side and couldn't pass up the opportunity. It is free. There are picnic tables, port-a-potties, parking areas and of course the beach with quite a few seashells. My shoes came off and the sand and water felt nice. It was a nice short stop.

I learned so much! It is so fascinating to hear the park rangers explain the fort from a historical role in our history- military tactics, battles, North vs. South, the culture of the time, the presidential reaction, the international impact to trade and export, etc. Even learning about life on the fort from rain water catchment, food storage, sewage plumbing and apartments for the families was all very intriguing.

Wonderful park for hiking, boating, relaxing, swimming or picnicking. Bring your own watercraft or rent one (various kinds available, such as kayaks, canoes, sailboats, etc.). Lots of walking and hiking trails around the lake and all over the park. The pool is open for swimming and lessons (nominal entrance fee). Large parking lot and no fee to enter park. State park staff are super helpful and friendly!

Good option for traveling to and from Northern New York City/Hudson area. I prefer it over the GW (George Washington bridge). There is less fuss, traffic and I believe it may also be cheaper. However, if you aren't heading to West Chester outwards to Connecticut, it would be much to far out of your way.. Too inconvenient.

I enjoyed the Strawberry Festival 2017! Awesome car show. Good music, nice selection of food vendors, lots of porta-potties, good amount of entertainment and games/rides. Great weather for an outdoor festival. Parking at the high school and catching the bus was a nice feature to alleviate parking/traffic frustrations.

Very neat museum showing historical, ecological, economical, geographical perspectives. The original Hezekiah Alexander homestead is also on the property.

Admission is typically $10/person. However, several nights throughout the year offer free events/admission. It's worth the trip. Good for adults and kids, alike.

Nice museum away from the city center, it is associated with The Mint Museum Uptown. I thoroughly enjoyed my visit a couple years ago. Just haven't had the opportunity to return. I forgot now but it's either Tuesday or Wednesday evening offer FREE admission after 5 PM. Great place to visit and check out exhibits.

This park is awesome. It has everything except swings. I love the Carolinas Panthers work out course! Some cool trails, ponds, fountains and playground equipment for all ages. Nice basketball and beach volleyball courts. My only complaint is that the restrooms get locked at in the evening.

Beautiful, waterfront park with nice benches and green areas. Nice fountains (people can cool off in them on warm days, just follow the rules) and relaxing pier with swings. Parking is slightly tricky (meters, garages and some street and lot parking is zoned for residential permits only).

Scary place. It's been voted best Halloween attraction by many large surveys for good reason. Pricing is reasonable. There are many attractions to pick and choose from. The actors and makeup is believable. Maybe you should wear a diaper... you may pee your pants. Muah hahahahahaaaaaa!

I love this beach! The water is fairly calm. It's more peaceful and tranquil compared to the tourist beaches. It's LGBTQ friendly with lots of families. Great place to take family beach portraits. Fishing is permitted to the left of the rocks. Lots of people also bring their dogs.

Cool Afro-American museum dedicated to art, education and social justice. Workshops are offered for kids and families. Music adult nights. Participant of Bank of America museums on us free weekends. Interesting exhibits as well as permanent collections. Will definitely be back!

Love the quotations, artifacts and general information not only from the time period, but specifically from the local region. Serves its' purpose- very educational. Visitor center is free. Tours to the island/Fort Sumter are not free, but are well worth the price and time.

Both the information cabin and the Visitor centers were closed during the day when we visited this past Thursday. Apparently, during the off season /non summer months, its only open on the weekends (Friday-Sunday). FYI

Restrooms were also locked during our visit.

Beautiful park. Varying hiking and walking difficulties. Love the wildlife areas and mile high swinging bridge. Staff and rangers are friendly. I learned a lot during the animal talks. Great all day, family activity.. Both naturalist and touristy.
Very cool park. Nice playground. Nice playing and ball fields. Nice to walk around with kids, friends, family or dogs. Good amount of seats and bleachers for spectating.
Beautiful. The corporate park has so many cool walking and fitness trails, fountains and ponds, as well as parks such as this one! Go explore!!
Awesome place to watch aircrafts take-off and land. You can sit in your parked vehicle or sit on various park benches. Very neat spot!
Very nice park or square outside the SC Aquarium and Fort Sumter historical museum. Nice historical markers and picnic tables.
Cool playground and splash pad. Large grassy area to play, lots of trails, basketball and tennis courts and a baseball field.

This park is very well design and safe for kids and adults. As I entered the park, there is a fishing area on the right and left as I drive over a short bridge, and to my left is the miniature golf area. The parking area was ahead of me as well as to my right. I parked on the right where the trees created shade in that whole area, keeping the cars parked there cool. There are picnic tables there. As I walked towards the larger parking lot, it is surrounded by small buildings that houses many different things. If I remember correctly, the first building on the right was the sweet building where it sells funnel cakes, ice cream, candy, etc... The next building is where you learn the history of Bushkill. The next one is the restroom, which has the men's on the tight, family restroom in the middle, and the women's on the left. The next building sells clothes and then the next has Welcome to Bushkill and that's the souvenir shop. After that is a playground for the kids, and it is where I exited the main Bushkill area with the trails and waterfalls. The next and last building is the Bushkill waterfalls entrance. Before I entered the park, I was greeted by a friendly staff at the window where I purchased mtly ticket this park is dogfriendly, and I didn't go into any building but this one to see the waterfalls. After getting my to ticket and a map of the park, I entered the building and they have a wildlife exhibit there. It's a pretty neat exhibit. At the end of this short exhibit, I was greeted by another friendly staff and she scanned my ticket and I exited the building and started my hike. The started of the hike was in paced trails with 3 informative signs. Then I walked up to a big signs with info on the trails with color codes. The Top of the Main Falls East (3) was below and I took a long flight of stairs down. Note: when you decend, you will eventually ascend. Keep that in mind. So if your health limits physical activities, please pick the appropriate trail. I did the longest trail with my 2 little terrier mixes. After seeing the Main Falls, I took the stairs back up, and to the left. The trail started off with lots of wooden walkways where I saw the Laurel Glen (13) upper canyon (14) to Pennell Falls (17). Then I hiked a reasonably flat Pennell Falls trail (18) with some rocks and tree roots and a small area on the right where you can stack the rocks. It is easily missed . Then passed the Pete's Corner (18) to the Bridesmaids and Bridal Falls (10-8) , there is when their stairs taking me down to the falls begin. A lot of stairs going down, which is the easy part. At the end of the stairs, a rocky trail starts. I saw some people playing in the creek on the left, and the trail gets very Rocky, be careful. The rocky section ended at the bridge crossing the Big Bushkill Creek. The rest of the trail is on wooden walkway which passes Gorge Falls (7-5) and there is where I picked up the yellow trail ahead instead of turning right to go back up. It took me to the bottom of the main Falls, with a beautiful view of the Main Falls (west) (4-12) then I took the many steps back up to the beginning of the park. That is the hardest part of the hike. I went backwards on the trail; you could go in the other direction, but either way, there is a long flight of steps to get back to the starting point. There are signs throughout the park with info on the section of the trail ahead, and the trail is so well design, you can't get lost as long as you stay on the trail. I really enjoy seeing the pattern on the rocks along the trail.  As I exit the park, there are signs guiding me to the exit. If you want to go back in, Do Not Exit the pack, you need to return to the wildlife exhibit area and get your hand stamp. I hiked 2.2 miles. Great workout. My pups passed out.

This Rock City Park is very unique. The owner is so friendly and very informative. He answered all the questions I have on the park and its history. I stopped by the restroom before I headed out to begin my adventure with my 2 little pups. The restaurant is a mini-antique store. It is unisex and you can stop while you are in there. LOL The building also sells rocks, souvenir, drinks, etc... This park is very dogfriendly!

The entrance fee was $5 per person; free for dogs. After paying, the entrance to the park is located in the back of the store. Once you exit the store and into the park, I was already standing on rocks - top of the rocks with the rock city park located below. There are large gaps between rocks, and there are little concrete bridge to help you cross from one rock to another. If you have small dogs or children with you, keep both eyes on them, because if they accidentally fall between the rocks, I am not sure if you can rescue them, at least not easily.

I got a little lost and headed to my right until I was at the top of an almost vertical drop staircase, the Indian Stairs. Luckily for me, I came across a couple who climbed up the staircase, and the nice man helped me carry one of my dogs down. On my way back up after finished with exploring park, I found the metal staircase that I should have taken to go down into the park. The metal staircase was pretty steep, too, and it has spaces in the steps. My girls wouldn't have been able to go up or down on either stairs. If you are taking your dog or very young kids, be prepared to carry them up and down these stairs.

I was going backwards on the trail since I took the Indian Stairs down, and because I was traveling backwards on the trail, I missed a lot of the rock formations. I ended up taking a shortcut in order to start close to the beginning as though I came down from the metal staircase. There are small trails that branch off the main trail. Stay on the main trail is a good idea. There is where you will see all the rock formation, and where you are likely to get lost. I used a GPS tracker to track my route so that I was able to find my way back and around.

The rock formations are pretty neat. My favorite is the Balancing Rock, and big foot at the end. One of my dogs was growling at Big Foot. LOL For $5, this park is so worth going to and exploring. It is amazing how big the rocks are. I highly recommend stopping by this park if you are in the area. This park is not wheelchair accessible, and you will need to be in reasonably good health.
dislikes: Gaps between rocks (safety concern for small dogs/children)

reviews_attraction.text:
A hidden Gem - I found this Washington Monument when I was looking on Google Map for a place to take my pups. I hesitated a little, because it looked like I needed to travel into the woods to get there. I really wanted to see the monument, so I took my chances.

As it turned out, the road to the entrance of the Washington Monument Park was interesting. It is a small road through an old residential neighborhood in the mountains. The entrance with the gate to the park isn't the entrance to take. Take the entrance next to it with a small road. If the park entrance is on your left, pass the entrance and take the first road right after the entrance on your left. Drive ahead, and you'll see the entrance with a metal post for entrance fee. It has envelops provided for you to put the entrance fee in, and a tag for your car. When I got there, the post was filled, and there was a stack of envelops sitting on top. They need to make a bigger post that can take more envelops with entrance fee. I always wonder if someone would steal the money. I hope not.

Anyway, once I paid my entrance fee, I drove down the 1 way road into the park. The park is very spacious and clean. It has a visitor center, bathrooms, and plenty of parking. When facing the visitor's center, the trail is on the right. The trail is very well kept, and it has signs along the way with historic information. Before reaching the monument, there is a sign on the right to the Appalachian Trail. Keep walking, and you will see the monument in front of you. The back of the monument (on your right) has an amazing view of the area. You can take the spiral stairs up to the top of the monument for a better view.

The entire distance from where I parked - which is passed the visitor's center and the bathroom - is 0.62 miles round trip. The trail is gravel, and in a way, you can take a wheelchair to the monument, but there are some steps at the beginning of the trail.
likes: Facilities & Services: Spacious, clean, visitor center, bathrooms, parking
Activities: Well-kept trail, spiral stairs, scenic view
dislikes: Facilities & Services: Inadequate fee collection post

reviews_attraction.text: I love this place. It is super dogfriendly. No dogs allowed inside buildings. It is a great place to walk my dog. On a busy day, parking can be a challenge. If you bike, recommend parking nearby and take the trail on bike. There are bike racks in the parking lot and also in the trail between the parking lot and the entrance to GW's Mount Vernon. There is a bag check point after you bought your tickets and entered the museum building. There is a bag size limit allowed onto the property. It is easy to miss the Forest Trail, a very short trail through the woods with informative and interactive signs. I wish the trail was longer. This trail is not for wheelchairs and for those with difficulty walking. The steps down are uneven and with small rocks that can be slippery. Be careful. I had hiking shoes on and I took my time walking down the steps toward the farm area. I live the water views and if you have time, take the cruise. When you enter the GW's tomb and the slave memorial area, please be quiet. There are signs asking visitors to maintain quiet and peace... For those who passed. I didn't go into the mansion because I have my pups. When you buy your tickets, you will have a mansion tour time assigned, printed in the tickets. The back of the mansion faces the river, a nice area to sit down and enjoy the view. Restrooms are behind the garden and next to the farm near the river. The property is always very clean. I visited today and they had a trick or treating Halloween event and I really enjoyed seeing kids and adults dressed up for the event. There are lots of trashcans and recycled bins throughout the property. Bring poop bags if you bring your pups. There is no poop bags available on the property. Bring water for your pups, too.
dislikes: Lack of poop bags for dogs

reviews_attraction.text:
This is my first time visiting this park. To my surprise, it is very clean. There is a small parking lot that will accommodate about 20 cars. There are ruins with description of each building. Very interesting and educational. The trails are dirt covered with many exposed roots, and very well mark - color code is marked on the trees. Along the water, there is a trail that is not part of the trail map. To get there, take the Green/White from the left side of the parking lot, with the road behind you. It is a short walk to the water, about 1/4 mile. Be careful when you walk downhill to the water, the trail slopes down with deep steps. Walking up to the trail from the water is a great workout... Up hill.

As I continue on the White/Green Trail, eventually, it parallels with the water, and there are 2 overlooks with fences along the cliff. Both provide a nice view of the river. To get to the overlooks, it is a steep downhill followed by an steep uphill hike. Great workout! I discovered that you don't need to back track from the overlooks back onto the trail. There is a trail at the top where the overlooks are that connects and continues you to the White/Green trail. So, when you get to the first overlook on your left, take the trail by the first of to the 2nd overlook on your left. It connects to the White/Green trail to  continue on. When I reached the part of the trail that gave me a view of the Leesburg Water Treatment Plant, the trail was blocked by a fallen tree. I walked around to the right and climbed over another fallen tree to get around it. From there, the walk to the parking lot was a short one.

I will definitely return to this park again. Great workout on the White/Green trail. Recommend wear hiking shoes.

This is one of my favorite State Parks by far. When it visited, it cost $5 to park. There are restrooms not too far from the parking area. There are lots of trails throughout the State Park, and the Red trail (main trail) is a mile one way (2 miles round trip) that goes through the swamp and to the beach at the end of the trail. Walking along the swamp is my favorite park. The beach is small, but after walking a mile, it was a nice reward to see the open water. It is dogfriendly, and my dog enjoyed playing in the sand. On the way back to the parking area, I decided to take one of the Blue trails on the left. I found that the trails are not as clearly marked as I needed them to be. I always use a hiking app to track my hike and often have a printed trail map with me, and I have to use both to find my way back to my car. I didn't enjoy that Blue and Yellow trails as much as the Red trail. The Blue/Yellow trails are in the woods, and part of both trails are located closer to the power plant. Kind of creepy. I recommend staying on the Red trail both ways. The Red trail has more people, while the other trails appear to be rarely used. I was the only one on the Blue/Yellow trails. I didn't encounter anyone. I love this park and I will definitely return.. and staying on the Red trail the entire time.

When you are driving on River Road, look for the sign to the C&O Canal National Historic Site, and the road sign for Swains Lock Road. It can be easily missed. Once you turn onto Swains Lock Road, immediately stay to the left because the right is a private property driveway. You will see the No Trespassing sign. Swains Lock Road looks like a one lane road and you will drive pass several beautiful homes, and the road dead ends at Swains Lockhouse and a small parking lot.

I turned left once I got onto the trail, and walked a little over a mile passing mile marker 16 and a building that I'm not sure what it is. Toward the end of the mile, the scenery wasn't too exciting, because there is no view of the Potomac River. When it rained, the trail gets very wet, and my little pups got real dirty. The trail is pretty well kept. I didn't know there are 6 Lockhouse available for rent.

There are also a few Don John's if you are looking for a restroom.

I stopped by this park on my way to Ocean City. This park is pretty unique. It is located at the exit at Northeast end of the Bay Bridge. I didn't know what to expect asides from having a view of the water. To my surprise, this Nature Park has a Meadows, Wetland, Marsh land, Beach and trails. It appears to be quite popular for walkers and cyclists as well as dog owners. The trails are not paved, and the smaller trail loop is about 2.18 miles from the parking lot. The larger loop, I believe, is 1.2 miles longer. There are other trails that go outside the park property. The beach is long but not wide. Some people would let their dogs run off leash on the beach, but I believe all dogs must be on leash. To my surprise, there are a lot of portable toilets throughout the park. There were 2 in the parking lot. One didn't have a lot on the door, and the other had urine all over the seat and floor. Gross!

I wanted to see the Boulder Field and with limited time, I didn't have a chance to hike on any of the trails. I didn't realize getting to the Boulder Field requires a 2.8 miles drive through the woods on an unpaved road. There are signs clearly pointing me in the right direction. Upon reaching the Boulder Field, I was surprised by how massive the field is. My dogs are 13 lbs and the boulders are taller than them. I took some pictures and headed out. The drive on the unpaved road out of the area was longer than the way in. I drove another 4 miles on the unpaved road. What's disappointing is that the 7+ Mile drive through the woods, I only saw 1 chipmunk and that was at the Boulder Field 🙄. If you happened to be in the area, stop by, but don't make a trip just to see the boulders. These boulders don't ring. Go to one of the ringing Boulder Fields/parks instead.

I am always looking for places to walk my dogs. Unfortunately, I have little interest in history, but I love that I pick up a little bit of it when I visit historic sites. I was driving through this area when I was traveling to and from Greenville SC. I decided to stop at this battlefield to give my dogs a break from the long drive. I am really glad that I did. This battlefield doesn't have much to see but lots of signs to read. The trails is half gravel and half paved. It is very cleaned and the park ranger in the visitor's center/museum was very nice and informative. If you are in the area, I recommend stopping by. I am not sure if many people know about this battlefield. It is located in the middle of nowhere. Definitely worth visiting, especially, if you like history.

Carvers Creek State Park is very unique. I didn't know what to expect, and upon arrival, the trees and field appeared to be recovering from a forest fire. As I was walking through the park, there was a sign on "The Forest That Fire Built", and it confirmed my first impression of the park. This state park is very unique to all the ones I've visited up and down the East Coast. It was a site to see, and if you are in the area and have never seen a park like this, I recommend that you stop by and experience it for yourself. The most interesting part of the park is observing the different stage of the growth of the trees, which was detailed on the sign. I took a picture of the sign, and use it as a reference whenever I encountered a tree and curious as to how old it is.

This little history farm didn't have much going on when I visited early March. Everything was closed. There was still a lot to see without going inside the buildings. I enjoyed seeing the horses and the donkey. The volunteers there are very nice, and they answered all my questions about the horses and the donkey. The Farm trail was a little creepy feel, because it goes through and under the power lines. Never really like being near power lines. We stopped by here as our last stop before we head home from our vacation, and my pups were already tired from all the hiking we did during our trip. They were too tired for us to stop by the military park. I will definitely stop by here again and hopefully it will be more eventful.

Driving from Charleston to Savannah with my pups and needed to stop for my pups to go to the bathroom. I saw this nature center and decided to pull over here. I didn't expect this Edisto Nature Center is so clean!! It is also unique with wooden walking paths which kept my pups' little paws cleaner than walking on muddy trails. We only walked about 0.37 miles round trip. If I planned in advance and mapped it out, I would have walked further. This is such a nice park to hike. There was a sign saying that this site is monitored with security camera. I hope so because it is pretty quiet when I stopped by. I'm not sure how popular this Nature Center is.

Not Dog Friendly ... NO DOGS ALLOWED ... but since I traveled 500 miles to this park, and it wasn't tourist season, I decided to take a sneak preview myself. I walked up to the beginning of the trails (where the sand starts) so that I can see what is hidden behind the trees, and took some photos and turned around. Boy, I kind of wish I didn't, the view was amazing! I really wanted to hike the trails and get closer to the water, and experience and absorb it all in. If you can leave your dogs at home or if you don't have dogs, I recommend visiting this park. The trails are mostly sand, and the view is amazing. Too bad dogs are not allowed.

This Park is very clean and spacious. it has a lot of trails, and things to do for the kids. Behind the Natural Center is a natural trail with activities along the trail. This Natural Center trail is not dog friendly - no dogs allowed. All other trails are dog friendly. I took the trail that took me to the creek. The creek is nice and peaceful, and I saw a little tiny frog camouflaged into the pebbles. It has a playground for the kids, restrooms, and some ruins.
dislikes: No dogs allowed on Natural Center trail

reviews_attraction.text: I enjoyed hiking in the Latta Nature Preserve  - Latta Plantation Trails. Hiking along the water was fun and relaxing. The water view was amazing. Definitely highly recommend the Cattail trail. The end of the trail takes you to the peck with a beautiful view of the lake. I really enjoy the Audubon Trail because the little guys built with sticks a long the trail and a wishing well, too. The restrooms are located between these 2 trails by the parking lot.

I was on vacation in Cleveland and learned about the Hot Diggity Dog Day event on Main Street Beach, next to this lighthouse.  Like any lighthouse, there is always some history. I only walked the grounds. If you like lighthouse, you will probably enjoy it more than I did. I do like that it is on Lake Erie, and the view of the lake is beautiful. To the right of the lighthouse is the Main Street Beach. There is where the dog festival was held.

I love this park. The section where the mansion is located is very clean and spacious with a garden, memorial, and other buildings. I love going hiking here with my dogs. The Ridge Top Trail is a great workout. It has a  upward incline than a down hill hike. Be sure to wear hiking shoes because the down hill is pretty steep in some sections. This part is dog friendly. That's another section of trail that I skipped this time.

This lighthouse is located in/behind the park fenced in and can't be accessed. This little park is perfect for the community. It is located along the water surrounded by homes. If you stand with the park behind you, you might see the top of the Hammermill Three Sister Stacks peeking out from above the trees. I circled the area to find a spot where I saw it in between the trees.

Neat looking bridge for pedestrians and dogs. The narrow concrete walkway on one side is where most people walk on. The wider area of the bridge is metal and it has small holes where you can see through to the water. Definitely not paws friendly and not for those with fear of height. It has a great view and f the river on either side.

This park is by the water and has a boat ramp for boats and other water sports. It has a 0.8 mi hiking trail into the woods and open field. I was hoping most of the trail was along the water but it's not. It has 2 portable toilets, of which 1 is larger than the standard size. The water view is beautiful.

I love this park. It has a lot of history and I love that they have a village set up with farm animals, and the caretakers live on site. One of the hiking trail takes you along the Potomac River with a view of George Washington's Mount Vernon. It is definitely a place to visit and experience.

This museum/park is truly unique. I didn't go in the museum because I have my 2 little dogs with me. I learned a lot from the signs outside. The park is small and clean, and well equipped with a fully functional restroom, trash cans, doggy poop stations.
Beautifully designed, very clean. It has chairs where people can relax and enjoy the view of the river. Dogs are not allowed in the park area, but allowed everywhere else.
Great spacious park with nice paved trails. Very clean. The Korean, MIA, and POW memorials are also there. The memorials are worth seeing. Dogfriendly too!!

I wasn't familiar with this museum. But I had gone to the Library of Congress, several weeks ago, and the location appeared to be close.
I arrived upon this huge marble structure.  A Security Officer greets me as I approach the entrance. I enter, I'm immediately drawn into the Great Hall, to The First Chefs Exhibit.
After exploring that area, at the adjoining room, I inquired about other areas. A very helpful Security Officer, paired me with a Docent. The Docent gave me a tour of the Founders' Room and Furnishings. The Docent was very detailed in her presentation.
She pointed out the most interesting items in the Founders' Room. For example, she relayed the history and details of the portraits, the character's names in the stained glass, the background about the Folio on display. She gave me ample time to photograph.
I thoroughly appreciated the tour and assistance. In another area, I was able to see the theater, which was in rehearsal for a play. I was not able to see The Research Room, it required advance reservation for that portion of the tour. Great tour, especially Founders' Room.

I always wondered where this park was located, found it today. One hour is not enough time tho explore this expansive area. I was alone with just nature, until I was walking my way out of the park in the rush hour of late afternoon. In my brief time, highlights were; I saw an eagle crash dive into the bay and caught a fish. I saw two turkeys just strolling down the middle of trail I was on. I got very close to Peter Rabbit, quietly observed him in the middle of a trail. Then I got too close and Pete scampered off. Plenty of insects also.

I finally stopped here for the first time, to explore Belle Haven Park. I would drive the GW Parkway, look over, mostly on weekends, and wonder what had brought the large crowds to this particular area. This weekday, I walked from the parking area down to the shoreline, where you see ducks playing in the water, views across the Potomac River, toward Maryland. Views of National Harbor, MGM Resort Casino, and views the Woodrow Wilson Bridge.

My hike covered parts of miles 1 and 2 of the 14 mile, Mount Vernon Trail, within the George Washington Memorial Parkway. If you're starting at Mount Vernon, the mile one trail runs into Riverside Park. Continue on pass mile two marker, you will observe signs for larger, Fort Hunt Park. Observe nature, Potomac River, picnic areas, and restrooms on site. Parking at various points along the trail, for site seeing, or other activities.

This park has something for everyone, tranquil enough for fishing. The trails are used for biking, hiking or jogging. Historical landmarkers and a lighthouse, not to mention the Woodrow Wilson Bridge. Catch a view of the Potomac River, look over from Virginia to National Harbor in Maryland. There are play areas for the children, a basketball court, picnic areas and public restrooms on site. Free parking and admittance.

Once a thriving military installation, now a monument, with more than 400 years of history. I arrived for the Sunday portion of the 1619 Commemoration Program. The four minutes bell ringing across the land at 3pm was significant. The Native American chants and prayers, presence of Tuskegee Airman, Gospel singers, even a sneak peek into the new museum exhibits, set to open later this year, all noteworthy.

High adventure, walking tour around Riverfront Canal area led me to this area by accident.  I arrived with several people, I described what I was looking for. They confirmed the location. You won't find this long name spelled out. I walked the rails, didn't quite trust my balance over the Pipeline that crosses over to Brown's Island. I will return after some balance training, maybe.

With all the visitors crowded around the cherry trees at the Independence Avenue entrance to the ANA Cherry Festival Stage, the Floral Garden, I found was practically unnoticed. You would walk right pass it crossing the street to get to the National Mall. But I found the spring flowers are starting to bloom. The posted sign did help me find this location.

Great crowd support for the Annual Chinese New Year Parade and firecracker ceremony. Crowds packed H Street under the Friendship Archway to get a glimpse of the cultural event. There were live performances, Dragon Dance, and pageant queens. The parade was followed by big firecracker and Dragon Dance Ceremony in the center of Chinatown.

My first time observing this statue, I was walking through the area, the statue had a group of costumed dancers surrounding it. It was used as a staging area for a cultural event. The event was the 19th Annual Food Festival of the Americas, held across the street at the Museum of the Americas. Enjoyed the event very much.

George Washington's Mount Vernon Estate puts on a big celebration of the first president's birthday each year. This would have been the 287th birthday. The public was invited for free tour of the mansion and grounds. The day was capped off with birthday cake and a concert from members of the U.S. Air Force Band.

A great location to connect with nature. My first visit, happened to be during the coldest time of the year. But I found walking trails to some higher elevation. A waterfront with scenic views of homes, as well as birds nesting. Recreational areas I observed were for kayaking, volleyball and has a cafe on site.

The reopening of Beach Drive after years of road work, encouraged me to get out and explore some new areas. Found parking across from Peirce Mills and hiked the Rock Creek Park Trail south to the Smithsonian National Zoological Park and back. Crossed bridges, streams, and observed the budding fall foliage.

The grand fountain is turned into an ice skating rink in the winter. In the warmer months, the same area flows with water and crowds gather on weekends for a weekly outdoor concert series. Bring your own skates or rent on site. The pavilion area also has a cafe and skating classes are available.

I like how this park has interactive programs, mostly free to the public. This program involved the live artillery firing of cannons, used in defense of Washington, DC, during the Civil War period. Period reenactors set up camp and gave demonstrations on weapons and ammunition of the period.

Had not visited since I was a small child. Had to take a peek before departing the Hampton area. The memory from that period is a photo with my sister at the beach. I lost her last year, so this was like a tribute tour with her in mind, and I must say for my brief visit, I was impressed.

When you get off the metro at the Gallery Place/Chinatown stop, you know you are in Chinatown. The reason is the iconic DC symbol of the Chinatown Friendship Archway. The Chinese New Year Celebration held was a great festive event that brought out all communities of the city and beyond.

I found a newly developed landscape project and artwork at Waterfront Park. Some colorful tables and chairs to take in the scenic view of the Potomac River. This area is only steps away from restaurants and the Torpedo Art Center and the Water Taxi and Cruise lines are also nearby.

I explored just the grounds on this visit, my first. Will return to share the lodge with a friend. There is a lot to see, there's a garden that attracts beautiful butterflies. I found their beehive by accident, good thing I had read about it. You don't want to excite the bees.

This location is across from the National Archives, is free and open for public viewing. Has names and sculptures of great Sailors, the likes of John Paul Jones. Also within a couple of blocks and view of Smithsonian American Arts Museum and National Portrait Gallery.

Visited on free Museum Weekend, certain museums offer no fee admission, took the guided tour which covered all interior levels. You can take the tour on your own as well. After the guided tour you can go back on your own for more in depth research if you desire.

A very nice memorial and tribute to the 32nd President of the United States. Located between MLK and the Jefferson Memorials. You have statues of he and the First Lady Eleanor. His most memorable words and sayings, as well as words and art in Braille.

I don't know what the park is like under normal circumstances, but for this special Alexandria Birthday Celebration,   visitors seemed to have a great time. There was food vendors, a symphony  orchestra, and the best fireworks in the area.

Followed the construction from the early stages, finally completed and days from opening. Good location between the National Mall and SW Waterfront, with some free transportation options, already available.
My first time walking this tour. Between the mix of architecture, especially in the banking district and the natural beauty of the river and forestry at play, makes for an awe inspiring scenic tour.

The family and myself love to come here, spend some times and shop. We love the staff at this location, and the place offers a wonderful experiences that we come to value. It's always in a good location to us as well. We would come back again in a heartbeat. We enjoyed the open space, and the many places within this place to explore and hike. This is a historic place for sure, but it's always epic as it stretches for miles.
