Hogsmeade village is located in universal Orlando studios at the far end of the park. At the entrance to the Hogsmeade village is Hogsmeade station.
As you enter the village you get to see Hogwarts express and pose with it. Have a  chat with the friendly driver and click few snaps with Hogwarts express in the background.

As you go inside, you get to see the snow-capped village. The snowy look gives the whole village a picturesque touch. There are carts selling butterbeer, pumpkin juice, and other goodies. Don't forget to get butterbeer in the souvenir mugs and get clicked with your frothy mustache ;)
Its lined with colorful shops. The notable among them are Olivanders and Honeydukes. Get yourself a bag of treats from honeydukes full of chocolate frogs, or Bertie Bott every flavored bean, peppermint toads or the jelly slugs and then move towards olivanders to witness the wand choosing ceremony and get yourself a magic wand.  It's very interesting to see it and the little magic threw along with it. Note strange looking muggle devices(read phones and camera) are discourage also it's not the wizard/witch who chooses the wand, the wand always chooses the wizard/witch.

You will always find a queue for entering olivanders but its worth the wait. Have your lunch at the three broomsticks and get a drink at hogs head pub. It's amusing to look at the owls at Owl post and at the caged monster book of monster which snarls and moves. Also, don't forget to visit the restrooms there where you will hear moaning myrtle singing :)
Just as Hogsmeade ends, you get to see towering castle which houses Hogwarts school of witchcraft and wizardry. There is a bridge beside the castle which takes you to the entrance of Jurassic Park. This offers the best view of the castle and is a perfect place to capture your clicks with the dreamy castle as the backdrop.

Hogwarts houses the ride - Harry Potter and the forbidden journey. This ride mandates that things must be stowed away in the lockers provided at the entrance. On your way to the ride inside the castle, you get to see the talking and moving portraits, go by dumbledores office to the defense against dark arts classroom. Dumbledore's office is marvelous with each and every detail in place. The ride is a simulated one with sudden movements and jerks where Harry, Ron, and Hermione guides you around from the castle to forbidden forest to a Quidditch match. You get to witness dementors, the giant aragog in the forbidden forest and swoop past the castle into the Quidditch field to catch the golden snitch cheered by Hogwarts students and staff from the stand.
The nighttime lights at Hogwarts which starts at dusk till park closing time is the icing on the cake. Its a must must watch. The music and the lights are treated to the ears and eyes. It feels absolutely magical to watch it.
likes: Attraction Type: Themed village, immersive experience
Cultural Value: Wizarding world authenticity, magical atmosphere
Facilities & Services: Butterbeer, souvenir mugs, variety of treats, wand choosing ceremony, themed shops, Hogwarts ride, lockers
On-site Activities: Photo opportunities, interactive experiences, wand magic, ride with Harry Potter theme, nighttime light show

reviews_attraction.text:
had an amazing day... food-shop-fun-themed stores.. what more do you want

the place was a really great spot for shopping and eating and having fun.  We parked in the orange parking garage ( they had two, orange and Lime) and it was free. what I liked in the garage is, it will actually tell you if the level you choose has any open spots as they have sensors at each parking spot so you don't waste your time driving around the garage endlessly. we visited this mall in offseason, still, it was crowded in the evening.

coming to the mall, I guess it was for me, For folks that don't want to actually go to Disney World ( i spent 3 days in Universal) but want a little Disney in their lives, Disney Springs satisfies that. it will take you about 5 to 6 hours to get around the site.
That's if you wander into each shop. With a massive Lego store to Disney Marvel and star wars stores,  Beauty shops and high-end Disney clothing shops. I liked the coke store though very much.  This is not an outlet store complex so expect prices to be higher.  The sprawling promenade features 4 distinct neighborhoods, The Landing, Marketplace, West Side and Town Center—built around bubbling springs.

There are tons of restaurants (and plenty of them also have nightly entertainment. some even have a 21+ after hours, which I really like) and there are things to do for kids and adults. Rainforest, Trex is the most popular one. there are plenty of attractions for visitors like us
I love the layout as well because it's not too small or big and you can't really get lost. If you're a photographer like me, there are a lot of areas to take colorful photos.  At night, there are several entertainers and that's also fun to see all the creatives come out and it's fantastic that it's not extra to enjoy their work. There’s a hot air balloon that takes riders straight up in the air that looks like it would provide a great scenic view.

There is also a bowling alley and AMC Theatre. It is very vibrant and full of energy. Near the Boathouse restaurant and bar, there was a DJ playing the best dance music and the crowd was rocking.  I do appreciate what Disney Springs had to offer. The welcome club has employees who solve your queries in quite effectively. they were very courteous when we enquired about the bus to the boardwalk. It's really low key and people are just shopping and having fun. No lines of humans waiting to get on rides, no exorbitant admissions fees; just the ability to hang out in a Disney-themed shopping district, eat, drink, and have fun.

I took the bus ( behind coke store) to Disney boardwalk. you can ride the bus free to any Disney resort and parks. Great place to shop and fun til you drop!!

final Drop is dope. Marvelous

we have visited this in off season so it was only 10 minutes wait for us. Lucky us :) as people have waited even 2-3 hours for this ride in peak season

Each boat holds plenty of people. when it starts, the Jurrasic Park theme music, and when the gate opens, you get goosebumps. The beginning is a little boring, where dinosaurs are emerging from water or bushes,  but the atmosphere is great and kids seemed to love it. you will feel the fire heat. You get squirt by water no matter where you sit. Then after you go off the path into the raptor containment area where you can hear a panicked voice telling you to turn around.  The tiny dinosaurs are eating an employee's shirt as you go underneath a shaking cage that emits enraged velociraptor sounds.

The last corner takes you straight into the path of a T-rex that looms out of the fog.  The ride eventually raises you up to the top of the control tower and from there to escape the Tyrannosaurus Rex you are dropped from a height with a splash.  the climb is in totally dark so you don't know how big the drop would be. that was fun.  The finale is fantastic and what really makes this water ride special.

I have read many reviews where people are saying you 'll get wet/soaked completely. See if you are front, chances are you 'll get wet, but not completely and no, you won't be soaked in water. I was at 3rd row and there was just a splash of water. I have carried our ponchos with me but if you don't carry, its still fine.

There is a great observation area outside the ride at the water drop and i have taken few beautiful shots of it

We visited Liberty science center- Empty sky memorial and this in one day. its 20 mins drive from empty sky memorial. its inside New Jersey marine terminals, not like in some park or crowded location so we were very skeptical "are we going in the right direction", but kudos to GPS, we reached here. it was not crowded at all. in fact you can find more people in your neighborhood public park.

Teardrop memorial is also known as To the Struggle Against World Terrorism or the Tear of Grief. when I saw the picture of this memorial on the internet, I did not think it would be this much bigger. its 10-story sculpture and was given to the United States as an official gift from the Russian government as a memorial to the victims of the September 11 attacks in 2001, 26 of whom were Russian and  1993 World Trade Center bombing. it's in Bayonne county.

It was dust time and it was shining in copper color. You can have a good view of the Statue of liberty and Manhattan in the backdrop. Staten island ferry-Brooklyn bridge-Manhattan bridge- one can have a great view of these from this place.  We spent around 45 minutes to 1 hr here. It was very soothing.
Parking: it's free and very near to the memorial. this is not very popular but it's one of the best memorial dedicated to 9/11 victims. its hidden gem.

Such a fun attraction and Free too..!!

I loved that the water show was so quick, something like 10 minutes. There are 4 different musical themes and they rotate all the time.  A nice walk to Bellagio to see the fountain show is perfect. I love that the fountains "dance" to the music. Viva Las Vegas was perfect! You would definitely find this picture of fountains in postcards or movies.

This is synonyms to Vegas and iconic fountain.   I love the choreographed water and music display. It's great that they don't display the same show over and over again. They ll play diff song each time.
Don’t worry if you are not getting place in the crowd, it happens at every 15 minutes, let this show go, and find a perfect spot for next show. This is one of the few Vegas Bucket List items you can check off in less than a half hour including drive time and parking

know the history related to this monument…

It was erected in commemoration of the Bunker Hill Battle. The battle was fought on June 17, 1775. It was one of the first major engagements between British soldiers and American patriots during the Revolutionary War.
The walk from the USS Constitution up through the surrounding neighborhood was beautiful. The monument is a hollow granite tower with a staircase on the interior.

Skip it if you're claustrophobic or if breathing isn't your forte. space is small and the views out over the area are not eye-popping by any means. We're glad we climbed to the top, but it may not be worth it to everyone.

The guy at the information desk was super nice and gave us more info on our next stop, the USS Constitution, and told us about the tour times and ferry information. I guess it the end of freedom trail which starts from Boston Common.

First off, many of the bad reviews have been written by people who had no clue what they were doing.  The Main Exhibit, which is two and a half floors of displays and artifacts, requires a ticket for timed entry during the busy months.  The rest of the exhibits are free but make up a very small part of the whole.
The Main Exhibit takes, at least, three to four hours just to skim through.  I have met people who have gone back three days in a row to see it from start to finish.  During the summer months, when tickets are used, it IS very crowded.  They also have reserved groups from schools and clubs and tour groups that can make the Main Exhibit VERY crowded.  It wasn't built to handle large numbers of visitors and the first hallway can become jammed.  The tickets were put in place to try to stop that but there are always VIPs and Membership card holders who can bypass the system by their very importance.  So there are always more people in the Main Exhibit than there should be.
This is not a half-hour visit.  IF you were smart enough to get a ticket plan to spend most of the day.  And have patience.
Now for the bad - security is not known for being polite and patient (even when I worked there).  And for some reason visitors are never ready to go through security even though they have had to go through security in many of the other museums.  The security here is like airport security.
Just put everything into a BAG.
And many of the Visitor Service staff who pass out tickets, work the desks, and such were not hired for their knowledge of history - they are there to help run the museum.  You want to learn?  Get ready to read for many, many, many hours.  Most of us who had degrees in history left, or were fired, many years ago.  The Manage treated their employees like the  security guards treated the visitors.  And the good guards have found better jobs with the Smithsonian.
The museum cafe is a museum cafe in another building on 15th Street.  If you want real food I suggest going to the Museum of Native Americans or maybe the National Gallery of Art.  Otherwise all the museum cafes have museum cafe food.  To complain about museum food just shows how many of the reviewers never leave the house.
There are bathrooms on each floor BUT the ground floor and there are gift shops and, unless being worked on, a checkroom.
And you will find lots of children, people using their phones and cameras, and being entitled.  The folks who respected it, who came to learn about the Holocaust, visited shortly after it opened so many years ago.  NOW most of the visitors you will run into are there to take a photo with the few remaining survivors, grab a postcard, and say they visited the museum.  In other words people who are just passing through.  People who are trying to visit as many places as they can in one day for selfies for their Facebook. And to the museum they are numbers, so many voters that pass through each day, so they can get a yearly allowance from Congress.
IF you don't want that - visit one of the art museums.  Few people go to those and there are no kids and very few people talking on their phones or using their cameras with flash.
In short - great museum where even the building was built to be part of the exhibits (like the American Indian and the African American Museums later were) but badly thought out when it came to crowd control and safety and the handling of security.

The National Museum of African American History And Culture took over a hundred to finally be built.  And it was worth it.  The main exhibit, three floors, is about the history of African Americans - from when they were taken from Africa right up to the present.  There are other exhibits that focus on Culture, art, and so on.  The whole museum could take all day depending how much you want to read.  I found the main exhibit to be a tad confusing but I did like that on the ramps to the next floor were benches and videos, to help focus and explain what you had seen and what you were about to see next.
The building, like those of the Holocaust and American Indian museums, was designed to house the exhibits.
The food in the cafe is, like most museums, somewhat pricey.  But I feel worth the price.  There is only so many places in DC I would say that about.  I REALLY enjoyed the Gulf Shrimp and Grits.
And the staff, and security, were the most friendly and helpful of any museum.
Just a few things to look out for - right now is slow season so no tickets are required UNLESS you have a group.  The building had TWO entry ways and the on one the Constitution Ave side was free of groups when I visited.  I think they line up on other side of the building.  Also, the only fault I can find, was there is only one set of restrooms in the main exhibit.  Don't worry, all the other floors have restrooms and, of course, elevators for wheelchairs or baby strollers.
Outside of that one flaw I really enjoyed my visit and will likely visit it a few more times in the future.

Want to know more about the history of Fredericksburg and the Civil War?  Well, this is the place.  Mostly ignored because, to be honest, I don't think a lot of people know it is just across the river from Frederickburgs.  Of course, Washington visited here - he visits everywhere - and during the Civil War the union army occupied it and artillery was placed to watch over the town.It ended up becoming a hospital for the wounded after the First Battle of Fredericksburg.
Walking around the grounds, and gardens, are free.  The manor contains some exhibits and, last I was there, was also free.  As many parts of the grounds (and building) have been restored from different periods it is a wonderful mixture of different styles.

Nice.  Big.  Flashy.  The SECOND FDR Memorial.  As the first one, the one he wanted, is by the Archives.  This one even has a gift shop and restrooms and HAD working water fountains.  Or it did before  flooding.  The Tidal Basin is a harsh mistress. The Memorial has statues of him, his dog, and his wife.  Funny enough, last time I saw, the dog is with him and the wife is by herself.  Both were great historical figures.  FDR and his wife, not the dog.  But I have to take a star away.  This is NOT the memorial he wanted and I am pretty sure he would not like the statue that shows him in a wheelchair.  He never wanted to be known as a good President in a wheelchair.  He just wanted to be known as a good President.

I have been to the Virginia Holocaust Museum.  Once in the old building and once in this new one.  Wonderful world class museum.  I am not sure if the people of Richmond or those of Virginia truly understand how impressive the building, the exhibit, the artifacts are.  Just very world class - I would put this up there with museums I have visited in Europe and the rest of North America.  If visiting out of the US, and you could only visit one museum, I would strongly suggest this Holocaust museum over the one in DC.  Just, it is THAT good.  You can feel how much emotion and energy went into trying to tell the stories of the people, the families, the victims in this museum.

A nice little museum.  Kind of small town museum for spending a couple of hours in.  Focused mostly about the town's history and trains, of course, it feels like something you would find made by the town's 4-H club.  If they had such a thing.  Two floors, full of real history.  Objects and letters and artwork from generations of people living and working in the town and region.  It also touches on the American Civil War, Strasburg potery (which is a big deal in this region), and the railroad.  It WAS a railroad station after all.  It is one of those museums that people of all ages would enjoy and, to be honest, it just made happy to visit it.

First off, this two museums in one, because the Portrait Gallery is also in here.  Second, they redid the whole building and made it into likely one of the top ten museums in the world.  At least on my list.  Lots to see.  Wonderful courtyard and always a treat to visit.  Unlike some of the smaller museums it WILL be crowded.  It is WELL KNOWN and right on top of a Metro Station which means easy access.  Also surrounded by dozens of food places and historical sites if you know where to look.  Close to Chinatown AND the National Building Museum.

This is a first class museum.  Trust me, I have been to a few.  One of the reasons it is so fun to visit is not just the modern feel to the displays and exhibits but how much they have to work with.  Not only were there Native Americans in the region.  Not only was the town in the middle of much of the American Civil War in Virginia.  But millions of years ago there were dinosaurs running about.  They know because they have all the footprints the dinosaurs left behind.  Perfect for visitors of all ages.

As a person who loves colonial history and American history and tavern history I was hugely impressed by my group's guide to the museum.  He REALLY did not just know his history.  He UNDERSTOOD it.  Learned a lot about the historical tavern and local history.
As for the working tavern the food was okay but, like most tavern/museum/tourist food places it may be a tad more expensive than you like.  And the waiting staff was a tad slow.

Visited it a couple of times.  Once with my Mom and once with co-workers.  Lovely exhibits, friendly people, and I can't really put in words just how lovely the whole structure is.  Even the grounds AROUND it give it a feeling of calmness.  There is so much history here and it is a MUST visit for anybody visiting Alexandria, the DC area, or visiting the state itself.  Just make sure to check the website for tour times and so on.

I have been here a few times but not lately so take this with a little salt.  I never found it crowded and it is easy to get out being right next to Union Station.  I felt the exhibits were more for kids and teens and also many of the interactive exhibits, at the time, never seemed to work.  Still, after saying that what it does have was interesting interesting as I always find history interesting.

Living in Virginia this is one of the places you should visit.  Not a place I would put on your A-List but still a good place to visit.  As a fan of Lovecraft and King of course I ended up going to The Edgar Allan Poe Museum.  Small house turned into a museum and while it was not crowded when I was there I can see CROWDS being a real problem when you go there.  I would say a half-a-day visit.

The pool does what it is named for - reflecting the Washington Monument.  Lovely place to rest and have lunch during a visit to the Mall.  Not as crowded as other areas but will FLOOD if the rain is hard enough.  I've been there when the sidewalks were totally covered in water and the ducks could swim about the sidewalks.  They even attacked my ankles the little monsters.

Lots of history and when I was there had a display from the not yet open African-American Museum.  Escaped slaves use to hide within the Swamp from their owners and even traded with slaves on the plantations.  Also a few wonderful nature exhibits.  And when I was there not crowded at all.  I don't think many people even know this place exists!  Watch out for wild animals!

The Visitor Center for the Jamestown site.  Not to be confused with the Settlement.  A film, a few exhibits and artifacts.  Restrooms of course and a gift shop.  Entry way to the Jamestown Historic site.  Partly run by the Federal government.  Remember to check the weather before going.  Also remember to check the websites to see what discounts are available for you.

Love this sculpture garden.  Has wonderful, silly, fun artwork and even a ice rink during the cold months.  A restaurant and restrooms if you need them.  Of course the food is pricey - but then again so is much of the cafes, restaurants, and food places on the Mall and in DC.
They also have special events so sometimes it may be crowded.

Great place to visit - make sure to check the weather before going - and never very crowded.  Not as well known as the Mall's museums so it will likely never be crowded.  Can get there via the bus lines or just take a car - there is parking.  Exhibits change and also just a nice place for the family or a jog.  And picnicking is okay.

The museum is, in fact, the result of two museums being put into one building.  In fact, right now, they are doing work to expand the building so parking can be hard to find.  Close to the Williamsburg exhibits and has something for everything.  The whole family can enjoy it.  Christmas is the best time to see it.

The Memorial is a little known one, not crowded at all, about one of the founding fathers.  Overshadowed by the Thomas Jefferson Memorial it is a nice spot to come, rest, and learn history.  If you are going to walk about the Tidal Basin you may as well visit this memorial.

Really something to go to Richmond to see.  How many Tudor houses are in the United States of America?  Beautiful building, good tour, could spend a lot of time in there if I had been allowed to. Wonderful part of the city also.  Enjoy the feeling of going back in time.

Rarely go to the Hirshhorn as I find 9 out 10 of its pieces either uninteresting or, to be honest, confusing.  Sometimes I find something I like, or is beautiful, or catches my eye, or makes me think.  But rarely.  I just prefer the other art museums.

A great little place to see many of the craft used in the space program and a nice little park by itself for bringing the family.  Lots of information for people interested in American history or NASA.
Wonderful place to visit, relaxing, good staff, just make sure not to go during special events because it will be crowded!  Outside of that it is a island of calm in a ocean of noise and chaos.

Wonderful historical Church - make sure to take your hat off - and was attended by the Washington and Lee families.  Went there with my Mom.
Worth a visit and the architecture is beautiful.
Archaeology museum with Native American artifacts, findings from the settlement, and changing exhibits.  First class museum.  Always fun to visit and also has a nice gift shop.

Wow! Nothing but great experiences here!! Very easy location to access, parking lot is large enough for everybody. Purchasing tickets was an easy process, there was a line so it was not really quick for my family and I, but that is understandable.  We got items from the gift shop (pair of sandals for a young girl) for under $10, which is astounding for any water park gift shop I have ever been in! When we were buying our tickets we were told that there was a special on for that day, so we saved nearly $50 off the regular admission prices. There is a great selection of thrills and fun here! I personally was not a fan of the two highest slides, but I can see how they would be fun for a wide range of thrill seekers (too much for me!). Both of my children had a blast here! The food we ordered was delicious and reasonably priced, as well as the lockers. Great place to come and play!

My family were super excited to stop here! Every moment of our experience was incredible! All of the staff were super friendly, especially Joan. She really added so much enjoyment to our time here while we were waiting for our event of a dolphin meet and greet to begin. She provided so much valuable information and really seemed dedicated to the work she does! The dolphin experience was incredible! It was so fun watching them, seeing how much the trainers care about the work they do and how well taken care of everything is. I am so thankful we decided to come here rather than Sea World for our first dolphin experience, and really if we are ever in the area again this is where we will continue to go. Thank you for such an amazing experience from start to finish!

My favorite children's museum I have ever been to! My children and their niece love this place! There are 3 levels of fun for kiddos to explore, with excellent hand-on-learning experiences within each floor. On the bottom, there is a sand play area, airplane, classroom, giant Lego blocks, rock climbing wall, Badger play area, and more. On the second level there is a nursery area, bubble table, post office, grocery store, bank, doll house, Hungry Howie's Pizza Station, House of Flavors Ice Cream Station, a giant model eye ball, and a veterinarian. On the top there is a new construction zone, a farm with tractor, and a band area with stage and instruments. There are so many fun things to do here, it is very easy to spend hours of play time!

Very fun and scenic place to stop! The gift shop where you start out at has an incredible variety of gifts and souvenirs at some of the most affordable prices I have ever encountered at a gift shop. The Paul Bunyan and Babe statues are very fun for children to see, as well as the Bigfoot in the woods at the beginning of your climb. There are benches to rest on if needed on the way up. The view at the top is incredible! You are able to see nearby islands and well as the Mackinac Bridge. I have been here a couple of times and every time it is always a great experience!

Was here on a rainy day, so no line for the front seat whatsoever! That being said, this was higher than any other coaster I have ever been on by nearly 200 feet! I was not expecting how quick the lift hill is (which is excellent by the way), nor the force, speed and exhilaration in which you fly down the first hill and every hill, twist and turn after that. The best coaster I have ever been on, and probably one of the most terrifying! Not sure I would ever ride it again, but the experience was incredible. A must ride for every coaster enthusiast!

Great experience here! Really easy directions to get here, ample sized parking lot so there is space for everyone. Admission prices are affordable. Staff and tour guides are super friendly and informative! The caves themselves are an amazing sight, accompanied by the tour it is a wonderful experience! The gift shop is surprisingly affordable with a great variety of items, souvenirs and gifts. I didn't have time to visit the other areas that are included with the admission tickets.

Beautiful place to splash and play!! We all had a lot of fun here! Playground was a lot of fun, plenty of variety to keep my entire family satisfied and running around. Beach area was very nice! Parking is free if you arrive early enough in the day, which is very nice! Parking lot is close by and very convenient. I came here two times, both times were incredible, though the first it was not good weather. Definitely will come back here if I am ever in the area again!

Very nice roadside attraction! Very cute site! We came here around 9 am on a Monday, we were the only ones there that morning. It was really foggy, and around the cars was super muddy, but we still went through the mud to get up close to the cars and do a little spray painting. This is a very neat attraction, so glad to have stopped here while in Amarillo! There is also a gift shop nearby, but I didn't have a chance to stop there.

Exceptionally beautiful! Arch Rock is always a must see when on Mackinac Island! The views are incredible. Nearby hiking trails add a lot of fun to this area as well. I usually walk here when on the island which can be quite a walk, but there are rest areas all around if needed. Love the different viewing areas as well! Even on a cold rainy day, this place is exquisite!

Very neat free roadside attraction. The abandoned gas station and other buildings add to the feel of this. Very cool place to stop and see. It is not well maintained, but you are able to spray paint on the vehicles. There is graffiti everywhere- the cars, buildings, but it seems to be acceptable. Cool and quirky, definitely worth stopping to see!

I didn't ride this, in the morning while at Hersheypark I honestly was too afraid, and when I finally mustered the courage to go on everything was closed because there was a thunderstorm coming so never got the chance to go on. Great looking roller coaster however, definitely looks very thrilling, surely it is a lot of fun!

Beautiful place to play on the Grand Traverse Bay!! Usually less crowded than the Traverse City Beaches. Has a lot of historic information about the Greilickville area on the walkway. Public restrooms, nice sandy beach, and a fun playground for children makes this a great place to come spend the day!
likes: Facilities & Services: Public restrooms, sandy beach

reviews_attraction.text: Beautiful public beach on Torch Lake! There is a small, but fun, playground for little ones, picnic areas, nice sized parking areas, as well as a boat ramp for those boating. Very fun place to play and you can't beat that crystal clear Torch Lake water! Always smiles when we stop here!!

Fun and educational place for children to visit! We all (4 of us) had a lovely time visiting here! Reasonable prices for admissions and gift shop. Staff was super friendly and helpful. Great location. Love the variety of hands-on-exhibits for children of all ages.

Great little water park for an affordable price! Kind of on the small side, but it is fun nonetheless! Great variety of thrills to meet the expectations of children of all ages! Always have great fun here! They also have an arcade which is an added bonus!

Great place to go skiing or snowboarding. Love the enhancement on the tow rope for the learning area. Also love the new ski lift. Great runs at Caberfae. Staff are always kind and efficient. Absolutely love coming here to ski and dine!

Very fun racing roller coaster! The lines move fast as there are two lines for two different trains. It is a lot of fun while riding to see who the winner will be. Wooden coaster but rides pretty smooth. Great fun!

Upper Falls are absolutely breathtaking!! Great views from all around! Lovely walk to get to the brink, a LOT of steps though, which makes the return interesting for those out of shape. Had a lot of fun!

Very large zoo! Excellent selection of exhibits, staff are all very friendly and helpful. Parking lot is large and easy to access. Admission prices are very fair and reasonable. Great way to spend a day!

Very beautiful State Park! Palo Duro Canyon has extensive views in all directions. Beautiful hiking trails of various difficulty level. Gift shops and scenic overlooks make this a truly great experience.

Beautiful state park in the Upper Peninsula of Michigan! The falls are beautiful! Great spots for camping, kayak/canoe rental, gift shop, bathrooms, ample parking, and more! Definitely worth the trip!
Beautiful public beach on Crystal Lake! Crisp, clear waters, fun playground, ample parking! A really great place to spend the day. Nearby shops in Beulah make this place even better!
Very beautiful park with lovely views of the Mackinac Bridge and the northern part of Lake Michigan. A really great park to relax and enjoy the views.
Beautiful little spot on the side of the road! We weren't able to stay long and explore, but really glad to have found this little place!
Great sight to see while in downtown Detroit! Always well maintained, and the area has a pretty safe feel to it!

This museum was awesome. I'm not an airplane enthusiast, but these were quite interesting. There is a WWII hanger and a WWI hanger. The volunteers are super knowledgeable and very friendly. I learned a lot about war planes. Come on a summer Saturday to catch an airplane show. In spite of the fact that you can't touch anything, my two boys, 4 and 7 yo, were intrigued the entire visit. Big parking lot available. Don't forget to stop by the dinosaur park on your way out. Entrance fee required to the museum, dinosaur park is free.

Do you miss walking on grass? This place offers a little bit of everything. Start behind the visitor's center for a short sensory walk on a shady path. Then head inside the visitors center to see a small, but well stocked reptile exhibit. Your little kids will enjoy splashing on Pebble Beach. It's rocky, so I recommend water shoes. Take a stroll on grassy or paved paths. It's calm and relaxing. There is also a small playground. Picnic tables also available. Bathroom was open and very clean. Loop

This is a cool museum for any train enthusiast or if you want to see something different. There are many displays and just the right amount of media to learn more. The staff are friendly and knowledgable. My 3- and 6- year olds had a great time. There is also a playroom with fireman costumes, a real fire truck, and other toys. There is a large, free parking lot. Don't forget to go the demonstration in the back about how fire alarms worked in the past.

This is a nice playground with two play areas. One area is enclosed for smaller kids and the other area is for the older kids. The enclosed play area has a large sand lot. There are plenty of benches and shadey spots to watch your children play or have a picnic. Adjacent is an open field, a basketball court, and tennis courts. There are bathrooms in the recreation center on the grounds. There is free street parking available.
likes: Play areas for different age groups

reviews_attraction.text: Fun place to visit. Kids will enjoy finding all the fairy houses. There are also sculptures along the path. Also neat is that they put together natural materials (branches, bark) for those who feel inspired to build their fairy creation. My kids enjoyed the playground. Masks are required inside. It was not very busy on a Sunday so social distancing was not a prblem. The bathrooms were open and there was plenty of parking.

Great gardens for strolling. Lots of pretty areas with views and benches to take a break. The ponds are full of lily pads and fish. My 4- and 6- year olds especially enjoyed the children's garden and the fairy garden. The paved path is accessible for wheelchairs and strollers. Open green spaces allow for social distancing. Lots of parking. Very modest entrance fee. Face masks are required to enter.

Scenic area with hiking trails. It is open with great views of the mountains. There is an historic area with a gift shop and bathrooms - both were open. We bought some vegetables at a small outdoor table. You can also feed the chickens with feed from a coin machine. There was plenty of parking and the trails were not too busy. Lots of people wearing masks and conscious of social distancing.

Large playground with several play areas: one for tiny tots and another for bigger kids with swings, climbing wall, slides, musical center, and kid's zipline. There is also an open green space (turf) and basketball court. Bathrooms are available. Plenty of benches and some tables. Street parking is available and can be somewhat difficult, but not impossible, to find a spot.

Good diversity of marine animals. One way traffic, 6 feet apart stickers, hand sanitizer everywhere, and timed entry tickets made for good safety precautions. However, it felt just a little crowded to comfortably enjoy all the exhibits. They could benefit from more staff to monitor crowds at popular exhibits and slow the number of people allowed at one time.

Cool park for hiking, picnicking, and tubing. There is a playground area at the Avalon entrance parking lot. The parking lots can full pretty early. We hiked the Gristmil trail which is shady and paved, so it's good for strollers & bikes. This trail also goes along the water. There is small per person entrance fee to the park. Kids in carseats are free.

The playground is big, but it was very busy. There are picnic tables and plenty of green space surrounds the playground. The train and carousel were closed. Most people on the playground did not wear face coverings and social distancing was difficult given the number of people there. We chose to leave for safety. We will return after covid.

Nice area to explore. We saw pigs, chickens and goats. The path is easy to follow. You walk along the lake or walk on the pier for a view. If you have little kids they will enjoy hunting for the fairy houses. Very cute. The parking lot is ample and there arw porta potties. Plenty of space for safe social distancing.

Big campground with lots of camp sights. There is a small camp store with various items including firewood. The lake is nice. Various trails including a loop around the lake. Bathrooms have plenty of signs requesting folks to wear masks inside. Most people were considerate of the mask rule, but not everyone.

Nice lake with walking parh. You can rent boats and kayaks. They sell live bait for fishing. There are lots of covered picnic areas all over the grounds. Plenty of parking areas too. Drawbacks: it can get busy and the bathrooms are currently closed due to Covid19. Only porta-potties available.

Nice, easy loop around the lake. Lots of walkers and runners. Some picnic areas and available rentals. There are also paddle boat and kayak rentals during the season. The playground is old and rundown and the carousal is closed for the season. Bathrooms were open. Plenty of parking.

We went to The Playgrounds at Patterson Park. This is a spacious castle-themed playground. There is also a smaller playground area. Lots of green space surrounds the playground  with some scattered benches. There are walking paths right next to the playground and a large pond.

Cute park on the smaller side, but sufficient. It's divided into two sections, one for smaller kids and the other for older kids. There is field attached with a track that goes around. Metered parking is available right out front. One drawback is the lack of bathrooms.

Quiet place for a relaxing stroll, reading or meditating. This place is small but very pretty with small doses of religious  artifacts throughout. There are lots of benches. The koi pond is popular with the kids. There is free parking lot right across the street.

Small playground geared more to younger kids and toddlers. There is a big green space with lots of trees. There is also a large sports field and a tennis court. Street parking is very restricted, but there is a parking lot located next to the tennis courts.

Calm gardens to take a stroll or have a picnic. Look for turtles in of the two ponds. There are a couple gazebos you can rent. The bathrooms were closed. Signs requesting face coverings and social distancing. Plenty of parking.

There's a little of everything here. Lots of fishing along the water, beach area, hiking, and historical fort. The furthest point parking lot was full, but there are parking lots in other areas. The entry fee is $7 per adult.

We visited the lake. Rowboat, kayak and pedal boat rentals by the hour or day. Fast and friendly staff. They spray down the boats and life jackets. Limited green space by the lake. There are also various trails.
Great museum with lots of interesting facts and exhibits. There is a kids play area on the third floor which includes interactive displays and a reading library. There is a cafe on the first floor.
Cool fort, short visit. You can go inside the buildings, which are meant to be historically accurate. There is 30 minute parking at the street entrance.
Cute, small stop with life-size dinosaurs. This is a great additional stop on your way into or out of the Military Aviation Museum.

Parking can be limited during the weekends so be sure to plan accordingly. Once you cross the wooden bridge with the tree through it you'll be going mostly downhill until you reach the river. There's a small dam at the bottom where you can do some mild "cliff jumping" and enjoy the water on warmer days. The swinging bridge will take you to the other bank of the river where you can take the trail to Mushroom rock or some nice overlooks.

What a phenomenal place. The main lobby is stunning and you can spend a while just staring upwards. I recommend taking the tours that are offered several times daily. They’ll take you to places that are available to people just walking around, but you’ll get a lot of background info that’s useful. Be sure to see the Gutenberg Bible, the first map with the word America on it, and get your library card to access the main reading room!

So we didn’t make it for an oral argument, but there was still lots to see and do. There’s an exhibit on the main level with lots of history on the building and the justices. You can go to the second level and enter the court room and gawk at the high ceilings and important furniture. At certain times of the day you’ll be able to listen to a lecture while sitting in the public seating area. Cool place to visit.

So I might be a bit biased since I grew up by this park, but I really enjoy what it was to offer. You’ll find one of the only “hills” in South Florida here and I spent a good amount of my childhood rolling all the way down it. They’ve also got a lake (which admittedly has seen cleaner days) that sometimes hosts an alligator and even manatee! There’s a new playground near the west entrance which looks great.

The national arboretum is funded by the USDA and is here for the enjoyment of the people. There’s a lot to see and driving around is probably the best idea. There is also a bike share station at the front where you can pick up a bike to explore. The Bonsais are probably some of the coolest things you’ll find here. But there’s also some columns that used to be a part of the capital building.

So if you didn’t know there was a national historic site here you would definitely pass it by because it’s super inconspicuous. There’s two floors of office space that Carter Woodson used in the fight to make black history more prominent during his time. You’ll be able to take an informative tour of the house and even do a junior ranger if you can. It’s worth a visit if you’re in the area.

What an awe inspiring building. This is where the rubber meets the road in our government. You’re able to see the statues and important places on the tour, but be sure to stop by your senator’s office to get passes to enter the house and senate chambers. It’s definitely worth making it in while they’re in session. Please don’t visit DC without taking this free tour.

This is one of the jewels Chattanooga is lucky to have. This is first place I think of going when the weather is nice and I’m wanting to go downtown. You can lay in the sun, play ball, go on the carousel, cross the bridge, or visit any of the awesome shops and restaurants that are close by. The views of the river and bluffs are what make me know I’m home.

It's so great that we have such a well done memorial park here in Collegedale. It's all very well done and pays our veterans the respect they deserve. You'll find a tank, a helicopter, and a fighter jet all displayed here. You can also look out for your state flag as all 50 states are represented. There is also a great tribute to Desmond Doss.

Not many people know that there are hiking and biking trails right next to downtown Chatt. It’s about a mile from Coolidge park, and offers a pretty great overlook of the city. The trails are well maintained and regularly used. Parking is on the south side of the park, and they have bike tools at the trail head if you need to do any repairs.

This large park in DC provides so much room to enjoy nature and feel like you’re miles away from civilization while still being close to everything. The nature center has lots of information on the plants and animals you’ll encounter in the park, and there’s also a planetarium to take you far beyond this earth.

I'm so glad we have such a great museum in our city. I've had a membership at the Hunter for as long as I've lived here because the permanent collection is vast and because there is almost always something new to get excited about. Also, come on, the location is amazing! Beautiful views from every angle.

What an awe inspiring building. The gothic architecture will take you right to Europe and save you the plane ticket. I wasn’t able to go inside, but it’s $8 for students and free on Sundays. There’s a gargoyle of Darth Vadar on one of the sides and plenty of other cool things to discover here.

A very impressive busy indeed. MLK deserves the greatest homage we can give him, and the placement of this memorial does just that. I love it. You can see the tidal basin and the Jefferson memorial clearly from this point. Be sure to read the engraved words and signs placed around.

What a sobering experience. More than 400,000 Americans lost their lives in this struggle and countless more from other countries paid the ultimate sacrifice. The grounds are mostly kept up, and it’s a great monument to the accomplishments of the time.

What a nice and well preserved building! I thoroughly enjoyed my time at this memorial. It is in a beautiful park and a quiet part of town. Be sure to look up the times for tours before showing up because they can be spaced out.

It's amazing to be walking around with your tour and look into rooms where dignitaries from various country are about to meet in. This massive building stands as a testament to what can be accomplished when people work together.

Please come for a visit if you're in town. There is so much to be learned about Dr. King's work and legacy. The park is more than just the visitor's center though. Visit his birth house and church all within a block's distance.

The figures are so real and live like. It takes you to the battle field in Korea and helps us understand the horrors they must have gone through to push back the enemy. Lovely park just off of the national mall(:
It's hard for me to say how I liked it. All there is to see is the part in the middle of this square. The Stonewall Inn was closed when I went to visit and the LGBT community center was also closed.
What an amazing museum. This is pretty much the top of the top when it comes to modern art. All your favorite artists are represented here. Come on certain Friday evenings for free entrance!
So many fantastic paintings and sculptures. The highlights for are the president’s corner, featuring the new Obama portrait, and the Grand Canyon portrait. Simply stunning.
Please carve out several hours out of your day to spend here. There is so much to take in and learn about. An hour or two is not enough. Be prepared to cry and to listen.
The ferry ride is very quick and the lines to go through security go by rather smoothly. Be sure to pick up your free audio tour at the beginning.
This place is so interesting!! You’ll find bonsai trees that are over 400 years old here and be calmed by zen of this place.

Outstanding military museum showing the history of the Eighty Air Force. Recommended three hours to enjoy the museum. The restaurant is excellent. Can order from menu or there is a daily two entree buffet. The B 17 is outstanding maintained. Several outstanding films on the history of air power during World War II. Children will usually enjoy the museum. Private non profit . Senior, student, and military discount. Highly recommended.

Outstanding museum on various period in news media history. Local news says the museum is scheduled to closed January of 2020. A big lost for Washington. The building is quite magnificent. Excellent food court with multiple selections. The Berlin Wall exhibit is outstanding. Also the FBI exhibit is well done. Gift shop is large and we'll stocked. Highly recommend a visit to the museum before it closes.
likes: Facilities & Services (magnificent building, excellent food court, large gift shop)

reviews_attraction.text: Excellent park for Civil War buffs and historians. One or two stars for others. The two 15" Rodman shore batteries are outstanding  but hard to get to there location.  Parts of the trails are rough. Tree branches to climb over. Wonderful  view of the Potomac.  National  Harbor and Jones Point park can be seen across the river. Wear good hiking shoes. A walking stick is also nice to carry.
likes: Scenic views (Potomac, National Harbor, Jones Point park)

reviews_attraction.text: Excellent residential park. Basketball court,  paved walking loop, playground,  and picnic tables. Limited used to the banks of the Susquehanna River. Beautiful view of the river and the bridge across the river. The old bridge pillars are still there. Historical view of where Richard Ewell Confederate troops were planning to cross the Susquehanna in June 1863.

I rate the trail 5 stars. The Manor House and stone barn were closed. Restrooms closed. The trail is a good representation of the underground railroad. Not a loop trail . There are a couple of paths off the trail to the road. Recommend walking the trail and having someone pick you up a designated place. Trail is shown on Google Maps.

30 acres park in the historical section of Savannah. Very well maintained. Multiple monuments to various wars. Beautiful fountain in the center of the part. DOT pickup/drop off stops on three sides of the parks. The park is very popular in Savannah for walking. Benches are available. The part is a MUST SEE when you visit. Savannah.

The Clara Barton site is not for everyone. History buffs will enjoy the visit. The home is in the process of being updated. The furniture has been removed. The National  Park Ranger gave an outstanding presentation on Clara  Life. The house is open on Friday/Saturday for guided tour. Highly recommended for people who enjoy history.

Five trails to hike. Between 1.6 and 5.5 miles in length. Trails are mowed with arrows and colored markings  on each trail. Limited benches and tables along trails. Very good parking area. Trails are probably wet during during rainy season.  Recommended  for hiking and nature walks. Trails are for hikers and horseback riders.

Outstanding park in the city. Multiple pavilions for rent for large groups. Smaller covered open pavilions for free. Several restrooms. Excellent boardwalk and walking/biking trail. Short but very good. Outstanding nature walk except for you can hear alot of road noise. Highly recommended for a relaxing walk.

Spent the day with friends at Disney Springs. Outstanding day. Many restaurants for lunch and dinner. It's easier to choose the type of food you want, not the restaurant. Numberous opportunities for shopping of all types. Good place to spend the day. Some days can be very crowded.

Rated five stars because I like historical sites. Civil War confedate fort bombarded for 30 hours prior to surrender. Excellent film on the history of the fort. The fort is in excellent condition. Highly recommended for Civil War buffs and people who like history.

Civil War battlefield that took place in 1864 in Maryland. Small but excellent visitor's center. The battlefield is spread over several areas. Recommend the driving tour. Excellent location for walking. Areas are mowed but not paved. Time spent one to two hours.

Excellent display of very large ship models. Three stores with no elevator. Small gift shop. Outstanding gardens on the grounds of the museum. Small children would not enjoy. If you like examples of maritime history, you'll find this museum outstanding.

Excellent group of buildings from early homesteading in central Florida. The Methodist  church is outstanding. These types of preservation a must to keep history alive. Good place for visit by children to see life in early Florida.  Highly recommended.

Outstanding tour guide for main house. More like an English Manor house than a plantation house. Excellent work on preservation. Lots of walking. Excellent dining room for lunch. Good service. Have cabins for overnight. Excellent view of the river?

The building that houses the Builder's Museum is amazing. The building tour is the only way to see the total building. The museum is average but the tour is outstanding. The tour includes both the history of the building and it's,s consternation..

A must see for people who like Civil War sites. Others might think it's a waste of time. Hard to find without some form of map quest or Google maps. The house is open only ranger is present. A must see civil war buffs and Stonewall fans.

Great for Civil War buffs. Google maps may take you to the wrong place. Lee's Lane had a small roadside parking area. 20 to 30 round trip walk to the top of Lee's hill. Good signage on the battle. Stop 3 on the driving tour.

Outstanding battlefield park with superior signage to describe the battle. Great place for a short walk(brick paved walk) by yourself or with your dog. Civil War buffs will highly enjoy the battlefield descriptions.

Five stars for Civil War buffs. Three stars for everyone else. Rough walking trails.  Excellent view on how the terrain looked in the 1860s.  Be careful when hiking, no paved trails and very little markings.
Small Memorial part on the road to Gettysburg from Tanneytown. Well maintained.  Large park with playground behind the memorial park. Excellent information signage.
Small museum but very informative. Shows George Washington St an early age. As  Colonel in the Virginia militia, he was tasked with building a fort at Winchester.
Out of way place not connected to the Battle of Gettysburg.  Walking bridge only. Accessible from roads of ever side. Saw or felt no spirits.  Good view.
Excellent small road side park. The covered bridge is single lane and used.  Restrooms available.  Small play area and one covered picnic  table.
One of many plaza honoring the military services, persons of history, or historical events. The small Navy museum is very nice.

Only found this by happen stance when visiting the nearby museum. It is a picturesque park and historic monument.  You can access the inside the monument for free but have to pay by credit card to climb the stairs.  It is recommended to pay online but walk-ins can usually be accommodated. Note the park in the outer circle by the church may have a few homeless laying around - eh, it is Baltimore after all.
Here are the year 2019 particulars:
Hours of Operation:
The Monument is open to the public year round, except Thanksgiving & Christmas Day.
• Wed. through Sun. 10AM – 5PM
• Open Wed. evenings during the summer for evening events in the park
Admission to the gallery and digital exhibits is free. Tickets to climb the tower can be purchased online or onsite:
• Adults: $6
• Children up to age 13: $4

When in Baltimore Inner Harbor, this should be one of your destination spots to visit.  This sailing ship is the "2nd" USS Constellation commissioned in 1855, after the famous 1st USS Constellation was broken up. Even so, the 2nd USS Constellation still had a historic career and is an excellent historic representation of the "age of sail."  Of interest is her 1850's career capturing illicit slave ships,  freeing and releasing the captive Africans to the country of Liberia.  The US government paid $25 per freed slave (to be returned to Africa) and the captured slave ships auction proceeds were divided among the USS Constellation's crew. Make sure to have a tour guide with you as they are very knowledgeable of the ship!

Nice place to walk around. On top of the casement/wall of the fort where the cannons used to be...soldiers and their families buried their pets over many decades, creating a pet cemetery walkway. Majority of the pet animal graves are above the Casement Museum and old Cistern. It is a very pleasant walk on top of the fort wall with some nice views of the water and around the fort. After the Civil War, Jefferson Davis, former Confederate President was imprisoned here. As a young US Army Officer, future Confederate General Lee was stationed here with his family. At great risk of their lives, Slaves fleeing bondage during the Civil War could find freedom here.

A small little gem of a museum that is not intuitively easy to access even though there is a sign off the highway. GPS is kinda wonky here, so may want to look at Google maps before visiting.  The museum appears to be staffed by very experienced people - this is probably more of an asset than the well done displays.  Though I did not utilize the tour, after visiting, would recommend taking the tour as it will add great enrichment & context to the displays.  Price of admission is free!

Nice place to walk around and explore the fort or take some of the trails to the battery's or picnic area.  There is a very small visitors center staffed by Park Rangers who just seemed ready to go home.  No cost to visit in the winter but cannot vouch for the summer.  Great views of the Potomac River!  Highly recommend if a history buff or just want to hike around and enjoy the outdoors. There is a playground for young children at one of the picnic areas.

An avid interest in trains and recent history makes this museum worth the $20 per adult fee. They do give active duty military discounts which includes family. Very interesting museum with lots to explore. Make sure to check out the repair car shop located in a separate building. The surrounding neighborhood is sketchy but parking is gated and free!

Good place to take the family for an hour or two. The natural bridge itself has an awe inspiring view. Further up the trail is a Native American re-enactment site. George Washington surveyed the area and later, Thomas Jefferson purchased Natural Bridge. There is a place to buy food and eat in an outside covered area in view of the Natural Bridge.

Excellent small museum of the New York Militia & New York Army National Guard. They have a well stocked, used military bookstore too. Lots of historical displays and it is located inside an original late 1800's armory! Place is also a research center which would be of interest to historical folks.

Interesting Apothecary in old town Alexandria - they have kid events periodically.  When crossing the threshold into the storage room, look up...a mummified chicken leg affixed to the top of the entrance way!  Ask them about it, if they don't mention it during the tour.

This rating is for the Halloween show called, "The Glow," held at Lake Fairfax Park. Lots of interesting Jack o' Lanterns to view!
At first I thought all the pumpkins were real but looking back at the photos, fakes can be noticed:( Still, it was a neat experience.

There is a small museum here and two gift shops (one is outside). Good place to walk dogs as long as they are on a leash. A local College Professor who was killed in an accident measuring the mountain is buried at the summit - interesting story.

To my surprise, very much enjoyed the historic park, a lot of history - did not know that the ranch was basically a second White House during President Johnson's time in office. For the full picture, visit all parts of the park.

Much to see and experience for those interested in 1st Armored Division and Fort Bliss history. This museum has room to grow as there is much available space to add new displays...expect to spend an hour here.

Very humbling to see each of the fallen's names...this is a very well done memorial. Opposite to the World War II's memorial's entrance is a special memorial to the Gold Star families - not easy to notice.

Nice park and the outdoor theater (band shell) is a great asset...to the left of the band shell is a paved path that follows along the water leading to the downtown Frederick area, it is a pleasant walk.
Small but well curated museum with plenty of interesting historical items highlighting the Army Quartermaster - a must see for military enthusiasts, logistics is everything in war!
Great place to view the falls! There is an entrance fee of about $10 a vehicle. Nature Center to see and places to hike too. Highly recommend visiting during non-tourist times.
Small but packed with interesting displays of local minerals/gems and historical facts. Note - bring an interest in minerals as that is the focus of 95% of the exhibits.
A small, interesting museum with a good amount of varied, US Naval artifacts. Highly recommend for those who are interested in history and naval military affairs!
Little ones love this place! Recommend for the pre-school and lower elementary grade age kids. Free to get into the park and the only cost is the carousel.
Take the kids, friends or a date during off tourist season for better enjoyment. There is no parking, be prepared to walk a bit to get to the building.
Bloody battle fought here during the Civil War Gettysburg battle with the Confederates smashing through the Union forces at the Peach Orchard.
Great place to walk around with a friend on a beautiful day!  Check out the ancient bonsai trees!  There is more, just go see for yourself!
Nice looking place with paved trails. There is a cost per car, however they offer discounts for qualified folks and military is free!
Great place to walk around, shop, eat and drink all while enjoying the unique, 1800's style sites! Parking and museums are free!

I highly recommend coming to this nature preserve. I don't even live near by. I was in the area and wanted to check out this place with my family. I was highly impressed. We only walked partially around the lake area of this nature preserve. It is very picturesque. We came in the Summer. However I would really love to come here in the fall to see the leaves change colors. I looked at the map of this place and it is much larger than it first appears. For those inclined, there are some more serious hiking trails that go on for miles. I definitely want to come back to this place when I have more time to explore all the different trails and have a great time. Hopefully I'll be back soon. The only downside is that this place is quite crowded on the weekends.

I am not from this area of New Jersey. However while my family and I were in the area, we decided to stop by the Campgaw Mountain Reservation. Even though it was Summer time while we visited the area, I still wanted to check out this place. I didn't know there was a place to go skiing or tubing so close to where I live. I thought I had to drive at least three hours to go skiing. I know this is not a fancy ski resort, but it looks to be a great day trip for the family. I can't wait until this coming Winter to have some fun. Too bad it is now the middle of Summer though.

What a peaceful and relaxing park to explore nature! It has now been over a year since I have first visited this park. I have now visited this park in every season: Winter, Spring, Summer and Fall. While the Summer is extremely hot outside, the vegetation is the greatest. I like looking at the lush swamp reeds. I have walked through this entire nature preserve and it is all gorgeous. I enjoy watching the birds and the wildlife (except the insects). I also like seeing the water rush in and out due to the tides. I highly recommend coming here.

If you are a nature lover, I highly recommend visiting the Great Swamp National Wildlife Refuge. There are several great walking trails to see the abundance of nature all around you. Living and working in the city, it isn't often that I get to experience walking in a forest full of life. I really enjoyed seeing all the green of the trees during Spring, even if my children did not enjoy their time here. Hopefully they will have some fond memories of this place later in life.

Definitely worth taking the tour. It is a beautiful building.  However now you need to go to your location congressional representative to get a reserved tour. In the past, you just show up and wait for the next tour. At least this way you don't have to wait for the tour at the US Capital. We also received tickets for the House Gallery tour. This is the balcony overseeing where the House of Representatives vote and where the Presidential State of the Union is held.

It has been nearly 20 years since I first visited this museum. I guess I first visited this place when it first opened. I went back to bring my family so they could learn more about the Holocaust. I do believe this museum is quite informative. However it is now a shell of what I remember the exibits were when it first opened. I remember spending hours going through the exibits. We saw everything in about 40 minutes. I'm glad at least my kids' tickets were free.

While we didn't really plan to visit the White House Visitors Center, it was an enjoyable experience. We we're actually just looking for a rest room and we were told by the White House Park staff to go to the White House Visitor Center. This place is free to visit and has many interesting item to see that once belonged inside the White House or were once gifts to previous US Presidents from other nations. I would recommend coming here.

After visiting the crowded Lincoln Memorial, it is a very relaxing walk around the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool. There are so many memorials surrounding this place. On one end is the Lincoln Memorial and on the other end is the WWII Memorial. On the other two sides of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool are the Vietnam Veterans Memorial and the Korean War Veterans Memorial. I highly recommend coming here.

If traveling to Gettysburg National Park, I highly recommend stopping by the State of Pennsylvania Monument dedicated to the soldiers who fought at the Battle of Gettysburg. This monument is gorgeous. Also you should climb up the narrow winding staircase to see the wonderful views of the battlefield.

2016- I've been to a similar Legoland in Dallas that was much better. This place was not really worth the time and money to get there.

2019 - This Legoland has improved the experience after introducing reserved entrance times. It was a much better experience this time.
dislikes: Not worth time and money (2016 visit)

reviews_attraction.text: Nice sculpture across from the United Nations in NYC based on a biblical verse. Unlike the other posters here, I walked down the stairs. I didn't have to climb the stairs, since I was walking east from 43rd street towards the United Nations building in Manhattan.

If you love history, the Alamo is a must place to visit if you are in San Antonio. I remember studying the battle here for Texas independence in elementary school. It was great to visit the real place. I recommend taking the tour. It is very educational.

If you love history this is a must go place. My kids enjoyed seeing history come to life by all the volunteers. I really enjoyed the historical reenactment of Washington's encampment of Morristown during the American Revolutionary War. Plus it is free.

Beautiful memorial for all those who sacrificed for our freedom. This memorial is one of the few you can cool off by dipping you feet into on a hot Summer day. After walking from the Lincoln Memorial, this is a nice place to sit and relax.
One of the smallest national parks grounds I've ever been to. But it is free and very informative. Definitely worth going to. There are great views of the New York Stock Exchange from the steps.
This is one of the most beautiful memorials in DC. This show what it was like to be in a platoon fighting in the Korean War. The sculptures are so lifelike it is scary.
I highly recommend taking the tour of this old historic lighthouse. The park rangers are very knowledgeable. The views at the top are fantastic.
While hiking through Watchung Reserve, I recommend visiting The Deserted Village. I never realized that this park had such a varied history.
This is a great place to visit for hiking. The scenery is gorgeous. I recommend visiting the ice caves is you are adventurous.
There is a great family destination, especially if you love looking at historical trains. The place brings history to life.
This park is ok. There is quite a lot of construction going on. However the views of the river make up for it.
I wish I could have seen this station in its prime. I wish all my train stations would look like this.
This used to be a "Putt Putt Golf and Games" when I was a teenager. I guess they went out of business.
Great park to come during ones lunch break on a nice day. The only problem is finding a place to sit.
This is one of the best zoos in the country. The Bronx Zoo is a great place to bring the family.

This is a perfect place to visit during the anytime of the year.  I love coming here in the Fall because its a beautiful time to come and the weather is not too hot.  The entrance fee is $3 and the workers here are extremely nice.  There are not too many farms in the Washington D.C. area and this farm is nearby and perfect for a day trip. The farm is not very big, so it is good for old people and young kids.  The main crops on the farm are tobacco and corn.  The corn and tobacco was harvested for the year so when you go now you won't see too much of those crops.  There are animals on the farm, such as pigs, chicken, and turkey.  There is a cute little garden pig that you will see on the farm.  The people working on the farm work on the farm and act as if they are in the 1700s.  The people working on the farm reminded me of Colonial Williamsburg.  The women I met who "lived" in the house were really nice and they showed me how to wash smoked meat.  They provided me with a great amount of information on the farm, farming practices and what they do with the crops and animals they have on the farm.

This place is what you make of it. If you are looking for a good ski weekend with friends and an affordable family vacation come here. The best part about seven springs is that everything is at the resort. If you want to ski the slopes are in the back of the hotel. There are multiple restaurants and hotel amenities.

The hotel reminded me of a 1980's hotel trapped in time.
The hotel has some quirky attributes such as single panned glass, little no heating in the hallways, only one place to have breakfast and no tunnel/indoor walkway to ski slope lodge.

Breakfast can be a crazy line here. The breakfast is excellent and worth the wait but the line took way too long. There should be more places to have breakfast here. Only one place does not make any sense.

Hotel beds are okay but I would bring extra blankets as you may want something more comfortable.

Not a bad place for a weekend vacation but wouldn't want to be here for a week.

Plenty of bars and restaurants.

I was here for an event recently and loved this event venue. This is a hidden gem that is tucked away on the Potomac. This is a great venue for a wedding, birthday, garden party or any event. The Manor is gorgeous, and is in fantastic shape. The ceilings, floors and doorways have great architectural features that you do not see everyday in the D.C. area. The outdoor area has a great garden area that overlooks the river. You can see National Harbor and  Alexandria from the gardens. There are many photo shot locations that would be great for any photo album. There is plenty of parking, so if you are having a large event there will be enough spots for all your guest. I would gladly come back and use this event for a future event venue.

Great place for a hike! I love coming out here in autumn to see the leaves change colors and to hike along the Potomac River.  I enjoy hiking the River Trail along the water. It is a beautiful palce to take the family, a date or friends. Bring a picnic with you and have a nice lunch or snack a long the river during your hike.  There are plenty of places to rest and to relax as you are hiking.  There are not too many water fountains once you leave the main area, where the parking is, so bring a bottle of water with you! It is amazing how close you are to D.C. because when you are here you feel like you are in the middle of the forest and far away from a city.  Nice place to get excersize and enjoy the nature.

Gorgeous is the first thing that pops into my head when I see this cathedral. There are not many churches in the USA that are this beautiful and that looks like a European church. The outside is very nice but the inside is also magnificent. The stain glass and the artwork inside is beautiful. The church service here is always lovely, tradition episcopal. The Easter service here is always a wonderful service as everything is perfect. The decorations and flowers are gorgeous and the service is the best in town.  Make sure to come prepared with tickets for the service on Easter, it gets crowded fast.

This is a great place for an afternnon walk or bike ride.  I love coming here because its not as crowded as the other monuments throughout DC.  You are still in Virginia, which is ncie for VA residents, you don't have to cross over the river.  The memorial has pelnty of areas to walk around or sit down.  Sometime you can see the Marine band practice playing during the mornings or lunch time generally.
The Sunset Parades are conducted on Tuesdays only beginning May 27 through Aug. 12,  2014 and the start times are as follows:
7:00 – 8:00 p.m.

Amazing wine! I loved my visit out here today. I came looking at Bull Run for an event venue. The venue is fantastic, they have several rooms to choose from and the facility is made out of beautiful wood. The management are nice and helpful. The wine tasting is a must! The bartender is very generous with the tasting samples. The wines are excellent. They have a large variety of whites and reds. I loved the merlot. They have a very nice port wine and other desert wines as well. Plenty of space to move around. Great day trip from D.C.

Absolutely beautiful here! The wines here are very nice and the atmosphere of this place is relaxing. I like to come here from dc because it's close and you are in a different world than the city. There are about 8-10 different wines to try. The price for a tasting is $5 and the tastings are generous. The staff is friendly. The tasting area has plenty of seating. I would recommend to bring a picnic with you. This is a great place to spend a couple hours. I loved the running hare house white wine.

Great way to spend a few hours walking around. The free tour of the house is a nice short tour. The house was General Lee's as well as the land that makes up the cemetery. You will leave this place learning quite a few facts. There are various memorials on the cemetery. My favorite is the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier.  It has a soldier there at all times watching over the tomb. Beautiful views of DC can be seen from here.

The restaurant here is the best museum for lunch. If you are looking for salmon or something other than burgers or chicken nuggets this is the place. There is food from Latin America here! Great spot for people who wish to learn about the American Indian.  I think the museum could have a few more exhibits depicting the history of different tribes, but it was still nice.  Not as crowded as other museums.

A beautiful hiking area close to Washington, D.C. The park is not as crowded as Great Falls and you can spend 3 hours or more here and be very content. Today I came with a few friends to see the waterfall that sits along the river. It's a wonderful place to go on a date or bring the kids. The parking lot is much smaller then Great Falls to be prepared for that. Trails are easy to intermediate level.

Not many people come here and it I love that. Every time I come I generally see bikers or walkers. This place is an area where you can think and enjoy being away from the busy parts of the city. This area is going to be busier soon when The Warf is finished, which is the new development in the waterfront area. This statue is very unique and unexpected as many people do not know this area exists.

This is a great place in the middle of Fairfax to get away and experience some nature. There is a small forest here and a small lake in the middle of the park. There is plenty of bird watching here. I have seen an eagle and a falcon. Great place for a picnic and for a nice run. Along the trail there are some pull up bars and other small exercise/ stretching stations.

Nice spot to come to in DC.  This is more of a place for locals, its not one of the more popular sites in DC so not as many tourist come here.  The columns are nice to see and take photos with.  You will see many people here having photo shoots.   The area is great for picnics so make sure to bring food with you.  Parking is available throughout the park.

DC always amazes me on what the city has to offer. The old Greek pillars that came from the U.S. Capital building are standing alone like an Ancient Greek ruin. Very different from the other parks in dc and also are located in a non traditional tourist area. There are a lot of meadows and paths here to wonder around. The bonsai trees are a real treat.

This is a fun place to take your family to either the day after Thanksgiving or during other main holidays. When you arrive to the museum with your prepaid ticket or the ticket you buy at the counter then you wait a long line to get into an elevator which will take you to the main exhibit hall. The museum can take up to a couple hours to see.

Fantastic museum that shows a variety of art. There are paintings here but my favorite section to see here, is the sculpture section. The sculptures are all very nice but my favorites are the modern pieces that are shown. This is one of my favorite museums as it's never too crowded and has some amazing pieces to see.
