Fun and very touristy are to hang out with kids and look at the lake.  Sandy beach and docks available for launching boats.  Water fountains for the kids to play in.  Nearby ice cream alley and restaurants for grabbing eats or treats.

It's a bridge where you can watch rowing history be made at rowing regatta.  There is a water fill station here and a TV monitor for checking on race starts/stats.  There is no restrooms.  Shade is ample with the seating area.

Nice walkway and park along the waterfront.  I will add that my wife and I felt as if we were going to be run over several times along the walk as there were many evening bike and scooter commuters screaming by at rapid rates.

Had a lot of fun snowshoeing around jughandle area.  Plenty of groomed and ungroomed trails to wander around and explore.  Will definitely come back to visit again (maybe in the summer months for some Mt. Biking).

Cool alley with old houses and original type setting and styling. Cooler alley to visit when it gets hot outside. Also safe for kids to walk around.  There's a gathering garden area if you walk far enough in.

Very well run museum focused on the history and fable of the Liberty Bell.  Staff was helpful and displays were informative. Will come back in another 10 years and hope it is just as nice then as it is now.

Impressive spire.  Unfortunately not currently open for visitors inside due to reconstruction, but will be renewed for opening later 2019.  Key landmark to visit while in DC... and guess what... NO LINES!

Impressive museum telling the history of many African American influential people.  Not just the typical slavery story, but more about African American parts and roles in shaping the America of today.
Zoo Boise mastu not be as big as the Portland Zoo, but it packs in plenty of events, and children learning activities to keep our family coming back year after year.  Always worth a quick break.

Great park for events such as art in the park or just a walk through the zoo.
It can be shady which is great in the summer, but cold in the winter months, so bring a jacket fall/winter/spring.
Interesting house and common area.  Forest service has story time events here if they aren't interested in the museum.  Flags are an important part of the nation's history.
Not really for adults.  Really hot location and totally a commercial carnival setting.   The mini golf was unimpressive and general area just felt over commercialized.
Great little park for a morning or afternoon visit.  Plenty of playground equipment, shade, picnic tables, tennis courts and open grass for kid activities.
Ben Franklin's apartment area.  Costs a couple bucks to get in.  Can see quite a bit from the outside as well.  About 45 min to walk through.
Great venue for a wedding reception or school dance.  Plenty of open space, kitchen and bathrooms available.  Nice view from the hill.
Great place to expose your kids to seafaring animals.  Small but will entertain the kids for an hour or two.
Fun place to hang out for a picnic or concert in the summer or see Christmas lights and Santa in the winter.
Great place to stop in and get advice for what to do in the area.  Very helpful staff and resources.

Cantwell Cliffs is one of my favorite trails in Hocking Hills. It's just far enough away that it's less busy than some of it's counterparts and the trail is beautiful and a bit more challenging as well. Fat woman's squeeze is at the beginning towards the bottom of the steps.
Cantwell is broken down between two trails. The yellow is a simple loop and mostly flat (though you do need to go down several stairs to reach it). The red is more challenging with several elevation changes (most include stone steps that can be a bit treacherous).

This place is located right next to the cemetery and memorial. It's very commercial and they are primarily trying to get you to go though one of their haunted attractions. Skip the haunted houses but enjoy the shops and atmosphere.

A beautiful nature preserve right in your own backyard. This place offers a nice hike no matter the season. You can walk through the forest or take the wooden walkway though the wetland preserve. Very educational.

It's easy to walk right past this great find along the Freedom Trail. Inside the cemetery is where both Paul Revere and Samuel Adams are buried. It's pretty quiet here as I think a lot of people miss it.
Great park for water sports. It also has a short trail that has the ruins of both the Fairfax house and what's left of the Lee home. This park does charge an entrance fee of around $4/ car.
A must see when visiting DC. If you want to be able to go to the top to need to book tickets months in advance or try your luck at the ticket office first thing in the morning the day of.
A must stop when doing the freedom tour. The cost of the ticket is nominal but the wealth of information you get is great. Try to time it so you are there between large tour groups.
This is a must do on your Salem visit. The tour guide was amazing and informative. If you like Hocus Pocus this was location they filmed the first scene with Thackery Binx.
The FDR memorial probably has the most thought behind it. Check out the detail and waterfalls in each section. This is also one of the few memorials where dogs are allowed.
This is a great trail where you can choose an easy mostly flat trail or take the steps and hike the rim. Once you make the climb the top is fairly easy all the way around.
If you have an event here arrive early so you can explore the building. There is a couple of gift shops on the main floor and a cafeteria and a nice restaurant upstairs.
This is the quintessential stop if you are visiting Salem for the history of the witch hunts. The tour is self guided as you read the signs and follow the history.
The museum here is great, very interactive and fun. Couple that with the chance to go aboard not one but two naval ships and this park is well worth the distance.
Great historical place to see the real Ford's theatre and the bed Lincoln died in. They get very busy and sell out of tickets early so book ahead of time online.
It has a quaint museum with Civil We era artifacts. The historical part of the park is fairly small but it still has plenty of interesting stops to check out.
A beautiful historic home that's a must stop for history buffs. The tour guide was informative and provided interesting insights into Jefferson's life.
When visiting Arlington Cemetery don't miss this stop on the bus tour. Gorgeous views of DC along side an interesting tour of an old historic mansion.
Great Falls is always a gorgeous hike. This can be a bit strenuous but manageable for even the youngest of kids. There are also flatter trails nearby.
Great piece of Civil War history right in the heart of old town. If you watch Mercy Street then I would highly recommend seeing the real thing.
Beautiful park that has great views of Mount Vernon from across the river. They do reenactments on the colonial farm on the weekends.
Plenty of grass for picnics and outdoor games. Check out the markers for fun historical facts about the fort that was here.
This is a gorgeous park packed with history. The park stays open until 6p but the fort and bookstore/museum close at 4:30p
George Mason is sadly the forgotten Founding Father of the US. The memorial is very peaceful as many pass right by it.
I recommend going after dusk as the soldiers give an even more eerie effect as they seem to walk thru the dark brush.
Large park area reserved primarily for soccer. It does have a nice walking path and a great kids playground too.

(Translated by Google) A very beautiful place. I recommend taking the subway to Cleveland Avenue, and then go on foot. You will see the real "one-story" America and its quiet streets. There will be no souls on the street, only fluttering flags over houses and parked cars. The cathedral will appear before you unexpectedly and will amaze with its beauty and grandeur. Find out in advance the mode of operation so as not to be in front of a closed door. Then you can walk to the Russian embassy.

Очень красивое место. Рекомендую доехать на метро до Кливленд авеню, а потом пойти пешком. Вы увидите настоящую "одноэтажную" Америку и ее тихие улочки. На улице будет ни души, только развевающиеся флаги над домами и припаркованные автомобили. Собор появится перед вами неожиданно и поразит своей красотой и величием. Узнайте заранее режим работы, чтобы не оказаться перед закрытой дверью. Потом пешком можно дойти до российского посольства.
dislikes: Facilities & Services: Closed door (implying limited operating hours)

reviews_attraction.text:

Yes, and in the end you can drink tea. Fresh.

Да, и в конце можно попить чай. Свежий.

But this building after difficult events was given over to the museum. Admission is $ 6, teachers have a discount of $ 1. All fans of this writer should visit it, since many things have been collected from his life. If you plan a visit, then you can get on a tour.

Вход 6 долл, учителям скидка 1 долл. Посетить его стоит всем фанатам этого писателя, так как собрано немало вещей из его жизни. Если спланировать визит, то можно попасть и на экскурсию.

Once I walked along the shore near the bridge, there is a very quiet and calm park, I recommend it to everyone. You can also see the bridge from the ferry that goes from Far Rockaway to Manhattan. On the bridge itself was not. Is he generally pedestrian?

А еще хорошо можно увидеть мост с парома, который ходит с Far Rockaway к Манхеттену. На самом мосту не был. Он вообще пешеходный?

In addition to a huge collection of books, the building is of architectural value, moreover, it is quite comfortable to be inside, there are places for work and leisure. The library catalog is also on its website.

The inside is actually very interesting, you can "touch" the math with your hands. There are many interactive things. You can buy books and souvenirs. I took a pizza knife in the form of the letter PI.

Внутри на самом деле очень интересно, можно "потрогать" математику руками. Есть много интерактивных вещей. Можно прикупить книги и сувениры. Я взял нож для пиццы в виде буквы ПИ.

You expect that in one day you will barely have time to see everything. Here you can also make many very interesting photographs.

If you book tickets in advance, you can climb to the top of this monument, from where you can enjoy a gorgeous view of the US capital and its environs. The Pentagon is clearly visible. You can safely take pictures. The ticket price is symbolic.

Lindo recorrido y se ven buenas vistas de la ciudad. Tomamos el que duraba 2 horas y media pero finalmente duro 2 horas solamente. Como alternativa a navegar y sacar buenas fotos aunque solo del downtown se puede coger el ferry a staten island totalmente gratis. (Translated by Google) You can enter and visit with a guided tour totally free, it is not necessary to have a reservation. At the entrance they check you the same as at an airport and you cannot enter with food. You can see the dome inside and not much else, it depends fundamentally on whether they are in session or not. It is a nice visit if you have time, but if you don't, you don't miss too much. If you understand a little more about US history with a movie that happens to you.

(Translated by Google) Very good museum and experience. You can see an aircraft carrier inside with a nice exposition of its history. On deck it has several planes on display and also in another room a giant NASA plane. Additionally, you have the option of visiting an atomic submarine that participated in the cold war inside. It is overwhelming to think of living there for several weeks submerged. The museum is included in the NY City Pass.

Ever since I was young I would visit this beautiful oceanfront park, and still to this day I'm captivated by it's beauty. Upon entering, you'll find a spacious parking lot (a rarity in this city!), then you'll walk past plenty of open-air gazebos and picnic tables where locals and tourists alike are enjoying themselves. The beachfront is among the cleanest and most pristine in all of Miami, with the beach regularly cleaned by park employees. There's plenty of restrooms (renovated only a few years ago, they're quite modern and clean). In addition to the beach, there's a track for running/biking/walking, plenty of "boardwalk" area to walk along the beach, and an old "abandoned" zoo where one can walk around and observe old structures that are still standing (they're planning to build a petting zoo in the near future) and the plethora of wildlife that roam the park (iguanas, squirrels, various birds including cranes and peacocks, and plenty of little critters). I definitely recommend this place if you're visiting Miami, and it's excellent for families and kids.

A harrowingly beautiful tribute to those that lost their lives and suffered as a result of the Holocaust. The museum itself is absolutely fantastic, one of the best museums I've ever had the privilege of going to. Be warned: tickets are incredibly difficult to get, so I recommend going on their website and pre-ordering them. I'm not sure whether there is a cost to reserve it, but I figure it's better to pay a small fee than not go at all, it's definitely worth the small fee. The exhibits are fantastic, going into great detail about one of the worst times in recent history (see my pictures for a good selection of what there is within the museum). If you're one who likes to read most everything, I'd say this museum will take you about 4-6 hours (there's that much stuff!), but if you're a skimmer you'll spend about 2 hours here if it's your first time. I love this museum with a passion and I encourage everyone visiting DC to give it a look!

Love this Theatre and Park! A fantastic reconstruction of the Original Ford's Theatre (the original was purchased by the government, used for office space, and it was eventually "demolished" and rebuilt to the exact specifications of pictures taken the night Lincoln was shot there), Ford's Theatre boasts an impressive museum describing the mood of the country around the time Lincoln was killed, going into fantastic detail about the conspirators and the eventual assassination of Lincoln. I thoroughly enjoyed that museum. After walking through the museum, you'll walk up a couple flights of stairs to be on the top balcony, overlooking the stage and booth where Lincoln was shot. When you're there, I high recommend asking a Ranger for a talk about that night, it's truly intriguing. Overall, I loved this place and consider it a must-visit if you're in DC!

A must-visit in Nashville! This life-size replica of the Parthenon (only one in the world) is a truly magnificent place to visit. The structure lies within Centennial Park, which in and of itself is a nice place to walk (also very close to the Vanderbilt campus). The building doubles as an art museum (ticket prices and hours in my photos, with there being an unlisted student discount for $5 with valid ID) and it is definitely worth the money! The museum covers the history of both the Greek and Nashville Parthenon, and there is a spectacular gallery of paintings and Greek-inspired art. The second floor features a massive 40+ foot tall statue of Athena (the real Parthenon also had a statue of the same height) and casts of the figures that adorn the exterior of the Parthenon. Overall, a great place and I definitely recommend visiting!

A great place within DC! The tour, in my opinion, is drawn-out and boring, but to each their own (it just had too much information that wasn't pertinent to what I was expecting to get out of the Library). Here's what I recommend: speak with a guard or desk-worker about getting a library card. They're 100% free, and you're allowed to tour the entirety of the library (the tour only lets you see the main reading room from a high balcony, having a library card lets you walk on the floor). Walking around with the card is a million times better than the tour. However, do take the time to visit the exhibits, seeing the first map that has "America" and Jefferson's library is truly extraordinary. Overall, I highly recommend visiting the LOC!

Indescribably beautiful park! An extension of Chattanooga & Chickamauga NMP, Point Park offers fantastic scenery (the best in Chattanooga) and a pleasant walk that’s sure to make your day. Heads up: it costs $7 per person to enter (minus one star) and the parking is not free (city pay-by-plate). (Local secret: there’s a very nice 1.1 mike hike from Sunset Rock to a staircase that leads to Point Park. It’s not too strenuous, and it saves you the $7 fee if you go from Sunset Rock to the park.) Beside that, it’s a great place to see the scenic Chattanooga Valley, learn about an important Civil War battle (definitely check out the museum in the visitors center), and just relax in the beauty of this park.

Fantastic and so much more! I spent a little over an hour here and only saw a fraction of what there was to see. The building itself is conveniently located near a subway station and a busy downtown full of food places and the likes. Also, the building is beautiful! Now to the art. So many famous paintings and sculptures lie here, some you may even recognize in an "oh, I know I've seen that one!" In my opinion, the coolest part of the museum is the Presidential portrait section, they have portraits of every US president (yes, even Obama's, Michelle's is also in the museum on a separate floor). Overall, I loved this museum and hope to return one day to see more!

A Chattanooga classic! Sunset Rock is the best place (in my opinion) to watch, well, the sunset! Overlooking a gorgeous valley and other mountains, Sunset Rock offers fantastic views and gorgeous scenery. Local secret: Taking a hike from this place down the long rock staircase, then following the map on the trail (mainly go up when there's a fork, you can't miss it) will give you a 1.1 mile trail that will leave you at Point Park, at the very tip of Lookout Mountain, without having to pay an entrance fee. Do be warned: parking is very limited. Overall, a fantastic park and a definite must-visit if you're in Chattanooga.

A fantastic National Historic Site! Upon entering the Visitor Center, you'll be met by a knowledgable ranger and a fantastic, decently-sized museum that revolves around Johnson's presidency and impeachment trial. Also in the Visitor Center is a massive cabin, used by Johnson and his family (see pics for various things you'll find). The site is split among a few different plots of land, with the closest being across the street (Johnson's home). The homestead and a few other places are scattered in a near proximity of the Visitor Center. Overall, this site is absolutely fantastic and I honestly loved this place!

A must-visit when you're in Chattanooga! Actually two building, the Tennessee Aquarium is a fantastic experience where you'll learn about a large variety of aquatic animals. Featuring otters, alligators, turtles, penguins, and jellyfish (the coolest room!), this aquarium is seemingly endless and a place guaranteed to make your day. Local tip: park using the street parking, although parking in downtown Chattanooga is pretty limited (if you can, arrive earlier to nab one of the lots nearest the aquarium, however be prepared to spend around $10 for parking). Overall, one of the best things to do in Chattanooga!

Gorgeous park! This park is an absolute must-visit if you're in the area (and it's well-worth the drive if you're not)! I unfortunately went when it was raining, but from what I could see (in addition to the awesome junior ranger badge I earned) this park is solid in what it offers. The ranger mentioned that there are over 500 miles of hiking trails available, in addition to numerous equestrian trails, fantastic overlooks, scenic drives, massive rivers, and so much more. I will definitely be making my way back when there's less rain so I can enjoy the full beauty of this park!

Massive variety and natural beauty lies within the United States Botanic Garden! Upon entering, you're greeted by a fantastic assortment of flowers, plants, trees, and decorations that will visually amaze all. I visited during Orchid Festival and my word was the variety and display of these beautiful plants beyond fantastic (see pictures for a couple of photographs showing what they have). The place is organized well, most will be able to walk through it at a slow pace within an hour. Overall, I loved the Botanic Garden and I consider it to be a must-visit within DC.

Trails of staggering beauty, this small forest is a true hidden gem within Collegedale. With more than enough to satisfy every level of hiker, the Biology Trails at Southern Adventist University has something for everyone. From easy to extreme trails, to tons of trails for mountain bikers, to kid-friendly walking trails, and even stunning biodiversity, the Biology Trails have everything to satisfy nature enthusiasts and appreciators alike.

Absolutely gorgeous park just outside of Washington, DC! This park, dedicated to LBJ, his wife, and their memory is a breathtakingly beautiful and peaceful place to visit and explore. Be advised: the park is mainly accessible by car, the nearest subway station is over a mile walk away. I was only able to spend a small amount of time there, and I cannot wait to go back! I highly recommend visiting this park to everyone!

One of the most beautiful parks in Washington, DC! Having driven and walked through here numerous times during my times in DC, I stand by my convictions that this place is worth a visit! Boasting a wide variety of activities (walking, hiking, jogging, driving, even equestrian sports) this park will satisfy most everybody's wants and desires. I encourage anyone visiting DC to drop by this park, it's worth it!

A fantastic museum that I will definitely be visiting again soon! For the short amount of time I was here I knew that this museum is top-notch. Diving into the history of the secret city (you'll find out about that when you visit) this absolutely amazing museum shows what life was like in Oak Ridge during the days of the Manhattan project. I loved my time here and like I said cannot wait to visit again!

This is one of the best visitor centers you'll ever visit! It's a gorgeous building, situated in a great location within the Chikamauga battlefield. The staff are incredibly knowledgeable, the gift shop is absolutely stacked with fantastic memorabilia, and I definitely recommend stopping here to have the best time possible within the park!

An absolutely beautiful cathedral not too far from other iconic D.C. landmarks! It’s relatively inexpensive to get in, however I found that the tours were a bit overpriced, in my opinion. Besides that, the church is fabulous, showcasing some of the greatest architecture you’ll find in the US. I highly recommend visiting this church!!!

Beautiful National Park unit that commemorates an important battle. Great place to drive, bike, walk, and explore the hundreds of memorials & monuments on the grounds. Definitely a great place to bring family and kids and learn about the important Civil War battle that took place here.

Absolutely fantastic park! You can walk, run, bike, hammock, explore, and so much more! There are super-cool TNT bunkers that you can walk in to and listen for echo, there's a hidden lake with beautiful swinging benches, and the nature trails are superb.

A hauntingly beautiful monument to the victims of a tragic war. It's one thing to see photos, but being there, seeing every name written on the walls, it's something a review nor a photograph can describe. A definite must-see if you come to DC.
A beautiful halfway point on the way to summit LeConte! I highly recommend taking a few minutes to break here and take in the natural beauty!
Absolutely gorgeous state park, easily one of the most beautiful I've been to. Nice visitor center. The waterfalls are simply phenomenal.
A quality visitor center. The Rangers and staff know their stuff, and it’s simply a beautiful place to go for a walk.
Fantastic place, one of the best in the NPS. A beautiful tribute to the work of MLK, this place did his legacy right.

Nice place to take a walk and see a nice sunset. There are two gates, so I don’t believe this would be a great place to watch a sunset. The opening hours are far past sunset and the gates will keep you from getting in to see the sunrise. There are many potholes on the road in, and it’s only a one-lane road, so definitely drive slow. There are a bunch of deer and many birds that live here, so there’s a strong chance you’ll see wildlife on your trip here. It’s a free park, so that’s also very nice.

The lighthouse is a lot farther from the point than I thought it was, so it was a bit difficult to get a picture worth saving with my phone.

I'll start by saying, you can use your annual national park card ($80) for entry here, so that's good. Otherwise, you pay the $10 fee for entry (per person). I would recommend hiking in/out of the cave through the natural entrance of you are physically able. The cave is a decent size, but if you don't have a camera worth at least $500, your cell phone or regular camera will be worthless inside the cave. The lighting is poor... Most other caverns I've visited have had significantly better lighting than Carlsbad. The earlier you are able to get to the cave, the better. It gets super busy between 11AM-noon.

I love caverns like this because they aren’t completely discovered yet. They’re still removing clay from this place, with the hopes of showing more of the cave to the public in the future. It’s $20 for an adult entry, although you can find $1 coupons out in town.

The owner of the cave (in the jazzy scooter) also rolled over to me after the tour, while I was putting my belongings back into my car, and asked if I was single bc he wanted to share his cave and property with someone... so single ladies... he’s available. Awkward encounter for me, but yeah the cave is still cool.

The parking here is definitely great, although there are tons of people who come here to hike the kokohead stairs (tourists and locals, alike). It's best to come here on a weekday because on the weekend it's packed. Sunrise and sunset are best for the hike because there's no shade at all... Make sure to bring water because you will exhaust yourself otherwise. Kokohead is almost a staple hike that all hikers in Oahu have done. Great workout and nice view. There are bathrooms below the second parking lot, too. Safe area, highly recommend.

Decent local spot. When the water is calm, you will see scuba divers out here. When the waves are here, it’s a nice place to watch surfers. More cars are broken into at this beach than other beaches. If you are a diver, make sure someone is watching your gear- several people I know have had gear stolen here. Locals have also attempted to steal food and items we had on our blankets while we were sitting right there. It’s a nice beach, but you have to be more aware of your belongings than at other beaches.

Nice trail, well-maintained. I’d suggest taking a picture of the trail map in the parking lot or screen-shotting it online before starting this hike, so you don’t lose your location- there are a few ways to get to the falls, so it’s just good to know where you’re at and where you can go to get where you’d like. The falls are really nice and it’s a peaceful place to sit and take it in. There are usually others on the trail, so you won’t be alone on this one.

Well-maintained trail. Easy to follow- well marked. Very rocky. There is a parking lot and ppl also park on the road shoulder, too. The view is alright. There is only a view on one side of the mountain because the tree coverage on the other side is too high/thick. The side you can see is kinda meh, but it’s a nice little walk. Kids could do this hike, but might need help when you get to the boulders. This hike is like... mid-size dog friendly.

I went here when the monument was under construction. There was no indication that it was under construction until after you had paid to get in the park (honor system- envelope at gate), so even after walking up to the monument, you can’t go in/on the monument to see the better view. I’m not sure if it’s still under construction but if so, I’d pass on seeing this until the construction is completed.

Really nice to see at night, but also not bad to see during the day! It’s certainly not as crowded if you visit during the day, although you won’t see the nice lights. Also- very cute trains running around the main tree. There are smaller Christmas trees for each state in the U.S., each of which is decorated by ornaments made by children from a particular school in the applicable state.

Decent view at the end. You’re going downhill most of the way there and uphill most of the way back, so keep that in mind. Also, the NPS has the parking lot blocked off right now, so if you park (still in the parking lot, but not blocking the lane) outside of the barriers (not on the road), you will get a $30 ticket. The local police are patrolling this frequently, FYI.

Nice spot to snorkel, but the visibility can diminish quickly. This is a spot where many people (local and tourists) come to hang out and spend time on the weekend. It gets pretty packed at times and I'd say there are better places on island to snorkel, but it's not bad. Bring your own snorkel gear- I'm not sure if they have rental stuff in the area.

I typically really enjoy aquariums but I’m not sure this one is worth the $25 it costs for entry. There aren’t enough fish, jellyfish, birds, animals in this building to make this worth the price you pay. They need to make this aquarium more interactive and a little more fun (not just for kids, but adults, too)! I likely won’t be back here.

Super easy trail, paved, and right along side the ocean. Beautiful view, especially for sunrise. Great place for whale watching in the winter months. Parking can get very tight in the middle of the day. Bring water if you're coming in the middle of the day because there is no shade and you'll be walking up in the hot sun.

I can't believe people would give this place 5 stars. They only had t-shirts and miniature rubber alien figurines. That's it. Not even coffee mugs! There is a child play area in the back, although it was empty. You'd be better off stopping at a nearby Walmart to pick up some Roswell gifts and knick knacks than this place.

Awesome place to stop and an awesome view to see from the bridge. Don't just drive over it... Pull over and walk out on the bridge. It's worth your time for the feeling and the view. There are also vendors on the side of the road selling leather, art, jewelry, wood carvings, etc. The rest area is also nice/clean.

Really nice park, the parking isn't bad, but it's a great place to go running, walk to the beach, shop around the tented areas, and the whole area is safe. I love Kapiolani and would move around that area if I could afford it!

Awesome science museum for kids- adults can definitely learn some things and have a fun time here, too. I’d definitely plan to be here for at least a couple hours, especially if you plan to go to the planetarium show.

Really nice biking/running/walking area. Parking can be tight. If you get there in the morning, you might be able to watch the row teams get ready to head out for practice. The cherry blossoms are blooming now!

Easy to follow trail, well maintained. Parking lot is small, but there’s another one on the side of 209. Walking along side the running water is nice and calming, and the waterfall at the end is peaceful.
Really nice park. Great for sunsets, yoga, running, watching fireworks, scuba (magic island), paddle boarding, swimming, etc. Lots of nice events held here. Really safe and beautiful area.
I can appreciate the effort out into decorating each room for the theme they were going for. It was impressive. I’m not a big art museum fan, but this was a good experience.
Cool thing to see as you walk near the water. Sometimes there is equipment stored on the sand, which kind of ruins the image, but it’s still a nice thing to see.
This place is pretty far out of the way for a few pictures of satellite dishes. Not to say they aren't cool, but two hours? Eh. I wouldn't do it again.
Decent trail, views are okay, decent for mountain biking. There's a picnic table along the way if you want to stop for a breather. Really easy hike.
Cool thing to see on the way to the kalalau trail but I wouldn't drive out of my way to see this.

Buccaneer Bay has been a staple of Weeki Wachee Springs for years! The natural clarity and refreshing feel of the water is a treat on any hot day! The park includes multiple water slides that end with a splash in the spring and a children's area with small slide and tunnel. Lifeguards are on watch at all attractions making it safe for swimmers of any level. The water is naturally a cool 72° year round so if your visiting during the colder months you have an increased chance of encountering a few gentle giants swimming with you (manatees)! Also, there is a snack bar and small gift shop available to browse with items including floats, bathing suits, towels, sunscreen and more. If your looking to bring lunch or snacks, small coolers are welcome into the park. Beach chairs and umbrellas are first come first serve so be sure to get there early if your looking for a good spot to lounge. Tubes are also available to rent for a river ride or to swim with in the swimming area. Also in the swimming area there is a dock which you can swim to (experienced swimmers recommended) and jump off of. Great place for families looking for a fun freshwater beach experience!

I live relatively close to the park and have been going since I was a young child and it has always been a blast, I always love seeing the mermaid show as it brings back so many memories, the river boat ride is also a favorite of mine and always has been. During Halloween they do a costume contest, put on a phenomenal show, and also have a haunted trail! During summertime and late spring time (depending on the weather) Buccaneer Bay is open and it's always fun. The park is fed by a fresh water spring that is around 72 degrees year round. If you don't mind the cold water you will love coming here. Slides, snacks, a store, and a kiddie area make this the spot to be for a family looking for a less expensive day or more of fun!

I work with developmentally disabled adults and I was able to easily schedule a visit for the photography lesson. The staff and volunteers were awesome! They were extremely friendly and inviting. They taught us many things and answered all of our questions. They showed us all around the site and showed us slides of the photographs they personally took and taught us tips to become better photographers. Definitely worth checking out a class or just going for a visit.

Hogsmeade Station is the station that holds, The Hogwarts Express! If you have purchased a park to park ticket or annual pass you can ride the Hogwarts Express from one park to the next without having to walk. The train ride is short and gentle and gives you an opportunity to see some of the sights and sounds of what it's like to travel between London and Hogwarts! You may even be able to see Harry and friends along the way!

Get here early because the line will continue to grow throughout the day! This is one of the best visually entertaining rides to go on in the park. Be cautious when on the que as there may be some locals looking to scare you off! The ride is pretty short but definitely fun and entertaining. Be sure to look for Kong near the end of the ride, he's hard to miss!

One of the few closer to original rides left in the park. This ride is fun for the whole family! I don't want to spoil anything but get ready to save the planet and compete with friends and family along the way. DONT PUSH THE RED BUTTON UNTIL TOLD TO DO SO! As a precaution this ride DOES SPIN!

Very nice park, large play area for children with slides, swings, and a big "castle". Multiple pavilions for eating or relaxing, the larger pavilion has a built in grill for cooking. There is also a baseball/softball field and a pond with fish and turtles to walk around on the walking path.

I love walking around city walk and seeing all the different shops with unique offerings at every one. There are also different types of clubs to visit (21+) and many different and fun types of restaurants. For the best family experience I recommend Bubba Gumps!

This is a fun little interactive fountain great for the whole family. Since it is interactive you may get wet so take pictures from a distance. You may be asked questions from this curious little fountain but nothing super outrageous and safe for kids ears.

On this water adventure ride you will see many different types of dinosaurs including ones that will be sure to be looking for you! Starting gentle and ending with a big surprise you'll have fun the whole time your riding this! YOU WILL GET WET!

Very fun attraction, this is a walk through type show, there is no "ride", just walking. Lots of special effects including a water- rotating walk through tunnel. There are many loud sounds and dark rooms so if you have children please be aware.

When I was in middle school we had the opportunity to swim here with manatees and it was amazing. Such gentle giants these animals are, and the water wasn't too cold either. Definitely recommend a pit stop here if your in the area!

Definitely a place to check out if your in the area, tons of figures from television, music, movies, history, and more. Plus for a small extra fee you can mold your own hand in any (appropriate) position with color of choice.

Some may say it's out of date but this attraction still brings me in every time I visit. It is a mainly visual show but there are many elements of live action during the show. Including a motorcycle scene and "gun" display.

If your planning a trip to Key West, Mallory Square is definitely without a doubt a place to stop! With all the amazing street performances, shopping, and food, you would regret not stopping here on your way through!
Awesome if your into bones and learning about various animals and how their locomotion works. Over 100 types of animals and also types of human ancestry skulls and how bones and movement has changed.
The legendary icon for Universal Studios, The Globe! The globe is a spinning monument to the theme park and picture company. Stop and gaze at it for a while, or take a picture with it or of it.
For the roller coaster enthusiast there is Kumba! With 360° inversions, drops, twists, and turns this is one of the more wild coasters at Bush Gardens. Good for older kids, teens, and adults.
likes: Suitable for older kids, teens, adults

reviews_attraction.text: If you like coasters with drops this is a coaster for you! It's just you, 200ft up and 90° straight down! Great coaster, kind of short but still worth the wait. Good for teens and adults.
If your visiting during the summer this will definitely be on your ride to-do list. Great water ride helping you to cool off and have fun on those hot days! Good for families.
Not my favorite beach but it is nice to come and watch the sunset or play volleyball. The snack bar is really nice and I definitely recommend the mozzarella sticks!
A lot of very cool items and displays to check out here, from exotic art to mysterious people and animals there is something here for everyone!
Very fun and exciting show for families and especially kids! Featuring sights, sounds, and smells all inside of the tree of life!
Good for kids to explore and play on, from here you can shoot water cannons onto riders of The Bilge Rat Barge water ride!
When they say 4D they mean 4D! Join Shrek and Donkey on this wild and wacky adventure in their attempt to save Fiona!

Sagamore Hill truly captures the personality of Theodore Roosevelt. Standing at the front door of the home waiting for your house tour it feels like he will burst through the doors any minute and greet you on the front porch with a big handshake. Tickets are needed to tour the home and  group sizes are limited for each tour. Try book a tour of the home in advance though, otherwise they are issued on a first come, first served basis at the visitor center and you might need to wait a while depending on the day.

The home is a big trophy room, not just for his hunting trophies (which also serve as his collection and both a sportsman, but also as naturalist in the tradition of the 19th century). It is also very much a home where his family would all gather for dinner regularly, and a trophy room for his vast love of books and literature and where the family would often read by the fire.

The grounds are a mixture of natural beauty with open fields, wooded hiking trails, and a section of beach on Cold Spring Harbor that you can still hike down to. With home to plenty of wildlife for suburban NY. Touring the grounds at your leisure is a great way to spend an afternoon or to kill time while waiting for your house tour.

A great tour guide will help bring the home to life with plenty of little stories about life in the home. For instance, the reason they added a second telephone to the home was because the original phone was put in the pantry. Edith Roosevelt kept the pantry locked and held the keys to keep Theodore out of the cookies. One day while he was in his Presidency a phone call came and his wife was not home so he couldn't get to the phone.

The Junior Ranger program here is good and helps guide kids through the museum exhibits to understand the life and contributions T.R. made. They also have a Junior Ranger program for both nature and wildlife at sagamore hill. Complete both booklets and the kids get a very  cool patch in addition to the badge! Check with the visitor center for the booklet when you arrive and before you head down to the museum or go on the tour of the home. There are also several programs for Boy and Girl Scouts, again check with the visitor center.

Not only the home of the 26th President of the United States from birth to about age 12, but it is also the location of the founding of the American Museum of Natural History. The museum charter was developed and signed in the front parlor of the Roosevelt home on April 8, 1869.

Your tour guide helps bring the place and it's former occupants come to life.

It has a pretty easy Junior Ranger program for the kids, which is a great introduction to TR (and the program if they haven't done them elsewhere) and the kids love the badge they get, but they need to pay attention on the tour to get most of the answers.  The rest can be figured out from reading the plaques in the visitor area or asking a ranger.

Unfortunately, the museum exhibits on the lower level leave much to be desired. The only real items of interest are the shirt, eye glass case, and folded speech that TR had when shot in 1912, all showing the bullet holes. Years ago they used to have many of his own taxidermy birds from when he was a teenager, but they removed them after the renovation because they didn't have the right controlled environment for them.

But if you are in lower Manhattan and have an hour to spare to grab the 40 minute tour and do it.

A great place of Natural beauty with plenty of places for hiking, camping, kayaking, fishing, etc. However, due to budgetary restrictions not all ranger stations are open all the time. They rotate which stations ate openned and manned throughout the park land. Call ahead if you want to stop in the visitor center, especially if you want to take a shot at the Junior Ranger program for the kids.

The Junior Ranger program here is well organized for kids and takes about 1-2 to complete, but they get a cool badge when they are done.

Definitely worth the stop even if you don't camp out or anything it is still a great place to stop even if you are just passing through.

Ranger led tour of the Springwood mansion are self guided following a brief set-up by the ranger, which is a nice change of pace from more traditional tours.   The grounds are nice to walk, but  spend most of your time in the museum/library, it has some great artifacts. Don't forget to go down to the basement of the museum to see FDR'S model ship collection, customized car, and White House desk.  Even if you don't like FDR's politics you can gain some appreciation for the man.

The Junior Ranger program can be tricky but with the tour of the home it is very accessible for kids. Ask for a booklet at the visitor center when you arrive.

A very historical Maryland home of Gabriel Duvall, one of the early Supreme Court justices, but now often forgotten. Stacy was a fantastic tour guide for the home; an expert on the lives of the Duvall family members in Maryland, and their relationship with other notable founding families in the state as well as with Jefferson, Madison, and Monroe.

You can explore the grounds at your  leisure. However to tour the home call ahead! They are short staffed and someone may not always be available if you show up without calling ahead.

Very powerful exhibit and information about the tradgety of 1889 flood. To understand it and raise awareness is a wonderful way to honor the memory of the victims and the town's resilience. The film is very powerful experience and highlights the true horror of the flood; not great for kids or sensitive viewers, bit very powerful and sobering experience.  The Junior Ranger program (takes an hour or less) is good and is based on age but doesn't quite guide a kid through the exhibits, it's a lot of hunting and finding answers.

A hidden gem of the National Park Service in the Washington DC area.  Grounds are well managed, beautiful and quite natural setting, and Ranger Lassman is truly dedicated to this location and is a wealth of knowledge. He not only brings the story of Thomas Stone to life, but the history of Maryland as well through the arc of the Stone family.  Also has a really good Junior Ranger program here too - not too difficult or hard but informative and educational for all ages.

I was only there once to attend a service; the architecture is typical Protestant Anglican of the period; sparse, whitewashed, with individual family pews. Nothing special except that George Washington worshiped here...although the church now seems to want to remove that historical reference now.

Unless you plan to go there to attend Sunday services you can probably skip it. Although the garden is nice place to stop and get some shade in the late spring/early summer.

After several hours visiting steamtown National Historic Site the trolley museum was a bit underwhelming. They have 3-4 refurbished electric trolleys and a few placards describing the acquisition and refurbishment of one of the trolleys. And an large play room for kids between the ages of 2-8. It's not a bad little museum and they do take a lot of pride in it, but there is not much to see.

We stopped in while visiting family in the area. What a great little museum on whaling on Long Island. The scrimshaw pieces they have are fantastic, they even have an example of scrimshaw on baleen. The kids had a great time and they usually have fun activities for kids going on too. The staff are great. It's worth the stop for an hour or so.

Grounds a great to walk and explore in spring, summer, and early fall. Tours of thea mansion (only gilded age estate in the National Park Service) is undergoing major renovations until 2018. But ranger led tours of the mansion are self guided which is a nice change from traditional tours. No flash photography though.

Great visitors center that ties the battle, George Washington, and the history of the openning of the road through the mountains to the Ohio valley.

One of the best designed Junior Ranger program for kids too. It really helps guide them through the museum sections in a great well organized and engaging way.

Offers an in depth view of the immigrant experience in the Johnstown, PA area, a children's activity area (best for younger kids, say pre-school to maybe 2nd grade), and a history of the city's iron and steel works which is actually pretty interesting. If you have an hour or two go ahead and make the stop.

An impressive zoo, with a mix of big game animals (male lions, giraffes, tiger, wolves) with smallermonies, lemurs,  birds. Animal enclosures are kept clean and staff are out and about cleaning enclosuelres and feeding animals. Some of the enclosures seems too small for some of the animals though...

The exhibits in the visitor center do a great job of communicating the real peril, bravery, sacrifice, and strategic importance of the events in September 1814.

The Junior Ranger program is very well done to take kids through the exhibits in the visitor center and the fort itself.

Home for former Governor and siege of Yorktown militia leader Thomas Nelson. Used by Lord Cornwallis as his headquarters during the siege. It's amazing that some 230+ years after the battle the scars can still be seen such as the cannon balls still stuck in the side of the house.

Nice historic fort, but you can see how the Park Service needs some appropriations for repairs.  The Junior Ranger program is pretty good to help kids explore the fort and natural surroundings. Pick up the booklet at the visitor center when you arrive.

We stumbled on this place while vacationing in southwest corner of Pennsylvania. What a little hidden gem of a National Historic site. It is closed during the winter months though. I recommend visiting this in conjunction with Fort Necessity too.

Nice park. Entrance fee. Can get crowded in nice weather. We found the Junior Ranger program here to be on the more difficult side as the hand drawn maps of the trails are confusing and hard to interpret when you reach a specific location.
Place where the Revolutionary war ended. If your children participate in the Junior Ranger program this has one of the more challenging booklets that can take about 2+ hours for them to complete.
Well managed zoo that isn't too big and not too small. Plenty of large animals with lots of smaller ones. They just expanded the elephant paddock so the have a lot more space.
Trails are well marked and the Potomac lookout has a lovely breeze, but the hike is pretty boring, mostly gravel roads. The trail map could use some improvement.
Public green space surrounding the American Museum of Natural History. A great place to eat lunch or take a break from the museum and sit outside.
Rangers are very friendly and engaging. Nice oasis in NYC.  The Junior Ranger program is good and well done. Kids get nice badge when done.
Pricey but a good mix of indoor and outdoor exhibits. Definitely take the boat ride out to the island, it's worth the extra cost.

I am amazed that it took me this long to get to this Stadium. We went to see a concert, and I was very happy with the entire experience. There was more than enough parking, and we did not have to walk more than a few blocks to get to the stadium entrance. Once inside, the seating areas where well-marked, as were the bathrooms. I will say that we were sent to our seats the long way by a worker, but once we got there, we were happy with the setup. Also, by walking a long way, we got to see more of the food offerings, which were okay. They did seem to have a lot of alcoholic offerings, which surprised me a little, but maybe not. I would definitely go back to the stadium to see a concert, or a baseball game. It was definitely a pleasant experience.

We love this small museum! The Roebling story is amazing, and the more you know about the family and their achievements, the more interesting it becomes. The museum is not too visible from the road, but once you pass the gates, they have a good amount of parking. The building itself is is nicely organized, with well-constructed and informative displays spread out among the various rooms. One of my favorite things is a painting of the view from (what is now) a main door; it shows you what was there when the complex was full of large industrial buildings. They even discuss how the town was one of the first "factory towns" in America. I definitely recommend this museum for young and old. It's definitely worth the ride!

We went here to view their Christmas show. The space is very well-managed, especially the parking area. We found a spot in an outer lot, and the buses ran quickly and the drivers were pleasant. When we got to the main gardens area, there was lots to see and it was beautifully laid out. There were families, and single people, and teens, and senior citizens. We really loved how everything was displayed, and there was so much to see, that we don't think we got it all within 2 hours. We will definitely be back to see the Christmas lights next year!

We love the Count Basie! This lovely space has a beautiful interior that makes it a pleasure to attend any event. I'm always impressed that the staff supervise the client traffic well, and the ushers are businesslike but helpful. The seats are comfortable, so longer events are still easy to sit through. They have some great events, too, and we've attended everything from school shows to pop bands to plays to lectures. And now that the Basie is being expanded, we look forward to seeing what's ahead for them.

This is a beautiful museum. We enjoyed the exhibit we went to, which was especially easy to view because we bought  memberships to the Museum. The exhibit was absolute wonderful, and had to do with mirrors. We were not necessarily fond of the rest of the museum, where many of the works were spread out a bit far, and seemed to be too similar to things we'd seen at other museums in Washington. We would definitely come back for an exhibit, but as just a museum visit, I think we've settled on the one and done.

This is a very cool historical site. It is easily accessed in downtown Plymouth. We did not go in season, but there does appear to be a good amount of parking nearby. You can then walk over to the Rock area. It has been enclosed somewhat, with a fence / guardrail around it, and a roof over the top. There is explanatory material around it, and it is located in a really nice Waterfront area. My friend and I view this while going over to a nearby restaurant. If it is a sunny day this is really beautiful area.

I love the Belmar boardwalk! It's great to walk on in the early morning hours, pre- and post-sunrise. It's a little over a mile both ways, and has a pleasant surface. It's nice to see the same folks walking every day, and even the same staff opening up businesses (hello, those who powerwash in front of Dejais). Belmar as a town is lovely, as well, with many restaurants and shops to check out, and the lovely marina on the Shark River Inlet. All in all, a great place to visit, and a nice beach to check out!

This is a nice public area. The Plymouth Rock has a cool building around it, and it's easily accessed. The waterfront area in general is quite nice, and easy to navigate. We loved wandering into the shops, checking out the rock and the public art display (6-foot lobsters!) and dining at a local seafood restaurant. This is a great area for families, as there are lots of shops mixed in with the public areas. We'll definitely be back to discover more in Plymouth!

This park is absolutely lovely. I had not been in this area for quite a while, and was pleasantly pleased to see that the park is being well-maintained. There was a Shake Shack, and we grabbed a table and did some people watching. It is within view of the Flatiron building, and when we were there on a weekday during lunch time, there was lots of action pretty much everywhere. We would definitely recommend this park to families and people just out for lunch.

Longstreet Farm is a great reminder of Monmouth County's past. This is a working farm, with real animals and crops being tended. They are open for visitors daily, but the events they have there really are the best. The staff and volunteers are dressed in period costume and are exceptionally knowledgeable. This is also connected to Holmdel Park, so you can attend an event here then have a picnic at the park, or hit the playground at the top of the hill.

The National Portrait Gallery is amazing! It is beautifully organized, and easy to navigate. The portraits are beautiful, and all indicative of times and places within our countries history. I was especially happy to see the new picture of President Obama, and an older portrait of the founder of Girl Scouts, Juliette Low. There is also a very neat area with American musicians, and that was very cool. We will definitely be back!

I went right after Christmas, and the Sstalls were still up from the holiday fair. I really enjoyed looking around everything, and the storekeepers seemed in good spirits even though it was really cold. It's cute to see the rink open, even in the cold. This is a fun experience for Midtown, or even if you're just coming up from Times Square. After this, I went to the library to warm up, and that was beautiful as well.

I went during a break from jury duty (the courthouse is across the street), and was welcomed by a friendly volunteer. The painting in the lobby is wonderful and original (Leutz, I think?) and the exhibits are always top-notch. I was lucky enough to be meet their archivist who answered some family history questions for me, and gave me suggestions for further reading. I can't wait to go back to the next exhibit!

Amazing state park. Lots of history here. We've had great times with the kids at the playground, and hiking the trails, and wandering the village asking questions of the reenactors / docents, and attending the crafts fairs and flea markets. the train rides are also great for the kids. Would definitely recommend for a nice day out when in the area, or as a destination on days when craft fairs are scheduled.

We stopped by on a sunny Sunday afternoon, and it was quite nice. The staff were helpful with parking, and the shop staff were friendly as well. Lots of mask wearing, and a clean bathroom. There was a program outside, with plenty of open space and families sitting enjoying the cool vibes. We will definitely be back, and will check out the event schedule too.

This church is lovely. It's small, so you need to arrive early to insure you're able to sit down. The artwork inside is beautiful, and the view from the front door is very pretty. The congregation does not cater to small children, so if you have little ones, I wouldn't take them here; each noise is amplified and people turn around, acting upset.

This is an amazing tourist attraction! I would definitely recommend it for families with children! The gentleman is friendly and has t-shirts available. He allows you to look into the house and will also share its history with you. While we didn't expect to see it, we were very happy we came upon it and will recommend it to others.

This is a standard tourist shop, but it has a really good selection of branded items (shirts, hats, etc.,) and the information area was very helpful when planning a day in the area. We definitely recommend checking this out when planning a day in Niagara Falls (NY)

We have loved our several visits here. The displays are very well-researched and very well presented. There are a lot of people here, so I would always recommend getting here early. But they handle the crowds well, and you can usually see everything in one visit.

This is a lovely vineyard that serves wonderful locally produced wine. We had actually seen some of the bottles in a more touristy shop, but stopped at the actual vineyard to buy it. They have tastings, and the staff are friendly. We will definitely go back!

We stopped in on a whim, and boy are we glad we did! This winery is a hidden gem! The staff were welcoming, friendly, and very knowledgeable, the location had great decor, and there was ample parking. We will be back, hopefully for a full tasting or meal!

This park is great! There are tennis courts, and a lovely bridge, and a path by the lake to explore. And the playground is just lovely for young children. We love exploring the surrounding area, and just sitting for nice afternoon visits.

One of the best museums in DC, if not the US. A wide selection of genres and eras, spread out just enough, and set in perfect viewing conditions. The shop is nice, as are the bathrooms. We love this museum!
This park is great. It's well maintained and used for many activities, like little league games, soccer games, tennis, platform tennis, and camp. It's situated well, and has ample parking.
The Lawn at UVA was quite lovely. A beautiful outdoor space that allows you to chill out during serious days. We enjoyed check out its beauty, and that of the buildings on the periphery.

What a great respite from the daily hustle and bustle of life.  To go and feel the peace of Heaven and once again focus on what matters makes the journey of mortality easier.  The Temple is splended in nature and architectural detail.  The grounds are landscaped beauitifuly and are family friendly.  The Visitor Center can help answer the great questions of life: "Where did we come from?", "Why are we here?", "Where are we going after we pass away?".  It also has amazing art displays, seasonal venues, missionaries to speak with, a family history center, a scale model of the Temple and what is inside, and a beautiful copy of the Christus Statue.  A place to go with your family or by yourself.  Ask the questions that have been on your mind and discover the answers that will come.

To go through Thomas Jefferson's home and see his inventions, books, artifacts, art collection, and how he lived brought to life much of what I have learned about him and taught me many new things.  The home is in amazing condition and the tour guide was very knowledgeable and answered all questions asked.  The grounds are expansive and showed his drive to explore and create new plants.  His garden is over two football fields long and is well worth the walk through.  Coming here helped me understand Jefferson so much better.

What a magnificent monument to remember the lives lost and the struggled fought for by Pennsylvania citizens.  It is a solemn reminder that freedom and unity is not free or easy to continue.  Upon plaques on the base and pillars are the names of those who fought at Gettysburg.  In one of the pillars is a stair well that will take you to the top so you can view the surrounding battlefields, monuments, and countryside.  A great stop on your tour of history.

Pine Hill is a beautiful park set near the top of the mountain.  It comprises 174 acres with baseball fields, a soccer field, skate park, pavilions, and over three miles of walking/mountain biking trails.  While on the trails you can see an amazing view of the valley, and wild life.  Pine Hill has had a number of 5K races that make great use of the walking trails.  This is one of the best little known parks in the Waynesboro area.

Lady Liberty is one gal you don't want to miss!  Her dignity, her consistency, her love of freedom, and the way she always hold the touch to light way is inspiring and shows complete dedication.  The exhibit inside shows the progress of her growth and the intricacies of her structure.  There are a lot of stairs to climb, but the view from the pedestal is amazing!  For those that can not do stairs they do have an elevator.

A great historic building to visit in the Old City neighborhood.  It is a well preserved building that has been continually owned by the Carpenter's Company since it was built in the 1770's.  This is where the First Continental Congress was held in 1774.  It is free admission to the public and very close to other historically significant buildings in Philadelphia that you would be interested in attending.

The grounds are quite and peaceful even though it is in the middle of the city.  There are many sculptures, water features, and flowers/plants to enjoy.  The flowers are season and continually change.  The architecture has such great detail, rich history, and symbolism to describe here in detail.  The interior of the Temple and ordinances thereof make an impact upon the soul.

The theater is very well preserved and it is not a rushed atmosphere.  You can view where President Lincoln was shot and then find a seat in the balcony area to contemplate what happened all those years ago, and the subsequent effects his President had on the United States.  There is a museum there that reviews the time in which he lived and it is well presented.

Depending on the day you go the line can be very long to enter the facility to see the Liberty Bell.  If you are short on time or don't enjoy long lines you can choose to stay outside and go to one of the windows of the room where the Liberty Bell resides.  You can see it from there, but it may be obscured by the visitors who are walking around it on the inside.

This Capitol is grandiose and shows the splendor of the Commonwealth when it was the worlds sixth largest economy.  A few of the features: terracotta roof, 52 million ton dome, stained glass windows by a student of Tiffany's, grand marble staircase, and priceless artwork everywhere.  A must see for the lover of history, art, architecture, or Pennsylvania.

Temple Square is a great place to come and walk around.  The grounds are immaculate, have flowers constantly changing, and a large variety of trees and shrubs.  On the grounds you have the Salt Lake Temple, Tabernacle, Visitor Center, water features, statues, and much more to see.  If you have any questions, don't hesitate to ask the Sister Missionaries.

The size and scope of what they can fit in this building is truly amazing.  Not only does it have the permanent Idaho and local exhibits, but also hosts many traveling exhibit.  I saw King Tut's Treasure and Bodies The Exhibition here.  These were fantastic and helped expand my knowledge of history and the body in ways I would not have imagined.

This Museum stands as a memorial to the atrocities of men, human suffering, and what can happen when we reduce our fellow human beings to nothing.  From recreating Jewish homes, Holocaust layouts, items and artifacts from concentration camps are found within.  This will make a lasting impact upon all who enter.

The FDR Memorial is set up chronologically throughout his years of Presidency.  Throughout the complex are inspirational, profound, and though provoking quotes by FDR.  Statues, water features, and stone formations add to the depth/impact the Great Depression and World War II formed his Presidency.

This Capitol is constructed of granite and has many beautiful details inside.  I was amazed by the amount of natural light that pours in, and the grand staircase.  It sits high above the city and the grounds are well maintained.  It is easy to explore and look at the items they have displayed.

What an amazing find amongst the potato fields of Idaho!  The Zoo is well maintained and the amount of animals/varieties was surprising for the population size of this area.  It coat a little more than I was expecting, but to see these animals it was worth it.

A well preserved Greek Revival building in the heart of old down town Philadelphia.  It was a stock exchange for years and has many fascinating stories.  Build in the 1800's it is America's oldest standing stock exchange building.

This is a beautiful park in the midst of a bustling city.  It was calm, peaceful, and a pleasant place to walk and sit.  The landscape is friendly, and there were a number of wedding photos being taken here one day that I went.

The St. George Temple is located on a beautiful plot of ground that is well maintained.  The architecture and pure white finish is quite stunning.  A peaceful place to think of Christ and remember why we are here on earth.

This Monument gives a straightforward and symbolic tribute to those who fought, lost their lives, and are buried at Soldiers National Cemetery.  It is powerful, demands your attention, and is at the heart of the states.

The trails and park are well maintained.  The major waterfall is well worth the hike, and fun to go around and discover.  It is peaceful and is in a part of Maryland that I had never though of traveling to before.

A wonderful place to contemplate the beauty of God's earth and your life.  On a clear day you can see across the county to next mountain range, and down to West Virginia.  A great place to go exploring.
A water park, streams, camping area, picnic area, and miles of trails!  Come and enjoy the beauty of Pennsylvania!  Close proximity to Gettysburg, I-81, and historic Chambersburg.
A spacious building filled with artifacts, antiques, PA stuffed wildlife, and art.  There is a lot of room to move around in and will keep kids attention.
Have you ever wondered by what authority Jesus the Reedemer was baptized by?  If so, this is the place to come and learn more about it.

Incredible roller coaster located in the front section of Cedar Point... A beautifully designed and very comfortable B&M winged coaster, Gatekeeper will exhilarate you every time u ride it. Having the first loop right at the top of the lift hill is insane and incredible. A nice fast moving line makes it seem like your not waiting on line at all. Get the front seat. The loop inside the gate is amazing. A must ride when u first get to the park.

2018 Update.. Still one of the best wing coasters on the planet... Front row is still the choice when choosing a seat. The lines have gotten much smaller over the years with all the other rides that have been created so it’s nice to just walk on to this one.

If I could give out 10 stars, I would for this magnificent piece of steel. Beautifully designed and crafted and has an incredible view. The drop is insane overlooking the lake and the rest of the ride lives up to all the hype as one of the best coasters in the world. Amazing air time and speed throughout the ride and keeps the adrenaline pumping like crazy. Highly recommended even with a long line. Loved the front row. A++++++++++++

2018 Review... still the best rollercoaster in the world. I rode it twice this past trip and it’s still amazing. Front row is just extremely exhilarating and the back row, which I tried for the first time, is wickedly fast.

It was, at one time, an incredible feet to hit 200 feet in height almost 30 years ago, but it's definitely showing its age. Its a very rough snd bumpy ride and was too much for me to love. You get a nice view of the park, but thats about it. Only ride it if your looking to add to your resume.

2018 Review. I’m adding a star. I actually really enjoyed the ride this time around sitting in the back seat... I didn’t enjoy the front seat 5 years ago, but had a fun time in the back row this year... There’s never a line so it’s a must ride... I love how it goes through the water park.

Five stars all the way. This coaster whips and turns you and shoots you out s few times while never making it over 100 feet in the air. And it does an amazing job at it. Just when you think its over, you enter a tunnel and it shoots you out again to finish the ride. Amazing roller coaster. A must ride... Lines are long so get there early.

2018 Review... still long lines like crazy. Thank God for Fast Land Plus. By 11am, there was an hr line for this ride... It well worth it since it’s a great ride... Note to anyone, don’t wear your hat on the ride...

A classic Disney water park. A nice refreshing different thing to do when your looking for something to do that's not one of the theme parks. Lots of great slides and water attractions. Wave pool is phenomenal. A giant surf wave plows itself down every few minutes throughout the day. The brand new Miss Adventure Falls is a great family raft slide and the Humunga Cowabunga still terrifies people just like it did 20 years ago. Also check out Crush n Gusher, 3 different water coaster slides that each have unique twists and turns...

A great addition to the Universal lineup, the Transformers ride packs a ton of crazy twists and turns and some serious 3D action that’s sure to have your head spinning when you get off. It’s Action-packed from the beginning to the end. Make sure you grab some Advil afterwords because you’re gonna need it. It really does a number to your head. It has the same ride style as Spiderman so expect the same kind of ride. Very busy in the summertime.

Exhilarating is the term that comes to mind when you think of Kingda Ka. Breathtaking also, from its gigantic existence to the 128 mph speed it gives off. After shooting out at 128, you climb 456 feet in the air and then plummet back to Earth on a 90 degree angle while still trying to catch your breathe. A must ride at the park for any thrill seeker. Always a line... Front row is the best.

The best thing Cedar Point ever did was change this coaster from a crappy stand up to a floor less, change the name and give it some new color and elements. It was so much smoother and it didn’t hurt at all, which stand up coasters are famous for. Floor less coasters are much better and this one gets 4 stars now instead of 2, which it would have had if it was still a standup...

An absolute must if you come to Hershey and for some reason, there is never a long line.. Usually a walk on...  A beautifully built launched coaster from Intamin located in the Pioneer Frontier section of the park...  After your initial launch, you fly up and back down into a huge drop and continue into a barrel roll.. Ride it multiple times and ride in the front row...

World Showcase is the perfect 2nd part of Epcot. Who wouldn’t love to hop from country to country with only having to walk a few feet between each. The food, the drinks, the shopping and the culture are brought together in perfect sequence. Give yourself enough time to check out each country and try to eat at at least one of the restaurants every time you go...

A fun and exciting 4D show built right into the Tree of Life at Disney's Animal Kingdom. One of the original attractions at the park, it's still a fun and exciting show to watch. The effects on screen plus the real life stuff make for a great show experience. Based on A Bugs Life. Doesn't draw much of a crowd anymore so you should be able to walk right on.

A classic boomerang roller coaster located in the Pioneer Frontier section of the park...  After you back up to the top of the hill, you drop down into a series of three loops until you hit the top again.  After making it up, you fly back down backwards and do it all over again...  Great ride with a 48 inch height limit so younger kids can ride.

Gotta love B&M coaster's and this one stands out for me as one of my favorite hypercoasters... Its a perfectly smooth ride from start to finish with air time hills throughout along with some great curves and helixes. I compare this to Nitro at Great Adventure. A must try and I've never actually had to wait for this ride. Front row is the best.

At my home park, we have the taller brother Kingda Ka. But the original stands up to all the hype. It may be a little shorter in height, but it still gives the insane adrenaline pumping ride that Ka does. There's nothing like shooting out at over 100 mph and climbing 400 feet in less than a few seconds. A must ride for any coaster fan.

The Simpsons is probably the only tv show franchise that I wouldn’t have had a problem with replacing Back to the Future, which was a classic. Love the simulator. You fly through Springfield and meet all the characters and have a wild experience. It jerks your head a lot. Take Advil with you... you will get nauseous.

Main Street USA is a replica straight out of Walt Disney's hometown... Relive what it was like for Walt when he was a kid walking down the streets of Marceline, Missouri... You have a bunch of stores, places to get a snack, to get a cup of coffee and to start your day at the Magic Kingdom.
likes: Facilities & Services: Variety of shops, snack options

reviews_attraction.text: Disney at its best!!!! As usual, Disney turns a simple little roller coaster into a fun and exciting mid level thrill ride with cool twists, turns and speeds through the world of Toy Story. A must ride when you come. Grab a fast pass early if possible. The stand by line takes for ever...

It’s great that Universal has stuck with this ride after all these years, especially since the film reboots have brought a lot of attention again to the ride. It’s amazing being able to take a boat ride through a fake Jurassic Park. And the drop at the end gets you soaked. Lots of fun.

Gotta love the Land Ride. It sucks they got rid of the live people speaking to you on the boat and replaced them with an automated version, but what you gonna do. Still a great ride with lots of interesting facts about fruits, vegetables and plants...

As usual, Six Flags ruins all there new rides. This one came out swinging with such high potential and it was such a let down and a disappointment. It barely spun as we crossed the track... I'll try it one more time, but only when there is no line.

Fantasmic is an incredible show of lights, music, action and fire... Join all the Disney characters on a fun filled adventure. Fireworks, lasers, fire and more make this show one of the best in the park...
One of the largest family raft rides in the country. This ride does not disappoint from the top all the way to the bottom. A must ride early when you get to the park.
Great place for sports. Fields are always in top condition for playing soccer, baseball and softball. And the surrounding woods is a great place to hike...
Great park for all kinds of activities... it’s great for hiking, great for basketball and a fun place for racing 5K’s, 5 milers and more...
A classic old school wooden coaster that still gives a rush after almost 100 years of existence. Great for younger kids.

The patio here aligns with the vines and gorgeous mountain views.  Plenty of outdoor seating in a beautiful setting. There is a good selection of wines and they also serve beer as it is the original location of Skull Camp Brewery.....so they have an extensive tap list from there. They also have a disc golf course on location. Thanks for the great service Ashley and experience!!!

Great experience that takes you to a time when it all started and finishes with the modern era. Museum is very educational and provides some hands-on kiosks and plenty of video to view throughout the museum to include a few theaters. Finishes with a NFL shop to buy your favorite team products.  This is a must see and allow at least three hours to do it right.

It is a very old and one of the longest running state penitentiaries that ran for over a century. Not as old or interesting as East Penitentiary in Philadelphia. Our tour guide Jason had good stories and was on point with the tour. Sounds like the ghost tours would also be interesting. Tour take 90 minutes and worth the price of the ticket.

Nice 9 hole short track that was in town. The fairways were in decent shape. The greens seemed to be well maintained. Plenty of parking there and greens fee with cart was reasonably priced. There were vending machines but no snack bar in operation.
Also has a pool, tennis, part, band stand, skate rink, playground, and put-put golf.
