Beautiful panoramic views from a spacious seating area. Plenty of parking and seating. Would have rated it higher but we were denied wine flights because it was late. It was 5:05 when we got there and they close at 6. Don't understand their rationale as we had almost an hour till closing. Nothing on their website about this.

This is a nice location that boasts lots of things to doin the outdoors. There are plenty of hiking trails nearby to include Flat Top and Sharpe Top mountains. There are flat trails around the lake area. The is camping and lodging there. It is also close to apple orchards and wineries.

Great house museum that dates back to the 1800s. Susan was our guide and was awesome. She provided insight to the history of the Jackson family and the mansion. This is a must see if in the area. Check websites for when it's open.......limited days and hours. It provides guided tours.

Good tasting experience here. Lots of good dry wine here. The owner was very personable as she takes the time to come around to engage guests. This place is building an 8,000 seat amphitheater and a event center. Nice relaxing g views from the spacious seating areas.

This cruise is well worth the money.  Our guide was very entertaining and provided many facts about the ships we saw. The experience was educational and provided many up-close views of the ships. Combo tickets are available that include the Wisconsin and museum.

If you have never been it is well worth the time. It is about a half mile walk to the dunes from the parking lot. The largest dunes provide anawesome 360 degree panoramic view. They also offer beginning hang gliding lessons for about $120. Plenty of parking.

Great experience well worth the time! Our guide was informative and personable. There is a gift shop on ground.....very reasonable prices. Ther is plenty of parking available. You have to get your tickets from the visitor center outside of the venue.

This is areally great place to hit for an afternoon. There is a hiking trail that leads to water falls........four miles round trip. Take a hike and come back to the vineyards for some good wine. Lots of parking and open seating.
This is a nice peaceful half mile loop. The wooden deck walkway goes mostly over water.  It has picnic area, canoe/kayak launch, and a nice fishing area. Has limited parking with a job johnny.
Great history depicted here for naval aviation which has been home to Virginia Beach for years. Definitely worth stopping by to honor the courage and commitment of those that served.
Great park designed for kids with all abilities. Easy access for strollers and wheelchairs. Kids seem to really enjoy this playground. Good location with parking and restrooms.
Awesome spacious outdoor seating area with fire place and vinyard views. Plenty of parking and seating and good service.. They have a nice variety of wines.......and snacks.
Definitely worth the money to access the pier. It offers great panoramic views and a different perspective of the beach. It also offers a great location to fish from.
Great piece of work dedicated to the Navy Seals that gave their life while serving our nation.......honor and valor!!!! It is informative and educational.
Great green space! Beautiful panoramic views from the point looking over the James River.  There is also a level 4.5 mile scenic hiking trail.
Nice green space on the water with restrooms, tennis courts and playground. Attended art festival here and it was a nice place for it.
This place is so much more than a lighthouse.  Allow a couple of hours as there is alot to see. Highly recommend! Very educational.
Good location however parking lot is small and limited to little over a dozen spaces. Its hard to get a spot during nice weather.
Cool bridge with nice view of the James River located in a quaint town with lots of historic buildings dating back to the 1800s.
Nice park with wonderful green space.  Great place for a walk and picnic. Nice house museum, nature center, kids zoo.
Spacious park with lots to do here. Good hiking trails, fishing, pavillions along with lots of parking and rest rooms

(Translated by Google) This, for me, is the emblem of Disney. The magical place, the place of fantasies of adults and children, the place that has accompanied us in our lives, through its films. When you are in front of him, your feelings emerge, to the point that it is difficult to contain a tear, for all that this moment means. And if at night, you enjoy the game of gunpowder with your family at the same time, there is no longer a simple tear that arises, there you cry abundantly, thanking God for allowing you to enjoy so much splendor, together with the beings you love. It is sincere gratitude that you experience, something difficult to explain, but that you live intensely. Speechless.

(Original)
Este, para mí, es el emblema de Disney. El lugar mágico, el lugar de las fantasías de grandes y chicos, el lugar que nos ha acompañado en nuestras vidas, a través de sus películas. Al estar frente a él, tus sentimientos afloran, al punto de que es difícil contener una lágrima, por todo lo que significa ese momento. Y si en la noche, disfrutas el juego de pólvora con tu familia a la par, ya ahí no es una simple lágrima la que surge, ahí lloras abundantemente, agradeciendo a Dios por permitirte disfrutar de tanto esplendor, junto a los seres que amas. Es agradecimiento sincero lo que experimentas, algo difícil de explicar, pero que vives intensamente. Sin palabras.

(Translated by Google) A magical place. Yes, hackneyed, but it's the only way to describe it. For Harry Potter lovers this is the equivalent of paradise on Earth. Wherever you look, you feel trapped in their world. The various shops, the Gringotts Bank, the night bus, the dragon on fire ... everything is madness on foot! If you get a magic wand, you can perform various magic tricks all over the place. The dark passage is a gem and not to be missed "Harry Potter and the Escape from Gringotts". At the end of the day, and if you have a Park to Park ticket, do not hesitate to cross the Hogwarts Express. Simply let yourself be caught in this magical world.

(Original)
Un lugar mágico. Sí, trillado, pero es la única forma de describirlo. Para los amantes de Harry Potter este es el equivalente al paraíso en la Tierra. A cualquier lugar que dirijas la vista, te sientes atrapado en su mundo. Las diversas tiendas, el Banco de Gringotts, el autobús noctámbulo, el dragón echando fuego... ¡todo es la locura andando! Si consigues una varita mágica, puedes realizar diversos trucos de magia por todo el lugar. El pasaje oscuro es una joya y no se puede perder "Harry Potter y el escape de Gringotts". Al finalizar el día, y si cuenta con una entrada Park to Park, no dude en realizar la travesía del Hogwarts Express. Simplemente, déjate atrapar por este mundo mágico.

(Translated by Google) The old school, whose first records date from 1716, is at the entrance of St. George Street, near the gates of the old city. It is said to be the oldest wooden school in the United States, but in reality that honor corresponds to that of Boston, which is from 1635. What is certain is that it is the oldest school that is still standing, since that Boston's already disappeared. The lessons were taught below and the teacher and his family resided on the top floor. Rigorously, at least one photo must be taken in this place.

(Original)
La antigua escuela, cuyos primeros registros datan de 1716, queda en la entrada de la calle St. George, cerca de las puertas de la ciudad vieja. Se dice que es la escuela de madera más vieja de Estados Unidos, pero en realidad ese honor le corresponde a la de Boston, que es de 1635. Lo que sí resulta cierto es que es la escuela más antigua que se mantiene en pie, ya que la de Boston ya desapareció. Abajo se impartían las lecciones y en la planta alta residía el maestro y sus familia. De rigor debe tomarse al menos una foto en este lugar.

(Translated by Google) Start calm and end "violent"! The beginning is a leisurely walk among peaceful dinosaurs, who live in harmony with nature. But after a while, the atmosphere suddenly changes: the velociraptors stalk you and you start to fear for your life, because ... a Tyrannosaurus Rex is on the loose! What a problem! The end is unexpected and I don't want to kill the illusion. Of course, as a tip, do the tour with a cape or waterproof clothing, because, by default, it will come out wet, even if it is a little.

(Original)
¡Empieza tranquilo y termina "violento"! El inicio es un pausado paseo entre pacíficos dinosaurios, que conviven en armonía con la naturaleza. Pero al rato, el ambiente súbitamente cambia: los velociraptors te acechan y empiezas a temer por tu vida, porque... ¡un tiranosaurio Rex anda suelto! ¡Menudo problema! El final es inesperado y no quiero matar la ilusión. Eso sí, como consejo, realice el recorrido con capa o con ropa impermeable, porque, de fijo, va a salir mojado, aunque sea un poco.

(Translated by Google) It is a small aquarium, but do not be fooled, since in it you can find more than 5,000 sea creatures and more than 30 exhibitions, each one built with great little details, which make it unique. Here you can see sharks, jellyfish (my favorites), manta rays, turtles and a long etcetera of species from the sea. It must be rescued that its administrators strive to create awareness of how we can help in its conservation.

(Original)
Es un acuario pequeño, pero que eso no te engañe, ya que en él puedes encontrar más de 5.000 criaturas  marinas y más de 30 exposiciones, cada una construida con pequeños grandes detalles, que la hacen única. Aquí se pueden apreciar tiburones, medusas (mis favoritas), mantarrayas, tortugas y un largo etcétera de especies del mar. Se debe rescatar que sus administradores se empeñan en crear conciencia en la forma cómo podemos ayudar en su conservación.

(Translated by Google) It is a symbol of Saint Augustine, which unites the city center with Anastasia Island. It is guarded by two lions, hence its name. It dates from 2010 and in that year it was considered by the magazine "Carreteras y Puentes" as the fourth of the top 10 bridges in the United States. If you like to walk, here is the perfect excuse to do it, with majestic views anywhere you want to look.

(Original)
Es un símbolo de San Agustín, que une el centro de la ciudad con la isla Anastasia. Está custodiada por dos leones, de ahí su nombre. Data del año 2010 y en ese año fue considerado por la revista "Carreteras y Puentes" como el cuarto de los 10 principales puentes de Estados Unidos. Si le gusta caminar, aquí tiene la excusa perfecta para hacerlo, con unas majestuosas vistas a cualquier lado que quiera mirar.

(Translated by Google) The tour is interesting, but you feel a certain depression when you appreciate the gorillas in such a small space, as well as other monkeys. In fact, their faces do not express happiness. It is done on foot, but it is not exhausting. On your tour you learn a lot and other interesting species are known, such as lemurs and a variety of birds.

(Original)
Es interesante el recorrido, pero se siente cierta depresión al apreciar los gorilas en un espacio tan reducido, así como otros monos. De hecho, sus caras no expresan felicidad. Se realiza a pie, pero no es nada agotador. En su recorrido se aprende mucho y se conocen otras especies interesantes, como los lemúres y una variedad de aves.

(Translated by Google) It is a milestone that marks the end of the old Spanish road that linked San Diego, California, with San Agustin, Florida. This road was a project of the early twentieth century and pays homage to the Spanish heritage. Like the San Francisco Canyons Fountain, which is almost on par, it needs greater historical dissemination.

(Original)
Es un hito que marca el final del camino viejo español que unía San Diego, California, con San Agustín, Florida. Este camino fue un proyecto de principios del siglo XX y rinde homenaje a la herencia española. Al igual que la Fuente de los Caños de San Francisco, que queda casi a la par, necesita mayor divulgación histórica.

(Translated by Google) The best golf course I have made so far. The decoration, the atmosphere and the obstacles are incredible (caves, waterfalls, boat, etc,). And it has the peculiarity that water, stream and lake style passes everywhere, which makes you have to be careful when hitting the ball, since you can lose it at any time.

(Original)
El mejor campo de golf que he realizado hasta ahora. La decoración, el ambiente y los obstáculos son increíbles (cuevas, cataratas, barco, etc,). Y tiene la particularidad de que pasa agua, estilo arroyo y lago, por todos lados, lo que hace que debas tener cuidado a la hora de golpear la bola, ya que puedes perderla en cualquier momento.

(Translated by Google) A good place to go to visit and slow down from the lines and stress of the theme parks. Its surroundings are very beautiful and it remains very well kept. It can be covered in a short time. The only drawback is that you are very much indigent and drug addicted, which makes you lose a little peace and security.

(Original)
Un buen sitio para ir a visitar y desacelerarse de las filas y el estrés de los parques temáticos. Sus alrededores son muy bonitos y permanece muy bien cuidado. Se puede recorrer en poco tiempo. El único inconveniente es que se aprecia mucho indigente y drogadicto, que te hacen perder un poco la paz y la seguridad.

(Translated by Google) I love that San Agustín takes care of its incredible architectural and historical heritage. This is the oldest house in the city, built in the 18th century. Initially it belonged to a soldier named Tomás González and later, from 1812, it became the home of Mayor Gerónimo Álvarez.

(Original)
Me encanta que San Agustín cuide su increíble patrimonio histórico arquitectónico. Esta es la casa más antigua de la ciudad, construida en el siglo XVIII. Inicialmente pertenecía a un soldado llamado Tomás González y luego, a partir de 1812, se convirtió en la casa del alcalde Gerónimo Álvarez.

(Translated by Google) Its decoration and buildings are formidable. Only the desert and the camels are missing. Even in its passages you feel like you are touring a real Moroccan market, or inside a mosque, or reliving the movie "Casablanca". Beautiful place. Don't forget to visit Jasmine and Aladdin.

(Original)
Su decoración y edificios son formidables. Solo falta el desierto y los camellos. Incluso, en sus pasajes te sientes recorriendo un verdadero mercado marroquí, o en el interior de una mezquita, o bien, reviviendo la película "Casablanca". Precioso lugar. No olviden visitar a Jazmín y a Aladino.

(Translated by Google) He was expecting a lot from the United States flag, for being the host. The setting is very good, but I feel like I was left owing. It does not present major surprises. A choir of a cappella singers dressed in colonial style, were perhaps the only ones who stood up for the place.

(Original)
Del pabellón de Estados Unidos esperaba mucho, por ser el anfitrión. La ambientación es muy buena, pero siento que me quedó debiendo. No presenta mayores sorpresas. Un coro de cantantes a capela vestidos al estilo colonial, fueron tal vez los únicos que dieron la cara por el lugar.

(Translated by Google) Excellent dolphin show! These intelligent creatures provide a unique show, in conjunction with their trainers. Simply ... surprising! Tip: sit in the center, well away from the front rows. I am absolutely sure you will thank me. Then, enjoy the show.

(Original)
¡Excelente espectáculo de delfines! Estas inteligentes criaturas brindan un singular show, en conjunto con sus entrenadores. Simplemente... ¡sorprendente! Consejo: siéntate en el centro, bien alejado de las primeras filas. Estoy completamente seguro que me lo agradecerás. Luego, disfruta del espectáculo.

(Translated by Google) It is a very nice place, with beautiful gardens and very well kept. It has a waterfall, special to put it in the background for good photographs. Its totems are very striking: very well detailed and placed in harmony with the rest of the setting.

(Original)
Es un lugar muy bonito, con unos jardines preciosos y muy bien cuidados. Cuenta con una catarata, especial para ponerla de fondo para unas buenas fotografías. Llama mucho la atención sus tótems: muy bien detallados y colocados en armonía con el resto de la ambientación.

(Translated by Google) It should be the closest thing to doing a real safari in Africa. It is impressive to see wild animals so closely. The tour takes its time and can even be interrupted by the blocking of an animal, as in our case by a rhino.

(Original)
Debe ser lo más cercano a realizar un safari verdadero en África. Es impresionante ver animales salvajes tan de cerca. El tour toma su tiempo e incluso puede verse interrumpido por el bloqueo de algún animal, como en nuestro caso por un rinoceronte.

(Translated by Google) Impressive simulator that makes you fly in a paragliding or delta over the best wonders of the world: the great Chinese wall, the pyramids of Egypt, the Eiffel tower, the Iguazú falls, etc. Its realism is incredible!

(Original)
Impresionante simulador que te hace volar en parapento o delta sobre las mejores maravillas del mundo: la gran muralla china, las pirámides de Egipto, la torre Eiffel, las cataratas del Iguazú, etc. ¡Es increíble su realismo!

(Translated by Google) It leaves you speechless! Just touring Hogwarts Castle alone is worth it. Attraction as such transports you to various passages in the movies, except that you are inside them. Captivating.

(Original)
¡Te deja con la boca abierta! Solo el hecho de recorrer el castillo de Hogwarts ya vale la pena. La atracción como tal te transporta a varios pasajes de las películas, con la salvedad de que estás dentro de ellas. Cautivador.

(Translated by Google) The Italian pavilion did not disappoint. The replicas of the Markus Tower, the canals of Venice and even one of its Neptune fountains are very well done. Every detail was exceptionally highlighted.

(Original)
El pabellón de Italia no nos decepcionó. La réplicas de la torre de Markus, los canales de Venecia e incluso una de sus fuentes de Neptuno, están muy bien logradas. Cada detalle fue resaltado en forma excepcional.

(Translated by Google) It is striking the details so representative that Disney achieves of this country. Inside the pyramid it is like being in a Mexican market. And if you're lucky, a mariachi surprises you at any moment.

(Original)
Llama la atención los detalles tan representativos que Disney logra de este país. Dentro de la pirámide es como estar en un mercado mexicano. Y si tienes suerte, en cualquier momento te sorprende un mariachi.

(Translated by Google) Place where your children can interact with some of the Disney princesses and take some good photos with them. They are charming and make you feel in their magical world.

(Original)
Lugar donde tus hijos pueden interactuar con algunas de las princesas de Disney y tomar unas buenas fotos con ellas. Son encantadoras y los hacen sentir en su mundo mágico.

(Translated by Google) A live show that entertains you, while you enjoy its songs. It's an attraction to slow down a bit and enjoy various scenes from the first Frozen movie.

(Original)
Un show en vivo que te entretiene, mientras disfrutas sus canciones. Es una atracción para desacelerarse un poco y disfrutar de varias escenas de la primera película de Frozen.

(Translated by Google) The temple is beautiful, very well maintained and with splendid murals and paintings. Sundays offer Masses in Spanish. The priest who officiates them is very pleasant.

(Original)
El templo es precioso, muy bien cuidado y con murales y pinturas espléndidas. Los domingos ofrecen misas en español. El sacerdote que las oficia es muy ameno.

(Translated by Google) A nice live show, with a lot of color, dances and stunts. He spends a very pleasant time with the characters of the Lion King.

(Original)
Un bonito show en vivo, con mucho colorido, bailes y acrobacias. Se pasa un rato muy agradable con los personajes del Rey León.

(Translated by Google) Yes, it is simply a bathroom, but its decoration is incredible. It is a good point as a rest area.

(Original)
Sí, es simplemente un baño, pero su decoración es increíble. Es un buen punto como área de descanso.

This is one of the nicest parks in the county with a wide range of amenities for the whole family. We use the dog park which has a huge fenced in area where our dog can run off steam. Concrete walking paths throughout the park connect the different areas. Tennis courts, ball fields, and volleyball courts with white sand are all here. There's a fitness trail with outdoor exercise machines such as step climbers. A large outdoor playground for the kids with castle, mini play tractors and all kinds of swings and slides. There is also a natural hiking trail along the perimeter of the park, and educational illustrated signs identifying Florida trees and plants. Public restrooms and picnic pavilions are available,  and everything is clean, well lit and beautifully maintained. A first rate public park we are thankful to have in our area! Update -also a great place to fly a kite!
likes: Dog park with large fenced area

reviews_attraction.text: Of all the dog parks we have visited so far in Central Florida, this is by far the most beautiful. There is a big clear pond for swimming, and the dogs were just loving it - plus it kept our black haired baby nice and cool and hydrated. When we were finished she pretty much conked out in the back seat of the car and slept all the way home without panting or needing cooling towels.  HUGE fenced area for running and playing- we were told the park is 17 acres. Separate areas for small and large dogs. Benches, big shade trees and a nice clean restroom for the people; toy shelf and a dog washing station for the pets (bring your own shower hose for the spigot, or $10 for the dog wash that dispenses shampoo and warm water). No charge to use the park, just pick up after your dog. Ample parking. We'll definitely be going back!

A wonderful resource for gardening ideas and information! There are a variety of garden types from xeriscape to sub-tropical, rose, camellia and butterfly gardens, herbs, edible landscape and vegetable patches to name a few. There are also multiple water features throughout the garden, keeping you cool on a warm day. There is an enclosed butterfly area and even a hedge maze for the kids to enjoy. Local plant and garden groups maintain the different areas and offer information about their specialties. Every season there is something different to see, so do go often. This is also a good place for a peaceful walk or meditation. As a final note, there are ongoing classes on topics from gardening to cooking with local produce- check their website for current offerings. We love it here and highly recommend it.

What an amazing place to visit, especially this time of year (January ) with hundreds of manatees to see up close in their natural setting. Nicely maintained boardwalk trails, clean bathrooms,  gift store with good quality souvenirs, and a well stocked camp store with concession selling ice cream and hot dogs round out the amenities.  Rocking chairs outside the store gives it a homey feel and of course there are picnic pavilions. We just go there for the day so we can't say a lot about the campgrounds but everything appears well maintained. We're happy that leashed dogs are welcome on the trails. The staff is friendly and welcoming. Definitely a five star experience, perfect for families and tourists looking to see natural Florida in all its beauty.

Also known as the Sharp Family Tourism and Education Center, this is the place to start your tour of the Frank Lloyd Wright buildings at the Florida Southern College Campus. You can take a tour with a docent at certain times of day, or ask for the map/pamphlet for the self guided walking tour. We thought it was worth the $5 donation and were happy to contribute to the cause. The center's gift shop was well stocked with gifts, books, stationery and art objects based on Wright's life and designs. We had a delightful afternoon enjoying the sights and the history. Well worth the trip, especially if you are interested in architecture and design.

This was actually a great place to take a toddler - plenty here to look at, big enough to be interesting but small enough not to be overwhelming. We spent a few hours here on a weekday morning with our daughter and granddaughter  and enjoyed the aquarium displays and habitats. They were very nicely done The underwater tunnel isn't as big as it looks on the website - we were through it almost immediately and momentarily thought we'd missed something - but overall we enjoyed our experience and would take out of town guests tired of Disney there again.

Truly one of Florida's hidden gems, a perfect place to spend an afternoon if you love history. There's no charge to enter the grounds. The guided tour by a knowledgeable docent is only $5.00 ($4.00 for seniors) and is well worth it. There's even a multimedia theater presentation- a steamboat ride down the St. John's River- with a gently rotating floor to simulate the boat's motion. We thoroughly enjoyed our two hours there on a Sunday afternoon.

A very pretty waterfront park, especially at sunset. Boardwalk along the lake, sculpture, and a historic bandshell that is still used frequently for concerts and special events -check the city's website for upcoming events. There is an aquatic center with public pool, and you're right across the street from historic downtown Eustis with its shops and restaurants, as well as the Bay Street Theater.

Wonderful place to learn about the ecology of the area, informative and educational displays. The volunteers and staff at the help desk are knowledgeable and friendly. The building is clean and airy, there is an atrium with 30 foot tree display in the center of the building. There is a rooftop observation deck that looks out over the beautiful St. John's river. Great for families with children.

My wife grew up in Florida and didn't expect to be so impressed - you can truly have up close and personal experience with a wide variety of birds and animals. During our visit, an 8 foot+ alligator was lying placid against a fence seemingly smiling for the excited visitors snapping pictures from a few feet away. Lots of birds as well. A great place to bring out of town guests and family.

Beautiful place for a walk or a bike ride, on gravelly nature trails thick with wildflowers,  butterflies and birds. The hilly views are outside the norm for central and south Florida so you really feel that you're in a different environment.  There's a covered picnic pavilion,  benches and a nice restroom if you need a break. Dog friendly for leashed pets.

Lovely waterfront park, very scenic- great place to photograph birds. Play park and water park keep the kids entertained, and with shaded pavilions, this is an excellent choice for birthday parties or cookouts. We take our dog for walks there quite often. Quite a few good restaurants with outdoor seating are within walking distance, too.

Gorgeous waterfront park with docks for boaters. Nice big playgrounds for kids,  nature/walking trails, clean restrooms and picnic pavilions for the day tripper, and beautifully maintained campgrounds if you want to overnight. The park staff here is very friendly and does a great job of keeping the grounds clean and well maintained.

Wonderful small museum with a beautifully displayed collection, principally featuring the art of modern expressionist Abraham Rattner. It was well worth the visit. We particularly loved the interactive "April Showers" installation. Enjoyed shopping in the gift shop, too!

Lovely place for a nature walk, great place for learning about local wildlife- bring the family! Hiking and boardwalk trails, waterfront, picnic areas, turtle habitat, and nature museum. Trails are pet friendly, too. We really enjoyed our afternoon here.

Nice park adjacent to the Chamber of Commerce in downtown Mount Dora. Hosting site for numerous town events including holiday celebrations, Taste of Mount Dora, and a weekly Sunday morning farmers market. Clean public restrooms are also on site.

This is a really nice park-great for families. It's fun to take the pontoon boat to the island and then explore the trails. There's a nice small nature/history museum there too. Take the kids and a picnic and enjoy!

Many different sections to experience in this park; all are clean and well maintained. We go to the dog park frequently and walk the mountain bike trails. We've also used the pool. Great for all ages.
A hidden gem! We discovered that this is a lovely area to walk our dog, along trails lined with wildflowers. We will be back to explore the waterway with our kayaks. Natural Florida at its finest.
Unexpectedly beautiful formal southern gardens and woodland hiking trails just steps from the beach give a perspective on natural Old Florida not to be found anywhere else.
The park grounds are beautifully maintained and the small museum had some very interesting items on display. A part of history we didn't know much about. Glad we went.
Loved this park, from the beautiful grounds with paved walkways, gardens and waterfalls, to the gorgeous springs and swimming hole. Great for all ages.
Scenic stop with historic building and springs. Clean restrooms. Good place to park and off load bicycles for riding on the paved trail way.
One of Mount Dora's prettiest parks. It's a great place to walk, jog, take your dog for a stroll, and just relax. Lots of paved pathways.
Fun, eclectic collection of folk art by local artists, well curated and beautifully displayed. Always fun to shop and explore here.

A federal wildlife officer aggressively pulled up to our party as we were unloading our canoes and quickly began to question us as to why we were there. Considering we were at a boat launch with canoes that should have been self-evident! All five of us were perplexed and annoyed by her unwarranted posturing and baseless line of inquiry. Harassing police officers notwithstanding, the swamp was very enjoyable and serene once we finally got under way. Sad that our parks are starting to feel like a paranoid police state.

The shoreline of the preserve doesn't look like much from the Shands Bridge but it is totally beautiful experienced from a kayak or canoe! Also, there are several shallow places that allowed us to get out of our boats and stand up for nice break as well as pic-nic area with a table. The hiking and off road bicycling opportunities here are numerous as well. Lots of long routes can created using adjacent land holdings. Watch out for ticks and yellow flies during the warmer months!

Perfect place to experience what this area looked like prior to mass suburbanization and beltways. This mostly quiet woodland area is excellent for short to moderate walks. The vast majority of the property is dry and there are many locations in which to put a blanket on the ground for a relatively secluded picnic or hang a hammock. The property abuts to an active airfield and there were a few flights the day we visited but it was calm and quiet most of the time.

Yesterday's Festival was so much fun! Many local enthusiasts showcased everything from homemade clothes, cast iron cooking, vintage farm machinery, military memorabilia and reenacting, live music, home made baked goods, junk picking, arts of various kinds, vintage vehicles and more. My personal favorite was the collection of very large antique chainsaws! The park itself offers camping, cabins and hiking. Beautiful location!

The Dali Museum is one of the most innovative and beautiful buildings in Florida! The location and surrounding garden are gorgeous as well. A perfect place to house and exhibit the incredible collection of surrealist masterpieces by the reknowned and utterly unique Salvador Dali. The newly added virtual Salvador Dali video experience is cutting edge video technology and fits perfectly in this very stimulating environment!

Staying in the yurt at Torreya State Park was lots of fun! The camping area is situated on a surprisingly high bluff that allows for an uncommon Florida vista across the Apalachicola River and surrounding country side. The vista faces west allowing for amazing sunsets! The hiking here is beautiful as well with lots of tree species, rolling terrain and different micro-environments along the river and bluffs.

Thank you Camp Blanding Museum for allowing me to film my WWII documentary film in your main building! My uncle Joe was inducted into the army there in 1943 and filming his interview there 70 years later in 2013 was a special privilege I will never forget! This film is now available on YouTube for anyone that cares to view it: China Burma India Theater of World War Two - A Memoir.

The canoe trip from Rock Springs (King's Landing) to Wekiwa Springs was beautiful and at times rather exciting in some of the narrow passages where the current can run quickly amidst winding turns. Lots of amazing birds, turtles and even an alligator were seen. The clear to amber colored water is very clean and a joy to paddle in!

Beautiful place to hike or ride a bicycle! Lovely and well maintained pic-nic facilities in the parking area as well. The famous driftwood forest along shore is one the one the most unique shorelines in the area. The bicycle trail is paved with several small hikes along its length. Beautiful place to visit!

This state park offers a unique glimpse into what this part of Florida was like during the 1920's. Reenactors are often present and give wonderful guided tours of this well preserved and obviously loved homestead. Plan on having a meal at the nearby Yearling Restaurant if you can for a complete experience!

Alexander Springs is by far the most family friendly spring in the Ocala National Forest! Lots of shady picnic areas and a large shallow wading area. The spring head itself is fairly deep making for great snorkeling for good swimmers. There is also excellent canoe and kayaking opportunities there as well!

Adjacent to the Jacksonville-Baldwin Rail-Trail, the Camp Milton Preserve is a beautiful location for walks and pic-nics. Remnant and still visible Civil War earthworks as seen from the interpretive boardwalk silently proclaim that military conflict swept through this area not so long ago.

The Big Oak Trail certainly lives up to its name! This relatively small area is beautifully located at the confluence of the Suwannee and Withlacoochee Rivers. Great place to hike with lots of great trees and even a cave! Best enjoyed in the winter months when the bugs are dormant.

In addition to ample natural beauty and wildlife, Tomoka State Park was also once the site of a Native American settlement of the Timucua Tribe. We love launching our canoe from the boat ramp and enjoying the adjacent waterways. There are also several shorts hikes here as well.

Studying tree canopy access techniques at FDR State Park was an amazing experience! There were many large trees not only in the group camping area but along the trails as well. Close proximity to Callaway Gardens was a pleasant surprise! Great area for nature lovers!

Beautiful location and a rare and vivid glimpse into Florida's pre-European heritage that's all but lost. The surviving limestone stele and pyramid remnants are a powerful silent testimony. The Museum is wonderfully done and filled with many amazing artifacts!

Beautiful location on the Santa Fe River! Great family swimming area and perfect on a hot summer day. Sadly, sometimes the river can run high which blows out the spring with darker water. Have a back up spring handy in case this location is a no-go.

San Felasco is a fantastic place to hike or ride mountain bikes! The rolling terrain contains several distinctive micro-environments and many beautiful trees! The mountain bike trails are lengthy and at times somewhat challenging. Love this place!

Amazing place to visit and find beautiful rose quartz. We even saw one person find an AMAZING piece of aquamarine! We enjoyed filming my friend Robert Krampf - The Happy Scientist - for his science education series on geology.

Riverside park is a great place for drum circles! There's plenty of parking and it's far enough away from the neighborhood so as not to cause a noise disturbance. There have been lots of drum circles here over the years.

Located behind the Jacksonville National Cemetery, this lovely boat landing has a small dock and pic-nic pavilion perfect for group get activities. The canoeing on Thomas creek is beautiful and very relaxing!

We visited Manatee Springs via boat from the Suwanee River and were delighted to see several manatees as we got close and docked! The park and spring were lovely and the swimming very refreshing on a hot day!
The canoeing here offered a divers array of fresh water habitats and terrestrial environments to enjoy in a relatively small area! We even saw manatees!
Very remote and beautiful place! Real quiet here and no light pollution at night. Great canoeing, hiking and bicycling opportunities.
Great beach but we were VERY disappointed that the ferry was still out of service due to budget problems in Washington D.C.

Rode my bicycle across Route 41 thru Big Cypress, then took Loop Road... If your vehicle can handle the rutted gravel Loop Road it's the way to go... I saw lots of gators sunning on the banks... This (November 2020) is the wet season making it challenging for riding or hiking the trails... Birds, also, not plentiful, too wet or just not migrating yet due to the warm weather... Post-bloom flowers were plentiful on the bromeliads (airplants), time to see these is Spring and into Summer... Overall, besides trying to avoid all the potholes on Loop Road thru Big Cypress is the way to go, it's a beautiful ride...

Great spot for an Airboat ride, cool gift shop and place to learn about alligators and the Everglades... Check out the restaurant while you are there, some interesting things on the menu... Gift shop has lots of great stuff, clothing, jewelry, alligator belts... And, plenty of airboats, so you won't wait long to start your ride... Restrooms available... Gave only 4 Stars as NO wifi (2020 & no wifi? Don't they want us to share & stay connected with our families?)

Beautiful preserve... Couple picnic tables at the entrance to the mini-ring so pack a snack... Mini-ring is great for a quick walk, bike ride, handicapped accessible... Was looking forward to hitting the main trails but it's the rainy season and they are underwater, at least the mile and a half to get back to them is... Have to venture back when it's dryer... Primarily these trails are for hikers & horseback.. Bicyclers this is not the place for you...

Interesting little park, about mile, mile and a half, of trails... Lots of signs identifying the trees, stay away from the Poisonwood... Crying shame they are not giving out brochure, nor have online, the self-guided tour, lots of markers, but you can not learn what they are for, can not learn about the machines, just what is in the trail map brochure... Could be a pretty cool park... Very clean, restrooms available, no wifi...

Cool half mile boardwalk thru this part of the Rookery Bay National Preserve... Lots of informative signs to help you learn all about the flora and the fauna of this area...  Boardwalk is old and well travelled... Bring your binoculars as there is a chance to see many types of birds and other wildlife... Two observation decks, one overlooking the bay and one on the ground for those of you patient enough to watch for wildlife...

Great little beach, bring the family... Nice playground for the kids, public restrooms available... Nice and clean...  No seashells this morning... Bring coffee, closest shop is blocks away... Come early, parking lot is small, but free... Or take the Conch Tram or Bus, stops right out front... Dog park across the street... Some other cool stuff right around the beach... No wifi...

Cool little trail in the heart of Pine Island just past Phillips Park & the Fire Station... Take a walk on the paved section or venture off onto the unpaved Dr Mauney Trail... Careful after a rain as the trails will be underwater... Also, bring some bug spray so you can enjoy your walk and not swatting at the bugs... Did not see a lot of wildlife today, still an enjoyable walk...

Beautiful little walking park, great for that morning wake up exercise or evening wind down stroll... Very clean and well maintained... Mini-billboards sharing with us about the park... Generally hard-packed trail good for walking and jogging...Only a dozen parking spaces, so don't know if it ever gets crowded, only two cars when I visited... Overall, nice place to unwind!

Gift Shop is open This, Fri, Sat & Sun from 9 am to 5 pm... Tours are still not open... Gift shop has some beautiful craftsmanship, jewelry to blankets and more... Snacks and drinks, also, available. Public restrooms and wifi available... Even with the tours closed this is a must stop on your travels across 41, check out all the cool jewelry, clothes, woodwork and more!

Great little park to bring the family for a little cookout, or just to walk the dog. There is about 25 feet of 'beach' to get wet. If you brought your kayak, just around the bend is a spot for you to launch. No trailer parking, about 5 or 6 parking spaces, one grill and 3 picnic tables. There is a port a potty on site. Relax and look out at the fishing boats going by...

Sign on the gate states Closed Monday & Tuesday, yet here on Google Maps you have stated you are OPEN... And, why the heck would a park that's as large as this one need to be closed, swing the gate open, swing the gate closed, really can't manage to accomplish that to stay open 7 days per week? We'll, least you can do is update your sites when you do make changes...

Small little aquarium for a $15 walk thru, doing some construction so there will be a bit more to see sometime... I like the storyboards, tell you about the animals and what's going on with our seas... Some pretty cool looking fish, sharks, turtles and more... Here are pix of just about everything you'll see there plus their Gift Shop...

Beautiful preserve, lots of trails... Rainy season make sure you are wearing your boots, biking trails are under water so plan on hiking...

Lots of butterflies & dragonflies, eagles and more!

Pollution (cans, bottles, plastic...) is all over the preserve, please pick up some when you are visiting!

7:10 am on a Sunday morning... And the place is both open & closed according to the signs... but the gate is closed??? My first full day in Naples (Collier County) and no first sunrise from the beach, how disappointing! Government is here to serve us, they're constituents, right? Alas, not today!

Great little bird sanctuary, do wonderful work here... The sanctuary is for injured birds that are unable to be released back into the wild... If you are here in the Keys this is a must stop for the family... Fun for kids to see the birds and learn about them and the care given them...

Cool bit of Key West history, take a walk or tour thru this fort that was built in 1845... Check out the big guns, the little holes that they would fire thru, where the soldiers slept & dined, and lots more. Great bit of history, bring the family then spend the day down on the beach...

At the entrance to the pier is the Key West AIDS Memorial... Then to the pier, or for me, a picture of sunrise and the pier... Few folks up and out on the pier this morning, looks like a great view of the sunrise over the ocean... Come over to Higgs Beach and check it out...

Great little park right next to the Naples Zoo... Playground for the littles, restroom facilities, and a couple nice trails for walking, jogging and biking... Plenty of parking and a very clean, well maintained park... Trails are hard packed so easy for walking and riding!

Nice little park, no playground but there are picnic tables and a spot to swim... Restrooms (spot-a-pots) available. Went for sunset as did a whole bunch of folks, lots of folks there with their dogs too... So, need to walk or run your dog, this is a good spot...

Great Events going on all year round, walking/jogging track, picnic area, ballfields, Community Center and lots more...    Located at 125th St & Jamaica just off Coastal Hwy, great restaurants nearby like The Crabby Pig, Abbey Burger, Higgins Crab...

Calling all art lovers, this is a must stop to check out the local art scene in Ocean City MD.  Lots of great classes for all ages, and put the 1st Friday Reception (1st Friday of every month) on your calendar!

Great time at the Summer season of Sunset Park Party Nights free concerts, Thursdays at 6:30 pm.  And, if you love a sunset, beautiful location, bring your camera.  Don't be surprised if a few dolphins swim by!
Beautiful preserve, great hiking trails, gazebos for a test or eat a packed lunch, markers to know your way and informational signage that helps you learn more about the preserve and the wildlife.
Busy day at the zoo... Did not have the time to take a tour, but from the look of the parking lot a lot of other folks sure did... I look forward to a tour next time I'm in town...
All the amenities, run by a great group (Centerplate), plenty of meeting rooms and convention halls, excellent for small concerts and lots more.

I enjoyed this place.  It was definitely cooler than local town temps but I was ready for that.  The day was 50% cloudy and 50% sunny.  The hike to the top is 6/10 mile and uphill all the way. During our visit the visitors center and gift shop were closed due to Corid-19 which means the shuttle buses were not running.  As I reached the top the clouds rolled in so I didn't get any good scenic photos but it was still beautiful.  They did have 1 vaulted toilet available.  The trail is paved the whole way.  The tower is closed but you can get to the observation deck.

This is a park of the US park service so I was able to us my life time pass so this place didn't cost us anything.  They have nice air conditioned restrooms and cool Information center.  The have guided tours at 11:00 or you can self tour.  Everything was very well keep up.  Many cannons to see and they fire them on Saturday at 11, 1 and 3. They fire a cannon and a mortar.  Trails to walk in the area and a lot to see at the fort. There is a moat around the fort.  Enjoy
likes: Facilities & Services: Air-conditioned restrooms, Information center
Activities: Guided tours, Cannon firings, Self-tour options, Walking trails

reviews_attraction.text: In general the historic part of Greeneville was wonderful.  Andrew Johnson house where he grew up was next to the visitors center.  It was closed due to Corid-19 but we still walked to his homestead a few blocks away.  On the way back we passed another antebellum home.  The historic downtown had several old buildings and a church built in 1780. A few blocks away was an old mansion that was very impressive.  More to see here besides Andrew Johnson house and homestead.

WOW, this sub is amazing.  If you ever wondered what it would be like to live on a sub. visit the USS COD.  You drop down in the front of the sub and work your way to the back or aft section of the sub. You travel through several air lock passageways and see everything from the mess area to where they sleep to both forward and art torpedo areas and the engine room. On top you can aim one of the guns.  Ladies,  my wife was very impressed.  This is a must visit.

Had a very nice guide who was very knowledgeable about the original family and the Amish ways.  We got a wagon ride and stopped by the old school house. Our guide told us about the old school and the Amish school of today.  Then we got a buggy ride, I really enjoyed it.  After the tour we stopped into the general store and purchased a few items.  The large round barn was amazing.  Great place to visit.

Was a really cool part to drive thru.  Several parking lots and a lighthouse you can climb. The lighthouse did cost $to climb.  Hiking trail and beaches that weren't crowded. They had a feeding frenzy for gators,  turtles and snakes at 3:00 pm. Picnic tables are available at several places. Public rest room available.

Parking was $5. We took a ride on the water taxi for $10 each.  The pass was good for the day.  Nice picnic area next to the fountain with plenty of shade.  Easy access to the river walk way and next door is the museum of science and history as well as River City Brewing Co and marina.  Great beer and food.

Lots of shops and restaurants.  Limited parking.  The lighthouse is small and not a true original lighthouse.  Has a nice fishing pier with a shelter and picnic tables.  Fishing trips,  dolphin site seeing trips and sailing trips available. Nice boats in the harbor and plenty of rocking chairs to sit in.

Wow.  Explodes with history,  beautiful mansions and monuments in the squares.  Also has a movie history and musical artists history. Streets that are canopied by moss draped trees.  Spent a whole day and going back tomorrow for more. We did the jump on and off trolley and would recommend it.

Very impressive.  It is hard to believe what happened here but they do a great job of portraying what the pow camp was like. The cemetery takes your breath away.  The park is maintained very well and there was no charge for any thing.  The pow museum is great also.  This is a must visit site.

Crystal clear cool water. 2 large platforms in the swim area and 2 level diving platform.  Life guards on duty.  Boat cruises every hour for $8 per person. Lodge has a restaurant and gift and snack shop.  Changing rooms and bathrooms. Plenty of parking but we were there on a Tuesday.

Beautiful park and close to everything.  Since COVID-19 the pool,  playground and exercise room was closed as well as the cavern.  Our site is looking right at Lookout Mountain.  They have laundry and bathroom shower areas.  Sites are gravel and staff is very friendly and helpful.

We loved this place.  Kids may not appreciate the experience.  Upper and lower trails.  Many different plants and flowers.  The price was $12 per person. Was not crowded when we were there.  Places to take a picnic lunch.  Would be a cool setting for a wedding or other event.

Amazing what happened here during the civil war.  Great sign plaques to explain everything.  There is also a memorial here from each state that soldiers were represented from. Beautiful site right on Altoona Lake. Other civil war sites in the area.

Very nice park.  Plenty of beach area so it wasn't crowded.  Boat ramp and plenty of parking.  Showers and changing rooms. Shelters with picnic tables. $8 Entry fee per vehicle,  more if bringing in a boat.

Love the history of these old places.  Amazing how they were built.  We couldn't go inside due to Corid-19 but looked in the windows and toured the grounds.  Neat old wagon and plaques telling the story.

Pristine beach.  Clean white sand and turquoise water. Not crowded and plenty of parking. Large shelters.  Showers and changing rooms and camp store. Boat launch and shuttle to shell island. Beautiful.
The park was under repair from the hurricane last fall but the caverns were great to visit.  There is a gift shop and a small museum to walk thru.  No change for that but $10.75 for the cave tour.
Nice sand and water is ok.  Facility had changing rooms and out door showers life guards on duty. Chairs and umbrellas to rent.  Beach was very crowded.  Places to shop and eat near by.
Absolutely amazing.  I have not seen a church like this since touring several in Europe.  I can't say enough to how impressed I was at the beauty both inside and outside.  Wonderful
Amazing.  Was more to see and learn about than expected. Gift shop had an incredible selection.  Grounds were kept up and plenty of information for a self guided tour
Small park and plenty of parking.  Not open till 11 am so we didn't get to go in or climb the lighthouse . Top of lighthouse picture is cut off when posted,  sorry
Cool board walk with lots of shops and restaurants.  Live music on the beach on Tuesday nights. Free parking at visitors center at the heart of everything.
Large parking lot and well maintained grounds.  Gift shop is very nice and lighthouse was open to climb. Other buildings are interesting and neat setting.
Truly amazing to see a tree of such size that was around when our constitution was signed.  The main trunk is unbelievably large.

This place was so wonderful,  the volunteers were so friendly and eager to answer all my son and I's questions about individual monkeys. They also brought clementine (their ball python out for guest and my son to hold. Tito was my absolute favorite,  he had a personality out of this world along with a few others.  We cant wait to go back for sure. Thanks to all those that help these animals! And a little note to those complaining about the "cages" and "grounds" you are more than welcome to donate money or simply your time to help . They aren't a zoo making 1000s of dollars a day they are a humble place that truly care for these animals.  After talking to workers I found that several of the monkeys were diabetic and from a horrible testing facility so I'm sure they are 100% happier ( I was sad at first we couldnt feed this pair and then realized it was due to keeping them healthy because some of the treats would not be good for a diabetic)  so before you make assumptions talk to someone and maybe then you can see how much better life must be for these babies.

This place was one of the most amazing trails I have ever seen in Florida! I use the app all trails and was just looking for a quick spot to get out at close by, it was listed as "hard" but only 3.7 miles . I am used to doing between 6-9 miles so o figured it couldnt be that bad for the distance....be prepared! The inclines and declines are dramatic even though it is kept up there are still roots and whatnot you can trip on and you definitely do not want to go tumbling down the banks. The loop itself is technically closed , my son and I decided to give it a shot anyway but I do NOT suggest it with all of the fallen trees we would have never made it back without my trails map and we went all the way down to the river and with the erosion from the storm it was extremely difficult to get back up. But all in all I hope that area is open soon because it is completely remarkable and seems like your not even in Florida anymore.  I will DEFINITELY be going back!

My mother, son and I stopped in to check out the place yesterday,  it was pouring rain and cold but still had an amazing time. Rick was our tour guide and extremely imformative. The caverns were absolutely amazing; I live in a county with caves so I wasnt sure how different it was gonna be to ours but these had such amazing formations and weren't just a muddy hole in the ground that you crawl through. We cant wait to go back and we are hoping soon they will have the rest of the park up and running from all of the hurricane damage. If you get the chance it is Well worth the stop and is also inexpensive, educational fun for all ages!

I have been going here since I was a young kid I now bring my son and still enjoy it. The fishbowl boat is amazing for underwater viewing, even if the manatees arent right near it the amount of native fish is awesome to see! The size of some of the snook and redfish are incredible!  I also love all the boardwalks and the fact they left so much natural vegetation in the park. Sometimes the bugs can be a little rough so you may want to wear or carry bug spray  but other then that if you want to see manatees and the local animals this place is a must!

This place was way better then I could have imagined!  The staff was so nice even willing to take a picture of all of us in front of the lighthouse. Everything was well kept and clean along with the prices were well beyond reasonable ( entry and merchandise)
Everything was listed on the map given for the self guided tour and was very informative along with a few interactive spots to help kids and adults understand how the light works. This is definitely a must see and the views you get to see from the top of the lighthouse are stunning!

The parking is hard to find for those that aren't locals if their arent any other vehicles already there, but my suggestion is drive by on the weekend to find it and go back during the week. These trails take you straight back to the caves but their is so much more to see in this forest. Lizzie heart sink is one of my favorite places to hike to off the beaten path the trees are beyond huge and it is beautiful!

I love the caves for a family outing, I would not recommend for children under 5 just because it's dark and moist and a small child wouldn't pay enough attention and could easily slip or hit their head. My son is 11 and wears his own headlamp and carrys his flashlight and goes to town! Today I just went out to take my pup for a hike the trails are beautiful and well maintained while keeping it natural.

I usually love this place, there is always animals out and about ( today I saw a rabbit,  several different species of turtles, many species of birds and water fowl and heard a gator) but what upset me was the amount of trash in the water . I mean for goodness sake it is right behind the sheriff's office and a well known park in town . You would think they would keep it clean for all to enjoy.

Brought the kiddos down here to play after walking the town and going down to the pier to get a bite to eat.  The bathrooms are always kept clean and stocked (the best they can it is a "beach" bathroom) I was able to bring my dog as well which made it even better because he loves swimming with the kids and made a million new friends. Their are dog friendly restaurants in the area as well.

I have to say the renovations they did are absolutely amazing.  The park is clean, their are plenty of restrooms throughout and also a wonderful playground,  volleyball court and shuffleboard court. I am very impressed.  Also their are many benches and areas to sit and eat along with a 9/11 memorial that is beautiful.

Though when I pulled up I expected something more than what it was it was very well maintained you can go up the 2 towers and look around but beyond that there's no educational plaques to explain what you are looking at and where you are. But it is a very nice area to stretch your legs and let kids run in the field.

This was my son and I's first time in tarpon springs,  honestly I was completely surprised at the array of shops and restaurants. We had an absolutely amazing time and got to pick our own sponges along with a great lunch at limani's and of course hellas bakery for some much needed baklava 😍, cant wait to go back!

It's a beautiful area , as long as you can get there before it gets to crowded it is amazing.  Unfortunately alot of the younger crowd are disrespectful whilst there are children around. I'm always down for having fun but the smoking weed and getting out of control drunk and belligerent are not necessary.

It seems to be a beautiful place but unfortunately we couldnt get past a mile due to the mass amount of yellow flies and horse flies even after drenching ourselves in bug spray,  may attempt again in winter.
Short wall to a nice observation tower, dog friendly and plenty to see.  Only suggestion is like everywhere in Florida this time of year the yellow flies are horrible, I suggest bug spray
I absolutely love being here,  I hike off trail 22 down to lizzie sink around 4 times a week , always new things to see, it is definitely a place I will never take for granted.
Ok so I looked at these reviews and laughed honestly at everyone complaining about the stairs but.....THEM STAIRS are brutal but soooo worth every step all 177 to be exact!
We had to take this as a detour....I wasnt complaining.  It is well maintained and absolutely beautiful.  I cant wait to head up here to play around and explore!
Loved it walked the shore with mom and son looking at all the hermit crab shells. Lighthouse under construction but was still a beautiful site
Can I say wow! This place is soooooo  beautiful!  My mother and son loved it as well paved walkways made it easier on my mom as well
Absolutely not a doubt one of the most beautiful places I visited,  them stairs though all 177 to be exact are brutal !
Very beautiful place where you can walk, jog or bike for excersise.  I live taking my dogs here as it is pet friendly.
Love to hike here with my son only thing I highly suggest is bug spray and shoes you dont mind getting wet and muddy!
Gorgeous park , well kept . was just passing through the memorial was beautiful and all the flags were a nice touch
Very pretty but bring big spray , went on a day after a few good storms so was muddy but to be expected.

This trail is one of my favorite places to hike as it is close to home and it is set down along Burnt Bridge Creek so it is always cool and beautiful. I am always surprised at how quiet it is even though it is right in the middle of Vancouver. During the fall the colors are amazing as well. You can choose to walk this trail in segments as there are parking areas dotted along the trail all through Vancouver.

I love the amazing ruins in this area. Gran Quivira is just far enough away from Albuquerque to not have the crowds of people that some other parks usually have. We spent an hour talking with the ranger and were the only other people there. So interesting to hear the history of this area. There is a good walking path up the hill to the ruins and its very well kept. Great place!

This place is a lot of fun. Its like walking in snow that isnt freezing. It can get pretty hot here in the summer so bring lots of water and sunscreen. I have been here several times in yhe fall and winter and it can be very cold too. So many places to explore and lots of photograpyh opertunities. Expecially when you get out away from the roads where the people havent been.

Since they totally rebuilt this park a few years ago it is a great place to take the kids. Before the rebuild it looked like a homeless shelter tent city but they have really cleaned it up. That being said, there is still a lot of homeless people hanging about the area and i have found used needles in the grass before so just keep your eyes out for your kids safety.

This is such a wonderful park. I love to come here all year around but Fall is always my favorite time because the trees here are all so colorful. The walking trails are all paved and easy to get around on and the entire park is kept clean and beautiful. Good place for a large or small bbq picnic or a cool dio in the lake in the summer as well.

Cinnabar was a booming industry in the early to mid 1900's in this area and this is just one of several really fun ghost town areas to visit. There are lots of old buildings and mining equipment just laying about ready to be photographed. The best thing about this area is that it is not on private land and it is literally right off the road.

This is a great place to park to hike the entire area. You will need a parking pass to park here but it is pretty centrally located on the Discovery Trail so it give you easy access to the beach, bird watching, or just hiking the hills on well maintained trails. The early summer months can bring a LOT of mosquitoes so bring your bug spray!

This is a great area. I have never seen any other place like this on the Rouge River. Great place to explore with the kids! We found all sorts of interesting rock formations and cool things that had been formed by the river. There seems to be better small beaches on the west side of the bridge than the east but it was still great!

What a fun and fantastic collection. It has been a long time since i have seen an air museum that has such a large and well kept collection of aircraft as this. The last time i saw the Spruce Goose was when it was in Southern California so it was neat to see it back on display. Good place to bring kids and adults alike!

This is a fun little park along the river. There is a large okay structure and plenty of places to have a picnic or play hames in the open fields. This would also be a great place to bring the kids on a hot summer day as it has lots of trees and it is right along the river. Very clean and well kept park.

This is a very fun place to get the kayaks into the water. There is a concrete boat launch right off the road and free parking right across the street. The bathrooms were closed on a Monday so don't count on the facilities and there is no drinking water but still a nice place.

Located just outside Albuquerque this is such an amazing place. Thousands of years of history that is now being surrounded by modern houses but a very fascinating place none the less. You could easily spend all day here and not come close to finding all the hidden petroglyphs.

This entire area is nothing short of amazing. It is a very distinct and stunningly beautiful area and a real treasure in New Mexico. The heard of elk that you can find here sometimes are amazing. Fall is the best time to be here by far as it is just amazing with color.

What a wonderful place! I always find so many things out here to take pictures of. The wildlife is always abundant but even more so in the winter when the sandhill cranes are in the area. It is always peaceful here and i simply like to be here at any time of the year.

This is a great place for a little walk around a small lake in the middle of an industrial area. That may sound like no fun at all but once you get on the trail you don't even see the businesses that surround it. The new parking area is very nice as well.

I love the history behind all this and i was not disappointed here! So much to see and as a photographer there is so much to shoot. The water is warm and the entire area is SO interesting! $5 to park is a cheap way to spend a day if you are asking me.

This is a fun place to swim or to get the kayaks into the river but it us pretty loud with the freeway right over head. Once you paddle 1/4 mile away it quiets down though. The trails seem pretty nice as well for walking along the river.

This is a fun place to go walk along the river and just take in the sights and sounds. The parking area is nicely taken care of and there is a great bike path along the river as well. Good place to explore with the kids.

Wonderful beach! Beautiful sand and easy to get to. There is plenty of parking with good bathrooms and changing rooms. The $5 charge for parking is reasonable and they have done a great job of keeping everything clean.

The reconstruction work continues so the lighthouse is closed off but it is still a beautiful location and an easy place to get to. You will need a Discovery pass to park but that is the case anywhere now days.
I love this place. We come out here every 3 years and it is always interesting to me. Great exibits and a good place to walk around by the water.
This place is just beautiful! Great place for kayaking or walking around looking at birds. One of my favorite places to be on the water.
I have wanted to come see these guns for years and they were just as amazing as i thought they would be.
This is mostly just a boat launch and not really a park. Nice place to put a boat in the water though.
Nice place to cool off on a hot summer day or just to get away from the city for a while.

A fantastic place to launch!
We came to paddle in the Bioluminescence of the Indian River.
We put our canoe in and paddled all around the little canals. We were not disappointed!
Every touch of the water lit up like tiny blue fairies were skimming the surface. If you want to experience this amazing natural phenomenon first hand, there are plenty of tours available to book online.  The groups we saw were loud and brightly lit. We prefer quiet darkness.
If you have your own boat, you can do this for FREE, like we did. I stood on the dock and actually played with the bioluminescence with my paddle.
This was my first bioluminescence experience. I wonder why I waited so long?
Did you know...this light is created by dinoflagellates, a kind of plankton, which are tiny marine organisms.
dislikes: Loud and brightly lit tour groups

reviews_attraction.text:
We have launched here a couple of times for Permitted National Seashore island camping with great success.
This is a very nice park. There's plenty of parking and everything is free!
There are bathrooms, a cool playground area, beautiful views, picnic tables, grills, etc... Plenty of room for launching trailered boats.
However, that being said, I withhold my last star for cramped paddle launch area. If a boat tries to back in while you are loading or unloading, it is not cool. Women's bathroom was okay, but only 1 of the sinks worked. Please, be forewarned, even with repellent...I left this park with so many bites and stings from no-see-ums and mosquitoes I can't possibly give it a 5-star rating😥
dislikes: Limited working sinks in women's bathroom

reviews_attraction.text:
Here is a nice neighborhood park in Oakland. There are two playground sets, a swing set, a small 2 hoop Basketball court ( and the hoops are lower than standard for younger children to enjoy. )There is a tennis court as well. The park is large and open with magnificent live oaks dripping with spanish moss as well as palms, magnolias, and azaleas in bloom right now.
There are plenty of picnic tables and grills around as well as benches placed throughout the park. I stood inside the lovely gazebo and took a 360° video.
There are however, no toilet facilities.
I could not locate posted hours. Limited parking spots available.

It was raining when we came here to geo-cache, but I shall return soon!
Did you know...
The Pasture Reserve is located in the ❤ of the Florida aquifer, in the middle of the Green Swamp, which is an area of critical concern for the state!
It was such a pleasant drive to get here, as it is still very rural. Please follow the speed limits and use caution, as there is so much wildlife used to running around out here you might miss the sight of it... yet, hit it with your car.
As with all Lake County parks of my experience, the bathrooms were well kept and the landscape was tidy with native vegetation throughout.

What a hidden gem this City of Orlando park is! It is free to enter and park. Right away you see the baseball field and it has clean well stocked bathrooms. Here at this park you will also find a cool geocache spot. There is a paved walking/biking trail that encircles the surprisingly beautiful and undeveloped Lake Fran. It was cold and blustery today, but we observed Sandhill Cranes, Anhinga, Egrets, and Vultures.
I for one, am so happy this little slice of wetlands exists.
What a great natural space in the center of urban development!

Absolutely fabulous real Florida! Gets super crowded and super noisy, so I only go here during off peak times anymore! I do like to launch my kayak from here and float away down stream on the quiet and peaceful run to the Wekiva River.
Did you know that Wekiva Springs Run, Rock Springs Run, Blackwater Creek and the Wekiva River are designated and protected  as one of the few "Wild and Scenic Rivers" in the whole state of Florida? I for one, am grateful to those who protected it for future generations to enjoy!

Words cannot describe the beauty here...
This place is so special to me!
Do yourself and your loved ones a favor and book your reservations asap for an experience you will never forget!
This was our first time putting up our new 'yurt' tent as well! Pictures included.
If you like the beach, nature trails, camping, wildlife, including wild ponies and deer, (although we never saw any deer) and birds, birds, birds, or rivers teeming with life, you will find something to enjoy here at Assateague State Park!

Deep in the heart of the Canaveral National Seashore. Here at the dock is where I know I will find manatees nearly every visit!
Did you know that between 1773 and 1777, Explorer and Naturalist, William Bartram paddled and portaged his way along this part of Florida's coastline? Right here at Eddy Creek you can retrace his now famous trail as far as you dare. Bathrooms on east side of road. Licensed fishing allowed. Abundant wildlife viewing. Boat launch motor/paddle access to Intercoastal Waterway.

We stayed here for one night. This is a local favorite for boat launching, fishing, picnicking, and camping.
It is quiet and totally off the beaten path. Lots of paved sidewalks to traverse.
Great for strollers or wheelchairs.
The picnic area is shady and large.
Great views of the creek and all the scenery is lovely.
When everywhere else we tried to camp was full due to holiday, I found this place had availability and it was good.

Our Orange County Regional History Museum in downtown Orlando is a treasure! There is so much going on here all the time. Retro game nights, Speaker Series, Field trips, and so many hands on educational, interactive displays to interest everyone.  I highly recommend bringing out your family and plan to spend a few hours here to explore all this wonderful museum has to offer.

We spent a couple of nice hours wandering through the gardens, and admiring the birds and plants. This is such a nice neighborhood park in the center of a very busy area, and yet once you enter, it very quickly beckons you further, until you are  immersed in the green space with the flowing water and it is easy to  forget the fast moving world just up the hill.

We are a geocaching family, and sometimes our geocaches take us to 'off-the-beaten-path interesting places we would never find otherwise!
This park is exactly one of those places!
As this is a neighborhood park, there is no official parking, so please use legal discretion for parking and plan to walk just a little.

Woodring is a great area! Hiking, biking, camping, picnicking, or just come to enjoy the views and the peace and quiet.  Another beautiful place to visit in Georgia.  The area is large and the views of Carter Lake are impressive at every turn.
Love mountain biking? You will definitely want to check this place out!

This is a wonderful place, however, if you start this drive which should take 1 hour, be prepared for clueless folks who block all traffic for as long as they want looking at one bird in places you cannot pass. This has made this drive take more than 2 hours for me at times, and can be frustrating.

Great little gem of a park!
Here is the launch of all 6 Edgewater Paddling Trails! I am super excited to return and check out these trails.
Restrooms unlocked until 8pm. Fun new playground in the works...
Pavillion, benches, boat ramp, and plenty of parking for a neighborhood river park.

Lovely garden and educational sugar mill ruins tucked away like a neighborhood park.
This would be a 5 star rating if the amount of plants on the current "Invasive plant list" for Florida were not being encouraged to thrive there.

This was my first visit here!
It will not be my last! The next time I come I will bring my bicycle and ride the 10.8 mile Loop around the Levee. Today we hiked to see the campsite and visited the viewing platform.
Well it’s closed due to COVID right now, but we did some exploring on foot around the exterior and it’s quite lovely and unique for its windows, obviously, but also the gardens and surrounding area.
We took our first hike to this part of the Florida trail on a Sunday afternoon in October. Wet and wonderful! We will be back to do some trail running!
My son and I wanted a place to swim and cool off while camping nearby and we found this spot to be perfect for picnic, swimming, and sunset viewing!
Excellent way to spend some time at the rivers edge contemplating, paddling, or picnicking. A world away from city madness just around the corner.

Sunset tonight brought to you from parking area #1 boardwalk.
04/23/21  What a Beautiful new boardwalk at carpark #2
Adding photos from tonight..
Great parking in the shade for West Orange Trail connection. If you like horses, there's are events here and there is camping on site as well.

Top notch State Park without a doubt. Hiking trails, camping, bird watching, disc golf, and more.
Everything you would want from a State Park.
Always a favorite for my family.  Today I shared it with guests from South Carolina and they too were impressed!

Excellent park! The camping areas are amazing. You have some privacy versus wide open camp grounds. The mountain bike trails are very unique for Florida, very impressive. And the park is extremely clean.

If you are looking for a short kayaking trip, you can check out the Thatcher Road Entrance (located approximately 1 mile south of main entrance). You can go up river about 1 mile before it gets very narrow. For going southbound, you can go about 1/10th of a mile before you run into falling trees blocking the river.

For walking trails, go to the Equestrian Trail and Fishing Entrance about 1.4 miles north of the main entrance. They have about 20 miles of trails you can share with fellow equestrians.

Visited this forest to complete a trail for the Florida State Forest Trailwalker Program. Trail is very well marked and path was great! Also it was during hunting season and there were signs posted making you aware - thank you for doing that! As a precaution for wildlife (bears in particular) I had carried bear spray and had a bear bell. The trail we walked was 10.6 miles long. Definitely recommend if you are looking for a longer trail.

Visited to complete the Buncombe Hill Interpretive Trail as part of the Florida State Forest Trailwalker Program. It helped to have the map printed out from the Florida State Forest website to locate the trail. The trail is very private, we didn't see anyone.

I recommend to call ahead to make sure the trail/park is open. They had closed down part of the forest when we were there due to dryness and potential for fire.
dislikes: Need to call ahead for availability

reviews_attraction.text:
Had the opportunity to hike the trails here. Completed all three loops for a total of approximately 9 miles.

Overall a great trail and enjoyed it. Bring a map and GPS it on your phone if you can so you can make sure you are in the trail. Between  mile marker 2 and 3, and also between 5 and 6 the trail makers are a little hard to see. Map and GPS helped. Definitely recommend if you are looking to hike for a few hours.

Great park for kayaking from beginners to more advanced. Able to kayak to various campsites (permit needed to stay overnight). Had a nice boardwalk trail (a little less than one mile). The 6.5 mile trail is closed, you can still use the service road to hike - it is about 2 miles. Highly recommend for kayaking or canoeing.

If you use a tent and don't go primitive, try to get campsite 1 - 19, they are more private.

Visited to hike two trails that is part of the Florida State Forest Trailwalker Program (Tram and Twin Mills). We were here most of the afternoon and didn't see anyone, very peaceful.

The trails don't seem to get walked much. Definitely GPS the trail on your phone as several trail makers on Tram Trail seemed to be missing. Nice place to relax.

The Withlacoochee State Forest has several trails to walk. Walked several trails that were part of the State Forest Trailwalker program.
