Even if you don't take part in their program, Crrom has some very well kept trails for hiking. Just make sure you have a map (you can get it from the State Forest website) as cell reception is not reliable.

Enjoyed the stay at the park. This park offers a lot of activities. Spoke to a few people fishing by the lake that were staying in the cabins. They stated they come here on a yearly basis to unplug. The park itself is quite large for a state park, it was suprising to see the camping sites so close to each other. Overall great park to visit.

Visited this State Forest to walk the Big Shoals Trail as part of the Florida Trailwalker Program.

Enjoyed the views from the trail albeit it was right before a big rain so the river wasn't in full force however it was very relaxing. I recommend this to anyone as it is a very short hike about 1.1 miles down to the main viewing area.

Had the opportunity to tent camp at this park for two nights. There is a tent only section that is very well maintained. The park overall was great. It is about a 2 mile paved drive from the entrance to the park to the campsite. Facilities were very clean, park has a decent amount of trails and a small lake for fishing.

As part of the Florida State Forest Trailwalker Program, completed the 1.4 mile trail. Trail is very well marked. There was a Ranger on site and he was a pleasure to talk to regarding the trail. I carried bear spray and a bear bell just in case. The Ranger stated it has been several months since the last bear siting.

The Ranger on site was amazing. He knew a lot about the park and surrounding area. The park is very well kept and the facilities are some of the cleanest I have ever seen at a state park or state forest.

The campsites are a little small so call ahead if you have concerns. Overall I highly recommend this park!

Visited the park with the goal of completing the loop that is just over 8 miles. The Florida Trail portion is very well marked. The White Trail towards to the connector trail to complete the loop wasn't marked as well. Definitely bring a GPS and compass as a backup if this is your first time on this trail.

Excellent area for hiking a wide variety of trails. If you are interested, check out the State Forest website for the Trailwalker program as you can earn badges for walking State Forest Trails. They also offer a similar program for equistrian trails and it is called the Trailtrotter program.

Visited the park to complete the trail which is part of the Florida State Forest Trailwalker Program. Trail is about 1 miles long. Trail is well marked and I had a map printed out from the Florida State Forest website - it was very easy to follow as the trail has several check points.

Walked the River Walk Trail to our campsite in Silver Lake Campgrounds. It is a on way trail so we parked one vehicle at the entrance and left one vehicle at our campsite. Great walk and one of the best trails I have walked so far of the State Forest Trailwalker Program.

Walked the North Loop today. Well marked trail, just bring a map because marker 8 thru 10 can can confusing. Was a little wet however no more than a foot deep in the deepest spot. South Loop was too far underwater for us to try.

Walked two trails that they have to offer as part of the Florida Trailwalker Program. Excellent park for trails and had a great time. If you enjoy hiking, check out the Trailwalker Program the Florida State Forest offers.

Had the opportunity to tent camp in this State Park while he hiked State Forests in this part of the state. The facilities are clean, tent camping spots are spacious and the park has a lot of history. I enjoyed our stay!
This park has a lot to offer! Kayaking, trails, plenty of places to setup a picnic along with a large number of camping and primative camping spots. I highly recommend visiting this park!
Very nice park! Not many people there and very well kept trail. The trail is part of the State Forest Trailwalker program and is 2 miles long. Well marked and a nice walk.
I really enjoyed this park. Around the springs there is a short hiking trail and plenty of spaces to sit and relax to enjoy the views of the crystal clear water.
If you visit, recommend walking Cypress Swamp Trail. Overall very well kept park and museum onsite provides some great history of the park.
Visited to hike the Anderson Springs Trail as part of the Florida Trailwalker Program. Very well kept and enjoyed the hike!
Very relaxing and easy nature walk. Most of the trail is on the boardwalk. Saw some wildlife, overall very nice walk.

It took an HOUR from the time we were seated until our dinner was served. Was it worth the wait? No. It was standard Mexican fare, not particularly well seasoned. There are good choices for beverages including the Stingray margarita which I enjoyed although drinks are pricey.  Complaints to management did bring dinner eventually and to their credit, they did comp the meal. But I would rather pay for my meal rather than having to rush through it. What we anticipated as a nice leisurely pre concert dinner was unpleasant and rushed after we were finally served. This place needs to do better.

Nice overview of the City of St. Augustine. This operates as a traditional narrated tour as well as a "hop on hop off" transport. However, the tours were so overcrowded that there was no hopping on the trolleys. People were clearly irritated that multiple trolleys had to pass them by because they were full. We wanted to disembark at several locations but didn't dare lest we were stranded. We took the full loop tour and were never able to get back on again. I realize that were there at a busy time but the idea of them selling unlimited tickets didn't work so well for us.

The museum is in a former hotel and the building itself is quite stunning. The courtyards are beautiful and it is easy to imagine the luxury life enjoyed by the guests there in days gone by. There is a cafe inside the museum located in what was once a large indoor swimming pool. There are photos throughout showing the museum as the hotel it once was. The experience was enhanced by live piano music. The exhibits are modest but interesting.  Paintings, crystal, antique furniture and self playing musical instruments.  A small but interesting natural history exhibit.

The France pavillion is very nice. They have done everything possible architecturally to enhance the experience, including a faux Eiffel Tower.  Street performers here are superb. There are artists as well. Well the food is great and so many choices. From formal sit down with classic cuisine, to cafe style dining, perfect for people watching to French pastries and coffee!
The stores offer perfume and other French exports. The film is a bit dated. I am looking forward to the Ratatouille addition here.

Easy to overlook pavilion sandwiched between France and Canada. There are some nice shops here and delightful indoor and outdoor dining. The Pub usually draws a good crowd for those seeking a pint or two.  Fish and chips are readily available.  The gardens are always beautiful here no matter the time of year.  In the gazebo to the rear of the pavilion,  various tribute bands play throughout the afternoon.  Enjoy the quick trip back through the 60's, 70's and beyond.

This ride inside the Mexican pavilion offers respite from the sun, rain or crowds. You are immediately transported to nighttime in Mexico. The boat ride, which rarely has a significant wait, provides a look at Mexico and it's fiestas with the 3 caballeros as hosts. I do miss the previous ride that was revamped to its current format to be more appealing to children.  But relax and enjoy the very ramen adventure.

What a gem!  Happened by this place and it's a great experiential learning center. There is a modest admission charge. $5 for adults, less for seniors and children.  Nice stingray touch tank, several aquariums including octopus and seahorse tanks. Turtles turtles turtles!  This is a great turtle hospital and they do remarkable work saving the sick and injured. Knowledgeable staff. Great educational features.

This is a great pavillion.  Soarin is an A+ attraction.  Great immersive simulator takes you on a flight around the world. Living with the Land is a great ride displaying technology and innovation in farming. Behind the Seeds is a backstage tour which is well worth the time and money. There is also a great food court as well as a family style character restaurant.

This aquarium is top rate.  Lots of fascinating exhibits. Lots of sharks. Amazing exhibit of jellies. Really interesting look at amphibians. The 4 d movies are  highly recommended.  Plan on spending 3 to 4 hours there to see everything. Great gift shop. Don't miss the touching areas for the sting rays and jellies.

This is the iconic entryway to the Maguc Kingdom. It's the most amazing place to people watch!  Grab a snack and a spot on a bench. There are numerous places to eat, whether you want a snack, a cup of coffee or some candy or ice cream.  Also table service restaurants.  Best shops slkng Main Street as well.

Like this nice hike that is away from the crowds and noise of the park. It's got some shade which is usually very welcome.  Great to be able to wander through this area at your own pace viewing the birds and animals. Like most animal areas of AK, earlier in the day is best, especially for the tigers!

Amazing museum that has something for everyone.  There are so many beautiful galleries here ranging from antiquities to contemporary art. Not to be missed is the gallery of miniatures on the basement level. There is a sculpture garden as well that is open seasonally. Don't miss a visit here.

This retro ride is as much fun now as it was 40 years ago. It's a great voyage through the jungle featuring all audio animatronic animals. The best part is the narration of the cast member "boat captain" which really amounts to a stand-up routine.  Relax and enjoy!

This show is an absolute "must see." Good production quality. Singers, dancers, acrobats, stilt walkers, aerial artists and more. Stunning costumes and choreography. Many of the familiar Lion King tunes. Indoor venue can be a break from the weather.

Great original land in Magic Kingdom. Home to great attractions including Thunder Mountain and Splash Mountain. To get out of the heat, rain or cold, stop in the country bear jamboree.  Food options are good here including the iconic turkey leg!

Can't resist visiting this classic attraction. Of course it's a bit dated, but that's part of the fun. It's a great way to get off your feet for a few minutes and into the climate controlled theater. Little ones will love these singing bears.

Large museum so wear your comfy shoes.  Lots of interesting and informative exhibits in all areas of science and industry.  Plan on spending many hours here. A great place for children and adults.  The building itself is stunning.

A must see museum! Real gem in Winter Park . Amazing displays of Louis Comfort Tiffany's works. You can easily spend several hours here. Don't miss the introductory videos. And make time for a stop in the fabulous gift shop.

This is an affordable alternative to the big theme parks. Lots of fun things to do here for all ages.  Kiddie rides, arcade, go carts and roller coasters as well as thrill rides.  You won't spend hours in line either.

What's not to like about this iconic Disney landmark! It is especially beautiful with the many projections done at the nighttime fireworks show. The illumination is spectacular and should not be missed.
Food is good but pricey here. Same with the shops. Entertainment is superb and generally a good atmosphere.  It's definitely one of the smaller pavilions without any specific attractions.
Visually the pavillion is nice. There are several shops and restaurants including some food and gift kiosks.  There is no attraction here per se, just the food and retail outlets.
Nice gem off the beaten path in the Canaveral national seashore.  The history of the area is quite fascinating and there is so much pride that the rangers show about the area.
Nice pavilion which houses Frozen ride as well as the Askerhaus restaurant.  But hidden among the shops and restaurants is a small but interesting museum. Don't miss this@
Great place for a visit. Family friendly up close look at the Bluebonnet Swamp. Nicely maintained wooden walkways. Very affordable.

We just finished our first experience at dare to escape.  We found a great deal on groupon for a group of 5 to experience "the dig" room.  When we called the office the staff was extremely friendly in answering any and all questions.  Upon arrival we were greated quickly by a friendly gentleman who asked several questions such as had we ever done a room escape and if so which one was our favorite, he was very polite and even gave us some of his choices for his favorite room escapes in the Orlando area.  We signed our waivers and Melody was our amazing game master she was bubbly, friendly and very informative of how to play, how the different styles of locks worked and answered any questions we had.  We completed the dig escape room in 49 minutes and change.  Melody was an awesome game master and made the experience that much better, we will definitely be back to take on another escape room and spread the word of the amazing fun staff at dare to escape!

The LaChua trail of Paynes Prairie is absolutely breathtaking from start to finish.  The trails are very well cared for, plenty of parking is available, the is an iron ranger at the entrance to make your payment to enter the park.  We saw WELL over 100 gator  throughout the trail and lots of bird.  When we made it to the observation platform at the end of the trail we spoted horses and a wild hog off in the distance.  On a side note there are 2 bathrooms on site at the near beginning of the trail.  We will definitely be visiting the gem again and hopefully in the near future.

Beautiful state park, the ranger station is the first building you see upon entering andbits staffed with friendly rangers offer lots of helpful information.  Take your time and drive slow to the visitor's welcome center as we saw 6 deer on our way while driving, at the visitor's center they have firther information and a beautiful large observation tower.  Multiple bathrooms located through the park, tons of trails and lots of wildlife, paynes prairie is a great place to relax and have a fun filled day by yourself or with friends and family.

This is a great place if you want to go on a short hike or two by the gulf coast.  When went during low tide.  The trails are nice and they have a map on their website that shows you where and how long each trail is.  There is a large tall observation platform onsite that overlooks the bay.  We didn't see a ton of wildlife on our visit which was slightly disappointing but hey it just means we need to return for another visit.  There is also a building onsite that appears available for rental for parties or gatherings.

Nice sports recreational area.  The facility has 3 baseball fields and one softball field, the baseball area has a concession stand in the back and there is a small play ground next to it.  On the other side of the park is the soccer fields which also has its own concession stand under a pavilion.  There is a small bike/walking trail that is paved that leads to the main bike trail (Withlacoochee state trail) that runs along side 41.  There are bathrooms on site and they are connected to the concession pavilions.

This is a great park to visit, you can make the visit last as long as you want depending on if you want to spend time at every exhibit and just watch the animals.  When individuals come from out of town we always try to bring them to this park as its not very expensive and give the person a great idea of all of the beautiful wildlife in the state of Florida.  Staff have always been very friendly and is always there to answer questions.

Cooter pond park is a small park right off our 41 in Inverness, there is a boardwalk that goes over Cooter lake and a large water fountain near the middle, benches and a pavilion area also located on the boardwalk over the water, there is also plenty of informational board along the board walk.  The day I was at the park there was two families fishing from the boardwalk and I could see plenty of fish right over the railing.

Beautiful place to visit that is dull of amazing law enforcement history.  This place is clean, the staff is extremely friendly and they have many displays to look at that will educate you about law enforcement from past eras till now.  If you or anyone in your family has even the slightest interest in law enforcement or the history of law enforcement than this place is a must visit!

Wesley Jones is a decent park it has a full basketball court, a small baseball field equal to little league size, a pavilion with multiple picnic tables and a charcoal bbq grill, volleyball sand court (I never see the net up), play ground area, mens and womans bathrooms and a wide ooen grass area that you see a lot of teams practicing soccer during the season.

Another one of Vermont beautiful covered bridges, this one has further history beyond how old it is, this bridge is also know as a local urban legend (Emily's Bridge).  Parking available next to the bridge, you can walk down to the water from the parking lot and they even have a display explain the bridges history.

Beautiful little park on the west side of lake Henderson, the park is located near the downtown area of inverness.  Liberty park has pavilions, BBQ grills, benches and a small little dock in the water to pull your boat up to.  This park also has a beautiful 9/11 monument near the main entrance by the flag pole.

Best quality Teddy Bears you will find anywhere.  If you are in the area or looking for something to do with the family take the kids and go explore this place they have a tour and show you how they make the bears and have a shop that has tons of different bear and accessories to choose from your new bear.

Wallace Brooks park is another park close to Liberty park (they are connected by a boardwalk that goes over the water of lake Henderson (wildlife can  be seen along with marsh area of the lake) the park has a small jungle gym, swingset, fishing pier, bathroom and a shuffle board court.

Great place for a short hike lots of open area and a small single story observation town over looks acres of prairie land where you might get lucky and spot bison, horse, hawks and other wildlife.  Trails are nice but lots of roots so watch your step.

This is a neat little park with some history to it.   There are lots of informative signs on the history of the property and its a nice area to stop and have a picnic as they has tables, charcoal grills and a pavilion will several electrical outlets.

Nice little sandy beach, they have a swimming area and the have a few spots outside if the swimming area where you can fish, on the south side of the beach there is a bick rock thst usually holds small mouth bass, target them with plastics.

A place you must visit if you enjoy outdoor activities on the water, tubing down the river is something my family does multiple times a year and it never gets old.  We geo cached and hikes the area and just room in the impressive sights.

Ive you've never done a room escape they are extremely fun and test your trouble shooting and puzzle solving skills.   America escape games staff is very friendly and explains everything very well before you start your challenge.

Beautiful area to go for a hike and just see what Florida's nature has to offer, while parking in the parking lot i saw a trophy buck cross the road and walk into split oak, it's going to be a good day.
Another beautiful area to visit in this area, they have a nice fishing pier on bear pond.  The area is well maintained and there road a pretty decent with some pot holes and some wash board areas.
Beautiful walk along the coast of Lake Champlain with large rocks you will see people sitting on watching the water or even sun, grassy area that would be great for a picnic water side.
Great area for hiking, camping, fishing, hunting (when in season) or just driving around to see the sites.  The staff is very friendly and they maintain the roads and land very well.
Stopped by this park visitors center on Labor day and they were closed (no problems that's expect on a holiday)  we walked the area by the water and just wated boat in the channel.
Very nice displays throughout the entire exhibit, nice and clean, great layout and they even offer scavenger hunts for kids with different difficulty levels depending on ages.
Nice small little park that offers lots of local history, picnic area with grills, and a seas wall that offers a fishing spot in the channel.

I love to visit the Everglades but I don't often have the time to travel all the way down to Homestead. Fortunately for me the Loxahatchee Refuge is located a mere thirty minutes from where I live. It's located directly off of 441, about 20 minutes north of Glades Road directly behind Bedner farms which is a great place to grab a snack or drink before you go into the park.

Once you enter there a park service booth to the right. Admission is $5 but usually no one is present to collect the admission. A soon as you pass the booth turn to the right and there you will find the nature visitor center. There is some nice displays and a cute little movie where you sit in a fake air boat and the movie makes you feel like you are zipping through the Everglades. You will also find park rangers and volunteers here to answer any questions you have. The visitor center closes at 4 pm. Right behind the nature center are the bathrooms and the entrance to the Cypress trail which goes through the cypress swamp. The trail is a quick little ten minute walk on an elevated boardwalk. Very pretty. The trail winds around back to the start and when the nature center is open there are some rocking chairs on the back patio to enjoy.

Once you finish the nature center you hop back into the car and drive up to the next parking lot on the left. If it is July it is worth looking into the water on your left side. It's a popular place for alligators to nest and I have seen mom's and babies many times. You just want to give them a wide berth. Once you park you will see a trail to your left that makes a nice circle around the wet prairie habitat ending back at the parking lot. It's an easy twenty minute walk but there is no shade so I like it best in the winter. As you walk you will see many birds. Some that I see often are Anhingas, Great Blue Herons, and Great Egrets. I have also seen alligators and turtles swimming along. There is a small observation platform which gives a nice view of the wet prairie.

A short drive up the road leads to another parking lot on the left where there a covered pavilion that abuts the slough. If you peer over the railing there is usually an alligator or two lounging around. This area provides a beautiful view of the wet prairie. The last time I was there I saw a family feeding the alligators grapes. This was despite a large sign that says do not feed the alligators. The sign also showed a dead alligator that the park rangers had to kill because it had become a nuisance gator from people feeding it. Let's leave the wildlife wild folks.

At the very back of the refuge is the slough habitat. A lot of people bring their boats back here and it's a popular place to fish. There is place here that rents canoes and kayak and you can take the five mile canoe trail that runs through here. I did it once and took several hours. There was no shade which can be brutal. They lily pads also make it difficult to get through the water. The wildlife however was amazing and it made it worthwhile. I saw alligators swimming right next to my canoe as well as many kinds of birds. The canoe place also offers moonlight canoe trips which I have always wanted to take.

In February of every years the friends of Arthur R Marshall Refuge have an Everglades Day. A ton of people come so you have to park offsite and ride a bus. The event has free canoeing, guided nature walks, arts and crafts for the kids, vendors, and food trucks just to name a few things. Last year my friends bought some very nice binoculars which I am seriously thinking of purchasing this year. Although crowded it is a really fun day.

The Everglades is a very important part of the Florida ecosystem. Some changes are being proposed that may threaten the future of the refuge. I wrote this review because I hope more people will come visit and love it as much as I do. If you love it like me, then you will be invested in protecting it too.
dislikes: Difficulty in paddling due to lily pads

reviews_attraction.text:
When the Wizarding World opened in Islands of Adventure in 2010 this was the premier ride. Located in the Hogwarts Castle replica the queue winds around Hogwarts and is a real thrill to see if you are a fan. You begin in the dungeons and enter the castle where you place your belongings in a locker.The line then winds around the greenhouse where you can see the mandrakes. As you enter the castle hallways you can see the moving portraits on the walls. Rooms you pass include Dumbledor's office, the defense against the dark arts classroom, and the Gryfindor common room. Favorite characters appear in the rooms and speak to you. The last thing you see before getting on the ride is the Sorting Hat. If you are a true Harry Potter fan this queue is not to be missed. The first time I waited on the line I didn't even mind because I was taking so many pictures. After my first trip through I now prefer the single rider line. It cuts out most of the castle tour and can save up to an hour of waiting time in line. Anyone who cares about Harry Potter and has not seen it should make a point of doing the walk through.

Once you get to the ride you step onto a conveyor belt as you make your way to the bench seat. Your bench becomes enchanted by floo powder sprinkled by Hermione and you fly up into the air. One time the ride broke down in the early days and the lights came on and I was able to see the mechanics of the ride. It was disconcerting to see that I was strapped down in a swinging bench dangling off a large robo arm on wheels. Take my word for it, it is better if you don't see what is going on. Fortunately the kinks seem to have been worked out and my experience lately has been that the ride operates continuously.

The ride is a mixture of screens and built sets. The movement is pretty intense and at times you will be on your back almost tilting upside down. It's not a good ride for people prone to motion sickness. During the ride you fly through a Quidditch match with Harry and Ron until you get chased by one Hagrids dragons. The screen projection switches seamlessly into a set piece as you race through Hogwarts arches in order to escape the dragon. You face an animatronic dragon that breathes fire at you. You then descend into the Forbidden Forest where Aragog the spider spits at you. You pass the Whomping willow and are chased by dementors until you finally confront Voldmort himself. Harry saves you with his Patronus and you fly back into the castle to see all of the characters cheering you on.

The night I rode this I was at Universal for a private party held after closing hosted by Orlando Informer meetup. For a separate ticket price you get to go on the rides with little to no wait time as well as having food and drinks included. The queue was closed and you could only take the single rider line. We walked on the ride with no wait which greatly increased my enjoyment of it. There are not many rides in the Wizarding World but the few they do have are incredible. If you are a fan of Harry Potter you will enjoy all of the details on this ride and even if you aren't this is still a thrilling ride.

This museum is located in an historic feed store built in 1901 in downtown Stuart. It is the oldest commercial building in Martin County. The building was originally the George W. Parks General Merchandise Store. George W. Parks and his family lived upstairs and the store occupied the first floor. In 1924 George sold the store and in 1946 it was purchased by the Truman Fertilizer Company and named the Stuart Feed Store. The City of Stuart purchased the building in 1988 and formed the Stuart Heritage, Inc to preserve and protect historic buildings in the town and artifacts from the city of Stuart. The museum opened in 1992.

It's free to visit the museum and parking is free too. I stopped by on a recent trip to Stuart. I didn't have too long before closing and there was a lot to look at. The museum has over 10,000 from the 1880's through the 1950's. The city of Stuart took root when the Florida East Coast Railroad came through in 1894. You can find pictures of the railroad in the museum. The museum also has an exhibit dedicated to the Seminoles who were the native people in this area. They lived on the banks of Poppolton Creek and used to come in to the store on Saturdays to trade. Some of the displays are dedicated to the local legends like Trapper Nelson who died from a gun shot that may have been self inflicted or maybe not and the Ashley Gang who like Robin Hood would steal from the rich to give to the poor in the 1910's through the 20's. A final shoot out with police in 1924 killed John Ashley and every member of his gang.  Another part of the museum is set up like a general store with ceramic chickens that are a nod to the chickens that used to run around inside the building.

Items in the museum are in chronological order starting with the Seminoles, the pioneers, the 1920's through the 1950's. Some of the items are things you might have seen in your grandparents home like antique sewing machines and vintage refrigerators, A favorite display was a recreated ice cream parlor from the 1950's. The executive director of the museum is Mary Jones whose own family makes more than one appearance in the museum. Her family moved to Stuart in 1907 and her father was the town fire chief and her grandfather was the contractor for the Lyric Theater.

While the emphasis is on Stuart and Martin County the museum also tells the story of Florida. You could spend a short time here or hours looking through all of the fascinating items. The museum also has a small gift shop with handmade crafts from some of the pioneer families in the community and a selection of interesting history books relevant to the area. It is definitely going to take me another visit to finish going through all of the photographs and treasures. If you are a fan of history like I am you will want to pay this quaint museum a visit.
likes: Activities (Diverse exhibits, chronological displays, recreated scenes)

reviews_attraction.text:
At 625 acres Tradewinds Park has something for everyone. The site was originally a horse farm. The original farm house still stands on the property and you can tour it. The park is so large it spans both sides of Sample Road. The south side of the park contains the immensely popular Butterfly World and the north side has the horse stables, farm, and mini train ride run by Tradewinds & Atlantic Railroad, Inc.

On a Saturday afternoon I found myself on a photographic expedition to Butterfly World on the the south side of the park. Admission to Tradewinds Park is $1.50 on weekends and holidays. Butterfly World is a separate admission price and is the largest butterfly park in the world with 20,00 butterflies. Also on this side of the park are large athletic fields. People who would like to celebrate a special occasion will find ample picnic shelters with grills. Further in the back of the park is a nice bike trail and the Cypress Trail boardwalk that crosses over a waterway and takes you into the woods. It is under renovation and hopefully will become a loop. Right by Butterfly World I was delighted to see a bat house where shelter was being provided for these important pollinators.

The north side of the park hosts the Holiday Fantasy of Lights every November and December. It is a drive through light display held during the evenings. Check the park schedule because on a few select nights they also allow you to bike through it which is my preferred way of seeing it. On this side you can find the mini train ride run by the Tradewinds & Atlantic railroads. They offer rides on the weekend and their schedule can be found on their website. Opposite the train you will see a field full of beautiful horses. It was quite the treat watching them being let out of the barn into the fields. Horseback riding is offered to the public for $35 an hour. Equine Assisted Therapies offers therapeutic horse encounters for people with disabilities. Also in this side is the McClean Country House which is open for tours. It was the farmhouse the first owners of this land lived in. There is a playground and an educational public farm that offers tours every weekend. The general store offers concessions on the weekend. If all that wasn't enough you can fish here and play disc golf if you provide your own equipment.

We are really lucky to have so many great parks in Broward County. They are so varied. I love seeing all kinds of people out enjoying nature on the weekends. Tradewinds Park is another addition i a stellar lineup of wonderful places to enjoy outdoor recreation in Broward County.
likes: Cultural heritage (original farmhouse, McClean Country House)
Recreational facilities (picnic shelters, bike trail, disc golf)
Educational opportunities (Butterfly World, public farm tours)

My daughter grew up being taken to this park. I have so many memories and pictures of her playing here through the years. They have a multi tiered climbing structure, slides, swings, spray mister, and a bone pit to dig in. I was recently at the dentist up the street and having heard that the playground had recently gotten a 1.5 million dollar renovation I wanted to swing by and take a look. It is so wonderful. It is everything my daughter had but upgraded and better. The climbing structure has been improved from splinter giving wood and is now even a little wider so parents can fit in and chase after their kids better. The playground has been redesigned to improve access for children with disabilities. The water spray area has also been upgraded with new misters.

In addition to the playground there is also a merry go round for only $1 a ride. I remember when it was installed and it instantly became a favorite. When I was here there was also some food carts like a hot dog one in this area for anyone wanting to get a snack.

If you get too hot playing outside there is the Science Explorium in the air conditioned building. It houses different traveling exhibits. When my daughter was young you could freely wander in and explore. When I peeked inside this time there was someone manning the suggested donation booth of $5 outside the door. It seemed to add to the pressure to donate before going in but you do not have to give.

The Willow Theater hosts films and live theater productions like magic shows and plays throughout the year. In addition to the shows many fun events are held throughout the year. One of my favorites was always the Halloween Spooktacular which includes a haunted house and film fest. They hold a contest for budding filmmakers to make a horror movie. My daughter won her age group one year with The Clown Woods. They also hold a snow day when they bring in snow for the kids to play in. Activities are discounted for Boca Raton residents but any one can register. Events are listed on their web site, sent via email if you sign up, and there are flyers inside the building.

This has to be one of the best free/inexpensive things you can do with young children in this area. I think this place is good for kids up to age 12. This is the perfect place to coax kids off their digital devices and out into the sunshine for fun and exercise. I hope the next generation of kids enjoys it as much as we did.

The park on Royal Palm just west of 441 is dedicated to 60's actress/singer Catherine Louise "Kaye" Stevens (July 21, 1932 - December 28, 2011).  She was known professionally as Kaye Stevens and she was arguably Margate's most famous resident until 2004 when she lived for over 33 years on Lakeshore drive. She once joked on TV to Johnny Carson that the entrance and exit signs to Margate were back to back and whenever she would appear on game shows she would say hello Margate!

The Kaye Stevens Park has a long history in Margate and some it was quite colorful. The park was first dedicated to her in 1972. There was some uproar in 1984 when the park was stripped of her name over an incident with her poodle Penelope Red. According to her a park official cursed at her and told her that she wasn't allowed to walk her dog in the park because dogs made a mess. Kaye complained to the city commission and in retaliation they took her name off the park. When a new city commission took office in the 1990's the Kaye's name was restored to the park, In 2008 the city of Margate looked into renovating it at a cost of $100,000 but many in the city thought that was a waste of tax payer money for fixing what was essentially a neighborhood park. The cost of the renovation grew and the first contractor hired was exposed for having done shoddy construction work forcing closure of the park temporarily. In 2014 the project was scaled back and finally completed. In 2015 the city opted to spend $35,000 on the bronze Kaye Stevens statue that sits at the edge of the park and which faces Royal Palm Boulevard. Under the statue is a quote from Kaye about how she thinks Margate is a great place to raise children.

With the finished renovations the park has four parallel parking spots, a 1/5 mile walking trail along the lake, covered picnic pavilion, and swing benches. On my visit I saw many birds and iguanas enjoying the lake front. It may have taken more money and effort than the Margate City Commission originally anticipated but the area now serves as a lovely tribute to a woman who who was a long time resident and who tried to get the word about the town she loved wherever she went. Kaye Stevens brought a little bit of Hollywood glamour to Margate Florida.
likes: Facilities & Services: Walking trail, picnic pavilion, swing benches

reviews_attraction.text:
This park is named for Galt Ocean resident and citizen activist Earl Lifshey. Mr. Lifshey was born in New York and graduated from New York University in 1922. In 1934 he became a newspaper editor and he wrote a daily column. He was so proud of being a journalist that when he wrote his own obituary he said he "regarded it as a profession demanding a high degree of personal ethical integrity." In 1968 he moved to Galt Ocean Mile in Ft. Lauderdale where he became vice president of the Galt Mile Community Association. He spearheaded the 3.8 million dollar Galt beautification project and persuaded the 4,300 people who lived in his condominium to tax themselves to pay for it. He was so highly regarded in the community that in 1996 he was named Fort Lauderdale's Citizen of the Year. Mr. Lifshey passed away from congestive heart failure in 1998.

The park named for Mr. Lifshey was established in 1998 and it is located between A1A and the Atlantic Ocean. There is a metered parking lot a few feet from the park and two handicapped spaces adjacent to the park. The park has a paved walkway that takes you to the beach. Along the way there is interpretive signs explaining how to reduce pollution, about native plants, and information on the coral reef. This park has showers but no bathroom. This is listed as a site where you can dive off the beach.

It was a stormy day but I saw this park on the map and I had never heard of it so I came to investigate since I am always looking for a hidden beach to take ad\vantage of for sun fun days. This park is hidden between high rises so you wouldn't see it from A1A. I saw a lot of people on foot leaving so I think it is mainly used by people living in the neighborhood. A lot of people had left the beach by the time I was walking back. As I was going back there were three homeless guys blocking the path back looking at me. The homeless in general don't make me uncomfortable but there was something in my gut that said something wasn't right. I think it was the way they looked like they were waiting for me. I went back to the beach and waited until I finally saw someone else on the path. For this reason I wouldn't come back and I'll stick with one of my other favorite beaches.
likes: Facilities & Services: Paved Walkway, Interpretive Signs, Showers

reviews_attraction.text:
I have long wanted to visit this nature center but when I am in the area I tend to go to Flamingo Gardens which is across the street from it. I finally got a chance during my vacation and I had to do my visit in between rain storms. I don't know what took me so long because I thoroughly enjoyed the 164.8 that make up one of Broward's largest natural areas.

You park in the lot and then take a path to the visitor's center. Inside the center you can visit the exhibit hall that included an excellent display detailing the Native American presence in this area by the Tequesta and Seminole. While I enjoyed the exhibit I did note that their artifacts were reproductions and not authentic artifacts. There was still a lot of good information though. In the center you can get park information, visit the playroom for children, or see some live animals in their display. On my visit there they were hosting a student photography exhibit. Oak Hammock Hall is available for rental for weddings and other special events.

Behind the visitors centers are rocking chairs on the porch. Perfect for taking in the gorgeous marsh view that had birds and turtles. An elevated boardwalk takes you across the marsh and to a half mile nature trail that goes through the oak hammock. Foxes and bobcats make their home here along with migratory and resident birds but all I saw on my visit where a few Zebra Longwing butterflies. Located in the back is a Garden of Reflection that stands in tribute to crime victims. A 90 minute ceremony is held here once a year.

On your way out don't forget to stop by the public art installation, Island Garden by Lorna Jordan. It is a metal gazebo that spirals up to benches and framed on both sides by a water feature. I really loved it and it was the perfect place to sit and relax after the trail hike. The art in this piece incorporates nature into it.

I really enjoyed my visit even though it was in the pouring rain. The next time I visit Flamingo Gardens I will be incorporating a visit here as well. While Flamingo Gardens displays their animals in enclosures here you can see them the wild and experience how Florida used to be.

The first thing that strikes you when you enter the park is the giant hill built from a garbage dump. If you live in Florida any hill is a weird sight indeed. What was once landfill has been now transformed into a beautiful park. Running and biking all over the hill were people. Old, young, in shape, and those working on getting in shape. I drove to to the top to get a better look. Standing on top of a hill is a surreal experience in Florida. At the top is a beautiful view of a canal and buildings including a church. After taking in the view I headed off to the right and the trail took me to a steep paved hill which people were sprinting up. I didn't have workout clothes on but I did have my sneakers and I couldn't resist trying it out. It took me two minutes to get up to the top and when I did I felt every muscle in my leg burning. I did it two more times and was able to fulfill the floors on my fit bit app, a goal I don't normally achieve because I just don't have stairs in my daily life. I can see why everyone loves this place, it takes your work out to a whole new level. In addition to the runners there were other people who brought entire trailers full of workout equipment. I saw one guy dragging huge weights as he ran. I even saw people horseback riding. Also located at the top of the hill is a section for people flying model airplanes.

After I finished my run I went to explore the rest of the park. At the bottom of the hill and to the left is a boat launch area. If you go to the right there is a fishing dock, basketball courts, playgrounds for the kids, and a fitness loop at the very back with different stationary exercise stations set up along it. If I had more time and the proper clothes I would have really liked to explore that. I can see why everyone comes here. I can't think of any where else in South Florida that you can add a hill to your running workout. The entry fee is also very reasonable. Free on weekdays and $1.50 weekends and holidays. If I lived closer I would come here all the time. I wish they would do something similar to the garbage dump in Coconut Creek.
likes: Unique Attraction Type (giant hill from landfill)
On-site Activities (running, biking, sprinting, horseback riding, model airplane flying)
Facilities & Services (boat launch area, fishing dock, basketball courts, playgrounds, fitness loop with exercise stations)
View (canal and buildings including a church)

reviews_attraction.text:
I really love this park. I think it is one of the most beautiful places in Ft. Lauderdale. For years I have shot my Christmas card and holiday pictures here. A wide path winds along the New River and curves around before ending at the Broward Performing Arts Center. Amenities include benches and a picnic tables. Directly across from the Museum of Science and Discovery is a huge lawn and a large gazebo perfect for cultural arts performances. There is a bathroom adjacent to the gazebo. Along the sea wall is the perfect place to sit and watch the boats cruise by. Near the Performing Arts Center is the Ft. Lauderdale Police Memorial honoring fallen officers. Also in this area is the Lone Sailor Statue which is a replica of one at the United States Navy Memorial in Washington D.C. It stands in tribute to all of those who serve in the navy.

The most popular event held here is the Sunday Jazz Brunch held on the first Sunday of each month from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. Other events held here during the year include the Riverwalk fall festival, Smoke on the Water BBQ Feast & Competition, Light up Lauderdale, and the Stone Crab and Seafood Festival. A full listing of events and dates can be found on the go riverwalk web site.

If you want to visit here especially during an event the best bet it to use the city parking garage across the street. There are a few street spots in front of the science museum. Himmarshee Village is located just a few steps down from the park offering a lot of great dining areas. Also nearby is the Old Ft. Lauderdale Village and Museum. With so much to see and do this area has become a vacation destination whether you are in the area for a visit or you are a local who just wants to play tourist for the day.
likes: Historical tributes (police memorial, Lone Sailor Statue)

reviews_attraction.text:
I love this park because there is so much to do here! The full name of the park is Burt Aaronson South County Regional Park. Burt Aaronson was a former Palm Beach County Commissioner who was the driving force to create the park. He passed away in 2018.

The park is home to the outdoor Sunset Cove Amphitheater. It hosts many shows throughout the year and a full list can be found on the parks website. A favorite memory was getting to see Imagine Dragons perform here before they were well known.

I also have great memories of taking my daughter to the Coconut Cove Water Park also located inside the park. It's a small sized water park perfect for kids 12 and under. They have two water slides, a lazy river, a splash playground and a pool. I spent many hot summer days there with my daughter and her friends when she was younger.

Another great place in the park is the Daggerwing Nature Center. There is a 3,000 foot exhibit hall with classrooms and displays. Behind the hall is a two trail elevated boardwalk that leads to an observation tower. The staff here puts on many educational programs throughout the year.

If all that wasn't enough there is also 4 lighted baseball fields, 2 basketball courts, volleyball courts, an almost 5 mile bike path, boat launch, picnic pavilions, exercise stations, a dog park, a playground, racquetball courts, and a golf course. Whether you are into team sports, fishing, playing with your four legged friend, or looking to cool off in a splash park you can do it all here. Mr. Aaronson did the Boca Raton and it's visitors a wonderful service by preserving this green space for so many people to enjoy. Although he has passed his contribution is serving the people in his beloved community every day.

Old Fort Park is located across the street from the Indian River Lagoon. It is located on the National Register of Historic Places and it turns out quite a bit of history took place here. The park was an important burial site and the large hill in the center of park contains the human remains of the Ais tribe from 1,000 years ago. The Ais were once Florida's largest group of indigenous people. They were hunters and gathers and their territory ranged from Central Florida to Jupiter. What we know about them comes from the journals of Jonathan Dickinson who was captured by them in 1696 after his ship was wrecked. By 1740 they had been completely wiped out by European invasion and slavery.

After the Ais died out the land the park now sits on later became the site of Fort Pierce which was built in by the US military during the Second Seminole War. The fort was named for Lieutenant Colonel Benjamin K. Pierce who was the brother of Franklin Pierce who would become president. The fort served as General Thomas Jessup's winter quarters. Jessup attempted to force the Seminoles west of the Mississippi on the Trail of Tears. During the battle of the Loxahatchee in Jupiter the army suffered four casualties including their doctor. They were forced to retreat back to Fort Pierce. The fort never saw battle and was decommissioned in 1842 and destroyed by a fire in 1843. A plaque commemorating the fort was placed in the park by the Daughters of the American Revolution in 1925.

Today you can climb stairs to the top of the burial mound although there are signs warning that digging and metal detectors are forbidden. Graceful old trees draped in Spanish moss are the only eyewitnesses left to the incredible history that took place here.

At 53.3 acres this is Broward County's most archaeological significant natural area. Artifacts found here show that people have lived here from 500 B.C. through roughly A.D. 1000 to 1200. Centuries later this area was home to Miccosukee leader Chitto Tustenuggee known as the snake warrior. He was designated chief during the Second Seminole war whose beginning was tied to the Cooley massacre in Ft. Lauderdale. For more on that see my review of Colee Hammock Park.  Two Seminole settlements once sat on two islands in the marsh and were occupied for a dozen years before the Seminoles were attacked and fled the area. In 1947 the land became the Perry farm. Community interest in the land as an archaeological and historic site caused it to be purchased in 1992 by the State of Florida through the Emergency Archaeological Property Acquisition Fund. On January 21, 2004 Snake warrior Island opened as a natural area.

As you walk around the area it is easy to see the beauty that attracted the native people to the area. The lake and eight created wetlands are surrounded by live oak, gumbo limbo, strangler fig, cypress, red maple, wild coffee, beautyberry, fire bush, pickerel weed, eel grass, and rushes. Wildlife in the area include wading birds and ducks, red wing blackbirds, wood storks, little blue and tricolored herons, anhinga, white ibis, and and osprey. On my visit I saw many iguanas and other kinds of lizards. Amenities include benches, signs, and picnic tables. A half mile paved walkway loops through the preserve and takes you back to the parking lot.

Blazing Star is 26 acres of scrub pine with a mile loop running on top of sugar sand. It is adjacent to the much larger Sugar Sand Park. This area was once part of the Atlantic Coastal Ridge, ancient dunes that lined the Atlantic Ocean. Part of the trail runs along I-95 and in addition to the cars you may hear the occasional train racing past.

Plants you might encounter include sand live oaks, myrtle oak, Chapman oak, saw palmetto, slash pine, sand pine, bromeliad, prickly pear cactus, marsh ferns and cinnamon ferns and the invasive Brazilian pepper. When I came upon the pink and yellow lantana growing in the back of the preserve it was covered in zebra longwing butterflies. If you want to see the blazing star (Liatris), with it's stalks of purple flowers that the area takes it's name from you will have to plan your visit for late summer and early fall.

If you are lucky you will see protected gopher tortoises. All I came upon however was a burrow. As you make your way through the preserve you will be serenaded by cicadas and crickets.

This is a pretty isolate spot, especially when you get to the back of the preserve. Unlike a lot of other preserves I have visited this one is not paved so it is not wheelchair accessible. It was actually quite hard to even walk in the back but when I came upon a hundred butterflies floating around the plants it made the muddy sneakers and trek worth it. You have to be slow and quiet to fully appreciate this area but once you focus in a lot of surprises await you.

I never knew that this incredible park was only a short distance from the Sawgrass Mills Mall. I always zoomed passed it on my way to the mall not realizing how much it had to offer. I finally decided to stop one night on a trip home and was amazed to find the huge wetland trail that runs at the back of the park. Some parts of the trail are paved and some are gravel and it crosses over several wooden boardwalks. I saw signs that it was used by the equestrians who have their facilities at the back of the park. My favorite part was in the water under one of the boardwalks where I saw at least 50 turtles swimming around with the fish. It had just finished raining alleviating the oppressive Florida heat for a moment making my evening walk among the wetlands pleasant.

The trail let me out at the huge playground called Camp Everglades. Opened in 2004, it was designed with an Everglades theme. Components of the playground include an Everglades village, fishing camp, and tree huts. The park also has a community center available to rent to Plantation residents for private events, picnic tables, benches, bathrooms, tennis courts, and basketball courts.

I loved my visit to this park. Birds were soaring overhead and fish and turtles were swimming below. I definitely won't be passing this park by again. It's a park worth taking your camera out for.

Riverside Park is located along a canal in Coral Springs. It has a really nice recently renovated boat ramp. Other park amenities include a sand volleyball court, basketball courts,grills and tables, jog/walk trails, nature areas, pickleball court, picnic pavilion, playground, restrooms and roller hockey rinks.

Coral Springs has just started opening the parks back up. According to the city website "As we continue to mitigate the spread of this virus, there will be no groups of more than six permitted in one area, while practicing social distancing.  If social distancing is not achievable, only groups that reside in the same household may be within six feet of each other. Following Broward County's announcement, the City of Coral Springs will open city facilities outlined below, which staff will take extra precautions to ensure they are cleaned and sanitized.Community and neighborhood Parks will be opened from 8:00 a.m. to dusk starting Wednesday, April 29. Parks will be available for limited activities such as walking, jogging, hiking and cycling, nature walks on trails and quiet enjoyment of the outdoors."

So you can use the park for exercise in small groups but for now the park amenities will remain closed. It's a step in the right direction and hopefully normal operations will soon return.

In 2013, Hollywood Hot Glass was opened in Arts Park in Young Circle by glass artist Brenna Baker. Baker learned to blow glass at the Corning Museum in New York and she trained in Murano Italy with the famous glass blower Pino Signoretto, You can see some of Brenna's work inside the building. She creates installations and commission work.

Thanks to Hollywood Hot Glass now anyone can learn to blow glass at the workshops held here. You can walk in to a workshop and in 20 minutes create a piece of glass art. Pieces range from $50 to $100 but they currently have two offers for less money on Groupon where you can create an ornament or a starfish or heart piece. During the workshops you get to do the fun part and the staff instructor does the hard work. If you aren't sure yet that you want to participate you can also watch the process for free from the bleachers.

This a unique and fun activity and you get to leave with a beautiful keepsake. Children as young as 4 can even participate but to get the most out of the experience children should be at least 8 years old. This would be great for a date or even as a gift. Hollywood Hot Glass is putting the art into the Arts Park in Young Circle.

I am a manatee fanatee and this is where I can catch a glimpse of the stars of the Florida waterways. FPL built this brand new eco center a year ago. There is no admission charge to come in. The building is two floors housing manatee displays and a small gift shop. On the outside is a snack bar.  Manatees can be viewed either from the ground floor or the upstairs balcony. They like to gather where the warm water is discharged from the power plant. The best time to see them is in the winter when we get a prolonged cold snap of at least two to three days. They like sunny cold weather. As soon as the waterway temperature equals the discharge water temperature they are back out in search of sea grass. Today was the perfect conditions, there were 169! It is so amazing to watch them in the wild like they are meant to be instead of penned up in an aquarium. You cannot feed them because they are protected wildlife. Just enjoy watching them do what manatees do. Check the manatee cam before you go to see if the manatees are present that day. Thank you FPL for this wonderful center.

This is a cute little neighborhood park that you probably wouldn't know about it unless you lived in the neighborhood. The waterway is surrounded on all sides by housing and the back of strip mall. Amenities include a boat ramp, picnic pavilion, walking trail, and swing benches. Populating the park are a huge flock of Egyptian Geese. They are actually a cross between a goose and a duck. This bird is actually from Sub-Saharan Africa, the Nile Valley and parts of the Middle East. The non native birds have either escaped or been deliberately introduced into Florida sometime in the 1960's. However they came to be here they have successfully made this park their home. Another thing to note about this park is it is a great place to watch Margate's Fourth of July fireworks. I like to sit on the edge of the dock to view them. The fireworks terrify the birds however and they can be heard crying in fright. This is a cute park that is hardly used which makes it a great place to kick back and catch a sunset.

Where is it Christmas every day of the year in Coral Gables? At Merrie Christmas Park of course. Randall Norton "Randy" Christmas was the Mayor of Miami from 1955-1957. He must have quite the sense of humor to name his daughter Merrie. Not so funny was the fact that Merrie passed away at the age of 15 in 1969 and her father named the park in her honor.

In 2014 the city of Miami discovered toxic metals at the park and shut it down for the next 2 years. Clean up of the park cost over a million dollars. Today the park is open and is a popular destination for the people who live in the neighborhood. The park has giant banyan trees and a large open area perfect for play. Other park amenities include an exercise path, picnic tables, and a playground. On the evening I visited people were having a party, kids were playing on the playground, and dogs were running across the lawn. This is a beautiful spot for the community of Coral Gables to gather.

Opened in 2012 Barkland is a little over 2 acres and includes separate areas for dogs under 25 pounds and a larger area for dogs over 25 pounds. The park is open every day 7:30 AM until sunset. Amenities provided included a dog washing station, water fountains for both pets and people, walking trails, covered pavilions, and benches. There are also things for the dogs to climb through and climb over. You don't have to register your dog to use the park and it is up to you to be diligent to watch and protect your dog. You are also expected to grab one of of the bags and clean up and properly dispose of waste if your dog goes to the bathroom. Parkland did a very nice job on the park. They added a lot of trees and pretty landscaping. There is a kid park next door with bathrooms and vending machines for drinks and ice cream but there are signs advising the dog park people to not take the dogs on the playground side.
likes: Separate areas for different dog sizes

reviews_attraction.text:
This a beautiful 6.83 acre beach front park. Parking is free which is amazing since there isn't free beach parking to be found in Broward County. A boardwalk takes you from the parking lot to the base of a small hill. After a not steep climb you come to the top where there is a playground, a restroom, showers and picnic tables. There is also steps that take you past the lifeguard station and down to the 600 foot beach. It is a bit of a hike if you need to carry a bunch of things with you so I recommend traveling light. The park and beach are meticulously maintained. I didn't see so much as a speck of garbage anywhere.
Close to shore are shallow reefs off shore for snorkeling. There is also a larger deeper reef 50 to 100 feet off shore that would require a dive flag. This park is an amazing find if you are looking for a relaxing beach day.

The historical museum had its humble beginnings in a back room of city hall. In 1985 the museum opened behind the library in the Plantation Botanical Gardens. The museum contains an annex dedicated to the history of the Plantation fire department.

Permanent displays in the museum include exhibits on the Tequesta and Seminole Indians, fire and police department memorabilia, an  Everglades diorama, and information about the towns founding families. The museum also hosts temporary exhibits. The current one, America in the 1960's will be on display until October 5,  2019. The museum hosts many events and speakers throughout the year. A complete schedule can be found on the museum's website. Admission to the museum is free.

This ride is a small roller coaster located in the Storybook Circus part of Fantasyland. During the Fantasyland expansion the ride was rethemed to add a cannon that Goofy apparently uses to shoot himself out of during his circus act. The ride is only a minute long so I wouldn't wait for it if there is a very long line. If you do choose to ride it is a fun small coaster good for young children up to adults. My 17 year old daughter still found it enjoyable. You are taken up to the top of a hill and you race to the bottom in a series of twists and turns. There aren't any sudden drops making this a good coaster for younger children.

This is just a beautiful authentic carousel. After the fireworks were over we headed to Fantasy Land and found ourselves in front of this ride with no line so we hopped aboard. It brings out the kid in everyone. It's great for all ages, especially if there is no line. If you rode it once you can probably skip it but I love it's old fashioned feel. There may be more exciting rides to go on at Disney but my daughter and I thoroughly enjoyed our two minute ride.

At the end of the platform a British Airways Concorde.

Intrepid: the hangar is set up as a museum for young and old alike (a model of the Lego aircraft carrier is on display, 250,000 pieces and 7 meters long), games, simulator intermingles with planes .

On the flight deck, a whole range of aircraft are on display, including the magnificent Blackbird SR-71. At the end in a furnished dome, you will find the ........ Enterprise shuttle, with eye-catching customers at Star Trek.

Superb place for those who love aeronautics.

Good visit

there are places like here where one has the impression that time does not flow at the same speed.

Take the time to look around, the squirrels, the life of this city of unimaginable contrast.

With coffee or chocolate the pose is pleasant.

Good visit
