Great place, especially this time of year, to shake the winter blues. It was cold today but sunny and hardly a cloud in the sky. Lots of outdoor activities to do ... hike, bike, golf, fish, picnic,  plus playgrounds for the little ones and a skate park and soccer field for the older ones. The pond is a great place to introduce small children to waterfowl. You should avoid feeding bread, chips, crackers, cereal, or sweets to the ducks and geese. Corn, oats, frozen peas thawed, lettuce, just to name a few.

*** Note: Just a comment on the previous review from S. Ewing... He states that a hiker should not venture too far off the trails and cites wildlife ie. bears, bobcats, and mountain lions as the reason. Bears?, yes, but you are not likely to see one. Bobcats, maybe, but a very high probability of not seeing one (plus they would pose no danger to a human  and therefore sighting one would be a rare treat).  Mountain lions? You could spend your entire lifetime with the express purpose of getting even a glimpse of a mountain lion in Coonskin Park or anywhere in the entire state or region for that matter, and the likelihood of seeing one would be virtually zero. Actually there is no definitive proof that mountain lions exist in WV.

i've loved Hawk's Nest since I was a kid. State parks in WV are taking an adverse hit due to Covid and even prior to, they haven't been funded as they should by the state. I hope one day that our many state parks can be restored to their former glory days. They play (played I should say) a big role with boosting economies and providing service jobs for the locals.
I thought it commendable that they made an effort to provide some much needed holiday cheer in these bleak times by putting up lights at the main park along Midland Trail as well as at the overlook. I hope you enjoy the photos I took when I stopped by while traveling home the other night. It was serene and magical... a scene from what could have been a Robert Frost poem.

What a geologic wonder! I was here on a beautiful day during low tide. I plan to come back sometime on a bright moonlit night when the sea is raging. Sparkling diamonds shooting up from the rocks would be a sight to behold! Check out my photos. The pictured driftwood was just downbeach from blowing rocks. The huge tree stump with roots would have been a nice addition to my wife's landscaping, but it was much too big to haul. If that doesn't look like a giant octopus washed up on shore, I don't know what does. Release the Kraken !!!

Deception Pass Bridge is one example of where an engineering icon fits perfectly in it's natural setting. Built in 1934-35, the double bridge connects Whidbey and Fidalgo Islands and is the centerpiece of the state park of the same name. It is one of the most visited sites in Washington state. We were there on a day trip to several spots in the north western part of the state. I must say Deception Pass was the highlight. I have included a couple of early photos I thought you might enjoy. I have given credit for both.

I am currently in the midst of a Google Map project whereby I'm locating places mentioned by long-time CBS News correspondent Charles Kuralt (1934-1997) in his book "On the Road with Charles Kuralt", copyright 1985, Putnam. Kuralt visited the mill (1968ish) and interviewed Captain Frank Langrell the miller. I have included pics of Frank and the book cover. The photo of Mr. Langrell  (1887 - 1974) pouring grain out of a bucket is from the book. This project has been a very enjoyable pursuit.

The past comes alive on this hallowed spot. You can feel the presence of these 409 enslaved Congolese who survived the passage. White privilege and black suppression should have long since disappeared by now. Alas... not the case.
One can imagine that the scene viewed at the Wanderer's landing almost 162 years ago would have been very similar to that of the pics I posted as they arrived at sunset.

Daniel Boone is one of not too many public boat launch sites on the Kanawha River between the Marmet and Winfield Locks. It's easy access and there are plenty of trailer spaces. The ramp is steeper than ones I've been used to launching from, so be aware and don't back down too fast (like I did the first time) and have to stand on the brake. Also the dock needs some treated boards replaced.

This is one of the areas best kept secrets. Located on A1A between Ponte Vedra and St Augustine, the research and education center is hidden just off the highway so that it is easily (and often) missed. This is well worth the stop,... especially if you have kids. The life-sized Humpback and Right Whales were awesome! Check out my pics

Awesome views from this spot. Don't pass up this viewpoint.

Wanted to add some pics from our road trip from Seattle to central West Virginia. The shortest route, of course, would have bypassed the Oregon coast, so looking back I'm so glad we took the 600+ mile detour from Seattle to northern California before heading east.

I'm a lover of lighthouses and give it 4 stars only because of accessibility. You can't drive up to it after hours. You encounter a locked gate in a residential area of Fernandina Beach. You also can't get a clear photo for the trees. The 4 pics I took were from behind the locked chain-link gate.

Great piece of still standing history. Many mistakenly call this the oldest schoolhouse in the US. The St Augustine schoolhouse (construction date unknown) first appeared on tax records in 1716. The oldest still-standing schoolhouse is the Voorlezer's House, circa 1695, in Staten Island, NY.

Great place for a relaxing stroll or sit on a bench by the waterway and watch the boats go by. A nice playground area is great for the younger kids. There is also the coolest circular pier fishing spot. It's about 40 feet across with the inside of the circle about 25 feet in diameter.

Hiked this trail a couple of times. Views are well worth the under 2 mile (one way) hike. Beautiful. Only gets a little steep at the end. If you have children make sure they are well supervised. There are no rails or anything,... just a rock ledge and a long drop. Be very careful.

What a great little park  on Winter Point on the north/west bank of the St Johns River just below the I-95 Fuller Warren Bridge. I spent a peaceful hour or so here a couple of years ago while waiting to pick my daughter up from work. Check out my pics.

The Lightner Museum is another iconic St. Augustine fixture. Christmas runs way past traditional times in the oldest city in the continental US. The photos were taken at and near the Lightner a couple of Januarys ago.
Quirky FREE, yes free, museum. Lots of antiques, old coin operated games, and stuff from the interesting to the bizarre. Jake the Lizardman is one of its attractions. A fun stop while on Long Beach.
Easy access for the lighthouse enthusiasts. Great views from the top. Got a smile seeing the Jimmy Buffet brick on the walkway up to the light. Really cool banyan tree near the base.
What a beautiful spot. Brought my 91 year old dad here on a little jaunt. His first time. There are a couple of benches where you can sit and reflect.... very serene and peaceful.
Beautiful spot. Nearly frozen over during this cold snap in late December.                  It also raged during heavy spring rains when I stopped by later in April.
Opened in 1932 this reinforced concrete arch bridge spans Cape Creek and carries US 101. The best view of course is from the parking lot at Heceta Head Lighthouse.
Great place for an outdoor family event. We recently held a baby shower there in the pavilion. It was a good afternoon and evening with family and friends.
View of Mt St Helens from the Astoria bridge over the Columbia River on the Wshington/Oregon border about 80 miles distant.
Only saw this from a pulloff on the Oregon Coast Highway (US-101). Why the 5 stars? I love lighthouses. What can I say?
Just west of the Hawks Nest Lodge the overlook is very easy access along Rt 60, Midland Trail. It is well worth a look.
There's not a enough places to park a trailer. The area is kept up well, however, and the lake is beautiful.

Great place to go to see big gators in the wild. The 24 mile loop runs off of SR 41 just west of the oasis Ranger Station. Then rejoins SR 41. There are plenty of places to stop along the way and see some large gators. It is a lime stone Road with some potholes but an average car should be able to make it with no problem. Just remember there are no fences, handrails Our other means of restraint for the animals. You were in their environment so keep a safe distance. This drive is very worthwhile and if you want to see wild Florida this is it. It is a free drive the only cost is your time and gas but it’s very well worth it.

Great Florida park friendly staff very interesting very educational great place to take your kids they have weddings their parties the gift shop is good if you want to see iguanas there is quite a few of them making a home there there are trails to walk and plenty of walking through the fort there are lotta artifacts around to see what they used at the time of the fort they offer a guided tour as well as a self-guided tour with plenty of signs to see what happen at the spot very well worth seeing play in plenty of time as it will take a little bit a time to see

Great Place. Lots of history there lot to see how people lived back at the turn of the century. To bad not able to see more. There is river access and a nature walk that goes through a bamboo forest. It talks about people as a person and  as a town. The Rangers are very friendly and very informative. The village Estero is the main draw to the park. Unless you’re looking for river access by using the boat ramp. The park is well taken care of very clean and the restrooms are very accessible.

Nice Place. Cool place to walk around. Bicycle rental there with lots of places to ride. Fishing Pier Nice but can be crowded at times. Lots of traffic great place to visit. The lighthouse is very neat  and still in use today. Plenty of beach to relax on and enjoy swimming. We saw dolphins their swimming in a surf. Lotta things to do around the island.

A place to go and see. The Greek people there are supper. Very friendly. Plenty of places to eat and drink. There is a husband daycare (the beer bar) so women can shop. There are fishing trips that leave from there. You can walk from shop to shop with bakeries in between. If you are in the Tampa Bay Area stop in.

This is a nice place to view the Everglades. You are over the water and have a chance to encounter all kinds of wildlife from the Everglades and some that is not. It is a short walk to the Observation tower. The tower is not that high but offers a great advantage point to look out over the Everglades.

Great place nice park plenty a hiking trail is plenty to see the natural Florida trails are elevated so you can walk to the swap and see what is like in the swamp plenty of parking picnic shelters restrooms plenty of people around so you feel safe if you’re in the area very good park just stop at

This is a very nice State Park. Preserves the history of Ybor City. The tour is very informative and a must see. Walking through the museum was amazing. Some of the things that happened are interesting. If you are in the area stop and take a look at one of Florida’s great State Parks

Another one of our amazing State Park. This is a nice place to go out and get away from it for a while. Picnic tables and pavilions are around. Great trails for nature walks. Florida’s state park system is a great thing. There’s a lot of history and areas of the state parks.

Nice little water park in Zephyrhills. Safe very fun nice place to cool off for the day. Good place good place to bring your kids. They have public restrooms. The restrooms are clean and stocked. There are picnic tables. And once a month they have a festival.

Great State Park they have kayak rentals. There are places to picnic. Good fishing in the area. They have several Nature trails to hike. There are several geocaches in the Park. The Rangers are nice and very informative. Thy have a beach for swimming too

Great place friendly staff they have wild horses Buffalo as well as all the other Florida wildlife there’s observation tower and plenty a hiking trail’s another one of Florida is great parks lot of paths you can ride a bike on

Stopped at this park to camp. The only thing they have is primitive camping and it’s a ways off the road. The staff it’s very nice and also extremely helpful. There is also a nature center that is extremely interesting.

Came for the Pioneer Day’s and said it would be from 10:00 am to 3:00 pm and nothing they are picking up nothing Happening. Drove all this way for nothing. what a waste of time and gas. Very disappointed.
Great Place very nice park. They have very clean restrooms. Park is very well kept. Trails well maintained. If you’re in the area stop in and take a look at one of the BEST parks in Florida
Great place to kayak. There is a launch fee, but small River is crystal clear. Chance of seeing manatees. They offer a pickup service included with rental. Can be crowded at times.
Great Place you can see manatees the best time is The colder months. They have kayak rentals. There is a nature trail to walk. Lot of educating signs around the park.
Great park nice trails can get wet at times we hiked through ankle deep water at times. We did get a great hike in. Not to far from places to grab something to eat
Great place to go see alligators plenty of gators to see an observation tower to look out for him I have a tram tour and very informative information center
Great place Nice swimming area with white sandy beaches. There is a boat ramp with plenty of parking. They have shell mounds there. Playground for the kids.
Great place cool trail lot a history as you walk on the trail.  I can be a little soggy at times but very well worth the walk to learn some local history.
Great place lots of history you will have lots to see park staff is great and is very helpful if you need them. Lots of people at times
Great park place to walk around. They have wild horses and Buffalo roaming around. This is a very nice state park to take a look at.
Great Place! Very nice park. Has primitive Camping and sites with power. They also have camper sites. There is a observation tower.
Great Place to kayak. Nice park to walk around there is a boardwalk with a good chance to see Wildlife

Scenic Florida... Old Florida look is beautiful. Originally owned by Edward Ball a millionaire who founded the St. Joe paper company. Interesting fact: The only individual allowed to put a fence across a navigational water way in Florida and it still remains today to keep individuals from accessing the head of the spring at night. Now owned by the State of Florida operated by Florida State University.

The lodge is very nice features a restaurant, lodging, ballrooms. Outside features boat tours of the springs, a swimming area, and a two story concrete dock for jumping or diving into the crystal clear water 💦 bring your snorkel and view the many fish 🐟 that call the spring home.

Before you leave say hello to Old Joe the 11 foot alligator who was murdered in 1966!!!

This is one pretty campground. Clean bathrooms, hot showers! We decided to do the ghost tour late one night during our visit boy did that make for a fun night tent camping, the raccoons enjoyed laughing an me jumping every time they rustled the leaves!

On our second visit we brought our popup camper and skipped the ghost tour ;) we live this campground because it’s right in the middle of all the action. Tons of wildlife and close to the beach!

Visited Chehaw Park today with my family it was a little cold but the animals seemed to love it. The zoo itself is very quaint without all the bells and whistles of a larger zoo. I personally loved it! The bathrooms are simple yet clean. Perfect place to take the kids to get away for the day.

Features: The Zoo of course, camping area, Massive playground, Frisbee golf course, and tons more!!! Enjoy all my pictures...

The City of Tallahassee designed a super park here hours of fun in the sun. The park features a massive climbing structure, swings, bowl spinners, and one rotating structure you have to try yourself. Down the path a skip hop and a jump is a really cool water feature. Bike need repairing that's here to they installed a bike repair station with tools and a pump.

Awesome place to take the kids in Tallahassee.

The Jacksonville Zoo is always working on something new to make your adventure amazing every time you visit.

This is Zoo is great for the whole family or even solo. Well manicured landscaping, and always something new! A massive selection of animals to view that are very well taken care of.

Put this on your list of things to do while in Jacksonville, Florida!

Fun place to go whenever! Beautiful Caverns!!! Our cavern guide was amazing and very knowledgeable made it especially fun for the kids. Bring your camera for some spectacular pictures and a good pair of walking shoes lots of trails. We stayed in the campgrounds which are clean and nice. The bathrooms were really clean as well.

Update: 3/19 Repairs look Great!!! See new photos!

Update: 8/18 Repairs needed on playground!!!

Original: Leon County did a phenomenal job planning this park out between the baseball field, the football field, walking paths, and the trails. Super Fun! An excellent place to take the entire family. Bring a picnic!!!

Absolutely stunning, another jewel 💎 of Florida history. The garden features tons of Magnolia Trees and lots of beautiful flowers. A must see if visiting Tallahassee.

The staff is super friendly and knowledgeable. I love that they've included a kids reading time as well.

Enjoy my photos!!!
likes: Facilities & Services: Friendly staff, Knowledgeable staff

reviews_attraction.text:
Beautiful springs with iconic ice cold Florida water 😉. It had been a long time since I had visited Ponce De Leon Springs and on our last trip we stopped by, it was just as I remembered it as a kid now I get to share it with my kids 😭

Features: Clean Bathrooms 🚽, picnic tables, and grills

This museum never gets old. Love the new signage throughout, the walking paths a lot easier to navigate. Tree to Tree as always is awesome!!!

Bring a good pair of walking shoes and some water it's Hot! Totally fun for the whole family. We just renewed our membership for another year!!!

An amazing place to take kids of all ages lots of fun things to see and touch!!! Probably the coolest museum on earth. Museum is kept super clean and neat! Awesome that you can take you family for free. We spent hours in the kids area and they loved every moment.

This is what make Disney amazing the ability to make part of their Park so fun and educational. Like a zoo on steroids! The kids loved this ride can't wait to come back and do this again soon. Once in a lifetime up close views at some of the coolest animals.

We went here for my sons Birthday and he loved it. The rides were just enough to keep him entertained for a couple of hours. Amazing what you can do with a couple thousand bricks! Definitely worth driving to Atlanta from Tallahassee, FL

This is one big park! It reminded me of being a kid again when I saw the massive steal slides. I agree with some that bathrooms would be nice but you come to a park like this to play. Worth the drive from Tallahassee, FL 😉
Beautiful park lots of great places to take photos! But just watch out on the trails for yellow jackets 🐝 they are super heavy in this area for some reason. If you have allergies carry your EpiPen!!!
Great place to take a walk, jog, run whichever you prefer. I love the layout! Tons of green space if you just want to hang out. Features large pavilions with massive grills.
I love that this park decorates every year for Christmas 🎄it's always so beautiful 😍 and makes for spectacular pictures of family and friends. See you next year!
A fun place to take the family for a walk, however the homeless population tends to call this home sometimes making some visitors a little uncomfortable.
This place will keep you and your kids entertained for your entire visit. Tons of things to see and touch. The fiddler crabs 🦀 were my personal favorite.
Best park ever... tons of places to play. Between the multiple playgrounds, dog park, bike track, trails you really would never run out of things to do.
Went with the family to see the Nina and the Pinta in port and stumbled upon this old fort. Awesome place for a walk with beautiful views of the river.
I love the fort! The cannon demonstration was my favorite part of the visit. A little pricy to get in with a family but totally worth it.
Tallahassee's place for go karts and laser tag!!! This place has some of the best cheap pizza I have ever had. Wide assortment of games.
A little Florida History here and a really nice trail. Clean Bathrooms 🚽 and Picnic tables. Go check it out
I think I had more fun than the kids! This place is the biggest play house you will ever visit!!!

The Orlando Museum of Art is a spectacular place to have your wedding. It's one of the most elegant Orland Wedding Venues in Central Florida. I speak from first-hand experience... I have been a DJ here for many weddings and receptions.

The rotunda is a spacious reception room, it offers something the a typical hotel ballroom cannot. It connects to other galleries, that offer a unique location to host a cocktail hour, ceremony, or pre-reception.

Even if you prefer outside, there is an ever-changing sculpture garden that is completely different than any other wedding location in Orlando.

Fun... but it is a relatively short ride for the money spent. It’s 18 bucks for about five minutes of fun. If you’ve never done this type of ride, it’s probably worth it one time.

The ride is surprisingly bumpy for a steel/metal track, I assumed it would be very smooth. Overall a good time, but it’s hard to justify $18 when you can go up the road for $65 -and have a full day of unlimited rides at Silver Dollar City.

I know it’s apples and oranges. At the Runaway Coaster, $20 for four rides would be a more fair value. I’d probably return at that price.

There is a TON of stuff here, sometimes so much it feels like a hodge-podge of unrelated items. But, still pretty cool. I wish there were more descriptions for the items; a lot of the displays were just that... displays with no descriptions.

The architecture is amazing, there are a lot of interesting nooks and crannies to explore. The stairways, old-time saunas and showers are a few of the highlights.

The glass rooms are a sight to behold, and the cafe inside the old pool is just too cool. There are two nice gift shops as well.

What can be said that hasn’t already? Probably the most spectacular themed ride ever built so far. If you are afraid of heights- consider this: it looks like you are up really, really high, but it’s all an illusion. If you can lose yourself in the story, you’ll be fine.

I’ve waited for this ride three times, all with 90-120 minute waits, and I’d do it again. It’s that much worth it. The best part- even if you’ve not seen Avatar, it’s all good. The ride explains exactly what is going on.

Hands down the best show in Branson. Not only that, you get dinner as well... all for $55. A STEAL considering most shows in Branson are $50 without a meal. And the other shows are nowhere near as good.

It’s a professional, state if the art production. No “tracked” music here. The band is live, the dancers are on point, the singers are fantastic, and the MC is hilarious. Best part? No corny hillbilly jokes. It’s a fresh alternative to the outdated shows in Branson. Go!

The bridge is high and there are good views driving across, but to get the full breadth of what is going on here, stop at the visitor center and take the stairs down to the lookout point. Going down is easy; the walk back up is a little tougher!

The visitor center is comprehensive; including exhibits and a short film about the gorge. Included is the obligatory gift shop, however there a a smaller, private gift shop next door with better prices.

If you are a fan of oddball Roadside Americana, it’s pretty hard to beat this place. Lots of great items that you cannot find in any other type of museum.

There are full-size carnival rides inside (sadly you cannot ride them) but there is plenty to see, from snack carts to circus wagons.

The displays for sideshows were particularly interesting, along with vintage ad posters for the area. A great trip for 10 bucks!

Amazing gardens and nature setting. It’s a piece of Florida history, going back to the 1920’s.

You can spend as little as an hour (or all day) here. There have been lots of improvements lately with the addition of a kids area and an example of a sustainable outdoor kitchen space.

The tower is what everyone comes for (and it’s amazing) but take the time to explore the trails and take in the quiet solitude.

Totally worth every cent. If price is an issue, buy the cheaper non-dolphin encounter ticket. (The dolphin portion is only 30 minutes of the day, anyway.)

Everything is included: food, alcohol, wetsuits, sunscreen, etc etc.

The best part: NOT CROWDED. if you want a relaxing, peaceful experience, this is it. It’s NOT your typical “water park.” Fun to see the live animals and swim with the fish.

Lots of opportunities for old-school Florida exploration. Camping, hiking and bird watching are abundant here. Spend an hour or a few days. The general store has lots of supplies, including kayak and canoe rentals.

Make sure you bring the bug spray though. The funky statue from the 1940’s is worth the price of admission (five bucks per carload).

This is an amazing spot... even better because you can only get there by boat. Which means FEW people. If you can manage to get your boat grounded and get out for a walk, it’s beautiful.

There is a narrow shoreline for walking, and lots of bugs (bring the bug spray) but the treasures abound if you look for them. Worth a trip over!

Beautiful place to escape the busy city. Plenty of parking and picnic spots. A nice treat: a bit of elevation within the park to offer some great water views. A nice surprise for someone who thinks of Florida as completely flat. There are lots of trees, shaded areas and spots to escape the crowds as well.

Modern with great views. There are informative displays inside, then you can take in the views from the upper levels, or walk outside along the trails.

Bring a bathing suit, you can go down to the water line and take a dip. Lots of shaded parking and restroom facilities as well.

Spectacular, this is real Florida. For only $4.50 per person, you get clear, calm, serene water. A great place to launch a boat or kayak. A little history of the Overseas Highway (walk up on the railroad trestle bridge). Incredible views. Completely worth it.

Having DJ'ed many weddings here, I can tell you it is one of the most picturesque reception spots in Central Florida. The Rose garden is a perfect spot for a ceremony, and the climate-controlled ballroom is just what you need for the reception that follows.

I hiked the Grandfather Mountain Trail going in on McCray and back on Underwood. It is definitely not for beginner hikers, or those who are afraid of heights. It also helps to have confidence with rock scrambling. Reaon being there are many ladders to climb that are on an open mountain face. One ladder feels it is half off the mountain, and you are high in the air and cannot avoid looking down to climb it. The top of one ladder leads onto a ledge with a tether to shimmy across, from there you scramble over a few rocks on the mountain face to a second ladder (the aforementioned half off the mountain ladder). The top of that takes you to a sharp right turn and more rock scrambling. This is the hardest part of the McCray trail, and I highly suggest if you do this trail to ascend this path and decend the Underwood if you want to do a loop. If you do not want to loop (and do a in and out hike instead) and want an easier ascent then go up Underwood and not McCray. For experienced hikers this hike is a thrill and a half!! This is the most from trail i have ever done!

GOOGLE MAPS WILL NOT GET YOU HERE! you can follow Google maps to a point: if you try to follow all Google maps direction you will turn onto a bridge with a sign that says "No access to Mingo Falls". If you try to continue down that road you will encounter a dead end one lane road through residential area. Turn around at the end of the bridge and when crossing back you will see a sign pointing further up the road. Follow the road signs to Mingo Falls and you will have no problem getting there. Once their the hardest part of the trail is the stairs at the very beginning. Once you've passed that point its a quick easy stroll to the falls, which are much bigger and more impressive than photos can capture!

So much fun! 11 zip lines, a swinging India Jones type bridge, and three rappels! The rappel is more akin to descending on a auto belay. Danny and Tersha (I believe that was her name I'm so sorry if I misremembered!) were absolutely amazing and made the trip even better! The braking system is awesome and doesnt bring you to a crazy hard stop. They also have a new system that can bring you to the platform if you dont make it all the way across, rather than pulling yourself in. Great for families and a great day trip from Asheville!

This was a great trip to The Everglades! The airboat ride was 28 dollars, and lasted about 30-40 minutes. We saw several alligators on the airboat. The guide stopped several times to explain to use what the wildlife was. After the airboat ride is a short little alligator show, where the tour guide explains several different attributes of the alligator. Afterwords, you have the option to pay 3 dollars cash to hold a baby alligator and get a photo. All in all a fun way to spend a few hours!

I loved this park! I went down with my boyfriend to watch the total eclipse, and LOTS of other people had the same idea. The small state park did it's best to deal with the huge amounts of people, and they did pretty well. The grounds were so well taken care of, and the piers were good for fishing. They also had kayak rentals, and they were higher quality kayaks. The lake is beautiful and the rental cabins are beautiful as well.

LOVE THIS PLACE!!!!!!! heres a few tips to start: 1. if you want to fly down the slides incredibly fast wear exercise pants; 2. Buy knee pads at the gift shop or bring them if you're planning on crawling in the metal tunnels (I still have bruises 2 days later on my knees) 3. Just run around and go crazy! Good for a quick walk-thru, and it's free! My only complaints is they close year round at 5pm, and the information on Charles Lindburg is just newspaper posters placed outside the bathroom. I hope the new area being added onto will have more about him! Also a shout out to Johnathan in the gift shop for the above and beyond friendly service and the great suggestions for sites to see during our stay. Kudos to you, and thank you!

I've camped several times in this forest, both on primitive campgrounds and dispersion camping. The forests are beautiful, and the rangers are friendly and helpful. For dispersion camping there are some regulations you need to follow. There are black bears reported in the area however we have not seen or encountered any problems from them. These forests are beautiful to both drive through and camp in.

Absolutley beautiful! Gorgeous gardens! Go in the morning when it opens over the summer so you dont feel like you're going to die from the heat. The swamp tours are really cool. There are alligators everywhere in the water, so keep you're eyes open and you'll see them. Go in April to see azaleas and all the flowers in bloom! Also a great place to get engagement or wedding photos.

The SkyWheel is an iconic image for Myrtle Beach. The tickets are on the expensive side, however it is fun to ride. I suggest riding during the day, not at night, so you can see more of Myrtle Beach. I rode at night and didnt get to see very much. The wheel is very pretty to see at night on the beach, it is light up and very pretty.

Awesome State Park  very beautiful area centered around the Blackwater river which has many small sandy beach areas to play, swim or just relax on. The park has many nice walking trails of Various lengths and all showcase the natural beauty of this park.
A canoe outfitter is just minutes from the park entrance where you can rent a kayak or canoe and they will shuttle you up river for Various length paddle trips. Also if you have your own kayak or canoe they will shuttle you to a put in spot and you can leave your vehicle at the take out location.
I can't begin to tell you how clean and well maintained this State Park is in every respect and the Host, Rangers and Staff are helpful, knowledgeable and friendly.
Campground has two loops, one with a large children's playground also a great shower house with restrooms which are kept clean at all times.
The campsites are of good size with pea gravel base each site has water, electric, sewer, clothesline, firepit and picnic table so come and enjoy another wonderful Florida State Park I'm sure you'll be pleasantly surprised.

This is a beautiful area to hike to and from with a slight climb up ridge returning to Collins Gulf main trail.
I will throw this cautionary statement in for those who maybe sight impaired, knee, hip or balance issues this may not be a hike for you.
As you descend ridge trail becomes very rocky with many roots with uneven footing most of the walk.
Once in the Falls area its a wonderful bluff with lush Mountain plants and beautiful rock formations. A great place to stop contemplate life and enjoy the cool air provided. As you know the Falls size depends on rain fall recently, it was minimal  day I visited but the beauty of this area makes this a worthy place to visit. Also there is a nice paved parking area with map of Collins Gulf area before departing parking area, trail is marked well both ways.
So if Falls hiking is your thing add this 1 to your list I'm sure you'll enjoy.

Hey Veterans and those interested in military and Carrabelle Island history this museum would be well worth your time to visit.
You will find it very informative on Camp Gordon Johnson military training camp about the training, history and a few of those who were stationed there.
They have many period items like weapons, uniforms, personal living quarters and much more and alot of their items are from the Camp itself.
It may look small on the outside but it is big on information on the inside and the price is right too!
It's Free to go through museum you may like to leave a donation on your way out to help support their efforts.
They have many more Camp G. J. Training camp items/artifacts yet to display but are in the works for the future.
So take a break get out and stretch the ole legs a while and take a tour thru history.

Great place to get into the outdoors whither for a few hours, day or weekend plenty of hiking trails, fishing opportunities and camping.
I fished Bear Lake and had a great time there the camp ground has Rv sites with electric and water the tent camping area has water and the sites are spacious some on the water.
Very nice bathroom's with shower in each individual bathroom and from what I could see on two day trips I made they were clean and well maintained.
So grab the family pack a picnic and head on over do a little bike riding, fishing, hiking or just relax a while you'll be glad you did.

If you're traveling in the St. Augustine area and enjoy seeing Lighthouses this one is well worth the time to visit. The surrounding, grounds, buildings and lighthouse have been maintained as if the lighthouse Keepers were still on the premises. Lots of historical items,  records, tools used by the lighthouse Keepers are still on site. Admission is very reasonable and the view from top of lighthouse is breathtaking of coastline and old St. Augustine so stop in and I'm sure you'll be pleasantly satisfied.

Good place for a day, weekend or vacation this park has cabins, camping and Resort rooms many many things to do while visiting like golf, fishing, kayaking, swimming, camping, hiking site seeing and much more.

The Park also has a visitor center, swimming pool, grill, general store, outfitters store and Resort Lodge with restaurant.

I would have given a better rating except that the Craven House was closed to viewing due to the Covid-19 issue.
I do plan on returning in the future and also there were a couple of trails accessible from the parking lot.

nearly on the water, plenty of trails to walk, canoe and kayak rental, picnic and swimming area. Not to mention the white squirrels appear daily to view along with other birds and wildlife in the forest.

Hey let me say that this is a wonderful place to camp, hike, trail ride, picnicking and visit the museum. There are plenty of things in the area as well to see and visit.

Plenty of places to eat locally all just a short drive away there's something for the whole family here or close by its worth a visit.

Crooked River Lighthouse is well worth the time to visit and take in the museum and a trip to the top of  lighthouse all for a meager some of $5 what a bargain.
The views from top of lighthouse on a nice day a beautiful of Carrabelle and Dog Island area.
So pull off the road and stretch your legs a while take in this historical landmark and I'm sure you'll be pleasantly surprised.

Museum is full of tools, weapons, books, treasure, artifacts, clothing and much much more to entertain and improve your knowledge of that era.
Also there is a real live pirate to take you thru museum and explain in more detail about artifacts on hand and pirating lore of that time.
You can go through museum at your own pace for there is plenty to see and learn about.

It's a good place to get in the outdoors and enjoy life hook line and sinker with many things to see and do like walking on the beach, riding bicycles, looking for shells, fishing, swimming, camping and boating of all types.
So pay them a visit and I'm sure you'll find something interesting whither it's a few hours or a few days pay them a visit and enjoy life .

Great state park to visit for fishing, swimming, camping, hiking, kayaking, and they have a great marina as well.
Many fishing docks and piers to choose from  for children, handicapped or adults to enjoy.
Many picnic tables with grills and so just tables to enjoy a meal so bring the family and enjoy this great state park I'm sure you'll be surprised.

We stayed 12 day and found this park to be a 5 star facility. Extremely nice and well spaced camp sites with 8 or 10 along lake shore. Good walking trails along lake and ridge also restroom and shower facilities are well kept and are kept very clean.
Camp host are always willing to help visitors.
Great place to visit enjoy outdoors and fish.

Great place for a picnic, fishing trip, kayaking, canoeing bird watching or sun bathing they have a two lane boat launch its wide enough for a big boat too. Lots of parking for vehicles and vehicles with boat trailers they have a public restroom as well so stop by check it out and I'm sure you'll be pleasantly satisfied.

Great place to hike out to see the beautiful stone formations, climbing, photography or a picnic. Trial is moderate to easy and the first third is paved its 1 mile from trailhead to Stone Door. Also while in this area take in Laural Falls too it's less than a quarter mile from trailhead and very worth the walk.

Excellent museum on railroad history in  and around Etowah Tn. very informative with many photographs and displays. Nice gift shop and you can buy tickets for a train ride as well. So stop by and pay them a visit and I'm sure you'll be pleasantly surprised.

Navarre Beach is well worth a visit plenty of restrooms, showers, fishing pier, pavilions and beautiful white sand to play in or just take a long walk on and look for seashells or enjoy a sunset. Stop by and check it out a while I'm sure you'll be pleased.

Great place to go for a ride, camping, hiking, biking, swimming, fishing or just plain relaxing so grab the family and get outdoors in the Yellow River Wma.
I'm sure you'll be pleasantly surprised at what you can see.

Navarre beach is a good place to go for a day or a few hours on the beach plenty of parking with restrooms, showers, pier and pavilions.
Great place to play, picnic, relax or just stroll along the beach.
Excellent park showing respect for our Veterans present and past with several memorials to our soldiers. I suggest every patriot stop by and pay a visit I'm sure you'll come away pleasantly pleased.
Get place to spend a few hours, day or weekend camping, hiking, kayaking, canoeing, swimming, fishing or photography pay this area a visit and I'm sure you'll come back many times over the years.
Most camp sites are close to each other with maybe a 5 or 6ft. buffer between sites and facilities there are dated and well worn but clean. Don't expect alot and you'll have a great visit.
Very nice park with picnic tables, boat launch camping sites, shelters and restrooms. Take time to visit and enjoy a picnic lunch there your sure to enjoy.
Hey it's 5 star come visit this beautiful park directly on the Suwannee river and expect to have a great day.

Awesome place to learn about space programs and rocket. Our son loved this place. I wish we had more time. We spent lot of time in queue for bus tour. It was busy weekend else one day is enough to explore this place. This entire facility is run using entry fee paid by customers and none of the taxpayers money is used. You can buy tickets online or at gate. At gates you can buy tickets at kiosk which was a breeze. Food there is typical amusement park food. Getting into parking took a lot of time. Google maps sent us to back entrance which is only for employees. So ignore your gps once you get close and just follow their signs. I would like to come back when there would be a launch. We also saw lot of wildlife around.

Very beautiful trail and must visit if you visit Everglades. If you have limited time and get a good view of Everglades then just do this one trail and you should be good. Saw 5 alligators and ton of anhinga birds and turtles and gars in the water. Saw one anhinga try to eat a fish which was too big for him. It was funny to watch this bird trying to gulp a big fish. Lose lose situation for both because there was no way this fish would fit this birds throat but it won’t let the fish go. This place has very scenic views and you can literally see most of the wild species found in Everglades. I would recommend spending more time on south side of Everglades park than the north side.

Meh. I guess I had high expectation from air boat ride. It was quick ride. We did see few alligators but saw more just walking on trails inside the Everglades park on south side. We did see a snake which seemed staged but I may be wrong. The boat ride itself was just okay. Most of these boat ride companies are only allowed to operate in specific lane/area which is a good thing. Less disruption to wildlife and habitat. If you are looking to see wildlife just take shark valley tram tour or just walk the trails.

P.S. just read the responses from owner to all one start reviews. It’s hilarious to see how they are blaming customers for everything 😄.

Great place for kids. Lots of activities for kids and adults. There is a small zoo and petting area. Looks like they are expanding so get more animals soon. Aquarium is small but decent. You can touch rays swimming around. There are puzzles which are fun to solve. There is a kids play area which is great for kids under 8. The shows are okay and need some upgrades. It’s wasn’t dark enough for black hole show. Parking was okay when we went during thanksgiving weekend. Food is typical. Expensive and meh.
dislikes: Insufficient darkness in black hole show

reviews_attraction.text: Best fireworks and shows ever. You have to stay late to see the fireworks and show but it’s totally worth the wait. After thanksgiving they do this every night until new year. There are always thousands of people here so try to come here an hr early and find good place to sit and relax. Some kids will just go to sleep because most of them would be super tired. Let them sleep until the show starts. Good way to get some rest and relax before last leg of your trip.

This is amazing show. Interactive and always fun no matter how many times you watch it. Kids in front have most fun so if you want your kids to participate in parts of show then try to sit in front. Cast will give your kids small role to play when show starts. Most of the kids in front ends up joining in the beginning of the show. Show has ton of space so you usually don’t need a fast pass unless you are visiting peak season like Christmas time.

Great place to spend few hrs on the way to key west. The beach has lot of sea grass but it’s part of natural habitat. The water is very clear and looks green which is beautiful. Water is shallow in many places so you can literally walk 50-100 feet in water and water would still be below your knees. Ton of parking available. There is a place to rent kayaks. Place to get snacks and sandwiches. You can walk up to old bridge and see the sunset.

Great place. Turn on some holiday music, relax and enjoy awesome holiday lighting. It’s about 5 miles of drive. You don’t have to get out of the car unless you want to spend time at gift shop. The line until the ticket counter was very long and took us almost 40 mins to get to counter. After ticket counter it’s non stop drive of about 5 miles inside park. Lot of good decorations. Our son had fun listening to music and watching the lights.

I had very high hopes but were shattered once the ride started. The chairs are not comfortable and 4 D effect makes sitting in those rock hard chair makes the experience unpleasant. Random jerks and shaking which does not synchronize with the show. Luckily the wait was not bad. We were in line for 15-20 mins they express line. I would skip this ride unless you have lot of time to kill.

Most happening place during sun set. There were 100s of people gathered here. Local artists showing their skills and people watching sun set in the ocean. Various places to grab snacks. It was partially sunny day and we were not sure if we will get to see the sunset but it was beautiful. We didn’t see the sun go all the way down because of clouds but it turned the sky all orange.

This is good little ride. Little bit of educational and fun. Lot of information about growing fruits and vegetables in innovative way. They use lot of vegetables and fish grown here in  restaurants inside Disney. We have done this multiple times and never gets boring. There is always long line here for some reason. I am guessing it’s because of soaring next door.

Really good ride and worth the 1 hr wait thru express line. I don’t know how people stand in regular line for any of the rides. None of them are good for long wait time. Almost half the population has express pass. So it’s not really express. Ride itself has nice visuals and enough attention to details. But it’s not the best ride in town or even in the park.

Beautiful scenery. We didn’t plan to stop but since the blue ridge parkway was closed right at this point we pulled over to figure out next place to go. Ended up hiking to overlook which was beautiful. Our son didn’t like climbing up or down because of mud. Not too many people on the trail. Didn’t see anyone while going up. Saw a couple while coming down.

It’s about 1.5 miles from blue ridge parkway. There are multiple trails to view the fall. We took Erwins view trail. There are multiple points where you can see upper side of the falls and go to chimney view for gorgeous view of the full fall. The climb is not crazy. Best views are from chimney view unless you want to climb further.

It’s a 4D experience and our son did not like it. We enjoyed it and think it’s a great show. Don’t waste your fast pass on this one unless you can’t find anything else available. The standby line is fun. It goes thru the tree and has animals and other creatures carved out through out the way to the show.

Great museum and it’s free. We spent about 30 mins learning about minerals and history of minerals found in NC. Staff here was very helpful. The parkway was closed in multiple places and we didn’t know why. She explained what was going on and showed us options. There were restrooms which were clean.

It’s a good ride and everyone should do it once but that about it. You can see most of the animals in your local zoo so don’t stand in line for hrs. Yes people stand in line for couple of hrs. If you have fast pass then do it. There are much better places in park to use your fast pass.

Must see show in Disney. This is one of the best visuals in Disney hands down. My wife thought the stage during the show was real. We had to go back to show her that it was 3D projection. There are 3 short stories and all of them are really good.

Fun ride and little bit of intense for toddlers. This was our sons first roller coaster and he did not like it the first time but now he loves it. Easy to get fast pass even during peak season. It ends quick but lot of fun.

This is hands down best ride in the park. We did it twice. Amazing visuals effects and synchronization. You really feel that you are in the movie. This ride does come close to some of the best rides in town.

Most underrated ride in this park. There was no line when we went there. It was during Christmas time when Park was packed. Frozen ride next door was crazy packed. But this one is better. It’s boat ride.
Ton of fun activities for kids and adults. You can spend hrs here. We went there in the morning and stepped out for lunch and came back and spent the afternoon too.
One of the older rides. It’s decent but not worth trying if you have limited time. Shoot aliens while driving thru the city. Fun but not that amazing.
Another time filler ride. It’s easy to get fast pass for this one. Typical ride which you will find in any park. So nothing fancy.
Great place for kids. Has a little playground. Plenty of space to walk around. Great view of water and city.

Its a decent place for kids and to learn, very educational. Staff is nice and friendly, they feed the animals in front of you and give you an interesting talk. It gets kind of crowded and hot, the space its extremely small for people to walk around and bump into each other. They definitely should have capacity control by certain hours. The place takes like at least one hour and a half to just see and walk around. So capacity control could be worked out in order to enjoy it more. It was extremely uncomfortable with so much people this is the only overwhelming compliant and the stars I didnt rate. Other than this its a cute and small place I would recommend, its worth it to learn and see the care these people are giving to perserve the environment with so little resources. The price its worth but it should stay that way unless more things are added and its ok. The turtle hospital should have a tour guide to explain more about what they do there, maybe I missed the tour idk. Dont miss the free donation bird sanctuary in your left side before entering the marine center.
dislikes: Missing tour guide at turtle hospital

reviews_attraction.text: This place its not bad but its really not good on rainy days. Its fantastic on sunny days and less crowded days. Ive been here five times and this last time was the worst. The times ive been here before has been very enjoybale. I gave it two stars this time because we didnt get to see the little mermaid show, it was cancelled twice due to rain and thunderstorms. Also the one show fish tail was so uunorganized  and idk wth they did but those mermaids were off way off. Two of them were ok but one of them was either a rookie or was totally lost. The show was very short and hurried. The boat tour was fun and faster because they did two boats but the spider monkeys are no longer available to see...i was disappointed. Since all was cancelled everyone decided to eat so we had to basically eat standing up. If it werent for the two hour drive and the low price i wouldn't even bother. I dont think I will go again in summer time maybe in off tourist season.

Nice place to spend rainy days in and interesting unique artifacts. You will really enjoy it if you like US history, antiques, cars, collectors, music. I learned a lot here. Beware that if you are offended by politics certain history artifacts from the south then you may not enjoy this place. Its clean and very organized. Kids ages 5 and up will love this place. Not very enjoyable for babys or toodlers since lots of things are not allowed to be touched. This place has things ive never seen before. I really loved it! The three stars its because its very tempting for kids to touch and most its untouchable items, otherwise its very enjoyable. Staff is friendly and helpful!

I love to go places in florida and this was one of my options...not anymore after reading so many complaints about the rules, private property and rude service. I see since its owned by private owner property they dont care about the reviews they dont loose anything. You can tell because they dont even reply or apologize to the ratings not even to reply a five star comment. Believe me this is not the only place on earth with a diving sinkhole, USA has many many and much more beautiful places to see and offer great services and smiles. If they think they are the last coca cola in the desert, they are wrong cause their is always Pepsi baby!

The beach is cute small and private although it was super crowded, can become uncomfortable and the bathrooms are disgusting...be ready to pee in a cup because those bathrooms are horrible. Its not even a bathroom its a concrete portable with roaches and the stink of urine. The only reason I give it an extra star its because you can see beautiful nature and flora in the way to this beach and it looks different from other florida beaches the layout its like a little piece of beach but crowded on weekends and holidays may have to wait for capacity because its small. Get there early.

Nice place, it needs more shade, but the grounds are very clean and well kept, the staff is on the move and filtering the water of the splash area. Sanitation is constantly going on because staff is making sure park is safe. It's one of the best well kept parks I've seen in FL. It has many mini trucks to drink and eat from, it has a restaurant environmental friendly and people can take their pets. Kids love it, worth the visit to relax and have a great day in the park! The place has a nice museum next to it but it's optional if you want to visit.
likes: Mini trucks for food and drinks

reviews_attraction.text: Nice park, overly crowded when its the weekends but its a huge park so you will not feel cramped. I wish people would take better care of nature and their surroundings. Although the park has wild life, people throw a lot. of birthday parties and activities, resulting in throwing trash everywhere and not keeping it clean. The bathrooms are the only down thing that I dislike the most, not clean at all. The part itself is a nice open wide environment good for sports, activities and to have a nice family time.

Very big and well maintained. We loved it specially the butterfly forest. We didnt get to see the frogs i think it should be included in the admission. Which I think it was a bit too pricey maybe instead of twenty dollars...fifteen dollars would be more reasonable since the butterfly forest is small. Very educational and beautiful setting lots of info and hands on items. Best place so far ive seen that butterflies are well maintained and beautiful different and alot of them.

Not really worth going unless its winter time to see manatee. The center its lacking so much character, its kind of boring and needs more stuff for the summer. Lots of information but outdated center. I understand ita non profit and only by donations. The only interesting thing was a huge salt water fish tank. The marina is beautiful and i assume the sunset must be amazing...i will give it another try in winter time.

Extremely beautiful. Friendly staff in gift shop. The beach is breathtaking, not a place recommend to swim but more like to explore and walk along the shore of the rocks are amazing their formation its a one time experience with you are a florida explorer. The garden is beautiful but the pond was under construction hoping to go back and see the pond with koi fish.

Super cool place. Avoid crowded days because it can get uncomfortable. A pain to get parking. Take an uber if not too far, the gated parkings are expensive and all in pay park app. If you do not know how to use this system then better get an uber. The outside parking is cheaper. Food is pricey around town, it is a tourist area. It is free to enter.

A fun place to enjoy with the family. I noticed they add on some areas. I just think there was too much celebrities and less informative characters that kids can learn about. The president part was interesting, I don't think trump looks like trump at all and maybe they should put first ladies in there too of current and previous presidents.

Cute zoo with lots of shade. Not lots of animals to see but its not crowded in week days, has a lot of character and its well set up. Nice water splash area for kids and the groupon deal its very good. I gave it a three star because all the iguana and bird poop in the floor was so much. Otherwise it was a nice place to take the kids.

I think it was better than a lot of other kids museums ive been in florida. The tampa is also in my top list. Clean, cool stuff kids would hands on play with. Two outdoor playgrouds. Although its a crowded place in the weekend but its spacious. I would recommend a big cafeteria, that subway is small and it gets crowded.

Its ok but pricey for what it really is...also the maintenance of the animals are horrible. If you dont like to see animals with small space, its best not to go. The shows are worth it especially the birds show its awesome. It could be cleaner. The petting zoo is cool.

Completely amazing little place. Best to come early when place just opened that way the volunteer girls can be great help explaining the hands on water creatures for kids and everyone. It was a one on one experience. We loved it and the setting is cute.

It was great. Well kept clean grounds. Animals looked and acted happy. Playground its pretty cool. Feeding alligator. They need rhinos in there that wouldn't survive in the wild more like sanctuary animals, after a while its too much of the same thing.

Great place for kids to play and entertain themsleves. Very good for rainy days as well. Facility was clean, safe and fun for kids to play. Like that you can go eat something in the mall and come back again. The front young lady was very friendly!

Very nice place to visit when its not crowded. Its a cute short aquarium but with a lot of character and interesting sea life. Unfortunately because ofnthe virus some things don't have access for a while but still a nice place to take the kids.

Great warm clear water shallow waters. The algae is annoying and so is getting parking, but you can snorkel and have a nice, relaxing day in this place. It was not crowded although the parking seemed like it.

Amazing rock formations here in FL. Beautiful shaded tranquil nature walks and trails. Make sure to bring closed up water shoes because rocks are sharp. Loved this place and enjoyed it. Very clean and quiet.
Amazing place. I saw dolphins and some people said they saw sharks. Lots of wildlife and starfish. Great place for fishing, very busy in summer time and weekends.
very nice, clean, informative and things not even local Floridians knew about FL. Worth going and taking kids to learn about FL history. My kids loved it!
Cute place to take kids. Water was a rough but the ice cream snack and water play area for kids its enjoyable. Its clean and less crowded in week days.
Unbelievably awesome huge playground. We loved it! Needs more shade for kids in hot days but very clean and a world of wonder for all ages.

We camp here for the weekend. The hike to the falls is a good work out especially going back up. The waterfalls are beautiful and worth every sweat. Its not crowded during weekdays. Love to camp out again this fall.The staff are friendly. The rangers are helpful as well as the host of the camp ground. Trails are marked. The steps going down to the waterfalls i think is more than seven hundred. All in all we did enjoy our stay here.

This is awesome place. We launch our kayak near Roger park and paddle upstream
I highly recommend if you have your own kayak just go straight to Rogers Park or some marina there cause too slim chance that they will let you launch in the statepark.  Still worth it. Its about 2.5 hours paddle upstream to the state park . We enjoyed the water. Highly recommended and worth the drive.

This place is traffic despite ample amount of parking area. Its a steep hike on a pave road going up but worths the pain. There are benches along the way to sit and rest. Its a half mile trail. We will come back again when the sky is clear to enjoy the amazing view surrounding the dome. Clouds stayed with us during our visit so we have a good reason to come back.

This place is well maintained. When in Austin, this is nice place for a walk, just few blocks away from all the good food places of Austin. The gift shop has plenty to offer. Staff are friendly. Best time to come is during after office less traffic. But if you want to see the inside of this place, be there during office hours.

One of most amazing waterfalls in Tennessee. Its a short easy hike from the state park office to the overlook. Permit is needed to hike the gorge. This place has a trails for hiking. Park office has restroom. Staff was helpful.it was not crowded when we came due to cold weather but we still enjoy the park for ourselves.

One of my favorite light house in Florida. The place is well maintained. Staff are friendly. Souvenier shops has plenty of stuff to break the bank account. The view on the top is amazing. Ifs not an easy climb. Parking is not much. Gets crowded because its popular. We enjoyed walking aroung the vicinity.

Crystal clear water. Be early because line is so long. Nice place to kayak. The rock spring run has gators. Its almost 8.5 miles from Wekiva Spring to the back park of Kelly Park one way. No shuttle bus to go back to Wekiva. Bring enough water and food of course courage to paddle with gators.

This is a pretty neat place and less crowded. Lots of stone formations inside the cave. Its also cold inside and some areas are wet like any other caverns. Tour guide is knowledgeable. The staff are friendly. If youre near here and visiting, its worth to drop by and visit this caverns.

This is such a pretty place and not crowded. Although the light house is closed but the drive is worth. Tons of wildlife can be seen here. Gators and different kinds of birds. Theres places that you can launch your kayak too. Very serene . Its a photographers paradise.

This is a very beautiful lighthouse and the garden around it is very well maintained the staff are very friendly and excellent. We kayak the river too and the view from there is amazing. Jupiter Florida is very lucky to have this awesome lighthouse.

Though there was no swimming allowed due to some alligators hanging in the river... well its Florida.  Still i enjoy my visit here. Kayaking here is fun. Seen manatees huge fishes , birds and gators.  Hope one day they will let people swim...

We enjoyed the beauty of this park. We started from the Arc Rock, Sugar Loaf rock, point look out and the cemetery. It was a good hike. We did self guided tour. The view on the top is breath taking. Well maintained park and clean restrooms.

Perfect place for family vacation. Nice trails to hike. Amazing view of the mountain. Waterfalls and rivers nearby. The downtown area is boasting with restaurants and stores. There are nice places to stay. Very relaxing place.

We passed by here and was amazed with the view. I cant wait to go home this fall so we can hike the trail to the waterfalls. The state park shop has plenty of souveniers with friendly staff. We will surely comeback.

This is also an easy hike or i can say its good for our beloved elderly family. Tends to become crowded during summer months amd parking will be an issue so come early.  Also come after a couple of rain.
One of my favorite light house in Florida. Fabulous beach too. Staff are friendly. Its a good place to spend with your family. Cheap entrance fee to spend a wonderful day. Hope to come back again.
Miles of hiking trails. Beautiful waterfalls. Area is crowded on summertime. Popular among locals and people from out of town. Camping sites available. Cant wait to come back on the fall.
Kayaking here is fun . We came here on a weekdays and place is quiet and serene. Lots of birds around. We paddle to the small islands and eat our lunch there. We had great time.
We hike this place on a very hot day. But the reward is vibrant colors of the canyon. Every sweat is worth for the amazing view. Will come bqck this coming fall.
This an easy hike with the kiddos. Just short distance from the parking lot.  Better come.on a weekdays after couple of days rain. Great place for the family.
This is another option to launch your kayak to paddle upstream to Weeki Wachi State Park. Parking is an issue so come early. Tend to be crowded on weekends.
Amazing place to visit especially in the fall. Friendly staff. Awesone place to hike up to the top. The view is beautiful. Coming back again this fall.
Its a nice place to.spend the day picnic. It was bit cold when we visited this place so i keep away from the water. Nice view of Lake Erie.
Staff are friendly .. nice place to stay but they have seaweeds/grass problem when we came and stay there. Load of manatees in the lagoon.
One of my favorite place in Georgia. Its crowded on the summer but super perfect scenery on the fall. We will.be back again fall season

We had a few hours to kill and decided to hit the Lighthouse.   Neat history walk and the grounds have been kept up nicely.  Not really onto old lighthouse lore, but always worth checking out what times were like.  They are several good side stories throughout the self guided tour.  The climb to the top of the lighthouse was the highlight.  Breathtaking view  of the surrounding area.  You could make this a 39 minute tour or leisurely stroll your way though the area.  It was worth it and the kids would enjoy the climb up the endless stairs.  Older folks may not however so be careful.

We had a great time exploring from the car.  We have been touring Iowa and her State Parks this year.  We will be back to the cabins or the resort here soon.  Would like to get some fishing done here and there looks to be a lot of choices for boats ramps and shore fishing alike.  The shelters were all well kept and the fall foliage was breath taking.  We took a short drive through the camp grounds and they looked very nice as well.  Not far off the beaten path and there are hiking trails and things to explore that I plan to come back and see.

Red Haw was a destination for us on our State Parks of Iowa tour.  I was amazed at the opportunities here.  We are earmarking next summers places we want to return to as the weather turned cold.  This was definitely a great fall tour if you are looking for fall foliage color.  Large bluegill and ice fishing caught my attention as well  What a great place to camp and small enough you can walk the entire trail.

Great place to visit for the family or for baseball lovers.  This place was a bucket list item visit for many reasons.  Just walking in the outfield and walking the base paths made the trip worth it.  Mt dad has been gone for 27 years and would have given anything to watch him come out of the corn.  Corny yep but the place brings that out.  Easy to find on Google maps and town has a great diner.

This was a nice park.  We had this point on our day trip to see if we would like to come back and camp or fish.  Well I was without my gear and the fish were jumping and it was an excellent fall day.  My loss, but we walked a while and enjoyed the leaves changing and watching the water.  Had a great shelter that would be a great place for a get together woth a bigger family.  Will be back.

Nice little park.  Wish the Interpretive Center was open....damn COVID.  We enjoyed walking a bit and seeing the buffalo and elk was an added bonus.  The Playscape area would be a neat place for kids to interact.  There is a little lake further in the park and has some good fishing in the spring.   Nice places for picnics and get togethers in the shelters as well.

I have to tell you this place was a flashback to 45 years ago for me.  Funny seeing a majority of the characters from my childhood still relevant today.  No cancel culture here.  We even got om the kiddie roller coaster just to say we did.   Can't wait to bring the grandkids back here at some point.  I know now how to get to Sesame Street.

Nice diversion today.   Nice walk through farming history and a little something for everyone.   We did not stay for the Oldies Ballgame but watched a bit.  Easy walk and fun tractor ride back in time.  Little ones will have fun but strollers may be a bit hard to get around.  People had them but they had them there.  Will be back.

Nice little park tucked back off the mad and hustling highway.   We stopped to eat lunch and this spot popped up on Google.  Birds and ducks were flying around and made it enjoyable.  Has a handicapped pad for those that need on e to park and get out.  6 or 7 tables around the park and only one did not have a water view.

Best $6 spent on our vacation so far.  We saw a lot of manatees and other wild life Friday.  Nice walk and would do this again.  It was not too crowded and we got there a little after 10 am.  Cool and rainy, but a sweatshirt did the trick.  Go....you will not be disappointed.

Knoxville is an interesting place.  Races and lots of Iowa scenery.  We visited Young's Park to see the Freedom Rock.  Was not disappointed.  All these rocks bring us to places we have not visited before and we discover lots of new things.  Iowa is a great place to discover.

Great history here.  You can bring the family and learn a little bit and look out over the bluff to see a large part of the Iowa and Nebraska areas.  There is enough room to social distance and there are a few picnic table set up to enjoy some family time.  Awesome place.

Mahatma County Freedom Rock is another patriotic work of art by Bubba Sorenson.  We have visited several and each pays tribute to local heroes.  Small town Iowa and the heartland is America.  These rocks remind us of the sacrifices made to make our country great.

Another Iowa State park hidden gem.  Beautiful bike trails and picnic areas.  Swimming beach is nice as well.  No life guard so you are on your own.  Fishing will be good early and late afternoon.  Great place to put a boat in and enjoy the day.  Will be back.

What an awesome time for free.  We walked down the board walk and watched people fish for about an hour.   Very cool just watching and enjoying the breeze and people watching.  Well worth a visit and Joe's Crab Shack is located at the pier as well.

Water levels have been lowered and the lake is dirty and I was astonished at the amount of junk in the water.  I think when water levels are raised and you can see infrastructure laid waste in the water, this could be a nice fishing hole.

Nice State Park along the Raccoon River.   You can picnic or hangout.  Big lodge if you have a big occasion tocelebrate.  The bird blind was amazing.  Closed because of COVID,  but if you stay quiet and still the birds will come.

It's a small park but nice.  It's probably a nice park to bring a dog for a walk, there are benches.  Bring water, I'm not sure I remembered seeing a water fountain, and there weren't any restrooms.  Also it's a little tricky to get to in a way, because there is no car entrance off of gulf to bay - you have to turn down S. Bayview then turn on CR 31.  It's literally the only road(s).  If you know this, it's not difficult - someone had said that in a post.  Also, I noticed a post about the path not making sense - they weren't going to plow over the 100 year old trees to make a certain type of path - the whole reason of creating this park was to preserve one of the oldest and historic sites in Pinellas. I would say that, yes, if you take the south trail to the end, I could imagine that there may be people hanging out under the bridge, so I would just be mindful - that happens at many bridges, all over, not just here.

I was on my way to visit a friend in Indiana (first time in the state), and saw a sign stating 'historic district', and anything with the word historic is an immediate hard stop for me - usually when I pull off to follow those signs it's a historic marker or museum, or roadside plaque, etc. - so it's always a pleasant surprise when it's something more than that - and in this case I was floored, what a absolute gem of a place this is tucked away.  I hadn't heard of it prior, or I would have certainly planned it out to visit. I wish I had more time to walk around and visit each of the shops and grab something to eat, etc.  I did take a good amount of pictures that came out beautiful.  The folks who live here live in a beautiful town.  I plan on visiting again for sure, hands down.

Really interesting 'hidden' gem.  Probably a good thing it's off in the cut, seeing as how it's been sized down over time to the smaller land it's on now, which is now protected by the state.  It's a really big temple mound, we have a large on in Safety Harbor, but you feel the climb going up the stairs, and when you are up there looking down you realize how high up you are.  vegetation has started to reclaim it's land, so it's thick to see through - but you can easily tell how high up you are.  There's a smaller mound which I didn't even realize was a mound until the little sign stated the mound on my right.
likes: Activities: Climbing stairs, viewing from height
dislikes: Cultural Value: Smaller, less noticeable mounds

reviews_attraction.text: I love this building, it's sort of like a crown jewel of of the county, not just the actual building itself but the grounds around it as well, the walkways are lined with little circular plaques with the family names of the founding families of the area.  The Pasco County historical marker is located on the grounds, and the court area around the fountain is a nice place to sit on a nice day, I saw multiple people last time I was there who had their kids there playing.

What a cool place to visit, I had no idea that this was here until recently while watching Adam The Woo's channel on YouTube, I've driven past Clermont before but not north / south, and had never heard of this place, but I'm glad I stopped by and went to the top.  I love the old roadside attraction relics that are still left, if you are in the area I think it's a must visit for sure.

I visited this park for the first time a few weekends ago, seems like a nice park for cookouts, each of the pavilions was full with groups, there's a little workout area, two lakes, one of which looks like you can fish from - the monuments to the military are cool to see as well.  There's an opening out to the sidewalk access by 19/49th street if you're on foot.

One of the nicer State parks I've been to in Florida, I visited here long ago in 2003, the first time that I was in the Keys, I remember most of it though some things have changed slightly due to the hurricane and restructuring, but it's still great for a walk, for some awesome pictures, swimming and boating as well.

A very beautifully done statue of an icon, stands out right away in the middle of the park even from the street parking.  I previously had no idea it existed but was glad to have seen it, it's a great starting point to any other community who might be thinking of possible ways to celebrate their local legends.

This is a great area for a few reasons, clearly the Arch itself but, also just to walk for exercise, there are benches, the waterfront is right there to enjoy, maybe just sit and watch the Mississippi River, take some pictures, things are right there in walking distance like other landmarks and things to eat.

This is a unique park that stretches in a narrow width from the shores of one lake to another lake across a few roads, there's a playground with benches in one area, and open fields with trees for the bulk of the other parts.  There is a historical marker located on one end for the Acton Community.

A nice traditional old style town square Park, there's Historical Markers located there as well as various other monuments from various time periods which offered local history and info.  It was quiet while I was there on a Saturday afternoon, nice park all around it seemed.

What an awesome park, the spring running through it is great, it's right on the waterfront of the river which is awesome, and there's rec areas for kids, picnic tables, looked like a good amount of parking, and the park was super clean and well kept.

This place is great, I like when counties put effort in to restoring historic buildings, and move them to a central location rather than let them be demolished.  It's a nice setup here adjacent to a park, great photography opportunities.

What a cool little gem of a 'park inside a park' almost.  Really cool to see.  It's always fun to learn / remember just where we were as a nation / world around those times that we had things like secret missiles hidden in the swamps.
