They run underground as soon as you approach so hard to get a picture. I also saw raccoon, iguana, squirrel, cruly tail lizards, and snakes all around. The shaded trees kept it cool on a hot day. I was even able to geocache. Loving this park. Will certainly be back. Rock the park

Awesome place to visit. The authentic history here is a must visit. The tour guide was very knowledgeable, and could answer a lot of questions. There are some monkeys in the tree and were able to view two of them. Also saw the largest iguana I have ever seen. The house and painting were intriguing. I would certainly encourage everyone to do this tour to learn more about the early life in Florida.

Really enjoyed this drive. Has been on my list of stuff to do in Dade county. The road was dusty and bumpy but very manageable. Any vehicle can drive on it. It was a cool day, so stopped a lot along the way and got out and take in nature. There was a lot of alligator to see and do much birds. Will do one of the trails the next time I am here. Worth the drive.

I have wanted to make it to this park and was not disappoint. Surprise that there is somewhere like this in the midst of an urban area. There is limited parking. Walking on the path was like walking in a mini forest. There was the sound of birds everywhere. I also heard but didn't see a real loud Woodpecker. I will certainly be back.

Thoroughly enjoyed this park. It was a cool day that I went here. They had a little flea market going on when I was there and had some unique stuff. The grounds were immaculate. Would have loved to come when they had a tour, however the signage was good enough. Would certainly go back. The company was great.

Visited here for the first Pre Basel African American Jazz and BBQ festival. To say that this was a blast is an understatement. The performances were great, the food was great and the art work on display was awesome. This will be an annual event for my family and myself to attend in the future.

I only drove here to pick up a geocache and do a quick check out of the place. What a drive to get to this place. It was long, but for me enjoyable. This is really what Florida use to look like. Can't wait to come back and spend a night camping here.

Love taking friends here when they visit from out of town. They are always amazed with the artwork, eatery and music festival that may be happening. I love that the art is always changing. As I always have out of towners I will certainly be back.

Stop on the tamiami road. At the time I went there building was closed but there was much to see. There is a fenced in area with a lot of alligator and also a boardwalk to view even more alligators and fishes. Real cool stop
Two hrs drive to get here and it was worth the drive. We got there early in the morning to see the low tide and what a sight. We came back later in the evening and that was also a wonder.
Seeing all those bats flying out was out of this world. It took a while for them to come out, but once they started it was like they never stop. Most see, glad I did.
This is an awesome park. The walk under the tall Cypress tress was so relaxing. Listening to the animals, even better. Would certainly be back while in the area.

Rented a kayak here to go out with my son. It was a beautiful day to be on the waters. Will certainly be back here.
Went back with my daughter and even better.
Would have loved to have been able to visit the animals but the price was too high for a family of six on vacation. We did leave a contribution though.
This was an awesome place to visit. My teenage daughter asked all these questions and the answers were forthcoming. Very attentive customer service.
Nice, small clean park. There is a boat ramp and a fishing pier. Mini soccer, volleyball and basketball a couple of things bin this small park.
Nice park, with cool play ground for kids. Also has a walk/run path with stops to try different workout. Can get crowded on weekends.
Awesome place to go hiking. The weather was great. Saw some huge gaters and a lot birds. We did a 6hr hike and that was enough.
This is certainly the most scenic drive that I have ever done in Florida. This drive is awesome. I would recommend to anyone.
Didn't get to go in, but from outside I know that this is a great park. I will certainly go in next time I am in the area.
This is the first time that I have been down here and there was no lines to take pictures. Always a picture perfect stop.
It's not the same since the covid review. There are no entertainment any more, but I guess you can't beat the sunset.
Love this end of fort Lauderdale beach, away for the hectic north or south. The little parking lot fills up quick.
Had a great time with the family. There were a lot of manatee when we went a couple months ago.

The Kingsley Plantation is part of the Timucuan Ecological and Historic Preserve like Fort Caroline. It's a bit off of the beaten path and visitors should be warned about the condition of the dirt road that leads to it; the road is rough with considerable potholes - if you drive a vehicle with low clearance, you'll want to take it slow and be careful. (If the road was better, I'd easily give it 5 stars). The historic site itself is most interesting. The first thing you see as you drive through the gate are the Plantation's Slave Cabins, one of which is restored. You then come to the barn, Kitchen House, and then the Plantation House, which sits near the St. John's River and is currently undergoing repairs and restoration. It can be toured twice a day by reservation (instructions on its website). The Plantation has a fascinating history with fascinating personalities and tells the story of both the owners and the slaves. It's well worth visiting to learn about what island plantations were like.

Located in the shadow of the Universtiy of South Carolina’s Williams-Brice Stadium, it’s operated by the South Carolina National Guard and located in the Guard’s compound on National Guard Rd off of Bluff Rd. It isn’t the easiest thing to find and you have to pass through a guard post to get back to it, but it is well worth the visit for any History or Military History buff. The South Carolina Military Museum presents the Military History of South Carolina primarily from the National Guard perspective, from the Spanish explorers in South Carolina through today. It is indeed a hidden gem and is well worth finding. They have a great collection and friendly veteran volunteers full of interesting stories and information. There’s no admission since it’s a government museum, but there is a collection box you should drop a donation in; operating a museum like this isn’t inexpensive and their government budget doesn’t cover everything.

A great place to watch and photograph airplanes at the Charlotte Douglas International Airport. It's a parking area with some benches on a hill between the north ends of Runway 18R/36L and Runway 18C/36C that overlooks Runway 18C/36C, the Air Carrier Terminal, and the Tower. You can even see downtown Charlotte’s skyline in the distance. On the day I visited, it put you at the departure end of Runway 36C (I don’t know if that’s the usual direction they work in or not) and in a great spot to get photos of the aircraft lifting off of the runway and departing. If you're a radio hobbyist and want to do listening to anything other than ATC frequencies, you'll be out of luck because there is a transmitter site right behind the overlook that causes interference.

Quite literally, there’s something for just about anyone who is a fan of motorized transportation at this museum. The museum is housed in the remaining buildings of the Spencer Shops, which used to be Southern Railroad’s largest steam locomotive repair on the east coast. They have a wonderfully varied collection of trains, motor vehicles, and aircraft and it does a great job of presenting the history of the Spencer Shops and railroads in North Carolina. If you’re a train buff, you’ll definitely want to visit this museum and if you have any interest in motorized transportation you’ll be interested in what it has to offer.

A very nice small museum dedicated mostly to the history of the rocket and missile launches at Cape Canaveral Air Force Station. They've got a nice collection of rocket and missile parts as well as rocket and missile models. It's organized by launch pad and along with the relevant artifacts/items, there is an informative display that tells you the history of the pad and what was launched there. The museum is just outside of the CCAFS gate and I can't recommend it enough for learning the Air Force Station's side of things - something you don't get as much at the KSC Visitors Center and the American Space Museum.

The Carolinas Aviation Museum isn't large as aviation museums go and features both military (mostly Navy and Marine Corps) and commercial aircraft, but the centerpiece of the museum is Airbus A320 N106US, the aircraft that was ditched in the Hudson River by its crew on 15 January 2019 after multiple large bird strikes. The aircraft are all well taken care of and beautifully presented and the staff is very friendly and helpful. It's definitely worth the trip to Charlotte for; it was the primary reason I included Charlotte on my road trip and I’m glad I did.

If you’re interested in military history, this really is a museum you should visit. It’s well kept and informative and they rotate special exhibits in addition to the regular exhibits. The museum volunteers, who are military veterans, are quite knowledgeable and readily share information and their experiences. Airborne units and Special Forces aren’t really one of my areas of expertise, so I learned a lot about their development here following on from a couple of visits to the National Infantry Museum at Fort Benning.

It's hard to fully rate this site because I was only able to walk one of the trails. The British Camp trail had just reopened, but the Park Manager recommended against walking it because of deep mud from where it had been underwater (she had just been able to reopen it). The Battlefield trail was in good condition, and a walk through it gives you an understanding of how hard it was to use conventional tactics of the Revolutionary War era in the Carolinas and why the guerrilla tactics of the militia worked well.

It's a small zoo, so the number of animals they have isn't very large, but it is varied. The tour through it is a approximately 1 mile and it took me about an hour to go through. Unfortunately, a lot of the enclosures for the animals are a bit small, but it looks like some of them are getting new enclosures - such as the Lions. That said, the animals appear well taken care of, and the ones that out on display but have health issues have signs stating so and that they're under veterinary care.

Definitely a place to stop at if you're into the Space Program. While the KSC Visitors Center is more flashy and high tech, it mostly concentrates on the rockets, spacecraft, and personalities. At the American Space Museum, they go deeper into the history of the Space Program with guided tours by Docents who have worked in the Space Program and are extremely knowledgeable. It's not very big, but they have a deceptively large collection that really digs deep into NASA's history.

The Visitors Center does double duty as a Visitors Center and Museum for both the Timucuan Ecological & Historic Preserve and the Fort Caroline National Memorial. The fort itself is a recreation and located a short distance down a trail behind the Visitors Center. Although it's currently being repaired due to Hurricane damage, it's well maintained. This site is very much worth visiting to learn about the French colonial presence in the southeast during the 1600s and 1700s.

It was hot, humid, and buggy when I visited, but I still enjoyed my walk on several of their trails. As I"m used to the marshland and brackish environments of the coast, it was fun to see the freshwater environment at Phinzy Swamp. I didn't see any alligators on my visit, but there were plenty of egrets and ibis. I'm really looking forward to coming back during the Autumn and Winter to see what kind of migratory waterfowl Phinzy Swamp attracts.

I visited just the the Augusta Canal National Heritage Area museum as it was just too hot to take the boat tour, but I learned a lot about the industrial history of Augusta during my visit. The museum has interactive exhibits that show how the Augusta Canal worked and how it changed and industrialized Augusta. I'll definitely be coming back in cooler weather to take one of the canal boat tours.

This is a must-visit for history buffs. The Spanish colonies are typically overlooked and this monument truly contributes toward filling that gap. It's amazing to see something of this era as well, there aren't many opportunities to do so in the United States. I highly recommend taking the guided tour, it's brief but the Rangers are very knowledgeable and it puts your visit in context.

The Little White House is set in a picturesque area, is very informative, and has a friendly helpful staff. The museum covers not just President Roosevelt's presidency and life in Warm Springs, but his entire life. The Little White House itself is well kept and it's both amazing and sobering to walk through the rooms where FDR stayed and where he passed away.

A must-visit in St Augustine. It's more than just the lighthouse, there is boat building and restoration and archaeology/study of area shipwrecks. It does a great job of presenting St Augustine's maritime history. I strongly suggest the guided tour, the volunteers are very knowledgeable and friendly.

A wonderful aquarium highlighting South Carolina's aquatic wildlife from the coast to the Piedmont, now with a Sea Turtle Rescue Facility added. The staff is friendly and informative. Sitting at the tanks at watching the fish swim around is amazingly relaxing.

A great place to visit to learn about the early history of Charleston and South Carolina. In addition to the museum and historical/archaeological displays, there is a small zoo with animals native to and that were native to the area.

A beautiful view at the beginning of the Battlefield trail at Musgrove Mill Historic Site - this part of the trail is paved and handicap accessible. It's not a big waterfall, but the view is gorgeous - I'd love to see it in fall.

A good small museum. Unfortunately they're still dealing with damage from Hurricane Irma. It's still worth visiting, though - there are a lot of unique items to see and continued patronage will help them finish recovering.

It has a nice driving tour through a variety of habitat including hardwoods, pines, mixed forest, fresh water, and brackish water. There are plenty of trails to walk/hike, and a wide variety of wildlife to photograph.
The Moss Cottage was part of the Historic District tour. The guide was very knowledgeable and it was interesting to see how the Gilded Age moguls thought they were "roughing it" in Jekyll.
Well restored/kept Third System fort of a different design than Fort Pulaski or Fort Sumter. The park also consists of plenty of woodland trails to wander, beaches, and fishing areas.
I visited because it was raining and it prevented visiting other sites. Fairly interesting for kids, I would think, but it just didn't turn out to be the thing for me.
A great place to watch vessel traffic on the St John's River and aircraft in the pattern at NS Mayport.

This beach and Kohanaiki are right next to each other. You can drive your car to either beach, or park in a lot between the two. These are a little more secluded areas that didn't have too many people. You access them via a road that goes through the volcano flow.

Both beaches had spots with finer sand and some areas that were larger more grainy and had shells. You can park on the sand if you wish. Neither looked conducive to swimming as the water area was very rocky.

There are lots of little alcoves formed by trees and shrubs that people were hanging out in, or camping in.

If you want a beach to hang out at that's off the beaten path without being crowded, and don't mind not swimming, this is a great spot.

This beach and Wawaloli are right next to each other. You can drive your car to either beach, or park in a lot between the two. These are a little more secluded areas that didn't have too many people. You access them via a road that goes through the volcano flow.

Both beaches had spots with finer sand and some areas that were larger more grainy and had shells. You can park on the sand if you wish. Neither looked conducive to swimming as the water area was very rocky.

There are lots of little alcoves formed by trees and shrubs that people were hanging out in, or camping in.

If you want a beach to hang out at that's off the beaten path without being crowded, and don't mind not swimming, this is a great spot.

This is a large falls a little outside of Hilo. They charge $5 for parking in the park, or $1 per person if you park on the road and walk in. While we were there it was extremely crowded. THere's a paved path about .4 miles long that takes you from the parking lot, through the forest, to the falls, and back. If you are in the area it's definitely worth checking out. I wouldn't drive to this area solely for this attraction though.

Nice little museum. I agree with what others have said, the 19 minute video on the history of Minneapolis and the flour tower elevator ride are by far the best part. The rest of the museum is interesting, but there's only so much you learn about flour. After the elevator ride you can go out on the top floor observation deck, which has a great view of the river.

The waterfall is about a 4 mile hike along the Kalalau Trail. You can swim there, although the water is fairly cold. Some of the trail can be a bit difficult to maneuverer if you're not a decent hiker. I'd imagine after heavy rains the trail would become even more difficult, even on a dry day many parts of the trail were wet and muddy.

Great beach that is pretty remote. You need to drive on a near 5 mile dirt road that is pretty bumpy. Once there you can drive your vehicle onto the beach. I'd recommend a four wheel drive vehicle if you do go into the sand, we saw some people almost get stuck. There didn't appear to be too many people on the beach, which is massive.

I would highly recommend going to the beach on Pea Island. You are able to park on the side of the road (route 12), or at some smaller designated lots off the road, and walk over the dunes to the beach. The beach here is extremely wide, and doesn't seem popular at all; we went and didn't see a single person at all.

This is a pretty nice Sandy Beach. there were multiple bathrooms, showers, and lifeguards. The beach was wide and long. It appears to be right next to a large resort and likely gets pretty crowded. There was a bit of rain when we were there and the crowd wasn't bad. This park charges $5 for parking as well.

This is a small park that was created around trees that lava engulfed, cooled, and left basically a statue behind. It's really neat scenery. It's only takes about 15 minutes to walk all around. I'd definitely recommend if you're in the area, but I wouldn't drive super far out of your way to go to.

This is a pretty small beach right off the main road in Kona. There's parking on the road or across the street for free. The beach had fine sand, but the water area was very rocky and didn't look conducive to swimming (no one there was). Also seems to get crowded as it's right in Kona.

This is the most popular black sand beach in the state. There's parking, bathroom, and a snack stand. Lots of people were snorkeling there, and boats were launching from there. While we were there, we saw 5 sea turtles sun bathing themselves. Beach did get a bid crowded.

You can visit the beach, or go hiking. Very unique setting, and a nice place to get some sand and sun in the mid-west. This park charges $7 for state residents, and $12 for out of state folks. There are national parks in the surrounding area that are free entrance.

The arch is at the end of the Chain of Craters Road. If you drive the road, you should take a stop and check it out. It's not worth driving all the way out for this specifically. There's also a small booth that sells some snacks and souvenirs close by.

The museum has tons of great info, and every few hours (I think it was 1:30 & 3:30 ) a ranger does a little talk and has tons of cool info and pictures.

The views at the museum of the caldera are awesome as well. Definitely recommend checking it out.

If you're in the city, you pretty much have to go around this, so you might as well stop in and check it out. You can walk up the ~300 stairs to the top for free, or pay $2 to ride the elevator. From the top you can get a great view of the city.

Nice start of the volcano journey. There's some information and souvenirs sold here. I think the souvenirs sold at the Lava House are better than here or the Jagger Museum, so make sure to check out that gift shop first.

Nice waterfall right outside of Hilo. It was very busy when we were there. There's nearly no walk at all to get the views there. There's also the ability to get directly next to the falls if you want to cross the river.

Absolutely stunning views. There's no place in the world like it, so if you can get out and experience it, you should. That said some of the hiking can get difficult, and it is a large area, so come prepared.

Great place to drive or hike around and see the unique volcanic history that formed the islands. You can check out the museum, listen/talk to rangers, drive, or hike to see all kinds of interesting things.
Great trail that will take you through the forest and then down into and across the crater. The crater is awesome, and worth checking out. This trail was what we had heard was the best in the park.
Extremely unique beach/water front. There are not a lot of parking spaces, and the trail down to the Bath can get a little muddy/slippery, but the views are definitely worth it.
Very unique park. You get into the park for free and walk around the massive sand dunes and go next to the sound. I'd highly recommend stopping if you're in the area.
Small national park that has a self guided tour of the ancient Hawaiian grounds via a map handed out. It can be done in ~20 minutes. Not a whole lot to see.
Mostly flat trail that winds through a plantation which includes mahogany trees, lagoons, a damn, and has wildlife such as horses and cows.
Looked really nice, however the lights weren't on (although they were supposed to be), so we weren't able to see all the details.

Really nice little pulloff from side of road. The view from the top little overlook part isn't actually as amazing as I thought it'd be - you can't see the big lake. But it is still super nice and peaceful. It's free, there's a place to parking, some nice walking trails, and a restroom with water fountain and sunscreen dispenser. Highly recommend a quick stop if driving by

Go to this park! Had no clue this little gem of a park existed off old Tampa Bay. Really cool spot to either do a quick drive or get out, walk, or hang out a bit. Beautiful views of the bay as well as a decent bit of elevation. There's a historical mound there built a long time ago by natives. Definitely recommend a visit - it's free.

This is a really neat little park at the end of a small road where it opens up into basically an island right on the gulf. It has some small sandy areas, covered tables, grills and bathrooms. also has a boardwalk thru mangroves which end in a cool scenic overlook. It's free. Not too much parking available. Highly recommend.

Really cool botanical gardens in largo. It is a bizarre in terms of layout - pretty much have to go through the same parts a couple times to get to every area. It's free admission but they accept donations. It's next to a cracker country type place. Worth the trip but the actually garden is not as good as sunken gardens.

This is a really cool park on the beach in tarpon springs. It reminds me of the drive over to honeymoon island - water on both sides of the causeway. Plenty of parking and areas to sit on beach. Palm trees on the beach so you can find a spot with natural shade if you forget your umbrella. Only costs 5 bucks

This state park has some really cool beach points as well as the old lighthouse. The lighthouse is a great experience and only costs two bucks per person to climb to the top. The park itself is 5 bucks per adult to get in. There's a decent little drive through wilderness to get to the lighthouse and beach

Really great park. Costs 4 or 6 bucks to get in depending on if you're alone or with others. There are a few nature trails for walking. Awesome view of hillsborough river where there are some rapids. Big swimming pool and concession stand with food. Tons of parking. Big camping area. Awesome spot

This is such a cool place to go when the weather is nice. There are some big areas to BBQ, hang, toss the football. There is also a cool wooden boardwalk out over the Hillsborough river where you can see wildlife and cool plants and trees. Only a couple bucks to get in. Highly recommend!

This park kinda reminds me of Bayshore in Tampa. Really long sidewalk running length of the bay. Park has a great view into the bay as well as some expensive waterfront homes. Can even see across all the way to Apollo beach. Has a little bit of beach and tons of grass and palm trees.

Flatwoods is a great place to walk, skate, run or bike. It's 11 miles total from bb downs entrance to bb downs entrance around the loop. But it's just 2 miles to start of loop, so could do a four mile round trip easy. There are water stations set up along the loop. Costs two bucks.

This is a really cool lighthouse in key West. You can climb the 88 steps to the top and then walk around the platform for 360 views of key west. There's also a small museum where you can see and learn more. Costs like 12 bucks a person to get in. Worth doing !

This is a really nice park in the palm harbor tarpon springs area. Really easy to get to. Plenty of parking and then you can walk around a path looking at the spring as well as piers out into the gulf. Really great experience. They have bathrooms. It's free !

Pine island is a really cool place to hang out and take in the views. It's a cool drive to get there. Parking is plentiful and there are bathrooms and a small place to get food. There is some sand making it a bit beachy. Really cool spot for a visit.

This is a really cool county park with a lot of area to walk around. Has views of a lake filled with alligators, birds, turtles, etc. Has restrooms and places to public and grill. Best part are definitely the trees with crazy root structure exposed

This is a really cool county park that is more like a botanical garden. Has an elevated boardwalk going through some cool wooded areas. Definitely recommend a visit if you want to go for a short walk and see some nature! Costs 2 bucks

This is a pretty cool state park. It seems primarily built around mountain biking trails. They have trails for novices up to experts. Also have a camping area. Costs 5 bucks to get in. Worth a trip but not that much going on

This is a pretty cool but bizarre state park that is technically off the gulf of Mexico but you pretty much can only walk to small coves and stuff as opposed to the gulf. Worth going if you like seeing state parks.

Really cool little state park off 301. Costs 5 bucks to get in just in a normal car. Has some nice trails for walking. Has restrooms, places to eat lunch, etc. Also has big camping area. Highly recommend!

This is such a cool place to visit if you live in Tampa or visiting the area. It basically is a Little Greek. Tons of Greek restaurants and gift shops and sponge attractions. Definitely worth a day trip.

This is a cool little botanical gardens spot in St Pete. Takes about 30 mins to an hour to walk around the whole thing. Really cool sights smells and sounds. Definitely recommend. Only ten bucks a person
Really cool little park with a 2.25 mile walking trail around a big lake. There are a couple water stations if you get thirsty. Costa 2 bucks to get in. Worth the trip !
Really nice little park near Apollo beach. Seems primarily for boats but has a small beach and playground with bathrooms. Has a nice view of downtown Tampa skyscrapers.
Caladesi beach was super worth it. You take a ferry from honeymoon island and then just hang at an awesome beach that is great for shelling. Highly recommend
Really cool spot to visit, especially during pandemic. Nice views of water, some cool facts about native americans here in Florida and public bathrooms
Hard to not know about this tower if you drive around Tampa! Definitely worth a quick visit if youve never been

The park has a historic component in the McKinnis house where special programs are frequently held. The house is only open at those times and is well worth the vist.
The barn is another historical component and has a modern food service area attached. It can be rented.
The natural area of the park with trails is the remainder of the park on the north side of US 224. A paved handicap accessible trail leads to a very nice overlook with benches. Beyond that the main trail has a gravel surface with side trails being soil or grass surface. The park is primarily wooded with nice sized trees. The western edge of the park does have some nice grasslands too.

They did a great job of taking the former site of a glass production facility and turning it into a park that pays homage to that history.  The museum is well worth a visit while you were at the park. It was staffed with a volunteer who used to work at the glass facility.
A bike trail runs through the park and the lakes which are part of the park are very inviting as well. One note is that the observation tower, which is well worth the trip to the top, is not open through the Winter.
dislikes: Limited access (observation tower closed in winter)

reviews_attraction.text: The trail is very nice, flat and in good shape. The parking area is very nice and the trailhead has nice educational panels about the history of the area. The trail heading toward Windsor will take you onto local roads VERY briefly before you pick up the continuous off road trail. The trail is fine gravel and any bike should be fine for the surface but I'd imagine most folks would prefer a tire that's not especially skinny.

A very nice small park with access to the water via Boardwalk. There are restrooms and a nature center with outdoor classroom space. There's parking for cars and a bike rack it makes for a very nice Bike Ride Along Rockledge Road which takes you to within just a few hundred feet of the park. The interpretive signage is quite outdated along the boardwalk but the walk itself and plants are very enjoyable.

A fantastic slice of the real Florida! The canoe rental price includes the first two hours and you can stay out longer if you like and pay just a bit more for each additional hour. The swimming area and River are fantastic. There are some nice trails to walk as well in addition to a small Education Center. This is a wonderful gem right in the Orlando metro area!

The view shortly before reaching the parking lot is great. The hike to the waterfall is not long, but it is vigorous. Don't plan on rushing there.  The waterfall was very cool, but it would take a recent rain to get it really flowing. Beautiful flowers blooming in the glade habitat ares with butterflies abundant.

Great place for launching a kayak, windsurfer or similar small boat. The paved boat ramp is also available too for trailered boats. The restrooms are well maintained.
One important note for launching from the beach, be aware that stingrays can be there and shuffle your feet accordingly as you enter the water.

A very nice Contemporary Art Museum. There was a nice variety of displays. The art ranged from the very abstract to the much more approachable. It was great to see local artists featured as well as women and African American artists. My favorite exhibit was actually the cafe. That's a spot I would not miss.

Fantastic place to enjoy a walk in nature!
There is a marked trail which is approximately a mile long and takes you through pineland scrub habitat. You can also walk along the fire breaks to have an even longer walk if you'd like. The Scrub Jays are very friendly, but as a reminder please do not feed them.

Excellent tent campground with a nice barrier of trees between each site. Nice showers and laundry too. Some nice historic sites at the park and a very good kayak launch. A lot of the park is the water area and the part on land is relatively small compared to some other parks, but very nice.

Great spot to launch from and be in the Sanctuary area right away. If you want a bit more paddling you can launch at Goode Park, which is near US-1.
The distance to carry your boat in is not far, probably about 200' or so. The launch ramp is very nice. Beautiful spot.

Very enjoyable park. Plenty space for just about any activity. Walking biking, grilling,  games, picnic shelters and just watching the river roll by. My only nit pick is the need for a public restroom sized toilet paper dispenser in the restroom.

A multi purpose park. Cross Country skiing in winter, many trails through natural areas including along the Blanchard River, primitive camping, a lake, shelters to use/rent and a disc golf course. Only pit toilets, but they are well-maintained.

Cliff Drive has minimal traffic and is completely closed to cars on Sundays. It's nice and shaded for summer bike rides or walks. There are mountain biking trails and spaces for rock climbing as well and great views to the north.

Nice museum at the trailhead for the Prairie Spirit Trail and Flint Hills Nature Trail. Only disappointment was those staffing the place were more interested in their own conversation than my experience at the museum.

Very nice combination of trails. Handicap accessible to climbing the rocks and in between. Natural beauty and human history are both found here.
Nice modern restroom currently with other facilities being opened.

Great combination of very cool historical features to look at and natural areas to enjoy as you hike along the historical Trail. The museum was not open when I was there but it looks interesting as well.
The National Nature Photography Center was a great place for a community organization meeting. Enjoyed a short walk in the snow afterwards. Nothing but praise forToledo Metropark in general.
Beautiful and fabulous place. Rock Springs Run is onw b of my absolutely top of my list places to paddle in the country. It's typically more quiet than the Wekiwa River and more intimate.
Great place to launch from for paddling! The restrooms are well maintained and there are loads of areas to explore. The islands also make for good wind protection on windy days.
Nice ramp/dock for launching into Turkey Creek. Restrooms were in very decent shape. Nothing especially amazing for me here, but nothing to complain about either.
A great place to experience the natural beauty of the Space Coast. Hiking trails to a boardwalk overlooking the river from high bluffs. A really great place.
Great place for the Vegfest! Also a great park anytime with a huge playground, paths, restrooms, water fountains, a store for snacks and more.
The campground is situated in a very nice spot and the facilities were in fantastic shape. Very nice staff and Campground host as well.
Nice campground. Good selection of trails. The spring was a great place to visit on a hot summer day hike.

Fascinating place! Very informative and such a beautiful scenery! You can walk around the mounds, Etowah river bank is peaceful and you can learn about herbs and tree parts used as medicine by the Cherokee as well. We have seen otters playing in the river! Don't miss the museum, they have lots or artefacts and also models of how the city really looked like. When you arrive, the best thing to do is go straight to the museum and pay $6 which is museum entrance with parking fee combined. Staff is very helpful!

This is a great place for picknicking. Redbird Creek Trail was closed (mid June) but we really enjoyed wandering around the fort, which is wonderfully preserved! We have seen a gopher tortoise and many woodpeckers! Just don't get fooled by the map they have on website, it's misleading - the fort is right behind the visitor center and there is no path to get there from the road heading to campground. We entered the wood thinking there would be a trail and all we found was ticks and poison ivy :-(
dislikes: Ticks and poison ivy in the woods

reviews_attraction.text: Such a large refuge! We drove to Drummond Lake, which is quiet and beautiful. We've seen lots of turtles on the way, also vultures, swamp deer, snakes and waterfowl. Your car will get dusty, biting flies are around, so don't forget to bring insect repellent with you. All you need to do is leave 5 dollar bill in an envelope by the entrance. We will definitely come back and explore hiking trails!

Great staff, well maintained grounds and amazing experience! You can pet and feed kangaroos and emus here. These animals are used to have people around so they are calm. We watched a baby kangaroo moving in it's mother's pouch for the first time. It's magical and you can observe it up close. The zoo is not too big but you need to go uphill a little. Watch for peacocks on the road!

This swamp is unbelievably beautiful and quiet! It's huge and full of wildlife. We have seen lots of waterfowl, turtles, crayfish and thousands of dragonflies. You can spend the whole day wandering around the ponds. Stunning! Just be aware that they don't have any facilities open due to the Covid situation. Not even bathrooms and water fountains. Bring lots of water!!!

These caverns are less crowded than Luray caverns, we went on the tour with a group of 15 people and it was amazing. Our guide Sarah provided lots of information and added some stories for fun :-) Caverns are very beautiful and temperature is mild, we didn't even need long sleeves. Don't miss their museum upstairs, it's nothing I've ever seen before!

This site is amazing to take a moderate hike in a quiet shaded forest while learning about history at the same time. We haven't been in the museum but wandered on the trails and it's a very nice place! Don't miss the log cabin, it's not far away from the museum. We have met like 6 people in there. Peaceful and pristine.

This is a small but very informative site! Don't miss the museum and also a short film. All staff is welcoming and knowledgeable. Just be aware that the Memorial building closes at 4:30 p.m. and you can't enter the cabin replica inside. Don't miss the spring, it's very cooling there.

Amazingly beautiful place! Especially if you're a spanish moss lover as I am! They are not afraid to tell you the truth about slavery and all the struggles, staff is amazing and very informative! Don't miss the little museum inside visitor center. We loved it!!!

Great museum with enthusiastic staff! They have even German and Russian planes and all aircrafts are still used for flying! Check out their calendar for airshows, we unfortunately missed one. And don't forget to visit Jerassic Park nearby :-)

Wonderfully beautiful garden! Large collection of orchids and other tropical plants like coffee, papaya or cocoa. They also have large variety of local plants outside! Shade garden is a heaven in this warm weather!

There's really nothing much to see since the museum is closed. It's a really nice place though, you can enjoy shade and quiet close to the marsh. But not worth the drive if you don't go anywhere else close by...
Cheerful welcome from the staff! It's cozy inside. Flight for $12 contains three wines, white/red/mix. Some of them were to dry for us. Don't miss the opportunity to buy the sweet dessert wine.
This place is not so crowded but pristine and beautiful! We went kayaking here and it was very nice. We got excited about the cabins because some of them have their own docks, convenient!
Small but very informative museum! There is a section with innovations discovered by African-American people, which you can't see anywhere else! Staff is friendly and helpful.
Amazing historic house with peaceful gardens. The staff is great here. Don't miss the gift shop, lots of beautiful items! I bought a few bird cards made of quilted paper.
Amazing and well maintained garden! All staff was very nice and welcoming. We loved fairy castles and pavilion with cactae. The whole ground is picturesque and quiet.
Relatively small zoo but very nice and filled with amazing creatures! Comodo dragon, giant anteater, cougar, snow leopard, lots of reptiles and also giraffes!
Green paradise of forest for hikers, dogs and kayakers. Lots of wild geese, blue jays, squirrels, we also saw a snake. Great for a long walk along the river.
It's a beautiful view! You can observe it from a distance but it's still an amazing place! Don't miss Hardman Farm right next to it, it's beautiful!
Such a funny place! It is very well maintained and impressive. You can spend quality time there before or after visiting the aviation musem.
This is an amazing place! It's pristine. Be careful down there behind the waterfall, it's muddy and slippery. But overall beautiful!!!
Beautiful and peaceful park! We spent over an hour hiking around the lake. Also encountered the two cats, Ms. Laura and Mr. Walker 🙂
Amazing views and lots of history! Be prepared to pay $3/hour for parking and $10/person admission. But it's worth every penny!!!
Informative museum, a lot to see there! We were lost a little. The main attraction here is obviously USS Wisconsin anyway.

Fascinating, scenic park named after a former Glades county elected official, Larry Luckey, Sr. who started the process to make this county owned land into a park several decades ago. Lots of things to see here and a nice display to explain the history of the area. You can actually hike around and over the ancient mounds here, noting what may have been canals the ancient Native Americans used centuries ago. There are also several geocaches located here and many shelters for picnics. A trail winds around Lake Wobegon, with a picnic shelter at the end. The western section of the park has numerous picnic shelters although strangely with no tables, and plenty of seating benches abound on the trails. Unfortunately a wood bridge and boardwalk have been in serious disrepair for about three years preventing a walk along those scenic trails. A building with rest rooms is at the parking area, although the men's was locked, but women's open. A "Cane Grinding" festival is held here each February.
dislikes: Disrepair of wood bridge and boardwalk
Lack of tables in picnic shelters

reviews_attraction.text: Collier county's 2nd largest park. It's always open in the Winter/Spring season on Friday's from 9 to 4 and most Saturday's and Sunday's but once a month it's closed on the weekend so call ahead or check their website for open days. It's also available for meeting rental on Thursdays and for picnic shelter rental and group camping.

A wonderful place to visit and spend a few hours at least. The gift shop is fun to browse around and pick up a book about Mr. Bok. Make sure to stay around for the carillon concert, and if you're lucky to hear it, you'll not soon forget the sound of those bells among the luxurious grounds here.

Nice riverside park with lots of giant oak trees for cool shade even on the hottest Southwest Florida summer days. Boat dock and renovated pier forms a nice edge to the park. A gazebo and seating for music and other events takes up the primary park space with tennis courts on one side.

Yesteryear Village is the location for the filming of the Amazon series "In Sanity, Florida." But Reynolds,  a resident of nearby Jupiter, Fl. plays himself in the series. By watching the free episodes you can see the interesting old buildings and items on display at the village.

One of the newer parks in Lehigh Acres give visitors an ideal view of just how a newly designed park starts out with newer plantings around the park and it's small ponds.  Good for a leisurely walk around the paths enjoying the nature in this residential area.

Very well laid out park and well cared for. There's lots to see here including shaded woody areas along the water and open space hiking There's a ramp for launching canoes and kayaks but you have to carry your craft a pretty long distance to reach the water.

Nestled along a fairly busy roadway, it has all the recreation you'd look for including a swimming pool and picnic areas. Because of the nearness to the busy traffic I've never enjoyed this park as much as other more off the beaten track parks.

Pleasant recreation area to spend a few hours, watching the boats go through the locks, and visiting the beach or having a picnic. Well kept by the Corps of Engineers, but very occasionally the beach has been closed due to pollution.

Lots of trails here to follow and picnic areas and boat launching ramp to make this a popular place to visit. There's even a bat house to attract those flying mammals near the entrance. Plenty of parking throughout the park area.

My favorite places are off the beaten track, especially the trails off of State Road 29 in Collier county. Miles and miles of trails to hike and explore. Keep an eye out for alligators, and the rare Florida panther.

One of the larger parks in the Lehigh area. Lots of nice walking trails and shady areas. Dog owners can bring their canines to the fenced dog park area. There are geocaches hidden here for fans of that GPS sport.

A very unusual park where visitors can not only enjoy the nature and wildlife here but watch manatees swim in the warm waters of the Blue Springs. A place you won't soon forget after a visit of a few hours here.

One of my favorite locations to get away from city life. Hike up the small sandy hills and rest at the observation deck at the top. Then walk down the trail to the lake and take in the view from the sandy shore.

A nice park right in the middle of a residential area, not easy to find but worth a visit. Hike around the ponds and a few miles of hiking trails are here. There's geocaches hidden here for fans of that sport.

Small church here is worth a quiet visit. It is an architecturally interesting space and I enjoyed spending a few moments here and enjoying the neighborhood with lots of flowers and plants along the streets.
Quiet park along the water with a nice boat launching area and observation platform to sit and enjoy the nature here. There are several geocaches hidden in the park and hiking trails around the park.
Nice quiet area for hiking and observing nature here. A small entrance fee get a lot of enjoyment of this state forest area down it's dirt roads with some nice spots to relax and view the scenery.
A well hidden park along the riverfront in a residential neighborhood. It's small but well kept by the county and with the many trees well shaded with some tables to spend a quiet few hours here.
A good sized park with lots of room to walk or hike the walkways. Plenty of things for the kids, even a hill to climb. Lots of shady areas for picnics make this a popular weekend destination.
Be sure to take the Shark Valley Tram Tour ending at the fantastic walkway high above the Everglades. You'l love the view and the quiet of the location away from the sounds of civilization.
Lots of trails around various ecosystems of pineland, swamp and a nice observation tower. There are dozens of geocaches hidden throughout the trail system discoverable with a GPS.
Lots of recreational opportunities here. Horseback riding, camping, and hiking along miles and miles of trails. You can spend lots of days here without seeing everything.
Small park with some nice easy hiking trails. Plenty of parking but no bikes are allowed on the trails. A very quiet area here off the beaten track for sure.
Excellent small park and beginning point for a hike or bike ride along the many miles of the linear park paved trail.

I do have complaints about Manta mostly regarding everything before and after the ride. Even though the station has two sides, only one is normally used, so the loading takes longer than it should. While this is bad for wait times, it's even worse when you're on the train not getting loaded waiting ages to get off. This wouldn't normally be a problem if you had any freedom to move, look around, or even be in a comfortable natural position while you're waiting to get off. The vest presses your chest, your legs aren't free to move, and your head can either hang or look ahead. This is frustrating because this issue, along with a slow moving queue, could easily be alleviated if they would simply use both stations. It seems illogical to not do so, as Manta is the most popular ride in the park, moreso than even newer rides like Mako and Antarctica.

Aside from this, Manta is perfect, and one of the best flying coaster experiences in the world. The theming is the best among the seaworld coasters, with an air conditioned queue that has its own aquarium. It's hard to get bored in this dimly lit and ambient queue with pretty music playing and rockwork and fish on all sides. The soundtrack becomes even more triumphant in the station, where an intimidating mechanical sound effect plays when the cars lift from sitting to flying.

The coaster itself is great. With swooping turns and slow inline twists, flying over the flowers and even near Antarctica is a fun treat. The second half is even better, as the wing dip gets riders on the far right a little wet, and swooping past a waterfall gets far left riders sprayed on their legs. The landscaping is beautiful and picturesque in this section, and it would be the best part of the ride were it not for the first element on the coaster: the pretzel loop. Contrasting the rest of the coaster's gentle flips and curves, the pretzel loop is one of the most intense elements on any coaster. You get airtime as you crest a hill, then nosedive straight down so far that you go upside down, and then experience huge G forces as you flip to the bottom now on your back... and as you level out again, you get airtime once more as you crest another hill. The ride is gentle after this, but the pretzel loop is not for the faint of heart.

The best way I can describe Storm Runner is that it's like riding a Sonic the Hedgehog level.  You take off like a rocket into a short burst of adrenaline, with only about four individual elements until the ride is over, and it's fantastic. Each element has something to offer.

For one, the launch is very fast and accelerates you to top speed faster than most coasters, a signature of hydraulic launched coasters.

Then the top hat that you go into is tall, but short enough that you go over it with speed. Front row riders will get airtime on the crest, and back row riders will get whipped down the drop. Then the cobra loop has strong positive G forces as you pull up 180 degrees, and then you twist out.

The third element, the flying snake dive, is my favorite. You soar upwards (you get airtime in the front here), and then do one barrel roll, which goes immediately into another barrel roll which corkscrew dives back to the ground mid roll.

When you get back down to the ground, the last element is like a twisted double-up, with two hard banks right and left as you rise back up into the air, whipping you from side to side, and you hit the final brakes at the top.

Storm Runner is fast paced and will get your blood pumping without fail every time, and the ride being short is a non issue. It's just long enough to be satisfying, especially because of how unique the elements are, and soaring over and near rides like Sidewinder and Trailblazer is also very cool, as well as darting through the trees at blitz speed. This is my second favorite coaster at Hersheypark.

If you like airtime, no coaster in Florida delivers it like Mako, and that's the biggest appeal of the ride.

Mako has nice theming. It has its own soundtrack that plays in the queue, in the station, up the lift hill, on the brake run, and even in the plaza when the train is flying overhead. It has a majestic feeling like Manta's soundtrack, but a little more forboding with some Jaws flavor thrown in.

There's nice shipwreck theming and some coral reefs, ambient lighting, and a themed car that looks like a fierce mako shark. Plus the coaster is gorgeous, with beautiful teal and purple against a setting over the water. You'll even be able to see Kraken very easily.

Mako is incredibly comfortable. Not only are the clamshell lap bars roomy, but they're body conforming and there's no seatbelt to get in the way of your airtime. But as long as you pull the restraint down at least a bit snugly, you'll stay in the car safely. In addition, Mako is far and away the smoothest coaster in Florida.

The coaster itself is outstanding. The first drop is long and incredibly floaty. The overbanked turns are very fun to wave your hands to, especially towards the end of the ride as you get lower to the ground and water. And all of the Airtime hills will provide whole seconds of endorphin providing zero gravity. The ride is well paced, fun, smooth, comfy, well themed, beautiful, and not too intense. Anyone in your party will enjoy Mako and many will want to ride again and again.

Most of my criticism of Cheetah Hunt is of everything before the ride begins. The queue is always the longest in the park, and because the trains don't hold very many people, the line moves slowly. Be prepared to wait several hours. On top of that, the queue is very boring with nothing to look at, as your view of the coaster is blocked by the giant roof. In addition, Cheetah Hunt breaks down more often than any other ride in the park, so don't be surprised if you experience delays during your wait.

With all of that out of the way, Cheetah Hunt is a great ride. It's a good mid thrill, somewhere between Cobra's Curse and SheiKra. It's not as intense as Tigris, but it's much longer, so it's on the same level. All three launches are forceful and sudden, the drops are sharp, the hills have great airtime, the heartline roll gives great hangtime, and all of the turns are quick with fast transitions. There are trenches, tunnels, and a canyon with water, and you will go over and under bridges, paths, and other attractions. Cheetah Hunt will be enjoyed by everyone in your party by the time you actually get on the ride.

If you're looking for a moderate thrill for kids too old for kiddie rides but not quite tall enough for the big rides, look no further than Cobra's Curse. There's one large drop facing forwards, a small slow backwards section, and a large section at the end where the cars spin freely. It does not go upside down and it is smooth and comfortable. This is still incredibly fun for thrill seekers as the first drop is sizeable, the backwards section is fun, and the spinning can be unpredictable.

If you like theming, Cobra's Curse has the best in Busch Gardens. The queue is extensively themed and has a nice atmosphere, especially if you're willing to read the archeological notes on the walls. The coaster itself has great theming with audio during the slow parts, a layout that goes over and under paths, interaction with Montu's wall, and a giant Snake King statue as big as the coaster itself. The wait can get a little long due to this ride's accessibility and proximity to the front of the park, but it's well worth it due to a themed queue and a fun ride.

You can never go wrong with an old school looping coaster like this one. SooperDooperLooper is the perfect starting out thrill ride, and is fun for thrill seekers too. Though old, Sooper is smooth as butter and very comfortable, only having lap bars as your restraint. It's in a scenic location near Spring Creek, goes through the trees, and passes by Coal Cracker and Great Bear.

The coaster itself is just thrilling enough. The first drop is sizeable and the loop is smooth and very forceful. The rest of the ride is mild, with smooth scenic turns and drops. You thread back through the loop like a needle, go through a tunnel, and take terrain conforming turns on the banks of the creek, which is where you may come face to face with riders of Great Bear. The ride ends with a forceful final helix to make sure you're satisfied.

This ride is gentle enough, but has enough thrilling and unique features to make it worth your ride, and riding a piece of history this well designed is a great time.

I'm not a Fahrenheit superfan myself, but I cannot deny that this is an excellent coaster. While the steep drop, cobra roll, corkscrews, and last airtime hill are all excellent elements, the crown jewel for me is the unique Norwegian loop.

You go up to the top and get airtime if you're in the front, and twist into a nosedive downwards. The positive gs at the bottom are awesome. You twist out again at the top, and drop back down again to get airtime in the back rows. This is two inversions in one, has airtime, and is essentially a regular loop flipped on its head, so you get all of those positive g forces from a 360 loop plus two spirals and an extra drop. The element completes the ride and makes it somethin truly special and unique.

No trip to Hersheypark is complete without a ride on Fahrenheit. Though Skyrush and Candymonium are newer, taller, faster, and closer to the front, in my mind Fahrenheit will always be the signature coaster of Hersheypark.

Fun Spot Orlando is both an affordable alternative for locals and a worthwhile visit for tourists. $50 all day wristbands are very worth it, especially because they're open late. White Lightning is an awesome wooden coaster and Freedom Flyer is a fun family inverted coaster. There is a large selection of flat rides with varying intensities, with some being classic models (Tilt a Whirl, Scrambler, Enterprise, Bumper Cars, Carousel, Ferris Wheel) and others being modern, like Hot Seat, an awesome and huge pneumatic swing ride. They also have, in my opinion, the best go-karts I've ever ridden. The four tracks tangle into one another and each have different track layouts and experiences. The food is also affordable and high quality, which I can't say for any other park in Florida. If you have any funfair nostalgia and want to experience it in a safer, more family friendly environment, Fun Spot is the best place I can think of.

SheiKra and Cheetah Hunt are the crowd pleasing and less intense thrill rides of the park, with sharp drops and very pretty track but not as many loops. But if you're looking for a somewhat more old school thrill that caters to roller coaster enthusiasts and adventure seekers, look no further than Kumba.

Kumba is as intense as steel looping coasters get with seven inversions all back to back. With a lush rainforest setting and the loud roaring track, the sense of speed is absolutely there. Kumba gets faster as it goes through its layout. The first drop and two loops are fairly intense, but you fly through the zero-g roll in a way that makes you float, and the cobra roll is very whippy, and is taken at terrifying speed. The g-forces on Kumba are sustained and powerful, the pacing is unrelenting, and the line is never long.

Great American Scream Machine might be an old coaster, but it doesn't ride like a beloved classic when the park puts so little maintenance into keeping the ride comfortable. The roughness is jackhammering at times, and all that kinetic energy gets wasted and the ride runs even slower. That means weaker laterals and airtime on a ride that would otherwise have it in spades. In addition, the buzz bar 3 seater trains have been replaced by regular 2 seater trains with lap bars, so there's less room for airtime and no middle of the train seat to avoid roughness. This ride was updated in the wrong ways. It needs new wood on the structure, a complete retracking of the layout, and fresh paint across the board to live up to its potential as a beloved classic.

This is a great ride, but it's not perfect. If you're afraid of bugs, crawlies, or bug guts like I am, there's a large section in the middle of the ride with only that, and the special effects squirts water on you to simulate bug venom and guts. It's true to the film, but still gross. There's also actors in the queue that jumpscare you, and I'm personally not a fan of that either.

If neither of those things bother you, you'll enjoy this ride. The queue is well themed, the screens are high quality and exciting, and the Kong animatronic at the end is absolutely amazing and stunning, and he's the best part of the ride. The only problem is that due to the safari truck style vehicle, it can be hard to see what's going on from the other side of the car.

This water ride - coaster hybrid has a lot to offer, and is quite family friendly. It has majestic and ambient Atlantic theming indoors, a beautiful structure to look at offride, and thrilling drops that will likely have you soaked by the end. Unfortunately, the effort to make the ride family friendly has been subtractive rather than additive. The theming of the siren with a Medusa head has all been turned off or removed, and replaced with nothing. For my nostalgic self, Journey to Atlantis is a shadow of its former self, though still fun. But if you don't have rose tinted memories of being scared to death by a medusa looking mermaid creature, this ride is excellent for all family members and is widely appealing and thrilling.

SheiKra is just about the most rerideable coaster at Busch Gardens Tampa. It's got its fair share of thrills, with two large drops, two particularly forceful turns, and a floaty immelmann loop. If you want the best view and sense of speed, I recommend the front. If you want to feel the force of the drops, loop, and turns more, I recommend the back seat.

It's rerideable for several reasons. Not only is it very smooth, but it's not as intense as rides like Kumba or Montu. It also has shorter lines than Cheetah Hunt and Cobra's Curse because the trains can fit more people and it rarely breaks down. I think that if you enjoy coasters at all, SheiKra will be the ride that you and your party will all enjoy.

Montu is a little bit out of the way in the park, but if you plan on riding Cheetah Hunt and Cobra's Curse, this giant inverted looping coaster is worth a ride. One of the largest inverted coasters on the planet, Montu has 7 inversions, an Egyptian theme complete with sandy trenches, and has cars that hang below the track with no floor, so your feet dangle freely. Don't worry, the g-forces still feel normal.

While the inversions are all very intense, especially the double inverting batwing, it is not as fast paced as Kumba, so if you want to work yourself up to Kumba, Montu is a great place to start. Nevertheless Montu is loud, proud, and sure to be a favorite of coaster fans.

Shrek himself and the movie they show are great, but the movement and special effects are incredibly outdated. The chairs moving are loud, jarring, and uncomfortable. If you have any back problems avoid this attraction at all costs. If they simply turned off the movement and used only the movie, the mist and water, and the visual effects, this could be a pleasant and funny attraction. But it's mostly just an unpleasant waste of time. If you want a 3D motion ride, I highly recommend going on Jimmy Fallon Race through New York instead, which is funnier, newer, has less grossout humor, and is a very smooth and pleasant experience.

If your kid is afraid of going upside down, Scorpion is the perfect ride to get them started. The ride has only one loop, and it's right after the first drop. There are no large drops. However, Scorpion is a forceful ride with forces similar to those on Kumba and Montu. It is also an older ride, so if you don't hang on tightly you will get jostled around. In my opinion, Scorpion is a great ride for anyone to enjoy and might spark a love for coasters in your kid in the same way it did for me, and I find this ride hard to skip due to my nostalgia.

While not full of special effects, 3D, or animatronics, or even much movement, the ride makes up for it in the great animation and especially the humor. Grown ups will appreciate the jokes and references much more, but this is still perfectly appropriate for children. It's not rough or unpleasant in any way. Look around the screen for hidden details and jokes.

Comet isn't the best thing since sliced bread, but it's still an excellent ride. Of all the wooden coasters in Hershey, this one definitely has not only the most airtime, but also the most history. It gets bonus points for its interaction with Skyrush and its very roomy buzz bar restraints. It's a very fun ride that you can't go wrong with and a true classic.

Good ride, and great if you've never ridden Top Thrill Dragster before. If you have, it's not as good. It's not as smooth and there are vests instead of lap bars. On the plus side you get a little floater airtime on the second hill, but I personally prefer Dragster's long straightaway. Again, a good ride with awesome speed and height.

Goliath is world class. Comfortable and smooth. The airtime over the large hills gives a flying sensation, leaping over the park entrance and going back into it with bunny hops that pop you out of your seat. The helix in the middle of the ride is very powerful. And of course, the ride is enormous and gives a great sensation of speed.

The line for this one moves very slow. Luckily the whole queue is indoors and has funhouse mirrors to keep your mind occupied.

The ride itself is alright. The theming is just okay, and the spinning isn't very intense. This is still a great ride for the park, as indoor rides give guests something to do if it starts raining.

When it comes to boomerang coasters this is as good as it gets, and that's all thanks to this ride's excellent restraints. The vests are comfy and secure, and there's nothing to hit your head on. As usual the drops are sharp and the inversions are forceful. Worth a shot even if you don't like Boomerangs.

I'm not really a fan of free spinning 4D coasters, but I don't hate them either. I think the restraints are pretty uncomfortable on the groin if you don't pull it down as far as possible, and the spinning just feels unnatural. But it's still pretty fun and the setting near the water is a big plus.

This is a fun little wooden coaster and I'm glad it's still around. Not too rough, looks nice, and has decent airtime and laterals. I'd give it 5 stars if it weren't for the trim brakes at the end that take away speed for the last bunny hills. Still a good time and worth a ride.

Wildcat is a pretty good wooden coaster. I've ridden better and I've definitely ridden worse. The layout isn't very intense in my experience, but the ride isn't rough either. The layout is also very twisty, so that makes it a fun ride. Worth riding to see if you like it or not.

There are so many different things to do, see places to eat to much to do in one visit make it more than one day . We took the anphicar tour around the lake , they start on land and then drive the car down the ramp in to the water . It is about 20 to 25 minutes long the driver tells you about the history of the cars/boats . Its next to the boathouse restaurant if you eat after the tour you bring the meal receipt to the counter where you paid for the tour they return $25.00 back to you. The restaurant is first class all the way great food. In the rear they have a vintage boat collection you can see free of charge even if you don't eat there worth taking a look. The balloon ride is awesome you will not get a better view of the area . Only if you fly over , while there take the free water taxi from one end of the park to the other with one stop in between.  These boats have an orange/red flag in front they are the free ones the others have purple/blue flags and go to near by hotels only if you are staying with them. There are plenty of things for the kids to see and enjoy.

We went there because the name sounded interesting and it was very nice.  The entrance fee was $20 for 2 people with vehicle. They give you a audio cd with map of the mountain you come to a sign that tells you to turn on the cd for narration. We saw wild deer along the road that didn't seem to mind us taking pictures of them . We stopped in the museum which seemed small but lots of information,  there was a cafeteria but didn't go over to it . We decided to see the animals the bears were out walking around saw 4 of them . They had a bald eagle looked huge it happened to spread its wings a nice surprise for a few seconds.  They also had elk only saw 2 of them . They have another enclosure we didn't go in it due to cleaning. The views are awesome,  the swinging bridge was nice didn't move much . Ths staff was friendly at the gift shop the attendant gave us some interesting details about the area very pleasant to speak to. Enjoyed this trip up to the top and then down would have liked to spend more time but was a little cold . A must do when in the area

This was the tour company,  they arrived on time to pick us up. The bus was clean and new it brings you to there location for you to get on the correct tour as they have several tours going on leaving from this location.  They have a small area for you to buy last minute coffee and drinks, snacks before you leave. They allow you to bring food and eat on the buses. The staff was very  helpful and polite they answered any questions you may have.  If I had booked my tour thru them on line direct we would have saved $20 dollars for each ticket .
We had the same bus we got picked up in for our tour ,each bus has a guide on board . They give you facts along the way of your tour and of places you pass famous people in the area that lived there and some people that still live there. Next time I will definitely book my tours thru them pick up and drop off at your hotel after a long day is great on your feet .
likes: Food and drinks allowed on bus
dislikes: Higher ticket price when not booked directly

reviews_attraction.text: The mountain was great its higher than I expected,  I didn't know there was an entrance fee but it was worth it.  The views are excellent you can see all around the area. The wild life is abundant we saw lots of wild deer along the road as long as you drive slowly they have no fear of the vehicle. The swing bridge was not as high as expected but nice to cross didn't swing for us as we were only two and no wind on that day . The gift shop was nice the staff was friendly lots of cute things to buy some bargains some over priced bug no pressure to buy any thing . The museum was small then you walk out to the area that has some animals.  The bears were out saw 4 of them  near the fence . The elk were to far for a good look . Didn't go to the fudge shop or the cafeteria.  Nice time will do again at  different season for the foliage change.

We stopped to eat and saw this little park not far from the restaurant actually on the same street. It has parking the entrance has a gate they close.  Located just before you enter are the restrooms and a soft drink machine , soon as you enter there is a children fountain pad area for them to get wet. We went on a  Sunday the sign said it shuts off 3 pm. They have benches for the parents to sit. This park is on the Indian river waterway,  there is a small dock for fishing or just watching the boats   traffic. If you bring your small children beware the dock doesn't have any  fencing you can just walk right off and into the water. The park is small a nice walk after a big meal . The photos show the entire park . We enjoyed it for an hour.

The best day to go is on sundays if you go  by car the area has plenty of meter parking which is free to park on sundays. Not much to eat in the area but for a good walk we enjoyed it.  There was a lot of boat traffic which very nice to see . Along the walk near the museum there was a stand that sells cold drinks and frozen ice pops. The public restrooms were open  , beware of children because they allow bicycles on the walkway.  Some riders were going a little fast and very close to people as you walk. But nice

I enjoyed this park it's on the water with great views.  A real nice place to watch the boat traffic go by . The park has 2 ramps for launching boats , one is newer the other is less used a bit in need of a make over but still usable.  They have an auxiliary coast guard office where you can take a safety boating class. The only drawback is parking it's limited so if you go in the afternoon the locals will get all the spots. I saw  a lot of people walking their dogs there are restrooms that were open .

We were in town and saw the lights in Patriot park.  The park is dedicated to the veterans they have a running, walking track. Near the river parking is free and near the Old Mill restaurant,  trolleys.  The walk is relaxing you can feed the ducks ,they have coin feeder machines you can buy feed and throw it at the ducks. The park is open 24  hours a day.  They hold different festival's thru out the year .They had a military display in lights for different branches of service.

This was our second time ridding the  ATV  rentals  . It was a blast but be prepared to get dirty bring a change of clothes they have a changing area . The staff was great our ride leader was awesome he gave great instructions and made sure everyone understood what was going on after the brief instructions.  It's off to the 4x4 ATV's and you are off for lots of fun and great memories. A must do if you can , we will be back soon .

We were on a tour trip when the driver told us that rams are the official wild animal of Neveda.  He stopped at this park , we got out to see the animals they were not afraid,  they just looked at us like wow more tourist with cameras.  They were amazing to see just relaxing and some feeding  on grass . The driver reminded us not to get to close these are wild animals and unpredictable. It was a great way to end the tour.

This is a great park to put your boat in the water,  the ramps are never over crowded.  They have three ramps . There are  bathrooms you can cross the street to buy snacks for your trip . There are lots of shops publix,  Jimmy John's, little ceasar pizza. The only thing I don't like is that there  is no area to wash boat , run your engines with fresh water. A nice place to get on the river .
dislikes: No fresh water for engine running

reviews_attraction.text: We pulled off the road to take in the views.  We wanted to stretch our legs from being in the vehicle for a long while. The views were nice you really can not tell how high you actually are. The parking area is a gravel parking area with a 2 foot high rail every one we saw climbed hop over it. So much for stopping any one from getting to close near the edge.

I remember going there as a child with my parents to fish and just walk around.  It has  changed so much , before there was no railing I would sit on the edge with a fishing pole seems so long ago. It looks nice the lot was paved very well on the day we went it was almost empty.  There was lots of broken glass on the road way . We were disappointed

A nice zoo very large be prepared to walk alot but once you get to the far end of the park they have a shuttle to get you back to the front entrance didn't really see that many animals as I expected. Park was clean didn't smell  bad . They charge a separate fee for some of the attractions doesn't seem fair. Not many food choices once inside.

This place is awesome the water is so clear you can just drink it right from the spring.  The manateess swim pass you like you are not there . I wish they had a larger parking lot it gets crowded. Parking is only $1 dollar an hour.  Worth spending time here if only to see the clear water and fish swimming by . Go early before  the crowd.

As a catholic I found the cathedral to be awesome,  its huge beautiful simply a wonderful place to see sit pray, even if you are of other faiths it will inspire you in ways only you can say. There were lots of tourists  walking around but everyone was organized  and very orderly.  We spent a short time but left very inspired

We got there late in the afternoon,  not crowded at all plenty of parking.  The beach had people keeping their distance from each other . The fishing pier was a little crowded, we didn't go to the end because of the crowd . Pier was clean the water was perfectly still. We will return early in the morning.
The park is very clean with clean restrooms. Lots of people walking dogs, most on leashes all seem friendly.  Tried fishing not much happening,  great for watching the boat traffic, free parking
I lived near this park for over a year and never new it was there . Liked it very much very nice and clean nice to bring the kids and the dog . Only downside is not much parking ,no bathrooms
Went there to bring the grand kids by boat, the sea wall is easy to moor the boat against plenty of kleets to tie up. Park was very cean with newer play area for the children. Lots of fun.
It was very crowded,  parking lot was far from the beach . The light house was open and went to the top it is 109 steps very hot going up. At the  top it has great  views.
I went with my 3 teenage daughter's they had a great time,  only one ride was not working. A good place to bring the kids.  Not crowded at all for a Sunday
Have seen other forts in Latin American countries, amazing how much a like they all are . Incredible technology considering how long ago they where built.
Park has construction going on , not well maintained.  It has horse shoe area that's dirty could be much better. There is a boat ramp
We went there to fish the  pier , price to go on the pier has gone up from 3.00 to 4.00 dollars . Fishing was not good

(Translated by Google) At first I thought about visiting this, because I had already visited the "Butterfly World" in Coconut Creek, but then decided on it and didn't regret it. Here too I can see thousands of colorful butterflies. Of course, there are also those that can hardly be distinguished from the surroundings, as they have camouflaged themselves well. But the "little ones" are just cute and lovely to look at. Small, colorful birds can also be found here. It's a real pleasure and I always enjoy looking at the photos that were taken there. And don't forget to thank every butterfly / bird for keeping still during the photo tour. In the adjoining shop, every visitor receives their very own butterfly, which reminds me of my visit every day.

A walk through Key West away from the so-called main street (s) is also worth seeing. Key West has some very nice (wooden) houses and front gardens. It is also not so crowded off the main street / s.

(Original)
Hatte erst überlegt, ob ich dieses besuchen soll, da ich bereits die "Butterfly World" in Coconut Creek besucht hatte, mich dann aber dafür entschieden und habe es nicht bereut. Auch hier kann ich Tausende bunt schillernde Schmetterlinge beobachten. Natürlich gibt es auch welche, die kaum von der Umgebung zu unterscheiden sind, da sie sich gut getarnt haben. Aber die "kleinen" sind einfach nur niedlich und herrlich anzusehen. Ferner sind hier ebenso kleine bunte Vögel anzutreffen.
