likes: Facilities & Services: Royal dining, Boutique services

reviews_attraction.text:
(Translated by Google) Inside the Norwegian pavilion, apart from enjoying the Frozen Ever After attraction, you can meet and interact with the sisters Anna and Elsa, protagonists of this famous story.
The site is called Royal Sommerhus, it is located right next to the Mexico pavilion.
The lines are usually very high.
The interesting thing is that the row enters a each totally acclimated with the royal family.

(Original)
Dentro del pabellón de Noruega, aparte de disfrutar de la atracción Frozen Ever After, puedes conocer e interactuar con las hermanas Anna y Elsa protagonistas de esta famosa historia.
El sitio se llama Royal Sommerhus, está ubicado justo al lado del pabellón de Mexico.
Las filas suelen ser muy elevadas.
Lo interesante es que la fila ingresa a una cada totalmente ambientada con la familia real.

(Translated by Google) This beautiful park is located in the heart of Kissimmee's care, right in front of an impressive and huge lake that gives you incredible landscapes. It is ideal to visit with the little ones of the house or with the pets, since it has facilities specially designed for the whole family.
Also if you want to make a family picnic.

(Original)
Este hermoso parque está ubicado en el corazón de la cuidas de Kissimmee, justo frente a un impresionante y enorme lago que te regala paisajes increíbles. Es ideal para visitar con los pequeños de la casa o con las mascotas, ya que tiene instalaciones especialmente diseñadas para toda la familia.
También si deseas hacer un picnic familiar.

(Translated by Google) The Moroccan pavilion is one of the most attractive due to its incredible architecture, decoration and attention to detail. Walking through its streets is like entering a Moroccan market.
You can buy souvenirs and typical objects of that African country.
Also at select times you can interact with Jasmine the princess of Aladdin.

(Original)
El pabellón de Marruecos es uno de los más vistosos por su increíble arquitectura, decoración y cuidado de los detalles. Caminar por sus calles es como adentrarse en un mercado marroquí.
Podrás adquirir souvenirs y objetos típicos de ese país africano.
También en horarios selectos podrás interactuar con Jazmín la princesa de Aladdin.

(Translated by Google) Right next to the Little Mermaid ride attraction, you can enjoy meeting and interacting with Ariel herself in her grotto.
This Ariel is sitting on a rock since she is in the body of a mermaid.
He is very friendly and you can use the Disney office photographer to take some photos with your camera or cell phone.

(Original)
Justo al lado de la atracción del viaje de la Sirenita, podrás disfrutar de conocer e interactuar con la mismísima Ariel en su gruta.
Esta Ariel se encuentra sentada sobre una roca ya que está en el cuerpo de sirena.
Es muy amable y puedes usar el fotógrafo oficinas de Disney para que tome algunas fotos con tu cámara o celular.

(Translated by Google) This attraction or ride inside Epcot quietly runs through the park's large greenhouse where much of the fruits, vegetables, vegetables and fish that are served throughout the Walt Disney World complex are grown and harvested. They seat you in a small boat that calmly travels the complex.

(Original)
Esta atracción o ride dentro de Epcot recorre de forma tranquila el gran invernadero del parque donde se cultiva y cosecha gran parte de las frutas, verduras, hortalizas y pescados que se sirven en todo el complejo de Walt Disney World. Te sientan en un pequeño bote que recorre tranquilamente el complejo.

(Translated by Google) The Italian pavilion within the World Showcase of Epcot is a very attractive one due to its gastronomy and architecture options.
It offers excellent options of photos, even at certain times you have Photopass photographers to capture the best moments in the company of family and friends.

(Original)
El pabellón de Italia dentro del World Showcase de Epcot es uno muy atractivo por sus opciones de gastronomía y la arquitectura.
Ofrece excelentes opciones de fotos, incluso en ciertos horarios tienes fotógrafos de Photopass para capturar los mejores momentos en compañía de la familia y amigos.

(Translated by Google) Impressive attraction where you can enjoy penguins, marine freaks, seals and other typical arctic species. The environment is excellently created and designed. The attraction can generate long lines during high and mid season.
It is one of the attractions that you cannot miss.

(Original)
Impresionante atracción donde podrás disfrutar de pingüinos, locos marinos, focas y otras especies típicas del ártico. El ambiente está excelente creado y diseñado. La atracción puede generar filas largas durante temporada alta y media.
Es una de las atracciones que no puedes dejar de visitar.

(Translated by Google) The United Kingdom Pavilion offers varied gastronomic options, souvenir shops typical of English culture and you can also enjoy good craft beers.
The pavilion offers excellent options and locations for photography.
Do not hesitate to try the famous Fish and chips.

(Original)
El Pabellón de reino unido ofrece variadas opciones gastronómicas, tiendas de souvenir típicas de la cultura inglesa y también podrás disfrutar de buenas cervezas artesanales.
El pabellón ofrece excelentes opciones y locaciones para fotografía.
No duden en probar las famosas Fish and chips.

(Translated by Google) Disney Hollywood Studios offers excellent spaces to meet and interact with personals. Among them are the protagonists of Disney junior: Dr. Toys, Sofia the first and the pirate Jack.
They also offer a live show in the best festive style with music and lots of fun.

(Original)
Disney Hollywood Studios ofrece excelentes espacios para conocer e interactuar con personales. Entre ellos están los protagonistas de Disney junior: Dra Juguetes, Sofía primera y el pirata Jack.
También ofrecen un show en vivo al mejor estilo festivo con música y mucha diversión.

(Translated by Google) This traditional attraction is similar to that of dumbo, it consists of small flying carpets to which you go up and they rotate, rise and fall and you can control this movement.
It is simple but ideal to share with the little ones in the house.

(Original)
Esta tradicional atracción es similar a la de dumbo, consiste en pequeñas alfombras voladoras a las cuales subes y ellas giran, suben y bajan y tu puedes controlar este movimiento.
Es sencilla pero ideal para compartir con los pequeños de la casa.

(Translated by Google) This is a small, comfortable and quiet ride that is located inside the Mexico pavilion.
Specifically within the pyramid.
The host is the Donald Duck. And it does a tour of the cultures and festivals of Mexico and its people.
Is recommended

(Original)
Este es un pequeño, cómodo y tranquilo ride que se ubica dentro del pabellón de Mexico.
Específicamente dentro de la pirámide.
El anfitrión es el pato donald. Y hace todo un recorrido por las culturas y fiestas de Mexico y sus pueblos.
Es recomendado

(Translated by Google) This new show up replaced the anti-bird show that had animal Kingdom.
Now it is the famous Russell and Dug who entertain the entire audience with wonderful acts involving exotic birds flying around the theater.

(Original)
Este nuevo show de up reemplazó al antigio show de aves que tenia animal Kingdom.
Ahora son los famosos Russell y Dug quienes entretienen a todo el público con maravillosos actos que involucran exóticas aves volando por todo el teatro.

This was the longest walking trail I have ever done. My Fitbit tracked down 7 miles worth of steps. These are the things I would do if I was to go again, I would print out the trail map in color, some of the markers throughout the trail are different colors and it's easier if you know the color of marker you should be going towards. The front entrance sign says no weapons, but I should of at least brought a knife, walking the trail you are able to tell there are large animals with large claws nearby, and I'm no Indiana Jones, but I would of felt more secure with a knife. There are no actual real city life- restrooms on the trail only the forest, so go before you go. There is no water on the trail, bring plenty to drink. Wear long pants! And go with someone who is not a drag. The trail is super long, super green, super quiet and super enjoyable. I will def be going again. I had an amazing time. I saw deer, cranes, a snake, possum, turkey, and I'm pretty sure the claw marks of a big cat. Can't wait to go back again.

Not the most exciting ride, but I do find it interesting. Science minded individuals may find this informative, but it's not for thrill seekers. We ride this when there is relatively no wait. The first portion of the ride travels through some scenes showing various natural environments and man's use of The Land. The second part is through Disney's "greenhouse" area, which explains new agricultural and other food production techniques being explored. I usually look for what is new in either food type or methods. The conveyance for this ride is a boat and it is another ride to rest your feet on. We usually swing by this ride after riding Soarin', check the line wait and get on if 10 minutes or shorter. Don't speed a lot of time waiting for this ride.

We had an absolute blast at Hogsmeade and all things Harry Potter ♥ First, before I say anything else, let me say that the Hagrid ride is worth the wait!!! It's the best ride of them all! We rode it 3 times while we were there (3 days) and it was worth the wait every time. The longest we waited was about and hour and 45 mins but the line moves quickly and alot of it in inside, so it doesn't seem that long. Of course, the food and everything else is very expensive. We got 3 soft pretzels and 2 waters and it was almost $40. It was cheaper for the 3 of us to eat at the Three Broomsticks for lunch than it was to buy those pretzels. We were also disappointed that a chocolate frog from Honeydukes is $12!!! So expensive.

Soarin’ is one of our top must do rides at WDW. It’s one of three at Epcot that we always try to get Fast Passes for. We liked both the original American Adventure flight and the current World flight. We love the details, like the smell of the surf as you cruise over an ocean. The top row of the ride is the best because you don’t see the other riders below you. This helps suspend the sense that it’s a ride and Not an actual hang glider. Beware though that on the top row the screen is rounded slightly, causing a minor warping of scenery. Sort of like a cat’s eye effect. Definitely worth a wait if you have to go through the Stand-by line. Try going first thing in the morning to avoid the longest lines.

To start with the guys and girls who operate this fantastic service we’re of the HIGHEST of professionalism. The office space is spotless clean. Toilets are very clean. Helicopter was both extremely clean inside and out. The pilot was of the highest standard and knowledgeable. The whole experience was nothing short of amazing. On my resent trip to Orlando, I asked my son “what would make this once in a lifetime trip”, he just said “a helicopter ride would mean everything to him”. I thought that this would be difficult as I tried in New York and unfortunately couldn’t make this happen. But on my trip to Orlando, this was possible. Only because of the professional attitude of the staff here.

We decided to take the $25 helicopter tour and it was worth every penny (cent). The lady on reception was very professional and explained the flight and photograph options. We decided not to go for the $40 photo pack. Once paid for, you get weighed in. We were a party of 3 and were really excited to experience our first helicopter ride. The crew take pictures of you as you enter the helicopter and get buckled in. The Pilot was very polite and we were soon flying high over sea world with a running commentary. It's really good to see places from a birds eye view and you can see Orlando city in the distance. I could have stayed up there for ages, it was simply brilliant !

We had an absolute blast at Hogsmeade and all things Harry Potter ♥ First, before I say anything else, let me say that the Hagrid ride is worth the wait!!! It's the best ride of them all! We rode it 3 times while we were there (3 days) and it was worth the wait every time. The longest we waited was about and hour and 45 mins but the line moves quickly and alot of it in inside, so it doesn't seem that long. Of course, the food and everything else is very expensive. We got 3 soft pretzels and 2 waters and it was almost $40. It was cheaper for the 3 of us to eat at the Three Broomsticks for lunch than it was to buy those pretzels.

We took our two sons here during some family time to have some out of the sun fun, and it did not disappoint. Three floors of fun with different areas for different ages. We have been to lots of these around the globe, and although nit as big as some, the OSC is right up there in the rankings. The facilities are nice and clean, and the staff were very nice, helpful, and professional. The large number of staff during our visit was a welcomed change from some science museums we've visited which are more messy and have a free for all atmosphere. Bonus - our membership to our local equivalent got us in free. Highly recommend.

If you plan to visit Fun Spot I totally recommend visiting Mark at the gokarts. He was so awesome. It was my daughters first time riding a gokart and she was a little nervous to drive them, and he took his time out to teach her the ropes and made her feel comfortable. I really appreciated that, he was the only one to do so. Because of this interaction I made it a point to let Mark’s manager, Joel, know. And it makes sense why Mark does his job so well, Joel was so professional and hospitable. If you plan on visiting funspot soon make sure you pay Mark and Joel a visit, you won’t regret it! We will be back soon. :)

I absolutely love visiting Universal's Wizarding World! It is like stepping into the pages of a beloved story for sure. That being said, I do wish there were more rides associated with that part of the park, especially on the Diagon Alley side. I love wandering through the shops but it bums me out that Escape from Gringotts is the only ride there. It's a great ride, but I'd love to see more experiences. The new ride in Hogsmeade is AMAZING! Keep adding rides like that and we will keep returning!! We just returned from our third trip and will definitely return...especially if they add some new rides :-).

Upon walking in we were greeted by Justin. He gave us a warm smile and was very nice. Justin advised us about our trip and we were able to get the best prices and most fun for our money. He was very knowledgeable and happy to help. The decor of the visitors center was amazing. We were able to walk around and take pictures while we waited. The center has a lot of information, it is for everything. Not just for theme park tickets. The promotions they have are great. There are no long lines to get tickets. I fully recommend the visitor center and fully recommend you talk to Justin.

Trinity @ Ripley’s Wax Hands was amazing and very accommodating! She worked with us to get every part of our wax hand sculpture to our very specific requests. She went above and beyond to make sure we had a great experience and came out with something better than we had expected. Would definitely give her a 5 star rating and would recommend the experience with Trinity. In addition to being great with our wax hands, she was very helpful to give us Orlando restaurant recommendations! Yamasan Sushi and Grill was an amazing recommendation and it was all because of Trinity!

I went out with my fiance and my friend. We arrived on the earlier side so it wasnt very busy. The cover charge is reasonable, drinks a little expensive but you're paying for the experience. They have a non-ice bar section with a spacious range floor. The actual ice bar is so cool (pun not intended, but fitting)!! EVERYTHING is ice!! Even the bar and the drink glasses. There's a few little novelty areas that are good for a photo-op. If you're having a night on the town, I would definitely recommend hitting this place up

Used a Groupon for a decent deal. There are a lot more live gators around the place than anticipated as well! An employee treated us to a feeding time show while we were playing on the front 9. Interesting and unexpected extra. The holes are in decent shape and challenging enough to be fun. There were about 8 or 9 other parties on the 18 holes while we played, but the pace was O.K. We rarely had to wait more than 2 or 3 minutes at anytime to proceed to our next hole. Overall, it was pretty fun time.

If you feel like having a quiet morning or afternoon surrounded by nature this is an excellent place to go. Its a great place to just unplug yourself from everything for a bit in the middle of everything. Just keep in mind to take a bottle of water with you and maybe something to munch on while you're there since the gardens are quite large and takes at least an hour to see everything at an enjoyable walking pace. There are lots of beautiful flowers and plants that grow locally.

We’ve always stayed near here on our 3 visits over the last 8 years and found this a nice little nighttime activity. Usually wasting some money in the arcade and watching the slingshot... not brave enough to actually do! Haven’t ever done the go-karts, they always sound very rickety on the track but guess no issues as been there so long. Little ice cream place bit disappointing as don’t have half of what they advertised. Staff always been friendly when we’ve needed them.

We’ve been to a lot of art museums, so I was really surprised when we didn’t enjoy this one as much. I spent most of that time wondering how some of these pieces were even considered art. The majority of the pieces in the museum were from the last few decades. There were a lot of political and cultural pieces. If there were a docent that could point out the significance of the pieces or the artist’s background, I think I would have enjoyed it a lot more.

As a first timer in ghost adventures, I enjoyed the experience and learning about Orlando's past in the process. I was able to help Identify a young 11yr old girl spirit named Jane who's mom use to work in the old brothel house. Our tour guide Christina was very knowledgeable about the area and its past residents. She made it a fun experience for myself and the other guests who also included 2 young kids and their parents. Give the tour a chance!

This place is geared for kids and adults; just enough for all ages. A lot of different ways/display styles to present in an Aquarium. A lot of information given for everything in there and not lengthy info; just the right amount. It was bigger than I expected. Places to sit along the way. Better than most aquariums I have visited. You will enjoy. If you stop in the gift shop, Quintisha is really helpful; not sure I spelled her name correctly.

This was our second time doing the R.I.P tour. Our tour guide Logan was excellent! He really did an amazing job with our group. He explained every Maze and Zone in full detail. He even went though each one with us. Our tour guide last year didn't go through each one with us and it really makes a difference. The best part of the tour is no waiting in line for anything. It is worth every penny and we will be doing the R.I.P tour again next year

We had about a half day to visit, but you could spend lots more the here. The "eye doesn't start to run until noon. Lots of restaurants and other things to do in the park area. There's an acquarium, wax museum, etc. The ride on the wheel is very smooth, and relaxing. You can see lots of Orlando and surrounding attractions. Even if you are afraid of heights, the enclosed cabin gives one a secure feeling. Take your time and enjoy yourself.

We are locals and have played quite a few of the miniature golf courses in the Orlando area. This course is the most attractive, well-maintained and FUN course we have played to date. Every employee was friendly. We appreciate the military discount, and the course was just challenging enough to provide competitive fun. We will definitely take out-of-town guests to Pirate's Cove for miniature golf.

The best experiences were in Universal's Island of Adventure! So many character meet and greets, awesome rides for all ages, the food is delicious and large portions, and the customer service is top notch! Hulk is incredible, my son loved Spiderman so much he rode it 4 times in a row - the water rides were perfect to cool down on, and everything is so clean!! Best time and highly recommend!

Thoroughly enjoyed our shuttle ride with Madelyn’s interesting facts about Florida and the Orlando area. The wildlife was interesting, the food at the Chomp Shack quite good! Madeline made sure everyone’s needs were met and we were in the right place at the correct time. Thoroughly enjoyed the airboat excursion with Matt! Great value all around for the cost of the trip!!

Wasn't really looking forward to visiting Madame Tussaud's but really glad that I did. Visitors are encouraged to 'interact' with the figures with props provided to help make the photos look better. Unlike the British versions where everything is behind ropes, this place really is a breath of fresh air. Great afternoon.

If you have kids, they will love it. They have a treasure hunt and some cool exhibits that kids will love. If you are a pirate fan like me, you will enjoy it as well. If you don't care about pirates but like history, you might enjoy it. They don't take American Express, don't have wifi and little pricey.

It's more of a zoo and that's not a bad thing. The animal spotting was really good. They also have a playground for kids, zip lines and a hiking trail. Not to mention a museum. The Cafe has wifi and the food isn't bad. You could easily spend all day here with the family and they will love it.

It was once a very active park. Back in the day when kids were allowed outside. It had a hotdog stand and pool open all summer.  Basket ball league, baseball and softball league. Equipment for kids to play on. Now, except when there is an event going on, it's a ghost town.

This is where the nightlife is. Put on your Sunday's best and picked up all the single ladies on vacation. They have clubs, restaurants and entertainment at the Citywalk. You will enjoy yourself if it's just hanging out with family or out with friends.

Family fun part of the park. Wait times are low and all rides are suitable for children. Has some eateries and a great dessert place. However no place serves breakfast in the area and Green Eggs & Ham eatery never seems to be open.

It's a fun area to hang out with family or friends. Shops, beaches and some rides. Parking can be a pain at times but the parking garage is usually never filled. My only complaint, no public wifi and quite a bit of panhandlers.

It's a park on both sides of the inlet. It has a place for swimming, site seeing, camping sites, picnic areas, child playground, fresh water, hiking trails, bike trails and many fishing areas. Only complaint, no public wifi.
It's free. No reason not to go. They have many exhibits and the museum is quite large. You will learn quite a bit and be impressed by the artifacts. Highly recommend this place. However, no wifi.
The zoo part is cool. It's fun to see the animals. However, the food at the park is absolutely horrible and there is no public wifi. The front desk seems short handed. No hand sanitizer anywhere.
Fun little tour around the town. Good way to get around the town, has many stops except they don't go to St Augustine Beach and they stop at 4 which is ridiculous. Way too early.
They have wifi, the price is reasonable and they don't just have cars. Sports, movie, Native American and everything else that is Americana is on display here. Really cool place.
If you are by the Old Jail, I say check it out. Especially if you take the trolley. You can get free admission. However, there is no reason to go out of your way for this one.
It's a roller-coaster that will not push you around. It's good for all ages and most people will enjoy it. I prefer the seven dwarf mine roller-coaster in Magical Kingdom.
It's amazing to read the story behind the legend. The artifacts where amazing and it's just fascinating what you will learn about that tragic day. It's worth admission.
The park system is quite large and there is much to do. From hiking, to kayaking to camping. They have some stores and access to the beach. However no Wi-Fi.
It's an amazing experience, that's for sure. Absolutely gorgeous. I wish they used improved technology of Soarin. 3D goggles can give some a headache.
It's not a horrible roller-coaster but it's nothing great. It's short and doesn't seem a good investment in time to wait for this ride.
I love Daytona Beach. It's my kind of town. But, I am not going to lie, the Downtown / intercoastal area could use some renovations.
Hands down the best ride in the park. If this is where VR is going, then it will be absolutely amazing when it hits the home market.
It is one of the more interesting museums in the area. It's completely free and gives you a good history lesson of St. Augustine.
Worst ride in the park. Not fun. It would have just been more relaxing without the stupid seats shaking. It's a waste of time.
It's not worth wasting a fast pass for. It's okay. The captain was more amusing then the ride. It is a great ride for kids.
A condense live version of the movie with some special effects. If you like the movie, you will enjoy the show.
If it was a little longer, be my favorite coaster in the park. Doesn't push you around. Great coaster for kids.
Fun little ride with a splash. You will not get extremely wet. It's great to cool down on a hot day.

I've heard the heroic story many times and was glad to see the new memorial. Although the main entrance is right off of Route 30 it's several miles to the crash site. First is the Tower of Voices, a 93 foot tower that will have 40 chimes, one for each victim. After that is the visitors center which contains display cases and artifacts from both the attack and the crash. The visitor center is on a hill overlooking the crash site and has a deck to overlook the surrounding fields. To get to the crash site you can either drive to the lower parking lot or walk the trail. Once there you have a path that leads to the memorial. As you head to the memorial you pass the actual crash site, marked with a boulder. Although you can get very close you can't access the crash site. The memorial is a long marble wall with the victims names. It's lined up on the exact path the flight took its final seconds. A wooden fence gives another view of the crash site from the direction the plane was traveling.

There are some nice rides here I'll give them that. The water park is also very nice with some great slides. However it definitely falls short of its Pennsylvania competitors. First off the rules are much stricter than competing parks. There are all so unnecessary rules such as two people per car on wild mouse and no picture taken from the Train, neither of these rules exist in nearby competing parks. Parking is also very pricey I paid $20 after 4 p.m. by far the best part of the park is the Thunder Canyon River Rapids ride as well as white water landing shoot the shoot ride as well as Thunder Creek Mountain log flume. Thunderhawk and steel Force we're alright but there are better coasters out there. With a little help this part could be much better but it's not like it's a terrible Park.

This is more of a community park than amusement park. Many of the offerings are offered at most community parks such as a playground, basketball court, volleyball court,  and batting cages. Skyliner is a decent coaster but a little rough. The go karts were nice as well. I didn't ride the train or antique cars but they looked decent. I don't understand why they need more than one miniature golf course, feels like that space could be used for something else. Leap The Dips was closed. If you come add something  else to your itinerary because you're only going to need a few hours. I enjoyed my visit but will only return when Leap The Dips reopens.

Two very different attractions in one. The cave is completely filled with water and you have to go through on a long boat. The tour guide must very good and showed details about the cave. You can't get out of the boat under any circumstances. The wild life tour is going out into their wild life area on a bus with a tour guide who takes you out to the various areas and shows you the animals. The tour guide was very good and offered treats to lure the animals over. You could tell there was a bond between the guide and the animals. Many of the animals weren't open ranches and could come close to our bus While others were in zoo like cages.

This is a great historical site that's best remembered for the Battle Of Baltimore in the War Of 1812. Not only was the city saved from further invasion but Frances Scott Key witnessed the battle and wrote the Star Spangled Banner to reflect how he felt when he saw the American flag flying instead of a British flag. The fort has seen lots of other history as well. During the American Civil War opponents of the war were imprisoned there. It was also used as a hospital during WWI. Visits are self guided however ragers are on site and do have programs to help the experience.

This building is very old. The dungeon has a long history from imprisoned pirates to prisoners captured by the British during the American Revolution to the storage and hiding of gunpowder. The dungeon is a guided tour while the rest of the building is self guided and includes a meeting room where representatives were sent to the Congress on the eve of the American Revolution as well as where South Carolina accepted the US constitution. George Washington also danced in the hall.

I didn't camp here but did manage to walk around the northside of the lake. The area is perfect for picnics and cookouts as it has seats and grills. There is also a concession stand, a sandbox, and playground. The lake itself is nice. One side allows boat renting and fishing and the other allows swimming. My only concern is that I didn't see lifeguards. However park rangers are able to quickly evacuate the lake as a thunderstorm closed in.

Great gem of a a park. Much of it is a walking trail around small creak with bridges and a gazebo. I was there in February and there were hundreds of ducks in the creek. It was also a small Caboose from 1942 that was open to the public; if open check it out. In the back of the park (which was almost completely abandoned because it was February) picnic areas and a band shell.

I went here knowing the visitor center was closed because of Covid-19. I knew little about this particular battle. It was a little tricky to get around but with the help of Google maps I found my way. Not knowing much about the battle wasn't an issue because there's so many billboards explaining the battle that was more than enough information to understand the battle.

This is one of the best 9/11 memorials I've seen. There's a steel beam from the World Trade Center. Around the loop are glass panels with the names of all the victims. A keystone symbol is next to the ones from Pennsylvania. At the center of the loop are the names of the victims from Bucks County.

I enjoyed this great track. There were several betting areas along with restaurants and concession stands. All looked clean and functional. The grandstand is enclosed and has great views. The only problem is that the grandstand isn't air conditioned.

A great place to overlook the Susquehanna River. The building has a museum and an outdoor deck. There's also a small walking trail and a boat ramp. If you come late in the day remember you are facing west and might have to deal with the sun.
Some of the best architecture around. Every inch of the building is stunning. When not on a tour, they let people walk around the building for free, after a security check point.
One of the best parks I've ever been to. Loads of trails to walk, a nice stream and pond. There are playgrounds and open spaces. Geese and ducks roam freely. Truly a hidden gem.
I love walking this historic bridge. Steel truss bridges are hard to find. Of course not dealing with cars is a bonus. Great views of Harrisburg and City Island too.
Great place to see Florida plant life and wildlife. I just loved seeing plants in their natural habitat I don't see back home. Very peaceful too.
I love walking through this tunnel. It's old and feels abandond. Very quiet with only nature around. Just wish it was closer to a parking lot.
A nice small garden that's free to visit. Conveniently located near Riverfront Park. Unfortunately I saw some homeless sleeping in the gazebo.
A nice little memorial. Pictures of the timeline of the war surround the monument. Conveniently located across from the State House.
Mostly just a deep wooded park with a boat ramp. It's nice to get up close and personal with wildlife and get views of the river.
Great airtime and surprisingly smooth, it's everything a wooden coaster should be and not anything a wooden coaster shouldn't be.
I'm not much for flowers but I can respect the vast selection of flowers here. Be sure to return in October for Pumpkin Glow.
Very nice view, saw four cargo trains in 35 minutes. Rail car only runs every 30 minutes but steps also lead to the top.
Very quiet and laid back and mostly wilderness. Yes there are wild horses but don't pet them, they are wild.
Great little zoo but wish they would reopen the front. Be careful, Druid Hill Park is not a good area.

At least once, go ahead visit this spot and the museum nearby that commemorates John F Kennedy, the US president who was assassinated here.
Controversies and conspiracy theories aside, visiting this piece of American history will leave you sober and serious. The spot marks the place where shots were fired at JFK to which he succumbed.
Although, the displays in the museum recount the life and the moments before and after his death, they also offer a profound hope for the nation to never bow down to any adversity that may come.
Controversial during his presidency, the event made the president rise in our conscious memory and estimation, not because of his politics but because of the price he paid for his convictions. The spot makes this a destination worthy of a pilgrimage.

Entertain, inform, fascinate...and on the way of doing that, educate all comers to vistas and mysteries of our cosmos. Exhibits about our solar system, Galaxy and the universe abound with a great number especially designed for younger patrons. space travel is another theme. Multiple theater like settings provide ongoing presentations. Additionally, Doan observatory offers a study through the 20" telescope. The day we were there, it was aimed towards Jupiter and it's moons. Whether you are interested in astronomy or cosmology, Adler is a great place to visit. Many amenities round out the experience.

Great family outing that seeks to recreate mostly European influence in populating Wisconsin. Staff and volunteers in period attire help the visitors learn and enjoy. The day we visited, hogs were being butchered outdoors in one part of the facility for demonstration. If you get tired, trolleys will transport you to different destinations within. On site restaurant and gift shop. If you or your family are sensitive to such things as hogs being slaughtered, read the information on their public demonstrations and avoid the one(s) that are hard on your sensibilities.

Experience a desert oasis, a tropical jungle and floral gardens . . .all in one afternoon! The Mitchell Park Horticultural Conservatory, better known as The Domes, is one of the most unique destinations in Milwaukee.
Discover cacti, succulents, shrubs and desert palms in the Desert Dome. Enjoy five seasonal shows each year in the Floral Dome and walk among 1,200 species of rainforest plants in the Tropical Dome.
The Domes are open every day of the year and host special events and educational programs throughout the year.

Honeymoon Island got its name from a Life Magazine contest for newlyweds in 1939; couples won a two-week honeymoon stay on the island. Many photos of these love birds can be viewed at The Rotary Club Centennial Nature Center. After the initial enchantment wore off, name still stuck. Now operated as a State park, it features beautiful beaches and natural habitat. There is a "per vehicle" entry fee. Plentiful parking, restrooms and other amenities. Pets are permitted on one of the beaches.
likes: Facilities & Services: Plentiful parking, restrooms, amenities

reviews_attraction.text: A working rehabilitation aquarium in Clearwater, Florida on the Gulf Coast, the CMA lives by it's mantra of Rescue, Rehab, Release. A working aquarium with hospital (including surgery) and rehab services and a dedicated rescue team has worked with numerous marine animals and after appropriate treatment, release them to their natural habitat (if feasible). A great place to learn about it's mission. With an ongoing expansion, it will be able to continue to serve it's mission even better.

Long history of the region comes alive through engaging exhibits, presentations, films and interactive displays. Truly a great learning place that tells the story of the area since the pre Columbus days. The displays are interesting enough for the youngest of children yet informative and thoughtful for adults and other history buffs. The iconic Columbia Restaurant has a cafe here serving some of the same dishes as the mother ship. Put this History Center on your itinerary.

Oh, the views you would have! Whether watching the sunrise over lake Michigan, or the moonrise on the lake...or the view of the cityscape leaves one mesmerized. No wonder it is a destination by itself during summer. Bring a picnic pac and stay a while. Parking is a bit tough to find and often becomes very limited during special events but go round and round and you are bound to score a spot. Worth waiting for. Gathering places for both skywatchers and citywatchers.

It raises the eternal question, why did the chicken cross the road? To get to the Centennial Park, of course. And as a matter of course, the chicken, hordes of them of all ages and gender, cross into the park with no fear. For people, the park is a nice refuge from the maddening crowds just a block or two from Ybor. Chicken friendly restaurants (no KFC or Chick-fil-A here) and interesting stores that sell touristy knick knacks surround the place. Worth a stroll.

One of the finest collections of art and sculpture in the USA. Rotating exhibits and special displays never cease to amaze. One can spend days here without exhausting the numerous collections that have come from all over the world. Beautifully laid out with sitting areas interspersed with displays keeps you engaged without getting you tired out. Various amenities to make your visit more enjoyable abound. A must when you are in Chicago.

Whether you want to watch sail boats, airplanes or take in a picnic or children's play time, you're arrived at the ideal place. Just relax and have fun as you let your senses take in what surrounds you. A wonderful spot for children and grown up children alike. The play area has beautiful equipment with an avionics theme and kids seem to enjoy their imaginary playtime. Be a kid for a day and you would be hooked to return.

Starting out with a whimsical and quirky notion, over time the House in the Rock has become a major attraction that welcomes visitors from all over. Divided into three segments for ease of navigation, it seems to offer something for everyone, sometimes even overwhelming your senses and sensibilities. To do justice to the displays, allow at least a good three hours, perhaps more. Even then, you would have only just begun.

Oh, the fun you will have! I was at the playground with four grandchildren ranging from 22 months to four years old. I think adults had as much fun as the children. State of art playground equipment including on demand sprinkler area had the children excited and busy. They didn't want to leave. If you want your kids (or grandchildren or other kids) to have fun and be busy, take them here.

Seventy acres of natural beauty with plenty of amenities such as a baseball diamond, rest rooms, picnic areas, playgrounds, nature trails, parking and much more offer a beautiful respite in this somewhat secluded setting. Great for children, small or large groups or just a place to hang out. Two entrances, north and south lead you to the parking areas. Fun for the entire family.

Kids love the, oh so close to you, exhibits of creatures from long ago that you can almost touch. Activity room for kids. Outdoor exhibits. Home of Carthage Paleontology Institute where recent digs are processed. A local gem. Admission is free, however, a donation box is located at the entrance to the exhibits. A sign there recommends a donation of $3. Donation is voluntary.

A showcase of horticultural exhibits as part of Milwaukee County's park system offers multiple observation trails, learning opportunities and a place to relax. It includes a special collection of designated by the American Hostas Society as a National Display Garden. Seasonal exhibits abound. Plenty of places to sit and enjoy the scenery, as well. Great experience.

Great, balanced and factual perspective of a sad era in US history. Scores of hands on exhibits, library, gift shop and a conference room etc make it a comprehensive facility. Well assembled and curated collection. Reasonable entrance fee. A unique museum for a northern state in the US. Popular for school field trips. Very nice educational experience.

Nice park by lake Michigan dockside with multi features such as a playground, water play, open field, picnic benches, beach areas, toilet facilities etc. In season vendors with snacks and other popular food items. Nicely landscaped areas. Plenty of no cost parking. No entrance fee. The park promises a fun-filled, enjoyable outing for all age groups.

Hands on experience for children in a number of different areas. Popular and greatly enjoyable active museum for activities that will keep your children occupied for hours in play learning and creative fun including a play grocery store, restaurant, theater etc. Creative art projects teach wonderful skills.

A dream of a playground, with enough equipment to entertain a crowd without getting crowded. A good number of equipment is adaptive or accommodative for children with disabilities. Very pleasant place to be. A nearby shelter can be used for special events. There was evidence of good maintenance.

Protected marine area ideal for watching Manatees, sharks and other marine life. Learning center, gift shop, amenities. Hands on activities and several walking trails. Plenty of parking. Fun and enjoyment for the whole family.

The historic basilica is a continually operating church with a historied background. A beautiful structure and setting that lends itself to respect and reverence, whether you are a believer or not. Enjoyable visit.
This historical but working building should be on your go to list for its architecture and rotating displays.  No entrance fee. Great place to dabble in a bit of Chicago history and Chicago issues.
Whether you are there for a simple walk, corporate shindig or a special event, it is a wonderful destination. Perhaps take a picnic lunch with you and enjoy the outdoors.
Acres and acres of garden like setting for all to enjoy. Kids will have fun in children's garden. Indoor or outdoor space for special occasions or corporate outings.

This our second visit to Suwannee campground.  We really enjoy the solitude and quiet suroundings except for the ocssional train passing by right outside the park.
Last time we were here we walked the trail along the river under the very large hardwoods. It is great easy walk to view the springs feeding the river and the many ponds.
This trip we took a walk to the Confederate earthworks that were camping grounds during the Civil War. This is near the junction of the Suwannee and Withlacoochee rivers.  Along the way there are some artifacts of a steamboat that proceeded the railroads.  The signage could be better as there was no mentioned of the what, where, why other than the plaque below.  The other trail led us past some family cemetary plots most dated late 1800's to early 1900's.  A few children were buried here...heartbreaking. This is called the Sandhill Trail.  One other interesting fact is the old stage coach route runs right through the park.  I wish there was more historical data available here at the park. The walks peaked our interest.  Possibly there is but we didn't find any like many other Florida State Parks.

Love this park!  Yes it is remote but the scenery is spectacular.  The rangers are especially friendly everywhere we went. At the border crossing we spent a good hour in the checkin building recovering from the heat and talking to the Ranger.  I believe we were one of the few people crossing the river into Mexico that day.  We spent two nights at the RV campground within the park.  This is not the attraction here but it does have full 50 amp hookups.  Air Conditioning was a welcome relief from the desert's heat. The mountains and desert floor make for a natural border between the US and Mexico in this area of Texas. The Border Patrol monitor the few roads in and out of the area.  I can't wait to visit again.

Awesome experiences for the grand children. The glass bottom boat trip to the coral reef was very educational. One of the best places to kayak.  A lot of protected waterways to explore.  We enjoyed it very much.  We clamped at the campgrounds with full hookups 2 week maximum stay at one time.  The Park Service does not treat for marauding mosquitoes.  So come prepared to fight the battle.  I probably need more education on this but it seems to me that mosquitoes can do more harm to humans than we could ever inflict on them.  One person catching the Zika virus is one too many!

Avery Island has been on our bucket list for a long time.  The visit there was awesome.  The Jungle Gardens has a little bit of everything from alligators to beautiful birds and trees.  Best of all if you don't wish to walk the trail you can stay in your vehicle and see it all.  We enjoyed the factory tour and musem at the Tobasco plant.  The history and artifacts are well documented.  This a true American family sucess story. RV's are welcomed but I would call ahead because parking could be a challenging.

We camped in the park.  Loved the covered patios.  Mornings were so pleasant under the shelter taking in the vistas from all sides.  The only downside was the lack of Internet service.  Some people might consider that a blessing.  A short drive to the top of nearby mountain provides service.  Visit the restored lodge.  It is an incredible building that dates back to 1933. We loved our time here so peaceful and fellow campers were so friendly.  It is back on our bucket list for a longer stay!

This Florida State Park lacks a personality. We also found out upon arival that the bath house was in the process of being rebuilt.  Not a nice surprise!  This is the first Florida State Park campground that we will not return to.  As Tampa continues its urban sprawl it will eventually become surrounded by developments of single family homes. It might become an oasis with plenty of property at its disposal at later date.  Right now 50 amp service is its saving grace.

This was a fascinating stop.  We were able to chat with one of the archeologists that is involved in restoring and  preserving artifacts from a British ship that sunk right outside of St. Augustine in the late 1700 hundreds. He was one of the divers that brought many of the artifacts to the surface.  He went to London to research the vessel and was well versed in the history sorrounding the sinking of the ship.  The site is way more than restored lighthouse!

Very nice, very quiet, very clean...but very narrow camp slots!  We are here at the end of April and the park is sparsely populated.  What is nice is its close proximity to both Naples and Marco Island.  We didn't get a chance to kayak because of family get togethers but it looked very promising.  We are going to return in the future. We were pleasantly surprised that the bugs were not as bad as we expected.

This is a very small State park, but a very nice State park.  Well maitained and most camping sites feel very secluded. Unfortunately is was a one night stand. We wish we could have stayed longer. We will return and use the convenient kayak launch site. Its proximity th The Villiages I think makes it very popular. It is populated with very large old Live Oak Trees. They are massive.

A nice place to camp the foliage provides a feeling of privacy. We stayed in a pull through site.  If you been here before you might have felt the bridge over the river was a bit tight.  That has been fixed.  The bridge is now paved and a lot wider. We like this park because it is close to some of FL best beaches and boating with restaurants right on the bay and intercoastal.

Re-visiting my childhoods favorite places.  Feel in love with the Silver River all over again.  I love that the Florida park system has taken over some of Florida's iconic tourist attractions. The water is crystal clear and the kayaking is great.  We took the glass bottom tour and was re-introduced to the history of the area.

We were at Capt. Andersons 2 days before hurricane Michael for Priates Days event.  We have eaten at the restaurant a few times in the past and it was very good.  The childern were having a great time.  It is also a good place to watch the fishing boats return with their catch of the day.

Full hookups and abeautiful river to kayak.  The white sandy beaches are a perfect place for a picnic. A isolated and quit place to camp.  The bath houses are excellent.  Swimming from the beaches are great for the kids.  The park also has a playground for the young ones.

We have been there several times.  The scenery is awesome when the cruise ships are gone.  The street entertainers can be overly agressive at times, but it is a great place to watch the sunset. When the ships are in port it gives you an opportunity to see them up close.

Campground is very nice.  We stopped there for two nights on our way north in early May.  The park was fairly empty diring the week. We enjoyed full hookups.  The lake is for human powered boats only.  The Rangers have many programs for the kids during the season.

Love this place.  It is late April and it seems that the park is open for only a select few. The water is crystal clear and the ramps to launch a small boat, kayak or canoe is perfect.  The camp ground near by is very nice and has access to the river.

Short walk or drive to the beach.  Boardwalk not as long as TopSail State Parks.  Beach is awesome and deserted in September. 30A is so nice not many high rises.  Seaside has a nice collection of restaurants some with views of the Gulf.
A very nice campground. Very dispersed campsites with extremely clean bathrooms.   They also have a family bathroom with shower at the lakeview campgrounds.  We had a 50 amp circuit with water.
Very nice campground.  Only stayed one night but it was very easy in and out close to town.  Many pull thru sites not necessary to even diconnet the toad.
Allways a treat to visit Disney Springs.  New restaurants to choose from brings excitement.  We dined at Wine Bar George and it was excellent.
Been here several times.  It is wonderful that this place is preserved in the middle of Hilton Head Island a very popular tourist destination.
We took some friends here for a visit to the welcome center.  We have been here several times over the years and enjoy the views and solitude.
It is a fantastic ride back in history that is being restored for all to experience.  Looking for a over active beach community...stay home.
When we visited the park the granite was 130°.  Be aware also of the danger to your pet.  5 dogshave died recently under these conditions.
Very interesting out of the way.  Massive structure cosideting the time period.  Much larger than the steam cannon on Hilton Head Island.

Muy buena adaptación de la película. Un show estilo Broadway. Si vale la pena verlo.

(Translated by Google) Very quiet park for walking, with a peculiar style and very close to the sea.

(Original)
Parque muy tranquilo para caminar, con un estilo peculiar y muy cerca del mar.

(Translated by Google) A show for young children, in which they teach them to be Jedi.

(Original)
Un show para niños pequeños, en los que les enseñan a ser Jedi.

(Translated by Google) Is incredible. Just great. Nothing like being there.

(Original)
Es increíble.  Simplemente genial.  Nada como estar ahí.

I always thought that there was only the dinosaur museum and the gardens at Thanksgiving Point, but boy was I wrong. The Museum of Natural Curiosity is a blast for kids and adults alike. The gardens are beautiful. The butterfly habitat is incredible and houses such beautiful creatures. The dinosaur museum won't disappoint either. It's fantastic. I would recommend getting the yearly family pass. It's worth it if you go more than once and you'll want to.

I am a huge fan of this place. It has SO much to do for children of all ages, and I even found myself entertained and engaged on some things. They have the building separated into sections. Each section has a lot to offer. If possible get the season pass for your family. It allows you to go as often as you'd like, this giving you time to see everything at this museum because there's so much to see.

I went into this one skeptical in that I wasn't sure that a butterfly exhibit would hold both mine and my kids' attention for long. I was wrong. This place was great! Beautiful things to see. Lots to learn and explore, and an amazing experience where everyone got to see and hold butterflies. We found that the kids wanted to go back!

While I don't skate, I do have a dog and children. This is a fun quiet little playground for my kids and a good time for my dog to run around off leash. It's completely fenced in. Has water stations and drinking fountains for the dogs. There are two different dog sections. One for smaller breeds and one for larger breeds.

Beautiful to see for Mormons and nonmormons alike. I can appreciate the architecture and history even though I may not be a member of their church. Just beware that the missionaries there will attempt to convert you. They are nice, however, and are good tour guides.

This park has gone way down hill and isn't worth going to anymore. Firstly, they tore down the castle. It is now an eyesore with a fence around it. Now on to the bathrooms. The men's restroom has no stall door, and was dirty. 1 star.
It's beautiful, and cooler than up on the main roads. I guess I just had it built up to something that it wasn't. It was a nice hike around the top and a few hundred steps down into the sinkhole.
What a great place to see fun things. Animals, old ways of doing things. Pretty scenery, and picknick tables. Playground for kids. Lots of activities going on. Check their website for times.
So nice to be able to take breaks and walk along the river here. It's pretty. There are ducks. There is beautiful plant life. Even a ferry. Come and enjoy a great part of San Antonio!
This is a historic Park for me. I grew up across the street. Skiing down the hill as a child. Riding the boats on the lake. Plenty of green open space for all manner of activities.
Splash pad is fun for the kids. There is a lot of interesting playground equipment here too. The electronic game is cool. Nice large covered picnic area. Huge, grassy field.
Beautiful to look at. It was too expensive and too long of a boat ride (2 hours) to see it closer. Although for what it represents and stands for, it was worth seeing!
Absolutely beautiful fountains and statues. The show is a bit distracting for some (you'll get it when you see it. It's throwing flags.)
I wondered around this art museum for awhile alone one day. It was some of the best time spent that day for myself. Beautiful displays.
Duuude! This is a great show for the kids. Neat how they made it come to life while feeling like you're looking at them through a tank.
Quite amazing. Well picked as a peaceful spot. It was far too cold at the time I visited to enjoy the water, but it was very pretty.
Beautiful castle from Cinderella. There are great photo opportunities from all over the park with this castle in the background.
It was fun for my daughter, but sometimes sad to me. The animals performed well, and the staff were all nice and accommodating.
I'm not Catholic, but the people are always friendly, and they host some of the best concerts for classical music in town.
Had a great time here! We love zoos and animal parks. A large area of gators. Pretty scenery with boardwalks throughout.
This was absolutely beautiful! The architecture. The famous people that are buried there. It was a great stop to make.
Quite amazing piece of our United States history. Check it out! Like others, I suggest making the climb up the stairs.
Really cool to see! Lots of sizes of alligators. They wanted to eat my service dog, but we were, of course, all safe.
Such an amazing ride. It was closed last time I went. Use the Disney app to make sure before you walk over.
This was so fun for my daughters! Great show. It's a must see for anyone with kids that like Belle.

One of Disney's must-see live-action performance, the seats fill up quick for this puppy. So getting there early is highly recommend. Fantasmic brings out the big guns when showtime swings around. Rotating through different Disney movies with a central story/theme, Fantasmic wows the crowd with hundreds of character costumes, well projected music and audio, toasty pyrotechnics, water effects, and an excellent stage set. Kids and adults will have their eyes glued to the stage the whole time. It can get loud and intense if you're up front so beware. There's concession stands nearby, and cast members walk around selling them too. You gotta see this show if you're a newcomer, I won't ruin it with spoilers, so you're going to have to see it for yourself.
dislikes: Loud and intense (for those up front)

reviews_attraction.text: Been coming here for years as a kid and as an adult. There's always something new to discover or learn when I go. If you're visiting Michigan, this is a MUST SEE. There's tons of olden and historical cars, farming equipment, industrial machinery, airplanes, furniture, artifacts, buildings, trains, and much much more. They're guided tours for many exhibits by well educated guides. The Henry Ford is also is great for kids. Their IMAX theater will put all other screens you've known to shame, it's huge! Coming here around the holidays is my favorite. The whole place is decked out in Christmas decor, with a giant beautifully garnished tree in the middle of the museum. There's so much to do I can't say it all here.

I do miss old Tiger Stadium, but Comerica does the job and does it well. Access is simple and fast enough on a busy day, if the line at one of the entrances are long, go look for another. Parking near, if you choose to, will cost you some $$. Games and events are easily viewed from all angles, bring binocs if you're elevated. Their carnival rides will keep the kids happy, the ferris wheel and a merry-go-round are fun to ride and are never too intense. The food/drinks are delicious, although a tad pricey, but what can you expect from a stadium? The place is usually pretty clean, if you don't mind the occasional peanut pile. The jumbotron is nice and big, it has excellent audio and lighting too. Go Tigers!

France's pavilion throws you into the middle of a Parisian neighborhood, all themed splendidly, you almost forget you're in America. There's a themed bridge similar to ones crossing over the Seine, a stone fountain, cobbled walkways, and a forced-perspective view of the Eiffel Tower in the distance. Romantic French music plays as you wander and explore their many shops and restaurants. Very expensive goods might I add. There's three dining venues here along with a few shops, wines are can be tested and bought along with perfumes and Frenchish souvenirs. Their only attraction is film projected on five screens with a 220 degree perspective. Stop by to experience a fun street performance too.

This is where of the history of Flint and the surrounding area comes alive. The Sloan Museum splendidly splays out important themes in the county's history, going back to it's Native American roots to it's labor disputes and strikes, the automotive industry, transportation, the grocery industry, and much more. Stilled scenes of yesteryear outfitted with fully-dressed figures and of-era decor present a glimpse into the past. Exhibits aren't too lengthy, and neither is the amount of reading required to soak-in each display. Overall an awesome learning experience for me and for the children.

A truly immersive pavilion, the colonial styled buildings are wonderfully made to reflect olden America. There's an informative animatronic show regarding the history of this great nation. A must-see if you're patriotic. The pavilion has it's own counter service dining, serving classic fare such as hot dogs, turkey legs, and burgers. Beer is served here too. There's a large amphitheater where performances are sometimes held. The eight-person a cappella group that wanders the rotunda gives an audience a singing they won't forget. Check em' out!

A beautiful reserve with easily walkable trails, 2.5 miles in total. In spring, the trails lead into blooming meadows and follow babbling creeks. There's a small parking area limited to about 10 vehicles. No dogs or bikes allowed. The only negative about this reserve is the TICKS. And oh Nelly there's a ton here! I picked off 15 ticks after a 45min walk. Spray yourself beforehand and check yourself after. Putting clothes in the dryer for an hour kills ticks off your clothes. Have fun!

Italy's pavilion does the country justice with it's accurate architecture, stone work, and stunning replicas of the Doge's Palace and St. Mark's Bell Tower. Cuisine sold tastes authentic, their brick oven pizzas are to die for. The shopping offers great candy and fancy wines. And like all the pavilion's, some workers are straight from the country itself. There's not much to do attraction-wise, but the street shows are hilarious and astonishing. Il mio hovercraft è pieno di anguille!

Visiting Michigan? Don’t even think about it, come here. The Greenfield Village has so many historical buildings, artifacts, and in-era knowledgeable staff members, it’ll have your head spinning with history. Holiday Nights at the Village and that Thomas the Tank Engine item are popular events to attend. Make sure you ride the Model-T’s, the steam train, and the carousel. Visit the many shops and restaurants too. You won’t be dissatisfied.

Admission is free, but parking has a modest fee. Wanna know about D-Town's history? Come here for a juicy lesson. This museum is great for the hungry mind, harboring artifacts and exhibits for and from Detroit's past. Like chunks from old tiger stadium, a full-scale functioning replica of a car assembly line, old vehicle models, and much more. My favorite section by far are the streets of Detroit located in the lower level. Check out it!

Strap yourself down and prepare for flight on Disney's premiere simulator. You sit on a suspended row of seats that can be moved and angled, Soarin' flys you over different environments and biomes, like the ocean, forest, city, etc. All the while using special effects such as scents, wind, and motion to enhance the illusion of flight. A long wait typically, fast pass recommend. A wonderful experience overall.

Admirers of the The Little Mermaid will find their Disney fan-fix down here, and no, I don't mean under the sea. It's in a deliciously dark air-conditioned building with a live-action abridgment to the original 1989 film. Actors play certain parts, while the use of giant puppets are used for others. Overall, a fun 17 minute experience that had me and my family singing along. I don't recommend that though.

Living with the Land has been teaching Disney patrons on agriculture and nature since 1982. Riders pile into a ten-person boat on a journey that whisks you through mock biomes with animatronic animals, massive greenhouses filled with hydroponically grown produce, an aqua farm swimming with life, and a stunning biotechnology laboratory. An educational attraction that I never miss out on when I visit EPCOT.

One of the more overlooked live-action shows at Disney, vastly entertaining nonetheless. The show casts live action actors to portray essential characters from the film it's based. The acting, singing, and set is all done live, it was great to see the beast act on stage. The show is an abridged version of the film. 5 stars for the singing.

Have kids that love Crush from Finding Nemo?  You gotta check this! Crush is displayed on a screen in front as the audience sits upon the floor. He's completely controlled and will answer questions, move, and even make facial expressions based on what you say/ask. The show is for kids but adults will defo enjoy watching. Radical dude!

Love fishes and wildlife? Then swim on down to the Cleveland Aquarium! The price of admission was well worth the entrance, there's a plethora of watery wildlife to greet you. Best parts were the jelly fish tank, hands on section, and of course, the Shark SeaTube. You gotta come check out this aquarium, it's in an old power plant!

A pavilion showing much architecture around different eras and themes to the Kingdom. There's lovely gardens to be had, a hedge maze for the tykes, a gazebo for live performances, and many stores and shops for your souvenir fix. The dining could be more vast in my opinion, but the Rose and Crown might make up for it.

A spectacularly red and distinctive lighthouse jutting out upon the pier towards Lake Michigan. If you're in the Haven and happen to be by or in the state park, look towards the water and spot this olden lighthouse, it's still maintained today. The walk on the pier gives you great views.

If you're cruising on M-25 and feel the need to stretch some legs, White Rock park is the place. The sidewalks are well-maintained, the wooden walkways by the beach are scenic, and the lakeside view is tremendous. Come enjoy your tax payer dollars and stop by!

I took the spray falls cruise which takes you farther than the others on their list. Would recommend the same if you're thinking of boarding. Saw great sights and wonderful formations. Keep an eye out for chapel rock, there's a tree growing out of it.

Great for hikes, days out on the beach, and bird of prey sightings. The trails and facilities are well maintained, so are the roads. I highly recommend bringing bug repellent if visiting during the warm months. 5 stars for a great hike!

A small museum that sure packs an educational punch! Admission is free for all, even the adults. Some if not most exhibits are oriented for children, so don't fret if you think your kid won't have a great time!

Camped here many of times. There's trails for miles, beautiful vistas, lotsa camping spots, pristine waters, and excellent pasties. If you're about the outdoors, come to Michigan's greatest gem in the north.
You must check out their nature center. The bird warning window brings in the most beautiful bird species around. I'd give this park 6 stars if it wasn't for the mosquitos.
One of the oldest still standing lighthouses in America. It’s great to see the society keeping these lighthouses tip top.

Not sure where to begin. The roof had several leaks, some dripping into buckets others just dripping on the tile floor. Some of the floor tiles cracked as we walked on them. It was dark, dusty and cluttered. We planned on getting ice cream and visiting the zoo but decided against both after seeing how poorly the main building was maintained. I imagine this place was probably much nicer at some point. The reason for 2 stars as opposed to one is because it is weird(in a good way) inside and we found ourselves joking about what we had seen all the way home. There are some pretty odd displays and it was fun looking at them. Maybe the zoo is nice but we chose to leave instead of giving it a try.

This is one of our favorite parks. We have hiked the loop many times and it never gets old. You'll walk alongside the Alafia River and cross over it as well on nice bridges. Depending on how far you walk you'll walk on a paved path, wooden boardwalk and/or natural trails. There is a canoe launch in one of the two parking lots. The park also has a playground area as well as shelters for parties or events.

I've visited this location several times. It's nice to see a historical site and to be able to discuss it with your kids and explain to them what it used to do. Very easy to see from the road and  easy enough to park for a visit. Unfortunately it it seems as if the site is in worse and worse shape. There used to be signs explaining what each section did and now most of them are gone.

Wall Springs is a great park with nice views of the Gulf. There is a large tower which is currently under renovation and numerous piers that extend into the water with great views. On our last visit we saw 5 stingrays swimming along and numerous fish near the pond where the spring is located. There is also a great covered play area. The park has access to the Pinellas Trail as well.

They've spent a good deal of money making this park a lot nicer. There is a new parking lot, building with public restrooms and a small boardwalk/walkway. You can rent canoes or kayaks here as well. In my opinion there are better parks around for taking hikes or walks. This park also does not have a playground for kids but that might be part of future renovations.

Key Vista nature park is a nice place to take the family for a walk. They have a decent sized parking lot that leads to several trail heads. There is a restroom on site as well. If you follow the trail you will come up on a river that leads out to the Gulf. You can usually walk out onto the beach and after a short distance arrive at a lookout tower.

Smaller park with a basketball court, tennis courts and playground for the kids. There is a bathroom on site. A small walking path loops around the back area with views of a lake and the zip line course in the background. The only bad thing about this trip were all of the mosquitoes that relentlessly swarmed us the entire time on the walking path.

This place is amazing. First off it's completely free. This Botanical Gardens is  nice place to take a leisurely stroll and enjoy the scenery. Cross over bridges, view the water, flowers, wildlife etc. As a bonus, connected to the property, is Heritage Village. The village allows you to view and walk through several historical buildings and shops.

My kids love this park. If you can get here during the week as opposed to weekends you'll skip the crowds. The playground area sits on top of the hill overlooking the lake. They have a dog park section and several picnic areas. You have great views of the lake from the covered shelter that sits next to the water.

This is an amazing park. They have a finished boardwalk that crosses over the swamp areas and the unfinished portion of the trail continues for miles if you're up for a hike. They have a great education center with hands on activities for the kids. The park staff are always very informative and nice.

Nice but small botanical gardens. We stopped by after a visit to another nearby park and walked through this garden pretty fast. They grounds are well maintained and there are restrooms on site but once again this is a pretty small location.

This is a great park with amazing views. There is a large boardwalk/trails throughout the park leading to a bird watching area and  large lookout tower. The park is clean, the restrooms are well maintained and there is plenty of parking.

Great park with a playground for the kids, canoe ramp, wooden boardwalks and unpaved trails. You get plenty of water views and picture opportunities. The park is never very crowded which is nice and the grounds are kept up very well.

Great park to spend a few hours or an entire day. There is plenty of parking and decent picnic areas. There are definitely better beaches to swim at but this is a good place if you want to find shells or just walk the beach.

Nice park with a nature trail that loops back to the main building. Two lakes, multiple streams and animal enclosures are part of what you'll encounter here. There is no entrance fee the trails are mostly shaded.
This is a great park with nice elevated boardwalks. You'll most likely see all sorts of birds and alligators during your visit. The park is well maintained and the kids love going whenever possible.
Great park with nice nature walks. They have a tower overlooking the lake with great views. There are picnic areas and playgrounds for the kids. A boat ramp is also located near the front entrance.
This is a small but we'll maintained neighborhood park. There is a nice playground for the kids as well as basketball courts. There are also a couple of racquetball walls/courts.
Nice bird sanctuary. Free to enter but they accept donations. The sanctuary is also right next to the beach so after walking through it you can walk right on to the beach.
Nice park but very small with limited parking. The park is located on the water and there are tables under a covered shelter. The park also has a restroom.
This is a great park to take the kids. We go on off hours so there is never a crowd and the park is well shaded. The park is well maintained.
This park has large, grassy fields and a playground overlooking the lake. There was plenty of parking along the street next to the park.
Smaller park located on the water. It's never been busy when I've visited. It has a small play area for kids and is fairly clean.
Nice place to bike, walk or jog. Shelters can be reserved for parties or other events as well. There is also plenty of parking.
Nice park with separate areas for dogs. There is also a large pier for fishing as well as a playground for kids.

I absolutely love this place. It meets a lot of needs for me... scenic... has water... beautiful place to take pics.. great place to walk for exercise... good meditation spot... historical... just a great location altogether. Been coming here for decades and continuing to find new discoveries and adventures!

No matter how many times i visit, i always find something new... and remain enthralled by the things i already discovered. Awesome history, breathtaking views, great walking paths. Fantastic place to go pictures or just hang out. Worth visiting repeatedly and is a gem for the Rochester area

Mertensia park is a hidden jewel to me. I frequent it for my own personal walks and meditation, as well as enjoying it with others and for photo shoots. The water is soothing. The flora is beautiful, especially when the Mertensias are in bloom. Just a great place to be overall!

I think that Turning Stone is top notch. I enjoy the slots as well as the entertainment offerings. The campus is beautiful and well maintained. Great place to visit and have some fun... and hopefully win some loot!

I absolutely love Highland. Expansive, scenic, tons to do... just a great place to do anything you need a park for.  And the activities associated with the park are awesome! Great gem of the city of Rochester

The fish hatchery is probably the biggest draw for most people and I also love it. But there is also a lot of cool scenery that I use for photo shoots. Not to mention the Mushroom houses that are adjacent.
I enjoy Cobb' s Hill park for various reasons but one of the main is the glorious view of Rochester. I typically go there for scenery and photography purposes and it provides that in spades.
This is hands down one of my fave places in the area, whether to commune with nature, do photos  (involving people or just the scenery) or to simply show others the beauty nearby
Pretty standard fare... not a lot to it, however,  it has a playground and lots of running room so i see it as a good place to tire out the kids. Pretty trees as well
One of my favorite places to just "Be". Great walking paths... awesome trails... breathtaking water and any perk I'd expect from a great park. Love this place!
Awesome park and i consider it a gem. Pretty flowers when in bloom, water, falls, places to explore, unique structures.. everything that i like in a park
Great park! Especially on comparison to the old Westgate Park, which was terrible.  The kids love it... lots of stuff to do... lots of perks. Nice place!
Great park with absolutely stunning views and tons of activities. I enjoy coming here to walk, hang out, do photo shoots or just meditate by the water.
I love this place. Always a great location to walk, chill, picnic, enjoy the water and just enjoy ones self. Awesome views and gives for water lovers.
Dean's Cove is a pretty place. I'm not a boater but can appreciate the scenery. Definitely good spot for hanging by the water and photo shoots.
What this park lacks in size, it makes up in personality. The log cabin alone seals the deal for me! Good trails and fun for kids as well!
Not a bad park at all. Great for sports and kids will enjoy the playground. Not a whole lot else to it but sometimes you don't need much!
I absolutely love this place. Great for water lovers and awesome scenery. Splendid for walks or just relaxing and communing with nature.
Cute little park that doesn't offer a lot of amenities but I can certainly see it being fun for kids or just a good place to hang out.
Cool community park. Kind of hidden but has good playground equipment and some unique visuals. Certainly a good spot to chill out
Awesome place for any fans of the Sweet science. Tons and tons of history and memorabilia. Certainly worth the price of admission
Lots of pretty trees and ornate benches. Good place to walk or chill out or even run the kids around. No real park amenities.
Great place for walking, water lovers, Erie Canal buffs, taking pics or simply hanging out. A nice gem for the Newark area.
I enjoy this place. No real amenities per se, but great views and water. Good spot for taking pics or relaxing.
Lovely place to walk, take pics and just chill out. Quiet and not a whole lot to it but certainly a good park!

We discovered this park when we took a break while kayaking down the Little Manatee River. We walked from the river a short distance past a couple pavillions to a playground.  Went back to check out the park and for a picnic after the Canoe Outpost people took us back to our car after a wonderful trip down the river. We would have been extremely disappointed if we would have come here for our kayaking. Thank goodness we found out about the Canoe Outpost on 301 just south of Sun City Center. We launched there and paddled about 3 hours down this unspoiled River.
