As far as Florida state parks go this one is best described as "very natural" or better yet as "not very improved". The map we got at the entrance was pretty bad, a photocopied map someone had drawn. We assumed this was a brand new park and thought that explained the lack of any information, either visitor center or signage to educate us about the park. The park is large with a rather sad play ground and a neglected parking lot way off somewhere down that long, long road circling the park. There was a campground that seemed to have most sites occupied.
I would recommend this park for those that want a very remote hiking experience (mostly unshaded) on sand, not paved trails and maybe equestrians. The canoe access from the park was extremely poor and unimproved. If you put in here you will have to paddle back up River to the same spot to get out. No designated swimming  area. There are a few large pavillions near the river, but you would have to carry your coolers, etc quite a way on sand trails to get to them.
This park has great potential to be more visitor friendly. Will visit it again sometime to give it another chance.

On Oct.23, 2019 very dissaponted because after paying our parking fee, we discover the River is closed due to high water. Understandable that it would be dangerous to be on the River when it was moving very swiftly and lits of trees and branches blocking parts of the water. Staff should have posted a note on pay station about it.
We decided to go to the other side of the park off 39 and had a nice round trip walk to the canoe input and back.
There are two entrances to Alderman's Ford. West of County Road 39 is the canoe launch site, where we go. $2 parking fee. Closes at sunset. It is a small park with a few picnic tables and parking for those people who go down the river. CLOSED on Christmas. Darn! Found out a couple years ago when the gate was locked.
There is a nice trail that connects to the park on the East side of 39 via a bridge across the river.
The river is beautiful, quiet, unspoiled until you reach the bridge at Lithia Pinecrest Road. Then there are a few houses, some "interesting" mobile homes, and finally Lithia Springs County park where we end our trip.
dislikes: Limited facilities (small park, few picnic tables)

reviews_attraction.text:
Surrounded by good restaurants and shops,  great place to walk around. Park has outdoor art that is interesting. Kids love running through the fountains in warmer weather. The fountains can get pretty crowded during the summer, especially on weekends. In the warmer months there are farmers markets and evening entertainment. Suwanee City Hall is located here. Extra parking available across Buford Highway in public library lot. Restrooms located behind amphitheater bandstand. Dogs must be on leash & picked up after.
Suwanee Greenway Trail ends here behind the condos near Friends Restaurant

Beautiful park. Been here several times. You can hike up to the falls or drive half way up and walk the ADA trail to the falls. Very busy on the weekends, especially during the fall. Sometimes you have to park quite a ways from the reflecting pool and walk up there on the road  (NO sidewalk). Lots of parking up near the top of the falls with space for picnics and kids to play.

We wanted coffee so we waited to be seated in the Lodge restaurant. 6 restaurant staff walked past us and ignored us. After 10 min we left. Sign said open 11am to 3pm. It was 2:30. Rude!

Located in Athens, GA. Beautiful botanical garden with a large glass-enclosed area with a stream running through it and filled with palms and orchids. Very nicely planned and maintained areas outside with benches to sit and admire the plants. We spent a lovely morning here wandering around outside and then felt as if we entered a jungle when we entered the huge greenhouse.
There is a gift shop with many garden themed items for sale and a small cafe with refreshments

Spent the night at Fort Yargo in a yurt. Very cool thing to do. Started our visit by mountain biking some of the trails in the afternoon. Then spent the evening sitting around the fire pit surrounded by a beautiful forest with the wind rustling in the trees. The next morning we enjoyed coffee on our private deck behind our yurt overlooking the lake. There are no cooking facilities in the yurts. Brought folding chairs, a picnic dinner and our own coffee maker.

Visited on New Years eve 2019 with family. We enjoyed walking around while vendors were setting up for the evening and listening to live music. My 3yr old grandchild was fascinated by all the boats at the marina and loved climbing up the huge Banyan trees. Lots of good restaurants line the street. Great place to spend a relaxing day. Parked in a parking garage 5 min walk from the parking. It was only $3 for the whole afternoon-what a deal!

I love coming here. Beautiful paved trails through the woods, some very steep, make for a great challenging walk when you are pushing a stroller. Could use better signage. There was a map display up by the ropes course that I did not find until my 3rd visit. The environmental center is very cool, both inside and out. Love the stream that runs behind the center. Saw wedding pictures being taken there. Great place also for family photo opp.

Also known as Alcovy Road Mill and Swann's Mill. Nice playground with an appropriate mill style theme. Mill is well preserved and there is a short trail through the woods behind the mill to the creek with a pretty waterfall. Wonderful place for family photo opps.
There is a paved trail starting by the playground. No map display, so no idea how long it is. 5 miles or 1/2, who knows? Too hot for me to find out today. Will have to come back.

Located in the University of Tampa, the museum was former Plant Hotel. Wonderful to step back in time to learn how Florida was developed by railroad baron Henry Plant in the late 1800's. There is an informative video on the history of the hotel which gives you a nice insight into life in Tampa over 100 years ago.
Parking available in front of the Museum and in the university parking garage. They also have a lovely gift shop.

We enjoyed spending a morning at this great park on beautiful Lake Lanier. Lots of parking. Many areas with picnic tables and grills located under shady trees with water views. 1 large and 1 small pavillion available for rentals. Boat ramp with truck and trailer parking. Paved trails along street to walk with strollers. Nice playground and swimming area for the kids. Park was clean and had plenty of garbage cans.

Big playground for the kids with nearby restrooms. Paved trail loops around, ending back at parking lot. There are seversl unpaved trails through the woods. Great place to walk, run, bike, stroller walking. 2 entrances both off Rock Springs Road. Tennis courts on the side with the playground and large pavillion. There is a ball field at the other entrance with a running track around it and lots of parking.

DeSoto National Park, not to be confused with DeSoto County Park north of here in Pinellas County, is a place where you can step back in time to 1539. Follow the Spanish Explorer Hernando DeSoto on his 4,000 mile expedition from Florida across Georgia, Arkansas and Mississippi. The film and visitor center were very informative. Park Rangers friendly. Nice nature trail along the shore of the Manatee River.

Definitley a challenge if you are afraid of heights, but the course has something for every skill level and age.  Was here the first time in the winter when the trees were bare. Amazing how different it is when you are surrounded by the lush green forest in the summer. Came here during the week and quite a few people here. Probably much more crowded on the weekends,  but that is to be expected.

Beautiful park. Located near the ferris wheel and the Aquarium. Lots of benches under trees to sit abd relax. Very clean splash pad for kids of all ages. Great place to spend a day.
We were there on a Monday morning so it was not crowded at all.  At noon there was an amazing show where the fountains performed to music. We enjoyed watching it while eating our picnic.

Old court house in Dahlonega is now the gold museum. Great place to visit to learn about the amazing story of the Georgia gold rush. There is a very interesting video and historical display in the museum as well as a gift shop.
While we visited, a group of men were playing the bagpipes across from  the museum. Wonderful to listen to them.

We were not  sure what the car in front of us was doing. Then we realized they  tried it 3 times.  Didn't work. We tried it twice. Didn't work. Very disssapointed. 2 of us had been here years ago and convinced our friend to try it. She said she ic complaining to the Mayor of Lake Wales that Spook Hill is broken. 😁

Spent New Years Eve eve here with family. Had fun kayaking around the mangroves. Lots of little secluded places to fish or sit and relax. Playground for the kids. Plenty of parking. Great place for kids to explore nature. We saw several Manatees during the afternoon

We love visiting this park any time of year. There is a paved path that circles around the lake. Several benches to sit and enjoy the view.  There is also a wonderful playground for kids and restrooms nearby

Love the view from the top of the mountain behind the visitor center. Hiked the Tennessee Rock trail in the fall. It was beautiful to be alone in the woods with the occasional passing of other hikers.
No fee to park here. Had a nice picnic  the day after Thanksgiving. Hiked over to the dam and my grandson loved feeding the goats with grass. Great day with the family 🦃
Jan. 2021. Closed. Again. I've never actually been in the park. It seems to be under construction or being repaired. Apparently there is a lot of mud on the astro turf.
Big park with trails, a lake with big Pavillion, 2 playgrounds, ball fields, volley ball court, tennis courts and several parking lots with some shade.
New Gwinnette county park. 3 yr old loved the splash pad and playground. Nice there is covered seating by the splash pad to sit and watch the kids
Love  bringing the kids here. Large partially covered  playground with lots of slides.  The splash pad is especially popular with kids of all ages

Probably one of the best places to experience nature. All dirts trails, except for a short boardwalk at the beginning, which become a mess and in some spots, impassable during rainy season. ALOT of gators, hogs, bears, and a few panthers, and a slew of Red Shouldered Hawks. These animals do share the paths with people, especially the gators, so if you're intimidated by wildlife, go elsewhere. Just a note, towards the end of dry season, April and May, it is the best, but there are times when you don't see a whole lot, so don't be discouraged

This is an awesome park. It was originally listed as a historic site. But when they realized there was much more to offer than just a site, they changed it to a state park. The koreshan people lived there in the early to mid 1900s and donated the land to the state. There are still 11 buildings standing from the community plus paths through a very cool bamboo forest along the Estero river. There is a lot for campers, a place to rent canoe and a couple of picnic areas. This is one of my favorite places to visit
likes: Recreational facilities (camping, canoe rental, picnic areas)

reviews_attraction.text: Another State park that we frequent quite a bit. Theres a bus you can take to the beach or you can hike to a beach a little closer (about half mile walk). This park is immaculate and extremely well maintained. If you take the bus, there is a concession stand on the beach, but if you do the walking trail to the beach (you cross over 2 bridges which you can fish off of) , it's about a 1/4 mile walk to concession. Enormous parking lot, great for when the beaches get crowded in winter time

My favorite beach. We are there usually 4-5 times a week. Has a boat launch, 5 parking lots with each one having a different style beach from the other. Tons of wildlife. I have told alot of people about this beach, and every one has said it's their favorite. Tons of picnic areas nestled in the wooded areas, and I believe 4 restrooms and shower areas. I can't say enough positive things about this state park or the rangers and sheriff's that patrol it. LOVE THIS PLACE

Still here. Been by this place 20 times and never saw it. Absolutely beautiful, and wildlife is awesome. Can't wait to bring my kids back here. Pics to follow later. Not sure if this is a city, county or state, but whoever manages this, does an absolutely sensational job. Came from Fort Myers and I will be back for sure

Didn't get a chance to really check it out, but we did talk to the ranger. He was a ton of info. They have one of the few spots in eastern US considered a dark zone, meaning it's dark enough to see the Milky Way galaxy. Summer is better for viewing the galaxy but fall, winter and spring are better for hiking and camping

If you want to party or just walk around or even go into novelty shops, this is the place. Complete with a FREE pier that you can fish off of. Times Square is right there and always something going on there, from live music to novelty acts. And theres the beach too. The park is right in the middle of it all

Love this beach. North tip of Estero island. Not to crowded. And there is a jet ski rental right next door. It's a short distance to the bay side and even has some trails through the woods. The boardwalk to the beach is one of the nicest entrances to any beach I have seen. And you can grill out there

Definitely better in dry season. Not quite as muddy. But if you're willing to forego the mud, it's an awesome park with alot of trails. There's a learning center, but was closed when we were there. Wasn't there 20 minutes, and saw a bobcat. Alot of birds. Going back as soon as it dries out a little

Absolutely awesome preserve. Bears, hogs, Panthers, Bobcats, alligators and a whole host of birds. All raised boardwalk and around 2 1/2 mile long. Personally had a bobcat jump on the boardwalk 20 foot in front of us. So cool. But there is grasslands, swamps and cypress forest all in one location

Very cool. Tallest lighthouse in florida at 175'. 202 steps, but the view is worth every step. Also can walk through various homes of the light keeper and his assistants homes from period times. Alot more to see and do in the area, which are all within walking distance of each other

Absolutely beautiful. 30 mile drive from ormond beach. Springs were crystal clear and 72 degrees F. Boardwalk and path were beautiful. Did see a bear den, but never did see a bear even though bear activity is common. Coming back in a couple of months to swim in the springs

Little over a mile of boardwalk with 2 overlooks out over the water. Also in the parking lot, there's a veterans memorial. Can't forget the people who sacrificed everything, so that I can live the way I want. Very nice memorial and thankyou to all servicemen and women

What an outstanding park. Cleanest I've been to. We did see 2 manatee, but a little late in the season. January and February are the best times. But the flora is also exceptional as well as the butterflies. Playground for kids, a gift shop and picnic areas

Has an observation deck for viewing gators. If you wanna see gators in their natural habitat, check this place out. There is personnel in the center that can answer and direct you to anything in the area. Very helpful to know

How can it be any lower than that. It's 2 iconic inventors/geniuses winter homes and Edisons Lab and a museum, which is a very good museum. Should be 6 stars. The Banyan tree alone is absolutely incredible
This place is awesome. Will be back for sure. Alot of great trails and you can kayak on Hillsborough river. Alot of wildlife. Drove 2 1/2 hours to get to it. Wouldn't do that if it wasn't worth it
Still haven't seen the whole place. But very well maintained and the real deal. Not a tourist trap. Going back again this week. All the employees are very friendly and extremely knowledgeable
Awesome park in the middle of it all. Has a boat launch, playground and very clean restrooms. Only problem I have is the pier has been shut down for 2 years for repairs. Come on, get it fixed
This beach is great. Free parking and there is a concession area although it was not open when we were there. Also found 4 shark teeth, which is what the area is known for
If you like art and just novelty stuff, this place as well as matlacha, should be on your list. Buy something everytime we are in there, but also get great ideas too
Excellent starter preserve. The raised boardwalk is not to long, but in excellent shape. Only problem is you can hear traffic no matter where you are in there
Absolutely beautiful. Tons of fish, which indicates waters are doing great. Traffic has let up now with spring break and snowbirds gone
Very unique wildlife habitat. Love this place. Just a side note, read it below in a comment, but this place IS NOT open on weekends
Dry season is the best. Mud can be a problem. Other than that, it was an awesome place to hike. Alot of trails

This park has got a little bit of everything. They of course have a playground and the nice part about it is that it is covered so even on hot days kids can still play. They have equipment for older and younger kids. Also it isn't on mulch and so your kids don't get mulch all up and down their shirt and pants. They have a huge field for sports or picnics or whatever you would like to use it for. The disc golf course is nice and easy to see. The only thing I did not like was how small the trail is. When I go to the park I go to run or walk and the trail is only .2 miles. It is too short to use for exercising as you will just be walking in short circles so there is no fun in that.

So cool! There are gators everywhere! You can get so close to them too! They have a splash pad for the kids and a petting zoo too! The shows are hilarious and very interactive. It is incredible to see the alligators jump out of the water and to see the guys wrestle the gators. There are buzzards and herons flying all over too. You can get pictures with snakes and baby gators, plus you can feed them yourself. They sell gator nuggets too that are so good, but way overpriced. If you are in the area, this is a place you have to go!

Very spacious park with a lot of room to run around. It is a very quiet part of town and everytime I have gone we have had the park to ourself. There isn't really a walking trail, which is a something I look for in parks cause I like to walk or run and then let my kids play on the playground. The playground is smaller and simple, but still fun and well taken care of. Not much for smaller kids to do, but still fun. There are really nice baseball fields here too.

I love this little zoo and have gone many times. It is little and I am surprised they charge so much for such a small zoo, but it is a good one. Especially the giraffe outlook! They have so many giraffes and if you want you can feed them, it is just really cool to be so up close to them! There are a lot of bird exhibits, but they still have quite a bit of other animals! The food is over priced like most zoos, but it is good food.

I come to this zoo every year and it is fun every time. It is a pretty zoo, there are flowers all over and the exhibits are beautiful! I love the squirrel monkey area, it is huge and there are a ton of little monkeys! It is a little smaller of a zoo, but still a decent size! You can go in a little caged in aviary and feed a ton of parakeets! It is a fun place especially to take kids!

This is a cute little museum if you have kids. It is more of a children's museum than anything. They have fun little stations for kids to do little experiments, plus a little mountain and ship they can walk through. It isn't really big, but it is still fun. My husband and I visited it and even as adults it was still fun, but it is definitely centered around children.

Super fun ride! My 2nd favorite in the park! It is nice and slow in the beginning as you admire the dinosaurs and then all starts to speed up as the Raptors get loose. When you get in the building is when the ride gets intense! The drop at the end is really steep and is definitely a thrill. You will get soaked though so if you don't want to get wet, wear a poncho.

Probably the coolest aquarium I have ever been to. It is not very big at all, but it very well designed! There are lots of looking areas under the tanks so it looks like you are in the tank and you can look closer. The tanks are set up where you will actually see the fish and not just a big tank of water. Friendly staff that are very helpful and informative.

Not a thrill ride like what I was expecting, but it does twirl you around quite a bit. The walk to the ride is really fun, it is like you are actually in the movies. The ride is a shooting laser ride and my husband and I really enjoyed it. There were a lot of aliens to shoot and the details were amazing. It is fun to do something to compete with others too!

The wait was ridiculous. First you wait in the line to get to the ride, then you are separated into groups and wait in that line, then you are sent to a smelly room and wait in that room before you even get to the ride. It was s pretty good ride, but the you are in bench seats and so you get tossed around into the people sitting next to you.

I loved this show! Of course I love animals, but my husband even like this show and he doesn't care much about animals. The trainer was so funny and the show was very interactive with the animals. The animals were very impressive and it was cool to know what movies they have been in. Definitely take the time to go to this show, it was fun!

This is one of our favorite parks! It has a really fun playground, a duck pond, and baseball fields. It also has a bathroom so that is super convenient! Only down sides are that the walking trail is short and it just randomly ends. Also they may have open fields for kids to run on, but they are covered in stickers that hurt like crazy.

I love this park! It is a peaceful place to just get out of all the hustle and bustle! It is really cool to see the big bullfrogs! We came here to get our family pictures this year! The only downside is that it doesn't allow pets. I love walking my dog, but since I can't bring my dog, I rarely come here.

Fun little show, there is no interaction, but it is fun to watch. The actor who took us on the tour was really funny. Walking through the water room was pretty amazing, but the rest of the show is pretty lame, probably because there were so many people, you don't get to see everything.

I probably will never go here again, but it wasn't a bad place to go. If you have younger kids, then the little children's interactive section is fun, but it is really little. The art was pretty lame, like pictures of Campbell soup cans and old toys, not really interesting.

We loved this park so much! There was so much detail every where you look! It was so fun to meet so many fun characters. I feel like there was something here for everyone to do! Each area was amazing and each ride was thrilling and exciting, we did almost all of them twice!

Not really that interesting of a museum. It is pretty small and especially if you have kids, not really interactive. There are a few things for kids to do in the second building, but we had a hard time keeping them from being too bored.

Sulphur Springs is a cute little town. The Vetrans memorial was nice and central to the city. Surrounding it is the see through bathroom, chess board tables, and when we were their the dairy festival parade! Nice little area to visit.
likes: Facilities & Services: Unique amenities (see-through bathroom, chess board tables)

reviews_attraction.text: Super crowded in the waiting room and we had to wait forever. Then you could barely hear the beginning show because people were talking. We were expecting a ride, but it was just a movie with some special effects. Not worth the wait.
dislikes: Only a movie with special effects

reviews_attraction.text: Not really that thrilling of a ride. It is super short and has no thrill to it. It is cool to see Hagrid's house and the Hyppogriff, but is not an exciting ride.
dislikes: Attraction Type: Not thrilling, Super short

reviews_attraction.text: This place is literally a dirt meadow with hundreds of prairie dogs all over! There isn't anything else here, but it actually is a pretty cool thing to see.
Pretty good ride. It was cool to transform from a car to and autobot. It was an exciting 4d show though and the ride had a couple of thrilling parts to it.
There is nothing really to see or do here!! The trail is so short and there is nothing to see. There are a few stuffed animals inside but that is it.
For a small zoo it is a nice one! We went when it was cold so not many animals were out, but that is to be expected. I really enjoyed it though!
Not really that interesting of a museum. I love interactive museums and their wasn't much to so at this museum, but a lot to read.

This was the first visit to Tarpon Springs in many years. There are lots of shops, restaurants,  boat rides and other activities available. There are lots of benches along the way for a rest or also several places to sit and have a beverage of your choice. The prices seem to be very reasonable. We spent a couple of hours or more just enjoying the scenery and people.  It was a Thursday and there were a good many people. Lots of food choices from seafood to greek bakeries.

Beautiful, very large park with a welcome center, marina, beach, picnic areas, boat ramps, a lake, cabins, RV sites,country store and lots of walking trails of different degrees of difficulty. The welcome center is manned by very helpful and friendly employees. The prices on their souvenirs and clothing are very reasonable. The marina is a full service marina  and offers boat rentals. There is some construction and improvements being done right now.

My first visit but will not be my last. There is a nice gift shop with coffee or milkshakes with very nice and helpful employees. They have a nice long pier that you can walk out on for free or fish all day for $3. The view is nice and there is also a park where several people were jogging or exercising.

Nice beach area with easy access and free parking. The park offers clean restrooms, volleyball courts, barbecue grills, tables and pavilions. Boardwalks lead from the parking lot to the beach. Wide beach offers lots of room to sunbath, Jogging , build sandcastles, shelling or metal detecting.

Lots of shops with a large variety of products. There are lots of restaurants and pubs with a good selection of cuisine. They offer deep sea fishing or sightseeing cruises. There is plenty of parking for three to five dollars per day. Great place to spend some time sightseeing and eating.

Dispite the hurricane damage this is a great place to visit. Boat ramps, rentals and bait store are all open. Great areas to fish from the shore. Nice beach area for swimming or working on your tan. Pontoon rentals available by the hour or day. Wild dear roam the wooden areas.

Great park geared more for kids. The mermaid show is very entertaining especially for kids. The pontoon ride was relaxing and informative. We did not get there until 2:30 and was not told that everything closed at 4 or 4:30. The charge for getting in is $13 per person.

Nice clean beach with lifeguard and restrooms available. Good beach for shelling, swimming, fishing, metal detecting, grilling out or just working on your tan. Boardwalk makes travel to the beach from the parking lot easy. Showers are available for use on the way out.

Three ramps and one long dock. Ramps are large enough and deep enough for even large boats. There is a picnic area with tables and barbeque grills. They have a playground area with swings and more for the kids. There is a large restroom facility near the beach area.

Very nice park with beach access,bay access, a bait and tackle shop, boat ramp, pontoon boat rentals, guide service and wildlife. Six dollars for a vehicle up to eight people. Lots of free parking available. Lots of places to fish on bay or gulf.

Beautiful beach park with restrooms and free parking conveniently located.  The beach is just minutes from the parking lot and is great for swimming, fishing, metal detecting or working on your tan. There are shops and restaurants nearby.

Great 30 plus acre park will picnic tables, barbecue grills, pavilion, beach, horseshoe pit, volleyball courts, playground, boat ramp and restrooms. Gulf of Mexico access for boating, swimming or fishing. Lots of free parking available.

This is a very fun and educational place. There is a large amount of educational material available in the form of printed material, a video, replicas of documents and photo opportunities. Kids and adults will enjoy a visit here.

Nice large and wide beach with plenty of room for swimming, sunbathing, metal detecting, fishing, building a sandcastle or just working on your tan. Restrooms and free parking are conveniently located just over the sand dunes .

Great place to bike, jog, throw a frisbee, walk your dog or play sports. A nice large park with more areas under construction including a playground area with equipment. Conveniently located at Hwy 369 and Wallace Tatum rd..

Very nice park with shoreline for fishing, picnic areas, several pavilions, boat ramps and beautiful views of the lake from higher ground. There are multiple restrooms available. There is also a nice camping area available.

Nice park with swimming area, covered pavilion, fishing area, restrooms and free parking. Parking is limited but convenient. There are multiple picnic tables and barbecue grills available. Views of the water are beautiful.

Small park that has not recovered from the hurricane Michael. There are restrooms, a play area for kids,a long walkway into the bay and limited but free parking. Bay fishing is available at the end of the walkway.

Beautiful park with large creek with area that used to have a mill. Kids can play in the water or on the swings or slides. Grills available and a large pavilion also. Kids can catch fish from the shore or swim.
A great place to see some of the equipment and training used by the elite navy seals. Everyone from kids to the elderly will enjoy all the many boats and other equipment.
Nice beach access area with clean restrooms available. Beautiful beach area  for swimming, fishing or just laying out and working on your tan.
Small park with walking track, volleyball area, pavilion and field for other sports. Plenty of free parking. No employees on property.
Fun trip for all ages. Stopped in Blue Ridge with time for shopping. Some of the cars are open so you can enjoy the scenery even more.
Nice small beach park with easy access to the beach. Restrooms available, handicap parking and lots of free parking available.
We did not get to spend the time that I would like to but it is a beautiful area and would like to come back.

Such a beautiful facility to visit. The drive over the dam is a great sight but much better viewed by walking across. It is only roughly a 1/4 mile and you wouldn't have to walk the whole way either. Plenty of parking on the overlook across the dam. There is a visitor center just before going across that again has plenty of parking. The gift shop was closed but there is one. The visitor center was open and manned by volunteers from BVI that were contagious in their enthusiasm about facts, not just the dam but the reasons for the location and even the needs for it. There are plenty of pictures and 3D effect art to describe the dam and region. There is a 360 degree observation deck on the roof of the visitors center that offers fantastic views. You can look down the tunnels, just barely, for the spillway water. There are four spillways that feed into two tunnels. You can see the relatively small motors that run through gear boxes to lift the spillwat gates and the very large chains that do that lifting.

The level of intricate details put into the rooms is incredible. We had a group of 8 people, at times that was an advantage and other times it was a detriment to our progress. You are given an hour and a light back story and locked in a room. There is a way to open the door if you need to use the restroom and return. There is a person in a control room monitoring your progress, and ensure that you don't cheat or damage their rooms. You can have up to 3 clues given to you and still qualify to break the record. Any clues in excess of your 3 will be given but exclude you from competing for the top time. You request your clues via a provided walkie-talkie, they will not talk back to you but simply place the clue on the tv monitor on the wall with the count down timer on it. A great way to spend time as a group, we burned up 45 minutes and it felt like 10! I can't recommend this activity enough.

Tremendous views from up here.  I am not sure how long of a hike from the parking lot on top to Sunset Rock.  We hiked up from the lower trails.  We parked in the lower lot at Ruby Falls and used the Guild/Hardy Trail to get to the Upper Truck Trail and finally climbed up Upper Gum Springs Trail.  Upper Gum Springs trail is 0.7 miles from the Upper Truck Trail
to Sunset Rock and is pretty steep.  The last few hundred feet are stones set into stairs.  This is really well done.  There seems to be a good amount of climbing done on this face and some permanent climbing points are installed.

Great place. You have options here, mountain biking, road biking, hiking & running. In the last year they have added two way connectors on the mountain bike trails. Pay attention to the direction indicated by day. They have also added a small mountain bike area for children. The hiking trails are wide and have nice beds, mostly of bark & are fairly easy grades. There are several picnic areas & bathrooms in the park. There are drinking fountains for people & dogs. There us a visitors center that has maps of the trails & roads. Plenty of wildlife in the park.

Plenty of parking available and easy on and off access to Hwy 153.  Large events will use the grass area adjacent to Hwy 153 for parking. There are picnic tables and grills in the woods for use. They just recently have added a playground with a large variety of equipment to play and workout on. Restroom building is down near the new playground and the water. Large area with steps to a sand and gravel roped off swimming area in the lake. Plenty of open grass areas for outdoor play activities like croquet, lawn bowling, lawn darts etc.

Always a great experience.  It is always something that we take out of town visitors to.  It is such a great piece of Chattanooga history and a great engineering feat for the time that it was built.  It is still well maintained and a great way to travel to the top of the mountain for the views and pictures without having to drive up the mountain roads.  You can venture around up at the top and see some of the other venues while up there then take a leisure ride back down

Nice place to put in below the railroad bridge.  We ran from there to Gee Creek Campground but you could continue on to 411 overpass where there is also a boat ramp.  You can even go down to where the Ocoee River combines with the Hiwassee River.   Parking is free and we were there early in the morning  and didn't have many people to deal with.  When we came back in the afternoon to pickup the drop vehicle it was much more crowded but still had parking spaces available.

Great disc golf course, The Sinks.  This is a wooded and challenging 18 hole course.  There is an open area when you park to use as a driving range and also a spot to practice putting while waiting to tee off.  You can start on the front 9 or cut through to 10 and start on the back 9 first.   There are some mando's and some areas that collect water.  The pins on most holes are movable so check the position prior to teeing off.  It gets busy at times so be patient.

Well worn path that you can easily follow. It is a moderate climb at times but we saw plenty of really young and older people make it. There are several stream crossings that are easy to get across with stones keeping you out of the water. Grotto Falls is definitely worth the hike. You can go under and behind the falls. Great spot for a break or to turn around. The water keeps it fairly cool on a day that was in the low 90's.

Easy access to this free attraction. Some parking at the star but more down the hill which has a paved access trail up to the star. There are public bathrooms available at the top too. Great view of the city from the lookout patio. Some of the walkways are paved, some are gravel between 4x4 lumber and finally some dirt trails. At the discovery center there is a trail condition indicator that is updated by users.

Easy access to this free attraction. Some parking at the star but more down the hill which has a paved access trail up to the star. There are public bathrooms available at the top too. Great view of the city from the lookout patio. Some of the walkways are paved, some are gravel between 4x4 lumber and finally some dirt trails. At the discovery center there is a trail condition indicator that is updated by users.

Plentiful parking in a gravel lot just off the roadway. A small playground is at the bottom of the hill with two small play areas by age with a good amount of benches and picnic tables available. There is a covered picnic area with a half dozen tables. There is a set of swings past the picnic shelter. Plenty of trails around the perimeter. The men's room was out of soap and the grass was in need of being cut.

We always enjoy going to these types of fairs. This year was a really good turnout of vendors to look through their goods for sale. Parking was plentiful, well controlled and set up. Water was flowing nicely over the dam which was great for viewing and pictures. There were plenty of options for food with many standing tables to take your food and eat.

Great small gem of a recreational area. It currently is a lot more difficult to reach since the Chickamauga Dam Lock work has closed the main access road. There are hiking and walking trails and access to the North Chickamauga Creek for canoeing and kayaking. It can be accessed from a trail but looking forward to normal vehicle access to be restored
likes: Creek access for canoeing and kayaking

reviews_attraction.text: Great hike to the falls. Is pretty well paved all the way to the falls but is not ADA certified. It is still a good elevation change so don't take it lightly. Having said that we saw plenty of people of all abilities making the hike. We continued on the couple miles past to the next trailhead. The trail past the falls was in great shape as well.

Really great experience. The introduction was unexpected and stimulating, no spoilers but it was really good as well. The puzzles were varying in difficulty within the room. Each room has a difficulty level listed so keep that in mind when booking. We had 4 of us and that was enough to work with but not so many as to get in each other's way.

Great place to take children of all ages.  Plenty of animals to interact with.  The corn maze is very large and a great time for a group to go through.  They have a hay ride that you can ride.  They have food and drinks to purchase.  Plenty of parking on site.  They have had a kids ride to pull around in a small path.

Great access point to both Universal Studios and Islands of Adventure. Lots of food and shopping without having to have a ticket for one of the parks. You can access from a car from the parking garage, bus drop off, Uber or Lyft, or by boat from one of the hotels. There's a large theater so you can watch movies.

Always a great place for day hikes, camping, staying in cabins or just a picnic. Hiking trails are well marked and see regular maintenance. Remember to have cash with you park fee for GA State Parks is $5, self service at stations near parking areas so having exactly $5 makes it easier.

This is a great community place that runs along the Tennessee River from the Chickamauga Dam all the way downtown. Many access points along the way allows you to start and stop in a large selection of distances. Ties into South Chickamauga Creek Greenway adding to access and distance

Great quiet creek for getting out on the water in kayaks, canoes, or just about anything man powered. Must know the flow because too much and it can be hazardous with strainers and other debris. Too little and you'll be out of the boat dragging or pushing.

Love this path. Following along the creek is a well maintained path with easy access from several locations. We have put in and taken out kayaks along this path. Several benches spaced along the path for resting or just sitting to observe nature.

We had an opportunity to visit after hurricane Irma. The speed in recovery was phenomenal with support from the local community and Sub Base sailors. This museum has an incredible amount of memorabilia from many generations.
Easy access off of 58 Hwy. Boat ramp doesn't have a lot of trailer parking available immediately but plenty of regular parking. The mountain bike trails are well kept and also has plenty of parking.
They have started charging $5 for the taste testing but give you a coupon for $5. It is great to taste the different flavors before we purchased them.

Excellent experience all around. From the moment you step foot into the museum to the time you walk out. It is worth every penny, I highly recommend taking the time to visit this museum, it is not very large but you could spend a good two to three hours if you appreciate Salvador Dali's work. The staff go above and beyond to make you feel welcome and help provide the best experience.

Really cool neighborhood park and play ground. There are a couple of basketball courts and a softball field. There is a historic house in the middle of the park and next to it there is a stone oven and counter that is open to the public and they have community cooking once every month. Very nice to walk around and to just sit and enjoy some time.

This place is very nice for a stop during a walk or bike ride around the neighborhood. The views of the Manhattan skyline are phenomenal. They have a NY ferry station that takes you to other stops in Brooklyn, Manhattan and Queens. The pier itself is a bit dirty but that shouldn't deter you from visiting it.

It's cool to see the bridge open for a ferry or ship to pass. If you're driving and don't have much time to spare, turn around and take another way because it takes at least 30 mins for the bridge to open let a ferry pass and close again. It's a nice bicycle trail between the two states

Lovely park anytime of the year. Good for laying around, strolling around, or just whatever you want to do in a public park. Great views of the Hudson Bay, beautiful trees and greenery and very well maintained walkways; there is also a children's playground

Excellent tours!!! This museum is definitely worth the price and time. The historical content of the tours gives you a nice perspective on the present and the future. Take the time to ask questions and visit the store afterwards, maybe get a book.

Really nice museum showing the history of Iowa City and Iowa in general. The renovation process shows on how clean and neat the building looks. Best part is that's free. There are some nice souvenirs for sale inside and the staff are very nice.

Way too many people even though this was during the pandemic so I can't imagine during"regular" times. Prices are high in most places and the staff in most places are nice. There are some good restaurants and a bunch of retail stores

Excellent place for a walk whether you're exercising, going out on a date or just a nature lover. You can feed the ducks and it's also dog friendly. Make sure you pick up after yourself or your dog. Leave it better than you found it.

There's a water park with outside and inside pools, some slides and a lazy river. It gets crowded and they are open during the pandemic. The service is ok and the food is hot dogs and so, beer selection is poor.

Nice trails and forest but it gets really crowded when the weather is nice out and it's the weekend. Be prepared to drive around for a long time to find parking. It's only about 1 hour from Brooklyn by car.

The place is nice and has some cabins that seem to be for rent. There is an eagle viewing area and also some nice hiking trails that are well marked and maintained, it is definitely worth the time to visit
Go there to chill, play walk or just about anything. Goes along shore road right by the water, it's very beautiful and well maintained. Beautiful views of the Verrazano bridge and the Hudson Bay
Nice open area to walk around or just sit on the nice painted benches and do some people watching. There's is a children's playground and a a few bars and restaurants where you can sit outside.
It's a very nice place to go for a walk or a jog. Lined up with stores, restaurants and bars at night it's probably the best time to visit. There's also a train station to downtown Orlando
Another great park in the city. This one is right by the water and if you're lucky on Saturdays when it's warm outside, they have smorgasbords, delicious food and great people watching
This is a very nice plaza with the vessel in the middle of it. To go up all you need is a free ticket from the booth and stand in line sometimes. Nice views and pictures
It's a nice place to bring the kids so they run. It should have a bigger and maybe better play area. There are some restaurants and bars that are catered to tourist.
Best park in Brooklyn and the largest. Very well maintained trails, paths, playgrounds and roads. Lovely to picnic on a spring or summer afternoon.
It's a great place for a decent hike up and down hills. The only cave that's paved it's nice but really small and nothing out of the ordinary.
Good place for kids to run around and play. There are some picnic tables and some bbq grills. You can spend a nice afternoon there
It's good for kids around 5 years of age. I took my 3 year old  niece there and she couldn't get on most of the playground rides
Great hiking trails and overall good place to be surrounded by nature. Went there in the winter and the landscape was beautiful
Very nice to take a walk or ride a bicycle. There are some restaurants and bars along the way as well.
Nice park to bring kids and to go for a walk or play tennis. It's got a bunch of open spaces

I cannot believe that I haven't reviewed my favorite coaster at Busch Gardens yet.  I have a paralyzing fear of heights but Cheetah Hunt doesn't trigger me at all. This is a launch coaster so there's no agonizing slow climb up a lift hill where you go higher and higher.  You just go flying around a nearby corner as you are launched.  What's really fun is that there is a second launch that gets you going 60 mph as you are propelled up into a really unique looking part of the track that wraps around itself.  This is the part you see in the Busch Gardens logo! After this part there's one last launch and some fun sections where you can get some airtime. On some of the other coasters such as Montu your view isn't so great if you're not in the front, but I think sitting in any part of Cheetah Hunt is fine. Another nice feature is that instead of the huge horse collars you have to wear for other coasters the overhead restrains are smaller and more comfortable because there's only one inversion on the track. I love this coaster!

The queue is entirely outdoors, but it is covered from the sun and there are fans above you.  However, you will get no real relief from the heat until you get onto the ride and get wet. Each round boat can hold 12 people.  And there are two sides for loading and unloading.  IF both sides are open, the line moves a little bit faster as 24 people can be getting on and off at the same time.  As the name of the ride may suggest, this is a ride of rapids. There are warnings posted throughout the line that you may get wet and possibly soaked from this ride.  I've ridden this many times and have been anywhere between getting just a few drops of water to being completely drenched.  DO NOT get on this ride unless you are ok with the chance of getting soaked!! Overall, a good ride, especially if you want to briefly escape the summer heat.

Today was my first on several thrill rides. I have never had the urge to ride Falcon's Fury, but peer pressure got the best of me today, so on we went. We came right as the park was opening, so there was ZERO wait times, which I instantly regretted on this ride because I use the wait times to hype myself up. No no! Not this time! Once you're strapped in you're lifted up, and that seems like it takes forever. Then the seat tilts you till you're facing the ground and as you guessed. Drops you. I'm not a fan of drops. Today was my day for drops apparently. It wasn't terrible but it also was three seconds that I never want to experience again. This was one ride that I was excited to get off of!

The museum offers a wonderful historically accurate look at the many different aspects of Carney life. Everything from rides,to games,to vendor carts and Barker's stands even the circus advance man's rail car. My favorite were displays and videos that explain and educate about an interesting dicotomy- people working hard at politically incorrect jobs by today's standards and successfully supporting themselves and building families and community, when in their day they were ostracized and outcast because of their color,ethnic background or disability.... the politically correct standards of their time. With that being said,the wild West show, girlie reviews, and oddities exhibits

Didn’t expect much but was surprisingly pleased. Beautiful , smaller gardens on the USF campus, seemed to be maintained and operated by students who were helpful, friendly and working in their career interests. Lots of individual gardens like the Salsa garden and the orchid garden, places to relax, picnic even, enjoy nature. We loved it ! The kids enjoyed the waterpark, we enjoyed the gardens, close to our hotel and about an hour or so walk thru, longer if you wanted. Little gift shop and plant store, green house. We would go back. It isn’t huge or crowded , just natural and peaceful.

What an incredible place. Few experiences will give you a sense of awe and amazement at what it was like for those who served our country during WWII, than walking around this ship. Just imagining what it must have been like navigating all those passageways and levels during actual missions. There are countless things to see on the ship. Crew quarters, engine room, mess hall, kitchen, deck guns, bridge and on and on. You could easily spend a whole afternoon just exploring and learning. Just trying to appreciate how these ships were built and operated will keep you engaged for hours.

I've been to this park countless times. I love it. There is so much going for it. They have tons of gazebos and grills for BBQs or for a party. Lots of parking. Large open fields.  Regarding the gazebos, rent it out early if you will for sure need one or you want to be near the kids playgrounds. Speaking of those, they have 2. The park is fairly clean, I've never seen trash out in open areas. They also have a fairly large doggy park that is divided in 2, one for the larger dogs and one for the smaller ones. The doggy areas always have people and I've taken my dog several times.

I was fascinated to see how the original residents of Ybor lived and worked. My tour guide knew so much about the Cuban, Spanish and Italian immigrants that started Ybor City and the tour of the casitas -- their original homes -- was absolutely fascinating. The tour started with a short film and then a walk through the casitas. Then I took my time and explored the musuem and checked out the original domed ovens that were used to bake cuban bread in Ybor's original heyday. This is definitely worth the $4 admission and would be a great family outting.

We visited the Tampa Museum of Art for the first time yesterday, as we wanted to see the Abstract Expressionist Exhibition. This is a wonderful museum, small but spacious, and the art is all displayed so tastefully. The Abstract Expressionist Exhibition was excellent! The collection of paintings was great, and displayed to be easily viewed and admired. I was also impressed with the permanent collection of abstract paintings that were on show. I would definitely recommend this Museum and this exhibition! Please visit if you are in Tampa!

I can't believe I have never been there before. Everyone needs to know about this place. The park is adorable with a little water park for children. The pier is breathtaking overlooking the city of Tampa. We saw dolphins and sting rays and enjoyed taking to people who were fishing. We relaxed on the pier for about 25 minutes then went to have some of the best ice cream ever. I can't wait for my next trip to Tampa to go to this park again. In addition, the parking is free and it's also free to walk on the pier. I loved this place!!!!!!

We rode the trolley system for free on a Saturday and stopped here to check out the park. The only negative is that the playground here is really close to the street so if you have little ones that run off or anything you might not want to take them here. But it is a nice playground and then a nice walk along the water. There is also a small splash pad and a sand play area in front of the Tampa history museum. The Columbia Café is there too. We didn't eat there or go to the museum but we plan on going back to check them out!

The art in this theatre is more that I ever expected! There is something interesting to see wherever your eyes fall. Perhaps it is a bit much for some people, but I just found it intriguing. The art is only enhanced by comfortable seating and interesting films. This is a definite place to see... if only for the art within the restored theatre. Smallish venue so killer place for a concert! I saw George Thorogood here and it was amazing! It is unbelievable inside! You can't even imagine it! Plus, its haunted so take the tour!

This is a well organized and designed viewing facility from the parking lot to the platforms, and finaly a great gift shop with interesting things to purchase that are not dust collectors. It is accross a canal from the Tampa Bay coal fired generating plant, and the warm exhaust water attracts a large heard (pod?) of manatees that can be viewed from above at fairly close range. A couple of hours is enough to devote to this activity unless you become enthralled with the seletion in the gift shop.

Came here for a picnic with my family and may I say this is a very nice park. It's right off the water. They have a number of activities such as frisbee golf, play grounds for children, fishing if you're so inclined, and gazebos for family get togethers, birthday parties, office functions, etc. It's a clean park. it is patrolled by the police, so it's safe (at least I felt safe). And we had a very pleasant time. I recommend coming if you've never been.

This was visited on the off-chance and we had a great day. Staff were brilliant very friendly and helpful. Everything was very reasonably priced. We went for the 10 tickets for $39.99 which worked out the best. Karts, mini golf, batter cage, ropes, trampoline, lots of fun for everyone. Would defo visit again and recommend to friends and family. Can't comment on food as we didn't eat there. The whole family had a great time; thank you Grand Prix Tampa

We had a great time at Empower Adventures! I’ll be honest and say I was skeptical at first considering Florida is mostly flat with not much to offer like some of our neighboring states but it was truly beautiful. Our tour guides were absolutely phenomenal - Shane and Piper - truly I don’t think we could have gotten better guides. They truly made our time together such a blast. Will be returning once our son is a bit older and can join in on the fun.

This park is waterfront, and yet has lots of Shade trees and Pavilions. Great for exercise, lunch picnics and family outings. The scenery is absolutely picturesque with the Spanish Moss hanging in the trees. There are several ball-fields and play-ground areas. Also, benches, picnic tables and jogging/bicycle access to Bayshore Drive. The Rest Rooms are always in very good condition and there is even a Boat Ramp for access to Northern Tampa Bay!

This state park is very clean. A wonderful place to spend the day swimming in the pool, hiking the trails, seeing nature and the rapids. You can even rent a canoe, kayak or beach cruiser. There is so much to do and not too expensive. The cafe is by the pool and very nice. All the staff and park rangers and very helpful and nice. I highly recommend. Oh and dont forget you can even go camping in this state park.

We started our visit with a jaunt around the boardwalk and saw lots of birds and sunbathing turtles. It is so peaceful and beautiful and the bridge makes for a beautiful pictures. We then proceeded to the other side and had a picnic and continued to walk the other path. They have restroom facilities but parking does cost but only $2. Lots of people were kayaking and fishing. We will definitely be back.

Great museum that provides a complete view into the history of the Tampa area. Everything from geography to cigars. Interactive displays and hands on exhibits add to the level of engagement and enjoyment while learning a fascinating story. There are 3 movies on various topics and all were very well done. The pirate area was particularly fun for the kids. Just a really nice experience overall.

This is a small riverside park with plenty of benches and a permanent canopies area for public events. We attended the St Patrick's Day party which was well organised with a variety of activities and lots of stalls. Everyone was having a good time. Security was long key and the crowd was good humoured. It was a great family day with lots of fun activities. Well done to all the organisers !

Our daughter took us to the Water Works in Tampa recently. A great place to visit right along the river. The children climbed on the nets in the playground then we walked along the river. The facility has several food venues in converted industrial buildings. A very interesting visit. We ate at Empamama's. had empanadas , chicken strips and fries. It was very good. We will visit again.

Lots for young kids to do here. I brought my kids. My kids love to play pretend so they had a blast. There was a huge water table, small rock wall, airplane assembly and play climb area. The kids can pretend to be a cashier in Publix, a fireman, a vet, and doctor. Parental guidance for how to play makes it so much more fun! Lots of sanitation stations are available.

I go to the Temple often in the spring when the weather is cool. There are picnic tables outside by the water under oak trees. It is so much fun to sample all the different kinds of food and we always take some home too. They also have plants for sale, usually orchids and I always buy several. Open on Sunday morning only and go early because parking is a big issue!

Horse enthusiasts will enjoy the riding at the Crescent J Ranch. Lots of wildlife to observe on the ride with wranglers who are knowledgeable about flora, fauna, bugs, and creatures. Lunch at the ranch was also very tasty and a welcome stop after the ride. Horses were well cared for, trained, and appropriate safety measures were enforced. Thumbs up!

Really nice park with a very good skate board, scooter area lots of different areas for various skill sets. New shaded play equipment walking trails all shaded, there are basketball and tennis courts here too. Probability one of the nicest parks in the Conroe spring area. However I am reducing the number of stars because of the state of the restrooms. They are full of roaches, the walls have brown marks on them, the floor has puddles of liquid, plus there is no soap in the dispenser. Very disappointing. This is the case for both the male and female toilets

A well used park with a couple of small lakes where you can fish catch and release with a leave trail around the lake, benches and picnic tables. There is a baseball field, a playground with older equipment which is still in good repair. The lake has ducks on it and coypus swimming near the shore. Thankfully the park has a fairly large car park and a public restroom.

Several playgrounds for the children
of different abjlities quite a bit of shady spots. Basketball and tennis courts plus an aquatic center with swim lessons. Has restrooms
Edit 08/13/2020..
Recently renovated the swimming area, now has really nice water slides, a kiddie area with slides, and a nice deep diving pool with diving boards

A pretty park with paths that you can cycle on jog or walk on, tennis courts basketball courts, soccer field and volleyball courts, plus a children's playground all of which I believe are free to Woodlands residents to use. Parking is available. There is a swimming pool which can be used for a small fee that has 3 water slides.

Steep descent into the cave slippery so wear good hike gear shoes.  Very humid inside the cave. Tour takes about 75 minutes, they warn you before entering just to make sure no one has heart issues. Our 4 yr grandson loved  it. Some spectacular chambers definitely worth a visit although I personally preferred Carlsbad Caverns.

The park has recently been repaired due to the flooding caused by all the rains
This is a lovely area to come to walk or bring the children for the play area  there are many shaded benches and tables although this is Texas so there is no breeze and the humidity is high so bring plenty to drink. Lots of parking

Very much a tourist attraction, but restaurants crowded and the ones we went into did not seem as clean as I would have liked. Food. Portions looked large. In the end we did not eat here as with very young children, we were not sure of quality. The zip line looked like fun, but plus a rock wall for climbing.

A really nice town park with sports fields lots of parking, walking trails skate board park playgrounds for both toddlers and bigger kids which are well maintained. Nice shade areas for picnics. The definitely worth a visit. Service has one of the best playground areas I have seen.

A very nice well maintained city park with walking trails a large covered basketball court, RV parking, archery area, scout camping, and more. Lots of picnic tables which are clean. Lots of parking. The playground area has a very tall slide and swings plus lots of climbing areas.

Easy parking on the highway in a pulloff of  both sides. Simple climber up to the arches provides beautiful views of the surrounding area. Make sure you wear good shoes as there are slippery areas due to loose gravil. Worth stopping for

A small park with lots of trees, quite a large play area one for 5 to 12 year olds and another for the little ones. There is also walking trails and a skate park. Reasonable sized free parking area. All the equipment is well maintained.

Interesting area, lots of restaurants and if you are there at the right time you can see a cattle drive of the Texas  longhorns. You have to pay parking but if you are willing to walk a bit there are areas where it is $5 all day

Very well maintained family park just off the I45 with a nice playground.for the kiddies featuring shaded play equipment with a variety of slides and climbing equipment. The paths are well kept with some bridges and pretty walks

I have visited crocodile farms in different countries. This one was impressive, they hadq crocodiles from all over the world plus alligators. They breed them to release into they wild when endagered. Definitely worth a visit

This nature reserve has several trails which are clearly marked and well looked after, particularly liked the live oak trail, not difficult, can walk with a stroller, good for young children. Good place for bird watching.

Playground is reasonable, skateboard park is very small, cracks between concrete slabs big enough for skooter wheels to get stuck in causing accidents. Basketball court is good swimming pool, tennis courts, no toilets

An old fort on an island with guided tours that run every hour at half past. The area is very pretty but make sure you use Mosquito repellant as they are very vi ious here. Also be prepared for the Florida heat.

Good size playground for children with lots of different well maintained equipment a D nice bouncy ground in case they fall  There are grass courts as well more sports. Not really good for walking though
Av very pretty park well maintained. This is a popular park at the end of the Katy Trail. There is parking here which is free, if there is a downside to this park is that I did not see any restrooms.
Very nice well maintained play equipment with a very large slide as a centerpiece. Lots of children and parents there so popular area. They have a public restroom, free parking and waking trails.
A quiet park with fishing boating artery cycling on pavced pathways that stretch for miles. Small children's playground well maintained. Shady areas picnic spots, lots of parking. Worth a visit
Small playground with innovative equipment all new. Children will enjoy playing there. Equipment is not shaded so it's gets hot in the summer. Parking available, plus running trails
Nice shaded park, part of the greenway, play ground obstacle course, nice trails, free entry, restroom, large car park, plus a large dog park. Lots of trails to explore
One of my favorite State Parks in Texas with some very enjoyable hikes a well designed RV parking/camping area with 50 amp electricity and water.
Nice nature walk, several loops, good for bikes. Be nice to have more signs for the different loops. Lots of wildlife if you keep your eyes open

When researching attractions in the twin cities, I was honestly surprised that a museum about flour production had such good reviews. Sort of at the last minute, due in large part to the weather, I decided to go here instead of Como Zoo & Conservatory.

The exhibits themselves are OK. Most, if not all, of them are interactive so very kid friendly. There is also a baking lab that sounds interesting but weweren't able to visit it. But I believe that what makes this museum great are (in ascending order) the short history film and the elevator ride. The short film is a humorous take on the history of Minneapolis. The elevator ride is harder to explain. It also recounts history of the building as you go up and down through the floors. I think this alone is already worth the price of admission. As a bonus, at the end of the elevator ride, you are treated to a great view over the nearby St Anthony Falls and the Stone Arch Bridge.

For parking, Mill Quarter Parking Ramp and Riverfront Municipal Parking Ramp have been suggested. We just did street parking though. If you decide to stay longer in the area, street parking will be inconvenient as there is a time limit.

This is conveniently located right in the center of Mall of America. There are rides for all levels of "thrill". The website does it's best to group the attractions according to this level along with showing height requirements and chaperone policy (if chaperones qualify, they ride free!). All this information is also shown at the ride entrance. This is very useful if you want to plan ahead and to see which ticket package is worth it. The rides themselves are cool to look at since they follow the theme for various Nickolodeon shows.

Lines weren't too bad when we were there (a normal summer weekend). One negative: I escorted my kid up the Pepsi Orange Streak ride, then waited in the far corner where I would not be in anyone's way. The attendant asked me if I was riding then told me to leave. I then told her that I was just waiting for my kid to board. I understand that there is likely a good reason for the policy but I did not appreciate her tone. Thankfuly, the rest of our stay was pleasant and the kids had a blast.

Buying online is almost always better. There are a lot of package options with other MoA attractions so mix and match to save money!

At Universal's Islands of Adventure we focused on the Marvel, Kong, Jurassic Park and Hogsmeade/Hogwarts areas. This seems to be the less crowded of the 2 Universal parks. The rides which seemed to have the craziest wait times are Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey and Incredible Hulk.
Universal as a whole seems to have more manageable waits than Disney although they lack a FastPass like system. (Virtual Line only applies to just a few rides currently) Compared to Disney, Universal really differentiates itself with more thrill rides and a lot of very impressive 3d/4d. This is typically more appealing to older kids. What it lacks though are the more laid-back rides that Disney has to take a break from all the crazy rides throwing you all over the place. Download the Universal app for the park map and to be able to monitor wait times.
Note that Park-to-park ticket holders can ride the Hogwarts express between the 2 parks. The ride is different for each way. This is worth it for Harry Potter fans.

2017 - If asked to choose which Church to visit betwen Basilica of St Mary and Cathedral of St Paul, most would say St Paul. Most would also also say to visit both as much as possible. The basilica is amazing in it's own right and would be a top attraction in many other cities. Just like St Paul, the design in the walls and ceilings are beautifully detailed. There is pay parking under the bridge beside it. Parking is free on Sundays like St Pauls (under the bridge and the one at the opposite side). This is a good complement when you visit Minneapolis Sculpture Garden/Walker Art Center. Loring Park is also nearby.

2019/03 - We attended Mass and there was a free tour after where you could learn about the history of the building (along with some tidbits about St. Paul's Cathedral)

2017 - I wasn't expecting much from this but the good reviews convinced me to go. I really enjoyed it. I regret not taking the package (FlyOver America+Canada). It's just really well done. You really feel like you're flying over the varied landscapes. They do spray a cool mist at certain points of the ride but you won't really get wet.

Note that FlyOver America and FlyOver Canada alternate so if you want a specific one, you may have to wait a while.

Buying online is almost always better. There are a lot of package options with other MoA attractions so mix and match to save money!

2019/03 - Went on Flyover Canada. It is more nature-based than the USA one. Similarly well done.

Good variety of animals and exhibits. If you are there at a specific time, you would have the opportunity to see certain sections of the aquarium have feedings. There are a lot of attendants around the area eager to answer questions. The passport activity and interactive exhibits gives kids (or otherwise) the opportunity to learn more about what they see.

Negatives: The smaller space means potential for more crowding. It would be nice if there was a washroom halfway in. We had to head all the way back to the beginning twice.

Buying online is almost always better. There are a lot of package options with other MoA attractions so mix and match to save money!

I would describe this as a heritage village on steroids. Even if we arrived at opening time I don't think that we would have been able to see everything. There's just too much to see and do. Our kids, of course enjoyed the rides on the old vehicles, especially the Model T. One thing people should note is that most of the structures are actual buildings transported from their original locations, not simply recreations. One thing not obvious on the website is that the rides are a separate cost from the entrance fee. If you plan to ride everything, it is worth getting the ride all you can package which entitles you to a horse carriage ride as well.

This museum has something for everyone. An aquarium, a small aviary, interactive game-like exhibits, an awesome planetarium. The occulus aquarium is something to see as well. Very kid friendly. Plus as a bonus - it has an amazing view of Biscayne Bay.
Note: If you purchase through Go Miami Pass, you don't get the Planetarium show which you get when purchasing directly from their website. You need to purchase the show separately. If you want the Planetarium show, it's not really worth including in the pass.
We parked on the 6th St & 2nd Ave lot for $6. A bit of a walk but close to other attractions.
dislikes: Planetarium show exclusion (with Go Miami Pass)

reviews_attraction.text: Visited during the Spring melt, so waterflow was really strong, but there was still some ice around the falls. This is contrast to pictures I've seen of it frozen and with a more peaceful flow in the summer. There is a trail from the falls/bridge down the river to another bridge but it was quite slippery and sloped towards the river so some people were turning back. You could still take the long way back up the stairs and down another set of stairs past the garden/fountain.There were a few parking spots available on a Friday afternoon. I could imagine this being more difficult in the summer.

With this building it's all about the interior. It was a weekday so visitors only have access to the lobby and atrium. It was very nice though, resembling the interior of a cathedral. Hopefully someday we could come back on the weekend so we could avail of the tour. We noticed workers seemed to be preparing some displays/info about the building. Hopefully this gives weekday visitor a bit more to do instead of just taking pictures without learning anything about the place.
dislikes: Lack of information (no displays or info)

reviews_attraction.text:
Pictures just don't do justice to the scale of this place. It's huge! The combination of paintings, carvings and sculptures from the walls to the ceilings and the dome are amazing. It's a good companion attraction to the Capitol building which you can see at the otherside of Summit/John Ireland blvd

There is a small parking lot beside the Cathedral which easily fills up when there is Mass. You also have the option to park on the street. Just note the restrictions.

Nice park which was smaller than I thought so not much time is needed. The sculptures are interesting though I'm no art enthusiast. Good opportunities to take some fun forced perspective pictures. There was mini-golf but it was pricey. There is whole day outdoor and indoor (at Walker Art Museum) parking for $4 and $5 respectively. A short walk away are Walker Art Center, Basilica of St. Mary and Loring Park so you can take advantage of your whole day parking.

This was included in my Go Miami Card. Impressive mansion with lots of little details. My family really enjoyed the audio tour. The dock was interesting with the ruins and a nice view of the sea. There were even a couple of iguanas sunning themselves despite the crowds. The gardens were beautiful with lots of space to escape the crowds in the house.
They have lots of parking but you may end up at the overflow across the street.

They are pretty good at building anticipation before allowing you to see the rocket. Pictures can't convey how massive the rocket is. The facility is not just about the rocket though. They have shows about the moon landing, various displays and a tribute to fallen astronauts. You could easily spend a lot of time here. Note that this area is only accessible if you join the bus tour (which is included in admission)

The Henry Ford Museum has an extensive collection, especially of cars, other vehicles and machines. They also have furniture, a hands-on math exhibit, the Dymaxion house, Civil rights displays and more. Some have said a half day is enough to see everything but we ended up missing a few areas. If you do this and the factory on the same day, do come as early as possible.

We made an unplanned stop here since Hart Plaza was closed. They have a display of current GM cars and a nice rotating display with an audio/video presentation of vehicles themed after their partners (ex. Disney, NCAA, etc). It looks like they have a fairly large food court but we didn't use it. It also has access to a skywalk and the people mover. Glad we walked in.

We visited this Park while strolling the Waterfront. It has great views of the lake and skyline. There is a beach and mini lake but the water was too cold during our visit. They also have these audio stations (don't know what it's called) where you have to spin a wheel to hear information about the Park. There are some portalets available for visitors.

Inexpensive attraction with an interesting collection of desert and tropical plants plus a small amount of animals well. One of the domes changes their displays so you could have a new experience every season.Be prepared for the Tropical dome, it's very hot and humid. Kids can do the scavenger hunt to keep engaged. Parking is free.

The bridge somewhat reminds me of pictures of old brick/stone bridges in Europe. It also gives you good views of St Anthony Falls, Mill Ruins Park, the Mississippi river and the Minneapolis skyline. Watch out for cyclists, especially if you have kids. Go the Mill Ruins Park to get good views from below and beside the bridge.

Great place that surprisingly isn't too well known yet despite being the only approved Marian apparition site in North America. Plus it is also within or very close to Door County. Aside from the church, the grounds and basement chapel are quiet and well suited to reflection and prayer. They also have a good-sized gift shop.

You have to walk through Universal CityWalk when entering/exiting either Universal park. It's a very visually appealing place. It does a good job of encouraging the crowds to hang around and maybe visit some of the restaurants and other establishments there. Also if I'm not mistaken, parking is free after a certain time.

Honestly, I wasn't paying much attention to Mill Ruins Park. I went there to mostly get good views of Stone Arch Bridge. There is more to see though with interpretive signs, trails and the ruins themselves. A good view of the ruins is from the Stone Arch Bridge, which I sadly missed.

Beautiful Spanish-style Church, especially the stained glass windows. Unfortunately, it was raining so we weren't able to explore the grounds. Location is great for Catholic theme-park visitors. No excuses people :)
We were only able to go outside the walls since it was late in the day (or due to the shutdown). It's a great location though with the historic walls and the sea in the background.
A nice place to hang out with several food trucks serving lunch in warmer weather. The beach is a nice touch as well. The tulips are nice in the Spring.

As far as museums go, we’ve seen better. It’s $25/ticket and the majority of why we visited was to see the art museum because I hate the circus and the countless years of profiting from animal cruelty. The art museum was disappointing. It was poorly organized and displayed and some rooms smelled very musty.
