Much of the work is of the same style and I can’t see making a return visit because despite being able to get an annual pass to share between the Dali and the Ringling, the collections are mostly unchanging. Once you’ve seen it, you’ve seen it. The Asian art area was nice but the majority of the work on display is European. For the size of the place, the cost of the ticket and how much they talk the museum up, I expected a more well rounded collection. The grounds were nice but not worth the $25 admission when you consider how many public grounds, parks and beaches are in the area. The estate is a completely separate ticket and there are varying price tiers which equates to “the more you pay, the more you see”. We didn’t do the house because the initial person who greeted us said it was missable. We ate at the small cafe between the museums and the estate and were extremely sick afterward. In all, if you’ve exhausted all of the museums and don’t mind throwing away $50+ and are willing to risk questionable food, feel free.

We ran into no less than a dozen people who said they'd gotten here via GPS. FYI, if both google and Apple maps tell people to go down trail 13 to trail 22 to park, perhaps it would serve guests to have a sign put up letting people who have never visited, relying solely on GPS, that there is no parking lot and that you shouldn't drive down it without an AWD/4x4 vehicle.

Also, serious amounts of trash all over the place -- from clothing in trees to beer cans and smashed wine bottles. Not really impressed that I've got to say "Watch out for that glass".

I guess if you're from the area, you know all this stuff already. If you're from somewhere that posts signs for park goers and doesn't think trash on the ground is cool, then consider this your heads up.

Worst membership we’ve ever had anywhere.

We were sold on all of the cool places we’d be able to use our reciprocal benefits at, since we live an hour away from Sarasota.

So far we’ve encountered two “90 mile exclusion zone” places near where we live. You need to tell people that before they become members. It makes no sense if you don’t live nearby to take advantage of the local benefits.

Their Christmas light thing is disasterous. It’s packed with drunks who have no plan on supervising their kids or grandkids. And you have to pay extra for it as a member because fundraising. You should tell people that before they show up, too. *puke* There were people having sex on a boardwalk overlook. Very classy.

If I ask "Transformers made me very motion sick, is this a more or less intense ride?" the answer should be "Don't ride this". Instead I got "Oh it's a lot of fun, it's way easier than transformers."

I was THISCLOSE to passing out. I could barely hold my head up by the time the ride ended.

I know there's a sign, but it's hit or miss with rides and motion sickness.

The screens were all very dirty and blurry.

The one saving grace was the fact that there was decent air movement, otherwise I'd have been done for.

The entrance to the ride was pretty cool tough and it would be nice if they had shops or something inside Hogwarts while you wait.

The locker area was a catastrophe.

As far as museums go, this was really weird. It’s basically one short hallway. 90% of what you see has no label. No artist label, no time period, no place of origin, which is pretty atypical for a museum. It is a massive building with extremely unique architecture — there’s barely anything that covers the architecture.

The rooms that are open are pretty but nothing is labeled. Are we looking at replicas? Is this a restored room?

Plus, parking is really hidden. If you drive by it the first time, have fun getting back to it!

We were extremely disappointed with our visit. For how big the building is, you definitely expect to see more.

This place is so cool!! We only lived here for a short time but visited frequently. There's a ton of parking in a bunch of different locations, monuments are unbelievably easy to access, it's clean, peaceful, quiet and so full of gorgeous history!! The only thing I didn't like was how people tailgate while you're driving through. The speed limit is low and it's a huge national historical park -- you'd think tailgating wouldn't be a thing but it is. There were lots of places to take a secluded walk or sit on a bench and just enjoy the scenery around you. We loved it here and actually miss visiting!

Even if you never go inside, it's worth seeing. This place is absolutely breathtaking. From start to finish you're given a really thorough tour that never feels rushed or boring. They're small, personal groups and have I mentioned how gorgeous the place is?! It is. But let me tell you something, when you're at the tip top of that place looking at the landscapes in front of you, you'll just be at a loss for words.

We sadly had to move out of PA before we could experience Christmas at Glencairn, we were really looking forward to that!

Go, spend the day, you'll love it,

Parking is a nightmare but if you can find a place, you’re good. It’s exceptionally clean and there’s a cute little shop and places to eat or drink as well. The sand is loose and nice to walk on but I’d recommend renting one of their umbrellas for the day because past the surface sand, it’s difficult to put your own beach umbrella in. (They use a drill.) it’s big enough that despite the parking lot looking like it’s on jam, you don’t have people right on top of you. There are a lot of shells, the water is always gorgeous and it’s a beautiful spot for sunsets.

What a beautiful place to spend a day! It’s so well kept, clean and quiet. It’s extremely relaxing and the volunteers have a ton of really cool information to share. We’re so glad we happened to see this place.

Edit: Second visit: It’s best to call ahead to see if there’s a wedding going on. When there is, parking is bananas, the two main houses and entire sunken garden area is closed off and you still pay full price. It would be handy if that stuff was on the website so people driving from out of town might pick another date or amend their plans.

Straight away, parking is weird. The lot is almost always full with some people even parallel parking behind parked cars and in the street. If you can maneuver past that, you're all set.

It's gorgeous here! The trails are clean and wide and a really great place to go for a peaceful walk.

You can climb (carefully) along a waterfall, enjoy awesome perspectives above, on or below bridges and despite the parking lot being crowded, you almost never run into any other people.

It's great year round.

If you've never been, maybe go once if you're really struggling to find something to blow $50+ on. If you're an adult, once is enough.

It made me miss the Detroit Science Center, to be honest.

Most displays were supposed to be interactive but were worn out and busted. Everything is really faded and old and kind of dirty. For the space it takes up, we expected to see non stop displays but the gift shop was the best part.

Even the IMAX screen was noticeably dirty and aged.

There is a nice permanent collection of glass art by a decent variety of artists. A medium I feel that is often overlooked in museums of fine art. The rotating collections upstairs are awesome — it’s not just a couple pieces in a tiny room — it’s a full multi room tour with multiple artists and just as good as the first floor. The staff is very friendly and it was nice to be able to park there instead of parking and walking.

This is the worst museum I have ever been to in my life. It's full of total garbage -- unless celebrating all of the things white people have killed or abused in the name of classism is your thing. It's just an old, disorganized museum that honestly isn't worth the $20 we paid. Sorry, I know it's a hot spot for a lot of area visitors but it didn't live up to the hype.

It’s fun to visit once but they need to advertise that the reenactments are ONLY on the weekends and ONLY between certain hours. If you’re there during the week, it’s your typical self guided tour around a fort with some cannons and a whole lot of places you can’t explore. Easiest to visit via one of the trolley stops because parking is ridiculous.

This is the cutest place!!! Everyone there is beyond friendly and knowledgeable about each building and how it tied into local history. I can’t believe it’s free. Truly. It would be so awesome to see this place turn into something like a Greenfield Village in Detroit. Heritage village is a lovely place to relax and putz around for an afternoon.

It’s short and they pack a few too many people into the groups so you’re extremely crammed together, smelling everyone’s b.o and touching strangers’ sweaty bodies. The folks leading the tours really do a great job of getting into it but for what it is and how geeked up they get you, I’d expect the tour to be more thorough.

We have yet to swim here, it seems like sometimes you can and sometimes you can't but if you're looking for a close place to see a gorgeous sunset in the Tampa area, this is it. There is a TON of well organized parking, huge clean restrooms and a lot of things for everyone in the family to enjoy.

Awesome parking area, they even have a specific lot for disabled parking which is really nice. There are ramps and sidewalks so it’s very inclusive for people of all mobility ranges. It’s a large beach and the facilities are always clean. Beautiful sunset location and really fun for shelling.

Not even remotely worth the ticket price. Some cool things to see but they broom you out of the store area within five minutes and the “warehouse” area is kind of a jumble. None of the folks guiding the tour interact with guests. It’s just get em in, recite the script and broom them out.

Great bunch of people, start to finish. We booked after hours online and they fit us in. Everyone we interacted with was friendly, made us feel safe and made sure we had a really fun time. It definitely felt like a surreal, once in a lifetime experience. 10/10 would recommend.

I wish we would have gone with another ghost tour. It’s two stops, a couple stories, a couple quick skits, and then you’re done. They really market it like you’re going to be exploring and immersed in this experience but it’s kind of felt like a school field trip.

It’s improved in the last few years. There’s a nice rotation of exhibitions and an attempt and a more diverse showcase of artists and their work. We visit a few times a year and enjoy the fact that they keep it fresh.

I’ve lost count of how many times I’ve said “The DIA is better...” or “Man, you should see the DIA.” I didn’t realize quite how fortunate I was to have such a collection of art so near, until I moved out of state.
Breathtaking & chilling collection, as well as visiting exhibits. Very friendly staff. On site parking is very limited, especially on the weekends. It’s best to park at a garage and just walk.
Slightly disappointed by the size for how spaced out everything is. Parking is extremely strange and inadequate for the crowds. Worth visiting once.

After hurricane Irma destroyed the boardwalk I came and it was understandable why the boardwalk would be closed, over a year and a half later I visited it and the boardwalk was still closed. Three years later due to the coronavirus supposedly they close the boardwalk again which had barely been open because they recently finished it a few months back, the damn thing was still closed. What’s the point of having the state park exist if visitors can never go down to the bottom. Every year it’s a new baby excuse. At least make the state park have free admission if the sink hole is that unavailable.

While the museum is nice and the exhibit was definitely worth the time to see, a volunteered annoyed the angered out of us. I understand the purpose of masks, but my family and I were hanging out in an open field away from people with our masks in hand and one of the people who ran the museum approached us and told us to put on our mask or that we would have to leave the property. YET this guy proceeds to hang out with his buddies at the bar just up the hill with NO MASK or SOCIAL DISTANCING.
Follow your own damn rules!
Most other volunteers were cool and kind tho.

I have been going to this state park ever since I was very small. This state park ever fails to impress me. If you love to see giant trees, beutiful hammocks and love history, than Highland Hammocks State Park is a great place to visit! I wish I had visited at a better time though. They were doing a controlled fire, and Hurricane Irma had hit hard, and they were still doing some repairs.

For many years, I have been going to Jonathan Disckinson State Park. This state park is one of my personal favorite places to go canoeing or kayaking. It is not very well known but definiatley a place worth cheaking out if you love the outdoors. Jonathan Dickinson State Park has beautiful trails to hike, and a fantastic place to canoe the Locahachee River from.

HOLY COW!!!!!!
The best things about this place:
- Giant rocks by the beach (Very unique for being in Florida)
- Not crowded at all (even on a weekend)
- Well kept, not trashy or dirty
- Beutiful salt and pepper sand

I have nothing to complain about this place.

This place is beautiful compared to what I had originally thought. The scrub jays are what makes this place so cool. If you are lucky they may land on your head while hiking. Just be cautious not to provoke them, as they are territorial.

This place is great if you love the outdoors. I have been here three times, and this place has always been fun to visit. Silver Springs is great for anyone who loves the outdoors. If you are lucky you might actually se a wild monkey!

This state park is filled wth history. It is a fantastic place to just relax and enjoy a hike. This place also has cool battle reanactments about the battles which were fought here during the Secound Seminole War.
If you love to go canoeing or kayaking for just an hour and not too much time, the lagoon or lake (I have no idea), is a great spot and you can do the entire trip to and from the dock within an hour.
I love this state park, and have visited this place several times in the past. Very historical, great camping. The misquitos are harsh though, but the friendly staff make up for it.
Took my son here, this place is definitely worth $1 to visit! We weren't able to see Manatees but were able to interact with several different marinewildlife.
Great interactive experience with lots of history and things to do. I had visited this place a little while back and was able to take some great pictures.
Breathtaking park, with much history behind it. The shrine of our Blessed Mother is fantastic, and the giant cross can be seen from miles away.
This place is GORGEOUS! Definitley a place worth visiting. I think I paid about $3 to get in, and I was able to hike for the entire day.
Pretty state park with some pretty nice beaches. If you have or can rent a paddleboard, the lagoon is an awsome place to go paddling.
I had been here a while back in December. Although this museum was very cool, it was a bit overpriced and parking was $8 an hour.
They have really done well with the remodeling that they had done with Disney Springs. There are many cool shops and great food.
This state park is rich with history and has amazing hiking trails. The view of the river is probably the best part of my trip.
Awsome gardens to visit. The people FIT were very friendly. If you are not a student there it may be difficult to find parking.
Great place with extremely friendly staff. The state park is free of charge and so is the ferry that takes you to the island.
Fun park to go swimming, camping, hiking, etc. I really enjoyed visiting this park, and plan to eventually go camping here.
This place is not half bad. Beutiful preserve, with lots of history. I don't know what's with all the complaints.
There is a beautiful river that runs through this state forest and great hiking trails that lead to the river.
Not state park to stop at, not to much to do. I have heard great things about the battle reinactments though.
This is a really awsome fort filled with history. This fort is a well hidden gem that is worth visiting.

(Translated by Google) The Magic Kingdom icon is everything that is expected of him, majestic, imposing, beautiful, magical, I would venture to say perfect! Inside it is beautiful, there are stained glass windows, you can hear the Cinderella music “A dream is a wish your heart makes ...”, there is the boutique where girls can become princesses, Bibbidi Bobbidi Boutique, based on the fairy godmother , with costumes of all princesses, it is expensive but for those with children I think it is valid! There is also Cinderella´s Royal Table, a table service restaurant with characters that offers breakfast and is very popular, you have to book before. In front of the castle, with a show at selected times (I watched it around 11 am) there is Mickey's Royal Friendship Faire, a beautiful show of music and fires and brings together Mickey's gang (Donald, Daisy, Goofy and Pluto), Tiana and Naveen, Anna, Elsa, Olaf, Rapunzel and Flynn and the vikings rs and the couple who own the house, with a beautiful song that can't help but sing together, I leave the lyrics here for those who want to sing together: the song calls “On This Day ”and has lyrics and music by Brendan Milburn and Valerie Vigoda - On this day… On this day… We will weave every thread, In a tapestry of tales for me and you On this day… (On this day) This very day… There are dreams in your head (This very day) But today's the day those dreams are coming true! Come one, come all, On this day! Be sure to see this show, it is beautiful, charming, this atmosphere of friendship created on the castle stage is very contagious! I made this park on a Tuesday in October and it was very crowded, it was Mickey´s Not So Scary Halloween Party, the Disney Hallowwen party and on these party days there is Hallowishes, the fireworks show in the castle with a theme Halloween, then it turns green, purple, orange, pumpkins, ghosts, Haunted Mansion people and more appear, and taking the opportunity to advise to arrive 40 minutes in advance, it is on the castle stage that the sisters show Sanderson, from the wonderful film Hocus Pocus, the “Hocus Pocus Villain Spelltacular”, an unforgettable show, totally interactive and with the presence of the villains we love, Maleficent, Hades, Evil Queen, Jafar, Cruella, Oogie Boogie, Dr. Facilier, Captain Hook and Cinderella's stepmother, the whole party is top but this show is fun, very well set up, everyone sings along with the final song is a very good energy, it makes the castle even more majestic! O ícone do Magic Kingdom é tudo o que se espera dele, majestoso, imponente, lindo, mágico, arrisco dizer perfeito! Just come on out and play! Come one, come all, and join the fun Come join the special celebration! On this day… We are links in a chain made of silver and gold We are part of a pattern about to unfold We are heroes of stories, as yet to be told We come together on this day! Come one, come all, On this day! Não deixem de ver esse show ele é lindo, encantador, esse clima de amizade criado no palco do castelo é muito contagiante! Fiz esse parque em uma terça-feira de Outubro e estava bem lotado, era dia da Mickey´s Not So Scary Halloween Party, a festa de Hallowwen da Disney e nesses dias de festa ocorre o Hallowishes, o show de fogos no castelo com temática de halloween, então ele fica verde, roxo, laranja, aparecem as abóboras, fantasminhas, o pessoal da Haunted Mansion e muito mais, e aproveitando para aconselhar para chegar com 40 minutos de antecedência, é no palco do castelo que ocorre o show das irmãs Sanderson, do maravilhoso filme Hocus Pocus, o “Hocus Pocus Villain Spelltacular”, um show inesquecível, totalmente interativo e com a presença dos vilões que amamos, Malévola, Hades, Rainha Má, Jafar, Cruella, Oogie Boogie, Dr. Facilier , Capitão Gancho e a madrasta da Cinderela, a festa inteira é top mas esse show é divertidíssimo, muito bem montado, todo mundo canta junto a música final é um energia muito boa, deixa o castelo ainda mais majestoso! Amo de paixão!
likes: Live shows (Mickey's Royal Friendship Faire, Hocus Pocus Villain Spelltacular)

reviews_attraction.text:
(Translated by Google) One of the attractions that I most wanted to visit and that did not disappoint, located in Future World, in Epcot in Orlando, in the area called The Land, is Soarin, a wonderful attraction that travels around the world, we sit in a kind of frame with banks that rise high and practically immerse us in the measurement of the 3D screen. It lasts about 7 minutes and is beautiful and very tasteful. By tips from other people I saw that the best place to sit is row B1, in the center, but this is an illusion, after all you cannot choose where to sit, it depends on your place in the queue and how many people are already in front of you, for example if you are the first in line you will sit at the bottom of the cart and so on. I confess that I was not very lucky in this attraction I sat on one end and one of the support bars bothered my vision a little. It goes high but doesn't move much. I was unable to book a Fast Pass for this attraction and I recommend that you do it because the queue was long, more than half an hour, but the queue for this attraction is interactive, there is a quiz about Disney and some other curiosities that appear on the screens along the attraction that are quite distracting, I thought it was really good. I was so excited to do this attraction that I put the song "Breaking Free" from High School Musical to play the part that scream "Soarin !, Flying!", How delightful I could have done that! Disney is pure magic! And Soarin is a classic, a must see!

(Original)
Uma das atrações que eu mais tinha vontade de visitar e que não decepcionou, localizada no Future World, no Epcot de Orlando, na área intitulada The Land, está o Soarin, atração maravilhosa que percorre vários lugares do mundo, sentamos em uma espécie de armação com bancos que sobe alto e praticamente nos imersa na mensidão do telçao 3d. Dura cerca de 7 minutos e é belíssima e de muito bom gosto. Por dicas de outras pessoas vi que o melhor lugar para se sentar é a fileira B1, no centro, porém isso é ilusão, afinal não se pode escolher onde sentar, depende do seu lugar na fila e de quantas pessoas já estão na sua frente, por exemplo se vc for o primeiro da fila sentará no último lugar do carrinho e assim por diante. Confesso que não dei muita sorte nessa atração sentei em uma ponta e uma das barras de sustentação me incomodou um pouco a visão. Ele vai alto mas não mexe muito. Não consegui marcar Fast Pass para essa atração e recomendo que o façam porque a fila foi longa, mais de meia hora, só que a fila dessa atração é interativa, tem quiz sobre a Disney e algumas outras curiosidades que aparecem nos telões ao longo da atração que distraem bastante, achei bem bolado. Estava tão empolgada para fazer essa atração que coloquei a música "Breaking Free" de High School Musical para tocar na parte que gritam "Soarin!, Flying!", que delícia poder ter feito isso! Disney é pura magia mesmo! E Soarin é um clássico, imperdível!

(Translated by Google) Located in the Islands of Adventure park in Orlando, Seuss Landing is the area dedicated to children in Universal's adventure park. Here we find characters like Cat in the Hat, Thing 1 and 2 (and whole families with these shirts, really cool!) If i Ran the Zoo: Play ground Seco, Caro-seus-el: a themed carousel with characters from the area as well colorful and cute! Adults can also be happy here and join the tour! A jewel in the children's area!
The High in the Sky Seuss Trolley Train Ride! it is a cute and colorful little train that makes a trip on top of Seuss Landing, the area for children in the park. At the time I went, in October, I took a moderate line and the cast members of this attraction were all elderly, just a sympathy. it is not a must-see but it is very pleasant.
One Fish, Two Fish, Red Fish Blue Fish- the attraction is simply a grace! Like the Dumbo of Magic Kingdom just with fish - LEGAL THE MUSIC EH FOFA BUT OF THE FEAR THE ASCENT SEEMS IT WILL FALL. FOR THOSE WHO UNDERSTAND ENGLISH THE MUSIC ASKS “NOW BLUE FISH IS GOING TO RISE- THOSE WHO ARE WITHIN THE BLUE FISH SHOULD PULL THE LEVER FOR IT TO RISE, AND AT THE TIME OF RED FISH IT IS THE RED FISH WHICH GOES DOWN THE BLUE OEO DOWN, IN MY BLUE IT DID RIGHT, BUT I THINK MUSIC HAS LEGAL TO HAVE THAT INTERACTIVITY, I THOUGHT IT WAS CREATIVE, GET OUT OF THERE WITH ENERGY!

(Original)
Localizada no parque Islands of Adventure em Orlando, a Seuss Landing é a área dedicada às crianças no parque da aventura da Universal. Aqui encontramos personagens como Cat in the Hat, Thing 1 and 2 (e familias inteiras com essas camisetas, muito legal!) If i Ran the Zoo: Play ground Seco,  Caro-seuss-el:  um carrosel temático com os personagens da área bem coloridinho e fofo! Adultos também podem ser felizes aqui e participar do passeio! Uma jóia na área das crianças!
The High in the Sky Seuss Trolley Train Ride!  é um trenzinho bonitinho e coloridinho que faz um trajeto no alto da Seuss Landing, a área destinada às crianças no parque. Na época que fui, em outubro, peguei fila moderada e os cast members dessa atração eram todos idosos, uma simpatia só. não é algo imperdível mas é bem agradável.
One Fish, Two Fish, Red Fish Blue Fish-  a atração é simplesmente uma graça!  Tipo o Dumbo do Magic Kingdom só q com peixes - LEGAL A MUSICA EH FOFA MAS DA MEDO A SUBIDA PARECE Q VAI CAIR. PRA QUEM ENTENDE INGLÊS A MUSICA PEDE “AGORA O BLUE FISH VAI SUBIR- AÍ QUEM ESTÁ DENTRO DOS PEIXINHOS AZUIS DEVE PUXAR A ALAVANCA PARA ELE SUBIR, E NA HORA DO RED FISH É O PEIXINHO VERMELHO QUE SOBE O E O AZUL DESCE, NA MINHA VEZ NG FEZ CERTO, MAS ACHEI LEGAL A MUSICA TER ESSA INTERATIVIDADE, ACHEI BEM CRIATIVO, SAÍ DE LÁ CONTENTE COM A ENERGIA!

(Translated by Google) Loved it !, beautiful! Relatively new park, the aquatic Universal is pure charm the volcano has a kind of "god" inside it the Vol called the spirit of Krakatau that gives name to the aquatic roller coaster which by the way is great! Inside it reflects a red face on the stone, it is very well done! The volcano rings a bell from time to time and invites you to clap your hands in the water. (Translated by Google) Flight of the Hipogriff is a light roller coaster, a delight, with a relatively short ride but very fun, she's beautiful, she has the hippogriff in front when she is climbing (with her eggs in the nest!), You can see the house from Hagrid, it's not colorful but it's perfect for the Hogsmeade area of ​​the Islands of Adventure! It has no long lines and is a roller coaster charm, would definitely go back! Here's a video showing how nice it is to slide it! You can spend a little time just watching her!

(Original)
A Flight of the Hipogriff é uma montanha russa levinha, uma delicia, com um trajeto relativamente curto mas bem divertido, ela é linda, tem o hipogriffo na frente quando ela esta subindo (com seus ovos no ninho!), dá pra ver a casa do Hagrid, ela não é colorida mas é perfeita para a área de Hogsmeade no Islands of Adventure! Não tem filas muito grandes e é um charme de montanha russa, voltaria com certeza! Segue vídeo mostrando como é gostoso o deslizar dela! Dá pra gastar um tempinho só a observando!

(Translated by Google) The Mystic Fountain, located on the Lost Continent in the Island of Adventure park in Orlando is simply an attraction in itself, it is a beautiful fountain, with a mythological touch in architecture, which is close to the Poseidon´s Fury attraction. Beautiful, she makes fun of our face and our clothes while letting the water run, she is cute, fun, I spent some time here laughing with her. Of course she speaks English so you have to know a little bit to understand. Cute!

(Original)
The Mystic Fountain, localizada no Lost Continent no parque Island of Adventure em Orlando é simplesmente uma atração à parte, é uma fonte linda, com toque mitológicos na arquitetura, que fica próximo à atração Poseidon´s Fury.  Lindíssima, ela tira sarro da nossa cara e das nossas roupas enquanto deixa a água escorrer, ela é uma graça, divertida, fiquei um tempinho aqui dando risada com ela. Claro que ela fala em inglês então tem que saber um pouquinho pra poder entender. Fofa!

(Translated by Google) Each land of Magic Kingdom has its station, which is where this nice little red train stops. It travels through the lands passing through a very beautiful green area, and it is a way to move between them without having to walk since the park is quite large, but the journey between one and the other takes a long time and there is not much special, it is nice to relax a little after lunch, but it's not a must, there are better things in the park.

(Original)
Cada land do Magic Kingdom tem sua station que é onde esse simpático trenzinho vermelho aporta. Ele percorre as lands passando por uma área verde bem bonita, e é uma forma de se deslocar entre elas sem ter que andar já que o parque é bem grande, porém o trajeto entre uma e outra demora e não tem muita coisa de especial, é bacana para relaxar um pouco depois do almoço, mas não é imperdível, tem coisas melhores no parque.

(Translated by Google) Located in the Sea World of Orlando, in the Sea of ​​Shallows area, next to the Dolphin Theater (where there is the Blue Horizons show), Dolphin Nursery is the Dolphin Nursery, one of the most beautiful things I have ever seen, I confess I didn't find the puppies so small but they are the height of cuteness. I spent a long time here watching this mesmerizing water and the dolphins dance while swimming, it is something that calms and enchants, I loved it!

(Original)
Localizada no Sea World de Orlando, na área Sea of Shallows, próxima ao Dolphin Theater (onde há o show Blue Horizons), a Dolphin Nursery é o Berçário dos golfinhos, uma das coisas mais lindas que já vi, confesso que não achei os filhotes tão pequenos assim mas são o auge da fofura. Fiquei um tempão aqui olhando essa água hipnotizante e a dança dos golfinhos ao nadar, é algo que acalma e encanta, amei!

(Translated by Google) Located at Sea World in Orlando, the Journey to Atlantis attraction is an old Splash. From the 3rd cart on, it doesn't get as wet, and the drop is quite steep! You can wet those who leave there paying 25 cent coins, a smart way to make money haha! In this attraction there is also the single rider, queue for people who like me were single and complete the carts!

(Original)
Localizada no Sea World de Orlando, a atração Journey to Atlantis é um Splash antigo. A partir do 3º carrinho não molha tanto,e a queda é bem íngrime! Dá pra molhar os que saem de lá pagando moedinhas de 25 centavos, uma forma inteligente de ganhar dinheiro haha! Nessa atração também há a single rider, fila para pessoas que como eu estavam avulsas e completam os carrinhos!

Small local place to swim in Crystal River. It has a cute sandy man made
beach. Springs always 74 degrees. Pretty packed on a week days with mother’s and kids. No masks or social distancing themselves on the crowded
Beach. One gal I talked to about where to go, cussed like like a sailor. Every other word was F-word, which says a lot about the locals, and she was about 9 years old. The locals don’t mask up and looked at us like we were from another planet.  Go where its safer not - here. Land of the red neck and big women!

This is a beautiful and large botanical garden with vast multi-level water lily ponds. The Asian, Brazilian and Caribbean gardens have a wide variety of plants and trees. Lovely fruit trees and orchids and bromeliads decorating the branches.  A very special orchid garden draped with vandas, occidiums and phales. The featured artist is Steve Tobin whose ‘Roots’ installations are fun. Wonderful cafe and gift shop.

Janaini Tschape exhibit “Between the Sky and the Water” is deep and the colors rich. The new museum is perfect for her monumental paintings and films.  This renowned German/Brazilian artist has captured the waves in “Melantropics” filmed in Rio and “Blood, Sea” filmed at Weeki Wachee.   Sarasota High  school new museum venue is a success. Good COVID precautions. Vets get in free and the Cafe has exquisite food.

There is so much to enjoy at this museum. They have a diverse collection spanning the ages from Ancient Greece to Hindu art, Dutch Maters to Impressionists, sculpture and more. The museum is perfect for all its great works. There is a fine touch of music that is chosen to pipe in the the galleries that highlights the experience.  Finally very good Covid precautions so you feel safe.

Wow‼️‼️ This museum and the Butterfly Rainforest are the best I have seen in Florida. Incredible exhibit on the Calusa with lifelike representation of their culture. Great display of shell middens, tools and decorative arts. The fossil collection is excellent and the exhibit is large and well done. Underwater mangrove exhibit is really cool. It’s all just a delight‼️

This section of Fakahatchee Strand Preserve gives you a fantastic snapshot of the beautiful Wverglades. If you are a bird watcher this is fantastic. We saw bald eagle, green heron, great blue heron, wood stork, ibises, swallow tail kite, hawk in its nest and gray catbird. Also have fun with the gators.  Royal palms, cypress and the often photographed strangler fig.

Wow. Manatees-arrive at feeding time.  Alligators- plenty and very big. All the wild life...bald eagles, cougar, manatees, birds galore, key deer, otter, bear. As a bird watcher is was a treat to see them up front most injured by cars. So many local birds that just come for the extra company and food. Love this place!! Staff were so nice😍

Mote is the very best!! They have done some wonderful new exhibits and it never disappoints. Great social distancing and Covid precautions. You can’t come to Sarasota without visiting this fantastic aquarium- great for kids. I loved touching live sharks and sting rays. The sea horse exhibit was phenomenal.

Lovely estate on the Caloosahatchee River in historic Ft. Myers. The museum is extensive and contains an excellent history of Edison’s inventions, his Lab along with sections on his travels with his friend Henry Ford. Grounds also have a nursery where you can purchase wide assortment of tropical plants.

This was the high point of our visit here!  The grounds meticulously maintained. The mounds were very accurately displayed. The temple mound was awesome. We saw Scrub Jays, Ibises, woodpeckers and a King Fisher. Also a few snakes. This is now one of our favorite parks. Good job‼️‼️

This was a fantastic state park!! The trails are well marked and maintained, we saw a lot of wildlife including deer, tortoise and many birds. The rangers were so nice and helpful. The swimming area was great and beautiful. Don’t miss this!!

Excellent Covid precautions. This museum is a spectacular experience and is also housed in an architectural gem. Take your time and just enjoy his genius. Outside garden so special and cafe had wonderful Spanish tapas and wine.

This is a spectacular state park with great hiking trails on the river. It was well maintained with plenty of nice picnic areas boat launch and clean facilities. A real gem especially where Gem Spring feeds into Suwannee.

Walk or run the bridge then pause to enjoy the sights and the park. Nice picnic tables and trees to hang a hammock. Go under the bridge to where the families fish and play.  Then catch the sunset and night lights.
This is an excellent museum and great for kids.  Wonderful videos, interactive history of indigenous people, Spanish Conquistadors and shipwrecks. Very good social distancing and Covid precautions.
Nicely maintained state park with plenty of picnic tables and clean facilities. You can hike along the old wagon trail and imagine the battles fought here. Beautiful oak trees, birds and wildlife.
Lovely park with very clean facilities, picnic areas and playgrounds. Kayaking and hiking very good. Helpful ranger and nice campground.  This place has so many great trails. Highly recommend.
This plantation was beautiful. We had a private tour by docent Bill Walters who was so knowledgeable and fun. The antiques are abundant and gorgeous. We loved this location.
These gardens are free to the public. Their specialty is rare fruit trees. This is a nice place for picnics and for viewing nicely maintained spaces.  We really enjoyed it.
Small but worth the trip for a dip in the Suwannee. It had nice little beach areas and a few trails. Porto potties no facilities.  Bring mosquito spray.
Small museum with great baseball history exhibit and interesting pieces of local history located in a beautiful area close to the pier.
Very nice river walk. Restaurants close by and fun to look at the yachts. Don’t forget to visit the Bishop while you are there.
Don’t get your hopes up - it’s basically a small wooden walkway to the top of an Indian mound. Bring mosquito spray.
Nice hiking. The trails were marked but take the map so you know what the numbers stand for. We enjoyed it.

Nice place to walk around and fish. Saw a manatee and some Tarpon. Close to
a lot of nice local spots.

For me there are two quintessential New England must do summer activities while visiting the town of Chatham:

1. Chatham Band concerts in the heart of town.

2. Cape Cod Baseball League - Chatham has the Anglers, who used to be known as the A's until 2008.

The Cape League is a *the* premiere summer league for college players from all over the country.  It's truly an honor to get invited to play with this historical organization.   According to Wiki, this league was founded in 1885 and in 2014 there were 265 Cape Cod alumni playing in MLB.

Some notable former Cape League players include Thurman Munson, Joe Girardi, Aaron Judge, Jacoby Elisbury, Kevin Youkilis, and Jason Varitek.

The games are free, but they have a 50/50 raffle at each one, merchandise such as hats and shirts are sold and local businesses also help sponsor this team.

There is a small lot near the field, so if that is filled you might wish to park in town in the public lots behind Ben Franklin.

Seating is bleacher style, but there are some grassy spots where you could put a folding beach chair.  Nights on the Cape can be cool, so bringing a throw blanket or sweatshirt can be helpful.  There is also a concession stand on premise selling snacks.

These games are truly a community event.  The players are housed with volunteer host families for the duration of the season.  Other individuals provide team meals for the players to eat after the games.

The season is fairly short, it only runs from mid-June through the first week of August.  This is the perfect activity for baseball fans while vacationing on the Cape!
likes: Facilities & Services: Free admission, 50/50 raffle, merchandise, community support
Activities: Community event, player-host family interaction
dislikes: Facilities & Services: Limited parking, basic seating options

reviews_attraction.text:
My husband and I are originally from the Northeast, but have spent the past five years living in coastal cities of California and Florida, so I have missed out on the traditional season of fall.

I would have loved a trip to Asheville to see foliage, but we were short on time and money with a house closing coming up.  I started poking around online and looking for nature preserves that might give us a similar experience.  This was a great place to come and see some gorgeous changing colors.  I'd also suggest Lake Johnson too, especially if you want a paved nature path.

I found this park and saw that they had a plethora of nature trails.  The Sal's Branch Trail looked good to me since it was only 2.8 miles long.

We came late on a Sunday morning on a beautiful fall day and luckily we found parking not too far from the trail.  There were also restrooms where we parked too, which is a plus.

I'd recommend wearing some solid footwear here such as sneakers or even hiking boots.  It's not that there is much of an incline, but the ground can be uneven in spots and rocks are sticking up.

I found the paths to be peaceful and it was nice to be in the woods again.  We found it very easy to follow the markers and stay on the trail too.

We brought our two small dogs with us, my one used to hike the Adirondacks and he loved it.

We will definitely be back in the cooler months to enjoy any sunny days we get on the weekends.

We were a bit pressed for time when we came here on Memorial Day Weekend, we had been staying in St. Pete and trying to cram a TON of stuff in.

I'd say you could easily spend 4-6 hours here if you have time.

There are three components to the Ringling:
1. The estate
2. Circus museum
3. Art museum

We spent most of our time visiting the circus museum and really enjoyed it!  We saw great artwork, historical costumes, a short film, circus posters and other fun artifacts.  This part of the museum was definitely not stuffy and some children may enjoy it.

There were two things that I LOVED here:
1. Mabel's garden - So pretty!  I love taking photos, so I enjoyed my time in here.  The grounds in general were beautiful!
2. The miniature circus village, this is MASSIVE.  This is a recreation of the circus coming to town in very small scale.  There are so many amazing details in this exhibit, it took us a while to take it all in.

Unfortunately, we did not get to see the inside of Ca'D'ZAN, which was Ringling's home.  However, we did get to see the outside of it, which is situated on the waterfront.  I loved all of the architectural elements on the exterior of the home, I hope to come back at some point and tour the inside.

We also missed the art museum. :(

This was a great experience and I'm glad we came and at least saw some of it!

Hollywood Studios is probably my least favorite Disney park, but this land is an improvement to the park.

I was aging out of Disney movies when the Toy Story movies came out, I don't think I've even seen anything other than short clips of the film.  Still, this land is so bright and colorful!  I couldn't wait to visit it on my most recent trip.

This land was like visual overload for my ADD brain!  So much to see and really fun stuff for all ages!  I spotted one of the "toy soldiers" marching around in the land, so cute!  The xmas lights overhead are awesome too and a nice touch!

The day I visited it felt like 100 out, literally.  I watched a few You Tube videos on this land before my visit and I agree with the people griping about the lack of shade.  They need more trees, but this shouldn't be as much of an issue from November through early May when Florida isn't blazing hot.

I visited two of the rides here.  Slinky Dog is great, perfect for younger kids.  Thrilling but not over the top.

I also took a spin on the Alien Swirling Saucers, that was just kind of meh.  I'd rather go on the Tea Cups at Magic Kingdom.

This land is worth checking out when in the park, but try to score some fast passes ahead of time.  It's worth strolling through to see all of the great stuff!

I'm a huge fan of boardwalks, so I was excited to come check this one out.  I hadn't been to Myrtle Beach since 2000, so this walkway was a new addition to the city since my last visit.

Boardwalks are always a great way to experience the beach without going on it!  This one is about 1 mile long, so the size was ideal in my opinion.

We came in the off season of mid-October so parking was not too bad.  We parked a block back from Friendly's and had a short walk over.

There are plenty of places here to eat for all budgets from pizza joints to sit down eateries.  We found a nice spot with a patio overlooking the ocean with friendly service.

We do not live near family, so we often travel with our two small dogs since we do not have a pet sitter.  I was pleased to see that the boardwalk is pet friendly from after Labor Day through the end of April.  We brought our fluffs in their pet stroller, but we spotted others walking their dogs as well.

I've been to a lot of boardwalks in California and NJ, so I think this one measures up to those quite well.  Myrtle Beach and NJ boardwalks do rival each other with the tacky factor.

We stopped here for the first time ever on Memorial Day weekend, most of our time at the beach was spent on the pier.

We parked at one of the public garages for a reasonable price, but the rates did vary.

As we approached the pier we noticed a small playground, also public restrooms are not far from here.

Upon entering the pier area, we noticed the signs for the nightly sunset celebration and another one about free movies under the stars.  We had the misfortune of visiting on a day where the weather was quickly taking a turn for the worst, but I would have loved to come back to check out the evening festivities.

I'm  kind of a pier snob from living in California, but this one is pretty good!  There is also a store in the middle of the pier for snacks, souvenirs, fishing supplies and much more.

I really enjoyed seeing the pelicans up close!  They have no fear, so watch young kids around them.

The other great part about the pier is gazing out at the beautiful blue water and beautiful beach.

Once you leave the pier, there are a decent amount of restaurants to pick from within a 5-10 minute walk.

We came here over Memorial Day Weekend.  There had been a storm earlier in the day, so we couldn't get in the buildings, but we were still able to stroll the grounds and see all of the building exteriors.

This seems like a place older children might enjoy as well, I imagine schools must come here for field trips.

This is a free attraction, which is a plus.  Hours are somewhat limited, so I suggest checking on the website ahead of time.  When we went, it was open Wednesday to Saturday 10-4 and Sunday 1-4.

They also have a small visitor center and a gift shop.  There are a couple of vending machines with drinks by the entrance as well.

The museum features a lot of historical buildings, there is a lengthy description next to each spot that tells you when it was built and moved.

There is a church, sponge warehouse, bandstand, smokehouse, garage, general store, barber shop, train and many more buildings to check out.

Be sure to visit the free botanical gardens that are adjacent to this property.  We left our car here and walked over.
dislikes: Building access restricted (due to storm, but noted as a facility limitation)

reviews_attraction.text:
This is a beautiful historical house in Fort Lauderdale.  Bonnet House is one of the first things I experienced after moving to this area.  This was also a great spot to take out of town visitors to.

This museum is located very close to Fort Lauderdale Beach.  We came for a visit at the end of July and it was scorching hot out.  I think it would be much more pleasant to stroll the grounds in Florida's cooler months, so if you can visit in winter I think you will get a lot more out of this experience.

I especially enjoyed the tour we went on, it was very interesting to learn about the former owners of the property.  Our tour guide was great!

I really liked seeing the interior of the house, but the exterior and the grounds were my favorite part.  There were so many cool architectural elements!

Photography is a bit of a hobby for me, so I enjoyed all of the great photo opportunities found on the grounds.

We went on a tram tour too, that was well worth the couple of bucks since it since it was brutally hot out during our visit.

I've been on this a couple of times since I picked up my annual Disney pass last fall.

I think the tour guide on your boat can really make all the difference for this ride, some are better than others.  Your guide will tell you a ton of corny jokes as you sail this river.

This ride consists of a short boat ride through the "jungle" within the Magic Kingdom.  This is not a thrilling ride, so I recommend this to anyone looking for calmer experiences.

Jungle Cruise has been around forever, but to me it is not that memorable.  I had been to WDW a couple of times growing up and this attraction certainly did not leave an impression on me the way rides like Pirates or Haunted Mansion do.

I've walked by this ride numerous times on various visits.  I'm always shocked to see a 50 minute wait, I'd say 20 minutes is the max I'd spend for it.

We had fast passes for this one day and it took 15 minutes to board the boat.  On another trip it was much faster.

Just kind of an average ride to me, nothing special, but not awful either.

The Jungle Queen is a business on Fort Lauderdale Beach that frequently runs Groupon specials.  For that price it’s a pretty good deal, but not sure that I would want to pay full price.

This is a very mellow riverboat style vessel.  I was not bothered by any of the motions of the boat.

You are on the boat for about 1 hour, you will see a lot of $20 million homes and see how the other 1% lives.

You next arrive on an island with some animals.  The main highlight is the alligator show.  There were also monkeys and other small animals to see.
There is also an opportunity to get your photo taken with a Macaw.

The island also has a snack bar, so that’s perfect if you are starving.

You next board the boat and cruise back to where you got on the ship.

Parking is not free, it will cost you $7 cash.

I live in Fort Lauderdale, but I feel like there isn’t a lot to do when visitors are in town.  This is a good place to take out of towners, but check Groupon first to see if you can save some $.

I'm not the biggest fan of Hollywood Studios, but it's nice to see this new land added to the park.  I know very little about the Toy Story franchise, but I still greatly enjoyed this ride and it's fun theming.

I'm so so on rollercoasters.  I like the ones that are more tame.  I've been on Animal Kingdom's Everest or Disneyland's California Screamin', those rides are a tad intense for me.

Slinky Dog is a BLAST!  This is similar to the Magic Kingdom's Seven Dwarfs Mine Train in the way that it is a much smoother ride than older coasters.

As far as thrill factor, I'd compare it to Seven Dwarfs or Big Thunder.  I wouldn't call this a kiddie coaster, but it's moderately thrilling.

I had such a big smile on my face when I was riding it!  It's just perfection with it's fun drops.  I really enjoyed it and wished I could ride it again, but the wait was around 70 minutes.

I definitely think it's worth waiting for this one up to 1 hour.

My friend showed me this beautiful area when we were visiting Burlington.  I have been in Colchester numerous times over the past 12 years, but never came here!

We came about 1 hour before sunset on a hot day in early summer, so it was quite buggy.  I'd recommend wearing long pants and sleeves if you can or bring bug spray!

Parking was pretty easy and we were able to find a spot quickly.

It was a bit of a walk to get out to Lake Champlain, I'd say about 10 minutes, but it's totally worth it for the views.

Once we got out to the water, it was great to walk along the path with the water on each side.  I just love seeing the lake and the mountains in this beautiful state!  This spot was very peaceful and serene.

According to the city website, this is a 4 mile long and 10 foot wide gravel path.  We spotted other walkers, bikers and people with their pets.

This would be an amazing spot to visit in the early fall!

We visited Boone Plantation while in Charleston, we had also gone to Magnolia on the same trip.  I think I liked Magnolia a smidge better because I loved the gardens there.

Admission was $24, which is high, but we got a decent amount of activities in during our visit.

FYI, the coach tour was basically an open air type of vehicle pulled by a tractor.  It was 42 degrees on the morning we visited, so it got quite chilly.

The house tour was just OK for me, we didn't see a whole lot of it, as this is still used as a private residence.

My favorite part of the visit was learning more about the Gullah culture, it's important to recognize the negative aspects of what went on here in the past too.

The gardens here were smaller than at the Magnolia Plantation.

Overall this was a picturesque place and a good way to learn more about Southern culture.  If I can pick my own rating, I'd give this place 3.5 stars.

I know little about the movie Frozen, but since I have an annual pass for a year I am trying to do every attraction at the parks while I am living in Florida.

I've been to this twice and I enjoyed it both times.

This experience is perfect for already established Frozen fans, as well as those who haver never seen it (like me).

There are two narrators who come out in the beginning to entertain you.  Next you see short clips from the movie throughout this approximately 30 minute show.

You will get to see all of the main characters from the movie too, which should be fun for kids.  Yes, Elsa makes an appearance at the end.

I left here wanting to see the movie Frozen, so Disney worked it's magic on me.  I think this show will be enjoyable for people of almost all ages!

I did not Fast Pass this, I only showed up about 10-15 minutes before showtime and had no troubles getting in.

I had been waiting YEARS to go on this ride for the first time!  My last visit to WDW had been 15 years ago and when I visited Disney California Adventure in 2016, this ride was closed for refurbishment.

This ride is a dated and tamer version of Flight of Passage, but I still love it.  Fortunately I did go on this a few months before the Animal Kingdom ride, so I appreciated this one a lot.  I walked out in complete awe!

This is a great ride for those who are seeking out something mellow, my mom is in her 60's and she LOVED this ride!  She enjoyed seeing some of the places she had visited around the world.

This ride is peaceful and zen.  It's definitely some amazing Disney imagineering, I especially like the various scents  you experience as you fly through the various countries.

If you don't have a fast pass for this, I recommend coming right at rope drop.

I have been coming to Cape Cod since I was two and I had never been here.

I have always spent most of my time between Chatham and Ptown, so it was nice to see a different part of the Cape.

I was here on a weekday a few weeks before the summer season starts up.  Nobody was there when I pulled in, which felt a bit eerie, but then a couple of other cars arrived.

The tower is located on a bit of a hill.  Once you enter the tower it’s a short climb up a spiral staircase.

If you have mobility issues, this may not be for you, but you can still enjoy nice views of the water from where you park the car.

The views up top where quite lovely and this is certainly a unique Cape Cod experience.  The only similar activity on the Cape would be to climb the Ptown monument, which is more of a workout.

I’d recommend checking this out if you are within a 20 min drive of it.

I discovered this park shortly after moving to Raleigh and I greatly enjoy it for long walks.

There are two walking loops around the lake, one is 1.6 miles and the other is 2.8.  I did the longer one the other day and it was so peaceful and quiet!  I spotted bikers, joggers, and other walkers with dogs.

I parked at the 4601 Avent Ferry location.  There are bathrooms here, as well as snack/drink machines, a nice shaded spot with walking chairs and a place to rent small boats.

While walking through the woods, I spotted some picnic pavilions with grills.  This would be a great spot to consider for an outdoor party!

There is also the Thomas G. Crowder Woodland Center at Lake Johnson, which you can rent for private events.  There is a posting with prices near the restroom and it all looked fairly affordable to me.

Awesome place!

We came to visit the Hemingway House while in Key West for a few days.

I don't know TOO much about Hemingway, but I was looking for some activities here that did not involve imbibing copious amounts of alcohol.

We came fairly early in the day, bought tickets and waited for our tour to begin.

I'm not much of a cat person, but hubby is and he loved the 50-60 of them that are on property.  These kitties have six toes and are descendants of Hemingway's own pets.

It's kind of funny to be in a historic house/museum and see the cats just climbing on anything they want.

The interior of the house was nice, but nothing that really knocked my socks off.

I liked the grounds better, they are very lush and tropical.

If you are interested in learning more about Ernest Hemingway, this is your place!

We visited here during the winter time. I'd HIGHLY suggest not coming during the blazing hot South Fl summers, as this garden involves a fair amount of walking.  Don't get me wrong, I love a good long stroll, just not when it's 90 and humid.

My favorite part of the gardens was seeing the Bonsai trees!

The other enjoyable part was the building with the Japanese schoolroom and other cultural aspects of Japan.

This was a peaceful and serene spot to visit.  The gardens were a bit lacking to me.

I'd give this experience 3.5 stars overall, it was a bit underwhelming compared to some other gardens I have been to in other parts of the country.

For tourists visiting South Florida this is a good alternative activity for those who do not relish sitting on the beach for hours.
dislikes: Lacking in comparison to other gardens

reviews_attraction.text:
Do you like creepy hillbilly bears?  Well this is the show for you!

I have vague memories of this show from my childhood, I remember it being dated back in the late 80s.

I do love a lot of the older rides at the parks, but not this one.  I think it needs to go.

I recently went back to this attraction, I haven't been here in at LEAST 15 years, maybe even longer.  It feels like nothing has changed since I was little.

The animatronics are so dated and the characters look worn.

This might be a great place to take young kids who love bears, but I suspect older kids will find this antiquated and boring.

Still, this is a good place to get out of the heat or take a load off your feet for 10 minutes.

To be perfectly honest, we mostly came here since it was pet friendly and our small dog was with us.  That said, I'm really glad we visited this attraction.

We were given a nice greeting and then invited to check out some exhibits in the lobby.

We next went into a room where our guide gave us detailed descriptions of various medical procedures from multiple centuries.  Wow, stuff sure was barbaric back then, but luckily things have changed.  Some of the stories were a bit gruesome, so if you get squeamish easily, this might not be for you.

Our guide was very enthusiastic and she did an awesome job!

I'd highly recommend visiting this spot while you are in St. Augustine.

This is a great little park located at the end of Dunedin's main drag.

The highlight of the park for me was the unique war memorial.  It features a variety of stone samples from all of the different states, so different!

I spotted a small pavilion with picnic tables underneath and a gazebo in the middle of the park.  There are a couple of trash cans and benches sprinkled throughout.

There is a small playground, nice spot to let the kids burn off some energy.

I was so happy to spot a public restroom, this is certainly handy if you are here at the park with kids.

Head across the road to the marina to watch the sunset.

My friend showed me this adorable little overlook when we were up in BTV.  Unfortunately, we came on an overcast day, but it was still nice to take in the lovely views!

This is an amazing place to see sweeping views of the beautiful mountains and Lake Champlain.  I imagine it would also be worth checking out at sunset.  This is also a great spot for budding photographers.

There is a small parking lot here, plus a couple of picnic tables.

I'd say this is a must do for first time visitors to this fabulous city!  Plan to spend 10-15 minutes here.

White Point Garden is a great activity to incorporate with your visit to the Battery and Rainbow Row in this historic city, it's a short walk away.

The park is open from dawn until 11 PM.  Pets are welcome, but they must be leashed from 9-5.

This is first and foremost a waterfront park, but there are a couple of things to see as you stroll through.  We spotted military memorabilia, a gazebo and a couple of statues.

I enjoyed seeing all of the beautiful homes surrounding this park too!

This was a cheesey, but cute ride in Epcot's Mexico pavilion.

I'd recommend this to those who are looking for something mellow.  This is yet another Disney boat ride.

I'd say this attraction feels like a cross between Small World and a Mexico tourism advertisement.

This is definitely a must for kids that love Donald Duck.

We really enjoyed our visit to the Boston Tea Party Ships & Museum; the actors were phenomenal and I really felt transported to the times.  They were great at explaining the events of the night of the Boston Tea Party and it was an immersive experience despite the Covid limitations.
I am giving this attraction 3-stars though, due to FALSE ADVERTISEMENT.  They offer "unlimited tea tasting" on their website, however in order to taste any kind of tea, patrons MUST purchase a $4 cup otherwise you can't taste it. I asked if I could bring my own cup (to make sure) and they said only purchased cups can be used for tea tasting.  This is a SCAM, considering an adult ticket is $20+.  The tea ISN'T FREE. I would skip this attraction based on deceiving promises.

Edited to add: I have since been contacted by Customer Service and they were gracious enough to review the error on their page and fix it.  I appreciate management taking the time to reach out and recognize that they were in the wrong and taking action about it.  Aside from the tea incident, this experience is well worth it. Thanks again

This museum has many wonderful pieces of art by multiple artists around the world.  I particularly enjoyed the Egyptian art display as well as paintings by famous European artists.  The building itself is interesting too; the juxtaposition of the older building and the more modern side, make for interesting architecture and very appealing altogether.  I also enjoyed the large sculptures located outside the museum.  The exhibits are well organized and neatly labeled.
I was a bit annoyed by the "self-perceived" bathroom signs, I didn't find that necessary. It's not necessary to bring a political agenda into a museum, considering they are visited by people of all walks of life.

This is a beautiful museum, not only as far as the collection goes but also the museum building is beautiful and located in a great area in St. Pete.
Parking is easy and decently priced, the museum shop has a great variety of items and the cafe seemed pretty nice too.
The reason I don't give it 5 stars are:
Not enough seating for the cafe considering the amount of people who visit this museum
Wifi quality is not good, and it should be perfect since they have an app that accompanies the visit
The app is not very user friendly.

Other than that, great visit and unforgettable experience.

Be prepared to wait!  The line to get in was very long.  We attempted to visit on Labor Day (Sunday) and gave up after waiting 1.5 hour and still having about 60 cars in front of us.  We returned the day after and our wait was 40 min long, which was better but still long.
The drive through is fun and entertaining and it's great to see all the animals roaming free. The zoo are is nice too, very well kept and clean; it was nice to see the animals eating and being themselves.
Nice souvenir store.  The place would be better if it had a cafe or snack bar.  We enjoyed it.

The museum is great and the wax figures are very realistic.  The layout is perfect and there are great photo spots.
My only complaint is that the figures aren't of mainstream celebrities but rather country singers which might make it unappealing to anyone who isn't into country music.  Of course it is understandable since it is in Nashville, but it still warrants a mention in order to keep the review as objective as possible. The museum isn't that big, so the price might be bit steep too..but there are always coupons online.

Such a great feeling to be "walking around history"; I love how this place makes everyone reflect upon the events of 1770 that led up to the American Revolutionary War and the path to the freedom we enjoy today.  The building itself is unassuming and quaint but once you start appreciating all the details, not only in the architecture but the positioning of the building in the city, you'll see that it's more than just a site, but a place rich in history and many other characteristics. A must see when visiting Boston

It's a beautiful place where you can be in awe of the wonders of nature and God's creation; lots of places to take it all in and take some beautiful photos.
You will see bison, pairie dogs, birds and even snakes.  It is vast so driving around it is probably the best idea.
Aside from nice scenery and lots of social distancing, there isn't much else to see at the Badlands so if you're looking for entertainment, this isn't for you.

Beautiful monument and so moving if you're into American History. I like the detailed map of the Freedom Trail that is posted on premises and it's really a nice place to reflect on the battles fought during the American Revolutionary War and to think of the cost of our freedom.
I'm giving it 4 stars because I wish they had public restrooms on site considering it's a spot visited by many; having one would be really convenient.

It is a great place for children with tons of interesting exhibits for kids of all ages.  I did see that many exhibits were closed or out of service and the museum was a bit messy.  I don't think adults should be charged full price since there is nothing to do for older people and their only purpose is to keep the kids company.  It isn't a "must see", but definitely a fun activity.

It's a nice park with beautiful scenery but you have to go prepared with your own gear and even your own chairs.  I didn't see any seating areas and very few places where you can actually enjoy some shade.  Entrance fee is $20 and it's valid for a week.  We didn't go with any camping plans or even our own kayak, so it was just an ok experience for us.  Lots of great photo spots.

This is such a nice park and in such a nice area in Boston.  Easily accessible by car or public transportation.  The lawn is well kept and the park is very clean; there are several food spots, a playground, clean restrooms and plenty of space to do a nice picnic with friends.  Also, lots of activities to do. Definitely a nice place to hang out when the weather cooperates!

This memorial leaves a lot to be desired, there is really nothing to see there other than stones with the victims names on them; there isn't even a memorable statue or a plaque that labels the memorial.  It is definitely hyped up to be great, but it will go down as a forgettable site on my path. Take a photo if you're close by, but definitely no detour is worth it.

Incredibly church; the architecture is amazing.
Even though we weren't able to get in because of Covid restrictions, the building itself was outstanding.  Located in Copley Square, it is such an iconic image in the Boston landscape.  I did see some questionable people walking around and parking is complicated, but it's definitely worth a visit. So beautiful!

This is definitely a hidden gem and worth a visit. It is a beautiful Scandinavian chapel on a perfect hill; small and quaint but rather interesting.
The carving on the wood was impressive and the calmness of the place was incredible.  I really enjoyed this visit and strongly recommend it to anyone driving around Rapid City.
Free entrance too.

Oldest graveyard in the city and an interesting stop along the Freedom Trail.  It is adjacent to King's Chapel, even though the chapel was built after the cemetery.
It's interesting to walk around the gravestones and read the inscriptions. It is a small place, located in the middle of the city near other important historical sites.

One of my favorite zoos. It is clean with a neat layout and easy to walk around.
The animal areas are kept very clean with lots of viewing areas.
Covid precautions were taken by everyone including staff and patrons.
They have good food/snack options. Parking is easy to access and souvenir shops are well stocked.  Very enjoyable.

Perfect for baseball fans; such a dream to stand in the middle of Fenway Park and experience the vibe. Even though it's one of the smallest MLB parks, it's so historical and so full of energy.
Parking is horrible and expensive, especially during games but the area does have a lot to offer, so it's definitely worth a visit.

Total waste of money.  I cannot believe I paid $30 to visit this place.  You can't even get close to the monument, which is half finished and very far away.  There is a terrible souvenir shop, mediocre restaurant and an attempt at a museum.  But all in all, terrible experience. I do not recommend.

Nice museum to visit while in Nashville.  Visitors get to learn a bit more about the man himself and maybe love his music a little.  It is cozy and appealing to all ages. I really liked the layout and the small collection they have. Definitely worth a stop if you're into museums.

Great area to walk around and enjoy the outdoors.  The Parthenon backdrop is great too and there's a playground for the little ones and a couple of sculptures too, but in reality there isn't much to do other than hang out and sit around.  No public restrooms in sight.

Beautiful park/garden, right next to Boston Common. Easy to access via car, walking or public transportation.  Many activities are closed due to Covid, but the park still has a lot to offer, especially on these sunny days.

Great playground for the kids when visiting Boston Common.  Restrooms are nearby and there's lot of seating space for parents. Only one entryway to the playground which makes it safer.  My son loved it.
Stop if you're in the area but it's not worth a drive.  It's a really old (and free!) attraction which might entertain the kids for a moment, but there isn't anything too exciting to see there.
Nice structure, but it is closed on Mondays so we couldn't get in.  I can't attest for the museum part since we didn't get to visit, but it is a nice building a great photo spot.

Nice place to walk around, most stores are open and following COVID protocol but some lines are ridiculous.
Parking is hard to come by if you visit at peak hours.

The museum looks huge from the outside so we had planned on a whole day but once you're in, it is very compartmentalized with a lot of open space. The exhibits themselves were very informative and we loved the aquarium and the movie but none of them were very large or time consuming. We saw Journey to The Stars and it is shown in a dome as your seat leans back and you watch above. In all reality, we were done in a couple hours and changed our movie to 4 hrs earlier than we had planned.  I feel the art museum ticket should be included as it is was overpriced for just the science museum.

One of the best museums to visit. World renowned due to the vast collection of art. I highly recommended a visit to the museum along with the glass pavilion.  They do live glass blowing displays that are phenomenal to watch. The front of the art museum is a popular spot for photographing weddings and prom. We went for my daughter's senior prom. They also hold weddings at the museum. I was one of the first people to get married there and hold my reception there as well.

What a quaint little winery tucked off the road just outside of Elk Rapids. Ellis was my wine connoisseur and she was very knowledgeable.  I did the wine testing. There were 3 of their wines, one fron Oregon, which is on the 45th parallel as well, and they had a cider.  The cider surprised me. It was nice and light. The wines were delicious. Highly recommend checking it out. They also do an airbnb and she took me on a tour. Would be a wonderful place to stay.

The self guided tour told us to skip this, but we opted to stop and we were glad we did.  It cost us $20 to get in. $15 for adults and $5 for kids under 18. My daughter is 16. This has a nice little shop and a place to eat. The botanical gardens are gorgeous with beautiful varieties of plants and flowers.  There are spectacular views of Pouhokamo Falls and Keopuka Rock. I highly recommend spending the money to stop if you have time.

This was a fabulous tour and boat ride. They knew just where to take us for great views of whales. We saw a dozen or so whales and also were privy to see one breach. The tour was very professional and on the ride out walked around and showed different informational facts about the whales. There is a snack bar on board as well. Highly reccommend.

My daughter and I spent the morning sunbathing and swimming.  Just a great beach.  This beach has black sand as well.  Not as dark as the state park but it's black.  There is a place to eat and change clothes.  There are showers for rinsing sand. We were here early and pretty much had the beach to ourselves.

I went to the original casinos back in the 80's where you entered through a canvas door so going to this casino took me back to those days. I really liked this place. Very small and private. Very nice man at the door helped me register for my card. I had a really good time and the machines paid out nicely.

Absolutely stunning.  As you are driving over the bridge.  To the left is a large parking area. Well worth getting out of the car to get some photos.  We actually went to Ono Organic Farms then back to Hana and the view of the falls from that way is gorgeous.  A must see.

A MUST see and just being there is a special moment. We opted to stand in line for that iconic photo and it was well worth it. The line went fast. They did a fantastic job restoring the buoy after the hurricane damage. I highly recommended stopping to see and for photos.

Every beach on Maui is beautiful and has its own unique qualities.  This one is no exception.  Cliffs make a beautiful back drop to the crashing ocean waves.  It was cool watching the surfers. They sell huli huli chicken close by as well. A must see.

Love Maumee Bay. Anytime of year is great but birding is my favorite.  It is a must for anyone looking for that one of a kind birding experience.  There is a wide variety of nature.  There is a nature center and hotel with indoor/outdoor pool.

I just love  my Sylvania community parks.  This is just a nice peaceful neighborhood park with trees, nature and a nice walking path.  It has a seasonal pond to swim in or rent a paddle boat. There is a nice playground for the little ones.

Beautiful park. The views are amazing. You can tour the lighthouse for an extra fee. I believe $5 and it does cost $9 to get in to tge state park but these fees cover the maintenance of the lighthouse and park. I'm glad I stopped.

The drive ul from Traverse City to see this lighthouse is gorgeous.  One of the most beautiful rides I have been on. The lighthouse is well worth the ride. Just really neat to drive to the tip of that  peninsula.
Loved this place. They have a guided tour and a self guided tour. Check prices before you go because it is pricey. Just a beautiful estate full of history. Plan 2-3 hours or so to stroll the grounds.
This is a must do. Spring time is great to see the migrating birds and Summer is great for ducks, egrets, herrons. Etc. They have boardwalks for walking.  Look close and you may even see an eagle.
I love to watch the people fishing off the pier and getting up close to the pelicans fishing off the pier as well. The shelling is great. Be prepared to pay for parking but well worth it.
Love, love, love this area. This is a must see.  Why drive all the way to the east coast? Drive the kids and family up here. You will not be disappointed.  Beautiful large sandy beach.
I absolutely love this area. There is something magical about this area. Seeing the bridge, the lighthouse and the straights. It's only a few hours North to drive, and well worth it.
Just beautiful out at the park. The Fall colors were beautiful.  My daughter used the park to take Senior photos. They turned out fantastic. Highly recommend exploring.
One of the many sights worth seeing in Salem. It is better to take a tour to get the real history behind all of the attractions.
This park has gone through recent renovations. This is a place where the locals go to put their boats in to get on Lake Erie.
An amazing area. The banyan trees are huge and very impressive to see. The whole town of Lahaina is very neat to see.
Great area. Seems very private. I visited in the Fall past swimming season but loved the area and the views.
Every stop, every turn is a sight to behold on the road to Hana and this is no exception.  Beautiful.

Overall, this is the least expensive attraction that bears the Disney name.  On that front, it's the best value for your whole Disney experience.  All that said, Disney Springs is an enjoyable time.  Plenty of dining and cool shopping options.  There is a Bibbity Bobbity Boutique which is a better proposition than doing the one at Magic Kingdom.  Its a big complex with a little bit of everything for most interests.  You can shop, saunter, dine and drink all with the guarantee of Disney quality control.

Approaching middle age, I'd never been here before and that is straight up diappointing! This place was fantastic.  Such an abundance of interactive living history coupled with an informative museum.  So much to experience and learn at Jamestown.  The significance of this location is grossly overlooked - as a whole its possible and advised to spend a half day here to absorb it all.  Not just a compliment to Williamsburg but a destination in its own right.

Absolutely amazed at this park! Nice amd accessible location with a great variety of activities.  The science cemter has an array of simple exhibits that the kids really enjoyed - simple isn't a derisive statement, simple just means easily enjoyable.  The playground was equally impressive. Its big and had enough activities to accommodate a large crowd.  Really kept the kids entertained and the cleanliness of the park was excellent.  Will be back.

Been biking for a while but never made it a point to try this trail. BIG MISTAKE!  This series of trails has just about everything I would ever want for a casual ride.  This is not a hard technical trail but it has solid climbs, nice features, technical turns, etc.  Plus its laid out in a way to make it really easy to pick and chose how and when you want to ride.  Nice river reviews and a helluva biking afternoon.

Always been a huge fan of this park as it offers really unique activities.  One of the only parks I know that features snorkling tours and glass bottom boat tours of the coral reef.  Just be warned - book those attractions in advance!  Otherwise, it has reallt nice camping in the florida keys, as well as hiking, biking, kayaking.  Really hard to get bored at this park.  True gem of Florida!

Seriously, the real exhibit is actual Colonial Williamsburg but the visitor center is really nice.
