I don't quitenunderstand the purpose of this off site visitor center and the long walk or bus ride to the Williamsburg site but it is a really nice building.  Vaguely reminiscent of a modern government office but only the not quite clear start of the experience of Colonial Williamsburg.

This is a dope park.  You get to ride in a boat tugged along by a donkey.  Very few parks offer scenic views of a canal facilitated by a beast of burden.  Typically, this wouldnt be cool but its about history.  Canal history.  While its a tad bit whitewashed - know that in a lawless place reliant on canals, most of the people succame to syphilis and dysentery.

For whatever reason, i really enjoyed thisnattraction at Colonial Williamsburg.  To be fair, it was the second place we visited.  However, the staff was impossibly good at describing the significance of the Wythe House amd its importamce in the birth of our nation.  Overall - just go to Colonial Williamsburg.  Its a real gem of America.

Williamsburg is a real gem.  No exception.  In mamy ways, the governors palace is the cornerstone of the whole place.  Its elaborate and has much of the history intact in terms of artifacts of relevance.  Learned so much about Colonial life and how this former British governors post became part of America.  Really cool experience.

We've been coming to this park for years and love it.  The beach access is outstanding and  the view is excellent.  Absolutely gorgeous! Additionally, the park has a nice bbq - picnic area as well as a nice playground for the kids.  Can't say enough nice things about tjis park! Be cautious- you will probably wait for parking.

Absolutely loved this park! Ironicly found this park because of the overly thick neck guy video.  The park was fantastic with angreat variety of activities:  sports fields, roller hockey, science exhibit and a nice playground.  The kids adored the playground.  Despite the crowd it never busy.  Absolutely plan on going back!

This is an absolute gem of the Detroit area and testament to its history.  We greatly enjoyed taking the kids here fornan emd of summer hooray!  It is largely out door centered so definately a weather permitting destination.  The Edison exhibit was fantastic.  Can easily spend an emtire day meandering and learning.

This is a cute little park in Bath.  The play structure is top notch.  Daughter absolutely loved it.  Park has decent parking and a nice bathroom facilities.  There is a public boat launch across the street.  Fun way to kill a couple hours and pretend the kids playground are obatacles from American Ninja Warrior.

I was totally looking for a.playground for the kids and to be fair - i found something playground-esque.  It.also resembled a ninja warrior obstacle course which my four year old did surprisingly well at.  Little bit scared by that.  Unconventionality aside, its a nice park with courts, a pavilion and open space.

A crown jewel of the Detroit area! This is bar none one of the finest museums of industry and technology in the world.  No hyperbole in that statement.  The HF satisfies interests of all types - history, science, manufacturing, Americana and then some.  This is worth a whole day's visit to take in the spectacle.

This was a fantastic little aquarium just a short drive from virginia beach.  Major focus on the local watershed and a fair amount of learning activities about hydrology, geology and the ecosystem.  Can easily spend 3 - 4 hours here with the kids.  Definately a destination if you're heading to Virginia Beach!

Very much so liked visiting this place!  The lighthouse is quaint and its a short walk from the parking lot.  As a Hessler, the Hesler cabin was a nice treat.  The beach front is small but adorable with crystal clear water.  The whole spot is a fun diversion for a couple hours when visiting Traverse.

Love this park! Love it so much I got married there.  Very nice place and great staff.  Clean orderly, and a real variety of activies.  Played out a weird Top Gun volleyball fantasy not but 50 yards from the scenic overlook where I said my wedding vows.  Plus - snow tubing in the winter!

Hidden gem in Lansing! This is a nice little zoo with a fairly intuitive layout.  Excellent for taking a stroll with the family & very affordable!  If you are looking for a huge zoo - this is not your place but the habitats are top notch and there is a great deal fornthe kids to enjoy!

This was a solid little park with lake access for fishing.  We were able to picnic and enjoy the water.  Pleasant for a couple hours distraction.  Be aware - not much a playground and not beach per se.  Also, facilities consist of a porta john and not a very pleasant one at that.

Very majestic view of the dunes and.  The whole scenic trail ride preceeding was quite lovely through the old growth forest and dune area.  Short hike to the overlook so it should be manageable for most.
This is a wonderful park for the city of East Lansing.  I have held my daughter's birthday party here twice.  Facilities are clean.  Plenty of restrooms. The playground is fantastic.
Very nice park a few blocks from downtown.  Vendor area for the tulip fest which is a delight.  There are bathrooms in the park under the gazebo but i wouldn't recommend using them.
This is a great county park.  Diverse range of activities for kids and families.  Held my daughter's birthday party here and everyone enjoyed it.  Facilities are all very well kept.
Loved this park! Went here to kill some time and it was outstanding. Really nice plauground for the kids. Place is clean and well maintained.

A cool place to visit just to hang or eat out with friebds/family. I've been on the ride twice once when it was fairly new and once on the NYE. The first time, which was just a regular day, my friend and I were given a cabin and seemed like everyone else was given a private cabin too. We rode around 6:30 and that was a perfect time to see the sunset. The second time I went with my husband, the advertisement banner about "ask a crew for a private cabin" was all over the entrance without the price. Of course, I asked a boarding crew since it was a special holiday and the crew member annoyingly shouted "it's $200" or something around that price range. Sure, it's a holiday but ridiculous... Anyway, riding once is enough. I go here once in a while now for the lively atmosphere and surrounding restaurants.

Wow. If I can give a 10 out of 10, I totally would. This cavern is huge and gorgeous. The tour is a guided tour that leaves every 20 min. behind the ticket booth. Tickets ($28 per adult) include the admission into smaller museums next door. The trip takes about 1 hour and 10-15 min. Use restrooms located behind the ticket booth prior to going under the ground floor. Inside is chilly but not cold. Please follow the guide's instructions and do not touch the rocky formations because the areas of contamination are clearly visible in contrast with the natural areas. This is a must go place when you are in VA. It's beautiful!

Such an amazing place. I highly recommend everyone to visit here in VA/DC. The outlook to the falls is very close to the parking lot and many parking places are shaded from the heat of afternoon sun. The entrance fee is small and well worth the visit. Bathroom near the visitor center is clean but I would recommend people to use it before getting on the trail because this is only one near the area. There are many little outlook points other than the ones listed on the guide map. The nature is absolutely gorgeous and walking through the trail paths is really refreshing away from the busy city life.

It is a cool ride but the queue area seems better than the actual ride itself. Neatly designed 4D ride with a traditional theme park storyline that uses screens from both sides of the ride. The first time I had to wait 90 minutes for a 5 minute amusement but the decor and design of the waiting areas really made up for it. Now, I was lucky to sit on the end seat but I dont know what the experience would have been, had I been on one of the middle seats. It may have been much better if the ride vehicle was not a covered up truck with lateral screens.

Oldie but a goodie!! A must-visit attraction for Florida visitors. I bring my families here when they visit from other states or countries. This outdoor place is large, full of other animals like raccoon, owl, crocodiles, deer, tortoise, snakes, and etc. Gators varying in sizes are found everywhere in open ponds. Albaino gators also live here. It can be very hot during hot summer days so bring a bottled water, however, no food is allowed. A separate swamp walk is cool to walk through as well. You may see wild turtles and a snake or two.

This is one ride that you shouldn't be sad about if you never get to "ride" it. The queue area has references to the movie, cool props and whatnot but they are nowhere near impressive. Matter of fact, this is one of the worst queue areas in this theme park. So boring... The ride mechanism is similar to the Kong ride in IOA but once again, worse. Universal should consider bringing Jaws back instead of this joke. Can't wait to see this getting torn down in [hopefully] near future.

The historical downtown area is really pretty. Lots of art shops, gift shops, cafes, and restaurants. Many benches are available for sitting and the atmosphere is very welcoming. The area is pet friendly as well. The best part is the boardwalk along the river. The structure is well maintained and nature-friendly. The side rails are not available for most of the walkways so be careful when walking with kids.

A must-try at IOA. This is a classic attraction that you shouldn't miss out. Among all the fancy new rides, it finds its way to standout through the times. Intro is awesome, as if you are really entering into the Jurassic park, though it appears aged. The climb into the tunnel is always thrilling and drop is amazing (I can barely keep my eyes open). I hope universal keeps this forever.

Such a cute little beach park that is free of access and parking. Public restroom stalls are available though you shouldn't expect a super clean bathroom. The beach area is not big but enough to enjoy a beach side picnic while watching sunset. I would rather give a stronger recommendation for this place for sunset watching then the beach side.

Various choices of Disney-themed shops, fashion items, restaurants, and entertainment options make this place great. It hosts shows and art showcases from time to time too. Parking can be a challenge but you'll always find a spot somewhere. The entrance is free of charge and it is suitable for both adults and families with children.

A smaller size of museum but there is a plenty of art pieces to look at. Admission price for college students with their ID is $5. Subject matter changes quite often so if you like art exhibits, this is a nice local place to come. It is near by the Orlando Science Museum so there are plenty of parking spaces around.

A small little open grassy field for a quick outing. The park is well-maintained with fountains and benches. Winter Park train station is right next to it so the area can be noisy but I like it. Mini concerts or events are often held including art shows. Good for families, couples, kids, and animals.

Lively place day and night. Lots of events for locals including food trucks. Holiday season is my favorite because of all the decorations. This man-made park is family friendly, pet friendly, parking is plenty, public restroom is clean, and small restaurant/cafe are within walking distance.

A quick access to the beach. The parking used to be free but now they charge you $20 for an all-day parking. However, the parking lot is well-maintained and so are the bathrooms, playground, picnic tables, and stairs. If you are wanting to have a beach day, this is a good place to come.

Love this park! Quick beach access with plenty of parking and it is free! As a non-Volusia county resident, paying $10 for a couple hour beach outing was a bit much but this park is free to all beach-goers. Public restroom with showers are nearby for a quick cleanup.

One of many beautiful overlooks of Shenandoah. Each overlook looks similar yet unique. When the weather is good, you will be able to see the gorgeous curves of mountain range. Sunset is really pretty too and that's when the animal sightings appear the best.

It's a fun ride for both little ones and adults. It's entertaining but without the extra intensity. It is nicely themed and if you get on it at evening right before the Hogwarts light show, you'll get the best seat in the house.

Well-maintained and lovely. The day when I was here the temperature was around 96°F. So even though the breeze was hot and humid, seeing the peaceful river made it all better. Shade coverings were definitely a plus.

A quiet secluded park away from a large crowd. Went here during a hot sunny noon but the shades kept the area cool enough to enjoy the walk. The light greenish hue spring looks beautiful but it is not large.
Such an easy access from the river walk/downtown Tampa. Size of museum is perfect and collections are interesting. Free to students with an ID or $15 per person. Gift shop is good to check out too.
Well-maintained walkway along the river. Don't expect a lot of shaded areas but if you avoid a very hot summer noonday, the breeze should be enough. I saw several dolphins while taking a walk.
Nice park with large trees and shaded areas. You can see people having photo shoots here often. It's really calming to hear the lake water waving toward the shore when boats go by.
A small park but very cute. I used to use their tennis court to practice tennis. Small lakes are pretty and peaceful. It's a nice place to walk with pets and kids.
An excellent beach park to visit. Free parking, free access, and pet friendly (with the leash please). It was clean and a bit crowded but otherwise, no complaints.
Small museum with wonderful visual offerings. The museum is well organized and super classy. The chapel area is my favorite because you can actually sitdown there.

UPDATED 9-4-18 - Unfortunately this place has changed dramatically and I’m lowering my rating from 5 stars to 2!

A massive new building now sits in the middle of the green space.  Where you use to be able to spread out anywhere, there’s now only a couple strips of grass to sit on.  It used to be completely dark, and now this big building spews lots of light, and takes up over 50% of the space.

The Trail lights are red, even the bathroom lights are red (to prevent white light), but it’s completely pointless because of the building!  There’s white light shining through the closed blinds.  There’s white lights on top of the roof.  The parking lots are right next to the seating area and car lights shine all over the area.  The building is event used for events, which is a total conflict of what this spot is meant for!  This serene spot is now polluted with car alarms, super bright car lights, loud people coming in and out of the event space.  Not to mention the cramped space to find a spot.

It’s sad what they chose to do to this spot... it used to be so remote, quiet, dark... now you’d be better off pulling off to the side of the road pretty much anywhere.

ORIGINAL:  A really cool spot, deep in the woods. We visited during a celestial event and it was cool. It’s gets quite busy actually, get there before dusk or the parking lot could fill up. It was a unique and cool experience to be around lots of people in a super quiet area. Lots of people with powerful telescopes that will likely let you take a look too!

Who would have ever imagined that Disney would have a park with free admission AND free parking?!  This is it, the catch is there’s not much entertainment and no attractions/rides.

But there are extensive shops, merchandise, and food.  There’s literally 49 restaurants here, and growing.  We walked through some of the amazing restaurants and we were in awe!  Paddlefish, T-Rex, Boathouse, Planet Hollywood are some of the themed restaurants that are incredible just to check out.

We had some wonderful Mexican food at Frontera Cocina, and some (Americanized) Cuban food at Bongo’s Cuban Cafe.  If you weren’t aware, Disney has a very high standard of food, and Disney Springs is no different.  Average dish is $20, and most restaurants we visited seemed to have dishes above and below that mark.

Springs great for strolling around, it’s big and very scenic with a beautiful pond in the middle and many restaurants have water frontage.  There is some entertainment (bowling, concerts, tethered hot air balloon ride) but you have to pay for them.  Overall, a must visit place, and you’ll likely want to return.

The TOP place for adventure on the UP!  This was our favorite place visited during our 1 week trip.
The rowboats go to an island, and there are falls on either side.  You have to take your own rowboat, and it costs $7 a person or $20 per family. That made us hesitate, but we’re so glad we did it.
There’s boardwalks to explore. You can take your dog anywhere.  You can walk into and out of the falls at any part.
We walked into waterfalls, underneath them, and it was wonderful and exhilarating. There’s dozens of platforms, paths, and waterfall features. Experiencing these natural features by being a part of it is incredible.

An incredible place to spend 2-5 hours!  In the top 3 out our UP favorite places. Go out of your way to visit if you’re at all interested. It has natural beauty, well restored ruins, an old slag rock beach, well documented history, and scenic trails.
We had lunch inside an old mansion, looking out over the water, in view of the huge rock face. Doesn’t get much better than that.
There are about 10 structures, you can walk around and inside all of them and touch anything you want.  The place has a beautiful 1.5 mile hike on the top of the rock facade. Look at the pictures for a fraction of what you’ll see here.

As good as it gets - a perfect Florida beach!  I think it has the softest, whitest sand I’ve ever seen.  Very important - go when tides are low!!  It makes the beach about 10x’s bigger, exposes shells, sea sponges, and lots more area to explore.
The south 1/4 of the island is dog friendly and is a big draw. It’s not off leash.  It about a third mile walk to reach it.
From Honeymoon you can take a ferry to get to Caldesi, another island with supposedly great and more secluded beaches.
Nice pavilion mid-way down the island road, it sells food, drinks, and toys with a nice 2nd level seating area overlook.
likes: Pavilion with food, drinks, and seating

reviews_attraction.text:
This is a nice feature, but don’t drive too far to visit it.  We stayed at a vacation home nearby and were able to walk to it.  The playgrounds along it are quite nice but you’ll only do that if you have young kids.
One big thing we didn’t realize before we visited - the Manatee River this Riverwalk is alongside isn’t nice.  It’s murky water, very little boat traffic, and you won’t see any fish or manatees.
We found more enjoyment in the things just OFF the Riverwalk - Pier 22, South Florida Museum and Aquarium, Old Main Street, Motorworks Brewery.

An awesome lighthouse to visit.  Has a very big gift shop, and you can climb the tower for $5.  Climb the tower.  The views are just incredible.  Kids have to be 40” to climb.  The steps are quite narrow and there’s 2 narrow hatches that take some contorting to get through.

Be aware - there’s NO parking at the lighthouse.  You have to park in the State Park and take the 1.5 mile hike on a sandy but flat trail.  This makes it more special for us, but it does take some time and energy, and a nice day to take the trip.

Not much to do here, but nice facilities and story boards.  They admit to this being a long shot that it was the actual spot where DeSoto camped at, there was really no structures or documentation proving it.  It’s more of a tribute to his southeast US expedition.
There’s basically a small indoor building with gift shop, then a mile long trail through woods and along some coastline. There is a nice open grassy area in front overlooking the water, but not a beach or access to the water.

As good as it gets. The park is one of our favorite places on earth. Hiking Trails, cliffs, a private island, beaches, equipment rentals, overlooks, its own full length golf course, its own play and musicals Northern Sky Theater, kayaking, biking, camp store, rich history, ruins, nature center, campgrounds, lighthouse, scenic spots. I can't think of one additional thing I wish this state park had. We drive from southern Michigan and camp here for a week each year.

Kitch-iti-kipi is here!  A must see site in the UP. It’s free to visit with a State Park pass.  It’s not much, but take the 10 minute raft ride and enjoy the quiet smooth water and look at all the sights below surface.  Visit on a sunny day.
It’s amazing in Michigan to see 40’ down in completely clear water.  The jade green tint is beautiful. A surprising amount of very large trout inhabit this spring too.
Very nice gift shop, any kind of collectible you want.

This is a complex of 4 buildings including a nice shipwreck museum.  It’s next to the spacious Michilimackinac State Park, right on the lakeshore.

It’s a $9 admission but worth it, and the lighthouse tower climb is free.  That’s a must see, it’s not very high but the views are great, and you’ll have a tour guide to give you some info.

The shipwreck museum, narrated movie building, and nice merchandise shop round this place out to a 5 Star visit.

Not easy to find and a bit secluded, but’s it’s no secret and it’s quite busy here.  The parking lot will fill up, and there’s zero parking outside of their lot.  We had to wait for 10 minutes just to get into the parking lot, that was at 11:15am.  But it’s worth a wait, large white sand wraparound beach, decent beach restaurant on site, shaded areas and kids playground.  Watch the tides as it changes this beach quite a bit.

Different than an average Florida spring area, you can’t walk into the springs at all.  There’s only a platform from which you can jump into a swimming area, and it’s 10+ feet deep.
But - the big plus of this place is it’s trails.  Lots of winding and paved trails, numerous waterfalls, scenic spots, and grassy areas for picnics.
It’s $2 for adults to get in, and is dog friendly.  Large store and gift shop on site also.

A beautiful piece of Mother Nature, easily accessible in northern VA. The overlook platforms are very close to the visitor center, so you only have to walk maybe 300 yards total. But take a walk down their trails, you'll find picnic areas, areas of historical interest, ruins from old canal locks, and off the beaten path scenery of the river and even more falls and rapids. Visitor Center is nice as well with displays.

This is a common launching and landing spot for those exploring the Weeki Wachi looking for Manatees.  The main kayak and equipment rental shop is right across the river.

It’s busy and the parking is limited.  It is quite challenging to get in and out of - especially with larger vehicles and/or trailers.

You can visit just the park, there is a small beach and swimming area.  I believe there is a fee to use the lot.

An incredible visit within Pictured Rocks.  It’s a 1/4 mile walk out to this big dune. It’s an inspiring view as you crest and go over the top.  You can take the super steep slope all the way down to the water - there are warnings so don’t do it if you’re not healthy.  If you like hiking and adventure - do it - view at the bottom looking up is incredible too!

One of the better State Park areas in southwest Michigan. Camping, boating, fishing, day-use, biking, hiking is all excellent. I really like the lake - very irregular shaped so there's lots of inlets and such to fish and explore. My wife visits here twice a year on an overnight trip for team building. They stay in really nice lodges on the property.

It’s beautiful and a must see.  Great viewing platform but only from one side.  Your visit here will be pretty quick... not much to see other than the falls from the one platform.

But - make sure the visit the Camp on this same property - it has 6 shops and restaurants including a massive gift shop. You could spend a couple hours at the Camp alone.

Great wines and a fun experience. Tastings are free. It’s located in the Settlement Shops - a couple old multi-level repurposed buildings with lots of other fun shops to visit.

Cedarburg Spice and Settlement Gold are our favorites.  You can take your glass of wine outside and enjoy on a patio near a peaceful river.

After the city beach, this is probably Ludington’s best park!  Water and trails all around, the marina, the Badger nearby, 2 areas of kids play equipment, and some very nice sculptures that tell the story of Ludington’s past.  An excellent spot for a sunset, a romantic stroll, a picnic, or some kids play time.

Below average for a northern VA winery. Wine slush was small for $10. I did a full tasting, didn't find any to be great. And for some of the views you get with other wineries in the area, this one has a small outdoor area with really no view. Wine servers didn't seem happy at all to be there.

Very cool rural setting, indoor area feels like you're in a cave. They have live music on Saturdays on their nice porch overlook into early Fall. The wine tasting experience was a bit slow, wines were good but too pricy to buy a bottle.

A nice find, excellent view of mountains from the outside seating. Wines were good, Chardonnay was superb. Only downside was employees - a bit unprofessional as they were talking openly about personal matters between themselves.
Nicer shoreline spot in TC. Pavilion is brand new and has a full food and snack bar. Bathrooms are air conditioned. Splash pad and very nice beach. Saw the Blue Angels from here.
The best spot to relax with a view of the bridge.  Picnic and grassy spots, a couple short paths. Bathroom facilities.

This is a beautiful and easily accessible park with a nice boardwalk. I've been here a half a dozen times and I've never been disappointed. During those visits I've encountered a great variety of bird species and their babies, iguana and other lizards, as well as alligators and their babies. Bring your binoculars and/or camera and enjoy the nature!

A very cute and cozy park in an easy to access location with good amount of parking available. Beautiful green areas and fascinating pieces of art are on display all over the park. Good walking path and pier offer an opportunity to observe wildlife and nature in an sub-urban setting. Could use some cleaning up.

A great natural area to explore the not so common scrub landscape in an easily accessible location in Boynton Beach. Both paved and unpaved paths take you right in the middle of nature and offer an opportunity to observe several different bird species and see tortoise, for example.

The Japanese Gardens at Morikami Park are a sight to see and a relaxing place to spend a few hours i n a very peaceful environment. For example, the bonsai garden is one of the best in the world and I have not seen anything like the stone gardens in anywhere else in Florida.

A beautiful and easily accessible natural area right in the middle of urban Boca Raton. A good portion of the nature trail is paved and offers great chances to observe wildlife like tortoise, lizards, and birds. The unpaved path takes you even closer to the nature.

A great Natural Area right next to the Spanish River Library (they share a parking lot). Offers a good amount of paved and unpaved walking paths to experience the beautiful South Florida nature in a very easily accessible and welcoming location.

A very versatile park that takes you on a boardwalk over the intercoastal to one of the most beaches that you will ever see. Also offers a Satinleaf nature trail in a tropical hardwood hammock as well as a nature center with a lot to offer.

Cozy natural area in an easy to access location with easy to access paved nature trail. Beautiful scenery and good birding opportunity. Don't forget to check out the Saw Palmetto Natural Area, which is a short walking distance away!

A beautiful and cozy natural area in an easy to access location with good parking. Lots of wildlife to observe, for example birds, butterflies, and lizards and I was fortunate enough to meet a gorgeous grey fox during my visit.

Great cozy park in central location. While this park looks small it still has a lot to offer like a mile long walking path with exercise equipment, picnic grills and tables, as well playground, and clean facilities.

A nice cozy park in the middle of a nice neighborhood on a beautiful lake. On my visit I encountered several different birds and close to 30 iguanas. Fishing pier and fishing from the shore options also offered.
A nice little park with a walking path, playground, and sports activities available. There is also a youth activity center there. Easy to get to with a good amount of parking space available.
A beautiful park in a very central location in downtown Delray Beach. Right on the intercoastal with great views. Good parking and a lot to do in the close proximity of the park.
Beautiful cozy park hiding in plain sight in the middle of a beautiful neighborhood. A big playground, picnic tables, and grills. Do not miss the nature trail across the street!
This is one of the cleanest parks that you will ever see. It's also beautiful and cozy with plenty of parking and a lot to do. Excellent picnic areas and good facilities.
A nice casino in a very convenient and easy to access location. Courteous staff, fairly priced drinks, and fun gaming at any time of the day. A bonus: great restaurants!
A very nice and clean park on Lake Ida. Plenty of parking available and clean facilities. Playground, dog park, good fishing opportunities, and nice walking path.
Good size Nature Center with friendly staff and a lot of information to offer. Easily accessible boardwalks offer an opportunity to observe nature and wildlife.
A clean and beautiful park in a middle of a neighborhood. A good-length walking path and an outdoor playground are available. However, very limited parking.
A beautiful and good size park with lots of sports amenities and a playground. Very clean, including the facilities. Plenty of parking available.
Nice clean Nature Preserve that offers a great opportunity to observe wildlife. Paved and unpaved walking paths provide easy access to nature.
Huge park with plenty to do for audiences of all ages. Clean, easy to access, central location, a lot of parking available, beautiful scenery.
Great park in a convenient non-busy location. Lots of amenities such as picnic tables and grills, a water park, walking path, and a dog park.
Cozy Nature Center in central location. A lot to do and learn for audiences of all ages. Very friendly staff and volunteers.
A clean park in a central location. A good length walking path, clean facilities, and playground are among the amenities.

Great Ball Park. Good views of the City, and the Roberto Clemente Bridge.
No parking - have to arrange in advance, or do as the locals do and park downtown and walk over the bridge. Good sightlines from almost all the seats. Nice scoreboard, but no clock? Two hotels just across the street.
Pricey food, pricey beer, just like every other stadium. Riverwalk, and 4 statues of great Pirates' players. Best shot of the stadium is from across the River.

A really nice ride on some really nice equipment. Restored vintage cars.
Can opt for a most excellent dining car.
Diesels on both ends, but the steam engine is being restored. Delightful Disney-esque station.
The original line started construction in 1865, with first train in 1869.
Lots of high level bridges. All it needs is a destination, and they are working on that.
Competent and friendly staff.
Ample parking.

Mortally wounded in the attach on Fort Duquesne in Pittsburgh which he led, General Braddock was buried in the road, and the horses and wagons obscured the location, so he could not be dug up and desecrated. Years later, during the construction of the National Road, remains were recovered and reburied to the side, with a monument. That piece of land is considered British Territory. Quiet, respectful location.

Very nice. Easily reached on foot. Includes the sites of British and French Fortifications from the French & Indian War era. Interpretive displays in the museum are very good (as are the bathrooms). Great view of the river traffic. Good views of downtown and North Shore, including the baseball and football stadiums. Good view of the Duquesne Incline. Quiet place, many shade trees and benches.

The canal museum is located in the basement of the train station.
A must see. The large grassy area is the old canalboat loading
basin. The boats were drawn up under a bridge, and the coal dumped
form railroad cars. There is a replica canal boat,  and a monument
to the Irish workers who labored on both the canal and the railroad.
good restaurant, and a bike shop.

Very nice National Park, no admission fee, ample parking. restrooms. Mostly intact. The furnace and water-powered bellows, workshops, the coke burner. Lots of wagons. Barn and workers housing, mostly furnished in period stuff.  Working farm, with horses and sheep. Knowledgeable and helpful staff. Gift shop with relevant books.

Ride the empire Builder, and walk over to the Glacier Park Lodge.
Pricey, but it's the retro angle that is going on. Nice, original train station
originally built by the Great Northern RR, back when cars were few.
Now served by Amtrak. Lodge built for the tourists, back when there was no "motels." Luxury of a by-gone age.

The mountain will decide whether you get to see it or not. Weather is hte issue. If you are lucky, you will see the iconic mountain with its snow cap.
It is visible from a great distance, being over 14,000 feet tall. It is an active volcano. ah, well, it may go the way of Mt. St. Helens, but it will be worth the view.

Well, I wasn't disappointed. A really nice hiking area, with great views. Lewis & Clark Museum, with friendly, helpful, knowledgeable staff.
It is actually a World War-2 defensive position, repurposed. Day use fee, which you can pay (couple of dollars) via credit card at machines in the parking lots.

Built around the time the railroad was considering steam engines to replace horses. In daily use for commuter and heavy freight. When E.F. Baldwin's father sent him to Europe to study architecture, he studied cathedrals. His bridges and stations look that way. He also did the marc station in Laurel.

Way out in the swamp, an elevated boardwalk. There are some nasty critters down in the water. Interpretive center, knowledgable staff. Rest rooms. Somewhat limited parking. DO NOT pet the gators. Some aquative species I had not heard of. Good tree canopy over the walkway for shade.

Incredible selection of plants. There are quite a few things in the herb garden that I had heard of, but never saw before. Arranged in little ecosystems, that you can walk through. Unfortunately, next to the airport, so not very quiet. Great place for photography. Adequate parking.

In the old train station. Very knowledge and helpful staff, who got us oriented. There was a big festival going on in town when we stopped by.
There is a very interesting building adjacent, marked "Amazon." It was 19th century Industrial, and had been repurposed to Condo's.

Great park for all ages. Take the tram tour, get up close and personal with bison, elk, caribou, trumpeter swans, etc. Extremely knowledgeable and helpful staff. Clean restrooms, snack bar. Elaborate play areas for the little guys.

Awesome. Aircraft and spacecraft. Gets crowded. Nice light restaurant. Clean rest rooms. Lots to see and do, great for kids.
Dont miss the other part across the street, accessible by overhead walkway with elevators. Ample parking.
Nice facility. Most people clean up after their pets. 2 areas, one for small and one for large. Source of water. Throw a ball, and all the retrievers are after it, and the non-retrievers are "what?"
Amazing that such a place exists. Drive-thru, frequent pull-offs. Great interpretive center. Active fossil lab. Gift shop, clean rest rooms. Water. Awesome. Dont miss this. Bucket list item.
amazing. and I believe they are going to finish the torso, and his horse. Nice interpretive center, with displays. Ample parking, clean rest rooms. admission fee. A work in progress.
likes: Facilities & Services: Clean Restrooms, Ample Parking

reviews_attraction.text:
Ypi would think this would be in a major U.S. City on the East Coast,.
but its on a Reservoir. Great hiking and just hanging-out spot.  Day-use watersports and fishing. Restrooms.
Nice entrance to Yellowstone, north. He got to lay down the cornerstone, and the Army Corps of Engineers did the heavy lifting. Plenty of photo opportunities from either side.
Many Native American artifacts, and poster presentations. This is a complex subject, still in litigation. Sometimes, the government is not right. A discrase.
Very nice facility. Ample shaded parking. Free, but check the closing times. Ample water birds. Big wooden bridge over the inlet. Very friendly and peaceful.

A chance to visit a war hero from ww-2. Shows some signs of wear and tear, but gives you some insite
of the working conditions of the men who sailed her.
Very nice. Interpretive movie. Clean restrooms. Drinking fountain. Nice shop. See the dinosaur workshop. Ample parking. Friendly and helpful staff.

Rugged and wild. 4wd recommended.
Camping. Carry in your own water.
Hike down to the canal and the PawPaw tunnel.

Great place for the complete family!....The agro-market is awesome, fresh and local products, all knd fruit and vegetables, at a very reasonable prices....Sea food very expensive!...
Very well conserved the Koreshan settlement with late 1800's architecture style...So beautiful, simple and comfortable. Furnitures in the houses well conserved and clean, it made me feel in time with the residents.
Native plants for sale, but if we need people be serious with native plants, it need to be cheaper than Home Depot...The worker there, all are volunteer and very nice.
The many paths to walk around,  loose gravel, very bad for any kind of shoes, trolley or wheelchair...
The natural trail very nice for the natural vegetation and the Gopher Tortoise is found in the trail, but hard to walk on. Part gravel, part sand, the nice one, the part in bamboo area which is natural and is river side with many spot to river view....The bamboo, even if is not native to florida, here should be ok since it was used for Koreshan people to fence.

Went to this preserve so I love wild life.  My meanly interest was to walk the trail. Saylor Trail  1 1/2 miles. My surprise, at the trailhead, the corner with the city trash big container full and bunch of shopping bags around everywhere, beach chairs, beach umbrellas and all kind of beach and garbage...Smelling very bad, also coming from the restroom. Very disappointment , meanly for the travelers or tourist that have to pay $8.00 to go in the park....Free for Collier resident with the updated sticker....
The first part of the trail was easy, nice walk  throwout  a shady, natural sandy path, beach side with many access to the beach. found some wild flowers, the tortoise a couple of time, .....On the way back , the other part of the trail,  all nice same around , except the gravel path , the make really hard the walk for any kind of shoes.....The Sea Oat well conserved,  and  beautiful  sun set ....The park close at sunset....

I got there early morning, the GPS took me to a gate that was not the right one. ...a poster hanging on the gate, put me on the road again for 1/4 more mile, straight to the parking lot at Crew Cypress  Dome Trailhead.... Trails are designed by colors, ... Yellow, Green, White and red, all connected continued. Many blue sign in between (shortcut) in case you change mind and want to go back... Wild flowers all kinds along the trail, birds and deer...  I was interested in the Caracara Prairie Preserve ( Red Trail) but I missed this time.  I made the mistake to walk yellow, green first, was tired when got the red one. Didn't finished watching the prairie... I will be back to start for the red trail
All trails comfortable to all ages, shaded mostly, wide and visibility through the bushes , many people in the trail, sound good to me

Since the place is visited for people that drive many miles to get here, I think Tennessee State Park could take care of few detalles that have been missed and it does not cost any money: Trailhead across the road just beside power plant tower, missed information about all trails and secondary trails . Others "trails", that take you to the wrong place, missed sign for how many miles for some  of the trail.  etc, etc, etc.....
Any way, it worthy all sacrificios....The place is really amazing!  ...By the way, take away the photo with the tower that say: "Short Springs Recreation Area"..It does not exist....The closer place to camping is Barton Spring, about 10 miles drive. A good sign to get the trai head is the Power Plant....

Went to the 43 annual canoe race. lot of amenities....band playing, food, drinks....Te competition is a fantastic show....lot of fun but very organized.....The Crayton Cove itself has many option for dining, bar, souvenir shopping ,  boat ramp,  all accessible. Just a walk along the big dock is an amazing view....From the dock leaving many different ships tours, during the day to keys or fishing and private rental...Sightseeing tour...Just the are around the Naples City Dock sign is needing more attention, need updated with native plants and more plants near the area to beautify it since this place is usually visited for peoples all around the world  ....
dislikes: Area around Naples City Dock needs beautification

reviews_attraction.text: Park-beach very nice. Kayaking and a long board walk that take you to the beach, good the option of transportation....particular beach with shell-sand mix....and and lot of birds and wild flowers....lot of option for comfortable laying down and shade....Drink can be served to your site. But i have been charged $5.00 for a drink, a coke in a plastic cup, with more ice than coke.......This beach is accessible to expensive Resort but it is also a public beach......It is a great place, with a wonderful particular sunset....It good be good pay attention to this created prices for the prestige and serious of the place.

Visited this place few weeks ago with my camera searching for birds and wild flowers. I found some road side flowers, but not many birds....The 1/2 mile, wooded fenced trail perfect for every one, accessible to wheelchair. along this walk, all kind of plants, wetland plants and tree. no birds or alligator, actually.... Higher, over the lever of the lake, a comfortable , roofed place with great view to all around. bench to seat , with your lunch wait for bids with a good 400 to 600 mm lens.....Butterflies Garden plants and native plants abandoned.

The mark was incorrect placed on Google map It get right now.......The camp ground does not exist any more . Now is there a trail . The trail name   is Shutes Branch Mountain Bike Trail. Trailhead is at the beginning of Shutes Branch Road....  with many option to take the trail along this rd....and Weather station rd
The Recreation and access area is located at creek shores, other side of Saundersville rd...with just  a picnic area with tables and grill.....where the mark is placed now...

Was not my destination today. Just want to check it out... The side visited was awesome.... A typical florida swamp wildlife, exuberante vegetation , wild flowers, birds and people....just 17 miles from downtown naples, very relaxing... a long boarding walk accessible to all ages end or take you to a natural trail the it is suppose that you will share with alegate but safe thought. ... I decide not to do it by myself and come back sooner and walk with a programed guided group....

In the heart of down town Naples this trail offer us all we can ask. Beautiful for kids, and seniors, long we'll protected boarding walk, accessible from three different road, accessible to kayaking and fishing ramp. Big,  with bench and picnics table.  The board is surrounded for diversity of wildlife make the walk very relaxing...a nice natural trail, observation of wild flowers and birds..
Would be nice add some many more pollinator, butterflies attractiv plants...

I was at The Conservancy Center for the Earth day Celebration with my grand kids. We had an awesome day, all very organized, lots of activity for the care of our Planet.  Very instructional. Great job of volunteers and workers  in all areas, helpful, nice, patience with kids....We really had fantastic day! Awesome and free eco-tour in the Gordon river. Very well trained guide , the boat captain, very nice and fun . Kids really enjoyed it.

Love the lighting of the buildings around the park... A special playground look great for exercise the kids and parents. Picnic tables. Awesome 👍 River Walk, bench and resting areas  along the river.  ... Very sad many homeless all day and night ... some of them grouped together ocuping the testing areas...all of these make the park no safe and ugly....

well shaded trail, sanded path which makes easy the walk. amazing Butterfly garden few feet from trailhead. fantasy overlooks with view to the water way allow watch dolphins, birds and kayakers... some of the overlooks blocked by bushes thought.... since the Gate was open 8 am, I still was in the trail at 11 abut firmnd heat beat me really bad.

Love this Park......the view of Att tower fantastic from many different spots...a great collection of native and wild flowers, butterfly and birds,  along of greenway, free parking every body can enjoy the down town activities,.....beautiful designed stage for free concerts all kind......Absolutely amazing!....

Beautiful Victorian style house built around 1860.....Located just at  about interception Gallatin Rd and Vietnam Veteran in Hendersonville.....is now home of the Henderonville Arts Council.....Great arts activity for children after school, Display of arts works gallery from artist in the community....

Visited the place with my Grand kids. Awesome day full of all kind of activities for all ages. All was a great learning about wild life and conservation...was added to it a boat tour to the Rookery Bay with very experienced guide. place accessible, water and very clean restrooms...

Very dissatisfied. Park closed when 🌞 sun is already in the halfway to the meddle of the sky and heat it up Florida beaches.... Out of sense!... Give a good reason for what, all gated Parks can't open at 6 am at least spring and summer season....???!!!.

Fantastic, absolutely gorgeous. Good care. Large variety all kind of plants. Native and not native grown with beautiful color... Garden design allow photographer go around for all way of view. A little expensive. No senior discount. Sad.

Abandoned!... And covid-19 shouldn't be blamed for it... Abandoned Butterfly Garden... No gophers, or bees... A nice primitive Trail very shaded connect us with the shell trail at Cullum's... Along imperial river...

Very bad organized for Easter. Sun was very agresivo, no water, vendors machine no working....The area was divided for children ages, some of the area had more eggs than others. Just I stayed for the kids.
Big, awesome park, great parking areas, all of it take you to the beach. Pick-nick space with tables and grill area at the shade of the tree, beautiful vegetation with wild flowers and butterflies.
Awesome driving in Fall Season.... Shade, curving road inside the park with many picnics areas along the drive.... Beautiful colorful trees.... Just in the heart of the city of Nashville
Abundance of wild life in its own world... Safe boarding walk.... $14.00 pass expensive. Still 2 area closed for Irma hurricane.... Butterflies garden abandoned...
Pink Muhly Grass, Beach Sunflowers y Lantana... Very clean, well maintained. The park very well conserved and protected, is watched all time.
It is in the city of Naples Veteran park, good for exercise, walk under fresh tree shade. Good play ground with roof.

this is a really excellent and fun-loving place! A lot of locals coming here that are really friendly and fun to hang out with. There's not much in the way of food just some cheese and meat platters along with some bags snacks. The wines are really kind of this is a really excellent and fun loving place! A lot of locals coming here that are really friendly and fun to hang out with. There's not much in the way of food just some cheese and meat platters along with some bags snack. The wines are really kind of foreign selection. They only make six different wines to white sand for red. The chambourcin and the Noiret are really excellent in my opinion.
A very fun place to spend an afternoon.

What an incredible place!
It never fails to amaze me how they built them back in the day. The entire complex has huge Parks, a very helpful staff, and many different parts to the museum. Pay the extra $5 and go to the display on the first floor and up on the tower, it's worth every penny of it. Don't forget their to side museums up on the second level with the tower, one of them holds a display about American and Australian cooperation and more from World War II Afghanistan. A really interesting display.
I must see if you're a history buff and in the Kansas City area.

They really need park down along the river. Lots of Open Spaces, with plenty of picnic tables and Pavilions for you to have an event in it. The old Ford is kind of cool but it's close for the summer of 2018! Lots of Open Fields to walk around in very well-maintained. There's an old Tomahawk throwing area at 1 Park, which is kind of cool. Lots of picnic tables for you to sit and relax and enjoy the weather. It's right down along the river, so right now the rivers up and it looks like the park may actually flood when the water is really high.

What a really delightful State Park! I have to give it to the state of Indiana, and they did a really good job with this. I am a big history buff, and I really enjoy going to the historical sites around the country. This was right up there with the best of the.  The museum, the 1920s living Farm, the Native American village, all the museum displays, and the headquarters were extremely well done and delightful. A very informative place I highly recommend it.

I don't think that I need to elaborate on just how beautiful the Florida beaches are, and this one is no exception. The truly unique thing about this section of the beach though, is that it's so lightly used. This is way off the beaten path apparently and I I didn't see the parking lot filled the whole day that I was here. It's just as beautiful as any other Beach, and has far far less traffic through it. The parking is free and so is the beach!

I am a major history buff and love coming to places like this. Feel of history in actually is a very good one to come to. The display, the movies, the theaters and everything on the inside or really informative. It's really kind of incredible to see this portion of History brought forward. It really was a crucial time. Well worth your time if you're in Kansas City. Don't miss walking out into the courtyard, it's worth a stroll back there.

I'm always amazed that the beauty of swope Park. I love these huge Park set in the center of these large cities, not many cities had this much for thought over a hundred years ago to save a large area like this for an open Park. The zoo here is amazing, The starlight theater is amazing, and all the pavilions that they have for used by the public are really need to look at. Always a nice experience to come here.

Kind of a neat Park. Very well maintained, if you read the signs it was newly renovated not too long ago. There's a section that's blocked off that's being renovated right now, and it kind of cuts the park in half. There is one way in and one way out, if you try to walk the loop like there would be if there was no construction, you end up walking out of a bank parking lot and trying to get back to the entrance.

I really need park right here in the middle of the city really. I didn't even know this was here. You park in a large parking lot actually, and the Falls aren't even a 30-second walk away. And you're right at the top of them with a great view of the falls. They're actually for different Falls here, with one main one that looks to be at least 30 to 40 ft tall.
Definitely well worth the time to check out!

what a beautiful setting for this. One of the many many places that I visit that tries to preserve the history of our nation. Apparently there used to be a lot more statues and memorials, before a bunch of short-sighted History revisionist force their removal. The park itself is still very beautiful in the cemetery itself is still moving. Definitely worth the visit if you get a chance.

Really neat downtown park. Lots and lots and lots of parking, so you should have no problem finding a place to park down here, and it's all free. Some really need historical stuff around here to look at 2. The bridges are kind of worth coming down to have a look at. Lots of picnic tables and volleyball courts and all kinds of stuff down here to have fun with. Lots of room!

What a beautiful spot!
When you're walking around down here in the museum area, there are lots of parks and plenty of places to walk around in. But, this is one of the more beautiful ones. It's really calm and Serene and ran into one other person while I was here. Seems to be a nice out-of-the-way spot where you can relax a little bit listen to some waterfalls.

All that I can say is wow, just wow!
everything in here is incredible, the building alone is worth coming in to look at, even if you don't enjoy the yard. Every form of art you can think of is in here it is really an amazing collection. The building itself is just incredible, it really is. Just another example of how they used to build them in the day.

I didn't get to go inside, they have very limited number of tours on the weekends. You have to go 4 blocks away from here to the downtown office in order to buy tickets to get into the tour. Then they will let you know when the next tour is scheduled up, and you can go on the tour. You can't just walk up and walk in after buying a ticket.

A very nice selection of wines. They do a tasting in the room which was very nice, 5 wines for $5 which is very reasonable. A lot of dry wines and a lot of red wines at this Vineyard. They do some very good Merlot's which I really enjoyed. There were some sweet and semi-sweet wines also to choose from but they're not my favorites.

What a very surprisingly nice place. I really wasn't expecting anything as nice as what I found here, this far off the beaten path. But is very nice park, a very nice Visitor Center, I really need old house that is very well restored and kept up, well worth the trip if you have the time, it's a really neat place to visit.

kind of a weird place that have a marker on maps for. It looks like it's somebody's house. I drove up to have a look at it, and it honestly looks like it's built in and it's being used as somebody's house. I didn't bother to stop or get out of the car, because I just wasn't sure if you were allowed to go in.

A really neat museum, a little pricey for what you get IMHO. The displays are really neat, and the Gift Shop is pretty cool. The Museum is located in the middle of the River Side Market, so if you go on a Saturday you have a lot of things to do around the outside of the museum also. Worth the trip.

a beautiful city park located right next to the Jupiter Beach. This park has its own Beach and little Bay on the inside that is absolutely gorgeous. Lots of picnic areas and parking, both of them are free which is a great option. Pavilions and all kinds of things here for a family outing.

really kind of a neat place, the staff is very friendly. You must come down to this Visitor Center before going to the home, get a ticket and sign up for one of the scheduled tours. You can't just show up at the home and go on a tour. Kind of something you learn when you show up.

Very beautiful Park. Amazing views of the river as you hike along the old railroad bed. The new railroad is just below and can cause you some noise occasionally, but that doesn't last very long. The trail is very well maintained and is loose gravel for most of the distance.

A really need Museum. Lots of living displays out here. An actual working farm, with lots of animals present. Associated smells are very real also! Very interesting displays around including Old Edison victrolas and old radios.
I really need Park. Very well maintained has bathrooms, a playground for children, soccer fields, softball fields, and lots of parking.
A very large open space, but right in the middle of everything! Really pretty place to just go wind down and enjoy the breeze.
I agree with the other reviewers, not much here. A great place for a picnic or die just hang out for an afternoon.

Well run and laid out the display's are all first rate the painting's and stories with them about pilots from North Dakota was a bonus.If you like history and war planes this is a must visit great place to bring the family.

If you want to learn the real history of the under ground railroad this is a must visit,tour guide was very knowledgeable about the history of the house and the under ground railroad best tour we have had in a long time.

The staff that run the mill are first rate they really know the history and how to operate the mill.the products they make there are some of the best l have ever bought from a working mill great place to bring the family

The guides were very knowledgeable about the old jail and the history of the area.my wife and I go to lots of country museums and this one is best we have see in a long time.Great place to take the family.

If you are in the area this center is a must visit it has display's for everyone taste. The building and grounds are beautiful with a friendly staff, I would rate this center not a five but a big ten!
What a great tour guide we had, Ashleigh was great she really knows the history of the entire area.entire staff was friendly and helpful great place to bring the family.
Very nice full of information about him and the movies he made, if you are in the area this is a good place to visit. Friendly staff and the museum was very clean
The tour guides at both houses were knowledgeable and the houses we interesting to visit to see how well houses were made years ago.Well worth the visit.
Good place to bring kids Mary Todd Lincoln house is the first house saved that a first lady lived in.lots of history of her family and early life.
we covered the entire bourbon trail and the people here were great our tour guide Adam was better than all the rest.this tour is a must visit.
Our guide was knowable about a mine operation was easy to understand and took his time explaining the working great place to bring the family
Our tour guide was very knowledgeable about the life and work of TC Steele she was great and the grounds are beautiful well worth the visit.
Very nice staff was helpful and friendly the museum has great displays easy to follow the self guided tour great place to bring the family
Great place to bring the family to show the young ones what was like trying to get a letter back then. Staff is was helpful and friendly.
We were given a great tour if you are in the area this is a must visit,tour guide really knows the history of the owners of the home
Great place to bring the family if you like to laugh this is must visit. Mr.Skelton did a lot more than just entertain people.
Great place to bring the family all of the displays are well done you will learn not just about the area but the hole country
Very clean with a friendly staff all of the displays are well done with lots of information great place to bring the family.
If you want to learn about windmills this is a must visit.very friendly staff who really knows the history of windmills
Staff was very helpful lots of railroad memorabilia.All the displays are well done and easy to see and read about.
Very good place to bring the family all of the displays are well done with lots of information and friendly staff
We saw bears, turkey and the beautiful landscape plus the bighorn river what a great place to bring the family
If you are interested in the civil war you should visit this battle ground park very clean with great trails
If you want to learn the history of the area you should visit the center,all the displays are very well done
What a great place to bring the kids the park has a lake to swim in and trails to walk

Lovely area to explore but not all of the buildings are open for viewing. Not sure when, if at all, the farmyard is open to the public. Really enjoyed the primitive living  education aspect. Thestivals there are small and not really worth the extra cost. Was sad to hear they no longer do reinactments.

We went here for the Poe Experience but instructions were unclear and we missed part of the skits because of it. Although the actors were decent the writing could have used some work and the ad-lib didn't live up to expectations. It is fun for the atmosphere but the cost was too much for what we got.

The beauty of these resting places never fails to touch me. Dead but never forgotten! Every time I visit here I learn something new and am so glad this cemetery is still open to the public at no charge, unlike St. Louis cemetery no. 1 where you have to pay a tour guide just to go inside :(

A wonderful place to visit. The wonderful and inexpensive boat ride shows you all the diversy ecology here. You see birds, alligators and even manatee. Be sure to visit the spring observation tower, too. All staff are nice and the Lodge restaurant was a pleasure to dine in.

We visited the Square for Chalktoberfest and the quality of the chalk art was just stellar! Be sure to take photos because the visuals really come to life on film! Great little shops here, too. Parking was easy to find, as well.

An excellent place to snorkel and swim but be careful of the rocks. The reef is very close and the waves can really bash you if you aren't careful. Strong swimmers can make their way around the points for better views.

Of all the National parks I have visited, I think this is my favorite. The scenery is unmatchable. Hikers check out the Pipiwah trail, sacred pools and the volcano, too! Loved the waterfalls and bamboo forest, too.

Sadly, these tide pools aren't really accessible. We drove dangerous roads to make it here only to find that we couldn't actually get down to the ocean safely. Still, it was nice to see the views on the way.

This is a nice little beach with a very busy pier and boardwalk area. Be aware, it does cost money to go out onto the pier. Fishing costs more. For a less busy area head West toward Daniel's seashells.
A great place to view sea turtles basking and monk seals. Clean restrooms and usually a lifeguard on duty. There can be strong currents here so beware. Parking can be difficult as it is a busy beach!
Small park with very nice staff. We took the pontoon over from the opposite bank of the river and although  me didn't have long to explore we felt very welcome. Camp sites and cabins available.
This wonderful, little active flow cavern is a sight to see and the cost for admission is affordable. Out guide, Jesse, was excellent and knowledgeable. A must see when visiting Linville!
Nice little trail that now connects to the larger trails in the area. Be sure to check out the box turtle enclosure near the school.  Very nice volunteers,  too
I remember when this was all hidden under kudzu. Roswell did a fantastic job of making it into a beautiful, educational and accessable park. A must see!!
Picnic area was clean and we felt safe. Went to see movies in the park but did not see any clear signs as to where they were or if they were canceled.
I am in love with most of these Natl parks around the Chattahoochee. They are kept clean and in good repair,  for the most part. Never a bad time!
This is a great park for both adults and children. There is a renovation project going on, too. Nice to see the creek is being taken care of.
A very informative little museum about forestry in Georgia. Dont miss the mummified dog! It takes about an hour to fully explore this place.
Went here for a grilling picnic. Nice shady spots and a beautiful  view of the lake. Our only complaint  is that the trash was overflowing.
A lovely little park with a pleasant dam but it seems like they are doing construction so I wasn't sure where I could and could not go.
Like all museums there is something to educate you. Gifts and soueviners are expensive though. Plus one for good air conditioning :)
Lovely place with nice staff. Easy trails and lots of animals and plants to see. Be sure to visit Pebbles, the resident tortoise!
Nice place with a large, busy fishing area and informative war memorial. This is a great place for walking or running in trails
Lovely place for a walk. Usually quiet and serene, too. There are plenty of hills, too, if you want a harder workout.
I love this park and staff were very pleasant when I called to report an injured duck on the property.

Fort Island beach is a small little diamond in an otherwise marsh and island filled coast line. A well kept sandy beach literally at the end of the road. Nice beach, good swimming and great views, nice place to relax and play. Adjact are a large boat ramp and a fishing pier. An outdoor person's dteam. Lots of parking, but on nice summer days there could be more and it would be used. Lots of wildlife as well. I'll go back when i am in that corner of the state.

Florida has one great state park after another. This one is based on a series of lagoons and estuaries with a very large walkway/tramway over the top. The views and clear water make walking the long wooden bridge an adventure. The walkway ends at s protected beach, one of the few in this ares according to the literature. Very nice for sunning, collecting shells and swimming. Snorkeling is a highlight but you must rent a divers flag to do so.  Great Place

This is a recovery center for injured and sick sea turtles from across  southern Florida. Emphasis in the center is put on education and of course viewing the sea turtles as they recover with the goal of release back to the oceans. The center is wonderful, the staff very friendly and willing to answer sny question. Nature trials are available as is plenty of parking. This is a must consider for any nature lover.

Great, huge, natural beach on A1A north of Jacksonville. Easy to find, I have seen the parking lots full during summer peak times, especially holidays. Lots and lots of room for stunning, exploring, surfing, fishing etc. $5 per normal car. I really enjoy just walking the seemingly endless beach, shelling and watching the waves. Open year round. No life guards any time of year. Currents can affect swimming.

Great state park with beach, river, hiking, biking, picnicking, camping, and of course the fort itself. Love the place for the diversity. If you are very lucky you might see a submarine in the river. Too much to do to talk about. Great place. Easy to find, lots of parking, facilities available. Fort staff is very educational. The pier was badly damaged by hurricanes. Great place i go every year.

Great place even though we were there out of season to see Manatee. Saw barracuda and several other types of fish. Big hats off the FPL for building and supporting such a facility.  Pleanty of observation areas. Very excellent educational building. Plenty of parking. Not far from the beach so it not an imposition to visit. Thanks again FPL!!

Very nice, well maintained, feels relatively new pier. Obviously lots of fishermen but lots of gawkers and tourists as well. Easy to find once your in Vilano Beach. We parked on the street. Shops, food, etc nearby. Beach across town, still not very far away. Nice place, relaxing, feels out of the way, not crazy like nearby st. Augustine.

Wide Sandy road walk, maybe a quarter mile to the house. You can walk the grounds and surrounding trails on your own. The house itself is only open when a ranger is available. It is kind of special to sit on the back porch in a rocking chair and watch the intercoastal waters. Very scenic. Very relaxing. Parking area easy to find.

Great place to learn about the port Canaveral area as well as experience great views from the different levels of the tower. Well laid out, very informative, yours available. Plenty of parking. Easy walk over to the port area, shops and restaurants. Very easy to see from almost anywhere in the area. Convenient hours.

Beach with lots of drift wood and fallen trees. Embankment to get to the water. Nice wide dirt trail. Beach is not directly on the ocran, kind of on the corner of a river, bay and ocran. Amelia island visable across the way. Fishing bridge just up the road. Easy to find off a1a. Parking available. Bring bug spray.

Huge city park featuring baseball/softball fields, skate board park, 18 hole disk golf course, lots of walking, running paths and tons of places to relax, picnic or just hang out. Well kept clean park, safe as police frequently pass through. Also a dog park on the north side of the facility. Very nice place!

A fun zoo with many many many cool animals usually displayed well. Big wide open paths really help on busy days. I have never taken the train. The giraffe feeding blind is great fun for all ages. My only warning is this place can get kind of sniffling in the summer months. But is great fun.

Very popular oceanside/beach park. Lifeguards on the beach. Lots of parking, has an inland lake, great for picnics, family gathering, walking, biking, surfing, swimming, shell collecting, children's area with swings etc. Only negative is it can be extremely busy on summer weekends.
likes: Family-friendly facilities (picnic area, children's area with swings)

reviews_attraction.text: Very nice outdoor venue. Great place to view a concert or other shows. Reminds me of a mini SPAC, Sandstone or Red rocks. Has great potential with hill side seating and good stage. I think with the building of Daily's  at the stadium my guess is this place will be forgotten.

I have only been there once since the hurricane, but i really like being able to walk down the river, drive on the beach, see the commercial ships, see the navy ships right across the river, play in the waves, look for shells snd just hang out all in one spot ... Awesome!!

Area park with tennis courts, playground, community building and rest rooms. Very nicely kept. Just a few blocks from the beach. Limited parking but seems ample for the park, some of the parking is taken up by beach goers. Scenic,  quiet, family friendly, community park.

Just beautiful, nice museam, well kept grounds, very scenic adjacent walking trail and beach. Life guards on duty. Harbour with your and fishing boats, sail boats. Lots of bird and wyld life. Outstanding veiws from stop lighthouse. Food, restaurants near by. Great place.

Park in northwest Arlington with river views, hiking, picnics, fishing and boating in mind. Quite scenic, usually fairly quiet, fishing does kind of dominate the pier. Free, ample parking, off the beaten path but not hard to find. Nice place!

The MOSH is an excellent science and history museum located in downtown Jacksonville.  Displays are well planned and keep your attention.  A portion of the displays rotate so that you can go over and over. Well worth it for all ages.

Great place and staff for additional information about the park and surrounding area. Not real hard to find. Several nice attractions near by including hiking, nature observation, lookout area, exploration, etc. Plenty of parking.

Ok museum, good hiking from easy to a few small hills, watch the tree roots. Ribault monument has excellent views of the St. Johns river, boats and ships, and surrounding area looking mainly north and north east.

Fantastic, fun, great, super place to see, learn about, even swim with dolphins. Increasing number of other sea wild life species exhibits. Interesting that even the wild dolphins hang out in the adjacent ocean.
Well kept, well developed park centered around a small lake and numerous hiling trails. Many signs along the trails pointing out and describing points of interest. Restrooms available.
Great place to see manatee.  Swim, snorkel or scuba in the summer. Very busy during the summer. Services are sufficient. Lots of parking.
Nice city downtown park. Has events throughout the year. Street parking. Nice place to chill out when in the city.

I gave this place five stars for a number of reasons. First, it is 100% free. All they ask is a donation. Second, the doll part of the museum, which is one 10x10 or so room, has one heck of a donated doll collection. For anyone interested in the subject matter, I am sure they will enjoy. Third, the train layouts. Two separate and fairly elaborate spreads in the HO gauge depict a realistic scene from days gone by as well as a made up town with little gems such as an alien ship and what I think was either a brothel or an adult movie theatre. My kids spent two hours running up and down following the trains back and forth (as they were the only ones there on a Sunday). If you are in the area, I highly recommend visiting. You can't beat the quality or the price.

Great museum if you have 2-3 hours to kill. Situated in a number of barns and other buildings, the museum offers a glimpse into the world of Appalachia mostly over the past 125 years of so. The owner has an impressive collection and offers great detail into each piece concerning where it came from and what the story is behind it. There are some large collections of specific items which may be of interest to a niche group of people. Make sure to pet one of the friendly kitties on your way out of the gift shop. Also, moderately stroller friendly. Some of the farther out buildings only have stairs for access.

Ok, the tram ride itself is really cool. I could have done without the lame jokes, but our host was certainly working hard at it and I respect his efforts. The informative parts of the tram tour were amazing. To think it was all dug out by people, and it does go on and on. Would have liked to have been there for the Christmas lights. Some of my group also participated in the obstacle course which was well liked. You can also do dirt bike riding and intense zip lining if you so choose. Good restrooms and snack bar available.Fun way to spend an afternoon.

Awesome place to take the kids for the day. We spent half what we spent at Sesame Place and had 10x the fun. Lots of shade and pay as you go rides. Skee ball bingo is the bomb! Perhaps the best thing is to take the train ride (train by the front of the park) at night. The lights from the train dancing on the tree limbs as it goes through the forest is magical. The carousel horse museum is informative and worth taking a look at. Log flume ride, two thumbs up (and you hardly get wet). This place is in the middle of nowhere but well worth the drive.

A wonderful tourist trap worth visiting. Take an elevator down into a cave. Watch out if you are over 5'8, cause you might bump your head. Not too cold. Everyone in my group was wearing shorts. The falls are something else. You could sit there and stare at it all day long. Getting the right tour guide always helps, as some are more entertaining than others. Try to go at the very end of the day or early on a weekday when there will be few people in your group. More one on one interaction with the tour guide is definitely worth it.

Yeah, look, this is the cave of all caves. If you want sheer size and volume, go no further. You won't see fancy cave formations, but you will see rooms big enough to play a football game in. The history is worth listening too as well. The museum part of the trip is informative but not particularly exciting. Something to do while you are waiting for your cave tour. It's cold in the cave, but with all the moving around, most people seemed to be fine in shorts.

Loved it! We were the only people there, because they had just started a new schedule and no one knew. Some of the stuff didn't work too well (bubble juice was a little weak), but most everything was a delight. I enjoyed watching the scarfs get pushed through the tubes. Most importantly, the kids really liked it and spent many hours here. Parking in nearby parking lot was not too difficult.

Lots of fun stuff for kids to play with here. They really like the water exhibit where you can make it rain and float boats around. There's a fun climbing apparatus and a little kid's grocery store where they can check out groceries  (and the staff hopes the kids then restock the shelves to help them out). Lots of other things to keep your kids busy for a good 2-3 hours. Clean restrooms!

Great place to watch the bats wake up from their daily slumber. Parking is available for a reasonable fee. I recommend downloading the app to pay as opposed to waiting in line at the one automated ticket device. Bring a blanket or something to sit on. Would have been better if someone dressed like old-school Batman was walking around telling us about his family under the bridge.

If you like horses and horse racing and such, this is a nice place to visit. It is actually a wonderful museum for the subject matter. There are a number of interactive activities for the kids including a virtual betting booth to help get them hooked young. All they need are some candy cigars to go with it. The 360 film they show is worth watching. Restrooms are top notch.

Great place to visit if you love horses. The tour is informative. I was kind of surprised that the general seating was not fancier. I forget that they run regular races there all year long and the KD is just a once a year event.So on the tour you get to meet a couple horses and ask all your questions. Definitely worth it. Make sure to visit the museum next door.

Came for the Lego exhibit which was nice. There is lots of Florida/Tampa history here to check out. It's a comfortable museum, temperature controlled and easy to get around. There are some fun things for kids to do, but there is lots of reading that is probably more for adults. The pirate section was fun.

Neat circus-themed park. Lots for kids to do. I liked that there was a little misting cool zone for the kids. Wish there was more shaded seating for the adults. For the older crowd, there is a half-mile track that goes around the park and a small lake where one can admire the local wildlife.

$5 for parking gets you into a nice beach area that, on a February Thursday morning was almost void of human traffic. Nice sand beaches and facilities. Would highly recommend for someone more interested in a quiet beach than the people watching at Clearwater.

Great place for kids to run and play. Playground, slides, lots of open space, fruit trees, water fountains, public restrooms, benches. Everything you need. My son and I kicked a ball around in the field for about an hour. He had a great time.
