I thought this was going to be a memorial to the Dennis Quaid movie or something, but it was still a nice cave. Lots of cool formations to check out. Not a cold cave by any means, so no jackets (in the Summer at least) required.

Nice open park. Windy evenings make this a good place to relax with the kids as the sun is setting. They have two jungle gyms to choose from and lots of running room. Watch out for the occasional dog poop on the playground.

Great views. Fun elevator ride to the top. They are doing construction, so there is a lot of roundabout walking to get to the attraction. Really fun to step out on the glass and look more than 100 stories directly below.

Nice playground for the kids (one for bigger and one for smaller kids). Swings and picnic benches were also available. Lots of grass to walk on, and there was a nice little bridge the kids had fun running up and down on.

The little kids love this place! What can I say, if you have some time to kill in and around Naples, check it out. We didn't even get to see everything there because my kid wanted to run the grocery store the whole time.
If this is your kind of thing, I totally get it and would recommend it. The staff is quite friendly. Not entirely sure it is worth the price of admission, but like I said, the staff is wonderful.
We accidentally showed up while Thomas was here, so everything was moved around. Nobodies fault really. Would definitely come back when it is nice and quiet and we can actually tour the museum.
Nice place to play some quick miniature golf. Prices are reasonable, and I have never seen a huge crowd. They have games and go-karts, but I have not partaken in any of those.
Last time I was here, the rifle on the far-left offered unlimited shooting. I was going off on the targets like I had a machine gun.
Ha ha, Little Mermaid gets a huge indoor adventure while Aladdin gets a remake of an old county fair ride.

Free beautiful display display in the main greenhouse during Christmas time of poinsettias and other various plants. The grounds are beautiful all year round. I went when it was snowing, it was like a winter wonderland.
Bathrooms are outside, if you're **handicap** make note that there is a semitall threshold to get to the bathroom building as well as a rocky terrain. However it is manageable to get through with assistance if you're in a wheelchair, and definitely manageable independently if using a walker or cane.

It was nice. But for the price and size I wouldn't go more than once or buy an annual pass. We had a Florida resident discount. If you're not from Florida, majority of the tourist maps and magazines you can get for free at any tourist center and hotels brochure counters will have coupons for this place. The worker Christian was amazing at his job, he was very lively and fascinating. He was our favorite part of the day. He was really into his shows.

Great place to go for a run or stroll. Parking is usually easy after the summer season. During the summer it is difficult to find parking. But the views are beautiful.
Handicap accessibility is good. Easy on ramp and easy surface. There's usually two or three spots of handicap parking near each parking entrances to the boardwalk and around 4 along the main street all along each section of parking.

During the summer they host movies on the great lawn. During halloween they host rise of the jack o' lanterns. During the winter they have a wonderful Christmas experience, where each room is decorated beautifully in period time christmas decor and in the sun room they provide free cookies and hot apple cider, and upstairs pictures with Santa.

My favorite zoo! On Wednesday it is pay what you wish donation, so you only have to pay for parking. Get ready to walk alot, since the ground is not a flat surface, it is alot of walking up and down hills. From those handicap, use a scooter or wheelchair, they are limited with rentals, so do your best to bring your own.

The best ice cream comes from a small little shop in the back of this pavilion. Fresh made and so flavorful. My favorite is the chocolate candied peanut butter fudge ice cream. On a cone, as a scoop, or freshly pressed into a small brioche bun it is all so good! And definitely a nice break from the heat of Florida.

I usually go here during the spring and summer months to go to smorgasburg. Tons of delicious eats during that time. The view is beautiful, however there are not alot of places to sit and enjoy. The parking around the area is not that bad if you're street parking a block away.

One of my favorite museums in Manhattan. It's interactive which is perfect for kids. They have a room with the history of pixar art.
Plus the garden is beautiful and for those gossip girl fans...yes that's where Lilly got married to become Mrs.Bass *fan girl*

Safe fun place to go. It's a really controlled environment. You have to go through metal detectors and bags are put through a scanner before entering, so there's a peace of mind with that. It is a party zone for adults, yet playful for young ones too.

It's a great place for all ages. There's plenty to see and do. It's a really interactive museum. I loved the slot car racing and the dinosaur room where you can uncover "fossils". Possibly one of the best museums I've ever been to

Best time to go is before the summer really starts. I had season tickets here. Best thing is to pay regular admission then apply it for a season ticket, the one that includes parking is best because parking went up.

Definitely buy the combo attraction ticket. This is a cool little aquarium. It's a quick walk thru but it is beautiful. The kids will like it. They have a large area for petting starfish near the end of the walk.

Very nice music. I had a student id so it was only $5. But the regular admission price is not that expensive either. My favorite exhibit was the one where you get to sit in water tubes, it was super unique.
Great discount for students. One of my favorite spots that I visited while in town. If you're looking for the rocky statue it's down the main steps on your left if you're walking from the museum down
Small but really nice. Spring for the boat tour it was my favorite part. They made this place so beautiful. And it's convenient that they have a catering hall/hotel attached onto the property
Good price. I got chills when walking thru here. For all the tall people, watch your head getting in and out of the cells, my boyfriend smacked his head pretty good getting out of one haha.
Nice variety for the kids. Perfect local place to bring them when they're off from school. Right around the corner they have the carousel for $2 a ride. Bring snacks/packed lunch though!
The hours are very limited. But the place is beautiful. The staff there is very knowledgeable about the place and can give you great information with whatever questions you have about it
It was nice. But in comparison to all the other parks in orlando it's subpar. Perfect place to bring the kids, if you don't like the overwhelming crowds in other major parks
They have a student discount like most museums in ny, which is great. There's never a slow day, so you're fighting thru the crowds. But it's a beautiful modern museum.
Beautiful place to explore. The views are breath-taking. The building is truly a work of art in itself. When I went I had done the pay-what-you-wish donation.
At the moment it's free, they have tons of war memorabilia and great explanations of the items they have. It's one room, but worth it to go.
Suggested donation of $5. The art is fantastic! Very talented artist and great thing about it, is that you can purchase anything there!
Great event venue. But it gets crowded and busy, so keep valuables close so you don't lose it from squeezing thru the massive crowds
Always a fun activity especially after a long day at the beach. Do the scavenger hunt, it's a fun plus!

The park is beautiful and has great facilities and trails, but you really have to be careful where you go in the park.  We stopped to take a trail and noticed a lot of window glass in the parking area.  As we were getting ready to take the trail we saw another car in another parking area a little bit up the road.  The people in it seemed to be watching us.  We went ahead and started the trail, but I just had a bad feeling.  After going a few hundred yards I decided to go back to the car.  As we came out of the woods the car we had seen up the road was pulled up behind ours.  One of the people ( a woman) was walking around our car looking in the windows.  When she saw us she dropped a rock she had in her hand, jumped in the car and the driver sped away.  So stay near your car or park some place with a lot of people around, or risk being broken in to.

We stopped in the park to get dinner at the lodge and really enjoyed it.  The lodge had live music and a buffet.  The food was home cooked with all of the favorites that you might have at a family reunion or a great summer get together.  I must say I ate too much but couldn't resist one more piece of fried chicken and another piece of home made desert.

Afterwards we listened to the music and explored the cave.  The lodge is in a perfect location overlooking the river.  We might try staying here the next time we are near.

This is a nice clean park with paved trails for walkers and forest trails for horses.  There isn't a lot of parking and sometimes the lot is full.  There are a lot of dog walkers and many don't use leashes.  The dogs seemed nice, but our dog and us have been attacked by unleashed dogs at other parks so it always makes us nervous when dogs come charging up to us.  Overall a nice small park.

This is a beautiful park with great views of the Lake Superior shore line.   In the morning we walked the breakwater to the lighthouse which ended up being much more challenging than we expected,  but was worth it.  In the evening we watched the sun set from the North end of the park.  Which was a great way to end the day.

Peaceful Acres is a small lavender farm.  There is a small shop that sells oils and everything lavender. The festival that they have each year is fun with about a dozen vendors.  Most are artists of some sort, but there is also food, honey, and some live music.  We enjoy it each year and look forward to seeing what is new.

This is a beautiful old home.  We stopped to walk the trail which was quite challenging.  There are some enormous old trees along the path.  The trail needs some trimming back but was easy to follow.  We also enjoyed seeing some rare running buffalo clover by the old family cemetery and trail head.

Au Sable Light Station is a peaceful, secluded destination.  The trail to it is paved with gravel and an easy walk.  There are also several places where you can walk down to the beach along the way.  The station was open while we were there, but it was fun to walk out to and see.

The museum has been beautifully restored and is one of Cincinnati's treasures.  Recently we saw the holocaust exhibit which was very well done.  It is something that everyone should see so that we don't forget history an allow something like this to ever happen again.

We enjoyed the Mounds trail on a beautiful fall day.  We started at the causeway parking area and went from there to the longer Mounds trail, about 8 to 9 miles. Most of the trails were well maintained except for the longer Mounds trail.  Overall it was a great hike.

I visited with a large group of art teachers from Indiana and Illinois and they thought the museum had a fantastic collection.  We also took a tour and our guide Nina was alot of fun.  We ate at the café for lunch and the food was great.  We had a perfect time.

This park is a hidden gem.  We stopped by to walk the trails and do some teaching.  The trails are well maintained and the hike back out is a good workout.  The picnic area, parking, playground, and shelter make it a nice little community park.

This is a beautiful museum.  There are large open galleries and exhibits and even a little cafe if you need a snack.  They have a very nice collection of western art as well as a large variety of native American art displayed by regions.

Great park with lots of things to do.  We really had fun at the dog beach, I've never heard of a dog beach before, but it seems to be a big hit.  The human beach seemed a little run down, but everything else seemed nice.

This is a beautifully maintained park with outstanding gardens.  There were several groups having professional pictures taken when we arrived in the garden settings.  There is also a children's area and a wooded trail.
Beautiful trails.  We wished we had more time to explore them all.  Unfortunately some of the best trails you can't take your dog on so it's best to leave them at home if you want to see everything.
This is a nice secluded park with some very scenic trails. It was a little hard to find but worth the effort. The terrain is a little rugged in places but is something most families can handle.
The Krohn Conservatory is a Cincinnati treasure and one of the places I always take guests that stop in from out of town.  The seasonal displays are beautiful and shouldn't be missed.
Lot's of great beaches.  Even though it was a busy 4th if July weekend we found free parking and quite beaches in a several locations where we could walk, wade, and enjoy the views.
This is one of our favorite beaches to collect shells, sharks teeth, and fossils.  The area has seen some damage from storms but is still a nice place to go to avoid the crowds.
Music hall has been beautifully restored.  We attended the Nutcracker again this year and it was great to be back in Music Hall, it is definitely a Cincinnati treasure.
This is a nice park with beautiful gardens and amazing views.  The trails were clear and easy to follow.  We hope to come back and explore a few more of the trails.
This is one of the most beautiful Hamilton county parks.  Every season the gardens are beautiful to see.  They also have nice trails and nature center.
We stopped to see if we could get some pictures along the frozen creek.  Stop by and see some of the beauty of the Hamilton county park distrct.
We walked all the trails and had a great time.  Parking can be a little hard to find on the weekend, but the trails and views are great.
This is a nice quiet park and we had a great time walking the trails.  There is a lot to see and do, so it is well worth the visit.

Lakemont Park in 2018 has a lot less rides than it used to, and a lot less than DelGrossos. But the Skyliner is still Central PA's only real roller coaster, and it's a good ride. The Leap the Dips is the world's oldest roller coaster and a national treasure. The new Lakemont is much prettier, and instead of carnival rides, it offers more active recreation (batting cages, 2 miniature golf courses, basketball courts, sand volleyball, etc.). And general admission is now free, you only pay for rides and food. So in ways, it's moving towards becoming more of a community park and gathering place. It's a bold move, and I can see it working. But as of the date of this writing (May 26, 2019), most of the improvements are still under construction. So it's too early to pass judgement yet. But for the price, it's still a nice place to spend an evening.

A good museum that was worth the money, even if, like me, you're not a big fan of Andy Warhol or modern pop art. If you don't know that much about modern pop art, it can still be a fun time even for kids. My 10 and 12 year olds really enjoyed it. But it really helps to read the explanatory material on the walls before entering each room and seeing the film on the first floor if you don't know Warhol. They kind of explain the philosophy and promotion of Warhol, which were more interesting to me than his art. The gift shop is great and surprisingly funny. It is very unique. But it is a little r rated.

This is a very important historical site in world history given that it began the seven years war. That the fort itself is so little to see is interesting in and of itself. But the museum does a great job of explaining the importance of fort necessity to the seven years war. The museum is very nice, has plenty of parking, and it's worth the drive even though it is somewhat isolated. Don't forget to see Braddock's grave and jumonville Glen while you are there, but the latter is only open in the summer.

Great museum. One of the most underrated in Pennsylvania. The Brig Niagara is fascinating when it is in port (call & check before going), but the museum tells even more interesting stories of the Battle of Lake Erie & the USS Wolverine. While in the bayfront, I recommend driving around to check out the lake freighters close up, as well as the bicentennial tower.

A great collection of engines in a nice, clean, warm viewing area with plenty of explanatory materials. Very interesting and entertaining if you are into trains. Most, although not all, of the displays are accessible. Plenty of parking. I only wish that it was in a more historically important railroad location, like Altoona, where many of the engines were made.

This had a lot of different activities for the kids to do, and they had a blast. It was crowded, though. My only warning would be to dress light if you are not going into the water. The facility is very, very warm. I was sweating a lot in a simple sweatshirt. It is worth the drive to Erie, especially in the winter. In the summer, I'd rather be at presque isle.

This is a nice State Park with a small damned in lake, some unique plant species, and some hisorical relics. It is clean enough and offers plenty of services at a reasonable price. However, it is not nearly as unique or spectacular as some of the best state parks, like Presque Isle, Pymatuning, or even Black Moshannon.

A specular natural setting along the shores of Lake Apopka with great educational sign boards about the unique species that can be easily observed there. They also.cover the history of Lake Apopka, it's environmental degradation, and it's inspiring comeback. The garden spot of Winter Garden.

Get there before 3:30 pm. The boat tours fill up early. We could not get in a boat tour, so we just left without paying. I really can't honestly rate anything else, since we didn't go in. Just make sure you get there early enough to get on a boat.

One of the coolest buildings in Pennsylvania. Gorgeous to look at. But make sure to save a few hours to hit the nationality classrooms on the first three floors. They're definitely worth a stop when you are in Pittsburgh.

A must-see when you're in downtown Philadelphia. It helps to have a tour guide, and they are sometimes available. But this site has enough history to put it right behind the Pennsylvania state house in terms of must see.

Surprisingly decent museum. It really puts being an American and Philadelphia's history in perspective. Worth the cost. It often has deals with the other attractions on Independence Mall, so make sure to ask.

It is an interesting and educational site, but it is at it's best during special events like Rev War Days in July when there are plenty of reenactors/living historians around. Don't miss the nature trails.
One of the most iconic collegiate settings in America. Very few other universities have a central green this large or impressive. It is definitely worth a stop in your tour of Columbus. Go Bucks!
One of the five best scenic overlooks of Pittsburgh, and the best of Oakland. Getting there is tricky, the Google maps does a good job of guiding. Picnic tables are nearby as is a playground.
Kind of an all-in-one facility with skating rink, bowling alley, library, playground, outdoor pool, and community fairgrounds all included. Good for kids, year round. Something for everyone.
Very unique, huge rock formation that you can visit for free. Really seeing it will require some hiking. Good shoes or boots wouldn't be a bad idea, and accessibility ain't here.
One of America's finest and most beautiful parks with beautiful views of Oakland and downtown in the distance. All kinds of facilities + the Phipps Conservatory. Worth a drive.
One of the greatest natural history museums in the United States, and a solid art museum thrown in for the same price. Definitely Pittsburgh's biggest museum.
One of of America's most unique and photographed urban parks. Reasonably priced parking is relatively close by, especially on the weekends.
Beautiful sight and an impressive damn. Worth the drive. The path down to the viewing area is gravel though it may be hard for wheelchair.
This is an older park with some really nice picnic shelters. The grounds could be rough for someone in a wheelchair.  Decent playground.
Great history retold masterfully. A great real life story presented very well. Make sure to see the downtown museum as well.
A beautiful location, a neat historic site, and a cool place to watch trains. Worth the stop if you have time.
It's a nice park in pretty good condition. I was there at night for an event, however. So I couldn't see much.

23rd annual Green River Race, in the Green River GameLands in Saluda NC. "The Green River Game Lands is a beautiful, rugged, natural area of forests, rivers, gorges, and hillsides consisting of more than 10,000 acres along the Green River in Henderson and Polk counties. The area is owned by the state and managed for the primary purpose of wildlife conservation and management, which means that fishing, hunting, and trapping are allowed.

All the trails have a sense of the wild—although there are trailhead signs, the trails are not blazed. One of the best trails for dogs is the Pulliam Creek Trail, and one of the best times to hike is in spring, when it is not yet hot and the wildflowers are blooming in abundance."

Visit these wonderful state park on the first week of June right after the spider lilies bloom in full! I need to bring my kayak next time to cruise down the Catawba river, really easy and accesible trail. DescriptionLandsford Canal State Park is a South Carolina state park in Chester County, two miles from US 21. The 448-acre park contains the ruins of the Landsford Canal built using slave labor to bypass rapids on the Catawba River between 1820 and 1825. The coming of the railroad caused the canal to be abandoned. I need to come back to this park in the near future and look for the pair of bald eagles 🦅 that call these state park their home.

This 240 acre park is Greenville County Rec’s jewel in the foothills of the Blue Ridge Mountains. It was developed by the SC Commission of Forestry and the SC Department of Parks, Recreation, & Tourism in the 1940’s to promote tourism in the Upstate. The park was established for the African American community. Neighboring Paris Mountain State Park was built for the white community. In the 1960’s both parks integrated. In 1985 the State decided that other parks like Jones Gap within 30 miles of Pleasant Ridge were capturing most of the tourism traffic and offered Pleasant Ridge to Greenville County Rec.

I decided to visit this Hindu temple on December 29 of 2018 the last weekend of the year, I choose this place for the spiritual significance and beauty of the place where this temple was situated, I was the only not Hindu person in the temple, there was a big group of different Hindu families with their traditional dresses, everybody was really friendly and I check the Nandi, Hanuman and Ganga parks in the property, the beautiful shrine and statues combine with the gorgeous vistas and surround nature, I will comeback again great place to meditate.

Riverside park featuring remains of historic textile mill & post office, plus dog area & picnicking. The Pelham Mills Site, sometimes referred to as the Buena Vista Factory, Hutchings Factory, or the Lester Factory, is the site of the ruins of the Pelham Mills cotton factory near Greer, South Carolina on the shores of the Enoree River.Included on the property are stone and brick foundations, the bases of two steam smokestacks, brick pilings, and a mortared stone dam with six sluice gates across the Enoree River.

The original Tybrisa Pier & Pavilion stood for three-quarters of a century as a landmark on the South Atlantic Ocean. Built in 1891 by the Central of Georgia Railroad it became a well-known destination for day-trippers and seasonal visitors during a time when advertisements hailed Tybee as the Premier South Atlantic Resort. Its open dance floor amid a coastal setting made it a legendary stop on the Big Band tour and for five decades of entertainers.

Visitor center for the City of Charleston SC In a centric location, great place to park your car and be to walking distance of all the attractions near downtown area and king street, they have some great art display and history regarding the city of Charleston, there is also a scale map of the city of Charleston and surrounding areas, this is a must stop to find all the attraction info in the city.

My first hike in 2019 I choose this location and trail because of the landscape and geography of the trail and how is a trail inside the Appalachian trail. The city of Hot springs North Carolina tuck in on The Valley and cut by the French broad river. The city is really picturesque and you have the hot springs spa the reason the city got their name from.

Nine Times Preserve lies at the intersection of South Carolina’s Southern Blue Ridge Mountains and its piedmont region, where mountainous terrain begins to slope into gentler hills. Black bear, peregrine falcons and freshwater trout are just a few of the species you may find on this incredibly biologically significant property.

A hidden gem in South Carolina this whole Heritage preserve area have some amazing landscape in the middle of the state, the waterfall with the cave were one of the most interesting spots in the whole park, and the pools in the top of the rock with moss and vegetation make this place feel out of this world 🌎 🛰 👽 🏞

The best thing that happen during our honeymoon, the highlight to our west coast trip, after a disappointing morning in crater lake with all the smoke from the wildfires, we decided to leave the National park and head towards the Umpqua Forest to soak in the hot thermal water of this natural spring

Some great views from the top of The Valley with the outcrop of boulders and rocks, all mark with local graffiti art, unfortunately there is a lot of trash 🗑. I wish there was a clean up or that this place will get recognize as a preserve or park to get some help from the local authorities.

A beautiful state park in key biscayne Florida, located on a barrier island and on the premises of Bill Baggs Cape Florida state park the beach 🏖 near cape Florida is so refreshing and clear, you will notice a lot of wildlife in this area, specially raccoons 🦝

Historic cedar-and-cypress building offering a glimpse of school life in Spanish Colonial times. I have a great experience checking the oldest wooden school in the USA 🇺🇸 a rare glimpse of the life of people in the first day of this new nation.

Beautiful waterfall inside the toccoa falls college, is also an wedding venue there was a wedding actually about to be held, I wanted to choose this place for my own wedding but they don’t allow alcohol or pets and they strictly Christian.

This was an interesting hike to the summit of the wesser bald fire tower the incline trail is a little strenuous but you will be rewarded with a great view and we were alone for most of the time a great way to end my fiancée girlfriend.

Super cold 🥶 water 💦 but is such a worth place to go and relax on a hot summer day, the trail is not that hard and I love the fact that the blue ridge parkway have so much more to offer after jumping on this amazing water hole.

A great hike in the Pisgah National Forest, the start of the trail is on HWY 276 is a side road waterfall, there is a lil incline to the waterfall, but this place is gorgeous, I felt secluded, I went in the evening
Great hike to the top of Craggy pinnacle hike, great views and beautiful and rare plants and wild life, the weather was a lil treacherous with some clouds and some light raining.
My first time seen a sunset 🌅 on the west coast! The rock formations and the sky 🌌 with the moon and the stars ✨ made this a once in a lifetime experience.
Great green space to walk around and enjoy the farmers market and the Tennessee State capitol over the hill with a skyline of Nashville downtown.
An easy less than .5 mile hike to this 50ft waterfall that drops into a crystalline water pool! Perfect for the hot summer days.
Great hiking day near Caesars Head visitor center to a couple of unnamed waterfalls and cool boulder and cave formations q
Beautiful Preserve area for marine wildlife and migrating birds. With a picturesque light house at the end of the trail.
Wish I could have the opportunity to enter the home of Ernest Hemingway, a true American Legend and phenomenal writer

Beautiful home built in the 1920s designed to reflect the architecture and feel of a manor seen in Salisbury UK. The home is furnished worn some replicas and some authentic 16th century architecture and furnishings. Some of the paintings on the wall are quite gorgeous. Tours of the full house are only offered three times a day, but you can pay $8 to walk around the first floor only. I opted to self guided tour which ended up being very few rooms and the front garden.

Warning: tours start on the hour, and you cannot get in until ten minutes before! The museum is on the grounds of the Indiana state mental institution. This is the building where research and autopsies were actually done. Including a theater with original chairs than you can sit in. The tour was about an hour and the guide was very knowledgeable and took adequate time in each room. Very enjoyable. Real brains in jars!

The library was closed while we were there, but we did get to go though the museum and walk the grounds. All in all it was a very educational experience and the building is quite beautiful in and of itself. Harry Truman and his wife are buried in the center of the courtyard which was a little creepy, but I think that's a me thing. But it was cool to be able to "pay tribute" after walking through the museum.

Friendly museum staff, reasonable admittance price, and a lot of cool cars and memorabilia to check out. There were a number of cars and motorcycles from the movies which was really cool, including a car Dom crashes in the fast and furious movie. The museum is downsizing so a few of the items are for sale. There were a lot of mannequins which I found a bit disconcerting.

Museum admittance is free but they encourage a $3 donation. The exhibits included modern day religious art and paintings by Jim Cantrell. The Cantrell exhibit took up the majority of the museum and though interesting, was a bit repetitive. Would have liked to seen different artists. There is a small gift shop with a few hand made crafts and artwork.

Really awesome place to visit and look at vintage signs! The admittance fee isn’t very high and you get plenty of bang for your buck. With numerous signs to see and places to view, you can even walk through the workshop where they refab the signs. A gift shop includes reasonably priced souvenirs and a variety of books.

The museum features corvettes throughout the years, highlighted milestones in competitions and design history. The museum is also infamous for the sinkhole that swallowed 8 priceless cars. The cars are on still on display and there’s an interesting exhibit on the event and even a window into the hole itself.

Very interesting and interactive! The museum entrance fee was very reasonable ($10). The exhibits have thorough information and the psychology experiments are quite interesting to learn about. The museum offers numerous interactive mental or physical acuity tests. I definitely recommend a visit!

The tour was interesting to start, but as you go through you get the feeling you’re not seeing anything. You only get to see the outside of some studios but don’t go inside any. The security guard had a complex and was quite rude. Overall slightly unenjoyable and not worth the $15.

Very beautiful memorial, only $10 to go on a tour, missed out cause a storm was approaching but you can go to the top. The area surrounding was very beautiful both in design and the views. Some re-inactions we’re taking place with period dresses and musket firing, was cool to see.
likes: On-site Activities (view from top, period dresses, musket firing)

reviews_attraction.text: Absolutely awesome immersive ride! The concept is that you’re riding on the back of a banshee around pandora. The visuals are stunning with added 4D water sprays and smell. With fast pass there was virtually no wait, but midday the stand by wait times were quite long.

Amazing experience! So great to be in the town of Wakita where part of the iconic movie twister is filmed. The museum is small but contains many items from the movie and memorabilia. The museum owner is so nice and willing to share her first hand experience.

Nothing to complain about, the view of Kansas City is breathtaking, worth the walk up to the monument. You have to buy a ticket to get into the museums and tower, but I didn’t partake. Looked like the line go into the tower was a bit long.

Amazing museum dedicated to county music. Exhibits include instruments, archival music videos, costumes, and much more. The tour has a good flow and tells the history of county music up to the modern day. It was really quite enjoyable.

Beautiful building and history. The tour didn’t take very long but was very educational. Not only the state capitol of Tennessee but also the final resting place of the 11th president James K. Polk. Had a great visit!

Awesome place to visit! The tour guide was great, sharing the history of Waverly hills as well as some of her personal experiences with ghost encounters. The tour took the full two hours and was super fun at night.

Fun train museum near downtown Cheyenne. The train tracks behind the museum are still in use so you can see locomotives. The museum ticket was reasonably priced and the information and artifacts were interesting.

Certainly an interesting building, a full scale replica of the Parthenon just kind of in the middle of nowhere. I would recommend at least taking on the sight of it, not much else on the grounds, but a nice park.
The rio grande gorge bridge offers magnificent views of the river and the gorge. Plenty of room on the sidewalks to keep away from traffic. Also, an amazing smoothie bus hangs out on the south side.
Gorgeous mountain range! Beautiful trees and a long winding road through the mountains. Many side roads to go four wheeling or pull of to camp.
Kind of an expensive ticket for not much art to see. But I can see where it would be nice for local artists to get their artwork out there.
Went to the Christmas fantasy light show set up at the park and was pleasantly surprised. Price was reasonable for the quality of the show.
Had such a great time here! You can walk around at you leisure and even look at books in the library. The gift shop had a nice selection.
Quaint memorial to President Grant and the home he was born in, located in point pleasant. Historical plaques are very informative.
Beautiful lighthouse with a great history. The lighthouse observation deck also overs a great view of the town and river.

(Translated by Google) Upon the visit date (August 2019), neither the Byzantine Chapel nor the Chapel of Rothko could be visited. Then he loses a lot of interest.
In any case, as the entrance to the museum and parking are free, you can always get closer for a moment at any time.
Hour and a half is enough.
In short, acceptable, but not the 3 stars granted by the Michelin Guide.

(Original)
A la data de la visita (agost 2019) no es podia visitar ni la Capella Bizantina ni la Capella de Rothko. Aleshores perd bastant d'interès.
De tota manera, com l'entrada al museu i el pàrquing són gratuïts, sempre podeu apropar-vos una estona en qualsevol moment lliure que tingueu.
Amb hora i mitja n'hi ha prou.
En fi, acceptable, però no pas les 3 estrelles que li atorga la Guia Michelin.
dislikes: Lack of interest due to closures

reviews_attraction.text:
(Translated by Google) Place to visit if you are in Miami. No doubt. Take a tour and enjoy mangrove swamps (mangroves), boating snorkel, and a natural frontline environment.
The tour I've done (Eco Tour) has allowed you to visit a little everything throughout the day.
Other options are to visit sunken ships or the coral reef.
And much less people than the Everglades, even in August.

(Original)
Lloc a visitar si sou a Miami. Sense dubte. Feu un tour i podreu gaudir de manglars (mangroves), snorkel del bo, i un entorn natural de primera línia.
El tour que he fet (Eco Tour) ha permès de visitar una mica de tot durant tot el dia.
Altres opcions són visitar vaixells enfonsats o la barrera de corall.
I molta menys gent que als Everglades, inclús en agost.

(Translated by Google) Is it worth it. Caves very large, easy to visit.
The route called Discovery is better in terms of content, but it has too many people. 1.3 km of non-circular route. Spectacular!
The route called Hidden is shorter (500 m, two times -circular-), with stairs, but there are a lot less people, it's more rude.

(Original)
Val la pena. Coves molt grans, fàcils de visitar.
El recorregut anomenat Discovery és millor en quant a contingut, però té massa gent. Fa 1,3 km de recorregut no circular. Espectacular!
El recorregut anomenat Hidden és més curt (500 m, dos cops -circular-), amb escales, però hi va molta menys gent, és més agrest.

(Translated by Google) The best I can say is that it does not look like you're in Miami. It is a peninsula converted into State Park, with dunes and very little massive sandy beaches. How to pay $ 8 to access the Park, there are not many people, nothing to do with Miami Beach. There is a lighthouse and a small park, well preserved.

(Original)
El millor que puc dir és que no sembla que siguis a Miami. És una península convertida en Parc Estatal, amb unes platges de dunes i sorra blanca molt poc massificades. Com cal pagar 8 $ per accedir al Parc, no hi ha gaire gent, res a veure amb  Miami Beach. Hi ha un far i un petit parc, ben conservat.

(Translated by Google) An unknown curiosity Illot is 110 km from Cayo Hueso (Key West), with a fortress above, not too well preserved, but surprising.
Nice place to snorkel, especially following the wall surrounding the fortress. Beaches of white sand.

(Original)
Una curiositat desconeguda. Illot a 110 km de Cayo Hueso (Key West), amb una fortalesa a sobre, no massa ben conservada, però sorprenent.
Bon lloc per fer snorkel, sobre tot resseguint la muralla entorn la fortalesa. Platges de sorra blanca.

(Translated by Google) Best of Houston. Impressive tunnel system and also 10 km long walkways, to go through the city without sustaining the heat. Tickets from the main buildings.
They have restaurants, shops ...

(Original)
Del millor de Houston. Impressionant sistema de túnels i també de passarel·les, de 10 km de longitud, per recórrer la ciutat sense suportar la calor. Entrades des dels principals edificis.
Tenen restaurants, botigues...

(Translated by Google) Little known place, but interesting to visit. Good views over Tampa Bay. Beautiful walking tours. 15 minutes report (subtitles in Spanish) about the history of the explorer Hernando de Soto.

(Original)
Lloc poc conegut, però interessant de visitar. Bones vistes sobre la badia de Tampa. Recorreguts a peu macos. Reportatge de 15 minuts (subtítols en castellà) sobre la història de l'explorador Hernando de Soto.

(Translated by Google) Neuralgic Center of Harvard, and reference point for university life. Many shops, restaurants, bars ... Subway stop. Visit the university area (late Harvard), next to it. Is it worth it.

(Original)
Centre neuràlgic de Harvard, i lloc de referència de la vida universitària. Moltes botigues, restaurants, bars... Parada de metro. Visiteu la zona de la universitat (Harvard tard), al costat. Val la pena.

(Translated by Google) It's worth the trip to Saint Augustine just to see this citadel. Very large, very well preserved, very good views.
Has parking in front ($ 2.50 per hour). The entrance costs $ 15.

(Original)
Val la pena el viatge a Saint Augustine només per veure aquesta ciutadella. Molt gran, molt ben conservada, molt bones vistes.
Té pàrquing al davant (2,50 $ per hora). L'entrada costa 15 $.

(Translated by Google) Unexpectedly interesting It is not a zoo-style aquarium. It is a center for research and animal care.
You will see manatees, crocodiles, etc.
Price: $ 24

(Original)
Inesperadament interessant. No és un aquari estil zoo. És un centre de recerca i cures d'animals.
Hi veureu manatins, cocodrils, etc.
Preu: 24 $

(Translated by Google) Very interesting. It is a huge plantation, which reflects the life of the nineteenth century.
Very well taken care of. At 1 h from New Orleans, upstream.

(Original)
Molt interessant. És una plantació enorme, que reflecteix molt bé la vida del s.XIX.
Molt ben cuidada. A 1 h de Nova Orleans, riu amunt.

(Translated by Google) Very good service and everything very well organized. Good time control for breakfasts and lunches. Clean and straightened. Now, it has its price ...

(Original)
Molt bon servei i tot molt ben organitzat. Bon control del temps pels esmorzars i dinars. Net i endreçat. Ara bé, té el seu preu...

(Translated by Google) The current one is very small, but during 2020 they will open a huge one. Offers a boat for a freshwater pond (interesting).

(Original)
El d'ara és molt petit, però durant el 2020 obriran un d'enorme. Ofereix recorreguts un barca per un estany d'aigua dolça (interessant).

(Translated by Google) Interesting explanation of a lost people in History. Request the 30 minute video with French subtitles.

Interessant explicació d'un poble perdut en la Història. Demaneu el vídeo de 30 minuts amb subtítols en francès.

(Translated by Google) Well preserved, it is the home of an old politician and businessman. Visit: $ 4. Nothing special

(Original)
Ben conservada, és la casa d'un antic polític i empresari. Visita: 4 $. Res d'especial.

(Translated by Google) Nothing special, but nice to see. Interesting setting, on the edge of the Mississippi.

(Original)
Res d'especial, però bufó de veure. Entorn interessant, a la vora del Mississipí.

(Translated by Google) 55-meter high lighthouse, with great views. It goes up on foot. Price: $ 12.50.

(Original)
Far de 55 m d'alçada, amb molt bones vistes. S'hi puja a peu. Preu: 12,50 $.

(Translated by Google) I do not find interest There are some more interesting ones in Houston.

(Original)
No li trobo interès. N'hi ha de més interessants a Houston.

Només té el valor històric. Artísticament té poc interès.

Maco per fer-hi un passeig, per exemple tornant del castell.

Res d'especial. Si et va de pas, doncs hi fas un voltet...

Curiós. Pareu-hi al davant post fer una foto. Res més.

(Translated by Google) It's worth a 15 minute drive. Very well taken care of.

(Original)
Val la pena fer-hi un volt de 15 minuts. Molt ben cuidat.

(Translated by Google) Not bad. But it's nothing really impressive.

(Original)
No està malament. Però no és res de realment impressionant.

(Translated by Google) Well taken care of Wide On the banks of the river.

(Original)
Ben cuidat. Ample. A la vora del riu.

First, the lady at the front desk should have stayed home. What a terrible reception and attitude. How about a nice greeting and a smile. If you don't want to be there, call in sick or get another job. Everybody in our party felt the same way. Secondly, 20 bucks for an adult to enter is ridiculously high. They don't offer veteran discounts and they don't offer senior discounts. Very sad. I am sure both Edison and Ford would have promoted those discounts in a big way. The light show was less than spectacular. I know a nearby neighborhood that has huge light displays, charges zero to go see and all you have to deal with is the traffic jam to see it. That light show was worth the wait in traffic. The Edison and Ford estates were nothing to look at and we made our way through those pretty quick. They only thing worth seeing was the museum and lab and that was not worth 20 bucks. Not worth the money. Maybe if it was 10 bucks. No pics to post as I was not impressed.

I have seen the signs for Koreshan State Park on the highway and had heard about it in the news and so we came for a visit. I did not know what to expect but it was a very nice visit. There were only a few buildings open but the signs and pictures gave you a glimpse into a cult back in the very early 20th century. I am not sure when the activities start and stop for the season but the cafe on the backside of the property said they were closed. I wish there were some people of this group still around because I would have loved to pick their brains on what life was like here back in the early 1900s (secret - the last Koreshan member died in 1982). Come down for a visit

We had a great time today at Billie Swamp Safari. When we first arrived, we were told that the boats and buggies may not go out due to thunder and lightning in the area so we visited all the exhibits. So much to see and do, even without the boat rides. We fed alligators and crocodiles along with otters and parakeets. See my pictures and you will see all that they had to offer. The weather cleared out while visiting the facilities and we went out on an air boat ride. Great staff and a great time to be had. Two thumbs up.

I go to NCRP to use the gym. The gym is very nice and the price is not bad. I paid $107 dollars for a year membership. They have treadmills, steppers, ellipticals, rowing, stationary bikes, weight machines, free weights, yoga and spinning classes and coming soon, kickboxing classes. They are supposed to have kick bags for the kickboxing classes as well. We shall see. They also have changing rooms, showers, etc and a full basketball court (I have never used, just have seen).

The Bird Gardens of Naples is a wonderful place to visit. Very friendly staff that give a clear and informative visit. Many Macaws, Cockatoos and other birds to visit. Bring unsalted nuts and berries or grapes. The Macaws seem to like unsalted almonds and the Cockatoos seem to like unsalted walnuts. The Purple Hyacinths like both but the one you meet at the front seems to favor almonds. A wonderful visit. This Bird Gardens could be so much more.

I love Bonita Beach Park and Barefoot Beach. Such a wonderful beach. Limited parking makes for a nice quiet day at the beach so plan to get there early. They have limited grilling spots along the beach so get there real early to grab one of those. I like these beaches a tad bit more than Vanderbilt beach, my other local favorite beach. It's a great place for seashell hunters. The flip side is that there are a lot of seashells. :o)

We didn't get to spend a lot of time here with this visit due to weather. The park seems nice and they have a nice tram service that brings you to the beaches. There are also bathrooms, a gift shop and I have read about snack shack. The beaches are nice for "sea shelling" and so so for castle building. We will have to come back on a nicer day.

This was our first visit and we checked out three or four of the trails. We saw one baby alligator and one orange snake (rat snake?). Other than that all we saw was common Floridian flora and very little fauna. :o(

I have heard that the park is an awesome place so I will have to give it a second chance. Not much to show but a few pics.

We came to Cambier Park for the empty bowls event. It was a perfect day for this money raising event. Perfect weather and overall great support from the contributors and event help. A wonderful selection of soups, bread and even the water was priced reasonably ($1). Good times and good soups.

It was an okay visit this time. We went for the BBQ and music festival. The BBQ offerings we're not so great. We have had much better. One vendor's offerings looked undercooked and we ended up throwing out good portions of what we bought from that vendor. Just an ok visit this time around.

It was a cold day and it might have been nicer if the weather was warmer and we could have walked around to enjoy the area more. Our guide was very informative and friendly. The historical information was very good. It was ok but I am not sure if I would recommend a visit there to friends.

Our first visit to Mote Marine but we had a great time there. Lots of Florida aquatics and native animals (fish, sharks, otters, alligators, manatees, caiman, etc). Lots to see and worth the visit. We didn't get to stop in the little town but that looked like an interesting place to visit.

Five thumbs up for Delnor-Wiggins State Park. We loved our day there. Nice beach. Water was great. Nice wave action due to a tropical depression on the East coast. There are bathrooms, picnic tables, stoves for bar-b-ques and great staff. Just a great day with everyone social distancing.

We had a great time playing mini golf. It had been many years and this place was similar to the ones we played on back in Massachusetts. I don't have any photos of the course but they have a camen feeding area as well. The staff were courteous and welcoming. We will be back for sure.

I read the book A Land Remembered and was told to come visit Cracker Country at the Florida State Fair. It was a great glimpse into the paste for the state of Florida. The people were all dressed in 1800s attire and we're busy doing things from that time period. A good time. 😀

This is a real swamp and there is wildlife in there. Be prepared for alligators on the walking paths and lots of other wildlife. This is also a great place for biking. The total trail length, our and back, is 12 miles so be sure to allocate enough time for your visit.

Very nice battlefield park. Well maintained and the signage is very informative. It would have been nice if the visitor center was open along with the buildings but I understand with covid. Beautiful scenery where such an awful event occurred. Well worth the visit.

It was a great day at the beach. I did some snorkeling and the water was a little stirred up but it was great anyway. When we were done at the beach we went to the fort and had a nice visit there. I would definitely return for beaching, swimming and snorkeling.

We came "off season" (June) to see the manatees and they weren't there so buyer beware, they are typically there between November and March. I'll update this again during the chilly season here in Florida when the manatees come up to the park to stay warm.

My favorite beach of all was Vanderbilt Beach until I visited the Barefoot Beach County Preserve. I loved it there. Spacious beach. Great for shell collecting. Water depth increases much faster than Vanderbilt Beach.
Just not my cup of tea. I've been to other science and art museums in the world and this one pales in comparison to those other museums. We left after quickly observing three floors.
I love zoos and the Naples Zoo is one of my favorites. From the animal shows to alligators, lions, tigers, giraffes oh my. Just a wonderful visit each and every time.
First visit to these caverns. Our tour guide was excellent and presented the caverns very nicely. The mile long tour was fun and educating. Well worth the stop.
Fun tourist place. Everybody waiting in line to take their picture. To Hattie's with that. Took our pic from the street and edited out other tourists. LOL.
Fun, fun, fun. Loved the ride and the attraction. The parks always make such a great presentation of their exhibits and rides. Awesome

This place is great for kids and adults. There are very few places where you can pet certain animals that you get to pet here. You get an opportunity to play with wolves. Pet a kangaroo, a sloth, parrots, a python, a crocodile, a tarantula, and a few other animals. You get to see the rest of the animals up close as well. You can also feed a number of animals including alligators, goats, foxes, lemurs and some others. They do have a more personal tour of the place where you get to interact with animals you wouldn't normally get to pet if you just paid for a regular ticket. It's $55 per person and I thought it was well worth it. Kids younger than 4 are free.

Really neat place especially if you've read the book. Our 5 year old was a little afraid of the caves and tunnels as it is actually pretty dark, practically pitch Black in some areas. Otherwise a really cool place for kids. It's also pretty shaded so a good place to get out of the sun. Also there are plenty of tables and benches where you can relax and enjoy a nice lunch without the hussle and bustle of the park.

Great place to look for shells. This beach park has everything you'll need for a day at the beach. They have plenty of bathrooms, changing areas, a shaded playground for the kids, BBQ grills with tables and plenty of parking, which is hard to find at certain beaches on Sanibel Island. The beach is pretty wide here so there is plenty of room to set up an umbrella.

Very nice gardens. They are not big but well laid out. They have nice trails and easily walkable. They have a very nice cafe with a good selection of vegan options. Very well priced too. The location is a bit out of the way of everything, but if you bundle it with the Vero Beach Outlets, it's a good day trip.

Very nice lake. There is fishing, swimming, kayaking, and boating. The beach area is a little small along with the swimming area, but a pretty nice lake nonetheless. Costs $2 per person to get in and they have bathrooms and showers. Although I probably would not use the showers. Plenty of parking as well.

Very nice zoo. It seemed a little smaller than most other zoos I've visited before but it was more intimate. The animals are close so you can actually see them. The variety of animals is pretty big and the exhibits are very nice. I enjoyed this zoo and the price is well worth the experience.

This is a great place to take the kids or go for a walk, especially on a nice day. Very nice garden that's just the right size. Very well priced, especially the annual pass. At $50 for the family, it's a steal. Will definately come back again.

Very nice nice place. Relatively small so there is no bad seat in the house. I've been there once and would definitely go again. Prices for concerts are not bad at all. My only gripe about this place is that parking can be a bit tough.

Great hiking trails and nice waterfalls. You can walk around the trails for hours. There are lots of stairs, but the views are really nice. They have a picnic area as well so you can BBQ there and make an entire day of it.

Really nice place for a hike. There are a large number of shorter that add up to some long walk depending on how much you want to walk. Partly shaded and party in the sun. There is a really nice mix of animals as well.

Merida meet and greet. Go there in the second half of the day as the sun is shining in a way that you can get some shade from the trees while standing in line. In the morning you are in full sun and it's brutal.

Very nice place to lounge around and have a cold beer. They have hammocks tied to the trees where you can relax. Franklin Fountain sells ice cream there. Federal Donut is also there. Good place for a family.

Great place to cool off in the summer. This place gets very busy so come early to get parking and a good spot. Water is always nice and cool. The hiking trails are pretty long and easy to hike with kids.
It's Disney. Family friendly and lots of slides and things to do for the little ones. Their splash area is really nice and pretty pig. We can spend the entire day relaxing in the lazy river.
Great educational ride. You won't be able to see all of the animals there so you may want to go their a couple of times at different times of the day to see as many animals as possible.
First zoo in the country and still one of the best. They have limited space and did a great job with all of the exhibits. We have an annual membership and come here all of the time.
I didn't find it very interesting. All of the animals are mechanized. The only thing that made this ride interesting was the cast member telling jokes the entire ride.
Great hiking place. Dogs are allowed and it's a very nice trail partly along the river. Lots of animals along the trails and the place is pretty good for birding.
Love this place. It's very peaceful and Zen. Just walk around for a couple of hours and have a bento box lunch at their restaurant, overlooking the gardens.
It's a pretty small zoo, but what it lacks in size it makes up in its exhibits. The selection of animals is nice and they are very close to the visitors.
Meet and greet for Goofy/Donald on one side and Minnie/Daisy on the other side. It's two separate lines that you have to wait to meet all four.
Nice park with relatively new playground for kids. It's pretty big as well. There is a basketball court and a baseball field there as well.
A must for anybody visiting Philly. Line could be very long depending on the time of day and weather, so be prepared to wait.
Nice place for kids to run around and have hands on experiences with many things. I think it's best for kids 3.5 and older.
Great ride just like Dumbo. Kids can ride this while one of the parents stands in line to meet Jasmine and Aladdin.

To say that I enjoyed my time here is putting it mild. Two things you have to love to appreciate this, cars and history. They focus very much on three brands of cars that were crucial in the early automotive industry but are no longer in business. There is a great number of antique cars here, many restored, some in original condition. Each car has a history of some sort to go with it.
They also have a floor with many other brands and a great deal of history to go with them. Truly a gem in the Midwest.

This is a great drive to make.
My personal tips.
- You're going to want to hike at least a few of the trails because it's beautiful back here. Make sure you wear hiking shoes.
- Get started as early as possible in the morning. The few parking spots for the cabins and the trails fill quickly.
- The road is one way so if you want to see something, stop for it when you can.
- The road is small and winding, it's not for the faint of heart.

Enjoy the scenery!!

This place is amazing! Three things
1. You're going to want to be in shape, there quite a few stairs and if you're going here, you don't want to miss out on anything.
2. Give yourself the whole day. There's a lot to explore and once you get back in the trails you might as well see it all.
3. Do your best to avoid the weekends and holidays. This place is extremely popular, the trails get busy and it becomes impossible to find parking.

It's a good small town zoo. The pricing is reflective of that and affordable for a small family to go have a fun day.
The exhibits seem to be getting outdated as do some of the other areas. It's quite small but once again, it's a small town zoo.
The monkeys are probably one of the most fun exhibits as they are active and play around a lot.
Make sure to climb the tower, it's beautiful at the top and more than worth the climb.

It was a cold rainy day so we decided to check this place out as it's all indoor. We're made a great choice.
While the price is a little high per person, it you enjoy reading, you'll be able to spend hours in here. This is a museum on crime in general. You'll find history in the stories and real crime scene items. They have fun interactive things for the kids as well.

I've been here twice now, once for a ball game and once for a concert.
Here's my gripes -
$6 for a bottle of water. Water is a necessity and not something to price gouge on. It shouldn't be over $3.
Men's bathrooms are open stalls, no dividers for urinals.
Not my first choice for a good time but would go back for the right concert.

This is an awesome state park. I would assume that it's often overlooked due to how treacherous and yet short some of the trails are. Many of the most beautiful and scenic trails can be walked within a day however there are rugged. I don't think I would spend a weekend hiking here but it definitely would be a good day trip.

The tulip festival held here is great. Of all the festivals that I have visited, I don't think I have ever been to one that has such great vendors. There were no cheap products, most everything was unique and handcrafted in some way. If you enjoy shopping for unique products, I suggest you visit this place.

We all know it's an overrated tourist spot but you are going to do it anyway so just go see it and get it over with. You won't be any happier or any more sad for having done it, you will just have fit in with all your other Facebook and Instagram friends which really is all we're trying to do.

We have frequented this zoo quite a bit in the last few years and now that we have a child we get a yearly pass. It's a great place to hang out and see the animals play. They are always making new improvements and keeping the zoo in great condition. A wonderful piece of South Bend.

It's a beautiful spot. Many places to park. Some of the beach is rather rocky and some of it will require a significant amount of walking. If you're not on the beach, expect to be bit by mosquitoes. We had the chance to see dolphins swimming. That was quite a treat.

A great place to visit. This park has multiple areas to enjoy. My family has went here for several different activities including picnics, an outdoor show at the barn and hiking.
There are open fields, a boat launch, hiking trails and several pavilions for picnics.

A splendid place to visit. It's quite beautiful here.
The state park has done a great job of building and preserving history here.
The staff is very knowledgeable about the history and able to answer any questions.
It's exciting to get to see the mill run!

This is a great place to have picnics, grill, bring groups of friends to get together. There are numerous parking places equipped with outhouses as well as pavilions. You'll also find great walking/biking trails and locals say the fishing is good here.

This place is amazing! So beautiful at night.
Depending on when you go, the lights are different colors. If there are special events or special holidays going on, it's always fun to go see the new light display.
Such a beautiful gardens. I recommend giving yourself at least 4 hours just to stroll and relax. You can easily get through it in a half hour but you can also easily take much longer.
If you love classic cars and history, don't miss this place. Not only is there a lot of great history about South Bend but also a large amount of American history as well.
This is a nice small park. The beach isn't exactly beautiful but it's a nice spot to stroll and look out over the water. The boardwalks are nice and have great views.
Beautiful place. Several festivals are held here and it's a great location. When not having festivals it's a good place for walking, running and taking pictures.
A very beautiful place! You're going to want to make sure you do some exploring here. Depending on what time of year, there is some unique scenery here.
Love it! It's only $1 to go to the top. It's a lot of stairs but it's an amazing view. You can also get a selfie with Paul Bunyan so that's a plus 😁
A lovely park with a great historical story. The trails are very nice and kept up. There are many pavilions around the park for a picnic or cookout.
A great place for Niles! Walking, strolling, biking, skating. A nice view of the river with swings to sit and enjoy nature.
A wonderful view. If you are ever in the scenic route, you've got to stop and take a look. They also have restrooms here.
A neat Park to visit. Plenty of area to go for a stroll or fishing. Plenty of parking. Nice picnic areas. Unique history.

Exact same review as for the library. It is on the same property.

They have done a great many repairs since Hurricane Katrina damaged it so much in 2005. It faces the Gulf of Mexico. I am currently listening to the podcast "1865" which discusses the assassination of Abraham Lincoln, and the repercussions and how the ending of the Civil War came to an unraveling so much.

Jefferson Davis may have been the 1st and only President of the Confederacy, the emphasis here is on the states rights, specifically to own slaves. This is a narrow view of states rights, but the only one they held. I missed out on the beginning of the tour, but what I did get was informative, if a bit too narrow. The grounds, cemetery and library are immaculate, and this should be enough of a testament.

The staff members are very friendly, this is a good place. I just think that the view of the history should be broader, especially when so many are still disenfranchised even in 2019. I would suggest coming here to see it as a reminder of the past and that it should not be repeated. There are reenactments, though I have not seen it, I would be interested. Pretty informative.

This is the stuff of dreams. I have been to something similar in the past, but nothing this interactive. You get your ticket, and wait in line. You can also purchase various packages of stuff to feed the animals. I came with my supervisor from work who wanted to go with her step mothers group from a nursing home. It was so cute to see these elderly people so excited over the animals, though some of them were quite scared of the animals. You ride around in these HUGE trains whose cars look like covered wagons and are pulled by a tractor. Very country, very fun. Nice to see buffalo, giraffes and other animals close up. They did tell a story of how they once had a monkey, but had issues with it misbehaving badly, and they had to find a new place where it could not leave visitors gifts on their cars. Too funny!

I came a few years ago and a large bird got on my car and pooped on it! Only kidding, but I kept having visions of that happening. I have actually been here twice, the first time was in November when the bears were hibernating, so I was unable to see them, so I went back in the spring and was able to see them. I have only done the drive thru part. I went by myself both times, and spent several hours both times just sitting and watching. Amazing! Large spaces for the animals to meander, separate areas to keep enemies apart. You are warned to keep your windows up when you go into areas where the animals want to eat you for lunch. Wonderful, wonderful, wonderful.

Recreation of the original house on this site. Due to time and Hurricane Katrina, all was destroyed. This is a lovely house with a basic layout. You are not allowed upstairs for some reason, which is a shame. It would be nice to see the view. A few years ago when they had the anniversary reenactment, it was totally neat to see all the people dressed up. So much history of life and the Revolutionary War. The largest battle of the Revolutionary War was here. I'm not sure how much use from the Civil War this location was, but I am sure there was something.

What a great place! For a very reasonable price ($15 + tax), I spent about an hour wandering the halls of this small but jam packed aquarium. It was not busy at all. There was a small group of adults and kids that came in after me and it was nice to watch the kids have fun. Packed full of things that will set off your imagination. Some of the more interactive exhibits are closed now due to the virus, and the restaurant is temporarily closed. I wish they had some adult animal masks, but they don't. I would recommend this to everyone.

Ok, so the docents here put an emphasis on this being the past and do not act like sore losers for how the war turned out (the Civil War that is). There are basic historical markers, facts about what happened, uniforms, weapons and just so much interesting stuff. There are a few steps in front to get in, and I do not know if there is a ramp or any way for handicapped to get in. Set in a fully restored building, there is just so much to the displays to look at. There is a small gift shop. This was an enjoyable visit.

Very cute museum in Kentwood. The docent is very proud of the displays. Set up as a tribute to their pride and joy, Britney Spears, you can tell the love they have for her. 3/4ths of the museum is set up and dedicated to her, and the remaining is setup as a tribute to all of the military service members that came from this area to serve in the US Armed Forces. Amazing pride this community has. And the pictures of the Dairy Festival they used to have is pretty amazing as well.

The aisles can be a bit narrow, and I am not sure this is a good place for small children, but this is an interesting museum highlighting the foods and cuisines of the Southern part of the US. It seems like a monumental task, and some visitors think they have their own connections and can be upset when they are not represented. It just seems like a lot of stuff crammed into a space that is increasingly becoming too small for all of this. Parking in the area can be an issue.

Every time I have visitors from out of town, I bring them here twice. Once during the day so they can see what it looks like and what the area looks like. Then once in the evening once the fountain has its colored lights on. It is cool to see all of the different Mardi Gras Krewes represented all around this large fountain. I love it in the day, I love it at night, I love it when its hot outside, and I love it when its freezing. Come and enjoy.

Very interesting museum. The owners of this location also own one in LA, and they said they often switch things between the two. I enjoyed coming in and looking around. There are letters from killers, newspapers, news casts about it, shows, movies and so much more that goes in depth. The tour is self guided, and I think it is worth the time and effort to come in. It is off the beaten path, and I would love to come back.

Great location. Very informative. The people who work here are very proud of this PT boat, for good reason. A lot of time and effort was put into getting everything exactly right.  All of it is original, and it takes a lot of effort to keep something that is more than 60 years old in peak condition, even running condition. And the fact that this particular boat was made here in New Orleans is a point of pride for them.

Great small museum documenting the largely poor, displaced citizens that have always been at a disadvantage. Hit hard by every hurricane in an attempt to save the wealthier people. No one seems to really care. It took over 10 years to get a public library to reopen after Katrina, let alone a public school. This is a great way to have a voice for the voiceless.

Great little museum that details the history of the area. Small shotgun building that is one of the original travel hotels for workers that migrated thru the country. Pictures of how it looked long ago and of how the area looked. The docent was full of information and more than happy to talk all day to a willing recipient. Quite delightful in all ways.

I have been eyeing this place for a few years now. There is no parking lot, but you do not have to pay for street parking. A few steps up to the museum. Cash only. Amazing guide full of information and passionate about the history. Fully recommend for locals and tourists alike. Well worth more than the $10 admission.
dislikes: Facilities & Services: No Parking Lot, Cash Only

reviews_attraction.text: During the summer, this is packed with kids and their parents hoping to expend some energy. Rides, food, all kinds of fun. During Christmas, they have the lights, decorations, all thing Hannukah and Christmas. A train ride thru the park with the large decorations. A delight for children and adults alike.

This interactive film is just amazing. You really feel like you are in the scene. It can set you on edge during several moments, but it was totally immersive. I came with my handicapped parents, and it is wheelchair accessible, which is nice. I suggest this for everyone who comes to the museum.

This park is close to my childhood home, and I remember when it was built in the 1980's. My family would walk on the trails, play on the equipment, have picnics. It is lovely. There are fields for the sports balls, and restrooms as well. Plenty of parking.

The trail goes from east to west across St Tammany parish. The part I have been to had a spot for concerts, restroom area, sandwich shop, a brewpub. Looks like a great place for gathering. Large space to practice hula hoops, dances or just play.

I am fairly new to Mardi Gras as I moved to the area about 10 years ago. The video at the beginning was useful. Seeing all of the works in progress was amazing. The staff here were wonderful. I would recommend this to everyone.
Park area, boat launch. Small fenced area for dogs. There is an annual take back the night event in the fall with food and the ability to meet the local police force which is very nice.
Great park with a rich history. Lovely statues, water features. Has the Mahalia Jackson theater. Deep history and probably full of spirits from those who were bought and sold here.
Great sculpture garden. Located right by the museum in City Park, this is great to walk off those beignets you just ate while looking at artwork. Just lovely.
Cute park with a walking path that has markings so you know how far you have walked. People set off fireworks here for the major holidays.
Whole city blocks as parks with statues, benches, green spaces. Very nice to sit and eat a sandwich on your lunchtime.
In the west hills, a lovely park and hiking area. Nice place for a picnic with a view of the city.

At the park entrance the Ranger can give you good information.   There is an extra fee to visit the gardens during the blooming season.  Pets not allowed in the gardens.   But the park is much bigger than just the garden area.

The first turn off leads the the lake,  the second area you come to is the parking for the gardens,  and you can continue past the parking area and down a dirt road to the back area of the park where dogs are allowed.

We strolled the gardens and met the very helpful volunteer at the house who can give you lots of historical info.   Everything was left exactly as the family had it.    We missed peak bloom by just a week or two.  Visited in late march 2017.  Its still a great garden to visit, with lots of garden "rooms"   lots of people were there taking photos for engagements & sororities.   The previous day a triathlon had been held at the park.

We got our bikes and then rode from the garden parking area to the 4 mile loop around lake Overstreet.   There are also other trails you can take for a longer ride if you have a mountain bike.   We had hybrid bikes and they were able to do the trail ok but a mountain bike would have been better.   Very shady.   Lots of poison ivy off of the trail so beware if your walking dogs.    I think I also picked up tiny ticks here too, and I was biking not walking.

Its a beautiful treasure for Tallahassee

Nice park with a swimming area (closes at 6:30 due to gators)  Boat tours - they do sell out!   So go purchase your tickets at the river front when you arrive to get your tour time.   If they are sold out the ranger at the front gate will let you know so that you don't pay to come into the park.   They do take credit cards for the boat tours.    Have to line up 15 min or so before the tour.    Entertaining rangers point out lots of gators and some birds on a mile or so down the river and back.   They do not go the entire length of the river in the park.  The ranger explained that part of the river gets no human contact except for an annual survey.   No private kayaks or boats allowed to launch at the park.  Swimming is restricted to a roped off area, and you understand why after seeing all the gators on the boat tour.     There is also a 7 mile walking trail.   We were able to ride hybrid bikes on 1 mile of it with no problem.     A lodge with a good dining room is on site.   Excellent sea food - very fresh.  I got it grilled and it was amazing.   Someone else got a fried platter and it was HUGE.    The soda fountain closes early - around 5 I think.   And was very slow service.

amazing park!   We stay just outside the park at a condo and we bike,  drive, hike and kayak the park.    We have not yet made it to the tip yet but hope to someday, its a long hike or kayak to the tip.    Have to be careful biking the roads as there is a lot of traffic and after the picnic area the road to the cabins and back country trail is narrow.   You can drive to the last parking lot and hike thru the dunes to the beach and have it almost to yourself.     The bay is incredible,  like a fishtank,  shallow water and you can see everything from a kayak.   Different areas have different type of sea life so explore them all.   Too bad the cabins are not dog friendly, or the beach in the park.   Otherwise we would be staying in the park!   In May we saw lots of migrating birds sheltering in the trees making the short bayside hike an incredible experience.   Crystal clear waters and lots of wildlife.

We were riding the paved bike trail and decided to take a quick detour into this park.   As others have mentioned the Osprey main trail is still being maintained but the return Limpkin trail and 2 boardwalks are closed.  It was cool to see the spring.    Wear bug spray!  we were eaten to death if we stopped.   We ride hybrid bikes and the main trail was ride-able as it has rained recently and was packed down.   I could see that if it was very dry the sugar sand would be trouble for our bikes.   Its not a smooth ride as there are old bricks and concrete used to stabilize the trail but it wasn't bad.  Would be easy on a mountain bike.     Such a same the park is not being maintained.  Would be an easy 5 star if maintained.   Sadly a 3 because so much is closed.   This was July 2017

Arrived by Kayak from Goode park,  paddle was pretty easy on an incoming tide.    Several intersections are well marked so boaters can find their way.     Once in the sanctuary the water is shallow so only Kayaks can go up to the dam.   We had to limbo under one fallen tree, but our experienced group of kayakers had no problems.   There are two areas you can stop in the sanctuary.   One was a launch and another had a boardwalk overlook.  we just hauled our kayaks up the steep bank and hung out for lunch.   The Turtles here come up and check out the kayaks and will even try to bite a paddle.    I would return to walk the boardwalks.  Nice and shady thought the bugs were bad on land.  On the water we were not bothered.

Came across this park as it is along the Pinellas Trail, what a great find!   Has lots of parking,  a natural spring head,  and an easy flat wide loop trail out to several lookouts over the bay.     The benches in the park are artistic - some are wood and some are metal - one shaped like a dolphin.   Unfortunately both times we visited the lookout tower was still closed and being re built due to a fire.   On the walk we saw spoonbills, and many other wading birds feeding as it was low tide.   We had hoped to see Manatee but due to the springs construction they can not swim up to the spring.     There is a great group of photos around the spring showing how it had been developed when it was private property.
