Beware Google maps tried to have us turn on a fire break road.  The actual road to the parking lot is right across from the old Wakulla Park Drive.    Go down the one lane road and it opens up into a decent size parking area.    Have cash, Pay at the un manned pay station with an envelope.  Has a porta potty (handicapped size)   service gate is locked to keep you from driving farther than the parking lot.   The sand was too loose for hybrid bikes.   A beach bike or mountain bike would make a quick and easy ride.   Unfortunately they had just done a controlled burn so all the dogwood blossoms we came for had been burned, so we turned back.   Next time!

Nice small park with a boat launch and separate Kayak launch located behind the restrooms.   Good clean restroom.   A wood dock that people were fishing off of and a tour boat came to pick up customers there too.   Make sure you have a map and gps,  there are wide canals and also some very small areas you can squeeze through in a kayak but it would be very easy to get turned around in the mangroves.   These are all protected mangrove islands,  no place to stop and get out of your boat.    Couldn't see much in the water but saw lots of birds.
dislikes: No place to stop and get out of boat

reviews_attraction.text: Dogs not allowed in the park,  though many businesses in Winter park are dog friendly.    There is a parking garage at 150 W Canton Ave that has free public parking on the weekends on the upper floors.   Beware the stairs are dirty so you may want to take the elevator.    The park has beautiful planters along the street side,  I love to get ideas.   A rose garden at one end which has just been updated.   The park has a stage at the other end,  and the SunRail and Amtrack station in the middle.   Sun Rail only runs on special weekends.

Very unique beach.  Turn at Buccaneer Trail,  there is a self pay kiosk,  a good amount of parking in a circular drive.   Can park and ride the paved bike trail from here as well.    There is an overlook at the parking area, but access to the beach has been fenced off due to erosion.  But no worries its a short trail through the woods to the beach.    Bikes and dogs allowed on the trail.  Hard packed wide trail.  No dogs on the beach.  the longer you look the more you see when exploring the trees on the beach!

Small parking lot so arrive early and bring cash for the self pay entry.  Second visit for us.  First time we went out with the Kayak tour and that was great.  This time took the 1.3 mile walk to the end of the island.  Shaded most of the way.  Multiple places to stop on intercoastal or gulf side.  Dogs not allowed on beach but our dog could swim at the multiple small access points to the intercoastal.   Lots of turtle nests on gulf side.  Great small park for the nature lover.

On Easter Sunday we launched our kayaks from the paved boat ramp.   there was a steady stream of people launching boats, kayaks, paddle boards on the late Sunday morning.    The covered pavilion had bathrooms that were open, and clean.    Paddled up to Turkey creek.  Fairly good signage up river to keep you going in the right direction.   Go by some homes and then wilderness areas.   Saw manatees, birds, the begging turtles in Turkey creek.    Can get windy near the dock.

We are garden members and its nice that with the membership they provide some free passes for friends.    We took a friend with us to see the azaleas and camellias blooming.   A nice walk around the garden.   We arrived at 9:30 and found parking.  With the dinosaur exhibit until April 30th  the gardens were packed by the time we left at around 11 .     Membership also gives you free access to reciprocal gardens across the USA.    This is a great benefit

It was closed on a Sunday morning but we came by as we were riding the Springs to Springs bike trail.   Good amount of parking.  No one was there but parking lot was accessible on this sunday morning.  Downhill from there to the main trail.   We will be back when they are open.  Looked like a neat place to visit.  Gift shop window showed a $4 fee for entry to the house.

NO dogs, no bikes.   Horses ARE allowed and probably the best way to see the park, as the deep sugar sand makes hiking difficult.    No dog rule IS strictly enforced.   it is a cool park but without a bike or horse its a long slog to see much.  The pond in the back with the overlook is very cool.   I only give it a bad rating for all the rules.

Kind of funny as this is listed as a dog park.  It includes a dog park but it is a large park with springs, sidewalks, board walks, several pavilions, a dock to fish off of.  The Springs to Springs trail also goes through the park.   There are also some grass mowed trails you can follow if you have a mountain or hybrid bike.   Beautiful park

Small Gem in Jacksonville.   Parking is across the street.    Member of the reciprocal gardens so we got in for free.    Only took us an hour or so to see the gardens,  a small gem but worth the stop.    Right on the river, views were beautiful.    There is a cafe,  and plenty of galleries of art inside as well.   Nice volunteers.

Second visit.  We parked here last year to ride the bike trail.  This year we were riding the trail and stopped here for a quick break.   No one was at the spring at 10 am on a Sunday morning.  Bathrooms clean.   Moderate amount of parking.   Very shady so a good stop along the bike trail.

Closed visitor center in summer off season.  But we will be back.  Really cool building overlooking a small pond.  Nice trail updates on chalkboard by parking lot warning of flooding and bugs.  Also listed activities at other parks in the area that are affiliated.

Beautiful boardwalk that overlooking the bay.  A good place to watch birds if you time the tides right.  Places to sit and education signs.  Ramps on each end.  Park also has pickle ball court and screened in pavilions.   Fire ring with seating and a pier.

Pretty park, heavily used.    We arrived as a half marathon had ended and they were just breaking down.    The farmers market is on the far end away from the historic district.     Interesting that a guide we took said the fountain was mail order!
dislikes: Farmers market far from historic district

reviews_attraction.text: Stopped here during a Kayak trip.   There was a shore we could pull our kayaks up on.    Is a great place to watch the sunset.  One person big clean bathroom.   Very small park.   Big beautiful cypress trees.  Very shady park.

Amazing small park!  Part by the road is a formal garden with a small gazebo and restrooms and then a boardwalk through the mangroves to the river.  It's right on a sidewalk bike trail so a nice stop along the way.
Huge area,  I have only visited the 1,000 islands which are mangrove islands.   The water there was not clear but we did see lots of birds. Great kayaking adventure in the shallows.
We did not go in but walked the park.  $2 fee and it looked really small from the outside.  They close for an hour for lunch.  Beautiful views down the park towards the water.

amazing place to go in the fall so many different types of trees they're labeled and named the grounds are clean and fast and well-cared-for there's a beautiful Creek it separates one part of the grounds from the other I love the fact that they do have a restroom inside the main building they also have porta potties available there is a small garden community garden on the grounds as well it is not pet friendly they want to keep the grounds as natural as possible so they recommend you not bringing dogs or cats. Right now it's the fall and you get so many arrays of colors from the trees in the foliage there's places for you to sit and eat lunch or just relax after the long walk it's very peaceful and Serene here

This place is another one of my hiking spots that I was glad that I went to go see the road is or the walking path is paved which makes it nice be prepared to do a lot of uphill walking in order to see the light house but it's definitely well worth it parking is also pretty ample and I'm pretty sure that there's a bus that will drop you off at the bottom are kind of at the top to get to the bottom to get back to the top of this lighthouse

The lovely park that has one of the coolest radio Flyers inside. there's a lot to do they have a pond where you can feed the geese, there's a place for you to run, it meets up with the Centennial Trail in the summer months they hold eating events it's across the street from a large Mall easy to get to ample parking. It also leads up to Spokane Falls which is this beautiful waterfall in the heart of downtown Spokane

This place was absolutely beautiful I was very happy to see this place I'm actually stumbled on it on my way to the pill boxes to go hiking one of the coolest things that happened to me while I was at the speech as I seen my first sea turtle in the wild he popped right up out of the water and showed himself to me which was amazing very family-friendly there's ample parking along the beach as well

I am so glad that I had the opportunity to work on the Olympic Peninsula and go to the many parks that the Olympic National Forest holds the Hoh Rainforest was magical hurricane Ridge was very cool marymere Falls was priceless just so much you're so much do there's so much to see what I like about it is that if you pay $25 you have a whole week to investigate the different parks around here

The perfect park to come to when you just want to get away from everything it's my first time in Ocala really touring around. This park has ample parking for your vehicles it has an open Trail for you can ride bikes or just walk around and filled with very helpful information along with beautiful flowers. Also has a clean restroom. To keep the Ruffians down the Police tour the area

I love this part because it gives you a nice Trail if you want to do like off in the woods trail they do have a paved trail for you to ride your bike or if you don't like the off-roading type thing there is a playground for kids it also has restrooms. I enjoy it because I can just bring my lawn chair and set up under the shade tree and enjoy my just relaxation for the day

This is a beautiful Park to visit is nestled inside of a residential area that you have to turn off of 51st Street to get to if you're on Biscayne they have a lot of trails there is like play areas for kids it's great for camping there's a boat launch they also have a place where you can rent Kayaks and it's really clean and just a great place to go

What I love most about this place with the fact that is your hiking along around Arts Center you come across some beautiful pieces of art that are just kind of woven into the natural landscape when you go into the main building there was an exhibit that you got to vote on for the best or your most favorite which I thought was really cool

Friendly staff it's a awesome fairy to be on as you're making your way from Port Angeles to Victoria on the ferry there's tons of information about how long the fairies been in business how it was founded who created it there's all type of little artifacts on it there's a cute little store to where you can buy souvenirs

It was my first time walking this Preserve. It's very lovely I like the fact that the trail has wood chips on it so it makes it very comfortable to walk. I would recommend to have a map because it's very easy to get lost and I was with a group who traveled this Trail quite a bit. You can bring pets it is very marked

This is a large vast Botanical Garden make sure you have hiking shoes cuz you will need them it rains on that side of Oahu a lot so make sure that you have an umbrella or don't mind walking in the rain the staff is very helpful there's so much to see it's almost impossible to do it all in one day

This park is everything that you could ever want it has gazebos for sitting and just reflecting while you're watching the waves move.it has a park for kids to play at there is a interesting little Trail it's clean it has ample parking have nothing bad to say about this place is beautiful

A very Lush beautiful well-kept Japanese garden with Bridges and koi and that peaceful Ambience that makes you just want to sit and meditate in your Zen. There is also bathrooms on site and it is wheelchair accessible. The only downside to it is that there's not a lot of parking

Another very good hike did I made this area is a very muddy path but it is the start of the only way that you can get to The Stairway to Heaven legally there's actually some ruins there along the path and once you get up a ways it's beautiful there's a lot to see

It's the perfect little Cove to just like sit and relax and gather your thoughts, write in your journal,or have lunch with a friend I've went there on sunny days and it was beautiful I went there on a rainy day and walk down the coast with my umbrella

The customer service representative inside the visitor center is very very friendly and knowledgeable. Even if you don't stay for the feeding which is at 1:30 everyday the elk are so close that it's impossible not to get a good picture

I stopped at this place on my way to Cape Flattery and it's absolutely magical and beautiful I found my very first sea lion hanging out on one of the Rocks just relaxing so I got a cool picture but the views are just priceless
I spend a lot of time at this particular park it is off the beaten path very clean it has Hills for hiking you can run around it it's great for kids they have bathrooms on site and also ample parking
Very beautiful well kept Park it's attached to a Japanese garden as well as a rose garden and a perennials Garden they do have on-site restrooms and it is wheelchair accessible
Beautiful park with plenty of parking lots of shade trees and a nice Pond that people actually use the fish. They do have clean restrooms and it's a very well-kept Park
This park you get to see all types of wildlife whether it being deer or Birds. Or you can just walk down the trail and maybe see owl or just view the lovely coastline
Very clean well-kept area with tons of things to do there's all types of bars and restaurants and shopping areas ample parking always some type of an event going on
Very clean Beach there is a lifeguard that is not directly on the beach but he's not too far away visible signs posted because part of the beach is a nude beach
A very Serene and beautiful place to be excellent use of Port Angeles and the Olympics if you're into finding painted rocks it's one of the better places to go

Tallulah Gorge State Park is roughly 100 Miles north of Atlanta at border with South Carolina. The gorge is roughly 900 feet deep with 3 major falls, Hurricane Falls, Oceana Falls and Bridal Veil Falls.
From visitor Center you can take a trail leading you down 310 stairs to 200 feet long Suspension Bridge that perches 80 feet above Hurricane Falls, you can then go further 221 stairs to the base of the falls then back or climb 347 stairs to south rim up on other side to continue on a loop taking you back to visitor center.
You can otherwise take a trail along the north rim to highest point in park called Inspiration Point with very beautiful view of Oceana Falls. Naturally there are other trails to explore the park.

Parking cost $5 unless you have a yearly Georgia States Park Pass. Parking lot is however limited. On weekend rangers may direct you to parking lot at camp ground.

Amicalola Falls State Park is roughly 75 Miles north of Atlanta, GA in Dawson County. The main feature of the park are the beautiful  729 feet high cascading falls. At the bottom of the falls you find the Basin Pool with picnic area and parking lot which are roughly 0.75 Mile drive from the visitor center.
Naturally you can walk a beautiful trail to the Basin Pool if you like.
You can also either drive or walk a trail to the top of the falls then go down the total of 604 steps to the bottom crossing a bridge that goes over the falls.
There is a lodge in the park if you like to stay overnight.
The views of the falls, and the view from the top of the falls of the mountains and valleys are very enjoyable in any season of the year but more so during the changing colors of the fall.

Beautiful park roughly 120 Miles north of Atlanta. On the peak of Black Rock Mountain which is about 3334 feet high you find the visitor center with a shop and bathrooms. Next to it is an observation platform with marvelous views of the valleys and mountains. After the visitor centers there are cabins for rent. There is also a camping ground in park.
The drive from Mountain City up to peak of mountain is very beautiful with multiple observations platforms.
There are also multiple trails one at least is 7 miles long, another 2 miles.
I visited in May, wild flowers were abundant mainly on ridges and edges. Definitely worthwhile visiting. As in all State Parks there is $5 parking fee per car, not visitor unless you have yearly pass for Georgia State Parks, then parking is free.

The Pine Mountain Trail East is a loop that start in a small parking lot that accommodate roughly 10 cars and go up to Pine Mountain Summit which is about 1562 feet high above see level with elevation gain of about 742 feet. The loop is about 2.8 miles long but if you go up to the summit using left  branch and return on it not looping the round trip is about 2.4 miles or less. The trail is relatively narrow and occasionally steep but not very difficult to climb. It is shady surrounded by trees, and the Boy-scout put some signs describing the type of trees you see.
The views from the top are beautiful including the views of Altoona Lake but not stunning.
The East Trail is less busy than the more popular West Trail but both meet near the summit.

An amazingly beautiful place roughly 38 Miles from Santa Fe with narrow canyons you can walk on their bottom and enjoy the fascinating stone formation. then climb to top and enjoy the view of mountains and valleys from the top. You gain 630 feet elevation. The walk from parking lot to top is roughly 1.2 Miles. There is another loop with cave in stone called Cave Loop and is roughly 0.7 Miles.
This is a national monument with parking fee of $5 unless you have National Park Pass. Though parking area is not small but this national treasure is very popular and you may have to wait for parking spot.
I suggest you go early to enjoy the place before the crowd comes and take nice pictures that you would not forget.

Piedmont Park is the Central Park of Atlanta on smaller scale. It is the lung of Midtown Atlanta not far from many business and condo high rises. It share the ground and parking house with its neighbor the Atlanta Botanical Garden.
It is a beautiful green area With a lake, sport facilities including for swimming , tennis etc. naturally there are picnic areas. Scattered pieces of art are also there to see.
There are many trails shaded with big trees to walk or bike. Squirrels are in abundance. Ducks swim in the lake.
Parking in parking house is not expensive. I think it is $2 for first hour then $1 per each subsequent hour.

Just an excellent combination of history and nature. Fort Zachary Taylor built in 19th century hold the largest collection of Civil War era weapons, and a beautiful sandy beach with trees in background next to each other in one state park. There is also a cafe on the beach with outdoor seating area where you can get drinks or something to eat. Presumably sunset view from this park is very beautiful. The park has 3 adjacent park lots, one for the Forte, one for the beach, and one for sunset observation. Entry fee $7 per car.  Do not miss it if in Key West.

Beautiful State Park not far from Asheville, NC with multiple hiking trails the main of which are the FourSeason Trail that goes from lower parking lot to the feet of the main attraction in the Park, namely Chimney Rock itself, and the trail takes you fown roughly 1.4 Miles from Chimney Rock down to the bottom of Hickory Nut Falls. From the top of Chimney Rock (You have to climb 491 steps or take elevator if active to get up there), you have impressive views of Lake Lure.
Entry fee is fairly expensive, $17 per adult, not car. But it maybe worth it.

Beautiful park in heart of Roswell with ruins of old mill, pedestrian covered wooden bridge and beautiful, I believe manmade falls over small dam in addition to hiking trail. All can be ideal for photography but I think professional photographers need a city permit.
Parking could be tight on weekend given the parking area is shared with surrounding restaurants and stores.
It certainly worth visiting if in area, and repeat visiting if you live not far in metro Atlanta.

New Manchester Mill Ruins are located inside Sweetwater Creek State Park on the bank of the creek few minutes walk along a shaded trail from the Visitor Center which contain more historical information.
The original mill was built by slaves in 1847 and destroyed by federal troops in 1864 during Civil War. It is worth visiting while you are in the beautiful park. Parking fee in the park is $5 per car, not person. Unless you have a Georgia State Parks yearly pass.

Brasstown Bal Visitor Center is on the top of the highest mountain of Georgia with fascinating panoramic views from the top of the building. The center has a small movie theater where you can watch a less than 1.2 hour movie about Brassrown Bald. There is also a small historic museum about Brasstown Bald and naturally bathrooms.
A bus ride from parking lot to the visitor center at the top cost $2 per adult roundtrip. You can also walk the steep trail up.

Bust Your Butt Waterfalls are strangely named small falls on the road between Franklin and Highlands in North Carolina. The falls are beautiful surrounded with rocks and trees. They are directly visible from the road and few steps from it. You can park off the road and climb the ricks down to the falls.
They are worh a stop if driving that road, but not as impressive the Dry Falls which are close on the same road.
dislikes: Less impressive compared to nearby attractions

reviews_attraction.text:
Turtleback Falls are few minutes walk/hill-climb after Rainbow Falls on the same trail originating in Gorges State Park though both falls are technically outside the park. These water drop of these falls is not as high or impressive as Rainbow Falls nevertheless they are beautiful.
So do not stop at Rainbow Falls. Gather your energy and push yourself up the hill to these falls. It is worth it.

A nice park with about 2 miles paved pedestrian trail with multiple fitness station loops around and up and down a hilly area mainly covered with grass with relatively few scattered trees.  There are 3 ponds/lakes where you can fish but have also to release. There are creeks too. There is a children play ground and multiple picnic areas. Parking lot is relatively large and adequate.

It is 0.7 Miles from the large parking lot up hill to the overlook. Waking uphill is not very easy but not really difficult either. You get rewarded with magnificent 360 degrees views of surrounding valleys and mountains including Mt Mitchell which is roughly 14 to 15 miles drive away.
Do not miss the trail if traveling along Blue Ridge Parkway.

Very beautiful falls not far from Cherokee on edge of Great Smokey Mountains National Park. You have to climb long stairs to get there which could be difficult for people with health problems.
Parking area not large, but parking is free. Distance from parking to falls is about 0.4 Miles.
Do not miss it if in Great Smokeys/Cherokee.

It is the Great Smoky Mountains National Park Visitor Center coming from Cherokee. Nice building, with history exhibit, and museum. Parking lot is large.
More interesting is the open field right to center where you can see large number of elks, but possibly other wild animals. There is also a trail behind the center.

Beautiful park in north-east Atlanta within the perimeter with good size lake and looping trail shaded by trees around the lake. There pedestrian bridges along the way. On edge of the trail there picnic areas, and playing ground. Across the street there are sport facilities.
Parking is free.

You get to it through a short loop of Georgia Route 52. You park in small parking area on side of the oneway road then climb the trail to top of the hill and enjoy a fascinating almost 360° view of mountains and valleys. Do not miss it if going to Fort Mountain State Park.

The trail is roughly 1.5 Miles from parking area up the Pine Mountain to the top where the views are very beautiful. It is on strenuous side of a hike but beautiful and not very difficult.  The parking area is very close to exit 288 from I-75 north.

Nice historic park in center of Savannah/Historic District with live oak trees, and the famous fountain with coffee shop in the park.
Across the street is the Law School with the famous Candler Oak tree in yard (Presumed to be 300 years old)
This is a small park for kayaking with play ground between Roswell Riverwalk Trail and Chattahoochee river  with few benches to sit down and admire surrounding nature
Ruins of historic mill on Nickajack Creek close to the end of Heritage Park trail. From the area you walk up to join Silver Comet Trail in Smyrna. Nice place.
Deerlick Gap Overlook is not very far from Little Switzerland on Blue Ridge Parkway with beautiful views of mountains and valleys with adequate parking.
Relatively small county park in Smyrna with baseball and tennis fields. Not big enough for hiking. Parking adequate and free.

My husband and I's first time visiting the Statue of Liberty even though we have been to NYC so many times! We were blessed to have gotten Pedestal tickets for the Statue of Liberty the day before we went! Normall Crown tickets are booked out 3 months ahead and Pedestal tickets are weeks ahead. We booked online so we skipped the long ticket line and the regular line at the cruise port, and we went through security within 5 minutes. When we got onto the island for the statue, we got lockers to put our bag in for 25 cents, then went up to the pedestal. The view of NYC is very nice from up there, and on the lowest level of the pedestal you get to take PERFECT photos of the statue of liberty up close behind you. It's well worth the price to get pedestal tickets compared to just reserved tickets that gets you onto the island. I heard that the crown tickets get you all the way up to the top of the crown of the statue's head but photos from up there are not great because you only get to see through small windows.

I came here for Vacation and purchased Seaquarium tickets through Miami Go Card. I love animals so I enjoyed my time here. I saw the dolphin show, sea lion and seal show, and the killer whale and dolphin show. I visited the Mangrove Forest and saw the sea turtles, saw the two manatees, and fed the seals at the feeding area (extra $5 per fish bag). I petted the sharks near the entrance and petted the stingrays near the dolphin stadium. The sea lion and seal show was my favorite! The killer whale and dolphin show is great, but if you sit in the front four rows you will DEFINITELY get wet each time the killer whale jumps up! I wouldn't eat here since the restaurants charge very expensive food. We spent 3 hours here then left for lunch.

My husband and I came to Miami for vacation in January 2019 and had high expectation for the beach. We were quite disappointed.

The Good - Lummus Park has a nice green area with bathroom facilities and places to park your bike or rent a bike to explore South Beach. Also, there are trash cans everywhere which encourage people to throw away their trash
The Bad - the beach was not good. We care about swimming in the ocean and there's too much seaweed on the beach and in the water. I was not encouraged to walk into the water and be covered in seaweed. We did lie down on the beach to enjoy the sun and breeze, but that's the highlight of the beach.

I have been here several times to watch the July 4th fireworks. It used to be not as croweded and the view would be great. But this year it was so crowded I could barely see the fireworks, I had to stand on a railing. Also, the park stopped maintaining the trees on the hillside, and a lot of the trees were blocking people's view of the fireworks. They should trim them before they go out of hand. There is a building facility here with bathrooms and a rooftop, you can rent that out for events. Parking here is non-existent, only a few spots. But if you come during the day it's very quite and the daytime view of the city is still nice.

We were on vacation in January 2019 and came to Key West. We purchased the tandum parasailing for $85 online. It was one of the best experiences of my life! My husband and I have been waiting to parasail for a long time and this was so amazing! It was so peaceful when we were sailing in the sky. The staff were very friendly, and you can pay an extra $45 for photos. The photos taken by the staff were great, and they even gave us a video of us being lowered into the water. Please note, the parasailing booth is on the other end of the beach where the boat is docked, not at this location. (Sunset Watersports have two huts!)

It was a fun experience, but I wish it was a longer ride and they did more tricks. We sat in the front of the boat and we did get wet but not too much to be honest. The captain did a few boat tricks, then took us out to two islands and showed us the different rich houses (Will Smith, Elizabeth Taylor, Ricky Martin, famous CEOs, etc). Then we came back into the harbor and the captain did a few more boat tricks, and that was it. It was half boat tour, half thrill tricks. But it was a nice boat ride. I would wear a sweater if you can't handle the sea breeze.

My family flew here to visit a few days. It was thunder-storming for most of our trip, but the river walk was still beautiful and nice to walk along while the rain stopped. The boats sailing along, the many restaurants and gift shops, the ducks swimming around, and the walk bridges over the river, it is a pretty romantic and historical place to be at. My only complaint is the trash. I saw a lot of trash in the river, and some people trying to pick it up. But I wish the tourists and local residents are more considerate with keeping the river clean.

I went on a sightseeing cruise. It wasn't bad. The guide gave a lot of useful information about Pittsburgh and pointed out the different buildings downtown, and talked about the three rivers. However, I wish they offer free water or drinks on the sightseeing cruise since it wasn't a short cruising experience. I also knew a lot about Pittsburgh already so I was quite bored. But the boat ride was okay, mingled with my co-workers, and the breeze was nice. I think I would check out the dinner cruise next time.

They call it the great American pass time for a good reason. My husband and I love coming here to watch the game, eat food and relax. The crab fries are our favorite food here! I usually get free tickets to come to baseball games. I usually sit in the upper-most section, but it's okay though. The stadium's restrooms are usually clean, and the restaurants are plentiful. The food is not cheap... a small bowl of ice cream was more than $6! Sometimes they have deals... for instance they have $1 hotdog days.

This beach is not well advertised but it's not a bad beach! If you want to walk your dog at the beach or do windsurfing, this is the place to be! There's a lot of parking, there's bathroom facilities, and there's a few food stands if you are hungry. My concern with this beach is there's some seaweed and trash in the water, but not too horrible. The water here is pretty shallow so you can walk out into the sea for many feet and the water still doesn't reach your waist yet.

I have visited many lighthouses, and this is VERY NICE! We came on a sunny clear sky day, and the view from the top was beautiful! You can seen far into the ocean, the long beach, and the Miami city skyline. If you are afraid of heights, I would hold on tight when you get to the top! A volunteer stands at the entrance to keep count because only around 10-15 people can be at the top of the tower at the same time. This is a must-see when you come to this State Park.

We stopped by Ohio Pyle on the way back to Pittsburgh. It was a much-needed rest stop!! It ois very peaceful and quiet here, and the air is so fresh I have a cold and I didn't even once cough or blow my nose during the hour we were here! We went to the observation deck to take some pictures, then we drove cross the bridge and parked to hike along the river and to the rocks at the river. My husband and I thoroughly enjoyed this peaceful moment in the wilderness!

My husband and I came here for a two-day vacation. It was amazing! Kayaking in the lake was fun and affordable. There are at least 12 beaches along the coast, all of them equally beautiful. There's a historical lighthouse for you to visit too. We will definitely come back again!

Update - we came back for a second time this past weekend, and we had a wonderful experience. This time, we finally was abke to climb the lighthouse and get a nice view!

I came here to fulfill a requirement for my art course at University of Pittsburgh. I can see why Andy Warhol is hailed to be a great artist... his sense of style and wild imagination is impressive. However, I didn't particularly understood some of his artwork (too confusing) and there was a "naked" section that I was uncomfortable with. I also don't particularly like his artwork. But hey, I still came and walked around!

Beautiful place! A great place for me and my husband to take pictures, sit at the edge of the river, take a jog, or sit at the fountain. This is the best place to see fireworks over the river. If you come here early you can get a spot on the river to watch the fireworks. Also, this is a place that hosts many festivals on the lawn area, with tents that sells different food and merchandise and a music stage.

This is literally a neighborhood park. I live two streets away. You wouldn't know about this park unless you live around here. It's a pretty quiet park. There's the playground on one side, the baseball field in the middle, and the basketball field on the other side with a lot of parking there. Also, a police car usually parks next to the playground, probably for their break time or security for the kids.

Best view of the city is on Mt. Washington! You can get a nice view of the city during the day, but at night it's the most beautiful! It's also a great place to see fireworks, but it gets very crowded here on 4th of July and it's hard to find street parking here, so come very early to get a good spot. Make sure you come on a warm and less windy day to see the view.

Hubby and I came here to do rock climbing and the rope obstacle. Kids taller than 48 inches can participate, but adults can still have fun doing them. It was a hot day (over 90 degrees) so it was nice to do these things indoors, and admission to the museum and parking were affordable. I definitely recommend coming here.

This is our second time ice skating here.

Pro - Free entry for active military personnel plus one other person, a cute little pond to ice skake in, they offer blue seals for an additional $15 to put your child on it and skate the child around
Con - overpriced, not enough benches for people to rest on

I really liked this submarine tour. this is definitely one of the best highlights of the science museum. It's part of general mission, or pay $7 if you just want to visit the submarine. I have never been inside a submarine, so it was fascinating to see and learn how people live in a submarine.

When I was a kid I visited the science museum often and never got tired of it. As I got older I got more interested in the arts, so I visited the art museum more often. Let's be honest, it's a very small Museum. I have visited the museum coutless times, and I haven't noticed much change.

My husband and I came to Erie for a two-week vacation. Splash Lagoon was fun! We enjoyed ourselves as adults. Only problem is price. We had a military discount due to my husband being a veteran, but regular price to enter is pretty expensive.

I learn so much history of different cultures and civilizations at this museum, and their jewelry area is amazing to be in (my mom loves looking at diamonds in that area). Admission price is not cheap though.
Not a bad park. We came here for a graduation party. The shelter that was for the party had a lot of seating and protected us from the rain.
Great view, I kid you not! My husband and I always enjoy walking along Mt. Washington and enjoy the view.

Hi there, I have summarised about the Trinity park for the first time visitors ,hope its helpful.

* Nice trail park located very close to I-35 and is located in Forthworth Downtown. Nearby attractions if you are planning for a day are Forthworth Water gardens/Sundance square & Forthworth Stockyards.
* Do carry water bottles as there are not much water fountains nearby
*Ample parking is available but weekends and holidays might get crowded so arrive early to grab a spot.
*Kindly be courteous to birds and others and don't overfeed them. If you wanna take pic with ducks, stay grounded near the pond ,the ducks shall cross by.
*Biking trails are available around the river park
*There's an sot where you can cross the Trinity river through rocks, extend caution as some of them are slippery.

Hope you have nice time around the park.#HappyTrails

Most beautiful park in Austin located on banks of Colorado river. The location is so serene and has an separate camping location for RV & trailers.

The park is pet-friendly and has space for entertaining the pets. Trash cans were kept at every corner of the park to dispose pet wastes.

Park is also good for biking/walking and there are tables for dine-in area along with family.
Kids shall definitely be enjoying this park and has wide playing area along the shores.

Camping needs a permit beforehand but for a causal visit, you can take-in receipt at park entrance. Currently only credit cards are accepted and no cash are accepted.
I have attached the park pics for reference. Have a happy and safe family time. #HappyVacation

An awesome park near the Orlando downtown. Overlook view of the lake is most recommended. The reception lady so helpful in guiding us the garden map and here shall walkthrough important areas of garden in case of time shortage.

If you have lot of time in hand, you can view the park for entire day and rose garden & camelia areas are good for photo shoot.
If you have 4hrs or less, then first visit Rose garden ,then the camelias ,floral clock, butterfly garden, idea garden ,bamboo garden and later based on timeline you can see marriage hall, gazebo n vegetable garden

If you have recently moved to Austin or staying in Downtown on a temporary visit then it's a must see location in Austin. A well maintained park with Ducks and Pigeon in their natural environment looks beautiful.
There's an walk stroll along the lake with a shade to spend a good family time. There's also a children's park near the lake for kids.
Parkings are always crowded in the weekend. Paid parking is available near the shores Mon-Sat. Neat Restroom is located in the parking area.#HappyVisiting

Beautiful trail located next to Austin downtown.Its an hidden gem located within the Austin city to feel the nature.I have attached the seren location of the trail so that you can get the feel of the place. I has an ample parking space and has an attached dog park. You can also bring your kids to the trail and have a walk. Right now the trail is very hot and dry in summer but i feel the streams will be flowing once the rain showers fall over. Kick off your couch and hit a trail. #HappyTrailing

This place has a  great historic significance. Its always crowded and if you planning to visit other destinations,make sure you arrive early in the morning and plan to visit this place first.
They host light shows in the evening to explain the great war that happened in same location.Also next to Alamo is the San Antonio hop on- hop off bus tour is located where you can purchase a bus tour around the city.
Lot of malls and restaurant are located nearby Alamo to grab a quick bite.

Great outdoor park located on a island formed by Tom Miller dam. The most bike trail is from Redbud isle to Mount Bonnell. You can view the curves and the beauty of Colorado river all along amd have coffee @ Mozart's on the way. You have an dedicated bike trail and dog park inside the park. Don't miss the view at the rear end of the park. Many ppl prefer fishing and boating as well in the park. Parking is bit limited so plan your timings on the off-season or on non-peak timing

Important landmark in Florida where people come from all places to get a glimpse of this place.
You need to travel over 2hrs from mainland and is single lane(prone to delays). Our travel time grew over 40mins from original time due to traffic. And once you cross over plantation key, there are no restaurants/cafe to stop over. Better finish your food in Key largo before proceeding to key west.

Lighthouse is another attraction nearby if you an extra time to spare.

One of the happening places in Austin. It has an high tower and a grand arcade to watch the F1 formula race. On the off-season you can rent the car in the race track on hourly basis. The place is located bit far from Austin city near the Airport(15mins from Airport). Has a huge parking location so never have to worry if arrived late.

In holiday season they host lighting festival each year. Attached the pics from year 2020 celebration.

Awesome park located in the Austin downtown.
There are two parking lot is located -one near the Vic Mathias shore & other at Douglas Art center but both of them gets filled up in weekends/holidays.
Plan a bit early if you planned to explore the park. Summers are very hard here,make sure you stay hydrated while in park. Cars aren't allowed inside the park beyond the parking lot.Sunset at South Congress is another attraction nearby

Nice park located in the Georgetown , close to I-35(10 mins from the Interstate) . It has an awesome lake view and a vast trail of over 5miles around the Lake George town. The park operates from Sunrise to Sunset. Arrive early to grab a parking space as the parking is limited. Additional parking can be availed near Crockett Gardens rd adjacent to the park. It has reserved Parking space for wheelchair accessible. #HappyTrails

Nice small park located on the side of the Lampasas main road.
Its located on the banks of lampasas river(/stream) ,has a small walking bridge and hosts couple of ducks roaming inside the park.
Its a good place to spend family time with kids and is currently decorated with Christmas lights for holiday season
No restrooms available within the park.
Wheelchair accessible parking is available within the park.#Happyvacation

Awesome park located in the Colorado river basin. This park located in the downstream of the Mansfield Dam and river takes in 180 degree turn in front of this park(attached pic). Park is very seculded and is good for a walk or cycling. They have lot of benches to sit over and have a snack/meal at the river park.Please avoid visiting in late evening as the park isn't illuminated well.

Its a very small park i would say situated close to Galveston beach. Its mainly aimed for kids and teens. Parking is available right in front of pier payable by Parkmobile app.
Parking could be limited in the weekends and towing is strictly enforced at all.
Fill your water/refreshments before entering beach as shops are bit far to reach. Nice place to spend for an evening beach walk

A calm & lovely place in Austin. We spotted few deers on way to dam.
As of Mar1,2020 the fees has been set to $5 per person. Please carry cash or cheque only(cards not accepted). Had an hour walk and felt so peaceful n alone.
Few people got in boats in their trailers and were cooking barbeque along the shore.
Good place to lookout for potluck or family gathering

Landmark location for every tourists & people coming to Austin. Its an emotion to get photographed in front of this symbol. Its located very close to downtown with other attractions (6th street and capitol is minutes away from this place). Its also located very close to Austin railway station. #HappyVisiting

Nice walking place close to south congress and zilker metro park.
You can also kayak in Rowing dock nearby or can stroll with your dog in the evening.
The jogging trail leads all the way till lady bird lake.
This walking lane is separate from road traffic so no fear of crossing lanes as well.

Loved the park in front of Miami beach. It so lively in the evening with the Art Deco shows put up.
Parking is bit of difficult here and you need to advance bit far.
Parkmymobile app was so handy in spotting an parking. A evening shall be enough to spend a nice time over the park

Awesome park near Southwest Austin near Mansfield Dam. The water is currently low due to summer but its refreshing to walk on the park sideways parallel to the dam spillway.Its a very small park compared to other parks in Austin but nice to spend sunset evening at the park

Nice Hindu Temple located on a hillock near Bandera road. The road splitting from main road towards temple is short steep. Drive cautiously while at night. Parking is very wide.
Temple is calm and peaceful. We can also do pradhakshana after darshan.
Have a nice darshan

Currently this place is closed and the public cant climb over the graffiti park.
Also they have placed a guard to watch out for people trying to paint the walls. Better to skip this location to avoid disappointment
Its located on the awesome trail in the downtown Austin. Parking lot is available next to the trail for car/bike parking. Might get hot during summers ,do carry the water bottles.#HappyTrails

Water is good to bath only during spring/fall and is seasonal. During summers its very dry n pond looks dirty with stagnant water.
Good place to place with family/dogs

Nice lake shore nearby to NASA. Sunset/sunrise is so visit to visit there.
You can feed the sea gulls or enjoy the fishing on the lake shore
If you have an extra day in Houston, if you can visit swami narayan temple. Great to visit for clicking pics

This was our 4th time visiting! One of my favorite places on the world! The first three times we took the scenic drive up,  ate lunch and played around at the top,  amd then drove back down. (Two of those times we also climbed down and up the dune.) THIS TIME we boated over to the bottom of Sleeping Bear from Frankfort.  I thought it was awesome to see that dune from the perspective of the water. When we first approached in the boat I thought it may have been closed because I didn't see any people. We had to get pretty close to see people because they were so small! It was wonderful to climb up (the other adults in our party only went part of the way up) as far as you want and then run back down. If you approach from the water, you don't have to climb the whole thing! By the way, I'm not going to downplay the seriousness of that climb,  but I think there used to be a sign there that said it would take like 3 hours or something?  For perspective, my 9 year old takes about 15 minutes.  I am not an exercise person (but I'm not obese) and it takes me about 25 minutes. The view from top (or bottom!) is definitely worth it of you're in decent health condition.  Bring your camera and a water bottle. (This time we did it without water bottles.... not a smart idea but we made it.)
If you have long toe nails or finger nails, you might want to clip them short. The part that always hurts me the most climbing that dune is toes! I do it barefoot amd crawl like a bear, very slow and steady. But I've seen people use hiking boots and a walking stick. There are a lot of rocks in the sand until you're almost at the top.

I visited yesterday with my kids - the first time I've been there in 18 years. Much has changed... I used to go one Saturday every August as a teenager and it was NOT crowded. I couldn't believe how crowded it was yesterday, like a Florida beach on spring break.  It took us 30 minutes to get the 1.5 miles from the visitors center to the parking lot. We had to wait in line that long to pay our $7.00 to get in the park. We were directed to the west beach parking lot, but our friends had already arrived and settled on the far east end, so we had quite a haul over there with baby and cooler, etc.
I was not a fan of all the new touristy stuff like food trucks and stands of souvenirs. The loudspeaker was annoying. I just wanted to come to a natural beach. I don't think they had lifeguards 18 years ago, either.
All that being said, it's still very beautiful,  and if you do go far to the east end like my friend did, you get out of the crowd a little bit. The restroom facilities are large and nice. It looks like they're doing some construction on the pavilion?
The moral for me is, don't ever go on a weekend again, and don't haul so many heavy things with me. I'd like the try out other beaches in the area as well.

This hike has been on my list for 3 years and finally got to do it. I thought it would be more sandy, but 95% was woods and dirt.  Pretty easy hike. Good for a hot day because it's all shady. The views were wonderful and we loved playing on the beach for 10 minutes before completing the 2nd half of the hike. We did it about 30 minutes before sunset and the woods were getting dark-ish. There was a fair amount of poison ivy so stay in the middle of the path if you get itchy! A small parking area, but it wasn't filled. I don't think it's a super high trafficked hike. The trails were very well marked.

I brought my children here today. I think the museum was very clean and very well done. There was such a large collection of memorabilia. I think if someone was really into high school basketball or actually played high school ball themselves,  it would have meant much more to them. I did enjoy the movie at the beginning and especially the little exhibit about the very beginning of basketball with Naismith and Crawforsdsville. The peach basket and oldest basketball, etc. I also particularly enjoyed the photography exhibit. I think the kids and spent about an hour and a half here.

This is actually our second time at BH. Several years ago we beached the Gulf Side and this time the Atlantic. It cost 10.50 for our family of 5 to enter. The beach was just beautiful that day. Plenty of sand for everyone. Had fun finding mini shells and coral remnants. Ample parking, gift shop, cafe, restrooms. Take a walk to the top of the old bridge. We wanted to do the nature center but the worker had to leave early that night for vacation the next day. Found a large conch with a crab and a small shell with a living creature as well.

This was our 3rd or 4th trip here. The landscaping is absolutely beautiful. The animal ride is always super fun. If you go, you have to be ready for an easy relaxing day of strolling around. Everything is pretty spread out. Not a great place for someone who has a hard time walking. There are only two restrooms on the property so when little kids have to go, you have to walk a long way to get there. I feel like the price is very reasonable. Wear sunscreen on a sunny day! A few different picnic locations, so bring a sack lunch!

We arrived here about 330 PM with approx. 2 hours before sunset. The fort was honestly pretty boring-I would reccomend going on the daily tour. I'm sure it would be interesting if someone explained everything.
We went out the the beach to hang out for a couple hours. Nice little cafe. Picnic tables throughout. I looooove the pine trees on the beach. It was so picturesque. The beach itself it of course pretty rocky except directly down by the water. We watched the sunset and sailboat. Watched a cruise ship depart.

This was a fantastic walk/hike. Super easy to get to the overlook. Benches to rest about every tenth mile I would say. The Overloom isn't super great, though, so I'd you're not physically impaired, definitely take the trip all the way up to Baldy. The Baldy hike was not physically exhausting by any means but about the last tenth mile you do have to walk up and down sand.  The view is fantastic for sure. I went once on a clear day and once on a cloudy day.

I went here a couple years ago and plan to go back. We stayed in a 6 person cabin.... 5 of us. My mom had her own room and the kids and I bunked. We loved being right on the lake. My mom took the kids fishing and we took a great hike. Saw a gigantic black snake curled around the trunk of a tree. That was a highlight for sure. Cheap, nice lodging. The little cabin was nice for simple food prep. Wish I had some pictures to post but they're on an old phone.

This was a fun place! I had never heard if it until this year. We brought our youth group and our family and everyone found something fun to do. It was pretty well kept up for being so old. Lots of space to spread out, didn't feel crowded, even on a Saturday.  I loved the surrounding farm animals and gardens! Areas of shade and sun, grass and sand. Food concessions were VERY limited.

We love this little town and beach area. 4 stars only because the sand isn't quite as nice as Elberta or Frankfort. There is a public restroom, playground, fishing dock, picnic tables, shade trees, and not far from town if you want to walk and get lunch or coffee. Parking spaces are not super hard to find. We keep coming back, even though we did get swimmer's itch in 2017.
likes: Public facilities (restroom, playground, fishing dock, picnic tables)

reviews_attraction.text: It was really,  really crowded after we stopped for lunch, but overall a super fun day anyway. We got to link 19 from our group together and that's the best. We tubed for 3 hours.  It's nice that it's small enough that you don't feel like you're going to lose your kids and can give them some independence.  Decent lodge and food.

This was such a sweet little zoo!! Perfect for little kids. We loved the wallabies and the petting zoo and the butterflies the best. I thought the train ticket prices were a bit much. We spent about 2 hours here. I'd go back with my little kids, probably not big ones.

Very expansive park. Lots of space to play soccer, throw frisbee, birdwatch, walk, take a stroller, fish. There were two playgrounds, a lighthouse, a cafe. The splash pad was out of order for repairs, so my kids were a little disappointed.

We visited the ruins, the nature center, the playground , and the trails. Kids ages 1 through 11 and they loved it. Spent about 3.5 hours but could have stayed longer if the weather was just a bit warmer.
Clear water. Beautiful. We swam, walked the paths, ate concessions. Wonderful place to lazily pass the day. Ample parking and restrooms were decent. Must have mask inside concession building.
We had a family reunion here and it was a great little space. The kids loved playing in the creek behind and the walking trail was fabulous! Good parking.
Came here for Homeschool Jamboree.  I thought the nature centers weren't as good as others I've visited. A big building without a lot of substance.
Good place to get maps and restroom break,  but kind of a large building that didn't have much in it. The paintings outside were cool.
This was a nice tour, lasted 45 minutes. I can't say I really loved it or would go back, but I'm not a huge wolf fan, either.
A really nice place to walk around. Walk around the lake with a stroller,  lots of wildlife,  and then stop at Starbucks!
We used the Walker boat ramp,  which was very nice (had a bathroom), and enjoyed the lake for the day. Beautiful lake.
We did it all! Ruins, nature center, playground, and trails! I brought kids ages 1-11 and they all loved it!
Without a doubt you have to stop here for a picture but be prepared to wait in line and fight traffic.
Did the Pierce Stocking drive while it was open for a few days in Aug.  2020. Wasn't crowded at all!

Temple in mountains is the best. I stayed here with family and family friends for a night and it was good experience. We had breakfast included with stay and it was decent for this location. During peak times and want to see colors, this is one of the best place to stay as well. Houses are good but single bathrooms so be aware of them. Booking and communications will be a challenge as mostly no phone signal. Owner need to be available at landline or will callback with voice mail.

This place is beautiful. Especially ocean drive. Started walking from south point pier. 2 different experiences on ocean drive walk. Right side is of the street with looking at buildings and ocean side trees. Left side of the street restaurants with variety of food and drinks. Walk 2 sides of the road to experience the difference. Parking is tough. Park elsewhere and use free trolleys.

Beautiful park for joggers and kids. Evening times are really good. Tennis courts are busy most of the times, nice kids play area and facilities. There is cricket ground with lights but not seen much of cricket games here.  It’s mostly used for family, kids oriented activities . Bit crowded sometimes.
Update: ongoing icc cricket tournament is encouraging for cricket.

It’s natural beauty with trails, water falls, pond and more. Visitor center staff was very helpful. Hanging rock trail is good and it’s worth going to the rock for nice view.  This trail is 1.3 miles long and has about 360 steps at the end.  There is picnic area close to visitor center. There are other places to see depends on time and interest.

Good place for walking and some picnic spots.  Nice Small lake with bridge into it. Can take nice pictures from there. There is a little park area where some are playing and relaxing. The trails are okay and have wet patches on the way. Not clean. This park can be improved more so can attract more visitors as it is in nice location.

This is adjacent to world trade center area which is no more now. The deck is crowed  and hard to get place for taking pictures. you need to wait for long or squeeze in somewhere. spend more time to get better chances. Best time to visit is in the evening, so you can see day view and night view. no limit to time to stay there.

It’s very nice place for walking, jogging and boating. There is a bridge on water connecting 2 sides. There are few types of boats to suite one, two , three, and four people including standup boards. I have seen more standup boards are being rented at my visit. There are shelters too. Parking available 2 sides.

There are no parking or entrance fees. There is lot of parking space. Center has museum, rest rooms and entrance to fort. Museum is smelly but can understand. You can donate if you want to. Fort rooms are air conditioned. Overall it’s worth a visit if you are in that area. It has beach as well.

Its beautiful park with oak trees. We had pleasant walk in the morning. Fountain is the beautiful. There are places to sit and relax .Parking was easy in the Sunday morning and its free. There was a marriage event at fountain. There are several tennis courts within the park.

It’s very good park. It has 5 kids tennis courts, 1 normal, nice and big play area, basketball and baseball. Kids play area mostly made of wooden. Place to sit when kids are playing     Or can walk around . It is designed to cover most of the things in small area. Well done.

As the other reviews says the view is partial and can see only take off.  It has kids play area and place to sit and eat. Better to go there on peak time to see more flights, otherwise you have to wait for long. I wish there is one to cover landing area as well.

It's hidden gem and must visit place in spring. Visited in April 1st week and there are beautiful flowers. You will finish the park just like that looking around. Parking is small inside but there is long road side parking. I tried to capture most of pictures.

The beach is very nice and there is a free parking available. This beach seem to be designed for the hotels as i had to enter through private parking. There was no changing room and bath room. so be aware of it. There was a pub event with music at beach.

Most of them are Soccer fields and also there is a cricket ground. Most of the times you see someone playing . The internal roads and parking lots can be improved. Nice greenery..
soccer fields are seem to be maintained regularly so that’s great.

Best time is to visit during spring. Beautiful tulip flowers. Getting parking at peak times is difficult but if you are ready to walk there are options.  Can take good pics and have long walks around . Garden staff are helpful and no issues.

Too much crowded, no easy parking, hard to get solo photos avoiding crowds especially during holidays. There is small beach close by in walking distance and it is too crowded too. Location is nice. Best option is to park elsewhere and walk.

Main items here are mini golf court and skating area. Mini golf is paid $5 per person. Others are free. There is splash pad , basket ball court, store, and kids swing area. It seem to be targeted for locals than visitors.

Nice community park . It has 2 pickle ball courts, big basketball court, kids playing area, walking trail can be used for bicycling, sand pit. Small park with modern facilities. it’s quite busy at times. Overall good.
I went to this park on 5th July for fireworks event. Surprisingly it’s good. Plenty of space for such big events. It was beautiful evening and memorable. Very close view to see fireworks display.
It has 6 tennis courts with lights and basketball courts. When I went there for playing tennis, I was told that these courts are reserved. I got one after sometime. Limited parking.
Nice little park and trails for walking, jogging and bicycling. The trail from park towards town hall drive extends to another 1.2 miles behind neighborhood houses.
Beautiful park in the center of city. Kids play area, picnic spots. free parking. it  may be hard to find parking at a times. good place for walking and relaxing..
It’s very nice beach having facilities. Paid parking $2/hr any time 24/7.  There are few shops and bathrooms at pier. Parking may be difficult at times.
The only beach in key west with free parking and little big. There is another small one close to south most point but very small. Had good time.
This year no sunflowers planted may be due to covid19. Its empty land. But open fields around are used for picnic, relaxing etc..

Enjoyable Way to spend a Day. We thoroughly enjoyed the boat ride over to the island.  This was not the usual boat they use for the trip but it served the purpose. It was very scenic. The weather in a.m. and during day was sunny so we had wonderful views along the trip. It took about 45 minutes. We had opted for the tour with guide. You can rent a golf cart and do your own tour. We had time for a tasty lunch at the Old Daufuskie Crab House. Don't expect a fancy place but do expect excellent seafood.  We sat outside under umbrellas. It was delightful. We understand that on certain times of the week they have live music. We then met our guide at General Store.  The General Store had a lot of basics plus some souvenirs. Wish they had some of the Gullah related arts & crafts. They did have some beautiful t-shirts.  The tour guide was very friendly & informative. The speaker system on bus was excellent. We visited a number of locations which I so enjoyed.   The Gullah history is interesting as well as the history of the island. You also got to see how the island is doing today.  We got to see the old school house & the Mary Fields School along with a beautiful old church.  Bloody Point Lighthouse tour of grounds, history (nice film) & info on the very tiny winery was enjoyable. We had a couple of people who wanted to see the pottery & iron fish gallery but that was not included. We got back with minutes to spare for our rainy trip back to Hilton Head. We did get to see 3 Dolphin on way back. Trip back uncomfortable & cold due to the wind and rain & the boat is not enclosed (remember this boat temporary).  Pick a nice day without rain predictions.  Enjoyed the people who ran the tour. All were friendly & information. The sound system on the boat they were using could not be heard if you were in the back of boat by motors. Go & enjoy being taken back in time.
dislikes: Exclusion of pottery & iron fish gallery
Uncomfortable return trip due to weather

reviews_attraction.text: Nice science & history museum. The history behind the Secret City & how what happened here affected the entire world. Watched 2 very informative movies. Participated in a few experiments with a very educated docent. Kids would enjoy them. The museum is laid out well. The first part about what happened when it was decided Oak Ridge would play a large part in the Manhattan Project. Very informative as to how it affected the community, how it was built & the such.  Lots of artifacts & great pictures. Amazingly few people working here then even knew what they were working with or building toward other than it was top secret and something that might help win WW2.  The next part of exhibit goes into more detail of what was happening & how the science of what exactly they were making. There is another room where u can "play" with experiments & it actually was pretty amazing & a lot of fun. If u want to see this original museum go now as I understand they are cutting the size down dramatically from I believe around 55,000 sq. ft. to around 15,000 (could be a tad bit off here)  They are moving the museum to a former store front (Sears) near the J.C. Penny store in town. If you have kids or grandchildren or just curious yourself I'd take a few hours & go. You won't be sorry.  Plus the area is nice. A couple of good restaurants in area Soup Kitchen and Calhouns on the lake. Make it a day I am sure you will have a lot to talk about after!

Went to the 2nd Annual Butterfly Festival here. I had never been before. Such a beautiful area. Lots of trees, flowers and other types of plants abound. Stunningly beautiful place.  They have a lovely air conditioned auditorium. There were 2 excellent speakers that I so enjoyed. 1 spoke about flowers & plants to attract butterfly. The other spoke about the various types of butterfly & moths in the area. They had some UT students working with kids in an excellent manner. The children were having so much fun. They had 2 Monarch butterfly releases which the children & adults loved. I got a couple of plants to attract more butterflies. I also got some honey that tasted delicious. I like to purchase my honey from local beekeepers. Also got a dish made from a leaf that u put a bit of sand in & dampen it with water and set on a rock for the butterflies. You also could put a bit of banana peel or orange rind.  I am signing up for 2 events coming up. There were other vendors there too.  Very nice place. It is not too far from Calhouns on the Lake so I meandered over there for a lovely late lunch.

Fabulous park. I went for the first time today and it was a special morning "learning about dragon flys".  There were about 9 of us and our guide & instructor Mark.  You can go to this park anytime and u don't need to wait for a class. There is no admission fee. Lots of paths to walk on and also paved biking trail to river. There is also a boat ramp. There were a few kayaks & canoes. Scenery beautiful. While you do have views of mountains in distance this more woods, meadows, ponds and river. Lots of various flowers, birds, insects, butterflies, Dragon flys and the such. Kids found some frogs and were very excited.  You can go on their web page for dates of various events. There were some benches at more scenic spots.  I can't wait to go back.  We are so lucky to have this park in East TN.

Absolutely beautiful gorge, falls & interpretative building.  The building you walk in to get to trails is stunning. What a great job. We found the employees knowledgeable. There was a nice store,  There is a nice easy walking ramp to exhibits prior to you walking outside. The movie on the gorges history well done. There were many exhibits to view. Take the time to view them. There was a number of young men asking about swimming and it was allowed. We did not see all the falls. I believe there are six. We did walk to a number of them Just spectacular. The beauty of this area amazing. You do need some stamina to walk the full area. It was very hot & humid so we only walked half.  There was a small parking fee. No Other charges.

Floridians fortunate to have this great preserve. I went 2 x this week and each time saw so much wildlife plus such varied vegetation all in one place. The swamp land & lake areas had many alligators, raccoons scurrying about & a wide variety of birds from  egrets, herons, ducks, moor hens, anihanga, pleated woodpeckers & more.  Such beauty in 1 location. There is a lot of info available on the various trees and vegetation. I believes the various trails exceed 3 miles. There is an area where they care for injured birds of prey. Amazing opportunity to see them up close. Small gift shop with restrooms & some educational displays. $3 admission to walk trails very reasonable.

Fsbulous preserve. Lots of hiking paths and done are paved. Beautiful stunning views of bays & inlets. Lots of birds, fish and other wildlife. Great viewing area that is elevated.  Walk along mangroves that make you feel you are far away from city hustle.  There is a put in for kayaks & canoes. You can even rent. When driving in look for the ospery nests & these large birds. Nice visitor center. It is not open every day so you may want to check web page. I have taken a camer a hike and also attended an archaeology seminar here. There is a rest room close to visitor center. Great places along the paths to sit & contemplate the beauty. Just love it here.

Excellent museum. Everyone should visit especially children & young adults.  The museum is laid out well. It is certainly not as large as 1 in D.C. but it certainly can be an eye opener as to what happened and is still happening in parts of the world we live. You can walk around with a sound piece that you can coordinate to numbers or just walk around & read about what you are seeing.  The museum has many artifacts and many pictures. Go it will be both a sobering & educational experience. The curators have accomplished a lot.  Take at least a 2 hour window of your time to fully appreciate all the exhibits.

We truly enjoyed this lovely center. We first went to the fresh market. Bit disappointed as only 1 vendor actually selling fresh food. It was the off season so we should have realized it would be this way.  There were jewerly, fresh meat, soups , chips salsa vendors.   The museum well done for the size. This is an excellent way to learn more about the history of Hilton Head.  The gardens & grounds lively. We got to see oyster & clam beds. There is a butterfly habitat. We so loved the camellias.  Nice gift shop area too. There are many books available here by local authors.
likes: On-site Activities (Butterfly Habitat, Oyster & Clam Beds)

reviews_attraction.text: I love driving on this Nature Trail. It is wonderful in every season. I went late fall and the views were spectacular. I was so sad to see some of the area that was burnt by the Gatlinburg fires. You could see some new growth & that was so comforting to see. There are a lot of turnouts to stop at. Many old homes and barns to explore . Loads of places to take short hikes.  Some waterfalls & streams along the way too.  Just love the ability to explore. Road in excellent condition. If weather bad the rangers will close road.

Lovely morning at the Spring Garden Event. This 1 of my favorite Spring events here in the area. Was pleased to see it looked like it had grown a bit this year. I happily left with a car full of native plants. Enjoyed the craft & yard items.  People are always very nice. If you haven't taken a tour of mansion you should. It is very informative if a docent accompanies you.  Love the history. Appreciate those trying to keep this bit of history alive. Oh my gosh the strawberries I purchased were amazing. Delicious!

If you are in the Robbinsville area don't miss visiting this national forest. There was a fire a few years ago that downed some large trees and vegetation but the 2 trails are open. There is a lower loop & upper loop. The trails are easy to moderate. It us gorgeous & so peaceful.  I already can't wait to go back. There are restrooms available in parking area. Great place for a hike. Be sure you keep your eyes wide ooen. There is a lot to see. The fungi is amazing but the trees are kings here.

St. Petersburg is so fortunate to have this fabulous museum. The exhibits are amaxing. I love how every few months or so they bring in another creative artist, fashion designer or the like who was a friend of Dali. When they change exhibits they usually tie in with a local restaurant for dinner at restaurant followed by reception at Dali. I believe Saltwater at Sundial is the new exhibit restaurant coming up. Love their gift shop too. Affordable unique gifts.

Great place to put in your kayak or canoe . Not a while lot of parking.  May be tough on weekends. You always could get your boat off or out of your car and then park car at preserve main lot. There are rest rooms here. There is a nice pier for fishing off of or for just some amazing views. There is also a rental service for canoes, kayaks, etc.  There are also marked water paths for your kayak.
Beautiful & stunning easy to find.

Love this area. Lots of nice paths. For those of you who don't like strenuous walks this is for you. Always see wildlife especially birds, owls, fish, dragon flies & butterflies in warmer weather. Lots of flowers in spring& summer. You can put in your kayak or canoe.  Love the trails by the river. They have some festivals during the year. They also do butter fly tagging.  Great place for families.

You have to stop here if you are in Tellico Plains. Just a shirt ride in from main road. Scenery is stunning. The falls are right in front of you. Drive and park and walk the few steps back. So besutiful. There some people picnicking off to side and others in bathing suits attempting to climb lower portion of falls.  Worth the short scenic drive in. Drive further on to see Baby Falls.

First of all makeshift sign on door of visitor center shop with snacks closed even though signage that was permanent had noted it was supposed to be open. The visitor display center was open & the 2 people there were pleasant. Truly not much of a center. Could be updated. You can drive across dam. There is a covered picnic area & some short trails, views are pretty.

Loved this orchard. Nice drive up mountain. Extremely friendly & informative staff. We got apples, some jellies & surprisingly lovely pottery pieces. There was fresh apple pies, Apple cider & alcoholic cider too. Don't leave without having some hot apple donuts. Delicious! They close December for season   so you need to enjoy this place. Best orchard around area.

Wonderful morning at the St. Petersburg Fine Arts Museum. So beautifully done. Right on Beach Drive. Museum had so much to see. There is a lovely museum store too. This exhibition of jewelry & related items truly breathtaking. Tiffany played an important role here. If you enjoy flowers & gardens this will make your eyes pop.

Love to visit area craft centers when traveling. This one is a gem & a bit off the beaten track. The various mediums are displayed nicely. Quite the variety in 2 large rooms. They had some lovely & unique seasonal items too. This center is used for the local community for local events & shows. It is truly worth the stop.

What a great fun place. Amazing scenery and all kinds of activities available. Great place for family bonding. You can hike, zip line, raft, canoe, rope climb, mountain climbing, mountain bike, kayak, fish & more. Great food & friendly staff at all locations. Great camping areas, small hotels and bed & breakfasts.

Wow is all I can say! Beautiful drive today to the lookout area.  The views are beautiful. Probably a week away from full color. Easy parking and a nice level walk. I would say wheelchair accessible.  Seems like you can see forever! The path & overlook paved.

I love this Arboretum! It is so beautiful. Lots of area for walking. There are number of paths & garden areasq. I also love the events they hold. Free parking. Be sure you get a map cause if you don't get you will miss some areas.

Love this park. Steps to down town & right on water.  Great place for a walk or just to sit & enjoy the magnificent scenery. There are benches and there is a sidewalk. Complimentary parking. I even saw dolphins swimming.

Easy to reach these beautiful falls. Walk very short. Interesting history. Take time to read. I believe we actually went through a bookstore to get to path to falls. We actually enjoyed as everyone was nice and helpful.

The staff was friendly, knowledgeable, and professional.  My two kids (12 and 9 years old) were eager yet nervous to try indoor skydiving.  The staff reassured them they'd love it.

Needless to say, they loved the experience!  The instructor assisted them during their session.  Everyone was safe and exited the tunnel with looks of amazement and joy in their faces.

Scheduling, instruction, waivers, suiting up, and completion of the session was easy and efficient.  If you are staying in Pigeon Forge area, this is a great family activity from parents to the children.  It is a great value!

First time visit to the Columbus Zoo.  The temps were 95° and the sun was blazing on Labor Day weekend.

We had a blast!  My kids (11 & 8) loved all the exhibits.  The zoo is expansive and there is plenty to see and do.

The animals were taking it easy the day we visited due to the heat.  We the humans kept ourselves cool with refreshments, ice cream, and myself with a beer.

We did not get a chance to visit the water park or even ask the exhibits for that matter.  There was so much to see with not enough time to see it in one day.

We will definitely return to see the rest.

Fantastic and unique miniature golf experience.  The owners were very friendly, inviting, and grateful for us being there.  They understand there are many entertainment options in the area, so they show their appreciation to each customer.  They aren't a corporate entity, so it was great supporting them.

Golf wise, the course is challenging. It is kept up nicely. There are two different course layouts and neither of them should be approached lightly.

Check out the historic Hillbilly Golf if you are in the area.

It was a beautiful and physically demanding hike in January. The ice dunes were spectacular as the water crashed and splashed.  The path was marked with orange blazes, but the path was impassable at times due to water.  We circumvented these challenges to make our way to the point.  It was a gray, snowy, and windy day with temps in the mid-20's.  I strongly recommend a snow hike for the fitness component.  Be safe and stay off the ice dunes, though.

We've been to many children's museums over the  years: Erie, Philadelphia, Cleveland, Columbus, etc.  Explore and More is a nice facility to spend a couple hours with the family.
