Being that it is one floor, parents don't have to worry about their kids getting out of sight.  My eight year old daughter had a blast. My ten year old son enjoyed the more analytical type of displays. We are eager to visit again when it moves canalside in 2018.

This is a nice, updated playground with some great amenities for kids off all ages to enjoy.  It is close to the picnic pavilion, so it is easy for parents to keep an eye on their kids while sitting at a picnic table.   The playground is a short walk from the shorelines of Lake Erie.  Peaceful, quiet, and safe environment.

Visiting from Erie, PA, for a weekend getaway... There was a lot of activity and energy this weekend.  I believe there was a lantern festival going on.  Food trucks, music, activities for kids... Looked like a great time.  Nice to see communities coming out to support events like this.

Awesome place to visit when you are in key West.  The performances are are incredible.  If you love people watching, this is a place you could spend hours!  The sunsets are a special experience while visiting the southern most key.  Be sure to check this place out during sunset hours.

Nature's playground... swimming,  fishing,  bicycling,  roller blading,  kayaking,  running,  hiking,  sunbathing,  beach play,  sunsets,  bird watching,  boating,  kite flying,  snow shoeing, cross country skiing,  ice fishing,  duck hunting, lighthouse tours... lots to do

Well worth the admission.  We spent over two hours here with a larger group.  Everyone in the group from 41 years old to the 1 year old had an enjoyable time.  There is a lot to see, a lot to interact with, and plenty to do.

Check it out if you are visiting the area.

Each time I visit Key West, I make an effort to get to Higgs Beach.  It is a calm, relaxing place to experience the energy of the ocean.  If you visit the keys, you need to put this location on your list of places to visit.

Many many go kart tracks to choose from.  This location has a family track so kids under 56" are able to drive the karts.  My son is just shy of 56" so this was a popular place for him to be able to drive.

First time visiting.  Beautiful park. Clean facilities. Lots to do here beyond visiting the viaduct.  Walking, hiking, and biking on the trails just to name a few.

Well worth the visit with the family.
The staff & volunteers do a great job with this facility.  There have been some nice upgrades in the attractions over the past several years.  It is a nice children's museum for the size of Erie.
The kids had a blast here with their first trip to the science center. We drove up from Erie. Parking was easy and inexpensive.  The kids enjoyed all the activities and displays.
Great atmosphere to sit outdoors with a glass of wine.  The grounds,  decor,  and feel of the place was relaxing.  Grab a group of friends... this place is a fun place to go.
If you've lived in Erie for any amount of time, you've been to Rainbow Gardens for something.  The place hasn't changed since I was in high school at McDowell in 1996.
Used to sled ride and play here as a kid.  Always seemed like there was unsavory activities going on at night... still seems the same from 30 years ago.
It was fun exploring the covered bridges of Ashtabula County on a bicycle during the Hike and Bike for MS event hosted by Debonne Winery.
It's bridge... rode my bike across the pedestrian sidewalk portion.  The repairs they made over the years made the experience smoother.
Went here as a child... now I bring my children here.  Harborcreek park services does a great job keeping the place clean and updated.
Great landmark to visit whether you are visiting the area or live in town.  Great views from the top of the observation deck.
Great park for the neighborhood. Easy to get to. Kids stay entertained and it is a great place to sled ride in the winter.
Great views.  I visited the pier on my fourth trip to Key West.  I enjoyed venturing off Duval for this sightseeing trip.
A great place to hold a picnic, party, or even a workout.  Plenty of pavilions, picnic tables, playground, and more.

Last week we booked for parasailing; we were the last ride of the day at 5pm. I  really want to give benefit of doubt that crew had a long day or some kind of tough customers before us, so the crew gave us the real hard time at the starting. They started not interested at all to take us. I asked if I could leave stroller anywhere they said it’s my problem and said me to cancel and asked me to come back tomorrow. They were giving all kinds of looks and attitude toward me.  So I went and kind of asked if they had any problem with us and said I will cancel as I don’t like the way they treated.

Later they seem to realize that they were indeed rude and came to their senses and offered to put the stroller in one of their shops.

They later took at to about 1.5 miles into ocean to do parasailing. After this they were really friendly and offered to watch my kid while my wife, and daughter along with me went for parasailing.

We paid $45 for 16 sec video and lots of photos, unfortunately all the photos were taken facing sun so we didn’t get any clear shots but good enough to save them as memories.  They did some cool trick photography as well. So, good job on that!

Due to their quick turnaround of their behavior I offered them $20 tip as good gesture to make them feel better

Will I go back to them? Yes, again they had bad day so I forgive them for this; I am giving only 2 stars as they didn’t apologize for their initial behavior otherwise would have rated them better!

Tickets were expensive to start with. There is northern trail which is more of outdoor animal look out. This trail will also lead you to farm animals section where kids can pat domestic animals. There is also ice cream place at this section. At this point I thought it was waste of money as there were few animal than I thought. Kids didn’t see any lions, giraffe, zebra or gorillas here but you can see this at Como zoo for very minimal donation. However once I took the indoor trail(Tropic trail)  this has changed my opinion. There is lot to see inside and it’s pretty big and well presented. Truly amazing!   You can see from small kinds of apes to bird sanctuary where you kind of interact with birds. I would definitely recommend this. I am not sure how this will be in winter for outside trail but Indoor trail will be worth every money. Only one complaint is that they should NOT  charge for parking which is a rip off. Rest kids will love the place. Try to take food than buy at this place as its kind of expensive and adds up to bigger budget than you would plan for.

Great location, beautiful views of river, National eagle center is a place where they not only support the eagles who cannot survive in the wild but also they seem to have conservation programs. You get to sit in for 1/2hr interactive and Informative
classroom ,which is fun stuff. Kids get to know more about these fine raptors and their characteristics. While is not a zoo or bird sanctuary please don’t expect to see lots of live birds here. There are about 4-5 eagles, Golden eagle and bald eagle , can be seen up close who cannot fly due to hit by car or displaced from their nest. $10 for entry for adults and $7 for kids, while 4 and under go for free. There is a Gift shop and rest room facility on site. Parking is limited at site however you can park near by along the streets for free. There are also stunning paintings in upper deck on display and for sale.  Overall worth once a visit for your kids who are interested to know about these fine Raptors!!!

Mini Grand-canyon! There are about 12 lookouts.  1st  , 2nd and 3rd , close to visitor center, being top picks. I saw all 12 as didn’t wanted to miss anything. Spring is best time as summer could get very hot. If you are driving from MN and going to SD enter via ‘Ben Reifel visitor center’ and do the 240 loop. And if traveling from SD to MN do the other way around. There are walking trails, few fossil hunt trails, though I didn’t see much of fossil, but walk is not bad. Some trails are can go from easy to expert level. Please be cautious around small plants and holes as this place is known to  have rattle snake.

$20 entry fee per car. I saw about 3-4 restrooms in span of 24 miles in the park, which is not bad. There is also a lodge for you to stay near visitor center. Allocate min 3hrs for this place. Carry ample water  for hikes and at-least 50 miles of gas before you enter the park. Picnic area near visitor center to eat.  Rest enjoy the views!!!

This place is one of the spots on earth where laws of gravity doesn’t work like you knew it. I strongly recommend this place for family fun. I didn’t want to give much away as you need to feel and witness the force of Gravity. This is not an optical illusion.  Older people need to watch as gravity is very strong and you can’t control you body as you would on land. MUST see and visit this place if you are around here.

This is a laid back town/city mostly with Greek style restaurants on the strip. They have lots of sea sponges theme shops. Cruises 🚢 seems to be there main attraction to see dolphins and diving to see how sea sponge is extracted. $5-$10 seem to be parking in the Main Street however you can have this for free at certain places if you buy new from there

Good place for relaxed stroll along the creek. There is small peer and long one. Picnic area and rest rooms on site. You need to monitor your kids as there is no fence to water or to road on other side. So this place is not to let your small kids play by themselves and you relax. However very pleasant place at heart of the Eden Prarie city.

This is a paved, stroller friendly path. You go through some bushes and trees.I appreciate the variety of plants you get to see here and admire. This is one of the trial walk in Everglades. Not much happening to watch for animals and birds but when you walk under canopy of tress is definitely something you can appreciate as nature lover

This is a MUST and the BEST trail you can find in Everglades. We got to see alligators, crocodiles, different birds, Frogs,  and lily pads and different trees. This is fully paved trail so you get to take your strollers all the way. This trail is not stressful and you can get this done within 15-30 minutes of time.

They are doing great job preserving with concept of protect, rehabilitate and release of various forms of life e.g Turtles. There is butterfly garden with some butterflies in it. While this is free to visit Please donate and help support the people who protect and preserve.

Little park loaded with fun play equipment for kids of all ages.  Car Parking area was full and found hard to find a parking spot. Restrooms were on location and were maintained  clean. There was open ground by the play area, which is good for picnic or play ball 🏈 ⚽️
likes: Open ground for picnics and sports

reviews_attraction.text: Fun for kids, I didn’t like that we waited to see the robotic animals. Choose  this ride only if you have fastpass+ as waiting 40-60min is not worth it. Ride was short but the crew keeps you entertain.  It’s better to go to zoo than choose this ride in Magic Kingdom

4 star for the 600hrs of Effort put in the create this giant snow snail.  Friendly people at site, parking on the street side. Free to visit however do donate for their charity work.  I wish there were more than 1 sculpture to give 5 star. Excellent work of Art

Nature Park within reach. This place has limited picnic areas and no large open ground for kids to play.  This is only good for kids 4+. There is a play area and few creeks. This place can get crowded making it difficult for maintaining social distancing

If you want to know how the main st look like in 1880s well you can see it first hand here.  Gift shop, rest rooms available at premises.  Came to know summer is more happening here than Spring. 45min is sufficient to go around and look at this place.

Drive through safari experience to see Elk, wolf, Bears.  Fun for kids. You cannot get out of car or roll down windows in certain parts for safety. It will talk about 1/2hr to do the loop.  Cool Gift shops, restrooms at site.

Free to visit, ample of parking, interesting  to see how sculptures are made and the material used in it. This place is massive and rest rooms on site. If you have 15-20min to spare you can visit this place.
This is one of the best beaches in Florida. Beach has white sandy beach, jetty to walk on and some instant shops and food stalls near by. Changing rooms could be closer, hard to find them.
dislikes: Changing rooms far and hard to find

reviews_attraction.text: Great place to walk, run by the beautiful and serene banks of river. There are some trails which had fun steep inclines and decent. Woods with happy birds chirping and sight of deers.
Variety of Roses🌹 to see and admire. Peaceful place. You can also take a stroll along the lake near by. Paid parking lot adjacent to it. It’s $1.25 p/hr . Overall OK to visit.
Great falls in this cool little town. Falls you can walk into and have fun!!!. Steps are bit steep down to go to falls so older people and kids need to exercise caution.
We came  across this  place while we were searching for gas station. Nice views out side the building and cool plane model to look at. Didn’t go inside as it was closed.
Small beach but not that crowd, 3 life guards were keeping a watch, splash pad near by beach with couple of picnic spots. Overall nice place.
This is a nice beach location. To park the car on the premises is expensive so you can park across the road for $2 an hour and save money.
Fun, safe indoor slides for year around fun. $7.50 entry fee applies per kid and under one year old plays for free.
likes: Free entry for under one year olds

reviews_attraction.text: Very nice little cove/bay area for snorkeling, we even bumped into a turtle. Bring some water shoes, it is very rocky.  Be careful there is a lot of activity with fishermen in boats so just stay alert when snorkeling. We rented a buggy and drove down to the national park and walked around for an hour. Finished the morning off with a nice swim.

Nice stop on our way to the North Shore. Great little plantation, can get VERY busy. There is a maze and train as the main activities, but also a gift shop that sells souvenirs and pineapple products. There is a restaurant on site - you must try the fresh pineapple, to die for... and the pineapple soft-serve ice cream... YUMMY!

One of the most iconic landmarks in the US. Stop in for 5 mins just to see it and snap a photo. Obviously there are peak hours and the wait time will be longer if you want your photo in front of it. Pull off to the side and take a selfie... in and out in 2 mins :)

We used the pier to tender out to our cruise boat. It is very central and close to shops and restaurants. You can even use it to go swimming if you wanted. The view overlooking the bay is nice though and you might see some dolphins.

Absolutely Phenomenal! Amazing to see the all the different lava flows from the various years. The park is huge and you could spend a whole day in there. The good thing is, you can just pull over wherever you want and take photos.

Great lil park with an amazing view. We stopped here on a Road to Hana tour to stretch our legs, but wow what a great view. Looks like it could be a great place for a family pic nic as there are some tables and benches etc.

Very interesting national park with a lot of history and culture. Definitely worth the visit. We rented a buggy and drove down to the park and walked around for an hour. We then went swimming at the nearby cove.

Pretty interesting to visit this area of Volcanoes National Park to see and smell the sulphur deposits along the trail indicating thermal activity. Its a nice walk down the trail so I would recommend it.

Simply Amazing - this place is spectacular. They were setting up for Chinese New Years and the statues, flowers and plants required hours of work. Definitely worth a visit after watching the fountain.
likes: Cultural Value: Chinese New Years setup

reviews_attraction.text: Pretty interesting to visit this area of Volcanoes National Park to see the stream vents along the trail indicating thermal activity. Its a nice walk down the trail so I would recommend it.
Awesome gun range with a great selection of guns and shooting packages. It is one of the smaller ones so book ahead to avoid waiting in lines. The range staff were phenomenal.
Pretty amazing aquarium displaying all sorts of animals and fish. Obviously the shark tank is spectacular. A must visit on a rainy day or people who love zoo's/aquariums.
Awesome! Our tour guide pulled in and told us how there might be turtles down on the beach. There were! They were pretty huge too. It was amazing to see them up close.
Amazing ski resort - the trails were very well groomed and the ski rentals were easily accessible. Good restaurants at the resort too. Great ski school for kids!
Beautiful beach park. The beach had black sand which had peridot stones in it. The gardens were well manicured. Nice stop before a long day in Volcanoes Park.
Beautiful park that houses Rainbow Falls. Probably one of the biggest waterfalls I saw while we were in Hawaii. It can get very busy. Beautiful gardens too.
Very historic site. A must see while visiting Hawaii. There is a lot to do so if you are a historian, plan to be there for 1/2 day to take in everything.
This is an amazing show that kept me guessing what he had just done! The show is the perfect length, but you wish he could keep going. Memorizing!
Very nice lagoon that this is shelter and calm for beginner swimmers. Has a great view of the beach and on Friday nights there are free fireworks.
Beautiful view. If you get a chance, go down to the beach and see if there are sea turtles, its not too far of a walk down and worth the visit.
Impressive art exhibit of the human body. Visual displays contain actual bodies and body parts in action showing muscle contraction etc.
Stopped in for a little break on out Road to Hana tour. The view was nice. It was a nice little area with a famous banana bread place.
One of the many waterfalls on the Road to Hana. It is very beautiful and if you can find a parking spot, definitely worth a quick dip.
Great range with large selection of packages and firearms to chose from. The staff were very helpful and professional. Awesome time!
Impressive art exhibit of one of the greatest ships of all time. Visual displays contain actual artifacts salvaged from the wreck.

Stayed here for a couple days in midst of a southwest RV trip. Despite not having sewer hookups, it is an excellent campground.

You can drive on the beach down to the lake and use your car as a base of operations for lake fun. Some people even launched boats right from the beach! The lake itself is cool and inviting, and I can only assume it's more so in the dead of summer.

The RV spaces are large, flat, and paved, and there's 30 amp electric and water. If it had sewer hookups it would literally be a perfect campground.

This was a quick, free stop during our stay in Hurricane. It only took about an hour to check it out because we were able to drive to the trail head on the rustic dirt road. Note, if you have limited ground clearance youll.at the vey least need to take it very slow - the road is far from excellent. If you're driving a sports car, you'll want to park near the road and hike the mile or so on foot.

It's free and unregulated, the dinosaur tracks are very visible, and the kids thought it was really cool.

We stayed here as part of Harvest Hosts in our RV, and it was a great experience. There were several other RVs there, and we met some great people. They had 50 amp electric service and water available, too!

But most importantly, the wine. I wasn't expecting a lot from OK wines, but they had some really good stuff. From sweet to dry, something for everyone. We ended up buying a case, which is unusual for us. The staff and owners were friendly and accommodating. Highly recommend!

As a Marylander, I'm here to tell ya that hiking in New Mexico is not the same as hiking through the forest back east. This park is very New Mexico - dry, dusty, and hot. However, it was a neat experience to hike the well maintained trails there.

The lake is really kinda marshy, and smells accordingly. There are lots of ducks and other wildlife. Overall I'd say it's worth a stop if you're in Roswell, but don't go out of your way.

We stopped here as part of the Harvest Hosts program to spend the night in our RV. It was a good site with plenty of room.

We also visited the museum which was smaller than we expected but very nice with friendly staff. It was also very affordable for a family of six. Overall I'd say if you're in the area, it's totally worth checking out!

A very excellent car collection. Despite the entry fee being a little steep, I still feel it was worth it. Some of the cars here are rare masterpieces worth millions.

We visited in our RV as part of Harvest Hosts, and although they don't have any RV hookups, the parking lot is large and they were very accommodating.

It's a fun attraction but very short. At any time other than opening you'll wait in line for at least a half hour. Then the ride takes about two minutes. It's also pretty pricey - I have a family of four and it cost $70. That said, my oldest insisted on doing it again, and it really was fun for a couple minutes.

This is a fantastic place where the kids can get up close and personal with lots of different animals. They have standard petting zoo faire like llamas and goats, but they also have large and exotic animals like camels, hippos, and alligators.

A great place to spend a day with the family.

Neat place with lots for the kids to see. If you take the time to read the exhibits you'll probably learn something new, too. Covid limited the activities but the rest was good to go.

It was, however, about 25% more expensive than I felt it should have been.

Although the out of state entry price was a little salty at $20, it was worth it for the day I think. There's a paddle sports rental place on site where we got a kayak for the kids. The park is nice and everyone there was laid back and having fun.

A neat, free stop along Route 66. The history of the structure is interesting, as is the structure itself. The gift shop and mini museum inside also have some neat items. Worth a look if you have 30 minutes to burn along the route.

A decent selection of wines, particularly if you're into the sweet and fruity varieties. The tasting room is lovely and the staff was very friendly. $5 for a 5-shot tasting. We did 3 flights and found several bottles to buy.

Great spot, great wines. The proprietor stopped his tractor to talk to my kids about the farming of grapes, and let them taste some off the vines! If you like real wine, this is some of the best that VA has to offer.

We camped here for 5 days while visiting family in Stuart, and it is an excellent campground. Full hookups, level sites, and great facilities. We didn't have time to take in the park itself - maybe next time!

A little pricey for large families, but otherwise largely worth it. Live reenactors are knowledgeable and answer all questions happily. Lots to see for kids and adults alike. A really great historic site.
Priced reasonably for a family with kids (kids are free) and with a great representation of classic autos. It's not the Petersen, but it's well worth visiting and a great way to spend an hour or two.
Covid has tour options limited, so ultimately my family felt the cave was underwhelming. I suspect it would have been better given the option to see more, so it was all pretty disappointing, really.
This is a fantastic museum that has constantly changing exhibits. You can visit multiple times a year and always see something new. Excellent examples of classic and antique autos.
A great and relatively easy trail with many nice views of the reservoir. Bring a fishing rod if you like as there are many prime spots along the trail to trow a line.
I've been to several caves all over the country, and this is easily the best I've seen. The variety, quality, and quantity of formations is second to none. Wow!
Nice place with a handful of quality wines. Traditional varietals and nothing too sweet, if you like proper wines you'll likely find something to please here.
We only scratched the surface of the park by visiting the beach and doing the snorkeling tour. But that was enough to know that it was an excellent place!
Fantastic hiking spot with easy trails and harder ones, with great lake views along the way. The dog had just as much fun as the family, too.
This is a fantastic campground. Full hookups, big spaces, and great facilities.  Just make sure you book early, as they fill up quick!
A really neat place to spend the day with the family. Excellent food options and no shortage of things to do!

If you’re doing the Saranac 6ers then it’s not an option to skip this peak but After climbing an unlimited amount of mountains on the Adirondacks I would say that this is probably the last one I would go to.  The parking is horrendous.  There’s literally no spaces and there are locals that put fake parking tickets on your window basically warning you.  Even if you park off the road on the grass the best you can.  It’s an incredibly heavily used trail. Which makes things even worse.

My deal is if you don’t have proper parking and no one can use it then shut the thing down.

The peak itself is incredibly fast you can literally go up and down in an hour.   It has a small section of a decent incline but it’s great for smaller kids and older people who are maybe not regular hikers.  The top is pretty wooded with obstructed view but there are a few little outcrop areas for a decent view.

Like I said I had to get it done for the Sixers but I would never come back again.

This place is pretty unassuming but is a great stop.   The sand dunes are amazing to see and walk over.  There is a visitor area too explaining the local history of the location as well as the animals and plants in the zone.  My only suggestion to anyone would be to make sure you have sunglasses on.  The wind is tossing sand around everywhere you go.  You’ll be happy you wore them.  Also if you have a small child (baby) it’s not the greatest place for them on a windy day.  Saw people walking around with babies trying to wrap them up as millions of grains of sand pelt you like bb’s.

I have no clue what anyone has to complain about.  This was a great stop.  There is a ton of great history and architecture to take in, not to mention the incredible views.  Make sure to follow the self guided tour in the pamphlet you receive.  It will guide you through the maze of rooms and fill you in with great tid bits of information.  My only suggestion to them would be to add small placards near many of the items to get a little more information about them.

The Stone Valley Trail is a beautiful little trail to take a hike with the family.  It has some areas with some ups and downs but for the most part small kids and non-hiking people can handle the terrain.  The views are beautiful and there is enough distance to make a decent workout with it.  Roughly 3 miles in and 3 miles back give you a 5-6 mile jaunt.

Beautiful state park.  Decent size too. Lots of full hook ups, electric and renting areas scattered around the grounds.  Bathroom facilities in some areas are brand new.  Beach area has life guards and lots of trees near by for people who like the shade at the beach.  Boat launch on site with docking.  Playground area for the kids right at the beach.

This is a good stop.  The service men/women on hand are very informative and it's a unique experience.  If you have anyone elderly going down to the lower decks can be hazardous, so I would keep them on the top deck.  The steps are steep and difficult.  Make sure you stop at the Cassin Young across the shipyard.  That was even better in my opinion.

Decent stop to see migratory birds, turtles and other critters if you get lucky.  There is a decent walking path that takes you a ways back.  There is a visitor center on premise (currently closed due to CoVid) and there is a bathroom on the grounds, although there are no sinks in the bathroom to wash afterwards. Weird.

This place is a nice little find.  Super tiny little zoo.  Great cost.  Family of 4 getting into a zoo for 20something dollars.  I don't know how anyone could complain.  It's small but has a ton of things for the kids to see.  We would stop again for sure if we were passing through the area.  Staff was friendly too.

Pretty small pier.  Great tackle selection In the shop.  Also ice cream, beer and cold drinks.  Pass for the day and a thing of bait will cost you about $20.  Fishing wasn’t great while I was there.  No one caught s single thing over a 3 hr period, but I’m sure that’s hit or miss. We all know fishing.

So glad I stopped here.  I was almost going to skip it for the Museum of the American Revolution and I actually liked the National constitution center better.  The projection show was amAzing and does a great job of giving a quick overview of the events leading up to and post constitution.  Loved it.

Worth the stop for sure.  Some great history inside from Hawthorne and the building itself has some great historical value.  The national parks people working are a wealth of knowledge make sure to stop and ask them about the customs house.  They have some great information to share with you.

Free.  Pretty neat experience to go on the ship.  There are free tours if you have a 45 minute commitment.   If you don’t take the tour all you get is the top deck.

There is a 20 MM anti aircraft gun you can grab ahold of and feel what it would be like with a Japanese plane coming in.

This is a really cool pier stop.  There is an interactive learning center for the ecosystem around the pier.  There is also some aquarium fish, along with a gift shop and supplies to fish.  Then there is the actual pier too!   Great fishing spot and in good shape.  Good stop !

This place is absolutely amazing.  Has incredible views that you can see just by driving through the park and stopping at the various over looks.  It also has a ton of trails to hike for people that have the time to get more active in the park.  Bathrooms all over.

The aquarium was a great stop.  There was a ton of things to see for a small museum and some great hands on experience for small kids as well as middle aged kids with the Ray's and crab touching tanks.  Turtle rehabilitation area was really cool to see too!

Let me be clear.  It’s a great stop.  It has a ton of amazing things to see and experience.  I did enjoy the National Constitution center more, but you can combine both at a discount and purchase a dual ticket for each.  Do it.

Incredible history in this elementary.  From the memorial stones of each of the victims from the Salem witch trials to some of the first people to come over on the Mayflower, this is a must stop if you're in Salem.

Parking is extremely limited.  There are only a few parking spots.  There is a nice little boardwalk down to the lighthouse.  Not sure if it’s always closed or if you can normally go inside the the lighthouse.

If you’ve seen the move dolphin tale you obviously know about this place.  It’s worth the stop and your money is going to a great cause.  The dolphin show was fun.  Staff was friendly and informative.
This is a stuck in time little retro strip filled with food shops and a really big arcade.  Great big park picnic area and an ocean view.  Great place to bring the kids for a few hours of fun.
Really interesting stop.  Try to hit it early in the morning when it first opens or at the end of the day.  The crowds during the peak time have you waiting a bit to get in.  Free admission.
Great rest area to stop at.  The staff on duty are very informative and can help you with questions about the area and share current events happening in the area.  Glad we took a break!
Definitely worth the stop.  Grounds are impeccable.  Staff is very informative and the view is amazing.  The houses on the grounds have some great history in them as well.
Sites are large.  Quiet park.  Beautiful St. Lawrence River to fish right outside.  If you're into camping this is a great destination.
Great pier.  Bait available. $10 to fish for the day.  $1 to site see.  Saw all kinds of fish puffer, blues stripers, sharks.

I visited the Pritzker Military Library during the Chicago Architecture Foundation's Open House Chicago 2013.  What a treat!  This amazing space is open to visitors for a nominal fee, opening a world of historical books, periodicals and displays highlighting our nation's military history.  Colorful posters, photographs and multimedia exhibits will peak your interest in this material, as will the state-of-the-art theater, oral history room and computerized resources.  Don't miss the Medal of Honor exhibit to see an actual Medal of Honor on display, as well as an interactive exhibit allowing you to review details of the complete Medal of Honor roll!  This is a worthwhile diversion on your visit to the city, allowing you to not only experience the famous Monroe Building, but to take in a cultural museum experience as well.

This is a terrific spot in the middle of the busy Gold Coast neighborhood of Chicago.  Along with nearby Mariano Park just north, these two places make a nice respite from the crowds of the city.  Connors Park is unique in that it's got an Argo Tea outlet occupying much of the park.  While some lament the commercialization of open space, this Argo store has cleaned up the park and created an inviting place to relax, indoors or out.   Check out the placard in this park providing a brief detail of William J. Connors, prominent Illinois legislator after whom this park is named.

The last and only surviving of Chicago's grand railway stations.... now converted to rather routine retail uses.  Step inside here and step back in time to when dozens of ordinary and famous people traversed the halls on arrival to the city.  No longer so grand ..... but if you use your imagination you can still hear the hustle and bustle while you see the horses and buggies outside waiting for their passengers.  Check out Sandmeyer's bookstore down the street for some great reading on this area's historic past.

This building is an amazing treat right in the middle of Chicago's Loop.  Step inside the lobby, look up and gaze in wonderment at the impressive art that surrounds you.  When you're finished gawking, take the steps up to the second level for a different perspective.  Finally, return to the lobby and head for the interpretative display which details the history of the Chicago skyscraper and the Marquette's place in that history.  We are so lucky to have a living history of architecture in Chicago!

We love this place all summer long!  It seems like there is a concert or movie here every night of the week!  There are major performances as well as offbeat, international events to highlight different cultural arts all summer long.  Whether it's a symphony performance, a classic movie on the giant screen or a rap music festival, this place has it all.  I suggest you visit the nearby Mariano's grocery store for all your picnic needs prior to heading to the lawn!

This is an out-of-the-way monument to a significant part of Chicago's past when the city was "hogbutcher of the world", in Carl Sandburg's terms.   This spot is also the home of the Fallen 21 memorial, a monument to firefighters killed in the Stockyards fire of 1910.  It's interesting to stand in this spot and imagine what life must have been like back then when this area was bustling with activity.  Today, it's a quiet industrial park.

This is a very small museum, but very interesting with views of the actual gears that raise the bridge!  If you time your visit right, you'll see all this in action!  Bridge lifts are infrequent, but you can generally catch it every Wednesday and Saturday around mid-day during peak Spring and Fall seasons when sailboats are moving to and from the lake.    This is a great stop along Chicago's terrific riverwalk promenade!

This is a magnificent piece of artwork overlooked by many even as they pass right by!  Take a moment to relax here!  Walk around the perimeter of the wall and take note of the many scenes, delicately forged in mosaic tiles.  You'll be glad you stopped to become familiar with another piece of public art which is equally at home in our city along with the nearby works by Picasso & Calder.

My only complaint is that the water by the beach smelled like decaying something.  Hopefully that was an isolated incident on the day we were there.

This is an awesome park, just a few blocks walk away from the commercial area of Chinatown.  You can take a watertaxi here from the loop and then walk for a meal in Chinatown!  Walk along the Riverwalk here to the north for some great views of the city.  Good place for photography.
