You have to visit Ringing Rocks when you are in Bucks! Bring a hammer, and find a song in the rings of the boulders you discover when you go clinking away in the boulder field. I come here more than a few times a year to take the Loop trail down and back that takes you down stream along High Falls creek. Where hiking shoes/boots, the trail gets tricky after a heavy rain, branches and rocks hinder the way, a walking stick or two is also recommended,  you will definitely use them to safely traverse the boulders and downed trees to reach the creek. The creek here is very loud especially when it has rained. Check out the cliff on the opposite side, very steep, I have hiked all of this ,many(20ish)  years ago, be very careful the at the top, its a long way to fall. The trail is relatively short, 1/2 mile or so each way, but it is a steep hill climb back up will definitely work your glutes and thighs. I would not recommend biking, unless you are a professional 'rock climber ' on a bike. Weekday visits you may find yourself alone, meditate on a boulder or do yoga on the rocks along the creek . It is a very tranquil and spiritual place. Keep your eyes to the woods, many chipmunk! Trail blazed in white, on a rock, or tree, even fallen trees may be marked. Check out my videos & pics. So on that note I say to you "GET OUT" !! And Love Nature!!
dislikes: Tricky trail conditions (after rain, branches, rocks)

reviews_attraction.text: I FINALLY made it out here today, so glad I did , January 13th, 75 degrees F. Awesome weather for me to spend nearly 4 hours walking around the grounds and out to the Historic Lighthouse. I love the all history about the fort ! Just moved here from Philly 6 weeks ago so I  learned about it before going there , not knowing anything about it, on the Savannah government TV channel, and now I live here. I was fortunate today, the mosquitoes apparently weren't bad like I hear they can be when it's hot. Wear long sleeves, bug spray , I prefer patchouli oil mixed with eucalyptus oil , keep moving and go out to the lighthouse, it's less buggy out by the water . I was also lucky enough to be all alone today. It's so peaceful here !! Quiet , breezy, birds... Watch whilst you walk for the little sand crabs running around, I thought to be big spiders at first...lol I'll be back to fort as much as possible, I have a National Parks Pass . Buy some souvenirs!!! Slap a sticker on your truck or car . It takes a lot a love and labor to keep this awesome piece of History alive !! Enjoy it !! 😎😇💖💖

Nice hike to the river. Sweet views. Wear hiking shoes/boots , not sneakers like I did....and be careful near the bluffs edges. Look for humming bird moths in the grass field in summer.
Update Nov.26,2019 I made up here again for a late autumn hike , I love the very noisy dried tree leaves on the trail along the bluffs , the sun beaming down on me ,warming me in the chill of the day today , no other humans around today , it was truly a ZEN experience. I was sure to wear my hiking boots today !  An old fighter plane was flying around on this day, echoing all around me , other than that , silence . I later watched said fighter plane (T-6) landing at The Historic Vansant Airfield (i posted the video to the airield) over in Pennsylvania and was indeed excited for that and the awesome view of the sunset from here is always amazing.  I look forward to hiking up here again when it snows . Be careful driving up the rough gravel road ,if you are in a little car. Enjoy 🤗🦃

This is an awesome farm park. Very friendly and informative folks , farm animals, many  buildings, historic farm tools and machinery , HONEY , weekend programs all year long, this weekend (Nov.16) is focused on Bacon Sausage and Scrapple making from the turn of the 19th century , should be amazing . I hope to make it back for this , it'll be cold but ...its Bacon & Scrapple!! Enjoy!!
Excellent experience with all the friendly folks today involved in making sausage & Scrapple with the Butcher . A real hands on job . Horse drawn wagon ride around the farm . Kid friendly!! NO pets allowed.
They also make and sell maple syrup !! Yummy with scrapple . All $$ goes to the farm !! Awesome to experience 19th living . I posted more pics from today. I can't wait to go back and get honey and maple syrup! 🤗

Just $5 for adult admission, helps to give and help them help the ocean marine life !! I met Chelsea at the front desk. She is awesome and freindly, and local she gave me some history on the place . I talked with the women in the husbandry section ,marine biologists   in the back, they  nurse back to health marine life people find or catch . Very very cool project. They have much information to learn about all types of marine life. And a large selection of marine life in the mini "zoo". Even a baby alligator, a loggerhead turtle some Terrapins . A small gift shop too. I got a sticker for my truck . I'll go back there soon , to see what's new and support this awesome place and it's freaking cool yo!!!❣️❣️❣️❣️❣️😎🐸🐢🐊🦎🦈🐬🐋🐳🐟🐠🐡🦐🦞🦀🦑🐙🐚🐌

I love this park and lake the middle of Bucks , and it's a fun 15 to 20 mile drive from my neighborhood. Today was very windy so there was nobody out on the water.  You can kayak and sail here . There is a paved trail around the entire lake , share the trail , bikers and walkers, runners and crawlers. Stop in at the Nature center and school yourself in some nature. Maybe you saw that really cool 'what-cha-ma-call-it' and here you can find out what it is, so next time you'll know. Clean restrooms all around the park trail and water fountains .

I love it here , I love the old trains and history of it all, Morgan issued an informative and excellent tour/demonstration of the steam engine , I especially enjoyed the hand pump rail car with you. I felt like a kid again !! So awesome!! I got myself the toy train in a cool tin box and a whole bunch of postcards and bumper sticker. Huge model train set up  of Savannah is awesome!!   You all are doing a wonderful job keeping this place going. Kudos everybody!! 🚂🚂🚂🚂🚂❣️❣️❣️❣️❣️😎

Secluded and peaceful woods to find your Zen , the walk is good too, 2 miles round trip. As of today , there is a huge hornets/bees nest in a large tree on the right hand side just as you start into the wooded area after the short walk from parking area. You will HEAR them easily as I did and I walked back and forth a couple times before THEY came into view. I walked the other way back on the return, I didn't feel like pressing my luck with that horror.

What an awesome little Park !! Big beautiful water fountain, fields of grass , statues , playground, outdoor ampetheater ,  farmers market every Saturday (I love that most) lots of friendly people, the Sentient Bean across Park Ave, free parking , tennis, huge shade trees like giant guardians protecting us ,cooling us off a bit from those harsh sun rays that we love so much too ! I love Savannah ❤️❣️🤩

Cool little spot . You need to park on S. Ocean Dr. There are only 12 spots, I don't know where else you can publi park, I didn't see anything else. There are many roped off areas for the seaturtle eggs. Be careful climbing on the rocks and watch for some big waves of the weather is stormy in the area, I got soaked and was a bit shocked too, atleast the water is always warm...lol

This beautiful fountain in beautiful little Forsyth park in Awesome Savannah is a MUST see !! Farmers market every Saturday! Take a stroll and then just sit by the fountain , enjoy a coffee, people watch , talk to strangers it's cool man ! I love Savannah ❤️! So I moved here , got an apartment just a few miles away on December 31st . Cheers to starting over !! 👣👣👣👣😎💖🙏😇❣️😍🍻☕🥂🍾🤩

Beautiful old forest not too far from Phillipsburg, I spent the night in Still Valley, cruised up and took a nice stroll in the crisp cold morning, down to the little old wooden foot bridge over the creek, took some nice pics, walked up to the pond. Very Serene and Zen out here on this quiet lonely morn in the woods.

First time here today. Not crowded for a Sunday midmorning walk surprisingly. Very well maintained paths with highlight markers for trees and wildlife and benches . Paths are one way due to coronavirus protocols. Watch for the giant golden orb Weaver along your path just above your head , especially if you're tall.

I love it here , never too crowded especially weekdays. Get yourself lunch and a drink at the Hideout or bring yourself some chicken and BBQ, there are many here , lots of picnic tables too. They are presently doing a beach replenishment project here. So that does take up some beach space, for now. 🌅🌤️🥰

Awesome park for a variety of activities!! I met Paul today walking, he's also a park volunteer, he pointed out to me some invasive plants and some poisonous plants too, I was surprised to find out there are so many poisonous plants in Florida. I just moved to Dania Beach,from Philly... 😇♥️🌴

I came here to see Avril Lavigne !! It was awesome !! Small-ish crowd great concert venue . Much less traffic than driving into Philly to see a concert ! Oh, and I guess you can gamble and stuff if that's what you are into or watch a horse race , that's always fun !!

Awesome! A very cool learning experience inside and out, staff is extremely knowledgeable about all the wildlife here , especially the birds and water fowl. Many examples of the wildlife inside the center, stuffed of course ..lol with history on the area as well.

I like to visit here still after 40+ years . There is archery season here during the fall and winter . Sweet view of Philly from shores along the Delaware river . War re-enactments swimming pool playground restrooms . Peaceful place yo ,to seek out yo ZEN. ☮

I love taking a stroll out here from Fort Pulaski , and you may even see the dolphins in the water , lots of water fowl to see, also jelly fish that get stranded when the tide rolls out. Awesome part of Tybee Island history indeed!!

Stroll or hike along these awesome trails along the Tohickon creek up to High Rocks , excellent veiws , birds of prey
Find your Zen Get Out.     It's out there !!!🤗 if you're lucky you can catch a wicked cool sunset too 🌞
Cool little Park area , dog friendly with in the ground foot operated dog waste container, first I've ever seen. Great shade in the summer. Give the street musicians a few bucks Yo.
Nice little park to picnic or stroll, tennis, kayak, look at wildlife or the clouds. I'm told there is one alligator in the lake, I have yet to see him tho.lots of fish.

I love it here , when no one is around
Peaceful little park , scenic views along the Neshiminy creek  , awesome arch bridge above for "the train" ....boss. lol
Clean restrooms here during your walk about river street. Information you may also need for your self guided tour of Savannah.
It's beautiful here, I hope to get a chance and stay out for a night on the island this year.

This park is well maintained with many hiking paths and a small but nice waterfall. The waterfall is especially nice in the winter when it is frozen. The rest room facilities are much nicer than I expected. The park is well kept, but it is hard to know when the water will be flowing over the falls...we were recently disappointed when we went and there was no water (in July that is probably to be expected). However a number of wildflowers were blooming. The falls are awesome when frozen in the winter. They keep the paths, boardwalks, and stairs cleared in the winter...kudos to them.

Take Communications Blvd off of Hwy 444 to get to this historic location. Also find the Huffman Prairie State Natural Landmark at the same location...a bonus for your visit The prairie is beautiful with wildflowers, birds, and butterflies in the summer. A well kept path winds through the prairie. 2020 Update...Field and Prairie are open, the wild flowers are very nice this year around the hanger.  The grounds are pretty well maintained. The hanger has a number of barn swallows...quite harmless, but they can't tell an early 1900s airplane hanger from a barn.

This park has a nice trail through a wooded area that parallels the Beaver Creek. It is a mostly underdeveloped park, but that has advantages. It is accessed from the bike path that runs from Xenia to Beavercreek that is also called Creekside. There is also a path that runs under the large power lines that parallel the bike path. This trail is more open and has a wide variety of wildflowers. Both Creekside trails are seldom used so they are very peaceful.

This a very nice place to hike, especially in the Fall. The parking lot at the Smith House entrance is very nice and the paths that start their are all well marked. The paths have signs pointing out different natural features. The purple path is very nice and is nearly all flat and most places have nice wide gravel paths. We saw a number of visitors pushing baby carriers. There is a playground at the next door Forest Field Park.

This is a very nice facility with hiking trails and picnic areas at the site. The Visitor Center has many interesting displays on the history of the area and the very helpful rangers can answer your questions about the park. The lake overlook platform is a very nice place to take fall photos. The trails nearby are well maintained and very colorful in mid October. The little nearby pond is also very scenic.

This is a very well kept park with shelter houses, playground and hiking/biking paths. I especially enjoyed the wildlife around the Mad River.  One of the nicest parks in the area. It has playground equipment, many shelter houses, a bike/walking path and is next to the Mad River which attracts much wildlife. I usually see many types of birds here. There is a nice hiking path along the River.

We live in the area and go to the Museum 2-3 times a year. We really like the special events. Recently we attended an event honoring military working dogs (Wounded Warrior Dogs). It was first class...very educational and  it included a free iMax movie. They also brought in some real working dogs and their handlers. I have never been disappointed in the exhibits or programs.

Next to the marina is a Young Anglers Pond. It is easy to miss if you are not looking for it. The pond has a number of benches and apparently it has fish as there were many men fishing. Unfortunately they were not suppose to be there as the pond is reserved for anglers 15 and younger. There were a number of geese at the pond. The large number of young geese was impressive.

The road through the park is one way with a walking path on the side. Even if the forest paths are snow covered and icy in the winter, one can walk along the road and feel safe. The waterfalls are interesting in the winter as they have many icicles. Patty Falls is close to the road and has a nice stairs down to the bottom of the falls.

This park is in the process of being developed. It is currently mostly soccer fields, but there is some playground equipment. The Greene County Pumpkin Glow was help here this year and I think it was a huge success. The black light tent was especially impressive. The number of carved pumpkins was almost overwhelming.

The 151 foot tall Carillon Tree of Light is wonderful in December. Be sure to walk under the lights and look up. The main park is closed due to the COVID-19, but surrounding areas are open. If you are lucky you will see one of the eagles that nest there. I did and was able to get a nice picture or two.

This is a well maintained park. It is known for its Labor Day weekend Fair at New Boston event and there is an entrance fee for the Fair. I visited to see the lake and to hike which was free. It also has a museum which I did not see, but I think there is a charge for that and it is open limited hours.

The animals are amazing. The farm house and barns are amazing. We enjoyed every minute of our visit. I recommend driving through the wild animal park in your own car if you want better pictures. But you would probably learn more on the wagon ride.

We enjoyed our short visit to this park. They have a great view of the Miami River and its wildlife. They have lots of places to park, a stage, and playgrounds and picnic tables. The Dayton rowing club is located on the southern end of the park.

This is small but pretty falls. The vegetation along the gorge prevents a good view in many places. It is a short hike to the falls from the parking lot and the path is well maintained. The view up the creek from the path bridge is very nice.

This is a 43 acre park along a creek with not much more than a parking lot, a foot bridge, and trail. It is kept up well and has a nice boardwalk across a wet area. Some of the trail is muddy and could be improved.
This is a beautiful spot in the summer...and so easy to get to. There are plenty of places to sit and there are so many lovely flowers you don't notice the traffic on Hwy 40 next to the Garden.
This is a small but diverse garden with two main parts. The conifer garden has a lovely pond and small waterfall. The woodland garden has nice tree covered paths and places to sit and relax.
This is a smallish museum, but the cars are top notch and the staff is friendly and knowledgeable. The Model T gift shop is very nice. I very much enjoyed the visit and it is inexpensive.
The lake water was low when we were there so the birds were fairly far from the boardwalk. There were rangers on the boardwalk to help answer questions. An osprey was fishing.
The tour was very informative. There is a lot of glass history in this town. The historic pieces are amazing. If you like history and glass items you will love this place.
Magee Marsh has a very nice visitors center with many trails and the boardwalk through the marsh is nationally known. The amount of wildlife at Magee Marsh is remarkable.
This area is very scenic and the trails are fairly easy. Stairs lead down to the path that follows the river and leads to the historic area known as the "Blue Hole".
The boardwalk down to the falls is very well maintained, but there are a large number of steps. There are a number of places to view the falls from along the way.
We took the entire family. The grandkids really enjoyed all the inter-active displays and activities. We especially enjoyed the Apollo 11 display.

Great history stop. Have been here several times. Find something new every time. Some of the tours are a little bit hard. You will have to climb or go down a ladder. Do the whole tour if you can. The aircraft carrier Yorktown, the destroyer Laffey and the submarine Clamagore. There is also a medal of honor museum on board the Yorktown. There are also several old planes to see on board.

We rode our motorcycle up the interstate and got on the Blue Ridge Parkway where it begins near staunton Virginia. The Blue Ridge Parkway is free to drive on but if you get on the Skyline drive it will cost you. We rode the parkway home to South Carolina. Got off where highway 276 crosses.

Good historical place to stop and visit. There is a lot to see over a large area. A fort, an Indian village and three ships. You can go down into the ships and see the inside of them. There people stationed everywhere to tell about their area that they are stationed at.

Great place to stop to get a good look and pictures of table rock mountain. Pretty lake and nice big building to look around inside. There are restrooms and snacks available. You can also buy souveniers. It is a must stop and see place because it is so beautiful.

Nice park. This entire park has been redone. Greenville little league has several fields there now. The old greenville Braves field has been reworked and turned into a useable  field again. There is a Korean war monument there right next to the dog walking park.

Beautiful place to stop and see. Really neat to see the prairie dog communities. My wife went here as a child so she really loved the chance to come back and see it again. It does take awhile to see it all but there are some nice rest stops and souvenier shops.

Great walk through charleston. This is mainly right on the waterfront on the east side. The houses are painted all different colors. There are also many other things to see and do all within a short walk of each other. Parking is limited close by though.

Neat place to go. There are a lot of shops and restaurants right in the area. There is a playground for kids. You can go for a paddleboat ride. There are some great views for taking pictures. Lot of history in the area and it's all in walking distance.

On a clear day it is very beautiful. We usually stop here when we drive by. It is a short walk to the overlook area. Great place to take pictures. One of the interesting things you can see here is the fact that you can look down and see a bird flying.

Very pretty area. The Edisto river runs through the park. It is close to interstate 95 on the east side. It has a large campground. There is also a ranger station close to the entrance of the park. There are several nature trails all over the park.

This is a beautiful place. The parking lot is gravel. There is more parking if you drive in farther. The steps down to the river need some repair work. The road is ok. It is not an easy walk up and down the steps or road because they are steep.

Beautiful place. Drove around the area and found out you could drive on the beach if you had a four wheel drive vehicle. Luckily I was driving one. Had a great time driving on the beach. Finally had to leave because I was getting low on gas.

Beautiful place. There is a lot of things to see and it is spread out. There are also a lot of stairs. I don't get around to well anymore so I am glad I got to see it when I was able. My favorite place was at the top of Hickorynut Falls.

One of the prettier overlooks. The weather plays a big factor at this scenic overlook. Sometimes it's clear and beautiful other times it is cloudy and cold. Not unusual to be there when a cloud comes through and you can't see anything.

Interesting tour of a world war 2 destroyer. It has a very interesting story to tell. It was hit by several kamikaze planes during the battle of Okinawa and survived to fight again. Not a big ship but still has a lot of things to see.

Fun thing to do. We went early. We were the first group of the day. There was about 20 of us. Didn't take long to get spread out but it was a quiet easy ride down the river. Wasn't standing room only like it becomes later in the day.

Beautiful park but a little off the beaten path. Takes awhile to get there but worth the drive. There is a very nice and wide trail to take a hike. It is connected to other trails. Biggest problem is there isn't enough parking.

Good place to learn some revolutionary war history. There is a large area just outside of town with a lot to see. There is also some places to see downtown. The state of south Carolina is full of revolutionary war history.

Good stop for kids. It has the ability to breathe fire out of its mouth. If you go into the true value store you can get tokens to make it breathe fire. A token will last for several seconds. Great roadside attraction.

If you like being in clouds this is the place. Several times we have been there when low clouds go through here and fog up the area. The whole area is prone to it but this overlook seems to get it the most.
Interesting place. It is out in the middle of nowhere but there is a rest area right there with it so it is a good place to stop, stretch out and walk around and look at all the airplanes.
We enjoyed tremendously. We got seats on first class so we had ent we're raiment and a meal. Scenery wasn't great because there weren't any leaves on the trees and it was cold.
Good view of the waterfall. It is a moderate walk to the viewing place. There is a trail to the base of the falls but it isn't an easy walk.
This is easy to see from the road but it's in the middle of a pasture. Not sure if it's ok to walk out to see it or just get closer to it.
Neat place to stop and learn how and why this portion of the blue ridge parkway was built like it is.

It's easy to spend a whole day here. I was anticipating the new update, but it doesn't seem that great. Maybe they have more to do. The food is okay at both Sunrise Cliffs and Wo Zha Wa. They have plenty of slot machines, but they seem tight.

The table games are often packed until late in the night and they start to close them down at midnight.  The dealers are smart asses, but alright if you want to give it back. I don't think they know their payouts very well and will take your money thinking it didn't win, so pay attention. The bar tenders are pretty bad and don't pay attention, so that service is no good.

I found out there is no drinking after 2:00am. Last time I was there, the pit boss snatched my drink out of my hand, without saying anything, and threw it in the trash. I told him if he would have used his words he would avoid making people angry.

The rooms are nice, especially the big ones, but depending on when you go, it seems you can sometimes find better deals for nearby hotels and resorts; which you're probably better off doing. The shuttles also run 24hrs which is nice, and you never have to wait long.

The pool are is great and I've never seen it busy. They have two hot tubs, one very large, a sauna, and a decent pool.

Great time with so much to take in! The ultimate experience is the way to go if you have all day. If you read everything and take your time you'll need more than a day. They give you 4 tokens for their "machines."

There are around 30 different machines you can put tokens into so you may want more. 15 are before the Whale and 15 are after/in the music of yesterday.

In the Whale area there is a two token Octopus' Garden machine and two token fortune machine. On the way to the restaurant there are two of those seats that you sit in and they randomly light up an answer. (Like what kind of lover you are). In the restaurant there are three fortune machines and a penny machine.

Once into the music of yesterday there are the other 15 machines. The 8th and 9th ones are big sound machines and the 12th one is The Red Room. Save a token for that.

Great place if you want a scenic hike, short or long. There are multiple parking areas of Pheasant Branch Trail and you can also park over at Orchid Heights Park.

If you want to do a short hike you can walk the Southern trails. These trails are in the woods more and can go longer; leading in to some area parks. One trail leads to a deck and overlooks the water. There are multiple trails going up hill and leading to an overlook of the conservancy on the North end. This can be a shorter hike as well.

If you're looking for a longer hike (a few miles/ a couple hours) you can walk around the whole conservancy. It goes, through woods, Orchid Heights park, and along the road.

This would be an interest place to explore if you're looking for certain things. I went on the one trail that I assume ends up taking you to the end of Forest Dr. It's the only trail I know that exists. The trail didn't circle around so I ended up turing around after around 45 minutes. 15 minutes in all the overgrowth ends and it gets muddy in some places. 20 mins in is the "Hollow" area. 30 mins in it didn't seem like there was much else to see. On Maps, Stones Pocket Rd isn't actually a road that far in. I'd go back, but it's not something I HAVE to keep going back for.

This is a great short hike for any skill level both in the Winter and Summer. At a slow pace it can be hiked in around an hour and a half. If you want to see the small waterfall you will have to adventure past the  maintained trail and climb over some rocks.

In the Summer plan to hop across rocks and possibly get you shoes wet. In the winter you won't have to hop across as many rocks, but it does get slippery. The water isn't deep if you fall in.

Once passed the maintained trail you have to stay within 20 ft of the water and cannot go past the waterfall.

The trails are unique here, not difficult and you can see a lot in around an hour. One trail leads you through the marsh to a bench and overlooks the Yahara River. Another trail leads you to a raised deck looking towards the river and overlooking the marsh. You can walk one trail uphill through the woods and see all the way to the interstate.

This is a great place for kids, field trips, and is definitely worth more than one visit.

Nice place with a playground, shelter with a lot of picnic tables and a large grill. The bathrooms we're clean. The trails were under maintained. Unfortunately the tower was closed and I didn't see any signs of it reopening. Could be closed just for winter. Definitely seems like a good Palace to gather with people for a short period of time and maybe to a quick short hike.

For a small museum there is a lot of info here. It is a lot of reading, but there are items on display from when it was in operation. There was one guy working while we were there, Rolland. He worked at Badger Ammunition while it was running and if he is around he is full of knowledge and willing to answer questions. Really cool place for gaining past knowledge.

One of the best Museums I've been to. So much history and so much to learn. We could have asked the guy questions for days and he wouldn't have run out of answers.  There is always something being brought back to its original quality or brought in and it's unbelievable the ways they've been able to recall the past in order to do what they've done here.

This park is scenic and peaceful. It even has a dog area in a different parking area down the road. The hike around the lake is really nice. They have nice new dock and plenty of benches. There is cool little structure at the top of a hill that overlooks the lake and is not a long hike. I only wish you didn't have to hike the same trail back.

Best mini golf course I've ever been to. 36 holes of golf fit into this small area and every hole makes it worth it. The price is inexpensive, you can get a hole in one on every hole, it's interactive, and will keep you coming back for more. The staff is friendly and you can even get a free game with a hole in one on the last hole.

It's one of those things you have to see to check off your list. It's unique and fun to see. There were a lot of people around, so if you wanted a picture of just you and "the bean" it was near impossible. You might get a couple of people handing things out asking for money for the homeless too.

Would be a nice place for camping. Campsites are pretty open. There is a playground and sand beach area. You can also walk down the hill behind each campsite and walk the sand edge by the water. There are a few other trails in the woods past the campsites you can walk out to the water as well.

Nice place to meet friends and hang out. Never seems like a lot of people are here. It has a pier to swim off of, a small building with bathrooms, playground, and fire pit. Tennis courts are across the street. Maple Bluff fireworks are also shown here.

The bridge is interesting, but you can't go up, under, or around it. The trails are okay, but there aren't very many and they are short lived. It's a good place for a quick, low key, hike, but seems like more a one time stop.

Everything around Warner Park is great. Baseball fields, Soccer fields, trails. You've got the the Rec Center and Mallards Baseball. In the winter you've got the ice rink and ponds to skate on. Everything is kept up great.

There wasn't a whole lot of action when I was there last and it seemed like a deadzone, but a few animals were out and it was still nice to walk through. The best part was the syrup making that was going on.

Nice park area with beach and a place for the dog to swim. Great views of Lake Mendota and plenty of parking. The trails don't amount to much in the Summer, but seem to be enjoyed while cross-country skiing.
First time here was a good time. Had a fun time with all the fans and the servers were friendly. I didn't like that they had a women's bathroom and no men's bathroom next to it, but I made it work.
Great spot for fun and adventure. It has a playground, tennis and basketball courts, and a large amount of field. Nearby to water, Lake Wingra and the free zoo.
Free pier with a lot of room and places to out you pole. The chairs and roof over top the middle portion of the pier is a nice feature as well.
Was there for some fair. It was interesting and good way to spend half a day checking things out and hopefully learning something.
Two baseball fields, lots of parking, three sets of bleachers, and right next to Goodman pool. It's a pretty simple set up.
I was only here briefly, but the sound sounded great the area was large and it looks like a great place to enjoy music.
Great place for a quick hike. The view at the top of the stairs is amazing, but be prepared to walk A LOT of stairs.

I had a fantastic time today in the water at both sites. I did the Snuba at the first stop and then just snorkeled at turtle town. I saw tons of turtles and lots of cool fish. The equipment was in good condition and the staff was super friendly. The drinks are cheap as well. I only give it 4 stars because I hate crowds and this boat was packed. I prefer snorkeling with a dozen or less people even if it drives the price up. It was also hard with 8 people doing Snuba to cover a lot of ground in 20 minutes. Still fun and I recommend it.

It’s going to be the hardest thing you do in Hawaii! It will also be the most rewarding. It’s 1032 steps from what I hear. I have done it twice on both my trips to Hawaii. It is absolutely amazing once you get to the top. The trail is hard. Wear shoes that grip and light clothing. Bring water a snack. It also gets very crowded. I recommend going early before the heat of the day.

This is always a great thing to do if you haven’t done it or haven’t done it in a while. I come every few years usually bringing friends that are in from out of town. Such a cool piece of history that we have available here in Norfolk. Make sure you check out Nauticus too. I had the opportunity once to do yoga on the Wisconsin and that was amazing.

An amazing beach to see turtles, when I went there were several just laying on the beach sunbathing. See the photos below. There are frequently volunteers on site marking areas around the turtles so you don't get too close. Remember this is their home and we don't want to invade their space. They are super cool to look at though.

When I lived in Atlanta, I spent many days and many afternoons in this park. They have all kinds of festivals here and it's always a good time. I have spent many afternoons on the hill in quiet contemplation or reading a book and the views from the park to the Midtown Skyline are absolutely breathtaking.

This is a super cool experience! The property is 1 acre and is the largest residential lot on the island of Key West. There are currently 55 cats on the property. The guided tour is really cool. Look for the ones with 6 toes! The property has been well preserved since Hemmingway’s time.

Definitely a must see on your trip to the Washington DC area. It's easy to forget history until you get to experience it. I highly recommend checking this out, especially if you get to see when they do a change of guard. Definitely make time for a moment of silence to remember.

Absolutely check out the Norfolk zoo! There are so many cool exhibits to check out and they just opened the new reptile house! I always enjoy going to the zoo and it seems every time I go they have something new. They also do private events and birthday parties!

I think I learned more watching the video and then touring the memorial about WWII than I did in history class. This is such an integral part of our history and they have done a great job putting this memorial together. Get there early because it fills up fast.

It's a nice beach, the sand as you walk into the water is a little rough. The beach is also crowded. The water is warm though, although there aren't many fish to see. All in all it's not bad. Every Friday night there are fireworks at 7:45pm.

Absolutely amazing snorkeling or Snuba site. So many cool fish. I hope I can upload some pictures that I took with my go pro. The reef here is so cool. I would definitely come out here during your Maui stay if you get the chance.

Looks like a very nice beach in Maui. Not sure about parking as we walked over from the Hyatt. Turtles can be seen in the rocks so make sure you bring your snorkeling gear or at least a mask. Just remember not to get too close.

Absolutely my favorite ride at Busch Gardens. Maybe it's because I remember stories from my childhood of my dad telling me how much this ride scared him as a little kid. I always start and end my day at BG with this ride.

It's always a great time at town point park! From Wine Fest, to Pride Fest , to the in Water Boat Show. We are so lucky to have a great park on the waterfront like this. View of the park from the water attached.
From a tourist perspective this is a great locals beach park. The views are amazing, the sunsets out of this world. I wish I had gotten to do more than just come check out the sunset.
This is a cool spot to check out! Make sure you bring your camera! The rock island you can see with the hole in it is super cool. It's definitely worth the drive from Waikiki!
I always have a good time on the rover but I'm giving it a 3 because it needs some updates. They also need a bar upstairs because I always get sea sick going downstairs.
Love, love, love the Passion Fruit Gose, it is probably one of my favorite beers of all time. This is a cool brewery that you should definitely check out!
This is one of those things you have to check out and get your picture made in front of while you are staying at the oceanfront. Typical tourist spot.
Definitely add this to your list of museums to check out in Atlanta. I never visited this until I moved away from Atlanta and I was not disappointed.
If you are looking for an afternoon getaway from Hampton Roads this is a great place to go. Lots of trails to walk down and view the barrier islands.
Great place, really cool atmosphere, indoor and outdoor seating. They have one of the best Moscatos around. The food is good but the wine is better.
Probably the prettiest of all the public beaches in Key West! And they have parking available! There is a very large area to swim as well.
The trail around Freedom Park is some of the best running in Atlanta especially now that it connects to the belt line.
This is a popular tourist spot so get here early if you want to see the absolute best sunset on the island.

This is, without question, my favorite miniature golf course anywhere that I've ever visited. The landscaping is amazing, especially with the construction of everything into an existing department store building. The combination of in and out, winding up and down creates an incredibly unique place to play. Do not expect to score a slew of holes in 1 on your first few go-arounds but do expect to enjoy a one-of-a-kind setup. I especially like when I get to the top level and can see everything below. Both courses are a lot of fun. I've come soooo close to getting the ball into the 19th hole at least 5 different times and while that is far from the only thing that motivates me to return, it's definitely a fun perk.

I used to really enjoy Luray Caverns (it was my favorite cave touring experience as a kid) but over the years, it's turned into a bit of a nightmare. The cave itself is still lovely but man, there are too many people being shoved through, an inadequate touring experience, and an ever-increasing price to go right along with a lack of parking. The side attractions are okay but don't really make up for the mind boggling amount of people who are filtered through. Virginia has 7 other commercial/public caverns to tour and none of them is like this. Luray is still worth visiting but you'll probably be very unhappy if you visit on or near a holiday or weekend. Maybe a Thursday morning in the fall or spring.

I don't care what any park literature says, you have to ride in the front row to truly experience this ride. You may get a similar view from the raised seats in the second and third rows, but the true "dangling over the side of the coaster" experience is not the same back there as it is in the front. I've ridden so many times that I know the number of seconds you hang, but it never ever fails to feel like much longer than the actual time, which is pretty impressive. You get some amazing views of the park up there, plus the downward motion and loops are really great ride mechanics. It's also very smooth and fairly comfortable for a roller coaster.

Stopped by and was unable to do much of anything due to "ongoing logging" as noted by signs posted very inconspicuously. Had I not stopped to read all the various messages on one posted board, I wouldn't even have known that the trails were technically closed. I wouldn't be surprised for the park employees to constantly find people walking the trails without the knowledge that they were "closed" because there is nothing to signify this on the trailheads nor any barriers. It seems to be in a pretty spot but there's really nothing to see or do but look at a bunch of dead trees stacked in piles.

The "Smithsonian's home in Pittsburgh" slogan made me a tad sad since museums in the Washington Smithsonian are free admission. Nonetheless, I enjoyed my very immersive experience in walking six floors of various exhibits. The lauded Heinz exhibit is okay but I very much enjoyed seeing the Mr. Rogers memorabilia and the sports museum. There's a lot to see here, including sets from the 18th, 19th, 20th, and 21st centuries, with a heavy bent on local Pennsylvania. If you go, take the "smart steps" and get your stamps so you can get your free pickle pin.

I know it's not exactly easy to get lost per se but my only wish is for there to be more trail blazes so that it's easier to tell where different amenities lie. If you're in the woods, it can be difficult to tell which way your particular parking lot is or where the recreation center building is. Other than that, it has quite nice shaded walking and a good view of the lake in the middle, where you can stop and sit or simply pass and admire on your way.

I genuinely love the experience of climbing up and walking over the floodwall, even though I swear it seems intimidating at first. I wish the loop for the canal walk and the flood wall were slightly better marked once you walk over the bridge but the views you get from on top of the wall are amazing. The surface is not always well-maintained and it can feel a little spooky in places, especially when the signage is missing but it's a great walk.

Definitely not ready for prime time yet. If you're nearby, possibly worth the trip for kids to use the playground and or to have a picnic/boat launch spot. But don't travel here from any distance; it's not worth it. I know the park is still under development which is why I am not dismissing it as being useless, just offering a caution that it's not worth more than a 30 minute trip at this point in time.

One of the best waterfront and water experiences in Richmond. The trails out to the water are nice, too. It can be extremely crowded in summertime (especially on weekends and after regular business hours) and parking can be a problem but if you manage to hit the space earlier in the season or at a slightly earlier point on a weekday, you'll likely have a very nearly perfect experience.

I feel slightly awkward rating a cemetery because this isn't Google Graves or whatever. But as a tourist location (which its marketed to be) it's a pretty nice one, I suppose. The overlook from the far side to the river is gorgeous and the variety of famous people buried within make it an historic trip. If you're into ghosts and legends, you'll get that here too.

I went for an after-hours event, and it was pretty nice to be able to see everything right around sunset. The inside isn't as expansive as expected but it still has a lot of very interesting set pieces and content to explore. The gardens are gorgeous as is the view from them overlooking the river. Everybody there was very, very nice.

Definitely fun to wind through. If you sit in the back, be prepared for intense pressure on the sides of your head compared to the front, where you'll be more subject to high wind in your face, no matter what the outside temperature is like. Best bet on this ride, for the greatest experience is to head towards the middle.

My rating for this location comes largely from the beauty of the Mapparium, which is pretty and a unique experience, although the lack of photography is a little confusing, since modern cameras don't rely on flash to take pictures in the same way, and also photos don't replace the experience in the slightest.

An incredible space! Has been turned into a very unique interactive museum experience. I loved that everything on the first floor somewhat invites your direct engagement through touchscreens and exhibits with moving parts. The art galleries and rotational displays upstairs are impressive as well. I loved it.

I've only been for LanternAsia, and it was dark and rainy, so my ability to review the garden as a whole is somewhat lacking. That said, the LA event was pretty, and enjoyable, and it was clear even during it, that there is more to see, which I will be hopefully someday returning to observe.

I like the theming, and getting to play one hole on the pirate ship (if you opt for that path). It's not an especially unique theme but it's still fun and getting to see the dragon once in a while is just a bonus. They pipe in music throughout so you can better feel lost in the world.

Definitely an up and coming space, with a really great set of curated first exhibit artists. Best of all, the free admission means you can keep coming back and seeing things as they get updated. The actual grounds are really nice as well.

A gorgeous Virginia State Park. I liked the wooded trails and also the beachfront. I do think some of the mileage indicator signs are not quite right-- based both on step tracking, GPS, and even google maps, but I still enjoyed my walks.

I wandered in from my journeying on the Freedom Trail and had a good time with the exhibits and looking around the building itself, which is interesting in its architecture and even just its historical significance.

Nice little somewhat hidden spot with good places to walk around. I appreciate that its busiest times tend to be during working hours so later afternoon visits can be fairly quiet, though not isolated.
The lake water itself is underwhelming and often looks more grungy than inviting. Still, it's a nice outdoor space and the little nature center itself is pretty cool for what it is.
The trails are a little lacking in maintenance and in direction. They also don't cover a lot of ground but it's still a pretty nice park and the actual hidden rock is pretty cool.
Park itself is pretty nice. It's often booked with RCSSC and other community group sport activities which makes it hard to park but the disc golf course is pretty fun.
Nice little loop trail around the water and some woods to make you forget that you're in civilization. Nice for walking or running.
Not a lot of "facilities" per se, but the walking trails are nice and shaded, and the water access is good.

As one of the oldest of the Missouri State parks, it is historically a fun place to visit. The Wilderness trail has been on my bucket list of hikes near STL for a really long time, and it's nice to finally have crossed it off the list.  We ended up taking the entire loop, and doing it counter clockwise, which in fact got us slightly lost.  If you choose to take that route (which also btw makes the harder hilly parts come first while you're still fresh!) once you pass the copper hollow springs, keep an eye on the orange blazes.  It is easy to just continue following the stream channel, however after a mile or so, this is not the trail any longer as it veers right and climbs the ridgeline.

The trail IS well defined and blazed, however if you aren't paying attention like we were it can get you off-trail.  Luckily it also puts you off trail in the middle of the loop so no matter what you'll pass the trail again and realize your mistake.

Fantastic trail, and a super fun hike.

Rarely have I ever given one star but I’d have given zero if I could. Missouri wine can be a bit different for people depending on their style preference. Personally I really have enjoyed it and have usually found a vintage or two I like at each place.

Bias is not one of those. The other reviews have it spot on. The wine was brown which was a huge red flag. All of it tasted of vinegar. I can’t imagine why people were buying bottles to take home. Even the sweet wines had an underlying vinegar taste.

Save your time and skip the crazy driveway.

Run, run away.

The Lewis and Clark Trail is an 8 mile loop and has some great views as well as some very different ecohabitats to explore. This is one of my favorite trails in the St. Louis metro area some amazing views from the bluffs are the best part of the trail. There is a good amount of uphill climbing, but if you just want to experience the bluffs over the view of the Missouri, take the Lewis trail directly south to the river and then come back to the parking lot. It’s a mostly flat part to the trail and let’s you experience the view without the climb.

Cedar Lake Cellars is one of the best afternoon winery spots in the St. Louis metro area. They have an expansive lawn area to sit outside and drink their nice wine selection. We’ve not used the barn but we have definitely loved the restaurant. The Prime Rib is out of this world. The wait staff are amazing and twice now we’ve had Angi as our server - she’s professional friendly and makes us both feel right at home. They even put a fire in the fireplace for us when we asked!

One of the older State Parks but a hiking enjoyment nonetheless. We did the look through the north part of the park, running past the river and then up the bluff. There are definitely some hefty climbs and the one up from the river to the overlooks is almost a straight up climb. However the views are worth it. Weather couldn’t have been any better. Some of the trails deeper in the park can be overgrown but all the trails we took were well blazed.

Possibly the biggest botanical garden that I've ever been to in any city.  The gardens are massive, taking several city blocks.  Expect to stay here for at least a few hours, and then only seeing the big highlights of the gardens.  There is so much to see here and well worth the admission price.  If you're a STL resident, be a member and help support this amazing place.  The gardens also hosts events days and evenings which make this even better.

We had a great hike through the bluffs on a loop trail through the Cuivre River State Park. The views are pretty impressive and the trails are well marked and pretty easy to get around. Well worth a visit especially with it’s close proximity to St. Louis. There are a couple different ways to access the lower loop trails so a visit to the ranger center is well worth the quick stop before hitting the trailhead.

Cliff Cave is one of my favorite parks and trails to visit close to the city and my home. There is a nice large series of loops and back-and-our paved trails that make for easy walking as well as some well maintained mountain biking trails. The lower 5 mile loop is still flooded and muddy in spots and is closed off (although you can still access the loop if your adventurous, and like trail detours).

Like many others have posted, this place is truly a hidden gem near St. Joseph, MO. Easy access, and a great auto tour. I stopped at the first hike spot between the two pools and took many pictures. I was the only person in sight and felt like I had this place to myself. Although a hot day, and although not on a migration heavy day, the experience was still awesome. Highly recommended.

Doing the southernmost B access area makes for a long 6 mike hike when taking into account the elevation gain (over 900 feet). Bring water if it’s a hot day. Some of the trails can be very steep and rocky which make for some unsure footing. Grassy areas abound so ticks and chiggers can be heavy in summer. However the views are pretty great and the ridgetop meadows are worth a visit.

Although the moniker of the highest point in Missouri may be overrated (the high point is in the forest on a flat area and a plaque), the hiking trail down to Mina Sauk Falls is really awesome. If you’re feeling very adventurous I’d suggest continuing down the Ozark Trail past the falls to the Devils Tollgate which is a really cool couple of towering boulders framing the trail.

Great trail, with some sections probably being a bit more closed in during the warmer months when the weeds and bushes have filled in. We managed the lower loop before lunch time, and enjoyed the huge bluebell covering through many sections of the trail.  With a number of trails, both short and long, this park is a pret destination right outside STL.

Really enjoyed the park and the scenery on a cold day, but the cave tour was by far the most enjoyable part.  Its about a 90 minute tour, and although some parts are steep, wet and not made for my 6'4 height, the entire family enjoyed the sights inside a truly mammoth cavern.  This is a great example of a dolomite Missouri cavern.

The new museum is absolutely fantastic. They’ve done a great job with the grounds and taking the tram up to the top truly was a fun time. I didn’t think I would enjoy it as much as I did and I am really glad that I went. Even if you’re skeptical whether you’d appreciate the view and ride, I highly recommend going!

After visiting a few times in the past couple months I still think I haven’t seen it all. It’s an incredible museum and well worth the visit. We went during the underwater Egyptian traveling exhibit and really enjoyed that part. For a free museum, the experience is well worth it.

First time to Grants Farm after living in St. Louis for 18 months and definitely had a blast. Sure it’s really a place for kids, but we had a throughly good time checking out the animals, riding the tram and sitting in the sun drinking some beers.

One of the highlights of our stay on the Leelanau. Great views from several spots along the ridge as well as many sand dunes that the kids absolutely loved. Also connects up with the M22 bike trail and makes for a few great stop along a ride.

Great hike with some fantastic views. Moderately strenuous hike with a lot of small short climbs up and down the valleys. Bring lots of bug spray and still be prepared to pull ticks off your clothing. The trails are close in and very grassy.

Some of the trails can be really thick! We were here on a wet and rainy day and it really added to an enjoyable hike. Highly recommend all the trails although bug spray is a huge must with the grasses as thick as they are in places.

There are a few nice trails throughout the park. To be honest next time I would skip the 4$ museum. I don’t mind donating for the upkeep of some educational artifacts but it seemed a bit steep for a single room.
Really great views of Lake Okeechobee, but not really a lot of places to enjoy the park. The only majorly redeeming factor is access to the trail that runs around the entirety of the Lake.
The views say it all. We lucked out on a beautiful day and could see for miles. So much fun and an easy hike to the top. One of the must-do items on the list for Leelanau.
Fantastic park and short hikes when you want to take a respite from the wineries in Augusta. Make sure to hike the white sand beach and hike up to the viewpoint.
You don’t have to be a kid to really enjoy the Butterfly House. On a winters cold day the tropical butterfly house is a definite plus.
Wickedly cool old town in Leland. A great cheese shop and the kids loved the candy store. Many cute shops to wander into.

(Translated by Google) The largest park in the city! On the territory of the park there are tennis courts, picnic areas, with barbecue facilities, there is where to run. For children - a swing. Parking is free. Yes there is a mountain river, the water temperature is consistent. There are places for swimming along the river, in March two girls crossed the river along, we were eyewitnesses, the water was icy. There are sharp stones at the bottom. You can ride a bike :)

Самый большой парк в городе! На территории парка есть теннисные корты, picnic areas, с мангалами, есть где побегать. Для детей - качели. Паркинг бесплатный. Да есть горная река, температура воды соответствует. Вдоль реки есть места для купания, в марте месяце две девушки переплыли реку вдоль, мы были очевидцами, вода была ледяной. На дне острые камни.
