Stone Mountain State Park in North Carolina is a great state park that has many natural resources on display. There is no charge for admission to the park as it is free for all to enjoy and be a part of at no cost. The park is very clean and well maintained with plenty of nice trails to hike and experience and many other activities to participate in. The trails have varying levels of difficulty as there are easy trails and even more strenuous ones that can provide quite the work out. My favorite was the Stone Mountain Falls trail as you can see the waterfall all the way from the top to the bottom more the two hundred feet up and down. There are several other waterfalls on display nearby and they are all worth the hike to be a part of and feel. This is a great opportunity to be a part of nature and it is very accessible.

The Charleston Museum is a great experience that has been consistent and excellent throughout the years. I have been coming to The Charleston Museum ever since I could remember and it always seems to deliver a unique and educational experience every time no matter what year. I really like the exhibits about the history of Charleston and all of the different exhibits that rotate in and out. This museum is very well run and organized. I also really like the building and the feel it has with the architecture with the bricks and the courtyard. I also like the museum and its auditorium as an event venue as it is a good place to host different events and speeches. The Charleston Museum is awesome and I look forward to coming back here many times in the future.

Gorges State Park in North Carolina is a great park to get outside and be with nature in a great environment. The park is very well maintained and cared for as you can witness all of the work that went into making this magical place so accessible and easy to get to and navigate. The visitor center at this park is awesome and has many features including nice bathrooms, educational exhibits, beautiful views, and rocking chairs among many other cool things. I really like the trails at this park as they are somewhat challenging, but keep you going with all that they have to offer and have really good payoffs at the end. The Rainbow Falls one is great and well worth the trip and getting wet to get close to it and witness it.

Azalea Park in Summerville is one of my favorite parks as it has a lot of open green space to run around and enjoy. I like the bridges and sculptures throughout the park as they really add a lot of character and variety to the park. This is a great place for a picnic or to just find a nice spot to sit and relax on a busy day. There is plenty of activities to take part in in this park and there always seems to be something going on during different parts of the year. I have always found this park very clean and well maintained each time that I have been here. This is one of the best parks in the area and I look forward to being able to come here as often as I can to have a good time and get some fresh air.

Brittlebank Park on Lockwood Drive in Charleston is a one of my favorite parks. This is a nice wide open green space that is situated on the Ashley River and has unobstructed views of the water that are beautiful. Most times of the day this park is quiet and peaceful and is great for finding a spot to relax and clear your head in the middle of everything. I like having picnics here and even finding a nice spot to go fishing at this park. This is also a really good event space that can hold larger or smaller event very well. This park has plenty of trees and shade to keep you cool on a warm day. I have been coming to this park since before I could remember and have always had a positive experience here.

Marion Square is one of my favorite parks in Charleston. It is great to have this wide open green space in the middle of everything to find a quiet spot to sit, walk, read, lay out, have a picnic, have a meeting, or get some work done. Marion Square has good wifi that is useful when you need to connect. This is also a great event space several times a year where some of my favorite big events in Charleston are held and it is perfect for that purpose and seems to fit everything just right. There is also a lot of history to this site as you can feel all of the years of Charleston surround you any time of the day. Overall this is a really awesome park that I like to visit and use regularly and enjoy.

I really like the Gibbes Museum Of Art on Meeting Street in Charleston. I have been coming here since I was a little and this museum always seems to inspire imagination and inspiration to create. I like that there are really good exhibits, programs, and events held here that makes it seem like a different experience each time, but still familiar and something that you can remember and return and enjoy again. I like all of the pieces that show the history of Charleston and South Carolina and all of the different stories that they tell of all of the different centuries. This museum is very consistent in the quality it delivers. I look forward to being able to come back here many times in the future.

The Fort Sumter National Park Service Visitor Education Center is a great place to learn about the history of Charleston and of South Carolina. There are many displays and panels that are really educational and you can really learn about many different aspects of history and culture in addition to just Fort Sumter. I really like the big flag that they have on the wall. The best part is that it is free to visit and it is well worth your time to see all that they have to offer. The staff here is very friendly and knowledgeable and can answer questions you have about the history of Charleston. I look forward to being able to come back here in the future and learning more.

Hutchinson Square in Summerville is a really cool town square that is very Summerville and maintains the small town main street feel in the middle of a growing town. I like the renovations and all of the space it created and all of the different places features that it has. There are plenty of spaces to sit and relax and get some cool shade on a warm day and watch all of Summerville pass by. The park always seems to be clean and well maintained every time I have been there. I like when there is events here and it works well as an event space with plenty of room to move around. This is part of what makes Summerville a special place.

The Unitarian Church on Archdale Street in Charleston is a beautiful and historic church in the middle of everything. This church is very open and inviting and offers a warm welcome to anyone that wants to come in. I liked learning about the history of this church and was surprised at how long it has existed. I really like the interior of the church and all of the colors and architecture that it provides from the cool carpet to the bright stained glass windows and the ceiling and arches. I also like the outdoor area and the walkways and paths and landscaping. I have had a really positive experience every time that I have been here.

Cloudland Canyon State Park in Rising Fawn is an awesome state park that has plenty of scenic and panoramic view of mountains and canyons along with really cool trails for hiking. This park is well maintained and has much to offer to be in the middle of nature for hiking in the mountains and waterfalls. This park is easy to access and get right in the middle of everything and choose your adventure from there. They are well worth a visit for a memorable experience.

Gahagan Park on Boundary Street in Summerville is a great place to get some fresh air and run around when you need. I like that they have something for everyone with a lot of open space, athletic fields, and a playground. This park is well managed and maintained and always seems clean and taken care of. This park also works well as an event space. I have had a really good experience every time I have come here.

Caesars Head State Park in Cleveland is an excellent place to visit for some of the best Mountain Views in South Carolina. This park is well worth the visit for everything that you can see, do, and experience.  The park is well maintained from the lookouts to the visit center to all of the trails. I am happy that this park is here. This is a memorable park experience and one of my favorites to be a part of.

West Ashley Park is one of my favorite parks in the Charleston area. I like the large size of this park and all of the different features that it has to offer. This is a great place to get some fresh air and peace during a busy day or even have a picnic. This park is clean and well maintained throughout. I have had a lot of good times at this park and it has been very consistent throughout the years.

Rainbow Row on East Bay Street is a cool part of Charleston that is nice to check out when you are walking or driving. The colors are cool and a nice variety and it is something that adds a little flavor to the street. Little things like Rainbow Row are what makes Charleston a great place to be and visit. This is a nice and quick thing to see and show people. My favorite color is the green one.

Fairyland Caverns in Rock City Gardens on Lookout Mountain is an awesome dreamlike experience that transports you to another world and dimension. I really like how everything is arranged with the lighting and glow in the dark florescent paint. It is a living fairytale world that is meticulously crafted and detailed and cool to be a part of. This is one of my favorite parts of Rock City Gardens.

James Allen Park in Summerville is a cool park that is hidden in the middle of Summerville and provides a great place to stop during the middle of the day to get some fresh air and relax. I like that there is a trail and a bridge and water in the middle of the park. This park is well maintained and works well when you need a park for a picnic.

Rosebrock Park on Beech Hill Road in Summerville is a well managed  and maintained county park and has really good trails for hiking in the forest. This is a great place to go to during the middle or end of a busy day to relax and connect with nature in a meaningful way. I have had a really good experience every time I have been to this park.

Hunting Island State Park is a well managed and maintained state park that has much to offer including a great beach, a historic lighthouse, add on tours, and maritime forrest trails that are really cool. It is well worth the visit here as you can experience the nature and beauty of the coast that is well preserved and an unique experience.

St Philip’s Church is a beautiful and historic church. I really enjoy visiting here and being able to take in all of the history and architecture. They are warm and welcoming here and it is worth a visit if you are in the area. I have attended numerous services and events throughout the years and have always had a positive experience.

The Mace Brown Museum of Natural History is a cool museum on the campus of College of Charleston. They have really cool collections of dinosaurs and other interesting prehistoric creatures. I have learned a lot and have been surprised every time I have visited. I really enjoy this museum and it is a great educational resource.

Colleton State Park on Wayside Lane in Walterboro is a cool park that is perfect for kayak and canoe access on the river. The park is easy to access and has plenty of room and may not be as busy as some of the other parks which can be a good thing if you want some quiet and relaxation. This is a good park for river fun.

The Cathedral of Saint John the Baptist is a beautiful and historic church in the middle of Charleston. It has an awe inspiring interior with arches and stained glass windows. I really like being able to visit and attend services at this church. This is a great church overall.

Really cool place to walk around and enjoy Charleston with views of the harbor and historic homes. It is very walkable and accommodating with plenty of on street parking available at most any time. One of my favorite places to go and walk around at all times of the year.

The Basilica of the Sacred Heart of Jesus on Peachtree Street in Atlanta is a beautiful and historic church that is a great place to visit. I like the design of this church and everyone is warm and welcoming here. It is well worth checking out if you are in the area.

Don't ignore your guidebook's admonition to dress warmly. The difference in temperature from ground level is surprising. You'll love having your knit cap and down jacket! The night sky is startling up here. Even with just the naked eye you will marvel at how much we are missing when we view the sky from down below! Plus, everything about the center (at night, anyway) creates something of a hushed, awe-filled sense - the eerie red lights, the darkened giftshop, the out-of-place hot chocolate machine outside. There's a wonderful other-worldly sense of being on a movie set!
Staff members are gracious, very friendly, and quite knowledgeable. There are no exhibits nor any sort of introductory film. I'd have liked to know a bit more about the center itself - it's mission, specializations, finding, etc. There is only an odd and quaint video screen with some very old-style computer-BASIC script at the front desk which provides a little background. But it doesn't work very well so you end up just asking the staff what you need to know. The gift shop, as well, is quaint. An odd collection of merchandise: technology games, noodle soup, knit caps, parkas, and post cards. Also, of course, an array of astronomy-themed books, games, and toys. The eerie red lighting after dark is perfect for minimizing light pollution, but there are some tripping obstacles that can be problematic. (One young woman tripped over a curb and fell during my visit.)
There are announced star talks periodically. I thought we'd missed the last one of the day but was delighted when the PA System announced a group was gathering for another. The staffer who have the talk was great. She used a laser pointer to point out a dozen or more constellations, talked about the night sky in general, and the current night sky, specifically. She even worked in some Polynesian folklore and Hawaiian language. Well worth the drive if the night is clear.
dislikes: Lack of exhibits and introductory film

reviews_attraction.text:
You'll enjoy your visit best with a few simple preparations. Properly prepared, it's a great spot to visit!
First, be prepared for several types of experiences but taking a backpack with water, both sturdy-soled shoes (like athletic shoes or chakas AND water shoes, like flip flops. One trail is very rocky. One is on sand. And one is on boardwalk. Your feet will be happy is you can accommodate each surface.
Second, soak up all info you can before you begin AND grab all the different trail information fliers. The large park flier is a nice overview, bit leaves many questions unanswered. Like, we tried hard to find all the petroglyphs, once we figured out we were in the petroglyph section (which wasn't easy). But they are hard to spot. Finally at the end of that section, we saw a box designed to hold laminated descriptive fliers about the petroglyphs, but we'd already completed that part of the trail, and there was only one flier, and it was missing a page! Later we learned we could have picked up a free flier from the visitors center.
Third, they're is no introductory film and the ranger was only helpful if you asked specific questions. So be sure to ask lots of questions at the front end. Read what educational signage there is at the beginning and ask the ranger about what you'll be seeing.
Fourth, when near the water, look for turtles. The ones on the sand are easy to see, but lots are in the water, too. you just have to be watching.
The birds are gorgeous. We had field glasses, but no field guide, so we didn't know what birds we were seeing. Again... Ask in advance.
This place is larger than it appears; allow more time than you think you'll need.
dislikes: Limited staff assistance (ranger only helpful with specific questions)
Missing educational materials (no introductory film, incomplete fliers)

reviews_attraction.text: This is one of the finest galleries in the world for modern art and should not be missed, even for those with only a passing appreciation for modern art. And unlike most museums, the audio guide is free, actually works well, providing vivid and easily understood commentaries. On my first visit I arrived at 3:30 on a Friday afternoon. With wallet out, I was prepared to pay full admission and was informed by the sales desk that free admission begin at 4 pm on Fridays. Yay! I checked my coat (also free) and was delighted to find they were allowing free admission folks in 15 minutes early. I was able to attend one docent-led tour of just two paintings, but was disappointed. She basically just read her notes, and the audio guide commentary which I listened to later was more informative. But the collection not only did not disappoint, it far exceeded my expectations, and I was expecting a lot. The collections are thoughtfully arranged, and the signage is not distracting, yet very accessible. The guards in each Gallery do a good yet respectful job keeping the crowds at arm's length from the works, so even when the galleries are crowded, you can see all of the art well. It's wonderful that Moma allows picture taking, and I saw no one trying to sneak in a Flash photo. There is no point in referencing specifics about the collection, it simply is mind-boggling and fantastic.

This is a limited-time-only mediocre review, but due to installation of new exhibits, the collection was VERY limited during my visit. They were giving a reduced entrance fee, so I knew I wouldn't be seeing the full collection. But still....  I was shocked that only about 15 or 20 works were displayed. TOTAL! You're not told, on entering, just how limited the viewable collection is. I asked "is that all there is?" of three different guards (once I was finished), that's how incredulous I was that I'd seen everything. Also, the audio guides were clunky, difficult to use. The guards were poorly trained, knew nothing about the audio guides or the collection and didn't seem to care about visitors. Even the restaurant was closed. I had $75 in cash coupons, good for the restaurant (thanks, Hilton Grand Vacations) and I assumed the very small cafe would accept them since the restaurant was closed. Nope. Bright spots....Gift shop is nice and there are lots of staff in the lobby to help... But I wasn't sure what there was to help with?!?  The couple of works I did see were marvelous and I am anxious to go back on my next visit to NYC; just wish I hadn't wasted my time this time around.

We had only 2 hours so instead of purchasing the full package, we just bought the garden tour tickets. (Thanks to information staffers at the museum. They were a huge help.) That ticket allowed us to tour the history museum (well done; great chair exhibit if you're into furniture) and to see the short but very informative intro film. We toured the gardens of the governor's mansion, which are not in the greatest shape, but the venue is very attractive and the educational signage very informative. (Inside, and in the blacksmith's shop, re-enactors in costume provide info, but we didn't have tix for that.) We then walked through some of the buildings and gardens sprinkled through the historical District. Loved The Academy - a couple of blocks away - which has very well done exhibits of both the Academy and its role as a hospital during the civil war, and of the role of New Bern during the Civil War and subsequent era of Jim Crow law and a little bit of civil rights history in Craven Country. A shuttle service, free with your ticket,  makes getting from the museum to the Palace entrance easy. Only negative is that upkeep of the Palace garden needs a little boost.
likes: Civil War and civil rights history

reviews_attraction.text: Such a tiny, hidden gem! Ok, compared with  Chicago's Field Institute or NYs or DCs museums of natural history, it's zero stars. But for a tiny facility that is free and perhaps convenient during a visit to WS, it's delightful! Staff is on hand to answer questions and everyone was genuinely nice and concerned that my questions were answered. At one point, spouse and I were pondering a fine point of one of the exhibits. When we turned to the nearby receptionist (a student) to ask, he'd already started researching the question online! The exhibits change periodically and the only real cohesiveness is anthropology in general, but introductory panels provide an excellent overview of the many sub-specialties within the field. Clear efforts have been made to make the visit interactive, including an Escape Room option in the Africa room. Throughout, displays are nicely done with up to date and attractive signage and cases. There is clearly much love, great thought, and keen intelligence that goes into the exhibits and making this "mini museum"  worth the hour it'll take you to enjoy it.

Love this area and have hiked it in spring, summer and fall. This was my first winter hike here. Hiked from the Boulders Access point on this visit and loved the mix of wooded trails and lake side trails. Not too much elevation, but enough to get the circulation going!  In general, signage and blazing is exceptionally well done. Hard to get lost. One exception was shortly before midpoint when we had to search about 10 minutes for the trail. Turned out a blazed tree has fallen, just where the trail made a turn. Even after we found the Blazer on the fallen tree, it was difficult to know which why the blaze had originally pointed.
The loop trail we took Incorporated several other trails,  two with trailheads that had restrooms. Though the restrooms were primitive with TP but no hand sanitizer, it was nice that they were open, even in the dead of winter.
At one lakeside point there was an interesting homemade memorial to a pre-teen girl who apparently drowned at the spot several years ago. Nice that sort of memorial that is allowed by the park.

A home run for the National Park Service & a Must Do for anyone with an interest in the history of the American West, the Native American Indian, or military tactics in the war with the Indians. The ranger talk was the best I've ever heard... Full of detail and delivered with passion. The film, though shown on small screen, lived up to the high standards of the National Park Service. the museum was a bit uneven, some exhibits were quite well done, others a little on the cheesy side. But overall, the respect, the dignity, and the balance demonstrated in this presentation were extraordinary. As you walk about the property, which is on Crow reservation land for the most part, there are historical markers showing where both indian warriors and u. S. Cavalrymen died. The auto drive and tour are quite detailed and moving; you really feel that you are on sacred ground here, regardless of whether your sympathies are with the American Indian, the American soldier and the government, or somewhere in between.

DON'T MISS IT! We'd toured the museum previously on another trip through the area. This time we came intentionally to take in the center more thoughtfully, and to participate in the bus tour. Oh my gosh -- what a fabulous glimpse into another time. The volunteers who lead the tour were amazing. One was a retired college history professor, another a chemist. They really made the history of Oak Ridge come alive, and the knowledge they imparted was invaluable to appreciating the area's place in US and world history. Our 11 year old grandson (a history buff) enjoyed the visit as much as we did, and he learned so much. Recently, i watched a NOVA special on WWII and the bomb that ended it. Thanks to my visit to Oak Ridge, i heard and understood nuances I'd have missed otherwise. A must do experience for any student of WWII, the America of the late 40s, and of nuclear energy.

Gorgeous, rigorous, rewarding walk to a river, a waterfall, & a beach. Or, just to a lookout point if you're not in the mood for a steep-grade hike! The grade going down (and back up!) averages 25% so it's pretty good exercise, plus you have to be alert for, and step aside for, passing 4-wheel drive vehicles! ( Nice to see that most of the vehicles carried locals, not tourists!) When I was there it had rained all morning so the river could only be passed by wading through, which added a bit of adventure, but that same rain meant that all three waterfalls were visible high above us! The surf at the black sand beach was gorgeous and surfers and fisherman were all in great spirits. Flora throughout the hike is breathtaking with many amazing blossoms of all colors in every direction. (my visit was in early April). Take water, a poncho, and flip flops to change into.

Nice place to hike for a couple of hours, or longer if you loop around on some of the Mountains to the Sea connecters.  Very easy to get to. Trailhead is right off the road, with restrooms, trail maps, and educational and historical signage. Beware, parking lot fills up, but there are people leaving all the time since there are a number of shorter trails. The lower falls are easy to get to and nice to relax at. The high to the upper falls is another story. All paths are well worn and the hiking is perfect... Not too easy, not too rigorous. And where there is signage, it's helpful, easy to read, easy to follow. Problem is.... There are lots of turns & intersections that are not marked. You just scratch your head and flip a coin. Fortunately, even a wrong turn doesn't take you terribly far afield!

Attended the "First Day Hike" on January 1. Co-led by a NC and a SC ranger. Wish rangers had been more informative throughout the hike, and arrangements for transport back to parking lot were poorly done. BUT the park and the facilities themselves are great. It's clear neither state is investing enough in its parks, but the terrain is beautiful and the trails are well maintained and daily well marked. I've visited the area in summer when all facilities are open and staffed, so I felt bad for first time visitors who weren't treated to the nicely appointed & informative visitors center operations. But overall, this is a park Carolinians can be proud of.

An easy, paved round-trip trail, this hike is accessible to almost anyone, yet the views are some of the most stunning on the island. Photo ops abound at the top, and the educational signage - especially at the trailhead - will add excellent historical and geological perspective to your visit. (If you are too excited to stop and read it at the start of your hike, catch it at the end.)   I was there in early April and looked and looked for whales - to no avail. But if you go in February or early March, the whale watching surely must be spectacular. Allow an hour at a moderate pace. High energy hikers could run it in a fraction of that time.

This is a great experience, even though the zoo is slightly old style, and many of the exhibits were closed due to the cold weather. To my surprise even the Polar Bear exhibit was closed, but I learned later it was because the Polar Bear died the week before. Every staff member we talked to was extremely kind and helpful. It was a very slow day and we practically had the zoo to ourselves. The 4D movie was excellent. We literally had the entire theater to ourselves for that! Many of the restrooms were closed, which was a bit inconvenient, but I completely understand in view of the weather and the few visitors that day.

Tiger World is small, but the animals appear to be well cared for, the cages and environment clean, and the staff knowledgeable. Some of the signage is incomplete and slightly dated, but it's obvious they're putting an effort into educating the public on the animals as well as climate & environmental threats. A few volunteers or staff mingling amongst visitors offering education and answering questions would be a very nice addition; most were very busy cleaning, feeding, running the gift shop, etc. Go to Group On before you visit; you'll save considerably by purchasing your tickets there.

The "Behind the scenes" tour was fabulous, included a tasting of four varietals, and was a good bargain. you can follow the tour with a visit to the open wine tasting room. And taste even more delicious North Carolina wines.. TIP:  Plan your winery tour for the day following your visit to the estate, purchase it over the telephone, and if you ask, they will include a second day admission pass to the estate for no extra charge.

Such a gem! From the history of cameras and film, to the opportunity to dub a voice over, to a tribute to Martin Scorcese, this place has it all! Film students, critics, and makers will find the collection captivating; more casual film lovers will like the many interactive displays. Well designed screening rooms make this a "living" museum that's attractive to those active in filmmaking today.

Simple welcome center but worth a stop. Displays are OK. Volunteer staffer was knowledgeable and anxious to help though she'd only been there a month. The path out into the man made lakes was well done and loaded with geese, ducks, and turtles. Saw one other critter scamper across the path - maybe a fox or coyote pup. Observation tower allows nice view of the area.

The small visitors center has a few exhibits worth a look, a small gift shop, and telescopes trained on interesting sights within the refuge. The refuge itself provides a wonderful opportunity to walk along a well maintained path past man made lakes and estuaries, to a 20 foot viewing tower. Nature lovers should allow 45 minutes to explore.

We loved this lovely hike on the beautifully shaded, well defined Manoa Falls Trail. Gorgeous falls at the end and an interesting, easy trail to get there. Terrific bird watching. Stop for one of the excellent shaved ice cups at the family owned and managed tiny gift shops after your hike! Over 44 types of home made syrups!

What a treat! Though the focus is heavily on the Confederate side of things, all displays are professional, accurate, attractive. Guest experts were there showing guns of the war and flags of the war. Those experts were interesting, patient, and enthusiastic about their topics.  So glad we went!

Small but well displayed collection in a beautiful seeing. I love the building. Great kids programming. Very nice glass pieces and an impressive Chihuly in the entrance area. Wish they had audio guides available and free daily docent tours.

A short, beautiful, satisfying hike with interesting flora, some educational signage, culminating in breathtaking 360° degree views. Just a short drive from the small, staged visitors center, which has clean, stocked restrooms.
Lovely trail, nicely marked & platformed over swampy areas. Enough flora and fauna to make it interesting. Very few other hikers, which was nice. But still a lot of mosquitos. Ugh.
Parking a nightmare, but the facility itself is perfect for a large meeting. Lots of great audio visual support, good acoustics, comfortable seating.

Beautiful scenic view at the top of Crowders Mountain. We took our kids (9, 6 and 4 years old) to a hike and our goal was to reach The Pinnacle. Generally it would take 1 hour with an steady pace walk, but because our little ones, it took us 1.5 hour extra time, as we had to stop several times to rest, drink water, have snacks and make sure they didn't do crazy things in the trail. There is a section of the trail with rocks where the kids can climb fairly safely (with the watch of adults), and they loved it.

The trail is strenuous at some parts, with rocks  and roots making it easy to trip over and fall.
My advice: take it easy and enjoy nature. Take the opportunity to discover around and don't rush.
In our way back, we took the Thumback trail, which cut our walk half the time. But it's not preferred for going up if you are not used to hikes.

This park is a hidden gem in the Carolinas. Perfect park to come with little family and friends. It has different levels of bikes suiteable for kids, elders and people with disabilities.

There are four fishing spots. One of them is handicap accessible.
Plenty of room for picnics, cook out and run. We came with our kids and they had a blast running around, fishing and just enjoying nature.
The trees and plants are described with a good sign so anyone can learn about the types of diversity this park is full off.
You might hear the owls in the evenings and some deer running.

Beautiful mountain and state park. There are plenty spots for swimming, fishing and having picnics.

It is well maintained and the roads are paved in most of the park.
Looking forward for some catch and release fishing soon. Be aware some areas of the river are private property beside the park, be nice and don't leave trash behind.

Beautiful waterfalls and plenty of space for people to hang out. We had launch and snacks.
Be careful with the stones being slippery when wet.

The trail is easy and we'll marked. Downhill all the way to the falls, but be ready for a workout when returning to your vehicle.

Our kids loved this place.

It is a beautiful park, well maintained and with plenty of room to walk, run and enjoy the park. There is a nice playground for the young kids, two baseball fields, two shelters, a batting cage and good parking space.

The Police station is right beside it.

Very nice park with two trails that are well maintained.
The reservoir is located 1.3 miles from the parking lot.
The only downside: there is not a public restroom (or porta-potty).
The landscape is beautiful and waterfalls so calm and refreshing.

Great place to come with the entire family and have a picnic, do some hiking, swim in the small beach area, fish from the pier or rent canoes/kayaks to enjoy the lake. Good amenities, clean bathrooms and wheelchair accessible in many areas.

This is an "OK" pier. This past summer the price was $9 per person to fish. $1 just to walk in at the pier.
It doesn't have rod holders as other piers.
At night, the view is amazing to contemplate the sunset and reeling in a nice catch.

Beautiful park with picnic tables and grills. Restrooms and parking area. Plenty of space in the creek for kids to play.

Fishing is allowed but only catch and release. Single hook, and artificial lutes or flies. No bait.

Beautiful waterfall beside the road. Advice: don't park as someone might get hurt. Slow down and ask the passenger to take photos/videos. Going up the mountain there is a place you can see the entire valley. Amazing view.

How much fun we have had at Lazy 5 Ranch. We even saw some wild deer running at full speed at front of our vehicle and climbing up the hill. That was pretty rad for all of us.
The kids loved the ride and feed the animals.

Beautiful park with several trails and waterfalls.
The kids had a lot of fun.
There are picnic tables, restrooms,  plenty of parking space and great staff.

During the weekends it is crowded, but worth the visit.

We love coming to this train station/museum. Even it is a short ride, it provides a good entertainment for the whole family.

The round house is a great stop to learn how the trains were being serviced.

Fun place for the whole family. Space to run, play volleyball, Frisbee golf court, ride bicycles. There is a nice playground area with splash pad for the kiddos.
And boat landing for the lake.

Very nice hanging bridge with amazing views.
Please, keep a good watch of your kids, if they run around there are no fences or anything to stop them to fall out from the ledges.

Beautiful lake in the middle of Blowing Rock, at walking distance from downtown.
You can walk around it, it is perfect for photoshoots.

There are ducks coming here sometimes.
Great place to do some kayaking, hiking, picnic or just relax in a beautiful park. Well cared and maintained. Police patrol this park very often which makes you feel safe.

Nice spot beside the road in the Blue Ridge Parkway.
There is plenty of space for vehiclea to park. But only one picnic table.

The view is limited by the tall trees.
Very nice park, with a creek running through it. It is well maintained. It has several baseball fields, a Walking/cycling trail and playground.
Well kept park with plenty of trails and options. Boat launch area, beach, restrooms, picknick tables, mountain bike trails and a lot more.

Great play public beach access. Parking spots, showers and restrooms.
There is also an small playground for the kids and picnic tables.

Great place to bring the kids and family. We usually do picnics here, fishing and rest in the sand.

It's well maintained and cared.

Fun place to bring the kids, play soccer, run or have a picnic. Good and clean facilities.
It has a freebie golf course as well.

Cool museum with a good amount of artifacts.
Spacious areas to roam around, there is a cafeteria and a gift shop as well.
likes: Facilities & Services: Spacious, Cafeteria, Gift Shop

reviews_attraction.text: Beautiful architecture piece to adorn Savannah's port area. It doesn't distort the old view of this side of the town.

As someone who works in this building, I can attest to the Willis Tower having amazing views of the city. However, it's fairly expensive and you should be prepared to wait in long lines to get up and get back down again. A fast pass (for a lot more money) will get you up faster, but not down any faster. At the top, there isn't much in the way of amenities other than a gift shop, but after all, you should really be there for the views. In my honest opinion, I would go to the John Hancock Tower instead. It's nearly as tall, has many of the same views (plus it's closer to the lake), and you can go up for free if you choose to eat at their reasonably-priced restaurant and bar. For me, it's a better deal for views of Chicago.

While a nice scenic spot, don't plan to spend too much time here. It's very small, and the walking paths are short (many of them have been closed off, although locals seem to disregard the signage to get near to the water). We were wondering why most people parked on the road leading into the parking lot, rather than the lot itself, until we realized there is a $5 parking fee for non-Hawaii residents. Even though it's not technically an entrance fee, we were happy to pay it to support the parks. If you're around the Wailuku/Kahului area, it may be worth a quick stop, but I would not make it a destination.

As far as escape rooms go in Chicago, I think this is the best one that I've done. We did "Prison Break", and the decor and props were top notch. You could tell that they actually put some effort into the experience, and the clues were just helpful enough that you didn't feel as though you were cheating the experience by using the occasional one. I also really appreciated the needed for collaboration (you'll have to play it to really find out why). The staff was friendly, and the price was comparable to other places. I'll be back to try their other games, for sure.

Beautiful, buy potentially dangerous. The path starts at the top of Punahele Road (there is a small parking lot and signs pointing to the trailhead), and winds its way down to the shoreline. The relatively short trail is full of roots and mud on many days, and is not best for sandals. There are a few signs warning people of the dangers of Queen's Bath and they should not be ignored. Stay a safe distance from the edges, never turn your back to the water and don't even bother in high surf. However, the view is spectacular when the weather and sea permit.

Great place to bring kids and enjoy a few hours away while still being in the "city". Nice network of unpaved and paved trails to enjoy a number of activities: splash near the river, have a picnic, do some hiking, go for a bike ride. The wooded area is undergoing some significant reforestation, and the trails are not really well marked or maintained (wash outs, fallen trees, rickety bridges and stairs), but it is still a nice place to go, just with a bit of caution, especially for younger children.

Lovely setting along the lake to enjoy the many museums and attractions on offer, or just take in the lake and skyline. The only downside is parking, where it will cost you an arm and a leg to park in spots that are quite a hike to where you probably want to be (unless Soldier Field is your destination). Given that public transportation also isn't very convenient (other than the bus), best to take a cab or ride share, or carpool.

A beautiful place to watch the waves and kite surfers, but be careful what you leave in your vehicle. It's such a nice string of small beaches along the coast, but there are quite often a number of people wandering around. Given that most of the locals leave their vehicles empty and unlocked, no doubt theft can be an issue. So for vacationers, I recommend not bringing anything of real value that you won't take with you.

We came for the dog beach, and had a great time on a wonderful strip of sand in the Gulf of Mexico. There are lots of playful dogs, and nice amenities such as a hosing station to have a worry-free time. Fees were reasonable, but we made sure to come early, as the crowds really build on nice days. By the time we were leaving in the early afternoon, the lineup along the causeway was quite long.

Absolutely stunning. You just wouldn't expect such a spectacular topography only a few minutes and miles from tropical beach. The colors and cliffs defy description, and are amazing by car, by foot or by helicopter. I suggest driving to the end of the road into Napali Coast State Wilderness Park, then back through the Koke'e State Park and eventually to Waimea Canyon State Park.

I love the level of interactivity here, especially for younger children. There are a wide variety of spaces to explore, and many of them are designed to engage both the children and the adults, too. It's not cheap, especially if you park onsite, but there are hours of fun to be had, and there are adjoining areas to relax, eat and see the rest of the Chicago shoreline.

Beautiful park overlooking the world. It's a long, winding drive up the mountain, and perhaps more challenging one back down, but the rewards are with it. Expect it to be 20-30 degrees cooler at the summit, so pack appropriately. There are only limited facilities once you leave Kahului, so be prepared. Popular at sunrise and sunset.

Worth a quick stop. Not too much to do here as the beach is very rocky and there are only minimal nearby facilities, but the sand really is black, and wonderfully granular in the feet (and in your hand). Unfortunately we didn't see any turtles around while we were there, but that's probably just the timing or season.

Spectacular location on Kauai. You have to view Napali from the bottom and the top (and maybe, if you're lucky, both by helicopter), but the drive up to Napali really gives you the sense of the altitude change, and the views are other-worldly. Best to get here early so you can experience it without the crowds.

This is a nice, quiet park nestled between houses. It's different from the other neighborhood parks because it's really meant as a place of relaxation, rather than a playground. Meandering paths, benches and bushes, with lush grassy areas are great for reading a book, having a picnic or just enjoying the day.

Nice variety of play structures for big and small kids. Also a nice set of benches for adults, and a grassy area to play on away from the other equipment. It is at a busy intersection and has two separate gates, so attention must be paid at all times to where kids are in and around the park.

A great place right in the city that feels as though you're miles away from it. The views of the lake and skyline can be spectacular, and because it's hidden away next to the museum campus, it's not terribly busy. This makes for a great place to escape, even if for a short period of time.

Beautiful spot on the north coast of the Big Island. However, you cannot get down to the beach without a 4x4 or a significant hike. Most people just look from afar, and it you're familiar with the north coasts of other Hawaiian islands, you will know that it can get quite rainy at times.

Amazing piece of nearly unspoilt coast. The road is rough and sandy enough for pickups and Jeeps, but you see a fair number of subcompact cars making the nearly 5-mile journey off the pavement to get there. It's well worth it if you can endure the bumps and not get stuck on the beach.

Great place for a quick stop. You can walk a short distance and see the blowhole from afar, or spend 15-20 minutes hiking in to experience it up close. Caution should be exercised, as the coast can always be dangerous, so best to not take young children too close.

Nice neighborhood dog park with plenty of room. Especially like the water hoses, doggie refuse bags, and separate section for smaller dogs. Be aware that the L tracks are right next door, so dogs who don't like loud noises may be a bit frightened.

Nice little park tucked away on bustling Southport. Has a few slides and climbing equipment, but no swings. The ground is soft rubber, and there's also a chalkboard, a drinking fountain and a few benches. Good for a short stop.
Wonderful gallery space, with expert staff and even an enjoyable museum shop. Their exhibitions are always very well done. Parking, however, is expensive and the attached lot is frequently very full.
Nice, tranquil park in Central Florida. Popular for swimming in the spring, kayaking on the river, and picnicking in the park. If you bring a pet, know that some trails are off-limits to dogs.
Great spot to capture a panoramic view of Chicago. Staircase on the southwest corner connects to the River Walk below.
It's hard to beat a free zoo in the heart of the city. Well-maintained year-round, there's lots to see and do.

Great hike! The views of the river and the hidden bamboo forest are your reward for suffering through the steep inclines & declines. As others said I wouldn’t recommend this hike when it’s raining or has recently rained (it can be quite muddy in sections of the trail). Hiking pools will help with stability for the inclines and declines. The trail is well marked but pay attention to the markers or you’ll get lost. The bamboo forest is between E16 and E 26. If you are short on time the fastest route there from the Indian trail head is to walk down the gravel road and enter the trail from the end point at E13 and from there hike to E21, E22, E23, E17, E16 to E26 and then double back. Come early on the weekends by 9:30am the lot was full, parking is $5 (paid online), they do tow cars out there and the road in and out is single lane traffic so watch for oncoming cars as you’re driving in and exiting. Enjoy!

Met up with a hiking group here for an early morning hike on a Sunday (around 7:30am) parking is $5 and there were plenty of spaces. However by the time we wrapped up at 10am there were no spaces so come early on the weekends. We did parts of the green and yellow trails (our route ended up being 3 miles). The hard core folks connected with the red trail to do 3 more miles — I had chocolate chip pancakes on the brain from the blue eyed daisy so I called it a day...lol The trail was shaded, gradual inclines, the waterfall and places along the trail where you’re climbing the granite added to the scenery. If I didn’t live so far away I’d probably visit more. It was worth driving down south to explore. Enjoy!

Went here on a Saturday morning and it wasn’t too crowded. There was even a race going on there for the 4th (limited capacity of people due to c19). The trail ended up being about 5k and loops around so I didn’t get lost even when parts of it were blocked of due to fallen trees (I just cut through one of the disc golf tees. If you do cut through a disc golf path  please pay attention so you don’t get hit by a disc zooming by your head). Otherwise when you’re on the trail you are free to zone out (listen out for bikes calling out on your left). The trail is loose gravel so wear the right shoes. I’ll definitely be back for another weekend stroll. Enjoy!

Even on a cloudy day this park serves up scenery! I did the paved trail around miller late and it was wonderful. A mix of runners, walkers & bikes but everyone is maintaining space. There are several unpaved trails that veer off of the paved trail in case you want to hike a little. The only thing to watch out for is there are tons of spider webs along the paved trail make sure you don’t walk into one because some of the spiders are huge. Other then that I’ll definitely be back to explore more of the park. Enjoy!!!

We were in the area hiking so decided to pop in to buy a couple bottles to take home. Beautiful property, they had live music and a food truck. No tastings on the weekends due to COVID but will let you sample before buying a glass or bottle. Would love to come back and sip for awhile when I’m not funky from hiking..lol People wore masks while in the tasting room, hand sanitizer was everywhere, also kept their distance from each other and outside there was room to spread out. Enjoy y’all!
dislikes: No tastings on weekends (due to COVID)

reviews_attraction.text: It was worth the hour drive to me from Duluth. The museum is open but you have to book a spot online in advance because of COVID so I just explored the mounds and trail along the perimeter. Beautiful scenery by the river with benches to sit for awhile. I enjoyed climbing up the mounds. Cool place I’d go again. Have fun! Oh yeah as with most state parks parking is $5.

Nice shaded trail. Once you pass the lake the scenery is a little dull but shade, not a lot of roots and gradual inclines makes it an easy 2 miles that I’d do again. Next time I’ll bring my pup. One note, I had on sneakers next time I’ll wear my trail shoes for some grip on the gravel section and on the parts that have granite. Besides that enjoy!!!

Making spirits bright for sure! We visited Santa’s Fantastical for some holiday cheer and of course cool pics for IG. The staff was super friendly and helpful with taking pics. The show was good I almost skipped it - glad I didn’t. We visited on a week night so we had room to move about since it was less crowded.

Great short hike. I did a 2.5 mile loop but you can make your hike longer or shorter. Exploring the mill ruins and hopping rocks along the shoal was cool. Don’t forget to stop by the lake. Also if you cross over one of the mountain biking trails be sure to pay attention so you don’t get hit. Enjoy the trails!!

Gravel and dirt trail that runs along a creek with an mill ruins and connects to the silver comet trail. I only gave it 3 stars because as others said it can be extremely muddy (if there has been recent ran). Other than the mud which makes the trail slippery we enjoyed our stroll.

Exactly what I needed for a Sunday stroll - beautiful scenery, a few hills to make it a work out and a variety of distances to choose from. Loved this park - can’t wait to see what it looks like in spring. Was worth the 25 minute drive over to Woodstock - enjoy!

It’s ok. I probably won’t go back again. The pluses for me were the mile long paved trail and the side trail to get down to the river. The minuses were the sewage, weed and cat pee smells that hit my nose quite a few times while roaming along the river trails.

Nice open green fields and a few ok views of the river (also boat ramp to enter the river). Me and the pup took a walk around here. It was ok. I live in the area so I’m checking off parks. This was a one & done for me.

This is one of my favorite places in Atlanta. Me and the pup love taking early morning strolls here. There’s two entrances (one side has dog park & playground) and the other side has the old farm buildings. Enjoy!!
Stairs, stairs, stairs and more stairs. Excellent workout, bring OFF, bring water and snacks, bring your mask (for passing others or resting on the various platforms) and enjoy the beautiful scenery!
Lovely place inside the perimeter to roam around. The trail is marked well but pay attention to the map because you have to cross the street two times in order to do the entire 3 mile trail. Enjoy!
Nice place for a short stroll with or without your pup. Nice size parking lot and bathrooms available. We came early morning (before 9am) so not that many cars. Enjoy! We did!
Me and the pup walk here a few times a week since it’s so close to home. We are early am strollers so there’s not a lot of foot traffic when we are there. Enjoy your stroll!
We stopped by after taking pics of the old mill. You can sample 4 wines for free. We purchased two bottles - one wine & one cider. Worth a look see if you’re in the area.
Zen. Nothing more to say except go and get yourself some of it here ASAP. It was worth my 40 min drive to spend a couple hours relaxing. Bring a book and your lunch.
This is a peaceful and cool place. Totally worth the drive from metro Atlanta. The rock castles are so neat and they sit along a meadow so it adds to the scenery.
Nice in town hike. You can easily forget that you’re in the city. Parking is a little tight if you get there after 9am other than that it’s great. Enjoy y’all!
Worth the drive. Grab yourself an open gate ticket & go. Be careful hiking down to the falls (it’s very rocky). I used hiking poles for that section. Enjoy!!!
We enjoyed the “waterfall” it’s very peaceful and chill back there on the shoals. I imagine this spot gets packed in the summer. Enjoy!
Nice pit stop for a photo op. There are a few benches to sit on so you can even bring lunch to enjoy the view of bridge and water.

I came here today for the first time and thought Google Maps had misdirected me (wouldn't be the first time). I drove through a residential area that turned into a dirt road ending at Winnebago Rd. There was a parking area for hikers but no trail map nor even a trail head marker.
I followed the yellow trail for about half an hour until it abruptly ended on the bank of the lake. The white trail connected at the yellow's terminus and I followed that around the lake. The coolest part of the hike was seeing a beaver dam. There's also a road around most of the lake that seems to be used by dirtbikes or quads that allows you to get up against the water. But all in all, it was a mediocre hike with a relatively flat trail that seems to be minimally up kept.

This was, by far, one of the best interactive museums I've ever been to. It was immersive in that we got to tour an actual Tenement house from the 1800s and see how people lived when they immigrated to NYC. Appalling conditions... Sometimes a family of twelve would share a three room apartment with one window and no electricity!
We took the Sweatshops tour and saw the setup of a Jewish immigrant family who had a garment sewing business in their tiny apartment. It was amazing to see what people did to scrape a living when they came here and how much America has changed. Truly a mind bender. We ended up becoming museum members so we can come back and take the rest of the tours they offer!

I'm glad me and my sister came here. We're fans of NJ as well as fans of this museum.
Our favorite exhibit, which was PERFECT for kids, the animals and dinosaur room, was interactive and fun and informative.
Signage regarding which animals are found where would be helpful. There were things like toucans and jaguars, stuffed. The taxidermy was amazing but I was confused why some of it was in a museum about our great state.

Walked through 2/3 of the exhibits in less than an hour.

Cute little shop with lots of NJ paraphernalia. Loved some of them for gifts or tchotchkes.

One Andy Warhol print of Jackie O. And one Roy Liechtenstein pop art. Would recommend.

This place is pretty dope, with a fairly easy elevation gain from the trailhead to the overlook point. There's also a sweet reservoir, with picnic tables and a playground for the kids. My friend and I went in February (unseasonally warm) and spent a nice afternoon hiking along the well-maintained trails and enjoying the tranquility.
Bonus: the nature center had a maple-tapping event the day we were there!

Many of the trails lead up to a lookout point with gorgeous views. Easy to spend an hour or two hiking and exploring among the moss-strewn boulders. I took the blue and white trails and got a great workout!

We didn't make it for the Van Gogh, Monet, and Degas exhibit, but we checked out the museum otherwise. There's not much to see. The recreated 19th century sitting rooms are magnificent. The building itself gives you a real sense of the era of the height of Pittsburgh and the influence of men like Henry Clay Frick. But as far as extensive exhibits, you won't find much here.
There is, however, an impressive car and carriage museum on the site with impressively restored cars from the 1920s and earlier. The guide was extremely knowledgeable, and we got to sit in a 1930s Model A!

This is a pretty, kid-friendly place. My friend and I drove here from Central Jersey (just over an hour) for a peaceful afternoon by the falls.

There's a wooden staircase leading to the top of the falls, and some trails from that point. It's really cool. You're level with the falls the entire time, and there are great views.

Plenty of parking. And on a hot day, you can bathe in the pool at the bottom. Some guys had climbed the waterfall itself, but I wouldn't recommend that unless you're a sure footed climber with water shoes on.

So weird. I parked here and didn't see any clearly marked paths. Now that I'm reading other reviews, I must have missed something?

The path I took led me to the Deer Blind on the creek. In early spring, it was muddy and had a lot of sticker bushes. Trail maintenance mediocre.

Took me about fifteen minutes to walk to the water. Very peaceful. The only sounds I heard were water, planes, and birds.

Might return to find the marked paths.

Near S Hunterdon HS

This museum is quite large, with varied exhibits. My favorite was the Impressionism gallery, with paintings from Monet, Renoir, and Degas. There was even a Van Gogh thrown in.
The modern art was impressive, and there were even a few PGH artists thrown in the mix. But, for all its space and diversity, I wish there had been more of a focused theme for the collection of paintings upstairs.
6/10 would return on future trips to the burgh.

Not sure if we missed some of this park, but I felt like we did.
There were some observation decks and access points to the beach (where you cannot swim).
The lighthouse was closed during the COVID pandemic... As was the visitors center.
I wish there had been a map of the park outside the visitors center, tho.
Def would come back during the migration to see the birds!

This place has definite creepy vibes, but is great for a hike or casual stroll. The real hidden gem is the NJAA observatory tucked away here. It has a massive powerful telescope that the NJAA casually uses to observe and photograph the cosmos. It's open to visitors on Saturdays and is completely free. Check it out if you're at all interested in the stars!

Very cool historical place in NJ. We took a free tour of the Ford mansion and got to see where GW himself slept. Amazing to imagine life 300 years ago when there was barely any development here. The story of the soldiers in winter was jarring as well, and the museum did a great job of showing us what it was like. Good for kids.

This place is expansive and beautiful! Perfect for a date or a picnic and it's 100% free to peruse. Beware that it closes at sundown, and the attendant will come looking for you if you linger!
On Saturdays in the spring, they even have a farmers market with fresh meats and fruits and vegetables. Definitely worth a visit!

This place is amazing, with sculptures reminding you how small you are. I went on a hot day in July, and in addition to rides in golf carts, storm king gives free water away to patrons.
Storm King is large and stunning, a perfect day trip for any season. I look forward to coming back with a picnic basket.

Loved it. Tranquil, gorgeous, clearly marked paths. We saw ospreys, terns, ducks, and one more endangered bird species.
Mad respect for the people who preserve this place. It's sad that this is one of the last places unique species can habituate. Down with Cape May development!

Had a nice, intimate free tour with one of the docents.
Very cool impermanent exhibits.
The space is well preserved and taken care of.
Thought the gift shop could have more art pertaining to the exhibits.
$8 student entrance fee, $12 regular fee.

Interesting signage relating to the history of this settlement/area. Broken down buildings abound behind this parking area/ranger office/forest trailhead. The yellow trail along the river (kind of) rocked. I'd come back for a few hours!

As always, I enjoy visiting for an afternoon. Beware the summer crowds.
I just wish they had rotating installations outside (inside, there are always new, featured artists). Keep doing what you're doing, GFS!

Excellent place for a brief or long hike. Being next to the water is incredibly soothing, and the paths are well trimmed and clean. I even saw a blue heron take off from the water.i felt truly blessed!
I really like coming here to sit on the rocks next to the river and waterfall. There's a walking trail along the river, a gondola, a playground, and a basketball court. Local gem.
Stopped here for a picnic at the upper part of the park near 202. Picnic tables scattered throughout, clean (campground style, no electric) bathrooms, and a dog park. Lovely time.
There's something for everyone here. Walking trails that connect to the LHT. a covered picnic area. Beach volleyball court. Lake for fishing and boating. Great for a Sunday walk.
This is where dreams are made. Tubing, hiking, waterfalls, camping. This place is so worth the drive from Central Jersey for a day or afternoon of fun.
Why haven't you been here already? This place is crazy cool! The museum is very informative and the Ford mansion is authentically preserved.

Nice to walk around. Could not go in during COVID pandemic.
Def got the suspicion this place is haunted, but...
Nice for a day trip.
This place is very cool. There are walking and hiking trails very easy to access. I set up my hammock and called it a day.

Wow! What a beautiful and we'll used nature park! The trails offer a good workout and extremely beautiful veiws of the area. There are several swimming holes and picnic tables along the way! During my visit, I hiked 5 miles and I feel like I only touched a bare minimum of hiking options. There is a trail here that supposedly connects to the Appalachian Trail, which I hope to find. The only downside is there are no printed trail maps available at the park entrance. There are no restrooms available. There are two sizable parking areas available, however by 2 pm they were full and cars were waiting to find spots open. My recommendation is to go early if you want parking and a good swiming spot!

This Historic Battlefield has so much to offer! It has a wonderful history/visitor center. There are several trails for biking, running or walking. There are so many monuments to explore. There is even a driving tour you are able complete and listen to points of interest through an app.

If you stop by here, male sure to visit Wilder Tower to see the amazing view of the battlefield and surrounding mountains.

This is one of my favorite places to take a stroll and enjoy nature. Definitely worth a little drive to explore some history.

I LOVE this park! I usually just float the lazy river but the slides are awesome too. There are at least 5 big slides and a really nice kids section.  It can be crowded at times but still is worth it! There are tons of tables w/chairs as well as lounge chairs. There are huge community cabana awnings so you can get out if the sun as well. They have cabanas for rent  which comes with some extras. They have a really nice gift shop and concession stand serving a variety of food.  This is a great place for a day trip.

This is one of the most beautiful views in  Chattanooga!

It is a must see whether you are a local or a tourist. It is a short walk from the parking area to the viewing area where you can enjoy a beautiful panaramic view of the Chattanooga valley. If you are an adventurous spirit, there are several hiking trails to explore.

This area is also known for experienced rock climbing.

This beautiful Tennessee State Park is located approximately  an hour and a half from Chattanooga.

It has several breathtaking  waterfalls and scenic overlooks. There are multiple  hiking trails. The park offers various lodging and camping options as well.

If you are seeking a beautiful waterfall adventure, I promise you this park will not disappoint.

This 2 mile trail to the falls and back is fairly easy. The rainbow lake falls are beautiful after heavy rains. During the summer they are pretty dry. The swing bridge is pretty neat. If you cross over the creak you are on a section of the Cumberland Trail. There is a campsite just up the side of the mountain on the opposite side of the creek.

This is an amazing art museum in one of the most beautiful areas of Chatanooga. It is not a large museum, however it offers very interesting and beautiful exhibits.  The historical experience is a plus. The museum is also a spot on the Chattanooga ghost tours.

This is a nice enjoyable hike no matter the season. Since it has been a little dry there was not much water flowing so we were able to hike up the creek bed.  This is a really easy hike and there are some beautiful rock formations to see and enjoy!

Foster falls is absolutely gorgeous!. Pretty steep hike down to the bottom of the canyon to view the base of the falls but it is definitely worth it. There is a really cool swinging bridge to cross over the creek get a good view of  the falls.

This is a beautiful overlook with a breathtaking view! The hike to the overlook is only 2 miles from the Woody Gap parking area. There is a bit of a climb right before reaching the view, but it is definitely worth it.

This Tennessee State Park is amazing because of its natural beauty and history. The Old Stone Fort Loop Trail showcases all of the beautiful waterfalls the park has to offer.

It is definitely worthy of a day trip!

This visitor center is very nice and has lots of unique and relative souvenirs. The historical buildings are really interesting to explore. The drive through the Cove is absolutely beautiful year round.
Went for a sunset hike (this past summer) on the West Rim loop. Very beautiful scenery and very relaxing hearing the forest come alive after dark. The hike was guided by G3 Adventures!
This indoor recreation spot is very clean and we'll maintained. The cars are well kept and they are FAST.  Other than being a little pricey, this is a great place to take the family.
This is a hidden gem in Ringgold. It is a very nice park offering a great place for a quick hike or a family gathering. There is a beautiful shelter house and restrooms available.

Such a beautiful old Bridge! The cascades were a nice suprise for an adventure lover like me!

If you are in the area, stop and see this bridge. It is well worth your ti.e!
This is a decent palce to swim, however you will need water shoes unless you dont mind the rocks under your feet. There is a very nice playground and restroom facility.
This is an AMAZING historical gem! The history of Martha Berry and the founding of Berry College is beautifully displayed and comes to life on the tour of the grounds.
Harrison Bay State Park is a beautiful park with some great rangers! We hiked into 2020 on the midnight hike this year! Cannot wait to return and do some more hiking!
The people at this church are super loving and make you feel welcome. You can attend in person or watch online. This church also offers a Celebrate Recovery program.
This is the perfect place in Collegedale to take a walk or run. There is some beautiful scenery along the way. Even though you are in town, it doesn't feel like it.
This is a very nice easy trail. Good for an evening walk or run. There are a couple connectiing trails that provide access to some awesome rock climbing pads.
These photos are from several points on the Tenn River Park. There are several access points, all of which allow you to enjoy the beauty of the River!
Coolidge Park is a great place to take a walk or ride the carousel.  There are plenty of places situated around the park to eat or have coffee.
This place was unfortunately closed when we were passing by it. It looks like an extremely  cool place to learn and conspire about Bigfoot.

It was great to see an actual working American factory. Hard to believe but it was actually the first time I was actually able to show my 11 year old daughter people making things. It is a small factory, but enough to get a taste of how things are made, but even here a lot of the work is being computerized. My favorite part of the museum was the opportunity to stand on the receiving end of a 95+ MPH pitch (I literally could not see the ball until it was just a few feet in front of me). Also cool was seeing the Bat Vault containing the bats of some of the greatest of all time. This summer they are also hosting a small exhibit about the movie, The Sandlot. Give yourself at least 2 hours to visit and expect some lines.

This is an amazing museum and it is truly about much more than the assassination of MLK. It is as the name says a museum about civil rights in the United States. Why were civil rights necessary? How were civil rights fought for? I had read in some guidebooks that plan on 2 hours for the museum.... Give yourself much more time. We were rushing through the museum because the museum was cousin, we spent 2.5 hours and it wasn't nearly. The displays are very dense with information... And you are going to want time to let the information soak in and process all of the feelings that go with that.

I was really surprised that this was such a high quality aquarium. The shark tunnel  exhibit was probably my favorite, I liked the conveyor belt that kept traffic moving so that people could block the view for long periods of time. The layout can be confusing, we wanted a snack at the beginning and we had to walk through half the exhibits to get to the snack bar. We spent approximately 3 hours viewing the aquarium.

The zoo has a nice layout, but there is a major construction project occurring so there is a fairly long stretch of no animals just construction. There were a sizable number of exhibits that had no animals on the day of our visit (first week of April). We did enjoy seeing lemurs, polar bear, baked mole rats, snowy owls. We spent about 4 hours doing the full circle route.

Very unique hiking trail with its sculptures carved into the cliffs. Keep your eyes open because you could easily miss them. Two warnings, parts of the trail are not well marked and the trail is extremely muddy in spots, you will trash your shoes on this trail. Even with those warnings we really enjoyed our hike.

Great place to learn more about the Women's Rights movement in America. I wish we would have given ourselves more time here, lots to learn. We only had about an hour, another 1-2 hours would have been great. The rangers were so knowledgeable, they really bright the place and time to life.

This was actually a lot of fun. My wife, daughter, and I all equally enjoyed it. One downside, when we bought our add on ticket to this attraction at the aquarium we were told they were open until 10pm, but we found out they actually closed at 9pm so we rushed through the exhibits.

Typical playground. It was a good place for my daughter to run off some steam. Play equipment was mainly geared toward younger kids (5 and younger), also basketball court and picnic areas. As with all of Tybee you will have to pay to park.

An amazing museum about industry and inventions. Why doesn't this place get more publicity. Highlights: original 1905 Weight brothers flyer, a working 1800s style brewery and restaurant, a working print shop, and much more.

Disappointed that you can't actually see the river from the bluffs, but still a gorgeous view. The information station needs to update their maps to include this section of the park. No restroom at this section of park.

The meadow and ridge trails will give you quite a with out with their ups and downs. The view of Columbus was disappointing from the observation deck because of the haze. Will definitely give the trail another try soon.

The falls are impressive but they only let you spend about 5 minutes in that part of the cavern. It is about a mile walk round trip to the waterfall so be prepared (especially since there is no restroom in the cavern).

Very cool gorge and waterfall. Hopefully the mill will be open for tires in the future. We went on a particularly warm summer day and we were able to watch some crazy teens cliff dive into the small one in the gorge.

Beautiful, quiet, and secluded. We had the park entirely too ourselves during this visit. There are no restroom facilities here, so plan ahead. Lots of flowers were blooming during our early June visit.
Very cool rock formations. Hiking trail does require some minor rock scrambling. Check out trail map in parking lot first, going counter clockwise on the trail will get you to the top quicker.
How did I not know that the longest covered bridge in the United States was here in Ohio? It is just a short drive I-90. I would like to come back another time to explore the gorge and trails.
Big park with large variety of activities. Very limited parking on Saturday mornings because of youth soccer. Make sure you explore Rose Garden and prairie. Playground recently remodeled.
Such an important monument, give yourself at least 3 hours to explore the monument.out you want to see his birth home get the free tickets early, they only give a limited number each day.
An interesting place to learn more about religious history in the United States in the mid 1800s. Free, but you will get talked to about the Mormon faith by very friendly missionaries.
Nice place for a short walk. Lots of variety for a small area: a creek, a pond, hilly forested spots, and open grasslands. Not at all crowded. No bathroom facilities available.
The best nature center of all of the Metro ParksMetroparks, the live stream exhibit it's a family favorite. Footgolf was a blast this fall.
Great little splash pad to cool off on. Why don't they keep it open for more of September, the hot weather doesn't seem to be going away.
Excellent playground with a wide variety of activities. Things for a wide age race as well. Usually not that crowded.
I love walking to the end of the pier at night and staring at the starry skies and listening to the waves crash.
The beach is small and rocky, but the water is very clear. Nice alternative to the buddy side of the island.
