This state park evokes images of the American Southwest and though the key to all of what you see is due to erosion, most canyons are formed by a rivers or meandering streams. A variety of rich colors which includes Georgia’s own “red clay” can be seen in the strata of the canyon walls. A quick google search can be enlightening in explaining the formation(time period) and the minerals and colors and where they derived. It’s a quick little nerdy exploration into some geological terminology but makes the trip a lot more interesting before or after your visit. I felt most of what one could appreciate in the vastness of the formations can be seen from several vantage points along the rim trail at the top of the canyon. I highly recommend this state park for all ages as it has something to offer all.

An awe striking look down the valley of Path Valley Rd(Rt.75) with mountain shears on both sides and eventually into(on a clear day) the start of mountains of the Tuscarora State Forest. Just great views and typically a buzzard hang out for them to catch thermals and ride them out for what seems an eternity. A little disappointed at those who feel it necessary to litter, but whoever maintains has done a decent job at keeping up with covering up the graffiti. Just off of Augwick road onto a gravel road Tower road. This is right down the road from Cowan’s Gap State Park. Conveniently located also is access from Pa turnpike(76)off the Chambersburg exit. Highly recommend it for a nice drive, some fresh air and beautiful picturesque view.

From the trailhead it is all switchback trail downhill to both falls that includes a forge across a stream because of bridge that is in disrepair(hint hint Eagle project propositioners;) to both falls. This trail, in my opinion, is very well maintained and has very few “rough sections” as some refer to in other reviews. Kids, Moms and Dads and some adventuresome 60+ are worthy of hiking in and out of this trail. Would love to see more practice carry in/out but this fall is the grand daddy of this trail and the one drop at 85’ that one has to get a glimpse of.  Awesome observation deck. I loved the comradery of friendly people that one runs into in hiking this trail..it made the experience all that much more fun and enjoyable.

Visited this park on a Saturday as I wanted to do the Northern scenic trail/Slippery Rock Gorge trail(15 miles out and back) as it's rated very high on Pa's best hikes. I was not disappointed. This trail is total gorge hiking and  involves many climbs and descents. It does have slippery rocks and plenty of mud so heed warnings and bring proper footgear. I was impressed by the lack of trash in park. Typically a park that offers so many things(white water rafting/kayaking, hiking, rock climbing) tends to attract the element of those who don't care about what they leave behind. The park is beautiful and literally a stones throw away from Morainne State Park. I loved my experience here.

Probably one of my more favorite falls in and around Ithaca. Is most likely beautiful in all seasons but I favored winter for good water flow, ice build on on adjacent sides of falls(which also hides a bit of graffiti on abandoned Van Nattas pumping station building). It’s a series of drops the first of which is man made near bridge the crosses over creek. Down below there are some trees with intricate root structures that lend themselves to some interesting photos. I especially like this winteresque time of year as the freeze thaw cycle has helped in dissolving and introducing calcium carbonate from the limestone canyon and it gives the water a green to aqua colored effect.

This venue is absolutely gorgeous...the views are outstanding, the layout is such that you feel like your an integral part of the vineyard in the location of the facilities, the architecture and decor both inside and outside of the buildings all lends itself to a positive tasting/drinking experience.  I can not fault this winery but it’s wines did not appeal to my palette. I’m a red drinker and unfortunately most that I sampled were blends rather then traditionally crafted wines from one style grape. Would have preferred to select my own wines from a those on hand rather then have them selected for me. All in all a positive experience and great ambiance and atmosphere.

A phenomenally accessible frozen fall along roadside. I am told by locals that water flow is intermittent typically at best and flow is best, like most Falls, in spring and after heavy rainfall. I felt blessed to have seen this completely frozen as it seemed to expand itself wider due to freezing reasons. Got and up close and personal look with a set of micro spikes which facilitated me taking some angle shots I typically wouldn’t get otherwise. It’s definitely a stop and check out kind of site and especially if your staying at one of the local B&B’s.  I see in other reviews...can’t beat the coziness of the Bear Creek Inn right up the road to stop in.

Great state park for a bike ride, a leisurely stroll or taking the dogs out and getting them some exercise.  The Swatara Creek runs down through this park and adds to the serenity and appeal of the park.  Creek also attracts a number of kakakers but can be a bit temperamental at times in terms of water levels. The AT crosses through this park so it makes for good conversation for those who are thru hiking. This park is situated that its butted up to 44000 + acres of woodland in State Game Land 211. I encourage all to get outdoors and explore this park.

Took a 5 mile hike on white trail on Wednesday afternoon in mid June. This park is very peaceful despite its urbanesk like setting. Walking in the park is very peaceful and it provides a number of forest habitats. The constant sounds of birds chirping or squirrels and chipmunks crunching forest floor debris or the sounds from water flowing in Ridley creek are quite soothing to the ears. The plush greenery surrounded by a stand of hardwoods that are quite mature gives one the effect of being in a different world...it's amazing! I enjoyed my hike.

A small, but notable set of falls that’s squeezed in as Falls Creek changes direction and this is the culmination of that. The only safe viewing platform for this set of falls is from Stewart’s Ave bridge. Unfortunately unless you have a decent zoom or can access to a picture that doesn’t have safety netting in frame and you shoot your pictures at a time of the day that the sun illuminates the gorge/falls and does not interfere with flares on your lens this falls poses its challenges in photographing.

This tribute park includes both tributes to those from Irish and Scottish immigrants. It’s fitting since the sculptor who did the William Penn statue on top of city hall building was of Scottish decent. The park and presentation of art/statues is very well done. Is located next to a small little dog park and is very well located being close to River Rink park and City Tavern and entrance into historical district of Philadelphia. It’s worth a quick walk through the park if you are on the area.

I actually have hiked through this picnic area on Ironhorse loop. It appears to have numerous pavilions, all of which can be reserved, fire pits and fireplaces. Great place for kids to run and around and have fun in the woods. Bathroom accommodations. Excellent parking facilities and it appears the are redoing the entranceway and macadam to the driveway into facility. This picnic area is very remote and cozy..great for a family reunion or a summer picnic with family and friends.

I have visited this state park twice, in two different seasons and I’m from out of state and each time has been incredible. The canyon that has formed from this once flowing massive river is phenomenal. The major fall is fairly impressive. I am disappointed at those who visit this site and decide to leave trash behind;(. It’s location is right next to Lake Cayuga which is beautiful onto itself. A hike upstream from the falls is also very impressive. Very photogenic!

Wife and I needed to get of dodge for the afternoon as the puppy was starting to drive us a little crazy. Love this remote, rustic location nested back in behind Blue Ridge.  Cozy cabin inside with doors to open air pavilion style patio with plenty of seating. Real wood fire pit on side of building is perfect for staying warm and still enjoying outdoor music venue. We thoroughly enjoyed our cab sav and will definitely return in warmer weather. Place is dog friendly.

My gf and I were just passing through on our way to Helen when this appeared from a distance to be a good viewing platform for a sunset that we had been enjoying from lower ground. Upon driving up and taking it in..we said what the heck! Everybody has a smile on their face and it looked very nice! Was not disappointed at all, we both loved it and the ambiance, the music, crowd had a great vibe to it! Just a 5 star unplanned serendipitous experience! We loved it!

Back a state game land road that road sign states “Road closed” “bridge out”. Small parking area. Steep initial trail that descends down to rock outcrop for viewing falls. I’ve witnessed people walking across bridge..I would say do so at your own risk. There are numerous trails to explore further downstream. I wouldn’t say it’s “kid friendly” but certainly if your kids are the explorer type you’ll be fine.

Spectacular hiking with glen style hiking trails with rhododendrons on either side with stream running. Great views in and out of glen...plenty to explore and you can access Pinnacle Point overlook by utilizing the Conestoga trail(orange blaze). Great for dogs. Get some views of the Holtwood hydroelectric facility. Good for a day hike or an evening adventure after work.

Part of the Neversink Mtn trail system this handmade rock structure doesn’t disappoint in terms of its presence and stance as it’s peaked. Unfortunately power lines cloud view of Mt Penn/Reading view and the landscape of Pagoda and Fire tower skyline drive. Is a worthy structure to visit and has great patina. I would say a definite must see for Berks County.

Outstanding for hiking, biking, kayaking/canoeing, photographing, waterfallin’, small town shopping for unique gifts or taking a date, loved one(s) or the family to get outdoors. It offers both beginner and novice levels of each of the activities I️ listed. I️ return there at least twice a year and find something new or different. I️ love it

Trailhead starts on outskirts of Elizabethtown across from Crowe's Trucking. The parking area is nice. It starts out paralleling ETown road and from a field into eventually forest. Thus segment runs for 5 miles and transitions right into the Lebanon Valley rail trail. Thus section is very well maintained.

This park provides adventure for any level of those seeking it. A most unique and picturesque area that it unique onto itself. It exemplifies small town Pennsylvania while providing a bit of swagger and a wealth of beauty and adventure. I can’t say enough in the draw to this park and its surroundings

This was the perfect little park to launch my kayak from. The park is clean and grass well manicured. The pavilion was up to date and clean and I felt safe leaving my vehicle here. I will tell no one about this park as it a best kept secret for those who know about it.
Ample parking areas on either side of road with access to Hawk Falls trail or trail to Boulder field, both of which are part of Hickory Run State Park. I recommend going to both.
There is over 44,000 acres of woodland fun this area has to offer. It's my hiking adventure playground and I'm constantly discovering something new in this area.
Great views of Susquehanna river. A nice little getaway park for a picnic-cookout or a walk in the wilderness. Great area to explore both sides of river

The Battle of Musgrove Mill State Historic Site, located in Enoree, South Carolina, was a visually and historically pleasant visit.  They have a beautiful visitor's center, clean restrooms, knowledgeable staff, and AIR CONDITIONER. Lol.  The first trail was approximately 1.1 miles in length and circles around the old Musgrove Mill area.  The second trail sported a short travel down a wheelchair accessible paved walk to the waterfall.  It is a small fall, but very picturesque waterfall.   The trail continues to complete a 1.5 mile hike through the battlefield area.  Well worth the trip over to visit.  Stopped by the nearby Old Rock Quarry Winery afterwards to complete a wonder afternoon.

Tallulah Gorge State Park, located in Tallulah Falls, Georgia, was absolutely amazing.  It has been on our bucket list for several years and we finally got a chance to see and enjoy it.  The views of the Gorge from the numerous overlooks were breathtaking.  There are several waterfalls through this stretch of the river, which were all large and great flow.  You will get your workout in here, so wear comfortable shoes and bring some water.  The interpretive center was very nice, complete with exhibits involving local wildlife and information about the town, the dam, and history of the area.  They had clean restrooms as well.  Great experience. Can't wait to go back!

A bucket list place for a long time, I finally got to experience Chimney Rock State Park.  We hiked up the endless staircases to the top, stopping at several lookout points along the way.  We didn't utilize it but there was an elevator that takes you to the top, which makes it accessible for everyone.   There were a few really cool things to see along the way up. Those include Hickory Nut Falls, Gneiss Cave, Pulpit Rock, Vista Rock, the Grotto, and the Subway.  The crown jewel was Chimney Rock, elevation 2270'. Loved the giant American flag.  And the views of Lake Lure and the surrounding countryside was breathtaking.  Highly recommended!!

Conestee Park, located on Mauldin Road between Greenville and Mauldin, South Carolina, is absolutely amazing.  It is built on the old Greenville Braves Stadium property.  It is home to ball fields, play grounds, a dual dog park, walking paths, nature trails, and biking trails.   The scenery along to nature trail is breathtaking.   Much to see in the way of fauna and flora alike.  It ties in with a section of the Swamp Rabbit Trail, which eventually will be connected to the main Trail that currently runs from Greenville to Travelers Rest.  Give this place a try, you won't be disappointed!!

Wow!  Cool place for some family fun.  Wanted to visit for years and finally got a chance.  Plenty of fun for the whole family.   The biggest draw is the corn maze.  Acres and acres of corn with many paths through it.  There are twelve check points throughout the maze to find and you can scan the barcode to get credit for each find.  It is HUGE!  They have a petting zoo, fire pits, an obstacle course, a couple stages for live music, cornhole, a giant rocking chair, tractors, and of course the hayride.  Great family fun!  A must visit for something off the beat and path.

The Destin Harbor Boardwalk, located in Destin, Florida,  was an absolute pleasure.  There were so many fun and exciting things to do.  There are a number of great restaurants, many shops and boutiques, bars, boat rentals, zip lines, games, and much, much more.  There is ample parking to access the boardwalk, as well as additional parking if you are eating at one of the restaurants.   The mood was exciting, even in the winter when we visited.  And hang out until sunset for  spectacular view of the sun setting over the Gulf of Mexico.   A must visit if you go to Destin!

Anastasia State Park, located in St. Augustine, Florida, was absolutely amazing!  We rented a couple kayaks and paddled up the waterway to the St. Augustine Lighthouse.   Beautiful views or the wildlife and surrounding flora.  The staff were all friendly and helpful. We also walked a few miles on the beach.  Nice white sand and not overcrowded.   There is ample parking at the beach and several restrooms, complete with showers.  There is a little store, which has a few odds and ends for camping as well. Great place to take the family or go for an outdoor adventure!!

Wildcat Wayside Station, located on Geer Highway in Cleveland, South Carolina, is amazing!  You get to see four waterfalls along the one mile hiking loop.  There is ample parking across the street and along the road.  A vendor is setup at the entrance, selling all kinds of treats that make the day fun and enjoyable, especially for the kids.   The falls surrounded the site of an old wayside station, with the remains of an old chimney located just above the first two falls.  The hike is easy and can be done by most, young and old alike.  Highly recommended!!

Wildcat Branch Falls, located on Geer Highway in Cleveland, South Carolina, is amazing!  You get to see four waterfalls along the one mile hiking loop.  There is ample parking across the street and along the road.  A vendor is setup at the entrance, selling all kinds of treats that make the day fun and enjoyable, especially for the kids.   The falls surrounded the site of an old wayside station, with the remains of an old chimney located just above the first two falls.  The hike is easy and can be done by most, young and old alike.  Highly recommended!!

The Ed Austin Reguonal Park complex is awesome.  A very large complex with a number recreational opportunities.  We played disc golf, and man what a great course.  They have a full 18 hole course with a number of bonus holes.  They also have multiple launch pads for the short to power throwers.   They move the basket positions weekly in order to keep the course challenging. The park hosts tournaments regularly.  A walking track flanks the course which provides ample social opportunities.   Beautiful course, challenging but fair.  Highly recommend!!

Wow! Perfect timing often makes a good day a great one.  The first Saturday of the month they have Militia in uniform doing a reenactment.  We got to witness the informative and rather funny 5 gentleman shooting muzzle loaders.  The area around the visitor center is flanked by numerous live oak trees, complete with the drooping Spanish moss.  The original fort was destroyed a long time ago, but the history was worth the trip.  There are many more eye catching sites in Saint Augustine,  but don't miss this hidden gem.  Support your State Parks!

Fred W. Symmes Chapel (better known as Pretty Place), located in Cleveland, South Carolina, is all that was promised, and then some.  It is part of the YMCA  Camp, and is open for general spectators or can be reserved for special events, namely weddings.  The views are spectacular and breathtaking.   The chapel itself is quaint and romantic.   This place is well worth the drive up Ceasars Head to view.  Jones Gap State Park and Dupont Forrest are within close proximity as well, so make a day of it and enjoy the views!!

Conestee Dog Park is located in Conestee Park and adjacent to the Lake Conestee Nature Preserve in between Greenville and Mauldin, South Carolina.   It is two parks in one, with one side for larger dogs and the other for their smaller brethren.   There is ample room for them to run and get exercise.  The also have disposal bags and trash cans available.   The park has public restrooms for their human friends.  If the dogs are completely worn out, take them for a walk on one of tbe many trails in the park.
likes: Separate areas for different dog sizes

reviews_attraction.text: Beautiful lighthouse on the Saint Augustine coast.  This is still a working lighthouse, which is really cool.  You can ascend the two hundred plus stairs to the top and get a really nice 360 degree view of America's oldest city.  There is a really nice maritime museum as well, complete with many artifacts about the lighthouse and the surrounding seaport.  They have a well supplied gift shop if you wish to take home a memento from your visit.  Don't miss this one when planning your Saint Augustine tour.

King Creek Falls is one of our favorite falls in the Upstate of South Carolina. There is a tremendous amount of water flow for such a small creek. It has a single drop of about sixty five feet and has a wonderful pool at the base. In the warmer months it is not uncommon to see kids splashing around in the pool.  This waterfall is located just outside of the Burrell's Ford camping area and just off the Foothills and Chattanooga Trails.  Highly recommended for waterfall lovers and hikers alike.

Spoonauger Falls is a beautiful small to medium waterfall located in the Burrells Ford area in Long Creek, South Carolina.  The waterfall is around fifty feet, in a single drop.  It is a short hike off the Chattanooga River Trail, and an easy hike, fun for the young and old alike.  There are several smaller falls along the creek on the way up to the main waterfall.  When you are done, take a short hike over to view the Chattanooga River or Kings Creek Falls.  Don't miss this one!!

Cancer Survivors Park is located on the Swamp Rabbit Trail in Greenville, South Carolina.   It is in the section of the trail between Falls Park and Cleveland Park.   A wonderful memorial to cancer survivors, it brings attention to the disease and highlights some local success stories.   The overlook and park area are landscaped beautifully.  There are great views of the river below.  Don't miss thos section of the trail on you next visit.

The Walhalla State Fish Hatchery, located off Highway 107 in Long Creek, South Carolina.is an amazing place.  They grow the trout that are eventually released into local tributaries, including the Chattooga River and Chauga River.  Each section of the hatchery has increasingly larger fish.  The full grown fish get released into the rivers.  Great place to visit, the kids will love it.  FYI...it is currently closed due to Covid-19.

Visited Little Talbot Island earlier this Summer.  Nice views and relaxing atmosphere. This undeveloped stretch of coastline has five miles of prestine beaches.  It takes you away from the hustle and bustle of Jacksonville to a more laid back beach atmosphere.  Lots of wildlife can be seen while visiting Little Talbot Island, not to mention some good fishing.   So come relax, fish, swim, camp, or just stroll the beaches.

Yellow Branch Falls, located in Mountain Rest, South Carolina,  is a magnificent fall.  The hike in is moderate, and the payoff is amazing.  This is a popular fall, so don't be surprised to see a large number of people on the trail.  There is ample parking at the trailhead.  The entrance to Yellow Branch is just down from the entrance to Oconee Park, which is home to Stumphouse Tunnel and Issaqueena Falls.

Riley Moore Falls on the Chauga River in Westminster, South Carolina is magnificent for a shorter fall.  It is a 12 feet drop on the Chauga River.  The width spans the entire width of the riverbed.  The flow is strong and the volume loud.  There are several rapids above and below it.  It is a short hike, about 2 miles round trip.  Great place to take the family.   Great swimming in the warmer months.

Long Creek  Falls, located in Westminster, South Carolina,  is a magnificent fall along Long Creek.  The fall is about 75 feet and tumbles down into the Chattooga River.   The like is about a 3.3 mile round trip, that is moderate.  The very end descends rapidly for the lasy several hundred yard, which is a steep hike back up.  This is a don't miss waterfall.

I road my bike on the Doodle Trail, which runs from Pickens to Easley, South Carolina.   The trail was smoothly paved, and wide enough for two way traffic with ease.  There is a great park on both ends, giving the kids somewhere to play.  The trail was about 17 1/2 miles end to end.  It was a little hilly, but manageable.  Highly recommended!!
Out of the way spot on the Upper Chattanooga.   Nice fall and great place to trout fish.  Great experience and a short hike.
Not so secret fall but well worth the short hike.   There was a lot of fellow hikers but nice, wide open trails.

I'm a natural-born citizen of the United States of America. I love this country. I love to learn and experience everything I can about this country. Pin Point is a large part of this country's history. It is even the hometown of one of our Supreme Court Justices. We found Pin Point because of my curiosity. We saw a small sign that said " Pin Point Heritage Museum", and I turned down the narrow street. One of the best turns I've made in my life. I had made the statement to my wife only about 3 hours earlier: One day I am going to visit a Gullah/Geechee community. Never dreamed this would be the day. We were greeted and escorted by a native of the community and treated like honored guests. We had arrived late in the day so did not see and experience everything there, but did see the documentary film and one of the buildings. We will be back in a couple of weeks to finish the tour. I absorb a historical area when I visit so I expect to spend another 3 hours or so on top of the hour and a half I've already spent there. You could probably take in the whole site in one hour but you would miss the full value of the place and its history if you rushed through in such a short time. Take your time, look, read, ask questions, listen to the staff, they want to share everything with you. Then stop and listen to the site itself. There are voices there that will speak to your heart and add richness to your experience and increase your love for America!

This was part of the history tour I've longed to take for years. When my grandson said he wanted to go, that's all the incentive I needed. We spent a day here and hardly scratched the surface of what there is to see and do. The video was great,  touching. (My grandson said, "That's a sad movie.") The driving tour guided by cellphone was a neat experience but we are definitely going to have to do it a couple more times to actually see and hear everything. And then there is the museum. It will take me at least three days to see all of that! And then I'll have to drive all the interconnecting roads and stop at all the monuments and artillery displays and markers until I've relived the battle in my imagination. I'm figuring at least a week to experience it all. Then we will tour Tunnel Hill and follow the battle lines on down to Picketts Mill and Kennesaw. That will take another week. Fortunately, there are many great Georgia State Parks nearby to stay at, all with their own attractions and events.

I have had conversations with campers at other state parks in Georgia that have gone:
"Where were you before you came here?" "Skidaway." "How was it?" "Awesome. We love this park, too, but we visit Skidway every chance we get." And:
"How do you like this park?" "Oh, we love this place. We come here at least once a year." "Where you headed next?" "Skidaway. It's our normal routine: here one week; Skidaway the next. Or, vice versa."
We went today to find out why. Clean, shaded sites. Many large sites easy to pull through. Clean comfort stations. Nice large covered picnic pavilions. Modern safe playgrounds. Interesting interpretive center with host/interpretive guide. Great friendly, helpful staff. Close to so many other attractions/historical sites/restaurants. I could go on and on. If I didn't like camping, Skidaway Island State Park, would change my mind!

Called Georgia's Little Grand Canyon and appropriately so. It is a marvel to see and experience. Well worth the drive. Be sure to take the rim hike and the canyon basin hike to get the full impact. Sounds like a lot of walking---and it is---but plan on arriving early, hike the basin, enjoy a picnic lunch, then hike the rim. Please stay on the trails, too. Wandering all over the place causes stress on the habitat, and getting too close to the crumbly brittle rim might cause you to get a fatal view of the bottom of the canyon! Visit the information center for a history of the canyon  but be prepared for a bunch of over-imagination concerning the age of the canyon and how it was formed. Man might have contributed, but he didn't make it. And it didn't take millions of years to form. The earth isn't that old!

Another one of Georgia's great state parks, especially if you own a horse. Beautiful safe trails to ride and enjoy any time of the year. Really nice stables for your horse and a campground right beside there for you to stay, rest, and keep an eye on your horse. If you are a history buff like me, the house and grounds provide a great opportunity to learn about Georgia and American history. If you like to fish, there's a good- sized lake to put your small boat and wet a hook. Always plenty of trails for hiking and plenty of playground for the kids, including a zip line! The staff at this park are super friendly and helpful. We didn't have time to stay as long as we wanted to, but my grandson and I had a lot of fun. It is close to his house so we will be back soon.

Once again, I'm quite sure I have previously written a review of this place. This is one of the newest historical sites managed by the Georgia DNR, State Parks and Historical Sites Division. They have done an incredible job of restoring and interpreting this site and its history. I am a history buff so I truly enjoy every visit here. Indeed, I dream of being one of the role-players at such a location. But an interest in history is no requirement to enjoy this place as it easily stirs interest in itself. If you are ever in the Helen, GA, area, be sure to walk the short trail from Helen to Hardman Farm. Pack a picnic lunch and make a day of it. It will be an event you will relive many times as you share the memory and experience with family and friends.

Visited here with my grandson and had some great fun. This should be a site visited by every real U.S. citizen. There is much to see, do, and learn here. Pack a picnic lunch and stay long enough to take it all in. The folks are wonderful, warm, and welcoming. They are very knowledgeable and will take great pleasure in guiding you and answering your questions. So many treat children the age of my grandson as a nuisance, but these folks made every effort to ensure he had a pleasant memorable experience, leaving not just amused but also enlightened. It was a good first-stop on our history tour as his interest was piqued and he was inspired to learn more. We plan to return this summer for a refresher course!

Beautiful park with interesting history. Small and not loaded with a lot of amenities but quiet, peaceful, clean, and managed by some awesome folks. The old covered bridge is one of the few remaining in the nation and is even more rare because you can drive across it. There are several easy trails for hiking, and you can even drown a worm in the lake. I would call this a very family-friendly park because if you take the family there for more than one night, you will have to engage in FAMILY time. I'm looking forward to taking my grandkids here for their first genuine, serious camping experience. If you want a perfect respite location, head to Watson Mill Bridge State Park.

You've got to get to Jekyll Island and see the historical section and all the amazing lights and decorations. Be sure to get out to Driftwood Beach, day or night, but the sunsets there are breath-taking. The whole island is dramatic under the full moon. Don't forget to enjoy an amazing meal at any one of the great restaurants. I highly recommend Wee Pub: great food, great service, great prices, great atmosphere every time I've been there. I love being made to feel like they want me there, they want me to enjoy my meal, they want me to come back. Oh, I'll be back as soon as I can!

Another of Georgia's incredible state parks. Some awesome sights to see here, from beautiful flora and fauna to remarkable rock formations. An interesting nature center/park headquarters. Several hiking/biking trails. Fishing. Ranger-guided hikes. Historical sites and buildings. Fun activities. Wildlife, neat playground, and an outdoor exercise yard. Good grief! It will take days to see and do it all. Which is fine since it is all close to unlimited accommodations in Atlanta. Or you can campout, if primitive camping is your style. And you will never beat the price!!

Great natural wildlife park. Animal exhibits, boat tours, train ride through the edge of the swamp, historical farmstead, clean, reasonable price, safe, educational, wonderful staff, close to excellent accommodations and other attractions. This place should be on the list of every American to visit! Just be aware that this is an open preserve where the wildlife roam free in their natural environment. You are safe as long as you respect the fact that you are in THEIR house. Look and enjoy but keep your distance. They are wild animals, not pets for cuddling!!

It's really kind of hard to go wrong with a Georgia State Park. This one has been around for a long time and is extremely popular---and there are a good number of reasons why. Sadly, their popularity seems to have produced a cocky, negligent attitude in the staff: "We are the pinnacle and we are gracious to allow you on the property. If you don't like it, go away." So sad. A beautiful location. I enjoy the site every time I'm in the area, but I prefer to stay where I am made welcome and wanted. And popularity is no justification for overcharging.

This place was trashed by Hurricane Michael. The roads and campsites are cleared but the debris is piled everywhere. Georgia State budget cuts have caused a severe shortage in manpower and equipment to handle the cleanup. The lake is seriously down affecting the fishing and pretty much any other recreation. They have a stupid rule disallowing tents on lakefront camp sites. I guess if you can't afford a $50,000 RV, Georgia Veterans State Park prefers you stay somewhere else. Can't have tent trash folks ruining the neighborhood.

A very interesting place if you enjoy art and history as I do. The admission price is fair in my opinion because I enjoy touring such places and the fee I pay helps preserve such places for my enjoyment and education. I have spent three hours at one time here and have yet to take it all in. You could probably walk through in just a few minutes but you will have seen and enjoyed little and gained nothing. Take your time; make some memories; absorb all the richness this place has to offer.

Awesome Georgia treasure! This should be a required visit for every student in Georgia. No, every student in America! Events going on all year that vividly relate this part of American history. Knowledgeable friendly staff. Located in town that deserves a visit in its own right. And the Friends Of Dahlonega Gold Museum are a wonderful bunch of folks providing incredible support!

Load the family and go see this place, but plan about 3 days to a week. There is that much to see and do just here, but if you range as far as 20 miles away from here in any direction, a week won't be enough time. Plenty of accommodations close by. Clean, safe, healthy, educational, interesting family fun at an affordable cost.

Beautiful family-friendly natural wonderland. Lots to see and do as a family, as a break from the stress of life in the work-a-day world, as breath of fresh air---just a great place to get away, relax, and renew. An incredible exposure to nature with much history to learn and experience.

Another of Georgia's State historic sites. Well-maintained, well-managed and providing abundant education, information, and experience. There are several other sites nearby that need to be visited, altogether providing at least a week's worth of wonderful lifetime experiences.

Georgia has numerous awesome parks. This is one of her finest. It was perfect in my estimation before but the recent renovations have added immensely. The whole atmosphere of this park can best be described as therapeutic. I never leave here without feeling rested.

I've been to Tunnel Hill; I've toured the tunnel and surrounding property with the old house and general store. I have no recollection of any Westside Park. Gave it 3 stars just so I could say, "It's ok" because I guess it is.

Another one of Georgia's awesome state parks. Nice cottages, plenty of camping/RV sites, great golf course. Plenty of trails to hike and other activities to engage in with plenty of attractions and history nearby.

This park has seen many improvements over the past few years. A premier South Georgia campground. Plenty to do at the park, but make it your hub for surrounding activities. A week will not be long enough!
Nice park. Another of Georgia's treasures. Much to see and do. One day will not be enough. The cottages are really nice, the campground is nice, and the campground hosts are awesome.
Nice park, interesting area. Sure would love to see the lock in operation and to fish the river for a while. Got that planned for a future trip with the grandkids.
Awesome place, perfect for family outings, educational, fun, healthy. I'll be back when I can stay longer and enjoy it more.
