Snorkling , ma attenti agli scogli davvero molto appuntiti

Very beautiful landscape area with two paved trails 1 is the Woodland Trail with many very interesting pieces of folk are spread out along the path then the animal Trail which is a paved trail in a beautifully wooded area it is a loop trail that takes you past the different habitats very interesting animals one part of the trail is wild animals bison calories black wolves many different birds owls Hawks Eagles the other is the Barnyard animals didn't go down that trail because of time I'm sure it was as well laid-out is the wild animal Trail Visitor Center very nice are the very great view of lake below there is no charge to go into this place very good place to bring the family and especially children

National pow Museum located at historic Andersonville Civil War camp site beautiful both outside and inside, especially interesting history and for those who have been in the military  or have lived the POW experience. All of the displays done in respectful tasteful and informative manner staff in the POW Museum very friendly helpful and respectful of where they are. The Civil War prison camp site and Cemetery is a beautiful setting in what was once a horrible place, very informative beautiful monuments and static displays scattered around site also the National POW museum has a good gift shop and there is a jar for those who wish to make a donation
likes: Facilities & Services: Informative displays, Respectful presentation, Friendly staff
On-site Activities: Educational experience, Monuments, Static displays

reviews_attraction.text: Canal boat Excursion up the canal I'm bad what's nice scenery was pretty good historic sites along the way with laceration only negative was part of Route was blocked because of work being done so trip shortened and narration was unnecessary on return trip would have been better just to have the quiet and scenery to enjoy on the return trip it was nice to have the Discovery Center to explore prior to the Excursion on the canal also the Discovery Center and Canal Excursion Associates were all very pleasant a knowledgeable

Beautiful Cypress filled lake ,nice picnic area Campground along the lake, four fairly decent Scenic Trails one that branches off to a natural spring
Located right outside of the Small Town of Twin City Georgia just east of Swainsboro Georgia nice little place to visit and for people that enjoy camping nice little campground next to the lake boats for rent nice fishing pier covered bridge going across the dam on the lake with a nice stream below the dam

Snall less than Five Hundred Acre Park along Lake a few cabins, small Beach campground on Lake shore.Interesting Spillway to the dam on the lake unfortunately Park office closed for lunch and two of the three trails closed because of high water,worth another look at another time  not located on Georgia parks and historic sites map for some reason but it is a state park or at least the name says it is

Fairly small Park mainly setup for equestrian campers with riding trails, a couple of nature trails one was a paved one way mile and a quarter. The park could use couple of more walking trails with natural surface through the forest, would be more interesting to walk, staff at Visitor Center ,1 Ranger was pretty helpful and nice guy ,pretty scenery right there at the offices with the lake in front

Rustic and historical buildings laid out roughly on a circle in hilly wooded area ,many  interesting historical items inside buildings, living history actors a nice touch. Visitor Center many items for sale that were of Interest,the staff friendly  and infomative

Great a great view of the Flint River from high up unfortunately this is not a state park anymore but still must pay $5 parking fee however Trading Post has very many interesting items with very friendly staff Overlook of the river is right across the street

Great City Park in Richmond Hill Georgia any events held there nice walking area around the perimeter of the old rice patties from Rice Plantation great covered picnic areas in view of small legs playground area for children great place for the whole family

Very beautiful setting easy to access on the grounds of Toccoa College not expensive just a couple of dollars per person to access waterfall up short rail beside stream coming from waterfall very friendly staff in the gift shop at the entrance to the falls

Very informative and educational Visitor Center great Trail to the overlooks of the waterfall easy to access overlooks one and two mild difficulty as far as grade all Trail a little harder hike down trails to the other overlooks 3 and 4 and I think five

Very picturesque Covered Bridge spillway underneath beautiful stone bottom stream coming out from Dam beautiful landscape all around great trails under Shady canopy running along quiet streams beautiful views at different plants long both Loop trails

Great Park located on Shore of beautiful Lake Blackshear  static display Area with airplanes ,tanks artillery Etc also very informative and interesting military museum inside Visitor Center nice lakeside restaurant located at the marina in the park

This was more of a chamber of commerce exhibit but still some interesting displays and some history in a compact area and there  is a play room for children,the museum  is in the vidalia Visitor Center it was free but there is a jar for donations

Excellent place to educate children about Air Force history, three buildings full of all kinds of jets, helicopters glass case displays with  airplane models, uniforms,pictures Etc.I took my six year old grandson and he thoroughly enjoyed it

A little Rough Around the Edges but has a nice rustic feel, nice views of the lake from the loop trail around the lake, only negative is doesn't open till 9 a.m. office  no open till 11 a.m. ,otherwise very nice

Very nice little Park beautiful stone buildings picturesque Lake and a natural Mineral Spring housed in a stone building beautiful natural area also has miniature golf and picnic area that was pretty setting
Well preserved fort with lots of history on display  with beautiful views from the parapet of the Savannah River ship traffic coming down from downtown and the docks above downtown Savannah
Pretty area, informative about the Battle of Rlvers Bridge, markers all around and pretty nice picnic areas nearby just not much to do other than look around and maybe have a picnic
Beautiful structure in a fairly remote area near the end of a dirt road very well-built been there since late 1700s just a nice place to see very interesting
Stunningly beautiful scenery in the park and in the surrounding area very inexpensive to visit several fun and challenging trails and beautiful waterfalls
Friendly staff great scenery interesting exhibits fun and informative train ride and boat tour many interesting items for sale in Visitor Center
Great historic ruin just something about the immediate surrounding area something to do with the trees in Spanish moss on the remote area
The trail needs a little maintenance fallen trees removed,trail widened and cleared in places, some of the boardwalks need to be replaced
Nice city park with three free fishing lakes and playground and covered picnic area, just off Highway 1 Southside of Swainsboro Georgia

I think I would call this place more of a roadhouse then I winery. I was there on a very busy weekend and they have lots of outdoor seating on plastic chairs and tables and a band playing in the gazebo. I came with a large bus group and we thought we would have a reserved table but we did not, and it was very hard to find seating and had to stand around most of the time. We were also told we cannot bring anything off our bus to eat or drink as they sold those items there I did not like this policy

The tasting area consists of a few plastic tables with some kids pouring out sample wines. This was very unorganized and not very classy.

As I walked around the vineyards were roped off so you cannot walk through and look at the grapes. They do have barns and they have rescue horses, there were quite a few on display and some of them were even friendly enough to walk over for a nice petting.

They do have walking tours but only every hour or so and we were unfortunate and not were not able to go on one. You would think when you have a large tour group of 50 or more they would accommodate you with a private tour.

Inside the main building they do have additional seating, a gift shop and a few restrooms. The lines can get quite long for the restrooms and they do have some porta potties outside on the grounds

If you like the roadhouse type atmosphere with the live music and a lot of people in a crowded place this is the winery to visit not as classy as some of the others I visited that day but very nice on it's own.
dislikes: Lack of private tours for large groups

reviews_attraction.text:
From the old school hand lettered marquee announcing up coning shows this place screams of day of old. Once inside you are transformed into another time. The beautiful main hall is a sight to see. Once inside the theater you are greeted with hight ceilings a stage like no other.

There are 3 balconies, but sitting in the back of them is not a problem as the view is still grand. I have seen many concerts here and the sound is good from anywhere in the house.

The seats are plush velour and very comfy and there is plenty of leg room.

Of course the highlight are the Rockettes. So step back in time and enjoy whatever show your attending in this great classic hall.

Not the best museum in NYC but nice none the less. The panorama of NYC is worth the pice of admission its self. Though it is a bit out of date, that is a good thing because the Twin Towers are still there, it is still fun to look at to see the grand scale of NY and where things relate to each other in size and location.

The only other exhibit that is with seeing is the Tiffany glass room.

Just out the back is the World Sphere from the 1964 Worlds fare and a great park to walk around and have a picnic, so plan to spend the day and enjoy this part of Queens.

This is the place. Sports or music, you have not made it until you have played the Worlds Most Famous Arena!!

It all stated for me in the 80's seeing my first concert, Billy Joel here and was hooked. Since then I must have seen hundreds of performers here and let me tell you they are always at there best when playing the Garden.

The Rangers also play here as well as the Kincks, if you can call what they do playing. Lol.

Funny that it have come full circle with Billy now taking up residence here playing every month. I love it!

One of three vineyards I visited on a North Fork tour. They gave a nice tour or the brewing room and explained the process. Then they took us down to the storage room where the barrels are kept and have a few tastings. The guide was super nice and answered a lot of questions.

The grounds are beautiful. When we were there there was wedding so it can be rented out for your special occasion.

There are plenty of picnic tables to eat a snack on and take a rest. Don't forget to go up to the pouch for a even better view.

I like to bike through here when in town just to take in the sites.

During the week there is not much going on, maybe a few volleyball games and people working out in the gym area. But on the weekends it's a whole new ball game.

All the volleyball courts are filled and it fun to watch. There are people on seqways, roller blades and other modes of transportation.

The place is usually clean but there is the homeless element. They just sleep and hangout. They don't bother you with begging.

Though this is a public beach I would bet most visiting would be locals as it is a bit out of the way and parking limited and expensive.

There is a large snack bar with cabanas for rent and bathrooms, though when I was there the Friday of Memorial Day weekend it was not open yet.

I am told there would be shuttle buses during the season but I guess the season did not start for one more day.

The sand is a hard grain type of sand and clean. And shells can be found a plenty.

This not a park like its big brother Central Park that has a concert venue, ball fields, running tracks etc.. But a small oasis just off Times Square. Many tables and chairs surround the large patch of grass for sitting civilized while eating some tasty snacks offered from the kiosks near by. There are many events held like game day (chess and checkers), movie night during the summer months and many others.  There is free wifi and is only a few steps from the main library.

Easy to get to and very clean.

I usually bike over the Marine Parkway bridge but you can also get there by the Q35 bus. The water is cool and refreshing during the summer months. There is a also a golf course hidden away towards Ft. Tilden. There are plenty of snack stands on the board walk but if biking look out for the snack truck just over the bridge, the best value on the beach.

The boardwalk was destroyed by Sandy but I am sure it will be back better than ever.

A very nice and well maintained playground for the kids. Lots of jungle gym and in the summer the sprinklers are always on. Kids love the giant snake that wraps around the park. Plenty of benches under the cover of trees so parents can sit and watch the kids playing in a nice cool breeze.

Sometimes it can be a bit noisy from the traffic on Ave. U but only when a large truck or motorcycle goes by. Plenty of parking usually on the side street near by.

A very nice sized park with a kids playground at one end and a Shake Shack at the other. Though the line at the Shack can be VERY long. There is a very nice art installation using ropes there now that bring some nice color to the park.

Has some great views of some NYC landmarks like the Flat iron building and the Empire State building. If you need a place to relax while touring the city this is a fine park to do it in.

Right next to the HighLine the building is beautiful on the outside as well as the inside.

7 floors of art, there will be something for everyone. Started at the top and worked my way down. The upper floors have balconys that offer great views and places to eat some snacks.

I didn't get some of the art but enjoyed my stay.  The staff was nice even when they told you to step back because you are to close to the art.

A nice starting place for biking the westside greenway.

Just a few steps form the Staten Island Ferry, there is a great view of the harbor. This is where you get the ferry to the Statue of Liberty, though the lines can get quite long. The lawns are nicely kept and there are plenty of benches to rest your feet. The best times to hangout here is during the week mid day, the weekends the place is filled with tourists.

It once had a fancy restaurant that is now just a run down building.  People leave pieces of fish all over the place so the place is dirty and disgusting. On the weekends people have party's with very loud music and leave a mess.

This once great outdoor destination is in a sorry state and really needs a uplift. Maybe after the Belt construction is done they will work in the pier.

Took my young niece there during the summer and we had a blast. She enjoyed all the shows and even got to touch sea lion. Though she had fun I was a bit disappointed as to what they had on display. From what I understand budget cuts have hurt as well as Sandy.

I hope once Coney Island is restored the Aquarium will return to its past grander.

Went for a ceramics class and had a great time. The instructors were friendly and very helpful.

I was also taken aback by the programs they have. There were signs all around promoting many different speakers that they have had or coming in the future. It read like a who's who.

I will defiantly add the 92Y to my list of places to watch.

No better place to people watch than this park. Right in the middle of the Village this is where it all happens. Performance art, clowns, skate boarders all doing there thing.

And from what I was told years ago, don't know if still true,but only place in city with view of both Empire State Building and trade center in one spot.

Located just outside City Hall this parks always has some nice art to browse that is installed on the grounds.

Its a bit noisy because its not very big and there is heavy traffic on all sides. But it is a nice rest spot before taking the long hike over the Brooklyn Bridge or on the return trip.

Driving over is nice except for the toll, but you can ride or run over if you do the 5 borough bike tour or run the NYC marathon. I did the bike tour once and let me till you riding over the bridge is not easy. That arc is huge and not easy after a long ride. But the views are second to none.

What used to be a great venue for the Seaside Concert series is now just a rundown patch of grass. The bandshell is in disarray from Sandy and since is no longer in use it's been left to rot

The playground in the rear needs some fixing up before someone get hurt. And there are no restrooms.

I love just walking around, so peaceful and quite. In the area they rent kayaks to paddle around the marsh and bikes to peddle around. No bike in the preserve though.  The Nature Center is staffed with very nice rangers and offer activities for the kids.

A nice place to sit and relax away from the Seaport. Not as crowded and more peaceful. You get great views of lower Manhattan, Brooklyn and the Bridges. There is a coffee shop and plenty of seating in the area.

A beautiful open space park to just take in some sun or even fly a kite. With a DecoBike Station very close by its easy to get to. Offers a fantastic view of the inlet and there is food and shopping close by.
Great park in the heart of the city. Always something going on here. Great playground with sprinklers for the kid on those hot summer days.
Ok I don't get it pay $20 to sit on ice and have a drink? Why? And that does not exclude drinks. $45 with the fur coat. Tourist trap.

I'm giving this fivestars strictly because of the Mead offerings that they have there.  While they have some excellent fruit wines there in general they are sweeter than I really like.  Although if you like fruit wines this is certainly the place you should be visiting.  They are the oldest meadery in Virginia with a excellent selection of various types that they have brewed.  So if you like Meade you definitely do not want to miss this place, also don't just settle for what they pull out for tasting make sure they know what you like and they have other varieties they'll let you sample.
likes: Fruit wines (for those who enjoy them)

reviews_attraction.text:
Overall an outstanding distillery for traditional liquors.  they have their own unique take on how they distill their liquor everything comes from Virginia with some awesome recipes for the various ryes and single malt liquors they do.  they have two locations the one in Williamsburg and the original location in Sperryville.

Just wanted to make a quick update their location in Williamsburg.  They have now finished remodelel the hotel and their tasting/speakeasy room is great and is an awesome place to do cocktails and shop.  Well worth the stop if you're in the area.

First Meadery we had ever gone to. I don't have a lot of places to compare it to but this one was very good they're running small batches so it does change. Also never went to a place before where I tasted different types of honey.

Have to update this based on our last visit and I must admit they've really improved overall.  They now control the entire building and have expanded to additional Meade flavors and overall the honey tasting has approved.  So well worth it if you're in the Williamsburg area and like meade.

This place would normally be maybe 5 stars but I can't say for certain as due to The COVID nonsense we couldn't do a full tasting.  it is a very nice and scenic location with a wonderful porch you can set out on and have a bottle of wine or a glass whichever you prefer.   They don't sell food here although I was told they do have food truck available.  Of course if you're cheap like me you can bring your own snacks.

Very nice place to visit I was surprised if some of the history in the museum. Didn't know it was for Jefferson Davis's last White House was for a whole 7 days. Even though the house has went extensive Renovations over the years it's still easy to see how people live for the times. Well worth taking the audio tour takes about an hour and worth all the time going through the rooms.

Not really fair to rate as we didn't stop to sample.  We made it into to parking lot but all the 'Do Not' (walk in in yard, etc.) signs completely turned us off so we departed.  Just didn't feel welcoming and there's too many vineyards to feel uncomfortable.  It's a shame as we sampled their Apple wine at Stribling Orchards and it was outstanding.

This is a very large Vineyard and Winery with some outstanding wines. The only reason I'm giving it 4 stars is because I don't like the commercialized aspects such as the assembly line tasting process. To me this really takes away from the whole experience of what should be a smaller vineyard with a more Personal Touch.

Second, and last, tourist stop of the day.  I expect the rest will be shopping, microbrewery, etc.  Really like this place and the view is outstanding.  Right now the museum is closed, but all the outdoor stuff is open as well as restrooms.  Keep in mind it's still 10 dollars per head to visit without an annual pass

Very nice trail with a homestead halfway up and some pretty cool freshwater springs.  this is a moderate hike with all the elevation gain done in the first mile the trail is very well maintained.  We use this trail to the AT and then up to Mary's Rock overlook.  Total distance up and back about 2.9 miles.

Overall a very historic and well laid-out Winery with lots of outdoor seating and a large and modern tasting room.  With the virus nonsense there is now a 3 sample tasting method with 2 oz pours.  I will say that between my wife and I we had six different wines there and all of them were very good.

Essentially the grounds are closed.  All you can do is walk up to the lighthouse via this long ramp.  The old lighthouse keepers house is privately owned and not open to the public.  Worth going to if you're on the island, but I wouldn't come here just to see the lighthouse.

It's not free at roughly $14 per head for an adult but it's well worth the money in the tour is outstanding I highly recommend the guided tour and or the audio tour. We went there also for the beer and Blacksmithing on the lawn was extremely interesting.

Outstanding micro distillery with a lot of flavors and my favorite was the Honey Whiskey and Carthuasian (I'm sure I spelled that wrong) Whiskey.  Also they have a great tour and lounge/bar where you can taste everything.

Outstanding Museum the very topics from early Schoolhouse, Maritime, American Native (for the area), and architecture exhibits.  Try and time your visit and get a guided tour it's free and very informative.
This is the actual place where Stonewall Jackson eventually died after his wounds. It's a lot nicer than I expected with one of the original houses there where he was treated from the Old Farm.
Overall nice set up, but be ready to walk, a lot.  It's all spread out with well defined areas, but if you've been coming to the State Fair you can tell they're still refining their layout.
Gotta love a good sand dune.  This is a have too place to visit if you're in OBX.   It's a pretty good walk up loose sand and you definitely want to go early before the sand gets HOT!
Outstanding condition of the palace and with very knowledgeable people that take you through the tour.  There are also beautiful gardens surrounding the palace that are worth seeing.
It's a good aquarium for this area with a lot of interactive displays and educational nooks.  they also have various movies playing all day and a nice outdoor Marsh walking trail.
Outstanding Museum overall and the price is very reasonable. We do highly suggest you go any day other than Sunday since they do not serve drinks at the end of the tour that day.
very nice family park with pavilions, playgrounds, or at least playground equipment, a wonderful stream and trails that will entertain kids 4 hours.
Can't say much about the place because they're one of the few wineries that aren't doing tastings so we just left and went to a local microbrewery.
It's part of the overall lighthouse tour.  Very interesting battery that has been converted to a museum and you can walk through.
Building is in very good condition with very knowledgeable people that take you through the how laws were created at the time.
The place is amazing if you like history.  Make sure to wear good walking shoes as you'll be doing a lot of it.

Beautiful building, lots of souvenirs. Ticket sales were a huge mess, the camera didn't work, it took forever to get it to work right, the sold me tickets to Yorktown,  that I had no need for once I got there, they were tickets to some museum,  not to the battlefield park. The first ticket desk we went to told us all the benefits for veterans,  but they did sell tickets, got on another line for tickets, and they told me all the benefits for veterans.  Just go to the ticket couter, and buy just what you need, or they'll waste your time and money.

We played at the Wake Forest Winter Classic, the turf field were perfect, plenty of room between the two fields for player benches, we even had room for a tent, the facility looks brand new, however, there are no concessions, , and the bathrooms were completely out of soap, paper towels and toilet paper all weekend, could use a couple more parking spaces, plenty for the two games, but, when two teams are playing and two more teams arrive, well, alot of people were forced into parking on the grass after driving around to no avail.

An amazing place! Very interesting, the gardens were teaming with wild life, the people were all extremely nice, Joe gave us an impassioned tour of the slave quarters. There is so much to see and do we had to go back a second day. I got to pet a deer! Walk with peacocks, see armadillos up close, in the wild. So many different types of birds was very impressive.

Great place, really geared for kids, with lots of things to see and do, and experience science, anthropology, animals, nature, with a ropes course running all over above you as you visit the zoo. A real gem, you need to take you kids here, there is something for everyone, every one will learn something. And the kids will Thank you.

This is a terrific place for young kids, the carousel,  the kiddy play area, with cars, and boats, it's just amazing! Then there's a ball field, and concerts in the evenings (but you need to check the schedule for dates, and times). Plenty of places for a picnic, and enough parking. A must see when visiting Burlington.

We just happened across the gardens, what a pleasant surprise! We were there in the dead of winter, and it was gorgeous, the huge live oak, stepping with Spanish moss, loads of Camillias, beautiful vistas, and just a lovely stroll, well worth the nine dollars to get in.

We went to the naturalization  ceremony  on July 4th. They put on a wonderful show, and bused us in and out like clock work, they did a terrific job. I think they did everything they could to make it a wonderful experience despite the oppressive  heat that day.

Beautiful, well maintained, quiet place I love the little farm with the many farm yard animals.  My granddaughter loves watching the equestrian activities, my wife loves walking the dogs to the waterfall. There's  something  for everyone.

Plenty to see and do. Ride in a real train, ride in a trolley style bus, walk through so many exhibits about planes, trains and automobiles, but mostly trains, a fully functional train turn table, just a good day.

It's a small, shallow beach maybe thirty yards from the street to the water, nice sand, clean, with plenty of new amenities,  children's play area, plenty of parking, a couples piers, gazebo, picnic pavilions.

Great place for social dogs, and people. Room to run, sit in the shade, water for the dogs, two areas, active, and inactive dog areas, sally port for safety, and parking for about eight cars, six foot fence.

Fabulous, fun, plenty to do and see, we went to the international music festival,  so much food and terrific music at every turn,  looking forward to my next opportunity to visit Fayetteville. Great Job!
Beautiful park with easy access to the fields field 2 has bleachers so you won't  need to bring a lawn chair, easy access to clean restroom, but concessions were closed when I was there for tryouts.
Great place to take the kids, so much to do and see, and experience. So many animals, and exhibits, so much to learn about, it's a wonderful little known gem in Greensboro, but it won't be for long.
Lovely pedestrian area, many unique shops,  but I was a little put off by some of the street musicians/performers, and other people who didn't look like they were there for the shopping or dinning.
If your looking for a great hike this is the place well marked trails, but not amenities  due to covid 19. Lots to see, a tremendous view from the top, but you'll have to earn it.
Best zoo! I've been to, Bronx, Atlanta, Little Rock, just to name few, this one is amazing! So many animals, and so easy to get around, and so many amenities,  well worth it.
Great place to stroll,  and relax, nice shops, and food all around the square. There's a parking deck in the NE corner, it's always difficult to find a parking place.
Your kids will love this PLACE! We took a 3 year old girl and she just took off running investigating  everything, wonderful safe space for kids well worth it.
New Bern is a beautiful old town with plenty to see and do, the Birthplace of Pepsi Cola is among them, friendly people there to help you purchase a Pepsi.
Very interesting, I learned a lot about early American history, and it's a beautiful place to walk, bike, walk your dog. A hidden gem, well worth a visit.
Acres of land full of the history of the American revolutionary war. Very interesting, and well maintained,  beautiful just to drive through.
Beautiful fields, loads of historical signs, and cannons, all the historical earthworks have been rebuild as they were back in the day.
This is a beautiful park right on the waterfront, plenty of benches in the shade, well maintained, nicest people just having a stroll.
Beautiful! Several overlooks to see, some involve a good deal of steps, but some are an easy walk in the park, you choose.

If you are into lava tube caves as much as we are, this is a MUST STOP N FIND!
The walk along the beach is just so beautiful in itself. The flooded lava tube has 2 openings. The water was a bit chilly, but not so bad we did not go in. We did bring flashlights, I brought my caving helmet ⛑ and headlamp. Worth bringing these! 💯%
We explored the cave from one end to the other. Know how to swim, know your limitations!
This was by far one of the best cave experiences I have had! The warmer, the better during the day, the more sun, the more spectacular the colors will be when inside the cave.
PLEASE BE RESPONSIBLE AND RESPECTFUL!! 🙏❤💕🙂

As usual, I love anything to do with education and the ocean. The Marine Science Center is no exception! They have tanks to look at the critters, and so much more!
Take the time, explore! Please donate and support the science center! They are so much more than just a few "fish tanks" they help with education with the schools, education programs for the general public, conservation efforts for our watersheds and local marine areas! This is our center so go down and enjoy it! The park surrounding the center is really nice too! Enjoy the dock, the beach! Look across and see Canada.

What an amazing place with such a history. Well worth the drive out. The rugged coast line was spectacular when we were there. We did need 4 wheel drive, we took our jeep. It was 80 degrees so remember some water!
The stone work is just amazing and the grounds are very well maintained.
Found really big Grasshoppers along the trail up. They were fun. The road is narrow, plenty of room to get around on coming traffic.  Make this a stop along your journey exploring Hawaii

We arrived with heavy surf pounding the rocks. Simply amazing. Stayed for nearly 2 hours taking photos and video.
Be careful out there! Fall in, not sure yiu are coming back out alive.
Explored the tide pools, read up on the history. Really sad to read the names and ages of the victims of the tsunami April 1st.
The grounds were well taken care of. A massive rock did roll out into the road. Watch that... the signs are up for a reason!

This has been one of my favorite bridges since I was a kid. The crazy storm that washed it out made national news of course... but that made it so decades later I could dive sections of that bridge at the SCUBA diving park in Edmonds. I have dove the west side of the bridge that is there now, walked the beaches, and watched marine traffic pass through. It is an engineering marvel. I have enjoyed rolling over that bridge for decades.

Great place for a stop, walk, or have a day out on the water. Cool place to stop and see the views!
But I have one very major issue... if this is a bird sanctuary, who thought it would be a good idea to feed the feral cats?
Where is the humain Society or Fish & Game? Not only are the cats being fed, some idiots are housing them.
Highly disappointed about that.

Now this was spectacular! Walked the entire grounds. An amazing place and incredible views. The stone work is epic. The size of it and history is just amazing. Took an hour to see it all. The staff there was excellent, full of knowledge! Ask question!!
Plenty of signs and displays telling you the history of the islands and of the Hawaiian people. A MUST stop!

Worth the hike down or having a 4x4 to drive down the spectacular road. The black sand beach stretches out with beautiful surf. Plants are incredible of course. Glimpses of the epic water fall up the valley are seen from the beach. It was a must stop on our list of places to see. Even just from the lookout at the top it is worth the pleasant drive out.

An amazing Japanese garden to quietly explore and remember the victims of the tsunami.
The small structures, plantings, paths, and water features are really very nice. We had breakfast there. Despite the rain, it was a beautiful place to visit. I will be back.
There was quite the variety of birds there too, along with a few mongoose and stray cats.

A long time ago I used to walk out to the other side. Now they have wire up and there is a fine if you are caught on the bridge. Not worth it. Still fun to come and see. It is great that my children get to see it now too. It is very interesting history. If you go, take a trash bag and help clean up.

This is the trail to take if you are heading south along the coast. Have been going to this beach for over 40 years. Love the trail and the beach. While a bit of a hike, it is spectacular! Absolutely love that area and section of the coast!

While crammed away inside a resort, this park is filled with lava tube caves!
Tread lightly.... we saw and explored 8 of them. Some are very tight. Wear gear if yiu go into anything but the large one. The rock here is very sharp.

So far, best place to take a photo of the sunset. Parking was interesting... plenty of photos to make it worth while!
Lots of people there to see the sunset, everyone was super friendly and respectful.

An adventure awaits anyone who visits.  The park has changed over the decades, but it is still stunning to visit. I am the 4th generation to visit and I have brought my children here. Live this place.
A very fun place to walk the trails, look at the trees and breath in nature. It has been slowly improving over the years. A fun place to visit and bring the kids. I have spotted many a bird there.

Worth EVERY step it takes to get here. Green sea turtles were in the water n sleeping on shore. Went snorkeling. Water wasn't super clear, I assume because of the rains.
Saw so much!!

Most people will associate Hawaii with volcanos 🌋 and you should!
Take the time to go intontheboark and explore. Plenty to see and do!
Animals and birds, out standing plants!
Loved it! Stayed for 3 days! The weather was ever changing and taking photos of the sunsets was just amazing. So much to see and explore on the coast!
The visitor center is in covid-19 lockdown, but take the time to see the art gallery next door! Absolutely beautiful art on display and for sale.

Epic place to go snorkeling! Arrive early, have reef safe sunscreen!
Amazing fish to see. Watch the water outside the little protected cove.
What a treasure to find! I had no idea this park was even here! Stumbled upon it. So glad I did! Absolutely stunning beauty.
Into art of all kinds? Then stop and see what is new! Bring the whole family, a great place to spend a few hours relaxing.
Anywhere in the park can be magical. It is a precious place that must be seen to truly experience. A must see and explore.
I love this park! A safe and beautiful place to walk. Very well maintained trails and the pond is terrific!
My family donated this land in memory of my great aunt. It is still a special place for me to visit!

An awesome place to visit! Catch a ride out to the crater (there are multuple companies that go the crater) and enjoy the cryatal clear water, abundant & colorful coral and the fish. There are no natural foods here for turtles, so you will not see a seat turtle sadly.

Water ranges from a few feet to over 30. Make sure you are in a group or swimming with a buddy as the currents here can change quickly and get rather strong. Tour groups offer flotation devicea, which I recommend unless you are a rather experienced swimmer with fins. DO NOT SWIM ALONE OR SEPARATE FROM YOUR GROUP. I cannot stress this enough as the ocean will chew you up and spit you out (dead) without hesitation.

I highly recommend this place. The only downside was the day we went at least, there were not a ton of fish (I see more fish at Shark's Cove on my home island of O'ahu) but the beautiful coral made up for it. As a bonus, en route to/from the Crater you can see the occasional dolphin, sea turtlea and during season, humpback whale. And a second bonus, great views of Lana'i, Mau'i, Big Island and Moloka'i on clear days.

Enjoy, be safe, pack out all of your trash, respect the wildlife and swim with Aloha!

An awesome hike with lots to see and learn about the 1959 Kīlauea Iki erpution and lava lake.

The trip from trailhead to lakebed is about 1 mile in length and 400ish feet in elevation change. Recommend taking water and a light/raincoat as the weather changes constantly. The trail starts out as blacktop but transitions to hard packed dirt or gravel in spots with some steps and tree roots to help on your way up/down.

With my wife, five and six year old daughter we made it to the bottom in appx. 35-40 and back up in 45 minutes. The trail is not terribly difficult but be prepared and stretch beforehand if you do not exercise regularly. The lakebed is flat and stretches about one mile across for easy walking but it is volcanic rock so be careful and trips/falls onto volcanic rock will cut you much easier than dirt or even regular rock.

I recommend 2-3 hours if you want to go out and back across the entire crater (~4.4 miles). Check the weather before going, bring sturdy shoes and have a good time learning the history of the crater!

Also, if you ask for more Kīlauea Iki crater pictures at the Visitor Center, they have some really cool 8x11s and lots of more info!

A hidden gem of a beach, located on the south side of Hickam AFB. It is a small beach, granted, but it is on a military installation which limits visitors. The beach is situated between runways  4L/22R and 4R/22L. It is also situated on the waterway the flows out of Pearl Harbor. Why is this important? Constant civilian and military aircraft taking off and landing, along with naval ships coming and going. You also have a great view of the Honolulu shoreline! There is also a bar/grill right next to the beach and you can rent canoes, kayaks and surfboards at the beach at reasonable prices.

The beach is safe, usually having low waveand the beach patrons are friendly. Lifeguards are on duty until 1700 I believe and the JB PHH military police patrol the parking lot. It is not the most scenic/touristy beach but if you are military it is free, safe and cool jets/boats are great to see.

If you are looking for gorgeous, mountain ringed beaches, try the east side at Bellows AS, Waimanalo and Lanaki (they are all great too) but if a small beach with many amentities, an awesome set of views, friendly people and safe parking is your thing, give Hickam a shot.

A quaint and small museum with a good number of aircraft to climb on and in. There are some military aircraft but also an DC-8/60 that you can touch and get inside of. Why does this matter? The DC-8 and Boeing 707 were  revolutionary jet aircraft that changed the way people traveled. There are few left flying and this is one you can get inside of.

There are a number of rotary winged aircraft (HH-3, HH-53, UH-1 and more) to get inside of. There is also a collection of fixed wing aircraft that include some A-4s, a F-4 and propeller aircraft (there is a DC-6 that is not museum property but you can sneak off and see this old bird).

All the aircraft are on the ramp, so on warm or sunny days bring water as you will get warm. There are also some Army tanks and artillery pieces outside you can clamber over, but again bring water and be prepared. The workers are friendly and knowledgeable, bathrooms are there. A good place to take the family.

The Lookout is great and all, but to get the best experience, find the secret cave, about 100m to the north of the Lookout. We Love this secret place. You park at the Lookout, cross the highway, head north to a non-descript bridge/overpass, scramble down the non-ocean side of the bridge to a small tunnel (there is a spray painted arrow on the bridge pointing the way). The tunnel is not very tall, so if you are 74" like me, prepare to duck a bit and bring a flashlight as the tunnel has a lot of "potholes."

Not many tourists go here because it is not the typical Waikiki/Honolulu/east side beaches thing. A word of caution, it is also a bit dangerous to get to as you have to cross the highway, then parallel to the highway. Once you pop out of the cave, you can climb down the cliff to the water's edge but be careful and not get to close. A rogue wave could easily pull you into the water and no one is going to get you out alive.

Fantatic memorial! Come and see the entire Harbor, not just Pearl Harbor. There is the USS Bowfin, USS Missouri and Pacific Aviation Museum also. You can purchase tickets for one place or all of them in a bundle at a discount.

The USS Arizona Memorial is free, as is parking. Free tickets are first come, first serve to the first 1300 people that arrive. A short movie is watched before boarding the boats to the memorial. The memorial is just that: a memorial. Be respectful, stay off you phones (unless taking pictures) and appreciate the magnitude of what you are seeing.

Parking is tight, so be prepared to drive in circles for a bit.

Also of note, there are Pearl Harbor survivors who are usually there to talk, shake hands and share stories. Take time to meet these people, listen to them and appreciate them (and thank them as there are very few left).

An awesome memorial to the US Armed Forces. Take a guided or unguided tour, your choice, but make sure you see the place where a war that killed an estimated 60 million people ended.

There are tour guides to walk you through and along the self guided tour to answer questions. Tours are on the main deck and also the deck below.  Be careful and mind your knees and head. As with any naval ship, things are tight and cramped so bumping into things is common.

Prices are $27 per adult, cannot remember kid prices though. Gift shop, food trucks and more are on premises too.

In late June and July 4th weekend, there are also picnics with discounted admission ($15 per adult, $10 per kid day of, but $10 per adult and $5 per kid if you buy in advance). You can bring your own food or hit up one of the food trucks, with a hands on exhibit and Lego play area.

An awesome, fun and safe expereince!  My wife and I took our two girls (6 and 7). They had no issues and loved it. Boat ride is about 15 minutes out to the sharks. Each group of swimmers gets about 20 minutes in the cage and the sharks come right up to the cage. We saw Galapagos Sharks, ranging in size from six to 10 feet.  Masks are provided but I would recommend bringing your own.

A safety briefing is given prior to departure and again when the cage is being dropped in the water. The cage remains attached to the boat but it is pushed about 10-20 feet from the boat. At no time did any of us feel unsafe. The masks were sanitized prior to being distributed.

Kama'aina and military rates are available. We highly recommend this tour (we might go again in the future) and you are supporting local when you use North Shore Shark Adventures!

I love this place! Come prepared for temperatures about 30 degrees below the valley temps, so long sleeves are a must and pants too if you plan to spend a good amount of time up here. Visitor's center is small but has a little guft shop with Haleakalā specific stuff.

Lots of kids activities, hiking opportunities and camping. Call the day before for the sunrise viewing, it is well worth it! The road to the top takea about 45 minutes with the drive bring half the fun (lots of switchbacks) but can cause car sickness in some folks. Be careful on the road as their are hikers and bikers along with changing weather (wind, rain, fog, etc...).

Remember to be careful of the wildlife, do not need or touch the wildlife, pick up your trash, respect the mauna and be kind to her and she will be the same to you.
dislikes: Potential car sickness on the road

reviews_attraction.text:
I love this place. Weather that can suddenly change to rain (and occasionally snow!) Then back to warm summer temps and then drop to almost freezing. On a clear day you can see the Big Island, Mau'i, Moloka'i, Lana'i, Kaho'lowe and the Molokini Crater. The gift shop is a little small but has neat stuff to buy and the workers & Rangers are full of good info.

The drive to the top run 30-45 minutes, depending on where you start. You can see multiple climate zones on the way to the top. At the top, the former crater makes you think you might be on Mars. There are also multiple hiking trails that are well worth it. Lots of stuff for people of all ages! Bring a sweatshirt/jacket and be prepared for random rain showers!

An under-visited memorial on the west side of Ford Island. While not as famous as the USS Arizona or USS Missouri, this is still an excellent memorial to visit as it is quiet, out of the way and not as trafficked. The memorial is nice, well done and it is customary to leave a coin when you visit (I suggest you do).

As opposed to the Arizona, there is more left of the ship to see. It is the rusted, hulking underside of the ship. You can see it rusting away but you can also see where cuts were made to (try to) extract Sailors and Marines. Please visit but be mindful as this is the resting place for the dead. And remember to bring coins to leave on at the base of the flagpole, as is customary.

A great little zoo nestled near Kuhio Beach on Waikiki.

While small, this zoo has some animals I am not accustomed to seeing at typical zoos such as komodo dragons. The smaller size of the zoo is nice in that you can see/do most everything in 1-3 hours, before your kids melt down and destroy your outing. Also, if your kids do go volcanic on you, the beach is within a one minute walk so all you have to do is go straight from the zoo to the water and cool them off.

Prices are reasonable but even more so for military and the military rates applies to your spouse and kiddos too. There are a bevy of potentisl discounts so do not hesitate to ask.

A cool piece of history in the harbor that everyone should visit. The ten story tower has lots of history, 360 degree views of the harbor, city, ocean and airport. It is also free and there is a quick elevator ride to the top, so need to worry about stairs (if you are againat3stairs that is).

Parking is NOT free. Expect to pay $3-20 for parking, depending on how long you stay. There are some shops nearby that are nice also, but do not expect a full blown mall. The tower is clean and being a famous landmark is a bonus. Highly recommend you take 10 minutes out of your day and explore this piece of history!

A great park! Sadly, some of the places you might want to see are closed. Damaged or destroyed due to the 2018 lava. Stop by the visitors center for the most up to date info on closure. Bring plenty of food and water as resources are not as common here. Bathrooms are few and far between. If you are male, this is not as much as issue. If you are female, like my daughter who got an introduction to nature's bathroom, it might be an issue.

Also, fill you gas tank before going as there are lots of places to drive and see! Highly recommend this place, even if there are currently no lava flows!

This is a cool stop while you are on the south side of the island. A short walk from the free parking lot takes you to an elevated vantage point where a fence prohibits you from getting close to the blowhole.

The blowhole shoots eater between 50 and 100 feet in the air about every ten seconds. It is an impressive natural phenomenon and I recommend you check it out.

Also, there is a flea market on premises. It was not open when we were there and I suspect it is shut temporarily due to COVID but I cannot confirm that.

Go and enjoy this natural wonder!

Neat lookout, great views and a nice viewing area. You MUST pay to park but it is a state park and is only a couple bucks. Parking lot is ckose to the lookout area and is handicapped accessible. Be for warned it is usually very windy at the lookout. Umbrellas, small children and houses from Kansas will be difficult to control (Wizard of Oz joke) so be prepared to either hold on tightly or not bring things that can fly away. Highly recommend this lookout!

Tourist beach. No bathrooms nearby but most people who go here have a hotel room. Lots of shopping, food and the usual tourist traps here. The beach is nice and well kept but there are also a lot of homeless people so be prepare to be accosted for spare change, the occasional odd behavior and what not. Not much surfing here but you can slide out past the wall and catch some if you try or gropve down to Kuhio Beach and catch more regular waves.

A great place to stop before getting too far into the park. Lots of information and sadly, a lot of up to date information on all of the closed areas (as of September 2019). Currently the Jaggar Museum and Thurston Lava Tube are closed, along with roads and trails that are no longer in use (in part....because the crater swallowed them!).

Please stop at the center before going into the park for the most up to date info!

I love this place. Cool old cars, a decent gift shop, free to military and IndyCar drivers are known to stop in fairly regularly. Tours of the track are available here also, and I recommend the more expensive tour as you get to go behind the scenes and see stuff normally resereved for teams and IMS workers only. Well worth your time and money.....GO!!!

Went here for Alan Davis Beach, a very non-tourist beach frequented by the local population. A secluded, volcanice sand beach with a large natural pool that has diving boards shoved into the walls. Takes about 10-15 minutes to hike to from the parking lot. Small beach, a little bit of litter but great views and fantastic swimming.

Probably the best non-ocean beach you can find. Reminds you of the ocean in terms of beach size. Good views of Chicago...and also the mills. Bathrooms are new and fairly clean, some small food offerings are available and entrance fee is reasonable. Lots of hiking trails, wildlife and camping.

A good, touristy beach in Waikiki. Sand is clean, water is warm and most of the folks are polite and friendly. If you are looking for seclusion though, this is not the place for you. Finding parking is a pain and can be expensive too. Be mindful of others and have a good time!

A great, oversized statue of one of Hawai'i's most famous citizens. If you are a tourist or local, the trip to see Duke's statue is a must. Be prepared with very long selfie stick or ask a passerby to take your photo because Duke's statue is easily 10 feet tall.

A solid, small harbor for your only water borne access to Lana'i. The Expeditions ship will drop you off here and pick you up to go back to Mau'i. The harbor is a 10 to 15 minute walk to Hulop'e Beach and a 20 minute walk to thr Four Seasons.
Nice park, good beaches, lots of turtles and sea life to be seen even when not snorkeling. Park is a little dirty and there are finite number of toilets and TP....so pack accordingly.

A Must Do while visiting the island of Kauai!
Waimea Canyon also nicknamed The Grand Canyon of The Pacific is one of the beat places to visit on the island.
It is a totally different experience, and you will not find anything like this on any other Hawaii Islands.
You can drive and stop only on specific lookouts, but if you really want to see the canyon, you definitely want to hike some trails for a better overlook of this beautiful place.

I love the vegetation and the three waterfalls on this hike. I prefer just to hike to the top of the waterfalls and return on the ridge parallel thwn hike the whole thing.
Unfortunately the trail after the waterfalls got very eroded, small landslides, and after you reach the top, the traverse to the other side is very over used and slippery.
I wouldn’t suggest to hike it when it’s raining, it can be very dangerous.

Probably one of the most touristic trails on the island, but still nice and worthy to go here. It's all paved road leading up to the Lighthouse lookout. On the way you can stop on different places and try to look for whales on the winter months, or just relax your eyes on the ocean.
The access to the lighthouse is closed, but at the end of the trail there is a nice view of the lighthouse from the top!
Enjoy!

Kailua Beach Park is a great place for kiters, beach lovers, familys, paddleboarders. Dependent on weather you can do many things on that beach. The water is nice, but it can get windy, that is when the surfkitees are out.
The only problem with this place that it became very popular for tourists, so there is a lot of people usually, and in the weekend is packed!

Pu’u O Kila lookout is the last stop when you drive from Waimea Canyon to Koke’e State Park. It has one of the beat views, and if you continue from the lookout the hike on the rim on Pihe trail, you can have even more amazing views.
Your beat chance to have views is in the morning, afternoon the clouds can roll in, so make sure you are out there early.

If you want a nice stroll at the end of the island right by the ocean, this is your trail. On the way you can see some sea arches, blowhole, seabirds and if You are lucky, even monkseals.
It can get very hot, so you better start early or late in the day! If you are into running, it makes a nice running trail too.

This is one of the places I go a lot. This is where I learned Stand Up Paddling, the bay part is very nice, very calm usually. The paddling to Chinaman's hat is easy and nice.
The view from the top is amazing!
It's not the perfect beach that's why I give 4 stars instead of 5, bit other then that is great place!

One of the best easy seacoast trails in Kauai.
There are amazing views wherever you look.
It can get hot, so make sure you have a hat, sun protection and enough water with you. Depending on how long on the trail you are planning to go, prepare accordingly.
Happy trails!

This is one of my favorite place on the island for hiking, sightseeing.
It's a beautiful area! It's the wettest place on the island, but that makes it so green and beautiful.
You can go paddleboarding on the bay, or sometimes the waves are good for surfing too!

It’s a great place to start your hike or just to hang out or do a picnic between those beautiful Cook Pines.
I like to take the state trail up to Waahila Ridge all the way to Mt Olympus for the full experience and great views when weather is cooperating.

This is a short family friendly hike with beautiful views to the whole Kaneohe Bay. You can see from the MCBH through the Sandbar all the way to Mokoli'i Island (Chinamans Hat).
When the sun is shining over the ocean, the bay just amazing and colorful.

The Pali lookout is one of those olaces you have to see while you are driving from Honolulu to the Windward Side. It’s a historic place with a beautiful view to the whole Windward Side.
Don’t forget if you are a tourist you have to pay for parking!

If you want to have a nice view of the whole North Shore, Kealia trail is a good place to hike.
It is switchbacking up for a mile and a half to this nice little bench where you can rehydrate or get aome snacks while enjoying the views.

There is always a great time when you get away from the crowds and go to Mokuleia.
You can go for a hike, check out the climbing wall or just chill on the beach.
Weekdays you barely see anybody here, weekends are not as crowded either.

This beach is mostly use by people doing watersports, moatlu wind surfing and kiting.
It is a good spot for a beach walk, and for a short dip in the ocean too.
You are overviewing the whole West Maui mountain range from it.

Waimea Bay can be a perfect flat water beach experience or a total "wave monster". This is the spot where they hold the historic Eddie Aikau Big Surf Competition!
If you want to jump off a cliff this is a good spot too.

Likeke Falls is an always flowing nice waterfall.
It's an easy and short family friendly hike.
Usually I take friends here who don't want to do a longer waterfall hike, but still want to enjoy a nice stroll.

Definitely one of my favorite waterfalls in Kauai! Easy to get to it, very photogenic, and always flowing.
Sometimes tou can see the wild pigscoming out asking for food whileyou enjoying the waterfall :)

Aiea Loop is an easy hiking trail with a lot of beautiful eucalyptus trees around. Such a nice hike!
I prefer to do a nice trail run on it, so it makes it even more interesting!

Byodo In Temple is a really nice replica of a Japanese Temple in Kaneohe, Temple of Valley side. It's a nice place to visit and experience.
There is an entrance fee of 3$.
Very nice local beach! When the wind is down, the snorkeling is great, water usually very clear. The mountains in the background are giving the beach an even better look!
It's a small little park, but is a good stop when you are running or having a bike ride. This is the only place where you can rent kayaks to paddle out to the Sandbar!

What a great place to be!
Long, beautiful beach on Molokai’s west side.
Perfect for a stroll, sunsets or even stargazing.
It is a place you definitey want to visit!
It is a great trail up to the Koolau Summit Trail. The 1st couple miles are more open, then it gets more narrow and muddy, but overall a good trail.
It can be a good stop, to capture Chinaman's Hat in the distance. The park is not a big thing, and the water is pretty brownish.

The national park includes an extinct volcano on a tropical island and is one of the most stunning parks in the whole of the US. The summit can be easily reached by car, so that everyone can enjoy the views from the peaks, which usually involve being higher than the clouds and can include the whole island and beyond without. However, parking can be a severe problem, so you may have to drop passengers off before finding a space in one of the lower car parks. Additionally, I would highly encourage doing one of the listed treks on the top of the mountain to take in the martian landscape fully. However, do your homework: please read the path description, including length, height difference, etc. carefully before starting. If there are a very small group of you with two cars, one-way trips from top to bottom or bottom to top may be more enjoyable.
It is much, much colder on top of the mountain than at water level, so dress appropriately (you can check the weather forecast). Remember also to take water and suncream with you (there is less protection from the atmosphere at heights).
I highly recommend a visit for sunrise or sunset, too.
Before Covid, the park was very, very popular, so do not expect to be alone...

This is arguably one of the most beautiful and special parks in the US. Kauai's NorthWest coast is rugged, lush and uninhabited, thus offering spectacular natural scenery. The coast can be viewed from the top from the lookouts at the end of the road that comes up from Waimea. Additionally, I highly encourage you to take a half-a-day or a full-day boat trip, if possible starting from the North Coast. Only the boat will enable you to fully visit the secluded beaches and take in the full view of the island. If you are sporty, alternative solutions are kayaking or even hiking for a few days around the coast. Note that there are no man-made stopping stations, so that even finding drinkable water can be a problem. For the high flyers, helicopter tours are also a possibility. Note that in my limited experience (5 days in June/July), the weather tends to be good and sunny up to 10am and then clouds come in.

This is a stunning, tropical valley. I was stunned particularly by the lushness and richness of the vegetation. I would highly encourage a visit when in Maui, as I think that this is one of the most underrated locations on the island.
The trails beyond the paved pathways are not well signposted, so I would recommend doing your homework and checking out the length, altitude difference and exact location of the trails before starting. I took a circular trail that took about two hours to complete to get back to the entrance to the park and that went to the Iao Needle. However, the terrain is a bit difficult to navigate because of the vegetation and some steep climbs. So, bring proper hiking/trekking shoes. Additionally, it was very hot and humid, so bring plenty of water.

This is a great trail that can get you to the top of the extinct volcano or back to the road from the top. If there is a very small group of you with two cars, I would seriously encourage you to think about parking the two cars at the start and end of the trail to avoid having to go back the same way (and this way you can do the easier route of starting from the top and going to the bottom). However, this route is long, with significant height difference (especially if you are starting from the here and going up). So, I would recommend it only if you are fit and a good hiker. Otherwise, you simply risk getting extremely fatigued and spoil your holiday. There are great views and shooter trails on the top, which are shorter and more easily accessible.

This is a stunning botanical garden. Although prices are not low, I think the cost is totally worth the visit. You can get to see some lush forests and beautiful flowers as well as learn about Hawaiian plants and witness the centre's conservation efforts. I was really amazed by the suitability of the Hawaiian land and weather for growing extra large plants, as exemplified by the fig trees used to film Jurassic Park.

I probably wouldn't advise a trip to this park if you intend to spend the day on a beach, but it is definitely worth a stop and a nice stroll if you are driving around the island. The park is rather unkempt and faces a narrow, dark sand beach. What really makes the stop worth it is the stunning view onto the beautiful shoreline of the Kualoa Ranch. The area is quiet and there are no specific facilities.

This lookout is definitely worth a stop when driving along O'ahu South Coast thanks to the stunning views on the rugged coastline and the island's extinct volcanoes. I would encourage you to take a short stroll along the coast, whilst being careful not to get too close to the edge of the cliff. I think the best light is in the morning and the earlier you go, the easier it is to park.

This is another great lookout, although I prefer the Kalalau stop. The difference is that here you can take breathtaking views of the Napali Coast as well as of the island's interior. Be careful & check the weather forecast before visiting. When I was in Kauai (end of June), it was regularly very sunny until 10am, but got cloudy afterwards.

The Needle is a stunning rock formation surrounded by lush vegetation and a creek. It is possible to reach an overlook that better looks out to the Needle by walking through a less signposted trail. However, as the climb is steep, in thick vegetation and in hot, humid conditions, bring appropriate shoes and plenty of water.

Personally, I wasn't too amazed by the pools, as I have seen better natural pools and they are very crowded (I guess they are a safe place for kids to take a swim, though). However, I would highly encourage taking the trail up through the bamboo forest and the waterfall because I found that stunning.

This is my favourite lookout in O'ahu. The views onto the West coast are stunning and offer the perfect setting for great pictures. If you are short on time, this is still a great place to stop. If you have longer, you may consider reversing back to the larger car park and walk to the lighthouse.

This is a beautiful, secluded, small beach. The park is very clean and I didn't see many people when I visited. I agree that the beach may not be very convent if you are based in Honolulu/Waikiki, but this is a true hidden gem definitely worth a visit if you prefer to avoid the crowds.

The State Supreme Court is in a stunning building, which is fronted by a statue of Hawaii's king. There are signs with detailed history information in the park. Next door, there is the ancient palace, too. I would encourage a visit to Downtown Honolulu to learn about Hawaii's history.

I highly recommend a visit to the McBryde Garden despite the cost. Note that the gardens can only be accessed via a guided tour that starts from the Tropical Botanical Garden gift shop. You will be taken to the garden with a bus and then be walked through the main highlights.

The pier is worth a quick stop when in Waimea. The pier is well kept and allows you to take a nice look on the South coast of the island. The sand in this area isn't a beautiful, sparkly colour, but the scenery is still impressive.

I would highly encourage a quick stop in this lookout to take in the beautiful views on the North's interior and in particular taro fields. Then, you can proceed to Hanalei and beyond to explore the wild North of the island.

This is a great stop on the South coast of the island. From a high vantage point near the car park, you can look at waves breaking on the rocky coast and causing a blowhorn in a natural rock formation. Simply stunning.

This is another great stop on the road to take in Waimea Canyon. As other reviewers pointed out, check the weather forecast to select a time with sunny weather / fewer clouds (in the early morning when I visited).
This is a lookout onto a beautiful black, basaltic, rocky coast. I would encourage you to travel further at least up to the black sand beach to see similar, but even more stunning scenery.
This is a great lookout onto the spectacular Waimea Canyon. I would highly encourage a stop. Additionally, many beautiful trails into the canyon or the Napali Coast start nearby.
The park is well kept and offers shower facilities and pitches for beach volleyball. As the park faces the sea and West, you can take in beautiful sunsets from the promenade.
This is a beautiful, well kept city park that offers shade and quiet from the bustling Waikiki. The park is perfect from a break from the beach or busy shopping streets.
The tree is utterly incredible and the atmosphere around it is special. Although it has been downside, the oldest tree in Lahina is still the largest one in the US.
This is a beautiful park with a great view on cliffs and a lighthouse. Depending on the season, the place is a refuge for many different species of seabirds.
This is a nice beach, with good snorkelling opportunities. However, the beach is very crowded due to the many nearby resorts.

My favorite beach on the East coast, it is great to watch the sunrise also. The sand is white and soft, and waters are so green and clear. I love snorkeling there as well as kayaking or paddle boarding.  I also love to bring my family to barbecue on the beach. It is very pretty, and also popular among tourists. People drive from Waikiki to spend the day here. The beach and ocean waters are nicer here. Just check the weather before heading here. It rains often on this side of the island, and it can get windy too.

A favorite hike on the West side of Oahu! It is a beautiful cliff walk, which will take to the most western point of the Island. The tip of the hike is absolutely stunning; you will encounter many Albatross, and if you are lucky as we were, you will see some monk seals sunbathing as well. I love the fact, that this hike is more wild, non touristy, and you will drive though a more local area. Make sure you have plenty of water and sun screen, and also sturdy shoes.

Definitely a hidden gem on Oahu! Most tourists hike the Manoa Fall which is right next door, however almost never get to go to this Botanical Garden that appertains to Manoa University. This place is perfect! Never crowded, simply beautifully kept, and you will see tons of tropical flowers and trees. Get up early, hike Manoa Falls first when it's not too crowded, then take a short walk to the Arboretum; I bet you will like the later better!

A great hike on the North East Shore of Oahu! I like it better than other hikes, because it is never crowded and if you are luck as we were, you might find Likikoi( Passion Fruit), Strawberry Guava, Noni, Wild Peper, etc. The views get better as you hike upwards as well. Make sure you have plenty of water, and a snack to enjoy when you get up there. There is a table and benches shaded, a perfect spot for a picnic after the hike

Best Luau show on the island! I highly recommend it, look no further. I do live on ths island and I’ve been to all shows on Oahu. Bh far, this one is the best! The entertainers are so professional and the food is amazing. Great activity for families with children as well. Get there early, choose your seat and go enjoy the cultural activities and Hawaiian games. So much fun! The show is fun, engaging with lots of laughter.

Nice family activity while visiting Oahu. Don't miss the pineapple ice-cream which is fantastic! I also too my nephew on the Pineapple Express train, he had a blast! It took us through the tropical farm, with bananas, Mango and Papaya trees, Cocoa and Coffee plantations and gave us a little history about the Polynesians and Hawaiian Culture and history. They also have a great souvenir shop, which tends to be very crowded.

My absolute favorite place to sunbathe in Hawaii. The lagoons are pristine and water is always perfect to snorkel. This place is so quiet and much nicer than busy Waikiki. I prefer to come here anytime. It's never crowded and beach is very clean and well maintained. I always feel at home and cozy here. You can walk to many restaurants, luxury hotels, and tons of shopping.

One of the most beautiful falls I've ever seen. For sure the best one in Hawaii! There is a short and nice walk from the parking lot to the fall. The area around the fall is set up with chairs and tables, perfect setting for a picnic. I loved the country side roads, farms and the views from up top. This waterfall topped all of the others that I've seen in Hawaii.

My favorite hike on the North Shore Oahu! An easy and fun hike, good for families with children as well! Site parking is small though, or maybe you can find street parking. Take lots of water and  pictures! A hike that is a favorite among locals! Check out insta account @luxuryretreathawaii for extra info and perks!

A very nice site to visit and appreciate our history at Pearl Harbor! I enjoyed every site here, and I highly recommend it. Ensure you plan a full day, as there is so much to see and fo. It is great for families with children also. There are food courts and snack shops.

A great place for family activity! I highly recommended if you are in Waikiki area! I loved the intimacy of this place, it is not too large, however there is so much to see. Great for families if you ever get a rainy day in Hawaii

Beautiful experience and understanding of the Hawaiian culture and heritage. A great walk which ended with a beautiful waterfall that one can swim in it. A must do, if you are planning a trip to North Shore Oahu

Beautiful place on the North Shore. I love the fact that it is private, rarely crowded and it has a nice walk through the forest. You can also rent paddle boards and enjoy some waves. The price is $25 per hour.
A favorite of mine while visiting Big Island! Make sure you have a rain coat, hiking shoes, lantern and have fun. The cave has 2 wings, and if you feel adventurous, you can walk for miles!
Beautiful trail, one of my favorites on the west side of Oahu. We saw many albatross, whales and monk seals along the way. We also stopped and jumped in some of the tide pools by the ocean
We went there a few times. Very pretty, intimate, and lots to see. They café next door has great salads. It is never crowded. A must see if you like museums and if you are in the area .
I loved the view from up there, plus no one came while we were on top. Superb view, if you are in the area, must go. There is paid parking near by, and there is no fee to go up.
Very nice beach park, however, we felt parking is an issue. The parking lot is too small and crowded. You can park on the street though. I particularly loved the jumping cliff.
A nice place for surf lessons and beginners. The beach is never crowded, and it give you a more local feeling. It is also a great place for camping.
Best place to visit on the Big Island. Make sure you visit it during summer, if you want to reach the summit by car. A bucket list for Hawaii!
Such a beautiful and spiritual place! One of my favorite spots on west Oahu. We combined it this trip with a hike at Kaena Point. So pretty!
We have visited Bishop Museum Twice. Highly recommend it as an indoor activity in Oahu. Beautiful building with great history artifacts!
We have visited this temple many times now. Amazing experience each time! A place of solitude and quietness that we enjoyed each time!
Beautiful park, with plenty of space for  a picnic. I mostly love the view of Chinaman’s Hat Island and the surrounding mountains.
A difficult hike, please be prepared with tons of water and try to avoid extreme sun! the views from up there worth every effort.

(Translated by Google) A wonderful park! An experience that is not easy to live in other places in the world!
The crater with the bubbling lava, the road in a lunar landscape, the fumaroles, the lava tube, the Jaggar museum. All beautiful!
Highly recommended to stay until sunset to see the crater light up at night.
Unfortunately we were unable to get where the lava enters the sea, they are about 18km between there and back, with 42 degrees and the scorching sun we had to give up after a few km also on the advice of the rangers.

(Original)
Un parco meraviglioso! Un'esperienza che non è facile vivere in altri posti al mondo!
Il cratere con la lava che ribolle, la strada in un paesaggio lunare, le fumarole, il lava tube, il museo Jaggar. Tutto stupendo!
Consigliatissimo rimanere fin dopo il tramonto per vedere il cratere illuminarsi di notte.
Purtroppo non siamo riusciti ad arrivare dove la lava entra in mare, sono circa 18km tra andata e ritorno, con 42 gradi ed il sole cocente abbiamo dovuto rinunciare dopo qualche km anche su consiglio dei ranger.

(Translated by Google) It is not easy to reach it, even by asking people who live in the area we have not been able to get directions. It seems that nobody knows him and in fact once reached he gave us the impression that we were the first tourists for a long time.
It is surprising to think that these engravings date back to 200-300 years ago while in Europe they date back to the Stone Age.

(Original)
Non è facile raggiungerlo, anche chiedendo a persone che abitano in zona non siamo riusciti ad avere indicazioni. Sembra che nessuno lo conosca ed infatti una volta raggiunto ci ha dato l'impressione che fossimo i primi turisti da molto tempo.
E' sorprendente pensare che queste incisioni risalgano a 200-300 anni fa mente in europa risalgono all'età della pietra.

(Translated by Google) The view from this elevated position is something sensational, a lush green valley that flows into a blue sea. But keep in mind that it is located near one of the rainiest places in the world, so it is normal to find yourself wrapped in clouds. With a little patience and luck, you can wait for the right moment.

(Original)
La vista da questa postazione sopraelevata è qualcosa di sensazionale, una rigogliosa vallata verde che sfocia su un mare blu. Però bisogna tenere presente che si trova vicino ad uno dei luoghi più piovosi al mondo, quindi è normale trovarsi avvolti nelle nuvole. Con un po' di pazienza e fortuna si può aspettare il momento buono.

(Translated by Google) It is a small black sand beach. When we went there were very few people besides us so much that we thought we had the wrong place. Instead there were 2 large turtles who swam near us while swimming in the sea.

(Original)
E' una piccola spiaggia di sabbia nera. Quando siamo andati noi c'erano pochissime persone oltre noi tanto che pensavamo di aver sbagliato posto. Invece c'erano 2 grandi tartarughe che hanno nuotato vicino a noi mentre facevamo il bagno in mare.

(Translated by Google) A beautiful traditional village, well rebuilt to allow you to discover how the life of the locals was organized.
The road to reach it is a bit steep and not well paved, but it can be tackled with any car.

(Original)
Un bel villaggio tradizionale, ricostruito bene per permettere di scoprire com'era organizzata la vita degli abitanti del luogo.
La strada per raggiungerlo è un po' ripida e non ben asfaltata, ma si affronta con qualsiasi macchina.

(Translated by Google) A small, but very beautiful, Buddhist temple located in the valley of the temples (a hill with cemeteries of various religions).
The place offers a break of peace and serenity.
For $ 3 it is absolutely worth a visit.

(Original)
Un piccolo, ma molto bello, tempio Buddista situato nella valle dei templi (una collina con cimiteri di varie religioni).
Il luogo offre una pausa di pace e serenità.
Per 3$ vale assolutamente la pena visitarlo.

(Translated by Google) The lighthouse is beautiful, but the real attraction is the animals around it. A protected area where birds live freely. There are also Nene. We also got to see a flock of dolphins under the reef.

(Original)
