Bello il faro, ma la vera attrazione sono gli animali che stanno intorno. Un'area protetta dove gli uccelli vivono liberamente. Ci sono anche delle Nene. Siamo anche riusciti a vedere un branco di delfini sotto la scogliera.

(Translated by Google) Small church, nothing exceptional. It is not indicated along the road and you need to know where to take a road to get there. The only peculiarity is that in the cemetery there is the grave of Charles Lindberg.

(Original)
Piccola chiesa, nulla di eccezionale. Non è indicata lungo la strada e bisogna sapere dove prendere una stradina per arrivarci. L'unica particolarità è che nel cimitero c'è la tomba di Charles Lindberg.

(Translated by Google) One of the most powerful blowholes we've seen. Very high sprays of water rise. There are no indications, but when you see the cars parked on the street you have come to the right place.

(Original)
Uno dei blowhole più potenti che abbiamo visto. Si alzano degli spruzzi d'acqua davvero altissimi. Non ci sono indicazioni, ma quando vedete le macchine parcheggiate lungo la strada siete arrivati nel posto giusto.

(Translated by Google) It is a very nice beach for snorkeling. You log in by paying 7.5 $. The view from the top of the bay is also very beautiful and worth a stop even if you don't intend to access the beach.

(Original)
E' una spiaggia molto bella per fare snorkeling. Si accede pagando 7.5$. Anche la vista dall'alto sulla baia è molto bella e vale la pena di una sosta anche se non si intende accedere alla spiaggia.

(Translated by Google) A place to breathe peace and serenity. This Japanese Buddhist temple will allow you to see some of this reality. Also interesting is the nearby cemetery practically close to the beach.

(Original)
Un posto dove respirare pace e serenità. Questo tempio buddista giapponese vi permetterà di vedere un po' di questa realtà. Interessante anche il vicino cimitero praticamente a ridosso della spiaggia.

(Translated by Google) An opportunity to find out how a typical Hawaiian village was formed.
Also in the sea you can see turtles and tropical fish. Around the pond, however, it is nice to do birdwatching

(Original)
Un'occasione per scoprire com'era formato un tipico villaggio hawaiano.
Inoltre in mare è possibile vedere tartarughe e pesci tropicali. Intorno al laghetto invece è bello fare birdwatching
likes: On-site Activities: Birdwatching, Marine life observation

reviews_attraction.text:
(Translated by Google) One tree of truly impressive dimensions. Planted in 1873 it grew to cover the whole square and forming a beautiful park where you can stand in the shade of its leaves.

(Original)
Un solo albero di dimensioni davvero impressionanti. Piantato nel 1873 è cresciuto fino a coprire tutta la piazza e formando un bellissimo parco dove si può stare all'ombra delle sue foglie.

(Translated by Google) Difficult to reach, there are no roads for cars. The only alternatives are on foot (walking one or more days) or by ship to appreciate the landscape from the sea.

(Original)
Difficile da raggiungere, non ci sono strade per auto. Le uniche alternative sono a piedi (facendo uno o più giorni di cammino) o via nave per apprezzare il paesaggio dal mare.

(Translated by Google) A waterfall of considerable height, a pity that the observation point is not the best, but it is worth seeing. Parking is close and costs a few dollars.

(Original)
Una cascata di una notevole altezza, peccato che il punto di osservazione non sia dei migliori, ma vale la pena vederla. Il parcheggio è vicino e costa pochi dollari.

(Translated by Google) This beach has a convenient parking, but if you want to find the best sea point it is advisable to go right along the beach until you get to Tunnels Beach

(Original)
Questa spiaggia ha un comodo parcheggio, ma se volete trovare il punto di mare migliore conviene andare a destra lungo la spiaggia fino ad arrivare a Tunnels Beach

(Translated by Google) We saw it in the evening and the illuminated building with the gardens makes a certain scene. It would certainly be more interesting to visit it better during the day.

(Original)
L'abbiamo visto la sera e fa una certa scena l'edificio illuminato con i giardini. Sicuramente sarebbe più interessante visitarlo meglio di giorno.

(Translated by Google) In winter it is a destination for surf professionals. In summer there are waves but much less strong. If you want to swim, however, better choose other beaches.

(Original)
D'inverno è meta per professionisti del surf. D'estate ci sono onde ma molto meno forti. Se volete fare il bagno però meglio scegliere altre spiagge.

(Translated by Google) A beautiful botanical garden, for $ 10 you can admire a wide variety of flowers and plants of all kinds. It is definitely worth visiting.

(Original)
Uno stupendo giardino botanico, per 10$ potrete ammirare una grande varietà di fiori e piante di ogni genere. Vale sicuramente la pena visitarlo.

(Translated by Google) A small ancient church overlooking the sea and still in use for religious celebrations. The nearby cemetery is also very characteristic.

(Original)
Una piccola chiesa antica affacciata sul mare ed ancora in uso per le celebrazioni religiose. Molto caratteristico anche il vicino cimitero.

(Translated by Google) Close to where the path to the point where the lava meets the sea begins, this arch of rock on the sea is a point for great photos.

(Original)
Vicino a dove inizia il percorso verso il punto in cui la lava incontra il mare, questo arco di roccia sul mare è un punto per ottime foto.

(Translated by Google) There is not much to see, more than anything else it is interesting to read the story that is linked to this place and to King Kamehameha.

(Original)
Non c'è molto da vedere, più che altro è interessante leggere la storia che è legata a questo posto ed al re Kamehameha.

(Translated by Google) The guided tour that presents the history of this ship is very interesting. Inside you realize how mammoth it is.

(Original)
Molto interessante la visita guidata che presenta la storia di questa nave. All'interno ci si rende conto di quanto sia mastodontica.

(Translated by Google) The monument testifies to the place where James Cook lost his life. Nothing exceptional to see but a piece of history.

(Original)
Il monumento testimonia il luogo in cui perse la vita James Cook. Nulla di eccezionale da vedere ma un pezzo di storia.

(Translated by Google) A park with a very oriental look, where you can take a walk in peace while admiring the park and the sea.

(Original)
Un parco dall'aspetto molto orientale, dove fare una passeggiata in tranquillità ammirando il parco ed il mare.

I am so happy to say that I am happy that we decided to do the Pictured Rocks Cruises tour!

$37 a person is really steep but I am glad that we did it. We were visiting the U.P. for the weekend as my niece had just graduated high school down in Escanaba and we were up there for her open house. But since we had a free day we decided to be tourists and see what the U.P. had to offer. We saw several ads for Pictured Rocks National Lakeshore and decided that is what we wanted to do. Originally the plan was to hike through the park but then we noticed that you could take a boat tour of the shoreline. We decided that we would give it a short and chose the 12pm tour time.

When we arrived we purchased our tickets and stood on the dock waiting for boarding. For the 12pm tour they took out 2 boats (I don't know if all times are 1 or 2 boats). We saw a lot of people headed towards the 2nd boat so we chose the first. We sat on the upper deck despite the fact that it was a little cold with the breeze off Lake Superior. We managed to get a front row seat and waited for the tour to begin.

12p on the dot they started up the engines and we pulled away from the dock. Since we were boat 1 we left first. Very shortly after leaving the dock a voice came on over the PA announcing that we were 30 minutes from the start of the tour, a rundown of all the rules, how to put on your life jacket if needed, and other random information. The boat travels about 13 miles an hour and the tour is appx 2 hours and 35 minutes long. If you sit on the upper deck I strongly recommend wearing a light jacket or hoodie as once you're out on the water the temperature drops 5-10 degrees from the shoreline.

As you go along the route the captain gives stats about the lake, rock formations, how they get their color, and sometimes the bad joke. No harm in that, just trying to keep things entertaining. When they can they get up as close as possible to give you a better view of the rocks. It is a very peaceful and relaxing tour with some amazing views...views that you cannot see from the shoreline. What they didn't really explain very well is that the return route is exactly the same, so if you are on the right side of the boat, you get obstruction free views for pictures on the way back, vs trying to take shots without people's heads or boat parts in it.

I strongly encourage anyone and everyone to take this tour. The time flies by, you learn a thing or two about the area as well as Lake Superior, and its a great way to relax and enjoy nature and the water! Worth every penny in my book!!!

I have never been in a cave before so I did not know what to expect. People have told me in the past that when you go into a cave you end up crawling and getting dirty - and that just sounds awful. But Ruby Falls is nothing like that.

When you arrive you stand in a line waiting to take the elevator down to the bottom. They take you down in 2-3 groups depending on how many are waiting at that time. Once you are all reunited at the bottom the tour begins. Due to lack of space you walk in a single file line. If you like to take lots of pictures, I recommend that you make your way towards the end of the group. This way you don't hold up the people that are a little less interested in taking tons of pictures.

The temperature down there is somewhere around 60 degrees. So it's comfortable. Your tour guide will stop at various points of interest, explain why they're interesting and then move you along.

When you make it to the falls you walk into a fairly dark room. The lights are on a timer so that once everyone is inside you can enjoy the falls. The lights change color and there is music. Once the lights come on you have maybe 3-5 minutes before the shut off and you continue your way back towards the beginning.

The tour is about 1 hour long - maybe a little less. But I think it is worth every minute. Because it is technically a cavern there aren't spiders, cave crickets, bats, etc...which is perfect if you don't want creepy crawlies all around.

I definitely recommend taking the tour and seeing the falls. It's cool. Not sure if I would do it again more or less because I feel that once you see it you don't need to see it multiple times. BUT it is something that you NEED to see if you're in the Chattanooga area.
likes: Light and music show at the falls

reviews_attraction.text:
Words can truly not explain nor give credit to the DeYoung Family Zoo.

The DeYoung Family Zoo is a true hidden treasure in Michigan's Upper Peninsula. Hidden in the middle of the woods just outside Walden, MI is something that you would never expect to find. My family has been here before but my first visit was Sunday. It seemed strange as I am used to the standard zoo where you have cement and water separating you and the animals. BUT not here! All of the animals are just two fences away from you. Though this can see a little unsafe, it is not. AND it is really cool to be able to get that much closer to the animals.

As we walked around you can see monkeys, tigers, lions, alligators, wolves, hyenas, and many many more. All throughout the day they have different shows that are designed to educate you about the animals, vs putting them on display to entertain you. We caught the end of the wolf talk and did the "feeding the big cats". Between shows they bring out baby animals that you can actually touch and hold. I held a baby spider monkey and a baby dingo. It was so very cool!

As they fed the big cats they educated us about the animals. They have more tigers than most any other zoo that I have been to. Even though tigers are tigers they still made sure to educate us about each and every one.

Unlike your typical zoo they don't have lots of food options, BUT they do have some food vendors set up across the street from the zoo. It is very easy to spend an entire day here at the DeYoung Family Zoo. Even though it may not change all that often, I would totally visit again just to be able to hold more baby animals and learn about some of the other animals in their zoo that we didn't watch the shows.

Being a big fan of Ford, on a day trip to Detroit, I decided to stop by and pay this home a visit. When you arrive you are directed to the former greenhouse. At the greenhouse there is a restaurant as well as gift shop and place for you to purchase your tour tickets. You have to purchase a ticket to the guided home tour in order to see inside the home. You can also just walk the grounds for a fee of $5 but it's at your own pace, which is nice.

Once you purchase your ticket you are given the option of walking to the home, or waiting for a shuttle bus to take you. We chose to walk as we had 30 minutes to kill and it was a very nice day out. When you walk to the house you walk along a man made cove that was made by Edsel Ford when he was alive and lived in the home. This leads you to Lake St. Claire as well as the home.

It was nice today as we were the only ones on the 12pm tour. We were greeted by our guide, explained the rules (don't touch, don't take pictures, etc). Our guide was very, very knowledgeable about the history of the home, as well as the family. Room by room you are guided (only the rooms that the family used, not the servant quarters) given the history, and seeing the amazing detail in the home. The architecture is amazing, the décor is original and stunning. The views of Lake St. Claire are amazing!

The tour is 45 minutes long on average and then you are free to roam the grounds. The additional buildings on the grounds (power house, garage, play house, etc) are open to walk through. Those take just a matter of minutes.

All in all this place is amazing, and if you love architecture, history, and stunning details this is a must visit if in the Detroit area.

This is probably my new favorite State Park in Indiana!

I had no idea this place even existed until one of my employees went hiking with their boyfriend. She showed me some pictures and talked about how nice it was. So it was a nice day so we headed the 1.25 hours west to Shades.

When we arrived it literally is in the middle of nowhere. Not being there before we just followed the road until we found a good place to park with access to some of the trails.

What I liked is this park is small enough that you can access every trail in the park from any place that you park.

The trails here are rugged. Even the "easy" trail has some obstacles that you'll have to climb over. Trail 2 and trail 7 will have you walking through a creek. We hiked for 2.5 hours and only were able to complete trails 1, 2, 6, & 7 with partial completion of 9, & 10.

A lot of the hills have stairs with places to sit along the way in case its a bit much for you. There are also picnic areas at the start of trails 2, 6, 9, & 10 as well as an area just before you begin all the other trails (1, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 & backpack). It is not as busy as nearby Turkey Run (which is amazing) and the trails and views are just as amazing.

I want to go back very soon and complete all the trails that we didn't get a chance to this past visit. GO! HIKE! You won't be sad that you chose Shades State Park!

This, I believe, is the largest home in Savannah. It was also made popular by the movie "Midnight in the Garden of Good and Evil". The tour begins in the stable house out back from the home. If you want to tour you're better off buying tickets ahead of time vs walking in and hoping you can tour.

The tour guide begins by taking you out into the garden and immediately beings giving you the history of the home. When you walk in you get to see almost every room on the first floor. Again, you are given tons of history and they even explain paintings, artwork, etc. When you get to the office area they do mention the "incident" that happened which is what the movie is based off of.

The tour lasts maybe 45 minutes tops and includes the 4 main rooms on the first floor. You do not get to see anything on the upper or lower floors. You also do not get to see any of the servants quarters or the kitchen.

The home is occupied and the living quarters are on the upper levels. The home is also still in the family and was opened up for tours to help with the bills and upkeep.

For me, the tour is not worth the money. You don't get to see enough and you are basically left wanting to see more.

Belle Isle Aquarium is the oldest public aquarium in the United States. Opened on August 18, 1904 at the time it was the 1st in the United States, and the 3rd largest in the world. At the time too, it was the fanciest public aquarium.

The aquarium closed in 2005 and reopened in 2012. It is now run by volunteers and operates under donations. The aquarium is free to visit and is worth a visit. The tile work in the aquarium is amazing. The tanks, tile work, lighting are all original. Even the bathrooms are original. It is small by today's standards and you aren't going to see any exotic animals/fish.

They are only open on Fridays and Saturdays (as they are all volunteers), so you have to plan accordingly. Also, Belle Isle is a Michigan State Park so you will need a recreational pass to gain access to the island and all that Belle Isle has to offer. But it is worth it. Total visit is maybe 30-45 minutes depending on how busy they are - but again it is worth it.

Alpine Coasters are my new thing - they're so fun!

I don't like roller coasters so when I was dragged here I was anything but thrilled to be doing this. Little did I know that they are so much fun! You get to go down the hill by yourself and you control the speed! The way they work is they take you to the top of the hill and allow gravity and the incline of the hill to bring you back down. There is a lever on the side that you can pull back on to apply the brake if you get scared and want to go slower. Otherwise you push it all the way forward and go down the hill at about 30mph!

The prices are a little steep and you have to pay if you want to ride again - but at a reduced price of $8. Its just so much fun that no review can do it justice. The staff is nice and friendly - and even when you do something wrong like I apparently did they weren't jerks about it!

If you're in the area ride them...ride them all!

Amazing! That's all that I need to say about DIA.

DIA makes some of the other art museums that I have been to look like nothing. There is such a wide variety of exhibits and artifacts that there really is something for everyone. Today was my first visit to DIA, and I was far from disappointed. The building in and of itself is amazing. Just a beautiful building with great details around every corner. You definitely need the map they have at the counter so you can make sure not to miss anything.

In the atrium they offer food and drinks in such a cute setting. It would be so fun to just hang out there with some friends and waste the day away. You can do an audio tour as well and take the museum to a whole new level. There are even little "lets play a game" to make it more interesting for kids.

Definitely one of the best in the US and a must see for any art lover!

I've been here before for the butterfly exhibit in the spring. Our visit this time was for the display of the world Christmas tree displays. The displays were nicely done and the exhibits in other parts of the building were changed out from this past spring. I was expecting the trees to all be together in one room, but instead they were spread out throughout the building, which was nice. It was also nice that each tree had the country it was inspired by and a little bit of that nations traditions for Christmas. I think the kid in me enjoyed the train room the best. It was neat to see miniature buildings from around the Grand Rapids area. The broken glass exhibit was really neat too. Everything in the display was made completely out of glass.

Overall I like the gardens and feel that you could visit once a season and each time would be different.

This place is fantastic. We made our first visit over the weekend and fell in love. The cost is $5 per adult to get in, and its worth the price. You are lead through the home by a tour guide that is knowledgeable about the history of the home and the family that built it. When you walk in the front door its like taking a step back in time. The home is restored like it may have looked in the mid 1800s. We weren't able to see the east wing because they are restoring it, but even not seeing the servants quarters and kitchen it was still amazing. The tour guide walks you through room by room on all 3 floors of the home. There is a basement to the home, and it is opened to the public during certain events mainly during Halloween. When you're in the Madison area this is definitely worth the stop and hour of your time

This is a great park on the west side of Indianapolis. The park offers swimming, hiking, boating, kayaking, picnicking, etc.

There are places to fish, bike, and just enjoy nature. There is no overnight camping and they do not allow fires. Nessled up against the Eagle Creek Reservoir the park has something for everyone.

The grounds are kept clean and the hiking trails are clearly marked. The paved roads allow for lots of areas to ride a bike and not have to worry about being taken out by a car or truck.

There is a fee to enter the park - $5 for Marion County residence and $6 for everyone else. They do also offer annual passes that run January - December for $50 per year for Marion County residence ($60 for everyone else).

Its a nice way to escape the craziness of the city without actually leaving the city.

This park was made famous from the movie "Midnight in the Garden of Good and Evil". But even if that park was not in the movie it is a must see!

The park spans several city blocks that rounds out the outskirts of the historic district. The tree lined sidewalk, fountain, kids area, and cafe are all great. You can lay out in the sun, chat with friends, roller blade, bike, etc all in this park.

My favorite area was probably the area that you were not allowed to ride you bike. This allows for you to be able to walk slowly and enjoy the park without worrying that someone on a bike might hit you (by accident of course). So much possibility in this park.
likes: Facilities & Services (tree-lined sidewalk, fountain, kids area, cafe)
On-site Activities (lay out in the sun, chat with friends, roller blade, bike)
dislikes: On-site Activities (bike riding in certain areas)

reviews_attraction.text:
About an hour south of Indy you'll find this gem in the heart of Brown County. Brown County State Park offers places to hike, horse back, cycle, camp, fish, swim (not really but they have a pool on the campgrounds), and even a lodge if you want a cabin over a tent.

The grounds are kept clean and even though its a popular park you rarely come across tons of people out on the trails. You may encounter 2 or 3 at a time but most of the time you feel like you're all alone.

It's a great escape from the busy city life to the north.

Just like the Aquarium, Belle Isle Conservatory is free to view. There are 3 different rooms besides the main room with different plants. They have tropical, dessert, and everything in between. Just like the aquarium everything is original.

I think my favorite room was the tropical plants. They're just so colorful and unique vs a typical plant you would find outside in the woods somewhere. The conservatory has a nice flow and it is easy to move from one room to the next. There is even an outside area with a koi pond.

This place is amazing! There is so much to look at and see that it is easy to spend all day here. The price is steep once you start adding on the extras like Brick by Brick, U-505 Tour, Coal Mine, etc. All of the displays are interactive so its good for keeping kids occupied. I think my favorite was the Tesla Coil. It was loud though! Ok, let's be honest...my favorite was Brick by Brick! And honestly, the U-505 tour was really cool as its an actual German U-Boat from WWII.

Very cool guided tour through the cave system leading to the Lost Sea. The tour guide was very knowledgeable and entertaining while on our tour. The "sea" itself is cool and the tour includes about a 10 minute boat ride out onto the water. It's about 58 degrees in the cave and was a comfortable walk. The steepest hill isn't that bad, but if you dont like hiking you may not enjoy it. Round trip is about 3/4 of a mile.

Beautiful part of Savannah. So much history and easy to spend all day wondering around checking out all the squares.

The architecture is amazing and there is a good mix of new and old - the new doesn't even look new. It looks as though it has been there for hundreds of years.

So much to see, do, eat, and shop! Amazing historic district.

Small park with nice hiking trails. Being a smaller state park it keeps the amount of people visiting at one time lower. We spent 3-4 hours hiking the different trails and rarely came across other hikers along the trails. If we did it was 1 or 2 people and then it was back to feeling like we were the only ones out there. Highly recommend!

If you want to see the whole house you have to pay for both tours. The grounds are nice and you get a free wine tasting with your tour. You are limited to the 4 wines they choose for the tasting because there are so many people. But it's nice and the tour guides make learning the history of the property interesting and fun.
likes: Facilities & Services: Wine tasting, Tour guides

reviews_attraction.text: Interesting place. We came for Jingle Rails which is a display that they set up every year around Christmas. Several floors of art, most native American inspired. It was cool. My favorite was the large 3 part painting of the Grand Canyon. It was amazing.

Great park in downtown Newaygo. There is a walking trails that connects both ends of the park. The east side has river access and provides a nice area to enjoy the river on hot days. The west end has mature trees and offers more shade for picnics.
We came here for the Christmas Tree Display. I don't know much about the place to be honest. But it was nice inside. The tree display was cool and represented several local Indiana businesses.
Very cool art deco building in downtown Detroit with lots of history. The main lobby area has amazing tile work, a seating area, Bank of America, and a tourist gift shop.
Overall this is a great place to gather in downtown Indy. However, they need to make it more pedestrian friendly. At night, the whole area is not well lit.

nice arena, went here when there was a concert going on so they make you check your bags outside. luckily they don't charge for it. jordan statute is inside. there is a missed opportunity to add some bar or restaurant on the bottom floor. you can buy drinks there but there's no place to sit. overall decent place but could be a bit better. i was hoping to watch a game at the bar while i was here so there's some missed opportunities

Definitely one of the more challenging trail if you are not an active person. Try to go before sunrise to avoid the sun beaming on you. It is pretty much a railroad going straight up to the top. There are no railings. Halfway through the tracks you can potentially fall through the cracks if you are not careful. Overall it is a fun trail and totally worth it but I wouldn't do it again :)

This was an interesting experience. Staff was nice. I bought this off Groupon as well and it was worth it just to try. While you are waiting to go on the scooter you can snorkel. During the first few minutes there's a lot of pictures taking so I wasn't sure when I can go. The fish feeding experience was fun as well. They will nibble your hand so just be aware. Remember to tip well!

parking is limited here. you can park along next to the no parking signs and hope for the best. hike is very narrow and steep. it is one path up and one path down. use the restroom ahead of time because it will be challenging to go because there's always someone in front and behind you. great view of the lake once you traveled up a mile

I came here specifically for fishing. I did see quite a few people fishing here as well. Went on a sunny Sunday morning and spent about 5 hrs here. Only saw one guy catching one fish.  I personally wouldn't recommend it for fishing but might just be one bad experience. I might give it another try one day and change my review.

awesome free zoo! tons of gorillas, i have paid more for other zoos that aren't as good. great place to bring your kids, seems like they have a lot of activities going on. the animals seem like they are treated pretty well. there were swings and a bunch of toys for the animals

nice building with a lot of historical background. i live in boston so i personally only come here for the Ruth Chris restaurant inside of the building. it is pricey but if you are here during  Dine Out boston week should definitely check it out

i was power walking by here to get to my scheduled time for courageous sailing nearby. seems like  a nice historical area with the freedom trail leading through it. i definitely recommend try sailing at least once if you are in the area.

Good place to walk around and enjoy the scenery of Boston. It is minutes away from the movie theatre, shopping and dining area. There's always a bunch of festivities going on during the weekend. Good place to catch pokemon too ☺️

Good low key hike with an interesting beginning. There is a very high incline hill up depending on the path you take. It eventually evens out and got a decent view on top. Went here on a weekday afternoon and it was not crowded

nice close hiking place in boston. parking can be challenging in the summer, there are often cars just parked on the side of the streets and hoping for the best. not much of a view up top but there's still a decent rest spot.

Nice place to walk around and catch vulpixes in pokemon go. Always a lot of people here. Theatre is nearby and it is a historical area too if you are into that. It is minutes away from Newbury so you will find something to do

Nice looking place I guess. Grew up in Boston so nothing too special here for me. I would imagine tourists and city dwellers would enjoy the area. Plenty of restaurants nearby. You can go admire Harvard school as well

Seems like a decent park but not many seats or picnic table near the parking area. You would need to walk in further. Other than that park looks spacious. I was short of time so did not have much time to walk around

Been here a couple times. It is always lively and they have a lot of chairs in the grass for you to hang out. Definitely worth a visit if you never been. It is nice to see all the history around the area
Awesome place to play Pokemon Go. Plenty of free parking. You can jog and enjoy the scenery. There is a free tour here too I believe but check the hours. You can go inside the castle and look around.
Best zip lining place i have been too! I love everything from the rocky rides to the actual zip lining. I tried the second highest package but I will definitely go back for the highest.
Never really go to this park. It was always a bit out of my way and Dorchester was more dangerous back then. It seems safer now and I do see more people walking around at night
Definitely a must visit if you are in Hawaii. Pineapple 🍍 ice cream is delicious. The maze is fun too. Nice scenery and gift shop. My favorite part is still the ice cream.
Has track field here and it is minutes away from the baseball fields. It is close to the jfk UMass train station as well and the beach is within walking distance
Good place to go if you are into history. The general exhibits are free. If you want to do the audio tours and go on the boats then prepare to pay more.
This is a nice place to go biking and walking around. Awesome place to watch fireworks on 4th of July but can get crowded. Prepare to come really early
definitely a good alternative compared to the willis tower, you can go to bar at the top, buy a drink and enjoy pretty much the same view
Great park to play sports, fly kite or just run. There's a nice playground there for the kids and bunch of places for a picnic.
beautiful view of the pond. there is a nice long bike path as well if you want to walk/ride along

(Translated by Google) Take a sightseeing boat ride for about 25 minutes one way. The outbound route is usually an English guide by the captain, explaining the history, culture, geography and plants around the Wailua River, and Hawaiian entertainment (hula and music show) on the return route. (Depending on the time of day, the order may be reversed.) It is highly likely that a Japanese guide will accompany you on a 2pm tour. There is a cave just 2 minutes walk from the state park dock. Before 2006, you could enter the cave, but now you can't enter the cave. Look up at the cave from the front stage, receive a historical explanation of the cave, and enjoy romantic music and hula.
Some people say that the charm has been halved without entering the cave, but it is a tourist attraction that represents Kauai, so I would definitely recommend you to visit once. Boat departure times are 9:30 am, 11 am, 12:30 pm, 2 pm and 3:30 pm (as of October 2016).

(Original)
遊覧船で、片道約25分乗って観光します。通常、往路が、船長による英語ガイドで、ワイルア河周辺の歴史、文化、地理、植物の説明を受け、復路にハワイアンのエンターテインメント（フラとミュージックショー）があります。（時間帯によっては、順番が逆になります。）おススメは、午後2時発のツアーで、日本人ガイドさんが同行される可能性が高いです。州立公園の船着き場からは歩いてわずか2分ほどの距離に洞窟があります。2006年以前は、洞窟の中に入ることができましたが、現在は洞窟には入られません。手前のステージから洞窟を見上げ、洞窟の歴史的な説明をうけ、ロマンチックな音楽とフラを堪能します。
洞窟に入れず魅力が半減したという方もいらっしゃいますが、カウアイ島を代表する観光スポットですので、是非一度は訪れることをおすすめしたいと思います。ボートの出発時間は、午前9時30分、午前11時、午後12時30分、午後2時、午後3時半となっています（2016年10月現在）。
likes: Facilities & Services: English and Japanese guides

reviews_attraction.text:
(Translated by Google) A bronze statue of King David Kalakaua, donated and produced by a Nikkei community in 1985 to commemorate the 100th anniversary of the government immigration. On the way to the world tour, King Kalakaua stopped by Japan and met with Emperor Meiji. At that time, he was also called “Father of Japanese Immigrants” because he begged for Japanese workers to travel to supplement the labor shortage in sugarcane fields, which was a growing industry in Hawaii. The ferocious figure standing near the entrance to Waikiki has become a landmark and impressive.

(Original)
1985年に官約移民百周年を記念して日系人社会が寄贈制作したデービッド・カラカウア王の銅像。カラカウア王は世界一周旅行への途中、日本に立ち寄り明治天皇と謁見。その時、ハワイで成長産業となっていたサトウキビ畑の労働者不足の補充として日本人労働者の渡航を懇願したことから「日系移民の父」とも呼ばれる。ワイキキの入り口近くに立つ精悍な姿は、ランドマークとして定着し、印象的である。

(Translated by Google) Kokee's Natural History Museum also serves as a gift shop. There is a small-scale display of the birds and animals that live on Kauai, as well as a panel exhibit on terrain models, weather, and nature. Some are available only here, such as moss trail guides and plant brochures. Admission is not compulsory, but optional donation of $ 3 per person. I think it's nice to buy something at a stand and contribute to sales.

(Original)
ギフトショップを兼ねているコケエの自然史博物館。小規模ながらもカウアイ島に生息する野鳥や動物の展示説明や地形の模型、天候、自然に関するパネル展示があります。コケエのトレイルガイドや植物のパンフレットなど、ここでしか手に入らないもあります。入館料は強制ではありませんが、任意で一人3ドルの寄付。売店で何かを買って、売り上げに貢献するというコクア(手伝い)もナイスだと思います。

Izumo Taisha is one of the major Shinto Shrines which has about 300 branch shrines in Japan and their headquarters is located in Izumo city, Shimane Prefecture.  The history of Izumo Taisha is as old as Japanese myth and their original remains can be traced back to the 3rd century.  This Hawaii branch was established in 1906 when many immigrants from Japan came to work for Sugar plantations.  Since then it has served both local communities and people and now many tourists from Japan too visit this shrine, especially for new year blessings.  There are many kinds of Omanori (good luck charm) available here.

(Translated by Google) Great spot for taking photographs! A sightseeing spot representing the eastern part of Kauai and a wildlife sanctuary. The Hawaiian bird "Nene" and seabirds are always flying around, so it's worth watching. Also, between December and March, humpback whales come to the waters near Hawaii for childbirth and child rearing, so if you are lucky you can see a powerful bleach.

(Original)
Great spot for taking photographs! カウアイ島東部を代表する観光スポットで、野生動物の保護区になっています。ハワイ州の鳥”ネネ”や海鳥が常に飛び交っていますので見ごたえがあります。また、12月から3月の間はザトウクジラが出産と子育てにハワイ近海へきますので運が良ければ迫力あるブリーチ(鯨のジャンプ)を見ることができます。

(Translated by Google) Jodo sect temple. One of Hawaii's most famous temples, and the priest is also a celebrity. It is familiar to many people. The precincts with the main hall, the Great Buddha and the triple tower are adjacent to a beautiful and quiet beach. The scenic landscape stands out. In particular, the sunset seen on the beach in Lahaina is superb.

(Original)
浄土宗寺院。ハワイ屈指の名刹であり、住職もまた有名人。多くの人に親しまれている。本堂、大仏、三重塔を有する境内は美しく静かなビーチに隣接。風光明媚な景観が際立っている。特に、ラハイナの浜辺でみる日没は絶景。

There are two lookouts to see canyon and Niihau island.    But both views are not so impressive.  Niihau can be seen better at the lower viewpoint of the Waimea Canyon Drive.  Canyon is more spectacular at Waimea Canyon Lookout.    Waipo'o falls is actually very close but not visible from here.  You can see canyon trail and mist of the falls from the lookout.

My kids and I  liked this small but well-maintained aquarium.  As long as you don't have high expectation, I believe you will enjoy it.  Explanations about coral ecosystem were excellent.  Great place to learn and enjoy ocean's various creatures.   Parking space near the entrance is limited but there are lots of parking space by the roadside near aquarium.

(Translated by Google) One of the most beautiful cemeteries in Hawaii. There is an altar in the room behind the statue of the goddess in front, where you can dedicate prayers and books at any time. The view of Honolulu city from the observatory is superb.

(Original)
ハワイで最も美しい墓地の一つ。正面の女神銅像裏の室内には祭壇があり、いつでも祈りと記帳を捧げることができる。また、展望台からのホノルル市街の景色は絶景。

(Translated by Google) Must-see on Kauai. Rainbow could be seen at the lookout from afternoon. The rainbow time zone on the canyon side is from noon to evening.

(Original)
Must-see on Kauai.  Rainbow could be seen at the lookout from afternoon.カウアイ島で必見の場所です。渓谷側での虹の時間帯は、正午から夕方にかけてです。

(Translated by Google) Entrance to the place where the park gate was built in the movie “Jurassic Park”. You can enjoy the best forest bathing while listening to the murmur of the river.

(Original)
映画「ジュラシックパーク」で、パーク・ゲートが建っていた場所への入り口。川のせせらぎを聴きながら最高の森林浴が楽しめます。

Used to be 5 stars (★★★★★) but now 3 stars because growing bushes and trees are in the way to see great views!  Well, it's still good but as compared to 2008 picture,  much less Taro field can be seen.  So County? please trim trees well for better views.

This garden is one of the treasures of Kauai.  There are many well-explained signs about plants in the huge property.  A great place for walking, picnic, learning nature or meditation.  I call this self-guided tour as a little great adventure!

(Translated by Google) An observation deck with a breathtaking view. In principle, parking is charged ($ 3), but if you have a Hawaii driver's license, it will be free.

(Original)
息をのむ絶景の展望台。駐車場は原則有料（3ドル）だが、ハワイ州の運転免許があれば無料になる。

Easy access and good view but there are many better views on the way to Waimea Canyon.  So only if you have time, it may be nice to visit.  During rainy season, rainbow often appear in the morning between 7:30 am to 10 am.

Guided tour was very good.  Make sure to have enough time to visit Pacific Aviation Museum, too.  During winter (September to May), they close at 4:00 p.m.  Also closed on Thanksgiving, Christmas and New Year's Day.
Worth visiting this museum.  Plan to have enough time to visit Arizona Memorial, USS Missouri Memorial and this museum.  There are remains of Zero aircraft which force-landed on the island of Niihau.
The must-see view on Kauai.  Better to bring a jacket.  It becomes cold when it's cloudy or raining.  Since clouds move fast, if you can wait for a longer time, you can see this spectacular view.

(Translated by Google) A beach where you can swim, walk and rest. The sunset and night view here are also wonderful.

(Original)
泳いでよし、歩いてよし、休んでよしのビーチ。ここでのサンセットや夜景も素晴らしいものがあります。
Good place to visit during holiday season!  People of all ages could enjoy Honolulu City Lights and Honolulu City Hall.  Great decorations with colorful lights.
Educational place to learn history but not entertaining site.  Maybe just a short visitation to take photos/read explanation panels would be nice.
Great beach park which has gated ocean pools, pavilions, kids' playground and lots of shade, too.  Good for picnic, birthday party and so on.
A great place to experience Japanese Buddhist temple and garden in Hawaii.  Also a good place to photograph beauty of the temple.
The tour is a little great adventure!  Both manmade and natural gardens are excellently maintained and there are so much to see.
Good place to photograph island of Niihau and sunset.  Also good for fishing from the pier and eating at the picnic table.

This small roadside monument is the final resting place along the old road of Major Braddock who fell in 1755 while fighting the French and Indians along the wilderness road they were constructing. George Washington accompanied Braddock as an aide in the army and stayed with his from when he was shot until he died 4 days later. They buried him under the road then had the entire army walk over the grave to erase all traces of it so his body wasn't ransacked by the natives.  In the 1800's workers found the body and it was moved slightly closer to the modern highway. Amazing to visit this spot and think about how it was such a wilderness frontier not that long ago. Portions of the original road remain so you can get an idea of what the wilderness road looked like.

Small but well kept park right on the lakefront of beautiful Skaneateles Lake. This is one of the few spots to really enjoy being on the lake as most of Skaneateles is privately owned. Thayer park is nearby - take a walk through the village and you'll come to that one on the other side of the last buildings.

Clift Park has benches, a swimming area, access to the public docks and pier, and the launch of the lunch and dinner cruises. The bathrooms are located underneath the gazebo, so people often miss them.Great place for sunrise and sunset as well!

In my opinion, one of the best library and grounds of any President. The entire Hyde Park area is beautiful, and the rich and amazing history of the FDR library just tops it off. This is where he gave many of his fireside chats and his office where he helped chart the course of the world during those tumultuous times is still there and intact. Many of his hand written famous speeches are on display in the building as well. Don't miss the story of this amazing man if you're in the area.

This is an amazing experience to camp in this quiet and primitive area. There are many first-come first-serve primitive campsites with a pit toilet in this area. You travel down a dirt and gravel road and choose you campsite - no cost! The sites all have a fireplace as well and are all very secluded. Many hiking trails are around for you to explore this wilderness area. Keep a watch out for deer, bear, and moose!

Haven't been here in years - but it was well worth it to visit this place again as an adult. You pay a little under $20 and you get to explore a small museum and then watch a movie about the history of the commercial exploitation of the falls. Then you change into sandals and a poncho and proceed to get soaked and blasted by winds as you wander around the boardwalks underneath the American falls. Awesome time!

A great walk through history here to see what native Hawaiian settlements looked like and how they were setup. This was a sacred site where all Hawaiians could go to rest and recuperate during tough times. The stone walls are still intact and the original wood buildings have been reconstructed. The location itself is beautiful with great tide pools and beach areas for exploring. You can also snorkel next door.
likes: Activities: Exploring tide pools, Beach access

reviews_attraction.text: As of July 2017 half the trail is closed because of downed trees. You pay $6 to walk about 200 feet to the falls overlook with about 50 other people. While the falls are beautiful the park simply isn't big enough for the crowds it receives. That being said learning about the fish that actually climbs the waterfall is pretty cool. See it if you're in the area but don't make a special trip just for it
dislikes: Small size (not enough space for crowds)

reviews_attraction.text: This is a PRIVATE garden - you can only go here when they do certain public events such as fundraisers, community garden tours, Mother's day, etc. That being said, Karen and George have created an absolutely amazing labor of love that is an amazingly and beautiful place full of unique statues, gardens, walkways, and even an incredible maze. Be on the lookout when they are open to the public!!

It's nice that this is finally a park - as these falls are beautiful. That being said, it's very small so far, just consisting of a small trail that goes to the base of the lower falls. There is only a couple of outhouses here, the parking lot, the the home that is on the property. Once they finish the park, it should be a beautiful place to have a nice stroll to the upper falls.

This is a nice uphill hike that you can combine with the Tinker Falls trail to make a nice 2 mile loop. The trail to the hang glider launch is steepest at the bottom but non-technical. The views from the top overlooking Labrador Pond and the valley are stunning. If you're lucky you'll see the hand gliders launching on a nice day!

Really wonderful stroll through history here. The new Seneca cultural center is amazing with a wealth of artifacts from the Seneca from the 1500's right up to today. Take a stroll around the beautiful trails which are full of historical signs showing the areas where the French and Seneca fought in the 1600's.

Great hike to see some ancient native Hawaiian artwork on the volcanic rock. The whole hike and loop takes less than 30 minutes but you're best off if you arrive early since the entire hike is over black lava fields with no shelter so it gets rather hot early in the day...and usually very windy as well.

A beautiful spot for hiking with sweeping views up from the south end of Skaneateles Lake. The trails are a mixture of woodlands and open fields going through old foundations and fireplaces of homesteads long since abandoned. Be sure to check out the old 1930's Chevy truck too that sits abandoned!

A nice hike through woods and along the sandy bluffs overlooking Lake Ontario. At the end you can come back down and walk along the beach and lakeshore back to the parking lot. Beautiful place to cool off on a hot summer day. Entrance and parking is free here.

This was a blast getting to hurtle down the same track as the Olympic athletes. The price is a bit steep ($75+) for a one minute ride, but it's worth it at least once to feel what it's like to hit 40-50mph on a bobsled track...plus the great views from up top!

An amazing place to experience the history behind the Women's Suffrage movement. The original church where the first meetings were held has been rebuilt and next door there is an excellent museum with the history of the movement throughout the years.

One of the most brutal battles of the Revolutionary War was fought here. You can walk the same pathways and forests that the participants of the battle did, really making you feel like you've stepped back in time.

Great hike. First it leads you through views from on top of the crater rim then you descend through some of the only tropical rainforest in the United States to the amazing cracked lava floor of the crater.
Love this spot, one of the few places to do some actual creek walking. Try and go after a wet period as the falls will be roaring then. The walk itself isn't too long but be prepared to get wet.
A stunning wilderness area with many great lean-to's to camp in, most of which are right on the lake shore. Enjoy many hiking trails up mountains directly from your campsite as well.
Always a great spot to take the kids to look at the fish in the holding tanks. Also make sure to walk in the hatchery room to see how they hatch and raise the trout from eggs on up.
Great place. It's amazing to stand above the lake and think a huge waterfall coursed over the cliff and formed the pool below. Home to many rare plants as well!
Great spot to see artifacts and relics from the Finger Lakes areas history. Great art displays and an all around beautiful old house to walk through.
Small but beautiful beach. Can get pretty crowded later in the day. If you're lucky you can see sea turtles resting on the beach.
Great place, but  very popular and can get crowded. Hit the smaller lake for less crowds and the Frisbee golf course as well.

I have been here three times  in 2018 and loved it every time I went. They have a great dog park and nice walking trails.
There's a fenced area for big dogs, and a separate fenced area for smaller dogs. They have a bathroom in the middle for humans. There are drinking stations for the dogs which are available in the summer months. There is a station with dog poop bags and the dog owners are great about picking up their dog's poop. The ground surface is wood chips. There are a few bins that were built by Girl Scouts that hold some toys you can throw for your dog.
There's ample parking, with a rocky gravel surface.
My family also likes to come here for the walking trails. The trails are stroller friendly, and you could probably do a wheelchair as well. But there is a bridge with a long slope so you would have to be able to control it on the way down and up. Also, if bringing a wheelchair, the ground surface in the parking lot is near impossible to push one through, so the poeson would have to be able to walk a few steps on gravel, or be carried a few feet to get from the car to the sidewalk.
On the walking trails,  after you get over the bridge you can go left to walk the paved trail towards I 92. Or you can go right to walk the paved trail towards Woodstock. The trail towards 92 is pretty flat. The trail towards Woodstock has a steep incline for the last quarter mile before you get downtown. We have used this as a alternative parking option for downtown Woodstock events. We park at woofstock dog park and walk a little over a mile along the trail to get downtown. It's a pleasant walk and shaded for more than 50% of the way.
This park has multiple things to offer, and I recommend everyone come check it out.
dislikes: Rocky gravel surface in parking lot
Difficult wheelchair access from parking to sidewalk

reviews_attraction.text:
New playground good for older kids, well manintained, no shade.
I gave it 4 out of 5 stars because it's a nice playground facility, but there's no shade, not much for the little kids to play on, and a somewhat dangerous zip line.
I brought my 3 year old here and it was fine because he's a great climber, but he was too short/young to access some of the playground elements and got bored quickly. My friend had her 18 month old and it almost wasn't worth her time because he could only climb a couple of things with close supervision.
The playground surface is wood chips. There are some benches around the edges of the play area, and a picnic table. There wasn't any shade to sit in at 10am in the summer. The bathrooms were adjacent to the playground.
There's a cool swing/Zipline built into the playground. Which I'm sure is a hit with the older kids (8+?) But too fast/high for my little one. It was also a bit dangerous, as the path is not easily noticeable while walking on the playground. If you have kids who are well aware, or parents watching closely, it would be ok. But easy to hit someone/get hit. I accidentally walked into the path a couple of times while chasing after my son.
That being said, the tennis courts and baseball friends looked really nice and the roads/parking lots were well maintained and laid out. I'm happy we checked it out and maybe we'll be back in some years when my kiddo is older.
likes: Availability of benches and picnic table
Nice tennis courts and baseball fields

reviews_attraction.text:
Great family campground, easy access to Lake Superior, beautiful nature and stargazing.

This is a lovely campground. I visited with my husband and two young kids, as well as my mother-in-law and her elderly friend. We stayed in a travel trailer and a camper van. We enjoyed rock hunting along Lake Superior.

There are tons of sights and there was plenty of room on each one. The campground backs up against the lake with a small sandy beach. And it's a 10-minute walk/hike across the road and down a hill to Lake Superior.

The only issue we had, is that there were tons of bugs at night time. We had to severely limit going in and out of our camper and we still ended up bringing home five or so flies, among other bugs.

There is a playground with swings and a slide next to a field area and some picnic tables.

I was able to send text messages, but had no internet connection. However the office has Wi-Fi connection with the password is posted in the window so you can access it at any time.

The other campers were very friendly and nice. Some of them were regulars with reservations lasting a couple of weeks.

The fire pits were built up cement rings. Our site had electric hookup, but not water or sewage. I'm not sure if other sites have those amenities. But they did have apull up area for sewage and water management. It was double-sided so two vehicles could access it at one time.

Update Jan 2020: Their newly renovated playground is amazing!! AstroTurf surface, accessable for kids of all abilities, and lots of new play elements within an expanded fenced in area. Come check it out, you won't be disappointed!

Original review from 2016: This is one of my favorite parks in the area. I bring my pup here for the dog park. It's wood chips surfaced and there's a park of large and one for small dogs. It's well maintained with a water bowl in the summer (water turned off in winter).
The playgrounds are excellent. The 2-5yr old playground is fenced in and has modern, well maintained equipment. There are some picnic tables and shady areas within the fence. The 5-12yr old lot playground is unfenced but equally clean and modern.
There are a couple of bathroom houses which are clean and well maintained.
There are walking paths throughout the park which are smooth and have light hills. They are a mix of sun and shade based on time of day and season. Sometimes it can get quite hit with the sun and heat in the summer. There are drinking fountains and work out stations along the way.
It's a great park and an amazing asset to the community.  Come check it out!

Unique playground focused on climbing elements, entire park fenced, covered pavillion, clean and convenient location. Not enough parking. This is a great park to give kids unique climbing challenges, great for working on gross motor coordination and upper body strength. My two year old had a great time with the lower parts of  the playground. I bet kids up to 10/12 would love it too. The ground surface is wood chips, surrounded by grass. The parking is super close to the pavillion/playground but there aren't many spaces. Nice men's/women's bathrooms plus high/low drinking fountains. 6 metal picnic benches under a new looking pavillion with an electric fan in the ceiling and a fireplace on one side. There are some mature trees in the park, and trees along the sides for some shade at times during the day. A fence surrounds the whole park so you can let your little one run and play without worry of them going too far. It's a great little park in downtown Milton and worth coming to check out. We went after story time at the Milton Library, just around the corner.

I visited here in May of 2018. It was a clean Park, well organized, with nice trails. It cost $8 for myself and my one year old to enter. The guide gave us a five minute introduction to the history and sites of the park. Then we walked outside to check out the Mounds and fishtrap. We also took the nature trail around one side of the park. The trails were pleasant and well lit. The nature trail was shaded most of the way. My son really loved seeing Turtles laying on the logs in the water of the river. There was ample parking and plenty of spaces open at 10 a.m. on Tuesday. After our walk, we ate lunch at the picnic tables next to the parking lot. It was a large green space with plenty of trees for shade. My son loved running around and playing with sticks and leaves. It was wonderful to spend all morning out in nature. We spent 4 hours total. This is an amazing historical site, worth checking out if you are passing by or live in the area.

This is an awesome park that I've been frequenting for 4 years. First I would come with my dog. The trails are paved and go through woods and fields with a mix of shade and sun. Then I had a baby and would come for stroller rides/walks. And now that I have a toddler, we use the new playground. It opened in 2017 and has a fenced playground with one side for toddlers, the other side for school aged children. My son loves the slides and swings, and I've seen older kids (8-12) enjoy the new climbing elements of the park. I think the playground  equipment of this park encourages kids to run and play. I see more sweaty, laughing, and running kids here than I do at most parks, which is exactly what it's there for. There are bathrooms and picnic pavillions and ample parking. For anyone who likes to walk and/or has kids, I recommend they come check out this nice new park.

Beautiful state park. Hiking trails, cabling, boating. I love to hike here with friends and my family including my two year old. You are to pay $5/vehicle for parking, or $55 for a GA State parks pass. The trails are well marked and there are several options for routes. Stop by the visitors center for a map and study it to decide which route you will take. They vary from 1-5 miles and have fairly flat trails, and ones with more moderate incline. They are almost entirely shaded since they're in the woods. We like to find places to stop along the way that are on the lake so we can do a picnic lunch and/or splash in the waters edge. This could be a fun place to kayak/canoe. The trails are not stroller friendly, as they are Rocky and uneven in places. I always take my baby backpack. It's a great place to get out and enjoy nature go check it out.

Short trails, nice wilderness, beautiful stream.

This is a nice little park In historic Roswell. If you're looking for a place to go hike some trails, this park alone won't give you much. But it does connect to the larger trail system. The trails in the park are pretty short, but they run along the stream which is really nice. There's evidence of civilization with large drain pipes and cement structures along the trails. They have nice but run down stone benches along the trails, as well as some nice wooden benches built by an eagle scout project in 2020. Definitely not stroller friendly, there's a long set of stairs to bring you down to the trails, and lots of roots and rocks. It would be a lovely place to just go sit in nature, watch the stream go by, or have a picnic.

Great hiking/walking trails. This is an awesome park. It has walking trails through the woods, almost completely shaded. The trails are well marked with maps showing the way. There are a few different routes to get different distances. The main parking is limited, but there's a one lane road through some trees that leads to overflow parking. There's a wheel chair accessable outhouse at the parking. The trails are packed gravel/dirt. I've always brought my backpack carrier for my two year old. You might be able to do a jogging stroller with good wheels, but it might be uneven/slightly rocky in places. There is a nicely landscaped area between the parking lot and the road, with some benches for resting or eating lunch. Go check it out.

Great facility, nice trails. I became a member this year with my 2.5 yr old and he loves coming here. They have some animals to see downstairs:fish, turtles, a possum, and a gecko. And lots of books, plus items to look at under a microscope. They also have a few small toys littler ones can play with. And a mini museum style area to learn about water systems. They have trails, some of which are paved and stroller friendly (although some hills) that take you to about 10 aviaries with birds of prey. There are also hiking trails that are dirt surface. I believe it's $10 for an adult to come visit, so not bad if you're going to spend a few hours there. Definitely worth checking out if you're in the area.

This is a nice park tucked away where you wouldn't expect so much green space to exist. There are two playgrounds, one is where Google maps puts the balloon for Noonday Creek Park. The second is about 0.6 mile walk from the first. Both seem to be new, with wood chips ground surface and  a roll in enterance. I walked from the first to the second and back, and the walking surface varies. In some areas it's paved, others it's gravel/sand. Great for walking, not terribly stroller friendly, but we managed fine. The bathrooms were fine. Unlocked, stocked, and generally clean. The picnic pavillions were nice enough, but previous visitors left some litter. Worth checking out for the playgrounds alone.

This is a really nice park with lots to do. We went on a Sunday afternoon and there were tons of sporting events being played by kids. We went to the playground, which has one for kids up to age 5, and the other one is for kids 5 to 12. they have really unique playscapes, which my husband even commented on. He's an engineer and for an internship he worked on playscapes, he was pretty impressed. My two-and-a-half-year-old loved going back and forth between the two playgrounds. The ground surface is wood chips. There's plenty of parking really close by. And a nice clean bathroom right next to the playground. Definitely worth checking out if you're nearby.

Park along the river with a playground and picnic pavilion. We attended a library story time under the pavilion this summer. It was a nice venue for my kiddos. We played on the playground for a bit, especially enjoying the bucket swings. The playground equipment seems newer and the ground surface was wood chips. Then we walked along the riverside. There's a Little Free Library at one side of the parking lot. At the next parking lot over there was what looked like a rental place for canoes/kayaks and another pavillion. There's a paved sidewalk connecting the areas together. Beautiful area to come visit.

Edit: I added a picture of the colored trails.
Our local park! Great shaded walking trails and playground. One playground area is fenced, with a woodchip surface and child sized picnic tables. There's a work out station near one of the parking areas. And paved/packed gravel walking trails. There are some hills, so not wheel chair accessable, but ok for a stroller with decent wheels. There's also a Little Library that my son and I like to visit. And several sporting fields and courts. It always has people so you don't feel like you're alone. Come check it out, especially if you have young kids.

Amazing new park!! AstroTurf ground surface, close parking, several climbing structures. Regular swings and bucket swings as well as a smaller structure for crawlers/early walkers. Short walking trails through the woods and around a pond which are earth/gravel type surfaces - flat enough for jogging strollers. Picnic pavillions around the perimeter of the park. A small dog park off to the side. Nice bathrooms in a central location with changing tables and drinking fountains. Only complaint is that there's no shade on the playground for the hot sunny days in the summer.

This is a unique and neat place. The parking is close and convenient, and handicap/stroller accessable. The museum is interesting and well laid out. The staff is also very friendly. I spent about an hour but could have spent a bit longer to read more of the signs. I also saw a puppet show, Rainforest Adventure. My toddler and I liked it so much that we brought the whole family a few weeks later. This is a fun place to visit as a local, and also a great place to bring visitors.

I took my kids to an event held here. It was a nice visit and I hope to come back to learn about the history of this area. I gave it 4 stars because the parking was a bit far from the venue, we were in a small building set back from the street. Without wrangling little kids it would have been fine. The landscaping was nice and well groomed, and signage was well managed to get us where we were going. This would be a lovely venue for an event like a wedding.

Worth checking out if you're nearby and want a playground for young kids. This is a large park with sports fields. I only visited a small party of what this park has to offer, the playground. My 1 year old absolutely loved it. It has nice modern equipment. It is unfenced, but pretty small so not difficult to keep an eye on your kids. There is tons of parking, and it's very close and convenient to the playground. There are a couple of benches on one side.

I can't say enough good things about this place. I came as a child/teen, and just revisited with my toddler. We went on Sunday Dec 30 and it was so busy but there was enough room that the kids weren't on top of each other. My kiddo lasted three hours (a long time in a crowd!) and was sad to go. We got in for free with the ASTC program - we are members of the Tellus Science Museum in GA. Go check this museum out, you won't be disappointed!

I love this hike. The paper mill ruins are a neat place to climb around. It's close to the waters edge and my kiddo likes to splash on the river. Great place for a picnic lunch. I took off a star because the trails aren't marked very well, but if you have a phone with gps and pay attention, you'll be fine. Parking is $5, you pay in an envelope at the parking lot. I think they had a credit card machine there too. Get out and check it out!!

Sprawling park, two playgrounds, sprayground, picnic pavillions, sports fields. Neat park right next to the East Roswell Library. We played at one of the playgrounds and had a picnic lunch at the pavilion. It was a nice park and I'm sure we'll be back. Well maintained, woodchip ground surface. Kind of hilly for walking, but there were sidewalks along the road if you wanted to walk. Nice shades areas from trees.

A nice park with access to trails. I visited during lunch break on a Friday. There were a few people walking or running, it was nice to see the park being utilized. They have a little free library, a "play me" piano under the gazebo, water fountain, dog water station, and bathrooms. There are also some benches around the short paved area. This seems like a nice little park to pick up the trails.

Nice area in central Woodstock, where the city events are held. I have attended several holiday/summer events here. There are good parking options during non-events, where you can park near the gazebo and enjoy a walk or picnic lunch. My two year old likes to run around the ampitheater lawn. It's a great green space for big community events.

This is a nice green space between the Coke museum and the aquarium. At Christmas time, they decorate it with large Coke themed ornaments. In the summer it has beautiful green lawn. It is always very clean and well maintained.

Admission cost is quite high but remember that all of the funds raised help restore some of the greatest airplanes and jets from American history. The main museum takes about an hour to tour, depending on how much you wish to read. There are plenty of dioramas which our children truly enjoyed. The next building is a large hangar with holes in the walls and windows from the Pearl Harbor attack. It is filled with many artifacts from our aviation history. Expect to spend another half hour to forty-five minutes in this area where restoration work is going on regularly. We enjoyed it even with the high admission cost.

Oak Openings is one of those lesser-known gems among the many places to visit in Northwest Ohio. It is filled with miles of hiking, bicycle and horse trails, camping areas, the Wabash Cannonball rails to trail that cuts through the middle of the park, lodges and now tree houses as well. Take some time to hike the many wonders of this park. How many places can you walk through and evergreen forest and to suddenly find yourself in a birch forest before setting foot onto a sand dune? This is the place and it is amazing!
likes: Unique ecosystems (evergreen, birch forests, sand dunes)

reviews_attraction.text: Don't miss the beauty of this park! It is amazing to drive only ten minutes from what amounts to a desert climate into the lush and vibrant jungle climate of Iao Valley. Be aware that it rains a lot! Have your poncho ready and get set to enjoy one of the most beautiful places on Maui. Also be aware that it gets extremely busy at times and parking can be tough - but worth the hike if you have to park next to the road.

What an amazing and wonderful park! You have Mokoli'i (Chinaman's Hat) just offshore in front of you and the the Pali-ku of the Koʻolau Range right behind you meaning that you have views that are truly amazing! Add to that a beautiful white sand beach and plenty of picnic areas to enjoy a meal with family and friends. Some of our family kayaked out to Mokoli'i while others swam or sunbathed. We loved it.

Go a little past Hana town and you will find a beautiful little beach park. Huli Huli chicken is sold in a little tent (just get there early enough - they do run out) and there are restrooms. The beach itself is rugged and gorgeous. The colors in the sand are remarkable with blacks and reds dominating. The islands just offshore add to the beauty. You will enjoy yourself in this special little place!

This trail is both fascinating and beautiful. The colors present in the mud pots, geysers and hot springs almost look as if they are part of an abstract painting. The trail is located on a boardwalk and well-worth the stop. The parking lot fills quickly so get there early to avoid the crowds. You will be astounded by some of the views. Our children enjoyed this even more than Old Faithful.

Beautiful park whether you choose the summit, the many trails, the south side Seven Pools or just to wander in the clouds! The National Park Service Rangers are extremely helpful as well. In most areas, restrooms and fresh water are available and the visitor's centers located throughout the park are great places to get further information!

Access to the pools is limited due to both falling rocks and dangerous (waterborne) bacteria but the views are still worth the trip on the well-marked trail. The National Park Service Rangers are extremely helpful as well. Restrooms and fresh water are available and the visitor's center is a great place to get further information!

Another wonderful gem in New Orleans. We had the delight of visiting on a Congo Sunday when around thirty people were gathered playing various percussion in the park. Visitors were invited to join in the fun which included a lot of great rhythm and dancing! The park itself is large and easy to find right off the French Quarter.

Beautiful little stop in Grand Teton National Park. Restrooms are available (which aren't plentiful in other areas so it is a good place to go whether you need to or not). Big stop for for bus groups and tours so make sure to get there early. There is a large parking area and everything is kept clean and well-stocked.

We always love our visits to Maggie Daley Park! However, try to find a weekday as it is tremendously busy on the weekends. There is plenty for the kids to do - especially for children 12 and under. Lots of security was present during our visit. The playground had lots of original and fun activities for our children!

Worth every minute and the low admission price to discover the history of sugar in Hawaii. Not only are there wonderful artifacts, but you also learn the complete process of turning sugar cane into sugar (and molasses). Our children enjoyed the informative displays and the machinery on the grounds. Great place!

Sadly, the museum is closed and according to a local who met walking a dog it is always closed. The building is used for special events. Through the windows we could see dusty exhibits and an old gift shop. So sad this wasn't open for us! No times for openings were posted anywhere. Very sad.

The city of Maumee is blessed to have one of the top water parks in the area! Wow! For years I have driven past it on the turnpike assuming it was some kind of commercial venture only to find out that the city runs this amazing place. Our children enjoyed a wonderful time - we loved it!

The Toledo Zoo should be on your list as one of the top places to visit in the entire Midwest! It is one of the most customer friendly attractions you will find. The reopened tunnel is another highlight. Don't miss your chance to check out this treat and become a member!

Fantastic little FREE museum located on the University of Wyoming campus. Well worth your work to find it in the geology building. Fantastic activities for children, a wonderful black light gem room, great fossils and wonderful history of the area. Don't miss it!

The Toledo Metroparks continue to expand, grow and develop into an amazing string of parks across Northwest Ohio. The Maumee State Forest is a wonderful collection of areas to hike, ride ATV's and just enjoy nature.
Don't miss this National Park treasure! Seriously one of the most amazing National Parks! Plan well with your camera ready. Bring extra water and shoes appropriate for some light hiking. Fantastic!
What a great place to begin your visit to St Louis! Fantastic help with recommendations, tickets, information and local attractions. Lots of history and a great gift shop, too.
Great place to see the history of Deadwood, the Days of 76 annual celebration, the Lakota and a huge collection of stage coaches. We enjoyed it tremendously.
Even if you aren't riding the train, the property and museum are worth a visit. Great displays including an operating model railroad and a full caboose.
Huge museum with plenty to see! Huge model railroad, great displays, fun gift shop and the train yard right outside the windows for real train action!
Don't miss this amazing part of the country. Astounding diversity of flora, fauna and topography. Sights around every corner. Animal life abounds!
See Ulysses Grant's future wife's home. Julia Dent's family home has been restored and a wonderful museum is located in the stables.
Great place to explore and learn more about one of the lesser known "gems" of the Black Hills. Our family loved it!
