My cousins and I went here after we celebrate another cousin's birthday party. We arrived around 9:30 and we were fortunately lucky that we were the last group to ride the go-karts. The only complaints I have is to remind people not to mini-golf after sunset, since it can be difficult to see where your balls is on the green with the poor lighting. It is recommended to not buy tickets for go-karts an hour before they close, since I am not sure if they'll refund you when they close down for the night. If you like to mini-golf and it's dark outside, try doing it inside. Other than that, this place is still holding up.

I did the Pend O'Reille Train Rides twice (once inside and once outside) and my last train ride in October was special, since I got to ride on the outside. I also shot this photo of Box Canyon Dam from the railroad track. You won't be able to get this outstanding view anymore, since the train rides ended in late October. Thanks for the memories.

My mom and I made a stop here a couple of years ago and took a couple of tours there, since the first time, we didn't put enough change, so we went a second time. The capitol building is very interesting to look at and it's very educational for the students, as well as the adults. Definitely recommended to check out when you are in Olympia.

My girlfriend and I went here for luxury of relaxing after a long week. It was nice and peaceful, lifting up our spirits. Definitely recommended and also if you are a bus rider coming from downtown, it’s better to go across the bridge across the freeway on Government Way and Rosamond than climbing up Sunset Hill.

My mom and I have been to this place a few times throughout the years. It only costs $5 per car to go to an informational documentary about the Cataldo Mission and also exploring the church and the house, as well. Definitely recommended for people who wants to learn about the history in the Pacific Northwest.

My dad and I stopped by Snoqualmie Falls on our way back to Spokane from my aunt's and uncle's place outside of Redmond. It wasn't too busy and the falls was breathtaking. Sadly, I didn't get a chance to go to the bottom part of the falls, but I'll have to do it the next time I come over that way.

My girlfriend, my mom, and I made our second stop after Steptoe Butte. The views were awesome. Only downsides are it gets too hot easily in the summertime, the road to the park is bumpy and basically gravel. Overall, it's well worth the drive to see the Falls at least once in your lifetime.

I went here with the Spokane Parks & Recreation group. The tour guide guy was very informative and friendly, too. The place was run well. Only downside is that the place can become too congested, especially being located next to the railroad tracks.

I have been across the Pedestrian Bridge to see the Upper Spokane Falls numerous times and this photo was taken the day before they closed it off temporarily, due to the high water level last month. Definitely recommended to see.

One of my co-worker suggested me to go out here and check out the waterfall. The scenery is refreshing and it is located not too far from the Centennial Trail and the Spokane Transit Buses (Routes 32, 97, and 174).

My mom and I went across the bridge last summer on our way to visit with our cousins in Puyallup from Bainbridge Island. The toll was a little spendy, but not as expensive as the ferry to Seattle would've costed.

My girlfriend and I made a trip here after dinner. I have made many visits here with my late Nana Bertie when I was a kid, since she lived a couple of blocks from there. The scenery is relaxing and refreshing.

We played softball here for the past couple of weeks. The first week was fair, but this week was awesome, since we got to play under the lights. The softball field is well maintained and located near Division.
I have been to Manito Park a lot throughout the years with my late Nana and with my girlfriend the other night. The park is well taken care of and the scenery is phenomenal. Definitely recommended.

the zoo is very interesting, they have a wide selection of animals. Intersting place to visit within the city.

For this rating I'm wavering between a 3 and 4. They're doing maintenance right now so some of its covered up and you couldn't get to one area. It's interesting if you've never seen a battle ship before but if you have I'd probably skip it.

The exhibit itself is well done and would Def recommend visiting. Wear sunscreen and bring water.

Nice ski resort for all levels of skiers. The lines get pretty busy on teh weekends, the best times to go are early in the morning or for night skiing. The beginner area is a great place to learn, the runs are on the shorter side but interesting enough to spend several hours skiing.

Really enjoyed our visit. Would high recommend the daytime happy hour special for $28 (buy online) you have open bar for the 30 min trip. The bartender was great. The night happy hour is more expensive and I'm not sure it'd be worth  it. Although the views may be better at night.

Good assortment of sea creatures. The one thing I would say is they do not have descriptive info posted for every single fish. They have a touch pool and a under water tunnel to better see the sharks and fish.

Honestly, I feel like the museum is overpriced. We did the space needle and glass museum ticket and I'm glad I didn't pay full price. The pieces themselves are somewhat Interesting but the museum is small.

They had frequent dolphin shows, I would highly recommend going midday as that seems to be the most active time of day. The lions/tigers usually just lie around, but the dolphins are quite interesting.

Great place to relax, hang out right near the ocean. The park has picnic Areas, shade and great places to sit back and enjoy the area.
Legendary place, a definite must go in the city. The food and drinks are of course overpriced, but the atmosphere is unparallelled
Nice park to walk around and spend time in. Would definitely be much more interesting in the summer and the warmer weather.

It may seem like a museum of taxidermied animals is just a holdover from an older era, but there are many things I learned here specifically because none of the animals are alive. For example, there are quite a few extinct species on display beside the existing species; I had heard the stories of passengers pigeons but had obviously never seen one. Well now I have, and I understand better how sad extinction really is.
For kids there is the chance to get much closer to the animals than they ever would in a zoo, and of course the distance between exhibits is much smaller so you can see more animals in a shorter amount of time. There is also a play area with a slide and interactive displays, and if you show up at the right time there is a live animal presentation in the basement.

A very well designed and maintained park. A little Creek (fully fenced-off) separates the playgrounds from the sports fields, and provides a lot of tall shade trees. There is a junior playground, which is set down in a shallow pit so that the little kids can't escape by mistake. Lots of slides and swings, as well as an electronic dance-off style activity I'd never seen before. Restrooms and water are nearby, as well as a large pavilion with picnic tables. And best of all, it is right across the street from the Draper TRAX station. Well done Draper, we will be back.
likes: Safety features (fenced-off creek, shallow pit playground)

reviews_attraction.text: Perhaps the best park for letting the kids run free. There are two awesome playgrounds for big and little kids, enormous grassy areas for games and sports, pavilions and large trees for shade, and water and restrooms, which are nice for picnics. I-15 is very close and causes some noise, but there are also railroad tracks, and my son always gets excited for trains.

This park has a lot of potential. Playground, walking track, tennis and volleyball courts, nice big trees and open space, and great views of downtown. However, it isn't in the best neighborhood... for example, we couldn't use the whole playground because there was a homeless man sleeping on it and wouldn't move.

Beautiful historic old building full of paintings, sculptures, monuments, and historical exhibits about the history and people of Utah. I could have spent the whole day there and still not have seen it all; my small kids with smaller attention spans were happy for a few hours, which is above average for them.

An impressively large natural cave with cool formations and interesting geology. Tours last about 90 minutes depending on how fast your group can climb the hundreds of stairs. Reservations are needed for larger groups to avoid long waits at the mouth of the cave.

Expansive public park, built in the same movement as central park in New York City. It includes playgrounds, sports fields, a fish pond, a lake for boating, an aviary, and a 1.5 mile track for biking/ jogging. Great for families, groups, or individuals.

Residents of Morgen ought to be really proud of their park. There are separate playgrounds for big and little kids, lots of grass and shade trees, pavilions, sport fields and courts, and a walking path beside the Weber River. Well worth the visit.

We loved the covered playgrounds. Other playgrounds get too hot in the summer - not this one. Big shady trees, two creeks with walking paths and bridges, and lots of seating areas make this an awesome place for kids to run loose and explore.

Historic ranch land ranging from hilly forests to sagebrush fields to grassy meadows, all laced with trails for hiking biking and horseback rides. Some of the old ranch cabins are for rent for overnight stays, and are very comfortable.

A beautiful old-fashioned amusement park for teens and families. A mix of old and new rides. Also the history collection at Pioneer Village is severely underrated. This place takes way longer than a day to fully explore.

Greenspace with a playground, tennis courts, a baseball diamond, and amazing views of the city and Ensign Peak, but not so much shade, no restrooms, and of course everything is on the slope of the hill.
This park checks all the boxes. Playground, restrooms, picnic tables, shade trees, lots of grass to run around on, and paths for kids to explore. It would be nice to have access to the Creek nearby.
This place is practically a theme park-except instead of rides and expensive tickets they have awesome playground equipment and it's free (besides the train). Must be seen to be believed.
One of the most massive playgrounds I have visited. Lots of unique play elements. Almost all of it is geared towards older kids, younger ones will not be able to play on most of it.
Expansive playground with everything you could want: climbing areas, slides, swings, playhouse, splash pad, sand box, xylophones, and picnic area - and all of it is ADA accessible.
A very scenic little lake to hike around. Close enough for small kids to walk to, with great views of the mountains and the valley (from the Boulder trail head, anyway).
Worth the price. There's interesting stuff for all ages. Most of it is interactive. We spent a good three or four hours there and still didn't get to see everything.
The trailhead is just street parking, and the trail itself is very steep and narrow for the amount of use it gets. But the views of the valley are totally worth it.
It's remarkable how close you can be to downtown SLC and still feel like you're in the middle of nowhere. Highly recommend exploring this place.
Well preserved pioneer house of Brigham Young. The tour takes you through every room. Very cool history but not so long that kids get bored.
Awesome playgrounds fit into the hilly landscape. The wading area down at the bottom of the canyon is especially nice on hot days.
They are always adding new things. We go about once a year and each time I am impressed by the new creatures and displays.
Paths and monuments in a natural hollow. It's amazing that such a secluded little forest can exist so close to downtown.
There is far too much stuff to see here than can be seen in one day. It boggles my mind.

Get there early. Don't leave any valuables in your car or let anyone see you putting them in your car trunk. With those two bits of advice, this is a must see when visiting Oahu. There is a lot of security so don't even try to bring bags in. There is a unique feeling here. Workers seem pretty happy to be there. They will answer your questions much to the displeasure of people behind you. You will want to get your tickets for the boat ride out to the Arizona ASAP. The movie is informative. The boat ride brings the history home. The actual memorial was closed due to structural failure when we visited. Lots of parking, but again there are predators lurking to score your valuables. Egress is not straightforward, but you can get out if you pay attention.

Stunning light display set to music in a garden environment. I knew the lights would be good, maybe even great, but after my first visit, I would label them exceptional.  There is a long field of LED Lights inside translucent "bowls" that are choreographed to music. Similar, in a way, to the display on Fremont Street in Las Vegas. There are many other themed light displays throughout the tour. There is even a religious area apart from the main path that is inspiring in it's own way. Members of the Church of Jesus Christ of latter Day Saints will get the most out of it, but the Biblical theme is most prominent. Price is steep, but there are ways to save money. Parking appears to well coordinated. Egress wasn't much of an issue.

I rounded up on this rating which I would probably give 3.5 stars were that an option. I did enjoy my experience here. Prices for 2 out of the 3 activities were not altogether outrageous. The maze and the gardens were very enjoyable. I now have more info about the growth cycle of a pineapple then I believed I ever needed. The dole whip was reasonably priced and delicious. There is an extreme amount of Dole branded merchandise in the gift shop. Probably more here than exists in the rest of the world combined. I recommend get here early for parking and crowds. There is a fair amount of parking, but as we left there were some people stalking us for our spot. Egress is typical for two lane highways on Oahu.

Scenic trail at the top of the road in Mill Creek Canyon. This is a trail with a significant amount of branch-offs and cross paths. I usually end up here for the Dog Lake path. You can even access the Great Western Trail if you so desire. There are streams and creeks running together for most of the trail. Dogs are allowed and have opportunities to go off leash. Remember to pack out everything your dog leaves along the way. There are parts of the trail that can only be described as lush, not what you can normally expect in Utah. Some parts of trail are steep, but overall not a challenging trail. Parking can get overcrowded in evenings. Egress is also dependent on the time of day.

A lot of WWII history here. If you are willing to spend the money, and have the time, then I recommend this place highly. Your tour guide will probably be a volunteer dedicated to preservation of the memorial. Ours had a lot of insight and little known facts. There are plenty of photo ops. It takes a while to walk the whole ship. You are allowed to go off on your own below deck. Bring your own water if able. The price is considerable vs. Pearl Harbor. You have to take a shuttle from the Pearl Harbor memorial. There is parking at PH, but be aware of thieves and other scum that are looking for an easy score. Egress is a bit confusing so use a GPS to get out OK.

Fun hike up the mountain side near Sunset Beach. This is a trail you probably won't find unless someone tells you about it. You park by the elementary school and the do a bit of scouting for the trail head. The hike itself is not overly strenuous, but there are some steep parts. The Pillbox is a WWII bunker. There are several signs warning you about private property. I observed varying levels of compliance when I was hiking here. Beautiful views of the ocean at several points. Parking is limited, but not inadequate. Egress onto the main road is dependent on peoples willingness to let you turn left.

I am always thankful that this place remains an underappreciated destination. Granted, it doesn't make a dramatic first impression like other NPs in Utah, but this place has a charm all it's own. Thankfully, you can get away from crowds here almost any day of the year. There are arches, bridges, box canyons, and slot canyons here. Plenty of top notch hiking. There are some hidden gems too. My one disappointment was the trail down to waterfall on the Fremont River was closed. Please get this fixed ASAP please! Plenty of room at all attractions with ample parking  and a leisurely feel everywhere.

Pleasant surprise in downtown SLC. I was only aware that this place existed due to a minor infamous theft  that took place here last year. It is a nice refuge for those looking for a break from the hustle downtown. there is a significant amount of shade too. There is no parking lot, but I assume if you are downtown you have that issue covered. I doubt I'd go out of my way to visit, but when in the area I would check in. There is no playground here. In fact, not really a traditional recreational park at all. But I really did enjoy my time here.

Beautiful religious building dedicated to the Lord's work in an exceptional location. I have wanted to see this building for myself since I was young. I was not disappointed. The volunteers were wonderful from start to finish. There was a calm and assuring atmosphere.  I wanted to stay longer, but the vacation schedule was in conflict with the re-opening. The grounds are immaculate. There was plenty of parking. Egress was simple and uncomplicated.

Very scenic beach that never seemed to be too crowded. This beach is located near some high traffic areas, but the people don't seem to want to overcrowd this one beach. Parking is a bit further away than most other beaches, so that may be a possible reason. Sand is nice, water is just as warm as other places. There are a lot of rocks so that also may be another disincentive. Parking is limited. Egress can be frustrating.

Another LDS owned attraction in downtown SLC. Very well done and informative, assuming you have interest in LDS Church History. The missionaries here are very helpful and knowledgeable. You can let them guide you around or wander around on your own. There are some authentic artifacts here. I have not seen it get too crowded, but keep in mid it is free. Parking is limited and egress can be an issue during rush hours.

This is an incredible feet of engineering. Form and function were considered in the design here. A beautiful building that was built with the neighbors in mind. The events held here are community strengthening. Tour guides are friendly and give you a lot of inside details. A really great place to find out about the LDS faith and see a world-class building. Parking is available underneath. Egress is not a problem.

Classic religious building in the heart of SLC. The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter Day Saints has built many temples, but this is the classic one. A lot of history, a lot of great work, and a lot of peace. The grounds are first rate and a huge attraction. The patrons and workers are kind and friendly. There is plenty of parking under the Conference Center if you are a patron. Egress is relatively simple.

Excellent city park in a great location. This is an exceptionally spacious park. Plenty of room and areas to find something to do. There is a lot of parking as well. Access is limited, which can be frustrating on a busy Saturday or holiday. People seem to be happy to be there and tend to not be intrusive into "your space". Close restaurants can be a relief if you get hungry. Egress can be frustrating too.

Beautiful forested spot along the northern coast of Oahu. Interesting to see the different plant growth as elevation changes. Some parts of the forest canopy are pretty thick. Beautiful views of Sunset Beach are found here. We hiked around here in the evening and were pleasantly surprised at the cool temperature. You kind of have to know where to park. Be wary of any private property in the area.

Terrific public park with a large pond and other amenities. You almost feel as if you are in the wilds while here. The park is well kept and maintained. There are some short walking trail and access to the Murdock Trail. People attempted to fish, by I didn't observe anybody landing a single catch. This place can get crowded and parking does get tight. Egress is usually not much of an issue.

This ice rink is fine as far as skating venues go. It gets used for a lot of different ice activities. Public skating is usually pretty crowded. Employees are friendly enough and they try. The price is just about right for rental and skating. They just seemed to overwhelmed by the ever present youth groups. They need to consider their parking capacity and expand it. Egress is usually fine.

We decided to have a picnic at this beach. There were some picnic tables right near the ocean and it just seemed like a good opportunity. Couldn't beat the view or atmosphere. Most people seemed to be enjoying themselves. There was a limited amount of parking and sometimes you had to make up your own. Egress is limited by how busy the highway is.

Nice regional park that is becoming overrun with the homeless of SL Valley. This is a large park with a lot of shade trees. We observed families, dog owners, LARPERs,  loitering teens, and ubiquitous homeless people here on our visit. We decided to head to another park after eating lunch. There is plenty to do. Plenty of parking. Limited egress.

Nice surprise on a road trip through southern Utah. Impressive size. Can be a bit overrun. Be wary of vendors. Some can't take no for an answer. This is not a point of interest to plan a trip or even day around. It really isn't even far enough away from Moab to justify a pit stop, but I still recommend taking a 1/2 hour or so to look around.

This place is a bit of a hidden gem. I was interested in playing some disc golf and was unaware this place was so close. It is a nice park that a lot of people seem to enjoy. There are some trails and a creek as you'd expect. Playground seems fun for the kids. Plenty of shade. Parking doesn't appear to be an issue and neither does egress.

This is a nice , medium sized neighborhood park. Dog owners seem to love this place. There is a large , open field, some shade trees, a pavilion, restrooms, and a playground. Parking is adequate, but may be too limited for extremely busy days. Location is great, right off of a main thoroughfare.

Overpriced.  Less access every year. No reason to go there unless you want to see a movie or there is some sort of festival. Yet, people continue to utilize this place and invite me to go there for any number of celebrations. All in the middle of Lehi's worst traffic.

This us one of those classic city center parks that every town in Utah has. The old trees are starting to decline, but the shade is plentiful.  One little kid play ground and an older kid playground is nice.  Aside from city events, never too crowded.
Drove through here on our way to Glacier NP. Stunning. Trees as far as the eye could see. A lot of lakes. Next time we go to Glacier, I plan to spend some time in Flathead.

I was not able to fit into the nooks and crannys and climbing spaces, but I think I enjoyed it as much as the kids did! I was so enthralled with the artistic element employed in the construction. It truly is fantastic! It was much enjoyed by all who went. Shoes are a must. There are plenty of bathrooms, and even a spot that we brought a picnic lunch in and ate there. Not the best of places for a wheelchair, but there are places they could go as there is an elevator, and the 4th floor is an art show of types.

The museum is only open Friday, Saturday, and Sunday, so we missed seeing inside. However, there is a nice walking tour that you can bring up on your smart phone, outside, along with the memorial stones and plaques. It was interesting to hear about the war, though, I felt sorry for those who lost their homes and we're driven out. A sad day for America. There is also a little collection of local stuffed and preserved animals with a nice volunteer who explained answers to our questions.

I love walking the nice trails of IN. Nicely made bridges and stone or wood stairs. I gave this less a star as I thought that their Botanical gardens really lacked. It is September so most plants are dying off, however there wasn't a thing to see there. They were in the process of making a nature totem pole in front of their Nature center. It was man made mainly with a chain saw and then defined with other tools. It was impressive work!

The Amana colonies are a great place to visit. There are restaurants, a woolen mill, wooden furniture shop, quilting stores, lace store, chocolate shop, gem stone shop, a book store,  children's toys store, and general store which has a Christmas shop within and more. It is a fun place to walk around. They have festivals at Christmas, May day, and Octoberfest. There are 5 different colonies and well worth the drive out to visit!

I don't even like racing for all the noise, but seeing the museum and hearing more about the history was really quite interesting. I would recommend it! They have a lot of trophy's, cars, and memorabilia to see. I enjoyed the wall of winners and their times with all the changes through the years. It closes at 4 so plan accordingly. To view the museum and have a bus tour took several hours and we missed the last movie even.
likes: On-site Activities: Bus tour, Wall of winners

reviews_attraction.text: What a nice place! The playground was recently upgraded and is very kid friendly. The restrooms are clean and nice with a light, running water, and paper towels. This place would be gorgeous with fall color in the coming month! There are benches to watch the children from. Nice parking places and trails to hike on. A top notch stop to stretch your legs!

Beautiful slot canyon that seems like a green paradise. It's a pleasant place to hike and have outdoor time. They have an Inn that includes a small restaurant and public restrooms. There are several nice hikes. It's a great place to take company when they're in town. I love to visit there. It so cool in the trees and such a beautiful area.

A nice park for kids to play. Their is a softball field,  basketball hoop, jungle gym play area and picnic tables. The restrooms are available only in the warmer months. There is parking available. A nice place to walk as well. There is a trail that connects this park to Thomas park and then on. They keep the grass lovely and inviting.

It was a fun place to walk around on a nice day. Lots of plaques to read and little instructional things to see. I suspect that it's more during the normal times. They were having a concert on the lawn which sounded lovely. A nice park, though for picnics and concerts not a playground. They also have a dock ramp for entering the river

Well cared for park with a welcome center, which includes restrooms. There are a lot of hiking trails around. A memorial to the Indians who were unjustly ran off the land and their Confederacy broken. A sad remembrance of our history. The place of the battle called Tippecanoe.  Worth the stop. There is a waterpark close as well.

They have playground equipment for both younger and older children.  I appreciate the swinging chairs that surround the playground to give the parents a place. I would have liked to have a restroom facility, but they do have a water fountain. They could also use some garbage cans. It seems to be well maintained.

What a great little walk for a nice day. The paths are pea gravel, so they're not muddy. A lot of teaching opportunities for the kids. Nicely built and well maintained. Restrooms, water fountains, and tables. I'm not sure if I would take a wheelchair on the trail, but in the center would be fine.

There are some great hiking trails around the park which twist around the bluff over the river. They are used for trail biking as well. There are soccer fields above and an amphetheater. There are outhouses near by the soccer fields. It is a nice place to go for a walk.

Slides aren't slippery, you get hung up on them. The place is brightly painted with fans to keep you cool. Not a bad place. I liked that I saw them cleaning inside the climbing gym. The kids had fun. The arcade isn't worth buying tokens for though!

Such a relaxing and enjoyable park. I love the nature and wide expanse. There are nice pavilions with barbeques and picnic tables, to have picnics under, close by are playgrounds and restrooms. Handicap accessible. Lovely flowers on the summer.

The tunnel under the dolphins was just amazing! We went to see the light show and really enjoyed it. Even with the chill in the air, there were many others out enjoying it as well. I will enjoy going again, perhaps when it's warmer!
There is a collection of local animals preserved on display as well as information about the for.ation of the area and the park. They do have restrooms available and a small gift store.
I enjoyed the walks and fresh air with the grandkids.  They have a nice play ground for them and good outdoor sites. A good place to let the kids get outdoors and have some exercise.
Nice bathroom available, as well as a working water fountain. The playground looked quite big and could handle a lot of children. Beautiful green lawns and shade trees. A nice park.
There us a pavilion and tables within. There are out houses to the side and a spigot for water. There is a big grassy field to play sports in as well.
Great fun with the kids! The goats we're the most we've seen so far. They are trying to be safe with distancing. A new penguin exhibit will open soon
Their food was down home comfort food and the best I have had in a restaurant! It was delicious! The waitress was one of the best!
A nice selection of displays both hands on and not. We had a great time there with a 3 yr old. A lot to learn from and enjoy.
I appreciated them letting me warm up a cold 2 it old in the lobby. I don't think they usually do, but thank you!
I think that the Ellis park area is cleaner than it used to be. It is a nice place to canoe and go fishing.

We started out early driving from Makena, all day adventure. 6 miles in and 6 miles out with a 2000’ elevation gain.

The trail is extremely varied from hard dirt to quite muddy, all different zones of plants and trees and quite windy, very nice temperature but be cautious due to falling trees and branches. Also, if it rains or mists even lightly, the trail becomes extremely slick. TAKE A WALKING STICK.

Once at the ‘top’ (overlook) there are several options to continue on other trails, which were clearly marked along the way but lacking mile indicators.

We parked at the DT Fleming beach parking lot and thoroughly enjoyed using the restroom and shower to wash our feet and legs at the end of our hike.

Enjoy a forest of all different groves of beautiful cactus, pine trees and all sorts of fauna, including Guava trees and Lilikoi vines.
Take plenty of water and snacks, good shoes or sandals, bandaids for blisters and TP or wipes. I enjoyed phone service the entire hike, just in case.

We took our Daughter and 2 grandsons visiting from Ohio, they go to Hogle Zoo every year and the Zoo is much improved over the last few years. They fed the giraffes, enjoyed the snakes and big cats and ate ice cream cones.
I think admission is overpriced as are the concessions, train ride and carousel.
Don't go if you don't like being around lots of children and some annoying parents. Go early especially if the temperature is upper 80's or above, animal activity is slowed down and if it's crowded the heat makes it miserable.
The employees are very knowledgeable and pleasant, the park is clean and easy to navigate, with plenty of restrooms and drinking fountains! Very limited in expensive food options, so be prepared to spend your budget!
We stayed for 4 hours and that was plenty of time to get around and see everything including the 2 minute train ride.

Beautiful place to watch birds, spend time on the beach and observe the ever changing scenery!
I go to the beach behind the boardwalk fairly often to take photos and walk, every time I go there is something new to see and photograph. There is a bridge as part of the boardwalk which crosses over an outlet where the pond sometimes bursts through the natural sand plug. What a sight to see when that happens!
The parking lot is small so it’s best to go early in the day. It can get extremely hot so take plenty of water. There are no restrooms.
This stretch of beach is one of the very few that you can walk for several miles!

Another great trail! There's street parking at the trailhead, there are no visible signs giving trail directions, which can be off-putting. As you go up the well traveled, moderately strenuous path, there are NO signs and many more narrow trails taking off from the main path, confusing, but we don't care! We just want to hike, it's all beautiful!
We never did get to the 'Living Room', but we definitely found the Kitchen and a few Bedrooms!!
Go early, watch for snakes, take water and poles are a great addition. Going early keeps you in shade for quite awhile if hiking during hot summer months.

Best Farmers' Market in the U.S. in my opinion! Goes from June until October 8am told 2pm and if you plan to attend, go early in the morning because it gets very crowded and it's difficult to get up to the vendors tables.
There are always plenty of dogs and strollers and when it's crowded it becomes difficult to navigate. Plan to walk, there is free parking to be found, but there's also plenty of paid parking.
Veggies, breads, Cheeses, salsas, many ethnic food trucks. Also, artisans, performers, musicians, it's a great time! So much more, no admission fee! A must see and do!

I’ve hiked this 4 mile up and back trail many times, in extreme mud, rain, chilly, hot and very sunny conditions. Always be prepared with a hiking stick, lots of water, garbage bag for muddy shoes, snacks, rain jacket and maybe even a change of clothes.

Arrive early as the trail can get quite crowded and parking spots at a minimum.

You’ll know when you’ve reached the top because of a fence and picnic table.

The hike is strenuous in spots but well worth any effort, incredible views and lots of changing flora, especially the Anemone Stinkhorn!

There's more than Big Beach, Little Beach, porta-potties and Food trucks. Incredible views if you choose to hike the Puu Olai Mountains!! There are unofficial trails, just head into to bush and hike! I would recommend a hiking stick, lots of water and sturdy shoes. I took a swimsuit and towel in case I ended up on a beach, which I did. Without knowing exactly where I was headed, I ended up smack dab in the middle of Little Beach where the water and waves are always perfect! Challenging and wonderful hike!

How could you go wrong at any park on the ocean on Maui?! Kalama Park offers many amenities including skating, restrooms, generous parking, large trees and grass with several picnic pavilions and so much more. While I was there this morning just walking on some of the sidewalks I was able to watch three turtles eating off the rocks!
There does tend to be a few homeless people hanging around and there’s a sense that some upkeep and cleanliness would be helpful, hence the 4 star rating.

Not a five star beach due to the dirty feel of the park, limited parking and a disgusting porta potty.
BUT.....4 star because you can walk for miles on the beach, see turtles in the wave, find sea glass and small shells and observe the Kealia Pond from the ocean side. Great photo opportunities and diverse sand. Take plenty of water or go early in the morning to walk as it can get very hot.
Other than the porta potty at the park, there are no bathrooms for miles.

CoVid19 has sure changed the look and feel of everything. The beaches are empty, the chairs are stacked, no one is here.
Beautiful even still, the walking path that goes for a couple miles is quiet, but the solitude is very nice in a way. Photo ops are abundant and the breezes are even nicer.
I hope things return to the old normal soon, but finding peace and joy in the quiet solitude causes a much greater appreciation for almost everything.

Nice spot to park and enjoy watching big waves, surfers: board, kite and wind! Today, no surfers due to a large swell and the churning waves even though the tide was 35-40’.
This is a point overlooking a lower beach where many turtles come to rest and get away from predators.
There is limited parking, bathrooms and showers near the beach.
Be cautious since there are dangerous cliffs and slick rocks.

Such a beautiful canyon with many hiking trails, picnic sites, beautiful creek, ample parking and pit toilets. Go early during summer because it gets very hot as the day gets long. Take plenty of drinking water and hiking poles are quite helpful.
Hiking is easy to strenuous depending on the trail, dogs are allowed on leash on odd days, cyclists on even days.
There is a fee or an annual pass.

Not a hike if you have a fear of heights! Beautiful none the less, the views are incredible and the cave tour is fantastic, especially with Ranger Katherine as the guide! She has great humor and also very knowledgeable!
Be sure to make reservations as the tours are limited in number of bodies, go early in the morning because of the heat and BE SURE TO TAKE A JACKET!
#rangerkatherine

Beautiful Park with gorgeous ocean views, lots of parking, picnic tables, bathrooms, large trees and very serene!
Easy to find but very out of the way and off the beaten path.... local folks more than tourists and there are some permanent car campers on the road to the park.
The are several unconnected parks, 2 of which are The Kahana Beach Parks with paved road and parking.

If you’re only going to the cove just beyond the parking lot, be careful while snorkeling and hiking over the lava rocks, lots of sharp rocks/coral. There is no beach to speak of but ample parking and porta potties.
You can park here and walk back up the main road going north and enjoy some amazing snorkeling. It’s a little over a quarter mile walk!

Whether rollerblading, jogging, picnicking, playing tennis or relaxing and people watching, Liberty Park has it all!

Beautiful large trees, pond with ducks and picnic tables, even an Aviary. It would be easy to spend the entire day.

Go early on a weekend or you won’t find a place to park. There are also many restrooms and a nice swimming pool.

Definitely not a place for hiking but a beautiful wetland and boardwalk with many signs to read about the birds and wildlife and several areas to sit and enjoy the peacefulness.
The parking lot at the trailhead is very small but well maintained. You can park along the busy highway and take time to stroll along the immense expanse of beach.

Nice hiking trails, not strenuous except keeping balance on some of the lava rock. Go slow driving to and from the trailhead, lots of blind spots, narrow and bumpy, potholes in the road, at least the last leg. Go early and take water, it gets very hot. There are 2 parking lots and portable toilets. Watch for the wild black goats!

Short initial trail but you can go from there to the Bonneville Shoreline Trail or the Hells Canyon Trail.
Ensign Peak Trail is somewhat strenuous but short and the view of the Salt Lake Valley is great.
Do go early and take water. There are no bathrooms. Parking on the neighborhood street.

What an excellent day, visit to the cemetery to remember loved ones then on to Brownville, NE, many years ago vying to be the 1st Capital of Nebraska, this weekend was the 60th annual Spring Flea Market with down home finds, food and entertainment! Good time! Over 300 vendors!

Excellent combination of meadows and woods with several options for length of walk/hike. There's plenty of parking and a very nice building available to reserve for gatherings, as well as 2 pit toilets, no water though.
Watch for bird houses and frogs! Great photo opportunity.

Strenuous hike and lots of rock climbing options. Nice creek along trail, large trees for shade, a few places necessary to cross creek.
Definitely NOT the place to be in Springtime or during heavy rain or runoff.
Parking is limited, no bathrooms.

A must do while on Lanai, very informative pictures and artifacts along with some beautiful art and a quilt that is all hand sewn.
Some very interesting history and knowledgeable staff.
Pay heed to the hours of operation.
One of the more beautiful beaches on Maui! Never very busy, great snorkeling, always turtles to be seen! It's also a great beach for boogie boarding, stand up paddle boarding, kayaking and weddings!
Conner Theater and Foster Theater are a must see while here! We were here 5 hours and didn't see all there was to see. Be sure to pay for enough parking or you'll have a $15 fine!

Hiking is my passion and this is one of the best hikes in King County. It's a bit of a steep unrelenting climb,  but the payoff views at the top make it all worth it.   No ripoff fee for parking or the trail. Not a big fan of hiking on rocks,  but the flat stones are necessary, and they are more like steps. This trail can be crowded, most people stepped aside as I was ascending.  People must love this trail,  it's well maintained and mostly clean.   The killer view at the top is not to be missed.   If you are tired or out of shape,  you can stop at the first viewpoint of Mt. Rainier.  There is a bench to sit on and eat a snack.  Bring a real camera, you can thank me later.   To get to the point (top)  head East  past the last square of AstroTurf.  You are now about 13 min from the top.   Oh my what an incredible view,  and on a clear day you can see forever.   Impress your friends by naming all the features you can make out. To the North you can even see Mt. Baker.   This was fun and so worth the effort.

This is hands down the best get ready hike in the Gorge.  So much to see and do.  Native American history abounds.  To add to your adventure near the top on the West side is the best natural bench (tree limb) in the whole gorge.  The view is astounding.  Pro tip:  there is a side faint trail about 1/4 mile into the hike, to your left.  It's hella steep, only attempt with proper footwear.  As you pop out the view will leave you gobsmacked.  Be careful as a miss-step will certainly lead to your demise.  Bring a real camera, your phone can't do this place justice.  The trail up is just that up and up.  This trail is in okay shape. Way easier than the suffering on nearby Dog Mountain.

The Rock has it all,  a good hike, incredible views, history,  science, campgrounds, superclean restrooms, and a boatramp nearby. The only drawback is the rip off $10 fee.  However WA in their Infinite Wisdom will let you use the restroom for 15 minutes for free without a pass.  If you have the time go a mile West and turn left to the boat ramp and Park for spectacular views of Beacon Rock.

Relaxing huge riverfront park, great place for a stroll. Large playground for the kids, lots of room to run around. A ramp leads to a cool public dock.  Don't forget to head SW to cross a fantastic pedestrian bridge with sweet views of a natural area. They also have a indoor Carousel.  Take a spot on a bench and take in the sun setting across the water.

You can't tell from the highway, but this is one cool park.  Walk a little or a lot on the extensive trails.  So many things to do and see.  They have the best picnic areas along hwy26.  Super clean bathrooms.  The five buck entry fee is cheap. Washington charges a rip off $10. for a lot less.  Wheel chair?  No problem you can still watch the fish.

This is the best Lighthouse tour on the coast.  The fact that it is free increases the enjoyment.   Our guide was patient and knowledgeable.  You learn so much that adds to the fun of climbing the stairs.  Don't forget to put something in the donation box.  As always bring a real camera.  Enjoy the quick view from the top.

Super spot to take incredible view pictures.  Bring a real camera, you want to remember this view.  You can see the dam and all the way past Beacon Rock.  Best time is Sunrise as the viewpoint faces East.  If you have limited time you can drive to the top and take a short walk just follow the signs.

This place is a dream, and worth the price of admission.  So much to see and do.  The granite stones set as the stairs and pathway are the best I have ever hiked.  Just when you think that was all you could see you come upon a granite picnic tables and benches.  Bring your real camera.

This is a must visit stop on the coast.  So much to see and do.  Cool black pebbles on the beach.  Fantastic tide pools to explore at low tide.  Check out the visitor center for the history of the area.  The Lighthouse tour is free, and it's the best on the coast.

This park has it all, cool fenced play area for the kids, and nature trails below. Bathrooms and several large sports fields. Tennis courts, + a swimming pool in the summer. Shade trees, picnic tables. Great place for a kids B-Day party.

Wow what a cool state park so close to a huge suburban area. You can even get here by bus. Miles of good hiking trails , camping , and a beach. Good place to take Photos. The only downside is the year round ten dollar ripoff fee.

Great park,  large play area for the kids.   Cool small lake with lots of critters, including  bald eagles.  Look in the top of the trees. A nice waterfall is just South of the trellis.  Fun place to walk,  jog or work out.

This place has something for everybody.  Kids can play in the water or toss rocks.  The more adventurous can hike up to Rattlesnake ledge.  Parking us free, no WA ripp off fee.  Several porta potties, no water on the hike.

A one time visit is all you will ever need.  A huge part was closed off to us. Okay if you can get someone else to pay for your ticket. This is a one and done place.  Where is HEART?   They should  have a whole room.
Great park to wander and decompress. Watch out for rude people who don't have their dog leashed. When you don't have the time to travel to the Gorge this place could have your bailout hike.
High falls low in volume cool hike.  It's unavailable a few months of the year from the top.  No rip off fee for the parking area.  Please keep this relaxing natural place free of litter.
An uphill short hike leads you to a cool falls.  Several view points and a cool bridge.  Restrooms at the trail head and a playground make the ten dollars RIP off fee easier to take.
Cool falls you can also go for a hike if you want. So worth the drive. Bring a real camera your phone won't do the view justice.  Bring a picnic they have tables, and restrooms.
Incredible views, play area for the kids,  workout equipment, nice wide open area. Good sunset shots. Great place to relax and watch boats in the bay. Free parking.
Easy place to stop. Watch out for the rip-off ten dollar fee.   Not much here five bucks would be just about right. Stroll to the beach from the small parking area.
Cool easy to get to small falls.  You may be able to park in the tiny lot just before the RV park.  The main trail head parking lot makes for a better hike.
Short hike from the top past a tunnel to a fantastic Lookout Tower. The trees block most of the view,  but it's still cool. Kids will love this place.
Quiet neighborhood park.  Great place for the wee ones to run and play.  The grounds are well maintained with tons of room.
Great wide open park.  Lots of things to do year round. Go for a half hour nature walk or spend all day on the water.
Cool bridge,cheep to cross, go slow enjoy the view. You can buy local fish and other seasonal food at either end

Boise has a numerous beautiful park and Ann Morrison Park is one of them which is situated just by the the Boise River and behind the Boise State University Campus. It is a 153 acre urban park.

It is of free admission and has parking lot of its own in various places of the park. It's a spacious place with facilities for picnic, cycling, outdoor gym, tennis court and fields for soccer or cricket. In the golf disk course of the park, you can spend a day of playing golf disk or Frisbee. The water fountain here is another attraction. The park is full of ducks and goose.

The 4th of July Celebration and the Balloon festival are arranged big in this park. During these festivals, it is hard to find parking spots, so it is better to park elsewhere than inside the park. Since it is next to the Boise river, you can take the $3 shuttle from Ann Morrison Park to Barber Park where you can rent the tubes, rafts or kayaks and the tubing finishes at Ann Morrison Park where you can return your tubes, rafts or kayaks.

When I was in Boise, it was my favorite place as it was near my apartment. An evening walk, Cycling with friends, having picnic during weekends were my favorite memories in the park.
likes: Variety of facilities (picnic, cycling, gym, tennis, soccer, cricket)

reviews_attraction.text:
Julia Davis Park is an 89.4 acre park which was created in 1907 and located along the Boise River. The park contains a Rose Garden, the Boise Zoo, Boise Paddle Boat Rental, a Tennis court, a toddler playground, picnic pavilions and several museums. The friendship bridge connects the park with Boise State University.

This park provides access to the Boise River Greenbelt. The scenic view that the park provides is the main attraction. The rose garden has a pavilion where anyone can arrange an event only by reservation. There is a larger than life size bronze statue of a seated Abraham Lincoln adjacent to Rose garden.

You can enjoy different activities here like paddle boating, fishing, playing tennis, cycling etc. You can have picnic or get together event under the pavilions.

The park has its own parking lot. The restrooms are clean. The park is nicely organized and you can observe different seasonal view in this one park. Many events are arranged throughout the year in the park, i.e. art, music and music festival etc.

If you are in Boise,  you must check out this place.

The Basque Block is one of Idaho’s unique cultural blocks of a living ethnic neighborhood- Basque. It is comprised of two boarding houses -­ the Cyrus Jacobs-Uberruaga house, and the Anduiza.

The block has its unique indoor frontón court, the Basque Center, the Basque Museum and Cultural Center, Bar Gernika, Leku Ona restaurant, and the Basque Market. The cultural food is one of the main attractions here.

There is Basque History Mural completed by Noel Weber and The Letterheads in 2000, located on the Basque Block off of Capitol Blvd. One of the original Letterhead Members, Bill Hueg, hand painted a reproduction of the work which was translated into this new digital version displayed on the west-facing wall of the 104-year-old Anduiza Fronton building.

The Museum Hours are Tuesday – Friday: 10am to 5pm and Saturday: 11am to 4pm. It is closed on Sunday, Monday, and Holidays.

If you are in Boise or visiting Boise and you are a history geek, I would say definitely check out this place and also try the food here to taste a different ethnic food.

If you are in Boise or visiting Boise and you are a history geek, I would say definitely check out this place and also try the food here to taste a different ethnic food.

Boise Depot (8.7 acres) is the former train station in the western United States, opened in 1925, at an elevation of 2,757 feet above sea level.

You can see the stunning city skyline and foothills from the Depot patio. The bell tower is 96 feet tall and can be seen throughout the city at night.

The great hall of the Boise Depot is a 3,542 square foot multi-story atrium. It has six arched entrances. Big Mike (Engine No. 2295), a Mikado-type steam locomotive, built-in 1920, is placed on the east side of the Boise Depot which is one of the main attractions here.

The Boise Depot has a garden with a winding walkway, benches, a pond, a monument of volcanic rock, and planter beds with seasonal flowers that were designed by Spanish landscape architect Ricardo Espino. The pond has different types of large fishes swimming in the pond.

It is the best place for picnic and taking photos. I used to go there during my evening walk and I always felt refreshed visiting there. I love this place. I definitely recommend it if you are visiting Boise.

C. W. Moore Park is a 0.28-acre urban park which includes architectural historic artifacts from some of Boise's demolished buildings, i.e.

1. W.E. Pierce Building Turret (1903),
2. Bush Building Entrance Arch (1904),
3. Cast-iron Columns & Streetlights (1880s),
4. Dr. Springer’s Carriage Stone (1890s),
5. A.T. Ellis Building Date Stone (1902-03),
6. Pioneer Building Name Stone (1894),
7. Central School Name Stone (1905),
8. Morris Hill Cemetery Waterwheel.

The waterwheel raised water from the ditches and provides the water to a small rivulet which is symbolic of Boise’s early canal system. The park is available for reservation for formal ceremonies. There is on street parking available. It also has bike racks and drinking water facilities.

It is a very small park. One day I saw the turret while walking back home. After that I used to go there, listen to the waterwheel and have my lunch. I was very surprised to learn about the artifacts included in the park.

Deer Flat National Wildlife Refuge is surrounding Lake Lowell which serves as resting, breeding and wintering area for the migratory birds. The refuge has two units - Lake Lowell (10,588 acres) and the Snake River Islands (800 acres).

There are over 250 bird species and over 100 nest observed around the refuge. Ducks, Canada geese, bald eagles and other raptors are the main migratory bird here. There is a visitor's center where the staffs discuss about the wildlife conservation projects.

The Upper Embankment adjacent to the refuge is a 74 feet high and 4165 feet long dam  impounding the water of the Boise River in off-stream storage.

The refuge has diverse recreational activities like bird watching, fishing, boating, hunting etc. Since it is only 40 minutes away from Boise, we used to go there for weekend picnic or just to enjoy the serene beauty of the refuge.

This place is a must visit if you are in Boise.

There are over 250 bird species and over 100 nest observed around the refuge. Ducks, Canada geese, bald eagles and other raptors are the main migratory bird here. There is a visitor's center where the staffs discuss about the wildlife conservation projects.

This place is a must visit if you are in Boise.

Hyde park is the famous historic place at the north of downtown Boise and popular for eateries and locally owned specialty shops; including the Hyde Park Pub & Grill, Goody's, G. Wilikers, Java and Hyde House. The buidings, architecture of the area, the retail area and restaurants are the main attractions here. It is just a walking distance to Camel's back park.

Throughout the year, diverse events and activities are arranged nu local merchants. Hyde Park Street Fair is the biggest one which includes  vendors, food, live music, demonstrations, a children's area, and a parade.

Last time when I went there, I visited an antique shop and discovered my liking towards unique antiques. I used to go there to have ice cream and candies from Goody's. They have various kinds of flavors.
I highly recommend it if you want to discover Boise's history.

The Rose Garden is located inside Julia Davis park. It's the second oldest rose garden in the Northwest and the largest rose garden in the Inter mountain region. It has over over 2000 rose bushes in every type and color. It was established in 1939.

The garden has a pavilion, a fountain and a larger-than-life size bronze statue of seated Abraham Lincoln statue. The statue was created by Gutzon Borglum and established in 2010. The Garden pavilion is used for wedding ceremonies which you have to gate by reservation. You can have a great photo shoot here. The fountain spray blue streams of water. The parking lot is just beside it.

If you are in Boise,  you must check out this place.

Jack's Urban Meeting Place (JUMP) is a 7.5 acres creative activity center in Boise for arranging various kinds of meetings, festivals, workshops and exhibition etc. There is a collection of 52 tractors on display at various locations in the facility.

Jump has a beautiful park and playground, a natural grass amphitheater, sweeping terraces, rooftop parks, a spiral slide, celebration circle, a green lawn, a climber, colored light fountain. There is a colorful pinwheel on the premises of the lawn which rotates if air blows.

The Spiral slide is a tubular five-story chute in which you can slip and slide. If you are in boise, you should keep this place in your visit list.

Ponderosa State Park is a 1515 acres peninsula of Payette Lake. Its elevation is 5050 ft from the sea level. The park's namesake, the 150-foot-tall ponderosa pine, is the most noticeable species of tree at the park area.

The park offers hiking and biking trails, guided walks, beaches, picnic areas, clean restrooms, showers and opportunities for boating, skiing, snowshoeing, and wildlife watching. There is a visitor center which has a fire place to make you warm. Also the visiting center has wifi.

I went there during summer. Had a barbecue picnic on the beach picnic are. Walked around the beaches with my friends and enjoyed the natural beauty of the lake.

Freak Alley Gallery is the northwest's largest open-air, multi-artist mural gallery, located in a service alley between 8th and 9th street in downtown Boise. It started in 2002 when local artist Colby Akers painted the back alley doorway of Moon’s Cafe in downtown Boise, Idaho. Now every summer the murals are painted over and also new paintings are added by more than 200 artists.

I went there last when I was in Boise. I used to go there and enjoy the murals and try to understand the hidden meaning of the murals. If you are visiting, I would highly recommend this place to visit.

Celilo Park is is a small, well established park on the banks of the Lake Celilo. Lake Celilo is a 24 mi (39 km) long reservoir behind the The Dalles Dam on the Columbia River, between Washington and Oregon. The lake was created in 1957.

Celilo Park offers free camping with a 14 day stay limit. The Park offers  a paved public boat ramp, restrooms but no showers. You can go for fishing, boating, camping or have a picnic down by the lake

Open year round. If you are visting to Oregon through Vietnam Veterans Memorial Hwy, you can see the lake. at the Celilo Park.

It’s one Boise’s historic landmark. It was built in 1870 and was a functional prison from 1872 to 1973 in the western United States, east of Boise, Idaho. It is surrounded by a 17-foot-high (5.2 m) sandstone wall.

The elevation of the site is approximately 2,770 feet (845 m) above sea level. It is open only in Friday and Saturday from 10.00 am - 4:15 pm. You can join a tour or explore the place by yourself. You will not be disappointed.

The Idaho botanical garden is just beside it. You can also see the site if you go on a hike to table rock.

Julius M. Kleiner Memorial Park is a 58 acre park adjacent to the Village at Meridian Mall and Meridian Community Garden.

The park has an amphitheater, picnic shelters, picnic tables, clean restrooms, a playground, 2 ponds and a tree arboretum. There is a 1.25 times life size bronze statue of Julius M. Kleiner made by Thomas Jay Warren in the center of the Grand Promenade on the Grand Plaza.

You can enjoy fishing, picnicking, playing basketball and bocce ball here. If you are in Meridian, you can visit the park and have picnic in weekends.

Boise Paddle Boat Rentals rents out paddle boat to boat around the lake in the middle of the Julia Davis park. I went there twice. I loved paddle boating. The scenery was beautiful. The geese swimming around the lake was very cute and funny to watch.

Ticket price is $10.00 for a half hour, after taxes, per boat and $15.00 for a full hour, after taxes, per boat. They only accept cash. They supply life jackets. The staffs are very friendly and let you know all the precautions before starting to paddle boat.

Legacy Park is located near the McCall downtown area and the central location for enjoying the view of Payette Lake. The park offers volleyball court, picnic tables, an enclosed swimming area, clean public restrooms, a public boat ramp for watercraft and a parking lot.

I went there during winter, so the whole lake was frozen. The natural serenity of the frozen lake was mesmerizing. If you are visiting McCall, it is a must place to visit.

It’s a great park to have a picnic or walk/run. It’s also great for photography and enjoying the nice skyline view. It has many trails. You can see the skate park from there.

The love lock fence is just beside this park on a pedestrian bridge which resembles the famed Pont des Arts bridge in Paris. The chain link live lock fence holds dozens of love locks placed by H-town lovers.

No entry fee. Huge parking lot. It’s open 24 hours.

Idaho Black History Museum is just beside the Rose Garden and located in Julia Davis Park. It was built in 1995. This is the oldest black history museum in the Pacific Northwest. The museum is very educational and you will surely enjoy it.

In front of the museum there is a larger-than-life size bronze statue of seated Abraham Lincoln statue. It was created by Gutzon Borglum and established in 2010.

The waterwall is a 64 feet high fountain in 3 acre setting spilling 11,000 gllons of water per minute! It is adjacent to Williams tower.

It is a tourist attraction in Houston. A song called "Dilbar dilbar" from a Bollywood movie "Sirf Tum" was shot here. It’s a must visit place. Great for wedding or graduation photos!!! It’s free for everyone. Parking is available nearby and it is paid parking.

Eagle Island State Park is a 545 acres public state park which was established in 1983. Its elevation is 2524 ft. The park offers swimming, boating, playing volleyball and disk golf, beach and picnic area, equestrian trails, a water slide and a zip line.

Went there with my friends. Enjoyed spending the day in the park a lot. If you want a day out, you can keep the park on your list.

Caribou–Targhee National Forest is located in the states of Idaho and Wyoming, with a small section in Utah. The forest is extends over 2.63 million acres (10,600 km2). It is surrounded by Yellowstone National Park, Grand Teton National Park and Bridger–Teton National Forest.

Saw the beauty of the forest while driving towards Yellowstone from Boise.

Quite a large park with numerous trail. A lot of parking spots. But on weekends, hard to get a parking spot. The natural view, a smooth walking and biking trail, the uprising skyscraper view and many artistic sculptures are the main attractions of this place.

Fresh air and nice picnic spot!!! Houston zoo and Houston museum of Natural Science is just beside it. Parking available. Also the park has Monument of Sam Houston, Pioneer Memorial Obelisk, and Mary Gibbs and Jesse H Jones Reflection pool!!!

Very nice state park. A state pass is required. There are multiple camping areas with various levels of utilities. It is highly recommended that you make online reservations months in advance.Many types of trails for hiking, biking, and horse riding. There are a couple of easy to access lakes which are stocked with trout and have boats, kayaks, paddle boards, etc available for rental. Anyone can drive, bike, or hike to the view point at he top of Mt. Constitution.
The camp sites can be quite noisy, especially the tenting sites. People are often up late, deer wander into tent site throughout the night and get into things (just like raccoons would). Late nights and early mornings sound like an old fashioned military encampment with snoring arising from every direction. Tenting sites have shared water about every 100 yards and latrines with showers ($1.00 / bring quarters) for about every 20 campsites.
If you found this review to be helpful please consider giving a thumbs-up.

BIG park on the Mt. side of the lake. The access road is one vehicle wide, but has many turn outs for passing; it's about 2.5-3 miles off the road. Parking for about 10 vehicles. NO facilities! Trail up is about 2 miles & will take 45 mins - 1.5 hours to hike up to top. 6.5-7 difficulty for person in average condition. Conditioned hiker or runner 5 out of 10. Walking sticks & H2O are strongly encouraged. Plan a minimum 3 hour round trip hike; 4 is better.
Lake side park is wonderful. We'll maintained, easy access for RVs and boats. Campers give very favorable reviews. Family friendly beach area with large lawn and good changing, restroom facilities

Very enjoyable trail hikes in spring, summer, and fall. I believe the Eastern loop is easier and it is definitely shorter. The longer Western trail many people would consider challenging on its inner (eastern) side. Parking usually is not a problem, especially for early birds. I believe the two best times to go are at high tide or when the inbound/outbound tides are at their highest volume (1st half). Low tide is great for exploring around the bridge and tidal flats. There are no facilities out here so plan ahead. Be sure to take bug repellent during peak season. Many benches and places to sit. Well behaved dogs are welcome.

Over 1000 acres and miles of trails. The trails are well marked but some, such as the orange trail is often narrow with lots of obstacles, are not for everyone. It's a very peaceful place to get in touch with nature and probably as wild as many want to endure without really getting into the Maine woods or wilderness. There are no vistas or view spots, it's intended to be a bird sanctuary.  There is plenty of parking with information signs and a pavillion. Note to whoever...the restrooms should not be locked during open hours.

This is a big park for s small town. Most of it is well maintained, but the restrooms need upgrading and can barely handle s large event. It is a great place to park for the rail trail. There's a nice water feature was highlights the area's quarrying history. Ball fields are in good shape and available for use. Most of the park is handicapped accessable, however I did not notice handicapped restrooms (as s public facility I'm sure they're there).
If you found this review to be helpful please consider adding a thumbs-up.

This is a very big area that is state owned and fully public accessible. There are many trails to hike and some logging roads to drive. There is usually active logging occurring somewhere so heed the signs / notices and watch for trucks. The popular established trailheads have designated parking and some have facilities. You will often encounter mountain bikes and horses. Be properly prepared for your hike by always packing essentials such as water, first aid, etc.

This is one of the Longmire camp buildings. It displays the history of the camp with photos and antiques. Beside it is the snack bar / restaurant,  outside is the tree ring historical display,  and across the road is the old park headquarters. This is very accessible to all. There is easy parking for cars and RV's on the backside parking loop. Restrooms and litter disposal with recycling is also located here. Please provide a thumbs-up if you found this helpful.

This is a well maintained historic arboretum (1890s) used as a city park. It has good facilities to include a children's playground. It has very good gravel trails throughout which are popular with walkers and joggers.There is an increasing number of tent residents near the pond area. Some of the residents can be loud and aggressive, but most are not bothersome. Finding parking can be a challenge,  but not if you're willing to walk a bock or two.

Nice biking / walking trail with plenty of parking. This is handicapped accessible although the parking lot and access path are not paved. There is a handicapped accessible porta potty at the lot.
The trail has numerous turns and a few minor incline / decline averaging 2-3%. Most of the trail is shaded and abuts private residential properties.
If you found this review to be helpful please consider adding a thumbs up. 👍
dislikes: Unpaved parking lot and access path

reviews_attraction.text: This island is a real treasure. A few distinct trails that are easy to walk, hike, or bike ride (horses are allowed). The island is full of wildfire. The single road from the causeway to the beach and back is about four miles. The same distance to and from the tower at the south end of the island. Rarely will there be more than 30-40 people on the entire island at the same time.

Excellent place to walk, run, bike ride, etc. A good place to start is the city hall building where there is also free parking and porta potties. From this location it goes North a short distance, but south all the way through Rainier and on into Tenino or Olympia and Lacey. A good place to take kids and pets. It is also fully handicapped accessible.

Beautiful park with something for almost everyone. Easy parking, access, and exit.
Great views in a fairly quiet place located in a residential neighborhood about five blocks from downtown. Adequate restroom facilties. Areas for grilling / BBQ and playgrounds for children. Would be better if plants had name signs on them.

Easy to access with well marked parking lot. Restrooms are at the parking area. Another half mile walk down to the trail start at the barn. There's a bald eagle pair that nests every year on the right / north trail river bend You can go left or right about one mile each way. This is a slow pedestrian traffic area.

Community park located in a busy administrative business park. A nice park in an unexpected place. There is a stage that is used for regularly scheduled lunchtime and evening events which are published and online. There's plenty of lawn for seating on bring your own blankets or chairs.

Easy to find from downtown Freeport with clear road signage. Fee access, like most state parks, with ample parking. Full facilities including handicapped facilities and trails.Miles of trails with good signage and maps. Easy water view access, some handicapped accessible and some not.

This is a nice, clean, green community park. It's a treasure in an environment that is generally dry, brown, and dusty. It has restrooms and an paved walking trail around it. Plenty of parking nearby. It's easy to find, access, and exit. Co-located with the Visitors Center.

Stunning 300 degree views of the Camden hills and Rockport-Rockland coastline from a beautiful turn-of-century timber & stone structure. Easy hike or bike in from the east side. The Southside mountain trail is rough and undeveloped. There is a port-a-potty at the top.

The park on the former Army coastal artillery base of Fort Williams is a true treasure. Within is the famous national landmark of Portland Headlight. It has changed a lot since my first visits in the 70s - for the better.  The pictures for this site say it all.

Good park on the edge of downtown. It is used by hundreds of walkers and joggers every day. There are public restrooms and parking on both sides of the lake. Street side parking is also regularly available. Virtually all of the trail is handicapped accessable.

Always a great place for a walk and views of the sound. Great place to view the Olympic mountain range, watch the ferries, etc. It is a one-way road South to North. Some exceptional homes to see also. Parking spaces are available on a first-time basis.

Easy access for WA state Dept of Natural Resources permit holders. Walking / Hiking only with the primary trail being paved its I'll length. Nearly flat, easy sloping trail at 8 tenths of a mile from parking lot to pier / cove view point.

A favorite spot of locals, plenty of parking spaceswith easy access to trails or the beach. There's a boat launch here used primarily by local working boats. Located right between Two Lights State Park and Crescent Beach State Park.

Small, but nice facility. Ample parking with easy access & exit. Nice display gardens with ample lawn / mowed areas. Trails need lots of maintenance and barely have signage. Overall worth the visit; it's an easy to track oasis.
Great views and easy access / exit. It's right on the water at the boat launch and parking lot for cars and trucks with boat trailers.
Easy access public use park. It's popular for walking, jogging, yoga, & kite flying; there's also a boat launch with trailer parking.

This is a great spot to start the hike up to the beautiful Mt Townsend or Silver Lakes. There are some nice campsites along the way, a few with some amazing views. Pretty easy to get to the trailhead and good parking, but can probably get full quick on the weekends because the parking lot is a bit small.

You start near a river in some very nice forest, it was a little buggy in the lower areas while I was there even at 3 in the morning. You start off with switchbacks, really they are there almost all of the way to the top, with a decent grade up hill. After a bit of hiking you get into some of the quietest and most peaceful forest I have ever been in.

Pretty soon and after a couple of steeper parts of the hill you start to get some really incredible views of the valley down below that really only hint at what is to come. And one of the nice rest spots comes at a curve in the trail keeps taking you upward, it looks like the trail has a fork here but a sign marks where the trail is and a cairn had been placed here. There is a nice little pond here that acts as a reflecting pool for some great pictures. There are also a couple of spots here that you can camp that wouldn't be too bad.

After that you definitely start to get into more and more picturesque views as well as the climbing starts to get a bit more difficult and you get to see more of everybody's favorite thing, switchbacks. Shortly before the fork to Silver Lake, which strangely enough had a fork on the sign,  is Camp Windy, there are a couple of good spots and at least one great spot with an incredible view. After the fork is when the climbing feels good, but is still steep, because you can start to see some really good views of your destination ahead.

After what seems like an endless amount of switchbacks you get near the top of the hill and the hill gets to its steepest point. Multiple paths start to appear, just follow the one to the top of the hill. You soon get out onto smoother ground that allows you to start to see panoramic views all around you.

Once you reach the top, you have one of the most amazing views in the area. You have a 360 degree view all around you. Looking out into the Strait of Juan de Fuca and on to the Cascade Range and Mt Rainier as well as into the Olympics with a great view of Mt Olympus.

I made the hike up for sunrise and I had the peak all to myself for over an hour. It was in incredible time worth every step of the hike. It looked like the peak might be a little busy if you go during the day though, I passed quite a few people on my way back down and I left the top at 7:30 A.M. on a Thursday.

This is a great trial and the WTA does a great job with upkeep, but there can still be a bit of blowdown along the way due to a burn that happened here. So depending on when you go and how conditions have been it can be a lot harder hike than other times. Other than that there are quite a few beautiful spots that are easily reachable on a day hike.

I went in early April and was there before the WTA had been able to get some of the trees out and it was a bit tougher hike than I had planned for on my way out to Five Mile Camp, that is as you guessed it about 5 miles in.

You start near the river meandering through dense mossy forest and going over rocky creek beds. There are a few amazing spots hiking right along side of the river that rolls by you with its beautiful blue water. After a while you start to make your way uphill to Lunch Rock, an amazing spot to rest, take some pictures, and have a snack. After this you get to keep make your way up to to the next viewpoint. After this point you start to level out a bit and come along the beginning of the burn and the possibility of a lot more trees.

The trail here has a peaceful serene feeling to it where you are surrounded by trees and rock and you cant hear the river anymore. It is a great hike. Soon you start to head downhill again, where I believe you would come across 5 mile camp, but I ran into a lot of fallen trees that became to hard to climb over and under where I had to turn around and call it quits for the day.

This is definitely a hike I want to try again, maybe later in the season. But really was worth every step of my day.

This is one of the most incredible National Parks in the country in my opinion. There are so many things to see with such different environments. You can see an amazing rain forest. You could hike for miles, on or off trail. You can see magnificent beaches. Experience mountaintop vistas. Relax in river valleys. Enjoy incredible lakes. Fish, camp, swim, photograph... The possibilities are endless. If you ever wanted to check out an incredible National Park, this is the one to go to.

I love this bridge. There is a good view driving either direction, you are nice and close to the water which can be good for people afraid of heights, and you sometimes get cool views of things like submarines going through the bridge(even though that does mean you are stuck waiting for the bridge to close back up). That is the only thing that can suck about this bridge, the super long wait to get across it sometimes. I have waited over 2 hours to get over the bridge before, lame.

Nice trail here that brings you right down to Third Beach and the rest of the hike down the beach. The trailhead has bathrooms which is nice and it is easy to find.
And Third Beach itself is beautiful. I think its great to get over the overland trail(complete with ropes, ladders, and stairs to help you climb up and down) because things get a bit quieter and the beach and seastacks are just as nice, if not even a little better.

This is a great place full of all sorts of options for recreation and relaxation. It is great for kids or adults. You can go as a group or even solo trips are amazing. There are caves, climbs, hikes, river rafting, kayaking, snow sports.. and than more. I would definitely recommend this place to friends and I will absolutely be making many trips back.

This place is incredible and I would definitely recommend coming here to check this out. The beaches here are incredible. Please be kind to them and pack it in, pack it out. Plus it is always good to make an effort to take out any trash you might find when you are out there. Be a good steward to our land and keep it incredible for future generations.

Nice little park in the middle of portland. Not much wildlife, but a nice fountain and good places to sit. It has been relatively quiet every time I have been here and has never seemed like a dirty place to me. If you need a spot to rest or eat your food I would recommend this spot.
