It is worth at least checking out if you are nearby.

This was a very nice little park. I stopped in on a road trip hoping to fly a kite but the wind wasnt cooperative so instead I just enjoyed the park. It was quite nice to see and be at. Very relaxing environment with a lot of options for how to keep yourself entertained. And the bathrooms were nice.

This place is great, with excellent staff. They are there to make sure you have a good time and make sure you are safe doing it. They also have awesome fields to play one, including woods. And they do a great job of keeping everything fresh so that you experience something different all of the time.

This is a great spot but it is always a bit crowded it seems. Very popular. But there are some beautiful views to see. Lots of good hill like the rest of this side of the Olympics. Definitely worth going up at least once. I will likely go back even though it is crowded. Still more to see.

This was definitely a great place to check out. I loved seeing the incredible powers of the ocean and the amazing way it presents itself to us sometimes. I would really recommend this for anyone travelling along 101 looking for a spot to stretch the legs and see some incredible views.

What a great place for so many different people. There is definitely a lot of history to learn about here when it comes to Mount St. Helens. There are also a lot of great sites to go see such. If you are looking for something cool in Washington state, this is definitely worth a stop.

This is a great place with a lot of different opportunities. The first part of the trail leading up the Sol Duc Falls can be very busy, but the falls are beautiful. After that there are so many places you could go to see the incredible Olympic National Park.

These Tent Rocks are incredible as well as the slot canyon they have there. There are incredible views, a moderate hike, and a lot of fun places to be. There is even a cool little cave that was made many years ago by some human that used it as a home.

This is a great little park, maybe a little crowded, but otherwise a beautiful place to be. There are lots of benches all around and even a playground if you want to bring your kids. Worth checking out especially if you just need some time to relax.

Definitely a great hike, a little strenuous with a full pack on since there is quite a bit of elevation gain. But every step was worth it and the veiws were amazing. And from Marmot Pass it is just a short hike up to the top of Buckhorn Mountain.

Nice little park to stop by and catch a view or lay in the sunshine. This would also be a good park to take the family or ride a bike I suppose, I prefer a unicycle myself though. Definitely worth checking out at least one time in my opinion.

Pretty decent state park, when I went they were running the sprinkler system for over 12 hours, maybe a little overkill. But the upshot is that you do get some nice trees and there are some large patches of good green grass around the park.

This is a great little park with a good view of the water and the Olympic mountains. The camp area is pretty nice and quite private but in my opinion it is a little expensive, but which park campgrounds aren't getting pricey these days.
It is a nice hike out to these falls, the trail can be very busy. But the falls are great and the air is nice and cool on a hot day. There is also a nice shelter nearby that is great to check out.
What a great spot in the middle of the forest. Cool, easily accessible bridge with an incredible veiw from the middle of the span. Fun stop if you are out this way, or just enjoy bridges.
This is a great hike up to the peak. Some beautiful views on the way to the top as well as amazing views at the top. Worth every step. The trailhead looked in condition as well.
Nice little park with a great pavilion and some nice benches. The benches are extremely close to the ground, good for kids, not adults. The playground also looked nice.
The campground is quite busy and a bit expensive for what they offer. The sites were decent but not enough privacy.

This museum is downright amazing.  To be anywhere near Dayton and to miss it would be a sin. Dayton is very fortunate to have this national historic treasure.  I am fortunate that I grew up in Kettering with a Father who appreciated this museum and would regularly take me on visits.  It started in 1971 as a young boy when we went to the Museum's dedication and got to hear President Nixon speak.  I even remember shaking the President's hand after the dedication.

I no longer live in Ohio but when we visit, I make sure to take my family.  I recently visited the WWII Museum in New Orleans and found it disappointing, overpriced and overrated.  The Smithsonian Air & Space Museum is good, but this one ranks number one in comparison with the quantity of national treasures.

As you wind past the aircraft, you're met with some national treasures.  One of the main ones that you see (and arguably the most famous plane in the main hangar) is Bosckscar--the aircraft that ended world war II by dropping the second nuclear weapon ever used in combat.  You'll also see the Dolittle Raider's exhibit, complete with their goblets; and the stories of the raiders that commemorate the raid.

The museum takes you through aviation history from the perspective of the Air Force so there is a lot of war history.  The World War II section has always been my favorite.

Another favorite is the Presidentail area in the last building with all of the Air Force One's.  You can walk through JFK's Air Force One - the very one that Lyndon Johnson was sworn in as President.

What is most impressive is the insane number of planes on display in each of the four huge hangars. Including a B2 Stealth bomber. If this is your first visit to the museum, you need to plan an entire day or days to see it all.
One piece of advice, get there early if you want to take pictures of the aircraft, before the crowds arrive!

This has to be the best museum in the USA and its in Dayton, Ohio - the birthplace of aviation.

Anyone thinking about a zoo membership.  Think twice before you do so, or just make plans for the Como Zoo.

We were zoo members for two different years.  We had a good experience the first time and therefore, joined again in 2020.  January 2020 was a good visit for our entire family seeing most of the animals close up and some even active outdoors in the cold.

Then we visited in September 2020 and what a terrible visit.  We understand the zoo like every business is working hard to keep operating during the pandemic. We did not like how we were herded into a line with so many other people (no social distancing hapening here) and then we were kept inside while we wanted to be outside.  Once we finally got outside into the zoo grounds there were signs and barriers to keep you away from seeing the animals.  Our favorite exhibit- the farm animals were very disappointing since the zoo keeps you away from the buildings and the animals.

We could not visit the zoo for many months when you were closed because of the pandemic and then it's disappointing when you finally open up.  Memberships should be extended because we were unable to use them for many months but you decided not to do this.  Why would we renew our membership when we could not use our current one.  Many other businesses have extended their membership programs because they have been closed but not the zoo.

Fort Sill has two museums, the Artillery museum and the old fort museum. Both are good but the Artillery Museum is very fascinating and full of history. We came to attend our son's BCT graduation and this was one of the first places we visited and we are so glad that we did - our son's AIT will be Artillery and this museum has a wealth of artillery history from pre-revolutionary times to modern. I especially enjoyed the video showing us what our son will be doing in the Army Artillery.

The old post museum requires some imagination because it’s still fully integrated into the base and officers still live in the old houses surrounding the parade field . Be sure to start in the main building and look at the diorama to get your bearings before you walk around. The best display is the old cavalry barracks which is set up exactly as it would have been around 1890-1900.

Ft. Sill played an amazing part in our frontier history and this post does a good job of explaining it.

Fort Sill has two museums, the Artillery museum and the old fort museum. Both are good but the Artillery Museum is very fascinating and full of history.  We came to attend our son's BCT graduation and this was one of the first places we visited and we are so glad that we did - our son's AIT will be Artillery and this museum has a wealth of artillery history from pre-revolutionary times to modern.  I especially enjoyed the video showing us what our son will be doing in the Army Artillery.

They have an excellent collection of artillery pieces in simple but well done historically correct displays. Outdoors you will dozens of larger artillery and rocket systems from the more modern area. Younger kids can run outside and not be bored.  We especially were fascinated by "Atomic Annie".  This museum alone is well worth a trip to Fort Sill.  It was our favorite attraction in Lawton that helped make our visit so memorable.

This review is just based on the casino and not the hotel or the concerts.  I am not a regular casino player at all but felt inclined to rate this place based on our observations as we passed through the casino to attend a concert.  It is basically a senor center for smokers.  Sick and sad is what I would call this casino.  The decor is so outdated, unfriendly and dirty.  We were shocked but not surprised with the lack of security to observe teenagers playing the slots.  My son who is 16 years old found a group of teenagers playing the slots most of the evening with no security to be seen anywhere.  Easy to observe since the place is full of smoking seniors.
The place was busy probably because it was a Saturday night.  I can't think of anything positive to list about this Casino.

Just about six miles from the Canadian border and Grand Portage State Park is Grand Portage National Monument.  No fees are required.  Highly recommend that you start your experience with the 15-minute movie in the Visitors Center that is very good at explaining the history of the area and the fur trade run by the Northwest Company.  We also visited the Fort William Historical Park in Thunder Bay, Canada.  We found the movie and interpreters in Grand Portage more informative.  We got more of the history in Grand Portage than we did in Fort William (a fee is charged).  The fur trade by the Northwest Company started in Grand Portage and later moved to Thunder Bay when the international border lines came into existence.
likes: Facilities & Services: Free admission, Educational movie

reviews_attraction.text:
Since we now feel like Minnesotans, we often ask of all the historic and scenic sites in Minnesota what is the most familiar and best loved.  Opinions vary from the headwaters of the Mississippi River to Minnehaha Falls but the Split Rock Lighthouse stands at the top of the list for many. Its our personal favorite and our #1 site to visit on Lake Superior.

Built in 1910, well before the road was completed along the North Shore of Lake Superior, Split House Lighthouse has been a signature Minnesota icon that many feel a deep personal connection to.  Its well worth the admission price.  The trails are easy to access and be sure to take the steps to the Lake for awesome views of the lighthouse.

I visited this historic treasure with a great friend and my mentor.  My friend had visited Baltimore many times and I have visited at least five times.  Neither one of us had been to Fort McHenry.  I am glad that I finally visited this wonderful place.  This is a DO NOT MISS attraction if you visit Baltimore.

This historical site will help anyone appreciate this country all the more! It is well worth the $15 adult admission.  Be sure to start at the visitors center where you will pay the admission and see the movie.  The  movie should not be missed, especially the unveiling of the flag at the end of the movie.  The movie is well done.  The staff and volunteers make history come alive.

This was our first visit to Whitewater State Park and we enjoyed the hiking to Inspiration Point on a warm Saturday afternoon.  Not too crowded and the swimming hole was pleasant to cool down. Be sure to take water bottles with you and the maps provided were easy to get acquainted with the trails.

Because of COVID the public restrooms are closed. The outhouses are gross. We asked about restrooms and they don’t tell you about the nice ones at the campground. The park has new clean restrooms at the campground easily accessible right across from the park office (see picture).

This state park is easy to access less than six miles from Interstate 35 on your way to/from Duluth. We missed it numerous times on our trips up north to Duluth or the North Shore.  We finally included this state park experience as part of our North Shore trek.  You don't want miss it.  The beautiful banks and ravines of the Saint Louis River are the main attractions of this state park and easy to access from the park's parking lot.  You can choose to spend an hour walking on the park's signature bridge and then through the park or several hours hiking its beautiful trails.

This is a must stop on the North Shore tour.  We moved to Minnesota seven years ago and I am surprised how many people have not been to Grand Portage State Park.  Many have come up the North Shore, but they still don't make it all the way to Grand Portage and the Canadian border.  This was our second visit and it has become one of our favorite state parks.  The main boardwalk trail to the High Falls is fun and easy to follow.  It is only a 1/2 mile to the falls.  The Visitor Center and Gift Shop are a plus.

The renovated capitol is so worth the time to visit. Our family of five took the free 45-minute tour and it was enjoyed by all of us - adults and teenagers. The history and artwork depicted throughout the capitol building is very impressive. We really loved the Civil War paintings in the Governor's reception room and the paintings in the Supreme Court chambers. Recommend to start with a tour and then take a self-guided tour to enjoy the paintings, history and sculptures on all floors at your own pace.

We came to visit Ely during the last weekend that the Bear Center was open October 20. We appreciate that the attendant informed our family of seven that only one bear might be seen since the remaining bears were already in hibernation. Happy that we did not pay for all seven members of our family. So, only a few of our family members paid admission and found exhibits boring. No Bears to be seen. We felt the International Wolf Center was more interesting.

What a wonderful park to spend some time with family and friends. You can't go wrong with a visit to this park - it the best price in town - ALL FREE. Plan on at least a one hour visit or longer if you love artwork. Walk around, get some exercise, enjoy the unique sculptures and the Minneapolis skyline as some of the scenic backdrops. Parking is easy to find - we parked in a nearby free lot but all of the attached parking is affordable and easy to access.

This museum is a fun interactive way to learn about the history of the flour industry and the importance of the Mississippi River.  The Flour Tower and the elevator ride to the observation deck with beautiful views of the Mississippi River are worth the price of admission.  For a large family (we have five children) it makes more sense to purchase the annual pass than pay the daily admission.  Plus, it allow you to visit again.

This is an awesome indoor amusement park in the middle of MOA.  It has something for all ages from young children to teenagers.  Our first time was over four years ago with our five children.  This was our second trip with our 14-year old teenager for her Birthday and we spent the entire day at this park, the MOA and the attached Fly Over America attraction.  Be sure to purchase the bracelet online with a package discount deal.

We moved to Minnesota after being spoiled living next to Kings Island in Mason, Ohio.  Our family grew up loving Kings Island so Valleyfair can be disappointing in comparison.  Valleyfair is 1/3 the size of Kings Island and its roller coasters are disappointing.  It's nice for Minnesota families.  Ohio has nothing else to do so it needs major amusement parks and roller coasters to enjoy (such as Cedar Point and Kings Island).

This is a very nice park.  Buffalo is fortunate to have such a nice park with a beach walk, playground, canoe rentals and even a large chair to take some nice photos. The small splash pad is inviting on a hot summer day.  Its a park for all ages and interests. The music trail is a unique park amenity we observed adults and children using.

This is the best neighborhood park in the City of Elk River offering a lighted basketball court, a nice playground, hiking paths and the only lighted tennis court in the city. The barn is an awesome place for group rentals ideally for up to fifty people.

This is a state park that anyone who visits the North Shore needs to include in their itinerary.  Its a great stop and a must to start or end your trek on the North Shore - the most beautiful drive in Minnesota.

Excellent place for learning about train history. Good fun for the kids and anyone who loves trains.  The staff was accommodating and knowledgeable and they know everything about trains. Hiighly Recommend!!
This was a disappointing park with dirty restrooms and trash everywhere.  The bandshell looked nostalgic and the trees were nice for shade.
Well worth the admission price of  only $5 to learn about the Wright Brothers and the importance of America’s first military flight school.
This is a quick easy hike for some beautiful views.  We found the best time at sunset to get some picturesque views to remember.
A nice park to take a stroll in winter or summer along the river.  It has ice sculptures during the winter seasons.

Either the start or end to the incredibly popular Beaten Path. The trail gets the hype for good reason. The Rosebud side of the trail from Fossil Lakes is more majestic. That's and the difference is why most like to start from the Cooke City side. I might propose skipping the Cooke City side and do an out and back route. Then you could have a day with just a day pack for a day hike up to Fossil Lakes. But hey that's just me. I ran the trail and it was fun too for that purpose.

The Shorelands Preserve is a beautiful place to get out and stretch your legs for a short 1.5 mile loop around the marshlands. The boardwalk is wheelchair accessible and provides decent views of the area. There are numerous interpretive signs to explain the ecology of the salt lake marshes. If you are lucky you will get to see a decent number of the birds that are detailed in the signage. Great free activity for the family.

The history surrounding the construction of the obelisk is interesting and if you are walking along the Freedom Trail it is worth checking out.  A lot of the beauty can be appreciated from the outside.  If you have bad knees it isn't worth climbing the stairs and fighting the crowds.  Just peek in from the bottom to get a feel for what interior is like.

Most amazing stone arch built in all of Yellowstone!
Built in 1903 it is a real beauty and it is hard to drive by and not take a picture.  There is plenty of parking nearby so it is easy to stop and appreciate the arch.  Be sure to go inside the doors on either side and look up to get an inside view of the columns.

Great hike if you are looking for some quick elevation and don't want to drive North to the M. Never very crowded but the views are somewhat limited. After a few miles you will hit logging roads where you can walk or run for miles. Hey drop down into Sourdough for a long loop

Great park close to downtown Bozeman.  Grab a picnic lunch and hang out in the shade of a large tree.  Bathrooms and playground equipment makes it a perfect place to bring the kids and burn off some steam.  Good starting point for tackling the Peet's Hill walking trails.

Fantastic walking/running trails to get you or your dog some exercise.  Wide trails will bring you up to an amazing view of the city of Bozeman.  If you want to catch a beautiful sunset then this is the spot. You won't have the trails to yourself but still worth it.

Beautiful light house and worth stopping by to walk around it if you are in the area.  There are a couple of days a year that it is open so that you can walk up and see the view from the top.  Check the website for times to see if it coincides with your visit.

Excellent museum.  The dinosaur collection is fantastic thanks to the amazing paleontologists they have working with them.  The rotating exhibits make it worthwhile to visit several times a year.  Our son loves the play area upstairs.

Popular with bikers but if you are a runner and go early you can have the trail to yourself. Nice gradual elevation gain on a good trail. The road up to the trailhead has a couple rough patches so little cars may want to be cautious.
dislikes: Rough patches on road to trailhead

reviews_attraction.text: Very cool bridge and easily makes it worthwhile to stop in Shelburne Falls.  We went in mid October and it there were still plenty of things in bloom and it was beautiful with the fall colors in the hills surrounding Shelburne Falls.

Nice way to glimpse in the past to see how life used to be on the island.  The garden in the back looked good as well!  If you enjoy looking at old wooden plank flooring or old construction then this is a great place to visit.

The Silver Summit playground section of this park is a wonderful example of what a community can accomplish when they come together to do something great.  This is all access playground that kids of any age will have fun on.

This is a wonderful facility to tour.  Everybody makes you feel at home as soon as you arrive.  You will have all of your questions answered about the distilling process after the tour.  It is well worth a drive to visit.

This is a great place to take your kids and have a good time playing with them. If you are in town for a while the membership option makes a lot of sense since they switch out play areas very regularly. Friendly staff.

Wonderful place to get out and walk and enjoy scenes of the waterfront. If you are staying at Seattle Children's Hospital then this is a very close place to get out and clear your mind. Take a deep breath and relax.

If you have young children and enjoy being in a crowded playground then this will be a gem of a find for you!  Also if you enjoy spending an hour standing in line to ride a small train then you will love it here.
Great park with plenty of space to stretch out. Play in the water, jog on the trails, pick blackberries to your heart's content. Nice gem in Seattle and easy access from Seattle Children's Hospital.
This is a great park for kids of all ages. We were there early on a Sunday and were the only ones playing on the equipment.  Wonderful variety of things to choose from.
Great trails for all abilities. Not hard to find the true uphill route initially. Take a hard left as soon as you cross over the gate to enter the area.
If you are a train enthusiast, a kid, or a kid at heart you will enjoy this museum.  Well preserved locomotives and a nice stop in this cool town.
Parking may be limited but this is a great place to stop, admire the lighthouse, read about some rescues, and take a stroll on the beach.
Clean bathrooms and great jumping off point to hike Sacajawea. The parking lot does need to be bigger because this is a popular spot!
Was here during a cowboy poetry and singing event. It was an added benefit. Cool history on the ranch and some neat artifacts.
Great place to park and hit the Sourdough trail system.  Watch out for the bears that like to hang out along the steam.

This is a MUST VISIT if you are around Las Vegas. The Museum has tons of awesome pinball and old mechanical games. They have change machines and each game costs 25 cents to 75 per play. I visited with a large group with very diverse tastes and everyone had a blast! The building is nondescript, and the exterior is almost a little off putting, but don't be discouraged. Finally, look for neon colored note-cards taped to the machines. These cards have a bunch of really interesting information about the game you are about to play (which may be the only one left in the world!).

This is a must-see if you are in the area. The cavern is not huge, but the quality of the tour is incredible. Bill, the owner and guide, is very knowledgeable and accommodating. The history is interesting, and the formations and features are beautiful. As other reviewers mentioned, you should bring a light jacket or sweatshirt. The tour is somewhere between 45 minutes and an hour. Bill answers any questions you ask, so the duration varies. I would recommend this site for all ages. Follow your GPS and then look for signs with arrows to the Caverns!

This is a LARGE museum, and you can definitely visit more than once and not cover everything. That said, the layout if very unique and engaging, but also confusing at times. The map they provide is a big help, but there doesn't seem to be an established direction to flow through the exhibits. Everything is just kind of there, and you wander through. Maybe it's intentional, and it isn't a huge detractor from enjoying your visit but I found it frustrating every so often. I would definitely return, and I would also recommend a visit to others.

A world heritage site, Falling Water really is great in all seasons. Tickets are cheaper online than on site, and the 1 hour tour is well worth $30. Walking the grounds is not always available for visitors without a guided tour pass. There is just enough parking, concessions are available, docents are engaging and knowledgeable, and there are a few other minor attractions on the grounds. No matter what time of year you visit, Falling Water is worth the trip.

This is a beautiful park with lots of concerts and festivals in the summer. Plenty of green and open space, surrounded by two beautiful rivers. There are public restrooms near the Point State Park Fountain. Parking is a pain because essentially there is none. You have to park somewhere in town and walk through town to get here. You can also park on either the North Shore or South Side and walk across one of the bridges to get here (which I recommend).

This ball park is so cool I feel guilty I do not know more about it! The seats and lay out hold true to what the old parks used to be like. You almost get the feeling you're watching the game in a museum. I'll leave out my opinion on the team, but this place is definitely worth a visit even if you are not a baseball fan. On the bad side the food and drink prices are very high, and you can not order nachos.

Our docent was pretty incredible and made for a high quality experience. She did a great job explaining the history of the location, and connecting it with current events. She even tactfully managed some of the more "uninformed" adults in our group very well. It was a shorter tour than most, but very engaging. I would recommend visiting.

Who knew the NATIONAL Aviary was in Pittsburgh? Well it is, and the professionals here are great! I am not a fan of animals in captivity but the majority of their animals are rescues who would die if left in the wild, and the rest are given pretty spacious enclosures. Be sure to check out the fruit bat feedings when you visit!

This is a quaint park in the heart of the cultural district. Often, when the weather is nice, there will be live performers here. There tend to be a handful of homeless people here which takes away from the ambiance a bit, but I guess that can be expected with most parks inside of a city.

This was a pretty neat stop, and it's free. They have different shows and are sometimes closed to visitors as they setup so check their website for availability. If their horticulturalist is available I recommend you chat with him. He is very friendly and knowledgeable.

This is a smaller park but the trails are well groomed and on most you don't hear any road noise. Hell's Hollow is super short and pretty. There are a few other trails that are longer, and they all seem to be well marked. A great escape from nearby Pittsburgh.

This is a very nice city park. It's a little lower key than the others, and the various gardens have their own charm. There is a constellation lighting feature in the upper most garden that, when functioning, is really neat.

Unsure of when they finished renovations, this is a really attractive stop. The statues that great your entrance to Highland park, followed by the repaired fountain, and the flower gardens are all a sight worth seeing.

Waaaay more than you can experience in a single day, this is a high quality and high quantity museum. Docents are knowledgeable, and exhibits are beautiful. If you're busing Boston, this is a must-see.
Well maintained hiking trails and plenty of parking, this is an easy stop if you need to burn some energy while in the area. There is also fishing, boating, kayaking, mountain biking, and running.
Fun for kids and adults. The lines can get a little long, but this is worth a visit. There are enough activities between here and the Science Center that it can fill a whole day.
Surprisingly this place didn't show up on many tourist resource lists and the like, but it is definitely worth a visit. Larger than you would expect, educational, and beautiful.
The trails are well groomed, and the ranger station (and parking) is very adequate and informative. A cool stop if you are looking to get out of Las Vegas for a bit.
Beautiful park with great activities like a ropes course, kayaking, tennis, hockey, and more. They even run a small amateur race track near the pool in the summer.
This is a beautiful park that is managed very well. Jazz festivals, fund raisers, 5k races, and more are all held here. Definitely worth a visit.
Very nice venue. It has an attractive view, renovated restrooms, and plenty of space. Parking can be a little cramped, but overall pretty nice.
Beautiful park, and well worth a visit if you're in town. Tickets are cheap, there is always a give away, and every view is awesome.
Plenty of shops and places to eat. Prices on the high side, but everything in LV costs a lot. Worth walking through at least once.
It's free, and the open park and look out offer a refreshing break from the much more urban parts of the trail leading you there.
A big beautiful park with an amazing fountain. I was only here briefly to see the fountain but it was worth the trip.

Very beautiful state park! Parking in summer can be tricky - we arrived around 10:30am, and we were the last few visitors who could get parking space in overflow area. For people staying in the lodge, the lodge offered a guest only parking - very close to the trail. The trail was beautiful and had a good view of the river. However, sometimes it could get pretty crowded, so social distancing might be challenging in the park. Would recommend to people who enjoy hiking!

Additional note: We came in the winter again, and the trail was super slippery and icy. Would suggest visitors in the winter to bring hiking poles and wear shoe traction aid gears. Also, visiting Ottawa Canyon and Kaskaskia would be must easier due to the flat trail. Walking toward French canyon would be actually a bit tricky (or even dangerous).

We visited the Mirror Lake State Park during Thanksgiving, and it’s still not too cold and pleasant. However, compared to Devil’s Lake State Park nearby, I feel Mirror Lake might have less attraction spots for people coming from places far from here. Would recommend people traveling from other states like us to visit Devil’s Lake first, and then if you have time, you can spend some time in Mirror Lake. If you are local people, then Mirror Lake can definitely be a good place for a weekend getaway!

Highly recommend to visit the park during winter! We loved the frozen falls, and the back of frozen falls were usually also beautiful. Walking on the icy stairs might be tricky, so it’s important to bring traction aid and hiking poles. Be mindful when walking on icy roads since some of them might break (water underneath). It took us ~2hrs to finish walking around upper dells and lower dells with plenty of time taking picture and enjoying the view.

Second time visiting the arboretum and still felt like we have only explored less than 10% of it! It’s a very big area with gardens, trails, lakes, etc. Definitely recommend to families for a relaxing day. Biking and driving are on the same road, so just need to be slow and careful. The fragrance garden is small but elegant. The trolls have added a lot of fun to the arboretum. We got the membership and can’t wait to come back for the fall foliage!

A hidden gem in the north part of Chicago! We brought our bikes and biked along the biking trail - very enjoyable afternoon. Sculptures were done by many different artists, so we could enjoy different styles and appreciate the variety of messages the artists tried to convey. Not many people even in a sunny day, making it a very tranquil place to enjoy a weekend afternoon. A good place for families and friends to picnic too!

Very nice lakefront park! Although there’s still some place under construction, it’s pretty enjoyable. The parking lot has plenty of space but is not for free. When facing the lake, there’s beach in the left hand side - also beautiful. When the weather is good, you can see Chicago from here. During the day we visited, the air smells a bit awkward - the only thing that I would call out here... (probably just that day)

Very beautiful lighthouse and have a great view of the surrounding areas! We came on a rainy day, but it’s still very pleasant to walk around this area. The museum was closed - not sure if it’s due to the Christmas/new year holiday or COVID. We look forward to coming back during the summer! Also, the town seems to be cute and interesting to walk around when the weather becomes better.

Beautiful and special national park! Impressed by the tranquil lakeshore and the interesting experiences to climb on dunes. Would suggest to go a bit further than the popular trail 7 and 8 to avoid the crowd on the beach. We packed our lunch, blanket, slippers and enough water, and really enjoyed the tranquillity along the lake. Would definitely come back!

Very beautiful place! We visited it both in the morning and at night. Every part of the monument has some beautiful details - would recommend visitors to take some time and enjoy the details of it. This area could be a bit confusing for pedestrians while cars and horses all get into the roads - it might be much better to set it a pedestrian only area.

One of the most beautiful state park that I have ever visited in the Midwest! We visited the Old Man’s Cave two days after the snow storm. Although the road was very slippery, the overall trail was not dangerous at all - would recommend people to bring the hiking poles to avoid falling. Overall, it’s a enjoyable and not too difficult trail.

Very large and beautiful falls in the park! Although we couldn’t get to the lower view point due to COVID (social distancing) and slippery steps (just after a snow storm), the upper view point was great. Would recommend coming after rainy days to see larger water volume! The trail was pretty short that could be finish within 10-20 minutes.

Very beautiful waterfall! It’s within the Galena territory, so it would be great to check the rules when you visit here. The place is pretty close to the downtown Galena, so a short stop-by would be great. From the description, it seems to be an artificial waterfall for the overall water system in this area. Recommend to visits to Galena!

Cloud Gate is definitely a must-see in Chicago! The artist, Anish Kapoor, successfully used the “big bean” to capture the beautiful skyline of the downtown Chicago. It looks different during daytime and at night, and both are amazing! Will also recommend visitors to walk around the park and also visit the Crown Fountain and the Pavilion!

Visited the memorial in the morning. It’s very beautiful. We climbed up stairs to take a look at the city - great view! Didn’t get a chance to go in tho... For first time visitor like me, I suggest to walk around this area with other beautiful spots (e.g. monument, public library, fountain) and then visit the restaurant street nearby.

We visited the Ash Cave two days after a snow storm, and the view here was amazing!! The white snow and the yellow sunshine made the place look magical. Also, they had the one-way trail design to provide enough social distancing for visitors, and the trail was easy and short. Would highly recommend people to visit in the winter!

Crown Fountain is one of my favorite art works from Jaume Plensa. It shows faces from different genders, ages, ethnicities, etc. In the summer, it’s a fountain with water coming out of the mouth of those faces. In the winter, they shut down the fountain, but it’s still a nice place to walk around. Highly recommended!

The view of Cleveland from this park was very beautiful! We went there in the early afternoon, and the sunlight looks beautiful on the sign. If you want to avoid backlight in the picture, probably afternoon might be better time. We enjoyed walking around this area and also walking along the lakeshore.

Herrick Lake Forest Preserve is a hidden gem! It’s not far from the Chicago downtown, and it provides a very nice area with the Lake, picnic areas and trails for both walking and biking. Will recommend to families for a relaxing afternoon or social distancing gatherings on the lawn during summer time.

Very interesting installation art created by Polish artist, Magdalena Abakanowicz. It has a bigger group with a smaller group of sculptures spreading out on the lawn. It’s also a very nice spot for picnicking with shadow of trees and great view of the city. It’s also very pretty during winter!

The Riverwalk park was very beautiful in the fall foliage time! There are some private properties along the riverside that visitors shouldn’t go into, but there’s still a narrow trail that visitors can walk along the river. It’s very tranquil, clean and beautiful. Highly recommended!

Nice and short walking trail. We went there on Sat afternoon, and there were not many people. When all the leaves grow back in the spring/summer, this place should be even more beautiful! From this area, you can also see the railway (roughly 10-15 minutes walk from the parking lot).

We came here one week after the Winterfest, an ice sculpture competition, and luckily saw most of the ice sculptures still standing in the beach and the nearby area. The whole lake was covered in snow that some people even walked directly on the lake. It’s cold but beautiful.

Interesting fountain with different stories on each corner of it. Besides just looking at the beautiful design, it would also be nice to listen to some stories behind it in a walking tour or searching it online. It’s just a short walk from the nearby plaza.

We arrived when the museum was closed, but it’s still a beautiful building to look at and walk around. The parking lot is large and convenient. We will definitely want to come back when the museum open and there’s good social distancing policy in place!

Nice park in a beautiful neighborhood. We came here two days after a snow storm, and the road was fully covered in snow. Would need to be careful in walking a bit, but the view of snow in the park was still beautiful. Recommend to family with kids.

This place is almost too good to be true. They don't charge admission but there is a donation box - please throw in at least five dollars, it's well worth it. If you like flowers or gardening you must go here. There are things for kids and adults of all ages. Tropical plants, desert plants, vegetable gardens, flower gardens, bee hives, carnivorous plants, a pond with turtles and fish. It's truly amazing, you will be inspired. 11 acres of outdoor areas with walk paths and patios. The entire property, including the free parking, is fenced in and guarded - it is safe!

Midewin is a great place to relax and enjoy nature. There are  brochures available to help identify  the many wildflowers and birds you'll see in the prairie restoration areas. You could easily spend a full day here. If you have a good camera bring it. Bring your backpack with water bottles and Cliff bars. The bison move around and may be not be close to the fence first easy viewing - BRING BINOCULARS. There are picnic tables and outhouses at the Iron Bridge Trailhead. Walling paths are wide, flat, well-groomed, and suitable for strollers and bikes.

Great place to hike in all seasons. Waterfalls are beautiful in early spring time.  Cross Country skiing in winter. If you like the outdoors you'll love this place. There are a lot of long stairs leading to the hiking trails. Wear comfortable clothes and shoes and plan to be exhausted when you're done.

Best place to go for a walk or hike through the woods. The two lakes are stocked every year for fishing. Miles of paths through open fields and hilly woods. The spring itself is crystal and delicious fresh water. Lots of picnic tables and grills. There are bathrooms and a concession stand.

What a great beach. It's generally crowded so pay to park and take the first spot you can find. The sand is nice and the views are beautiful. There's a carousel museum and a splashpad you won't want to miss. And make sure you walk out to the lighthouse for some amazing pictures.

What a great place to visit, right in the middle of Naperville! Go back in time looking at all the old buildings and history displays. Kris Kindle Market is day after Thanksgiving to Christmas Eve day. You can even get married in the Century Memorial Chapel, like we did.

Anytime is a great time to visit Phillips Park! There is a lake for fishing, running trails, playgrounds, zoo, Christmas lights, gardens, picnic grounds. Take the kids, take the grandparents, or just go by yourself to relax and read a book. Lots of free fun!

Northerly Island has one of the best views of the Chicago skyline. There is a prairie restoration with walkpaths that is amazing. You can relax and have a quiet interaction with nature here. There is pay parking. Spend your lunch hour here and reenergize!

The view of the Rock River from this location is beautiful. Make sure to read the history signs and take the 212 step stairs down to the hiking trail along the river. This is a beautiful place and well worth the time to visit.

This is a fabulous park for walking/hiking. Not wheelchair friendly.
there is an elevated wooden walkway with wonderful views of the Galien river.
Well worth the stop for a little side visit.
Port-a-potty only, no facilities

Nice, small park for family and kids. You can picnic here and let the small kids play in the playground. You can fish in the pond and feed the ducks. It's right off of Roosevelt Rd but feels private and is quiet.

great, Great, GREAT! Quiet park, well maintained and good for all ages. There are a lot of benches for resting while the kids play on the jungle gym and swings. There are two bathrooms and plenty of parking.

This is a fun place to stop and take some pictures. It's very pretty, kind of tucked away in the woods. There's some history markers and a picnic area but no facilities. Definitely worth a little side trip

This is a small, quiet park where you can fish, or just sit and watch the Rock River go by. There's a children's park with playground and a wooden walkway like a deck for viewing the river. Very peaceful
This is a very nice place to just sit and reflect. There are benches where you can sit and enjoy the peaceful view of the water. Kids can play in the large lawn. It's a nice place for a picnic lunch
If you like outdoor activities you'll like Blackwell. This is an old quarry that has been turned into a beautiful lake and natural area. Great for fishing, boating, walking, pictures
This is like an undiscovered gem! Never crowded, great facilities, beautiful, quiet, wow! By yourself or with the family this is a great place for outdoor activities and picnics.
Beecher Center has open areas for field games, a very nice children's playground and is next door to the high school track where you can run. Lots of parking.
Wow, what a great place! If you are interested at all in Route 66 this is a must. Three floors of memorabilia, you could easily spend three hours here.
Great place for pictures and the relaxing sounds and sights of the beach. Walk to the lighthouse, enjoy nature, forget about your problems...
great, Great, GREAT! Lovely park to walk and relax. Benches are available for resting. Walk paths are easy to traverse. Ample street parking.
Are you in shape? You'll find out after you climb the stairs to the top of Mt Baldhead. The view from the top is amazing!
Great place to relax. Listen to and watch the river run by. Outdoor dining, outdoor ice cream, kid's playground, fishing.
This place is beautiful! No entry fee, just drive in and enjoy. No dogs permitted in park except in closed vehicles.
Great water park! Well staffed and clean park out in the country. Look for a Groupon for big discount before you go!

I had done no research on this museum prior to coming here and didn't have very high expectations. I'm glad to say that this place actually wow'd me and is one of the best art museums I've ever been too. This place is huge and you could literally spend all day here looking at everything. Even being rushed it took almost two hours for me to just go a quick go through. You have some amazing pieces here and this is top notch. Seriously, if you are an art fan, this place needs to be on your bucket list. Toledo has a gold mine with this treasure.

Such a unique place, I've never been anywhere like it! The forest giants are amazing pieces of art and definitely worth checking out. One warning is that this place is HUGE! I think it would be hard to see everything even in a couple of days, this place is a hiking lovers dream. I just wish I would've had more time to explore this wonderful place. Also know that this place is super popular and there was plenty of visitors there when I visited. It was still a great experience though and this is a place I'd definitely go back to.

A fascinating place whether or not you are Catholic or even a believer!. Amazing architecture and a lot of history here. The artifacts are hard to tell what's what. Most things are labeled and you have to look them up in a book, so it's really hard to know what exactly you're looking at. Also the authenticity of some of the artifacts can be questionable. It's morbid to see these saint relics but also I'm sure comforting to some people. If you're into this sort of stuff you need to add this to your bucket list.

Amazing place to go if you love bikes and even has some Neil Armstrong memorabilia. From the outside it looks like this place is tiny but they have quite a big collection. The highlight for me was getting to see the dream bike from my childhood, the Pee-Wee Herman bike up close and personal. I would have liked this place to have more celebrity bikes but there was some bikes of Robin Williams on display. Overall this place is definitely worth a detour and to put on your travel plans if you're in the area.

This is an impressive collection that you could easily spend several hours looking at. The layout of the museum isn’t the best and it can be somewhat confusing as to where to go and it’s easy to miss rooms. The collection is huge but lots of art pieces get crammed together which gives it a cluttered vibe that can take away from the experience. Overall this is definitely worth checking out. However, my favorite art museum in Ohio is still hands down The Toledo Art Museum.

What an amazing find. I was looking for something to do in the Dayton area and heard of this but didn’t know much about it. I’m so glad I decided to check it out. If you’re a Wright Brothers or aviation fan this is a must see with the National Wright Brothers museum. Also there’s plenty of classic cars, trains, buildings and artifacts here from Daytons history. There’s super knowledgeable and friendly staff here as well. This is a must see in Dayton.

The location is the highlight here. The Cincinnati Union Terminal is an Art Deco wonder and such a beautiful and historic location. The museums however left a lot to be desired in my opinion. If you aren’t going with kids you’ll probably be slightly bored and the size is fairly small. You’ll be able to see the entire museum in about an hour. Overall come to see the union terminal and keep your expectations for the museums on the low side.

I had no idea this existed and it was an awesome find! It's not the same size as the Leaning Tower of Pisa, don't go in expecting an exact replica. However, it's still a very accurate smaller scale replica and a lot cheaper than making a trip to Italy. When I want there there was no other visitors so I got the whole place to myself. Great place to check out if you're in the area and worth a detour.

Beautiful architecture and so peaceful and relaxing. When I went there I was the only visitor so I had the whole "church" to myself. This is unlike any church you'll ever see and is very unique in that aspect. You don't need to be spiritual or a believer to enjoy this space and I highly encourage anyone in the area to check it out and feel the peace you'll get being here.

Loved the Bob Ross Experience here and the history of this place. We should treasure having this local gem. I personally support them with a yearly membership even though I haven't got to experience a lot of their programs they are always great when I do get to see them. They also have some of the best apple cider around at their orchard shop.

Amazing architecture and a beautiful place! Despite me not being Hindu they were extremely welcoming and gave a great tour of the interior and general overview of the Hindu religion. Definitely a must see and extremely informative whatever your belief system is or lack thereof. This is a treasure to have here in the Indianapolis community.

Definitely a must see if you’re a Coke fan. Overall a nice collection that took about an hour to see. It wasn’t busy at all and there was some interesting artifacts. The staff could’ve been friendlier but overall this is a very good quality county museum and history buffs will enjoy it.
likes: Attraction Type: Good for history buffs

reviews_attraction.text: A great little place and while I'm not a huge fan of signs I did enjoy it here. I would've liked for it to be a little larger, it took only about 30 minutes to see everything here. Overall this is a nice little piece of Americana that I miss seeing these types of signs out in the wild.

One of the better state parks I've been to in Indiana. Lots of hiking trails and great river views. One downside was that it was packed with people when I went there which made it not as peaceful as I'd like. However, this is a great state park and one I'd go back to in a heartbeat.

This place is huge, I really wasn't expecting it to be as massive as it was. There's some great hiking trails here and when I went was relatively deserted which did make it feel a little isolated. Overall though this park is a win and a must see for nature lovers in the Indy area.

A historic treasure. Unfortunately the inside of the home was closed when visited because of covid. However, just the outside and the recreated street was a great trip back in history. I'd love to revisit once the inside is re-opened and tour the home.

This was a beautiful little park with nice hiking trails. It's a great place to do some photograph and portraits. It's pretty crowded but not so much that it makes in unenjoyable. Overall, this is a park worth checking out and one I'd go back to.

An amazing place with an amazing collection. Every rock and roll fan and music fan in general should add this to their bucket list. The building itself is impressive too and this is a fitting tribute to all the great bands that are members.

Ali is by far my favorite boxer and had such a unique personality. I loved getting to see some of his artifacts here. This place is a must see for any Ali or boxing fan. If you're in Louisville also remember that his grave is here as well.

A must see for classic car lovers. I would've like it to be larger than it was however, you can see everything in about an hour. Overall though definitely worth a visit and if you're in the South Bend area this should be on your list.

I enjoyed this park, there's plenty of great views and it wasn't overly crowded when I went. There's some nice hiking trails and I got to see some beautiful birds flying around. Overall one of the better parks in Indy in my opinion.

Gorgeous place with plenty of hiking trails. Not a ton of traffic either so relatively quite. I wouldn't detour too far out of the way for this one but if you're in the area and want to get some nature views then this is a winner.

Great park with great gardens. It's not as big as I'd like to to be though and there's better hiking trails at other parks in the Indy area. Overall though a solid park that is worth checking out and enjoying.
The park itself it's very big but it's a beautiful tribute to George Rodgers Clark. Overall this place is worth a detour if you're in the area to see and a must see for history lovers.
Inspiring place that will give you a history lesson and make you think. Loved it and so glad I got to visit here. One of the must see museums in Cincinnati.

I do have one complaint I am currently sitting in front of the park and it is 7:30 a.m. the park opens at 7. I pay for a recreational State pass I should be able to enter the park when it opens. I am currently leaving the park because the park ranger is not present to open the gate this is a holiday weekend amazing.
Really nice Park with shelterd picnic areas and hiking trails. Open from May 1st to September.
Jasper State Recreation Site is beautiful riverside park that is very popular for weddings, reunions, and large family picnics. There are 4 reservable group shelters with cooking areas, sinks, picnic tables and flush restrooms nearby.  Ball fields, playground, river access, volleyball and riverside trails provide for plenty of activities for kids and adults alike.

The upstream end of the park provides walking trails through a grand riparian forest, with the rush of the river a constant companion.  Angling is popular in this stretch of river, and there is easy access for launching canoes or kayaks to float the Willamette River Water Trail.

The park is OK at best. The bad review is for incompetent Park Rangers that share Duties between Willamette Mission State Park and this park.
My thoughts are that SOME not all of the park rangers are racist at these two locations and that is my honest opinion. They will find a reason to invade your space and be a nuisance. Nobody wants you annoying idiots buzzing around there picnic area, get the point.
Besides the annoying Park Rangers there is also a weird park host that resides in the park. I wonder whose tax money is paying her paycheck for camping in the park all year.

I would not recommend, you can't even have tours of the old Queen Anne house located in the park.

It's nice out there great wildlife viewing and hiking. It's a gavel road that is pretty washed out to enter the refuge. Very nice wheel chair accessible trail with viewing blinds at the end.
Just keep in mind the area is patrolled heavily by US Fish and Wildlife law enforcement  (The US Government). So please respect the wildlife and no poaching! Don't forget to pack out what you packed in and enjoy!

Great park and the biggest in Salem with a little under a thousand acres. History was made here with the whiskey brown home site some where on the island, a early pioneer that was friendly with the local Indians, trading tobacco that was grown by Mr. Brown on the island and of course a lot of whiskey drinking! Come enjoy the park and remember pack out what you bring in or even better pack out something some one else didn't pack out! Be aware there has been reports of Cougars being spotted in the park.

Dexter State Recreation Site, on the western edge of Dexter Reservoir, provides convenient access to the reservoir with docks and a two lane launch ramp.  A picnic area with bbq stands and fire rings overlooks the lake.  But the lake is not the only attraction!  A popular 18-hole disc golf course winds it way through oaks and Douglas fir trees and you can reach nearby Elijah Bristow State Park through a system of connecting trails that follow the Middle Fork of the Willamette River.

Very nice City Park area and Green Space stretches for several blocks. Has some cool elephant sculptures with a playground and benches.

Nice park with plenty of hiking trails and access to water. There tent camping isn't the best in my opinion pretty close together kind of like Tent City!
Drive Thru water areas with a good restaurant nestled in the park. There are cabins as well that can be rented and a nice gift shop with some great chocolates and so on.

This is a awesome park with multiple Pavilions, kayak / boat launch, soccer fields and baseball fields along with several play grounds. There is also multiple restrooms throughout the park.
