Going to school in the medical field, or just Interested in the history of Surgical Science?  Then this museum is a must for you!

I did not even know of it's existence until I was invited to a private VIP after hours event here.  This is "North America's only museum devoted to surgery".

Located on Lake Shore Drive in an architecturally gorgeous former mansion, with a breathtaking view of Lake Michigan, it is easy to pass by without knowing what a treasure of a museum awaits inside.

When you enter the foyer, you are taken back to the early 1900's when the mansion was built, and marvel at the Italian marble, brass fixtures, stone fireplaces, limestone statues, and gilded metal staircase that have been preserved for us.

The museum is 4 floors of Surgical artifacts, paintings, illustrations, murals, and sculptures.  It is a museum dedicated to early treatments, discoveries, and successes that have led to how modern medicine is applied today.

Make sure to visit the Early American Apothecary, the hall of statues, the eyeglass exhibit, the iron lung (this blew my mind) ,and the rare books display in the former study. There are also a lot of artifacts in cases such as amputation kits, and early x-ray machines.  Don't miss the Nursing exhibit, it is an awesome tribute to the Nursing profession.

There are paintings and murals throughout that depict some of the early practices of surgical medicine.  Make it a point to read the large plaques that are installed on the walls behind the exhibits, they make it easy and more enjoyable to understand with all the information that they supply.
likes: Facilities & Services: Architectural beauty, preserved interior

reviews_attraction.text:
There's nothing better than enjoying the Chicago Riverwalk on a warm sunny day except enjoying the Chicago Riverwalk on a cooler sunny day.

If you go during the summer you will encounter lots of people, my suggestion is you wait for cooler weather so go in the spring and fall and it will be much more enjoyable.

A nice location to enjoy some of the best sights of the Chicago river and Chicago's gorgeous architechture.

Unfortunately people waiting for a table at the bars and restaurants block the walkway so it's crowded in some spots.

Especially crowded at City Winery where they have seating and stairs where you can sit and enjoy the boats passing by. In fact, it looks like most people bring their own drinks to enjoy by the river and not that many are actually purchasing at City Winery.

Bike owners, dog owners, and strollers should all be banned from the Riverwalk

Bicyclists are supposed to yield to pedestrians but they don't.

People leaving their dog poo in the carefully landscaped shrubs/flowers right across from a restaurant is not very appetizing.

You can hop on board the Chicago Water Taxi for a different view of the city and the Riverwalk.

In fact, you can walk right into Navy Pier if you want to lengthen your stroll and see another iconic Chicago landmark.

If you can avoid the rude bicyclists, the dog owners who do not clean up after their dogs and the people with strollers who will Ram into you at a moment's notice, you'll have a wonderful day.

A FREE zoo? That's practically unheard of these days.  Lincoln Park Zoo is awesome!

The zoo is free, but you do have to pay for parking.  There is some free street parking available nearby, but you will have to get there early and search for it.

The zoo is open 365 days per year and the hours are:  weekdays from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m April to October,  and 10 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. from November through March.  On weekends from 10 a.m. to 6:30 p.m. The only exceptions being Memorial Day and Labor Day when their hours are 10 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

There are several entrances to the zoo, however, my favorite way to enter is through the nature Boardwalk where you can stroll through native plants and see native birds, fish, turtles Etc.

Lions and tigers and bears oh my!

You will see animals from Africa to the Arctic tundra.  Giraffes, rhinoceros, zebras, polar bears, penguins, monkeys, gorillas and apes.

My favorite part of the zoo is the waterfowl Lagoon and the McCormick bird house.

With exhibits both indoor and out, you have an excellent view of the animals.

They also have options for food anywhere from snacks to a full service menu at The Patio at Cafe Brauer.

Don't forget to stop in at one of the stores where you can choose from a selection of wild things that you can take home with you.

Plan on spending at least a couple of hours so you can take your time and enjoy your day at the wonderful Lincoln Park Zoo.

We went here on a Sunday for the Barrio Arts Fest.

They are normally closed on Sundays so this was a treat, as every time we go past this location, it seems like they are closed because I never see any cars in the parking lot or any activity of any kind.

Their hours are Tuesday through Friday 10 to 5 and Saturdays from 10 to 2. And they do have a free parking lot in the back.

The sign outside says this is the national museum of Puerto Rican arts and culture.

The building itself is fantastic, in fact that's the best part of the museum.  This building has undergone a major renovation and it was well worth it. However the art inside the building is sparse and very little to speak of.

On the first floor they had an exhibit by Oscar Lopez Rivera and not much else.   Large rooms with hardly anything in them, I don't think that this building is being used to a it's full potential.

On the second floor they had an exhibit of poetic science which is an artistic scientific approximation about El Yunque however it was closed on the day that we visited because of the Art Festival.  The supervisor told us that they did not have enough employees working that day to open the second floor.

Now that I know that they actually are open and the hours that they are open, I will return on another day to check out the second floor.

2.6 miles of trees and Lush vegetation.  In some parts the vegetation is over running the walkway, I don't know why this hasn't been trimmed back.

You will see flora and fauna in a multitude of colors.  Red, yellow, pink, white, purple, orange, blue, and of course lots of green.  For an enjoyable experience take the 2 small nature trails that are very close to both ends of the 606.  Be sure to look for the large mushrooms as it is nature in the wild.

There are water fountains at the 1.5 and 1 mile markers in the middle. But there are no washrooms.

The 606 is surprisingly Litter free, considering I only counted 6 garbage can locations.  I did see lots of cigarette butts on the ground, so maybe smoking should be banned from the 606.

It's a shame that there is graffiti on most of the signs. I took a picture of one of the only two graffiti free signs.  The city should clean up the graffiti.

Dogs and dog owners should be banned from the 606.  Dog owners are not picking up the dog poop.  Watch out for feces on the ground.  I'm also not a big fan of having a dog sniff me while I'm trying to take a leisurely stroll.

Be on the lookout for crazy bike riders as they seem to think that this is a race track.

If you can go during the week it's less crowded and much more enjoyable.

The Chicago Sports Museum is located in Water Tower Place on the 7th floor at 835 N. Michigan Avenue.  It is adjacent to Harry Caray's 7th Inning Stretch restaurant.

The museum itself is highly interactive and great foyer kids.  If you pay the $10 admission price and then eat in the restaurant on the same day before 6 pm, they will give you a credit of $10 for each ticket that was purchased.

Take your time to walk around and soak in all of the Chicago memorabilia that is on display here.  You should reserve anywhere from 1 to 2 hours to really be able to enjoy the Chicago Sports Museum.

There is a gift shop where you can purchase your own souvenirs to take home with you, but I was disappointed to find that most of the items were made in China. As the prices are on the higher side, I recommend that you go to Walgreens or any of the local stores nearby as I have similar items for less money.

Also, take time to check out the items on both sides of the walls in the hallway between the museum and the restaurant, you can take a picture with the bronze bust of Harry Caray & make yourself into a football player with the standee that is at the end of the hallway.

Walking into Garfield Park is like walking into another world.

Lush foilage exotic plants and flowers.

It's a perfect place to spend an afternoon or day in a very enjoyable atmosphere.

Don't forget the outdoor section of Garfield Park. There are awesome walking paths, activities for children, and a really pretty pond.

There are nine sections to the Garfield Park Conservatory check out:
the Palm House
the fern room
sugar from the Sun
Elizabeth Morse genius Children's Garden
the desert house
the aroiid house which includes the Persian pool and features 16 yellow lily pads which were created by the world acclaimed glass artist Chihuly expressly for the aroid house
the show House
Horticultural Hall
the outdoor Gardens

Come spend the day with family and friends and enjoy a little taste of nature in the city

The Garfield Park Conservatory is truly an awesome place!

Love to come here in the winter!

You feel like you have just stepped into the jungle.

Always something different, lush plants, & flowing water make this a peaceful oasis in the city.

The best part is It's free!!!  Donations are gratefully accepted.

#CityExperts @GoogleLocalCHI

We decided we needed a nature getaway for a couple of hours, so  on Monday July 20th, 2020. We drove 2 hours to Starved Rock State Park. Luckily we had done our homework. We got their relatively early at 9:30 a.m. we visited three of the Lesser traveled paths, Ottawa,  Kaskaskia, and Illinois Canyons .

It was very muddy, but it was serene. It was so nice to be surrounded by Nature. We only saw a handful of people there.

Our mistake was in going around 12:30 p.m. to the Central Area:  the Starved Rock Visitor Center where most of the trails start from..

The Visitor Center was not open but the cafe and bathrooms were.

The trails leaving from The Visitor Center were jam-packed.  There was no social distancing of any kind and 99% of the people there were not wearing masks.

It was a single file line with people right on top of each other, and blocking the entire walkway so you couldn't even get around them.

Took a quick picture at the Starved Rock overhang and we left quickly.

If you are planning to visit, I would suggest that you get there very, very early and / or visit the less popular trails in order to avoid the huge crowds.

The city’s “new masterpiece" is really something to see.  The huge playground area is outstanding and everyone can climb up the giant fort and walk across the hanging bridge.  The time I was there, some Parcore enthusiasts had taken over a section of the playground.  People were enjoying time spent with their children despite the frigid weather.

The ice skating ribbon is really unique and really crowded.  The line was very long to not only rent skates, but the ine to just get onto the ice with your own skates was super long too.

Looks like dogs are not allowed into the park, but on the sidwalks surrounding the park, there were reminders left that some owners neglect to pick up after their pets.

A little disappointing that the area for the Cancer Survivors Garden has been changed.  It was a beautiful area that was quiet and serene, now there is too much foot traffic going through this area and they took out the trees and bushes that mad it a unique space.

I would have given it 5 stars, but I am anxiously waiting for all areas of the park to open and explore at my leisure.

#LocalGuides @GoogleLocalCHI
dislikes: Long wait times for ice skating
Increased foot traffic in quiet areas

The Art Institute of Chicago has something for everyone.  This wonderful Art Museum is well-known around the world.  The building itself is an architectural wonder. Take your time and you the wonderful Building inside and out.

Every style of painting is represented here from Modern,  classical,  renaissance,  to abstract and more.

Its not just paintings either.  They have exhibits with sculptures, antique furnishings, pottery and much more.

Famous works of art such as American Gothic, A Sunday afternoon on the island of La Grande Jatte, The Bedroom,  Nighthawks, The Guitar are all displayed here for your enjoyment.

Degas, Matisse, Monet, Picasso, Renoir, Rodin, Seurat, Toulouse-Lautrec, and Van Gogh are some of the artists whose works are on display as well as many others.

We went here in January to see the excellent Vincent van Gogh exhibit that featured many of his works from around the world. There are always special exhibits on display here.

Enjoy a quiet place, step back in time and feast your eyes on some of the most beautiful artwork on the planet.

An Urban Oasis in the Concrete Jungle.

Take the half mile hike around the nature Boardwalk which is connected to the Lincoln Park Zoo.

Take the Less Traveled fork to the right to go around the pond when coming from the south, as most people go left to go straight into Lincoln Park Zoo

On a relaxing walk down the boardwalk around the pond, you will see some of the plants and wildlife native to Illinois.

Look down in the water and you will see egrets, turtles, as well as fish.

The vegetation is Lush and in some places currently taller than 8 ft.

This is a great place to take a leisurely stroll, meet up with some friends, enjoy nature, or see the Fantastic Chicago skyline.

Take time to stop and read the plaques around the pond it will give you some good insight into the care and thought that was put into this gorgeous location.

A place to relax, unwind and enjoy the day.

We just discovered the Museum of Contemporary Photography and I don't know why it took us so long.

We went to a a discussion led by Kristin Taylor, the Curator of Academic Programs and Collections.  It was stimulating and enlightening.

The museum is technically free, but, there is there is a donation box in the front of the entrance, feel free to donate!

The actual exhibit area is 3 floors, but the actual exhibit area is small and located in a Columbia College building, Definitely check out the second floor.

They have an inventory of approximately 15000 photos, so they have lots of material for exhibits.  In fact, there are new exhibits every couple of months.

They have well known and lesser known photographers in their collection, all of them interesting and worth a look.

I highly suggest checking out their website for the current and upcoming exhibits and events.

A bird lover and nature lovers Paradise.

Montrose Point Bird Sanctuary can be found by following Montrose Avenue east until crossing Lake Shore Drive and into Lincoln Park.  From there, take a right at Montrose Harbor Drive, the street next to the gray-painted bait shop.  Follow the curve and Montrose Point Bird Sanctuary will be on your left. If you drive, park on the street.

Visit the magic hedge, on the west side of the sanctuary, but stay on the trails as much as possible in order to not disturb the nesting and resting Birds. Make sure you take the path in One Direction and return in the opposite direction in order to navigate the whole area.

Don't forget to walk down to the pier where you will see rare ducks,  loons, and possibly peregrine falcons.

We went here for a private event.  We did not have to wait at all but I understand that it can be a long wait time as much as up to two to three hours.

Once you arrive at floor 103 you get a spectacular 360 degree view of the awesome city of Chicago.

Another great feature is that you can stay up there as long as you like.  They do not have any lines or supervision for people to step onto the ledges that are on the side of the building so that it's kind of a madhouse and could be a long wait time.

Definitely a must do in Chicago.

You can also get your picture taken by a photographer there for around $25.00.

Take lots of pictures and have fun!!!

#CityExperts.    @Localguides

Has been here for a couple of grand opening events.

The latest is the shape of Chicago John Massey's 1968 banners Revisited and reimagined by Chicago's creative youth.

Although the space is relatively small, the exhibits that they feature here are worth the time you take to not only look at the art, but discover the history behind the art.

A lot of people will just come in here and look around and leave, but I urge you to find out the background of the designs as it will make your visit here more enjoyable.

The museum is free, but there is a donation box at the entrance.

I have found my visits here enjoyable and enlightening, you should check it out for yourselves!

One of my favorite places to visit in downtown Chicago.

They always have such interesting art exhibits.

The building itself is a marvel in architecture.

You can come in relax from a hectic day of shopping, grab a drink and pastry from the cafe and find out about events in the tourist center.

Free performances, quiet room to read, what more could you want?

What a great place to stop in!

Went to the Keith Haring the Chicago mural exhibit at the Chicago Cultural Center.

It's there through September 23rd, go see it if you can it's really inspiring!

Interested in Space, Science Our Solar System?  Then The Adler Planetarium is a must visit for you!  Destination Solar System is a great show for all ages.  Adler After Dark is a great way for adults to see the all the Planetarium has to offer without sidestepping the little ones. Don't forget to walk around the outside of the Planetarium as it has some of the best views of our great city Chicago, The view of Lake Michigan is truly beautiful, you could spend almost as much time outside as inside. #CityExperts @GoogleLocalCHI

This museum is a little out of the way & one of the smallest museums in Chicago.  However, I always find something new & interesting when I visit this museum.  The admission is $12.00 (suggested) for adults, however Illinois resident are free on Tuesdays. There is a new David Bowie exhibit (seperate feeof $25) that I am really looking forward to seeing.  The museum store has very unique and different items for sale, great for gifts! #CityExperts @GoogleLocalCHI

There is something for everyone here.  With 3 levels and changing exhibits,  it's a great place for families and singles alike.  Kids of all ages can touch and explorea lot of the exhibits.

It can be pretty pricey, especially if you add the interactive exhibits and tours check your local library for kids passes or the free days for Illinois residents.

Wish there were free days for Chicago residents only.

#CitiExperts.    @localguides

The Alfred Caldwell Lily Pool is a great place to relax and unwind.  A peaceful oasis to walk through or stop and enjoy the natural landscaping and natural wildlife.

It's a quiet part of the Lincoln Park Zoo, and you can enter from the street or from inside the zoo.  A perfect place to take your lunch and enjoy a little bit of wilderness in our great city!

#CityExperts @GoogleLocalCHI #PartyonLG

The actual art gallery space is very small, but this is located in a Chicago historic landmark.

You can get away from the cold or heat in Chicago for a few minutes depending on the weather and it is located in a cute little park where you can take a break from shopping for a few minutes.

It would be nice if it was bigger, but still a Chicago treasure none the less!

#LocalGuides @GoogleLocalCHI

A very interesting museum with interactive displays representing the military history of the first infantry division.  I was really impressed with the walk through exhibit that makes you feel as though you really are in the middle of combat.  There are actual tanks lining the path to and from the museum that the kids can climb on for fun.

#CitiExperts     @Localguides

A hidden gem located in Jackson park Behind the Museum of Science and Industry.  A small Japanese Garden that's really beautiful and really well-kept.

It's really peaceful and normally not crowded.  Bring a picnic lunch and be sure to clean up after yourselves.

Parking used to be free, but now you have to pay so be prepared.

#CitiExperts     @Localguides

Their summer camp is good.  They have an indoor pool at this location and tennis courts. You will need to chase away people if you want to play tennis as there's always someone playing on the tennis courts.

As with all the Chicago parks, the field house could use a major update.

Generally good for kids.

#CitiExperts.    @Localguides

One of my favorite places to spend an hour or so exploring nature.  They have lots of great activities for kids,  including hands on exhibits.

There are also some rescued wildlife in cages outside the facility.

Check for their nature programs, I believe they are free!

#CitiExperts     @Localguides

My family enjoys the Cascades. It is a venue for holiday fireworks celebrations. It hosts large events like an annual Civil War muster.  It is sometimes a setting for "B" list bands. All of that in the setting of a pretty park complete with walking paths, tennis and Bball courts, ponds, a golf course, and a driving range.  The world famous Cascades Falls (which I think everyone would enjoy seeing at least once) is the center stage. A good ice cream stand can be found here, too.  In the winter, it is probably the most popular local sledding hill.
likes: Recreational facilities (walking paths, tennis and basketball courts, golf course, driving range)

reviews_attraction.text: Immaculately maintained historical site. Charcoal pig iron was prepared here in the mid to late 1800's. Many structures are so well preserved (especially the smelting ovens) that you can imagine being there while the place was in full function. The park is also beautiful. It sits on a peninsula in Lake Michigan with rocky cliffs, a pretty bay, and lots of green.

The Black Rocks cliff jump, located inside the park, can keep the family occupied all day. It's in a very beautiful setting, and in August the water temperature of Lake Superior it is tolerable to pleasant. Also the sunsets at Sunset Point are gorgeous and should be experienced by everyone visiting the park.

Beautiful. We visited on a sunny day and the sun lit the surrounding bay/harbor awesomely. We were able to climb the light (which I recommend, if possible). This is one of the prettiest lights and settings in Michigan, in my stupid opinion. No kidding, don't miss this.

I think that these falls are among the prettiest in the state. There is a steep set of stairs that travels up the side of the falls - if you are physically able, don't miss this - it's a beautiful walk and gives you varied perspectives of the falls.

We use the park as a base camp during vacation time in the North West part of the state. Petoskey is special - loaded with great restaurants, shopping, and with pretty stuff to look at wherever you turn. The camp is quiet, clean, and wooded.

It is a very good thing that people cared enough for this treasure to turn it around and restore it to its former beauty. It is important to visit and donate so as to avoid repeating history and potentially losing this gem forever.

Consider waterproof boots when the weather is warm and it has been raining. Easy walk, but wheelchair use would rarely be possible. Bug spray is a must between the last and first frosts unless you like being lunch.
Great art that can be seen at a great price (free). Funny, thought provoking, and some of it beautiful. We liked it so much, we made a donation (which certainly wasn't expected). Don't skip this.
This is a well done tour.  Beautiful scenery, well informed historical guides/captains.  My family really loved this experience. It's worth every penny.  Don't forget your camera!
Our family enjoys being able to see these beautiful black bears in a place where they are obviously well cared for.  Pay the money and feed a cub. I bet you go back again!
We enjoy the Yankee Springs park and Gun Lake! Redneck (in a good way) activity abounds, the lake is shallow and gets pretty warm. Good fishing, swimming, and skiing.
1840s lighthouse is well maintained on beautiful grounds. The last keeper was appointed by President Lincoln. Pay the $5 and go inside and climb the lighthouse.
I enjoyed the variety of tree species the most.  Many of these are identified and some facts about the plant described.  I'm glad that we didn't skip this.
5 stars for nostalgic value.  It was a great place to take our daughter when she was young to run and play.  The park is aging, but still enjoyable!
Pretty state park on the shores of Lake Michigan.  The upper campground, "the Pines" has a little more room between you and your neighbor, fyi.
On the south side of the channel. On this side, you can see a nearby submarine. Also on this side, you can access the red channel light.
You probably wouldn't expect to pet a hippo in this area of the country. You can do that here. You can see lions, tigers, and bears too.
Manicured trails. Lovely walk through hardwoods and conifers. The Kalamazoo River winds through and adds to the beauty of the place.
This park is a good gift to the community.  Beautiful and interesting.  We don't hesitate to drive 2 hours to enjoy it for the day.
Certainly one of the best museums in the country! I have loved it most of my life and continue to look forward to visits.
Easy to see these very pretty falls via a boardwalk.  Many stairs along the way require some modest degree of fitness.
If you're a history buff, this is one of your places. The kind you want to stay behind with when vacation is over.
Well maintained "put put" course with a river of blue water. Not "water blue", but "blue" blue. I like it.
My wife and I think that this is a lovely Metro park. Nice trails, a great view of the lake.

First time, I came here, I hated it. We came in bikes off the rail trail and got lost. The park's bike paths were full of hills. I havent rode a bike in the last 5 yrs. The second time, we drove around and found all these beautiful beaches! Definitely would recommend for a camping trip or a day at the beach. The ponds are more warmer than the beach

We loved it. Loved that there was a starbucks inside the museum. Get your energy  before walking around the museum. I loved the experience.  It was interactive  and definitely  worth a visit. It's cheaper if u buy tickets online and you skip the line. Loved this place. Worth a visit.

A little confusing with the signs from the road. If you are not from the town, you wouldn't know it was behind another house. It was a very cute and small museum. I loved the pictures of the different time eras of jello. Pretty neat. They sell the jello for $1 here

It was a little packed, however it was worth it. You can walk on the path or along the river by skipping on rocks. Great way to get your kids into nature. It had little small waterfalls along the way. The end of the waterfall was so breathtaking.

Truly sad to see. The minute you enter this small space, an overwhelming sad feeling washes over you. But only if you know the true history. Even if you dont, that feeling will come over you, once you read each memorial.

If you are an nyc fanatic then this is best museum for you. The movie downstairs is the best part!!! I loved watching it and seeing all of these nyc artifacts. I love seeing Calvert Vaux tools. That was amazing to me.

It is slowly recovering from hurriance sandy. They do have a new center that is still under construction but will be worth the price. Its still a small aquarium however you get a 4D movie on top of it.

The best relaxing hidden gem in nyc
It is quiet and completely closed off from the everyday nyc noise. You feel deeply relaxed after spending only a few minutes here. The waterfall is amazing
Beautiful playground. It is currently open during this time. Big enough for adults to social distance but the kids still mingle somewhat. Make sure to wash hands after they are done playing.
An amazing museum and its FREE. It had so much to see and so many different things. Mr. Walters had spend most of his life collecting the very things u find in this museum. Worth a visit!!
Love this fountain. It has different water pressures during different  times. I loved getting wet during a hot summer day. It's also lit at night. Gorgeous  architectural fountain
This is one museum that is a must see. Always have cool event and never have the same displays. I love this museum because it's modern and weird and retro all rolled into one
Absolutely loved it here. Great vibes and for smaller kids. It was well priced and definitely lots to do and see. I would recommend for all families with smaller kids
Beautiful place. The waterfall is relaxing. Bring a picnic and blanket. You must pay 10 for parking if you don't have the parking pass. I will definitely recommend
The attendant in the front was trying to make some money by asking for $25, after 6pm. He told him, we just wanted to look around and he stated its $25
Very rocky and not the best beach to enjoy a swim. Even with water shoes, the rocks are a bit annoying. This beach is better as a hang out spot.
Some places to hike are very dangerous and slippy. Make sure you have decent hiking shoes. If you stay on the trails then definitely rent a bike
Great place to relax and play for kids. The beach is very rocky and you need beach shoes. The water smells a little that's why I gave it a 3
Even tho it's free on Wednesdays, it is so packed! I wished they had more free days but besides that largest metropolitan Zoo in the world.
Its amazing to see how New England started and it starts with the landing rock. A must see for people who live in the new England area
Its was an okay view. Nothing special. They have benches and its worth sitting and watching the sunset. Pretty good price with groupon
A cute museum. Not really much to see but the trolley ride was worth it. It ran along the Hudson and some amazing views.
Such a huge space but not much to see. This museum needs some updating. The only great thing about it is the panorama.
Really cute farm. Saw alpacas which I thought was pretty cool to see in nyc. You can feed the animals if you wish.
So much do and so much to see. Take the ferry from brooklyn, its free. Pack a picnic and go!

The parking area is too small. There are too many spaces meant for boats with trailers. The view of the lake is nIce. There are 4 covered picnic areas with grills that looked nice, reservations recommended. Saw 3 picnic tables close together near the main road. Would rather they be away from the road and under some trees.
Saw 3 wooden docks to fish from. Tried several wooden benches that were very uncomfortable. More benches that are comfortable would be appreciated. There's a large playground.
There's a new nature trail through the woods which is still very uneven and muddy so would be difficult with strollers and isn't wheelchair or walker friendly. Not recommended for anyone with balance issues. Couldn't find a description of the trail on the Web site so no idea how long the trail will be and what improvements will be made. Recommend gravel or bark mulch to help with mud, and have the trail be more level so it's easier to walk on.

There is a nice paved walking trail that makes a 1.5 or 2 mile loop. Benches are  scattered around the trail. Nice campground and picnic areas with clean restroom. Good dog park near the campground area. My only complaints are I wish the trails through the woods weren't just for bikes. Would like if they were open to walkers a few days a week.
You can access the walking and biking trails for free from the parking lots near the dog park and campground, at the North end of the park.
There's a fee to go past the main gate to get to the pool, tennis courts, manor house.

It would be nice if the river trail actually had more than one obscure place to see the river. Some more river viewing areas and seating would be great.

Visited yesterday. Served by Van who was very friendly and knowledgeable about the wines. The facility , patio and grounds are very nice with a great view. I liked several dry wines but really liked the red table wine and ardella sweet wines. He has a special deal now on 2 bottles of cabernet sauvignon with 2 packs of mulling spice for $27, a $23 discount. Good deal!
The property is easy to find from route 268, but I came via scenic back roads off of route 67. Either way is scenic.
However, GPS told me I had arrived, but I was at a private white house. The entrance to the winery was actually a few hundred yards further west on the left.

The view and tasting room are nice. Did the standard wine tasting. The only wine that my friend and I could tolerate was the white sangria. I'm not into dry wines but can usually imagine having the wine with a meal. Not so here! All the other wines I tried were horrible! A week before, at another winery, a Roanoke area man said his wife described one of the Valhalla red wines as making her think of licking a sweaty horse! I think I know which one she referred to. I may return for the view some time, but not for the wine.
Maybe the reserve wines are better, but they're pricy.
If you like dry wines, Maybe you'll like their wines.

Walked here Saturday from Byrd Branch campground nearby. The tasting room building is very nice, lots of sunshine and light colored wood. Good, comfortable seating is there. Our group did a tasting and I liked all of their wines. We purchased about 10 bottles of wine which the owner delivered to our campsite so we didn't have to carry bottles 1.5 miles through the woods. Very accommodating.
The scenery is rolling farmland, ponds and trees. A nice relaxing place to visit with a good variety of wines. I've been to 30 other wineries in the area and this is one worth coming back to.

The winery is recently under new ownership, a couple from South Africa. So if you were scared off by previous owners arguing, they're gone, so come back!
New owners bought the remaining wine from previous owners and have added a new wine. They also are selling champagne and beer.  Some snacks such as cheese and crackers are available but you're welcome to bring a picnic.
The view is pleasant. Sit under the vine covered gazebo for nice experience.
This is a very quiet, low key place.
The wines are good also. They sometimes have live music. This is a nice, low key place

They have wines for different tastes, good homebrew beers, and raspberry cider that is moderately sweet. They're having food trucks and free music on weekends. Definitely worth a visit! However, sometimes the music is too loud and interferes with conversation.
Their tasting room needs more inside seating and is very noisy. They really need acoustic ceiling tiles.
The older, historical building on the west side of Williams road is now a restaurant - the Grapevine Grille. Beautiful old wood building with a nice, calm atmosphere and nice view of vines.

I grew up 2 blocks from this park but have been away for years. Great improvements! New steps down from the parking lots are nice and will last a long time. There's now a boardwalk going to Cary Avenue beach. The 2 new swimming coves look nice and new rock breakwater protects the beach from erosion.  Cary Avenue beach has beautiful new interpretation center and bathrooms. A new walkway from the parking lots heads back up hill to Rosewood park.  Nice new benches too.

The visitor's center closed for remodeling. Bathroom was smelly and out of soap.
The paved trail around the property was nice. Good, educational signage. The area has interesting history.
The view of the Cape Fear river was nice. Could see across to Carolina Beach State Park and places to the north. Haven't been to the park for special events, but they're probably good and educational. The park is definitely worth a visit.

Beautiful tasting room and scenery. I liked some of the wines but some were too dry for my taste. They plan to have music on weekends in the future. The snacks available were limited but maybe were just low on supplies. They don't allow outside food or drink on premises.
This is a great place to stop after going to nearby Stone mountain park. Easy access off highway 21.
There was nice seating on concrete patio outside.
dislikes: No outside food or drink allowed

reviews_attraction.text:
Friendly staff, nice views, nice tasting room with a few tables and bar stools. Went recently with a very picky friend and she enjoyed all the wines.  I found multiple wines to enjoy.
The covered patio area is nice with comfortable rocking metal chairs.  A tent area has more seating for larger groups.
Twice now have enjoyed the low key live music of Dave Porter. Now that I live 35 miles away, I'll visit regularly.

Park has nice playground for young kids, soccer fields and covered picnic area. There are 2 unisex bathrooms in the picnic area. I've been here twice to get on the Ararat Greenway trail. Easy trail access, lots of parking
I rode 3.5 miles south  to where the trail turned and started following highway 52. I turned back then to avoid riding near the highway. The trail was very nice with good views of the creek.

Beautiful scenery. If you leave from the lower parking lot, it can be easy to get on the wrong trail. We didn't want to go on the trail to the top with the 650 steps up, but the trail sign wasn't clear where to split off for the trail in the valley, so be careful. Otherwise, the park is great. They could use more, cleaner restroom.
Watch out for snakes. We saw a large Copperhead snake in the trail.

Great access to the Dan river for swimming. The picnic tables are old and sagging and should be replaced. More of them would be great.
I noticed lots of dog suit on beach area, so maybe more trash cans would help people be less lazy.
Update 10/01/18 -  this area was completely flooded during recent hurricane. Check with the town for conditions before going here

They recently added a really nice new covered patio area with fireplace to the north and expanded other seating areas. They occasionally are having music and food trucks.
Their wines are good with a nice variety. I'd love to buy their chocolate wine sauce but have to cut down on sugars. Will definitely return whenever I visit Swan Creek valley.

This is a new addition via the Piedmont Land Conservancy. There are 2 nice loop trails through the woods. There's a nice  picnic area and restroom. A new trail along the creek is in the planning stages. I forget if you can launch canoe or kayaks here so check their Web site.

Great view but very little space for pulling over, plus it's on a hill near a curve. Pay close attention when pulling out.
Update: heard a rumor that the road in the area is being expanded. Not sure when construction starts. Maybe check with DOT and be wary or construction

Pretty, easy trail through woods. A few hills with about 50 foot elevation change. Decent restroom in parking lot and picnic tables at parking lot, and one on the trail.  Worth going back to if live nearby. The marsh area is the starting place of the Haw river

There are some nice trails through the woods. The trail in the marsh  dead ended when the map showed it as making a loop. The historic buildings are nice and the signs explaining the history  are good. The visitor center was closed so can't rate it

Nice trails through the woods  and into campus. Close to the garden and stores. There are good restaurants nearby - Village tavern and the Silo. Since there are several ponds, mosquitoes can sometimes be a problem. Reynolda House museum is nearby.
North end of park has massive construction underway. Not sure if south end ok now. Lake level very high so lots of beach erosion along the lake. Almost no beach left at Ravine Drive in Highland Park.

Great overlook to watch sunrise and enjoy eastern view of the mountains. A campground and picnic area are nearby.
Watch out for deer along the road.
A few more benches would be nice. Nice paved pathway, good playground for young children, and soccer fields. Nice park for 1.8 mile loop walk.
The facility is nice, great overlook and restroom. There's a few picnic tables but no shade. The trail is nice but more benches would be great
Beautiful park with lots of trails and picnic areas to choose from. Nice visitors center where you can rent kayaks. Great views of the lake.

Awesome museum hidden in the middle of Elkhart. It was bigger than I thought and will easily take you a couple of hours if you read most/all of the stuff inside as well as venture out into the yard and walk up and down the tracks and see everything out there as well.

In addition to all of the stuff to see and read, it's cheap to boot. Only $6/adult and $5/kid.

Great place to come for auto buffs just looking or looking to buy/sell.  Great collection of movie cars and some props and a bunch of various artificats from different wars in the special war museum section. Retro camper museum and multiple buildings in their antique mall. Easily a full days adventure.

Nice park with some walking paths and playground equipment for the kids. Pokemon hunters - a nice handful of stops to loiter around. Pop downtown for a quick bite or to the movie theater for a summer flick all without having to drive anywhere since everything is in close proximity.

One of many great parks in MKE. On the smaller side but still a couple hours of enjoyment on the trails. The best part is of course the stream in the valley heading towards the lake with a bunch of bridges crossing back and forth over the stream. Picturesque no matter the season.

Awesome zoo. Bonus: many of the animals have indoor exhibits as well so you can see a lot of the animals year 'round. For the last week of December, the Zoo has free admission (you only pay ~$12 for parking) making it a great time to go. (read: very little people there).

Fun little winery in Cedarburg.

During the busier times this place can get slammed. But when it's calm and quiet, chat with the employees and enjoy the quaint atmosphere.

When the temps are lower, try the spiced wine. 👌🏻

A great trail to hike and a ton to see. If you want to get to the base of the big fall, be prepared for some heavy maneuvering through multiple giant fallen tree heaps and steep climbing. But the reward is worth it.

Who doesn’t like scenic backdrops, water, and lighthouses. Take an hour and walk out to the lighthouse and/or along the beach. It’s calming. The water along the pier out to lighthouse is insanely clear to boot.
Nice big park in northern Indiana with a decent amount of trails and lots of outdoor space for activities. Tons of Picnic pavilions and other stuff to lounge around on a hot summer day as well.
Nice little park south of town. It’s not super huge but it’s pretty wooded and the trails are nice. Scenic. Disc golf course is decent as well. Most holes are fairly technical given the trees.
Cool little museum in Ft Wayne. Overall 1-1.5 hours max to walk through and see/read everything. Lots of cool, old firefighting gear and pictures from decades past.
Great little car museum in South bend with a rich history. 2-3 hours if you take some time to see each car and exhibits in the history museum adjacent to it.
A great little museum in Elkhart priced decently and one that doesn't take all day to get through. ~1-2 hours. A lot of awesome blasts from the past.
Awesome gem hiding out in the middle of a field in central Indiana. Tours available. Sad to see so much has already been lost over the years.
Awesome fort on the bluff overlooking Mackinaw. It’s a little bit of a hike (twice as far if you don’t take the steps) but worth it.
A great place to visit no matter the season. Lots of cool stuff to see and nature to explore. Bring the family or come alone.
Nice place to walk, walk the dog, bike, Pokemon hunting, have a picnic and simply enjoy the outside with some nice scenery.
One of many great parks in Indiana. Plenty of space to roam and attached to Bertrand so you can continue the adventure.
Fun place to kill an hour. I wish there were more animals as well but as is, for plants, it's potentially a playground.
Great state park to hike. Picturesque with the trails, the lake, and the other quarry and a couple of small waterfalls.
Lots of trails to hike with different scenery. Exploring the dry creek beds / finding the waterfalls is a lot of fun.
One of many fantastic parks around MKE. This one has picnic areas and a great view of the lake with a sandy beach
Awesome park with lots of trails that aren't just a boring, flat path. Woods and trees and curvy paths oh my!
A nice museum in downtown MKE. Plenty to see. If you take your time, plan on a good 3-5 hours to see it all.
Cool place to visit or hike around in all seasons.  May - November you can go high up to the scenic tower

Great experience from climbing the lighthouse. Fantastic spot for photographers. Worth all steps! Kind work from volunteers and it was a pleasant surprise for the kids to receive a real useful activity book targeting kids from toddlers to second grade. Sad part was all the micro garbage dragged to the shore. If someone thinks styrofoam and plastic in general are not a problem, just watch what the currents bring to this area of the Lake Michigan... Time to compromise to reduce plastic consumption and disposal in no other than landfills.

Little gem of this neighborhood! Ample space for events and looks well maintained. Little shelter not so many trees. Ideal in spring or fall but hot during summer time. Big, two mostly new playground for kids 2 to 10. Different climbing structures. Infant and regular swings. No water fountain or portable potty. Few picnic tables and benches, it looks like grilling is not allowed. Two tennis courts nearby. Parking looks pretty limited. One bike rack close to the playground.

Great park. Maintenance could be better such as improving bathroom doors or switching to a water fountain with cold water/or bottle filling during the summer. Artificial turf is quite suitable to infants starting to crawl but it gets extremely warm during sunny days. The sand box used to have a water fountain, now it's dry all the time. It would be awesome if there's some budget to remodel that area. It would be great to include some shadow (tree/canopy) there.

Awesome beach, not too crowded on weekdays. Very clean bathroom facilities. A nearby sandbox is complemented with a big size playground structure ideal for climbing. A section of the playground is dedicated for toddlers. Small paved path for bikes and walkers some paths for hiking. The water park has had a history of erratic opening time so call ahead unless you have a anual pass. The disc golf area is being upgraded a little.
likes: Paved paths for biking and walking

reviews_attraction.text: Don't go for the kid's playground but for the view. It's a great spot for stone skipping or simply walking around. Recently paved, the pathway can be flooded pretty easily. Several picnic tables and grills, brand new. Accessible very close by car. Open spaces are suitable for playing outdoor games. If you go after a big rain most of the grass will be muddy. Sometimes I've found ticks so you just need to be careful.

It's a great zoo. If you live within 70 miles and have kids, you'll get a great time during the whole year. There's usually something changing so you might not get bored visiting every couple of months. Usually very well organized, staff is quite attentive and honest servicing their visitors. Food is ok but it can improve. During Covid-19, cleanliness has been taken seriously so please follow the signs and rules

Interesting place for kids and curious visitors. Real, life species from Michigan habitat. Bones and feathers to touch and feel. Kind staff able to address your questions and decent clean restrooms. This space is ideal as a meeting point. Several trails start from there and they are quite well identified. Maps are also available. There are vending machines outside if you forgot bringing something to drink.

Worth to try but only when it's free (Ford days). Lot of the exhibitions are broken or malfunctioning (almost a half I tried). Not so much science on these exhibitions (they are minimally interactive). Pressing buttons requires no brain. It was not pleasant to wait in line outside while it was 24F when this museum enforced visitors to get tickets in advance. It looks staff doesn't plan too much.

It's definitely a typical township park worth to try if you are nearby. Free if you're biking but some fees apply coming by car. Splash Park and wooden playground are well built and kept. You  an bring your own food but concessions are available. With exception of the beach, there are plenty of shaded areas but not so many trees. You can rent a kayak or bring your own too.

We entered as a part of the passport science museum. However, this looks like a military museum and most of the exhibitions in the two floors are not interactive. Recommended for kids interested in these artifacts. It worths the effort and staff is quite attentive. Price for general admission is in the expensive side, specially if you bring a family with you.

If you were a kid you would like this park. It has ducks, geese, swans, turtles, playgrounds, paved and scenery paths, wooden bridges, a big sandbox, good food from the snack shop... you can bike, have a picnic, rent a spot for a party, canoeing, walk, jog, even swim if you like. It hosts a lot of events in the summer. Parking can be difficult sometimes.

Great university museum with several exhibitions changing during the year. There's something new to see and do there every season. I'd recommend tours and family activities. Attentive staff, pretty well organized. It's a museum suitable for kids (ample spaces) but there's not so many interactive environments.

Huge park with 5 trails averaging 1 mile each, mostly easy accessible. Two entrances with ample parking spaces. Three ponds. Bathroom & water fountain. Small playground. Great for group activities (there are several pavilions). Nice for flying kites (strong winds, not a hill but open areas).

Great neighborhood park for kids up to 6 years old, mostly shady during the summer. It has a merry-go-round, sandbox with toys, a decent basketball court, a volleyball sand court, a playground structure, infants and kids swings, and a nice moebius climbing structure. No water fountain.

Nice park. Wooden playground for all ages and few sand boxes. The city should install more water fountains since there's only one and it was broken at the time we visited this park. The sprays pace wasn't open Memorial day. Looks like it needs repairs.

Great park for a stroller/toddler walk. Nice layout with a stream all around. Good for all seasons. A new water play pump was installed a little bit down the mill house so it's great for entertaining kids and grown-ups.

Decent park. Four baseball fields, a skate park, pool with water slide, shelters, parking lot, lot of port a potty. The shelter and the little playground are in bad shape. Lot of garbage everywhere but functional.

Awesome place for let kids experiment and get tired. Some exhibitions require better maintenance. Most of the museum is quite entertaining and educational except the DTE fuel-exhibition which has no sense at all.
Beautifully kept farm with kid friendly, interactive activities for kids. Not so much shade, I have been in warm summers and cold springs and there's always something to discover.
Overpriced. Parents don't encourage kids to keep toys in each area so it's common to find everything mixed across the museum. Not so much educational value.
I did not feel comfortable with my visit to this museum: staff looks like a marketing agency and even parking is paid! Finding a place was a nightmare...
Weird park with a skate ring and pool. We did found people sleeping there. Apparently this park has not had any maintenance in a decade.
Nice park with a  great layout. A playground for little ones, toddlers and big toddlers. Heated restrooms, pavilion and a small pond.
No trails but nice playground for toddlers around three year old.  Tennis and baseball courts. Water fountain and portable bathroom.
Nice, shady park. Playground, few picnic tables and restrooms. Toddlers will love it. Good for the hot days of summer. Sandbox.

This is the last operating farm in Queens County . It has various educational programs & tours and is a great way to teach kids about nature. In addition to the crops, they have all kinds of farm animals- sheep, goats etc. that are fun to see.

Many school groups came here pre pandemic for that reason ; hopefully these programs will start up again soon. The staff at the farm are very conscious of proper procedures in terms of the pandemic. Most of the people, though unfortunately certainly not all, were properly wearing masks and social distancing

In addition to the farm part, this time of year a pumpkin patch is made where you can buy pumpkins  and show kids different types  of pumpkins. Its  a lot of fun to go there and see kids wandering thru the
pumpkins.

They also have a giant maze  made out of corn- "The amazing maize maze". This definitely  needs adult supervision but its a great family activity to figure out your way thru the maze , get all the clues and go out the exit . It will take you over an hour  even if you have a better sense of direction than I do.

Finally there are these very large , say 10 feet tall or more, flower sculptures (not sure what to call them) made out of flowers. My favorite was the 10 foot tall coffee cup made out of flowers . The floral show and maze are both a few dollars for admission while the pumpkin patch and the farm itself are free.

Obviously its all outdoors so I wouldn't go when its cold or raining. Wear clothes' that can get dirty because its a farm- someone when I was there was complaining to their companion that their white high heels were getting dirty. Going to the Queens Farm Museum is a great place to take kids but adults enjoy it as much as the kids if not more.

This is the New York branch of a Scandinavian photography museum. It was recently opened in NY, a few months ago. The building was formerly some sort of church building.

My first thought when I saw that on their brochure was that should have taken pictures of what changes were necessary to the building. Unfortunately, they didn't do this.

Each floor had a different theme, with several smaller exhibits on certain floors. The top floor was photographs of celebrities, with the floor underneath glitzy photos of women. Neither of these were especially engaging to me.

I found more interesting and engaging  exhibits of African Americans in African Garb. There was also an exhibit of the aftereffect of mining operations on the land being mined. Many of the pictures from this exhibit were from Iceland.

There was also some interesting pictures about the interaction between nannies and the children they take care of. A group of photographs from an Israeli photographer with biblical names were amazing and my personal favorite exhibit.

The museum was well worth attending. It's quite expensive. There is a half price discount now. Like me, you will find some of the exhibits more interesting than others. However, the museum is a great way to be exposed to all different types of photography.
likes: Cultural representation (African Americans in African Garb)

reviews_attraction.text:
This state park  is a pedestrian (bike and people only) bridge over the Hudson River, from Poughkeepsie, New York in Duchess County  to the little town of Highland  in Ulster County. Especially this year when we cant leave our own state and are looking for outdoor locations, this is a great place to spend a few hours.  Free parking is available and you can take Amtrak or Metro North from New York City or various stops in Upstate New York.

We took their suggested route, from the Poughkeepsie train Station through this Park  and back to the FDR bridge . Its approximately 4 miles. There are plenty of places to sit on the bridge if you want to look out and take a break and at the end of it, before either turning around or going to the other bridge  there are bathrooms and water and soda machines.

The bridge back is not  pedestrian only and there is a narrow walkway, so some people may prefer just staying in the Walkway over the Hudson Park.  The park is completely outside and its over the Hudson (obviously) so it gets quite hot and during the winter, quite cold at times. Be sure to bring plenty of water. The panels on the bridge give a good explanation of the area, when the bridge was built, etc and if you want more, there is a web tour you can download.

This is one of the touristy things you feel silly doing but feel you have to do as a first time tourist to Key West. A large metallic sign that looks like a marine buoy is located as the point that supposedly is the southernmost point in the US.  People go and have their picture taken at the sign.

There is often a wait of  a half hour or more to have your picture taken near the sign. If you don't want to wait, you can sit near the sign and not touch it but be near it and have your picture taken that way.

Southernmost Point is a big tourist thing in Key West. There is a convenience store called Southernmost point convenience store selling southernmost point trinkets, southernmost point bar, t-shirts, etc.   It amusing that actually the Navy has a base that is not easily accessible but actually is the true southernmost point. There are rocks near the sign that are actually more southernmost. Its part of the fun so go get your picture taken at the official (but not actual) southernmost point in the US.

The Queens Botanical Garden is next to Flushing Meadows Corona Park on Main Street in Flushing, Queens. You can get there by bus or subway though in both cases its a bit of walk from the bus or & train stop. Its a bit confusing when you get to the entrance to the Garden- the parking entrance and attendant is also for walk ins.

This Garden is open now despite the pandemic as it is outside, except for the visitors building. The roof of that building is open and gives you a great view of the area as well as explanations about "green roofs". Unlike most of the places that have reopened, you don't need to make a reservation in advance, so its a great thing to do on the spur of the moment when  you are looking for something to do.

It takes about an hour or two to walk the entire garden though I see that many peoples stay longer, siting  in one of the gardens, resting, relaxing  and meditating. If the weather is nice, the Queens Botanical Garden is a great place to go and is highly recommended.

This art museum in New York City  was recently extensively enlarged and renovated. Previously, it was extremely crowded , so much so that you often could not get close enough to the art to look at it.

MOMA has also changed the way it presents art. Previously, art was displayed chronologically within general art types- e.g. impressionism, etc.

Its now being displayed within individual galleries with an overall theme.- e.g.abstract expressionism, design, etc.There are more mixing of say photography and sculpture as well as more less well known artists , women and minorities.

The presentation gives you a fuller picture than a chronological view does . The explanation by the art seems much better and there are ways to access explanations about the work from the internet on your phone and on audio devices they give out.

This is a unique museum. Firstly, it is housed in an aircraft carrier that was used in the Vietnam War and other wars. Secondly, they have as exhibits airplanes and have exhibits about planes , other military equipment and have a new exhibit related to the space program

However, admission is quite expensive. In addition the hours of the museum as listed on the website sometimes don't match the actual hours. I once checked the hours on their website and then went to the Intrepid, only to find out it closed early that day because of a special event. Other people who had been effected told me it had happened previously to them.

Finally, the museum often has large school groups that can be quite noisy. if you can, going at a time when it is less likely to have large school groups is a good time.

The Queens Zoo  is located in Flushing Meadows Corona Park. The Zoo has recently opened. You need to make an on line reservation and get timed tickets.  On a nice day like today, the Zoo gets quite crowded, even with timed tickets. There was a long waiting line to get in when we left.

This zoo is much smaller than the Bronx Zoo. It is about the same size as the Central Park Zoo. Its a great way to spend a few hours on a nice day.  They have many activities for kids but it is also great for adults.

In addition to the main part of the zoo, there's also a petting zoo. For a quarter you can buy pellets to feed some of the animals. There is no extra charge for the Petting Zoo

This is a nice park on 23rd Street , up to 25th, near 5th Avenue in Manhatttan.  There is also a nice playground here for kids. The park itself has areas for sitting and picnicing .

There is a Shake Shack fast food resturant near the entrance to the park and various other fast food resturants close by. The subway (R, F, 6 train) is not too far away. Parking can be hard to find but especially on the week  end can be found and there are parking lots not too far away if necessary.

Madison Sqyare Paek is by the standards of New York City Parks not too noisy orcrowded- I have been here several times .A visit, while you are in the neighborhood, is recommended.

This art museum is in Flushing Meadows Corona Park in Queens, New York. Their is also an entrance off the Grand Central Parkway.It was originally built for the 1939 Worlds Fair. From 1946-1950 it was the home of the UN General Assembly.

The building was also used for the 1964 Worlds Fair. The Panorama of the City of New York was built for the 1964 Worlds Fair; it is still at this museum. This is a large scale map of New York City with every large building in the NYC (as of 1964- it was updated several years ago) shown.

Its great fun to pick out your building . Even if your not an art museum fan, its worth going to this one for the Panorama.

This is the building  at the Bronx Botanical Garden where the Holiday Train Show takes place. The indoor flowers and plants are here as well. During the fall and winter, the Conservatory  is the main location at the Bronx Botanical Gardens, since of course the outdoor plants don't survive.

In addition to the trains itself the Train Show has models of many of the more prominent buildings in the greater New York City area. Its amazing to see these models .There are also many wonderful plants in the conservancy. Although kids  love the trains and will be amazed by what they see in the Conservancy, it s also worth going if you don't have kids.

Hopefully this small amusement park in Flushing Meadows Corona Park  in Flushing Queens opens up this summer. It is near  the petting zoo and the Queens Zoo. New York Hall of Science is also in FMCP.

All of these are great places to take kids  on a nice spring or summer day. Fantasy Forest Amusement Park is for smaller children, up to about 7 or 8 years old. There are several cute rides in this amusement park and some arcade type games. its not very expensive.

No one will mistake this amusement park for Great Adventure or Disneyworld but for small children its really a great way to spend a few hours.

The Baseball Hall of Fame is the location of records for Major League Baseball. It's a great museum for fans of baseball.

The exhibits at the museum are pretty detailed so if you are not both at least somewhat knowledgeable about baseball and interested in it, this museum is not for you.

The town of Cooperstown , where the Baseball Hall of Fame is located is a lovely town . Their are all kinds of baseball memorabilia stores and baseball exhibits in Cooperstown. There is also several art and culture related museums, refineries and breweries, so its a nice place to spend a few days in.

This is the New York office of the Federal Reserve Bank. They have extensive out reach programs to explain what this government agency does.

These activities include a display about what the Fed does. One of the things they do is hold the gold assets of various governments. A tour of their display on their various activities and a tour of the vaults where they hold the gold is available.

People have to sign up well in advance - several months at least- for this tour. The tours are a lot of fun, especially the gold vault part is a lot of fun. It's free.

This is a wonderful modern art museum in Long Island City, Queens

Currently, all the galleries are showing works by
Iraqi artists and deal with the Iraq war and it's aftermath

The museum is free for New York City and I think New York State residents. Due to its affiliation with MoMA, it is also free for people who have a recent MoMA ticket.

This is an underappreciated little gem of a museum. I n most places in the world, this museum would be regard as the best art museum in the city. Here, its often forgotten but shouldn't be.

I was in FMCP yesterday. Most of the people in the park  were responsibly social distancing, though I saw some teenagers had apparently climbed over the small fence around the Jurassic Playground and were on the equipment.

The playgrounds, the peddleboat concession and the bicycle concession were all closed. However, many people were running around the park, having a great time. I saw lots of kids in strollers in the ball field which is now closed for group play. People with kids should still come to the park.

This is a park in Manhattan on 42nd Street between 5th and 6th avenue. The park is often crowded with people from the office buildings in the area, especially around lunch time. It's small but a great little park.

In the summer the park has movie night's and various other activities. In the winter the park has an ice skating ring.

This park is one of the top tourist attractions in New York City but is also great for New Yorkers.

This museum in Seattle has a series of exhibits about computers, computer systems and artificial intelligence.

The exhibits starts with the first computers made during WWII. They explain , better than I have ever seen it before, how computers really work. This museum has activities for kids. The Living Computer Museum is a great place to go as part of a trip to Seattle and is highly recommended.

This small park is at the end of a approximately half mile walk from the Walkway over the Hudson Park. It's  a good place to see the Park and the bridge over the Hudson. The Johnson Park is right next to the FDR Bridge.

There are some explanatory panels about the area and the various parks. There is not much else in this Park- it's essentially just a way of getting from one bridge to another.

I've been here for a Billy Joel concert, to take my grandkids to Sesame Street live, etc. It's right next to Penn station, so there are plenty of mass transit options

Street parking is minimal. Lots close by are expensive but prices decline a few blocks away.

It's certainly not the prettiest arena around . People come for the concerts or whatever, not for the building.

This museum is the leading design museum in New York and one of the leading ones I'm the world . It's housed in a old mansion. Its worth going to the museum just to examine the building.

Surprisingly even though it's a Smithsonian, there is a admission fee- it's not a suggestion it's a substantial required amount. However it's well worth the charge and a great museum.

Last year I took a tour of City Hall.
I presume its still closed because of the pandemic. Hopefully it will reopen soon.

For people who are interested in local politics and in history, the tour is great. The people giving the tour are volunteers , often retirees who have tremendous knowledge about City Hall and local governence.

This park is on Yellowstone Boulevard near Queens Boulevard. It has a playground with equipment appropriate for smaller children and another for older kids.

The park is behind an elementary school. It's relatively clean for a NYC Park. The neighborhood and the park itself is fairly safe.

This public park is on 14th street in Manhattan. There is  always a lot going on.

The playground is divided into an area for children below 5 and 5 and above. It's a small play area but has some of the best playground equipment in New York City. Its one of the best parks in the city.

This structure was built for the World's Fair back in 1964. It was used for rock concerts and other events in the 1960s and 1970s.

Since then it has not been used very much.

The price was steeper than I liked because I didn't prepurchase tickets. Ticket buying online requires a set reservation time, and driving in from Austin, we weren't quite sure when we'd actually arrive. So we paid full price for the first available tour once we'd arrived. Coming here first thing on a weekday during the school year was a great idea. We ended up on a tour with one other family, and it made for an almost private tour vibe. Our tour guide was Jessica, and she was very informative about the history and geology of the caverns. As for the caverns themselves, this has to be the best cave I've ever visited. Simply stunning! The various rooms within the cavern each had their own draw. My favorite may have been Sherwood Forest or possibly the room she called Purgatory. It's hard to pick a favorite. I kept being amazed by each new room. I found I wasn't prepared for the humidity inside. It's as close to raining as you can get, and you may look like you survived a rainstorm when you finally exit. Just go with it, it's worth it.

The trails are poorly marked, poorly maintained, and loads of trash. A total lack of trail maintenance makes several of the trails you find unpassable. This has caused quite a bit of trailblazing and subsequent erosion. I wish I'd brought a bag to help carry out some of the trash. Also, it's interesting to be on one of the few marked trails, only to run into a sign claiming I was about to enter private property, with a threat of prosecution. I'm not sure how that happens in county owned land. Trail marking needs improvement and consistency. Anyway, it was good to get out in the woods for a hike, and an additional workout swatting bugs.

Didn't end up completing the hike because it was getting late and we needed to get back home. The trail has no shade, and you're walking on rock faces most of the hike. It starts out through a section of the park that burned several years ago. It was a freak mid 80s day when we went, so we hadn't planned on going through water so quickly. So we are saving completion of this one for Fall. The loop trail, and ice cave road, up to this point are easy hikes, just a bit steep at points. The Verkeerderkill Falls trail adds 4 miles (out and back) to your day.

The trails are geared towards runners, bicyclists, park vehicles, and general dog walking. They have a few offshoot trails that aren't maintained, and I've found tend to house a collection of debris including TV's, picnic tables, milk crates, cigarette butts, and general trash. I feel it's somewhat open border to the surrounding neighborhood contributes to this issue. If you stay on the gravel 'trail', it's a beautiful hike around Belmont Lake.

Beautiful preserve. Most of the trails are fairly well marked, although a recent storm has left part of the red trail unpassable near fishing post 16a. I hate going off trail, but had no choice at that point. There appears to be plenty of wildlife for the avid bird watcher, although it was a bit limited today to mostly swan and the annoying geese. I'm definitely coming back to hike the 8.4 mile blue trail at some point.
likes: Long hiking trail (8.4 mile blue trail)
dislikes: Limited wildlife variety (mostly swan and geese)

reviews_attraction.text: I've been to the Cincy zoo many times, but recently made my first visit as an adult. A few things have changed in the almost four decades since I last visited the zoo. I remember there being more cats. Also the hills are much easier now. The enclosures seem smaller. The primates seem defeated. I couldn't help but wonder if the enclosures were too small. I still enjoyed my time at the zoo.

Great place for a hike, and to explore the woods. The trails are fairly easy to hike, with the only challenge being not getting lost. On that, grab a map from the nature center. It has mileage listed for each trail, but I'm not sure that it's accurate. But it is good for navigation. My favorite part of hiking the site is the trail marking. It works very well.

Beautiful site to hike, even in the winter. It might be the better time to visit as the tourist population of the island is so low. They have some fairly easy hikes, at varying distances to choose from. I think we ended up hiking around 6 miles all counted. The only real difficulty was how muddy some parts of the trail were, due to the recent rains.

It's the north shore starting point for the Nassau-Suffolk Greenbelt Trail. If you start on this end, be prepared for the steepest and most challenging portion of the trail. If you only hike out to the first road you come to, and back, it makes for a quick ~2 mile hike that you can complete in under an hour (depending on your pace).

I love visiting this place and exploring the gardens and surrounding property. Unfortunately, the house is closed for much needed restorations, but that is also a good thing. I hadn't been in a couple of years, and they've added quite a few kinetic sculptures since I was last here. Some of them are very interesting.

Beautiful scenery to be had, and decent hiking in the area. We hiked over, once, from River Bend, and it was a nice hike. On our latest trip, we got to see it after a heavy rainstorm. Just awe inspiring. After seeing the difference, after just one rainstorm, the record flood stage signage seems totally doable.

I like visiting college and university art museums, as you're never really sure what you might encounter in the collections. My alma mater is no exception. So to visit the collection at Vassar was also treat. It's a small collection of of varied works, but they have a little something for nearly everyone.

It's a beautiful place to hike. It's so tranquil once you hike a few yards in. The trails are a bit confusing, and I found it somewhat easy to get on a path that takes you nowhere near the parking lot. Parking is scarce, at only 6 spaces, but I think it helps keep the site peaceful.

We stopped in to hike over to Great Falls. It's an easy ~2 mile hike over, as long as you find parking near the river. So you could get a beautiful 4 mile hike in, by parking at Riverbend. Even as packed with people as it was when we stopped by, the hike was fairly peaceful.

I parked near this park once, Google keeps asking me to review this place now. It looked like it could be a good park for dog walking. It looks pretty close to lake Anne, or the river, or whatever that technically is over here. People I know in the area love the place.

I like visiting here at least once per season just to observe the changes to the various gardens. There is plenty of land to hike and explore, but in the deep of winter you may just want to visit the greenhouse to see the orchids in bloom.

It seems it's mostly just a pass through for the Fall Creek pathway, but it has some poorly maintained offshoot trails that are a nice hike. It's also very loud due to proximity to 465, so it's not a good place for tree therapy.

I've never been able to justify to myself paying to get closer to this site than the gate. The view from there is sufficient, as it's just a lighthouse. The real beauty, to me, is the shore and state park that surround it.
I stopped in for the restroom, but ended up learning a great deal about the area, including its fishing history, from a volunteer that was also sharing his personal family photos and memorabilia.
Very informative museum about the life and escapades of a founding father. It doesn't cover his more salacious escapades, as you'd expect, but I enjoyed seeing a glass armonica up close.
It's undergoing some much needed restoration work. The grounds outside are beautiful. And I'm sure the views of the sound were great before the trees grew up and blocked it.
The trails here tend to have great views of the sound and the various birds that thrive off it. It's also my favorite north shore beach for swimming.
I wasn't expecting much, but I was pleasantly surprised. I also enjoyed touring the live history of the surrounding buildings.
Quaint, yet very informative. I also enjoyed the living museum aspect of this and the stories of Betsy's day-to-day life.
Beautiful, but after a long day of walking the city the steps are less appealing. There are great views from the top.

Archaeological History museum, nature trails, golf and country club.
The museum in the country club has a lot of info.
I did not look around the country club but apparently they serve alcohol.  There are nice restrooms at the entrance and a wonderful museum with the history of the different people that lived here long before us.
12.00 fee to get in beyond the gates...you can get to the canoe launch without paying as it is on the opposite side of the street.
We went to the very last trail which is to the actual Shawnee Lookout. This trail is covered with pawpaw trees which were bearing fruit.  It is well manicured and there are a couple of benches along the trail and at the end. It is a moderate uphill climb but mostly downhill on the way back which takes you across a flat area at the top of the ridge.

The Vista overlooks 275 South and a train trestle bridge  275 South is over the Ohio River and the trestle bridge is over the Great Miami.  They call this area the oxbow because of the bend in the river there.

IDNR could do a lot better with this place.  There are some nice things about it.  They have a campground with nice showers and a beach but it is surrounded by Canada geese (an invasive species Introduced here by DNR).  There are no trails here.
There is a dock to fish on that is wheel chair accessible, an archery range and a gun range.
They have an awesome boat ramp but the courtesy docs are too short for houseboats.  The marina is privately owned and doesn't offer much.  Pontoon and jon boat rentals, worms, minnows, gas, candy bars and pop.  They could do so much more as well.  Lots of gravel instead of concrete.  Doesn't seem to ramp up in quality from year to year like a good business would do.  They need to go to Lake Cumberland to see a real marina with super long courtesy docks, a well stocked marine store with a restaurant, etc.

Wonderful experience.  Ride an antique steam powered train on a regular or special excursion.  They have trips that stop for dinner at the Laurel Hotel or all the way to historic Metamora for a day of shopping.
They have special trips as well, Mother's Day, Father's Day, Memorial Day,  Murder Mystery Train, Wild West Train, Labor Day, Music Fest,  Fall Foliage and Winter Holiday trips.
