The historic rain Depot has a nice gift shop and adequate parking in the area.  Most of the neighboring businesses, Courthouse, Banks, Senior Center, are usually closed when the train is in operation.

Nearby - Historic Museum with cars made in Connersville,
Rips Barbecue (ice cream), CVS, Brian's Book Store & Coffee (sandwiches and pastries), Daniel Girls restaurant (American, lots of seating), El Caballo Blanco, excellent Mexican Restaurant.

Thoroughly enjoyed this cruise.  The mountains surround you as you enter black canyon and head towards the Hoover Dam.  There is an pre-recorded narrator who gives all of the historical and geographical information while you ride.
There are 3 levels.  The second level has snacks and a full bar.
Ordered the "Best Damn Margarita".  It was pretty but too sweet, like a popsicle.
The staff was super friendly and the boat took off on time.  The ride is smooth.  It was very hot so we ducked in and out of the AC.
The photo opportunities abound as the mountain views are unobstructed to you across Lake Mead.  As well they take your picture before you board and have a framed photo for purchase at the end of the cruise.
Parking is down a gravel road so don't drive your black vehicle here.

27 acres of chill.  This park has several playgrounds including one just for smaller kids, a water park, 4 covered pavilions, basketball courts, a community building with gym that can be rented, an amphitheater, half mile race track with horse stables, shooting range, an historical covered bridge to explore, lots of shade, picnic tables and barbecue grills.
Good place to stop and eat lunch or watch the kids play on the playground.   No alcohol permitted,.

Food was good. Wait was normal.  Service was good.  They have a lot of common Mexican favorites.
Subbed regular salsa without saying anything bc they were out of the fruit salsa.
Their complimentary salsa is big chunks of tomato and onion...not easy to dip.
Weakest Margarita in town. Many from our crowd commented on the weak margarita. Says best margarita in town but Bubba Gump's got them beat.
dislikes: Complimentary salsa not easy to dip

reviews_attraction.text:
Nice park. The kids playground was good. Had a real set of monkey bars, twin straight slides, very tall curly slide, old school merry go round, swings and baby swings.
The best blessing was the restrooms were open.
Pavilion.
Pretty well maintained.
Needs a bit of attention...swings, slides and merry go round need filled in to avoid puddling...faucet wouldn't turn off in men's room.

Enjoyed paying respect to this man who fought for more than just to be a World Champion.
He has a very stately memorial with a bench. Well manicured and cared for. There is tasteful landscaping as well as flowers left by an adoring fan.
It would be over the top if there were a life size bronze statue of the Champ.

I'm sure there is a lot to do here, boating, bike rental.  Did get some info from the friendly people at the marina store.  Not much for finding a quick trail.  One of the trails is sloped bush hogged path along the  lake.  Difficult to walk on unless you have one leg shorter than the other.

Nice spot to launch a boat, take a bike ride or walk. Plenty of parking, long spots for boat trailers.
There are spots to sit on a log and look over the water or fish. A girl had a stringer with perch and sheepshead.
Good spot for birding.
There was a portolet at the end of the lot.

Only Y Bridge in the world.  Had to drive it and take a walk.  The water moves very swiftly over the dam and under the bridge.  Love the impressive light poles.  It looks good on the city of Zaynesville how well they have preserved this historic asset.

Amazing park. Great for bird watching. Peaceful drive around the entire peninsula with many water views of Lake Erie, marshes, beaches, pulloffs and trails. Nice bike trail all the way around. Campground at entrance.Rent bikes and kayaks locally.

Enjoyable place to sit on the steps and watch the world go around.  The monument itself is nice and has many impressive statues about it.  There is a war museum inside and you can ride an elevator to the top for a view of the city.  Enjoy.

Nice place to just park and eat lunch or take the kids to the amazing playground.  There is a small lake and an impressive statue from the Daughters of the Revolution.  Many areas to walk, or play Frisbee or picnic.

Wonderful place to hike.  Dogs allowed on leash.  Nice restrooms near the parking lot/entrance.  4 miles of trails.  The waterfall was serene and the red buds on red bud trail were in bloom when we went.

Nice walking / biking trails through thick canopy of pine and other native trees. The surface is easy to walk on and we'll maintained. Good for kids and dogs. Did not see any poison ivy along the sides.

Easy short hike to get to a  beautiful trail and waterfall. Some parts have a boardwalk. There are stairs on the boardwalk. You can also get a above the falls on the bridge above. Parking at entrance.

Nice local history museum. McFarland, Army Jeep and other vehicles made in Connersville. Pioneer display, military display.
Very well kept and continuously evolving. Great asset to the community.
Great trail for walking, running, biking it fishing along the river. Main trail is paved but there are unimproved access trails to the river. Can park near the playground and make a loop.

Interesting history about how it was created with dynamite and changed the course of the river.
Parking lot. Also a trail head for Meigs Mountain Trail.
Be careful with small children.
Beautiful landmark and tribute to our veterans. Auditorium, meeting rooms and museum. Safe place, officers inside, they don't frisk you but they don't allow bags, food or drinks.
Loved the shaded trails, benches with scenic views of the water. Great for birding. Connects to the boardwalk and main multi-use trail.
Enjoyed the drive and many little stops along the way. Zubrinski's point, Devil's Golf Course, Artist's Pallette, great salt basin.
Nice pace to walk or ride a bike. The path crosses the river to an old Fort. Miles of manicured trails. Handicapped accessible
Park has a stern wheeler boat at one end and soldier statues at the other end.  Nice view of the water and Y-bridge.

The roses in the spring are just breathtaking! I love how each rose is labeled with its name and type. It is like a rose lesson learning about the varieties of flowers! The pictures I attached are all from July. The flowers are beautiful most of the year though. There are multiple pavilions to house events. I frequently see weddings and quinceaneras at the grand terrace. People are always around taking pictures for various occasions. It is definitely a perfect spot for pictures!!

Nice little park for a walk. Big pond to walk around and enjoy the view.  Became a park about a century ago after the last reunion of the Grand Army of the Republic (and even a few Confederates). It was a farm before that, and was the site of a Civil War hospital, I think. The city recently decided to build a large indoor aquatic center here, and construction will begin this winter. There will be major disruptions for about a year and a half. Enjoy it while you can.

We recently had out of town guests and were looking for interesting sites in Evansville.  We visited this museum and had a wonderful tour.  Kayla gave us a very informative walk through, and we all enjoyed it so much.  Everything on display is super clean and shiny and what a remarkable collection!  We would highly recommend this museum - if you haven't visited it yet, make it a priority.  Kudos to Mr. Bennett for such a top notch addition to Evansville!

so we decided to road trip up to Evansville, Indiana while we lived in the Nashville area. This was not a very large, nor expensive zoo.over the animals, love the exercise walking around the complex where you don't even realize you are even exercising because of the enjoyment.until Fit bit texts you CONGRATS you just walked 5 miles. Best way to exercise, oblivious to It!!! I love the flowers too, there is always GORGEOUS flowers and fauna everywhere..

We have our reunion there. The building is clean and plenty of room, Has a kitchenette that helps. The trails are nice and pond for fishing and swimming.he weather was beautiful and showcased the fall colors. The trails were easy to navigate. The park allows the lodge to be rented for private parties.Matea Park is a great place to get back into nature and just stop and take a minute to relax. Plenty of walking trails to and sights to see

This place is less than 5 minutes away and has a large newer play area that she loves to go to. Also plenty for the rest of the family with lots of walking trails, baseball diamonds, soccer fields, and tennis courts. They even have a splash pad in the summer months so we will definitely be back then as well. What a large well maintained park this is with lots of space to walk, play tennis etc. and a real plus is the restrooms are clean.

I regularly visit WWII ships anytime a city in which I am visiting has one on display. While certainly not the most impressive ship onto which I have ever boarded, the tour guide made the visit most interesting by pointing out many items of interest that one wouldn't see on a self-guided tour. I knew very little about LST ships upon arriving and left with a full understanding of the functionality and history of these craft

Saw Christopher Cross live there. Haven't been there since I was a kid. Super cool venue, tons of seating, great acoustics, beer, wine, food. I wish they'd have bands that might entice a younger crowd - don't get me wrong I love the oldies but the crowd (mostly geriatrics) makes it maybe a little less thrilling for 20 somethings. Great times though, if there's a show you like playing there then definitely go!

This is the place to go if you want a sense of Indy (other than the track in Speedway).  The heart of Indy is found in this circle that was originally intended to be the site of the Governor's Mansion until the then Governor's wife said she would never live there because everyone would be able to see the family's laundry!There are numerous websites that talk about the art and sculpture of the circle.

Love taking my kids here in the summer! They love the playground and the splash pad that is located right in front of the entrance of the zoo!Yes.   Potawatomi Zoo.   It is a great dining a few hours kinda zoo.   Affordable family fun, friendly staff, and a nice mix of animals to see.   Parking can fill up fast,  but if you aren't a lazy butt, there is plenty of Parking on adjacent streets.

During our visit the Scholastic Art & Writing Awards featuring the Gold and Silver Key winning art and writing by students in grades 7-12 from the local area was on display. This was a juried competition and there was fantastic work on display including poetry but the exhibit felt very packed! Loved all the pieces but it probably could have been edited down to better showcase the winners.

The park boasts a beautiful rose garden that is breath-taking in the spring and summer. You will see many weddings taking place here in the warmer months. The park has huge, open grassy areas - great for soccer or to play fetch with your pup. The basketball court/tennis courts are a little dated and rundown but you will still see people using them and enjoying the warm weather.

The food! Each vendor, while offering similar fares, had something unique to offer. Desparados, a long running Ribfest favorite is known for their tender and smoked flavored rib. New is the beef rib. I respect those that prefer beef over pork, but once you get past the gristle which seemed to have a brontosaurus factor, it was that heavy, real talk, the meat was limited.

Legos, and sand tables, and magnet gears oh my! Go on a dinosaur dig, build your own house...Weigh yourself on a giant construction claw or crawl through an enormous nose.  Play a concert on bongos and pipes or  dress up and put on your own theatre production. Wonderful gymboree-like crawling area for babies and toddlers with mats, mirrors, ramps, and obstacles.

Located only a stone's throw from downtown Indy, Eagle Creek is like having a state park in your backyard yet with urban resources easily accessible. We love the 2-3 mike loop that kicks off at the bird watching center and along the way, we pause to enjoy the scenery, listen to the lull of the waves and enjoy the birds. Simple pleasures, you guys.

Having grown up within walking distance of the grave of "Johnny Appleseed" can attest that the site is essentially unchanged. To think of the legend of the man planting apple trees throughout the valley is so  encouraging for growth and spirit. Surroundings fairly tranquil, river nearby. I'd stop if passing by hwy 30 famous unto itself.

Great way to experience a piece of Fort Wayne history! Fun, informative and a great place for adults and children.The History Center has an amazing collection of documents and artifacts that document the history of this geographical area. There is an array of material about the founding of the city. Worth the time and effort! Try it!

This is a nice place to hike - especially in the early spring or late fall. (The insect population is greatly reduced during those seasons). The hiking trails are longer than what they appear so be prepared to do some walking.I absolutely loved Eagle Marsh and how quiet it was. It was beyond beautiful and cannot wait to visit again.

We have a membership which seems to be worth it once you take into consideration parking ($8) and each admission ($28). Kids 2 and under are FREE. Kids love it and with the membership we can go as often as we'd like. Awesome during summer! The zoo is very clean. Staff is always friendly, helpful and knowledgeable about the animals.

I love going here in the winter and spring to enjoy the tropical atmosphere. Makes winter seem a little shorter!I went and had lunch with my son during farm camp and checked out the farmer's market.Good deal's at the farmer's market,definitley a nice place to visit and relax.Good place for a picnic,there kid camp's are really cool.

This museum is a car enthusiasts dream and even offers interesting tidbits for those not as into cars. The museum starts off with wagons and carriages which is very intriguing to see. They give a lot of interesting facts regarding all the exhibits. Even if you're not a car fan, there are still so many interesting historical facts.

So much to offer! I finally made it down to the park on a beautiful, sunny day this spring and I'm so glad I did. There is a ton of green space with nice walking paths that border the river, canal, and through the park. There are lovely spots to sit for a picnic lunch, before or after your visit to the zoo, Victory Field

We drove from Louisville and it was absolutely worth it. We went on a Saturday and it wasn't super busy. Not long waits to enjoy attractions. I had a three year old and five month old. Overall stroller friendly and easy to navigate. Not enough can be said to explain the outdoor space and how awesome it is.

We have been to the Grand Prix, Carb Day, Legends Day, and obviously the Race. We have also been to the Snake Pit before the Race. Every event at IMS has been so incredible. In 2017, we went to the Air Race and I am sad that event is no longer happening. Hopefully, they'll have it there again some day!

This collection is disgustingly good for those who are into modern western art. These people pretty much had it all. Wilson hurley, thomas Hart Benton, single digit cast remingtons. My favorite piece: Shelling Corn by Joseph Sharp. Incredible to see it in person. Check it out!
likes: Specific Artists (e.g., Wilson Hurley, Thomas Hart Benton)
Particular Pieces (e.g., Shelling Corn by Joseph Sharp)

This review is full of useful info for anyone exploring the state park and are wondering about anything concerning the geography of the park and vicinity.

First of all, Google, get your marker in the right place. (Edit: Hey look they got it right :D) The park is 6 miles southeast on Dale Miller road (Decatur J66) and is clearly marked, you cannot miss it. Some signs in the park are misleading, as you do not need to pay for anything if you are day hiking. Read the signs carefully. Day hikers are allowed to park in the middle of the grass in the camping area free of charge. The multi-use trails that allow horses can be muddy so don't fall. If you are hiking around the lake, there is no trail over or around the spillway, you need to rock hop across the creek, (this is a good thing to incorporate your mind into the hike, you have to think about where you want to step next. Trails were quite muddy but it rained all day the day before. Getting from the north trail to the lake trail at the southwest end is possible but you will have to hop a fairly dry creek, only took me about 30 seconds and 1 6 foot leap in the brush. The redbud trees are beautiful in the spring even though they are few and far between. They give the trail more color. Doing the north trail all along the top of the park and connecting to the lake and hiking along the bottom shore to get to the camping parking lot is just a little over 6 miles. Definitely would recommend if on a road trip and you are looking for a place to stretch your legs for about an hour as its only 10 miles east of 35.

Beautiful Park Right in the heart of the Waterloo-Cedar Falls area. Note that if you are using the trail maps on the Iowa DNR site, the PT trail is called the Twisty Trail east of the road and Joe's Trail west of the road on park signs, and the perimeter trail is called the Wonderland Trail in the west and Prison Break in the east. Awesome lakes, tons of kayakers, a tad humid but that comes with the river valley. Very uncrowded (on dirt trails) for a memorial day weekend.

I did all 7.2 miles around the lake. The clubhouse/event center is huge and it looks really cool. When on the trails, avoid the sun as much as possible because all the bugs hang out there. There is one stretch of trail in the southwest corner of the lake that is on the edge of a cattlefield. Try to get through this area as quickly as possible. Going around the lake counter-clockwise was a good idea because you got to see the view from the dam last, which is the best one.

Wow this place is awesome! I parked near the lodge and took the woodland trail down to the overlook trail, then walked near the picnic area to get to the cedar cliff trail. I did all 1.3 miles to the end and then went back a half a mile and took the cool hollow trail back to the lodge (this trail has lots of hills and I would not recommend taking it if you are a beginning hiker or if you ran out of water like me XD).

Really crowded at the beach but we were hiking on the other side of the lake. Bring bug spray. We did the east loop and the lakeshore loop which totaled 4.16 miles. One thing google doesn't show is the bridge over the lake on the southeast end near the fishing piers. They are pretty leanient on parking so if you park in the grass in the group camping area for hiking thats fine. There is also one parking spot there.

SD state park with an awesome trail system and a great view of the lake and slough. It's interesting how the slough is in the middle of the peninsula. The park's elevation above the lake makes for some great views, especially on the eastern edge of the park. Comparable to Oakwood Lakes, difference is there is only one lake here, no island trail, and less trails. Views are better here though.

A tad muddy but SUPER quiet, everyone uses the boat ramps so the hiking area is dead, you could walk in the middle of the road with headphones on and not have to worry about cars. Find the shelter on the south side of the road and take the grassy trail down to the cliffs on the lake, thats where the best view is. We also saw a baby turtle in the middle of the road.

Of the 51 Iowa state parks i've been to, this one is my favorite. I still have 3 left, but this will likely stay number one. You can see 3 states from some places on the sunset ridge trail. The bear grass is cool to see because that can only be found in Iowa in this park. Lots of unique prairie plants as well. I will definitely be back.

My favorite SD state park of the 3 I've visited so far (going for all 12). The views from the top of the hill overlooking the lake are amazing, and the stream with waterfalls on the west side of the Robar trail is an interesting thing to walk along. I will be back when it's greener for sure.

Amazing views, of the northern black hills and great plains. Quiet, and removed from the traffic the black hills get. Note: The lake trail does not go all the way around the lake and if you want to go all the way around you will have to walk on a dirt road and on the edge of the highway.
dislikes: Necessity to walk on dirt road and highway edge

reviews_attraction.text: One of my favorite parks in eastern SD. Good 7 mile hike from the parking lot in the tent campground, completing the hiking and multi-use trail loops. Great views as you come to the northeast trailhead for the multi-use trail. I will be back, especially when it has greened up.

My favorite state park in the great lakes region of Iowa. Fort Defiance wins if you bring bug spray but with no accessories, this one is the best. The interpretive trail is full of things to check out, so take a brochure. Its about 1 and a half miles so nothing too hard.

Very run-down park, but in a good way. No trails, as the bridge has been wiped away, but good spots to walk along the riverbanks. Probably wouldn't go back unless I'm in the area, but interesting place to walk around for 15 minutes.

This is one of the best "Little Parks" in Iowa. I hiked just about every trail in the park (1.5 miles) and it was wonderful to see the whole park and how green it was. If I lived closer, I would go back often.
When the DNR refers to it as rugged, they mean it. These are some of the most challenging hiking trails in Iowa. If you want easier trails, stay towards the north and east ends of the park.
Great park, not somewhere to go on a nice day during the pandemic, lots of crowds. If you want to avoid the crowds, come early in the morning as the park opens at 4 AM.
To anyone who is wondering, the trail around the lake is not clearly marked in front of Keomah Village, but it belongs to the state park and is not private property.
We did 10 miles of hiking here, all of them amazing, if you hike on the back of the ridge, you will find wild strawberries, great views on the front ridge.
We only had time for about 2 miles of hiking here. There are 45 miles of trails in the park. We will definitely be back to camp for 2 nights.
A standard forested lake park in southwest Iowa. Lots of wild strawberries along the trail, just make sure they aren't over-ripe.
Its 2 miles around the lake and the spillway on one side and the causeway on the other makes it more scenic than it would seem.
The trail clearly doesn't go all the way around the lake. Nice lake though. I like the rock bridges on the ends.
Awesome park with some great views of the interstate. In the top half of state parks for South Dakota for sure.
I expect the trails that run through the WMA to be very buggy in the summer, but they are great in the spring.
The trail system has a perfect 4 and a half mile loop that I do every time I come here.

This park has *lots* of potential to be a welcoming, inviting spot - waterside views of Manhattan, open green space, a fun kids play area, a baseball diamond, a sprinkler, basketball court, and restroom facilities. It's also a "no barbeque, no open fire" space, HOWEVER, when I visited, there were at least six portable grills going on the premises in violation of this policy. This, plus a general feel of deteriorating, unkept facilities and grounds have the park a "rundown" feeling throughout. This park has lots of potential but needs some protective attention from the NY Parks system first.

The parking lot is very expensive. $40 for more than 3 hours. The exhibits and relatively few. However, the shark exhibit and sea lion are definitely worthwhile. The 4D theatre is also enjoyable, though the only "effects" are done puffs of air and vibrating seats. Could definitely have used some water spray. To enjoy your visit, you should arrive at 9:30am to 10:00am, when they open. Otherwise, the lines are long and the crowds get congested inside. Also, purchase your tickets online; that's much more efficient than waiting in long lines at the ticket counter.

MSG provides a cozy and centrally located place to watch sporting venues. I've watched the Rangers hockey team and St. John's 🏀 team play and enjoyed both experiences. The pizza and hotdogs are nothing fancy and a bit pricey. The apple churros good though and for only $3@. The cheapest seats (like the 418 section) are slightly obstructed but comfortable, but you cannot see the jumbo Tron from there. You'll enjoy quick entrance and exit to events and immediate access to all of the 🚆 and subway services coming in and out of Penn Station.
dislikes: Jumbo Tron not visible from some sections

reviews_attraction.text: First, let me emphasize that Austin, our tour guide, was the absolute best - friendly, cheerful, humorous, informative, and engaging! The tour itself was fascinating. Both my wife and I and our six young children thoroughly enjoyed the experience. There was something for everyone! The youngest especially enjoyed sitting in the gunner seats and steering the guns 😊 If you're visiting Albany, then apartmenyt from the downtown museum, tower, and capitol stop, this is an absolute must-see.

Our church in Queens, NYC visits takes an annual summer day hike to this park once a year and we always have a blast. The grounds crew takes immaculate care of the park and the scenery is uhMAYzing. The trail loop around the lake offers multiple breath-taking scenic overlooks and the trail difficulty is easy enough for kids to do. The Minnewaska Falls are also a NY jewel of nature that you'll want to check out, too. Parking is $10 per vehicle, but admission is free otherwise.

This is a fabulous park, cared for meticulously. Only $7 to enter. Offers ample green space for picnicking and a wonderful variety of hiking trails. Wolf Cave is especially fascinating, though it is a tight squeeze for adults and not all will be able to get through. The nature center is really well done, providing an engaging learning experience for children. The birdwatching station in the center is relaxing and noteworthy for sure. The entire park is spacious and peaceful.

You can enter this building for free, but will need to pass through a security checkpoint. The stairwells are historic and fascinating. They best thing to see here though is the Senate and Assembly chambers. Each chamber is ornate and extraordinary in its own way. You may also appreciate the hall of governors (with paintings of each NY governor) and the collection of flags gathered from each war that NY soldiers fought in. Elevators are available to get up and down.

This iconic structure is definitely worth visiting if you're in Corona, and especially if you're visiting Flushing Meadow Park or attending the US Open. In the warm/hot season, out features water fountains around the perimeter. This is a terrific spot for taking a photo. You may even want to bring a picnic lunch to eat on the grounds nearby before you explore the rest of Flushing Meadow Park. Best of all, there's no admission. You can visit the Unisphere for free!

This botanical garden is a hidden jewel nestled in the heart ❤️ of Flushing. $6 admission for teens, $2 for children, 3-yr. and younger are free. An annual family pass is only $85! There's lots of space, lots of plant variety, and plenty of fresh air. If you like birdwatching, you'll find plenty of birds as well. Saw bluejays, cardinals, and hawks on our last visit! This is a relaxing, fresh space that you'll definitely want to visit from time to time.

This museum offers 1-2 hours worth of displays for viewing, all focused on the history, archaeology, topography, and wildlife of New York State. All of this is on Floor 1, and a free, historic carousel is available to ride on Floor 4. This museum will not appeal to young children and is not particularly engaging for the reluctant visitor. But for anyone who enjoys history, it's a good way to spend some time in Albany for sure

This is a captivating park! I've been here once with my children and we plan to return multiple times again. The trail is straightforward (literally), without lots of intersections to other trails. While it lacks outstanding vista views, it offers ample tree cover and a truly relaxing hiking experience. It features some varied terrain and inclines, but nothing extreme. I'd give the difficulty level a 5 of 10.

This is a worthwhile spot to visit, but I would definitely recommend the Empire State building first. The Freedom Tower gives you a good Manhattan view northward, but the other directions are uninspiring. Plus, you will encounter a variety of sales gimmicks on the way to that I found distracting. The Empire State gives you an excellent view on all directions, including a great view of Central Park.

This experience impressed me deeply. It wasn't as dark or overwhelming as a Holocaust museum, but it was impactful and sobering in it's own way, in a way that is most appropriate and fitting. A good variety of exhibits, both informative, inspiring, and reflective. Whether your are familiar with the events of 9/11 or not, this experience will impact and educate you in a meaningful way I assure you.

This fascinating spot presents a unique and inviting perspective on the problem of hunger and famine in our world. I visited this site with some native Irish friends and they were especially pleased! They said it was a very authentic Irish scene. You will notice that some of the "boulders" along the winging walkway have names stamped onto them. These names are the names of counties in Ireland.

Our entire family of seven enjoyed this zoo immensely. You can tour the zoo in 1-2 hours max without rushing, and it offers a variety of kid-friendly features and activities. The outdoor hiking loop is relaxing and features my favorite - the red 🐼. The indoor exhibits feature an engaging variety of animals and a pleasant experience overall, and so does the outdoor farm area.

Enjoyed an 11th wedding anniversary here with my wife. Arrived at the start of dinner, which is 5:30pm. Received a seat almost immediately in a pleasant outdoor dining area. Waterside seats were unavailable though due to customers with reservations. The food was fantastic and the wait staff was excellent. A bit pricey, but a good choice for special occasions.

This park is uhMAYzing. Tucked away in College Point, it offers superb waterfront views of the city in a quiet, forested space. Walking trails, a large playground, a handball court, a basketball court, and benches throughout. No grills makes this a quiet, relaxing environment. We hosted our church picnic there this year and will be doing it again for sure.

This stadium offers a fabulous view, nestled in downtown Pittsburgh by the river, with each access by walking from downtown across the Roberto Clemente Bridge. Fireworks night featured a 20-minute show from the river. The stadium also features a nice children's corner with a small baseball diamond and a playground.

This trail is an intense hike. It spans 3.6 miles of mixed, rugged terrain. Wear good hiking shoes/boots to handle the rocky path. Parking is free at the trailhead. Once you reach Anthony's Nose lookout, either return back again or keep on hiking .6 miles further to another parking lot at the Appalachian Trail.

This park provides ample space for walking, running, and family strolls. The children's playrooms on the southwest corner by 111th Street is the best! The Queens Zoo by 111th Street is perhaps the best kept secret in Queens. On warm days, parking will be hard to find, so you'll need to walk or bicycle in.

This is a surprisingly large, spacious playground with multiple play spaces and equipment for young children. Plenty of places to sit as well, along with a very nice basketball 🏀 court. There's also a restroom facility, too. There's no dedicated parking lot, neither is there any picnicking spots.

This Room Escape location offers some challenging, engaging, and enjoyable rooms for groups as large as eight persons. If you want a challenge, then you definitely need to choose the Clock Tower room, though I hear that the Dinosaur room is also a thrill.

Our family loves to visit this park whenever we vacation in Huntingdon, PA near Raystown. The suspension bridge, water falls, balancing boulder, and creek make for a fascinating hike. Other lengthier, more challenging hikes are also available!
This is a fantastic place for a day filled with hands-on learning for kids. Having been there many times as a kid, I'm looking forward to taking my own kids there next month!
For a small zoo, this features a fascinating and surprising assortment of animals. You can easily see everything within an hour.

After enjoying caves for years I had an incident about 15 years ago that ended my enjoyment.  Whilst in a very deep cave I suffered a claustrophobic panic attack out of nowhere and never entered another cave.
Missing the experience I decided on a lark to try Cave of the Mounds.
I figured it was a small cave, not deep, and popular so busy.  I loved it.  The staff were very friendly and knowledgeable.  The cave has a very wide variety of formations for one it's size.  Cave of the Mounds is also a "living" cave which commercial caves often are not.
In the mid point I took a rest and was asked by a guide what my favorite part had been so far.  I tokd her it was the very fact that I was sitting there.  I did have sone brief PTSD in a narrow low section which I quickly overcame.
dislikes: Brief PTSD in narrow low section

reviews_attraction.text:
The Franconia Sculpture park is quite a good experiment in public art.  Though many pieces can easily be discarded as junk and a few really need repair there are some fine pieces in the collection.  I've never been here when it was busy and it's free.  Defiantly worth a stop on your way to or from Taylors Falls.
My only criticism would be it is a rough walk for folks with mobility limitations.

North Dakota can be tedious sometimes for sure.  The Enchanted Highway is a wonderful way to break that up.  We visited all of the ones on the left side going down and then the right side coming back to I 94.
Honestly this project gives so much joy with it's whimsy, engineering,  and creativity.  It is well worth the adventure.

I really enjoyed this place.  Just the idea that one guy put this whole thing together is stunning.  There is a place to eat about half way through and if you bought the full ticket it's a perfect place to take a break.  The House on the Rock is the sort of place you should see once in your life but you may want to go back.

This is one of my favorite sites.  The visitors center is very good.  It's both comprehensive and informative.
The stockade itself is a great and masterful recreation.  This site is a jewel in the crown of MN historical society.  It is worth a trip to see on it's own.

Jewel cave is a quintessential cave.  This is a cave lovers cave.  They use an elevator to go down into the cave and well constructed walkways through out.  The tour was only slightly rigorous.
This was the first cave I ever got claustrophobic and I still loved it.

Cosmos is a classic Mystery Spot.  They do it all and each time I've been here they do it right,  Well priced and a fun for everyone.  My daughter says that when we went to Cosmos she was taller than her younger brother.  After that he was.  A true mystery.

This is a very nice and quiet park and has a very interesting historical story about the big battle that was fought down river a piece.  A nice break from the crowd in town too.  They have playground stuff, a boat and fishing dock, and picnic facilities.

Came here just to see this place and what a wonder.  It was worth the trip.  The name says it all.  Some of his displays get switched out so  there is always something new to see.
Whilst in Gladbrook be sure to get some of their home town mustard too!

I've been to Fort Abraham Lincoln several times as a reenactor and as a visitor.  The Custer house  is a highlight for sure.  They are doing a very good job here as they've grown over the years.  I'll be back.

The Badlands are magical.  Pictures do not do them justice.  You have to go there, get off the road, and walk into wonder.  Sunrise, midday, sunset, or after dark...magic.  No time is a bad time to see them.

A very nice reconstructed Sioux Uprising stockade.  Not open all the time but new stuff over the years has kept it fresh.  Good family stop when they are open.  Wish it was open more but great when it is.
Like Wall Drug it is an I 90 road trip icon.  They have a "General Lee".  They also house the Geology Hall of Fame.  Only reason I gave it 4 stars was it was a bit run down and goes on forever.
likes: Cultural exhibits (General Lee, Geology Hall of Fame)

reviews_attraction.text: Nice side trip but not the main attraction.  When we've been there it's always been quite and not crowded.  Which is a nice change from the hustle and bustle of the other areas of the Hills.
You saw the giant buffalo, you visited the giant catfish, you wondered at "Sal" the 40ft cow, you drove the Enchanted Highway,  so you really cannot pass up 'Sandy".  And why would you?
I loved this.  As a man born the year the wall was erected and who's child was born the year it came down this was very cool.  The best treatment of wall sections I've seen to date.
We make this a part of every trip to the Black Hills.  Custer Park is always a good time and the Wild Life loop is our favorite part.  Absolutely a "must see".
I came here for one reason, Wild Bill Hickok's grave.  I was not disappointed.  It's a steep walk up to the cemetery from the parking area.
This a true classic road trippers stop.  Pretty remote but that is part of the charm.  really a treat to see.  And they have GIFT SHOP
Kind of pricey for what you get.  However, a well done western town is hard to find these days and this is one of the best.
Yet another truly inspired artist doing his own thing.  There is some real cool stuff here.  When I was there it was free.
Cool site, I wish they did more with it but what is there is fine.  It's marked and if you know the story it's very cool.
A classic Rapid City and Black Hills stop.  Old school Dino statues and a gift shop.  The Dinos are free! So is the view.
Just a simple stop and wonder.  Grab a cone a postcard and some snapshots.  Worth it to say you've seen it.
Good local park but there is no way that Jesse James jumped his horse over that gulch.  Nice story though.

How do I give bonus stars?! If you see Niagara Falls from the American side, do yourself a favor and buy tickets for Cave of the Winds! Traverse a wooden walkway built along the crashing sheets of water of Bridal Veil Falls and feel the POWER. Firstly, the view from below is even more awe inspiring than from above. If you don't mind getting wet, hit the hurricane deck for the full effect. You will get soaked, and you will love it. Simply exhilarating.

It's just shy of $20 per adult ticket, but it is worth every penny. They provide ponchos, sandals, and a plastic bag to put your own shoes in. I would suggest bringing baggies for your phone, keys, and wallet, as they can easily get wet. It starts with a history of the falls video, but once you take the elevator down to the bottom of the falls you are welcome to stay as long or short as you like.

Do this. Do this. Do this. Highlight of the Niagara Falls experience.

If you love marveling at the wonders of nature, this is a park you're going to truly enjoy. Distant views showcasing the power of mother nature are pretty much available throughout the park and in every direction. There are many places to pull over along the route to stop, take photos, take it all in, or simply to rest.

There are quite a few spots where you can climb some of the formations as well. We were able to spot a good amount of wildlife during our trip. A few things I wish we would have brought along would have been binoculars, extra water (it was August), and a few snacks. You can easily lose track of time here and end up spending several hours. There are a few man made structures for restroom stops, a museum, etc.

Gives you excellent views of the falls, but it does not extend out as far as you might think - you won't get a complete viewpoint of the entire Horseshoe Falls. Still, for $1.25 per person for an unlimited time on the deck, it is well worth it.

The main problem you'll find is that it will be tough to get to the edge of the deck for a good photo. Also, be prepared to have a lot of strangers in your photo background if it's busy (which it more than likely will be). As a side note, if you plan on doing the Maid of the Mist boat tour, that ticket includes admission to the observation deck, so hold off on buying a ticket to just the deck if you are also planning on going on the ferry.

Large crowds gather at terrapin point thinking that the fireworks are going to be shot off over Horseshoe Falls. That was not the case for us, they were actually shot off further down the lower river, near the observation deck and loading dock for the Maid of the Mist boat tours. That's important to know ahead of time because a lot of trees block views of the fireworks along the cliffline so plan accordingly.

The fireworks themselves were of high quality...very large, loud, and beautiful. They are short however, I would guess the duration of only 3 to 4 minutes.

This museum is jam packed with artifacts, history, newspaper clippings, videos, photos, memorabilia, the list goes on. You could literally spend hours in here and not see and read everything. It really is a pretty cool and entertaining place to experience - and it's all free. If you ask the staff (which are amazing by the way), they will start a film for you regarding the history of the Okoboji area which I found to be pretty interesting. I've probably come to visit a dozen times and see something new every single time.

I had my wedding reception here and had a stellar evening. The main lodge stays cool in the summer heat due to the stone construction, even without modern AC. The view from the lodge is beautiful for photo backgrounds as well. I believe it was only $200 to rent this space for the night...which is some serious value. No hard liquor and I believe you have a midnight curfew, but these rules actually kept guests in line so it worked out even better than I could have hoped for.

I would highly recommend renting this space.

Excellent, excellent, excellent! What amazing tour guides - they really made the tour come alive with their real life accounts of times when the prison was in working order. This is a trip that I'll never forget. Visiting the gas chamber was very eerie indeed - it's surreal to think that you could be standing in a room when so many men were deliberately executed. The whole experience really opens up your eyes to life outside of your own little world. Bravo to the staff. Well organized tour, great information.

It's a pretty decent neighborhood park, and in a very real sense - there is no parking lot OR street parking here, so unless you live close enough to walk or bike, you probably won't be visiting and taking advantage of this green space and playground. Regardless, it's nice to have small neighborhood parks, but it would be nice if even a few dedicated parking spaces were available for families that are little further away. Still a nice park and glad to see its presence.

We went for a late fall walk along the trails here on a lazy Saturday. The parking area and trails themselves were well groomed and clean. Trails on the west side of the park, between the west entrance and the campground are relatively flat and not much of a hike, but come with nice views of the stream down below in the ravine. There are a few benches scattered along the trail we walked which is nice if you want to gaze down and across the hill or need a break.

Really enjoyed an afternoon here. Right near the old market, but somewhat secluded at the same time. The water features are nice,  and there is a popular spot near the pond and fountain for outdoor weddings.

It can get pretty busy here though,  there was both a wedding and large groups of high schoolers here for prom photos at the same time. Throw in the daily mix of runners, bikers, dog walkers, and sight seers and you've got yourself a pretty busy park.

A top-notch aquarium giving memorable experiences to its visitors. The employees were all very knowledgeable - especially the gal running the snake show...scared the daylights out of my wife as she thought she was only going to see harmless fish, etc. I actually left my rental car keys in the room and was off looking at another exhibit when an employee actually chased me down and returned them to me, somehow recognizing me. Now that's service!

Such a secluded and peaceful area for a walk with the dogs, a run, or a bike outing. I wish I would have taken advantage of this place more while I lived in the area. It's a bit of a jaunt to get here, but it is most definitely worth it.

It combines grasslands and plains trails with wooded and river trails. Crushed gravel and dirt paths. I think this place is mostly a hidden gem most people never hear about, and they tend to miss out on.

I loved this place. My wife and I took a leisurely stroll along the dunes and just lost track of time wandering around, writing messages in the sands with our hands, and enjoying the wide and distant views. Great place for photo opportunities as well. If you're an outdoorsy person you'll likely thoroughly enjoy this state park - I know I did. Be sure to bring sandals if you're wearing shoes unless you like sand in the socks.

Warning: Nerd leaving a review. I thought it was so cool that something I learned about as a kid and found interesting came to life during my visit to Kill Devil Hills. I had a blast and read every scripture and plaque that I came across. Had it not been for my family urging me along, I'm sure I would have spent a lot more time here. If you love history or aviation or both, you're going to really enjoy this place!

A sad but interesting part of history. If you're in the area and have a little but of time to spare and enjoy museums and history this might be just right for you. You can learn a bit about the history of the area that most people have no idea about whatsoever. It's a rather small museum, you can't go inside the cabin, and the grounds are also limited so you won't need a ton of time -perhaps half an hour or so.

There aren't a lot of parks in the Sioux City area,  so this one is all the more important.  A paved path around the lake is nearly a 5k, and several dirt paths veer off into the woods and hills... Just be aware of bikes flying down these and around corners.

The dog park is large and even has a separate smaller area for the little pups. There's plenty of parking and room for cookouts and picnics.

Really neat area with lots of trail options,  essentially surrounded my rivers. You've got the old fort you cab visit on one side and downtown Fort Wayne within easy walking distance if you need a drink or a bite to eat.

There's a large parking lot nearby but I believe it's a self ticket pay to park service. I hear there are festivals here so I'm looking forward to attending them in the future.

Beautiful sunken garden area that provides great backdrops for senior photos, homecoming, prom, or even wedding photos.

The landscaping is well groomed and park is pretty clean overall. Not really a park that you would go to for a run or bike ride due to the smaller size, but more for a leisurely walk with your four legged friend. Good location too, right near downtown yet still peaceful.
dislikes: Small size (not suitable for running or biking)

reviews_attraction.text:
Trails were abundant and very well groomed. The bathroom facilities were large, well maintained, and very clean. Really cool structure for relaxing next to the lake and beach. Plenty of fishing options and cheap boat rentals! Dog friendly!

One thing - if you have a large SUV or truck,  the parking lot might give you some trouble as it's pretty tight. Overall though we loved it!

Really enjoyed being at this park on a lightly rainy day. Was saddened to read the signs about the PCB ridden fish that you shouldn't keep or eat. It's terrible the effect we can have on such beautiful environments.

There's a really fun observation tower here and well constructed and maintained boardwalks. Paths are pretty well groomed and there's ample parking.

We spent an afternoon on the sandy beach and in the lake swimming area. This park is well cared for and offers public restrooms, playground, splash pad, picnic area, and basketball, volleyball, and tennis courts.

A short walk to the north is The Village, a quaint shopping experience with unique stores and a few restaurants. You can also rent kayaks for $20/hr.

It’s a big pink elephant. We did what everyone does and took pictures with it. In 15 years, we will probably find those pictures and wonder where was that and what was the point? Nonetheless it’s still a fun and innocent way to kill some time and take a photo opportunity while traveling. Kids seem to LOVE this thing.

It's a pretty basic beach with pretty compacted, hard sand. There's not much of the soft free flowing "top sand". You've got a single short dock that kids enjoy jumping off from and a buoy protected swim zone that offers a generous area of various depth.

There are public bathrooms and a little shade as well.

Excellently groomed park, from the paved path to the short wooded mulch path, and everything inbetween. There's a splash pad, volleyball courts, horseshoe pit, and restrooms.

They have neat signs along the trail that help motivate you to keep walking or jogging. Great park, cool location.

The sunken gardens really jazz this park up. It's very beautiful on that west side of the park. The east side includes the playground, walking trails,  and fishing area.

Nice little park that's quiet and refreshing. I really enjoyed it.

Visited here for the first time in July 2018. As far as "support faculties" are concerned, there are barely anything at all: a rather small parking area, with a picnic table nearby, two stone benches, and a "bulletin board" type display giving a few rules but no other info like park hours or a trail map. There isn't any on-site trash can or restrooms (apparently visitors are expected to use a tree for any bathroom breaks).

However, the two hiking trails are pretty nice. Seems like a really nice place for a weekend outing for the family, or to spend some solitude time with nature. Amazing that this great little place exists only fifteen minutes from a major urban center (Topeka).

December 2018 addition: Had time to explore the area more thoroughly. There are two trails here, both looping back around to their starting point. The Oregon Trace Trail is the easier option, being more level, but there isn't anything to point out what traces of the Oregon Trail there are (unless I simply missed them). The Post Creek Ridge Trail is a lot more challenging, going up and down some rather steep (and rocky) inclines. This trail isn't marked out all that well; there sere several points where I wasn't completely sure if I was even on the trail at all (not good for a person with a horrendously bad sense of direction).

Not the best state park I've been too. The hiking trail itself is rather nice, with good views of the creek, several benches, and a picnic table. However, the trail is also incredibly short and just about the only good thing about the park. There are no trash cans, so visitors have to take any trash with them.

Also, for all I know, there might be more of the park on the east side of the creek but I wasn't able to get across the creek, since there's no bridge. The only way to get across is to drive right into the creek. (All I can imagine is that scene from It's a Mad, Mad, Mad, Mad World, when Phil Silvers tries to drive across that stream.)

This is actually an aggregate rating. If based solely on the sculpture itself, I'd give it a negative rating if possible. It was one of those "hunk of junk" things that was popular back in the 1970s; I can't imagine how anyone can possibly see this as a windmill. Is this really worth a four or five minute climb up a trail barely wide enough for two people to pass and has about a dozen switchbacks?

However, the four star rating is actually for the view from the top. It is absolutely BREATHTAKING; you can literally see for miles and miles to the north. I would have given it five stars if it wasn't for all the tress interfering with the view.

Very nice little park. Lots of shade trees and picnic tables. Beautiful pond, very nice to just sit there and read quietly for a while. There's also a history museum located in the park; unfortunately, it was closed at the time I visited (while the museum's website lists it as being open 10 am to noon, apparently according to the sign on the door, this is only during the non-summer months, which they define as Nov 1st to March 31st., Would have been nice if they had posted this to their website.)

Personally, I've always thought that this bridge is one of the most beautiful spots in the area. Awesome being able to walk across it, look down at your feet and see the mighty Susquehanna River flowing underneath. Of course, the best time for this would have to be during December around twilight, with the bridge covered in lights and the sunset over the shoreline. Absolutely beautiful!!!!!

Fantastic little park, great hiking trails. The view from the two overlooks are absolutely AWESOME!!! (especially form the Jeffrey overlook). There's even a pavilion with picnic tables (and bathrooms!) on site for family picnics. However, I'm not sure what purpose the "amphitheater" is serving. (There's no sign offering any explanation of this thing.)

My only visit here was several years ago, when my parents dragged me here against my will on a cold, windy day and I didn't have a hat or gloves. I'm simply not interested in aviation history (especially when I'm freezing). If you're really into planes and all that, this place is probably worth four or five stars.
dislikes: Facilities & Services (cold, no protection from weather)

reviews_attraction.text: Absolutely wonderful amusement park. Wonderful that I only have to pay for the specific rides that I want to enjoy rather than having to pay a general admission fee for the entire park (including kiddie rides that I can't go on). Great place to bring the family.

Very nice bridge for the area. Unfortunately, the traffic on here moves at a snail's pace during "rush hour" (a misnomer if there ever was one). Really need about five or six (or a dozen) more bridges like this over the river to help with the traffic.

Fascinating place to visit. Very easy to lose yourself among the displays for at least two or three hours. Plus they have a special exhibition that changes every few months (which gives an extra incentive for returning at least once a year!).

One of my favorite places to visit in south central Pennsylvania. Wonderful layout, the animal enclosures constructed to look like the animal's natural habitat. This place is one of those rare places that is both fun and educational.

Awesome stat park with great hiking trails and good locations for camping. Personally, I really appreciate the bathrooms located throughout the park, especially near the camping locations. So happy that I never had to use a tree.

Drove past the archway many times over the years as I dove on Interstate 70. Very impressive looking structure. Really would love to be able to pull off the interstate and visit it one of these days pretty soon.
Great place to learn what the Continental army had to experience during the Revolutionary War, their living quarters, etc. The visitor's center is awesome too, amazing exhibits, great giftshop.
Nice place to learn about the state's railroading past. Lots of interesting exhibits. The Strasburg Rail Road nearby gives very nice rides too, for the complete historic experience.
The Union headquarters for the three day battle. I've seen pictures of it in different books, but to actually stand where Meade lead the army of the Potomac is just spooky-weird.
Good memorial, nicely situated near where several North Carolina brigades started in Longstreet's Assault on July 3rd (and made it further than the Virginians).
To me, while the stand of the 20th Maine is a tad overrated (the other two brigades deserve equal credit, at least), this is still a cool place to visit.
This is actually the very first roller coaster that I've ever rode on (and so far the last). Great old fashioned wooden roller coaster. Loads of fun.
Undoubtedly the most impressive Civil War monument in the N.P.S. The view from the top is immensely impressive, great way to see the battlefield.
Awesome sight! They've got it perched on a bit of a mountain, with lots of lovely plants all around. Must be a spectacular sight in the spring.
Awesome place. Everything set up like in the glory days of trains. So much great stuff, kind of hard not to feel like a little kid sometimes.
While it might not compare with other big city zoos (like Omaha), this is still an excellent place to spend an afternoon with the family.
Very cool place to visit, the preserved miners' village, the coal mine tour. Got to see what the Molly Maguires really had to go through.
Impressive monument but not really helpful in understanding what happened here. Although this gives a nice view of Oak Ridge.

Plenty of parking here. The view from here is magnificent. And walk across the road to see some cool things and visit the gift shop. And on the west side of the parking lot, there is a trail that takes you to Turkey Creek. This is a must see, as there are a couple waterfalls that are very beautiful. And if you continue on the trail, you will see some scenic cliffs. Definitely worth your time if you stop here.

Creation Falls and the Rock Bridge are fairly close to one another. The trail is a loop and well defined. There is a little sandy beach at the waterfall and saw lots of people playing in the water and just chilling. If you're feeling adventurous, continue down the Wildcat trail (downstream) a couple miles to see another waterfall (although it will take some climbing to reach the bottom of it).

Came here to see some waterfalls. Started on the North Bank and eventually made it to the South Bank and wasn't disappointed. Fairly easy to find and it helps if you have a 4 wheel drive, as some of these roads are in rough shape. Didn't get to see all the waterfalls, but had a great time.

This waterfall is very colorful, I've never seen anything like it before. The water below the falls looked like a swimming pool,  although I'm sure it's nothing that you would want to swim in. And after visiting this waterfall, continue downstream to see more which are also very beautiful.

Large parking lot and a picnic shelter here, but no restrooms. I saw a total of 4 waterfalls here, but not sure what's downstream. Still lots of trees down beyond the last large waterfall. But even with that, this is a must see as you can get up close to them all.

Went here to try out my kayak. The kayak launch is right beside the beach (which is open) and there is plenty of parking on both sides of the road. It seems like a peaceful little lake (I went on a weekday, the weekends may be busier) with a few spots to explore.

Plenty of parking available and its a good walk to the waterfall, but the path is nice, with plenty of beauty to see on the way. And the steps at the waterfall will take you to the edge of the stream at the base of the waterfall. Well worth the visit.

Simply gorgeous! And you can play in the water at the base of the waterfall. A few parking spots here along the road with just a short walk to the Falls. And continue driving down the road to see Woodhill Tunnel. Its worth a visit since you're here.

Came here to see some waterfalls, found plenty of small ones. The Cedar Falls trail had quite a few and was very scenic. Also the covered bridge was beautiful and there are a couple mini-waterfalls upstream from there on a little side stream.

Very beautiful park. The restrooms were clean and open, plenty of parking, has a playground for the kids  and plenty of places to explore in the woods. And the waterfall was spectacular and the walk to it is very easy. Very glad I visited

I personally think this is the prettiest waterfall in Ohio. It does have a small parking area and it's just a short hike to get to. Although getting down to the base of the Falls can be tricky, it is definitely worth it.

Nice park with an overlook, a tower and a waterfall. The trail to the waterfall is rocky, brutal, about 3 miles in and out and probably best seen after lots of rain (was barely flowing when I was here).
Enough parking for a few vehicles, and there is a restroom here. The view of Sandstone Falls isn't that good from here, or maybe it's just me. I just think the views are better from across the river.
Out in the middle of nowhere, but atleast you don't have to fight the crowds. Take the path behind the shelter into the woods and follow the trail to see a few waterfalls
Simply beautiful here with some gorgeous waterfalls. There is another waterfall off the beaten path downstream from Bridal Veil Falls, just takes some work to get to
Beautiful place. Nice and easy paths to walk. Was my first time here, as I live 2 hours away and was just in the area. The waterfalls are gorgeous and must be seen.
I've stayed here many times and have never been disappointed. Love it here and the lodge is fabulous. Make sure you go see the stone house and hosaks cave.
Many waterfalls around here and a couple caves. Park at the rappelling area parking lot and follow the path into the woods behind the parking lot.
Nice state park with plenty to see. Various places to park and most walking paths are well defined. Definitely worth a stop if you're in the area.
Been by here a hundred times so I finally stopped in today. Great walking trails and very scenic. Well worth your time if you enjoy walking
It's an easy walk to the waterfall, but unfortunately it wasn't flowing today when I visited, but are beautiful when the are flowing.
Nice park and very few people when I was there. Make sure you take the Bluebell Valley trail to the stream to see some waterfalls
It is a bridge. Not sure whats so special about it, but it is something to see if you're in the area.
It's a long hike the the waterfall and bridge, but worth it. Probably best to see after lots of rain.
Very nice with plenty of fun things to do with the kids. And even a couple waterfalls in the woods.

You can park both sides of the road one facing inland or center of the park and the other facing the river many beautiful arched foot bridges perfect for photography events portal potty is everywhere. There is a large Banquet Hall right by the river it is rented for wedding reception or any other events. River side walk path is very beautiful and peaceful for a relaxing walk, dog friendly environment and please clean after your pet. Nice place to take children or spending afternoon fishing while watching boats passing by. There is also a full marina service over night dockage as well as boat ramps. Some grills in certain areas. You can kayak the moat surrounding the entire Island and it's a really beautiful. The whole park is accessible friendly ♿️ including the path by the water.

Brighton Recreation Area is Bishop Lake, Appleton Lake, Murray Lake and a few other small Lakes. Camping modern camping with electricity running water full facility hookups on Bishop Lake only and rustic camping on Appleton Lake and Murray Lake. They have rustic cabins that are available for rent, for cabins there's a private beach. A  jumping Island located in the lake for children to play there's an extra fee to jump on the jumping Island per hour also great fishing great kayaking Three Lakes are actually linked together by small canal so you can go from Lake to Lake kayaking or canoeing and there's also a boat ramp. Dog friendly in certain areas please clean after your pet. This park requires a State Park pass to enter. This is a wheel chair accessable park.

What a nice place to visit, the trail is 1.6 miles long with black asphalt top perfect for jogging or running. A romantic walk in the evening? Kid and dog friendly. The suspension bridge will take you to the island. A footpath along the river is nice with beautiful view (not wheelchair friendly). I visited this park on early April (facility is not fully open yet: museum and restroom). The Richardville Building which can accommodate 200 people is for rent for wedding reception or any kind of party and it can be modified per the needs. Accessible van parking and wheelchair friendly trail ♿ with many bench to stop along the trail.
dislikes: Some facilities closed in early April (museum, restroom)

reviews_attraction.text: This is a State Park it requires to have a State Park pass to enter you can buy it just for a day or annually. Nice place for walking, bicyling, jogging with long distance. Many gazebos to protect you from the sun. Beach is nice for children to play some area of the beach allows dog please clean after your pet. There is boat ramp. The park also provide camping ground for people who likes to camp. I am not sure if there is rustic sites but full hooked up is for sure. Camp Sites are right by the lake. It is a handy cap facility. All footpath are asphalt and there are planty of fishing spots and boating.

Very nice and well maintained. I visited this park on first week of April 2021. It looks like it got flooded lately they just cleaned the path for the wheelchair. Access for the wheelchair ramp is on the right side of the information building and the stairs is right behind the building. Many valuable info regarding the ecosystems can be found in the building there is a tour fee. The whole park is designed for easy access for wheelchair ♿ and they provide device for hearing impaired as well👂Please do not forget to wear mask!

What a beautiful, quiet, nice, neat park with great view of Ohio River. Free five campsites with picnic tables and fire rings. Asphalt parking spaces. Trail hikes in both sides of the park make sure to wear hiking boots and walking stick, these will help. The one on the right is a bit rugged please be careful it will slippery after raining. I saw barges being pushed by a tug boat up and down the river transporting coal. No trash can, take out your trash. A unisex restroom is wheelchair accessible friendly ♿ and very clean

Need a hike, go camping, stay at
the cabin, enjoy the sun rise or sun set, admire the view of the lighthouse, and visit the museum. Only minutes away from downtown East Tawas which has beaches, shopping, dining etc. This park offers its beauty as a place to visit. The sad part erosion got this place quite good. There are cabin, log cabin, tent cabin all accessible friendly ♿️ with wheelchair ramp adjacent to the restroom. There are available for rent. Also seasonal campgrounds

GM Renaissance Center is one many mascots of Detroit. Four sections of the building are used by the General Motors corporation. Inside the building, the current models of GM products are displayed from trucks to sport cars. You will find public bathroom on the main floor, restaurants are also located on this floor. The back of the building is the Detroit river walk. Many outdoor activities are going on in the summer time. There is paid parking garage underneath the building.

This is a big park with picnic tables with grills. Small play ground for children. Big gazebo attached to the restrooms has a very big grill (may need reservation for the gazebo, please check). Tables in Gazebo are wheelchair accessible.There is also porta potty at the parking. Access to the beach from the parking lot. No dog at the beach. This place is wheelchair friendly ♿. Restroom has changing rooms. Spotted a red fox at the beach, it ran away as soon as it saw me.

Island Lake Recreation Area has kayak rentals, canoe rentals, a bath house on the beach that serves concessions. There is many nature trails to walk on,  biking trails, fishing areas, and swimming ponds. There are 2 spots for kayak or canoe camping pre register online at their website. State Park pass required for entry daily or annually. This is a pet friendly park please clean after your pet !! Grills and picnic tables provided by the park

Nice park there is a play ground with swing set a very clean bathroom and picnic tables with bbq grill. This place has kayak or canoe launch to Clinton River, also fishing pier for people who loves fishing. Parking lot is quite big and it is handicap accessible. There is a bridge accross the river it looks like nature trails on the other side. This park is also pet friendly please bring plastic bag with you to clean after your pets.

This park is truly amazing with a view of the lake. You can enjoy the lighthouse from far away. It has a camp ground, marina, beach, biking and walking trail. Waterfall Area is in it. If you go up the stairs you will find Sunset Park. The restrooms are very clean. The whole areas is wheelchair accessible friendly ♿. Parking is along the shore. Pet friendly and please pick up after your pet.

This is a beautiful park with Huron River running along side it. Paddle boats and canoes are available for renting. Miles of bicycle trail or walking trail with picnic bench all over. Nice path for crusing with scooter for disabled people. This park is very well organized there is fee for car parking. Good for family event and very dog friendly please don't forget to clean after your pet.

Tthis is a very big and beautiful park its a wheel chair accessible too the play ground there are 2 of them are right by the beach parking access is very easy there is gazebo with tables and chairs connect right to the bathroom I am not sure if you have to pay to use the gazebo though. The park is very shady with many tall trees.

The rock formations make you say awesome! and it makes you wonder how it happened. It is a short hike but worth every inch of it. The arch is amazing in how it forms. We started from the north side thru the south. Bring walking stick and hiking boots with you. Be sure footed! Not wheelchair accessible. No public restrooms.

Many spots for pre wedding, engagement, etc photography a good place to have a picnic dog friendly environment please bring your own doggy bag to clean after your lovely pet open from dawn untill dusk portal potty at the entrace of the park. There is gazebo in the middle of the pond for day use. Overall its worth a look

A hidden gem everyone has to check it if you are in the area. Just tuck in from I-23. Camping/cabin facilities, beautiful beach, park for children, grills, bench, restroom. Accessible parking and restroom ♿. Nice place for stone hunting. Pet friendly, please clean after your pet. Has to have park pass to get in.

Some benches by the lake to sit down while enjoying the view. This park is alongside the road and next to a private property. It has a sandy white beach to enjoy the water. Not too many parking spots, no facility. A nice place to stop and take photos of the Mackinac Bridge from the distance.

McGulpin Point Lighthouse is located at Mackinaw City. There is a cute store inside. The fee to get into the museum is $3 per person, it's worth it. Big parking area with van accessible ♿. If you go to the point it will take you to right to the shore. Also parking is available by the Point.

There are play ground, fishing pier, seasonal food court, seasonal bathroom. It is definitely a disability accessible. Strolling alongside the water ia very beautiful or even just sitting by the bench. American Legion Post 217 is in this area. Have a drink and enjoy the view.
Nice view from the top if you are in the area please stop by $1 admission fee and free sticker employees are very friendly too
Never got bored to be back here its one of the place you have to visit in Michigan if you in the area highly recommended
A place to get away for us beautiful sunset or sunrise ... Many people fishing on this location open from 4 am to 11 pm
Its a beautiful park surrounded by the Lake good for biking or jogging or walking dog unfortunately its close today 😞
Love this mid-size park good for dog walk or jog or just to relax enjoying the beauty of its scenery

It's amazing. One of its kind. Driving through this was fun. There are places you can find prairie dogs, big horn sheep, bisons etc. There are so many scenic points to click pictures and take a look at rocky mountains, land formations, steep canyons. We were there on a sunny day so would recommend travel with energy drinks, water, sunscreen, hat. Do stop your vehicle at various overlook points, it's beautiful ; The Fossil Exhibit Trail, Pinnacles Overlook, Yellow Mounds Overlook, White River Valley, Panorama Point etc.

Loved it! This park has many things to do like hiking, biking, swimming, camping, fishing, kayaking, picnicking, bird watching. They have LJ Family Conservatory, Butterfly Garden, Horses, Kids Area, Slides, Go App Tree Activities, Lakes, Deck, Boardwalks, Mini Golf etc. We dint book any cabin but it seems will be an amazing experience there, locations of cabins are amid of forest.Observation Tower but it is under maintenance so they have closed it.

Great easy and moderate hiking trails!! Loved hiking at Sunset Ridge Trail, came across many plants and trees of different types, got a spectacular sunset view. Worth spent evening. While hiking late in the evening do take care of bugs. They have campgrounds, kids play zone, well maintained picnic areas, shelters and overlook points as well as boat ramp but there was algae on its surface. Herd of deer made our day! Take a trail map from entrance.

A good stop to learn about Native American history. The monument is under construction and it will take many years to be completed but one can see the under constructed structure till now. It does cost you an additional entry fee. There is a great shop of Art work and Cultural Center about them and an amazing display of the history. There are some scheduled Native American shows inside the cultural center.

Loved it. Scenic views, rocks, river, boardwalk, trails, overlook points everything is worth spending time there. Rocks and river flowing through it is much enjoyable. From the entrance to various points everything is awesome. You can swim, catch fishes in the river and relax on rocks. There are trails to go up to many overlook points and down to the river.

Beautiful, lovely place to relax and enjoy the beauty of falling water and it's music. Parking is a problem there, but visiting that structure from the near will make you forget everything, only you would experience serenity and lovely music of from the fall of water from such a great height of the walls. Its a small park with big buildings around.

Liked hiking and beautiful serene waterfalls there. Take a look of waterfalls from up and if you feel it is safe then must go down near it. We went. Picnic areas under long green trees with fire pit is awesome, enough park benches and lot of parking. It's nice to go for biking, walking and hiking. There are many other parks around.

Relaxed on shores of lake, beautiful places to sit and chill with lovely sceneries. Those who enjoy fishing it is a great spot for them. You may visit the park for fishing, boating, hiking, biking, picnicking, beach, mini golf, boat ramps, shelter, kids play areas and campgrounds. Water in the lake is green due to algae.
likes: Family-friendly amenities (kids play areas, mini golf)

reviews_attraction.text: Awesome, amazingly natural site! Loved driving through Custer State Park. Very supportive staff. Although we visited amidst Pandemic but full care taken care of. A drive worth enjoyable between many of its beautiful spots like Legion Lake, Needles Highway, Stockade Lake, Sylvan Lake. Trails are worth to hike on.

Nice walking paved and natural trails. There are many trails, I liked the boardwalk and ledges trails. Glacier cave is also a scenic point. They have a Nature Play Area for kids, beautifully created and maintained. Enough parking area and park benches on trails. We can't bike here.

A nice and well maintained park, it has something for everyone Kids Play Area, walking trails through nature, paved trails, lake shore, lawns, playgrounds, picnic shelters, swings, park benches, baseball court, frisbee golf and grounds. Watching Sunset here was nice.

Magical!! Not an easy trail but was full of adventure. Rocky trail so watch your steps. Worth hiking for 3 miles. It says waterfall but if it doesn't rain much then you won't get to watch a fall. However trails there and natural views are captivating.

Loved walking on trails, the best thing colors in the sky during sunset along fall colors. Serene place. Campgrounds, beach, boat ramps, shelters, park benches, kids play area, trails to hike. Liked spotting deer, bucks from trails in the forest.

Nice but needs a lot maintainence in the park. However few people were camping there but water in the Elkhorn has been reduced, ramp is damaged, bugs in the grass. This has benches, grill, kids play area, fishing, park benches, ramp, mini golf.

Located in downtown, quite a happening place. Visited it to see season of light in Omaha downtown. Beautiful lighting on trees in Turner Park. Loved driving around this. Trails to walk, ping pong table at the entrance of the park.

Worth visiting. So much to know the history, adventures and about the minerals here. Very experiential tour. Staff at Meramec Cavern take care of safety of participants and natural resources. Amazing and mesmerizing formations!

Beautiful park! It has access to Current River. This place is under Ozark Scenic National Riverways. It s nice to relax here. There are campgrounds, boat ramps, trails. Get a map from visitor center and can explore it fully.

Superb! A place for all nature lovers. Overlook spot is just awesome. Seems it will be wonderful in Fall Season. Place is for family fun, picknicing, hiking, walking, relax and enjoy the wonderful views of nature.

Beautiful! Strolled around the falls. There are paved trails and craggy rocks you may walk on but be careful with the kids. A small bridge to walk and take a view of falling water, it has shades to relax.
Amazing natural trails for walking, biking, hiking.  Walking in loops through the rows of big and small trees is wonderful. Biking on trail is a fun. There is a kids play area and baseball field.
Amazing history and a demo for using fire arm was awesome to attend. Great monument. Watching blue water from the park trail was soothing. One can take a walk near the shore through paved trail.
