It s a small but nice and clean park. It has a small lake with waterfowls and walking trails. Park has lot of park benches with grill and kids play area.
Stunning views and wonderful Indian Ladder Trail spot. Must go there if you visit this state park. Fall season look will definitely be awesome.
Beautiful location and scenic views. Relax, enjoy icecream, coffee and the sound of falling water. It's a place for photography.
Beautiful and open park! A place to relax, lots of benches and shades around. Kids play area  and walking trails are available.

This is actually part of the Petroglyphs National Monument. The map in Google is wrong as of September 25, 2016, but that aside, look up the correct info and explore this place.  It is quite large and their is lots of space to explore.  I really enjoy Piedras Mercadas Canyon and Boca Negra the best.  However, you really should check out the volcanoes and other canyons.  Be warned, there are no trees and it can be hot and dry at times.

For a forest not out west, this one has some beautiful places to see.  They've done a really good job of maximizing trails in an area where national forests tend too be very patchy instead of continuous like they are out west.  Some of the trails are hard to follow due to being overgrown but it is the wilderness and they lack enough personnel and money to do everything.

What a neat urban forest area. There is a nice amount of trails for a city recreational area and they are actually maintained trails.  Something taste in this area.  Plus the area is free to use.  I'd love to see more areas like this because there is not enough open spaces for the amount of people here and that means most trails are too busy and loud.

If you've never been here, you will be amazed at the surreal scenery.  You just have to sled the white sand dunes and hike the back country dunes, but please take water and pay attention. Also, hook up with a ranger and learn about the crazy stream work fish that live in a amazing environment that'd kill most animals.

There is a reason this garden is in the top five in the nation . It is extremely nice and well laid out.  plus, when you buy a year membership, it's a great bargain. with a membership , not only do you get to go to the garden as much as you want , you can go to the zoo and the aquarium as often as you wish .

There is more to this place than most will ever figure out. So many hidden jewels. Arches, lava tubes, ruins sites and lots of solitude to list a few things. You could spend weeks here and still not see everything.  Rangers typically helpful too

For a Urban park, this one is very nice.  Many miles of trails. The trails are not always maintained well, so summer can be tough with weeds and ticks.  A little nosey but not horrible.  Jefferson City is lucky to have such a place as this.

When the trees mature and they get the community center in, it will be one of the city's best, but for now it is a nice park but it is still too new. It's hot in the summer.  Great in the cooler months and lots of space and parking.

We are so blessed to have so many trails and wilderness this close to the Metro.  A person could hike for weeks straight without hitting the same trail.  I love there are trails for most any time of the year as well.

Very nice park with lots of things to do. Only this that would be better are trails.  I'd love to see a park like this in Warren county not built next to such a busy 4 lane highway, but I'm grateful it's here.
St Louis is fortunate to have such a nice museum.  The building is achitecturally pleasing, and they have a wonderful collection of art.  Plus, unlike the zoo and park, it's not wall to wall people.
It deepens in your purpose as to how you'll view this area.  Fishing is great, hiking, not so much.  It has a lot of area but it is a bit busy, even in winter. Still glad it's available to use.
Neat lake with some nice trails. They aren't maintained super great, but I'm glad they are there.  It's a bit busy, but most people were respectful with regards to their noise level.
This was an unexpected surprise. I didn't expect it to be so doin but it was.  Got to even tried my hand at sheering a sheep. That was hysterical.  Go and take your kids.
It's a unique experience that you should try once.we take all our tourist friends and everyone enjoys it. Great views and fun. It's expensive, but a cool treat
For the area it's not bad.it's cheaper than most amusement parks.  Clean and Dave feeling. The water mania area is nice. The staff is rather nice too.
One of the best parks in town, with a awesome community center across the street.  The park is safe and clean, with lots of space to spread out.
It's pretty but too busy and noisy.  Moore like a city park feel too.  Glad it's there however.  It's some place quick to get to
Small museum with mostly fake fossils.  The trails are fun to hike but nothing to really see since the bone yard is filled in.
Spread out over 3 locations, it'll take all day to see, but so worth it.  The ruins are like no other, including Chaco Canyon.
Great place to knock around.  Only bad thing is you can here I-70 traffic more than you'd expect thought most of the area.
Nice access to several trails. Great views but it can be a bit busy and some of the trails are rugged, so be prepared.
We are so lucky to have such a great bio park.  We get a membership every year because we feel it's a bargain.
I'm not a car person, but this was so fascinating to see and to learn near things about the Corvette.
This is the coolest place. It's so neat that such a large cave is right there in the middle of town.

The rustic and striking personality of the tower is established by the natural stone construction rising from the top of the hill against the backdrop of open sky and expansive terrain. It is surrounded by lovely landscaping with Japanese overtones. Very appropriate as the site honors the state of peace between the United States and Japan. Their is also a historic reproduction of a bell  in the Japanese garden the original of which is in a city in Japan symbolizing their sister city relationship. An impressive pagoda at the edge of the bluff overlooks the lake offering not only a beautiful view but a place that can be reserved for events.There is a building housing restrooms located near the picnic area.

Primarily a place for baseball, it does provide spaces for children of all ages. The primary feature is 2 very nice baseball fields. There's also a small children's play area, unpaved walking paths, a parking lot,  pavilion, building for concessions, and wooded bike trails which I suspect were not part of the original plan but rather something kids established over time. A creek runs behind the baseball fields, and a bridge connects to a small open area of mowed grass bordered by a street, so not a great place for children to run around in.
dislikes: Limited safe open space for children

reviews_attraction.text: Nice little neighborhood park with a baseball field, full size basketball court, children's play area, small walking trail around the perimeter, and a pavilion. It's set back from the road, so there's less chance of children running out into the street. It's a good park for children, but very little for a couple on a date wanting to go for a walk. Not a park worth traveling for, but good for the immediate neighborhood.

I could spend days at this park. I once got lost on Pike Island after sunset and almost did spend days there. I prefer thinking of Pike Island as Bdote, the Native American meeting place, although nearby in the park was also a Native American concentration camp. Horrible history notwithstanding, the park is beautiful, Fort Snelling is fascinating, there are miles of walking trails, and it's a wonderful place to visit.

Nice neighborhood park connected by a tunnel to an elementary school playground. This park has a children's play area, a full size basketball court, a baseball field, a large open mowed grassy area, a pavilion, a hill for sledding, a parking lot, and walking trails. It doesn't have very much nature, and it borders streets a bit more than I would prefer. I always worry about children running out into the streets.

We had so much fun pretending to run from the giant robot Jesus. The wooden people in the Last Supper sculpture look a lot like the wooden people in the Peter Jackson movie Heavenly Creatures. We took a picture where I was pretending to be a waiter. "Seriously, just the bread and wine. We have some exquisite halibut." Oh, we had so much fun here. This place is great!

Cool tour. Nice slice of history. We went on this tour right after the Saint Paul Gangster Tour, and the two paired well. Apparently the caves also had some gangster history, with an implication that for all we know, bodies could be buried in there. Technically, these are not caves, but rather tunnels, since they were dug by humans and not naturally occurring

Goat Hill Park appears to be a part of the Lexington-Diffley complex which includes athletic fields, children's play area, a skate park, and walking  trails, each of which has its own Google maps designation. The area called Goat Hill Park seems to center on an area with baseball fields, although it could also reference the children's play area

We went as part of a group and stayed over night. We got there early enough to watch them feed, which was impressive. They devoured a deer. This roadkill was definitely appreciated. we watched the wolves until dark. After dark, we listened to the wolves. It was an amazing and powerful experience getting to spend time so close to these wolves.

Nice neighborhood park with a baseball field, basketball court, tennis courts, ice rink in the winter, batting cage, children's play area, picnic tables, pavilion, parking areas, and a restrooms.i appreciate the way the basketball court and tennis courts are set up inside the ice rink area, ensuring that the space can be utilized year round.

Wonderful park with many amenities. There's a band shell, a children's play areas, picnic tables, pavilions, tennis courts, basketball courts, baseball fields, a lake, volleyball courts, walking trails, wooded areas, and parking lots. Some of the pavilions can be reserved. It was delightful walking through the natural areas around the lake.

Great swimming beach, fishing dock, concession stand, children's play area, picnic tables, pavilions, tennis courts, basketball hoop, volleyball net, walking trails,  and a parking lot. This park has many amenities. The lake is beautiful with lily pads. The park has many old trees. It's a very nice park with options for a variety of ages

This is a wonderful place for a walk, or a date. It has Ingress portals and Poke Gym. I did enjoy the previous installations immensely over several years, so there were strong feelings attached to them, with memories of experiences around each, but I am looking forward to creating new memories around the new installations

The May Day celebration is legendary. I loved it so much that I bought a house nearby just to be a part of such a diverse and artistic community. It's also one of the most densely Pagan areas of the cities. The park is a popular place for rituals for Pagans, but popular for walking and playing for everyone else

Beautiful path through nature by a lake. Every photo could be an oil painting. Seriously, I plan to put my photos through an oil painting filter. It was wonderful seeing so many ducks and bees. There's a tremendous variety of wild flowers. It is just majestic watching the sun set over the park

Good park. Nice picnic areas, good place for fishing, and plenty of trails. The power of the river against the dam is a moving experience. I love standing on the spillway and just feeling the power. The place is a nice place to go on a date. There are also several Ingress portals

Bob Dylan is one of the most influential musicians of the twentieth century, and this is where he lived until he was 6 years old. It's an ordinary house in the middle of the block. They don't offer tours, and there's no museum,  but it's a significant place right here in Duluth

This is one of the most sacred places in the area. I visit it with reverence and awe. I loved it before they enhanced the park aspect, and it's even more enjoyable now. I just wish that engineers would stop engaging in activities which reduce the flow of water to the site.

I love this park. We had many Pagan rituals here because of how well it preserves nature, while accommodating easy access and parking. Also the pavilions  are reservable for very reasonable prices. It has great views great trails and great spaces. It is an amazing park.

I find much of the art here to be truly inspirational, by which I mean I look at it and say, "Ah hell, I could make art better than that," and so I do. Every time I  am in there, I come up with an idea of something that I can do better. I do really like their Labyrinth.

Nice little neighborhood park. It has a children's play area, basketball hoop, and some open grass. It's bordered by back yards , woods, and dead end streets, so there's little chance of children running out into traffic. Excellent park for children 5 years old to 11.

Beautiful and huge. Practicing witchcraft,I spend a lot of time in cemeteries communing with the ancestors and this cemetery is exceptional. Gorgeous tombstones, monuments and mausoleums. I often see people jogging here. The residents seem like good people

I had a good time here. Every time I go there, I remember the first time I was there when a rather confused older gentleman complained about the animatronic lecturer that refused to acknowledge him or answer any questions, and he regarded it as very rude.

This is perfect for little children. My year old granddaughter loves the padded area with uneven walking options. She is exploring walking, and this is wonderful for her development. She also enjoyed watching the wind tube blow things up and out the top.

Nice neighborhood park with a children's play area, 2 baseball fields, a basketball hoop, an ice rink with a warming house, a large mowed grassy area, walking trails, and a parking lot. It has something to offer many people of diverse ages and interests

This is a very unique monument that can be seen from the road.  There is a trail that you can take across the railroad tracks to get to it but if you decide to take the trail please take extra care on and around the tracks as they are used multiple times on a daily basis.  The monument itself is 23 feet high and 30 feet square.

--Usually thought of as a Union monument, the large pyramid in front of you was in fact erected by the Confederate Memorial Literary Society. In 1897, the society contacted Virginia railroad executives asking them to erect markers at historically significant sites along their lines. The president of the Richmond, Fredericksburg, and Potomac Railroad embraced the proposal, but rather than simply erected a sign, he constructed a stone pyramid modeled after the memorial to the unknown Confederate dead buried in Richmond’s Hollywood Cemetery.

The monument here marks the point where General George G. Meade’s Union division penetrated the boggy gap in “Stonewall” Jackson’s lines on December 13, 1862. Over the years it has become known as the Meade Pyramid. The monument in not accessible.-- (Source: Historical Marker)

I took my grandmother to this museum as she has always wanted to go visit.  I went expecting that this museum would be something that only my grandmother would like and my brother and I would just have to "suffer through" for her sake.  I was pleasantly surprised that that wasn't the case. The quilts inside the museum were not like any quilts that I've ever seen before.  They were more like works of art.  The different styles, colors, and sizes were amazing.  The kind of care and love that were put into each quilt by their artist clearly shows.  I am not a quilter or "quilt person" but I really enjoyed this museum!  I would recommend this museum for quilters and non-quilters alike.  It's definitely something to see if you are in the area.

(I know there wasn't any photography or videos allowed in the museum but I couldn't help but snapping off a few shots.  I have included them with my review.  I hope the artists can understand that I only took the pictures to highlight their works and attract more visitors to the museum.)

This museum is amazing! It's huge! If you want to know anything about the history of the area this is the place to go. The women that work there are very friendly and made me feel like we were family from the start. They took 2 1/2 hours out of their busy day to give a personal free tour of the place for me, my grandmother, and my great aunt. I cannot thank them enough for giving their time and sharing their knowledge with us! There are 4 stories to the museum and in the basement there is a hidden entrance to a cave under the town. It is one of the best little museums I have ever visited!  It doesn't look like much from the outside but the inside is full of priceless gems of our nation's history.

The Cove is a great place for families.  It is actually a part of Concord Park.  It includes a sand volleyball court, a nice children's playground, many picnic tables, a pavilion, a outdoors store where you can rent various manual water equipment to use on the lake.  It also has a man-made beach and a small paved walking trail.  The view from the park is always beautiful.  There is also always an abundance of water fowls that you can watch or feed them with the food that is provided at the park.  It is usually crowded during the summer and nice days but still has a very relaxing feel to it.

There are also 8 Pokestops and one gym for the mobile game Pokemon GO.

This monument is a pleasant and unexpected surprise for anyone traveling in the back country of Kentucky.  The concrete obelisk is 351 feet high.  It is the tallest unreinforced concrete structure in the world.  It is also the second tallest obelisk in the world after the Washington Monument which stands at 555 feet high.  It's the fifth tallest monument in the United States. The view from the top of the monument is breathtaking!  Because the surrounding land is completely flat, you can see for miles and miles on a clear day.

In addition to the obelisk there is a nice playground for kids and a nice little museum and gift shop.  It's definitely worth a visit!

Chatham Manor is a Georgian-style mansion home completed in 1771 by farmer and statesman William Fitzhugh, after about three years of construction, on the Rappahannock River in Stafford County, Virginia, opposite Fredericksburg. It was for more than a century the center of a large, thriving plantation, and the only private residence in the United States to be visited by George Washington, Thomas Jefferson, Abraham Lincoln, and Dwight D. Eisenhower.

It's a beautiful place to visit. With a large beautiful garden, enormous house to tour, and a beautiful view of the entire city of Fredericksburg, it's a must see for young and old alike!

This is a great little park in the town of Farragut.  The Farragut branch library is within the park and a beautiful clean little stream runs through it.  There is a short trail winding up and down a large hill. The restrooms are clean and the park is very well maintained.  My only complaint is that it is small and right up against a busy 4 lane road.

P.S.  There are 9 Pokestops (4 in the same area) and 2 Gyms (literally a few feet away from one another) for the mobile game Pokemon Go that are located here.  It's a really popular place to play and enjoy the game.

Mount Vernon is a very beautiful place full of history and information about the first President of the United States of America.  Stepping foot on the grounds is like stepping back in time.  There is a truly special feeling that one gets when they set foot on the grounds. The museum is amazing as well! Don't be alarmed by the amount of vehicles in the parking lot.  Once you enter the property it almost seems like you are the only person there. It is a must see for everyone!

This state park is a great place to visit. Alvin C. York is a true American hero. Here you can visit his home, where he worked, and even where he was laid to rest after he passed away. It is the perfect place to bring your family and give them a history lesson and show them what it truly means to be an American. The staff is very friendly and the buildings and trails are very well kept. This is truly a gem in a beautiful country.

I've gone here several times throughout my life. I even spent the night there once when I was a child. It's a really cool cave! Where else can you take a boat ride underground?! Our tour guide Savannah was nice and a good tour guide. The only thing I wish they would do would be to update their tour guide script. She said the same things that have been said for at least 25 years, probably longer.

This is a great place to come and learn about the history of Clarksville! The Fort itself is very well preserved and you are able to walk around inside it. The grounds are very well maintained. The museum is free (at least it was when I visited) and tells the story of Clarksville's past. It is full of artifacts as well.  It's definitely worth a visit if you are in the area!

This is a very beautiful small park in the middle of a residential area.  There are a few picnic tables there and several fields to walk and play on.  There is a little wildlife here as well.  It's well kept and kind of a local hidden gem.  It is a nice little place to relax and recharge.  Please take the time to read the monument while you are there.

Don't let this place fool you.  It's a great place to visit.  The museum is really small and disappointing but the tour through the different train cars really made it great! Our tour guide was wonderful and knowledgeable about the railroad, the different train cars, and it's history. It's worth a visit if you are in the area.

This bridge scared me to death driving over it!  There is no solid flooring, only see through metal grates.  It's a very skinny two lane bridge.  The grate flooring made my car feel hard to control.  Forget paying money to ride a rollercoaster.  You can get your adrenaline rush for free driving over this bridge!

This is a wonderful place full of history that you will never learn in school. The story of these people is both interesting and sad. It was a lot of fun walking through the different buildings and imagining the ones that are no longer there. This place is a must see for anyone who is passing through.

This is a nice little park. The waterfalls are beautiful! I wish you could swim in the water but I understand why it's not allowed. The trails could use a little work and they need to repair an overlook that's been damaged by erosion. But the waterfalls are well worth a visit.

We went there to see the fields of sunflowers but were a week late as most of them had already wilted.  It's a nice area to walk around in.  It's a bit too close to the city for my liking but it seems like a nice place to walk for locals who live near the area.

It's a well maintained trailhead. The restrooms are nothing more than a permanent porter potty but they look nice. There is a picnic table and the gravel parking lot and miles of gravel road that lead to it is well maintained. The trail itself is beautiful!

Great park in the middle of the city! The paths are very well taken care of.  The wildlife is abundant.  The atmosphere is quiet and peaceful.  It's a great place for a walk or just to go and reflect.  Overall it's just a very beautiful place!

Great Aquarium in a cool town! The Aquarium is very nice.  It is pretty big.  There is a nice moving walkway through a tunnel underwater where you can see all sorts of fish swimming around.  It's definitely worth a trip.

This is a nice park with a great view of the natural arch. There are also a trail that will take you to the arch. It's a nice place to visit. It does cost $3 to visit though. But the money goes to help maintain the park.

We traveled over an hour to visit the tour only to find out that it was closed the entire week of July 4th.  It would have been nice if they had updated their website to let people know that they were going to be closed.

This is a very nice little museum and well worth the price to get in.  The staff is very friendly. Its filled with interesting information and artifacts. It's definitely worth a visit if you are in the area.
One of my favorite places to hike. There are over 80 miles of trails, many beautiful waterfalls, and plenty of wildlife. It's an awesome place!
This place is a great little place to visit. The mill is a sight to behold. The scenery is beautiful as well. It is definitely worth a trip.

Pleasant surprise! Hadn't visited this Zoo in years- my mistake. Exhibits laid out on opposite sides of the freeway connected by a sky bridge. Giraffes, elephants, rhinos, gorrillas, orangutans, crocs, and wolves on site. There is a reptile house, aquarium, greenhouse, aviary, and primate house. They also have a kiddie splash park, ropes course and ziplines  (seasonal) as well as a beautiful amphitheater. Thumbs up...
likes: Interactive activities (splash park, ropes course, ziplines)
Educational facilities (reptile house, aquarium, greenhouse, aviary, primate house)

reviews_attraction.text: The Hall is an awesome experience each/ every time. My favorite is always the constant stream of live/ local music. The exhibits are updated accordingly with features and new inductees. The Rolling Stone covers and interviews are amazing. The food options are wonderful with representation from several of Cleveland's culinary talents.

Nice little park , off Lakeshore Blvd, to watch the sun rise/ sun set. It also works as a "chill spot" if you want to ditch someone shopping in the area and enjoy some peace/ quiet. There are picnic tables, grills,benches, swings, and an observation deck. There is a Fire Station attached and the area is regularly patrolled.

Very cool eclectic little space within the Gordon Square Art District. The pinball machines are amusing (especially Deadpool), and Adult beverages are available at the bar with finger food items. They also offer board games for customer use. My favorite part was the music- classic rap, rock, grunge, and punk elements.

Back to basics visit this classic slice of americana. It is a stationary carnival for lack of a better words. Food, fun, games, a beach, a marina, and an affordable water park. Rides are super cluncky,cla gy ,and herky jerky but that's the charm. See how far we have come in amusement park technology.  Thumbs up!

Great place to learn about the history of the State of Kentucky. I love the atrium/ garden area outside. I would not recommend for little children it’s not geared to hold their interest. Gift shop is cool and the photo opportunities are endless. It’s a beautiful building.

Renovations ongoing but the utilization of the this space is great. The memorial is fantastic and representative of all the branches of service. Photo opportunities with a tank and helicopter, bordered by a creek, also housing picnic areas and a playground.

Decent experience, nothing of note. The admission fee is lower than most zoos I have visited. Their are renovations being done but there were too many animals off exhibit. No interaction from employees during my visit. Lots of room for improvement...

Love these smaller lesser known museums. This one didn't disappoint. There is much history on display and the layout is open and flows from one display to the next. Admission is more than reasonable, they usually have Groupon available.

Full disclosure very small aquarium but big things come in small packages. Highlight is the glass tunnel which offers amazing views of the aquatic specimens. Take advantage of the special events/ programs- swim with sharks!

Great place to be. You will be pleasantly surprised by the interactivity and volume of the exhibits. No better place for photo ops and exposure to the beauty of nature. Located in cluster with other museums- visit them all

New aquatics center is amazing, this will be my family's "go to" spot for the time being. Concerts and  festivals are scheduled through the summer. There are multiple areas to cookout, tennis courts, and a small pond.

Smaller installation of the Metroparks System,  charming nonetheless.Good pavilion with electric access, Bunn Lake, and several loops through woods. It's a nice little secret if you happen to be in the area.

Great park to catch a night time baseball, soccer, or rugby game. Playground and volleyball pit and great concession areas. Great place for a creek walk and park is attached to Cleveland Metroparks Zoo!
Not just for kids! Very interactive exhibits will keep all of your senses engaged. Located next to the Rock Hall and First Energy Stadium- make a day of it. Omni max theater also on site
Get ready to get your steps in. This Zoo was awesome and I will be visiting regularly. The aquarium is fantastic. The polar bear is a born entertainer and deserves his own spin off.
Smaller zoo with a lot of surprises. You will get your steps in though. My favorites are the bears, the carousel, and the jellyfish. The staff is great and very knowledgeable
Visiting the toboggan chutes as much as possible during the season. I love this place- tobogganing, zip lining, and a fantastic chalet as the center piece.
Decent area with some great views. The tennis courts seem to be well maintained the baseball diamonds- not so much. There is a nice dog and skate park.
Nice mid-sized aquarium geared more towards kids. A lot of interactive exhibits, gift shop, and cafeteria ( with multiple options!)
Nice spot for beginner canoeing, paddle boarding, or boating. Took the voyager cruise with my family- big thumbs up from all.
It is similar to other Ripley's I have visited across the country. They got me with Optimus Prime! I love the Transformers.
Great insight to history of the Great Lakes region and into the vital role of the Bayfront economically and historically.
Cars galore from every source you can think of and ones you forgot. Admission is pricey but not a deal breaker.
Cool park in the center of a great neighborhood. Explore this area on a Sunday afternoon you will love it.

It was a very nice place to hike really close off the Interstate 24. It was nice to get out of the car and stretch the legs . The trail was well marked and TVA workers were there working on improvements clearing out sections of the fallen or dead trees to open up the land for more plant growth. If you visit the alltrails app will lead you back onto the hwy but the trailhead is just a few feet from the onramp. The trail if you hike it clockwise will take you up the mountain thru lots of rock formations and then when you get to the top you can see views of Nickajack lake. It will wind around the lake then descend back down to complete the loop. Enjoy!!

This is a small but very lovely park. The General Store serves as the visitors center and they have it set up with old relics and things to make it look like it was back in Sgt. York's day. It was really nice. They also sell candy, souvenir and other stuff in there. They also have some old stuff from the war in there. The Park Rangers we're very nice and informative. We went across the swinging bridge which I LOVED! The water was the most beautiful shade of turquoise blue. The very best part was the old Grist Mill. It was amazing and the river was beautiful. It was DEFINITELY worth the two hour drive to visit.

I was surprised that it wasn't as hard as I expected after reading reviews saying that it is not good for hiking. I found it easy and worth the hiking. There was one person biking and we had to step off the trail but he was very pleasant and didn't mind that we were sharing the trail with bikers. The only thing I found a bit hard was navigating the trail as it isn't very clearly marked. The trails have a lot of turns but we made it ok. It was late when we started and getting dark quick, the biker even kind of waited to make sure we made it out ok. Nice Trail and I will be back again, next time just earlier.

This area offers breathtaking views, great trails, spectacular waterfalls . Something for everyone . There are spots for picnics and grilling out . You can walk easy trails or longer harder trails. The views are spectacular and there are several waterfalls that are in close proximity to each other. We visited Stone Door , Laurel Falls and Overlook then we drove a short 10 minutes to get to Greeter Falls which was gushing full of water after the rains the night before. It was absolutely BEAUTIFUL. I love this area and it was worth the 2.5 hours we drove to get there. Can't wait to return.

OMG such a GORGEOUS PARK. BREATHTAKINGLY BEAUTIFUL!!! We hiked to Rainbow Falls at the advice of the ranger and she was right on point. It was SO worth the hike! We went on up to Turtleback Falls as well and it was amazing as well. Fabulous way to spend the day. We came from Nashville to visit the parks here and it was worth the drive. I highly recommend this park it is a must see.

Very beautiful park and hiking trails. We saw turtles, great blue heron, cardinal, chipmonk and an owl while hiking the lake trail. We also enjoyed the visitors center as well. Very friendly lady working in the visitors center and I enjoyed talking with her. We can't wait to go back to visit Radnor Lake State Park again.

I've been in a few caves but this is one of the BEST ! There was lots to see including the pool of water that was flowing inside the cave. Lots of unique features and formation's. We even saw a few bars flying around, although they were shy . The guide was very nice and funny. We loved our visit to Appalachian Caverns.

I have been to Gatlinburg before and have always wanted to go to the Space Needle. This time I was determined to go and FINALLY got to go. I loved it. The views were SPECTACULAR! I am SOOOOO glad we went up. You can see the whole town of Gatlinburg from up there. The views of the mountains were AMAZING!!

We spent a few hours walking around and watching the wild life. We saw lots of turtles, fish, and beavers. We even saw a small but shy little snake. The plants and flowers were beautiful. Lots of birds too. There's a discovery center too but it was closed on Mondays. Looking forward to visiting again.

Beautiful park with natural trails in the woods. Lots of various types of plants and colorful mushrooms. You can walk a short trail or combine them for a longer hike. Loved the trail that runs beside the creek. Afterword you can relax in the rocking chairs on the back deck at the Nature Center.

Hiked a portion of The Trail of Tears there is so much historical significance there and it was heart moving experience to walk on these trails. Hope they find funding to maybe put some replicas of camp or something of historical significance to illustrate what went on here .

Great way to see the park. You get to cover a lot more cause you drive. There are a lot of spots to stop and get out of the car to explore the area. Historical old buildings to learn about life here before the park formed.

Absolutely BEAUTIFUL!  One of my favorite parks and best waterfalls ! There are more than one waterfall and tons of trails to hike. There's a beach area and gift shop as well . They have picnic areas and a campground too.

One of the most beautiful waterfalls I have seen. The trail starts off with a bunch of stairs leading up to a very rocky trail but not too bad that most people can do it with no problem. Totally worth the effort.
Loved it!! So many different themes and the decorations were fantastic. I just heard about this place a few days ago and we wanted to check it out. I am so glad we did! The kids really enjoyed it!
We love this aquarium!! So much to see and plenty of things to do and explore for the children. Learning couldn't be more fun!! We went with the grandkids and they had the time of their life.
Loved this beautiful waterfall. We visited in January and it was frozen. Absolutely breathtaking. Easy to walk to not far from parking lot. Would love to see it again when the spring comes.
This is a FABULOUS park. Great place to spend time. Beautiful trails and lots of wildlife to enjoy. Staff super friendly and answered all my questions. Thanks Edgar Evins State Park !!
Great place to spend the day. Walk the beautiful Greenway and enjoy the beautiful outdoors. We enjoyed feeding the ducks at the little lake in the park. Very relaxing park.
Nice paved trail that later turns into gravel . The trail ends at a small but beautiful waterfall. The lake was nice and we saw ducks and a goose swimming.
Nice Greenway with lots of things to see. We saw an Owl and a Blue Heron while on our walk today. It was very enjoyable walk. Hope to visit again soon.
Beautiful park with fabulous Trails. We passed thru Cedar Glades, the river ,  wooded area . Much to see such a find right in the middle of the city.
Beautiful park that has a museum, waterfalls, camp grounds, hiking trails, picnic areas,  clean bath houses. I am enjoying my stay here.
So interesting and pleased that they actually protected this historical site. It was very interesting to check out the building!
One of the many beautiful waterfalls and trails here in North Carolina. Was very nice and a great way to spend the day.

OH MY HEAVEN - EXPENSIVE!  Just to walk through? Really?  Even the gift shop was expensive! (I mean, REALLY Expensive).  On our travels we had the pleasure of going to many different places and seeing the cost of "Tourist Memorabilia" all across the Southland - this place was more expensive than them all.  And the tour was super costly as well.  We have a family of 5 going with us - which causes us to have to evaluate where the money is getting spent - This would have taken a big chunk of change out of our pocket just to walk through to see where some stars performed, and we would not even see anyone special.  What's the point of that?  SO, we took pictures outside at the giant guitars and left.

Traffic getting into this place (Because it's also right by a mall) is seriously HELL - We spent more time just trying to get into this place and park than we should have.  There should be an easier way to get here or get access to it - but the location is just poorly laid out. Also, I have a conceal carry weapon, and they would not let me go through with my weapon on , which only leaves me feeling unsafe in today's society.

We were pleasantly surprised by this tour.  It's not something that I thought that the kids would really be into - but I dragged them along anyway.  By the time we were done, they had all but converted to using Tabasco exclusively.  The gift shop gave a little something extra with our purchases too - which was a pleasant surprise as well.  Totally worth the visit and the walk through to see the process of how they make this delicious hot sauce and what goes into each bottle.  We were there while the assembly line was running as well - and that was super amazing to see also.  It is a self guided tour, and you can take as long as you like to really look at everything and read about this making of Tabasco.

We were a LITTLE thrown off about the Guinness World Records Adventure place - I thought it would be more like the other Ripley's establishments in Gatlinburg.  We were wrong.  I wish that we had more time while we were there.  This was not necessarily a museum type like the other Ripleys - this was where you could play games and challenge to see if you can beat the record holders time.  We spent HOURS of time in here playing games (until it closed).  I wish that we had more time because it was so much fun that we didn't even realize that the time was passing so quickly.  There was not as much as I thought when it came to reading about records, but the gaming was pretty awesome.

An amazing experience.  One of the best parts about this tour is that part of the boat is indoors so even though it was cold and rainy, we were able to stay toasty warm.  The Naturalist Team gave us a lot of information.  And even though the whales were sighted way  out of our way, they took the time to drive everyone there so that we could get a glimpse of the Orca's in their natural habitat.  We really enjoyed our experience with this team.  They even took pictures and emailed them to everyone as part of the excursion experience.  Would definitely recommend to anyone who has a love for nature and wants to get up close and personal with the whales.

Christmas-time is one of the best times to come and visit Temple Square.  They always have nativities set up as a tribute to other nations, and the grounds are decorated nicely.  I know that in the upcoming years, as they do construction on the Salt Lake Temple, that the grounds will not have nearly the same amount of lights and display as they have had recently, but that's alright.  Just make sure that you plan appropriately.  The grounds are beautiful and they always have flowers or lights or something that is seasonally appropriate going on.  A nice quiet area in the heart of the city to eat lunch and ponder on life.

This park has 4 Soccer Fields / 4 Baseball Diamonds - so if you are going there to be part of a team sport, you might have to look around to find your team. As with most parks in Utah, if the fields are numbered, we don't know how to tell... The park is nice and open, has plenty of trees and shade as well as a pavilion for barbecuing or meeting with family.  The restrooms are clean and the small playground is nice. It also has a walking path around the entire park.

This time of year the Mosquitoes are getting yucky - as well as the gnats - so bring some bug spray just in case you are out there for a while.

Ripley's does not disappoint - it's always such a fun place to visit with so many things to see and do.  In fact, so many things to read that there is not usually a lot of time to get it all in.  This museum was well laid out and packed full of freaky and fun things.  Check GROUPON and a few other places to see if you can get discount tickets for the Ripley's adventures and sites.  Gatlinburn and Pigeon Forge are full of Ripley's places and you will want to see them all, so make sure that you get a good deal on your adventure!

We purchased Mini Golf as part of our Ripley's ticket adventure.  When you get there, there are two courses to choose from - all are fantastic.  The little gofers and outhouse jokes are awesome. My family and I did all 18 holes and it was so pleasant.  The course has lots of trees so it was in the shade, super easy to walk, well taken care of.  We would definitely go again when we visit Gatlinburg.  Ripley's does a great job of keeping everything well tended.

So, we have been to a lot of aquariums in my lifetime.  The aquarium of the America's in New Orleans, LA, is probably the best one that I have been to - however, this Aquarium is right up there with that one.  Such an easy flow to get through everything - you can even touch Jellies!  It was a great experience, clean inside, a good flow- plenty of room for all of the people.  We definitely recommend and would go again!

The Gallery of Iconic Guitars is so worth the trip.  It's truly amazing to see so many different guitars in one place.  The collection is very comprehensive.  Considering the fact that Gibson shut down their factory where you could truly get your hands on a splendid guitar, this is a great second option (Now a first - Thanks Gibson for nothing!)  GO VISIT!  It's a must see in Nashville.

I think that the Fort is open on every day of the year  - well preserved and shows the history of the settlers in Bluff.  Totally worth going, but make sure that you plan for plenty of time so that you can listen to all of the stories in each of the houses that are there.  Also, the video is really cool - talks about how they had to lower wagons over the cliff walls - super crazy.

You want to be able to do the Jungle Gardens at the same time that you go to the Tabasco Factory.  The drive through is beautiful - watch out for the Alligators. There are a few short, easy walks to allow you to get out of your vehicle.  Plan for a day where you can get there before the rain (If possible).  The Magnolia trees were also blooming - it was beautiful and amazing.

The Salt Lake Temple is always a beautiful place to visit in Downtown Salt Lake City. The grounds are quiet and serene, and you can really meditate about life in a place like this. Remember, it is closed for the next 4-5 years - so all you really get to do is come down here and look at the construction as it is renovated... but when it is open, it's a great place to be.

It was a great experience!! You can touch and interact with anything here. The stingray tank is amazing. You can feed them and touch them. Get lots of tokens!! You can also feed the birds and touch all kinds of things. We had a great time. The wrist band allows you a full day access so you can return if you would like. Groupon has good deals too.

Disappointing - this was not near as good as Madame Tussauds in Vegas. The Wax figures did not look like the real people - not even close. Also, at Madame Tussauds, you can touch take lots of pictures with the wax figures. Here, at Louis Tussaud's - there were people around telling you not to touch and such. It was a real bummer.

The hike is a little bit steep (If you are taking the main wall and not going out to the three kings).  It's a great hike and the pathway is clearly marked with things to not miss.   Bring a little bit of water with you if you plan on going in the middle of the afternoon - it does get hot down here.

12 Miles before you reach Monticello, there is a turn off towards Canyonlands and Newspaper Rock.  This is about 12 miles from the main road.  It's easy to find, just a short (Maybe 50 foot) Walk from the parking lot to the petroglyphs.  There is a restroom there too.

We play soccer here - it's a lovely park.  There are two sides to the park - One is close to the Botanical Garden walkways (Very lovely) and the other is across the street.  Both are excellent areas for play in a safe environment. We love it here!

As with most parks around this area - the fields are not clearly numbered and this park is so large we could not find the party we were meeting up with.  Needs more trees - but it is sufficient for the soccer game that we went to.

He had our socially distanced company meeting here. The space was open and clean. Everything is spread out so you can be distanced from people playing sports or children on the playground. There is a nice pavilion here as well.

I hope that they always have a Tiger! :)  Mike was out, lounging in the little river that they have for him.  The Habitat is clean, and well kept.  A good place for Any Tiger - but especially for Mike.
Wilson Arch is RIGHT OFF the road on your way to Monticello - Just past Hole in the rock. Easy to find, great spot to stop and take pictures if you didn't go into the Arches National Park
Nice little area with an easy walk path around the park. 5 Pokestops - What?  And right by the Library. Has a splash pad and they do movies and events in the park. Well Lit and Safe.
We love the zoo!  Even when it's crowded you can still get around and see all of the animals!  Hogle Zoo is a wonderful family environment, and well laid out too.
Lovely Place for a walk right in the midst of downtown San Antonio. Lots of Restaurants - But all of them are a little pricey.

This park has some great and some not so great aspects. The train is really cool and it has just been refurbished and made even cooler and much safer than before. However, it still isn't safe the steps are very steep, and although there's a better rail than before it would still be very easy for any kid to climb through. It's great for bigger kids, but definitely not for younger ones. This seems to be the theme for the whole park though, great for big kids, terrible for small ones. The playground equipment is all very tall with plenty of drop offs. The only medium sized slides are only accessible by a rope ladder, a rock climbing wall, and a steep bridge, making it difficult for small children to get to. The only equipment for small kids is a couple of swings. There is also no fence around the park and it's right on the main street, so once again, very dangerous. Now, this park is great if your kids are bigger, but if you have little ones I would stick to Pershing Park or Paris Park.

It was kind of disappointing. We got the at about 9:30 (because we had to drive around searching for the visitor's center) and they were already out of tickets for the day. The visitor's center is about five blocks away and I guess you need to be there when it opens if you want to get tickets for the tour. So we could see the outside and that's it. There isn't really anything in the visitor's center besides a gift shop and a 12 minute movie. We were lucky to stumble across people coming out of the Noble House b across the street (Truman's aunt and uncle's house where he stayed while courting his wife) and it's set up with displays like a museum so that was cool to see. The ranger DID NOT inform us that this was here and part of the historic site even though we (and several other groups) were upset that we couldn't do the tour or really mitch of anything.

If you live in Wichita or are visiting, GO HERE! This is a great place to bring the kids or to go for some solitude. The trails are in wonderful condition. They are paved other than the boardwalk area. You can see many native species while out walking and if you start at the visitor's center first you can get food for the turtles. There are lots of benches along the path to rest or have a picnic too!

The visitor's center is amazing. There are fantastic exhibits about native plants and animals including several live animals such as an owl, kestrel, frog, and lizards. There is also an aquarium with native fish. The displays have tons of information and they are interactive for children. All of the displays are very professionally done. The gift shop has some really great stuff too!

This is a must do if you're in the area, and it's free!

The tower itself is a really cool state of the art lookout point. It costs $8 and an elevator takes you to the top. From the top you have a 360° view of the area and is a really pretty view. Now, if you're afraid of heights you will probably be just fine once you're in the top of the tower because to just see out, not down (this was the case for 2 in our group with a bad fear of heights). The elevator has a glass wall though and that really affected my son who is afraid of heights.

Once you get to the top and see the view that's it though, unless you purchase the zipline tickets.

It was a very nice, clean facility.

Probably the worst visitor's center I've been too. The ranger was not friendly or helpful. She didn't tell us about other parts of the site (Noble Home) that were could visit without a tour ticket. There are no displays about Truman in the visitor's center. There is a 12 minute video about Truman and his wife, but that's all it's about, nothing about him growing up or his presidency or anything like that, so don't expect that. The gift shop is pretty good. This is probably the smallest visitor's center I've been to and there just wasn't much there and it's a ways from the actual home so it's hard to find.

This fort is a wonderful piece of history to visit. All of the buildings are restored beautifully and you can see what life was like for soldiers stationed here. During our visit the museum was being disassembled so we did not get to visit it, but the visitor's center was clean with very nice bathrooms. All of the park rangers were helpful and knowledgeable. Our favorite part was the blacksmith's shop. The blacksmith patiently explained what he was doing to my children and made them a chain link.

This is a nice, large park. It has three separate playground areas for little, medium, and big kids. There is a very nice shelter area, with bathrooms and running water,  that can be reserved for birthday parties, reunions, or other events. It is located just west of Cowley College. To the west is the Arkansas City Ag building and some tennis courts and to the north is the public pool. This park has lots of trees for shade. It is the home of the annual car show as well.

This is a great park to visit with kids. We took a 3 year old and an 18 month olds and they had a blast digging for crystals and playing in the sand. The crystals were very ready to find and we very quickly had a large pile of them. We had the place to ourselves and I was shocked that there weren't more people taking advantage of this unique state park. The few staff members we encountered were very helpful, but the visitor's center was small and only had one bathroom.

Great place but I took off a star because it's day use only. There's picnic tables and walking trails outside but you have to be out and they close the gate at 5pm. We got there kind of late so we had to rush through the museum, but it was great! The gift shop didn't have a ton, but what they did have was very good and the ranger was awesome! She was very knowledgeable and helpful. If you're pressing through the area, definitely stop and check it out!

This place is amazing! The only negative is that you can't take pictures inside. Younger have so many artifacts as well as being modeled after the titanic. The staff were extremely knowledgeable. When you go in you're given a boarding pass of an actual passenger and at the end you find out if that passenger survived. My entire family enjoyed the museum, including my 3 and 5yo boys. We all learned something new too! It's definitely worth a visit!
likes: Facilities & Services: Knowledgeable Staff, Interactive Experience

reviews_attraction.text: This is a wonderful children's museum! The exhibits are all hands-on and very high quality. My children couldn't get enough of the airplane exhibit! The staff were all very friendly and helpful. The entire museum, including the bathrooms, was very clean. The dome theater was huge and the Kurds lived the show, although there are no booster seats so the seats are hard for little ones to keep down. It is a little pricey, but it is worth it!

Great food! Great entertainment! Fun for the whole family!
The food is delicious and they feed you enough to eat for a week. I shared with my 3 year old and still took a lot home.
The show is a lot of fun. If you like singing, dancing, and animals this is for you! The highlight of the show is definitely the Roman rider, but there are horses, bison, pigs, dogs, and acrobats. This is the must see show in Branson!

I was pleasantly surprised by this museum! The exhibits were very professional. There were hands on things for the kids. The fossils that were found right here in Kansas were amazing to see and it was a great educational opportunity for the kids. The neatest part was the dinosaurs that actually move. This museum is definitely worth the visit!

Silver Dollar City is the best!! This was the fitst trip for my three year old and he loved it! The reenactors are always amazing and the rides are great. This trip we mostly stuck to the little kids areas and there was more than enough to keep us busy all day! Make sure to get some apple butter before you leave!

This was way cooler than I was led to believe! To quote my four-year-old, "That's the biggest egg I've ever seen!" The sheer size was very impressive when we caught our first glimpse. The symbolism of the egg is very interesting and the work put in to make it was really cool. It was definitely worth the detour.

This is a nice big park with some cool history (once upon a time it was a horse track). There is a large parking lot, tons of open space, a duck pond, a wildlife exhibit, and a splash pad. The playground is a good size with areas for different sizes of kids. There is also a nice walking/ jogging path.
likes: Diverse facilities (duck pond, wildlife exhibit, splash pad)

reviews_attraction.text: This is such a nice park! The playground is a perfect size for both little and big kids. There's an open area with a backstop for baseball. There are lots of mature trees all there is plenty of shade during most of the day. The only bad thing is that it is very close to a pretty busy road.

Such a neat place to visit! All of the buildings are really interesting and the craftsmanship is amazing! There are a ton of trails, but unfortunately you can't drive through which makes it difficult if you have little ones. The scenery is beautiful though and it's worth the trip!

This museum is very well done! The displays are professional and include all the information you could ever want about Conoco. There was also information about Ponca City in general. The staff were very friendly and helpful. Even my 3 year old enjoyed the exhibits. And it's free!

My boys are 1 and 3 and they both loved it. It's set up very well with lots of information and so much to see. The best part was the little pool with star fish that you could touch. It was a little expensive for the size but over all it was great!

Beautiful view! If you're afraid of heights you'd probably isn't for you, but otherwise it's fantastic! There's a parking lot on top where you can get out and enjoy the view and climb some rocks. You can hike up, but you'll be hiking on the road.
dislikes: Not suitable for those afraid of heights

reviews_attraction.text: Beautiful view! It was very crowded at the top when we went and the actual observation platform was packed with people. But there's room to spread out on the rocks look around without the benefit of the guardrail.

The museum is wonderful! Both the size and quality of exhibits make it a must visit! There are also a wide variety of animals to see and a mountain man encampment to visit. This is a fun place to take kids!
This place is so cool! My children (3 and 5) lived exploring all of the buildings and it was so fun to learn more about the background of one of my favorite children's books!
This is my favorite local park. It is usually not too busy and it had a playground that is a great size for toddlers.

It's wintertime and cold, but we didn't let it stop us from finally coming out here. We found an old homestead that we weren't expecting to see and an entrance to what I can only assume to be Big Bone Cave. Can't find a whole lot about the cave but apparently there are to known entrances and one is collapsed. I can only assume this is the other or one not documented publicly. Went to the entrance and was surprised at the complete change in temperature. It was 22 degrees when we went and the cave was at least 80 and humid. It would have been nice to know about the homestead here and the one we found later leaving just off the road, but I guess that will just be a trip to the archives. The place was beautiful and peaceful. There were a few bird chirping and we even saw a coyote. Definitely going to go back and explore the area more.
dislikes: Lack of Information (about the homestead and cave)

reviews_attraction.text: Part of the Manhattan Project NHP. Because you can only visit one site from a distance because of the radioactivity still in the ground, and the other two sites being off limits except for tours, this is the place to go. The first floor is set up with interactive displays. The museum is extensive and the staff are highly knowledgeable. We got a history lesson right when we walked in, pretty much a rundown of the entire history. There were a lot of displays and a few artifacts, but the place is loaded with information. Well worth the trip and the fee is low. And you don't just learn about the Manhattan Project, the other half of the museum is dedicated to energy and electricity and how it all works. Great for children and adults alike.

Place runs off volunteer help. The guy we met today was very helpful and was a fountain of history, not only with what you'll find in the museum but experience of passed down knowledge. The tower itself is free to climb, but beware there are a lot of idiots that etch their names on the water tank and the wood at the top. I'm sure that if they could they would carve them into the stone walls. Great place to step back in time. An 11 minute video gives a great look into why the place is there. The cost is extremely cheap and for a little more you can visit one of the homesteads. Gift shop has some wonderful items and in the fall they have the best apples for sale.

Nice little place. It's quiet, there is some history here and a small fall at the end of the trail. The problem though is the graffiti, which covers the historical buildings, and it isn't just the art, it's the sexual propositions plastered all over. There are used condoms strewn by the buildings, there were several pairs of panties, one in the building and another on the trail. Obviously a lot of sexual activity going on here. Talking to a couple of people their, they say they don't go unless they have a big dog or another person with them. So don't go alone, and if you can ignore all the rest to focus on the beauty, then this is a great place.

Went here after visiting the Homestead Tower and House museums. There are some nice trails. The damn holds historical significance but it stinks down at the bottom. The view from the bottom is worth the smell if you can tolerate it! Saw a squirrel or two, heard a lot of birds. The river that runs through in the afternoon took on different colors with all the shadows that played through the trees. Lots of friendly hikers. There is a bird aviary with four rescued birds. Each has a tragic story, but very beautiful. Can't say anything about camping or RV because we went for the history and to hike. Will be going back for the other trails though.

The hike to the falls, at least to the outlook is pretty good. It is by no way difficult. The beauty and the scenery is great. Saw a couple of deer, found a nest full of baby birds. It isn't a long hike either trail you take. The outlook take you to the top of the falls with a path down to the shore. Found some fossils walking along it. The water is flowing pretty good even though it's winter. It's not deep, we walked through it and it didn't even come close to our knees. There is even a set of picnic tables set up along the well maintained trail making a great little place to have a picnic.

Pulling into the park I didn't think the drive out out here out here was worth it, but after walking the trail to he outlook it definitely was. Plan to go back for the other trail soon. Didn't see either mill so that will be a further expedition. Did find quite a few fossils along the shore. The bottom of the falls looks like a great place to swim. And surprisingly for it being winter the water wasn't too cold. It ranks the eighth largest fall by volume and flows well in the winter considering other falls are drizzling or not even flowing this time of year.

Stumbled into this place looking for another. What caught my attention was the free part of it. There was a Where's Waldo event going on in the city and this was one place that participating in it. The museum is filled with art of all different kinds, divided by types of art. There is also a kids area where kids can create a variety of art with different mediums. And the museum isn't just in doors, it continues out into a courtyard. Overall a pretty neat little museum to visit.

Got there a week before they close for the year. Great little place that has a collection of artifacts. Each room is a different era. The lady that was there was highly knowledgeable and helpful. There are some interesting parts including graffiti made by some of the original prisoners that were kept there. There are also the records of those that were arrested and housed there including their charges all in hand written ledgers. All in all a quaint little museum to visit.

Definitely wear shoes and winter does provide great views. This is a big hill with an interpretive board. It's quiet and peaceful. As a history buff you can sit back and just feel, thinking of how many lost their lives in this little place. The place was very clean of trash, most likely because of the neighborhood. There is a little bench to sit on once you reach the top, so a great place to just sit or take a break from the climb. Definitely worth the trip here.

Great architecture. The top looked like it was being repaired or restored, so it would have been great to see it in all its glory.  Nice, peaceful place to walk through and around with many statues and dedications. Hard to believe it was built over a hundred years ago. The grounds are very well maintained, but the fountains weren't running, probably because its winter. It is probably even more impressive when they are running.

Not too bad of a little museum. It seems to be more geared to riding the train. There is a small museum with a large model train. The best part, excluding the train ride, is the train yard that comes with the museum. You can only view a few trains, but it gets the kids up pretty close to those being worked on. There was a nonprofit there with horse for kids to ride, so it turned out better than we expected.

Great place with loads of history. There is a lot to see and many documents and artifacts. The place does a good job at providing the history of Casey Jones, separating the fact from the fiction. The restaurant across the way is not too bad. It is a buffet with southern cooking, not too bad but honestly I can name a number of places with the same style at a better value for your dollar.

Quiet and clean place, great for a picnic or to stand where soldiers once stood. Lots of history here and plenty of signs giving that history. It is a bit breathtaking to see how so few can build something so grand and it still be here after so long. A must see for those interested in forts and the civil war. Plenty of parking and a decent amount of shade especially in the heat.

Very well kept park. It is pretty large and expansive. There is a children's garden way int he back that contains a little library. Where as the majority of the par is well kept, this small piece of of it seems to have fallen a little into disrepair. Either it isn't as maintained as the rest or neighborhood children have wrecked havoc on it. it's kind a of a shame.

Quaint little village. There is quite a bit of history here from the village itself to the exhibit of tractors and everything in between, The people here are nice as can be. There is even an art gallery that promotes local artists along with a small museum highlighting the area. Next to it is a scenic walk, though recommend the walk when it isn't so hot.

Cool place to check out. It's pretty quite and if you follow the trail around the bottom there is a natural spring at the end. There are several little "caves" and it has a great view. The fun part is going over the bridge. Parking is okay so long as there aren't a lot of people there, but it seems most come, take a few pictures and then leave.

The splash park is a great place for children. The carousel is great for any age at only a dollar per person per ride. Many great restaurants around the park and a couple snow cone stands at really good prices.  The is a great place for anything else and walking bridge running over it is worth the walk.

Great park to walk or jog through. Plenty to see from the natural beauty of the place to the various historic sites and statues and interpretive areas. Perfect for families to spent some time together or even picnic at. There are things for history lovers, arts lovers and nature lovers.

Very well kept landmark. It leads right into a local park. Good place for walks, hiking, running and biking with lots of history. There are also a large variety of insects like caterpillars for those that enjoy seeing all varieties of nature.

Pretty big place with many picnic tables and pavilions. Well kept with lots of trash cans. You can grill out here. There is also an outfitter to rent kayaks and bikes. Pretty quiet. Great place for kids and adults.

Quite a bit to see and learn here. There are large ruins of the mills that operated here and well as several trail. Combine those with the river, falls and the mound itself makes for a wonderful experience.
A great visit for a piece of history. There is a small trail that follows the river. The museum was closed because we got there late. A pretty good place for kids to run around.
Great place to hike with a few campsites and places to take a dip. Found a small swimming area teaming with crayfish. Waterfalls and plenty of beautiful nature.
Beautiful forest and land. Please donate a few bucks when you visit. Hate to see places like this go because of funding issues.

Of course Texas had to go and build its Capitol taller than the federal Capitol building. Everything is bigger in Texas, right? With an odd pinkish sandstone color (with matching paint on the steel dome oddly enough), this magnificent building towers over the beautiful Capitol grounds and surrounding area. Inside--after a security check with real live Texas State Troopers--you can tour the rotunda with paintings of all of Texas's presidents and governors and the chambers in which the two houses meet every two years for six months. I'm looking forward to the choral group that performs here in December and other events that take advantage of the great space while the legislators are out.

Love it! We have the family plus pass and it's fantastic with our kids. We make trips down from the North shore regularly and have found the good times to go so that it's not crazy busy. The zoo is an amazing park in its own right and the animals are decent. They're adding a lot all the time. The aquarium is small but really nice and they're adding more too. The insectarium is great but probably not something you can do every couple weeks.

For a small price (8.50 for kids and adults alike) you can get into some really fun activities. From the nola-specific stuff like a kid-sized shipping boat and Jackson square where your toddler can replace the shady president in his statue, this place is great. Near other museums, the location is good too. It's not as amazing as the Indianapolis children's museum that I grew up with but it's a fine one for the region.

This is a friendly family-oriented establishment with an assortment of small to medium-sized animals. There is very little in the way of amenities though there are a few food trailers and a gift shop. The exhibits are linked by dirt trails and the animals pretty up close and personal. There are no large ungulates, but there are some big cats and some amazing turtles. Go with low expectations and you'll be happy.

An Austin original, this natural spring-water pool is a great spot to hit after sweating it out in 110 degree Texas summers. The water is freezing (around 65 all year round) but feels good once you're in. If you're too scared to jump in, just dip your feet in to cool down your entire body and occupy yourself with the fascinating people watching, which may or may not include topless 70-year-old women.

It's great in a city to every once in a while take an entire city block and make it a park. Republic Square Park has a great name and a great location. Once they're done with the construction nearby, this will be a perfect spot to take a break from downtown Austin. This is a great place for events and take shuttles to ACL fest. It's not perfectly kempt but that almost adds to its historic appeal.

I've been here a couple times--once for a chili cookoff on Independence Day (can you get better than that?) and then recently for a friend's birthday. The wine tour was the best I've had in all my tasting experience with a knowledgeable guide and some pretty good wines. This is one of the oldest wineries in what has become the second most popular wine regions in the country behind Napa!

In the shadow of the Long Center, this park area across from downtown hosts concerts and other arts productions as well as millions of dogs in the leash-free zone right on the water. It would be better if the trail didn't run through the chaotic zoo, but you can't beat the location and there are exercise stations and a nice little gazebo and pond area right on the water.

This is an interesting place off the beaten path. With expertly design landscaping and a beautiful pond area, Mayfield plays host to dozens of gigantic peacocks. It's really amazing to see these creatures mulling about as if they don't have stunning coats of shiny blue and green and purple all up and down themselves. This was free to check out, so there's no risk.

One of my favorite spots on my jog around the lake. Crossed by city streets, this park isn't as secluded as it could be, but it has a nice view of the water and plenty of shade trees to hide from the sun under. Festival Beach plays host to quite a few festivals (hence the name) including the Celtic Fest in November.

Greenbelts all over the place! This makes for a nice north/south bike ride or hike when you coming to or from the river. Generally very little traffic in the greenbelt on on the adjoining streets, which makes the trip nice and scenic. Also there is park equipment all along to satisfy the nearby residents.

While it's not the most attractive church ever, the community is great and they keep the liturgy fairly legit. I'd live some incense now and then and the schola should perform weekly, but I like the robust altar server program and the priests are great. You can always count on a great homily.

We went for caroling and it was a nice environment. It's a great central location with a fun stuff all around including a brewery and plenty of parking. Of course, there's the train right there too. If I had the wherewithal I would totally buy one of the townhomes going up across the street.

I can't speak to the school here, but the historic building of Laguna Gloria is gorgeous and a real Austin treat. The tour is minimal but I'm really looking forward to one of the festivals that are held there annually (Italian fest and the Dolce Vita fund raiser are two that come to mind).

While the collection fits is minimal floor space, The AMOA deserves five stars for its events (members only), which it hosts itself or in conjunction with the Jones Center. AMOA is affiliated with the beautiful Laguna Gloria and members also get discounts on classes and events there.

There are dozens of absolutely stunning churches in the new Orleans area, but I haven't found another with such a beautiful liturgy. In either the Latin Mass at 9:30 or the high norvua ordo Mass at 11, this is the place to be. Great community and wonderful clergy make this a must.

Really fun for a group of guys. Fast and not smelly carts. We went for a bachelor party and then a couple times after. I have one beef and that's that they put us with a reckless little jerk who spun me out causing a pileup. Getting slammed by another cart at 30 mph was not fun.

Part of the zoo membership, we took our little 1.5-year-old and he had a blast. It gets a little crowded and the food isn't much to write home about but the variety of aquatic beasts are good. There's a nice jungle setting in there too but the tree house was off limits!?

A wonderful day trip from most parts of the north shore and even the southshore, you get to see some amazing beasts up close and personal- in all their slobbering glory. If you want to see giraffes you need to book the private tour. I recommend just a few cups of feed.

We went with two kids 2 and under and it would've been great for papa and the oldest except for the fact that the ride that we had been hyping up to our son for weeks (the train) was down. The splash pad thing was out of commission too. #Sixfails

This course is probably really fun (I didn't get to putt), but it looks really run down and not kept up. The BYOB feature is nice and probably attracts a wide range of golfing enthusiasts. It's colorful and lively and you can't beat the location!

Went with a group of 5 others for a birthday party. It was a blast, though it probably could've been a little longer. Not that we were super fast, but it just seems like a lot for 30 minutes. I would certainly check it out again though.
One of my favorite places in San Antonio. It's gorgeous, action-packed, and educational. The kids loved the dinosaur exhibit and I love the grounds and the historical exhibits.
This is a unique spot in Austin overlooking Lake Austin and downtown from a perch on a hill. There isn't much hiking or anything, but the views are great.
Pretty good spot to catch a sunset but the restrictions on picnics and the general pretentiousness leads to an air of discomfort.

The Visitor's Center at Colonial Williamsburg is a large place. There was ample parking when we were there. I'm not sure how it is when it is the busier season. They had reduced rates on tickets during this time. I assume that was due to just opening back up after Covid19 restrictions. We purchased our tickets at the Visitor's Center, but you can also purchase them online. The Cafe here is ised right now I assume because of Covid19 as well. The staff we encountered were friendly. There's a walking path to the village or you can take their free shuttle buses. We walked over and took the bus back.

This is the battlefield at Yorktown, Virginia. It is a great historical location if you are into that kind of thing. We did not go to the battlefield section. We have already been to the battlefields in Gettysburg and figured it is all pretty much the same. The people in the area have been pretty friendly so far. Most things are open with covid restrictions. Most places have done a good job of helping people to social distance while they are there.  Masks are required and most people are abiding by the rules. The weather has been amazing so far since we have been here.

The National Military Park was a great place to visit. Be sure to check out everything there, so you don't miss out on something. You buy tickets for several thing there and then take a bus to actually visit them. Familiarize yourself with the area before you visit and make a list of things you want to see and do while you are there. The staff is helpful, so don't be afraid to ask. Even the bus drivers are open to answering questions.  Lots of history to explore in the area. You'll need several days to see everything.

This is an amazing bird park with lots of different kinds of birds to see. There are overlooks where you might be able to see other animals as well if you are lucky. We saw some baby raccoons today and turtles. Some birds are in individual enclosures and others are in bigger enclosures that you can walk into as well. You can buy bird food to feed them with. We found a snake in one of the enclosures, told the staff and the rescued the birds from the snake. Its a great place to take your kids and very educational.

This is the Capitol building that is a part of Colonial Williamsburg. A period dressed person takes you on a tour of the building and tells you the history of the building and the people associated with it. It lasts about 25 minutes for the tour.
