The staff we dealt with were friendly and likes for you to ask questions. All of Colonial Williamsburg makes accommodations for Covid and everyone had on masks. If you enjoy history be sure to take in the Capitol building while you're there to listen to their story.

This is the Governor's palace at Colonial Williamsburg. It is one of the buildings you get to go inside of when you purchase a ticket. There are period dresses people throughout Colonial Williamsburg who will answer questions for you. The period costumed people at the palace take you on a tour and talk to you about the history of the building and the people who lived there. There are also outbuildings and gardens that you can visit. Its a quick tour of the first floor only. Nice and educational.

This is a park in the City of Goldsboro. It has been here for many, many years. There is a fountain in the center that used to have fish in it, but there are no longer fish there. They have tennis courts, a train for the kids and the kids at ❤.  There are picnic tables and a gazebo. They have soccer nets and playground equipment. Most of it is still closed now because of the virus. The grass needed to be cut today. More attention needs to be paid to the uo keep of various things in the park.

Monticello is a place you should visit. There is a lot of history and it is a beautiful place. It always amazes me to see places that were built so long ago. Take the guided tour and learn everything you can. It is usually very busy and you get timed tickets. Luckily we were handed tickets that were time stamped long before our original tickets. Get there early to insure you don't have a long wait. They have a nice area to wait with stuff to do while you wait.

The Constitution Center was a great place to visit. The young girl who helped with our tickets was NOT friendly at all. She acted like she did not want to be there. We enjoyed the center itself. There were hands on activities you could participate in and lots of thing to see and learn from. You will need at least a couple of hours to do it justice and see it all. Hopefully you'll have someone different to help you when you arrive.

This is fun for kids, but none of the track or go carts are fast enough for adults. The staff is nice and friendly and most of them do a good job interacting with the public, especially the kids. You do spend a lot if time waiting in line to get on a go cart. You spend a lot more time in line than you do on the track. It was super hot today too which isn't anything they can control but it makes the waiting even worse.

We only stopped here to get a picture of the Welcome to New Orleans sign. The view of the river/swamp area was pretty as you go over the bridge. There's a NASS Space Center nearby that we didn't go to euthwr5, but it might be a nice place to explore. The welcome center just past this was CLOSED.  They don't open until 8:30 AM & it was only 8:00 AM when we arrived. Not a very welcoming experience unfortunately.

The Titanic Museum in Pigeon Forge is awesome. It's amazing to see all if the interesting stuff about the ship. They have an audio tour. They have audios for adults and also ones designed just for kids so the little ones will enjoy it more. They have a cold room with an iceberg in it so you will know how cold it was when she ship sank. The visuals and information are interesting.  I could have stayed longer.

The Gettysburg National Park is a great place to visit if you like history. We were there the weekend of the 4th of July, so it was a very busy time with lots of other people there as well. The good thing about that weekend is that it's the anniversary of the Civil War battle, so they had reenactments and lots of people in costume.  We took tours and also explored on our own. There is a lot to see and do.

We came herr looking for their LOVE sign. It's actually between a park and the zoo. We weren't sure so we asked one of the ticket sellers at the front of the zoo. She was very helpful and directed us as to how to find the LOVE sign. We did not visit the zoo itself while we were there though so I can't really say anything about the zoo. If you want to know, you'll have to visit it for yourself.

This is an awesome little park in Kinston. There are mosaics, a mural, quotes, etc related to music as the name implies.  There is a nice sized stage where a band could play or a DJ. It would be a great place for an outdoor party which would be perfect for Covid19 times or any time. It is a nice park that is well maintained. Check it out if you're ever in the area. You'll be glad you did.

We love to explore history and we enjoyed our visit to James Madison's home. The home itself is beautiful and the staff is friendly too. We have enjoyed visiting several Presidential homes in the state of Virginia and hope to visit more in the future. If you enjoy history or learning about Presidents, this is a place you should see. It is a nice place to bring your children to as well.

There is no admission to visit this place, so be sure to stop by. There are lots of interesting things to learn and see here. There is a place to leave a donation if you enjoy your visit. They have interactive things for kids to do, so be sure to ask but they should tell you about it when you enter. The staff was nice and helpful. They also have a gift shop and people in costume.

The Barnes Foundation is an amazing place to visit and a MUST see if you have any interest in art. This is an AMAZING collection of art by some of the best artist of all time. Give yourself plenty of time when you come. Believe me, you will want to see it ALL. I have told numerous people about this place since our visit last year and will continue to spread the word.

This is a rose garden. I still haven't managed to visit when it was at its peak as far as the roses and blooming. From what I have seen here, it seems to be a nice place. You could rent it for an event if you'd like. I'd still like to see it at the peak of the rose blooms. This is just one of the interesting places that you can visit in Wilson, NC.

This is your typical city park. New Orleans has several parks in the city and Most of them are very beautiful. Check them out if you are in the city and want to take a break or get away from the bustling city life. We enjoyed the brief time we spent in the parks of New Orleans on our trip there. You can even take your pet with you.

Today was a perfect weather day to be at the mill. It would be a nice place to have a picnic. Great place to take pictures, go for a walk, family time, etc. You can tour the mill if you are interested in that. Some people were fishing today. Nice place for some quiet reflection.  Venture out there one day to see for yourself.

We only stopped here on this day to get a flat penny from their machine. The lady st reception was helpful in pointing out where the flat penny machine was located and she wanted to see my penny before I left. Can't really speak to anything else because we didn't visit there. It seemed like a nice place to take your kids.

We were running out of time when we got to the Betsy Ross house, so we were unable to see the interior. The outside was nice and we can say that we've been there
There's so much to see in Philadelphia that you need several day to explore the city. Bucket list item checked off. Now on to more adventures.

We attended the Wilson Winter Lights at the Wilson Botanical Gardens. The lights were nice.  They had some really pretty pieces and had lots of volunteers there in the parking lot and also in the gardens. Santa is also there so if you get a chance, take your children to see the lights and Santa.

We only stopped here to get a flat penny from their machine. We did not actually visit the museum,  so I can not speak about it. It seemed like an interesting place to visit if you have the time. We just had a different mission on this day.

Some jerk wrote that it's a bunch of "chips and imported crap you could get at a truck stop."  That is simply untrue.  I live in PA and have been here more than once and will be back.  Western NC is a rockhound's paradise.
At Emerald Hollow, you can choose from buying buckets of dirt and rock that are native to the area and sifting through them with screens in the sluice OR you can do what I do and go to the "dig it yourself" areas within the property.  I have found emeralds, a couple of rubies, numerous garnets, two hiddenite specimens, several sapphires, and a topaz specimen that was appraised at $250.  All from digging for myself and having fun with my screens and pans.  I would hardly call that "chips and imported crap."  Definitely wear old shoes and old clothes because you're gonna get dirty...and it's worth it.

Beautiful and well-maintained park in the middle of Lititz, PA...complete with a spring, a stream, playground, pavilions, lots of open space for picnics and letting the kids run around in a safe environment.  There's a great acoustic band shell in the back of the park where community concerts are held and in the summer they show movies where the family can come, bring a picnic, buy popcorn (it might even be free...I can't quite remember) and have a nice evening out. I lived just a couple of blocks from Lititz Springs Park for the better part of 13 years and it is a true treat for families that live there.  The July 4th celebration and fireworks are second to none.

One of our fave places to hike.  Scenery is just beautiful, you hike along Kelly's Run all the way the Susquehanna River, there are edible wild berries along the trail during the right time of the year, the atmosphere changes with the seasons (so it's worth coming back repeatedly), and the hiking trail is a great mixture of easy to moderate to kinda challenging in a couple of spots.  Love it!!

Another of our favorite places to hike.  No facilities, so be aware.  Parking accommodations are small, but the trail is just delightful...along the water and difficulty level ranging from easy to moderate in most places while there are a couple of spots that could prove challenging with roots, etc.  Just beautiful and well worth your time for repeated hiking visits:)

I've come here for years.  The Cades Cove loop is wonderful as we have seen wild turkeys, bear, deer, elk, wolf and coyote here over the years.  We always stop at the visitor center, as it is always well staffed with courteous people and the souvenir selection is nice.  Lots of cool history, historic buildings, etc. make this a must-see when you visit the area.

Would love to camp here sometime.  Well worth the drive and short hike to the top to the observation tower.  Get ready for some amazing views of these amazingly beautiful mountains.  The hike to the tower is mostly sidewalk and is only about 900 yards...however, it's all uphill to get there.  Good news is that it's all downhill on the return.

This is an absolute MUST when you visit South Padre Island.  We did the Moonlight Dinner cruise and everything was great.  VERY reasonable price, excellent grilled shrimp appetizer, excellent all you can eat grilled fajitas, excellent fresh fruit for dessert, excellent acoustic entertainment.  We couldn't be happier with our experience

We'll be back.  Spycat and Reisling wines are really, really nice.  Just saw Pat Benatar and Rick Springfield there.  Terrific venue for an outdoor show like that...it rained, but the staff handled things very, very well.  Heck...good wines, great outdoor concert venue, well worth the nearly two hours to get here!

Fantastic experience for the whole family.  The exhibits are just super.  I've brought my kids here many times and we never get tired of it.  My girls love the jellyfish exhibits and the staff is very kind and helpful.  Can't tell you the first thing about the food area, as I don't come here to eat. lol

GREAT experience!  The house and farm are fun, interesting and educational.  The tour through Amish Country is not to be missed.  You'll learn a lot and have fun doing it...AND you'll get to stop at one or more Amish markets along the way.  Our tour guide was Delores and she was wonderful.

Wonderful state park.  We never get tired of visiting here!  Wild ponies, sika deer, beautiful beaches, clamming, kayaking...just a gorgeous park and a unique experience whether you're camping or just making a day trip.  Don't miss the Welcome Center at the bridge when you come here!

Nice atmosphere and the wines are good.  We were referred here from the lady at Shenandoah Winery.  Clio was very, very good and Petit Verdot was also quite nice.  Worth your time and recommended, but some of the other area wineries feel a bit more personal in the experience.

We picnic here every time we're in the area and go wading in the creek here.  Joy is just everywhere...kids and adults wading and swimming, families picnicking and playing in the water, a real sense of community and peace here.  A must-visit when you're in the area:)

This is a nice museum with a courteous and very knowledgeable staff.  They have  a historic film they show there that is well worth the time and the gift shop is probably better than the Smoky Mountains Heritage Center.  GREAT handmade lye soap that they sell there!

Of course, you can get all of your Orioles gear here and the food options are surprisingly diverse.  Prices are okay.  The main thing is that the ballpark is a great experience.  Really nicely laid out so there's really not a truly bad seat in the house.

I found the wines to be too similar in taste when we were there on Monday.  Riesling was ok.   I hate to say it, but the girls who did our tastings with another couple were really disengaged and it felt like they were just going through the motions.

Water was low when we were there recently, but that allowed us to better see the rock formations and better understand why these formations are called "The Sinks."  Beautiful place to stop for a walk, rest and enjoyment of waterfalls and nature:)

Like the current state capitol, the old state capitol has a wonderful, knowledgeable staff and the museum is really nice.  A lot of history to be seen inside here.  Great location and a must-see for out of town visitors!

One of our fave local places to hike.  The nature preserve as a whole is wonderful, but we especially love the hike along Kelly's Run to the Susquehanna.  You follow the water the whole way and it is just joyous.

Oh my word...any chance you have to drive on the Blue Ridge Parkway, do it!  Beautiful and well-maintained mountain roads with some absolutely gorgeous scenic points and vistas.  Beautiful and peaceful driving:)
Beautiful collection of artifacts and history of the area.  Very much worth your time when you are here.  Sweet location right by the Oconaluftee River, too:)
Nice hiking and I'm sooooo glad they've let the water back in.  Nice family outing and I'm looking forward to more years of enjoyment:)
My wife and I went parasailing here on our honeymoon.  Great, fun staff and a wonderful parasailing experience.  We will be back!
Completely underrated as far as I'm concerned.  GREAT place for a family outing or a date with someone who appreciates nature.
We LOVE South Padre Island!  The sign gets 5 stars because when you see it...it means you're entering South Padre Island.

Tres Bien.  Delightful and informative tour of a historical Louisiana home.  We were there early in the year so the weather was mild and bugs were on holiday.  The tour was quite extensive and included some of the out buildings.  The most amazing part was the history and artwork of  Clementine Hunter.  A folk artist whose work you will see reproduced on a variety of objects like platters and plates.   I understand that they also have events here and I imagine weddings must be very special in this grand old home.

Beaux Arts. The architectural style of the DIA and an apt description of the building contents. Believe it or not, but the DIA is one of the top 6 art museums in the United States. It is a huge collection of many artistic styles and is very well curated. Additionally, the building itself and the surrounding cultural district campus is worth the trip itself. Lastly, for residents of the tri-county area, the museum is free of charge except for special events.

Bunnies. Great place around metro Detroit to learn to ski. It is nearby, it is inexpensive, and the hills are relatively forgiving. There are classes and private instruction that also will not break your bank. The food is forgettable and more expensive than it deserves to be, but it is again, not going to break you. All in all, you get what you pay for sometimes, this sure ain't Vail, but it is way more affordable.

The Nature Center is one of many attractions on Belle Isle that is free. A small zoo appropriate for younger children, it is conveniently located near a playground and one of the inland island lakes. It is on the far eastern side of the island, so you will have to drive almost all the way around the island to get to it. If you see the driving range, slow down because it is right across the road from it on the left.

Shipwreck. This museum is awesome. And, like a fight at the hockey game and a crash at the race course - the shipwrecks are so cool.  You can not take your eyes off the wrecks.  Sure sure there are many cool things to do and see here but do I have to sing the Wreck of the Edmund Fitzgerald for you? Come to Belle Isle and do the Dossin.  For a super interesting time, ask for John McLean - he's a stitch.

Spectacular. The Cathedral of Finance. An art deco skyscraper from the golden age of Detroit. Built in 1929 just before the Great Depression the Guardian Building is still spectacular inside and out. Make sure to look at the exterior closely to see the incredible and never to be duplicated details. Inside, it feels like being in a European church. Visit the shops and services and extend your enjoyment.

I have been going here for decades and continue to love it.  Most recently here for holiday nights celebration and was amazed at how many people were there. A really popular attraction for the metro Detroit area.  Food and beverage selections were good in the village but the dinner at the eagle tavern is incredible.  Horse carriage rides were a nice bonus with no additional charge.

Golden. Wow, a classic American family success story all on display in this beautiful mansion. The Dodge family rose to prominence in the golden era of the auto industry. Their stories along with the Ford family and others are fascinating and a great part of our heritage in the greater Detroit area. We were there around Christmas and the mansion was dressed in its holiday finest.

Historic. A must see for KC. You will want to do this over the course of two days if you can. There is so much to see and learn about. I think that over time, world War two has been given all the attention and world War one has been largely forgotten. This is a really great museum and worth your time. Also the museum cafe is surprisingly good.

Peaceful. A beautiful park surrounding the WWI museum. Well maintained and surprisingly quiet considering the fact that it is right in the middle of the city and across from the train station. On a bit of a hill so be prepared for a little workout. It is worth it though, so huff and puff a little and you won't regret it.

Indoor. Okay, so it is really an indoor outdoor adventure center. Super cool family friendly and pint size kid friendly place. Located in the Milliken State Park in downtown Detroit, right at the Riverwalk. Free parking, reasonable prices, friendly staff. Take your kids here and then go get them a coney island hot dog!!

Charming. Friendly, lazy river, well maintained park, special events, farmers market and more. In a beautiful, historic town, this is just one more reason to visit this hard to spell place. Southern hospitality abounds in spades you are surrounded by history, flowers (yes, there are magnolias), and fine foods.

MustSee. Kid friendly and free. A small but historic aquarium with tropical and Great Lakes fish. All the tanks are relatively small so they provide a more intimate setting for younger people. Between the conservatory and the aquarium I don't know which one would make the better destination for a second date.

Grand. Great for walking your dog or for special events. So much cleaner than it used to be. It used to be a bum hotel every night. Nowadays there are flowers and fountains and Fido. I like the statues and fountains the best though. It is also a very practical park with a parking garage underneath it.

Undervalued. Too many people overlook this pretty little park hidden in plain sight. Too bad for them and too good for us!  River views, island views, city views and peaceful relaxation. Surprisingly easy to find considering how few choose to do so.  Maybe I should shut up before everyone notices?

Visit the Freight Yard in the Dequindre Cut and hang out.  Makes for a nice break in your walking or biking trip down the cut.  You can also visit before or after your trip to Eastern Market since it is so close to the cut.  Look out for other special events happening all along the Dequindre Cut.

Art. Artist club and event venue in a beautiful old building hidden in plain sight. Consider yourself lucky if you get in.  A real Detroit bucket list destination.  I do wish that they could have a tiny speakeasy inside, but that is only because I am not artistic enough to get in as an artist.

Beauty and the Beast, Sweet and Sour, and a Gorgeous Alley!  The Belt is a must see if you can find it. A real alley that has been transformed into the most stylish and artistic thoroughfare in Detroit. There are two bars and some pop-ups and a lot of cool street art. Meet me at The Belt.

Tropical. Plants of all kinds from all ecosystems. The tropical plants are the most beautiful to me. A favorite winter destination in Detroit. Recently renovated and looking incredible, the conservatory is to me the best part of Belle Isle. If you have time, visit the aquarium too.

Upswing. This place will only get better.  Long an overnight stay for drunks and the homeless, it is a wonderful place for events and for those of us without addiction issues also. In fact, the more often you go and the more often you use it the better and better it will get.

The Tigers aren't going to be very good for a while, but baseball is really nice at the "new Tiger Stadium".  Even the cheap seats have good sight lines.  Check StubHub for even better deals.  All in all, it's one of the best value sports entertainment around.

The new park downtown, serving the western part of downtown Detroit, near Cass and Grand River.  It completely changes the feel of this part of the downtown.  Mucho events happening here almost every day.  Many kid friendly activities too.

Historical and under-utilized.  Unless you are going in to one of the businesses in the building it is not accessible.  Too bad, because it is a beautiful building.  For many years it was the tallest building in Detroit.
The city needs to invest in some serious improvements to Hart Plaza.  It works for big events, but looks really shabby if you visit it when nothing is going on.
Dream Big.  Opening soon and we cannot wait.  I am giving 5 stars for imagination, effort and for making what once seemed impossible a reality.

best place to hike mt mansfield. lovely park and strenuous hike to the summit. the view is awesome from the top !

I can't wait to review the new building. But for now, the existing museum is a good example of world history with a hyper-local lens. Many of the great exhibits provide information on how the topics (dinosaurs, early inhabitants, geology, etc) are relevant to the Pacific Northwest. There is an open area where families can watch scientists work on artifacts, and great anthropological exhibits downstairs. There are also games and programs for all ages. I would note that the museum is probably not very fun for children under 6 years old. (my 3 year old only wanted to spend about 20 min in the whole place) Otherwise, a great adventure for almost all ages!

Cowen park is a fun extension to the already big urban trail that makes up Ravenna park. Located at the boundary between Roosevelt and the University district, it collects a mix of urban and residential citizens. It has a wonderful playground for the kids, large grassy areas with trees for activities, and even a ball-park area. I recently attended a birthday party for one of my son's classmates in the picnic area and we had a great time! If you're nearby and want a place to relax for a bit, this would be a good choice for your day.

The Seattle Olympic Sculpture Park is an amazing stretch of shoreline, views, art and culture. Free and open to the public, it offers running and biking, picnic and urban hiking. Downtown workers rub elbows with tourists and city dwellers rain and shine. At any time, one can see the Olympic mountains across the Sound, large public art, the Space Needle, enormous cargo ships, public watercraft, and more. It is one of the best resources the city has to offer, especially on a sunny day! I highly recommend a visit.

Carkeek Park is one of the best parks in NW Seattle! It features trails, an education center, large grassy areas, BBQ and benches, a play area for children and beach access. But what does my son like the most? The bridge over the train tracks where the young in body and young in spirit gather to watch huge locomotives pass under them. Also offering beautiful views of the sound, you'll be hard pressed to find a better park in this part of the city.

Great Basin National Park is a hidden gem of the National Park Service! The caves, the camping, the trails and the hiking are accessible, fun, wel maintained and best of all, not crowded. The country is pristine and still holds the feeling of a time in the past. Worth a visit no matter the season, but Spring and Summer are some of the best times to go. I highly recommend this to all people who love the natural world.

I like this park because it's close to my son's preschool. It has a lot of shade from trees and a great play structure and skate park. The only downside is it also has a lot of grafitti and trash, used needles, cigarette butts and beer cans / liquor bottles strewn about. It seems to be a struggle the community endures, as it is also a great resource for local Lake City families and is an otherwise beautiful park.

This was an at the moment side trip. My partner and I were good we stopped by. It's a fascinating location with a geological mystery. Very easy to walk; be sure to bring a hat and a Discovery Pass. There is a gun range nearby, which is a little distracting. However, the beauty of the mounds and the meadow overcome this nuisance. If you're in the area, this is a quick day hike great for kids of all ages!

Richmond beach is a wonderful place for families and friends. Beautiful views of the Sound, as well as access to beaches for play and strolling. This is a great place to bring children! There is a bridge over train tracks to access the beach areas. It is the place to be for families with toddlers, as trains pass by underneath, honking their horns for the children. Worth the visit on a warm sunny day!

Since being renovated this park is one of the best in Seattle. It offers a wide range of park amenities like a running track, sports areas, children's play area with modern equipment (like a zip line!!!!), etc. One of the best parts is that it is one of the highest points in the city! It has a view of Mt Rainier that is to die for... especially on a clear morning at sunrise. You cannot beat it!

Westlake Park is truly a Seattle city common area. It's located in the downtown shopping district and plays host to a number of celebrations throughout the year. It is also the gathering point for numerous protests, and a place where people from all walks of life intermingle. While I wouldn't call the park "kid friendly" (even though there is a kid play area) it is definitely worth visiting.

Of all the amazing local places for Seattleites to hang out on a beautiful day, Gasworks has to be one of the best. Sporting amazing views of the city, large open green spaces, nearby eats and craft beers, and a new playground, it has it all. If it's sunny, wear sunscreen as there arent many shady areas. And definitely bring your camera to share the beauty!

MAPS is a wonderful mosque and community center with a mission of peace making and justice building in the Puget Sound area. They are welcoming of visitors and do a lot of outreach into the community. They are a thriving religious community who are dedicated in charity, good works and living an ethic of love. I am always grateful when I'm able to visit!

Greenlake is one of the best parts about living in North Seattle. It is a wonderful community resource and a gathering place no matter the weather or time of year. Surrounded by walking paths, recreation and popular restaurants/shops, it really is a hub for locals in the city. Definitely worth visiting, especially in the summer afternoons.

The "Ballard Locks" as they're locally known are a beautiful collection of gardens, architecture and engineering that goes back to the city's early days. It is a popular destination for locals as well as tourists. Be sure to come during peak salmon season to view the fish ladder! Whenever I have friends in town, I take them here.

The west end of Greenlake has wonderful beach and swimming areas that are popular in the summer. It also has a community theatre, walking and biking trails, and a snack shack. While there aren't as many businesses on this end of the park, it does offer fun and relaxation, as well as great views from across the lake.

I'm a little biased, but I volunteer for the Clark County Wetland Park... it's the best kept natural secret in Las Vegas! Completely free, open Mon-Fri dawn to dusk, and offers some great trails, plant and animal life, and a wonderful way to experience the Mojave without having to drive very far. Check it out!

This is a beautiful play field with wide areas for sports or sunbathing. A skate park as well as swings and fun for all ages. This is a great neighborhood resource. If you are nearby and need some serenity, stop by this park and take a walk... you'll feel better almost instantly!

Juanita Bay Park was such a beautiful experience. I visited with my son in springtime 2017 - the sun was out and the day was warm. Flowers were popping out and all the birds were on full display. I highly recommend this natural area for a nice stroll or natural photography.

One the most beautiful parks in Seattle, the Arboretum offers miles of trails, gardens and views that is a must visit at any time of the year. I consider myself very lucky to have this public resource available for my family! Do not let the experience go to waste. :)

Great neighborhood park with everything you need for the family! Not only is there an offleash dog area, but a water playground, sports field, bbq area, trails, you name it... and it is tucked into a hyper-local setting. Best kept secret in North Seattle.

West Woodland Park playground is a great place to play for children of all ages. Rope gym, slides and picnic areas are well maintained. Access to sun and shade in all weather conditions. Close to the zoo. A wonderful resource for Seattleites!

One of the best parks in Seattle! Offers a tour of NOAA sculpture gardens, huge dog park, access to lake Washington, tons of trails. It is very popular with the NW part of the city. Worth a visit every weekend!
A wonderful natural area converted from an old naval base. Miles of trails, views of Puget Sound, beach access, and more! Definitely worth a visit any time of year.
This is my local playground. It's a simple park and play area but serves as a community commons. I love to come walking here with my son and our dog.
It's a nice simple park with historical markers. Nice for a picnic or a stroll. Big enough for an event. Worth a visit!

We went here on valentines weekend, and visiting here was not one of the best experiences i have had at a zoo.  My wife and i have been to many zoos in many states and sadly for every plus there seemed to be a minus. They did have a good number of animal species for the price you pay - mostly bird species, and unfortunately the back part of the zoo was heavily under construction but it was impossible to tell if they were preparing for new exhibits or tearing down old ones. So i do have to take off points for this inconvenience. Another star must be removed for the fact that this zoo openly sells alcohol at their snack carts, as well as having a full fledged bar as one of their restaurants. I have never seen this before in the many zoos i have visited and was not pleased to have to avoid other patrons stumbling around with a beer can in their hands as i tried to enjoy looking at the animals. I also need to mention that the parking situation was terrible - make sure you arrive early if you come, there are not a ton of spaces in the lot and once it fills up, the whole park is jammed with traffic of people walking and driving. They did have park cops trying to direct traffic, but there were just too many cars for the 2 lane road. I do try to not be too critical of the places i visit, however there were too many factors that put a damper on my visit to ignore. I felt like we were at more of a playground for all ages with some animals in cages, than at a zoo focused on the education and preservation of animals around the world, so if that is the experience you are looking for then this is the place for you. Otherwise their are much other finer zoos to choose from in the state of Texas.

Wow! There was so much to see and do while we were here, I can't wait to go back! They had the greatest displays from the many brave men and women who explored space and there was so much to learn. The staff here was super friendly and taught us a lot about the trials of space exploration. I definitely recommend starting your day with BOTH tram tours to visit the rockets and mission control - they get very long lines by the afternoon and you might not get to see it all. There are tons of interactive and educational games for kids to play to keep them engaged while you roam the exhibits, as well as several short movies to watch if you need a break to get off your feet. Tickets are about $30 each, and it's $5 for parking, but it is worth every bit. They had souvenirs for every age and every budget, and even the food court had way more options than I expected, and most meals were under $10. We will definitely be bringing our kids back and I would suggest everyone to make the journey here at least once to walk in the same space as the greatest pioneers of our generation!

This place is a great hands-on aquarium experience, as well as they have many animal exhibits. They have animal handlers who will allow you to handle all kinds of animals and answer all of your questions. We went on a Saturday morning, and although there was a long line to pay for tickets (about $14 for adults) there was enough room to get around the exhibits and experience each at your leisure without getting pushed around. They sell snacks for you and for you to feed the animals as well. Also, take time to peruse the gift shop, they have lots of great animal trinkets and toys that you dont find anywhere else. Parking was free, this is located in a shopping center so there are lots of places to park. It is a little difficult to get to from the freeway from Austin, so taking one of the main avenues near it is better. Overall, a wonderful experience will definitely be back

One of the greatest little big zoos in the state of texas. They have so many breeds of animals, but it is easy to get through the entire park in less than 4 hours. The highlight we found at this zoo is their African Savannah enclosure, with all of the major African animals - from zebras, giraffes, elephants, lions, and more - in the same grassland area, safely separated as needed of course. We also enjoyed the keeper talk as they fed their African penguins, the staff was friendly and knowledgeable and it's always great to watch happy penguins playing. All the enclosures were top notch and the layout was easy to navigate to walk by all the animals, with lots of shady areas to keep the Texas heat at bay. Parking is free and tickets were under $15. If you're in the area and looking for something fun, put this at the top of your list to visit!

On the outside the O. Henry house in Austin doesnt look like much. But little does one know the house is a living monument to what many argue is the greatest short story writers of all time. I have always enjoyed his writings but neve realized he had ties to Austin. Combine all of this with the fact it is free, well I was ready to go. There is no gift shop , there are no bathrooms but for thirty minutes you can walk in and enjoy history. It is something one should visit just for experiencing written history and learning about our past.  I also need to mention that the convention center parking garage was the most convenient and only 1 block away, if there is no street parking (about $1 per hour) available, the garage is only about $5 for 2 hours. My wife and I througly enjoyed this museum and we will definetly be back.

This park is right by the zoo parking. So even if you  don't go to the zoo you can still go to the  park. We ate here after the zoo and had a nice picnic lunch at some of their tables all covered. There were men's and women's restrooms  nearby and water fountains as well.  Now it is by the lake and one would go swimming. However they do advise not to, do to the alligators. We did not see any but it was well marked and we didn't take any chances. The highlight here though is a little train that starts in the parking lot goes around the zoo and across the lake and back. It is separate from the zoo and cost 2 dollars per person and 3 dollars for a whistle, all of this sponsored by the loins club. Overall I think it was the best thing to end our trip and my family loved it.

This is a wonderful park! There is a little bit of everything and fun for all ages. Games ranged from larger-than-life checkers to ping pong tables to foosball. They have a splash park, and a giant sand pit with water well to make the perfect sand castles. There are lots of places to sit and have a picnic lunch, and a large, clean restroom. Unfortunately, there is no free parking, street parking runs under $5, and parking lots and garages range from $7 - $20, so make sure whatever you carry is portable because you will have to walk a distance to get to the park from parking. It can get busy on the weekends, so plan accordingly. A sweet hidden gem, i definitely recommend visiting!

Ok so I tried to post this earlier and my phone fritzed on me. This was the last place my wife and I went on our anniversary and it was very unique and very pleasant. If you have time in Shreveport take the time to come out to this free museum. This is a great place to learn and discover about our past as a country. What did those before us do? What did they build? Although this is just for this region you can see what one would have to do survive and care for what was around them. It is near the current water works and it just shows part of a by gone era that we still need to learn from. The staff was great and I look forward to coming back.

Great zoo for the family especially little ones. We took our now five year old to it and he loved it.  A lot of the animals were out and he tried to name them all or pose with the statutes. There are some great places to take pictures here. They raised the prices from 8 to 10 for adults recently and i was a little taken back. However they have redone all the signs and added a few new animals that werent there a few years back. Parking is still free and yes you do have to follow the signs to make sure you get there. However it has improved and for the positive. So it was nice and our family will be back.

Would give this place 6 stars if i could. My wife and i love aquariums however they all cost over 20 dollars a person. This was 12 dollars each and they had an amazing selection of aquatic life. There was hands on exhibits including sting rays and even sea stars. They had lots of exotic fish as well. There was also a nice souvenir shop with items ranging from 3 dollars to 20. The parking is free and if you get hungry there is a nice cafe inside. Overall a great experience and i will be back.

A nice place and one of my family's favorite to visit. You can get some great family photos by the longhorns. Their is bathrooms nearby  with water fountains, which comes in handy if you got little ones. Also all of it is easy to walk to. If you have time walk over to the other side and check out the Martin Luther King mural and lookout platform..    worth the few extra steps. All in all a hidden gem in Waco. You can never go wrong making a stop here even if you're just passing through.

My wife and I came to this area for a staycation. We noticed this huge park with quite a bit of shade. It had a huge playground with two areas that are covered and fenced for the kids to play. This is something we always check because of our four year old. Also they have a huge train engine that you can take a picture in front of. The water park is right  next to it so you could actually do both. One of these days we are going to do just that.  Had a great time will definitely be back

This is a very well done collection of statues paying tribute to the classic storybook characters, my son very much enjoyed seeing these characters brought to life. When you arrive at this park, be sure to check out the sign because it will also give you a map to other statues that are scattered throughout downtown, all within a few blocks of each other. It was easy to navigate and the streets were not too busy to walk across. This is a definite must-see to bring children to enjoy.

Great stadium to come to. It has a really great atmosphere for a ball game. Even on the third level one can see the field quite well. If you are a rangers fan you have to go and watch  a game. Stadium parking is around 15 to 25 dollars which is reasonable for a professional game. Food is anywhere from 5 to  10 dollars. Get the souvenir cheese fries for 9 dollars you get a tasty snack and souvenir in one. Will definitely be back.

Went walking here a few weeks back on a mini vacation. Nice area beautiful scenery and lots of wildlife, suprising considering it being in the middle of  the Arlington entertainment district. However my son had a great time even enjoyed chasing the ducks trying to imitatate them. With the stadium in the background it is a very pretty place. Definitely worth the stop

A great place to take your kids. Also a great place for adults to learn too.  It has many things to offer from live theater to a art gallery, to a history museum,  to a planetarium. My wife and i got to check out some things including the art gallery, which was quite nice. It was cool that they had so many things in one spot. Will definetly be back.

If you are looking for great outdoors this is it. This is a nice free little spot where you can enjoy outdoors and learn how to protect it. I had been to a few wildlife refuge before and this is one of the nicer ones. It is a great place to take the kids and to get away. Will defiantly be back when i come back to Shreveport.

It was cold when we went here and we were able to only walk a little bit. However the scenery was amazing and the waterfalls were gorgeous.  There is some nice parking nearby that is free. The park is also easy to get to from the main road. Will definetly be back when it is warmer. It is a beautiful little spot.

Great park  showing the history of the medal of Honor. What an honor to learn about the modern day heroes of this country. Even if you are not a history buff it is a amazing place to visit. Great place to bring your kids. Thank you military for all that you do.

This is a great place to take your family. The staff is always courteous and very knowledgeable about the animals. Huge zoo will take you 5 to 6 hours to go through. However it is worth every minute and every penny. Also free parking you can't beat that
Really neat place with lots of history. Great place to learn about music too. It is definitely worth stopping at. Perfect ending to walking the canals of bricktown.
Beautiful inside and out. great selection of cactus on the back end of the bridge.  great views up top on the skybridge. Cost 8 bucks but worth it.
Coolest and weirdest thing ever but it rocks.  it is a little hard to get in to for lack of signage but it is a great freaky fun spot
Pretty bridge to drive across. However very difficult to get to if  from out of town. however our four  year old enjoyed the bridge
Small tiny museum but the rose rocks are awesome. Also you can buy one for really cheap. Worth stopping and seeing

One of the most amazing trails in the Cape. Very scenic and a very interesting mile hike. Plenty of amazing views and scenery all around. The dunes are fun to walk and run along. There are plenty of different trails to take from the start to the end at the water. The views are magnificent. Definitely carry some water and snacks when hiking because it gets tiring walking on sand for a mile. A must see location when in Cape Cod

A must visit location when in the Berkshires. Amazing history here. There is about 5 parking spots right across the main entrance to the tunnel. The tunnel is completely dark so if walking in, please be careful and bring plenty of lights. This is an active railroad so be aware of trains. Enjoy the view of the mountain in front of the entrance and the waterfalls right next to it.

Beautiful location to go for a relaxing time.  There is an open area to walk around.  It is right by the water and have beautiful views all around.  There is plenty of parking and people can sit in their car and enjoy the view.  There also is a lighthouse.  In the summers, camping is allowed here.  Beautiful area for a picnic, camping, hike, bike ride and a leisure walk.

Loved this place.  Boat cruise cost $20 round trip and we had plenty of time to walk around the island.  They had free guided tours.  3 options for guided tours which took you to different parts.  Staff there are very friendly. Unique items at the gift shop and visitor center.  Fort Warren is built uniquely and has a lot of unique views.

Amazing scenic location with an amazing trail right next to the water. You can walk along the water all the way to the end. Amazing place during sunset and the views are amazing. Perfect place for a photo shoot or landscape photography. Definitely check it out when in Bourne or around the Cape. Some of the best views in Bourne.

Very unique beach located next to Stage Fort Park. Really does look like a half moon when standing on the rocks on the right or left. Water can be a bit dirtyonly because there is a lot of weeds and leaves but other than that, its clean. There is plenty of parking across the stree. Free on weekdays but paid during weekends.

Amazing company with great service.  There are boats going to all the islands in Boston and the greater Boston area.  Amazing views and the crew and captains on all boats are awesome.  I have always had a great experience with them.  I take a trip to different islands or their locations every summer.

Amazing place to be specially because of the views. The water is amazing with great views during sunsets and the lighthouse is the best. Not alot of parking during busy times but there is alot of parking at the Salem Willows and walk down to the Fort. There is a lot of history here and its amazing.

Amazing place to explore an old abandoned fort with spray paintings all around and underground tunnels connecting the entire fort. Plenty of places to walk and hike. The tunnels are very dark so make sure to bring a light. Great place for photos and views of the water.

Great experience spending the day here.  Walked the whole way and enjoyed the whole area. Gets busy in the summer and people bring picnics and coolers for the day.  All surrounded by water and the fort in the middle. It's a fun place to go to when in Boston.

Amazing historic location in the heart of Salem. Very close to the other main attractions and restaurants.  This sight has amazing views all around.  Walk all the way down to the wharf lighthouse and you have an amazing view of the water and docks.

Loved the place and the environment there.  All courts are very well maintained. Beautiful architecture all around the venue.  Gift shop has a wide variety of souvenirs. Restaurant inside the HOF has great food but slightly highly priced.

Amazing park in the middle of Boston city. Plenty of space to walk around and enjoy yourself.  Food stalls and stores all around.  There is a train station on all sides to get out.  Peaceful place for a stroll by the water.

Very historic location in Salem with old styled houses that have been maintained to preserve the history. Located in the Forest River Park. The village has a lot of history. It shows how the witches used to live in Salem.

Amazing location with one of the best views in Salem. There is plenty of parking on the streets to get here.  The walk down the wharf is relaxing and has amazing views.  Definitely check it out when in Salem.

Perfect location for an evening stroll. Very scenic and panaromic.  Beautiful sunsets by the water while watching the boats coming back to dock.  Free to enter and plenty of tables and chairs for picnics.

Amazing place for hiking.  The view at the top is amazing. The hike is amazing too. There are tough climbs and many boulders and great locations for pictures.  Plenty of parking on sides and its safe.
Amazing state park in Rhode Island with amazing water and great places for strolls. Visit here if ever in Rhode Island. The place is amazing. There is plenty of parking. It does get very busy.
A very scenic area with a comfy benches with an overview of the water.   Great view.  Best place for a picnic.  Many trees to rest under.  Great location to relax and have a calming stroll.
Walked by this multiple times and it looks very beautiful from the outside.  They offer tours inside during the day. Very busy street but a fun place to visit at least once when in Boston.
Great park with plenty of parking. A large baseball field to enjoy on and 2 beaches right there. A very unique location in Gloucester. Enjoy a stroll around the park
Amazing location. Visit the docked ship when in Boston.  It's beautiful.  There is a lot of history to this ship and has been modified to be a luxury house.
Very well maintained park in the heart of Boston.  Clean and family friendly.  Goo place to have picnics out in the open. Right by the Marriot at the Wharf.
Beautiful location with a great view.  Right behind SMCC and a great place for a walk right down to the water.
Great zoo and a perfect place for a family outing. They have tennis courts too. Great place for a picnic.

Loved the trail!! Well maintained and lots of scenic stopping points. I want to see a sun rise/sunset here! Once you have crossed  the causeway on the main Rd in you will come to the little shack where you can pay if there is an attendant. Immediately after that on the right is a parking area with a public restroom. There is also a small box for a fee deposit if the gatehouse was not staffed. From the parking lot there are several direct spots to access the Beach or to proceed to the trail around the island. There are numerous little access points to the shore line which are fun to explore when the tide is out. Halfway around there is a really cool little wooded area with a sign inviting people to leave a fairy house. It has very clear rules and is quite charming. The middle of the island is the school for the deaf and I don't believe the public is invited so please be respectful of their privacy.

I always end up here whenever I am in Portland!!! Beautiful views and so peaceful. It is in Fort Williams Park and plan to spend the day if you come here. The park is open year round and the lighthouse is fully maintained. It is well worth it to come back more than once in all types of weather. I can't resist coming her whenever I have a free moment. Every picture seems to come out different! The parking directly in front of the lighthouse is limited and I only use it in the winter. During the summer you are better off parking in the larger parking lots and walking around because the sights are amazing from all points!

Extremely well maintained and well marked. You will want to come back more than once!
Finally made it there while the museum was open. Will still be going back as many times as I can!! 7-22-17

Don't follow GPS because it takes you to a non parking and not through traffic rd. You have to park on Macy ST. This is an Amazing location! All in all it's a half mile one way. But plan on spending lots of time after you get a fitness walk in! So many birds! Bird watchers paradise. I am here in early spring and the trees are just coming into bloom. So I am sure there will be lots more. The main path is well maintained and the smaller side paths are kept in the natural environment. The pond itself is a work in progress and you can see in a few spots where wildlife Wade's to shore. There are a few rocks that are covered with sun bathing turtles! I will be back here frequently I think!

Clean and well maintained gardens! Beautiful walking areas. There are several parking areas so you have a variety of locations to wander. There are several that are not maintained during the winter so pay attention to signs and barriers. Also the walking paths are not fully maintained all winter either. There are still a lot of locations to walk around just wear appropriate clothing and foot wear and be careful. The lighthouse itself is fully taken care of year round and there are a few spots to park close to it. If the spots are all taken park further away, enjoy the view and then check back because most don't stay long and parking rotates quickly.
dislikes: Some areas not maintained in winter

reviews_attraction.text: I didn't go to ski. I hate winter! We attended a Christmas ugly sweater party. Dj was excellent however very little attendance which was a good thing because the room by the bar was small. Very cozy atmosphere and you could see the mountain from the large windows along the building. I was disappointed though because they had already closed the food down. It was  only a little before 8. The sweater party was listed tili 9 but we found out it was planned to go later than that. I would go back but I would plan ahead if I had more information. Also the parking lot wasn't very well lit and had little signage.

I stumbled across this shell of a mansion and fell in love with it!! The architecture is amazing and it is sad that it is in such disrepair. If ever I wish brick and mortar could talk then this is it. This can be accessed by the first parking lot on the left as you enter Fort Williams. I would like more signs to direct you to it. It can be accessed year round and in the summer there are trails all the way around the structure so you can get a full view of the amazing building. There is a cute little memorial stone with a description of the history of the building as well.

Plan to take your time to enjoy this area. I would like to see it kept cleaner and scrub grasses mowed to provide more space for flower gardens, however the wild flowers that grow in the unmaintained area are rather pretty. The light house can be viewed from several vantage points and there is quite the panorama of the boats on the water as well. The area looks neglected in places but that may be part of its charm. The parking is limited but if you are up to the walk you can park at Buglight or Willard beach parking lots and spend time wandering around.

Such an amazing location!!! There are several historical items and a couple of gorgeous memorials. There is a large amount of space for people to lounge in the sun and enjoy the view of the ocean and boats. I could easily spend a whole day here. There is limited parking on busy days but plenty of nearby places to park and walk. The park itself is on top of a hill however the trails wind slowly down to the ocean and Eastern Promenade Trl. The only down side is it is difficult for wheelchairs. Definitely going back!

Very clean and trails are easy to find and navigate. I only had a short amount of time and it was just enough do a quick jog/walk to Jewell falls and back. The parking area could use some attention and I wish it was clear if it is ok to cross the tracks and use the trail there. There was alot of birds and squirells to keep it amusing to listen to and I am sure if you took a moment to read you would surely see alot of nature in action! I will definitely keep this on my list of places to return to!

Very cute beach and a lot more space than I would have thought. I enjoyed the walkway to the beach and the food booths that are available. There a lot of surfers and availability to utilize the water. The parking is a downside as there is only one lane in and out and they don't tell you when you pay that there is no parking available. So you may have to wait if someone ahead of you is waiting for a previous beach goer to leave. All in all not bad but not one of my favorites.

Such a well maintained site!!! And I love the memorials and dedications all along the walkway. They are a treasure for sure. Great views and I would love to watch a storm roll in across the horizon. You can walk all the way out around the lighthouse and get an amazing view of the harbor. The footing can be slippery but there is a fence to prevent falling into the ocean. Very simple and well maintained location.

Nice little area to sit and enjoy the boats on the water or stroll downtown Wiscasset. Free 2 hour parking within site of the Wiscasset bridge. Very soothing. I have been here in the winter and will go back in the summer for new views. There is a cute little ice cream shop down on the docks and a small railroad station right near the parking area as well.

Loved it!!! Will be making numerous trips! Well marked and clean trails. It is easy to access. There is a large play area for kids and plenty of picnic tables for families to eat or rest at. There is also plenty of open lawn area for picnic or hanging out with family and friends. $4.00 per adult and $1.00 per child under 12.

Didn't get a chance to tour it but will go back for sure.
Went back today with family and walked to the lighthouse along the rocks....it's further than it looked. 7/15/17
I have been back several times and I like the views. You can access this year round just use caution and plan accordingly for the weather.

I loved strolling along the water. There are plenty of benches. Plenty of space to view the harbor and lots of informative boards to understand the history of the area. There is a perfect blend of the cobblestones and newer pavement to make walking easier.

I absolutely love the beach and the trails beyond the beach. Beautiful scenery and amazing views, however the parking lot is not maintained very well and the bathrooms are extremely outdated and not very inviting. Plenty of stalls but not very safe.

Beautiful and naturally maintained! Love it. there are alot of places to sit in the shade and view the water as well as very informative signs explaining the history of the fort. Well preserved and maintained!
I LOVE this place. This was my third year for the gardens aglow and it has gotten bigger and better every year! Staff is amazing and helpful and there are plenty of things for everyone to see.
at the time it was a work in progress and my favorite thing was the mini golf which has since been taken out. the other rides were ok but I am not a daredevil and didn't enjoy them as much.
This was very easy to find and has great parking. You can walk down on either side of the lighthouse but there restrictions because a coast gaurd family lives at the lighthouse.

This was so peaceful. I could hear birds and ice cracking when it floated by. Absolutely beautiful view! I will definitely be returning here!
3/14- second trip! still gorgeous!
Beautiful view with several benches to sit and enjoy breeze. I don't recommend sitting during low tide as there is an odor however it's a gorgeous location.
This is a little hard to find. You can't access the lighthouse however there is a small beach where I found some unique treasures and ledges to climb on.
well maintained play area for kids as well as a gazebo and a beautiful veterans memorial. The lights in the trees for the holiday season are delightful.
So unique, very accessible, lots of historical accuracy and information. Highly recommend. I did not go on the ships however I will definitely go back!

I highly recommend World's End! It has a very relaxing atmosphere about it. Big, open meadows with seaside views sprinkled with a little bit of woods makes this an ideal place to take a walk and to take in nature. The trails go in loops so that even if you lost your map you could easily work your way back to the entrance. Only downside is that it has an entrance fee, but it's worth the money since the Trustees do a great job keeping the land in good shape. If you get a Trustees membership you get discounts across all their properties. This is a great place for a picnic and they have lots of parking. They also have porta potties near the entrance if you need to use the bathroom.

I'm not from around here so after doing research this trail came up time and again so I did it with my wife. We couldn't be more happy with it!! If you don't have much time but have a day to fit in something that embodies Ranier, this is the hike. Great views all around with close up views of the glacial peak and vistas spanning all around. I went late September when the huckleberry bushes were turning to fire red color. It was gorgeous! We had a lot of wildlife sightings too. I highly recommend this whether or not you have a lot of time, but especially if you only have 1 day to fit something in. There's even a bathroom at panerama  point.

Definitely neat to see the glass there and the ornate designs. The glass blowing demonstration was informative and fun too. The museum could use a little upkeep in areas though. Also they have a lot of the same kind of glass work on display which started to get a little old to me. A little more variety would be nice. Then again, it's important to remember they are showcasing SANDWICH glass, not necessarily all forms of glass art, hence the repetition of the same glass designs. That being said, they do have an exhibit room where they showcase pretty cool glass art from various glass artists.

Don't know what to review about this other than what people already know: that Jaws was filmed here and that it's a bridge...Aside from that it's a nice area to go for a dip. The sign says no jumping off the bridge but everyone does it anyway. Not really sure what's going on with that, but it seems that you wont get in trouble for jumping into the water. Just be careful and don't sue the town if you get hurt after breaking the rules! If jumping off the middle area you should be safe since it's deep enough there.

Very nice setup here at the visitor center! Great information about the history of the area and about the flora and fauna found nearby. You can go upstairs where they have a small museum with artifacts from the area. This is a great place to find information about the area, especially the Blackstone River Heritage park. They also do events year round out on by the parks department. I recommend coming here to learn about the area and to get all the info you need for the local hiking and biking paths

Great park to hike in! Not far from the city or other civilization so you really can't get TOO lost. You get variety with anything from short, flat loops around ponds to long, rocky hikes with modest elevation gain and nice views. These don't in any way replace going to the White Mountains, but for a day hike in nature and a break from the daily grind, this is an excellent choice! Trails are mostly well marked and intersections are numbered so you can always see where you are on the map

Friendly staff. I appreciated the effort put forth to remember Essex's shipbuilding past. They could use some more informational material to read if you choose to do the self-guided tour as there wasn't much explaining the tools and things they had on display. I would recommend the guided tour as I'm sure the tour guide goes through all the information you would miss doing the self-guided one. Definitely a small museum but it's nice in that it's not overwhelming with content to read.

Definitely worth the money. A very beautiful site with cool waterfalls and water running over moss and fern covered rocks. It has a boardwalk built into the rocks that allows a close up view. The hike is family friendly but there is a decent uphill all the way to the gorge so just be aware for anyone with some physical issues. They also have a nice visitors center with bathrooms and food to purchase.

A nice park. It's not overwhelming in scope but there's a nice trail with good views and an ocean/beach aspect to it. I got to see seals sunbathing on the rocks in April, great place to see them! This is a great place for looking at tidal pools and exploring, not so much for a sandy beach, although there are spots to lay blankets. Also close to good dining options in Plymouth.

Nice area of New Bedford. It has a lot of nice cobblestone roads and historic Captain's houses/other historical buildings. Make sure to stop at DNB burger in the area for a bite to eat! Just be careful because the moment you leave the historical area it gets sketchy real quickly. Definitely avoid going to far out of the historic area if you're visiting

Gorgeous park!!! I knew it would be nice but it was nicer than I thought. The grounds are well kept and the park is huge. They do a great job with the landscaping and the view is great. The lighthouse is very nice and there's lots of parking too. It's set a little way away from the main action of Portland but it's well worth that 15 minute drive!

Great museum with a lot to see. It looks newly renovated and they have enough different things to keep you interested. Staff was friendly and tickets were reasonable. It's in a nice historic section of New Bedford where you can walk afterwards weather permitting. Also good food options within walking distance.

The views by the cranberry bogs were pretty unique! The rest of the hikes through the woods was nothing special, but the paths were marked out and I didn't have a problem finding my way around. I think the markings could have been better though. It's worth coming here for a stroll in a nice day

Beautiful views and a nice walking trail nearby. There are some informative plaques too for those who are interested in the local history. Definitely worth the drive to get away from the busy Bar Harbor side and enjoy the more relaxing west side of the island.

Nice place for a stroll and to grab some fried seafood or tacos during the warmer seasons. The beach itself is nothing special but there's a lot of parking that's free and it's a good place for walks and to see sunrises and for grabbing some food.

Very ornate and has beautiful architecture. Their indoor globe room is very unique. I don't think it's worth full admission however. Look for a promotional deal or something. That's what I did and it was well worth the time and money with a deal.

One of America's oldest parks. It's nice for getting away from the bustling city but there's also plenty of activity opportunities. It's nicely lit for Christmas in the winter and has the frog pond for cooling off in the summer

Very nice mansion. They had lots of tour info but it wasn't overwhelming. I like how they let you walk around and take in the property at your own pace. The parking was easy too and the staff, friendly
Delicious mead! Very small meadery but one of the few in New England. They have all kinds of varieties such as berry, apple, or cinnimon meads or the go to original meads. Owner is very friendly.
Beautiful falls. Short hike to the view although it can be a little steep at places for those who don't like any hills. Isn't a gruelling hike though. I recommend a visit to this beautiful park
Nice little overlook. There are trails nearby as well, but other than that it's a simple overlook. It's great for quickly driving to a view instead of going on a hike to get to one
A nice oasis in the city. The park is very clean and well shaded for a hot summer day. It's a beautiful park and it's away from the other, more crowded parks around the city
Great church that is very involved in the Boston community and with helping the poor. Very transitional church as many members come and go due to school etc.
Neat building if you see it from the inside. It isn't much from the outside, so I recommend taking the Adams tour (bus comes out of Quincy Center)
I'm not a member here but it was fun visiting. Lots of character and it was fun to just walk around and take in the atmosphere.

It's great, loads of nicely paved paths that are easy to get around with the kids and then a few trails that are easy enough to walk but some aren't so good for pushchairs, so a bit of something for everyone.

The Vietnam Memorial is rather lovely and tranquil and then near that is the farm which is free and pretty cute. The kids seem to love it. Across from that is plenty of picnic benches and tables and not to far away is a concession stand, baseball field and playground.

The playground is geared to slightly older kids though, so bit of a disappointment and also no swings as well as not much shade, so the slides got pretty hot.

There's a public golf course too in one corner. Cracking views around the pond and great for cyclists. Not many restrooms though, some at the farm and then some dubious looking ones in the middle of the park, but there are at least plenty of parking in various places around the park.

We visited as we were in the area for a family event and had free entry due to a reciprocal art membership, other wise this place might be a little expensive for what it is.

That said, it did have a decent and varied collection of art, with a focus on Maine and there is a lovely garden with a small sculpture park and a further gallery across the street out the back in a old church. Enough to entertain younger kids, but realise it isn't geared towards little children too.

The museum store is also very good. Plenty of on street parking around the place as well.

This place is great for kids of all ages. There's a nice mix for the older tweens and the young toddlers with a lot of hands on crafts and activities with various themes. Can spend several hours there.

They don't have much of a gift shop or options for food, but there is plenty of places nearby.

Parking is a little limited at the place, but there is a fair bit of street parking in the area.

They do a fun kids party.

Great place for the kids on a nice day as there are some lovely, simple trails around the grounds. Lots of birds and other animals to see and great selection of interactive exhibits inside. A lovely party ground out side too. There is a couple of cafes up eat at but a nice place to bring a picnic. The tree top walk and train rides weren't open on our visit but they did look impressive. There is also plenty of parking.
dislikes: Some activities closed (tree top walk, train rides)

reviews_attraction.text:
We got in free as we have a reciprocal membership from else where, so I don't know how this fairs for value.

I brought my daughters with me, both young kids and they enjoyed it. A nice mix of things on display and something a little different to look at when you have an afternoon to kill time. Parking is a little iffy as they don't have their own lot, but there's enough parking in the surrounding streets.

A nice set of trails that make a couple miles for the main loop with some shorter cross trails through the loop. Pretty well marked and for the woods, not particularly buggy and quite suitable for young kids, my 5 and 8 year old girls had no fun. There is a fair few parking spots around the hill, but we went from the back of The Discovery Museum.

Lovely place for a nice, short hike that is good for kids. There is a fair bit of parking and rest room facilities. Lots of birds ranging from woodpeckers, hawks, herons and ducks, a lot of turtles, beaver activity and deer in the area. There are military training grounds across the river do when they do exercises it can be noisy.

Fab collection of butterflies, but it's rather expensive if you didn't have a coupon along for the kids.

Decent amount of parking and picnic benches outside to make an afternoon of it, but it is quite a short visit.

Also, it's very warm inside, so dress appropriately and in layers, especially the kids.

Open at odd days, compared to other museums so it's worth keeping an eye out. That said, there's plenty to see for all ages. My young daughters loved the armour collection as well as some of the older sculptures but generally have fun browsing around.

There's a fair bit of parking too.

This place is small and has limited parking but we have a reciprocal membership from another place and this makes for a great short visit if in the area.

Lovely exhibits, especially in the kids section and really nice staff. They also have fun kids events too.

A lovely place to go for a picnic and walks asking the trails. The buildings are also interesting and a few crafts and things to get kids interested especially in the art and native Indian stuff. Nice gift shop and lovely restaurant. Fab views too!

This was a lovely place to visit in the summer with the kids. Very relaxed but spread out with easy trails to walk around and lots to see. Also a nice place to bring a picnic along and eat at one of the numerous benches along the historic sites.

We go here regularly as membership is really good value and have done for a few years. Kids are now 8 and 5 and both love coming here for either building and for the crafts they do. Great place to have a picnic lunch during a half day of school.

Nice place to go for a walk or a run. Biking isn't bad either with a few trails with differing difficulties but it's not terribly hard and mostly well marked. Parking is a little limited though, depending on which entrance you find yourself at.

Fantastic place to come for a picnic with friends. Lovely views and a great store. The beer is pretty decent and the growlers are great value and they even fill growlers from other establishments.

Great place to bring the kids too.

Small but charming museum! A collection of steam cars, photographic stuff, musical instruments and other info from the Stanley family. Staff were very friendly and it was a nice tour, about 20 or so mins of puttering around.

The kids love it here. Plenty to see outside so it's great for a walk and a picnic. The art gallery inside is okay, little limited and not as little kid friendly. The cafe is lovely but pricey. The gift shop is fantastic.
Quiet, small pond. Decent amount of parking. Seems popular for fishing. Plenty of benches and a few swings. Not much to walk around but a nice place for a lunch picnic. Ice skating during the winter.
Pretty small but interesting place. They have a little kids scavenger hunt and some nice things for little kids to see and certainly worth a visit if you had a short time to kill in the area.

We came for a concert and thought the place was great. A lot of character and info. The stage was great with nice seating too. Good views and comfortable.
Plenty of parking in the lot too.
likes: Facilities & Services: Stage, Seating, Views, Comfort

reviews_attraction.text: This place is great. Fair bit of parking, nice trails that are good for kids. Can get buggy in the summer so bring bug spray but it's a great place to see dragon flies and butterflies.
Only stopped into the store to kill a bit of time. Friendly staff and a lot of fun products and materials for sale in a good range of budgets. My daughter (7), loved it.
Expensive even with library discount. Fun place though and good for a couple hours. Some hands on activities. Not a great place if you have a pushchair though.
A lovely park that is a delight to walk through. Great history here with lots of info dotted around for you to see. Fab views too.
Nice little walk out to the lighthouse, with little spots along the way with historical notes that the kids found amusing.

This is a large, marble monument of George Washington atop a tall column in the center of historic Baltimore. Completed in 1829, it stands at the top of a narrow strip of park dotted with lovely trees, bushes, flowers and other statuery, most notably an equestrian statue of Washington's trusted Marquis de Lafayette. It is possible to climb the 227 marble steps in the winding staircase at the center of the monument to the top. The staircase is brick-lined and very narrow. At one point, it is a little too dark to find one's foothold. There is a railing available for assistance. Upon reaching the top, the climber is "rewarded" with excellent views of Baltimore. Sadly, Baltimore does not offer any excellent views and the entire enterprise is at that point called into question. The viewing deck is off limits out of safety concerns, but we may take in views from behind three windows. A fourth opening has had a gate fashioned over it, which allows ventilation, but which also blocks the "view." $6 admission fee for adults, children aged 13 to 17 pay $4 and it is free for those 12 and under. Cash not accepted. Receipts can only be e-mailed. No restroom facilities available.

This is one of the best-preserved historic houses in the United States, especially considering the original furniture and other contents. It is like stepping back into the late 19th century. George Washington lived here for 8 months while controlling Boston-area military operations in the Revolution. The house is better known for its association with the Longfellow family and it is laid out pretty much as Longfellow left it. The staff are friendly and professional. Each tour guide adds his or her own interests to the tours, so there is always an opportunity to learn something new. This is a must for all lovers of history and literature. Free admission as it is administered by the National Park Service. Parking is always challenging in Harvard Square, but the house is a lovely 10-minute walk from the MBTA red line Harvard subway station.

Historic Jamestowne is an open-air museum and active archaeological site preserving the legacy of the 1607 English settlement that would
later become the United States. The site is extensive (21 acres), and requires a full day to see everything. Most visitors are very satisfied with a two-hour visit, however. Aside from foundations, only part of one of the original buildings remains. Despite being a National Park, the entrance fee is $14 per person 16 and older, free for those under 16. The site features a very impressive museum, the Archaerium. The museum indicates that photography is not allowed, but one of the staff informed me that this applies only to the human remains on display.
