A highly recommended visit for anyone in the Virginia area and history lovers.

Although this library is touted by locals as a wonder of architecture and design, all of this supposed glory has been buried beneath a massive restoration project which is scheduled to be completed in the spring of 2019. Having peered into the construction areas, I do not believe that the beauty of the finished product will rival that of the centerpiece libraries of the Boston or New York public library systems. That said, it is, of course, a library first and foremost and I imagine that it serves this purpose admirably well, from what I observed. There is a large children's room, but it is not suited to children's needs or interests. Management would do well to consider renovating this section of the library next.

This is probably the best art museum in the United States, north of Boston. It is medium-sized, so it is possible to fully explore it in about two and a half hours. It has some excellent pieces and a gallery dedicated to art depicting Maine. It is housed between two buildings; a modern, purpose-built structure which holds the majority of the collection and patron services, and a historic house, which appears to have lost its original charm through renovation. It is largely devoid of art, but I expect that this will change. Located in the tourist center of downtown Portland. Free on Friday evenings.

Small, city of Somerville park on a historic site. The trees at the street-level create shade which prevents any kind of grass. This leads to a slope around a rocky crag which looks very inviting, but terribly dangerous, for children to climb. A path appears wrapping around to the top of the hill, which is home to the oldest stone structure in Massachusetts, a windmill which was later converted into a gunpowder storage depot that played a role in the American Revolution. Okay park. Beware of trust fund hipsters walking with their dogs unleashed, in violation of Somerville city ordinances.

Built in 1798, the State House is the seat of government of Massachusetts. The governor's office is here, as well as the legislature. The building has been added to over the centuries, but all is richly adorned with fine Italian marble, stained glass windows, wrought iron railings and full of artwork depicting the history of the area. As a government building, it is free and open to the public, but only during normal business hours. This is a must-see for history buffs. Free tours available. Reservations recommended, but they will always take walkins. Yes, the dome is real gold.

The Walters Art Museum is the preeminent art collection of the larger Maryland area. The fact that it is free makes it a boon for the local community and a must see for every tourist in Baltimore. Although the collection spans the world and thousands of years of civilization, its European galleries are the  best represented, especially the medieval ones. Very well presented. Located in the historic center of Baltimore. Small cafe and gift shop on site. This was the highlight of my visit to Baltimore.

This was the highlight of our visit to Hampton Beach, New Hampshire. Fun, friendly, passionate, informative staff introduce you to the creatures of the Gulf of Maine. We were able to handle starfish, crabs, horseshoe crabs, lobsters and a variety of other critters. I have had similar experiences at Boston's New England Aquarium, but Ocean World Oceanarium is far better. We learned more and interacted more here in one visit than in several to the New England Aquarium.

This is a lovely equestrian statue in bronze of the Marquis de Lafayette, erected to the honor of this hero of the American Revolution in 1924. It is located near the top of a narrow strip of park in the historic center of Baltimore, just below the Washington Monument. Taken together, the two monuments make an excellent photo opportunity for tourists in Baltimore, especially considering the neighboring buildings, greenery, flowers and antique lamp posts.

Great beach in the town of Hampton Beach, New Hampshire. Although popular, plenty of cheap parking and spots in the sand available. I was impressed by how clean the beach was. Towards one end, there is a large outcropping of rocks. This creates some tidal pools, which are fun for exploring marine life. The beach is bordered by Ocean Boulevard, which is a commercial district catering to tourists: gift shops, pizzerias, and the like.

Who knew you had to pay to use the road to the top of Mount Washington? $35 per car, $10 per "extra" adult. ("Adult" is defined as 13 and older.) $7.00 for kids. This is a private company which somehow owns and operates the road. For the price you pay, you would expect it to be better maintained. I am sure the state of New Hampshire or the National Park Service would do a better job. Compare with the the Acadia roads, for example.

Monument Square is a small park on Congress Street, in Portland Maine. The main feature is a lovely statue erected to the memory of the Union Civil War dead, "Our Lady of Victories." As it is in an urban area, there are a number of homeless people and drug addicts who congregate there. This is in the arts district of the city, so numerous restaurants, bookstores and art supply stores.

I have been on the whale watch twice and never saw more than a few whales and those were at a distance. This was in the high season, too, when there are supposed to be more. Convenient location for tourists who are at the aquarium and harbor area, but really nothing special.

Although the existing structure is a reconstruction dating from only 1978, it is a picturesque building set against the lovely backdrop of Rockport harbor. Throw in a couple of lobster traps, and you are all set for your next selfie, sketch or oil on canvas.

It's a lighthouse in Portland, Maine. Meh. Charging $4.00 for a minimum of two hours of parking, when most visitors stay about thirty minutes, means you can really afford to invest in proper restrooms and not point us to porta potties.

Fun statue of the children's literature character "Pollyanna." it is located on the grounds of the Littleton public library and just a stone's throw from the site of the home of the Eleanor H. Porter, who created the character.

Lovely covered bridge in the quaint town of Littelton, New Hampshire. The bridge spans a nice stream and offers a view of a water wheel. There is a nice pathway with plenty of flowers alongside one bank of the river.

Fun, inexpensive activity on a beautiful pond in the Public Gardens, great for tourists and locals alike. The ride is short as the pond itself is small, but provides great photo ops. Nice start to a first date.
Excellent resource for 20th American history. Beautifully executed building and wonderfully presented collection. Easy parking. Free shuttle bus from the MBTA red line JFK / UMASS subway station.
Lovely little park which was renovated just a few years ago. Well-planned with lots of features for its small size, it includes a sprinkler for kids and a nice little playground.
Excellent recreation of an early 19th-century New England town, complete with period buildings, furnishings and involved historical interpreters. Great for the 4th of July.
I have always enjoyed this museum, but it speaks more to some than to others. The courtyard and garden are considered one of its highlights, but sometimes less is more.
Best place to score drugs in Cambridge. Sure, the Cambridge police headquarters are there, but they don't mind. Clean up your act, Cambridge.
I have visited 3 times and have never been impressed. Many of the historical interpreters just don't seem to be into it.

A water park that tries to emulate Aquatopia but comes up short. The prices are very expensive and they have a tendency to gouge. Tried to order tickets online and there was a $10 "convenience fee." The food is very expensive ($75 for fast food for three at Johnny Rockets)  and the lines do not move. After paying $15 for parking, we were told the tram was down and we had to walk a good distance in 90 plus weather. Very easy to drop $500 for a family visit.

Went to the Rise of the Jack O'Lanterns. It was during the evening but the grounds looked well tended and manicured. The event was a little pricey but a lot of work went into carving ornate pumpkins. It took a total of twenty minutes. Even though there was a huge crowd, the lines moved quickly and parking wasn't an issue. It was a really nice time but I probably wouldn't go back next year.

This church I also known as the Actor's Church because of the thespians who frequented it back in the day. (A relative, stage actor, Joe Jefferson, actually gave it the moniker, "The Little Church around the Corner"). The ground and buildings look like you took a step back in time to an English country church. The interior is very well kept with ornate woodwork. Very tranquil setting.

A large working farm and petting zoo. Admission is free but they charge you for everything at every step of the way down to  the piece of lettuce to feed their animals. You can easily drop $100 bucks for a small family. On street parking is next to impossible. Drive a little further and go to White Post Farm which is definitely more family friendly.

A very nice pre-Colonial era church in the Wall Street area. It is currently undergoing renovation but the chapel is open. I wandered the historical graveyard and although the stones are badly eroded, you can locate the final resting places of Hamilton, Fulton, Frances Lewis, etc.  Nice respite from the hustle-and-bustle of Manhattan.

A really nice Church but not the original structure which was located a short distance away.  It was originally known as the "Printers Church" for the very early morning masses held for those in the printing trade. My great-grandparents were married here in 1859 so it holds special significance for me. Definitely worth a visit.

An outstanding, three mile stretch of boardwalk with literally dozens of stores, eateries and dessert establishment. You can meander parallel to the beach and see buskers and artisans playing their wares. It is well lit and secure. There is even a public restroom and fee applicable tram running the length of the strip.

My family went snowtubing so I can't comment on the ski area. It was moderately priced at $25 per person for a two hour block. However, the lines at the top move very slowly so you might be able to go down maybe four times in that two hour block. The lodge gets ridiculously crowded and the food is very expensive.

A nice park in my community. A lot of people allow their dogs off leash and monopolize the tennis courts leaving local residents shut out. Unfortunately, this nice gem has been "discovered" by people from outside the Middle Village leading to some crowding and litter issues. All in all, a nice park.

It is basically a small, two level indoor playground with very vague math themes. Likewise, staff members don't explain anything. It was enormously crowded and didn't have a place for the kids to eat lunch. The options were the bus or the park in 38 degree temps. Save your time and money.

If you positively, absolutely need to see fish behind glass and be charged a ridiculous amount at every turn (from the food to parking), this is your place. Prepare for a royal screwing! You can see everything in about twenty minutes  Pales in comparison to the aquarium in Riverhead.

A small, well-kept park in the Village. It's a nice place to sit and relax with a friend or read a book. It is especially nice around Christmas with the ornamental wreaths and tree. I like that local US servicemen were honored for their service in WWI with an large Doughboy statue.

A really nice place for children and adults to spend an afternoon. I believe the entrance fee was $8 and less for children and seniors. Personally, I thought there would be more exhibitions to check out.  Do spend some time at the panorama of New York City.

Standard NYC park in Astoria. It was recently renovated and there is now exercise equipment. I used to live in the area and this park has never attracted a disruptive element or been a hangout. In fact, it is never really crowded. Overall, a nice park.

While currently under renovation, I visited when it wasn't. It's in the Chelsea area of lower Manhattan and was once part of the estate of Clement Clarke Moore (who wrote the Night Before Christmas). Definitely worth a visit when it reopens.

A great place to visit if you're interested in late nineteenth century urban history. You'll learn about the deprivations and struggles that legally arrived immigrants endured as they built my city.  Fascinating way to spend an afternoon.

My family enjoyed the buggy ride although it was a tad short and a little expensive. It is a difficult to hear from the back of the buggy especially if other riders are taking nonstop (Be courteous of others). The driver was all-business.

Huge park which was the site of the previous two World's Fair. You can find the Museum of Science, ice skating rink, etc. Lot of open space including bike rentals. Can get crowded at times and parking can be difficult.
A newly renovated city park that is a pleasant place to idly sit or have lunch. The only drawback are the transients that occasionally smoke and drink. (So, minus two stars for lack of enforcement).
A beautiful church that preceded the more famous St. Patrick's uptown. There is an adjoining cemetery and catacombs. I don't like that the church and grounds are open only for paying your customers.
dislikes: Facilities & Services: Limited access for non-paying visitors

reviews_attraction.text: Smaller kids entertainment center with the usual assortment of games, laser tag and the like. There is a small snack bar and public restrooms. Looks a tad run down. Good to pass an hour or two.
A small city park located right off the LIE service road in Middle Village.  There are a few stationary swing sets and climbers for kids as well as bathrooms which aren't the cleanest.
Really nice park in central Queens. There are a number of trails and it's a great place for cycling. Seating and benches are scarce and parking in the adjacent area is easy to find.
A beautiful, inspiring Cathedral located in midtown. It is usually very busy and there are quick security checkpoints. Try to visit for a mass or a prayer or two.
A Dutch era farmhouse right in Queens. There are various festivals throughout the year and a small gift shop. Definitely worth a visit if history is your thing.

My sister and I went on a walking tour with Jamie Foster (Mistress Marian) as our guide. I have lived in the Annapolis area since I was a toddler, and am very familiar with downtown Annapolis. It was nice to be a tourist for a change. We walked down some streets I don't normally go down on my visits so it was nice to see buildings and places I wasn't very familiar with, or haven't payed much attention too, and understand their history better. My 16 year old sister also learned a lot, and was able to fill out several pages of notes in a notebook she carried with her (she is currently writing a comic that is a locally based historical fiction, and has been taking great interest in learning about as much local history and folklore as she can). Our guide was very knowledgeable about the local history, and how different things tied together. She was also kept the child who was on the tour very engaged, interacting with him and having him help her show and introduce things. The groups are not very large so you never feel lost in a crowd. I don't recall any steep hills, just one thing of steps to the state building. Frequent stops, and benches to sit if needed. Many of the stops are under trees too, which is nice for shade (or in our case a very light drizzle that came and went a few times). You leave from the visitor center and end at the dock, ego alley, which is the heart of the town (it also has public bathrooms,  a info booth, and other amenities if needed) so that you can finish off enjoying the best of downtown Annapolis, a place you now have a better understanding and appreciation for.

Probably the nicest garden I will ever see, and it was free. Parking is $1 a half hour (takes card) but there is free parking nearby if you dont mind a short walk. The photography rules seemed scary at first, but that is really just for for people only there to do professional photo sessions. We brought professional equipment but were just doing images of the plants and family for personal use, so no issue at all. Lots to see, we were there for about 3 hours (including resting and eating breaks) and saw about 80-90% of it. The native garden is spectacular with many "attractions" to see. Very nice paths to walk in that were well maintained with TONS of shaded benches and places to rest. Beautiful structures, including a traditional japanese tea house and many pavilion are on the paths, along with many pinds were you can get up close with animals such as frogs and ducks. The map also marks the best paths for handicap access. Most paths are in the shaded woods, but there is an area with a large open field kids can run around and let their energy out. There is a cute little cafe with locally made ice cream and sandwiches you can enjoy in the garden, a small giftshop in the visitor center and 2 bathrooms on the lot. I also saw many couples and families enjoying picnic lunches in shady spots. The garden has many entry/exit points so you can easily explore other areas durring your time there, my parents made a short detour to see the chapel.

I admit I am not a huge train person, but my dad is, and a large portion of my upbringing has been dedicated to trains and train hunting. This is one of the nicest train museums I have been to. it is very large and the trains are well maintained. I liked how you could go inside many of them, I hope even more open up as restoration continues. I would love to go inside of  dinner car.  The gift shop is large and even has some food (premium jerky and granola bars). Inside the museum there is also a area in the back right corner with multiple picnic tables and vending machines (chips,
jerky, teas, soda, water... took cash and card) where yo can get a drink and snack. A good thing to help prevent cranky hungry kids (including me lol). They also have a kids area with tons of toy trains for kids to play with, I suggest adults check out the area too as it also had adult displays to see (including a really cool large lego display, and more traditional displays and writings on the walls).  The museum has a section of large glass windows that give a very nice view of the hills, farm land, and animals. Parking is free and you can walk directly across the street to the Strasburg railroad  for a train ride when your done. There was also a guy selling novelty ice cream right out front when we went (cash only)

Got a group on thinking my dad would enjoy this place, and we could drag along. But my sister and I ended up really liking this place. Free parking  with a nice view of the water and the Dominoes Sign, they said it was fine for us to leave the car there while we walked to other places ( the visionary art museum is a short walk away,  just park off to the side and leave before closing time).  The way the place is set up is basically a bunch of different totally themed rooms you walk into and explore.  from a corner store, pharmacy, black smith, theater and more.  They had people who can explain the rooms to you and do demonstrations of the black smith work and printing press (you can take home printing samples, including a calendar) I liked the room showing pictures of places in Baltimore through out the years side by side with modern pictures. Neat to see the changes and development.   No places to eat, but they do have a room with a vending machine and tables. Also have a really cool exhibit on the video game industry in Baltimore where you can go station to station creating your own video game.

I was a little skeptical going at first, after reading reviews, but I was happily surprised. Animals looked clean and happy and while they aren't as big as huge zoos the cages were adequate in size. The zoo is a bit pricey, they normally have a $3 off coupon you can find with a google search, i think it is through the value pack website. Do get some food to feed the deer, sheep, and goats, a cup is $1 if you use the $1 off coupon. we also did the $5 camel ride which was short but a fun thing to say we did.  BRING YOUR OWN FOOD.  the cafe is only open on weekends and has no hot foods, just drinks and things like chips. we brought in a small cooler ( type with a strap you carry)  and ate at one of the picnic tables in the park, and brought the cooler back to the truck once we were done.

Wished we lived closer to visit more and do the many art classes/workshops. Love how nature and art come together. Lots to see during your peaceful outdoor walk. Great for kids. They have a craft room where you can do a free craft, was expecting something for very little kids, but they had a neat craft for older people making flowers out of old plastic soda bottles.  If you have the chance you must go to the holiday lights, it is so pretty to walk through a lit up woods at night. No feelings of being rushed by the car behind you, just walking at your own pace.  Different sections had different themes, most not Christmas themed, but still very pretty and creative. They had a live band inside playing traditional Christmas music. The gift shop is nice.

A great way to end our camping trip. Our saturday ride got bumped to sunday due to rain, but it worked out really well as sunday 9 am was cool, sunny, and no clouds in sight. Our group ended up being just the four of us and the staff was very friendly and patient with us as we are all complete beginners. We did the 1.5 hour ride and we were really glad we chose that instead of the shorter time we were going to do at first. The trail was fun, going through the woods with rocky slopes and narrow paths keeping it exciting and interesting. We also got to see many deer up close along the way. Guiding the horse was really easy as they know the path well, just got to guide them around low hanging branches and stop them from eating everything in sight :)

Steam into History AKA Northern Central Railway or New Freedom Rail,  is a fun stop for people of all ages. Extremely nice gift shop. Good layout and decorated neatly. Many affordable items. Very clean bathroom. Model train room in the back. Went for the mock jesse james robbery event. The robbery cast is very funny and interacts with all the riders. The gun shots can be loud for young kids. Cold drinks, local chocolates, and vintage candy available at the gift shop to be enjoyed while waiting for the train. Only a black away from the train museum and sandwich shop (highly recommend getting lunch there). Bottled water sold on the train for $3

Used a groupon, but even without it is not badly priced. The most interesting art museum  I have been to. Since the art is made by :everyday people" You can feel more of a connection with many of the pieces.  Very colorful. What ever you do, do not miss he gift shop, It had really cool stuff in it. Also don't miss the outdoor sculptures, the barn, and the other building with the interactive displays and whirly-gigs. I think many people didn't realize those places are part of the museum too. This was our first time going, We plan to go back again to check out the annual rotating exhibits.

Good place to start. Larger than it looks inside. Has bathrooms, lots of brochuresand maps, and people at desks that can help you. Nicely decorated interior. The trolley and walking tours start here. Had a couple benches to sit at and a drink vending machine. However the machine was sold out of many drinks and was exact change only (none of the drink prices were even dollar amounts, you need nickles or dimes and quarters). We were here for a watermark tour. Has a small conference room too.

Such a great free zoo. Mostly north American animals like bears, flamingos, deer and such but a couple Australian animals too. Big and small. Best part is that it's free. Went early in January. Weather was decent. Bathrooms clean. Gift shop and snack shop closed for off season but they did have employees walking around with animals to show off. Nicely paved for a nice stroll. I think we were there for about 2 hours taking photos and such.

Loved our visit, it's small but has all the big animals like giraffes, tigers, lions, so it doesn't feel like you are missing out. Infact it's actually a great size to enjoy it all and not feel worn out at the end of the day.yiu will still get a solid 2-3 hours, if not more.  Wish the food stall wasn't cash only, but atleast the tickets and gift shop take card. Fed the giraffe and that was a fun bucket list item and only $3.

Great walking trail and plenty of open fields to play in. You can wal the full trail (part shade part open, goes by playground and dog park) or do the short part that is in the shade and is just by the playground. Also has stations you can stop at durring your walk with workout/stretch equipment. Shaded pavilion is great for picnics.

Fun walk. There is a flat-er paved easy road (about a mile or less, can take a stoller on it easy) to the falls from the parking lot or you can take the longer rugged nature path to get there, but know you will be stepping over rocks and such. There is also a beach area. Does get crowded, and there is an entrance fee.

Easy parking and lots to keep u entertained even if u aren't a big sports person. Many food options, and prices are definitely better than what they could be. Parking was easy, tho we normally take the light rail. Got to do a backstage tour once as a kid as part of a mom's group which was fun.

We had a very enjoyable and relaxing your on this boat. It was a great way to add some knowledge of the area to our honeymoon trip to cove haven and get to enjoy the lake for our lake trip. The water is calm, and the breeze is cool. You will stay seated the entire trip.

Great art on display. Staff is friendly and I got to go home with my very own original piece of art for a great price.  A wonderful painting of the place I went on my first date with my now-husband, so forever a part of my history, and now my home.

Visited on a open house day a while back. Food and activites for the whole family. Had some old buildings to look at, a small trail, gardens/greenhouse and a speaker giving a lesson on the areas soil. A fun and educational day. Friendly people.

Went here after getting back from a cruise (You can see our ship in one of the pics). Nice stop. Lots to see both inside and outside. They do a group green-screen photo when you arrive. We saw many dolphins in the water too.
Very fun to explore. I love the rooms set up and decorated for the doctor's office, dentist, surgery suite, post office, general store, cafeteria...  Can definitely spend the entire day here.
Great zoo. Lots of interactive areas. Neat displays/set ups, animals had many toys and stimulants. Loved how you could get so up close to many of the animals, and even pet some.
Such a great gallery featuring some very famous and well known artist. Great variety of pieces too for the size. Perfect date spot.
Glad we saw this while driving by. Nice quick pull over to take in the sights and read a bit about the dam in 2-3 minutes.
Had my wedding here Aug 22 2020, it's was perfect for about 50-60 people and the staff are super helpful and friendly.
Loved going here as a kid. Never crowded like big name aquariums, but still a lot to see and interact with.

I've loved the Fells for many years and used to do the Skyline Trail 3 or 4 times a week. It takes you up and down through birch and aspen forests, meadows, tall pine tree woods, a lovely lake (natural reservoir), over rocky surfaces, by old rock quarries, small natural ponds...a wide variety of scenery and great views of the Boston skyline. I can't really do it justice with a description but when I went today, Jan 11, 2019, the temperature hit 68 degrees and it seemed everyone was at the reservation! I had a wonderful time.

You're visiting Mrs Gardner's home, just as she left it so many years ago. Truly an immersive feeling wandering around her palace home filled from floor to ceiling with priceless treasures. The lighting is atmospheric and during midday when the sun is shining, it splashes light all over the garden courtyard and illuminates religious stained glass outside-facing windows. The sublight also bursts through the multitude of interior door openings and windows. I felt privileged to be a guest in this legendary woman's home.

Doesn't get any better than this for up close and personal with marine life!  There are so many colorful and interesting individual aquariums showing life in different ecologies along with a very generous area filled with penguins, and then the huge central tank that is 3 stories high and circular.  All the marine life are so healthy and well-cared for by their keepers. There is even a petting pool with a guide who encourages children to touch the very small rays and sharks as they pass.

Love the Blue Hills, 125 miles of trails through varying terrain in 7,000 acres and so accessible to those in those of us in the eastern part of the state. I hike there a lot, especially the Skyline Trail, and the views from Eliot Tower and the Observatory are incredible! I often go there in remembrance of my son Brian who passed away a little over 5 years ago at age 34. We loved hiking here and taking photos. Sweet memories.

One of the most appealing public parks I've ever visited! It's beautifully maintained and retains a very natural feel on the trails through the woods and by Kenoza Basin and Lake.  I was here for the peak fall foliage, the trees and leaves glowed with the sun and autumnal hues. Managed to get a good photograph of a heron, that was a wonderful few minutes!

Wonderful family owned and operated multi-generational community-oriented lines! I just went on the Save the Harbor / Save the Bay Marine Mammal Safari on Mass Bay Lines super cat M/V Freedom that Bay Lines provided, how generous for both organizations to provide a harbor opportunity at no cost for us locals. Thank you, from the bottom of my heart!

Ideal alternative to the famous Mt Monadnock hike because it's a short hike, albeit a rocky one (and tree roots) that's pretty much uphill all the way, the views are spectacular, and you don't have hordes of people. You can see Boston from the top and there's always a pleasant breeze to cool you off on a hot summer's day. Highly recommended!

Been out a bunch of times on full harbor tours, Georges Island, Boston Light, Spectacle Island, always a great time! Boston Harbor is not to be missed, BHC boats are comfortable no matter what the weather, the staff are friendly and attentive and the sights are both picturesque and historical. Highly recommended!

Mix 104.1's MixFest is New England's premier FREE music event! This year, Mix welcomes Kelly Clarkson, Blondie, and Andy Grammer to the stage at the DCR Hatch Memorial Shell on Boston's Charles River Esplanade !

I had an awesome time, LOVE YOU, Blondie!

An easy bike ride for me and I'm worlds away from the busy activity of Copley Square. A treasure that is always changing with the seasons, weather and people. A lot of 5k fundraisers go along here and then cross Mass Ave...fun and inspiring!

Heroic! A commanding location on the crest of the hill on the Boston Common, wonderful metal sculptures and bas reliefs. The Memorial Flag Garden is very moving, 37,000 individual flags laid out from the Monument down the slope.

Can't recommend highly enough! You'll see many artworks you will recognize but you'll also discover other pieces that delight. A truly magnificent but not overwhelming museum, we are so blessed to have this gem in our city.

A national and local gem, not to be missed, for sure! I'm a volunteer tour guide at Fort Independence, Castle Island, and we have visitors from all over the world. Wonderful place to experience history, nature and relax!
Fun place to visit if you're in the area, artwork changes constantly. There's also a lot of commissioned large scale public artwork within a few block radius. Great for picture taking and admiring.
I love this zoo, the animal residents are healthy and well-cared for with lots of stimulation. The staff are friendly and helpful. A treasured resource for all of us who live in the area!
Kinda feel like you're the only person who knows about this place so despite the overh traffic noise, it's "private." Colorful and fun pathways going in different directions.
I cycle down to the waterfront a couple of times a week just to sit in the sun or catch a Boston Harbor Islands ferry. Wonderful place to watch people enjoying themselves!
One of my most favorite places, for rock scrambling, chillin' and photography. Cool people hang out here.  Many RIP memorials here, my son Brian's among them.
Love the countryside feel of our Common, we're blessed to have so much open sky in the city. People out and about, young and old, on a beautiful autumn day!
Ten minute bike ride from my home, almost has the feeling of enchantment, locals and visitors, young and old, everyone is having a great time!
Wonderful open space with lots of points of interest...the zoo, overlook ruins, old bear dens, fogxFLO sculptures, woods, trails and stadium.
Truly lives up to its name! Something here for everyone whether sitting by a pond or hiking up the mountain for a magnificent view.
We in the Boston area are so blessed to have such beauty close by, along with the Harbor Islands, God-given treasures, indeed!
Fun spot in the heart of the city! Lovely walking paths all around and benches for people watching and catching some rays.
1st place I take an out-of-town visitor so they can get a good overview of the city before we hit the pavement!

The Old Government is one of the most important public buildings in the United States.

There was an exhibit called 50 Objects as well as a photography exhibit of Worcester Center that just amazed me. Time flew by wandering from room to room.  I remarked to my companion that I enjoyed this museum more than my recent visit to The Smithsonian.  I believe that is because the local history was so relevant to me and gave me the opportunity to appreciate just how rich and diverse this city has become over the years.

First time visit and we were pleased. Not crowded and the surroundings were absolutely beautiful and peaceful. Tried the cafe and was quite pleased with local food sourcing. Some organics were available and we were very pleased. Nice atmosphere and great tasting fresh food. Will be back soon.Nice walking trails. Didn't see as many flowers as I thought I would, but still lovely greenery.

I definitely think this is something more for small children and families when it comes to the level of light display but it was such a cute little date night for me and my fiancé, we talked and sang Christmas music, it was a fun night! Overall I don't think I would go back, once is definitely enough but it was something different and put you in the holiday spirit!

Beautiful and peaceful. My dog and I know each and every inch of the park, due to the fact that we spend most of our mornings walking there. It has hiking trails for when you're in the hiking mood and a beautiful running spot. Absolutely love this place.This park is quite large - with lots of water and open space for picnics/games and a few covered pavilions.

This was a wonderful visit! It's unfortunate that you can only go on weekdays since most people work during the week but I managed to score a day off to visit. Beautiful old building with plenty of History. They offer tours and it was completely worth it. You just need to make sure you go on a weekday! Be sure to check out the Women's Hall of Fame hallway

58,000 names are listed on the two 200 ft walls. Think about that.... 58,000 lives lost. For comparison, Yankee stadium has a 52k capacity. With SO many lives sacrificed, it's only fitting to have a memorial to honor these veterans. I even witnessed an older gentlemen who was emotional after a family member said, "Your name could have been on this wall."

We live locally and I'm honestly surprised that people gave this restaurant some of the reviews that I read below. This restaurant is a gem and classic in western mass.  It has always been a great restaurant with amazing food and really incredible staff.I would highly recommend going there to experience the atmosphere as well as some great food!

The museum itself is easily walkable in an afternoon and though the whole thing isn't HUGE it has a lot of various periods and really well curated and designed collections. We especially loved the huge center atrium with the paired wall mural and floor mosaic. I don't want to describe it and spoil it, it's that good and that visually arresting.

Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum is a hidden gem in Boston. It's a historic building south of Fenway with a gorgeous indoor courtyard that spans three levels with fountains, plants, etc. In addition, there are several galleries in the new building, many galleries in the old building, a restaurant, reading rooms, theaters, and a gift store.

A wonderful and free National Parks Service (NPS) site that is plenty entertaining for all, young and old, local or from abroad. The rangers are very knowledgeable and the site appears to be well-staffed. They are continually working to restore and maintain what most be a costly landmark mansion to be as historically accurate as possible.

At 16 acres, this park has a large playing field, lawns, monuments and lots of pathways. Bicycles are common but so are regular walkers and joggers and moms pushing strollers. It's a lovely green space, surrounded by busy roads and the Harvard University campus.The playground is a significant feature, with a mini landscape of its own

We visited during very busy time - graduation weekend at Harvard.  We were meeting one of my sister's professors for dinner and this was a spot she picked.  It's not fancy, kind of your basic student hangout with burgers and beer.ou could do a dinner with a little one if they don't run around if you could contain them in a chair.

New England winter would be A LOT harder with my kids if we didn't have an Ecotarium membership. This is our go-to place on cold days. I love that there is indoor and outdoor space for the kids. The outdoor space is worth the membership in and of itself. If you get a membership it pays for itself rather quickly.

We had a great afternoon here. It doesn't take all that long (we took maybe 1.5 hours) but it was enjoyable. My partner is a scientist and I love art, and it was the perfect intersection of art & science for us. As a student, it was only $5 per ticket - totally worth it. They have a cool little gift shop, too.

Several buildings with their own themes. The ladies selling admission were extremely friendly and knowledgeable about the museum setup. They recognized it was our first time there and gave us tips. We only went to 3 museums, the art museum with the sculptures was our fav as well as the Japanese history room.

The temporary display had the theme of 'Threads of Resistance'. If you like and/or support Donald Trump, I would not recommend seeing this part. There was a separate section of the 'Threads of Resistance' that was borderline pornographic. If one dislikes Donald Trump, this could be for you. Personally,

Harvard Square is a great place to checkout if your visiting from out of town. The shops, eatery's and live street performers make it a must to visit. If your local then your probably annoyed by the tourist and I'm sorry.  There is construction around a few of the areas I walked. Come and enjoy.

Beautiful! I really was impressed and surprised at the size, cleanliness and safe keeping of the park. Very scenic and organized. The Rose Garden, the Tiny Zoo and a lot more wonderful sites. $3 for MA drivers, $5 for out of state drivers to enter the park. A separate fee for the Tiny Zoo.

This is open to the public almost all the time, but for graduation and the night/day following admission required a ticket or student id. Once again, there were people who didn't think the rules applied to them and then when they weren't allowed in, there was an unpleasant conversation.

The fact that they have an actual weaving floor with working looms is AMAZING! You will definitely need some ear plugs but it is worth it. There is usually someone there actually working the machines and making dishcloths that you can then buy at the museum store...how cool is that!

The Peabody Museum is one of my favorite museums of all time! As an Archaeology student here at Harvard University, the Peabody has been an amazing resource for my studies and interests. The staff is incredibly friendly and helpful, and the exhibits are amazing and wondrous.

The money was worth it since we got so much from our visit. Next time I may check out the two art museums as well. Parking was close and free, which was a nice bonus. Since Main Street isn't far, there are plenty of restaurants nearby but nothing to eat inside the museums

Also, from the outside as well, the basketball museum is shaped in the form of a round circle like a basketball. It certainly stands out as you drive along the road towards the parking lot. The museum is named after the founder of professional basketball, James Naismith.

It's a must stop for gun enthusiasts if you are in Springfield, Ma. It's free admission. Great historical museum. Gift shop reasonably priced. You get welcomed by the staff. There is a 15 minute film you can watch regarding the history of Springfield armory.

On a coolish, but sunny April Sunday afternoon, there were still people enjoying this great place despite in not yet being open for the season.Great place to have a cook out and spend quality time with family and friends. Safe for kids and families!

Absolutely Beautiful and peaceful park we didn't pull in to set up til after 9:00 pm and it was already quiet.If tent camping we would suggest using one of the regular sites instead of the three for tents .All 3 positioned as walk in and up on a hill with a small evened area for a tent .Kinda gravely in areas and hard to stake tent down. Bathrooms are within short walking distance .There are two separate playgrounds one with just a swing set setup and another with little more . Seems to be a very popular place for fishing .Does have at least one gender neutral / family bathroom. Stamps were located outside office for book

Wonderful experience.No we didn't see any breaching or spectacular behavior.But we are there to see the whales in there natural habitat and cape ann whale watch did its best to fulfill its promise.Tried there best to inform and teach the passengers on the boat about the whale behavior being witnessed.Also saw porpoises and other sea life .The ride out to the whales can be just as enjoyable with the coastline and surrounding scenery including the tuna boats hard at work.I very much so plan on making a return visit to Gloucester and Cape Ann whale watch.

Number 1 first thing to do find the self guided walking tour PDF online before arriving.The 1 page map found in parking area telling you what the numbered posts represent do not do this place justice .The PDF does.It will tell you to go 20 paces north and so on to get to the next site .There was a clear trail most of the way we had trouble finding vesper hill .Be ready to spend an afternoon.It is very eye opening and mind boggling to realize this was all here at that time .

To start off is enter at your own risk seems to be visited by lots of people.But it is very beautiful great photo opportunity bring proper foot wear for walking across rocks and walking through water Unless your two foot tall you will have to bend.We only made it so far back because we didn't have the proper footwear or enough light need little more than a head lamp because there is no natural light further you go back.

Huge state park have to drive to go to the different shores.Definately a better kept park.Has a gift shop saw opens march 26th .Luckily we came across a ranger who could stamp our state park book because there were no stamps located outside and we traveled over 100 miles to visit. Seems to be more geared for water recreation but there are trails to explore and you can take a boat tour .Can also rent pantoon boats.

Huge park lots of trails .Campgrounds set off from parks.Saw sign can earn free badge for helping pick up litter from around park that's cool .Camping area not particularly big and tent sites are gravel.Huge river for water recreation didn't see much for swimming though  . Does have a small playground at the campsite.Has a nature center Definately a place I desire to explore.

Very nice park we met a couple comes every season she showed us the changes from season to season .Small bog with lots and lots of pitcher plants .Well taken care of hiking trails .Think there was one pavilion for picknickers and trash is carry need to definitely do something with the composting toilets get it to compost faster.

You wouldn't know it from the parking area.But when you hike back the views are simply breathtaking.I actually liked it in its own way better than presque isle for its uniqueness.You can hike down to the sandbar via the fisherman trail to get a more level view dO.Definitly worth the hike and visit.

Very nice park lot of trees down from storm damage .Was unable to drive into park .Rim trail was beautiful with lots of photo opportunities. sure more colorful in other seasons. Not sure if stamps are outside office if closed we got this one outside Leonard Harrison outside office

Beautiful campground.Cheaper in off season .Hot showers and the ocean right directly by the campsite.Make sure you keep your stuff up and away from the horses .Soon as I started cooking two showed up and wanted to route through the stuff.

Beautiful large beach especially when the tides are low can walk across to the island.Has views of the twin lighthouses.Shows great views of the surrounding coastline and large houses.Seems a popular place for paddle boarders and surfers.

Very interesting park.Hard to believe so much stood there when you walk the path and read the signs of what stood there.The millions made and lost. It teaches you some wonderful history.Definately recommend.Lot to see and learn here.

Small but significant park. Lots of info provided .knowlegable and very helpful staff at visitor center has a large diarama upstairs gift shop below. Has a driveable audio tour although a lot of the audio boxes on site do not work .

Well taken care of park.Afraid of heights but long as stay inward not to bad a walk out. Staff was extremely friendly told us about the other parks in the area.Nice little interactive set up downstairs
Nice selection in gift shop.

Cool little park has a forgotten cemetary way up in the woods on one of the trails .There is a waterfall but haven't seen much water on it last two times I was there I'd recommend good walking shoes for the trails .

Very nice state park.Going through a major clean up up right now due to flooding and major damage from the gorge. But they are still trying to do there best to make it accessible to the general public
Beautiful state park with views of the mountains.Probably a very popular state park in the fall.We got our book stamped in the campgrounds by the park ranger because the main office was closed
Very nice stAte park.Campgrounds are well kept .Was filled to capacity when we stayed.It is well taken care off . Has a concession stand .The park rangers are very polite and helpful.
Didn't actually make it in think this is where most of the horses are didn't bring enough cash to be able pay the entrance fee next time will be brinking bike because its free
Up to date more modernized park.Seems very popular with the locals as it should be. Has a beach it's very unfortunate they were unable find someone run concessions this yr.

We went to Rockport entrance saw butternut falls close to parking area. Can tell rail trail is used by many. Clean park everyone was just out enjoying the weather
.
Alot of the buildings were closed while we there due to covid.But you can still learn alot from what was available.Definately worth a return visit when open .
Didn't make it in time to visit actual museum will have to return but went on guided tour .Was very interesting will definitely be back to visit museum
I think more care goes into Greenwood furnace couple miles down the road.Little more could be done here but still a very nice park to visit .
Not a lot of parking at visitors center .But the staff are extremely friendly and helpful .Lots of trails and great views.

A gorgeous place. Hiking even the red trail was only moderately difficult. The rocks make the trail unsteady and footing loose. Overall there are about 5 different trails that vary in length and difficulty. Well worth the trip. Very clean. Most of the wood stairs and walkways were new. So it looked great. The walkways can be narrow at times. So be careful at peak times. Bugs are somewhat of a problem but it's hiking just use bug spray with Deet.  It overall took 2.5 hrs on the hard red trail. That is with breaks and pics. There isn't much supervision when you go on the trail but do be careful because the falls can be trechorous if you go off the trails. A little expensive about 16 Dollars but for the cleanliness and nice wooden walkways. It is worth it. Beautiful falls.

Best razor/dune buggy riding ever!  No guides. Just you and the machine in the logandale trail. You can go at your own pace.  Stop when you want. Take pics when you want.  See lots of different terrain sand dunes, hills, gravel, mud. Excellent variety. Emergency service always a button press away if needed. Jill is the best person ever. Fully explained everything and really made the experience personal and unforgettable. Great time. Just remember to either rent a car to ride to the location or have some kind of transport back to Vegas. Uber and Lyft do not serve that area very often to go back to Vegas.

Lots of fun. Needs a snack bar. Our axe captain split the teams waaaay uneven. We crushed the other team. Paul...Bunyan. Smaller groups of 6 should have their own lane or have the option to pay a bit more for private lane at least on less busy days.   Minimum group is 8. Super clean and new. Parking lot is small. Need numbers of local delivery places and discount when ordering. Axe throwing gets you hungry. Offer 2 liter drinks if you start offering more food options

I wouldn't say it's bad but the fall splendor foliage ride was very underwhelming. The trees that are on the route are like saplings and they had very few leaves. The service is good. The price of snacks is decent. The open air car is very nice. But fall splendor this is not. It's mostly made up of thin saplings, rocks on 1 side, and a fair amount of houses. Would not do again for fall splendor.
dislikes: Presence of houses along the route

reviews_attraction.text: Great place to spend the afternoon. Only a couple hrs and you seen the whole place. Not huge to spend a whole day. Need more interactive/feeding exhibits. People would pay mad money to feed these animals. Parking is pretty easy and they are still renovating. So it should be real good when it's all done

Beautiful park. Lots to see and do. They do have a large lot under construction but it does not affect the majority of the park. Looks to be an expansion. Lots of trees so can be buggy but overall pretty nice pavilion for picnics and big multiple playgrounds for kids of different age groups

The rides require separate adult tickets if your kid is below 36 inches I believe. Maybe 40 inches. Just FYI. The riverrink is roller skating during the warm months. And ice skating when it's colder. It's sort of a carnival atmosphere but they serve beer and food too.
dislikes: Separate tickets for adults with small children

reviews_attraction.text: Great place for kids under 10.  It really is for younger crowd try Hershey for teens.  Lots to do lots of rides. Lots of shows. Relatively clean. Not alot of shade. Can get roasted. Food expensive but normal for amusement park. Staff very nice. Parking is pricy too.

A beautiful art installation. It is small and during inclimate weather you won't be able to see the outdoor portion. So plan accordingly. Otherwise parking is on the street or in a garage. The mosaic art is very nice and a great piece of Philadelphia PA history

It's a good place to spend a couple hours. It's huge. But not really that much to do. It is clean and the food is good. The staff is also very nice and accommodating.  Parking is on the street and is ample on off days. There is a parking lot on the side too.

It's a nice place to spend an hour. There are board games, free telescopes, nice views. But there isn't like a walkout bridge or anything to take "floating" pics. Gift shop is absurdly overpriced. 70 for a hoodie. What a joke.

Very nice park. Playground kinda small. Couple benches to sit and nice field. There are some ATVs and dirt bikes riding in the area so can be smelly it noisy. But they usually steer clear of the playground area. Creek nearby.
dislikes: Noisy and smelly due to ATVs and dirt bikes

reviews_attraction.text: Very cool.  Lots to see if you are into that. My kid was super scared. Interesting specimens. Bigger than it looks. Can be all done in about 1.5 hrs. Very nice staff. Used a Groupon to visit. Clean. Didn't stink.

Much nicer than before. The steps and sidewalks are flatter and not dilapidated. I went for Christmas village and it was such a joy to walk through. When it's all completed it will be great to have near city hall
I remembered it being bigger but overall very nice place. Fairly expensive to enter but can spend 2+ hours easy. Kids will like it as will adults. Lots to walk and see. Clean and service was good
Beautiful Attraction. Runs very frequently. There is no bad spot to watch the fountains. The shows are varied and different ones run on the same day. If you can watch it at night it very lovely
Beautiful park. Pretty well maintained. Nice water areas. No alcohol so don't even try it. Like 50 signs forbidding it. If you get caught it's a fine and ejection from park. Keep it clean.
Very nice park playground. Lots to see and do. Kind of congested in it's layout. Lots of corners so be careful running around. There is a nearby basketball court and skate park.
Beautiful park. Right at City Hall. Some bums but police presence is good here. Parking lot underground is best street parking if you are bold. Hold lots of events here.
likes: Facilities & Services: Police presence, Underground parking

reviews_attraction.text: It's not that expensive. Around 30 bucks to get in. Parking is expensive. 20 bucks. But can be extremely crowded. Do not go on a weekend or major break or holiday
Small. But a beautiful place. Maintained well. Koi fish to feed. Lots of beautiful scenery. Like transported to Japan pretty. Especially with cherry blossoms.
It's a nice place. Beautiful cherry blossoms when in season. Shofusu Japanese house is pretty too. But small. If u want a picnic this place works
Really beautiful playground. Lots of stations for kids to play on. Parking is plentiful and it's clean. Bathrooms clean too
Beautiful grounds. Excellently maintained. The foot is the cafe is ok but the price for it is fine dining. Very overpriced
Nice park. Baseball on one side and two playgrounds on the other. Bathrooms are available but did not see inside.

I have been visiting since I was a kid. Either I played on the playground, explored the rocks at low tide looking for life forms, ate at picnics, rode my bike or swam in the beach 🏖️ next to the park, though I always found it to rocky (Yo Adrian!). I even partied there as a teenager.
I've bought my kids here for walks and the playground, which is closed right now, bummer!! My daughter made a beeline for it and I had to tell her "Sorry, it's closed."
Fee is low for getting in, but, you have to do it online. You can combine a trip to the Seacoast Science Center and parking admission. I've had no problems with phone reception at the park.
Park is huge, long trails and sidewalks. Boat launch is in a separate area. Old forts are at the park as well. Very little litter. Bicycles welcome, pets aren't. Great place for kids. Nice ocean 🌊 views. Bathroom was in decent shape.
I recommend a visit.
Update: Saturday afternoon, November 2020;  Returned for a hike and to see if Christina Levitan's review of places inside the park were what I remembered. They were. The 155 Gun mounts, the bunker and ammunition storage bunker have their own spot on Google Maps. If you explore the entire park, you will come across them.
Even with the cold and Fall foilage almost gone, the park is popular and charging admission.  The playground is still closed, but, kids were playing on the equipment while wearing facemasks. Can't the playground be reopened? People are being cautious.
Trails to explore and rocks to climb! Great views all around!
⛵ Boat launch area charges admission and you have to reserve online.
likes: Historical sites (Old forts, gun mounts, bunkers)
dislikes: Online reservation requirement (for entry and boat launch)

reviews_attraction.text:
If you enjoy 🎨 artwork, history and exploring, I will recommend this museum 🖼️.
The current exhibitions include modern and contemporary. Artifacts and artwork from medieval times and exhibits from South America, Europe and the Mid East.
Two exhibits, one 🕐 being advertised by WCRB, are the Japanese kimono 👘 exhibition and the second 🥈, which I didn't know about, exhibition of artwork stolen by the Nazis and slowly being returned to the family of the original owner, Richard Neumann. I am reading the 📖 book "Monument Men" and the second exhibit I find extremely fascinating. I've always been into Japanese artwork, that was what lured mean to this museum.
Lots of information ℹ️ and history posted about the artists, paintings 🖌️, artifacts. It will take awhile to read! I was there for about four hours.
I went outside to the garden and I encountered a bird 🐦 at her nest that let me take pictures. Amazing! Others who walked into the garden I informed about the bird 🐦 and that bush became the most popular spot in the garden.
Facemasks required to enter. Floor is marked with ⬆️ arrows to show which path to travel. Hand 🧤 sanitizer available. Bathrooms were in good shape. Cafe and library are closed 🔒. I became hungry and I was disappointed 😞 there was no where to eat.
Gift shop is restricted to 4 people at a time.
Plenty of 🅿️.

Be prepared for spending a lot of time exploring via walking and climbing narrow stairs. If you have a mobility issue, you may be confined to the outside deck. You may need all day and the next day to explore everything!
The USS Massachusetts is also a museum with two inside levels and three outside decks to explore. Audio and video playing in certain sections. Boy and Girl Scouts preparing for a sleepover. Cafe in mess hall, but, it closed early.
USS Joseph P. Kennedy, destroyer, and Lionfish, submarine,  available for touring. Both were interesting and all the ships made you wonder if sailors had to be a certain height and build to work and live onboard.
The museum didn't avoid the issue of women who worked to help build the ship and how they were treated. Also, the issue of segragation was addressed as well.
Only issues, the Hiddensee,  the Maritime Museum and carousel were closed. Discount for the museum was applied, but, not for the Hiddensee. Cafe closed early. Upper decks were closed on the USS Massachusetts, but, probably for safety reasons.
PT Boat exhibits were interesting, especially the documentary shown that talked about John F. Kennedy's time as captain of a PT boat.
Bathroom next to the entrance needs door lock to the only working stall replaced.
I recommend a visit, but, early in the season.
dislikes: Early closure of facilities (cafe, some exhibits)

reviews_attraction.text:
Don't blink or you might miss the parking area. It is marked with a hand made sign. Bathroom available at parking area. Two trails available. The trail that connects to the mill from the parking area is also circular. The second trail leads from the mill along the river, but, becomes overgrown with brush. The second trail is easy to moderate. I would recommend a sturdy stroller.  Be careful when walking your 🐕 dog for there are thorns, even at the parking area. The mill is closed up. It may be more interesting to observe in early spring time when water levels are higher. Nice views along the trails. I wouldn't recommend mountain biking or cross country skiing. Lake reminds me of Friday the 13th. I saw a falcon, chipmunk 🐿️, small dragonflies and something bob at the surface. 🐟 ing is popular here, though, some kids were saying the fish kept taking the bait off the hook. Picnic table available. Only issue, litter! I picked up two shopping bags full of trash left by people who fished. Also, an abandoned stroller. Leave a place in better condition than how you find it.
No entrance fees. If you want a nice place to take a walk, relax or go fishing 🎣, I recommend a visit.
dislikes: Limited activities (not suitable for mountain biking or cross country skiing)

reviews_attraction.text:
I have been about four or five times and it has improved each time. I went one time when the center tank leaked and they had the sharks where the penguins are now. So, I have seen the changes. I enjoyed the rays/shark touch tank. My davughter was nervous when the rays congrigated around her hand. They didn't bite. She was more interested in the touch screens, especially when she could spell her name in bubbles. The shark display room is ok. Only small sharks in a few aquariums.
When the octopus is awake is it interesting. What a showoff. The middle tank is interesting. Sometimes, the fish, turtles or shark will watch you. Their is another touch tank with starfish, crabs and other creatures I can't spell. Other smaller tanks are interesting but there is always a crowd of people in front of it.
My daughter had an okay time. I think her being short and so many people took away from her experience. But, she loved looking at the penguins. I think she liked the seals
Place is a bit pricey and parking expensive. I went through Get Your Guide to bypass the lines. I still would recommend a visit.

I used to bring my kids here when they were much younger. The multilevels and interactive displays they really seem to enjoy. They loved the noise walls where they can just slap paddles and produce sounds. My son really enjoyed the small cubicle they had upstairs where he could just sit quietly and play with the toys.
I haven't been for a while. My kids got older and they don't seem to enjoy it as much. They still have every first Sunday an event open to for special needs children which they can visit for free.
I did the Jingle Bell Express with my daughter. We got to ride in a double-decker bus. We went to the Cochecho Country Club and we listened to a quick story of the Polar Express. We had an opportunity to have our photo taken with Santa with donuts and refreshment were served. My daughter got a little gift, a silver bell.
The staff were very friendly. They did a great job with the special needs children.
Children's Museum is geared for more younger children. Teenagers might have not as much fun as small children or toddlers. I still would recommend a visit.

A quiet place which fascinated me because I remember a number of these telephones while I was, basically aging. I especially remember the Mickey mouse telephone.
I visited years ago with my son. He wasn't very interested  and I really didn't get a chance to read all the information with the displays. Groupon had a discount ticket for sale, so I thought I would visit again. I'm glad I did.
You can download the app and have a self guided tour. Staff was very friendly and Wi-Fi worked well. They had a bathroom which was clean and accessible for people with wheelchairs or mobility issues. Interactive displays were shut down due to covid-19. They even had displays where you would need your QR reader to access more information. They had displays showing the contributions of African Americans to the telephone industry.
They currently have a small display about the railroad history around Warner.
If you enjoy history and nostalgia, I would recommend a visit. Very young children may not be interested in this. Face mask required to enter building.
dislikes: Limited appeal for very young children

reviews_attraction.text:
I have not been inside for a full tour in about a decade. We only checked out the freebies while waiting on the 🦆 ⛵: The animal care center, there were a lot of bugs and a turtle, the windmill with rolling balls and the bathroom. Men's room was in good condition. They still have the IMAX. I saw a documentary on Mt. Everest and it made me dizzy. I remember enjoying the exibits. They have added a butterfly exibit. I will visit again. Parking garage next to center.
Update, January 2019; I took my daughter and she wanted to get through it quickly, until we got close to leaving. Typical. Parking was easy, with outlets available for hybrid cars. Parking prices reasonable for Boston. The museum is geared to younger children. Informative and interactive displays. Nice view of the Charles River. The butterfly exhibit was short and not a lot of butterflies. Pretty garden. Other interesting insects on display. You will need time to interact with the exhibts and to see other parts of the museum. Food court available.

I loved it!! I enjoyed seeing all the animals and exhibits I could see! I wasn't able to see all of the animals and exhibits or try the tree top adventure, but, I had fun!
The gorilla exhibit was the best. Seeing and interacting with them was great! Seeing the young silverbacks act up was funny.
The monorail was relaxing and informative. My favorite view was the elephant. The conductor was pleasant and kept security a priority.
A few animals came close. A 🦒, monkeys and even a few 🐦 s checked us out. A few 🦚 were walking around with people. There were 🐿️ s that were unafraid. ALVIN!
The butterfly exhibit was interesting, but, the Butterfly Place in Westboro, Massachusetts was the best!
The food courts were pricy, but food was decent. Dippin' Dots had several locations.
Bathrooms were a little beaten on but okay.
Bring water and sunscreen!
I am thinking of going again!

I used to visit at least once a week in the summers of my younger days to go swimming and mountain 🏔️ biking. I later brought my kids a few times to swim. I had a friend who lived on Bennett RD. and I would park and ride my bike to the falls. There isn't a real waterfall. It is part of the Lamprey River and it is a popular swimming 🥽 and 🎣 fishing area. Popular with families. The chance of encountering a Lamprey eel is slim. They are further upstream and hang out in the shallows. Better fishing 🎣 further down river. I have encountered 🐢 turtles, though not the snapping kind. They do live and nest along the river. I've even seen beavers, but, at night.
I visited today and there was a young guy sitting in a yoga position meditating in the freezing 🥶 cold.
Parking is limited.  The early summer is the best time to visit when the water levels are at the highest.

I've been twice, once with my son and now with my family.  You can explore everywhere in under an hour. There are rooms that make your voice boom. My son liked those rooms. The fort is three levels. The observation deck is closed. There are picnic tables and an outhouse. Nice views of the ocean 🌊 and lighthouse. You can bring your pet, including your 🐐 goats. You might even see a sailboat after it encountered Bruce the 🦈 Shark! Bring a quarter for the view finder. It's the honer system for payment at the entrance. Different prices for ages, average is $3 for Maine residents and $4 for non-resident. (I paid for everyone:). Parking can be limited. Depends on timing.
I recommend a visit if you want a relaxing time or outdoor lunch.

I had a good time, so did my daughter. I think it is bigger than the indoor water park in North Conway. They had a individual family changing room. Plenty of lifeguards who were paying attention. I did not get a chance to try all the slides, ones I did were fun. Lagoon was crowded with kids pushing into you. Bottleneck at entrance/exit of lagoon. Water was warm. Felt cold walking around. Could not be helped. Lockers are small. Try not to bring much. I believe they provide towels. Showers have body wash. Handicap accessible for lagoon. Same price as North Conway. Tried to call ahead of time but only got automated message. North Conway has a wave pool, CoCo does not.

Seeing how sailors worked and lived in such a crampt space, you can feel a little overwhelmed in such a tiny area. You have to be mentally fit and prepared for it. Then, even without visiting the memorials to those who lost their lives in submarine disasters, the feeling of dred imagining being trapped when the submarine your on fails hits you. Marvelling at the sailors who traveled in such tight spaces, listening to the audio narration inside and outside of the Albacore, the museum itself, makes me want to visit again.
If you have claustrophobia, DON'T go! Disabled people will not be able to get through. If you are tall or big, you may struggle.

I visited last week with my daughter and I found it relaxing. About less than twenty people there. Kayakers where there. Perfect for launching small kayaks and canoes. Small trail by the river. River is deeper thanks to the recent rains we have had. Ball field only had a dad with his sons hitting the baseball around. Since schools are shut down, games are not going to be played. My daughter and I had fun tossing a few stones into the stream. We didn't explore all of the park.
For quiet short excursion, small boats and playing baseball, for a small group, I recommend a visit, especially with the stream having more water flow.

I've always enjoyed the walk here. Well maintained. Not to long, not to short. Scenic all seasons. Ducks hang out in the pond. Great place for a picnic, if people would pick up after themselves:(  Public bathrooms available, not outhouses. The bathrooms are a little beat up but useable. Playground active with children. Manchester public pool next door.
Update: June, 2020; Still an enjoyable walk! Listening to birds, seeing chipmunks and a family of ducks, people fishing and on their canoes. Moderately busy. Picked up, but, trash cans were overflowing.
Bathrooms were closed.

What a view! To see so much of Boston and to learn the history of the city. You can use a phone with recordings that explains an event or part of the city while looking out the window. Museums, displays, and interactive boards set up along the walls for you to learn more about Boston. The person at the front ,who I paid to get,  in was very friendly and helpful. My daughter wasn't as much into it as I was.
Only issue, it can get very warm there on a bright sunny day. Try not to overdress while you're there.
I recommend a visit!

We have been there three times and have had a good time. We only went snow tubing but there is plenty of room for skiing and snowboarding. It is difficult to tell the employees from the customers. Our recent visit, there appeared to be no supervision of snow tubing. People on the bottom nearly got hit by people coming down. The staff on the conveyor were helpful. The snow tubes can be heavy on the conveyor with the hard plastic bottom. Please be aware of this if you have little children.

Friendly staff and I wanted to stay and explore longer! Imagining how sailors worked and lived on such a ship, without getting lost, made the experience more enjoyable. Multiple levels and decks. Not accessible for wheelchairs or walkers. Narrow stairs. Bathroom available onboard. I had fun and I recommend a visit!
If you bring kids, watch them! They can get lost easily and you may want to give them instructions ahead of time in case they do.
1 Coke machine on board.

I remember walking the trails and sledding here when I was a kid, long before the tornado nearly destroyed the park and killed a small group of people.
The park looks better and is well maintained. I haven't had a chance to walk the trails, but, the play area for kids and the covered picnic table area are great additions. The Stratam Hill Fair is nice.
I'm glad it has reopened!

Nice eighteen mile 🚆 ride along Lake Winnipesaukee. Turkey lunch, supplied by Hart's Turkey Farm, with trimmings served, along with coffee. Friendly staff. Comfortable seats. Trains in good condition. Only issue, bring window squeegees. The tray that the food was served on steamed up the windows and you could not see out of! Bathroom available on train.

I'm looking for places to bring my kids that might interest them. My son has handled animals and the touch tank has animals either in a container at or animals near the surface. There are smaller thanks with 🐟 that are colorful or active. A few interactive displays. Small gift shop. Friendly staff. Seats to sit and view the ocean.

Park in good shape. Long lines for rides and slides. I buy season passes during Black Friday. Wave pool usually crowded. Food a little pricey and usually a wait. After four you can park for free.  $5 for all day parking. Minus the crowds, you can have a good time.

A very well maintained park, playground, soccer and baseball fields and parking lot. Very scenic. Kensington is a very nice town to drive through. Pleasant short walk on paved walkways. Well groomed lawns. I recommend a visit or picnic. Parking is free.

Closed due to bald eagle 🦅 nesting. Confusing! "No parking" sign when there is a sign at the beginning of the street saying parking for the trail. Abandoned couch in possible parking area.
When the trail reopens, maybe it will be a better walk.

Nice fall foliage that you can see. Nice view of the lake. Clean white sand that borders the lake. I would like to check this place out in the summer. Boat launch, picking tables and restrooms available.

I had some time to kill between when I arrived and the rest of my party arrived at the Burlington, VT airport. I looked for something local to do. The Ethan Allen Homestead was only 20 minutes from the airport.

This tour was one of the best tours that I had been on in a while.  My tour guide - Bob - sat me down inside the theater/remake of a tavern in the visitor center. He gave me about 25 minutes worth of history on Ethan Allen. It was really detailed.  I'm a history major and I was impressed.

Then he took me over to the Ethan Allen Homestead and proceeded to go through each of the rooms and describe the items found there and how they were used during Allen's time.  The building and the grounds were in impeccable shape.  Bob was very knowledgeable and answered questions thoroughly.

A great family outing.  Nice gift shop and artifacts to view.

I have been going to this park since I was 14 years old and a Boy Scout in Bucks County and Montgomery County.   That was 44 years ago, very little has changed.  There is plenty of space at this park to hike, fish, kayak, and camp. If you bring your bicycles along to our plenty of good roads that are flat and not heavily trafficked. There’s a playground here, 20 some campsites with a main shower building. There is also a swimming pool and a large pavilion for picnic usage.  The high rocks are close by if you are a climber, but if not there are several nice trails to get to from the campground to hide rocks. The red shale that is all around makes for a nice trails.  Very photographic location. There are even several cabins and lodges to rent close to the water and the pool.  Lots of deer in the evening.

Awesome place.  Very well cared for.  COVID ready and practicing.  Checkout the video and learn from the knowledgeable and super kind docent staff.  You’ll love the feel of the place if you dig historic sites and landmarks.  The whole area comes alive in its historic setting when you are in a place like this.  The staff make that happen as does the feel of the house.  It feels like you would see wooden frigates out the window when you look to the waters!  Definite must see. AND FREE!!!  Great art on display as well.

Another sensational Havre De Grace museum.  This one is so well organized, clean and laid-out that it only adds to the wonderful collection they have to exhibit.  From early Native American inhabitants to the nautical history of the area, these well designed exhibits do justice to their themes.  The readings placed with the exhibits are not too lengthy and they are helpful.  The artifacts are in excellent condition as well.  A really good thing to do in the town.  Very cheap.

This was a superb museum.  Excellent renderings of culture, history, and milestones on the isle.  Clean, well displayed and adequately marked.  Personal and collective in nature at once.  Hard to find well documented local lore and history like this.  Worth stopping to see - rain or shine.

Oh, and I almost forgot, Misty is here.  Yes, the stuffed Misty is "in the house".  So, it's a gotta see
for your young pony lovers - all the books are available on site, too.

Loved the great hike out to the lighthouse.  The grounds are well kept and the structures are in unbelievable shape - maintained well.  The view is spectacular and gives you a great sense of the enormity of the Chesapeake Bay and a sliver of what it must have been like to have been a keeper.  You can just imagine the storms and sunsets seen from this promontory.  Take the time to hike to the Turkey Point Lighthouse.  Well worth it.

Completely AWESOME Park.  Tons of opportunities throughout the huge venue.  Camping is great here - and so are all of the other opportunities.
This place has been around a long time and used by families, groups, and individuals successfully down through the years.  Trails are lush and travel along water if you set out from the park office - The Shades of Death Trail.  Would be tough in rain as a lot of roots and rocks underfoot.

This is a great little spot where you can fish the Brodhead Creek. There’s a little pavilion with a 14 foot picnic table.  The area is large enough for maybe a half a dozen fisherman up and down the stream. Easy to get to, very peaceful and tranquil, has wild trout in it and not stocked trout, and you really don’t have to wade in order to fish, but you can.  It is at the confluence of the Brodhead Creek and the Stony Run Creek.

I am so glad that they have updated the museum on the park grounds. Such a noble and ominous event in the history of our country was embarked upon from these very shores. It is so nice to see an exhibit that exemplifies and amplifies the magnanimity of the historic Crossing.  The presence of this historic offering ennobles the American soul.  Do not come to this area without stopping here, your Patriot heart depends on it.

Very well maintained grounds and buildings with an historic appeal, but also an historic feel to the place.  The buildings are in exceptional shape.
