The museum and store are chocked full of great details.  The guided tour was out of this world - informative and flexible.  All of the staff were unbelievably kind and helpful.  Definitely stop in when in Ephrata.  Very responsible entrance fee.

Superior trail in the Poconos.  Close enough to Route 80 for people to approach directly.  20 minutes from Route 80 exit in Bushkill.  Public Beach, trails, rentable bikes.  Cash for entry fee and bikes.  Locals can by an annual pass for $45.00 (2018).  Flat trail and easy on the feet.  Over 30 miles available one way!  Bring bug repellant.  Runs aling the Delaware River.

This spot is exceptionally still and quiet.  Love walking the space here and taking in the breathtaking glory of the sanctuary.  The sanctuary sponsors artist in residency programs here in addition to being a space to find tranquility and ease.  Great place to shoot photos and walk with family and friends.  Be sure to check it out when in the area.

Great spot for walking and relaxing.  Also a fine spot for flyfishing.  Beautiful place, well kept, clean, and well patrolled.  I love going here cause it is accessible, plenty of parking, and has tables to have lunch after a few hours of fishing.  Don’t miss this spot if you flyfish or love to walk.  Great for dog owners, too.

We saw a friend’s painting exhibition here. The space is wonderful, clean, well cared for, and extremely well lighted. Everything you need in a gallery.  The staff were warm and friendly. The opening reception was exquisite!  The space added to the fine art we came to see.  The outside is well kept also; beautiful gardens.

I love this park, not just for it's exceptional access to the trout waters of the Brodhead Creek, but for its beauty, trails, and picnic area.  It is a great location year round and is peppered with some fine flowering trees in the picnic grove in spring.  Always a breeze along the water so bring a sweater or sweatshirt.

Love this spot along the Brodhead.  The walk and the environs are peaceful and quiet.  Bald eagles in the trees, and trout in the Brodhead Creek. What more could you ask for?  A new building is going up and should be a great asset on this local preserved open-space.  Catch and release year round on the waters.

Great park for day use or camping.  Plenty of trails, boating, fishing, and fields for a ball game.  There are a full range of camping options from, tenting, cabins, and RV hookups.  Great store in town - about a mile away- that has about all you need plus camping and fishing gear!  Bears.

Wonderfully kept and inviting museum.  Detailed explanations of the clear and accessible exhibits.  Two current art shows available on separate floors in a portion of the museum.  Very knowledgeable and hospitable attendant at the front desk.  Very kind and personable, as well.

We found this little gem while looking for a place to swim in the Delaware River - close to home.  A superb find.  The swimming is good - plenty of beach to lay out.  Ample picnic areas.  Space to set up tarps and games.  Picnic tables available.  Clean bathrooms.

We’ve been here any number of times. I love the beach here, and driving through the park to see the ponies. Excellent hiking trails. Everything is in wonderful condition and it’s nice to be in a park that has no trash. I like the discovery Center and Bookstore.

A quaint little home in sensational condition.  It was not open, but you could get ample interior views from the windows.  A real lesson for children of the way homes looked and were constructed in an earlier period of our history.  A must see on the island.

Great place to hike, fish, grill and picnic, or just come and sit. If you’re in the Blakesley area stop here to get some fresh Pocono air.  Also, soak in the music of one of our exceptional streams. Her singing will open your heart.  You could stay all day.

We loved the State Park.  It was clean, well marked, and accessible.  We made several forays onto trails here and they were worth the trip.  We boarded a friends boat easily at the pier.  Make it a part of your trip.  The lighthouse is awesome as well.

Very clean and well groomed community park.  We stopped here with crabs and corn from just down the road at Captain Chris's Crab Shack.  Friendly guests, plenty of space and trash receptacles.  Nice place to visit with your kids and family.
Great park for fishing.  Plenty of access to the stream.  Special access pond for kids and handicapped fisher folk.  Nice picnic areas.

The ICA only has a small permanent collection, and the total gallery space is only really one floor of a building whose total floor space is less than either or the more major art museums in Boston (the Gardner museum and of course the MFA). Given that, the $20 admission probably won't be "4/5 as good" as admission to either of the only slightly more expensive museums. That said, some of the rotating art has been spectacular (not all of it, but it's "contemporary" and time hasn't had it's sway as to whether certain things should be remembered or noted and then left for history). The ICA also really is an "institute" with event space and some room for classes and the like. As a whole package, it's probably worth making sure the rotating exhibit appeals before dropping the cash (and the cost of transportation) but if the current line up seems interesting, it is a good enough museum to be worth killing a few hours enjoying.

There is some green space nearby, and of course it's on the ocean, so the aesthetic can be nice - the area is a strange mix of parking lots and construction mixed with shops filled with clothes and trinkets that most of us can't even afford to think about. That makes it a weird place for a date, too rich for most people but too mixed for the target audience. Also, despite sprawling lots on two sides, if you can avoid parking, you'll save yourself a good amount of money. Plan your trip accordingly.
dislikes: High admission cost relative to value

reviews_attraction.text: There's nothing in particular wrong with the Seattle children's museum, it's just boring. Even within the area, Imagine Children's Museum stands out with a massive floor plan, a phenomenal water play area, and an entire roof space playground, the children's museum in Bellevue has a climbing structure and better programs, and even the pay-what-you-will Tacoma children's museum hasbetter place basis, better water tables, and a cool interactive sculptural play structure. SCM has... a small ball elevator and a "hiking path". There's almost nothing here for toddlers, some imaginative play that you probably could imagine in your own home, and some okay school activities, but it is the weakest of the area's Children's museums, and does little to inspire new and interesting curiosity, does not tie in well with the region, and varies between sparse and overly complicated for the main audience AKA children below school age. If you're looking for a high-value experience for children at Seattle center, the Pacific Science center has a large toddler area, and a broad array of items to inspire curiosity and play and a wide range of ages.

As a member of the MIT Community (note that I do not work for the museum or sponsor it) I get in for free, which is a pretty great price. Still, when I took my father, I wasn't disappointed with the cost, and there are some really incredible exhibits. My personal favorites are the holograms (because they are great! I want one for my house) and the kinetic sculptures. While some of the exhibits rotate, the MIT museum is most like an art museum, so if you enjoy that kind of thing, you'll probably do well. Their schedule includes interactive events, mostly aimed at youth, but otherwise the museum is not so much like the Museum of Science or similar museums, or like natural history museums (the Harvard museum is really the best in that last category). I don't think I would drive to Cambridge from outside the metro area for the MIT museum, but it's certainly worth a stop if it falls in line with your existing travel plans.
dislikes: Not as engaging for non-local visitors
Limited to art and less on science/natural history

reviews_attraction.text:
The staff at this small museum are great, but the commitment to always rotating galleries and the floor plan make the space feel both small and under utilized as compared to similar sized galleries in the area. Notably, the third floor was closed for installation while I was there and I am sure this dramatically reduced the feel of the size of the space, but the same was true at the Henry when I visited and the space still seemed full and well utilized.

If you enjoy art museums, you will still still enjoy the BAM, and they seem to have a fairly good set of events to supplement their space. It's probably worth planning about 2 hours to see (depending on your read speed), and seems comprable to an average college/university art museum in terms of size and subject matter.

With the newly rebuilt big ocean tank, the many smaller exhibits, and the ray touch tank, this is a great 'smaller aquarium' (as opposed to, for example, Mystic, with a much larger footprint but no single thing as special as the big ocean tank). NEA also has a clear conservation mission, putting it above other animal exhibits in the area where the conservation mission may be less clear. The facility is also well kept, and the staff are generally friendly and knowledgeable. It would be great if the aquarium were open an hour later on weekdays, as trying to get from school to downtown and actually have time to see anything is a challenge and makes the annual membership somewhat less worth while.

My 3 year old and I spent more than three hours here and only saw half of it. He had a great time and was very entertained. There are many great, hands on, 'displays' here (exhibits isn't really the right word either, as the focus is on interaction and discovery). It isn't the Exploratorium, but it certainly aspires to be, and does a great job of facilitating hands on play and, of course, discovery. The staff were overall very friendly and pleasant (I did have one negative interaction with a staff member in the wood working area, but I think it was a misunderstanding). Overall, I hope to be back and I think anyone in driving distance should make an effort to check it out!

Magnuson is a massive and diverse park on the shore of Lake Washington. It houses a hanger sized event space, an active community center a massive dog off-leash area (including dog beach) a boat launch, human beach, hiking trails, playground, several small nonprofits (the park used to be a military base) and NOAA (okay, if we are being honest NOAA is just adjacent, but you can check in during certain hours and have a nice stroll through the art on the campus). If you like parks, are looking for interesting events or a good place to host a small or moderate event, or just are looking for a good place to let kids or dogs run around, be sure to check this park out.

The Otis House is a nicely preserved bit of New England history, and the tour guides (at least on "First Night", when we went) were knowledgeable and moved at a good pace. Having said that, it is just a house, and only really remarkable by virtue of it's age and the work put into maintaining it as an exhibit of colonial life. This is best taken in with the other small downtown historical sites like the old state house, and the granary burial ground, but the few extra minutes to walk over to it from these locations are probably worth while.
dislikes: Requires additional effort to visit (walking from other sites)

reviews_attraction.text: Okay, first off, park: 5 stars, parking: 3 stars. If you can get here without driving, especially near the community center, you will save some heartache. The park itself is very fully featured, but generally quite used and fairly developed. If you want quiet solitude or amazing views, this probably is not the place. But for canoeing, running, walking, biking, playground, classes, swimming (seasonal in the lake) and a popular but not completely bonkers wading area.

This is a great local children's museum. Though the floor area is fairly small, there are some good activities, a nice climbing structure and a pretty good water play room. There is a free lot, though it's a little small. All in all, a great place if you live in or around Bellevue and have younger children (any kid below teenage will probably find something to enjoy).

Great spot to go with the family! This spot manages to be both accessable and a little bit wild, so that you can drive right up but also sometimes see seals and often see  ducks, and other birds, and it has enough green space to feel like it isn't backed right up to the city. It does get pretty busy on nicer days and weekends though.

In addition to being a nice bit of history, it provides a place to stop and sit off the main sidewalks and therefor out of the bussle of the area. Don't expect a park though - you're in the wrong part of town to have anything but back to back shops and resaurants anywhere that isn't designated as a historic landmark.

Boston's largest park, it includes some great playgrounds and green spaces, but also old creepy bear cages that are unsafe and were supposed to have been taken down to stone a decade ago. In general, the park is nice, but it isn't as well maintained as parks in Boston's more white and gentrified neighborhoods.

This neighborhood park has some great soccer/baseball space, a good skate structure, a nice wading pool during the summer decent play equipment for younger kids and a restroom. The kids equipment has some ware on it and the southeast portion of the field has some pretty significant drainage issues.

This is an amazing and well cared for area. We went up for the annual swing dance and lawn party, and it's well worth a modest ticket price to see and wander around this property. Truly a beauty... but expect to be stuck in traffic for Crane Beach for an hour if you come on a nice day.

Franklin park is a nice size park that, despite the city's obvious inattention in places, contains a lot of beauty and history. The old homestead ruins have some interesting stonework, and the landscaping of the overlook provides a nice place to observe or to find a quiet space.

This is one of the few high traffic parts of Boston that manages to be regularly beautiful, trash free, and reasonably friendly. A good mix of shade trees and gardens break up the flow of open grass found in the adjoining commons and makes this area pleasant year round.

This is a nice art museum with some unique features. It's not the MFA, and certainly not The Met, but it is a decent sized museum with some interesting collections and worth the trip for any local or semi-local art buff.

Harvard's art is an endearing mishmash. While not as consistently architecturally pretty as Yale, the campus has a large amount of beauty and historical significance squirreled away into pockets throughout the campus.

$5 Parking, no dogs (they can't even wait for you in your vehicle), but hundreds of people walking around a... well a pond. Not exactly true to the vision that made this location famous in the first place.

The new contemporary art wing is nice, and the collection is reasonably extensive for a mid-size city art museum. The several eateries are decent though prices are high (as you would probably expect).
The tours here look cute (didn't take one, but was here on my own and overheard a minute or two of one) and there's a lot of history to be had in a compact space. Best of all, no trash on the ground!
It's a nice little area for festivals or a relaxing afternoon. The rose gardens are great, but it can be a little hard to get through on wheels (there are ramps, but sometimes you have to backtrack).
This park is an extensive green space with bike path and several playgrounds through JP. I've taken a few long walks covering the entire distance, which makes for a long and fairly pleasant trip.
The locks are fun and busy, the museum is small but informative, and it's cool to he able to actually see the fish ladder.

Massive green grounds, which is a perfect place to relax, let the kids burn off energy or take in some 1600s history. It's easy to see why Reader's Digest named it the Best Picnic Place in Michigan, with a beautiful view of the Straits of Mackinac, and nearby islands. It's also surrounded by historic building.

A statue of Jesuit Priest Jacques Marquette stands prominently in the middle. Marquette preached to the Straits area Native Americans beginning in 1671, from a Birch Bark Chapel, recreated at the west side of the park. That brought fur traders, making it the most important French western fur trading place. It also has a peace garden to explore.

The area that is now Marquette Park was known as the garden for soldiers at Fort Mackinac, built in 1780, which stands above it on the highest hill on the island.

Great place for #ToursAroundMichigan groups to rest and take in the moment in a beautiful place. #HistoryTours #GroupTours #CustomizedExperiences #GreatLakes #NativeAmericanHistory #Religion #LakeHuron #ChurchTours

A great place to experience history and to actually see what's happening today watching the trucks being built. My Great-grandfather William J. Smith was overnight supervisor at #RiverRouge and worked with Henry Ford. He even built a one-of-a-kind 1930 Ford Private Bus that was a 4-wheel drive. My dad now owns it and takes it to car shows including Greenfield Village Old Car Show. (See Facebook page "1930 Ford 4WD Model A")

I recently visited #RiverRouge with a #DiscoveryMichigan customized group experience from Brazil. They loved it!

#HistoryTour #EduTours #AutoHistory #PoliticalHistory #CustomizedTours  #VisitDetroit (See Discovery Michigan Facebook page for pics.)

Truly standing out on its own in the Straits of Mackinac is the 1895 Round Island Lighthouse. It was built for $15,000 by Frank Rounds, who also helped build the Grand Hotel on Mackinac Island. It's stood through fierce Great Lakes storms, winds and dangerous ice. It became automated in 1924, and deactivated in 1947. You can easily see it on the ferry running to Mackinac Island, and also in the movie Somewhere In Time, shot mostly on Mackinac Island in 1979.

#GreatLakes #ToursAroundMichigan #ExperienceLife #LakeHuron #StraitsOfMackinac #LighthouseTours #CustomizedExperiences #GroupTours

Founded in 1854, Grand Rapids Public Museum is Michigan's oldest museum. Permanent exhibits include Native Americans, industry (Furniture City history), and my favorite, Old Grand Rapids, where you can walk through the city in the early 1900s. Take a seat on a bike that requires a bit step up. The museum also has the Roger Chaffee Planetarium, named after the Grand Rapids astronaut who died during a training exercise. We circle the 1928 Carousel as we listen to the Grand River flow under us during our #ToursAroundMichigan tours! #HistoryTour #GroipTour #CotyTour #CulturalTours

Gerald R. Ford was not only a great President, but a great man who sacrificed himself for his country. I love talking about him during my #ToursAroundMichigan city and political history tours. Very few people realize who he truly was and they're always very impressed once they learn more. Betty Ford was one of the most popular first ladies we've ever had. Much of her popularity was due to her openness about her own struggles and her fight for equal rights. It's always an honor to take people to visit their final resting places during a tour.

The Lowell Area Historical Museum preserves Lowell area history, including Native Americans and how the river helped residents. It is inside the Graham Building, built in 1873, and used as a residential duplex for a family. The building now houses Victorian rooms, early Lowell history, businesses and industries, and decades of the Lowell Showboat. It's listed on the National Register of Historic Places. If you love history, check out #ToursAroundMichigan tours and experiences. #HistoryTour #LowellTour #ArchitectureTour #DiscoveryMichigan

This has always been my favorite beach to bring my children. I recently brought a family here considering moving to Michigan. Through my company Tours Around Michigan, we spent the day exploring the Muskegon area, including this great family beach, ranked #9 Best in Michigan. We stop by the Gillette Visitor Center, then to the beach and dunes. They loved it like I knew they would. I've always loved it here because the kids can spend hours playing in the water, sand and dunes! What a magical place!

I love local history.  The museum focuses on Berrien County and has five buildings used for exhibits and programs. It has special attention toward Native Americans,  lake resorts, rural schools, Lake Michigan shipwrecks, daily life and businesses like Watervliet Paper Mill. The Nicols-Beverly Barn has lumbering and agricultural history including how area went from forest to fruit farms. If you love history,  check out #DiscoveryMichigan tours and experiences!
This place opened in 1992.

This museum is housed in a former county poorhouse built around 1884. It has three floors of historical items and exhibits, including a one-room school, general store, music room, old-fashioned kitchen, turn of the century parlor, old dentist office and military room. There is also a replica log cabin and blacksmith works on the grounds. It's open June-September. There is a charge to get in. If you love history, check out #DiscoveryMichigan tours and experiences! #HistoryTour

I love history and often structure my travels around visiting new historical locations. The History Center is the oldest surviving county government complex in the Midwest. Visitors can self-tour the 1839 Berrien Co Courthouse, an 1830 log house, an 1870 sheriff's residence and jail plaza, and a working forge. The center also had extensive archive collections. If you love history, check out #DiscoveryMichigan tours and experiences!

Great museum with 90 exhibits. You can get a quick look, but can spend hours there if you want. It's a deep dive into the companies that made Muskegon from decades ago to now. Ask them to run the Brunswick bowling pin resetter. It's cool. Fantastic stop for people from the area or from out of town. Staff is fantastic.

Will share with my #ToursAroundMichigan #GroupTours #CustomizedTours #PrivateTours #HistoryTours #LakeshoreTour

This 1934 United State Coast Guard station in Ludington just reopened in 2017. It's been a landmark on the city's waterfront for decades. The museum has family friendly, interactive exhibits, and a captivating look at the rich maritime heritage of Ludington and the greater West Michigan region. If you love history, check out #DiscoveryMichigan tours and experiences! #LakeshoreTour #HistoryTour

This is a standard stop on my  #DiscoveryMichigan #WineTours - a one day group excursion from #GrandRapids to #TraverseCity and back. Now I can add it to my #CiderTours also. The staff has always been helpful. The owners are down to earth and work hard to create a welcoming atmosphere. Todd Oosterhouse gave me a wonderful tour, including the science behind the wines. Fascinating!

Love the bridge that goes from the northside of the Grand River, hops on an island and lands on the Southside in another part. Great addition to the park. If you cross over, go to the new North Grand River Riverside Park with ice cream and historic fur traders cabin.

Potential great stop for #ToursAroundMichigan #HistoryTour #IceCreamTour #RiversideTour and #NatureTour

When this pier and lighthouse officially opened January 1905, it was a big deal. Unfortunately, the ship captains did NOT know the lighthouse had been relocated north. When the ships came in that night, captains were really confused. Luckily, they knew the port well enough not to crash.

#ToursAroundMichigan #HistoryTour #LakeshoreTour #DiscoveryMichigan

A good future stop on my  #DiscoveryMichigan #DistilleryTours - a one day group excursion from #GrandRapids to #TraverseCity and back. Extremely knowledgable place that loves the science of making distilled spirits. You'll find products here that are extremely rare. Plus a library to read up on the process. Worth the trip! #PureMichigan

A good future stop on my  #DiscoveryMichigan #WineTours - a one day group excursion from #GrandRapids to #TraverseCity and back. Traverse City and the state of Michigan have great options and it's a joy to help people experience what we have to offer. The staff was extremely friendly and informed. The view by the narrow is lovely.

Beautiful stop on my #DiscoveryMichigan tours in Muskegon State Park. It's the highest point in Muskegon County. This is a recreation of the 1930s original, which burned to the ground in 1962. The original was build part of President Roosevelt's New Deal in the CCC - Civilian Conservation Corps.

This amazing collection of historic items has potential for many of my #DiscoveryMichigan customized group experiences #HistoryTour #MusicTour #EduTours #CulturalTours #AutoHistory #AfricanAmericanHistory #CustomizedTours  #VisitDetroit (See Discovery Michigan Facebook page for pics.)

Small town history museum in one of the first settlements in the area. It includes Rix Robinson homestead rock out front. Robinson is considered the first white resident of West Michigan. Great stories to share on #ToursAroundMichigan #HistoryTours

#GroupTour #CustomizedTour

The Eyaawing Museum has a nice display at Turtle Creek Casino off US-31 between Traverse City and Elk Rapids. It's on an upper level of the casino in the walkway between the hotel and casino. It's a great thing to share on a #DiscoveryMichigan #CasinoTour or #CulturalTour

This beautiful cathedral also has a great history. It's a perfect place to include on my #DiscoveryMichigan #ChurchTour. This 1875 church went through major renovations in 1901 after a fire nearly destroyed it. I've attached pics. Take our tour to learn more.

A good future stop on my  #DiscoveryMichigan #WineTours - a one day group excursion from #GrandRapids to #TraverseCity and back. The staff is helpful and friendly. The view is astonishing, like you're on top of the world. The building gorgeous! #EduTours

This is a great way to share a unique ecosystem on my #DiscoveryMichigan #NatureTours. The dunes are a version of nature found almost no where else. Learn what makes the dunes change and people almost destroyed them. #CustomizedTours #PureMichigan

I'm working with #VisitMuskegon to bring more #DiscoveryMichigan group experiences and tours to Muskegon. The historic Union Station is well preserved and has a lot great items to check out beyond the incredibly cool building.

Great grassy park right by the Delaware river, with historical marker and statue indicating the location of the great elm tree under which William Penn signed the treaty with the Indians. He treated the natives fairly and respected their rights. Some descendants of the great elm are still at the park

Great fishing pier and fish hatchery. The trail is short, and there is a place where there used to be a swimming beach. With the Delaware River cleanup, it would be nice to reopen the beach. Also the Delaware River trail should get connected to this park

Wonderful walking trails and the huge Council Rock, along with a footbridge and covered bridge. Also there's access to the Pennypack Trail. The Pennypack Rail Trail goes right through the park and continues to the Pennypack reserve and beyond

I enjoyed walking on the abandoned railroad line and bridge - the original part for the Trenton Cutoff.  Next time will walk as far as possible in the park and on the old rail line.  I hope they can turn it into a rail trail.

I discovered this place by driving along the beach at Newport. The trails are great and there is a volunteer at the visitors center named Norm who has lots of stories as well as historical and geographical perspectives

Great historic bridge from the 1920s. There is a wide path on the side for bicycles and pedestrians, with spectacular views. You can also cross by train, with commuter PATCO trains to Cherry Hill and beyond
I love the walking trails in the park. Next time I want to get to that covered bridge.  Actually got to the Schofield Ford covered bridge twice already - it's beautiful, and in a very scenic setting.
This is a beautiful park with several pavilions and playgrounds, numerous hiking trails including much of the Wissahickon Green Ribbon Trail, and access to the Wissahickon Creek in many locations
This is a great historic place.  The buildings are from colonial times and from the early days of our nation.  It's tucked away behind the airport, but seems centuries away.
Great miniature golf course with Philadelphia landmarks. The fountain is beautiful and the landscaping is pretty. There are special events like Chinese Lantern Festival
I love walking around this place. There are benches, streams, dirt paths, and a variety of vegetation. It's close to my Prudential office and to Staples Willow Grove
Great Waterfront promenade on the Roundout Creek in historic Roundout neighborhood of Kingston, with lots of boats, bridge views, and nice restaurants and shops.
Great museum with art and prints by Norman Rockwell. I enjoyed the original studio from Stockbridge that was moved here and maintained the way Norman had it
Convenient for travel to and from New Jersey. You can take the Betsy instead of the Ben Franklin to avoid congestion in Camden and central Philadelphia
Great maze of trails on the plateau, with panoramic views of center city. Too many bikes on narrow dirt trails make it sometimes dangerous for hikers.
Nice venue for concerts, and a good place to sit and enjoy the river breeze, looking over into New Jersey. There are lots of historic markers, too
A nice place for walking in the woods with a cool pond. They need to maintain the trails, since fallen trees block the path in several places.
Great house museum where the famous writer once lived. The basement is suitably spooky, and the bare rooms fit in well with Poe's personality
There are great walking paths and it will soon be connected to the extended Pennypack Trail along the old train line to Newtown
Really cool waterfalls up a narrow path. The trail to the biggest waterfall was closed when I went. Not commercialized at all
I enjoyed visiting this place, looking at the Lehigh River and the old railroad bridges, and climbing up to Glen Onoko Falls
I love walking in this park. It also has memories of the founder of the Curtis Publishing Co and the Saturday Evening Post
Great views and walking trails. If you have the time you should take the full red trail and see as much as possible
A great bridge structure built in 1929 but still very solid. The toll is a little cheaper than the Betsy Ross
A very special place showing the poor lodgings and potato crops of the Irish who were emigrating to the US

A Michigan treasure.  The wildlife was scarce due to the time of year and the time of day (mid afternoon in July).  I went seeking Loons and saw them but they were out of range of my lens.  I did see a Caspian Tern tho' as well as Sandhill Cranes, Swans, and many other critters.  This is a great place to view wildlife as the roads wind through the many ponds and you can stop when you feel the need for photos, a picnic or just to enjoy the area.  I travelled 8 hours one way just to be here.

Trails are well marked and nicely groomed.  I took the 'River Loop' and it follows the Chippewa River along the upper banks with paths down to the water for closer views.  There were people enjoying the river in Canoes, Floating on tubes and swimming all along the path.  The Wildwood path goes thru' a Red Pine forest for a different look at the area.  A really nicely done County park...

Nice place for deep woods hiking but the signage is really bad.  They have occasional arrows but no trail names or other way of identifying where you are.  It's easy to go around in circles.  In places the 'single file' trail can get quite slippery if wet due to clay soil.  Many small brooks and the trail does have wooden walkways in some of the real bad areas.

A Bird Sanctuary, I came at the wrong time.  Saw one Robin only.  However, this is a really nice place for a walk and pictures.  The trail winds around a marsh with woodlots and grasslands along the way too.  To be fair, I only came here at this time of year (early April) because I was going stir-crazy at home due to the Virus.  Nope, I'm clean.

Beautiful LH with the surrounding dunes adding to the uniqueness and the long hike adding to the flavor.  The area is available for those who want the 'lighthouse experience' in 2 week blocks to maintain the site.  However, the person I talked to said that she mostly 'reads'.

Make sure you get a map of the trails.  The intersection signs have names and the maps numbers for the trails.  A nice variety of ecosystems along the many trails, with 'Swamp Overlooks' and boardwalks over the wet areas.  I came seeking Lady Slippers and found one.  Yay.

Small but important Wetlands as it was created to filter street rainwater runoff by providing a series of cascading ponds that allow settling of solids.  The area flows over limestone raising the pH and is used to irrigate a nearby golf course.

The mostly hard packed sand trails winds its way up the Dune in the Cedar Forest with small creeks meandering through to the overlook of Pyramid Point, and both Manitou Islands.  The hike back down is a blast...not too steep and quick.

I've hiked all over Michigan and this is one of the worst for trail ID.  You approach the trailhead and there are 3 choices all unmarked, left, straight and right.  Zero maps, zero intersection markers, zero me a second time.

Swan, Geese and Mallard, with the occasional visitor.  They ffed the waterfowl, and they have become dependent on the feedings, which is not good.  They must have lost some funding because it was much nicer in the past.

I hope the fishing is good here because the photography stinks unless you like tall Grasses, Geese and a half dozen or so Swans.  The site looks like it has not been taken care of for some time either.  I won't be back.

No sign (I drove past the site 3 times), gated, and the one mowed trail ends at a picnic area (with no picnic stuff).  This place may be discontinued as it had the look of a neighbor's yard.  Don't go.  Nothing to see.

Great for photography.  I was there in April which was a bit too early for a lot of the WF's however, I went to find a 'Trailing Arbutus' and found 2.  Also a couple of Hepatica.  I will be back in May for more....

Trails have maps at each intersection so all you have to do ts decide how far you want to go, and go.  Variety of habitats from wetlands to upland forest.  Distance is far enough for a good workout but not overly.

Really nice area with a variety of habitats and choice of trails which have maps at each intersection.  I was a little early for the Wildflowers but this preserve has the potential to have many species.
Like a mini Rosy Mounds area with trails into and over the dunes.  Just a short trip to the overlooks tho' with anything below that off limits due to Dune erosion prevention.
Really nice place and I'll be back when the main color scheme is not brown.  A variety of trails and each intersection has a map so the hikes can be planned.
Nice place for varied lengths of hikes, some near ponds and some near woods and fields.  Well marked but get map if there are any (none when I was there).
The Park needs maintenance.  There is a huge tire on the beach and trash in the culvert near the bridge ruining any pictures that might be taken...
The best view for pictures is from the Breakwater at the Presque Isle harbor docks.  The LH is just a short walk up the path from the parking.
Very well laid out and maintained gardens.  The whole place can be seen in about 2 hours depending on how many pictures you take.
Nice place, just  not for photographs.  The trails are well marked and not difficult but it's best to leave the camera at home.
Easy to get to and very rewarding.  This LH is typical of the style of many in Michigan but it is a good one.
Bring your telephoto lens, a small a simple structure out on the pier.  Saw Swans and Geese in the pond.
Not a well known place to view the Bridge and you'll learn some history of the Great Lakes too !

We got here a little after 4. The zoo staff was a little hesitant to let us pay to get in just because it takes a while to really walk around and enjoy everything. We wanted to take the wagon ride since you can see everything that way but the park closes at 5pm everyday it is open. We were not staying in town except for two days so this was the only day we had and we couldn't get to town any sooner due to work so we worked with what we had. We ended up paying the 13.50 per person to get in and bought some giraffe crackers (3 crackers per cup and we got 2 cups). This was the best part - feeding the giraffes. I had never done that before and I love to feed animals. We opted not to pet them since they pulled back at bit and I don't like to force the animals to let me pet them. We took a bunch of pictures. We got to see some lions, lemurs, leopards, hyenas, cougar, sloth, monkeys, lynx, zebras, wallaby, tigers, gibbons, peacocks were just walking around free as well as some other birds that I did not recognize, camels, wildebeest/water buffalo?, barnyard animals like goats, chickens, calf, etc. We did not get to see all of these animals but we saw at least half. Part of them you could only really see with the wagon ride and part of them were in their little shaded areas where we really couldn't get a good view. I don't blame them at all as it was super hot out. They do have animal encounters that you can pay for and I would have loved to do that but since we weren't even sure we were going to be able to make it to the zoo I didn't want to spend a couple hundred and not be able to experience the encounter. We will probably never be back in this area again but if we are we definitely would try to work our schedule to take the wagon ride and schedule an animal encounter to be able to pet and hold different animals because that would be absolutely awesome. Do those if you have the time and money for the encounter!!! It was super hot out and we were sweating all over but it was worth the 50 minutes to walk around the parts of the zoo that we had time for and were allowed to (part of it is only available to the people who take the wagon ride and we missed that by about 5 to 10 minutes of our arrival. My boyfriend also went back to get some feed for me to feed the goats, calf, and little deer looking animals too. I have always really liked goats. I have milked one before and fed them by the bottle before too. The little goats are really awesome to be around. We took a look into the reptile area (not my favorite area) and we were about 1/4 of the way in the door when one of the zoo staff was actually going into the main room to get one of the snakes because it had escaped. It was just trying to hide. That was a bit of a shock but I didn't feel my life being threatened or anything. She just picked it up and put it on her shoulder and brought it back into the room where it belonged so it could get fed. The serval was really walking along side of the fence and several of the other animals actually walked up to the fence and looked at us about 30% of them I would say. I thought that worked out well since it was so hot out and they didn't really need to do that for us. Anyway, there was one of the deer looking animals that followed me along the fence. I assume you can feed them and that is what they were wanting but I didn't see any food nearby to get to feed them. Maybe that is at the front desk to ask about. If I ever go back I will have to get a lot of feed for all of them!!! The giraffes and goats were my favorite out of everything. Not being able to access everything by walking was the least favorite part of this zoo for me. They also have ice cream, a gift shop, places to eat inside, etc. You should spend at least 1.5 to 2 hours here to enjoy everything (their recommendation when we were buying tickets) even if you do not do a special animal encounter.
likes: On-site amenities (ice cream, gift shop, places to eat)

reviews_attraction.text:
We had a good time here even though it was small. We enjoy all the zoos, aquariums, and animal parks that we have visited.

They offer elephant rides for $10 bucks. It is written on the chalkboard in the gift shop in the admission area about the elephant rides, that they don’t take credit cards at the elephant stand, times the rides are available (12pm – 3pm when we visited), etc. All the info you should want about the park on times and prices should be available at the admission desk and around it. Just ask if you have any questions. She was helpful and friendly to us.

We got to do some interactions with the animals. We don’t get to do as many interactions in the big cities with animals at zoos, etc. The little baby pygmy goats are the cutest but I loved feeding all the goats that came to the fence. We fed some of the deer. The budgies were not interested in our food. It is a small aviary and they must have been already full since it was about 12pm and there just wasn’t that many of them. They would look at you from afar. A few people got them to eat but majority did not get any takers. We left our sticks in the bag near the ones where you pay so someone could have them for free. We got to see several of the animals at the zoo eat like the chickens, lemurs, turtles, monkeys, camels, etc. The zoo had food laying out for all of these animals. Some of the food did not look fresh as it already had ants on it but I am not sure the animals really cared. We did not see shading for all of the animals but I am not sure they needed it. We got some videos of half of the animals moving around, and jumping from branches, etc. Some of the animals were just sleeping like the bears or hiding like half of the lemurs, baboon, etc. It was a hot day so I can’t blame them!

The admission line was really slow and gets backed up. There was only one person working on a busy holiday weekend. The admission/ticket desk is right in the gift shop and that is where you enter the zoo as well. Our hand got stamped so we could leave and reenter the park which was great because we forgot some things. The entrance is right next to the admission desk. The prices for adults, children, etc. is right above the desk so you can see how much it is to get in. Very easy to see. Also, when you get up to the desk there is a sheet of the prices of the multi-pass/combo ticket so you can buy to save some money for the zoo + caverns + dinosaur kingdom (right across the street). The prices for the feed and budgie sticks are up there too. We bought some feed (a large bag) and the budgie sticks we got like 6 of them. We did not see an advertisement on where to get the carrots to feed the giraffes but make sure you get them at the front desk when you buy tickets because apparently that is where people got them when we saw people walking around the park with them. Don’t forget if you want to do that!

There are restrooms but they are only inside the park. One set of restrooms is right near the gift shop and the other is near the reptiles but you will see it on your map inside the middle of the animals (no air conditioning in this bathroom). However, the map does not have all of the animals that are at the zoo. You really need to walk around the zoo, go down all the paths, and the unpaved paths because we did our own thing before we even looked at the map and got to see several more animals than was mentioned on the map.

The gift shop is two rooms and there are several things to buy just like any animal gift shop which includes cups, mugs, shirts, sweatshirts, umbrellas, stuffed animals, rocks, pencils, etc. Also, there is an aquarium in there and you can see the lemurs because they have a big glass window right there in the gift shop and they have food outside of that window so the lemurs will likely come up and eat the food and you can see them up close.

Friendly staff.
dislikes: Lack of shading for some animals

reviews_attraction.text:
180 acres!!!!!!

Safari Drive-Thru: was a bust for us. There were not a lot of animals walking around. The safari park did not have nearly as many animals as Lazy 5 Ranch in NC. The upside to this is they did not have goats in the drive-thru part. At Lazy 5 Ranch the goats really scratched up our doors. At Virginia Safari Park, the animals were not really coming up to the vehicle much, they were actually skiddish of the vehicle 95% of them, and they did not seem interested in the food much at all unless you tossed it on the ground and even then some of them just ran away. I only got to actually feed one emu and he/she only took like 4 pellets of food then it walked away. We were there around 3pm on July 4th weekend. It kind of alarmed me at how scared they were of the vehicles/food. Also, after the drive-thru part is done you are supposed to throw out the food in the big bin they have. However, you can go back through as many times as you want. We opted to go to the village walk-thru instead of going back through since we kind of glanced over and people weren’t having much more success than we did when we went through and the weather was cloudy and going to rain so wanted to maximize our time. We noticed throughout the drive that several of the animals were far back into the woods hunkered down resting and the rest of the animals that were not near the roads were in the big pond across from the exit area either in the water or lying around the water.

Village Walk-Thru: We loved this part of the safari park. We got to interact/feed animals which we enjoy. There are oodles of budgie’s in there so you are bound to have multiple on you and wanting food like we did. They had some other type of birds in there two – it was a pair and I fed them each a stick and then after that they actually flew to me later on and landed on the rope right next to me and looked at me so I fed them some more – I thought that was very cool/cute. They had a kangaroo walk-about where you could walk along a wire. It was very hot and the kangaroos were just lying around under the shade though. Go in the morning; if you can. There was a petting zoo area with the goats, etc. I always love feeding the goats. There is an ATM near the goat station so you can get quarters. It takes 50 cents (quarters only) to get a few balls of goat food. I liked this even though you do not get a lot of food. I liked it because I got to hold the little food ball in my fingers and hand fed the goat like that by just placing it gently near its mouth and it took it. You can feed the giraffes if they are at the giraffe feeding station. The lettuce was 5 bucks for a leaf and you got to keep the Virginia safari park plastic cup. We got to feed the pheasants in their own aviary with ducks and some other birds. We got the meal worms and pellets from the giraffe feeding station for 3 bucks. In the walk-thru they have other animals like anteaters, penguins, turtles, cheetahs, wolves, etc.

Other details: They do have wagon tours that you can take but costs extra (on top of the regular $25 per adult admission price). The park is very hilly so beware when you are planning on going to the drive-thru and to the village. There are two bathrooms on the grounds. The gift shop is a good size and has your usual items like magnets, cups, shirts, rocks, collector pennies, mugs, pencils, stuffed animals, toys, bags, food, drinks, etc. The guide book is really awesome. They have pictures of everything you see in the safari park drive thru and there is a map of the village walk thru park and where everything is at.

The staff was friendly.
dislikes: Lack of animal interest in food (Safari Drive-Thru)

reviews_attraction.text: Great place for history buffs to learn about the American flag, Star-Spangled Banner, the war of 1812, Fort McHenry, etc. We got a chance to participate in the Ranger's Choice Talk (4:15pm) which was on the American Flag, etc. We held the American flag with over 20 other people while the ranger talked and at the end she asked questions (a quiz) on what she talked about and every question we got right we got to roll up a stripe on the flag. We also got to see the Evening Flag Change - Star Fort event which was at 5:00pm in the fort. The fort itself wasn't huge to me especially for over 1,000 men but they have removed a lot of the buildings that were once on the entire property (as you will see when you go into one of the buildings in the fort and see the old picture of the property). My boyfriend really loved this place because of the history. He loves history. I loved walking around and I enjoyed the views of the city and other scenic views right by the waterfront and in the fort at the top. The price to get in to the actual Fort McHenry grounds for us since we did not fall into any of the discounts was $15 each. They have other events that you can take part in / watch such as morning flag change, other flag talks, battle of Baltimore talk, etc. The first one starts at 10am. The fort and visitor center actually close at 5:45pm, just be aware. The fort and grounds are extremely well-kept and clean except for some bird mess but you can't control that. There is a gift shop that you can get into for free that has a ton of American and Fort themed gifts including postcards, pens, shirts, pencils, figurines, tokens, etc. There is a museum that is free to get into that is right across from the gift shop. The bathrooms in the visitor center (not any once you enter the fort grounds so make sure you plan accordingly unless you are going to make a trip all the way back to the visitor center) are very clean and several stalls, all the soap, etc. are fully stocked. There is a water fountain and also a water bottle refill station. There is plenty of parking and it is free. They have a Star-Spangled Banner National Historic trail that you can walk/hike, run, or ride your bike on that is over 200 miles. We walked on part of that that is inside of the fort/national monument/shrine. There is a monument of the General (Armistead) who led Fort McHenry during the war. His monument is outside of the fort grounds so you do not need to pay to see the monument or take a picture of it. Go here to Fort McHenry if you love history or want to visit a huge attraction in Baltimore.

We really enjoyed going to the ranch. This was our first time driving into a drive-thru zoo. We drove through with our own vehicle and that may have been a mistake but we were too late to get on a wagon ride and could not go back another day due to the short trip to this town. On our way into the Lazy 5 Ranch we saw a bunch of animals and roaming around but only a donkey came up to our vehicle. We parked after that and went into the shop to buy tickets to go through the ranch and bought feed to throw out. The ranch has over 700 animals. The property is very pretty soo and rustic. It is a 3.5 mile trail to drive. Some of the animals include: cattle, zebras, sheep, goats, deer, giraffes, buffalo, etc.

There was a paper we got when we paid for tickets and it said the animals may autograph your vehicle and several did actually "autograph". I had told my husband before we went here that it may be a possibility. When we left we had several scratches on the doors of the driver and passenger door. If you don't want to take this risk, I highly recommend you make sure you plan your visit around getting a wagon ride. I would suggest you call up ahead of time and get a spot or ask how you can secure it.

You are allowed to honk your horn to try to get the animals to move out of the way. The goats, emus, and ostritches were the ones that really didn't want to move much. I was weary of the emus/ostritches as I had been warned it may not feel good if they hit your hands when trying to eat from the bucket so I kept my window up for them and was weary since it was my first time with this kind of experience. The speed limit is only 5mph.

We really enjoyed driving around and seeing the animals roaming free and feeding them. The little goats and deer were the cutest.

After we got done with the drive through part we actually went to the walk around area and saw more animals and fed some of the goats. I love feeding the goats. Goats are one of my favorites animals at farms and zoos. They have petting areas, a playground, picnic areas, and also a gift shop and snacks at Lazy 5 Ranch. Check out all they have to offer and stay here a few hours to enjoy it all.

It closes 1 hour before sunset so watch your time and don't cut it too short.

It was 11 bucks per adult.

We would definitely go back again if we are in the area again and also would either take the wagon ride this time or put the floor mats on the side of the vehicle to make sure we don't get anymore scratches.

We thought this aquarium was more up and close to fish and other exhibits than other aquariums. They had a touch zone for sting rays. Escalators throughout the building and stair options. The sharks are a big exhibit you go deep down where they are and their tank is all around you. This was the highlight of our visit. The jellyfish exhibit was very cool too in the pavilion. We didn't go to the dolphin show because we missed it but they have dolphin exercise shows and dolphin talks- don't miss those. There were multiple staff around the aquarium willing to answer questions, all staff was very friendly. Especially the young lady on the main floor - she talked about how they train the sharks to not eat the other fish, etc. and fold us about some of the history of the aquarium about one of the octopuses. We thought it was cool going up and down the levels of the aquariums seeing the big tank area and looking down into the bottom part of the aquarium with the big stingrays, huge (and I mean huge sea turtle), small sharks, and other fish. The most memorable were seeing the sharks, jellies, giant octopus (very active during our visit) and dolphins. There were plenty of bathrooms and fountains throughout the aquarium. Lots of walking.  We did try out the cafe and I liked the brownie, chocolate pudding with crushed wafer crackers, mixed berry granola parfait and brisk tea were delicious. I would get all those food/drink options again. It was almost 40 dollars per adult, non member. If we had waited till after 5pm we would have got half price admission but we didn’t want to wait and hour to get in. There are plenty of parking around inner harbor with all the parking garages but you are going to have to pay for it and walk a ways. We parked in a big parking garage that was a national aquarium validation participant so you'll see that outside the parking garages that participate in that for the aquarium. Ours had at least 7 floors and it since it was one that the aquarium validated we saved $10 bucks. Overall, we really liked this aquarium and wouldn’t mind going back again but would probably plan our trip so we can go after 5pm since it is very expensive.

This really is a beautiful place to go as far as the landscapes. I don't like part of the history here but it is what it is and none of us can change that. It isn't a good feeling hearing about the slavery back then. I enjoyed going to this place for the scenic views. You weren't allowed to take pictures on the inside of the house - not exactly sure why. We got to go on the first floor and actually some down below since there was bad weather. We saw Jefferson's bedroom which was unique to say the least. When we first walked into the house I wasn't expecting how it looks I was expecting something more grandeur but it just wasn't in the entrance way. The There were animal antlers, European/Indian looking stuff on the wall, etc. We enjoyed the walk outside - grounds, pond, garden/slavery tours, etc. They have little exhibits where they brought up the wine in the wine cellar, the iron they used to use, some history downstairs under the main house of sally and other slaves and people from back in the day. All of the tour staff were very knowledgeable. The visitor center staff was friendly. They do have bathrooms near the visitor center and bathrooms near the Jefferson house but they are on the outside of the house so you have to walk around. Near the bathrooms near the house they had demos of some items from back in the day such as you could write with a calligraphy pen. We did that and it was cool to do.

I think this was a unique place to go to given its history. I don't really have any interest in going back but it was good for a one time visit. If you walk everything I think you'll be here for 3 hours or so. There is a shuttle to take you from the visitor center to the Jefferson house. Also, the tours are timed so you get a ticket from the visitor center and then you can get on the shuttle. There is a farm shop gift shop place on the house grounds nearby the restrooms that you may want to check out for some goodies. They have a gift shop near the visitor center too that we checked out before we left. Enjoy your visit! Plenty of pictures of the landscape were the best part.

My boyfriend had researched and saw that this park has the nicest view of Baltimore. It does have the best view of Baltimore (Inner Harbor) so far. From this park we saw the Hard Rock Cafe, museums, restaurants, aquarium, baseball field, the harbor, ships/boats, the volleyball courts right next to the water, etc. It is an awesome place to visit. It is on a big hill. We found parking for free near the park and just parked there and walked around for about 30 minutes. So far it is my favorite place in Baltimore. It feels really relaxing here. It has a ton of trees for perfect shading. We did not see any restrooms though so keep that in mind if you have a picnic here or plan to stay for a while. A lot of people walk their dogs here and play with the dogs with frisbies, etc. It is a very clean park. There is a gated playground (not locked) for children (dogs are not allowed in this portion of the park). There were several people with their dogs and children at the park, couples (one couple was getting professional photos done with the Baltimore background), people alone, runners, walkers, and people just hanging out/sitting on the several benches that are all over the park. There is a monument of US Senator/ mayor of Baltimore/Major General Samuel Smith in this park. This was the first monument I saw while walking around. There is a Memorial statue of George Armistead here as well. He is the officer who served as the commander of Fort McHenry (Baltimore attraction) during the Battle of Baltimore in the War of 1812. Worth checking out this park. We sat on the bench and just relaxed. I loved this park and hope to go back again someday.

Great area for relaxing, pictures, watching the boats, having a meal, or shopping. We came here to sightsee and have a date night. We went to one of the restaurants and then walked to the docks and on Main Street to checkout some stores. There are several local restaurants nearby since you are in historic downtown Annapolis. Several shopping as well nearby. The dock itself has benches to sit on. There are newspaper machines too. Cobblestone walkway creates part of the historic feel but beware you can trip easily since it is not flat/even and some of them are coming up.  There are bathrooms and showers for boaters. They have parking but it can be a bit tight – some of it is free while others are metered. It is very beautiful at the docks. We did not partake in getting the famous ice cream nearby (Storm Brothers) since we were still full from dinner but it is a popular place. We hung out a while just looking at the water. Great area for people watching if you are into that. The Naval Academy is nearby as well if you want to visit that but check the times. I would definitely recommend going to the city dock. It is great if you are by yourself, with friends or family, or a date night.

We stopped here on our way out of town because we love escape rooms and wanted to try one in Raleigh. We preferred to try another business but this one fit into our schedule. There is free 2 hour parking behind the building. It is in a older looking house in Raleigh. We (2 of us) did The Experiment room and did not get out. It had a 30% success rate. The lowest we have tried before. The game master was very friendly and helpful. We have been to several escape rooms in the past 2 years and this place was one of our least favorite rooms ever. We though the room was kind of bare bones. Some of the items we had to use did not measure accurately which already makes the room less fun. There was nothing special or cool about this room. No sound effects, etc. When we got a clue it was written on a piece of paper and slipped under the door after a knock occurred.

We aren't sure if we picked the wrong room to do at this place or if it just wasn't our preference of an escape room because there were no special effects and it was not immersive.

We won't be going back here but we will try another escape room in Raleigh, if we have time when we are in Raleigh again.

We tried out Black Cat Escape Room this weekend and had a blast. It is located in a big huge office building but once you go in the main doors you just go to the right and the business is right there. We didn't think we were in the right place at first. This place is really neatly decorated with time period pieces/antique looking furniture, etc. It is different from all the other escape room businesses we have been to.
We did the Speakeasy room. We had a great game master and owner of the business too was nice and friendly. We got clues when we were stuck. We loved the design and layout of the Speakeasy. We enjoyed the puzzles we had to solve. It is interactive and has surprises. There were 3 levels we could do the room on - beginner, intermediate and advanced. We selected advanced (you tell them when you get there - they will ask) since we have done escape rooms in the past. We got out with about 5:30 minutes left to spare. We will be back at this location to try out their other rooms later this year with more friends. We are excited to have new room experiences!!! Check this place out if you love escape rooms. You won't be disappointed!

This was the #1 park I wanted to visit on our trip to Annapolis. We got here much later than we wanted and only had about 25 minutes before the park closed (8:30pm on a Wednesday in August, closes at dusk) so we just drive around for 15 minutes or so and I got some pictures. We did not have to pay to enter/for parking since the gatehouse was closed. Usually it is $6 to enter the park. This park has some beautiful views and great opportunity for photos. It has several hiking trails, picnic areas, dog park, dog beach, boat launch, boat rental, streams, ponds, compost area, playgrounds, a ton of parking, pavilions, a visitor center/gardens/blue heron center, gazebo, 3 separate restrooms, etc. The park is very clean. We saw some people walking and running at night. The best part about this park is all the deer we saw! We saw over 40 deer (bucks, does, and fawn) randomly driving through the park. I love animals so this was a treat. We would have loved to get here early and walk around. If we are back in Annapolis again in the future, we will spend more time here.

I went in here with friends and my boyfriend after the Luray Caverns. You get a free ticket to visit this place with your Luray Caverns ticket. It is worth going into just because it is free if you don’t like the cars/carriage attraction. Plus there is a fudge store inside this building as well as a gift shop so more opportunities to find gifts for your family, friends, or souvenirs for yourself. The museum itself was very descriptive in separating out the different eras. They had info on each vehicle they had in here. Most of them had the price of the vehicle at the time it was made, horsepower, detailed description about the vehicle, and some of them had extra info. It isn’t a huge museum but it is big enough and has at least 20 or so cars, etc. They had a little area with a military uniform with descriptions for the items as well. My friends loved it because they enjoy anything antique. My rating is based on the layout of the museum, what it offers, and the descriptions. I can imagine all antique/car lovers would love this place.

USS Constellation gift shop/entrance to the ship/museum. They have a pressed penny machine which is I came to the museum/gift shop so I could get the lighthouse penny. I collect these pressed penny souvenirs. We did not tour any of the ships but we did check out the lighthouse ($1 admission). Ships they have are the USCGC Taney, USS Constellation, LV116 Chesapeake, and the USS Torsk. They are located at the Inner Harbor in downtown Baltimore. They are spread between the piers – pier 1, 3, and 5. You can purchase a squadron pass and go to 2 ships or you can get the fleet pass and go to 4 ships. Pricing and other information are located on their website. I had e-mail correspondence with Dayna and she was very helpful with hours of operation for the lighthouse since the hours for it really depend on staffing each day. The female staff member inside of the Historic Ships USS Constellation museum was nice, kind, and friendly. The gift shop had cold drinks as well as souvenirs available like hats, ships, shirts, pens, pencils, etc.

We went up here for a weekend and went on the trails with our 4x4s. The trails were great and well-maintained. Some were hard, some were easy. Some marked easy were actually difficult. The maps we had were not that great for the trails. This was the first off roading experience we had in a National Forest. We went down many of the off roading trails. We found campgrounds, picnic areas, people fishing, groups of jeeps. We even found some people who gave us a better map to use for the trails. Friendly folks on these trails.  We all just wanted to have fun. We parked at the Badin Lake area and had our picnic. We used the facilities there and they were what you would expect for a forest. Some bugs. We used the grill to cook the hamburgers and hot dogs on and it worked perfectly. No issues. Afterwards we took several photos of the lake and surrounding area. It was a ton of fun going here to Uwharrie and I am sure we will be back for more fun and trails in the future!

Great area for having a party at the pavilion. They have a playground right there for kids.  There are tennis courts.  There are port-a-johns available near the pavilion and throughout the park - maybe not as many as it should have though. This park is very open with a ton of space. There is a dog park fenced in area near the pavilion for your furry companions. It is huge with plenty of space for your dogs to run around. They have benches in the fenced in area for you to sit down while your dog just gets a chance to run and play. The park is very secluded away from the city. It is quiet and peaceful here.

$1 cash to visit the lighthouse. We paid the woman that was inside the lighthouse at the counter and then walked around inside. Great views inside of the lighthouse looking outside at the harbor, federal hill park, etc. Stairs to go up to the lighthouse is very sturdy and I felt safe. They have information in the light house about its history, what they used in it, tools, bed, past lighthouse keepers, etc. I had e-mail correspondence with Dayna and she was very helpful with pricing and hours of operation for the lighthouse since the hours for it really depend on staffing each day.

We visited these in Spring 2019 the day before we attended the Duke basketball game. I loved walking around the gardens. Everything is so beautiful. It was relaxing. People were walking, painting, laying around, playing in the open area, reading, talking, etc. The flowers are very pretty. There are several themed areas. There was a little farm area. There is over 5 miles of walkways/paths to walk. If I lived in this area I would visit often. I felt safe and felt super relaxed walking around. Visit the gift shop too! The staff we talked to were all friendly and helpful.

I love this area for the multiple food places and shops as well as the walking around. Good exercise. I agree that there are homeless around here quite a bit and that is why I won't give it 5 stars. Several stores to go to. There is a little of everything here for anyone. Plenty of seating outside if you want to eat out there or just hang out. We saw several people doing both. Some places even have a water bowl outside for dogs. Go and enjoy yourself!

I have went here several times in my lifetime. They have changed it a bit over the years since I was a kid but it is still fun. You can walk around the park, read, fly a kite, bike, bring your kids, have events/parties/picnics, etc. here. They do have plenty of parking and restrooms. It is fun all around but probably more fun if you have kids so you can see them enjoy the playground. Perfect for burning their energy!

We have done multiple rooms here. We love escape rooms and frequent them. We have always had great hosts/game masters at OB-Xscape Rooms. We love that the rooms are interactive, immersive, and they have very cool/interesting stories and decor. We will be back here soon to try out the new rooms they have in 2020. Check it out if you love escape rooms. It is worth it!!!

This free trail is one you can walk/hike, run, or ride your bike on. It is over 250 miles. We walked on part of it since a portion of it is inside of the fort/national monument/shrine. It was a great walk. On it you have beautiful views of Baltimore and the harbor. Worth walking even if you just do some of it. Great exercise and it is a safe area.

We looked up some parks to visit and chose this one based on the pictures for shading while walking and a good sidewalk. When we got to the park there were a ton of homeless people laying around the park and the park itself looked rundown and trashy. We did not stay long at all.

We love going here during the season and off season. We go every year. They have bathrooms here you can use. There are pavilions for picnics, grills you can use, a boat ramp, and the horses tend to frequent this area (but make sure you stay the safe distance).
Nice memorial/sculptures located right by Main Street and the city docks of Annapolis. The location of the memorial is beautiful. Located in the heart of Annapolis.

A huge sprawling park/ reservation, has hiking, bird watching, paved trails, gravel trails, dirt trails, deer trails, beach volleyball, duck ponds, 2 separate wetlands, horseback riding, giant meadow's, a raptor center with live birds, and even an eagle. Additionally, they have large rooms to rent for occasions, and an awesome play room area for children.

Fantastic park! Miles of trails (blacktop, gravel, and dirt), birds of prey (eagle, owls, falcons, worlds largest eagles nest, ect...)mini-zoo, indoor educational play area for kids, indoor bird watching area, attractive meeting areas, big fireplace, maple syrup cabin, and much more!

A really nice park. It's not huge, but it has some really cool stuff. Like a totally awesome water park, and a totally awesome playground, and really nice tennis courts. The locals really get some good use out of this park. The people were very nice, and we're all having a good time.

A very nice park, with a really cool putt-putt golf course.

There's also miles of very nice trails through the very nice woods and wetlands. There's a lake that's overrun with lilly pads too.

That's not all either! There's also a very nice playground, and a snack shack!

Awesome little hidden away park, with really cool access to a really cool part of the river.

There's also has a trail that leads to the falls that Olmsted Falls is named after.

The restrooms are the stuff that nightmares are made of.

Great for kids, good for adults. I was lost in the maze for awhile, and the cave is an actual cave. Mini golf is decent, as is everything else. Gift shop has neat and interesting trinkets, and the restrooms are acceptably clean.

Nice quiet park, with easy access fishing, and a big wooded area with lots of big tall old trees. Great trails and paths to walk, along with nice grassy lawns to picnic or play in. There's restrooms, and a cool pavilion.

A very nice charming park, that is also quite interesting. Lots of people enjoying water. Bathing, kayaking, playing. It was very nice to see so many people enjoying the park in such a relaxing way. Awesome experience.

This place is really great! The roof slides open to expose the large telescopes inside. There are also 2 concrete observation pads outside the building, complete with electrical outlets and calibration markings.

A nice park with 2 lakes, water park, tennis, basketball, horse shoes, fishing, great big playground, lots of trees, fishing, a cool hill, pavilions. In a nice area, close to police station and library.

Not the biggest or best park in the world, but it's plenty good for picnics, cookouts, frisbee, and all kinds of other activities too. Not to mention that it hosts the fireworks celebration each year.
The most dragonflies that you're likely ever to see in your lifetime, in one place. Very rustic and enjoyable to traverse. The paths are narrow so plants are going to touch you.
This is a damn nice park! You fer's should check it out if you haven't yet. If ya fixin' to have some fun then bring yer kin from the holler over yonder with ya too.
Awesome! The place is amazing, if you appreciate and respect the ancient indigenous peoples of this great land. The construction of the mounds is mind blowing.
Probably the nicest park in the city. It has a carousel, a snack shack, a sprawling lawn, and plenty of benches. There's also a stage for events.
A nice park for all kinds of outdoor stuff. I saw people having picnics, and others just lounging enjoying the day. It's a nice place.
The metroparks are great, I love them. This one has a nice path that takes you to a cool bridge, that goes over the Black River.
This paved trail is LONG and INTERESTING! There's so many different landscapes to take in, and the path is well taken care of.
As far as public beaches around here go, this one is great. It's one of my favorites, check out the Virtual Tour I did for it.
The only skiing to be found around here. It's not very big compared to Colorado, and New York, but it will get the job done.
Good for kids and if you have a few extra bucks  to spend to see something quaint. Don't go in expecting something amazing.
It was okay. They had buoys for park decorations. I saw nothing for kids to play on. But it's right by the river, yay.
It's nice here, and there's some cool stuff to look at  I had a great time riding electric scooters here.
A very nice park, with a good beach. Not quite what I was looking for, but it did the trick.
This is a really nice, clean little park. It even has a skate park at the front. I dig it.

This park has so much lost potential.  At one time the park had a well maintained wood chip trail in the original park and a boxwood maze.  The trail is overgrown and half of the boxwoods have died.  The hopscotch game and boccie ball court are in need of maintenance .  The Giant Adirondack Chairs seem to be in good shape.  Under a small pavilion is a slice of a 330+ year old White Ash Tree.  Trees have fallen in the main part of the park and all they have done is mow around the downed trees.

The park has two trail entrances off the back of the park that would be nice if the trails were maintained.  One trail is completely impassable as a down trees have completely blocked the trail.  There are two bridges on the trails but unfortunately someone has intentionally worked on destroying the bridges.  More bridges are needed as some parts of the overgrown trails are completely under water.  The trails need more markers. Some of the markers have been ripped of the trees and dumped on the ground.
On the back end of the property there needs to be an effort to clean up old construction waste.  Since this park is an Arboretum it would be nice if some of the trees are given identification markers.

Work on this park would make a great Eagle Scout Project.

This 27 acre preserve is a marshland that surrounds Darby Creek and itself is surrounded by housing.  This preserve has a lot of unmet potential.  First the bridge that is supposed to cross Darby Creek right near the entrance to the preserve is rotting in the creek.  Other bridges are in disrepair.  Much of the preserve has flooded trail areas that would benefit for either more board walks or cleaver placement of stones.  There are several bridge sections scattered haphazardly by Leopard Road.  There are households who have used this preserve to discard their yard waste especially the neighbors from Hawthorne Place and to the left of the entrance.  One of the Hawthorne Place homeowners has run a hose from their pool across the trail and into a tree in the preserve to drain their pool.  There is a pile of empty beer cans and other trash.
Natural Lands Trust has some really great preserves so don't let this preserve be your guide to their work. According to their webpage Sharp's Woods was their first preserve.  I hopefully they go back and show it some love as this place could use a kiosk with a map of the park, trail markers, replacement of the missing bridge and other trail maintenance.

Mariton is perched on the steep slopes of Bougher Hill overlooking the scenic Delaware River. This preserve has over six miles of trails that are very well marked.   Two highlight of the preserve’s trail system is the River Lookout Trail and the Squeeze Trail.  The River Lookout Trail provides an overlook of both the Delaware Canal and the Delaware River 300 feet below, do be aware that the is a huge drop off the ledge.  The Squeeze Trail provides a great view out to the hills on the New Jersey side of the Delaware River.

This is a great place to bird watch as you may see Wood Thrush, Ovenbird, Black-and-White Warbler, and Red-eyed Vireo.  The preserve is has a test area to see what damage deer are doing to the preserve.
Other animals include living in the preserver include red fox, eastern chipmunk, northern redback salamander, meadow vole, and milk snake.
of this preserve is woodlands dominated by oak, tulip poplar, birch, rhododendron, and tuliptree.  The small meadows with native grasses and wildflowers like milkweed and goldenrod

Mariton’s Wildlife Sanctuary has a Nature Center that includes a library, meeting space, and ADA restrooms,.

This is a small preserve right off of route 252 in Media.  It has an old stone farmhouse that was built in 1806. Natural Lands  built an addition onto the farmhouse and use it as their headquarters.  The property also has a frame bank barn and a springhouse.  Most of the property is open wild grassland. I saw several Eastern Meadowlark take flight on the mowed grass trail on the eastern edge of Hilda's Meadow.  In addition to the numerous birds you can see in the meadow there are many other birds by Crum Creek and in the wetland behind the Office.
