As for deer, I had not even parked before I saw three deer and saw a total of 11 during my time in the Preserve.

Area to improve: The Preserve should increase its trail signs.  Some trails are unmarked but clearly within the Preserve and at others it is unclear if they are withing the Preserve,  private property or part of the Greenbank Farm Park.

Unfortunately this park also has a dog owners who just dumped their dog poop filled bag right on the trail.

A great park 300 acre passive park with working farm,  forest, small pond and Indian Creek.  You begin your visit by driving up an oak and beech tree lined drive.  This land has been in agricultural use since the 1700s and is currently maintained as a demonstration farm to educate visitors.
The property has the mansion that can be rented, gardens, the park office,  education area and bathrooms near the first parking lot.
The lower parking lot gives you easy access to the fenced fields where you can see of Scottish Highlanders, Belted Galloway cattle, mules, sheep and goats outside the restored barn.  There are additional bathrooms in this area.  The lower lot also is where a paved trail that will take you to the pond and fishing deck.  If you follow the road out of the back of the lot (it is closed to traffic) down to Indian Creek you can easily access the Indian Run Trail that runs along the creek and across bridges and around the entire park.
likes: Variety of facilities (mansion, gardens, park office, education area, bathrooms)

reviews_attraction.text:
Great 87 acre hiking park.  The falls are very pretty. I would have given this park a "5" except that the noise from Everett Turnpike was very loud on the eastern part of the park.
The Souhegan River wraps around half of the park from the northwestern side, down the western side to the southeastern edge.  Wildcat Falls is a really nice and should be viewed from lower, middle and upper falls.  Dog beach is below the falls and has a sandy beach area.  I would  choose anyother trail before picking the power line trail as it runs directly under the power lines.
Hiking, biking, horseback riding, and xc skiing are permitted. Swimming is not prohibited but is discouraged. There are a ton of wild blueberry bushes and a good mix trees, bushes and wildflowers.  This park is great for bird watching.  During my visit I saw and photographed a great blue heron and some mallards.

Wonderful  large preserve in the Lehigh River Watershed.  Three crystal clean streams run through this preserve: Shades Creek, Stony Run, and Bear Creek. There are beautiful waterfalls along the streams which support a high quality cold water native fish species including brook trout.  Several simple bridges and one suspension bridge provide safe stream crossing.
The variety of species you may see starts with a warning at the main entrance where you are warned that black bear, bobcat, and Eastern coyote inhabit the preserve. Bird watchers may see Bald Eagles, Osprey, hawks, falcons, owls, warblers, scarlet tanagers, veeries, overnbirds, and indigo buntings.
The preserve center has a great variety of plants including oaks, maples ash mountain laurel and   Rhododendron.  On some trails you will go through a Rhododendron tunnel.

This is a wonderful park with many well marked trails for hiking.  The park also permits biking on over 20 miles of the nearly 40 miles of trails.  Horse back riding is permitted on some of the trails in the park and all of Horseshoe Trail.
The park has two lakes for fishing and boating: 22 acre Scotts Run Lake and 68 acre Hopewell Lake.  Boat rentals are available during the summer.
The park has a large swimming pool that is open Memorial weekend until Labor Day weekend for a fee and has bathrooms and a concession stand.
The park has lots of picnic tables and barbecue as well as a playground.  The park has camping, cabin and yurt rentals.

The only thing missing from this park is handicap playground access and equipment. This park connects by a trail to Copeland Park (where there is softball field and soccer fields and a basketball court).
This park has two baseball fields, a soccer field, tennis courts and a walking trail.
The park has a large sandbox and two playgrounds but niether are handicapped accessible.  The park has bathrooms , a picnic pavillion, a gazebo, and an ampitheater where they hold free concerts in the summer.
The addition of birdhouses along the treeline and some butterfly gardens would make this park outstanding.

Beautiful views,great trails, pretty waterfalls, good camping sites, nice "comfort faclities" (bathrooms) but the road itself is full of potholes.
Daniels Brook Chasm, Hawthorne Falls, Parker Brook Cascade are three smaller waterfalls in addition to Lulu Falls.
There are 40 camping sites.  The most scenic are atop Berry Mountain (downside is primative facilities)  camping at the base of the mountain has easy access to the modern comfort station that has men, women, and family bathrooms.
Berry Pond, atop Berry mountain, is said to be one of the highest natural water bodies in Massachusetts.

Great place to start your ride on the Schuylkill River Trail and head south.  Parking here is free and not time limited like some of the southern access parking areas. This is 26.2 miles from where the trails start in Philadelphia.  The trail is well maintained until you get into Philadelphia. (NOTE: It can get a bit smelly near Norristown when you pass the two waste water treatment facilities.)

Port Province Trailhead had picnic tables, bathrooms and a bike repair station.
It has a water trail landing where you can access the Schuylkill River.
This place also has two dog parks.

This nice little 4.8 acre park  is ideal for picnicking, fishing and bird watching. The park has picnic tables, multipurpose field and a scenic observation deck overlooking Fry's Run.
Fry's Run Park provides an access point to Delaware Canal State Park and the D&L Trail. The park features the historic M. Opp Bridge, which is a stone arch bridge over Fry's Run built in 1824.
The park is open Sunrise to sunset.
The park has undergone a restoration of the stream bank that included the planting of 190 trees and shrubs.

This 120+ acre park
Smedley Park, located on 120 acres of land between Media and Springfield, attracts many outdoor enthusiast, scout groups, and local sports teams. The park has a picnic pavilion with one working barbecue and broken barbecue.  The park has two playgrounds for children, ball fields, trails and walking bridges over Cum Creek.  The park also has the Environmental Center and the Lewis House, headquarters of Penn State's Cooperative Extension of Delaware County.

Henry Lane Park is a 22 acre natural park that provides trails for hiking and horseback riding.  The park connects by  an unnamed trail to the trails in   Natural Lands Trust Saunder's Woods.  Part of the trail that shows up on Google and appears to connect to Ashburn Field is cut off by a gate to the entrance of the Henry Botanical Garden.  The trail off the northeast corner of the park connects to the Bridlewild Trail to the Kenealy Nature Park.

This park has a small modern playground that is very nice for small kids but the park lacks a bigger playground for bigger kids. The park has other play equipment including swings and a cool seesaw setup. The park has a picnic pavilion,  a baseball field, basketball court, a memorial monument and a boat launching area.

Nice park with 4 tennis courts, 4 basketball courts, 2 sand volleyball courts, a softball field, a Frisbee golf course, a small skateboard park, large playground, picnic pavilions, open space and a connector trail to Johnsontown Park, bathrooms (open in summer months).

This 12.6 mile trail shadows the Wissahickon Creek and connects to other parks and preserves along its path.  The trail runs from Parkside in Upper Gwynedd Township to Stenton Avenue in Whitemarsh.   Along the trail you will see diverse wetlands, woodlands and meadows!

This park has a lot to offer. A playground with play equipment for very young children 2 to 5 and children 5 to 12. Unforunately the young children's equipment is between the older children and the swings. An 18 hole golf course, picnic tables, Bathrooms and trails.

This is a wonderful 72 acre park is a great place to enjoy nature. This park has several tennis courts, a roller hockey rink, soccer fields, picnic tables and a pavilion, benches swings and playground equipment. Only real complaints is the graffiti and trash.

This 50 plus acre wooded preserve lies along the Wissahickon Trail/ Green Ribbon Trail. Great bridges and stepping stones.  Only downer about this little preserve is the amount of trash left behind from when the Wissahickon Creek overflows its banks.
This is a great park for hiking and fishing at the lake.  This park could be amazing if they labled all the trails (not just the main few) and added a safe way to get down to the view below the dam.
dislikes: Lack of safe access to dam view

reviews_attraction.text: Great mountain and park.  Just dont go on a fall weekend as tons of people go to see the foliage.  On a clear day you can see for miles all the way to Vermont and Massachusetts.
This is the best Pennsylvania State Park. Excellent trail and great views including several waterfalls. Hiked on a week day in January and had most of our hike all to ourselves.
This small 26 acre preserve in Bryn Mawr of mostly open farm fields. This preserve has a small tree section near Black Rock Road (which has loud traffic noise).
Could be great but the power boats and jet skis were darting all over this area making bird watching less enjoyable

One day I came up with plans to do upper West Michigan. One was a trip to Traverse city, another was to go canoeing- but I forgot which river we went on- I think it was the Au Sable. On the way back we went down the west coast and dropped in on a lighthouse museaum and a random park for a picnic. Exploring turned out to be fun and traverse City has alot to offer, crystal bottomed lake cherry festival and now I heard they added a wine tasting tour. Next time I'm up that way I want to stop by the music camp Interlochen.

Out with my new foreign/ Chinese friends I was invited by their house for a party, out to a apple orchard, picked some pumpkins and had an invite to a church for a potluck and over to a host family walk. Had a good time at all of these. Sure was a fun experience with all the intl students and would recommend choosing that style if you're on campus soon.

Kind of cramped but still worth your time. Founding of Mt C. period displays, crafts for sale and occassional events such as tea talks,  visits by Rosco or holiday specials out in the garden walk. One of many on a stamp collecting booklet to do with friends when you have a chance. Cheerful staff- worthwhile visit
likes: Facilities & Services (Crafts for sale, Cheerful staff)
Activities (Tea talks, Special events, Garden walk)

reviews_attraction.text: If I'm not mistaken do to many a years gone by, this is the park my grand folks took us to as kids. Also the Autorama museaum and Fenton,/ Higgins lakes to meet up with extended family. Saw a fawn in the park whom must have just been born. Fun times there bird watching and hiking nature trail paths.

When my dad had a boat we took a ride to a cove near this historic place. Detroit is proud of this family and the estate is frequently visited by tourists. Classically made stone and majestically built. Would most definitely would recommend you to visit that and memorial nearby. See you there!!

Pops took me there upon return from Free China. Most remembered was their eels. Chicago has free Aquarium visits also. This idle also had a zoo butterflies and a famous fountain. It also is now a national park I believe after isle royal. They host the Grand Prix race which is world famous.

Was invited down there by a group from MtC st Frittz bar. Fun time in the ride down but turned out to be expensive for concessions and beer. Got separated from friends and had to take a taxi ride home. Good game!! Also went to z game in Taipei before with different type of crowd antics.

This was one of my fav places to visit due to its historic nature. I liked the period  pieces, the costumed guides and buildings saved and preserved telling tales of Michs past trading with the tribes, defending and molding a  settlement on a still new unfirmiliar land.

What a nice job they did converting this land from a golf course & country club to a winding path, fountain bridge playscape family centered park. Went there with a former friend and saw filming/ pic taking of couple's on the bridge. Will most likely return if invited.

One fond memory was walking the nature trail up the river bends. Short path but good scenic views. Bike or walk as you please. Good place for a group meetups or use the field for a sport. Occasional concerts- library and municipal buildings across the street.

Kind of small but nice staff with historical knowledge with displays. They may have a train ride on a nearby track that stops at a park then continues on to Selfridge Air National Base. They are usually one of the stops during holiday celebrations.

If you're from here we all are proud of several landmarkd it statues. One is the heart plaza, another is the spirit of Detroit and this one. Also had a good memory of heading to the arena for a hockey game and new years concert with our man Ted.

Have a fond memory of visiting s park with an archway. Think it might be this one or in Kentucky. Think back to my Gpa named Archie. Fun breathtaking and scenic. Good place to take family and be in the awe of nature's majesty.

Mightwlly impressed with the size architecture and layout of buildings and offices. Didnt know the size if this town was so big. Enjoyed walk a mile evrnt and people supporying us. Tour and offices visits was amazing.

Still remember the trip up north like it was yesterday. Very scenic, beautifull and awe inspiring. Liked the falls and sourounding park. Not a huge fall but still lovely and sereen. Stop by you'll love the experience.

While it's been a long time since visiting, the trip still stands out as a fond memories of. The start of a travel bug addiction, part 1. Remember the gift shop and awesome view. Therefore would love to see it again.

1 of the best parks around. Had fun with s close friend if mine who took me to there to meet up with family. Found out you could ccano there. Pleasant scenery and not to far away. You'll enjoy for this park sure.

A coming of age tradition for kids 19 to cross and drink. Many countries have these tunnels such as in England Taiwan or here. I like the bridge view but tunnel is faster I discovered. Hope to drive it again.

A few slight improvements but still very nice and appealing park grounds. Airport of same name has been replaced near arena but nice shopping plaza and mall has opened up. Worth a glace to see improvements.

Went there a few times as a kid with friends, classmates and band members. Enjoyed the days there by roasting hot dogs, walking the trails, playing frisbee and jamming music. Fun place, go check it out.

You simply can't find a more pleasant time and more beautiful scenery anywhere else. Techkuanamin Falls St Ignace The Locks and Fort Mich near the by bridge are other popular destinations I recommend.
A favorite family get away while growing up. We traveled there many times- it's easy to get to. It was so nice I would love to return again sometime soon. Picturesq and quite memorable visits. Thx!!
Great memories of going down there for festivals in and concerts like the techno/ industrial music celebrations. Good seating and views. Bring by a friend, pack be a lunch and kick back and enjoy.
Thought of this place cause me and some old buddies went there to check the nearby places like greek town the people mover and attended a festival there some night. Liked Cobo hall for a show.
First time seeing the up is a blast like any tourist attraction. Got on the boat and enjoyed the trip while being risen from one level to another. Suitable for a family visit on a day trip.

Just a short distance from Bellevue is the absolutely beautiful trail network by the Michigan Audubon Society. The Bernard W. Baker Sanctuary is a bird sanctuary devoted to the preservation of Sandhill Cranes. Throughout the preserve, you can hear hundreds of them calling with their beautiful songs, as if it's beckoning you to come like a siren in Homer's Odyssey. Only difference is the Sandhill Cranes are beautiful and glorious, whereas the sirens were ugly and monstrous. Tales from other hikers include sightings of Osprey and Bald Eagles, foxes and coyotes. You can hike any of their three loops from dawn to dusk - the half mile bluebird loop, the 0.3 mile Quail Trail, or the one mile main trail. You can hike all three or split them up into multiple visits. Truly a birder's paradise!

Bysterveld Park has a playground for the kids, a huge pavilion for those family get-togethers, and three hiking trail loops that total just over a mile to walk all three. The North Loop can be missed as you can see and hear more of the highway and less of nature. The Middle Recreation Loop is the most scenic equipped with an overlook to a pond and abundant in wildlife, where you can also fish for bluegill and catfish. The South Loop is the largest of the three and winds through a forest. The trail itself offers wide footpaths of pavement, gravel, and boardwalk terrain going through different intervals of wetlands and forest. This may not be Yankee Springs, but this little haven is definitely worth seeing, so go on and take a hike!

This is a very nice boardwalk trail that runs through two ponds. Parking near the Dyer Kiln, the boardwalk winds a half-mile to a very green meadow park that's furnished with a pavilion that's perfect for picnicking, and an overlook with lower railings so persons with handicapped disabilities can fish. The area used to be a limestone quarry in the 1800s, the first in Eaton County. The limestone was mined and burned into mortar in the neighboring Dyer Kiln. The two limestone quarries were abandoned and flooded into the two ponds you see today. However, the area has a lot of littered garbage, and would be nice if Eaton County would clean up the area. Still, that's a small price to pay to enjoy both history and nature.

The Fallasburg Covered Bridge is awesome! It was built in 1871 when the city of Fallasburg was declining because business was being diverted to Lowell. It was built shortly after the covered bridge in Ada was with the same design. You can visit both bridges in a day because of their close proximity, the only difference being Fallasburg you can drive across at a whopping 5 mph. On the other side of the bridge, you can visit the historic Fallasburg village which includes a house museum and a school museum. The few houses that remain are all that's left of Fallasburg. The bridge is a great historical landmark and deserves more visitors who are passionate for preserving the past and learning from it.

The Otsego Area Museum is very quaint, full of exhibits all about the thriving community of Otsego and it's surrounding areas. Come and see exhibits about how Otsego started as a community, how it endured during the war years, the lost civilization of Pine Creek, and its industrialization through Bardeen's Paper Mill. The museum is located in the old water works building at the beginning of Otsego's Riverwalk, and has some impressive views of the river. The staff is very knowledgeable and helpful, and are more than willing to give tours. Otsego and Plainwell residents won't be disappointed here when learning of their rich local history.

Me and the fam went here on a Sunday, and it was very overcrowded. From the parking lot, they have a short paved pathway to the beach. The beach is very rocky and good for rockhounds. Past the creek we found a more secluded part of the beach. The trails really didn't offer very much. They were exceptionally short, and because of how overcrowded it was we didn't see any wildlife. At the heart of Pilgrim Haven is a lone chimney, which used to be a part of the camp lodge back in the 1960s. Overall, I was a bit disappointed because based on the photos I was expecting a lot more that Pilgrim Haven didn't have to offer.

This off the beaten path trail network can be a little tricky to find since it's surrounded by private residences, but is also the reason why this place is so great, making it just you and nature. The trails are color-coordinated and very well marked with the most rugged trail being the Red Trail. The Blue Trail offers great views of the lake, but my favorite was the White Trail which offers views from a cliff of beautiful wetlands where we even got to see a pileated woodpecker. Me and the fam have been here 3 times and love blazing through these trails for they offer some of the best views in Cass County!

This museum is not really what I was expecting. Its two floors of near yawns and utter boredom. There was only one other couple in here when me and the fam went, and I now know why. Self tours aren't the best because of the lack of information they post, and other than the posters and famous magician memorabilia they don't really offer anything. I may be biased because I'm not into magic at all, but I really wouldn't recommend coming here, rather if you're in Marshall, they offer so many better museums, because this one isn't really an asset to Marshall at all, it's just sort of there.

The curator of this hidden gem is very knowledgeable to the history of Galesburg and is very passionate about helping others. Learn all about the Frank Lloyd Wright houses in the area, a mysterious property in Galesburg that keeps burning to the ground, the life and times of a Spanish-American War veteran, and the history to how Galesburg became the community it is today. Located in the back of the Galesburg Library, you can schedule your visit by appointment to this very quaint asset to the Galesburg community.

Although they tore down the water wheel on the gristmill ages ago, this park is still absolutely stunning! The grounds are very well kept up not to mention a great location for get-togethers and photo opportunities, as well as the perfect picnic location. There's also so much to explore here - the former gristmill, the mill pond, Nottawa Creek, a couple of waterfalls, the gardens and pathways, all of which give this park its A grade class as well as so much peace of mind when walking about the premises.

Me and the fam highly recommend walking the Marshall riverwalk and always make the trip to walk it when we're in the Marshall area. It's generally peaceful, unless they're doing concerts at Stuart's Landing, and it's a great place to fish or get in touch with nature. This last time we went we saw two Blue Herons, a muskrat, and some cedar waxwings. We are always impressed by the nature we find and the views of the waterfall, and you can't ask for better scenery in the city of Marshall.

A beautiful park at the heart of the village of Middleville. At Stagecoach Park you can walk along the Thornapple River, and access the Paul Henry Thornapple Trail. Although the best reason to come here would probably be to see the Good Intent Stagecoach, which has become the local mascot for the village, but also serves as a unique reminder both to how far we have come in advances of technology and to the utmost glorious modes of transportation used in the past.
likes: On-site Activities: River Walk, Trail Access

reviews_attraction.text: This trail is a beautiful place to get in touch with nature in the heart of downtown Kalamazoo. We saw deer, mallards, canadian geese, muskrats, red-winged blackbirds, and woodpeckers. The trail itself is a nice loop that goes around a marsh pond with several branches that sprout off of it. However, I would suggest going before 3PM when everyone is at work, because we went after 3 and it was heavily trafficked (super busy)! Wouldn't recommend coming here after 3.

Me and the fam fell in love with Fellinlove Farm! Those with special needs will enjoy everything this therapeutic farm offers including your usual barnyard favorites - goats, pigs, horses, bunnies, and tons of hilarious Dachshunds! Also sit and reflect at one of two koi ponds and even enjoy a nature trail. The staff here are incredibly sweet and helpful and are even willing to give tours. Although, visitors beware! Stopping here may mean you never want to leave.

The trails at Townsend are beautiful! We did a 1.3 mile loop at the north end of the park. The trail is wide, perfect for groups, and is moderately trafficked as well as moderate terrain as it is very hilly. There is also access to the North Country Trail on site. The Scotch Pine Trees are what give this park its beauty - they are so closely kitted together and seem to clap as they swayed in the wind. Definitely worth making the trip!

I love trailing at this place! I almost stepped on a garter snake and saw a herd of deer running through a meadow. Also, the visitors' center has some exhibits of animals they're currently rehabilitating that wouldn't be able to survive in the wild. With 16 trails, there's a lot of variety at this nature center that needs recurrent visits to experience everything they have to offer.

Yankee Springs is a beautiful state park. I love coming out here and getting in touch with nature! Or lost, whichever comes first. They got tons of trails. Tons! There's also a modern campground on Gun Lake and a rustic campground on Deep Lake. Two public beaches, ten miles of horse trails, and a great place to go boating, swimming, kayaking, and fishing.

Formerly state-run, this fish hatchery is now one of the largest city parks in Hastings. Remnants of the fish hatchery remain with three historical buildings, and several fish-occupied ponds. You can also find your normal sports fields and playground equipment here. But as a word of caution - bring bug spray - lots of it!... the horror! The horror!

There is a great natural beauty to this place. Not as popular as Silver Beach to the south, but this place is a great hangout to swim, access the pier to see the lighthouses, and partake in water sports and other fun recreational activities. Me and the fam had a wonderful and fun experience here and highly recommend making the trip to visit!

This beach truly is a gem. With free beach access to Lake Michigan, a playground for the kids, accessibility to two lighthouses, an ice cream stand, and dining at The Deck Restaurant, this beach is perfect to make so many memories. A great place to have a romantic getaway, play day with the kids, or your new favorite hangout.

This isn't where the nature sanctuary is. The real Dowagiac Woods is down the street just past the Dowagiac River and is an amazing trail. This location on the map is only farmland. So if you make it here and are lost, just keep going down Frost and it'll be on the right.

The Old Jail Museum was surprisingly fun. The house is divided into the house and what used to be the old Allegan jail. Only open Fridays and Saturdays, but if you happen to be in the area during one of those days, make the stop to one of the areas best free museums!

Part safari, part petting zoo this place rocks! Get an up close encounter with kangaroos, monkeys, giraffes, camels, and your usual petting zoo favorites. Me and the fam absolutely loved this zoo and highly recommend it for other families!

Had so much fun here with the fam. We had a cookout, went swimming, and got in touch with nature - saw Great Blue Heron, baby Geese, swans, and even a salamander! Me and the family plan on coming back here real soon!
A great place to wander the trails, see the historic bridges, or just get some peace of mind. Get in touch with nature at this awesome park!

A fun windy drive leads you to this remote shoreline, where one of Michigan's most vulnerable lighthouses still stands.  What remains has been beautifully restored.  You can climb the tower and walk the sandy shoreline, taking in the dunes and forest.  There's not much else to do out here since it's so far from civilization!  Just remember to stock your car with ketchup packets in case you get trapped on the road in winter.

Loads of history about the Copper Country!  It's very cool to have a national park site right in our backyard, and they've done a great job of preserving historical sites and the story of our area.  While the park doesn't own a lot itself, it does partner with other organizations and private individuals to do what they can to keep history alive for future generations to discover.

One of the ugliest "beaches" I've ever been too.  In addition to the garbage that is lying around (including broken glass bottles), the stamp sands themselves can be considered the be a hazard to your health.  The sunsets are nice out here at least, as is the view of the lighthouse.  Don't go here for supreme natural beauty though, as there is almost nothing natural about it.

Amazing natural resource open for the public.  The best places here are the ones that the touristy folks don't get to.  Hike off the beaten path to some remote corners.  If you're within range of a road, prepare for busloads of tourists.  Or go in the winter, hardly anyone hikes around then and the woods are still beautiful.  Either way, there's a lot to see.

Nice little public beach that's quite a ways away from most population centers.  It's a beautiful white sand beach, with picnic tables and swings, as well as porta-potties in the summertime.  Local goons often dump or burn trash near the beach, which is kind of a bummer.  The views of the Lower Entrance Light are spectacular from this location!

Historic theatre with all of the fixins.  Creaky seats? Check. Old murals? Check. Steep nosebleed sections? Check.  Lots of random shows come up here and it's a fun atmosphere to be in here in the modern era.  Plus, the building looks great from the outside!

A HUGE local natural resource that gets better every year.  Extensive white sand beach (when the lake level isn't so high), thousands of acres of wetlands, and loads of wildlife to search for.  Excellent location for non-motorized exploration.

A great spot to check out wildlife!  There's a observation tower to look out over the wetlands, and a mowed (sometimes) trail that leads around the wetter areas.  The tall grass often has ticks though, so check yer socks before you leave!

All waterfront parks are nice, and this one especially so because it has so much great grass.  The pavilion also is nice, although some of the picnic tables have seen better days.  Plus there's a skate park!  Parking here is kinda weird.

Scenic site with a little bit of history too.  Disrespectful people often will set up their campers right on top of the historical marker, so if you can't find it hunt around, it could be being used as someone's kitchen table.

Remote little state park far from any communities.  The lake is beautiful, if a bit crowded with houses and camps.  The park is great though.  Visit in the early summer or fall and there's hardly a soul around.
Amazing slice of rugged terrain!  Beaches on both sides of the peninsula allow for many chances to see the lake and hike along the rocky shoreline.  The trail feels much longer than it actually is.
Cool old ruins that are hidden away out of sight.  Unless you knew to look for them, you wouldn't even expect there to be ruins around here.  Industrial stories are everywhere you turn in da U.P.
Neat old lighthouse way out on Lake Superior.  You gotta hike here which keeps *some* tourists away.  It's closed up in the offseason so if you want a tour, you gotta go in the summertime.
The biggest collection of rocks, minerals, and neat stones this side of the ground.  Definitely spend some time here to learn about what makes our Earth (and the local area) so amazing.
How many towns have an ORE DOCK!?!  That's what I thought.  +1 for Marquette's iconic industrial leftover, inspiring generations to think outside the box as to what is beautiful.
Scenic and historic lighthouse that has been well-maintained by the Fort Wilkins Historic State Park.  Go on a tour or paddle over yourself!  You can't drive to it however.
Beautiful old lighthouse, glad they saved this one!  Hard to get to unless you've got adventurous spirit or a lot of money and a boat you don't mind beaching on the rocks.
Super amazing piece of land protected by the Keweenaw Land Trust.  Thank goodness we've got organizations like theirs looking out for our shared natural resources!
Quiet local beach that only the locals know about!  Not very busy, expansive white sands, and wide open views of Lake Superior.  Great for chilling and grilling.
Beautiful waterfalls that are easy to view from the constructed boardwalks and paths.  I once found a big snapping turtle under the falls, so watch your step ;)
This range light sits in the middle of a residential neighborhood and that's about it.  Just sits there.  No signs, nothing to do, nothing fancy about it.
Neat little stop off along the highway before you hit the doldrums of northern lower Michigan or the endless nothingness in much of the U.P.
Little lighthouse sitting in the middle of the neighborhood.  Not much going on.  Don't disturb it, it's doing its job!
Great big local waterfall!  Although man has impacted it quite a lot, it is still very scenic at all times of year.

This is undeveloped property and should really be called a state game area. There are no published trails and I am wildly guessing, it's mostly used as a local fishing and hunting area. There's farmland between the lake and the entrance and no visible trails. There are absolutely no signs announcing the park on the roadways (I guess that's good so more visitors won't be disappointed). There's a tiny parking area and just a DNR sign. There's no lake access via trail. You would have to follow hunting trails and wear Orange if you do. Visitors beware if you are not a hunter, most reviews here are about the lake accessed via other means and not of the park.

A must see for Michigan in winter! Fairly easy trail, crampons or ice trax required. Crampons would make it a better hiking experience than the yak trax. Beautiful ice formations, this location gets a lot of visitors over the Munising ice festival. Although it's only a 2.2 mile round trip, allow a minimum of 3 hours to visit. There's a chain of ice caves, we saw 3 of them. Roads are plowed and trails are pretty tamped down by other hikers. Over the weekend, there was a popcorn stand and a hot chocolate stand. There are Porta potties courtesy of the farmer who owns the land, right next to them is a donation box. If you visit, please donate what you can.

Lovely place. Interesting history behind the park, it's the only National Wildflower Sanctuary in the US. About 2.5 miles of loop trails. There's a cultural trail to learn the history of the place. Best time for the wildflower trail would be early April and then summer to catch the ephemeral spring flowers and then the summer flowers. There's a connector trail to NCT to the North and Diamond Lake County park campground to the South. Loda Lake itself is a great spot to just sit and watch and listen to the birds.

Very large campground, good for tent camping or an RV, right on the Superior Lakeshore, beautiful sunsets. There should be some restriction on after hours lighting though, one of the campers had lit up the campsite with bright LEDs strung up on a tree, was too bright to see any stars. Showers are a bit of a walk depending on which campsite you choose.

Gem of West Michigan for beaches! Takes a hike to get to the beach but still gets a lot of visitors over weekends. Lot of trails in the park as well. There are flush toilets and picnic benches before the trail to the beach, and  there's a rustic toilet closer to the beach. No potable water source or changing facilities at the beach.

Interesting park with a nature preserve for waterfowl. A 5-6 mile trail that provides views of farmland mostly. The trail is very open so there are beautiful views of the sky and land far into the horizon. It's well maintained for being a state park in a remote area. The nature preserve while small is a treat for bird lovers.

A nice little historic state park with a 2 mile in and out trail to see the survey markers for Michigan meridian and baseline. If you are interested in cartography, surveying, history of surveying, it's a very cool place to visit. Park and trail is well maintained and easy to get to. Michigan is unique in having two markers.

Love this area! Several hiking trails and bridle trails, and an MTB trail that's one of the best in the lower peninsula! Haven hill nature area is one of Michigan's 12 National Natural Landmarks. Two beautiful lakes and rolling hills and to this parks beauty. A historic park as well with ruins of Ford's estate!

Love this park! Awesome hiking trail. 4 miles of NCT within the park. Park has well groomed ski trails and an awesome bike trail. Lot of neat geological features. Rolling hills, groves of evergreens, very quiet park makes it a wonderful time forest bathing. A must visit if you are an avid hiker.

Great trail for hiking in winter! Challenging hikes, lots of options to do different loops. If you are hiking, check website, since bikes switch direction from clockwise to anticlockwise on different days of the week. Hikers should hike in the opposite direction to the bikes.

A really cool Oakland County Park. Serene, quiet and lots of wildlife, away from highways, you can hear so much. Multi-use bridle and hiking trails, wide trails, short and long loops, can easily make it 8 miles or more. Trails loop around many water features, rolling hills.

What an awesome park to hike! Lots of elevation change makes for a challenging hike. We hiked the snowmobile trails and really had a great time. Lot of options to combine different loops to make short or long trails. Would be great to visit again in spring, summer and fall.

Lovely, peaceful, quiet park for hiking! Trails crisscross so you can make your hike anywhere from a mile to 13 miles if needed.  Mixture of marshland, coniferous forest, grassland, pond and proud lake! Great for fishing, canoeing and kayaking as well.

Love this park! Shower stalls, changing stalls, flush toilets close to the beach, two large parking lots, trails, picnic benches, miles of beach to spread out and dunes to climb. Sandy Beach with sandy bottom, great for swimming. A Michigan gem!

This is a great hike with two observation towers to view the marshes and the area. Bring binoculars to see the many bird species. Fall hike is beautiful. It's a registered National Natural landmark. A must hike location!

Nature center has something for kids and adults every weekend. About 6 miles of trails in the area makes it a great place to visit. Highlight of any such visit would be feeding the birds right out of your hand.
Lovely little park! Has both paved and nature trails, about 3 miles of it. Great park for kids, has a splash zone, nature center and lots of activities for kids. In the winter, there's a sled hill.
What an awesome place to visit all year round! Beautiful flowers native and exotic, rolling hills, scenic Huron river, beautiful stately trees, a must-include spot for a visit to Ann Arbor
A really great park, hike/bike trails loops of 5 miles and 9 miles and a completely new 5 mile loop added recently make this a nice park to hike longer distances. Very scenic park.
Great Metropark! Nature trails are a mix of grassland and wooded trails. Enjoyed the trails, my first time visit and will be back to explore other things of interest.
Peaceful, beautiful park! Great park to watch birds, take a hike and immerse yourself in nature. Portions of the trail can be wet or underwater after rains.
Beautiful hiking trails! Mature woods make it a really pleasant hike in the fall! You don't feel like you are in the city at all within these woods.
Short 1 mile trail, it's quiet and pretty. Good for kids to hike and learn about plants and trees. The gardens nearby are also cool to stroll by.
Wide open hilly trails, lot of loop options. Great for cross country skiing, they have groomed trails, ski rentals. A great park!
Really small park. Not much of a trail, just 1 mile in a tiny section of woods. Great beach and lake.

Shiawassee National Wildlife Preserve is just that, it only has primitive facilities and nominal changes to the natural surroundings in the area.

It has good views of wetland areas, extensive woodlands and some dirt trails and roads to follow.

The Nature drive is still closed for the season and construction that isn't completed.

The main wooded areas are completely covered in a foot or two of standing water due to enormous amounts of rainfall this year. One of the trail shortcuts is flooded and cannot be crossed without wading in water covered in algae.

We did see a lot of Great Egrets, a mature Bald Eagle, and several Great Blue Herons.

We also surprised a groundhog who was sleeping 5 feet up in a tree because the forest is flooded. We didn't even know groundhogs can climb trees!

Because of the standing water, there are hundreds of mosquitos and biting black flies all over the trails. Be sure to bring bug spray if you plan on walking in the Preserve.

The scenery is beautiful, and I'm sure it's even better when the woods aren't flooded and animals don't have to either flee the area or climb into trees for refuge.

We really enjoyed our short visit for our first time at Watkins Glen State Park. The scenery is very pretty with the road splitting two lakes so you can see wild fowl on both sides of the main road.
Before we had even gotten to the parking lot we had already spotted 3 Blue Herons crossing the road, many ducks and terns, and Canada Geese all over the place. There was two swans in the smaller pond too.
The park is so new that it really hasn't been improved or developed yet which makes it even prettier for the wildlife and enjoying nature

There were hundreds of frogs croaking loudly in a small pond just across from the parking spot. That pond is so close to the parking area that the frogs heard the car door close and stopped singing.

We didn't get to walk the grassland "rail to trail" path because of freezing rain and gloomy skies. But we will come back and explore more.

There are several months between Feb. and May, and again in the fall, where the lakes and wetlands are closed to activity so that the waterfowl and other birds aren't disturbed by too much noise or too many people.

Sleeping Bear Dunes is a great place and well worth the travel time to visit. We liked the different variety  of areas to explore, from the huge sand dunes, the lake shore, the pine and beech and birch forests, then driving around on the Pierce Stocking Scenic Trail. The whole park is so huge you can't explore it all in a day and just walking along the high dunes could take all day. The surrounding area is also very pretty and the  local wildlife is fun to watch, the squirrels and many different birds you see while exploring are interesting too. There is a lot of hills to climb and the wind along the shoreline coming from Lake Michigan is very refreshing after a long day exploring the isolated dunes.

The Deadman's Hill Overlook has a great view of the Jordan River valley and has lots of short trails to explore along the Jordan River Trail from 3 miles to 8 miles or even more if you follow the North Country Trail which connects at the bottom of the hill.

It is beautifully forested with Maples, Oaks, Birches, Beeches, and some Northern Red Cedar trees right at the bottom of the hill.

The shot 3 mile hike is an easy walk down but a harder and steep walk back up the hill but the view from there is worth it too.

It is a popular Fall colors spot and the dirt road there from M-131 was packed with cars from a half mile away from the Overlook itself when we were there on a late October weekend.

We really enjoyed visiting Sleeper State Park up in the Michigan Thumb area for our first time there. It was a relaxing visit to a nice beach, with nice views of Saginaw Bay and lots of shoreline to explore.

We enjoyed the trip even though the facilities on the Day Use side were not open yet. It will be even better once it warms up and the beach will be more fun when you can actually enjoy swimming.

The sand dunes we're pretty too, and we still have a lot of explore there, the wooded trails and the campground look like it would be fun to visit too.

We always enjoy Dodge Park in the Spring, Summer and in Fall. We enjoy following all the nature trails and walking along the river. We really enjoy seeing the animals there, and all the different birds we have seen there. Little ponds in the spring holds hundreds of frogs and there is always ducks and Canada Goose around the park and along the riverside. We have also seen a young Horned Owl and a Great Blue Heron, and always enjoy hearing lots of birdsong from the Northern Cardinals, and the chirping and croaking of all the frogs.

We really enjoyed "the oldest aquarium in America" even though it's still being renovated. I loved seeing the hand-placed green tile ceiling I had heard so much about while Belle Isle Aquarium was being restored. There is quite a few interesting fish, some interactive displays for the kids to enjoy, and room to grow as more display tanks are still being worked on. You can see the long history here, as you look around into nooks and crannies like the gift shop and how the workmanship is so different from today.

We stopped by the U.S.S. Edson on display in the Saginaw River during the Tall Ship Celebration 2016. We were on the way to visit the Saginaw River Rear Range Light and our shuttle bus stopped at the ship so we visited the ship on the way. It looks nice sitting in the river, and looks good even when it still needs some renovations. I thought it was very cute that their little landing craft on display was called "Ed's Son"😁 The ship is still being worked on but it's worth the time to visit.

Fort Gratiot County Park has a great view from a small beach along Lake Huron. It is not far from Port Huron.

There are several picnic shelters available and there are lots of rocks to investigate along the shoreline.

The beach was not crowded when we are there, probably because LakePort State Park and Lighthouse Beach are not far away.

We enjoyed our trip to the Riverwalk to see the Tri-Centennial Lighthouse, which is a replica of Tawas Point Lighthouse in a smaller size 😊 The marina looks nice, there is good views of the downtown Detroit skyline and the Detroit River and Ambassador Bridge. Parking was hard to find though because of where it is and how crowded it was.

The museum is great, it has fun things for kids to do and lots of history lessons for adults. It has a lot about the Edmund Fitzgerald shipwreck, and the bridge of the William Clay Ford freighter to show what the deck is like on the river. Very nice displays of model ships from long ago are very interesting too.

A short bridge with a great view of the Detroit skyline and Ambassador Bridge. It's fun to walk along the bridge and watch the ducks and geese floating under it. You can see most of Belle Isle and up and down the Riverview area of Detroit, and even see the Tri-Centennial Lighthouse downriver at Milliken Park.

We spent a morning exploring the Yankee Air Museum and going to the gift shop. There is a lot of history shown here, about the old Bomber plant and many aircraft on static display, Also information about military history after WW2. There is interesting displays for the kids to enjoy too.

We really enjoyed the Blue Water River Walk, and it will be even better once it is finished. There is lots of good views and lots of birds to enjoy watching along the river. There is a wetlands area that is fun to walk by and also visiting the USCGC Grayfox along the waterfront pier.

Nice little zoo. We enjoyed the live displays of turtles, albino deer, a couple of Black Rat Snakes, and the educational displays for the kids. There is a nice birdwatching area which drew in a Bluejay, the first I have seen all summer. It even had a groundhog hogging the food 😁

We visited Point Betsie just before the lighthouse grounds and gift shop opened for 2017 season. It is an easy lighthouse to get to and visit and has a nice beach area with lots of lake rocks and great views. We really enjoyed the waves and walking along the beach.

We loved the view from the lookout point, which is the highest lakeside dune in Michigan. It is a very pretty spot and very windy. We were able to watch the fog rolling in along the shore and drifting across the road and that was a great scene overlooking the town.

We always enjoy visiting this lighthouse and exploring the grounds and the old United States Life Savers Service quarters. The park next to the grounds is nice too. There is a sandy beach shoreline to explore and lots to choose from in the museum shop.

This is such a pretty State Park. It has a very nice Birds of Prey lookout point and nice shoreline to explore. There is also sand dunes and woods with trails to follow. We wished we could have enjoyed the Dark Sky Preserve to see the night sky...

We enjoy walking along the nature trails and along the river. There is always something to see like the ducks or Canada Goose flocks in the area and wildflowers to find and enjoy. A lot of local birdlife is  close enough to enjoy from the trails.

The Round Island Lighthouse looks great after all the renovations since it was damaged so badly in the storms back in the early 1970's. It is a very pretty structure and very easy to get great pictures from the Mackinaw Island ferries.

We really enjoy this lighthouse and the museum, it has a great staff that was very nice to talk to about the history of the area. There is a lot on display in the old Keeper's house and a lot about the local shipwrecks.

We loved seeing this unique lighthouse at the last part of our trip "Up North" before heading home. It has great views of the lighthouse and Mackinac Bridge, and a lot to see and a beach to explore too.
We love watching baseball here, it's a great park and parking is easy if you use their garages. The Tiger's Den has good food and the kids like the ferris wheel in center court.
We enjoyed the view of Lake Huron, Saint Clair River and Fort Gratiot Lighthouse. The park is nice with several different play areas and a beach along the lake.

This place has so many things you can see and explore. Admission was free and parking was 8 $ . The 1st floor has community art work and kids art classes. There is children interactive art stations. Then you can tour all the gallery's in the 2nd floor when your done you can stop by the gift shop of cafe then you can cross Monroe street and go to the glass blowing museum. Outside the museums are more sculptures and some you can touch. They have glass blowing exhibits too.

My kids had a blast on our trip here. We did the scout day and got a fun patch. It has something  for all ages and the lay out is very nice and easy to access my kids can wander and not get  lost in the building. The playground  is huge and a lot of fun. My littlest kid was overwhelmed  so I helped her though the playground  the 1st time and she was off. Cafe wa as reasonably  priced as well

Best family day trip! This place has everything and yes the tickets are expensive but get the membership it is totally worth it. The aquarium is great the splash pad is a perfect cool down spot when it's hot. they are hard at work over the tunnel. The zip line and high top course is great

This place was worth the 8 dollars for unlimited  maze fun. As an adult  I had a hard time the first few times trying to get out. My kids have a blast. They do have you wear gloves so you dont get fingerprints  all over the mirrors. The staff was friendly  and it was a nice adventure.

We came for the Christmas lights. This place is a delight and we can always stop for are favorite place for some chicken and sports as well. This place makes downtown fun again and brings life to our city !! We love hensville and we will be coming back for years to come.

This is a small and clean park. The rangers we very helpful and nice. Did you know they do scout events and birthday parties even... Very nice quite area shelters to have a picnic pretty water view across the street ... Great education base

Great place to see out Detroit  tigers .this is a great  experience . It's more than just a ball park they have a carousel  and rides as well as tons of food options  the field is huge you got to see at least 1 game in your life time

Love this park and the 1st girl scout trail is here the Juliet low trail and archery this trail is a hidden gem and so quite ... Enjoy walking the trails or shooting a bow . My girls enjoyed achery with scouts here . Great place!

This place is one of the coolest places to visit and there are attractions around  this area too like the castles of ohio and hocking hills we stopped here every year we went as a family  and now I take my girls

This place is absolutely breathtaking come the trees to the cliffs to all the beautiful nature around you this is a great place to disconnect from reality and relax with your life good reflection time
my kids spend hours digging and looking for fossils. This is a free park and the kids can dig for endless hours they have a picnic area as well so you can make a day of it and trails not far too
This was a great little change of pace. This is a little gem in our area check it out we will be back. This is a great little trip to just explore and in the fall they have a corn maze as well
Neat small park. Really cool trails we create when it was raining so there wasn't a ton of people but the animals were running around from frogs to squrrels to birds this place was very neat
The art museum was a great experience for my kids to walk through it was a great tie into all of the history and it was really neat to see all the different galleries that were offered
This was such a nice day trip my kids got to play in the sand and got to play in the clean clear water this is definitely an experience that they will remember the sand was so soft
this place was a cool little stop on our road trip to knox county. It was a fun road trip for me and my husband it was a little jem  in the country. You need to check it out
This park is a great way to disconnect from wilderness and just relax me and my kids explored the blue and part of the read trail for hours
This a such a pretty park we were at the ice carving festival and walked down here and the snow was starting  to fall. Such a pretty  park.
Lovely park. We went for the cherry fest . This place is very nice natural environment. I felt like I was at home and it felt invitating.
This is such a pretty park. I have taken senior pictures here and family shoots. It is just a relaxing and peaceful place
This place is so much fun they have winter craft days and it's cool to explore on a empty  day or with all the reenactors
Nice park and nice play ground I am glad they updated thier playground. I broke my wrist on the monkey bars in 95'
Nice park and we can watch the baseball games in the spring/summer I used to go here regularly my brothers games.
We love to play at the beach and walk the boardwalk. We also visited the lighthouse festival and had a blast
This is one of my most favorite places to visit when down here. It is a one of a kind time of hike.

Adena mound is a historical place in Indian Mound Reserve or Peterson Park. There are two beautiful Rim & Gorge trails with an amazing waterfall. The new wooden stairs are easy to climb onto the mound. Well maintained paths and bridges. This is an awesome place to visit in all seasons. There is separate parking at each entrance. You can park on either side and walk through the entire reserve.

Nice state park with lake. The park has several picnic areas with restrooms. Restrooms weren’t clean though. Dogs are allowed on trails. Family friendly Park with multiple activity like Boating, Fishing, Hiking etc. We particularly enjoy the 5 mile loop trail that around the lake in a circle. It goes through the woods, picnic areas and campground. Definitely revisit.

Well maintained historical place. Adena Mansion was built for Thomas Worthington in 1807. Ohio History connection organization  kept this mansion very well. So many old artifacts you can find there. Our tour guide lady was so good she shared all the information about the Mansion and Thomas Worthington and his family.

The Tahquamenon Falls are two different waterfalls on the Tahquamenon River. We visited both the upper and lower falls. There is a small island and few areas to play in the falls. I also recommend stopping at the gas station next to Tahquamenon state fall entrance. Old gas pump with manual operation.

Small place with limited parking. Just 10 minutes’ walk to the water falls. The water fall is gorgeous and definitely worth seeing in all seasons. It's very peaceful. There are no bathroom facilities and no picnic tables. But you can also go to Grigg's Dam for a hike and picnic.

Small place with limited parking. Just 10 minutes’ walk to the water falls. The water fall is gorgeous and definitely worth seeing in all seasons. It's very peaceful. There are no bathroom facilities and no picnic tables. But you can also go to Grigg's Dam for a hike and picnic.

Small Historical landmark on the highest point of Mackinac Island. It's just a reconstruct of an old fort, I did not get much from internal fort design. But magnificent views from there. Seriously, it offers the best view on the island. It was a good hike up to the Fort Holmes.

Historic landmarks, breathtaking views, spectacular rock formations. A great variety scenic resources provides something of interest for every Mackinac Island visitor. Wonderful experience for kids and adults. Had an awesome time. Would do it all again.

This park has multiple playground areas. Has shelter house, basketball court and several soccer fields. Big walking trail around all of it. My kid's soccer club used this field for foot skill practice when Avery park not available.
Nice park....with Christmas decoration.....This park is good for both seasons winter as well as summer....you can enjoy downtown look from park.....can have food with family in downtown after park
There is a nice little moderate trail with a beautiful natural bridge. There are couple of other trails towards the creek/river. No real parking, there a small parking space at entrance.
Lovely waterfall. You can go down to the bottom of the fall through the stairs.  Small town surrounding this fall. Good options around for casual meal, coffee and Ice-cream.
Great place to visit in Lancaster. You can walk up the mountain and around the pond. Great city view from the top. It has tennis courts, playground for the kids.
Great place to visit. The castle was small but beautiful. Guide told the history, how one man built this lovely castle. You can spend 2-3 hours.
A great family beach. Beach is narrow and long. Excellent for kids. Nice campground. Great place to relax and enjoy the sand water and nature.
Multiple playgrounds available for the kids. Also have two small ponds for fishing. It's close to my place. Always come back here for picnic.
Spray Falls cruise was great. It’s around two hours of the trip. Cruise crew was excellent. Great tour with excellent pieces of information.
It’s a big beautiful park. It is a hub of outdoor recreation. We were there in hot summer day. We will definitely be back to explore more!
Quick scenic stop. Small beautiful waterfall. Small parking area and a half-mile trail with an observation deck overlooking the falls.
Nice little amazing park in the middle of dublin. Chief Leatherlips monument and access to Scioto River. Overall good picnic place.
It’s a great riverside park.  I just love coming here to walk, relax, picnic or just simply getting some fresh air all the time.
It is a nicely restored lighthouse. Beautiful Park area. There's a great view of the Mackinac Bridge from the lighthouse.
A nice park in our neighborhood. Nice trails and playgrounds. It’s very crowded at times, but kids love the company.
It's really a great metro park. It has lots of trails, a couple of nice ponds and picnic area. I loved this place.
Love this park...has splash pad and  wide open field and a hill with rabbit statues on it.  Good place for kids.

Great collection of medieval art. This is not everybody's cup of tea, but the wonderfully detailed carvings, sculptures, tapestries, stained glass and Decorative Arts are really amazing. Take a moment to see how amazingly detailed they are. Works of great artistic skill, effort and patience. There are also some lovely little gardens, and great views of the Hudson River.  More terrific views and forest trails are at hand in Fort Tryon Park, where the museum is located. The medieval architecture is pretty cool too. Much of it brought over from monestaries in Europe.

BEAUTY ALERT!!! THE TREES OF THE GRAVEYARD HERE ARE BLOOMING RIGHT NOW.  (SEE PIX) COME AND SPEND SOME TRANQUIL MOMENTS HERE.  IT'S JUST A LOVELY LOVELY SPOT.  FYI THE INSIDE OF THIS CHURCH IS GORGEOUS BUT IT'S COMPLETELY CLOSED FOR LONG TERM RENOVATIONS.  I THINK THE REAR CHAPEL IS STILL LEON FOR PRAYERS ETC
Beautiful gothic church.  Currently closed for major rehab work.  Grave yard is a nice peaceful tree filled place.  Out includes graves of Alexander Hamilton,  Robert Fulton and some other interesting folks

This is an unusual but very moving Memorial to the 1 million plus Irish citizens who died during the Potato Famine. Another million Irish emigrated to America. The grassy slope that is created recreates the Irish countryside. The stone cottage is actually from Ireland. On the walls below the slope are quotes about the famine and about famines in general. The recorded voices that you hear, as you pass through the corridor leading into the slope, are readings of those quotes.

ARE YOU A JRR TOLKIEN FAN?!! The Morgan currently has exhibit of artwork about Middle Earth created by Tolkien himself.  Including the first book jacket of the hobbit. Very cool.    This is a small museum part of which was JP Morgans offices and library.  The library room is unbelievably beautiful.  Parts of Morgan's collection of original manuscripts and first additions is great.   They rotate displays of them. Guttenberg Bible is just one of them Great artwork too.

NOW EXHIBITING A WONDERFUL COLLECTION OF PAINTINGS ABOUT COAST GUARD.   40 PAINTINGS. MANY  ARE DRAMATIC & POWERFUL.  THEY ARE ON 2ND FLOOR.  HARD TO FIND BUT WORTH IT. CLOSES 9/19/2019                                            DO U LIKE  ALEXANDER HAMILTON? CHECK OUT 2ND FLOOR EXHIBIT ALL ABOUT HIS LIFE AND ACCOMPLISHMENTS.        Small but worthwhile historical stop. Washington was inaugurated here. The Bill of Rights was written here. THIS PLACE IS FREE.

MUST SEE. VIRTUAL REALITY EXHIBIT CALLED "THE LAST GOODBYE".  BUT NOTE!! ONLY 1 PERSON CAN DO IT AT A TIME AND IT LASTS 20 MINUTES SO IT BACKS UP VERY QUICKLY.  YOU CAN RESERVE A TIMEBUT IT COULD EASILY BE 2 HOURS LATER. I WENT FRIDAY AT 11 A.M. AND I HAD TO WAIT 1 HR. WEEKENDS MUST BE IMPOSSIBLE.    YOU ARE VIRTUALLY TAKEN TO THE SITE OF AN OLD KILLING CAMP AND A REAL SURVIVOR OF THE CAMP TAKES YOU ON A TOUR.  VERY EFFECTIVE AND MOVING.

Another lovely part of the park. It is a wide, tree-lined walk with the statues of famous writers spaced along it. Writers include Shakespeare, Robert Burns and Walter Scott. A recent addition is a statue of three women's rights pioneers, Sojourner Truth, Susan B. Anthony and Elizabeth Cady Stanton. The trees are some of the few American Elms still standing. Dutch Elm disease has wiped out most.

This is a truly beautiful suspension bridge between New Jersey and Manhattan. When it was built it was the longest suspension bridge in the world almost doubling the previous record-holder. It has eight Lanes of traffic on its Upper Deck and six Lanes of traffic on it's Lower Deck. It Carrie's more traffic every year then any other bridge in the world. Over 1 million cars and trucks every year

This is a very underwhelming structure.  It's just a small bridge between two  buildings.  There are other skybridges in Manhattan prettier than this one.  It's got a little architectural charm but i wouldn't go out of my way to see it.  Tribecca is a wonderful area to walk around with lots of great architecture both old and contemporary. So do visit it.  While your there check this out.

This is the pretty Arch Bridge that runs parallel to the Cross Bronx Expressway as it crosses the East River. It mostly takes local traffic. Some people refer to it as the Martha Washington Bridge because it is so much smaller then the George Washington Bridge which is just a few miles west which crosses the Hudson River and links New Jersey and New York.

This Garden is on the small side but it is beautifully landscaped with lots of flowering trees shrubs and flowers. The paths are very interesting. Beautiful rock gardens are a highlight.  We saw two snapping turtles in the Stream behind the visitors center. The only negative is the nose from nearby highway.  At least you can't hear it

World class art museum with fine art from all over the world and all time periods. Must see is their large set of murals called "Detroit Industry". Powerful,  beautifully drawn and touches on several themes.  Museum is very strong on European and American art. Also a lot of beautiful decorative arts; furniture,  porcelain,  etc.

Nice little park. Nothing flashy just a nice combination of trees, shrubs, grass and seasonal flowers that are planted...well. for the season.  The flower beds full of tulips in the spring is particularly stunning. Also lots of benches for people to eat at, or just to sit and enjoy the peaceful calm amidst the big city.

Great views over the Hudson.  Check out Tom  Otterness's whimsical,  fascinating sculpture,  The Real World.  Its actually a group of several sculptures, all related to each other.  They are even on  the tops of the nearby light posts.  it's at the north entrance of the park at the end of Chambers St & River Terrance.

This is a less frequented area of Central Park, but still very pretty. Designed it reproduce the feel of the Catskills Mountains which are North of the city, it is a very wooded area. South of here is a stream that runs through this area which has a couple of water falls and bridges. All very lovely and peaceful.

Beautiful architectural wonder. Take a moment to look at all the little masonry details and designs of the building. Also check out all the stone creatures and people around the front door. The inside lobby is beautiful also but you can't get in there unless you were on a tour or you work in the building.

Small little park with lots of benches for sitting and munching of lunch. The curving flower beds make it seem bigger than it is, and add a lot of interest. The buildings around it are very attractive too. The park is dedicated to the British victims of 911.  And yes, the Queen was there to open it.

Nice little park. This was the main location of Occupy Wall Street. Some interesting sculptures. Trees lit up by strings of little lights from end of october to after Christmas. Check out the nearby restaurant where you eat in an old bank vault!! Food is good too

This is a small waterfall at the north east end of a beach.  When we were there at the end July the water flow was very low and it wasn't worth trying to find (it's not easily spotted from the beach). Locals say it is very pretty when there's more water flowing.

Awesome collection of artwork from all over the world and many ages. I particularly liked the collection of American art. Paintings, sculptures and decorative arts ( furniture, ceramics, etc). Strong in European and Egyptian art also.

This is a moving and very powerful Monument. The names of allthe  sailorsand  soldiers that died in the waters off the east coast during World War Two, are inscribed on the walls around a powerful eagle statue.
Pretty little park with benches, a water fountain (in season) and plantings. It is next to 7 World Trade Center, and just north of the new performing arts center that is being built.
Kind of dull, but make sure you go into the buildings. One has four scale models of the area at different eras and the many changes are very interesting.
Lovely little pond with model sailboats that can be rented.  Just a very peaceful,  pretty place. Just north is the Alice in Wonderland statue.
Small but interesting museum with models and paintings of ships.  Cost of ticket also includes tours of the historic ships at the piers.

We came here to check out the train display. My children loved looking at all of trains going around and pushing the buttons to make things move! There are several different rooms full of trains to look at. There's a large tree with tracks going up and down in it! There's even a train going around the ceiling!
Right outside of the train museum, there was a nice playground that was fenced in! My only complaint is that there's no sign directly in front of the building and where we parked, we couldn't see the train signs. We went into the historical museum and when asked about the trains, we were rudely informed that we were in the wrong area. I had never heard of this historical museum before, but after encountering this rude staff member, I can see why people might not want to recommend it to others.

This was our first visit to The Blowing Rock and I'm so glad we stopped here for a visit! It was $7 for each adult to get in. It was an easy walk around the whole area. Remember to bring quarters for the viewing machines! The views were amazing! There is a small snack and gift shop on the walking path. There is also a photo gallery that had a lot of information about the area! The main gift shop had a lot of neat little gifts! You could pick out a bag of rocks for $6, which was better than the $10/bag that I saw in a lot of shops in Boone!

This was our first time at the New Hope Valley Railway and my family loved it! We rode the train for Santa's Reindeer Roundup! There was an hour long train ride in an open air train car where we looked for different reindeer! During the ride, Santa came through and he sat down with each family and we were able to have some family pictures taken. I have been to many different train events and I thought this was priced very reasonably! This whole operation is run by volunteers, which I think is neat!

This was our first time here after it reopened and I was very pleased! It wasn't crowded and there were plenty of hands sanitizer stations throughout the outdoor area. I wish there were a few more water bottle refilling stations though, as all of the drinking fountains were closed and the vending machines weren't working. Even though only the outdoor area is open, there was still a lot to do! All of the water features were great on a hot day! We will definitely be back!

Very nice fishing pier! We came a little before closing just to walk out to the end for a few minutes and the person working just let us go out there for free, which was very nice and saved us from paying $3 per person! I've been on several fishing piers and this was one of the cleanest ones I've seen! There were lots of benches for fishermen. There are bathrooms at the start of the pier. The store had a variety of items, from snacks to decor items, for purchase.

We decided to check this place out with our kids and they loved it! Lots of different fun exhibits for all ages. Be ready to climb, because there are tunnels and slides that go from the top to the bottom of the building! There are several huge picnic tables outside that are in a shady spot, which was a great area to eat our picnic lunch! They have a room in the farm area for mothers to feed and change their baby, which I think is great!

I really wanted to get a close up view of the river, so after leaving the annex store, we headed down to this park. They have a nice paved walking trail that goes right by the river! They have plenty of benches to sit on and enjoy the view! They had little information plaques about a bunch of different trees, which was neat! There was also a nice playground area and an area with a bunch of play houses!

We were looking for a mini golf place and since it was freezing outside, I'm glad we found this indoor mini golf place! It cost just under $40 for 2 adults and 2 kids to play. It was kind of dark inside. My children didn't love the theme because it was a little scary, so they just wanted to hurry up and be done with it. Overall, it was nice to be inside but I'm not sure that we would go back.

This is a great place to take toddlers! We've been several times and mine love it! The zoo area is big enough to have some neat animals, but small enough to not be overwhelming for young children! My children love the indoor play areas! I like that they provide indoor and outdoor places for eating packed lunches. I would suggest getting there right when they open on holidays and weekends!

This is a great park for families! There's a nice picnic shelter and clean restrooms. There were several different types of play structures for children to play on. Most of the stuff here seemed to be geared for older children, but they do have slides, swings and a few other things for younger children. The little water area was closed for renovations, but hopefully it will open soon.

Great nature center for kids and families! We came here two days in a row, so we decided to purchase a membership, which was cheaper than paying for admission for 2 days! Most of the center was shaded, which was really nice. There are little play areas for kids spread throughout the park! The otter feeding program was neat and informative! Definitely glad we stopped here!

We were in the area with our kids and looking for a park, so we decided to stop here. I saw that it had a train display, which I knew my train loving boys would be excited about, but when we got there, it was locked up. We were only able to look at it from outside of the fence. That was kind of disappointing. The splash pad was a refreshing end to our walk though!

Very nice nature preserve! There is a parking lot a block from the entrance. The walking trails are child friendly! There are little info plaques that talk about the plants and animals in the nature preserve, which were fun to stop and read! It was nice to be able to walk out and see the intercoastal waterway and watch for dolphins and birds!

We came here for a group picnic and were very pleased with this park! The playground area is very large and has something for everyone from toddlers to older children. The train and carousel are also very fun and inexpensive! They offer an all day pass for the rides. This park also has one of the largest swimming pools in the area!

After learning about pirates and the ocean, I wanted to bring my children here! There were lots of neat things to see and read about! There were a few hands on things, but not many, due to covid-19. Definitely more things that would interest adults. They did have a huge whale skeleton and heart, which was cool!

One of the best children's museum I've been to! There's so much to do here! It really take almost a whole day to explore all of the exhibits. They have a nice Cafe here with plenty of seating. There's a parking deck across the street but this museum is also located within walking distance of the train station!

Just took my twin toddlers here for the first time and they loved it! We only visited Africa, because it took us about 4 hours to go through it all and by then, my boys were done! We got to feed the giraffes, which was so neat! We got there when they opened and parked right up front! Wasn't too crowded either!

This railroad museum is one of the best that I've been to! Lots of different interactive activities, even during covid. There was a caboose, steam engine and boxcar that we were able to go in! The whole back of the museum is a model train layout with several different gauge engines. We will definitely be back!

Nice little park to visit. There are several different playgrounds geared to different age groups. This  park has a variety of things to do including a volleyball court, walking and nature trails, and a disc golf course. There are also several picnic shelters that are available for rent.

This was a nice place to visit with our kids! Very quiet and peaceful! There was an easy walking trail next to the visitors center that went down to a viewing area and then back up to the parking lot. We were disappointed that the visitor's center is currently closed due to covid-19.

This is a great park to take children to for the day! There is a lot to do here! We played at the playground, had a picnic under one of the picnic shelters, took a walk to the waterfall and then saw a bunch of animals on the homestead area!

What a great place for children of all ages! There are so many neat things to do here! I thought the price was very reasonable. While only drinks are available for purchase, there's an area outside where you can eat a picnic lunch.
Nice pier to walk out on and look at the beach and the ocean! Lots of people fishing! There was a little area that sold food and ice cream. Cost $1 per person to walk out on the pier.
A really nice park not too far from the beach! There is a playground for little kids and then down the hill, there's a playground for bigger kids! There is also a nice walking path.
This tubing was so much fun! I came here with a bachelorette group and we all LOVED it! I'm so glad we paid for the hour ride! The staff was so fun and helpful!

We spent the day here, and it was beautiful! We did the Empire Bluff hike, which was challenging and spectacular. We saw people climbing the dunes. We had a picnic lunch at the old historic village. We checked out the beach, which was gorgeous. We went out on a boardwalk. We did the Pierce Stocking Scenic Drive, which had many beautiful places to get out and enjoy views or hike. Sometimes it gets windy and you have to watch out for getting sand in your face, but otherwise it was the perfect day!

This park is well-worth the two-dollar entrance fee. There are a lot of pavilions and picnic tables for eating lunch. There is a big playground with good equipment for children. There are some basketball hoops. I think there is boat access for people to go on the river. But the best part is the beautiful trail which goes along the river. It is very well maintained, and the view is scenic!

We camped here for three nights, and this campground is really nice! The bathrooms and showers are clean. There is a large, new playground with lots of fun things for children to play on. The fort buildings are highly informative of what fort life was like. The campsites are large, and the campground sits on a nice body of water. We really enjoyed our stay! The only downside was no beach.

This is such an amazing scenic drive! We had to wait for it to open until 4:00 on a Friday, and it was totally worth it. There are many stops where you can read information about the dunes, get out to view the gorgeous scenery, and go for some hiking. Don't skip the last stop!
