It is the most scenic and breath-taking overview you will see all day.

This is an AMAZING hike!!! It is a little challenging, but not terribly difficult. There are a few spots to stop and enjoy breath-taking views of the dunes. Once you get to the end of the trail, there is a wide open space to rest and enjoy the view of Lake Michigan. Totally worth the effort!

This is a beautiful state park along the lake. The beaches are gorgeous. There are plenty of fun hiking trails, but the sign does say to watch out for bears. We saw people fishing and kayaking, too. This is a kid-friendly park. Lovely scenery to see. Watch out for racoon families!

This is a really great park. There are lots of trees, so the paths are well shaded. There are many different paths from which to choose. There were quite a few people when we went, but it was not crowded at all. It is very quiet and peaceful. Also, there are tons of geocaches.

We went here on a week day, and it was very quiet and pleasant. The beach area is beautiful. The camp sites seem to be a decent size. There are some well-kept paths with geocaches. There is a bridge going above the road to take you from one side of the park to the other.

This state forest encompasses a huge area of land in the UP, and there are tons are camping parks, trails, lakes, etc. It is beautiful. There are so many sights to see; if you like nature, you could probably spend at least a week here seeing places and hiking.

This is a beautiful inland state park! There is a playground, a pavilion where we had a picnic lunch, and a nice sized beach area. The campground seems nice and quiet, and there are trails across the road for hiking. Might be a nice place to camp!

We were camping sort of close by and decided to come here for an afternoon. Not only are the historical buildings interesting to view and read about, but the water sights are superb. It was a very lovely afternoon.

This is a really neat state park near a music conservatory. There is camping and a day use area. The beach is on an inland lake, and the playground is good-sized. We were here for the Michigan state parks geotour.

What a beautiful park! Both the upper and lower falls are beautiful sights to see, and there are spots to get in the water in the lower falls, which is quite fun. A gorgeous destination with great hikes.
We have been here a couple times searching for geocaches, and we have hiking a few of the paths. This is an awesome park, and they have information areas set up so you can learn about the park, too!
We were here for the 100 years of state parks geocaching tour, and that part was nice, but there was a needle in one of the bathroom stalls, so that was a little scary.
This is a really cool place! The road to get there and back is incredibly scenic, and the walking trail is awesome. We were here in the fall, beautiful colors.
This park has a neat historical area with lots of old buildings to learn about. There are parts of old towers people used to use to watch out for forest fires.
This is a cool state park! The water is fun colored, the ice cream from the store is yummy, and the ride on the raft was a good time. We will be back!
This is a good park for families. You can fish, there is a playground, and it connects to the Riverwalk. There is also a large, grassy field.
This is a nice nature preserve! The spot we were at had a little pond, a pavilion, and a picnic table. We did some geocaching here.
This is an extremely scenic state park! We enjoyed the view while we geocached for the 100 years of Michigan state parks geotour.
It was very foggy the day we stopped here, but I would imagine on a clear day the view of the lake would be quite beautiful.
It is not extremely scenic, but there are some nice paths on which to take walks. The paths are quiet not very busy.
We were here for the Michigan State Parks Geotour. This park has yurts! It might be fun to stay here sometime.
This is a neat park! It has a great playground for children, and there is a boardwalk by a lake.

Tawas Point State Park is a must-visit. We stayed for one night during the off-season, and got a prime spot right on the bay next to the campground beach.

The campground beach is very small, but it's ok for the kids to play, or to watch the sunset. The larger day-use beach is on the Lake Huron side, but be aware of the changing conditions of the water levels and rip currents. At the day-use beach you can find a concession stand with a deck/seating area overlooking Lake Huron.

The campground is wide open, with no privacy between sites. Sites are all grassy, except for a few paved handicap accessible sites. In peak season you will be cramped in with lots of neighbors! Just make friends and share some s'mores! The bathhouses are newer. Some have environmentally-friendly nozzles (in other words, navy showers!), while others are regular. A nice feature is a large industrial sink on the outside of the bathhouse to do dishes in.

Make sure to visit the lighthouse and go inside for a tour to learn the history of Tawas and the park. Admission varies by the season and day - peak season is a set price, off-season tends to be a donation. Be sure to climb the tower for an awesome view of Tawas Point and the surrounding water.

Palms Book State Park is Kitch-iti-Kipi spring. For all practical purposes they are synonymous. There is nothing else at the park except amenities (gift shop, rest rooms) related to the spring. Camping is down the road at Indian Lake S.P.

That said, the spring is one of the coolest natural resources in Michigan. It is worth it if you are anywhere near the area at all. The spring is crystal clear and stocked with various fish that can be seen all the way to the bottom. There is a large covered observation raft that runs on wires out over the spring. This means the viewing conditions are good in all weather. Park staff on the raft also keep the raft not-too-full so there is room to walk around and see the spring from different angles. They must dive periodically too to clean it out because for all of the people leaning over to take pictures I didn't see a single dropped phone, sunglasses, or litter at all.

Fun hike in the woods that lead to the sand dunes. There’s a trail that will take you right down to the lake. It’s fairly flat and improved surface so most people can take advantage of this access to see the lake and dunes. I chose the trails through the woods and adventures on some of the non-marked trails that are in the network. These lead to the tops of the dunes where you can get a great view of the lake and dune ecosystem from above. Then there’s a trail that will lead you down the sand dunes out through the grassy area right to the water. Be sure to wear proper footwear for this hike as you have dirt, sand, mud, water and more to work through

A picturesque little dune landscape at the shore of Lake Michigan. As its name implies, this park contains Silver Beach, which was ranked among the top beaches in the country for families a few years ago. I visited in the off-season (late September), which meant that the amusement park, beachside restaurant, and other amenities were closed. The beach itself seemed to be a nice spot for swimming and sunbathing, and I really liked the cement sidewalk path through the dunes that leads out to the pier. It’s nice to think that even a person with limited mobility would be able to get out into a beach environment and appreciate the beach grass up close.

We arrived in the later afternoon - the traffic was really a lot. Very popular park/beach. We paid the out of state - $20 parking fee per car. - Park/Beach is worth the fee to visit. There is a significant amount of parking but It fills up fast. Once you have parked - you cross over the park area to get to the beach - not a long walk. The beach is wide and long enough that you are not on top of each other. It appears many people set up in the park and walk to the sand. A great sand shelf allows you to sit in a tube and not move very far from where you start. Great relaxing setting in a nice place.

This was the second time I'd visited and I was not disappointed. It's so cool to be around the butterflys in their element just flying around. I could have stayed for a long time (but sadly could not). They had a good number of butterflys in the butterfly area. There was a bench to seat so you could relax and enjoy the butterflys (just had to make sure not to sit on any). The insects were also a cool addition to this visit. I believe there are 2 butterfly houses on the island, but this one is me and my husbands favorite one.

We started to climb the sand hill. The trail was the center marked with the blue stick. Since we claimed the hill on the left, we took a longer course. It supposed to be 1.75 mile each way, but we walked 2.5 miles in 90 degree. We had plenty of water. We are physically fit and spent a little more than two hours for round trip.
Once we cross the half way, the trail was well marked and easy to follow. We had to stop and took our sands from our running shoes. Lake Michigan was beautiful and very private.

I absolutely love this State Park. The beach is beautiful and the water generally cool and relatively clear. I highly recommend taking a hike up to Big Sable Lighthouse. My suggestion would be to take the service road one way and the beach the other way. A long walk on the sand can be a very long walk indeed, and I would not suggest taking toddlers. 2-3 hour visit if you'e doing only the lighthouse, longer if you are going to swim. I have been here many times and cannot wait to return.

This is a bit out of the way, but well worth the visit. There is a wonderful Visitor Center situated on one of the ponds for wildlife viewing, and an auto drive route around several of the other impoundments. When I was there I saw Trumpeter Swans, Loons, Canada Geese, Sandhill Cranes and a myriad of other waterfowl and birds. There are also a variety of mammals living on the Wildlife Refuge, but I did not see any that day. It is free to get in, and well worth taking the time to stop.

Turn off Hwy 41 on Second Street and follow the aging signs to the Nature Sanctuary. On the day we went there was plenty of parking, but I can see how it could get crowded. The trail was moderate on the Cathedral Loop that we did, including finding a Native American copper mining pit hidden among the trees. Lots of ups and downs, we went a day after a rain storm and the trails were dry enough or there are paving stones and board walks. Don't miss it.

This beach/park is absolutely gorgeous! Very clean and well kept. There is a separate area area at the top with shade trees, grills and picnic tables for a get together. There is plenty of beach for all to enjoy. The views are absolutely amazing! Plenty of parking and there is a pavilion with a snack bar and indoor bathrooms and changing area as well. For only 10 bucks for the day it seemed like a steal for how much of a good time I had.

Situated on the East end of Little Traverse bay, the Petoskey State Park is one of the most amazing beachfront areas in the Great Lakes. It's like a smaller version of Holland State Park. Miles of sandy beach, amazing water, a really nice concession stand, the ability to bring your own picnic and beverages - just wow. We visit at least a few times a summer to "get away" from it all because it is so relaxing. Highly recommend! 5 stars

We took the carriage ride through the park; at this point in our lives, riding is much more comfortable than walking/hiking, especially for long distances.
The ride was leisurely; and our driver/narrator provided a wealth of information (and humor). The story of the Post cemetery was particularly poignant.
This is wonderful place to explore, experience, and enjoy a walk (or ride) back in time.

Clean area, felt very safe. There is limited parking at the Beach side park (50 cars) (Not suitable for larger RVs and large trucks). If you are using the beach area, it is sandy and water shoes work the best or old tennis shoes. The boardwalk is handicap accessible and stairs to the beach. Great for getting your stroller and little one to the beach, , , but stroller not usable on sandy beach.

This was a nice quiet reprieve after coming from Mackinac Island. We could leisurely stroll around the village to explore the old buildings. Lots of photo opportunities. We had a state park sticker on our car, so it did not cost us a thing. This is the second time we have been there and will probably go back again with a picnic lunch to enjoy a relaxing atmosphere.

Although it had been several years since I last visited the KNC, many things remained familiar. Its "Tropical Sun/Rain Room" was still well maintained with live birds flying about. We chose a series of the center's linked outdoor nature trails to enjoy the grounds. All had been decently maintained, and provided a momentary retreat into the ground's natural beauty.

This place is great to bring friends and family and it is nice all seasons too I believe. In the summer it isn’t too busy, in the fall it has great colors, in the winter you can see the lake freezing over and in the spring it is nice and great. The views are great and the hike is fun. I feel like people don’t know about this place which is nice

Beautiful garden and natural area in Ann Arbor. We took a very long walk along the lovely nature trails; through forests, by streams and lakes, really fun. It was a warm sunny fall day when we visited but there was plenty of shade along the trails. Impressive botanical garden inside too. Great place to spend a couple hours out in nature.

There is a constant stream of traffic driving around/thru this park adjacent to Lake Michigan. Many trees, picnic tables, benches, and a war memorial honoring veterans. They also have a sandy beach, a rest room building and concession stand. This is where you can access the Ludington North Breakwater Light.

We visited a waterfall while at Porcupine Mountains Wilderness State Park and then drove across the park and stayed in one of the campgrounds. WORTH IT. We drove 6 hours to this destination and well worth it. My friend and I want to go back just to camp on the lake. Beautiful sunsets, great wilderness.

This is my favorite time of year to drive around up north. We pull into State Campgrounds, pick out our spot then self register. It is very easy and you can get the best spots. Had good weather, great campfire and went to Mulligans in Cheboygon for dinner, very good.

I showed up in the early morning hours and it was absolutely quiet and peaceful. I enjoyed watching a family of swans as well as walking through various habitats. No bikes allowed on the island though bike rentals are available in the parking lot for other trails.
dislikes: No bikes allowed on the island

reviews_attraction.text: The falls are beautiful! Both Upper and Lower. They can both be viewed by a short walk. Wheelchairs are available for use if needed. The park and bathrooms are very clean. The giftshop is recommending mask use. Pets are welcome on a 6 foot leash.

There are miles of gorgeous views walking through this park. The gardens are exploding with color! There is a neat miniature village with train and even venues for weddings. Recently went for the first time and I was not disappointed!

Beautiful views of Lake Superior! I found it relaxing & took many pictures. We tried hiking but the mosquitoes were too much for the kids. I definitely recommend stopping here if you’re visiting Marquette!

A multi-purpose park. One outhouse that is fairly well taken care of as long as others doing their business do it cleanly. In the west you will find a small parking lot and a large baseball field which eventually slopes down toward a basketball court. In the middle a playground is available year round for all ages. They have a handicapped chair but like many other playgrounds in the area it is not handicap accessible. There is a city owned building with covered picnic tables next to the playground with a grill that has yet to see use. Moving towards the east we have a hockey rink and then some tennis courts. A parking lot in need of repair is to the northeast. A bit east and south are soccer fields. This is a beautiful area for a walk on the paved trail though some of it is in bad need of repair.
dislikes: Parking lot in need of repair
Paved trail in bad need of repair

reviews_attraction.text:
A backwoods playground. An after thought in an older park area. Materials of plastic and metal, not ideal for hot days. If it's buggy avoid like the plague as it is located 10 ft from a swamp. All sand, perfect for your zen moment.  Has a handicapped accessible swing with a paved path leading from the parking lot.

The main park area is a bit rundown and doesn't seem to see much use. BUT! The walking path is wonderful!! I won't spoil anything so go walk it yourself. You'll be done in less then 10 minutes.

Rating only for the playground. In a nice residential area very close to the highway but not close enough to be worrisome. Also close to a lake, more like a pond, but it's surrounded by a lot of vegetation so no worries on the kids running towards it. Typical play groubd with slides monkey bars swings a rock climbing wall and some other  features found in many of the parks around here.

I'll makes a new and old playground equipment but the old equipment is still in pretty darn good shape. Great for toddlers that are sure footed to about 10 years. They have a brand new bball court alongside a gorgeous wooden pavilion. Also has a wading pool, soccer field, a few bbq grills, a baseball field and a sad looking sand volleyball court. Plenty of space to walk your dog

Great playground! Areas for all ages. They have a handicap swing but no handicap access to it. A few swings and baby swing. The big slides are a bit fast so watch your tiniest ones. Take your kids for a walk before playing on the playground or they may be too tired to walk or sit I  the stroller. It's a wonderful walk with a great view at the other end of the lake.
dislikes: Slides too fast for young children

reviews_attraction.text: This park is mainly known for its hiking trails and for the art house that is located on it but more recently they have added the city of Eagan Nature Park. This wonderful extension of the Patrick Eagan Park is a wonderful way to get your kids playing more with nature and discovering things that maybe they didn't see before. It also has a really cool zip line.

Holy duck moley!! There were a good number when we came in the summer but apparently the winter is where it's at if you are sighting ducks. You can bring feed bit do not bring bread! The paved walking paths are nice and the playground is great for those who are on a trip and need to let the kids run a bit. Also get some history by checking out the helicopter.

Very nice playground with many different features. Like a rock wall and a pull bouncer, come see what I mean for yourself that sounds weird. Also has swings though the handicap swing is not handicap accessible. Plenty of picnic space and one Grill next to a trash and recycling bin. They have a porta potty a basketball court and soccer field / baseball field.

The animal diversity at this zoo is amazing. The exhibits are great and you can really tell they are very aware of what is needed to properly care for their animals. They are expanding and remodeling in different areas but nothing too large to ruin any enjoyment. Become a member if you live close. It's worth it. Especially if you have little ones.

A great place for all ages. They have an activity center that is great for toddlers up to school age children. And for the older kids they have good educational activities. Even adults will find educational tidbits. The bathrooms are nicely kept and the larger stall has a changing table. It's a great place to come and relax with a book.

The dinosaurs have seen better days but the kids will still have fun. This is not a suitable activity for those who can't climb stairs, also the pavement is uneven so please watch your step. If you don't come for the dinosaurs, come for the view. Also stop in the gift shop. They are very kind and have an assortment of things.

What a great playground! If you have kids 7 and under they are going to have an awesome time here. If you have kids under 3 they have a wonderful area for them. Probably the best toddler playground I've seen yet. They have a handicapped swing but it's not handicap accessible. Also have covered picnic benches.

Not your usual playground. Best for ages 2 and up but the main structure seems to be better suited for those over 4. Challenge your kids to see if they can go through the set without touching the ground. There's a port a potty, covered picnic benches, trash & recycling, and two grills.

Why do people ruin things with graffiti? It's all over this park. Besides that this is a good park to walk around. Has paved walking trails for those who are less mobile and a variety of off trail routes that range from medium to difficult. Please bring your trash back out with you.

A fun playground for those over 2. Those who are under 2 need to be supervised carefully due to some of the unique structures apart of the playground. There is a parking lot nearby but it seems ok to park on the street closer to the playground if that's the only place you'll be.

An impressive park. Mini golf, zip line,  zip line swing for handicapped or others but please let handicapped go first, various other playground equipment, batting cages, baseball fields. All nicely maintained. Oh and a small library. They've something for everyone.

Rated mainly for the playground located close to the fire station. Fire truck themed with a fire truck at the front of the playground. Lots of features like swings, a excavator, slides, spinning monkey bars, and lots of sand. Bring your toy trucks for extra fun.

A perfect place to spend a hot day. Get cooled off in the splash pad and then warm up on the playground. Best for above 3 but doable for younger with constant supervision. There is a pavilion and public bathrooms. Please be sure to pick up after yourself.

This is a nice little area to traverse. It has become a lot more popular though and can become quite busy depending on the time you go. Do not miss the waterfall or the hike on the new boardwalk they created from recycled something.

This is a playground built for kids who are agile and who love to explore. Not good for those under two or kids who aren't sure footed. There is a paved trail to walk down and plenty of grass to run around on.

Rated five stars for the playground. Awesome play structure for all ages. A swing for handicapped. Restrooms nearby. Lots of swings. Your kids will have tons of fun. So much fun they won't want to leave...
Rated for the playground. They have one for 2.5 and up and a separate one for those who are younger or less athletic. No handicapped accessible gear. Watch your bags as the ants are abundant.
Great area for the kids to run off some energy. Playground great for 2 and over or those who are sure footed. The splash pad has a nice covered shelter and plenty of picnic tables.
Great water feature to cool off in. Safe for all ages but can be slippery on some of the rocks so please tell your kids to walk.
What a treasure! Portage areas. Built in bag toss. Huge playground. Nice restrooms. And a long but not too long walking path.

Don't expect this to be a "regular" park; it's not.  This is not where you go to toss around a frisbee.  The I-5 Colonnade is a place to be thoughtful and appreciate a different perspective.  To most, I-5 is just a fact of life, a part of the daily commute, but from beneath it feels grander, almost monumental.  Listen to the cars going past above and remember that this road was part of one of the largest construction projects in world history.  Think about the fact that it goes all the way from tiny border town Blaine, WA in the north to San Diego in the south.  And, most importantly, appreciate the fact that if you're underneath I-5, that means that you're not driving on it!

Very nice little museum.  Good place to learn about one of the most important events in early Seattle history.  I played the computer game Yukon Trail a lot as a kid, so I thought it was pretty cool to find out more about the real life experiences of people heading north back then.  It's not the kind of place where you'd plan a whole trip just to go there, but if you're in the area anyway (Pioneer Square, International District, football/baseball/soccer game), I definitely recommend stopping by.

Seattle has a truly stunning skyline.  If you want to see it all, including the Space Needle, and Mt. Rainier (and for free, to boot!) then you'll be hard-pressed to find a better spot than Kerry Park.

We hiked up there from the Seattle Center, which took 15-20 minutes. If we had to do it again, we would probably drive--Queen Anne Hill was steeper than we were expecting.  But the fact that it's located so close to an area that has a lot of other stuff to see is pretty nice.

This is a really cool museum. It looks small from the outside, but they have a lot of information packed into not that much space. And it's important information. It's stories and people that we all too often tend to forget. It's an aspect of Cincinnati history that I had never really considered before. Plus the location just by the river is incredibly scenic. Take a walk across the bridge afterward! Think about what that journey could have been like 160 years ago.

My favorite park in Seattle.  As soon as you enter, you're surrounded by trees, and it really feels like you're no longer in the city.  There are some great trails, and the views from Magnolia Bluff are great, but the best spot is the West Point Lighthouse way out at the western end along the Sound.  The parking there is rough, but you shouldn't be driving down there anyway unless you have no choice.  Take a walk--you'll enjoy it.

It's less than 2 hours' drive from Seattle, and there really aren't very many national parks that are that close to a major metropolitan area, so you should really take advantage of it if you're in the area.  Mt. Rainier is a stunningly picturesque mountain, but the park is not just about the summit.  There are plenty of waterfalls to see on the way up, and interesting hot springs history at Longmire.

It's not perfect.  Depending on when you go, you might be stuck in a line for quite a while--maybe half an hour or more.  And let's be honest, now that it's no longer the tallest building in the world, not even the tallest building in the U.S., a certain amount of cool factor is lost.  But it's still a spectacular view of Chicago, and Chicago's one of the most view-worthy cities I know.

Best art museum in the state of Ohio.  It has an extensive collection that you could easily spend multiple days looking at.  The special exhibits are also usually good--we saw a very nice one on paintings of gardens (lots of Monet, of course).  But the coolest part is the building itself--the way they built the newer portion around the original building is very visually impressive.

My second favorite aviation museum (the first being the Air Force Museum in Dayton, OH).  There's a good collection of planes in the main building, but the best part is definitely what they have in the open-air hangar across the street.  You can go in a former Air Force One (that Nixon flew to China!) and a Concorde, plus a few standard Boeing airliners.  Very cool experience.

I like this park.  It has easy, shady hiking trails, some nice waterfalls to check out, and it's a pretty convenient location.  It's just . . . it doesn't feel like a national park to me.  Every other national park I've been to has something--something remarkable, something unique, something stunningly memorable.  Cuyahoga Valley has nothing like that.  It's just a nice park.

Excellent "off the beaten path" Seattle destination.  It's free, which is awesome, and the neighborhood where it's located (First Hill) is a nice place to walk around as well.  Most of the traditional art (which is more my thing) is concentrated into one room, but it's a very impressive room.  You could spend a couple hours in there and still not fully appreciate all of it.

Excellent small park at the south end of Lake Union.  One of the best places to enjoy Seattle in the summer (and it's not terrible in other seasons, either).  Gas Works Park in the north has the better views, but Lake Union Park makes up for it with the Museum of History and Industry and all the historic boats.  Plus it's a lot easier to get to on public transit.

One of my all-time favorite museums.  If you have any interest in aviation or U.S. military history, this is a must-visit if you are traveling to Dayton, Columbus, or Cincinnati (or maybe even Indianapolis, though it's more than an hour away from there).  There is easily enough in here to occupy an entire day, and the exhibits are very well put together.

One thing I love about Seattle is its collection of spots that fall under the heading, "I don't know why this exists, but I'm glad that it does, because I think it's hilarious."  The Gum Wall is probably the most representative of this category.  Tell your friends about it and watch the looks on their faces as they say, "You're taking me to see WHAT?"

Very interesting stop near Seattle Center.  It's free, so you might as well head on in if you're in the area.  The exhibits are very well put together, and they fit a lot of information in a relatively small area.  Everything is very thought-provoking, and it lets you know both what has been already done and what you can do in the future.

A small museum with a very nice collection.  We visited over the holidays, and they had an excellent exhibit on Christmas in the Soviet Union that was fascinating from both and artistic and a cultural perspective.  There was also some artwork on mushrooms that I thought was cool and quirky.  Plus the building itself is pretty cool.

Very well done museum.  The subject matter may not sound like the most exciting thing in the world, but there's a lot of interesting information in there, and it really connects with the history of the city.  Plus the location right by the river and the Stone Arch Bridge makes for gorgeous views from the observation deck up top.

Not a bad ride.  It's conveniently located near Pike Place, so if you're there already, think about stopping by.  Personally, if I want a view of the waterfront, I'd rather take the Bainbridge Ferry or go to the Sky View at Columbia Center, but if you don't have that much time, the Wheel is a faster option.

The best place to see Seattle from above.  It's taller than the Space Needle and significantly cheaper.  It's also never been crowded when I've gone.  You get a magnificent view of Elliott Bay and South Lake Union, and on clear days you can see the Olympics and Mt. Rainier.

An interesting idea, but going to see it in person was a little underwhelming.  Stop by if you're in the area, but if your time is short, there's other stuff in Fremont that's more interesting.  If you want your picture taken with it, you will probably have to wait.

A smaller art museum, but not a bad one.  I especially liked their African and Native American collections.  It's not going to match up to the big-time art museums in places like New York or Chicago, but it's certainly worth a visit.
Sky View is awesome. Best place for high-elevation views in Seattle. That is, however, literally the only thing in this building I have used, so I can't comment on anything else.
I usually think these tourist-trapy obvious photo op spots aren't worth it, but I actually like this one.  More fun than it seems at first glance.
Nice, but not as cool as Narada Falls.  Good stopping spot if you don't have the time or energy to do the full Skyline Trail.
Seems like it would be a nice place to hang out if it wasn’t raining like the day we were there.

This place is bigger than I thought it would be and there is a lot to see. The first thing we saw was the river otters. They were so fun and adorable! I loved watching them swim upside down. We wanted to feed the penguins but you have to sign up for that weeks in advance. The place seemed more like a zoo than an aquarium as we also got to see leopards and a sloth. There is a section where you can touch the sting rays, and you can feel the shock of an electric eel. The 3D movie was not great, you could barely tell it was 3D. Also, the shark reef was underwhelming; the coolest thing in the shark reef was a giant sting ray that was bigger than most of the sharks. My biggest annoyance when I was there was that there were more little kids there than adults; they could easily take over. It’s frustrating to pay $40 for an afternoon date and not be able to see anything because of all the kids. They should really think about dedicating a certain time each week just for adults.
Overall it was a fun experience. There is a lot to see. I’d like to come again to participate in the penguin experience.
likes: Interactive experiences (touching sting rays, feeling electric eel)
Variety of species (river otters, penguins, leopards, sloth)

reviews_attraction.text: I’d never heard of this place. We drove from Utah to see Crater Lake last October 2018, and Crater Lake was foggy and it started snowing on us. We were disappointed in our visit, especially having come a long way. The locals told us to check out the Natural Bridge before heading to California so we wouldn’t leave disappointed. It’s not far from the hotel near the Crater Lake National Park, so we planned to make a quick stop. It’s hard to describe, and even with the locals description, we didn’t know what to expect. It’s the Rogue River, but at a certain point, the river disappears under ground and shoots out again a few yards later, causing a Natural Bridge (you aren’t allowed to walk on it, apparently people in the past have disappeared along with the water!) It was pretty darn impressive, and we stayed longer than we originally planned. We loved it! I hope to see it again!

This was 4-5 miles round trip, depending on how much of the Trail of the Cedars loop you do. It wasn’t too difficult, and it was BEAUTIFUL. The lake at the end of the trail has 3 waterfalls feeding into it. It was one of our favorite places we saw in the whole west side of the park.
The trail was closed shortly after we started on it due to bear activity- a woman we saw hiking back with a ranger had been attacked by a bear at the lake (but story goes that she was approaching the bear while others were backing away). The bear left her alone after she dropped her backpack and the bear shredded the backpack to pieces.
We never saw the bear, it had left the area before we got to the lake. It was so beautiful and we feel very grateful that we got to see it before the trail was closed.

Beautiful waterfall! There are several ways to get there (longer hike from Sun Point or the Sunrift Gorge, or the St. Mary’s Trailhead or shuttle stop if the shuttles are running).
It was a popular spot, and the day was HOT, and lots of people were jumping into the water.
The water is from glaciers, so it is clean and COLD. It felt great to jump in on a hot day. When people jump in, they say it is “fresh” when they really mean “freezing balls cold.”
It is the coldest water I’ve ever felt in my life, but we felt refreshed and clean afterwards. We actually jumped in at the Redrocks area, not at St. Mary’s Falls.

We stopped here on our road trip up the Oregon coast. There are shops and restaurants and a Ripleys, but I didn’t find any of that stuff appealing enough to spend time in. What I loved was all the sea lions basking in the sun and barking at each other. We watched them for probably a good half hour because they were so funny! They’d jump back in the water occasionally and another sea lion would take its place on the platforms, and then the other sea lion would come back and be upset that its place was taken. So entertaining to watch! I could’ve stayed longer!

Lots of fun! If you’re driving along the Oregon Coast, this is a must-do!  It’s a column in Astoria that you get to climb up several flights of stairs to the top. The view from the top is amazing. It overlooks the bridge and river that connect Oregon to Washington. On a nice day, it’s a very satisfying experience. Go to the gift shop BEFORE you climb the stairs as you can purchase little airplanes to throw off the top of the column. We learned that the hard way by visiting the gift shop after the climb.

While visiting family in Portland, we did what is called the 4T (trail, train, tram, trolley) through Portland. It’s a fun way to experience Portland in a day. The trail portion takes you to Council Crest Park. It’s a beautiful and well kept park with an area to sit and appreciate the view. You can see all the major mountains in this area (Mount St Helens, Mount Rainier, Mount Hood, and Mount Adams). It’s beautiful and well worth the hike!

Beautiful stroll that people of all ages and skill levels can enjoy. It is a wooden path that can accommodate strollers or wheelchairs. The cedar trees are big and beautiful and smell amazing. The scent of cedar was thick in the air. It was lush and dense and it reminded me and my husband of some of the trails we enjoyed at the Redwoods National Park (just with smaller trees). You can also hike to Avalanche Lake from this trail.

I’ve been here three different times on three different Vegas trips, and it’s definitely worth the admission price. It is located at the very end of the strip, so it is a trip to get there. You travel through tunnels made of glass and you can see a variety of fish, turtles, and sharks. You can also touch the stingrays, which is always fun. You can go at your own pace, so you can go through quickly or take your time. It’s great!

Amazing. We were able to see about five shows during our Vegas trip. Uptown Funk, Ecstasy of Gold, My Heart Will Go On, Con te Partiro, and Bad Romance. Our favorites were Con te Partiro and Ecstasy of Gold. We saw Bad Romance from above at the Eiffel Tower viewing deck. It was fun to see from a different angle. But up close while you can hear the music is the best. The music and water show make you FEEL. Amazing.

Fun and romantic! We were in Vegas celebrating our five year anniversary. We shared the gondola with another couple. Our gondolier was Lina, who is actually from Italy. She sang us 3 love songs, including the love spaghetti song from Lady and the Tramp. She had a beautiful voice, and it really added to the experience. It was maybe a 15- minute trip around the pool and under the bridge. Great experience!

This place was interesting and fun. It’s good for a 45-60 minute visit. There is a fee to get in which we didn’t have to pay because we have a National Park pass. Without the pass, it may not have been worth the entrance fee, but it was really interesting to see the temporary home Lewis and Clark built on their expedition. This place made me feel interested in their travels and want to learn more.

This is a fun little gem smack dab in the middle of busy downtown SLC. It offers a peaceful place for quiet contemplation in the middle of chaos. The sculptures are interesting and unlike anything anywhere else. There are fun pathways to walk on and everything about it was free. Free entry and a free guide to explain the significance of the sculptures.

We drove this road from Canyonlands all the way through Potash and to Moab. It took about two hours, and we were driving a Chevy Silverado with 4WD. It was pretty steep and sketchy at some points, but definitely not a dangerous road. It was beautiful and had an awesome view of Dead Horse Point. We’ll definitely do it again!

Very unique experience. It’s an hour and a half well spent! The drumming sessions are so fun to watch, especially with the paint. Who knew drumming on pipes could be so cool? They engage the audience by walking on the chairs and hucking marshmallows at you. Such a fun and unique experience, I’d love to come again!

This is the spot people think of when you think of the Oregon coast, and it’s even more famous because of Goonies. For all the hype, I wasn’t super impressed. We weren’t allowed to climb the rock, which I was really excited to do. It’s a nice beach and it’s fun to look at, but it doesn’t measure up to the hype.

It’s a quick trip around the museum. There’s a statue of Will Smith sitting in one spot and I really thought someone was sitting there. The statues are kind of creepy. I got to swing on a wrecking ball like Miley Cyrus, which was my favorite part. Staff was nice. It’s not necessarily worth the entrance fee.

This is one of the best free shows you’ll ever see! Fire and lights flare and it’s so much fire that you can feel the heat on your face. It’s exciting to watch, and it’s right in the middle of the strip. It only goes off three times per day, and it’ll be totally worth your time to squeeze it in!

This is a beautiful and short (2 mile) loop. It was an easy stroll with beautiful scenery. One side of the loop is in the beautiful trees, and the other side is next to MacDonald Falls.
This was a nice and relaxing stroll. Perfect for kids- we were carrying our 8-month-old baby.

This is a 3-mile round trip hike which I did with a 6-month old baby on my back. The first mile is a pretty rough uphill climb, but the last 1/2 mile isn’t bad. It’s a fun hike with interesting desert landscape. And of course the destination is amazing!

This was a great family hike! Not too long and not too short. 2 miles round trip. I did it with a 6-month old baby on my back. It was pretty windy, but very nice other than that.
The destination is stunning! It was my favorite hike in Canyonlands!

This was one of our favorite stops along the Oregon coast. We were planning to make a quick stop but we ended up staying close to an hour. The crashing waves were mesmerizing. On a nice day with a high enough tide, this stop is amazing!
Really fun quick stop! The plants are unique, I’m not sure where else you can see them. It is small; you can be satisfied with your visit after ten minutes, but it’s ten minutes worth taking!
Big field, lots of parking, pavilions for picnics, and a free disc golf course. Great place to take your dogs for a walk!
Definitely an underrated park. It was our last Utah National Park to visit and we loved it! We’ll definitely come again!

This is a great little hidden park right around the Hillsboro area! I didn't even know it was here for years and years and I have lived here for a long time. They have awesome parks where you can hang out at with your dogs. May have Trails you can walk all around and even a kayak and canoe boat launch, that you can float the Tualatin Hills River 4 hours and hours. There is destinations where you can drop off a second vehicle and pick up your boat. But the boat launch at Eagle Creek I believe it's called is a hard one and it it's a lot of work. But the two-hour float is wonderful. Very relaxing and the current isn't strong at all so if you were to float there you could definitely paddle all the way back if you only had one vehicle

I only love going to McMenamins for the atmosphere and the fire pits outside. The beer and their cocktails are way overpriced. Best just to stick with one beer and one cocktail and maybe buy a fifth of whatever they are selling. You're not supposed to pour it yourself but it's like whatever. The food is not really good. But you can't go wrong with the hummus platter and cajun tater tots. Best thing on their menu that I have had. The staff are okay, they're not anything special more like they're on autopilot and just there to work and get it over with. They're not very social and they don't seem very personable. This isn't the place to hang out alone unless you are outside by the fire pits.

This is a really cool place to get a tour around Halloween but make sure you go during the week day and not on the weekend. Because it goes right underneath the bars and it's not really scary when you hear the Spice Girls above you LOL. The guide was really nice and he tried to get everybody in the scary mood which I liked. Get your tickets on Groupon and save yourself some extra money. It's fun but it's only worth going to once. It's better to do some research before you go so you can get a better idea of what the Shanghai Tunnels were really before.

One of my favorite Lakes I like to go to all year around. They didn't raise the price for parking it is now $7 but it is still worth it. I believe you can get a year pass for $30. This park is pretty well maintained. I've never had a problem with anyone breaking into my car or causing any problems. There is a trail that goes around the lake, not sure if it goes all the way around but I've been on it a few times and I've seen a few bike riders I love to go kayaking hair or just to take the dogs out. They do have public bathrooms that are very clean

This is a pretty big Park great for holding large events. I went there for a company party and it was pretty nice and they have some great shaded picnic areas. A huge baseball field but only a small playground. The porta potties were clean and even the restroom they have at the park. Even the grass was pretty green in some places which that's impressive during the summer time. If I'm ever in the area I definitely will take my dogs here and go for a nice walk around the park

This is a pretty cute park right in the center of a neighborhood. I enjoyed walking with my boyfriend and my dogs. A great place to throw a kid's birthday party or have a family picnic in the park. There's a small playground and a trail that goes all around the field and the playground, visible no matter where you go. There is also picnic benches that are covered. And the field is big enough to throw a frisbee, football, or kick a soccer ball around

This place is fantastic and there is a building outside with a lot of knowledge about the park and all the species that live here. You cannot bring your dog. Probably the only sad part about it but I totally understand with people not picking up the poop and scaring all the wildlife. I have seen deer run through here also a couple of coyotes. I have even seen a white and black rabbit. Pretty cool to see but would be scary if my dog was around

What a beautiful area. Was just driving on by on my way back to Portland and had to stop at the spark to check it out. It's pretty hidden and you would pass on by if you weren't looking for a place to pull over. Right there with my dogs and just hooking all the beautiful scenery. Lots of Wildlife and a bridge to look over it down at the water. It's a great area, I didn't notice anybody else around oh, so it was nice having the place peaceful

It's an amazing square. Well-maintained with bus information, but the place closes early. There's usually a security guard or two walking around the area. You cannot skateboard or bike. Only walk. I've always wondered why but there are names in the bricks at the square and I don't know who the people are or how they got their name but it's been like that for many years. They also do a amazing tree lighting ceremony

I used to come here a lot and I don't mind walking to the lake from the trailhead it's very nice relaxing. Trails are nice and easy and mostly flat . You can easily  ride a horse or walk with kids. I only give it one less star because the bathrooms are disgusting! People are just so gross with their trash and getting feces all over the place. I'd Rather take a pee in the woods then use their facilities.

Really cute train ride. With a show and everything. The one shoes that are $12 are overpriced. And I would save your appetite for the little town in the middle. It's a little confusing when you get the Groupon, I guess you have to make reservations but it's not a big deal. It's a a great way to spend a rainy day. Bring a jacket and comfortable closing. It does get cold and the boxcars are not heated.

The park is really nice and well-maintained but those power lines are horrible. You can hear the buzzing sound and it hurts my ears. I don't find it very safe to be around. Not that it's going to shock me but maybe whatever energy is putting off seems like it would be harmful. I don't like to come to this park for that main reason.

His face is really cool to hike down to. Great views no matter where you are on the river. And lots of information to read about. It was fantastic reading about how they used to log trees back in the day. And the gift shop was awesome as well. I definitely would come visit this place if you are visiting Michigan

I love visiting this place if I have time before I head back home from my vacation. The view is awesome in the water or is fantastic during summer time. Great place to view the old Dam and have a picnic. It's also really good Watering Hole. There is a slower current if you move farther away from the waterfall.

This is a fun doggy park. Lots of places to take your dog. And I like how they are kind of fenced-in in a big area. That way if you want to put your bigger dog with the big dogs you can or put it with the small dogs. I like this place everyone picks up their poop and there are good places to sit on benches.

This place is beautiful. A great place to stop and taking some fresh air. Which I was driving along the highway for a couple hours and needed a break and so did my dog. It was awesome. I couldn't believe I seen people kayaking even in the fall it was a great River to view on a sunny day

I love the witch's castle! It's such a really nice historical place. I enjoy the history and the nice clean trails. It's usually always packed especially on a nice day but if you go on a rainy day and decided to learn about The Witches Castle it's a nice read. A little spooky.

It's a beautiful part great place to take your kids and your dog. The fields are really nice and I enjoy walking around the area. It seems to be pretty safe I haven't seen any gangs or even graffiti around the area. I can't remember if they had a bathroom or water fountain

This is a really easy Trail for kids and older people. Unless it was snowing then it's difficult. Has a lot of good history easy access not a lot of parking the bathrooms are usually clean in the trails are well-kept. I love coming here I'm going on a long easy hike

Really cute park ride around a lake. Great for picnics a quick run or a bike ride. There's also a few geocaches around the area so that was fun finding well going on the stroll with my dogs. They also have a really old Historical house on the premises.

This is a fantastic place to walk the beach. Especially when the tide goes out. You really get to see all the sea creatures you can heal the sand shrimp we go between your toes if you dig your feet in the sand. I really love it here. Very peaceful
Great place to spend a hot day. But you better be a good swimmer because there is a current and the water is very deep. There is no lifeguards on duty. Also if you bring it pack it out.
Mount Tabor Park is amazing. Good for The Young and the old. Great for family get-togethers or for a solo. You'll dog will love it and it is amazing all year round. I love coming here.
This place is a great hike to go on any day. Regardless of the weather. They have public bathrooms and really good history and the trails are really maintained
This is a beautiful Park. And has amazing campgrounds all around it. The worst part about it as it has bad porta potties and restrooms.

First and most important: it's a very small zoo. There are not many animals there like at a typical zoo. There is free admission and free parking. The animals are in good shape and are those that they take in that were hurt or injured and no longer able to survive in the wild on their own. I give them credit for that.  They have a cougar, two eagles, some owls, a hawk, falcon, turkey, goat, otter, two alligators, and an iguana, tortoise, a bunch of snakes and turtles and fish in the reptile house. You might just need an hour to see them all, or up to two if you walk slowly.  It's stroller friendly and the zoo is kept in good shape. There is a visitor center next to it with a sunken garden that is worth seeing, so you can see all of that in one trip and it would be a least 2-3 hours worth to see.

Great little museum. Very educational. Small, so it's not one you'll spend hours at, but you can definitely spend an hour there, if you read a lot of what is shown on the exhibits. There's not much hands-on, but the giant 4x4x4 glass cube of dollar bills (one million) is worth standing next to and getting your picture taken. Might be the only time you will ever get that close to a million!  It's a great place to educate yourself on the birth and history of money and it's evolution in America as well as the birth of the Federal Reserve Bank and it's role in American history. You need to check it out.
likes: Unique exhibits (e.g., glass cube of dollar bills)

reviews_attraction.text: Great place to take your kids to learn and have fun! There are two levels/floors to explore! There is many exhibits that are hands-on for them have fun with!  See my pictures to see the variety! it's great for ages 2 and up. They have a nice little gift shop on the second level, and even have a picnic tables on the first level for parents who bring a lunch with to eat there. The cost is very reasonable: $8 per person. There is even an attached parking garage so you don't have to walk outside. Costs $8, but less if you are a member.

I love walking among the large bronze legs, but feel that they overdid it. Instead of 106, they could have done better by just using 56 or even 66. When you stand next to one, you feel small and feel the artwork. But when you are surrounded by many, it's like being in a forest among tall trees. You can't absorp the unique beauty of a few among you because there are just too many around you and it tends to overwhelm you. But it's still worth checking out if visiting Chicago or even if you live in the Chicagoland area.

Absolutely crazy place! It's great for pre-teens and teens, but not really for younger children and toddlers. It's too adventurous for them. Plus it's easy to get lost there with it being dimly lit and all the mazes, staircases, hidden entrances and path, as well as tons of people that are walking around and going up to the various floors. Plus it's pricey, at $12/person. Bring a flashlight and long pants or knee pads if you go because you'll need them!

My kids love going there. It's got a lot of fun and educational things for them to be hands-on with. They have a water table and two sand tables on the first floor. The second floor has a whole lot more to see and do. There is arts and crafts, a children's grocery store, a solar system exhibit, a medical area kids can pretend to be a paramedic or doctor and more. It'll keep your kids busy for a couple of hours easily.

Great place to go for a peaceful, quiet nature walk! Very affordable. They have long trails that take you through a variety of landscapes. You can have the kids go through the kids garden and have fun there. And before leaving can stop at the gift shop or Visitor Center for something to eat. Plenty of benches along the paths lets you stop and take in the scenary.

Great place to take the kids. I was impressed with their nature-themed play area which is pretty big and adventurous for the kids. There are benches for parents alongside, as well as a large picnic area with many picnic benches under a canopy. Their nature trails are paved and go around the lagoon, and is well-kept. They also have a parking lot on 109th Street.

Great little zoo. Even though you need to pay to get in it's not much and it goes to help take care of the animals. They have a good variety too. You can easily spend a three or four hours there. The snow leopards​ are very active and fun to watch. They have a good reptile house. It has an area in that house where kids can be hands-on with educational puzzles.

Great little park with baseball field. Actually has two play areas. One for toddlers, on south side, the other is for older kids, on north side. Nice trail cutting through park, good for little ones on bikes or rollerblades. Small parking lots on south and north sides with dog park on northeast corner if you have a dog you wish to take for a walk.

Had a great time there! It's a pretty good sized zoo, so you will spend a few hours there easily! They have a great variety of animals to see once you get past the north gate entrance which is very colorful and interestingly decorated. Just have to find free parking along one of the many roads in Forest Park to get a total free experience.

Nice little park with a few items for kids to play on. It has a nice variety of slides, swings for older kids as well as toddlers. There is a couple benches for parents to sit on while their children play. There is an attached skate park for the older kids/teens. Plenty of parking in the attached parking lot.

What a great place to have to take your kids to!  It's very affordable and costs $10 per person! You can easily spend a whole day there, so go early. The kids will love it! We went for 3 hours but it wasn't enough time to see and do everything. They have plenty of fun and educational activities.

Great place to go for a stroll on a nice day with the family or by yourself. The trail goes around the lake and it is very pleasant. Doing so gives you a chance to unwind and get closer to nature as well as inner peace. Lake Katherine is beautiful!  And what's best is that it's free!!!

Great park with lots for kids and toddlers to do. The tot park has about 5 fun and safe slides for them as well as a few benches for the parents to sit and relax near the lagoon. Well kept area with two parking lots, but I didn't see a public water fountain or bathroom.

What a feeling standing at the base. It's tall and magneficent. There is a tourist store underneath. You need to go through a metal detector to enter the underground area. They are still working on the grounds around it to make it a wooded trail park setting.

Great little zoo. Love the walking paths. Lots to see. They have a great Aquatic and primate exhibit. Only bad thing is that it is a little expensive. Costs like $14 for an adult and $11 per child. Car parking is $12. For a family of four it's about $60

I came across this place by accident. Costs only $5/car to get in. And I was very impressed! It's a great place to go to relax and enjoy the walking path along the bubbling spring and to see the trout they raise and release later into the water.

Great little area park. Has lots of things for kids of all ages to see, try and have fun with: slides, climbing, swings, tot park and more. My five year olds loved it and got tired out after playing for a couple of hours there.

Am from Chicago, so was glad to see that it was doing well in Branson.  it's near the Andy's Frozen Custard.  It was beautifully lit up at night and is now a gem for Branson to have and offer it's guests!
They have artsy, creative rooms for kids to play in, pretend and dress up. Lots of clean tables to eat at. Outdoor play area for the warmer months. Plenty of free parking.
Excellent place to bring the kids. Three levels of adventure. The rope climb will give them something to do for awhile and wear your kids out afterwards.
One of the worthwhile places to visit while in Chicago!  Great place to take pictures because of the beautiful background - the Chicago skyline.
Not sure how much it costs to ride, but it's a great attraction for the Landing. Bet you get a great view of the Landing and more from the top.
Not a bad place to visit, but overall it's small. So you can tour the entire area in an hour or so.

At over 6400 acres Cuivre River State Park is one of Missouri's largest parks, and it's got something for anyone who loves the outdoors. We didn't explore the entire park, but what we did see was awesome! Sugar Creek provided a chance for my dog, Lacey to cool off in crystal clear water, and then we drove up Cheatham Road (which runs alongside part of the Cuivre River Trail) where we were treated to spectacular views of the Cuivre River valley.
We didn't get a chance to check out Lincoln Lake, but I understand it offers opportunities for boating, swimming, and fishing.
Both modern and primitive campsites are available at the park.
The park has 14 trails, which range in length from 1/3 of a mile to 7 1/4 miles, there's also an equestrian area, which has it's own separate campground.
We thoroughly enjoyed our morning at Cuivre River State Park, and plan to return with our camping trailer when we can spend a few days exploring!

Unfortunately, the roads leading to both the lake and the scenic overview were closed due to damage caused by flooding, so we weren't able to see either of them. The sections of the park we were able to explore, however were absolutely beautiful. We camped at the Mississippi River Campground, thus had an up close view of the river. One drawback to the campground is the railroad tracks running right by it, and the trains coming through at all hours of the day and night. This really didn't bother us all that much, but some people might not deal with it very well. The visitors center has a nice little museum, which offers insight into the plight of the Cherokee Indians, who were forced to relocate by the U.S. government.
The staff was extremely friendly, and helpful, and we will definitely return to this park so we can see what we missed the first time around.
dislikes: Closed roads to lake and scenic overview

reviews_attraction.text:
I have fond childhood memories here, touring the cavern with my family. I wanted to stop and see the area again. I took my dog, Lacey, with me, as I do on all of my adventures, so I wasn't able to take the tour this time around. They do have kennel rentals available, but the whole point of taking Lacey with me is to SHARE my adventures with here.
The site is beautiful, but has become far too commercialized. In addition to the cavern tour available activities include camping, a "riverboat" tour, and a zipline, and canoe rentals. Lacey really enjoyed cooling off in the Meremac River, so that was a plus, she also barked at the statue of Jesse and Frank James a lot. LOL

The Union Covered Bridge was built in 1871, as part of the Paris - Fayette route, and derives its name from the nearby Union Church, it's now part of the Union Covered Bridge State Historic Site, which was established to preserve the bridge, which is one of only four remaining historic covered bridges in Missouri. A partial restoration was done on the bridge in 1968, and it was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1970. Although the site has no park or picnic tables, there is a small parking lot, and we very much enjoyed the beautiful surroundings and the sound of the river below. Lacey also enjoyed the opportunity to cool off in the water!

This park offers beautiful scenery, as well as a lot of history. It's got a nice walking trail, and an overlook where you can see the Mississippi River. Because it's only about 5 minutes from home, my dog, Lacey, and I frequently visit Jefferson Barracks Park. There's also a disc golf course, cork ball fields, and a really fun aquatic center, as well as several museums. In addition, there's plenty of wide open spaces where you can relax and commune with nature.
The annual World War II Weekend gives visitors a glimpse at military camps and equipment, and there's even battle reenactments every year.
This is a must stop for history bluffs and nature lovers.

This is a long, narrow strip of land which runs along River Des Peres, and includes a couple of playgrounds, a nice trails for walking, jogging and biking, and a baseball field and soccer field (we never did see the soccer field, or the water fountain we read about). The only parking lot we found was at the Fultz baseball field, but we also parked on a side street further up Des Peres Boulevard, so we could explore that part of the park. Established in 1934, this is a scenic park which is part of the River Des Peres Greenway. We really enjoyed our walk here.

It was great seeing the actual house in which Samuel Clemens (Mark Twain) was born. The house is now enclosed within the Mark Twain Memorial Shrine, in Florida, Missouri. I wasn't able to spend enough time there to explore everything the museum has to offer, as my dog Lacey was waiting for me in the car, but I did enjoy seeing the house.
The staff was extremely friendly, making my experience even more worthwhile. I also enjoyed viewing Mark Twain Lake from Clara's Overlook, which is just a short walk from the museum.

Frontier Park, also part of the statewide Katy Trail State Park, is a great place for an outing, and the park is host to many events throughout the year. In addition to the old MKT depot (aka Katy Depot) there's a larger than life statue of Lewis and Clark, with their Newfoundland dog, Seaman. St. Charles was a stop along their Corps of Discovery Expedition. We took a leisurely 1 mile round trip walk, and enjoyed the views of the Missouri River on one side and the historic town of St. Charles on the other.

Castlewood State Park is a beautiful place to commune with nature, but when we visited, there were several renovations going on in the park, and due to all the recent rain we've had lately, the trail we tried to hike was muddy and sloppy. Swimming in the Meremac here is NOT recommended, but Kiefer Creek is a great place to enjoy the water, as it's fed by two springs, making the water crystal clear and very cool. We thoroughly enjoyed our visit, and will definitely return once all the work is completed.

My memories of this park date back to the mid 60s. When I played baseball here, then later hung out with my friends in my late teens and early 20s. Until now, I hadn't returned to Southwest park in approximately 40 years, and a lot has changed. There's now a great little playground where there once was a wooded area, and there's now a picnic pavilion, and public restrooms which I don't remember being there back in the day. It was nice returning for a walk down memory lane.

This was a great place to spend a couple of hours! We I did the self guided tour, and found it all fascinating. The grounds are extremely well kept, and all the staff members we encountered were really helpful and friendly.
The experience really gave us a sense of what life was like in the days of good ol' Daniel Boone! It's only about an hour drive from St. Louis, so the trip wasn't bad at all. If you haven't seen it I suggest you put it on your list of "must see" places!

This is a relatively small park, but it's really nice. The first thing we noticed is that it has two separate ramps (one of which has handrails) which lead down to the park from the parking lot, making it wheelchair accessible. There's a nice little playground, a baseball field, a reservable picnic pavilion, and a couple of other picnic tables. While it's not as big and glorious as some of the parks we've visited, Ohlendorf County Park is a nice place for a family outing.

This is a great park, with a playground which looks like it would be a lot of fun for kids. There's also a nice walking trail, which has obviously been very recently repaved. The trail took us past Westside Park Lake, where public fishing is allowed. We didn't take any of the trail "offshoots" to see where they led, we'll have to more thoroughly check out the park on a future visit. We thoroughly enjoyed our visit to Westside Park, and highly recommend it.

This is a great park with a beautiful lake, a campground which is really close to the water, 3 boat launches, and a nice beach (unfortunately, the beach was closed due to high water when we were there). It also offers opportunities for fishing, bicycling, hiking, and picnicking.
The scenery is absolutely beautiful, and I will probably plan a future camping trip at Long Branch State Park. If you love water sports this is definitely the park for you!

This is a nice little county park with athletic fields, tennis courts, a basketball court, a playground, several picnic areas, including a picnic pavilion, and little pond with a boardwalk. There's a great walking path which winds through the park, making it a great place to walk my dog. We enjoyed our visit, and will definitely return, as it's only a 10 minute drive from our house.

This cool little park has a skate park, a playground, and a splash pad, as well as picnic pavilions. It's also home to Sylvan Springs Beverage Garden, a World War Two beverage garden and picnic area which was built by the CCC, for use by all troops stationed at Jefferson Barracks. The park also features some nice open areas. This is a great park for speeding time with the family.

This is a beautiful park, with a nice fishing lake, lakeside picnic areas (including a reservable pavilion, a playground which features a small rock climbing wall, and river walk, which is part of the Meremac Greenway. We enjoyed walking along both the lake and the river. Simpson Park is clean, and well maintained. We had a great visit!

This gem of a county park features a 10 acre lake, which is stocked by the Missouri Department of Conservation, picnic areas, including reservable shelters, a nice playground, and plenty of good ol' open space. The scenery is awesome, and the environment extremely tranquil. Bee Tree County Park is one to which we'll return.

This is another gem of a small park, with a nice little playground, and plenty of trees. There's also a little creek, with a cool stone bridge which was built in 1941, and a picnic Pavilion with several tables. It was very relaxing. The park, as with the others we've visited during our stay, is very well maintained.

This is a beautiful Park for a walk along the Meremac River, and it's part of the Meramec Greenway. It's a serene setting, and the paved trail is perfect for walking, jogging, and cycling. The two mile trail leads east, to Simpson park, and west, to Arnold's Grove Trailhead. The park also has a concrete boat ramp.

Don Robinson State Park has a diverse and beautiful landscape, and an extremely interesting history. Mr. Robinson recognized the importance of preserving this land for the enjoyment of future generations. The park offers a nice picnic area and 2 hiking trails with views of sandstone cliffs and shelter caves.

This is a cool little park with a big ol' observation tower (no longer open for climbing). There are a few picnic areas, including a nice pavilion, and a playground area. There's also plenty of parking, and his & her outhouses. It's a fun place to spend a little time.

This is a great park, with a trail which ties into Grants Trail. There are also workout stations along the way. It's got a nice playground and sports fields, as well as picnic areas, and restroom facilities. This Park is a definite winner.
We were extremely excited to visit Johnson Shut-Ins State Park, until we got there and saw the sign which informed us that pets weren't allowed on the trail. What the heck? SHUT OUT at the Shut-Ins!
Nice soccer fields and an archery range, great access for a riverside walk. We enjoyed our visit to this park.

Surprisingly complete look at the man and his life. The tour guide was excellent and well informed.

We used the upper level for an event dinner. The Petroleum Club handles the food and catering. The price structure is simple, without nickel and diming you. Our needs are extensive from an A/V standpoint and with a professional sound system and video distribution to several TV's throughout the area, the PTZ camera we were able to use. Just outstanding in every aspect.

The visitor center was cool. I walked the Rinconada trail and it's a short hike, but, please remember you are in the desert. Take water, sunscreen and pack your bottles back out. Kids and dogs are out here. I go in the very early morning for the quite and the angle of the sun makes the glyphs easier to see.

It's a converted movie theater. Some of this is clearly a small town home grown but the dioramas are well put together and the information provided is pretty expensive even if again some of it is a bit sophomoric. so if you're in this part of the country this is a place to stop at.

A really neat place, the staff from the docent to the gift shop staff are all incredibly helpful and knowledgeable about the sculptures and the artists. The outdoor exhibition area is little slice of calm in the middle of downtown. The diner is a great place to take a break.

There is so much to list for the entire Lake area. With the Route 66 Park, the Overholser boathouse for standing paddle boards and kayak rental. This also includes the zip line and the Grill. The Overholser dam and drainage area are one of my favorite spots for photography.

A really cool place and the view is amazing. Take a camera! Get a photo of being in both states at once as you straddle the painted and marked line in the middle of the span.
While totally safe, this bridge does move ever so slightly and some folks might find disturbing.

It's fantastic for kids of all ages. Some of the interactive exhibits are the same ones from when I was a kid way too long ago and some are brand new. Five stars all around. The food's not bad and the gift shop's gotten bigger too.
It's about 15 bucks per adult ticket.

I'd lived in Grants for years and only visited as a tourist years later. The museum is thoughtful, we'll put together and I certainly learned more about mining, Grants and the history of the area.
It's not a huge location and absolutely worth it if you are in town.

While it was under renovation, the quality of the exhibits was outstanding. More than just a museum, the informational callouts and detailed information allow you to tie what you see into the history of the country they highlight, giving it more relevance.

Amazing views. There is a caravan of suvenior sells on one side of the bridge. Make sure you both walk across and stop at the rest area. From the rest area you can see the bridge and gorge from the side. There are facilities at the rest stop.

The latest addition to the Riversport group of  events and venues the rapids are affordable and fun. Additionally, it is City Park. You don't have to pay to just walk around and check things out. There is a cafe and a store as well.

Certainly out of the way. Totally worth it. If you aren't from the altitude, please remember that the short walk around the rim, (1.2 miles, has a lot of altitude changes itself) can be trying as you'll have less oxygen.

It's not a Park. It's a wildlife refuge. I've walked the trail all the way to where it exits by the Wilshire off ramp of the turnpike. I've gotten some great photos of snakes and even a coyote or two.
One of those unexpectedly well done little museum's that will surprise you when you find them. This is great look back on both western Oklahoma and the US. Mostly the early to mid 20th century.
A neat Park with a variety of things to do. I added it to my travel list as a place to see while in Omaha. For a person who likes to feed the animals and people watch. This is a neat place.
An excellent spot with a unique architecture and design highlighting local artists in different shops along with a rare book store and a Mexican restaurant with indoor patio dining.
Few churches in the US can be thought of as a tourist attraction. This is one of them. A beautiful building. To know your in a place older than the Country it's in. Mind blown.
Still in great shape and a lovely park. A bit out of the way unless you are the lake. Much easier to reach from 10th Street though maps indicate it's in Yukon. It's just not.
Another place it took me way to long to go to. I was amazed by not just the Crystal Bridge but the surrounding park area as well. (Take your allergy medicine before you go!)
The permanent pieces, detailing the history of the building is really cool. The temporary exhibits are neat. But the whole building is simply a marvel on the plains.
A plentiful amount of options and wide spaces. Soccer fields, playgrounds, skate park, walking trail, picturesque pond. Very clean and there are portable bathrooms.
It's fun and the hikes are easy enough to be dog friendly. It's certainly on the small side and the only reason it gets less than four stars.
It took me a long time to go. It seemed morbid. I can see that I was wrong about that and the solemn nature helps keep a person grounded.
Nice equipment but on the small side. It is right next the Bluff Creek trails, so a nice place to take a break.

I am disappointed in this zoo.

My real disappointment began in the ticketing area.  There was a sickly sweet odor that I was having trouble placing.  It concerned me because the room was full of toys and food for children.  I was told later that it was because of some goat cheese that was on sale but it seemed to be emanating from the reptile exhibits which were placed in the walls immediately facing on the ticketing area where the food and toys previously mentioned are.

Yuck!

When I got outside the first thing I saw was the chicken coop.  The birds seemed to be in good shape.  They were quite large.  There were two guinea fowl in the coop.  There were two unclaimed eggs that appeared to have been there for a couple of days at least. The coop itself appeared to be showing its age.  There was accumulated detritus from the trees above weighing down the top screen.

Nearby was a pig exhibit.  The shelters for the pigs are very small.  The one I saw was exactly the size of the pig.  I believe it was some sort of a boar.  I couldn’t tell.  It didn’t exit its house and the exhibit was closed.
Further along was a large cage with two small monkeys in it.  Obviously not from the area they appeared a little on the exposed side.  The cage was uninteresting and barren.  I didn’t see any fresh fruit in the cage though there appeared to be some food in there.

Around the corner were some other monkeys.  They were unlabeled.  They were isolated in separate cages.  They looked forlorn.  The cages were barren and uninteresting.  They were exposed to the elements.
There was a cage with two small baby black bears in it.  No mother.  They were taking turns tearing up a piece of black cloth they had pulled off the top of the cage.  One of them busied itself chewing on the straw on top of its bamboo ‘shelter’.  The cage was stark and small especially for two bear cubs.

Next was the caribou enclosure.  One male was moving around the pen aggressively.  The other caribou sat in the small lean-to in the back.  The enclosure is small, poorly drained and devoid of greenery.  There was no fresh, dry feed.

Further along we came to an enclosure with wallabies.  There were two albino wallabies.  One of them appeared to have some sort of eye infection.   Two others seemed to have trouble with their eyes.  The lot was somewhat spacious but had only one manger.  It was poorly drained and smelled.

They have a small herd of tortoises.  They were moving about.  The compound was generally dry but it smelled.  There didn’t seem to be any fresh feed and the water was questionable as little as there was.  The area was denuded of greenery.
