The ride seems incredibly slow, not sure if its the seats or what, but, the excitement level was very low. Almost casually floating through twist and turns that never quite truly thrills.

I personally wasn't a fan of the chest straps either, found them very restrictive, uncomfortable, and hard to breathe.

I will ride everything once, but, there's much better coasters in the park I would rather spend that sort of wait on.

Always have a good time visiting Cleveland Museum of Natural History.

Theres always plenty to see, inside the actual Museum and outside in the wildlife sanctuary. Typically, there's one major attraction that changes periodically to keep people coming back. I've often based my trips of return around those changes.

It's always quiet, friendly staff, and just an enjoyable time to view exhibits and educate yourself. A great place for all ages.

I particularly like to point out, my favorite addition to the Museum, the actual stuffed remains of the famous sled dog - BALTO!

Highly recommend museum for anyone who enjoys history to any degree.

Been riding on this bike trial for more then twenty years now.

Used to ride the entire 13 mile length from Danville to Mount Vernon as a kid, now just use it for casual strolls, and to enjoy the outdoors.

Lots of great entry points rather it be Danville, Howard, Mount Vernon, or Kenyon.   Very well kept, clean, some nice little historic points along the way.

The trial is great for jogging, walking, or riding and is very scenic at times along the Kokosing. Not uncommon to encounter plenty of wildlife.

Nice gem of Knox County,  and has been even more of a blessing during the COVID19 pandemic as a great keeper to normalcy.
likes: Suitable for various activities (jogging, walking, riding)

reviews_attraction.text:
Pretty nice little exhibit.
I really enjoyed the "hands on" , having been able to touch and try on some things, more specifically, we loved the 'Cellar' experience in which you could hear and feel the sounds of battle.
Price was somewhat high but it was worth the experience for one time.

The gift shop here is one of the best in town. It's loaded with incredible books and you can go from as cheap as a post card to truly expensive artifacts. I've spent too much money here, but, always one of my first stops when I come to Gettysburg!

Highly recommended stop.

General Meade's Headquarters during the Battle of Gettysburg.

No access to the building, but well preserved. Furniture from the HQ is located at the museum at The Gettysburg visitor center nearby.

You can peak through the windows and get an idea of what it was like inside.

I do wish that they would do something more interactive with the building that might allow for visitor's to access the home and get a more in depth lecture on its role from a park ranger or volunteer.

Nonetheless, an incredible historic location to stand and see.

Very nice and free sculpture garden in the midst of the city.

A relaxing and fun area to escape the hussle and bustle around you, smack dab in the downtown area, but turns quickly into a nice escape from the "city life", where one can enjoy peace and tranquility.

Lots of nice art pieces to see, and full of friendly tourist and locals.

I walked clear across the city to visit and was well worth the walk, specifically the crown jewel, the famous Cherry on a Spoon.

Must stop if visiting Minneapolis.

Nice little dog park at the entrance of the trials, plentiful parking, and secluded area.

There's hardly anybody ever out here which makes it a nice little getaway spot, that feels much farther out of town, then it actually is.

Peaceful and beautiful area.

Only negative is the trials seem to be poorly marked, not really sure at some point's which direction you are, or aren't supposed to go, somewhat unclear boarders of the park in general.

Nice place for a quick walk, or some exploration.

Incredible natural falls, and great hiking trials. Very clean, very well upkept.  Many sculptures along the paths, an old rail depot, and some history into the first settlers.

An absolute paradise in the middle of Minneapolis that's a MUST visit, a great escape from the downtown hustle and bustle, to reset mind and soul.

Probably my favorite place I found as I was exploring the city.

Highly recommend.

Nice quiet park, located along the Kokosing River, near by Bike Trial starts right next to it.

Great place for family get together's, baseball tournaments, and taking children.

We host many of our family birthday parties here and they're always quiet, undisturbed, and fun. Lot's of room to grill, eat, play. Swimming available, as well.

It's very clean, and well maintained. Great community Park.

At 80mph and 215 foot drop this is the fastest and highest Roller Coaster at Kings Island and in my mind is clearly the best attraction by a long shot...

Rather it be the speed, the drop, or skidding across the water towards the end this is an incredible fast and smooth coaster that will excite any true thrill seeker.

This is a MUST ride if you're visiting Kings Island!

To say this place is spectacular is an understatement. Not sure how I came across this to want to visit, but I think it was a YouTube video. We had the park entirely to ourselves on a chilly December afternoon. The scenery is absolutely beautiful. The waterfall is bigger than I thought. The viaduct is really neat. There is ample parking lot for 15-20 vehicles. The path to the waterfall is a moderate hike on a paved trail. Plenty of signage to read about the history. The only negative I have is that for such a nice place to visit, there was no picnic tables or restroom facilities. Will definitely stopped back in the summer.

Was I so glad I stubbled across this park. Was just driving around to small villages I've never been to and Gibsonburg was one of them. Such a awesome little town. This park was we'll keep with several ball fields, basketball court, etc. They have received a piece of the World Trade Center tower that was put together for a remarkable display. The park has several art pieces throughout. Make Gibsonburg a weekend destination.

Great park in a perfect location. Plenty of shelter houses available for picnics or reunions. Playground areas for the kids. Basketball courts, tennis court, and baseball and softball fields. Pool open during summer. Very picturesque pond with a cute little bridge. Haven't fished here since I was a kid, but I believe fishing is restricted to those 16 yrs old and younger. Fantasy of Lights event during winter.

The Columbus Zoo is probably one of the best zoos in the country. It is famous for Jungle Jack Hanna and has plenty of sponsors throughout Columbus. The manatee coast exhibit is awesome. To see these animals in their habitat eating away on the lettuce is really cool. You can definitely spend all day here, from open to close. Pay them a visit if you're from Ohio or visiting from out of state.

Always have wanted to visit this masterpiece for years. Even if you're not a big architecture fan, you will be inspired my the design, and thought put into this house. It would be amazing to have the chance to spend an entire weekend staying here. The facilities are nice as well. The staff and guides were all very friendly and knowledgeable, being able to answer almost all questions asked.

Awesome trail to hike and enjoy the surrounding nature and geography of the area. It is a pretty simple trail for the most part. Level trail with little hills. The unfortunate thing is there are no kind of restroom facilities, or shelter house of any kind. The map of the trail could use some improvement as well. But a good spot to spend an hour to so. Fairly ample parking as well.

Most incredible place to visit within an hour drive of Marion Ohio. Found this place one day on Google Maps, then seen it in several magazines, and even on tv. Give yourself anywhere from 4-6 hrs to enjoy the scenery, and read the history of this place. Big thanks go out to everyone who donated money, and spent the time to make sure this place happened.

This place is awesome, and it's right in town. There is a decent amount of parking available. They have 2 shelters and tables to use for picnics. There are 2 viewing decks and both are wheelchair accessible, as the path to those is flat. Nice place to spend some time listening and viewing the falls. And Hayden Run Falls is just a short drive from these.

This place is remarkable. The beach was closed as it was October when I stopped. Everything looked nice though. New facilities, nice covered playground for the kids. The allow scuba diving here. Talked to some guys that were going in and they explained everything to me. Plan on coming  back here during the summer to enjoy.

Nice park right in the downtown of Gallipolis. Surprised to see all the thriving businesses in the downtown. There were a lot of people out using the park picnic tables on a Tuesday after 8:00pm. They had public restrooms just across from the park, but they lock the doors at 5:00pm. There was a porta potty at the park.

This was really neat to see. I had heard about it from friends who have visited the area. I wish I would of had more time to read all the information they have at every murals and check out all the details. You could probably easily spend 1-2 hours here if you read everything. Great job to the artist who painted these.

Awesome stop while in the Dayton area. They have an old farm there that they are maintaining. Neat to see the buildings. Saw 5 beautiful white horses on the farm. Also have a pretty nice size lake. Seen several people fishing it. Unfortunately the visitors center wasn't open. Also, several people there taking pictures.

This was a neat stop while driving the Ohio River. The park is very good size with plenty of parking. There is lots of history to read about. Ran into an older gentleman that brought his grandkids to see where his family used to come and have picnics when he was younger. I hope he had a good day.

This place was an awesome find while out Ohio road tripping. They have a restaurant here. Had some kind of big festival or something going on for fall. Wish I had more time to stay and explore. They have their own soda, beer, and wine. A little bit on the expensive side, but worth the stop.

So cool to see how Yellow Springs got it's name. Definitely neat to see for sure. A decent trail gets you there, about a 10-15 minute hike depending on pace. The only thing that I found really disappointing is that they have no kind of signs making sure you are going in the right direction.
dislikes: Facilities & Services: Lack of directional signs

reviews_attraction.text: Awesome park for Bucyrus Ohio. Pretty cool suspension bridge. They have an 18 hole disc golf course. The ballfields look well taken care of. The pool didn't look open, probably due to Covid-19. The Bell tower chimed while I was there. Nice park for a small town.

One of the most incredible places to visit in the state of Ohio. So much to see, and all relatively close o each other. This place is a must every year, and always fun to switch up the seasons when going to visit.
Nice place to take a walk through the woods. Seen several species of birds. Not an extremely long trail. The marsh could use some brush removed to open up more water, but still a nice wooded area.
Gotta appreciate any historical significance if you're from Ohio. Great fact that Grant was born in this little town. The place was closed when I stopped, but you can still meander the grounds.
Nice addition for activities in the Marion area. Short drive from town. Kinda gets you out in the country a little bit, to maybe see some wildlife. Not the most picturesque of places though.
Mt Gilead state park is pretty decent place to visit. They have ample shelter houses, places for kids to play, disc golf, hiking trails, etc. Could spend about half a day here having fun.
Decent area to view different wildlife. Not sure how good the hunting or fishing is? Usually stop at the viewing deck off of Rte 95 to view sunsets since it has a long unobstructed view.
Very beautiful lighthouse, especially for Ohio. The park is always busy on weekends. The have lighthouse tours and reasonably priced. Good place to enjoy for an hour or so.
So cool to visit this lighthouse. Porta potty available. People there just enjoying the beach and waves. Seen a lady breastfeeding, not a complaint.
Cool park. Didn't know they charged so much to launch a boat. But was a nice park. Good place to stop if you have to pee pee.

Brookside Park is located on Broad Street in Bay Avenue in Bloomfield New Jersey it’s a pretty decent sized park and it’s a very nice park it has a nice river front walkway which is very nice and there’s often ducks and geese which makes the park even prettier there’s also a very small playground for a much smaller little kids and there’s also a bunch of benches in the baseball field right by the river front it runs along the third River my overall experience at Brookside Park is very good it’s a very nice scenic park that you can walk through perfect for a walk or anything else

The Historic Strawberry Mansion is located in Fairmount Park in North Philly the place is not fun because i drove by it and it did not look special now mind you this was during Thanksgiving so the mansion might not be open for tours but it is in close proximity to other historic places in  Fairmount Park it is also located along the Skuykill River as well so thats fun overall i don't really recommend this place because there is not much to see but if im wrong im sorry

Paterson falls is a very beautiful site and get a beautiful view of the amazing waterfall it’s very scenic and there are many places to sit the park is very nice thereIt’s all so many surrounding parks it’s also in very close proximity to downtown Paterson so my overall experience every time I come chill Paterson falls in Paterson jersey is always pretty good five stars highly recommended

The Cherry Blossom Center at branch Brook Park is huge it’s in the northern most part of the park near Belleville on the border of Newark it’s a very pretty area you could the Cherryblossom’s especially in the spring in very late winter or very nice and it’s a great welcoming to spring my overall experience at the Cherry Blossom center is very good five star is highly recommended

Upper raceway park is located in Paterson north of grand Street and south of Paterson falls it’s located in the old Great Falls historic District which has Paterson falls the gun mil Garrett Mountain Reservation and upper Raceway Park up a raceway park has a huge reservoir that’s blocked off there’s also some sort of abandoned building in the middle of the stony Ridge Trail

Very nice Forest located in Warren county This Forest is one of the most haunted forests in New Jersey there are a lot of legends and goes down the infamous Shades Of Death Road in Green Meadows this park has a legend that a girl Named Jenny Jumped of a cliff from some bad guys and died they also have a cave as well as a Lake called ghost lake because of the Fog on the lake

The Devil Tree is located on Mountain Road in Bernards Township to get there park on a side street and walk down the trail you will come up to a really big oak tree the tree looks like it has been burned down there are tons of legends on the tree  like suicide deaths and hangings from Slavery days and after you leave the road there is a black car that chased us to 7-Eleven

Dundee Island preserve is located in Clifton  along with Passaic River It’s right off of Route 21 so it’s not a very quiet preserve but it’s very pretty because it has a waterfall there’s two sides of the park the first side in the main part is in Clifton and then the other side is in Garfield the Garfield side is nicer because that’s where the waterfall is

Overlook Park is right across the street from the historic Paterson falls the park is also a much quieter park with a beautiful view of Patterson their rocks flowers and beautiful murals my overall experience at Overlook Park is very nice you can also get in the close proximity of downtown Patterson so if you want to see the Paterson falls come here

The tree is so cool I love the effort that people put in to decorate the tree the crowds are kinda annoying and you have to be in and out but it’s still worth the trip very very nice it is a tourist trap but is still very nice just be aware of crowds I also love the star and the lights and ornaments make the tree look very nice

Edgemont park is located on Valley Road in Montclair New Jersey it is a very pretty park with a very huge pond a new and improved playground and a beautiful memorial My overall experience is really nice if you want to relax or just look at a pond in a nice warm day this place is very good for you five stars highly recommended

Turkey Brook Park is located on Flanders Road In Mount Olive Budd Lake the park is huge it has a veterans memorial area as well as a great playground a great dog park as well as sports the park has a bunch of trails as well the park also has a kiosk and the service was good at the Kiask the park has great parking as well

Military Park is located on Broad Street in Newark it’s located smack dab in the middle of downtown Newark the park has a carousel with little animals on it also it’s a perfect place just to relax in a very nice neighborhood They also have a wide variety of flowerbeds which is extremely nice to

Turtle Back Zoo is located in West Orange I used to go here when I was younger it’s been I while but the memories were amazing I love animals they have lots of cute animals I can’t remember what kind of animals they had I know they had giraffes sting rays and birds

Love this place there are lots of rocks on the paths and there hard to walk on but there is a stream on the path that has crystal clear water and it’s not busy here either so that should not be a problem great place to take your dog or just go on a hike by yourself

Very nice bridge it’s not as nice as the Ben Franklin Bridge that will take you into Downtown Philly the Walt Whitman Bridge will take you in to South Philly And the Lincoln Financial Field And The Wells Fargo Arena you can see the Delaware River it is very nice

Back in the spring of 2014 when I was younger I went one one. Of these I was 10 at the time it was kinda scary so high up but it was a good memory and it was very fun and you had to keep a good balance as well fun and scary but I Totally enjoyed it

Rifle Camp Park Is located on rifle Camp Road in West Paterson the park is a decent sized park I was only in it for a few minutes but it was a cute park and also has some very interesting trails and there’s a Reservoir in it

Very Nice Park there are lots of deer and a very nice mountain with a view of NYC there is also a reservoir and great hiking trails and has a Lenape trail my problem with this place is there is no streams and any Swamps

I hiked here a few years ago when I camped here in 2017 the place was so nice and scenic place I loved it the waterfall was not huge but it is still nice and pretty the trails are very bumpy so that’s the only problem
Colgate Clock is located in Jersey City waterfront in the Hudson River the Colgate clock is very old clock but it is still amazing you can see it if you take a ferry into Manhattan
Van Vleck Gardens is located on Van Vleck Pl in Montclair it is a botanical garden and has tours and other things to offer as well the tours are fun and the flowers 💐 are great 👍
The Pine Barrens are home to so many mysteries and it is so isolated and scary but so pretty many abandoned villages and there is not much agriculture except for Cranberry’s
Bellefonte Park It’s located on water Street it’s very beautiful there’s a waterfall and a bunch of other fish is an abandoned railroad and there’s also a gazebo

Thank you so much for being open to the public. I never knew this place existed until I saw it in a magazine article, and I only live an hour away. I have yet to travel to India so coming here helped with my fix for a while.
This place is so amazing and peaceful. The carvings cannot be described, especially the ones inside the Mandir. Was such a wonderful experience to come visit and see one of the services. I have been telling everyone I know about this place to come and experience another culture first hand.
The staff was so helpful without even to have to ask them anything. They took it upon themselves to show you where things were and how they worked. A gentleman visiting even offered to take a bunch of photos with me and my friend in them, without even asking.
Anyone who is into photography (like me) and also wants to learn more about a culture other than yours, and have a peaceful day in a beautiful setting...this is the place. They offer a guided hearing tour as well. Have a small cafe with food and drinks and a gift purchasing area.
Stay for the sunset! The building and fountains light up beautifully.

Went mainly for the planet shows but was a bit disappointed. One was just a live show w/ someone talking about the constellations & wasn't so much a movie as I thought. The 2nd show, beyond the universe, was traveling to the planets & seeing photos from probes that have landed & from hubble. Was a bit more interesting but I have seen better planet shows on TV. Mainly just went for the experience of IMAX.
Something to keep in mind if you visit: there are free shows offered but you need to get tickets from the main ticket line downstairs before you can go to them. Getting the ticket reserves your seat for the time slot you pick. Since I did not know this beforehand, I missed out on what might have been some cool shows. The lines were way too long to wait. They should have that set up differently. The planet shows are not free, I purchased a combo ticket with general admission for those. There is not much else to do there that was of interest for someone who does not have children. Saw the bees exhibit which I enjoyed and also the live animals. Skyscrapers was pretty cool also.

Must see stop in Moab for any dinosaur lover. Save some time and skip the theater, not quite sure what they were trying to show in there but it has nothing to do with dinosaurs and it would be boring for any child and comedic for any adult. We were the only ones in there and now I know why. For sure do the aquarium,  a 4D experience that makes you feel like your really viewing prehistoric sea creatures. Only takes about 10 to 15 min to go through and it's a guided walk and explanation at every "tank". Museum doesn't have too much inside, a few cool things that kids would enjoy as well as adults but, the main thing to see if the dinosaurs outside. There is as cafe on site and gift shop. Some workers seemed to hate their job being there and some seemed to not really understand what you were saying. Sad if they are not being paid well at a big touristy attraction.

This park behind and down the hill from the capitol is a must see. Its a bit of a walk but they have things to see along the way. They have a map imprinted of the state in the concrete and a nice water show with facts about Tennessee. Picnic tables, restrooms and vending machines are right there so you can sit and relax. Head further on and get to their black world globe rotating on water and the pillars with the Tennessee flag imprinted on the ground. When I went they had a flea market and a farmers market, which might be permanent, with tons of food spots to eat. Grab a picnic table outside,  sit inside,  or go sit in the park. Either way you sill enjoy your time here. On the way back read the wall about the civil war and Tennessee history that spans your whole walk into the park.

Awesome little trail that connects to the lenape trail. Parking lot is somewhat small, but there is parking across the street at the library. Just be mindful of the signs for the days/time you park. Porta potties in the lot.
Fairy trail is a fairly short loop. When you get to the end of the creek, you can make a right and follow the flat trail which will take out back out to the parking lot, but just a different way. There was a few little houses up there as well. Lots of people with kids. Was still a peaceful little walk and great photography. Be sure to look good! Some houses are hidden or behind you once you pass :)

4.2021. Did not get to see the Fort on this particular trip as I was too caught up filming an Osprey flying around with a fish. On the right chimney on officers row, there is a huge nest. Be on the lookout if you are there anytime soon.
You can spend all take here if you are into photography or biking. I had my bike but I walked around to photograph. There is a little cafe close to the Fort/lighthouse parking lot just in case you need a snack. I had brought my own food cause I was out biking all day. Next time I will check out the cafe and fort and bike trails all around Sandy Hook.

Beautiful place with a large parking area and bathrooms..in a building and also porta potties. Few miles of blazed trails and if you're not feeling adventurous, you can walk around the lake at the entrance on a smooth sandy surface. Picnic tables in a bunch of places so bring some snacks. I hiked mainly the yellow and blue trails on my first visit. Terrain is very uneven and super rocky. Definitely a more medium difficulty. Proper hiking shoes would be best. Great views, especially in the fall. Hiked about 8 miles and still did not see it all. Highly recommend place to visit.

4.2021. Gardens are beautiful. Parking lot is very spacious. Walkways start at lot and then continue across the street. There is a walking path in the woods that starts to the right side of the parking lot from where you come in. Lots of benches and places to enjoy a nice lunch or book. Buildings are closed as of now.  Porta potties in lot were super gross and seemed like they were not maintained in a long time. No toilet paper either. Be prepared. Overall a beautiful, peaceful area to enjoy the afternoon and do some photography. Will go back again once more has bloomed.

Beautiful and peaceful place. I felt like I was in Japan while walking through here. The grounds are pretty big and there are lots of paths to take but they circle back. You can explore around the greenhouse, the barn, and the building across from it with a beautiful little garden area. You can dial the number they have listed there and do a type of audio tour. I opted to not do this. Bathrooms were closed but a porta potty was in the lot.
I came here after hiking Hacklebarney State park so if you need something else to do in the area, it's only a 10 min drive.

Variety of trails. Though there is no biking on the actual trails, you can bike around the park either on the path or in the street. Also other off trail spots for bikes. Playgrounds for kids, great for dog walks and just relaxing on all the benches they have.
Picnic tables by the beach and seasonal snack stand are great. Osprey and other bird watching, great for photography. Be sure to stop in the nature center close to the beginning of the trailhead. Def recommended.

I've taken 2 birds there that I have found. They take all kinds of birds and rehabilitate if possible. It's a great place to go and view all the birds they have that are there permanently. They even take birds when they are closed . They leave a room open with cages and heating pads and instructions if you need to bring a bird after hours. They take donations. They also have a small gift shop on site.

What's so great about Goblin Valley is you get to walk down in it. Your even allowed to climb all over as long as your careful to not be disrespectful and knock over rock formations. This is def a must see! There are picnic tables at the top where you can look over the valley and enjoy a meal in the shade. There are real restrooms in the parking lot with about 2 stalls in each.

My dad has been taking us here since we were kids. I have been back countless of times to do photography and just enjoy nature. With 3 short trails and potential to see bald eagles, hawks and lots of other species, this place is a must see, especially in the spring where you can view much more wildlife.

Amazing dinosaur exhibit. Highly recommended. Had lunch in the cafe there as well and food was awesome and super fresh. Staff is really friendly as well. $15 to get in and you can expect to spend at least 2 hours there, more if you want to read all the info or if you have children wanting to play.

Canyonlands is amazing. Better than the Grand Canyon in my opinion. Def need to hike the brim trail which is 2 miles round-trip but you can go as far out or as close as you want. End of the trail view is gorgeous though.

Museum was really cool. Cost $25 to get in and takes about 1.5 hours to complete,  depending on if your read everything or not. The clothing exhibits were my fav part. They also have a few nice gifts shop and small cafe.
I only went here to see the 911 memorial so I cannot speak much on the park. I can see it's not a huge area but s nice paved trail around the lake and some picnic benches on the trees.
Parked across from the Catheral and walked around within that area. Great trees here directly across from there. There is a paved walkway and benches as well. Great area for a picnic.
Great spot for walking/biking and wildlife viewing. Also entrance on the blvd that's kinda hidden if you don't know the area. Check it out!
You will wait in line here to take a photo but it's worth it! Mural is right around the corner from Buscuit Love in the Gulch.
Right across the street from country music hall of fame, see your fav singers and bands with with a nice view of the skyline.
Awesome aquarium if your visiting for a day or two. $20 to get in and was worth it. Lots to see and staff is really nice.
Uphill, somewhat short hike to the viewpoint, you can make it a longer hike if you continue on. Gorgeous view either way!
Thought this place had work out stations but was disappointed it didn't. Still nice for a walk or bike ride.
$20 to get in but worth it. Done really well. Gift shop and cafe all in one with the museum.

It is a nice cool historic park.Most of the batteries are closed but you can walk along them. There’s also a nice marsh for birdwatching.
The view is also great of the Delaware river. Also there’s a very nice playground and picnic area and the bathrooms are open. The parking lot isn’t in March but at least in November it was not crowded.

This park is a hidden gem among nc parks. Plus you don’t have to canoe in to camp. The shower house is awesome and the one section has camping that you can walk in, they even provide wheelbarrows to hall your gear the few hundred yards to the site!

Amazing for backpacking or day hiking in the wild ponies are fun to see. Plus you can park and do an easy two night backpacking trip. The Appalachian trail shelters makes camping easy as well. If you go in August you can find lots of wild berries!

One of the best places to go backpacking within 2 hours of Chapel hill. There typically isn't much traffic and the weather is wild so you can hike in the winter without much increase in gear. I recommend the Uwharrie trail and running a shuttle.

This park has a great campground and nice hiking trails. If you can camp and watch a moonrise from hanging rock I highly recommend it. Also, there are nice hiking trails to the waterfalls that are often overlooked by most people.

This is one of my favorite things in Pittsburgh. The gardens are well thought out and certein areas have exhibits that change. I also like going year after year and watching some of the plants grow. This is a very peaceful place.

The Pittsburgh Zoo isn't the largest I have been to but the exhibits are done well. The animals appear healthy and well maintained. I personally like the aquariam alot as well. Plus free parking is a nice thing in Pittsburgh.

Fantastic place for being so close to the triangle. The trails by the eno are beautiful just mind the snakes in the summer. There are also lots of bird life there as well. The picnicing facilities are nice as well!

I enjoy the ANF alot. there are some great hiking trails, a dark sky zone and the North country trail goes for almost 100 miles. the kinzu region is neat with the lake. and the allegheny river is fantastic.
A fun ski resort. Price isn’t bad and the snow was nice in the morning when we went. There are a lot of good hills for learning to ski and enough challenging ones to entertain experienced skiers
This gardens are pretty, mostly native plants. The massive garden chess set is a must see. You can access the trails outside the fenced gardens afterhours for running or walking as well.
I enjoyed this park alot. Being next to the Cape fear river and seeing the fish traps from the cliffs is neat. you can canoe camp here as well, though i haven't been able to do that.
This is a nice coastal forest with some nice trails for backpacking. The Nuesioktrail is just over 20 miles and nice one night trip if you run a shuttle.
For a park in a city they do a great job. Miles of trails, nosiy due to the airport but if you  need a quick getaway while in Raleigh this is the place!
This is a cute/fun place for kids 10 and under I would say. Our 9 month old loved it. Small but well managed with space. The tree house was a favorite.
I always enjoy going to this animal park. It is a cross between a petting zoo and a regular zoo. I enjoy you can feed the goats and camels as well.
nice short ride. however the path hasn't been connected under MLK yet. when it is it will be great linking umstead parks to the one at the fordham
The lake is really pretty, we stopped here on the way back from the outer banks and ate lunch. the picnic sites are nice as well
Has a great campground, awesome hiking trails and really neat views. The rock dome of the Stone Mountain is an instant classic!
This is a fun place to run, walk a dog, single tracks or just enjoy the stream. I recommend the pumpkin loop/vine for running.
The steam engine is cool! Going along the river was nice, lots of pretty views and along Fontana lake lead to great views too!
This lake is really cool! Shallow but has a unique habitat and clear water, but dark water. Also alligators in the canals!
Fantastic little park on the eno! The mill is a very cool piece of history and you can even buy corn meal there!
This is a nice park for a weekend backpacking trip or just a day trip to see the first oil well ever built!
We went to moonlight in the gardens. It wa a nicely done and very pretty. The gardens are small but fun!

This huge park offers a variety of recreational activities, hiking trails, scenic lookouts    and historical sites. South Orange Avenue bisects the park into two areas linked by a bridge. In southern areas there are two parking lots without restrooms. Here at a lookout you can have a scenic view of nothern NewJersey and Mahattan. Crest Drive starts here and is very popular and used for walking only. You can cross a bridge to enter southern area and to walk around Orange Reservoir. You can try boating and other recreational activities.

This place is much more improved and much better mantained than the time when I visited there three years ago. Clean trails for walking and well maintained and paved loop road for biking and driving. Nice picnic area with BBQ facilities.If you drive to Auto Overlook,  you can have commanding and scenic views of northern New Jersey including Patterson, the birth place of American industrial revolution.

The last battle in the north fought here during the American Revolutionary War, which eventually led to the birth of a new nation, the United States of America. If you stop by a visitor center, you will learn a lot about this historical event in American history. It has one of the best visitor centers in New Jersey, a separate building for class rooms, trails for a long walking and picnic areas.

An environmental park on the landfill. If you are interested in preservation of salt marsh, come to this place. It is a good place for education on the environment. It emeged by ending illegal dumping and attempting to protect thousands of acres of wetlands and open space. Easy trails for children and the elderly. It has 3.5 miles of walking trails, panoramic views and birds galore.

It is conveniently located. Our church members gather here to do barbeque and walk. Nice place to hike easy trails. It is surrounded by highways and residential areas. No scenic views but it offers several huge picnic areas around Hooks Creek Lake and viewing areas. Stop by Nature Center to learn about a natural history of this area. I like to hike the easy trails during winter.

By visiting this place you will realize that Edison was not only a great inventor but also a facilitator  of globalizaton. The institution of  research and development originated here. Well informed guides. Its space is small and can not accomodate more than 20 persons. A nice trail is accessible from here. Picnic tables and one unisex restroom. Limited parking lots.

This place is more than a park where you can walk, barbeque and do fishing. It is the place of historical landmark, the northern terminus of D&R Canal, which played a crucial role in development of central New Jersey. A small museum is needed in the park to tell the histories associated with this landmark.

It is a great joy to walk through an isolated swamp of wild life surrounded by hostile human development and activities. It has a good visitor center where you can learn a lot about the Swamp. Many trails here are wet and vulnerable to floods. The elevated paths are well maintained.

It is a cozy botanical garden. It is good for young couples with kids, old people and young lovers. It has three large parking areas. you may stroll around the garden with many kinds of plants. You may hike Ringwood State Park. From the garden you can enter several trails.

It has a secnic paved trail along the creek, which is meant for walkers only. It has clean restrooms, playgrounds, boat launch, a dog park and ample parking lots. You can enjoy music conerts. A Korean American ethnic festival, Chusuk festival, is annualy held here.

A great place to learn about how a family farm was run at the turn of the nineteenth century. It is good for group tours.A large picnic shelter and a big tent for rental.It has a fine visitor center. Staff members are well informed .

A drive- through park with a brook flowing through it. It has a new, beautiful bridge over the brook. But it needs more improvements. It needs water control. The soccer field is flooded and becomes a small pond, a habitat for ducks.

This place offers easy hiking trails for children and seniors. No stunning scenic views. It has a nice group pinic areas. Take yellow trail to "top of Tourne" where you can have a view of northern New Jersey.
Great place to walk around a flower garden and see an old mansion. Three large parking areas and clean restroom. If you want to hike, take the green trail which leads to  the Ramapo Mountains.
In the middle of an affluent town, they cultivated a "wilderness" for children to learn about nature  A lot of gardening progrms for children as well as adults. Short trails are available.
The highest point in New Jersey where you can see Pennslyvania and New York. Short trails around the lake.  Walking up to the top of the tower is not recemmended to old people.
If you are in Princeton University area, it is worthy for you stop by this site of the battle field of American Revolutionary War. To stroll the field is a good excercise.
It is an oasis surrounded by high ways and towns. Enjoy the cool trail along the lake and launch boats to the lake. Nice restroom and small parking area.
A park good for large groups who can enjoy multiple recreational activities. Park rangers are responsive and kind. It is clean and well maintained.
It is a nice place for us to learn about preindustrial green energy source---water. There is an excellent guide and teacher. I forget his name.
Clean park for recreational activites. Frequent police patrols. It offers access to hiking trails to Wanaque Ridge and Ramapo Lake.
It has an access to Pyramid Mountain. Large parking lot without restroom. No sign leading to parking lot. It could be improved.
This is a historical site where you can have a commanding view of  northern New Jersey and take a short trail with your lover.
It looks like a town beach. A place good for walking and family picnic. You can enjoy a magnificent view of the Hudson River.
Clean park maintained by nice people. It is free of dog poop. It is located along the Passaic River and its wetland.

4/13/2021

When we were arriving Branch Brook Park for the Cherry Blossoms Festival, we passed thru this splendid Cathedral church. Since it’s right by a side of the park, why don’t we pay a visit to this church?

So we visited Essex County Cherry Blossom Center and enjoyed the cherry blossoms all along Branch Brook Park Drive by Branch Brook Lake. Then up to the bridge above the lake we kept going for about a quarter mile, then we came to the church.

I really admired the beautiful structure and all the details of the church building! Everything seemed so sacred and beautiful to me even though I am not catholic. I wanted to go inside to pay a visit but the doors were locked.

When I walked along the left side of the church to keep admiring the building, I saw some signs on the side doors about the public time. And bravo! It’s open to prayers from 7:00am to 7:00pm during weekdays, and 8:00am to 1:00 on Sundays, 8:00am to 7:00pm on Saturdays. But oops, this door’s locked, too!

Then I saw some people going inside another smaller door at the rear. So I decided to go there and see my luck. Haha, the door could be opened and it led to an office with staff inside. I asked if I could pay a visit to the interior, the answer was yes. All I needed to do was to sign in on the visitor log.

So I felt blessed to be able to see the interior of the church!

Once inside, I felt serenity and sacredness. And it’s breathtaking!!

After visiting, I asked the staff if I could make a small donation, she pointed an Offering box hanging on the wall right by the exit. So I was happy to make an offering just for letting me see the beautiful interior!

BTW, you can drive directly to the church and park on the street.

Alert: No pets allowed.  I didn’t notice the sign so I took my dog for a walk with me until a gentleman kindly reminded me of it.

Updated 12/22/2019: I brought my family and friends for a walk today. This time we passed thru the long boardwalk connecting Delaware Rive and Palmyra Cove. Then I realized there’s a very long boardwalk leading to another side of the cove, where Pennsauken Creek runs thru to Delaware River. We thought we could go around the cove and get back to the nature center from there but couldn’t find a path after about 1/3 miles away from the Pennsauken Creek lookout. So we had to come the same way back.

Nevertheless, it’s very nice walk to enjoy different views and watch wildlife.

I first went here on 12/12/2019. As soon as I parked, I was attracted by the lively beautiful painting of the hawk on the park building!

When I started walking, I enjoyed the nice views of the Delaware River, bridges and park at such a pleasant sunny day. There are lots of access to the river from the trail. You can walk at the sandy shore at low tide time but must watch out as the tide fills up very quickly. This morning before noontime, I was able to walk on the riverside toward another bridge. But when I came back, the sandy walkable edge of the river was filled up with water already. However, I would suggest that you wear shoes to walk on the shore any time as there‘s too much junk washed onshore, you never know what you would step onto.

The boardwalks for birdwatching are really nicely built and maintained. Bring your binoculars or long lenses camera if you are a bird lover.

The trails are very easy for all ages. So I think it’s good for outdoor activities with families.
likes: Facilities & Services: Well-maintained boardwalks, Access to river
dislikes: Facilities & Services: No pet policy, Lack of path around cove

reviews_attraction.text:
Update on 1/12/2021:

Today I stopped by this area to explore the lake only to find out that besides the broken parking area, there was a flat area you may park though it didn’t look like a parking lot. And from there thru the boardwalk, there is a viewing deck. Yet downed trees were blocking the short path to it. Not a place for hiking. Scroll down to see the pictures I took.

01/09/2021

I saw this lake when I drove from Magnolia Rd to Brendan T. Byrne State Forest. So I decided to stop by and check it out on my way back. I found quite a big parking place right by the lake on Colemans Bridge Rd. From there I walked along the lake a little bit but the trail was full of puddles all along, not really easy to walk thru. So I just walked a couple hundred yards and turned back.

By the corner of the Lake on Magnolia Rd, there’s a sign of Pemberton Lake Wildlife Management Area with a small parking lot that’s almost unusable! But I saw there’s a boardwalk. Need to go back to check it out some time later.

Nevertheless, the lake is beautiful with abundant wildlife. Lots of wild geese sunbathing on the lake.

01/24/2021:

It’s my second time visiting Washington Crossing State Park NJ side. This time is one of  my pass-thru D&R Canal Trail hike.

The entrance to the parking lot by River Road is a little bit tricky. You have to turn into it at the traffic lights by the tavern instead of going straight. Parking lot is ample.

Walking in the park itself at my first trip was a live history book for me to learn about Washington’s Christmas Night Crossing. It is definitely a good place to take kids over for history education.

I am a hiker. So I really enjoy walking by the canal in winter when the bushes around have died out and vision in unlimited.

After finishing 9 miles by the Canal, I was lucky enough to see the sunset over the river by the bridge. The view was definitely gorgeous.

Next time I am going to go across the bridge to take the loop trail to PA side.

4/13/2021

Today when we visited the park, the beautiful cherry blossoms are at full bloom although a lot had started to fall after rain. The peak blooming time should be during last week and this week.

It was quite crowded although on a weekday. You may have to park on the street if parking lots are full.

The restrooms are all open. And there are a lot of portable toilets.

If you don’t mind walking, stop by the visitor center and enjoy the cherry blossoms around there. Then walk towards the lake thru under the bridge. You will get to see another kind of beautiful views with blossoms and the lake and reflections of the cathedral church. Or, cross the creek directly thru the crossway under the bridge, walk on another side of the lake, which will also lead you to the splendid cathedral church: Cathedral Basilica of the Sacred Heart. Don’t miss it!

01/30/2021

It’s the parking spot I chose for the #7 section of my Hiking-thru-D&R-Canal-Trail from Bull’s Island to/from Bridge Street, Stockton. After I finished my hiking in such a sunny day, I told myself why not take a walk in the park and see what’s over there. So I crossed the canal bridge, saw an park office building with a bigger parking lot. There’s a playground behind the building and many picnic tables by the river. There’s a boat launch by the canal with picnic area too. I am sure it is a very nice recreation area in summer.

To my surprise, there’s a pretty pedestrian bridge right across the river to Lumberville, PA. So I took a walk thru the bridge high across Delaware River. The river views are definitely gorgeous! Don’t miss a walk on the bridge if you plan for a trip to Bull’s Island area.

04/08/2021

Today I arrived at 10:22am with friends before the 11:00am open time. By the time the door was open, there was already a pretty long line. And the line kept building longer and longer.

Parking along the road is free. Admission ticket costs $12/adult, $8/senior/student/kid 5-17. Kids under 5 is free.

If you walk around the outside of the garden, you can get some perfect shots of the whole view of the garden.

From inside the Japanese House, you get to see a scope of the Japanese building structures and lifestyle.

The Garden has a koi pond with stream and waterfalls. You can pay $2 to buy a small cup of fish food to feed the koi.

After visiting the Japanese garden, you can stroll around the park and enjoy the beautiful blooming season in spring.

It is definitely worth the trip.

This preserve has a lake with lily pads blooming flowers all over! It’s really amazing! And there are wild blueberries everywhere! I didn’t get to walk too long as my daughter was whining about mosquito bites.  I will definitely be back and explore the whole area!

Updated 01/22/2020:

After the first hike in this park, I have been back with my dog or with my family several times. It’s become my most favorite place to hike. The trails are very well marked and very serene for hikes. I like to “get lost” in the trails so that I can hike longer time.

From the trails you will get to see a lot of bogs(ponds). Some sections could be flooded but you can always find an alternative to keep going.

More pictures uploaded on 10/27/2020.

The autumn view of the lake is always breathtaking. Check it out now! 10/30/2018

Update:

More pictures taken in a foggy day, 10/22/2020.

The trails are mostly accessible for all except some small trails thru the woods and the one by the lake, which I won’t recommend for people with walking disabilities.

There’s another trail thru the field by the entrance parking lot, where you will get to use the boardwalks in the woods. But use cautions after rain as they turn really very slippery. I slipped and fell once as soon as I stepped on the boardwalk one day. Later I had to mount my steps one by one, sometimes I even had to avoid walking on them.

05/18/2021:

Today we came for our 4th Delaware River Loop Trail hike from Lambertville, NJ to New Hope-Washington Crossing, PA, then back to Washington Crossing, NJ. So this is the bridge we pass thru again. Loved to see the spring colors changed from winter reflecting on the river!

It’s nice to walk on the bridge which connects two pretty small towns: Lambertville NI and New  Hope PA.

On the center of walkway of the bridge you can see the marked state line of PA and NJ. Views of the Delaware River are gorgeous from the bridge and the towns.

You may find it very relaxing walking in either of the towns.

It’s worth a hike here. On your hike, you will see several outlooks by the riversides: you can see the confluences
of the Delaware River and the Rancocas Creek, the skyline of Philadelphia, the views of harbors, as well as deer families, wild birds...Some area of the trail could be muddy, so better wear a pair of waterproof shoes to avoid getting shoes wet. It’s about a 2-mile trail around the island. They are marked at Red, Blue, Yellow or Black. But you won’t get lost anyway since it’s only an island. If you detour all the trails, you may make it a longer hike.

We went for hiking at the Botana Trail (South)  in this pine forest. We were the only ones hiking there, except that we saw an outdoor group training at the beginning and a lady riding a beautiful black horse when we went leaving. It was very quiet and serene park that we fully enjoyed the nature.

But watch out when you drive thru the sand road in the park. Some deep loose sand spots can trap your car, even with a SUV! So make sure you avoid driving thru such spots.

The park is virtually flat, but not much to see besides hiking and camping, I guess.

Pictures taken on 09/25/2020:

Love this beautiful park with all the trails very well-marked by colors. From all the parks I have hiked, I must say this is the park with best-marked trails!

I hiked thru all the trails: green, yellow, white and blue. I covered totally 8.2 miles.

There are a lot of parking spaces with lots of recreational areas, a beach by the lake and some campsites, picnic areas.

The hiking trails have lots of board stairs or board walkways. But people with climbing problems can walk on the roads.

05/20/2021:

Came for my last Delaware River Loop Trail hike from Frenchtown, NJ to Uhlerstown-Lumberville, PA back to Bull’s Island Recreation Area, 10 miles (skipped the NJ canal part because I did that already and friends couldn’t take a 18.9-mile long hike).  So we crossed this bridge. The view is beautiful as on other bridges. In a hot day, the breeze from the river makes it much cooler and pleasant.

If I live nearby, it would be my regular everyday morning and evening strolling place.

The trails in this nature preserve  are in a wooded area, have some slopes up and down, which makes hiking more fun. When you go into the swamp, it seemed like you are in a jungle, so it’s pretty hard to walk through the swamp. I would suggest stay in the woods.

Many people unleash their dogs to play in the brook, so use caution. I was told that early in the morning at around 8:00am is the busiest time, because people come before going to work.

It’s my first time walking in this park. There are easy and short trails & lakeside boardwalks to walk with some historic sites to see. There’s a pretty size of playground for kids to play with seating for parents to watch. And there are lots of seatings around the park. There are also some kayaking access to Rancocas Creek. See some of the pictures I posted on Google Map.

It’s my first time hiking here in the woods. Due to the lack of marks at crossroads and Google Map’s misleading directions, a hiker as me even got lost several times. The trails are just like a puzzle. I saw three girls who also lost directions to the swinging bridge. Even though, overall it’s a woody park you can enjoy hiking either alone or with family or friends.

Today when we hiked to the tower, we were lucky that it’s open to the public with someone there watching. It’s usually fence with alarm and cameras. Last year when my dog approached the fence, it triggered the alarm. But today when I go halfway on the tower, I saw such open view of the pine barrens! It’s really beautiful view!

A one-mile loop walk without much shade. So walk early in the morning or at a cloudy day in hot weather.  It’s very easy walk for kids and older people with all the benches by the trail and the observatory places. Also it would be fun to observe the wildlife. Bring a pair of binoculars for it.

1/30/2021

I passed thru this site on my canal trail hike today. The red houses attracted me to walk around a little bit. Then I found out it’s a mill park. A canal lock is right by side. Lots of parking and some picnic tables in it. Seems full of history to me.

We went there hiking and fishing with friends. Loved the serenity around the twin ponds with a family of 5 swans swimming gracefully on them, and the beautiful water lilies!

The short hike to the mountain top was fun with elevation for me from a FLAT land. 😄

This park definitely has a very good and open view of Raritan River. It looks neat. Must be very relaxing to enjoy a nice sunny day here.

But I saw some sprays on signs, broken trail lights...That took away a star from my review.

09/27/2020:

When we arrived with our dog at the park, we realized pets were not allowed anywhere around the park. So we had to find a place to hike with our dog and the staff were friendly and told us the nearby Jocky Hollow.
It’s a part of the pine barrens and the 50-mile Batona Trail that’s closer to my home. It’s close walk to the campground. You can virtually plan for short or long hikes at your will here.
The park itself is quite muddy in winter. There’s a pavilion for picnic. Parking lot is not very big. Right across the road is a kayak rental place.

Small local playground where moms can take the kids for a day to run, play and have fun. This playground is mostly popular with the Hasidic Jewish community families as they live all around this area. Don't get me wrong, there are other mix families who visit as well.

The park has some rules that need to be followed. It's not a dog friendly park and that's a good thing due to, there are many people with dogs and don't clean up after them. So there shouldn't be any dog poop and that should make it safer to just sit on the grass. To be honest, I've see people still take their dogs there. There's always those who just don't care or don't read the signs posted out front.

I believe the name for the park, Jacob's Ladder is the connection between the earth and heaven that the biblical Patriarch Jacob dreams about during his flight from his brother Esau, as described in the Book of Genesis. - This is mostly a Hasidic Jewish community, so this makes more sense because it's part of the Old Testament.

One of few bridges that connect into Manhattan from Queens area. One of the best parts about this Bridge is, there is no toll for it. Yet again, one of the worst parts of this Bridge is there is no toll for it and the traffic can be horrendous at times. So you got the good with the bad. It also has the tram way/cable carts that connects to Roosevelt Island.

This part of the review below is from a Google search.

The Queensboro Bridge, also known as the 59th Street Bridge – because its Manhattan end is located between 59th and 60th Streets – and officially titled the Ed Koch Queensboro Bridge, is a cantilever bridge over the East River in New York City that was completed in 1909. Construction started: 1901 and total length is 3,724′ feet long.

Did you know: The Queensboro Bridge is one of New York City's great bridges, along with the Brooklyn Bridge and a few others that connect into Manhattan.

Nice place for a family outing, if your ok with the new rules. Sea lion shows are funny and enjoyable but the changes are not. It's been frustrating that construction has been going on for so long. We are talking about, since Hurricane Sandy. Some exhibited are closed. They use to give members free parking, now after two hours they start to charge you. If your a member and the parking lot is full, guess what; you need to look for parking outside on your own. People come and park their cars in the lot and don't come for the aquarium tour, it's just for parking. You use to get a discount for the 4D movie, now they charge even members full price. So money has become more important then members fees. That's my reason for stopping to become a member with them. I have since changed my rating due to these facts

I came to this part of the park back in April 2011 to take my engagement pictures with my wife to be. I need to add, this part of the park is very large and has something for all ages. You have a lot of walking trails, jogging areas and benches to sit on and take in the views. You should also visit the Soldiers’ and Sailors’ Monument for picture taking. If you look at my pictures posted, you can see it offers many areas to take nice photos.

To be honest, with all the concrete jungle that just a few 100 feets away from this location, as you enter this park you feel that you're in a whole new world. I recommend this area for an enjoyable experience.

The Bayonne Bridge is the oldest arch bridge in New Jersey area. It was built back in 1920 I believe. Nowadays it's a work in progress. This is one of a few ways to cross over to the Bayonne New Jersey area.

The new construction work to raise the Bridge is long overdue and at the same time, the work is horrendous on traffic and autos/trucks/busses. At times you don't know if the Bridge is open or closed. The $15 dollar fee doesn't help the cause either. Plus you need an ezpass to go over or get a ticket in the mail as there is no longer any ticket booth clerks. We can only hope, things get better in time.

Local small playground for both kids and some adult activity. Adults have basketball courts and hand/paddle ball courts. Kids have a few choices to choose from as well. They have small toddler swings and larger set as well for the bit older kids, a large set of small village monkey bar with bridges, slides and ladders to climb on up. They also turn on a small set of sprinklers for cooling down the kids for summer time. They have a small building that has bathrooms as well. Theres no BBQing, dogs, drinking alcohol beverages or smoking permitted as park rules are posted.

Nice museum to visit. The art and exhibits are ok if your into those things. They change the exhibits from time to time. So check their web site for up coming events and new exhibits. It's not my cup of tea but it's ok. The surrounding area is very nice with Brooklyn Botanical Garden, Prospects park, Prospects park zoo, Brooklyn Library. Just dont wander off around the neighborhood unless you know your way around here.

If I'm going to a museum, then I'll go to the better of all in the Museum of Natural History in New York City, Manhattan area.

Love the pool and I can also remember being a young boy and coming here with my brothers and sisters to enjoy the cool water for summer time. So I have been coming to this pool/park area for over 40 years now. The views are great and the pool just adds more fun to this park/neighborhood. You have a big parking lot under the bridge, playground area for the kids behind the pool area, a skateboard/rollerblades arena, tennis court and large open grass area for sunbathing or picnicking. Plus a lot of trees for those who want to stay out of the sun.

The famou Cyclone rollercoaster ride. I mean this is an iconic ride and been a big part of Brooklyn New York City for many years now. You also have many different other activities and stops to make in this area. Many places to eat at, many stops to entertain yourself. There's so much going on here. From the NY Aquarium, Astro-Land Amusement park with many rides, the Wonder Wheel, world famou Nathan hotdogs and you can't forget the long wooden board walk to enjoy the views of the sea. Hit like/thumbs up if you enjoyed my reviews.

Basketball playground for the local kids to enjoy a day of activities. You really only really notice the full size basketball courts, one on each side of the park. They are separated due to the small hill they where made on. There's also a few sets of beaches to sit on. There are two entrances/exits on both ends of these basketball court, one for each court. From time to time you get the local families and/or Hasidic Jews to sit on the benches to enjoy the weather around them, not much else to this location.

Dumbo area in Brooklyn, New York City location. Nice place to visit and spend the day just walking, taking in the views of your surroundings and many places to visit plus places to eat at. You can visit pebbles beach and take in the views of passing boats or just sit on a bench and look over to the Manhattan skyscrapers. Visit the Jane's carousel, Gleason's Boxing GYM which is the oldest Boxing GYM in America. Just come for yourself and enjoy what Dumbo has to offer.

Nice little Dock area where you can come and enjoy some beautiful scenic views and surrounding area. You can see the Bayonne Bridge from here. You can enjoy a few tugboats and boats alike that past by. Just to sit and enjoy the ocean water views are always something to add relaxation to any person inner soul. People also come here to fish but I'm not sure about eating them but to each his own. You also have a few places close by too enjoy as well.

I like the new Bridge and we have noticed some major improvements but at the same time. The old Goethals Bridge had nice workmanship and class.

Don't get me wrong, I really like the two Bridges that offer 3 wider lanes to travel on both ways nowadays. The smoother road also makes it safer and nicer to travel on. Plus let's not forget the walkway. At rush hour time, it can become a bit hectic with traffic but that's New York/New Jersey for you.

The good old Manhattan Bridge to get over to downtown Manhattan area, either by train, car, bus, biking or walking. When your across, your at China Town and walking distance to Little Italy areas. As soon as your over, there's a few shopping and eating businesses on both sides of the bridge. For the rush hour time, get ready to wait in traffic. The bridge did get a make over years ago but if you ask me, there's still a lot of work to be done.

Came by here after my visit from Calvary church with some new found friends I made after a stay in their Airbnb.

This is not normal from where I live at in Brooklyn, New York City. So this was a pleasant surprise just to see and a pleasure to cross over it. On the day I came and saw it, it had rained over the previous night and that morning as well. So the River/Creek was higher and faster then normal. It was just a delight to cross over.

This was worth making a stop here from my visit in the Lancaster area. You have a few trails to explore and the sights of the River, the water flowing down stream and midsize to small waterfalls added a delightful treat to the eyes. They have a few small parking areas to park your vehicle and take a walk around the surrounding area. Just take my word for it, make a stop and enjoy the views yourself.

The Rose Garden is always a must visit area and more if your coming to the Brooklyn Botanical Garden with the opposite sex. I mean who doesnt like to see many roses and I mean some rear ones at that. The colors and the many different in size and shapes. That's rigth, I mean shapes because you'll see roses with lesser Rose flower palette then others, some are so small and others are so large.

View is nice park area to just see some nice views but the water is not always the best color. New York City water ways from all five boroughs have been bad for sometime now. The ground are ok most of the times but there are those other days that it could use the park department to clean things up. My English Bulldog dog seems to really likes this park area right next door to Domino's park.

Local kid playground, parents bring there little one's here in the mid-afternoon hours. (swings, slides & ect..)My only concern is that you need to keep your eyes on your kids due to, this playground is on a very busy traffic street. So if the little one runs out the park, it could be an accident. They also have a basketball court as well where the teens, young adults come to play also.

This was a visit worth taking from Lancaster area. The sight is beautiful to say the least. The sight of the mountains in the background and lake/River from the top overview was breathtaking. You don't always get to see these things in life. So when you do, it's time to sit and enjoy the view. I serve a mighty God who paints a picture unlike what anyone ever can.

Small park area with a boardwalk path that leads around the park. The walk around the park is about two to four minutes total depending on how fast you walk it. They have lots of plants and different trees. It provides a few benches to sit. Due to the trees, it provides much shaded areas. It's not doggie pet friendly and bikes are not permitted inside this park.

Small corner park to just sit at. It's a bit noisy with traffic from the Brookly Queens Expressway aka BQE. You also have noise from the B or D train that crossesover the Manhattan Bridge. Not the best park to un-whine at due to the noise but it's ok to just take in a breather and move on. There's another small park across the street with basketball courts.

Like this park but the neighborhood is a 50/50 shot. You can enjoy the park and areas close by but don't wander off around the neighborhood unless you know your way around or where your going. There was a time I didn't come here but time has gotten much better. There are a few attractions to visit at this park and surrounding areas.

I've come to like the new bridge but the traffic is still the same. It just seems to slow down around this area. So it's a new look but same results all around. I took some pictures one morning coming off the bridge. The sunrise looked beautiful but to be honest the pictures don't show the real look that morning.
Very nice place to go visit and take a stroll around the park. I came here to take my wife and mine engagement pictures. This area and the surrounding area are very good place.

I am an opera singer. So, a design museum is the most uninteresting thing imaginable to me.  Therefore, when I discovered this place I couldn't believe how much of a fascinating Museum it is. This is the original mansion on Fifth Avenue which has lovely little parties in summer with champagne and everything under the sun. It is very sad that it seems to be closed indefinitely.

The pastor at this Episcopal Church, Father John, is eloquent. This is a warm, hospitable church on the Upper East side. They welcome Catholics and Protestants alike. Fr. John got on my case about not being vaccinated after Mass, and it ruined the beauty and worship I received from the mass. I wish the media in general would relax about Covid vaccines.

I like classic movies like Sunset Boulevard, and Cat on a Hot Tin Roof. This Magnificent museum has three full floors. An amazing amount of movie history, including silent movies! Television cameras. old movie cameras. Excellent place to eat pizza outside with wide-open Avenues. I'm going to be going back to this Museum constantly!

This is a superb museum with a lovely wait staff. I recommend highly the rebel women exhibition on presently. These are women from the late 1700s to Mid twentieth century who could definitely be an example to all of us. The movie on the actual finding and establishment of Manhattan is a must-see.

An absolutely spectacular Roman Catholic Church of neoclassical design. Plan to go at high mass when Fr. Bergen or Fr. Yesselonia are conducting the sermons. I truly wish the excellent choir would perform more traditional classics and get out of the 20th Century repertoire!!!

The largest church on Earth. One must go inside during the day when you can see the massive structure of this place. So many separate rooms on the side! Don't use your cell phones. The place is too huge. Take your digital camera.

A very bucolic clean and lovely park right in the heart of the Charming Cobble Hill. It is never noisy. An excellent place to take all ages of children. With a tiny little historical mention of Brooklyn at the front entrance.

Beautifully preserved treasure of Roman Catholicism sandwiched in between Chinatown and the Bowery. There was one other person besides me in the sanctuary. The adjacent graveyard is great, but closed to the public.

The 7th Floor Cafe and Restaurant is excellent. The Andy Warhol Exhibition on two floors is not to be missed. I love the gallery guides there. Try to go when it's not crowded. Splendid views of Freedom Tower!

The design of the building is the art form itself. Additionally, the Robert mapplethorpe retrospective is very provocative and unique. I am thrilled that the Guggenheim is presenting this to the public.
the pool is beautiful. The pool is closed. The woman wouldn't let me in because I didn't have a key. It's a beautiful pool. But you have to have a lock and a key and look good in a bathing suit...
Everyone, regardless of their heritage or faith, should see the current Auschwitz exhibition. Incredibly detailed. I prefer using the Acoustiguide tour. Then, when you're through, eat in the Cafe.
Original Shakespeare. Original Charles Dickens books. The Vedi  exhibition was unfortunate to me. I thought it was going to include most of his life. It only included a Otello and Falstaff.
The American history that one receives by visiting this museum is phenomenal. The front two rooms were constructed in 1719 remain as they were then. George Washington drank beer here.
This is a breath-takingly beautiful Anglo Catholic church with phenomenal acoustics and a superb choir. I like to sit in the middle; and to me, I have been transported to Europe.
Raoul Wallenberg gave sanction to thousands of Jewish people. A small concrete announcement on the ground in the front of a large park in Forest Hills.
80% of the New York Mayors have lived in this Mansion. Bloomberg did not. I have seen it go through many changes. A beautiful view of the East River.
The interior of the Archdiocese, St Patrick's is spectacularly beautiful. Take a little extra time and see the statue of Saint Therese of Lisieux.
When I went, only the second floor had an exhibition. I learned an immense amount of information. Every artist was making a political statement.
The new MOMA is sensational. They have expanded the museum by 33%.  There are many artists I've never heard of.  Wait staff is pleasant.
A very sweet tiny austere Roman Catholic Church. You do not take pictures there. 116th Street. A dangerously dark Roman Catholic Church.
A wonderful bucolic oasis east of Gramercy Park. If one gets in the middle, one would almost not be aware they were in a large city.
George Washington walked through here. Here is where you buy your tickets to go to the Statue of Liberty and Ellis Island.
This is a monument in honor of the civil war. Honoring the south as well as the North. Nice views of the Hudson River.
Magnificent view. Very quiet on Randall's Island. A beautiful way to escape from the noise and stress of New York.

The largest municipal park in the country- tons of trails, classic architecture, and history all around. A few museums, and performance venues also dot the park. Some of the original buildings and various other oddities from the Worlds Fair and US Centenial can be found throughout the grounds. Read up before a visit- you'll be glad you did.
The park was originally property that the City bought outside of its city limits to protect the water supply in the Schuylkill river. Other pieces of property were eventually added. As the City expanded- the boundaries encompassed the park. Some of the homes near and around the park were used by the wealthy to 'escape' the City and the Yellow Fever that tended to break out during the summer months due to poor sanitation. Also make sure to checkout the Water Works (originally pumped water to the city, later served as an aquarium, pool, and now museum), Boat House Row, and the Schuylkill River Trail- all which offer some spectacular views.

(AKA the Mutter Museum) worth the adventure and the cost of admission. Containing a wide variety of medical maladies presented in a respectful and educational manner. Go during a low volume time as there's a lot to see and read. My favorite parts were the cross section slide of Einstein's brain, various conjoined twins, and the wall of skulls. For public transit take the regional line to 30th street and hike it to 22nd and Chesnut. Driving? Park at the garage on Chesnut between 22nd and 21st, or on Market (same blocks). May not be the best museum for small children.

I love Franklin square.... the only down side is it is difficult to reach as a pedestrian. You really have to dodge some cars! There's a nice fountain, seasonal food offerings, a playground, mini golf, and even a carousel! If you're feeling brave- you're footsteps away to walking over the ben franklin bridge! My kids love telling people they walked to new jersey.
Near by is the Constitution Center, and down a few blocks are the race street and cherry street piers... check out the fringe arts on Columbus Blvd. Too!

Participated in an overnight tour and sleep over with the cub scouts. The most decorated ship in the US navy and had served in multiple conflicts since world war 2. It offers a perspective of what it must have been to serve abroad this ship. Knowledgeable tour guides provide a wealth of information. Those staying for the sleep over- prepare for cramped and loud overnight conditions. Worth it for the experience of the boat, history, and Philadelphia skyline views.

A lot of exhibits really geared towards school aged kids. It's frequently crowded. Consider visiting a time where there are less school trips. Some of the exhibits need to be refurbished and really show wear and tear or outright do not work. Check their calendar for special events. There are occassionally events held at night for adults. My faviorite parts are the observatory up on the 4th floor and the planetarium which also hosts it's own events.

A little expensive for a smaller museum however tickets include admission to the USS Bucuna (submarine) and the USS Olympia (know as one of the first US warships that brought the US to the world stage during the Mexican American war and deciding factor at the battle of Manila. Kids enjoyed the museum. Has a fully functioning boat workshop. Consider trying to find on street parking on front st. Or market st. Crossover. Much cheaper then the garage.

Its free- and arguably one of the best zoos in the tristate area. There's a variety of different species that you dont find at a typical community zoo. Theres also a great park, play ground, and a little lunch spot. There are clean public bathrooms and its a great spot to check out on your way in or out from the shore. Make sure to check it out! Sometimes parking can be a challenge. Consider visiting early.

Dollar for dollar I think this is a great museum. It's run by Drexel university and I believe this is a better experience then the better known Franklin institute. Check out the new baby dinosaurs exhibit- my kids loved it. The docents are knowledgeable and host little interactive stands throughtout exhibit space. The food in the cafe is sub par so consider eating before or after your visit.

It's part of one of the largest urban parks in the United States. It has beautiful trails, a variety of mansions from when the 18th and 19th centuries 1% needed to escape the cities yellow fever outbreaks. There's some really great views of the skyline. Also make sure to check out one of the few remaining Centenial Buildings now occupied by the Please Touch Museum.

Got a good deal on a hidden gem. Small location with 3 floors of bug themed exhibits. Good for smaller kids. There's a 7000sf butterfly pavilion that the kids really enjoyed. Free on site parking. It's probably about a 1.5-2 adventure. There's a cafe, small gift shop and you can host kids parties there. Look for significant discounts on Groupon/ Living social.

Great panoramic views from 12 stories above ground level. Now has a small dog park and resturant (that was not open during our visit). Park in the garage or walk in and take the elevator up. Also added a new 90bazillion inch TV on the side of one of the buildings showing episodes of the office- and who doesn't need that on a January day??

The waterworks functioned as a water pump to a reservoir which is now the site of the Philadelphia art museum. Currently the site hosts a small free museum which is worth a stop. The site once hosted an Aquarium, recreation center, pool. The buildings upstairs host(ed) a restaurant and is highly sought out for weddings and other events.

Camped here with my kids during the weekend between Christmas and new years. We stayed in a lean to which was pretty nice and had propane heat. We were able to hike the park and check out some area attractions. There are heated shower houses and coin operated laundry. Worth checking out. Reasonably priced.  Close to shore points
