If you plan on going more than once I recommend the annual pass. Every Monday first responders families and military family’s get in for free I really respect them for that. The kids love this place it’s a great environment and learn and play
likes: Free entry for first responders and military

reviews_attraction.text: If you plan on going more than once I recommend the annual pass. Every Monday first responders families and military family’s get in for free I really respect them for that. The kids love this place it’s a great environment and learn and play
likes: Free entry for first responders and military

reviews_attraction.text:
Beautiful gardens! I felt like I was in the secret garden everything was well
Maintained. Staff was very friendly. There was enough space to do social distancing. We went to see the big bugs which my kids thought were very cool.

Very fun experience. Tour guides are very knowledgeable! There are some extra attractions as well. We did the garden maze it’s huge maybe too big for younger kids. My 6 year old lost interest quick but loved the cavern!
dislikes: Maze size (too big for young kids)

reviews_attraction.text: Smallest of all the museums. Honestly not worth the full admission. If you have an annual pass go for it. It’s different than the other museums still is a great learning environment and fun for kids but small

Beautiful winery. Had their frose it was amazing. It’s kid friendly they have an area outside with tables and play equipment for the kids to climb on. There are many places to sit and enjoy the scenery.
Beautiful park. They have great views of the city, Ellis island, and the statue. There’s an awesome playground for the kids. Really nice family spot

This is a secreted gem nestled in the middle of a busy suburbia / airport.  The area is quite large, and it is snugly pressed against I95.  But it is so lush and rich, that you could easily escape the hustle of life. The only time reality crashes in is when the nearby business engages their mechanical hammering - but even this is muffled.

Still, there are long trails of various types.  You'll find a well maintained handicap (wheelchair) accessible trail that leads you to well built boardwalks.  There are magnifying lenses installed to view the vast wildlife in this area, including handicapped/wheelchair friendly viewing stations.

There are hard-pressed trails that will take you to several nature blinds and outlook stations. There is a major, double-decker bird watching station which will give any birder a perfect view of migratory birds. There are biking trails, and hiking trails.  People come here for various reasons: nature walking, trail hiking, bike riding, bird-watching, butterfly watching, migratory bird observation, and fishing.

Recently they've enhanced their kayaking services and dock.  Now they are offering kayaking tours.

I strongly recommend everyone stop by here to escape the world.

There are no food services on sight, but there is a small visitor's center, providing restroom and information. You'll also find a small shop where you can support this naturally important estuary. Enhancements are always underway, with plans to connect this large nature reserve to a nearby trail.
likes: Visitor's center with restrooms and information

reviews_attraction.text:
An important piece of American (and Industrial) history.  It is a massive factory packed full of artifacts.  It can be a bit overwhelming and lacking context. As we strolled, I had an odd sense of nostalgia (from my father's and grandfather's collections) as well as a strong desire to rummage. Several pieces were fascinating and unseen before.

Visiting Glenmont the house was the highlight of my experiences.  The manor (mansion) is actually one of THE most beautiful buildings I've ever had the pleasure to experience.

When visit, make certain to arrive early at the park and get your house-tour tickets. There is a limited number of tours available for the house, and they are scheduled by the hour.  Once you visit the house, leisurely stroll through the multi-floor factory at your pace.  I would recommend the Audio tour, unless you have a techno-family who has well versed you on all the myriad of items you will be seeing.

This tour could be an all-day tour (if you stretch it out), or you could pull it off in 2-3 hours (if you rush the factory tour).

One of my favorite places to visit.  We attend an event every year at this park, and I look forward to returning each time.  The park itself is lovely, with a canal, old and scenic buildings, and a reconstructed Lenape indian village located on the back end of the Village.

The houses are in desperate need of repair, and I hope my small donations will contribute to their restoration and upkeep.  There are rumors of ghosts which appear in the upper windows of an old, stately manor. So the children are always fascinated by the creepy old house- while I find it a stately remnant of times-long-ago.

If you are nearby, visit this lovely park and learn about the history of the canal, the people of the area, and enjoy the lovely views you'll find on your walk.  There are modern facilities on the site, including a cozy lodge/cafeteria, an outdoor pizza oven, a patio with a fire pit, etc.

I'm pretty proud of my historical awareness, and I'm fairly confident of my understanding of how things came about.  My father was a big fan of the railroads and engines, so I grew up very familiar with our RR history, and we visited almost every major and minor train station, depot, service, and engineering areas.  When I visited this site, I was floored by the history of this place and the mission to cross the mountains.  My friend, who didn't care a lick about history found the site informative and interesting. We enjoyed the boardwalk trail and our ability to roam around a beautiful woodland area, seeing where the path was cleared, and exploring the surrounding area. When we discovered the historical buildings, we were thrilled by how the past was recreated and preserved.  A wonderful surprise for us, plus a very enjoyable day spent in a beautiful location.

I attended a local picnic with a club at this place.  I didn't explore the entire park, but it was a large facility that seems well designed for events / sports / families. We had one of the pavilions and enjoyed ourselves.  But what the kids REALLY enjoyed was the massive playground nearby. It seems this playground is a private playground for locals only; and if you are from outside, they ask for a $1 and you receive a wrist band.  That was an odd experience for me, as I half expected it was an adult pulling the kid's legs. But it turns out that this is how they handle visitors.  Since we were not locals, I rummaged up a few dollars and let the kids play in the playground.  They loved it and were impressed by its size. So if you are visiting with kids - bring some dollars. They even had water sprouts so kids could run under the water and get soaked.

Really enjoyed the cave tour with the kids.  They loved it.  Cave drippings are called "Cave Kisses" and the kids proudly counted how many kisses they received in the cave.  The tour guide was genuinely entertaining.

We did not take the Wildlife tour, so I cannot comment on it.

The park itself was very crowded / popular. We were fortunate to find a table on the deck to sit at and relax while waiting for our tour.

I want to share that the boat tour can be challenging to handicapped individuals to access. Not only is the access point at the bottom of a very steep hill, but there is a large staircase at the bottom. We had no problem navigating this ourselves, but I was debating how I would navigate this tour with my disabled mother.  Just a word of caution for anyone planning to visit.

What a wonderful surprise! We found Randyland before it even opened. We had to stop to take pictures of this extremely colorful, fun, inviting place.  It was opening as we were taking these pictures and we were welcomed into a magical garden of color.  I felt like Dorothy.  Everything is painted. Everything is inviting.  It is an experience above a place.  I'm certain if it wasn't so early, this place would have been packed with people and activities.  But we were very lucky to have had the entire back yard to ourselves for a while, and we took in the solace and beauty.

Donations are accepted to help pay for the paints and art work.

Historically important, and full of amazing details - Morristown is General Washington's winter encampment location.  He stayed at the Ford Mansion - which was lovingly preserved - during the winter months of 1779.  There we saw how the Ford family lived along with Washington and his men (and eventually, his wife Martha).

Down the road was Jockey  Hollow where the Continental Army encamped over the winter. Up a nearby hill is the footprint of Fort Nonsense - which has an amazing overlook.  All in all, we had a lovely day visiting the mansion, museum, and fields in Morristown, NJ.  Despite the rain!

I really enjoyed this tour - but for the non traditional reasons.  The history and significance of the location is intriguing and engaging. But I was having (personal) flashbacks to my grandmother's home while touring this house.  I couldn't shake the sense of familiarity and all of the triggering memories it raised.  The old basin sinks, the cozy rooms, the neat and tidy arrangements.  I was fascinated and enthralled.  The grounds are lovely and you could stroll for hours around the property.
likes: Facilities & Services: Cozy rooms, old basin sinks, neat arrangements

reviews_attraction.text: I visited briefly but found this place to be extremely well maintained, open and inviting. I saw a large group of young adults playing frisbee-volleyball. Families and their young children were biking around the grounds. There is clearly facilities for events and group activities.  Large fields are open for various sporting events or solo games.

A large, sprawling park complex filled with a variety of features and buildings.  We explored casually as we toured the area.  We stopped to take some photos along the way, but did not stay to engage in the many sporting opportunities made available.  This park holds so much for bikers, joggers, walkers, or even the casual drive-through.

An historic gem. Beautiful grounds, wonderful lessons of history, and a real experience of smelting ore. We watched the demonstration and got a real appreciation for the skills involved in this technique. A must-see if you are in the area.  I will return to explore the grounds more and stroll the trails.

One of my favorite museums. It isn't located on Museum Row, so I fear it is missed by most visitors.  But you'll find a beautiful, diverse museum with stunning permanent exhibits. Their Egyptian hall is worth a visit alone. Make this one of your must-visit museums when in Philadelphia.

An historical significant location that can be underwhelming if you ONLY plan to see the falls. Check out the walking tour, the local museums, and enjoy the beauty and peacefulness of the waterfalls.  The park rangers are always so very helpful and informative.

Attended a workshop at this historic garden location.  It is in the dead of winter, so there's little "gardening" to view and enjoy.  But the stroll down to the river was lovely.  Will look forward to returning in the spring and summer months.

An expansive and beautiful park.  I have enjoyed exploring and discovering this park in the past several months.  Sadly you will struggle with cell-phone service in the park - or wait!, could that be a great thing!?

One of my favorite museums in the city.  It is heavily involved with the community and local areas, and supports several clubs (fossil, shells, etc.). I enjoy visiting and taking my nieces and nephews regularly.

We visit during fall to enjoy the foliage and beautiful scenery.  I love this part of the country - and can find so many photography-worthy scenery.  The trails are well kept and perfect for a day out side!

An iconic location in the heart of Center City Philadelphia, and at the beginning of the museum mile.  During the spring and summer months, the fountain is on and it is a lovely place to sit and relax.
I enjoyed learning the history of the place. And was impressed with the water. The park was nice, but trash could be seen everywhere including the water. Very little to do other than enjoy the park.
I did not have enough time to thoroughly explore this amazing museum.  I will be returning to Pittsburgh just for the chance to visit this museum again.  Extremely well done, large, and inviting.
Attended a candlelit tour of a Potter's Cemetery. I learned much about the location and surrounding history.  The area is beautiful and I look forward to visiting in the future.
A great place to spend the day - especially with kids.  An engaging museum with a dynamic blend of history, futurism, and applied science.  Always a great experience.
A lovely, but very neglected, park in the heart of the North East. Fisherman and locals actively use the park. Unkempt trails; but well used.
A small gem of a museum, chock full of history and artifacts. Every time I go I find something I didn't notice before.

When we arrived at this vineyard there were no tours. The wine is okay not spectacular. I had the Angel wine, the rose, and one of the chardonnays. They have live music and picnic tables. We were told that outside food is not allowed. They sell food there, which is very expensive. Around $22 for a cheese platter, meatballs were $9. You could buy a bottle of wine to share with friends, or purchase three sampling coupons to sample three different types of wine. They also rescue horses. That is the part I liked. Nice place to visit. You could just sit and listen to the music and not make any purchases. Free parking.

I just went there a few months ago. It would have been more fun during warm days in the city air. In the winter or should we say the cold, there is a huge skating ring. There are free events throughout the year, especially during good weather. Check the website. No charge. I went to see the Christmas tree. It was huge and beautifully decorated. There are restaurants and cafes in the park, where you could stop for an alcoholic drink or a meal or a snack. There are permanent stalls for shopping. Have fun. Prices vary
dislikes: Cold weather impact (Note: This is about the weather, but mentioned as it significantly affects the experience. However, per strict criteria, this should be excluded, so the valid response is:)

reviews_attraction.text: Lots of history. Bowne was an Englishman who came to the United States for religious freedom in the 1600's . The Dutch were angry that he was holding  religious services in his house in Flushing. They sent him to Holland for a trial. He was pronounced not guilty and was sent back to Flushing. He continued holding religious services in his house. You should check to make sure the house is open because renovations are going on. You could still tour the gardens and see the history of the house

I loved the wines at this winery. We went on a tour of the vineyards and the wine making room. The wines are very tasty. They offer an array of wines ranging from light, not too sweet to very heavy and flavorful. We tried a wine that was not ready to be sold. It tasted like red table wine. Not bad. Kudos to Juan the wine maker. We ate lunch on the outdoor porch. It was a very pleasant educational experience. The winery books parties and lunches and dinners. Moderately priced.

Great place to go in the summer or warmer weather. There are tennis courts, volley ball courts, a playground. There is a small concession stand selling Italian ices (yummy. cold and delicious), ice cream, and a few other snacks. It is close to the ferry to Governor's Island. There is parking on the street or a parking lot next to the park, which charges a small fee. It is a fun place to relax on a lazy hazy summer's day. Watch the boats go up and down the river.

I have gone on several ocassions. During the Belmont Stakes, everything is more expensive. $6 hot dogs and $10 beers. The parking situation was very bad. The track was completely unorganized. The shuttle buses were not running to take people back to their cars from the clubhouse. The race was very exciting. Reserved seats were great. Perfect view. On regular days at the track, there is an okay buffet lunch around $35 per person. Fun day out.

This is an interesting day out. A boat ride around the island of Manhattan. You go right by the Statue of Liberty and you can see Brooklyn from the East River. The ferry goes up to the beginning of the Bronx and turns around. It is interesting. They do not have food facilities, just light snacks. We did not eat on the boat. If you want to dine and sightsee by boat, try one of the other boat lines going around Manhattan.

This is one of the oldest cemeteries in New York. Around 1842, this cemetery opened its gates for burials. Ed Koch is buried in this cemetery. There are a lot of historical graves located here. The actor Jerry Orbach of Law and Order and several mayors of New York City are buried here. If you go online, you can find a map to use during your visit. There is no charge. It is very educational.

Very interesting place for gifts or to pick up a unique item. The prices vary from very inexpensive to expensive. There are books, paintings, posters, and more. I like to browse to find items. You could spend at least an hour looking through the wares. But check online before you go. Then you will be ready to make an instant purchase. Check the hours the shop is open before going there.

Madison Square Garden is a unique entertainment center in New York City. There are many different type of shows. The circus, basketball, hockey, concerts, and more. The shows take place in different arenas. It is very easy to get to. In addition to parking (for a price), you could take public transportation. Subways, buses, Long Island Railroad, PATH trains, and Amtrak all stop here.

Governor's Island is a great place to go for a picnic or bike riding. I went there for a bar b que. It was wonderful. There are complimentary ferries going from Manhattan and Brooklyn to the island. The ferries leave every 15 to 20 minutes. Cars are not allowed on the island. But there is a tram, which circles the island. It is a fun day.

I took my niece to this small children's amusement park. It was okay for a few hours of entertainment. It is on the side of the Belt Parkway in Brooklyn. There are other amusement parks in the area, which may be more exciting, but if you are in the area; we had a fun time. Prices are reasonable.

An educational fun place to visit. There is a lot of science to learn about many different subjects. The planets, electric, locomotion, and much much more. There are a huge variety of interactive exhibits. The children will love it. They will not even realize they are learning new facts.

The Botanical Gardens is a wonderful peaceful beautiful place to visit. There is a small charge for entering the gardens. But know that your admission fee is going toward upgrading the gardens. They are installing benches now in the gardens. Soon you will be able to sit and relax.

I love the Botanical Gardens. It is beautiful and peaceful. They have a lot of different workshops and classes. Check the schedule online or give them a call about the schedule. You could take your class to visit the gardens. It is an educational and fun day

There is a lot of history on the Statue of Liberty Island. You take a boat or ferry out to the island and then you could either go on a tour or just do a self guided tour. Prices range from $10 to $30 or more per person. It is a fun educational experience.

Great museum about Native Americans. The building housing the museum is just as interesting as the building housing it. The U.S. Custom House is full of history. There is no charge to visit the museum. Definitely go to see the history.

I feel this museum is one of the most interesting. It is very interesting. I think there is a free day to go to the museum if you are counting your pennies. Give them a call. There is always a new exhibit going on.
Every performance I have seen here has been great. The building has been here since the late 1800's. The inside is beautiful. The prices vary depending upon which performance you go see.
A lot of history and a very interesting building. It is one of the oldest synagogues in the United States. The building is in Moorish style. There is no charge to visit the building.
Interesting museum in the heart of Manhattan. There are wax figures of famous people that look real. It is expensive. If you have seen everything in Manhattan then try this museum.
Definitely a church to go visit. It survived the 9/11 attacks. One of the oldest churches in Manhattan. It has an old graveyard, which is very interesting and historic. No charge
Interesting place to visit. It is at the lower end of Manhattan. The ferries leave from nearby. The ferry to the Statue of Liberty leave from here. Fun day out.
The Museum of Modern Art is filled with treasurers. One cannot view the entire museum in one day. Come back time and time again. Very educational.
This is a very educational day out. The structure is beautiful. General Grant's tomb. There is a lot of history here.

After quite an extensive tour of the park I can honestly say this was my favourite place. The Bethesda Terrace is a architectural marvel, a perfect place to relax, watch street performers, listen to music, or simply hang out and pass the time. It's one of the most easily recognisable landmarks of Central Park featured in many Hollywood movies and TV shows, like John Wick, Elf and so many more, it was so cool to see it in real life. A very beautiful impressive arcaded structure with carved limestone decorations, the arches and ceilings at the terrace are simply breathtaking with beautiful decorative ceiling panels of Minton tiles in stunning vivid colours. From the terrace you can view the world famous Bethesda Fountain and the lake beyond, so beautiful and romantic. There were 2 string musicians playing Canon by Pachelbel when we arrived and we enjoyed listening to them. There is a bathroom on site but is very crude but functional, be sure to use them if possible as bathrooms are scarce throughout the park. You can take some amazing photos here, definitely a must see.

The Cathedral Basilica in Newark is stunningly beautiful, inside and out, and a fine example of French Gothic Revival architecture right here in New Jersey. From the marble altars to the intricately carved woodwork in the ambulatory to the sculptures throughout, fine artistry is on display here. So, too, the beautiful stained glass windows — including the enormous rise window at the end of the central nave — the soaring columbs and the vaulted ceilings are outstanding examples of the artisans’ crafts. Individual chapels, dedicated to different saints, ring the ambulatory. And one chapel — dedicated to Our Lady of Lourdes — contains the kneeler used by Pope John Paul II on his visit to the church in 1995. The exterior architecture, reminiscent of Paris’s Notre Dame, is also stunningly beautiful.

Did not expect the medieval exhibits to be as detailed and lovely as they are. Admission is expensive; friend had a discount, otherwise I probably would have passed this wonderful place up as budget-breaker. Fir us poor folk, worth making admission arrangements ahead of time and figuring out the bus transit system. #4 bus can take you right to the entrance and pick you up later. Get a transfer to other bus lines. Beautiful wooded setting next to the river, would not have imagined this was in Manhattan. Just an enchanting, wonderful small museum. A few people in oeriod costumes were roaming around. Place was crowded with visitors when I visited; friend who lives in the neighborhood told me this was unusual

This arch with its stunning statues of Grant and Lincoln on horseback, along with street names like Lincoln and Union, is a reminder that this neighborhood was built in the years after the Civil War. It is really a triumphal arch. Beautifully lit at night, with gently varying shadings of color. Tastefully decorated with a Christmas Tree over the holidays, with an enormous Hannukah display across the street. This arch is a real center of the neighborhood. It marks the entrance to Prospect Park and the lovely open space behind it which Flatbush Avenue goes around. The classic Art Deco main branch of the Brooklyn Public Library complements its structure. Definitely a destination in Park Slope,

We stumbled upon Shakespeare in the park our last visit and compared to our December visit where we took advantage of the free ice skating it was just as amazing. The weather of course could not have been more perfect the first weekend in September and the courtesy blankets from The Bryant Park Foundation enhanced the cozy atmosphere. Bryant park was down the road from where we stayed. I originally was going to walk round it for exercise but it turned out not to be that sort of park. They did show outdoor films there so that was quite cool but I didn’t stay to watch the whole thing as I didn’t have time. Nice outdoor space though in the busy mid town hustle and bustle.
likes: Cultural events (Shakespeare in the park, outdoor films)

reviews_attraction.text: Upon completing a Hudson River cruise that left from pier 78 my sister and I noticed this aircraft carrier in the distance so decided to go and have a look. We had no idea what was in store. Moored alongside was the old decommissioned aircraft carrier USS Intrepid. As we got closer we saw how massive this ship was and went aboard for a tour that took us some 3 hours overall to view what was on display. It is one of those exhibits that you have to see for yourself to appreciate its size and importance in history. On the flight deck there is a large array of aircraft that have all had a role to play in the ship's history. Overall it was nothing short of awesome.

We just love the Boat House and it never disappoints, it just gets better & better. After 4 days of business/pleasure in New York we decided to finish our last day with a delicious lunch. Jonathan Abbott and his team are so professional, not only does Jonathan run his restaurant with precision and complete enthusiasm, he is so caring for his clients and staff alike! Sunny our server was superb as was Amanada who too was attentive and kind. The food was delicious as always, setting is so beautiful and ambiance is perfect. Thank you Jonathan... see you next time we are in New York, you made our trip.

Essex County Cherry Blossom available now (April 2019) for a short time in Branch Brook Park due to Blossom short term. Gergous coloring, Great park and pathes to walk around (some area can use bike, not too long of a strech). Awesome nature walk, visiting center available, awesome day for a family. Some benches to sit and enjoy. Recommend to take a good 1-2 hours stroll around park. Didnt observe much biz travelers or professionals, seems more newark local residents from the area. Several residential buildings/ garden apartments in close proximity. Magnificent sunsets!

There's really been a resurgence of this area by the Passaic River in recent years. Riverfront Park went through a facelift and a lot of effort has been exerted to revive/reinvigorate the area. The City of Newark has supported many activities at this park, such as the boat tours and diverse musical events. This park has a sports-designated areas (baseball field, tennis courts, baseball courts, and this behemoth soccer field) and two playgrounds. I'm not a sports person, so the thing I like about Riverfront Park are the walking paths and the views of the river.

Highly recommend Under One Roof tour for Asian American families especially. The multicultural tour includes interviews with the Wong family whose home is toured as well as interviews with different generations of Chinese Americans in the garment industry. This kind of historic preservation and material specific to the Chinese immigrant experience in mid century America is so rare to find in the US and offers an important perspective for third and fourth generation Asian Americans who do not know much about the original hardships of the older generations.

This huge (25 foot tall?) outdoor sculpture of steel and aluminum, perched on one end, survived both 9/11 and Occupy Wall Street (That’s a small joke, as OWS, which occurred across the street, at Zuccotti Park, was totally non-violent). Red Cube has been there for fifty years, I think. Just wonderful and is a delight to see, every time. Controversial new redesign of the plaza is afoot so you might want to see it now, before the original architectural concept is corrupted by the addition of trees, walls, seating. Red Cube will make you smile.

Stumbled upon Federal Hall when we went to see the NY Stock Exchange. As a history enthusiast, I was so excited to find this. There were tons of tourists in the area taking pictures with the statue of Washington, but inside was very empty and quiet. I had no idea this was where Washington was inaugurated. I love stumbling upon historical places. I wish the National Park Service was fully funded to upkeep this building as it should be, but the small offerings they had were very nice! I would recommend if you're in the area.

A nice little park to stop off at and have a rest while wandering around NYC. We were fortunate to come here are part of a tour and learn a little bit more about the park and some of it's history. It has it fair share of odd balls though, got approached a couple of times for money. There are chess tables and rest rooms, be careful though as again in the restroom was a homeless person washing in the sink. The fountain is lovely and big and you allowed to get in it if you wish, great if you want to cool off on a hot day.

I have been going to madison square garden since i was 10 yrs old and i saw janis joplin with my dad in 1969 . . we were in the last row all the way in the back as he got the tickets for free for doing some work there as security , but no matter where i was sitting i still remember that night . i can still remember janis and johnny winter with his white long hair . till this day i talk about that night . through the years i have seen tons of concerts at many venues but this is the one that is the best to me

I was very pleased that I was able to tour the observation level at One Wold Trade Center. The inside observation deck is ideal for taking in the view and in our case within an hour of rain clouds setting over Manhattan. The wide concourse and vaulted ceiling seemed to reduce the angst of falling I sometimes feel at extreme heights. The use of realistic digital displays throughout the elevator system was very impressive and speaks to the technological prowess of the building.

The kids loved it specially because they had the opportunity to feed the birds, the giraffe --the BEST experience and there was something for everyone to enjoy. The admission costs is reasonable, but you do have to pay for every extra activity like feeding the animals. The cost is not much and at least it goes back to the zoo for the upkeep--so don't fret. For the price you can see a lot of animals, including penguins, bald eagles, lions, a leopard, and a red panda.

At night the top of the Chrysler Building is lit up and extremely attractive in the NY skyline.During the working day the foyer/lobby is open to the public to view the fantastic 1920's/1930's art deco architecture. A must to see and visit if you're in the area of Lexington & 42nd street. A couple of the security guards are little grumpy however there is an area in the foyer/lobby set aside for us travellers to view the interior. Go on, give it a go, it's free.

I came from the city on the subway, which leaves you right off at the museum. It was not hard at all. The museum took all day. There is a lot to look at. There was an exhibit on Pierre Cardin, which costs a few dollars extra. Which was huge. And, right now they are changing exhibits. So, one floor was closed. But, still so much stuff. They sell food, if you want to take a break. Also, tables and chairs outside. Very nice. Bring comfortable shoes.Enjoy!
dislikes: One floor closed due to changing exhibits

reviews_attraction.text: We arrived early to the museum and received passes to go to the Glenmont Estate (Edison's house) about an hour or so later. The best thing about both of these locations is that almost everything you see is original. I am often disappointed when I go to museums and they are loaded with reproductions but that is not the case here. Edison was a fascinating, brilliant man and I learned a great deal about him. Admission is free with a National Park pass!

The foyer of the UN Building is very interesting, but going on the tour is even better. To see the Security Council and General Assembly chambers gives a real sense of history. Hearing how the UN works is very informative. Access. To access UN Building need security clearance which is obtained across the street. One of family or couple need to produce govt issued ID with photo eg passport or drivers license. Bag check and metal scan before entry.

This Catholic Temple always means a lot for me, because of my primary and secondary aducation, which was in a Catholic School. It's Neogothic Style and the fact that it is the largest Church in North America, was predominant over the city until the skyscrapers were built. It is a must when you walk the 5th Ave. Also I visit the altar dedicated to Saint John Baptist De La Salle, which was the founder of the religious order back in my School.

Very interesting exhibits throughout the museum, of interest and relevance to most people. We enjoyed learning the history of the Revolutionary War in New York (George Washington encamped there), the history of the Hudson River and the first environmental protection efforts, historic photos of Muhammad Ali, the garment industry, Tiffany lamps and jewelers, and The Stonewall. The museum is well air conditioned and there is a nice snack bar.

The Brooklyn Botanic Gardens is a little sister to the Botanical Gardens in the Bronx. Do not confuse the two. In Brooklyn you will find lovely paths and specimens of all things growing in the Northeast, it is relatively contained. It is beautiful in the Spring, but less enchanting in the heat of the summer. It is a lovely walk outside after you have visited the Brooklyn Museum next door. My suggestion is to do both in one day.

If you want to meet New Yorkers at their happiest come to the long meadow or neathermead which are fields in prospect park between 7am and 9am when they let their happy dogs play off leash. The first Saturday of the month Fido Brooklyn meets outside of the picnic house on the long meadow. Dogs also swim at the dog beach and at the lake on the peninsula. The peninsula is near the new bathroom at the top of breeze hill.

We decided last minute to go through the Central Park Zoo and got there just in time for the penguin feeding. This was great - all the kids visiting were so excited - as were the adults. The grizzly bears were napping - but visible. We got to see one of the snow leopards and also the red pandas (must see.) We spent about 1.5 hours here and thoroughly enjoyed it.

This is difficult for me to write as the Penn Center is part of Reconstruction Era Momnument NPS and I have never had a terrible expierence at a NPS site.  I also appreciate that this is a very new National Park but nonetheless a NPS site.   Please know this review is strictly our expierence at the Penn Center and not the other parts of this new National Monument.

One of the youngest members in our party is an avid Junior Ranger and was super excited to be able to add this to her growing list of parks visited. However we did not feel welcome here. Rather we felt that we were imposing on asking for her book to be stamped and to go through the Junior Ranger program. Though she was given the form.  Additionally they did not have badges and they didn't seem to be able to direct us in the right direction. When we asked what we could do at Penn Center we were told we had to pay $7 but we're not told what we would be seeing.  When my daughter asked me a question about her work on the Junior Ranger book she was told that she was supposed to do it and that I wasn't allowed to help her.  As a 9 year old learning g about reconstruction helping with some of the concepts should be expected by any adult working at a museum but we were met with the opposite.

We opted to leave and figure it out ourselves. We did try to take a picture of the NPS sign and we're told absolutely no pictures. The entire expierence was extremely off putting. We frequent national parks and have never experienced anything like this. Fortunately we ended up at the Arsonel on Craven Street where the staff was extremely warm and welcoming and embraced us and our Junior Ranger!

History is alive and well at Sagamore Hill and it is well worth the visit.  There is so much to see and do here that I would not suggest trying to squeeze in everything in an hour.

First and foremost , if you want to see the inside of Roosevelt's home, you must get tickets ahead of time or get to Sagamore hill when it opens as there are a limited number of tickets for each session and they sell out quickly.  It is important to note that 80% of the house is original, however, you can not take pictures inside the actual house.

If you do not get tickets into the actual house, there are still plenty of other things to do on the site.  There are several wonderful trails, some that lead to water as well as a museum and a few other structures that you can explore.

For the Junior Rangers in the group there are several different booklets to complete.  One booklet will earn them a badge, however completing three or more will also earn them a patch.

There are plenty of restroom facilities on the site, however there is limited options for buying food.  Tickets into the house come with a fee but the actual site is free.

I did not expect to enjoy this location as much as we did.  As avid NPS visitors, we try to see as many spots as possible.  To be able to say you rocked in chairs on Roosevelt's porch is definitely something that we will treasure forever.

Not the first place one would expect to find an NPS site but then again our history is everywhere and St Paul's Church is filled with some of the founding history of our country.

This location is truly fascinating and worth a visit. You do not need to plan to be here for more then a few hours but you do need to be prepared to take your time and take in all the different learning opportunities this site has to offer.  From the movie about the roots of the church to the ranger led visit inside the church itself, you can truly get a deep appreciation of how this site placed an intergral part in shaping our country.

The cemetery is a truly beautiful tribute to a number of famous and not so famous individuals from the area. The monuments are beautifully crafted.  The little known fact that an unknown nber of Hessuam soliders buried in one grave at the site is just one of the many secrets that lies within the cpnfindes of the property.

St. Paul's Church is definitely worth a visit and for the kids in your group the Junior Ranger Program is a great way to bring history alive.

The site is free and some areas are ADA compliant but the cemetery may be difficult to for some people with mobility issues.

Beautiful county park with sweeping views of the Hudson River. Great playground and ample space for picnicing.

Gazebo and other enclosed spaces can be rented with permits well in advance of your event which can be a complicated and difficult process through the county office which is why I lowered the rating.  These are common areas that are limited to those who have paid to use them, rather then being available to anyone.

I appreciate that the county of Rockland takes pride in it's parks. However, given the taxes that the residents pay in this county, being asked to pay additional fees to use county parks for gatherings of people over 12 (including family gatherings) is bordering on excessive.  Especially when these fees are at times hundreds of dollars and require insurance certificates.

Staff in the park however are friendly and helpful and work hard to help guests.

Over the years they have definitely added to this swimming option in Clarkstown and I do find myself here a couple times over the summer.  Diving area is well monitored as is the slide but is pretty much a hangout for the kids.  The splash pool small and has one water feature.  The pool is large and always monitored by lifeguards who do train daily for an emergency.  Limited areas for shade exist and the few trees that are there do not have dense foliage.  Food service is what would be expected with limited options beyond the standards - hot dogs, pizza, burgers, fries, ice cream.  Bathrooms/showers are gender specific and while large feel dark and damp.  The price to get in even for residents is high, visitors is extremely expensive.  If given a choice would probably pick one of the other options in Clarkstown or skip it altogether

Nice place.  Crowded by the time we left at 9pm.  I would suggest if you are going after 6pm and are not partial to your mini golf course research prices and coupons.  This one only takes coupons before 6pm.

Course has stairs so if you have mobility issues this is not an option.  Course is also not easy for left handed golfers.  Limit of 5 per grouping.

Overall place is clean. Course takes about an hour to finish with reasonable wait times.  Most holes can be completed in the strokes if putted right.  At the ball return you have a chance of winning a free game.

Overall would return.

The cruise line is your go to for the Statue and Ellis. I recommend everyone do the statue first, spend a little time there and then go to Ellis. The cruise is fast and they move a lot of people around pretty quickly. Be fair warned though it is still a boat. As smooth as it is. If the wind is hitting NYC the right way that boat is going to what boats do, especially at the dock. Also remember this is lower Manhattan the nature of the area is high security.  It can create some anxiety.

This is a fantastic museum and National Park run by NPS. The history here is over whelming. As one who frequents National Parks, this one is definitely in the top five for historic parks. The staff is extremely friendly and helpful. The building is well kept and the bathrooms maintained. Food is available in the cafe and often times there are people dressed in Civil War era clothing who are will to pose for pictures and answer questions. Parking can be tough but it's worth the walk.
likes: Facilities & Services: Friendly staff, well-maintained building, clean bathrooms

reviews_attraction.text:
As a big advocate of the museum I encourage everyone to visit. They have great program for kids and it can be bundled with the Planetarium on Sunset Beach.

The work the muesum is doing is so important to protecting and reserving the wildlife, plantlife and history of the area.

The touch tank is great for kids and the opportunity to engage in some amazing g kid programs is well worth it. There is not a lot of stuff to do on Ocean Isle outside of the beach so this is a nice break.

Dater mountain hike a great hike for both experienced and modestly expierenced hikers. Could be very challenging for novice hikers as there is some spots that can be tough to follow. It includes almost perpendicular which is a fun section, especially for kids. Also great for picture taking in the midst of the fun sections of the vertical rock climb. When you get to the top the views are stellar.

This is a small local park. What makes it unique is the flat rock near the river which makes it easy to launch small river floatation devices like tubes and kayaks.  I have lived near the river for a decade and advise anyone considering spending time in it to be mindful of the weather. The Ramapo River can be calm and peaceful one day and completely destructive the next.

This is a unique short stop during your Hilton Head vacation. As someone who feels historical sites are important to visit this one definitely surprised us with the fantastic ruins of tabby as well as the description of the site.

This is a nice little stop on your way to Harbor Town or the stables and worth taking the time to see what plantations used to be made of.

Great place for crabbing or exploring the ICW. Everyone friendly. Everyone we have encountered is helpful.  If you are looking to do a little fishing/crabbing/clamming make sure you check your regulations.  If you have kids this is a good spot to meet the needs of a diverse group. Also being on the quiet side of the island it's not as busy as some other spots.

As a National Park person we try to incorporate or create trips around the parks. This was a last minute stop for our Junior Ranger and it was a nice program for her. I would come during the spring and summer to see the site more alive but the history is deep and we enjoyed learning about this once thriving industry.

We opted for a private tour of the sanctuary and it was worth it. We got to see all the wolves and learn about the different personalities and traits of each of these magnificent animals. Fan favorites from the group were Thor and Little Joe!  Our volunteer tour guide Rosemarie was fantastic. Well worth the visit.

Enjoying Gettysburg not during an event was fantastic. Highly recommend getting a guide. I did not grasp how amazing this place was until I was fortunate enough to be able to drive around.  The junior ranger program has a wealth of info in it and rangers get a badge and a patch.

While I did not visit in season it was moving to walk around the orchard and look at the fence that slowed the south down. It's amazing how one little thing can drastically change the outcome of things. In this instance it was a more traditional fence.

Harriman is a large park so knowing where you want to go or being willing to explore is a must. Hours vary and parking is in marked locations. Do not park anywhere. Roads do close in the off season. Great for hiking, fishing and enjoying nature.

Good place to get out and walk around as you tour Gettysburg. Lots of places to climb but it felt like solemn ground to me so I was hesitant to let my kids do to much.  You can feel the history that happened here..
Great National Park. Be prepared to drive between the two main locations. Lots of artifacts in the museum. Lots of areas to explore. If you like history, then this is a must see on the list.
Great park rangers. Junior ranger program is engaging with secret service theme. You can feel the history of the site as soon as you park. Beautiful views and easy to navigate. Lots of land.
If your not looking you will miss one of the NPS sites in NYC. Near Riverside church this is a nice place to take a walk and enjoy the city energy and  amazing history without the crowds!
Very friendly staff. Junior ranger program is great. The views are stunning. Very peaceful and filled with history. Great NPS site for an afternoon of taking in history and nature.
Great history here. The castle like momuments really make it almost surreal. You can feel the history that happened here.
If you can support this foundation please do. The staff is so helpful and the work they do so important.

What a wonderful local museum!  The price is right at $3 per adult and the friendly staff are happy to have you and very helpful. It's quite an interesting history of not only Annie Riggs, but the local area. They've done an exceptional job of restoring the antiquated adobe building, which used to be a hotel. There are quite a few rooms to visit with a separate focus in each and placards which give you a succinct and informative history of that focus. The wide surrounding porch is a nice place to sit and relax or perhaps picnic. We spent over an hour though you could easily spend twice that much time. Kudos to the Fort Stockton Historical Society for the job you've done!

This Park is one of the best kept and wonderfully restored historical sites I've ever visited, not only in Texas, but the entire nation. You can take a volunteer tour of Independence Hall, visit displays and go through the store in one area. Next up is the Star of Texas Museum. A 20 minute video is worth your time before enjoying the two story museum. It's amazing how much they have on display and the depth of what's available. The grounds are also beautiful. We spent an easy 3 hours here and I'd suggest allotting at least that much time. Be sure to bring a picnic as not much is available close by.

Davis Mountains State Park is a lovely and remote getaway in the desert. At almost 6000 feet elevation the climate is cooler than much of the surrounding area though make no mistake that it's still quite hot in summer. There's plenty to do for all with hiking, viewing and bird watching. The Indian Lodge Restaurant does take out and the food is wonderful and staff exceptionally friendly. Plan on lovely drives in the area for party of your days as you'll be amazed at the gorgeous desert scenery!

This refugee is one that would be worthy of a bucket list, especially if you live in Texas! It's a small, quaint Wildlife Refuge for the migrating Whopping Cranes though you're very likely to see plenty of other wildlife. It's nice to be able to drive through at your own pace and stay quite a long time. The Rangers are knowledgeable and enthusiastic and during normal seasons provide tours. Be sure to check during these Covid times for availability and such.

Such a little green not far off the highway! The take reservations or first come first serve. We had electric, all that's available and there are clear restrooms (no shower) a dump station and pump water to carry. It was a quiet pine Forest area and we we're fortunate to see an Albert's Squirrel for the first time! I'd say this is not for to large of a rig if you're pulling another vehicle.

We visited after the museum was just closed, however the grounds were beautiful and thoughtfully done. There's a small version of  the Vietnam Memorial. There's a star shaped walkway with plaques describing the history of each war beginning from the Civil War. It's well kept and peaceful and we hope to go into the museum next time around.

Quite an interesting museum! You'll learn everything you ever wanted to know about cotton and cotton ginning. There's a nice little store, museum, and 20 minute video which are free to enjoy or you can take the $6 tour which was well worth it with Tynan as our guide. There wasn't a question he couldn't answer! Thanks much!

Fantastic place to visit or revisit! Be sure to walk the Natural Cave Entrance down is you can (about an hour) though you can take the elevator up. Take a reserved tour of possible and even ask at the last minute in case someone didn't show up. We thoroughly enjoyed both the King's Palace and Left Hand Tunnel tours.

This historical area is a wonderful place to visit. The museum is informative, staff friendly and ground beautifully kept. Do be sure to check with them as some building are closed to entre if they've had rain in order to protect the floors. Take your own picnic and enjoy their lovely area!
dislikes: Some buildings closed due to rain

reviews_attraction.text: What wonderful history they're preserving! If you can, watch the PBS video or some other before you go so that you'll have a greater understanding because they do just a short introduction before leaving you to type at your own pace. It's free though they certainly accept donations!

Amazing place! Well worth taking the time to spend half the day and take in all of the information and activities. It's easy to find and to get around. There are two tram tours of about 45 minutes, a 15 minutes movie and plenty of other things to see.

Enjoyed this historical area tremendously! There are several areas to visit including the museum and store, old log school house and amazing church. The attendants are knowledgeable and enthusiastic. We'll worth your time!

Easy to get to, nice camp spots and lovely swimming! A very family friendly and quiet place I'd say and as an older couple here very inviting. The sites are a decent size and shady and each has a covered picnic table.

Loved this museum and the wonderful Nancy J. who gives you the tour. She's personable and knowledge and made the entire experience worthwhile! Be sure to combine your Caverns of Sonora tour with this Historic tour!

Great little place not far off the highway for a picnic and/or let the kids or pets get some time outside. It's nothing fancy but will do. The only bathroom is up by the pool but it was open and clean.
Great museum of a nice size for this small county. It's full of beautifully kept items and exhibits in a pristine former home. As it's a Country museum it's free. We'll worth a short stop!
Enjoyed the many details of Pioneer life in this and surrounding areas! Beautiful place to stop for a picnic even if you don't go to the museum (though it's well worth a visit).
This is such a wonderful quaint small town museum! Leslie was out tour guide and it was clear she loves her hometown and knows its history. It's free though accepts donations.
Excellent wine and personable wine steward (Thanks Christy)! This is a beautiful venue in the middle of nowhere and great place to spend an hour or so. We will be back!
Beautiful place to visit, swim or stay in an RV for the night. You just can't go wrong with the view and being close enough to town to walk, finding anything you need.
Lovely little museum full of information about the local history of the area. Free to attend though donations are accepted. You'll surely learn something new!
Great place anytime to be in the Llano River though especially so this weekend with the LEAF Festival happening. Come check it out!
Visited the Ranger office out of Lajitas. Took the beautiful drive on the edge of the park to Presidio. Well worth your time!
Nice place to spend an hour though not too terrible much there not a large amount of information and no person in site.
Lovely place to visit and share s glad if wine with friends. Thanks Jason for the professional and friendly service!

When my sister and her friend came to visit, we took them to many attraction in Niagara Falls on the American side and she said that the Cave of the Winds was the best attraction. They give you a poncho and some foot-ware before you go in. You'll be glad that you have the poncho especially when you go up to the Hurricane Deck. It's a blast being right next to the falls and getting soaked, and you'll have a happy smile on your face due to the positive ions that get generated by the water crashing down onto the rocks. You can stay down there as long as you want so just relax and take lots of selfies for your friends back home and enjoy it. It’s an excellent attraction, and my sister said its one of the best ways to experience the falls.

From the picture I'm posting you can see that there is still construction going on (they are building a new penguin habitat). The Sea Lion show is still very good. It's a small aquarium (because some of it is still under construction), so it won’t take up your whole day to spend some time there. They also have a decent  variety of animals and the exhibits are informative. The prices are great considering that they are an nonprofit organization that’s opened all year round. The trainers and staff are very knowledgeable about the animals and the whole setup fosters a good educational environment.

What a great place to bring back ol memories. We like taking  my wife’s nephews and nieces to the Olcott Beach Carousel Park for the whole day. Even though the kids have visited many of the modern day carousel rides, the old wooden ones still bring joy. The gift shops there have plenty of items to buy that for sure you can’t find anywhere else.

If you and your family members are looking for some real great adventure in Niagara Falls, then you need to make a stop at the . Niagara Falls Adventure Park. The staff there are friendly and knowledgeable in knowing how to handle all the amenities. If you have any kids, they'll be in for a real treat when you take them there..

This Marina has the perfect combination of a very well maintained area and friendly people. There’s a playground for the children, fishing spots, pavilions for cookouts, 3 slips to launch your canoes, kayaks, small boats, and excellent parking space. Great place for a family outing and don’t forget to bring your pets.

What a great scenic park that overlooks the Niagara Whirlpool, to take friends, family and your out of town guests to. You can see the beautiful gorge, go on hikes, fishing, picnicking, plus they have plenty of  kids' play areas. This is a must see place to go to. And you will never regret it.

If you are looking for a place to do walking, bicycle riding, picnicking, fishing, all along the Niagara River, then Broderick Park should be on your list. Over the years, all of my friends, family members, and out of town guests that I took there; were always thankful that I did..

I’m sure most would agree that touring the Niagara Falls area on the ground is great, but doing it from the air is spectacular. The staff and pilot were very friendly and knowledgeable. You get safe flying while site seeing from the air, folks it don’t get better than that.

Even though it’s a Wax Museum, believe it or not you can really learn history there. After running around seeing all the attractions in the Falls, it’s nice to take a break and enjoy a little indoor activity. So overall the wax museum is worth your time to come and visit.

Great small (but there is a large picnic tables area under a roof, plus a playground set) park located along the Erie Canel. It has a path for walking and bicycle riding. You can also sit or lay on the grass and take a nap. There’s lots of wild life there as well.

If you are in the need of a very nice picnic area right next to the Niagara river, then the Aqua Lane Park is the place to go. The outdoor picnic area is great for a large gathering. Plenty of space for outdoor games, music, tables, benches and a restrooms.

People from around the world make a pilgrimage to Our Lady of Fatima Shrine. The number of life-size statues of Saints throughout the property is absolutely stunning. Mass is held in the domed rotunda, and the gardens and outdoor picnic areas are superb.
likes: Facilities & Services: Life-size statues, Gardens, Picnic areas

reviews_attraction.text: This chimney has survived another move and has been placed next to the scenic Niagara River. It is still a part of Niagara Falls history and I hope they will continue to preserve it for the hundreds of tourists from around the world who come to see it.

Wow, what a great State park. I go here often year around because there is always something going on. Today they held the National Rugby tournament and it was so nice to see the young people from all over the United States to come here and try out.

Are you ready for the best hiking, fishing, natural beauty, water rapids, wild life, picnicking and forgetting all your worries for the whole day(s)? then the Niagara Gorge Discovery Center Niagara Falls is the place to be.
One local spot to check out a beautiful botanical garden plus a kayak and/or canoe launch; it cant get any better than that for a family outing to enjoy the great outdoors in Tonawanda wildlife.
Finally a place where your pets can run free and have loads of fun. All the pet owners have been so kind and respectful to everyone and to keeping the park is such clean conditions.
What a great bus tour system for the whole family, friends and especially out of town guests. They really know how to show all the highlight spots this area has to offer.
Great park for outdoor sports and games. We’ve had several picnics here over the years and never been disappointed. Its also a nice spot to set off small rockets.
Very nice and pleasant park next to the Niagara River for the family. Clean restroom, picnic tables and a gazebo makes it a perfect spot to relax for the day.
When my father in-law was still alive he told me that his dad who came from Ireland had spoken about this particular tree. Lots of history in this tree.
Great park for the whole family. Be sure to bring your pets. Places to picnic, walking, bicycle riding, jogging...etc. Its a great place to do all that.
What a wonder full monument of one of the greatest inventors of our times. And yes, the statute looks a little bit like president Lincoln.
This was the spot where we saw this guy catch a large fish when we first moved to this area. Real nice park to take the whole family to.
This park has everything for the local community. We really love watching the Fireworks display on the 4th of July over the  many years.

What a history behind Kykuit. I enjoyed the tour to Kykuit. We took classic tour on last Sunday and our guide was excellent. She did not rush during the tour and given us ample of time for pictures where it was allowed. JDR family spent plenty money in acquiring art from all over the world. There is a tremendous European influence in the architecture of this house. Most striking thing that I found out on the tour was, when one of the descendents of JDR thought one day because of so much development in the Hudson valley area and around the river, they will lose their excellent view so they bought entire area from kykuit to GWB to save their view of Hudson river. That's call wealth and power through standard oil. However they gave it back where it is now palisades parkway. In my opinion, this is must see tour if you are in US history.

I drove on whiteface mountain and Mt. Washington auto road so compare to that this was nothing but so close to NYC, this is the best auto road on the top of mountain in bear mountain state park. Views are fantastic and NYC is visible in the distance on clear day. You can easily spend an hour or two on the top and few trails are around for you to hike. Top of the tower gives you 360 degree view of surroundings. You can use low gears while going down the mountain to avoid overheating of your breaks. They should post signs for recommending lower gears. When you are coming down, take a scenic route exit to go to overlook that gives you amazing view of Hudson river, bear mountain bridge, Anthony's nose, and Hessian lake. I would recommend people who loves going on the top of mountain.

I went there week before Cheery Blossoms festival and enjoyed it very much. Early morning is a good idea to beat normal crowd. I am sure after cherry blossom, park is even more beautiful and crowded.  Good place to take pictures and look at the skyline of NYC. This park is very good for kids to run around and have lots of fun. United nations is in the background. Guards are always there in case someone needs help. There is no place to eat around the park but I was told by one vendor that Cornell Tech has cafeteria which is open on weekends. I would love to go again and explore more on Roosevelt island. There is a donation box if you would like to contribute.

I had amazing time today at Paterson Great Falls. It  wasn't crowded though temperature was around 65F in early January. Easy to park your car and walk to lower part of the falls and you can go very close to falls by crossing the bridge. There is a passaic river access very close to falls in case someone want to enjoy the river. I must say, city of Paterson has done excellent job of providing visitor center and clean path to falls and plenty seating arrangements for the visitors. Falls provides excellent photo opportunities. Good place to walk and relax. I would be definitely coming back to Paterson in warmer weather.

Beautiful trail but challenging. You must be ready to walk at least 4 miles back and forth. Sign posted where it starts says 1.7 miles to fall but it seem like way more than 1.7 miles. You need to have proper shoes, water and umbrella with you in case you get caught in rain. You will find unique dwarf pitch pine trees along the green colored marked trail. Once you reach verkeerderkill fall, you will find worth having challenging hike. Give yourself 3 hours for hike. Parking lot is small but clean bathrooms at visitor center and parking fee is $10.

I walked this old railway trestle bridge that is converted in walkway. This walkway over Hudson has revived local economy for sure. Nice place to jog and walk. As you go in the middle of the bridge, you will feel slight change in temperature. It's gets cool and windy as you reach in the middle. I parked my car on the side of the connecting road and walk since there is no dedicated parking space for visitors. Also proper restrooms were under construction at the time of my visit. I am sure proper restrooms are operational now.

I have been playing Cricket and Tennis at Merill Park for sometime and experience have been excellent. Park Ranger is always polite to let everyone know that playing singles in Tennis only allowed due to COVID 19. There is a small zoo for kids which has ducks, chicken, rabbit, goats and peacocks. Peacocks are always vocal when it is pleasant weather. Parking is always available around the baseball field and tennis courts which is a plus. Good place for picnic with friends and family.

Simply beautiful garden for only $8 per car. No need to go to over pricey and crowded botanical gardens in NYC anymore. It is easily accessible by long island expressway. It is extremely peaceful inside planting fields Arboretum. You won't find constantly staff walking behind you. You will have freedom to enjoy everything in respectful fashion. No picnic allowed and please keep gardens clean. I would definitely go to planting fields again. This place is awesome for wedding pictures.

It was a unique experience inside the ice caves. Temperature drops more than 15F inside. It is a loop so you will be coming out of an exit which is very close to entrance. At two location in caves where it is completely dark but there is a motion sensor light installed which will help you. You cannot go wrong with $10 parking you get ice caves, view of Sam's point, lake and awesome waterfall. I went over the weekend and it was not at all crowded inside the cave.

Very beautiful garden in Yonkers for free to visitors thanks to city of Yonkers. I wish they start charging fee so entire garden can be brought back to its former glory. Some part of garden is renovated but some part need some serious help and that can only achieved by bringing revenue for renovation by charging nominal fees. Parking is limited but if you wait, someone will come out soon. Garden provides immense photo possibilities.

I visited this park while I was in Warwick valley, NY. High point monument is must see around the Veteran's day since it is dedicated to War veterans. Elevation of the monument is around 1800 ft above the sea level and it is 220 feet high. This monument is the highest point in state of NJ. When I visited high point monument, it was very cold so couldn't enjoyed the height  but will visit again in summer time.

There are two very small parking lots to Raymondkill falls. Both can accommodate approximately 15 cars. Restrooms are available in one of the parking lot. Raymondkill falls is walking distance from parking lot. Good overall couple of hours of fun. I saw some folks were having fun at the bottom of fall but not sure how they reach bottom because there are no marking on trails.

This is the must if you are in the tri-state area. It is only two hours away from NYC. Within the $10 parking fee, you will get to see Sam's point, Ice caves, Verkeerderkill fall and Lake Maratanza. Awesome place to hike for hours. Staff at the visitor center was courteous and parking attendant was very helpful. I would return to Sam's point in Fall to enjoy foliage.

Montauk lighthouse museum got closed before I reach there because of traffic but still enjoyed the lighthouse from distance. There is a hugh parking lot, clean restrooms and children playing area along with cafe for you to enjoy the end of long island. Plenty swings placed strategically for you to enjoy the amazing views of the park.

What a history attached to this place. I recommend this place if you want to know more about our first president. Our guide who gave us the tour of the house was very humble and knowledgeable. He was able to answer all our questions. Revolutionary war history lesson at very low cost. Going to the top of tower of victory is a must.

I have been playing Cricket in Eisenhower Park during summertime under NYTBCL and both grounds and pitches are amazing. I have been playing at EH1 and EH2. Restrooms are near the both cricket grounds. Grass on the ground is well manicured. Overall fantastic experience at the Eisenhower Park.

I visited Van Vleck House and Gardens in early January and enjoyed the walk in the Gardens. I will be coming back in spring to enjoy this Garden. Good place to sit, relax and enjoy the beauty of this place. Admission is free to public and any donation is very well appreciated.

Very nice and clean park for recreational activities like Swimming, Tennis, Golf and may be Cricket when everything is open. There is a fee if you would like to use the park and you are not Nassau County resident. It is a wonderful place for waking and jogging.

Walking on the top of the dam is always fun. When you are on the top of the dam, you will realise the enormous body of water is holded by the dam. Lots of cultural activities at the plaza every summer so check out the summer activities calendar.

Enjoyed it completely. Looking for the parking so close to lighthouse is very difficult. However, there are steps right under the bridge that leads to the lighthouse. One local guide me to the steps after finding parking under the bridge.

Visitor center was closed on the day when we visited Dingmans falls. Parking lot can accommodate around 25 to 35 cars easily. Restrooms are right next to parking lot but serious odor to welcome you as soon as you park your car.

Falls is easily accessible by car. Parking lot is right in front of the fall. I saw blue color trail around the falls. If you drive to falls then you are driving on very remote dirt road for few miles.
Vey nice bridge connects Queens and Manhattan. There is a tram service if you would like to take back and forth between Roosevelt island and Manhattan. View of the bridge from Roosevelt is amazing.
Pretty cool waterfall and easily accessible from Lake Rose parking lot. Saw lots of kids were playing under the waterfall and it is very safe.
Very nice park in long island city. Hard to find parking around the park. Famous Coca-Cola sign which is a New York city landmark now.

Wonderful park in the middle of the Energy Corridor.  Nice trails, pretty scenery and quite.  The trail is great for an extended bike ride when you include George Bush Park trail, making an out and back from Fry road about 35 miles.  Just one thing......do your riding during the week days.  On the weekends the trails are overcrowded with everybody from 3 year olds on trikes to 80 year olds using walkers.  The trails are then an accident waiting to happen.

It's a great place to take out of town guests and especially good for kids.  Lots to see and do and there is plenty of history on view.  The one real disappointment for me was that Houston did not get a real shuttle, just a phony mock up.  That model on top of the 747 just isn't the same as the real thing.  How they decided to give a real one to NYC is a real mystery to me since they had absolutely NOTHING to do with any space flight ever.

A large rambling city park with a lot of different things to do.  There are running trails, playgrounds, sand volleyball courts, baseball fields,  bike riding routes, you name it.  They are very spread out so come by car.  The biggest problems are 1) the facilities are not well maintained or possibly the maintenance staff can't keep up with the vandalism, and 2) I would be leery of safety and security at dusk and after dark.

I am fairly sure that this wasn't what Rockefeller had in mind when he endowed the place. It is grossly expensive to get into, much of it is a tourist trap designed to separate people from their money, and the modern-day logos on the shops don't do anything to Foster the idea that you are in Colonial Williamsburg. I had been hearing about this place all my life had my first visit yesterday was grossly disappointing.

This is a huge park/sports complex with multiple baseball fields of various sizes anywhere from tiny tots to adult. There are restrooms, a snack bar and picnic tables.  There are several cricket pitches as well and two playgrounds,  one for wee ones and one for 6 and up. BTW,  each ball field has bleachers with sun roofs.  The entire park is well maintained.

The museum is very nicely done if kind of small. The exhibits are well explained by the signage. The walking trails are fine over the paved portions but where they are not paved, they are mud holes.  For some reason the signs seem to direct you to the worst of the mud.  The maps at the various stops do a good job of explaining what you are looking at.

A very good playground / sports field for all kinds of play.  They have a modern playground with restrooms, baseball fields of several different sizes, a covered area with 5 basketball courts, 4 tennis courts and fields for soccer or football.  The area is well maintained and the equipment is in great shape.  A town asset to be proud of.

Spark park next door to an elementary school. The day I visited they had not cut the grass in a week or so.  One of the baseball fields was flooded.  The playgrounds were fine as was the covered basketball court.  There are several picnic tables and even a charcoal barbeque in decent condition.  Be careful of the mosquitoes.

This park is overgrown and poorly kept. The grass has not been cut in a while and is full of weeds and fire ants. It does have several picnic pavilions that are covered but they are surrounded by trash.  It looks as if many families had Easter egg hunts there and left their trash behind.  I would not let my kids play there.

A place of calm in the middle if a tourist mob.  There were three tour buses full of people scrambling to buy souvenirs and a whole crew of electricians laying wiring for a film crew to use the next day.  I went into the church and the quiet and calm were immediate.  Ten minutes re-energized me .

A large park with a playground,  baseball fields,  under cover basketball courts, soccer fields and restrooms. The facility is well maintained and is open to all.   There is adequate parking with lots on three sides. There are several places to picnic under tall old live oak trees.  Really nice!

Reasonable park with a playground for children. The grass is torn up in spots from people driving on it.  There is a lot of trash in the grass as well. All in all, it looks like it gets used by a lot of people who don't care about the place.  Not a dump but it could be a whole lot nicer.

Incredible to look at and a joy to play in.  Just 100 m off the road it's so quiet you can hear your heartbeat. Step off the road between parking areas and you can see the tracks of literally hundreds of small animals. Who would have thought such a harsh desert had so much life in it.

A really nice park / playground with a picnic shelter, restrooms, and a playground for kids.  The grounds are well kept, there is adequate parking and the large shade trees give plenty of protection from the summer sun.  It's a bit out of town but worth the trip.

Large wilderness area close to Houston with a small natural history museum and a 1830 farmstead. They do demonstrations of 1830's farm life on weekends and two larger enactments in February and November.  Nice people. There are picnic areas too.

Large park with a good selection of playground equipment for the kids. Plenty of space for sports and a reasonable path for jogging. Big trees for shade in the summer.  Needs some work for drainage after it rains.

A very large Park with all sorts of things to do. It includes a playground, several ball fields, hiking trails, and picnic tables.  There are several rest rooms that are reasonably clean.  Watch out for fire ants.

A pocket park in West Houston with a little bit of everything.  Playground, picnic tables, tennis courts, baseball field, and grassy play area. A bit noisy from all the traffic but still a nice place to rest.
A nice enough playground but the location makes it way under utilized.  There is almost no way to get to it except by car so no neighborhood kids are there to use it.  A big waste of taxpayer money.
Nice park for the kids to play.  There is a picnic pavilion and playground equipment suitable for little ones.  Needs a rest room but doesn't have one.
Interesting museum but the star is the working cotton gin. Find a day when it's running (not often) and go then for a special experience.
They were getting ready to film a movie the day I was there. Pushy people stringing wire all over the place. Not the best experience.
Huge park mostly for soccer. The fields are well maintained and there is adequate parking.  It has a restroom and a snack bar.
Rude guards who ran me off for walking on the grass.  I thought that was the whole point of having a green place in a city.
Great open swaths of green grass for children to play on. That tends to be at a premium in this High Desert City.

I see the riverwalk as a tourist attraction where visitors throw their trash inside rather than the river being a part of San Antonio history. There are some parts where there are no handle bars so watch your step when walking. I do like the parts of the river where there aren't many people and I can enjoy the view of the river and the tall trees. Don't go during parades, Christmas time, or fiesta if you want to avoid the chance of not being pushed into the river.

Parking needs improvement because it is a tight spot. Other than the parking, it is an awesome place to get engaged in art and architecture as well with photography. There are many showcases at this museum that can be fun and interesting to learn. I certainly love the library. One spot to visit inside the museum is the garden. Either its raining, its cold, or hot; any kind of weather fits the outside garden and it's lovely.

Very amazing place to walk, see, and feel. The whole place is something to learn about, it's not just a park but it was an area that provided water to flow towards the other presidios. The parking is small but it's okay. Plenty of room. Good bike and walking trail and there is an education center nearby so everything is pretty much here. Watch for the weather and bring plenty of water. Texas weather is no joke.

What a beautiful place to overlook the lake in this hill country. I love how trails begin to appear around the park where people mostly gone through. On restroom at the end of the park, no soap, plenty of parking not just in the parking slots, must see.
