Other than that, the other side of the dam looks pretty too with white tailed deers hanging around the slope of the dam. Its gergous in its way.

It is a nice new "riverwalk" but I recommended going in the morning or near sundown. The rest of the is not so pretty. They designers did a bad job on keeping us safe from the sun. So beware of sunburn, bring protective gear from the rays. There is no shade whatsoever. There are some near trees but most of all none. This is only a part of the project, let us see if they will improve.

This place is so spread out, so green, so foresty, so muddy. Well it's muddy because I gone to the park after weeks of rain. Still good though, it's so spacious and smells wonderful like I'm at the monte. Good place to run around, bring pets, picnic, lay down, bike, play. It has it all. Also for y'all who live picking up pecans, this is the place for you pecan lovers.
dislikes: Muddy (due to rain, but not a permanent condition)

reviews_attraction.text: I love the place and I like how they made another parking in the westside of the park since the only parking has been provided by the church. The park is small but it's okay for a little bit of fun. The field is nice, the track is okay, the basketball court is good enough for those who like basketball and the playground is alright. It's a good small community park.

YES!!!!!! This place was awesome. Our first time seeing snow, me, my father and my primo, was the greatest thing that has ever happened to us and this place was the place to play. We rolled down the hill and acted like children. Me and primo lost our phones in the snow so that was a struggle but at least I had fun. I wish San Antonio would have this much snow.

I liked this park, it shouts out cozy and friendly. Of course there is a down side where there is no public restroom. We have to use the restroom inside the center located at the park. Park on the street or park at the college is fine to. Parking is limited here but it is nice for a barbeque and the small hill makes of more fun for kids to run up and down.

This is a nice place to learn about our cultures hence in the name Texan Cultures. It is big and there is so much to see, might take about an hour to see all of them, an hour or two. Very fascinating. Especially the activities they do and demonstrate there such as how to weed cotton on the wheel. I recommend this for you and your family.

A good place of history and architecture. Learn good and educated myself with the traditions and culture that the early people had and do. I recommended going to this place not because I am an San Antonian. Have a good time in this mission and the others. Bring plenty of water and watch out for the weather especially the hot summer air.

Fresh area to walk and explore. Make sure to see the acequias nearby and imagine how they made the trough to water their crops. Imagine the location back then. Enter the cool chapel and see how the windows were placed to light up the area during the evening hours. Watch for Roman Numerals nearby. Lots of things to learn here.

It looks very nice, the park looks like hasn't been cut for a long time and really need some park improvements especially a sunscreen over the playground. But other than that it looks nice. It's not like Woodlawn Park but it is close to a lake, or pond. Fishing seems openly and love how barbeque is possible near the pond.

Oh this park was amazing. I believe there was a lot of parking spots so it's not an issue, since they renovated the area, I say it looks better. It looked better before but they added more activities for kids to do. The cool grassy lawn is still there. It really looks like a nice park in the city near the bay.

It is a pretty beautiful place to explore and to see how it feels to be in the forest in the city. The big space green grass meadow, the forest trail, the baseball complex. Yeah everything is pretty much here. Have fun in the area. There is plenty to do for about an hour more or less. Enjoy the day.

I love this park, we have to pay for a table which is kind of messed up but it is worth it to see and feel the open area out if the heated city. I love the small river that's shapes the area and the trail. There is alot of things to do here and it is a fun way to spend time with family.

I'm a San Antonian and I say go this place. And ask about the basement though. Seriously, this place has history not just the events but the way this city is built and what the villagers grew up with just because of the San Antonio River which was the main settlement here in Texas.

Love the open area and the foresty trails. Nothing really bad about this park unless you don't like walking and getting exercise. :) But all is good here. Need to clean the tables though. Not just the ones who work there but make sure to clean up after yourself. Have fun.

This multi-tiered park is full of mini activity hubs....basketball and handball courts, sprinklers and water fountains, swings and slides, various levels, different pavement treatments, sprinklers, lots of benches, bathrooms.  If you can’t find something or some place in this park to enjoy yourself, well then something’s wrong!  It is nestled behind a public school (PS 55) in a quiet little area of Eltingville (SI) surrounded by private detached homes.  It’s a ‘find.’

It is named for FDNY Lieutenant John H. Martinson of Engine Company 249, who died in the line of duty in 2008 in Fort Greene, Brooklyn.  This fully accessible playground is one of the most innovative in the city, offering great views, two levels of play areas for younger and older kids, and a blue-seated amphitheater (‘sprinkler room’) that can be used as an outdoor classroom.

For 15 years, I used that 6 subway stairwell to travel uptown and never realized what a beautiful building this was...until I saw it featured on NYC Arts (11-26-20) program on WNYC (Ch. 13).  15 years!  The building was typically covered by scaffolding and never beaconed passersby as to what was housed there.

Now retired, I’ll make time to not just be a passerby or pass by the building but enter it to see the latest photography exhibit...and I’ll try to do so at dusk to see the subtle exterior lighting that highlights its architectural flourishes and features.

I don’t know why this was named after one of the City’s worst mayors, but this building hasn’t changed in over 100 years (see the photo of a hand mirror below of the building on the far left).  Whenever I went to it for city-agency meetings, it was always steaming inside, elevators were slow, and it’s just a horror to be in.  The only saving grace is the views outside its windows of the Brooklyn Bridge and its proximity to subways.  Other than that, all I can say is “ugh!”  Maybe that’s the irony in naming it after worst-mayor-ever (S)Dinkins...🤣

Best to skate first thing in the morning when it opens at 8 AM before the other cheapskate kids come.  (I know no admission fees attract skaters, so it’s no surprise it gets crowded and the ice quickly gets chewed up by amateurs. 😖)  It may be tough to get to Midtown so early, but it is worth it on an outdoor clean sheet of glass!  And the views are breathtaking.  Love the passersby gazing at the skaters, thinking they should be out there or wishing they could glide along with us.

My fav secret place to visit...and I do with family and pets often.  If you circumnavigate the entire park, it’s a 2-mile up and down trek.  There’s access to a beach strewn with granite remnants of the old school once on the grounds, and populated with seals, a small family of bald eagles, all sorts of birds, sea glass bits here and there.  One local bus from the SI Ferry (takes about an hour to get there) provides local access, and a small parking lot provides free spaces.

Yeah yeah yeah I know, it’s a tourist photo spot.  That said, it’s part of a great location in all of the city, with the great shiny gold/bronze Gen. William Tecumseh Sherman statue, a natural meeting place, and the Central Park entrance leads to the zoo a few blocks north.

And btw, the great 70s television sitcom “The Odd Couple” filmed a closing credit scene with a Oscar and Felix having a sandwich along a bench to the left.

The reflecting pools, meant to be the inverse of the old towers, are...well, there’s no ‘there’ there.  You cannot see the other pool (tower footprint), so these features are just ok.  Best to be there very early in the day before the rude tourists arrive thinking this whole area is an amusement park like the Seaport...it’s not.

Btw, go check out the lobby of 4 WTC...it’s shown in my pic...a beauty of a panorama.

Such a beloved building in the City.  My wife once worked on a building up on 50th Street, with windows facing south.  Sometimes I’d go in with her at 7 AM, and we’d “have breakfast with the Chrysler Building’s gargoyles” down at 43rd Street.  It’s just a unique structure we NYers love, and that it’s right next to GCT makes it that much more endearing!

A quiet little corner for your pensive thoughts with the former First Lady.  Get yourself a cup of coffee from a nearby deli in those ubiquitous NYC wax cups, take a seat for 10 minutes, put away the damned cell phone, and enjoy some time alone!

There used to be an old highway ramp to the Henry Hudson Parkway; his ship was the Half Moon 🌙 .

So beautiful and majestic, but so so forgotten.  But remember why it’s there: it marks the end of the Great War (WW1), the ‘way to end all wars.’  General Pershing was right to want to end it in Berlin and finish off the Germans.  An armistice was no end, and 20 years later, Hitler and Nazism was born.

One of my 3 or 4 fav pedestrian places in the entire city, especially when the statue of Pomona is bathed in the running fountain mist!  (Pomona is the goddess of fruitful abundance in ancient Roman religion and myth. Her name comes from the Latin word pomum, "fruit," specifically orchard fruit.)

What’s not to love in this historic building that faces St. Patrick’s Cathedral across the street and Charles “Lucky Lindy” Lindbergh one level up.  The lobby looks like how it might in a Fort Knox gold vault, with shiny glowing walls fed by lighting...the aura makes one feel riche.

Not to be missed...take time to read somebody the etched-in-glass heartbreaking letters.  The pool, when it is on, sounds like the blades of a helicopter (no coincidence given that the war was fought from helos).  It is often UNpopulated and forgotten, just like that war.

This park is better named as the Park of a Million Stairs...jeez, so many steps to traverse to go between levels.  The pathways are dirty and dusty...forgotten.  The one view that is noteworthy is that of St. John the Divine’s rear east side.

I love this park with a variety of “rooms” in different levels...2 workout gym area, baseball field, 2 basketball courts, a sunken grassy area, and a strange cobblestone pyramid to climb (the park attendant storage area is under it).

Meh...an unused piece of land that’s open so not every single piece of land has to be developed and we Staten Islanders don’t feel crushed like the Brooklynites that began their invasion of 60 years ago.
Not the greatest neighborhood park but it not bad either.  I recall when I was I high school going I’ve skating here with some friends on a Friday night just off the Miles Avenue side.
The cathedral has to be seen to be believed...well over 100 years of construction and as of 2020, building continues!  Best to go midday during the week when fewer visitors are there.
A wonderful Art Deco experience...the W. 50th Street side of the center features 3 polychrome roundels by Hildreth Meiere representing Dance, Drama, and Song.
Nice quite little local park, at least in the winter...I was the sole person walking thru at noon on a weekday.  Love the old houses surrounding the park.
What is the damn big deal with this little area...it’s a circular plaque in the ground with a few Bohemian types playing guitars in summer.  That’s it...
Can’t quite give this statue a 5 bc of the misogyny of the 9 naked black women holding Duke up.  Really?  Who the heck approved that?
My pictures say it all: quietude in a contemplative space.  It’s great to have someplace on the Island where you can’t hear traffic
I don’t know what’s so great about it...it’s just a big open area that not even all that quiet given its proximity to traffic.
1888.  It’s worth the hike up the paths, especially in the fall when the views are all lit up with leaves turning

We had fun, but two of the water slides were closed. We rented a Cabana and when we took off, some people came and rummaged through our stuff and stole some souvenir cups and other trinkets. Of course, everything of value was in the locker, but still, how desperate are you to steal souvenir cups?

The staff told us they confronted the robbers but that they ran away, and staff advised us to go to customer service to see if they could help us out by replacing our stolen cups. We recovered 3 out of 5 cups. Why they didn't give us our 5 cups when the staff themselves were the ones that confirmed we had 5 cups is beyond me.

I would have rated 4 stars, but them not wanting to cover $14 (the cups costing them probably not more than a dollar) left a bad taste in my mouth. We had fun, but management needs to step up the customer service.

We've been to the two caves here, and just so you know, it's always best to come after there's been some rain, or if there's been recent rain. If it hasn't rained in a while, the cave doesn't look as good because the formations will be dry and they don't look as "shiny." Tour guides are knowledgeable and take their time explaining formations and answering questions. The temperature in the caves is cool (somewhere in the high 60's or low 70's, if I remember correctly) but the humidity in there is 100% so dress accordingly. It's on the pricey side, but well worth it if you like to enjoy natural wonder like this!

I remember there being a whole lot more trees here than I saw today. Perhaps the storm that went by here a few years ago felled many trees? During our visit we saw many county employees, a Constable and 3 border patrol vehicles, so don't even worry about Mexicans trying to cross the Rio Grande River here! The grounds are well kept but the paving needs a bit of attention in certain areas. Overall it's a good little park, but it used to be even better.

Rented an air conditioned shelter. Everything was clean and in good repair. We had to drag a picnic table from the cabin next door since ours seemed to have sprouted legs and walked away. Restrooms were also good, but didn't have hot water. Who cares when you're supposed to be roughing it and it's almost 100 degrees outside! Wish the dam had more water in it, but I know the State Park system doesn't control the weather.

A bit on the pricey side and the employees seem to be going through the motions, nothing like the treatment you get at an actual LEGO theme park. That being said, if your little tykes love LEGO, you can't go wrong here. If you're a patient parent, you can be here with your kid for hours on end. And this being at the mall, you can incorporate it into your shopping trip.

Great experience. There's a lot to see and do here. Lectures are given by honest-to-goodness astronauts! We got here at opening and didn't leave till 5PM. There's a large food court on-site so you don't have to go and come back, and the prices are reasonable. The interactive exhibits are out-of-this-world awesome!

Good little museum out in the boonies! Entrance fee is very reasonable, the train cars need a bit more TLC, but I suppose it would be better tended if there were more volunteers. Model trains are well kept, and the restored vehicles (fire engines, cars, etc.) look fantastic. Will drop by again when time permits!
dislikes: Facilities & Services: Train cars need TLC

reviews_attraction.text: This is right next to Mission county park. It's also kept clean and tidy. This is an awesome place to visit when it rains and the river rises, because you get to see the usually calm river water turn into a roiling, churning force of nature! Good to bike and hike along the river walk trail!

The duck park! Great place for a jog. There's always people here on the walking trail, playing soccer, etc. There is also a pool here that you can get into for a minimal fee to do laps, and the park is well maintained and clean. The pond has a flock of 🦆🦆 🦆 🦆🦆🦆🦆🦆🦆🦆 constantly on patrol.

Make sure you come on a day that the park is open! The first time I came here I made the mistake of just driving here without checking hours and I came to find a locked gate. Other than that, this is an excellent park. It's clean and well kept and the staff are friendly and helpful.

Beautiful park to spend a day in the outdoors in.  Walking and biking trails are ample and well maintained, some of them being put in place very recently. You can get great views of the Houston skyline from the trails and enjoy nature to the absolute fullest. Good job, Houston!

Fun place to spend the day with the family for a reasonable amount of money. Just be aware that the main attraction is supposed to be the restaurants and you will be marketed to incessantly. Other than that, the staff is courteous and helpful and everything is super clean.

Awesome park, but the parking situation is horrible. The park was clean on the Thursday we visited. The vendors were just setting up shop and the restrooms were in need of paper towels. Overall it's a great location for a park in this part of town.

Great park to go jogging or take your kids to enjoy the playground equipment. I think this is one of the oldest public parks in make but it has gotten many updates and it looks beautiful. Spend an afternoon here with your family!

Awesome garden with plenty of history! It's right next to the zoo, so you can go either before entering the zoo or after. Stunning views when everything is in bloom and an excellent feature in the Breckenridge park area.

This is a great place for a group picture, not as full as I expected it to be. It's clean and in an up-and-coming neighborhood. If you're looking for a good place that has 'Austin' written all over it, look no further!

Great botanical garden for the South Texas region. Give yourself enough time to see and study some really interesting plants. We had a blast here, the facility is clean and well kept and staff is friendly.
Quiet and natural experience along the San Antonio Mission trail. Good place to have a picnic with the family and enjoy the scenery while learning some history.
Well maintained park next to the jogging trail on Bentsen with disc golf being the main claim to fame of this park. Has a playground for kids and lots of trees.
Went inside to see the architecture. It's beautiful in there. This church has a rich history of which you can read and appreciate inside the church building.
Awesome museum with great exhibits showcasing Texas history. Staff are friendly and helpful. But a yearly membership so you can come again and again!
Great bridge. I couldn't believe there was actually a bridge named "Rip van Winkle." Awesome! The bridge is in good condition and well maintained.
Great little park to bring the family for a hike, dip and a picnic. Everything is well kept and maintained, with no visible trash.
An absolute stunning building with a lot of history. Good place to visit with the family and friends if you're a proud Texan.
Have to park a ways off from the trailhead, but once you're on the tail, it's well worth it. Absolutely stunning views.

(النص الأصلي)
Beautiful downtown NYC Cathedral.
St. Patrick's is a beautiful, classic, European Gothic style cathedral. We have visited dozens of churches and cathedrals here in the U.S. and in Europe and St. Patrick's can hold its own with most. It is beautiful inside and out and unlike many NYC downtown churches you can walk completely around this one and appreciate the outside as well as the inside. It has gorgeous stained glass and a beautiful pipe organ. It is open and welcoming to the public. My reason for the four stars instead of five was that perhaps it is too welcoming. Inside, despite the beauty, it felt more like a tourist attraction than a church. It was crowded, which is not unusual for a large European cathedral, but it was also noisy. There was little feeling of awe or reverence. The balance between welcoming and maintaining reverence is perhaps harder to achieve in New York. That's not necessarily a criticism, but simply an observation on the personality of the city. New York is a busy, noisy, boisterous, beautiful city. St. Patrick's was much the same the day we visited. We did not take a tour but would have liked to had we more time. If we ever visit NYC again I would certainly go back.

非常有名的绿木公墓，建于1838年，纽约地标收録为国家历史名胜。景观非常独特，连绵起伏的丘陵和山谷，天然池塘和人行步道穿越茂密的緑色草坪，点缀的鲜花，多肉植物，精美雕塑和建筑纪念碑，还能遥望自由神像和帝国大夏的远景，当你访问绿木后，你就很容易理解为什么人们会聚在这里漫步甚至在草地上野歺，每年这里吸引几十万游客（当然大部分是家人）参观绿木的人们都会被它自然美景和庄严感到震撼，毕竟有60万人埋在这里，很多还是著名的古迹，精彩的故事😀

(Translated by Google) Pelham Bay Park is New York City's largest park, 2,764 acres, three times the size of Central Park, which has many geographical features, salt marshes, coasts, bays, lagoons, ancient forests, bushes and rare coastal tall grasses. Oh, there are fewer wild animals and waterfowl. Turtle Bay is the first stop I went to, because I was in the cold January, the freshwater swamp in the Turtle Bay area was frozen and all the waterfowl migrated, leaving only a grassland, crossing a small bridge in the middle of the river. There is an 11-acre forest that freezes on the trail, but the mute swan and the squid seagull are photographed at Eastchser Bay across the road, where there is no ice on the beach.

(Original)
佩勒姆湾公园是纽约市最大的公园，面积2764英亩，是中央公园的三倍，该公园拥有许多地理特征，盐沼泽，海岸，海湾，泻湖，古老森林，灌木丛和罕见的沿海高草草䓒，更少不了野生动物和水禽。海龟湾是我去的第一站，因为我是寒冷的一月去的，海龟湾区里的淡水沼泽结冰了所有的水禽都迁移，只剩下一片草原，穿过河中间的一座小桥有一片11英亩的森林，小径上也结冰，但在对面马路的Eastchser Bay拍到疣鼻天鹅和鲱鱼海鸥，这边是海水滩没有结冰😎😁
likes: Natural landscapes (salt marshes, coasts, bays, lagoons, ancient forests, bushes, rare coastal tall grasses)
Wildlife and waterfowl (mute swan, squid seagull)
dislikes: Limited wildlife in winter (fewer wild animals, waterfowl migration)

reviews_attraction.text:
(Translated by Google) Croton Canyon Park, located at the bottom of Croton Dam. Covering an area of ​​97 acres, it offers spectacular views of the dam and spillway. On the bridge that spans the Croton River and offers the best view of the spectacular spillway, you can explore the waterfalls and the clear water at the bottom of the dam. Get as close as possible to the waterfall, feel the mist and listen to the roar. Then along the trail, through the green woods, while admiring flowers, insects, birds, scenery, while on the top of the dam, overlooking the momentum of the dam and the calm lake. There are natural scenery and unique architecture here. The Old Croton Water Historic Park is definitely worth a visit😍

(Original)
巴豆峡谷公园，位于巴豆坝底部。占地97英亩，可欣赏大坝和溢洪道的壮观景色。在横跨巴豆河并享有壮观溢洪道最佳景观的桥上你可以探索瀑布和水坝底清澈的水流。尽量靠近瀑布，感受薄雾，聆听咆哮。然后沿着小径，穿过苍翠的树林，一边欣赏花、虫、鸟、景，一边到水坝顶上，俯瞰整个水坝的气势和平静的湖面。这里有自然风光又有独特的建筑，老克罗顿水上历史卅立公园，绝对值得一游😍

(Translated by Google) Caesar Park is a park named after an educator. It is not big, there are stadiums and football fields, there is a fine beach and bay, very beautiful sea view, fine sand to set up to be particularly comfortable, spring and In the autumn, there are many waterfowls in the tranquil waters, and you can enjoy the spectacular views of the Verrazano Narrows Bridge. The residents around the summer gather here to play games, play with water, and love this natural summer resort. Here, there is a very good Mark Twain. In middle school, every parent wants to send their children to this school. I also harvested a lot of waterfowl.

(Original)
凯撒公园是以一位教育家的名字命名的公园，不算大，有捧球场和足球场，还有个精致的沙滩和海湾，非常漂亮的海景，细细的沙子踏上去特别舒服，春天和秋天宁静的水面飞来很多水鸟，还能欣赏到Verrazano Narrows大桥的壮观景色，夏天周围的居民在这里聚会游戏，玩水，热爱这个天然的消暑胜地，这里特别的是有一间很出色的Mark Twain 中学，每位家长都希望把自己的小孩送到这家学校读书。我也收获很多拍到很多水禽。

(Translated by Google) Calvert Volks Park, surrounded by the Gulf of Gravesen, not only can see the seascape but also the wild waterfowl and animals attracted by this natural environment, as well as synthetic lawns, stadiums, etc., with Caesar Park On the opposite side, although you see the same scenery here, the same bay, but the feeling is different, because the angle is different, there are many native tree eucalyptus, and bushes, there are black Rotten wharfs and wooden boats, this is a good place for waterfowl to inhabit and rest. You are here to wander the sea breeze and watch the ducks play, how happy it is. 🤩😻👍

(Original)
卡尔弗特沃克斯公园，主要由格拉费森湾所环绕，不仅可以看到海景还能看到被这种自然环境所吸引的野生水禽和动物，还有合成草坪，球场等，跟凯撒公园是打对面的，你在这里虽然看见的是同一样的风景，同一片海湾，但感觉是不一样的，因为角度已经不同了，这边有很多原生树🌲木，和灌木丛，有发黑的烂码头和木船，这正是水禽栖息和休息的好地方。你在这里漫步吹着海风看着鸭子嬉戏，是多么愉快写意的事。🤩😻👍

(Translated by Google) Humpside Manor, there are two castles in the manor, and the building is made of granite and Indian lime. The largest Humpstead House and the small Gould Castle, but the interior and the two castles on the other side are not open, and it is impossible to appreciate the Tudor art and decorations inside. preserve covers an area of ​​216 acres, six clear paths, open lawns and ponds, different ecological environments, walking and hiking, natural habitats, characteristic buildings, wishing sites, cliffs overlooking the sound of Long Island and rocky beaches, beautiful Scenery, a leisurely and pleasant day😍

(Original)
享普斯德庄园，庄园内有两座城堡，建筑以花岗岩和印第纳州石灰的外观。最大的享普斯德宅邸和小的古尔德成堡，但室内和还有另一边的两座城堡不开放，没法欣赏里面的都铎王朝艺术品和装饰品。preserve 占地216英亩，六条明确的小径，开阔的草坪和池塘，不同的生态环境，漫步远足，自然栖息地，特色的建筑，许愿地，俯瞰长岛之声的悬崖上和岸石海滩，优美的景色，悠闲愉快的一天😍

(Translated by Google) On March 15th, 2019, located in the West End of Manhattan, a spectacular new landmark called Vessel was opened. The building was inspired by the honeycomb, consisting of 8 layers of overlapping and interwoven, 154-story steel-cast staircases and platforms. Starting from a hexagonal base with a diameter of 15 meters, each layer is gradually widened, and the top layer has a twist of 46 meters. It is very creative. It is a sneak peek at 18th tonight. It climbs a 2,500-story, 150-foot building. It is very beautiful. View the Hudson River and the West End from different heights

(Original)
3月15日2019座落在曼哈顿西区的一座名为Vessel的引人注目的新地标落成开幕，建筑灵感源自于蜂窝，由8层重叠交织，154段连接互通的钢铸楼梯和平台构成，从直径15米的六角形底座开始，每层渐渐加宽，而顶层的陓度则达46米，非常有创意，今晚18日先睹为快，爬了2500级楼梯150英尺高的建筑，观感非常漂亮，从不同的高度，角度尽览哈德逊河和西区的夜景🌃😍

(Translated by Google) Cross Bay Bridge crosses the northern end of Crossbay Boulevard through the Jamaica Bay Marsh, where the waterside community is clean and beautiful, the scenery is very beautiful, overlooking the North Channel Bridge, residents love to fish at these two points, through the bridge To the Jamaica Wildlife Sanctuary, it’s a bit uncomfortable. The bus stop here is too long. Visitors want to see the view of the bridge and the bay after crossing the bridge, but there is no bus stop to get off. If you take the subway, you will cross the North Channel. The bridge is equally beautiful. 🤗

(Original)
跨海湾大桥跨越北端的Crossbay Boulevard 穿过牙买加湾沼泽，这里的水边社区很干净漂亮，风景非常优美，望过对面就是北海峡大桥，居民热爱在这两个点钓鱼，穿过这座大桥就到牙买加野生动物保护区，有点不放便就是这里的巴士站距离太长，游客想在过桥后观看桥景和海湾的风景，但没有巴士站下车，如果坐地铁就会穿过北海峡大桥，风景同样漂亮。🤗

(Translated by Google) Jamaica Bay is the only wildlife sanctuary managed by the National Park Service. It covers an area of ​​9,000 acres of open bays, salt marshes, mudflats, highlands and woods. It is a bird paradise with different birds every year, waterfowl gather here. It is one of the most important bird sanctuaries in the United States. It is mostly composed of open waters and intertidal salt marshes. It is close to JFK Airport. There are mosquitoes and scorpions here. Come here to prepare for insecticides. Protect yourself, hiking trails are very good, it’s easy to walk

(Original)
牙买加湾唯一由国家公园管理局管理的野生动物保护区，占地9000英亩的开放海湾，盐沼，泥滩，高地和树林，它是一个鸟类天堂，每年有不同的鸟，水禽聚在这里，是美东最主要的鸟类保护区之一，范围大多是由开阔的水域和潮间带盐沼泽组成，靠近JFK机场，这里的蚊子🦟大还有骚子，来这里参观要准备杀虫剂保护自己，徒步小径修的很好，很容易走😀😍

(Translated by Google) Trinity Park, the official scenic spot designated by New York City, overlooks the Hudson River on a ridge of Upper Manhattan and enjoys the beauty of the Harlem River and the Washington Bridge, where the Metropolitan Museum of Art is divided. The museum houses a lot of European art and cultural relics, wide walks, large lawns, wooded hillside scenery and various garden plants are very beautiful, fresh air and invincible seascape, make people feel comfortable, I walk While listening to various bird songs, I also photographed a cute owl. 😻🤗

(Original)
崔恩堡公园，是纽约市指定的官方风景区，在曼哈顿上城的一个山脊上，可以俯瞰哈德逊河，享受哈莱姆河和华盛顿大桥的秀丽景色，这里有大都会艺术博物馆之修道院分馆，里面收藏了很多欧洲艺术品和文物，宽阔的步行道，大草坪，树木繁茂的山坡风景和各种花园植物都是非常漂亮，清新空气加上无敌海景，让人感觉舒服，我一边走一边听着各种鸟鸣，还拍下一只可爱的猫头鹰🦉。😻🤗

(Translated by Google) The Verrazano Strait Bridge, a two-story suspension bridge spans the beautiful bridges of the two New York administrations (Brooklyn and Staten Island), no matter what season you look at it, it has the most beautiful scenery, I am I went to a twilight in July in summer, but also took the sunset, the most beautiful but the sunset red, with my caterpillars, warm and calm, the sunset is infinitely good, why fear near dusk, life is like a changing season, with different colors Come and go in a hurry, we must fully enjoy life while creating life.

(Original)
伟拉札诺海峡大桥，以双层结构的悬索桥横跨两个纽约行政区(布鲁克林和史泰登岛）的美丽大桥，不论你从什么季节看它，它都拥有最美丽的景致，我是夏天7月的一个黄昏去的，还拍了夕阳，最美不过夕阳红，带上我的毛毛虫🐛，温馨又从容，夕阳无限好，何惧近黄昏，人生犹如变化的四季，有着不同的色彩，来去匆匆变化无常，我们在创造人生的同时，也该充分享受生活👍🤗

(Translated by Google) The Brooklyn Bridge Park is located on the East River, with a highland promenade above. The park can enjoy the magnificent views of the Manhattan and Brooklyn bridges, and the two walking bridges are free. The pier includes pre-existing, as well as the Fulton Ferry and historic Fulton Piers 1-6, various playgrounds, pitches, waterfront greens, gardens, halls, the Statue of Liberty vision, Manhattan's highest landmarks and more. Beautiful sea views, must-see attractions for tourists😍😎

(Original)
布鲁克林大桥公园位于东河的一则，上面有高地长廊，公园中可以欣赏到曼哈顿和布鲁克林两座大桥的壮丽风景，而且两徒步走桥是免费的。码头包括先前存在的，还有富尔顿渡轮和历史悠久的富尔顿码头1-6，各种游乐场所，球场，海滨绿道，花园，歺厅，自由神像远景，曼哈顿最高地標等。海景漂亮，游客必到的景点😍😎

(Translated by Google) Pointed beach surrounded by the sea breeze, broad sandy beaches, rocks, sand dunes, coastal grasslands and a lot of waterfowl birds. A 7.6 miles long, sparsely it populated circular trails, beautiful scenery insisted, but not very convenient to buses. Mainly about 1.5 hours on foot to the beach, for people like outdoor sports, there is no provision of public transport, and public facilities such as car park, so to make walking or running prior to the preparation 😍

(Original)
微风尖海滩三面环海，广阔的沙滩、岩石、沙丘、沿海草原和非常多的水禽鸟类。一条7.6英里长的人口稀少的环行小径，风景非要优美，但很不方便没有巴士可到。主要徒步大概1.5小时到沙滩，适合喜欢户外运动的人们，这里不提供公共交通，和公共设施如停车场，所以来之前要作好步行或跑步的准备😍
likes: Diverse landscapes (beaches, rocks, sand dunes, grasslands)

reviews_attraction.text:
(Translated by Google) The Manhattan Bridge is a suspension bridge that bridges the East River between Manhattan and Brooklyn. The bridge is designed in two levels, including two-way lanes, subways, sidewalks, and bicycle lanes. On the left is the bike path, and the scenic sidewalk from the right-hand entrance of Baoli Street, with stunning views across the Brooklyn Bridge, the East River sea view, and Manhattan's highest landmark. Have time to walk around and see, both bridges are free 😍🤩

(Original)
曼哈顿大桥是一条悬索桥，跨越东河连接曼哈顿与布鲁克林，桥的设计分上下两层，包括有双向车道、地铁、人行道和自行车道。左边是自行车道，看风景的人行道从包里街的右手边入口，可欣赏对面布鲁克林大桥的壮丽景观，东河海景和曼哈顿最高的地标。有时间走走看看，两座桥都是免费的😍🤩

(Translated by Google) Bush Pier Park is a small waterfront park located in the industrial waterfront of Brooklyn. Artificial tidal pond wetland, the purpose is to create an ideal habitat for wild animals. Two small hills, football and holding the field. Along the newly reclaimed waterfront promenade, you can get a panoramic view of New York Harbor and the skyscrapers in the distance. Of course, the sunset and the sea breeze are indispensable.

(Original)
布什码头公园，位于布碌仑工业滨水区一个不大的海滨公园。人工潮汐池塘湿地，目的为野生动物创造理想的栖息地。两个小山丘，足球和捧球场。沿着新填海的海滨长廊，一览纽约港全景，欣赏远处的摩天大楼，当然少不了黄昏的夕阳美景和吹吹海风😍

(Translated by Google) Silver Lake Park, on one side is an 18-hole golf course, tennis courts, sports fields and other facilities, providing a wealth of entertainment activities, beautiful lawns, numerous trails and open spaces, and on the other side is a natural lake, a calm lake, and various water birds , Flowers and plants, beautiful environment, years of improvement and increase keep the park attractive😍

(Original)
银湖公园，一边是18洞高尔夫球场，网球场，运动场和其他设施，提供了丰富的娱乐活动，美丽的草坪，众多的步道和开放空间，另一边是自然湖泊，平静的湖面，各种水禽，花草，环境优美，多年改进和增加使公园保持着吸引力😍

(Translated by Google) A leisure park named after the blue heron, a hand-carved blue heron welcomes visitors at the park gate. It consists of a low-lying and moist second growth forest and three ponds. The lotus, frog, various turtle and insect diversity, dense vegetation and woods are ideal habitats for many birds. It is very beautiful and the park trails are clearly marked 😍😎

(Original)
一个以蓝鹭命名的休闲公园，一只手工雕琢的蓝鹭在公园门口欢迎游客。由低洼潮湿的第二生长林和三个池塘组成，这里的莲花，青蛙，各种龟和昆虫多样性，茂密的植被和树林，是许多鸟类的理想栖息地，非常漂亮，公园步道标记清晰😍😎

(Translated by Google) The pond park is not big, and the trails are not easy to walk. There are three ponds with a clay bottom, and they are full of penny grass. The yellow flowers are very beautiful, and there are many sedges and cattails. Attracting all kinds of birds and fishes, it is the habitat of painted turtles. The painted turtles with orange patterns are very beautiful😍

(Original)
这池塘公园并不大，而且小径不好走。粘土底的池塘三个，里面都是萍蓬草，这种黄色的花很漂亮，还有很多如莎草，香蒲等。吸引着各种鸟类和鱼类，是彩绘乌龟栖息地，有橙色花纹的彩绘龟非常漂亮😍

(Translated by Google) Wadsworth is a 200-year-old, one of the oldest military bases in the United States that guards New York City. It is located under the Verrazzao-Narrows Bridge and has beautiful scenery, but there are not many tourists, overlooking the most scenic spots, and have time to explore. Let's take a look at its military history! 😺😻

(Original)
沃兹沃斯堡是一座超过200年历史，守护着纽约市的美国最古老的军事基地之一，位于Verrazzano- Narrows 桥下，风景优美，但游客不多，俯瞰景点最全，有时间来探索一下它的军事历史吧！😺😻

(Translated by Google) Enter from the west side of 103st Central Park and walk down the creek of The Loch. The picturesque scenery, the creek of the flowing water, the variety of birds are playing in the water, the fragrance of spring cherry blossoms, green willow Swinging in the wind, tourists stop and go, take pictures and rest, not too happy

(Original)
从103st中央公园西侧进入，沿着The  Loch的小溪往下走，这里风景美如画，潺潺流水的小溪，有各种小鸟在戏水，适逢春天樱花芬芳飘香，绿柳迎风摇摆，游客走走停停，拍照休息，不亦乐乎😍👍

(Translated by Google) There are 52 acres of salt marshes, tides, and creeks. This is a beautiful and wide place, a wildlife and marine nature reserve, rich in species, used for environmental education and learning, a clean elevated boardwalk leads to eight observation points, many amazing places, Walk slowly, suitable for all ages😻

(Original)
这里拥有52英亩的盐沼、潮汐、小溪。这是一个美丽宽阔的地方，是野生动植物和海洋自然保护区，丰富的品种，用于环境教育和学习，一条干净的高架板人行步道通向八个观察点，许多令人惊叹的地方，悠悠慢步，老少咸宜😻

(Translated by Google) There is a man-made salt marsh between Randall and the Ward Islands, with boardwalks and walkways, arches, gardens, information signs and decorative fences indicating that the site is a nature reserve, visible from two merging islands Beautiful scenery to East Harlem😍

(Original)
在兰德尔和沃德群岛之间有一片人造盐沼泽，带有木板路和人行步道，拱桥，花园，信息标志和装饰围栏表明该地点是自然保护区，从两个融合的岛屿上可以看到东哈林的美丽风景😍

(Translated by Google) Central Park is centered on the Bethesda fountain sculpture 🦅. It is a must-see place for tourists. The eight-foot-tall female angel with wings. Below her are four little angels, representing temperance, purity, health, peace, and beautiful scenery. , 👍🤗

(Original)
中央公园以貝塞斯达喷泉雕塑🦅为中心，是游客必看的地方，八英尺高的女性带翅膀的天使，她下面有四个小天使，代表着节制，纯洁，健康以及和平，风景秀丽，👍🤗

(Translated by Google) After a small autumn rain yesterday, it was five colors, blue sky, warm sun, yellow leaf trees, multicolored, always showing the beauty of the park, and the endless changes, let your eyes stare at it, never tired. , lingering and forgetting

昨天的一场小秋雨后，便是五色彩地，蓝天，暖阳，黄叶树，多彩多姿，总是演绎出公园美景的层出叠见，无穷变幻，让你的目光紧盯着那里，乐此不疲，流连忘返👍🤗

This was an unexpected find during our visit to Oyster Bay.  It’s pretty much right on the main downtown area of Oyster Bay.  We didn’t get a chance to go inside the homes but we had a fabulous conversation with their resident historian, Claire Bellerjeau who is the author of Espionage and Enslavement in the Revolution.  She is absolutely very knowledgeable!! She was able to educate my 4th grader about the Culper Spy Ring which they are learning in the classroom.  We did their virtual tour on their website.  Definitely if you are in Oyster bay check this place out.  Or check out their virtual events.  They will eventually do in-person tours and Claire can run those too!!  I highly recommend this place!

This place is a MUST to visit for tourists and locals.  There is so many walking paths to explore.  The surrounding is peaceful, calm and serene!  You can come visit and just relax and take in nature.  Only go when weather is nice.   The whole place is outdoors.  The monk parrots nest on the entrance spire is amazing!  So don’t forget to look up and take a moment to listen and observe and check them out.  If you’re going to take a citibike,  there is not one on site but there are a couple of stations a few blocks away.  But if you have your own bike, there is a place to park and lock your bike. This place out is awesome.

Not the most kid friendly museum in NYC.  If you have kids younger than 10 years old I definitely would not go here yet. The staff do not appreciate kids! As a long time member and now with kids,  it’s a little annoying.  The art is good.  They do a good job ensuring COVID-19 safety protocols. The highlights are the outdoor spaces.  Great views!  This has become a NYC icon.  The area has really gotten affected by COVID.  I would have given a 5 star but the workers are a bit intense and uptight and the lack of family friendly space. Click the thumbs up if you agree this is not a family friendly location.

If you’re into architecture and modern art then this place is perfect for you.  The outside and inside is amazing.  It’s very whimsical.  I brought it one star because it’s really not very young kid friendly.  It needs to be organized more appropriately for all families regardless of the age of the kid.  The cafe needs more food options and at appropriate pricing.  Seems a bit pricey for what you get.  If you’re a tourist.  You can check this out and check out Central Park across the street or Cooper Hewitt Museum a few blocks away.  This can all be done in one trip if you don’t mind walking.

What a magical place even in early Spring!  This was a well thought out and put together garden.  Beautifully done.  It has wonderful space to explore.  It was easy to get to from MetroNorth just off the Greystome station.  It’s about a 20 minutes uphill hike if you are going on a slower pace.  There is no place to eat onsite but there is a halal food truck Just outside the park. This is all outdoors so
I’m sure it’s not great when it’s raining.  I highly recommend this place.  I definitely will be back when things are more in bloom.  It’s so close to NYC - less than 20 miles from Manhattan.

New York Aquarium is nicely renovated in a small
Section of it.  They have some wonderful water life.  The new shark exhibit is wonderful but needed to be longer to give that wow affect.  The outdoor shows were just okay.  It’s a bit flat in action and very quick.  The other outdoor exhibit needs attention.  It’s a bit dirty.  The food options are not great either.  This place gets very very crowded and takes forever to get in.  Especially in the summer when it seems all the summer camp goes here.  Plan ahead.  It’s not too far from the subway and it’s right on the beach.

Very lovely garden!! Very well Maintained.  Very clean.  Beautiful flowers around the property.   The representation of the trees planted was a wonderful idea to honor those who served in the military.  The playground had a nice slide.  Be careful there are what looks like yellow jackets burrowing in the sand.  The bathroom facilities is maintained very clean.  In fact,  the whole park is clean.  There are tables to have a nice meal or snack on.  It’s a short walk from the main section.  It makes it easy to get something and walk over to the garden afterwards.

This was a wonderful unexpected place to visit for the Summer!  The Actors did a phenomenal job talking about the history of the Fort and the area!  It has so much history.  The fort was a wonderful place to explore with the family.  They even fire a cannon.  The garden was well kept and it was beautiful.  This place was amazing!  You get a wonderful view of Lake Champlain.  You even get a token to drive up to Mount Defiance,  where can see an overview of the Fort and the area.  I would highly recommend a visit to this place!

This is another very NYC icon!  I went during the week at Noon.  They did a great job of making sure they checked your temperature, wearing appropriate masks and provided sanitizer.  It was very quiet but I noticed it started to get busy in the afternoon.  There is nowhere to eat inside.  Maybe why people were not there at that time.  This is a wonderful museum for modern art!  Tons of artwork to enjoy!  I highly recommend this place when visiting or for locals!  It’s free for the month of September!

What an amazing place to celebrate Earth day!  Beautiful blossoms!  Beautiful grounds!  The indoor greenhouses are closed so only the outdoor places are available at the moment.  They have wonderful grass area but they do not let you picnic there.  So don’t come here thinking you will lay out a blanket.  They won’t allow it anywhere.  But the new paths are fantastic!  This is easy to get to from the 2/3 train stop - Eastern Parkway/Brooklyn Museum

This is a lovely place to visit despite not being able to go inside the houses.  The grounds are serene and peaceful.  It was amazing to be able to explore around the houses.  The view from the house was beautiful.  I got an explorer kit with some wonderful things.  My kids especially enjoyed them.  I recommend a visit if you’re in the area.  Afterwards,  you can have a walk over the RIP Van Winkle Bridge, it’s around the corner. A plus!

Very interesting place for New York City.  Nice architecture.  Getting here is a bit of a hike from the train.  Best to be on your guard to .  The area can be a bit questionable at times.  Best to know your surroundings.  Great artifacts inside and the special exhibits are fantastic.  Good option is very small.  There is a cafe but food is just ok with very little options.  But I still recommend this place.  Go when the weather is nice.

What to find how to ride a bike with square wheels?  Then come to museum
Of mathematics to find out how.  This place has a lot of stuff to engage and interact with.  This place is not that big so it can get really busy and crowded.  I do find it more crowded in the morning versus after lunch.  So I would suggest having an early lunch and come here after noon so it’s not that crowded.  Highly recommend this place!

This historic covered bridge looks amazing in the winter!!  The snow in the backdrop just makes bridge look magical! The frozen waterfall is crazy unbelievable to see.  I love how it looks frozen with the water running underneath.  There really isn’t parking so you sort of have to just park on the shoulder for a bit.  Luckily it’s a wide enough shoulder.  Definitely worth checking out even in the Winter season.

Such an easy hike with a phenomenal view!  You can bring a light snack or wine and just admire and take in the view.  It’s so easy to go with young kids but be careful.  There is rail or guard so you have to keep your eye on them.  There is some seating.  There are remnants of the old hotel if you
Look.  The history of it all is interesting!  I recommend this place for the amazing view!

This place is wonderful when the weather is nice.  It’s definitely a unique experience while in NYC.  Hard to get tickets but it’s worth going to if you can get them.  Easy to get to and tons to do around it before or afterwards.  Went to this place again and it’s just as nice as I remember.  Less crowded now so it’s a great time to check it out.
dislikes: Less crowded (preference for more lively atmosphere)

reviews_attraction.text: Awesome awesome awesome place to visit with the family or for anyone really!  The place is well maintained and made sure things are cleaned and well kept.  Nature is easily blended with the various installations!  The staff are very friendly and helpful!  The children’s play area was amazing!  I highly recommend a visit here for the Summer!!

A wonderful look back at the history of the area.  Pretty basic what you see is what you get.  You can hike to the duck pond area but it’s far about 1.5 miles I think to get there but the trail is flat so it’s just like walking on a dirt road!  They need more things to see.  Plenty of parking.  I still recommend a stop over to check it out.

Even in early Spring season this place is amazing!  Beautiful grounds with tons of nooks and crannies to explore.  The grounds are wonderfully looked after.  I can imagine how beautiful this place is when the plants awaken.  This place is a must to check out when in the area!  It’s a bit far from the train but worth the trek!

Nice place to walk over even on a rainy day.  The view is not scenic more industrial views if you like that kind of stuff. Interesting history associated with the bridge.  I wish they would beautify both sides more to make it more a destination from both sides.  Easy to get to via subway.  I recommend this nice walk over!

Looking for a place to go shopping with tons of stores and great dining around the Columbus Circle area?  Then stop by the Time Warner Center.  They have everything from grocery shopping at WholeFoods to getting some running shoes to Amazon Go to bakeries!  All things in one!

Love the architecture of this cathedral.  So much history.  It’s very quiet right now which makes it a great time to enjoy a service or enjoy the interior of the place.  The gift shop could be better.  If you’re a tourist this is a place to stop and check out.

Amazing experience!  The ball pit is a must! It will bring the kid out of you.  This place is fun.  The treats they provide is so yummy.  They were a bit stingy with the ice cream though.  Definitely worth going.

Train show is fantastic!  Everything is made of wood, plants, and flowers.  Amazing what they can build!  It’s very busy in the weekend so be mentally ready for the crowd.  But absolutely worth seeing
Amazingly whimsical garden.  Late spring is the best time to see the lavenders and middle of summer to see the roses in full bloom!  The garden and house is fantastic!!

Gorgeous park with lots of cool spots/things to do! My girlfriend and I came here for a lake day and then came back another night for some stargazing. The lake was awesome! Although there wasn’t a formal beach, there was an outlines swimming space, as well as tanning space. The water was perfect temperature and the designated swimming area was large enough to accommodate large crowds. This spot is great for kids and families. I’d definitely recommend if you’re looking for a free spot to cool off! Also, we brought food for a picnic (they have picnic tables), but there is also a concession stand right by the beach. I really want to come back and try some of the fishing spots!

As I mentioned before, we came back for stargazing - we made the right choice doing so. The sky is so clear here, I guess there’s minimal light pollution. It was my first time ever stargazing (lame, right) and I already know that this experience is going to be hard to top. Great date spot, just make sure you bring layers because it does get cold right on the lake.

Considering how small this zoo is, it does a great job! The zoo itself is stunningly gorgeous, and the exhibits are pretty too. I thought the reptile house was pretty neat, but it was pretty hot and stuffy in there (that makes sense given their habitat, just giving visitors a heads up). The rainforest exhibit is incredible too, featuring various birds that fly right over your head! My favorite animal was the red panda, mostly because my hair matches their fur, but also because they’re just so adorable. It would have been cool if the grizzly bears weren’t sleeping because they have a cool exhibit, but that’s alright. If you have young kids, or want a change in scenery you should check out the petting zoo. All in all, a fun, little zoo that is especially good for families with young kids!
likes: Facilities & Services: Stunning exhibits, neat reptile house, incredible rainforest exhibit
dislikes: Facilities & Services: Hot and stuffy reptile house

reviews_attraction.text: My favorite type of art is by far realism and I didn’t see too much of that in the Guggenheim. I actually think that’s a good thing, though, because I was able to see a lot of sculptures and other types of paintings. Another cool tidbit about the exhibits is that they follow the stages of each artist’s career. You can see the difference in works between Picasso’s blue and red phases, which is very intriguing. Regardless of the actual exhibits in the museum, the architecture of the Guggenheim is cool, and well laid out. I enjoyed being able to walk through the spiral and check out all of the exhibits, and once you move up a level you can peer down at the exhibits you’ve already seen. I had a great time here, and the museum definitely opened me up to other art forms!

Super cool place! I don’t really know why I enjoyed the Vessel so much since it’s really just a lot of stairs, but I thought it was really cool. I though the view was pretty cool, and I thought that it provided some great pictures. If you aren’t able to do a lot of stairs, there is an elevator or two that goes to the top which saves you the trip. Also, the surrounding area is being built up which means that the Vessel is a great place to spend a few hours, because right after you see it, you can spend some time in the new mall. As far as tickets for the Vessel go, you can book them online, or in person, and they will give you a time slot that you can enter during. Plan for about an hour long time window, but I’m not sure if you’ll want to stay the entire hour.

I hate to say it, but this is by far my least favorite museum/art collection that I have been to in the city so far. Granted, I’m no art expert or connoisseur, but the art that was featured simply wasn’t my style. With that being said, the Whitney gives out free tickets to NYU students so I was lucky enough to go for free. Therefore, if I’m going for free then I see no reason to complain excessively about the place. With that being said, I also really enjoyed the various balconies that they established. They provided some really great views and pictures. All in all, I personally wouldn’t go back to the Whitney, but I definitely think it’s worth checking it out at least once - especially the balconies.

My girlfriend and I had a great time here despite having to social distance! We found it really cool how each room had different themes and plants from different regions in them. Our favorite was the Cuba room. The atmosphere was very laid back and tropical. We gave the rumba a shot which was fun - I definitely held her back to say the least. One thing you should definitely check out if you get the chance to is the rooftop/balcony thing that can be found by going out the doors at the back of the Cuba room; the view is great, and the space is very peaceful. We had a great time here, and would both definitely recommend this place if you’re passing through the Pittsburgh area!

Awesome museum! I would certainly suggest starting with the exhibits downstairs, and the galleries upstairs first. These exhibits are very cool, but they aren’t the main attraction, which is why you’ll want to save the library/study for last. The library and study are truly stunning. I wish I had rooms like that in my house! I don’t really have much other advice for navigating the museum. However, I will say an early time slot might be better because it will be less crowded, enabling you to move freely throughout the exhibits. I definitely want to go back sometime soon!

This park is awesome! My girlfriend and I had a great time doing 2 different hikes, but we didn’t even do everything this park has to offer! Each trail has crazy good views, but we really wanted to get to the one with the huge waterfall. We found one with a tall, “stepped” waterfall and we spent a lot of time hiking/climbing there. I really want to come back another time and check out the other spots. This is a great place to stretch out your legs during all this self isolations stuff, too!

My trip to the New York Aquarium was definitely worth it. I thought all of the exhibits were pretty cool, but my favorite was definitely the shark exhibit. There’s a hallway in that exhibit where the sharks can swim above you which I thought was incredible. It was a bummer that the touch exhibits were closed because I’m sure that that would have been a fun thing to do. The only negative feedback that I have for this place is that I felt that it could have been cleaned more thoroughly.

Moma was actually a pretty neat place. My favorites were definitely the Van Gogh paintings, but there were some other famous works there, too. I really enjoyed the sculpture garden, especially because of how nice it was outside. It was a very peaceful place to reflect on the art, and chat with my friends. I got in for free because I’m a student, which was nice. Since it’s free, I’d consider going back again. I think it’s worth the trip.

I think this is my favorite park in NYC. The views of the Manhattan skyline are unparalleled. I came with my roommate for the sunset (coincidentally) and the progression was gorgeous. I’m so glad I made it here. I’m going to bring friends who visit me here from now on. I can’t say enough good things about this place. It would be a fantastic to propose to your significant other, if that says anything about the view.

Definitely a neat little spot to relax and escape from the bustle of the city for a while. Climbing the ramble is a fun little exercise and I thought the view was pretty good. The walk to get to the Ramble is super pretty, and trails are provided so you can explore the little stream that passes nearby it. If you’re looking for a place to relax in Central Park, this is a good place to do it!

Gorgeous oasis within NYC. The skyscrapers surrounding the area make for a spectacular view. I would 100% recommend coming here to read, people watch, etc. on a nice day. Also, the bridge up here provides such a cool view down 42nd street. This would be a cool spot to watch Manhattanhenge, by the way. I definitely will be back here to relax and escape the hustle and bustle of the city.

I had a great time at Schenley Park! My girlfriend and I took a walk around the park, and then settled down on the hill across from Phipps Conservatory. The view was beautiful, and the abundance of trees/shade made it peaceful and relaxing. I bet the park looks really great in the fall, too. I’d 100% recommend Schenley Park to anyone who wants a good hike, view, or picnic, etc!

Amazing venue! I saw the NY Philharmonic here, and I thought it was gorgeous. The plaza is super clean and well kept. I really enjoyed seeing the fountain lit up at night. I’ve been here a bunch of times just to look around, but I finally saw a show here and I was really glad about that. Definitely want to go back again sometime soon.
likes: On-site Activities: Fountain lit up, Show experience

reviews_attraction.text: Grandview Overlook is awesome! I’ve been twice, once at sunset and once at night. I would recommend it at any time of day/night. The overlook provides an incredible view of the city and it’s usually not too crowded which makes it admirable.

Great spot for a picnic! I’m bummed because a lot of it was blocked off due to COVID but it was still pretty to walk, through. I’ll be sure to take my girlfriend here once it’s fully open. It seems like a really enjoyable, peaceful place.

Cool view! It’s a nice quiet spot right by the water if you want a relaxing spot to chill at. It’s right off of the Hudson River Bikeway so it’s a perfect stopping point. There’s even space nearby to have a picnic or something here.

Gorgeous, bustling park with lots to do. Great views, especially for people watching. From spring to fall the flowers in the park are amazing! They create a lot of vibrant color! Sometimes there are cool shows in the park as well!

Cool place. I, unfortunately, didn’t get the chance to go to a service, but I really liked the architecture of the church. It seems like a addition to the Morningside Heights area! I want to get to a service at some point soon!
Not the most attractive building from the outside, but it sure is gorgeous on the inside. Went for a Knicks game and had a blast. The seats are super comfy too which is a great plus.
Great park! The hilly traverse is gorgeous and the trees are at perfect climbing height! The park also features gorgeous views! There is such happy energy at this park!
Beautiful park. It’s a gorgeous oasis in the middle of downtown Manhattan. The landscaping is incredible. I’d recommend for a lunch break or a date. Great spot!
Gorgeous view from here as well as the boulder behind it. Climbing up the rock lets you see the surrounding buildings which sure is a sight to see!
Glad that I hit this spot! Super cool piece of history, and a great sight. Glad I didn’t catch smallpox... knock on wood!

Been here twice and no cover charge each time. Although it seems they do charge to get in on special occasions. So call ahead if need be. First time I took the family there for pumpkin picking in 2014. It was busy of course, parking was tough. But we found a place to park on a side street. No map for the place, but big deal. We strolled around, figured out our bearings and it was very festive. Picked and bought pumpkins. Got hot cider and put a blanket down on some grass to rest. Second time we did the petting zoo on a random Sunday in July (summer 2015). $4 per adult, the one year old was free. Animals seemed happy enough. There was a "corn" box instead of a sand box. Kids loved that more than the animals. Bought fresh picked produce at the market. Checked out the cute store and bought a cookie. They offer adult classes that seem cool, but I haven't taken any. I also can't speak for renting the place out for events. But as far as family fun time on the weekends we had positive experiences both times. Oh, we saw an alpaca eat a banana whole, peel and all. Crazy. As always, do your homework ahead of time, find out what's going on there and call ahead to make sure the day goes smooth.

Constructed on land where a bunch of huge gas tanks once stood, Elmhurst Park is a destination greenspace and the playscape found within the encompassing parkland earns the epic title with flying colors. You name it, this playground has got it: lots of swings for big kids, toddlers and special needs kids alike, a slide built into a stone hardscape, a toddler water sprinkler set apart from the big kid sprinkler (huge plus), shaded benches for parents to chill on, an innovative play zone with stationary bicycles and "engine room" sound units for communication games. There's lots of shaded patches of grass in the surrounding parkland to throw down a blanket on, an astroturf field for sports, and a brand new relief facility within easy access. Only downside: it's a milelong walk from the nearest subway stop. Extra bonus: there's a big hill in the center of the park for wintertime sledding.

Wow, I'm the 166th reviewer of the first museum in the U.S., if not the entire word, dedicated to children. Hey adults have fun learning things here too. This is a wonderful institution, but I do have some construction criticism. First, the architecture of the building itself. It doesn't fit in with the aesthetic of the neighborhood. And although there are so many incredible exhibits here, they could reduce the number of them in favor of making more room for the visitors. This place is immensely popular and successful, but it gets so crowded. For example, they should quadruple the size of the water play area and eliminate the reading area altogether. That's what libraries are for. I'm just saying is all -- you've got kids packed into the main attractions and then these other areas that are almost empty. So why not lose the areas that are underutilized in favor of the areas that are?

Being from Astoria (NYC) it's not always easy to get the family out of the city to see something other than concrete. But as a 50 minute ride away from town, visiting this historic farm was a great day trip. Farm animal sightseeing is great. No petting zoo element, but that's ok. It's more real. You can throw a blanket down anywhere and bring your own lunch. The snack bar is just fried, greasy food and no vegetarian options. (Which is ironic seeing as it's a farm.) The museum / historical elements are nice and walking through the old farm house is cool too. There was a farmer's marketing going on the day we where there. And there was a "fairy" walk event going on where families with little girls were invited to dress them up in fairy costumes and walk them along a trail in the woods. I mean, wooded fairy walk? How freakin' cute is that? Can check that one of the list.

One shouldn't base a review of a place off of nostalgia--but on the real quality of a place. I grew up near a park that wasn't this one and although I love visiting it to relive the old days, it's still a dumpy park. Now, of course, Astoria Park isn't dumpy. But there's room for improvement. Ignoring the roar of the bridge traffic (nothing a local alderman can do about that), the playground sprinkler needs a redo and the entire grounds and landscaping need serious attention. But the riverside location is very nice and the trees are plentiful and shady and yes, the pool and athletic areas are solid. And there's a lot of history here. All good positives. But a great city park needs to be more than rec facilities and jogging paths. It needs a real sense of escape and just a touch of wild nature. So, yeah, it's a GOOD park, but far from a GREAT park.

This review is for the playground itself. Not the river views and soccer field. Basically my reaction is this: nice sprinkler feature, but for such a popular area, you'd think this playground was a bit bigger. This park deserves one of those super playgrounds. Also, there are only two toddler swings nearby. TWO. And the person who designed and authorized the toddler swings probably doesn't have kids because the swings are super low so you need to strain your back while bending over to push your kid. Tip: rise those suckers up by shortening the chains. And with only two of them, you have a situtaion where the  most impatience beings on earth (16 month olds) have to wait. There are some cool wooden play features here: like the bounce pads and the train and the wooden bridge. Fun features for sure. And yes, great river views.
likes: Wooden play features (bounce pads, train, bridge)

reviews_attraction.text: "Nature" walk might be a bit of a misnomer. But perhaps it's used more like the word "democracy" or "freedom." Something to strive for... Anyway, it's certainly an interesting place with a very cool conceptual stairway that tapers down into the creek's water. But be careful. Newtown Creek is an environmental disaster and is a designated superfund site. In the mid 1800s, the creek was "one of the busiest hubs of industrial activity in New York City. More than 50 refineries were located along its banks, including oil refineries, petrochemical plants, fertilizer and glue factories, sawmills, and lumber and coal yards." Yikes. But I'd say this place is still worth a visit if only for the historic curiosity factor and to show support for what a greener, cleaner and "natural" creek could someday be like.

Five stars for an inspiring and fun visit to RAM. The wife and I visited right before Christmas and we were treated to a wide variety of surprises: festive holiday decor, an incredible glass exhibit, a found / recycled materials exhibit, repurposed wood / furniture, textiles, household crafts, et cetera. The list goes on. Local and global artists alike. And all in a beautiful space and in a beautiful location along Lake Michigan in downtown Racine. Wustum Art Museum (free admission) is in another part of town and also worth checking out.

Check ahead of time for hours and for the hours of other nearby attractions so that your day goes smooth. RAM admission:

Adults - $5
Seniors (over age 62) - $3
Students - $3
Under 12 - Free (with adult - maximum of 3)
Members - FREE

One word: epic. This is easily one of the best playgrounds in NYC. It's a real go-out-of-your-way type place to visit. You make a whole day out of it. Unlike most playgrounds, the natural stone used for the play facilities (not to mention the real bedrock it's built next to) has that genuine outdoor adventure quality. The slides are super fast unlike some dinky ones other playgrounds have. It's spacious, there's good separation from the toddler and big kid areas. Heck, toddlers even get their own water sprinkler set apart from the big kid one. That's unheard of right there. That helps with safety. Add the Central Park location and historical factor and, yeah, like I said. Epic.

Like many old industrial zones next to all the new real estate development happening up and down Queens' and Brooklyn's East River frontage, this area has been turned into a very nice park. The trees are still too young and few for babies 'n blankets, but the playground and water feature are great. Wasn't too busy on a hot Sunday in late July, but maybe we just got lucky. There's even a long pier to stroll out on and views of the city are an extra bonus. In the summertime, Brooklyn Ice Cream factory has an outlet up near Newtown Creek. It's great.

This review is for the playground, not the entire park. Here's the thing, yes, the views are incredible. Wonderful location, no doubt. And cool, new age playground equipment. All great positives. But here's the catch: no toddler swings. How can a state of the art playground in the 21st century not have a high stock of toddler swings? Also, as of summer 2015, the water feature is busted and the signs that were posted said it would be fixed; but, alas, it never was. Anyway, this place is a family destination. The playground is still a lot of fun.

Not giving it five stars because it's the biggest and best botanical garden in the city, but because I support any effort in Queens to bring some countryside wisdom into the bowels of urban asphalt and concrete. Yes, it's a tranquil and beautiful place and they have a nice, new parking lot. But for me, as a local, it's really about what it represents. Nature is a key part of any future city plan and we need places like this to be thought leaders and to inspire us. Grab the kids, grab the girlfriend, grab grandma, whatever. Just go there. Do it!

This review is for the playground only, not the entire park. Playground is really an amazing place. It's probably in the top three playgrounds I've ever visited in NYC. Yes, location is incredible. Playground equipment is cutting age. BUT, the thing that just amazes me, and why I don't give it five stars: no toddler swings. Incredible. There are two big kid swings. Two. And there are two swings for special needs kids. Great. But what about the wee little ones? No swings for them? Hard to believe. Anyway, still an incredible playground.

New park built on a historic factory site along the river. Not a lot of shade for babies and blankets, but good for older kids, sunbathers and frisbee throwers. Nature lovers might find the term "state park" a misnomer if they are used to more lush, green places. This park is kind of ho-hum in terms of beauty. But history buffs might appreciate it. If you have kids, go to Transmitter Park or the Gantry State Park instead. Playgrounds at those spots are much better and the views of Manhattan are just as good, if not better.

This is one of NYC's "destination" playgrounds. One that stands above the rest. Interesting water feature, great separation between early years, toddler and big kid areas. Lots of swings, great equipment, cool educational features, large astroturf field and located near lots of cafes and restaurants. I hail from Astoria and my family likes exploring new parks and this one was on the list. Glad we visited. Lots of fun. Very busy of course, but hey, you can say that about any real destination in this little town.

Wonderful "destination" playground. By that I mean it's not just your average neighborhood playground but one that a New Yorker (with kids) can seek out as a city excursion.  It's rather huge and there are different areas for big kids and toddlers alike. Equipment is in good condition and there are public bathrooms. You can park right along Myrtle Avenue for free. Of course bringing a lunch is key and Forest Park's nature trails are right nearby as well. You can add this place to the fun family-day check list.

Yes it's one of the city's more extraordinary sites and it's easy to forget you're surrounded by 8 million people. But it's also among the greatest examples in all the world of a totally human-made landscape that perfectly mimics a naturally occurring wild place. Central Park was designed by people: even its rock outcroppings, lakes and, yes, waterfalls. That fact only adds to how amazing Hallett's Sanctuary is in my opinion. Peace. Tranquility. Wildness. Love it.

Playground is big but outdated. Would be nice to see new playground equipment added. Old, tall trees are fantastic however. Great shade for hot summer days in the park. Nice grass areas for babies 'n blankets. A farmer's market was going on the day we visited. Nice touch. Water spray feature was pretty bad. If they update that, then this park gets four stars for sure. An A+ for trees and history, C for playground.

There's so many great things about the playground located in the park. The play equipment is so inspired and has a nautical theme. And there's so many different kinds of play equipment to explore. It's even fun for adults. It's new, modern and innovative. It's worth taking a day trip out of NYC just to see this playground and visit downtown Mamaroneck. Walking the harbor is pleasant as well. Magical.

One of my favorite playgrounds in Central Park. It's has a secret garden feeling to it. It's low-key and "hidden" to some degree. It has as delightful gated entrance and a slide built into the bedrock. Bucket swings for toddlers, a water spray future, a storybook stone bridge, picnic area and a massive sand pit. One of Central Park's magical spots.

Not your best playground but certainly not your worst. Actually a nice surprise when I took my toddler here was how much fun we had watching the dogs run around in the dog park. You can look down into the dog area from up above and the doggie action is as primordial as you might expect.

This park's renovation has turned it into a great park. It's great for kids of all ages. Great water feature for those hot summer days and lots of swings for small toddlers. Dog park too. It's not far from LIC's riverfront and my family walked to the nearby smorgasbord to grab lunch.

Brooklyn's third oldest public park, with a WWI monument, gardens, bocce courts and cultural events. Great separation between toddler and big kid playgrounds. Lots of toddler bucket seat swings and good water spray feature.
The toddler swings were broken when I visited there with my wee one, but it's a great park for sure. Good separation between toddler and big kid areas. Nice water feature and athletic fields too.
The playground is literally epic. Epic! Great stop for out-of-towners looking for a place to let the kids blow off some steam.

The Butler Institute of American Art is a magnificent and shining gem. Deceiving in its size as viewed from the road, Google Maps, and even from the imagery on their own homepage, ‘The Butler’ as it is commonly referred to has an extensive collection spread out over two floors in its main building (with three floors of art in the newly opened and quite modern attached-annex), and in several wonderful galleries in the upper floor of the church next door (accessed by an impressive glass-enclosed elevated walkway). Masterpieces by Winslow Homer, Fitz Hugh Lane, Robert Vonnoh, Thomas Cole, Herman Herzog, Mary Cassatt, John Singer Sargent, Norman Rockwell, and Albert J. Bierstadt are among the vast collection that spans centuries (18th to current) and genres (Impressionism to Modern, and a combination of Art and Technology). I was lucky enough to see a special exhibit of art by Tony Bennett, which included quite a few wonderful pieces.

Parking is free, and on the ride side of the main building (the gate at the guard shack will automatically raise for you as you drive up to it). Employee parking is on the left side of the main building, and the security guard on duty appeared to be taking down license plate numbers so maybe don't park there.

The entrance to the museum is through a set of double-doors on the front porch, itself framed by two gorgeous columns and a tiled deep-blue and mosaic ornate ceiling. There is an information desk to the left with free gallery floor plans and other literature, as well as a visitor registry, and to the right is the security desk. Admission is free. There is a donation box in front of you as you enter the foyer. Just ahead of the foyer is the Fine Art store (visit this last), and the elevator to the upstairs exhibits.

The best way to see the museum is to start with the galleries to the left as you enter the museum and go clockwise through the main galleries that surround the great two-story main hall. After this I would suggest heading into the new annex and see everything there, on all three floors. Next, tour the exhibits in the great hall in the main building – first floor, then the second floor, followed by the galleries on the second floor that surround the great hall, and then proceed via the glass walkway into the galleries in the church.

There is a small, well-lit café and a gift shop on the main floor at the rear of the museum. Both are well worth stopping in for a visit. Rest rooms are on the second floor just off of the elevators.

If you truly enjoy art, and are the type of person that will stand there and appreciate a piece you love while becoming absorbed into it, allow about three hours to tour the museum.

This museum is well worth your time. I drove three hours one-way from north-central West Virginia and was extremely happy that I took the time (on my birthday) to visit this wonderful American treasure. Highly recommended.

WOW! Let me preface this review by saying I really had no intention of ever coming here. I had thought maybe it was going to be "swoosh, right over my head", like some of what I had seen down at the Wood Street Gallery and the other installation,  "boutique", or one-room, one-piece galleries downtown. They were very nice, unique, some quite memorable, others just out of my league. I drive about two hours one-way from WV to see the Broadway National Tours at the Benedum, the shows at the Byham and the Cabaret at Theater Square, the concerts and performances at Heinz Hall, and enjoy the Cultural District's many offerings, and with upwards of six hours to kill I had already visited just about every every museum, gallery, vista, and sightseeing attraction Pittsburgh has to offer in the preceding sixteen months (25+ trips) since I had been coming to Pittsburgh. With my time winding down here in the area, and with only one last opportunity remaining to see the Mattress Factory, I finally told myself "let's get this over with". Man, what the hell was I waiting on. This place was just simply amazing. And the staff were all so very friendly and helpful. The pictures I've seen simply cannot do it justice. Installation art of this size, this scale, well, it slaps you in the face, wraps around you, surrounds you, and it absorbs you into it like no other art form can.  I really believe the key to enjoying this is catching it with as FEW people in the exhibits as possible. Be the only one in the room. I was the first person in the building on a Saturday morning, and for the most part the only one in each gallery or on every floor, every time, in two out of three buildings. I can't imagine trying to appreciate this when there are a dozen or more people all talking and flocking around each other all angling to see the exhibit. Go see this. I can't believe I waited this long. Or maybe it's a good thing I did.

I think the most important thing to remember is that the Frick is not just the one small building with a once privately held art collection. The Frick, as the brochure says, is an ‘experience’. From start to finish the entire estate needs to be savored; one painting at a time, one building at a time, one automobile at a time, one flower at a time, and one room of the Clayton at a time. Enjoy the Visitors Center, the souvenir shop filled with all sorts of amazing items, and last but not least, enjoy the Café. If you arrive first thing in the morning when they open, allow a couple of hours to see everything, and then have an elegant lunch.

Yes, the art museum is small - one of the smallest I’ve seen next to the Kennedy Museum of Art in Athens, Ohio. But it’s the small museums that are the most manageable - ones that when you’re done there’s no ‘burn out’ syndrome. I love art, all kinds of art, and there are some truly fine examples on display. Take the time to appreciate what is there, and don’t try to critically compare it to museums you’ve been to ‘all over the world’ as far as the quantity or quality. I too have been to museums all over the world and still found this enjoyable. Loved the collection of fine vehicles in the Car and Carriage Museum. The Greenhouse was mostly under renovation and only the center room contained plants and flowers, but there was still something beautiful there to enjoy.

The staff were all very kind and helpful, we shared names of artists and influences, and they couldn’t have been nicer.

Overall my time at the Frick was amazing. I plan to go back again in the summer to see what’s new!

The entire experience was absolutely exceptional, incredible, from the ticket counter and all the floor staff, the lady taking the souvenir pictures, to the two floors of amazing exhibits. And this from someone not particularly a pro football fan. I spent three hours here, bought the Bronze Membership, and took over 250 pictures myself. The exception to my absolutely exceptional, incredible experience being the girls at the pick-up counter where you get your souvenir pictures, who are completely void - and I do mean ZERO - of any customer service. Brandi all but snapped my ticket from my hand, no greeting, no eye contact, never even looked up at me, as she sat there on her stool feet bundled up under her like she was polishing her toes or something, and handed it off to another staff, who apologizes to Brandi! It was like I was interrupting something they were all already doing. And I was the only customer standing there at the moment.
