Brandi then walked off and eventually one of the girls finally asked how I was doing, to which I replied that I as doing fine "...up until about 60 seconds ago." I filed a formal complaint against Brandi with the supervisor of the PFHoF. Turns out Brandi was the Supervisor of the girls in the photo shop. If Brandi is the last point of contact guests have at the Pro Football Hall of Fame, maybe the Pro Football Hall of Fame needs to have a chat with Brandi.

There's parking for about forty cars at the visitors center and gift shop. It's also the main parking lot for those wanting to see the iconic grist mill, one of the most photographed spots in the state of West Virginia. Best bet is to get there in the early morning when the light is most suitable for photography.

There are two main scenic overlooks, both easily accessible from the road, and well worth the drive to get to them: the first is along the road (about half-way) heading towards the upper cabins, the other near the upper cabins picnic area. There's another overlook (Island in the Sky) that's best accessed by driving the road that heads toward the lake, and at the first hairpin-turn there's a small pull off: take that short trail (always going to the right of it forks), and after an easy five minute walk, there's a shelter and a rocky outcrop. Be careful if you have kids because there's a bit of a cliff there.

The lake is nice and scenic but was closed when I was there due to it being 'past season' for boating and other activities, though you could still park there and walk the trail around the lake.

Overall a great way to spend the day!

The 2-hour In-depth tours (the ONLY one that allows interior photography of the home) are limited to just 10 people, and no children. Get the first tour of the day, as you'll literally open the house and be 'first', with much better opportunities for pictures too, as well as better parking. So much of the furniture, art, and other assorted pieces in the house are from a different 'time and place', and I can easily see myself living here. The expansive patio off of the master bedroom is truly wonderful, as is the beautiful Guest House above and behind the main house. All of the rooms in both buildings have lots of little fascinating objects to admire, think back to the original owners who owned them, and the family that actually lived here. Remember, this began as a country retreat, and a home to getaway from the big city. Truly a wonderful experience to step into the mind of the designer and architect. There's a sales pitch at the end of the tour to become a contributing member. The cafe at the visitors center was a bit expensive but well worth it as the food was very tasty. The house, guest house, and grounds are all amazing!

There's plenty of parking at the visitor's center - make sure to stop there for the informative video, displays, gift shop, park maps, brochures, and a scenic view of the New River from the back deck, the latter perfect for those with mobility issues who may not be able to descend the stairs to the other bridge-view observation decks.

From the large stone National Register of Historical Places marker and trail-information placard there are two trails: to the right, an overview of the bridge-deck and highway; to the left, descend to two different observation decks. The first observation deck offers a nice view (somewhat semi-obstructed) of the arched bridge, whereas a very steep descending stairway takes you to a grand view of the gorge and bridge. It'll take you maybe five minutes to get to the lower observation level. Getting down there is easy. Going back up is rated as 'strenuous', but there are numerous places to stop and rest. I'm not in the best of shape, took my time, and made it with little effort.

Parking is in a small reserved lot on 2nd Street between Julianna St. and Ann St. under the Hwy-68 off-ramp. There's a 7-foot maximum clearance bar at the entrance to the lot, so no tall vehicles allowed.

The museum itself is a true gem of local history, with everything from extensive collections of Indian artifacts to cars, furniture, portrait painting, and steamboat memorabilia. Start in the basement with the video (a fact they neglected to tell me), then tour the first and second floors. My personal favorite was the second floor displays with the model boats and pictures of the local riverboat history.

Highly recommend stopping here. If you're also going over to the island, tour the museum afterwards. It'll be more meaningful and put everyone into a better perspective. There's also a wonderful gift shop with lots of really great items.

If you tour the the museum as well as take the riverboat ride to the island for the mansion tour and wagon ride expect to spend about four hours minimum.

The museum is most definitely worth your time, there's no doubt about it. The staff - from the customer service desk to the gallery attendants - were all very, very nice.

The entirety of the museum's main galleries are on the second floor, the collections ranging from Contemporary, Folk Art, and 19th/20th Century. With lots of delightful and thought provoking pieces (I caught 'The Art of Movement' exhibit and thought it incredible, mind-boggling, and amazing), there is something here for everyone, and everyone will find something here to like. The only issue I had was with the 'Southwestern Pennsylvania' room, as overwhelmingly beautiful as it is, there is simply no way to enjoy art when displayed 20 feet over your head.

Allow at least 90-120 minutes to enjoy the museum. There's a very fine gift shop that also has a limited choice of small beverages and snacks, but no other food, so eat before coming.

I'm glad I took the time to come here.

About 45 minutes from The Greenbrier Resort, this is another must-see state park, albeit the main attraction - the boardwalk twisting through the rock formations and wooded area - will take you no more than 30 minutes tops to make it through the entire circuit, even at a slow pace. Only a small portion is HC accessible since this course winds up and down and through a lot of woods and steep hills.

There is no visitor’s center, no refreshment stand, and only one uni-sex toilet swarming with flies that reeked beyond words.

The road leading in is quite narrow. There’s limited parking, so if it’s real busy you may have to run over to Droop Mountain Battleground State Park (10 minutes away) or the wonderful Pearl S. Buck Birthplace Museum home (17 minutes) in Hillsboro and come back.

Lots of picture opportunities here of nature at its weirdest and most wonderful deep in the woods in WV.

Updated: Sept. 22, 2018
The HEROES & SHEROES exhibit was gorgeous. This is a must see! Don’t miss the Visible Storage, a wonderful collection as well. The entire museum is a staggering and impressive collection.

Review from April 2015...
One of the best museums in Pittsburgh (second only to the Carnegie Art and Natural History Museum) and definitely a 'must see'. Take your time and allow at least two to three hours: there's a huge sports collection that any sports fan would be impressed by; floors and floors of local history that as a non-local I found it to be very informative and interesting; and detailed special exhibits, all worthy of the $16 admission. Only about a 15 minute walk from the Cultural District this is a great way to spend the day before a concert, show, or a game at PNC Park. Don't miss this museum!

Despite being directly across from the Fort Pitt Museum - which is run by the Senator John Heinz History Center - the Fort Pitt Blockhouse is privately owned and operated by the Fort Pitt Society of the Daughters of the American Revolution of Allegheny County, Pennsylvania.

It was open on the early Sunday morning when I was down at The Point taking pictures, and is free of charge. The second floor is not accessible due to safety reasons, but about half of the floorboards have been removed so you can see some of the architectural details and flood-level markers.

The nice custodian on duty (Feb. 21, 2016) was very friendly and eager to talk about the history of the blockhouse.

As of March 14, 2019, the main church is undergoing massive renovations and no one is allowed inside. The cemetery grounds are still open. Notable markers include those of Alexander Hamilton and his extended family and associates (Hercules is buried further away near a tree, and Angelica is buried on the opposite side of the church from Alexander and Eliza), Robert Fulton, as well as countless unknowns with markers dating back to 1681. There is a small prayer chapel still open, only accessible through the rear of the church. Overall a stunning example of early American history. Reverence and respect are of course expected at all times.

Down a winding road several miles off of the interstate is Prickett's Fort State Park. Just when you think you've missed the turn-off and you're lost, there's the parking lot for the Visitor's Center. Prickett's Fort is a wonderful re-creation of a 1774 fort, complete with blockhouses, a trading post with handmade items for sale, meeting house, several living-cabins, tinsmith, and a working blacksmith's shop. Very educational. There's a 2+ mile walking and bike trail that goes off of the upper parking lot, and boat launch area down by the lower parking lot. The Visitor's Center also has a nice gift shop. Highly recommended.
likes: Variety of facilities (blockhouses, trading post, meeting house, living-cabins, tinsmith, blacksmith's shop)
On-site activities (walking and bike trail, boat launch)

reviews_attraction.text: An old-style in-depth museum where three long corridor walls are lined with large, deep display cases fronted by divided glass panels and dozens of other display cases fill the galleries and halls. Take your time and examine the exceptional quality artifacts and historical references. From start to finish expect to spend at least an hour here. Anyone interested in American battles and wars should make this a must-see on their list of places to visit in Pittsburgh. Don't forget to stop into the Memorial Hall (auditorium) if only just to see it's grand size.

I almost didn't go to the West Virginia State Museum, but hey, it was free. Turned out to be an amazing labyrinth of history spanning time: from the formation of the Appalachian Mountains thru to today. It was truly a wonderful museum, the entrance lobby displaying dozens of large, hand-made quilts. Do yourself a favor and take your time, browse through the many wonderful displays, room-sized recreations, and the countless intricate details documenting the history of West Virginia. Do not miss this. Highly recommended.

Stunning. Arrived here an hour before opening to take the time to tour the outside gardens on the north side (between the main facility and the Columbus statue) as well as the the aquatic pools on the south side. Was the first ticketed guest of the day; took my time to enjoy the amazing flowers and plants, had a great lunch in the café - all together spent about four hours here. Free parking in the center-island across from the main entrance. Well worth a visit and highly recommended!

It's a piece of baseball history. Only a portion of the outfield wall remains, but worth a photo-op for any sports fan. Just across the street (on the sidewalk) is a commemorative plaque, and inside Posvar Hall (the large building across from the outfield wall) is the Home Plate for Forbes Field (go in the main entrance and it's about half way down on the left). Metered parking is available along the street. Spent about 30 minutes taking pictures.

Make sure to take some refreshments and snacks. Be careful on the stones in the river as they can become VERY slippery and dangerous. The gazebo is lovely and a nice place to have a small wedding. There's also a small children's play area up away from the river as not to distract from the peace and quiet of the falls themselves. Definitely worth the time to trek out here and see!

Gorgeous day on March 14, 2019 when I stopped through the park to see the arch. It’s very impressive. From alternating angles you can get a picture through the arch of the Empire State Building or WTC in the distance. There’s a plaque in the ground under the archway that describes the arch and it’s construction. So glad I came. It’s quite remarkable.

An imposing and formidable monument with its grand sculptures on the exterior and relief castings on the interior. Take your time to notice the West Virginia reference. If it's busy it can get a bit crowded, but don't let that deter you from visiting this amazing tribute to the fallen heroes.

Closed for through traffic as of 29 Aug 2015 due to renovation, but you can still get decent pictures, and on an early Saturday morning there was no one around, affording the opportunity to walk through the bridge from the town-side and take pictures of the interior without getting run over.
Very enjoyable tour although photography is not permitted in the interior of the home. The view from the back yard is breathtaking. Take time to enjoy the walk back down through the sculpture's path.
Very cool (iconic) Philly sculpture, looks better at night. There’s some street and/or sidewalk construction going on around it (as of Nov. 11, 2017) but you can still get good pictures of it.
Architecturally one of the finest buildings in Philadelphia. Make sure to walk completely around it, as it looks different from every angle and aspect.

We went to the Phil Collins Not Dead Yet Tour, we were seated in section A row 13 seats 15 and 16 which are the last two seats on the inside row. Great view (until people stand up) and great sound and acoustics. Our usher took is right to our seats. The lobby area is very nice and we had a snack and something to drink before the show. Contrary to the three other venues we went to see plays at (3) Madison Square Garden lets you in earlier than everyone else (easily an hour plus before the show) other venues it is 30 minutes before show time pretty much. Phil, in my opinion, is at about 80-85% of his peak from a voice perspective, the good news is that 80% of his voice is better than most at 100%. Great show, great band, his son is a joy to watch on the drums. The backup singers and the horn section are great and so is the rest of the band (some from Genesis) that have been with him for over 40 years and the Bass Player, Leland Sklar, that has played with, Toto and numerous other bands. Great Show must see while you can don't think he will be touring after this.
dislikes: Obstructed view when people stand up

reviews_attraction.text: Shakespeare Garden is a colorful, flower-lush 4-acre spot in Central Park, on the western side of the park loop at 79 - 80 Sts. 20 blocks north of Columbus Circle. It's a lovely span of enclosed garden beds, walking paths, benches, lovingly stone stairways, and some isolation from the hubbub. Partly on a slope, the garden is adjacent to steps that in one direction lead to the unique pseudo-medieval Belvedere Castle (opened after long 2019 repair and renovation) and a fine view uptown, over Turtle Pond. In a slightly different route is Delacorte Theater, famous for its outdoor stage and amphitheater that has hosted many plays by, you may have guessed, William Shakespeare. (Delacorte, by the way, is a venture of the Public Theater in the East Village.) Take a brief walk from Shakespeare Garden to the front of the Delacorte to find two evocative statues dedicated to the works of the Bard: the namesakes of Romeo and Juliet, and Prospero and Miranda of The Tempest.

I took a stroll along the Pumphouse Park in August evening, it was one of most scenic walk I had ever seen. The skyline of Jersey City in silhouette added color to this dramatic scenic esplanade. I highly recommend visiting this beautiful park in the evening. Small circular park with ample benches and trees. The place looks beautiful all year long but is breathtaking during early spring. Nice little park. Not what I'd call peaceful but a nice place for a shady bench or a picnic on the lawn. It does have some good running space for a toddler. The ground can be hit or miss. Blank spots in the grass and dlow drying mud. Over all it is a nice spot to escape the insanity of the financial district. Considering poor good choices nice place to head on a sunny day for lunch.

My 3rd grade daughters classroom has been doing 3D traveling Oh, and one of the places my daughter enjoyed visiting the most was the Statue of Liberty. We had a school break so we planned a trip to NYC and my daughter loved seeing the Statue of Liberty. She had done a bunch of homework about the facts of the statue and she was basically like my little tour guide. All of the visitors were very kind and many people asked if they could take our picture oh, and we would ask to take their pictures. We enjoyed the museum. We wish we would have eaten on the ferry ride over because the pretzels looked amazing. We were very tired on that trip so we passed on visiting Ellis Island but we are happy to know that was included in our ticket package. A very enjoyable experience.

We came to this operational church totally unprepared for what awaited us. It was referenced several times in Joan Didion's "The Year of Magical Thinking", which spurred my interest. To begin with the outside garden (free) has a fantastical huge sculpture surrounded by, perhaps, nearly 50 small sculptures created by children. It was fun to walk around it and discover more and more of its intricacies. We were able to take a guided tour ($) that took us all the way up to the top under the eaves of the ceiling. On the way we stopped off on partial rooftops to view the outside architecture, as well. I appreciated the physics of the construction despite not being an architect. It would probably be best not to go in July or August because of the heat.

The Japanese Hill-and-Pond is probably the most famous feature of the Brooklyn Botanic Garden.  A man-made pond with well manicured plants is especially accentuated during spring by the flowering cherry blossoms.  The red gate (torii) in the middle of the pond is a popular structure that really helps photo pops.  There are also 2 stone lanterns (daidoro) in the area, which are great features for photos as well.  The pond isn't so large that walking the circumference of the pond becomes difficult, especially for children and the elderly.  In terms of cherry blossoms, the trees in this area consistently blooms earlier than the ones in the Cherry Esplanade, so visit approximately 2 weeks prior the Sakura Matsuri to get photos of the peak bloom.

I really enjoyed your work. I liked to buy the passes, because we had access to many attractions, and the values would be much more expensive if we were to buy individually. I would like to make this constructive analysis in order to alert the company to the improvement of the services provided.Some information is out of date on the Brazil website. Overall we liked it a lot because we had VIP access to the attractions. I found the tour buses very old and dirty, you should constantly clean them. For those who go on the first floor of the tour buses, the air conditioning is not turned on in summer, we get very hot, and the windows must be transparent, and without stickers so we can see the sights.

My friend and I went to the Brooklyn Museum (suggested admission price) to see the JR Chronicles. It is an exhibit replete with murals, photographs, videos, dioramas, etc. Photographs of monumental size stud the walls with subjects having fun making grotesque faces for the camera. These photos are pasted onto walls of public spaces - many times illegally. This multi-media installation is not to be missed. You'll spend an entire afternoon at this exhibit alone. In another gallery on the same floor (the first) is an exhibit of prints from the 15th to 20th centuries. It is a large collection very worthwhile seeing. Don't miss both of these wonderful exhibits.

As we entered the park we obtained a map and advice as to what to see and where to walk from the information booth and set off to explore. Along the way we found various statues and at the start of Literary Walk immediately recognised a tribute to Shakespeare in his traditional attire to the side of the path. In practice just one of several statues to well know people of the literary world. To compliment a walk along the path numerous artists were selling their works adding colour, interest and atmosphere to our stroll, with the occasional squirrel scurrying around. What a lovely place for a walk, to relax and take in nature, in the middle of a busy city.

Another attraction included on our NY passes and we only visited because it was nearby and we didn't have anything else in mind. Glad we did though. We all thoroughly enjoyed it. There's 2 sections, the first bit is an immersive movie experience culminating in a 3D movie as part of a bait ball swarm. This bit was great, well worth the entrance fee alone and took about 45 minutes to get through. The next section was also advertised as taking a further 45 minutes but we felt the second half was quite small and 15 minutes was pushing it. However, as an overall experience we all enjoyed it and were glad we went.

The Met Breuer is small - a rowboat compared to Mother Met a few blocks away. When it has really good exhibitions, its small size and intimacy make it a great place to absorb the art on offer without the crowds that can make a visit to the Big Met challenging - and even exhausting. My advice is to check out the exhibits first and then, if one or more really tempt you, then go to the Breuer. Even if exhibits sound unusual, all the more reason to visit. Unusual can be mind-expanding. Different should be tempting too! Just be careful about the cafe on the lower level. It's oh so trendy and expensive.

Wave Hill is a wonderful place to observe Greenhouses and their plantings from all over the world. The grounds are nestled directly parallel to the Hudson River which makes the scenery marvelous.There are benches located strategically where one can meditate on the majestic Hudson River, and the Palisade Cliffs.There is a food concession selling fresh eats,i.e.: sandwiches, salada, desserts,beer/wine, coffee and tea.One can tour the different houses on the property that sometimes have artistic exhibitions. Wave Hill is a hidden jewel that is worth the visit.Great day trip.Francisco

If you are doing New York with a toddler in tow, then put this on your to do list! They will love it, and you will be rewarded with a few hours peace. The museum is very much hands on, and aimed at young children. Out three year old LOVED playing at being a chef n a pizza restaurant and driving an MTA bus. We loved watching her play and enjoying herself. The museum is clearly signed from the subway. The only disappointment was the lack of suitable food fro toddlers in the cafe . I would advise bringing your own. Apart from that, the museum is well worth a visit.

We really enjoyed this place while we were in New York. If you’re ever in the city this is one place to go. Very good information nice displays and fun time. The very good time was well spent. There was so many displays you will have to go and experience yourself. We were both in awe, curious and shocked at the many unique exhibits in this museum. It was a huge hit with my family and we would highly recommend this experience. Note: Some content (torture room) is not age appropriate for some but overall, the exhibits were family friendly.

Stumbled upon Federal Hall when we went to see the NY Stock Exchange. As a history enthusiast, I was so excited to find this. There were tons of tourists in the area taking pictures with the statue of Washington, but inside was very empty and quiet. I had no idea this was where Washington was inaugurated. I love stumbling upon historical places. I wish the National Park Service was fully funded to upkeep this building as it should be, but the small offerings they had were very nice! I would recommend if you're in the area.

The park itself is pretty good. Nice green space and normally full of activities of some sort. The main reason for 5 stars is because this area is one of my favorites. NYU is here and that means affordable and tasty dining, eclectic activities and the area is not focused on tourists but the locals. If you want to see real NYC, then this is a good starting point. The archway and fountains are really nice, and the park is well maintained with lovely greenery. Great place to pass the time and close to lots of coffee shops.
likes: Proximity to dining and coffee shops

reviews_attraction.text: If you love classical music; this would be your best place to watch new gigs by seasoned and upcoming artists. A visit here would get you a catalog of the upcoming events for a month to three months where you can choose the artists or genre you'll like to see performed, the dates, time and ticket cost. There's also the Avery Fisher Building and an outside garden for meditation, reading and coffee or whatever suite you....please be warned; it's mostly a very quiet place where loud talking would be out of place.

We opted to eat at Sarabeth's since it was next door to our hotel. We were seated right away and the service was good. The bread options were really good. I had the chicken with vegetables. The chicken was good, but I didn't care the for mixture of vegetables. The wine glasses were not clean as we could still see lipstick stains on the rim. Great options nice brunch drinks service was fast and pleasant. Pretty decent wait to,get a seat. Food was fine and hot, prices were reasonable.

The Radio City Music Hall a famous vintage Art Deco theatre from the 1930s, the home of the Rockettes.. I have been coming to the Christmas Show since 1965, they used to show a Disney Movie during part of the show.. now it's all show time, dancing, singing, some great sets with large animals, camels, etc.. a show not to be missed, some great effects.. & the this theatre is old & unique, a vintage classic, .. the Rockettes signature falling down line dance is not to be missed.

Prospect park is a mini Central park, but with a local charm. Parking is difficult but the subway is available. The west side of the park has a few (but good ) restaurants. Try not to hang out on the south side, it can get a bit dangerous as it gets dark. When the leaves start to change color, prospect Park is beautiful. Keep in mind that the Brooklyn Botanic Gardens is next door. Don't bother going to the Zoo. It is very limited in sections of animals to see.

This is a small museum that brings Art and Science together in interesting pieces by designers, scientists, architects, etc. Many of the attractions are interactive, and I left inspired with some DYI project ideas of my own. This place should make success with children as well. Spring and Summer are the best times to visit since the garden holds a tree made out of 40 different species. So it must be a show on its own to see it in blossom and fruits.

This is one of NYC's finest parks (IMHO). It's centrally located in Manhattan, and it's a shady place to sit in the summer. There are always chairs available, and the public library is right next door (for clean restrooms, cooling if needed, etc), 5 min walk to Grand Central too. In the winter, they construct an ice rink in the center and you can watch people fall down on the ice! I've always enjoyed Bryant Park.

Took some friends from out of town to see the panorama exhibit of NYC and they loved it. It was so much fun trying to figure out what part of the city different areas on the map were. A really cool part is when the overhead lights dim and lights on the panorama light up to provide a "night" perspective of the city. It is definitely a must see for native New Yorkers as well as visitors to the Big Apple.

Viewed through the roof of the NY BIG BUS TOUR, the Fuller Building known popularly as the Flatiron building is an urban Juxtaposition, an architectural intervention responding to the triangular format of the site at 175 5th Avenue... The architectural massing of this urban icon is a breathtaking sight... my aim is to experience this mesmerizing view on foot during my next visit

I guess gone are the days that these rides are a few dollars a piece, That being said the rides were clean and fun and the evening enjoyable. I wish they would clearly indicate what rides are included and overview there locations as there are three parks in the area and they are easily confusable as you walk between them.We enjoyed the evening but done expect it to be cheap
dislikes: Lack of clear information on ride inclusions

reviews_attraction.text:
People who are giving this a bad rating....shame on you. They went here expecting something that this attraction doesn't claim to be. This place is awesome! It's about seeing, reading, and learning about amazing things. It's not an amusement park. It's not a place for your children to play with blocks or toys. It's a museum. And yes, it is for children - children whose parents want them to experience and learn, who want to take the time to teach their children and explain things other than how a video game works.
1. Anyone who "flew through" in 20 minutes, obviously wasn't here to see/learn about amazing Ripley's things. You could spend 20 minutes in the lobby with BumbleBee, Captain America, the world's tallest man, the gorilla built from tires.
2. Small children may not be too interested, as there is not a lot of "hands on"....but I brought a 9, 7, 4, and 3 year old here. We showed them things, read things to them, asked them silly questions about things, took pictures - it was great! They all enjoyed it, all learned new things.
3. The staff is top notch - very friendly and they leave you alone - you could spend one hour or all day in here - no pressure to keep it moving.
4. Pay attention for the things you can do - pose in the illusion with no legs, stick your head in with the bugs, play music on the musical stairs, do all the optical illusions, stick your head in the mirror box, take a picture falling off the Empire State building, get a fortune from Zandar, put your head in the jars in the medieval room, dance infront of the red screen, listen to the story the mini hologram tells you, etc.
5. The Blackhole is crazy and amazing - the kids must have done it 20 times each trying to master walking through without holding on.
6. They also have a laser room where you test out your spy skills trying to make it through without triggering any lasers - no extra charge, self serve, do it as much as you like.
7. The bathrooms are in the middle of the museum - and even they are amazing. My sons couldn't get enough of the button in the mens room that made a loud farting sound :-)
dislikes: Limited hands-on activities for small children

reviews_attraction.text:
(Translated by Google) The United Nations consists of the General Assembly Building, the Secretariat Building and the Hammarsk Library. Visitors need to make an online reservation in advance, 18 dollars a person, with a different language tour, need to leave enough time to complete the entry procedures, otherwise miss the appointment time to buy another tour ticket. Access to the visit requires a security check, and the procedure is similar to airport security. The length of the tour guide can be arranged for an hour or so. On the basement level of the visit hall, there is the United Nations' own post office, which can be bought with a stamp attached to the United Nations postmark. This postcard can only be sent by the United Nations, and it also provides a stamp for customizing your own photos, a version of $14.95, a stamp for the United States, and a United Nations chapter on the passport. It makes sense.

(Original)
联合国由大会场大楼、秘书处大楼和哈马舍图书馆三部分组成。游客参观需要提前网上预约，18美金一人，带有不同语言的tour，需要留出足够时间办理入门手续，否则错过预约时间就要另买下一个tour的票。进入参观需要通过安检，程序类似机场安检。长度约一小时，没开会的厅导游可以安排进入参观。参观大厅的地下一层有联合国自己的邮局，可买张邮票盖上联合国的邮戳寄出。这个明信片只能由联合国寄出，还提供定制自己照片的邮票，14.95美金一版，邮票美国通用，另外可以在护照上盖联合国的章，很有意义

(Translated by Google) I really enjoyed our trip to the fearless museum. The museum was built on an aircraft carrier and exploring the aircraft carrier is as exciting as those exhibitions! The space shuttle booth is also worth a look - you can get in touch with it. There is also a cockpit and deck to visit. There are many planes, helicopters and space shuttles on the flight deck, and there are some exhibitions on the deck of the pylons, showing some planes and pointers. There are also submarines and Concorde in the museum. We went there on Tuesday morning, not too many people. We didn't book tickets in advance, and we didn't wait too long to buy tickets on the spot. Standing on the flight deck is very cold, because you are standing on the Hudson River, so wear a warm spot!

(Original)
真的很喜欢我们的无畏博物馆之旅。这个博物馆建在一艘航空母舰上面，探索航空母舰跟那些展览一样令人兴奋！航天飞机展区也值得一看-你可以近距离接触它。还有驾驶舱和甲板可以参观。飞行甲板上有很多飞机、直升机和航天飞机，吊架甲板上有一些展览，展出一些飞机和指针。博物馆里还有艘潜水艇和协和飞机。我们是星期二早上去的，人不太多。我们没有提前订票，现场买票也没有等太久。站在飞行甲板上的时候很冷，因为你高高地站在哈德逊河边，所以穿的暖和点！
likes: Variety of exhibits (planes, helicopters, space shuttles)

reviews_attraction.text:
(Translated by Google) Saint Paul's Chapel is located in the heart of the financial district. It was a pre-revolutionary church that survived the events of 9/11 (a block of projections). The interior is maintained and it has an interesting history-a place to miss George Washington. There are currently many displays in the church to commemorate those rescuers who used this as a base in the September 11 incident, and people came to reflect and miss it. Behind it is a cemetery, a good place to stroll-there are many tombstones dating from 1700. To my surprise, I actually saw my relative who was surnamed Turner buried here!

(Original)
聖保羅禮拜堂位於金融區的核心位置。是一座大革命前的教堂,在9.11事件中倖免於難(是爆心投影點的一個街區)。內部經過維修保養,它有個很有趣的歷史--懷念喬治華盛頓的地方。目前在教堂中有很多的陳列品,用來紀念在9.11事件中曾將這作為基地的那些救援者,人們來到這反思和懷念。在它的背後有一個墓地,一個適於漫步的好地方--這有很多從1700年來的墓碑。令我驚訝的是我居然在這看到了我一個姓特納的親戚葬於此!

(Translated by Google) Sitting physically and mentally on the floor, as if you were in the sea of ​​stars, this is really a very interesting experience. Of course, Nair Degras Tyson also made a very clear and informative commentary on the exhibition. We have witnessed an exhibition called the "Dark Universe" about the history of the formation of the universe. We are flying through the stars of panoramic perspective. This experience is so cool. The Planetarium is located in the Museum of Natural History (although you need to buy a separate ticket to watch this exhibition), you can include this link in the museum tour.

(Original)
身心放松席地而坐，仿佛置身星辰大海，这真的是一种非常有趣的体验。当然奈尔·德葛拉司·泰森也为这场展览进行了非常清晰令人增长见闻的解说。我们目睹了一场关于宇宙形成史的名为“黑暗宇宙”的展览，我们在全景透视的星辰之间飞驰而过，这种体验太酷了。天文馆坐落在自然历史博物馆里面（尽管观看这场展览需要另外单独买票），可以顺便把这个环节包含在博物馆的参观行程中。

(Translated by Google) This building looks very beautiful. The sun rises from one side of the building and (apparently) falls from the other side. If you have the opportunity to watch the building at different times of the day, it will give you a completely different perspective and dimension of the building. It's very easy to find here, there is a park opposite the thinnest part of the building, where you can take pictures (there are also some tables and chairs for you to rest)

(Original)
这个建筑看起来非常的漂亮。太阳从建筑的一侧升起，（明显地）从另外一侧落下。如果你又机会在一天中的不同时刻观看这栋建筑，它会让你看到这栋建筑完全不同的视角和维度。这里非常容易找到，在建筑最薄部分的对面有一个公园，在那里你可以拍照（那里也有一些桌子和椅子供你休息）

(Translated by Google) I was interested in this building. I didn't take a photo inside, but I took a few shots at the bottom. I can understand that they don't allow us to take pictures of the artwork, but I don't know why we don't let us shoot the building. The iconic building, I don't think I will come back to the coffee shop here, because the drinks are generally not very tasty and the cake is very expensive. There are art exhibitions, but not my dishes.

(Original)
我就对这建筑感兴趣，在里头没有拍照片，就在底层拍了几张。我可以理解他们不允许我们对着艺术品拍照，可是不知道为什么不让我们拍建筑。标志性的建筑，我想我也不会再来这儿的咖啡厅，因为饮料一般和蛋糕也不怎么好吃，而且还很贵。有美术展览，不过不是我的菜。

(Translated by Google) This sculpture is an excitement for all fans of Lewis Carroll. This bronze statue captures all the tasks in Alice in Wonderland. Alice, Mad Hatter, Caterpillar, and even you can find Cheshire cats behind the tree. In addition to taking a self-portrait with these statues, take some time to recall the master's original work that inspired the statue. Really worth a visit

(Original)
这个雕塑是一个能让所有刘易斯·卡罗尔的粉丝们异常兴奋。这个铜像捕捉了《爱丽丝梦游仙境》里面的所有任务。爱丽丝、疯帽子、卡特彼勒、甚至你都能在树的后面发现柴郡猫。除了和这些雕像自拍以外,拿出一些时间来回忆一下激发了这个雕像的大师原著。真的非常值得一游

(Translated by Google) The Historical Society gave a complete review of Al Hirschfeld's career, starting with film posters in the early 1930s. Mickey Rooney and Judy Garland look good in their early work. Be sure to sit in Hersfeld's barber chair, who once sat in this chair to paint. You will see more after visiting the Hirschfjord exhibition.

(Original)
历史协会完整地回顾了艾尔赫施菲德（Al Hirschfeld）的生涯，从30年代初他做电影海报开始。米基·鲁尼（Mickey Rooney）和朱迪·嘉兰（Judy Garland）在早期的作品中看起来状态很好。一定要在赫施菲德的理发椅上坐一坐，他曾坐在这把椅子上作画。参观完赫施菲德展览你会看到更多。

(Translated by Google) On the fifth avenue of the drunken fans, everywhere is more fashionable and the latest fashion. So when you first see the St. Thomas Church, you will be attracted to this medieval architecture in the Harry Potter story! I suggest that you temporarily enter the time tunnel, stay away from the bustling city, sit down and enjoy the grace given by God!

(Original)
在紙醉金迷的第五大道上，到處比的都是時尚和最新流行。所以當你第ㄧ眼看到聖托馬斯教堂時，你一定會被這宛如哈利波特故事中的中古世紀建築所吸引！建議大家，暫時走進時光隧道，遠離繁華的城市，坐下來享受這神賜與的恩典吧！

After seeing the film Woman In Gold we wanted to see the Klimt paintings at the Neue Galerie. We went on a wet first Friday of the month when it is free entrance. Quite a queue formed & because of the rain the staff let us in before 6pm. There is only 1 room of the Klimt paintings but they are fantastic. There was another exhibition of Berlin in the Galerie which we walked through quickly. There is a cafe in the Galerie which is very busy.

(Translated by Google) The location is good and you can take a short break while going to the Washington Monument. Buy a hot dog, sit on the bench and watch the pedestrians walk past Village to Island Ferries the Twin and Tower Memorial. Reproduce the moment of Harry Met Sally under the arch.

(Original)
位置很好，可以在去Washington Monument的时候短暂地休息一下。买个辣热狗，坐在长椅上看面前的行人走过Village去往Island Ferries the Twin 和Tower Memorial。在拱门下重现Harry Met Sally的时刻。

We were walking by and saw this huge bronze sculpture in the garden of the church, which is in the image of a massive tree uprooted during 9/11 fallout from the Towers. I had to go inside and sit for a moment of reflection on how this church is still standing despite being so close to ground zero. It is about a block from the NY Stock Exchange, and it evokes a quiet peace inside. Step inside if you have the time, well worth it.

(Translated by Google) The lobby of this building is spectacular - sparkling mosaics are like boasting American capitalism. It is a pity that for security reasons, it is no longer possible to hang out in the lobby. If you want to glance at it, look up through the door and keep staring until the security guard leaves you.

(Original)
这座建筑的大堂非常壮观－闪闪发光的马赛克像是在夸耀美国资本主义。可惜的是由于安全原因，现在已经不能再在大堂里随意闲逛了。如果想瞥一眼，那就穿过门堂向上望，然后一直盯着直到保安让你离开。

(Translated by Google) We had a very pleasant evening, and the performance here was also worth seeing. For me it was more of an overall atmosphere. Disc jockey, crowd, dance and soul! This is the most memorable place I missed in New York! We also brought our 7-year-old child, and he likes it too.

(Original)
我们度过了很愉快的一个晚上，这里的表演也很值得看，对我而言更多的是整体的氛围。唱片骑师、人群、跳舞和灵魂！这是我在纽约待过最难忘最想念的地方了！我们还带上了我们7岁的孩子，他也很喜欢这里。

(Translated by Google) This is a very special exhibition hall, which records how different people can see the experience 911 from different angles. Here are the stories of firefighters, survivors telling, short stories, and more. There is also an oversized blue sky gathering map that makes sense.

(Original)
这是个很特别的展览馆，记载了不同的人怎样以不同的角度去看获取经历911。 这里有消防人员的故事，幸存者讲述，短篇等等。还有一个超大的蓝天聚集图，很有意义。

(Translated by Google) This is my favorite place, it is very suitable for shopping. The food market here is very large, and there are a lot of good foods for sale. Everything is very clean and easy to carry. The architecture of the Time Warner Center is also very modern and beautiful.

(Original)
这是我最喜欢的地方，很适合逛街买东西。这里的食物市场很大，而且里面有很多不错的食品贩售，所有的东西都很干净，携带也很方便。时代华纳中心的建筑也很现代，很漂亮。

(Translated by Google) You don't have to look at all the brilliant buildings inside. I was going to wander around, but in fact, I am satisfied with the gorgeous hall and the fine woodwork on the elevator. There are many interesting buildings around.

(Original)
你不必把里面所有辉煌的建筑都看遍，我本来打算四处逛一下，但是实际上光是欣赏华丽的大厅和电梯上细致的木工就让我心满意足了。周围还有许多很有意思的建筑。

We visited the museum in Feb and caught the Fairytale fashion exhibit and the history of Denim exhibit which were both wonderful! The exhibits change so check out the website before visiting. Best of all...these exhibits are free.

Belvedere Castle is a very nice place in the middle of Central Park, overlooking the water and the Metropolitan Museum of Art. You can walk up the stairs to take a look from the top, where the view is the real highlight.

(Translated by Google) Located at the northern end of the island, medieval art, in a beautiful park. It's great to rely on the subway line.

(Original)
坐落在島的北端,中世紀藝術,在一個漂亮的公園中。靠着地鐵線,很棒。
This is a wonderful park to stroll through, enjoy the views and the vast array of flowers! It is well maintained and a perfect, peaceful spot outside of a hectic city!
Having not been in New York City for a while, I was taken aback by the expanse and beauty of this park along the riverfront. Great addition to Manhattan.
Emotionally draining and educational experience. You need to spend hours here to fully appreciate everything on each floor. (especially the 2nd floor).
We had a lovely dinner with a great view of the lake in Central Park, Reservations are a must and meals are not cheap.

This state park is a hidden gem. I spent 2 days here hiking and camping. I reserved one of the Streamside Walk-in Tent Sites and couldn't have been more pleased. The site was right on the bank of the stream, fell asleep listening to the water flow by. Also, hiked a couple of the trails in the park which were very nice. This park is nearly completely surrounded by the Elk State Forest, if you cross 155 from the campground you can hike the Sizerville Nature Trail up to an overlook of the town of Sizerville. There are also plenty of picnic tables and pavilions as well as a pool near the park office. The staff here is also very friendly. Loved my visit!

Prompton State Park isn't your typical State park, and that's what makes it such a great place. The park surrounds Prompton Lake, a man made lake maintained by the U.S. Army Corp of Engineers. There are over 25 miles of trails, most of which are on the east side of the lake, for hiking and biking. The 290 acre lake is open to fishing and boating (up to 10hp motors) and is great for kayaking. The south end of the park is where you will find the picnic area and 18 hole disc golf course. There is no camping. Keep an eye out for the family of Bald Eagles that live at the park, Osprey, Great Blue Herons, Egrets, Black Bears and Bobcats among many others.

Did a section hike of the Appalachian Trail from Wind Gap to Lehigh Gap, southbound. A lot of diversity of ecosystems along the way, some great views and 1 difficult descent at Lehigh (if you're heading north it's just as tough to ascend) so if you are afraid of heights or have trouble with vertical climbing you might want to skip the Lehigh Gap end.

If you plan on hiking the southern section, from Lehigh Gap to Little Gap bring water. The old zinc mining operation there has made the water unsafe to drink, even filtered.

I've done several overnight trips along the Pinchot Trail System and it is absolutely beautiful. For the most part the north and south loops are fairly flat and well marked. The south loop is a little marshy during the wetter times of the year. The only negative would be trail upkeep. Although the DCNR is working to reroute some of the trail to eliminate forest road hikes, the existing sections could use some clearing. In spots the trail is completely overgrown which is more of an issue in the warmer months due to ticks.

Good mix of hiking trails, with some awesome views to reward yourself with if you follow some of the more "moderately difficult" trails. If you're an experienced hiker the trails out to spots like Boulder Rock at the Southern end or up to North Point will be fun with small sections of rock scrambles and some elevation gains. For not-so-experienced hikers there are some easier spots to access like the old Catskill Mountain House Site, the other trails are still doable you just need to take your time and place yourself.

A beautiful, rare Heath Barren overlooking the Lackawanna Valley. There are several trails that take you through all kinds of terrain and ecosystems from rocky formations to deciduous forest. You can see the different stages of recovering land from past development. Most trails open for hiking and biking unless noted. Be sure to check out Stonehenge Trail for it's rock formations, Blueberry Trail for it's view of the valley and Gene's Trail for the peaceful reservoir.

This is quite a large park with great views and some awesome hiking trails. Even just the ride to the park is great if you are driving on Route 44 from Route 29. Hiked the Red Loop, Yellow Connector and part of the High Peters Kill Trail at the north end and went south to Sam's Point. There are also areas for swimming and picnicking as well as a ton of other trails. I will definitely be returning here to explore more.

Very quite little state park with a couple nice hiking trails, including one that connects to nearby Tobyhanna State Park. There is a picnic area and a swimming beach along the lake. The lake itself if peaceful and a great spot to kayak and/or fish. The park would get 5 stars if the state would invest a little money in the park roads and amenities.

Spent a couple days at the Allegheny Reservoir on a kayak camp trip. Very peaceful, besides the rain, but that just added to the adventure. I stayed at the Morrison Campground and launched from the Elijah Boat Ramp, both were clean and well maintained, I suggest picking up some firewood locally though as there was not much around the camp site.

Camped here for a couple nights while on a road trip to Lake Erie. My camp site was right by the boat launch and it was amazing. The park itself was clean, quiet and well maintained and the park staff was great. If you go here you must check out the spillway... nothing can prepare you for the amount of fish you will see there!

Hickory Run State Park is a beautiful place to visit. Take the time to hike some of the trails and party attention. There are several unique features here including the boulder field and the glacial line that cuts through the park.

There are areas for camping, swimming, picnicking as well as lots of hiking options.

Another stop along my Lake Erie road trip. Foggy weather and a little light rain actually made my visit here more fun, I think. I spent most of my time down near Petroleum Centre checking out the old derricks and the old town. Id didn't get a chance to visit the museum, so I'll have to make back out there some day.

Bear Creek Preserve might be the best kept secret for day hikes in the area. You would never expect to find a place this beautiful right off of busy Route 115. Great trails along Shades Creek out to Bear Creek with a few out croppings for some nice views along the Yellow Loop. Still a lot more to see here.

Loved the campground, was here late November so I pretty much had the place to myself for 2 days. Park staff was awesome, had a great conversation with one of the rangers who gave me a lot of local history and directed me to an awesome hike up Love Run Trail and back down Panther Run Trail.

Some very nice hiking trails within the park, and many trails heading in to the Moshannon State Forest including the 73 mile Quehanna Trail. Hiking up the Trail of the New Giants takes you to an overlook of the park. There's also kayaking/canoeing, a beach, picnic areas and camping.

Hands down one of my favorite places! Miles upon miles of hiking trails, 2 lakes to kayak, fish and swim and lots of camp sites and some very nice CCC era cabins to rent. Don't be surprised to see some wildlife too... Deer, black bear, Bald Eagles, beavers and more.

The reservoir is great for kayaking, the two sides are like 2 different worlds. One surrounded by trees and grassy flatlands, the other surrounded by giant boulders and an old flooded forest. Be prepared for a long day on the water if you hope to see it all.

A state parks built around a bridge with a tragic story, that makes for a great experience. Venture out on the Sky Walk to look down into the valley and see the ruins of what was once the highest and longest railway bridge in the country.

Visited here in September, kayaked and hiked for a few hours. It was very peaceful and a good start to the road trip I was on. I imagine the water can get crowded during busier times but the day I was there I had the place to myself.

Beautiful area. Recently spent a little time at Alder Lake along the Finger Lakes Tail and hiked up to the Balsam Lake Mountain Fire Tower. Both very nice hikes and I didn't see a single other person while out hiking.

Huge area right on the edge of Raystown Lake with swimming and picnicking. They have a pretty reasonably priced concession stand and a huge marina. There are several hiking trails and camping areas as well.
Nice, quiet  little park with a great lake to kayak in and some nice hiking trails surrounding the park. Lots of space for relaxing and picnicking!
A great piece of local history, that as a local, didn't even know existed. The engineering behind this former Aqueduct is quite impressive.
Nice lake, and some nice hiking trails as well. If you are hiking here make sure to find the waterfalls, beautiful spot.
Made this my last stop on a 3 day road trip through the PA Wilds. Amazing views, well worth the drive up the mountain.

Enjoyed staying here in September. The trails are nice but need to put a lot of bug spray. They mosquitoes still didn't care that we had spray on though, they are demons. The campground was nice and you can walk on over to the beach which was nice and not crowded that time of year. Definitely a nice place to get away and camp near the water. Fair warning, you will get sand in your tent, you can try but so did we.

So far the best Japanese garden I have been to outside of Japan. It was great and reminded me a lot of my time I had spent in Kyoto and the gardens there. Nice a big, I rarely had people over my shoulder which was nice. I didn't get the feeling of being rush by people on the path. If I lived in Portland I would get a membership here easily.

This camera museum  is small but has a lot of history inside. They have different models from the 1800's till now (maybe). The actual history behind some of the cameras they have in their collection is pretty cool. Have a few things on sale and the staff are very knowledgeable about the items inside. I have been back.

Great place to go to the beach or check out barrier island wildlife. The horses are all around and I usually see one or two in the distance every time I go. Can walk along the beach for miles. Cold in the winter with the winds but the trails off the beach in the summer can have lots of mosquitoes.

Nice hike down, have done the loop and out and back. Coming up the fire road was nicer to go back on. Less steps. Water wasn't much in October because it was dry but the waterfall back in the winter was full and icy. Trail is easy to follow, done it back in the dark.

Lots to see, can get a little busy in peak season though. Watch out as they will stick their heads in the car and knock cups of food out of your hands and have a lot to vacuum later. The girlfriend had a blast and it was a nice few hours to spend.

You can drive right up to the overlook of the falls. Worth just that but you can also hike to the base. Park also has swimming area and places to relax next to the lake which is nice as well. Park staff were friendly.

Has a great selection of mead. Meads on tap and bottle to try and you can buy mead by the bottle for off sit consumption. Has new stuff added every week ususlly and seasonals. Buce fridnfly and knowledgable staff.

Very cool piece of history. This place has been here for a looong time. Very informative and the tour/talk in the dungeon area. The guide was friendly and presented the information well with some funny parts.

Two adults had a blast here. As cheesy as it is, we had a great time reading the "history" of the Dino's and the war. Definitely worth a stop if you want an off the beaten path experience in the area.
Great park. Camped here as well, bice facilities. Visitor center isnt much but the hikes make up for it. Plenty of waterfalls to see, trails can be tricky when wet and slick so be careful of that.
Big park with a lot to offer. Pickle ball courts, archery range, baseball fields, basketball courts and a dog park. Trails in the woods as well although you cant fish in the pond.
Great collection that is permanant and free. Has a nice restaurant and events through the summer. The grounds are nice as well. Get great exhibits like the Terracotta Warriors.
Nice little park with trails in the woods. Has a boat launch ifnyou want to take your kayak down through pony pasture. Fishing from the bank has been decent
Lots of history here. The building is nuce to tour and the grounds are great for a walk. The visitor center has a lot of info and nice exhibits.
Great place to check out, go when they are doing tours. Really interesting inside and hope it gets to the point where more things happen there.
If you want a quick short hike over some rock scramble, bear fence is a great one right of Skyline Drive. 360 views just about. Worth the stop.
Great art space. All staff are friendly and helpful. I have entrred a few shows and it is a smooth process. Great place to look around too.
Interesting place to go to and dry. Didn't have much people visiting which gave us a lot of time to enjoy the sites with people around.
Great place to check out. Nice long bridge over the river. Can go up the Appalachian trail a ways if you want on the opposite bank.
Very awesome piece of nature. This tree has stood the test of time and might make it for another 400 years. Can get a bit crowded.
Lots of information about the sightings and stories of the area. Lots of merch and the people running were nice and helpful.
Great waterfalls. Beautiful and had it to our selves. The hike down was easy and was overall a great place to check out.
Nice quiet park, camping was nice and the bsthroom/shower house looked new. Lake and the run was nice to walk around.
All the way down and then you have to come right back up. Nice trail and gets you to the water.

Hudson Highlands State Park offers a tremendous number of opportunities for adventures at numerous levels. Breakneck Ridge Trail offers both genuine risks and rewards for those looking for an adrenaline bump. The Cornish Estate has some of the coolest ruins you can find without worrying about getting a tetanus shot afterwards. The Washburn Trail offers a solid ascent with great views, but little challenge in the footing as one climbs. Additionally, Little Stony Point offers a spectacular view with little physical challenge (although I would not say that the trail is navigable by individuals using wheelchairs).

Finally, the volunteers and rangers that run Hudson Highlands State Park do an absolutely fantastic job. Not only are the trails and facilities in excellent condition (and obviously maintained), the individuals working to maintain and improve the park are far more present than in the majority of state parks. This is a group of people who clearly care about their park, and they share what they value superlatively.
likes: Scenic views (Washburn Trail, Little Stony Point)

reviews_attraction.text: The National Park Service runs this small but impressive museum in the one-time residence of Zane Grey. Grey, an avid fisherman, chose the site because it sits at the confluence of two rivers, the Delaware and the Lackawaxen. As an angler, Grey remains of interest and importance, as he still holds numerous world records in sport fishing. As a writer, the Zane Grey house is the site where Grey wrote Riders of the Purple Sage, a best seller that later helped to make major inroads for Grey into the movie industry. These aspects of Grey's life and more are incisively addressed in the excellent tour of this estate.

Come for the hike, and stay for the waterfalls. There is a lot that is offered beyond these attractions (for instance the picnic areas and the playground), and it is free. This is a matter of some consideration in this case. This is the rare example of a state park that could really, genuinely use a few bucks, as its funding is not derived from tax dollars (so few of which are required for the upkeep of parks that benefit all, but I digress). So, by all means, check it out, enjoy your visit, and toss a coin to your bewitcher in this valley of plenty.

For one of the most beautiful, striking swimming holes north of NYC, check out the Peekamoose Blue Hole. The water is absolutely frigid, so be aware of that fact before you come (my most recent trip in mid-July featured water temperatures that I would approximate to be south of 55 degrees). Also, reviewers are quite right about the trash that some unscrupulous individuals will stew about rather than carry out. Visit the Blue Hole for what it offers (highly individual beauty) rather than the shortcomings that some folks will create for it.

There's no two ways about it: Seven Tubs Nature Area is a beautiful place that has been seriously and repeatedly tagged since the beginning of the pandemic. Perhaps the ease of access and the attractiveness of the area have combined in an area especially put upon since the first lockdowns.

This is a fantastic place to visit. If you're new to spending time in nature, please treat the earth well. The Seven Tubs took millions of years to form, and it would be a true tragedy to ruin them within anyone living's lifetime.

The level and volume of programming alone make SteelStacks a place worth checking out. However, both the quality of facilities and the care that has been taken to tell a succinct version of the story of Bethlehem Steel make SteelStacks genuinely unusual. There's always something going on at SteelStacks, oftentimes something that would appeal to a diverse crowd, but it's the stuff that's always going on that makes SteelStacks a great destination.

This is something of a hidden gem in the Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area. In most parks, Hornbeck's Trail would be a highlight in its own right. However, in the superabundance of sights found within the Rec Area, it's easy for an excellent hike like this one to go without the fanfare or notice of some of the more renowned spots. If you enjoy a nice hike, do yourself a favor and check this one out. You'll be happy you did.

The Mount Tammany Red Dot Trail has some of the best views of the Delaware Water Gap from the New Jersey side.  The trail is generally moderate, which is unusual for some of the views that can be found in its handful of miles. This is one of many places in the Water Gap that reminds you why the area was once considered a natural wonder of the world, and another great reminder of the awesome power of water, ice, and time.

Raymondskill Falls is a two-stage waterfall that is the tallest in the state of Pennsylvania.  The upper part is easily accessed from the Raymondskill Falls parking lot. The lower portion is not as easily accessed, and it is unwise to do so during the winter months without proper ice climbing gear, as the path to the lower falls can quickly become completely frozen.

Prompton State Park offers a number of interesting and less common amenities, most especially its disc golf course. The dam offers less common opportunities, including the view of both sides from the top, and fishing on its south side. Add hidden waterfalls and the east and west shore trails to the mix, and you have more than adequate reason to spend  an afternoon.

The degree of care and effort that go into the Pocono Environmental Education Center is immediately obvious. The wide range of activities are matched by the depth of experience that is possible, and the staff are equally knowledgable and kind. Nature and the classroom meet in the PEEC, and they both prove themselves as worth the time to make the trip.

The Reflecting Pool is essentially the center piece of Saratoga Spa State Park. This is probably the most monied state park that I've visited (which is a way of saying that I've never in my life previously thought of a state park as synonymous with obvious, genuine wealth). However, there's many worthwhile options within the park that are free to all.

The Varden Conservation Area is a quiet, well-kept gem. Visitors can expect trails that will be more commonly undisturbed. The area also doubles as a good spot for a light trail run, as little in either portion of the conservation area can be taken as overly technical, yet runners are certainly off paved roads for as long as is desired.

Taughannock Falls is the tallest single-drop waterfall east of the Rockies. Beyond this distinction, the falls are highly accessible (which is not necessarily true of many striking waterfalls), the area is well maintained, and the entire gorge is as peaceful and contemplative of a setting as one could desire.

The trails are well-kept, and the views are outstanding and various. Beyond this, the hike is not nearly as difficult as many of the hikes with equally excellent vistas. This is another example of why the Delaware Water Gap should be on the list of places to visit in the tristate (PA, NY, NJ) area.

The park contains not only the stone bridge, but also several trails and even a nice playground.  My visits have made it seem to me like the park is largely uninhabited at most times on most days, but that could be a function of when I visited (typically, in the morning).

Laurel House Road is one of the easiest ways to reach Kaaterskill Falls. The parking lot gets busy, so you probably want to arrive early. The public porta-potties could use more than a little work, but the positioning of this parking lot could not be much better.

The Neversink Unique Area has a lot to offer, including waterfalls, rivers, and trails. Be sure to check out the available maps in advance, as the trails can be somewhat confusing if you're trying to figure them out in any sort of impromptu fashion.

Tanners Falls is a picturesque spot that sees little traffic. There's not a tremendous amount to do here, but the falls are serene enough to easily pass an hour, while the changing seasons add enough variation to recommend return visits.

There are a lot of amazing views in Slide Mountain. If you're willing to pay the price, the mountain will yield spectacular views equal to the challenge of the ascent. Wear proper shoes, take your time, and enjoy the journey.

Hackers Falls is an excellent place to visit precisely because it is not the attraction that Raymondskill Falls is.  The spot is somewhat secluded, and it's likely that you will be able to enjoy the falls in solitude.

The Hickory Run Boulder Field is a National Natural area, and it will likely be immediately apparent why that's the case. As others point out, mind both your footing and footwear, and your ankles will thank you.
This is a great little state park, the centerpiece of which is Chittenango Falls. The hike to get to the bridge (for the best view of the falls) is well maintained on both sides.
Vernooy Kill Falls is a scenic spot with much to recommend it. It will potentially be too crowded for some, but this can be mitigated by visiting early or late in the day.
Of the TMR trails, this is one of the easier options. Combine that with the payoff view, and you have a worthwhile hike.

Just come to Beavertail SP if you want to experience the best Rhode Island has to offer. The drive through Jamestown is beautiful and the entrance to the park has a nice big sign welcoming you. There is plenty of parking but try to arrive early since it will fill up quickly on a nice day. The actual park is nothing short of spectacular thanks to the expansive panoramic views of the bay as well as the stunning rocky shoreline. You can even go down to the water's edge since there is a small stairway leading from the walkway in front of the lighthouse. From there you will get an amazing view of the lighthouse. It is also notably cooler than the surrounding areas thanks to the consistent sea breeze. We stopped here on our way home from Newport so be sure to check it out if you are in the area. This is a truly breathtaking piece of Rhode Island!

The Delaware Water Gap makes for the ultimate outdoor experience! You can do so many activities including endless amounts of hiking, fishing, rafting and rock climbing. I spent a few hours hiking up Mount Tammany which offered spectacular views of the entire gap including the river below. Make sure to stop here if you are heading to PA or NJ  since I-80 snakes right through the water gap making it extremely easy to notice and access. There is a nice parking lot right off the highway where the trail immediately begins. The terrain is rugged in spots which makes the hike fun and interesting. There are  plenty of spots for capturing beautiful photos as well thanks to the many trickling streams and massive rock formations. You will definitely have a memorable experience here and the scenery is unbeatable even if you are just driving through!

Truly spectacular RC church with some of the most awe inspiring architecture you will ever see. The exterior is traditional yet grand and stately with the two towers and massive dome on top. You just can't miss it from the street. The interior is simply amazing thanks to the beautiful stained glass and prominent arches throughout. Some of the glass is actually from France! The ceiling is a phenomenal work of art with so many intricate details and symmetry all working together to create this splendid architectural masterpiece. Everything flows perfectly making this church one of the greatest in NYC. There is no better place to spend time in God's presence. I highly recommend stopping in if you are passing through the area as you will surely be amazed!

This is a beautiful beach when it is empty, which is a rare occasion. There is a non-resident fee of $10 on weekdays and $20 on weekends for cars. These hours are in effect from 9am-9pm on weekdays and 8am-9pm on weekends. The lot fills up very quickly since people also use it for the nearby cliff walk so be sure to arrive as early as possible. The views are expansive and peaceful. It really smells like the ocean here due to the sticky and salty air. I would recommend stopping by here but don't make it your first priority when visiting Newport. Plenty of other better sights to see, some of which are less expensive.

Such a beautiful church! The first RC church in the state of Rhode Island. JFK even got married here back in 1953 too. The church is a bit dark on the outside but very bright and welcoming once you walk in. The stained glass is colorful and vibrant. They also have a fully restored organ which sounds amazing. The architecture is spectacular and full of intricate details which make this church unique. I recommend to at least stop by if you are in Newport just to see it. I went for Mass during my vacation and everyone there was extremely kind and welcoming.

Amazing place to hike with beautiful cliffs and views. The wide carriage roads are great for walking and biking. The main sites are Awosting Falls and Minnewaska Lake Beach which are beautiful however the carriage roads are a great getaway from all the crowds in these popular locations. Along the way you will come across plenty of species of trees and plants as well as some great views of the Catskills. Lake Awosting is also a great spot to unwind. The park is nestled in one of the most scenic parts of NY state with rugged terrain and plenty of trails.

Montauk SP may just be the most beautiful place on LI. From the lighthouse and beaches to the spectacular views, Montauk makes for the perfect getaway. You can easily see Block Island and the main coast of RI on a clear day while taking in breathtaking panoramic views from the top of the lighthouse. Parking is $8 and admission to the museum is $10 per person; however, it is well worth it if you can go during the off season to beat the crowds. The view from the beach is stunning since the waves are huge on a windy day.  It's definitely worth the trip!

Ocean Drive is what reminds people of how beautiful Rhode Island really is. I visited for the first time this past weekend and the scenery on this drive blew me away! You have the spectacular mansions on one side and the rocky shore on the other. Simply amazing! There are plenty of spots to take photos. One of my favorites was the little rocky cove just past Gooseberry Beach. You have to take this drive if you are visiting Newport so you can fully appreciate how stunning this small state really is.

Fire Island is one of the best places to visit off of LI. It is such a nice retreat from the congestion as it has a very peaceful beach and a wooden walkway leading to the lighthouse. The lighthouse itself is very historic and the climb to the top is definitely worth it. The view is unbeatable and you can see for many miles on a clear day. There is also a museum at the foot of the lighthouse which has a ton of history. A trip to Fire Island makes for one of the best day trips near LI.

The trail and falls itself is truly spectacular however accessing the trailhead is a different story. There is no designated parking lot so you must park on the side of the 2 lane road which winds through the area. You then have to walk along this road which has no shoulder against a stone wall with cars coming around the blind curve. It is quite dangerous but the destination is well worth it if you are cautious and get there safely. Definitely worth checking out!

Such an amazing park in a beautiful location. There is so much history to see here. The visitor's center is great and overlooks the main battlefield with rolling hills in the distance. The Wilkinson trail is great and leads you past Benedict Arnold's boot monument as well. There is also a fantastic section overlooking the Hudson. The cannons really make you feel as if you are still in the late 1700s. I highly recommend it if you are into history and enjoy hiking!

Gorgeous North Shore beach with picturesque views of the bay and surrounding areas. The drive here is quite scenic and direct. This beach is perfect for nice walks and fishing. The boulders lining the middle make for some pretty cool photos too. The beach is very rocky but that is just a unique characteristic of all North Shore beaches. Hobart beach is a great spot to spend a sunny summer afternoon. By far one of the most beautiful beaches on the island!

This waterfall is truly a hidden gem. I went on an early Saturday morning in March and was the only one around. The waterfall is beautiful and offers a great escape where you can only hear the rushing water. It's the perfect place to unwind and get some great pics! Just be aware of the fact that there are only 8 total spots used for both the falls &  Constitution Marsh down the road. Both are well worth the visit!

Bushkill Falls is one of the most exciting places in the Poconos. There are so many amazing wooden walkways and bridges that lead you all over the park to the many spectacular waterfalls and rock formations. There is also a really good fudge kitchen where you can buy homemade fudge and other sweets. It does get quite crowded in the summer but it's definitely worth checking out.

Spectacular Roman Catholic Church in Lower Manhattan with beautiful stained glass and ceiling murals. The exterior is very traditional and not at all indicative of the ornate interior. While this church is not massive like some others, it is one of the most impressive in the area. They even offer Mass in Italian too. I highly recommend stopping in if you are in the vicinity.
likes: Cultural Value: Stained glass, Ceiling murals

reviews_attraction.text: Quiet park with great water views. There is a nice little paved walkway that circles the park. On a clear day you can see out over the bay area to the Jones Beach Monument. There is always a nice sea breeze so it is the perfect place to visit on a warm summer day. They also now have a really nice mini golf course near the entrance which is great.

Steamtown NHS is one of the most interesting places in the Scranton area. This is a great place for enthusiasts as you can take a ride on the locomotive and get an idea of what the steam age was like. The site itself houses a ton of history regarding the railway's past. There are a plethora of locomotives on display inside the museum as well.

Great views and trails! The trail leading to the  overlook of the LI Sound is really cool. They are well marked and clear of brush. The bluffs are amazing and offer unbeatable views of the sound. The park is home to an abundance of wildlife including plenty of deer and birds. It's definitely worth checking out if you are in the area!

Pretty cool museum with an abundance of history pertaining to the local area. The building itself is very historical and the town does hold a lot of history despite it being a popular vacation spot in the summer. It's also conveniently located along the main walk near many other shops and attractions so it's easy to spot.

One of the most elegant suspension bridges on the East Coast! The view from the deck is fantastic and offers an unbeatable view of the Narragansett Bay and surrounding areas such as Jamestown and Newport. There are so many spots to get some great photos of the bridge as well. Simply spectacular!

Large park with tons of activities from golf to basketball and everything in between. It is conveniently located right in the heart of Nassau County near the mall and many restaurants so it is the perfect place to spend a nice afternoon in. There is also a small pond with a walkway around it.

The High Peaks is one of the most exciting regions of NY state. This expansive wilderness has everything one can ask for with plenty of boating, fishing, hiking, biking, snow sports and spectacular views. You can easily spend months exploring all this region has to offer.

The Manhattan Bridge is one of the most architecturally beautiful structures in the NYC area. The view from Washington Street in DUMBO is unbeatable and one of the most picturesque scenes of this bridge. You can also walk or bike over it which is a plus.

Really nicely preserved mansion with very impressive grounds and history. There are tours in which you can see most of the rooms in the house. There are special seasonal events such as the Christmas tree lighting.
Great venue for a multitude of events from hockey games to concerts. Conveniently located in the center of Midtown with easy access from the LIRR and Penn Station.

I love getting to visit this historic site. It certainly worth a visit when in the area. It's one of the oldest houses around, as it predates the American Revolutionary War. The house originally belonged to Phillip Alston, but it was also occupied by Benjamin Williams, who was the governor of North Carolina four times. There are still bullet holes in the walls and above the bed from a skirmish that happened here during the time of the Revolutionary War. While not a direct battle in the Revolutionary War, it did take place during the War. It's a beautiful piece of history that has been wonderfully preserved.

Cape Hatteras is probably the most iconic of the NC Lighthouses. It is well known across NC, the United States, and probably the world. The lighthouse is easily accessible, there is a wonderful gift shop, and there are lots of camping areas and beaches. There is also a very nice trail on site. I would certainly recommend visiting. The best time to visit the lighthouse is in the off season (November through February). While you can't climb during this time, the benefit is that it's not very busy, and you can get great photos.

I love visiting Raven Rock. There are lots of trails at this park, and the views are spectacular. The trails can get quite muddy after a rain, naturally, but they can be muddy for several days as well. The trail to the Overlook is not very difficult, but the trail down to Raven rock can be a bit challenging for some. The park is well-maintained, and there are restrooms, picnic areas, and a visitor center.

The trails here are great, with beautiful views of the river. The trails aren't very difficult to hike, and the park is overall maintained. The trails do get very wet and muddy after rains, so do prepare for that. The river also floods after heavy rains, so some of the trails are not accessible during flooding. There are no restrooms, water, or other facilities on site, so plan accordingly.

The memorial is such a wonderful sight to see. I certainly recommend stopping and checking it out while in the area. It does cost a little bit to get in, but I think it is well worth it. The cost to get in includes touring the museum and touring all the grounds. You cannot drive up to the memorial, but you can get rather close. You can, however walk up a paved path to the memorial.

I love visiting here when I get the chance. Despite our difficult history as a nation, it is still important to learn from it. This place allows such an experience. I love getting to visit the visitors center, as there are some great items for sale, and it offers a bit of history on the battlefield. There is also a very nice walking trail, but it can get muddy at times.

This is a fantastic aquarium. Aquariums will maintain, and the staff is very friendly. I think the prices are very reasonable. The exhibits are really nice, and I would certainly recommend visiting. During the week and in the off-season (September through February) is the best time to visit. It is not very crowded during this time.

I love visiting here. I visit every other month or so, and there's always something exciting to see. They recently opened the lower decks for touring, and it is such an amazing opportunity. The gift shop is also fantastic, with plenty of great finds. My great-grandfather served on a ship very similar to the USS North Carolina.

I love visiting Lumber River State Park. The trails are nice, and the park is well maintained. There is beautiful scenery of the Lumber River, great fishing, and wonderful picnic areas. The river does flood after heavy rains, so do prepare for that. This is one of the best places to camp if you love camping.

This is such a beautiful and lovely place to pray and meditate. It is simply breathtaking, no matter what time of year you visit.
