If you're in the area, I would certainly recommend visiting when they're open. I enjoy coming in the summer and fall, as the winter can be a bit tricky depending on the weather.

I love visiting here and learning about the history. This is one of the battlefields that predate the American Revolution. Some call this the first battle of the American Revolution, but it actually wasn't a part of the American Revolution movement. This was more of a state's rights/melitia movement.

I love getting to visit this national military site. The visitor center is very informative and has a wonderful gift shop. I love being able to drive the trail to see the various points of interest, but the walking trail is fantastic also. It's definitely worth visiting.

I love getting to visit here and learn about the history. It's a nice walk, about a mile. There are beautiful views of the bridge, and there is lots of history to learn from. Despite history being a difficult time in our past, it is important to learn from it.

I love visiting the North Carolina lighthouses. This lighthouse is the only one in North Carolina that is left in the natural brick. The others are painted. It is one of the four northern lighthouses. Is is certainly worth the stop to visit and climb.

I love coming to Oconeechee Mountain. The views from the overlook are breathtaking. The trails are also well maintained, and they are fun to hike. Most of the trails are not for the faint of heart as some of them can be intermediate to strenuous.

The Riverwalk is lovely. There are lots of nice restaurants, ice cream parlors, and shops to peruse along the way there are gorgeous views of the bridges, the battleship, and the waterfront. It's a very pleasant and well maintained walk.

Very nice trail and well maintained. It has beautiful views of the marsh, and it’s easily accessible from the parking lot of the aquarium. Just a tip, the trail contains hills and is not paved/traveled, so it is not handicap accessible.

It's a beautiful park with gorgeous views. The trail is a little over 2 mi all around the lake. There are additional trails that branch off from the main trail. The park is very well maintained, and the trail is very easy to walk.
I love walking at Carvers Creek State Park. The trails are very easy to walk, are well maintained, and there are gorgeous views of the Cypress pond. It's a very convenient and easy park to walk.
I love visiting this park. I enjoy getting to see the old grist mill, and I love that it is being preserved. There are also beautiful views of the Eno River. The old house is beautiful as well.
This is a lovely piece of history. I love getting to visit this museum when I am in New Bern. It is amazing to be able to stand in the place where a staple of American culture was invented.
I love getting to walk on the boardwalk when I'm in Myrtle Beach. there are beautiful views of the ocean, and there are lots of shops and places to eat along the way.
This is one of the few remaining covered bridges in North Carolina. It is a gorgeous bridge with beautiful views of the creek. The walking trail is nice as well.
This is a must see when in the area. It is such a beautiful and amazing place. The best time to visit is summer and fall.
The museum is housed in the Old Saint Paul's Methodist Church. It's definitely worth a visit when in the area.

This over look is a great place for a picnic. Take a blanket down in the field and a book sit a read or just lay back and look at the beautiful sky .         ( maybe even take a nap! )     The view is a little grown up but you can still see the cliffs. If you want more of an Adventure go hike the cliff . The trail is a couple hours long  and a little hard but they are worth it.  I don't recommend that  you take young children on this hike .

This is a great place to take a walk . It's a easy trail . Then you get up to the top  the flat rock  you have a beautiful view of Grandfather Mountain and the valley below and the rolling mountains in the back ground . Simply gorgeous !
Flat Rock is full of blueberry bushes if you come sometime around July and August you can enjoy eating them .
I could stay up here for hours and never get tired of the view and climbing on the rocks .

It's a small little park with a small creek and falls a good place for a picnic . There's not much else to do here . No playground and I wouldn't let my kids in that water . It has a Very Small walking path.
It does have the old Mill and water wheel . That the nicest thing about the park.
People come here a take pictures .

It is a nice place to take the kids . Love the animal's ! We road the wagon , the driver was   hilarious and had a lot of information about the animal's. I would suggest the wagon after that you can take your car in for another look . Bring a picnic lunch and some water & soda  and stay a while .

This is a peaceful trail by the creek, but if you want to make it longer don't stop a the creek keep going up the side of the hill through the cow pasture to the top, it's a good place walk take in the scenery . But please remember that at this point you are on private land and be respectful  .

Nice hike up the side of the Mountains . Not to hard it's about a half mile up . You can't go up in the tower  ( little disappointed ) but I understand people will either vandalize it or do something stupid and get hurt ! Well enjoy the hike .

I love to hike here . On the trail  there are several big boulders that I like to climb up .  After hiking you can sit and rest and watch the cars go by.( probably shouldn't climb them it is dangerous) . It's a great trail to hike .
This is one of my favorite places to ride and to hike . Take some of the dirt roads see were they go . Explore the towns around you . There are some of the most beautiful mountains and views here !
Nice park , they have frisbee golf , walking track , soccer and baseball fields , a play ground for the kids and very clean restrooms . You can have a picnic or go fishing or take your boat out .
I love it here ! There's so many places to go . Trails ever where . Long ,short ,hard , easy  .  You can fish, and camp play in the water have a picnic.  Go to the falls or go to sliding rock.
This is a nice park for people of all ages . They have a play ground for the kids,  a large walking track , a place to walk by the creek and feed the ducks , picnic tables,  frisbee golf .
This is a great place for the kids . There are several different play areas . My grandson likes to play here . You can watch the airplanes coming in to he really liked that .
I like coming up here and taking a nice stroll through the garden.  I like to go on up to the other trail it a short walk maybe a half mile,  it has a nice overlook .
It's so nice here . Take a hike or just sit by the creek and have a picnic , play in the creek, read a book , take a nap . Do all of them spend the whole day here !
My grandson and I went to the park and he loved it . With all the sprinklers and the play ground , and all the kids running around he had a great time .
This is a great place to relax have a picnic by the lake or walk around the lake . If you had rather go for a hike there are lots of good trails here .
It's a very steep trail . But once you get to the top you have a great view. And if you are tough enough you can keep on going over to Table Rock .
I like the rock formation here . Years ago we could climb around and down under the rocks , not sure if you are allowed to now .
This is a beautiful view,  but it also has a nice little trail . You can pick blackberries and apples up on top of the hill .
Great place to relax and enjoy the day.  Camping, hiking, canoeing ,fishing, picnic, let the kids play in the creek .
They have a nice walking track . It's a nice place to bring the kids and the dogs to let them burn off some energy .
I had a great time hiking the trails here . So many places to explore !  I'am looking forward to coming  back .
Great place to walk , jog , bike or just relax read a book , fish , take out a small boat , to walk the dogs.
There is a beautiful view of Table Rock here . It has a nice little trail and picnic tables .
It wasted my time going out there . The place was not very clean . Not much of a geyser .

Cave Ridge has some of the best wines we have tasted from VA wineries!  They have an excellent tasting room, and great views if you want to enjoy a glass or bottle of wine after your tasting.

We were seated at a table with wine club members, and got great service from our tasting server Kelly.  We asked enough really hard questions about the wines that Kelly eventually tracked down Randy the owner and winemaker.  Randy treated us to some wine club only selections which were also excellent, and answered all of our questions.

We got back to Cave Ridge in June 2017:
Cave Ridge has some of the best wines we have tasted from VA wineries!  They have an excellent tasting room, and great views if you want to enjoy a glass or bottle of wine after your tasting.

I did the standard tasting and an additional Cabernet Sauvignon, and Danielle did the reserve tasting. Our wine server was pretty knowledgeable, but we asked enough really hard questions about the wines that she tracked down Randy the owner and winemaker. The Chambourcin was aged in medium plus plus barrels and combined with the flavors produced by the vineyard created the smokiest wine I have every tasted, and so good that I had to buy some for later!

We stopped here because we knew they served lunch, and they had wine and food pairings. We stopped by on a Saturday with great weather, and the staff seemed at bit overwhelmed. However, all the staff was very friendly including the owner Bandit was going around greeting everyone.

They had a few options for tasting, and I chose flight #2 and Danielle chose flight #3.  Basically we ended up tasting one white, one rose and 6 reds and one port style with the combination of both flights.  We did have a brand new server to host our wine tastings, she was energetic and pleasant.  When we asked questions she could not answer, she asked co-workers and got the answers.  We each ordered a glass to have with our butter chicken for lunch.  At the conclusion of our meal, we shared one wine and chocolate pairing which allowed us to taste some of the member only wines. This was the highlight of the visit! If you like red wine, I would just select this tasting.

Great wines and a great view!

They have a really nice selection of wines, and they let you taste any seven for $2.  That makes it really nice because I got to try almost all of their red wines.  $15 for a bottle of wine and two tastings was a great bargain!

Our wine server did not have a lot of details about the grapes, and how the wines were aged, but we could reach the google which answered most of our questions.  For example, the server thought Vincenzo was Vincent grapes (versus St. Vincent), and the google found that Vincent is a clone from a Lomanto and Seneca clone and Chelois.

The view from the tasting room was awesome.  We need to get back there when we have more time to grab a cheese and cracker plate and enjoy a glass or two of wine.

We stopped by Quattro Goombas fairly late in the day, and the parking lot was completely packed. We were pretty lucky that when we got to their tasting room there was no wait at all. Our wine server was the brother of their new winemaker, and he was very knowledgeable about their wines. Quattro Goombas buys grapes from various vineyards in VA, and from around the world. They were out of various Perfect Truffles to have a complete wine and truffle pairing, but we bought a few to match up with their Petit Verdot and then found out they were out of that wine! However, the Lavender Truffles were still really good with the Bourbon Barrel Aged Tradizione served as a substitute. A bottle of that wine even followed us home.
dislikes: Incomplete wine and truffle pairing options

reviews_attraction.text:
Herrera has an excellent pair of tasting rooms, but we were there on a Friday and only one was open and it was full. One of the servers gave us a tasting at a table in the tasting room after she finished the tastings at the bar.

The wines were very good, and our server was very knowledgeable about the wines. We decided to stay for dinner, and my wife and I had the Filet Oscar which was excellent, and the Chocolate Raspberry Devil's Cake for dessert was also excellent. The bottle of Solera that we had with dinner was a perfect match.

Our two tastings, the bottle of wine, and dinner cost us $130.  This was a great deal given the quality of food and service we received.

A new vineyard with the tasting room added in November 2016. The tasting room is surrounded by the vineyard providing a great view from several windows. The vineyard has been producing wines for several years, we tasted their 2011 Clio which is a Bourdeaux blend. This is noteworthy because most wineries will not taste wines with this much aging! The Clio was a great blend with too much french oak for my palate, but Danielle loved it. Wine glasses were included in our tasting fee.

This Vineyard is worth a visit, and I expect that over the next few years when their new vineyard plantings mature that they will be producing a great variety of good wines.

Serenity Vineyards has a nice outside view from picnic tables in the yard. The tasting room is also their winery, and they had the large overhead door open to keep the temperature moderate. They have an unfinished tasting bar where you can leave a message and the old tasting bars are displayed in the winery. They have a much larger selection of reds, and we got to taste some vertical tastings (same wine different year) in addition to the normal horizontal tastings (same year different wines & blends). We had a very knowledgable tasting room staff discuss the different year's growing weather, and details on the wine making at Serenity.

We showed up when the painting and wine event was just about to start, and everyone involved was finishing their orders. They had about 40 people there for the painting and wine! Once the mad rush for the wine subsided, we got an excellent tasting from the owner of the winery. We love that because he could answer any questions we had, and we also got some of the history surrounding the winery. We had perfect weather for the open air wine bar in an old barn, we did not go upstairs to the air conditioned wine bar. A first for us was that they used a barrel with Heavy Toast, and it produced a very nice wine.

Damiani had ten dry reds, so I actually could not taste them all (great reason to go back). Dani chose a mixture of whites and reds. The chocolatier was also on site so we got a reduced price set of chocolates to use for our tasting. There were some very unique chocolate flavors which is worth tasting separate from the wine. Our wine server was very engaging and knowledgeable, and we also had an excellent view of the lake during our tasting. Very nice tasting room, deck, and lawn with Adirondack chairs to enjoy a glass after your tasting.

This is still very new as the tasting room is currently in the owner's basement.  They had a blended white in 2014 and 2015.  They had a bordeaux style blend in 2014 and 2015.  It is always a nice treat when we get to do a vertical tasting.  They had an incentive where you get one tasting free if you purchase two bottles of wine - so we left there with a bottle of Cabernet Franc, a bottle of blackberry merlot "Pazzo", and two wine glasses.  While we were there, a local musician was playing a great mix of easy listening rock classics.

I tasted their five red wines; including the rare Pinot Meunier. Dani had a mix of whites and reds. Based on other reviews we went here when we needed a lunch break, and it was an excellent decision.  I went with the Cabernet Franc and Dani choose the Gewurztraminer for lunch. The Tapas were excellent and went with the glasses of wine we chose after our tasting. Weather was great so we tasted outside on the deck with a great view. They had a huge wedding area set up on the vineyard too, and it looked like a great spot for a wedding.

We tasted four white wines, two apple wines, and three reds. The white wines were all done at 2% residual sugar which is unique tasting. I like my whites really sweet, so it was nice to try the different varietals at 2%. The Cabernet Franc got too much rain before harvest so it was a very light version of the varietal. The Caroline Red was blended 50/50, but the Chambourcin was the predominate flavor. They have a "White Chambourcin" produced by removing the skins immediately which was worth the trip all by itself.

We tasted two dry whites, two dry reds, then a sweet white and a sweet "sunset wine" made with Muscat Hamburg for a hint of red. The Lake Side White was 3.5% residual sugar and Lake Side Sunset was 4.5% residual sugar. They were made for sitting at Lake Anna on a hot summer day. They were light on dry reds, with several still in the barrel. They had also run out of their Montmorency Cherry juice, so they were out of their Concerto wine which contains 10% of the juice.

One of the owners, Clyde, met us on our way into the tasting room and gave us some good information about the vineyard before we even got started on our tasting. They have really good wine and a very nice tasting room. We bought two bottles of Cynthiana (Norton) because they had done such a great job with this native grape. We had two tastings, and took home two stemless wine glasses and two bottles of wine for $39. Semper Fi

Mount Nittany is currently unable to do tastings, and you must buy food to order wine. We ended up ordering two flights of wine to try all of their dry reds and a few other wines too. We liked several of their dry reds, but bought a bottle of the 2018 Vermelho Port Style wine which was very smooth. They have a lot of nice outdoor seating areas where you can enjoy the wine if the weather is nice, and some covered seating too.

Fabbioli Cellars does a food pairing with their wine tasting which we really love! Their tasting does have several fruit based wines, and we would have enjoyed more of their reds. However, we solved that problem by ordering a flight of red wines after our tasting. They have an adult only area for the wine tastings, and outdoor seating where we took our red flight to enjoy the views of their vineyard.

Dani did the wine tasting of wines by Maison Shaps from Meursault France - 1 white, 2 reds.  Dan did the tastings from Michael Shaps from Virgina - 3 whites, 3 reds.  This was a small tasting room with no view. Dan found the wines unique, unusual in blend; worthwhile to taste, yet not our palate for purchase.  There is a small area for enjoying a glass outside with a little view of the vineyard.

They have a very nice tasting room that was built in an old stable on the original farm.  Our server was very knowledgeable about the original farm and transition to vineyard at Grassy Creek.  Their wines were very good, and we loved the story about how they tracked down a milk bottle for some of their wines.

We had two tastings and purchased a bottle of wine in a milk bottle for $27.

The Loving Cup makes organic wine, and their selection is a bit limited with their red wines all based on Marquette and/or Corot Noir. We tasted one white wine, three red wines, an apple wine (not cider), and two Sangria’s. The wines are good, and there is a fantastic view of the vineyard from the tasting room and porch area. Mom says to give them an extra star for being organic.

They have a lot of options for tasting their wines, and we choose to just buy a Red Wine Flight with a glass of Meritage so we could taste all their dry reds. They have very good wines with an excellent tasting room. There was live music in the event room off of the tasting room so we grabbed a table in the tasting room to listen in. The flight and glass of wine was $19.

We tasted 7 Estate Wines (grapes grown at the vineyard); 3 whites and 4 reds. We got to taste their Thomas Great red blend as a bonus, because they had an open bottle. The wines were good, but nothing that I loved. The tasting room is small, but they have an outdoor area that has a great view of their vineyard.

Wisteria is a very small vineyard on a working farm, and the tasting room is in an older farm house. They served eight wines, but the Merlot was made from grapes from another Virginia vineyard. After our wine tasting, we enjoyed a glass of their blended Adonis wine  under a trellis of grape vines.

Bocce is on tap with regulation fields on the lawn near the grapes!  Live music here too.
Their tasting menu included three whites, a rose, three reds and we paid for the tasting of Nebbiolo.   We liked their Merlot enough to take home a bottle, and the tasting includes a wine glass.

Loved their wine and tasting room.  We had a knowledgeable server who got the answers to all the tough questions we asked. They were running out of some of our favorite dry reds, but we still walked away with several reasonably priced bottles of wine.

The view from the parking lot was awesome.  Unfortunately the tasting room is behind the restaurant, so you don't get to enjoy the view during your wine tasting.

The wines were okay, but only a few dry red wines which are my favorite.

Honestly, I'd classify Raleigh's bike trails as the city's leading attraction, and Anderson Point Park is the starting point for many of its trails. From here you can bike to Clayton, North Hills, NC State, and so many other places. The prime trails are along the Neuse river. Lots of well maintained asphalt paved paths, quaint bridges, and ample shade, and teaming wildlife. The park itself is relatively large, with lots of families using it for picnics, frisbee, and general fun. There's a cottage that might be rented out. There are two parking lots, one just before the bridge to the park, and one after. Although the lots can can fill quickly, you never feel crowded on the bike trails. Thanks you to the Raleigh city fathers that planned and paid for the park and bike trails. Your foresight is appreciated
likes: Facilities & Services: Well-maintained paths, ample parking

reviews_attraction.text: The Behind the Scenes tour is offered periodically and I would highly recommend. It's offered by the NC Dept of Natural and Cultural Resources. The tour guide was very enthusiastic, knowledgeable, and passionate about the tour which lends to a more entertaining and interesting experience. You do have to climb a lot of steps so be prepared with good shoes. The tour guide was very accommodating and was sure to let us know in advance of tight spaces and narrow climbs so you could opt out at parts of the tour. We had been on a regular tour some many years ago and this was by far so much better. We also had a good group of like minded history oriented people so that made it even better. We finished up with light snacks on the second floor portico overlooking the grounds.

In the area where we live there is nothing like Frankie's. We live in our local bubble most of the time and rarely go to that side of town. We've definitely missed something. Frankie's arcade area is impressive! Variety is the word. Outside there are amusement style rides and three eighteen hole mini-golf courses. We had plans for dinner so we didn't eat there but will another time. Frankie's works on a card system. You choose how much credit you want on a card to use the games and entertainment. I wish we had something that all ages can enjoy closer to where we live. But now that we've been to Frankie's, we are planning our next trip.

The main exhibits now are by Christina Weisner. One focuses on the Ries Meteorite Impact Crater in Germany, 15 miles across and containing the entire city of Nordlingen, built before anyone understood that the great depression or bowl that nestles the city is actually a 14-million-year-old impact crater. Weisner also has an imaginative assembly of glass spheres, originally used to house underwater seismometers. These are connected to the United States Geologic Service's earthquake reporting website so that the spheres ring each time there is an earthquake anywhere on planet earth! Very interesting.
likes: Attraction Type: Art and science fusion

reviews_attraction.text: I took the Sunday 2pm tour of the backstage view of the Mill. Very informative. It starts with a video presentation and then a volunteer guide takes you on to various spots at the park, and then you head off to the actual working Mill where they grind the corn, to make corn meal. The guides are not just some kid that needs a summer job, these are adults who are passionate about what they are speaking about and showing, and the quality of what they are showing you and telling you comes through. If you have not visited here, you are missing a real treat.

I love the Greenway one of the best investments the City of Raleigh ever made. The Neuse River Trail is 27.6 miles of paved trail that runs from the Falls of the Neuse to close to Clayton. I love to ride my bike on it but it is suitable for walks and jogging as well. There are multiple locations for launching kayaks and canoes. I often see deer, hawks, owls and rabbits by the dozen. I even saw a coyote one evening on the Walnut Creek branch of the Greenway. If you are in Raleigh you should check it out.

My office took 15 of our employees to do three escape rooms here and all three groups raved about how much fun they had. We did the dark room, the experiment, and Sherlock. A group of five of us also previously did the heist and everyone enjoyed that as well! The owner/manager of Room 5280 is so nice and happy to help! We will likely go back not only as an office, but individually as well! I was asked by many of the people who participated for the details of how I booked the rooms for us.

Spent a few hours here on a Saturday morning while passing through town. The museum is very well done and FREE! I couldn’t believe it! Kids explored whales and an under the sea simulator. They also spent quite a bit of time exploring the science lab, conducting experiments and testing hypothesis. The dinosaur exhibit is impressive as well. We sat in an animal encounter class and had lunch at the cafe before leaving. So much to see and do, it could easily be a multi day experience.

This visit was a planned stop. I had read a bit about the Joel Lane Museum and wanted to know more. We went on a 45-60 minute tour of the house and small grounds surrounding, guided by the museum director. He was very informative and gracious and obviously had a true interest in sharing what is known about Joel Lane and his family. We enjoyed this tour immensely and would recommend it to anyone with an interest in history and culture who is traveling in the Raleigh area.

I have used this facility for many years when a significant part of the trail system was gravel. Now the trail system continues around the entire lake/pond. As a marathon runner (46 completed) I used this as my starting point for my long training runs. A runner or cyclist can easily log 12, 15, 18, 20+ mile training ventures. The Greenway system is a great un-tapped resource. It should be utilized before ever considering to use the Raleigh Bike Path system.

I used to take my kids here all the time. Prices are reasonable - it's not like Disney World where you pay $400 to get in the gates. Per person. It has all the amenities you've read about (golf, go-carts, batting cage, laser tag, etc). Great place to take a ton of kids. Dining options are perfect for kids (think Chucky Cheese without the noise machines). Now that my kids are older I remember how great this place is. Still go back for minature golf.

On the outskirts of Raleigh, this is a small hidden gem to get away and take a walk in nature. Middle of the week could have few people so you can really enjoy nature. The water level was low and there was some construction still going on, but it didn't detract from the beauty of the place.  We went here on a trip and had a chance to canoe on the lake so much wildlife the staff was very friendly and made the trip worthwhile

We took our 3 children, along with our dog to this fabulous park on a beautiful Saturday. We practically had the park to ourselves, definitely wasn't their busy season! All three of our kids loved the history and the goats were a huge hit! The walking trail was fun and there was a nice picnic area to enjoy our lunch. We definitely give this park 5 stars and plan to bring visitors to check this out. Enjoy!

Moore Square is a regular destination for us, with and without 'out-of-town' visitors. We cruise ArtSpace, dine and listen to music in TirNaNog, enjoy various events (especially FirstFriday), shop/cafe in the historic cobbled streets of City Market, enjoy sidewalk music and park events, and more. This is a gem just a couple blocks from Raleigh's beautiful downtown and Fayetteville street.

We recently visited this historic house & park. Even though the day was hot & humid, the house & structures are cool & comfortable. Our guide, Marissa, was superb! She had a large group (our seniors as well as a family with small children, etc) and she made the presentation relatable to all, interesting, and fun. She really seems to enjoy what she does and it shows. She made history fun!

Must see this five acre sunflower field if you visit Raleigh Durham in the Summer. There is a Saturday festival in mid July. Great photo opps! Wear closed toe shoes and hat. Watch for bees; they were on the flowers, not flying around. The flowers were beautiful and it was a fun stop to take pictures. Not a park. Grateful the city is using the space in an unique, beautiful green way!

The impressive Bell Tower and lovely Harden Family Memorial Gardens, adjacent to the North Carolina State Capitol, Raleigh, make a fine place to rest and meditate on life's blessings and challenges. Being right next to the First Presbyterian Church makes the spot convenient for worshipers, as well. Very nice tower, represents the university. Lights up red when NC State win a game.

We just moved to this area and discovered this park in driving down Aviation Parkway. The park has walking trails, a huge lake with rental boats (pedal, canoe, kayak), and picnic areas. You can also bring your own boat to launch. There is a small playground and large covered areas for large parties. The area was clean and inviting. We can't wait to come back and bring our kayaks.

Visited the lake 5 times during July and August for beach/ swimming. $7 fee per car per day. Clean beach, sand at bottom of water. Clean water. Restrooms/ changing rooms clean. Able to find shade to sit in . Picnic tables and charcoal grills available for use. View is beautiful. Was never crowded. Playground, volleyball court. Beach sloped doen gently, swimming area roped off.

I dropped my Duke student off after coffee and decided to “waste” an hour walking through Duke Gardens. I could have spent a day just strolling through and enjoying the peace. It is laid out so nicely. There are so many varieties of plants. I will come back. Dogs, kids, students, walkers, joggers, meditators, sleepers. There are great sounds, bridges and overlooks.

This place is mostly used as an entry point to the Greenway, and its great for that, but it has a nice little charm all its own that if you walk the fields or even around them on the path you have a far quieter experience and much less hectic than sharing the path with all the bikes, dogs and runners. I really like this place and it is super convenient.

Visited over the Labor Day Holiday and we all had a blast. My kids had so much fun. I couldn't get my son away from the Lego area and my daughter loved the Crafting area. We were with my sister-in-law and 10 month old niece and even they had a blast. It was so hot when we went so we didn't go outside and do the outdoor activities. I do highly recommend.

Recently redone, enlarged and made safer, there was playground equipment that was innovative and different than any I have seen before. Soft surfaces protect little knees. I was there with my family and all had a great time. I saw smaller kids also enjoying the facilities. There was ample parking when we were there despite it being a school holiday.

We came here on a recommendation and it was Amazing! Lots of activities, even an Interactive section where you can do experiments! Great exhibitions and area where you can watch the Palientoligists work, also has screens to watch presentations. The Dinosaur exhibits are fantastic and on an enormous scale, this place is a Must if you are in the area.

A great place/deck to watch airplanes take off and land. Most planes you see will be the regional jets operated by American, Delta, and United. The only B777 wide-body operator is the American Airlines that's scheduled for 19:25hrs to Heathrow. There are two runways, of which only RW23R one can be seen from the deck.

11 years in Houston and my first time visiting the Space Center! Who knows why I left it so long. Definitely worth the time and money; be prepared as you'll stand in lines (outside, though there are large fans and it's undercover) for quite a while if you decide to go via tram to the Orion facility or the astronaut training facility. Mornings seemed busier than the afternoons, at least on the day I went (a Sunday - possibly not recommended as nothing was happening in astronaut training when we went). The main exhibits are fun and interesting and there's a lot for kids to do. The food court is decent though of course massively overpriced.
For me, the highlight by far was the restored Historical Mission Control. This has a timed entrance, and you'll need a ticket (though it's free with the cost of admission) so make sure you organise that first up if you're interested. We arrived shortly after 11:30am and even then the first available time was 2:30pm. So plan ahead.
The mission control experience is also reached by tram, and you wait outdoors for this too, though it's shorter because you have your ticket. And the experience is ACES - though be aware you have to climb three flights of stairs (there's a small lift but it only fits 6 people). You sit in the restored viewing area and there's a short presentation made up of archival footage and other materials. And you get to watch the screens in mission control showing what they actually showed during the moon landings. It was fabulous and my highlight of the day for sure. And crazy to realise how rudimentary their tech was! I'm sure every audience member had more technology in their pocket than mission control had in the entire room back then.
Anyway, go, even if it's just for this. You'll feel like you're part of history :)

UPDATE 2018: The gift shop has moved back from the information center at the top of the hill and is now once again in the little gate house just past the bridge. They'll let you visit the shop without paying admission to the house and gardens, if you want.
Absolutely love this place. The collections are wonderful and worth paying for, but they also have 'family days' a few times a year when you can go for free. We've been on July 4 when they had a fife and drum band and someone in costume reading the Declaration of Independence; on election weekend when they were running a colonial-style election; we've seen some of the 'hidden sides' of furniture, when they had drawers pulled out and certain items turned over to show labels and more, and we've been on special days like at Christmastime for the candlelight tours and on Mothers' Day, when it was free for mothers. Oh, and one excellent visit had every room done up for a different holiday - there was Easter, Christmas and Thanksgiving, but also celebrations like christenings, weddings, Valentine's Day, and more. EVERY visit is different and every one is enjoyable. And in recent years with the new gift shop it just gives me an excuse to stay longer!

I've wanted to visit for ages and finally made it! A gorgeous old stately home in Galveston which is well worth a visit. The enormous gift shop in the basement is fun to browse and the room with the displays on wild weather - the focus is on the big storm of 1900 and on Hurricane Ike in 2008 - also very interesting. Maybe of most interest to me in homes like this is the old "technology" - if you can even call it that - old water heaters and the bell system and the dumb waiter and stuff like that. I wish there was more still extant.
The handset tour guides are a good idea but with even a few people in the  same general area it's like walking around with a flock of ducks. It would be great if these could default to personal level, not speaker.
Also, adult price is now $14 per person (as of end 2019). Some old info is out there on the web so be ready with updated info.

I learned of this place on Atlas Obscura (side tip: ALWAYS check Atlas Obscura when you visit a new town or city! there will almost always be something cool they tell you about, often more than one thing). And it's absolutely gorgeous. You can tell the care that's gone into the design (it commemorates a beloved son after his untimely death) and there are beautiful personal touches all over the park, from his handwriting on the benches to the "Wednesday's child" installation. I was expecting some fountains, from previous descriptions, but didn't see any, and they would have been a lovely addition on such a burning hot day. But this is a green, cool(ish) oasis in the middle of a hot city; definitely take the time to visit.

Really lovely place with friendly staff and a laid-back, show-yourself-around kind of vibe. Having the handsets is good (and it's great that they talk into your ear like a phone rather than being on speaker like the handsets at the Bishop's Palace), but it would have been great to have just a little more signage around. If you didn't want to listen to the entire piece on every number, you couldn't easily pick and choose what to find out, the way you can with an info board. Nice gift shop and just a fun experience all round.
The price per adult was $12 (many websites for Galveston have outdated info, it seems) and we understand prices will go up in 2020, so plan accordingly.

How can you give the Riverwalk anything less than 5 stars?! This is an absolute gem of a space, thanks to those stalwart ladies back when it was being debated, deciding that this needed to be a THING, goldangit, and seeing it through to completion. The walk itself is just gorgeous, with so much variation as you meander along - stepping stones and waterfalls and bridges back and forth and so much to see. It's lovely to be below street level and in the shade by the water. And there are some fab businesses that line the route so there's always somewhere to stop and rest and have a margarita or coffee or whatever takes your fancy. Love it; wish I could visit every weekend!
likes: Facilities & Services: Rest areas, dining options
On-site Activities: Variety of views, relaxing

reviews_attraction.text: Y'know, I pay to be a member of the MFAH, and the Contemporary Arts Museum is always free, but I think I might sneakingly like the CAM better. I never know what I'm going to get when I visit - I have only once or twice visited intentionally for a specific exhibition - but I don't ever feel like my time is wasted. Some of the things I think about for years afterward. And, in addition to the exhibition space, they have one of the best little museum shops ever, crammed in under the stairs. No, you can't waste your time if you visit the CAM - there'll be SOMETHING to enjoy, and odds are it will be everything.

I love visiting the missions and this is one of the most interesting. The complex is large and there's a lot to see; the information centers are good without being obtrusive. The church is a highlight - it's so peaceful and beautiful and they often have music playing which makes the experience even more reverent.
Of course, the history here is complex, with the native people being taken over by European influences, and it's important to keep in mind that there was violence and a lot of negative activity at the same time these beautiful spaces were being built. It can be hard to reconcile the two.

Gorgeous community space with all sorts of amenities. Great facilities including bathrooms, stage area, TONS of portable seating - including rocking chairs!! - and a fabulous play area for kids. We went for the Nowruz festival (Persian new year) and it worked well for an event of that kind, with lots of space for booths as well as lots of seating.
Parking is tight; not much on the street so you can use the structure attached to the nearby hotel. First 30 min free then $1 per half-hour; not the worst rate but even so, something to know before you get there.

I love that so much has been made of relatively little. This is just a little slice of a park - really just the space between two buildings - but it's delightful. Green and lush and quiet and there's the constant sound of splashing water from the two fountains (well, they're more like pumps than fountains, but they're more decorative now than useful). Interesting to read so much about the town's history. I only wish idiots didn't have to write their names on every damn thing; it spoils the look of things to have everything scratched up.

This was listed as open for tours on a (very old) website so when we fronted up we were sorry that that is no longer the case. There's a tourist information office in the building to the right and the staff were friendly and helpful, including giving us a brochure with a $1 discount to entry of the Bishops' Palace and some other local tips. It would have been nice to see the house though. We peeked through the windows and it was all set up for an event - a wedding by the looks of it - so that seems to be the main use these days.

I've only been here twice, but really valued it both times and am now on their mailing list so should get there more often. There's just one large space - sometimes partitioned up, other times not - so there's just one exhibition at a time. The things they put on are thoughtful, provocative, interesting. Sometimes unsettling, as with the exhibition we saw today on Torture. Free admission, some parking out the front; the people working there are helpful and friendly and will answer any questions you have. Worth a look :)

REALLY interesting concept and fabulous actualisation. I love that this place exists! The only disappointment was that we weren't able to get into the tenement apartments themselves - even though we were booking two days ahead, all the tours to those rooms were sold out. We did the Shop Life tour instead and enjoyed it very much, but it wasn't quite what I had wanted to see. However, everything else was good - the introductory film and the wonderful bookshop were also highlights.

There's always something going on at Discovery Green. Of course, parking can be an absolute bear, so plan ahead (and maybe even take the bus!) but you'll enjoy your visit. During the winter there's skating and Discovery Green Flea by Night, and there's a regular schedule of other fun events, movies, activities, and more. A great asset to Houston. There are some places to eat right there and more in close walking distance, so you can make an evening of it.

I just missed the annual bowl event - I don't know why I never hear about it until it's too late - and so when I went they were packing up and a whole large room was out of commission. That meant what was there was pretty limited. A couple of artists had their studios open but otherwise the main display was jewelry, which was fun, but our visit probably only lasted around 20 min. However, I'll go back; I'm sure there will be something new to like soon!

OK, this is NOT TO BE MISSED, Y'ALL. Houston landmark of weird and wonderful creativity. We went with kids which was the way to do it; they absolutely loved exploring and discovering all the parts of it. Their pleasure was half of mine but it's enjoyable in it's own right too. Definitely check out Smither Park, too, right next door, which is free - the mosaics are beautiful and the swings a ton of fun. "Time for oranges!"

Loved our visit here, on a cold and grey spring morning (plus we went in the side entrance by accident so it felt like an adventure). For a while we were the only visitors and it was wonderful to explore the space with no one else around. Really beautiful garden and big enough to find new elements around corners and really spend some time. Worth the small entrance fee.

It was our first time at this venue; we went as guests to the Ramadan Iftar dinner held by the Bay Area Islamic Center. It was a wonderful event and the venue was great. Lots of space, good amenities, and plenty of parking. They had a little trouble with the sound system throughout the evening but not sure if that was the venue or operator inexperience :)

This is a beautiful building and worth a visit if you can. Free tours take place throughout the day and every guide will tell you something a bit different. Parts of the building are still in regular use while others have been re-created to evoke a particular historical period. I wouldn't spend hours here but it's worth a visit, for sure.

I've just loved my visits to Victoria. This is a fabulous big small town and the square is definitely the heart of everything. Parking around the edge, a lovely grandstand (one visit was near Christmas and there was a choir in there singing), and the Trail of 6 Flags in one corner, along with a war memorial. I'd encourage you to visit!
likes: Attraction Type: Small town atmosphere, Central square

reviews_attraction.text: Not the most exciting thing you'll do in Austin, but it's free, interesting, and air conditioned, so why not?! Check out the gift shop and tiny O Henry museum (a single room, but still well done) downstairs, and go upstairs for an interactive kids' area and some more information about how white people settled in Texas.

What a great asset for the city of Houston. The whole park is great but of course holds gems like Miller Outdoor Theater and the always-gorgeous Japanese Garden. Parking can be awful, but you expect that, and sometimes you get lucky. Even the hottest days of summer can be pleasant walking under the trees here.

We had a lovely visit here, for the Islamic Arts Festival. Really great exhibition space and lovely grounds as well; everything was well laid out and signposted so you knew where you were and what you were doing. Friendly, welcoming people and just a great experience all round.

Just stunning. Definitely worth the short drive out from town. Beautifully preserved with a lot of spaces that that you can access and look at, and the architecture is glorious. I loved that there is still some art visible on the walls inside and the profile is just iconic.

I love it here. The building is interesting but I just love the garden. It's rarely crowded and you can sit out in the quiet under the trees and listen to the fountains. It's not expensive to go to the museum so I visit most times I'm in San Antonio.

The battleship contained a wealth of history and personal narratives. We watched the 15 minute video and browsed through the small indoor exhibits before boarding the ship. There were so many nooks and crannies to explore on the upper and lower decks. Along with photo ops. I most appreciated the "crew memories" placards with quotes and stories from sailors. Having toured the USS Wisonsin in Norfolk and Yorktown in Charleston, I was prepared for the dozens of ladders and steep stairs, as well as enclosed spaces. There were numerous fans to help cool off in lower decks

This drive requires navigation since there are so many turns to get there! There's no parking lot so you'll have to be comfortable parking along the road. It was very secluded when we went early in the morning. We attempted the 10 min easy blue trail, but turned around because it was so overgrown and hard to see with my 5 year olds. I regret not getting to see alternative views, but the main view is quite breathtaking. This is a great spot for people who want a scenic view without a hike. And you can't beat free.

This is a hidden gem for any naturalist. There's an emphasis on taxidermied animals and American Indians. There are some exhibits that have been closed for renovation for over a year, so there is less to see. Planetarium prices are NOT included in regular admission or even membership. The outdoor area is free to the public and has nice trails and historic structures along the way. Few things are interactive so there's not a lot for younger kids, with the exception of the pirate ship and a small puppet area.

The park is nice. $5 for weekday parking for residents. (I've never been asked to show a license or proof of residency.) The water is very shallow, making it perfect for young kids but frustrating for anyone wanting to actually swim. If swimming with fish creeps you out, this is not the place for you. There is such a thick bed of rocks, it's painful to walk. Water shoes are recommended. No grilling or alcohol allowed,  but coolers and umbrellas are.
dislikes: Painful to walk (thick bed of rocks)

reviews_attraction.text: Our family loves Zootastic! The $13 feeding pass provides multiple opportunities to feed the giraffes and tigers, as well as all animals during the wagon ride. We've been going to this unique zoo for 6 years and the animals are always eager but not aggressive. Staff are friendly and informative. There are so many opportunities to touch animals that you'd likely never be near at other zoos. We've always had the best time at Zootastic

We live on Charlotte but go here at least once a year and spend the day. We spent 6 hours leisurely exploring and still did not see everything. Main features of the outdoor areas include treehouses, far animals, butterfly garden, dinosaur trail, mist area, and boardwalk to live animals. Inside are so many interactive exhibits, from origami to create your own movie, blocks, and dance areas. There is so much to enjoy!!

This is a great space with a lot of outdoor walking. Some of the animal enclosures are fairly small, which is good for viewers but questionable for animals. I really enjoyed the multiple play areas for children, with a variety of creative play spaces and natural materials. We happened to visit on the day they were celebrating twin goats' birthday. The staff was so friendly, knowledgeable, and passionate.

This is a gorgeous park with well maintained trails and clean restroom facilities. The park ranger at the visitor's center was very friendly and knowledgeable. He highlighted a recommended trail for us and gave us the map. The waterfalls and fall foliage were stunning. There were multiple picnic tables near the campsites and restrooms that allowed us to wash up and enjoy a spot for lunch.

Our family absolutely loves this library. There is something for kids of all ages, birth to 17. They have a variety of programs, story time, book clubs, etc. The architecture is inviting and beautiful. Almost everything is interactive and educational. It's also an excellent location in the heart of uptown with ample green space, restaurants, museums, and train stop nearby.

I was skeptical that the drive would lead us to the waterfall, but the gravel road leads to a small lot at the trailhead. This is more a nature walk than a hike, with a few switchbacks toward the end of the trail. Pictures do not do these cascading falls justice! There is a small overlook, or you can continue further to climb the rocks and get near the falls.

This is an enormous zoo with large exhibits. You can't guarantee seeing any animals up close since their habits are nicely spaced. There are lots of hills, so bring walking shoes. Trams and shuttles run from the two continents. Food is overpriced so we always bring our own. Plan to stay 4+ hours.

We always have such a great time! You can drive or take a wagon. We prefer the wagon since the kids couldn't enjoy it as much in the back of our van. Animal feed is included in park fee. There's also a petting zoo, stand with food for sale, a playground, and picnic tables.

Bizarre is a very accurate name. This is an odd collection of creepy "artifacts". Limited photography is allowed. We also did the mirror maze, which was 2 minutes of fun. It was a quicker stop than expected, which is reflected by cheap admission.

As far as aquariums go, this is slightly above average, with mostly small exhibits. We were able to attend a kids program on jellyfish, which kept our kids interest. The animatronic dinosaurs were the highlight of our visit.

This free museum is smaller than I expected, but provides plenty of information. Looking through the periscope was very cool. There are plenty of interactive elements throughout that make it a more engaging visit.

The lighthouse is beautiful, though there is very little to do here. Even as a lighthouse lover, I only spent 15 minutes here. It is easily accessible with a 2 minute walk along a boardwalk. Parking is limited.

Listen to the audio through the app so you can hear all the fascinating stories! The cemetery itself is very picturesque but the quirky and somber stories make this historic site a must see while in Beaufort.

This is a free, unexpected gem in the heart of Cherokee. On this hot summer day, I observed families swimming, hiking, laying on rocks, and enjoying a picnic. It's a refreshing space to connect with nature.
Nice playground with covered picnic tables, restrooms, two playgrounds, and a splash pad. There is a lot of brick seating around the perimeter, I just wish it had shade.
This is a well designed museum that tells the rich history of the Cherokee tribe. Kids under 5 are free, though there is very little to engage young children.
This is such a beautiful park with bright colors, rubber flooring, green space, and creative design. My children especially love the slides.
Clean, spacious park with fields, trails, and playground. I've been a dozen times and we're often the only family there.
This iconic part of the Parkway is a geographic and historical gem in the High Country! The views are spectacular!
I try to scream with my hands up, but the wind is knocked out of me every time. So exhilarating!
We go a few times a year and have a great time. This is a place for train lovers of all ages!

Such a beautiful gem of our city! I just found out about it and can't believe I didn't know of it sooner. My toddler and I had a great time at the indoor play area (pretend kitchen, farm and supermarket toys) before exploring the outdoor grounds. I had read to bring treats for the goats to feed them, so I brought a bunch of carrots with us (an employee also suggested apples). There were about 6 goats we could feed, and my son loved it. The goats are very friendly and enjoyed being petted. There's also a barn with an old tractor and life-size animal sculptures, chickens, and plenty of room to run around. I appreciated all of the informational plaques and exhibits in the main building — such cool history that has been preserved so well here. We ended our visit by walking on the trails behind the shaded parking area. The staff we met were exceptionally friendly and we were some of the very few visitors on a late weekday summer afternoon. I'm already planning our next visit here!

Nice historical park with new carousel house (original building is still on the property), pool, and playground. The playground has vintage equipment for older kids — metal slides and ride-on toys — that creates nostalgia from my own childhood, but get much too hot to be usable on a sunny day. The toddler equipment (the label says it is designed for children aged 2–5) is made of the newer recycled plastic material, and this portion was under the shade of trees, which was nice on a hot day when we visited. The ground is sand in the entire playground area, which is quite large. There are also swings, including a few bucket style for young kids. The water fountain wasn't in operation and there was a little bit of trash on the playground, but nothing too unusual.

My family stumbled upon this park while on the 2018 Tour D'Coop — otherwise it's pretty hidden back in the South Park neighborhood and would probably be hard to notice. It was remodeled in the last year and has a wonderful variety of equipment for ages 2–12. The older kids area is shaded with canopies (the small play set isn't shaded). There is a nice grassy area at the edge of the park that was heavily shaded in the early morning. The whole playground is enclosed by chain link fence with two gates. It was very clean on our visit. I like that the equipment is quite unique and we plan to visit again! Parking is just on the street next to the park (on a corner lot) and there aren't bathrooms, but there is a water fountain.

Nice, clean, modern playground. I had hoped it would be good for my young toddler, but the equipment was slightly too big for him (the small structure has a label that says it is designed for 5–12 year olds, though the park website says ages 2–12 can play here). There are two bucket seat swings he could use, and he did enjoy the interactive elements of the play structure. The rubber surface on the ground is very soft. We were the only people there on a weekday afternoon, so I suspect not many people know about this park. The actual playground equipment isn't shaded, but there is a roof over a group of picnic tables nearby. There are also water fountains, which was nice just in case we needed them.

Such an incredible park area! So much equipment and green space, it's easy to spend hours here. My extremely active toddler loves the chicken coop area and climbing on the "big kids" (ages 5–12) play structure to go down the yellow tube slide. There are a variety of swings, including a tandem swing for a caregiver/big kid to ride on with an attached bucket swing for an infant or toddler. The bathrooms are clean and close by. The two water fountains at the bathroom building weren't working on our visit on 3/28/2018, but there is another working foundation near the covered picnic shelter. I appreciate that there are a lot of benches (some covered) around the perimeter of the park.

Nice, shaded neighborhood park with a mix of natural areas and playground equipment. My toddler was obsessed with the fire truck that had two steering wheels that he could "drive". There's a lot of equipment, so there seems to be a variety of things for kids aged around 2 and up. Sand surface over most of the park (I wish I had thought to bring sand toys) and some concrete areas that are nice if you bring chalk. My only complaint is that there was a bit of trash that I picked up, but there were at least a few trash cans to put trash in. We were the only people at the park when visiting on an overcast weekday afternoon. Will be back to explore more!

Fun park that has sections for younger children and older children, and is also gated in for a main portion of the playground. The parking area is set back from the park for even more safety. There have never been unlocked, open bathrooms when we have visited — especially in winter when they understandably close to prevent frozen pipes, but their signage says they open in “early spring” which I learned the hard way means around mid-April instead of the actual beginning date of spring, March 21.

Played here as a kid really often in the 90's, and loved coming back at their reopening in late 2016 with my infant son to check out the new equipment. It is SO FUN! And he barely was old enough to use anything yet. I just smiled as I walked around checking everything out and seeing so many happy children of all ages and abilities having fun. What a gem from our Parks & Recreation department, Raleigh is so lucky to have this free park! I can't wait to use it more often as my son grows up.

What a neat attraction with a lot of interesting exhibits! Once inside, it contains more than I expected. The touch tank was a neat experience for our young toddler, and he also really enjoyed the room that had puzzles, books, and puppets. I was really impressed with the exhibit hall that showcased life-sized ocean animals and learned new things. Each employee and volunteer that we encountered was incredibly friendly and knowledgable. This was a great activity for a very hot afternoon!

This is a great neighborhood park with updated, unique play equipment for young toddlers all the way to pre-teen. Most of the playground was shaded on our summer morning visit around 8:30am. It would be nice if there were public restrooms however. I picked up a few items of trash on the ground, but otherwise the park area was very clean. We will be back to visit again soon, and next time plan to explore the pond and trail around it too.

Pretty park with outdoor playground, dog run, sports fields, tennis and volleyball courts, and shaded garden (with gazebo and walking paths). We came for the playground, which is outdated but was still fun for our young toddler. The only downfall is that there isn't much shade over the playground equipment. After playing, we enjoyed walking on the paths of the horticultural garden area. Plenty of benches are nice, too.

This is a beautiful space with a nice playground. Tons of green space to run around, lots of unique equipment. I was surprised that the park was pretty empty when we visited on a warm fall Saturday recently. There's some wear to the equipment and there was a little bit of trash on the playground, but we just picked it up and put in the nearby trashcans. There were working water fountains, too.

I stumbled upon this park on my search for something that was on my way home, and I'm so glad I did! It is incredible — such a variety of fun equipment (play sets, swings, sandbox, interactive structures) for a wide range of ages. And it is very shady, something I really appreciate on a hot and sunny day! There is just street parking, but there was plenty of room on our morning weekday visit.

Nice neighborhood park set far back from the street. There is a lot of shade around the playground from trees, but not great cover on the equipment once the sun starts coming out. We were the only people on the playground on a weekday morning, but there were a dozen or so people using the disc golf course. Plenty of parking and bathrooms are available! There is also a covered picnic shelter.

Fascinating model railroads, great for kids and adults of all ages. Enjoyed going inside an old caboose, seeing all of the detail in the models, and the outdoor garden railroad area (complete with a model steam engine that actually runs on steam). Our toddler son had so much to look at and enjoy! Admission was free, but donations are gladly accepted.

Nice variety of playground equipment in a shaded area (with extra canopies for more shade). The park is designed for ages 2–12, but my 14 month old son could easily play on the smaller set and loved it. There's plenty of parking, bathrooms (they were out of hand soap in the women's on my visit, though) and easy access to the greenway.

World-class art experience on a large, beautiful campus. I love walking or running on the greenway trails and seeing the outdoor art installations, visiting any of the special art exhibits, having a picnic outside on the newly expanded outdoor park area, and grabbing delicious food at Iris before or after visiting the museum.

Great playground area, separated out for 2–5 year olds and 5–12 year olds. My son isn't yet 2, but still was able to use the playground with supervision and he LOVED it. The equipment is new, clean, and age appropriate. I was surprised there weren't more kids here on a Saturday afternoon. I can tell we'll come here often.

Nice walking/running trail around the lake (approximately 3 miles long), mostly on a shaded trail. Ducks and geese hang out near the shore. The main parking lot can get full on a nice day, but there are alternate options across and down the street. I appreciate that they have bathroom facilities here, too!

Great green space with beautiful landscaping, sports fields, a plethora of benches, and a decent playground (regular swings, bucket swings, sandbox with two sit-on diggers and two vintage riding animals). Large trees provide ample shade. This is a such a nice place for a picnic or a walk!

Tree-shaded park with a variety of equipment for ages 2–12, two unisex bathrooms (the one we used as a family didn't have a diaper changing station, though), and a sandbox area with three sit-down diggers. The large parking lot is very shady, too.

A gem of downtown Raleigh! So many exciting and fun exhibits keep my toddler entertained, and I never feel bored. Staff are very friendly. Buying a membership was one of the best investments I made this summer!
Nice, shady playground with versatile play equipment and swings for toddlers and older. However, it has a trash problem — including a used condom and wrapper on the actual equipment 😳😫
Great heavily shaded playground area with a variety of unique equipment for ages 2–12. It's partially fenced in and has a wood chip surface. There were a number of seating areas, too.
Nice, shaded park with a wide range of play equipment for toddlers and up. The space was clean and I appreciated the large parking lot, too!

I'm going to rate Mayo River State Park high based on its potential and the fact it is a newer park. First impressions go a long way looking at what a state park can and should be. Does this park have professional staff? (Yes) Do they have clean restrooms? (Yes) Do they have reservable facilities? (Yes)  Do they have well kept hiking and running trails? (Yes) Do they have picnic areas and grills? (Yes) The basics of this park are on a solid foundation and the local community should be proud to have this park in their respective area. Look for great things to happen in the near future along the Mayo River portion of this park. (Life's Short, Take a Hike)🚶

Really enjoyed my visit to Chimney Rock State Park. Wife and I went to put in some hiking miles. Started Hiking at parking area on Four Seasons Trail up Hickory Nut Falls Trail to lower falls. Working our way back to the steps up to Gneiss Cave, Pulpit Rock, Vista Rock, Chimney Rock to Exclamation Point Trail and intersecting Skyline Trail to upper falls overlook. Not sure how many stairs we climbed, but estimated around 1500. Climbed over 2000 feet high. Loved this hike and recommend this to all. Beautiful Views all the way up and down. Enjoy the town and a bite to eat before you leave.

Enjoy a day at the zoo privately owned and operated in Troutman N.C.. As part of the admissions you can experience exotic animals up close and personal. First, walk thru and enjoy interacting with the giraffes, tigers, kangaroos as well as vast number of species from around the world. Then when you are ready to exit take the drive thru the farm to finish your experience. Don't forget the gift shop. Staff were great and very helpful.

One of the great beaches in N.C. Bird Island is conjoined with Sunset Beach. This beach is a reserve sanctuary for birds and sea turtles. You can swim and Sun bath here as well as anchor you boat in the inlet waterway area. Bird Island is also home of the Kindred Spirit Mailbox and has a trail loop inside the dune area. Visit the lower area at the waterway inlet to watch boats go in and out for fishing, site seeing, casino cruises.

I have been so blessed with the health and abilities to have hiked all of Grandfather Mountains trails. I have enjoyed the beauty of this mountain range in all four seasons and have found that I discover something wonderful and new each time venture into these woods. Hiking is not just rewarding to your health, "it changes your soul". Life's short, take a hike.

One of North Carolina's most scenic and beautiful state parks. Primitive camping, hiking, fishing, site seeing, waterfalls, swimming, horseback riding, and more in one big park. Over 7,000 acres. Visitor offers education events, park history tutorial, gift shop, restrooms. Plan and reserve picnic areas with grill and fire places. (Life's Short, Take A Hike)

This is a nice convenient fishing pier and store. Has a gift store as well as small grill. Fishing tackle, bait, accessories. Also has restrooms. For a small fee you can walk or fish on the pier. They have a fairly big parking area right beside public access to beach area. Nearby are ice cream shop, snow cone, taffy-candy store, bike rentals, house rentals.

This is a very nice park with well maintained trails, beautifully staged picnic table areas, group gathering area, restrooms, overviews of West Jefferson N.C., you can hike the mountain from rangers office or drive to top. If your a Romantic you can hike the Mountain Ridge Trail where you can see a knotta kissing (see photo). Life's short, take a hike.

Absolutely beautiful place to visit if you enjoy the natural environments of mountains and forrest. Some of the best hiking that you can experience from Hard to easy. The observation platform gives you the breathtaking views of surrounding mountains and valleys. Restaurant, gift shop, education museum and nature center. Life's short, take a hike.

Beautiful State park to visit. Camping, hiking, fishing, rock climbing, historical home place. Trails are well marked and maintained for all levels of fit individuals. Several of the trails can be fiscally challenging with high elevations and plenty of steps to climb. Choose your trails well and ask for information before starting your journey.

Another N.C. State Park to visit and enjoy your time at. Nice trails to hike beside river or wade in on hot days. Camping is available as well as group gatherings. There are historic sites and a small museum. The staff here was very friendly and helpful. I highly recommend spending your day here. "Life's Short, Take A Hike"

Nice park in Catawba County located at Oxford Dam.  This is a all around park that offers hiking, biking, canoeing, fishing, kayaking. They also have a dog park that is fenced in for safety.  If you have a family gathering you can reserve their shelter areas or first come first serve picnic areas.

This is a beautifully maintained park with great scenic trails meandering under a awesome canopy of trees. The plant life and natural rock formations enhance its beauty for those who love nature. The Summit Trail offers another great view of our spectacular Blue Ridge Mountains. Happy Trails.

Nice hike from visitor center to summit. You can also drive to top where there is parking, picnic areas and covered shelters. The overviews at the top are spectacular. You can also hike around the pinnacle landmark. Camping is available at lower elevations. Highly recommend, but go early.

Crowder Mountain Has plenty of things to do from hiking, canoeing, camping, picnics. Nice park with friendly staff. Small museum to help educate about surrounding wild life. This park connects with Kings Mountain State Park via a one of it's trails. (Life's short, take a hike.)

Nice park in Catawba County, Hickory area. Brought my kids here often when they were young. They have picnic areas that you can reserve. They also have hiking trails, a play area for kids and frisbee golf course. You can also fish from thier pier in the wet land area.

Morrow Moutain State Park has plenty to offer from kayaking, canoeing, hiking, horse back riding, primitive camping and cabin rentals. Nice facilities that can be reserved for get to togethers and events. A historic museum and gift shop. Life's Short, Take a Hike.

Beautiful park with plenty to do for the whole family. Camping, hiking, picnics, kayaking, canoeing, boating activities, 30.5 miles of bike trails, educations events, swimming, group functions. Highly recommended. (Life's short, get out and play.)

One of the best state parks in North Carolina. Fishing, camping, hiking, horseback riding, small museum, education center, guided tours, picnic areas. Very well maintained and staffed. Beautiful waterfall with overview platform. "Go Take A Hike".

Great place to enjoy by yourself or with your family. Swimming, boating, camping, hiking, biking, group gatherings, picnicking. Plenty to do and lots of fun. Park offers activities for children and adults. "Life's Short, Take a Hike"
This land is utilized very well as a park. Rock climbing, hiking, trail running for all experience levels. Picnic areas and group gatherings. All in Alexander County. Life's short, take a hike.
Great park for a walk or just relaxing on one of many park benches. Great place to watch the sun rise over intercoastal water way. Beautiful views and pleasant place to walk your dog.
Great community-based museum to visit. They are always expanding activities for the area to explore. They have strong community support system for the areas art and science programs.
This state park offers a lot of activities to choose from, so plan to spend the day and take a picnic with plenty of water. Make sure you take lots of pictures to share with friends.
I have hiked all of the trails in Grandfather Mountain Park, views are best in North Carolina. Trails are challenging and rewarding. Life is short, go take a hike.

As good as it gets for Fayetteville (and, I'd venture to say, the surrounding area). Always well maintained, the park is a rectangle covering a block or two in the center of a nice housing area. One may walk the path tracing its perimeter, stopping for the kids to play on one of two playgrounds, or at the "castle," or  to run across the baseball field, etc. Trees, grass, and water are in sufficient supply. It is all clean and open and soothing, I'd say.

Its a decent water park kids had fun we did too ive went hear since i was a young one , they do close to early at the beginning of june 10 to 5 ??! Atleast 7 would be good but they do begin to  extend to that time after the first week when kids are out you cant bring in outside food but hey they want to make money and no telling how much the cleanup would be with outside food there are picnic tables out in the front if you want to bring your lunch

I attended a wedding reception here last June and this was the perfect spot for it. We had a chance to enjoy some drinks outside. Some people took advantage to wander the grounds; I opted to sip on some drinks in the meanwhile. The ballroom (if that's the right terminology for it) was wonderful - the dance floor was strategically placed in the center, and the tables around it, so everyone could get a view of everything.

I've been going to the Frankie's in Charleston since I was a kid. After I moved to Columbia, I've grown to like this one. Compared to the Frankie's in Charleston, this one is bigger so they have more selection with the video games and have more non-arcade activities including laser tag, larger putt putt course, and a fun house. It's located in Harbison so there's a lot of shopping and good restaurants nearby.

The kids can walk, stomp, jump etc on the keys to "make music"... made me feel like I was in the movie "BIG" with Tom Hanks :) They also can play various instruments from drums, cymbals, chimes etc... again, loud, but fun! They also have an area with animals from different times such as a tigers, mammoths, deer, beavers, and also live fish! The kids loved the tree-house area where they could climb

This is a cool area of Downtown Durham! Lots of events are held here from time to time. If you are visiting the Durham area and want to do something fun be sure to check their website to see what events (food truck rodeos, etc) might be going down during your visit. Concerts are often held here as well. This area is super up and coming and there is alot of great things to do around the DC Park.

This is a public garden like no other in the area, always pushing the envelope of horticulture practices. The highly-skilled staff here demonstrates their mastery of techniques like pleaching, espalier, and other pruning and display techniques. The combinations of plants in each bed give home gardeners ideas about how to decorate their own landscapes with flowering plants and foliage textures.

I've visited Old Salem numerous times over the years. I was pleased on my latest visit that new buildings and exhibits were open.In the buildings you can see various trades performed and learn about the Moravian history. I enjoyed the Doctor's House; Boy's School as I had not seen those before but it was great to see the other buildings again and get questions answered by the staff.

There is a large parking area at the Visitor's Center. Tickets are $27 for a two day pass.  The staff provides you with a map and circles all the stops so you will not miss a thing. You can go in any order you'd like. There is a lot of walking so make sure you have comfortable shoes on. There are also restroom stops along the way that are marked on your map as they are not obvious.

Excellent park for seniors, children, families, handicapped. Excellent park for those who love to fish and hike. Beautifully maintained. Staff on premises. Easily accessible. Beautifully landscaped with river birches, crepe myrtles, and trees native to the area. The walking trail is paved and winds through the woods. The lakeside has benches for fishing and picnic tables/grills.

As has been said, the Gateway Gardens is a lovely park.  The one negative mentioned was the "side of town" it is on.  There is nothing wrong with where it is placed and it makes a lovely entry into or exit our of Greensboro.  It across from the brand new Hayes-Taylor YMCA and a block from Barber Park were so many outdoor concerts, and other activities, are held.

Eno River State Park is on more than 4,000 acres. It is absolutely beautiful! It has many entrances throughout Orange and Durham counties. The park has beautifully maintained hiking trails - and many of them! The many times I have hiked in this park, I have never found any litter.There are canoe access sites, camping sites, historic sites and picnic areas.

the shade disappears about 1130 am so plan on coming before then or later in the day. Bring a water bowl to fill so you can take it and your dog into the shaded areas at the base of the park- then you won't have to keep walking all the way back to water your pup- we fill a jug and fill our bowl that way because you're sure to make new thirsty fur friends!

The most unique peculiar place! We attended the Christmas by Candlelight Tours and it was awesome! We arrived around 5:30pm based on the suggestion online that 6-7pm was a busy time. We purchased our tickets online while others in our group had to purchase a ticket there. The line to purchase tickets was not long and we moved right through to our tour.

If you are in Fayetteville, NC or near Fort Bragg you should definitely make an effort to see the 82nd airborne division war Memorial Museum. It was very educational with lots of sites and information. We appreciated the Modern building two houses such a special military tribute. It was a moving experience as you walked the different sections.

The gardens are beautiful and a great place to visit after visiting the Reynolda Home. The gardens are free and there were so many beautiful flowers in bloom in July. The tropical flower building was closed in July yet there was plenty to see outside. Next door are shops and the Village area and it is all within walking distance.
