A beautiful, wooded park that provided the backdrop for mine & my dog, Milo's pictures yesterday. On a lovely, pre-summer day around 9 AM, the park wasn't quite busy, but had folks milling about setting up "camp." Others were hiking & walking. There are a few old barn-type looking buildings, plenty of picnic tables & a beautiful

A great historical park for walking/running/bike riding. Just please observe the signs that keep pedestrians and wheeled traffic separated. And if you have a large group it would be nice to not spread out all across the lane, be courteous of others who may be walking/running faster than your group and yield some space.

This was exactly what I hoped it would be, our tour guides were awesome Lee and Liz were great and entertaining the kids had a great time and even when things got a little difficult for my younger son they were patient and helped give him confidence. I would recommend it for great family building skills and fun.

This is a very nice park with many amenities. I just went there this year for the Tanglewood Festival of Lights. We went opening weekend and it was already pretty busy. They loop you around a big area before even letting you through the gates. Then, it's pretty much bumper to bumper traffic through the park.

What a wonderful place for children and adults alike. We have been members for over 2 years & our 3 year old has learned so much from this facility. The staff are super friendly and accommodating. We have been over 30 times. They  showcase different areas quite often. They are growing as well as expanding.

Nice park! Trails are well maintained. The lookout makes an interesting stopping point.  This is a great park for a hike with your dog.  There are some steep trails, a lookout, some history lessons, and 2 ponds.  There is traffic noise from Rt 85 that kind of takes away from the natural setting.

This museum is small but had great items when I went today. There is a sculpture garden at the entrance. It was playing a thunderstorm from the speakers today.The basement has storage of items that the museum rotates through every few monthes. Large free parking lot in back of building.

A museum that truly celebrates the diversity of life and the wonder of science via a myriad of interactive stations...! There's truly something here for every one, across the age ranges, and makes the life of this toddler mom so much more interesting, educated and full of joy.

Fayetteville keeps getting better and this year's International Folk Festival was evidence of that. Thanks to the Art Council! We had a wonderful time. Music, Sirius B and others, was great and Mystic India was spectacular. Will be going next year for sure!

This place was definitely an unexpected pleasure.  There were quite a few trails here that offered different varieties of nature and scenery.  The views at the top of the hills were really nice.  Also really liked the multiple ponds and the views around them as well.  Trails are very well maintained and well marked.  You can definitely hike 5+ miles as most all of these trails connect with one another.  Note: the Johnson Loop trail across the highway isn't nearly as good as the trails that start near the big red barn.

This is a great lil nature preserve that is literally a hidden gem out in the middle of no where.  It is an all-boardwalk trail (1.5 miles) in the woods that loops around a small pond.  I've done many boardwalk trails all over the country and this is the 2nd longest one I have done (Congaree National Park in South Carolina being my longest one).  It also has an observation deck at the pond.  Could be a lil better if there were a few more scenic things to see, activities, and/or trails.

Very nice lighthouse that you can actually go into during the Covid-19 pandemic (there arent many lighthouses that allow people into them now)  and can climb the stairs to the top of it.  Though there is a fee ($8 for adults) and also not counting the ferry ride fee to the island...it is walking distance from the ferry loading/unloading docks or you can rent golf carts or a bicycle.  Also know that the ferry rides fill up quick and are limiting the amount of people on them.

This place was definitely an unexpected pleasure.  There were quite a few trails here that offered different varieties of nature and scenery.  The views at the top of the hill was really nice.  The pine tree forest was also really nice.  There was a very cool scenic bridge that you can go under and walk across. Trails are very well maintained and well marked.  You can definitely hike 5+ miles as most all of these trails connect with one another.

This is a great park with lots of wonderful different things to see.  It has a lot history, variety of scenic things and activities to do.  The hiking trails were really nice, well maintained and well marked.  You get to see a small waterfall, a pond, bridges, and the Rookery Romp play area was pretty cool.  Highly recommend checking out this place, especially if you're in the area, you wont be disappointed.

The old guy who runs this place is an absolute clown and obviously needs some social & people skills workshops.  Would also be nice if the 'rescued' owl & falcon had cages a lot bigger than the closet size ones they're in now.  This place is an absolute joke and a disgrace to all Ohio state parks & nature preserves.  What kind of place like this closes at 4:30 pm on weekends during the warm seasons?

Very impressive park that shows a wonderful tribute to military veterans.  Has a lot of variety of activities to include: ball fields, ball courts, kids playland, a paved path that loops around the park, etc.  It also has a large portion of the park dedicated to the veterans with a clock tower, memorial, flag court, full size tank, etc.  Highly recommend visiting this place!

This is a pretty nice lighthouse with a great boardwalk across the street that has a lot of informational and historical signs on it.  Also sits right across the street from Caswell Beach.  Parking lots aren't that big and are limited.  It's located right next door to the Coast Guard station as well.  The lighthouse itself is closed and you cant go inside it.

A pretty nice lil Revolutionary War battle site that's kinda out in the middle of no where.  The history trail around the battlefield is really nice with lot of monuments, memorials and a long boardwalk over the creek.  The Visitor Center is also pretty nice with a friendly staff that has a lot of knowledge of this particular battle.

One of my favorite state parks to visit in the country.  The hiking trails here are better and more scenic than some National Parks.  Great place with lots of amazing things to see. Hiking up the stairs to the rock is very challenging, but well worth it.  Highly recommend also taking the hiking trail to Hickory Nut Falls.

This was definitely an unexpected gem of a place.  Lots of Revolutionary War history with beautiful monuments & memorials.  The Visitor Center was open and had a nice tour through it.  The staff was very friendly.  There are quite a few hiking trails along with an audio driving tour around the park as well.

One of the best hidden gems in central Ohio.  Was definitely a breath of fresh air, literally & figuratively because almost all the people there were actually friendly.  The park was so clean and the trails were well maintained.
Perhaps the people in all the metro parks around Columbus should take notice.

Nice trail with a lot of scenic things to see.  The north end of the loop could use some trail maintenance with its overgrowth.  This place can get crowded, but mostly  within a mile each way of the trail head...after that you dont see too many people doing the long distance hikes around the lake.

One of the best metro parks in Ohio.  It's so big I would have thought it was a state park and is actually taken care of better than a lot of state parks in Ohio.  The hiking trails are really nice and there are a lot of them!

One of the best hiking trails in Ohio, if not the best!  It has multiple different trails, to include a mountain bike trail.  Only down fall is the 1st walking bridge is closed, would be great if they repaired it.

Coming from a guy who isnt really into flowers or plants, this place really blew me away. I was lil hesitant to pay the entrance fee to tour these gardens, but so glad I did.  Staff was also really friendly.

Can't even believe this is the same Mirror Lake of once before. They literally rebuilt this to look more like a swamp. It's an embarrassment that this major university allowed this to become absolute trash

Decent park to hike at. Horseshoe Falls is very small and not that exciting to see. Would be nice if there was a trail that allowed you to walk out onto the dam tower like you can at Mohican State Park.
The hiking trails and site seeing are amazing.  So many wonderful things to see here and love the fact that you can bring your dog to this place!  One of the best state parks I have ever been to.
Very nice place with great hiking trails. The swinging bridge at mile high is amazing. Love the fact that they give you a tourist CD that you can listen to on your drive up the mountain.
One of my favorite places in the country to visit. Endless amounts of beautiful beaches, wonderful light houses, great nature preserves, ferry rides to other islands, etc etc etc.
It's one of the better metro parks in the Columbus metro area. Buffalo are cool to see if the grass is cut so you can actually see them. Lots of trails to hike
Great place with all kinds of wonderful scenery.  Hiking trails are in excellent condition. Both waterfalls, dam, and covered bridge are all worth seeing.
One of the best waterfalls I have ever seen.  Nice hiking trail to get there.  A must see if you are in and around the Smoky Mountains!
Not a bad place, would be if they added/extended the hiking trail on the other side of the creek...plus fix the bridge.

Awesome display of tanks, uniforms, and weaponry.
Only complaint is the not so friendly staff. We arrived with disabled elderly (with wheelchairs) and we were not given nor offered any assistance (especially at check-in). We called ahead twice and still weren't given the correct information on how to enter the building correctly and upon arrival they acted as if we burdened them because we didnt know.
We still put on our smiling faces but i was greatly disheartened at the staff's attitudes....all except ONE guy...didnt catch his name...but he was at the side where we were finally told to go in with wheelchairs...he wore a gun on his side...he was a real nice gentlemen who offered above and beyond service.
dislikes: Lack of assistance for disabled visitors

reviews_attraction.text: Great park. Beautifully kept. Huge shelter area with nice long picnic tables also with handicap accessibility on each end. Great area for the kids with swings and slides...very nice equipment and well maintained. Great lengthy walking trail that surrounds the entire park. Excellent place to walk, fairly flat and well paved all the way around. Bathrooms available. Baseball field. Plenty of room to picnic, throw ball or frisbee. Pet friendly with bags to pick up after your pet. Lots of well kept trash cans for trash. All in all one of the best parks around. Very peaceful.

Beautiful Area. Plenty of nice picnic areas with tables and grills. Nice walking paths. Very nice covered shelter area near beach. Nice beach area. Dock for fishing or just viewing the lake. Lots of trails to take you all over Hanging Rock mountain and beyond. Lots of parking.

Beautiful spot. One of the most recognized spots on the Blue Ridge Parkway. Coming here for years. A must visit to anyone, with a beautiful drive here you can't go wrong. Amazing peacefulness here even when crowded. Beautiful landscape, bring your camera or your painting gear.

Beautiful spot. Right off the road and easily accessible right off route 8. Great to walk thru and take pictures. You can't drive thru it but you wouldn't want to its history! Also a great area around it for relaxing or taking more pictures by the creek.

Awesome little spot. Beautiful cave down a long walking trail with steps. Easily accessible off the main road. .2 miles... Paved parking area with many parking spots and signs giving directions on trails, history, and destinations.

Amazing views. Well kept. Flowers, a garden, fish...but the best is the overlook. Not only the Blowing Rock view but the platform near the back is simply amazing (see pictures). Stunning area. Very pricey for families but worth it.

Very nice museum. Very clean. Friendly staff. We always have a great time when we visit. Great place to go on any day especially a rainy one. Lots of interesting exhibits. Easily accessible in the heart of Martinsville City.

Nice park. Great walking trail. Great play area for children Dinosaur themed. Plenty of area to walk, run or ride a bicycle. Baseball field. Bathrooms. Plenty of parking. A little hard to find entrance.
Great lights! Love the radio music follows the lights. Plenty of parking. Thankful it's setup for families to enjoy. Thankful for the horse drawn carriage rides. Great staff! beautiful lights!
Fun for the entire family. Kid's pools, play areas, and great slides. Huge slides for the family / adults. Love the lazy river! Friendly and Helpful Staff. Lifeguards on every corner. Clean.
Great park. Very clean. Fishing, Boating, Camping, Cabins, Lake, Beach with sand, Waterfalls, Playground equipment, Walking trails, lots of things to explore and do. Lots of parking.
Beautiful! Excellent view. One of the best I've seen on the parkway. Work the visit. Huge. lots of parking. rocks to climb and walk on. rock picnic table to eat on. large rock wall.
Great downtown. Lots of neat shops to browse and buy. Eat in the street from local restaurants serving. Lots of things to see. Beautiful brick street. Walk, walk and walk.
Very nice replica of the Mayberry courthouse and jail. Was nice to just walk in and take out time. Great photo opportunities inside and out. Worth the ride to visit.
likes: Cultural Value (replica of Mayberry courthouse and jail)

reviews_attraction.text: Really neat to see the beginning of the Blue Ridge Parkway. Small Pull off area beside the road so you can get a picture of the enter sign and a rockfish gap sign.
Family Fun. Pricey for Families. Several Rides and lots of Games. Roller Coaster is a classic. Could use some upgrading, same every year but still a good time.
Beautiful place. Great stop right on the Blue Ridge Parkway. Man-made "dam" waterfall. Great fishing spots. Good parking in a lot right off the road.
Great place to visit. Very historical. Amazing views. Great location to walk around Richmond and visit various locations. Beautiful architecture.
Not worth the price but still very entertaining. Doesn't last long. Kids enjoyed it for what it's worth...very quick after a very very long wait.
beautiful park. lots of picnic tables. plenty of parking. lots of area to walk. Beach area. great place for a group get together.
Great Museum. Lots to look at. Very spacious. Very friendly. Great place to visit and bring the family. The trains are amazing.
Beautiful. Wild roads to get too. Lots of turns and traffic on backroads that go up and down. Worth the trip. What a view!
Great little area to picnic. Shelter with tables and trash cans. Well taken care of with a nice area for children to play.
Great overlook. I can imagine its best at night with such a large skyline. Across the road is also a great view.

Great park with a lot of history, it's a revolutionary war park. The park has plenty of parking and things to do. That main battlefield trail is paved (but it's very steep at parts, so be prepared for a good hike) and if you don't do a ranger guided tour you can call a number and have an automated phone guided tour. There's a lot of activities at the park so check the official website to see what all's going on. They have a gift shop and film in the main building. This park is a must visit!

This is really cool park, there's a couple of trails to hike and a nice campground. Note that hurricane Matthew breached the dam in two places really bad and it could be a year or so before it's fixed and the lake is back up to normal. It's still a nice park even with that. When I went the hurricane had washed out one of the roads in but you can get in the park by going around the area to another road, not many good signs to get in so make sure you're paying attention to gps or map.

This is a really neat park with a lot to do and see. If you want to camp here reserve months (like a year) in advance!!!! It's extremely popular and camping fills up fast. Aside from the beach there's trails, a lake and Atalaya Castle. The only disappointment is you have to pay an extra fee to tour the castle, you'd think the park fee would cover this but no. They have a gift shop/store here as well.

Awesome park! It's a smaller park - I'd say cozy. There's still a lot to do though, trails, volley ball court, boat rentals and more. They also have a really nice event building right on the lake. Make sure to check out the dam area built by the CCC in the early 1900's - very cool! This is a great park to camp at, hold an event or just visit for the day.

Very surprised at this park! We were in the area and decided to stop by and see the site, didn't expect such a nice well preserved park. Beautiful scenery, what's left of the furnace is kept in good shape as well as all the barns, houses and grounds. There is a lot to see here and experience. They also have several trails. Visit if you can!!!!

Nice historic area. They have a picnic shelter and nice grounds with a short nature walk. There's also a trailhead for a 2 mile river hike here. There's not a lot as far as buildings just mainly the house and a few small sheds but a nice place if you're into history or old plantation style places. Kept up real nice.

Surprised at how nice this park is! They have several picnic areas and a nice 1 mile trail that goes by the river. Great if you're a history or a nature person. Make sure you check out the battlefield trail and horseshoe falls, you have to drive to another spot to get to it but it's not far, check with the ranger.

Great park with something for everyone. They have a really nice campground, cabins, a nice lake with boat rentals and swimming all at the park. They also have several trails you can take from easy to difficult. If you can make it to the top of table rock it's worth it, amazing view! Very affordable admission.

If you love history, this is a must visit. Grounds are kept up good and the place looks as if it's been untouched since the burning. Parking is across the street, just a large open non paved area. Be careful as there's no signs, you'll pass it before you know it.

This is a nice large park. There's plenty to do including canoe tours. The trails are good but could use some work. The campground is really nice, the reason I gave this a four start over three, nestled in a lot of tall pines and very well maintained.

This is mainly an equestrian park, they do have a campground. There are a lot of trails but they're equestrian trails and mostly not that great for hikers. The equestrian facilities look like they're in good shape and well maintained. All dirt roads.

This is a nice park there's just not a lot to do here. Not bad if you just want to spend a day at the lake or have a picnic. Despite claiming they have a trail it's just a trailhead to a bike trail that's not a part of the park.

Awesome park with a lot to see and photograph. My only complaint is parking, it's been bad since I can remember and they could easily fix it but haven't. Plan on waiting to get in, don't even attempt during peak season.

This is a must visit. Very beautiful hike and falls. Do NOT climb to the top of the falls, there have been several bad accidents by experienced hikers and climbers on these falls. Moderate to difficult hike.

Awesome park right in Greenville, plenty of hiking/biking paths, two lakes and a campground. The only downside is during peak season the price is a little steep and the bike traffic can be a bit much.
This is the better of the parks in this area. Large park with campground, beach area, plenty of playgrounds and picnic areas. They have one trail, tennis courts and a basketball court.
Awesome park with a lot of history. The canal trail is long but well worth it, there are still parts of the canal in sections and an old Mill. They also have eagles that nest at times!
Pretty good park but definitely geared toward equestrian. They have a few small hiking trails but one of the trails doesn't even have parking, you have to walk a bit to get to it.
A must visit! You take about a 30 minute boat ride out to the fort. The fort is well maintained and preserved. There's a lot to learn here and plenty of photo opportunities.
This is a great state park - the beach!! The beach is great, there's a ton of shells on the beach so if you love shells check it out.
Really nice national park, nice walking trail and kept up really nice. Park is a little small, probably a half days worth.
Really nice park. Open field and a few benches. Park will suffer some of they keep building around it like they are.
This is a great park almost in Columbia. The lake is great and the trails are in great shape. A great day trip!
A nice little park, the main draw is the river for kayak and canoes. There's not a whole lot besides that.
Awesome park! There's so much to do and enjoy here. During peak season it can get full fast so go early!

Perry's Cave is named because of its use by Commodore Perry during the War of 1812 and in his decisive victory on Lake Eerie. The cave itself is easily accessible to any who wish to visit. There is also a butterfly house, a gift shop, mining for precious stones, a play area for kids and a barn that showcases some of the vehicles used in the early 20th century.

Right across the street is a local winery (which also has a cave to explore) where visitors can refresh themselves with local wines, beers and snack items.

Perry's Cave is just a short distance from downtown Put-In-Bay but you might still want to rent a golf cart or bicycle to get there.

Malabar Farm State Park is the former home of Louis Bromfield. For years it served as a place for Bromfield to write, entertain the Hollywood elite of the time, and demonstrate his ideas about farming. Today visitors can tour the house and grounds, catching a glimpse of what life was like for Bromfield and his friends. Throughout the year Malabar Farm holds festivals, such as Heritage Days, that bring to life what like was like in the early 20th century.

Fort Laurens Museum sits on the site of the Revolutionary War fort for which it is named. The museum has a number of artifacts and memorabilia from the time of the ear. The museum also includes a small theatre. The outline of the fort is etched into the ground and there are placards detailing significant events from the time the fort was occupied. Finally, there is a tomb to the unknown soldier from the Revolutionary War who died at the site.

It was fascinating to peer into the history of the Loudonville area and to see the contributions that local business men and entrepreneurs have made. At the time that I went there was an area devoted to photography that showcased not only the development of cameras and photographic techniques but also displayed and told the stories behind some of the more famous photographs taken.

Just off the square, the old Soldiers and Sailors building now holds the Mansfield Memorial Museum. The museum is home to a couple of the original Westinghouse robots (including Electro). There are artifacts from the area dating back to the civil war. There are even a couple of preserved stumps from trees planted by Johnnie Appleseed.

This is a short trail that circles the lake with an optional trail into the woods. The trails are easy, providing more of a casual walk rather than a hike. Perfect for just getting out. There is a boat launch ramp providing easy access to the lake. There are also plenty of spots along the lake to set up and enjoy fishing.

This is the place to be for anyone who is a fan of aircraft. From the very beginnings of flight to reaching the moon and beyond, NMUSA tells a compelling and informative story. And if that's not enough then there are films and simulators that bring you even closer to experiencing what few have experienced.

The lighthouse is still a working lighthouse that has been continuously running for over 100 years. Visitors can climb up into it as well as visit the house and other facilities. There is also a large picnic area with plenty of tables for a bite to eat and to just enjoy the beautiful park and Lake Erie.

The Boston Mill Visitor Center is a great jumping off place to explore the Cuyahoga Valley National Park. There is a small shop, public restrooms, and plenty of places to just hang out. On a recent visit I got to speak with one of the park ranges and got some good information about the area.

I stopped in to walk around expecting a fairly pleasant but easy going trail. Part way through I found a number of real gems along the way and got to see some spectacular rock formations.

The two trails do provide some good exercise with some hills to climb but neither was difficult.

Home of the Ashland Balloon Fest, Freer Field is a great local place for walking. The main path is paved and circles the property. Inside the woods there are several dirt paths that allow the casual hiker to stray a little from the proverbial "beaten" path into the surrounding woods.

This is a real gem located in Mansfield Ohio. Three architectural design of the building entices you in and promises a different view of art. Giving back to the community, the Art Center offers classes on a number of artistic disciplines including its latest: acting for film.

Nice, easily traversed trails that are well kept. Some great photo opportunities along the way. At one point along the path there is a long bridge that crossed the river, providing an excellent view up and down the river. The highlight of the day was seeing the waterfall.

Greater Cleveland Aquarium is located in the FirstEnergy Powerrplant. Great care was taken to create interactive displays of thousands of fish and other water creatures, including many from Ohio rivers and lakes. The sea tube alone is fascinating.

This is an enjoyable nature preserve nestled in Ashland Ohio. Trails weave in and out throughout the preserve. There are benches situated along the trails to allow the traveler a time to rest or just soak in the beautiful surroundings.

The grounds are well laid out. Although the museum wasn't officially open I was allowed to look around for a few minutes. There is also a path through the town showing other sites relevant to the fort and the battle fought in the area.

Running alongside the Scioto.River, this park complex has something for everyone. The Audubon area showcases conservation efforts in the area. Nearby, there is an obstacle course, a climbing wall, and plenty of trails.

This is a small trail located in Ashland Ohio. The wetlands are fascinating to see, specifically in the spring and summer months. Along the way are marshes and a river which provide some excellent photo opportunities.

Brown's Lake Bog is a fascinating place to take in life "on the bog". There are a number of interesting and unusual plants including several species of carnivorous ones. Great for pictures but don't try to pet them.

Every room, and there were many, was filled with "brews" and memorabilia about brewing. It was a kind of maze to get to the room where the meeting was being held but it was a maze of cosy and fascinating rooms.
A small park located in German Village. The topiary are based upon the painting of A Sunday on La Grande Jatte by Georges Seurat. Their is plenty of space to walk or just stretch and for a picnic.
Wahkeena Nature Preserve has a number of very pleasant trails to hike and plenty of opportunities for taking pictures. The preserve has wooded areas,  marshlands, and ponds/lakes.
One of six Cleveland signs scattered throughout the city. This one is located near the Foundry and next to the Cuyahoga River. Visiting all six of them is a unique "date" option.
Flat,  easily traveled trails that bring a mix of woodland and prairie.  Trails are all well marked and signs along the way help in navigating the trails.
This is a small but charming park. The trails are easy and good for a pleasant afternoon stroll. Plenty of places to just kick back and enjoy nature.

This is a very nice museum, and I like the fact that the exhibits change periodically. The good news is admission is free, both for the museum's permanent collection and park, which is a work of art within itself. While art museums may seem geared for adults, that is not true of the NC Art Museum. There are hiking trails in the park along with sculptures as well as sitting areas. The permanent collection is full of a variety of wonderful pieces, including but not limited to: Ancient Egyptian, African, Ancient American, American, Jewish, Italian, Classical, Contemporary, Modern, and a collection of 30 pieces by Rodin, including "The Thinker." The temporary exhibits are always unique and there are always a wide variety of subjects, so there is something for everyone.

The tour guide was very enthusiastic, knowledgeable, and passionate about the tour which lends to a more entertaining and interesting experience. You do have to climb a lot of steps so be prepared with good shoes. The tour guide was very accommodating and was sure to let us know in advance of tight spaces and narrow climbs so you could opt out at parts of the tour. We had been on a regular tour some many years ago and this was by far so much better. We also had a good group of like minded history oriented people so that made it even better. We finished up with light snacks on the second floor portico overlooking the grounds.

I never realized that we could also review parks, trails and even hiking areas. This is news to me! This is not a current review. My friend like to go for walks, hikes, runs, walks with the dogs... you name it. This was a beautiful park. Lots to explore and the birds you can run into are so pretty. We came here with the dog. The dogs enjoyed it. Lots of people walking, running, chilling out and even playing games. Everyone we passed was super friendly. If you have never been here before, don't wait. Get out and visit this park. It's worth it. Love this city. Lots to see and do. Highly recommend this spot.

Although I have been to the Harrison entrance to Umstead, this was my first time going in the Glenwood entrance. It's a little longer drive to get to the parking lot than at Harrison, but it is shady and beautiful along the roadway. We walked down to Big Lake and then took the 2.8 mile Sal's Branch loop. Lots of elevation change and a nice, wide path. Not many other folks out on a Monday morning so it was pretty quiet, except when a jet was revving up for takeoff from RDU. You really don't hear that on the trails on the Harrison side. Regardless, this is a nice place to take a break from the summer heat!

We wanted to see something different in the Charlotte area so decided to check out DSBG. What a treat! The gardens are so well laid out, with beautiful vistas around each bend. There are lots of benches scattered around the grounds, so it’s accessible for everyone. It was a hot day so all the fountain features were most welcome. The gardens and orchid house were decorated with gorgeous glass pieces; I think they’re illuminated at night but we were only there in daytime. We also enjoyed the butterfly bungalow—so many beautiful butterflies to see! In all, a wonderful afternoon!

We played for a while in the arcade. There are plenty of games for whatever you're looking for. Ticket-oriented chance games, skill-based like skeeball, racing, air hockey, DDR, and many more. The place gets very loud and pretty crowded, so be aware of your little one gets overwhelmed easily you might want to plan for some breather time outside. When one of the machines didn't give tickets, the guy behind the counter was quick to come and fix it. The prize counter is pretty typical and my daughter easily chose a few things as her prizes.

We really enjoy their activities, and they added even more this year. It's a great family adventure for some fall weekend with tons of things to do outside, yummy kettle corn and food truck food, and a corn maze that's not at all scary that's perfect to take the little ones through. We will continue this tradition for many years to come. We love the corn pit, the "milking cows" game, the giant spider web to climb on, the pumpkin cannons, the hay ride, the cow train ride... there is SO much to do, and our girls love it.

Getting a chance to see raptors up close is special. The people at the Carolina Raptor Center spend time rescuing and rehabilitating injured raptors. You can see various species of birds of prey. I have volunteered there multiple times and it is always a rewarding experience. Take the family and walk the trails. We had a wonderful time walking around here and seeing and learning about the various birds. It is quite a large place with many raptors in residence. The displays were well done and very informative.

I love the Greenway one of the best investments the City of Raleigh ever made. The Neuse River Trail is 27.6 miles of paved trail that runs from the Falls of the Neuse to close to Clayton. I love to ride my bike on it but it is suitable for walks and jogging as well. There are multiple locations for launching kayaks and canoes. I often see deer, hawks, owls and rabbits by the dozen. I even saw a coyote one evening on the Walnut Creek branch of the Greenway. If you are in Raleigh you should check it out.

I recently enjoyed my experience at this particular Park. Well small oh, it is quite gorgeous. Beautiful landscaping and the chance to enjoy some of Charlotte's finest architecture. This park has the feel of a small town with all the class of an upscale big city. The fish Fountain is enjoyable spot for children to cool off in the summer months. Great place to walk the dog and sit a spell. Exceptionally clean & religiously manicured. Surrounded by many of Charlotte's finest restaurants.

The collection here of the Bechtler family is fairly small but carefully collected curated. The building is quite lovely. It's a once in a lifetime chance to view works by the modern masters such as Picasso, Chagall, Miro, Lichtenstein, and Leger. There is a parking lot across the street that charges $5 on the weekends, but there is a problem leaving it - it took me 20 minutes with not much traffic. Try to get something on the street.

The park itself is relatively large, with lots of families using it for picnics, frisbee, and general fun. There's a cottage that might be rented out. There are two parking lots, one just before the bridge to the park, and one after. Although the lots can can fill quickly, you never feel crowded on the bike trails. Thanks you to the Raleigh city fathers that planned and paid for the park and bike trails. Your foresight is appreciated.

I was looking for something to do in the area of Cary and found this place. It’s free to get in and it has a nice facility with bathrooms and a small interactive museum for the kids. The mill itself is so beautiful and peaceful. The waterfall and rocks made me feel like I was in the mountains. They have tours of the mill on the weekends only. They also have a mile of hiking trail around the lake there. Easy walk with small children.

These gardens were within walking distance of my hotel. This a beautiful way to spend a day. The greenhouses are a treat and the staff are outstanding! If in Charlotte and you love botany - this is a must visit experience. The Gardens have lovely inside and outside areas with large collections of plants in each. This time I was able to take a workshop and learn how to make fairy houses and it was really a fun experience.

Spent the day there, but didn’t get there till nearly midday. Booked day pass online. Went kayaking, lovely, adventure white water rafting, absolutely superb, but of food which was good, mountain biking, rock wall climbing and ran out of time for zip lining. Go early, it was the best day of my vacation especially the rafting. Prepare to get wet, to smile, giggle and scream all in the same moment.

We recently visited this historic house & park. Even though the day was hot & humid, the house & structures are cool & comfortable. Our guide, Marissa, was superb! She had a large group (our seniors as well as a family with small children, etc) and she made the presentation relatable to all, interesting, and fun. She really seems to enjoy what she does and it shows. She made history fun!

Came here to take a break from my daugther. She had a great time. Not only did she live the zip line activity but she wanted to explore the trail and look at the pond. We had a great time as a family here. One of the best playgrounds we have visited. One the best children’s playground we have visited. Clean, lots of options, accommodates younger and older kids. Great experience!

My friend and I along did “Dark Room” at Room 5280. After doing many escape rooms throughout the years, Room 5280 did not disappoint. Andrew who was our game master was friendly and did an excellent job briefing us about the room. You could tell each puzzle was made specifically for that room and the locks, hints, and props added a cool atmosphere to the whole game.

The museum and everything within the compound is top-notch. The interactive exhibits are superb for kids. The butterfly house is absolutely amazing. And the outside exhibits are awesome. The tree houses, the boardwalks, the animal exhibits in their outdoor habitat, dinosaur trail, are all excellent. A truly wonderful way to spend a day with the family.

Visiting area for the afternoon and need to wait for a friend to come in at the airport. A pleasant 2 mile walk that was mostly shaded. A great diversion for the afternoon. The best thing about the park is the greenway runs through it. You can ride your bike around the lake and take the greenway back the way you came or you can continue to head north.

Recently redone, enlarged and made safer, there was playground equipment that was innovative and different than any I have seen before. Soft surfaces protect little knees. I was there with my kids and all had a great time. I saw smaller kids also enjoying the facilities. There was ample parking when we were there despite it being a school holiday.

We love this park! So much history to see, gardens, farm animals, adventure backpacks, and an area for children to play. They even have some eggs and veggies set out to take a sample of. I would definitely recommend!! This is a great place for children to play, for families to fish, visit a historic farm, take a hike, travel back in time.

I always bring visitors here on their first trip to Durham in spring, summer, and fall. Nestled in Duke University's campus, its a total escape form the suberbs and downtown areas nearby. We came here with Emily Carol Photography for our engagement photos and loved it! Definitely bring comfortable shoes for gravel pathways, though.

This is a great park that we stumbled upon when we were headed to the 7th street market right across the street. The fountains are so nice! The sculptures and surroundings are gorgeous and fun to play on. The exercise area is great too! The Imaginon is right across the street for kids as well. Great day of fun all in one area!

This was so interesting to us - it is a huge art installation in the middle of an industrial park! We enjoyed seeing the pieces spin around to form a human head....The head is based on a beautiful fountain and as the pieces spin - the water flows over the different sides of the fountain. It is really fun to watch and enjoy.

Super nice park. Many beautiful old trees. Has ball diamond, basketball court, multiple tennis courts with night lights. 6 tennis practice stalls with murals on the outside. There are two sets of playgrounds and many swings. Two outside shelterhouses and another one that is very large and enclosed. There is a beautiful grove of older trees and a pond.

Part of Olentangy Trailways.  Wonderful walkways including through Prairie Reforestation.  Whetstone Park includes the Park of Roses, and the Whetstone Pond.  In front of the park, close to High Street is a playground and a building that hosts community events and classes.  There are also several baseball diamonds and tennis courts.

Very BIG park - 142 acres.  We did not have access to see shelterhouse.  You must make a reservation for the shelterhouse.  Park has nice pond.  On this day the geese and their chicks were making the most of it.  Some picnic tables by the pond.  There is a walking trail (not around the pond) that is alongside Big Walnut Creek.

Nice open sports field west of Kroger in Graceland. No paved walking trails. There are walking trails through the woods that lead down to the river. Amazing old trees. Advisable to use bug repellent and long pants. Did pick up poison ivy somehow.

Nice place with sidewalk around big field park. Has new playground equipment. Shelter house with tables and plenty of trash cans. Two port-a-potties. One is wheelchair accessible. Outdoor basketball & tennis courts. And has rec center.

Columbus.gov indicates there is Conner Park here. There is no "Conner Park" here.
Nice walking loop in park which leads by the creek. There is a playground here - currently under construction. There is port-a-potties here.

A few side trails.  Lots of steps from both Cliffside/Glenmawr and Indianola entrances. Walking slope entrance at 4th & Cliffside.There is a creek through the park. Under Indianola bridge are awesome bird paintings!

Has playground, basketball court & shelterhouse. Best entrance is to park @ Woodspring Dr.  & Willow Park Ct. and use walk-in entrance from the street on Woodspring.  Has small walking loop trail around park.

Part of Olentangy Trailway. Beautiful walk through the woods by the Olentangy River.  Parking at south end of Northmoor park or you can park at Park of Roses and walk South past Prairie Reforestation.
Big walking trail around loops that is not shaded. Has playground and swing sets. Several mega size fields for sports. And a couple hundred geese in parking lot near parking lot and port-a-potty.
Nice park with large open field. Bike station here on way to Camp Chase Trail also the Ohio Erie Trail that goes to Cleveland and Cincinnati. Port-a-potties by parking lot behind wooden screen.
This is a wonderful flowers & other plants park in spring and early summer! Many roses/plants/trees have identification plaques.  Later in summer the park can be pretty hot during the day.
Arch from former downtown train station moved to this park. Nice size park well shaded and plenty of benches. Easy to walk around park. Park is across from Blue Jackets hockey arena.
Nice walk by the river. Has playground and shelter house. BEST place to park is W. Lakeview Ave  & Riverside Dr. There is NO parking at Pacemont, but there is a walk-in entrance.
Very nice walking trails into wooded areas. Another sidewalk trail goes around large field. Nice playground equipment and shelter house. Definitely want to visit again.
Audubon Park is currently closed. There are NO sidewalks and crowded streets 3 sides of park. 4th side is houses.  Nearly got rear ended at 2 stop signs near park.
Very nice multiple playground areas. Has shelterhouse, basketball court with port-a-potty near it. Has several soccer fields. Big walking trail around all of it.
Has walking trail around pond. Had 3 different sets of playground equipment for different ages. Large fields. Has basketball & tennis courts. Off street parking.
New basketball court from Nancy Lieberman charities. There are two tennis courts. Park has a couple playground sets. Some off street parking from 22nd St.
Nice big park with Turtle pond. Definitely mosquitoes through  shaded woods. Good walking trails. Has playground. And nice flushable toilets - yeah!
Big park with walking trail loop. Has playground equipment, tennis & basketball court. Has gazebo with picnic table. Located next to St. Stephens.
Good size square park with walking trail. Has older playground equipment. There are very nice basketball & tennis courts. Portable restroom here.
Large wooded area with some large open areas. There is a playground and picnic tables.  Nice walking trails. There is a large port-a-potty here.
Good size park. One side has water park of sprinklers. Other side of building has a nice playground and a short walking trail. Street parking.
You can see 2,000 lb. bison in the fields. Walking trails on gravel & grass paths. Tends to be windy.

I love a good Park, I enjoy just sitting on a bench and letting the Solitude enfold me and take me to a much more calm and peaceful place. I especially enjoy listening to the leaves rustling in the breeze. If you are wrapped up in the stress of life, it's time to unwrap yourself and go to a park and let nature take you by the hand and lead you to a calmer more peaceful place. This part may not have all the amenities other Parks do, but it's still pretty nice.

This Meadowlake Park is probably the best park in Enid. It has just about everything you could want. There is a golf course to the West, there is a miniature golf course to the east. They have a train that rides around the park, and several rides for the kids. Including a merry-go-round with beautiful horses. There are picnic tables and Pavilions, slides and Teeter totters and swings, and every fourth of July they have the fireworks display here. Come on by.

The 45th Infantry Division was one of General George S Patton's cracked divisions during World War II. He always requested that it be one of his divisions. Here in this Museum you can see all sorts of memorabilia from the divisions role in World War II. Captured Nazi flags and weapons, and ambulance that was used to take injured soldiers to the hospital, and much much more. Tons of weapons and other military equipment.

I have to admit that I am a convert to this place. For years I put off going here, because it was just too low on my priorities. But then my daughter insisted, and am I ever glad she did. The place is absolutely breathtaking, the array of plants is mind-boggling. Come prepared for a lot of humidity, but the beauty of the place is so well worth it. I look forward to returning again and again.

In 1889, a pistol shot was heard, a whistle blew, and tens of thousands of hopeful people raced across the Prairie to stake a claim in what would become Oklahoma territory. This Monument is a memorial of those Brave Pioneers who struggled to establish a home here in Oklahoma. They came from all over the country, and even from foreign countries, hoping to find a place to call home.

Leonardo's was the pet project of mrs. Owen K Garriott, our local astronaut. She spearheaded the drive to build it, and it is a wonderful little Science Museum. It has all kinds of cool things to Fascinate children and adults. Plus there is Adventure Quest, which is a children's playground built entirely of wood where they could spend all day climbing and running and playing.

I love a good Park, And as far as I am concerned no city has enough of them. We all need to be able to escape from the hustle and bustle of daily life. We can't all drive out to the country, but if we can find a nice plant Shady Park or we can sit on a bench and just let the world go by, it helps us recharge our batteries and prepare ourselves to Take On The World again.

I love these small parks in the middle of a bustling City. They provide a great place to get away and escape from the hustle and bustle of City Life, and enjoy a few moments of peace and rest away from all the noise and bustle. They may not have all the amenities you would find in a bigger Park, but the Solitude and the quiet or something worth the well worthwhile.

This is a small one block Square Park, just east of the downtown area. It has some very nice shade trees, as well as some very good tennis courts. I used to go here in the evenings to play tennis with some of my friends. I think I would have enjoyed it a lot more had I been any good at tennis. But oh well I'll just have to settle for a devastating good looks.

This Museum was a labor of love for a lot of old-time railroad workers. It has quite a number of memorabilia items from the old days of fine dining on the railroad. It has a large display of other items as well. Plus, it has a miniature train set up that I would almost be willing to kill for. The cost is free, however they would like a donation as you leave.

Government Springs Park is the oldest Park in Enid, and it is a wonderful place to go for children. There are large tall trees to give plenty of shade for Mom and Dad, there are swings, slides, and other places for kids to play, and there is a lake with an arch bridge over it and a waterfall. I used to go here all the time as a kid and I always loved it.

One thing I like about Oklahoma City, is that it has lots of parks. Big parks small Parks medium-sized Parks Parks everywhere. This is not your biggest park, nor does it have the nicest amenities, but still it is a place in the city to get away from the hustle and bustle of daily life and spend a few moments decompressing and connecting Back To Nature.

Women Pioneers in Flight have been neglected for far too long. It's more than just Amelia Earhart. There are many more women who quietly pursued excellence in flying, design in aircraft, and setting World Records. If you like airplanes, this would be a great place to come and visit. You can see all the exhibits and have a great time with the family.

This is a great place to spend the whole day, looking at all the exhibits, and many of them are hands on. Your kids will love this place, because they can learn so many fascinating new things that they never could new before. The whole family will enjoy it. I have been here several times, and that always and frilled at the things to do here.

If you love trains, like I do, this is a great place to visit. I remember my mother taking me on a train when I was just two or three. Ever since then I've been in love with trains. You can stroll through luxurious club cars, see how the crew lived in the Caboose, and see all of the other displays including an enormous model train set up.

Looking for a wide clear place where you and your kids can fly a kite? This is your place. I love kite flying. It is 8 fun and relaxing activity for the whole family. My kids enjoy flying kites. If you are looking for a good place to take your kids and to spend an hour or two looking at a piece of plastic in the sky, this is your place.

This is a memorial to those who were killed in the Oklahoma City bombing of the Alfred Murrah building. It is an awesome place to go. It is magnificently design, and no expense was spared in making sure it was beautiful. The museum also has a tremendous number of exhibits. If you haven't been there, please go. It will touch your heart.

I enjoy a great park. It doesn't have to have all the amenities that you expect, I enjoy just the peace and quiet and the silence. The feel of the wind in my face, the sound of the leaves as a rustle in the wind, all these help take me back to a better place. If you need a break from the world, this is a great place to go.

If you ever wanted to be a fireman when you were a kid, this is the place for you! You can while away an afternoon looking at all the equipment, the firefighting gear, the clothes, the mass, the helmets, everything a firefighter needs. This is a place you should visit, especially after 9/11.

The Oklahoma History Center is a great place to visit. They have a brand new building now, that is much better than the old one. You can spend hours in here doing research or just looking at the displays. Every time I come here, I discover something new. I think you will enjoy it.

This is a pretty nice art museum. Don't expect to find anything by Leonardo da Vinci or Michelangelo, but it still has some good pieces that I think most people would enjoy. It's a great way to spend a pleasant afternoon browsing through the various displays and Exhibits.

My grandkids love this place. Every time we bring them here, it is a chore to pry them away to go back home. The only reason I didn't give it five stars, is because poor grandpa just can't find enough places to sit down and rest here. Otherwise, it is excellent.

This is an excellent City Park. I've been coming here since I was 5 years old. The zoo is great, and there are lots of activities for families and children. A great place to spend a day relaxing or vigorously playing sports of all kinds.
This is a great park, with lots of activities for kids. There is adequate seating, my only complaint is that there simply aren't any shade trees.
This is a great park, with lots of room for kids to run, and lots of things for them to do.

We love Cheraw State Park!
We have "cabin camped" 5 of the past 6 years and have loved the charm and nature of this gem of a state park. The cabins are of CCC vintage (1930's) but you would not know it because they have been renovated and cared for well. The staff members are personable and knowledgeable.
Our annual kayak trek to the southern end of Lake Juniper is a thrill every time. I love the way open water changes and suddenly we are enveloped by towering Bald Cyprus trees and maybe have a chance to see an Osprey or two. One year my son and I tried to get to the headwaters and it was as if we were real adventurers. Pushing through ever tightening streams, until, I came face to face with a rather large water snake... We decided to turn back then.
The park has nice trails, you might see the beaver or deer. We love the boardwalk at the North end of the lake. Amazing sunsets at the boat ramp!
The cabins are well equipped with nearly everything you need. Just add food! Bring your own propane bottle for the grill if you can as the rental is a little steep.
As of our visit in 2013, the beach is back! Many new benches (some swingers ! ) have been added to enjoy the scenery from.
We usually visit Sunday - Wednesday and have always nearly had the whole Park to ourselves.
Even after seeing the wonders of Alaska and Hawaii, we enjoy our little piece of Heaven a short drive from home.

I love birds! I don't want to hype your expectations, but I can not believe the quantity and diversity of birds in this little piece of bird spotting heaven. On a hot July afternoon (not exactly peak birding time) we saw easily 300 birds. Anhinga, white Ibis, Cormorant, Green Heron, Great Blue Heron, Great Egret, Snowy Egret were just a few I could name. I rate this as my favorite bird watching location. Go!

Very friendly and knowledgeable staff. I'm sure the programs they have for kids are wonderful. Can't wait to go back and hit the kayak trail. I wish they had more information about their offerings available online though.
The Tree Bridge Trail was not as long as I had imagined but, it was way more fun and exciting than I had thought! I can't believe my wife went on it. Way to go girl!

The Villas are awesome! Everything you would want is there...  except gas grill, grilling supplies, lawn chairs for waterside sitting. Don't forget your hammock! Don't expect much from the wifi. Everything else is covered but food. New camper cabins give a spartan opportunity to enjoy this great SC State Park.

Nice to be back open after Covid scare. Bathrooms are indeed open.
Great walking trails. Watch out for Poison ivy which is  creeping at the edge. Great views of the catawba river. Dip your feet and enjoy the shady breezy trails on the summer dog days to cool off. Bring your hammock and your kayak too!

I wasn't sure what to expect, but it was well worth the visit! Ed was extremely informative and really gave us a lot to consider about the importance and production of cotton. The displays are well though out and executed. A nice part of a day trip to the area that might include Lee State Park.

A peculiar, small natural wonder right next to the 485. A short trail leads to large rock formations. It seems the parks dept is warring with graffiti vandals. If you like these rocks, you should visit Hanging Rock Park in SC. It's one of the greatest little know natural wonders of this area.

Cool. Free. Fun. You should stop if you are passing by. A lifetime collection if icons of the past. Show your kids what a record player looked, how Gramma washed her clothes, what kid of toys you had when you were a kid. Lots O' memories. Tons of cool cars too!

The are mountain people and beach people. My wife and I discovered that we are swamp people! A wonderful day trip destination for individuals and families.
Enjoy a boat ride and a nice hike. The staff is especially friendly and helpful. Can't wait to go back.

Small museum with a large gun collection! A Smithsonian level collection of historically significant and military weapons as well as some quirky devices too. Staff was very helpful, knowledgeable and friendly too! They have Dillinger's Tommy gun!!! Wow

A good park. It could use some improvements like better bathrooms and ant hill treatment. Bring bug spray as the mosquitoes can be pretty bad. I love the bald Cypress trees. Hiking might be better in winter months. Didn't see any alligators.

The staff takes pride in their park and it shows. Our cabin was amazing in the attention to detail in the styling. From the furnishings to the handmade local soap, great care for your experience was in practice.  I can't wait to go back!

Great trails! Take a picture of the map at the trail head so you don't get confused as you go. Definitely bring bug spray in warm weather. Giants of the forest and amazing beauty surround you in this boardwalk abundant trail. Hidden gem.

Great South Carolina State Park! So much to see and do. A prisine beach and maritime forest with endless views. A historic lighthouse which is accessible (if you have the stamina). Don't forget the marsh trail and the nature center too!

The grounds are very nice. The swarming mosquitoes were unbearable, even with bug spray. So much nature (snakes) on the nature trail, they had it closed. Staff members were nice and knowledgeable. Visit in cool weather if you can.

Do you love Andy, Barney, Opie and Aunt Bee?
Stop by and see many props and memorable items. See Andy's Sheriff's star. Not too big, but nice to see for a fan of the show. Howard Spraige fans need not come. Black & white rules!

The uphill fight for American independence turned in the Patriot's favor here proving freedom is worth fighting for. Walk in the very place where history was made. Beautiful trails and interpretation and monuments.

A beautiful walk to explore gardens and a black water river on an extensive boardwalk system. You might want bug spray in the heaty seasons. Though our visit in late April was bug free. Bring your camera!

Words can not describe how wonderful this place is.  The staff is exceptional, helpful and knowledgeable about the wildlife and historical significance of the forest. Can't wait visit in other seasons!
Awesome State Park with walking trails a boardwalk and Artesian wells. A wide variety of plants and animals can be seen in this wetland hardwood forest. Unique experience with beautiful scenery.
It's amazing to think that this is what a lot of mature forest in America looked like just a few hundred years ago. Before almost everything was clearcut. Cheers to conservation!

Nice little park. Paved walking trails. Designed with the disabled in mind.
A fenced in dog park area.
Oh, bring your fishing pole too!!
Historic church meticulously restored to its glory. You can get a key at the chamber of commerce in town off the green
Really cute park to chill at. Ducks, geese, turtles and fish to enjoy at the dock. Nice little gem of a park.
Great place for a stroll with your Honey or quality time with the kids. Lots to do in a small space.

The Strand is a great district to visit. So much to see and do. There is a Starbucks of course. There are ice cream parlors, bars, live music, Rocky Mountain Chocolate,  museums, restaurants and so much more. You can walk to the pier and may see huge jellyfish or take a dolphin tour. There is a trolley also than you can ride.  I love the carriage rides that are also informative.  Most of the people are very friendly in the shops. There are great finds. A little helpful fact is that lots of these shops have coupons to the Landrys restaurants for things like priority seating and free appetizers!  Must pay for parking but it is reasonable.

Memorial Park was nice, clean and very quiet. if you are looking for a social distancing place to go, this is one place that you can do that. There are lots of different places where you can sit or just hang out. There are lots of photo opportunities here. There is a nice paved area to park on two sides of the park. They do have handicap parking right near the playground. There is a submarine missile that is there to show a missile from a past war. There is also a memorial marker for someone who had died and was in the military. You will see lots of squirrels and birds. It is a very Serene place to go.

It was a little difficult to find this place based on following the Google Maps directions. It actually took me to the next intersection and then rerouted me as it was not where it said it was. There was a sign though on the road directing where to turn. It is actually not alone. It sits in a retirement community. It was accessible by the parking lot in front of the tennis courts. There's plenty of handicapped parking. There are benches to sit on out there. I love how the county has lists of all those who have died, separated by conflicts/wars.

A great spot on many levels. Its about 45 mins from Missouri City, Tx and about 1 1/2 hrs from Conroe.  It sits off a waterway.  It is easy to spot from the road. Parking was about $7-$8 per car. Most handicapped up close are free. There are lots of restaurants, attractions like rides,  shopping, games and live entertainment.  Some food spots are several Landry's restaurants as its owned by them and a Starbucks.  They do have a Bubba Gumps as Aquarium restaurant.

This park can be entered from several roads. You can see it off 281, Riverside Dr and the neighboring streets. There's a lot of space and parking. They have bathrooms, a playground, grills, seating, ducks, grass to run and play and several small docks. You can see fish if you walk along the edges of the river. Great place to eat lunch, bring the kids, or just relax. The only downside for me was all the gnats flying around as you approach the water.

This park is in a quiet area off FM 2410 in Harker Heights about a mile or two past the high school. There are bathroom facilities, handicap parking, a playground and a track among other things. There are lots of trees at the playground. Many walk with their dogs there. The annual suicide prevention walk has been held here the last three years. The only downside is that the track has a bit of a hill which may not be good for some.

Drove from Killeen here as it's a historical spot. There is not much to see. The sign gives you the history of it. It's a gravel drive but easy to find if you take 281 and FM 2417 I believe. It's very quiet. There will not be anyone else there or maybe one other car. When we went, there was one person but they weren't going to see Deadman's Hole. It is not accessible to wheelchairs.

A great place to take the kids and see sights (science wonders) for all. The parking could be better and more handicapped spots though. There is a play area, train, animals, interactive exhibits and so much more. Gifts shop is available for those who want to take a souvenir!  I recommend going at least once. When we visit from TX, we stop by even though I feel its too pricey.

I like that Conder Park is tucked away in Killeen, but it is not in the best part of town. I wouldn't recommend going at night as there is not enough lighting or any security.  If you go in the daytime though, it is fine. The pond is nice. Kids can do catch-and-release fishing. There is a playground, disc golf area, basketball court, a walking trail and nice field area.

Winderful but somewhat small zoo. Just found it by riding through on the way to OK. Saw this off to the left. It had a park beside/in front of it and was looking at the park and saw the sign for it. It just so happened that that day, everyone got in free. The amount to normally get in though was not much.  There was a small gift shop also that sold mini snacks.

Took the kids after after leaving the resort right down the road. Had never gone here before so decided to just drive down to see what it looked like. It was a beautiful little spot. Great for walking but not much shade. People go there to fish, walk or sight-see. Some were even in the water. Be cautious though as the area can be steep to walk down.

I would have to say it can get very pricey. There are things to do for kids as well as adults. Lots of rides, games and food. It so much prettier at night with everything lit up. They do offer a military discount also. Once you pay, its all you can ride while there that day.

Even though we missed seeing half of the bats take off, it was still a great experience. Had family out of town visiting so to do this with them was fun. There was even an ice cream truck there and electric cabs taking people for rides. Everyone should go at least once.

Really enjoyed going here. You can get a deal if you are military.  Great views also. Kids enjoyed it. Steps lead up to it though which I did not like. Great find. The pictures were actually taken across at the musuem of history but its all close to each other.

I would recommend going here. We visited for basically nothing. They even have a restaurant inside that has nice food and specials.  We had a guide walk us through the museum and told us about some local artists. I enjoyed the visit.

Enjoyed visiting here. Its much more than a ship. There are other things right in front with historic value. The staff is great.  Easy to get to off the parkway. It was not crowded either in case you want to avoid big crowds.

Great place to bring the whole family. There is a lazy river, beach area, bar, place to buy snacks/cooked food. Sometimes like the end of Summer, there is a beach bash with live music. A great deal with fun atmosphere.

So many options in this area for information.  This is one of them. Its right off the road way literally. Just pull off and you'll see it. Very historic area. I loved it as I enjoy learning about history.
Parking is across the street from the museum. There is not a lot to see inside for the price. The only benefit is to see how the soda is made and if you like floats, you do get a free one at the end.
First time coming to any events in Salado. The park has lots of shade. Love the bridge nearby and the stairs leading to the street. The festival was great. Many attendees and lots of food.
A great place to check out. Lots of historical information.  Great place to take the kids. There's a nice restaurant near by also. There were great views and there is a ferry.
Loved going here for Spring break that year. Lots of activities for the kids. The tour of where the astronauts train was nice. It gets very crowded at the space center though.
Loved going here. Found it in a magazine at our hotel. Even though it stormed during the show,  it was still entertaining.  Wish the parking lot was better though.
This place was smaller than expected. They give $5 Military and fire discount. There is a food bar and serves alcohol too. For one ride, it was $22.
A nice quiet museum. It was not crowded so even better. Lots to see. Good parking and other museums are close by.

The Pro Football Hall of Fame honors the best 346 NFL Players and Coaches in NFL history.

The American Professional Football Association, later renamed the
National Football League, was founded in Canton on September 17, 1920.

Must See Exibits:
Hall of Fame Gallery Bronze Bust Room
Lamar Hunt Super Bowl Gallery
The Lombardi Trophy for Super Bowl LV
Super Bowl Championship Ring Collection
Super Bowl Theater
Pro Football Today Gallery
The Hunt/Casterline Pro Football Hall of Fame Card Collection
Hall of Famer Lockers - Class of 2020

The museum houses a diverse permanent collection of more than 61,000 works of art from around the world!

Some of my favorites at the Museum:
Stag at Sharkey's is a (1909) oil painting by George Wesley Bellows.
The Crucifixion of Saint Andrew (1607) is a painting by the Italian Baroque master Caravaggio.
George Washington at the Battle of Princeton (1779) by Charles Willson Peale.
Water Lilies by Claude Monet.
La Vie by Pablo Picasso.
Fifth Avenue by Childe Hassam.
Marilyn x 100 by Andy Warhol.
The Trinity by Laurent Girardin.

Orchids Forever ends on Sunday, April 11th.

Founded in 1930 as the Garden Center of Cleveland.

The centerpiece of the $50 million 2003 expansion is The Eleanor Armstrong Smith Glasshouse, a 17,000 square foot conservatory home to plant and animal life from two separate biomes, the spiny desert of Madagascar and the cloud forest of Costa Rica.

The monument was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1973.

20th president of the United States, serving from March to September 1881.

Memorial dedicated to assassinated President James A. Garfield located in Lake View Cemetery in Cleveland, Ohio.

An observation deck provides views of downtown Cleveland and Lake Erie.

Opened in 1931, Severance Hall was named after patrons John L. Severance and his wife, Elisabeth Huntingdon DeWitt Severance.

The Cleveland Orchestra performs at Severance Hall.

The Grand Foyer is surrounded by marble columns and decorated with papyrus and lotus flower patterns.

The Towpath Trail is located in Cuyahoga Valley National Park and delivers picturesque views of the Cuyahoga River.

Must See Areas In Cuyahoga Valley National Park:
Canal Exploration Center
Frazee House
Boston Mill Visitor Center
Ledges Trail
Brandywine Falls
Station Road Bridge

USS Cod is credited with sinking more than 12 enemy vessels totaling more than 37,000 tons, and damaging another 36,000 tons of enemy shipping. All seven of her war patrols were considered successful and Cod was awarded seven battle stars, for her service in World War II.

The Free Stamp is an outdoor sculpture located in Willard Park. Created by Claes Oldenburg and his wife Coosje van Bruggen, it has been called the "world's largest rubber stamp". The dimensions of the sculpture are 28 ft 10 in (8.79 m) by 26 ft (7.9 m) by 49 ft (15 m).

This is the south end parking lot for Aurora Sunny Lake Park.

Aurora Sunny Lake Park Highlights:
Sand volleyball court
Playground
68 acre fishing lake
Boathouse with row boat and paddle boat rentals
1.8 mile loop paved multipurpose trail

The most iconic waterfall in Cuyahoga Valley National Park.

Brandywine Falls at Cuyahoga Valley National Park is Ohio's tallest waterfall.

An upper and lower level boardwalk provide extensive and precise views of Brandywine Falls.

The upper garden is a tribute to composer Franz Liszt and was dedicated on the anniversary of his birth. The upper level includes a large fountain, and has a expansive balcony overlooking a wooded hill leading to the lower level.
likes: Facilities & Services: Large fountain, Expansive balcony

Fascinating park in downtown Akron.

Muralists El Mac (Miles MacGregor) and Aiseborn, both of Los Angeles, began work on the Civic’s exterior wall facing West Bowery Street overlooking Lock 4 in September.

The interior features two mosaics on the right and left hand walls, and a large stained glass window.

Wade Memorial Chapel was added to the National Register of Historic Places on June 18, 1973.

Longwood Park in Macedonia, Ohio contains:

Fishing Lake & Pier
Hiking Trail

The GE Chandelier is 20 feet in height and adorned with 4,200 crystals.

The Edgewater Beach House is closed for the season.

Adam Run Trail and Spring Hollow Trail are located at Hampton Hills Metro Park.

Adam Run Trail leads to the Top O’ the World.

If you have older children who don't need strollers, then this is a 5 star park. Otherwise, I'm giving it 4 stars because you are forced to share the road with bicyclists and cars. The pathways, which are actually roads, are narrow and cars come barreling towards you constantly. This is especially nerve-wracking if you're pushing a baby in the stroller.

However, there is beautiful scenery off the beaten paths, and lots of paths through the grass and fields away from the cars. There is an awesome playground with tons of cool things to play with. See my pictures.

The azalea garden, which is huge, has a 1 mile walking/jogging/car ride path around in a loop. Blooming season is from April through the end of May, weather depending.

This seems like the place to ride your bike, walk your dog, or play frisbee golf. If you have older children that don't need strollers, then this is great. Or just take the young ones to the playground!

A cheap, fun beach alternative. In this state park you'll find hiking, biking, cabins, boating galore, and a small but fun beach on the lake. The beach is a lot of fun for small children and younger teenagers, and is a lot cheaper and less crowded than Virginia Beach and the Carolinas. It's also tiny, but all the better if you have little ones. There are plenty of shaded picnic areas under trees and on tables near the beach, and the tables have grills nearby. There is also a small snack bar with candy, chips, pizza, hot dogs, ice cream, and the like directly adjacent to the beach. In the same complex, you'll also find a small discovery center with animal pelts, skeletons, live animals, and a little more. There is also an air compressor on site for filling up the inflatables. Very fun and inexpensive beach trip!

This review refers only to the grounds and gardens surrounding the mansion, not the inside of the manor which we didn't get to see. The grounds are beautiful and wonderful kept. There are flowers, herbs, roses, trees, shrubs, and so much more laid out in a wonderful, relaxing space. The views are gorgeous. The outside of the manor is gorgeous. There are paths down to the river below as well, but come to relax and picnic in the shade surrounded by beautiful gardens. Tours of the mansion are available for $7 per person, and a small gift shop is located near the main entrance. There is a decent sized parking lot directly adjacent to everything. Truly a beautiful sight to behold!

An expensive adventure that your toddler will enjoy. As other reviews already mention, the price of admission is very high relative to quality of the exhibits. That's the big downside. On the upside, there is a full day's worth of fun to be had here. The inside parts of the museum are small but have a good variety of activities, especially for toddlers and older children. The butterflies are great. The animal exhibits are most likely going to be boring, since the bears and wolves will be sleeping. The lemurs are okay, but Duke has the real lemur deal. Overall, pricey but fun. A membership would definitely make sense if you live nearby and have kids.

Completely beautiful. You'll find flowers of every color, shape, and size, all arranged in a gorgeous, well-kept array. There are 4 themed gardens, each equally beautiful. There are ponds with fish and frogs, a small farm with chickens, fruits, and vegetables, a lake with ducks, a bird watching station, and much more. The gift shop is actually surprisingly tiny but has some cool items. There's a good amount of shade and benches to relax, and some paths that feel like little secrets. I wish there was more interactive activities for children, and more children-focused play areas in general, but the beauty and the price are hard to beat.

I'm blown away by the research side of this museum, and massively impressed overall. This is really two museums in one: the classic science museum has butterflies, dinosaurs, insects, and the like. This side is small but well-maintained and has a good number of exhibits. Then there is another building attached to this part, and it's filled with laboratories and hands-on activities. These labs include a microbiology lab, a 3D printing lab, am archeology lab, and more. It's fantastic and amazing, and I love it. The museum is also free (other than the theater and another area), with inexpensive membership options.

Very large park with an all ages playground, tennis courts, soccer fields, baseball fields, kickball field, batting cages, and walking/running paths. Tons of green space for lounging, walking the pets/kids, and just enjoying nature. The soccer fields are huge and obviously well cared for. Likewise the baseball fields and tennis courts. The walking paths are asphalt and perfect for learning how to ride a bike. The playground is pretty good, but nothing fancy. Kids will love it, of course. The only downside is that parking can get crazy when there are soccer and baseball games going on.

Beautiful new building with lovely, interesting architecture on the outside and provocative modern art on the inside. You will find three large art galleries, and large auditorium, an outside terrace, lockers and coat storage, plenty of seating inside and out, and Elwood Thompson's Cafe (they serve beer!). Plenty to see, hear, and touch. All for free! It really is a beautiful installation, and we look forward to seeing the collections as they are installed. Definitely worth checking out, and a wonderful addition to the already great museum scene in Richmond.

A small and sparse museum with good content and lots of interesting science on offer. The parking is a hidden gem in the museum district. It's $5 (pay inside!) which gets you a prime parking spot for as long as you want, and the lot was not full even on free Thursdays after Christmas. The museum is on the small side and doesn't have a ton going on. What's there is nice, with interactive exhibits and some good science. The theater/auditorium was a bit disappointing since it just payed tv clips. This is 4 stars on free Thursdays but 3 if you're paying.

Tremendously fun playground with area for all ages, and some very cool swings, gliders, and rockers. It's beautiful, large, and bordered by a small lake and a large community center. There are covered pavilions for picnics and birthday parties. There are so many cool pieces to play with, and several playgrounds, including a sand pit for the littlest ones. A small path surrounding the park is good for light exercise. There is also a basketball court, baseball field, and soccer field directly adjacent to the playgrounds. Absolutely awesome!

Awesome park with multiple playgrounds, walking trails, a lake, and plenty more. This is a well maintained park that is great for the kids, walking the pets, or just enjoying nature. There are several playgrounds--one larger one for young and older kids and two for younger children. There are walking trails around a decent sized lake that are bike and pet friendly.
