Plenty of nature to observe and lots of space to get away. There are several picnic shelters with bbq grills that can be reserved for parties.

Excellent park for toddlers and school-age children! There are paved walking and biking trails all around, plus some short off road trails to explore. The best part are the two playgrounds. One is a conventional affair with a great selection of climbing equipment, slides, spinning things, and so on. The other is a natural playground with wooden see-saws and a really fun slide. There are shelters galore dotting the park and everything is well kept. Overall just a great time...For free!

Hiking, biking, fishing, and lots of playgrounds for the kids. All for free. There are trails running everywhere, most with generous shade provided by trees. A lake supports bass fishing (with limits). Picnic shelters with BBQ grills are everywhere. There are 3 playgrounds: one larger one for bigger kids, a medium sized one for younger kids, and a tiny one for babies. They are all well maintained and fun. You can also find a nice soccer field near the big playground.

A very large and beautifully landscaped oasis for children! There are multiple amazing playgrounds here for children ages 0-12. Tons of interactive equipment, sandboxes, bike trails, and more. The landscaping and art decorating the park is beautiful. There is a trail that connects to a greater greenway and go another playground (ideal for younger kids). Great for bike riding, exploring, and playing. Parents will appreciate the shaded seating and clean bathrooms!

An amazing farm and 200+ year old house which you can view all for free! The house tour was very enjoyable. Every 30 minutes on most afternoons you can enter the house for guided tour. The tour guide was great and very knowledge, and the house is a fantastic period piece filled with antiques. The farm has cows, sheep, horses, and more, and is fun to explore. Lots of great older buildings surround the farm. And everything is totally free. Quite amazing!

Lots of old machinery and mechanical goodies to gander at. Very friendly staff inside the museums. One museum is free, the other costs money per person. On site parking costs money as well, though a ticket to the non free museum covers parking costs. The buildings are well preserved and you could easily spend a nice afternoon exploring the iron works grounds. Tons of walking trails lead away from the grounds and towards the river.

Great place to bring your family. Super crowded on weekends, almost like a zoo. Weekdays are much quieter and nicer for the parents. Lots of activities including making art using paints, colored pencils, etc., water activities both indoor and outdoor (in spring and summer), slides, caves, sandboxes and more. Tons of events during the summer as well, including visits by Sesame Street characters, paw patrol, Daniel tiger, and more.

Large park with lots of gazebos and semi-hidden paths that take you up, down, and around. For older kids, this is a pretty cool park to explore because there are trails going down to other green spaces. For younger kids, there are no playgrounds (there are two nearby, but not in the park) and not much to do. Great for strolling around or walking the pets. Plenty of nice views from on high. After a good rain, bring your mud boots!

A quiet sanctuary on the UNC campus. Completely free to visit, though you will probably pay for metered parking ($1.25 per hour). Serene and green, there are paths in and around the trees and plants. Plenty of benches and seating if you want to relax and observe. Probably not very interesting to children, though. There is a planetarium in the science building directly adjacent to the arboretum. Kids will love that if it's open.

Large park filled with baseball, football, and soccer fields, with walking, jogging, and bike paths connecting everything. Plenty of parking, and plenty of shelters for cookouts and parties. There is at least one small playground that is good for toddlers and older kids. An overall very nice park for taking a stroll, walking the pets, or letting the kids burn off energy.

Beautiful site for remembering those lost in wars past.  Harold is amazingly knowledgeable and friendly, and can help guide your tour. There is a small theatre, gift shop, amphitheatre, outdoor memorial, and much more regarding the history and losses incurred during world war II and our conflicts in Asia and the middle East.

Small but beautiful park in downtown Raleigh. We saw lots of wedding parties taking pictures here, but beyond being a scenic photo spot or a relaxing place to eat lunch, there's not much here. It seems safe enough and had lots of families strolling through on the weekend. Worth a stop if you're walking around in the area.

Great little park with lots of winding trails covering big changes in elevation. Some long sets stairs where you'll find people engaged in intense workouts running up and down them. We saw a big yoga class in session in the flat grassy area at the top of the park. Fantastic vistas of the city of Richmond!

The building, grounds, and art contained within are all gorgeous. Great place to take your family, a date, or just yourself to enjoy the serenity. Motorized carts are available for those unable to easily walk. No backpacks or cups allowed into the collections.

Much smaller than the Richmond central location but still very nice and with lots of things to do. Staff is super friendly and helpful as they always are. Compactness of the museum makes it easy to keep an eye out for the little ones.

Great place to view the downtown sights....but also be aware we do have a homeless population that lives down along the waterfront....and yes the grass is nice to see and walk on .......but just like everywhere else there are some pet owners that just don't care if you step in their dogs excrement!.......Sooooo watch where ya put your feet!....otherwise a wonderful place to spend some time...😀

Really cool that they took the time to fix this area up....and connect it with the area farther down toward the city.
Recently I discovered that the sea lions hang out near here...you can often hear them bellowing along the rivers edge...usually around the dock areas.....would not want to meet one on the river in my kayak...😬...these guys are HUGE!

So cool up here.. Walking around on a old volcano! What's not to love with all the trails... Good parking... Great views... Nice picnicking areas... And fenced in areas to run the energy out of your dog!.... Can't go wrong here! N. W. Side even has a small play ground over across from the vent.... Also b-ball hoops... 😀

Even though it takes a little bit of effort to walk up here ...you most likely will have the place to yourself....and there are lots of well definded walking trails to explore......Go online to the parks deptment to learn more about the history of the park...and how it was once used for a 911call center.

Just love this spot...frequently have pinics here in the summer months....and they do have restrooms here ....and views are just gorgeous!!...sorry didn't get any pics...guess you'll just have to come here yourself....if you can do stairs...it is well worth the short distance down to the falls!!!...😀

What a really cute little place to come play....do note that the restrooms are closed during the winter ......and around the edges of the park are a couple of homeless tents...(as of 11-20-18).... I add the date cause things often change....they could be there then gone then back again!

Love hiking around up here...many places to park...check out Google maps....and the views are wonderful!!... But do try to catch it on a sunny day
There is info center there....just not much info....
Don't know if there are restrooms.

Great little neighborhood park...not very big.....but has little duck pond off to the right...and a few trails that wind through here.... Sometimes it does have homeless issues....so watch yourself for loose or stray dogs.

Like coming here ....but there are lots of dogs here....most of them running freely...so if you have little ones you need to keep an eye out so you don't get run down by over zelous pets burning off some energy.

Just love coming to this little park..also a starting point to go to Elk rock island...lots to see...but BEWARE....there is alot of poison oak here and on the island....so keep the kids on the paths provided.
A must stop along the hwy.....besides the view there is history here...I won't give it away but long...long....looonnggg ago there was a VERY LARGE LANDSLIDE HERE!!....stop in and discover more!!
Really busy little park.. yet still lots of room... I went to the far (last) parking lot around 2pm on a Sunday and found good parking.....the beach area might be a little bit crowded.
What a great place to hang out and stretch your legs and if your up for it you can walk down the path.... Of course the town has many spots to eat...just depends on what you want.
Love to come and watch the swimmers...then take a nice walk around the park....it's quite a large place. ..bathrooms and play ground makes it easier to bring kids of all ages.
Nice little walk thru the neighborhood brought me to this cute little park...its got a couple benches and a couple of picnic tables.....and is next to the gardens.
One of the neatest little historic parks....well hidden from the pubic....great view of the river and the Willamette Falls...there are really cool trails here!
Just a really nice area to walk along the river ....very, very, small parking area....no restrooms...one picnic table...like I said...small!...but really nice!
Love it here....can get a really good look at all the kite-surfers..😛...they can really get moving!...bring a picnic cause you won't want to leave!
Just love it here ...so much to see....yet very relaxing....new bathrooms are a plus!...and I m sure alot of you will like the new boat ramp.
Great place to kick back and have a picnic....or to launch your watercraft...I have seen very large fish swimming back and forth right here!
Love it here....if your tight for money...there is a free day..I just can't remember which day....your will just love it here!##...😃
Just wanted to kick back and relax...found some shade and had me a nice picnic...stayed to walk around..enjoyed the views.
This area never gets old! Just love it here....lots of room to take a walk....or ride a bike....bring the kids!!
Can't wait till the snow melts...and I can find time to come hike the area again....lots of really cool trails!
It not the most scenic park....but the little ones can still run around and burn off their extra energy !!

Great local restaurant, winery and craft brewery!  Really nice selection of brews and wine.  All brewed on site.  Food was very good.  Prices were in line with what you would expect.  Not cheap. But not very expensive.
We were there for the Fall festival and balloon launch.  So the wait to order food was very long.  But again, I was there for a special event.  So that is to be expected.
My only suggestion would be to have a samples line for tasting.  What took so long to order food was people sampling before placing their order.  If on these events they had samples at a separate bar, I think that would have improved the time it took to get to placing my food order.  Again, I was there on a busy weekend.  So I was not expected super fast service!
Only other suggestion (ok, I lied about only one suggestion) would be to have a simple child menu.  Hot dog and drink.  Grilled Cheese and drinks.  Stuff like that.  Hot dog was $6.  But no drink.  Would be nice to throw in soda for the price for kids
Overall great atmosphere to hang out and enjoy some brews and wine.

Another great Summit MetroPark!  We were working on the Fall Hiking Spree and we selected the Redwing trail as we wanted to hike a trail with plenty of shade!  It was a very hot (90 degrees) day and we weren't prepared for a very long hike.
The Tuscarawas area of Firestone MetroPark is where this trail is located.  The trail is rated easy and is 1.1 miles long.  It is mostly level with only one hill.  In fact, if you wanted to bypass the hill you could.  The hill is towards the end of the hike and instead of turning left, you could go straight and walk to the parking lot.  The trail is very scenic and goes along the banks of the Tuscarawas River for a short distance.  Little Turtle Pond is also along this tail.  My son likes the boardwalk section the best.  During the wet seasons, there is usually water under the boardwalk.
The Tuscarawas area includes a shelter, sled hill and picnic areas.  Most of the picnic tables are in shade.  But they are spread out and some would take some walking to get to. In case you are carrying a large cooler.

Fantastic Summit Metro Park!  Liberty Park includes several different areas.
The Nature Center area offers several different hiking trails, a couple of picnic tables (but not a designated picnic area), a shelter house, and a staffed nature center.
Some of the trails are fully paved which would allow hikers of any ability as well as strollers to be taken along.
There is also a nature play area where the kids can play with things made from the fallen trees.
We did the Coyote Run trail and the brand new Black Bear trail.
The Coyote Run trail is fully paved 1.2 miles trail and travels around a large meadow.  Very few spots for shade. So be ready if hiking on a
very hot day!
The Black Bear trail recently opened. It is just over two miles and is completely within the forested area.  It has a few hills to climb, but nothing major.  There are many things to see along this trail. Springs, fallen trees and some large rock formations can be seen.
I really enjoyed the Black Bear trail!

Another wonderful Ohio State Park!  The beauty of Kelleys Island is that most of the island is protected by the state park.  So there are allot of areas of the park open to the public.
That park offers camping, a boat ramp and a beach.  On the interior of the island is an old quarry that has biking, hiking, bird watching, etc.  There is a blue lake in the middle of the quarry.
The town of Kelleys Island has a few bars and restaurants to choose from.  My favorite is the Kelleys Island Winery and the Cantina.  But this is NOT Put In Bay.  So don't come here expecting that bar scene.
Great place to simply relax.  Do some hiking or biking or simply do nothing!  Without the hustle and bustle, you get that "island time" feeling.
Since it is an island, getting to and from it involves the ferry boat.  So additional planning is required.
We have been there for a day trip and a week long camping trip.  And we are already planning another for next year!

Wonderful and well taken care of State Park!
I have camped in probably 30 different state parks in Ohio and West Branch is one of my favorites!  I will admit that Mohican and Hocking Hills are on that list too.
It is getting extremely popular!  I find myself having to reserve a site two months in advance! And if the park has something going on (Halloween), then you can guarantee that it will be 100% full.
Ohio totally rebuilt the park about 12 years ago. All roads were rebuilt. They even rebuilt every shower house.
You can get to the lake from must camp sites easily.  Might involve a hike down a short cliff, but doable.  The campground has it's own boat ramp and beach.
There is a very active volunteer association that really takes great care of the area.
If you are into Mountain biking, there are several bike trails nearby. From beginner to advanced.

Largest park in Stow and has many things to do for the family.  Two shelters that can be reserved. Access to the Summit Metro Parks hike and bike trail.  Basketball courts.  A rental hall with kitchen. Bow Wow Beach the the dogs.  And my favorite, a fantastic playground. In fact, I would rate the park three stars.  But the playground is excellent.  My son loves to play there.
My reason for the four stars are the picnic tables.  They are not well maintained.  Most don't have cooking platforms.  And there are not many of them.  They could use quite a few more picnic tables!  Especially around the playground.
Other than that, there is plenty to do for the family

Really nice campground.  Only about 40 sites.  Most of them have plenty of shade.  The sites are shorter than many of the other State parks I have visited.
The campground is right next to the lake with several sites right next to the lake.
Several docks for those who bring their boats.  But for those of us who didn't.. we can use them to fish from!
The camp store has kayaks and paddle boats to rent.
A very small sandy beach is located within the campground for swimming.
The campground is very well maintained and in my opinion the restrooms and shower house were very clean.
This was our first time here, but now we plan to come here allot more often!

Fantastic Metro Park!  There is quite a lot to do here.  Ball fields, shelters, several hiking trails, a small lake, sled hill, wide open fields as well as a building with two large rooms that can be rented.  And since we are in North East Ohio, the building is heated and can be used is the winter.  We have rented it several times during the winter and enjoyed the sled hill nearby.
There are many picnic tables in several different shaded areas.  Since the park is centrally located, it is a very popular. The Metro Parks do an excellent job maintaining the park.
Great place to take the family for a picnic and some hiking or frisbee!

Very well maintained dog park.  Located on Rock Spring Road at the entrance to West Branch State Park Campground.
Separate areas for small dogs (less than 25 pounds) and large dogs (more than 25 pounds).  The large dog area is considerably larger than the small dog area.  This gives these big guys plenty of room to run around.
There are no facilities or running water.  So be prepared.
There are a couple of picnic tables inside the dog areas.  But other than that, no other places to sit.  Also very little shade.  Area was very clean and well taken care of.
likes: Separate areas for different dog sizes

reviews_attraction.text:
Very nice hike!  A little strenuous due to the hills, but not bad at all.
The falls are falls based on the rainfall.  But no matter what it is still a great hiking trail. The falls are closer to Pleasant Hill Dam.  But you can also park at the covered bridge.
There are two falls along the path.
Definitely worth the time to see.
The entire trail is within the forest.  So even on a hot day you will not be hiking in the direct sun.  But still bring water!  There is no water located at the dam.  There are latrines... but no running water.
dislikes: No running water at the dam

reviews_attraction.text:
Located right off the freeway and parking is located directly across the street.  This is a very popular location.  So the day we visited there was a small line of families waiting to take pictures.  But we only waited about ten minutes.
The view of downtown is great. And a very nice view of the Cuyahoga River too.  There are historical markers nearby pointing out the history of the Voinovich Bridge and a market pointing out all the tall buildings in Cleveland.

Great place to spend a few hours hiking around.  Several trails with different levels of difficulty to choose from.  My son really enjoyed climbing on and under all the different rocks.  One trail has you do some climbing and crawling.
The waterfall is worth the extra effort to get to.  With some extra climbing you can get behind it.
For little kids... there are allot of cliffs... but there is plenty for them to crawl on without going to the top.

I am giving this five stars because the historical significance.  This is the field that the Wright Brothers really learned how to fly and improve their plane.
There are no facilities. So be prepared. It is also wide open, so it can be very hot!
There is a replica of the barn and the catapult that was used. You can also hike the one mile circle path around the field, but there is little to no shade.
Again, five stars for the historical value.

If you can find a better ferry service to Kelleys Island.... Take it!
For being the ONLY choice in ferry service, they do an excellent job!  Very efficient loading and unloading.  For bicyclists and walkers, there is an area for you to sit during the short trip across.
During the peak times they run every thirty minutes. PROMPT!  If you are walking up to the waiting area, they won't wait!  But then it is only A thirty minute wait.

So glad we stopped by to see the USS Cod!
Very well restored WWII submarine.  You really get a feel of what life was like for our brave sailors who served in a submarine.
The volunteers are packed with knowledge.  And several served on it... so they have firsthand knowledge.
Watch your head!  It is a sub... so not a lot of headroom.
My 8 year old son really enjoyed the visit.  And we got to see the Coast Guard pull in to dock!

Great place to take the family!  Even if you are not interested in a canoe trip, there is still plenty to do!
For the river enthusiasts, they have several options.  Canoes, kayaks, tubes and rafts.  Plus two options for how long you want to stay in the river.
Beyond the river they have a huge climbing adventure with several different courses based on skill.  Miniature golf and two go kart track.
I am glad we stopped by!

I really like this trail! It is one of the more strenuous trails in their system as it has a very large hill to climb.  It is also 2.4 miles long, making it one of the longer routes as well.  But the tail is excellently maintained.  The views of the Cuyahoga River are great.  The trail is mostly covered by trees.  But there is a part of the trail that travels along the hill top that is exposed to the sun,.

I would not consider this place a "must" see.  But it is worth visiting.  If you are not going to make the short drive to the Huffman Prairie, then consider visiting the memorial instead
There is a very nice overview of the surrounding area a well as another great museum about the Wright Brothers. If course, this one focuses on their time spent experimenting at the prairie field.

Fantastic Metro Park to explore!  The hiking trails here are great.  Some of the trails are paved, making them accessible to anyone.  You can walk all the way to the lake on a paved trail.
The Glens trail across the street is a very nice hike with great views of the river a well as several overhangs and rocks to explore.
Definitely a great park to spend the afternoon.

Wendy Park is a work in progress!  But it is going to be a great destination!
Cleveland is almost finished expanding the bike path to it.  The bike bridge over the railroad tracks is almost complete.
Add a few more picnic tables... maybe a small pavilion and playground... and the park will be a great destination.
A little bit off the beaten path... but worth a visit.

Very nice short trail with a fantastic view overlooking the Cuyahoga River (which is where the name comes from ;-).
Very easy and flat trail that is paved.  There is a connector trail heading into the valley that will loop back as well.
Almost entirely shaded, so a great trail on hot some days.
This is our favorite metro park trail to hit with the family.

Fantastic restored home.  Volunteers are extremely helpful and knowledgeable.
There are so many things to see in the house.  Love the details in the chandeliers. Some are gas and some are electric.  A few are both!  Plan on about 90 minutes if you go.  That would be plenty of time to see it.
Well worth the visit.  Close to downtown Akron.

Giving it five stars because of the perfect view of Cleveland!  You are looking directly at the heart of downtown.  Parking can be a hassle as you are competing with The Rock Hall... and as it is downtown... parking is not free.  But thankfully the rates were cheap.  $1 for one hour!

Great quiet and secluded campground.  Restrooms (latrines) are kept very clean. Park is is a beautiful forest. Plenty of trails to do.  The park is also a horse campground so my son enjoyed seeing the horses and watching the people ride.
This is is usually not crowded!

Very nice and well maintained park.  Signal Tree is a truly unique and ancient tree with a lot of history.  The Metro Parks have done an excellent job of preserving it.  It is only a short walk from the parking lot.

In the Texas State Park system there are 79 parks where you can RV camp. On a beautiful Spring week end in 2019 we load up Ms V OurV and head east to spend two nights at Martin Creek Lake State Park. This beautiful and scenic Texas State Park is located on the banks of Martin Creek Lake. Travel Due east from Dallas on I30 for about 2 hours and then south from Longview for about 40 miles and you will be smack dab in the wonderful east Texas Piney woods. Martin Creek Lake State Park is just across the lake from a large coal fired power plan and that is the only real draw back due to the constant noise. Martin Creek Lake State Park is an excellent boaters destination thanks to the two boat ramps and huge parking area. If you enjoy fishing then Martin Creek Lake Ste Park is also a great place for you to visit! Come along with me as I tour Martin Creek Lake State Park!

I LOVED IT! I did not plan on riding the train I just wanted to shoot some video of the train for my video about visiting Beavers Bend State Park on my YouTube Channel, Dude RV,  but when I saw how happy everyone was when they were getting off of the train I just had to go for a ride! It really took me back to my childhood! The staff was so friendly and helpful! Please note that this is not a paid endorsement, this is my own personal opinion, It was fun and I enjoyed it!
The YouTube video I created was an independent production and not a paid production.

It is so very sad that the great state of Texas chose to relinquish the fantastic piece of history. Built by the CCC in the 1930s this recreation of the original does such a great job of telling the story of early Texas settlers.
The current management has added RV connections and hotel type rooms to support recreations and rallys.
The rooms are in two different WWII POW barracks that were saved and repurposed.
You can even stay in a well restored 1800 home!
I have some footage of my visit on my Fort Parker State Park video on my YouTube...DudeRV.com

What a beautiful hidden gem! We ended up camping here because our state park reservation was bumped for a scheduled deer hunt. I am so very glad! I had no ides this campground even existed! Our visit was on Jan2 2021 and co-insided with a cold rain but never the less we really liked this campground! I look forward to a return visit when the sun is shinning and I can do some fishing on the lake! I have posted videos of our visit on my YouTube...DudeRV.com

We were there at the wrong time! Jan 1 2021. Cold, rainy and so very windy! Please remember that there are no showers or flush toilets. Also there is no dump station for your RV. I was very surprised by the freaking huge mosquitos that would swarm me when I found shelter from the strong wind. needless to say we did not enjoy our visit. I am not sure I can talk the wife into going back. I have posted a video of our short visit on my YouTube...DudeRV.com

We were so excited about visiting Beavers Bend! We had heard so many people say so many great things. What we found was a beautiful park that was badly in need of updating. The facilities were not up to the task of the huge crowds. Every where we went there were long lines of cars and people.
The park was beautiful but the experience was not, we will not return to this one. I have posted videos of our visit on my YouTube...DudeRV.com

I have mobility issues and rely on a scooter to get around most of the time and this makes getting out into the "woods" a real challenge. The Randy Bell trail is amazing! It is only a little over 2 miles but the scenery is so beautiful and the wildlife was just incredible! I highly recommend this trail to anyone but especially those who rely on a mobility devise! I have a video of the complete trail on my Youube channel...DudeRV.com

I have always loved this State Park. I was very sad to learn that the Old Fort Parker Reconstruction is no longer a part of the State Park. So much history there!
I enjoyed fishing from the pier and watching all of the birds in the woods. The handicap accessible trail to the bird blind is in need of some work but I was able to get my scooter all the way back to the blind.
I have a video of my last visit on my YouTube...DudeRV.com

This is a nice little Texas State Park with a beautiful little spring fed lake as the center piece. It is a great park for family camping. The main draw back is the limestone mining opperation on the SW side of the park. When the wind is blowing from that direction, moswt of the summer, there is a dust cloud that blow across the park. If you have breathing issues this could be very bad. Other than that, the park is great!

What a quaint little Stte Park! The campsites are a bit tight but everything else is wonderful! Our visit was in Dec of 2019. We spent one night on our way south. We enjoyed visiting the town of Blanco as well as strolling along the river. The restrooms were very clean. I really enjoyed exploring the constructs of the CCC. I have posted videos about our visit on my YouTube... DudeRV.com

What a great little Texas State Park! I dont play golf but if I did my visit would have included a 9 hole round! There is not a whole lot going on in this park besides golf hiking and the swimming pool.  My site was so level ! the sream that flows through the park offers up the possibility of catching a fish or two.
I have posted a video tour of the park on my YouTube.... DudeRV.com
dislikes: Limited activities (besides golf, hiking, and swimming)

reviews_attraction.text: What a great Texas State Park! Everything you want in a great state park! I really enjoyed the huge aluminum fishing pier! The 30 amp campsites were a little on the tight side but they were all pull-throughs. I did not catch any fish but a couple of the locals said they catch a whole lot of fish here. I have posted a video of my visit on my YouTube....DudRV.com

Not one of my favorite Texas State Parks mostly because of the very low water level. The park facilities seem to be suffering from neglect due to lack of use. I was surprised to find a spacious recreation facility in the park and very disappointed that I could not really get to the water in the lake. I have posted videos of my visit on my YouTube...DudeRV.com

WOW! We were really surprised by this little Texas State Park! Our campsite was a little tight but it was level, shaded and private. The day use area was not very handicap friendly and was not too accessible for me but I really liked this park and our visit to the Big Thicket Preserve. I have posted videos of our visit on my YouTube ...DudeRV.com

What a nice surprise at the end of the world, I mean Texas! LOL. here you will learn a lot of history about the importance of the Sabine Pass during four different times of war. I was very impressed by the phone tour and encourage everyone to take advantage of the resource. I have a video of this park on my YouTube...DudeRV.com

Here is where it all started for the Republic of Texas, this is also where one of the tradgeys of the Texas war for independence occurred, the slaughter of Col. Fannin and his men. Remember Goliad! Remember La Bahia! I have a video of this incredible place on my YouTube...DudeRV.com

What a beautiful place to RV camp! We were camped down by the river and came up here to see what the RV sites were like and really wished we had been camping here! Next time we come back this is where we will camp! You can see driving tour videos of this on my YouTube...DudeRV.com

What an excellent restoration of the mission! The park staff is very friendly and helpful. If you enjoy exploring history then this is a must see! I have some video footage of the mission in my Goliad State Park video on my YouTube Channel...DudeRV.com

I camped in RV site #6. This is a nice little park! the lake is beautiful. My visit was during a heavy rain system so the primitive side of the lake was closed off due to high weather. I really enjoyed staying here and look forward to a return visit.

I was unable to visit due to the migran triggered by the cologne being worn by the guy who was collecting the $20.00 per person entry fee. I did get  picture of the resident Bison, he was very spoiled.
I can only go four stars because it was closed due to flooding and we did not get to swim. Lots of history here though. I can imagine that this is a great place to cool off on a hot summers day.
dislikes: Facilities & Services: Closed due to flooding

reviews_attraction.text: some of the most mind blowing wood craft I have ever seen! My pictures sure dont do this justice! You just have to see it to know what I am talking about.
A fantastic view of the canyon! Our visit was during a heavy rain storm so we had the opportunity to see how the canyon was actually created! LOL
Closed on Sunday afternoons, bummer! I did get to look in the window and that really made me want to come back and visit!
I cant give it 5 stars because they dont want RVs in the park and it was difficult to access the water.

Wow! Great experience! We hiked above ground first, all the way to the north entrance of the upper cave. We entered and followed the cave south. The majority of people do it the opposite direction and we were told our way was the more difficult route. It wasn't bad. Bring a headlamp, flashlight, good boots, gloves, and maybe a light jacket. It was very packed on the Saturday afternoon we went but we lucked out on front row parking. You'll need a forest pass to park or you can buy a day pass there.

A wonderful hike with great views of the Columbia River Gorge. So many wild flowers in early spring! This is a pretty tough hike, so be prepared. There's also a permit requirement to hike on weekends during the summer AND an additional parking fee on top of that. Parking lot fills immediately. We went on a non-holiday Monday and the lot was full at 11am. Shuttle service is provided at times. Search Google for more info.

On the way home from a different state park we decided to stop by here and check it out. Glad we did! This park is pretty big, with lots to do. Some of the things we saw: a beach, tennis courts, horseshoes, and lots of trails throughout. The tent site camping is on a peninsula, quite a walk down but they provide wheel barrows to haul your equipment in, and it's beautiful down there. We'll be going back soon!

This is a fantastic little hike! Read up on the history of the place, as it's pretty interesting. Besides the trail on the rock, there's other things to see and do within the state park. Be careful when parking since it's right along the busy highway. And make sure you have a Discover Pass, the park ranger was out writing tickets when we left.

Great place to stretch and get some fresh air. The trail goes back into the refuge quite a ways. The further back you go, the more quiet and peaceful it becomes. There's lots of birds out here, and bird watchers who seemed very excited to find whatever they were looking for. We also saw deer way off in the distance.

Glad we stopped here! There's a lot of signage with interesting history of the area. The views of the Columbia River are wonderful. If you look across the way you'll be able to spot the Ginkgo Petrified Forest State Park and it's interpretive center, that's a must see once you cross the bridge!

The park offers lots of open space areas, access to the beach, a playground, camping opportunities, and more. The nearby factory (or whatever it is) is a bit loud when you're down at the water. On a clear day you can see across the water to the Olympics, great for photos.

Very small state park with a very short hiking trail. Campgrounds are available here but they're right next to the busy and noisy highway. We hiked the short trail and that was it. Be careful on the trail's bridges, very slippery when wet.

Wow! This is one of the top 5 hikes I've been on. The 360 degree views from here are spectacular! Make sure you choose a clear day when doing this hike. The old lookout is pretty neat to explore and photograph. Be careful of the cliffs!

For being in such a dry part of the state, this park is very nice. Lots of large grassy fields, the tent sites have plenty of grass, and there's a trail that leads over to the river. And lots of trees to keep you shaded from the sun.

Nice state park to stop off at on your way to Mt. Rainier. There's a good loop trail, interpretive center, and restrooms. Only bad thing is it's right next to the busy highway so you hear vehicles passing by.
What's not to love about a National Park? 3 campgrounds, 2 main visitor centers, lots of trails, open year round with amazing snowshoeing opportunities, and more! Get a yearly pass to save money.
Pretty nice place. We had to backtrack to here from Staircase for one night since the camping there was all full. We had a peaceful stream of water running next to our site.
Beautiful beach that everyone should visit at least once! Since there is no drive to it, and it requires a hour long hike in, it wasn't that crowded when we visited.
We didn't make it to Col Bob Peak due to snow at the upper elevations. Very tough hike, steep! Great workout. Good amount of parking at trailhead with a bathroom.
The historical aspect of this castle is interesting, but that's about it. It's overpriced to stay the night in. The rest of the park is a great place to explore.
We stopped to check the place out while heading home from Bridgeport State Park. Looks like a great place to camp next time! Make sure to find Abe while here 😃
Amazing views! A minor annoyance is that you don't get to go outside at all. So the glass windows make it difficult to take some photos. Still worth it!
Great lake with a nice trail going around it. The additional trail was also a pretty good one. Well, except for the clear cut section it went through.
Pretty large state park with plenty of trails and open spaces. Check out the old cemetery; it's a very short walk from the main parking area.
Unreal views from here! There's so many hiking trails and a lot of information at the visitors center. Well worth the long drive out there.
Amazing place with a lot of history, hidden in the woods. Park down at the sculpture park and walk to the trailhead from there.
Open daily and free for all. Amazing that there's a National Park inside of a small building. Lots of history here.
This park doesn't look like much from the parking lot, but once you start on the trail it's pretty nice.
Lots of wildlife to see here. After walking a mile or so out we could still hear the noise of traffic.

Another great harvest festival at HVP, this year it was also a Oktoberfest. Got some cool free pumpkins. 🍊🎃This is one of our favorite parks,we live in Portland, and it is a quick drive right up Foster road. It has it all. 3 play structures for multiple ages. Splash pad. Picnic tables. Skate park. Tennis courts. A nice loop nature walk with a pond with ducks. A rec. Mobile comes weekly in the summer. They have summer concerts. And they have a annual Fourth of July celebration, beginning in the morning with a nature walk,then a parade, a all day event with food venders, music,rides,crafts,giveaways, ect.. concluding with a firework show.

Love this place. We have been going here for years. Good for all kid ages. Water slides, wave pool, diving boards, regular pool,and kiddy pool area. They rent out tubes for a low fee. We get there early and get in line for we can have a table to hang out at during the swim lesson. We bring our own snacks, but they have a snack bar to. Bring a water bottle  for the session,it gets warm in there. We always go during the week,so it is not crazy busy at all,  I assume it is madness on the weekend. The prices are reasonable. For a water park. Only drawback is if your not a resident in the area, the price is higher.

I enjoyed coming here, we parked in some public parking near a medical center off Sunnyside.  I didn't even know w there was a lot or bathroom, I must of been shown by my friend a different side if the park. Starting the hike we saw several deer, just hanging out under the trees. Most of the hike we didn't see a soul. Towards the end on another side we saw a couple people. I didn't know dogs weren't allowed. I agree on that point,it was very quiet and peaceful. The deer were still hanging out when we left.😁

Nice little place for a picnic by the river. Little parking lot. By the house there is a picnic table by the river. Walk down the path and there is a trail down to the waters edge. Connects to other trail system, to a park and playground. Lots of wildlife,including deer sightings. During the winter holiday,it is a great walk,especially for young kiddos. They light up the forest, and have a hunt for the kids. Great year round walking park.

We loved this little local park with a lovely beach. Sheltered by the Jetty and cliffs, so not windy at all. Great beach access, with plenty of easy parking. Great waves, good for body boarding. Cool driftwood and fun place to make a sand castle. We saw people fishing off the Jetty and on the shore. Tip, cool pond nearby with natural wildlife. Our favorite place to go to the beach.

We go here every year, during blackberry season. We pick so much blackberries  they are seemingly endless. And they're so good. We have never seen anyone else here picking, I am not sure why,but I am sure they do. We freeze them and have berries all year long. They make the best jam. Please go, and pass on this place for picking. I hate to see the berries t rotting on the bushes.

Nice place to spend the day. Nice nature trails,picnic tables, and water views. You can even fish. I have seen people swimming,but no thanks for myself, I don't swim in the Willamette river. Walk the little bridge over to the island. Great place for picking berries,so bring your basket. There are maps by the parking lot. There are also biking paths.

This is a wonderful place to visit, so many choices of things to do. A nature walk, a light home, a connection to hard hike. Playground for the young ones. Picnic spots galore. Fish viewing area. And our favorite swimming hole around. Tip, go early for swimming, it goes into shade around early afternoon. And being your debit for day use fee.

We really enjoyed our stop here. Helpful information, clean bathrooms, beautiful views outside the center. Nice nature trails. We decided to spend the day here on the beach. It has a small creek or river that flows into the ocean, you take your floaty into the creek and take a ride into the ocean,fun.

If your in the area you have to take the time and stop here. I know many of you have driven by and said to yourself we must go here some day. Do it😁. It is a great place for kids and adults alike. Kids under 10 are free. Very educational and fun. We loved the history. A surprise awaits upstairs.🐒🐒🐆🐆

This place is awesome. If you have the time you have to go here. They have several hikes to choose from. One that goes to a bog. A ocean one. A lake one. A river one. All awesome. The center has rabbits running all around outside. Plenty of parking, also trailhead parking. Also a bathroom.

Great place. Worth the time and money. Adults only 3 dollars. Children free. Great location in a cool town on a great scenic drive. Friendly staff. Great place to view seals in the boat basin. Awesome. Tip, borrow the magnifying glass to attach to the camera on your phone.

I have mixed feelings about this place, but I won't get into those. They are there and I am only rating our experience. My kid loved it. Got to pet many animals including a baby bear and a wild cat. Cool animals. Reasonably priced. Cool shirts in the gift shop.

We loved this place. If you have the time and love local history, this is a must stop. Free for kids, adults only 3 dollers. Tip, free on Sundays. Definitely do the scavenger hunt. The gift shop is wonderful. We enjoyed our time in this great museum.

We loved our experience here. A cool place in a natural setting. It should be called Prehistoric Forest. Very cool place. Reasonably priced. The gift shop was overpriced, and I am used to the high price of gift shops. We had a great time here.

We really enjoyed our experience here, worth the time and money. Fun time for all. Enjoyed the history. Take the time to watch the video. A cool and reasonably priced gift shop. The best gift shop in the area.

Love this hiking area, love the close proximity to the city,but seems a world away. Love that it connects to other trails, so you can do in and out or a loop. Pretty and a nice retreat from the heat in summer.
It a time of social distancing, we need to be socially responsible,the people and business owners are NOT.  But the view is great. And in the past the center and boat rides were wonderful.
My child went here on a field trip. She had fun. It would of been 4 stars, but she said she should of brought googles, she didn't want the nasty Willamette river water in her eyes.
Great beach. A nice beach access, if you don't mind steps. A cool overlook. Easy parking. A very cool nature walk. We enjoyed our time here. Also called Coquille Point.
We love going here for a pretty and easy stroll on a non-rainy day. Relaxing and peaceful. Free in off season. They also have free times during the season.🐹🐌🌳🌾
We loved visiting this park and play structure. Had it to ourselves for a picnic and  playing on the structure. Close to the  campground we were staying at.
We like this little walk in the city. Easy parking in ample lot. Love that it connects to a loop walk near the pond. Plenty of wildlife to spot,even deer.
We love this spot out of the city. Bring a picnic,they have tables. Take a short or long walk. Your choice of trails. Pretty forest.
We loved visiting this museum. Awesome displays,and fun activities. We loved the Morse code exhibit. Great views. Fun fun fun.

You park off the road, and walk on a boardwalk towards the coastal mountain you climb. There lies a valley, usually with a herd of grazing elk that doesn't seem fazed by humans. Although last time we hiked this, they were up by the summit! Anyhow, you continue beside the road until it becomes an actual trail. This is where is climbs steadily. The section is muddy, bug infested,  and trees close you in so the air is thick. 1/3 of this hike you will dodge tree roots and poison ivy. Cross the 3rd bridge and you will come upon a clearing on the southside of cascade head's base. The view makes the effort and sweat  worth it. Continue alongside the mountain until it curves right and stop for a rest. There's a 600 foot steep drop off overlooking a cove to the right, and to the left in the distance is God's thumb, and a river emptying into the Pacific. It will take your breath away. This is the best view on the whole hike. If you dare, continue STRAIGHT up 500 feet to the actual summit through thick tall grass on switchbacks until you see a small marker in the ground saying you made it. The final 1/3 is the hardest part. Enjoy!

The first time we visited, we went the wrong way. Instead of driving to the trailhead parking lot, we drove down the road to the East of the trailhead parking lot. It was a decomissioned forest road that becomes barricaded about a half mile down so we got out and walked about 2 miles before it dead ended on a cliff overlooking the 26 that we just came from. Although a waste of time, the section of abandoned road was an adventure itself to see nature take it back. People even set up a make-shift skate park back there. Sections of it had been blasted back to gravel and you must bushwack some sections. The second time we visited, we went to the correct parking area that is well marked and completed the trail which is short and pretty. The falls are beautiful. Also drive to Sahale Falls and look at them from your car!

This is the 172nd Oregon waterfall I have visited this year, and I'm glad I put it off so long... because they is MASSIVE. It's basically three waterfalls in one. Make sure to also see Elk Creek Falls... and the massive road-side waterfall just 0.1 miles from this trailhead as well. In the Winter, go all the way down to the base of the falls and see the power up close. It was raging and mist hits you in the face. Although just half a mile... the hike back up is a workout of it's own. Well worth it! (Side note, this is the 1st falls I visited where google maps completely crapped out on me. And I have been in some REALLY rural areas.)

Kentucky falls are very pretty, and you can scramble right up to them! Depending on the season, there are two different waterfalls next to each other making a perfect photo opportunity! Beware, the drive here is pothole infested gravel, and you will be on a cliff about 2/3 of the drive. High clearance vehicle strongly recommended. The first time I got lost trying to find the falls and ended up on a logging road that hadn't been driven in years, ontop of a mountain with grass taking back the road. Make sure you use GPS before entering the coastal mountains maze of forest roads, and be prepared.

WARNING: If you visit, do NOT take Goodman Creek Road.. it is horrible. Instead take EAGLES REST ROAD from the other side... which is perfectly paved and smooth. People don't know this, and they continue ruining their vehicles. Smooth easy trail about 2/3rd of way. After the switchbacks, your at the summit. There are 2 short cut switchbacks that make it shorter if you choose. There is not 360 views at the top, but atleast 200 degrees of view. Thats the only reason I'm giving 4 stars. Still beautiful and worth the drive. (Also, BRING BEAR SPRAY. Oregon has more bears than CANADA.)

Easily one of the top 5 of the 150 Oregon waterfalls I have seen. The hike itself is a adventure, you drive down a pothole ridden gravel road on cliffs until you see the trailhead sign on the left. Then hike straight on the trail until you reach the ropes you have to use to assist you on your decent down to the river, then walk left along the river until your breath is taken away by the beauty of these secluded falls. Moderate hike, if in good shape. High clearance vehicle recommended, this is one of the worst forest roads ever.

This is a very scenic and unique waterfall located right off the road. I have seen over 200 in Oregon and this is easily in my top 20. There are 2 tiers, and a trail leading up to the top tier on the right. Be careful climbing the big boulders to get to the top as to not disturb the earth, or slip and fall. Beware, the road here is ROUGH. There is no avoiding the potholes, there are too many.

One of the most beautiful waterfalls in the state of Oregon. The hike is less than a mile, and goes along the Umpqua River. The first time I visited, I made the decision to move to this state from Texas. So this waterfall is very special to me. Must see on your roadtrip! Also nearby, check out Umpqua hot springs, columnar/suprise falls, and the many other waterfalls of Umpqua National forest!

I honestly don't even want to leave a review, because flocks of tourists will take this place over. But, it's absolutely beautiful. The falls are interactive, so you can climb all around them. Make sure to keep going past the lower falls on the trail to the right, for the upper tier. If you're a waterfall collector... there are about 50 hidden waterfalls within a 10 mile radius of here.

One of my favorite Oregon hikes. There is a bench at the tiny summit you can celebrate and crack a beer at with your friends! Wear good shoes for this one because one slip can cause a pretty bad boo boo! About 6 miles round trip. A MUST SEE on anyone's bucket list! Pretty difficult even if your in shape, so don't bring Grandma! unless Grandma is a avid hiker!!

I love these falls because they are less crowded than the nearby Opal Pools. I recommend taking it slow because the gravel road there is pothole infested and bumpy. The trailhead is short, and the waterfall is massive. Next to the cascade is an abandoned mine you can enter about 15 foot deep into before hitting a locked gate. Enjoy!

These falls are spectacular and are less known than the nearby attractions to the west. Tip, if you want to see these falls, then hike from Cabin Creek Falls, all the way to Lancaster falls for an epic view of the Gorge! Easy hike too! In my opinion, this is one of the top 5 waterfalls in the gorge.

Beautiful secluded drive down a gravel road to get here. Some construction going on when i visited. The hike itself is not hard and the falls are stunning. The flow is very powerful year round and getting pictures is very difficult as the mist blows DIRECTLY your way at the end of the trail.

This forest is home to some BEAUTIFUL Oregon landmarks. Speed limit 65. Check out the sisters, Mt.Jefferson, Diamond peak, the Coffin Mountain lookout, Gold butte lookout, Salt creek Falls, Diamond Creek Falls, etc. You can spend weeks here and not cover everything!

These are a very pretty set of falls. Lower bridge creek dumps directly into the river, while Upper Bridge Creek is just 500 feet upstream. There is a nice trail leading to them and above. You'll have to cross the highway for the upper ones.

Rating 3 for now because of the poor road maintenance (I'm going to help clear some of the brush encroaching on the road) and also because I was unable to see the main falls. The trail I followed ended at the lower tier of these.

This observatory is made out of natural rock in the middle of a lava field that looks like your on Mars. The lookout has holes in the walls facing each mountain, and on the top deck is an arrow reference to each mountain.
Beautiful rainforest, huge snowcapped mountains, and rugged coast, this secluded corner of Washington is well worth the drive! Chech out the Hoh rainforest, hurricane Ridge, the town of Forks, etc!
Serene little park off the highway before Detroit Lake. There is a mile long trail that takes you down the river. Look across the river for Sevenmile Creek Falls! The hike back up is a bit steep.
My favorite Washington Waterfall! The drive itself has endless views of Eastern Washington's rolling hills and countryside. You can view the falls from a platform just steps from the parking lot!
The tallest waterfall in the Oregon coastal range. It towers over the trail as you hike through the forest. Very short hike, and some people go past the end of the trail to get a closer look.
Beautiful, secluded waterfall in the tygh valley.  The old dam is a bonus to see and the trail is short, ending not far from the parking lot. Well worth the scenic drive as well!
Beautiful 0.5 mile loop trail that takes you on a boardwalk through the Pained Hills. Easy for all skill levels with informative signs along the way!
A must see on your roadtrip through the Columbia River Gorge! Beautiful vista house with endless views of Mt. Hood and beyond!
A not very crowded hike through a windy trail along a set of pretty rapids! Nice little getaway from Bend!

Wonderful state park.  This was our first visit here, as we were from out of state and didn't have a parks pass or the cash, we were able to call a number and purchase a day pass.   The seminary is being turned into a lodge, so you cannot tour through it at this time. There is information on the transformation of the property, along the fence that surrounds the seminary and when it will be open.  You can also visit the website for more details.    We didn't hear any construction noise while we were visiting, yet they were all actively working.   The walk down to the water is quite the climb but well worth it.   There is a large play structure for kids and plenty of walkways to amble along.

We stumbled upon this beautiful park and equestrian facility.  Also a lovely place to walk around.  Everyone was so respectful and kind and seemed to take pride in the property.   There are places to sit and even picnic tables for dining.  Good to read the board before hiking on one of the trails, lots of helpful information posted there.    They have a website that lists all the horse events throughout the year.   A beautiful little oasis right outside the city.

We had a family event at the Lion's Shelter where we ate at this 93' long table.   This shelter area is handicapped accessible and has restrooms, several barbeques and a covered sink and eating area.  Avery Park is a stunning park with lots of open grass areas, a train engine and dinosaur bones.  The Rose Garden is beautiful as well.  Park is easy to get to either from south town or right off the highway by Oregon State University.

What an incredible location.  The lighthouse wasn't open as it is waiting for an inspection by the county on work that had just been completed.  The gravel road up to the lighthouse is  handicapped/powerchiar accessible.  The views are stunning all along the way.  There were a couple Oregon State Parks volunteers, up at the lighthouse,  they were happy to share the  history and chit chat.

What a beautiful park, right on the water.   Lovely trails, a children's play area, restrooms, handicapped accessible outhouses, picnic tables and so much more.  There is quite the steep, paved viewing platform, over the water.   Parking by the water can be challenging as there aren't a lot of spots.   Plenty of parking throughout the park.

What a splendid area to take a walk.  There are several trails, the one with the waterfalls is handicapped/power chair accessible.   Lots of photo opportunities, wildflowers,  listening to trains being hooked up in the background and the beautiful waterfalls.

Wonderful park.  Play structures for kids, a paved, fully accessible walkway, natural area, skate board park and and benches to sit on.  Plus there is a couple covered area with tables for picnics. Great place to take a stroll.    Restroom is an outhouse.

Beautiful location for a walk or sit and take in all the beautiful scenery.  The water lilies are beautiful throughout the year.  If your lucky the frogs will either be sitting on the logs or the water lilies themselves.
What a beautiful location.   The boat ramp is frequently used.  There is car parking nearby to walk around the area.   The bridge is stunning from many angles.  A very popular park in the summertime.
Simply stunning gem in Seattle.    A peaceful, tranquil location to take a walk, watch the koi and look at the well maintained landscape.  We hit peak fall season on our visit.
Very nice updates to the entrance.   We appreciated the shuttle to the top of the garden.   Prices, to see the garden, seemed a tad steep.  Don't forget to pay for parking.
Beautiful park!  If you have kids their is a playground for them.  Nice place to walk and look at the Willamette River.    There is food nearby as well as frozen yogurt.
Take a step back in time in this cozy church in a very small town.   The yard is beautifully maintained,  so many flowers in the summertime.   A peaceful place to visit.
High tide,  big waves and the seawall, winters the best time of year to visit Depot Bay.   If you don't want to get soaked don't stand near the seawall and blow holes.
A wonderful natural area.  Parking is a little limited, best to get there early in the morning.    There is a handicapped accessible paved path.  Restrooms available.
Our first visit here and what a great time we had.  Wonderfully quiet, handicapped accessible trails.  Such beautiful scenery.   We highly recommend this Arboretum.
A wonderful park right on the water.   Many places to sit to take in all the awesome scenery.   There are accessible areas to get you close to the water.
Great storm watching location. The wind blowing through the tall tower is quite relaxing.   Signs indicate a portable toilet will be in place soon.
Beautiful place to walk or put your boat onto the river.  There is also a fenced dog park.  Pay to park with easy to use parking kiosk machines.
What a beautiful location to visit.  Even though it is in a neighborhood it was very quiet.   It is a short drive, off I-5, in Cottage Grove.
What a wonderful,  accidental find.  Beautifully maintained property, plenty of places to sit and watch the fish navigate the ladder.
Wonderful place to take a walk.  Many trails to choose from, each having their own great scenery.  Beautiful at anytime of the year.
Beautiful area to watch a fall sunrise from.  There are little pull out spots off the highway to take in the scenery of the lake.
What a lovely park with many places to walk, sit or take photographs.   The Conservancy is a great place to check out too.
The boardwalk is wide enough for a person in a power chair, wheelchair or mobility device to have access to the park.

A beautiful escape from the suburb that surrounds it.  I love St. Edward St Park's trails, as it allows you to adjust the difficulty of your walk.  Each trail is clearly marked with the difficulty so if I am taking my old dog with me I can stick to the easy or moderate trails or can do the difficult ones when it is just me.  The grounds and trails are well kept up.

I finally visited and wonder why I haven't gone before. It is beautiful and spans several of Chihuly's styles.  Definitely bring your camera as some of the pieces are too amazing to forget.  It has a great gift shop as well at the end and there are glass blowing demonstrations outside.

Easy layout. Lots of table and machine options in the casino itself.  I got to go the last time to a concert and it was held in a wonderful large ballroom that was perfect for the event.  Parking is via valet as well as self park in a lot and a parking garage so it is ample.

This is a huge community park.  i use the large 3 section dog park, but it also has play fields and volley ball pits and a community center of some kind.  The landscaping is nice and well maintained, and there is now ample parking even during games.

Park has a ice small parking lot.  Trails are a mix of paved with picnic tables as well as dirt paths through the forest.  many of the paths dead end but it is fun for short walks and there are lots of creek access points.

A really fun tucked away park in Kenmore. It has a large playground area and some good walking spaces. Lots of open grass as well as the famed rhododendrons. Definitely visit in the spring when you can.
I liked this museum it covered all of Johnny Cash's life both the good and the bad. I liked the section where you could hear his music on vinyl, cassette, cd and digital that was really interesting.
It seems pretty well maintained, but I walked for over a mile and it was simply uphill, so not as beautiful and interesting as i like for my hikes,  The parking space is very nice though.
A great spot for a quick stop/picnic.  I stopped to walk my dog during a drive to Lake Wenatachee and it was perfect.  Lots of parking in 2 areas.  We wandered along the water as well.
Lots of trails and it feels so far from the city but is minutes from the freeway. It is designed for horses but is easy to use for all. I will definitely go back to explore more.
A wonderful way to experience the part but remodeled to still be a wonderful venue. The type is worth it to learn more about this classic music venue and the people involved.
A nice spot in a residential area. It has a playground and splash park as well as spring fields and I have heard a dog park. A few trails as well for walking or running.
Wonderful displays and so much history in one space. It is worth your time if you love or are interested in the music style and the influences then and now.
A unique way to use this house. It is a wonderful art museum with visiting as well as permanent collections. Be sure to save time to walk around the grounds
Lots of parking due to the pool on site. The trails by the pool are boring but there are some great spots farther down. Definitely worth a visit.
This is a beautiful little park.  It has clean public restrooms, picnic tables and lots of walking options.  We dogs love to walk through.
A wonderful relaxing spot on the lake and next to a busy part of town. Lots of benches and trash cans make it a nice spot for lunch.
I only saw one little part of the park, it seems be be quite immense.  Would have been nice to have a sign/map easily accessible.
Relaxing spot perfect for picnics and sitting in benches looking at the water. A fountain for kid's to play in as well.
The heart of this little touristy town. You can do and see everything from here. Great sledding hill in the winter.
Not very big but when you need a cute tree lined spot for a picnic and to just be outside this one is very nice.
Large park on the Burke Gilman Trail. It has access to a large amount of lake shoreline so a great picnic spot.
Huge open park. Great for social distancing. People do let their dogs off leash here so be on the lookout.
Beautiful place with lots of wildlife and it is a very nice place for a walk and to experience the area.
Nicely laid out gardens for a little walk. Easy to grab a spot on the wall or grass for a snack.

This is a fantastic place to stop a couple hours, for visitors of all ages.  Don't miss the replica pithouse you can climb down into and the authentic granary near the museum!  Has a wheelchair accessible trail from the museum to see petroglyphs, which can also be seen from the car in places. Very easy access to see them along Clear Creek Canyon Road.  The museum is nicely done and really let's you see what they discovered here. Some very interesting artifacts here. It is child-friendly, with a mano and metate they can try grinding corn with and a play area with Fremont outfits to try on.  Clean restrooms are a plus!

This is a beautiful place,  with plenty of parking, restrooms, and a place to wash feet. I understand there are nice trails to walk here.

But if you want to play at the beach with kids, this may not be the best place. The dark sand was hot, and a lot of the beach was pebbly and rocky, which doesn't make good sand castles. The creek feeding into the ocean here is brownish, which didn't look inviting to play in. (Try the beach down steps at Otter Rock/Devil's Punchbowl if you want an excellent place for kids to play at!)

So, depending upon your activities, this may or may not be the beach for you!

Very rewarding hike! Amazing view! Today, the trail was pretty dry.

There are porta potties at the beginning of the Main Route trail, and there are two picnic tables a few hundred feet down the trail. Plenty of parking.

Though the trail marker refers to this trail ad "easy," it is somewhat strenuous, with increasing incline as there trail goes on. The end consists of series of steps and rough, rocky upward trail. It is just over two miles round trip on the Main Route trail.

My four-year-old niece, who is sure-footed, got a bit tired but made it to the top easily.

This is a fantastic small zoo! Well worth $4 per person. There is a fun variety of animals you don't usually see in the zoo, more than I'd expected, and you get to see them up closer. I was impressed with how active the animals were. The reindeer, parrot that says "hi" and "hello," and monkeys are a must-see. For $1 you can feed any birds that roan free, including peacocks! And for 25 cents, you can feed sheep and goats at the petting zoo.  There were large sheep, young sheep, and even a baby goat there! This was a nice outing for 1-2 hours for people of any age.

This is a terrific park for people of all ages! There are walking trails, clean bathrooms, picnic areas up by the parking and down by the playground, and two nice swings overlooking the park and Santa Clara River.  The playground has an area for younger children, while also having neat equipment for older children, with a neat bridge and rock wall they can climb. The walking trail connects to Tonaquint Park to the South.  Nice greasy areas where I have seen people do yoga or exercise.

Very nice park! There are three parking areas. The lowest one has access to a pit potty, and is a short walk from a waterfall.
.
The top parking area provides easy stair access to the most impressive fall (this parking area is off a small road to the north of the main road.)

There are picnic tables at the middle and upper parking areas.

It's also a nice park to play in the creek.

This is a gem of a stop! There is a .6 mile loop with signs explaining the history of this interesting site, from Native American to Fort to pioneer history.

It is a beautiful location, with an old orchard and valley view.

There are well maintained restrooms and a very nice, large covered picnic area.

I want to return to go on the 1.2 mile hike to the wildflower meadow!

Clean park with spacious grassy areas. There is a medium amount of parking, which is okay since it's a quiet park.

The small play area is appropriate for approximately ages 2-12, with swings (baby and big kid) and a boat themed play structure.

The bathrooms are open seasonally (locked in winter). There is a nice, large covered outdoor kitchen and many picnic tables.

This is a new favorite family beach!

There are many picnic tables and a well maintained bathroom near the large parking lot.

It is about a quarter mile walk to the beach, on a moderately maintained asphalt path, and over a bridge. The beach is large and had nice sand for kids to play in, as wel as interesting richa to explore another quarter mile down the beach.

We were there today and Quail Creek is completely dried up. This may be helpful to know! The Red Reef hike (along the dry stream bed) is still impressive.

You need to arrive early for a parking place as parking is limited and this place is popular. The trails to the dinosaur prints and the escavated Ancestral Puebloan site are also fantastic.

The McKenzie Highway is ther longer way to go, but it's so worth it for the beauty and for this jem of a stop!

There are clean pit toilets here.

There is an educational half mile walk through the lava flow, in addition to the short but steep hike and flight of steps to the historical observatory.

What a pretty spot, with an unusually long wooden boardwalk through a marshy area! It's about 0.7 miles long. A good spot to go even when it's been raining, since it's not muddy.

We did not see much wildlife, but lots of wildflowers are blooming.

It has a small parking area with a porta potty.

This is a special carousel! They are currently making more pieces for it and you can see them carving and painting them in ther gift shop and in toursof the workshop downstairs. They sell snacks, have a small museum, gift shop, and nice public restrooms. Terrific downtown Albany must-see!

There is a surprisingly good variety of marine life for being an inland aquarium.  Some of our family's favorites are the penguins, eels, otters, and sharks. The touch pools were a highlight, with seastars, stingrays, and sea anemones. There are also many non-sea creatures as well.

Beautiful green park that fills a city block. There is a newly remodeled play area that's great for younger and older children.  There's also public bathrooms, covered group areas, six tennis courts, plenty of parking, three sand volleyball courts, and wide open grassy areas.

Beautiful windy drive to get there, only $5 fee, picnic tables and pit toilets at the parking area. From the summit we could see snowy mountains to the east and the hazy ocean to the west. We took part of the Meadowedge trail on the way down from the summit fur fun variety.

Beautiful outdoor area tucked away on the south side of Corvallis. Fun, wide open area for kids to free play, with the train engine, "dinosaur backbone," and play equipment for young children.

Plenty of parking and picnic areas.

VERY muddy if it had been raining recently!

This past is bigger than it looks from the street! Very nice concrete walking path goes around the field. Two play areas, one for younger and one for older children. Covered picking areas, sand volleyball court. No public restroom, but there is a large porta potty.
likes: Play areas for different age groups

reviews_attraction.text: Fantastic piece of authentic Albany and Oregon history! The tour guide was dressed in pioneer clothes and shared interesting information and stories. This home is nicely restored and furnished, including some original pieces.

A lovely, hidden St George spot! There is a picnic area (no restroom), pond with ducks (bring bread!), and the beginning of a trail that takes you to the top of the red rock cliff (school age children can hike it easily).
Snow Canyon is like a mini Zion! It provides a terrific variety of hikes and picnic areas, with the tremendous and unusual backdrop of white, red, and black Rock all in the same place.
They did not offer the most helpful local information (ie: on hikes in Kanab area), but the display on Anasazi and Fremont history in the area was nicely presented.
likes: Cultural Value: Anasazi and Fremont history

reviews_attraction.text: I wondered if this zoo would be worth the price, and it was! Very nice displays, clean, lots to see close together, and animals were easy to see. Great viewing!!
The new Thunder Junction All Abilities Park offers train rides for $1 from 10-6, Monday tough Saturday. It's open from 10-dusk.
Nice clean park with fun play equipment for kids ages about 3-10. There are only porta potty here. Nice covered picnic areas.

This is a pretty well trafficked viewpoint at the middle of a 4-5.5 mile hike depending on which route you take down. The point itself is very beautiful; you can see mount Rainier and the surrounding mountains very clearly (assuming the weather cooperates). This hike isn’t necessarily for the faint of heart, though. The beginning 2/3rds of a mile of so are VERY steep. Once you’re through with that it’s not too difficult, but it is still uphill and is pretty steep at certain points for the next 1.5 miles after the initial steep section. Just make sure you’re well equipped.

This is a very nice park. It’s one of the three that attracts a ton of visitors from the Seattle Metro and from my experience is the most popular. The park has a ton of views to offer and is quite easy to access. As I mentioned before, it is quite popular, so you probably need to reserve campsites in advance. Most of the trails are pretty well trafficked as well, so if you’re looking to be on a trail alone Rainier is not your best choice. Still, it’s a great park with lots to offer. Lovely place to get away.

This park is very nice for what it provides. It’s a very simple, run of the mill park that also happens to have 4 baseball diamonds. The park is your average park, nothing special, but nice. The baseball diamonds are well kept (they are used mostly for kids’ baseball) but are available to public use if not being used already. I’ve played many baseball games with my friends here and the quality of the diamonds is never in question. It’s also a nice stop along Yankton trail, the bike loop around the city.

This was a very quaint stop along my drive home from the west. My friends and I kind of just stopped because we wanted to stretch our legs, but it was a worthwhile stop. The petrified wood was awesome and the museum (and museum curators) were amazing. So much history in something 99.9% of people will never see, think, or hear about in their entire lives. Stop if you have the chance. Places like this have a lot more to offer than most people give them credit for.

The whole area of Cape Perpetua was. Very beautiful. The tide pools especially were amazing to see. So many starfish, sea urchins, crabs, and more. A word of caution to those visiting tide-dependent attractions like Thor’s Well and Sprouting Horn: go during high tide. My group was excited to see both of the aforementioned things, but couldn’t see either because we visited during low tide. Go during high tide if you want to see Thor’s Well.

This is the only zoo in Sioux Falls and the surrounding area other than Omaha and it does not disappoint. They have a huge museum sections with a multitude of animals from various continents. Once you enter the park there are plenty of things to see, like tigers, bears, leopards, wolves, anteaters, crocodiles, giraffes, zebras, and so much more. There's also a large petting zoo area for little ones to interact with the animals.

This is a very nice and very unique state park in Oregon. After being on the Oregon Coast for a few days and seeing nothing but ocean, rivers, and forest, it was surprising to see what reminded me of Colorado or Idaho. There are many hikes to do, some of which take you up and over smith rock. The views of the park and the surrounding agricultural areas are amazing. Worth a stop if you’re ever in the Bend area

This is a very high quality national park. Most people that come to South Dakota come for Mt. Rushmore and Custer state park, but the badlands is also an amazing stop. It stands out from anything I’ve ever seen in my travels, and it keeps drawing me back for another visit. Even the badlands in Teddy Roosevelt National Park in North Dakota don’t compare. A must see if you’re ever in South Dakota.

This was a very nice hike. Nice distance so you don’t really get sweaty or have to work very hard, and very unique scenery you aren’t going to see many other places. They are strict about taking obsidian, so if that’s your goal, go elsewhere. The picnic area is nice as well. The ground squirrels are definitely not afraid of humans, and will jump up on the table if you allow.

This was a pretty nice historic site. The staff was knowledgeable, and the museum area was very informative. Not too much in the line of actual historical artifacts; the fort is just a recreation. I went to one of the short films they offered as well; it was cheesy but was informative, which is about what to expect at a historic site theater.

Very nice beach and rock. Lots of area roped off, but you could still see a good amount of tide pools and beach area accessible. Only problem I had was that there were an extraordinarily large amount of people. Any picture you take will have people in it, but not the end of the world. Nice stop if you’re driving along the coast.

This is a pretty nice visitor center in Mt. Rainier National Park. Pretty average visitor center but the hikes leading away from it are pretty awesome. Deji peak is amazing and not very difficult, as well as other random split offs for unique views. The people in the visitor center are also very knowledgeable.

This is a very nice visitor center. It has free WiFi, water bottle station, a nice gift shop, plenty of sitting room, and VERY nice exhibits. It is also situated so it is close to plenty of breathtaking hikes. Panorama Point is amazing and the trailhead is located just outside the visitor center.

This trail was a very nice, fairly easy trail. It was about two miles, maybe a little longer. It’s an in and out that takes you to Ross dam. It reminded me a lot of the Hoover dam, and the views of Ross lake and the surrounding mountains were amazing. There is also a waterfall along the way.

This is an amazing national park. It would take weeks to see everything it has to offer. The western coastal area is an awesome place (split rock and hole in the walk are amazing to see) and Hurricane ridge is breathtaking. I was only able to be there for two days, but I would 100% go again.
