The tour costs $6, and you get a bucket of food which costs $4, so getting to ride in the wagon, with a much better view and access to the animals costs just $2 per person if you were getting the food anyway (you should, because it makes the animals love you more).
Best thing I have done with my kids all year.

This was a very fun place to visit with the kids. It has many educational and interactive activities for the kids to engage in. The staff was friendly, and the prices reasonable.  It makes for a fun "play day." Looking around, however, it seems full of amazing resources for organized programs, which makes me think that a camp type program there would be amazing.
The only reason I don't give it 5 stars is because I think that in many ways the setting really begged to be used for structured play, to the point that I felt that we were missing something significant as the kids ran around and had fun.

This beach is ok, and pretty great if you want no waves and a bit of quiet. However, it is near a boat dock. The problem with this is that the trash from people's boats all seems to blow down onto the beach. This means there are water bottles, paper bags from fast food places, and other trash around that little ones will get into. It also doesn't look great. I would suggest a fence to catch the trash, and making sure there is someone to pick it up.

This is a very pleasant place for a walk, or to have a picnic. It is a very well resourced, organized, and run botanical garden. It has a definite Asian feel to it in overall aesthetic, which is a very good thing. The lantern festival we saw there was beautiful, and the kids had a great time paying and looking at everything.
There bathrooms are somewhat dated, with small stalls. However, they are well maintained, and clean.

There is a elephant your can ride, and cassowaries, which is cool. However, maybe it was because it was a kind of hot day, but none of the animals cared that we had food, and the parakeets in the bird area super did not want anything to do with anyone. Moreover, a lot of the enclosures, especially for the bears, were simply sad cages. Choosing between here and the nearby Safari park, is no contest.

Rode the Jamestown island loop. 5 miles, paved with some slow and slight elevation changes (slight incline going up like 40 feet or so). It is a pretty location, and well maintained. As for the rest, it seems pricey for what you get in the time of Covid, but will probably get a membership with another family to bring the kids several times some other year.

This is a nice park in a good location. There is something for everyone, with facilities ranging from a skate park to basketball court to playground, tot lot, and sand box. There are also open green areas for just running around or playing frisbee. It is also right by the Fairfax police station, so I cannot think of a safer place to take your kids to play.

Beautiful park, worth visiting multiple times. The falls are very different depending on the water level. There are adequate bathrooms and a small snack bar in the visitors center. There are trails for walking and hiking for any interest level. To just see the falls is a light walk only. I brought my 2 year old, and she had a great time.

This is one of the coolest community parks I have been to, including those in wealthy areas of the country. It is a great resource with amenities for the regular sports, as well as boating, fishing, and even a BMX track. There are restrooms available, picnicking areas, and several playgrounds for the kids.

This makes a great rest stop to eat and let the kids play on a trip. There were a few other families here, so the kids had someone to play with. There are picnic facilities that are clean and well maintained. There are several places to get food within 5 minutes, and it is close to the highway.

This is a pretty all right museum. Being inside the fort walls is really cool, and the exhibits are informative. Some letters by Poe showed some unexpected aspects of his personality. The down side of the museum is that there is nothing interactive, and not much to appeal to the little ones.

Worth going to, especially for a family with kids just having gotten big enough for the slides. Definitely reserve a Cabana ahead of time if it is a very hot day.  They have a great lazy river, and a few good waterslides, and a wave pool

This is a nice nature preserve. There is a good amount of seating along the trail, thanks to the boy scouts. The beach is nice, and it makes a great spot to get away. Because it is a bit of a hike to get to, the beach is not crowded.
This is a great place to spend the day. It has rained the day we went, so there were probably fewer people than usual. It was very pretty. I imagine that it is better in the late spring and summer.
Best ride in the park. It is an older style ride, with less height and speed than others. However, it is very well designed and ends up being more exciting that the tallest and fastest rides.
This is a nice green area park, and there are occasionally some very cool events held here. It is just on the edge of downtown Hampton, and makes a nice place to stage a walk through town
Awesome rec center for the whole family. There are plenty of organized events and classes, as well as resources for independent exercise and fun. The water park is amazing for the kids.
This is a nice area for walking or running, and the playground is a nice one for the kids. There are greasy and wooded areas nearby. It is a good place to spend an afternoon outside.
Wonderful place for a walk with the family. The woods are nice, and there is plenty of small wildlife. The trails are well maintained, and there are occasionally historical tours.
This is a nice park with a good playground area and picnic/grilling facilities. The volleyball area is a bit run down, but you can prop the net poles up to make it playable.
It is a really fun place to take little ones, with plenty for adults to learn. It is basically a mix of a zoo and a museum, focused on Virginia wildlife.
This is a really neat, very old chapel. It is worth a visit if you are in the area. The fort as a whole is a nice, and unique setting.
This was a great overlook, solid view, and nice area to walk around or sit. There is a .6 Mike trail to a pond, which it a nice walk.
Beautiful spot to see a natural bridge without having to walk far. There is even handicapped parking at the bottom of the stairs.
The wait for the light exhibit is kind of crazy, but it is fun for the little ones. They did a great job putting it together

One of the best Greenbelts I’ve seen. Super wide trails. Mostly clean even creek. Green and water flowing even late August. Mostly great place to walk. But I probably won’t be back. Group of young kids that wouldn’t leave me alone. The least safe I’ve felt in any park.

Nice out of the way park on the east end of the Trinity trail system. Water fountains but no restroom. Lots of parking. A little sketchy. West toward Ft Worth. Nice trail. Restroom at an unnamed park about a mile west. About half along road. 1/2 shaded

Trail around a cove. Some shade. About 9 miles round trip unless you add in extra mile to Dove Road.  Scenic trails w breeze most of the way. Benches tho mostly in the sun. Lots of off-road bike trails. Can beat hot in summer. Take lots of water

Wow what a great linear park through a bunch of small parks. Some beautiful sections. Several ponds and fountains. Lots of shade and benches. Only a few port-a-pots and some are closed off. Lots of parking here but sadly not much anywhere else.

Sorta sketchy. Lots of trash. Lock on bathroom broken. But lots of benches. Lots of families. A lot of picnic tables in the woods Mostly wide paved trail. But across the river at Gateway Park and Audubon Park it’s much cleaner

Great park. Parking is 1/2 mile from street. Small parking lot but lots of street parking. Some portable toilets. Lots of benches. 1/2 mile loop trail past 2 ponds. Soccer field and playground and gazebo at parking lot.

Nice trails. In the Preserve there’s lots of picnic tables on trails. One restroom. Lots of parking. Connects to trails going to lake but nowhere to sit on them. Take lots of water. Hiking boots best for trails to lake

An interesting setup for a neighborhood park. No parking except on street. Path between drainage canal and playground. Then a big open field w lighted and paved trail. A creek but private property signs every 20 feet

Big park with well-defined trails. Lots of branches but most loop back so it’s difficult to get lost. Some steep hills. Lots of shade. Not many people on trails. They’re mostly at the beginning taking family photos

Short paved trail, probably 1 1/2 miles, through a disc golf course. Nice tho. Some unpaved trails. A river. Lots of benches. At least 1 restroom  that’s not locked. Small playground and 1 basketball court.
Great trail system but too many intersections and not enough trail markers. Gate doesn’t really close at 7 but unless you’re experienced you don’t want to be here after dark
I/2 mile paved then unpaved trails. Some wide , some narrow. Lots of snakes. Cell service is very poor so a Locator Beacon if you have one. Take lots of water. No benches.
Big park. Lots of picnic tables, benches, several playgrounds, big pond for fishing. About 3 miles paved trails. Some restrooms and water. Couple hundred parking spots.
Wow. Great park. Lots of trails tho some get wet/muddy. Lots of benches. Prairie, quarry w fossils, river, ponds, forest, wetlands. Bring lots of water and bug spray
Nice trails. 2 miles paved around outside.  Lots of dirt paths in the forest.  Needs more benches and only one set of restrooms about 1 mile back are open.
Nice new trail about 3 miles. No parking yet. Have to park at Audubon Dallas for now. Mostly right along 1382/Belt Line so very noisy but also very scenic
Nice park. Big lake. Nature trail on other side of river that probably most people don’t know about. Looks like a good Disc golf course. 3 parking lots.
Nice city park. Pond. Pavillion. Several picnic tables. Restrooms that are actually unlocked. Only about 3/4 miles of trails. Ducks will chase you down
About 3 miles of trails. Limestone creek. Old settlers relics, fireplaces, bridges, streets? Open restroom outside senior center. Lots of picnic tables
Small neighborhood park about 1/4 mile around. Playground, picnic tables, even restrooms tho they are closed. Private lake behind the park
Small park tho larger than it looks. Only about 3/4 mile track. Playground and splash pool. Lots of picnic tables w grills. Lots of shade
Great rabbit warren of trails along a creek w several ponds. Restrooms in the parking lot/playground. Lots of picnic tables and benches.
Nice neighborhood park. Lots of trees. Connected to a short linear trail along a creek. Some dirt trails. About 4 miles round trip
Parts of this are great. Much better and longer than map indicates. Some unpaved trails. Lots of picnic tables. Pond. River
Wonderful big meadow w a maze and paths. Always something else to explore. More people than I’d expect but still not many

I was here in 1986, then 1996, before the tornado, and the new Visitor's Center. It was unrecognizable. I agree that it has lost some of it's rustic charm due to the shiny new visitors center, and I agree with the other review about the water;  it has a high iron content, so the toilets look like they haven't been flushed, and the water from the fountains did not taste good. All of that being said, the PA State Park service has done an excellent job in making this unique structure accessible to most Pennsylvanians. There are trails that are paved, benches to sit on, and  If I am not mistaken, there is wheelchair accessibility to the Sky Walk . There is a difficult trail to the bottom of the ravine;  it is steep, rocky and lots of loose gravel, but well worth the trip, if you're in shape for it.  From either down below, or up above, there is lots of scenery to behold. The gift shop had a fun collection of Made in PA items, including t-shirts.  The visitors center itself had some great interactive exhibits for folks of all ages. We just happened to go on a day that a food truck was parked, called "Little Sister's Big Rig". The food was great.  We went on a pleasant sunny summer day, and everyone seemed to be out.  If you want to appreciate the glass-bottom sky walk, you might consider going during non-peak times. We could hardly get near it long enough to get a picture without someone photobombing it.  Still, this is one of my favorite state parks, very family friendly, and well worth the 4 hour car ride. Just gotta go back when the fall foliage is at it's peak!

You can go someplace like Ricketts Glen and see waterfalls for free, but what makes Bushkill unique is the accessibility for most people because of the boardwalks. There are 4 trails, and the two more strenuous ones offer a little more wildlife and a lot less people. I am 51, not skinny, and recently had foot surgery,  but still managed to keep up with my 20 year old on the 2nd longest trail which has a combo of Boardwalk and dirt paths. Not sure if I could have done that on the longest trail. On the hottest day of the year, this place was crammed with people, and we had to make allowances for people who were there for a few photo ops on the shortest trail and children who were trying to get away from their parents.  Still worth the $16.50 entrance fee.  There are other activities for the kids, and some very nice gift shops. The cafe was simply awful; poor quality food at outrageous prices, and precious few indoor tables. Good thing they offer picnic facilities,  which would make it an even grander adventure. The bathrooms need an update. It smelled pretty bad, and the floors were wet because of the tsunami like flush which sprayed toilet water everywhere.  So, bring your own water, pack a lunch, bring extra spending money for the gift shops and don't forget the bug spray.  I don't know what you could do to  deal with the bathrooms.  Hope to get up there in the fall!

This bridge, only a few short blocks from the center of Mifflinburg, and only 10 minutes away from Hayes Covered Bridge is, in my opinion one of the most nicely situated bridges in Union county. On the northern side, closest to town is a trail head for Koon's Trail, which is a mile long trail that follows the Buffalo Creek. It appeared to be the safest and easiest place to park. If you walk just a short distance on the trail, you'll find the best views to get photos . The bridge is open to car traffic, so walking through it felt a little risky. When a car goes through it (and there were several that came by while we were there), it makes a thundering sound, since the floor is made of metal grid work. It is also appears that the Koons Trail area is the ONLY accessible public land to the bridge, limiting our exploration of the surrounding area. On the southern side is a beautiful home. Graffiti was moderate. .

This was an organized school field trip, and the folks, in full period clothing, could not have been more genuine. They were engaging, and great with the kiddos. There were several hands-on activities, which made it that much more enjoyable.  Even though Daniel Boone did not spend a great deal of time there, the people who run this have taken full advantage of the educational value, giving people a very real sense of what life was like back in the 18th Century. They combined lessons in military, Pennsylvania, early U.S. and agricultural history.  We came on a cold rainy day, but I could see where this would be a great place for a family hike or bike ride. One thing worth noting as a parent of a young child; there is a gift shop, but all the items for sale related in some way back to the homestead. There were very few useless nic-nacs or souvenirs. That alone deserves a 5 star rating.

We came here on a Friday morning, and other than a few people who seemed to be doing a self-guided tour, we had the place to ourselves.  While there seemed to be a fair amount of parking on either side of the bridge, we approached it from the eastern side, coming from Route 15, and were treated to parts of the Battlefield. The bridge is in pristine condition, and unlike a lot of other covered bridges in Pennsylvania, there was access to the creek at every angle. There a little dam on the eastern side of the bridge, and because of the low water levels, made for a fun spot for some photos. Again, visiting there on an early Friday morning made it for a pleasant stop. This is not a drive through bridge.

My review is based on a field trip we took with my kids school. We pretty much had the place to ourselves, and I have no idea how much it costs to get in, other than the fact that most games in the arcade were. $. 50 to $1.00, and that the bumper cars were $5. There is something for every age group, and most impressive by far is the ropes course and indoor jungle (think McDonald's Playland, only 100 times more elaborate and much cleaner.)  The snack bar was unexpectedly impressive, offering pizzas, salads, wraps, plus more, and the prices were fair. This place may be more chaotic on the weekends a during peak hours, but I was impressed with the place and plan to go back.

Easily one of the best playgrounds on the West Shore. There is something there for every age group, and there's an area set aside for the younger kids.  The floor is made of foam rubber, and there's only one way in and out, making it easier to keep track of the kids.  A large covered pavillion, complete with picnic benches, trash and recycling bins, and soda machines, is available if you want to pack a lunch, and can be reserved for parties or private picnics.   This park is a popular place for local moms to meet and let their kids play without much fuss.  It was built by the community, initiated by Capital Area Christian Church, and is regularly updated.

Went here on a school organized field trip, and it was a favorite for my little fly guy. The volunteer staff were fantastic with the kids of every age. This place is about as close to a "please touch me" museum as you can get. There were so many helicopters that the kiddos could get in and out of. There was also a themed play area for the littles.  Entry to the museum is reasonably priced and the gift shop offerings had items in every conceivable price range.  Based on their activity calendar this place seems very community minded as well. It is on the southeastern end of Chester County and seems closer to Exton.

Honestly, one of the nicest covered bridges we've been to so far. There are places to park when coming from Route 75, there is easy access to the creek bed (rock skipping, anyone?), it's actually handicapped accessible if you can push a wheelchair up the the incline. There is great information about the history of the bridge on the other side, and there's even the foundation of an old mill that you can check out. But for how neat and tidy this is, there are a LOT of cameras, so don't get any ideas. :-)

The shiny new visitors center is stunning and still smells new, but it lacks the charm of the old one down the road.  Boulder Field was good, but you couldn't get near the falls for how crowded it was,  people were parked soo illegally that it was as though they were asking to get hit.  It was a holiday weekend, not long after our state went "green" from Covid, so some of the crowds were to be expected.

It has beautiful views of the lake, stunning landscaping, a walking trail, plenty of parking, an interesting, interactive history of Raystown in the lower level, a gift shop with fun, reasonably priced apparel, gifts, toys and maps, a bunch of free brochures with helpful information on the region, a comfortable sitting area, and exceptionally clean restrooms. This place has it all.

Easy balance of thrill rides, roller coasters and more gentle rides like the carousel and Pioneer Train. Pay as you go or get an all day hand stamp. Bring your own food, or enjoy really good, and less expensive concessions.. Cool off in the swimming pool and water slides. Free parking.  Can't compare to parks like Hershey or Dorney. It is a breed all its own.

Since you can't drive over it, it was cool to linger on the bridge..The embankments are too over grown to get to the creek without shredding your legs. There is a spot to pull over (safely) on the Covered Bridge Road side, but you get a better side view of it when approaching it from Creek Road. Its a nice country drive, from all directions.

Sorry I couldn't post any pictures; No flash photography allowed. :-)  This place is well run. They have people directing traffic during special events , and are super friendly.  They are also great with the younger kids, and provide educational materials free of charge, but gladly accept donations.

This really is a nice park and you can tell it is a central part of the community. There are wide open grassy areas, and two different types of playground. The wooden one is showing its age, but you can tell where they are trying to make it safer. It is just a unique playground.

Pretty impressive cross section of animals. Some exhibits are in better shape than others,  and most could use a little sprucing up. Still, it is impressive for being a privately owned roadside zoo. And there's a great deal of educational value.  You gotta go at least once.

There are several spots to get photos of the bridge,  and they all have their advantages.  The pull-off area on Route 92 offered the safest vantage point, and had additional information on the bridges history. Going up during the fall colors was a bonus.

Just about one of the nicest state parks in northeast PA. Well worth the dirt roads to get to the different vistas. Super clean visitors center with a decent interpretive wildlife display, plus, t shirts and sweatshirts for sale

Went on a school field trip. Our guides were well versed in Amish culture.  Fun, hands on independent activities for the kids, goats, picnic facilities (sheltered), and seriously one of the best gift shops on Route 30.

Fantastic views of the confluence of the western branch of the Susquehanna River. Plenty of parking, with some picnic facilities. It looks like there are some nice hiking trails which we did not take advantage of.

Nice local park that the township is working to revitalize. Easy access to the creek, dog friendly walking path, and a disc golf course. It also offers a large pavilion and a playground area for younger children.
This is the best rollercoaster,  wooden or steel that I have ever been on. Secured by only a lap bar, you couldn't have more air time than if you were to parachute out of a plane.
Over priced. Exhibits leave a lot to be desired. The Canada Geese have taken over the stream that runs through the park, and have terrorized the customers.
Opens right at sunrise. Large parking lot to accommodate cars and trucks with trailers. Shady trees, a boat launch,  and access to a view of the falls.
Worth the back road drive to get there.  But office was closed (which we knew) but the bin that would normally have the passport stickers was empty.

Lost Maples is a great state park to visit. The trails on the east and west have challenging pieces. The West Trail is much quieter and a longer hike. I saw more people on the East Trail and it was easier to follow the path. I got off the path on the West Trail a few times as it looked like a path but ended up turning into a section that was not maintained, thus not the trail. The West Trail was more shaded but the downside to being the first on the trail in the morning was hitting all the spider webs.

Bring water and lots of it, especially in the Texas summer heat!! There is a water station to fill up water bottles at the day area where you can park, right in front of the restrooms. If you want to camp here, book your trip earlier, even for day trips. You need a reservation to get in and both days I hiked there was a sign that said all day trip spots had been filled.

Lost Maples is a tough hike in certain areas and when the sign says steep, they mean it. Big upward climb- you stay on your feet and don’t need your hands to climb it but your thighs will be burning with the huge upward climb.

Fall would be beautiful with the leaves changing colors but probably really busy then too. Also, hard to predict when the colors will hit, some years it’s December.
dislikes: Spider webs (early morning on West Trail)

reviews_attraction.text: McKinney Falls State Park was one of the more lengthy hikes for me hitting up the two big trails: Onion Creek (2.8 miles) and Homestead Trail (3.1 miles) along with other trails too. There were a lot of people at the Upper and Lower Falls where you can swim in the water, but I didn’t have anyone on the trails with me! Between hikes I hopped into the Upper Falls for a refreshing dip. McKinney Falls is right by the airport so not far from Austin. To get to the northern portion of trails, you will have to cross over the falls. You will get wet! The rocks are slick, especially barefoot. I’d recommend bringing some shoes with grip to change into, or just wear throughout if they are good hiking shoes. Nice relaxing place!

LBJ State and National Historical Park is a beautiful part of Gillespie County right along the Pedernales River. One side of the river is the state park with trails and a working farm, Sauer-Beckmann Living History Farm, and the other side of the river is the LBJ Ranch. The ranch side has the Texas White House, where President Johnson went to escape from the bustle to the Texas Hill Country. There is a collection there of his cars (currently closed) and his Air Force One Half (smaller plane) is housed here. You cannot go into the house, or plane, just a heads up. As you drive through the ranch, there are cattle roaming the property.
dislikes: Limited access (Texas White House, Air Force One Half)

reviews_attraction.text: Seminole Canyon State Park was a fun trek into basically uninhabited territory. There is no cell service for miles so download your maps before you go. It was cool to be so close to the Rio Grande and not see a giant fence at the border. It was a dry heat when walking in the desert so bring plenty of water! The overnight camping is not available at this time unfortunately. You have to take the guided pictographs tour as well seeing remnants from an ancient civilization. The Rio Grande and Canyon Rim trail, although lengthy, bring you right to the cliffs on the water. I enjoyed my time at Seminole Canyon!

Enchanted Rock State Natural Park has perfected the camping experience. The camping sites fill up quickly, and you can book reservations 3 months in advance. For the summer/fall months at least, you have to reserve both Friday and Saturday night for camping. Everyone hikes The Summit at Enchanted Rock, which is quite the workout on the thighs, so you have to do it. But there are a lot of other trails to hit up as well. And you need to be up on one of the higher trails for a great overlook at sunrise and sunset- definitely worth it! I cannot say enough about Enchanted Rock.

San Angelo State Park is really 2 parks in one with the size of the park. There are horse and bike trails and you have to leave one park to access the other trails. There are a few entrances that aren’t labeled as well and you have to use the code from the office to open the locked gates. The trails aren’t labeled very clearly so make sure you know where you are going. It is a pretty area. You should check it out. I wish I had a bike for some trails (or a horse) but got some good hiking in! And watch out for rattlesnakes, we saw one on the trail.

Lockout Austin was so much fun!!  It was a great team building event with my coworkers.  We did the CSI Murder at the Asylum and it was one tough room.  Well done in setting it up.  I will definitely be back with some smart friends to escape again.  Thank you Lockout Austin- great challenging rooms and nice staff! The only thing that was tough was the window in the room had writing on it from the previous group which confused us just a little.  The room takes a lot of working setting up so I can see why it of all things could get missed.

Martin Creek Lake State Park is a popular fishing spot as there were plenty of fishers along the docks and shore.  I really enjoyed the Island Trail on the smaller island that’s connected with a pedestrian bridge. There are campsites on the little island too and this is where I’d want to be! P01-P06 is the better side of the island so try to book one of those sites. The trails were quiet and it was cool walking though the evenly spaced pine trees.  The trails were easy too so perfect for the whole family.

Newman’s Castle is in Bellville, TX about 2 hours outside of Austin. Mr. Newman lives in this castle that he has built over the last 20 years. You stop by his bakery in town to get your tickets (reservations prior is a must). I’d recommend calling about 3-4 days in advance. A sandwich lunch is provided in the castle and the bread is fresh from the bakery. It’s a cool castle to see. Mr. Newman isn’t the most friendly man which is why it got 4 stars instead of 5. It’s a fun spot to visit, go check it out.

Buescher State Park is a great hiking spot but not as visited as the neighboring Bastrop State Park. There are different types of trails which makes it a fun spot. There is hiking through the woods and then also some sandy and grassy spots on the trail. I didn’t see anyone on the trails when I was there. I camped here and there was no one to my left or right so it was nice and quiet! There are showers here which is a plus. Buescher is about 30 min outside Austin so very doable for a day trip or weekend!

I booked my campsite at Daingerfield State Park a few months ago because this is a spot in Texas to see the leaves changing colors. It’s hard to predict though when this will happen. The end of October was too early this year as more colors will probably show in I’d say 2 1/2 weeks. It was a pretty place and very well maintained, including the restrooms and showers. It felt like a great place for a church camp. I enjoyed camping here and liked the hikes too.

Garner State Park is one of the busiest state parks in Texas. The day passes can be purchased about 30 days in advance and camping up to 5 months in advance. You’ll want to book early. Bathrooms and showers are clean. It is a beautiful park right on the Frio River with lots of spots to rent tubes to float the Frio in the summer. The Crystal Cave isn’t too spectacular as it is just a small cave with one room. I’d recommend hiking up to Old Baldy instead!

Devils River is a beautiful area but it takes a bit to get there. Drive your SUV or vehicle with 4-wheel drive or you may get stuck. It was 19 miles of dirt roads at about 25 miles per hour. Not a ton of hikes here but lots of spots along the river to fish and kayak if you bring your own. You do have to hike in about a mile from the nearest parking lot. They have a few camping spots but it fills quickly. It is a beautiful area so go check it out.

Quest Waterpark and Wakeboarding is a lot of fun and quite the workout! I’ve been 2 times and really enjoy the obstacle course. That’s actually the only thing we did this time. Some of the inflatables could use a little more air but you’ll have a great time. They also have a giant slide and wakeboarding that you hold on to the cables above the water. No reservations needed and it’s better and more affordable than the course on Lake Travis.

Lockhart State Park is a smaller hike with around 3 miles of total trails. It was interesting to have a 9-hole golf course right in the middle of the park. It was a nice clear day with some pretty surroundings. It wasn’t crowded either which was nice. The bathrooms, however, were locked but there were plenty of trees that needed watering.   :)

We saw 4 baby armadillos and some fish in the river and overall it was a pretty tranquil hike.

The Escape Game Austin has really cool rooms! We did Gold Rush and it was a really cool setup. It had some challenging pieces in the room but was so much fun! The toughest room at The Escape Game is Prison Room but they also have the top rated Playground Room. I have been to a number of escape rooms and this was my favorite! I see why there were so many great reviews here. Go check them out and have fun escaping with your friends.

SeaWorld isn’t what it used to be. I used to love going there but maybe that was just the age I was at. They are doing well with distancing and keeping things clean. They have limited each of the animal shows to two per day and with distancing they fill up quickly. I think little kids would enjoy the climbing on the playscape and water area; it was not busy in that part. I don’t have a need to go back anytime soon.

Lost Maples Winery is a great boutique winery just two minutes from Lost Maples State Park. It’s the spot to go to relax after a nice hike (and to get away from the kids). The owners are great and know their stuff. They have a number of award winning wines so I had to take a bottle home. Due to the virus, wine tasting wasn’t available and I couldn’t drink by the nice pond but I’ll be back for that part!

The Escape Game Houston has awesome escape rooms that are both challenging and a lot of fun. They have 5 great rooms with the most challenging being Prison Break. I have done 3 rooms and escaped Prison Break today with friends. Dominick and the staff at Escape Game Houston were helpful, and I can’t wait to try Special Ops! There are many unexpected surprises in each room. Schedule your fun today!

Lake Brownwood is a pretty area and the spots around the lake had lots of people there grilling and hanging out. I took the Nopales Ridge Trail and was glad because there was no one around. It was a good hike. The Texas Oak Trail does not seem to be used much as the grass and trees were growing across the path. Going to Lake Brownwood made me wish I had a boat!

Guadalupe River State Park is a great park in Spring Branch. Crossing the river or driving to the other entrance is the way to go for the hikes. I was crazy and crossed the river and it was freezing but it is worth it. I didn’t want to drive 15 minutes more to get to the other entrance so walked across the cold. Go check out the state park.

Palmetto has been my favorite state park to visit so far! It feels like a tropical retreat that somehow made its way into Texas. I loved the little palms throughout the park and the green swamp was really cool. Hiking here right after it rained was the perfect time to go. I’d highly recommend visiting Palmetto State Park in Gonzales.

Goliad State Park and Historic Site is an important piece of Texas history. I thought this was the "Come and Take It" site but that's actually in the city of Gonzales. Goliad was a mission with a school and living quarters. You can walk around the mission and go into 2 buildings. If Texas history interests you, go check it out.

Atlanta State Park is a nice park with good hikes. The largest number of people were gathered in different spots on the lakefront of Atlanta State Park. I enjoyed the hikes and was by myself for the most part on the trails. The Volksmarch Trail was probably my favorite.
Half buried and graffitied Cadillacs just outside Amarillo, pretty cool. Bring a can of spray paint and have fun taking pictures and leaving your mark. Go at sunset, it’s  better!

The park is a nice size and there are lots of trees around.  It's in a very quiet neighborhood which is nice because so many parks in Arlington seem to be located next to busy roads and all you here is the noise of traffic.  The parking situation is a little odd.  There is a parking lot, but it's not close to the playground.  Normally I don't mind walking, but if I'm having to haul an exhausted toddler back to the car, it helps to be parked close by.

The playground is nice and there are even a couple of outdoor exercise stations.  No bathrooms or gazebos that I could see.  It's always nice to have a bathroom at parks even if they cost some money to build and maintain.  I personally think it's better than having little kids wet their pants or pee on bushes because there's no other option.

The water gardens are a very fun place to visit in Fort Worth.  They are within walking distance of Sundance Square so if you're touring downtown this is a must see.  There is the main fountain/pool area and several smaller ones.  All are unique and offer a different experience.

There are lots of stairs so people with mobility issues might have difficulty getting around.  The main fountain has large steps that can be traversed.  Anyone can enjoy this fountain from the top but the steps are not a place for small children or adults without good strength and balance.

I've seen lots of people doing wedding photos and other portraits in the gardens.  It's a beautiful place to be around sunset on weekends.

I love how large and isolated this park feels.  It has a playground, some portable toilets and a small parking lot.  The neighborhood nearby is very quiet and I hardly see many people out here any time I go.  Sometimes you can hear buzzing from the aero modelers flying a few hundred feet away, but it's not an issue.  The walking path is extensive enough that you can get a pretty good workout in one lap.  The ponds and trees are amazing too.  I like to visit parks during my lunch break.  Some parks in the middle of the day give me the vibe that I could be jumped at any moment.  This one is nice and secure; a great place to visit for some solitude or to play with the kids.

I've loved this park since I was a kid and I'm glad that they've added to it without taking out some of the older playground equipment.  The big robot is my favorite part and I'm happy to see it's gotten a new coat of paint over the years.  There are several baseball fields and a fishing pond nearby too.

We came on a Saturday morning and it was pretty crowded as there were lots of families there and they had softball games going on at the time.  If we hadn't already had Covid we probably would have turned around.  Just because you're outside doesn't mean you're completely safe.  Getting the kids outside is important but exercise some common sense while you do it.

This is a good sized park with a playground, expansive walking trails, and a war memorial.  It looks like there is an area for outdoor concerts but I have no idea if anyone will be using it in the near future.  Lots of wide open space to fly a kite and parking is ample.  I think there was a even a restroom, which  is always a good thing to have at parks.  I plan to come back much more in the future, but my first visit will forever hold a special place in my mind because my son didn't want to leave so I basically had to drag him back to the car.  As I coaxed him along, a random guy started questioning me as if I was kidnapping him.  Fun day!

It's a nice little park that connects to the Trinity Trail.  They've expanded the trail heading east, so now you can go all the way out to I-820 E.  Hopefully more to come!  The entrance to the park can be hard to miss if you're not looking for it.  You have to turn and drive down a narrow road through a wooded area before you hit the open space and parking lot.  I love coming here in the morning and evening.  It can feel kind of isolated, even though you're close to a busy roadway.  There's no shortage of people hanging out in their cars in the middle of the day.  I don't know if they're playing Pokemon or what, but it just seems weird.

This is a large park with a lot to offer.  It has beaches, a boat ramp, ball fields, covered picnic areas, you name it.  We came out to go kayaking on the lake and had a wonderful time.  The boat ramp was closed, unfortunately, so we had to park near the beach and drag the kayaks out to the water.  No biggie.  In the summer, the city does weekly fireworks over the lake, and this park is a great place to watch as they launch from one of the peninsulas.  We have a great time on each visit and are willing to go the extra distance to come enjoy it.

I've enjoyed coming to the gardens my whole life.  It's a beautiful part of Fort Worth and is truly worth visiting, especially in the evening before it closes.  We came out to see the lantern festival and had a great time.  They also have concerts and other special events.  I'll never get tired of coming out on nice days and enjoying the trees, ponds, and serenity.  There is usually plenty of parking and a cafe is on site.  The Japanese garden is a special area but it's worth the cost of admission.

I love the size of this park and the trees.  It's beautiful in mid fall when all the leaves are changing color.  There's a walking trail that goes around the perimeter of the park which is a good distance.  The playground is nice and there is a community center, pavilion, and free mulch area.  All in all it's pretty great.  You'll probably see homeless people kind of camped out at some of the picnic tables scattered around, so if you're skittish about that you'd better just stay home and watch TV.

It's one of my favorite parks in Tarrant County.  The trail is meant more for walking but you can ride along it for sure.  You have to cross a few streets at the end to connect to the other riding trails in the area.  The playground is so so but still a good option for younger kids.  I've always loved coming out here in the spring and fall.  When the weather is perfect and the trees are changing colors or blossoming, it's the perfect place to spend the evening.

What a great place to walk around and soak up some San Antonio.  The park is massive and contains lots of interesting sculptures and structures.  It's easily accessible from the river walk and there are public restrooms in the base of the Tower of the America's.  We really enjoyed being able to take an early morning stroll and see everything the park had to offer.  There are plenty of great spots to take pictures so go ahead and bring your camera!

It's a very large park that includes a walking trail, fishing pond, baseball fields and ample parking.  It's very open with few trees around so it's a good place to bring the quadcopter for some flight practice.  The walking trail makes a loop around the park so you can take the little ones for a short walk.  There's also a decent playground and picnic areas.  It would be a great place to spend a warm, sunny afternoon.

This is a huge natural area full of rolling hills and beautiful views of downtown. A network of crisscrossing trails leads through prairie grasses and pockets of trees. It's easy to spends hours walking around and exploring. About two hours before sunset the light is perfect for taking outdoor portraits in the tall grass. The freeway is nearby buts it's easy to ignore unless you're hiking right next to it.

It's a pretty good sized open space with a creek and gazebo on top of a hill. The walking trail isn't too long and the parking lot could use some repairs. There's a restroom but it's a portable toilet that's also seen better days. You can tell someone has been sleeping in the gazebo and there was a tent out on the edge of park. It would still be an okay place to take a walk on a sunny day.

I've been coming here since I was a kid.  It's changed a lot in the last twenty years but it's still a great place to spend a weekend afternoon.  They've expanded quite a bit and it's much more interactive than it used to be.  Our son loved playing there, so even though it's not as 'museum-y' as it used to be, it's still worth visiting.

It's a nice little park with a playground and benches.  It's a good place to have a little picnic but the playground isn't expansive so the kids might get bored with it quickly.  A concrete trail runs through the park and connects it to other trails and parks in the area.  There's no parking lot so you'll have to park on the street.

Nice big park with playground and boat ramp. There is plenty of parking and it's a little off the main roads so there's no noise from traffic. A walking trail encompasses the park but you can also stroll right throughthe wooded area. Lots of picnic tables and a great view of the lake make this an idea spot to enjoy nice weather.

The park is massive and has miles of concrete and dirt trails for hiking and biking.  Most times you'll be surrounded by tall trees but sometimes it opens up to the lake and river.  It's a great place to go for an early morning ride.

Small park next to a creek with walking loop. The playground equipment is in good shape and another walking path splits off from the loop. There are permanent restrooms but they're usually locked in the evenings.

Good sized park with pond, playground, walking trail, baseball fields and water park.  Ample parking and great bird watching.  The trail loops around the whole park and makes for a great early morning hike.

Fun place to visit when it's dry.  Don't bother after a heavy rain; the ground gets very muddy.  If you don't bring a can of spray paint, no worries.  People leave half full ones lying all over the place.
Large sprawling wooded area that runs along the trinity river. Great trails, playgrounds and pavilions. Amazing views of the buildings downtown at sunrise and sunset.
Nice wooded park right off a main road. A long concrete walking trail branches off the small parking lot and provides good views of the trees and river.
Great park with long concrete walking trail that stretches a couple of miles along the creek.  Several playgrounds can be found along the way.
It's a little hidden gem right near the freeway.  Early morning is the best time to come by and see wildlife and spectacular sunrises.

Hiked McAfee Knob in the dark in order to catch sunrise.  We were the 2nd car there at 3:40, took the service road up to make it easier on ourselves in the dark & give plenty of time. You definitely can walk a quick pace until turning onto the trail to the final ascent.  It took us 2 hrs to reach the top, a whole hour and half before sunrise.  A few others joined later and we helped one another w pictures.  The rock outcropping is pretty spacious and beautiful.  You can literally walk around the rim on it.  So cool. It's the best viewing and rec site in the Crown.  Hiking down the trail took much longer, because it is longer.  All the trails are well maintained and pleasant to walk on.  They offer a variety of terrains and scenes to trek thru which is entertaining.  For early risers, we happily discovered Catawba Shelter has an outhouse.  It also has a spring water source for those in need.  Awesome experience.

This is a strenuous loop trail that climbs 1400 ft in the first 3.5 miles.  In fact, there's an inner loop whose trail is shorter & less difficult. The advertised distance never seem to match up w ours.  We clocked in at around 6.5 miles w stops. It will be very helpful to bring at least one trekking pole. The climb is immediate & continuous w enough leveling to catch a breath or view the valley at 7 distinct vistas. Otherwise, the foliage blocks everything as you hike the ridge. Some parts of the trail were impeded by fallen trees & overgrown plants, creating obstacles to navigate. But this only added to the unique nature of the hike. Thankfully, once we hit the summit, it was ALL downhill from there. Logged steps and the absence of rocks made the descent much easier and faster. However, the trail seemed to never end.  It eventually did after 3.5 hrs.

Located outside of Charlottesville, this is a beautiful and moderately challenging hike. The trails wind along a scenic lake and meander through the woods & slopes nearby. There are two labelled trails. I took the Lake Front Loop from the lower parking lot (first you see on the entrance road). You can continue on road and find parking at the lake. Be aware, from the 1st lot, the old trail to the left is very strenous w huge step ups.  It is straight up! The easier ascent is to the right. Much to my relief, the remaining trails are all smoothly worn and easy to walk. There is frequent elevation changes that makes this a challenging hike.  The total length of the loop is nearly 6.5 miles w rest stops every mile if you choose to make use of them. I decided to stop every 2 for water.  I'm looking forward to returning and bringing my wife & others.

Humpback Rocks never disappoints!  On this cool, crisp, autumn morning, we immediately leaned into a steady upward climbed until we began picking thru a indistinguishable trail of wet rocks and leaves.  Before long, we had reached the summit. Hiking up to Humpback overlook is both challenging & great fun. The sharply angled rocks jutting out offer amazing views of the valley. I'm convinced the most scenic in the region. By mid morning it was ridiculously crowded.  Both on top and w the numbers of cars parked everywhere below when we returned.  My advice: make a good hike better by adding the AT on the way back.  It's twice as long and nearly all down hill w switchbacks, but none of the rocks going up. Well worth it!

This nice county park outside of Charlottesville has a wide sandy beach for swimming, a large lake for kayaking and fishing, and trails for hiking & biking.  I chose the longest Willis Loop (4.3 mi) that begins across the road from the map kiosk in the first lot.  I unknowingly took the hardest route going counter-clockwise.  It felt like I was climbing the majority of the time.  There's not much to see, lots of fallen and sawn up trees contributing to a debris field of stumps & logs. Guess that didn't really didn't matter as I was focused of the roots and rocks in front of me most the time. It's a strenuous, moderate hike that'll offer a tiring workout at a quick pace.  For me, once here will suffice.

This museum is located 6 miles from city center and overlooks the beautiful skyline of Philadelphia. Here liberated slaves arrived under cover of night arrived despite great danger to find safe haven in the Belmont Mansion's attic enroute the freedom.  The exhibits were primarily recorded testimonials of slaves' reflections during their times living in slavery.  The main house focuses more on the abolitionists' efforts and the role of the Peters' family and the use of their property for the Underground Railroad.  I hope the museum will continue to improve w funding for expansion and upkeep.  I only wished there were personal tours rather than self guided ones.

Easy, level trails that wind through pine and deciduous trees. Once you get off the paved or gravel paths you will enjoy the soft underfooting. I chose the forest trails over the paved ones. They can be rooty so be careful. Do your best your best bet is to seek a dirt path heading to the outside. If you do you'll catch the loop trail that circumnavigates the entire park.  You will scoot the fencelines and nearby apts. & homes, and the creek.  It's all quite pleasant, while a good workout. By the time I finished I had hiked over 4 miles and almost 1.5 hrs. The loop is 2.6 mi

Paid a visit to the Capital to see the new Virginian women's monument - Voices From the Garden.  Though still in progress, the 7 of 12 planned statues are very expertly crafted and worth the trip to see.  Surprisingly diminutive in size, the statues are realistically crafted and pleasantly life size. The memorial lacks information and context at this time.  There are no plaques nor hint of who the women are. So it's necessary to Google and learn who the figures are and who's to come. Not really a problem. All the more reason to pause and enjoy.

Been to Humpback several times, but this was the most strenuous of all the outings.  We followed the trail up from the parking lot and the AT down.  I guess we forgot the long, steep initial climb and the mini rock scramble before making it to top, then the relentless impact of stepping over smaller rocks coming down the AT.  We came early in the week. Hardly anyone was there. At one point we were the only ones at the overlook. We all had a great workout and loved the hike.  We even sighted a snake and young black bear running across the AT🐻

Years ago I only walked along the river, but today was quite pleased to discover additional trails in the surrounding woods. The white trailhead loops through the entire park. It begins at the rear of the first parking lot on the right.  The trail is wide, smooth with very little elevation change.  I was able to put in 3 miles, but there's shorter routes if you preferred and longer ones too. If you're looking for a relaxing, easy hike under the pleasant canopy of towering shade trees, you'll like this.

Near the Dell Music Center in East Fairmount is Sedgley Disc Course.  This place has over 40 holes!!  We had limited time and completed just 18 of them. The next day, we took a long hike/walk by following the Boxers' Trail.  You can use the same parking lot and find it by walking along the road past the Dell Music Center & across the intersection. You'll see the trailhead to the left. The trail takes you down to the river and then past several divergent paths leading you up to historic mansions.

I've never been to Ancarrow's Landing, but thought since they have a few trails to check it out.  Well, beside the trail along the river with glimpses of Rocketts' Landing, the only other designated trail is for bikes and not worth walking. My advice is to go in the other direction (downstream) and follow the Slave Trail.  This is where it starts.  With frequent pauses to read historically signs, it is well worth it.  Especially, if you are not rushed and have the legs.  Round trip around 7 mi.
dislikes: Bike-only trail not suitable for walking

reviews_attraction.text: Well marked trails, viewing platforms, floating walkways, and marshes typifies what makes walking this area so enjoyable.  Whenever possible venture off the main path (white) to the Adventure Trail and the Yellow Trail.  Both of these will lead you into less used and more scenic areas. To locate: drive to the back of the park to the playgrounds. The trailhead begins beyond them.  It a short, easy hike which can be extended by going off the beaten path. Good for families w young children.

Located a few miles off 64 in Kent County, the Wahrani Nature Trail consists of 4 interconnecting trails for bike and hiking - A,B,C,& D.  They can be somewhat confusing as blazing is pretty much non-existent, except for loop D.  Otherwise, there are directional signs at major intersections, and fortunately printed trail maps,at the first of 3 trail kiosks. The trails are moderately difficult and can be combined in one large loop by keeping to the outside. 4.5 miles

Besides a few picnic tables and parking spots, the trails are the only attraction in this tiny city park. I like that it first follows along the nearby Powhite Expressway before heading in to the bush. There the seclusion of the woods and hills make for a nice get away.  Good for hiking & biking, you can choose an outside loop and several interconnecting trails. No views to speak of. With some backtracking, you can put in a good, satisfying hour of hiking.

We were hiking in the area and heard the view from beneath the Star was a must see.  We weren't disappointed!  We drove to the top at dusk in order to see the valley & city illuminated after sunset.  Being able to identify the distant mountains and see the moving headlights of autos on the highway below was a treat.  The Star is totally impressive and the grounds are very well kept and reflects a sense a civic pride. So glad we made it to the 🌟.

Went on a cold, overcast Saturday morning.  We had the place to ourselves.  We hadn't visited for several years and we impressed by the improvements and upkeep of the facilities.  Modern looking direction signs are found everywhere.  Expanded parking and renovation of nearby historic home adds to the sense that Maymount is a growing, happening place.

In Cumberland Co, Bear Creek Lake offers camping, swimming, fishing, and hiking. I went there to hike and found two larger loops on either side of the lake.  The trails are well marked and are pleasant to walk on.   Lost Barr Loop is a bit more challenging than Channel Cat Loop. The park provided trail maps at the trailhead which was very helpful.

I enjoy this park. There are a variety of things that can be done; basketball, soccer, playgrounds, walking & running, and health course. Everything is well maintained.  I usually come to use the running trail, as well as newer trails found spurring out.  All the trails are well shaded, even in the middle of the day.

I was unaware of these secluded trails hidden beneath the Huguenout Bridge.  I parked at the furthermost trailhead and wound along the river, coming out on Riverside Rd, where I continue to follow a trail along the river to Pony Pasture Park and the trails therein.  All told, 5.5 miles r/t.  Very enjoyable.

We walked up Church Hill and then to Libby Hill to take in the autumn view of RVA and the James River.  The surrounding neighborhoods are all charmingly historic.  From there it's not a far walk either to Chimbrazo Park or back to Richmond Hill.  The view is amazing up the river and over the city.

Found near New Kent, the Cumberland Marsh Nature Area offers a boardwalk view and a woodland trail that gives a pretty overlook of the marsh.  The trail begins along a field of soybeans before ducking into the woods.  The trail is easy and flat and well marked by the Nature Conservancy. 3.5 mi

Well marks trails that follow along and down a ridge overlooking a broad creek. The Heritage Trail is the longest and intersects w a few others. About 20 Mi east of  Charlottesville in Fluvanna Co. Other amenities incl dog park, picnic pavillions, restrooms.

I was pleasantly surprised by the rolling terrain and narrow, earthen trails of Poor Farm Park outside of Ashland. These trails wind through the woods & along a shallow creek. They are great for hiking, running, biking and easy enough for families.
Easy to enter & exit w wide open parking. Clean, well maintained restrooms.  Plenty of picnic benches and green space to enjoy.

Very big park with lots of things to do. It has a running trail (Marvin Taylor Exercise Trail), small gardens like Rose Garden, Family Garden, Woodland Garden, Arid Garden, McGovern Centennial Garden etc, and a beautiful Pergola Walk.

Apart from that there are 'Mary Gibbs and Jesse H. Jones Reflection Pool', Hermann Park Railroad, a two-mile, 18-minute journey around Hermann Park [Monday - Sunday: 10 a.m. - 6 p.m.] will cost only $3.75 per person, adults and children 1 year, and older

Japanese Garden, a beautiful park to explore. There are two children's parks with a splash pad. One is for ages 2-3 and the other one is for 5-12.

Location has a dedicated 3-hr parking area but it will fill up very quickly. Park has few restrooms and drinking water fountains. Very clean and well managed but I saw few homeless people sleeping around the park and also inside the pavilions.

Very beautiful and huge park with lots of things to do. Visitors can rent bicycles, kayaks and canoes from Buffalo Bayou Park. Things you can do are,

1. Visit The Water Works
2. Visit Buffalo Bayou Park Cistern (Paid)
3. Visit Lee & Joe Jamail Skatepark
4. Visit Barbara Fish Daniel Nature Play Area and Picnic Pavilion
5. Visit Eleanor Tinsley Park
6. Visit Houston Police Officers’ Memorial
7. Go to Johnny Steele Dog Park
8. Visit Wortham Foundation Grove
9. Checkout Waugh Bridge Bat Colony
10. Visit Lost Lake
11. Hike & Bike Trails

There are public parking areas available at Lost Lake, Eleanor Tinsley Park and The Water Works, as well as along Allen Parkway, Memorial Drive, and city streets surrounding Buffalo Bayou Park.

Big park with paved running/biking and jogging trail around the Marshall Lake. Very beautiful. There are few fishing piers and you can also go canoeing. Along the trail you will find garbage bins and drinking-water areas (Better bring a water bottle to fill the water from the station).

The park is well-maintained and clean. There is a restroom near the main parking lot.

Have few dedicated parking areas. One near to the entrance and the other one near the lake and the main parking lot at the middle.

Nice park with a large Football ground, Tennis Court, baseball field, basketball field, two kids play areas and a paved walking trail around the park. There are few benches around the park with shades. Kids will love this place.

The park is clean and well-maintained. I couldn't find the vehicle park, only street parking available I guess. There is a small park near the school area but I don't think that one is assigned to this park. I didn't saw any public restrooms also.

Nice beautiful park with kids play area, butterfly garden, cricket & soccer fields. There is a running trail. You can see few seating around the park as well as exercise equipments around the trail.

The park is clean and well maintained. Kids swing area is covered with a shed. There is a Spider Web Rope Climber too. You can see two picnic sheds with tables near the play area.

Average parking area. There is a public restroom. No playground for kids under 5.

Large park with a pavilion, running trail (N Trail), a lot of benches around the park to relax, Small trail near the pavilion so that you can do a small jogging. There is a splash pad but it is not working at the moment. Few drinking water fountains around the trail and a restroom.

Apart from the trail there are four large baseball fields, four football parks, The Alkek Velodrome, it is a 333 meter concrete track.

Good parking space for vehicles.

Nice little nature park with a lot of walking trails. Calm and quiet. For parking, set the location to 'Houston Audubon Society' if you are visiting here. You can't see the entrance very clearly but when you see the wooden board of 'Houston Audubon Society' that is the place where you have to enter.

Most of the areas around the park is clean and well-maintained. Average vehicle park may be for 10-12 vehicles. There is a restroom.

Small park inside the "McGovern Centennial Gardens", opposite to the "Houston Museum of Natural Science". There are lots of different trees, flowers etc. Also there is a beautiful artificial 30 ft. mount with city views featuring a water cascade.

Very clean and well managed. Parking (Free) and restrooms are located on Cherie Flores Garden Pavilion

Street metered parking available along the Hermann Dr.

One of the best park in the downtown area. There are 2 splash areas where children can play in the water and a small children's playground and a sonic playground. Don't forget to check the 'Mist Tree' near the children's playground.

Also you can go for a boat ride around the small lake for $5/per person.

Finding parking around the park is difficult but there are few parking lots around the park.

Very large park. A nice place to visit with family and kids. You can see some farm animals and birds. Specially tortoise, Ducks, swans, ponies, pigs, goats, and birds (All of them are rescued birds). They have small kids play area as well.

The place is clean and neat. Lots of seating and parking lots. No need to worry about parking as well. Not so crowded, lots of space for walking, jogging etc

There are two children's parks with a splash pad. One is for ages 2-3 and the other one is for 5-12. There are lots of seating around the play areas so parents can rest while their children playing. Restrooms are near the large play area and there are few in the large pavilion.

Very clean and well managed. Location is inside the "Hermann Park". Free 3hr parking at Lot A.

A wonderful place to bring your kids. I went on one of the public days, the ride is free where they just take donations. They sell some drinks and shirts, etc.

Lines are long but the wait time is short because there are so many trains. It's a 1-mile ride and the best time is when the train runs through the woods. The ride was great. There are bathrooms.

Small little park with a walking/running trail around the park. Nice and calm, not so crowded. Historic Gazebo - Quiosco (Gazebo with concrete columns and railings to look like tree trunks) is also nearby. There is no kids play area but have a splash pad, basketball court, Baseball Fields etc.

There is a parking lot. There is Porta Potties.

Nice small park with a walking track around the park. Plenty of shade. You can see few seating around the park as well. No Kids play area. Couldn't find anyone because it is in the middle of a very busy street.

The park is clean and well maintained. There is no dedicated parking area. No public restrooms.

Nice park, Park has a walking trail, big pavilion with lots of benches, kids play area, Dog park etc.There are few big green grass banks, kids will love it.

Big parking area so you don't need to worry about parking and a restroom. Well maintained. There are some sign-boards about "alligators" Beware!

Beautiful park with kids play area, walking trail, fishing pier, and big football fields. There are lots of seats around the park as well as around the trail. The park is clean and well-maintained.

There is a big pavilion near the kids play area.

Have a dedicated parking area. There is a Restroom.

Very cool place, well equipped with military equipment from WW1 up to today. A really knowledgeable and friendly crew. Our tour guide was knowledgeable and explained the vehicles and events in great detail.

*** Call ahead of time before you go there.

Small but have a dedicated parking lot.

Nice place to visit, even though there are no lots of exhibits around. There is a touch tank, kids will love that. The entrance to this facility is free. There is a hatchery tour but you have to reserve in-advance. Tours will last about 45 minutes.

The volunteer staff were fantastic!

Nice park with a disc-golf course. You can see few seating in the front and there is a creek.

Be careful if you are going with your kids, there are venomous snakes inside the woods. Average parking area. There is no public restroom available at this location.

Small park with kids play area, soccer field, Swings etc. Not so crowded also. There is a pavilion with few picnic benches.

You can find a 'Officer Lucy Dog Park' next to it.

They have their own parking lot. Small one but manageable. Has a Porta Potty.

Beautiful park, good for biking jogging or walking. There is a small kids play area too.

Parking won't be an issue because there is a large parking lot. Limited seating around the play area but you can find a restroom and a water fountain.

Big park with paved running/biking and jogging trail. The trail is very long and beautiful. The park is well-maintained and clean. There is a portable toilet near the main parking lot.

Have dedicated parking area but is it not paved.

Great place to go with family. Beautiful scenery! No kids playing area though. Very clean and quiet. Not so crowded. There is a small lake so that people can do fishing. There may be Alligators around the lake. Average parking area.

Small Park with kids play area, Walking trail around the park, and an open playground. Park is fairly clean.

There is a small pavilion with tables/seats. Didn't saw any restrooms or porta potties. No dedicated vehicle park.

Small little park with a walking/running trail around a wetland. Nice and calm, not so crowded. There is a pavilion with an observation deck. There is no kids play area.

There is a parking lot. There is no restroom.

My wife and I went bicycling from Bayou Parkland and rode accross the bridge into Hermann Park. Bayou Parkland was a convenient place to park for access to the trails and the restroom there was clean. I can't say if it was typical but at least on this day there was plenty of parking.  I was a little bit concerned about security because there was a person sitting in his car that wasn't going anywhere. I did not see any security cameras.
After circling the park we rode along the bayou for a few miles then back. It was a beautiful sunny day and overall the trails were in pretty good shape.  the trails could have been been maintained better but they weren't bad.  As we got farther away from Bayou Parkland, the trail system had more grade crossings than I was used to on the trails around San Antonio.

This is one of the most beautiful state parks in Texas. It is heavily wooded with a small lake in the middle. Camp sites are well spaced out giving some measure of privacy. There is a well stocked park store, swimming area, playground,  boat launch ramp (no wake), canoe, kayak and paddle boat rental.
There are full and partial hook-up sites for RV or trailer, tent sites, cabins and group facilities.
Most of the year this is a very peaceful place. I was here over July 4 and it wasn't too noisy. Fewer insects than most of the Texas state parks.

McAllister Park has something for eveyone. My recent visit was to use the trailhead for access to the Salado Creek Greenway Trail for a group ride. The trailhead has abundant parking and is conveniently located near the Wurzbach Parkway entrance. McAllister Park also has a dog park lots of ball fields and I've even seen people playing cricket in the open fields near the dog park. There are many trails for walking, running and hiking. There's also a children's playground.

This Mission has the most colorful history of the 6 San Antonio missions.  Much of the history is portrayed by the NPS signage around the grounds, but the much of the story can only be learned from the archives or a guide who is familiar with local history. The Acequia is worth a look, as is the modern "Tree of Life" sculpture. Descendants of the original first citizens of "New Spain" (native indians) still attend mass at the church in this  mission.

This is a fascinating place. There are a number of people groups that immigrated to Texas not to mention a number of native groups that were here already and there's information and displays and narratives about all of them at the Institute of Texan cultures. The layout is thoughtful and comfortable. I was there during the Folklife Festival and they had six stages going with cultural presentations on each of them. It's a lot of fun.

This is a great place to access the Salado Creek Trail and the trails of Hardberger Park. There are deer often present, and there are usually plenty of parking places, although you have to find the hidden driveway behind Blanco BBQ. There is a bathroom (portapotty). The Salado Creek Trail is around 20 miles continuous paved and is great for walking, running or biking.

My wife and I like to walk and ride our bikes on the Leon Creek Greenway Trail.  Fox Park Trailhead usually has open parking places and is easy to get to now the nearby road construction is complete.  Situated between the Babcock Rd and UTSA Blvd access points it is the northern most point on the trail before you hit the iffy construction area around UTSA Blvd.

If you're looking for peaceful, this is it. This state park is off the beaten track and is adjacent to the Walter Buck Wildlife Management Area. There's lots of wildlife and swimming hole and river to play in.  If you were here more than a couple of years ago then the swimming hole will look different. You can't shoot under the bridge anymore in a tube.
dislikes: No longer can tube under bridge

reviews_attraction.text: This is a nice park with a little bit more ecologically sensitive landscaping than most of the parks around San Antonio. There's some educational exhibits about being sensitive to the ecosystem. Of course there's restrooms. I didn't see any playground or stuff for little kids. It is a trailhead for the Mission Reach Trail along the San Antonio River.

Mission  Concepcion is the most architecturally complete and original of the missions of San Antonio. It was built on bedrock and did not decompose as the other missions did that were built on sand. There are many amazing features including window that spots light on the statue of the Virgin Mary on the fall and Spring equinoxes

Lost Maples is an appropriate name, as I don't know of any other place in Texas where you could find Maple trees.  In the early night time hours there are fireflies.  This is a small park with limited facilities but very pleasant with great hiking trails. It is quite rural and usually uncrowded.

The park is lovely and the facilities are well maintained.  The San Pedro Springs were flowing today because of the recent rains and the high aquifer level. My only complaint is that the park seems to be a gathering place for homeless people. Some of them are quite vocal and rude.

A unique and interesting bit of living history that I thoroughly enjoyed. This historic mission is still an active Catholic parish church. Each of the missions of San Antonio have their own character, and you can get a feel for what life was like here 300 years ago.

This is one of the nicest parks in San Antonio. For those of us who like bicycling it's the southern terminus of the south segment of the Salado Creek Trail. There's a lake that lots of people like fishing in. Lots of Open Spaces and a kids playground.

I use Roosevelt Park as my start/finish point on the Mission Reach Trail. I have always been able to find a parking place, even during Fiesta and other holidays. It's a nice park for family outings with picnic tables and big trees for shade.

The history is fascinating.   To see the means of irrigation from before there was a United States helps to put the history in context. I am pretty sure there are no other surviving aquaducts of this time period anywhere in North America.

This is one of the few Salado Creek Greenway Trail trailheads with parking in the shade. There is a water fountain with a bowl at the bottom for your dog. The rest of the park includes a dog park, ball fields, skateboard park and a pool.

Plenty of parking... this is a good meet up point for group bike rides on the Salado Creek Greenway Trail. There is water and port-a-potty. The trailhead is easily found at the end of the parking lot closest to the dog park.
The observatory is small but it is well equipped and the staff was knowledgeable.  On this night we viewed Mars and also several constellations were identified. I enjoyed the experience.
The Tobin Park Trailhead is well maintained and has primitive facilities (Porta-potty). The location is very convenient right off of Interstate 410, but there is not sufficient parking.
This is one of the most scenic areas associated with the Leon Creek Greenway Trail. I like to take the turn-off from Leon Creek Greenway Trail to come up here just for the scenic view.
Playground for the kids, quiet spots, walk, run or bike the mission reach, kayak down the ladder, picnic ... this park has something for just about anyone but a coach potato!
A very nice city park with children's play areas and ball fields, a large pavilion and restrooms. Large green areas include and outdoor movie venue.
The park is nice by the river with shaded picnic tables and many trees.  I docked 2 stars because the restrooms were locked.
Pleasant environment, cheerful servers, good wine but a tad pricey. They could use a bit more space at the bar.

Took my 9 yr old son to the museum. He's as much a history buff as I am so he thoroughly enjoyed our visit. It's a little smaller than the Frontiers of Flight museum in Dallas, but it does offer more military aircraft. We enjoyed our tour and took several photos to record our visit as one of the summer activities we enjoyed together. I'd recommend a visit to the museum if you enjoy learning about history and your looking for something to do without spending too much time or money. Also be sure to spend some time in the art gallery, as that is a unique display that isn't readily available at other more high profile museums (i.e. Smithsonian). One thing I do recommend, especially if you aren't local to DFW, is that in the summer plan your visit in the morning as much of the displays are outside, so the Texas summer heat can be miserable for out of state visitors.

A truly humbling and somber experience... If you find yourself in the heart of Texas, make sure you take a tour of the JFK Memorial and pay your respects to one of our nations most celebrated presidents and one of the most tragic heartbreaking disasters of our time.Retrace the path of his motorcade as it took its final turn down elm Street in those final moments that have been engrained in our memories since November 22, 1963. Walk the streets and reconstruct the scene of the crime in your own mind as you listen to the stories retold by street venders and historical markings at the grassy knoll. A tragedy still marred by conspiracies, you will leave this memorial with more questions and a stronger desire to uncover the truth about what happened at Houston and Elm...

We’ve lived in Dallas for five years and didn’t visit the village until my sister and niece were in town. I admit that I didn’t realize what an interesting place this is. There is a large number of buildings and exhibits, many of which one can go inside. The volunteers are very friendly and knowledgeable and showed great patience answering my nine year old niece’s many questions. My niece got to feed the chickens, and grind corn which she fed to the sheep. She also helped to chop wood! We actually ran out of time as the village was closing, but we will definitely go back to see the rest of the exhibits. Please go and support this worthy cause - so much of the local history has been lost, and this place captures a time long gone.

How proud we are to be Texans! Our State Capitol building and grounds are praise worthy. We had not planned to take a tour, because we had visited many times before, but we are so glad we did. We first visited informally with one guide, who is a retired history teacher, and, because of his encouragement, we decided to take the next tour available. Becky was our guide, and she was a wealth of knowledge. Instead of a 1/2 hour tour, she spent a whole hour with us. The visit to the Capitol and the tour were definite highlights of our short trip to Austin. We highly recommend enjoying one of the tours offered by the outstanding staff.

We were heading to the Holocaust Museum and actually came upon Grassy Knoll in error. However we loved seeing this part of history which I absolutely remember as being one of those "Where were you when JFK died" moments. Lucked upon one of the replica newspaper guys who spent a long time giving us the history and locations of all the incidents that happened that day. The coffee shop/book shop across the road is actually fantastic with great quality gifts and memorabilia. The Knoll itself was packed with conspiracy theorists keen to give their take on the whole unfortunate event. Well worth a visit.

Even if you don’t know much about the day or the occurrences, it is very neat to be there in person and soak it all in. I enjoyed walking around and reading the plaques and learning more. This is still a very busy road with lots of traffic, but plenty of opportunities to snap pictures.In true city fashion there was some garbage and homelessness debris, which is sad in such a historical place. There will will be people trying to convince you to give them some money for old newspapers from the 60s and their own version of a “tour” and information. Kindly deny them and they will leave you alone.
