The museum is huge. I only got through a very small portion of it; the music section. It was really neat to look at the videos, exhibits and read about old and new performers. There are 4 floors broken up by African American slavery, Civil Rights Movement, the museum store, sports and the top floor explores music. I would estimate it takes a solid 4-5 hours to see everything. The museum is open from 10 a.m. until 5:30 p.m. every day of the year except for Christmas Day, December 25. Admissions is free although you will need to print out a ticket. An eye opening and educational experience.

The greenbelt is incredible and it's an activity that is different each time. You can go for an easy or medium hike, go swimming, mountain biking, rock climbing, the list keeps going! There are so many entrance points and often lead to a very nice swimming hole. In peak summer time, July and August, often the water has dried up so this isn't the best time to go. After the rains in the fall, September, October, November, or early spring, March, April, May are the best times for swimming. Would recommend packing up some snacks and drinks and making a day of it!
dislikes: Water dries up in peak summer

reviews_attraction.text: Very easy to get to. Prices were fair. Combo deals saved money. All the employees were very courtious and polite. Rides were awesome! I could tell safety was always a priority. I could hear the radios going off when they were communicating. Making sure that one of the other staff members was watching from a second angle to make sure everything looked right. With our couples package We got videos, i am too big to do all the rides but they were very accomidating and let my friend  ride an extra ride in my place. Overall worth the visit and screams!

We visited the Sixth Floor Museum in August. We really liked the way the tour was organised, audio tour is included in the ticket price and the audio is recorded by a journalist who was reporting back from J. F. Kennedy visit in Dallas on the day the tragedy happened. Hearing him itself gave us goosebumps. The tour is very informative and interesting. And you can look through the window from which the President was killed. I would highly recommend visiting this place.

Amazing view of the city, but not much to do up there than looking at the view. I bet the best time would be during the evening with all of the beautiful lights of the city. I would highly recommend going to see Downtown Dallas from the Geo Deck!! Gabby V and Jody Lee both helped to make this experience for my wife and I absolutely amazing! They were so helpful and informative, we would highly suggest going here and don’t forget to say hi to these wonderful ladies!!

We did this last year. I loved it. We did the boat tour and our guide was amazing. He told tales about the city. It was great. Would recommend giving it a shot. Just don’t open your mouth when you are under the bridge. This is my favorite places to relax in Austin. Sit back relaxing and reflect on life and how good God has been to me and what he has brought me from. Take this spot personal. I recommend couples to come up there especially since fall is approaching

Very nice park, great for family gatherings or just a quick couple get away,$10 fee to enter,restrooms with showers and open air changing rooms.Built in grills/BBQ pits,sand volleyball,closed in beach swim area with to lighted piers(no life guards). Lots of ski boats & jet ski's going by,like every 5 minutes. Lots of large shade trees,RV camping at the very end of the park,tent camping also.Busy all summer long,get there before 10 am,nice long drive to the park.

We visited this beautifully designed nature campus today as the laughter of children drew us in. Kids of all ages, some camp counselors and some visiting parents with children were exploring the grounds, the trails, the native birds and animals that have been rescued and rehabilitated over the years, the creek, a large pond filled with fish and a paleontology dig site where kids could try their hand at unearthing large “bones”. It was really fantastic.

The Dallas Museum of Art is a must see destination. The rotating special exhibits bring evocative subjects to life. The permanent collections are worthy of numerous visits as you can't really take it all in at once...and there are favorites to return to such as in the American art galleries--O'Keefe, Church, Moran, and others. The café offers some great lunch choices but the food trucks along side Klyde Warren Park next door are totally accessible.

This museum is awesome. We scheduled their short “Star” film for 11 and IMAX of American Journey for 2 pm, all in the same building. Together with a Noon stop at the cafe, made for a great day. The museum is beautifully laid out with artifacts galore. Lots of small films and activities in each section. We arrived about 9:30 which was perfect. Recommend start on floor one (oldest history). Progress to floor 2, finish on floor 3 (most recent events).

We went for a walk around this lake. Saw a ton of turtles on logs, variety of ducks and some birds. We also noticed two snakes swimming in the lake and some flowers among the grass. Very enjoyable walk. Lots of joggers, bike riders and walkers. Plenty of room for all of us to enjoy the lake and nature along the way. White Rick Lake has good walking and biking trails. The few houses in the area are huge, lovely. Great place to relax.

This is a fascinatingly curated and constructed pile of junk in someones private backyard. Reach out to him ahead of time. We didn't realize we needed to do it but he was kind enough to let us walk around since there was already another small group there. There is so much to look at and his story about its growth over the years is interesting. Small suggested donation- well worth it. It's also a 15ish minute drive out of downtown

Hippie Hollow is not a beach. There is no sand. It is more like a quarry with rocky formations that need to be navigated to get to the water. But the rocks are often flat and level so the sunning areas are more than adequate. I do recommend bringing water shoes and a thick yoga mat, in addition to towels. Pack a cooler with your lunch and your favorite beverage (alcohol is allowed) and you're all set. Don't forget the sunscreen!

We came to Circuit of the Americas (COTA) for the Inaugural Indycar race. The facility is very expanse and you can walk a bit to get from place to place in the track. We sat in turn one and you can see a lot of the track from there. We were in Grandstand 15 - Awesome view of the stadium portion of the course... Perfect spot to see the racers for a decent period of time .... Weather was awesome , people are very friendly ...

We booked the combo pass for LEGOLAND and the aquarium. Worth it! We went at 11 AM to LEGOLAND first and absolutely enjoyed it. 4D movie, building lego cars, seeing all the displays. Fantastic. Kids 10 & 15. Spent 1.5 hours there then went over to aquarium. It's in a mall so it's small but really enjoyable. Took about 45-60 min to walk through. Kids loved LEGOLAND more but if you have time, it is worth seeing aquarium too.

This site is a great place to take a break, get out and enjoy nature without traveling out of town. It's especially amazing to thinking about and experience when you learn the history of the site as an illegal dumping ground. The trails are all well marked and in great shape, even despite all the rain the area had been having. None of them were too difficult either. It was a nice way to spend a couple of hours.

Tucked at the foot of Mount Bonnell in Austin is Mayfield Park and Preserve. Parking is free but dogs are not allowed. Peacocks roam this property freely and perch on the rooftops and fences and are fun to photograph. There are beautiful gardens to explore and ponds with ornamental carp and lily pads. This outing can easily be combined with a visit to neighboring Covert Park at the top of Mount Bonnell Rd.

Want to relax on the weekend or just do a walk for your lunch hour, well this place can offer both of those options. Food trucks are available with a variety of food, there is a kids play ground and a bunch of open space for you to play catch or sit on the lawn with your pup. Oh, and there is plenty of tables and chairs if you prefer that to sitting on the green space.

The Arboretum is a must-see for anyone living in or visiting Dallas. The most beautiful displays of flowers and seasonal decorations are available to see at the Arboretum. Also, overlooking White Rock Lake makes it a perfect place to have a picnic, or you can purchase food and drinks which are reasonably priced. The Gift Store is also a hidden gem.

Would be worth visiting for the third of the admission price as the place does have some interesting artifacts, fun activities (I liked the sound lab the most) and, I admit, it might be a super cool place if you are big fan of certain artists or genres (or if you are an artistic type yourself). For the regular guy it just doesn't have much of the interesting content for the price you have to pay to get here.
dislikes: Limited interesting content for general audience

reviews_attraction.text: This is a pretty cool place to stop. Nice public park that used to be the former Seattle Gas Light Company. The remnants of the only remaining coal gasification plant in the US is here. There's a playground for kids (or us adults when the kids aren't watching) and a nice walk to the top of a hill overlooking Lake Union. Pretty neat way to enjoy the sunshine.

House is made with more then 50,000 beer cans all consumed on the property making it really unique property. They have a tour and video created by the creator of the house and actual beer cans from the 80s and 90s. I think it's a must see if your in Houston.

Bring tour own toys, table games and music. Two sinks with tap water a huge grill and a preparation table.  Clean restrooms. Check weather, it could be very hot. Reserve for $125.00 and get your money refund when you let the place as you get it.

A small bottle of soda is $5 and the least expensive ride is $4 per person. With a family of 4 you will spend $200 easily on the rides alone...add $200 for dinner and snacks...I would plan on $500 per day if you really want to enjoy yourself.

We visited there in Sunday evening, there were many activities for kids. The garden is beautiful. There is live music. Inside the house, there were guides every room to explain the history. It is a good place for recreation and education.

It's probably the coolest tourist attraction in Houston. The staff are super knowledgeable. We go every time there's a special event or we have friends in town who've never seen it. The pictures don't do it justice. See it for yourself.

The Victorian Radicals exhibit was spectacular as were the the other displays I looked out. The staff was helpful and polite even when pointing out to people that they were to close to a item. I will definitely be back...... soon!

Plenty of interpretive signage explains how the locks work and their history.  There is also a fish ladder where you can see fish migrating into the lake (and occasionally a seal!).  Also check out the adjacent botanical gardens.

Doesn't look big but you can spend some time Here seeing and learning!! Very cool displays, easy yo read descriptions and very interesting.  Lots of cool real artifacts and hurses.  Very inexpensive to enter and well worth it.

I love botanical gardens, it was really relaxing and stress free place. It was just a busy and a quick visit just to be in here. Experiencing and feel the fresh atmosphere from all beautiful creatures around. Love this place.

I don’t use the trials though I really should. The playground area could use some improvements. The bathrooms are really nice, the trails are clean. The surrounding bayou areas is clean as well. A nice relaxed place to be.

Definitely bring swim shoes for the kiddos, Houston weather keeps the ground scorching hot and will burn their little feet. Otherwise, no complaints. Try to make it here a few times a month. My little guy loves it here!
Snapping at guests to mind the camouflaged partition that's the exact same color of the hardwood floor in order to protect the art is a great way to get patrons to dislike a very impressive museum.
He didn't want to leave.  We spent 3 hours there and I know we didn't see or do everything.  The cafeteria is also decent with a few choices for every age.  Definitely going there again!
Nice place to spend some time and relax. You can take some pictures and just hang out around. You can find free parking in the red garage at The Galleria, it is really close to the park.
Tons of exhibits with daily schedule for "Ask the Astronaut "; several times a day.  Plentiful parking, and a " Kodak Moment " as you pull in, as well as after you park your vehicle.
Definitely the best in the area, the Lenin statue is also a few blocks away and definitely worth checking out! The troll is  marvelous, enormous, and located in a lovely location.
Take a romantic photo during the day or bring your tripod to get the best night shots of the city. Walk along Nob Hill and see the beautiful bespoke homes of the well heeled.
The gum wall is a unique idea planted at the heart of a unique place, the Pike place market. Loved the few minutes spent there. Some very colorful memories to carry along...
Fairly new, extremely clean. Docents are volunteers and were all very knowledgeable. Could easily spend an entire day between the tour and exhibits.
Amazing new design, the exhibits are awesome and the staff is very welcoming and always so helpful. I've learned so much by going there.
Great place to get individuals attention and peak the interest of young minds to the anatomy and physiology of the human being.
This is a great weekend getaway to take kids to learn some history and see an actual ship real close. Great parking.
Went here on field trip with a summer camp I'm working with and the kids loved learning the history of the houses!

It's worthwhile though you are in an area that is intended as a quick tour through the house with no photography allowed (you can go online to discover virtual tours if need be,) and shouldn't consider the experience as a "ride through history" because you probably won't be able to sit back and reflect on it as much while there. A lot of history can be read up on and it is probably expected if nothing else; and I advise anyone to realize you are in an environment where excavation is going on still, and much of the subject surrounding Thomas Jefferson is still mercurial (one would argue it was due to the British Colonial laws that forbade Jefferson from selling his slaves, and genealogy has concluded that Sally Hemmings did have children related to Jefferson--apparently blamed on an relative of Jefferson--etc. and that those children were fathered after the country became independent should still raise eyebrows if Jefferson composed in the Declaration of Independence that "all men are created equal," the words he is known for. I might be mistaken in this, and believe he is maligned for things we can only speculate on at this point because it's evident that many "slaves" were merely fulfilling societal roles at a time when they might have considered themselves fortunate in certain ways; however when they likely had little choice in the matter. . . I don't want to seem "out of place," if I misinterpret it.

Old review (which I am editing because I'm pretty sure I forgot one of the bottles was $20, which would have brought it in close range of $40 with tax added) and being edited because no one should ever travel with little sleep and trying to explore as many places when new to an area. I still believe much of Virginia's history is being used to generate tons of money, as tourism is a major business; and I'm the kind that likes to roast my own coffee beans and brew my own beverages, though it was fully my choice so I will let anyone else determine whether I was right to be critical:

I was overcharged for two cider bottles ($12.95 x2 and it was $40); I had already paid $28 for entry and $20 for 1lb of coffee beans and a root beer which was great,) though it was an enlightening experience if you simply want to experience what the house has to offer. . . Though really, I just spent $90 dollars after driving 2000 miles on an 18 hour drive trip that I planned around  to see other things in the east coast, that cost less for gas to get here from Texas? And I suspect the reason for the overcharge is that I was carrying a bag from the vendor as  I was leaving the cellar area, and they "assumed" that by my having absconded with an item as result of the a bag in my hand from the less than 1 minute walk up to the cash register; that I must have been stealing something else? Perhaps it was just an "oversight." Keep an eye on your wallet. . .

I've probably driven over this area numerous times, as it's just beneath a highway, crossing over the 'Elm Fork' branch of the Trinity river system, where you can spot alligator gar (a fish that can resemble alligator and grow to be as big.) This is a very similar--small--trail to the Elm Fork Nature Preserve which is adjacent to baseball fields, only this area seems a bit more wet and difficult to walk across without getting muddy if it has rained recently, so parts of the trail system are flooded, during these times.

I also spotted what looked like some kind of hooved foot prints, though I don't believe any hogs were in this area, at least they are more common south of here. What are shown on the signs are beaver that are in the pond and river system which I didn't see, and I suspect are nutria (very similar to beaver) have been spotted in places like the Carrollton public library; the one next to a retirement community on Josey, not the one off Hebron pkwy,) which I have photographed devouring the cattail plants. The red tail hawk shows up here and I saw it at the Elm Fork Nature Preserve. Both areas are great, though this one is great, if not a bit obscure with the steep drive down (and I just happened across the sign and was looking for a place to start photographing.)

One thing to mention is you can walk the entire trail and not encounter anyone. It also helps to download a Google Lens app whenever you spot anything interesting. If you are closer to downtown Dallas, Joppa Preserve is a great place to go to, and it's far more accessible and has a park atmosphere with cement walking paths. The Google directions seemed to point towards an entrance way further down from the actual entrance, so it might be easy to overlook. . . I just edited the google maps location to the correct address, of 1199 Valley View.

This place reminds me of the historical sites on the east coast, which usually cost money to see, and often you have less to explore openly (though I suspect most of these exhibits can normally be seen through the windows which are hard to see without long-exposure images such as ones I uploaded and plan to add to my background image collection.) A lot is available to explore and this is the perfect place to showcase history; and I have no idea why I waited so long to check it out despite knowing about it for some time now. The General Store also reminds me of photos I came across when researching one my family would have owned from around the same time period (though just before the end of the 19th century) and it was great to photograph it, and even the buntings look like period pieces; in fact it reminded me of a video game called Bioshock Infinite which was turn of the century based, and used a lot of patriotic symbolism. Don't hesitate, it has something for everyone, and I plan to find out when events are taking place.

Update: While attending a 'Star Party,'  just before dark, I snapped some photos with my cell phone (I forgot to bring my D-SLT camera.) I'll admit that I can capture images with my cell phone that I can't get with my D-SLT (DSLR variant.) I can't really say it's "better" but it does tend to make it easier (most great photos are achieved using a tripod, and due to lens design you can get much easier compositions, but it becomes less contrasty and has lower depth of field, hence a "shallower" focal plane.) — at Farmers Branch Historical Park.

Update: baseball

I was indecisive of where to park when checking out this lake (basically three options exist, though primarily it's this one which has an art deco era kayak storage unit not available to the public and covering for picnics in addition to neat water utility buildings to check out, or alternatively you can park on the opposite side of the lake where a 'Bath House' has been converted into a cultural museum which I didn't check out. I did stop by the third area which is north of this one and is just general parking adjacent to the trail for biking or jogging, with nothing unique other than the ubiquitous piers that seem to exist on all areas to park at.

Since I didn't want to get wet by staying long (it was drizzly) I did intend on either sitting at the picnic area under the rain, or using my bike (even though I intended to bring cycling gear, the way I was dressed was not suited for this occasion either.) It's a 10 mile area circling the lake and an ideal spot to check out for the peculiar features of the landscape.

I was also reminded to stop here as result of the ghost legend referred to as the 'Lady of White rock Lake,' whom would have died around the time many of the buildings and features of the landscape were constructed (1930's.) Even in spite of noticing the age of the structures it's well kept and has modern updates, such as the roads being modern and the trail being well maintained.
likes: Facilities & Services: Well-maintained trails, modern updates
dislikes: Facilities & Services: Limited public access (kayak storage)
Activities: Lack of unique features in some areas

reviews_attraction.text: An excellent place to observe nature or photograph it, with many areas that would be ideal for photographing people for special events in their lives (truly some extremely idealic spots depending on where you look.) Plenty of squirrels, lizards, koi, insects, and plants of course. I was expecting more birds to be present though I mostly just spotted a hawk near an outskirt zone, and the wooden walk path near the middle of the place can give you a sense of entering a jungle, where birds are evidently heard. If getting tired, plenty of benches are scattered throughout, and near the end at the Japanese garden (included in the $12 price) you can buy a drink which you will probably need to avoid dehydration (perhaps one thing to consider is bringing your own water, and they have them available when you buy the ticket, however most things will be about $2.) I had underestimated this place somewhat and consider it better than just walking through a park environment, and I missed the greenhouse near the end, so I consider planning on seeing that before seeing the main walking path. I suggest a 3 hour window to enjoy most of it, however, I was also photographing, so I consider 1-2 hours very feasible for those that aren't just walking through it.

I should point out that the restaurant next to it is how you will enter the museum, and there you can get a drink before seeing the museum after checking out the area nearby (plan on coming here if you drive into Ft Worth for any reason, as most places will be right along side this location.) It's a very intriguing glimpse into a time in retail that seems to forget that Walmart wasn't the first "one stop shopping center." I highly recommend looking through the photos and newspapers (advertisements and news articles about the company) and realize that no matter how successful a company is, it's days will eventually come to an end, even when they had a business model that wasn't too different from more modern companies (admittedly the subway transport system confuses me still. . . and I wasn't able to get a good idea of how that worked, but I suspect it might have compromised their business with people relying more and more on private transportation instead of public transit, with people increasingly moving to suburban areas.) Also, Ft Worth has been greatly effected with business moving more towards Dallas after the cattle industry relied less upon trains and more on trucks.

This is an amazing area of Dallas adjacent to the former Ambassador Hotel (the location of many former Presidents that had visited this location, and it was largely abandoned in the 1980's, intending to be restored to it's former glory) which burned down recently. Within the park exists many glimpses into a life that was very different from today, and a history that exists and is encouraged to be preserved. The $10 entry fee is well worth preserving history, and this site can also be used for wedding events and other catering. Four Corners Brewery opens up after this place closes at 4 pm, and it's not far from downtown Dallas.

Some amazing homes are present with some pioneers of industry (a 1880's home is likely the first to have central plumbing with an original bathroom from that time, and had a recent roof flooding that costs upwards of $200k to restore.)

Just ask for the amazing crew, Gene and Peggy, whom are helping keep this site alive and constantly improving to maintain it's preservation of history. Literally it's like walking back in time and it reflects some ancestry that I've seen remnants of in the east coast that are rare glimpses into this pre-1900's era.

The entire site of the settlement is accessed from this building, and you cannot see any part of it without paying an entrance fee, however it is certainly worth it. One thing I noticed with the area is that you are expected to go along on the tour and remain in groups, and though straying from the tour in order to save time but also to photograph is certainly possible, you might feel a bit awkward. One part of the site that I overlooked is the Ambler mansion structure that became a ruin following a fire over a century ago, though even when it was constructed it was rather "new" on this location and was built during the early 18th century. The majority of the sight is centered around the church, but most of the history shines in the museum where the excavation uncovered artifacts, as well as reveal some of the grisly history of the location (which you are not permitted to photograph.) I wish I had a bit more time to look over some of it better and read the notes on it though that was my fault for piling up my schedule to visit the location. The drive on the way to this settlement really contributes to the feel of the area.

Though characteristically religious as would be expected, a lot of existentialism is the more predominant theme, along with some very large paintings that you have likely seen before, including massive paneled artwork which is less common. Some of the rooms were less impressive, and the vast majority of the bottom half of the building is intended as conference rooms , and even ones that weren't, the walls were bare or blocked off. At the SMU campus, on weekends you are allowed to park on the side of the museum during the day without any special parking requirements (however I did spot a vehicle that had a citation, and perhaps it was because they had left it parked there overnight?) Overall it's some excellent artwork that demonstrates some excellent representations of the subject matter, and the location is very quiet, so it is probably worthwhile to those hoping to avoid more crowded places such as other museums around Dallas (which are also usually free.)

This is part of the (usually $12) entrance fee, and they have performed tea ceremonies and a cultural exhibit which had cost more and was limited to a short time frame, which I missed out on now that I looked back. Included is a koi pond, a zen stone (sand) garden, and various pond and waterfall themes, in addition to the Japanese gardening methods. Don't go here thinking it's a quick walk just to focus on this area, and instead think of it as the "finale" to the Ft Worth Botanic Garden, where you will probably need to get a soft drink at the gift shop before heading back to the parking lot before passing out (It's a bit more involved and confusing if you hadn't been here before, and I would plan on about 2-3 hours at the least, especially if you are photographing the place, which I suggest is a good hobby when visiting somewhere like this.)

FIRST OF ALL, this is not your typical museum. . . No, ignore that within the corridors is a law office, and other offices (which reminds me of the Stanley Parable, PC game. . .) rather, as you peruse the unassuming exhibit, you will find many art that will demand your attention (literally) and will fold out like animatronics, or will be noticed from behind a veil (should you peak?) and realize it's dancing in the dark, and you must give it your attention least you find yourself oblivious to the reality that it exists, and forever perplexed to the strange sounds from behind that veil (impressively, the exhibits originate from the 1960's, and have been fully operational from that time.) Don't miss this exhibit, and also check out the gift shop to the left, after you've walked up the stairs from the entrance to your right. It's FREE!

Within quick walking distance from DMA and across the street from Nasher sculpture (which costs $10,) and just like DMA it is entirely free, so theirs really no excuse not to. You basically start at the samurai armor and walk around, and up the stairs, making your way to a large cloth tapestry exhibit, and then down the stairs to more of the same, to then exit with the option of buying something from the gift shop such as matcha tea and the usual variety of ceramics. Some parking meters are accessible near this area, and both the Crow Museum and Nasher will take approximately 1 hour if you are diligent with time, though a safe bet is 2 hours if you were to rush through some of the DMA, where it might be much easier to park at and not worry about a parking meter (if you are willing to cross traffic these are usually an option.)

I've been here since trips during elementary school and have always had a distinct impression of the amphibian and reptile exhibit. I have a few photos I particularly enjoyed, and may come back to update the review with new photos (note: updated 2020.) These images were capture about 8 years ago. I had a few black and white images as well using 35mm film though believe these will suffice. Many areas of the Zoo really stand out, and I also enjoyed the exhibit with the boat and the coastal birds.

Update: March, 2020, a lot of new changes are taking place with a strong focus on on immersion within each habitat exhibit, such as regional emphasis on areas. I was a bit surprised to spot what looked like remains from Halloween near the children's area, and in more than one spot.

One of the best museums I've visited, and it costs absolutely nothing. Many of the pieces are considered some of the best representations of historic artifacts (I imply that you could literally go from section to section and identify something you've recognized on the cover of a book or highlighting the best artistic example of civilization.) Several times I was surprised to find works of art/sculpture that I had no doubt seen at some point; whether it be a depiction of Mithras, a Roman cup with unique features, or a sculpture that you recognize from somewhere, and an amazing silver and Faberge collection. The museum is very calm with very little foot traffic, and is widely spaced out, so you could literally feel as though you were the only one checking out the exhibits.

This chapel is a memento of Richmond and the space it occupies in the history of this nation, though it will probably be understood in a manner that misappropriates a direction that the Confederate states had occupied at the time of it's inception; no doubt the challenges of considering it's reputation in a different age is likely to upset many. If talking about museums it is likely an important foundation of the culture. I've noticed many of the stain glass windows have (likely been broken out) and replaced with regular glass. No matter what it represents to an individual, it is still an important representation of a time and place lost in time.

I went there in 2012 (and had to dig through my photos to find them as I had titled it Joppa Preserve). If I recall correctly It was a nice trail that I had sought out to find some red ibis (or a similar bird--either way I didn't find any) that were rumored to have flown outside of their coastal region, in search inland for small lakes (they were posing an ecological destruction in some wetlands due to dryer climate requiring them to search for freshwater climate.) Some had photographs from the area online (I think I had uploaded some photos online from an airshow and came across it.) It's a short trail and is far more an outdoor park.

Adjacent to a Grain Mill, the location has a main museum (which seemed to have a close sign but I might have been mistaken, they were still open in the rest of the buildings.) It's mostly a representation of the industries (cotton mill building, printing press stamps and demonstration at select times) and artifacts from the area's history (Indian arrow heads, police force equipment from some time ago, fireman axe, etc.,) whether it be political related such as elections, or a school house. The surrounding area is also worth checking out and this is a good starting point on what to check up on.

It's important to read up on the misconceptions regarding this landmark (in that it was likely only used for food crop storage prior to the Civil War, and that Cornwallis likely used Nelson House to seek refuge which would explain all the interesting "character" the house has acquired from that time period.) The notches in the cave exterior is the result of it being used for military purposes in which it was fortified for the Confederates. Still an interesting landmark in spite of the misnomer.

I visited a few years back and recall the impression I had of looking at some of these paintings; the size and enormity of some of them really needs to be appreciated up close. Though many of these were painted during the early stages of photography, the paintings seem to be one of the best ways for the scenery to come alive. Even when paintings worked well as a median, some of the best photography of native Americans had also been on display.

Find any parking meter and plan at least an hour to walk around the area. Check out the JFK tribute memorial and Burnett Park to see the massive steel sculpture while at it. Even on the weekend the streets are surprisingly barren. Don't pay $10 to park at the Convention Center unless you have a reason to do so, as most anything to see (other than if you went to a restaurant, etc.) can be done in an hour.

It's more than just oil history and an oil derrick; but also including the workshop of H.C. Nicols whom worked as an acetylene torch welder for the oil field from 1912 and appears to have been sitting on this site. The large yellow machinery is called a "Cooper" double drum pulling unit. and the cannon probably has nothing to do with oil, though is a nice addition, including a wooden jail cell.

I was driving through from my trip to Arkansas, back to Dallas, and in a previous drive to the east coast I had planned to visit Eisenhower National Historic Site where he lived the last years of his life in Gettysburg, PA. So many times I had driven past Denison though was always too tired from driving, and I couldn't pass by this time and not see some of it, so I have uploaded some photos.

I believe this was the location of Poe's girlfriend; his house he lived in is located in Baltimore. This location has some interesting features and is great if you simply wanted to explore old buildings that have the old skeleton keys (I'm not from the east coast. . .) Though photography is not permitted, I did snap one of the sculpture.

I remember the excitement that was generated when they discovered a halberd and hauberk armor from within the well; and even though I have known of Jamestown's history from early on, I was especially wanting to check this out. Many other artifacts have stood out in the exhibit as well, and I wish I had more time to check it out.
I wasn't part of a guided tour and only viewed the outside structure, however I certainly felt the presence of the landmark.

Visited this State Park from Nov 16th-Nov 20th for a training course, the Park Staff was very friendly and knowledgeable about the park and history, park grounds were well maintained and clean, hiking and biking trails were awesome, and the facilities were clean and very nice as well. This park is a great place to do night photography as it is an International Dark Sky Park, so you will be able to have some awesome night time viewing of the stars.
Plenty of different activities to do here from camping, fishing, mountain biking, hiking, and more. I was even able to check out the official Texas longhorn herd and learn about their history while at the park.
If you are in the Quanah area and looking for a great place to visit, I would highly recommend Copper Breaks State Park to anyone.
likes: Diverse activities (camping, fishing, mountain biking, hiking)

reviews_attraction.text:
This is an awesome off-road adventure park! I went here with a large group of friends for a weekend. It rained most of the weekend we where there unfortunately, but we still made the best of it and had a lot of fun in our trucks. The park is really well maintained, plenty of trails to explore for all difficulties, and the camp areas have plenty of space. We used Area 51 as we had a lot of people and wanted to be away from everyone and it was a great location close to the creek and under trees.

I would like to return here when the weather is better and maybe not as cold. So will hopefully be able to do that sometime in 2019!

This was a quick stop on my way to another State Park, I was only here for about 2.5 hours, but it was well worth the time to walk around. I did a self guided tour of the main area and walked around the outside of the buildings and learned some of the history of Fort Richardson. Did a short hike along the creek before departing to continue my journey. The park staff was very friendly and answered the few questions I had. I would love to make a return visit here when I could enter the buildings at the Historic Site to be able to learn more about the history of them.

A well worth stop if  you are in Abilene, the hiking trails here are just amazing with plenty of wildlife and things to do. I have been here twice and enjoyed both times for sure. The staff here is amazing as well and some of the nicest people you will ever meet. Would love to come back and hang out by the pool for the day after exploring more of the trails. If you get a chance, go check out the bird blind trail and just sit and watch the birds for a while, well worth it.

I came here to check off a goal for 2019 which was to hike the Guadalupe Peak, I got to the National Park at night and stayed overnight and then started the hike in the morning and without a doubt, this is something that I would loved to do again and camp closer to the peak at the campsite up there. This is an amazing National Park and one that everyone should visit. The views from the top are like none other in Texas.

This is a pretty awesome place to hang out for a day with friends. Was here for a bachelor party and we spent a pretty significant time on the Lazy River and it was well worth the $20 admission! Was not very crowded, but was still a lot of fun to sit back and just float along!

I did not participate in the big slides but some friends did and they had a lot of fun, even though they were pretty sore the next day.

I stopped here for an overnight visit and I can already say that I want to come back and stay longer! The staff here is amazing, the park is beautiful, and there is a ton to do! So many hiking trails you will never be bored, the scenery here is just amazing as well. I cannot wait to go back and spend some more time here and be able to hike the trails and experience more of Ft. Davis.

When I visited they were doing renovations of the visitor center so I was only able to drive through and that was about it. Seems like a great little park for Day use, but other than that, not sure what else this park would be used for honestly. It is great if your are local, but other than that, for a brief stop headed out to west Texas, that is really about it.

An amazing park right outside of Austin. I was only here for a brief moment during the hottest part of the day, but it was still worth checking out and exploring a little bit. The falls were not very large as it had not rained for a bit, but they were still flowing and still great to see. I will have to come back and explore more of this great park!

I came here for a weekend camping trip and loved every minute of it. The campsite we had was perfect and right on the water, the entire park was kept very clean as well as the trails we hiked. I did not have any interaction with park staff except when checking in and buying fire wood and they were very friendly and answered any questions I had.

An amazing park with plenty to do! The campsites are great, the staff is some of the nicest people and they put on the best programs. The park store is one of the best I have ever seen and is run by some great people.
I was here for 5 days and loved every minute of it and cannot wait to go back and explore more of this amazing park.

A great park with a great path that has plenty of space to ride a bike or run and not have to worry about running into people. It is usually well maintained and always people there. I have always felt safe walking, running, or biking at different times of the day. Also a great place to go with your pet as well!

I stayed overnight in this park and it was BUSY! But it was in the prime time of camping so that is understandable. The campsites were really nice and the hiking I did in the morning was great as well. Hope to visit again and be able to spend some more time here.

An amazing Texas State Park in North East Texas. The piney woods here are a hidden gem! Lots of trails to explore, plenty of places to camp. Came here for a quick hike and will be back to enjoy some camping in the future and to explore more of the trails!

I was here in the morning and got to explore around the trails and do a little bit of hiking. The staff here is very friendly and was able to provide recommendations on their favorite places to eat, which I did try and was glad I did.

A great place to visit to ride some of the ever expanding and very well maintained mountain bike trails!  Well worth a visit with friends, a recently added section for advanced riders has been a great addition to Faulkner park!

A little oasis in the hill country, the hiking here is really nice and good for anyone. I only spent a couple hours here but it was well worth it and I hope to be able to visit here again soon to explore more of the park.
A great Texas State Park in North East Texas. Tons of camping options and lots of trails to explore. Right against the lake which is great for boaters and the like. Great for fishing and exploring.
I stopped here very briefly and was not able to really walk around much as I had to continue on with my journey, but the staff was really nice and the place was kept in good condition.
If you are at Cedar Hill State Park, you have to visit Penn Farm and do the self guided tour, it is well worth exploring and learning about some great Texas History.
I was here for a day trip and did a couple of the hikes here as well as went caving with a local guide. I cannot wait to come back to this park and stay the night.
I stayed the night at Buesher State Park and explored a lot of the hiking trails here. It is a really great park with friendly staff and great campsites!
This is a gem in this part of Texas, I plan to come back here when I have more time, but had to come by and visit it while I was in the area at least.
This is a great park full of great trails to explore. I was only here briefly, but plan to return and explore more of it someday.
This was a great park to visit and explore. Plenty of hiking trails to roam along on and friendly staff!

Gotta love the BYU "dinosaur museum."  We have been coming to it since my first child was little (now 22). Let's start with the fact that there is no entry fee--awesome, but don't forget to leave a donation to support the program.  It is kid friendly, never crowded, and always fun.  Dinosaurs, rocks, and prehistoric fossils...what's not to like? This time we didn't get to see any of the students working in the lab but it's awesome when we have that opportunity.

I don't know which trailhead I started out at, but Dimple Dell Park is an excellent, massive area to get some quality nature time without heading into the mountains. It's certainly not a "hike," but you can definitely get a good workout in because there are so many different trails and the place, like I said, is massive. That being said, if you're not paying attention and just enjoying the terrific views

We have made it our tradition to at least attend the museum each spring break. My boys love all the animals and they always learn something new each time. It is such a nice perk to be able to attend for free. We have been following the progress of the beautiful mural upstairs and can't wait to see it finished. We always finish off the trip with ice cream just around the corner at the BYU creamery.

Very cool spot to visit for all your landscaping ideas and especially when looking for plants that are great for the Utah weather. Make sure to take your kids with you, as they have a life-size chess board in the middle of the garden. We have had a lot of fun playing chess with friends and learning chess as a family on the very large interactive board. I need to also mention that it's free!

When Bridal Veil Falls is too packed, just cross under the bridge to Nunn's Park. I'll admit, you don't get the beautiful view of the falls from this park, but you're right next to the river. If you're close enough to the river, the sound of the water drowns out the cars driving by on the road. I came to this park last week when I wanted to get away from the apartment for a while.

I walked to this park in August when I stayed at a nearby rental. I was SHOCKED to see how beautiful and HUGE this park was. Lots of beautiful shade trees. I think there were 2 ponds with giant water fountains. It's very family friendly, I felt very safe here, no gangs, homeless, trash or drug deals going on (yes, I've seen it in other city parks). Green grass, well manicured.

This is a really great off leash dog park and I would come here regularly if it was closer, but if you are luckily nearby it's worth coming to because:on a sunny weekend, expect it to be crowded! This is a good place to go "dog watching," like people watching, but cuter and cuddlier (especially if you're in search of a new pup), because there are SO many different breeds.

We absolutely loved the Springville Art Museum as a location for our bridal pictures. We love to come back and remember the places where we took those special pictures. We called ahead and were able to come before opening time so that we didn't have to worry about other people. They have a dressing room in the basement, so I didn't have to wear my wedding dress outside,

This park is the most awesome park. Just scroll through the photos and you can see how elaborate the playground is. It's pretty much like a huge fort, and so much fun for kids. It's not really the kind of park where you can just sit under a shady tree and let your kids go. You kind of have to follow them around so you don't lose them, but hey at least you get a workout.

Wonderful for our 2yo, he loved every room on the first floor at least! Parking was easy (North lot on S 400 W--on the opposite side building from the planetarium corner) walked right in. I wish there were more people helping to keep it tidy for example all the water proof coats were wet and on the floor and the kitchen play area just had the plastic food EVERYWHERE..

This is one awesome park. If you are in the area and you have kids that want to play bring them here. It's is a very new park that covers a massive amount of land. There is a huge field where you can play football, frisbee etc. they have basketball courts, tennis courts and pickle ball. The playground itself is massive and tons of fun things for little up to big kids.

Beautiful mountains and rivers. Lots of camping space and hiking trails. Love this canyonRiver is amazing, and when the ice melt starts, it is a rushing torrent. Fun to watch and walk near with kids as long as they're being safe.This  has so many tails, walkways, and places to explore. I've explored the Provo Canyon for 30 years and I am still discovering new secrets.

Of all the years I have known and loved this park, it was today's visit that finally solidified the need to perform my civic duty and review the damn place. After all we've been through? Please forgive me Sugar House.Sugar House Park often gets compared to Liberty Park. This makes sense as they are both two of the larger parks in the city, they're only 2 miles away

One of my favorite things I did on my trip to SLC. Tracy aviary is unique in that it is one of the only aviaries in the world. They have a wide range of exhibits with unique birds from all over the world. There is parking in the front and a fee to enter. There is a gift shop, water fountains, and clean bathrooms. We spent about 2 hours here and saw everything.

Loved taking my kids to their Try Hockey For Free Day! It really gave us some good insight to whether our kids are even interested or not. They had an hour from exactly on the hour to the hour, which was more than enough for my 5 and 7 year olds. The snack stand is a great deal for typical sport snacks; we especially love their $1 kiddie hot chocolate sizes!

Excellent park for family events, a quiet picnic, or just to relax by yourself and your dog.Start your walk from 4000 west and continue SW past the culvert. Explore the oakwood groves for wild and delicious berries and fruit.Good park. Never very busy. Good for holding events.Good place for a photo shoot, tree lined pathway, with good view of the mountains.

This place is beautiful and we really enjoyed roaming around the meticulously manicured lawns and looking at the flowers.  It was lovely with some foundations and a beautiful reflecting pound around the "castle" building.  We were able to see the Tabernacle Choice practice and spoke to some friendly missionaries who were around.

Seriously, if you come to SLC on a vacation, you need to ride out to Antelope Island. Majestic isn't a strong enough word to describe just how nice this area is. The views are OUTSTANDING. You'll never see anything else like it. Everywhere you look, there are mountains surrounding you. It's so quiet and peaceful here.

We came here for the 24th of July celebration, food trucks, large crowds and cool fireworks. My dog loved the people and the smells of the food. My parent's used to take me to this park as a child and I remember they had the tallest swings in the area and I got butterflies in my stomach from being pushed so high.

Our new (to me) Natural History Museum is excellent. We have it all: awesome new building (great for receptions and events which is why I originally visited), interesting exhibits that rotate and it is all in the beautiful foothills of SLC with a good view of the city and access to Red Butte Garden Hiking Trails.

I love how this is also clearly a small family establishment. The manager is married to the chef and when something is off she fixes it immediately. My wife had a dish with a cool looking pickled onion garnish. But eating it whole was intense! The waitress noticed and every dish afterward had the onions diced

Thursday night rehearsal is amazing.  I'm glad I followed tips of others.  No need to stand in line.  I arrived at 7:45 and folks were coming and going the whole time.  Do as I did and every couple songs move to another spot to experience it from various vantage points, the balcony, the main floor, front row.

Creek runs right next to it. I sit by the tables near it to listen to the running water. Lots of shade near Creek. Walking path around park. Open field for play and dogs.Park with nice toys for the kids to play on the river next to it was relaxing very nice we had a great time the kids had a great time

My youngest boys absolutely love this park! So many fun things to do. Great slides, zip line, water activities and other playground equipment.Love this park! It's very interactive and even has a zip line. I'd give it five but there is no bathroom here and that's not fun with little kids.

This has to be one of the largest parks I have ever been to! This park connects to the public library, the pool and the rec center. They have disc golf, play equipment, and walking/biking/running trails. Oh yeah, and the basball fields are there too.

This park is top notch, and a must see. We saw a large herd of bison around the lake, when we first arrived. We parked and watched them for a while. Then, the entire herd crossed the road right in front of our car. It was truly an amazing experience!! We then went hiking through the canyon, and along the little river. We then continued to hike up the Haynes trail all the way to the top. That part of the trail was steep and rugged, but fairly well marked. Be sure to wear hiking shoes and comfortable clothing, and bring lots of water. The view from the top is breathtaking!! We want to go back for camping.

Beautiful park!! We went hiking in May. It had rained a lot, the week before, so the trails were muddy, but still passable and enjoyable.  The trails are a perfect mixture of climbing and flat land. There was a little bit of challenge, but still easy in parts.  There were wildflowers everywhere. I counted at least ten different types. The scenery was just gorgeous!! There were lots of others out hiking, and enjoying the lake. There is kayak rentals available. This would be a great place for camping. I will definitely go back.

This place is definitely a hidden gem. I have been going to Cedar Hill State Park for hiking for quite a while. I never knew this place was right next door. The trails are very well maintained and very pretty. There are plenty of benches along the way, if you need a rest.  There is an easy, flat, short trail, and a longer steeper trail for those who want more exercise. I saw lots of butterflies and wildflowers. There is a shop that sells toys and misc items. The staff was friendly.  I will definitely be going back.

The park is small, but has everything needed for a great outdoor experience.  We went paddle boating around the lake. It was a lot of fun, and a good workout. The cost waa only $10 for an hour. The lake is clean and pretty.  The hiking trails are easy to follow and well marked. There are lots of beautiful,  tall trees everywhere.  There are benches to take a rest and enjoy the beauty. There is a nice picnic area, as well. I also enjoyed the quiet.

McKinney State Park is so wonderful!! There is a lower and an upper falls. You should definitely go to both!! The upper is good for diving and swimming. The lower is good for fishing or just relaxing. We went in late April. The wildflowers were abundant and so beautiful. I even got a photo of a cardinal bird. The hiking trails are well maintained, and there are plenty of picnic tables.

We arrived at the park at sunrise to start the Guadalupe Peak Trail.  The views of the park driving in at sunrise were outstandingly beautiful.  The trail was a challenging climb. The backpack was heavy with all the water needed. We took many breaks along the way.  These were perfect opportunities for photos.  The views were breathtaking.  Making it to the top was very rewarding.

I love this park.  You can take a dip in the cool, clean spring water, then go on a beautiful hike.  The hike to the waterfall is a little rocky and challenging.  Wear good hiking shoes. There are wildflowers and cactus on the hikes.  I even saw an armadillo cross the path. I think I might've heard a mountain lion at sundown.

This is a wonderful state park. The rock climbing area is so stunning and fun. You can actually do some rock climbing!! There is a well maintained trail that goes around the lake, with some lovely views. There is another trail along the grasslands area of the park.  That trail is wide and flat, and an easy, pretty walk.

This park is small, but very well kept and pretty. The hiking trails are short, and easy to intermediate level. There were pretty cactus and some wild flowers. There were also some beautiful big, live oak trees. There are plenty of places for photo shoots. There were also lots of birds, but no lake.

I am so glad I decided to spend a few days at this park!! The lake and river are amazing!! The Spanish moss hanging from the beautiful bald cypress trees is spectacular and unique. The hiking trail is like being in a fairytale forest. Watch out for the poison ivy, though.

Beautiful lake, with great swimming area. The trails are easy hiking, and well marked.  There are lots of different bird species. The lovely bird sounds can be heard throughout the park.  There are two fishing piers. Sunsets are amazing over the lake.

The mustang are so beautiful!! The detail on the horses is immaculate and amazing!!  It is really relaxing to just sit and listen to the water, while admiring the artistic value of the sculptures.  Viewing them at sunset is extra special.

I love love love this place!! There are beautiful flowers, pretty trees, nice bridges lovely gazebos,  benches, etc. This is the perfect place to take photos, or just have a lovely relaxing stroll. Dogs are also allowed!! ❤❤❤

We go to the trails every year. Some years are better than others, but we are never disappointed.  There are horses, farm animals, and picket fences along the way. There is also a winery we always stop at for a tasting!!

This place was,so much fun!! We were there when it opened on a,weekday. There were no lines. I love the ferris wheel over the water. We went back at sunset, and rode it again. The sky was so beautiful.
This is the perfect place to have some fun, get creative, and get some amazing photos. There are instant film cameras for rent for $25, which includes 10 photos. That just adds to the experience.
The park is very clean and well maintained.  The paved hiking trail is so nice, with many beautiful views along the way!! The lake is sparkling blue, with a nice beach swimming area!!
This was such a nice place to visit. It's like stepping back in time. There are people dressed in costume along the way, who tell you about the history of the different buildings.
This is a wonderful place to camp!! We camped right on the lake. There was a spectacular view of the sunrise!! The hiking trails are very nice, clean, and well maintained!!
Such a beautiful state park!!  The hiking is amazing, with rock climbing and a trail that goes around the lake, water's edge.  The lake was so calm, it looked like glass!!
The garden is so beautiful!! The fall foliage is especially breathtaking.  My son lives in Japan. He says that this garden is very similar to actual gardens in Japan.
This is definitely one of my favorite state parks!!.  The hiking is challenging,  but not too difficult.  The scenery is really beautiful and the park is clean!!
This is a really nice state park. I had so much fun paddle boarding, and hiking. I was there in the summer. There was lots of cactus and wildflowers.
This is a beautiful park!! The water is so clear, you can see your feet!! The hiking trails are great!!
This is a nice state park.  The hiking trails are great. The park is very quiet, with lots of birds.

A wonderful art gallery. On the day of my visit there was a composer sharing his creative process and playing some of his music in the foyer. While I reflected on the Latin American art and language exhibit I heard the sounds of this beautiful music. That was very special. The main galleries are upstairs and were divided into historic European and modern American exhibits. I first went to the American exhibit and in retrospect should have visited the European exhibit first, the transition from political and modern pieces to classical and religious pieces was jarring. You could easily spend over two hours here but if you get overwhelmed by volume you may want to focus one exhibit and return again if time permits. Thursday is free admission (awesome) and there are many other pricing options available. The gift shop had a great selection of items for purchase covering a wide range of price points and while I did not visit the cafe it was clearly popular with numerous folks enjoying the food. I cannot comment on parking but can say that accessing the museum by public transportation was easy. The website is informative and up to date so use that as a planning guide.

Being originally from Dallas, we were skeptical, but it is preset cool! It is well kept and there is never a concern for safety due to many visible security guards throughout this two block park. There are 6-8 food trucks there most weekday evenings and usually a line at most of them. Depending on the activities/events happening determines the crowd at the park. You can go to their website to find out the happenings for a specific date. There are also many restaurants walking distance from the park, if the restaurant or food trucks do not appeal to you. Also, the FREE McKinney Ave Trolley stops at both ends of the park on its trip through the Arts District and Uptown.

It’s 9.5 miles around. Takes an hour to bike depending on your setup. The views are worth it and in the spring the mornings are such a treat. The lake has been here since the 30s and it has many stewards promoting sustainability. Keep in mind after storms there will be trash, all surrounding creeks feed it and as such trash follows the water. That aside, Dallas parks and groups like For The Love of the Lake do an amazing job mobilizing clean up efforts. Do yourself a favor and go see the big catfish a the spillway. Also get out of your damn house and take a walk get a breath of fresh air.

I really enjoyed our trip to Reunion Tower. It's been on our Dallas bucket list for a long while. It was easy to park nearby and get tickets inside. Just a quick wait and we were on our way up. The staff at all levels were kind and helpful. The kids were so excited at the top. Lot of opportunities to look through telescopes and see Dallas landmarks close up. There were also a lot of fun, interactive games and computer simulations inside the deck. I'd recommend it to anyone living in or visiting Dallas. We went during the day but would love to go back at night!

It’s an odd thing for this destination to be a must see tourist attraction. It should be a somber place. A great man lost his life here and all that some will remember is an X marks the where a sitting President was slain. the grassy knoll is now prone to selfies by domestic and foreign visitors to commemorate our loss as a nation. Tourist morbidity aside the museum offers a glimpse into a time where American exceptionalism was wearing thin as it paced into a frightening new dystopia. Be brave and consider how the actions then are in play now.

We were excited to go to this park to experience the coasters. We went in April 1st & didn’t expect it to be as busy as it was. We arrived at 11am, waited about 1/2 hour to get entrance I to the park & found that most of the good thrill rides had wait times of approximately an hour. We waited in line 1.5 hours for X2 but admittedly they were giving announcements that only 1 carriage was running which resulted in the delays. If your into thrill rides then this park is worth the visit, otherwise give it a miss. Tatsu was terrifying but awesome

Try to fit in a visit to the Water Gardens, esp. at night. This was one of the first places I visited when I moved to Ft. Worth and it's still one of my favorites. They have small festivals at the gardens throughout the year, but mostly it's a great place to go and just chill. The water features are impressive and one features allows you to surround yourself with rushing water. Definitely make a night trip there if nothing else. When the lights are on and you need a break from the city hustle and the warm TX night.

I am a huge batman fan and learned from my son who goes to college in Austin of the Capital Bridge Bats so we had to check it out. It was amazing to be able to see 750,000 - 1.5 million bats emerge from inside the bridge at sunset IN A MAJOR US CITY! I was amazed at the sight and so was my wife and college-aged son. Be sure to arrive 30-45 minutes before sun set to get a spot under the bridge on the shoreline. Be patient in waiting because it is well worth it.

impressive historic park that contains many gems, including the Japanese Gardens. Tucked away on a sweeping hillside above the International Rose Test gardens, the Japanese Garden includes many architectural features, as well as carefully orchestrated plantings and water features. Cherry and Camellia trees now in full bloom. Demonstrations of art and tea ceremonies on weekends. Great place for quiet reflection in spite of the crowds.

You must take the tour as you'll learn the intricacies of the building and the state legislature. Living in Colorado and from Michigan originally, I loved seeing another state capitol building by the same architect. The capitol sits in such a nice park-like setting, it seems more peaceful than what goes on in any government offices. If you love history, this is a must do while in Austin.

I love the Space Center. it is like walking through the history of our US space program with hands on exhibits. It can be very noisy with lots of kids at times but it still has heart-warming experiences that i don't think you can get elsewhere. I would be lying to say i am not still mad the Space Shuttle didn't come to her real home but there is a tribute to her on the grounds.

Mercer is open year round [except with major flooding like Hurricane Harvey]and is quite convenient to Houston's big airport, the gardens are lovely as are the hiking trails through the forest. Every spring in March they have a fabulous plant sale with lots of volunteers on hand to answer all your questions. So many wedding photos have been shot in this gorgeous locale.

Made a trip specifically to this park after reading about it on the internet. Lots of trails and the ones I went on were very gentle and not challenging. Enjoyed seeing the buffalo but did not see any prairie dogs. From the boardwalk we spotted a gar fish which we found very interesting. Also enjoyed seeing the hawk in the cage near the visitor center.

Went with a big group of family, young kids and pre teens, and absolutely love and recommend this place! Affordable and lots to see and do. Pet the sting rays, rode the train & other rides, and saw all the cool aquarium life and even a white tiger. Restaurant is really expensive but was a nice treat! Totally going back to the aquarium.

When we went, we were told there were some exhibits down, but even with that it was still a lot of fun. There was one exhibit open, so it didn't take too long to get through it, but they had a few things that the kids could play on that kept my kids busy for about an hour. We will definitely be back once everything is opened back up!

It was small but like the other reviewers said it's nice for smaller children as the exhibits are right at their eye level. Also it's not expensive and that helps when you have a small child with a short attention span. The stingray exhibit was nice and all the children that were there loved it!

Another free museum in downtown Dallas. It has some beautiful Chinese chests, jade carvings, and other artwork. I was hoping for Japanese artwork but did not find any. The area has construction work in progress so it is a little difficult to walk around especially if you have a cane or walker.

The McGovern Gardens are an easy and lovely walk from the nearby museums, zoo, Japaneses Garden, or Miller Outdoor Theater. It is a beautiful green space that includes rose gardens, and herb garden, and lovely spots to sit down and enjoy the day. Very similar to gardens throughout Europe.

The 6th Floor Museum is a must-see in Dallas and they have put it together very well. It seems to be quite busy and the audio-tour is well organised and allows you to make your way through the exhibits at your own pace. The gift shop has a good range of JFK stuff too.

One of the very best place in the South Dallas area for hiking! There are scenic views of the surrounding hills and lake. The trails range from short to long with an excellent view! Autumn and Spring is the best time to visit to see the colorful leaves and nature

Overall, it was a nice place to visit. The trail was calming, it was active, which made it feel like you were not in some random place in the woods, and was not huge, but a good size for a decent walk. Overall, I would definitely recommend visiting

Great place to see some amazing wild life. They are also rescue for injured animals and even took some in from hurricane Harvey. Its just south of downtown Austin. You can even see them feed the animals at different times. Worth check it out!!

We went to this park in Houston and we were amazed by the waterwall that was built in the park, it was so wonderful to look at and nice to have some selfies. My family enjoyed the view, we had a great time! So come check it out yourself!

The collection is well worth a visit. We love the extensive Remington and Russell collections. Also Stuart Davis and other American art. The collection keeps expanding. The view out the front of the lobby is lovely. The museum is free.

Traveled from Pittsburgh to Dallas for the weekend almost solely to do this. The rides were so much fun and definitely worth the trip! Employees were all very pleasant and fun to be around. Will definitely be returning!

A nice beach area by the water.
Easy to go to.
I recently revisited the Picnic Point Park and I was able to photograph some nice pink and red sunsets of the sun from the beach.
A nice creek called Picnic Point Creek runs through the Picnic Point Park and beach.

I visited the Ladder Creek Trail and it is a nice loop around walk.
You can walk through the forest on the trail to the Ladder Creek Waterfall.
Just about anyone can walk on the easy trail. Nice waterfall to take photos of.

A nice easy drive to Teanaway Community Forest in Teanaway.
The Teanaway River and other interesting sites to see.
Good walking trails in some areas.
Good campsites near the river.

Goldwater Lake trailhead is a nice area and a nice trail to walk on.
The trail goes along Goldwater Lake,
A few views of Mount St. Helen's and Goldwater Lake from the trail.

Adams Street boat ramp is nice place to visit and rest.
On a clear day to the north you can see Mount Baker Volcano and to the south you can see Mount Rainier.
I visited West Point Lighthouse and the Caretaker's house in Discovery park one time in the evening at sunset and is very nice area to visit and take photos.
The Twin Falls Trail is a nice trail to walk on. It is flat along some of the trail and a few short hills to walk up for hiking to the Twin Falls Waterfall.

Kiwanis waterfront park is a nice park to visit and photograph.
A picnic site and benches.
Playground set.
Nice views of Guernes channel and Guernes Island.

The Wild Horse Scenic View is a nice place to stop at and rest. Good parking. Very nice views of the Columbia River in Eastern Washington.
Good trail.
The trail of the shadows is a nice trail to walk on in Mount Rainier National Park. Some interesting geology rock walls can be seen in the distance.

Snoqualmie Lower Falls waterfall is a nice place and site to visit.
Nice walking trail to the viewing area of Snoqualmie Falls.
Nice restrooms.

Green River Natural Area is a nice natural area to visit and photograph.
Nice walking trails to Green River.
Can hear the sounds from birds.

Double Bluff County Park is a nice park to visit and photograph on Whidbey Island. Good sand beach. Good trails.
Good picnic tables to use.

I like visiting the Snoqualmie Falls near North Bend.
Sometimes lots of rushing water falling down the falls into the Snoqualmie River.

Bracket's Landing South is a nice area to visit.
Nice benches to sit on and enjoy the views.
Nice sunsets.
Good views of Puget Sound.

Twin Harbors State Park is a good and nice park to visit by the beach.
Good walking trails.
Good camp site.
Good beach to walk on.

Waikiki Beach is a nice beach to visit and photograph.
Waikiki beach in Cape Disappointment State Park with nice views of ocean.

Lime Kiln Lighthouse is a nice lighthouse to visit on San Juan Island.
Easy to get. And by the water for nice views.

North Jetty is a good place to visit and photograph the ocean waves or watch the ocean waves.
Nice beach to walk on.

Genesee Park is a nice big open park.
A few good long trails to walk on.
Good restrooms.
Near Lake Washington.

It is a nice Admiralty Head Lighthouse to visit.
The Lighthouse is in a nice park setting by the Puget Sound.

A nice park to go to and by the water.
Good parking
Easy access to the park.
Easy to walk down to the beach.
A nice viewpoint to rest and stop at. If the weather is good you can get some nice views of the area.
The Ira Spring Trailhead is good and a good hiking trail to see good views if the weather is nice.
A nice overlook to go to and see more of the puget sound. Sometimes you may see a good sunset.

Beautiful spot to walk, sit, enjoy a meal and absorb some history. I work nearby and walk here at least twice per week. The flowers are worth the visit, and they change with the seasons. I love the tulips, daffodils, dogwood, etc. in the spring. The autumn flowers hang on until very late in the season. Tour of the Capitol is free, and the other monuments in the area are very interesting. The fountains add a really nice touch. My favorite is the old buildings, though. So much more character than the new glass and steel showing up everywhere.

A nice little pocket park along the river. Mostly in a residential area. Lots of walkways, lots of bicycles, but there are Pathways for bicycles are not allowed. I only found one way to get in if you are not especially mobile. It's mostly stairs. Union Street has one path that you could consider handicap entrance. The views of the river are nice. And the little playground was getting some use. It generally looks like a place for the locals stroll down and play with their kids, or ride their bikes through the tunnel.

A very nice little pocket park here in Williamsburg, about two blocks from Colonial Williamsburg.There's parking on the street on both sides, but they tend to fill up fast, especially on weekends. People walking their dogs, riding bicycles and having picnics. It's spring time now so I was enjoying the flowers. And the little sculptures are really nice. That Cedar Waxwing is beautiful, the picture does not do it justice. Easily accessible, nice brick paths. A nice pretty, quiet place to spend a little time.

This is a really nice park. Great trails, paved and dirt. The trail maps were very helpful.The Go Ape adventure look like a lot of fun, if a little bit expensive. A lot of bicycles running around today too. They have different levels of trails for them, from nice and smooth to a little bit scary. LOLToday I was just hiking and geocaching, but I have been to the Botanical Garden before and it's informative and quite pretty.  Freedom Park would be a really nice place to spend a few hours with the family.

I would never have found this place if it wasn't for geocaching. Nice little museum, but I didn't really go inside, I just talked to a couple of people. Great garden area with some really interesting learning activities. And the nature trail was very nice, with informative signs all the way through it. The whole area seems to be in the middle of a neighborhood, but it wasn't very obvious when I was hiking. Trails are flat, and wide enough for strollers and wheelchairs. There's parking for 6 to 8 cars.

A couple of years ago I lived across the river, and worked at Beaumont Juvenile Correctional Center. I like to come back and see what has changed. This park has been a work in progress. A nice parking area, some really great trails for just walking and exercise. Nothing rough, all flat and gravel. The dog park is huge, and divided for large and small dogs. The views of the river are lovely. A small picnic area, and one portable restroom. There's also a very small children's playground.

Didn't expect it to be so interesting! This was a really nice stop along the way, and I spent more time than I had planned, just walking, reading and "touristing". I had no idea Jefferson Davis was imprisoned here before my visit. And I only saw a small section of the fort. Would definitely suggest you plan to spend an entire day. Also, Oozlefinch is on the property, and it is excellent. As is The Deadrise - an excellent restaurant at the marina.

A really nice area for hiking, strolling, dog walking, photo opportunities and trail running. On one side of the road there is the lake with a nice paved trail around it, along with some interesting history. Cross through the tunnel and on the other side there are trails in the woods. My visit today was early, and there were plenty of people out enjoying the park before the heat of the day set in. It's lovely no matter the season.

In Roanoke for a conference and searched for interesting spots to hike, geocache and spend a few hours outside. Elmwood Park was great on both counts. A very interesting area, especially the Art Walk. There were people walking, biking, lounging and just enjoying the open space and all it had to offer. Returned a second evening just for the exercise and relaxation. Very close to restaurants, shopping and other entertainment.

It's a beautiful beach park, no matter what time of year. There's been construction going on this summer, but that hasn't stopped people from enjoying picnics, volleyball on the beach, fishing, and hiking in the sand and on the boardwalk. The bathrooms have always been clean, and the playground has opened up to a few children at a time. A lot of parking. Handicap access to both the pier, the fishing pier, and the beach

Truly one of the most photographed spots in Virginia. Submitted a photo, despite the fact that there are so very many already available for you to view. It's a working mill and you can purchase grits and corn meal made here in the little gift shop. Some historic information and a really nice little walk in the woods to help break up a trip up the Blue Ridge Parkway. There is no bad season for photos here.

I did not go into the caverns as it was a bit late in the day when I got there. I was mostly looking for geocaches. The grounds are wonderful.
