There is a playground, lots of area for picnics, a ball field, fishing... and other activities for the family. The trail system was very nice, and I hiked all around the area. The river, especially, was beautiful. I would return for the hiking trail, alone!

Nice little park, but mostly a bike trail. Pretty views along it, and it runs along the river. The biggest surprise was the actual park under the interstate. Parking lot there, although I never figured out how to get to it. Basketball, picnicking, Skateboarding, fishing and it looked like they might have been a concession stand down there in the middle of it all. Handicap accessible.

Fairly large park, with lots of activities, events and play areas. I was here for a geocaching event today. There was also a baby shower, what appeared to be a disc golf tournament, and several pick up games of basketball, football, and even tennis. There's a hiking trail, a seasonal swimming pool and lots and lots of area for walking dogs and having picnics. Plenty of parking, too.

The Potterfield Bridge in Richmond is a wonderful spot to hike, bike, enjoy lunch or just relax. The ever-changing river at the Fall Line is a fascination, and there are many enjoyable events on Brown's Island. The bridge itself includes quotes on the Civil War and the burning of Richmond, with a nice view of the remnants from that time, and signage that tells the story.

Love this park. The trails are great fun, and the views are breathtaking. I have hiked all over it, assisted kayakers with getting down to the water, picnicked, geocached and just stood transfixed at the power and beauty of the water. Wonderful place to spend a few hours.

Love this place. Wonderful ocean beach for strolling, fishing and playing in the surf. Great trails, although I could do without sharing with the snakes. The Sunset Point Trail is very pretty, and I would enjoy seeing it at sunset. Well worth a 2-hour drive.

Really nice park that was not treated well by recent rains and flooding. Nice quiet trails, utilized quite a bit by trail cyclists. Playground was loud, crowded and fun today. Families picnicking and some visitors on solitary rambles

It's a very pretty park to spend an hour or two on a nice sunny November day, or probably any other day. People everywhere, enjoying the volleyball, reading by the river, the interesting little garden and picnicking on the grass.

A beautiful and quiet little spot I never knew was here before. Saw a few people fishing from the docks and their boats. Small parking lot, kayak launch area and short hiking trail leading to the rather personal docks.

A park for everyone. Built to allow wheelchairs, as well as walkers, crutches, strollers... everyone was there this beautiful day. Right on the beach where everyone can enjoy the sun, sand and sound of the waves.

Stopped here for some hiking and geocaching. Noted the multi use trail. It's a really nice trail system, and a nice little park. I sat on one of the picnic tables and enjoyed my Clementine in the sunshine.

A very nice little park. Lots of people roaming around. Lots of special photography going on. Couples, families, children posing. A nice relaxing morning. A lot of steps, if you choose to go that way.
Nice little park for some exercise while "Social Distancing". A little rundown and could use some TLC, but there is a trail along the lake, tennis and basketball and playground.
Beautiful hike in a really great area. Hard to believe when looking up at that arch that there is a highway running the top! Impossible to understand how big it is.

American History is usually my forte. Learning about it in history books and even in historical television reenactments / movies doesn't do too much to explain how it all went down. It was nice to find this museum on a road trip to Richmond, VA. After a search on Google Maps and TripAdvisor, I decided to spend the afternoon along the James River and visit the Richmond National Battlefield Park on a nice Tuesday afternoon.

This is easily   my favorite park in VB. Barely my second time here and I like how there's two playgrounds here. First time was at the old er playground..lots of shade, a big shaded picnic area, and lots of picnic tables. The ground i believe is wood chips. The new one is much bigger, has rubber ground and swings that little kids can actually get on themselves. I love the shade in the late afternoon/early evening.

To reiterate what other reviewers have said: this satellite of the larger museum is small and meant for little kids- best for walkers to kindergarteners. While the daily admission is good for all of the Children's Museums of Richmond, I can't imagine traveling to more than one per day.Price is on par with other similar style play centers, but they charge adults entrance fee too, which makes it a bit pricier.

Now, I am not in the Navy.  No ties to Virginia.  So I thought it was boring.  However, some of the pictures and stories are pretty fascinating.  I am just not a museum kind of girl.  The Navy friends I have loved going here and got in for free since they were in the military.  I had to pay though!  I guess it is a nice place to visit if you are looking for something to do.  Very cheap to get in to also.

Nice lake and trail (1.5 mile loop).  They is  a descent playground and the fishing is ok with plenty of small blue gills to keep the kids entertained.  Kayaks, canoes, or swimming are not  permitted.  parking can be difficult at peak hours.Great park for walking your dog,  going for a walk or run, or just having a picnic with the family.  I come often with my wife to walk our dogs.  They all love it.

We do enjoy this park as we come to play Pokemon Go and walk with our dog. The only real complaint I have is lack of shade when walking the entire park. It's hard to walk with your dog that doesn't like to be chased by other dogs that are bigger than him when there isn't much shade. He loves long walks, but we have to wait until we're near the picnic tables for more shade again after a certain point.

My toddler and I love coming to visit Three Lakes Park, whether it be in the morning, afternoon, or evening. In the morning, we play on the 2 different large playgrounds and chase the geese. In the later part of the day, we will walk around the lakes, under the shady and cool trees. We enjoy visiting the nature center because we get to see a variety of fish, turtles, snakes and other animals.

I have no idea what possessed me to want to pay the Ol' Dismal Swamp a visit as we were a good 45 minutes away then after leaving it would take us an hour to get back to the hotel in VA Beach. Maybe because it was free but more than likely because I was intrigued at something which had dismal in the name or maybe because I was hoping on the off chance to encounter a Black Bear.  Who knows?

Parking is free. The beach is well kept. The best area to park is near the restrooms in the lot right a few steps from the beach across from the shopping center. I enjoyed my stroll with family here. I loved being able to have my own little space not feeling right on top of other beach goers. I would recommend. The beach even has yoga events for the community to take advantage of too!

There is parking available all around the bridge area. I park then walk up a ramp. I remember when I first saw this bridge, I would call it the hot wheels bridge because it really looks like something out of a hot wheels set. Yes, to actually use it you have to pay a toll, which sucks but hey. The EZ pass can help with that. I wouldn't suggest going on it if it was icy.

There is nothing not to like about this park. It's family, animal, boat, fishing, grilling, corn holing, biking, walking, running, hand-holding and nostalgia-friendly. Morning, afternoon or evening are the best times to come--yes, that's any time! Launch your boat, have a picnic, toss a line in the water or just simply relax and enjoy the magnificent scenery.

Gorgeous views and family friendly. I came by to people watch and take a lunch time out from reality. This park is well maintained and a soul-restoring break from the hectic pace of daily living. The trees, shrubs and flowers are beautiful and you can catch children stooping down to look at the flowers eye to eye then smiling back at their adult caregivers.

Love this park, found it a few years ago from word of mouth and I liked it because of the size of the dog park. Now they have cut the dog park down by approximately 10 ft. to put a park beside it which is still more than enough room for dogs to run around. I can even throw my chuck it and have her run after it so it's a pretty decent size.

Admission was $1 so it I didn't like it no big loss! However, I was really pleasantly surprised with this museum. There were lots of exhibits and some really cool artifacts. I especially liked the news clippings of Titanic survivors from the area, the sailing exhibit with clips from the America's cup and learning about the Monitor.

At first I must admit, I was a bit disappointed when we drove up to the museum.  It was a lot smaller then I thought it would be. The pictures on the internet were very different than in person. There is limited parking spaces so I had to make my own on the grass. However, when I first came in, we were greeted very welcomingly.

I have been to a number of Holocaust Memorials and Museums. This one in Richmond is just as powerful and just as evocative as any of the others. Similar theme, it starts slowly building up the history of Jews in Germany and Poland before video of Kristallnacht (the night of broken glass) and gets deep into the Holocaust.

The nature trails are well maintained and a fantastic place to explore for animals or foliage. During the fall, they do a haunted hayride that is usually sold out.This 90 acre park is interesting because it's really TWO parks as it is cleanly split by Military Highway but between Rokeby and Paramont Avenues.

We just came from the medical tour led by Karen. She was extremely knowledgeable about the house, Norfolk, and Jewish religion and culture.You can see the exterior (and interior) of this home if you do the Cannonball Trail Walk - pick up a brochure at the VisitNorfolk center on Main St. Well-preserved.

Got to love how this park in Norfolk can unite so many people for many different events and yet remain an open, public, beautiful space to relax in, have a picnic, or a pleasant stroll through - when not under event occupation.I love coming here to watch the sunset over the water on a normal evening,

General: The park is flat and bordered by water on two sides with swampy wetlands in the middle. My wife and I went there to enjoy a 2 mile jog in the park rather than drive to the oceanfront. Considering how few walking, running, hiking trails there are in Hampton Roads (especially Chesapeake)

I genuinely believe that we could not have found a better place than Lakeside for my grandmother, and we feel confident in recommending it to others.They could also have more picnic tables. There is only 2 party areas so you have to get there eariler if you want a  table. Very beautiful park

No matter what type of art you like, or even if you think you don't like, you'll find something special here that will engage, enrich, and make you think.Plan a day here and take your time strolling through the museum, it's worth it and you'll find treasures around every corner.

There is no elevation gain (or loss), so you need to constantly pedal. Rainwater tends to stay for long periods in deep puddles making washouts common.Nice place needs a little bit of daily cleaning and path clearing but it is the middle of the hit summer so I kinda understand.

Great National Park in which to experience one of the most important battles in American history. Easy to walk around and a well prepared visitors center make this site a must. I would visit again. Plan on spending 4 or more hours here to savor the experience.

Second largest municipal park in the country.  This is nestled in the city of Newport News and given the bad rep the East side gets sometimes, we were leary.  However, we were very pleased with the cleanliness and the well maintained facilities.

Great idea for getting energy out quickly. I took my kids and their friend in the morning. We were the only ones there. My son, who is a couple days older than his friend was not allowed to go on the Ninja course while his friend, who is just over 46" could. So that was a bit problematic. Because no one else was there we were able to jump everywhere and they let my big air and little air jumpers jump together. Just be aware if you have friends around 46" that they may not be allowed to actually play together because of the restrictions. Also if your kid is under 46" go on Tuesday or Thursday from 10am-12pm when they actually let them jump. According to the map there are very few things the little guys can actually do when it's not toddler time.

Lots of great activities for the kids! Large playground, but not too big. You can find a few spots where you can see all parts of the park and keep track of your kids. The splash pad is small and simple but very cold and refreshing if it's hot. There is a fake volcano that "erupts" every 35 minutes. My kids were nervous the first time that it would actually spew lava. It just thunders and smokes. It was very crowded when we were there, but there was still plenty of equipment for the kids and the line for the train helps with crowd control a bit. Overall a great experience. I recommend paying the $1 to ride the train. It was a huge hit with my kids.

We love this place! So much to wander around and see and do and play on. So good for kids imaginations. They love all the duck and geese and the canals and the pond. The tree stump carvings are incredible. My boys particularly love looking at so the old tractors and climbing on the ones they can. They love watching the tractors work and haul stuff. They enjoy throwing rocks in the river and getting dirty. Plenty of space to run and play with dirt, grass, gravel, and trees. Plus there's an awesome playground and park as well. It's great to see the animals being taken care of and petting them.

Nice, cute, small park. Has a fun little playground with nothing fancy. There is a basketball court and lots of places to sit, with sidewalk paths throughout. But if you're looking to bike or walk, there's not really much there. There's a cool trail that goes under the road next to the river, but then it stops. Go the other way and you've got about 200 yards before you hit an abandoned parking lot.

Great park! Got a discount by buying a season pass over black Friday, but they keep getting more expensive every year without improvement to the park. Plus parking has increased as well. Really fun rides though. My 9yo loved cannibal. It's a very smooth ride. But we also love the classics like Colossus! It would be nice to have more hours in the spring, and even to be open during spring break.

Nice park, adjacent to TRAX station and near a dog park so kids were in heaven with dogs and trains. There are 6 pickleball courts as well. There is a paved path that follows the TRAX line, also giving access to the gully for a fun walk/hike. However, you do run the risk if running into druggies, homeless, and other interesting characters in the gully. Keep your kids close.

Love the new updates to this park! There's a Zipline and many spinny toys, swings for all abilities, a kiddie play tower with small side, a bigger slide, a climbing net, a saucer swing, with a bed of soft turf below. It makes it a little hotter but so far it's not been terrible. There are lots of big trees for shade and lots of benches to supervise from.

Great short trail, a little steep but my 3yo hikes it fine. Beautiful waterfall at the end. Best in June when the runoff is high but in September there is still water an it's at a safe level you can splash around in the falls. Super cold water though. In earlier months wear shoes that can get wet as sometimes water can be on the trail.

Great spot for kids starting out on Mt bikes, or any beginner. Whole family can start out here and not experienced riders have access to longer more complicated trails and younger kids can stay on the small loops. Lots of signs with good riding tips. I recommend no training wheels or carrier trailers. Most trails are single track.

I love this park. The water is plentiful and refreshing. It's a unique design with concrete, there's a dry part of the park to play on, and a big grassy hill. It has the most beautiful view of the valley. My kids love this place and it's just the right size so I don't lose sight of my kids! Unless they go down the grassy hill.

Butterflies are beautiful! It's not a long trip, particularly because in the biome it's 80 degrees and 80% humidity! But there's a lot to do outside the biome like play on the indoor playground, build a bug, examine real bugs, use a microscope to inspect bugs and their cells, make butterfly rings, and a lot more to explore.

The butterfly biosphere is beautiful! Almost magical! Also incredibly hot. There is a pretty good wait to get in, and you really can only take 15-30 minutes in with the butterflies. There are a lot of cool activities to do outside the biosphere though, but I'd say max it's about a 2 hour visit.

Such a beautiful hike! The wildflowers are amazing. Lots of different trails you can take of different lengths and destinations. The construction kind of ruins some of the nature but it will be done someday. One of the most beautiful hiking areas in Utah!

Beautiful lake surrounded by all kinds of gorgeous trees. There is a nice trail around the lake. Very little cell service except at certain turnouts which is a plus for me. Great place to relax and get in tune with nature!

Great park, usually pretty quiet, horse trails, access to dimple Dell gully, wood chip running trails, fun playground for the kids, pavilion, bathroom. Gorgeous view of the mountains. Popular photography spot.

Super steep but incredible views. Very dry and hot in the summer. Pick an evening time like after 7 for more shade. Not a nature hike but definitely worth it. Short and steep so be prepared for the downhill.
Great park, very large, 3 parking lots, it's the hub for soccer so it's very crowded in the evenings. Great skate park. Has 2 bathrooms near the 2 playgrounds. Has 2 baseball fields too.
Not too crowded on a Wednesday night, water was about 64, just got a cool little wind that froze my kids that wake boarded. Tubing was fine though since they didn't get that wet.
Not a great beach, but the water gets warm when the tide goes out so it's fun for kids to dig in the muddy sand. Lots of shells and crabs. Great for paddle and skim boarding.
Great park, huge variety, plenty of space to play even when crowded. It's big. Went with 5 kids, impossible to see them all at the same time but it worked out okay.
We love it here but the prices are so high now it makes it hard to go unless you buy a pass. Those used to be reasonable but I assume they've gone up as well.
Could use more benches in the shade but it's a great place for kids of all ages to play and a great path for walking, biking, scooters, skates, blades, etc.
Super roller coaster! They really move the line too. It was backed up all the way past the ride exit, but total wait time from there was 30 minutes.
Great little park with lots of grass and a fun play ground. There's a drinking fountain but no bathroom and no path for bikes or walking.
Kids are entertained for hours! Would be nice if there was somewhere to eat our own snacks, but it keeps us from staying too long.

Washington Park is a real find in the Northwest.  The loop road gets you to some incredible shoreline viewpoints (i.e. Fidalgo Head, Green Point) to watch the water, the sky, and the boat traffic headed north and south.  I've never camped here, so can't comment on that.  The loop road is pedestrian only for the first couple of hours early in the morning, and that's the perfect time to walk it.  There's a little bit of a climb headed up to the high point, with views of Burrows Pass, but really it's no big deal.

Fine little state park that's quite close to I-90 as you make your way up to Snoqualmie Pass.  If you want to hike, bike, or climb on the Iron Horse / John Wayne Trail, this is a pretty easy and quick access point.  The climbing area is just east of the junction where the spur trail from Ollalie hits the Iron Horse.  Also, this is a Plan B strategy for hiking the Twin Falls trail -  you can usually park here even when the standard Twin Falls trailhead is completely full...

If you like music (who doesn't?) this is a great place to spend an afternoon. There are so many creative and historic exhibits and artifacts.  If you're a sci-fi fan, you must come here if you're in Seattle (currently Star Trek exhibit).  And if you like architecture, this Frank Gehry building will be a must-see, since it is unlike any other structure in the U.S.  It's not a cheap admission ticket, so you'll want to have enough time to make it worthwhile...

This new museum (or new at this location, anyway) is a fun and interesting view of how Seattle became the city it is now. Lots of exhibits, done in a way that tries to make it colorful and involving, for kids as well as adults. They have everything from artifacts to displays and you'll learn a lot. The park it is in, South Lake Union Park, is perfect for a picnic or a view of Lake Union.

Along with SAM and SAAM and the EMP museum, this is one of the must-see art venues in Seattle.  They used to be mostly Victorian / Edwardian art centered, but in the past couple of decades have booked more contemporary shows.  They usually have at least 2 or 3 shows running, along with the permanent collection.  Unique among Seattle museums, they have free admission and free parking.

OK, it's the state capitol building and grounds.  So there's a lot of marble and monumental architecture in a Classical Greek theme.  It's actually one of the more scenic state capitol complexes around, at least as far as I've seen.  It's especially nice to see it on an April day when it's not raining (good luck...) and all the cherry trees that are planted there are in bloom.

You could call this tiny park a real diamond in the rough. It has remarkable views of Mt. Rainier. The story I heard was that so many people were trying to stop by this viewpoint and blocking traffic, that they decided to put a viewpoint park here.
There's a gravel parking lot, a fence to keep the cattle from wandering over, and some stupendous views of the mountain.

This is one of the unique Seattle visitor locations that is a must-see for tourists and family members coming to town. It has a constant parade of vessels, large and small, passing through the locks.  In summer, there are also volunteers working to explain the process.  Don't miss the lush Carl S. English gardens adjacent to the locks operation.

This is a short, flat walk along the water with great views toward Mt. Pilchuck and Mt. Baker and the North Cascades. It goes through some wetlands, so is often pretty damp, and maybe muddy. It's a hotspot for birding - be sure to bring your binocs. It used to be a staging area for loading the cut timber into log booms (thus the name).

One of the very best WA state parks.  Plus, you get to drive on Chuckanut Drive, a classic scenic view road.  It turns out there are many more trails and areas to the park other than the well-known Clayton Beach.  I discovered some very nice little hidden coves and a bluff trail I didn't know about before.

Great little neighborhood park with killer views west over the water and down over the Shilshole marina.  In summer it's a picnic spot or a place to watch the sun set over the Sound.  In fall and winter it's less of a gathering place but people still stop by while walking the dog or just taking a walk...

Pretty nice forested trails, along with the large athletic fields. This is a good spot for a summertime picnic, which we did. If it's a hot day you'll be glad for the leafy and cool trails through the creek valleys. The soccer fields get a lot of use.

Surprisingly wild and green little gorge in the heart of the city. It has several paths that run the length of the park, and you can use one of them as a shortcut when biking from the Burke Gilman trail up to Cowen Park.  Nice and cool year round.

This is a trail around the sloughs and wetlands in the Snohomish River delta area. Great area for birding, although the area north of this is hunting grounds in the fall, so probably better to go for spring, summer, or winter.

This place is awesome for photography. You can shoot toward the west for the sunset and get some water and Olympics shots. The lighthouse is also a popular photo-op.  The buildings there give it a bit of a New England look.

New and unusual neighborhood park created by putting a lid on the reservoir.  Great for families and for sunrise / sunset views of Mt. Rainier.  Has walking paths, green playing fields, and basketball / pickleball courts.

One of the older bridges over the Ship Canal - and it can get pretty gridlocked at rush hour.  But great views of Salmon Bay and the Fisherman's Terminal from the middle of the bridge, especially at dusk or sunset.
This is a real pleasure to visit -  the expanse of water, the views, the lighthouse, and the beaches all provide year-round outdoor fun. Pretty good salmon fishing at certain times of the year too...
Cool little waterside park. You can watch all the boat traffic on the Canal. During the winter, you can also check out some of the visiting ducks like pintails and scaups. Not usually crowded at all.
Great point to watch the boat traffic on the Ship Canal going from Lake Union to Portage Bay.  Also, you can launch a kayak or canoe from the little park - though there are rocks to watch out for.
This public beach is a little hard to find. It's down at the end of a tiny beach front road. The views are great. There are some good possibilities for birding here especially in winter.
Good spot for semi-dark night skies for stargazing and night photography that's not too far away from the Seattle metro area.  Sometimes there are star parties here.
This is a rare public access point on the shore. It's used by fishermen a lot. Also, there are some pretty nice views. It's worth a look if you're passing by.
The building is a classic Victorian palace.  Shows vary, so what you see may or may not interest you, but the venue is interesting anyway...
Cool little state park.  It's pretty tiny but with a bit ow waterfront. I think it's most popular with boaters, with moorage available.

During our second visit to visit our son, we continue to explore all the local parks, especially those who have open spaces and off leash spaces for our canine friends. Magnuson Park fits the bill with several trails that meander throughout this 20 acre park and along Lake Washington. I never saw so many people and dogs so happy. For the dogs , there were multiple types of off leash areas (small/ close areas for the brave and large fenced in fields that permit active running for your furry friends). But this park is awesome for people to enjoy well cultivated trails and brand avenues of poplars that lead in every direction and every type of elevation. We went counter clockwise and explored most of the trails and the off leash areas but the best was coming down a hill to Lake Washington. There by our parking area, an ingenious "swords to ploughshares" project took the diving fins of WWII submarines and randomly inserted them into a sort of memorial along the lake shore. Very moving. Each fin is labeled as it its sub's history .Afterwards both dog and people were well exercised opening our appetite for nearby's Junebaby

As soon as we arrived at the museum the staff welcomed us very friendly and immediately informed us about the on-going presentation about how to pan gold. The educational value of the presentation was incredibly informative. After the presentation we walked around exploring the museum on our own. Firstly we took a look on the ground floor that provides many different interesting exhibits, displays and pictures. As soon as we entered the basement, it felt like we were going into an actual gold mine. This might be good for children as it has many possibilities to interact with the physical exhibits that are, for instance the gold panning that you can try out by yourself as well as a wheel that you can spin, which shows you the probability of actually finding gold. In conclusion we can say that the staff is very helpful and extremely friendly, the interactivities with the exhibits are easy to understand and fun to use. Due to this the educational value is really high. It is an absolutely need to go when you are interested in american history!

When I want to go for a walk and get totally engrossed with nature, I head to this park. The access to the park is right behind QFC grocery store on Holman NW near 6th Ave NW. The path works its way down by a creek and you can easily follow the main path all the way out to Puget Sound. There are lots of bridge and lovely views of trees covered in moss. You will walk by a farm with fruit trees, a water processing plant and finally when you get to Puget Sound, there is a walkway that takes you over the railroad track that runs right along the beach. the walkway will take you right to the beach. The beach is a rocky beach lovely for sight seeing but not for bathing. It takes about 20 mins to walk from the entrance by the QFC to Puget Sound.

Like other visitors, I lived here a long time before visiting the Columbia Tower. What a surprise for only a few dollars! It was a beautiful morning when we visited and watched the fog burn off to reveal the Cascade Mountains. Definitely worth a visit when downtown - we'll be back. If you're a cheapskate, the Starbucks on about the 40th floor is pretty cool, too, and you don't have to pay to go there. I am not fond of heights, so I sent my husband up to take some photos. Wow, what a view---it cost him $3. The Bank of America Tower makes everything else look so miniature in scale. This is an excellent place to view the city and get some really good shots.

If you are headed down to Seattle and wanting something cool to do that's free, I recommend coming to see the troll bridge. There is free parking along the street or you could walk. It is about a 10-minute walk from gas works Park. you get some cool views of the underside of the bridge on one side and of course the troll on the other. There were several people there when we went and you just have to take your turn getting your picture with a troll. There are people there at all times of the day even when it gets dark. But it's in a nice location and there's not a ton of traffic on the street. It is a unique and cool piece of art.

My family and I had a beautiful hiking experience just a few minutes out of Spokane. Mt Spokane has numerous well marked hiking trails with varying degrees of difficulty which are clearly marked. We took are dogs (on leash) but there were also horses, mountain bikes, walkers and joggers. Plenty of room and views for every taste. We took the trail up to Quartz Mountain, well-named, and the cool, crisp clean air brought us an expansive panoramic view of lakes, rivers, Mt Spokane and rolling mountain sides. Plenty of areas to breakout your picnic lunch and just listen to the wind in the trees.

We ended up here as part of a tour otherwise we might not have come. We did get the benefit of a tour guide explaining the place so that certainly added to our experience here. Coming from the middle of the country, the idea and the need for locks such as this is something you've rear about with the Panama Canal or something like that. It was interesting to see it in person and watch them work and the engineering involved to make this all work while also providing for nature and having the salmon ladders and getting to view the salmon use them. Pretty cool.

Great day as the clouds cleared up just prior to sailing from Seattle. The arrival begins once you can see the long house then being greeted with a cup of clams and broth. Nice touch. Next you watch the staff cooking the fish on an open fire and you take you place in the tables. Buffet was fantastic and the best wild rice I have ever had. The fish was remarkable and nothing came short of that mark as well. The dances and presentation by the staff was great and interesting. Overall a great adventure.
likes: Facilities & Services: Clam and broth greeting, Open fire cooking
Food Quality: Buffet, Wild rice, Fish

reviews_attraction.text: We spent half a day enjoying the flora of the great North West. The garden is broken down into areas of various species of trees and plants with places to relax and enjoy your surroundings throughout the garden. There are even places to picnic if you are so inclined. Of special interest to me was the Japanese Garden, it was strikingly beautiful and peaceful. There are parts of the main garden that could be considered wheelchair accessible but in general would say it would be an effort for most.

When I lived in Spokane I used to bike the Centennial trail and found out about this spot from some friends. It's a beautiful park full of hiking trails, which are also great for mountain biking. And if I ever get back with my climbing gear, there is some Sport climbing available. Walk across the street to the Spokane river or hike to the top of the hill for a sweeping view of Spokane and the valley. John C. Shields Park is a great spot to get away from the city without having to travel far!

Golden Gardens is a scenic, quiet spot to stroll along the water and take in the beautiful surroundings. My toddler daughter LOVED running along the beach (a novelty to a resident of a landlocked state) and even rolling around in the sand. You can't help but feel anything other relaxed and happy here - the environment doesn't allow for anything else!  We have been here a few times but it usually too cold to sit and swim. This time the weather was perfect! not too crowded which was nice.

We were fortunate to visit during the Apollo 11 exhibit and say the capsule. The rest of the museum was interesting, too. Lots of planes, sure, but for those less interested in planes they did a nice job of sharing relevant stories. We also loved the cool old woodworking shop In the OG Boeing red barn and the fact that you could walk through planes in the pavilion. The Concorde was a real treat. We spent four hours there, I could see people really into planes wanting even more time.

Everything you could want is on the South Hill. Beautiful old homes, roads made of bricks, some even still have the street car tracks. Every type of architecture you're looking for with numerous Craftsman bungalows and mid-century homes. Intriguing to walk or drive, you can travel from park to park or visit high drive trails. You may encounter a herds of turkeys walking the streets or play chicken with a squirrel. It's a delightful section of Spokane

One of the best views of Seattle on a clear day. We had no wait to get to the top. We were able to walk around the observatory to see 360 degree views. Had a drink with the best view of the water and sunset and had a meal that was surprisingly good for a place that you would think the views would be the main attraction. Unique environment, atmospheric music, interesting drinks and a few good food choices. Definitely a place to visit when in Seattle.

I've been to several extensive gardens...in London, Victoria B.C. and other locals, but I've never seen a Japanese garden that can surpass the one at Manito Park. Built in concert with a sister city in Japan, the garden is beautifully arranged and filled with water features.I It's free to enter and there is nearby parking. It's a quiet, reflective place in the a large park, no visit to Spokane would be complete without a visit.

Fascinating to see what Chihuly made in glass and how he did it. A huge range of objects, mostly glass plants, including giant flowers. Some are inside the building and some intersoersed with real plants in the gardens. A riot of colour, unlike anything else we've seen. Beautiful exhibit! Loved the gardens and how the gorgeous landscaping enhanced the beautiful glass. Enjoyed each aspect of the exhibit both inside and outside!

We were visiting Spokane when friends told us we could not leave without seeing the Cathedral of Our Lady of Lourdes. The church is located in the downtown area and is a really imposing structure. The interior was remodeled and is lovely. We were amazed at the peaceful feeling that pervaded the whole space. Lovely cathedral right downtown. Go there, relax and feel peace. The dual towers at the entrance create a grand feel.

The riverfront Park is awesome! The kids had fun running around with the ducks and playing in water. There’s a carousel ride they really enjoyed and the joy of running together statues. We enjoyed an afternoon here. We rode the Carousel and the gondola. The gondola gave a good view of the falls. The Carousel is fun and if you get an outside animal (the goat is the oldest) you can grab rings that you can throw later.

We enjoyed a day there as a family. The kids played laser tag which was updated since the last time we were there. They said that it was way better! We went outside to the go karts and it was a blast!! However the outdoor mini-golf needs quite a bit of a facelift. Super run down and outdated. Not very much fun. Pizza is extremely over priced and not that good in our opinion. But overall, pretty fun!

Recently visited Splash Down on a Friday afternoon with a group that included kids, parents, and grandparents, and all had a wonderful time. It has a relaxed and easy-going atmosphere and friendly employees. I loved that you could hang out on the lawn - in the sun or shade - and that it was mostly grass, not concrete. If you're looking for a relaxing and fun day outdoors, this is a sure bet.

My neices boy is mildly special needs autism, he had an abolute ball, this place is great for stimulating brain activity. Its not mindless play everything in this place is knowledge based and so much fun it really should be used as a therapy for every child age range. There wasnt a frown in the place running from one station to another happy as can be while learning.

SAM or Seattle Art Museum is located in central Seattle, not too far away from the waterfront area. It has quite good impressive collections of arts, not only from USA but also from many other countries or areas such as China and other countries. It is an interesting museum to visit while in Seattle if you like arts, and has pretty nice shop and cafe on site too.

Went to Kubota Gardens and enjoyed this calming, colorful and texture-filled park. The contrasts between trees, shrubs, flowers, ponds, bridges and stones is stunning and well worth the visit. Consider the Gardens for a photo shoot, a picnic, or just a nice walk through nature. Thank you to Seattle Parks for maintaining this wonderful Seattle landmark.

What a fantastic find. I was fortunate enough to attend the Kilkenny Choir perform 'Sacred music from Paris' supported by the Kilkenny youth choir. A polished professional performance given by all, testament to the talents of founder and conductor Phil Edmondson. If you see a concert advertised make sure you book it. I can't recommend them enough. .

This place has amazing views that extends higher than the Space Needle. Additionally, the tickets to get in this place are much cheaper compared to the Space Needle, which is about $45 per adult compared to the $18 per adult at the observatory. Additionally, Sky View Observatory is incredibly uncrowded making the experience all the more pleasant.

What an amazing park. It is set in an industrial area but very nicely done. A paved path that is wheel chair accessible as well as stairs meander up to a view point that is above the water overlooking  Eliot bay towards of the city skyline. There is also beach access. Wow I am impressed and it is also a pesticide free park. The natural greenery is fenced off but what a view. The restrooms are the cleanest public restrooms in the city. It is heavily fenced so the hours are exact . I will say I never knew it existed and the signage is not great do maybe a well kept secret except to locals in the neighborhood.

This is a must visit for parks in Seattle. I would rate it five star if it were not for the din from the traffic nearby. If you choose the mountain path through the center of the park you will not hear the traffic as much and you can enjoy the plant collection from around the world. The plants are carefully marked with easy to read signs. The other pluses are the smooth paths and good access with plenty of parking. The rhodenendrons and Camilla are in full bloom during mid spring. Enjoy!

This is one beautiful park that is renowned in Seattle. It has wonderful views of Mt. Rainer as well as the downtown skyline. For a nice 3 mile walk or bike ride around the waters edge that paved and mostly flat or  you can go for a hike in the old growth forest. The summer you can swim and there is a play area for kids. Lots of dog walkers and people enjoy this park . You can picnic or bbq. It is huge so plenty of space and parking on site.

Madrona park is a great place for pick nics birthday parties. Great views from Lake Washington to Mt Rainer at the south and Bellevue across the way, sit under shady trees or take the kids to the beach area . Sit in the sand and enjoy a swim in fresh Lake Washington.  There are restrooms and lifeguards on duty during the summer.

This a wonderful museum of glass. You can watch glass blowing from the masters in the hotshop . The seating has great views as video so you can see glass blowing at its best. The gallery has whimsical artists work as well as visit the gift shop and eat in the restaurant.  A must see for glass enthusiasts.

This is a wonderful park that truly feels like you have walked into the forest when you are still in the Seattle city limits.  It is a steep climb not for those with limited ability and many stairs to climb back down as you enjoy the the trees and the creek that runs through it.

A civilized park on the most southern end of Lake Washington complete with Kid valley, and Ivars if your hungry. The cement path is a perfect length for getting a nice bit of exercise with a pleasant view. Very popular with families and accessible if your wheelchair bound.

I love the beauty and nature of this park,but you can hear the din of I-90 which distracts from the nature preserve feeling of the park. The trails are rather steep and have many stairs so not a place for those of us with less abilties. Very strenuous conditions.

This is classic Seattle park on a main street with lots of grass and bbq areas .Great play structure for the kids and even adult gym equipment. The castle in the middle is the public restroom is historically cool. Check it out on a sunny day it's packed.

Wonderful park, great views, nicely landscaped very modern . A city park on Lake union. The Wooden Boat center has a new building that sits in the center i have yet to visit, but a must see for wooden boat enthusiasts.  Easy accesable for all. Enjoy!

A nice place to bring kids for swimming , picnic under the trees. Wander down the beach to the T DOCK, a spot for teens and fishing a little further a few nice restaurants and Leshi Market for all your pic nic needs also a huge selection of wines.

Absolutely beautifully redone park. I remember as a child it was just a a water reservoir. Now the space has a play ground, skatepark,pea patch and food forest. The wide opened space is great for picnics with a view of the city skyline.

One of the best places to visit on a sunny day in the Seattle center  kids and grown ups , bring a towel because you'll want to run in it and that s encouraged. People watch and listen to the classical music along with  fountain.

The best dog park in Seattle. Plenty of space in the park to run free for your dogs to get exercise and play with the pack. Around the dog park are many nature trails for exploring and enjoying the forest feel in the city.

What a gem. I happened apon this lovely park that is being restored and maybe it was a sunny fall day with the colors changing on the trees or the children playing . It is cute spot . We will be back to explore more.

Easy paved walkways down the beach.A breathtaking view. What more could you ask for. Located along Seattle waterfront
I can't wait till construction is done. This will a world class waterfront.
A perfect city park on Seattles waterfront with beach access , walkways, bike paths. The paths lead up to the Sculpture park a must see as well with fun Art and great views of the water.
A great spot for those wanting a walk in the woods in the middle of busy university district. Many trails as well as habitat restoration make this enjoyable for forest bathing.
This park is connected to I-90 trail,for biking and running.It is a nice wide opened space Next to the African American Museum as well as the new Jimi Hendix park.
This park is a really nice place with water views,play area and fog park. The best dog park I've been too with swimming for the dogs and plenty of place to roam.
This is a very minimalistic design that you might miss ,but worth the visit as Jimi Hendricks was bigger than life and an important musician to pay homage to.
A good park by the water, with boat launch , picnic area, bbq, and childrens play area. An taste of Rainer Beach the view of sunrise is the best.
A very surreal park set in an  natural area that is on the edge of industrial sprawl. It will take time to restore it to its natural beauty.
A playfield , a playground that connects the community to the Holly Park neighborhood. Its nicely landscaped along the inside of the park.
I do hope the restoration of this odd park in the middle of a suburban shopping area is someday complete. It is not a clean as the photo.

We usually frequent Everett's Children's Museum but decided to venture down here to see what it has to offer.
Parking is limited but they do have a sign as you pull in telling you of other parking available. This info is also on their website.
They have a challenging 3 story climbing structure for kids 4 and older and an attendant is always present to help. You can also access the top via the stairs.
It also has a toddler climbing area.
They need to do something about air circulation. It is only a 68 degree day but the air was hot and stuffy for climbers. They had small fans on the top floor trying to cool the air but they are inadequate for such a large space.
The water area is fun for little ones but not much of a challenge for kids older than 4. It is designed poorly so water ends up everywhere. It is safe though as the floors do not get slippery.
There is a cute farm themed toddler area to play in on the second floor.
A semi cab you can enter and a packaging processing room are very fun and popular with the kids.
There is a two story reading tree, barn and mercantile store also.
A very large train table with beautiful murals on the wall keeps kids happy.
There is an art room and a workshop room for creativity.
There is a small outdoor play area that is geared towards younger kids.
dislikes: Lack of challenge for older kids

reviews_attraction.text:
Fun indoor play area for kids up to 8 years of age. Located inside the Woodland Park Zoo near the food pavillion. It is free with the purchase of zoo admission.
There is a cute mini door for the kids to enter.
Be aware that crows regularly stalk the strollers parked outside the entrance, stealing food.
The building is divided into several play areas, including active spaces for exploratory play, a stage for theatrical demonstrations, storytelling, puppet shows and video presentations, and a Project Place for guided learning.
At 10:30 daily they have Creature Feature. Puppets telling a fun animal story.
At 11:30 daily they have Shake Rattle and Roar. A fun toddler dance party.
The play area for bigger kids has a mountain, rope bridge, rock walls to climb, a slide down the mountainside, caves to explore (with video's playing) and a 20-foot tree to climb up inside and exit via a slide.
There is also a toddler area with an aquarium, a smaller climbing structure, slide and soft structures to climb on.
There is a darling life size bronze baby elephant that the children love to sit on.
There is a reading area with comfy chairs and books.
My grandson loves the Zoomazium.
likes: Facilities & Services: Diverse play areas, Comfy reading area
Activities: Exploratory play, Theatrical demonstrations, Puppet shows, Toddler dance party, Guided learning, Climbing structures, Interactive features

reviews_attraction.text:
Superb Children's Museum!
So much fun to be had. There is an an airplane, bus, train, two-story tree house, reading room,  sprawling hands on wooden train set, farm, restaurant, vet clinic, bank, barber shop, construction zone, art studio and theater.
Water room with lots of fun water gadgets, including a small toddler area. There are interactive musical and light rooms.
Toddler play area with fun, colorful and soft climbing structures and a wall unit with air tubes that scarves can be put into and sucked up and out into the room.
There is a large area with tracks you can build and send balls flying down the loops and curves. There are also tables set up with games.
Impressive roof top play area with a dinosaur archeological dig, oversized musical instruments and a huge play structure.
There is an area with tables and chairs for dining and there are snack and beverage vending machines.
There is a construction room with nice murals. The kids can wear hard hats, vests and build things.
There is an art studio where kids can create things.
Birthday parties can be held here.
There is a small museum store.

My grandson and I loved this ride!
Kids must be at least 3' 4" and 12 & under have to be accompanied by an adult.
Really feels like you are flying. As you glide, swoop and soar over many of Washington's beautiful and unique areas, you feel the wind and experience thrills as you come close to waterfalls, the Blue Angels, mountain tops, the ocean, the Space Needle and more. Using a drone for filming they were able to create an amazing experience for riders.
We will definitely ride again.
Great location on Pier 57. Where you can also take a ride on the big Wheel and have a delicious meal with great views at Fisherman's Restaurant.
Head inside the Pier for a ride on a vintage carousel, browse the shops and enjoy the many life size carved figures and totem poles.

Tours run from March 1-Oct 30.
Wednesday – Sunday, 10 a.m., 12 p.m., 2 p.m., & 4 p.m., Closed Monday & Tuesday

Please be sure to arrive early as tours leave on time, any late arrivals will have to wait until the next tour time.
If you bring a lunch or snack, there are tables you can eat at.
I love being able to take our grandchildren here. The only place where you actually get to be in with the animals. You get to feed the Kangaroos, wallabies, donkeys, goats, ponies, alpacas and more.
There also are ponies, bunnies, tortoise, lemurs and peacocks.
They also sell kangaroos and wallabies.
Family-run and family friendly. Cute little log cabin gift shop that is also home to some beautiful birds.

We really enjoyed our zoo trip.
The fact that this is a zoo and two aquariums combined, really makes this place special.
There's also a nice cafe with indoor and outdoor seating.
There is also a gift shop.
There's a beautiful vintage carousel that is enclosed. It has many animals not just horses.
There are two play areas also.
They have a nice outdoor theatre where they give talks and exhibit animals.
The Zoo is set on a hill, so if you have limitations or small children you may want to rent a scooter or stroller. They are available at the zoo.
During the holiday season they have the zoo lit up with lights.
likes: Outdoor theatre for talks and exhibits
dislikes: Hill terrain (may be challenging for some)

reviews_attraction.text:
This year was not as good as a few years back. Gone were some of my favorite, most dramatic displays.
It still is beautiful but not the same. It is not a big display like Zoo Lights or the Lights of Christmas at Warm Beach but still it is nice to stroll through the gardens all lit up.
It gets very crowded so you probably want to go early.
They have an area where you can purchase snacks and beverages.
Price is reasonable. Parking is same price which seems too much.
You can park free just past the entrance heading east. Down the hill and on the right.

Beautiful views....lots of tourists because of the view and movie and TV fans.
Kerry Park was in Sleepless in Seattle.
The park was one of the many stops on the finale episode of the third season of The Amazing Race. The park was also featured as the opening scene in the 1999 film 10 Things I Hate About You. In Fraisiet, the view from Frasier's apartment is a photograph taken from the ledge in the park.
There is a unique sculpture that makes a great photo op and people love to climb on it and pose with it.
There is a playground down the hill.

Picnic tables, sandy beach, large grassy area, playground, rv and camp sites, cabins, boat launch, restrooms and dock.
There is a designated swimming area but no lifeguard on duty.
You need to have a Snohomish County Park's day pass which can be obtained at the entrance or you can buy an annual pass for all Snohomish County parks online or at the at a Snohomish County Park's office. There is one at the Willis Tucker Park.

Wonderful park with lots of picnic tables, some under shelter. A really fun Spray Park, large play area with a smaller Playset for toddlers.
Lots of tall trees for shade but lots of sun for the sun lovers.
There was a funky smell when we first arrived, I think coming from the wastewater treatment plant. After a little bit we didn't notice it....hopefully we're not breathing any toxic air.

Beautiful park with plenty of beach for all to enjoy. There are fire pits, picnic tables, benches, covered picnic area, volleyball area, walking paths and playground.
Often seals can be seen swimming near shore.
If you are lucky you may see an otter or two.
There are boat ramps and docks.
You can tour the lighthouse on weekends and watch the ferry coming and going.
Parking is not free.

Pathways and boardwalks through native botanical gardens and wetlands. There are 16 covered kiosks with informative plaques about the flora and historical facts.
There is a 115 year old church with a quaint cemetery beside it.
You can stroll through the gardens and see old log cabin structures.
Best time to visit is in March/April when the daffodils are in bloom. Hundreds of them!

This park has a great little playground for little ones as it is completely fenced in. It is also right next to the restrooms and picnic shelter.
There are structures for little ones and big kids to play on. No slide though 😟
There is a large dog park and trails to wander.
There is only one large trash bin in the parking lot. Very inconvenient but at least there is that.

My 4 year old grandson enjoyed the sand table with toys and looking at the tanks with sea life.
They need lighting on the tanks and the glass cleaned as it is difficult to see things in a few tanks.
Small informative center with friendly staff. Beautiful murals painted outside on the walls of the building.
Nice murals inside too.
Great viewing tower on the dock.

Really enjoyed our visit here.
If you have been here but it was before 2013 or so, you need to visit again. They have improved it greatly!
Helpful, knowledgeable, friendly staff.
So many fascinating creatures to see.
Open 10am - 6pm, everyday except Thanksgiving and Christmas.
Located on Highway 2 in Monroe.

Beautiful woodland Park.
Large play area, picnic area, spray park, small but fun petting farm with reading station, swimming pool and a rental hall.
Summer camp programs.
Nice big shade trees by picnic tables for those hot days.
Trails to explore through the forest.
Free parking.

Lookout tower with amazing views. Nice little beach. There are restrooms.  Murals and sculptures are very nice. Walking path along beach.
The only down side was people begging for money and cigarettes.
It is sad but it seems cities and parks  everywhere have a homeless problem.

Beautiful beach with a rocky shoreline.
Spacious, clean restrooms.
Picnic tables, large grassy area, 2 boat ramps, biking and hiking trails.
We were there on a hot day and there was a lovely cool breeze coming in off the water.

This area is a grassy marsh surrounded by towering cottonwoods. Bird life and small mammals are abundant in the refuge.
The area is accessed by a trail from 1st street to a path along a river dike.

Beautiful views from the top of the park. Great spot to bring a picnic. No picnic tables but lots of natural seating on the rocks and fantastic views.
Deer frequent the park and are not shy.

Very colorful.... Kind of gross.... Kind of creepy...kind of intriguing....a little unerving going down into the dimly lit alley.
A quirky addition to our amazing Pike Place Market.

Sweet little farm and beautiful woodland trails with meandering creeks.
Large grassy areas, two small playgrounds and picnic tables.
Birthday party rentals available.
Beautiful setting, great playground for the kids, ample picnic tables and covered shelters. Love this park. There are also camp sites, yurts and a home for rent.

Nice play structures and grassy area for playing.
Loved walking the trails and boardwalks through the wetlands.
Unfortunately the only restrooms are portables.

Great views! Love the ocean sculpture with a treasure chest and sea creatures.
Nice fountain. There picnic tables and benches.

This is a fairly developed trailhead on Squak Mountain. Discover pass required. There is a stone parking lot that probably fits 30 to 40 cars. There are restroom facilities, and a large map of Squak Mountain trails. Additionally there is a basketball court in disrepair. There is a large building that is used by the park employees. An excellent relatively new trail that was finished around 2014 I think. Margarets Way is about 2.8 miles to the Chybinski trail. There are two veiw points on the route, one is a fairly long spur to a large lookout that overlooks the cities below to the west. There have been many improvements to the trail and it ascends 1300 ft at an average grade of 8.6%. Margarets Way trail is the only trail option, and in the early part of the climb it weaves through an old campground that is no longer in use. Overall a great place to start an exploration of Squak Mountain.

This is an obscure, difficult to see from the road trailhead. There is a large birm on the road for parking, that accommodates about 10 vehicles. The trail is well maintained with several offshoot options at various points along the way. Basically it braches to Samish Lookout, Oyster Dome, and the lakes. The forest is relatively young due to logging in the 1800s, but there are extensive forests with meandering streams.   It is a part of the Chuckanut Mountains, south of Larabee State Park. The trailhead is located within the 4500 acres of Blanchard State Forest, which is a working forest. Great trail with minimal access, if theres room, check it out.

Excellent trail head location. The road in is stone/dirt and quite smooth (no washboarding and few potholes). Additionally, it is quite gradual for as much elevation as it gains in nine miles. The trail over to Obstruction Point stays high with little elevation change and excellent views, particularly the last 4 miles. If you are looking for a relatively easy trail with amazing views, this is the trailhead to start from. Limited parking in the lot, but there is roadside parking too.

This is a great beach park with a nice wetland and woodland section as well. There are excellent views of the Tacoma Narrows and the bridge. Additionally there is a long beachfront trail both on a short bluff and near the waters edge. Trails meander through the forest and are complete with wooden bridges and crushed stone surface. There are many waterfowl and gulls in the pond and songbirds in the wooded areas. There is a playground, bathroom facilities, and plenty of parking.

This is an interesting park with some unique circular ponds in the main area. There are also some impressive bridge and staircase structures. The paved trail ends and a narrow footpath continues all the way through the canyon. There are excellent views of the canyon and Mill Creek. The trail kind of just ends in an area with tons of dumped trash. It is mostly beautiful, but it is unfortunate that there is so much litter in certain areas.

This is an excellent little trail network with access from two separate roads. There is ample parking at both the upper and lower entrances with restroom facilities. There is a switchbacking trail to the upper section on a forest hillside. The lower section has a webbing of dirt trails through marshland and prairies. There are wooden bridges over Evans Creek and boardwalks through the wetland. Great place for birding and enjoying nature.

This is an excellent beach park. There is a paved road down to the beach with a large parking lot. There are several restroom facilities. There is camping available. Additionally there are about 3 miles of trail in the upland areas of the park. There are a number of wooded ravines with bridges and boardwalks as well as a groomed dirt trail. There is a large beach front with excellent views of the Olympics to the west.

This is an excellent place to hike, bike, run, and explore. It connects seemlessly with Black Diamond Open Space, Summit Ridge, and Cedar River Trail. This natural area includes conifers, deciduous trees, welands, ponds, streams and some open view points. There are a few entrances with decent parking options along neighborhood streets. I highly recommend making a long run to link up this park to surrounding parks.

A very nice park, preserved riparian zone along Issaquah Creek. Open flat grassy fields, a small aspen stand, willows, and some landscaped garden beds. There is also a pavilion, restrooms, and a playground. There is also a small network of trails, anchored by a 600 meter loop and about 1.5 miles total. The bridge crossing the creek is a little over the top, but looks nice. Overall definitely worth the trip.

This is a good starting point for a run or hike in Larrabee State Park. The parking area fits 6 to 10 cars and it is across the street from the campground with restroom facilities. The trail leads to a lookout in .9 miles and Fragrance Lake in 2 miles. The lake features a .75 mile loop. There are also sever offshoot trails and loop options. This trail head also provides access to the interurban trail.

This trail head is easily accessible off May Valley Road. There is one main trailhead that has three options: pretzel trail with interpretive signs and story for children as you walk the trail, the forest road which leads up to Central Peak, or the May Valley Loop. There are two vault toilets, and parking for about 30 vehicles. The entrance and parking spots are mostly paved. Discover pass required.

This is an excellent park with parking for hundreds of cars, many pavilions, facilities, restrooms, and kayak rentals. There are open sandy beaches and soccer fields. There are several miles of trail traversing wetlands, fields, and forests. There are many boardwalks and bridges. Additionally there are several interpretive signs. There are also opportunities for swimming, boating, and fishing.

This is a great park, there are some ball fields and a playground in addition to ample parking and facilities. However, my favorite part of the park was the hiking trail behind the ball fields. It is not an extensive network, but there is a descent dirt path through the forest with some impressive scenery given the very minimal acreage of the park. Definitely worth a trip to this park.

This is an excellent trail with both a paved section and a dirt trail section. It has several road crossings, but most have crosswalks. The trail parallels Soos Creek and has several parking areas and restroom facilities at various check points. There is beautiful wetland scenary with numerous little ponds. It is a perfect spot for birding, numerous song birds, raptors, and waterfowl.

Ran the West Seattle Beach 50K which started from this park. Great facilities and excellent waterfront views. There is a great trail network, several parking areas, restroom facilities, and pavilions. There is beach front access with great views of the Olympics to the west. There are several Madrone trees and old growth conifers. Excellent green space in the city.

This is a small protected area with a dirt trail that runs along the shore of the Black River. An excellent place to bird! I saw upwards of 15 heron, 10 different species of waterfowl, and several passerines. It is a peaceful place that provides an excellent sanctuary from the busy city streets and highway. Limited parking and no facilities.

This is an excellent trail network in the Tri Cities. There are well groomed trails with panoramic views of the surrounding area. It is home to sagebrush and many vibrant wildflowers. There is an expansive parking lot and restroom facilities. I came here for the Badger Mountain 50 miler and really enjoyed Badger and Candy Mountain.

This is an excellent 2 mile paved trail that leads to the Sound. It passes through a narrow forested canyon with great views of the creek and surroundings. The trail is plenty wide to accommodate foot and bike traffic. The parking lot holds a dozen cars and has restroom facilities. I highly recommend this trail.

This is a very nice ravine with a peaceful running stream. There is a wide main trail and several offshoot trails. It borders a salmon hatchery. Unfortunately like most city riparian zones it seems to attract litter and debris which detracts from the experience. Very minimal access and virtually no parking.

Great access point to Cougar Mountain. I have never actually driven the road to this trailhead, only run to it from another. Starting point on the mountain. However the parking lot looks sizable and there are bathroom facilities along with numerous trail access points in several directions.

Excellent urban park covering over 700 acres in Tacoma. There are several miles of trail: ranging from bluff veiws, old growth forest single track, water front beach paths. There is a fort museum, rhododendron garden, and beautiful forested landscape. Opportunities for birding as well.

Extensive trail system that is well developed and signed. Well preserved coastal forest and wetlands. Sound infrastructure including impressive bridges and staircases. Over 3000 feet of waterfront, some of which is a sandy beach. Multiple access points to the park and a campground.
I run the Bridle Trails 50K each year, excellent event. The park offers a solid 5 mile outer loop and other offshoot options. Beautiful thick forest, one of my favorite urban state parks.
This is an excellent preserve that abuts Soaring Eagle Park. It consists of wooded gravel trails. There are a number of streams and a large lake with very little public access.
Great stop over park when driving across the state. Clean facilities, lush grass fields, great access to river, and diversity of trees.

I love coming to the zoo. Has recently underwent some new upgrades. I love the aquarium. I could sit there for hours just watching the fish. It's definitely my favorite. But the zoo in a whole is great. It's clean. The keepers are all so nice and knowledgeable and willing to answer any questions. They love to chat even with the kids. It's so inviting here. While the zoo is a little smaller it definitely hits the spot when wanting to see some animals. It's also really close to me so that's an added plus. Then the park outside the zoo is also amazing. Love this entire area of Tacoma. I do come here often. Highly recommend checking out the zoo if you haven't, you won't be disappointed. The tigers are my next favorite. Have many photos of them over the years. Always a lot of fun to watch them play and interact. Was great when they had cubs a few years back... sooo cute. My kids love it. The variety of animals here is great. And the viewing areas are perfect to get just the best eyeful of each. The other things in the park are awesome too, the merry go round, gift shop, restaurants, petting area, insect area, budgies, camel rides, play area, shows... its a lot of fun for kids and adults of all ages. Paths are all paved, which makes for easy walking... its a great zoo/park.
likes: On-site Activities (merry go round, gift shop, restaurants, petting area, insect area, budgies, camel rides, play area, shows)

reviews_attraction.text:
Was here today for a wedding. I was the photographer. Got to the park early so my husband and I decided to go for a hike. We're avid hikers so it worked out well. Just wasnt exactly the most dressed for it. Anyways. We hiked around the park on the trails about 3 miles. Trails were nice, clean, well marked. Was also nice that they were heavily shaded. The park had a great play ground, football/soccer field. Also had tennis courts.
The wedding/venue was nice. The arbor for the ceremony on the back deck area of the venue was great. I felt the getting ready area (office space) and the two one person restrooms were a bit lacking for a bathroom/preparing space. There is another set of bathrooms adjacent to the venue but those bathrooms you share with other park goers. So be prepared to bring a motor home or get ready elsewhere. The space is nice. Come the evening summer time it does fill with sun, gets bright and a bit warm. But other than that definitely a great space if your on a budget.
Pictures are a sneak from the wedding I shot. These are cell phone pics. Then a few snaps of the hiking trails. ♡ darlenestewartphotography

What an amazing hike. Have done this one a few times now and it never gets old.

First time was a sunrise hike. Started at 4am in the dark to be to the top for sunrise. Absolutely amazing. One of my most memorable hikes. Absolutely loved the view. There was a lot of people going up for the sunrise. So plan accordingly. The next time I did this hike was a later in the day hike. Less people. Both times people did good at social distancing and wearing masks. If you're doing this hike in the summer and planning a day hike. There is no tree cover. You will be out in the sun the entire time. The trail to the lookout is 80% up the whole way. Nothing terrible. Clocked around seven miles each time on this hike. Was fun going for the sunrise because you make a slight hurt once your almost to the top and you can see Olympia, Tacoma and Seattle lights. Was really amazing. Also you can see many other peaks as well on this hike. From southern WA all the way to Canada and even the Olympics. Trail is great. Some larger rocks in parts and sand at Frozen Lake. But all worth the hike to the lookout.

I'm a photographer and I recently just shot a wedding here. The venue is great. Pretty, clean, people who worked there were nice and very willing to help. Everything that was inside was great. Once you stepped outside... not so great. Tons of homeless. They were everywhere. They were interfering with photos outside, by getting in the photos on purpose then just in the background with their carts of stuff. There were even broken TVs laid up against the building. I know that it's really out of the control of those working the venue. It just killed the outdoor vibe. Also when leaving once the event was over walking through the parking lot near the library was a bit sketchy. While the venue is nice, the price was great to rent and the wedding wonderful, the outside is a bit of a let down.

Came down here with the family. Seems like a hidden gem. Wasn't busy. Was extremely clean. Enjoyed each aspect to the park. The beaches, hiking, park area for kids, checked out the camp sites those looked amazing. Could even rent little cabins here. Would be a GREAT place to spend a few days. There was a little store for essentials, laundry facilities. The restrooms were very clean and well kept. The views were amazing, the history and all the literature boards everywhere we great. Light houses, the battery... Coast guard, the learning center... all really cool. So much to see and do here. Definitely recommend. I was here during covid. So could imagine just how wonderful it is when it's all up and fully running.

Great hike. Dont recommend for kids under 10. It's only 1.6 miles one way. Once to the top the ground is a shear rock. Very slippery, loose gravel, definitely a slipping/falling hazard. The building is literally on the edge of the cliff. Cool history. Drive up is rough, hard to navigate if you dont know where you're going. Research the drive on the forest service roads ahead of going to know which turns to take and when. Its approx 9 miles from the highway to the parking spot for the lookout. Come early fills fast, there is additional parking further down the way, but it adds to the hiking distance. Hike is about a 4000/5000 ft. elevation gain. So be prepared, be careful and have fun.

Came out on a whim. Was great. Parked up near the street. Vault toilet available there. Was decent and had TP. Walk to the beach was nice. Continued on the trail there is three trails to the end. We took the middle, DOWN hill. Got to the bottom looked around on the beach took some pics. Was no one there. Picnic tables another vault toilet. Again, open, decent and had TP. Went back the south trail. All the way to the right. Easy going, hardly any hills to go up. Suggest this route. Was beautiful there. Complete Solitude and peace.

Enjoyed my time spent here. Lots of information to read, trains to see, and even climb up on for a closer look. The gal running the gift shop was super nice and offered a ton of information on the train station and surrounding areas and information on other historic stories. Purchased an autographed book that touched on the 1910 avalanche on Steven's Pass. Highly recommend stopping in if you're in the area visiting the falls or just passing through. Great place, amazing little town. Fun for the kids too.

Reason for the low rating is because I feel a way needs to be made to get to the base of the falls. Yes... there is a way. Down the muddy cliff. Its is a huge hazard that can be avoided if stairs were etched into the hill side rather than risking going down the muddy embankment. Otherwise the park was nice. Port toilets at the parking area. Nice grass area to walk. Very small. Has the viewing area of the falls and a place to walk to the top of the falls, but that was it.

Park was beautiful this morning. Took a nice walk on the beach. Views were amazing. Bathrooms were clean and stocked with essential items. Hiked a bit also. Trails were nice and well marked. Could've used a few more garbage cans as I observed some trash on the trails. But had there been a garbage can at the trailhead there may of not been the trash on the trail. But overall great park. Lots to see on the beach and the park portion was nice. There is even camping here.

Really cool place awesome history. Its a nice walk. Pretty open allowing people lots of space. Lots of broken buildings. A lot of hazards. Wouldn't trust going inside most of the buildings as they're falling apart. Wouldn't recommend for small children if you want to look at the ruins. Also lots of crude and inappropriate graffiti on walls. Tons of broken glass and debris around buildings.

Park was nice. My husband and I had it to ourselves. Down fall was the park had only a port potty which didn't have supplies and was very dirty. But the rest was nice. Great views. Light house is cute. Grounds keeper house cute. They I guess have tours on the weekends. Says the sign... very small park. But definitely nice for a picnic.

Forest was nice. Only seen one other person there. The roads were OK. Bit of potholes here and there. But not terrible. Was able to get up there in my MKT which is pretty low.

Was a tad foggy and drizzly while up there, so that cut into the usual great view at the top. But it was still a nice getaway.

Way to many homeless at this park. They're living in the bathroom stalls, which the restroom is right next to the playground. There are some sleeping under the trees. There is garbage strone about. This park used to be so nice. But I find myself needing to carry protection whenever I'm here.

Was really nice here. Amazing views of the Narrows Bridge and Chambers Bay. Lots in between. Had the beach to myself. Park was nice, clean, restrooms were also nice and clean. Fully stocked with tp, soap and seat covers. Was a beautiful day to check out this hidden little gem on the island.

Fun hike. Tad muddy. Port potty at trailhead. Bridge/tunnel is really cool. Tracks to no where were fun to see. Beach also nice. Suggest checking tides before going. A lot better at low tide. More beach to explore, otherwise the water is right up against the land/bank.

I enjoyed myself here. But felt there wasnt much glass/art inside the actual museum. Only two galleries, then the blowing area. Was cool. Not sure if I would come again given the fact there wasnt much to see. But clean, staff was nice, bright and colorful.

I like this park, its like a hidden gem hidden in Puyallup. Definitely a less populated park. Has year around restrooms. Playground. Near by ball field. Exercise trails. Cute cabins and picnic areas, even a waterfall.

Beautiful day at the park. Love coming here. Lots to see and do. Picnic, camp, hike, beachcomb, kayak the options are limitless. This park is fantastic and really big. Highly recommend checking it out.
Have been coming here for years. Husband brought me on Valentines to have some buffet. Choices and quality were horrible. Worst buffet and I generally LOVE the food here. Such a disappointment. :(
Beautiful day. Beach was nice. There was port potties here. They were stocked and as clean as they could be. Have been here many times. Definitely won't be the last time either.
Definitely a pretty park. Fun to be able to explore and see under the Narrows bridges. There is only a porti potty here. Small parking area and a short walk to the beach.
Mount Rainier is my home away from home. Absolutely love coming up here. So pretty, so informational, great hikes in this area... ♡♡♡ photos:darlenestewartphotography
Super cool place. Have lived in WA all my life and finally got to check this place out. Very fun. Lots to see and do in and around the locks.
Walked the five mile drive this morning in the pouring rain. True Washingtonian style. Was fun. Viewpoint wasnice, clean and well kept.

(Translated by Google) In fact, this is not so much a park. It looks more like a trail in the city. There is a small parking lot at the top. It is possible that when you arrive it will be completely full and there will be no free space. But don't be upset. Very often people come there only to go down and up to the top. Walk your 4 miles. So if you wait a few minutes, then someone leaving to free you parking. The path itself is quite wide. You can walk along it even with a stroller.
