True, it will be difficult on the way back up the stairs. In the beginning (or in the end it depends whether you go up or down) the slope is quite strong. But on the trail there are a lot of benches where you can sit and rest. At the end of the path you will find a large, beautiful meadow with several tables and a volleyball field. There is also a place for frying meat. If you go further you will see a small tunnel. A railroad embankment hides a beach on the bay. So as you walk through the tunnel, you will gradually get a view of the beach. It is like opening a gift. And this is another beauty of this place.

По сути дела это не столько парк. Больше это похоже на тропу в городе. На верху есть маленькая стоянка. Возможно что когда вы приедет она будет полностью заполнена и не будет свободного места. Но вы не огорчайтесь. Очень часто люди приезжают туда только для того чтобы спуститься вниз и подняться на верх. Пройти свои 4 мили. Так что если вы подождет несколько минут то кто то уезжая освободить вам парковку. Сама тропа довольно широкая. По ней можно пройти даже с коляской. Правда на обратном пути на ступенькам будет сложновато. Вначале (или в конце это зависит идете вы вниз или вверх) уклон довольно сильный. Но на тропе есть очень много лавочек где можно посидеть и отдохну. В конце пути вы найдете большую, красивую поляну с несколькими столиками и волейбольным полем. Там же есть место для жарки мяса. Если пройти еще дальше вы увидите небольшой туннель. Железнодорожная насыпь скрывает пляж на берегу залива. Так что когда вы будете проходитчерез туннель вам постепенно будет открываться вид на пляж. Это похоже на раскрытие подарка. И в этом еще одна прелесть данного места.

(Translated by Google) My family spent about an hour here. There are many parking lots in the area, so we pretty successfully found a place to park. There were many people, but there was no feeling that everyone was interfering with each other. People walked freely, photographed, and looked around. Actually, we were doing this. A very beautiful place. All houses and all trees are decorated with colorful lights. The feeling that you were in some kind of fairy tale. A quartet played on the stage on long wooden pipes (I don’t even know what they are called). We played very harmoniously and very beautifully. Well done. Nearby there are magozinchiki with various souvenirs from small, cheap to large, expensive. In general, for any color, taste, size and wallet. You can go into them as a museum to see, photograph, and if you liked something, of course, buy. In general, we had a great time. What we wish you.

Люди свободно ходили, фотографировались, и смотрели по сторонам. Собственно этим занимались и мы. Очень красивое место. Все дома и все деревья украшенны разноцветными огоньками. Ощущение что ты оказался в какой-то сказке. На сцене играл квартет на длинных деревянных трубах (даже не знаю как они называються). Играли очень слаженно и очень красиво. Молодцы. Рядом есть магозинчики с различными сувенирами от маленьких, дешевых до больших, дорогих. Вобщем на любой цвет, вкус, размер и кошелек. В них можно зайти как в музей посмотреть, сфотографировать и если что-то приглянулась конечно же купить. В общем мы здорово провели время. Чего и вам желаем.

But there were quite a lot of people on the beach. If there is not enough space at risk, then you can sit on the grass. The entrance to the water is very shallow and shallow. For children, exactly what you need. But if an adult wants to swim, you will have to walk on the water for a long time. The beach itself and the entrance to the water are sandy. But at the same time, the water was visibly transparent. There is a small shower where you can wake up or rinse your feet.

Сейчас там перестраивать детскую площадку. Судя по увиденному площадка будет интереснее. В парке есть много парковок так что может разместиться много народа. Правда если парковки почти все заняты то и на пляже будет людей непротолкнешся. Мы приезжали под вечер и парковки были на половину пусты. Но на пляже было довольно много народу. Там есть небольшой душ где можно проснуться или ополоснуть ноги.

Long walk in shallow water (for adults)

In general, I really liked it and if I want to stay a little by myself and whether I come here together with my wife.

И конечно сам берег. В общем мне очень понравилось и если хочется побыть немного самому и ли с женой вдвоем я сюда приезжаю.

(Translated by Google) The park is located in the apartments. But there is free access. Quite a lot of parking for such a small park. My eldest son really liked it. There are two types of swing. And there is a carousel that you can spin while sitting right in it. My children really enjoyed riding it with me. There is a playground with different slides and climbing devices. There are two one-sided carousels. There are many benches, tables and a small grassy field nearby. The park itself is very cozy and people on the site are friendly and welcoming. There is a place where you can cook something on the grill and a toilet, which is also important.

Парк находиться в аппартментах. Но есть свободный доступ. Довольно много стоянок для такого небольшого парка. Моему старшему сыну очень понравилось. Есть два вида качелей. И есть карусель которую можно раскручивать сидя прямо в ней. Моим детям очень понравилось кататься на ней вместе со мной. Есть площадка с разными горками и приспособлениями для лазанья. Есть две одномесные карусели. Рядом много лавочек, столов и небольшое травяной поле. Сам парк очень уютнее и люди на площадке дружилюбны и приветливый. Есть место где можно приготовить что то на гриле и туалет, что тоже немаловажно.

(Translated by Google) A secluded place on the shore of a large lake. There is a small playground. Small pavilion for celebrations or small events. But the best part of this park is the very shallow beach. An adult can reach Anton standing in the distance and will never find a place deeper than waist-deep. Half way down the water is sometimes just below the knee. Once we saw how one mother put a folding chair in the middle of the water and her children sank around her. But the stool was dry. If you are not willing to walk all this distance on the water, you can go around it on the platform.

Уединенное место на берегу большого озера. Есть небольшая детская площадка. Небольшой павильон для празнованя или проведения небольших мероприятий. Но самая лучшая часть этого парка это очень мелкий берег пляжа. Взрослый человек может дойти до стоящего вдалеке Антона и так и не найдет места глубже чем по пояс. На пол пути вода иногда чуть ниже колена. Однажды мы видели как одна мама поставила посредине воды раскладной стул а вокруг нее опускались её дети. Но стул был сухой. Если вам не охотно идти все это расстояние по воде вы можете обойти его по помосту.

There are benches around the playground where you can sit while your child runs and climb. But there are also disadvantages. We found there was only one beat toilet. He had to walk well and it was closed. The biggest minus is the complete lack of sources. Neither near the site nor in the parking lot or even near the toilet. We found none. So if you take something for your children to eat garbage, you have to bring it with you.

Вокруг площадки есть лавочки где можно посидеть пока твой ребенок бегает и лазить. Но есть и минусы. Мы нашли там только один бил туалет. К нему надо хорошо пройтись и он был закрыт. The outer one is longer. She walks along a gravel embankment. You can walk along the paths and enjoy the silence and tranquility of the forest. If you just love nature and love to walk or ride, then this place is created for you. If you like to go to a certain goal. Without a goal, the path is meaningless. Then you should look elsewhere. Enjoy your walks. And good mood.

Она проходит по насыпи из гравия. По тропинкам можно прогуляться и наслодится тишиной и спокойствием леса. Если вы просто любите природу и любите пройтись или проехаться то это место создано для вас. The transition itself was made very soundly and safely. On the other side of the railway, you will find a small park with a strip of shore. Depending on the time of day, the shore can be less or more. There are several tables in the park and a barbecue area nearby. A beautiful view of the bay opens from the shore. You can find crabs but I have not seen alive.

The park also has a place with distance indicators to various countries of the earth. The park area itself is quite large. There is a place where to run, take a walk or sit on the grass.

(Original)
Прекрасное место с большой детской площадкой. На площадку есть заезд для людей с ограниченными возможностями. В парке также есть место с указателями расстояния до различных стран земли. Сама площадь парка довольно большая. Есть место где побегать, прогуляться или посидеть на траве.

(Translated by Google) Location nice people (staff) polite. We, like many others, while we were riding a wheel, transported a stroller to the exit platform for the younger one. But the impression is spoiled by difficulties with parking. The cost of the ride must be added to the cost of parking.

(Original)
Место хорошее люди(обслуживающий персонал) вежливые. Нам как и многим другим пока мы катались на колесе перевезли коляску к платформе выхода для младшего. Но впечатление портит трудности с парковкой. К расходам на аттракцион надо прибавить расходы на парковку.

(Translated by Google) We had a good rest here. If you go to the left, you can find a quiet place with a very shallow river. On the right there is a beautiful beach where you can swim and dive.

(Translated by Google) Here you can sit on the grass or at small tables. Play volleyball. And for lovers of privacy, you need to go down the road on the left to a small beach.

(Translated by Google) A place where you can fly a kite, walk around and look at military installations and cannons, go down to the bay. A lot of space and always spacious.

(Translated by Google) I was only on the playground. The playground is quite large and varied. There are many slides, entrances and places for climbing.

I visited the historic Daniel Boone Homestead for the first time on Saturday October 26, 2019.  I recently purchased a new lens for my camera and I wanted to break it in so I chose this location to give it a try.  I was not disappointed in what I saw.  My first stop was the red building which is the visitors center.  I paid for the self-guided tour and I received a map.  Before going off on my journey I viewed a brief video about the site and its namesake.  There is a gift shop inside the visitors center.  I was facinated by the colorful early American buildings.  Unfortunately there was no real fall colors because of the many pine trees on the property.  The trails are stone covered which can be a little difficult to walk on but at least the trails are not muddy.  Be sure to check out the dam and the very muddy lake behind it, plus the grave site nearby. What was most enjoyable about my visit was how quiet and peaceful the homestead grounds were.  The only noise I heard was an occasional airplane, a few birds, and the waterfalls. What an enjoyable afternoon it was at my visit to the Daniel Boone Homestead in Berks County Pennsylvania.

I was a first time visitor to Natural Land’s Crow’s Nest Preserve on Sunday June 9, 2019.  The visitor center was closed which was no surprise but the uni-sex restroom was open.   I grabbed a trail map from the display and decided to hike the yellow-marked Creek & Chief's Grove Trail which is listed at 2.5 miles.  The low areas were quite muddy.  The higher parts of the trail go around corn fields.   I didn’t see any wildlife other than a few butterflies and dragonflies.  I saw a farmer spraying the cornfield which was the only wildlife I was able to observe.  The hike took about two hours in the intense sun.  I found that the trail was quite boring.  I ended up only took a few pictures.  The high feathery cirrus clouds in the crisp blue sky were the highlight of the trip.  On some trails horses are allowed.  No bikes are allowed.  There is a small but ample parking lot.  The hours are dusk to dawn.  Be aware of the constent gunfire from the nearby gun club.  Desturbs the peaceful atmosphere.

I was in Rochester last weekend for the 2019 Clothesline Festival and I was not disappointed at all.  The festival is huge!  I had planned on attending both days setting aside a half day to tour this great institution. The festival was a lot of fun.  There was food and music for all kinds of tastes.  I bought a print from a New York State artist.  The art gallery/museum is huge also.  Plenty to see so plan accordingly.  Someone was playing the huge pipe organ upstairs, probably trying to wake the mummies.  There is a restaurant on location also a fine gift shop.  Some of the artwork in the gallery is for sale so ask about it at the shop.  Plenty of parking when the festival is not running.  Memberships are also available which offers money saving benefits.  The Memorial Art Gallery (MAG) is located on the University Of Rochester Campus on University Avenue, Rochester New York USA.

Hunsicker’s Grove is located at 9350 Longswamp Rd, Mertztown, in Berks County PA 19539.  The park  is named after Mr. Hunsicker himself.  This is a nice park. The day for my first time visit was Wednesday June 12, 2019.  There were a few people fishing but nothing was biting even though there were fish jumping around in the lake.  There is no swimming or boating allowed.  Leave your bike in the car because there are no trails to explore.  There were public rest rooms and thankfully they were open.  Located a few miles outside of Topton,  the park is easy to find on Longswamp Road near the county line.  There is a small parking lot available with a few handicap spaces available. Make sure your fishing license is up to date.

I was in Rochester for the Clothesline Festival and before I went home I went exploring the Braddock Bay Wildlife Management Area.  Part of this area is actually a state park which does not show up on Google Maps.  I did not see any wildlife.  No birds or butterflies.  The swampy areas were, of course, muddy so dress accordingly.  Parking was free.  Watch your speed along the Parkway because the troopers were taking pictures.  After being at Braddock Bay I drove up Edgemere Road and took some pictures along the lake shore.  Braddock Bay also has a boat launch.  I did not see any restaurants nearby.  I doubt I would visit again on my next visit to Rochester.

Pros:
•	Lots of really rare automobiles.
•	Friendly staff of volunteers.
•	Pictures are allowed.
•	Location is easy to find.

Cons:

•	Poor lighting in the main building.  In the newer building in the back skylights were added.
•	Not many information displays have the vehicle location of manufacture listed.  I had to ask about one of the cars.
•	The clothing displays add nothing to the experience.  It’s just like the Pierce-Arrow museum in Buffalo.
•	Get rid of the silly music.  The theme music from the Viagra commercial playing in the background brought a chuckle.   Actually it’s rather tacky.  No, I haven't lost that lovin' feeling but I got a headache.

After buying my new hatchback on Thursday I wanted to go mountain biking so on Sunday 25 August 2019 I visited Evansburg State Park for the first time.  It was as I expected but it is not my favorite state park.  I did manage to take some interesting photos which I'll upload later this week. Check out the historic EIGHT ARCH BRIDGE.  I nearly fell in the mud trying to get to it and it was well worth it for me.  The bike parking is off of Fern Avenue which was not easy to find on  my new navigation system. I saw a huge butterfly near the bridge but was unable to capture a photograph.

Beautiful historic site located abou two miles from the FDR PRESIDENTIAL MUSEUM.  The museum gave me a small map with directions to Eleanor's cottage which was very helpful.  There was no admission fee.  I was given a guided tour of the estate by a park employee and I learned a lot.  There was a brief video before the tour started which was also interesting.  Since my visit I have ordered books on Eleanor's life and her autobiography.  This site is a must see on your presidential tour.  Bring your cameras but flash is not allowed.

Not being from Lancaster County I did not know about this landmark bridge until yesterday when I discovered it on Google Maps.   I was on my way to the Green Dragon and I made a special stop on the way to visit this fine bridge.  I was not disappointed and I liked the way my pictures came out so I posted the here.  There is no park for picnics and the bridge is surrounded by private property and a muddy field.  Bucher's Mill is worth the detour in your travels through Lancaster County Pennsylvania.

This wildlife sanctuary is operated by the county and it is open to the public.  The paved parking lot provides plenty of spaces.  Unfortunately when I was there the rain prevented me fro exploring all the trails.  I think the rain put a damper on any wildlife making an appearance that day.  I would come back again if I am in the area.  It is a long drive from home.  The trails are marked making them very interesting subjects to explore.  Bring the kids.  They'll love it!

Well off the main highway, Lyman Run State Park offers some scenic views and a cool dip in the water on a hot Sunday in June.  Be sure to bring your bug repellant and sun screen.  There is a concession stand which I did not use.  The kid that was running it had set up a boom box with loud, horrible music which spoiled the whole connect with nature thing.  Other than that it was a nice afternoon.  Next year I'll try a different park because there are many along Route 6.

It was such a beautiful fall day on Saturday November 2, 2019 that I had to stop at the Paoli Battlefield Historical Park and take some pictures.  I enjoy history and this park with its monuments did not disappoint me.  I thought the two small cannons in front of the memorial were cool.  Quite a few people brought their dogs to the park on this day. There is plenty of room for the dogs to run. The park is located in the residential area of Paoli Pennsylvania.

First time visitor on Wednesday July 24, 2019.  I liked the park even though my personal experience was less then ideal.  The park seems to be well maintained and the grass was being cut while I was there.  The parking area was unpaved.  I think there are restrooms at the park but I did not visit it. There are no signs on the main road that directs you the park entrance.  I actually drove by it the first time.

Wonderful place to spend some time at.  Scenic along the river and it's usually quiet except for sporting or special events.  The track is an added plus for walkers or cyclists.  Come and enjoy.
UPDATE:  May 13, 2020.  The park was open.  No large groups were seen.  A new park bench was put in since my last visit.  Lots of birds singing today.  Love this place.  I always  ride my bike here.

The Da Vinci Science Center is an ultra modern hands-on science center offering a learning experience and fun for all ages.  Located on the beautiful campus of Cedar Crest College, the Da Vinci Science center is easy to reach from all main highways in the Lehigh Valley.  Free parking is available and it is open seven days a week.  Check website for current hours and exhibits.

I was fortunate to visit the top of the William Penn Memorial Fire Tower while attending the Reading Hospital Road Run on October 14, 2018.  It was my first visit to the tower and I hiked up all the stairs with my camera and the views were well worth the effort.  I will bring my zoom lens next time.

Date of visit: June 30, 2019.  The lock house was not open for visitors when I was here.  They were opening the following weekend.  The lock house is a charming looking building from the outside and it appears to be well kept.   I did not see a walking trail that was mentioned in another review.

I driving through Boyertown over the weekend and I spotted the trains so I had to stop and check it out.  I will make plans for a future train ride. There is a parking lot and a small restaurant directly across the street.  I'm not sure if the restaurant is connected with the railroad.

Not too many automobile museums in the world feature the notorious Tucker automobile.  That alone is worth the price to the AACA Museum in Hershey Pennsylvania.  Come and explore when you have lots of time and don’t forget your camera.

First time visitor on Sunday October 21 2018.  Walked halfway.  Great views.  Very windy.  Actually too much wind so I walked carefully back to safer ground.  Will visit again when visiting Harrisburg.
Cool trains.  Make your reservations in advance to be sure to get a seat.  Tours sell out quickly especially the fall leaves trip to Jim Thorpe in Carbon County.  Free parking at all their locations.
The park is wonderful especially for the young ones.  Ellicott Creek tends to flood during heavy storms.  I used to live on Holly Lane and I remember the high water events.
Wednesday May 15, 2019. Now that I know where the railroad museum is located I will make plans to visit when they are open on weekends.  Looks interesting.
Small neighborhood park with ball fields, basketball courts, picnic area, and a playground.  Plenty of parking in the lot and on the street.
This scenic covered bridge is a great way to relax anytime of the year.  And don't forget to bring your camera!

Someone once told me that going to this Basilica is like going to Europe, without ever leaving Milwaukee. Now I know what they mean. It is absolutely gorgeous.I came in here and just wandered around. They have a nice little exhibit that talks about the history of the Basilica. However, apparently they have a tour Sunday after mass. I think it would be worth you doing a tour to hear more about the architecture and the history of this fantastic place.

We were looking for some fun and affordable things to do on our last full day in Madison. And nothing is more affordable than free! Free is the best! To add to that, I adore exploring art museums. And I love me some contemporary art!! I mean...really. I was sold in a heartbeat. This was the second museum we visited on the day, following a morning at the Chazen. It is an easy walk between the two, if you are interested, by the way.

I absolutely love this zoo. Its not the biggest or has the most animals but it's a perfect size for a city like Milwaukee. They have been updating specific exhibits over time. Elephants got a huge update that just finished and now they are using that area for a new hippo exhibit. It definitely shows the contrasting differences on how you built a zoo now vs 20-30 years ago when you look at the older buildings vs the new additions.

We enjoy this park for hiking, pick nicking and the play ground. The park is never very busy and they have carts to use to haul things to the park area. Nice mix of trails that are through the woods and prairie. You do have to watch carefully when hiking since the trails aren't marked great. We enjoy the park area for the view of the water and Madison. Also like all the shade and breeze, perfect for relaxing or a picnic.

Definitely worth going to if you are in the area. Our group of three adults and one toddler spent about an hour here, but you could definitely spent a couple hours looking at everything. Suggested donation was $3 which I thought was very reasonable.It's in a very cool old building (guess it used to be the old post office). But it's not much of a museum. Really it's just one big room with dinosaur skeletons.

Best park in the city, absolutely gorgeous running paths. My favorite run is starting at the entrance on Lincoln Memorial and Lake Drive, past the bocce ball players and infamous lawn bowlers,  and winding down and around Lake Park Bistro - across the beautiful bridge that leads to the North Point Lighthouse, turning left at the end of the path and running past the gorgeous mansions and beautiful homes,

The bathrooms were really clean. The showers were in good condition & clean. There are flush toilets near the ranger station & by the beach. The campsites were nice & spacious. Lake Kegonsa has a pet beach! The regular beach is nice with plenty of picnic tables but a little rocky. You need to go about 30ft from the shore to get to the sandy ground. The whole swimming area doesn't get deeper than 4ft.

Been here a few different times now, each time for a special event going on.  First time was near Halloween for their pumpkin patch picking event.  It was a lot of fun and very well done.  We did go very first thing in the morning for that one so it wasnt super crowded on the train ride or really that crowded inside.  By the time we left a few hours later the parking lot was completely full.

This is a nice park. Went to the larger pillion for a birthday party. Plenty of things for the kids to do in the park. They even had a merry-go-round which the kids loved. The bathrooms were clean and the pavilion was large enough for all of the people when it rained on and off. The parking is a tad confusing though and it gets really dark at night. Could use more lighting.

This place is such an exquisite milwaukee spot. Today was my third time at the Villa Terrace. The first I toured the museum, the second I took photos on my wedding day, and today for a lovely networking event. That being said, the space is versatile for all different things. It's located high up on the hillside facing Lake Michigan and the overlook is gorgeous!!!

Visited the Schlitz Audubon Nature Center while I was in town for the Audubon Convention 2019. I visited everyday just to see new birds. I photographed cardinals, black-capped chickadees, a blue jay, and so much more. The place is beautiful, peaceful, and serene. The educational facilities on site are amazing.  I love that they have preschools there.

Always a great experience, park is very nice and scenic. There is something for everyone to do, from the kids playground to disk golf, volleyball, walks. Something for everyone.There are also picnic areas and a large playground that kids love spending time in.  There are also pavilions for rent and enough space to take long walks.

We had about 150 people, DJ setup, ice cream vendor, food vendor, bar vendor, and a cake vendor dropped off and set up. You just have to be out by 10 PM; plenty of time for an early afternoon wedding.This was my first time at Green isle Park I brought my dog along for a new stroll. I absolutely loved it!! And so did my little guy!

I've been to many museums, but none have been quite as fantastical as my home museum, the Milwaukee Public Museum.It's almost as if it has a way of transporting you. Not just through time, but into a magical land of wonder. The twists and turns of the dark hallways always beckoning you further to see where it will take you next.

As a Detroit resident and car guy extraordinaire, this was a great surprise in Downtown Green Bay.  This collection was really fantastic - The collection has a Fireball 8 that was owned by former Packer great Reggie White, and the Corvette that Bart Starr was given for winning the Super Bowl is on loan there currently.

Boring is the first word that comes to mind when I think of Wisconsin but Mitchell Park Conservatory is far from boring. I'm so glad we decided to drive here from Chicago to visit the three domes. Admission is $8 per adult and $6 for students or those 17 and under so be sure to bring your student id or id of some sort!

Love coming here with my daughter. Awesome little treasure Green Bay has. We love first stopping to watch through the window of the little animal hospital to see what little babies they may be helping at the time! They have birds and wolves and snakes and bats and more birds! So fun to walk around and see them all.

Although the museum has a reasonable range of activities, it is somewhat small and will likely not appeal to kids before 3.This place does not participate in inter-museum membership we had (from Chicago area), which meant we had to pay full admission despite having bought an expensive annual membership elsewhere.

A fun place to spend a bit of time if you're in Green Bay. Lots of 1 cent slots, free non-alcoholic beverages, smoke shop attached. I especially enjoy the big buffalo, Goonies, and Flintstones slots.Smoking is permitted inside the casino, but for those who dislike smoke there's an area that's smoke free as well.

A spectacular view of the University and downtown Madison. And a spectacular sunset vista the opposite way. Truly a great walk but bikes are no longer allowed.I love it here, very scenic. Sometimes a little flooded so prepare to get dirty. Reserve the fire pits and have fun with friends.

This place is super cute ! I should've took more pictures but the staff (I don't even want to call them that) were super nice and helpful.I did the $5 wine tasting and fell in love with the Wisconsin Maple Brown Cider .... it's delicious now my favorite angry orchard has competition :-)

I like that I can bring my dog here as well, since she is so tiny I’m not comfortable bringing her to a dog park and here leashes are required. The only downfall is the parking can be pretty full at times.The jungle gym was awesome, kids didn't want to come home.

Magnificent architecture. The wings, the bridge, the glass windows. Photos don't do the place justice. Admission is not free but if you're not afraid of heights, go up onto the bridge at no cost and take some beautiful pics.Parking garage located underground.

Today I found lots of turkey eggs taken for grab...everyone needs to eat..found a pile of lily of the valley to smell and a nice turkey feather. It's close and though I can hear the highway, I am in the woods and the bird song is so wonderful. Grounding.

Had a great experience here! Their website had the wrong tour time posted, but a volunteer gave me and my daughters a personal tour of the museum. Very cool information about our state right in the middle of Capital Square. We will definitely be back.

Sky View Observatory has an amazing view of Seattle, a complete 360 degree view and from 73 floors above to be exact. Nothing is obstructed since it is located in the tallest building in downtown, Seattle. We have been here several times and everyone we've spoken to is very friendly and knowledgeable. And if they aren't, they find the right people who can help you. They throw some really great events that I would highly recommend checking out such as Pride events, 4th of July, yoga, Sunset experiences, etc. The events get pretty busy and packed but if you go on any regular day, the views are breathtaking and it's rather tranquil. They also have fun games like Connect Four if you just want to sit and take in the views. Regardless, definitely a place to check out with the whole family or a perfect place for date night!
likes: Diverse events (Pride, 4th of July, yoga, Sunset experiences)

reviews_attraction.text: I go running here for the un-paved trails. There are paved trails and walks but my knees don’t like those. There are also some good hills and stairs to get that uphill and downhill workouts on. But the best thing is just the natural beauty and the quiet once you get away from the road. I also go walking here with my wife and do some slack lining from time to time as well as picnics and I sometimes use it for portrait sessions as I am a photographer. It has playgrounds, picnic tables, ball fields, waterfront beaches, driftwood, and spectacular views. It can get crowded and parking can get scarce later on a nice sunny day. I’ve also launched two or three kayaking day trips from here. Twice we’ve crossed the Puget sound to Blake Island and another we just paddled the west Seattle coastline.

Washington Trails Association is the organization for hikers and lovers of the outdoors. From their website: "We protect hiking trails and wild lands, take volunteers out to maintain trails, and promote hiking as a healthy, fun way to explore the outdoors." $35 a year for a membership and you get a monthly magazine plus hiking and volunteering information. In the magazine and the website, you get information on the best places to hike, where to hike with children and pets, and the best gear for your hikes. You can also volunteer in one of the Work Trail Parties where you can help for 1-4 days maintaining different trails. If you love hiking and the outdoors, this is the organization for you. I haven't become a member yet, but I plan on joining in the near future.

Many people do not realize that the Green Lake Park and surrounding attractions were inspired by Central Park and Golden Gate Park. Green Lake is a man-made lake with a 3 mile trail around it. The lake itself offers SUP, kayak, and paddle boat rentals. Early in the morning you can enjoy watching the crew teams row. Connected to the park is a mini-gold course, an off leash dog park, baseball fields, tennis courts, the Woodland Zoo, the Woodland Park, and even a small fishing park...all of these green spaces are link together, though locals tend to view them as separate entities. Much of Seattle visits Green Lake on sunny days and it is a common date site with coffee shops and restaurants around the perimeter.
likes: Recreational facilities (mini-golf, dog park, sports fields, zoo)

reviews_attraction.text: This was once a US Navy airfield called "Sandpoint", built on the edge of Lake Washington, an ideal place to test seaplanes. In the fifties, the base was turned into a park named for Washington Senator Warren Magnuson. Its a large park that's usually pretty empty, as it's slightly off the beaten path. There are few amenities here (you'll have to hunt for the rest rooms), but its free and has copious parking. Magnuson has a long shoreline on the fresh water Lake Washington. You can swim there, or use the boat ramps to put in and tool around looking for salmon. Lake Washington is still a major seaplane training area, and you're likely to see numerous practise "touch and goes" here.

We went on a rainy day, and I got soaked. There's very little coverage to get out of the rain, but I didn't care. It was so amazing to watch these animals up close. You stand behind a fence that's about 5 feet from the animal's cage, and so close that you can hear them purring. Others have said that the cages are too small for these large animals, but they were pretty large...at least larger than I thought they'd be, and there's only one animal per enclosure. These people are doing their best to take care of these animals. The enclosures are clean and the animals look healthy. The staff are really friendly and willing to talk to you about the animals.

Why did I wait so long to visit the Museum of Flight? This is a gem and core to the Seattle experience. The docents are passionate about their airplanes. Many have worked on individual planes and speak eloquently about them. The sheer number of exhibits is perhaps overwhelming but they are laid out well and thematically. Be sure to be prepared to walk a lot. By all means, save some time to visit the planes across the street. On the day we were there, the cafeteria was very crowded. Food was acceptable but nothing to write home about. If the weather is nice, you can sit outside to enjoy your meal while watching the active runway of Boeing Field.

This is a magnificent cathedral. Built in 1903 it is a perfect example of the beauty and majesty of cathedrals built at the beginning of the 20th century. Inside is tastefully ornate with beautiful stained glass windows, detailed marble stations of the cross and a towering pulpit. The alter is imposing and flanked by two huge circular stained glass windows and five stained glass windows behind. The rounded ceiling resembles waffling. There is a majestic pipe organ upstairs in the choir loft. The grounds are simple and there is a grotto nestled on the right side. Worth a few minutes for any cathedral junkie.

We only came across this garden when looking for something to do whilst waiting for a flight to land at Seatac. Definitely worth seeking out for anyone nearby. Not many free entrance tickets in Seattle and this is one. Beautiful gardens, beautifully kept. Despite not being huge and the presence of severalf' photographers ' using the gardens as backdrops, the wast still space to find a quiet corner. Extra bonus- when we visited of a performance piece taking place which definitely added to the atmosphere. Very small car park but street parking available . Great location, throughly recommended.

Golden Gardens is a scenic, quiet spot to stroll along the water and take in the beautiful surroundings. My toddler daughter LOVED running along the beach (a novelty to a resident of a landlocked state) and even rolling around in the sand. You can't help but feel anything other relaxed and happy here - the environment doesn't allow for anything else! Parking can be dicey, but otherwise this is a terrific park. Very nice beach, lots of areas to sit, a cute café. On a nice day it is beautiful but I'm guessing it would be a fun beach walk even in weather that is overcast or even stormy.

We walked the trails on the Dishman Hills side off of Appleway. There are many trails to wander around on. There are no maps from the trailhead and I wished we had printed one off. So we just went here and there and had a good time. Very cool rock formations. We did run across a somewhat hidden area that might have been used as a homeless camp. There were clothing items and a flashlight hanging from a tree. I sure would not walk alone. The only restroom we found was at the lodge.But it was a great outing and I want to go back and maybe also go to the Iller Creek area.

If you have any free time you will want to go to Manito Park on the South Hill off Grand Blvd. The park has beautiful grounds, Japanese Gardens, Duncan Gardens (beautiful rose and flower gardens) a large wonderful pond and great areas for walking, picnics, family gatherings, etc. In the winter there is a sledding hill or two. The homes around the park are old and beautiful as well - many are of the Arts and Crafts style and date back to the 1920's and 30's (many newer ones too). Give yourself several hours to wander through the park - walk, bike or drive.

Slightly under renovations when we went, the proposed changes look amazing when completed. Cool 1909 Carousel, they actually do the bronze rings that you read about in turn of century stories. The Radio Wagon slide is a hoot. I'd like to go back to see the Urban Falls - we got turned around and didn't make it there before we left. Parking can be a bit of a challenge, the only thing I'd like for them to include after they finish up the renos is some more signage with directions to the various options. Overall, great place to stop for an afternoon.

The 2.8 mile walking/bike trail around the peninsula in the park is the best spot for clocking in those 10,000 steps. The pathway is just steps from Lake Washington, shaded by towering trees. In certain seasons, eagles are perched on the trees at the northern point of the park, and in summer you can watch the rowing teams from the nearby Mt Baker Rowing Center working out. Parking can get tight on weekends and nice summer days, but there are good restrooms and some nice picnic areas too.

The museum usually has multiple exhibits going on. i went t see a Dale Chuilly exhibit and also saw an exhibit of native dress and lifestyle. There was another room with photos, paintings and artifacts from the far north. There is a restaurant and a gift shop on site, and ramps to walk to the exhibits so stairs and the elevator can be avoided. This is a small but interesting museum and my ticket included entrance to the Campbell House. I loved the collection of glass sculptures.

Assuming your here on vacation this is a must see location. Lots to see and do with some of the most stunning views of Puget sound. It touristy but traveler or tourist you need to visit and experience. The Crab Pot restaurant was great. We had Snow Crabs and they were a treat. Definitely recommend visiting and dining. Plenty of public parking across the street. If you haven’t been to Seattle parking can be tough and often pricy. Public parking is a welcome sight even at a fee.

Even if you don't enjoy pop culture, it is hard not to have a great time and learning experience here. Great collection of famous guitars (i.e. Eric Clapton's "Brownie"), costumes from movies and TV ("Cowardly Lion from Oz and Mork's suit), temporary exhibits on Prince, Hendrix and Pearl Jam, all housed in a wonderful Gehry building - with fabulous A/V facilities. Would have stayed much longer than two hours, but our parking in the adjacent pay lot was running out.
likes: Attraction Type: Music and film memorabilia

reviews_attraction.text: Blake Island State Park can only be accessed by private boat or through the Argosy Tours which leave from the Seattle waterfront. I have. This is a great place to hike, fish, camp, birdwatch, play with the Deers and experience Tillicum Village, Seattle’s Premier Native Cultural Experience and Home of the Famous Salmon Bake. I have come here many times, even camping with my scout Pack & Troop a number of times. A truly amazing place.

An opportunity to walk among the trees and greenery while enjoying the various art sculptures. Beautiful area, where you can find a spot, sit and relax before moving on to explore the rest of this fun city. This is a regular park to sit down and rest up and see the waterfront. There are couple of sculptures around. We walked to it and its definitely a hike from the city. We took a taxi to the cruise. Its not a must do in Seattle.

This park is a very local site, with amazing views and a nice walk. This park is great for small children because of the nice playground and great for dogs because of the open grass space. If you go late winter and very early in the morning, you might catch the rare snow that falls on Seattle, giving it a magical feel. You can sled and kite on this hill! This is a great year-round destination.

Recently visited Splash Down on a Friday afternoon with a group that included kids, parents, and grandparents, and all had a wonderful time. It has a relaxed and easy-going atmosphere and friendly employees. I loved that you could hang out on the lawn - in the sun or shade - and that it was mostly grass, not concrete. If you're looking for a relaxing and fun day outdoors, this is a sure bet.

This is a fun and engaging hands-on science center that kids will love, and learn a lot while having great fun. As an adult, its hard not to try out some of the exhibits, and that’s encouraged as well. The staff is wonderful. They wander around the space periodically to check on how you’re doing and answer questions. Every city should have a science center this wonderful. Bravo Mobius!

Everything about the gallery was well done. We wanted to visit an art gallery whilst in Seattle and chose this one as it seemed to be the one most mentioned. We saw a touring exhibition (victorian radicals) and then visited the main galleries. The works are well lit and well labelled and the gallery is spacious enough for one to not feel crowded. There is a good cafe and gift shop.

We stopped in to tour the cathedral and accidentally interrupted a group of ladies having a meeting. They graciously stopped to greet us and share information about the church and surrounding area. There was not a formal tour going on at the time but we were encouraged to take a brochure and visit at our own pace. The cathedral is beautiful and peaceful and well worth a visit!

I always see about the Klondike on Discovery channel , we came across this museum by mistake but I was pretty excited to take a look. Free enterance which is super nice and the museum is built in a very interesting way with a lot of pictures and information. We were there for about 30 min , if you're in the area I recommend coming insode for a few min :)

I'm giving this railway four stars because I support the volunteers and the nonprofit behind the railway museum in their goal of keeping the line alive and running for the community,  rail enthusiasts,  and the general public.

The rail line is short and from the Snoqualmie station, the whole trip lasts just 45 minutes (Snoqualmie to North Bend, back to the end of the line with a partial view of the famous waterfall, before disembarking at the Snoqualmie station).

The diesel engine-pulled train itself is nothing to crow about, the carriages look sad, the upholstered chairs are dusty and have seen better days (remember that it's almost a century old). Also, eighty-percent of the view along the line is a snooze.

So is the fare worth it then? At $20/adult, $10/child yes. Why, you ask? Because the last stretch, is the view that you paid for. The train takes you by the side of the Snoqualmie falls and stops to let you marvel at the beauty of the river as it continues down the valley (see the pics).

You'll have about 5-10 minutes to enjoy the view so bring your good binoculars and long photo-lense cameras on the trip.

After the train ride, drive over to the viewing platforms for the waterfall and enjoy the vantage point from the other side (it's free).

The Snoqualmie station is surrounded by small local stores, with multiple food options.

You can enjoy the train ride, a hike and views of the fall in half a day so plan accordingly.
likes: Cultural Value: Volunteer support, Nonprofit mission

reviews_attraction.text:
Awesome place for kids and adults alike. The admission fee can be steep, for my party of two adults and a 3.5 year old, we paid roughly sixty-two dollars, so plan on going in the morning and spending as much time enjoying the whole place (you can go in and out with a hand stamp after initial entry in case you need to go out and eat).

Went there for the dinosaur exhibit (a small, permanent exhibit of a few of the most famous ones) plus the special three-day train show happening this MLK weekend for my train then dinosaur fan toddler.

Unfortunately it was a little too crowded for my son who got jostled by bigger and/or aggressive kids. So if your little one is still learning to stand his or her ground, a bit shy or averse to big crowds, come on a weekday.

Parking is also a bit challenging on a weekend at the Seattle Center so keep that in mind. The restrooms are clean, there are water fountains in strategic areas, a cafe if you want to sit down for coffee or a snack by the dinosaur exhibit, or get popcorn, soda and candies down by the IMAX theater.

If you are a big crowd, say at least eight people, purchasing a family membership will be cheaper. And after an exhausting (and expensive) trip to the Science Center, save on dining costs by heading to the Metropolitan Market (less than a 10 minute walk away) and check out their hot bar, deli and numerous dessert options.

Beautiful lakeside park in downtown. It is a must stop for locals and tourists alike.

The park is right beside the Kenmore Air seaplane dock and the Argosy Ship Lake tours and is the launch pad for other smaller (check out the pirate and ice cream-themed cruises) lake tours in the area.

Lots of open space for playing frisbee, getting a tan, or lounging by the water as you watch the seaplanes land and depart, kayaks and all shapes and sizes of boats.

Bring cash if you'd like to explore some of the boats docked (for donation). The Sea Shepherd boat is there this summer to promote their mission and sell merch to raise funds. It's a beautiful boat for a noble cause.

Plenty of pay parking though you are limited to maximum of four hours (you can just move your car to another spot to start the 4 hour clock over again).

There is a small strip of beach for swimming though you have to share the water with the seaplanes arriving and departing - so keep an eye out. You can also launch your kayak from the beach.

There is a Starbucks nearby, and a cafe at the MOHAI. Otherwise, food and drink options are limited.

Must see aviation museum in Seattle. There's lots of interesting exhibits, plenty of space for kids and adults to explore, and a wonderful museum store to shop aviation-themed merchandise.

Particularly enjoyed the kids port where small children can play, interactive exhibits, docent lead tours (the volunteers are just wonderful and so knowledgeable) and strategically located benches if you need a short break (the museum is huge).

If you love history, airplanes, and space rockets don't miss this place. We plan on coming back after the Seafair weekend.

Tips:
1. Visit Georgetown's highly rated food scene first (2-3 miles from the museum)
2. Plenty of parking but it does get busy, and when it's full at the main parking area, head to the museum building across the street
3. Spend time outdoors too, on the lawn facing the runway, and enjoy watching all the airplanes zipping overhead

Wonderful park in the middle of downtown Bellevue. Love, love the huge grassy field that is perfect for playing ball, badminton or frisbee, or playing catch with your dog.

There's plenty of parking on site, or at the mall just across the street. There are restrooms at the corner by the children's playground.

An unpaved trail that run the whole of the park for walkers and joggers, numerous benches if you get tired and just want to people watch, and three or four picnic tables clustered together one level above the playground are some of the features of the park.

It's a nice place to visit in the spring through early fall, and the only place to go to for ice skating in December (well, there is the rink in Lynnwood but that is another review).

Awesome park for everyone. We came here on a cool summer day and had an impromptu wade in the kids' wading pool. This large pool is great for little ones with the deepest part barely reaching the knee of a short four-year old. So make sure you take along a change of clothes and towels for the kiddos if you are coming to the park.

I also liked that the park had a staff watching over the pool fishing out debris and telling irresponsible pooch owners that the pool is for kids and not a drinking bowl for their animal.

Parking is notoriously difficult for this popular park so instead of trying your luck in finding a rare open spot in the parking area, park on the street along East Green Lake Way.

Small, quiet park at the north end of Lake Washington where you can watch the seaplanes take-off and land. Picnic tables by the playground and at the entrance to the boardwalk are available for visitors.

Parking (<20 car slot) is often full as this place is a favorite staging area of cyclists on the Burke-Gilman trail. A bicycle self-repair station was recently added.

Children's playground (toddler to 7yrs old) is well maintained. Paddle boards and kayaks are for rent in the summer. Clean male and female restrooms.

Overall a great park to spend a few hours in. Recommended for all ages.

Note: Pictures are from today 08.24.2018, where the air quality (WAQA) is at an unhealthy level.

I have a toddler so I love taking my little one to places that have multiple features that'll keep us busy and engaged in one trip.

Marina Beach Park is one of those places. It has an off-leash dog park, a long stretch of clean sandy beach, a playground, and a big grassy area.

There is ample parking space, a water fountain, a faucet for rinsing off sand, park benches and picnic tables. There are two portalets although if you want to use a proper toilet, you should walk over to Anthony's restaurant and use the public toilet located on the side of the building.

There isn't much shade so if you aren't planning on getting a tan, visit when the sky is overcast or bring an umbrella.

Updated (Feb 2020):
Now open with better curated exhibits, and facilities for museum-goers' comfort. Free entrance on the first Thursday of each month (and very busy).

Small museum at the UW Seattle campus that contains the only dinosaur exhibit in the state.

Small exhibits on culture and natural history of Washington. Fully enjoyed in under two hours and great for kids who love dinosaurs.

Notes:
Museum closes in January and won't open until Fall of 2019

Parking is limited so taking the bus is recommended

Entrance free for UW faculty, students and staff and kids 4 and under.

The park has a large playground with features to delight kids eight years old and below. For adults accompanying their kids, there are plenty of spots to sit and watch as the kiddos run around.

There are bathroom stalls at the entrance with a changing station, a drinking and washing fountain, a huge shelter for picnics, a basketball court, and a wide grassy field perfect for frisbee-playing or practicing your kids' batting.

Parking is ample enough though expect it to be at full capacity as the days are sunnier and with school almost out.

There's a huge field that

If you or your kids want to see horses, you can fold in a hike and horse watching on the trail in this multi modal hike haven. Take note though that in the preserve, the hierarchy on the trail has the horse at the top, followed by humans on foot, then bicycles. And of course, follow common sense and be respectful of the horse (or you might end up spooking the animal).

There's picnic tables out in the parking area by the restrooms. Parking is sufficient (small but there's not a lot of traffic anyway) and toilets clean.

Huge park with play fields, a playground, wide grassy fields, an Audobon trail, a concert field, an off-leash dog park, a self-service dog wash, picnic shelters, washrooms, and park benches.

Plan to spend a whole day at the park if you only have one to spend in the area. Bring binoculars to spot eagles, hawks, woodpeckers and other birds. A pair of boots if it just rained (some trails and paths can get muddy). A picnic basket with all the requisite provisions. And bicycles.

A must go to park!

Wonderful park with a local museum, bridge access to the Burke-Gilman trail, kayak and paddle board access to the Sammamish slough, a short trail beside the water, a nice playground and plenty of benches and spots to lay out a mat and have a picnic.

There's a drinking fountain and clean restrooms onsite. For food if you forgot to bring any, there's a string of higher end and medium priced restaurants, a bakery, and a hamburger place just a short walk away.

Highly recommended.

It's a beautiful beachfront park. There's plenty of metered parking - all day is $10 so plan on staying awhile and you will considering all the exploring, picture-taking, bird-, seal/sea lion/whale- and ferry watching you'll do on the visit. There's fire pits, benches, a brew pub, ice cream, and Ivar's nearby. Walk to the ferry to admire the new terminal building and take a short ferry ride to Clinton and back. The outdoor fun options are endless. Highly recommended.

Beautiful park in Bothell. There is walk-on access to and view of the Sammamish slough, a large playground, a disc golf set-up, a short trail into the woods and the former Wayne golf course and flat grassy ground for playing frisbee, soccer and other activities.

Plenty of picnic tables, two large shelters (one of which has a fireplace), lots of parking and clean toilets for park visitors.

We had the added bonus of a mama and young deer sighting!

Awe-inspiring, it was my first hike in Mt. Rainier ever and was glad I chose to hike to this landmark.

It was a long hike from the Sunrise Visitor Center and on a hot, busy summer day, it was extra challenging. You have to mind your hiking manners on the narrow and dangerous stretches of the trail that I couldn't stop and take pictures along the way.

But, pictures be damned, I enjoyed the hike, the view and the challenge. I'm sure you would too.

This is a wonderful high elevation trail for novice hikers who want to be challenged on their first few hikes.

Expect to encounter chipmunks along the trail on the hunt for scraps and favors from humans - please do not fall for their adorable antics. They are still wildlife. Think small rat just with stripes and bushy tails.

Mind your hiking manners on the narrow and dangerous lengths of the trail, stopping and allowing others to pass.

Easy, level trail in the Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Park. Accessible from I-5 passing through the towns of Oso and Darrington. About 6 miles roundtrip from main trailhead (with toilet, bigger parking lot, and picnic tables) to the minor trailhead (smaller parking lot and no toilet).

Recommended for all abilities, small children and pets.

Huge park of mostly flat surface, numerous trails, restored wetlands, athletic facilities, explorable shoreline (though currently discouraged due to high bacteria concentration), dozens of birds, and plenty of parking.

Lots of off-leashed dogs though despite signs to keep them leashed so careful if you are bringing small kids

Park with lots of space and multiple features (trails, beach, open grassy areas) that's great for everyone. Wonderful for families with small children. Picnic tables, benches are interspersed throughout the park. Toilet facilities available. Ample parking (different areas) though it can get crowded on sunny days.

Nice little park in Kenmore with (two) playgrounds for toddlers and older kids, a huge flat and open grass ground, a shelter with picnic tables, and a basketball court. Toilets and drinking fountain available. Small parking lot shared with the senior center. Shelter can be reserved for small parties.

It's a nice quiet park with a view of the water, plenty of parking, a picnic shelter, restrooms, and a large playground for small to big kids.

We stopped by after we took the whalewatching tour boat from the Everett Marina. Glad we did!

Nice little park with plenty of parking. Perfect for introducing small children to hiking. Look out for dog poop when veering off the hiking path, there were several when we were there. Also some dogs were off leash.

Wanted to check out the center for whale info before we went to the park to try to spot the grey whales but it was closed. Will have to come back next time and maybe we will get lucky with a whale sighting.
The beach, train spotting, almost 180 degrees view of the Puget Sound, lots of parking, multilevel park, playground and picnic areas. Something for everybody. One of my favorite parks!

Wow! This place is gorgeous! Great scenic trails lead up to a really tall set of stairs that seriously kicked our backsides. I've hiked up Rib Mountain many times in my life, the stairs here are much more strenuous. A great view at the top makes it all worth it though.

The petroglyph area is very cool, and worth coming here to see even if you don't get to the top of the stairs (though I'd suggest going up there at least once in your life).

We'll be back again sometime to take the rest of the trails, as we didn't get there early enough time this time around. I suggest the winter parking area to start your hike. It's very scenic and beautiful.

There is a playground area, shelter, picnic tables, grills, and vault toilets. There are many informational signs to learn about the area.

There are several Pokestops and gyms here for the Go players.
likes: Facilities (playground, shelter, picnic tables, grills, toilets)

reviews_attraction.text:
I'm not sure if I came at a bad time, or if I wasn't on the same trails as the other commenters, but the trails were BAD after the initial rock formations (going down to the backside). All torn up, overgrown with thorn branches, and I lost the trail completely on the back side by the water. I had to go up through extremely rough terrain by the tower to get back to a trail and get down before losing all sunlight. I made it back to my car about 10 minutes before dark.

That said, beautiful area! I'd like to visit here again in summer, and in autumn before the leaves drop. Phenomenal views! Well worth the trip, but give yourself more than two hours before sundown to hike it, lol. Also, you might want to wear some pretty thick clothing, and/or bring a machete. I got all cut up from the thorns.

I feel like if I had been alive at the right time, in the right place, I would have joined Muir on his journey. Of course, I probably would have died of dysentery before making it to Oregon...

A very pretty park with historical significance. You can definitely see what gave John Muir his love of nature and wanderlust as you hike around this area. Probably the easiest Ice Age Trail segment, but still very much worth doing. The hike took us around 45 minutes, but we stopped frequently for photos and just to look and listen.

There is a paved parking area, shelter, restrooms, a boat launch (non-motorized), and a fishing dock here.

There is at least one gym and one Pokestop for the Go players.

This is my third trip here, (elementary school field trip, once in my teens, and now as an adult), and it's still a great place to visit.

Less than $20/person, and now they're doing self guided tours.

The area around it is beautiful, and the cave itself is breathtaking. It takes about and hour to work you way through, and you may want to bring a light jacket, as it is cool and damp (you will get dripped on).

It has a gift shop with photos, polished rocks, geodes, fossils, and swag available for purchase.

The staff is friendly and knowledgeable, and great with young children.

This is worth seeing at least once in your life (or three times!)

A very unique state park. The mounds look impressive enough from the parking lot, but when you get a different perspective from the water, they're HUGE! Beautiful area. Lots of informational signs. Definitely worth visiting! Someone was playing a flute (or some instrument) from the top of the big mound while we were by the water. It carried very well, and added to the beauty.

There are three separate parking lots, two of them have restrooms (the first does not). There is a shelter and a place to put in a canoe or kayak. It looks like they allow fishing as well.

Quite a few gyms and Pokestops here for the Go players.

A small charge to keep this place going is well worth the money spent. Play around with the virtual reality headset, see more trolls, and learn about the history of Wisconsin. This place has some very unique pieces you won't find elsewhere. A menagerie of different artwork, it's truly one if a kind. I was disappointed to see Little Norway was no more, but this has many of their pieces. A must see when you're in the area, please stop in to keep this around for future generations. It is an interactive museum, art gallery, and gift shop, the likes of which you won't find elsewhere.

Great all year around, this is one of my favorite places to go to see the beauty of nature.

A very pleasant drive (or walk/bike) up the mountain leads to chair lift rides (a must at least once in your lifetime during autumn), the tower with its unparalleled views of the surrounding area, giant boulders, lots of color, and the smell that is the definition of fall.

For those that love hiking, skiing, nature, and spectacular views, you'll love Rib Mountain.

If you're visiting from out of town, or if you've just never been, you must stop in to see this amazing site.

Had to stop here before heading to Roche-a-Cri. A very clear lake with lots of catfish, turtles, and ground-nesting birds. The hike is fairly quick and very easy. We spent a little more than an hour here. There's several terrain changes and this place really packs in a lot to see. Whatever the white bunches of flowers are (Elderberry, maybe) add a wonderful, clean smell to the area. The bridge/boardwalk is well made and really adds a special something to the area. Well worth the trip!

There is a Pokestop at both entrances for the Go players, no gyms.

A very nice large park with history. The beginnings of water ski competitions, I never would have known if not for stopping here.

This park has quite a lot going on. Several shelters, restrooms, picnic areas, playground, trails for hiking and biking, big beautiful beach. It looks like they have events here and have concessions. The park seems to go all the way around the perimeter of the lake.

I wonder if they'll ever add a suspension bridge like at North Wood County Park, that would be pretty cool.

Several Pokestops and gyms here.

This place is huge and gorgeous! Lots of things to do here: disc golf, fishing, swimming, kayaking, hiking. Many great picture opportunities. There are restrooms and shelters, picnic tables and grills. Lots of camping space. A playground area. The suspension bridge is fun just walking across. Lots of wildlife and flowers. Beautiful views! Well worth checking out!

For the Go players, there's at least one Pokestop and one gym. We had a very weak connection there, so not sure if there were more due to loading issues.

This place is gigantic and very beautiful!

I'm not sure why it was closed to driving traffic, but open to walking. A note on the gate said due to Covid, but that doesn't make any sense.

We walked through for a bit, but we had gotten there late, and didn't realize it would be closed for vehicle traffic, so we didn't make it very far. We did get to see more wildlife driving on Ball Rd, but it's a pretty rough road.

They really should get this place opened back up.

What a beautiful park!

I don't know how I had never heard of this place (or maybe I did and just forgot), but it's gorgeous here. The path by the river was a little difficult with all the leaves covering it, but well worth the hike. No bugs and not a tough hike, just filled with beauty and serenity.

We'll have to stop back again sometime in summer to see what it looks like then.

If you haven't been here before, you should stop in and check it out.

I think we came a week or two early, we didn't see very much wildlife. Still, there were beautiful sounds of nature and it is a nice serene area. The view from the tower was very nice, and we liked seeing the few birds, turtles, squirrels, and chipmunks. We plan to go back sometime when everything is green again. Worth checking out if you're in the area, but wasn't really worth the time for as far as we drove to see it at the time we went.

What a beautiful place!

It was a little difficult to get a decent picture of the waterfall with the constant traffic, but managed to get a couple shots. I wonder if someday they'll add a walkway to make it easier.

We met the new owner and his dog, and they were both very nice!

We didn't get to go inside on this trip, but that's alright.

Well worth visiting!

One gym and two Pokestops here for the Go players.

Haven't been here since I was a teenager, but it's still an awesome place to go! It's surprising the different animals they have. Some you'd expect for northern Wisconsin, but others you wouldn't think to see here. You can pet a lot of the animals, give a bear a drink, and get covered in Budgies. They have food and drinks, and you can get food for the animals. This is a must see at least once in your life!

We had a great time here. Think we spent about six hours taking it all in. Got some (relatively) old time candy from Old Town, spent some time in the old theatre (we watched a movie about a guy wrongly put in an insane asylum). All the different areas were unique and enlightening. The butterflies were a great addition to an already great museum experience. We would return again.

Great walking paths, bridges (including a covered one, excellent photo opportunity), lighthouse, grandstand, and views of the lake. Would have spent more time there, but it was too early in the year, still very chilly with a strong wind. Could easily spend an afternoon there in slightly warmer temperatures. And there are deer you can feed. They come right up to the fence.

We didn't get to spend much time here, so I can't really give a proper review.

The waterfall was pretty, and the park looked nice from what we could see. Unfortunately weather and time were not cooperative for an extended hike.

We'll be back at some point to check out the park interior and get down by the water.

Possibly one Pokestop at the entrance.

"Worlds Largest" things are always worth checking out!

We got here pretty late at night, and there's really not much to say about this. We had planned to go to the Community Soup Day, but then the Coronavirus happened. Maybe we'll make it next year.

There are a few Pokestops and Gyms in the area for the Go players.

We didn't get the chance to go inside, but it's a beautiful area. The house looks well built, and is a nice design. Saw some otters (I think, wasn't fast enough to get pictures) running through the back yard. We would like to stop in again sometime when we're in the area to see what the inside is like.

A little weird, a little creepy, very cool! We had a great time walking around here. Some of the molds took me back to being a kid, like the Big Boy restaurant mascot. There was even a Koopa standing on its shell, kind of curious what that was used for. A very unique place, and we're glad we stopped.

Beautiful area, and the rest of the park around it was great! Fair grounds nearby had a concert going on, so we got to hear good music while visiting. Unique garden area, river, steamboats, giant statues, a cannon, lots of birds and ducks, all very well maintained. A nice place to spend an afternoon.

Very nice exhibits, though the Houdini exhibit was small, and seemed geared much more towards young children. Still offered interesting facts about the man and his tricks, but guess we were expecting a little more. Beautiful building with a giant mural painted on the side.

Some nice trails, accompanied by the songs of many types of birds.

Some of the trails need a little work, there were a bunch of dead fish, and I had several ticks on me afterwards, but otherwise still had an enjoyable hike.
A very nice park with trails, fishing areas, shelters, a playground, restrooms (one with plumbing/electric, one without), and lots of wildlife. Plenty of parking, and easy to get around.

Nice hike, we would go again. Limited parking, it might get tight during peak hiking times. We took our 2 and 4.5 year olds, it was a bit long for them but we brought a carrier for the 2 year old and lots of snacks!. The climb down is a bit tricky, the kids needed a decent amount of help but they made it and the rest of the hike was fine! Definitely lots of mud, so just plan on getting dirty. There are side trails in the worst mud spots so you can bypass some of it. We did see others hiking, and saw some signs of horses but it was not crowded at all. We did not have cell service there either (we use AT&T), at least for a lot of it. I stopped paying attention so maybe parts of the hike have coverage...but if you need directions make sure to have those on hand and dont count on looking them up just in case.

Well kept, clean trail, we only saw one water bottle on the ground. Boardwalk is nice and flat and easy for kids to walk on and there are benches all along the route. It is stroller friendly too, but maybe hard if two stroller tried to pass each other. I took my 2 and 4.5 year olds and it was a good length but we all thought it was a bit boring overall. There are some neat big trees, and we did see several ducks, birds, two rabbits, a worm and a slug so there was plenty of wildlife. Maybe it is more interesting during the wet season. The bugs weren't too awful but I'd consider bug spray if we went back. The parking lot is small but there was plenty of space when we went and has had space everytime we have driven past. Also interesting cabins at the start, they would be fun to see inside.

Nice little aquarium to bring the kids. Can touch some of the animals and enough others to look at. Volunteers are friendly and knowledgeable. Fun to walk down on the beach afterwards too. Parking is across the road... $1 for an hour or $2.50 for 2 hours. The machine takes cards and cash but DOES NOT give change. And after trying like a dozen times to get my card to work I ended up having to pay $10 for an hour of parking which is really annoying. Bring some $1 bills incase the card reader isn't working! Lesson learned. :-/

Beautiful views at the top but not a hike for kids or people who don't like heights. A lot of the trail is right on the edge and narrow, and there isnt a ton of room to move around at the top near the lookout. Not a very long hike, although it is pretty steep. We went in mid-June and the top was very, very windy and cold with some of the bushes covered in ice yet. My husband climbs mountains and thought it was great, our kids and I can say we did it...but would be fine never going on it again :-)

Good museum. Definitely smaller, but our two little kids (2.5 and almost 5) had a lot of fun, especially in the dinosaur section. They didnt really understand the lower level but had fun wandering and looking at some of the items. We went on the free Thursday and we had to park a couple blocks away but it was totally fine and easy. Everyone was super kind too. We only spent an hour there but it was worth the trip, and we will go back and spend more time as the kids get older.

A cute little hike/walk that was very easy for our 2 and 4 year olds to do. They looked at the falls and the little power dam and then we saw a number of giant trees and a few slugs. There were a couple spots we could get to the water's edge and they could toss rocks etc. Small enough we will probably only do it once and not over and over, but it was still a good experience to get the kids outside, loving nature and practicing hiking

This park is ok, worth a visit but maybe not my fav. The geyser doesn't flame anymore but the trails are pretty easy for the kids and it's nice scenery. There is a little creek spot my kids like to look at and it does have bathrooms, picnic tables and a small playground. Lots of parking. We have been here a few times because its easy and close and we always see a number of other people out, especially walking dogs.

Great park, love the three level climbing structure and the smaller one for smaller kids and baby swings. Lots of grassy area, my oldest saw a deer.  Bathrooms, picnic tables and benches, generous parking lot.

Only things I don't like is the lack of big kid swings, and the playground doesn't really get shade so everything gets hot. It is off a busy road too, but the play area is set so far back it's not bad.

Fun spot to visit, neat old buildings to explore and learn about and the trail is pretty wide and flat making it good for little kids. We managed to take our jogging stroller alright, and besides other walkers we saw one person on a bike and a few horses. We did not see all of it and would go back again to wander more. There is a nice pavilion to have a picnic in and there is a big porta potty there too.

Great place to go for a walk with the kids, pretty plants and well taken care of. There is a little library with a bench you can stop at, a little pond with stepping stones over the top, a number of fun trails, and a childrens discovery area that is used during the week for a preschool/camps but is fun for little kids to explore after hours. Good place to find painted rocks too.

This is a nice park, has some unique climbing choices, a couple of smaller slides and a pretend tractor to climb on too. I think it's cute but my 2.5 and 4.5 year olds were not as interested in it and got bored after a short time. Lots of open space, a nice pavilion with tables and trash bins, grills, a little enclosed soccer field and bathrooms.

We have been here only twice but both times it seemed like a pretty quiet park. We saw other people but it wasnt crowded and parking was fine. It has nice enough bathrooms, a number of picnic tables and grassy areas along the river. The short Weeks Falls trail is quick and easy to do, especially for young kids.

Nice trails and a beautiful area but we always run into SO many bikers so it is hard for our family to hike... we are always having to look behind us, and keep an eye out ahead of us and move to the side of the trail.  It ends up being pretty annoying and now we tend to find other places to hike!

Fun spot for the kids! Very limited parking so definitely just plan on parking in a parking deck somewhere... there are some options within a couple of blocks. Can get a bit crowded, especially if the weather is bad but the kids still have a good time!

Pretty park, nice playground for the kids, lots of picnic tables and grass area and the fields look nice too. The bathroom was pretty clean and it even has a changing station. We never have trouble parking, but have only gone at quiet times too.

Decent park, a lot of parking, and it has bathrooms. Playground is ok but maybe a little old and at least one of the baby swings could use some help. The sports fields look nice but we didn't use them etc so I'm not totally sure on those.

Nice trail to walk around the lake, it's pretty short and flat and great for smaller kids. Our son made it around walking when he was just under 3. Has nice bathrooms and parking and a nice little playground for the kids too.

Popular place but a fun walk down to the beach and back. Its downhill all the way out so the walk back with kids is more difficult. We made it with a 2 and 4.5 year old though and saw plenty of families out doing the same.

Cute little museum with bugs and reptiles...a lot of good displays of preserved bugs and a number of living animals too.  Totally free to go to the museum and there is a nice little gift store there too.
Cute playground for the kids and a lot of beachfront to walk and play on. Lots to find and explore, especially at low tide. Nice bathrooms and picnic areas. Seems like a really popular place.
Super basic concrete tower, not super high, not very handicap accessible...but a tower that gives good views of the surrounding area. Bring quarters if you want to use one of the telescopes.
Nice quiet, semi-shaded playground, has a climbing structure with slides and swings and there is a tire swing further away too. Lots of grassy area to play in and plenty of parking.
Nice playground equipment for the kids, and a lot of green space for them to run around and play.  The beach is nice to play during the summer or go wading in with rain boots on.
We have only been here once but it seems like an older park and maybe better for bigger kids. Does have a lot of green space though.
Fun trail for a family walk. It is uphill on the way out but our 3 year old was totally fine with it and we carried a baby with us.

Enjoyed the Perseids meteor shower here this past Saturday. I've been to this park multiple times and it never disappoints. We arrived 2 hours before dusk and decided to hike the horseshoe loop and Elm Lake trail. Wow the skyline around the Horseshoe loop had so many spiders, way up high so don't worry, a few were spinning their daily catch. Also saw 2 armadillos on this trail, but the best thing was seeing about a 200lb boar cross the trail about 75 yards in front of us. As we were leaving the horseshoe loop we saw an 8 foot alligator swimming across the water. Walking around elm lake there were lots of 3 to 4 foot alligators dotting the lake with just their eyes and snout above water. This is a very popular park and you will meet all kinds of friendly faces from around the world speaking multiple different languages.
