The camping fills up pretty quickly here so it's best to make reservations if that's what you want to do. There are multiple sites, tents, rv, electric, water, primitive. The park is so big that if you're not into walking much you could bring bikes and ride around. One of the best features of this park is the George Observatory. Every Saturday night you can line up and look through the telescopes for a fee or there are other astronomers there with their own telescopes set up and they are more than happy to talk to you about everything. My first time looking through the telescopes I saw a binary solar system which was so cool and Jupiter with 3 of its moons viable. I highly recommend this park!

Do not try to drive to this location. You can only access this via the Spring Creek Greenway. Park at Pundt park and hike, bike, or horseback ride a little over a mile to here or park at Carter park for around a 3 mile distance. Stahl Preserve has a nice little pond with lots of cypress trees in it. Fishing is catch and release. If you're lucky you may see a beaver or river otter. Plenty of benches and trash cans. Halfway between Carter and Pundt park is a water cooler to refill your water bottles. Hiked an 11 mile loop from Carter park to Pundt park. The 2 extra miles was exploring trails off of the Greenway trail. Was exciting to see a Piliated Woodpecker, Mother racoon with 4 babies, Green Heron, soft-shell turtle, rabbit, and many more birds, butterflies, and dragonflies. The hike took a total of 5 hours and 15 minutes with 4 hours of actual hike time. It was dusk during the last 2 miles and I heard a hog squealing. Then about a mile later heard a lot of hogs at the edge of the treeline. Precinct 4 officers take periodic strolls through the trail to make sure everyone is fine. They will offer a ride or assistance if need be. I'd advise not going on a Saturday. You hear gun shots from the nearby shooting range nearly the whole way. Last weekend I hiked the section from Carter to Jesse Jones park and didn't hear any gun fire.
dislikes: Noise pollution (gun shots from nearby shooting range)

reviews_attraction.text: First of all don't confuse this for the splash pad. The splash pad parking lot is about 5 minutes away. With that said there are still 2 jungle gyms for kids to play on but the real winner of this park is the soccer fields, jogging track with workout stations, and the newly installed disc golf course. The disc golf course doesn't have any maps yet and at first the layout looked erattic but I believe if you hug the right side and make the turn back at the water treatment plant and pond. I spent time jogging the trails and trying to figure out the layout of the disc golf course and got a good workout. Between this park and the splash pad that shares the same acreage I got 4 miles out of it and could do more with the loops. The restrooms at this location were pretty putrid. You must HOLD the flush button to flush your urine and some people haven't figured that out. There are plenty of trash cans, benches, grills and pick nick tables and so much room that you should never feel crowded and tons of parking. I'm so glad we found this place!

Had the best day here on my wife's 40th birthday. Lived here for 16 years and have always wanted to visit. We decided to finally go and see the Christmas lights as well as the Ice Land exhibit that was on display. We opted for the after 3pm evening all inclusive pass that is quite a deal. Pretty much the same price as 2 attractions but you have 7 hours to do pretty much everything in the park. We started off in the aquarium, went to the rainforest pyramid, let the kids slide on the big slide, took a walk on the mile long path of Christmas lights, boarded the Colonel paddle wheel boat and opted to freeze on the windy upper deck, climbed on the ropes course and finished off freezing in the super spectacular Ice Land exhibit. If you see this review while it is still here I strongly recommend seeing it. Its really a once in a lifetime experience. Make sure to wear long John's and plenty of layers. Its 9°F... Thank you Moody Gardens for an evening filled with Awesome memories!!!

Very nicely marked trails with some impressive boardwalks, benches and observation deck. The first orange loop trail is very easy for any beginner. If you decide to venture onto the turquoise trail, know that you may not be able to make the complete loop due to high water. It is wetlands you know. And be aware that there are wild hogs out here. I observed a bunch of them on the pipeline. When I saw the big boar it was time for me to head back. Wildlife seen today: Great Blue Heron, Great Egret, Juvenile White Ibis with brown wings; Wild hogs - females, piglets, & boar; black caterpillars with white hairs - hickory tussock, Barred owl, white tail deer, turtle, crow, squirrel, rabbit, cows, funnel web spiders, lots of orb weavers, and a ton of misquotes!!! The owl flew right beside me. I guess it was overhead and I didn't notice it. It swooped down beside me and flew off. Was very impressive! Had a great time here hiking 6.5 miles.
dislikes: Incomplete turquoise trail due to high water

reviews_attraction.text: Pretty cool 18 hole disc golf course that's about 2 miles with separate hiking trails. That said, be prepared to Brown Blaze, as restrooms are not available at this park. The first 2 holes aren't marked very clearly and 3 thru 5 take a little figuring out, but after that it's one continuous trail to the next hole with a junction between 7 & 8 then again towards the end. After the first few holes you won't find any benches or trash receptacles. Be forewarned that the old creek beds are littered with broken glass and ancient oil filters and tin cans. It probably wouldn't be a bad idea to bring a small bag for trash and do a little trail maintenance while you're here. I removed sticks and logs and such that were in the trail but didn't have anything to remove the broken glass. The first few holes are in the sun but after that it's nice and shady. Bring the MOSQUITO SPRAY!!! FYI...Telge park is the closest public restrooms to here.

This place has some decent trails and I actually saw my first black with red stripes grasshopper. I loved the sounds of the different birds I heard while walking through the trails. There are a lot of road walks and powerline trails and the observation point is actually a dead end into a small mud puddle. The place has plenty of portapotty's but no toilet paper. They also have lots of trash cans which is nice if people would actually use them. The cops won't do anything about people letting their dogs run around without a leash even after they attack your dogs so I wouldn't recommend bringing your pets with you. This place may be better through the week but definitely don't go here on the weekend looking for solitude. There are also a lot of roots on the trails so watch your footing, 3 out of 5 of us tripped. Saw a lot of bikers out so this park maybe better suited for that.

Enjoyed a nice afternoon hiking 10 miles with the family today on the Chinquapin trail, Prairie Branch Loop, Dogwood trail, a small portion of the Triple C trail and The Lone Star trail. The trails have some nice elevation changes, we gained a total of 1399 ft. Trails are mostly packed dirt and is rooty with a few sandy spots here and there with a lot of board walks, wooden bridges and plenty of benches to stop and rest for a few. Saw a Piliated Woodpecker, Great Blue Heron, Egrets, baby turtle, and many different dragonflies and butterflies. A few horse flies but not too many. The trails were mostly tree tree covered and not too crowded and if you have a filter there are many spots to refill your water bottles. Much to my surprise there was  plenty of trail maps at the trail heads, you don't get that at most parks.

Came out here yesterday and we didn't have bug spray, big mistake. Today we saw our first owl on a hike. A huge one over on the left side from the entrance along the creek. Awesome experience! Lots of birds, bird houses, and bat houses. A bunch of crisscrossing sandy/dirt trails that would be fun on a mountain bike or a nice woodsy hike thru some wetlands. We got 4 miles out of it today and could've kept going but we turned at the water treatment plant because the sun was setting. Bring your own water. They have a porta-potty. I wanted to find all of the numbered posts but fell short. Not even sure they are there post Harvey. No maps and the trails aren't marked well but most of the trails loop around each other. Loved it and will be back.

1-29-2017 A huge place to explore. Lots of equestrian/ bike trails and there are lots of hiking trails tucked away for the woodies feeling. We heard one of the protected woodpeckers that take up residence in the park but couldn't manage to see it. Even though there was a lot of people there, the place is so huge that it's not crowded. A great place for dog walking as well... 11-17-2018 Don't put this location into your GPS, it will dump you in a neighborhood dead end street with no parking. Instead use the trailhead locations for directions to the 2 parking lots. West parking lot has a Porto potty. No trashcans, so pack out what you bring in.

Awesome splash pad, huge jungle gym area for the kids and the best part is this park is open when most are closed. There's plenty of parking and room for everyone. 2 huge pavilions with monster grills and kitchen with reservation. There is also other pick nick areas with grills as well.  The whole park is being upgraded and connects to the disc golf course, soccer fields, and train station, but the parking lot for that area is about 5 minutes away. You can walk if need be. The restrooms are really clean and there are plenty of trash cans so there shouldn't be any litter around. They also have a gym area with tons of equipment on it.

Love the 1 mile long 9 hole disc golf course here. Easy enough for beginners and gives the more experienced players a nice short course to hone their skills. Played a round and was going to play again when two really cool people invited me along. They helped me by giving me some welcome advice. I've played this course off and on for a couple of years. Just added some new discs to my collection so I'll be back to break them in... Restrooms are here as well as plenty of trash cans. There is also a baseball & soccer field here with goals, playground, splashpad, and picnic tables for a nice family day outside.

Pretty nice paved trails that connects to the Spring Creek Greenway. We hiked a little over 3 miles here. Restrooms were very clean. If you have kids there's a small playground here for them. They have a beautiful butterfly garden and a couple of ponds you can fish at, (catch and release only). There is a cover pavilion that you can rent. They also have cabins but I don't know if they are for rent. We saw some birds that we haven't seen before out here, some rabbits, and the smell of the blooming white flowers on the trails is truly aroma therapy this time of year.

This is a great coastal area that has a playground for children and even a musical instrument area outside. Lots of people come here to fish, crab, and barbecue under one of its many pick nick areas. There is also a small nature center and learning plaques throughout the parks nature trails. There was a huge Nurture Nature Festival yesterday that is free to the public. Any other time there is a small fee per person to enter the park daily. We hiked 5 miles here today and only covered about half of the available trails.

There are loads of covered pavilions, and playground structures here. I actually like the fact that they have red barrels set up for dumping you hot coals in after you're finished barbecuing. There's also a big fenced in area to let your dogs run around with a bunch of things for them to play on as well. High police presence. I don't know if there were that many bad people here or not but I saw 3 of them pulling people over and 1 was at a pavilion with their lights on.

Huge park with nearly unlimited parking, cricket fiels, softball fields, 2 dog parks, jungle gym for the kids, nice clean restrooms,  fishing, bird watching, and about 5 miles or more of hiking if you do all of the loops. If you plan on hiking bring your water and sunscreen and be very mindful of the rotten wood on the decks and bridges!!! Definitely worth seeing!!

Nice woody trails with lots of vines. Take bug spray to help keep the horse flies from biting. Lots of sand bars and views of the creek. About 2 miles of trails. Closed past the bridge though. You can walk to cypress creek nature center from here but it's not recommended yet. The trail is grown up, but will be connected in the future.

Had a blast here and the kids loved it. Entered the cricket eating contest and got 2nd place. Also loved sampling the cricket buffet. Lots of fun puzzles to exercise your brain and many physical activities too. Different movies play throughout the day in their theater. I can still hear the auditable heart beating.

It's a small rock path less than a mile. On our walk today it was windy and a widow maker got blown out of a tree behind us. Luckily no one was around it when it fell. This is a nice urban hike but if you're looking for more of a woodsy hike this isn't it. It has a really nice play area for kids though.

Cool scenic drive and equestrian trails. There's a few ponds to fish at (catch and release) we hiked 2 miles on some overgrown trails that went by the creek. Saw some kayakers enjoying themselves. Loads of blackberries too. There's also a nice playground for kids and a fenced in dog park.

The gps ends in a cul-de-sac and there is no parking. I presume that you would park at the Zube park close by and walk here. I got here late so I didn't get a real chance to experience it. Will come back at a later date because the Zube park, splash pad, and disc golf course are GREAT!!!

No place to park or walk. Some people were parked on the side of the road next to the water fishing. But that's about it. Imilda flooded the area and boats were parked in odd locations, that was the most entertaining thing we saw.
Wetlands Park with soccer fields, basketball goals, playground, and trails to walk on. Word to the wise don't go down the power line and gas line trails.
Nice paved path in the trees around some ponds with a ton of turtles, squirls, birds, and butterflies. 1.5 miles of trails if you do all of the loops.
Beautiful beach not crowded like the others, plus there is about 5+ miles of hiking trails and camping here along with a nature center.
